title: [Bugfix][MLA] Add logits size budget to sparse indexer prefill chunking
body:
Alternative to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35488, credit to @haosdent 

## Summary
- Adds a logits tensor size constraint to sparse MLA indexer prefill chunking to prevent CUDA OOM
- Introduces `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` env var (default 512 MB) to bound the [M, N] float32 logits tensor
- Replaces `split_prefill_chunks` with `split_indexer_prefill_chunks` that respects both workspace and logits size constraints

## Test plan
- [x] Added unit tests for `split_indexer_prefill_chunks` covering various constraint scenarios
- [x] Run existing MLA tests: `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py`

title: [Perf] DSV3.2 Indexer Fused Weights Projection
body:
## Purpose

Fuse the WK and Weights_Proj projections in the DSV3.2 Indexer. This is an alternative optimization to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35968, which overlaps the projections instead of fusing them. Doing the fusion provides a greater speedup:

Benchmark timings for DSV3.2 NVFP4 on 8xB200 (TP8, No Specdec)

### BS128 8k/1k
```
Fused WK+WeightsProj (Decode):  21.6 ms
Baseline             (Decode):  22.3 ms
```

### BS1 8k/1k
```
Fused WK+WeightsProj (Decode):  9.5 ms
Overlap              (Decode):  9.8  ms
Baseline             (Decode):  10.2  ms

Fused WK+WeightsProj (TTFT):  339 ms
Overlap              (TTFT):  340 ms
Baseline             (TTFT):  341 ms
```

## Testing

GSM8k shows a slight decrease.

title: [Refactor] Improve indexer decode path metadata preparation
body:
## Purpose

### What changed                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                               
This PR refactors the decode path of DeepseekV32IndexerMetadataBuilder and the supporting C++ kernels. No behavioral changes on any existing path.         
                                                                                                                                                               vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py                                                                                                                  
- Remove offsets from DeepSeekV32IndexerDecodeMetadata. Per-token effective lengths are now pre-computed in the builder instead of being reconstructed at each call site.                                                                                                                                            - Allocate decode_seq_lens_buffer with the correct shape at init time: (max_num_seqs, next_n) for native MTP, (max_num_batched_tokens,) for flatten/plain decode. Fixed shape ensures stable CUDA graph addresses.                                                                                                   - Extract _prepare_decode_tensors() — the 60-line if/else block in build() is now a dedicated method returning (seq_lens, block_table, decode_lens, batch_size, requires_padding).                                                                                                                             - Fuse two repeat_interleave calls in the flatten path into one by pre-computing the per-batch scalar offset: `seq_lens - decode_lens - query_start_loc`.
- Fix requires_padding always being hardcoded False — now correctly set when decode lengths are non-uniform.

csrc/sampler.cu
- Add `seqLensStride` parameter to topKPerRowDecode. When seqLensStride == 0 (1D), the kernel computes rowEnd = seq_len - next_n + next_n_idx + 1 as before.
- When seqLensStride > 0 (2D), it reads the pre-computed per-row length directly as seqLens[rowIdx].

csrc/topk.cu
- Relax large_context_topk input validation from requiring a strict 1D lengths tensor to accepting any contiguous tensor with numel() == batch_size, allowing 2D (B, next_n) input.

vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py
- Remove offsets-based length reconstruction at call sites. All three kernel paths now receive seq_lens directly from metadata.
- Remove dead commented-out code.

### Why
Previously, seq_lens in metadata held raw per-request lengths and each kernel call site had to compute per-token effective lengths inline (seq_lens - next_n + offset + 1). This scattered the same logic across multiple files. Centralizing it in the builder makes the data flow explicit and keeps kernel call sites simple.


### Testing
- Verified on B200 with DeepSeek-V3 (MTP next_n=2, next_n=4) using gsm8k eval for correctness
- Plain decode (next_n=1) unaffected — code path unchanged.  

## Test Plan
```
vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-V3.2-NVFP4  \
  -tp 4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8  \
  --max_model_len auto \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v3 \
  --speculative-config.method deepseek_mtp \
  --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 1
```

gsm8k command
```
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args "model=nvidia/DeepSeek-V3.2-NVFP4,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8001/v1/completions,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None,num_concurrent=2048,timeout=5000,max_length=32768" \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --log_samples \
  --output_path "gsm8k_results"
```

title: [Bug] Fix rocm sparse attn indexer issue
body:
## Purpose

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39219#discussion_r3047394497

In `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py`, we have 

```py
    attn_metadata = attn_metadata[k_cache_prefix]
    assert isinstance(attn_metadata, DeepseekV32IndexerMetadata)
    slot_mapping = attn_metadata.slot_mapping
    has_decode = attn_metadata.num_decodes > 0
    has_prefill = attn_metadata.num_prefills > 0
    num_decode_tokens = attn_metadata.num_decode_tokens

    # During speculative decoding, k may be padded to the CUDA graph batch
    # size while slot_mapping only covers actual tokens. Truncate k to avoid
    # out-of-bounds reads in the kernel.
    num_tokens = slot_mapping.shape[0]
    k = k[:num_tokens]
```

The same logic applied to rocm as well, this PR solves the issue

title: [ROCm] Add MLA dual RMS norm fusion (Q, KV) pass for DeepSeek/Kimi-K2
body: ## Summary Add a `torch.inductor` post-grad pattern-matcher pass that fuses the paired `q_a_layernorm` and `kv_a_layernorm` RMS norm operations in DeepSeek-V3 / Kimi-K2 MLA attention into a single `fused_qk_rmsnorm` HIP kernel call via AITer. In the unfused graph, each MLA layer runs two separate `rms_norm` calls on the q and kv compressed latents: ``` qkv_lora = gemm(hidden) q_c, kv_lora = split(qkv_lora, [1536, 576]) kv_c, k_pe = split(kv_lora, [512, 64]) q_c = rms_norm(q_c, q_weight, eps) # norm #1 kv_c = rms_norm(kv_c, kv_weight, eps) # norm #2 ``` The pass uses `torch._inductor.pattern_matcher.register_replacement` to match the connected subgraph — both splits and both norms — and rewrites it to: ``` q_c, kv_lora = split(qkv_lora, [1536, 576]) kv_c, k_pe = split(kv_lora, [512, 64]) q_normed, kv_normed = fused_mla_dual_rms_norm( q_c, q_weight, kv_c, kv_weight, eps1, eps2) ``` This reduces kernel launch overhead from 2 launches to 1 per MLA layer (61 layers in Kimi-K2). ### Changes - **`vllm/_aiter_ops.py`** — register `fused_mla_dual_rms_norm` custom op wrapping AITer's `fused_qk_rmsnorm` HIP kernel - **`vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/rocm_aiter_fusion.py`** — `MLADualRMSNormPattern` + `MLADualRMSNormFusionPass` using `register_replacement` pattern matching - **`vllm/config/compilation.py`** / **`vllm/config/vllm.py`** — `fuse_mla_dual_rms_norm` PassConfig flag (ROCm-only, auto-enabled when AITer is available at O1+) - **`vllm/compilation/passes/pass_manager.py`** — register the pass - **`tests/compile/passes/test_fuse_mla_dual_rms_norm.py`** — unit test verifying pattern match, op replacement, and numerical correctness ### Enable Enabled by default when AITer is available (optimization level ≥ O1). Can also be toggled explicitly: ```bash --compilation-config='{"pass_config": {"fuse_mla_dual_rms_norm": true}}' ``` ### AITer dependency Requires AITer PR [#2442](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/2442) (`fused_qk_rmsnorm` HIP kernel, commit `149a8f613`). ![PR Status](https://img.shields.io/github/pulls/detail/state/ROCm/aiter/2442) ## Accuracy | Benchmark | Metric | Score | Threshold | Status | |-----------|--------|-------|-----------|--------| | GSM8K (5-shot, 250 samples) | exact_match (flexible-extract) | **0.94** | 0.90 | ✅ PASS | | GSM8K (5-shot, 250 samples) | exact_match (strict-match) | **0.94** | 0.90 | ✅ PASS | Model: Kimi-K2-Thinking-MXFP4, TP=4, MI355X, fp8 KV cache ## Trace showing fused kernel Two separate RMSNorm CK kernels `_ZN7ck_tile6kentryILi1ENS_12Rmsnorm2dFwdINS_27Rmsnorm2dFwdPipelineOnePassINS_27Rmsnorm2dFwdPipelineProblemIDF` replaced with single AITER kernel `ZN5aiter23fused_qk_rmsnorm_kernel` ## Performance **Kimi-K2-Thinking-MXFP4, TP=4, MI355X** | Config | Concurrency | Baseline (tok/s/GPU) | QK RMSNorm Fusion (tok/s/GPU) | Improvement | |--------|:-----------:|------------------:|--------------------------:|:-----------:| | 1k/1k | 4 | 190 | 194 | 1.02x | | 1k/1k | 8 | 321 | 326 | 1.01x | | 1k/1k | 16 | 521 | 533 | 1.02x | | 1k/1k | 32 | 783 | 801 | 1.02x | | 1k/1k | 64 | 1173 | 1177 | 1.00x | | 8k/1k | 4 | 799 | 819 | 1.03x | | 8k/1k | 8 | 1348 | 1367 | 1.01x | | 8k/1k | 16 | 2051 | 2074 | 1.01x | | 8k/1k | 32 | 2917 | 2975 | 1.02x | | 8k/1k | 64 | 4038 | 4026 | 1.00x | | | | | **Geomean uplift** | **1.02x** | ## Test plan - [x] Unit test: pattern fires, ops replaced, numerical correctness (`test_fuse_mla_dual_rms_norm`) - [x] Pass fires on all TP workers: `MLADualRMSNormFusionPass: fused 1 q/kv norm pair(s)` - [x] FX graph dumps confirm before/after rewrite - [x] GSM8K accuracy check passes (0.94 >= 0.90 threshold) - [x] Throughput benchmark (see table above) ## Related - AITer `fused_qk_rmsnorm` HIP kernel: [ROCm/aiter#2442](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/2442)

title: [V1][Metrics] Add MLA attention metrics for DeepSeek MFU estimation
body:
## Purpose
 
Adds `MLAAttentionMetrics` to the V1 performance metrics module to correctly estimate FLOPs and memory bandwidth for models using Multi-Latent Attention (MLA), such as DeepSeek-V2, DeepSeek-V3, and DeepSeek-R1.
 
The existing `AttentionMetrics` assumes standard MHA or GQA attention patterns with separate K/V projections and large KV cache representations. MLA introduces a fundamentally different architecture:
 
- Compressed KV cache storing a single `(kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim)` vector per token per layer instead of `2 * num_kv_heads * head_dim`
- For DeepSeek-V3 this results in 576 bytes vs 32,768 bytes per token per layer (bf16), approximately 57x reduction
- Low-rank Q projection: `hidden → q_lora_rank → num_heads * qk_head_dim`
- Shared KV projection: `hidden → kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim`, then expanded via `kv_lora_rank → num_heads * (qk_nope_head_dim + v_head_dim)`
 
Without this change, MFU and memory bandwidth estimates are significantly incorrect due to overestimation of KV cache reads/writes and incorrect projection dimensions.
 
## Design
 
This implementation introduces a clean, extensible design:
 
- `AttentionDetectionParser` - prevents standard attention metrics from being instantiated for MLA models
- `MLADetectionParser` - ensures MLA metrics are only applied to valid MLA models
- `MLAConfigParser` - extracts MLA-specific configuration fields
- `MLAAttentionMetrics` - implements correct FLOPs and memory calculations
 
A separate MLA metrics class is introduced instead of modifying existing logic. This preserves backward compatibility, keeps the implementation modular, and enables future extensions for additional attention variants.
 
## Impact
 
- Correct MFU and memory bandwidth estimation for MLA-based models
- No impact on non-MLA models
- No runtime overhead - detection happens during config parsing
 
---
 
## Test Plan
 
The implementation was validated using a combination of unit tests, numerical verification, and regression checks.
 
### Unit Tests Added (9 total)
 
| Test | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `test_mla_config_parser` | Verifies MLA configuration fields are correctly parsed |
| `test_mla_attention_metrics_decode` | Ensures KV cache writes use compressed dimensions (1152 bytes vs 65536 bytes in standard attention) |
| `test_mla_attention_metrics_prefill` | Validates two-stage Q projection FLOPs against hand-computed values |
| `test_mla_kv_cache_vs_standard_attention` | Confirms MLA KV cache is approximately 56.9x smaller than standard attention |
| `test_mla_per_gpu_with_tensor_parallelism` | Ensures correct per-GPU scaling with tensor parallelism |
| `test_mla_per_gpu_with_pipeline_parallelism` | Verifies correct scaling with pipeline parallelism |
| `test_mla_model_metrics_excludes_standard_attention` | Confirms MLA metrics replace standard attention metrics in model breakdown |
| `test_standard_attention_still_works_for_non_mla` | Regression test ensuring standard models remain unaffected |
| `test_mla_attention_scaling_with_layers` | Validates linear scaling of FLOPs and memory with number of layers |
 
### Commands Executed
 
```bash
pytest tests/v1/metrics/test_perf_metrics.py -v --noconftest
ruff check vllm/v1/metrics/perf.py tests/v1/metrics/test_perf_metrics.py
ruff format --check vllm/v1/metrics/perf.py tests/v1/metrics/test_perf_metrics.py
```
 
### Additional Validation
 
- Verified KV cache compression (~56.9x reduction)
- Verified FLOPs calculations against manual computations
- Verified parser-based mutual exclusion between MLA and standard attention metrics
- Verified correctness under tensor and pipeline parallelism configurations

title: [MLA] Optimize mla indexer prepare uniform decode for MTP > 1
body: # Purpose While profiling DeepSeek-V3.2 + NVFP4 with MTP > 1 speculative decoding, I noticed that `_prepare_decode_tensors` in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py` was adding per-step overhead from pytorch ops like `repeat_interleave`. This function is called once per decode step to build MLA attention metadata, and the expensive path is taken whenever decode lengths exceed what the kernel natively supports, which is 2. This is the common case for speculative decoding with MTP > 1, where the target model validates multiple proposed draft tokens. I realized that the `if` branch can be further split into the uniform decode length and variable decode length cases. During speculative decoding with uniform decode lengths (the common case, because the target model validates the N speculated tokens from the draft model), we can simplify the ops considerably. I decided to fuse those ops into a single triton kernel. NOTE: I'm working on [another PR](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37588) to add full cudagraph support for the draft model prefill during speculative decoding in MRV2. title: [Bugfix] Add deepseek_v32 to Quark dynamic MXFP4 model type check
body:
## Summary

Add `deepseek_v32` to `_DEEPSEEK_V3_FAMILY_MODEL_TYPES` so that Quark correctly enables `dynamic_mxfp4_quant` for [amd/DeepSeek-V3.2-mxfp4](https://huggingface.co/amd/DeepSeek-V3.2-mxfp4).

Without this fix, excluded layers (e.g. `self_attn`) are not dynamically re-quantized when serving MXFP4-quantized DeepSeek-V3.2 checkpoints, causing silent correctness degradation (all-zero or garbage output tokens).

## Root cause

`_DEEPSEEK_V3_FAMILY_MODEL_TYPES` is defined as:

```python
_DEEPSEEK_V3_FAMILY_MODEL_TYPES = frozenset({"deepseek_v3"})
```

The `maybe_update_config()` method uses this set to gate `dynamic_mxfp4_quant`. DeepSeek-V3.2 uses `model_type = "deepseek_v32"` in its HuggingFace config, which is not in the set. As a result, `dynamic_mxfp4_quant` stays `False`, and `get_quant_method()` returns `UnquantizedLinearMethod()` for attention projections instead of applying the correct quantization scheme.

## Fix

```diff
- _DEEPSEEK_V3_FAMILY_MODEL_TYPES = frozenset({"deepseek_v3"})
+ _DEEPSEEK_V3_FAMILY_MODEL_TYPES = frozenset({"deepseek_v3", "deepseek_v32"})
```

One-line change. Adding `"deepseek_v32"` to the frozen set enables the dynamic MXFP4 path for the V3.2 model family while preserving existing V3 behavior.

## Validation

Validated on **8× AMD MI355X (gfx950)** with `amd/DeepSeek-V3.2-mxfp4`, TP=8, `attention_backend=ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`, `--enforce-eager`.

### Configuration

```
--tensor-parallel-size 8
--max-model-len 8192
--block-size 1
--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9
--no-enable-prefix-caching
--enforce-eager
```

### Functional Tests

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| `/v1/models` endpoint | ✅ Model listed successfully |
| Basic math (`What is 2+2?`) | ✅ Correct: `2 + 2 = 4` |
| Short summarization (JWST paragraph → 2 sentences) | ✅ Coherent 62-token summary, `finish_reason=stop` |
| Long summarization (AI history → 3-4 paragraphs) | ✅ Coherent 934-token / 4-paragraph summary, `finish_reason=stop` |

### GSM8K (lm-eval, 5-shot)

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Questions | 1319 |
| Few-shot | 5 |
| Strict-match accuracy | **0.9515 ± 0.0059** |

### Throughput Benchmark

512 random prompts (~4503 input / ~140 output tokens), concurrency 128:

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Successful requests | 479 / 512 |
| Request throughput | 2.12 req/s |
| Output token throughput | 297 tok/s |
| Peak output token throughput | 861 tok/s |
| Total token throughput | 9689 tok/s |
| TTFT p50 / p95 | 1583 / 29246 ms |
| TPOT p50 / p95 | 342 / 430 ms |

## Notes

- This fix was validated alongside #37682 (MLA zero-init). Both are required for correct DeepSeek-V3.2-mxfp4 serving on ROCm.
- The `deepseek_v32` model type is used by the official HuggingFace checkpoint at `amd/DeepSeek-V3.2-mxfp4`.
- No changes to test files needed — existing Quark tests pass as-is since this only widens a model-type gate.

title: [ROCm] Cast score correction bias tensor during model construction for DeepSeek/Kimi-K2
body: ## Purpose The moe score correction bias tensor was being cast to the gate output dtype on every forward pass. The datatype that this tensor needs to be cast to is known at model construction time and never changes beyond that. So this repeated cast is redundant work that launches an extra GPU kernel per MoE layer per forward call. This PR moves the cast to the model construction thereby eliminating the per-forward-pass overhead. ## Summary ### Before ### After The trace shows the elementwise operation kernel responsible for this typecast operation happening before the grouped-topk operation in every forward pass. With the following changes this typecast is shifted to model construction thereby avoiding the call during every forward pass: - **`vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py`**: Pre-cast `e_score_correction_bias` to match `gate.out_dtype` during `DeepseekV2MoE` construction. Since all downstream consumers (FusedMoE, router) share the same `nn.Parameter` object, this single mutation propagates everywhere. - **`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/rocm_aiter_fused_moe.py`**: Replace the runtime `.to()` cast with an assert that the bias dtype already matches the gating output dtype, catching any future regression where the init-time cast is missed. - **`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/fused_topk_bias_router.py`**: Same change — replace the runtime `.to()` cast with a matching assert. ## Test Result ### Accuracy Benchmark | Metric | Score | Threshold | Status -- | -- | -- | -- | -- GSM8K (5-shot, 250 samples) | exact_match (flexible-extract) | 0.936 | 0.90 | ✅ PASS GSM8K (5-shot, 250 samples) | exact_match (strict-match) | 0.936 | 0.90 | ✅ PASS ### Performance | config | conc | Baseline | type-cast fix | Improvement | |--------|------|----------|---------------|-------------| | 1k1k | 4 | 190 | 194 | 1.021053 | | 1k1k | 8 | 321 | 323 | 1.006231 | | 1k1k | 16 | 521 | 528 | 1.013436 | | 1k1k | 32 | 783 | 799 | 1.020434 | | 1k1k | 64 | 1173 | 1180 | 1.005968 | | 1k8k | 4 | 108 | 110 | 1.018519 | | 1k8k | 8 | 188 | 191 | 1.015957 | | 1k8k | 16 | 307 | 309 | 1.006515 | | 1k8k | 32 | 485 | 491 | 1.012371 | | 1k8k | 64 | 730 | 734 | 1.005479 | | 8k1k | 4 | 799 | 816 | 1.021277 | | 8k1k | 8 | 1348 | 1365 | 1.012611 | | 8k1k | 16 | 2051 | 2064 | 1.006338 | | 8k1k | 32 | 2917 | 2949 | 1.01097 | | 8k1k | 64 | 4038 | 4012 | 0.993561 | | | | | **Geomean** | **1.011355**| ## Test Plan - [x] Accuracy test - [x] Performance benchmark

title: [ModelRunner V2] Speculative Decoding NGram GPU Implementations
body:
## Purpose


1. Added a new NGram GPU speculator.
The main feature is a new implementation at: `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/ngram/speculator.py`, similiar to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29184.

2. Updated request state storage for NGram GPU.
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/states.py`
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`
This changes how RequestState is initialized so that all_token_ids can stay densely resident on GPU instead of defaulting to UVA when ngram_gpu is active. As discussed in   #29184, the new n-gram speculator repeatedly scans active request token history, doing that from GPU-resident dense storage is much more appropriate than pulling through UVA-backed memory, this is a performance-oriented architectural change supporting the new feature.
The `model_runner.py` also injects req_states into speculators that need direct access to the persistent token store.

3. Added variable-length draft token plumbing
Several files were updated to support draft proposals where different requests may have different numbers of valid draft tokens:
`vllm/v1/outputs.py`
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/utils.py`
`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`
`vllm/v1/engine/core.py`
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`

DraftTokenIds now includes:
`num_valid_draft_tokens: list[int] | None`.
Scheduler logic now truncates speculative tokens based on `num_valid_draft_tokens`.
`EngineCore adds _maybe_update_async_draft_token_ids()` to consume draft metadata from async execution and update scheduler state at the right time.

title: [DSV4] Support `max` reasoning effort
body:
## Purpose

Extend Chat Completions `reasoning_effort` beyond the previous OpenAI-compatible `none` / `low` / `medium` / `high` set so documented model-specific values can be passed at the top level.

For example, DeepSeek V4 can now use top-level `reasoning_effort="max"` directly, instead of requiring users to pass it through `chat_template_kwargs.reasoning_effort`. The field description also calls out that `max` is specific to the DeepSeek V4 series and is not part of the standard OpenAI API specification.

DeepSeek V4 thinking mode follows the documented compatibility mapping and fallback behavior:

- `low`, `medium`, `minimal`, and other fallback values map to `high`
- `xhigh` maps to `max`
- `none` disables thinking

Harmony keeps its own local validation and reports a clear error for values unsupported by Harmony.

## Test Plan

- Add Chat Completions request tests for top-level model-specific `reasoning_effort` values and unknown-value rejection.
- Add a Harmony utility test for unsupported local reasoning effort values.
- Add DeepSeek V4 tokenizer tests for the compatible thinking-mode effort mapping, fallback behavior, and `none` disabling thinking.

title: [ROCm][perf] Use workspace manager for sparse indexer allocations
body:
## Purpose

Replace dynamic per-call allocations in the ROCm sparse attention indexer with workspace manager allocations.

The sparse attention indexer uses temporary buffers in both prefill and decode: `k_fp8` / `k_scale` in prefill and decode logits buffers in `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits`. These buffers are runtime scratch space, and their sizes vary with request shape, batch size, and speculative decoding state. They are a good fit for `WorkspaceManager`, which is already used elsewhere in vLLM to reserve and reuse bounded scratch buffers instead of relying on repeated hot-path PyTorch allocator calls.

This PR is primarily an allocator robustness and consistency change:

- It avoids repeated dynamic `torch.empty` / `torch.full` allocations in the ROCm sparse indexer hot path.
- It makes the ROCm sparse prefill behavior match the existing CUDA sparse indexer pattern, where temporary buffers are workspace-managed.
- It lets profiling reserve the required scratch size up front, so later execution reuses the profiled workspace instead of growing allocator state unexpectedly.

Earlier validation of the stale predecessor PR showed plain-image failures under sustained MTP load, including memory access faults and `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`. On the current nightly stack used for the tests, that exact MTP=2 failure no longer reproduces reliably in the plain image. Therefore this PR can not be said to fix MTP=2 crash that occured eariler. The argument for PR is that sparse-indexer scratch allocations should be workspace-managed on ROCm for the same reason they are workspace-managed elsewhere: bounded scratch reuse, less allocator churn, and lower risk of fragmentation or late hot-path allocation surprises.

This continues the work of stale PR #38704 by @gronsti-amd, rebased onto current `main`. AI assistance was used for this PR.

## Solution

- **Prefill path:** Replace per-chunk `torch.empty` allocations for `k_fp8` and `k_scale` with a single `workspace_manager.get_simultaneous()` allocation, slicing the workspace views per chunk.
- **Decode path:** Allocate the temporary decode logits buffer from `WorkspaceManager` and pass it to the existing AITER paged-MQA logits kernels.
- **Memory profiling path:** Reserve workspace for the prefill and decode buffer sizes in the real implementation's early-exit path, while keeping the fake implementation compatible with FakeTensor mode during `torch.compile`.

## Test Plan

**Environment:**

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-f6490a28413526adefae8dd7af32906d060e0436`
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2`
- Hardware: 8x MI355X, TP=8
- Attention backend: `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`

**Four experiments were run for validation:**

1. **No MTP (baseline):** Verifies the workspace manager changes do not regress the non-speculative decoding path.
2. **MTP=1 (1 speculative token):** Validates workspace-managed allocations under MTP with a single draft token.
3. **MTP=2 (2 speculative tokens):** Validates workspace-managed allocations under MTP with two draft tokens.
4. **MTP=3 (3 speculative tokens):** Validates workspace-managed allocations under MTP with three draft tokens.

**Server command:**

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --seed 4321 \
    --dtype auto \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \
    --max-num-seqs 256 \
    --max-model-len 16384 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --no-async-scheduling \
    --block-size 64 \
    --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE \
    --compilation-config '{"custom_ops": ["-rms_norm", "-silu_and_mul", "-quant_fp8"]}' \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": N}'
```

(The `--speculative-config` argument is omitted for the no-MTP baseline, and `N` is 1, 2, or 3 for the MTP experiments.)

**Benchmark command:**

```bash
vllm bench serve \
    --backend vllm \
    --dataset_name random \
    --ignore_eos \
    --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 \
    --ready_check_timeout_sec 3600 \
    --percentile_metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \
    --random_input_len 1024 \
    --random_output_len 8192 \
    --max_concurrency 128 \
    --temperature 0 \
    --seed 3 \
    --num_warmups 128 \
    --num_prompts 384 \
    --port 8000
```

## Test Results

title: [DSv4] Use `cvt` PTX for FP32->FP4 conversion

## Purpose

Currently FP4 quantization logic for `_fused_indexer_q_rope_mxfp4_kernel()` and `_fused_kv_compress_norm_rope_insert_indexer_mxfp4_attn()` does a linear search, which is inefficient, and more importantly, does not do round-to-nearest-even correctly. This PR switches to inline PTX `cvt.rn.satfinite.e2m1x2.f32` which is cleaner and should be faster too.

- Extend `test_fused_indexer_q_rope_quant_matches_unfused` to include FP4 version. Also provide a PyTorch-only FP4 quantization with correct round-to-nearest even (matches reference TileLang kernel [here](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro/blob/main/inference/kernel.py#L129))
- Test for `_fused_kv_compress_norm_rope_insert_indexer_mxfp4_attn()`
- ~~Sanity check by running vllm serve: the output looks a bit weird, but doesn't seem to be different from before this PR. Perhaps I should do an accuracy eval or something~~ GSM8K

title: [DSV4] Align aux stream API with DeepseekV4DecoderLayer
body:
## Summary
- PR #41061 changed `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` to take `aux_stream_list: list[torch.cuda.Stream]` (3 streams) and dropped the old `aux_stream_dict` path, but missed `DeepSeekV4MultiTokenPredictorLayer` in `deepseek_v4_mtp.py`, which still constructed an `aux_stream_dict` keyed by `AuxStreamType.Attention` and forwarded it as `aux_stream_dict=...`.
- Construct `aux_stream_list = [torch.cuda.Stream() for _ in range(3)]` in the MTP layer and pass it through, matching the new interface used in `deepseek_v4.py` and removing the now-unused `AuxStreamType` import.

## Test plan
- [x] DeepSeek V4 + MTP startup smoke test (model loads, no `TypeError` on `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.__init__`).
- [x] Spec-decoding correctness on DeepSeek V4 MTP (greedy + temperature).

AI assistance (Claude) was used for this change; the submitter has reviewed every line and is accountable for it. No existing open PR addresses this MTP-side interface mismatch (checked open PRs touching `deepseek_v4_mtp.py` / referencing #41061).

title: [Bugfix] Fix persistent_topk cooperative deadlock at TopK=1024
body:
## Purpose
Top issue: for topk=1024 and MTP=1, this kernel will deadline since there's no enough SMs to launch the grid and since each kernel is persistent, no kernel will finish. Hence the process will hang. 

Query occupancy for the actual <TopK, vec_size> instantiation being launched, reserve one CTA per SM as headroom for co-resident kernels on other streams, and TORCH_CHECK that total_ctas does not exceed the hardware-resident cap. Without this the cooperative spin-wait barrier deadlocks whenever any CTA in a group fails to be scheduled co-resident.

title: [DeepSeek] Use torch.mm for bf16xbf16->fp32 gemm
body:
It turns out that `torch.mm` natively supports bf16xbf16->fp32 gemm, so we don't need to wrap cublas ourselves. The following script confirms that `nvjet_sm100_tss_16x64_64x16_4x1_v_bz_TNN` is being launched under the hood.

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn


with torch.inference_mode():
    import torch.autograd.profiler as profiler

    x = torch.randn(8, 1024, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
    l = nn.Linear(1024, 2048, bias=False, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
    y = torch.mm(x, l.weight.T, out_dtype=torch.float32)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()

    with profiler.profile(use_cuda=True, use_kineto=True) as prof:
        y = torch.mm(x, l.weight.T, out_dtype=torch.float32)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()

    print(prof.key_averages().table(sort_by="cuda_time_total", row_limit=30))
```

title: [DSv4] Improved fused Indexer Q quant kernel
body:
## Purpose

Replace `_fused_indexer_q_rope_mxfp4_kernel` Triton kernel with a CuteDSL version to utilize 256-bit loads. Initially I wrote this in CUDA C++, but couldn't build vLLM from source, so asked Codex to port it over to CuteDSL. Hopefully this will be the first of many CuteDSL kernels to come in vLLM.

Update: I keep the original Triton implementation for fallback (potentially for ROCm). Also put CuteDSL kernel in a separate file and add import guards for platform doesn't have CuteDSL.

### Microbenchmarks

<details>
<summary>Benchmark script</summary>

```python
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
import torch

from vllm.v1.attention.ops.deepseek_v4_ops.fused_indexer_q import (
    fused_indexer_q_rope_quant,
)
from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti
import statistics

NUM_HEADS = 64
HEAD_DIM = 128
ROPE_DIM = 64
MAX_POS = 100_000
TOKENS = [1, 8, 32, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384]
ROPE_DTYPE = torch.float32


def make_inputs(num_tokens: int):
    positions = torch.randint(MAX_POS, (num_tokens,), dtype=torch.int64)
    query = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    cos_sin_cache = torch.randn(MAX_POS, ROPE_DIM, dtype=ROPE_DTYPE)
    weights = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    return (
        positions,
        query,
        cos_sin_cache,
        weights,
        HEAD_DIM**-0.5,
        NUM_HEADS**-0.5,
        True,
    )


def benchmark(num_tokens: int):
    torch.set_default_device("cuda")

    kernel_args = make_inputs(num_tokens)
    timings = bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(lambda: fused_indexer_q_rope_quant(*kernel_args))
    median_ms = statistics.median(timings)

    bytes_per_token = 8  # position int64
    bytes_per_token += NUM_HEADS * HEAD_DIM * 2  # q in bf16
    bytes_per_token += ROPE_DIM * torch.empty((), dtype=ROPE_DTYPE).element_size()
    bytes_per_token += NUM_HEADS * 2  # weights in bf16
    bytes_per_token += NUM_HEADS * HEAD_DIM // 2  # q out fp4
    bytes_per_token += NUM_HEADS * HEAD_DIM // 32  # q_scale uint8
    bytes_per_token += NUM_HEADS * 4  # weights out fp32
    total_bytes = bytes_per_token * num_tokens

    return median_ms, total_bytes


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for num_tokens in TOKENS:
        median_ms, moved_bytes = benchmark(num_tokens)
        bandwidth_gb_s = moved_bytes / (median_ms * 1e-3) * 1e-9
        print(
            f"T={num_tokens:6d}  "
            f"{median_ms * 1e3:7.2f} us  "
            f"BW {bandwidth_gb_s:7.1f} GB/s  "
        )
```

</details>

Result on GB200

Couldn't quite get to SOL yet (8TB/s), but still should be a good improvement for now.

title: [Bugfix] Fix persistent_topk inter-CTA init race on RadixRowState
body:
The `RadixRowState` per-group state (in `topk_workspace`) was initialized inside the kernel by CTA-0 only, with a plain global store followed by an intra-CTA `__syncthreads()`. CTA-1+ skipped the init entirely. There was no inter-CTA synchronization between CTA-0's init writes and CTA-1+'s first `red_release(&state->arrival_counter, 1)` in `radix_topk`, so two distinct races existed:

1) **Within a single launch.** CTA-1+'s atomicAdd could fire before
   CTA-0's plain ST of `arrival_counter = 0` reached L2. CTA-1+ would
   read whatever was in `arrival_counter` from the prior kernel call,
   add 1 atomically, then CTA-0's plain store would *overwrite* the
   incremented value with 0. The barrier counter would no longer reflect
   the true number of arrivals, so subsequent `wait_ge` calls could
   either return too early or hang. Empirically the chunk-load loop in
   Stage 1 of `radix_topk` (~10^4 cycles) gives CTA-0's init enough time
   to commit, masking the race in non-cooperative launches — but the
   bug is real on paper and would fire under tighter scheduling.

2) **Across launches.** `arrival_counter` is monotonically incremented
   throughout a launch and never reset. After a call, it ends at
   `total_phases * ctas_per_group`, a large positive value. The
   `topk_workspace` returned by the workspace manager is reused across
   calls without zero-init (`torch.empty`), so the *next* call's first
   `wait_ge(counter, ctas_per_group)` sees the stale large value and
   returns immediately on every CTA. Histograms have the same problem
   — they accumulate atomicAdds onto whatever the prior call left
   behind. This was the more impactful failure mode: every kernel
   invocation after the first one was effectively skipping the
   cooperative barrier and producing undefined results, hidden only
   because CTA-0's in-kernel init sometimes overwrote the stale state
   in time.

**Fix.** Replace the in-kernel init with a host-side `cudaMemsetAsync(workspace, 0, num_groups * sizeof(RadixRowState))` issued on the launch stream before the kernel runs. This:

- Provides a stream-ordered happens-before edge for *all* CTAs (memset completes before the kernel begins), removing the inter-CTA race without needing `st.release.gpu` + acquire-flag handshakes.
- Resets `arrival_counter` and `histogram` to zero between launches, fixing the cross-launch state leak.
- Removes the CTA-0-only init branch from the kernel entirely (`persistent_topk.cuh:894-909`), simplifying the prologue.

Cost: ~30 * 3088 = 92KB memset on the persistent path, dominated by the radix kernel itself (which spends most of its time in chunk loads and atomic histogram updates). Negligible.

This only affects the persistent-kernel path
(`num_rows <= 32` on devices with `max_smem >= 128KB`); the `FilteredTopK` paths are unchanged.

title: [ROCm][CI] Fix MLA prefill scale for DeepSeek GSM8K
body:
This restores the MLA prefill softmax scale used by DeepSeek-style models. The prefill backend refactor in `f3fef12350` (#32623) started constructing MLA prefill backends with `model_config.get_head_size() ** -0.5`. For DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite, that head size is the 576-dim latent KV cache, not the 192-dim query/key attention head. It also missed the DeepSeek YaRN mscale correction applied by the model attention module.

The fix derives prefill scale from `qk_nope_head_dim + qk_rope_head_dim`, applies the DeepSeek V2/V3 YaRN mscale correction, and leaves DeepSeek V4 unchanged because its attention path disables YaRN mscale.

cc @kenroche

title: [Test] Add DeepSeek MTP parallel-load tests
body:
## Purpose

`test_mtp_correctness[deepseek]` covers TP=1 only. This adds parallelism coverage for DeepSeek MTP weight loading and basic correctness: TP=2, EP=2, EP=2 + EPLB via the inline `LLM` constructor, plus DP=2 via `AsyncLLM` (mirrors `tests/v1/distributed/test_eagle_dp.py`). Each parametrize entry builds spec and no-spec engines at the same parallelism shape, runs greedy decode under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, and asserts output token ids match. The inline entries additionally check `vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts > 0` from `llm.get_metrics()` so a silently-broken drafter that falls back to verifier-only decoding does not pass trivially. PP=2 is statically skipped pending #38104.

Closes a gap that allowed #29545 (TP+EP load-time crash) to land without an upstream regression gate. Tracking: #36264.

## Test Plan

```
pytest -v -s tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_mtp_parallel_load.py
```

## Test Result

GB200 (SM100), torch 2.11.0+cu130:

```
test_deepseek_mtp_load_inline[tp2]      PASSED   493s
test_deepseek_mtp_load_inline[ep2]      PASSED
test_deepseek_mtp_load_inline[ep2_eplb] PASSED
test_deepseek_mtp_load_inline[pp2]      SKIPPED  (cites #38104)
test_deepseek_mtp_load_dp               PASSED    38s
```

Also ran a falsification check: dropped `speculative_config` from the spec run to simulate a silently-broken drafter; the metric guard correctly failed the test before the output-equality assertion could pass vacuously.

title: [ROCm][DeepSeek] Enable V3.2 TP4 AITER MLA
body:
## Purpose

This PR enables the remaining DeepSeek-V3.2 TP4-specific pieces needed for ROCm AITER MLA serving.

DeepSeek-V3.2 TP4 reaches local MLA `num_heads=32`. Current ROCm AITER MLA rejects that head count through `_AITER_UNSUPPORTED_HEADS = [32]`, so the model can fail before reaching the HIP graph accuracy path with `unsupported head_num: 32`. This PR removes that stale block now that the AITER-side MLA kernel support for this shape exists.

This PR also preserves DeepSeek's fp32 MoE correction bias when `GateLinear.out_dtype` is unset. The previous fallback cast `e_score_correction_bias` to the gate weight dtype, which can lose routing precision for DeepSeek's biased grouped top-k path and contribute to wrong expert routing or incoherent output.

This is the DeepSeek-specific split from Frida Andersson's original draft PR #41760. The shared ROCm AITER HIP graph replay fixes were split separately into #41816. This PR intentionally does not duplicate those graph replay changes. The full DeepSeek-V3.2 TP4 HIP-graphs fix is expected to require this PR plus #41816, along with an AITER build that includes `num_heads=32` MLA kernel support.

Special thanks to Frida for the original investigation, patch direction, and DeepSeek-V3.2 validation. This PR is a minimal split of her DeepSeek-specific work so it can be reviewed independently from the cross-model graph replay fix.

Co-authored-by: Frida Andersson <fanderss@amd.com>

## Test Plan

ROCm runtime validation still needed:

- Launch DeepSeek-V3.2 TP4 with ROCm AITER MLA enabled.
- Confirm the model no longer fails with `unsupported head_num: 32`.
- Confirm the runtime image includes AITER MLA kernel support for local `num_heads=32`.
- Validate with HIP graphs enabled using this PR plus #41816.
- Run GSM8K 5-shot or equivalent accuracy validation.
- Run serving benchmark before/after if reviewers want DS TP4 perf data.


Suggested validation matrix:

| Configuration | Expected result |
|---|---|
| Baseline `main` | DSv3.2 TP4 AITER MLA can fail with `unsupported head_num: 32`. |
| This PR only | `num_heads=32` is no longer blocked, but full HIP graph accuracy may still require #41816. |
| This PR + #41816 | DSv3.2 TP4 HIP-graphs path should launch and produce coherent output. |

## Test Result

Runtime result from Frida's original full draft fix stack in #41760 showed DeepSeek-V3.2 TP4 GSM8K 5-shot recovered to:

| Filter | Metric | Value | Stderr |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| flexible-extract | exact_match | 0.9318 | ± 0.0069 |
| strict-match | exact_match | 0.9113 | ± 0.0078 |

Those numbers were produced with the full #41760 fix stack before splitting. After the split, complete runtime validation should be rerun with this PR plus #41816 applied together.

title: [Bugfix] [ROCm] [DSV4] [Perf] Add aiter mhc support
body:
## Purpose

This PR integrates the aiter mhc kernel based on AITER `v0.1.13`, there are API changes in newer aiter versions. I will follow up with a new PR when we upgraded to new AITER version.

This PR also clean up the mhc kernels so that tilelang is lazily imported, avoid causing import error on platform that does not support tilelang.

IR Ops is not used because there seems to have some report regarding to some overhead with ir op abstraction. Kernel abstraction is also considered but since it does not manage weights nor require `preprocess_weight_after_loading` logic. So `CustomOp` is picked instead to capitalized on its hardware dispatching logic directly in the `layers/mhc.py` to avoid introducing complexity and inference overhead for now. 

This aiter mhc enablement PR is addressing the following issues

1. Main point: Optimize aiter mhc for ROCm.
    1. mhc-pre: `aiter`
    2. mhc-post `aiter`
    3. hc-head `ATOM`
2. [Critical] During integration it also bugfix the broken ROCm path caused by PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41536
3. During integration it also remove the dependency to tilelang on platform that doesn't support tilelang
    - `CustomOp` is used to capitalize on its hardware platform dispatching logic, `forward_cuda` and `forward_hip`.
    - `_tilelang_ops.py` is introduced so that we can lazily import the tilelang op in `mhc/kernels/tilelang.py` function preventing throwing import error on platform that does not support tilelang.
    - Separation of ops based on its implementation approach to keep the file clean. e.g. `mhc/kernels/tilelang.py`, `mhc/kernels/torch.py`, `mhc/kernels/triton.py`, `mhc/kernels/aiter.py`

title: [ROCm] Restore fast top_k_per_row kernels for sparse MLA when topk_tokens=2048
body:
### Summary
[#40871](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40871) replaced the C++ `top_k_per_row_decode` / `top_k_per_row_prefill` kernels with a generic `torch.topk`-based fallback (`_topk_indices_torch`) in `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer_native`, so that non-2048 `topk_tokens` values needed for DeepSeek-V4 would work. The fallback runs an unfused `torch.topk` + `torch.where` + dtype cast over a `[num_tokens, max_model_len]` logits tensor on **every prefill chunk and every decode step** — significantly slower than the specialized kernels.
On DeepSeek-V3.2 TP4 (MI355X) this regresses TPOT meaningfully (~26 ms vs ~18 ms in our internal benchmarks).
### Fix
DeepSeek-V3.2 uses `topk_tokens == 2048`, which is exactly the value the specialized C++ kernels were written for. Route `topk_tokens == 2048` back to `torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_prefill` / `torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode`, and keep `_topk_indices_torch` as the fallback for other `topk_tokens` values used by DeepSeek-V4.

### Updates
- Split fast-path dispatch into `_topk_indices_prefill` / `_topk_indices_decode` helpers (review feedback)
- Decode path now slices `topk_indices_buffer[:num_padded_tokens, :topk_tokens]` to match the kernel's row count when `requires_padding` is true (Gemini review)

### Test plan
- DeepSeek-V3.2 TP4 on MI355X — TPOT recovers to pre-#40871 levels
- GSM8K 5-shot flexible-extract score **0.9363**

title: [Bugfix] Fix DeepGEMM context lens contiguity in MLA indexer
body:
## Purpose

Fix an MLA indexer crash in the DeepGEMM metadata path:

```text
RuntimeError: Assertion error (/workspace/.deps/deepgemm-src/csrc/apis/attention.hpp:201): context_lens.is_contiguous()
```

This can happen in the native MTP/spec decode path when `max_decode_len < next_n`. The MLA indexer used to slice the 2D `decode_seq_lens_buffer` as `[:, :max_decode_len]`, which can produce a non-contiguous `seq_lens` view.

DeepGEMM requires contiguous `context_lens`, so this PR stores native MTP `seq_lens` in a preallocated flat buffer and reshapes it to the runtime `(B, max_decode_len)` shape before calling `get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata`.

title: [Bugfix] Fix DeepSeek v4 topk numerical issue for unaligned max-model-len
body:
## Purpose: It is observed that DeepSeek v4 has numerical issues when passing certain values of `--max-model-len` (e.g., 900000). For instance, the following figure shows the distribution of the number of completion tokens with 100 responses sampled for a selected question from GPQA. It can be seen that the number of generated tokens has a noticeable distribution shift when `--max-model-len 900000` is passed, compared to that not passed. Investigation shows that the root cause is that the indexer persistent topk kernel uses `const int64_t stride = logits.size(1);`. However, the logits produced from [deepgemm's](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/891d57b4db1071624b5c8fa0d1e51cb317fa709f/csrc/apis/attention.hpp#L361) `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` pads the `max_model_len` dimension to align with 256 and later slices the view to `max_model_len`. Thus, when `max_model_len` is not naturally aligned, the logits become incontiguous, thus the stride calculation is incorrect. This PR fixes this bug. To reproduce the experiment: ``` VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 \ vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --block-size 256 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \ --attention_config.use_fp4_indexer_cache True \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --max-cudagraph-capture-size 2048 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \ --max-model-len 900000 \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 ``` Set and unset `--max-model-len 900000` to see the difference. Prompt: ``` QUESTION = ( "You have prepared a di-substituted 6-membered aromatic ring compound " "containing 8 carbon atoms in total. title: [DSv4] Improved dequant gather K cache kernel
body:
## Purpose

When I did an nsys profile of DSv4 prefill, several memory-bound kernels show up as taking quite a bit of time. So I did microbenchmarks on some of them, finding out that `dequantize_and_gather_k_cache()` is currently having very low bandwidth utilization (it can only reach ~60GB/s for a single request). Hence, this PR introduces a CuteDSL version to improve it.

This kernel somewhat follows the Triton kernel design: launch `(num_requests, num_workers)`, where `num_workers` is a large number to have multiple CTAs working on a sequence. To keep things simple, 1 warp handles 1 token. The first 448 FP8 elems are dequantized, while the last 64 BF16 elems are copied as is. There is also multi-stage piplining with `cp.async` to slightly improve perf.

## Test Plan

### Microbenchmarks

<details>
<summary>Script</summary>

```python
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project

import statistics

import pandas as pd
import torch
from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti

from vllm.v1.attention.ops.deepseek_v4_ops import (
    dequantize_and_gather_k_cache,
    quantize_and_insert_k_cache,
)
from vllm.v1.attention.ops.deepseek_v4_ops.cache_utils import (
    dequantize_and_gather_k_cache_triton,
)

HEAD_DIM = 512
TOKEN_FP8_DIM = 448
TOKEN_BF16_DIM = 64
TOKEN_SCALE_DIM = 8
TOKEN_DATA_SIZE = TOKEN_FP8_DIM + TOKEN_BF16_DIM * 2
HEAD_BYTES = TOKEN_DATA_SIZE + TOKEN_SCALE_DIM
BLOCK_SIZE = 64
MAX_MODEL_LEN = 1048576
COMPRESS_RATIO = 4
COMPRESSED_OFFSET = 0
SWA_OFFSET = (MAX_MODEL_LEN + COMPRESS_RATIO - 1) // COMPRESS_RATIO
BYTES_PER_TOKEN = TOKEN_FP8_DIM + TOKEN_FP8_DIM // 64 + TOKEN_BF16_DIM * 2
BYTES_PER_TOKEN += HEAD_DIM * 2 + 4

COMPRESSED_FULL_SEQ_LENS = [
    1,
    8,
    32,
    128,
    512,
    2048,
    8192,
    16384,
    32000,
    MAX_MODEL_LEN // COMPRESS_RATIO,
]
SWA_CASES = [
    (8192, 128),
    (8192, 512),
    (8192, 1024),
    (16384, 128),
    (16384, 512),
    (16384, 1024),
    (MAX_MODEL_LEN, 1024),
]
BATCHED_FULL_CASE = [97, 1024, 8192, 16384]
BATCHED_SWA_CASE = ([97, 1024, 8192, 16384], [33, 128, 512, 1024])


def bench(
    label: str,
    seq_lens_list: list[int],
    gather_lens_list: list[int] | None,
    offset: int,
) -> dict[str, float | str]:
    blocks_per_req = [
        max(1, (seq_len + BLOCK_SIZE - 1) // BLOCK_SIZE) for seq_len in seq_lens_list
    ]
    block_offsets = [0]
    for num_blocks in blocks_per_req[:-1]:
        block_offsets.append(block_offsets[-1] + num_blocks)

    total_blocks = sum(blocks_per_req)
    max_blocks_per_req = max(blocks_per_req)
    physical_blocks = torch.randperm(total_blocks, dtype=torch.int32)

    compressed_kv = torch.randn(sum(seq_lens_list), HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    slot_mapping = torch.cat(
        [
            (
                physical_blocks[block_offset + torch.arange(seq_len) // BLOCK_SIZE]
                * BLOCK_SIZE
                + torch.arange(seq_len) % BLOCK_SIZE
            ).to(torch.int64)
            for seq_len, block_offset in zip(seq_lens_list, block_offsets)
        ],
        dim=0,
    )

    k_cache = torch.empty(total_blocks, BLOCK_SIZE, HEAD_BYTES, dtype=torch.uint8)
    quantize_and_insert_k_cache(
        compressed_kv,
        k_cache.view(total_blocks, -1),
        slot_mapping,
        block_size=BLOCK_SIZE,
    )
    torch.cuda.synchronize()

    block_table = torch.full(
        (len(seq_lens_list), max_blocks_per_req), -1, dtype=torch.int32
    )
    for req_id, (block_offset, num_blocks) in enumerate(
        zip(block_offsets, blocks_per_req)
    ):
        block_table[req_id, :num_blocks] = physical_blocks[
            block_offset : block_offset + num_blocks
        ]

    valid_lens = seq_lens_list if gather_lens_list is None else gather_lens_list
    out_len = offset + max(valid_lens)
    out = torch.empty(
        len(seq_lens_list),
        out_len,
        HEAD_DIM,
        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    )
    seq_lens = torch.tensor(seq_lens_list, dtype=torch.int32)
    gather_lens = (
        None
        if gather_lens_list is None
        else torch.tensor(gather_lens_list, dtype=torch.int32)
    )

    ref_out = torch.empty_like(out)
    dequantize_and_gather_k_cache_triton(
        ref_out, k_cache, seq_lens, gather_lens, block_table, BLOCK_SIZE, offset
    )
    dequantize_and_gather_k_cache(
        out, k_cache, seq_lens, gather_lens, block_table, BLOCK_SIZE, offset
    )
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    for req_id, length in enumerate(valid_lens):
        torch.testing.assert_close(
            out[req_id, offset : offset + length],
            ref_out[req_id, offset : offset + length],
            rtol=0,
            atol=0,
        )

    torch.cuda.synchronize()

    cutedsl_ms = statistics.median(bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(
        lambda: dequantize_and_gather_k_cache(
            out, k_cache, seq_lens, gather_lens, block_table, BLOCK_SIZE, offset
        )
    ))
    triton_ms = statistics.median(bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(
        lambda: dequantize_and_gather_k_cache_triton(
            ref_out, k_cache, seq_lens, gather_lens, block_table, BLOCK_SIZE, offset
        )
    ))
    moved_bytes = sum(valid_lens)
    moved_bytes *= BYTES_PER_TOKEN
    cutedsl_gbps = moved_bytes / (cutedsl_ms * 1e-3) * 1e-9
    triton_gbps = moved_bytes / (triton_ms * 1e-3) * 1e-9
    return {
        "case": label,
        "triton_us": triton_ms * 1e3,
        "cutedsl_us": cutedsl_ms * 1e3,
        "triton_GB/s": triton_gbps,
        "cutedsl_GB/s": cutedsl_gbps,
        "speedup": triton_ms / cutedsl_ms,
    }


def main() -> None:
    torch.set_default_device("cuda")

    print(f"\ncompressed full gather (offset={COMPRESSED_OFFSET})")
    full_rows = [
        bench(str(seq_len), [seq_len], None, COMPRESSED_OFFSET)
        for seq_len in COMPRESSED_FULL_SEQ_LENS
    ]
    full_rows.append(bench("batched", BATCHED_FULL_CASE, None, COMPRESSED_OFFSET))
    print(
        pd.DataFrame(full_rows)
        .rename(columns={"case": "k_len"})
        .to_markdown(index=False, floatfmt=".2f")
    )

    print(f"\nuncompressed swa tail (offset={SWA_OFFSET})")
    swa_rows = [
        bench(f"{seq_len}/{gather_len}", [seq_len], [gather_len], SWA_OFFSET)
        for seq_len, gather_len in SWA_CASES
    ]
    swa_rows.append(bench("batched", *BATCHED_SWA_CASE, SWA_OFFSET))
    print(
        pd.DataFrame(swa_rows)
        .rename(columns={"case": "seq/gather"})
        .to_markdown(index=False, floatfmt=".2f")
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

title: [Core][DSV4] Skip caching SWA blocks that can never serve a prefix-cache hit
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4 pairs full-attention layers with SWA layers with different block sizes and window sizes. The full attn layers have block size of 256, while SWA layers and compressors have block sizes of 64, 4, or 8.

- Within each 256-aligned segment, only the trailing `tail = ceil((sliding_window - 1) / block_size)` blocks are reachable by SWA's right-to-left scan.
- Hash-blocks past the last 256-aligned boundary are unreachable because hits are always lcm-aligned.

This PR drops the unreachable blocks at cache-time via a new `alignment_tokens` kwarg threaded through `cache_blocks` -> `SlidingWindowManager._cache_block_mask` -> `BlockPool.cache_full_blocks`. Non-hybrid coordinators pass `alignment_tokens=None` and hit a fast path identical to the existing behavior.

## Test Plan

New tests in `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py`:

- `test_hybrid_cache_blocks_swa_tail_window_only` — full-attn `block_size=32`, SWA `block_size=8`, `sliding_window=8` (`lcm=32`, `tail=1`, `per_segment=4`). After caching 8 SWA hash-blocks, asserts only hashes 3 and 7 are in the prefix-cache hash map; 0–2 and 4–6 are not.
- `test_hybrid_cache_blocks_clamped_to_lcm` — full-attn `block_size=32`, SWA `block_size=16`, `sliding_window=32`. After caching 7 SWA hash-blocks (112 tokens), asserts hashes 0–5 are cached and hash 6 (past the last lcm boundary) is not.

## Test Result

Passed. Claude is used to generate test cases but I have reviewed them.

Fix the DeepSeek V4 MTP path after #41536 changed `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.forward` to take `post_mix`, `res_mix`, and `residual`. The main model path was updated, but the MTP draft layer still used the old call and failed at startup/profile run. Key error lines:

```text
torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: failed to bind arguments when attempting to inline

```

title: [Model Runner V2][Bug Fix][DSV4] Ensure lazy attention state initializations happen during cudagraph capture
body:
# Context
DeepSeek V4 Flash with full CUDA graph capture in Model Runner V2 produces corrupted output (gibberish or repetition loops). The root cause is that `CudaGraphManager.capture()` runs a warmup forward pass before the actual graph capture, and both passes share the same `FlashMLASchedMeta `objects.

FlashMLA's C++ decode kernel (`sparse_decode_fwd` / `dense_decode_fwd`) has a conditional initialization path: if `tile_scheduler_metadata` is `None`, it allocates the tensor and runs `run_get_decoding_sched_meta_kernel` to compute a work-partitioning plan across SMs based on the current `topk_length` values. If `tile_scheduler_metadata` is already populated, it skips planning and reuses the existing plan.

During MRV2's capture flow:
1. Warmup (eager, not recorded) -`FlashMLASchedMeta` starts with `tile_scheduler_metadata=None`. The C++ kernel allocates the tensor and runs the planning kernel with dummy `topk_length` values. The metadata is now populated.
2. Capture (inside `torch.cuda.graph()`) - The same FlashMLASchedMeta objects are reused. The C++ kernel sees the already-populated metadata, takes the reuse branch, and skips the planning kernel. Only the attention and combine kernels are recorded into the graph.
3. Replay - The planning kernel never re-executes. The attention kernels run with a stale plan derived from dummy warmup values, producing incorrect work partitioning and corrupted output.

MRV1 is unaffected because `CUDAGraphWrapper` goes directly into capture with no warmup. The planning kernel sees `tile_scheduler_metadata=None` during capture, so it gets recorded into the graph and re-executes on every replay with current `topk_length` values read from persistent buffers updated before each replay.

# Fix
Call `create_forward_fn` separately for warmup and capture. The warmup uses a throwaway `forward_fn` and `attn_state`, and the capture gets a fresh `attn_state` with fresh `FlashMLASchedMeta` objects (`tile_scheduler_metadata=None`). This ensures the C++ kernel takes the allocation+planning path during capture, so r`un_get_decoding_sched_meta_kernel` is recorded into the graph and re-executes on every replay with current inputs.

While specifically intended to fix the issue for DSV4, it protects any attention backend that performs lazy initialization gated behind a first-call check.

title: [Bugfix] [ROCm] [DSV4] Fix AITER MXFP4 MoE weight loading and shuffle…
body:
… for FlyDSL kernels

## Purpose

Fix three bugs in the AITER MXFP4 MoE integration path that caused garbled output when using `--moe-backend aiter` with DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm (gfx950).

**Bug 1 — TP weight loading offset with padded dimensions:**
`_load_w13` / `_load_w2` used the padded `shard_size` (512, rounded up from 384 by `mxfp4_round_up_hidden_size_and_intermediate_size`) to compute checkpoint offsets. With TP=8, ranks 6 and 7 computed `start_offset = 512 * 6 = 3072` which equals or exceeds the checkpoint's 3072 rows, so those ranks loaded zero weights. Fix: derive `loaded_per_rank` from the actual checkpoint dimension divided by `tp_size`.

**Bug 2 — Incorrect de-interleave in `convert_weight_to_mxfp4_moe_kernel_format`:**
The AITER branch applied a `view(e, n//2, 2, k).permute(0,2,1,3)` de-interleave assuming the input w13 was stored as interleaved `[g0, u0, g1, u1, ...]` (as in the GPT-OSS checkpoint format). However, the standard `_load_w13` path loads w1 and w3 separately into `[gate_all, up_all]` layout. Applying de-interleave on already-separated data garbled the rows. Fix: remove the de-interleave step for the standard checkpoint path.

**Bug 3 — Wrong shuffle functions for FlyDSL kernels:**
vLLM used `shuffle_weight_a16w4` for both w13 and w2, but the AITER FlyDSL kernels expect different shuffle functions per stage:
- Stage 1 (w13, gate+up): `shuffle_weight(w, (16, 16))` + `e8m0_shuffle` for scales
- Stage 2 (w2, down-proj): `shuffle_weight_a16w4(w, 16, False)` + `shuffle_scale_a16w4` for scales

This matches the pattern in `aiter/ops/flydsl/test_flydsl_moe_a4w4.py` which passes all correctness tests. Fix: use the correct aiter-native shuffle function combination.

## Test Plan

Run lm-eval GSM8K and `vllm bench serve` on DeepSeek-V4-Pro on MI355X with TP=8.

Baseline commit: `bf0d2dc6d7` (`vllm-project/vllm` main, 2026-05-14)

### Server command (baseline — `triton_unfused`):

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR=1
export VLLM_DSV4_ROCM_GRAPH_SAFE=1

MODEL=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
vllm serve ${MODEL} \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001 --dtype auto \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --max-num-seqs 128 \
    --distributed-executor-backend mp \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 \
    --moe-backend triton_unfused \
    --enforce-eager \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --async-scheduling \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4
```

### Server command (after — FlyDSL MoE via `aiter`):

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR=1
export VLLM_DSV4_ROCM_GRAPH_SAFE=1
export AITER_CONFIG_FMOE=/path/to/dsv4_fp4_tuned_fmoe.csv

MODEL=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
vllm serve ${MODEL} \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001 --dtype auto \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --max-num-seqs 128 \
    --distributed-executor-backend mp \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 \
    --moe-backend aiter \
    --enforce-eager \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --async-scheduling \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4
```

### lm-eval command:

```bash
MODEL=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
lm_eval --model local-completions \
    --model_args model=${MODEL},base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8001/v1/completions,num_concurrent=8,max_retries=10,max_gen_toks=2048,timeout=60000 \
    --batch_size auto \
    --tasks gsm8k \
    --num_fewshot 8 \
    --output_path .
```

### Benchmark command:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
    --base-url http://localhost:8001 \
    --model ${MODEL} --tokenizer ${MODEL} \
    --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len 1000 --random-output-len 100 \
    --num-prompts 20 --max-concurrency 10 \
    --num-warmups 1 --seed 0
```

title: DeepSeekV4-Pro enable cuda graph full and piecewise mode
body:
## Purpose Enable "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE" cuda graph mode on Deepseekv4 pro ## Test Plan env ``` vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly ( a0e392a1cdeb ) ``` server.sh ``` export HF_HOME=/data/huggingface-cache export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR=1 export HSA_TOOLS_DISABLE_REGISTER=1 export VLLM_DSV4_ROCM_GRAPH_SAFE=1 vllm serve /dev/shm/models/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --host localhost \ --port 8001 \ --dtype auto \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --max-num-seqs 128 \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --trust-remote-code \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 \ --moe-backend triton_unfused \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' ``` client.sh ``` PORT=${PORT:-8001} MODEL=${MODEL:-/dev/shm/models/DeepSeek-V4-Pro} NUM_PROMPTS=${NUM_PROMPTS:-20} CONCURRENCY=${CONCURRENCY:-10} INPUT_LEN=${INPUT_LEN:-1000} OUTPUT_LEN=${OUTPUT_LEN:-100} vllm bench serve \ --base-url "http://localhost:${PORT}" \ --model "${MODEL}" --tokenizer "${MODEL}" \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len "${INPUT_LEN}" \ --random-output-len "${OUTPUT_LEN}" \ --num-prompts "${NUM_PROMPTS}" --max-concurrency "${CONCURRENCY}" \ --num-warmups 1 \ --save-result \ --seed 0 ``` accuracy.sh ``` MODEL=/dev/shm/models/DeepSeek-V4-Pro lm_eval --model local-completions --model_args model=$MODEL,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8001/v1/completions,tokenizer_backend=None,tokenized_requests=False,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=10,max_gen_toks=2048,timeout=60000 --batch_size auto --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 8 --output_path . 2>&1 | tee -a eval.log ``` ## Test Result I think the next accuracy-related changes should focus on DeepSeek-V4 FP8/FNUZ handling, especially: - `vllm/v1/attention/ops/deepseek_v4_ops/fused_indexer_q.py` - `vllm/v1/attention/ops/deepseek_v4_ops/fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py` These paths currently hardcode NVIDIA-style FP8 behavior (`torch.float8_e4m3fn` / `tl.float8e4nv`). On ROCm, they should use the platform FP8 dtype (`current_platform.fp8_dtype()`) and emit `tl.float8e4b8` for FNUZ. If accuracy is still low after that, I would next look at UE8M0 scale handling in: - `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py` - `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py` ---

title: [Model][Hardware][AMD][Kernel] Part 2/2 -> Enable e2e QK Norm + RoPE + KV Cache runtime fusion for Qwen3-30B-A3B on ROCM_ATTN
body: ## Purpose **Depends on #42749** (Part 1). Please review #42749 first. This PR currently shows Part 1's diff as well because Part 1 hasn't merged yet. Once #42749 merges, I'll rebase this branch onto `main` and force-push, and the diff will reduce to just the 2 incremental commits in this PR. This is **Part 2** of a stacked PR series that splits the original `jhu96/optimize-qwen30b` branch (PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39527) into two reviewable PRs. - Enable e2e runtime QK Norm + RoPE + KV Cache fusion for Qwen3-30B. At compile time, we swap the aforementioned fusion pattern & fuse with aiter's high-performance HIP kernel `fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_pts_quant_shuffle ` for all decoder layers that satisfy a preset token compile range guarded by `rope_kvcache_fusion_max_token_num`. - For ROCM_ATTN, modifications were needed on both the prefill and decode path kernels (prefill Triton, decode Triton 2D for non-power-of-2 block sizes, and decode paged attention ll4 GFX9 variants) so that they can read the value cache in the interleaved mode, which the fused kernel writes in when shuffle=True. The key cache read logic remains untouched, as the fused kernel already writes in the format expected by the prefill and decode paths. - When shuffle=True, the fused kernel writes K with shape (blocks, heads, dim/x, block_size, x) and V with shape (blocks, heads, block_size/x, dim, x). Decode paths already natively read K in the same format, but they currently hardcode reading from the V cache with an expected shape of (blocks, heads, dims, block_size). ## Test Plan To test this fusion out, please pass the attached toggle through the pass config under the `--compilation-config` when launching with `vllm serve`: `'pass_config': { 'fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache': True, 'rope_kvcache_fusion_max_token_num': 256 }` For example, something like this: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \ vllm serve /path-to-your/Qwen3-30B-A3B \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8080 \ --attention-backend ROCM_ATTN \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ -O1 \ --compilation-config '{ "pass_config": { "fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache": true, "rope_kvcache_fusion_max_token_num": 256 } }` In addition, one can verify the unit test for this fusion with: ` pytest tests/compile/passes/test_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py -v` ` ## Test Result ## Recent Sweep Most recent sweep using this fusion for 3 models: ISL=1024, OSL=1024 (balanced config) Accuracy: 1) Hy3 (TP=8) 2) GLM4.7 (TP=8) 3) Qwen3-30B-A3B (TP=1)

title: [MM][CG] Enable encoder CUDA Graph for MiniCPM-V
body:
## Purpose
Add encoder CUDA Graph support for MiniCPM-V 2.5, 2.6, 4.0  as part of tracker #38175. This implementation follows the existing workflow introduced in #38061. 

The captured graph covers both the ViT encoder (VPM) and the resampler.

MiniCPM-V 2.0 is not included, as it predates the slice-based vision architecture required by this implementation.
MiniCPM‑V 4.5 is not included, as its dynamic frame fusion introduces input-dependent encoder shapes that are not compatible with the current static-shape CUDA Graph capture mechanism. It continues to use the eager path and does not benefit from encoder CUDA Graph replay, which may reduce performance.

## Key Updates
This PR extends the multimodal encoder CUDA Graph cache to key captured graphs by` (token_budget, secondary_capture_axis_key)` instead of `token_budget` alone.

`token_budget` continues to determine greedy packing and output buffer sizing for resampler tokens. However, for vision encoders such as those in OpenBMB's MiniCPM-V models, the encoder capture shape also depends on discrete patch-grid / pixel-layout tiers. As a result, different input shapes can share the same token budget while requiring distinct CUDA Graph captures.

Without this secondary capture axis, inputs with the same token budget are forced into a single capture shape, which can introduce unnecessary padding and reduce the efficiency benefits of CUDA Graphs. By including `secondary_capture_axis_key `in the cache key, the encoder can maintain separate captures for shape-dependent tiers while preserving the existing token-budget-based scheduling and memory allocation logic.


## Test Plan
**Unit test**
```bash
pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -v
```

```bash
  --served-model-name MiniCPM-V-4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video": 1, "image": 1}'
```

```bash
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video": 1, "image": 1}' \
  --compilation-config '{
    "cudagraph_mm_encoder": true,

    "encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch": 32
  }'
```

title: [ROCm] [Bugfix] Fix DeepSeek V4 Functionality and Accuracy
body:
## Purpose

This PR addresses the following issues

1. Functionality broken after this PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41263 (fixed by removing `x = self.ffn_norm(x)`)
2. Fix the DeepSeek V4 accuracy degradation at high concurrency.

I have added self-review comments to explain the changes.

### Point 2
It is a compounded issue.
1. AITER MHC has accuracy issue when number of tokens is large. New AITER version is coming soon, so the code path is kept documented so that we can easily reenable it in vLLM once we upgrade the AITER version. For now we are falling back to torch implementation.
2. The prefill mqa topk buffer is corrupted by incorrect logic. It is fixed by calling the `torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_prefill` .


Other changes are code cleaning and also invoking faster kernels e.g. replace `_topk_indices_torch` with `torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode` . 

## Test Plan

lmeval score of `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro` and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`

```
    --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
| tee deepseekv4_graph_mhctriton_block256_topkindicesvllmop_syncmain.log
```

title: [KVConnector][DSV4] HMA support for Mooncake store connector
body:
## Purpose

Add hybrid KV cache manager support to `MooncakeStoreConnector`, so models with mixed attention layouts (e.g. full + sliding-window, DSV4) can use Mooncake Store as a shared external KV pool.

- Declare `SupportsHMA` on the connector and validate the `KVCacheConfig` up front (reject `CrossAttentionSpec`, non-`align` Mamba, and multi-group + PCP/DCP > 1 combinations).
- New `MooncakeStoreCoordinator` mirrors `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit` over an external `(group_id, hash)` existence set, so cache-hit length on the scheduler side matches what the in-GPU hybrid coordinator would compute.
- Thread `kv_cache_config` through scheduler and worker; per-group store/load masks replace the prior single-group assumptions in `data.py` / `worker.py` / `scheduler.py`.

title: [ROCm][MLA] Replace torch.cat in sparse-MLA forward_mqa with fused concat_mla_q
body:
## Summary

In the ROCm sparse-MLA backend, `forward_mqa` builds `q = torch.cat([ql_nope, q_pe], dim=-1)` once per layer per forward pass. On DeepSeek-V3.2 (61 sparse-MLA layers on the decode path) this adds up to **61 fresh tensor allocations and 61 `aten::CatArrayBatchedCopy` kernel launches per decode step**, ≈ 360 µs at MC=4 (≈ 4% of a decode step measured at TP=4, ISL=1000, OSL=100 on MI355X).

The fused `ops.concat_mla_q(ql_nope, q_pe, q_out)` already exists in `vllm/_custom_ops.py` and is already used by `FlashMLASparseImpl.forward_mqa` at `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py:1028`. This PR plugs it into `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` against a preallocated workspace buffer sized `(max_num_batched_tokens, num_heads, head_size)`, so:

- No per-layer allocation on the decode hot path.
- Output address is stable across CUDA graph capture/replay (same pattern `FlashMLASparseImpl` uses today).
- One fused kernel instead of one ATen cat.

The patch is numerically identical to the `torch.cat` it replaces (no change in GSM8K, see below).

The workspace buffer is allocated using `vllm_config.model_config.dtype` so both bf16 and fp16 paths advertised by `ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend.supported_dtypes` get matching-dtype storage (per @gemini-code-assist review).

## Performance

Setup: DeepSeek-V3.2 (sparse-FP8) on 4× MI355X, TP=4, MC=4, ISL=1000, OSL=100, 32 prompts per run, 4 runs per build (seeds 42/42/7/13), deterministic integer-prompt feed.

Build matrix (everything is the published nightly image except the file in this PR):

- **Baseline**: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-32b7177909d1c9928bcedd81de7de5a1fa21d2b3` (upstream `0.21.1rc1.dev28+g32b717790`, file `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` matches `main` at the time of writing).
- **main + this PR**: same image, with this PR's `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` bind-mounted on top.

Both builds run with the AITER `module_custom_all_reduce.so` from the upcoming AITER v0.14 (pinned to ROCm/aiter@`c71075ced`, "Fix 2-stage fused_allreduce_rmsnorm memory ordering", #2890) bind-mounted on top of the image's AITER 0.13. This is unrelated to the change in this PR — it is needed to keep the GSM8K accuracy comparison meaningful and is symmetric across baseline and patched (so it cannot account for the delta below).

| Build | Mean TPOT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | P99 TPOT (ms) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline (n=4) | 17.54 | 17.08 | 21.45 | 183.5 |
| **main + this PR** (n=4) | **17.09** | **16.92** | **18.57** | **194.1** |
| delta | **-0.46 ms (-2.6%)** | **-0.16 ms (-0.9%)** | **-2.88 ms (-13.4%)** | **+5.8%** |

Run-to-run noise on a single node is ≈ ±0.4 ms mean TPOT; the patched run is below the baseline range for every seed. The P99 improvement is the strongest signal — eliminating the per-layer ATen allocation removes a recurring tail-latency contributor.

Server:

```
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 4096 --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

Bench:

```
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1000 --random-output-len 100 \
  --random-prompt-as-token-ids \
  --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 4 \
  --ignore-eos --seed {42,7,13}
```

## Accuracy

GSM8K, n=200, num_fewshot=5, `--gen_kwargs temperature=0,seed=42` (greedy), evaluated against the raw `/v1/completions` endpoint (matches `.buildkite/lm-eval-harness/run-lm-eval-gsm-vllm-baseline.sh`), `transformers==4.57.1`.

| Build | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 0.945 ± 0.016 | 0.945 ± 0.016 |
| main + this PR | 0.945 ± 0.016 | 0.945 ± 0.016 |

Identical accuracy; expected, since the patch is numerically identical to the existing `torch.cat`.

## Single-prompt sanity (patched server, greedy)

Spot-checks against `/v1/chat/completions` with `temperature=0`:

| Prompt | Output |
|---|---|
| `What is 17 times 23? Return only the integer.` | `\( 17 \times 23 = 391 \)` |
| `What is the capital of France? Answer with the city name only.` | `Paris` |
| `What is the largest planet in our solar system? Reply with one word.` | `Jupiter` |
| `A train leaves at 3:00 PM and arrives 2.5 hours later. What time does it arrive in HH:MM 24-hour format? Reply with just HH:MM.` | `17:30` |

All four expected answers; no spurious continuations, no language drift.

## Static checks

- `python tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 1 "3.10"` — clean
- mypy for Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 (full CI matrix) — clean
- `ruff check vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` — All checks passed
- `ruff format --check vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` — already formatted

## Cross-reference

Mirrors the workspace-buffer + `ops.concat_mla_q` pattern that `FlashMLASparseImpl.forward_mqa` already uses at `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py:1028`.

title: [Bugfix] Fix DSV4 Base model swiglu limit issue in FP8 path
body:
DeepSeek V4 Pro Base FP8 routed MoE needs the model-provided SwiGLU clamp limit to be applied before the second expert GEMM. Without this clamp, DSV4 Pro Base produces garbled outputs and very low eval quality.

This PR patches FP8 MoE backends ('auto' and 'triton') as the Base model's moe experts are FP8.

After this PR, we saw mmlu pro bench has macro 0.7409 / micro 0.7298, which matches model card.

Related PR for instr model's FP4 path (#42287, #42541)
