title: [Perf] Use native DSA indexer decode path for next_n > 2 on SM100
body: ## Purpose On SM100, the DeepGEMM paged MQA logits kernels support any `next_n` natively (multi-atom decomposition, FP8 and FP4 indexer caches), so the FP4 indexer cache no longer needs the flattening fallback for `next_n > 2` — flattening is kept only outside the SM100 family, where the FP8 kernel requires `next_n ∈ (1, 2)` (deepgemm `smxx_fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits.hpp:233`). Implements the in-tree `TODO (matt): integrate kernel with next_n = 4 support`. Behavior matrix ("native" = kernel sees the real batch `(B, next_n)` with 2D per-token context lens; "flatten" = requests expanded into `B × next_n` single-token pseudo-requests): | Platform | Indexer cache | `next_n` (= spec tokens + 1) | Before | After | Changed? | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | SM100 (B200/GB200) | FP8 | 1 (no spec decode) | native | native | — | | SM100 | FP8 | 2 (MTP, 1 draft) | native | native | — | | SM100 | FP8 | > 2 (MTP, ≥ 2 drafts) | native | native | — | | SM100 | FP4 | 1 | native | native | — | | SM100 | FP4 | 2 | native | native | — | | **SM100** | **FP4** | **> 2** | **flatten** | **native** | ✅ **this PR** | | non-SM100 (SM90, SM12x, …) | FP8 | 1 | native | native | — | | non-SM100 | FP8 | 2 | native | native | — | | non-SM100 | FP8 | > 2 | flatten | flatten | — | | non-SM100 | FP4 | any | rejected at startup (assert) | rejected at startup (assert) | — | Exactly one cell changes: for `next_n ∈ {1, 2}` both gate expressions evaluate to `False` everywhere, and the `use_fp4_indexer_cache` term was redundant off-SM100 because the FP4 cache is rejected there by the assert directly above the gate. ## Test Plan & Result - Verified via torch profile that next_n > 2 is natively supported by the kernel: - Ran speed-bench on DeepSeek V4 Flash with MTP=3 before and after this change with 1 GB200 node. title: [ROCm][DSv4] Functional fixes for DeepSeek V4 on MI300X/MI325X
body:
## Purpose

This PR fixes DeepSeek V4 / DeepSeek V4 Flash functional issues on ROCm gfx942 (MI300X), while preserving the gfx950 path.

The main fixes are:

- Avoid unsupported FP8 arithmetic when converting UE8M0 block scales.
- Make the fused DeepSeek V4 qnorm/RoPE/KV-insert path emit the correct FP8 bytes on ROCm:
  - gfx942 uses FNUZ encoding.
  - gfx950 uses OCP encoding.
  - FNUZ uses max value `224.0`.
- Propagate the FNUZ/OCP choice through DeepSeek V4 cache utility helpers and sparse MLA decode paths.
- Keep the sparse decode cache formats explicit: the main/SWA cache follows the platform FP8 encoding, while the compressed extra cache remains OCP.
- Provide the gfx942 Triton fallback for `fp8_mqa_logits` so the DSv4 ROCm path does not depend on an immediate aiter update for that kernel.
- Fix the fused-kernel test references:
  - allow a narrow 1 bf16 ULP tolerance for the RoPE region, where the GPU kernel and PyTorch reference can round opposite ways at ties;
  - use the correct ROCm FP8 store dtype in full-cache per-tensor FP8 reference checks, so gfx942 FNUZ bytes are decoded under the same encoding used by the kernel.

Continues #42893. AI assistance was used for this PR.

Co-authored-by: maeehart, [markus.hartikainen@amd.com](mailto:markus.hartikainen@amd.com)
Co-authored-by: ganyi, [ygan@amd.com](mailto:ygan@amd.com)
Co-authored-by: Jin Tao, [jintao12@amd.com](mailto:jintao12@amd.com)

## Test Plan

```text

- Run a prompt sanity check against the OpenAI-compatible completions endpoint.
- Run full GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 questions, local completions, concurrency 128.
- Run `vllm bench serve` with random 8192 input / 1024 output, `--ignore-eos`, and max concurrency `1,2,4,8,16,32`.

Serve command:

```bash

vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \

  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --disable-log-stats
```

GSM8K lm_eval command:

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=128,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=none,max_length=32768 \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --batch_size 128
```

Bench command:

```bash
for C in 1 2 4 8 16 32; do
  vllm bench serve \
    --backend vllm \
    --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
    --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \

```

title: [M3] Tune Triton indexer score decode for spec-decode
body:
## Purpose

Reland of #45665 after M3 is merged


Currently, to support spec-decode case, we simply launch extra CTAs for each decode token. This is simple, because the kernel remains mostly unchanged. However, it is not good because we could have batched multiple Query tokens together for QK MMA to improve efficiency. This PR does exactly just that.
- Before: launch 1 CTA per **token** across all heads. Each CTA loads `num_idx_heads` Query tokens. For TP=4, this is just 1 token
- After: launch 1 CTA per **request** across all heads. Each CTA loads `decode_query_len x num_idx_heads` Query tokens. For TP=4 and spec-decode=3, this is 4 tokens. Crucially, when there is no spec-decode, this kernel should behave exactly like the old kernel.

Other design considerations:
- In spec-decode, the max number of decode tokens per request is `1 + num_spec_tokens`. But the scheduler can pass fewer tokens too. To avoid recompilation, we use an extra metadata `max_decode_query_len`, which stays constant throughout the lifetime of a vLLM worker, as the constexpr for the kernel.
- To keep the kernel simple, we don't introduce extra tiling over `num_idx_heads` nor `decode_query_len`. This is because at the worst case, TP=1 and 3 spec-tokens, we only have `num_idx_heads x decode_query_len = 16` Query tokens. This is still a small number that the kernel works just fine. I did some extra `num_warps` and `num_stages` tuning for this case though.
- Also reduce `TARGET_GRID` to 512 since 4096 was too much
- Also remove `sm_scale` since it doesn't affect the subsequent topk

title: [ROCm][Bugfix]: Fallback GFX942 sparse MLA ops to Triton
body:
## Purpose This PR resolves severe generation accuracy degradation, numerical instability occurring in sparse MLA-based models on ROCm platforms. During our internal evaluations on the main branch, we identified a critical regression: - GLM-5.1-FP8 suffered from a massive accuracy collapse (dropping to ~55% on GSM8K). - DeepSeek-V3.2 experienced a slight but noticeable accuracy degradation (~3% drop on GSM8K). ### Key Changes: Fallback to Triton Indexer Kernels: Completely removed the hardware-specific C++ branches for _ON_GFX942 within vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py. Work is now routed unconditionally to the verified Triton implementations (indexer_k_quant_and_cache_triton and cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache_triton). Memory Alignment Bug Mitigation: Bypassed underlying vectorized memory operations in the custom C++ indexing layer that triggered hardware exceptions and memory faults when block_size was unaligned or not a multiple of 16 (e.g., block_size=1). ## Test Plan Comprehensive Accuracy & Stability Testing (Sparse MLA Models): Verify that shifting from the native C++ indexing kernels to the Triton execution pathways fully restores generative coherence and accuracy benchmarks under multi-GPU tensor parallel configurations. Models: zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 (TP8) and deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 (TP8). Configurations Tested: Evaluated across varied block cache layouts including --block-size 1, --block-size 16, and --block-size 64. Evaluation Metrics: 1. Downstream mathematical reasoning accuracy via GSM8K (LM-Eval, 20-shot). 2. E2E Serving Performance benchmark (Throughput, TTFT, TPOT, ITL, E2EL) using vllm bench serve. ## Test Result 1. LM-Eval Accuracy Comparison (Resolution of Accuracy Drop)
command ``` GLM-5.1-FP8 as example: server: #!/bin/bash SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd) max_num_seqs=256 tensor_parallel_size=8 max_model_len=${max_model_len:-16384} block_size=${block_size:-64} run_tag=${run_tag:-blocksize${block_size}} # if [[ "${VLLM_CLEAR_CACHE:-0}" == "1" ]]; then # rm -rf ~/.cache/vllm # fi rm -rf ~/.cache/vllm export PYTHONPATH="${SCRIPT_DIR}/fixglm5${PYTHONPATH:+:${PYTHONPATH}}" export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 \ --host localhost \ --port 8001 \ --block-size "${block_size}" \ --tensor-parallel-size "${tensor_parallel_size}" \ --max-model-len "${max_model_len}" \ --max-num-seqs "${max_num_seqs}" \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --trust-remote-code \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 \ --async-scheduling \ --enable-prefix-caching \ | tee "glm5_graph_accbugfixpr2_${run_tag}info-main.log" lmeval client: #!/bin/bash SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd) SYSTEM_SITE=${SYSTEM_SITE:-"/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages:/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages"} HFVENV_SITE=${HFVENV_SITE:-"${SCRIPT_DIR}/hfvenv/lib/python3.12/site-packages"} export PYTHONPATH="${SYSTEM_SITE}:${HFVENV_SITE}${PYTHONPATH:+:${PYTHONPATH}}" LM_EVAL_PYTHON=${LM_EVAL_PYTHON:-python} MODEL=zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 run_tag=${run_tag:-blocksize64} "${LM_EVAL_PYTHON}" -m lm_eval --model local-completions --model_args model=$MODEL,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8001/v1/completions,num_concurrent=256,max_retries=10,max_gen_toks=2048,max_length=8192,timeout=60000 --batch_size auto --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 20 \ --output_path "./results_glm5_fixaccbugfixpr2_${run_tag}_numshot20" \ --log_samples \ | tee "lmeval_glm5_fixaccbugfixpr2-3_${run_tag}_numshot20.log" ```
The routing optimization effectively eliminates token corruption and output derailment on GFX942. The exact match scores of GLM-5.1-FP8 recovered by up to 76%, while DeepSeek-V3.2 fully recovered to its baseline (~95.5%) across all tested cache granularities. 2. Benchmark Serving Performance (block_size 64)
command ``` GLM-5.1-FP8 as example: server: #!/bin/bash SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd) max_num_seqs=256 tensor_parallel_size=8 max_model_len=${max_model_len:-16384} block_size=${block_size:-64} run_tag=${run_tag:-blocksize${block_size}} rm -rf ~/.cache/vllm export PYTHONPATH="${SCRIPT_DIR}/fixflm5${PYTHONPATH:+:${PYTHONPATH}}" export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 MODEL="zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8" vllm serve $MODEL \ --host localhost \ --port 8001 \ --block-size "${block_size}" \ --tensor-parallel-size "${tensor_parallel_size}" \ --max-model-len "${max_model_len}" \ --max-num-seqs "${max_num_seqs}" \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --trust-remote-code \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --async-scheduling \ --enable-prefix-caching \ | tee "glm5_graph_accbugfixpr2_${run_tag}info-main-1.log" benchmark: #!/bin/bash set -euo pipefail TARGET_PORT=8001 TARGET_MODEL="zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8" RESULT_DIR=${RESULT_DIR:-./bench-sparsemla} RESULT_PREFIX=${RESULT_PREFIX:-ds-v4-pro-nomtp-sparsemlahiptritonhybrid} CONCURRENCIES=${CONCURRENCIES:-"16"} INPUT_LEN=${INPUT_LEN:-1024} OUTPUT_LEN=${OUTPUT_LEN:-1024} mkdir -p "${RESULT_DIR}" for C in ${CONCURRENCIES}; do NUM_PROMPTS=$((C * 5)) NUM_WARMUPS=$((C * 1)) vllm bench serve \ --backend openai-chat \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port "${TARGET_PORT}" \ --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \ --model "${TARGET_MODEL}" \ --dataset-name random \ --input-len "${INPUT_LEN}" \ --output-len "${OUTPUT_LEN}" \ --num-prompts "${NUM_PROMPTS}" \ --request-rate inf \ --max-concurrency "${C}" \ --num-warmups "${NUM_WARMUPS}" \ --random-range-ratio 0 \ --ignore-eos \ --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \ --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 \ --save-result \ --result-dir "${RESULT_DIR}" \ --result-filename "${RESULT_PREFIX}-C${C}.json" \ --metadata sparsemlatriton=false concurrency="${C}" workload=random_${INPUT_LEN}_${OUTPUT_LEN} num_prompts="${NUM_PROMPTS}" done ```
Beyond fixing the accuracy collapse, the Triton fallback slightly improves the token generation latency (TPOT/ITL improved by ~3%) and overall throughput (up ~2.45%). *Disclaimer the perf figure collected before the PR is just as hypothetical reference (assuming that the acc is correct); It is a hypothetical reference given that the lmeval acc table shows the accuracy regressed before this PR.*

title: [Bugfix][PD] Fix DSV4 disaggregated serving
body:
### Bug 
Recent changes broke DSV4 PD disagg. 

The `is_mla_region` check in `base_worker.py` only recognizes MLAAttentionSpec, but DSV4's compressor layers are `SlidingWindowMLASpec`. 

### Fix
Include `SlidingWindowMLASpec` in the isinstance check so these regions are treated as MLA region.

### Test ### 
- DSV4 Flash 4P4D on 8xH100 starts and serves requests after this fix.
- PR #42310 adds test cases for DSV4 PD disagg to nightly.

title: [NVFP4 MoE/Deepseek V4] Marlin: wire SwiGLU clamp + allow it for clamped models on non-Blackwell
body:
## Purpose

Address https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45859.

NVFP4 MoE models that declare a SwiGLU clamp (`config.swiglu_limit`, e.g. DeepSeek-V4) cannot be served on any non-Blackwell GPU (SM80/SM89/SM90). `select_nvfp4_moe_backend()` raises:

```
NotImplementedError: No NvFp4 MoE backend supports the deployment configuration.
```

When `swiglu_limit` is set, the selector restricts candidates to `NVFP4_BACKENDS_WITH_CLAMP`, which previously contained only `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` (Blackwell/SM100-only). On SM80/89/90 that leaves no candidate. The Marlin NVFP4 MoE backend runs on those architectures and its kernel already applies the SwiGLU clamp (`swiglu_limit_func`), but it was excluded from the clamp-capable set and was never handed the clamp value.

This PR wires the clamp through to Marlin and allows it for clamped models on non-Blackwell:

1. `nvfp4_w4a16_moe_quant_config()` accepts `gemm1_clamp_limit` and forwards it to `FusedMoEQuantConfig.make()`.
2. The `MARLIN` branch of `make_nvfp4_moe_quant_config()` passes `gemm1_clamp_limit=swiglu_limit`.
3. `MARLIN` is added to `NVFP4_BACKENDS_WITH_CLAMP`.

All three are required together. Without (1)+(2) the clamp would arrive as `None` and Marlin would silently skip it, producing unclamped (numerically incorrect) output — so adding `MARLIN` to the set alone would be unsafe. With all three, `MarlinExperts` receives `gemm1_clamp_limit` and the kernel applies `swiglu_limit_func` (identical math to `SiluAndMulWithClamp`), reproducing the intended clamped SwiGLU. Unclamped models (`swiglu_limit is None`) are unaffected — the filter is skipped and Marlin is selected as before.

## Test Plan

- Serve an NVFP4 MoE checkpoint that sets `config.swiglu_limit` (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) on a non-Blackwell GPU (SM90 / H100) at TP=4 and TP=8.
- Confirm the model now selects the Marlin NVFP4 MoE backend instead of raising `NotImplementedError: No NvFp4 MoE backend ...`.
- Issue a `/v1/chat/completions` request and verify a correct response.

Sample H100 invocation:
```
  vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \
    --tokenizer nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \
    --served-model-name dsv4flash-nvfp4-sanity \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --max-model-len 16384 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 2560 \
    --max-num-seqs 1 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
    --port 8652 \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --dtype auto
  ```

## Test Result

- **Before:** serving the clamped NVFP4 MoE model on non-Blackwell fails at load with `No NvFp4 MoE backend supports the deployment configuration`.
- **After:** the model loads and serves on H100 (SM90) at TP=4 and TP=8; `/v1/chat/completions` returns `200 OK` with a correct answer (e.g. *"What is the capital of Japan?"* → *"Tokyo"*).

---

This change is self-contained (only `fused_moe/config.py` and `fused_moe/oracle/nvfp4.py`). Serving DeepSeek-V4 end-to-end additionally requires, separately from this MoE-backend fix: sharing tied weights for quantized embeddings or model that use tied embeddings, and an fp8 KV-cache path for the model's MLA attention. (Available on Hopper but not Ampere today)

title: [Frontend] [Parser] Port DeepSeek V4 to streaming parser engine framework
body:
## Purpose

Replace the old DeepSeekV4ToolParser (V32 subclass) and DeepSeekV3ReasoningParser delegation with a unified ParserEngine subclass, matching the pattern used by Gemma4, Qwen3, MiniMax M2, and NemotronV3.

title: [ROCm][DSV4] Disable TileLang MHC dispatch on gfx942
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek V4 can produce incorrect output on gfx942 when the ROCm MHC path selects TileLang. The non-TileLang fallback path produces coherent output, so gfx942 should not silently route through the known-incorrect TileLang MHC kernels until that path is fixed.

This is a correctness guard, not a TileLang kernel fix. A future follow-up can re-enable TileLang MHC on gfx942 after those kernels are fixed or replaced with a gfx942-correct implementation.

This PR:

- Adds a `HAS_TILELANG_MHC` capability check for MHC-specific TileLang dispatch.
- Disables TileLang MHC on gfx942 only.
- Preserves CUDA and non-gfx942 ROCm TileLang MHC paths, including gfx950.
- Keeps gfx942 on the existing torch/triton MHC fallbacks.

Fixes #45698.

## Test Plan

### Environment

gfx942 validation used an MI300X node. gfx950 validation used an MI355X node.

```text
Focused kernel test runtime image:
vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-6607a80dabfa03932515808895b016d2666b0a55

DeepSeek V4 Flash prompt validation base image for gfx942:
vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:base-nightly-54bbf5166842932fa7abc34a14df850594daeb5e
  + vLLM PR #45681 source
  + native extensions rebuilt for gfx942
  + this PR overlaid as Python source for the guarded case

DeepSeek V4 Flash prompt validation base image for gfx950:
vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:base-nightly-54bbf5166842932fa7abc34a14df850594daeb5e
  + vLLM PR #45681 source
  + native extensions rebuilt for gfx950
  + this PR overlaid as Python source for the guarded case

GPUs: MI300X / gfx942 and MI355X / gfx950
```

The intended validation matrix is:

| GPU | Baseline before this PR | Patched after this PR | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| gfx942 | TileLang MHC selected | TileLang MHC disabled, fallback selected | Baseline fails, patched succeeds |
| gfx950 | TileLang MHC selected | TileLang MHC still selected | Both succeed |

This PR includes gfx942 and gfx950 validation.

The primary validation is a focused kernel A/B on gfx942:

- Baseline: this PR's base source with TileLang installed.
- Patched: this PR branch with the same runtime image and TileLang install.

DeepSeek V4 Flash prompt validation used vLLM PR #45681 as the functional MI300X DeepSeek V4 base because this PR's base source does not reach generation in the tested image due to an unrelated FP8/FNUZ model-load error.

### Focused MHC Kernel Test

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py
```

### DeepSeek V4 Flash Prompt Check

Serve command used for prompt-level attempts:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1

vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --moe-backend triton_unfused \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --disable-log-stats
```

Prompt request:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
import urllib.request

payload = {
    "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash",
    "prompt": "Q: What is 17 + 25? Answer briefly.\nA:",
    "max_tokens": 64,
    "temperature": 0,
}

req = urllib.request.Request(
    "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions",
    data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
    headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    method="POST",
)
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=240) as resp:
    print(json.dumps(json.load(resp), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
PY
```

## Test Result

### gfx942 Focused Kernel Validation

| Source | TileLang status | Result |
|---|---|---|
| This PR base | installed | `15 failed, 36 passed` |
| This PR branch | installed, `HAS_TILELANG_MHC=False` | `8 passed, 43 skipped` |

The baseline failures were in TileLang MHC pre and fused post+pre tests, with large numerical mismatches against the torch reference. The patched run skips TileLang MHC tests on gfx942 because this PR disables that path there.

A direct patched fallback smoke also called:

- `MHCPreOp.forward_hip`
- `MHCPostOp.forward_hip`
- `MHCFusedPostPreOp.forward_hip`

with `HAS_TILELANG_MHC=False` and compared outputs against torch references. Result: passed.

### gfx942 DeepSeek V4 Flash Prompt Check

Prompt validation used a rebuilt image based on vLLM PR #45681 with native extensions rebuilt for gfx942.

| Source | TileLang status | Result |
|---|---|---|
| This PR base | installed | Did not reach generation: `NotImplementedError: "mul_cuda" not implemented for 'Float8_e8m0fnu'` |
| Rebuilt vLLM PR #45681 image | installed, no this-PR guard | Did not answer `42`; produced gibberish beginning with `bal") A proposal...` |
| Rebuilt vLLM PR #45681 image + this PR Python overlay | installed, `HAS_TILELANG_MHC=False` | Answered `42` |

### gfx950 Focused Kernel Validation

| Source | TileLang status | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Rebuilt vLLM PR #45681 image + this PR Python overlay | installed, `HAS_TILELANG_MHC=True` | `51 passed, 38 warnings` |

The gfx950 run confirms the TileLang MHC tests were not skipped by the gfx942 guard.

### gfx950 DeepSeek V4 Flash Prompt Check

Prompt validation used a rebuilt image based on vLLM PR #45681 with native extensions rebuilt for gfx950.

| Source | TileLang status | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Rebuilt vLLM PR #45681 image | installed | Answered `42` |
| Rebuilt vLLM PR #45681 image + this PR Python overlay | installed, `HAS_TILELANG_MHC=True` | Answered `42` |

This confirms the patch leaves TileLang MHC enabled and coherent on gfx950.

title: [Attention][MLA][DCP] Query replication for MLA decode (DeepSeek-V2/R1 + Kimi-K2.5)
body:
## Purpose

With Decode Context Parallelism (DCP) the KV cache is sharded across the DCP group, so the standard MLA decode path **all-gathers the query** across the group every step so each rank can attend its KV shard with the full head set, then LSE-reduces the partials. That all-gather sits on the decode critical path.

This PR adds an **opt-in** alternative: replicate the (small) MLA query projection *within each DCP group* at load time, so every rank already materializes the full group-local query head set locally. Decode then **skips the query all-gather** and
runs a group-local `W_UK_T_dcp_qrep` BMM. The query projection is tiny relative to the KV cache, so replicating it costs little memory while removing a collective from the decode hot path. Gated behind `VLLM_DCP_Q_REPLICATE` (default off → exact current behavior).

RFC: #34018 (prematurely closed)

## Scope & dependencies

qrep is a **self-contained, opt-in feature**: it replicates the MLA query projection within each DCP group so decode can skip the query all-gather. It is **backend-agnostic** — it only requires the MLA decode backend to return decode-LSE
(a base-DCP property) and does not re-implement LSE or KV handling. On any backend whose DCP decode-LSE is already merged, qrep runs on merged DCP alone.

Validated here with `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA`; that backend's DCP decode-LSE is in flight upstream (#44044 / #43729), so reproducing the evidence below requires it — mentioned for reproducibility, not because qrep is coupled to it.

## Compatibility & roadmap

**Supported today (opt-in, `VLLM_DCP_Q_REPLICATE=1`, DCP world size > 1):**

| Dimension | qrep support | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| MLA decode backend | **FlashInfer-MLA** ✓ | needs the backend's DCP decode-LSE (#44044 / #43729) |
| Head-padding MLA backends (e.g. CutlassMLA `q_pad_num_heads`) | ✗ guarded | `W_UK_T_dcp_qrep` is built unpadded `dcp*num_heads`; validated once at weight-load |
| aiter FP4 / FP8 triton MLA BMM | ✗ guarded | qrep builds the BMM weight on the bf16 path only; validated once at weight-load |
| KV-cache dtype | **fp8 ✓** / bf16 ✓ | orthogonal — qrep replicates the *query projection*, not the KV cache (validated with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`). |
| q / kv projection **weights** | unquantized bf16 ✓ | quantized q/kv sources raise `NotImplementedError` (see roadmap) |
| Models | DeepSeek-V2/V3/R1 (dense MLA), Kimi-K2.5/2.6 (wrapper loader) | |
| Default-off / DCP=1 | exact baseline | pure no-op; every touched site takes the original branch |

**Roadmap (follow-ups, not in this PR):**
1. **DSV4 support** along with DCP support (WIP, Preparing for two PRs specifically for DSV4)
2. **Quantized q/kv projection replicas.**
3. **Head-padding MLA backends.** Would require a padded `W_UK_T_dcp_qrep` to serve CutlassMLA-style `q_pad_num_heads`.
4. **Per-subset (decode-only) projection.** Investigated as a way to drop the projection's prefill overhead; currently shelved because it did not beat the compute-both path in decode-dominant traffic. Revisit only with a graph-friendly form.

## Test Plan

Three matched arms (same image/model/harness), toggling only DCP + qrep, on both models:

| Arm | TP | DCP | DCP backend | VLLM_DCP_Q_REPLICATE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DCP (all-gather) | 8 | 8 | `--dcp-comm-backend a2a` | 0 |
| DCP + qrep | 8 | 8 | `--dcp-comm-backend a2a` | 1 |

### Reproduction (serve args / commands)

Enable qrep with `VLLM_DCP_Q_REPLICATE=1` + `--decode-context-parallel-size N>1`
(gated; no-op at DCP=1). No CLI/EngineArg change.

```bash
export VLLM_DCP_Q_REPLICATE=${QREP}   # 0 or 1, per arm
vllm serve ${MODEL} \
  --trust-remote-code --enable-expert-parallel \
  --tensor-parallel-size ${TP} \
  --decode-context-parallel-size ${DCP} \
  --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA \
  ${DCP_BACKEND} \
  --max-model-len ${MML} --max-num-seqs ${MNS} \
  --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill
# Kimi only (vision encoder): add
#   --skip-mm-profiling --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}'
```

## Test Result

**Setup.** 
- (8× B200); **TP8 / DCP8**
- `--dcp-comm-backend a2a` 
- `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA` (`mla_prefill_backend=FLASHINFER`) 
- fp8 KV 
- `--max-num-seqs 32`
-  **FULL CUDA graph** (capture `1 2 4 8 16 32`). 
- Two regimes: 
    - **decode-dominant** (random 128/1024)
    - **mixed** (1024/1024)
    - 256 prompts
    - concurrency 32.

**Decode latency / throughput — qrep removes the decode query all-gather:**

| Model | Regime | qrep P50 TPOT (ms) | all-gather P50 TPOT (ms) | TPOT Δ | qrep tput (tok/s) | all-gather tput (tok/s) | tput Δ |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-R1-NVFP4 | decode | 16.55 | 17.04 | **−2.88%** | 1891.14 | 1837.62 | **+2.91%** |
| DeepSeek-R1-NVFP4 | mixed | 17.57 | 18.07 | **−2.78%** | 1758.09 | 1721.94 | **+2.10%** |
| Kimi-K2.6-NVFP4 | decode | 15.32 | 16.04 | **−4.51%** | 2052.93 | 1959.96 | **+4.74%** |
| Kimi-K2.6-NVFP4 | mixed | 15.97 | 16.60 | **−3.75%** | 1942.95 | 1867.40 | **+4.05%** |


**GSM8K accuracy (full-1319, 5-shot, c32) — qrep is accuracy-equivalent:**

| Model | qrep (flex / strict) | all-gather (flex / strict) | Δ flex (pp) |
|---|---|---|---:|
| DeepSeek-R1-NVFP4 | 0.9553 / 0.9538 | 0.9538 / 0.9530 | +0.15 |
| Kimi-K2.6-NVFP4 | 0.9371 / 0.9363 | 0.9393 / 0.9386 | −0.22 |

## Evidence (single-commit bisect)

DeepSeek-V4-Flash, `-dp 4 -ep`, greedy, prompt *"What is the capital of France? Answer in one word."*:

| commit | output |
| --- | --- |
| `9c7c74bf1` (#45857, **parent** of #45309) | `Paris` ✅ |
| `2a47a9ff0` (**#45309**) | `the the the the …` / code spam ❌ |

`2a47a9ff0`'s parent is exactly `9c7c74bf1`, so #45309 is the only change between good and bad.

## Tests run

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash -dp 4 -ep --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter --port 8003
# greedy chat: "What is the capital of France? Answer in one word."
```
- parent `9c7c74bf1` → `Paris` (correct)

This revert is a clean `git revert` of the single-commit diff (one file, `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py`), restoring the `@eager_break_during_capture` split that the parent had. (Revert-on-`main` build not yet separately runtime-verified beyond the bisect above.)

## Not a duplicate

This restores correctness; the perf optimization (26.8%~27.9% TTFT) should be re-landed with the eager-break capture split preserved.

title: [DeepSeek-V4] Support TEP=16 for the block-FP8 shared expert
body:
## Purpose
Currently TEP=16 is not supported for DeepSeek-V4.
The shared expert is a block-FP8 MLP (`weight_block_size=[128,128]`,
`moe_intermediate_size=3072`). A per-rank TP shard must be a whole number of
128-blocks (a block's FP8 scale can't be split). At TP=16, `3072/16 = 192` is not
a multiple of 128, so the standard linears fail to build:
`Weight input_size_per_partition = 192 is not divisible by block_k = 128`.

## Layout (`DeepseekV4MLP`)
Keep ordinary TP linears (no `disable_tp`, no manual all-reduce — `down_proj`
`reduce_results` does the reduce). When block-FP8 and not sequence-parallel, round
the per-rank block count up with `cdiv` and resize `intermediate_size` so the
linear's own `// tp_size` split lands on it:

```python
n_local = cdiv(intermediate_size // block, tp_size)
intermediate_size = n_local * block * tp_size
```

At TP=16 this is a uniform **256/rank**: the 24 blocks fill ranks 0–11 (256×12) and
the 4 trailing ranks hold zeros. Zeros contribute nothing (gate_up→act→down partial
is 0), so the all-reduce still sums to the full shared-expert output.

## Weight loading (`_load_shared_expert_weight`)
The checkpoint stores the full intermediate, so `load_weights` slices each rank's
blocks (replicated/SP and unquantized shared experts use the standard stacked path):

- Same uniform `cdiv` split as `DeepseekV4MLP`; ranks past the real blocks are zeroed.
- `gate` (`w1`) / `up` (`w3`) `[I, H]`: cut dim 0 (`up` = 2nd half of merged `gate_up_proj`).
- `down` (`w2`→`down_proj`) `[H, I]`: cut dim 1.
- 1-D cut along the intermediate-block axis; the non-swizzled block scales
  `[I/128, H/128]` slice on the same axis. E8M0 checkpoint scales are numerically
  converted into the float32 FP8 scale params on copy.

## Relation to existing PRs
#41312 fixes the same TP=16 FP8 load failure but is a broad, bundled change: it
zero-pads the weights into a balanced block layout and adds a cross-node aux-stream
determinism env flag, across several files. This change is deliberately minimal and
contained to the V4 nvidia model — a uniform per-rank `cdiv` block split, slicing
whole real blocks from the checkpoint in `load_weights` with surplus ranks left
zero (no in-weight padding, no env/determinism changes, nothing else).

## Tests
`pre-commit run ruff-check / ruff-format / mypy-3.12 --files vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py` → pass.

```
|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr|
|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9560|±  |0.0056|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9553|±  |0.0057|
```

## AI assistance
Developed with AI assistance (Claude). The human submitter has reviewed every
changed line and is responsible for running the tests above before merge.

title: [MM][CG] Support ViT full CUDA graph for DeepSeek-VL2
body:
## Purpose

Support ViT full CUDA graph capture/replay for DeepSeek-VL2, as tracked in #38175.

Previously, `DeepseekVLV2ForCausalLM` ran vision encoding (SigLIP ViT + MLP
projector) eagerly on every forward pass, incurring repeated CPU kernel-dispatch
overhead. This PR implements the `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` protocol so
`EncoderCudaGraphManager` can capture the ViT + projector forward pass once and
replay it, eliminating that overhead for batches that fit within a captured
budget.

**Key design decisions:**
- `encoder_cudagraph_forward` returns raw per-tile projector output
  `[N_tiles, hw, D]`; newline tokens and the view-separator are reattached in
  `postprocess_encoder_output` (outside the graph), keeping the captured
  computation simple and shape-static.
- `encoder_eager_forward` calls the existing `_pixel_values_to_embedding` and
  returns a flat `[total_tokens, D]` tensor, matching what `scatter_output_slices`
  expects in the eager-fallback path.
- `_proj_hw()` derives projector output spatial size from config
  (`ceil((image_size // patch_size) / downsample_ratio)`), consistent with the
  token-count formula in `DeepseekVL2ProcessingInfo.get_num_image_tokens`.

## Test Plan

**Unit test:**
```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py \
    -v -k "DeepseekVL2"

# Full suite to confirm no regression
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -v
```

**Functional test:**
```bash
# Enable encoder CUDA graph via compilation_config in run_deepseek_vl2()
python examples/generate/multimodal/vision_language_offline.py \
    -m deepseek_vl_v2 --modality image
```

**Benchmark:**
```bash
vllm bench mm-processor \
  --model deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-tiny \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --dataset-name random-mm \
  --random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 \
  --random-mm-num-mm-items-range-ratio 0.0 \
  --random-mm-bucket-config '{(336, 336, 1): 1.0}' \
  --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}' \
  --num-prompts 100 \
  --seed 42 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true, "encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets": [64, 128, 256, 512, 1024], "encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch": 4}'
```

title: [Bugfix] Preserve FP8 indexer WK pairs across incremental load_weights
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #46078.

`_pending_wk_fp8` was local to each `DeepseekV2Model.load_weights()` call. When a streaming loader (e.g. S3 / RunAI) delivers `indexer.wk.weight` and `indexer.wk.weight_scale_inv` in separate `load_weights()` calls, the pair never completes inside `_try_load_fp8_indexer_wk()`, so the fused `wk_weights_proj.weight` is never dequantized from FP8 and stays non-finite — producing corrupted sparse-MLA generations. Dense MLA looks coherent because it bypasses the sparse indexer.

This implements the fix proposed by @bvolpato-dd in #46078: persist the pending buffer on the model instance (`self._pending_indexer_wk_fp8`) so a (weight, scale) pair that arrives across separate `load_weights()` calls still completes. Completed pairs are already removed by `_try_load_fp8_indexer_wk()`, so the dict self-empties after a full load. The common single-call load path is unchanged.

## Test Plan

As reported in #46078, this was validated on vLLM 0.23.0 with GLM-5.2-FP8 (native sparse IndexShare) under incremental S3 / RunAI streaming.

I don't have a GLM-5.x FP8 sparse-indexer checkpoint to add an automated regression test; happy to add one if a reviewer can point me to a suitable small fixture.

## Test Result

Per the report in #46078: after the final load the pending buffer is empty, the fused WK parameter is fully finite, and generation is coherent. No behavior change on the single-call load path.

title: [Attention] Add FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE backend for Hopper sparse MLA
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a Python-only `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` backend for sparse MLA
models on Hopper GPUs. The backend reuses vLLM's existing FlashAttention MLA
wrapper and sparse MLA index conversion path, then calls
`flash_attn_varlen_func(..., fa_version=3)` for BF16 KV-cache sparse decode.

The tested GLM-5.1-FP8 checkpoint has:

- `num_attention_heads = 64`
- `kv_lora_rank = 512`
- `qk_rope_head_dim = 64`
- compressed KV dim = `576`
- `index_topk = 2048`
- FP8 weight quantization, with BF16 KV cache in this backend

The vLLM reference serving configuration for this checkpoint uses tensor
parallel size 8. Under that configuration, the query head count is
`64 / 8 = 8`. The current vLLM FlashMLA sparse implementation, following
upstream FlashMLA kernel constraints, **supports only `q_head = 64` on Hopper**. When
GLM-5.1-FP8 runs with TP8, the local `q_head` is 8, so the current **path pads it
to 64 before running the sparse attention kernel**. On Blackwell, the FlashMLA sparse kernel constraint is `q_head = 128`. This PR does not add Blackwell support.

Code references:

- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py`: `prefill_padding` is set
  to 64 on Hopper and 128 on Blackwell.
- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py`: for BF16 KV cache,
  `_forward_bf16_kv()` calls `_bf16_flash_mla_kernel()` for the token batch,
  including decode tokens; that kernel pads `q` to `self.prefill_padding`
  before calling `flash_mla_sparse_fwd()`.
- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py`: for FP8 KV-cache decode,
  `_fp8_flash_mla_kernel()` separately pads `q` to 64 or 128 before calling
  `flash_mla_with_kvcache()`.

## Related PRs and Issues

Relevant open work:

- [#39924: `[Attention] Add FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE backend`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39924)
  - Status: open.
  - This targets FA4 DSA support on Blackwell through upstream
    FlashAttention DSA support. This PR targets Hopper/SM90 and reuses vLLM's
    existing FA3 wrapper path, so it is not the same implementation target, but maybe can be combined together.
- [#39941: `[Attention][SM90] Add CUTLASS FA3 sparse MLA attention backend for Hopper GPUs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39941)
  - Status: open.
  - This is another Hopper sparse MLA direction, but it adds a separate
    CUTLASS-based extension and kernel wrapper. This PR is Python-only and
    routes through the existing vLLM FlashAttention wrapper.
- [#34744: `[WIP][Attention] Enable masked MHA for topk sparse attention using FA4`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/34744)
  - Status: open.
  - This focuses on short-context prefill routing through dense/masked MHA.
    This PR focuses on sparse MLA decode with the existing FA3 varlen API.
- [#31473: `DeepSeek-V3.2 Performance Optimization Tracking`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/31473)
  - Status: open.
  - Tracks sparse MLA performance work, including support for TP without head
    padding.

## Implementation

The new `flashattn_mla_sparse.py` backend is implemented by following the two closest existing vLLM MLA backends:

- It follows `flashmla_sparse.py` for sparse MLA metadata, top-k index handling, and logical-to-physical KV-cache index conversion.
- It follows `flashattn_mla.py` for using the existing `flash_attn_varlen_func(..., fa_version=3)` wrapper.
- It is registered as `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE`, marked as both MLA and sparse, and enabled only for Hopper with BF16 KV cache.
- The current implementation does not support Blackwell, DCP, or KV-cache quantization such as FP8 KV cache.

## Test

Environment:

- model: local GLM-5.1-FP8 checkpoint
- GPU setup: 8-way tensor parallel serving
- backend under test: `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE`
- random dataset
- `temperature=0`
- `ignore_eos`
- `seed=20260619`
- `--max-model-len 8192`
- `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.80`

Launch shape:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/mnt/data2/dakai/vllm_adk_glm_optimize \
/mnt/data2/dakai/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve \
  /mnt/data2/models/zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 18081 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --served-model-name glm-5.1-fp8 \
  --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE
```

Benchmark command used for each shape:

```bash

/mnt/data2/dakai/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench serve \
  --backend openai \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18121 \

## Kernel benchmark

Single-GPU synthetic operator benchmark:

- `kv_lora_rank = 512`
- `qk_rope_head_dim = 64`
- compressed KV dim = `576`
- `index_topk = 2048`
- FA3 wrapper path uses actual local `h_q = 8/16/32/64`
- FlashMLA path uses H=64 padded query heads

For GLM-5.1 TP8 (`h_q=8`):

| KV length | num tokens | FA3 wrapper ms | FlashMLA H=64 ms | FA3 wrapper speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096 | 1 | 0.0447 | 0.1828 | 4.09x |
| 4096 | 4 | 0.0449 | 0.1834 | 4.08x |
| 4096 | 8 | 0.0559 | 0.1845 | 3.30x |
| 4096 | 16 | 0.0775 | 0.1839 | 2.37x |
| 4096 | 32 | 0.1450 | 0.1813 | 1.25x |

| 4096 | 128 | 0.3680 | 0.3506 | 0.95x |
| 512 | 1 | 0.0429 | 0.0575 | 1.34x |
| 512 | 8 | 0.0440 | 0.0584 | 1.33x |
| 512 | 32 | 0.0550 | 0.0576 | 1.05x |
| 512 | 64 | 0.0746 | 0.0584 | 0.78x |

## Accuracy Validation

Deterministic GSM8K eval:

```bash
tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py \
  --num-questions 1319 \
  --num-shots 5 \
  --max-tokens 256 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --seed 20260619
```

Results:

| Run | Accuracy | Invalid rate | Questions | Shots |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:
| baseline | 0.951478 | 0.000758 | 1319 | 5 |
| this PR | 0.952995 | 0.000000 | 1319 | 5 |

Delta:

```text
this PR - baseline = +0.001516
```

This is not the same because we change the attention backend, but the difference is minor.

## Limitations

- Hopper/SM90 only.
- BF16 KV cache only.
- FP8 KV cache is intentionally rejected by this backend for automatic fallback.
- DCP is not supported yet.
- High-concurrency serving may not benefit as much as small-token decode because
  the FA3 wrapper path crosses over against the padded path at larger active
  token counts.

## AI Assistance

AI assistance was used to prepare this change and PR description. The human
submitter is responsible for reviewing every changed line and validating the
final PR before submission.

title: [ROCm] [Bugfix] Bugfix ROCm Sparse Indexer
body:

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSV4] Enable split sparse decode on gfx942
body:
## Purpose

Enable the existing split partial/reduce Triton sparse decode path for DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA decode on AMD gfx942.

gfx950 already uses this path. gfx942 currently falls back to the monolithic `_sparse_attn_decode_ragged_kernel`, even though the split path runs correctly on gfx942. This PR extends the tuned-architecture guard to include gfx942 and updates the ROCm DeepSeek-V4 sparse attention tests so the split decode path is covered on both gfx942 and gfx950.

This is a targeted decode-path improvement. The latest MI300X/gfx942 profiles show the sparse decode work itself drops by about 40% with the split path. Serving-level impact is modest and workload dependent: in the repeated-pass validation, high-throughput output throughput was effectively at parity with lower observed TTFT, while the low-rate decode-heavy workload showed lower TPOT/ITL and lower observed TTFT.

AI assistance was used for this PR.

## Test Plan

- Run ROCm DeepSeek-V4 sparse attention tests on gfx942:

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py
```

- Start a vLLM OpenAI-compatible server for `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` on an 8x gfx942 node and run:
  - deterministic completion smoke request
  - GSM8K smoke evaluation
  - `vllm bench serve` high-throughput random workload: input 128, output 96, 128 prompts, request rate `inf`
  - `vllm bench serve` low-rate decode-heavy random workload: input 17, output 96, 32 prompts, request rate `1`
  - repeated-pass high-throughput and low-rate comparisons, reporting first pass separately from later warm passes

Testing environment for DeepSeek-V4-Flash prompt/e2e validation on gfx942:

```text
Image:
  vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-9e57de7197f234f9d9187715d96e07e007048c0f
Hardware:
  8x AMD Instinct MI300X OAM, gfx942
Common server args:
  tensor_parallel_size=8
  kv_cache_dtype=fp8_e4m3
  max_model_len=4096
  tokenizer_mode=deepseek_v4
  moe_backend=triton_unfused
  max_num_batched_tokens=8192
  VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
```

Baseline used the installed gfx950-only guard, so gfx942 took `_sparse_attn_decode_ragged_kernel`. Proposed changed only the guard to include gfx942, so gfx942 took `_sparse_attn_decode_partial_kernel` plus `_sparse_attn_decode_reduce_kernel`.

## Test Result

ROCm DeepSeek-V4 sparse attention tests passed on gfx942:

```text
41 passed, 16 warnings in 26.43s
```

ROCm DeepSeek-V4 sparse attention tests also passed on MI355X/gfx950:

```text
40 passed, 16 warnings in 26.35s
exit code: 0
```

DeepSeek-V4-Flash serving correctness on 8x gfx942:

| Check | Baseline fallback | Proposed split |
|---|---:|---:|
| Deterministic smoke request | returned `42` | returned `42` |
| GSM8K limit-20 flexible exact match | 0.95 | 0.95 |
| GSM8K limit-20 strict exact match | 0.95 | 0.95 |

Kernel-level sparse decode benchmark, `MAIN_LEN=80`, `EXTRA_LEN=32`, production DeepSeek-V4 cache packing:

| NUM_QUERIES | Correctness max abs diff | Fallback ragged mean | Split partial+reduce mean | Improvement |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.000122 | 42.754 us | 22.836 us | 46.59% |
| 8 | 0.000244 | 42.260 us | 23.088 us | 45.37% |
| 32 | 0.000244 | 42.547 us | 24.490 us | 42.44% |
| 128 | 0.000244 | 43.463 us | 34.121 us | 21.49% |

High-throughput profiler comparison on gfx942 confirms the intended kernel replacement:

| Category | Baseline CUDA ms | Proposed CUDA ms | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Sparse decode total | 2542.147 | 1535.915 | -39.58% |
| `_sparse_attn_decode_ragged_kernel` | 2542.147 | 0.000 | replaced |
| `_sparse_attn_decode_partial_kernel` | 0.000 | 1369.342 | added |
| `_sparse_attn_decode_reduce_kernel` | 0.000 | 166.573 | added |

Serving benchmarks used one baseline server and one proposed server per workload, with six sequential benchmark passes each. Pass 1 is reported separately from the warm average over passes 2-6.

High-throughput random workload, input 128/output 96, 128 prompts, request rate `inf`:

| Variant | Pass 1 output tok/s | Pass 1 TTFT | Pass 1 TPOT | Warm passes | Warm output tok/s | Warm TTFT | Warm TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline fallback | 1887.34 | 2585.36 ms | 41.02 ms | 2-6 | 2908.57 | 831.55 ms | 35.42 ms |
| Proposed split | 2022.96 | 2243.84 ms | 39.89 ms | 2-6 | 2930.17 | 777.70 ms | 35.65 ms |
| Proposed delta | +7.19% | -13.21% | -2.75% | 2-6 | +0.74% | -6.48% | +0.63% |

Low-rate decode-heavy random workload, input 17/output 96, 32 prompts, request rate `1`:

| Variant | Pass 1 output tok/s | Pass 1 TTFT | Pass 1 TPOT | Warm passes | Warm output tok/s | Warm TTFT | Warm TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline fallback | 90.44 | 65.91 ms | 22.02 ms | 2-6 | 90.43 | 60.05 ms | 21.94 ms |
| Proposed split | 90.67 | 64.59 ms | 21.05 ms | 2-6 | 90.65 | 57.79 ms | 20.95 ms |
| Proposed delta | +0.25% | -2.00% | -4.41% | 2-6 | +0.25% | -3.76% | -4.50% |

title: Run DeepSeek-V2-Lite prefetch-offload eval eager on ROCm
body:
The mi300_1: deepseek-v2-lite-prefetch-offload-accuracy nightly is flaky on MI300X — ~1 in 5 fresh servers emits ~45% garbage decode tokens, dropping GSM8K accuracy below the 0.25 threshold. 

The corruption is nondeterministic across identical runs and reproduces on the plain non-offload baseline. Root cause is a HIP graph capture/replay regression in the ROCm runtime (ROCm/clr), not vLLM or the offload feature: bisecting libamdhip64 (rest of stack fixed) shows clr 7.1.1 clean and 7.2.0/7.2.2/7.2.3 broken; the same kernels run clean under HIP graphs on CUDA and on ROCm 7.13. Eager is always correct.


 This forces --enforce-eager on ROCm only until the runtime fix lands. CUDA path unchanged. Restores deterministic ~0.34 accuracy at lower decode throughput (still within timeout).

title: [Attention][MLA] FlashMLA sparse: DCP on the fp8_ds_mla mixed-batch path + MTP
body:
DCP support for the `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` backend on the `fp8_ds_mla` KV path, including MTP spec decode under full cudagraphs. `fp8_ds_mla` is what the backend selector picks on Hopper for DSA models with small per-rank head counts (GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek-V3.2 at TP4/DCP4), and this path previously refused DCP outright.

Earlier revisions stacked on #46076 and carried the sparse-indexer DCP machinery (global top-k merge, `--dcp-sparse-indexer-mode`); all of that has since landed in main via #46076 and its follow-ups, so the PR is now backend-side only: +234/−34 across `flashmla_sparse.py`, `flashmla.py` and one test file. (#45426 was our earlier standalone version with its own indexer; this supersedes it and reuses the upstream merge machinery instead.)

## Changes

`flashmla_sparse.py`:
- Opt the backend into the shared DCP decode merge (`can_return_lse_for_decode`): the fp8 mixed-batch kernel now returns decode LSE, sliced together with the head padding and reshaped to the `(tokens, heads)` layout the reducer consumes.
- Under DCP the indexer emits global token ids: keep this rank's shard and convert to local `fp8_ds_mla` slots via `triton_filter_and_convert_dcp_index` with `compact_valid_to_front=False` — the scattered `-1`s stay in place and the fp8 kernel masks them natively, skipping the per-call front-pack. Rows where this rank owns none of the selected tokens get `(0, -inf)`, the identity of the cross-rank LSE merge, so they drop out of the reduce.
- Allow varlen decode under DCP (`supports_dcp_with_varlen` when `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size == 1`): causality comes from the indexer's top-k indices, not kernel metadata. This is what makes MTP + DCP work under full cudagraphs.
- Fail-closed guards instead of silent corruption: `ag_rs` comm backend only; fp8 mixed-batch path only (the split prefill/decode path returns LSE for decode tokens only, and the bf16 sparse path is rejected under DCP); a head-envelope guard rejecting configs where local and DCP-gathered head counts pad to different fp8 decode kernel envelopes (e.g. 128 q-heads at TP8/DCP8).

`flashmla.py` (dense FlashMLA decode): flatten the kernel's `[batch, heads, seq_len]` LSE to `[tokens, heads]` for the DCP reducer — matters under spec decode, where `seq_len > 1`.

Tests: `test_fp8_dcp_head_envelope_guard` in `test_sparse_mla_backends.py`, parametrized over local head counts × DCP world sizes, both accepting and rejecting cases.

## Testing

4×H200, GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4/DCP4/EP + MTP, `fp8_ds_mla`, current rebase:

- `test_sparse_mla_backends.py` + `test_indexer_dcp_localize.py`: 140 passed / 0 failed (SM90).
- Full cudagraph capture clean; exact needle recovery at 198k context across all ranks.
- Warm decode 78 tok/s at batch 1, 854 aggregate at batch 32 (786k context window).
- dcp=1/2/4 byte-identical on long (>2048-tok) contexts in earlier revisions of the same merge path.

The branch has also been soaking continuously since mid-July on a production 4×H200 GLM-5.2-NVFP4 deployment (TP4/DCP4/EP + MTP) via nightly-based images carrying this PR.

Related fixes in the surrounding DCP infra that this path exposed were split out and handled separately: #48379 (fp8_ds_mla boot on main, merged), #50823 (block-table width under DCP, merged), #50883 (offload block-size scaling under DCP, open).

AI assistance (Claude) was used; every line reviewed by the submitter, tests run by the submitter.

<details>
<summary>History: pre-rebase description (union indexer mode, perf vs #45426) — superseded</summary>

Earlier revisions added an opt-in `--dcp-sparse-indexer-mode {exact,union}` on top of #46076's global top-k merge, motivated by a ~30% batch-1 decode regression of the exact merge vs our standalone indexer (#45426): 52.0 → 36.4 tok/s warm at batch 1, with union recovering to 43.5 and a follow-up localizer opt to 50.7. After the indexer machinery landed upstream in its final form, the flag and the indexer-side changes were dropped from this PR; the numbers above no longer describe the current diff.

</details>

title: [Bugfix][DSv3.2] Skip indexer weights for index-cache-skipped layers
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #45895. With `index_topk_freq>1` (or an `index_topk_pattern`), only some layers build a sparse indexer; the rest are skipped at init via `_skip_topk`. But the checkpoint still ships `indexer.*` weights for every layer, so `load_weights` tries to assign them to params that don't exist on the skipped layers and the load fails.

Hit on DeepSeek-V3.2 with `--hf_overrides '{"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": 4}'`.

## Fix

Collect the layer prefixes that actually built an indexer, then drop `indexer.*` weights for layers not in that set. With the default `index_topk_freq=1` every layer has an indexer, so nothing is dropped (no-op). Not ROCm-specific.

## Related

- Loader companion to #45895 (init skip).
- Orthogonal to #46168 (FP8 indexer WK pair across streaming loads).

## Test

- DSv3.2 TP8 with `index_topk_freq=4`: loads and serves; previously failed at weight load.
- Default config: unchanged.

title: [Perf] Remove redundant clone for GLM, Deepseek etc
body:
## Purpose

These clone are not needed

```bash
    def forward_native(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        residual: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    ) -> torch.Tensor | tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """PyTorch-native implementation equivalent to forward()."""
        if residual is None:
            return ir.ops.rms_norm(
                x,
                self.weight.data if self.pass_weight else None,
                self.variance_epsilon,
                self.variance_size_override,
            )
        else:
            return ir.ops.fused_add_rms_norm.maybe_inplace(
                x,
                residual,
                self.weight.data if self.pass_weight_add else None,
                self.variance_epsilon,
                self.variance_size_override,
            )
```

As in rms norm, when residual is not None, we will return a output instead of doing it inplace

## Test

Covered in CI

The larger tensor is, the more perf we get.

title: Fix write-after-write hazard in xpu KV RoPE triton kernel
body:
The KV branch of `_xpu_qnorm_rope_kernel` copied all HEAD_DIM elements into the output, then overwrote the RoPE region with the rotated values. These stores target overlapping addresses with no ordering guarantee, so on XPU the RoPE positions were non-deterministic run-to-run, making greedy decode unstable.

Mask the full copy to the NoPE region so the RoPE region is written only by the rotated stores, matching the Q branch.

title: [ROCm][DSV4] B-preshuffle the attention fp8 projections
body:
## Purpose
Speed up the DeepSeek-V4 fp8 attention projections `fused_wqa_wkv` (fused Q/KV
down-proj) and `wo_b` (output proj) on ROCm (gfx950) by routing them through
AITER's weight-preshuffled block-scale GEMM instead of the default block-scale GEMM.

## What it does
- **Load time:** B-preshuffle the two projections' fp8 weights via the existing
  `shuffle_weight((16, 16))` and cache the block scales (`prepare_attn_preshuffle`).
- **Run time:** quantize the activation to fp8 group-128 with a **column-major**
  scale and run the preshuffled GEMM, replacing the default `gemm_a8w8_blockscale`.
- Adds **2** ops to `rocm_aiter_ops`: `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle` (the GEMM)
  and `group_fp8_quant_transpose_scale` (the matched transposed-scale quant the GEMM
  requires); reuses the existing `shuffle_weight`.
- ROCm-only, gated by `VLLM_DSV4_AITER_ATTN_PRESHUFFLE` (default on). All preshuffle
  logic lives in `DeepseekV4ROCMAiterMLAAttention`

## Performance — pinned aiter `v0.1.13.post1` (8× mi355, TP=8)
DSV4 Pro, ISL/OSL 1024/1024, NP=10*C, MoE fixed to `triton_unfused` so the delta isolates the
attention change.


| concurrency | output tok/s (off → on) | Δ | median TTFT ms (off → on) | Δ | mean TPOT ms (off → on) | Δ |
|--:|--|--:|--|--:|--|--:|
| 16  | 422 → 423   | +0.1% | 936 → 908   | −2.9% | 36.9 → 37.0 | +0.3% |
| 32  | 728 → 735   | +1.0% | 1325 → 1263 | −4.7% | 42.7 → 42.3 | −0.9% |
| **64**  | **1179 → 1221** | **+3.6%** | **1610 → 1535** | **−4.7%** | **52.7 → 50.9** | **−3.4%** |
| 128 | 581 → 588   | +1.3% | 1766 → 1682 | −4.8% | 218.5 → 215.8 | −1.2% |


## Accuracy — gsm8k 5-shot

| aiter | OFF | ON |
|--|--:|--:|
| pinned `v0.1.13.post1` | 0.9522 | 0.9515 |


## Related work
The only related work is the long-stale draft **#27652** ("Add block scaled
bpreshuffle gemm"), which adds a *generic* `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle` op but
no DSv4 application and no matched transposed-scale quant. This PR is the DSv4
attention integration plus the partner quant op

## Notes
- **AI assistance (Claude) was used** for the code-structure refactor, the
  verification runs, and this description; every changed line was reviewed by the
  submitter.

title: [ROCm][Perf][Bugfix] DSv4 indexer: use platform FP8 dtype (fnuz) for Q-quant on gfx942
body:
## Motivation

On gfx942 the DeepSeek-V4 Flash indexer quantizes Q and K to different FP8 types. K already uses the platform type (e4m3fnuz on gfx942, via current_platform.fp8_dtype()), but the fused RoPE+quant kernel in fused_indexer_q.py hardcodes Q to e4m3fn. The FP8 logits kernel then gets fnuz K with fn Q and falls back to a mixed-dtype path on every call. This change derives Q's type from current_platform.fp8_dtype() as well, so on gfx942 both are fnuz and the logits kernel runs its native fnuz/fnuz path.

This is gfx942-specific by design. is_fp8_fnuz() is true only for gfx94x, so on gfx950 the platform type is OCP e4m3fn and Q/K are already fn/fn. Nothing changes there, and the NVIDIA cutedsl and MXFP4 paths are untouched (the two new kernel constexprs are defaulted).

The fnuz quant max is set to 224.0 to match get_fp8_min_max() in quant_utils.py, the value the K cache already uses.

## Results

End to end serving of DeepSeek-V4 Flash (TP4, gfx942 / MI300), mean TTFT, prefill-heavy (OSL=27, concurrency 4):
| ISL    | OSL | main (mixed fp8 q=fn / k=fnuz) | This PR (fnuz q/k) | Speedup |
|--------|-----|-------------------------------|--------------------|---------|
| 8,192  | 27  | 3283 ms                       | 1260 ms            | 2.6x    |
| 32,768 | 27  | 39744 ms                      | 5350 ms            | 7.4x    |

Bonus correctness check: the existing kernel test tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_rope_quant.py matches the unfused reference bit for bit on 9 of 10 gfx942 shapes. The one miss is 3 of 8,380,416 values at float32 / 1023 tokens, from fused vs unfused RoPE rounding at FP8 boundaries, not a dtype or scale error.

## Note

The same indexer dtype handling was included in the larger ROCm enablement PRs #41601 and #42033, both stalled on rebase since May. This is a minimal, standalone version of just that fix for the gfx942 path; main as of today still hardcodes Q to e4m3fn.


<details>
<summary>Repro: serve + bench commands (DeepSeek-V4 Flash, TP4, gfx942)</summary>

Serve (4x MI325):

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --max-model-len 132096 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --max-num-seqs 156 \
  --async-scheduling \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --disable-log-stats \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
  
  vllm bench serve --backend vllm \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --host localhost --port 8000 \
  --dataset-name random --ignore-eos --trust-remote-code \
  --seed 5678 \
  --random-input-len 8192 \
  --random-output-len 27 \
  --max-concurrency 4 --num-prompts 12 --num-warmups 4

# 32K ISL: same command with --random-input-len 32768

title: [DSV4] Implement Sequence Parallelism
body:
## Summary

Implement DeepSeek V4 sequence parallelism using the collective path introduced for Kimi K3.

- Move the Kimi K3 SP helpers into a shared model-ops module and use the TP device communicator's optimized `custom_all_gather` and `custom_reduce_scatter`, with the existing generic collectives as fallback.
- Keep token padding, sharding, padding-mask propagation, and output trimming in the DeepSeek V4 model code. This PR does not add an `sp-threshold`, config/CLI plumbing, or model-runner changes.
- Keep MoE/MLP activations sequence-sharded and perform one all-gather/reduce-scatter pair around attention. Shared experts and fused MoE are configured for SP, avoiding redundant FFN collectives.
- Apply the same model-local boundary handling to the target model, MTP, and DSpark paths.
- Give DSpark decoder layers a shared model-local top-k index workspace, matching the target/MTP construction and allowing the FlashMLA path to profile and capture graphs.
- Extend `sp_shard` for token IDs and mHC tensors while padding only the token axis.

SP is selected for PP=1, EP enabled, TP>1, and either DeepGEMM MegaMoE or DP>1, matching the constraints of the recent Kimi K3 implementation.

## Duplicate-work check

Ran:

```text
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "DeepSeek V4 sequence parallel"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "DSV4 SP"
```

No other open PR implements DeepSeek V4 SP. #50656 concerns the Kimi K3 shared-expert SP optimization used as the implementation reference; it does not duplicate this DeepSeek V4 integration. There is no linked issue number to query.

## Tests

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_sequence_parallel.py -q
# 15 passed, 16 warnings in 6.74s

pre-commit run --files \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_sequence_parallel.py \
  vllm/models/common/ops/sequence_parallel.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/dspark.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/mtp.py \
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py \
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/mtp.py
# All applicable hooks passed

git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
# Passed
```

### DeepSeek V4 Flash: TP4 + EP + SP

Hardware: 4x NVIDIA GB200. Flash checkpoint revision: `60d8d70770c6776ff598c94bb586a859a38244f1` (BF16 model dtype, FP8 block-quantized weights).

```bash
HF_HOME=/mnt/lustre/hf-models CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1 .venv/bin/vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --attention_config.use_fp4_indexer_cache=True \
  --port 8011
```

Result:

- Loaded successfully at 38.87 GiB/rank and captured both PIECEWISE and FULL CUDA graphs.
- Used the checkpoint's native maximum model length of 1,048,576 tokens; no `--max-model-len` override was supplied.
- Runtime logged `Using the MNNVL Lamport all-gather kernel` and `Using the MNNVL Lamport reduce-scatter kernel`, confirming the optimized collectives.
- A one-token prompt completed successfully, exercising model-local padding at TP=4.
- No server errors occurred during valid requests.

### Full GSM8K evaluation

Both evaluations used all 1,319 GSM8K test examples, five-shot prompting, deterministic decoding (`do_sample=False`, `temperature=0.0`), no `--limit`, and `max_length=1048576` to match the checkpoint's native context length.

| Model | Flexible exact match | Strict exact match | Harness time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `DeepSeek-V4-Flash` | 0.9492 ± 0.0060 | 0.9500 ± 0.0060 | 283.4 s |
| `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark` | 0.9522 ± 0.0059 | 0.9522 ± 0.0059 | 131.5 s |

Baseline evaluation:

```bash
.venv/bin/lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args "model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8011/v1/completions,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None,num_concurrent=128,timeout=5000,max_length=1048576" \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 \
  --output_path /tmp/dsv4-sp-gsm8k-full-native
```

DSpark checkpoint revision: `62af8fffb2f7030cac4de2f0169f5b8d1101b646`. The DSpark server used five draft tokens (`dspark_block_size=5`) and `--max-num-seqs 128` so target-plus-draft slots fit the 4,096-token scheduler budget:

```bash
HF_HOME=/mnt/lustre/hf-models CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1 .venv/bin/vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --attention_config.use_fp4_indexer_cache=True \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
  --port 8011

.venv/bin/lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args "model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8011/v1/completions,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None,num_concurrent=128,timeout=5000,max_length=1048576" \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 \
  --output_path /tmp/dsv4-dspark-sp-gsm8k-full-native
```

The DSpark run loaded all 96 draft parameters, captured target PIECEWISE/FULL and DSpark FULL CUDA graphs, and completed without request failures. Steady-state draft acceptance was approximately 64-67%, with mean accepted lengths around 4.2-4.4 tokens.

The installed external `deep_ep` and `deep_gemm` wheels emitted PyTorch ABI undefined-symbol warnings. The vendored DeepGEMM fallback initialized and served successfully; DeepEP was not selected in these runs.

## AI assistance

Developed with assistance from OpenAI Codex. I reviewed every changed line, understand the implementation and testing limitations, and take responsibility for the change.

title: PD disagg with Mooncake Connector: GDN support (Qwen3.5) and MLA support (Deepseek-V4-Flash)
body:
## Purpose

Mooncake P/D disaggregation did not work correctly for hybrid KV-cache models such as Qwen3.5, where one model has both full-attention KV cache groups and GDN state groups represented as `MambaSpec`. Nixl now has supported GDN pd disagg here https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41869, but mooncake connector lacks this implementation.

The previous Mooncake path treated request block IDs and registered cache regions too much like a single homogeneous KV cache. That breaks hybrid models because:

- full-attention KV pages and GDN/Mamba state slots have different block semantics;
- HMA returns per-KV-cache-group block IDs, but Mooncake flattened/reused them across regions;
- FA logical blocks may need expansion to physical kernel blocks, while GDN/Mamba state blocks should stay in state-slot space;
- blocks-first FA regions may need K/V splitting, while GDN state regions must stay whole;
- remote decode for MambaSpec-style state needs the N-1 prompt boundary so decode recomputes the last prompt token locally.

## Related PRs / Issues

- [#39482](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39482): initial Mooncake hybrid attention support for Qwen3.5. This PR builds on that direction and includes a coauthor trailer for the PR author.
- [#41869](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41869): NIXL P/D disaggregation support for Qwen3.5 GDN. This PR brings the corresponding direct MooncakeConnector path closer to that validated NIXL behavior.
- [#44456](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44456): broader KV-cache layout refactor around Mamba cache standardization; related but not the same request-level Mooncake P/D transfer fix.
- [#46334](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46334): Mooncake logical/physical block-ratio handling; related to physical block mapping, but this PR handles hybrid FA + GDN group semantics.
- [#46004](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46004): Mooncake shared KV metadata for DeepSeek V4 PP/PD; related Mooncake region metadata work, but for a different model/topology.

## What This PR Changes

This PR turns direct `MooncakeConnector` from a homogeneous KV-page transfer path into a cache-spec-aware transfer path for Qwen3.5-style hybrid FA + GDN models.

First, the worker no longer assumes that the first layer's attention backend represents the whole model. Qwen3.5 can expose GDN as the first backend, and treating that backend as ordinary attention reaches `GDNAttentionBackend.get_kv_cache_shape()`, which is not implemented. **The connector now resolves all current attention backends and initializes `TransferTopology` with `is_mamba=kv_cache_config.has_mamba_layers`.**

Second, memory registration is separated from transfer-region metadata. Mooncake still registers each shared backing allocation only once, but it preserves every logical transfer region, **including FA and GDN regions that share the same base allocation under HMA**. This removes the old assumption that all cache views have the same block dimension: FA regions can be physical/kernel-block based while GDN state regions stay in logical state-slot space.

Third, request transfer planning keeps KV-cache group identity all the way to descriptor construction. Full-attention regions consume full-attention group block IDs, GDN/MambaSpec regions consume their own group block IDs, and null placeholder blocks from aligned MambaSpec state groups are skipped instead of transferred as real state.

Finally, logical-to-physical block handling is applied only where it is valid. Attention group block IDs are expanded to kernel/physical block IDs when the logical block size differs from the selected kernel block size, while GDN/MambaSpec state groups are not expanded because their block IDs represent recurrent state slots rather than per-token KV pages. 

The scheduler path also mirrors the MambaSpec N-1 boundary used by NIXL because the P/D transfer path transfers KV/state, not the logits for the final prompt token. For a prompt with tokens `[t0, ..., tN-1]`, the prefiller therefore transfers recurrent state after processing through `tN-2`, and the decoder recomputes `tN-1` locally before generating the first output token. This lets the decode side obtain the logits for `tN-1` and advance local recurrent state consistently. If the prefiller instead transferred state after `tN-1`, the decoder would have the state needed to continue decoding but would still miss the logits needed to sample the first generated token unless logits were transferred as another cross-node artifact.

## Evaluation

GSM8K evaluation settings:

```text
configs: 1p1d, 2p2d, 4p4d, 4p1d, 1p4d
connector: mooncake or nixl
model: Qwen3.5-0.8B
tp_per_instance: 1
num_questions: 1319
num_shots: 5
max_tokens: 256
max_model_len: 4096
concurrency: 256
```

Mooncake runs used `--mooncake-protocol rdma`.

## Test Results

Qwen3.5-0.8B, GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot, `max_tokens=256`, `concurrency=256`:

title: [ROCm][DSv3.2][Perf] Cap sparse MLA decode KV-splits with a work-per-split heuristic
body: # [ROCm][DSv3.2][Perf] Cap sparse MLA decode KV-splits with a work-per-split heuristic The ROCm aiter sparse-MLA decode backend calls `get_mla_metadata_v1` without `max_split_per_batch`, so aiter defaults to `-1` and splits the decode reduction across every CU (304 on gfx942). The reduce only covers the selected tokens per row (`<= index_topk`), so for `topk=2048` that's ~7 tokens/split — the reduce kernel ends up dominated by launch and combine overhead. This computes `max_split_per_batch` from a small heuristic instead, following `triton_mla.py`: aim for a minimum work per split, round to a power of two, and cap by the CU count. It's sparse-MLA only and TP-invariant, and numerics are unchanged (partials recombine via LSE). At higher concurrency aiter's device cap `min(num_clusters, max_split * num_batches)` converges back to the old all-CU behavior, so the cap only helps the low-batch / long-context case. ## Results (gfx942 / MI325X, DeepSeek-V3.2, TP8) Decode reduce kernel `kn_mla_reduce_v1_ps` (torch profiler, 187,941 calls): | | Baseline (`-1`) | Heuristic | Δ | |--|----------------:|----------:|--:| | CUDA avg | 22.136 µs | 5.387 µs | −75.7% | | CUDA total | 4.160 s | 1.013 s | −75.6% | Before: After: End-to-end serving (1k ISL / 100 OSL, concurrency 4): | Metric | Baseline (`-1`) | Heuristic | Δ | |--------|----------------:|----------:|--:| | Mean TPOT (ms) | 13.41 | 13.18 | −1.7% | | Output throughput (tok/s) | 253.72 | 264.67 | +4.3% | | Total throughput (tok/s) | 2790.97 | 2911.40 | +4.3% | The serving gain is modest here because the reduce is a small slice of a short-context step; long-context decode recovers a larger share. GSM8K is unchanged within noise: | Config | 5-shot flexible | 5-shot strict | 20-shot flexible | 20-shot strict | |--------|----------------:|--------------:|-----------------:|---------------:| | Baseline | 0.9196 | 0.8787 | 0.9492 | 0.9462 | | Heuristic | 0.9166 | 0.8802 | 0.9500 | 0.9477 |

title: [Bugfix] Capture final-layer aux hidden state in deepseek_v2 backbone
body:
## Purpose
The `deepseek_v2` backbone captures EAGLE3 / `extract_hidden_states` aux hidden states only at decoder-layer *inputs* (ids `0..num_hidden_layers-1`), so an aux id equal to `num_hidden_layers` — the final layer's output — is silently dropped, returning one fewer hidden state than configured. This makes deepseek_v2-family models (DeepSeek V2/V3, GLM-MoE, Kimi, …) unusable as aux-hidden-state targets whenever the final-layer state is requested.

This captures the final layer's output as well, mirroring the `llama` backbone. It is a no-op when no aux hidden-state layers are set, so normal inference is unaffected.

## Test
With a deepseek_v2-family target (GLM-MoE) and `eagle_aux_hidden_state_layer_ids` that include the final layer, the model previously returned N-1 hidden states (RuntimeError on the consumer's fixed-size buffer). With this change it returns all N requested aux hidden states.

title: [Spec][V2] Support MTP speculative decoding under pipeline parallelism
body:
## Purpose

MTP speculative decoding does not work under pipeline parallelism on the V2 model runner. #50514
landed the generic PP spec-decode transport; this PR covers the MTP-specific gaps that remain on
the PP>1 path.

**Depends on #55745** — a one-line `record_stream` guard in #50514's `broadcast_drafts`, without
which this path trips a device-side `IndexKernel` assert under async launches. It is the bottom
commit here and can be dropped once #55745 merges.

**1. MTP drafters do not implement `SupportsPP`.** The engine refuses to build the draft at all:
```
NotImplementedError: Pipeline parallelism is not supported for this model.
Supported models implement the `SupportsPP` interface.   [DeepSeekMTPModel]
```
The draft runs only on the last PP stage, so it never consumes PP intermediate tensors, but the
interface still requires the `make_empty_intermediate_tensors` factory. Applied to `DeepSeekMTP`
and `Qwen3_5MTP`. Mirrors #39704 for the V1 runner.

**2. Qwen3.5/3.6 MTP draft head skips its `fc` projection.** It branched on `is_first_rank`, which
is False on the last PP stage where the drafter is built. The head then fell through to the
intermediate-tensor path with nothing to read (~1% acceptance). Now branches on
`intermediate_tensors is None`, which is equivalent for a pipelined module and correct for a
whole-drafter-on-one-rank module. @hackxixi suggested this as the general rule for draft heads.

**3. DeepSeek MTP does not load its own `embed_tokens`.** A checkpoint storing it as one top-level
tied weight has no spec layer to rewrite from. The loader dropped it, and the draft embedded with
uninitialised weights. Under PP the target's copy is a `PPMissingLayer` on the draft's stage, so it
cannot borrow the target's. Per-spec-layer checkpoints are unaffected.

**4. `DeepseekV32MTP` carries neither of the above.** It was forked out of `DeepSeekMTP` after this
branch first added `SupportsPP`, and took neither that nor the `embed_tokens` load.
`speculative.py` routes `deepseek_v32` and `glm_moe_dsa` there, so this is the GLM-5.2 and
DeepSeek-V3.2 path. Missing `SupportsPP` raises the error above; the missing `embed_tokens` load is
silent — the engine serves correct output, because rejected drafts are discarded, and only
acceptance shows it: 32.69% against 93.51% once the weight loads. Both restored on the nvidia and
amd variants.

**5. Stale `topk_indices_buffer` in sparse MLA backends.** `LLMBaseProposer.load_model` repoints
the draft's indexers at the target's buffer, but that runs after the backend impls snapshot it in
`__init__`. Its `named_modules()` walk reaches the indexer but not the impls, which are plain
`AttentionImplBase` objects. The impls then read a buffer nothing writes: garbage DSA attention and
degenerate drafts.

A `SharedTopkIndicesBuffer` mixin now resolves the buffer per read, so `forward_mqa` is unchanged
and every `SparseMLACommonImpl` subclass is covered, including `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90`. The
three impls that are not subclasses (`flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm120`, `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse`,
`xpu_mla_sparse`) use the same mixin. An explicit assignment still supersedes the indexer, which is
how skip-topk layers and the proposer's module walk set it. The mixin is in
`sparse_mla_attention.py`, not `v1/attention/backend.py`: every consumer is sparse MLA, and the
four span two bases whose only shared ancestor is `AttentionImplBase`.

`DeepseekV32Model` (nvidia) held the buffer in a local, so the proposer's sharing block never ran
for DSA at all. It is now exposed on the model, as the ROCm variant already does.

**6. Draft MM embedding gather on ranks without an encoder runner.** `ModelState.encoder_runner`
exists only on the first PP rank, so a multimodal-capable MTP drafter died in warmup on the last:
```
AttributeError: 'MambaHybridModelState' object has no attribute 'encoder_runner'
```
Later ranks have no cached embeddings to gather. `Qwen3_5MTP` is the first in-tree draft that is
both `SupportsPP` and `SupportsMultiModal`.

## Not duplicating existing work

- #50514 provides the PP draft-token transport. The earlier revision of this PR carried its own
  version; that is dropped. The only change here to `v1/worker/gpu/pp_utils.py` is #55745's guard.
- #53408, #54635, #55081 (@JasonKeyiL) implement `SupportsPP` on other MTP families; neither
  `deepseek_mtp.py` nor `qwen3_5_mtp.py` is touched by any of them. #55081 overlaps fix 4's
  `SupportsPP` half, which can be dropped if it merges first.
- #54709 (qwen4_exp draft head) is the same bug as fix 2 and takes the same one-liner; left out to
  keep this focused.

## Test Plan

```
