title: [Spec Decode] DSpark
body:
## Purpose Adds support for [DSpark](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark) speculative decoding, using both DeepSeek-V4 DSpark models as well as [DeepSeek-trained Qwen3-DSpark](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_8b_block7) models. ## Design DSpark uses non-causal sliding-window attention. To implement this, instead of manually reimplementing the MLA attention, we instead utilize the existing SparseMLA backends with an expanded topk size, in which the queries all include _each other_ in their topk indices, independent of causality. This implements exactly-correct attention with respect to causality (see test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py) while also minimizing changes to the KV cache utilities and allowing reuse of existing, efficient sparse attention kernels. For CUDA Graphs, we capture the full DFlash backbone and autoregressive sampling loop in a single graph. This decreases host and kernel launch overhead. ## Testing I ran GSM8k at high concurrency, with and without prefix caching (and num_fewshot high enough to trigger prefix cache hits), and got good scores with DSV4-Pro + DSpark. I ran multiple categories of SPEED-Bench at BS32 + BS8 + BS1, with and without thinking enabled, with CUDA graphs + prefix caching enabled. Performance is strong: At BS1 with 7 draft tokens, the verification is ~11-13ms, DFlash backbone is 0.6ms, and autoregressive sampling is another ~0.6ms. E2E step time on 8xB300 is ~14ms; with ALs of ~5, that works out to >350 TPS (observed on speed-bench coding + no-thinking). May improve further once probabilistic drafting stabilizes (see below). Comprehensive evaluation and detailed benchmarking to follow. ### Example Commands
Launch commands

```bash vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --speculative_config '{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 7, "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic"}' vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --speculative_config '{"method":"dspark","model":"deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_8b_block7","num_speculative_tokens":7, "attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN", "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic"}' ```

Benchmark Commands

```bash vllm bench serve --dataset-name speed_bench --dataset-path . --speed-bench-category "coding" --num-prompts -1 --save-result --save-detailed --disable-shuffle --max-concurrency 32 --temperature 1.0 --speed-bench-output-len 2048 --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --skip-chat-template vllm bench serve --dataset-name speed_bench --dataset-path . --speed-bench-category "roleplay" --num-prompts -1 --save-result --save-detailed --disable-shuffle --max-concurrency 32 --temperature 1.0 --speed-bench-output-len 2048 --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --skip-chat-template vllm bench serve --dataset-name speed_bench --dataset-path . --speed-bench-category "coding" --num-prompts -1 --save-result --save-detailed --disable-shuffle --max-concurrency 32 --temperature 1.0 --speed-bench-output-len 2048 --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --skip-chat-template --extra-body '{"chat_template_kwargs":{"thinking":"true"}}' vllm bench serve --dataset-name speed_bench --dataset-path . --speed-bench-category "roleplay" --num-prompts -1 --save-result --save-detailed --disable-shuffle --max-concurrency 32 --temperature 1.0 --speed-bench-output-len 2048 --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --skip-chat-template --extra-body '{"chat_template_kwargs":{"thinking":"true"}}' python3 vllm/tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-shots 5 python3 vllm/tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-shots 50 ```

### Acceptance Rates Measured using `vllm bench serve`, Thinking ON, see above commands. Both using probabilistic acceptance. Max output len 4096.
DSV4-Pro-DSpark v.s. MTP Acceptance Rates

| Category | DL 1 | DL 2 | DL 3 | DL 4 | DL 5 | DL 6 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Coding | 1.87 / 1.89 (0.99x) | 2.55 / 2.45 (1.04x) | 3.07 / 2.66 (1.15x) | 3.42 / 2.72 (1.26x) | 3.74 / 2.75 (1.36x) | 3.90 / 2.75 (1.42x) | | Humanities | 1.80 / 1.84 (0.97x) | 2.36 / 2.32 (1.02x) | 2.73 / 2.50 (1.09x) | 2.99 / 2.54 (1.18x) | 3.11 / 2.56 (1.22x) | 3.17 / 2.56 (1.24x) | | Math | 1.85 / 1.87 (0.99x) | 2.51 / 2.42 (1.04x) | 2.99 / 2.63 (1.14x) | 3.34 / 2.72 (1.23x) | 3.58 / 2.75 (1.30x) | 3.68 / 2.73 (1.35x) | | Multilingual | 1.86 / 1.90 (0.98x) | 2.54 / 2.42 (1.05x) | 3.05 / 2.58 (1.18x) | 3.47 / 2.63 (1.32x) | 3.63 / 2.63 (1.38x) | 3.66 / 2.61 (1.40x) | | QA | 1.80 / 1.85 (0.98x) | 2.37 / 2.35 (1.01x) | 2.74 / 2.54 (1.08x) | 3.01 / 2.57 (1.17x) | 3.21 / 2.61 (1.23x) | 3.20 / 2.58 (1.24x) | | RAG | 1.88 / 1.90 (0.99x) | 2.60 / 2.47 (1.05x) | 3.16 / 2.72 (1.17x) | 3.59 / 2.78 (1.29x) | 3.86 / 2.78 (1.39x) | 3.91 / 2.80 (1.40x) | | Reasoning | 1.85 / 1.88 (0.98x) | 2.51 / 2.43 (1.03x) | 2.99 / 2.66 (1.13x) | 3.35 / 2.73 (1.23x) | 3.56 / 2.74 (1.30x) | 3.68 / 2.74 (1.34x) | | Roleplay | 1.72 / 1.76 (0.98x) | 2.15 / 2.15 (1.00x) | 2.44 / 2.26 (1.08x) | 2.58 / 2.29 (1.13x) | 2.66 / 2.28 (1.17x) | 2.67 / 2.28 (1.17x) | | Stem | 1.82 / 1.85 (0.98x) | 2.44 / 2.36 (1.04x) | 2.85 / 2.54 (1.12x) | 3.14 / 2.60 (1.20x) | 3.28 / 2.61 (1.26x) | 3.41 / 2.61 (1.31x) | | Summarization | 1.83 / 1.87 (0.98x) | 2.48 / 2.41 (1.03x) | 2.93 / 2.60 (1.13x) | 3.24 / 2.62 (1.24x) | 3.34 / 2.60 (1.28x) | 3.50 / 2.62 (1.34x) | | Writing | 1.74 / 1.79 (0.97x) | 2.23 / 2.18 (1.02x) | 2.50 / 2.31 (1.08x) | 2.69 / 2.34 (1.15x) | 2.80 / 2.33 (1.20x) | 2.82 / 2.34 (1.21x) | | **Average** | 1.82 / 1.86 (0.98x) | 2.43 / 2.36 (1.03x) | 2.86 / 2.55 (1.12x) | 3.16 / 2.59 (1.22x) | 3.34 / 2.60 (1.28x) | 3.42 / 2.60 (1.31x) |

### Performance Disclaimers: - Only TP, no EP or DP. So high-end is not accurate (bs >= 64 tend to use DP) - Only 8 gpus, so y-axis is normalized a bit unfairly - Forced AL per-method + per-draft-length, calibrated on speed-bench category average, thinking on, temp 1. See above. - DSpark vs MTP gap at BS1 widens approx +7% if using coding-category ALs. And even more if using thinking-off and/or low temperature. - No dynamic scheduling (see below) ## Known Issues - ~Probabilistic drafting runs but leads to correctness issues; the completions slowly degrade into junk/loops and acceptance rates are inflated. I suspect a subtle issue with how we are running rejection sampling. For whatever reason, GSM8k still passes -- more comprehensive evaluation is needed for final verification.~ - - ~Lead: looking into NaN sanitization as a few ops have some dummy torch.empty inputs that might be corrupting the draft logits.~ - - ~Lead: Seems like DSV4-Pro + MTP + Probabilistic is also giving some bad outputs. Dense-model scenario seems to work fine with DSpark + Probabilistic. Investigating.~ - - Solved, two bugs. d0d2c854443729af4eea364b491d01e434791393 and 54b454fa99e15f96155f0995756216341f22fb10 - ~Dense-model (Qwen3) DSpark is having some IMA when using CUDA graphs. I likely missed a buffer somewhere, and will debug promptly~ seems fixed by rebasing to latest main and using FLASH_ATTN backend. Further evals ongoing ## Scope - dynamic drafting and confidence-based scheduling are out-of-scope for this PR. Track DSD here: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45953, and we will unify with DSpark in a follow-up work - Gemma4-DSpark is left for follow-up as it has its own arch (cannot reuse the Qwen3 DFlash) and I'm not sure we'll want to support it just for DeepSeek's checkpoint. It'll probably be easier just to train a DSpark for the Qwen3 arch and reuse the current implementation.

title: [ROCm] Enable DeepSeek-V4 on gfx11
body:
## Purpose

This PR enables DeepSeek-V4 checkpoints on ROCm gfx11/RDNA devices.

It removes Python-side blockers in the ROCm sparse-indexer path and allows DeepSeek-V4 checkpoints mapped to `INCConfig` to pass ROCm platform validation:

- Register ROCm sparse-indexer ops on gfx11.
- Let `SparseAttnIndexer.forward_hip()` delegate to the ROCm sparse-indexer custom op and use the op-level fallback instead of failing early on platform capability checks.
- Add `inc` to `RocmPlatform.supported_quantization` so the checkpoint passes ROCm validation.

## Test Plan

The validation checkpoint is:

```text
Intel/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-W4A16-AutoRound
```

Manual validation on ROCm gfx11/RDNA:

1. Build the branch for ROCm gfx1100:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm \
PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1100 \
python setup.py build_ext --inplace
```

2. Serve the model with fp8 KV cache:

```bash
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
	--model Intel/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-W4A16-AutoRound \
	--served-model-name dsv4-w7900d \
	--tensor-parallel-size 8 \
	--dtype bfloat16 \
	--kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
	--trust-remote-code
```

For gfx1100 validation, the following Triton workaround was used:

```bash
export AMDGCN_USE_BUFFER_OPS=0
```

Without it, Triton 3.6.0's AMD backend fails compiling the DeepSeek-V4 `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm` Triton kernel with `TritonAMDGPUCanonicalizePointers / make_ttgir: PassManager::run failed`.

## Test Result

Manual validation passed on:

- 2x Strix Halo / Radeon 8060S / gfx1151 with `TP=2 + EP=2`.
- 8x Radeon PRO W7900D / gfx1100 with `TP=8` and source-built ROCm extensions.

Validation covered:

- DeepSeek-V4 model load.
- OpenAI-compatible serving startup.
- `/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions` smoke tests.
- Concurrent decode benchmark.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Track allocated block IDs when num_external_tokens is 0
body:
Fixes #46951.
 
  update_state_after_alloc() returns early when num_external_tokens == 0 without recording allocated block IDs in _current_batch_allocated_block_ids.
  Blocks allocated by other async connectors (via MultiConnector) are invisible to re-allocation detection — pending store jobs won't be flushed if those blocks are reused.

  Fix: record block IDs before the early return, matching the same pattern already used later in this function and in _update_req_states().

title: [Spec Decode][DSpark] Add Gemma4-12B DSpark draft model
body:
## Summary

Adds **DSpark** (semi-autoregressive block speculative decoding, built on #46995) for **Gemma4-12B**, for the `deepseek-ai/dspark_gemma4_12b_block7` checkpoint. Following the Laguna DFlash review, this is a **thin subclass reuse** of the existing stacks, not a standalone model.

## Design
- **`Gemma4DSparkModel(DFlashQwen3Model)`** — inherits the fused context-KV precompute. Gemma4's `attention_k_eq_v` is isolated behind the `_build_context_kv_buffers` / `_project_context_kv` hooks: project once through `k_proj` for all layers; **K** gets `k_norm` + RoPE downstream, **V = `v_norm`(same projection)** (no RoPE, no separate `v_proj`). Only `forward` (sandwich norms + `layer_scalar`) and `embed_input_ids` (`sqrt(hidden)` scaling) are overridden.
- **`Gemma4DSparkForCausalLM(Qwen3DSparkForCausalLM)`** — inherits the DSpark speculator contract (Markov head, `combine_hidden_states`, precompute delegation, `compute_logits`); overrides only the self-contained-checkpoint setup + flat weight loader.
- Attention / decoder-layer / MLP reuse the native Gemma4 MTP draft (`Gemma4MTPAttention` / `Gemma4MTPDecoderLayer` / `Gemma4MLP`).

## Changes (5 files, +408)
- `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_dspark.py` (new)
- `registry.py`: register `Gemma4DSparkModel`
- `config/speculative.py`: detect `method=dspark`, normalize `target_layer_ids` / `block_size`
- `tests/models/registry.py`: `Gemma4DSparkModel` example → `test_can_initialize` builds the draft over the base classes (**catches base-class API drift**)
- `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_spec_decode.py`: `test_gemma4_dspark_acceptance` E2E smoke (build + chat + acceptance > 1; `slow_test` + 80 GB gate)

## Usage
```
vllm serve google/gemma-4-12B-it \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"deepseek-ai/dspark_gemma4_12b_block7","num_speculative_tokens":7}'
```

## Validation (1x H100, TP=1)

**E2E** (`test_gemma4_dspark_acceptance`): coherent generation ("The capital of the United Kingdom is London.", a correct `square_number` function) and DSpark drafting confirmed (acceptance length > 1).

**Speed** (single-stream, 256 tokens, greedy):

| | tok/s | speedup |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (spec-off) | 78.9 | 1.00x |
| **DSpark** | **327.5** | **4.15x** |

Mean acceptance length ~3.06 (GSM8K) / ~5 (open-ended). At high batch the speedup narrows toward the compute-bound target, as expected.

**Quality - no drop** (spec-on vs spec-off):

| benchmark | baseline | DSpark |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K (n=200) | 93.0% | 93.5% |
| MMLU (n=250) | 78.4% | 78.4% |
| HumanEval (164) | 94.5% | 95.1% |

Serving note: vocab is 262144, so the rejection sampler's fp32 logits buffer is large - run with e.g. `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.8` for headroom.

title: [ROCm][MiniMax-M3] Cross-layer lightning-indexer top-k sharing
body:
## Summary
Adds opt-in **cross-layer sharing** of the lightning-indexer top-k block selection for MiniMax-M3 sparse attention. When `use_index_cache` is set, only 1 of every `index_topk_freq` sparse-attention layers recomputes the indexer score + top-k selection; the rest reuse the selection the preceding compute layer wrote into the shared `topk_indices_buffer` in the same forward pass.

Adjacent sparse layers select nearly the same blocks, so this cuts the indexer score/top-k cost ~`freq`× with negligible accuracy impact. `self.skip_index_topk` is computed once per layer at construction (static → cudagraph-capture-safe).

**Disabled by default.** Enable via:
```
--hf-overrides '{"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": 4}'
```

## Why this isn't a duplicate
Searched open PRs for MiniMax-M3 index/top-k/index_topk_freq — no PR adds cross-layer indexer top-k sharing. Related M3 ROCm PRs (#46419 AITER MoE, #46474/#46545 shared-expert fusion) touch different paths.

## Test plan / results
`amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4`, MI355X (gfx950), TP=4, 8k1k:
- **Accuracy** — GSM8K (lm_eval, 5-shot, full 1319Q): **0.9515 flex / 0.9522 strict**, unchanged vs the recompute-every-layer baseline (index cache off).
- **Perf** — Mean TPOT ~**−10%** at conc=1, ~**−4%** at high concurrency (official 8k1k sweep, `index_topk_freq=4`).
- `python -m py_compile` on the changed file passes; no lines >88 chars.

## Notes
- Scope: `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/model.py` only. The NVIDIA twin (`nvidia/model.py`) can take the same change as a follow-up.
- Fully backward compatible (no-op unless `use_index_cache` is enabled).

AI assistance (Claude) was used to develop and validate this change; a human reviewed every line.

This is also a precursor to a masked MHA implementation (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/34744), which will enable speedups at `seq_len > topk`. ## Test Plan ### Layer-level benchmark `python benchmarks/attention_benchmarks/benchmark.py --config benchmarks/attention_benchmarks/configs/mla_sparse_mha_vs_mqa.yaml` ### e2e benchmark ``` vllm bench serve \ --backend vllm \ --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 \ --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 1536 \ --random-range-ratio 0.333 \ --random-output-len 500 \ --random-prefix-len 0 \ --num-prompts 2000 \ --request-rate inf \ --ignore-eos \ --seed 12345 \ --save-result --result-filename result.json ``` Verify correctness with CI ## title: [ROCm] Synchronize sparse MLA metadata before graph replay
body:
Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47196

## Summary

This patch orders ROCm AITER sparse MLA persistent metadata updates before graph replay consumes those metadata buffers.

The sparse MLA backend precomputes persistent metadata with `get_mla_metadata_v1()`. The resulting buffers are later passed to the AITER sparse MLA decode kernel. When CUDA graph replay consumes those persistent buffers, the metadata write must be ordered before the graph-captured decode work. Without that ordering, replay can observe stale or partially updated metadata.

This change synchronizes the current stream after metadata recomputation. The sync is only executed when `metadata_key` changes and `get_mla_metadata_v1()` is launched; the metadata cache-hit path is unchanged.

## Scope

- Limited to the ROCm AITER sparse MLA backend.
- Does not affect other attention backends.
- Does not change public APIs or model configuration.

## Testing

```bash
python -m ruff check --no-cache \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py

python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py -q
```

Result:

```text
All checks passed
1 passed
```

Manual ROCm validation was also run on 4 GPUs with a targeted metadata ordering reproducer using the real `ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadataBuilder.build()` path. The pre-sync variant can expose poisoned metadata to a graph-replay-like consumer, while the synchronized variant observes the valid metadata on all four ranks.

```text
baseline: observed=[-777], buffer=[12345]
fixed:    observed=[12345], buffer=[12345]
issue47196_sparse_mla_metadata_race_repro: PASS
```

I also validated a reduced GLM-5.1-FP8 serving configuration on 4 GPUs with ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE, MTP speculative decode, FP8 KV cache, and CUDA graph capture enabled. The original issue configuration with `max_model_len=200000` could not be fully reproduced on 4 GPUs because it OOMs before serving.

title: [ROCm] Enable DeepSeek-V4 DSpark speculative decoding on AMD (MI350X / MI355X, gfx950)
body:
## Summary

DSpark speculative decoding for **DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1.6T)** was previously **NVIDIA-only** in vLLM:
`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/__init__.py` sets `DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM = None` on ROCm, so
`--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark",...}'` fails at model-load time on AMD GPUs.

This PR enables DSpark on ROCm by porting the draft model to the AMD subpackage and wiring the two
pieces the draft depends on that were missing on the AMD path (the EAGLE3 aux-hidden-state interface
on the target model, and the non-causal sliding-window-attention ragged-buffer sizing). The base
DeepSeek-V4 model, the ROCm sparse-MLA / sparse-SWA backends, and the MHC
`aiter`/`triton` kernels already existed on ROCm — DSpark reuses all of them, so this is a wiring
port, not new kernel work.

Model: [`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark)

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/__init__.py` | Un-stub the ROCm branch: import `DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM` from `.amd.dspark` instead of setting it to `None`. |
| `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/dspark.py` *(new)* | ROCm port of `nvidia/dspark.py`: imports the AMD `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer`, routes the MHC head through the `HCHeadOp` / `MHCPostOp` CustomOp dispatchers (aiter/tilelang/triton) instead of the NVIDIA-only tilelang kernels, gates the trailing `mhc_post` on `use_fused_mhc`, and drops the mega-MoE weight path (absent in `amd/model.py`). |
| `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py` | Add the EAGLE3 aux-hidden-state interface (`EagleModelMixin` on the inner model, `SupportsEagle3` on `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`) and collect mean-pooled aux hidden states at the DSpark target layers in `forward`. DSpark consumes target layers `dspark_target_layer_ids = [58, 59, 60]`; this is the same mechanism EAGLE3/DFlash use to hand intermediate hidden states to a draft model. |
| `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/rocm.py` | Size the ROCm sparse-SWA ragged buffer for the non-causal (DSpark draft) index width. See below. |
| `vllm/config/speculative.py` | Reject `num_speculative_tokens < dspark_block_size` for `method="dspark"` with a clear error (DSpark is a semi-autoregressive block drafter, so sub-block speculative lengths are unsupported). |
| `tests/models/test_registry.py` | `DSparkDraftModel` is now supported on ROCm too; the registry-import test previously skipped it on all non-CUDA platforms. Skip only on platforms where it is still stubbed (i.e. not CUDA and not ROCm). |

### Why the sparse-SWA ragged-buffer change is required

`DeepseekV4ROCMAiterSparseSWAMetadataBuilder` allocated its persistent ragged index buffer for the
**causal** window width only (`max_tokens * window_size`) and passed `window_size` as the
max-entries-per-row to `_copy_ragged_to_graph_buffers`. DSpark's **non-causal** draft widens each
token's SWA index list to `noncausal_index_width = cdiv(window_size + num_speculative_tokens, 128) * 128`,
so the actual `nnz` overflows the buffer and crashes with e.g. `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a
(896) must match the size of tensor b (1792) at non-singleton dimension 0`.

The non-causal path was never exercised on ROCm before (its only user, DSpark, was stubbed), which is
why this was latent. The fix is backward-compatible: for the non-DSpark/causal path
`noncausal_index_width == 0`, so `max(window_size, noncausal_index_width) == window_size` and
`base.decode_swa_indices.shape[-1] == window_size` — i.e. a no-op for the existing base path, and
correct for DSpark.

## Results (8× AMD MI350X, gfx950)

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-09663abde0f50944a8d5ea30120666024b503faa` (vLLM `0.23.1rc1.dev714+g09663abde`)
- Recipe: InferenceX `dsv4-fp4-mi355x-vllm` (TP=8, `--moe-backend aiter`, FP8 KV cache, full CUDA graph `mode:3 FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`)
- Workload: `ISL/OSL = 1024/1024`, `--ignore-eos` (fixed 1024 output tokens/request), greedy
- The DeepSeek-V4-Pro checkpoint is mixed precision: FP4 (MXFP4) MoE experts + FP8 block-scaled dense/attention + FP8 (`fp8_ds_mla`) KV cache.

### Throughput @ concurrency = 8

| Config | Output tok/s **per GPU** | TPOT (ms) | Speedup vs baseline | Mean acceptance length | Avg draft acceptance | Per-position acceptance |
|--------|--------------------------|-----------|---------------------|------------------------|----------------------|-------------------------|
| **STP baseline** (no draft) | 32.6 | 29.7 | 1.00× | — | — | — |
| **DSpark** `num_speculative_tokens=6` | **51.9** | **17.9** | **1.59×** | **2.94** | 32.4% | `0.819 / 0.403 / 0.247 / 0.193 / 0.158 / 0.122` |

TPOT speedup vs baseline: DSpark n=6 = 1.66×.

**Quality:** on a fixed 10-prompt set (raw `/v1/completions`, temperature 0), STP and DSpark n=6
produce matching, correct answers. Re-running the DSpark n=6 config directly from this PR's committed
code reproduces the throughput (~52 tok/s/GPU, within run-to-run variance).

## Reproduction

All commands run inside the ROCm container. Environment: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`.

### 1. Serve

**STP baseline (no speculative decoding):**

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark --port 8000 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 --data-parallel-size 1 \
    --async-scheduling --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --distributed-executor-backend mp \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --trust-remote-code --moe-backend aiter \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}'
```

**DSpark** — add (`num_speculative_tokens=6` was the best-performing value in testing):

```bash
    --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":6,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}'
```

### 2. Benchmark (InferenceX `benchmark_serving.py`)

```bash
# from InferenceX/utils/bench_serving/
python3 benchmark_serving.py \
    --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark --backend vllm \
    --base-url http://0.0.0.0:8000 \
    --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0.8 \
    --num-prompts 80 --max-concurrency 8 \
    --request-rate inf --ignore-eos \
    --num-warmups 16 \
    --percentile-metrics 'ttft,tpot,itl,e2el' \
    --save-result --trust-remote-code
```

- `num-prompts = 10 × max-concurrency`, `num-warmups = 2 × max-concurrency` (InferenceX convention).
- **For the DSpark runs, add `--use-chat-template --dsv4`.** Spec-decode acceptance
  degrades on raw random tokens; the DeepSeek-V4 chat encoding is required for meaningful acceptance
  numbers (matches the InferenceX spec-decoding recipes).
- Output-throughput-per-GPU = `output_throughput / tensor_parallel_size`.

### 3. Acceptance metrics

```bash
curl -s http://0.0.0.0:8000/metrics | grep -E 'spec_decode_num_(drafts_total|draft_tokens_total|accepted_tokens_total|accepted_tokens_per_pos_total)'
```

- Mean acceptance length = `1 + accepted_tokens_total / drafts_total`
- Per-position acceptance rate = `accepted_tokens_per_pos_total[i] / drafts_total`

## Note: known limitation

Greedy DSpark occasionally produces intermittent, prompt/run-dependent garbled output (not tied to a
specific `num_speculative_tokens`). Root-causing this is left as a follow-up.

## Caveats

- Validated on **MI350X**; the InferenceX reference recipe targets **MI355X** (same gfx950 family,
  higher clocks/TDP), so absolute throughput may differ. STP vs DSpark were all measured on
  the same hardware and image, so the relative speedups are directly comparable.
- Measured with the pinned nightly image above; the InferenceX recipe pins `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.22.0`.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Add missing draft_id_to_target_id to DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM
body:
## What this PR does

Fixes #47418

`DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM` is a full-vocab draft model (draft ids are target ids, no d2t remapping). However, `DSparkSpeculator.load_draft_model` accesses `model.draft_id_to_target_id` unconditionally, causing an `AttributeError` when running DeepSeek-V4-Flash with DSpark.

### Root Cause

In `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/speculator.py:86`:
```python
if self.draft_logits is not None and model.draft_id_to_target_id is not None:
```

This line assumes the draft model has a `draft_id_to_target_id` attribute, but `DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM` doesn't define it.

### Fix

Add `draft_id_to_target_id = None` as a class attribute to `DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM`, consistent with:
- The full-vocab identity mapping already implemented in `map_draft_to_target()` (returns draft_ids directly)
- The pattern used in `Qwen3DSparkForCausalLM` (which sets it to `None` when draft_vocab == target_vocab)

### Testing

The fix is minimal and follows the existing pattern. The check `model.draft_id_to_target_id is not None` will now correctly evaluate to `False`, skipping the d2t scatter logic that isn't needed for full-vocab drafts.

title: [Perf] Optimize `fused_topk_bias` for DSv4, 1.5~2x kernel performance improvement
body:
## Purpose

Part of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45861

~Originally when `hash_indices_table` is None we will do a redundant `input_tokens.to(dtype=indices_type)` which can be removed.~

We make the conversion inside the kernel to improve performance

## Test

Acc covered in current unit test

Performance using this AI generated script:

<details>

```py

import torch

from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.router.fused_topk_bias_router import (
    fused_topk_bias,
)


def time_cuda(fn, warmup=20, iters=100):
    for _ in range(warmup):
        fn()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
    end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
    start.record()
    for _ in range(iters):
        fn()
    end.record()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return start.elapsed_time(end) / iters


def main():
    assert torch.cuda.is_available(), "CUDA is required"
    torch.manual_seed(0)

    vocab_size = 163840
    num_experts = 512
    topk = 8
    hidden_size = 1
    dtype = torch.bfloat16
    indices_type = torch.int32
    device = "cuda"

    hash_table_long = torch.randint(
        0, num_experts, (vocab_size, topk), dtype=torch.long, device=device
    )
    hash_table_int = hash_table_long.to(torch.int32)

    def route(hidden_states, gating_output, input_ids, table):
        return fused_topk_bias(
            hidden_states=hidden_states,
            gating_output=gating_output,
            scoring_func="sqrtsoftplus",
            e_score_correction_bias=None,
            topk=topk,
            renormalize=True,
            indices_type=indices_type,
            input_tokens=input_ids,
            hash_indices_table=table,
        )

    def old_python_cast(hidden_states, gating_output, input_ids):
        input_ids = input_ids.to(indices_type)
        table = hash_table_long.to(indices_type)
        return route(hidden_states, gating_output, input_ids, table)

    print("device:", torch.cuda.get_device_name())
    print(
        f"vocab={vocab_size} experts={num_experts} topk={topk} "
        f"table_int64={hash_table_long.numel() * hash_table_long.element_size() / 1e6:.2f}MB"
    )
    print("times are ms/forward")

    for num_tokens in (128, 512, 2048, 8192):
        hidden_states = torch.empty(
            (num_tokens, hidden_size), dtype=dtype, device=device
        )
        gating_output = torch.randn(
            (num_tokens, num_experts), dtype=dtype, device=device
        )
        input_ids_long = torch.randint(
            0, vocab_size, (num_tokens,), dtype=torch.long, device=device
        )
        input_ids_int = input_ids_long.to(torch.int32)

        new_w, new_ids = route(hidden_states, gating_output, input_ids_long,
                               hash_table_long)
        ref_w, ref_ids = route(hidden_states, gating_output, input_ids_int,
                               hash_table_int)
        torch.testing.assert_close(new_ids, ref_ids, atol=0, rtol=0)
        torch.testing.assert_close(new_w, ref_w, atol=2e-2, rtol=1e-2)

        current = time_cuda(
            lambda: route(hidden_states, gating_output, input_ids_long,
                          hash_table_long)
        )
        old = time_cuda(
            lambda: old_python_cast(hidden_states, gating_output, input_ids_long)
        )
        precast = time_cuda(
            lambda: route(hidden_states, gating_output, input_ids_int,
                          hash_table_int)
        )
        print(
            f"M={num_tokens:5d}: current_mixed={current:.4f}  "
            f"old_python_cast={old:.4f}  precast_int32={precast:.4f}  "
            f"speedup={old / current:.2f}x"
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

</details>


And we get

```bash
M=  128: current_mixed=0.0163  old_python_cast=0.0311  precast_int32=0.0157  speedup=1.91x
M=  512: current_mixed=0.0158  old_python_cast=0.0316  precast_int32=0.0159  speedup=2.01x
M= 2048: current_mixed=0.0162  old_python_cast=0.0308  precast_int32=0.0156  speedup=1.91x
M= 8192: current_mixed=0.0195  old_python_cast=0.0313  precast_int32=0.0194  speedup=1.61x
```

title: [Perf] Cache `token_to_req_indices` for dsv4, 5x~6x kernel performance improvement
body:
## Purpose

So we save two additional copy from CPU to GPU

## Test

### Acc

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash   --trust-remote-code   --kv-cache-dtype fp8   --block-size 256   --enable-expert-parallel   --tensor-parallel-size 4   --attention_config.use_fp4_indexer_cache=True   --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe   --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4   --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4   --enable-auto-tool-choice   --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --port9256
```

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions --model_args "base_url=http://127.0.0.1:9256/v1/completions,model=$MODEL,num_concurrent=1024" --tasks gsm8k
|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr|
|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9522|±  |0.0059|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9530|±  |0.0058|
```

### Perf

Running this AI-generated microbenchmark Script

<details>

```py
import gc
import statistics
import time

import numpy as np
import torch

from vllm.utils.torch_utils import np_to_pinned_tensor

WARMUP_ITERS = 100
CASES = [
    ("decode bs32", 32, 1, 0, 5000),
    ("decode bs256", 256, 1, 0, 3000),
    ("decode bs512", 512, 1, 0, 2000),
    ("mixed/short prefill 512 tok", 32, 16, 0, 2000),
    ("prefill 4096 tok", 64, 64, 0, 1000),
    ("prefill 8192 tok + cg pad", 128, 64, 128, 800),
]


def make_query_start_loc(num_reqs: int, query_len: int) -> torch.Tensor:
    query_lens = torch.full((num_reqs,), query_len, dtype=torch.int32)
    query_start_loc = torch.empty(num_reqs + 1, dtype=torch.int32)
    query_start_loc[0] = 0
    torch.cumsum(query_lens, dim=0, out=query_start_loc[1:])
    return query_start_loc


def old_three_builds(
    query_start_loc: torch.Tensor,
    num_reqs: int,
    num_actual_tokens: int,
    buffers: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor],
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Old path: Sparse MLA, SWA, and Compressor each build the mapping."""
    buf_mla, buf_swa, buf_compressor = buffers

    starts = np.asarray(query_start_loc, dtype=np.int32)
    lens_np = np.diff(starts)
    req_id_per_token = np.repeat(np.arange(lens_np.shape[0], dtype=np.int32), lens_np)
    mapped_tokens = req_id_per_token.shape[0]
    buf_mla[:mapped_tokens].copy_(
        np_to_pinned_tensor(req_id_per_token), non_blocking=True
    )
    if mapped_tokens < num_actual_tokens:
        buf_mla[mapped_tokens:num_actual_tokens].zero_()

    query_lens = query_start_loc[1:] - query_start_loc[:-1]
    req_ids = torch.repeat_interleave(torch.arange(num_reqs), query_lens).pin_memory()
    buf_swa[: req_ids.shape[0]].copy_(req_ids, non_blocking=True)

    query_lens = query_start_loc[1:] - query_start_loc[:-1]
    req_ids = torch.repeat_interleave(torch.arange(num_reqs), query_lens).pin_memory()
    buf_compressor[: req_ids.shape[0]].copy_(req_ids, non_blocking=True)

    return (
        buf_mla[:num_actual_tokens],
        buf_swa[: req_ids.shape[0]],
        buf_compressor[: req_ids.shape[0]],
    )


def cached_three_builds(
    query_start_loc: torch.Tensor,
    num_reqs: int,
    num_actual_tokens: int,
    buffers: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor],
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """New path: build once, then reuse cached tensor views."""
    del num_reqs
    buf = buffers[0]

    starts = np.asarray(query_start_loc, dtype=np.int32)
    lens_np = np.diff(starts)
    token_to_req = np.repeat(np.arange(lens_np.shape[0], dtype=np.int32), lens_np)
    mapped_tokens = token_to_req.shape[0]
    buf[:mapped_tokens].copy_(np_to_pinned_tensor(token_to_req), non_blocking=True)
    if mapped_tokens < num_actual_tokens:
        buf[mapped_tokens:num_actual_tokens].zero_()

    cached = buf[: max(mapped_tokens, num_actual_tokens)]
    out = cached[:num_actual_tokens]
    return out, out, out


def bench(
    fn,
    query_start_loc: torch.Tensor,
    num_reqs: int,
    num_actual_tokens: int,
    buffers: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor],
    iters: int,
) -> float:
    gc.disable()
    for _ in range(WARMUP_ITERS):
        fn(query_start_loc, num_reqs, num_actual_tokens, buffers)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()

    samples_ns = []
    for _ in range(iters):
        start_ns = time.perf_counter_ns()
        fn(query_start_loc, num_reqs, num_actual_tokens, buffers)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        samples_ns.append(time.perf_counter_ns() - start_ns)
    gc.enable()
    return statistics.median(samples_ns) / 1e3


def main() -> None:
    assert torch.cuda.is_available(), "This benchmark requires CUDA."
    device = torch.device("cuda")
    print(f"device: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(device)}")
    print(
        f"{'case':<28} {'old_med_us':>11} {'new_med_us':>11} "
        f"{'speedup':>8} {'saved_us':>10}"
    )

    for name, num_reqs, query_len, pad_tokens, iters in CASES:
        query_start_loc = make_query_start_loc(num_reqs, query_len)
        num_actual_tokens = int(query_start_loc[-1].item()) + pad_tokens
        capacity = num_actual_tokens + 16
        buffers = tuple(
            torch.empty(capacity, dtype=torch.int32, device=device) for _ in range(3)
        )

        old_us = bench(
            old_three_builds,
            query_start_loc,
            num_reqs,
            num_actual_tokens,
            buffers,
            iters,
        )
        new_us = bench(
            cached_three_builds,
            query_start_loc,
            num_reqs,
            num_actual_tokens,
            buffers,
            iters,
        )
        print(
            f"{name:<28} {old_us:11.2f} {new_us:11.2f} "
            f"{old_us / new_us:8.2f} {old_us - new_us:10.2f}"
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

And we will get 5x~6x kernel level improvement.

```bash
case                          old_med_us  new_med_us  speedup   saved_us
decode bs32                       194.97       32.73     5.96     162.24
decode bs256                      203.12       33.21     6.12     169.90
decode bs512                      209.25       35.05     5.97     174.20
mixed/short prefill 512 tok       201.54       33.65     5.99     167.89
prefill 4096 tok                  217.79       35.45     6.14     182.34
prefill 8192 tok + cg pad         240.92       46.40     5.19     194.52
```

title: [Bugfix] DSV4 TP16 garbage output
body:
Fixes DeepSeek-V4 garbage output (gsm8k ~0% #47783) with the `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` backend on the packed KV regression from #44577, coauthored by @LucasWilkinson. Remapping is adopted from #47895.

## Problem

#44577 packs a block's KV components (indexer + compressor + SWA) into one contiguous per-block allocation, so a layer's per-block stride becomes the whole block size. The FlashInfer sparse-MLA decode reads the pool by **flat global token id** (`addr = base + slot * token_stride`) and ignores the tensor's block stride, so once a token crosses a block boundary it reads the wrong address -> attention corruption (gsm8k ~95% -> ~0%). FlashMLA is unaffected (it honors the runtime block stride).

## Fix

Keep the packed layout (preserving per-block KV contiguity for KV-transfer / offload) and fix the read side:

1. **Remap sparse indices** so the flat-token kernel lands on the packed address: rewrite each global slot id `block*block_size + off -> block*block_span + off` (`block_span = page_stride / token_stride`). Done inside the existing index-build Triton kernel (`_remap_flashinfer_index` applied at the four slot-id write sites) — **no extra kernel launches**. `block_span` comes from the pool tensor (`_packed_block_span = stride(0) // stride(-2)`; == block_size for the unpacked layout, so this is a no-op there).
2. **Page alignment**: for the FlashInfer backend, align every DSv4 page to the 512 B compressed-KV token stride via the existing `MLAAttentionSpec.alignment` field (`576 if fp8_ds_mla else 512`), so the packed block stride is a multiple of 512 B and `block_span` is an integer. This mirrors the existing "576 B for FlashMLA" precedent and touches no generic KV-cache code.

Both are workarounds until flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3856 (the sparse-MLA kernel gains a real block-stride parameter).

## Relation to existing PRs (not a blind duplicate)

- **#47805** (disable packed KV for FlashInfer): different goal — it drops the packed layout and its contiguity. This PR keeps packing.
- **#47895** (config-side block-stride pad + remap): **same fix, same in-kernel remap.** The only difference is the alignment mechanism — this PR reuses the per-page `alignment` field at spec registration instead of adding a DSv4/FlashInfer-specific pad helper to the generic `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` (this PR leaves core planner code untouched; 5 model-local files). This is offered as the less-intrusive alternative.

## Changes (5 files, +61/-6)

- `models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/cache_utils.py`: `_remap_flashinfer_index` device fn + `swa/compressed_block_span` args to `build_flashinfer_mixed_sparse_indices`.
- `models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py`: `_packed_block_span` + pass the spans.
- `models/deepseek_v4/attention.py`, `compressor.py`, `v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_swa.py`: `alignment = 576 if fp8_ds_mla else 512`.
- No changes to `kv_cache_utils.py`, `backend.py`, `kv_cache_interface.py`.

## Testing

Hardware: GB300 (SM100), DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP16 across 4 nodes, fp8 KV cache, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, spec-decode off.

- **gsm8k** (lm-eval, 5-shot): flexible-extract **0.9492**, strict-match **0.9500** — matches the pre-#44577 baseline (~0.9484) within stderr; HEAD before this fix is ~0.0. Packing stays enabled; no alignment guard fires; KV cache 22.70M tokens (~0.03% below the unpadded layout).
- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py` — 8 passed.
- `pre-commit run` (ruff) and mypy — clean on the touched files.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude) was used to root-cause the regression and prepare this change. A human reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [ROCm] Disable persistent sparse-MLA kernel for chunked-prefill continuations
body:
# [ROCm] Disable persistent sparse-MLA kernel for chunked-prefill continuations

## Summary
Fixes #47042. GLM-4.6/4.5 / DeepSeek-V3.2-style sparse-MLA (DSA) models on ROCm
produce correct output up to ~20K tokens and then collapse into repetition /
garbage at longer contexts.

Root cause: the AITER **persistent MLA work-stealing kernel**
(`get_mla_metadata_v1` + the `work_meta_data` persistent path in
`aiter.mla.mla_decode_fwd`, enabled unconditionally for the sparse-MLA backend
in #41990) is **numerically wrong for multi-token (prefill) batches**. The
per-token error is small in isolation, but chunked prefill runs a request
through several forward passes and the error **compounds** through the KV cache
across passes/layers until long-context decode collapses.

This is why the failure is gated on **chunk count**, not context length:

| max-num-batched-tokens | 20K prompt | chunks | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8192 | 22K tok | 3 | garbage (0/10 needles) |
| 12288 | 22K tok | 2 | correct |
| 21504 | 22K tok | 2 | correct |
| 12288 | 33K tok | 3 | garbage |

The persistent kernel is correct for **pure decode** (`qseqlen==1`) and for
**fresh single-chunk prefills**. This patch gates it on batch shape: it falls
back to the (correct) non-persistent split-KV path whenever any request in the
batch is a chunked-prefill *continuation* — i.e. it has more than one query
token this step *and* part of its context was already computed in an earlier
chunk (`seq_len > query_len`). Decode and single-chunk prefills keep the
persistent performance path, so there is no decode throughput regression.

## Why this is not a duplicate
- #47404 ("Synchronize sparse MLA metadata before graph replay") touches the
  same file but fixes a *different* bug: a stale-metadata race during CUDA-graph
  replay. The bug here is a **numerical correctness** bug in the kernel itself —
  it reproduces with `--enforce-eager` / `-cc.cudagraph_mode=NONE` (no graph
  replay), so metadata-ordering is not involved.
- #41973 / #41990 is the feature that *enabled* the persistent path (the source
  of this regression), not a fix.
- No open PR references #47042.

## Isolated (kernel-only) reproduction
A standalone script (no vLLM/model) builds a sparse-MLA batch, regenerates the
persistent metadata via `get_mla_metadata_v1`, and compares the persistent
kernel and the non-persistent kernel against a torch fp32 reference:

```
N=  1 (decode):        persistent max_relerr=0.000   non-persistent=0.000  -> OK
N=512 (prefill batch): persistent max_relerr=7.15    non-persistent=0.108  -> PERSISTENT WRONG
```

The non-persistent kernel matches the fp32 reference tightly everywhere; the
persistent kernel is correct for decode-shaped batches but produces large
errors for prefill-shaped batches. (The underlying kernel bug is also worth an
AITER-side fix; this PR is the vLLM-side mitigation.)

## Testing (MI355X / gfx950, TP8, GLM-FP8, vLLM nightly + aiter 0.1.16.post2)
Needle-in-a-haystack via raw `/v1/completions`, greedy, `max-num-batched-tokens
8192` (default small chunk), cudagraph/torch.compile **enabled**:

| context | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2K  | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| 20K | **0/10 (garbage)** | 10/10 |
| 40K | garbage | 10/10 |

No accuracy regression on short context:
`lm_eval gsm8k --num_fewshot 20` (concurrency 256): **0.944 flexible / 0.945
strict** exact_match, unchanged vs baseline (decode path is untouched).

## Notes
- Python-only change; behavior differs only on ROCm sparse-MLA (`glm_moe_dsa` /
  DeepSeek-V3.2 indexer) backends.
- AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate and draft this change; a human
  author owns and has validated it.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`
  should be run before submission.

title: [MM][CG] Support ViT full CUDA graph for Idefics3 and SmolVLM

## Purpose

This PR adds ViT encoder CUDA Graph support for Idefics3 / SmolVLM as part of #38175.

Idefics3 computes vision position IDs from the patch attention mask during the encoder forward pass. To make the encoder compatible with CUDA Graph capture, this PR precomputes the position IDs and passes them as fixed graph inputs.

Changes:
- Implement `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` for `Idefics3ForConditionalGeneration`
- Add CUDA Graph capture/replay using `pixel_values`, `pixel_attention_mask`, and `position_ids`
- Expose position-ID computation from `Idefics2VisionEmbeddings`
- Add SmolVLM coverage to `test_vit_cudagraph.py`

I checked #38175 and open PRs and found no existing PR covering Idefics3 / SmolVLM encoder CUDA Graph support.

AI assistance was used for this PR.

title: [Bugfix]Fix DeepSeek-V4 fp8_ds_mla KV cache reshape
body:
Fixes #47648.

DeepSeek-V4 FlashMLA uses a custom `fp8_ds_mla` KV layout with 584 bytes per token. The main MLA and SWA cache specs already carry `cache_dtype_str`, but they did not consistently expose `kv_quant_mode`, and the GPU model runner used the global cache dtype when computing backend KV cache shapes.

As a result, DSpark serving on H200 could allocate/reshape SWA KV cache as the semantic 512-byte head size, then fail in FlashMLA sparse decode with:

```text
RuntimeError: kv must have shape (num_blocks, page_block_size, h_kv, bytes_per_token)
```

This PR propagates `kv_quant_mode` for DeepSeek-V4 MLA/SWA specs and prefers the layer-local `cache_dtype_str` when computing KV cache shapes.

Co-discovered and validated with @yy-fighting.

## Purpose

Fix DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark startup on H200/SM90 with FlashMLA when using `--spec-method dspark` and `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`.

Before this change, the DeepSeek-V4 SWA KV cache could be reshaped as:

```text
swa_shape=(83520, 64, 1, 512)
```

but FlashMLA expects the DeepSeek-V4 `fp8_ds_mla` layout:

```text
swa_shape=(83520, 64, 1, 584)
```

## Test Plan

Tested on 4x H200 with `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark`.

Serve command:

```bash
vllm serve /data0/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --spec-method dspark \
  --spec-model /data0/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark \
  --spec-tokens 5 \
  --port 30004
```

Small serving benchmark:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30004 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model /data0/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 128 \
  --random-output-len 32 \
  --num-prompts 16 \
  --request-rate 4 \
  --max-concurrency 4 \
  --ignore-eos \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
```

## Test Result

Before the fix, startup failed during DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA warmup:

```text
swa_shape=(83520, 64, 1, 512)
RuntimeError: kv must have shape (num_blocks, page_block_size, h_kv, bytes_per_token)
```

After the fix, the cache shape is correct:

```text
swa_shape=(83520, 64, 1, 584)
kv_shape=(83520, 64, 1, 584)   # compress_ratio=4
kv_shape=(83520, 2, 1, 584)    # compress_ratio=128
```

Full startup completed:

```text
DeepGEMM warmup: 100%|...| 1281/1281
Graph capturing finished
/health -> 200
```

```text
Failed requests: 0
Total input tokens: 2048

Request throughput: 1.34 req/s
Output token throughput: 42.99 tok/s
Acceptance rate: 2.56%
```

title: [ROCm][Perf] DSv4 two-stage compressor kernel for HCA prefill
body:
## Purpose
This PR adds a two-stage Triton implementation to the DeepSeek-V4 compressor for the prefill path in head_dim=512, cr>=128 to improve TTFT.

On upstream ROCm, the single pass compressor-norm-rope-cache fusion is dispatched one workgroup per token. In HCA where compress ratio is 128, only workgroups that live on the CR boundary (positions % 128 == 0) execute on 128x512 grids, and the others early exit. During perfill, the number of boundaries per step is `num_prefill_tokens / cr`, and for a 8192-token chunk, that leaves 8192/128=64 CUs in action, leaving most of the CUs unoccupied (e.g. 256 total CUs on MI355).

Following the strategy in CuTeDSL CUDA kernel, this PR breaks this path into two stages/kernels:
- Compress: this is the more compute-demanding stage. Instead of compressing the 128 rows for all heads in one single program, split workloads along the head dimension so that each program computes only a `head_dim / num_splits` slice of the output, and more programs can be spawned to fill the CUs. As the weighted sum is independent for each column, he split is exact and no cross-workgroup reduction is needed.
- Finalize: the remaining norm-rope-cache ops. As the workload is serial but light, this uses the original one-program-per-boundary dispatch strategy.

The number of splits for the first stage is sized to target `num_splits ~= num_CUs / num_cr_boundaries` to saturate the CUs. The two stage split is enabled for prefill whose workloads benefit more from filling the occupancy. In prefill-heavy workloads, this brings ~3-4% reduction in TTFT.


## Test Plan
E2E performance benchmark and lm_eval with gsm8k on MI355X

```

vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
```

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Key sparse-MLA persistent metadata on per-request context lengths
body:
## Purpose

Fixes the sparse-MLA persistent-metadata cache collision behind #47042
(GLM-4.6 / DeepSeek-V3.2-style DSA models on ROCm produce correct output up to
~20K tokens, then collapse into repetition/garbage at longer context).

The ROCm sparse-MLA backend caches the persistent work-stealing metadata and
recomputes it only when `metadata_key` changes. The key was keyed on
`min(seq_lens, topk)`, but the metadata actually depends on the per-token KV
length distribution: a first prefill chunk ramps `1 → topk`, while a
continuation chunk whose context already exceeds `topk` is uniform at `topk`.
Both clamp to the same value, so a prefill spanning ≥3 chunks reuses the first
chunk's work partition for later chunks and corrupts the output, which compounds
across layers and breaks long-context decode.

The persistent kernel itself is correct given correct metadata (see
ROCm/aiter#4076); this is purely a vLLM-side cache-key bug.

## Fix

Add the clamped per-request **context length** and per-request **query lengths**
to `metadata_key` so ramp-vs-uniform chunks no longer collide. Decode
(context ≫ topk) still yields a stable key, so it keeps hitting the cache — no
regression to the persistent perf path.

This supersedes the disable-persistent-for-prefill mitigation in #47567 by
fixing the actual cause and retaining the persistent path for chunked prefill.

## Test

NIAH via raw `/v1/completions` (greedy, cudagraph + compile on), GLM-5.1-FP8,
MI355X / gfx950, TP8:

| context | chunks | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2K  | 1 | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| 30K | 3 | 0/10 (garbage) | 10/10 |
| 40K | 4 | garbage | 9–10/10 |

Reproduces and is fixed on both pinned `aiter 0.1.16.post2` and aiter ToT.
`gsm8k` (lm_eval) unchanged — the decode path is untouched.

title: [Spec Decode] DSpark confidence-scheduled verification
body:
Adaptively sizes the DSpark draft-verification budget from per-request confidence instead of always verifying every drafted token. Motivation: fixed-k speculation collapses at high concurrency — once the GPU saturates, verifying 7 drafts per request burns more compute than the accepted tokens return, dropping **below** non-speculative decoding (see table). ## Design - A Triton kernel ranks draft slots by survival probability (cumprod of per-position confidence) and admits the prefix maximizing estimated accepted tokens per millisecond. - Step costs come from curves profiled with dummy steps at startup: a step function at/below the cudagraph capture limit (padding is physical), linear interpolation above it. - Batch-level budget sizing runs on CPU from double-buffered *stale* confidences (no sync); per-request allocation runs on GPU from live values. - Per-request confidence is smoothed with an EMA (`adaptive_verification_ema_alpha`, default 0.8 — measured bias-zero crossing across batch sizes). - Decode cudagraphs become varlen: captured on the token grid, dispatched via `max_query_len`, every captured slot non-empty. Requires `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS`, which the DSV4 backends report on SM100. ## Results DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark, TP=4, SM100 (B300), `speed_bench` 256 prompts, 512 output tokens; throughput measured at `32881ec177`; subsequent HEAD commits are audit fixes off the captured-graph hot path (decode `max_q_len` sourcing, CPU upper-bound restoration, non-adaptive request-ordering revert to main), accuracy re-validated at HEAD. Output tok/s: Adaptive matches fixed-k within ±3% at c≤64 and preserves the spec-decode win at high concurrency where fixed-k goes underwater (at c=256, fixed 7-token is 33% *below* no-spec). Acceptance length falls from ~3.9 to 3.5 at c=256 — the budget deliberately trims drafts as verification tokens become expensive. Note: the no-spec arm ran with a co-tenant job on the other half of the node; its numbers are directionally correct but modestly depressed. Adaptive/fixed arms ran on an idle node. Accuracy (re-measured at HEAD after the audit fixes below): GSM8K **0.945** (c=16) / **0.951** (c=64), 0 invalid (bar 0.84); MTBench **80/80** completed, completions manually checked for repetition/degeneration — none found.
Reproduction commands **Server** (all measurements; ablations via the noted config deltas): ```bash vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --trust-remote-code \ --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 8192 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --block-size 256 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 256 \ --compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size":1024}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark","attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","enable_adaptive_verification":true}' ``` - fixed 7-token baseline: `"enable_adaptive_verification":false` - no-spec baseline: omit `--speculative-config` **Benchmark harness** — `vllm bench serve` (the Python implementation; the CLI falls back to it automatically when the optional Rust `vllm-rs` binary is absent). If your install ships a Rust binary that rejects any flag below, invoke the Python implementation directly — still repo-only: ```bash python -c 'from vllm.benchmarks.serve import add_cli_args, main from vllm.utils.argparse_utils import FlexibleArgumentParser p = FlexibleArgumentParser(); add_cli_args(p); main(p.parse_args())' ``` **GSM8K** (in-tree runner; 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0): ```bash python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 \ --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 \ --temperature 0 --max-concurrency 16 # and 64 ``` **MTBench coherence** (80 prompts, temperature 1; inspect the saved completions for repetition/degeneration, not just the completion count): ```bash vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model dspark-full \ --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --dataset-name hf --dataset-path philschmid/mt-bench \ --num-prompts 80 --no-oversample --hf-output-len 256 \ --max-concurrency 16 --request-rate inf --temperature 1 \ --save-result --save-detailed ``` **Throughput sweep** (per concurrency; one warmup pass at `--speed-bench-output-len 256 --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 32` first): ```bash for c in 1 16 32 64 128 256; do vllm bench serve \ --backend openai-chat --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \ --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --model dspark-full \ --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --dataset-name speed_bench --dataset-path \ --speed-bench-dataset-subset qualitative \ --skip-chat-template --disable-shuffle --temperature 1.0 \ --speed-bench-output-len 512 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency $c \ --save-result --result-filename adaptive_on_c${c}.json done ``` `--disable-shuffle` plus the fixed prompt set gives every arm identical prompts in identical order; `output_throughput` from the result JSON is the tok/s reported above. The prompt set is an internal speed-bench "qualitative" subset; any fixed prompt set of comparable length distribution reproduces the relative behavior, e.g. `--dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512`.
## Limitations - Output logprobs are rejected when confidence-based verification is enabled (verification compacts logits after the forward pass). - Non-SM100 falls back to PIECEWISE decode graphs: correct, but without the varlen-FULL-graph throughput win. ## Tests ``` pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd_cug.py tests/v1/cudagraph/ -q ``` All pass; full pre-commit green. GSM8K eval config added at `tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark-confidence-TP4.yaml`. ## Not a duplicate Canonical PR for DSpark confidence-based verification; no other open PR touches adaptive draft budgeting. --- AI assistance was used for this change (see commit trailers). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Support DeepSeek-V4 AMD Quark NVFP4 with emulation kernel
body:
## Purpose

Add support for DeepSeek-V4 AMD Quark mixed-quantized checkpoints, where different parts of the model may use different quantization layouts, including per-block FP8 linear layers and NVFP4 MoE experts.

This PR focuses on the Quark/DeepSeek-V4 model-side pieces needed to correctly identify and load these mixed-quantized checkpoints. It avoids changing generic weight-loading behavior and keeps DeepSeek-V4-specific mappings out of the base `QuarkConfig`.

## Main Changes

- Add a dedicated `QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock` scheme for Quark per-block FP8 weights.
  - Keeps the existing `QuarkW8A8Fp8` path focused on per-tensor/per-channel FP8.
  - Derives activation group size from `block_size[1]` instead of hardcoding it independently.
  - Requires per-block FP8 configs to provide `block_size`.

- Move DeepSeek-V4-specific fused module mappings to the DeepSeek-V4 AMD model path.
  - Handles mappings such as `gate_up_proj -> [w1, w3]` and `fused_wqa_wkv -> [wq_a, wkv]` without injecting architecture-specific knowledge into generic `QuarkConfig`.

- Add DeepSeek-V4 AMD checkpoint name handling for scale tensors.
  - Supports checkpoint/vLLM parameter naming differences needed by the mixed Quark layout.

- Align Quark NVFP4 MoE fused `w13` global-scale handling with existing NVFP4 MoE implementations.
  - When `w1/w3` global scales differ, warn and use the `w1` scale for fused `w13`, matching the existing ModelOpt and compressed-tensors NVFP4 MoE convention.
  - This avoids introducing a new `max(w1, w3)` scale-selection policy in this PR.

- Keep generic loader behavior unchanged.
  - The previous diagnostic/debug changes to `parameter.py` were reverted.
  - The PR no longer modifies generic weight-loader logic.

## Out of Scope

- This PR does not introduce a new generic NVFP4 scale-selection policy.
- This PR does not claim full E2E coverage for a future Quark-exported per-block FP8 checkpoint until such a checkpoint is available.
- Broader refactoring of shared NVFP4 MoE scale handling can be done in a separate follow-up PR.

## Test Plan

- Inspect DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint tensor shapes and quantization configs.
- Verify Quark quantization config routing for DeepSeek-V4 fused layers.
- Run lightweight Quark regression tests:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_quark.py -q \
  -k "deepseek_v4_fused_mappings or preserves_existing_packed_modules_mapping or detects_per_block_config or rejects_per_block_static_input or per_block_requires_block_size"
```

| gsm8k | flexible-extract |      8 | exact_match | 0.9477 | 0.0061 |
| gsm8k | strict-match     |      8 | exact_match | 0.9484 | 0.0061 |

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

Serve:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
vllm serve amd/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4 \
  --host localhost \
  --port 8001 \
  --dtype auto \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-num-seqs 512 \
```

title: [ROCm] Fused Shared Expert Support for AMD Quark DeepSeek-V4 Model Checkpoints
body:
## Purpose

Enable serving AMD Quark DeepSeek-V4-MXFP4 checkpoints (AMD-Quark quantized, allowing MXFP4 shared expert fusion) in vLLM. The runtime layout implemented in this PR reuses the existing deepseek_v4_fp8 path.

## Changes

**`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/quant_config.py`**

- `DeepseekV4FP8Config.override_quantization_method` now also claims `quant_method="quark"` for `model_type=deepseek_v4`, guarded by `_is_quark_mxfp4_ocp` so **only** MXFP4 exports are rerouted. Other Quark DSV4 checkpoints (e.g. DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4) fall through to the generic `QuarkConfig` path untouched.
- `from_config` translates the nested Quark schema into the flat FP8 keys `Fp8Config.from_config` expects.

**`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py`**

- Weights mapper handles the AMD `.weight_scale` to `.weight_scale_inv` naming for FP8 attention/linear scales (checkpoint uses `.weight_scale`; the block-FP8 param registers `.weight_scale_inv`). Expert/shared-expert `w{1,2,3}.weight_scale` are left untouched for the MXFP4 loader.
- MXFP4 shared-expert fusion: the shared expert is loaded as an appended routed-expert slot and runs through the same MXFP4 grouped GEMM as the routed experts. Required to run with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS`.

Note: a related PR #47972 targets NVFP4 DeepSeek-V4 checkpoints via the **generic Quark path** (per-block FP8 in `QuarkConfig`, NVFP4 emulation). This PR targets MXFP4 checkpoints via the existing `deepseek_v4_fp8` reroute. An override guard is added so the two do not collide.

## Test plan

Launch (ROCm, gfx950, TP=4):

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve amd/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --trust-remote-code --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --compilation-config '{"mode": 3, "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
```

Launch with MTP speculative decoding (adds `--speculative-config`; `num_speculative_tokens` <= `num_nextn_predict_lay
ers`):

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve amd/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --trust-remote-code --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "deepseek_mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' \
  --compilation-config '{"mode": 3, "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
```

GSM8K 8-shot (`lm_eval`, `num_concurrent=128`):

| Checkpoint | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---:|---:|
| deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash | 0.9500 | 0.9507 |
| amd/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MXFP4 (this PR) | 0.9492 | 0.9500 |

Accuracy Recovery: ~99.9%

title: [Bugfix] Fix FlashMLA dense fp8 metadata crash (num_sm_parts clamp)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #47935

## Root cause

FlashMLA's `get_mla_decoding_metadata_dense_fp8` computes

```
int num_sm_parts = sm_count / num_heads_k / cutlass::ceil_div(num_heads_per_head_k, block_size_m);
```

This can be 0 when `ceil_div(num_q_tokens_per_head_k, block_size_m) > sm_count` (with `num_heads_k == 1`). The bf16/fp16 version clamps the minimum to 1: https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashMLA/blob/a6ec2ba7bd0a7dff98b3f4d3e6b52b159c48d78b/csrc/api/dense_decode.h#L79

In vLLM, `num_q_tokens_per_head_k = max_query_len * num_q_heads` (`FlashMLAMetadataBuilder._build_decode`), and short prompts (query length ≤ `reorder_batch_threshold == 128`) are routed to the decode pathway. So **DeepSeek-R1 (128 heads) crashes on any 67–128 token prompt** on a 132-SM GPU (H100/H200).

## Fix

**vllm-project/FlashMLA#14** clamps `num_sm_parts` to `>= 1` like the bf16/fp16 version

## Testing

On an H200 (132 SMs), with the patched FlashMLA build:

- Direct `get_mla_decoding_metadata_dense_fp8` call at `num_q_tokens_per_head_k` = 8449 and 16384 (both previously `num_sm_parts → 0`, assert): returns valid metadata, no crash.
- End-to-end vLLM `generate` on a dummy DeepSeek-V3 (128 heads, 1 dense layer, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, FlashMLA): 100- and 128-token prompts complete normally (previously crashed with the assertion above).
- Control (66-token prompt, `num_sm_parts = 1`): unaffected.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, build the repro, and prepare this change.

title: [DSv4] Remove sparse-MLA q-head padding for FlashInfer >=0.6.14
body:
## Purpose

Remove the query-head padding in the DeepSeek V4 FlashInfer sparse-MLA
attention layers. flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3545 relaxes the
`trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4` guard to accept `h_q ∈ {8, 16, 32, 64, 128}`
on **both** the SM100 and SM120 decode paths (previously only `{64, 128}`).

Before this, vLLM padded the per-rank head count up to the nearest kernel-supported
value — SM100 (`DeepseekV4FlashInferMLAAttention`) to `{64, 128}` and SM120
(`DeepseekV4FlashInferSM120Attention`) to `{16, 32, 64, 128}` — which wasted compute
on high tensor-parallel sizes (e.g. on SM100 the padded head count for TP4/TP8/TP16
was always 64: 32→64, 16→64, 8→64). Both classes now delegate to a shared
`_pad_to_supported_q_heads` helper and use the native head count for the usual TP
sizes; only exotic sub-8 per-rank counts (TP > 16) are still rounded up to 8.

For DeepSeek V4 (128 attention heads), TP 1/2/4/8/16 → 128/64/32/16/8, all of which
now pass through unpadded.

## Dependency: pending #47669

This change is **runtime-gated on flashinfer ≥ 0.6.14** and should merge after
(or stacked on) #47669 ("Bump flashinfer version to 0.6.14"). The repo currently
pins `flashinfer-python==0.6.13`, whose kernel still enforces
`num_heads ∈ {64, 128}`; merging this before the bump would regress SM100
TP4/TP8/TP16 with `ValueError: Expected 64 or 128 query heads`. This PR deliberately
does **not** touch the version pins — that is #47669's job.

- Version bump PR: #47669
- Upstream flashinfer change that unlocks the head counts: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3545 (first released in flashinfer 0.6.14)

## Not a duplicate

Per the contribution checks, no open PR modifies `get_padded_num_q_heads` or the
sparse-MLA head padding. #47669 only bumps the flashinfer version (for an unrelated
top-k sampler hang fix) and does not remove the padding. Other open DSv4 PRs cover
ROCm functional fixes, SM12x enablement, KV-cache dtype selection, and workspace
bounds — none touch this code path.

## Test Plan

- Lint/type: `pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py`
  (ruff-check, ruff-format, mypy).
- Verify the kernel guard in the installed flashinfer 0.6.14 actually accepts the
  wider head-count set on both decode paths.
- Unit-level check of the new `_pad_to_supported_q_heads` mapping for realistic and
  edge-case head counts.

## Test Result

- `pre-commit` hooks (ruff-check, ruff-format, mypy-3.10) pass on the changed file.
- Against `flashinfer==0.6.14`, both validators in `flashinfer/mla/_core.py` accept
  `{8, 16, 32, 64, 128}`: the SM100 `seq_lens`/`cum_seq_lens_q` path and the SM120
  `swa_topk_lens`/`extra_sparse_indices` path (error message "for SM120 DSv4").
- `_pad_to_supported_q_heads` mapping:
  - TP1→128, TP2→64, TP4→32, TP8→16, TP16→8 (all unpadded).
  - `num_heads=4` → 8 (sub-8 still rounded up); `num_heads=256` → `ValueError`.


## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter has
reviewed every changed line and is responsible for defending the change and running
the hardware-dependent evaluation.

title: [Bugfix] Fix FlashInfer non-causal draft attention (DFlash/DSpark) on Blackwell
body:
## Purpose

DFlash/DSpark drafts on Blackwell had near-zero acceptance or crashed with an illegal memory access when the drafter used FlashInfer; Hopper was fine.

Root cause: non-causal attention skips trtllm-gen and runs FlashInfer's prefill wrapper, which is only CUDA-graph-replayable when constructed with `use_cuda_graph=True` and persistent buffers — vLLM does not use that mode for draft attention, so replaying a captured `run()` after `plan()` returns wrong output, then an IMA as sequences grow. On SM100 the FlashInfer builder claimed `UNIFORM_BATCH` graph support based on trtllm-gen, so drafts were FULL-graph captured on this path; SM90's support level already kept them eager. Kernel numerics are fine (FI eager == FA eager, identical accepted tokens).

Fixes:
- Prefer FLASH_ATTN for SM100 non-causal attention (CUDA-graph-safe default).
- FlashInfer `get_cudagraph_support` only claims `UNIFORM_BATCH` for causal attention.
- Draft speculators build attention metadata under the draft's attention config and honor its cudagraph support; DFlash/DSpark fall back to eager draft attention with a warning (the model runner initializes the speculator's cudagraph manager after `set_attn`).

Follow-up: adopt the prefill wrapper's cuda-graph mode for draft attention to restore full graphs for FlashInfer drafts.

## Test Plan

B300 (SM103): `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --spec-method <m> --spec-model <d> --spec-tokens 7 --speculative-config '{"attention_backend": <b>}'`, greedy completions.

Larger draft, GSM8K acceptance (NVFP4 target needs bf16 KV + autotune off): `vllm serve txn545/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-NVFP4 --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": false}' --speculative-config '{"model":"z-lab/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-DFlash","method":"dflash","num_speculative_tokens":7}'`, then `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 200`.

## Test Result

| Draft | Backend | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.dflash | FLASHINFER | AL 1.11 (IMA on other ckpts) | AL 2.13, eager draft |
| deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_8b_block7 | FLASHINFER | near-zero AL / IMA | AL 2.62, eager draft |
| RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.dflash | FLASH_ATTN | AL 2.17 | AL 2.17, full graphs |
| deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_8b_block7 | FLASH_ATTN | AL 2.62 | AL 2.62, full graphs |
| z-lab/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-DFlash | FLASHINFER | — | AL 4.78, eager draft (GSM8K 0.82) |

title: [Bugfix][KV Cache] Don't route uniform-page-size MLA+SWA models into DeepseekV4 packing
body:
`group_and_unify_kv_cache_specs()` targets DeepseekV4, where MLA and sliding-window MLA layers have different page sizes and must be tuple-packed. 
It fired for any model containing a SlidingWindowMLASpec, so a non-DeepseekV4 model with a uniform page size was wrongly pushed into the packing path. 
This results in creating "one-element bins", while unecessarily triggering separate paths for things like PD eg
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/85c09e9885e346ea1612da30ebff5a75f67d2350/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py#L911-L914

The default HMA handling for these models should suffice.

cc @ivanium

title: [XPU] Support MXFP8 linear weights for INC DeepSeek V4 model
body:
## Summary

Enable the DeepSeek V4 XPU output-projection path to consume
compressed-tensors MXFP8 weights efficiently.

- Preprocess weight scale to match oneDNN expected format
- For BMM layers such as DeepSeek V4 `wo_a`, precompute contiguous
  `bmm_weight` `[G, K, N]` and `bmm_scale` `[G, K/32, N/G]`.

## Testing

Model: https://huggingface.co/INCModel/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MXFP4-Mixed-CT-AutoRound
GSM8K on 8x B70: `0.948`.

## AI assistance

GitHub Copilot was used to assist with investigation, implementation, and
validation. All changes were reviewed by the human submitter.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Optimize sparse attention prefill kernel for DeepSeek-V4
body:
## Purpose
This PR optimizes DeepSeek-V4's dedicated sparse attention ragged prefill kernel in ROCm. The optimization speeds up the kernel by ~2x, and in E2E benchmark reduces TTFT by ~10%.

In the current upstream ROCm path, this kernel has some slight inefficiencies that can be optimized. Specifically, this PR addresses three points of optimization.

- `num_warps` setting. In DSv4-Pro's architecture, the per-workgroup tile under TP8 is `[BLOCK_H=16, 512]` and reduces to `[16, 16]`. Setting `num_warps` splits the K dimension, however, splitting it as high as 8 gives larger cross-wave reduction and more barriers for LDS reads/writes. Therefore, this PR sets `num_warps=4` instead to lower this overhead.
- Remove redundant mask. In the upstream kernel, `kv` is loaded with valid regions masked, and immediately after masked with the same predicate. The later mask should be redundant as the `kv` elements are already `0.0` where masks are `False` at loading. This redundant masking also inserts a mask op right between the load-MFMA ordering, preventing the kernel from benefiting from software pipelining.
- Prefetch the next tile. Overlap the next-tile kv load with MFMA to bring further performance gain.

All these optimization combined, for DeepSeek-V4-Pro's running shapes, the kernel achieves ~2x speed up compared with the current upstream baseline.

Kernel latency under `num_heads=16`, `head_dim=512` (DSv4-Pro TP8)
shape | main kernel latency (ms) | PR kernel latency (ms) | speedup
-- | -- | -- | --
prefill S=2048 | 0.348 ms | 0.190 ms | 1.83×
prefill S=4096 | 1.065 ms | 0.526 ms | 2.02×
prefill S=8192 | 2.782 ms | 1.306 ms | 2.13×


## Test Plan
`lm_eval` with gsm8k and performance benchmark on MI355

Server command
```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --host localhost \
  --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}'
```

Performance benchmark
```
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro --trust-remote-code --dataset-name random --random-input-len $ISL --random-output-len $OSL --max-concurrency $CONC --num-prompts $PROMPTS --temperature 0 --ignore-eos
```

