title: [Attention] Enable FA4 sparse MQA decode on Blackwell
body:
[Attention] Enable FA4 sparse MQA decode on Blackwell

This adds `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE_FA4`, a sparse MLA backend for Blackwell with a BF16 KV cache. The FA4 CuTe DSL kernel from vllm-project/flash-attention#195 serves decode batches and the decode rows of mixed HiSparse batches. Every other batch runs on the trtllm-gen lane, as in `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`. At 16 or fewer query heads per rank the backend is the first choice, with and without HiSparse; above that head count it stays opt-in.

The first commit, "Share sparse MLA MQA cache handling", will go up as its own PR and is only here until it lands. It moves index conversion and the HiSparse lane split from the FA3 and FlashInfer sparse MLA backends into `SparseMLACommonImpl.forward_mqa`, so a backend implements only `_forward_mqa_kernel(..., is_decode)`. The design is by @LucasWilkinson. One FA3 behaviour changes with it: FA3's plain path converts top-k through the index group's shared buffer, as FlashInfer already did, instead of once per layer. The values are identical while the layers of a group share block stride, block table and request ids, which index groups guarantee. A test pins leader and follower layers.

The second commit is the FA4 backend on top of that hook:

- `flash_attn_varlen_func` forwards `gather_kv_indices`, `gather_kv_valid_length` and `q_v` to FA4.
- The impl subclasses `FlashInferMLASparseImpl`. Its hook runs the FA4 decode kernel when `is_decode`, otherwise FlashInfer's trtllm-gen call with the LSE converted to base e.
- The metadata builder subclasses the FlashInfer TRTLLM builder and declares `UNIFORM_BATCH` CUDA graph support. Inheriting the builder brings the DCP workspace pre-size: an earlier version of this PR used the default 394 MiB trtllm workspace on its prefill lane and crashed under DCP 2 on a prefill step of about 8192 tokens, where the softmax-stats slab needs 513 MiB.
- The backend class subclasses the FlashInfer TRTLLM backend for its gates (PCP with DCP rejected, head dims) and adds the FA4 gates: `index_topk` a multiple of 128, and a supported gathered head count under DCP.
- Under HiSparse, decode reads the hot buffer through the shared lanes. The inherited `autotune_hisparse_decode` compiles the FA4 kernel before graph capture.
- FA4 shares FlashInfer's masked-MHA thresholds.
- FA4 joins `_uses_flat_kv_cache`, since it reads the same flat KV cache as FlashInfer.

The last commit bumps the flash-attention pin to vllm-project/flash-attention 2e3a6694, which has #195 and the sparse decode split-rule tuning for DCP shapes (vllm-project/flash-attention#200).

## Performance

GLM-5.2 NVFP4-FP8 with BF16 KV on B300, TP4, FA4 against `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` from the same tree (this PR on `main` d71f662606), change in median ITL (negative favours FA4). Plain and DCP 2 are averaged over two runs. The HiSparse column assumes #59309 is merged: it applies that PR's diff, pins the MoE autotune tactics so both backends run the same MoE kernels, and averages two server starts with two runs each.

| Input / concurrency / output | TP4 plain | TP4 DCP 2 | TP4 HiSparse |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096 / 8 / 256 | -4.2% | -6.7% | -0.8% |
| 4096 / 128 / 256 | -4.3% | -2.3% | +1.3%* |
| 32768 / 16 / 256 | -5.3% | -5.1% | +0.2% |

\* One FA4 run measured 35.2 ms against 33.4 to 33.7 ms for the other three; without it the figure is +0.1%.

Under HiSparse FA4 is on par with FlashInfer, which did not justify a separate priority order. Per decode step, FA4's attention kernels take about 190 µs less than FlashInfer's at 4096 / 8, but start-to-start variance in all-reduce time is larger than that difference. On current `main`, #59235 makes HiSparse about 0.45 ms per decode step slower for both backends, because it writes `request_ids` in every layer. #59309 moves those writes into the group leader's resolve, which brings the 57 follower layers' 171 kernels per step back out of the decode graph.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py`: 475 passed, 672 skipped. `pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: 5 passed (FlashInfer and FA4). The FlashInfer, KV cache layout, backend selection and masked-MHA routing tests pass as well.
- Serving, GLM-5.2 NVFP4-FP8, TP4, HiSparse, GSM8K (500 questions, 5-shot): FA4 0.936, FA4 with MTP 0.948, FlashInfer 0.946. No invalid responses; 8K, 16K and 30K needle prompts answered correctly.
- FlashInfer on the shared base: latency within noise of `main`, plain generations byte-identical.
- The FA3 sparse backend did not run on hardware here (SM90 kernel, SM100 machine); its change is covered by unit tests only.

AI-assisted. The September 7 upstream search found no matching open FA4 sparse-MLA integration PR; related platform-specific work does not provide this SM100 backend.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Stabilize sparse-MLA DCP for GLM PCP evals
body:
## Purpose

Make the B200 GLM-5.2 PCP evaluation complete reliably across its TP/PCP/DCP configurations.

Exact main build [#89033](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89033#01a0a3bf-3adb-4bec-82f2-da92bed83c19) first exposed two independent memory-budget failures after merged backend repair #56677. Successive literal-head and actual-branch gates then exposed the workspace, empty-rank, warmup-key, packed-pointer, and backend-combination edges described below.

## Root causes and fixes

### TP2/PCP2 autotuning headroom

FlashInfer CUTLASS autotuning requests 12.22 GiB with only about 7.6 GiB free after the implicit 0.92 budget reserves 33.46 GiB for KV cache. Set `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85` to leave about 12.5 GiB more autotuning headroom.

### TP1/PCP4/DCP4 KV-cache budget

CUDA graph profiling accounts for 6.15 GiB and reports total non-KV memory of 161.16 GiB, leaving a negative 3.23 GiB KV budget at 0.92. The runtime calculates 0.9545 as the utilization needed to preserve the old effective KV budget. Set 0.96, which produces a positive KV-cache budget.

### FlashInfer sparse-MLA DCP workspace

Under DCP, the TRTLLM-gen launcher requests LSE and carves a softmax-stats slab proportional to gathered heads and scheduled tokens. The old fixed workspace was 413,138,944 bytes; an earlier gate requested 470,810,624 bytes during warmup and failed before evaluation.

This PR carries Jason Yao's byte-derived sizing fix from #50791 with its original author commit, then adapts it to current main's split sparse-MLA backends: preallocation occurs only in `FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMMetadataBuilder` (SM100), so the separate SM120 backend keeps its own behavior. Explicit `VLLM_FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BUFFER_SIZE` overrides remain respected and warn if undersized; non-DCP allocation is unchanged.

The GLM DCP eval now caps `--max-num-batched-tokens` at its existing 4,096-token model length. With 64 heads per TP1 rank and DCP4, that bounds the computed workspace to exactly 2,561,671,168 bytes (2.39 GiB) rather than 16.39 GiB at the previous 32,768-token scheduler cap. This preserves the evaluation's context-length and accuracy contract while keeping the up-front buffer inside the measured B200 reserve.

### Zero-local-sequence DCP warmup rank

CUDA graph warmup can give one DCP rank no local sequences while its padded LSE buffer still has rows. The eager empty-shard mask previously clamped the derived sequence index to `-1` and indexed an empty `seq_lens` tensor. When the statically shaped sequence count is zero, the mask now fills every padded LSE row with `-inf` and returns before the generic lookup. A focused CPU regression covers the exact shape.

### PCP+DCP first-request JIT keys

Actual-branch gate [#89065](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89065) showed DCP4 clearing engine initialization and graph capture, then stalling its first real inference batch after an unexpected `BuildPrefillChunkMetadataKernel` JIT. PCP chunk plans normalize this dispatch to `(DCP_RANK=0, DCP_WORLD=1)`, while startup warmup previously compiled only the configured per-process `(rank, world=4)` key. Warmup now includes both key families.

Actual-branch gate [#89083](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89083) narrowed the remaining miss: the PCP plan stores `global_cu` as the second row of one packed `3 x (rows+1)` allocation, so that input pointer is not always 16-byte aligned. Warmup had modeled alignment only for `uncompressed_seq_lens` and always replayed `global_cu` as aligned. It now covers the Cartesian product of both runtime alignment classes for both pointers, alongside the normalized DCP key.

### Unsupported FlashInfer sparse-MLA PCP+DCP combination

Actual-branch [#89087](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89087) proved the preceding fixes: TP2/PCP2 and TP1/PCP4 passed; DCP4 initialized with 29.45 GiB of KV cache, completed graph capture with no late JIT, and then hung on its first real batch. Diagnostic [#89089](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89089) reproduced the stall with NCCL tracing. The first PCP+DCP request had 153 query rows on rank 0 and 160 on ranks 1-3; the final DCP all-gather consequently entered with counts 9,792 versus 10,240 (`query_rows x 64 heads`).

The selected `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` backend filters top-k KV indices to the local DCP shard and returns LSE for every rank-local PCP query, but does not gather the full cross-DCP KV context first. The shared sparse-MLA wrapper then attempts to DCP-combine unequal PCP query-row tensors. `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` is the implementation that gathers each DCP KV shard before running rank-local PCP prefill queries and returns only the decode LSE that needs DCP combination.

`FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMBackend.supports_combination` now rejects combined PCP+DCP. Automatic selection therefore falls back to `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`; an explicit incompatible backend request receives an actionable error. CPU regressions cover both rejection of the combined mode and continued support for PCP-only and DCP-only modes.

### DCP decode rank scalar

Actual-branch gate [#89093](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89093) confirmed the backend fix: DCP selected `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, completed graph capture and warmup, and began serving mixed prefill/decode traffic. The first decode then hit the runtime sync guard because `get_dcp_local_seq_lens` constructed the static integer DCP rank as a new device tensor inside metadata `build()`.

The metadata builder now materializes that scalar once on its device during initialization and passes the tensor through the localization helper. The helper accepts and directly reuses a correctly typed, colocated scalar tensor; a CPU regression replaces `torch.tensor` with a hard failure during this path to prove that no per-build scalar construction remains.

## Existing work / duplicate check

- #50781 is the exact workspace issue. Open #50791 contains the original diagnosis and implementation, but its head predates the separate TRTLLM/SM120 metadata builders. Original authorship and DCO trailers are preserved here; the current-main adaptation is a separate signed-off commit.
- Searches found no open PR or issue for the empty-rank mask, normalized PCP+DCP warmup key, packed-pointer alignment miss, or unsupported FlashInfer combined-mode selection.
- #56677 is merged and the exact gates confirm its `ag_rs` backend repair is active.
- Open #55828 addresses device-wide versus per-process memory attribution under co-tenancy. These builds use one worker per B200 and report identical per-rank accounting, so it does not own these deterministic config budgets.

## Validation

- Negative control: main #89033 reached both configs; TP2/PCP2 failed in CUTLASS autotuning and TP1/PCP4/DCP4 failed with a negative KV-cache budget.
- Intermediate exact gate #89040 at `a4149f66f`: both PCP configurations passed their corrected budget stages, then reproduced #50781 at the fixed workspace boundary.
- Diagnostic literal-head #89050: TP2/PCP2 and TP1/PCP4 passed, DCP4 received a positive 29.45-GiB KV cache, and warmup isolated the zero-local-sequence failure. It is not counted as a PR-branch gate because it was attributed to `main`.
- Actual-branch #89065 at `2f9bdae78`: both non-DCP configs passed; DCP4 cleared sizing, initialization, and graph warmup, then exposed the normalized JIT-key miss.
- #89076 at `2d93cf0ef` was infrastructure-only: its Buildkite pre-commit proxy received a GitHub API 504, so no B200 job ran.
- Actual-branch #89083 at `2d93cf0ef`: both non-DCP configs passed; DCP4 reached its first real request and isolated the remaining rank-0 unaligned-pointer JIT key.
- Actual-branch #89087 at `5d2d5c905`: both non-DCP configs passed; DCP4 completed sizing, initialization, graph capture, and all warmups with no late JIT, then isolated the incompatible backend collective.
- Diagnostic #89089 at `5d2d5c905`: NCCL tracing recorded the exact unequal DCP all-gather counts (9,792 vs 10,240) on the first PCP+DCP request.
- `pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_workspace.py`: 10 passed.
- Focused zero-local-sequence regression: passed.
- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py -k indexer_warmup`: 2 passed.
- Both YAML files parse; `server_args` contain exactly the intended memory-utilization and scheduler-cap values.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks (including Ruff, mypy, SPDX, and forbidden-import checks) and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Actual-branch #89093 at `7b2f95468`: both non-DCP configs passed; DCP4 selected `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, completed startup, served mixed prefill/decode traffic, and then exposed the runtime DCP-rank scalar construction in decode localization.
- `pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py -k get_dcp_local_seq_lens`: 13 passed.
- Final actual-branch exact [#89097](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89097) passed terminally at `05d607a8b`: bootstrap, GitHub pre-commit, CUDA image, and the sole B200 PCP lane all passed without retry. TP2/PCP2 scored 0.9121, TP1/PCP4 scored 0.9454, and TP1/PCP4/DCP4 scored 0.8832; each completed all 1,319 questions with invalid rate 0.000. The exact job finished 3 passed in 17m54s.

AI assistance was used for investigation, current-main adaptation, CI configuration, and validation. No human review is claimed.

title: [KV Offload] Add per-request `max_load_tokens control`
body:
## Purpose

This PR adds the experimental per-request `kv_transfer_params["max_load_tokens"]`, analogous to `max_offload_tokens`.

- `0` disables external KV loading, so missing tokens are recomputed.
- A positive value caps how many tokens can be loaded beyond the GPU-resident prefix. The cap is rounded down to a supported KV-cache boundary.
- Omitting the field preserves uncapped loading. Invalid values are ignored with a warning.

Local GPU prefix-cache reuse and KV stores remain enabled.

`kv_load_tiers` keeps its existing semantics: it filters secondary tiers, while CPU remains available as a direct source and as the staging tier for secondary loads. `skip_reading_prefix_cache` is unchanged.

AI assistance (Codex) was used to inspect the implementation and draft tests and documentation.

## Test Plan

- [x] Test `max_load_tokens: 0` with synchronous and asynchronous scheduling.
- [x] Test positive caps, partial tails, alignment, and invalid values.
- [x] Verify that the store path and `skip_reading_prefix_cache` remain unchanged.
- [ ] Run the focused tests on the final revision.
- [ ] Validate the final API in a live multi-tier deployment.

title: [Perf] Improve BF16x3 router GEMM accuracy and make it default on sm100
body:
## Purpose

Follow up on #47973. This only concerns router GEMM with FP32 weights i.e. BF16xFP32->FP32

This PR adds master rmem accumulator for long accumulation chain, restoring accuracy against FP32, hence making BF16x3 GEMM suitable as FP32 GEMM replacement whenever the kernel is supported (sm100 family). Custom op wrapper is needed for torch.compile support since torch.compile-based models will execute this new kernel as well.

I also take this opportunity to add some features:
- Tuning table specifically for models using FP32 router weights: Minimax M2/M3 and Hunyuan-V3/V4. We can add new entries for future models as they are added to vLLM too.
- Warmup logic

## Microbenchmarks

GB300. MAE is computed against FP64 reference.

### Minimax M3 (hidden_size=6144, num_experts=128)

| num_tokens | Before us | After us | FP32 us | Before MAE | After MAE | FP32 MAE |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 9.41 | 8.10 | 15.36 | 3.3e-7 | 4.1e-7 | 7.2e-7 |
| 256 | 14.05 | 12.03 | 21.95 | 3.8e-7 | 6.2e-7 | 7.4e-7 |
| 1024 | 19.46 | 19.07 | 53.66 | 9.8e-7 | 9.8e-7 | 1.1e-6 |
| 4096 | 38.59 | 38.21 | 174.43 | 5.1e-6 | 1.6e-6 | 4.1e-6 |
| 16384 | 102.62 | 100.19 | 438.72 | 2.2e-5 | 1.6e-6 | 4.1e-6 |

### Hunyuan-V4 (hidden_size=2816, num_experts=256)

| num_tokens | Before us | After us | FP32 us | Before MAE | After MAE | FP32 MAE |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 9.22 | 8.42 | 13.09 | 2.1e-7 | 3.9e-7 | 4.2e-7 |
| 256 | 14.37 | 11.42 | 20.86 | 2.3e-7 | 3.8e-7 | 4.5e-7 |

Better accuracy than FP32, while slightly faster than Before column thanks to better tuning

title: [Model][Spec Decode] Enable EAGLE3/DSpark pipeline parallelism for Sarvam MLA
body:
## Purpose

Enable EAGLE3 auxiliary hidden-state transport across pipeline stages for `SarvamMLAForCausalLM`, including DSpark drafts whose target taps span multiple stages.

The change reuses `EagleModelMixin` to transport stage-local captures and assemble them in layer order on the final stage. Stage-entry capture runs only on the first stage to avoid duplicate boundary taps. The final stage also loads the target embedding when speculative decoding requires it.

This extends #53052's stage-local Sarvam support using #50514's generic transport; #53577 provides the separate DSpark runtime/model support. Only `sarvam.py` changes. No test files are added.

## Validation status

- **September 17:** rebased onto main `fdcd42350b`; current head `d9e3224dda`. Resolved one docstring-formatting conflict; the patch otherwise remains unchanged. All **94 focused CPU tests and pre-commit passed**, using the existing September 16 runtime/native extensions.
- **September 16 GPU results below:** tested head `00006af451` against main/native extensions `903285fbcc`. **GPU tests have not been rerun after the September 17 rebase.**

CPU coverage includes Sarvam forward with lightweight blocks, numerical equality across PP partitions, boundary and remote/local auxiliary captures, embedding placement, full-graph tracing, and existing worker tests.

## End-to-end results

Sarvam 105B MLA target with a five-layer GQA DSpark draft, taps `[2, 9, 16, 23, 30]`, eight speculative tokens, BF16, TP=2, B200 GPUs. Real-checkpoint coverage is DSpark; a separate EAGLE3 checkpoint was not tested.

GSM8K: all 1,319 questions per row, five-shot, greedy, 512 output-token cap, prefix caching off. Both compilation modes use full decode CUDA graphs; mode 3 additionally enables vLLM/Inductor compilation.

| Configuration | GPUs | Compile mode | Accuracy | Mean acceptance length | Eval seconds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Target only, PP=1 | 2 | 0 | 85.97% | — | 151.6 |
| DSpark, PP=1 | 2 | 0 | 85.90% | 4.13 | 121.3 |
| DSpark, PP=2 | 4 | 0 | 85.06% | 4.15 | 114.7 |
| DSpark, PP=4 | 8 | 0 | 86.20% | 4.13 | 154.8 |
| DSpark, PP=2 | 4 | 3 | 87.26% | 4.14 | 117.5 |

Acceptance is `1 + accepted/drafts`, including short warmup/smoke. These runs do not establish exact token parity or a general accuracy improvement. Evaluation times include residual inference JIT and use different GPU counts, so they are not a controlled efficiency comparison.

- **Eager PP=2:** eight requests ×128 output tokens passed; mean acceptance length 2.65.
- **Compiled PP=2 HTTP:** 28/28 requests passed, covering long-prefix reuse, concurrent streaming/non-streaming completions and chat. Recorded 9,856 prefix-cache hit tokens and 140 FULL CUDA-graph replays; mean acceptance length 2.83.

## PP=1 latency and CUDA-graph coverage

Compared unpatched main against the patch with identical dependencies, TP=2/PP=1, compilation mode 3 and prefix caching off. Each batch had two warmups and 12 measured calls in shuffled order, generating 128 tokens per request. Times include prefill, decode and host overhead; startup/warmup are excluded.

| Configuration | Batch | Base median seconds | PR median seconds | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Target only | 1 | 0.5779 | 0.5812 | +0.57% |
| Target only | 8 | 1.1677 | 1.1432 | −2.10% |
| Target only | 32 | 1.6532 | 1.6183 | −2.11% |
| DSpark, capture cap 288 | 1 | 0.3993 | 0.3960 | −0.84% |
| DSpark, capture cap 288 | 8 | 0.9348 | 0.9309 | −0.41% |
| DSpark, capture cap 288 | 32 | 1.4699 | 1.4512 | −1.27% |

No consistent PP=1 regression was observed. The patch adds no GPU operations or communication at PP=1. Larger-batch outputs varied within runs, affecting speculative acceptance; these measurements do not guarantee zero overhead for every workload.

Eight draft tokens require nine target verification tokens per request, so 32 requests need a **288-token capture**. The original custom cap of 256 left larger batches without graph coverage. With cap 288, the baseline and patched PP=1 runs recorded **238 and 240 FULL replays at exactly 288 tokens**, respectively. This expanded cap was **not retested at PP=2**; the earlier PP=2 replay count covers smaller batches. Prefill/non-uniform steps can still use NONE under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`.

## Runtime and test commands

Model Runner V2; PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130; FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1; CUTLASS DSL 4.7.1; quack-kernels 0.6.5. Target `FLASHINFER_MLA`, draft `TRITON_ATTN` (workaround for #54795 at test time). FlashInfer autotuning and adaptive verification were disabled.

title: [ROCm] triton+triton_kernels 3.8 mxfp4 MoE support (gpt-oss + DeepSeek-V4)
body:
`triton_kernels` 3.8 reorganized its mxfp4 MoE API (`matmul_ogs`→`matmul`, `RoutingData`→`RaggedTensorMetadata`, `weight_scale`→`b_mx_scale`, and dropped the in-kernel scatter+topk-reduce). This PR:
- adds the 3.8 triton_kernels MoE forward for gpt-oss and DeepSeek-V4, gated behind a shared `get_triton_kernels_version` dispatcher
- forward-fixes the other affected `AITER_MXFP4_W4A{8/16}` backends preparation for https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50605
- bumps the triton_kernels commit to ROCm `releases/internal/3.8.x` in `Dockerfile.rock`, since this image i.e. `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100` has triton 3.8 already


## Benchmarks

TP=8, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100` (triton 3.8) + triton_kernels `669b31ac`. Throughput = `vllm bench serve` Output token throughput (tok/s), random ISL/OSL 1024/1024, `--ignore-eos`, temperature 0. Accuracy = gsm8k 5-shot, limit 200, flexible-extract, `--apply_chat_template`.

title: [Bugfix] Parse DSML tool calls when the model omits the tool_calls wrapper
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #48931.

At long context DeepSeek-V4 intermittently omits the `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` opener while still emitting a well-formed `<｜DSML｜invoke ...>` block. Detection anchored solely on the opener, so the whole block leaked to the client as assistant text and no tool call was produced.

**Behaviour change:** trailing text after a well-formed tool block was previously returned as content on both V4 and V3.2, and is now dropped. 

## Test Plan
```bash
pytest tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py \
       tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v32.py \
       tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py \
       tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py \
       tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py
```

title: [ROCm][Spec Decode] Add Aiter MLA decode support non-causal draft block
body: ## Summary - Rebase of #53001 onto current `main`. Original PR is conflicting and this account cannot push to `JohnQinAMD/vllm-amd`. - Pass the real causal mask into Aiter MLA decode (`get_mla_metadata_v1` / `mla_decode_fwd`) instead of flattening a non-causal DSpark draft query block. - Probe `mla_decode_fwd` for a `causal` argument; keep Gluon and DCP verify causal-only; refuse fp8 2-token non-causal blocks until aiter folds that length. ## Rebase notes - FlashInfer MLA no longer overrides `_build_decode` on main, so it inherits the new `causal` kwarg. - `use_gluon_verify` now takes `dcp_world_size` and `causal`; non-causal still never routes to Gluon. - Persistent-metadata gating uses `_decode_num_heads` and still keeps the schedule for non-causal blocks. ## Test plan - [x] `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_support.py tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_decode_routing.py tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py` - [ ] Original #53001 bench/accuracy plan on 8x MI355X (pinned TritonMLA vs unpinned AiterMLA) Original description and results: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53001 Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][DSv4] Skip launch_pdl=True JIT warmup when PDL is unsupported
body:
## Summary
- JIT warmup after #50176 enumerated `launch_pdl=(False, True)` for DeepSeek V4 fused Q/KV RMSNorm and inv-RoPE FP8 quant kernels, even on platforms without PDL.
- On ROCm that compiles NVIDIA `griddepcontrol` PTX into an hsaco and `ld.lld` fails, so engine startup dies (`#56030`).
- Only include `launch_pdl=True` in the warmup space when `current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl()` is true. NVIDIA still warms both variants.

Fixes #56030

## Test plan
- [x] ROCm / gfx950: `vllm serve` DeepSeek-V4-Flash with JIT warmup enabled; startup should pass kernel warmup without `griddepcontrol` / hsaco link errors.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4] Remap Quark MTP layer_quant_config onto draft prefixes
body:
## Purpose

`--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp"}'` fails to load mixed Quark DeepSeek-V4 checkpoints (FP8 attention / shared experts + NVFP4 routed experts). The draft modules are constructed under `model.layers.{num_hidden_layers + i}.*`, but `_make_deepseek_v4_weights_mapper` rewrites Quark `layer_quant_config` keys from `mtp.{i}.*` to `model.mtp.{i}.*`. Per-layer lookups miss, every MTP linear falls back to the global NVFP4 scheme, and `PackedColumnParameter.load_merged_column_weight` then asserts on a packed vs unpacked shape mismatch.

This is independent of the ROCm PDL warmup fix in #56035.

## Changes

- Add `align_mtp_quant_config()` to re-key `model.mtp.{i}.` onto the draft prefixes before MTP construction.
- Give `DeepSeekV4MTP` the same `packed_modules_mapping` as `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` so fused `gate_up_proj` / `fused_wqa_wkv` unfold to `w1`/`w3` and `wq_a`/`wkv` for per-layer lookup.
- Apply on amd / nvidia / xpu MTP classes (same mapper mismatch exists on all three).

## Test plan

- [x] `vllm serve` DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 on 8× gfx950, TP=8, `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`
- [x] MTP weights load (`MTP draft model loaded: 39 params`)
- [x] Greedy completion and a short chat request succeed
- [x] Speculative acceptance is non-zero (46/51 draft tokens accepted ≈ 90%)


## Test result

ROCm serve reached `Application startup complete`. `/health` 200. Greedy `"The capital of France is"` produced `" Paris."`; chat `"Name three prime numbers greater than 100"` produced `"101, 103, 107"`. Spec decode metrics: 51 draft tokens, 46 accepted.

title: [4/N] Expose HiSparse cache metrics via KV connector stats
body:
Alternative to #53782, reporting the same HiSparse hot-buffer stats through the existing `KVConnectorStats` pipeline instead of adding a new `finish_step` connector hook.

## What stays identical

- Kernel counters (`atomicAdd` in the CUDA kernels) and the swap-ordering changes in `runtime.py` are unchanged from the original PR.
- Same 2000-step async sampling interval with a CUDA event for D2H ordering.
- Same three Prometheus counters: `vllm:hisparse_hits`, `vllm:hisparse_lookups`, `vllm:hisparse_l3_lookups`.

## What changes

Instead of a new `finish_step` hook on `KVConnectorBase` (plus edits to scheduler, outputs, aggregator, loggers, and `stats.py`), the worker now exposes the snapshots through the existing hook:

```python
def get_kv_connector_stats(self) -> Optional[HiSparseKVConnectorStats]:
    ...
```

and the connector wires it into the standard pipeline:

```
worker.get_kv_connector_stats()          # HiSparseKVConnectorStats (list of snapshot deltas)
  -> scheduler picks it up in SchedulerStats
  -> build_kv_connector_stats()          # HiSparseKVConnectorStats.from_proxy_stats
  -> HiSparsePromMetrics.observe()       # vllm:hisparse_* counters
```

This is the same contract NIXL, the offloading connector, and mooncake already follow — transfer/cache telemetry goes through `KVConnectorStats` and the connector's `build_prom_metrics`, with zero core plumbing. HiSparse's hot-buffer residency counters are connector telemetry, so they fit the same slot the offloading connector uses for its allocation-failure/lookup-delay stats.

Net effect: the diff drops from 16 files to 9 and avoids changes to `base.py`, `model_runner.py`, `outputs.py`, scheduler, loggers, and core `stats.py`.

Also picks up two small cleanups over the original:

- Stats emission is gated on the connector being configured (the connector owns its stats, rather than gating on `attention_config` in the model runner).
- The sampling interval advances even on no-forward steps, so long prefill stretches don't stretch the sampling cadence.

Because the stats flow through `KVConnectorStats`, CLI logging comes for free:

```
INFO ... Cumulative HiSparse stats: hits=12 lookups=4 l3_lookups=64
```

## Validation

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_stats.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py::test_hisparse_worker_get_kv_connector_stats_reads_completed_snapshot -q
6 passed

PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py
All applicable hooks passed, including Ruff, formatting, and mypy.
```

Model evaluation is not applicable because this change only reports telemetry and does not affect model outputs.

Duplicate check: this remains the `KVConnectorStats`-based alternative to #53782; searches for open PRs mentioning #56061 and HiSparse metrics found no duplicate of this implementation.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped audit CI and prepare the follow-up cleanup. Human review and ownership remain with the submitter.

title: [PCP][Spec Decode] Adds PCP support for single-module MTP and replicated DSpark.
body:
## Summary

Adds V2 model-runner PCP support for single-module MTP and replicated DSpark.

- MTP reuses the target PCP-local batch for its initial draft forward, then refreshes global-order block tables for subsequent replicated drafts.
- DSpark stays replicated while the target is PCP-sharded.
- PIECEWISE CUDA graphs are supported; full graphs remain rejected.

This consolidates #53653 and #53660 on current `main` with a smaller implementation.

## Validation

The latest fix refreshes `input_block_tables`, which PCP's separate local gather leaves uninitialized for later MTP drafts. A GPU check with two requests and two KV-cache groups confirmed zeroed tables before the gather and correct request mappings afterward. Focused tests: 52 passed.

Earlier four-GPU GLM-5.2-NVFP4 smoke tests, TP2 + PCP2 + DCP1 + EP4, with `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`; logs confirmed graph capture:

- MTP2, FP8 KV: 8 output tokens, 4/6 draft tokens accepted (66.7%).
- `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark`, DSpark8, BF16 KV: 8 output tokens, 7/8 accepted (87.5%).

These acceptance figures predate the block-table fix; full-model acceptance has not been rerun after it.

MTP:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"}'
```

DSpark:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark","num_speculative_tokens":8,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"}'
```

AI assistance was used for implementation, debugging, and validation. The human submitter reviewed the changes.

title: [watermarking] Dual-key gumbel-max watermarking for speculative decoding support
body: This PR includes work on dual-key gumbel-max watermarking, as well as generation-time context deduplication (taken from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56233). I've added the PR description of context deduplication to this PR as well, for the sake of future readers. ## Dual-key Gumbel-max ### Purpose Text watermarking in vLLM (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54053) currently is not compatible with speculative decoding. This PR proposes multiple changes to resolve this: - `"allow_target_only_watermarking": true` allows the use of speculative decoding with watermarking, but will not watermark accepted draft tokens: this will dilute the watermarking signal in proportion to the share of output tokens that are accepted drafts - `dual_key_gumbel` algorithm is a variation of the Gumbel-max algorithm, where we use different keys to watermark our generations: this allows for watermarking of draft tokens, and also for improved diversity of outputs when using watermarking Dual-key watermarking allows to support speculative decoding by using algorithm 6 of [SynthID-Text's supplementary material](https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-024-08025-4/MediaObjects/41586_2024_8025_MOESM1_ESM.pdf). To watermark the draft model's generations, without inducing a loss in acceptance rate (see algorithm 5): ``` Given distinct watermarking keys k^T and k^D, a target model p, a draft model q, a watermarked target model p_wm(.;k^T) and draft model q_wm(.;k^D) 1. We sample draft tokens from q_wm 2. We calculate target logits for drafts using p 3. We accept tokens with probability r < min(1, q(x) / p(x)) 4. If rejected, we sample from residual(p, q)(.;k^T) 5. If all tokens are accepted, we sample our bonus token from p_wm ``` Note how: - all draft tokens are watermarked by k^D - all target tokens are watermarked by k^T (residual, and bonus) - acceptance rate uses unwatermarked distributions, and is identical to acceptance rate without watermarking For justification of using distinct keys to preserve non-distortion, see section K.13 of [SynthID-Text's supplementary material](https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-024-08025-4/MediaObjects/41586_2024_8025_MOESM1_ESM.pdf). ### Test Plan Measuring impact, using standard models and methods, on: - inference performance (in particular the acceptance rate) - detectability of watermark ### Test Result Results for commit `97a264006f3d7ed9999fbd9b93319b780ac0631d` on 1x H100 per arm. GSM8K, 300 five-shot prompts, temperature 1.0, maximum 1,024 output tokens, and Qwen3.5 MTP with three probabilistically sampled draft tokens. #### Inference performance | Model | Disabled output tokens | Dual-key output tokens | Disabled tok/s | Dual-key tok/s | Delta throughput | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3.5-2B | 59,769 | 72,141 | 7,366.0 | 8,254.0 | +12.1% | | Qwen3.5-27B | 102,555 | 101,330 | 1,268.0 | 1,215.9 | -4.1% | The generated length distributions differ, especially for the 2B model, so these are end-to-end workload measurements rather than an isolated measure of watermarking overhead. #### Speculative decoding | Model | Watermark | Draft acceptance rate | Mean acceptance length | |---|---|---:|---:| | Qwen3.5-2B | Disabled | 69.6% | 3.09 | | Qwen3.5-2B | Dual-key Gumbel | 79.9% | 3.40 | | Qwen3.5-27B | Disabled | 81.1% | 3.43 | | Qwen3.5-27B | Dual-key Gumbel | 80.9% | 3.43 | Per-request speculative metrics were only populated for requests that performed speculative steps. The table aggregates the accepted and drafted token counts from those records. #### Quality | Model | Watermark | Accuracy | Mean completion length | Median completion length | Repeated 4-token context rate (micro) | Reached 1,024-token cap | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3.5-2B | Disabled | 25.7% | 199.2 | 128.0 | 20.48% | 14/300 (4.7%) | | Qwen3.5-2B | Dual-key Gumbel | 25.0% | 240.5 | 123.5 | 41.97% | 33/300 (11.0%) | | Qwen3.5-27B | Disabled | 64.0% | 341.9 | 165.0 | 20.44% | 59/300 (19.7%) | | Qwen3.5-27B | Dual-key Gumbel | 73.0% | 337.8 | 164.5 | 19.56% | 53/300 (17.7%) | These are single stochastic runs, so accuracy differences should not be interpreted as causal. #### Detectability Detection uses the exact completion token IDs, both derived keys, context deduplication, and a threshold of p ≤ 0.01. | Model | No-watermark positives | Dual-key positives | Median dual-key p-value | Mean dual-key scored tokens | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3.5-2B | 3/300 (1.0%) | 226/300 (75.3%) | 0.000145 | 139.5 | | Qwen3.5-27B | 3/300 (1.0%) | 69/300 (23.0%) | 0.113773 | 271.7 | Detection improves with completion length: | Model | <64 tokens | 64-127 | 128-255 | 256-511 | ≥512 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3.5-2B | 40.5% | 70.9% | 80.6% | 100.0% | 100.0% | | Qwen3.5-27B | 0.0% | 4.6% | 8.5% | 50.0% | 64.7% | Poor detectability on the 27B generations are due to low entropy, which reduces the amount of signal our watermarking bias can embed: | Model | Perplexity | Sampled tokens with p ≥ 0.99 | |---|---:|---:| | Qwen3.5-2B | 2.25 | 36.1% | | Qwen3.5-27B | 1.19 | 72.7% | ## Context deduplication ## Purpose Text watermarking in vLLM (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54053) currently uses a short context (4 tokens, by default) before each generated token to create the pseudorandom noise that we use to watermark its sampling. It is possible for multiple positions in a sequence to have the same context, and thus have the same watermarking bias applied. This makes gumbel watermarking single-token non-distortionary instead of single-sequence non-distortionary: expectation of token distribution, over all keys, is unchanged, but expectation of sequence distributions, over all keys, is changed. In practice, this leads to: - a reduced diversity of generations within a sequence, and - increased likelihood of poor behaviour such a repetition and infinite generations A solution to this is context masking, or context deduplication: if a context has already been watermarked in a sequence, we do not watermark it again. This allows for single-sequence non-distortion (see section G.3 of [SynthID-Text supplementary materials](https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-024-08025-4/MediaObjects/41586_2024_8025_MOESM1_ESM.pdf)). An initial instinct may be that reducing the amount of tokens we watermark within a sequence will reduce the strength of our watermarking signal, but we actually already deduplicate contexts during detection to avoid biasing repetitions: we only score the first instance of a repeated context, matching what we propose for generation here. In practice however, we may imagine a case where a user will manipulate watermarked text to excluse an initial watermarking of a repeated context, only keeping the subsequent unwatermarked repetitions: this would indeed lead to a reduced watermarking signal, but this is already expected with a tampered text, and we propose that this is acceptable if it allows for increased guarantees of non-distortion. ## Test Plan Measuring impact, using standard models and methods, on: - degenerate generations (repetition, infinite generations) - output length, intra-sequence diversity - output quality - inference performance ## Test Result Results for commit `42908fd643fb46744f78937dc39034b02c99b172` on 1x H100 ### Inference performance #### Microbenchmark - ms per sample step - mean of 100 + 20 warmup steps | Batch | History tokens | Unmasked (ms/step) | Masked (ms/step) | Delta ms | Delta % | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 2,048 | 0.036 | 0.110 | +0.073 | +201.2% | | 1 | 8,192 | 0.036 | 0.111 | +0.075 | +208.7% | | 1 | 32,768 | 0.037 | 0.110 | +0.073 | +197.5% | | 32 | 2,048 | 0.041 | 0.110 | +0.069 | +166.6% | | 32 | 8,192 | 0.041 | 0.110 | +0.069 | +165.6% | | 32 | 32,768 | 0.042 title: [Test][Renderer] Cover the reasoning -> reasoning_content mirror in chat message parsing
body:
## Purpose

`_parse_chat_message_content` mirrors an assistant turn's `reasoning` back under the legacy name `reasoning_content`, for chat templates that still read `message.reasoning_content`. No test covers that line, and it has already broken once: #33402 removed the mirror, which broke GLM and Kimi K2 style templates (reported in #33616), and #33635 restored it four days later without a test. A refactor can drop it silently again, and the model then loses its own earlier reasoning on every turn, which reads as amnesia rather than as an error. This PR adds tests only -- **no production code changes**.

`ChatCompletionRequest` normalizes an incoming `reasoning_content` message key to `reasoning`, so by the time a message dict reaches `_parse_chat_message_content` only `reasoning` is set. That function then puts the value back under **both** names on the `ConversationMessage` handed to the Jinja renderer:

```python
if reasoning is not None:
    result_msg["reasoning"] = cast(str, reasoning)
    result_msg["reasoning_content"] = cast(
        str, reasoning
    )  # keep compatibility
```

Three tests, in `tests/renderers/test_chat_utils.py` (moved there from `tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/` by #60522, together with `chat_utils.py`, which now lives at `vllm/renderers/chat_utils.py`):

- `test_assistant_reasoning_is_mirrored_to_reasoning_content` -- the mirror itself.
- `test_assistant_without_reasoning_sets_neither_field` -- over-correction guard: no reasoning in, neither key out, so a template that renders `reasoning_content` unconditionally does not start emitting empty thinking blocks for ordinary turns.
- `test_non_assistant_reasoning_is_not_mirrored` -- a user turn carrying `reasoning` must not get it.

They drive `_parse_chat_message_content` directly with a text-only tracker stand-in, so they need no model, no network and no accelerator. (This file already imports and tests the sibling private helper `_postprocess_messages`.)

An earlier revision also added a non-streaming test of `include_reasoning` against the usage counter. I removed it: I found no bug on record for it.

### Not a duplicate

Re-searched open PRs touching reasoning / `reasoning_content` / `chat_utils` on 2026-10-10. Two are adjacent, neither overlaps:

- **#52513** ("Normalize reasoning_content on tokenize and pooling chat requests") adds a new `normalize_reasoning_content` helper in `chat_utils.py` (it still edits the pre-#60522 path `vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py`) and wires it into the tokenize/pooling request protocols. That is the *input* rename on request types that were missing it; this PR covers the *output* mirror inside `_parse_chat_message_content`, which #52513 does not touch. Textually disjoint (different region of the file, and this PR changes no production line at all).
- **#53340** ("add reasoning_content field ... to ChatMessage") is the response-side protocol. Deliberately not asserted on here: an earlier draft of this PR pinned "`ChatMessage` has no `reasoning_content` field", which would have blocked #53340 for no good reason. That assertion was dropped.

On `main`, a search of `tests/renderers` for `reasoning_content` finds only the Cohere and Inkling renderer tests, which pass it in as input; none covers this mirror.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/renderers/test_chat_utils.py -q \
    -k "reasoning_is_mirrored or sets_neither_field or non_assistant_reasoning"
```

Re-run on 2026-10-13 on this branch merged with `main` at `2bea22002`, Python 3.13.15, CPU only.

## Test Result

```
tests/renderers/test_chat_utils.py (3 new tests)                    3 passed
```

Whole-file run of `tests/renderers/test_chat_utils.py`, `main` vs. this branch, to show the failure set is unchanged and only the new tests are added (measured 2026-10-10; the file is unchanged since):

| tree | result |
|---|---|
| `main` (`2bea22002`) | 25 passed, 72 errors |
| this branch | **28** passed, 72 errors |

The 72 errors are identical ids on both trees: the environment this was run in has no network, and those tests fetch multimodal assets from S3 or model configs from the Hub.

A test that cannot fail is not a test, so each new assertion was checked against a mutated production tree (mutation applied to a scratch worktree of this branch, the 3 tests re-run, the files restored byte-identical afterwards). The unmutated control passes 3/3:

| mutation to production code | result |
|---|---|
| drop `result_msg["reasoning_content"] = ...` from `_parse_chat_message_content` (the change #33402 made to these lines) | **1 failed**, 2 passed -- `test_assistant_reasoning_is_mirrored_to_reasoning_content` |
| set `reasoning_content` unconditionally (i.e. also when `reasoning` is `None`) | **1 failed**, 2 passed -- `test_assistant_without_reasoning_sets_neither_field` |
| mirror `reasoning_content` for every role, not only assistant | **1 failed**, 2 passed -- `test_non_assistant_reasoning_is_not_mirrored` |

The branch contains one test file only.

`pre-commit run --files tests/renderers/test_chat_utils.py` (ruff check/format, typos, mypy, SPDX, test-tethering): all passed.

No model evaluation: this PR changes no production code, so no output, accuracy or serving behaviour is affected.

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change. Every changed line was reviewed and the tests and mutation checks above were run locally before submission.

title: [Bugfix] Tolerate misspelled DSML tool_calls wrapper
body:
## Purpose

Partially addresses #51914.

DeepSeek-V4-Flash intermittently misspells the DSML tool-call opener while the rest of the block stays well-formed:

```diff
-<｜DSML｜tool_calls>
+<｜DSML｜toolcalls>            # also observed: <｜DSML｜tool>
 <｜DSML｜invoke name="get_weather">
 <｜DSML｜parameter name="city" string="true">Seoul</｜DSML｜parameter>
 </｜DSML｜invoke>
 </｜DSML｜tool_calls>
```

The parser matches markers literally, so the misspelled opener matches nothing, no `tool_calls` are produced, and the whole block is returned as assistant `content`.

### Fix

Let a terminal carry several spellings. `ParserEngineConfig.terminals` now accepts `str | tuple[str, ...]`; every spelling lexes to the same terminal name and shares its transitions. DeepSeek-V4 registers the observed corruptions as spellings of `TOOL_START`:

```python
"TOOL_START": (DSML_TOOL_START, *DSML_TOOL_START_VARIANTS),
```

### Alternatives considered

| Approach | Why not |
|---|---|
| One terminal name per spelling, transitions duplicated in the config | Transitions describe meaning; a spelling is a lexing detail. Every `TOOL_START` transition and every engine-derived classification (openers, exits, reasoning markup, skip-mode projection) would need to be kept in sync by hand, with silent drift as the failure mode. |
| Treat any unknown `<｜DSML｜…>` tag as protocol noise and drop it | Covers unseen corruptions, but cannot distinguish noise from the model deliberately quoting a tag. Registering only observed spellings keeps anything unlisted as untouched content. |

## Test Plan
```bash
pytest tests/parser
```

title: [Perf][MiniMax-M3] Triton indexer: decode grid retune + SM12.0 split-K
body:
## Overview

Two changes to the Triton MiniMax-M3 indexer (`vllm/models/minimax_m3/common/ops/index_topk.py`):

1. **Decode launch-grid retune.** `TARGET_GRID` goes from 512 to 4096 (decode index score) and `TOPK_TARGET_GRID` from 64 to 512 (decode top-k). This applies to every CUDA GPU on the Triton MiniMax-M3 indexer, not only SM120. ROCm uses its own `amd/ops/index_topk.py` and is not touched. Folded in from #49229 with its author's agreement; original commit by Zijing Liu, co-authored by Kyle Liang.
2. **SM12.0 prefill split-K.** On SM12.0 only, the prefill index score (`_index_block_score_kernel`) splits its K loop across CTAs when the launch grid is small, as it is for short chunked-prefill extends. Other GPUs keep the unsplit launch.

This PR was closed after the concurrency-12 point showed no gain, then reopened and narrowed:
- FP8 index-cache support and the operand casts are in #59081 (supersedes #47665).
- The fused decode top-k and the router change are dropped.

## Claims

Faster decode at higher batch sizes on the Triton indexer (grid retune), and faster short-extend prefill on RTX PRO 6000 (SM120, split-K).

## Validation

- **E2E:** MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 + EAGLE3 on 8x RTX PRO 6000, InferenceMAX recipe at c10 TP8.
  - Grid retune: removing it costs 4.6% throughput (tput 0.954x). Decode step p50 at 10 requests is 49.2 ms without it and 39.6 ms with it, matching the reference stack's 39.6 ms. #49229 separately reported +44% at B300 TP4 c24.
  - Split-K: short cached extends take 263 ms per iteration without it and 200 ms with it (reference stack 192 ms). This comes from a leave-one-out of the earlier fused-top-k + split-K version; split-K is the only part of that version on this path.
  - This PR as a whole: the split-K-only confirmation run already included the grid retune, so it measures exactly these contents. It reaches 0.985 tput / 1.004 interactivity vs the InferenceMAX reference stack, and per-request TPOT 0.997 [0.975, 1.008] vs the earlier fused+split-K version (n=1).
- **SM120 tests:** `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py` gives 95 passed, 0 failed, 58 skipped. Main gives 92 / 0 / 58; the only difference is the 3 new prefill cases, and outcomes on the shared IDs are identical. `test_decode_index_topk_correctness` passes all 6 cases with the new decode grids (256 score chunks; up to 16 top-k chunks). All 4 prefill cases take `USE_SPLIT_K=True`.
- **CI:** `test_prefill_index_topk_correctness` forces the split path on any CUDA GPU (incl. an uneven split), so L4 runs it.
- **Lint:** `pre-commit`, including mypy-3.12, passed.

## Details

- Decode chunk counts stay shape-constant, so the launch is still CUDA-graph safe. At 2 or fewer decode requests the score grid is unchanged, because both values hit the 256-chunk cap.
- The split count is `split_k = min(max_block, 48 // (n_q_tiles * batch * heads))`, on SM12.0 only.
- Each CTA writes a disjoint range of per-block maxima, so no reduction is needed.
- Splits past a query tile's causal window exit early.

title: [ROCm][Kernel][DSV4] Remove tl.constexpr to avoid cold-compile churn in indexer gather kernel
body:
## Purpose

The generic `_cp_gather_indexer_quant_cache_kernel` declared `NUM_TOKENS`, `NUM_BATCHES`, `BLOCK_TABLE_WIDTH`, and `NUM_BLOCKS` as `tl.constexpr`. All four are shape/batch-derived and vary at runtime (total token at each forward pass, sequences per batch, blocks per sequence), so their values entered the Triton compile-cache key and forced a fresh kernel compile for nearly every distinct shape during serving. This problem becomes more critical for individual local-inference situation when caches are usually cold.

### 4 Parameter breakdown:
`NUM_TOKENS` (**most critical problem, always changing**): can't afford recompilation for EVERY seq_len - this means nearly for every new user prompt, vLLM JIT compiles a new kernel. TTFT explodes and several seconds latency observed.
`NUM_BATCHES`: also changes rapidly under server setup.
`BLOCK_TABLE_WIDTH`, `NUM_BLOCKS`: don't change during each serve session, but making it `tl.constexpr` buys nothing as they are only used once in the kernel as boundary checks.

This mirrors the sibling `_cp_gather_indexer_quant_cache_gfx950_kernel`, which already uses `do_not_specialize=["num_batches"]`. The structural constexprs (`LAYOUT`, `HEAD_DIM`, `BLOCK_TILE_SIZE`, `HEAD_TILE_SIZE`) are unchanged. Pure cache-key change; kernel math and output are unaffected.

title: [PCP][DCP] Enable PCP+DCP on sparse-MLA models
body:
## Purpose

Enable DCP to run alongside PCP on sparse-MLA models, so a deployment can shard the KV cache for decode and still split prefill query work across ranks.

This change:

- gives the sparse indexer a DCP-gathered prefill path: this rank's KV shard is all-gathered across the DCP group
- gives the FlashMLA-sparse backend the matching prefill path, with a rank-major gathered KV workspace and a PCP-invariant chunk plan every rank derives identically without communicating;
- replicates prefills too short to fill all `2*PCP` chunks when DCP is on, which keeps the per-region row count identical on every rank — the invariant the gathered layout rests on;
- adds a MoE all-reduce fast path for steps whose rows are all PCP-replicated, replacing an unconditional all-gather + reduce-scatter that duplicated every decode row `PCP` times;
- relaxes the PCP CUDA graph restriction for PCP+DCP to everything up to `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, keeping only `FULL` over mixed batches rejected;

fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53573
Additionally
- fixes a pre-existing kernel/reference divergence: the top-k index kernel applied the block-table bound to prefill-workspace rows, while `_triton_convert_reference_impl` has always specified that only `-1` is invalid there. The existing test missed it because `token_indices[6, 150:160]` is an empty slice on a 128-column tensor;

## Test Plan

- NVIDIA GB200 x4
- GLM-5.3, NVFP4 weights
- TP=1, PCP=4, DCP=4

## Test Result

GSM8K, 1319 questions, TP1+PCP4+DCP4, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. Seven runs across the

| Run | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---|---|
| TP4 | 0.830 | 0.000 |
| PCP4DCP4| 0.832 | 0.000 |


## Benchmarks

Prefill, 32768 in / 1 out:

| Layout | TTFT ms | P99 TTFT ms | vs tp4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| tp4 | 5512.1 | 8141.1 | 1.00x |
| pcp4 | 3278.1 | 4814.0 | 1.68x |
| pcp4dcp4 | 3326.8 | 4888.7 | 1.66x |

Decode, 1 in / 1024 out:

| Layout | TPOT ms | out tok/s | vs tp4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| tp4 | 18.6 | 3412.7 | 1.00x |
| dcp4 | 28.4 | 2236.8 | 0.66x |
| pcp4dcp4, PIECEWISE (this PR) | 86.7 | 735.9 | 0.22x |
| pcp4dcp4, with FULL decode graphs and moe deduplication   https://github.com/PatrykSaffer/vllm/compare/patryk/pcp-dcp-sparse-mla...patryk/pcp-dcp-full-cg-no-duplication | 32.6 | 1944.1 | 0.57x |



Why pcp4dcp4 decode is slower than dcp4 decode:
CudaCommunicator.__init__ enables custom all-reduce, torch symm-mem and FlashInfer fused all-reduce for tp groups only, so that per-layer all-reduce runs on NCCL ring.
followup is to enable it, sth like https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56157/changes/590e9b7e185df741e5aabbecfed351dd3470c04f

title: [Kernel] Optional Q-norm in fused DSv4 MLA epilogue; group_size=32 for packed FP8 quant
body:
## Purpose

Two independent CUDA changes carved out of #56201 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) so the
kernel work lands and gets reviewed ahead of the model. Both are behavior-
preserving for every existing caller.

### 1. Optional Q-norm in the fused DSv4 MLA epilogue

`csrc/libtorch_stable/fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu`

The three DSv4 MLA epilogue ops
(`fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_quant_insert`,
`..._full_cache_bf16_insert`, `..._full_cache_fp8_insert`) hardcode a per-head
weightless RMSNorm on the Q side. Some architectures project Q with that norm
already folded into the weights, so the epilogue must apply RoPE alone.

This adds an `apply_q_norm` argument, defaulted to `True` in the schema, so
every existing caller is unchanged. It is threaded through as a template
parameter (`APPLY_Q_NORM`) rather than a runtime branch, so the norm-enabled
instantiation generates the same code as before — the norm block is
`if constexpr`-ed out of the RoPE-only instantiation entirely.

### 2. `group_size == 32` for the packed per-token-group FP8 quant

`csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/fp8/per_token_group_quant.cu`

`per_token_group_quant_8bit_packed_register_kernel` was pinned to
`GROUP_SIZE == 128` with `THREADS_PER_GROUP` hardcoded to 8 and the subgroup
absmax reduction written as three literal `__shfl_xor_sync` steps against a
hand-built 8-lane mask.

`THREADS_PER_GROUP` is now derived as `GROUP_SIZE / VEC_SIZE` (each thread
still quantizes 16 bf16/fp16 values), the lane mask is built from
`THREADS_PER_GROUP`, and the reduction is a `#pragma unroll` loop over
`THREADS_PER_GROUP / 2 .. 1`. The 8-lane (group 128) and 2-lane (group 32)
subgroups then share one code path, and the launcher dispatches `GROUP_SIZE`
through the existing `kx`/`ry` tiling macros.

The Python entry point
(`per_token_group_quant_fp8_packed_for_deepgemm`) is already group-size
agnostic, so no Python change is needed.

## Not a duplicate

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "56201 in:body"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "per_token_group_quant packed group_size"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope apply_q_norm"
```

- #56201 is the source PR this is extracted from; landing this first shrinks it.
- #56208 splits the frontend half of #56201 — no overlap with `csrc/`.
- Nothing open touches the DSv4 MLA epilogue kernel.
- #55330 touches the same *file* as change 2, but adds a separate kernel
  (`per_token_group_quant_8bit_register_kernel`, the unpacked fp32-scale
  layout). It does not change `..._packed_register_kernel`, so the two are
  independent; whichever lands second may need a trivial textual rebase.

## Test Plan

Both kernels already have suites; this extends them rather than adding files.

- `tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py`
    - New `test_q_path_without_qnorm_matches_rope_only_reference`: with
      `apply_q_norm=False` the Q output must be bit-exact (`rtol=0, atol=0`)
      against a RoPE-only torch reference, and the pad-head region must still
      be zeroed.
    - The two full-cache tests (bf16 and per-tensor fp8) gain an
      `apply_q_norm` axis with three ids — `qnorm_default` (argument omitted,
      pinning the schema default), `qnorm_explicit` (`True`), and `rope_only`
      (`False`) — so the default-argument behavior is covered as a distinct
      case from passing `True`.
- `tests/kernels/quantization/test_per_token_group_quant.py`
    - Five `group_size=32` shapes added to
      `test_per_token_group_quant_fp8_packed`, chosen to hit the padding
      cases the 128 shapes already cover: no padding `(32, 512, 32)`, MN-only
      padding `(1, 32, 32)` / `(3, 64, 32)`, both MN and K padding
      `(7, 160, 32)`, and a larger padded shape `(127, 4096, 32)`. Each runs
      with and without the poisoned-scale-buffer variant, so padded scale
      indices are verified to be zeroed for the 2-lane subgroup too.

### Results

Built incrementally against this branch (CUDA 13.1, `cmake --build --preset
release --target _C_stable_libtorch`) and run on 1x GB300 (SM103):

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py -q
189 passed, 16 warnings in 67.82s

$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_per_token_group_quant.py -q
130 passed, 16 warnings in 35.79s
```

`pre-commit run --files <the 6 changed files>` passes (ruff, clang-format,
mypy, SPDX).

### Model evaluation

Not applicable: no existing caller reaches either new path. `apply_q_norm`
defaults to `True`, reproducing the previous kernel exactly, and no in-tree
caller requests `group_size=32`. Serving output is unchanged by construction,
and the bit-exactness assertions above are the stronger check. The model-level
evals for the consumer of these paths belong to #56201.

## Note

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to extract these changes from #56201, run
the build, and run the tests. I have reviewed every changed line and ran the
test commands above myself.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Route softmax MoE top-k, including fused shared-expert sigmoid, through AITER topk_gating
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On ROCm, softmax MoE routing uses AITER's legacy `topkGatingSoftmax` launcher. This routes `FusedTopKRouter` and the fused-shared-expert router (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`) through `aiter.ops.topk.topk_gating` instead, which keeps selected-mass renormalization in-kernel (ROCm/aiter#4460), has the E=512 `prefill_n` dispatch (ROCm/aiter#5334), and with ROCm/aiter#6306 scores the shared-expert columns with sigmoid in the same launch. `dispatch_topk_softmax_func` decides per launch between `topk_gating` and the legacy `topk_softmax`. This PR makes the selection the default on CDNA3 and CDNA4 (gfx942, gfx950); every other architecture keeps the legacy launcher. gfx950 is the main sweep; gfx942 (MI300-class) was verified more lightly (see the gfx942 section). The blast radius is implicitly limited to Qwens, because based on my search other models won't use the `topk_gating`.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for `topk_gating` and `aiter topk softmax`; no other PR routes softmax top-k through `topk_gating`. #57246 fixes the eager `torch.topk` fallback in `fused_topk_bias`, and #55147 fixes the width of the `topk_ids` buffer AITER's kernels write; neither changes which AITER launcher is used.

## Claims

- On the same nightly, with only this PR and ROCm/aiter#6306 added, `topk_gating` is **+0.7% to +1.5% output-throughput geomean per cell** for Flash-Next (E=512, top-10, one shared expert) at TP2 with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` 1 and 0, at three `max-num-batched-tokens` (2048, 4096, 8192), and **+1.3% to +1.9%** for Qwen3-30B-A3B (E=128, top-8) at TP1 in two passes per cell, over the four rows that repeat. Single-stream decode (1k/1k, concurrency 1) is the largest effect: +2.0% to +4.4% in every cell.
- Kernel: for E=512 / top-10 with one shared expert, `topk_gating` is 37–47% faster than `topk_softmax(..., "sigmoid")` at T ≤ 1024 and level at T = 2048–4096 (AITER op test, table below).
- No directional accuracy change: GSM8K on all 9 cells, paired, 134 problems fixed and 126 broken in total (net +8 of 11,871), no cell below p = 0.12. The six cells of the Qwen3-30B rerun are also consistent with noise (no cell below p = 0.39).
- gfx942 (MI300-class): the kernel passes AITER's op test and the vLLM unit tests there with zero routing mismatches, is neutral to slightly positive end to end (+2.0% and +0.45% output-throughput geomean on Qwen3-30B at mbt 4096 and 2048; +1.4% to +4.7% on three Flash-Next-FP8 TP2 rows), and GSM8K is unchanged (no cell below p = 0.16). This is a lighter check than the gfx950 sweep; details below.
- Which launches change: on CDNA3 and CDNA4 (gfx942, gfx950), contiguous gating rows with T ≤ 4096 tokens, and shared experts only with sigmoid scoring and 1, 2, 4 or 8 shared experts. Everything else, and every other GPU architecture, keeps `topk_softmax`. **There is no env var to turn it on/off.**

## Validation

**Unit tests.** On one MI355X, in the candidate image (below):

```bash
pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py tests/model_executor/test_enabled_custom_ops.py -k topk
# 74 passed, 19 deselected   (at b4c61b0e0)
pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py tests/model_executor/test_enabled_custom_ops.py
# 93 passed
```

On gfx942 (MI300-class), on the nightly base with this PR's net diff and the gate change applied: 35 passed in `test_enabled_custom_ops.py -k topk` and 39 in `test_rocm_aiter_topk.py`.

`tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py` checks the shared-expert suffix against a torch reference; `test_topk_softmax_dispatch_aiter_topk_gating` pins which launcher each launch shape takes, on the enabled architectures and (monkeypatched) on another one: shared-expert sigmoid with 1/2/4/8 shared experts, an unsupported count, wrong or missing shared scoring, mismatched row strides, a narrow weights buffer, non-contiguous rows, T = 4096 versus 4097, and the kill switch (each launch shape on gfx950 and elsewhere).

**Kernel evidence.** `op_tests/test_moe_topk_gating.py` from ROCm/aiter#6306, MI355X, E=512, top-10, bf16, renorm, one shared expert. Mean kernel time per call, one run, lower is better. Every case has 0 routing mismatches against a torch reference.

| T | `topk_gating` (µs) | legacy `topk_softmax` (µs) | Δ |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 5.56 | 9.76 | −43% |
| 16 | 5.87 | 10.51 | −44% |
| 64 | 5.86 | 10.86 | −46% |
| 256 | 6.05 | 11.42 | −47% |
| 1024 | 6.56 | 10.42 | −37% |
| 2048 | 10.66 | 10.60 | +0.5% |
| 4096 | 12.84 | 13.14 | −2.3% |

Above T = 1024 the kernel runs its shared-memory fallback, which is level with the legacy launcher; above T = 4096 vLLM keeps the legacy launcher (`_AITER_TOPK_GATING_MAX_TOKENS`), where an earlier measurement had `topk_gating` losing at 8K-token prefill chunks.

**End to end.** MI355X (gfx950). Both arms are the same image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93`; the candidate adds only this PR's vLLM diff. Server flags in both arms: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `--max-num-seqs 256`, `--no-enable-prefix-caching`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`, `--trust-remote-code`, thinking off, and `--max-num-batched-tokens` as in the column. It was verified that every candidate server loaded `module_moe_topk`; no control server did. Router `T` is the decode concurrency in decode rows and `min(mbt, prompt)` per prefill chunk, so prefill chunks at mbt 8192 take the legacy launcher in both arms.

Flash-Next is `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4` at TP2 (`--max-model-len 262144 --reasoning-parser qwen3`). Qwen3-30B-A3B is `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` (bf16) at TP1.

**Flash-Next, TP2, FSE=1.** Output tok/s, control → candidate (Δ, higher is better).

| ISL / OSL | Conc | mbt 2048 | mbt 4096 | mbt 8192 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1k/1k | 1 | 156.3 → 161.4 (+3.2%) | 157.7 → 161.5 (+2.4%) | 157.0 → 163.3 (+4.0%) |
| 1k/1k | 32 | 2122.4 → 2147.4 (+1.2%) | 2140.1 → 2165.7 (+1.2%) | 2149.2 → 2186.5 (+1.7%) |
| 1k/1k | 128 | 3887.7 → 3920.3 (+0.8%) | 3942.3 → 3961.6 (+0.5%) | 3953.8 → 3983.6 (+0.8%) |
| 8k/128 | 8 | 193.3 → 193.8 (+0.3%) | 199.9 → 200.9 (+0.5%) | 202.7 → 203.6 (+0.4%) |
| 8k/1k | 32 | 1085.0 → 1100.6 (+1.4%) | 1123.7 → 1132.8 (+0.8%) | 1133.4 → 1145.8 (+1.1%) |
| 16k/128 | 2 | 86.1 → 87.0 (+1.0%) | 89.8 → 90.8 (+1.1%) | 91.7 → 92.4 (+0.9%) |

**Flash-Next, TP2, FSE=0.** Output tok/s, control → candidate (Δ, higher is better).

| ISL / OSL | Conc | mbt 2048 | mbt 4096 | mbt 8192 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1k/1k | 1 | 137.2 → 142.4 (+3.8%) | 138.2 → 142.3 (+3.0%) | 137.4 → 140.3 (+2.1%) |
| 1k/1k | 32 | 1841.4 → 1872.3 (+1.7%) | 1846.4 → 1870.6 (+1.3%) | 1861.5 → 1883.0 (+1.2%) |
| 1k/1k | 128 | 3588.2 → 3611.0 (+0.6%) | 3629.0 → 3653.5 (+0.7%) | 3644.9 → 3626.9 (−0.5%) |
| 8k/128 | 8 | 184.8 → 182.2 (−1.4%) | 192.3 → 193.6 (+0.7%) | 196.2 → 195.2 (−0.5%) |
| 8k/1k | 32 | 1003.1 → 1012.3 (+0.9%) | 1037.1 → 1042.1 (+0.5%) | 1046.7 → 1055.0 (+0.8%) |
| 16k/128 | 2 | 81.2 → 80.6 (−0.7%) | 85.2 → 86.0 (+0.9%) | 87.1 → 88.2 (+1.2%) |

**Qwen3-30B-A3B, TP1.** Two passes per cell, with the control and candidate cards swapped between passes. Output tok/s, candidate vs control, pass 1 / pass 2 (higher is better). 

| ISL / OSL | Conc | mbt 2048 | mbt 4096 | mbt 8192 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1k/1k | 1 | +3.5% / +3.8% | +4.4% / +4.0% | +2.0% / +3.9% |
| 1k/1k | 32 | +1.5% / +0.3% | +0.7% / +1.5% | +1.1% / +1.1% |
| 1k/1k | 128 | +0.6% / +0.8% | +0.4% / +0.8% | +1.5% / +0.9% |
| 16k/128 | 2 | +0.4% / +0.4% | +0.5% / +1.2% | +0.7% / +0.2% |

Control output tok/s at mbt 4096, pass 1: 237.6, 2782.6, 6956.8 and 115.7 for the four rows.

Geomean over these four rows, pass 1 / pass 2. Positive means the candidate is better: throughput up, mean TPOT and mean TTFT down.

| mbt | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT | Mean TTFT |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2048 | +1.5% / +1.3% | +1.5% / +1.5% | −0.4% / −0.5% |
| 4096 | +1.5% / +1.9% | +1.9% / +2.0% | −1.2% / +0.5% |
| 8192 | +1.3% / +1.5% | +1.5% / +1.8% | −0.2% / −2.3% |

**Flash-Next geomean over the six rows per cell.** Positive means the candidate is better: throughput up, mean TPOT and mean TTFT down.

| Sweep | mbt | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT | Mean TTFT |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Flash-Next, TP2, FSE=1 | 2048 | +1.3% | +1.6% | −0.0% |
| Flash-Next, TP2, FSE=1 | 4096 | +1.1% | +1.4% | −1.3% |
| Flash-Next, TP2, FSE=1 | 8192 | +1.5% | +1.9% | −0.2% |
| Flash-Next, TP2, FSE=0 | 2048 | +0.8% | +1.2% | −0.3% |
| Flash-Next, TP2, FSE=0 | 4096 | +1.2% | +1.4% | −0.0% |
| Flash-Next, TP2, FSE=0 | 8192 | +0.7% | +1.0% | −1.5% |

Reading the table:

- **Gain at small `T`, flat at large `T`.** Concurrency 1 gains +2.0% to +4.4% in every cell, while the 8k and 16k rows sit at about +0.5% to +1%: their steps are dominated by prefill chunks of 2048 tokens or more, where the kernel is level with the legacy launcher (and above 4096 the legacy launcher runs in both arms). That matches the kernel table, where the saving is about 4–5 µs per layer launch at small `T` and nothing at T ≥ 2048.
- **FSE does not change the picture.** With FSE=1 the candidate also fuses the sigmoid shared-expert scoring (the suffix from #6306); with FSE=0 `topk_gating` runs without it. The cell geomeans are +1.1% to +1.5% and +0.7% to +1.2%.
- **TTFT.** Prefill is where `topk_gating` helps least, so the TTFT geomean is flat: −1.5% to +0.0% across the six Flash-Next cells and −2.3% to +0.5% across the Qwen3-30B passes, which is the size of the run-to-run noise.

**Accuracy.** GSM8K, 5-shot, `local-chat-completions`, chat template, thinking off, `max_gen_toks 2048`, seed 4321, 1319 problems per arm, strict-match. Paired per problem with `scripts/compare_samples.py` (exact McNemar). 82–84% of Flash-Next generations and 52% of Qwen3-30B generations differ textually between arms, so the claim is "no directional change", not "identical"; there is no control-versus-control baseline for that textual churn.

| Cell | Control → candidate | Fixed / broken | Exact McNemar p |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Flash-Next FSE=1, mbt 2048 | 0.9629 → 0.9636 | 17 / 16 | 1.000 |
| Flash-Next FSE=1, mbt 4096 | 0.9629 → 0.9651 | 12 / 9 | 0.664 |
| Flash-Next FSE=1, mbt 8192 | 0.9666 → 0.9598 | 9 / 18 | 0.122 |
| Flash-Next FSE=0, mbt 2048 | 0.9613 → 0.9621 | 18 / 17 | 1.000 |
| Flash-Next FSE=0, mbt 4096 | 0.9621 → 0.9636 | 14 / 12 | 0.845 |
| Flash-Next FSE=0, mbt 8192 | 0.9629 → 0.9674 | 14 / 8 | 0.286 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B, mbt 2048 | 0.9045 → 0.9030 | 16 / 18 | 0.864 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B, mbt 4096 | 0.9067 → 0.9075 | 17 / 16 | 1.000 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B, mbt 8192 | 0.9007 → 0.9045 | 17 / 12 | 0.458 |

The lowest p (0.122, Flash-Next FSE=1 at mbt 8192, net −9 problems) is the same configuration that is +1 and +3 at mbt 2048 and 4096, and at mbt 8192 prefill chunks above 4096 tokens take the legacy launcher in both arms, so only the decode steps differ there. The flexible-extract scores move the same way. The Qwen3-30B rows above are from the first sweep. The rerun's six cells (two passes at each mbt) are also consistent with noise: strict-match 0.9014–0.9083 on both arms, exact McNemar p between 0.39 and 1.0.

**gfx942 (MI300-class).** This is a verification, not a repeat of the full gfx950 sweep. Node: 8x MI300-class (gfx942), image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93` (AITER 0.1.24.post1). Candidate: this PR with the gfx942 gate plus ROCm/aiter#6306 (`15f14c767`) with `module_moe_topk` rebuilt for gfx942; the candidate server loads `module_moe_topk`, the control does not.

*Kernel.* `op_tests/test_moe_topk_gating.py` passes on gfx942: NaN/Inf, exact ties, fake-EPLB balance and the shared-expert cases, all error columns 0 (max weight error at most 3e-8). Fused `topk_gating` time for E=512, top-10, bf16, one shared expert:

| T | 1 | 16 | 256 | 1024 | 2048 | 4096 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `topk_gating` (µs) | 5.35 | 6.15 | 6.32 | 6.75 | 11.67 | 14.31 |

Against the legacy launcher, measured on the same node earlier in the session, it is 37–44% faster at T ≤ 1024, about 7% slower at T = 2048 and about 3% slower at T = 4096, with zero routing mismatches. The per-T legacy times from that run were not kept, so those percentages are not backed by a table here. The shape matches gfx950, where T = 2048 and 4096 are level.

*End to end.* Qwen3-30B-A3B, TP1, arms side by side on one card each, output tok/s control → candidate:

| ISL / OSL | Conc | mbt 2048 | mbt 4096 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1k/1k | 1 | 236.0 → 245.9 (+4.2%) | 235.2 → 244.6 (+4.0%) |
| 1k/1k | 32 | 1934.6 → 1947.3 (+0.7%) | 1953.4 → 1987.0 (+1.7%) |
| 1k/1k | 128 | 4392.1 → 4314.1 (−1.8%) | 4373.0 → 4475.2 (+2.3%) |
| 8k/128 | 8 | 141.7 → 141.2 (−0.4%) | 179.1 → 181.1 (+1.1%) |
| 8k/1k | 32 | 668.7 → 666.0 (−0.4%) | 833.3 → 843.2 (+1.2%) |
| 16k/128 | 2 | 78.2 → 78.6 (+0.5%) | 86.7 → 88.2 (+1.7%) |
| geomean | | +0.45% | +2.0% |

Flash-Next-FP8 (`Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`) at TP2, FSE=1, mbt 4096. NB! The MXFP4 checkpoint does not run on gfx942. 

| ISL / OSL | Conc | control | candidate | Δ |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1k/1k | 1 | 119.2 | 124.8 | +4.7% |
| 1k/1k | 32 | 1259.4 | 1301.6 | +3.4% |
| 8k/1k | 32 | 677.8 | 687.3 | +1.4% |


*Accuracy.* GSM8K, same settings as the gfx950 table, paired, exact McNemar:

| Cell | Metric | Control → candidate | Fixed / broken | p |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-30B, mbt 4096 | strict-match | 0.9128 → 0.9121 | 17 / 18 | 1.000 |
| Qwen3-30B, mbt 4096 | flexible-extract | 0.9181 → 0.9174 | 14 / 15 | 1.000 |
| Qwen3-30B, mbt 2048 | strict-match | 0.9158 → 0.9090 | 12 / 21 | 0.163 |
| Qwen3-30B, mbt 2048 | flexible-extract | 0.9204 → 0.9151 | 11 / 18 | 0.265 |
| Flash-Next-FP8 TP2, mbt 4096 | strict-match | 0.9704 → 0.9727 | 4 / 1 | 0.375 |
| Flash-Next-FP8 TP2, mbt 4096 | flexible-extract | 0.9697 → 0.9719 | 4 / 1 | 0.375 |

No cell is significant. 

**Reproduce:**

```bash
# control: vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93
# candidate: the same image with this PR and ROCm/aiter#6306 applied
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --reasoning-parser qwen3 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --trust-remote-code \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'

python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm --dataset-name random --request-rate inf \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 128 --warmup-requests 32 --seed 302

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,timeout=1200,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,max_gen_toks=2048 \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template --batch_size 32 --seed 4321 --log_samples

pytest -q tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py tests/model_executor/test_enabled_custom_ops.py -k topk
```

The other rows use `--random-input-len/--random-output-len/--max-concurrency/--num-prompts/--warmup-requests/--seed` of 1024/1024/1/8/1/301, 1024/1024/128/256/128/303, 8192/128/8/32/8/304, 8192/1024/32/64/32/305 and 16384/128/2/8/2/306.

## Details

**What runs before and after.** Before, every softmax top-k on ROCm with AITER (`FusedTopKRouter`, and the fused-shared-expert router) ran `topk_softmax`, AITER's legacy launcher. After, `dispatch_topk_softmax_func` takes the launch's tensors and shared-expert arguments and returns `rocm_aiter_ops.topk_gating` on CDNA3 and CDNA4 (gfx942, gfx950) when `_aiter_topk_gating_supported` accepts the launch, and `topk_softmax` otherwise (including on every other architecture). `_aiter_topk_gating_supported` accepts contiguous gating rows with at most 4096 tokens; with shared experts it also needs sigmoid scoring, 1, 2, 4 or 8 of them, `topk_weights` and `topk_indices` sharing a row stride, and `topk_weights` wide enough for the shared columns. The shared-expert ids stay as the caller prefilled them, as with the legacy launcher. `_rocm_aiter_topk_gating_impl` is a plain call into `aiter.ops.topk.topk_gating`; the router runs inside the opaque `moe_forward` custom op, so nothing here changes graph capture.

**Why the 4096-token cap.** At E=512 / top-10 the kernel is level with the legacy launcher at T = 2048 and 4096 and was slower at 8K-token prefill chunks in an earlier measurement, so above 4096 the legacy launcher keeps serving. The cap is a named constant in the router, not a magic number.

**Why no env var.** The sweep shows a small positive effect at every shape tested on gfx950 and no reproducible loss, so there is nothing to opt into, and the path is the default under the existing AITER enablement (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE`) on gfx942 and gfx950. gfx942 was verified more lightly than gfx950 (see the gfx942 section); the gate is one line (`is_topk_gating_enabled`), so another architecture can be added the same way once it is measured.
