title: [Feat][Model] Support encoder-side SWA-bounded replay for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 keeps a 128-token sliding-window (SWA) KV cache per layer beside its prefix-cacheable compressed MLA and indexer caches. Storing that window for prefix caching and KV connectors costs more than it saves, so this implements DeepSeek's encoder-side "SWA bounded replay": the SWA caches leave prefix caching, and after a prefix hit ending at H the scheduler recomputes the hit's last window [H-128, H) to rebuild them. The replayed tokens keep their cached KV in every other group, their window attention reads nothing below H-128, and decode always sees a full window. Outputs after a hit are therefore not bit-identical to a cold run, by design.

- KV cache spec: `SlidingWindowMLASpec(bounded_replay=True)` derives `prefix_cacheable=False` and `prefix_replay_tokens=sliding_window`; `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` forwards both to the worker.
- Scheduler: a hit records `Request.replay_start = H-128` and rewinds the computed count by the window; async KV-connector loads replay once the KV arrives; chunks ending inside the replayed range allocate nothing new; hits no longer than the window are not adopted.
- Worker: only DeepSeek-V4.1 replays, so `DeepseekV41ModelState` owns the per-request replay start. `add_request` stores it; `prepare_attn` gathers it for the batch's prefills, pads the replayed tokens' slots in the prefix-cacheable groups with one Triton kernel, and hands the starts to the sparse SWA metadata builder through a `ModelSpecificAttnMetadata`. The runner core is untouched apart from an optional `model_specific_attn_metadata` argument on `DefaultModelState.prepare_attn`.
- DeepSeek-V4.1 kernels clamp the window at `replay_start`: the SWA index and gather-length kernels, the FlashInfer mixed index kernel and the FlashMLA combine kernel. The compressed slot mappings (MLA and indexer) inherit the padding of the tokens' own slots, so a replayed token never re-enters the compressed caches.
- Switch: `--swa-bounded-replay` (`CacheConfig.swa_bounded_replay`, default on), read by the V4.1 attention layer. Needs model runner V2 and no prefill context parallelism; otherwise it logs once and keeps the SWA cache in prefix caching.
- One bugfix rides along as its own commit: KV-connector hits are taken in whole blocks under replay.

Known gap: a running request restarted in place under `kv_load_failure_policy=recompute` keeps its worker-side replay boundary and would recompute with a stale clamp; a follow-up will preempt such requests instead. No other open PR implements SWA replay.

## Usage

Nothing to configure: DeepSeek-V4.1 replays by default on model runner V2. `--no-swa-bounded-replay` restores the previous behaviour (SWA KV stored in the prefix cache). With replay on, KV connectors transfer only the MLA and indexer caches, and hits of at most 128 tokens are not adopted.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_start.py tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py
```

Accuracy: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` on TP4 GB200 with `vllm serve`, gsm8k (5-shot) run twice against the same server; pass 2 re-sends every prompt, so each request is a full-prompt prefix hit that replays only its last window (92.6% prefix-cache hit rate).

## Test Result

All listed tests pass; pre-commit and mypy are clean.

| gsm8k, n=1319 (pass 1 cold / pass 2 all hits) | replay on (this PR) | replay off (`--no-swa-bounded-replay`) |
|---|---|---|
| exact_match (flexible-extract) | 0.9272 / 0.9212 | 0.9295 / 0.9295 |

Both arms are within run-to-run noise (one standard error at n=1319 is 0.0075); the gap is the same in pass 1, where only the shared few-shot prefix is replayed. An earlier two-pass GPQA-diamond run on an internal pre-release checkpoint showed the same parity (0.6869 / 0.6919 with replay vs 0.7020 / 0.6869 without, n=198).

title: [Model] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Model Definitions
body:
Split out from #56214 — this PR includes **only** the changes under `vllm/models/`:

- Adds the new `vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/` model definition package (nvidia, amd, and common code paths)
- Includes the associated modifications to `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/`

All other changes from #56214 (kernels, rust parser, config, tests, etc.) are intentionally excluded.

**Non-duplication:** This is not a competing implementation — it is a scoped subset of #56214 (same author group), split out so the model definitions can be reviewed independently.

**Rebase note:** `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py` conflicted with #50176 (which migrated the kernel to the `VllmTritonJitKernel` warmup class) and #56035 (PDL warmup fix). The resolution ports this change's `QUANTIZE` toggle, `NOPE_DIM`-based rope offset, and vectorized UE8M0 scale packing onto the new class structure, and keeps the `launch_pdl=current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl()` fix.

**AI assistance:** This PR was prepared with AI assistance (branch split and conflict resolution).

**Testing:** No tests were run locally for this split (no CUDA/ROCm environment on the authoring machine). The branch content is byte-identical to #56214 for all files except the rebased `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py`; CI on this PR plus the kernel tests in #56214 (`tests/kernels/test_fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py`) should be the source of truth.

title: [DSA] Wire DeepGEMM sparse MQA logits into the DeepSeek V4.1 indexer
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek V4.1 selects attention tokens in two levels: one indexer layer publishes the top candidate blocks of the context, and the indexer layers after it pick their top-k inside those blocks. Today the consumer layers still score the **whole** context with dense MQA logits and then mask everything outside the candidates. DeepGEMM 2.8 ships sparse MQA-logits kernels (deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#432) that score only a given list of blocks, so this PR lets the consumer layers score just the candidate blocks. Their logits work goes from O(context) to O(candidate blocks), a fixed 16K positions for V4.1-Flash, and their top-k runs in that compressed space and is mapped back to context positions.

Design:

- **A separate indexer, not a branch in the dense one.** The consumer layers use a new `SparseMQAIndexer` layer with its own backend and attention metadata (`DeepseekV41SparseIndexerBackend`, `DeepseekV41SparseIndexerMetadata`). It is a plain module rather than a custom op: V4.1 does not go through `torch.compile`, and the attention layer already runs the indexer inside its breakable-CUDA-graph eager segment. The dense `SparseAttnIndexer` op is untouched. The candidate-source layer and the indexers before it stay dense.
- **Every requirement is checked once, at engine start.** The metadata builder validates the model, the MXFP4 indexer cache, the GPU generation, the DeepGEMM version, the DeepSelect extension and the logits/top-k layout it needs, and raises a clear error instead of silently falling back per step. There is no PyTorch fallback anywhere on the path: the candidate expansion and the index remap are Triton kernels, the top-k is DeepSelect.
- **Nothing is allocated or recomputed on the hot path.** The builder owns the per-row scratch; the candidate-block expansion and the DeepGEMM schedule depend only on the candidates, which are identical for all consumer layers of a step, so the first consumer computes them and the others reuse them through the shared metadata.
- **No dtype casts on the hot path.** The sparse kernels take bf16 weights and emit bf16 logits. The fused Q RoPE-quant kernel that produces the per-head weights writes them in bf16 for this indexer (fp32 for the dense one), and DeepSelect (#56464) runs the top-k on the bf16 logits directly.
- **Opt-in** via `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "mxfp4", "indexer_sparse_logits": true}'`. Below ~16K tokens the candidates cover the whole context and the dense path is cheaper, so the default stays off; the feature is for long-context serving.
- **One KV-layout requirement.** DeepGEMM's paged kernels address pages as `base + page * stride` and need that stride 512B-aligned. In V4.1's block-major layout the stride is the whole block (all layers' pages), which is not 512-aligned. `MLAAttentionSpec` gains `block_stride_alignment`, and the block size is rounded up to it in the same place HiSparse already rounds it (`_get_kv_cache_bytes_per_block`). With the flag on this costs 0.8% of KV memory; with it off nothing changes.

## Test Plan

- `tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py`: candidate-expansion math and a randomized comparison of the Triton expansion against a PyTorch reference (including strided inputs); exact selected-value parity of the sparse path with `torch.topk` over dense bf16 logits masked to the candidates, for prefill and paged decode, including spec-decode rows, CUDA-graph capture/replay and schedule reuse by a later layer; kernel numerics vs a PyTorch fp32 reference. `tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_rope_quant.py`: the bf16 weights output of the fused Q kernel (Triton and CuTeDSL) equals the fp32 result rounded once. mypy and ruff via pre-commit.
- Kernel microbenchmark of the per-layer indexer pipeline (dense logits + mask + top-k vs sparse logits + top-k + remap) with an exact selected-value parity check, GB300, CUDA-graph replay.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP=4 on 4x GB300, MXFP4 indexer cache, greedy, prefix caching off, flag on vs off: decode and prefill throughput from 8K to 1M context, and long-context NLL.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 28 passed. The sparse kernels produce bitwise the same bf16 logits as the dense kernels on the candidate columns, so the tests assert that the sparse path selects exactly the same values per row as `torch.topk` over dense bf16 logits masked to the candidates; only tie order among equal values may differ.

**Kernel level** (GB300, speedup of the sparse indexer pipeline over the dense one per consumer layer; decode rows are one query per request, the prefill column is a chunk of query rows sharing their sequence's K. V4.1-Flash has 4 consumer layers, the first one also pays the once-per-step candidate expansion, which lowers its speedup by 20-50%):

| context | decode, batch 64 | decode, batch 256 | prefill chunk |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8K | 1.2x | 1.2x | 1.6x |
| 32K | 1.7x | 1.8x | 2.3x |
| 128K | 4.4x | 5.8x | 8.3x |
| 512K | 14.4x | 22.9x | |

**End to end** (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP=4, 4x GB300; decode and prefill throughput of the whole batch, from a linear fit of wall time against output length):

| batch x context | decode tok/s off | decode tok/s on | decode speedup | prefill tok/s off | prefill tok/s on | prefill speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 x 8K | 5,570 | 5,895 | 1.06x | 68,712 | 65,541 | 0.95x |
| 32 x 100K | 3,263 | 3,434 | 1.05x | 60,508 | 64,306 | 1.06x |
| 16 x 256K | 2,055 | 2,153 | 1.05x | 48,504 | 57,670 | 1.19x |
| 8 x 512K | 1,057 | 1,107 | 1.05x | 34,127 | 48,805 | 1.43x |
| 4 x 1M | 568 | 583 | 1.03x | 16,261 | 32,517 | 2.00x |

Decode gets 3-6% faster: the indexer is only a few percent of a decode step at these batch sizes. Prefill is where the O(context) cost shows: the dense indexer's fp32 logits grow with the context and are chunked, written and read back several times, while the sparse rows stay 16K wide, so prefill throughput is 1.2x at 256K, 1.4x at 512K and 2x at 1M, while at 8K it is 5% slower.

**Accuracy** (78K-token real document, mean NLL of the next token by position; the sparse kernels score in bf16, the dense path in fp32). Two runs of the same configuration differ by up to 0.002 per bucket (TP=4 run-to-run noise), and on/off differ by the same amount:

| position | 0-16K | 16K-32K | 32K-64K | 64K-78K |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| off | 0.4001 | 0.3715 | 0.3523 | 0.3735 |
| on | 0.4022 | 0.3706 | 0.3526 | 0.3755 |
| on, second run | 0.4010 | 0.3719 | 0.3534 | 0.3737 |

## Requirements and limitations

- SM100-class GPUs, DeepGEMM >= 2.8 (the repo pin is older; the flag fails at startup with a clear message on older builds), the DeepSelect extension (`vllm._deepselect_C`, built with vllm) and the MXFP4 indexer cache (the kernels take UE8M0 scales). `--sparse-indexer-topk-backend` must be `auto` or `deep_select`. Not supported with DCP/PCP.
- The sparse kernels score in bf16 with bf16 weights (no fp32 option), so the flag changes the indexer's score precision; greedy outputs are not token-identical to the dense path (see the NLL table).

AI assistance: this change was developed with an AI coding agent; the human submitter reviewed the full diff and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend][Renderer] Align DeepSeek tool-call arguments with deepseek-recipe
body:
## Purpose

Align Rust DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 assistant tool-call argument encoding with the shared [deepseek-recipe reference implementation](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-recipe/blob/8cadfede7063c896b944e7bae05daa3549ae97ea/deepseek-recipe-encoding/src/v4/mod.rs#L48-L69).

Both dialects attempt one JSON object parse. Objects are rendered as individual DSML parameters; invalid JSON and non-object JSON are preserved verbatim as a single `arguments` parameter with `string="true"`. This also preserves double-encoded JSON strings verbatim. For example, `not json` renders as `<｜DSML｜ parameter name="arguments" string="true">not json</｜DSML｜ parameter>` in V4.1.

## Test Plan

```sh
cd rust
cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat --lib -E 'test(renderer::deepseek)'
cargo clippy -p vllm-chat --lib --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings
```

`tool_call_arguments_preserve_non_objects_like_recipe` exercises both renderers with plain text, arrays, null, numbers, booleans, empty text, JSON strings, and double-encoded objects.

## Test Result

- All 50 selected DeepSeek renderer tests passed, including the existing object-argument fixtures.
- Clippy and pre-commit passed.
- CPU reference checks confirmed recipe's shared V4/V4.1 fallback behavior. GPU/model evaluation was not run.

AI assistance: Claude Code for the original patch; Codex for recipe alignment and validation.

title: [DSv4.1] Integrate Mega-Gate from DeepGEMM
body:
## Summary

Integrate DeepGEMM Mega-Gate into the DeepSeek V4/V4.1 DeepGEMM MegaMoE path, fusing the gate GEMM and expert selection. Prepare routing metadata once per model forward and reuse it across layers. Preserve hash routing for V4, image routing bias for V4.1, draft-layer expert counts, MTP warmup, and decoder auxiliary-state capture.

Two integration fixes are included:

- Let CMake FetchContent update an existing DeepGEMM checkout when its pinned revision changes. Previously, finding `csrc/python_api.cpp` skipped the update entirely and could rebuild 2.6.1 without `bf16_mega_gate` despite the new pin.
- ~~Clear padded hidden-state rows in place before Mega-Gate. NaN padding can trigger the kernel's finite-score assertion, later surfacing as a CUDA launch failure or NCCL error. `masked_fill_` avoids allocating a separate hidden-state tensor; valid rows are unchanged. Regression cases cover NaN padding for both main/draft and text/image routing.~~ Removed, fixed by https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/11

Update (17 Sep 2026)
- Since Mega-Gate underperforms for M<=16 (as LL-GEMM is very efficient), we only dispatch Mega-Gate for M>16

## Accuracy: full GSM8K

The final in-place implementation was evaluated locally through Vigil on **4× GB200**, using real `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` weights, the current repository checkout, CUDA 13.1, and PyTorch 2.13.0. No engine overrides beyond TP4, EP, and the MegaMoE backend were supplied; CUDA Graphs remained enabled.

| Metric | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Questions | 1319 |
| Correct | **1194** |
| Accuracy | **90.5231%** |
| Invalid responses | **0** |
| API failures | **0** |
| Worker errors | **0** |
| Evaluation time | 161.79 s |


## Kernel benchmark: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Gate

Measured on a **single NVIDIA GB300 (SM103)** with BF16 inputs `[M, 5120]`, BF16 gate weights `[384, 5120]`, **top-k=6**, `sqrtsoftplus`, normalization, and routed scaling factor **1.5**. **M is the number of token rows processed on one GPU**, not serving request concurrency.

The baseline is `GateLinear + fused_topk_bias`, using its normal shape-dependent dispatch. Mega-Gate fuses the gate GEMM and expert selection. The updated DeepGEMM pin allows non-finite padding scores, eliminating the separate hidden-state padding clear; existing input staging discards padded routes.

**Mega-Gate achieves 1.18–1.31× routing speedup for M ≥ 32, with no meaningful speedup for M ≤ 16.** Speedup is baseline latency divided by Mega-Gate latency.

| Tokens M | GateLinear + top-k (μs) | Mega-Gate (μs) | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6.640 | 8.096 | 0.820× |
| 2 | 6.848 | 8.032 | 0.853× |
| 4 | 6.752 | 8.032 | 0.841× |
| 8 | 8.064 | 8.224 | 0.981× |
| 16 | 8.256 | 8.256 | 1.000× |
| 32 | 10.112 | 8.304 | 1.218× |
| 64 | 10.353 | 8.448 | 1.225× |
| 128 | 11.200 | 8.896 | 1.259× |
| 256 | 11.488 | 9.696 | 1.185× |
| 512 | 13.520 | 10.720 | 1.261× |
| 1024 | 16.000 | 12.448 | 1.285× |
| 2048 | 18.913 | 15.872 | 1.192× |
| 4096 | 27.729 | 22.944 | 1.209× |
| 8192 | 46.752 | 35.745 | 1.308× |

**Method:** FlashInfer CUPTI timing of CUDA-graph replays with cold L2, 25 warmups, three rounds with alternating implementation order, and 100 samples per round. Values are medians of the round medians. Allocation, compilation, graph capture, input generation, routing metadata preparation, expert input staging, expert execution, and communication are outside the timed region. These measurements do not establish an E2E serving speedup.

**Correctness:** Expert IDs matched exactly at every batch size; routing weights matched with `rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-4`. Synthetic inputs and separated correction biases avoid ambiguous top-k boundaries. An additional 48 CUDA-graph replay cases passed with NaN/Inf padding across text, image, and hash/image routing.

**Versions:** vLLM `ef50fde183`, DeepGEMM `40d109bf`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA toolkit `13.1`, FlashInfer `0.6.18`, and CUPTI Python `13.0.1`.

## Related work and AI assistance

This updates the existing Mega-Gate PR rather than opening another implementation. Open-PR searches for `56266 in:body` and `Mega-Gate` were checked before reopening. Dependency/API changes overlap intentionally with #56876; that PR supplies the dependency update, while this PR adds the Mega-Gate routing integration. The upstream Mega-Gate implementation is tracked in https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/432.

OpenAI Codex assisted with the port, dependency alignment, conflict resolution, build-cache and padding fixes, compilation, debugging, and validation. Dependency/API changes adapted from #56876 are attributed in the commit history.

title: [Bugfix][Tool Calling] Tool parser non-streaming parse drops post-tool-call text that streaming returns
body:
## Purpose

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56263

For a model output that contains text before AND after a tool call, the two delivery modes disagree: streaming returns the post-tool text, non-streaming drops it. The tool parser is inconsistent with its own streaming mode.

## Changes made
The parser now appends text following a complete outer tool-call wrapper while preserving the existing behavior for an incomplete wrapper. The new test verifies identical content and tool extraction in both delivery modes.

## Test Plan
Added a regression test in `tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv3_tool_parser.py`. It runs in both streaming and non streaming mode.

## Test Result
Test ran successfully on my local machine.

title: [Quantization] Support packed NVFP4 Qwen4Exp PLE embeddings
body:
## Purpose

Enable the `local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` checkpoint to run on **1x DGX Spark without CPU or disk PLE offloading**. Its packed NVFP4 ngram table occupies 26.822 GiB and remains resident in CUDA memory. The PR's resident path was validated on one GB10 with a 4,096-token context, 2 GiB KV cache, and MTP disabled; model loading reported 97.47 GiB.

Fixes #56272.

Support `ple_embedding_dtype="nvfp4"` in Qwen4Exp ngram embeddings. The [local-inference-lab checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4/tree/ada4da32a583a78aa47299f45a70603c950490b8) stores each logical 160-value row as 80 packed E2M1 bytes and 10 E4M3 block scales, with one FP32 global scale. Upstream currently selects an unquantized table for this explicit storage format inside a ModelOpt mixed-precision checkpoint.

The change adds an embedding method to the existing device/pinned-host storage interface. Both paths keep packed weights and block scales in their original storage and decode only the requested rows. Lookup reuses the existing E2M1 decoder and produces activation-dtype rows before ETP reduction. The loader copies each checkpoint shard's overlap with the local ETP vocabulary range and validates coverage after all weight streams finish, along with the global scale, tensor shapes, and storage dtypes.

Related work was checked on September 10, 2026. [#54882](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54882) and [#55334](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55334) concern an FP8 PLE table inside a model with NVFP4 body weights. [#53899](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53899) contains an older NVFP4 PLE implementation within offload work, but its mixed-precision dispatch does not select this checkpoint's explicit NVFP4 table. [#42791](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42791) adds generic quantized vocabulary embeddings. This change targets the serialized split PLE layout through the storage interface merged in [#54371](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54371).

AI assistance was used to develop and test this change.

## Test Plan

Extend the existing PLE suite with streamed packed-weight/block-scale loading across ETP boundaries, missing row coverage, malformed storage/global scales, independent numerical decoding, compiled GPU lookup, CUDA graph replay with changing IDs, empty/padded inputs, and pinned-host prefetch. Add the NVFP4 cases to the existing H200 Qwen4Exp CI lane.

Test base: `b28c3e1568bfae930f61d4b24940e47528c85d4a`, with the matching upstream precompiled CUDA wheel, Torch `2.13.0+cu130`, and FlashInfer `0.6.18.post1`. GPUs: one isolated RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q and one DGX Spark / GB10. The Spark run used the published PR commit `e251861aab69d3eb438d1a76ddec036ae45cfd4c`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v --tb=short --timeout=300 \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v --tb=short --timeout=600 \
  tests/compile/h100/test_startup.py::test_moe_startup
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py .buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py
```

Full-model text-generation validation used the pinned checkpoint above (image/video inputs disabled), a 4,096-token context, 512-token prefill chunks, four sequences, 2 GiB of KV cache, and full/piecewise CUDA graph capture sizes `[1, 2, 4]`. The offline harness ran with `PYTHONPATH=/opt/ngram/vllm:/run/ngram /opt/ngram/.venv/bin/python /run/ngram/model_smoke.py` on Max-Q and `model_smoke_spark.py` on Spark. Spark used `engram_config={"cpu_offload":false}` and `cpu_offload_gb=0`; Max-Q used pinned-host PLE storage. It checked selected rows from the complete table against an independent decoder, then four chat prompts and the first 32 canonical GSM8K test examples (temperature 0, thinking disabled, 768 output tokens).

## Test Result

- PLE and configuration suites: 76 passed on Max-Q and 76 passed on DGX Spark.
- Compilation startup canary on Max-Q: 2 passed.
- Actual checkpoint sample: 8 rows of width 160 matched an independent E2M1/FP8/global-scale reference exactly after BF16 conversion, through both device lookup and pinned-host prefetch with simulated ETP ownership.
- CPU PLE/configuration suites: 43 passed, 33 skipped because CUDA was unavailable.
- Pre-commit, including Python 3.10 type checks, and manual Python 3.12 type checks: passed.
- Full checkpoint loaded with 26.822 GiB of packed PLE weights/scales in CUDA memory on Spark and pinned host memory on Max-Q. On both devices, selected rows from the full table, including addresses beyond 32-bit offsets, matched the independent BF16 reference exactly.
- Full-model startup captured all six CUDA graphs on each device. All four generation checks passed on each, including a prompt requiring chunked prefill.
- GSM8K smoke evaluation: 31/32 exact numeric answers (96.875%) on each GPU. On each device, the remaining response hit the 768-token limit. This is a small smoke evaluation, not a full benchmark or comparison with the checkpoint publisher's runtime.

The checkpoint uses preview architecture names. Validation normalizes them with `hf_overrides={"model_type":"qwen4_exp","architectures":["Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration"]}`. PLE offload is disabled on Spark and enabled on Max-Q. It selects `kernel_config={"linear_backend":"marlin"}` because the automatic MXFP8 linear backend rejects the checkpoint's 96-output GDN projection. Real multi-GPU collectives and MTP have not been validated with this PR.

## Single-Spark reference measurements

Separate end-to-end measurements on September 10, 2026 compared the [local-inference-lab checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4/tree/ada4da32a583a78aa47299f45a70603c950490b8) using its b12x runtime with the [NVIDIA checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4/tree/fc694b54fb0174e0913e6adf86691ef85a4ead47) using upstream vLLM plus disk PLE offload patches. These measurements provide context for fitting the checkpoints on one DGX Spark. They were collected independently of this PR and do not measure its performance impact.

Workload: 32,768 shared prefix tokens, 2,048 suffix tokens, and 256 output tokens; streaming chat, temperature 0, three warmups per cell, and concurrency 1/4/8 with 10/40/80 measured requests. Both runtimes used one GB10, TP1/PP1, a 40,960-token context limit, prefix caching, chunked prefill, and MTP with four draft tokens. Latency and TTFT are means; decode throughput is aggregate active decode throughput from AIPerf.

| Checkpoint / runtime | Concurrency | Requests | Latency (s) | TTFT (s) | Decode (tok/s) | Acceptance length |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| local-inference-lab / b12x | 1 | 10 | 11.27 | 3.40 | 32.41 | 2.40 |
| local-inference-lab / b12x | 4 | 40 | 28.19 | 5.44 | 36.31 | 2.13 |
| local-inference-lab / b12x | 8 | 80 | 45.99 | 6.75 | 43.44 | 2.20 |
| NVIDIA / vLLM with disk PLE | 1 | 10 | 14.30 | 3.45 | 23.51 | 2.64 |
| NVIDIA / vLLM with disk PLE | 4 | 40 | 29.60 | 5.09 | 34.25 | 2.39 |
| NVIDIA / vLLM with disk PLE | 8 | 80 | 44.34 | 7.12 | 45.92 | 2.59 |

Each checkpoint completed all 130 measured requests with zero errors and zero preemptions. Every measured response contained 256 output tokens. Acceptance length is `1 + accepted_tokens / draft_steps`, calculated from server counters.

The local checkpoint's packed PLE payload is 26.822 GiB, held in b12x's resident managed CUDA weight storage with no explicit CPU or disk PLE offload; KV cache was 8 GiB FP8. The NVIDIA checkpoint's FP8 PLE payload is 47.684 GiB, served through disk-backed mmap and the OS page cache; KV cache was 10 GiB BF16. Quantization, backends, and prefix reuse also differ (27,216 versus 30,704 reused tokens per request), so this is a comparison of complete configurations. Each cell is a single run, and accuracy equivalence was not evaluated. Host swap activity was observed, so no swap-free claim is made.

<details>
<summary>Reference runtime revisions</summary>

- Local runtime: [vLLM `aba94d396`](https://github.com/local-inference-lab/vllm/tree/aba94d396d27ea92a2044ad024c003b36da505d3), [b12x `75ffee637`](https://github.com/lukealonso/b12x/tree/75ffee6375b0577ce2c8d6931ffacefda3ecbdd6).
- NVIDIA runtime: upstream [`73029d424`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/73029d42441321b631779db3475031f5ec26dd6c), with [#54129 at `50a061f79`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/50a061f792f36364f5f95a93eee21f1e9d77f65e), [#54882 at `d4d703caf`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/d4d703caf908786416585ceb1f369e2e0363358b), [#55513 at `60ad959b6`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/60ad959b6f1a5c8f602edbd608c8decbc0788c50), and [#56026 at `4a365dee4`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/4a365dee4aed8ae3135213b4cf6ce04f6d82e756).
- AIPerf [`00ba1c5db`](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aiperf/tree/00ba1c5db3fbe5f7e9852fcba2f1f0e269d0f13a); Torch `2.13.0+cu130`, FlashInfer `0.6.18`, NVIDIA driver `580.95.05`.

</details>

title: [MRV1] Scope breakable cudagraphs to the piecewise path only
body:
`VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` no longer overrides FULL cudagraphs in ModelRunnerV1: with `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, decode dispatch now uses the standard `CUDAGraphWrapper(FULL)` and breakable capture only replaces `PIECEWISE`, matching ModelRunnerV2's `use_breakable_cg` gating.

`BreakableCUDAGraphWrapper` gains an optional runtime_mode (default keeps match-any behavior for MRV2) and wrapper `unwrap()` recurses through the nested FULL/breakable pair.

Co-authored-by: Kimi Code

title: [CI/Build] Add DSv4.1 auto-label rules and narrow DSv4
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 had no label of its own, and the existing `DSv4` patterns were
claiming all of its traffic.

`DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` is a distinct architecture from `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`:
its own model tree (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/`), its own `tokenizer_mode`
(`deepseek_v41`), and its own tokenizer, parser, reasoning parser, tool parser and
config class. It adds `common/engram.py`, `nvidia/model_state.py`,
`common/ops/indexer_k_store.py` and `common/ops/query_quant.py`, and carries none
of V4's `mtp.py`, `cpu/`, `xpu/`, `fi_moe.py` or `common/vision.py`.

Two concrete defects follow from having no separate label:

1. **`DSv4` captures every V4.1 title.** Nothing bounded the version after `v4`,
   so `deepseek[-\s]?v4` matched `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` and `\bDSv4\b` matched
   `DSv4.1`. #56228, a pure V4.1 PR, is labeled `DSv4`.
2. **The issue labeler missed space-separated titles.** Its `DSv4` matcher was the
   substring `deepseek-v4` plus the keyword `DSv4`, while mergify allowed
   `[-\s]?`. #56297 ("DeepSeek V4.1 rejects Responses API text content types") got
   `deepseek` and nothing else. This is a pre-existing V4 gap, not a V4.1 one.

## Changes

- `.github/mergify.yml`: add `label-dsv41`; bound `label-dsv4`'s title pattern
  with `(?![._]?1)`.
- `.github/workflows/issue_autolabel.yml`: add a `"DSv4.1"` entry; convert `DSv4`
  from substring matching to the same bounded regex so both labelers agree.

The 4.1 sources spell the model three ways — `deepseek_v4_1` (models),
`deepseek_v41` (most), `deepseekv41` (tool parsers) — so the file conditions cover
all three.

**Flash and Pro share one label per generation.** They are the same code path in
vLLM: one arch string, one config class, no variant branching anywhere in
`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/`, and the V4-Flash and V4-Pro eval configs are identical
but for the model name and load timeout. No file condition could distinguish them,
so a per-variant label would only ever be title-routable.

## Prerequisite

The `DSv4.1` label must exist before this merges; a rule naming a nonexistent
label does not create it.

## Not a duplicate

- `gh pr list --state open --search "dsv4.1 label"` — no results.
- `gh pr list --state open --search "mergify label automation"` — no results
  touching label config.
- `gh issue view 56217 --comments` (the V4.1 kernel tracking issue) — no labeling
  work claimed.

No open PR modifies `.github/mergify.yml` or the issue labeler.

## Testing

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files .github/mergify.yml .github/workflows/issue_autolabel.yml
.venv/bin/python tools/pre_commit/check_label_rules.py
```

Both pass, including `actionlint` and `check-label-rules`. I verified
`check-label-rules` is not passing vacuously: injecting a deliberately dead glob
makes it fail and name `label-dsv41`.

Beyond the hooks, I validated out of tree against 25 real V4/V4.1 titles taken
from this repo's history, in both engines the two labelers use — Python `re` for
mergify and JS `RegExp` for the workflow — and by executing the workflow's own
`labelConfig` and matching functions with stubbed `core`/`github`/`context`:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 25 real titles, Python | 25/25 |
| 25 real titles, JS | 25/25 |
| Workflow's real matching logic | all pass |
| File conditions vs tree | 44/44 V4.1 files, no overmatch, no bleed onto `DSv4` |
| `DSv4` conditions still live | 51 files |
| No title receives both labels | confirmed |
| Noisy body does not leak model labels | confirmed; title-only design holds |

Representative outcomes:

| Title | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[Bug]: DeepSeek V4.1 rejects Responses API text content types` (#56297) | `deepseek` | `deepseek`, `DSv4.1` |
| `[Model] Support DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` | `deepseek`, `DSv4` | `deepseek`, `DSv4.1` |
| `[Bugfix][DSv4] Keep indexer scoring in breakable graphs` | `deepseek`, `DSv4` | unchanged |
| `[Model] Support DeepSeek-V4-Pro` | `deepseek`, `DSv4` | unchanged |

Happy to commit the title-regex cases as a test if reviewers want a permanent
guard; there is no existing suite covering `.github/` matcher behavior, and
`check-label-rules` covers only the file conditions.

## Model evaluation

Not applicable. This touches CI labeling configuration only — no engine, kernel,
model or serving code, so there is no effect on output or accuracy.

## Follow-up

Once the label exists, ~14 open V4.1 PRs and 2 issues need backfilling, and
#56228's `DSv4` should be corrected to `DSv4.1`.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate the labeling gap, write these
rules and run the validation above. I have reviewed every changed line, confirmed
the architectural distinction the change rests on, and run the test commands
listed.

title: [ROCm] Auto-enable breakable CUDA graphs for DeepseekV41ForCausalLM
body:
## Summary
- On CUDA, architectures in `DEFAULT_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH_ARCHITECTURES` auto-enable `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`. On ROCm that helper currently returns an empty set, so DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash dies at capture: `piecewise CUDA graphs (cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE) unavailable, model is not torch-compiled and breakable CUDA graph is off`.
- `DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` does not support `torch.compile`. The ROCm sparse SWA backend only reports `AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_BATCH`, which downgrades `FULL` to `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. Breakable CUDA graphs are the path that can start.
- Keep V3.2, V4, and GLM off the ROCm default. Opt V4.1 in. Also add it to the CUDA default list.
- On MI355X TP4 with `public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-release-repo:79a7108d9aea27ddab99ce1779290d300b17fc23-rocm` and `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`, chat `17*19` returned `323`, and an 80-token count request completed with no worker death.
- Recipe-side env is in vllm-project/recipes#953.

## Test plan
- [x] `test_rocm_keeps_compiled_deepseek_defaults` now asserts `DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` is in the ROCm default set
- [ ] Run `tests/test_config.py::test_rocm_keeps_compiled_deepseek_defaults`
- [ ] `vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` on gfx950 without forcing the env, confirm capture starts

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend][Multimodal] Align DeepSeek V4.1 and Kimi K3 media with rendered placeholders
body:
## Purpose

  Rust chat rendering and multimodal extraction previously determined media
  order independently.

  DeepSeek V4.1 and Kimi K3 can reorder tool results to match the preceding
  assistant tool-call order. The rendered image placeholders therefore followed
  tool-call order, while media extraction still followed raw request order. When
  tool results arrived out of order, images could be silently associated with
  the wrong tool results.

  DeepSeek V4.1 can also omit historical developer messages. Images from those
  messages were still extracted even though no corresponding placeholder was
  rendered, causing multimodal placeholder expansion to fail.

  Make renderers report media source locations while emitting placeholders, and
  use that order during multimodal extraction. DeepSeek V4.1 and Kimi K3 provide
  their exact rendered media order. Renderers that preserve request order retain
  the existing behavior through the default implementation.

## Test Plan

```
  cargo nextest run --locked -p vllm-chat --lib \
    -E 'test(media_order_follows_reordered_tool_results) | test(media_order_excludes_dropped_historical_developer_content) |
    test(extract_media_parts_follows_renderer_order)'

  cargo nextest run --locked -p vllm-chat

  cargo nextest run --locked -p vllm-server --lib  -E 'test(non_stream_chat_image_url_reaches_engine_mm_features)'

  cargo fmt  --all -- --check

  cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
```

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode][MoE] Avoid uninitialized EPLB state in DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark drafter
body:
## Purpose

Fix DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark startup when EPLB is enabled for the target model.

The target and DSpark draft use different routed-expert topologies (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash target: 384 routed experts; DSpark drafter: 128). When target-model EPLB is enabled, the draft routers inherit `enable_eplb=True`, but the drafter is not registered with a compatible EPLB model state. Its router-level `EplbLayerState` therefore never receives `expert_load_view` / logical-to-physical mappings and profiling fails with:

```text
ValueError: EPLB requires expert_load_view != None
```

## Fix

- Keep EPLB enabled for the target model.
- Apply the override in the shared `load_dspark_model()` path while constructing the draft `ParallelConfig`.
- Use shallow config `replace()` calls only; do not deep-copy the full `VllmConfig` after target-model construction.
- Disable draft EPLB, redundant experts, and elastic EP atomically in the same `ParallelConfig` replacement.
- Preserve the target config and shared runtime/compilation state.
- Add a focused regression test for atomic target/draft parallel-config isolation.

This intentionally disables EPLB for DSpark draft models while leaving target EPLB unchanged. Full heterogeneous target/draft EPLB support belongs in the EPLB multi-model machinery and should be handled separately.

## Validation

Focused regression test:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_dspark_utils.py
# 1 passed
```

Revalidated on the original 8x NVIDIA H20 environment:

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
- TP8 / EP8
- NVIDIA driver: 595.58.03
- CUDA: 13.2
- Target EPLB enabled
- DSpark speculative decoding enabled with 5 draft tokens

Observed after the patch:

```text
Using ['PYNCCL'] all-reduce backends for group 'eplb:0'
EPLB is disabled for the DSpark draft model. EPLB remains enabled for the target model.
EPLB is enabled for MoE part of model /models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
Initialized EPLB communicator: NixlEplbCommunicator.
DSpark draft model loaded: 97 params
Rearranged experts (profile) in 1.09 s.
OpenAI server is ready to accept requests
```

A real completion request succeeded with speculative decoding active:

```text
vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total 5
vllm:spec_decode_num_draft_tokens_total 25
vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total 16
```

No `deepcopy`/pickling, EPLB-state, CUDA, or EngineCore errors occurred.

For transparency, the H20 runtime validation used the production DeepSeek image with this loader change backported rather than a full binary rebuild of the PR head. The focused regression test was run against the PR implementation.

Model-evaluation impact: not applicable to model numerics or output semantics; this only changes the draft parallel configuration used during DSpark model construction.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open vLLM PRs for `DSpark EPLB DeepSeek V4.1`, `expert_load_view DSpark`, and `expert_load_view EPLB speculative`; no other open PR addresses this startup failure. Issue #50576 concerns SM8x/Ampere DSpark support and is unrelated. Related precedent: #25311 added multi-model EPLB support for MoE speculative models with compatible expert topology.

## Trade-off

The DSpark draft MoE does not receive EPLB balancing with this workaround. The target model remains EPLB-enabled, preserving the primary EPLB benefit while avoiding the startup correctness failure.

## AI Assistance

OpenAI ChatGPT assisted with root-cause analysis, patch drafting, regression-test drafting, and PR text refinement. The submitter supplied the production H20 reproduction environment and failure logs, reviewed every changed line, ran the focused test, and performed the H20 validation described above. AI assistance is also recorded in the commit trailers.

title: [Frontend] Use XGrammar schema constraints for DeepSeek V4.1
body:
## Purpose

The Python DeepSeek V4.1 builder currently accepts missing, repeated, undeclared, and incorrectly typed parameters even with `strict=true`. Prefer XGrammar's new V4.1 builtin to enforce parameter schemas and the `string="true|false"` wire types. Serving already owns the reasoning boundary, so the delegated grammar uses `reasoning="disabled"`.

Requires the next XGrammar release. The existing format-only builder remains available for older versions. Human review of this AI-assisted draft is pending.

Duplicate-work check: #56235 changes only the Rust frontend and explicitly leaves the Python builder unchanged. This PR changes only Python's structural-tag registry and its existing tests, complementing that work. Also checked #56400 and open DeepSeek V4.1 PRs.

AI assistance: Codex implemented the change, ran local validation, and prepared this PR. Human line-by-line review and independent test execution are still pending.

## Test Plan

Tested with a development build for the next XGrammar release in an isolated environment:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py --tb=short
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/tool_parsers/structural_tag_registry.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py
```

Also installed the actual XGrammar 0.2.1 wheel into a separate target and ran the DeepSeek V4.1 registry cases with that target on `PYTHONPATH`. Native-only tests skip on older releases; the fallback tests compile real grammars and check accepted/rejected output.

## Test Result

- **110 passed** with the development build; pre-commit passed.
- XGrammar 0.2.1 compatibility: **4 passed, 7 skipped** (native-only cases), 79 deselected.
- Supplemental protocol replay: **10 passed**, **1266 next-token masks checked**, using the official encoder and tokenizer pinned to `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash@dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`. It covers reasoning on/off, auto/required/named choice, parallel calls, union/null/string values, nested JSON, `strict=False`, no premature EOS, and parser round-trip equality.

These are CPU protocol and parser evaluations, without model weights or inference accuracy/throughput measurements. The precompiled installation attempt could not resolve `wheels.vllm.ai`; local tests imported the current checkout with the existing extensions, Torch 2.11.0+cu130 and Transformers 5.16.1. This PR does not change kernels or model execution.

CI status after submission: upstream `pre-run-check` requires a `verified`/`ready`/`ready-run-all-tests` label or at least four merged contributions by the author. This PR has not passed that authorization gate, so upstream pre-commit has not run. DCO passed; local pre-commit passed. The gate explicitly tells AI agents not to request authorization labels.

title: [Perf][DSpark] Add KV-only context insertion across V4.1 cache formats
body:
Replace the DeepSeek-V4.1 DSpark context insertion call's unused query allocation and query work with a KV-only wrapper. Dispatch the existing CUDA KV math with zero query heads for packed uint8 `fp8_ds_mla`, BF16 and ordinary FP8 e4m3fn caches. Keep projection, `kv_norm`, scheduling and acceptance logic unchanged. Validate device/dtype/layout inputs and preserve padded page strides.

**Rebase validation (2026-09-14):** current head `17127220492339af2d5969003633a7ddbdaf5c45` is based on `main` at `dbf49dad11e30ec5d464be74b715a9a9e31c2c5a`. Rebased across the upstream `deepseek_v4_1` to `deepseek_v41` directory rename and updated the focused test import to the new module path. The original added/removed patch lines are preserved after normalizing that rename; the CUDA source and DSpark caller remain byte-identical. Changed-file pre-commit hooks (`.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files` on all five changed files), `git diff --check`, Python parsing, and a static check of the renamed import target passed. CUDA compilation and GPU/model tests were not rerun for this rebase. GPU/model results below retain the revisions and configurations documented for those earlier runs. AI assistance was used for the rebase, import fix, and validation.

**Related work was found:** #55654 adds uint8 KV-only insertion, fused `kv_norm` and projection changes for V4. There is overlap in the uint8 insertion goal. This PR differs materially by reusing the existing zero-query-head kernel paths across all three cache formats, including BF16/ordinary FP8 paths that #55654 retains as dummy-query fallbacks, and by changing only V4.1 insertion. It does not add another fused norm or projection implementation. The overlapping uint8 API should be consolidated if both approaches proceed. #54674's stacked projections are also a separate operation.

Resubmission of #56320 after `dsv41-feat` merged into `main` in #56214. The original feature-branch PR is closed; this is its existing `main` replacement.

## Focused native validation and resubmission checks

- Originally reapplied to `main` at `e77daef89e18e08321ae7b8b24827eedd5fe8673`; the diff contains five files after removing the standalone benchmark in response to review. Applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks and Python parsing passed.
- On 2026-09-11, the focused CUDA test below passed **24 tests, 84 deselected**, covering uint8 / BF16 / FP8 e4m3fn, token counts 1 / 17 / 1023 / 1024, and eager / CUDA graph execution.
- A CUDA launch observer recorded **72 actual `cudaLaunchKernelExC` calls**: zero query heads, one launch attribute with PDL allowed, and successful launch returns; 12 were observed during graph capture. The CUDA source SHA-256 matches this PR's current source (`f9e208daf1eb657b803265a39e335b9428a622adfde158764c81b31147425365`). [Raw launch records, observer source and environment receipts](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56441#discussion_r3988531382) are in the review reply. This verifies launch attributes and focused correctness, not a PDL throughput gain or a full-model run of the latest head.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
  -k test_dspark_context_kv_matches_query_insert
```

## Fresh H100 serving measurements — 2026-09-11

Full raw results, per-request timings, token comparisons, source hashes and environment receipts: [verified E2E evidence](https://gist.github.com/0z5a/605534e677a48e65fe2b3fe7dc45f7fe).

A new frozen-source serving A/B completed with **+14.87% / +12.77% observed output throughput** at 512 / 2048 input tokens, respectively. This is `FRESH_SMOKE_ONLY`: one non-interleaved A/B pair, 16 timed requests per input length per arm, without repetitions or confidence intervals.

| Input / output tokens | A output tok/s | B output tok/s | Observed change | Mean E2E latency A → B (s) | Latency change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 512 / 128 | 12.8313 | 14.7392 | +14.87% | 38.032 → 32.949 | -13.36% |
| 2048 / 128 | 8.3804 | 9.4507 | +12.77% | 59.604 → 53.242 | -10.67% |

Both arms used official `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` revision `df42c109f1defefcbfcedbe7d905718a12266e40`, 4×H100 SXM 80 GB (reported as NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, NV18 links between all four GPUs), TP4 + EP, PP1 / DP1, **V2 runner**, eager, 8 GiB requested CPU weight offload, Engram CPU offload, 4 GiB KV cache, maximum model length 4096, maximum batched tokens 512, maximum sequences 4, prefix caching and chunked prefill, and five DSpark draft tokens. Client concurrency was 4. Each workload used four separate warmup requests followed by a prefix-cache reset before its 16 timed requests.

The tested revisions were A `c9d909e802a39292f54101bff8a36096761ea605` (dummy-query insertion) and B `c27bfce422688de09701fcf63ed5001cbf4ee2f6` (the original #56320 candidate). **This full-model run did not execute the rebased `main` PR head `17127220492339af2d5969003633a7ddbdaf5c45`.** Both DSpark commits retain the same patch in `git range-diff`. The DSpark Python caller and CUDA translation unit remain byte-identical to the tested candidate; the declarations, bindings and correctness test file also contain subsequent upstream changes. The standalone benchmark was removed in response to review. The recorded E2E validates the DSpark implementation on its frozen baseline; the complete rebased main integration has not been run on GPU.

Serving checks: both arms answered 6/6 short questions as expected (all six answer texts match in this run), and B matched A token-for-token for 4 serial, 6 forced-input and 4 concurrent continuations. Prefix-cache self-comparisons and A/A repetitions were omitted under the single-pair scope. Each of the four timed workloads completed 16/16 requests, with 0 failures and 2048 generated tokens. These limited checks do not replace a standard model accuracy evaluation or prove equality for the random benchmark generations. Token IDs match in these continuations; logprobs are not identical (maximum shared-prefix absolute differences: 0.04112 serial, 0.02950 forced-input, 0.19136 concurrent).

| 2048 | 2.6570% → 3.8615% | 1.132852 → 1.193075 | 10946.54 → 10044.59 |

Draft acceptance differed between arms, and 512-token TTFT increased. Consequently, the total serving change cannot be attributed solely to KV insertion or PDL, and these single-run results do not establish a stable speedup. title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Cap DFlash/DSpark profiling query batch
body:
Fixes #56443.

## Root Cause
The memory-profiling dummy run can hand-build max_num_seqs requests without applying the scheduler's speculative query-token budget. For DSpark/DFlash, each request can require num_query_per_req draft query rows.
For example, with max_num_seqs=512, max_num_batched_tokens=2048, and DSpark K=5, the profiling path asks the speculator for 512 * 5 = 2560 query rows while its input buffers are sized for 2048 rows, so DSpark can read _anchor_idx past input_ids and later surface CUDA IndexKernel/device-side assert errors.

## Changes
Cap the initial dummy/profile draft-generation pass to the largest complete set of query blocks that fits the speculator input buffer, preserve the full target-context and sampler projection for memory profiling, and fail early with a clear ValueError if a real query batch exceeds the input buffer.

Other profiling dummy runs, including FlashInfer autotune, build target attention metadata and cannot use the initial skip-attention shortcut. Add a default no-op speculator hook that lets DFlash-family speculators cap the dummy request count before GPUModelRunner builds those synthetic batches. This does not affect real serving requests or other speculator implementations.

## Existing PRs

#53970 addresses the same `max_num_seqs * parallel-draft query width > max_num_batched_tokens` failure condition with a broader capacity-based fix: it raises `max_num_batched_tokens` to cover the worst-case parallel-draft batch and enlarges the DFlash input buffers. This PR instead leaves the configured target token budget unchanged and caps only synthetic profiling batches to the existing speculator capacity. It covers both the initial skip-attention memory profile and full-attention profiling dummy runs such as FlashInfer autotune, and adds a fail-fast check if a real serving batch violates the scheduler invariant already established by #51256. The approaches are alternatives for the startup crash, but differ in scope and memory/scheduling impact.

#53080 separates target and draft scheduler budgets, but it does not constrain model-runner-generated profiling batches that bypass normal scheduler admission. #53577 covers broader DSpark/PP and padded graph safety work, but it has no matching profile query-buffer cap. #55133 and #56387 address different DSpark failure modes.

## Test Plan

### Common Configuration

- Hardware: 4x NVIDIA H20
- Tensor parallel size: 4
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv41-flash-0909`
- CUDA graph mode: `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`

### DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

```bash
vllm serve /data00/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 262144 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --block-size 64 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --moe-backend auto \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","draft_sample_method":"greedy","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log
```

### Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2

FlashInfer autotune was left enabled by default.

```bash
vllm serve /data00/models/Qwen3.8-27B \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8001 \
  --served-model-name qwen3.8-27b \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"/data00/models/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7}' \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log
```

### Qwen3-8B + DFlash

FlashInfer autotune was left enabled by default.

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8001 \
  --served-model-name qwen3-8b \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16","num_speculative_tokens":16}' \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log
```

## Test Result

### DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

Without this PR, startup fails during memory profiling before the API server becomes ready:

```text
/__w/pytorch/pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/IndexKernel.cu:111: operator(): block: [0,0,0], thread: [...] Assertion `-sizes[i] <= index && index < sizes[i] && "index out of bounds"` failed.
RuntimeError: CUDA error: CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED when calling `cublasGemmEx(...)`
EngineCore failed to start.
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
```

With this PR, the service completed profiling, KV cache creation, CUDA graph capture, and API startup. `/health`, `/v1/models`, and two `/v1/completions` requests succeeded. The pod remained running with restart count 0, and the logs contained none of the failure signatures above.

### Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2

Without this PR, startup fails during the initial memory profile. DFlash2 tries to process 128 requests with query width 8, requiring 1024 query rows while its input buffer contains only 512 rows. The logs show:

```text
IndexKernel.cu:111: Assertion `... index out of bounds` failed.
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
EngineCore failed to start.
```

With this PR, both the initial memory profile and the default FlashInfer autotune completed, followed by KV cache creation, target/DFlash2 CUDA graph capture, and API startup. `/health`, `/v1/models`, and two `/v1/completions` requests succeeded. A 128-concurrency run completed 128/128 requests and generated 2812 completion tokens. The pod remained running with restart count 0, and the startup/request logs contained no CUDA, EngineCore, traceback, `ValueError`, or HTTP 500 failure signatures.

### Qwen3-8B + DFlash

Without this PR, the initial memory-profile phase completes, but the default FlashInfer autotune dummy run uses 64 requests with query width 17, requiring 1088 query rows while the input buffer contains only 512 rows. The workers fail with:

```text
CUDA error (.../flash_fwd_launch_template.h:199): an illegal memory access was encountered
EngineCore failed to start.
```

With this PR, the initial profile, default FlashInfer autotune, KV cache creation, target/DFlash CUDA graph capture, and API startup all completed. `/health`, `/v1/models`, and two `/v1/completions` requests succeeded. A 64-concurrency run completed 64/64 requests and generated 2048 completion tokens. The pod remained running with restart count 0, and the startup/request logs contained no CUDA, EngineCore, traceback, `ValueError`, or HTTP 500 failure signatures.

title: [Perf][Kernel] Integrate DeepSelect TopK for the DSA sparse indexer
body:
## What

Integrate [DeepSeek DeepSelect](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSelect) (MIT) — a high-performance TopK kernel library for DeepSeek Sparse Attention — into vLLM via CMake FetchContent, and make **every** decode top-k implementation on the DSA sparse indexer path explicitly selectable, with a measured auto heuristic on top.

- New `vllm/model_executor/layers/indexer_topk.py`: the indexer's decode top-k stage. Hosts every backend entry point (DeepSelect, cooperative, persistent, per_row, FlashInfer ragged, torch reference) and `SparseIndexerTopk`, an `nn.Module` that resolves and runs one per step. `SparseAttnIndexer` just calls `SparseIndexerTopk()(...)`.
- New `KernelConfig.sparse_indexer_topk_backend` (`--sparse-indexer-topk-backend`): `auto` (default) / `deep_select` / `cooperative` / `persistent` / `per_row` / `flashinfer` / `torch`. Explicit values fail fast with the specific unmet constraint.
- Per-row `seq_lens` map directly onto DeepSelect's `end` parameter; output is written into the preallocated `topk_indices` buffer (CUDA-graph safe; the test below captures and replays every backend).


## Why not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for "DeepSelect" and "topk kernel sparse": no PR integrates DeepSelect. Related but different work: #56346 (sampled filtering inside persistent top-k), #48726 (a custom fused LiteTopk kernel), #55872 (deterministic FlashInfer top-k). This PR vendors DeepSeek's kernels unchanged and adds a shape-based dispatch, rather than modifying existing kernels.

## Performance (NVIDIA GB200, torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUPTI timing, CUDA graph replay, cold L2)

Shapes from the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Lightning Indexer (`index_topk=512`; indexer "vocab" = KV context length). Scope of this PR is the sparse indexer only.

fp32 (vLLM's indexer logits), CUDA graph replay, vs the **pre-PR auto pick** for each shape (persistent for bs>64, cooperative for bs<=64), plus the other candidates:

| shape | DeepSelect | persistent (pre-PR default, bs>64) | cooperative (pre-PR default, bs<=64) | per_row | FlashInfer ragged | torch.topk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bs=256, kv=1M | **191us** (5.6 TB/s) | 616us | n/a (>64 rows) | 613us | 595us | 2878us |
| bs=64, kv=1M | **88us** | 303us | 132us | 206us | 206us | 905us |
| bs=8, kv=1M | 85us | 180us | **40us** (auto keeps cooperative) | 89us | 95us | 194us |

bf16 (DeepSelect's native dtype; vLLM's fp32 kernels don't apply), eager microbench: bs=256, kv=1M: **119us** (4.5 TB/s) vs FlashInfer 529us vs torch.topk 1855us.

## Tests

All in `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py`:

- `test_deep_select_topk` / `test_deep_select_topk_preallocated_output` — wrapper correctness (fp32/bf16, variable per-row `end`, -1 fill, NaN-filled dirty tail proving the kernel never reads past `end`, preallocated strided output buffer).
- `test_sparse_indexer_decode_topk_explicit_backends` — every explicit backend x next_n {1,4}: per-row length restriction, -1 fill, set/value equality vs torch.topk.
- `test_sparse_indexer_decode_topk_short_seq_lens` — seq_len < next_n with spec decode: derived row ends clamp at 0 (matching the reference kernels' `max(0, ...)`); negative ends would be OOB for the ragged kernels.
- `test_sparse_indexer_topk_backend_resolution` — pins the auto chain (unchanged from main) and the fail-fast errors of every explicit backend.

Full file: 42/42 topk-related cases pass on GB200; `pre-commit run` on all touched files passes.

## Model eval

  - GSM8K flexible：0.9333
  - strict match：0.9325

## Notes / open questions

- Blackwell-only for now: DeepSelect upstream compiles sm_100a/sm_103a only.
- DeepSelect's sampling top-k (fp32, vocab 129280) also beats torch/FlashInfer at large batch — left for a follow-up, this PR is sparse-indexer only.
- AI assistance: this PR was implemented with AI assistance (Kimi Code); I have reviewed the changes and run the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Ignore pending chunks in invalid sliding windows
body:
## Purpose

A pending CPU KV write can unnecessarily defer a request even when an earlier sliding window is ready to load. For a two-chunk window, `[HIT, HIT, MISS, HIT_PENDING]` currently returns `None`: the reverse scan keeps the pending flag after the miss has already ruled out that incomplete suffix. The core scheduler therefore submits no load for the ready prefix.

Track pending writes within the current consecutive window and clear that state when a miss invalidates the window. A pending chunk inside a usable window still defers lookup, and `RETRY` retains its existing conservative behavior. No timeout, transfer ownership, or external API changes are introduced.

## Why this is not duplicate work

I checked #49829 and #53087 discussions and searched open PRs for `_sliding_window_lookup`, `HIT_PENDING gap`, and related offload/window/defer terms on 2026-09-11. #53087 addresses bounded waits, #53330 addresses P2P supply/demand coverage, and #51787 addresses cache recency. This change fixes the stale pending flag for an already-invalid sliding window. It does not claim to fix the production stalls reported in #49829 or an underlying stalled transfer.

## Test Plan

The regressions fail against the unchanged base: the scanner returns `None`, and the real core scheduler plus CPU manager submits zero loads. With the fix, both synchronous and asynchronous scheduling load the earlier prefix and resume the remaining prompt while the unrelated CPU write is still pending.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py -q --disable-warnings

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
```

## Test Result

Tested on base `22258a26bc090bccf5473cf681bbe9bac41bd035` plus this patch. The two test files pass: **249 passed** in 81.88 seconds. Pre-commit passes, including the configured mypy check, and `git diff --check` is clean.

GPU output check: a two-layer Gemma2 with dummy weights, BF16, and native CPU KV offload on an RTX 4060 Laptop. After warming the earlier window and clearing the GPU prefix cache, the backend lookup boundary is made to report a missing chunk followed by a pending chunk. The actual CPU/GPU worker reloads 32 prefix tokens, and all 8 generated tokens match the reference run. This is a controlled output-consistency check, not a trained-model accuracy evaluation, real stalled-copy experiment, or throughput/TTFT benchmark.

Local environment: Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, Transformers 5.17.0, current Python source plus precompiled extensions. This is not an exact-commit source build; standard CI with the main branch's PyTorch 2.13.0 dependency remains necessary. The optional DeepGEMM extension was unavailable due to local ABI mismatch; the exercised model uses FlashAttention 2.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, test execution, and drafting. The submitting human has reviewed the change. The test results reported above were run by Codex.

title: [ROCm][DSV4.1][Perf] Use AITER mHC for the delayed pre block
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on AMD still runs its mHC block as the eager Torch reference (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/amd/model.py` imports `mhc_pre_delayed_torch` / `mhc_post_torch` directly). DeepSeek-V4 was moved onto the `MHCPreOp` / `MHCPostOp` dispatch layer and reaches AITER (#41946, #43950, #52737), but V4.1 was never migrated, so on MI355X it pays ~141 kernel launches per sublayer seam to Sinkhorn-normalize a 4x4 matrix.

That cost dominates decode. A per-layer census over a captured decode trace on MI355X (gfx950, TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash):

| launches/layer | share | source |
|---:|---:|---|
| 162 | 48.6% | mHC sinkhorn loop (4x4 comb matrix) |
| 122 | 36.6% | mHC pre/post mix + eager RMSNorm |
| 24 | 7.2% | MoE / FFN (already a fused custom op) |
| 12 | 3.6% | dtype casts/copies (bf16<->fp32) |
| 6 | 1.8% | attention + fused norm/quant |
| 4 | 1.2% | TP collective |
| 3 | 0.9% | other |

85% of the layer's 350 launches are mHC. Attributing GPU time through correlation IDs, the Sinkhorn roll-up is 37.5% of kernel time across 6,966 launches per decode step — ahead of `vllm::moe_forward_shared` at 15.4% — and `aten::sum` on `[6, 4, 4]` inputs alone is 21.5%, from 3,120 calls per step on 96-element tensors. Decode ITL on this machine degrades only 1.9x between concurrency 1 and 32 while per-GPU output throughput rises 13x, so the device is far from saturated and the per-step cost is dominated by something fixed rather than by bandwidth or compute.

## Why V4.1 cannot just reuse `MHCPreOp`

V4.1 collapses each sublayer's input with the **previous** sublayer's pre-mix, and returns the current one for the next seam. AITER's `mhc_pre` neither returns its pre-mix nor accepts an incoming one, so it cannot serve that shape as-is.

The staggering does not change the gates, though. Comparing the delayed and non-delayed formulations on identical inputs:

```
post_mix     max_abs_err = 0.000e+00   <- identical
comb_mix     max_abs_err = 0.000e+00   <- identical
layer_input  max_abs_err = 6.41e+00    <- differs (stale coefficients)
```

So the expensive part — the projection, the RMS, the gates and all 20 Sinkhorn iterations, i.e. 141 of the 142 kernels — is bit-identical between the two. Only the collapse differs.

## Approach

AITER exposes its two pre stages separately, and `mhc_pre_big_fuse` consumes the unreduced split-k projection output. This PR drives those stages directly:

1. `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` — projection against `fn` plus row square-sums (1 kernel).
2. `mhc_pre_big_fuse` — post/comb gates and every Sinkhorn iteration (1 kernel). Its collapse applies the current pre-mix, which the delayed form does not want, so it is discarded.
3. New `mhc_pre_mix_triton` epilogue — recovers this seam's pre-mix from the same GEMM output and square-sums that `mhc_pre_big_fuse` already consumed, rather than repeating the projection (1 kernel).
4. `hc_collapse_triton` — the delayed collapse, with the carried coefficients (1 kernel).

New `MHCPreDelayedOp` dispatches AITER -> TileLang -> reference, mirroring `MHCPreOp`. Two cases decline AITER and fall through to TileLang: the model-entry broadcast seam (it projects a narrower operand, `x`, for which there is no AITER equivalent) and a fused RMSNorm (the composed path folds none). `hidden_size` 5120 is also outside `_AITER_MHC_FUSED_RMSNORM_SIZES`, so the fused-RMSNorm variant would not apply here regardless.

## Result

Measured on gfx950, `hidden_size=5120`, `hc_mult=4`, 20 Sinkhorn iterations, against `mhc_pre_delayed_torch`:

| tokens | launches (torch -> aiter) | worst rel err | collapse |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 1 | 141 -> 4 | 2.4e-07 | bit-exact |
| 6 | 141 -> 4 | 5.4e-07 | bit-exact |
| 24 | 141 -> 4 | 6.6e-07 | bit-exact |
| 96 | 141 -> 4 | 8.9e-07 | bit-exact |
| 1024 | 141 -> 4 | 2.2e-06 | bit-exact |
| 16384 | 141 -> 4 | 1.2e-05 | bit-exact |

**35x fewer launches per seam**, worst relative error 1.2e-5, and the collapse is bit-exact because it is the same FP32 multiply-and-sum in both paths. `num_tokens` spans AITER's split-k choices (80 down to 2), which matters because the pre-mix is recovered from that unreduced output.

The model change also routes the three eager `(pre_mix.unsqueeze(-1) * x.float()).sum(dim=1)` collapses (including the DSpark head) through `hc_collapse_triton`, which is bit-exact for that reduction, and the `mhc_post` call sites through `MHCPostOp`.

## Test Plan

- `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py::test_mhc_pre_delayed_rocm_aiter` — AITER vs the delayed reference over tokens 1/2/7/128/1024, both seam variants (carried and model-entry pre-mix), asserting the collapse bit-exact.
- `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py::test_mhc_pre_delayed_rocm_aiter_declines_unsupported` — the broadcast seam and a fused norm must not silently take the AITER path. Asserted by recording which custom op runs, with a positive control so the two declines cannot pass merely because the AITER path is unavailable. (The earlier version checked this by comparing the fallback's output against a Torch reference, which fails for reasons that have nothing to do with this PR: `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang` from #56214 is broken on gfx950 with the pinned tilelang 0.1.10, reducing the RMS sum of squares inside a thread-divergent branch and recovering half of it, so `layer_input` comes out sqrt(2) high. Confirmed pre-existing by running the suite on main + #56214 with this PR reverted: the same 15 `test_deepseek_v41_mhc_pre_delayed[fused_norm=True]` cases fail there, and applying this PR leaves the count unchanged. It does not affect serving, since the AMD decoder applies `attn_norm`/`ffn_norm` separately and never passes `norm_weight` into the pre block.)
- End-to-end on MI355X (8x gfx950, TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash), gsm8k 5-shot via lm-eval:

  | | strict-match | flexible-extract |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | baseline (eager Torch mHC) | 0.9704 ± 0.0047 | 0.9697 ± 0.0047 |
  | this PR (AITER mHC) | 0.9727 ± 0.0045 | 0.9719 ± 0.0045 |

  Within one standard error on both filters, and well clear of the 0.91 gate. The run also exercises the TileLang fallback: `hc_prenorm_gemm_tilelang` compiles 8 times on this branch and never on the baseline, which is the model-entry broadcast seam declining AITER as intended.

  Re-run on the 2026-09-11 nightly (`0.28.1rc1.dev681+ge7edf17ce` + #56214), which is main as it stands rather than the image the row above came from: **0.9719 ± 0.0045** strict-match, 0.9712 ± 0.0046 flexible-extract, 1319/1319 problems.

- Controlled A/B of the block itself, same process and identical input tensors so only the kernel choice differs, under CUDA graphs (`CUDAGraphMode.FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, which is how decode runs here). Microseconds per call, median of 5 x 200 iterations:

  | tokens | torch (main) | tilelang | aiter (this PR) | vs torch | vs tilelang |
  |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | 1 | 259.4 | 22.5 | **16.3** | 15.89x | 1.38x |
  | 6 | 263.7 | 23.1 | **16.6** | 15.92x | 1.39x |
  | 12 | 271.4 | 23.2 | **16.8** | 16.15x | 1.38x |
  | 24 | 282.9 | 23.4 | **16.9** | 16.74x | 1.39x |
  | 48 | 303.0 | 27.0 | **17.2** | 17.63x | 1.57x |
  | 96 | 383.3 | 31.3 | **18.0** | 21.30x | 1.74x |
  | 128 | 391.4 | 30.4 | **18.8** | 20.87x | 1.62x |

  Timed eagerly instead, the AITER path is slower than TileLang (93.4 us vs 28.8 us at 1 token): the Python wrapper in `_aiter_ops.mhc_pre_delayed` costs roughly 75 us of host time per call that a captured graph removes. It remains 7.6x-8.2x faster than the Torch reference main runs today, so eager is not a regression against the baseline this PR replaces, but trimming that host overhead is a worthwhile follow-up for `enforce_eager` users.

- The end-to-end ITL figures in the thread below are from a time-driven agentic trace and are *not* a controlled A/B; the table above is the controlled measurement.

## Notes / follow-ups

- `mhc_pre_big_fuse` still writes a collapse we discard. That redundant `[tokens, hidden_size]` bf16 store is the price of composing rather than having a native delayed kernel; it is negligible at decode shapes and ~1-2% of a prefill step. A native `mhc_pre_delayed` in AITER (have the `mhc_pre` epilogue return `pre_mix` and accept an incoming one — `pre_mix` is already computed inside the kernel as a slice of `mixes`, so no new math) would remove both it and the Triton epilogue, taking the seam to 2 launches. Happy to take that up on the AITER side as a follow-up.
- `aiter/jit/module_fused_ar_mhc.so` could additionally fuse the TP all-reduce into the mHC seam (4 collective launches per layer today). AITER already exposes `fused_allreduce_mhc_post_{only,one_stage,split}` and vLLM calls none of them. Out of scope here; tracked in the RFC below.
- Separately observed while profiling and *not* addressed by this PR: ~1,220 AITER GEMM calls per step fall back with `using torch solution:0` for the indexer shapes (`N:128,K:512` and `N:32,K:5120`), i.e. no tuned config on gfx950.

Part of a broader set of ROCm gaps for this model, collected in #56506.
