title: [ROCm][DSV4.1][Perf] Stride the DSA decode candidate mask over the live context
body:
## Purpose

`rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` sizes its logits workspace as `(batch_size * next_n, max_model_len)` and hands the whole tensor to `apply_candidate_mask`, so the mask grid was sized by `max_model_len` rather than by the context actually resident. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with `--max-model-len 1048576` that is 1024 programs per row when only the first ~128 have anything to do.

The cost tracked row count and ignored context, which is the signature of a grid sized by the workspace instead of the data. On gfx950 at block size 8, 2048 candidate blocks:

| rows | mask kernel |
|---:|---:|
| 6 | 0.0127 ms |
| 24 | 0.0357 ms |
| 96 | 0.1252 ms |

96 rows is 402 MB of stores in 0.1252 ms, i.e. the kernel writes the entire workspace every call regardless of sequence length.

Sanitizing columns at or past a row's `end` is dead work. `top_k_per_row_decode` bounds its scan by `rowEnd`, taken from the same `seq_lens` passed to the mask. That invariant is already load-bearing upstream: when there are no candidate blocks the mask is skipped entirely and top-k reads the same uncleaned workspace.

This replaces the one-program-per-tile grid with a fixed 128 programs that stride to the row's `end`. The grid is still derived from `width`, a tensor shape, so a FULL cudagraph capture stays valid on replay; only the loop trip count is data-dependent, and it is read from device memory inside the kernel rather than baked at capture. `min(_MASK_GRID_COLS, cdiv(width, 1024))` keeps narrow widths from launching programs that would only fall through, so the grid never grows relative to today.

### Why this sits next to the ROCm caller instead of replacing the shared kernel

An earlier revision of this PR changed `apply_candidate_mask` in `model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py` directly. The clamp itself is sound on every platform — `persistent_topk` takes `min(lengths[row], stride, max_seq_len)` and `cooperative_topk` passes its clamped `sl` into `large_topk`, so neither reads past `end` either, and the CUDA path allocates the same `max_model_len`-wide workspace.

The program count is the problem: 128 is a tuning constant measured against gfx950's 256 CUs, and I have no way to measure the tradeoff on NVIDIA. Rather than ship an unmeasured grid change to CUDA users, the variant lives beside its only caller in the ROCm ops file and the shared kernel is untouched. The four ROCm call sites are not equivalent either — the prefill chunks pass chunk-sized logits, where there is nothing to win, so they stay on the shared kernel and only the paged decode path switches.

Part of #56506.

## Test Plan

`tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_candidate_mask.py` (new, ROCm-gated) is the unit test. Correctness is the load-bearing part, since the change deliberately stops writing to part of the tensor. Output must be bit-identical to the shared kernel over `[0, end)` for every row — the region a consumer can read — across the shapes that exercise the edge cases:

- ragged per-row ends, including 0, 1, tile boundaries (1023/1024/1025) and values up to 524287
- `end == width`, the only configuration where the edge flag at column `width - 1` is inside the compared region
- non-zero `starts` from the prefill path
- `row_repeat > 1`, where several logit rows share one bound
- `block_size` 16 as well as the model's 8
- widths either side of `_MASK_GRID_COLS * _MASK_TILE`, so both the saturated grid where programs actually stride and the `min()` clamp below it are covered
- a column stride > 1, since the caller slices a workspace

Two properties beyond agreement also get pinned: that columns past the tile boundary containing `end` are left untouched (the difference from the shared kernel, and where the speedup comes from), and that a cudagraph capture replays correctly against ends both longer and shorter than the captured ones — the property the static grid exists to provide.

Performance measured two ways: a standalone kernel benchmark at decode shapes over a range of contexts and grid widths, and in-situ torch-profiler decode traces on a live server at concurrency 1, 4 and 16, comparing per-kernel ms/step against an otherwise identical baseline. Accuracy via gsm8k 5-shot under lm-eval on the same node and configuration.

Hardware: MI355X (gfx950, 256 CU), TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, `--max-model-len 1048576`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` cudagraph mode, DSpark 5-token MTP.

## Test Result

Correctness: 9 passed. All cases agree bit-for-bit over `[0, end)`.

To confirm the test is not vacuous, two mutations of the kernel were checked: stopping one tile early (`while tile_start < end - TILE`) and removing the stride (`step = TILE`, so programs never advance past their own tile span). Each fails 8 of the 9 tests; the one that still passes in both cases is the tail-bound test, which correctly does not constrain under-masking.

Standalone kernel, 131k context:

| conc | rows | before | after | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 6 | 0.0128 ms | 0.0125 ms | 1.03x |
| 4 | 24 | 0.0356 ms | 0.0127 ms | 2.81x |
| 16 | 96 | 0.1236 ms | 0.0201 ms | 6.16x |

Across contexts at 96 rows: 32k 0.1249 -> 0.0125 (9.9x), 131k 0.1249 -> 0.0197 (6.3x), 524k 0.1464 -> 0.0786 (1.9x). The 524k case is where the kernel starts doing real work rather than padding, which is the intended behaviour. A grid clamped to the visible length — not capture-safe, measured only as a floor — gives 0.0192 ms at 131k, so the strided form is within 4% of the best a data-dependent grid could do.

In-situ decode traces, 4 mask calls per step, per-kernel ms/step:

| conc | before | after | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.048 | 0.018 | 2.7x |
| 4 | 0.133 | 0.031 | 4.3x |
| 16 | 0.464 | 0.077 | 6.0x |

Reproduced to three decimals across two independent trace runs.

At concurrency 16 the whole-trace kernel delta is -0.404 ms/step and -0.387 of that is this kernel, with every other kernel inside ±0.04 ms, so the win is attributable rather than drift. The indexer chain goes from 2.95 to 2.58 ms/step, 11.4% to 10.0% of the decode step.

gsm8k 5-shot, lm-eval, same node and configuration:

| | strict-match | flexible-extract |
|---|---:|---:|
| baseline | 0.9719 ± 0.0045 | 0.9712 ± 0.0046 |
| this change | 0.9727 ± 0.0045 | 0.9719 ± 0.0045 |

That run predates the move out of the shared kernel, so it exercised this kernel on both the prefill and decode call sites — a superset of what the PR now changes.

One caveat worth stating rather than hiding: at concurrency 1 and 4, step wall time is dominated by variance in `cross_device_reduce`, which absorbs TP rank arrival skew and moved by more than 2 ms/step between runs that differ only in this file. End-to-end wall time at low concurrency cannot resolve an effect this size; the per-kernel attribution above is the measurement that can.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Fold the mHC post block into the delayed pre projection
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 runs an mHC post block and then the next sublayer's **delayed** pre block at every seam. Each seam therefore pays for three things: a post kernel, a split-k projection that re-reads the residual streams the post kernel just wrote, and the pre epilogue.

DSv4 already avoids the middle read: `mhc_fused_tilelang` computes the updated residual in registers and feeds the pre-norm GEMM from there. V4.1 could not reuse it, for the same reason it needed its own pre in the first place — it collapses each sublayer's input with the **previous** sublayer's pre-mix and hands the next one back, and the DSv4 fused wrapper neither accepts an incoming pre-mix nor returns one.

## Approach

`mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_tilelang` runs the existing fused kernel and then the delayed pre epilogue (`MHC_PRE_NORM_KERNEL`, `use_pre_mix_in` / `save_pre_mix`), returning `(residual, post_mix, comb_mix, layer_input, next_pre_mix)`. Above the fused kernel's token range it falls back to exactly today's `mhc_post_tilelang` + split-k GEMM, so only the small-batch path changes shape.

Both V4.1 seams route through it, except one:

- **Attention seam** — fuses, unless Engram is injected. Engram reads the residual between the post and the pre, so the post cannot move into the projection there; that branch keeps the separate kernels.
- **FFN seam** — always fuses.
- **DSpark draft** reuses `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer`, so it inherits both.

The pre epilogue is JIT-compiled per split-k factor and warmed up from a token sweep that never produces the factors this GEMM picks, so `MHCPreNormKernel.get_warmup_keys` takes `extra_splits` and the decoder registers them. Without it the first decode step JITs inside the capture warmup.

### Tuning

The tile, split-k and block size were inherited from DSv4 unmeasured (the code carried a `TODO(gnovack): investigate autotuning these heuristics`). Sweeping all three against the separate post + split-k GEMM, on GB300 at `hc_mult=4`, CUDA-graph device time:

| tokens | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 24 | 32 | 48 | 64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| inherited config, 5120 | 8.21 | 8.01 | 8.42 | 8.82 | 10.25 | 12.73 | 13.51 | 16.81 | 19.70 |
| tuned, 5120 | **8.02** | **8.00** | 8.83 | 8.84 | **9.85** | **10.47** | **11.47** | fallback | fallback |
| unfused, 5120 | 12.74 | 12.52 | 12.72 | 12.92 | 13.32 | 13.32 | 13.37 | 13.53 | 13.49 |

Two things were wrong with the inherited constants: the 16-token cutoff was early (the fused path still wins 1.2x at 32), and one fixed tile starves the projection of parallelism as the batch grows — it is 18% off at 24-32 tokens and *slower* than the unfused path past 48. The tuned heuristic is two bands (`tile_n` 2 below 16 and 6 through 32, `n_thr` 128), within ~1-2% of the per-shape optimum for one extra compiled variant. Same bands hold at `hidden_size` 7168.

**The cutoff is 32, and it is set against a corrected baseline.** vLLM configures the TF32 projection's split count through `compute_mhc_pre_num_splits`, which buckets a good estimate into {1, 4, 16} to bound startup specializations — and that bucketing is itself 1.14-1.19x off the optimum below 128 tokens (measured: the estimator says 80 splits at one token, the bucket gives 16, the optimum is 64; rounding the estimate down to a power of two reproduces the measured best at every shape I tried). Against a GEMM given the split its own estimator computes:

| tokens | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 24 | 32 | 48 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fused | 8.44 | 8.23 | 8.83 | 9.03 | 9.85 | 10.61 | 11.29 | 13.55 |
| unfused, split as configured today | 13.13 | 12.74 | 12.76 | 13.33 | 13.35 | 13.55 | 13.56 | 13.35 |
| unfused, split=64 | 11.09 | 11.09 | 11.29 | 11.66 | 11.50 | 11.69 | 11.62 | 11.72 |
| **fused vs tuned baseline** | **1.31x** | **1.35x** | **1.28x** | **1.29x** | **1.17x** | **1.10x** | **1.03x** | 0.86x |

So the honest claim is 1.3x at decode widths, 1.17x at 16, break-even at 32. The cutoff sits at the break-even point rather than where a slow baseline would have put it (48, which is a 14% *loss* against a tuned GEMM). Fixing that split heuristic is worth 5-19% on every unfused seam — all prefill, all large-batch decode, and DSv4 as well as DSv4.1 — but it belongs in its own PR, not bundled here, since it changes a shared helper and a second model's hot path.

It is shared with the DSv4 wrapper, which uses the same kernel at the same shapes. The heuristic now also declines shapes the kernel cannot tile evenly (`mix_size % tile_n`, `hidden_size % (n_splits * n_thr)`) and falls back instead — previously those silently dropped whole tiles and k-slices.

## Relationship to the other open mHC PRs

- **#56255 (Mega-mHC from DeepGEMM)** — same two call sites, same 5-tuple refactor, same Engram carve-out. Its `mhc_shifted_post_pre` dispatches to DeepGEMM `mega_mhc` when `device_capability_family(100) and hidden_size % 1024 == 0 and hc_mult == 4`, and **falls back to the unfused pair otherwise** — which is what this PR replaces. The two are complementary and land cleanly together: benchmarked head to head below, the TileLang fusion is faster at small batch, Mega-mHC is faster at large batch. If both land, the right end state is one dispatcher picking between them by token count, and I am happy to write that as a follow-up (or fold this into #56255, author's preference).
- **#56513 (ROCm)** — same idea via AITER `mhc_fused_post_pre_gemm_sqrsum`, on `_aiter_ops.py` / `mhc/aiter.py` / `layers/mhc.py` / `amd/model.py`. No file overlap with this PR beyond the shared test file.
- **#56611** — a different optimization (overlapping the coefficient GEMM with attention/FFN), env-gated.

### Mega-mHC comparison

DeepGEMM 2.8.0 (`66081d4c`), GB300, `hc_mult=4`, `hidden_size=5120`, CUDA-graph device time per seam. Both paths are graph-capturable; `mega_mhc` lazily allocates per-stream split barriers and asserts that happens outside capture, so it must be warmed on the capture stream first (which vLLM's pre-capture warmup iteration does).

| tokens | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 24 | 32 | 48 | 64 | 128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| unfused | 13.13 | 12.84 | 13.02 | 13.54 | 13.32 | 13.54 | 13.54 | 13.55 | 13.56 | 13.97 |
| fused TileLang (this PR) | **8.43** | **8.22** | **8.83** | **8.84** | **9.65** | 10.47 | 11.28 | 13.10 | 13.54 | 13.96 |
| Mega-mHC (#56255) | 10.19 | 10.46 | 10.07 | 10.67 | 10.47 | 10.47 | **10.88** | **11.09** | **11.26** | **11.82** |

This PR is 1.08–1.27x faster than Mega-mHC at 1–16 tokens; they cross at ~24; Mega-mHC is 1.18–1.20x faster at 48+. A `torch.profiler` kernel-time breakdown agrees (at 1 token: 4.32 µs fused kernel + 5.03 µs epilogue, against a single 10.44 µs `sm100_mega_mhc_impl`).

Numerically the two differ in one place: the fused TileLang kernel projects the **FP32** post result it holds in registers, while Mega-mHC and the unfused path project its BF16 rounding. Against an FP32 reference at 8 tokens, max abs error: residual 9.77e-4 for all three; coefficients 9.25e-4 / 1.78e-3 (this PR) against 1.98e-4 / 3.46e-4 (Mega-mHC and unfused). This is inherited from the DSv4 kernel, not new — the stored residual streams are bit-identical either way.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py -v
```

New `test_deepseek_v41_mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed` (0/1/8/128 tokens x 4096/7168 hidden x carried/absent pre-mix) asserts the post-mapped residual and the collapsed layer input are **bit-identical** to `mhc_post_tilelang` + `mhc_pre_delayed_tilelang`, and the coefficients match an FP32-post torch reference to 1e-5 on the fused path. Plus a `torch.library.opcheck` case and a CUDA-graph capture/replay case, since decode replays this op from a graph. `test_deepseek_v41_decoder_mixes_match_torch` now covers both routes through the decoder.

## Test Result

```
164 passed, 23 skipped in 53.80s     # tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py, GB300
```

`pre-commit run --all-files` clean on the changed files (ruff, ruff-format, mypy-3.10).

### Model evaluation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4 GB300, gsm8k 5-shot via `mqa-run --api-type completions --temperature 0 --max-tokens 1024`, n=1319, `num_request_errors: 0` and 0 null answers in every run:

| arm | runs | exact_match/flexible |
|---|---|---|
| this PR | 3 | 0.9242, 0.9325, 0.9204 |
| unfused baseline, same serve config | 2 | 0.9348, 0.9249 |

The baseline arm's own two runs differ by 0.99 pt, so the arms' ranges overlap and the 0.42 pt difference in means sits inside the measured noise floor for this config (batching nondeterminism at concurrency 32). Dashboard history for this model is median 0.9314, p25–p75 0.9287–0.9333.

## Second and third commits: aux hidden states for draft models

Once the post lives inside the next layer's pre, the standalone `mhc_post_tilelang` the model ran per aux-capture layer is recomputing a residual that already exists. The second commit takes `mean(dim=1)` from the fused call behind a `capture_previous_aux` flag and drops the duplicate post — the approach of **#55575** (DeepSeek-V4), which only becomes available to V4.1 once V4.1 has the fused seam.

Two seams keep the standalone post: the Engram seam captures *before* the injection (matching the post it replaces — aux consumers read the stream before Engram touches it), and the last layer on a rank has no successor to fold into, so it takes its mean from the final post that runs anyway.

I did **not** port #55575's companion change that skips the `_mtp_hidden_buffer` copy when aux hidden states are present: that depends on its `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` edit, which is model-agnostic and would collide with #55575 in a shared file. It should follow from that PR, not this one.

### Third commit: fold the stream mean into the collapse

That leaves one pass still standing: `mean(dim=1)` over `[T, hc, H]`. The collapse in the pre epilogue already reads every one of those streams to weight them by the carried pre-mix, and the aux value is the *unweighted* mean of the same data — so the third commit accumulates it in that pass, behind a `write_aux` specialization so non-draft setups compile and run exactly what they did before. The buffer is allocated only when the caller asks.

Standalone `mean(dim=1)` is not cheap at scale (measured on GB300, `[T, 4, 5120]` bf16): 2.10 µs at 1 token, 17.9 µs at 1024, **72.1 µs at 4096**, 141.8 µs at 8192 — per capture layer, per step. Folded, the aux-capture seam costs:

| tokens | 1 | 8 | 32 | 128 | 1024 | 4096 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| seam + separate mean | 10.55 | 11.50 | 13.94 | 17.65 | 60.25 | 209.32 |
| seam + folded mean | **8.43** | **9.04** | **11.50** | **13.74** | **40.88** | **140.63** |
| saved (µs) | 2.13 | 2.46 | 2.45 | 3.90 | 19.38 | 68.70 |

Both epilogues carry the path — the one that applies RMSNorm and the plain one — so no caller falls back to a torch mean. Bit-exact against `torch.mean` on both, at 1/8/33/128/1024 tokens and 5120/7168 hidden, with every other output of the op unchanged when capturing is on. The Engram seam still uses a separate mean, since its aux is the *pre*-injection post and the epilogue runs after Engram.

### DSpark verification

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4 GB300, `{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}` with **real** verification (not `synthetic`), 8 fixed prompts at `temperature 0`, same branch with and without the commit:

| | drafts | draft tokens | accepted | rate | length | per position |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| neither commit | 106 | 318 | 204 | 0.6415 | 2.9245 | 92 / 64 / 48 |
| harvest | 106 | 318 | 204 | 0.6415 | 2.9245 | 92 / 64 / 48 |
| harvest + folded mean | 106 | 318 | 204 | 0.6415 | 2.9245 | 92 / 64 / 48 |

Byte-identical generated text (sha256 of the concatenated completions matches) and identical acceptance counters, which is the end-to-end statement that the harvested tensor is the one the draft model used to get. `test_deepseek_v41_capture_previous_aux` pins the same thing at the unit level with `atol=0`, for both the fused and Engram seams.

That probe pins the tensor exactly but is only 8 prompts, so both arms were also run through **GPQA-Diamond at full size** — 198 questions x 4 epochs = 792 samples per arm, chat path with thinking on, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, `max_tokens` 57344, concurrency 128, same TP4 GB300 node:

| arm | headline | answered-only | pass@4 | request errors | truncated | null answers | empty@stop |

| DSpark k=5, real verification | 0.9104 | 0.9138 | 0.9545 | 0 | 3 | 3 | 0 |

Acceptance over that run, from the engine's own counters rather than a synthetic profile: **1,467,764 drafts, 7,338,820 draft tokens, 3,207,521 accepted — rate 0.4371, acceptance length 3.185** of a possible 6.

**Both arms are this branch**, so this is not a before/after for the PR; the before/after is the gsm8k table above. What it establishes is that the code these two commits touch carries 1.47M drafts at an accuracy indistinguishable from the no-draft arm: 2 questions of 792, where one question is 0.126 pt and the sign flips between exact_match and pass@4. Finished generations ran to a median of 2239 tokens with a p90 of 16232 and a max of 56320 against the 57344 cap, so the three truncations per arm are a genuine budget limit rather than a loop — identical in both arms, so they do not move the comparison.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Replace the Torch prefill combine with the shared combine_topk_swa_indices kernel
body:
## Purpose

ROCm's V4.1 sparse prefill combines the top-k and sliding-window indices with ordinary Torch indexing, about ninety small ops per call. This sends it to the shared `combine_topk_swa_indices` kernel the CUDA path already uses: one launch, and it brings the SWA bounded-replay bound, the SWA-only guard and the JIT warmup with it. The ROCm-only Triton kernel and the Torch path are removed.

## What changes

- `amd/rocm.py`: prefill calls `combine_topk_swa_indices` from `common/ops/cache_utils.py`.
- The shared kernel gains two guards that leave well-formed input untouched:
  - both lengths clamp at 0. Warmup batches reach it with a negative position, and the Torch path had `clamp_min(0)` for that;
  - a negative top-k index stays -1 instead of becoming `M * b - 1`, a row of the previous request.

## Tests

`tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py` compares the kernel against the Torch path it replaces, copied over unchanged so the reference cannot drift toward the kernel: `seq_len` below `query_len`, `seq_len == 0`, `compress_ratio == 0`, a non-zero `query_start_loc[0]`, -1 candidates, and windows 64/128/256. It also checks that ROCm dispatches to the shared kernel. `test_v41_combine_topk_swa_stops_at_replay_start` covers the replay bound on that kernel. It runs on ROCm as well, and now includes the shorter replay chunk from #59136 (co-authored by @yuzhouo7), so #59136 is no longer needed.

```bash
pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py
pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py -k stops_at_replay_start
```

```
gfx950 (MI355X)   124 passed, 0 failed
gfx950 (MI355X)     4 passed, 0 failed
```

## Measurements

MI355X, TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Both arms run `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-0cbac6cd1`; arm B mounts this branch's two source files, so nothing else differs. Each slot is a fresh server with two warm-up rounds and three recorded ones, slots in A B B A order.

```bash
vllm serve DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --moe-backend aiter --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len 33792 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384

vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 256 \
  --ignore-eos --num-prompts 12 --max-concurrency 2 --seed 42
```

| metric (n=6/arm) | A (main) | B (this PR) | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TTFT median (ms) | 120.7 ± 1.7 | 59.7 ± 1.9 | **−50.5 %** |
| TTFT p99 (ms) | 166.3 ± 2.6 | 81.7 ± 1.3 | **−50.9 %** |
| output throughput (tok/s) | 225.4 ± 0.2 | 234.0 ± 0.2 | +3.8 % |
| TPOT mean (ms) | 8.42 | 8.33 | −1.1 % |

GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k`, 1319 questions, 5-shot): 0.9045 with this branch; main in the same session scored 0.8961 and 0.9067.

title: [Bugfix] Avoid repeated dummy initialization and random CPU Engram fills
body:
## Purpose

Avoid repeatedly initializing descendant weights under `--load-format dummy`. The loader already walks `model.modules()`, so each iteration now initializes only local parameters and persistent buffers. This matches default PyTorch state selection without recursively revisiting descendants and preserves parameter attributes used for dummy initialization.

CPU-offloaded DeepSeek V4.1 Engram tables request constant dummy weights of 1.0 and UE8M0 scale byte 127 (scale 1.0). Their lookup access pattern does not require randomly generated table contents. Checkpoint loading is unchanged; online quantization retains its existing materialize/initialize/process path.

Duplicate checks found #54958, which addresses full-size FP8 temporary allocations and OOM. This PR addresses recursive duplicate initialization and CPU Engram constant initialization; it contains no generic FP8 allocation or chunking changes. No open PR addressing the same changes was found in the dummy initialization/loading searches.

## Test Plan

Run the existing checkpoint-sharding, nonpersistent alias-buffer, and online-processing tests:

```bash
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py tests/kernels/test_engram.py -k 'online_processing_waits_for_late_registered_bias or head_shards_reconstruct_checkpoint or layerwise_reload_skips_non_persistent_parameter_alias_buffers' -q
```

Pre-commit was run on all three changed source files.

## Test Result

10 existing tests passed (101 deselected) in 5.26 seconds on the isolated PR branch. Applicable pre-commit hooks and git diff --check passed.

A standalone differential audit found exact old/new initialized values for nested and tied weights and persistent buffers. Tied parameter identities and nonpersistent alias buffers were retained; nonpersistent scratch buffers were unchanged and None tensors skipped. Tied parameters can still be visited under multiple owners: the change removes ancestor-level repetition, not all storage aliasing.

Development measurement on four GB200 GPUs with dummy weights and FlashInfer autotuning disabled: model loading completed in 19.66–19.80 seconds per worker; health returned HTTP 200 after 514.145 seconds and a 16-token smoke request succeeded. The previous run remained in dummy initialization at its 600-second cutoff. The development run also included separate mHC JIT and generic FP8 temporary changes, so its end-to-end time is not an isolated benchmark of this PR. No real-checkpoint accuracy evaluation was run.

AI assistance was used for diagnosis, implementation, and validation.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Restore MTP-retained sliding-window history
body:
## Purpose

Fix native KV offload restoring MTP-retained sliding-window blocks that lookup never checked and the producer may never have stored. Implements the conservative coverage option discussed in #56701.

For example, with a 64-token external hit, SWA block size 16, window 32, and three extra retained tokens, lookup checks chunks 2–3 while allocation also restores chunk 1. If chunk 1 is absent or still being written, `CPUOffloadingManager.prepare_load()` asserts after the hit has already been admitted. Hybrid store pruning can itself omit chunk 1.

Include `extra_retained_tokens` in aligned/partial lookup coverage, the existing in-flight-load check, and producer store reachability. Preserve the base coverage lower bound so retaining one extra token does not unnecessarily request another chunk. The store mask uses a temporary coverage spec; actual attention windows, allocation, cache keys, and transfer ownership are unchanged. Restoring the required older blocks can increase CPU cache usage and transfer volume.

Duplicate checks on 2026-09-13 found no open PR for `56701 in:body` or `extra_retained_tokens offload`. #55818 handles allocation scaling and #53499 page-size normalization; neither fixes this lookup/store mismatch.

## Test Plan

Extend the existing scheduler tests to cover retained history at aligned and unaligned hybrid boundaries, EAGLE tail handling, missing/pending/loading chunks, and a producer followed by a cold GPU-cache consumer. The consumer only hits keys actually stored by the producer.

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py -q --tb=short

.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py

.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
```

## Test Result

- Related suites: **474 passed** locally. Native H20: **378 passed**, then the remaining **96 passed** with `--lf` after seeding the missing public `facebook/opt-125m` config/tokenizer cache and enabling offline mode; no code changes.
- Focused regressions: **102 passed**. With only the production file reverted to base `de500290ffffeb7bd834872c0dea5331590dd40d`: **14 failed, 88 passed**.
- Pre-commit, including mypy 3.10, and the explicit mypy 3.12 hook: passed.
- Tiny Step3.5 smoke with two MTP modules, four speculative tokens, SWA window 32 / extra retention 3: both RTX 4060 V1 and native H20 V2 restored **64 cached tokens / 7 chunks**, with **16/16 identical cold/warm output tokens**.
- H20 V2 instantiated `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator`; the unmodified proposals exercised **30 decode calls with four rejected drafts**, entering the three-token re-prefill path. A separate controlled draft-rejection check also passed the restore/output assertions.

V1 used Python 3.12.13 / PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130; H20 V2 used Python 3.12.14 / PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 with UVA available. Compiled extensions were reused, and both changed source files on H20 were SHA-256 verified against `1e89fa93a662a321e29860f3f30a25a362070fc8` (the reused environment's package version metadata identifies the older build).

These GPU checks use tiny dummy weights, BF16, eager mode, and disabled optional JIT warmup. They validate the serving/re-prefill paths for this configuration. **Trained-model quality, acceptance rate, and performance have not been evaluated; no throughput improvement is claimed.**

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the H20 V2 functional smoke</summary>

Save the script below as `../tiny_mtp_v2.py` relative to the checkout and run:

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 \
  .venv/bin/python ../tiny_mtp_v2.py
FORCE_DRAFT_REJECTIONS=1 PYTHONPATH="$PWD" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 \
  .venv/bin/python ../tiny_mtp_v2.py
```

The temporary model directory below is generalized from the executed script.

```python
"""Tiny Step3.5 two-module MTP, real GPU kernels and CPU offload transfers."""
import os
os.environ['VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING']='0'
os.environ['VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER']='1'
import json
from pathlib import Path
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.transformers_utils.configs.step3p5 import Step3p5Config
from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import SlidingWindowSpec

model_dir=Path('/tmp/vllm-offload-mtp-smoke')
Step3p5Config(hidden_size=128, intermediate_size=256, num_attention_heads=2,
    num_attention_groups=1, head_dim=64, num_hidden_layers=2, vocab_size=256,
    max_position_embeddings=256, max_seq_len=256, sliding_window=32,
    num_nextn_predict_layers=2, moe_layers_enum='1', moe_num_experts=2,
    moe_top_k=1, moe_intermediate_size=128, share_expert_dim=128,
    architectures=['Step3p5ForCausalLM']).save_pretrained(model_dir)
llm=LLM(model=str(model_dir),skip_tokenizer_init=True,load_format='dummy',
    enforce_eager=True,dtype='bfloat16',seed=42,max_model_len=256,
    max_num_seqs=2,max_num_batched_tokens=256,gpu_memory_utilization=0.25,
    kv_cache_memory_bytes=16<<20, block_size=16,enable_prefix_caching=True,
    disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager=False,compilation_config={'mode':0},
    kernel_config={'enable_jit_warmup':False},
    speculative_config={'method':'mtp','num_speculative_tokens':4},
    kv_transfer_config={'kv_connector':'OffloadingConnector','kv_role':'kv_both',
        'kv_connector_extra_config':{'cpu_bytes_to_use':16<<20}})
try:
    core=llm.llm_engine.engine_core.engine_core
    cfg=core.vllm_config
    assert cfg.speculative_config.use_multi_module_mtp()
    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.multi_module_mtp.speculator import MultiModuleMTPSpeculator
    runner=core.model_executor.driver_worker.worker.model_runner
    speculator=runner.speculator
    assert isinstance(speculator,MultiModuleMTPSpeculator),type(speculator)
    proposal_trace=[]
    force_rejections=os.environ.get('FORCE_DRAFT_REJECTIONS')=='1'
    original_propose=speculator.propose
    def track_propose(*args,**kwargs):
        batch=kwargs.get('input_batch',args[0] if args else None)
        rejected=kwargs.get('num_rejected',args[6] if len(args)>6 else None)
        proposal_trace.append({'has_prefill':bool(batch.has_prefill),
            'num_rejected':rejected[:batch.num_reqs].tolist()})
        drafts=original_propose(*args,**kwargs)
        if force_rejections:
            drafts.fill_(75)
        return drafts
    speculator.propose=track_propose
    connector=core.scheduler.connector.connector_scheduler
    specs=[g.kv_cache_spec for g in connector.config.kv_group_configs]
    assert any(isinstance(s,SlidingWindowSpec) and s.extra_retained_tokens==3 for s in specs)
    load_keys=[]
    original_load=connector.manager.prepare_load
    def track_load(keys,ctx):
        keys=list(keys)
        load_keys.append(len(keys))
        return original_load(keys,ctx)
    connector.manager.prepare_load=track_load
    prompt={'prompt_token_ids':list(range(10,75))}
    params=SamplingParams(temperature=0,max_tokens=16,ignore_eos=True)
    cold=llm.generate([prompt],params,use_tqdm=False)[0]
    for _ in range(1000):
        if not core.scheduler.has_requests(): break
        core.step()
    assert not core.scheduler.has_requests()
    assert llm.reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=False)
    warm=llm.generate([prompt],params,use_tqdm=False)[0]
    assert cold.outputs[0].token_ids==warm.outputs[0].token_ids
    assert warm.num_cached_tokens>0 and load_keys
    assert any(not call['has_prefill'] for call in proposal_trace)
    if force_rejections:
        assert any(max(call['num_rejected'])>1 for call in proposal_trace)
    result={'proposal_trace':proposal_trace,'force_draft_rejections':force_rejections,
        'speculator_class':type(speculator).__name__,'cold':cold.outputs[0].token_ids,'warm':warm.outputs[0].token_ids,
        'cached_tokens':warm.num_cached_tokens,'load_chunk_counts':load_keys,
        'kv_specs':[str(s) for s in specs],'weights':'dummy',
        'mtp_modules':2,'speculative_tokens':4,'model_runner':'V2'}
    Path('../tiny_mtp_v2_rejection_result.json' if force_rejections else '../tiny_mtp_v2_result.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')
    print(json.dumps(result))
finally:
    llm.llm_engine.engine_core.shutdown()
```

title: [Bugfix][PCP][DCP] Respect interleave in indexer KV gather mapping
body:
PCP’s index gather assumes interleave 1. With DCP4/interleave64, token 1 reads the key for token 64. Use the configured interleave when mapping gathered shards back to token positions, and keep padded gathers in bounds. No new kernel.

Separate from #55802, which removes the interleave restriction; this PR leaves that guard unchanged. Duplicate searches found no open PR fixing this PCP gather mapping.

Validation on main `b6e2aa748b`: **72 ordering cases passed** (CPU; device copies stubbed), covering interleave1/64, DCP2/4/8, short/boundary contexts and split request rows. Restoring the old arithmetic fails all 36 interleave64 cases. Pre-commit/mypy passed.

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py -k pcp_plan_deinterleave_restores_global_order -q

All 32 GPU/CPU pairs matched tokens/log probabilities in each run, with confirmed CPU hits; 6,155-token retrieval also passed (6,144 CPU-restored tokens; continuations differed). title: [MRV2] Keep warmup out of the EPLB load stats
body:
## Purpose

MRV2 warmup forwards record expert load into `expert_load_pass` like real ones. The router kernel records during the forward, so skipping or suppressing the EPLB step afterwards does not keep that load out of the stats. It lands in the next real step. This happens at startup and on every elastic EP re-warm right after the rebalance.

This adds `EPLBController.suppress()` which turns off both the EPLB step and `should_record_tensor` and puts both back when done. It is used for `skip_eplb=True` in `step_eplb_after`, around MRV2 `compile_or_warm_up_model` and around `profile_cudagraph_memory`. `EplbState.step` now also zeroes the dummy load before the profile early return.

MRV1 has the same recording issue on a serving rank. #57151 fixes it there.

Split out of #53934

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py
```

## Test Result

12 passed and 1 skipped. ruff and mypy pass. Not run on GPUs.

CC @itayalroy

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] One-pass dequantize and a gather-sized grid for the compressed K cache
body:
## Purpose

`dequantize_and_gather_k_cache_triton` walks a V4.1 prefill's whole compressed prefix once per layer, and it did so on a fixed `(num_reqs, 128)` grid with a per-token loop that issued twenty-two memory operations. Two changes here: the grid follows the length being gathered, and a token is dequantized in one pass. They compose — the first raises how many dependent-load chains are in flight, the second cuts the work each chain does.

## Sizing the grid

Each worker walks its slice of the sequence one token at a time, and every step is a dependent load: block table entry, then the page it points at, then the token inside it. The loop is bound by that chain's latency rather than by bandwidth, so the grid has to hold enough chains in flight to cover it. At batch size 1 the whole grid was 128 workgroups on a 256-CU gfx950, while a V4.1 prefill gathers the entire compressed prefix once per layer: about 3.1k serial steps per worker at a 399k-token context.

A caller that knows a host-side bound on `gather_len` now passes it and the grid follows, aiming for eight steps per worker. The DeepSeek-V4.1 ROCm compressed-KV gather takes that bound from `prefill_seq_lens_cpu`, which the metadata already carries, so nothing new syncs with the device. Callers that pass no bound keep the previous width, so the CUDA paths are unchanged. The same file's sliding-window gather keeps the old width on purpose: it reads at most `window_size` plus the chunk's query tokens.

## Dequantizing in one pass

The per-token loop walked the 448 fp8 bytes in seven 64-byte quantization blocks, loading a scale byte per block and storing per block, then copied the 64 bf16 tail in four chunks of sixteen. The seven blocks tile 448 exactly, so the `qblock_start < fp8_dim` branch and the `offsets < fp8_dim` masks never excluded anything; what they cost is twenty-two memory operations per token where four will do.

The MXFP8 record added for the FlashMLA V4.1 layout already reads its token in one load, scales it with a reshape, and stores it once. This gives the `fp8_ds_mla` kernel the same shape. `scale_dim * quant_block` is 512 against an fp8 region of 448, so the tail of the tile reads into the token's own bf16 bytes, is scaled by a scale nothing reads, and is dropped by the store mask; the token record is 576 bytes, so the read stays inside it, and a `tl.static_assert` holds that.

## Kernel time

MI355X, one request, `torch.profiler` over ten calls after five warm-ups, same inputs on every arm:

| context | main | grid by length | + one-pass dequantize | vs main |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8,192 | 95.9 us | 18.9 us | **6.6 us** | **14.5x** |
| 32,768 | 480.1 us | 61.2 us | **19.9 us** | **24.1x** |
| 131,072 | 1945.6 us | 230.2 us | **65.9 us** | **29.5x** |
| 399,360 | 7767.2 us | 914.5 us | **343.9 us** | **22.6x** |
| 1,048,576 | 20359.1 us | 2385.1 us | **912.0 us** | **22.3x** |

The grid's own gain settles at −88% from 32k up, because `gather_num_workers` caps at 8192 and a 1M gather wants more; the one-pass dequantize then takes a further 62–71% at every length, since it changes the work per token rather than the parallelism. The combined factor peaks at 131k and eases to 22x beyond it: past the cap the grid stops widening, so the longest contexts keep the per-token win but not the rest of the parallelism one.

A width of 8192 is where widening stops paying. Sweeping the grid by hand on a 1M-token gather, with the dequantize already in one pass, 2048 and 8192 workers are within 3% of each other and 65536 buys 2.5%; at 131k a width of 65536 is 12% *slower* than 2048. The cap is not what bounds the long-context number.

## Correctness

The second commit adds a kernel rather than editing one: ROCm gets `_dequantize_and_gather_k_one_pass_kernel`, CUDA keeps `_dequantize_and_gather_k_kernel`. Neither had a test — the existing cases import the deepseek_v4 copy, and the two V4.1 cases cover the 528 B MXFP8 and 288 B NVFP4 records, both SM100-only. The 584 B record these two kernels decode is the only one a ROCm V4.1 server gathers.

The third commit covers both kernels, parametrized on the ROCm dispatch so each runs wherever the test lands. It checks that grid width cannot move the output — `num_workers` is only the per-token loop stride and each iteration writes its own row, so four widths must be byte-equal — and that the rows match a host-side UE8M0 dequantization, which is what catches a wrong tile or scale.

## End-to-end

MI355X, TP 4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, vLLM at `af1c01499` (this branch's parent, so the arms differ only in this PR's two files), [official MI355X recipe][recipe] config minus its `--speculative-config`. Two things the recipe omits are needed to boot: `--ulimit memlock=-1` on the container (the engram table pins 23.6 GiB per rank) and #57036 in every arm, without which the AITER fused-expert path indexes the expert weights with the -1 cudagraph padding sentinel and all ranks fault during the startup profile run.

`vllm bench serve --random-output-len 8` so the number is prefill, 40 prompts per repetition at concurrency 4. A repetition replays the previous one's prompts, so the first is cold and the rest hit the prefix cache. Warm rows are the mean of eight repetitions ± their standard deviation; the whole table was measured twice with identical seeds and agrees to within 2 %.

| shape | main | grid by length | + one-pass dequantize | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 131k, warm cache | 354.7 ± 4.3 ms | 224.8 ± 1.4 ms | **201.6 ± 1.8 ms** | **−43.2 %** |
| 131k, cold | 15638.0 ± 2.9 ms | 14409.9 ± 30.5 ms | 13985.4 ± 11.2 ms | **−10.6 %** |
| 32k, warm cache | 158.7 ± 9.4 ms | 137.2 ± 11.0 ms | **129.1 ± 9.9 ms** | **−18.7 %** |
| 32k, cold | 2223.7 ± 109.9 ms | 2192.5 ± 121.9 ms | 2096.3 ± 108.4 ms | −5.7 % |

The changes compose at 131k: the grid takes 36.6 %, the one-pass dequantize a further 10.3 %. The 32k cold row is four fresh-server runs per arm and every arm's spread is ~5 %, so it should not be read as a gain — a microbenchmark puts the gather at ~1 % of a cold 32k prefill, against 11 % of a warm one.

Percentiles over the 320 pooled warm requests per cell (`--save-detailed`); a single repetition puts only four requests above p90 and swings by 25 %:

| shape | | main | grid by length | + one-pass dequantize |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 131k | p50 | 389.6 ms | 250.0 ms | **219.8 ms** |
| | p90 | 402.7 ms | 259.7 ms | **232.7 ms** |
| | p99 | 549.1 ms | 335.8 ms | **313.5 ms** |
| 32k | p50 | 180.8 ms | 146.3 ms | **140.2 ms** |
| | p90 | 188.8 ms | **200.7 ms** | **165.6 ms** |
| | p99 | 201.6 ms | 216.8 ms | **195.8 ms** |

GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, `tests/evals/gsm8k`) with tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py : 0.9022 on the merge base against 0.9045 with the branch. Both runs report a zero invalid rate.

GSM8K via InferenceX's lm-eval config (`infx/evals/gsm8k.yaml`, 5-shot, chat template, strict and flexible extraction): 0.9765 / 0.9757 on the unmodified nightly image against 0.9742 / 0.9735 with this PR's two files applied 
Both arms carry the #57036 padding-sentinel fix, without which the server does not start on MI355X.


## Notes

The grid width becomes data-dependent. This call site is prefill-only, and `num_workers` is read inside the kernel through `tl.num_programs(1)`, so any width is correct — a replayed capture would use the width it recorded and only lose the speedup. #56686 goes the other way for the candidate-block kernels, which do run inside decode captures.

The sliding-window gather in the same file keeps the old width: 40 calls totalling 0.49 ms in the profile above. `deepseek_v4` carries a copy of this kernel with the same fixed 128 and is left alone; that path deserves its own numbers.

#42504 attacks this kernel from a different angle — gather only the top-k slots the sparse attention reads, instead of dequantizing the whole prefix and discarding most of it. That is the larger win and this does not conflict with it: after this change the gather is still 32.4 ms of a 97.8 ms prefill kernel budget.

title: [PCP][DCP] Declare FlashMLASparse MTP support at CP interleave > 1
body:
## Purpose

Make MTP reachable for PCP+DCP sparse-MLA prefillers behind NIXL P/D.

With `decode_context_parallel_size > 1` and a `NixlConnector`, `VllmConfig.adjust_dcp_kv_cache_interleave_size` raises `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` to the block size (64) for block-level alignment of the DCP → decoder transfer. `cp_utils.validate_cp_support` then asserts `supports_mtp_with_cp_non_trivial_interleave_size` on every attention impl whenever a speculative config is present:

```
AssertionError: MTP with cp_kv_cache_interleave_size > 1 is not supported in FlashMLASparseImpl.
```

The flag is declared `False` in `vllm/v1/attention/backend.py` and set `True` by no backend in the tree, so MTP + DCP>1 + NIXL is unreachable on main for every sparse-MLA model. This declares it on `FlashMLASparseImpl` only.

**Why this should be safe on this impl:** the mixed-fp8 path processes all scheduled query tokens together, and its slot mapping and sparse-index conversion both thread `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` through (`flashmla_sparse.py` passes it into the DCP index conversion at both call sites). Nothing in the impl assumes interleave 1 except the capability declaration itself.

## Status — draft, validation in progress

Measured on H200, GLM-5.3, PCP8+DCP8+EP8 (TP1) prefiller → TP8+EP8 decoder over NIXL, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=3`:

- With the flag, the arm starts and MTP drafting is mechanically healthy: **0.7755 per-token acceptance, 3.33 tokens/step** (ceiling 4), from differencing `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters across a gsm8k run. Throughput 1.82× the same arm with spec decode off.
- That run also scored **0.325 on gsm8k (200, 5-shot, temp 0)** vs 0.935 for a TP8 reference on the same build. That was on a base that had #55802 but **not** #56715 (*"Respect interleave in indexer KV gather mapping"*), whose description matches the failure exactly. It was not the drafting: acceptance was normal and the corruption was in the KV the draft and target both read.
- Re-validation on current `main` (which includes #56715) is running now; I will post the gsm8k + acceptance table before marking ready for review.

Not proposing this as ready until that lands. If the accuracy result on main is bad, this PR is wrong and I will close it.

## Test Plan

End-to-end: gsm8k (lm_eval, 5-shot, 200 samples, temperature 0) on PCP8+DCP8+EP8 → TP8+EP8 with MTP3, against a TP8+EP8 → TP8+EP8 MTP3 reference on the same commit; plus Prometheus-counter acceptance for both. Results to follow.

title: [PCP][DCP] Support DCP target model with non-DCP Dspark
body:
Run dense DSpark/DFlash drafts at DCP=1 alongside a DCP target, so the draft backend does not need DCP support.

`KVCacheSpec.dcp_sharded` keeps draft allocation, slot mapping, prefix caching, and offloading independent of target sharding. Mixed MLA/dense caches use block-outer packing; FlashInfer gets the resolved layout from attention metadata. Existing MLA-draft PCP restrictions remain unchanged.

Validation:

- CPU regressions: **456 passed, 1 skipped**. Draft input/metadata/block-table GPU regressions: **19 passed**. Ruff and mypy (Python 3.10–3.13) passed.
- GSM8K, GLM-5.3 + GLM-5.2 DSpark, TP4/DCP2, FlashInfer eager: **100/128** versus **104/128** target-only; mean acceptance length **3.81**. Zero greedy-token mismatches, but accuracy parity is not established.
- FlashAttention 4 full-graph capture/replay: **12/16**, zero greedy-token mismatches across **1,661 tokens**. FlashInfer disables full graphs for this mixed layout. PCP+DCP has configuration/allocation coverage only.

<details>
<summary>Test commands and evaluation setup</summary>

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' .venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
from unittest.mock import patch
import pytest
from vllm.platforms import current_platform
with patch.object(current_platform, 'device_count', return_value=8):
    raise SystemExit(pytest.main([
        'tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py',
        'tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py',
        'tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py',
        'tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_decode_bench_connector.py',
        'tests/v1/worker/test_dspark_utils.py',
        'tests/v1/worker/test_cp_utils.py',
        'tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py',
        'tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_lookahead.py',
        'tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py',
        '-q', '--tb=short',
    ]))
PY

chg run -g 1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
    tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py \
    tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle_draft_attn_metadata.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py -q --tb=short

git diff --name-only -z HEAD^ | xargs -0 .venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --hook-stage manual --files
```

The mocked GPU inventory supports CPU-only PP configuration tests.

Model runs used 4× B300, MRV2, `ag_rs`, target `zai-org/GLM-5.3` at `30333038ada1f1dacb294a93270305a890b50c14`, and draft `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark` at `cc714308fc4ad68b667a6a71bbf2a344c2ef903b`. Target KV dtype: `fp8_ds_mla`; draft: `auto`; k=7. GSM8K: five-shot, greedy, seed 42, max 256 output tokens, model length 4096, batch tokens 512, four sequences, 1 GiB KV per rank, prefix caching enabled. Each run repeated the first four prompts. Mean acceptance length includes repeats and equals `1 + accepted_tokens / num_drafts`.

FlashInfer used BLHNC. FlashAttention 4 used BLNHC with `compilation_config={"mode": 0, "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY", "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32]}`.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Stop dummy draft decode steps from writing KV through stale block-table rows
body:
## Purpose

Fix a KV-cache corruption in Model Runner V2 speculative decoding under data parallelism: an idle DP rank's dummy batch runs the drafter's multi-step decode, which computes real slot mappings through the *persistent* per-slot block tables using `idx_mapping = arange(num_reqs)` (real request-state slots whose rows are stale), and writes drafter-layer K/V into offsets `1..k-1` of the first block of whatever request last occupied those slots. Those blocks are typically already registered in the prefix cache, so every later request that hits them reads corrupted drafter K/V while the target model's K/V stays intact.

Observed on GLM-5.2 (glm_moe_dsa, MTP k=5, DP=4 EP, prefix caching) as a per-request, exactly-zero MTP acceptance (`p0 = 0.0000`, `acc_len = 1.0`, `drafts == max_tokens`) that latches onto a conversation and disappears after `POST /reset_prefix_cache`; the poisoned rows were NaN (fp8 `0x7F`) in `model.layers.78.self_attn.attn`, with the target layers and indexer cache of the same block clean. On current main the same stale write still happens on every idle step (the written values happen to be finite there, so acceptance is unaffected), i.e. the write path is latent.

#49757 protected the read side (`get_dummy_block_tables` zeroes `input_block_tables`) and the target's dummy slot mappings are PAD (`prepare_dummy_attn`), but `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` reads `block_table_ptrs` (the persistent tables), which neither protection covers.

## Fix

- `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel`: a row with `idx_mapping < 0` (dummy or CUDA-graph padding request) emits `PAD_SLOT_ID` and never dereferences a negative block-table row.
- `AutoRegressiveSpeculator.propose(dummy_run=True)`: mark every dummy row with `idx_mapping = -1` (already the speculator's convention for padded rows, ignored by `gumbel_sample`).

The guard lives in the kernel rather than in Python because the fused multi-step path re-runs `compute_slot_mappings` inside the captured CUDA graph between draft steps; only the kernel can neutralize a replayed dummy run.

## Test Plan

- `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py::test_dummy_request_slot_mapping_is_pad` (new): `idx_mapping == -1` yields all-PAD slot mappings; a real row still resolves through its block table.
- End-to-end on 4x GB200 with GLM-5.2 NVFP4, DP=4 + EP, `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'`, prefix caching on, fp8 KV, block 64, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs (the production decode geometry), driven by a growing-prefix multi-turn probe plus a unique-prompt load/probe "transition hunt":
  - f94666b60d unpatched: hunt trial 1 flips DEAD; 4/4 dead requests hit the same poisoned first block, all healthy requests on that rank do not; dumped drafter K/V rows 1-4 of that block are NaN.
  - f94666b60d + this fix: semantic gate passed, 3x20 chain requests 0 dead, 6/6 hunt trials 0 dead (mean p0 0.61-0.76); 66,164 dummy draft decode steps logged, every slot mapping PAD.
  - main dc07f1638f + this fix: semantic gate passed, 3x20 chain requests 0 dead, 6 hunt trials 0 dead; the dummy draft steps log `slots=[-1]`.

## Test Result

```
$ pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py      # GB200, main + fix
10 passed
$ pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/block_table.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/multi_module_mtp/speculator.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py
all hooks passed
```

End-to-end reproducer (4x GB200, GLM-5.2 NVFP4, DP=4 EP, MTP k=5, prefix caching, fp8 KV, block 64, FULL_DECODE_ONLY):

| tree | chain probe (3x20) | transition hunt | dummy draft slots |
|---|---|---|---|
| f94666b60d (production) | 0 dead | trial 1 DEAD (1/6, then 1/6 and 2/6 on confirm) | real slots; poisoned block rows 1-4 NaN |
| f94666b60d + fix | 0 dead | 6/6 trials 0 dead | 66,164 steps, all PAD |
| main dc07f1638f | 0 dead | 6/6 trials 0 dead | real slots (finite values) |
| main dc07f1638f + fix | 0 dead | 6/6 trials 0 dead | all PAD |

The acceptance metrics above (mean p0 0.61-0.79 in every healthy run) double as the model-quality check: the change only affects dummy batches, and the semantic gate (answer planted at the prompt tail) passed in every run.

## Notes

- Duplicate check: `gh issue list`/`gh pr list` searches for the dummy-run / stale block table / draft KV path found no existing report; the closest related changes are #49757 (read-side zeroing) and #55458 (excludes DP padding rows from draft attention metadata; likely why the written values are finite on main).
- A follow-up could make read and write sides share one source by computing slot mappings from the per-batch gathered `input_block_tables`; this PR is the minimal, backportable fix.
- AI assistance: this change was investigated and drafted with Claude Code and reviewed with Codex; the submitter has reviewed every line and run the tests above.

title: [CI] Extend DSv4 engine readiness timeout on main
body:
## Why

The optional H200 `DSv4-Flash Disaggregated DP EP` lane has now failed on two consecutive nightly/main commits because all four decoder API frontends exhaust the internal 600-second engine-readiness deadline while DeepGEMM warmup is still progressing:

- [#88612](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/88612#01a0995b-7d1d-4fbb-9b78-47621b0734f9): the warmups completed roughly 3-4 minutes after the frontend timeout, but the decoder had already been terminated
- [#88685](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/88685#01a09c93-304f-4dd4-8cfa-74ca0a7af3ac): the same four 600-second timeouts recurred while the warmup was active

The immediately preceding exact run [#88565](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/88565#01a0976c-f012-4596-b540-132e4a8531e7) passed, but its decoder frontends became healthy only about 9 minutes 57 seconds after launch, leaving almost no headroom under the current 10-minute budget.

Set `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=900` only for this large-model step. The outer 1200-second server wait and 60-minute Buildkite timeout already accommodate it, and healthy starts do not wait longer.

## Duplicate work

I searched open vLLM PRs for `dsv4 engine readiness timeout`, `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S DSv4`, and `dsv4-flash-disaggregated 900`; no open fix exists. Merged PR #53252 applied the same proven 900-second setting only to `releases/v0.28.0`; it is absent from `main`.

## Test plan

- `git diff --check`
- `uvx --python 3.12 pre-commit run --files .buildkite/test_areas/disaggregated.yaml`
- exact H200 `DSv4-Flash Disaggregated DP EP` validation

## Test results

- `git diff --check`: passed
- all applicable pre-commit hooks: passed
- model evaluation is not applicable because this changes only the CI startup budget; the exact DSv4 accuracy job remains the end-to-end validation gate

This draft was prepared with AI assistance. A human maintainer must review every changed line and validate the exact H200 job before promotion.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Optimize DSV4.1 K=512 decode top-k on gfx950
body:
## Purpose

Part of #56506.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash uses K=512 for decode indexer top-k, which misses the
existing gfx950 tuning and falls back to the generic 10-split kernel. Add a
ROCm/gfx950-only K=512 path for up to 384 rows and 1M columns. It selects
active splits from device sequence lengths so FULL graph replay remains valid,
reduces masked `-inf` histogram contention, and uses a smaller final sort when
possible. Other architectures, K values, strides, and shapes keep the existing
path.

This PR contains no multistream CSA, scheduler, or queue-management changes.

## Results

- All 1,008 matrix cases passed: concurrency 1/2/4/8/16/32/64,
  speculative tokens 1-6, context 10K/50K/100K/200K/500K/1M, compression
  ratios 1/2, and dense/masked logits.

| Cache condition | Cases | Geomean | Median | Speedup range | Slower cells |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Warm HIP graph | 1,008 | 2.310x | 2.191x | 1.008-12.344x | 0 |
| 256 MiB cache pressure | 1,008 | 1.824x | 1.730x | 1.023-6.246x | 0 |

Representative CR1 masked decode results from the warm matrix:

| Concurrency | Spec tokens | Context | Baseline (us) | Candidate (us) | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | 6 | 10,000 | 31.56 | 10.10 | 3.124x |
| 4 | 6 | 50,000 | 34.79 | 15.80 | 2.202x |

| 4 | 6 | 200,000 | 51.78 | 21.08 | 2.456x |
| 4 | 6 | 500,000 | 90.72 | 35.47 | 2.558x |
| 4 | 6 | 1,000,000 | 148.10 | 49.31 | 3.003x |
| 16 | 6 | 10,000 | 49.11 | 10.14 | 4.841x |
| 16 | 6 | 50,000 | 60.68 | 21.98 | 2.761x |
| 16 | 6 | 100,000 | 83.10 | 30.15 | 2.757x |
| 16 | 6 | 200,000 | 121.48 | 41.79 | 2.907x |
| 16 | 6 | 500,000 | 232.66 | 72.38 | 3.215x |
| 16 | 6 | 1,000,000 | 420.57 | 135.95 | 3.094x |

- A GPU trace captured 2,520 kernel intervals; 72 profiled pairs had a
  **2.291x** geometric-mean GPU busy-time speedup.
- Paired GSM8K strict accuracy was **1279/1319 baseline** and **1286/1319
  candidate**, with no invalid or truncated answers. Both arms passed 10K and
  100K token retrieval checks.
- Two short serving repetitions did not show a clear end-to-end throughput
  change, so this PR makes no serving-speed claim.

## Validation

```bash
cmake --build dsv41_rocm_bench/topk/pr-cmake-build \
  --target _C_stable_libtorch -j16

HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3 GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=4 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py \
  -k 'gfx950_long_c4a or gfx950_k512 or aiter_c4a' -v

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  csrc/libtorch_stable/sampler.cu \
  vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py \
  tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py
```

The build passed, all 27 focused GPU tests passed, and scoped pre-commit passed.

This does not duplicate #54682, which is a MiniMax-M3 Triton selector, #50470,
which dispatches a separate sparse-indexer path to AITER, or #56628, which
optimizes the adjacent candidate mask.

title: [Bugfix][CPU] Fix DeepSeek-R1 (FP8 MLA + MoE) correctness on CPU backend
body:
## Purpose

Fixes two independent bugs blocking `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1` (and any other DeepSeekV3-routed / FP8 MLA model) on vLLM's CPU backend.

1. `CPUExpertsFp8._supports_routing_method` didn't allowlist `RoutingMethodType.DeepSeekV3`, so the model fails to load with `ValueError: Unsupported FP8 MoE backend: NONE`.
2. `CPUFp8BlockScaledMMKernel.process_weights_after_loading` didn't honor `layer._cpu_skip_gemm_dispatch` (set by MLA's "absorb" optimization on `kv_b_proj`), so it unconditionally VNNI-prepacked the FP8 weight bytes for AMX BRGEMM. `get_and_maybe_dequant_weights` then dequantized those prepacked bytes as if still row-major, scrambling `W_UK`/`W_UV` against mismatched per-block scales — producing incoherent garbage output. `UnquantizedLinearMethod` already honors this flag for bf16 checkpoints; this brings the FP8 kernel in line.

## Test Plan / Results

- Root-cause isolation: built a real-weight-truncated 4-layer DeepSeek-R1 and compared vLLM CPU layer-by-layer hidden states against HF transformers on the same weights. A bf16-dequantized control run matched HF at cos_sim=1.0000; with FP8, divergence was isolated to attention output specifically (cos_sim ~0.25-0.48 pre-fix, its norm ~15x too small), confirming the bug was FP8-specific and inside MLA's kv_b_proj handling.
- `examples/basic/offline_inference/generate.py --dtype=bfloat16 --model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1 --enforce-eager` (TP=4): garbage output pre-fix; coherent, factually correct output post-fix (e.g. "The capital of France is" -> "Paris").
- Full GSM8K accuracy eval (`lm_eval`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1`, TP=4, torch.compile enabled, full 1319-example test set, `apply_chat_template=True`, `fewshot_as_multiturn=True`, greedy decoding): `exact_match,strict-match=0.8795` (stderr 0.0090), `exact_match,flexible-extract=0.9568` (stderr 0.0056).

title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Keep transient checkpoints out of prefix-cache eviction
body:
## Summary

Keep transient KDA/Mamba prefill checkpoints out of the ordinary prefix-cache eviction set when sparse retention is explicitly active.

This change targets Kimi-K3's hybrid attention path.

## Problem

FlashKDA creates internal checkpoints so the current prefill can continue from a recurrent-state boundary without an additional scheduling step. A checkpoint in the middle of a prompt is useful to the current request, but it is not necessarily a reusable shared-prefix boundary.

Before this change, such a checkpoint could be re-keyed and registered as a normal prefix-cache block. It then participated in the same GPU LRU eviction pool as reusable hot prefixes:

```text
middle checkpoint -> hash -> prefix-cache LRU -> evicts hot prefix
                                             -> later local hit becomes a miss
                                             -> extra load or prefill work
```

Before/after cache lifecycle:

```text
Before:

  KDA prefill
      |
      +--> temporary checkpoint
      |        |
      |        +--> hash + ordinary LRU
      |                     |
      |                     +--> competes with hot prefix
      |                                  |
      |                                  +--> local prefix miss

After:

  KDA prefill
      |
      +--> temporary checkpoint ------------------> current request can use it
      |                                              |
      |                                              +--> no ordinary LRU entry
      |
      +--> shared-prefix-boundary checkpoint ------> reusable prefix cache
                                                     |
                                                     +--> may be retained/shared
```

This is particularly problematic when `prefix_cache_retention_interval == 0`: intermediate checkpoints are not intended to be retained as dense semantic checkpoints, but their temporary hash could still make them eviction candidates.

## Fix

Pass the active retention interval into checkpoint publication. When sparse retention is active and the checkpoint is neither at the end of the prompt nor at the shared-prefix boundary, treat it as request-local state:

```text
middle checkpoint -> current request may use it
                  -> temporary hash is removed
                  -> no ordinary prefix-cache LRU entry
                  -> reusable hot prefixes remain protected
```

Prompt-end and shared-prefix-boundary checkpoints retain the existing publication behavior. This change does not disable KDA checkpoint computation or change the state written by FlashKDA.

## Performance

On a representative B200 Kimi-K3 hybrid workload using TP8/PP2/direct DCP8, the isolated production-style comparison was:

| Configuration | Output throughput |
| --- | ---: |
| Checkpoint disabled (diagnostic baseline) | 1013.00 tokens/s |
| Checkpoint enabled with transient-checkpoint retention fix | 1091.80 tokens/s |

The fixed configuration improved throughput by 7.78% over the checkpoint-disabled diagnostic baseline while retaining the internal checkpoint feature. A separate run with the GEMM-AR option disabled measured 1108.89 tokens/s; that result is included only as context and is not an isolated measurement of this patch.

These measurements are workload-specific and are not used as a claim that this small cache-lifecycle change explains every difference between software stacks. The primary regression signal is the cache-manager reproduction: temporary checkpoint publication changes which blocks compete in the local prefix-cache eviction pool.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- PR #55760 changes the default sparse/dense retention policy for Mamba + EAGLE; this change keeps the explicit sparse-retention behavior but fixes transient checkpoint publication.
- PR #56615 fixes MooncakeStore boundary pairing between Mamba/KDA and attention KV; this change is limited to local prefix-cache block retention.
- PR #56525 guards cache hits until the writing scheduler step is committed; this change addresses eviction eligibility, not write visibility.
- PR #52527 adds observability for sparse-retention misses; this change modifies the cache lifecycle.

## Validation

Focused prefix-cache tests should be run with:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q
```

The change is intentionally small and preserves the current-request checkpoint path. Model-scale performance validation is still required on a representative hybrid KDA workload.

This change was prepared with AI assistance; the author should review the complete diff and test results before merging.

title: [watermarking] add context deduplication support to speculative decoding
body:
## Purpose

Extend generation-side watermark context deduplication to speculative decoding.

- Build target verification contexts from committed and proposed draft tokens.
- Detect repeated contexts in committed history and earlier positions of the same speculative block while respecting `deduplicate_contexts_max_history`.
- Use the ordinary draft proposal at repeated contexts before running the unchanged acceptance test.
- Use the ordinary draw from the existing residual or target distribution for repeated rejection-recovery and bonus contexts.
- Leave disabled and greedy requests on their existing paths.
- Fuse committed-history and speculative-local context checks to avoid launch-heavy PyTorch bookkeeping.
- Fuse ordinary and watermarked draft sampling into one vocabulary reduction while preserving the pre-temperature draft-logit cache.

This keeps the standard `min(1, q/p)` acceptance rule and does not force rejection at repeated contexts.

## Test Plan

- Run the focused CPU watermark/configuration tests.
- Run all pre-commit hooks applicable to the changed files.
- Run the watermark suite and CPU/Triton parity tests on an H100.
- Microbenchmark draft, target-mask, rejection-resampling, and fused draft-sampling overhead separately.

## Test Result

- `python -m pytest -q tests/watermarking/test_watermarking.py`: 51 passed, 18 skipped locally.
- Watermarking and Gumbel suites on an H100: 95 passed.
- Fused draft sampling exactly matches the previous ordinary/watermarked selection, including draft-specific RNG streams and bit-exact pre-temperature logits caching.
- Applicable Ruff, formatting, syntax, mypy, configuration, accelerator API, and sign-off checks: passed.

### H100 microbenchmark

The new fused draft-sampling path was compared with the previous sequence—ordinary draft sampling with cache write, watermarked sampling, then `torch.where`. Both paths include temperature preprocessing and draft-logit cache writes, use float16 logits with vocabulary size 32768, and report the median of five 1000-iteration measurements.

| Batch size | Previous two-pass path | Fused mixed path | Time saved per draft step | Sampling-section speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 91.31 us | 57.40 us | 33.91 us | 1.59x |
| 8 | 92.96 us | 58.14 us | 34.82 us | 1.60x |
| 32 | 92.62 us | 58.13 us | 34.49 us | 1.59x |

These are isolated eager-execution microbenchmark timings, not end-to-end inference throughput measurements.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Skip non-prefix-cacheable groups in SimpleCPUOffload (GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail and QSA)
body:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash carries a kpool-tail scratch group (`KpoolTailSpec`, `prefix_cacheable=False`, `block_size=index_kpool=4`) next to prefix-cacheable groups that hash at 1152 tokens on this box (MLA 1152, 4× Mamba 1152 in `align` mode). Core (`resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes`, `HybridKVCacheCoordinator`, `KVCacheManager`) and the `MooncakeStore connector` already skip such groups. `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` did not, and treated every KV cache group as offloadable:

- `_select_eager_blocks_to_store` views the request hashes at each group's block size to build `BlockStored` metadata. For the tail group that is `resolve_block_hashes(hashes, hash_block_size=1152, block_size=4)`, which trips the divisibility assert as soon as `--kv-events-config` enables KV cache events. The engine dies on the first prefill store.
- `update_state_after_alloc` maps external (CPU-hit) tokens onto the scratch group and asserts alignment against its block size, although the coordinator never returns hit blocks for it.

This PR records which groups take part in offloading (`prefix_cacheable`) and skips the rest in eager store selection and in load pairing. Scratch blocks never carry a hash, so nothing is stored or loaded for them either way; the scratch slot in the per-group hit tuple stays empty, exactly as the coordinator leaves it.


## Duplication check

Two open PRs touch the same code path: #55033 (draft since 2026-09-02, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA ring, also adjusts `_estimate_lazy_target_blocks`) and #56404 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, gates `resolve_block_hashes` in the store path only, currently conflicting). This PR is scoped to the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool-tail layout and adds what neither of them covers: a regression test for the actual crash trigger (`enable_kv_cache_events=true`, `BlockStored` emitted for cacheable groups only) and an end-to-end store/load + accuracy check on GLM-5.3-Flash. Happy to fold the test into #55033 instead if the maintainers prefer to land that one. #54743 applies the same scoping to the *OffloadingConnector* (`build_offloading_config`) and does not touch `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload`; the two are complementary.

## Test Plan

Unit:

```
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
    tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py -q
```

E2E: GLM-5.3-Flash, 4× GB300, TP4 + EP, `--enforce-eager`, `--max-model-len 32768`, `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` with 16 GB pinned host memory per rank, `--kv-events-config '{"enable_kv_cache_events":true,"publisher":"zmq"}'`, dev endpoint `/reset_prefix_cache` used to evict the GPU prefix cache between runs (`?reset_external=true` also clears the CPU pool).

## Test Result

E2E store/load (10,277-token prompt, greedy, 32 new tokens):

| step | GPU prefix hit | connector hit |
|---|---|---|
| fresh | 0 / 10277 | 0 / 10277 |
| same prompt again | 9216 / 10277 | 0 / 1061 |
| after `/reset_prefix_cache` | 0 / 10277 | 9216 / 10277 |
| after `/reset_prefix_cache` again | 0 / 10277 | 9216 / 10277 |

Hits are 1152-aligned (the Mamba/MLA block); the kpool tail block is a fresh per-request scratch block at every resume, as with a GPU hit.

Accuracy (4 natural-text prompts built from `docs/`, 3.4k–24k tokens, `max_tokens=16`, greedy, `logprobs=20` at the first generated position; every case compared against the first fresh run of the same prompt):

| case | top-1 \|Δlogprob\| mean / max | mean \|Δlogprob\| over shared top-20 | max \|Δlogprob\| | identical 16-token greedy output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fresh again (no cache at all) | 0.10 / 0.25 | 0.42 | 2.06 | 3 / 4 |
| GPU prefix hit | 0.13 / 0.31 | 0.27 | 1.03 | 2 / 4 |
| CPU (connector) hit | 0.11 / 0.16 | 0.28 | 0.91 | 3 / 4 |
| CPU hit, second time | 0.11 / 0.12 | 0.32 | 1.88 | 3 / 4 |

The CPU-hit deltas sit inside the band that two *fresh* recomputations of the same prompt already show on this model/backend (the fresh-vs-fresh spread is not caused by this PR; it is present with the connector disabled as well, see the `fresh again` row), so the offload round trip adds no measurable error over a plain GPU prefix hit.

AI assistance: this change was developed with Claude Code (analysis, patch, tests and the reproduction scripts); the human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and evaluations above.

title: [Bugfix][SparseMLA] Fix piecewise cudagraph capture crash in index group
body:
## What

Fix an engine-startup crash when a sparse-MLA model captures decode batches with **piecewise** cudagraphs (e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash, a hybrid KDA + sparse-MLA model):

```log
File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/index_group.py", line 133, in _convert_once
    self.side_stream.wait_event(self.logical_topk_ready)
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument
```

Full startup traceback (4x GB300, TP4, `load_format=dummy`; identical with real weights, the capture path does not read weights):

```log
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 988, in profile_cudagraph_memory
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py", line 920, in profile_cudagraph_memory
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py", line 456, in capture
File "vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py", line 206, in add_eager
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py", line 1483, in unified_mla_attention_with_output
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/sparse_mla_attention.py", line 736, in _convert_logical_to_physical_topk
File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/index_group.py", line 95, in convert_logical_to_physical_topk
File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/index_group.py", line 133, in _convert_once
    self.side_stream.wait_event(self.logical_topk_ready)
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument
```

## Root cause

`SparseMLAIndexGroup` overlaps the logical→physical topk conversion with the compute stream via the `logical_topk_ready` event: the indexer records it on the compute stream after computing topk, and `_convert_once` waits on it on the side stream.

In piecewise cudagraph mode the indexer runs **inside a captured graph segment**, while the consumer runs in the following **eager break** (`unified_mla_attention_with_output` is an `@eager_break_during_capture` point, executed by `add_eager()` after the segment's `capture_end()`). An event recorded during stream capture is graph-local; waiting on it eagerly is `cudaErrorInvalidValue`.

Minimal reproduction of the exact pattern (no vLLM involved):

```python
g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
with torch.cuda.graph(g):
    ev.record(torch.cuda.current_stream())   # inside capture
side.wait_event(ev)                          # eager, after capture -> invalid argument
```

Why only some models: FULL cudagraph capture (non-hybrid sparse MLA, e.g. DeepSeek-V3.2 decode) records and waits in-graph, which is legal; prefill-sized batches take the workspace-overflow branch of `_convert_once`, which never touches the event. Hybrid models like GLM-5.3-Flash capture decode batches piecewise and hit the crash during `profile_cudagraph_memory`.

## Fix

In piecewise mode, skip the event entirely: `set_logical_topk_ready` does not record (a record inside a capture segment would be graph-local and unusable anyway), and `_convert_once` orders the side stream with `wait_stream(compute_stream)` — identical to the existing `has_indexer=False` path, and correct because the convert is always invoked after the indexer on the same compute stream. FULL/eager modes keep the fine-grained event. The same guard is applied to the HiSparse copy stream. Adds `in_piecewise_cudagraph()` to `forward_context.py`.

## Tests

- New regression test (record inside captured segment + convert in eager break under `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture`); fails pre-fix at `index_group.py:133` with the production error, passes post-fix:

  `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k piecewise_capture`

- Sparse MLA subset (convert / index_group / piecewise / hisparse): 47 passed

  `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "convert or index_group or piecewise or hisparse"`

- E2E on 4x GB300, GLM-5.3-Flash real weights, TP4: engine starts with cudagraphs enabled (crashed at startup before), generation works.

## Model evaluation

GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 questions, GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 on 4x GB300 (this branch, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, no speculative decoding): **91.8%** accuracy (invalid rate 0.0%).

## Notes

- Bisect: the crash starts with #53781, which introduced the side-stream + `logical_topk_ready` event for the topk conversion (before it, the convert ran on the compute stream with no event). Verified empirically: its parent commit starts cleanly, it crashes at engine startup. Purely informational for locating the change — the piecewise interaction was easy to miss.
- Duplicate check: no open PR covers this crash; #54851 is a different piecewise-mode issue (KV-cache writes baked into captured graphs for DSA models on multi-node TP).
- AI assistance: developed with AI assistance (Kimi Code); all changes reviewed and tested by the submitter.
