title: [Model][DSv4.1] FlashMLA mega attention and the NVFP4 compressed KV cache
body:
## Purpose

Supersedes #56344, which closed when its base branch `dsv41-optimized` was deleted.

FlashMLA's mega-attention kernel does Q RoPE, sparse attention, the output's inverse RoPE and its FP8 cast in one launch, writing straight into the buffer `wo_a` consumes. It arrives as `FlashMLAMegaAttnBackend` (`FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41`) with its own attention layer, plus the V4.1 NVFP4 compressed KV record that only this kernel can read — and, as of this revision, **it is the SM100 default** rather than an opt-in backend.

Rebased onto current `main`, which now includes #56441 (KV-only DSpark context insertion); that PR touched the same translation unit and its interaction with this one is described under *Rebase onto #56441* below.

## The interface capability the base layer acts on

`accepts_unnormed_unroped_query` — the attention kernel applies the Q norm and RoPE itself and reads Q in its own chunk-interleaved layout, so the layer's fused KV insert reduces to a zero-pad of Q to the kernel's head count, and to nothing at all once the shard is already that wide.

The output side needs no flag: the mega layer's `_alloc_attn_out` / `_o_proj` pair speaks `QuantizedActivation` where every other layer speaks bf16 and rotates in `_o_proj`. An earlier revision of this PR declared a second capability, `produces_inv_roped_quantized_output`; it had no reader — the dispatch is the override pair — so it is gone.

## Q reaches the kernel through the existing fused op, not a new one

Rather than a separate Triton pad kernel, `fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_quant_insert` gains two independent knobs:

- `apply_q_rope` — rotate Q as well; KV is always rotated. A runtime argument, on the `kv_mxfp8` precedent.
- `is_q_interleaved` — read and write Q in the mega layout (32 chunks of `[heads, 16]` per token), which moves the padding heads to the tail of every head-dim chunk. A template parameter, because it selects the address arithmetic.

They are orthogonal, and that is tested. A lane owns dims `[16l, 16l+16)` of its head in **either** layout — only the address differs — so the per-head RMSNorm and the GPT-J RoPE are equally valid interleaved. `test_q_interleaved_is_orthogonal_to_norm_and_rope` pins it over all eight of (16, 64 heads) × (norm on/off) × (RoPE on/off): the head-major result permuted into the interleaved layout must equal the interleaved path on a permuted input, bit for bit, with the KV cache byte-identical so the Q layout cannot leak into the KV half. An earlier revision conflated the two into one flag on the mistaken belief that the layout made RoPE ill-defined; that test fails against the conflated form.

`q_head_padded = 0` additionally asks for the KV insert alone, which is what TP1 wants — its 64 live heads are already the kernel's head count, so no Q pass is scheduled at all.

## One buffer pair per step

The output travels as a `QuantizedActivation` (`kMxfp8Dynamic`: fp8 e4m3 data, packed-ue8m0 MN-major scales). FlashMLA's fused ops take caller-provided `out_fp8` / `out_sf`, so a single buffer pair covers a whole step: the prefill chunks and the decode segment fill disjoint token ranges, and one `fp8_einsum` over all N tokens replaces one call per segment. The scale buffer's head-dim stride is `ceil4(N)` — both what the kernel requires of a caller buffer and what DeepGEMM expects for that N.

`wq_b` rows and `wo_a` columns are permuted once at load into the kernel's chunk-interleaved layouts, so the surrounding GEMMs speak them directly rather than shuffling per step. DSpark's draft layers are ordinary `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer`s and therefore take the engine-wide backend, so they owe the same post-load permutation; `DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM.process_weights_after_loading` now runs it, where before it finalized only MoE weights and every draft forward hit the layer's own guard.

## NVFP4 compressed cache

`nvfp4_ds_mla` now means the V4.1 MXFP8 sliding-window record beside a 288 B NVFP4 compressed record (256 B of e2m1 pairs, then 32 e4m3 scales of 16 dims). It rides the byte-width dispatch the fp8 records already use, so `rope_quant_insert` and `dequantize_and_gather_k_cache` pick it up with no call-site change; CuteDSL has no fp4 gather, so that record takes Triton.

This is the format the reference implementation itself stores: `inference/model.py` quantizes the compressed latent with `fp4_act_quant(latent, 16, True, scale_dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)` — group 16, e4m3 scales. `fp8_ds_mla` is *more* precise than the reference on that cache, not less.

Each layer declares the packed record its kernel prefers, and an unspecific `--kv-cache-dtype` resolves to it:

| layer | `auto` / `fp8` | explicit `fp8_ds_mla` | explicit `nvfp4_ds_mla` |
|---|---|---|---|
| mega attention | `nvfp4_ds_mla` | `fp8_ds_mla` | `nvfp4_ds_mla` |
| `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` | `fp8_ds_mla` | `fp8_ds_mla` | rejected by the backend |
| plain-row (FlashInfer) | `fp8` | — | `ValueError` |

## Default backend on SM100

An unspecified `--attention_config.backend` now resolves to `FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41` on SM100. The layer answers `is_available_for()` rather than letting the selector guess, because `__init__` raises on topologies the kernel cannot serve — it is SM100 only, it needs `WV_GROUP_SIZE` heads per `wo_a` group, and a build may not carry the kernel at all. On a 64-head model that admits TP1 through TP8 and declines TP16 (4 local heads), which falls through to `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` instead of failing at startup.

The default is chosen for TP1's win plus the 45%-smaller compressed record, **not** for a uniform speedup — see the table below, where TP2 through TP8 are a wash. Set `--attention_config.backend=FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` to get the previous path.

## Performance

`benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_mega_attn.py`, one GB300, CUDA graphs on, counting every per-step op each path runs (topk_swa=128, topk_extra=512, NVFP4 compressed cache), as mega / `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` microseconds on a 64-head model:

```
  s_q                    1      32     128     256     512
  TP1 (64 live heads)  29/29   31/31   31/40   53/72   96/140    up to 1.45x
  TP2 (32 live)        29/29   31/30   35/35   61/63  110/119
  TP4 (16 live)        29/29   31/29   34/34   59/58  109/109
  TP8 (8 live)         29/29   31/29   33/33   59/57  107/104
```

The decisive variable is live heads over padded heads, not batch size: the kernel absorbs the inverse RoPE and the FP8 cast, whose cost scales with *live* heads, while its own cost scales with *padded* heads — always 64, since FlashMLA's FP8 decode takes only `h_q` in {64, 128}. So TP1 wins and TP2 down cancel to within a few percent. There is no batch size at which falling back pays, so there is no minimum-token threshold and no fallback path to maintain.

An earlier revision of this table also charged the mega arm for a separate Q-pad kernel "that the split-KV path gets for free"; that is no longer true — the pad is now inside the same fused insert both paths run, and at TP1 it is skipped entirely.

These are decode numbers; **prefill is unmeasured**. Measure under CUDA graphs — in eager mode launch overhead swamps both paths and overstates the fused one several-fold.

## Accuracy: measured end to end, with DSpark

The earlier revision listed accuracy as not covered. It now is. Both arms on one GB300, TP4, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` at pinned snapshot `517ef625`, identical eval config, DSpark k=5 with **real** rejection sampling (`rejection_sample_method=synthetic` deliberately absent, so acceptance measures the draft rather than echoing the config). The two recipes differ by exactly one engine flag.

| | mega attention (NVFP4) | `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` (fp8_ds_mla) | history band |
|---|---|---|---|
| gsm8k flexible / strict | **0.9318** / 0.9318 | 0.9265 / 0.9265 | median 0.9287, IQR 0.9265–0.9318 |
| gpqa_diamond exact / pass@4 | **0.9053** / 0.9545 | 0.9066 / 0.9545 | median 0.9040, IQR 0.8990–0.9141 |
| draft acceptance gpqa | 0.4376 (len 3.188) | 0.4341 (len 3.171) | |
| draft acceptance gsm8k | 0.4957 (len 3.479) | 0.4945 (len 3.473) | |

All four scores land inside their interquartile range, and the two arms agree within sampling noise (gsm8k 0.53 pt, gpqa 0.13 pt; gpqa is n=198 at temperature 1.0, so one question is ~0.5 pt). **The fused kernel and the 45%-smaller compressed record cost nothing measurable in accuracy.**

Draft acceptance is the more sensitive check, because it reads draft-versus-target agreement directly: all four figures span 0.4341–0.4376 on gpqa and 0.4945–0.4957 on gsm8k, and they also reproduce the pre-rebase run to three decimals.

Scores were validated before being quoted: `num_request_errors: 0` on every eval, step durations plausible (530/114 s and 519/113 s), gsm8k > gpqa cross-task ordering, flexible − strict gap exactly 0.0000, and truncation of 3/792 gpqa and 1/1319 gsm8k rows so that answered-only accuracy tracks the headline (mega 0.9087 / 0.9332; sparse 0.9100 / 0.9279). GSM8K runs `api_type: completions` 5-shot greedy, so it bypasses the chat template and is not the deployed serving path; GPQA runs the deployed chat path with thinking on and the `deepseek_v41` reasoning parser.

## Rebase onto #56441

#56441 added a KV-only context-insert op to the same translation unit. Two of its call sites needed updating for this series and **git reported no conflict on either**, because neither side edited those lines — they would have surfaced only at compile time: `launchFusedDeepseekV4Templated` gains a template parameter (`is_q_interleaved`) and a runtime one (`apply_q_rope`), and the KV-only op calls it. Both are fixed at the call site, with a comment noting that zero query heads means no Q slot is scheduled so neither knob is reachable there.

The two series had also independently arrived at the same `kNumHeadsQPadded == 0` grid fix (I contributed it to #56441 during review); it collapsed to one.

## Test Plan & Result

```
pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py \
       tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
       tests/kernels/test_dsv41_mega_attn_layouts.py \
       tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_rope_quant.py \
       tests/kernels/test_fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py     # 522 passed, 17 skipped
pre-commit run --files <changed files>                    # all hooks pass
```

The last two suites are there because the op this PR changes is also called by the **DSv4.0** paths (`deepseek_v4/attention.py`, its dspark, xpu); the two new parameters are defaulted so those call sites still bind, which is worth testing rather than assuming.

New tests cover the NVFP4 record byte-exactly against a reference quantizer derived from FlashMLA's `tests/quant.py` (scales exact, values within half an e2m1 step, untouched rows and page padding preserved), an insert→gather round trip, the `wq_b` / `wo_a` permutations against a reference that permutes the activation instead, the interleaved Q pad (live elements bit-exact, padding heads zero, both grid variants, and the KV-insert-only launch), the norm/RoPE orthogonality described above, and graph-replay coverage that a captured insert refills its allocated Q buffer over changed input.

## Not duplicating

#56893 (merged) landed the V4.1 MXFP8 KV record this builds on. #56344 is the earlier flag-gated form of this same integration and is closed. #56441 (merged) added a KV-only wrapper op in the same files; disjoint in intent, and the interaction is described above.

## Not yet covered

- **Prefill perf is unmeasured** — every number above is decode.
- **Non-SM100 arches** are untouched by design; the kernel has no SM90 instantiation and the default declines there.
- Two commits in this series do not build standalone (a call-site fix landed one commit later than the parameter it fixes), which matters only for `git bisect` across the series, not for the tip or a squash-merge.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The backend, the interface capability, the NVFP4 record, the default-backend selection, the tests, the benchmark and the accuracy runs above were produced in that session and reviewed by me.

title: [DSpark] Support pipeline-parallel targets in aggregated serving
body:
## What

DSpark on a pipeline-parallel target in aggregated (non-PD) serving. The drafter runs wholly on the last PP stage; this PR makes that work correctly:

- **Draft broadcast across stages**: the last stage's speculator proposes drafts, but earlier stages need them for the next verification step. The last rank now broadcasts the fresh drafts on the PP group (`PPHandler.broadcast_drafts`), and the broadcast is gated out of the no-op second call site when a speculator ran (double-posting misaligned the recv FIFO and hung the pipeline).
- **Warmup**: the deferred PP post-update triton kernel never runs during warmup steps on non-last ranks; its first mid-serving compile would deadlock against the in-flight NCCL broadcast. `warmup_pp_decode_update` compiles it during capture, and the sampled-token broadcast is disabled for the warmup window.
- **Draft embedding under PP**: the drafter aliases the target's embedding table, which #50514 retains on the last PP stage when speculative decoding is active. (An earlier revision of this PR loaded a separate drafter copy; dropped per review.)
- **Padded graph batch safety**: the DFlash prepare-inputs kernel clears `input_ids`/`positions` and sets `is_padding` on CUDA-graph padding rows, and the DSv4 top-k router zeroes padded-row selections instead of reading uninitialized state.

## Not a duplicate

Split from #53577 (reviewer request): this PR is the aggregated-serving half; the PD prefill + KV-transfer half follows separately.

## Tests

- New/extended: `tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py`, `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py`.
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py -q` → 1686 passed, 6 skipped.
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py -q` → 34 passed.

## Model evaluation

DeepSeek-V4-Flash (0731) DSpark K=5, IFB PP2×TP2, GSM8K strict-match: **0.9484** (1319 samples; an earlier revision measured 0.9545 — both within noise of the target-only arm). Spec decode mean acceptance length 4.38.

Kimi-K3 DSpark IFB PP relies on the TritonMLA causal multi-token fix from #51065 (merged; included in this branch's base). Smoke-verified on SM120 (PP2×TP4): coherent outputs with healthy per-position draft acceptance (144/96/55/31/22/17/12/6 over K=8).

AI assistance was used in preparing this PR.

title: [Perf][Kernel] Integrate Mega-mHC from DeepGEMM for DeepSeek V4.1  (reopen of #56255)
body:
## Summary

- Reopen [vLLM #56255](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56255) (closed unmerged), rebased on the [#56876](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56876) base (`1b5a7abb58`) with the model path retargeted to `deepseek_v41`.
- Keep the original implementation commit separate from the follow-up adaptation; its elfutils dependency is already in the base.
- Preserve the current TileLang fused path for auxiliary capture and unsupported inputs, and preserve Engram injection order.
- Pin the #56876 vLLM DeepGEMM fork at `ad1f1726` (2.8.0), including its SM90/SM120 support and API fixes.

## Why this is not a duplicate

#56255 was closed without merging; this PR reopens that work. Open-PR searches show no competing Mega-mHC integration. [#56611](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56611) fuses TileLang statistics with attention/FFN instead; this change uses DeepGEMM Mega-mHC fusion. Dependency changes intentionally reuse #56876 rather than re-opening them.

## Benchmarks

Single GB200, H=5120 / 7168, `hc_mult=4`, BF16, 20 Sinkhorn iterations. Full post + delayed-pre + RMSNorm chain. CUPTI full-stage spans over CUDA graph replays, cold L2, 10 warmup + 100 samples per variant in forward/reverse (ABCCBA) order. Setup, JIT, and host allocation excluded; CPU launch overhead is outside the measured spans.

| H | Decode tokens | Split (µs) | Current TileLang fused (µs) | Mega-mHC (µs) | vs current |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 5120 | 1 | 16.29 | 13.30 | 11.68 | 1.14× |
| 5120 | 8 | 17.44 | 13.31 | 11.62 | 1.15× |
| 5120 | 64 | 18.21 | 18.30 | 12.64 | 1.45× |
| 5120 | 256 | 20.90 | 21.14 | 15.90 | 1.33× |
| 7168 | 1 | 20.67 | 17.02 | 12.86 | 1.32× |
| 7168 | 8 | 20.61 | 15.71 | 12.13 | 1.30× |
| 7168 | 64 | 22.27 | 22.37 | 14.85 | 1.51× |
| 7168 | 256 | 25.41 | 25.47 | 17.28 | 1.47× |

### E2E Benchmarks

GB200 TP4, official DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, `fp8_ds_mla`, no speculative decoding, `max-model-len=40960`. Same local source (`e7fcd569dd`) and dependencies; TileLang uses the existing fused-op worker hook, and #56611 Overlap is ported onto this base with TP4 enabled.

`vllm bench serve`: exactly 8192/32768 input + 1024 output tokens, seed 0, temperature 0, one warmup, ignore EOS, prefix caching disabled. C1: 20 requests/case; C32: 64. All **504 requests** completed with exact token counts.

Latencies are in ms. **Δ is relative to TileLang**, shown as mean TPOT / output throughput; negative TPOT and positive throughput are better.

**Concurrency 1:**
| Input | Variant | TPOT mean / p50 | TTFT p50 | TTFT p99 | E2E p50 | Output tok/s | Δ TPOT / tok/s |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8k | TileLang | 7.466 / 7.464 | 211.7 | 227.6 | 7845.1 | 130.5 | — |
| 8k | Mega-mHC | 7.352 / 7.351 | 190.1 | 192.9 | 7710.3 | 132.8 | -1.5% / +1.8% |
| 8k | Overlap | 7.355 / 7.351 | 204.7 | 215.1 | 7724.5 | 132.5 | -1.5% / +1.6% |
| 32k | TileLang | 7.503 / 7.502 | 788.2 | 807.3 | 8462.8 | 121.0 | — |
| 32k | Mega-mHC | 7.396 / 7.394 | 715.0 | 737.8 | 8284.4 | 123.6 | -1.4% / +2.2% |
| 32k | Overlap | 7.394 / 7.394 | 769.2 | 783.6 | 8336.5 | 122.9 | -1.5% / +1.5% |

**Concurrency 32:**
| Input | Variant | TPOT mean / p50 | TTFT p50 | TTFT p99 | E2E p50 | Output tok/s | Δ TPOT / tok/s |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8k | TileLang | 13.565 / 14.518 | 1016.7 | 5555.9 | 15799.0 | 2055.2 | — |
| 8k | Mega-mHC | 13.659 / 13.692 | 913.4 | 4948.5 | 15740.2 | 2069.2 | +0.7% / +0.7% |
| 8k | Overlap | 14.037 / 14.394 | 1007.7 | 5517.2 | 16318.7 | 1995.2 | +3.5% / -2.9% |
| 32k | TileLang | 23.500 / 27.256 | 2947.8 | 21745.9 | 31014.7 | 1039.9 | — |
| 32k | Mega-mHC | 22.827 / 26.943 | 2732.4 | 20366.1 | 29700.7 | 1083.7 | -2.9% / +4.2% |
| 32k | Overlap | 23.842 / 28.315 | 2907.7 | 21991.1 | 31213.0 | 1032.6 | +1.5% / -0.7% |

**Conclusion:** Mega-mHC and Overlap have essentially equal C1 TPOT; Mega has lower TTFT. At C32, Mega delivers **3.7% / 5.0% more output tok/s than Overlap** at 8k / 32k.

## Tests
`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py -q -x`: **174 passed, 32 skipped** — covers empty/decode/prefill and changed-input CUDA graph replay. FP8 DeepGEMM tests: **100 passed, 25 skipped**; matching-extension qnorm/RoPE tests: **6 passed**. Pre-commit checks passed.

| Task | Configuration | Score | Request errors | Output-limit hits |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K | 1319 problems, 5-shot, greedy, max output 4096 | 1225/1319 (92.87%) | 0 | 1 |
| GPQA Diamond | 198 problems, 0-shot, default high thinking, temp 1.0, top_p 0.95, max output 262144 | 179/198 (90.40%) | 0 | 0 |

Both accuracy evaluations used Mega-mHC with the official `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` checkpoint, on exclusive GB200 nodes with TP4+EP, `fp8_ds_mla`, DeepGEMM MegaMoE, CPU-offloaded Engram, no speculative decoding, and prefix caching disabled. One pass run at concurrency 32, request seed 0 and dataset/few-shot seed 1234. GSM8K: 1319 problems, 5-shot, completions endpoint, greedy (`temperature=0`, `top_p=1`), max output 4096 and server context 8192; strict-match and flexible-extract both scored **1225/1319 (92.87%)**, with one output-limit hit. GPQA Diamond: 198 problems, 0-shot, chat completions, `think=true`, default `high` reasoning effort (not explicitly overridden), `temperature=1`, `top_p=0.95`, max output 262144 and server context 1048576; **179/198 (90.40%)**, with no output-limit hits. Both had zero request errors; server max batched tokens was 8192, max sequences 256.


## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (OpenAI Codex); all changes were reviewed and tested by the human submitter.

title: [Spec Decode][Model] Support DFlash2 draft models with GLM-5.3-Flash
body:
## Summary

`incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` is the block-diffusion (DFlash2) drafter published for `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`. On current `main` the pair cannot be served: `vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2",...}'` fails during startup, and fixing one failure exposes the next. This PR makes the combination start and serve on NVIDIA (8x H100, TP8 + EP), adds unit coverage for the two non-model changes, and reports a throughput sweep against the existing MTP path. No kernels, defaults, or MTP behaviour are changed.

The three blockers on `main` (9d4d9aa5bc), in the order they surface:

| # | Stage | Error on `main` | Root cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | draft model load | `RuntimeError: Model does not support EAGLE3 interface` | `Glm5NextForCausalLM` / `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` (the architecture the DFlash2 checkpoint targets) do not declare `SupportsEagle3`, and `Glm5NextModel` is not an `EagleModelMixin`, so the DFlash speculator cannot register its aux hidden-state layers (`target_layer_ids + 1 = [6, 15, 25, 34, 43]`). |
| 2 | KV cache init | `NotImplementedError: Layer language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.indexer.k_cache: page size is not divisible by the maximum page size and cannot be padded. Padding is only supported for non-MLA attention layers.` | `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` bails out as soon as a non-MLA attention layer (the draft's sliding-window GQA layers) is present, so the generic page unifier runs on a spec set it cannot unify (MLA 655,360 B, indexer 21,120 B and draft 163,840 B pages at block_size 640). |
| 3 | config | `ValueError: Number of experts in the model must be greater than 0 when expert parallelism is enabled` | `create_draft_parallel_config` copies `enable_expert_parallel` from the MoE target onto the dense drafter (introduced by #55914 for the DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE drafter). |

### Changes

- **`vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py` (aux hidden-state capture).** `Glm5NextModel` becomes an `EagleModelMixin`; `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` declare `SupportsEagle3`. The tensor handed to the drafter is not `hidden_states + residual`: GLM-5.3-Flash layers run mHC with 4 residual streams and defer each layer's `hc_post` into the next layer's fused post+pre kernel, so at a layer boundary `residual` is the widened `(T, 4 * hidden)` stream (a naive `hidden + residual` fails with `The size of tensor a (8192) must match the size of tensor b (4) at non-singleton dimension 1`) and `hidden_states` alone is the raw layer output. `_aux_hidden_state()` completes the deferred `hc_post` through a dedicated `MHCPostOp` and contracts the streams back to `hidden_size` with `hc_contract`, which is the quantity SGLang's `_prepare_aux_hidden_state` feeds DFlash2. The capture is read-only: the layer loop keeps consuming the original `(hidden_states, residual, post, comb)` tuple. Non-mHC layer boundaries already carry the summed stream in `hidden_states` and are returned as-is. When any aux layer is requested, `forward` returns `(hidden_states, aux_hidden_states)`; otherwise the return type is unchanged.

### Relationship to existing PRs (duplicate check run on 2026-09-15)

Searches: `gh pr list --state open --search "dflash glm"`, `"GLM-5.3 speculative draft"`, `"create_draft_parallel_config"`, `"enable_expert_parallel draft model"`, `gh pr list --state all --search "dflash"`, `gh issue list --search "GLM-5.3-Flash dflash"`.

- #55682 (Leoyzen, open) implements the aux capture with the same semantics (materialize `hc_post`, then `hc_contract`, at the layer boundary) and adds a CPU unit suite for it. It intentionally leaves the KV-cache layout to a companion change (its description notes the draft sliding-window groups still need one); on the configuration tested here (TP8, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, H100) `main` + an aux-capture-only change still fails at blocker 2. The `model.py` change here is functionally equivalent for GLM-5.3-Flash's mHC boundaries; if #55682 lands first, this PR rebases onto it and drops its `model.py` hunk.
- #55423 (zixi-qi, draft, needs-rebase) covers aux capture plus a KV layout, but with a different layout design: the draft's sliding-window layers are re-blocked to the MLA block size, padded to the MLA page and aliased into the target's MLA slots (no extra bytes per block; `is_eagle_group` follows `use_eagle_block_drop()`; tested with `disable_eagle_block_drop=true`). This PR keeps the draft in a separate region with its native page instead; it is simpler and needs no block-drop override, but it costs KV capacity (numbers below). The two are alternative designs for reviewers to choose between.
- #56933 (hnt2601, opened 2026-09-15) is the same EP-inheritance fix with a different signature (`draft_model_config: ModelConfig | None`). If it merges first, this PR drops the `speculative.py` hunk.
- #55219 (ivanium, draft) removes the GLM-specific layout in favour of the generic packed layout; if that lands, the `kv_cache_utils.py` part of this PR is superseded.
- #54451 (ROCm: glm5next lacks `SupportsEagle3`) is the ROCm counterpart of blocker 1; this PR only touches the NVIDIA model file.

No open PR makes `GLM-5.3-Flash + GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` start on `main` end to end; this one does, and the parts overlapping with #55682 and #56933 are flagged above for rebasing.

Due to discussion for kv cache allocation,  this PR just submits the main support in advance.

## Previous full supported performance

**Setup.** 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (driver 535.154.05), TP8 + EP, torch 2.13.0+cu129, FlashInfer 0.6.18, Python 3.12, vLLM `main` 9d4d9aa5bc + this branch, V2 model runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`). Target `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (fp8 weights, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, `--max-model-len 131072`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`, `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`, `--tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice`). Draft `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` (5 sliding-window layers, sliding window 2048, block_size 8). Auto-selected attention backends: FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90 (target), FLASH_ATTN (draft).

**Workload.** 16 fixed prompts (code and prose), greedy (`temperature=0`), `max_tokens=512`, `/v1/chat/completions`. Single stream = 4 sequential prompts after 2 warm-ups; concurrency N = N simultaneous requests (prompts cycled). Aggregate output tok/s, per-request median tok/s in parentheses. `k` = `num_speculative_tokens`, "FA" / "FI" = FlashAttention / FlashInfer draft attention, the number in the config column is `--max-num-seqs`.

| Config | Single stream | Conc 8 | Conc 32 | Conc 64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DFlash2 k=16, FA, 48 | 178.7 | 848.5 (118.3) | 707.3 (23.1) | - |
| DFlash2 k=8, FA, 48 | 202.1 | 987.7 (136.3) | 2652.5 (94.5) | - |
| DFlash2 k=6, FA, 48 | 218.5 | 1064.5 (145.2) | 2844.3 (101.2) | - |
| DFlash2 k=4, FA, 48 | 220.3 | 1051.3 (148.0) | 2751.6 (98.8) | - |
| DFlash2 k=6, FI, 48 | 202.1 | 1021.0 (141.1) | 2578.8 (95.1) | - |
| **DFlash2 k=6, FA, 96** (run 1) | **223.0** | **1074.0 (145.2)** | **2850.7 (103.9)** | - |
| **DFlash2 k=6, FA, 96** (run 2) | **225.5** | - | **2923.6 (106.7)** | **4269.3 (77.5)** |
| MTP k=5, 96 (baseline) | 160.7 | 853.7 (117.3) | 2377.0 (84.0) | 3721.3 (66.7) |

Acceptance, aggregated from every `SpecDecoding metrics` log line of each run:

| Config | Mean acceptance length | Draft acceptance rate | Per-position acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|
| DFlash2 k=16 | 3.63 | 16.5% | 0.75, 0.54, 0.39, 0.28, 0.20, 0.14, 0.10, 0.08, 0.05, 0.04, 0.02, 0.01, 0.006, 0.004, 0.002, 0.001 |
| DFlash2 k=8 | 3.33 | 29.1% | 0.75, 0.53, 0.36, 0.25, 0.18, 0.12, 0.08, 0.06 |
| DFlash2 k=6 | 3.31 | 38.5% | 0.77, 0.55, 0.39, 0.28, 0.19, 0.13 |
| DFlash2 k=4 | 3.00 | 49.9% | 0.78, 0.56, 0.39, 0.27 |
| MTP k=5 | 3.13 | 42.7% | 0.81, 0.57, 0.37, 0.23, 0.15 |

Takeaways:

- `num_speculative_tokens` is the dominant knob. Acceptance decays to ~0 beyond position 8 (the drafter's block_size), so k=16 pays a 17-token verify per step for the same ~3.3-3.6 accepted tokens; going to k=6 raises conc-32 throughput from 707 to 2924 tok/s (4.1x). k=4..6 is the sweet spot on this workload, k=8 is slightly worse.
- Against MTP k=5 at identical settings, DFlash2 k=6 is faster at every concurrency: +40% single stream, +26% at 8, +23% at 32, +15% at 64.
- FlashInfer as the draft attention backend is 7-9% slower than the auto-selected FlashAttention.
- `--max-num-seqs 96` vs 48: +2-3%, no preemption at concurrency 64.

**KV cache capacity (cost of the separate draft region).**

| Config | Available KV memory | KV capacity | Max concurrency at 131072 tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| MTP k=5 | 23.61 GiB | 1,802,673 tokens | 13.75x |
| DFlash2 k=6 | 23.49 GiB | 1,358,649 tokens | 10.37x |

Per block (block_size 640) the target uses 11 x 655,360 B MLA pages plus 11 x 21,120 B indexer pages (kpool tails aliased into them); the draft adds 5 x 163,840 B pages and its own per-request block demand to the group-aware capacity estimate, hence 24.6% fewer tokens than MTP at the same memory. #55423's slot-aliasing design avoids this at the price of re-blocking the draft to the MLA page; that is the main trade-off between the two PRs. At `--max-num-seqs 96` this still leaves ~14k tokens per sequence.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Unit tests
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_get_kv_cache_config_glm5_with_dflash_draft_group "tests/test_config.py::test_draft_parallel_config_inherits_ep_only_for_moe_drafters" -v

# Lint and types
pre-commit run --files vllm/config/speculative.py vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py tests/test_config.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py

# Serve (8x H100)
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --served-model-name glm-5.3-flash --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --kv-cache-dtype auto --max-num-seqs 96 --max-model-len 131072 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":6}'
# MTP baseline: same command with --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'

# Tool-calling E2E: 8 scenarios against /v1/chat/completions (auto / required / named tool_choice, zero-arg tool, no tools, thinking off, streaming, multi-turn), see Test Result
# Throughput sweep: 16 prompts, greedy, max_tokens=512, single stream + concurrency {8,32} / {32,64}; per-config server relaunch with the speculative-config JSON above
# Accuracy
.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 1
```

## Test Result

**Unit tests.** `3 passed` (the kv-cache test and both parametrizations of the config test).

**pre-commit.** All hooks pass on the five changed files, including `mypy-3.10` (the follow-up commit fixes a `dict` invariance error in `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next`).

**Startup.** Each blocker above was hit and cleared in turn on this branch; the final configuration loads the draft (5 layers, `Overriding draft model max model len from 1048576 to 131072`), builds the KV cache (`GPU KV cache size: 1,358,649 tokens`), captures CUDA graphs and serves.

**Tool-calling E2E** against the running DFlash2 server (`--tool-call-parser glm47`, `--reasoning-parser glm45`): 8/8 pass, zero FSM or CUDA errors in the server log. Repeated after each sweep configuration with the same result.

| Scenario | Checks | Result |
|---|---|---|
| auto tool call | `tool_choice=auto`, one `<tool_call>` parsed into `tool_calls`, arguments valid JSON | PASS |
| required tool call | `tool_choice=required` forces a call | PASS |
| named tool call | `tool_choice={"type":"function","function":{"name":...}}` picks the named tool | PASS |
| named zero-argument tool | tool without parameters yields `arguments == "{}"` | PASS |
| no tools, plain chat | no tool schema, ordinary completion, no stray tags | PASS |
| thinking off | `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` with tools | PASS |
| streaming tool call | `stream=true`, deltas reassemble to a valid call | PASS |
| multi-turn | tool result fed back, second assistant turn answers from it | PASS |

**GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy, `max_tokens=256`, `--max-concurrency 1 --request-timeout-seconds 7200`; the default 600 s timeout acts as a global deadline at concurrency 1 and truncates the run).**

| Server | Accuracy | Invalid responses | Output tokens | Wall time | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Target only (no speculative config), same machine and flags | 0.931 | 0.0% | 121,390 | 1195 s | 101.6 |
| DFlash2 k=6 (this PR) | 0.939 | 0.0% | 123,732 | 607 s | 203.8 |

The two accuracies differ by 0.8 points (about 10 of 1319 questions), inside the run-to-run spread of this greedy-but-nondeterministic stack (see below); output-token counts match within 2%. DFlash2 delivers the same accuracy at 2.0x the single-stream decode speed.

**Greedy output determinism.** Exact token-level lossless verification is not possible on this stack: with `temperature=0` the same server produces different continuations run to run (16 sweep prompts, 512 tokens, sequential, prompt already cached): target-only 0/16 identical across three runs (median common prefix 272-306 characters before the first divergence), DFlash2 k=6 0/16 identical across three runs (median 237-306), and DFlash2 vs target-only 0/16 identical (median 222-237). The run-to-run spread of the target alone is the same size as the DFlash2-vs-target spread, so the divergence comes from the fp8 MoE + EP numerics of the target (near-tie argmax flips), not from the speculative path; the GSM8K parity above (0.919 vs 0.911) is the meaningful losslessness check.

**Pre-existing crash observed while testing, not introduced by this PR (#55626).** Any step that co-schedules a ~600+ token prefill with a speculative verify step, or a burst of a dozen ~630-token prefills, kills the engine with an asynchronous CUDA fault. It reproduces identically with MTP, whose KV layout on this branch is byte-for-byte the `main` layout, so it is a property of the target's FlashInfer SM90 sparse-MLA path with speculative decoding, matching the traceback location and the FlashInfer core dump posted in #55626.

| Run | Speculative config | Load | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | DFlash2 k=6 | `gsm8k_eval.py` unbounded (100 in flight): 12 prefills of 618-645 tokens in one step, 7578 tokens | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`, all 8 workers, reproduced 3/3 |
| A' | DFlash2 k=6, `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` | same | fault attributed to FlashInfer `BatchMLAPagedAttentionSM90` in the target's `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py::forward_mqa` (`Failed to run MLA, error: an illegal memory access was encountered`) |
| B | DFlash2 k=6 | `--max-concurrency 2`: one 661-token prefill + one 7-token verify step | `CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED` (sticky error surfacing in the next GEMM) |
| C | MTP k=5 (main layout) | unbounded: 7 prefills, 4518 tokens | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` |
| D | MTP k=5 (main layout) | `--max-concurrency 2`: one 637-token prefill + one 6-token verify step | `CUDA error: an illegal instruction was encountered`, surfacing at `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py:350 _kv_lens_host` (the same frame as in #55626) |

The throughput sweep and the tool-calling E2E never hit it because their concurrent prompts are short (~30 tokens) and their long prompts run one at a time; GSM8K was therefore run at `--max-concurrency 1`. Prefix caching is not involved (`prefix_cache_stats ... hits=0` in every crash dump).

## Known limitations / follow-ups

- #55626 (above) affects every speculative configuration of GLM-5.3-Flash on SM90 and needs a separate fix; the DFlash2 path inherits it.
- The separate draft region costs KV capacity relative to the slot-aliasing design in #55423 (24.6% fewer tokens than MTP at the same memory); the two designs should be reconciled in review.
- Aux hidden states are not all-gathered under sequence parallelism (`compilation_config.pass_config.enable_sp`); the tested configuration runs with compilation mode NONE, where SP is off. Pipeline parallelism is already gated off for GLM-5.3-Flash and was not exercised.
- Tested with greedy sampling for throughput and the default sampling of the tool-calling scripts; `disable_eagle_block_drop` was left at its default.
- Only the NVIDIA model file is changed; the ROCm copy (#54451) is not addressed.

title: [CI] Relax MTP sharded sampling cross-boot noise bound
body:
## Summary

- raise the MTP sharded-sampling cross-boot divergence allowance from 2 to 3 of 20 prompts
- align the spec-decode check with the general sharded-sampling test's measured allowance of 3
- update the docstring so it no longer promises bit-exact output while the assertion deliberately permits measured near-tie noise

## Why

The exact `seeded: 3/20 prompts diverged` boundary has opened and later resolved the same L4 alert repeatedly on main, including builds #88182, #88430, #88630, #88968, #89028, and now #89107. The triggering merges touched unrelated paths; #89107 is PR #56387's DSpark EPLB fix, while this test uses Qwen3.5 MTP TP=2. In the latest job, the other five commands passed 40 tests and only this one-prompt-over-bound assertion failed.

A real request-routing or gather bug produces wholesale divergence. Keeping a small named bound of 3 still catches that signal while covering the measured boot-to-boot near-tie tail already accepted by the non-spec sharded-sampling test.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_sharded_sampling.py`
- exact Buildkite #89120 at literal head `c90bd336390ed7a62cf1a20c250e28d58c027541`: L4 Distributed DP Basic passed all seven commands; the decisive `test_mtp_sharded_sampling_equivalence` case passed in 5m20s

Refs production Main-CI alert 1268 and Buildkite #89107.

title: [CI] Keep Qwen3 Omni DSpark config fixture complete
body:
## Summary

Use `ParallelConfig()` rather than an incomplete `SimpleNamespace` for the Qwen3 Omni DSpark embedding-sharing test's target parallel configuration.

## Why

Merged PR #56387 made the DSpark loader derive its draft configuration from the target's EPLB fields. The H200 Model Executor lane then failed deterministically in builds #89112 and #89113 because this unit-test fixture only supplied `tensor_parallel_size`; `_get_dspark_parallel_config` now correctly also reads `enable_eplb`, `eplb_config`, and `enable_elastic_ep`.

This is the same test fixture that needed one-field repairs after earlier loader changes in #56011 and #56600. Supplying the real default `ParallelConfig` keeps the mock focused on the model objects while making its production configuration contract complete, so the next added parallel field does not create another stale-fixture failure.

PR #53458, associated with the latest failed build, changes Eagle3 vocabulary mapping and is unrelated.

## Duplicate check

Searched open PRs and issues for `Qwen3 Omni DSpark EPLB` and `test_qwen3_omni parallel_config`; no open change addresses this post-#56387 failure.

## Validation

- `pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py::test_dspark_shares_target_embedding_with_smaller_draft_vocabulary` — 1 passed
- `pre-commit run --files tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py` — all applicable hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX, and configuration-default validation
- `git diff --check`

Model evaluation is not applicable because this changes only a unit-test fixture.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with CI failure analysis, the patch, and validation. A human submitter must review every changed line and the exact H200 Model Executor gate before marking this PR ready.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2][Spec Decode] Honor dynamic K in autoregressive speculators, 1.2~1.3x kernel perf improvement
body:
## Purpose

MRV2 did not propagate `SchedulerOutput.num_spec_tokens_to_schedule` to autoregressive speculators, causing unnecessary draft forwards and stale draft tokens.

This PR fixes the issue

## Test

Acc covered in current unit test

Perf can be seen in this AI generated script

```py
from functools import partial
from types import SimpleNamespace

import torch
import triton

from vllm.v1.spec_decode.dynamic.utils import build_dynamic_sd_schedule_lookup
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.input_batch import InputBatch, InputBuffers
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.autoregressive.speculator import (
    AutoRegressiveSpeculator,
)

MAX_K = 5
MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 48
HIDDEN_SIZE = 4096
NUM_REQS = (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 48)
DYNAMIC_K_SCHEDULE = [(1, MAX_BATCH_SIZE, 3)]


class SyntheticSpeculator(AutoRegressiveSpeculator):
    """MRV2 proposer whose model forward is replaced by a matmul."""

    def load_draft_model(self, target_model, target_attn_layer_names):
        raise NotImplementedError("This benchmark does not load a model")

    def __init__(self, device: torch.device) -> None:
        # Deliberately skip the real constructor: it allocates model-related state.
        self.num_speculative_steps = MAX_K
        self.max_num_reqs = MAX_BATCH_SIZE
        self.max_model_len = 8192
        self.dp_size = 1
        self.dp_rank = 0
        self.pcp_manager = None
        self.eplb_state = None
        self.use_fused_multi_step_decode = True
        self.prefill_cudagraph_manager = None
        self.decode_cudagraph_manager = None
        self.speculative_config = SimpleNamespace(
            uses_dynamic_speculative_decoding=lambda: True,
        )

        self.input_buffers = InputBuffers(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, MAX_BATCH_SIZE, device)
        self.hidden_states = torch.zeros(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, HIDDEN_SIZE, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
        )
        self.last_token_indices = torch.zeros(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
        )
        self.current_draft_step = torch.zeros((), dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
        self.sample_src_positions = torch.zeros(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
        )
        self.idx_mapping = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
        self.temperature = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, device=device)
        self.seeds = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
        self.draft_tokens = torch.zeros(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, MAX_K, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
        )

        self.weight = torch.randn(
            HIDDEN_SIZE, HIDDEN_SIZE, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
        )
        self.src = torch.randn(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, HIDDEN_SIZE, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
        )
        self.dst = torch.empty_like(self.src)
        self.count_steps = False
        self.steps = 0

    def _synthetic_forward(self, num_tokens: int) -> None:
        torch.mm(self.src[:num_tokens], self.weight, out=self.dst[:num_tokens])
        self.src, self.dst = self.dst, self.src
        if self.count_steps:
            self.steps += 1

    def _prefill(self, num_reqs: int, num_tokens: int, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
        self._synthetic_forward(num_tokens)
        self.draft_tokens[:num_reqs, 0].zero_()

    def _generate_draft(
        self, num_reqs: int, num_tokens_padded: int, *args, **kwargs
    ) -> None:
        self._synthetic_forward(num_tokens_padded)


def count_forwards(speculator: SyntheticSpeculator, run) -> int:
    speculator.steps = 0
    speculator.count_steps = True
    run()
    speculator.count_steps = False
    return speculator.steps


def main() -> None:
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        raise RuntimeError("CUDA is required")

    device = torch.device("cuda")
    speculator = SyntheticSpeculator(device)
    target_buffers = InputBuffers(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, MAX_BATCH_SIZE, device)
    target_hidden_states = torch.randn_like(speculator.hidden_states)
    temperature = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, device=device)
    seeds = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    last_sampled = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    dense_schedule = build_dynamic_sd_schedule_lookup(
        DYNAMIC_K_SCHEDULE,
        vllm_max_batch_size=MAX_BATCH_SIZE,
        vllm_num_speculative_tokens=MAX_K,
    )

    print("batch  sched_k  buggy_ms  fixed_ms  speedup  forwards(buggy->fixed)")
    for num_reqs in NUM_REQS:
        batch = InputBatch.make_dummy(num_reqs, num_reqs, target_buffers)
        common_args = dict(
            input_batch=batch,
            attn_metadata={},
            slot_mappings={},
            last_hidden_states=target_hidden_states[:num_reqs],
            aux_hidden_states=None,
            num_sampled=torch.ones(num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
            num_rejected=torch.zeros(num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
            last_sampled=last_sampled,
            next_prefill_tokens=target_buffers.input_ids,
            temperature=temperature,
            seeds=seeds,
            dummy_run=True,
            skip_attn_for_dummy_run=True,
            is_profile=True,
        )
        dynamic_k = dense_schedule[num_reqs]

        # Buggy: model_runner omitted runtime K, so propose() used max K=5.
        buggy = partial(speculator.propose, **common_args)
        # Fixed: model_runner passes the scheduler-selected runtime K=3.
        fixed = partial(
            speculator.propose,
            **common_args,
            num_speculative_tokens=dynamic_k,
        )

        buggy_steps = count_forwards(speculator, buggy)
        fixed_steps = count_forwards(speculator, fixed)
        assert dynamic_k == 3
        assert buggy_steps == MAX_K
        assert fixed_steps == dynamic_k

        buggy_ms = triton.testing.do_bench(buggy)
        fixed_ms = triton.testing.do_bench(fixed)
        print(
            f"{num_reqs:>5}  {dynamic_k:>7}  {buggy_ms:>8.3f}  "
            f"{fixed_ms:>8.3f}  {buggy_ms / fixed_ms:>7.3f}x  "
            f"{buggy_steps}->{fixed_steps}"
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

And we can get

```bash
batch  sched_k  buggy_ms  fixed_ms  speedup  forwards(buggy->fixed)
    1        3     0.151     0.115    1.306x  5->3
    2        3     0.148     0.115    1.286x  5->3
    4        3     0.149     0.115    1.298x  5->3
    8        3     0.148     0.115    1.282x  5->3
   16        3     0.151     0.115    1.315x  5->3
   32        3     0.150     0.114    1.306x  5->3
   48        3     0.149     0.115    1.287x  5->3
```

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] AMD-Quark mixed-precision DeepSeek-V4.1 support
body:
## Purpose

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-MXFP4` does not load today. It is a **mixed-precision** AMD-Quark export — MXFP4 experts, but 226 per-layer attention specs in MXFP8:

| | scheme |
|---|---|
| `global_quant_config` | `fp4` / `per_group` / `group_size=32` / `e8m0` |
| `layer_quant_config` (226 entries) | `fp8_e4m3` / `per_block` / `block_size=[32,32]` / `float8_e8m0fnu` |

Four independent bugs block it. Each one assumes DeepSeek **V4**'s `128x128` block geometry, or the DeepSeek-native scale naming.

| # | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | All 226 per-layer specs silently discarded | Decline mixed-precision Quark exports, let `QuarkConfig` take them |
| 2 | `NotImplementedError: No quark compatible scheme was found.` | New `QuarkW8A8Mxfp8` scheme |
| 3 | Attention shards silently fall back to global MXFP4 | Expose the VL wrapper's mappings as class attributes |
| 4 | Engram scale tensor never routed | Add a `weight_scale$` mapper rule |

### 1. The V4.1 config claims the checkpoint, then throws the specs away

`DeepseekV4FP8Config.override_quantization_method` accepts any Quark export whose *global* scheme is MXFP4 — this one qualifies. But `from_config` then rewrites the config into a single global FP8 scheme with `weight_block_size = [128, 128]`, discarding all 226 per-layer specs. `get_quant_method` then gates its MXFP8 path on `weight_block_size == [32, 32]`,
which that rewrite has just made unreachable.

**Fix:** a Quark export carrying `layer_quant_config` is mixed precision by definition, so decline it and let `QuarkConfig` handle it.

### 2. QuarkConfig has no scheme for 32×32 per-block FP8

`_is_fp8_w8a8` only accepts per-block FP8 at `[128, 128]` (V4 geometry), and the OCP-MX matchers only accept 1-D `per_group` weights. A 32×32 per-block e8m0 weight matches neither, so dispatch raises.

**Fix:** extend `QuarkOCP_MX` to handle MXFP8 as a first-class OCP-MX dtype. `mxfp8_e4m3` is added to `_WEIGHT_QUANT_KEY_MAP` / `_ACTIVATION_QUANT_KEY_MAP`, a normalizer (`ocp_mx_weight_dtype_and_rows()`) accepts both config dialects, and `QuarkOCP_MX` gains an unpacked MXFP8 branch with 3-way `packed_factor` (`1` for mxfp8, `2` for mxfp4, `8/6` for mxfp6).

The only difference from canonical 1-D MXFP8 is scale layout. MXFP8 carries one e8m0 value per weight *row* per 32-element group; Quark's `block_size=[R, 32]` carries one per *R* rows. The loader expands each scale row:

```python
loaded_weight.view(torch.uint8).repeat_interleave(rows, dim=0)
```

At `R == 1` the two layouts coincide and expansion is a no-op. The kernel is the shared `init_mxfp8_linear_kernel()` — the same one compressed-tensors and INC MXFP8 schemes use. Existing 128×128 per-block FP8 keeps
`QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock`, asserted in the new tests.

This also fixes a latent dispatch inconsistency: `get_quant_method()` and `get_quant_method_target()` now agree on MXFP8 layers, since both walk the same `QuarkOCP_MX` matcher chain.

Both MXFP8 config dialects are accepted:

| | Shape A (canonical MX) | Shape B (DeepSeek-V4.1) |
|---|---|---|
| `dtype` | `fp8_e4m3` | `fp8_e4m3` |
| shape | `qscheme=per_group`, `group_size=32` | `qscheme=per_block`, `block_size=[32,32]` |
| scale | `scale_format="e8m0"` | `scale_type="float8_e8m0fnu"` |
| `scale_block_rows` (R) | 1 | 32 |

### 3. The VL wrapper hides its module mappings from the quant config

`configure_quant_config` reads `hf_to_vllm_mapper` and `packed_modules_mapping` off the **class**, before `__init__` runs.
`DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` (vision variant) defined neither at class level, only as instance attributes. So per-layer keys naming `layers.N.attn.wq_a` never matched the runtime `language_model.model.layers.N.attn.wq_a`, and every
attention shard silently fell back to the global MXFP4 spec.

**Fix:** expose both as class attributes, with the prefix rules shared via one module-level constant so they cannot drift.

### 4. The engram scale name

Quark spells it `engram.embed.weight_scale`. The mapper's rules match `\.scale$` — a literal `.scale` suffix — so the rule never fires.

**Fix:** add an explicit `weight_scale$` rule alongside the existing one.

## Scope

ROCm/AMD path only (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/`). The `nvidia/` twins have the same shape for items 3 and 4, but this PR deliberately leaves them alone — only the AMD path has been validated on hardware.

## Test Plan

**Quark dispatch tests (`test_quark.py`):**

- `test_quant_method_dispatch_mxfp8_2d_block` — a 32×32 per-block e8m0 linear dispatches to `QuarkOCP_MX` with `scale_block_rows == 32`; experts still fall through to the global MXFP4 spec; 128×128 per-block FP8 still gets
  `QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock`.
- `test_quant_method_dispatch_mxfp8_canonical` — canonical 1-D per-group MXFP8 (Shape A) dispatches to `QuarkOCP_MX` with `scale_block_rows == 1`; `get_quant_method` / `get_quant_method_target` agree.
- `test_quant_method_dispatch_mxfp8_moe_raises` — MXFP8 experts raise `NotImplementedError`.
- `test_quark_override_delegates_to_quark_config` — all `quant_method=="quark"` configs (MXFP4, MXFP8, mixed, etc.) return `None` from  `DeepseekV4FP8Config.override_quantization_method`, confirming delegation to `QuarkConfig`. Parametrized over V4 and V4.1 model types (10 cases).

**FP8 / DeepSeek-V4.1 tests (`test_fp8.py`):**

- `test_deepseek_v41_declines_mixed_precision_quark_config`
- `test_deepseek_v41_vl_exposes_quant_mappings_on_class`
- `test_deepseek_v41_engram_scale_accepts_quark_name`

## Test Result

**0 new code failures.** 

### End-to-end

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-MXFP4` (48 shards, 475 GB) on 4x MI355X at TP=4: all shards load in 74.5 s, MXFP8 attention resolves to `QuarkOCP_MX` via the `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`, and the model is coherent.

| --- | ---: | ---: |
| MXFP4 | 92.34% ± 0.73 | 92.42% ± 0.73 |
| Base FP8 | 92.87% ± 0.71 | 92.95% ± 0.71 |

title: [Qwen3.8-Flash-Next] Fuse main QK-norm/RoPE/gate and KV-cache write into the QSA pre-indexer launch
body:
## Purpose

Each QSA layer of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next prepares its inputs with three launches before the sparse attention kernel:

1. `fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate`: main-attention Q/K RMSNorm, RoPE and the gate split.
2. `qsa_pre_indexer`: indexer Q/K norm and RoPE, compressed-K cache and raw-key ring.
3. `reshape_and_cache_flash`: main K/V cache write.

This PR appends the main-attention work to the `qsa_pre_indexer` launch and renames it to `qsa_prepare`. After the indexer programs, one program per (token, Q or KV head) normalizes and rotates Q/K, copies the gate and writes K/V straight into the paged cache: BF16, or FP8 scaled by the layer's `k_scale`/`v_scale` the way `reshape_and_cache_flash` does. Two launches and the round trip of K through an intermediate tensor go away. The fused path runs for every batch (decode, prefill, mixed) whenever both fused kernels are available; otherwise the existing path runs.

`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_qk_norm_rope.py` is unchanged; the logic lives in `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ops/qsa_prepare.py` (renamed from `qsa_pre_indexer.py`).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_pre_indexer.py
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py
```

`test_qsa_fused_pre_indexer_matches_unfused` now also checks the main Q, gate and K/V cache against `fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate` + `reshape_and_cache_flash` over the existing decode, mixed and 4097-token prefill layouts, with BF16 and FP8 caches.

End to end, the fused path is the default, so the existing accuracy eval `tests/evals/qwen4_exp/test_accuracy.py` (the optional H200 and B200 steps in `.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml`) runs through it without changes.

Microbenchmark per `.agents/skills/kernel-microbenchmark`: FlashInfer CUPTI timing with CUDA graph and cold L2, outputs checked against the three kernels before timing, arms alternated. Serving: GSM8K and `vllm bench serve` with the recipe's FP8 configuration, main vs. this PR.

## Test Result

8x H20, main `741edeebee`, torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1. The branch is now rebased on `72e7874fa6`; none of the 82 commits in between touch the changed files or the QSA code (the only change under `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/` is the PLE prefetch buffer, #58797). The microbenchmark and serving tables were measured on the previous revision of this PR; the last paragraph of this section covers the re-run after the latest review changes.

**Tests:** 16 passed (`test_qsa_pre_indexer.py`); 82 passed (`test_qsa_reference.py`, `test_config.py`).

**Kernel microbenchmark, one H20 GPU.** What is timed is the prepare stage of one QSA layer, from the projection outputs until Q, the gate and all caches are written. On main that is three kernels (`fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate`, `qsa_pre_indexer`, `reshape_and_cache_flash`); with this PR it is one `qsa_prepare` launch.

- M is the number of tokens in the batch. Decode batches are requests × 4 tokens (1 + 3 MTP draft tokens), each request with an 8K-token context; prefill batches are one request with M prompt tokens.
- Heads per GPU are those of TP8: the model has 24 query heads and 2 KV heads, so each GPU has 3 query heads and 1 KV head.
- The main KV cache and the indexer cache are FP8, as in the recipe; BF16 caches are in the details below.
- Time saved = 1 − fused time / three-kernel time. The three kernels are timed at their fastest `num_warps`: `fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate` ships with 4 warps for head_dim 256, and 1 warp was faster at every M. Against the shipped setting the fused kernel saves 56-70%. The fused kernel keeps the pre-indexer's single warp, which beat 2 and 4 warps at M=16 and M=16384.

| M (tokens) | Batch | Three kernels (µs) | Fused (µs) | Time saved |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | decode, 1 request × 1 token | 10.4 | 4.2 | 60.0% |
| 4 | decode, 1 request × 4 tokens | 10.7 | 4.2 | 61.0% |
| 16 | decode, 4 requests × 4 tokens | 10.8 | 4.1 | 62.0% |
| 64 | decode, 16 requests × 4 tokens | 11.1 | 4.3 | 61.4% |
| 256 | decode, 64 requests × 4 tokens | 12.1 | 4.8 | 60.4% |
| 1024 | decode, 256 requests × 4 tokens | 21.8 | 7.7 | 64.5% |
| 1024 | prefill, 1 request | 23.7 | 8.1 | 65.7% |
| 4096 | prefill, 1 request | 57.0 | 22.6 | 60.3% |
| 16384 | prefill, 1 request | 183.2 | 84.7 | 53.7% |

With BF16 caches the fused kernel saves 57-59% for decode batches and 37% for the 16384-token prefill.

<details>
<summary>Full numbers, FP8 and BF16 caches</summary>

"As shipped" is the three kernels with `fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate` at its default 4 warps. GB/s is the minimum number of bytes the operation must move (every input read once, every output written once) divided by the time; the three kernels' GB/s uses their fastest-warps time. H20's HBM peak is about 4 TB/s.

#### FP8 caches

| M (tokens) | Batch | Three kernels, as shipped (µs) | Three kernels, fastest warps (µs) | Fused (µs) | Time saved vs fastest | Fused GB/s | Three kernels GB/s |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | decode 1×1 | 10.7 | 10.4 | 4.2 | 60.0% | 2 | 1 |
| 4 | decode 1×4 | 11.0 | 10.7 | 4.2 | 61.0% | 9 | 4 |
| 16 | decode 4×4 | 10.9 | 10.8 | 4.1 | 62.0% | 38 | 15 |
| 64 | decode 16×4 | 11.6 | 11.1 | 4.3 | 61.4% | 146 | 56 |
| 256 | decode 64×4 | 12.5 | 12.1 | 4.8 | 60.4% | 523 | 207 |
| 1024 | decode 256×4 | 24.7 | 21.8 | 7.7 | 64.5% | 1297 | 460 |
| 1024 | prefill | 26.6 | 23.7 | 8.1 | 65.7% | 1199 | 412 |
| 4096 | prefill | 71.2 | 57.0 | 22.6 | 60.3% | 1726 | 685 |
| 16384 | prefill | 247.8 | 183.2 | 84.7 | 53.7% | 1842 | 852 |

#### BF16 caches

| M (tokens) | Batch | Three kernels, as shipped (µs) | Three kernels, fastest warps (µs) | Fused (µs) | Time saved vs fastest | Fused GB/s | Three kernels GB/s |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | decode 1×1 | 9.9 | 9.5 | 4.0 | 58.2% | 3 | 1 |
| 4 | decode 1×4 | 10.3 | 10.1 | 4.2 | 58.3% | 10 | 4 |
| 16 | decode 4×4 | 10.2 | 9.9 | 4.2 | 57.4% | 41 | 18 |
| 64 | decode 16×4 | 10.8 | 10.5 | 4.4 | 58.4% | 159 | 66 |
| 256 | decode 64×4 | 11.7 | 11.3 | 4.9 | 57.1% | 572 | 246 |
| 1024 | decode 256×4 | 21.0 | 17.9 | 7.4 | 58.9% | 1512 | 621 |
| 1024 | prefill | 22.8 | 19.5 | 8.0 | 58.9% | 1353 | 556 |
| 4096 | prefill | 54.6 | 40.4 | 21.2 | 47.5% | 2040 | 1072 |
| 16384 | prefill | 188.8 | 130.6 | 82.8 | 36.6% | 2095 | 1328 |

</details>

**Serving** (8x H20, TP8 + EP8, MTP3, Triton MoE):

| Cache dtype | GSM8K, main | GSM8K, this PR | Identical predictions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FP8 (recipe) | 96.97% (1279) | 96.97% (1279) | 1301/1319 |
| BF16 | 96.97% (1279) | 96.66% (1275) | 1304/1319 |

GSM8K is 5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy, 64 concurrent, one run per arm; the cache dtype applies to both the main KV cache and the indexer cache. For scale, stock FP8 and stock BF16 differ from each other on 17 questions.

Throughput, `vllm bench serve` random 8192/1024 with FP8 caches, one run each: C1 260.7 → 266.8 output tok/s (+2.3%), C64 1636.3 → 1759.4 (+7.5%). These are single-run sanity checks and do not establish an end-to-end throughput or accuracy difference in either direction. For reference, the kernel savings add up to about 1% of the run time at C1 and 0.3% at C64.

The latest review changes move arguments and buffer allocation around and keep the kernel math. On the final code, the QSA tests pass (16 + 82) and the fused kernel time is unchanged (4.18 µs at M=16, 83.2 µs at M=16384). A single GSM8K run with FP8 caches gave 96.59% (1274) vs. 96.97% (1279) on main, with 1303/1319 predictions identical; earlier single runs of the same kernel math on previous revisions gave 1279 and 1281.

Only H20 was measured. The change removes two launches and one write and read of K per token, and adds no other work.

AI assistance: developed with Claude Code; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and benchmarks above.

title: [BugFix][KV Connector] Fix Deadlock with KVConnector + MTP under KV Pressure
body:
## Purpose

Scheduler can deadlock under KV memory pressure with MTP + KV connector --- encountered in production deployment of GLM5.2

### Example

- 2 requests A (needs 4 blocks + 1 for mtp), B (needs 3 blocks + 1 for mtp)
- Total blocks 7

#### Step 1 — A and B arrive and get added to `skipped_waiting` queue

A is admitted (4 blocks), popped from `waiting` -> `skipped_waiting`, `status → WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`
B is admitted (3 blocks), popped from `waiting` -> `skipped_waiting`, `status → WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`

- result: 
```
skipped_waiting = [A, B]
waiting = []

A.status = WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV
B.status = WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV
```

#### Step 2 — A's transfer lands. 

Schedule the `skipped_waiting` queue first. Peek `skipped_waiting` → A.

`_is_blocked_waiting_status(WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS)` is True → `_try_promote_blocked_waiting_request(A)` succeeds → `A.status=WAITING` 

Then, schedule A. Need to allocate for the MTP blocks [these are only allocated after async load]. We need 1 block, but there is 0 left. `allocate_slots` returns None and we `break` (end attempting to schedule.

- result:
```
skipped_waiting = [A, B]
waiting = []

A.status = WAITING
B.status = WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV
```

As we can see, the queues are in the same state as before this step, and will continue to be in this state (trying to schedule A, asking to allocate blocks) forever.

#### Step 3 onward — Same cycle

Peek `skipped_waiting` → still A, now status WAITING. _is_blocked_waiting_status(WAITING) is False, so no promotion branch; straight to allocation; fails; break. Spin forever.

## Root Cause

Async KV load is allocated without lookahead slots (see `limit_lookahead_tokens`), and `_request_remaining_blocks()` -- which backs the `_inflight_prefill_reserved_blocks()` admission gate -- does not count them either. 

Then, after the `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV` is done, we ask `allocate_slots()` for the lookahead margin on top ---> if this block is not available, we `break` --- with this request at the front of the `skipped_waiting` queue. If no requests are running, then no new blocks come free and we deadlock in this loop

**So there is a mismatch in the blocks reserved and what is actually needed to start running**

## Test Plan

- unit test
- reproducer (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57104#issuecomment-5701283900)

## Test Result

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Avoid triton recompiles in the acceptance estimator
body:
## Context
Triton keys its compilation cache on whether each int scalar is 1 and whether it is 16-divisible, so the number of tokens/reqs args re-key as the batch size changes at runtime, causing stalls.

## Summary
Fixed by disabling specialization on `num_reqs`/`num_tokens` for the acceptance estimator kernels.

## Test plan
**Correctness**
`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_estimator.py -v` → 7 passed (NVIDIA GB200)

**Compiled-variant count**
Swept num_reqs/num_tokens over 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, 15, 16, 17, 23, 31, 32, 33, 47, 48, 63, 64, 96, 127, 128, 129, 192, 255, 256
| kernel | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `_accumulate_kernel` | 14 | 1 |
| `_local_max_sumexp_kernel` | 3 | 1 |
| `_predict_kernel` | 3 | 1 |

All collapse to a single variant.

**Lint**
`pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/acceptance_estimator.py` → all applicable hooks passed, including mypy.

AI assistance was used for this change (Claude Code), and I have reviewed every changed line.

title: [KVConnector][P2P] Register peers off the scheduler thread
body:
Addresses #55179.

## Problem

`P2PSession._on_connect` called `NixlTransport.add_remote_peer` inline before replying with `ConnectAckMsg`. Registration is `add_remote_agent` plus a `prep_xfer_dlist` over every block of the peer's region — 19,599 blocks per rank for the 64 GiB CPU tier in the reported deployment — so a cold handshake ran that work inside a scheduling iteration on **both** peers, and the lookup queued behind the acknowledgement waited for it.

## Scope: registration only, not the per-step gating

The issue proposes two independent changes. This PR implements only the first, because the reported numbers point at registration as the dominant term.

Within one scheduler step, `TieringManager.on_schedule_end` runs `get_finished_jobs()` → `_poll_once()` (drain + dispatch) **before** `serve_external_requests(parent)`, so receive-and-answer collapse into a single tick. The busy source's critical path is therefore about four ticks: `ConnectMsg` → ack, `LookupMsg` → `LookupRespMsg`, `FetchMsg` → `write_blocks`, and NIXL completion → `TransferDoneMsg`. The destination was idle in the measurement, so its ticks are effectively free.

That gives `13.6 s ≈ 2·T_reg + 4·T_step`. At the issue's own stated ~1 s/step, per-step gating accounts for ~4 s, leaving ~9.6 s for two registrations. For gating alone to explain 13.6 s you would need ~3.4 s/step, which contradicts the same description. Per-step gating is real as a mechanism but is the minority term here, so it is deliberately left out of this PR and should be justified by its own measurement.

## Change

- `DataTransport.add_remote_peer_async` — new method whose default implementation runs `add_remote_peer` inline and returns an already-resolved future. Transports with cheap registration are unaffected and need no override.
- `NixlTransport` overrides it with a single-worker `ThreadPoolExecutor`, mirroring the NIXL connector's `_handshake_initiation_executor`. `add_remote_peer` is split into `_build_peer_handles` (the expensive agent wireup plus per-block descriptors, run **unlocked** — holding a lock across it would stall the scheduler thread for exactly as long as the work being moved off it) and `_publish_peer` (the atomic install).
- `P2PSession` starts the registration in `_on_connect` and sends `ConnectAckMsg` from `poll()` once the future resolves; a failed registration marks the connection dead so the manager reaps the session.

### The acknowledgement is the safety barrier

`ConnectAckMsg` is what clears the peer's `_send_ready` gate, so the peer cannot send a `FetchMsg` until it arrives. Gating the ack on registration completion preserves the invariant that **any peer permitted to fetch is a peer already registered here**, so `write_blocks` can never observe an unregistered peer as a result of this change. The wire protocol is unchanged.

### Generation guard

Registrations carry a per-peer generation, bumped on every add and every remove. A worker that finishes building handles under a stale generation releases them instead of publishing. This closes the reap race: `_reap_dead_sessions` calls `session.close()` and then `_data.remove_remote_peer(pid)`, and without the guard a registration landing after that would leave a registered peer with no session plus leaked NIXL handles. A pending registration also counts as session pending work, so the engine keeps ticking until the acknowledgement goes out.

### No `NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_STRICT`

The issue suggests opening the agent with `NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_STRICT` or `_RW`. That is not reachable through `nixl_agent_config`: the Python wrapper hard-codes `agent_config.syncMode`, selecting `STRICT` only when `enable_listen` is true, which would additionally start a listener thread and bind a port that this tier does not use.

It is also unnecessary. `NixlConnector` already runs `add_remote_agent`, `get_xfer_descs` and `prep_xfer_dlist` on its single-worker handshake executor concurrently with transfer submission on the main thread, with the default `syncMode=NONE`. This PR adopts the threading model vLLM already ships rather than introducing a new one, which also removes the need to measure STRICT's cost on the transfer path.

## Why this does not duplicate an existing PR

Draft #55962 covers this ground as part of a larger change that also services the control plane during model steps, and does so by adding a `poll_pending_work` hook to `KVConnectorBase_V1` plus changes to `EngineCore` and both executors.

This PR is materially different in approach and scope:

- **No new connector API.** Nothing is added to `KVConnectorBase_V1`. The audit behind this is that only `ServerRole.serve_external_requests` and its four helpers need the `ParentManager` handle — the whole client role, the entire message-dispatch table, and all NIXL submit/poll/cancel work are already parent-free, and `on_lookup` already defers resolution to the existing `serve_external_requests` window. No fresh scheduler-thread window is required.
- **Registration only.** It does not attempt the per-step gating change, for the reasons in the scope section above.
- **Different files.** It touches none of `vllm/v1/engine/core.py`, `vllm/v1/executor/{abstract,uniproc_executor,multiproc_executor}.py`, `kv_connector/v1/base.py`, `multi_connector.py`, or `offloading_connector.py`.
- **No STRICT sync mode**, per the section above.

Landing this first also makes #55962's remaining half measurable on its own terms: with registration off the critical path, whatever delay is left on a busy source is the per-step gating component.

## Tests

Run from `venv/` (this checkout's working environment):

```
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ -q
  → 377 passed, 11 skipped
  (baseline on the untouched tree: 371 passed, 11 skipped; +6 new tests)

python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/ -q
  → 220 passed

pre-commit run --files <6 changed files>          → all hooks pass (incl. DCO sign-off)
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files <3 source files> --hook-stage manual → passed
```

New tests, one behavior each:

- `ConnectAckMsg` is withheld while registration is in flight, and sent once it resolves.
- A pending registration counts as pending work — without this nothing drives the acknowledgement out.
- A failed registration rejects the peer instead of acknowledging it.
- A duplicate `ConnectMsg` mid-registration is a protocol error.
- Registration provably runs off the caller thread.
- A registration landing after `remove_remote_peer` is discarded and its handles released.

The session test fake gained a `defer_registration` mode so the acknowledgement gating is exercised deterministically rather than relying on thread timing.

## Model evaluation

No eval was run, because this change cannot affect model output: it reorders when a control-plane acknowledgement is sent and moves NIXL registration to another thread. Which blocks are transferred, and their contents, are untouched, and the wire protocol is unchanged.

**Performance validation is still outstanding.** The change targets a timing property that unit tests cannot measure, and no multi-pod deploy has been run yet. The measurement that validates it is TTFT on a busy source with a cold peer versus a warm peer: if cold-peer TTFT drops toward warm-peer, registration was the dominant cost. This PR stays in draft until that result is in.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the analysis, implementation and tests in this PR. The submitting human is reviewing every changed line and is running the hardware validation described above before marking it ready for review.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Restore causal image SWA for DeepSeek V4.1
body:
## Summary

Restore causal sliding-window attention for image tokens in DeepSeek V4.1 VL.

V4.1 inherited the image visibility rules used by DeepSeek V4 Vision-Exp: tokens inside an image could attend to earlier image tokens outside the sliding window and to future image tokens. This differs from the [official V4.1 reference implementation](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/blob/dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277/inference/model.py#L410), where `_window_kv` uses `get_window_topk_idxs` and both image and text tokens attend to the same causal window. With a window of 128, query position `p` should see only `[max(0, p - 127), p]` through SWA.

The incorrect widening affects full-image prefill as well as continuation chunks. For example, at the beginning of image span `[1900, 3948)`, the inherited rule exposes future image tokens through position 3947; the V4.1 reference permits only positions 1773 through 1900.

The key line in the [official `get_window_topk_idxs`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/blob/dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277/inference/model.py#L421) is:

```python
idxs = torch.where(idxs > end, -1, idxs)
```

The reference masks every index greater than the query position with `-1`; this is a causal 128-token window, including the current token. Executing the published `get_window_topk_idxs` at query position 1900 produces exactly 128 indices, from 1773 through 1900, with no future positions.

## Changes

- Disable multimodal prefix-LM/bidirectional-range configuration for V4.1.
- Make the shared SWA metadata builder respect an explicit `is_mm_prefix_lm=False`, keeping V4.1 metadata and paged indices causal.
- Set the V4.1 attention-side image window extension to zero. Image preprocessing, the vision encoder, and `vision_max_n_token` remain unchanged.
- Keep the existing causal gather lengths and workspace sizes. The final diff does not change NVIDIA or AMD workspace allocation.
- Add six regression cases: full prefill and continuation prefill, each with compression ratios `0/1/2`. Verify causal key positions in both gathered and paged indices, gather/CPU-plan consistency, and absence of image visibility extensions.

V4 Vision-Exp retains its existing image visibility behavior.

## Validation

Run on GB200:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py \
  -k 'not test_builder_' -q --tb=short
```

**Result: 30 passed, 3 deselected.** The three existing builder tests require an inaccessible gated Hugging Face configuration. The new regression uses a local configuration and requires no model download.

Changed-file pre-commit checks passed. A local FlashMLA numerical sanity check also matched the causal reference, retaining a gather length of 227 and a first-query SWA length of 128 for `seq_len=4000`, `query_len=100`, and image span `[1900, 3948)`.

Full-model VL accuracy, generation-length evaluation, and AMD runtime validation were not run. The evidence here establishes attention-window correctness at the metadata/kernel level.

## Related work

Open-PR searches for SWA/gather, V4.1/prefill, and V4.1/causal/image found no other matching fix. [#56986](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56986) concerns cross-layer compressed-KV gather reuse; it does not correct the image attention-window semantics addressed here.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for analysis, implementation, and validation.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][KV Offload] Use private pinned tensors for CPU KV offload
body:
## Purpose

Native CPU KV offload stalled during startup on an 8x MI308X node with TP8 and a 500 GiB offload pool. Six ranks reported `cudaHostRegister failed (code=1)`, and the engine never became ready.

`_uses_shared_region()` includes ROCm through `is_cuda_alike()`, so each worker registers the entire shared mmap region. Exclude ROCm to use the existing private per-rank pinned tensor allocator instead. The CUDA path is unchanged; ROCm no longer uses shared-region replicated KV deduplication.

Unlike #51081 (chunked registration) and #52296 (coordinated registration), this change bypasses shared mmap allocation on ROCm.

## Test Plan

Tested with vLLM 0.29.0 and ROCm 7.2.3 on two 8x MI308X hosts, running GLM-5.3 with TP8, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, and:

    --kv-offloading-size 500 --kv-offloading-backend native

Check startup and generation, then evict a cached 32K prompt from GPU KV cache using distinct filler prompts and replay it.

## Test Result

- Both hosts completed startup and served generation requests.
- Transfer counters confirmed CPU-to-GPU KV reload after eviction.
- The tested 32K gold-answer prompt returned the expected answer on both the cold request and the post-eviction replay.
