title: [KV Cache] GLM-5.3-Flash: use the generic packed KV layout; CircularBufferSpec tail with speculative ring slots
body:
## Purpose

Move kernel block splitting from the block table into each attention group. Previously `BlockTable` split every manager block for the whole KV cache group (`kernel_block_sizes`). All backends in a group had to share one kernel block size, block tables and slot mappings were at kernel granularity, and packed (block-outermost) caches could not be split at all, since other layers' pages sit between a layer's blocks. Now block tables stay at manager granularity, and each `AttentionGroup` maps manager blocks to the kernel blocks its own backend needs.

On top of this, GLM-5.3-Flash moves to the generic packed KV layout, and its model-specific KV code is removed.

## Design

### Kernel block mapping

**Choosing the kernel block size**
- `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` picks a size per KV cache group with `select_common_block_size(manager, backends, specs)`. Packed groups keep the manager block size and are never split group-wide.
- Each `AttentionGroup` then picks its own size for its backend and spec. It sets `kernel_block_size` only when that is smaller than the manager block.

**Mapping block tables**
- The group maps manager block `b` to kernel blocks `b * stride + j` (`j < block_size / kernel_block_size`).
  - `stride` is the number of kernel blocks per manager block.
  - For packed caches it is the packed block stride in kernel blocks.
- The mapped table is persistent and preallocated per ubatch, so CUDA graphs capture a stable buffer.
- Mapping happens inside `build_metadata`, `build_metadata_for_cudagraph_capture` and `build_metadata_for_drafting`. All runners and drafters (V1/MRv2, EAGLE, Gemma4, Step3.5, DFlash) go through these. Fused multi-step draft decode re-maps before replaying a FULL graph.
- `BlockTable`/`InputBatch` (V1 and MRv2) drop `kernel_block_sizes`. Slot mappings, CP and DFlash stay at manager granularity.

**Mapping KV views**
- When KV caches are bound, each group views its cache in kernel blocks. Packed caches use `as_strided` with the packed block stride.
- Only compressed caches (`tokens_per_state > 1`) may be split this way, because their write slots come from the mapped block table. Token and pooled caches are written through manager-block slot mappings, so they are rejected.
- The KV block zeroer maps the views back to manager blocks.

**Alignment**
- `block_stride_alignment` accepts `MultipleOf(n)`, meaning whole kernel blocks of up to `n` tokens, so a packed block always splits into whole kernel blocks.
- Fixed-size backends get it automatically; sparse MLA backends set their own in `customize_spec`.
- Bytes per block: block-outermost layouts round to the lcm of all alignments; layer-outermost layouts pad each layer's page separately.

**Consumers:** NIXL, Mooncake and HiSparse pick kernel block sizes the same way as the worker.

### GLM-5.3-Flash

- Uses the packed `BLHNC` layout. Removed its custom groups, byte layout, `KpoolTailSpec` and `storage_block_size`.
- The kpool indexer is a compressed spec whose backend declares DeepGEMM page sizes (32/64; 64 on SM120). The tail is a `CircularBufferSpec` ring of `kpool + num_speculative_tokens`.
- FlashMLA fp8 on SM90 reads 64-token pages over flat rows, so packed blocks need not be split.

**Example** (GLM-5.3-Flash on H200, manager block = 640 tokens, `index_kpool = 4`):

| Attention group | States per manager block | Kernel block | Kernel blocks per manager block |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sparse MLA (`FLASHMLA_SPARSE`) | 640 | 640 (no split) | 1 |
| kpool indexer (`tokens_per_state = 4`) | 160 | 32 (DeepGEMM page) | 5 |

For a request with manager block table `[7, 2]`:
- **Sparse MLA** builds its metadata from `[7, 2]` unchanged.
- **The indexer group** maps it to `[7·S, …, 7·S+4, 2·S, …, 2·S+4]`, where `S` is the stride between manager blocks in kernel blocks:
  - In a plain (layer-outermost) cache, `S = 5`, giving `[35..39, 10..14]`.
  - In the packed `BLHNC` cache, each manager block also holds the other layers' pages, so `S` is the packed block size divided by the indexer's 32-state page. `MultipleOf` alignment keeps that an integer.

The scheduler, slot mappings and other groups never see kernel blocks. On main, the whole group had to share one kernel block size, so the indexer needed the GLM-only `storage_block_size` workaround instead.

## Test Result

Each cell is GSM8K / GPQA Diamond / acceptance length; no request errors.

| Platform | Model / backend | main | PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 | GLM `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, MTP5 | 0.9280 / 0.7323 / 4.73 | 0.9333 / 0.7374 / 4.73 |
| GB200 | DSv4.1 default, DSpark5 | 0.9257 / 0.8384 / 4.08 | 0.9261 / 0.8460 / 4.01 |
| H200 | GLM `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` | — | 0.9386 / 0.7323 / 4.78 |
| H200 | GLM `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` + `fp8_ds_mla` (GSM8K / accept) | 0.9325 / 3.937 | 0.9348 / 3.930 |
| H200 | DSv4.1 default | — | 0.9272 / 0.8535 / 4.05 |
| MI350X | GLM `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` | 0.9211 / 0.6768 / 3.33 | 0.9191 / 0.6835 / 4.82 |
| MI350X | DSv4.1 default | 0.9272 / 0.8333 / 4.03 | 0.9303 / 0.8535 / 3.94 |

- **Prefix caching:** mid-block hits give byte-identical outputs to main.
- **NIXL 1P1D:** GLM 0.9401, DSv4.1 0.9265, 0 failed transfers.
- **Mooncake P/D:** GLM 0.9136.

title: [Bugfix][PP][Spec Decode] MiniMax-M3 EAGLE3 aux-state relay at PP > 1 and per-stage FlashInfer autotune
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Enables EAGLE3 for MiniMax-M3 (NVIDIA model file) at PP > 1 on Model Runner V2, and scopes FlashInfer autotune to each PP stage's TP group, fixing a startup deadlock. Builds on #50514 (PP aux-state relay), changes the autotune sync from #50892, supersedes #57198.

Motivation: MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 PP2/TP4 + EAGLE3 serving on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (also needs #59081, which supersedes #47665). No performance claim; the speedup there comes from split-K admission (#45450 / #52879 / #56148).

## Claims

1. **MiniMax-M3 + EAGLE3 runs at PP > 1.** Base rejects it at load (`ValueError: ... does not support eagle3 with pipeline parallelism`). The drafter then gets all aux states every step; acceptance length and GSM8K match TP8.
2. **FlashInfer autotune no longer deadlocks at PP > 1** when stages tune different shapes. Each stage tunes within its TP group and writes `<cache>_tp_<ranks>.json`. PP = 1 is unchanged.

## Validation

**Setup:** 8x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4` + `Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3`, offline `LLM`, greedy, cold autotune. Both arms: vLLM 213c379 + FP8 Triton-indexer enablement (as in #47665; needed on SM120) + #56148's Triton-attention guard hunks (not its split-K path). Arms differ only in this PR's files as of 4683f1e3 (since then: `kernel_warmup.py` comments only; extractor hunk dropped).

| Config | Aux relay (steps) | Mean AL | GSM8K-200 spec / no-spec | Stage cache entries |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8 | – | 3.471 | 94.5 / 94.5 | unchanged |
| PP2/TP4 | 4600/4600 | 3.460, 3.449, 3.452 | 95.5 / 95.5 | 140 / 80 |
| PP3/TP2 | 7200/7200 | 3.469 | 94.0 / – | 140 / 80 / 80 |
| PP4/TP1 | 9200/9200 | 3.498 | 94.0 / – | 140 / 80 / 80 / 80 |

AL: 32 GSM8K prompts × 256 tokens. GSM8K-200: first 200 test questions, chat, thinking on, 0-shot, max 2048 tokens; all within ~1 SE. Autotune ≤10 s/stage.

Main engine args (PP2/TP4):
```text
-tp 4 -pp 2 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}'
--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --moe-backend marlin --max-model-len 65536 --language-model-only
--max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 12 --block-size 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95
--disable-custom-all-reduce --enable-prefix-caching --seed 0
--speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3","num_speculative_tokens":3,
  "draft_tensor_parallel_size":4,"attention_backend":"TRITON_ATTN","use_local_argmax_reduction":true}'
```

**Base** (same image, base files):
- With these args: the `ValueError` on all 8 ranks.
- Without `--speculative-config`: hangs in autotune; `--kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": false}'` avoids it. PR `model.py` with base `kernel_warmup.py` + EAGLE3 hangs too (both changes needed).
- Non-spec PP2/TP4 (autotune off, 16 prompts, two setups): identical greedy outputs 2–3/16 PR vs base, 2–5/16 PR vs PR (mean hidden cosine .95–.97): no detectable PR effect.

**Non-MiniMax, H200:** Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 bf16 PP2/TP2, PR vs base: both start; PR writes per-stage caches; GSM8K-200 96.0 vs 95.5 (default MoE, 0 tuned entries), 95.5 vs 94.0 (`flashinfer_cutlass`, 44 entries/stage): equivalent.

**Pre-existing, not fixed here:** a warm restart with a `flashinfer_cutlass` cache at PP2/TP2 hangs in base and PR (TP rank 0 hits the cache, rank 1 re-tunes); matches #57423 (fixes: #57579, #57635; untested).

@SloptimistPrime reported the autotune fix on 6x GB10 (SM121), TP2/PP3 (#57198); their test commit 1291f3fe is not included.

**CPU tests and lint:**
```bash
pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py
# 17 passed (11 added). Production files reverted: 8 of the 11 fail
# (incl. PP = 1 layer-0 tap); the 3 passing are PP = 1 / no-aux guards.
pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files $(git diff --name-only 5c3b61e9)
# all pass, incl. mypy 3.10-3.13 and test tethering
```

## Details

**Root cause, autotune.** Since #50892 all ranks sync over the world group (cache broadcast, barrier, per-tactic all-reduce). PP stages can tune different shapes (140 vs 80 `mxfp8_gemm` entries), so PP0 waits on a collective PP1 never joins. Fix: at PP > 1, leader, broadcast, barrier, timing average and cache file use the stage's TP group.

**Root cause, MiniMax-M3.** No #50514 opt-in; taps used stage-local layer indices. Fix: set `supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp` and use the `EagleModelMixin` helpers (global indices, pack local / collect upstream taps), like Llama, Qwen2, DeepSeek-V4, Kimi-K3. Tap 0 aliases `residual`, which fused add-RMSNorm updates in place, so it is cloned when layer 0 is a tap (any PP size; CPU-tested; GPU runs above use taps 2/30/57).

**Dropped:** #57290's `extract_hidden_states` draft PP = 1 hunk (extractor-only; EAGLE3 unaffected): at PP2 it turned a config-time `NotImplementedError` into a startup `AssertionError` (`ExampleHiddenStatesConnector` needs a change; separate PR). Supersedes earlier status comments.

**Size and tradeoffs.** 2 production files, +40/−13. Tests +342/−2 (CPU fakes). At PP > 1, old unsuffixed caches are not read (one re-tune) and stages may pick different tactics for the same shape (unmeasured). Each PP hop carries one extra `[tokens, hidden]` tensor per upstream tap (not benchmarked).

**Limits.** Aux relay is V2-only (V1: #45985); the autotune change also affects V1 (not run). Untested: MiniMax-M3 dflash/dspark and multimodal inputs at PP > 1 (both now accepted), ROCm (AMD model file unchanged), DP > 1 with PP > 1, MiniMax-M3 FlashInfer MoE (runs used Marlin). CI gap: `test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py` does not run on `vllm/models/`-only changes. #57579, #57635, #55671, #52292 also edit `flashinfer_autotune` (on conflict, keep the per-stage group); #53901 reworks the PP aux helpers. No duplicate found.

**AI assistance.** OpenAI Codex, Claude Code and Cursor agents wrote code and tests, ran and analyzed GPU validation, and drafted this text (`/pr-checklist` from unmerged #57084). The human submitter remains responsible for reviewing and defending every changed line.

title: [ROCm][Perf] W4A16: speed up skinny GEMM decode, including speculative batches
body:
## Summary

Tunes the W4A16 skinny GEMM decode path on gfx115x, and stops routing deep-K decode shapes away from it.

The kernel compiles for gfx11 and gfx12, and everything here was measured on gfx1151, so **every commit gates itself to gfx115x** -- the tuning and the routing alike. Off gfx115x the kernel runs exactly as it does today: the K * N bound stays at 1.2x LDS, the chunked path never launches, every tuple takes the checked K loop, the zero point keeps its own pass over the unpacked values, and the dispatch keeps its current tuples. The Python side gets an `on_gfx115x()` platform helper so the layer routes to match the C++ host check.

Eight commits, each measured against its parent on gfx1151 / ROCm 10.2, median of 3 passes:

| commit | what | effect |
|---|---|---|
| test coverage | asymmetric path and batch 4/5 at the op level | — |
| K loop | instantiate the whole-block loop without the bound check | mean **+18.9%**, 44 of 46 cells |
| zero point | fold it into the fp16 dequant constants | up to **+28.8%** at batch 1, asymmetric |
| group stride | scale and zero-point rows get their own row stride, HIP and Triton | — |
| LDS bound | stop rejecting K * N past the LDS budget | **+67% / +90%** on the shape that crosses it |
| chunked K | walk K in LDS-sized chunks so every activation row stays in LDS | **+30.5% / +51.7%** at batch 4, deep K |
| dispatch rules | avoid trimming wave slots, widen loads for deep-K batch 1 | **+9.4% to +16.3%** |
| LDS band | store the chunked activation band piece-major, conflict-free | **+1.9%** mean on chunked shapes |

## Results

The GEMM shapes a `cyankiwi/gemma-4-31B-it-AWQ-4bit` decode step issues, at group size 32 and asymmetric, driven through `rdna_hybrid_w4a16_apply` so the HIP/Triton routing is the production one. Percentages are bytes moved over elapsed time against 230 GB/s of practical board bandwidth. Median of 3 passes against `main`.

| Workload | Shape (M×K) | Kernel | main | this branch | Gain |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Decode, N=1 | 43008×5376 | sml | 634.8 µs — 92% | 499.2 µs — 116% ⁽¹⁾ | **−21.4%** |
| Decode, N=1 | 5376×21504 | sml | 360.7 µs — 81% | 325.5 µs — 89% | −9.8% |
| Decode, N=1 | 16384×5376 | sml | 266.7 µs — 83% | 242.1 µs — 92% | −9.2% |
| Decode, N=1 | 5376×8192 | sml | 144.0 µs — 77% | 129.9 µs — 85% | −9.8% |
| Decode, N=1 | 5376×16384 | sml | 296.0 µs — 75% | 263.8 µs — 84% | **−10.9%** |
| Decode, N=1 | 20480×5376 | sml | 334.8 µs — 83% | 303.5 µs — 91% | −9.3% |
| Spec decode, N=2 | 5376×21504 | Triton → chunked | 474.9 µs — 61% | 313.8 µs — 93% | **−33.9%** |
| Spec decode, N=2 | 5376×16384 | sml | 295.3 µs — 75% | 264.1 µs — 84% | **−10.6%** |
| Spec decode, N=3 | 5376×21504 | Triton → chunked | 498.7 µs — 58% | 315.3 µs — 92% | **−36.8%** |
| Spec decode, N=3 | 5376×16384 | Triton → chunked | 728.0 µs — 30% | 259.5 µs — 86% | **−64.4%** |
| Spec decode, N=4 | 5376×21504 | Triton → chunked | 499.2 µs — 58% | 316.0 µs — 92% | **−36.7%** |
| Spec decode, N=4 | 5376×16384 | Triton → chunked | 743.4 µs — 30% | 256.1 µs — 87% | **−65.6%** |

The speculative-decode rows carry the routing change: today any shape with K * batch past the LDS budget goes to the Triton prefill kernel, which at N=3 and K=16384 runs at 30% of bandwidth. Run-to-run spread is under 4% on every cell except that one, where it is 7.6%; the effect there is an order larger.

⁽¹⁾ Above 100% because the denominator charges scales and zero points to DRAM; for this shape that working set is 18 MB and fits the 32 MB MALL. The weight stream alone is 115.6 MB in 499.2 µs, 232 GB/s, which is the board's practical ceiling.

## Accuracy

GSM8K, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, seed 42, on `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ` with `max_num_seqs=4`:

| | main | this branch |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| strict-match | 0.8582259287338894 | 0.8582259287338894 |
| flexible-extract | 0.8612585291887794 | 0.8612585291887794 |

Identical to the last digit, so every one of the 1319 answers matches. `max_num_seqs=4` is load-bearing: Qwen3-8B has K = 4096 and K = 12288, so at batch 1 nothing crosses the LDS budget and none of the routing changes engage. At batch 4 the down projection gives K * N = 49152, which goes to Triton today and stays on the chunked path here -- the eval runs straight through the largest behavioural change in the series and produces the same output.

The deep-K tuple is not covered by this eval, and cannot be by any Qwen3-8B: it needs K divisible by 8192, and this model has neither. It is covered at the op level instead, by test cases at K = 8192 and K = 16384.

## End to end

`cyankiwi/gemma-4-31B-it-AWQ-4bit` served on gfx1151, 328 in / 256 out, 10 prompts each carrying one 640×480 image, batch 1:

| | main | this branch | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **TPOT** | 120.7 ms | **107.4 ms** | **−11.0%** |
| **Decode throughput** | 7.65 tok/s | **8.49 tok/s** | **+11.0%** |
| End-to-end latency | 33.47 s | 30.15 s | −9.9% |
| TTFT | 2691 ms | 2762 ms | +2.6% |

TTFT is prefill. Routing there is unchanged, and the Triton kernel's arithmetic is too, but its scale and zero-point addressing now goes through a row stride instead of assuming K / group_size; for a contiguous tensor that stride is the same value and the generated code is unchanged.

This understates the series: at batch 1 on an AWQ checkpoint the chunked path, the wave-packing rule and the deep-K tuple all stay inactive, so the number above comes from the first four commits alone. The last three target speculative decoding and deep-K projections, which this configuration does not exercise.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py` on gfx1151: 197 passed. Cases added for the deep-K instantiations, for each batch that reaches the chunked path, for a K that crosses a chunk boundary with a ragged tail, and for group size 32 where one unrolled step spans exactly one scale group.
- [x] `pre-commit run` clean on every touched file, clang-format included.
- [x] End to end served on gfx1151 with an image workload, `main` against this branch.
- [x] GSM8K 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, seed 42 on `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ`: identical to the last digit.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change, as required by `AGENTS.md`. Not a duplicate: the only other open PR touching `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu` is #57015, which adds an alignment hint to the activation load in the compute body and changes neither the K loop, the dequant path nor the dispatch.

title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Remove MegaMoE padding and shared padding workaround
body:
## Purpose

Remove unnecessary MegaMoE intermediate-width padding for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and revert the production workaround added in #56568. Routed and shared experts both retain the checkpoint width of 2304, so native shared-expert fusion remains enabled without padding either to 2560.

The bundled DeepGEMM uses `layout::Data(..., false)` for activation-scale rows in `include/deep_gemm/layout/mega_moe.cuh`; the old 16-byte TMA-row alignment rationale no longer applies. The existing runtime check still requires intermediate dimensions divisible by 128.

This removes 10% of the intermediate dimension used by the padded expert GEMMs and avoids the separate padded shared-weight copies introduced by #56568. Fusion keeps its existing eligibility checks and disable flag. A bare revert of #56568 would leave routed padding in place and disable V4.1 shared fusion again, so this change removes both together.

Retain the useful regression coverage from #56568, now checking exact checkpoint-shaped weight/scale preservation, native-width shared fusion, buffer reuse, and repeated finalization.

Related: #56217. Duplicate checks covered its issue/comments, open PRs mentioning #56217/#56568, and MegaMoE/shared-expert/padding searches. #56568 is already merged; this replaces its padding workaround. #54049 targets FlashInfer CuteDSL, #55275 adds GLM adapters, #40833 integrates a general fused-MoE backend, and #56697 targets SM90 Marlin. None removes this native DeepGEMM model-path padding.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py --hook-stage manual
```

Also compare this implementation directly with upstream `42919b49c5` on four GB200 GPUs using identical random expert weights, inputs, routes, and routing weights: hidden size 5120, intermediate width 2304 versus 2560, 384 experts, top-6, token counts 1/8/32/128/1024/2048, shared fusion both disabled and enabled. For the reference, upstream itself pads the native checkpoint-shaped shared weights.

## Test Result

Focused suite: **30 passed** on GB200.
Four-GPU operator comparison against upstream `42919b49c5`: **48/48 comparisons have exactly zero output error**, including all shared-fusion cases. Shared-expert outputs have nonzero contribution. Candidate commit: `21cda373e8`.
Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy 3.10, and explicit mypy 3.12 passed.

Previously completed real-weight model evaluation used this exact production model file with `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, TP4/EP4. Full GSM8K with lm-eval 0.4.12, five-shot multi-turn chat, thinking disabled, greedy generation, 1024 output tokens, seed 123:

| Configuration | Correct / 1319 | Accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Auto-MoE/FlashMLA FP8-indexer baseline, three runs | 1270–1274 | 96.2851–96.5883% |
| Native-width MegaMoE/FlashMLA FP8 indexer | 1271 | 96.3609% |
| Combined optimized configuration, MXFP4 sparse indexer | 1266 | 95.9818% |

These are prior model-path validation results, not a newly measured isolated comparison against current upstream with #56568. The combined configuration includes separate attention/indexer optimizations. No new end-to-end speedup over #56568 is claimed here.

## AI assistance

Codex assisted with implementation, validation, and this description. Woosuk Kwon authorized submission after the prepared diff and validation results were presented for review.

title: [A2A] Allow EPLB + SharedExpert Overlap + DeepEPv2
body:
## Purpose

Allow shared expert overlap when EPLB is enabled with the `deepep_v2` all2all backend, by adding `deepep_v2` to `_EPLB_OVERLAP_SAFE_BACKENDS`. This follows #50569, which made the same exemption for `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided` after validating it.

Not a duplicate: no other open PR touches `_EPLB_OVERLAP_SAFE_BACKENDS` for `deepep_v2`. Sequence-parallel support for `deepep_v2` is a separate PR (#57210); it was applied locally only for the SP runs below. When SP is active, `_disable_shared_experts_overlap` returns early, so this change only affects TP=1 deployments.

## Test Plan

- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite`
- Hardware: 8×H200, single node
- Backend: `--all2all-backend deepep_v2`
- Execution: `--enforce-eager` (see note on CUDA graphs below)
- Environment: `EP_DISABLE_GIN=1`, because the node has no InfiniBand NICs. vLLM's `_check_gin_support` does not honor `EP_DISABLE_GIN`, so the GIN query was skipped locally (after the communicator-init probe). That change is not part of this PR.
- EPLB: async (the default), rebalancing aggressively so experts move many times during each eval:

```bash
EP_DISABLE_GIN=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --enable-eplb --eplb-config '{"use_async": true, "window_size": 50, "step_interval": 100, "num_redundant_experts": 4}' \
  --all2all-backend deepep_v2 --enforce-eager \
  --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 2048

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --num-questions 1319
```

- SP runs: same command with `--tensor-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size 2` and #57210 applied. The logs confirm `sp_size=2`.
- Baseline (overlap off): same command with this PR's one-line change reverted.

## Test Result

GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot. Each accuracy is from a separate eval run against the same server.

| Config | EPLB | Shared expert overlap | GSM8K accuracy | Async rebalances |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP=1, DP=4, EP=4 (**this PR**) | async | on | 0.353 / 0.353 / 0.346 | 52 |
| TP=1, DP=4, EP=4 (baseline, PR reverted) | async | off | 0.349 / 0.346 / 0.354 | 52 |
| TP=1, DP=4, EP=4 | off | on | 0.352 | – |
| TP=2, DP=2, EP=4 (SP, #57210) | off | off (SP disables it) | 0.350 / 0.356 / 0.349 | 0 |
| TP=2, DP=2, EP=4 (SP, #57210) | async | off (SP disables it) | 0.357 / 0.351 / 0.359 | 51 |
| TP=1, DP=4, EP=4, `allgather_reducescatter` (reference) | off | – | 0.361 | – |

Enabling overlap with async EPLB on `deepep_v2` shows no accuracy change against the baseline, and there were no errors or hangs across 52 rebalances. SP combined with async EPLB on `deepep_v2` also works as expected.

**Known issue, unrelated to this PR:** with `EP_DISABLE_GIN=1` on this node, `deepep_v2` produces garbage output (GSM8K 0.000) whenever CUDA graphs are enabled. This happens with or without EPLB, and with the shared experts stream on or off. Eager mode is correct, so all results above use `--enforce-eager`. This will be tracked separately.

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to run the validation and draft this description. I have reviewed the change and the results.

title: [Metrics][KV Offload] Add Prometheus metrics for SimpleCPUOffloadConnector
body:
## Purpose

Exposes `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` telemetry through the existing `KVConnectorStats` pipeline, the same contract the offloading connector, NIXL, and mooncake follow. Scheduler-side only; the transfer path is untouched. The manager already tracks every quantity involved.

Five series under `vllm:simple_kv_offload_*`, drained once per engine step:

- `save_outcomes_total{outcome}`: store decisions as interval deltas, `stored` or one of `dropped_cpu_full`, `dropped_request_gone`, `dropped_null_block`, `dropped_not_hashed`, `skipped_already_cached`, `skipped_in_flight`
- `load_blocks_total`: KV blocks restored to GPU from the offload pool when loads finish; prefill work avoided through offload cache hits
- `used_blocks`: pool blocks pinned by in-flight transfers or cache hits. Warm but evictable cached blocks don't count; `info`'s `capacity_blocks` gives the pool size
- `pending_store_blocks`: blocks in queued, issued, or abandoned stores. If it grows without coming down, a transfer is stuck
- `info{backend,page_cache,lazy_offload,capacity_blocks}`: config fingerprint, value always 1

Because the stats flow through `KVConnectorStats`, the per-step CLI log picks them up too (via `reduce()`; the constant info gauge is skipped there).

One behavior change: `reset()` now seeds the fresh `BoundaryStoreStats` with outcomes counted since the last drain, so the new counter doesn't lose a window that straddles a cache reset (e.g. a LoRA unload mid-interval). `get_boundary_store_stats()` right after a reset reports that carried window instead of zero. The accessor is diagnostics-only; nothing in the control flow reads it.

## Related work

Not a duplicate of #41790: that PR instruments the worker-side DMA copy path (transfer bytes, DMA-only timing from pooled CUDA events, transfer-size histograms) on the generic offloading stats transport. This PR adds scheduler-side logical block counters through the connector's own `KVConnectorStats` pipeline; the transfer path is untouched. The two measure different layers — DMA transfer cost there, store admission and load effectiveness here — and the only overlap is a pool-utilization gauge exposed under a different name.

## What each metric is for

- `save_outcomes_total{outcome}`: classifies every eager-mode store decision, and is the first place to look when the cache hit rate drops. `dropped_cpu_full` means KV was lost because the pool was full. `dropped_request_gone` means the request finished or was preempted before the hand-off was processed. `dropped_not_hashed` points at hashing config. `skipped_already_cached` and `skipped_in_flight` mean the content is already stored or a store for it is in flight.
- `load_blocks_total`: KV blocks restored to GPU from the offload pool when loads finish, i.e. prefill work a request did not have to redo. Flat while traffic is flowing means data is stored but never matched, which points at hashing or prefixes.
- `used_blocks`: pool blocks currently pinned by in-flight transfers or cache hits. `dropped_cpu_full` starts exactly when this gauge reaches `capacity_blocks`, so alerting below the ceiling warns before data is lost. Evictable cached blocks are not counted because they are reclaimed on demand.
- `pending_store_blocks`: store backlog. Normal behavior is spikes that return to ~0 as stores finish. A value that keeps growing means a stuck transfer. Stuck stores also hold pool blocks, so this is the first warning before `used_blocks` fills and `dropped_cpu_full` starts.
- `info`: config context for the other metrics. `capacity_blocks` is the ceiling for `used_blocks`. `backend` tells you whether to read a growing backlog as disk latency or memory bandwidth. `lazy_offload=true` explains why `save_outcomes_total` reports nothing: it only classifies eager-mode stores.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_metrics.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/ \
  "tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_scheduler_kv_connector_stats" -q
```

## Test Result

111 passed, 2 skipped, including the 20 tests in `test_simple_cpu_offload_metrics.py`.

AI assistance: used for implementation and validation. Human review and ownership remain with the submitter.

title: [Spec Decode] Enable Gemma4 DSpark adaptive verification with FlashInfer
body: ## Purpose Enable Gemma4 DSpark adaptive verification with FlashInfer TRTLLM-GEN, building on #52157 (#51871): graph-safe variable-length decode, trained confidence-head loading, graph-cache separation, and RoPE config normalization. Adaptive verification replays FULL decode CUDA graphs in which each request has 1 to 1 + k query tokens, read from the device `query_start_loc` (k = `num_speculative_tokens`). On `main` it requires every target builder to report `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS`, which also promises graphs for mixed prefill/decode batches. FlashInfer's TRTLLM-GEN path can replay variable-length decode batches but not mixed ones, so, per review, this PR declares that capability separately instead of adding an enum member: - **`AttentionCGSupport` is unchanged.** - **New builder classmethod** `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len(vllm_config, kv_cache_spec) -> int | None`: the largest per-request query length L for which one FULL cudagraph replays any decode batch with 1 to L query tokens per request. It returns `None` for `ALWAYS` builders, which replay any batch, and for builders without variable-length support. | Builder | `get_cudagraph_support()` | `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len()` | Adaptive verification | |---|---|---|---| | `ALWAYS` builders (FA3, Triton, FlexAttention, Kimi-K3 KDA, FlashInfer MLA, ...) | `ALWAYS` | `None` | supported | | FlashInfer with its TRTLLM-GEN varlen path active (adaptive verification on, SM100 family, no DCP) | `UNIFORM_BATCH` | `1 + k` | supported (needs at least `1 + k`) | | FlashInfer otherwise, and other builders below `ALWAYS` | unchanged | `None` | not supported | - **Readers.** Adaptive verification is the only reader: every target builder must report `ALWAYS` or a bound of at least `1 + k`. CUDA graph mode resolution and capture are unchanged. - **Batches with a prefill no longer replay varlen decode graphs.** Dispatch matched those graphs on `max(num_scheduled_tokens)` alone, so decodes plus a prefill chunk of at most `1 + k` tokens replayed a decode graph. That is harmless for FlashInfer and FlashInfer MLA, which run short prefills on their decode kernels, but not for Kimi-K3's KDA builder (`ALWAYS` since #52988): it classifies rows by request state and does not restage its graph buffers when a prefill row is present. The runner now passes `max_query_len=None` for any batch with a prefill. - **Decode width on model runner V2.** Six copies of `1 + (2 if parallel_drafting else 1) * k` now share `max_decode_query_len()`. The 2× covers model runner V1's parallel drafter only, so on V2 the spec-as-decode width is `1 + k`, and DFlash/DSpark prefill chunks of `k + 2` to `2k + 1` tokens take the prefill kernel. Not a duplicate: #53929 proposes a `VARLEN_DECODE` member to enable adaptive DSpark verification for Qwen GDN; under this design GDN would override `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len()` instead. ## Test Plan On one GB300, BF16, model runner V2, rebased on `9ef37771be` (includes #52988): ```bash pre-commit run --files pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py \ tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py \ tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py \ tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py \ tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py \ tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py \ tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py \ tests/test_config.py tests/transformers_utils/test_config.py ``` The full list, 31 files, also covers the linear-attention, chunked-local, DCP, batch splitting and reordering, Gemma4 model and TRTLLM-GEN varlen kernel suites. title: [Bugfix] Honor skip_reading_prefix_cache for KV connector hits
body:
## Purpose

`skip_reading_prefix_cache` (#28194) means "compute every prompt token in this request". `SamplingParams` sets it for `prompt_logprobs` and `PoolingParams` for the token-level tasks (`token_embed`, `token_classify`, `plugin`), because a prefix served from cache has no logits or hidden states for those rows; callers may also set it explicitly. Today it only gates the local prefix cache (`KVCacheManager`). The scheduler adopts a KV connector's `get_num_new_matched_tokens` result unconditionally, so honoring the flag has been left to each connector: `OffloadingConnector` (#44592) and `SimpleCPUOffload` (#54998) got individual fixes, while NIXL, LMCache, Mooncake and MoRIIO do not check it (`grep skip_reading_prefix_cache` over `kv_connector/v1/` finds only the two offload connectors).

Consequences with the remaining connectors:

- A `prompt_logprobs` request whose prefix is served remotely (LMCache, Mooncake) skips those rows silently. `LogprobsProcessor._update_prompt_logprobs` appends per received chunk with no placeholder, so the returned list is shorter and its indices no longer line up with prompt positions.
- In P/D disaggregation the decode engine gets the whole prompt from the connector, ships an unfilled `LogprobsTensors` and crashes with `OverflowError` (#50792; #50795 patches that symptom in the runner by not shipping the tensor).

This PR fixes it where the decision is made: the scheduler discards the connector hit when the request sets the flag (4 lines), so the flag holds for every connector, present and future, exactly as it does for the local cache. The request still computes and stores its KV as usual; only its read is skipped, which is what the two in-tree offload connectors already do.

Relation to #50795: that PR keeps the remote hit and returns no prompt logprobs for the request; this one recomputes the prompt on the decode side and returns correct prompt logprobs, at the cost of that request's prefill. NIXL's decode side already handles `num_external_tokens == 0` as a full local hit and notifies the prefill side to free its blocks (`pull_scheduler.py`, "If remote_blocks and num_external_tokens = 0 ..."), so nothing leaks. Happy to reduce this to the runner-side guard if maintainers prefer that trade-off; the two are complementary rather than conflicting.

Found while auditing #54335 (fixed-token prefill scoring), which also sets the flag and needs every prompt row; that PR will depend on this one.

## Test Plan

- New `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_kv_connector_honors_skip_reading_prefix_cache`: with the mock connector reporting a 32-token hit, a plain request schedules 32 of its 64 tokens while a `prompt_logprobs` request schedules all 64.
- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k "skip_reading_prefix_cache or kv_connector_basic"`: 3 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: passes.

## Test Result

The new test fails on `main` (the `prompt_logprobs` request schedules 32 tokens) and passes with this change. No GPU path is touched.

## AI assistance

Implemented with Claude Code; every line reviewed by the submitter. Not a duplicate: #50795 addresses the same symptom in the runner rather than the flag; no open PR changes the scheduler's connector-hit handling (`gh pr list --search "skip_reading_prefix_cache"`).

title: [Fast Start] Cache the MTP draft model in a separate daemon group
body:
## Purpose

Under `--load-format ipc_cache`, the MTP draft model was not served by the weight cache daemon: the engine either reloaded it from disk or sent it to the target daemon with a mismatching fingerprint.

The launcher now starts a second daemon group for the MTP draft, with its own cache key, sockets (`*_draft0.sock`) and rendezvous port (`--weight-cache-draft-master-port`). On the engine side, get_draft_load_config routes an MTP draft to that group and lets other draft types (EAGLE3, DFlash, DSpark) fall back to disk. Only MTP drafts are cached; the draft must use the target's TP size.

title: [CI] Raise DSv4-Flash disaggregated engine readiness timeout to 1800s
body:
## Root cause

The `:nvidia: (H200) DSv4-Flash Disaggregated DP EP` step (`dsv4-flash-disaggregated`) fails on main: both API servers die with

```
TimeoutError: Timed out waiting for engine core processes to start. ... Waited 900s (configured by VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S).
```

Failing job: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89444#01a0ac07-f462-419d-a09e-726a5bb8ec48 (build 89444, commit e0705731be04aac90838f318fcdae15c56a53080)

Timings verified from the job log:

- API servers started at 02:11:08; both frontends raised the TimeoutError at 02:26:25 (~900s budget hit).
- Engine cores were healthy but slow: model loading took 656-739s per worker (37.8-43.05 GiB/worker), then the JIT kernel warmup (244 compile keys, dominated by `MhcPreBigFuseTileLangKernel` at ~52-78s/kernel) took another 320-329s, finishing at 02:30:01 — ~1133s total, ~3.6 min after the frontends gave up.

The 900s budget was set by #56735 (merged 2026-09-15), but the DSv4 mHC TileLang kernel migration (#50178, merged 2026-09-13) added hundreds of seconds of JIT warmup on top of the slow weight load, blowing the budget again.

## Fix

Raise `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` for the `dsv4-flash-disaggregated` step from 900 to 1800, following exactly the pattern of #56735. 1800s = observed worst case (~1133s) + ~670s margin, and stays within the step's 60-minute `timeout_in_minutes` budget.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for: `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S dsv4`, `dsv4-flash-disaggregated timeout`, `DSv4-Flash Disaggregated`, `engine ready timeout`, `disaggregated timeout 1800`, `kernel warmup timeout`. The closest match is #56761 (`[Perf] Parallelize TileLang mHC JIT warmup for GLM-5.3-Flash`), which is a perf optimization for a different model and does not touch this step's config — even if it lands, the 900s budget for DSv4-Flash would remain marginal (model loading alone is ~740s). No open PR fixes this CI step.

## Validation

- Parsed `.buildkite/test_areas/disaggregated.yaml` with PyYAML via the project venv: the file loads, exactly one `dsv4-flash-disaggregated` step exists, and its `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` env is now `"1800"`.
- Pre-commit hooks ran at commit time and passed (including "Check every Buildkite step declares an explicit key").
- Not run: the actual CI step (requires 8x H200 GPUs; this machine has no GPU).

This PR was authored with AI assistance (Kimi).

title: C3x SM100 FP8 blockwise - Pad activation scales to multiple of 4

title: [Perf] Remove CPU-GPU sync in heterogeneous vocabulary speculative decoding
body: ## Purpose Remove a CPU-GPU synchronization between target and draft model execution phases during speculative decoding. This occurs specifically when heterogeneous vocabulary is used. The CPU-GPU synchronization point prevents the engine from enqueuing more draft-model CUDA kernels asynchronously during the target model's execution. So the CPU kernel launch rate becomes a bottleneck given a sufficiently small draft model decoding time. **NSYS profiling**. Notice the async compute and GPU activity drops to ~0% between target and draft model execution for a decode step. ## Test Plan **Correctness test**. These new unit tests ensure that the output of the vocabulary mapping functions return the correct token ids. ``` pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_vocab_mapping.py -k "test_map_target_to_draft_ids or test_map_draft_to_target_ids" ``` **Performance test**. Run the following script for both this branch and main to compare the performance difference. Draft tokens are all synthetically rejected to avoid non-deterministic behaviour. ``` vllm bench throughput \ --model \ --speculative-config '{ "method": "draft_model", "model": "", "num_speculative_tokens": 8, "rejection_sample_method": "synthetic", "synthetic_acceptance_length": 1.0, "parallel_drafting": , "use_heterogeneous_vocab": true }' \ --num-warmups 1 \ --max-num-seqs 1 \ --random-input-len 128 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --max-model-len 4096 \ --num-prompts 1 ``` ## Test Result ### Correctness test The unit tests passed. ### Performance test Throughput was evaluated on a RTX 6000 Ada Generation GPU and Intel Xeon E5-2640v3 CPU. #### Vanilla speculative decoding (batch size: 1, speculative tokens: 4, parallel drafting: false, 'use_heterogeneous_vocab': true) target model | draft model | old decode throughput | new decode throughput | speedup -- | -- | -- | -- | -- Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B | Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | 21.33 tps | 25.74 tps | +20.7% Qwen/Qwen3-4B | Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | 24.08 tps | 25.03 tps | +3.9% Qwen/Qwen3-8B | Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | 18.92 tps | 26.01 tps | +37.5% Qwen/Qwen3-14B | Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | 15.47 tps | 26.15 tps | +69.0% #### Parallel Draft (PARD) speculative decoding (batch size: 1, speculative tokens: 8, parallel drafting: true, 'use_heterogeneous_vocab': true) target model | draft model | old decode throughput | new decode throughput | speedup -- | -- | -- | -- | -- Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B | amd/PARD-Qwen2.5-0.5B | 39.93 tps | 57.02 tps | +42.8% Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B | amd/PARD-Qwen2.5-0.5B | 30.50 tps | 52.31 tps | +71.5% Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B | amd/PARD-Qwen2.5-0.5B | 20.60 tps | 28.78 tps | +39.7% ### NSYS Profiling Notice the removal of this synchronization point improves the GPU and async compute activity, and the throughput for the draft model.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Enable layer-aware CSA2 multi-stream overlap for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
body:
## Purpose DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has three attention layer shapes: full CSA2 layers (2/8/14/20) run SWA + compressor + indexer and build a new global KV cache with their own Top-K indices; reindex CSA2 layers (24/28/32/36) run SWA + indexer only, re-scoring Top-K over an earlier layer's global KV cache; all other layers are dense or pure SWA. The shared v4.1 pipeline overlaps the full CSA2 layers with **three** fork/join pairs per step (input projections; Q/SWA-insert vs compressor; indexer vs cache-insert) and the reindex layers with one. On ROCm each fork/join is a HIP event pair per side stream, so the multi-stream launch cost outweighs the overlap benefit there. --- This PR gives the ROCm attention layer a layer-type-aware scheme with exactly one fork/join per step: **Full CSA2 layers (`_forward_csa2_full`)**: one 3-stream fork right after the input norm. - default stream: fused wqa+wkv → q/kv split+norm → wq_b → fused qnorm/RoPE/SWA-insert; - aux stream 0: the compressor chain (kv_score GEMM → save/compress/norm → RoPE-quant cache insert); - aux stream 1: indexer `weights_proj`. After the single join, the indexer K write (`_produce_k`, whose `wk` consumes the aux-0 latent) and the query path (`forward_q`, whose wq_b consumes the default-stream qr) run serially, followed by the indexer op and sparse MLA. **Reindex CSA2 layers (`_forward_csa2_reindex`)**: the input projections run serially first (the query path consumes qr, so overlapping the weight projection is not worth it), then one 2-stream fork overlaps the SWA q path with the indexer query path. **Dense layers**: fully serial (`aux_stream_list` disabled). --- A new shared helper `execute_in_parallel_default_first` (in `vllm/utils/multi_stream_utils.py`) mirrors `execute_in_parallel` but enqueues the default chain before the aux chains — the default chain is the longest, so starting it first shortens the step tail while the aux streams still only wait on the pre-fork default-stream work. The fork is gated exactly like the shipped v4.0 multi-stream gate (#51794/#56853): it only runs where the fork/join becomes static graph edges (inside capture, or with non-dict metadata such as the profile run); everywhere else — including MRV1, which keeps its wide eager region (#51430) — the layer falls back to the fully sequential base pipeline. The CUDA/NVIDIA path is untouched except for a behavior-neutral base refactor: the v4.1 indexer's query path is extracted into `DeepseekV4Indexer.forward_q`, still driven unchanged by the base `forward` (`_produce_k` keeps its private name). This is not a duplicate of #51794/#56853, which cover v4.0: v4.1-flash has a different topology (the indexer derives K from the kv-source compressor's latent, with no indexer-local compressor), so the overlap must differ per layer type. ## Trace Comparison (Take conc=4 as an example) **With regard to CSA2 layers with compressor and indexer (layer_id=2/8/14/20):** Before: > The default NV path launches multi-stream 3 times per layer, which is inefficient on ROCm path (multi-stream cost > overlap benefit). After (**20.76%** faster than the old pattern): --- **With regard to CSA2 layers only with indexer (layer_id=24/28/32/36):** Before: > No need to overlap indexer weight projection, since the benefit (4 μs) < the multi-stream cost (5 μs + 6 μs = 11 μs). Instead, we prefer to overlap SWA process and indexer process. After (**11.90%** faster than the old pattern): ## Test Plan Benchmark with SA InferenceX `8k1k` workload with server launch commands below: ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 export AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 GPU_COUNT=4 export HF_HOME=/shared/models vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8333 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --language-model-only \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \ --moe-backend aiter \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --max-model-len 1048576 \ --max-num-seqs 128 \ --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --disable-uvicorn-access-log \ --no-swa-bounded-replay \ --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \ 2>&1 | tee "${OUTDIR}/server.log" ``` Accuracy test with `gsm8k` dataset using `lm_eval`: ```bash lm_eval \ --model local-completions \ --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8333/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=10,max_gen_toks=2048,timeout=60000,tokenized_requests=False \ --batch_size auto \ --tasks gsm8k \ --num_fewshot 5 \ --output_path . 2>&1 | tee -a eval.log ``` > [!NOTE] > All tests based on latest `nightly-rocm100` image. ## Test Result ### Benchmark By the way, note that the e2e benefit could be small, since there are onlt **8** layers that we can optimize (overlap), while other layers always execute serially. | Conc | Version | Output token throughput (tok/s) | Change | Mean TTFT (ms) | Change | Mean TPOT (ms) | Change | | ---: | :------ | ------------------------------: | :-----: | -------------: | :------: | -------------: | :-----: | | 1 | main | 114.47 | — | 392.61 | — | 8.32 | — | | 1 | this PR | 117.28 | 2.45% ↑ | 266.06 | 32.23% ↓ | 8.25 | 0.84% ↓ | | 4 | main | 381.72 | — | 348.33 | — | 9.86 | — | | 4 | this PR | 386.47 | 1.24% ↑ | 331.76 | 4.76% ↓ | 9.76 | 1.01% ↓ | | 16 | main | 1018.13 | — | 496.96 | — | 14.73 | — | | 16 | this PR | 1018.69 | 0.06% ↑ | 495.02 | 0.39% ↓ | 14.73 | 0.00% | | 64 | main | 1912.44 | — | 1165.33 | — | 31.71 | — | | 64 | this PR | 1920.10 | 0.40% ↑ | 1160.00 | 0.46% ↓ | 31.59 | 0.38% ↓ | In summary, the performance data indicates that this PR provides consistent throughput gains and latency reductions without introducing a regression in the tested metrics. The most noticeable benefit is at low concurrency, while at higher concurrency (conc=16 and 64) the changes are comparatively small, suggesting that the optimization has limited additional impact once the system becomes heavily loaded. ### Accuracy Test Main: |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9363|± |0.0067| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9363|± |0.0067| This PR: |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9363|± |0.0067| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9371|± |0.0067| ---

title: [Transformers backend] Fuse MoE routers that score after the top-k
body:
Three related changes to the Transformers modeling backend's MoE path, smallest
to largest in blast radius.

## 1. `MoEBlockFuser._match_router` accepts scoring on either side of the top-k

`_match_router` only looked for `softmax`/`sigmoid` *upstream* of the routing
top-k. A family of HF routers scores the selection instead:

```python
# GraniteMoeTopKRouter, AriaTextTopKRouter, JetMoE, ...
top_k_logits, top_k_index = router_logits.topk(self.top_k, dim=-1)
top_k_weights = torch.softmax(top_k_logits, dim=-1)
```

These did not match, so the whole block fell back to routing in Transformers and
smuggling `topk_ids` through a custom op. They now fuse.

The two placements are equivalent: `sigmoid` is elementwise, so scoring before or
after the selection is identical; a `softmax` over the selected logits equals a
softmax over every logit with the selected weights renormalized, since the
full-vocabulary denominator cancels.

## 2. `renormalize` is read from the router's graph, not guessed from the config

vLLM's kernel always scores all `E` experts and then selects, so its weights sum
to less than 1. Reproducing a router that softmaxes the selection alone requires
`renormalize=True`. The previous logic was `norm_topk_prob` if present, else
`top_k > 1`, which is wrong for a router that uses raw softmax-over-all weights
(`RoutingMethodType.Default`) and for `top_k=1`, where renormalizing forces the
single gate to exactly 1.0.

`_match_router` now reports what the router actually does:

- `True` if it softmaxes the selection, or divides the top-k weights by their sum
  (the walk goes through the denominator's input cone, so it absorbs the
  `+ 1e-20` spelling that 17 models in Transformers use).
- `False` if a complete trace shows it does neither.
- `None` only if tracing stopped before it could tell, in which case the previous
  config logic still applies.

This is more reliable than reading the config, not less: `norm_topk_prob` is a
Python bool that fx resolves at trace time, so the graph already reflects it.
`Qwen3MoeTopKRouter` traces to 13 nodes with `sum`/`truediv` when the flag is on
and 11 without. It also handles per-layer heterogeneity for free, since `match()`
runs per block against that block's own router instance rather than indexing a
config list by `extract_layer_index`.

## 3. `_infer_meta` no longer recurses until the stack runs out

While tracing, fx patches `nn.Module.__getattr__` to record `get_attr` nodes.
`_infer_meta`'s `get_attr` branch read the parameter's value through that patched
hook, so inferring the meta value of a `get_attr` created another `get_attr`,
which inferred its meta value, and so on until `RecursionError` — swallowed by the
`contextlib.suppress(Exception)` in `create_proxy`, leaving a complete but
massively duplicated graph.

This fires for any module reading an `nn.Parameter` directly in `forward`, which
is every HF v5 `TopKRouter` and every `RMSNorm`. Nodes in the returned graph,
before and after:

| module | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DeepseekV3TopkRouter` | 5519 | 31 |
| `GraniteMoeTopKRouter` | 1970 | 10 |
| `Qwen3MoeTopKRouter` | 1775 | 11 |
| `Qwen3MoeRMSNorm` | 600 | 12 |
| `Qwen3MoeMLP` (only `nn.Linear` children) | 7 | 7 |

How many repeats got recorded depended on how much stack was left, so repeated
traces of the same module disagreed with each other. Matching that only walked
`all_input_nodes` upstream survived this; anything reading `users` did not, which
is what made change 1 necessary to fix first.

Meta execution now runs under `_unpatched_modules()`, restoring both `__call__`
(which the `call_module` branch already did) and `__getattr__`.

## Testing

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/transformers/fusers -q
111 passed, 1 skipped, 14 warnings in 15.38s

$ pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fx_utils.py \
    vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/moe.py \
    vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/moe.py \
    tests/models/transformers/fusers/test_moe.py
(all hooks passed)
```

New cases in `tests/models/transformers/fusers/test_moe.py`: post-top-k scoring
for both `softmax` and `sigmoid`, and `renormalize` resolving to `True` for
divide-by-sum, `True` for an epsilon-offset denominator, `False` for a router that
scales its weights instead, and `None` for a router whose trace is cut short.

Spot-checked against the real Transformers routers on the meta device:

| router | `_match_router` |
| --- | --- |
| `GraniteMoeTopKRouter` | `('softmax', float32, True)` |
| `AriaTextTopKRouter` | `('softmax', None, True)` |
| `Qwen3MoeTopKRouter` (`norm_topk_prob=True`) | `('softmax', None, True)` |
| `Qwen3MoeTopKRouter` (`norm_topk_prob=False`) | `('softmax', None, False)` |
| `DeepseekV3TopkRouter` | `('sigmoid', float32, True)` |
| `DeepseekV2TopkRouter` | `('softmax', float32, False)` |
| `OlmoeTopKRouter` | `('softmax', None, False)` |
| `FlexOlmoTopKRouter` | `('softmax', None, False)` |

These agree with vLLM's native implementations, which hardcode the same values:
`granitemoe.py:106` `renormalize=True`, `olmoe.py:100` `renormalize=False`,
`deepseek_v2.py:381` `renormalize=config.norm_topk_prob`.

## Model evaluation

**Not run.** This change affects model output and I do not have a GPU available,
so I could not run `tests/evals/gsm8k` or `vllm bench`. Flagging it explicitly
rather than leaving it for a reviewer to ask.

The two things most worth a real model behind them:

- GraniteMoE and Aria now take the fused path instead of routing in Transformers.
- Change 3 is shared by every fuser, not just MoE, so GLU/QKV/RMSNorm/MLA/Attention
  matching across the whole Transformers backend now runs against different (and
  correct) graphs.

## Not a duplicate

No open PR touches `transformers/fusers/moe.py`, `transformers/fx_utils.py`,
`MoEBlockFuser` or `_match_router` (`gh pr list --search` on each). The nearest
neighbours are #53811 (removes native LongCat) and #55690 (QKV-Fuser for Gemma4),
neither of which overlaps.

## AI assistance

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude Code). I have reviewed every
changed line and ran the tests quoted above.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Alias SparseAttnIndexerKpool.forward_cuda to forward_native (GLM-5.3-Flash boot crash)
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57424. `SparseAttnIndexerKpool` on the AMD/ROCm path (`vllm/models/glm5next/amd/sparse_indexer.py`) defines only `forward_native`. `CustomOp.dispatch_forward` routes *enabled* ops to `forward_hip` on ROCm, and `forward_hip` falls back to `forward_cuda` — which doesn't exist → `NotImplementedError` at the first forward of the indexer op.

On the `v0.29.1rc0.dev265+g0bfc7a15d` ROCm nightly, serving GLM-5.3-Flash crashes at `profile_run` with:

```
File "vllm/model_executor/custom_op.py", line 149, in forward_hip
    return self.forward_cuda(*args, **kwargs)
File "vllm/model_executor/custom_op.py", line 145, in forward_cuda
    raise NotImplementedError
```

because the resolved `compilation_config.custom_ops` contains `'all'` there, enabling every registered op — including `sparse_attn_indexer_kpool`.

## Why

The NVIDIA `SparseAttnIndexerKpool` defines both `forward_native` and `forward_cuda`; the AMD one is native-only but was never given the alias the ROCm dispatch requires. This blocks GLM-5.3-Flash boot on current ROCm nightlies entirely.

## Test results

- New unit test `tests/models/test_rocm_sparse_indexer_forward_cuda.py`: fails on the unpatched file, passes with the fix (run with `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`).
- End-to-end on 8×MI350X (TP8, GLM-5.3-Flash fp8, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-0bfc7a15d` + this patch in-place): engine boots Ready with 57 FULL + 106 PIECEWISE cudagraphs captured; chunked-prefill repro (20K prompt, 16K chunks) plus a long-context ladder 32K→524,212 tokens all pass with zero memory access faults, engine healthy after.

AI assistance was used in preparing this PR; the change was reviewed and hardware-validated end-to-end by the submitter.

## Related

- #57227 — original gfx950 16K-chunk memory access fault; root-caused by #57317
- #57317 — kpool tail slot-mapping OOB fix (the root cause of #57227)
- #57248 — nightly GLM-5.3-Flash ROCm boot regressions (`record_logical_topk_ready` + jit-warmup)
- #57252 — our fix for the `record_logical_topk_ready` AttributeError
- #56604 — base-class `record_logical_topk_ready` alternative
- #57192 — jit-warmup tilelang fix

title: [Kernel][DSV4.1] Fuse MXFP8 wo_b GEMM with sequence-parallel reduce-scatter
body:
## Purpose

Under sequence parallel, DeepSeek-V4.1's `wo_b` runs as an MXFP8 row-parallel GEMM followed by a TP reduce-scatter: two kernels and one HBM round trip per layer. This PR fuses them with the SM100 GEMM-RS kernel. It builds on @gau-nernst's MXFP8 support for the Kimi-K3 GEMM-RS/AR kernel (the first five commits), moves that kernel to `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/cute_dsl/gemm_rs_ar.py` so both models share one workspace, init gate, warmup, test and benchmark, and binds V4.1's `wo_b` to it behind `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1` (default off; this single flag replaces `VLLM_KIMI_K3_GEMM_RS` and gates the Kimi-K3 RS path too — `VLLM_KIMI_K3_GEMM_AR` is unchanged). The decoder layer skips its own `sp_reduce_scatter` when bound; RS zero-fills output rows beyond M for callers that pass an unpadded token count. Requires SM100, BF16 model dtype, sequence parallel, TP in 2..16, and FlashInfer CUTLASS or CuTe-DSL MXFP8 weights (what `linear_backend=auto` selects); anything else falls back with a warning.

No open PR fuses the V4.1 `wo_b` reduce-scatter: #57257 changes the SP all-gather side and #54151 is Kimi-K3 AG-GEMM.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/kernels/test_gemm_rs_ar.py  # 2 GPUs: bf16, flashinfer_cutlass, flashinfer_cutedsl
torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -- benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_gemm_rs_ar.py \
    --model deepseek_v41 --backend flashinfer_cutedsl --m 128 192 256 384 512 1024 2048 4096 8192 16384
```

### Deploy

```bash
VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
    --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --max-num-seqs 32 --no-enable-prefix-caching --seed 2026
```

Baseline: the same command with `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=0` (main's `wo_b` path).

### Benchmark

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model dsv41 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
    --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 2026 --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 96 --num-warmups 8
```

GSM8K: lm-eval 0.4.12, `gsm8k` 5-shot chat (`--apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn`, thinking off), greedy, 1024 max tokens, all 1319 questions.

## Test Result

4xB200, TP4 + EP4 with MegaMoE (sequence parallel), FlashInfer sparse MLA, fp8 KV, no speculative decoding. Kernel test: 3 passed.

Operator level (`benchmark_gemm_rs_ar.py`), TP4, `wo_b` shape N=5120 with K=2048 per rank, MXFP8 CuTe-DSL layout, activation quantization included in both candidates, CUDA graphs, median over 40 samples of the slowest rank. The baseline is the model's unfused path with vLLM's own collective dispatch (custom Lamport reduce-scatter for small messages, NCCL above its size cap):

| M | vLLM linear + `sp_reduce_scatter` (us) | GEMM-RS (us) | latency |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 26.6 | 29.2 | +9.7% |
| 512 | 36.9 | 38.9 | +5.6% |
| 1024 | 48.0 | 47.1 | -2.0% |
| 2048 | 100.9 | 63.5 | -37.1% |
| 4096 | 141.8 | 96.3 | -32.1% |
| 8192 | 226.8 | 162.8 | -28.2% |
| 16384 | 428.5 | 289.2 | -32.5% |

The fused kernel wins from about 1024 tokens; below that vLLM's Lamport reduce-scatter is faster than the fused kernel's fixed flag/exit handshake. Without speculative decoding, decode batches (at most `max_num_seqs` tokens) never reach the fused path and prefill chunks are large, so serving only sees the winning region.

Torch profiler, one 8192-token prefill step on rank 0: the 40 NCCL reduce-scatter launches (9.1 ms) and 40 `wo_b` GEMMs (2.8 ms) are replaced by 40 fused launches (6.6 ms); GPU busy time per step drops from 127.1 ms to 118.1 ms (-7.1%).

Online serving, `bench serve` with fixed-length random requests, mean of two runs per arm (arms off, on, on, off with a fresh server each), zero preemptions:

| workload | output tok/s | total tok/s | mean TTFT (ms) | mean TPOT (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192 in / 1024 out, c16 | 1697.8 -> 1708.0 (+0.6%) | 15279.8 -> 15371.6 (+0.6%) | 1050.5 -> 1038.5 (-1.1%) | 8.40 -> 8.36 (-0.5%) |
| 8192 in / 1024 out, c32 | 2592.0 -> 2668.2 (+2.9%) | 23328.4 -> 24014.2 (+2.9%) | 1565.3 -> 1512.5 (-3.4%) | 10.82 -> 10.51 (-2.9%) |
| 1024 in / 2048 out, c32 | 3178.2 -> 3324.3 (+4.6%) | 4767.4 -> 4986.5 (+4.6%) | 771.4 -> 767.5 (-0.5%) | 9.75 -> 9.27 (-5.0%) |

Run-to-run spread: baseline runs differ by 0.5% (c16), 5.4% (c32) and 16% (1k/2k); fused runs by 0.1%, 1.7% and 7%. The c16 change is within drift; c32 is at its edge with every percentile improving (p99 TTFT 4760 -> 3610 ms); the 1k/2k row is not resolved by two runs.

GSM8K, same server config:

| metric | off | on | paired changes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| flexible-extract | 95.98% (+-0.54) | 96.29% (+-0.52) | 10 became correct, 6 became wrong |
| strict-match | 79.45% (+-1.11) | 78.70% (+-1.13) | 30 became correct, 40 became wrong |

Both within one standard error; 417 of 1319 generations are byte-identical, the rest differ in BF16 partial rounding order between the fused FP32 multicast reduction and NCCL's ring.

Not measured: speculative decoding (decode batches near 192 tokens would also take the fused path) and TP8. The `off` arm runs this branch with the flag unset rather than a separate main checkout; the earlier commits only touch Kimi-K3 and `cute_utils`, so V4.1's `wo_b` path is main's.

AI assistance was used (Claude Code) for the V4.1 integration, the kernel relocation and driving the benchmarks; every changed line and result was reviewed by the author.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Fix FlashInfer DSpark non-causal attention
body:
DSpark's non-causal draft window has 133 valid keys at draft length 5, padded to 256 indices. The DSV4.1 FlashInfer integration passed the padded width as the active sparse length, so padding entered softmax normalization. A constant-value reference expecting 1 returned 0.51953125 (133/256). Short contexts also inherited causal visibility from the launcher's per-request query positions.

Use the valid SWA length, retaining FlashInfer's required 128-column minimum, and present each draft query with the full non-causal sequence length. Prepare the per-token active lengths and sequence lengths once in the metadata builder, using persistent buffers refreshed before FULL CUDA graph replay and shared across layers. Singleton query/output views remove the need to construct query offsets in each layer. This changes vLLM metadata only; no FlashInfer source changes or new Triton kernel are needed. The two int32 buffers use 8 bytes per configured maximum batched token per builder (64 KiB at capacity 8192).

Validation on 4× GB200 with FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`), DSpark length 5 and full decode graphs. DEP4 uses MegaMoE/adaptive verification; TP4 uses auto MoE/fixed verification.

Full GSM8K: 1,319 identical 5-shot chat prompts per pair, greedy, seed 123, thinking off, 1,024-token output cap. Accuracy below uses flexible extraction.

| Configuration | Acceptance before → fixed (including bonus) | GSM8K before → fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DEP4 | 3.1823 → **3.8248** (+20.2%) | 1268 → 1271 / 1319 (96.13% → 96.36%) |
| TP4 | 3.2075 → **3.8879** (+21.2%) | 1266 → 1263 / 1319 (95.98% → 95.75%) |

All 1,319 requests completed in each fixed run, with no errors or empty responses. DEP had no capped outputs; TP had one (versus zero before). Strict extraction: DEP 1042 → 1042; TP 1060 → 1049. These evaluations establish acceptance recovery, not exact greedy-output equivalence or an accuracy improvement. MegaAttention measured 3.8437 acceptance on the DEP cohort. These are short-context results, not 100K-context throughput measurements.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py \
  -k test_dsv41_flashinfer_dspark_window_matches_reference -q -rs
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_swa.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py
```

The original 12 regression cases failed before the correctness fix. All 12 expanded cases pass with persistent metadata: BF16/FP8, 16/64 heads, short/long windows, mixed query lengths, padding, and CUDA graph replay after Q/KV and visible-length updates, with unchanged buffer addresses. Attention outputs are bitwise identical to the initial correctness fix across eight FP8 shapes (16/64 heads, batch 1/8/32/128). Nine full draft-forward runs have zero observed eager/graph, changed-input, restored-input and post-replay error. Pre-commit checks pass. Validation ran on the optimization worktree; all three changed files are identical in this isolated PR branch. The GSM8K results above evaluate the correctness fix; the metadata refactor was validated by parity and replay checks, without repeating the full accuracy runs.

Metadata-refactor performance on GB200 ×4, relative to the initial correctness fix: synthetic weights and 102,400 KV tokens/request, draft length 5, TP auto MoE / DEP MegaMoE. Medians of five distributed-MAX samples, 20 graph replays/sample after 3 seconds of warmup; each comparison uses the same runner and repeats one endpoint to expose order effects.

| Workload | Initial fix (µs) | Prepared metadata (µs) | Draft-forward result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| TP4 B1 | 403 / 425 | 366 | 9–14% lower latency |
| DEP4 B8 | 703 / 691 | 669 | 3–5% lower latency |
| DEP4 B128 | 1370 | 1431 / 1327 | Inconclusive |

The forward boundary excludes metadata preparation, LM head, scheduler and sampling; these are not serving-throughput gains. Preparation costs 3.9–8.5 µs per build in a separate CUPTI/CUDA-graph/cold-L2 microbenchmark and is shared across layers. Exact commands and raw results are archived locally under `/home/woosuk/.cache/v41-dspark-opt/metadata-opt/metadata-paired-002-*`; the microbenchmark results are in `prepared-results.json`.

Duplicate check: searched open DSpark/FlashInfer, acceptance, noncausal sparse, and padding PRs. #52499 and #57292 address SM120 routing/page geometry; #54834 addresses dense FlashInfer cache-layout resolution; #55692 addresses block-table bounds. None fixes the SM100 DSV4.1 non-causal active lengths and visibility corrected here.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Reuse the decode topk ragged metadata across layers
body: ## Purpose `_forward_decode` rebuilds the ragged form of the topk indices on every compressed layer. The pack is a pure function of the shared `topk_indices_buffer`, which only `index_source_layer_ids` write, plus per-step metadata (`token_to_req_indices`, the block table, `is_valid_token`). The one per-layer term is `compress_ratio`, which divides the block size. So the layers between two index sources all rebuild the same thing. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, `compress_ratios` has 38 layers with a compressed cache and `index_source_layer_ids` has 8 entries, giving 38 rebuilds per decode step for 8 distinct results — a 4.8x redundancy. A 10-step decode trace on MI355X (TP4, rank 0) confirms the count and the cost: | kernel | total | calls | per call | |---|---|---|---| | `_pack_global_topk_ragged_kernel` | 1678.1 us | 380 | 4.42 us | | `_compute_topk_lens_kernel` | 1546.0 us | 380 | 4.07 us | 380 = 38 layers x 10 steps. Together they are 2.2% of all kernel time, ~322 us and 76 launches per step. ## What changes The index source memoizes the pack and the layers below it read through, keyed by compress ratio since that is the only per-layer term. Consumers resolve their source once in `__init__` through `static_forward_context`, the same way the layer already resolves its compressed-KV source, and raise the same `NotImplementedError` if a PP split lands inside an index-sharing group. Invalidation is structural rather than versioned: the source clears its own entry when it runs, and it always runs before the layers that consume its indices, so a step cannot read the previous step's pack. Prefill is untouched. Expected effect: 8 rebuilds per step instead of 38, ~255 us and 60 launches per step of GPU work removed, ~1.8% of decode GPU time on this model. ## Not a duplicate Searched open PRs for the neighbouring work: - #56638 re-enables the fused `combine_topk_swa_indices` kernel. Same file, but the mixed-prefill index combine, not the decode pack. - #57282 adds an opt-in HIP decode kernel. It consumes this metadata; it does not change how often it is built. - #57109 and #54394 touch the indexer that produces the indices, upstream of the pack. None of them change the per-layer rebuild. ## Test plan - `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py` - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 on MI355X: a 10-step decode capture to confirm the rebuild count drops to one per index source, and GSM8K for accuracy parity. The change is a pure memoization, so parity is the bar. ## Test results Unit tests, on the branch, MI355X: ``` $ pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py -q 68 passed in 75.03s ``` Decode capture, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 on MI355X, 10 engine steps at concurrency 1, fp8 KV, MTP spec decode. Per-step kernel time, mean over the four TP ranks: | kernel | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | `_pack_global_topk_ragged_kernel` | 173.1 us | 38.0 us | | `_compute_topk_lens_kernel` | 158.4 us | 34.1 us | | `_inverse_rope_gptj_kernel` (untouched) | 201.6 us | 206.5 us | | `_sparse_attn_decode_reduce_kernel` (untouched) | 218.7 us | 224.1 us | Launches fall from 380 to 80 per 10 steps, i.e. exactly the 8 per step the 8 index sources predict, and the untouched kernels stay put. Net 250.2 us per step against the 255 us the trace analysis predicted. Accuracy, GSM8K 5-shot, 400 questions, greedy, concurrency 32, spec decode off so that generations are model-faithful: | build | accuracy | invalid | |---|---|---| | main | 0.9025 | 0.0% | | this PR | 0.9025 | 0.0% | Note this stack is not run-to-run deterministic: `main` compared against itself disagrees token-for-token on 3 of 6 fixed greedy prompts, so parity is established statistically rather than by diffing outputs. ## What is not measured End-to-end interactivity, which this PR does not claim. Paired step-time samples on MI355X (TP4, MTP spec decode, profiler off, three 25 s samples per point, `main` and the patched build loaded side by side on opposite GPU halves) do not resolve a change of this size. The patched side here carries this change together with #57435: | concurrency | main | patched | delta | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 45.57 +/- 1.24 ms/step | 46.15 +/- 1.21 | +1.28% | | 32 | 44.65 +/- 0.21 ms/step | 44.41 +/- 0.08 | -0.54% | Acceptance was identical at 3.533 tokens per step, so the comparison is fair. The concurrency-32 point moves the right way and is by far the tighter of the two, but three samples cannot separate a sub-1% effect from this spread, and the concurrency-1 spread is larger than the effect being looked for. With spec decode off the loop is outright host-bound -- 12.61 +/- 0.00 ms per step, with the A/B at -0.01% and 0.00% -- so removed GPU work simply lands in host slack. The claim here is therefore the kernel-level saving above, not an ITL number. --- AI assistance was used to write this change. I have reviewed every line, ran the tests and evals above myself, and am responsible for it.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Fuse the inverse RoPE into the sparse decode reduce
body: ## Purpose The ROCm sparse decode writes the attention output twice. The reduce kernel combines the split-K partials and stores `[T, H, 512]`, and then `_inverse_rope_gptj_kernel` reads that whole tensor back, rotates the trailing 64 rope lanes and writes it out again — a full round trip per layer, for an epilogue on data the reduce already held in registers. From a 10-step decode trace on MI355X (TP4, rank 0): | kernel | total | calls | share of kernel time | |---|---|---|---| | `_sparse_attn_decode_gfx950_partial_kernel` | 4707.3 us | 430 | 3.24% | | `_sparse_attn_decode_reduce_kernel` | 2214.2 us | 430 | 1.52% | | `_inverse_rope_gptj_kernel` | 1965.5 us | 430 | 1.35% | 430 = 43 layers x 10 steps: every layer pays it, sliding-window and MTP layers included. FlashMLA's mega-attention kernel already folds this rotation and the FP8 cast into its epilogue on SM100 — `flash_mla_mega_attn.py` describes exactly that — and the layer interface for it is platform-generic (`_alloc_attn_out` / `_o_proj`, `accepts_unnormed_unroped_query`). The ROCm Triton path just never took it. ## What changes The reduce gained an optional inverse-RoPE epilogue. Reshaping the combined row into adjacent pairs puts the rope lanes in the last 32 of 256 pairs, so giving the NoPE pairs cos=1 and sin=0 lets one expression cover the whole row with no branch and no second pass: ```python even, odd = tl.split(tl.reshape(out, (BLOCK_H, COMB_DIM // 2, 2))) out = tl.reshape(tl.join(even * cos + odd * sin, odd * cos - even * sin), ...) ``` Which rows still owe a rotation depends on the batch: the reduce rotates the decode rows it produces, prefill rows have no such epilogue, and a decode path that does not fuse (for instance the opt-in HIP kernel in #57282) rotates nothing. `rocm_sparse_attn_decode` reports how many leading rows it rotated and `forward_mqa` pays the standalone pass for the rest, in place. On a decode-only step that leaves nothing to do, so the kernel does not launch at all rather than being replaced by a copy. That bookkeeping belongs in the eager attention segment specifically, not in `_o_proj`. An earlier revision of this PR handed the row count to `_o_proj`, which runs inside the compiled region; since vLLM compiles with `skip_all_guards_unsafe`, the Python int froze at its trace-time value and rows ended up rotated zero or two times. GSM8K fell to 0.087 against a 0.902 baseline with fluent output and no error of any kind. The lane arithmetic was correct throughout, so no kernel-level test caught it -- only the eval did. Two side effects worth noting: the rotation now happens on the fp32 accumulator rather than the already-rounded bf16 output, dropping a rounding step, and the NoPE lanes come through bit-exact (x1.0 + 0.0). Expected effect: ~196 us and 43 launches per step removed, ~1.35% of decode GPU time on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. ## Not a duplicate - #54894 fuses inverse RoPE with group quantization via AITER's `inverse_rope_group_quant` — different model (`deepseek_v4`), different mechanism, and it keeps the rotation as its own pass. This removes the pass. The two are compatible in direction: if the V4.1 ROCm path later adopts an FP8 `wo_a`, the natural next step is emitting the FP8 cast from this same epilogue, which is what the SM100 kernel does. - #57282 adds an opt-in HIP decode kernel for a specific batch range and falls through to this Triton path otherwise; the two compose, and the rotated-row count above is what keeps them honest. - #56720 and #56342 touch other kernels in the same file, not the reduce. ## Test results Unit tests, on the branch, MI355X: ``` $ pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py \ tests/kernels/attention/test_dsv41_rocm_fused_inv_rope.py -q 69 passed in 38.64s ``` Kernel equivalence, MI355X: running the real decode kernels fused, then unfused followed by `_fused_inverse_rope_gptj`, on identical inputs. NoPE lanes are bit-exact and rope lanes agree to bf16 rounding at every shape tried -- `(queries, heads)` of (2, 3), (1, 128), (8, 128), (32, 128): | | max abs diff | |---|---| | NoPE lanes | 0.0 (32 queries: 4.9e-4) | | rope lanes | <= 2.0e-3, against \|rope\| up to 0.29 | Decode capture, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 on MI355X, 10 engine steps at concurrency 1, MTP spec decode. Per-step kernel time, mean over the four TP ranks: | kernel | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | `_inverse_rope_gptj_kernel` | 201.6 us | 0.0 us (430 launches -> 0) | | `_sparse_attn_decode_reduce_kernel` | 218.7 us | 227.0 us | The pass disappears on decode-only steps and the reduce absorbs it for 8.3 us, so 193 us per step net, against the 196 us the trace analysis predicted. Accuracy, GSM8K 5-shot, greedy, concurrency 32 score remains the same --- AI assistance was used to write this change. I have reviewed every line, ran the tests and evals above myself, and am responsible for it.
