title: [ROCm][DSv4][Perf] Fuse the inverse RoPE into the sparse decode reduce
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4 shares the ROCm sparse decode kernels with V4.1, so the reduce
epilogue added in #57435 applies here with no kernel work at all — only the
call site has to opt in. On decode-only steps the standalone
`_inverse_rope_gptj_kernel` stops launching entirely; on V4.1 that measured
201.6 us per step against 8.3 us added to the reduce, for 193 us net.

#57435 has since merged, so this is no longer stacked: the epilogue, the
`inverse_rope` switch on `rocm_inv_rope_einsum`, and the
`rocm_inverse_rope_rows_` helper are all on main. What is left here is 27 lines
in one file.

## What changes

`_forward_decode` passes the positions and the cos/sin cache into
`rocm_sparse_attn_decode`, so the rotation happens on the fp32 accumulators in
the reduce rather than in a separate pass over the already-rounded bf16 output,
and `_o_proj` no longer rotates.

Which rows still owe a rotation is batch-dependent — the reduce rotates the
decode rows it produced, prefill rows have none, and a decode path that does
not fuse rotates nothing — so `forward_mqa` settles it from the count the
decode reports, in the eager attention segment. That placement is the point:
vLLM compiles with `skip_all_guards_unsafe`, so the same value read from inside
the compiled `_o_proj` freezes at its trace-time value. In #57435 that mistake
cost 0.087 GSM8K against a 0.902 baseline, with fluent output and no error.

One thing V4 has that V4.1 does not: the FP8 `wo_a` path from #54894, whose
`inverse_rope_group_quant` rotates while it quantizes. Fusing there would
rotate twice, so the fusion is gated on `self._wo_a_fp8_weight is None` — which
is exactly the condition under which `_o_proj` takes the BF16 einsum branch
that stops rotating. When the FP8 path is active the decode is handed no
positions, returns a rotated count of 0, the settle pass is skipped, and the
path is left byte-identical to today. The gate is a load-time constant, not a
batch-dependent one, so reading it here raises none of the tracing concerns
above.

## Not a duplicate

- #57435 is the same optimization for `deepseek_v41` and was the parent of this
  branch; it has merged. The V4.1 call site cannot cover V4: they are separate
  attention classes in separate files.
- #57078 tiles the standalone inverse-RoPE kernel for sparse prefill. The two
  compose rather than collide: this PR removes the pass on decode-only steps
  and leaves prefill rows going through that same kernel, which #57078 makes
  faster.
- #54894 moved `wo_a` to an FP8 output projection in this same `_o_proj` and
  has landed. The textual conflict predicted here is resolved, and the
  correctness interaction it created is handled by the gate described above.

## Test plan

- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py`
- A fused-vs-unfused A/B of the real decode kernels on MI355X.
- A DeepSeek-V4 serving eval. **Not yet run — this is why the PR is a draft.**

## Test results

Unit tests, on the branch, MI355X:

```
$ pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py -q
74 passed in 65.82s
```

Kernel equivalence, MI355X: the real decode kernels run fused, then unfused
followed by `_fused_inverse_rope_gptj`, on identical inputs, at V4's head dims
(nope 448, rope 64). NoPE lanes are bit-exact and rope lanes agree to bf16
rounding at every shape tried — `(queries, heads)` of (2, 3), (1, 128),
(8, 128), (32, 128):

| | max abs diff |
|---|---|
| NoPE lanes | 0.0 (32 queries: 4.9e-4) |
| rope lanes | <= 2.0e-3, against \|rope\| up to 0.29 |

The kernel-level evidence for the epilogue itself, including the decode trace
and the GSM8K parity runs, is in #57435, and those kernels are untouched here.

## What is not measured

**No DeepSeek-V4 model has been run end to end on this branch.** The V4.1
sibling was validated with GSM8K at 1319 questions (0.918 against a 0.901
baseline) and a decode trace, but that exercises the V4.1 call site, not this
one. What supports this change is the shared kernels plus reading the V4 path:
`forward_mqa` is the sole attention entry point for
`DeepseekV4ROCMAiterMLAAttention` (`forward_mha` is not implemented for these
model classes, so `sparse_mla_force_mqa` does not route around it), decode rows
occupy the leading rows of the output buffer, and the base class slices
`o_padded[:, :n_local_heads, :]` before `_o_proj`, which is exactly the region
rotated here.

The FP8 `wo_a` gate is likewise unmeasured on a real V4 checkpoint. It is
argued from the code — no positions in means a rotated count of 0 out, and the
settle pass is skipped — rather than from a run on FP8 weights.

That reasoning is not a substitute for an eval, and the V4.1 experience is the
reason to say so plainly: the failure mode of getting this wrong is fluent
output with wrong answers and no error anywhere. A V4 eval, on both the BF16
and FP8 `wo_a` paths, should gate this leaving draft.

---

AI assistance was used to write this change. I have reviewed every line, ran
the tests above myself, and am responsible for it.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Retain offload event metadata through batch translation
body:
## Purpose

`OffloadingEventsTracker` caches a `BlockStored` payload per offload key and drops it when the key's last residency goes away. The drop happened inline in `_take_removed_event`, so within a single `take_events` batch a removal could delete the payload that a *later* event in that same batch still needed — a primary removal preceding a queued secondary (KVCR) store. That store then fell back to the placeholder payload, publishing an event with no block hashes and no token ids.

Fix: collect the removed keys during the batch and drop their payloads once, after every event in the batch has had a chance to register its residencies.

Scope: this does not address a store that only completes in a later batch; that needs the in-flight store set and is left for a follow-up.

Not a duplicate of #52103, which touches the same files to add request provenance to stored events.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py
```

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Preserve NaN-scored candidate block indices
body:
DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4 MegaAttention can fail startup with a DeepGEMM sparse-slot assertion during dummy prefill/autotuning. The candidate-source logits contain NaNs. Although `torch.topk` selects their block IDs, `value > -inf` discards them, leaving only the pinned newest block. Expanding that underfilled row repeats its last block inside the prefix DeepGEMM expects to be unique (389 copies of block 388 in the captured failing rows).

Exclude only the `-inf` padding sentinel when storing selected candidates. This retains NaN-scored block IDs, keeps the active prefix unique for the observed configuration, and works with the existing DeepGEMM dependency. Finite-score selection is unchanged; this adds no kernel, buffer, fallback, or host synchronization. It does not sanitize logits or fix the upstream numerical source of dummy-run NaNs.

Extend the existing candidate suite with empty/partial rows and aligned/unaligned starts under zero/NaN scores, and update its reference to retain selected NaN entries.

Validation on GB200:

- Both new NaN regression cases fail against the original selector; both finite control cases pass.
- All 13 candidate tests pass on PR commit `707b81b021`; scoped pre-commit hooks (including mypy) pass.
- Four captured TP-rank inputs replay through unmodified DeepGEMM after the fix, recovering 389 unique blocks in each previously failing row.
- Selector checks at 8K, 50K and 100K cover random, zero, NaN and mixed-NaN scores; finite outputs match the original exactly.
- The identical selector change on the previously validated model worktree passes real-weight TP4 MegaAttention startup with sparse logits, DSpark5, autotuning and FULL target/draft graphs. Short (18-token) and long (16,526-token) chat prompts both return the expected answer `4`. This is a serving smoke, not a full accuracy evaluation or a full-model build of current main. No full accuracy evaluation was repeated.

Duplicate-work check: #56558 optimizes the candidate-source selector but explicitly preserves NaN exclusion. #50201 and #49897 address the downstream token top-k kernel. None fixes this candidate-store predicate. vllm-project/DeepGEMM#16 instead adds repeated-index support to the native metadata API; this PR prevents vLLM from constructing the invalid active prefix for the observed NaN case and needs no dependency update. No linked issue.

AI assistance: implementation, investigation and validation used OpenAI Codex. The human submitter confirmed reviewing every changed line of commit `707b81b021` and running the relevant GPU tests.

title: [Perf][Attention] Reduce GLM sparse MLA preparation overhead
body:
## Purpose

Reduce query packing and sparse-index preparation overhead around FlashInfer NoPE MLA attention.

The three commits:

1. Reuse a contiguous NoPE query when its rotary tail is empty, avoiding a redundant `torch.cat` before FP8 quantization. Preserve concatenation for nonempty rotary dimensions and strided queries.
2. Use one padded remap program per query for counted sparse capacities up to 4096. Initialize padding and reduce valid counts inside the remap kernel, removing separate fills and atomic accumulation. Preserve larger tiled cases and reusable buffers. Name the device entry point `sparse_mla_index_remap_kernel` for trace attribution.
3. Simplify empty-query handling: fuse dummy-entry preparation and safe-length calculation while preserving raw counts; skip preparation and masking for resident TP; mask only LSE for DCP and let its existing merge suppress zero-weight outputs, including NaNs. Preserve PyTorch output masking for HiSparse without LSE. There is no custom output-zeroing kernel.

Duplicate-work checks found no matching open PR. Related PRs #54258 (separate ROCm remap kernel), #38354 (DeepSeek pre-attention GEMM/RoPE fusion), and #57161 (GLM kpool/indexer scheduling) address different kernels or stages. No existing issue is being claimed or closed.

## Correctness

Prior TP validation on the experiment stack used GLM-5.3-Flash, TP8+EP8, all custom ops enabled, eager execution, no prefix cache, and exactly 32768 input tokens with either 1 or 16 generated tokens. Across 12 repeatability requests, all 8976 sparse-layer calls across eight ranks had positive valid counts (minimum 1). A direct full-shape FP8 attention comparison at 32768 queries × 8 heads × 512 dimensions, capacity 2176, matched the previous implementation bit for bit.

## Performance

Controlled end-to-end comparison on four GB300 GPUs, TP4+EP4, eager, `custom_ops=["all"]`, no prefix cache, no speculative decoding, and FP8 E4M3 KV cache. The actual upstream PR model stayed loaded while an idle-worker extension switched only the three preparation changes to their PR-base implementations. All four ranks verified the implementation selection. Compatible prebuilt extensions were reused.

Both implementations were warmed, then measured in four alternating baseline/PR and PR/baseline rounds with five matched samples per workload per round (20 pairs each). Each request had exactly 32768 input tokens, with a 32768-token prefill scheduling limit. Prefill generated one token; decode generated 128 tokens. These are client-observed serving latencies.

| Metric | PR base | PR | Latency reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32K prefill TTFT, median | 518.25 ms | 507.61 ms | 2.05% |
| Decode inter-token latency, median | 122.85 ms/token | 120.77 ms/token | 1.70% |

All 20 pairs improved for each workload. Per-round median reductions ranged from 1.78–2.27% for prefill and 1.21–1.98% for decode. These measurements apply to eager TP4 execution; CUDA-graph decode and other parallel configurations were not measured in this comparison.

Earlier isolated measurements on the same GB300 GPU, using CUDA graph replay and the median of five samples with 40 repetitions/sample:

| Operation | Before | Optimized |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Remap including initialization | 531.90 µs | 282.93 µs |
| Safe lengths and dummy entry | 12.32 µs | 4.12 µs |

Shape: 32768 queries × 8 heads × 512 dimensions, capacity 2176. These are preparation microbenchmarks from the experiment stack. Resident TP now skips safe-length preparation entirely. Earlier tracing also confirmed removal of all 11 redundant query concatenations. The final upstream revision has not been reprofiled; the controlled end-to-end results above are separate from these older microbenchmarks. Measurements of the removed output-zeroing kernel are excluded.

title: [DeepSeek V4] Fix fused MoE expert distribution
body:
DeepSeek V4's fused MoE path incorrectly used the TP size and rank to calculate expert distribution and the number of physical experts on each GPU. These values should be determined by the EP group.

Use the EP size and rank instead, matching the MegaMoE path and other MoE models.

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Address kpool tail blocks by the padded indexer stride in the NVIDIA prefill seed kernel
body:
## Purpose

Fix silent indexer-cache corruption for GLM-5.3-Flash on NVIDIA: the kpool prefill tail-seed kernel addresses tail blocks with a dense stride while the tail cache is stored with the indexer's padded block stride.

**How the tail cache is laid out.** `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` pads the `KpoolTailSpec` page to the indexer page (`page_size_padded = idx_page`; 38016 B for the default `block_size=1152`: 288 pool rows x 132 B), and `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` places every indexer layer's tail tensor at the *same offset* as that layer's indexer tensor with `block_stride = idx_page`. Tail block `b` is therefore the first 2048 B (`[2, kpool=4, 128]` bf16) of indexer block `b`; the two never collide because both groups draw distinct block ids from one pool. `create_kv_cache_views` builds the view with `as_strided`, so `tail_kv_cache.stride(0) == 19008` elements instead of the dense 1024.

**The bug.** `_kpool_tail_seed_kernel` in `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/kpool_compress.py` computed

```python
base = (blk * 2 * KPOOL + t % KPOOL) * HEAD_DIM   # dense 2048 B block stride
```

so for every prefill it (a) left the request's own tail block unseeded and (b) wrote 2048 B of raw bf16 K / gate rows at byte `blk * 2048` of the layer's indexer region, i.e. into indexer block `blk * 2048 // 38016` at offset `blk * 2048 % 38016` — fp8 key rows or the fp32 scale region of whatever request owns that block. The decode kernel (`TAIL_BLOCK_ELEMS` / `KPOOL_HEAD`) and the AMD seed kernel already address the tail through `stride(0)` / `stride(1)`; only the NVIDIA seed kernel did not, and the existing regression test for exactly this layout was `skipif(not is_rocm)`.

**Why it shows up as "the cached system prompt is broken".** Only indexer blocks with id below `num_blocks * 2048 / 38016` (~5% of the pool) can be hit, and those are the ids handed out first after startup, i.e. the blocks of the first prefix-cached prompt, typically a long-lived system prompt. Every later request whose tail block id falls in `[19, ~19 * k]` overwrites part of that prompt's indexer blocks `1..k`; prefix-cached blocks are never recomputed, so the damage persists and accumulates, on every TP rank identically. The MLA KV itself is untouched (all writes stay inside the layer's indexer region), so the effect is a corrupted sparse top-k selection for any context longer than `index_topk` (2048). The predicted signature is therefore: with prefix caching on, requests that hit a long-lived cached prompt degrade over time while the same prompt sent with a `cache_salt` (fresh, high block ids) stays correct even on repeated cache hits, and all TP ranks are affected identically. The reproduction below confirms exactly this.

**Fix.** Pass `TAIL_BLOCK_ELEMS = tail.stride(0)` and `KPOOL_HEAD = tail.stride(1)` to the NVIDIA seed kernel (same as the AMD kernel), assert the expected view layout in `kpool_seed_tail_cache`, and run `test_prefill_seed_honors_padded_tail_block_stride` on every platform.

**Origin.** The tail cache has aliased the indexer tensor with a padded, strided view since the tail spec was introduced on the GLM-5.3-Flash development branch (07-28); the prefill seed was a torch fancy-index scatter (`tail[block_ids, 0, offsets] = k`, stride-correct) until it was replaced by this Triton kernel with dense addressing (08-17, "perf: indexer eager path tail seed and scatter"). The kernel reached main unchanged with #53906 and is unchanged in the current main, so every NVIDIA build since #53906 is affected.

**Not a duplicate.** #56059 adds a `NUM_TAIL_BLOCKS` out-of-range guard to the same kernel for a ROCm fault (#56037); it does not change the addressing, and the two changes compose. No other open PR touches the NVIDIA seed kernel's addressing.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py -q
```

Kernel-level repro (SM103): build the runtime tail view with `create_kv_cache_views(KpoolTailSpec(block_size=4, num_kv_heads=2, head_size=128, dtype=bf16, page_size_padded=38016), ...)` over a sentinel-filled 256 x 38016 B buffer, seed one 6-token request whose tail block is 200 (and 18), then inspect which bytes changed.

End-to-end byte-level probe (GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 on 4 x GB300, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, `enforce_eager`, prefix caching on, `num_gpu_blocks_override=800` so the block pool wraps every ~130 requests): an offline `LLM` serves a 14.5k-token system prompt of 420 "vault -> access code" records, then `collective_rpc` snapshots the indexer K cache pages and the tail cache of the prompt's blocks on rank 0. Eight rounds of 50 unrelated filler prompts (200-2000 tokens each) follow; after every round one lookup question re-hits the cached prompt (keeping it hot in the LRU) and the cached pages are diffed against the snapshot taken right after the first request. Finally seven lookup questions are asked against the hot cached prompt. Same script, same seed, on main and on this branch.

Request-level reproduction against a running server (OpenAI API only, no GPU introspection): same 14.5k-token registry prompt, 7 lookup questions, then batches of 100 unrelated filler prompts (150-1500 tokens, unique prefixes, concurrency 16) each followed by the 7 lookups (cache hit), then the same prompt with `cache_salt` twice. Server: main, TP4, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, `enforce_eager`, `--num-gpu-blocks-override 800` so the block pool cycles quickly (with the default pool the same script needs several thousand fillers).

## Test Result

Kernel-level repro, tail view `stride = (19008, 512, 128, 1)` elements:

| kernel | tail block | own tail block seeded | bytes written (layer indexer region) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 200 | no (still sentinel) | `[409600, 411648)` = indexer block 10, fp8 rows 230..245 |
| main | 18 | no | `[36864, 38912)` = indexer block 0 scale region + block 1 rows 0..6 |
| this PR | 200 | yes | `[7603200, 7605248)` = block 200, bytes 0..2048 |
| this PR | 18 | yes | `[684288, 686336)` = block 18, bytes 0..2048 |

`pytest tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py`: on main the un-skipped `test_prefill_seed_honors_padded_tail_block_stride` fails (`tail[3, 0, 2]` is still the sentinel); with this PR 29 passed, 1 skipped (ROCm-only preshuffle test).

End-to-end probe. Runtime views match the analysis: indexer `k_cache` `[7200, 32, 132]` uint8 stride `(4224, 132, 1)` (800 blocks x 9 DeepGEMM pages) and `tail_cache` `[800, 2, 4, 128]` bf16 stride `(19008, 512, 128, 1)` share one `data_ptr`. The system prompt occupies indexer blocks 1..13; the 38 fully cached pages of blocks 1..5 were watched.

| filler requests since the prompt was cached | main: cached pages modified | main: bytes modified | main: re-hit lookup | this PR: pages modified | this PR: re-hit lookup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | 16 / 38 | 18.4 KB | correct | 0 | correct |
| 100 | 21 / 38 | 28.6 KB | correct | 0 | correct |
| 150 | 21 / 38 | 36.7 KB | wrong code | 0 | correct |
| 200 | 24 / 38 | 41.6 KB | correct | 0 | correct |
| 250 | 25 / 38 | 45.7 KB | wrong code | 0 | correct |
| 300 | 25 / 38 | 47.8 KB | no code | 0 | correct |
| 350 | 27 / 38 | 58.0 KB | wrong code | 0 | correct |
| 400 | 30 / 38 | 64.1 KB | no code | 0 | correct |

Final seven lookups against the hot cached prompt: main 1/7 correct, with garbled answers such as `vault harbor-harbor-7` and `raven-saffron-203? No, wait`; this PR 7/7 correct. The modified regions on main are contiguous 2048 B runs (e.g. page 9 offsets 0..2816), i.e. one misplaced tail seed per filler request, and on main the very first request already writes 2048 B into indexer block 0 (the null block); neither happens with this PR. In a shorter server-based run on main (default pool of 9259 blocks, only 120 fillers, no wrap-around) the cached prompt was still answered correctly, which is consistent with the sparse per-request damage: each filler misplaces one 2048 B chunk, so a hot prompt degrades as the free list keeps cycling through the low block ids, while a `cache_salt` copy of the prompt (fresh, high block ids) is never hit.

Request-level reproduction on main (correct lookups out of 7; `/metrics` confirmed 96768/101978 prompt tokens served from the prefix cache in every re-hit pass):

| pass | correct |
|---|---|
| fresh prefill | 7 |
| cache hit, before fillers | 7 |
| cache hit after 100 / 200 / 300 / 400 / 500 / 600 fillers | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| same prompt with `cache_salt` (fresh blocks) | 7 |
| salted prompt again (cache hit) | 7 |

After the fillers the model no longer even reads the question correctly (`vault velvet-tundra-143` for `velvet-tundra-67`, `they haven't specified which vault`, `the human turn is empty`): the cached prompt is unusable while the salted copy of the very same prompt is fine.

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation and the patch; every changed line was reviewed and the tests above were run by the submitter.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] Keep the Engram tables in host memory on ROCm
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's Engram n-gram tables are the largest single consumer of device memory — 47.2 GiB per rank at TP=4, about a third of everything the weights hold. CUDA moves them to pinned host memory and reads them over UVA (#56512); on ROCm two `is_cuda()` gates turn that off, so `engram_config` stays `None`, `amd/model.py` falls through to the base `Engram`, and the tables stay on the accelerator.

Nothing in the offload path is platform-specific — `get_accelerator_view_from_cpu_tensor()` already dispatches on `is_cuda_alike()`, and `hipHostRegister` backs pinned host memory — so widen the two gates and import `Engram` from `..nvidia.engram`, as `amd/model.py` already does for `DeepseekV41ModelState`. No new AMD code. The `cpu_offload` tests in `tests/kernels/test_engram.py` carried the same gate and are widened too. `DPSharedEngramStorage` and the DP head sharding arrive with the import but stay inert at `data_parallel_size=1`.

Duplicate-work check (2026-09-18): #56512 (merged) built the NVIDIA offload and left these gates behind; #56926, #57195 and #56757 continue that path and none touches `amd/` or the gates — #56757's `disk_offload_dir` requires `cpu_offload=True`, so it is blocked on ROCm by the same gate. #56400 has an AMD/ROCm section with no engram item. Prior art: SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#3217 by @functionstackx reached the same design as a local patch for an MI355X TP2 recipe, and recorded that hardware evidence was the outstanding gate before upstreaming. `vllm/config/engram.py` is also edited by those three, so this needs a rebase onto whichever merges first.

## Test plan

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py -q
python -m ruff check vllm/config/engram.py vllm/config/vllm.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py tests/kernels/test_engram.py
python -m ruff format --check vllm/config/engram.py vllm/config/vllm.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py tests/kernels/test_engram.py
git diff --check

# MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, TP=4, one session per arm, warmup then 3 reps
vllm serve $MODEL --tensor-parallel-size 4 --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --trust-remote-code --moe-backend aiter \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-model-len 33792 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --endpoint /v1/completions --model $MODEL \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 512 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 8 --seed 1234 \
  --ignore-eos
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 \
  --num-shots 5 --max-concurrency 64

# DP shared storage, TP=2 / DP=2
vllm serve $MODEL --tensor-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"dp_shared_memory":true}' ...
```

## Test result

- `tests/kernels/test_engram.py` on gfx950: the two `cpu_offload` tests are the reason for the test change in this PR. Their gates were `is_cuda()`, so on ROCm the whole file was 9 passed / 75 skipped and the offload path had no coverage at all. Widened to `is_cuda_alike()`, `test_engram_lookup_matches_torch` (2 cpu_offload x 2 background x 3 token counts) and `test_engram_head_shards_reconstruct_checkpoint` (2 cpu_offload x 4 TP sizes) give **20 passed**, including the bit-exact comparison against the torch dequant reference reading from pinned host memory.
- The alias is coherent on gfx950, which is what the stricter `is_uva_available()` proposed in #57404 probes for: host writes made after the accelerator view is taken are visible to the device, and device writes are visible to the host, for uint8 and float8_e4m3fn at 4 KiB and 1 MiB.
- ruff check, ruff format --check and `git diff --check` pass on all four files. mypy and pre-commit were not run — neither is installed on the test host.
- TP=4 serving: the offload log line appears once per rank per layer (8 lines, 23.60 GiB each), and `Resolved Engram configuration` appears at all, which it does not on base.
- TP=2 / DP=2 with `dp_shared_memory`: server comes up and serves, four shared allocations of 47.21 GiB logged as "shared across DP replicas", 190 GiB resident in `/dev/shm`, no errors. That run is also the only one that reaches `verify_model_config()`, the second gate, since only an explicitly supplied `--engram-config` gets there. Functional check only; no DP performance claim is made.

## Model evaluation

`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, all 1319 problems, five-shot, concurrency 64, MI355X TP=4:

| | accuracy | invalid rate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| base | 0.8999 | 0.15% |
| this PR | 0.9030 | 0.08% |

+0.31 pp against a 1.16 pp standard error for the difference of two proportions, z = 0.27. The acceptance band was fixed before the run. A second offload build measured 0.9052 (z = 0.46); see the note under Performance.

## Performance

The prefetch is what keeps this free. In the shape Engram actually issues — 3 n-gram orders x 6 local hash heads = 18 rows of 256 B per token, in 2 of 40 layers — a UVA gather matches HBM at decode batch sizes and falls behind only at prefill batch sizes:

| tokens/step | rows | UVA view | HBM | delta |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 18 | 9.3 us | 10.7 us | -1.4 us |
| 32 | 576 | 9.9 us | 9.8 us | +0.1 us |
| 256 | 4608 | 25.6 us | 9.9 us | +15.7 us |
| 1024 | 18432 | 89.0 us | 10.3 us | +78.7 us |

The model-owned prefetch stream, with `background=True` leaving half the SMs to the main stream, covers the last two rows.

**KV cache capacity**, TP=4, identical across three independent starts:

| | base | this PR | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Available KV cache memory | 107.8 GiB | 154.38 GiB | **+43.2%** |
| GPU KV cache size | 4,325,113 tokens | 6,194,599 tokens | **+43.2%** |
| Max concurrency @ 33,792 ctx | 127.99x | 183.32x | **+43.2%** |

Predicted from the startup memory breakdown beforehand as +43.8%; the measurement met it within 0.4%.

At TP=2 / DP=2 each rank carries a wider engram shard (47.21 GiB per layer instead of 23.60), so the same change is correspondingly larger. Both arms are the same topology and flags; the base arm simply cannot be given `--engram-config`, because that is the gate this PR widens:

| | base | this PR | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Available KV cache memory | 57.65 GiB | 151.45 GiB | **+162.7%** |
| GPU KV cache size | 2,313,707 tokens | 6,078,307 tokens | **+162.7%** |

The startup breakdown pins down what moved: per rank, "consumed memory (weights + non-torch)" is 182.05 GiB on base and 87.62 GiB with the offload, a difference of 94.43 GiB against the 94.42 GiB the two engram shards occupy at this TP.

**Serving throughput**, TP=4, random 4096 in / 512 out, 32 prompts, concurrency 8, three repetitions each (mean +/- sd). "paired" is the offload arm measured back to back with base in one session; "shipped" is this PR's exact diff, measured separately:

| | base | offload, paired | offload, shipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| mean TPOT | 11.35 +/- 0.02 ms | 11.35 +/- 0.02 ms | 11.35 +/- 0.00 ms |
| median TPOT | 11.22 +/- 0.01 ms | 11.24 +/- 0.02 ms | 11.24 +/- 0.00 ms |
| p99 TPOT | 12.54 +/- 0.01 ms | 12.54 +/- 0.02 ms | 12.56 +/- 0.01 ms |
| mean TTFT | 796.88 +/- 2.43 ms | 794.08 +/- 0.35 ms | 799.97 +/- 1.61 ms |
| p99 TTFT | 1061.31 +/- 1.69 ms | 1054.38 +/- 2.59 ms | 1063.68 +/- 4.60 ms |
| output throughput | 620.64 +/- 0.97 tok/s | 621.10 +/- 1.06 tok/s | 620.61 +/- 0.11 tok/s |

Paired against base: +0.46 tok/s on a pooled standard error of 0.83, t = 0.55. Shipped against the same base: -0.03 tok/s, -0.005%. Flat either way, p99 included. There are two offload columns because the paired arm reached the offload path through the local copy of `nvidia/engram.py` described above, which is not the diff here; the shipped diff reproduces it exactly, down to the same KV cache figures and offload log lines.

Host cost at TP=4: 47.2 GiB x 4 ranks = 188.8 GiB of pinned host memory, against 2954 GiB of RAM on the test node. Containers need `--ulimit memlock=-1`.

AI assistance was used for this change. Every changed line was reviewed by the submitter, and the measurements above were produced by the submitter on the hardware named.

title: [Qwen4Exp][ROCm] PLE n-gram table CPU offload
body:
## Purpose
- Enable `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` on the AMD/ROCm path: keep the Qwen4Exp PLE n-gram table in pinned host memory, read through a UVA view on the GPU.
- Free VRAM so `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` (FP8 table ~51 GiB) / `Inferact/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (bf16 table ~102 GiB) serve on one MI300X with the table entirely in host RAM.
- Keep the pinned lookup behind a custom op (`qwen4_exp_amd_ple_ngram_embedding_pinned`) with `mutates_args=["output"]` so the large embedding weight is never materialized by `torch.compile` (Inductor autotuning builds a bf16 copy of the table during compile, which OOMs on AMD setups without enough VRAM) and the op survives aot_autograd/Inductor.
- Move the PLE embedding storage classes to `qwen4_exp/common` so the AMD and NVIDIA paths share one implementation (NVIDIA re-exports).
- Relax the PLE enable gate to `is_cuda_alike()` so ROCm is accepted, matching the existing NVIDIA default (`VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` defaults on for both; `=0` opts out). Also, my local testing shows little to no performance loss for PLE offload while saving a good chunk of VRAM for more KV cache.
- Why this is not duplicating existing PRs: 
  - #54371 (merged — source of the UVA offload code, ported here)
  - #55040 (AMD FP8 PLE, different approach: FP8 storage + forward dequant vs load-time bf16 fold; no offload/prefetch)
  - #55334 / #54070 / #54129 (nvidia + mmap — complementary).
- AI assistance: developed with opencode+deepseek-v4-flash+vllm; the submitting human reviewed every changed line and ran the tests/evals.

## Test Plan
- `uvx --from ruff==0.14.0 ruff check <changed files>`; `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` (incl. mypy).
- `python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py -q` on ROCm (MI300X) — 52 passed, including compile and cudagraph-capture regression tests for the pinned lookup op.
- Offload-vs-device correctness: same prompt with `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=0/1`, top-8 logprobs bit-identical (max diff 0.0).
- Eval: 1× MI300X, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`, `--max-model-len 262144`, table pinned (weight_device=cpu), CPU KV offload tier.
- Offload ON vs OFF head-to-head (8192 ctx, identical engine): prefill TTFT, decode, and burst are equal within noise; the offload's value is VRAM, not speed.
- An async side-stream prefetch variant was prototyped and measured on the clean config (64k-token non-repeating prefill, default cudagraphs): TTFT difference was a wash vs the synchronous lookup and decode was identical, so this PR ships the synchronous version.

## Test Result
- 52/52 PLE tests pass on ROCm; offload-vs-device logprobs max diff 0.0; "17*23" → 391.
- Needle-in-haystack at 105k and 209k tokens recalled exactly; GPU KV pool 1.57M tokens (6.0× for 262144) on one MI300X.
- Perf: offload ON vs OFF at 8192 — TTFT (6144-token prefill) 0.33s vs 0.33s, decode 8.8 vs 8.9 tok/s (eager) / 87 vs 86 tok/s (default cudagraphs at 262144), 8-way burst 2.4s vs 2.4s. No measurable offload cost.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Retain offload mappings after unsafe KVCR startup failure
body:
## Purpose

If KVCR startup fails while its native thread is still running, the teardown path still unmaps the offload region — `CPUPrimaryTierOffloadingManager.shutdown()` calls `SharedOffloadRegion.cleanup()`, and `TieringOffloadingSpec.get_manager()` only logs a failed `tier.shutdown()` before continuing. NIXL has that memory registered, so the NIC can complete writes into pages the process has already unmapped and reused: corruption, not a leak.

KVCR now signals this case with `KVCRStartupError` (ai-dynamo/kvcr#43). This translates it into `OffloadingStartupError`, hands the affected buffers to `retain_until_exit()`, and skips the unsafe cleanup. A leaked mapping in a process that is failing to start beats corrupting one that isn't. Ordinary failures keep their existing cleanup, and interrupts still propagate as themselves.

Requires the paired KVCR change; the worker-side mapping is untouched, since NIXL registers the separate scheduler-side view.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_kvcr_tier.py
```

Both tests extend existing files and are parametrized over the three paths that must differ: an ordinary `RuntimeError` (cleanup runs), the startup error (buffers retained, cleanup skipped), and `KeyboardInterrupt` (retained, re-raised unchanged). One covers `TieringOffloadingSpec`, the other the KVCR tier; the latter asserts on a real `mmap` and `memoryview` rather than mocks.

## Test Result

All passing. Note `test_kvcr_tier.py` is gated by `pytest.importorskip("kvcr")`, so it needs an environment with the kvcr package to exercise.

No model evaluation: startup failure handling only, with no effect on the offload data path or generated output.

---

title: [EPLB] Add EPLB support to dspark draft models (DeepSeekV4)
body:
## Purpose
Enable EPLB for DSpark draft models on DeepSeek V4.

DSpark MoE drafters now implement MixtureOfExperts, so EPLB can register and rebalance draft experts alongside the target model when using --enable-eplb with DSpark speculative decoding. 

Dsv4.1 Dspark draft is not supported because EPLB requires target and draft models have the same number of routed experts.
Add logging of draft models to distinguish eplb run of target and draft models.

Scope / what does not need changes:

- Other DSpark drafts (Qwen3, Gemma4, K3 MLA) — dense drafts with no MoE layers; EPLB on the draft is N/A. If the target is MoE, existing target-side EPLB is unchanged.
- DSV4 DSpark on AMD/XPU those platforms don’t yet expose MixtureOfExperts on the target path either.

## Test Plan
- test_dspark_draft_registers_mixture_of_experts — draft model exposes MixtureOfExperts
- test_eplb_registers_dspark_draft_model / test_eplb_skips_dspark_registration_with_dummy_weights — EPLB controller registers DSpark draft
- test_v2_load_model_registers_dspark_speculator_with_eplb — v2 GPU model runner wires speculator EPLB at load

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Implement get_top_tokens() on the ROCm DeepSeek V4 MTP drafter
body:
## Purpose

Enabling `speculative_config.use_local_argmax_reduction` with a `deepseek_v4` draft model **fails
engine startup** rather than falling back to the full-vocab path:

```
ValueError: use_local_argmax_reduction is enabled but draft model DeepSeekV4MTP
does not implement get_top_tokens().
```

Both opt-in sites probe the draft model with `hasattr(model, "get_top_tokens")` and raise when it
is missing (`vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py:1606`,
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py:387`), and `DeepSeekV4MultiTokenPredictor` implements
only `compute_logits`. So the flag is a trap for every `deepseek_v4` checkpoint: it does not run
slower, it does not start.

`model_type: deepseek_v4` is rewritten to `DeepSeekV4MTPModel` by its own branch in
`SpeculativeConfig.hf_config_override`, which the registry resolves to the per-platform
`DeepSeekV4MTP`, so the generic MTP drafter fix in #56995 does not reach it.

**Fix.** Forward to `LogitsProcessor.get_top_tokens()` from both the predictor and the wrapper in
the ROCm implementation (`amd/mtp.py`), mirroring the `compute_logits` pair already in the file.
The `nvidia` and `xpu` drafters are not changed: this was verified on MI355X only, so they are
left to a follow-up that can be tested on that hardware.

V4 reaches its LM head through `hc_head` over the `(T, hc_mult, D)` residual and then the shared
head's RMSNorm, unlike V3 (`shared_head` alone) and V3.2 (an already-normed hidden state). Running
a different transform returns a *different draft token* instead of failing, so that transform is
factored into `_pre_head()` and shared by `compute_logits` and `get_top_tokens` rather than written
twice.

`use_local_argmax_reduction` defaults to `False` and gates every call site, so the default path is
unchanged.

## Test Plan

Hardware: MI355X (`gfx950`), HIP 7.2.53211, torch 2.11.0. Measurements ran against a substrate
built from upstream `releases/v0.27.1` (the sha the host's build names) plus that build's compiled
extensions; in the region this PR touches, v0.27.1 and `main` differ only in how the shared-head
RMSNorm kernel is re-exported, so the arms transfer. The two arms are one tree differing in exactly
one file (`diff -r`).

1. **Unit tests** (added, ROCm only; the module skips before importing the ROCm drafter elsewhere):
   `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dsv4_mtp_local_argmax.py`, asserting that the token
   `get_top_tokens` selects carries the row maximum of the full-vocab logits. Re-run on a v0.30.0
   substrate after rebasing onto current `main`.
2. **Falsifiability**: the same tests run against the merge base, and against two deliberately
   wrong implementations — the shared-head RMSNorm dropped, and `hc_head` dropped.
3. **Micro, TP=2**: both arms as methods on the same predictor over a real TP process group with
   the real `hc_head` op, RMSNorm kernel, `ParallelLMHead` and `LogitsProcessor`, swept over draft
   batch. Four pairs per point, pair 0 discarded, arm order alternated.
4. **e2e, TP=2**: `vllm bench serve` on `DSV4-base-tpl`, fp8 KV cache, 1024 in / 512 out, 300
   prompts, `--max-concurrency 68`. Four interleaved pairs, pair 0 discarded.
5. **GSM8K A/B**: `lm_eval --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5`, greedy, all 1319 items,
   `enable_prefix_caching=False`, per-sample logging, **with a base-repeat control** (`base2`, a
   second run of the same build) so the noise floor is measured rather than assumed.

## Test Result

**Unit tests.** 3 passed. All 3 fail on the merge base. Dropping the shared-head RMSNorm fails 2 of
3; dropping `hc_head` fails 2 of 3. The norm gain is `normal_(1.0, 0.5)` and the `hc_head`
scale/base are non-trivial on purpose: an argmax is invariant to RMSNorm's per-row rescale, so a
default all-ones weight could not detect a skipped norm at all.

**Micro (TP=2).** This is a trade-off with a crossover, not a uniform win, so the crossover and the
absolute per-step cost matter more than any median over the sweep:

| shape | crossover (draft batch) | worst cost below | best saving above |
|---|---|---|---|
| hidden 4096, vocab 129280 | 36 → 44 | bs=6: +80.8 µs/step (−42.7 %) | bs=1028: −2496.6 µs/step (+80.1 %) |
| hidden 7168, vocab 129280 | 12 → 20 | bs=6: +29.6 µs/step (−12.4 %) | bs=1028: −2511.1 µs/step (+71.9 %) |

**Token agreement is 1.0000 at all 32 swept points**, on both the selected index and the selected
logit value. The crossover had to be recomputed for V4 rather than carried over from #56995's V3
numbers, and it differs between the two V4 shapes.

**e2e (TP=2, concurrency 68, above the crossover).** No change in either direction:

| metric | base | patched | pairwise median | pairwise range |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total tok/s | 1935.13 | 1929.16 | −0.17 % | −0.92 … +1.26 % |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 31.25 | 31.22 | +0.55 % | −0.73 … +0.62 % |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 30.37 | 30.48 | −0.07 % | −1.72 … +0.89 % |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 584.73 | 588.33 | −1.11 % | −1.59 … −0.33 % |
| Acceptance length | 1.31 | 1.31 | −0.11 % | −1.08 … +0.67 % |

That is the expected result, and it is worth stating why rather than leaving it to be read as a
disappointment: the micro saving at the batch this run reached is 84.7 µs, while the measured
engine step is 40.83 ms (mean TPOT 31.25 ms × acceptance length 1.31), so the predicted e2e effect
is **+0.21 %** — an order of magnitude below the pair-to-pair spread. The e2e arm can show that
nothing regressed; it cannot resolve the win. Pair 0, had it been kept, would have read +8.41 %,
because the base arm alone rose from 1775.6 to 1935.1 tok/s between pair 0 and pair 1 on AITER JIT
warmup. Unchanged acceptance length is the e2e-level statement that the draft tokens did not
change.

**GSM8K (1319 items, 5-shot, greedy).**

| arm | strict | flexible |
|---|---|---|
| base | 0.9515 ± 0.0059 | 0.9507 ± 0.0060 |
| base2 (same build, control) | 0.9522 ± 0.0059 | 0.9530 ± 0.0058 |
| patched | 0.9500 ± 0.0060 | 0.9492 ± 0.0060 |

Effect (base → patched) is −0.0015 strict against a noise floor (base → base2) of +0.0008; both are
well inside the ±0.0059 stderr. Per-sample agreement is the sharper test and needs the same
control: base vs base2 produce identical text on **36.5 %** of items, base vs patched on **36.0 %**
— indistinguishable. Same-verdict rates are 98.1 % and 98.2 %. Two runs of one build already
disagree on most generations because vLLM's batching makes bf16 reductions batch-shape dependent,
so without the control column the 64 % of differing prompts would read as a regression. Claim: no
measurable accuracy change on GSM8K within the base-repeat noise floor — not bit-exactness.

**Not covered.** GSM8K exercises one shape of one path and says nothing about long context,
sampling or multi-turn.

---

AI assistance: the patch, its tests and the measurements above were produced with Claude via
Cursor, and reviewed by the submitter. Found by
[Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom).

title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Overlap mHC coefficients for small TP batches
body:
## Purpose

Overlap shifted mHC coefficient generation with attention/FFN on small batches. The decoder keeps one post/pre path: the existing mHC dispatcher
selects overlap or native execution, while the decoder joins the coefficient
stream before consuming its outputs.

`supports_mhc_overlap` in `.ops.mhc` requires SM100/DeepGEMM, no ubatching,
and compatible projection dimensions: hidden width divisible by 64, and
`hc_mult * (hc_mult + 2)` a positive multiple of 8 no greater than 32.
The exact H5120/hc4 restrictions and helper assertion are removed.
Compatible tensor/data/pipeline/expert-parallel configurations, attention backends,
and LoRA configurations use the same token cutoff, without a separate performance
allowlist. Larger batches, draft layers, and piecewise/breakable graphs retain
native execution. The cutoff is generalized from the TP4 measurements below;
those measurements do not establish a gain for every newly enabled configuration.

The cutoff is **16 tokens**, based on same-instance paired full-forward
measurements with matching tuned GEMM tactics (three samples per arm):

| Tokens | Native ms | Overlap ms | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4.763 | 4.692 | 1.49% |
| 6 | 6.204 | 5.929 | 4.42% |
| 8 | 6.644 | 6.360 | 4.28% |
| 12 | 7.408 | 7.292 | 1.57% |
| 16 | 7.966 | 7.877 | 1.12% |
| 24 | 9.153 | 9.365 | -2.31% |
| 48 | 11.915 | 12.040 | -1.05% |
| 96 | 15.292 | 15.247 | 0.29% |
| 192 | 18.820 | 18.977 | -0.84% |
| 252 | 20.040 | 20.230 | -0.95% |

All samples are retained; the 24/48-token overlap arms contain outliers
(SD 0.390/0.388 ms). Larger shapes show no reliable useful gain, so keep native
execution there. Selection uses the captured token shape, never actual KV
length. Split-kernel warmup is bounded by the same cutoff.

## Validation

Based on main `17e50b9b76`. Latest validation: **79 GPU tests pass**, covering
exact output parity and changed-input CUDA graph replay across `(hidden_size,
hc_mult)` = `(4096, 2)`, `(5120, 4)`, `(7168, 4)`, plus decoder/reference parity
and graph/batch fallbacks. Pre-commit passes.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k 'overlap_preserves_outputs or decoder_mixes_match_torch' -q -rs
```

Only transient input/scratch tensors (`x`, `mix`, `sqr`) need side-stream allocator
recording. The model retains weights, and callers retain coefficient outputs
until joining the side stream; the helper documents that ownership requirement.

Model/performance measurements below are prior results, not reruns on the new
main base or measurements of every newly enabled configuration.

Measured on GB200×4, model revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`,
FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, TP4, DSpark fixed length 5, and synthetic 100K ±5% KV.
These are fixed-forward GPU latencies; no default-O2 piecewise-serving gain is
claimed. The prior ten-sample native/automatic pair measured 6.206→5.932 ms (4.42%).

The refactored commit's three-sample same-instance native/automatic comparison
measures **6.210→5.928 ms (4.55%)**, with identical inputs, KV and tuned GEMM
tactics. Automatic selection activates all 40 target layers. Both arms have
finite outputs and zero eager/graph, changed-input and restored-input replay
errors. Replay checks do not assert native/overlap full-model bitwise parity.

Prior matched real-weight GSM8K: 1271→1268/1319 (96.36→96.13%; 7 improve, 10 regress).
DSpark acceptance length 3.870→3.874. Local FP64 and serialized/async checks support
the numerical change; full-model hidden states are rounding-sensitive. The
refactor preserves the evaluated kernel math and launch order, so this accuracy
evaluation is reused. Prior same-instance allocator peaks increased 16 MiB allocated
and 74 MiB reserved per rank; this is not a serving-capacity measurement.

The projection-width limit of 32 follows DeepGEMM's device-side output-swizzle
constraint. Newly enabled dimensions have correctness coverage, not additional
end-to-end performance measurements.

## Final-head validation (2026-09-21)

Exact head `479b025e45`, GB200×4, pinned model revision above, TP4 **without
DSpark or all-reduce+mHC fusion**, FlashInfer FP8 attention/MXFP4 sparse indexer.
Baseline uses the same head with overlap disabled before loading.

| Metric | Overlap disabled | Enabled |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Forward-only, KV8704 | 4.727 /4.730 ms (before/after) | 4.657 ms (−1.5%) |
| Real8K/1K C1 mean TPOT | 5.013 ms | 4.992 ms (−0.4%) |
| Median ITL | 5.011 ms | 4.974 ms |
| P99 ITL | 5.228 ms | 6.049 ms |
| Full GSM8K flexible extraction | 1266/1319 (95.98%) | 1271/1319 (96.36%) |

Forward harness: same initialized synthetic weights/KV, five samples ×20
CUDA-graph replays after5s warmup per arm; slowest-rank GPU time, excluding
lm_head/sampling/scheduler/HTTP. All arms pass finite-output and changed-input
replay checks (zero replay error). This is not cross-arm bitwise parity.

Serving: ten exact8192-input/1024-output requests per arm, greedy, C1, two
warmups; FULL_DECODE_ONLY with eager prefill. All requests succeed; candidate
tail bursts in2/10 requests mean this is not a strong serving-speed claim.
GSM8K: lm-eval0.4.12, five-shot chat, greedy, seed123, C8, max output1024;
matching prompts/targets,10 improve and5 regress, strict formatting79.68% both.

**Warmup caveat:** initial overlap-disabled GSM8K reproduced cached FlashInfer
CuTe tactic compilation under strict JIT monitoring. Final arms use identical
startup-only cached-tactic and DeepGEMM split warmup from the existing fix in
#57643, plus identical pinned tactics. Zero monitored runtime JIT afterward;
these workarounds are not part of this PR. No claim of stock-stack zero JIT or
coverage of every newly enabled topology/backend. The79 focused GPU tests
above validate the exact head.

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR found for shifted mHC coefficient/sublayer overlap. #52725 concerns
XPU norm fusion; #42735 changes BF16 shared staging in the older mHC kernel;
#56761 changes GLM JIT warmup; #51802 registers NVIDIA V4 warmup variants.
None implements this scheduling change.

AI assistance was used to implement, benchmark and test this change.

title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Optimize MegaMoE staging and NVFP4 cache gathers
body:
## Purpose

Reduce DeepSeek V4.1 MegaMoE/MegaAttention prefill overhead: tile multiple tokens
per MegaMoE staging program for sufficiently large inputs, and size the NVFP4
gather grid by request count and output capacity. Keep conservative launch
choices for small inputs. Both transformations preserve the existing arithmetic
and add no persistent buffers.

Dispatch uses eight-token staging tiles from 64 tokens, otherwise one token.
On GB200 at H5120, forced eight-token tiles regress 2–16-token kernels, tie at
32, and improve from 64 onward (both scale layouts):

| Tokens | Native staging us | Eight-token tile us |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 16 | 2.400 | 2.752 |
| 32 | 2.880 | 2.816 |
| 64 | 3.328 | 3.136 |
| 128 | 4.672 | 3.296 |
| 8192 | 175.616 | 32.416 |
| 16384 | 348.993 | 60.736 |

NVFP4 gathers retain 128 workers for short rows and chunks of >=16 requests.
Otherwise use `min(2048 // num_reqs, max(128, compressed_capacity))` workers.
At 100K gathered rows, 1/2/4/8-request kernel latency falls by 88%/76%/50%/18%;
16/32 requests are unchanged. The caller passes a view of the compressed region
so SWA workspace does not inflate its capacity. No allocation, device-to-host
synchronization or actual-KV decode dispatch is added.

Kernel sweeps use CUPTI, CUDA graphs and cold L2, checking bitwise equality
before timing. Final branch boundary/stride checks are recorded below.

## Performance and validation

GB200×4, DEP4/MegaMoE/MegaAttention, model revision
`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1.
Earlier paired ten-sample fixed-forward confirmations with matching tuned GEMMs:

| Workload per DP rank | Baseline ms | Candidate ms | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Q16K, KV100K | 415.559 | 400.955 | 3.51% |
| B31Q1 + B1Q8K, KV100K | 224.438 | 207.711 | 7.45% |

Mixed baseline SD 9.124 ms versus candidate 0.697 ms; all samples retained.
The earlier three-sample mixed screen improved 6.14%. B8Q2K improves 1.73%;
decode/draft are essentially unchanged. No new model or workspace buffers.
These are synthetic fixed-forward GPU timings, not serving throughput.

Matched full real-weight GSM8K: 1272→1271 /1319 (96.44→96.36% flexible extraction;
7 improve, 8 regress). DSpark acceptance length 3.8281→3.8289. Real-prefill
traces confirm both changed paths execute. Both accuracy arms carry the separate
sparse-remap correctness guard, which is not included in this PR.

GPU validation at `e2a2356a6229`: **29 staging tests and 24 gather tests pass**.
The gather cases cover 1/8/32 requests, 70/128/129/2051 rows, partial gathers,
non-contiguous request strides, untouched bounds, and CUDA-graph replay after
changing lengths in persistent buffers.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py \
  -k 'fused_input_staging or stages_shared_scale_tma_layout' -q -rs
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
  -k v41_nvfp4_gather_matches_insert -q -rs
```

All pre-commit hooks pass. The follow-up removes only benchmark scripts;
production code and correctness tests retain the validated contents. Final dispatched-kernel checks preserve short gathers
and small staging inputs. At H5120/N64, the final staging comparison is
3.360→3.264 us; the gain near the boundary is modest. At H7168/N64,
3.712→3.168 us supports the same cutoff. Large-input gains remain intact.
The earlier real-weight quality evaluation is reused: this dispatch refinement
preserves the evaluated arithmetic; the narrower view changes launch bounds only.

Validation commit `e2a2356a6229` full-model checks pass with finite outputs and zero
eager/graph, changed-input and restored-input replay errors:

- Q16K: 400.490 ms (three samples), consistent with the earlier confirmation.
- DEP B32 adaptive verification, draft length 5 and seeded lengths 1–6:
  112 total tokens; same-instance original/automatic staging measures
  **18.310→18.285 ms (0.14%)**, with matched inputs, KV and GEMM tactics.
  A post-timing trace confirms all 40 staging calls: summed kernel time
  144.00→112.16 us; MegaMoE time remains 11.703 ms in both arms.

An earlier unpaired B32 check measured 30.287 ms with high spread. It is retained
as an unexplained slow run, not used to estimate the staging effect. The paired
check above isolates staging and does not reproduce that regression. Compilation
is excluded from timing and guarded against during timed work.

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR found for tiled DeepSeek MegaMoE staging or CUDA NVFP4 gather sizing.
#56720 sizes a ROCm FP8 gather grid and explicitly preserves CUDA dispatch;
this change targets the separate CUDA NVFP4 branch. #43592 targets MiniMax-M2
prepared-input fusion rather than this DeepSeek staging kernel. #55109 fixes
block-table strides; #57489 adds gfx950 FP4 attention. Neither implements these
CUDA launch heuristics.

title: [DFlash] Capture the context K/V precompute in the draft CUDA graph
body:
## Purpose

Even when the query forward replays a FULL CUDA graph, the DFlash/DSpark draft step still runs the context K/V precompute (`precompute_and_store_context_kv`) eagerly outside the graph, because the number of context tokens varies from step to step.

This PR captures the context K/V precompute ahead of the query forward in the draft's FULL decode graph. Each graph stores one full verify of context rows per request; rows past the batch are padded with `PAD_SLOT_ID` so they write no K/V, and any prefill context beyond the graph's rows is stored eagerly before replay. The precompute has no host syncs, so every DFlash drafter captures it. The draft attention metadata build stays eager, as before.


## Validation

Capturing the context K/V precompute must not change the speculator's proposals. The checks below therefore compare acceptance and accuracy between this branch's parent commit (`c723a831a8`) and `d8de1d3a2f`, and serving performance against current main, with everything else held fixed.

### Setup

- **Hardware / software:** 4× GB200, FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`.
- **Model:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`).
- **Speculative decoding:** DSpark with 5 speculative tokens and full decode CUDA graphs.
- **Topologies:**
  - **DEP4:** MegaMoE backend with adaptive verification.
  - **TP4:** auto MoE backend with fixed verification.

### Acceptance and GSM8K accuracy

Each pair runs the full GSM8K test set (1,319 identical 5-shot completion prompts) with greedy decoding, concurrency 32, a 1,024-token output cap, and strict answer extraction.

Acceptance length is read from the engine's `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters over the whole run for DEP4. For TP4, it is aggregated from the engine's periodic SpecDecoding log windows over the steady state; the same method is used on both sides of each pair.

| Configuration | Acceptance length, incl. bonus (parent → PR) | GSM8K (parent → PR) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DEP4 | 3.411 → **3.434** | 1234 → 1228 / 1319 (93.56% → 93.10%) |
| TP4 | 3.471 → **3.463** | 1227 → 1219 / 1319 (93.03% → 92.42%) |

- The acceptance deltas are within ±1% and have opposite signs across the two topologies, and the per-position acceptance curves coincide. The captured precompute therefore does not change what the drafter proposes.
- The GSM8K deltas are run-to-run noise: two repeats of the same DEP4 parent configuration scored 0.9219 and 0.9356 (an 18/1319 spread), which is wider than any delta in the table.
- These results establish parity with the parent; they do not claim an accuracy improvement.

<details>
<summary>GSM8K server configuration</summary>

Common flags:

```bash
--reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
--attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128
```

DSpark is configured with 5 speculative tokens.

- **DEP4:** `--data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'`, with adaptive verification enabled.
- **TP4:** `--tensor-parallel-size 4`, with the auto MoE backend and adaptive verification disabled.

</details>

### Serving benchmark

TP4, DSpark (5 speculative tokens, synthetic acceptance length 5.5), random dataset with 128 input / 1,024 output tokens. **Base** is main and **PR** is `d8de1d3a2f`. CPU/step is the host time per engine step, measured with an injected per-step probe.

| Concurrency | CPU/step | TPOT | ITL |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6.77 → 5.03 ms | 1.27 → 1.08 ms (−15.2%) | 6.95 → 5.88 ms (−15.3%) |
| 8 | 6.64 → 5.24 ms | 1.87 → 1.84 ms (−1.6%) | 9.96 → 9.90 ms (−0.6%) |
| 64 | 6.82 → 5.43 ms | 3.90 → 3.87 ms (−0.7%) | 19.97 → 20.01 ms (+0.2%) |

The PR cuts host time per step by 1.4–1.7 ms. At concurrency 1 the step is host-bound, so this carries through to a ~15% lower TPOT and ITL; at higher concurrency the GPU dominates and latency is roughly unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Serving benchmark configuration</summary>

```bash
vllm serve <model> --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":5.5}'

vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --ignore-eos --max-concurrency <1|8|64>
```

</details>

### Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py -q
```

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change: the implementation, the evaluation runs, and this description were produced with Claude Code.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix multimodal embedding merge in Llama 4 and Mistral Large 3 EAGLE drafters
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57630.

Regression from #50417 (first released in v0.28.0): that change marked these drafters as `SupportsMultiModalEmbeddings` so the speculator started routing multimodal batches through their `embed_input_ids`, which had been an unreachable alias of `SupportsMultiModal.embed_input_ids` until then. cc @TQCB

`EagleLlama4ForCausalLM` and `EagleMistralLarge3ForCausalLM` implement `SupportsMultiModalEmbeddings` by borrowing the method object `SupportsMultiModal.embed_input_ids`. That method calls `self._embed_text_input_ids(...)` and reads `self._has_oov_mm_tokens`, both of which live on `SupportsMultiModal`, which the drafters do not inherit. Any multimodal target paired with one of these drafters fails during the first draft prefill (already in the profile run at startup):

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py", line 427, in _run_model
File "vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py", line 507, in embed_input_ids
AttributeError: 'EagleLlama4ForCausalLM' object has no attribute '_embed_text_input_ids'. Did you mean: 'embed_input_ids'?
```

Reproduced on main (bf13ecc) and present in v0.28.0 and v0.29.0 with `RedHatAI/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-quantized.w4a16` + `morgendave/EAGLE-Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct`, TP=4, `--speculative-config '{"method":"eagle","model":...,"num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, default cudagraph mode. The same aliasing exists in `EagleMistralLarge3ForCausalLM`; Model Runner V1 takes the same `embed_input_ids` path.

## Change

Replace the borrowed method with an explicit `embed_input_ids` in both drafters that embeds the draft input ids via `self.model.embed_input_ids` and merges external multimodal embeddings with `_merge_multimodal_embeddings`, the same shape `EagleMistralForCausalLM` already uses. No behavior change for text-only batches.

## Test plan

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py -v   # 21 passed (2 new)
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/llama4_eagle.py vllm/model_executor/models/mistral_large_3_eagle.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py
```

New test `test_mm_capable_drafter_merges_multimodal_embeddings` (parametrized over both classes) checks text-only embedding and the merge of multimodal rows; it raises `AttributeError` on main.

E2E (4x NVIDIA L4, TP=4, TRITON_ATTN, `RedHatAI/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-quantized.w4a16` + `morgendave/EAGLE-Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct`, `num_speculative_tokens=3`, `max_patches=4`, 18 text + 12 image prompts, greedy, 48 new tokens):

| build | cudagraph_mode | text AL | image AL | image per-pos acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main @ bf13ecc | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | startup crash (`AttributeError: ... '_embed_text_input_ids'`) | | |
| main + this PR | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | 2.637 (328 drafts) | 2.424 (238 drafts) | 0.710 / 0.445 / 0.269 |
| main + this PR | NONE | 2.674 (322 drafts) | 2.413 (240 drafts) | 0.708 / 0.446 / 0.258 |

Image prompts now draft with acceptance close to text prompts, i.e. the drafter is receiving the image embeddings.

## Disclosure

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate and draft this change; every line was reviewed and the tests were run by the submitter.

title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Fuse TP all-reduce with mHC input preparation
body:
## Purpose

Fuse TP all-reduce, mHC post mixing, delayed collapse, and RMSNorm at DSV4.1 decoder boundaries. This replaces three launches with one, preserves the BF16 boundaries, and retains coefficient overlap. The kernel reuses the existing MNNVL workspace without an additional persistent communication allocation.

Enabled by default for eligible SM100 TP4 forwards with 1–16 tokens, including speculative decoding. The selector requires hidden size 5120, hc_mult=4, EP disabled, and a multicast workspace; it does not restrict DP/PP size, LoRA, or attention backend. The existing overlap-support checks still apply, including disabling overlap for ubatching. Larger batches and graph boundaries use the existing operations. Sixteen is the largest size with a validated gain, not a measured crossover.

Builds on #57603, now merged into main, which overlaps coefficient computation but does not fuse collectives. This differs from #51244's terminal mHC/head fusion. Open-PR searches for `mhc allreduce` and `mhc fusion` found no duplicate of this decoder-boundary collective fusion.

The independent startup warmup fixes have been extracted: DeepGEMM mHC projection coverage is in #57843, and cached FlashInfer MXFP8 tactics are in #57842. Neither is included in this fusion PR.

## Communication choice and token cutoff

Keep multicast and the 16-token cutoff. A controlled GB200 TP4 experiment replaced multicast stores with explicit stores to each of the four peers, retaining the same math, Lamport synchronization, cleanup, and PDL. Push did not consistently improve performance:

| Tokens | Multicast kernel | Push kernel | Multicast model forward | Push model forward |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 14.348 µs | 14.634 µs | 4.054 ms | 4.060 ms |
| 8 | 14.395 µs | 14.972 µs | 5.724 ms | 5.728 ms |
| 16 | 13.910 µs | 15.795 µs | 7.133 ms | 7.130 ms |

Kernel timings use cold-L2 CUDA-graph replay, five samples of 50 replays, and the maximum rank time. Model timings use the same synthetic-weight model instance, KV8704, identical tactics, and three samples of 20 replays; they exclude the output head and serving. Multicast and push model outputs were byte-identical on every rank at all nine tested sizes (1–128).

Extending fusion to 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, and 128 tokens regressed model-forward time in this screen, despite isolated kernel gains; coefficient overlap remained disabled above 16. Some nonstandard sizes used default tactics because exact cache buckets were absent. A follow-up using normal serving autotune buckets confirmed the gain at 1 and 16 tokens (4.667→4.060 ms and 7.783→7.127 ms). Near-boundary runs at 17 and 20 tokens failed the unfused baseline's native-top-k correctness check, so no timings from those shapes are accepted. This supports retaining 16 conservatively; it does not establish the exact crossover. No new model accuracy evaluation was run for the experimental variants.

Multicast requires a supported NVLink/NVSwitch configuration and successful group memory setup; GPU generation alone does not establish support. Explicit peer stores could broaden support to Hopper-or-newer systems with suitable peer-memory access without multicast. That would require separate allocation/dispatch support and hardware validation: this PR remains SM100 TP4, and the experimental push variant reused the existing workspace. Push is a possible portability fallback, not a demonstrated GB200 performance improvement.

## Latest model-forward comparison against main

Measured candidate `dd63c1fa00` (runtime source identical to the subsequently merged PR head `7be123b000`) versus main `d2983f2f16` fetched at benchmark start, including merged overlap and the latest DSpark block-table fix in both arms. GB200 ×4, TP4/DP1, FlashInfer FP8 attention, MXFP4 sparse-logits indexer, auto MoE, KV8704, max model length 1M. Matched synthetic weights/KV and 210 cached tactics with normal hybrid token buckets. Five samples ×20 full-forward CUDA-graph replays after warmup, maximum rank time per sample; median reported below.

| Mode | Batch | Component / tokens | Main | Candidate | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| No DSpark | 1 | main / 1 | 4.651 ms | 4.055 ms | 12.8% |
| No DSpark | 8 | main / 8 | 6.236 ms | 5.668 ms | 9.1% |
| No DSpark | 16 | main / 16 | 7.806 ms | 7.127 ms | 8.7% |
| DSpark | 1 | main / 6 | 5.867 ms | 5.280 ms | 10.0% |
| DSpark | 1 | draft / 5 | 0.353 ms | 0.344 ms | 2.4% |

DSpark uses fixed draft length5. These are model-forward measurements, excluding the output head, sampling, scheduling, HTTP and acceptance effects. The draft implementation is unchanged, so its small difference is not attributed directly to fusion. All accepted cases pass eager/graph and changed/restored-input replay checks with zero error. Initialization manifests and source/final tactic hashes match between arms.

An additional candidate DSpark B2 target case failed the harness native-top-k score check at layer2; no timing from that shape is accepted, and main B2 was not measured. This run does not establish B2 correctness or new model accuracy. Untimed setup permits compilation and strict JIT checking resumes before validation/timing; neither arm includes the extracted startup fixes #57842/#57843. The comparison measures warmed execution.

## Test Result

GB200 ×4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, TP4/DP1, FlashInfer FP8 attention, MXFP4 sparse-logits indexer, auto MoE, no DSpark. Baseline disables only this fusion before model construction; it includes #57603. Both arms use the same checkpoint, configuration and FlashInfer autotuning cache (all 168 entries reused, checksum unchanged).

The latest polling/RMSNorm follow-up loads peer payloads together and distributes norm partials for local shared-memory reads. PDL completion stays early for multi-token forwards and moves to the end for one token. Compared with the previous fused kernel, a same-instance synthetic KV8704 forward comparison measured B1 4.558/4.588→4.044/4.044 ms, B8 6.014/6.012→5.969/5.979 ms, and B16 7.787/7.782→7.794/7.822 ms. B1 baseline varied between runs (4.184 ms in the prior controlled run), so the largest paired percentage is not a robust gain estimate. B16 is 0.1–0.5% slower in the final screen. Output bytes match on every rank for all three sizes; the final collective test also covers signed-zero sentinel collisions.

The serving and GSM8K measurements below are from the initial fused implementation (`fa59bb3883`). They have not been rerun after this output-equivalent follow-up.

8K input / 1K output serving, concurrency 1, three requests per run, forced output length:

| Run | Mean TPOT | Median ITL | P99 ITL |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline | 4.947 ms | 4.951 ms | 5.034 ms |
| Candidate, initial | 5.361 ms | 4.510 ms | 16.240 ms |
| Candidate, repeat after GSM8K | 4.578 ms | 4.506 ms | 7.676 ms |

The warmed repeat reduces mean TPOT by 7.5%, but the initial candidate had stalls and tail latency remains higher. These short serving runs do not establish a tail-latency improvement. All requests completed, with 8192 input and 1024 output tokens each.

A separate fixed-forward screen measured B8 6.565→6.028 ms (−8.2%) and B16 8.421→7.785 ms (−7.6%). B32 exercises fallback: 11.382→11.353 ms with identical output. These are three-sample synthetic-weight/cache measurements at KV8704, excluding the output head and serving.

Full GSM8K, 1319 questions, five-shot chat, thinking disabled, greedy generation, seed 123, maximum 1024 generated tokens, concurrency 8:

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Flexible extraction | 1267/1319 (96.06%) | 1275/1319 (96.66%) |
| Strict match | 79.08% | 79.98% |

Prompt and target hashes match for every question. Floating-point ordering changes outputs; this is not bitwise model equivalence. The paired results have 11 candidate-only correct answers and 3 baseline-only correct answers.

- Four-GPU collective test passed: changing sizes, all-gather interleaving in the shared workspace, changed-input CUDA-graph replay.
- mHC regression selection: 137 passed.
- 77 saved real operator inputs: maximum relative RMS 2.3e-5 for residuals and 1.5e-4 for normalized inputs.
- CMake `_C_stable_libtorch` build and pre-commit checks passed.



Serving uses max model length 1048576, max sequences 8, max batched tokens 8192, 10 GiB KV cache, prefix caching disabled, Engram CPU offload, and `--compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8]}'`. The sequence cap is a validation setting, not a recipe recommendation.

AI assistance was used for implementation and validation. The human submitter confirmed review and relevant tests for the original submission; the warmup follow-up validation is reported separately below.

## Warmup validation

The sparse-candidate alignment fix and its tests were extracted into #57667. The validation below was run on combined commit `2219a281f8`, before the split, and includes that fix.

The missing mHC specialization was DeepGEMM split=4, not a TileLang epilogue. Warmup now covers splits 1/4/16 for both projection widths on GB200. A fresh-cache test compiled six variants, then successfully checked 26 runtime shapes with further compiler invocations forbidden.

A fresh real-weight TP4 server with `enable_jit_warmup=true` and `--jit-monitor-mode error --jit-monitor-verbose` completed 23 requests (736 generated tokens), spanning 3–8192 prompt tokens and mixed batches of up to eight requests. All four ranks enabled the monitor before requests: zero runtime Triton/TileLang/CuTeDSL JIT events, and no DeepGEMM compiler commands in this run. The 66 focused tests below and pre-commit checks passed.

The original serving measurements above explicitly disabled JIT warmup. These fixes close reproduced intermediate-prefill compilation gaps; they do not establish the cause of the original decode tails or a new steady-state speedup. GSM8K was not repeated for this startup/specialization follow-up, which leaves model arithmetic unchanged.

## Test Plan

```bash
RAY_ADDRESS=local .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py -k all_reduce_mhc -q -rs
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py \
```

title: [Model][Engram] Share host tables across co-located DP replicas by default
body:
## Purpose

`EngramConfig.dp_shared_memory` (#56512) keeps one copy of the CPU-offloaded Engram tables per node instead of one per DP replica, with no per-step Engram DP collectives, but it had to be requested by hand and failed startup whenever its requirements were not met. This PR turns it on by default wherever it can work and falls back otherwise:

- `dp_shared_memory` defaults to unset and resolves to enabled when `cpu_offload` is on, `data_parallel_size > 1` and elastic EP is off. An explicit `true` keeps the existing strict validation.
- Before the layers are built, `can_share_engram_tables` falls back to the existing DP head sharding (same host footprint, one table per node) when the node-local Engram DP group has size 1 (replicas not co-located) or `/dev/shm` is smaller than the full tables: 188.8 GiB for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, against Docker's default 64 MiB. Both cases log a `warning_once` pointing at `--shm-size` / `--ipc=host`. The check compares against the tmpfs total, which is identical on every rank of a node, so no collective is needed to keep the decision consistent.
- The `load_format` allowlist is dropped: `dummy` (`fill_`) and `sharded_state` (`copy_`) write identical bytes into the shared mapping on every rank, so the restriction guarded nothing.

Duplicate-work check (2026-09-19): [#57195](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57195) shares host lookups for SP token owners, [#56757](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56757) backs tables with disk files, [#57491](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57491) keeps tables in host memory on ROCm. None changes the `dp_shared_memory` default or adds a `/dev/shm` fallback.

## Test plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py \
  tests/test_config.py -q -k engram
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/config/engram.py vllm/config/vllm.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py \
  tests/test_config.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files vllm/config/engram.py \
  vllm/config/vllm.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py
git diff --check
```

## Test result

- 68 passed on 4xGB200, including the four-process shared-memory storage tests, the new default-resolution cases (offloaded DP on; no offload, DP=1 and elastic EP off) and the new `/dev/shm`-too-small fallback test.
- Pre-commit, mypy-3.12 and `git diff --check` passed.

## Model evaluation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`dba1be0a`), one GB200 node, DEP4 (TP1 x DP4, EP), DSpark 5 tokens with adaptive verification, **no `--engram-config` flag**. GSM8K 5-shot via MQA, completions API, `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=1024`, n=1319.

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| exact_match/flexible-extract | 0.931 |
| exact_match/strict-match | 0.931 |
| num_request_errors | 0 |

This matches the 0.9303 recorded for the same model on main (2026-09-13). The engine log confirms the default took the shared path on its own: `Resolved Engram configuration: EngramConfig(cpu_offload=True, embedding_across_dp=False, dp_shared_memory=True)`, `Engram node-local DP group size: 4 (TP=1)`, and both tables reported `94.42 GiB shared across DP replicas` with no fallback warning. On the node, `/dev/shm` held 190 GiB and `free` reported 191 GiB shared, one copy of the tables rather than four private pinned copies.

AI assistance was used for implementation, testing, and this draft (Claude Code). Human review of every changed line and independent execution of relevant tests are required before submission.
