title: [KV-Offloading][TP] : Expand replicated_layout detection to multi-group MLA
body:
## Purpose
KV offloading for MLA models + TP need only offload KV values from one TP rank. 
This is controlled by replicated_layout determination in `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/config.py`

Building on top of @almogtavor 's work https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50667 (which was eventually closed) , this PR expand the replicated_layout check to include, 
 - SlidingWindowMLASpec
 - Multi-group MLASpec / SlidingWindowMLASpec
 models. 
 
Notably, 
- deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash
- deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp and 
- zai-org/GLM-5.3
fall in this category. 

### Changes:
 - `AttentionSpec.max_tp_shards: int | None = None`: how many distinct shards this cache splits into across TP. A value of means, all TP ranks are replicas. None means unknown and is treated as not replicated.
    * It's opt-in: no spec class has a default that claims replication, so a layer that forgets it only loses dedup, never correctness. This is the same pattern as MambaSpec.tp_replicated.
    * max_tp_shards=1 is set only where the cache has been checked to be identical on every TP rank:
        * generic MLAAttention (mla_attention.py), which covers the DSv3 / V3.2 / GLM-5.3 latent cache;
        * the DSv3.2 indexer cache (deepseek_v2.py; wk_weights_proj uses disable_tp=True);
        * DeepSeek-V4 attention and indexer caches (deepseek_v4/attention.py);
        * the DeepSeek-V4 compressor state (fused_wkv_wgate uses disable_tp=True);
        * the DeepSeek-V4 SWA cache (sparse_swa.py).
 - `KVCacheConfig.kv_tp_replicas: int = 1` : get_kv_cache_configs sets it through `kv_cache_groups_tp_replicas(groups, tp_size, dcp_size)` - The gcd of each layer's `tp_size // max_tp_shards`, taken per layer through `iter_layer_specs`. A layer counts as 1 if it isn't an attention spec, has no value set, or is DCP-sharded under DCP. 
 - Offloading: replicated_layout requires tp > 1 and kv_tp_replicas == tp. T

#### Justification for adding a KVCacheConfig member 
 MLAAttentionSpec shares `uniform_type_base_spec=FullAttentionSpec`, so one `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` group can mix MLA and GQA layers. `generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config` keeps an arbitrary layer spec, so the value has to be computed before that. Otherwise the scheduler could see an MLA spec and wrongly de-duplicate head-sharded KV.

## Test Plan
Add unit tests.

title: [Bugfix][CPU] Fix DeepSeek V4.1 import without Triton
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57653.

DeepSeek V4.1 fails to import when Triton is unavailable. `sparse_mqa_logits.py` calls `tl.constexpr` at import time, but vLLM's fallback sets it to `None`. This blocks model inspection and causes the MI250 processor tests to fail on main.

Make the placeholder's `constexpr` return its input. This allows modules to define constants without Triton. The real Triton implementation stays unchanged. The existing placeholder tests now cover integer and float values, so no model-specific test or guard is needed.

The error was [reported in #56254](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56254#issuecomment-5644796189). I found no other open PR for this fix.

## Test Plan

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_triton_utils.py \
  -k 'placeholder or no_triton_fallback' -v --tb=short

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=/tmp/deepseek-stub-after \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_registry.py \
  -k DeepseekV41 -v --tb=short

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=/tmp/deepseek-stub-processor \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py \
  -k 'DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash' -v --tb=short

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_triton_utils.py \
  -v --tb=short

pre-commit run --files tests/test_triton_utils.py \
  vllm/triton_utils/importing.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/gumbel.py
```

## Test Result

| Tests | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Placeholder and no-Triton fallback tests | 7 passed |
| Existing DeepSeek registry tests | 2 passed |
| DeepSeek processor cases from the failed CI jobs | 3 passed |

The two updated placeholder tests fail before the patch and pass after it. The existing DeepSeek tests also pass with the model-specific guard removed. All pre-commit checks passed.

The full Triton utility suite has 9 passes and 2 failures on this CPU wheel. Both failures also occur before this patch: `test_single_gpu_backend_keeps_triton` and `test_cpu_backend_alone_disables_triton`. They concern backend detection; the wheel's CPU version changes that path.

Tested on Linux arm64 with Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu and Transformers 5.16.1. The container uses vLLM v0.29.0 CPU native libraries and this branch's Python source. GPU kernel tests were not run locally.

AI assistance: Codex.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Restore the fused query RMSNorm + MXFP8 quantization path
body:
## Purpose

`can_fuse_query_quant` decides whether the DeepSeek-V4.1 attention block may hand `wq_b` a pre-quantized query, letting `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm_quant` do the q/kv RMSNorm and the MXFP8 quantization in one kernel. It probed `linear.input_quant_key`. #53793 renamed that attribute to the private `_input_quant_key` and introduced `get_input_quant_key` as its reader, but this call site was not updated, and it is the last one in the tree still reading the old name. The gate has been unconditionally `False` since that rename, so every layer runs a BF16 `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm` followed by a standalone `MXFP8QuantizeSwizzled` over the query — exactly the pair the fused kernel exists to replace.

Read the capability through `get_input_quant_key`, and pass `launch_pdl` to the fused kernel's launch. The kernel already compiles in `gdc_wait()` / `gdc_launch_dependents()` from its `LAUNCH_PDL` constexpr, but without the launch attribute Triton issues an ordinary launch, so the kernel cannot start before its predecessor retires and the wait is inert. Its siblings `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm`, `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` and the Qwen4 PLE/HC kernels pass both. The fused path is CUDA-only by construction, since `can_fuse_query_quant` returns `False` off CUDA, so the new kwarg is never reached on ROCm.

This restores a lost fusion; it does not change model output. The fused kernel reproduces the separate-kernel FP8 bytes, swizzled scales and normalized KV bit for bit.

## Duplicate-work check

No issue tracks this, so issue-number checks are not applicable. Open-PR searches covered `can_fuse_query_quant`, `input_quant_key`, `get_input_quant_key`, `query_quant deepseek_v41`, `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm`, `launch_pdl triton` and `deepseek_v41 pdl`. Nothing else touches `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/ops/query_quant.py`. #53793 performed the rename that stranded this gate. #55505 extends the same contract with input scales and does not change how the key is read. #48086 also adds a missing `launch_pdl`, but in `deepseek_v4/common/ops/fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py`, for a `TypeError` on non-PDL hardware rather than a lost overlap. #54063 and #53151 teach ROCm AITER kernels to consume `QuantizedActivation` instead of fixing a producer gate.

## Test Plan

```bash
PATH=/usr/local/cuda-13.1/bin:$PATH .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/core/test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/ops/query_quant.py
```

The existing suite already encodes this gate: `test_shared_query_quant_preserves_projection` asserts `can_fuse_query_quant` is true for the two FlashInfer MXFP8 kernels and that the pre-quantized `wq_b` projection matches the BF16 path at `rtol=0, atol=0`. It needs Blackwell plus a FlashInfer that can JIT, so `nvcc` must be on `PATH` or the whole group skips, which is how the regression went unnoticed.

Two standalone harnesses, not included in the diff, produced the numbers below. One times the isolated production chain `fused_wqa_wkv` GEMM → q/kv RMSNorm (+ query quantization) → `wq_b` GEMM and compares outputs bitwise before timing. The other serves the model and sweeps client concurrency, running both code versions inside one job so they share a node, with the order counterbalanced across two jobs.

## Test Result

Standalone commit `20538d465a`, based on `9d75dd4544`. **73 tests passed** in 107 s on GB200. On `main` the same file reports **24 failed**, all of them `test_shared_query_quant_preserves_projection` cases failing at `assert can_fuse_query_quant([linear, linear])`, so no new test was needed. Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including ruff, ruff format, typos and mypy 3.10.

Model output is unchanged. The microbenchmark checked FP8 data, swizzled scales, normalized KV and the downstream `wq_b` GEMM output for bitwise equality against the two-kernel path at all 14 shapes before timing, and the projection test asserts the same at `rtol=0, atol=0`. No accuracy evaluation is claimed, because the change cannot move a logit.

### Performance
Serving: `--tensor-parallel-size 4`, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41` with `indexer_kv_dtype=mxfp4` and `indexer_sparse_logits`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-num-seqs 128`, `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. Client is `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, 1024 input and 256 output tokens, `--ignore-eos` and `--temperature 0` so every request runs exactly 255 decode steps. Concurrency 1 is repeated 10 times and the others 5 times; each cell is the median of per-run medians. The two columns of raw ITL are the two jobs.

| Concurrency | Base ITL (ms) | Patched ITL (ms) | ITL Gain |
|------------:|--------------:|-----------------:|---------:|
| 1   | 5.020 / 5.055   | 4.983 / 5.037   | 0.55% |
| 8   | 6.321 / 6.357   | 6.255 / 6.295   | 1.01% |
| 32  | 8.313 / 8.325   | 8.309 / 8.142   | 1.12% |
| 256 | 12.153 / 12.157 | 12.076 / 12.127 | 0.44% |

All eight paired measurements favour the patched build and swapping the order flips no sign. Concurrency 8 is the most trustworthy row: the two jobs agree at 1.05% and 0.97%, and 48 tokens per step is the shape where the microbenchmark predicts 69.7 us out of a 6.32 ms step, or 1.10%. 


## AI assistance

Claude Code assisted with the investigation, the benchmarks and this description. Juntian Liu requested this PR after reviewing the root cause, the measured gains and the benchmark caveats.

title: [KVConnector][MoRIIO] Support K3 DSpark hybrid READ
body:
## Purpose

Enable Kimi-K3 DSpark support in MoRIIO hybrid READ without changing the wire format.

- Recognize wrapped full-attention groups shared by the target and drafter.
- Exclude speculative scratch blocks when selecting the running Mamba state.
- Bound the decode-only attention tail using padded target rows and drafter lookahead, applying DCP scaling only to sharded attention specs.
- Share `clip_ssm_state_blocks` with NIXL while preserving its existing behavior.

The change is limited to MoRIIO block selection and the shared clipping helper. It adds no scheduler policy, model-runner, or GPU synchronization changes. DSpark requires Mamba `align` mode and a single transferable attention group; unsupported hybrid configurations remain rejected.

## Test Plan

Run the MoRIIO suites separately to isolate their fixtures, then check the shared NIXL helper and KV-load recovery:

```bash
for test in tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_*.py; do
  pytest -q -o addopts='' -p no:cacheprovider \
    -W error::pytest.PytestUnhandledThreadExceptionWarning "$test"
done
pytest -q -o addopts='' -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py -m cpu_test
pytest -q -o addopts='' -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py
```

Validate READ payloads against an independent block-selection oracle, including scratch exclusion, suffix hits, state-only transfers, and untouched destination regions. Run full GSM8K at concurrency 1 with the feature patch rebased onto upstream, without additional scheduler or model-runner fixes.

## Test Result

- MoRIIO unit suites: **207 passed**, including **55** scheduler tests.
- NIXL HMA CPU suite: **97 passed**.
- KV-load failure-recovery suite: **14 passed**.
- Reverting the feature changes reproduces **6 targeted failures**; adjacent controls still pass.
- Independent READ validation: **2,880 transfers across 45 combinations**, with bitwise-equal attention, convolution, and SSM payloads and unchanged sentinel regions. All **64 negative controls** detect incorrect scratch-state selection.
- Full GSM8K, 5-shot, **concurrency 1**, DSpark K4, TP8/DCP1: **1,280/1,319 correct (97.04%)**, with no request errors or empty outputs. All results were independently rescored, and external-hit counters confirm prompt KV transfer.

title: [GLM5.3 Perf] Size the GLM-5 sparse indexer decode workspace, 3072 MiB GPU memory saved
body:
## Purpose

1. Rename `max_model_len` to `max_pool_len` for GLM indexer

2. Size the GLM-5 sparse indexer decode workspace using the pooled sequence length:

`max_pool_len = max_model_len // index_kpool`

This reduces the decode logits workspace without changing model behavior

By default model len `1,048,576` we get 4x memory reduction, namely 3072 MiB memory saved

## Test

Acc covered in current unit test

A sweep through different model len

```py
"""
import statistics

import torch

from vllm.platforms import current_platform
from vllm.utils.deep_gemm import (
    fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits,
    get_num_sms,
    get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata,
)
from vllm.utils.import_utils import has_deep_gemm

TOKEN_LENGTHS = (16_384, 65_536, 262_144, 1_048_576)
KPOOL = 4
BATCH = 4
HEADS = 32
HEAD_DIM = 128
BLOCK_SIZE = 64
WARMUP = 5
REPEATS = 50

# Realistic B300 server configuration. These values match vLLM's defaults on
# GPUs with at least 160 GiB of memory.
MAX_NUM_SEQS = 1024
MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS = 16_384
NUM_SPECULATIVE_TOKENS = 0
PREFILL_WORKSPACE_MIB = 512


def benchmark(run, width):
    for _ in range(WARMUP):
        run(width)
        torch.accelerator.synchronize()

    samples = []
    start = torch.Event(enable_timing=True)
    end = torch.Event(enable_timing=True)
    for _ in range(REPEATS):
        start.record()
        run(width)
        end.record()
        end.synchronize()
        samples.append(start.elapsed_time(end))
    return statistics.median(samples)


def profiled_workspace_mib(width):
    decode_rows = min(
        MAX_NUM_SEQS * (NUM_SPECULATIVE_TOKENS + 1), MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS
    )
    decode_mib = decode_rows * width * torch.float32.itemsize / 2**20
    return max(decode_mib, PREFILL_WORKSPACE_MIB)


@torch.inference_mode()
def run_case(token_length):
    pool_length = token_length // KPOOL
    num_blocks = pool_length // BLOCK_SIZE
    q = torch.zeros(BATCH, 1, HEADS, HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device="cuda")
    weights = torch.ones(BATCH, HEADS, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
    kv_cache = torch.zeros(
        num_blocks,
        BLOCK_SIZE,
        1,
        HEAD_DIM + 4,
        dtype=torch.uint8,
        device="cuda",
    )
    context_lens = torch.full((BATCH, 1), pool_length, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    block_tables = (
        torch.arange(num_blocks, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
        .expand(BATCH, -1)
        .contiguous()
    )
    schedule = get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata(context_lens, BLOCK_SIZE, get_num_sms())

    def run(width):
        return fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits(
            (q, None),
            kv_cache,
            weights,
            context_lens,
            block_tables,
            schedule,
            width,
            clean_logits=False,
        )

    before = run(token_length)
    after = run(pool_length)
    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
    torch.testing.assert_close(before[:, :pool_length], after, rtol=0, atol=0)

    before_ms = benchmark(run, token_length)
    after_ms = benchmark(run, pool_length)
    return before.nbytes / 2**20, after.nbytes / 2**20, before_ms, after_ms


def main():
    if not torch.accelerator.is_available() or not has_deep_gemm():
        raise RuntimeError("This benchmark requires CUDA and DeepGEMM")

    print(f"GPU: {current_platform.get_device_name()}")
    print(f"batch={BATCH}, index_kpool={KPOOL}, repeats={REPEATS}")
    print(
        "server: "
        f"max_num_seqs={MAX_NUM_SEQS}, "
        f"max_num_batched_tokens={MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS}, "
        f"num_speculative_tokens={NUM_SPECULATIVE_TOKENS}, "
        f"prefill_workspace={PREFILL_WORKSPACE_MIB} MiB"
    )
    print(
        "tokens     output MiB          latency ms       speedup  "
        "profiled workspace MiB"
    )
    print(
        "            before   after     before   after             "
        "before   after   saved"
    )
    for token_length in TOKEN_LENGTHS:
        before_mib, after_mib, before_ms, after_ms = run_case(token_length)
        workspace_before = profiled_workspace_mib(token_length)
        workspace_after = profiled_workspace_mib(token_length // KPOOL)
        print(
            f"{token_length:>9,}  {before_mib:>8.2f} {after_mib:>7.2f}  "
            f"{before_ms:>8.3f} {after_ms:>7.3f}  "
            f"{before_ms / after_ms:>6.3f}x  "
            f"{workspace_before:>8.0f} {workspace_after:>7.0f} "
            f"{workspace_before - workspace_after:>7.0f}"
        )
        torch.accelerator.empty_cache()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

title: [ROCm][Perf] Enable DPA+ETP prefill compute/comm dual-batch-overlap for DeepSeek-V4
body:
## Purpose This PR enables prefill dual-batch-overlap (DBO) for DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm in data-parallel deployments: attention DP, experts TP via flattened TP, no EP (e.g. `--data-parallel-size 8`). Today `--enable-dbo` splits a step into two ubatches and runs them as a two-thread ping-pong on a compute stream and a comm stream. However, only the DeepEP-HT prepare/finalize moves its collectives to the comm stream. The naive DP/EP path (`allgather_reducescatter`, used by DP deployments without `--enable-expert-parallel`) runs its MoE all-gather (dispatch) and reduce-scatter (combine) synchronously on the compute stream. Both ubatches therefore serialize, and DBO gives no benefit in prefill. On ROCm this path was also blocked by the microbatching config check. This PR makes the naive DP/EP prepare/finalize hand each collective to the comm stream, using the same compute/comm handoff as DeepEP-HT. While one ubatch's all-gather/reduce-scatter is in flight, the peer ubatch runs attention/MoE compute. It also fixes several DBO correctness issues that DeepSeek-V4 hits on this path. ### Key Changes **MoE prepare/finalize (DBO comm overlap):** - **`MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModular`** (`fused_moe/prepare_finalize/naive_dp_ep.py`): `dispatch()` / `combine_into_output()` now run inside a new `_comm_region()` context. Under an active DBO context, it yields the CPU to the peer ubatch, switches to the comm stream for the collective, and syncs back to the compute stream on exit. Outside DBO, and during cudagraph capture, it does nothing: the collective stays on the calling stream, so non-DBO behavior is unchanged on every platform. The class reports `supports_dbo()` only on ROCm, the only platform where this path has been validated. - **`FusedMoEPrepareAndFinalize.supports_dbo()`** (`modular_kernel.py`): New capability, defaulting to `supports_async()`, so existing implementations behave exactly as before. The synchronous `_prepare` / `_finalize` paths now assert `not dbo_enabled() or supports_dbo()`. The naive DP/EP class keeps `supports_async()` as `False`. This avoids overloading `supports_async()`, which also drives MK-internal shared-expert overlap on every forward. - **`VllmConfig`** (`config/vllm.py`): Allows `allgather_reducescatter` with microbatching on ROCm. **Ubatching fixes:** - **`UBatchWrapper._run_ubatches`** (`v1/worker/gpu_ubatch_wrapper.py`): Eager ubatch threads now call `torch.accelerator.set_device_index(self.device)`, as `_capture_ubatches` already did. A new thread starts on device 0. Without this call, each thread's first `current_stream()` created a stream on GPU 0 and waited on it, so every DP rank put work on GPU 0. That slowed rank 0, and every rank then waited on rank 0 at each MoE collective. This was the main cause of the earlier ~30% regression with DBO. - **`maybe_create_ubatch_slices`** (`v1/worker/ubatch_utils.py`): The last split point (`cu_num_tokens[-1]`, a `np.int32`) is cast to `int` at the source. Previously the numpy scalar reached the DeepSeek-V4 C128A metadata builder and failed Triton specialization (`TypeError: failed to specialize argument of type: numpy.int32`). An explicit `list[int]` `split_point` is now handled as explicit split points instead of being list-multiplied. - **`_make_metadata_with_slice`** (`v1/worker/ubatch_utils.py`): Slices `CommonAttentionMetadata.positions` per ubatch. Without this, startup fails with `positions is required for C128A metadata build`. - **`UBatchContext.token_offset` / `dbo_current_ubatch_token_offset()`** (`v1/worker/ubatching.py`): Exposes each ubatch's row offset in the parent batch. It returns 0 outside DBO. **DeepSeek-V4 (AMD):** - **`DeepseekV4Model.forward`** (`models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py`): Writes `_mtp_hidden_buffer` at the current ubatch's token offset. Previously both ubatch threads wrote from row 0, so the MTP drafter read misaligned hidden states for the step. **Tests:** - `tests/kernels/moe/test_naive_dp_ep_dbo.py`: Covers `_comm_region` handoff, the no-op without DBO, skip during graph capture, compute-stream restore on error, `supports_dbo()` being ROCm-only while `supports_async()` stays `False`, and the default `supports_dbo()` contract. - `tests/v1/worker/test_ubatch_offsets.py`: Covers per-thread ubatch token offsets and Python-int ubatch slice bounds. > [!NOTE] > **`supports_dbo()` vs. `dbo_enabled()`** > > - `supports_dbo()` is a static **capability** of the prepare/finalize class: *can* it run correctly under DBO? It does not depend on the current step. For the naive DP/EP class it is `current_platform.is_rocm()`. It is used only as a guard in the modular kernel: `assert not dbo_enabled() or supports_dbo()`. > - `dbo_enabled()` is per-thread **runtime state**: is the calling thread *currently* inside a ubatch context? It is True only inside the ubatch threads of a step that was actually split. It is used in `_comm_region()` to decide, per call, whether to hand the collective to the comm stream. > > | Platform | Step | `supports_dbo()` | `dbo_enabled()` | Behavior | > |---|---|---|---|---| > | ROCm | not split (below threshold, a DP rank opted out, or DBO off) | True | False | Collective stays on the calling stream (unchanged) | > | ROCm | split prefill | True | True | Collective runs on the comm stream, overlapped with the peer ubatch | > | Others | any | False | False | Unchanged. Microbatching with `allgather_reducescatter` is still rejected at config time. | > > Neither replaces the other. With only `dbo_enabled()`, a synchronous prepare/finalize that never handled DBO could silently run under it. With only `supports_dbo()`, `_comm_region()` could not tell a split step from a normal one. Previously the PR overloaded `supports_async()` to return `dbo_enabled()`, which mixed the two concepts. It also changed MK-internal shared-expert scheduling per thread, because `can_overlap_shared_experts` reads `supports_async()`. ## Trace Comparison (Conc=64, Prefill) Main (DBO disabled): This PR (DBO enabled, **9.25%** faster per layer): ## Test Plan Unit tests: ```bash pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_naive_dp_ep_dbo.py tests/v1/worker/test_ubatch_offsets.py -v ``` Benchmark with SA InferenceX `8k1k` (with `OSL=1`) and `agentic` workloads, using the server launch command below. Main runs use the same command without the three `--*dbo*` flags. ```bash export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S='10800' export VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL='32768' export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER='1' export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION='INT4' export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE='1' export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS='0' export OMP_NUM_THREADS='1' vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --port 8333 \ --served-model-name 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro' \ --trust-remote-code \ --async-scheduling \ --distributed-executor-backend 'mp' \ --kv-cache-dtype 'fp8' \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --data-parallel-size 8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.86 \ --moe-backend 'aiter' \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "rejection_sample_method": "synthetic", "synthetic_acceptance_length": 2.49}' \ --tokenizer-mode 'deepseek_v4' \ --tool-call-parser 'deepseek_v4' \ --reasoning-parser 'deepseek_v4' \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --prefill-schedule-interval 8 \ --long-prefill-token-threshold 16384 \ --max-num-seqs 64 \ --load-format fastsafetensors \ --enable-dbo \ --dbo-prefill-token-threshold 8192 \ --dbo-decode-token-threshold 8192 ``` > [!NOTE] > `--dbo-decode-token-threshold` defaults to 32. With MTP, a 64-request decode step has 256 tokens and would be microbatched, and microbatched decode is ~1.8x slower per token. Setting it to 8192 keeps decode on the regular FULL cudagraph path, so DBO only applies to prefill. Accuracy test with `gsm8k` dataset using `lm_eval`: ```bash lm_eval \ --model local-completions \ --model_args model=/shared/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8333/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=10,max_gen_toks=2048,timeout=60000 \ --batch_size auto \ --tasks gsm8k \ --num_fewshot 5 \ --output_path . 2>&1 | tee -a eval.log ``` ## Test Result ### Unit Tests All tests in `tests/kernels/moe/test_naive_dp_ep_dbo.py` and `tests/v1/worker/test_ubatch_offsets.py` pass. ### Benchmark **Fixed sequence length (prefill only):** > Uses the SA InferenceX `8k1k` workload with `OSL=1` to measure prefill only. This way, the requests received across DP ranks meet the DBO gate in more steps (microbatching is all-or-none across DP ranks). Concurrency | Version | Mean TTFT (ms) | Change | P99 TTFT (ms) | Change -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 1 | Main (DBO disabled) | 922.68 | — | 922.68 | —   | This PR (DBO enabled) | 1000.28 | 8.41% ↑ | 1000.28 | 8.41% ↑ 4 | Main (DBO disabled) | 1005.18 | — | 1220.48 | —   | This PR (DBO enabled) | 1016.20 | 1.10% ↑ | 1289.38 | 5.65% ↑ 16 | Main (DBO disabled) | 2140.47 | — | 3912.48 | —   | This PR (DBO enabled) | 2205.26 | 3.03% ↑ | 3767.09 | 3.72% ↓ 64 | Main (DBO disabled) | 5858.52 | — | 10182.92 | —   | This PR (DBO enabled) | 5477.98 | 6.49% ↓ | 9482.81 | 6.87% ↓ 128 | Main (DBO disabled) | 10858.97 | — | 19695.63 | —   | This PR (DBO enabled) | 10042.61 | 7.52% ↓ | 18934.63 | 3.86% ↓ DBO helps most at high concurrency (`conc=64/128`), where it reduces both mean and tail TTFT by ~4–8%. At low concurrency it adds a small regression, largest at `conc=1` (+8.4%). There the batch is too small to hide the collective, and the split adds overhead. Users can raise `--dbo-prefill-token-threshold` to keep small batches unsplit. **Agentic replay (conc=64):** > DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4 on 8x MI350X, DP8, MTP (3 speculative tokens), prefix caching on. Requests average ~97K prompt tokens and ~620 output tokens. 729 (Main) and 766 (DBO) requests were profiled, with no errors. Version | Output Token Throughput (tok/s) | Change | Mean TTFT (ms) | Change | Mean TPOT (ms) | Change -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- Main (DBO disabled) | 703.40 | — | 2,173.93 | — | 44.69 | — This PR (DBO enabled) | 752.46 | 6.97% ↑ | 2,112.09 | 2.85% ↓ | 43.15 | 3.45% ↓ The earlier ~30% throughput regression with DBO is gone, mainly because of the device fix in `_run_ubatches`. DBO now matches or slightly beats Main on all three metrics. Flat TPOT confirms that decode is not microbatched. Read these results as parity or a modest gain rather than a definitive speedup. Because microbatching is all-or-none across DP ranks, only a small share of steps are split in this workload. ### Accuracy Test Task | Filter | n-shot | Metric | Main (DBO disabled) | This PR (DBO enabled) | Change -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- gsm8k | flexible-extract | 5 | exact_match ↑ | 0.9492 ± 0.0060 | 0.9530 ± 0.0058 | +0.0038 (+0.40%) ↑ gsm8k | strict-match | 5 | exact_match ↑ | 0.9500 ± 0.0060 | 0.9538 ± 0.0058 | +0.0038 (+0.40%) ↑ ---

title: [Bugfix][KVConnector] Finalize saves on steps without a forward
body:
## Purpose
Run `wait_for_save()` on empty scheduler steps. Remove the CPU offload cleanup workaround and reset LMCache save generators between steps.

Empty steps skip `save_kv_layer()`, which previously initialized and reset LMCache’s layerwise save generators. Initialize the list upfront and reset it when binding each step’s metadata so `wait_for_save()` cannot access a missing list or advance stale generators.

#55142 adds a fallback in Mooncake; this calls the save hook for every connector. #48464 adds separate lifecycle helpers.

## Test Plan
```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_kv_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_{kv_connector_lifecycle,lmcache_connector}.py tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py -q
```

49 passed; pre-commit passed.

title: [Bugfix][RL] Load attention sinks through weight_loader for layerwise reload
body:
## Overview

Attention sink writes bypassed parameter `weight_loader` callbacks, leaving stale sink values after layerwise reload during RL weight updates. Register checkpoint-backed sinks with a common TP loader and factory, and route model loading through the registered callbacks.

This consolidates and supersedes #57798, #57801, #57803, #57804, #57805, and #57806.

## Claims

- DeepSeek V4/V4.1, HY-V4, MiMo-V2 (including MTP and Omni MTP), GPT-OSS, Laguna, and Qwen3-DFlash load sinks through their current parameter loader; GPT-OSS preserves MXFP4, Quark and other quantization dispatch.
- The loader partitions global checkpoint heads once, writes the local shard in place, and restores padded heads to `-inf`. The factory initializes sinks to `-inf` and registers the loader.
- Regression coverage checks changed sink values across two layerwise reloads, TP sharding, padding, storage preservation, quantization dispatch and pipeline-stage skips.

## Validation

### Current review revision: `7964a96f87`

Merged upstream `main` at `61d9c777bf` before committing the review fixes. Local Windows / Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu:

- Isolated CPU regression run: **35 passed, 1 skipped** (CUDA case). Runs the exact repository sink test functions with real PyTorch, unchanged production reload modules, and production model loading methods/helpers extracted from source. It bypasses unrelated vLLM startup imports and model constructors, with stand-ins for unrelated configuration/attention/quantization infrastructure. This is isolated verification, not a standard-suite or full-model run.
- The six new DeepSeek V4/V4.1 and HY-V4 dispatch cases (TP ranks 0/1) detect an in-memory mutation that loads correct sink values while bypassing the parameter's current loader. Mutation harnesses remain outside the PR.
- Ruff checks/format, `git diff --check`, SPDX, forbidden-import and test-tethering checks passed.
- Standard `pytest tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k sink -q` remains blocked during startup by missing `uvloop` on Windows. Full pre-commit could not initialize its environments because the configured local proxy is unreachable; commit hooks were bypassed for this revision after the checks above.
- No remote H20, GPU or full-model validation was performed for this review revision.

<details>
<summary>Historical H20 validation before this review revision</summary>

### Previous revision

Environment: H20 Slurm cluster, node `vllm-h20-02`, 2 x NVIDIA H20-3e, driver 580.105.08; Python 3.12.14 / torch 2.13.0+cu130. Compiled extensions come from the per-commit precompiled cu130 wheel built for this PR's base commit (`vllm-0.31.1rc1.dev295+gd4e92ccc3`) with the branch's Python files overlaid, so Python and extensions are from the same commit without a rebuild.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k sink -q` | **41 passed** (GPU node) |
| full `test_weight_utils.py` + `test_reload.py`, this branch | 18 failed, **110 passed**, 14 skipped, 2 xfailed, 7 errors |
| full same two files at upstream `main` (control) | 18 failed, 70 passed, 13 skipped, 2 xfailed, 7 errors |
| failure-name diff, main -> branch | **identical set** (25 names); every additional pass is a sink test |
| `run-precommit.sh` (every hook the diff touches) | exit 0, no file rewritten |
| DCO over the branch range | all commits signed off, `DCO pass` |

The failures are model-download / multi-GPU cases that fail identically before and after the change, so they carry no signal about this PR.

Additional out-of-tree verification (harness deliberately kept outside the PR, results in the review comments): each sink model's real attention module was built from tiny dimensions with dummy weights on H20, for TP=1 and TP=2, and driven through the real layerwise reload lifecycle, asserting the per-rank slice, the `-inf` padding and the preserved kernel storage; the pre-PR loading shape was reproduced as a control and never received the reloaded sinks.

These results were recorded before the current review changes and are not a rerun of the current head.

</details>

## Details

A dedicated sink loader derives shard length from the checkpoint rather than the runtime parameter: DeepSeek pads its runtime sink, so `sharded_weight_loader(0)` would use the wrong shard length. Unpadded sinks use the same loader without reconstructing storage. Checkpoint heads must divide evenly across TP ranks.

The loader keeps the divisibility check and relies on tensor slicing and the default loader for incompatible shapes. Empty checkpoints are no longer explicitly rejected. Lifecycle rationale stays here rather than in long helper docstrings.

Tests in the existing CI-selected `test_reload.py` and `test_weight_utils.py` suites cover actual model dispatch for MiMo MTP/Omni MTP, Laguna, DFlash, GPT-OSS, DeepSeek V4/V4.1 and HY-V4. The DeepSeek/HY-V4 tests replace the current loader and verify the unsliced global checkpoint reaches it exactly once for each load. AST factory-name scanning and redundant empty/padding tests were removed.

No full-model accuracy evaluation, real-checkpoint end-to-end reload, TP>2 or multi-node run was performed. Pipeline parallelism is covered by the skip-path test. Backend-converted sink copies and GPT-OSS expert reload follow-ups are outside this PR; their behavior is unchanged.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Reset SimpleCPU eager-store placement state on MRV2 resume
body:
## Purpose

SimpleCPU eager offload retains each request's accumulated GPU block table and
per-group store cursors. Under MRV2, preemption is reported through
`SchedulerOutput.preempted_req_ids`, while the resumed request is represented
as complete `NewRequestData`. Its `yield_req_data` entry is not marked
preempted, so the eager-store state appends the replacement table to the freed
placement and keeps its old cursors. In the regression, the resumed
three-block request therefore schedules no newly confirmed tail block for
offload instead of scheduling the third block.

When preemption is observed, immediately clear the retained block table and
reset every group cursor before processing any placement data from that
scheduler output. MRV1 resumed-cached requests and MRV2 `NewRequestData` then
consume their complete replacement tables through the same reset site.

The change is confined to eager SimpleCPU store bookkeeping. It does not alter
lazy mode, cache lookup, or eviction policy.

#47234 documents current below-cursor CPU-cache eviction behavior, while
#47235 proposes cursor re-scans for that case. This change is narrower: it
restores the existing preemption reset for MRV2's `NewRequestData`
representation and does not change eviction tracking. #57325 touches the
same files but contains no equivalent reset. #55033 also touches the
manager and scheduler tests for non-prefix-cacheable QSA/lazy sizing, but does
not reset retained placement after MRV2 preemption. #57505 guards
hashless sources at store completion; it is downstream of placement tracking
and contains no preemption reset.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with the current-main refresh,
implementation, testing, and drafting. I reviewed the final diff and the test
results.

## Test Plan

```bash
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::\
test_cached_request_data_resumed_all_token_ids_mrv1_only \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_kv_connector_handles_preemption \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::\
test_priority_scheduling_preemption_and_resumption_when_out_of_kv
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py
```

## Test Result

On upstream `main` commit
`155488d853a0bc42df227dbfc74005b3fd488e94`, the test-only control gives two
passes and two failures: both MRV1 controls pass, while both MRV2 cases return
no store blocks (`[]`) instead of the resumed tail block (`[5]`). The matrix
covers delayed resumption and same-output preemption/resumption.

With this change:

```text

SimpleCPU test directory:  95 passed, 2 skipped
adjacent lifecycle matrix: 13 passed
changed-file pre-commit:  passed
manual mypy (Python 3.12): passed

```

The reviewer-requested simplification removes the deferred reset marker and

runner's resumed placement. The runtime scenario and assertions are unchanged.

All runs above were local CPU runs, finalized on 2026-10-04. The fresh
duplicate search found no other PR that resets retained SimpleCPU eager-store
placement on MRV2 preemption/resume.

Model evaluation: no model-output result is claimed. This is a scheduler-side
placement-bookkeeping fix, and the deterministic regression directly forces

title: [MRV2] Release weight offloader on shutdown
body:
## Purpose

MRV2 leaves its process-global `PrefetchOffloader` alive after in-process shutdown, retaining model layers, pinned CPU weights, and GPU staging buffers. Reset it after device synchronization so the existing teardown can reclaim those resources before another engine starts.

## Reproducer

Save as `/tmp/repro_mrv2_offloader_shutdown.py`:

```python
import gc
import weakref
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

from vllm.model_executor.offloader import (
    PrefetchOffloader,
    get_offloader,
    set_offloader,
)
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner import GPUModelRunner

model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2, 2))
buffer = torch.ones(1)
refs = [weakref.ref(model[0]), weakref.ref(model[0].weight), weakref.ref(buffer)]

offloader = PrefetchOffloader.__new__(PrefetchOffloader)
offloader.module_offloaders = [SimpleNamespace(module=model[0])]
offloader.buffer_pool = SimpleNamespace(_buffers={"weight": [buffer]})
offloader.prefetch_step = 1
offloader._hook_module_forward(0, model[0])
set_offloader(offloader)

runner = GPUModelRunner.__new__(GPUModelRunner)
runner.model = model
runner.speculator = None
runner.cudagraph_manager = None
runner.fast_prefill = None
runner.vllm_config = SimpleNamespace()
del model, buffer, offloader

with (
    patch("vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner.torch.accelerator.synchronize"),
    patch("vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner.torch.accelerator.empty_cache"),
    patch("vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner.free_before_shutdown"),
):
    runner.shutdown()

gc.collect()
print(type(get_offloader()).__name__)
print([ref() is not None for ref in refs])
```

Run:

```bash
.venv/bin/python /tmp/repro_mrv2_offloader_shutdown.py
```

### Main

```text
PrefetchOffloader
[True, True, True]
```

### This branch

```text
NoopOffloader
[False, False, False]
```
## Test Plan

CPU and static checks:

```text
.venv/bin/python /tmp/repro_mrv2_offloader_shutdown.py
.venv/bin/python /tmp/check_mrv2_offloader_shutdown_idempotence.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/offloader/test_prefetch.py -q --tb=short
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_language_model_cache_is_weak.py tests/v1/engine/test_llm_engine_finalizer_is_weak.py -q --tb=short
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py --hook-stage manual
```

Results: deterministic main-versus-branch and idempotence checks passed; 12 CPU tests passed; all file-scoped hooks and Python 3.12 mypy passed.

title: [Bugfix][DSV4.1] Restrict mHC overlap to full CUDA graphs
body:
## Problem and fix

DSV4.1's small-batch eager warmup selected overlap, while breakable PIECEWISE capture selected Mega mHC. That could leave Mega mHC's stream-local barriers uninitialized until capture, causing startup to fail.

Use overlap only during FULL CUDA graph capture, still bounded by the existing 16-token cutoff and hardware requirements. Eager execution/warmup and PIECEWISE execution retain native mHC dispatch (Mega mHC where supported). Eager warmup therefore initializes Mega mHC on the capture stream. FULL replay retains the captured overlap kernels without executing the Python check per token.

The selection checks actual stream capture and excludes PIECEWISE. This works with V2's existing FULL-capture context, which advertises NONE while the runner explicitly wraps the model in `torch.cuda.graph`. CUDA graph runner/context code, AMD model code, and shared model-state code are unchanged. There is no separate warmup helper or cache. Mega mHC eligibility remains centralized in its implementation module.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k decoder_mixes_match_torch -q -rs

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/mhc.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/mega_mhc.py \
  tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py
```

- **20 passed**, 285 deselected on GB200. Decoder/reference parity covers broadcast, pipeline, residual, and Engram entry paths under disabled overlap, eager execution, FULL capture/replay, PIECEWISE, and larger batches. The FULL cases verify overlap is called during capture, never eager warmup.
- Pre-commit passed.
- Fresh-process real-weight GB200 TP4 FULL_AND_PIECEWISE startup/capture passed on all four ranks with capture sizes [1,2,4,8]. Both measured exact8192-input/1024-output C1 requests completed, with no monitored inference-time JIT warnings. Mean TPOT 4.553 ms, median ITL 4.385 ms, P99 ITL 10.368 ms. These two requests are a serving smoke check, not a matched performance comparison or a tail-latency improvement claim.
- Earlier revision's GSM8K 128-example smoke: 126/128 (98.44%) flexible extraction, strict 106/128. Checkpoint revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, TP4, FlashInfer FP8 KV, MXFP4 sparse indexer, greedy, five-shot, thinking disabled. This predates the FULL-only-overlap revision and is not a new accuracy evaluation of it. Eager small-batch execution now uses the existing native path, so cross-path bitwise equivalence is not claimed.

## Related work and AI assistance

Open-PR checks found no equivalent fix for the overlap/Mega mHC warmup mismatch exposed by #57603. #57843 warms standalone DeepGEMM prenorm projection specializations; it does not initialize Mega mHC's stream-local barriers. This PR changes DSV4.1 dispatch policy instead.

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and validation. The human submitter reviewed/tested an earlier revision and requested this FULL-only overlap policy; the revised validation above was performed by the agent.

title: [Bugfix] Profile maximum DeepSeek V4.1 vision features
body:
# [Bugfix] Profile the largest legal DeepSeek V4.1 image patch grid

## Purpose

The profiling dummy assumes a square maximizes vision features. The image-token
budget includes one newline token per LLM row, however:
`tokens = rows * (columns + 1) + 2`. A wider legal image can spend less of the
budget on newlines and produce more ViT patches than the square dummy.

With the Flash defaults (patch 14, downsample 3, budget 1024):

| Image | Size (width x height) | ViT patches | Image-span tokens |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Previous dummy | 1302 x 1302 | 8649 | 994 |
| Legal wide image | 2814 x 630 | 9045 | 1022 |
| New dummy | 42882 x 42 | 9189 | 1024 |

Enumerate LLM row counts, maximize the patch grid under the token budget and
optional aspect-ratio clamp, and avoid the minimum-pixel upscaler changing the
chosen aspect ratio. Runtime image preprocessing is unchanged.

Per review, the mock-based test file has been removed from this PR. Only the
profiling selector change remains; its implementation is unchanged. The earlier
validation covered budgets 64/256/512/1024 and six aspect-ratio configurations,
compared against independently enumerated legal grids, and included the
default-wide-image regression.

## Duplicate Work

On 2026-09-21, searches for open PRs matching `DeepSeek image profiling` and
`"DeepSeek" "most_features"` found no equivalent fix.

## Validation Results

The results below were collected before the test-file removal. No new GPU or
serving run is claimed for this review update. Applicable pre-commit hooks
(including Ruff and mypy) and `git diff --check` passed after the removal.

Base: `3c84ad13ed3f9fcd816bf1d15acb83c28cfa02f9`.

- Focused tests on unchanged main: 24 failures, 1 pass.
- Fixed CPU source with real PIL/torch: 25 passed.
- Both originally modified files passed applicable pre-commit hooks.
- The installed H20 runtime passes all 25 image-processor regressions; the
  combined installed-code suite passes 74 tests (including 46 CUDA/Triton cases).
- Restarted the real Flash TP8 H20 service: encoder profiling completed with
  eight maximum-feature images, and the service became healthy. Identical
  serial HTTP tests passed 10/10 before and after, with 5/5 additional unbiased
  image/color/counting checks passing after restart. Runtime: vLLM
  `0.29.1rc1.dev422+gd05da62e9`, torch `2.13.0+cu130`, real Flash weights,

  The original target module is byte-for-byte identical to the main base above.

The removed test file remains available in the
[pre-removal commit](https://github.com/xijiaat/vllm/blob/cec835cc67de537651594583991fc2e438c98fc2/tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_deepseek_v41.py).

for the current PR head:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_deepseek_v41.py -q
```

On H20, the harness invoked `pytest.main` on this staged file with
`--confcutdir=tests -o addopts= -p no:cacheprovider`, against the actual installed
module. All 25 image regressions passed. The combined suite also included the
separate Engram revision fix and its existing CUDA kernels: 74 passed, 38
deselected, one unknown distributed-marker warning from isolation of conftest.

Real-service smoke: 4 text cases, square/wide/extremely-wide/portrait image
requests, text and image SSE with usage and DONE; then 4 unbiased color questions

The change was developed with AI assistance (OpenAI Codex). The submitting human
has reviewed the changes and confirmed personally rerunning the relevant tests

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][DSv4.1] Disable SWA bounded replay on ROCm
body:
## Purpose

Disable SWA bounded replay on ROCm, where it currently faults the GPU.

SWA bounded replay (#56227, on by default) keeps the sliding-window KV out of prefix caching and rebuilds it after a prefix hit by padding the replayed tokens' slots in the prefix-cacheable groups. Correctness depends on the consuming prefill kernel clamping the window; that clamp landed in the FlashInfer and FlashMLA paths.

The ROCm sparse SWA metadata builders (`DeepseekV4ROCMAiterSparseSWAMetadataBuilder` in both `deepseek_v4/amd/rocm.py` and `deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py`) only gained the `replay_start` kwarg and forward it to the base builder. Nothing on the ROCm prefill path clamps the window, so the first prefix hit that carries a replay start walks off the padded slots and raises `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT`, which takes down the worker and then the engine core:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-6 (Agent handle: 0x5621a810) on address 0x7ba8c13ff000. Reason: Unknown.
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered'
RuntimeError: Engine core process EngineCore died unexpectedly.
```

This adds a ROCm guard alongside the existing model-runner-V2 and prefill-context-parallel guards in `DeepseekV4Attention`. Prefix caching itself is unaffected — the sliding-window cache simply takes part in it again, which is the pre-#56227 behavior. The guard should be removed once the ROCm prefill kernels clamp the window too.

## Test Plan

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 10.0, torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0, Triton 3.8.0, TP=4, `--max-model-len 1048576`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, DSpark speculative decoding, `--moe-backend aiter`.

Single prompt per request at `max_tokens=1`, sweeping input length across the prefill-chunk boundary:

```
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
    --moe-backend aiter --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,...}'
```

## Test Result

Baseline (`swa_bounded_replay` on, the current default):

| Input tokens | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 4,096 | OK |
| 32,768 | `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT`, engine core dies |

A prompt that fits in one prefill chunk passes; the fault appears once the prompt spans more than one chunk. Every fault immediately follows the first launch of `_pad_replayed_slots_kernel`. Setting `AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3` makes the same 32,768-token request pass, which is consistent with reading past the padded slots rather than with a bad constant. `TRITON_HIP_USE_ASYNC_COPY=0` only moves the threshold (32,768 passes, 131,072 still faults), so this is not a Triton async-copy issue.

With this change, on the same build and the same four GPUs:

| Input tokens | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 32,768 | OK (1.4s) |
| 131,072 | OK (5.5s) |
| 262,144 | OK (10.4s) |
| 314,510 | OK (4.3s) |

Zero memory faults, and `_pad_replayed_slots_kernel` is never launched.

End to end, a 16-configuration MI355X AgentX sweep (TP=2 and TP=4, concurrency 1-128) failed every point before this change and runs clean after it, with the accuracy arm reporting gsm8k `em_strict` 0.9750 / `em_flexible` 0.9742 over 1319 effective samples.

No new test is added: the two sibling guards in this function (model runner V2, prefill context parallelism) are likewise untested, and exercising this one requires a ROCm device with the model loaded.

title: [Docs] Add an Engram feature page explaining Engram usage in vLLM
body:
## Description

The docs had no coverage of Engram at all, although several recent PRs landed Engram support for DeepSeek V4.1 and Qwen4Exp. This adds `docs/features/engram.md`, an explanatory page covering:

- What Engram n-gram embedding layers are and how a lookup works (token compression, rolling hashing into prime buckets, FP8 row lookup, gating into the hyper-connection stream).
- Which models carry them (`DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` via `engram_layer_ids`, `Qwen4Exp` via `ple_layer_ids`) and that they are enabled automatically on CUDA-alike platforms.
- The `--engram-config` knobs: `cpu_offload` (pinned host memory + UVA, default from `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD`), `embedding_across_dp` (hash heads sharded across TP×DP), and `dp_shared_memory` (one `/dev/shm`-backed copy per node shared across co-located DP replicas), including requirements and fallback behavior.
- Limitations: no DBO/microbatching for DeepSeek V4.1 Engram, no `dp_shared_memory` with elastic EP, UVA requirement, and that Qwen4Exp PLE honors `cpu_offload` only.

The nav under `docs/features` is auto-globbed by awesome-nav, so no nav changes are needed.

## Not duplicating existing work

Searched open PRs and issues in vllm-project/vllm for `engram` (docs, documentation, engram in:title). All open Engram PRs are code-level perf/bugfix/model work (disk-backed tables, RDMA, SP lookups, packed exchanges); none adds documentation.

## Test commands and results

- `pre-commit run markdownlint-cli2 --files docs/features/engram.md` — Passed
- Verified all factual claims against the implementation (`vllm/config/engram.py`, `vllm/config/vllm.py`, `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py`, `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py`, `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py`, `vllm/distributed/parallel_state.py`).
- mkdocs is not installed in this environment, so a full site build was not run; the page is plain Markdown with a relative link to the existing `docs/cli/README.md`.

## Model evaluation results

Not applicable — documentation-only change with no effect on model output, accuracy, or serving.

## AI assistance

This PR was written with AI assistance (Mistral Vibe). The submitter has reviewed every changed line and will run the docs build before merge.

title: [Bugfix][Engram] Fall back when /dev/shm is absent before sharing tables
body:
Follow-up to #57651. `can_share_engram_tables` called `shutil.disk_usage("/dev/shm")` unguarded, so a host without `/dev/shm` raised `FileNotFoundError` at model construction instead of falling back to per-rank tables. This checks `os.path.isdir(SHM_PATH)` first and reuses `SHM_PATH` from `shm_broadcast` for the remaining `/dev/shm` references. No duplicate PR covers this. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used.

Also flattens `DPSharedEngramStorage._allocate` while touching it: the nested try/except, the `stage` tracker and the manual `finalizer()`/`mapping.close()` rollback become one try/except around the mmap+register step. On a peer failure the locals are dropped (`del tensor, owner, mapping`), so the owner's finalizer unregisters the pages and the mapping unmaps in the same order as before. Error messages carry the exception text instead of a stage prefix. No behavior change.

Test: `pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py tests/test_config.py -k "shm or shared_memory or engram"` -> passed
Test: `pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -k shared_across_dp_replicas` (4x GB200, covers the create/open/mmap/register/pinned failure injections and the mapping lifetime checks) -> 2 passed on the flattened `_allocate`

### Model evaluation

Evaluated with `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` at revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277` on one 4x GB200 node using DEP4 (`TP1 x DP4`, expert parallel) and DSpark with 5 speculative tokens and adaptive verification. MQA GSM8K 5-shot ran through the Completions API with `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=1024`, concurrency 32, and all 1,319 examples. It achieved `0.9325` flexible exact match and `0.9325` strict exact match with 0 request errors in 107.46 seconds. `dp_shared_memory=True` initialized successfully, and both Engram tables were shared across all four DP replicas (`94.42 GiB` per table/layer).

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Explicitly reject FSE=1 with DPA+ETP deployment for DeepSeek-V4
body:
## Purpose

Running DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm with data-parallel attention (`--data-parallel-size 8`) and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` fails during weight loading with an obscure error.

```bash
File "/.../vllm/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py", line 1243, in load_weights
    param = params_dict[name_mapped]
KeyError: 'layers.0.ffn.experts.routed_experts.w13_weight_scale_inv'
```

Fused shared experts are not supported under data parallelism: the fused path has no way to load the FP8 shared expert into the MXFP4 routed slot, so users end up debugging weight loading instead of the configuration.

This PR fails fast at model construction time: when fused shared experts are requested (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`), expert parallelism is off, and `data_parallel_size > 1`, the model now raises:

```bash
ValueError: DeepSeek-V4 fused shared experts (VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1) are not supported with data parallelism (data_parallel_size > 1). Set VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0 to run the shared expert as an unfused FP8 MLP.
```

The check lives in `_fuse_shared_experts_enabled()` in the ROCm-only model file (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py`), so non-ROCm paths are untouched. Configurations where FSE is already silently disabled (e.g. expert parallelism enabled) do not raise.

## Test Plan

Launch the DPA+ETP server with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`.

## Test Result

Directly raise `ValueError` so that users know they need to set `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0` for this scenario, instead of debugging the weight loading code.

---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

title: [SpecDecode] Add LiLiCorr drafter
body:
## What changes

Add `LiLiCorrDraftModel` (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20530) to the existing MRV2 DFlash path. The exported SGLang head reranks global candidate lattices using target embeddings, full-vocabulary log probabilities, draft hidden states and the normalized last committed target context. Both plain and grouped-convolution checkpoints are supported.

The port reuses DFlash2 convolution layers and extracts its existing candidate walk/cache orchestration into a shared helper. Greedy and probabilistic drafting use the current vLLM sampling and rejection machinery. No new scheduler, attention backend or verification algorithm is introduced. Correlator and convolution projections use the draft quantization configuration except for lattice QKV and the split-factor/fused-edge projections. Those retain floating-point weights and `F.linear`; `factor_input_proj`, `out_head` and `in_head` must be excluded during export. Reduced draft vocabularies are outside this scope.

ModelOpt exclusions use checkpoint-local draft layer numbers, while vLLM assigns global runtime layer numbers to draft attention layers. The quantization config now retains its exported exclusions and adds runtime-index aliases before constructing the draft layers. This lets mixed BF16/NVFP4 variants allocate the correct linear method without changing checkpoint names or attention/KV layer identity.

References: SGLang https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37462, DSpark https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46995, DFlash2 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52816. 

### Validation status

PR has been tested on valid LiLiCorr checkpoint using 4xGB200 GPUs. It has achieved identical AL.

title: [Engram] Drop redundant VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD env var
body:
TL;DR the functionality of this env var should now be covered by the engram config args (similar process to attention backend and other configs flags) @ZJY0516

## Motivation

`VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` predates `EngramConfig`, but today it no longer enables any behavior of its own. Its only consumer in the tree was `_default_cpu_offload()` in `vllm/config/engram.py`, the `default_factory` for `EngramConfig.cpu_offload`. No runtime code read it directly: the DeepSeek V4.1 and Qwen4Exp embedding paths branch on `engram_config.cpu_offload`, never on the env var, and `VllmConfig._resolve_and_verify_engram_config` already gives an explicit `--engram-config` value precedence over the env-derived default.

In other words, `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=0` was exactly equivalent to:

```
--engram-config '{"cpu_offload": false}'
```

Consistent with prior cleanups (e.g. attention backend env vars migrated into config), we want to minimize env vars since they are less discoverable, less documented, and invisible in engine configs and hashes. This PR drops the env var and makes the enabled-by-default behavior a plain field default, so `cpu_offload` is now configured solely through `EngramConfig` / `--engram-config`.


## Notes for reviewers

- Default behavior is unchanged: `cpu_offload` remains `True` when no config is passed. `VllmConfig._resolve_and_verify_engram_config` still constructs a default `EngramConfig()` for supported models on CUDA-like platforms.
- Breaking change for anyone setting `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=0` in their environment: the setting is now silently ignored in favor of the default. The flag was not documented in `docs/` and only affects DeepSeek V4.1 / Qwen4Exp PLE models; the replacement is a one-line config flag.
- `dp_shared_memory` validation and the `compute_hash` path are untouched; they already operate on the config field.

## Not duplicating existing work

Checked open PRs before opening this one; related PLE offload PRs (#57497 ROCm PLE offload, #54070 disk offload) add new behavior and do not remove or standardize this env var.

## Testing

- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on all changed files: pass.
- Full pre-commit hook suite on the commit: all pass.
- Direct verification against the changed tree (the local sandbox venv is older than `upstream/main` and cannot import `tests/test_config.py` as a whole, so the module-level pytest run was not possible there):
  - `vllm.envs` no longer exposes `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD`.
  - `EngramConfig().cpu_offload is True`; explicit `cpu_offload=False` respected; `dp_shared_memory=True, cpu_offload=False` still raises `ValueError`.
  - The `--engram-config` CLI parse path (`get_kwargs(VllmConfig)["engram_config"]`) parses `{"cpu_offload": false}` into an `EngramConfig` and round-trips through `EngineArgs`.
  - CI will run `tests/test_config.py` on the updated `test_engram_cpu_offload_default`.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance; the changes were reviewed end-to-end by the submitter.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Reach the fused QSA pre-indexer from the AMD path
body:
## Overview On ROCm, the Qwen4Exp QSA indexer now runs the fused pre-indexer kernel instead of the unfused Gemma RMSNorm / MRoPE / compress / cache-write chain. The kernel is an AMD-path copy of NVIDIA's (`amd/ops/qsa_pre_indexer.py`), as review asked; NVIDIA files are untouched. Follow-up: #59732 ports #57097's main-attention fusion onto this copy. ## Claims - One launch per QSA layer per step for the indexer prepare, replacing 37 (−20% kernel launches per decode step at 8k/1024 c4, TP2). - MI355X TP2 `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`: +3.1% to +9.3% output throughput, largest at 8k/1024 c4; TTFT flat (decode-only change). - No accuracy change: GSM8K 0.9636 → 0.9689 (MI355X). - NVIDIA unchanged: no NVIDIA file in the diff. ## Validation **Unit tests** (gfx950): 24 passed, 8 skipped. ```bash pytest -v -s tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_amd.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_pre_indexer_amd.py ``` - `test_qsa_pre_indexer_amd.py`: fused kernel vs the AMD unfused chain in 8 bf16 configurations (MRoPE and text RoPE, 1-D and 2-D positions, with and without the position cache, state size 4 and 8, a fresh 37-token request, and a 4097-token batch across the tile switch). Query and compressed cache within bf16 tolerance; raw state cache bit for bit. The 8 FP8 cases skip: the AMD indexer cache is bf16-only. - `test_qsa_amd.py`: the fused branch replaces the unfused chain and receives `raw_key_cache.kv_cache` (full width, so the MRoPE position tail is written); an ineligible config keeps the unfused chain; the eligibility predicate over five configs. - Runs in the existing AMD `models_basic` step (`.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml`). **Refactor to the AMD path.** From the first `@triton.jit` on, the AMD copy is byte-identical to the previous head's `common/ops/qsa_pre_indexer.py`. On the same inputs (12 cases: decode at c4/c64, MTP-3 verify, mixed, fresh, tiled; MRoPE and text), every output is bit-equal and the time ratio is 0.98–1.00. **Serving**, MI355X TP2, paired A/B, `control → candidate`: | ISL | OSL | Conc | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT (ms) | Mean TTFT (ms) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 60,000 | 600 | 4 | 118.19 → 121.86 (+3.1%) | 19.34 → 18.39 (−4.9%) | 8,712 → 8,671 (−0.5%) | | 60,000 | 600 | 16 | 152.13 → 154.28 (+1.4%) | 79.44 → 77.79 (−2.1%) | 15,447 → 15,568 (+0.8%) | | 8,192 | 1,024 | 4 | 367.23 → 401.53 (+9.3%) | 9.55 → 8.62 (−9.7%) | 1,385 → 1,378 (−0.5%) | | 8,192 | 1,024 | 16 | 846.90 → 898.96 (+6.1%) | 15.67 → 14.53 (−7.3%) | 3,309 → 3,350 (+1.2%) | ```bash # plus the checkpoint card's ROCm environment and flags, identical in both arms vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --max-model-len 262144 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code vllm bench serve --model amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \ --max-concurrency 4 --num-prompts 32 ``` **Accuracy**, GSM8K 5-shot on the checkpoint card's recipe: | | control | candidate | | --- | --- | --- | | MI355X, flexible-extract | 0.9636 ± 0.0052 | 0.9689 ± 0.0048 |
Launch counts, 8k/1024 c4 decode trace | Kernel | control | candidate | | --- | --- | --- | | `_qsa_pre_indexer_kernel` | 0 | 1,224 | | `_store_qsa_rows_kernel` | 3,672 | 0 | | `_triton_mrope_forward` | 2,448 | 0 | | `_compress_qsa_groups_kernel` | 1,224 | 0 | | `CUDAFunctorOnSelf_add` | 4,896 | 0 | | `bfloat16tofloat32_copy_kernel` | 4,896 | 0 | | `elementwise_kernel_manual_unroll<128,4>` | 4,884 | 0 | | `reduce_kernel<512,1,MeanOps>` | 2,448 | 0 | | `pow_kernel` | 2,448 | 0 | | `bfloat16_copy_kernel` | 2,448 | 0 | | `rsqrt_kernel` | 2,448 | 0 | | `elementwise_kernel_manual_unroll<128,8>` | 9,930 | 3,822 | | `index_elementwise_kernel` | 1,229 | 5 | | `vectorized_gather_kernel<16,long>` | 1,465 | 241 | | **all kernels, launches** | **195,384** | **156,228 (−20.0%)** | | **all kernels, device time** | | **−6.1%** | Before After
## Details - **Why a copy.** Review preferred duplicating the kernel into the AMD path over sharing it in `common/`, so either vendor can change its kernel without re-validating the other. - **The one difference from NVIDIA's kernel.** It selects the state source with two complementary masked loads instead of a pointer-typed `tl.where`, which ROCm Triton rejects (`'tt.addptr' op failed to verify that result type matches ptr type`). Every row comes from one source, so memory traffic is unchanged. Both bases keep `tl.multiple_of`; without it Triton vectorizes differently, the pooling reduction reorders, and the compressed rows stop matching the unfused path bit for bit. - **Launch config on 64-lane wavefronts.** The tile and warp constants came from NVIDIA's 32-lane tuning. A sweep on MI355X over `TILE_T_Q` 1–16, `TILE_H_Q` 1–4 and `num_warps` 1/2/4, from 4-token decode to 16k-token prefill chunks, found no config faster than the current one beyond noise, and 2 or 4 warps slower everywhere. The constants stay; the comment records the sweep. - **Eligibility.** `supports_fused_pre_indexer` is config-shaped (RoPE style, head dim, KV heads, compress ratio). Anything else keeps the unfused chain, which also stays as the numerics reference for the test. - **No CPU/GPU sync** on the hot path: the predicate runs once at init; the kernel takes device metadata only. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

title: [Perf][KV Connector][Mooncake] Pack hybrid/MLA KV into coalesced transfer regions
body:
## Purpose

Mooncake PD currently emits one RDMA descriptor per layer-view × block. Hybrid/MLA caches (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) expand into many views of one packed allocation.

Page-contiguous views stay addressable by layer name so heterogeneous PP can align the shared layers (#56033). Views in the same KV group merge across in-page padding. A run that starts at row offset 0 on both sides is lifted to the full row, so consecutive blocks coalesce. Groups are not merged: they overlay one row and own different block ids. A non-contiguous packed row is one region at the allocation. Mismatched PP rejects that shape. Mamba / KpoolTail stay unpacked. HNC-contiguous FA stays one region per layer.

There is **no extra_config flag**. Handshake carries layer names, group ids, and each view's row offset.

Relative to `origin/main`, `mooncake_connector.py` is +474 / −42 (net 432, under the 500-line RFC bar). No docs change: no new user-facing extra_config.

## Test Plan

```bash
pre-commit run ruff-check --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py
pre-commit run ruff-format --files <same>
pre-commit run typos --files <same>
pre-commit run check-spdx-header --files <same>

# Local Qwen checkpoint stands in for facebook/opt-125m.
pytest --noconftest -p pytest_asyncio \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  -k 'not test_kv_producer_heterogeneous_tp'
```

CPU unit tests cover packed registration, per-group full-row promotion, the row-bound anchor, heterogeneous PP partial spans, and same-PP registration of a non-contiguous packed row.

Same-node PD: DeepSeek-V4-Flash 4P4D, PP=1, TP=4, fp8 KV, block 256, prompt 483 tokens. The PR tree cannot serve this model here, so the coalesce/promote path was ported onto vLLM 0.29 and removed afterward. Prefill `KV Transfer metrics` and decode `external_kv_transfer`.

## Test Result

Unit: packed / coalesce / register filter **21 passed** on the current commit. An earlier run of the three Mooncake connector files was **104 passed** with `test_kv_producer_heterogeneous_tp` deselected (that case fails only when `facebook/opt-125m` is replaced by the local Qwen checkpoint).

DSV4-Flash 4P4D, same node, PP=1, TP=4, fp8 KV, block 256, 483-token prompt, 6 requests. `external_kv_transfer` = 2898 = 483×6. No failed transfers. Registration: `146 layer regions over 1 storage`. Coalesce: `146 aligned regions -> 5 transfer regions` (one run per KV group).

| window | xfer | MB | GB/s | desc |
|--------|------|----|------|------|
| first (includes connect) | 5.9 ms | 25.9 | 4.3 | 18.7 |
| steady | 1.5 ms | 25.9 | 16.9 | 26.7 |

Steady-state TTFT was 0.25 s. The 25.9 MB matches a full-row copy (the previous per-layer span was 18.8 MB and 3.5 GB/s on the same setup). Five groups stay separate, so the descriptor count stays in the mid-20s instead of one region.

Heterogeneous PP (P pp=4, D pp=2, max-model-len 2048) was run on the per-layer alignment before full-row promotion. Shared layers transferred, `external_kv_transfer` = 483, and promotion does not run when the two PP layouts differ.

An earlier full-row revision reported cross-node 781→22 descriptors and ~18 GB/s. That revision collapsed each allocation to its first layer name. It is not what this branch transfers now, and it was not re-run for this update.

## Documentation

No `docs/` update: behavior is layout-driven, no new extra_config.

## AI assistance

Non-trivial assistance from Cursor. I reviewed every changed line. This update ran ruff-check, ruff-format, typos, and the packed/coalesce/register unit tests above, and the same-node DSV4 measurement in the table. Commits include `Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>`.

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Scope DSpark non-causal capability to builder layers
body:
## Summary

`MLAAttentionSpec.merge` unions `non_causal_multi_token_decode` across every layer in a KV cache group. After #55234 a causal target and a DSpark draft can share that group, so the target's metadata builder inherited the draft flag and failed DCP validation even though it only served causal layers.

Resolve the flag from the builder's own layers in `static_forward_context`. Do not fall back to the merged group spec: that is the value that incorrectly marked the target as non-causal.

Command used that fails:
```
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
```

title: [Perf][MoE] Support fp8 combine in FlashInfer one-sided MoE all2all
body:
## Purpose
Forwarding fp8 combine flag to increase perf when low precision is supported in FlashInfer combine

## Test Plan
Use GB300 cluster to A/B test with and without the flag `VLLM_FLASHINFER_MOE_A2A_LOW_PRECISION_COMBINE` on, using DeepSeek-R1-0528 NVFP4, 8k input / 1k output.

## Test Result
- For the microbenchmark, there is a small gain at DEP8 (2–8 us per dispatch+combine, about 1–2%), mixed at DEP4. I ran this with just DeepSeek R1 shapes and a sweep across tokens per rank (benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe_a2a_combine.py)
- Then I did the serving with nsys (DEP4 and DEP8): the combine kernel is about 17% faster on decode-sized calls but slower on large prefill-sized calls. The fp8 kernel uses 191 registers per thread vs 96 for bf16, could be causing slowdown due to spilling for prefill-sized ones.
- I also tried serving without the profiler, DEP8 (2 nodes); fp8 gave +4.0% output throughput and 2.7% lower median ITL vs bf16. I ran that over 4 server launches (bf16, fp8, fp8, bf16) to balance the order with the benchmark running 3 times each.
- Had a small issue in one of the runs because one of fp8 runs hung shortly after the profiler was stopped. No run hung without the profiler.

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Clamp FP8 scales before UE8M0 rounding
body:
## Purpose

Without this PR, [this reproducer][reproducer] crashes during DeepGEMM warmup for `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base` with the DeepGEMM FP8 linear backend.

`QuantFP8._quantize_group_native` previously rounded activation scales to UE8M0-compatible powers of two before applying `_FP8_MIN_SCALING_FACTOR`. For zero or sufficiently small activation groups, the subsequent clamp replaced the rounded value with `_FP8_MIN_SCALING_FACTOR`, which is not a power of two. DeepGEMM requires FP32 scale factors used for UE8M0 packing to have zero sign and mantissa bits, so these clamped scales triggered a device assertion while DeepGEMM packed them.

This PR applies the minimum-scale clamp before UE8M0 rounding. The resulting scale therefore remains at least `_FP8_MIN_SCALING_FACTOR` while satisfying the exponent-only representation expected by DeepGEMM. The non-UE8M0 path retains its existing behavior.

The existing group-quantization edge-case test is extended to cover an all-zero input with UE8M0 enabled. It verifies both the minimum-scale bound and the zero-sign-and-mantissa invariant enforced by DeepGEMM.

[reproducer]: https://gist.github.com/rao-ashish/8a648b7aadbf4380bc3a6e643b1cb471

## Test Plan

Run the targeted `QuantFP8` group-quantization edge-case test:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant_group.py::test_quantfp8_group_edge_cases
```

Run the [reproducer][reproducer] on an NVIDIA GB300 with the DeepGEMM FP8 linear backend and verify that model initialization and DeepGEMM warmup complete without the scale-layout device assertion.

## Test Result

- The targeted pytest test passes.
- Before this change, the reproducer triggers the assertion in `smxx_layout.cuh` that FP32 scale factors must have zero sign and mantissa bits, followed by `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED`.
- After this change, the reproducer completes model initialization and DeepGEMM warmup without that assertion or CUDA launch failure.
- No documentation update is needed because this only corrects existing quantization behavior.

---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>
