title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Optimize low-concurrency speculative KDA
body:
## Purpose

Optimize the active ROCm Kimi-K3 `fused_recurrent_kda_fwd_kernel` for
low-concurrency speculative decoding on MI355X.

The shipped gated configuration uses `BV=32`, `num_warps=4`, and
`num_stages=2`. With Kimi-K3 TP8 (`H=12`, `V=128`) at concurrency 1, this
launches only 48 workgroups for a four-token verification step on a 256-CU
MI355X. This change increases grid parallelism and removes recurrent-loop
runtime work when speculative requests have a uniform query length.

## Changes

- Select narrower V tiles from the number of head-sequences (`H * N`):
  - at most 24: `BV=4`, one warp;
  - 25-96: `BV=8`, one warp;
  - larger multi-sequence grids retain the dynamic path.
- Specialize equal-length speculative batches with a constexpr sequence length.
  C=1 additionally avoids sequence/head division and `cu_seqlens` loads.
- Detect uniform speculative query lengths from existing CPU metadata. Ragged
  batches retain the original dynamic loop. Token-padded graph inputs are
  checked against the packed tensor size before specialization.
- Tune pipeline stages by sequence length: 2 for T=1, 4/8 for T<=3, 6 for
  T<=6, 10 for T<=10, and 12 for longer specialized loops.
- Hoist `exp(A_log)` and `dt_bias` loads out of the token loop.
- Normalize Q/K with `tl.rsqrt` instead of division by `tl.sqrt`.
- Extend the existing KDA and metadata tests with C=1/2/4/8 uniform cases and a
  ragged fallback case.
- Keep static-loop eligibility separate from launch-configuration selection so
  the tuned thresholds and fallback behavior are explicit.

## Why this is not duplicate work

Open-PR searches were run for Kimi-K3, KDA, and `fused_recurrent_kda` work.
This does not duplicate:

- #57753, which tunes the shared `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_kernel`;
- #54103, which proposes routing ROCm Kimi-K3 to ATOM kernels;
- #52988, which adds adaptive variable-length decode plumbing but does not
  specialize this AMD Triton kernel;
- #53525, which optimizes the NVIDIA non-speculative C=1 native/CuTe pipeline;
- #52375 and #56974, which fix launch-grid dimension limits.

If #54103 changes the active ROCm route before this lands, this PR should be
reassessed.

No issue is linked.

## Performance

Fresh validation was run on PR head `ec8d9db6db` with one MI355X (`gfx950`)
using image
`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-d05da62e9ccdf8e342b15bf6785d83224cc165af`:

- Python 3.12.13;
- PyTorch `2.12.0+git6bbd260`, HIP `7.2.53211`;
- Triton `3.7.1`;
- Kimi-K3 TP8 dimensions `H=12`, `K=V=128`;
- BF16 inputs and FP32 recurrent state;
- 69 independent KDA layer launches captured in one HIP graph;
- 30 warmups, then 3 rounds x 100 replays; values below are the median
  microseconds per layer.

These are controlled, within-image comparisons of:

- shipped baseline `79468c20ef` (`4df8dc9a10^`);
- current PR `ec8d9db6db`.

The absolute timings are not directly comparable to the earlier ROCm
10.0/Triton 3.8 measurements in this PR because this validation uses the image
versions listed above.

Representative uniform speculative batches:

| C | Query length | Baseline (us) | Current (us) | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4 | 16.198 | 5.606 | 2.889x |
| 1 | 7 | 27.003 | 9.108 | 2.965x |
| 2 | 4 | 17.545 | 7.451 | 2.355x |
| 2 | 7 | 28.186 | 10.480 | 2.689x |
| 4 | 4 | 18.934 | 10.180 | 1.860x |
| 4 | 7 | 29.448 | 14.551 | 2.024x |
| 8 | 4 | 22.502 | 13.244 | 1.699x |
| 8 | 7 | 34.468 | 19.086 | 1.806x |
| 8 | 16 | 69.085 | 36.727 | 1.881x |
| 8 | 32 | 130.414 | 73.073 | 1.785x |

Non-specialized and fallback paths were measured separately rather than
assuming the uniform-length result applies to them:

| Case | Baseline (us) | Current (us) | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ragged C=2, lengths `[4,3]` | 17.328 | 7.674 | 2.258x |
| Ragged C=8, alternating lengths 7/6 | 34.171 | 20.531 | 1.664x |
| Graph-padding fallback, C=2/T=4 + 4 padded tokens | 17.547 | 7.976 | 2.200x |
| Uniform C=9/T=7, H*N=108 dynamic policy fallback | 34.712 | 33.275 | 1.043x |
| Regular decode C=8 | 8.965 | 8.744 | 1.025x |

## Test results

All fresh GPU results below use the image and PR head listed in the Performance
section.

- `git diff 4df8dc9a10..HEAD --check`: passed.
- Python compilation of the five changed Python files: passed.
- Focused KDA metadata test: `5 passed, 27 deselected`.
  - Uniform C=2/4/8 is detected.
  - Ragged `[3,2]`, regular decode, and no-scheduled-draft-token cases return
    the dynamic-path sentinel.
- Focused AMD speculative-decode correctness:

  ```bash
  pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py \
      -k "test_kda_spec_decode_correctness and amd" -vv
  ```

  Result: `20 passed, 79 deselected`.
- Complete `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py`: `71 passed, 28 skipped`.
- Candidate-versus-baseline kernel validation: 12 case classes x 5 seeds using
  Kimi-K3 TP8 `H=12`, `K=V=128`.
  - Covers uniform C=1/2/3/4/8 through T=32, `fuse_gate=True/False/None`, lower
    bound enabled/disabled, no `dt_bias`, ragged inputs, graph-padding fallback,
    H*N=108 policy fallback, different accepted-token counts, and regular
    decode.
  - Maximum output absolute difference: `1.220703125e-4`.
  - Maximum recurrent-state absolute difference: `2.384185791015625e-7`.
  - No NaN or Inf was observed.
- HIP graph capture followed by 20 replays was stable for uniform, ragged,
  graph-padding fallback, and H*N=108 dynamic-policy paths.
- Pre-commit on all five functional/test files passed on `2a7b3938b7`, before
  the final launch-selection-only refactor. The validation image does not ship
  pre-commit; the final refactor was checked with `git diff --check`, Python
  compilation, metadata tests, the complete KDA pytest file, the correctness
  sweep, and the performance sweep above.
- All three PR commits contain `Signed-off-by` and AI-assistance trailers.

The image does not include `tblib`; pytest was run with the Kimi-K3 test
directory as `--confcutdir` and importlib import mode to avoid the unrelated
repository-root test dependency. No replacement Python packages were installed.

## Model evaluation

A concurrency-1 GSM8K A/B evaluation was run with the same protocol as
[SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX run 34332168553 attempt 3](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34332168553/attempts/3).
Both sides used image
`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-0961bbae2894d574be790d219651824eb199318e`
and the same model, server configuration, prompts, seeds, and evaluator:

- `lm-evaluation-harness` revision
  `b315ef3b05176acc9732bb7fdec116abe1ecc476`;
- GSM8K v3, 5-shot, `local-chat-completions`, and `--apply_chat_template`;
- `num_concurrent=1`, `max_tokens=12288`, temperature 0;
- TP8, `max_num_seqs=2`, DSpark K=6 with the TRITON_MLA draft backend and
  block rejection, FP8 KV cache, and FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graph capture sizes
  2 through 14.

| Revision | Flexible extract | Strict match |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline | 96.97% (1279/1319) | 96.97% (1279/1319) |
| Current PR `2a7b3938b7` | 97.04% (1280/1319) | 97.12% (1281/1319) |
| Difference | +0.08 percentage points | +0.15 percentage points |

All 1319 requests completed on both sides without request failures. For the
strict metric, 16 examples changed from incorrect to correct and 14 changed
from correct to incorrect, for a net gain of two. For flexible extraction, the
net gain was one. These differences are smaller than the approximately 0.47
percentage-point standard error, so this evaluation shows no model-level
accuracy regression.

The earlier custom raw-completions run used a different prompt and a 256-token
output limit, causing truncations and non-comparable aggregate scores; it is
superseded by the evaluation above.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex was used for code editing, benchmark analysis, testing, and drafting
this description. The human submitter must review every changed line and
validate and understand the change end-to-end before requesting review.

title: [Refactor] Abstract DeepGemm MegaMOE backend
body:
## Purpose
Refactor DeepGemm MegaMoE integration behind a DeepGemmMegaMoEBackend abstraction to unblock non-SM100 backends; no behavior change on SM100. The DeepGEMM MegaMoE kernel is a very high-performance MoE implementation, and is expected to be reused by more models and hardware. For example:
- An equivalent MXFP4 MegaMoE on SM90, where the activation quantization scheme has to change to fit the hardware and different precision requirements.
- Today MXFP4 MoE weights are the default; follow-ups will likely need FP8 and other weight formats on top of the current implementation.

This PR adds an abstract DeepGemmMegaMoEBackend so more models can enable the DeepGEMM MegaMoE kernel quickly, and so external vLLM plugins can support more scenarios flexibly.

Main changes:
- DeepGemmMegaMoEBackend currently exposes transform_weights (routed / shared), bf16_mega_gate, run_mega_moe, supports_shared_experts, and supports_bf16_mega_gate; it also abstracts mma_type and the hidden-state activation scheme.
- The existing DeepGEMM usage in DeepSeek V4 and Kimi K3 is moved into DeepGemmSm100MegaMoEBackend, keeping the implementation completely unchanged.
- prepare_megamoe_inputs is extended to support a new quantization mode fp8 with group_k=128 and fp32 scales.

## Test Plan
- On SM100, the code logic is unchanged, including DeepGemmSm100MegaMoEBackend and prepare_megamoe_inputs.
- Test DeepGEMM MegaMoE variant on SM90.

## Test Result
Run TP4+EP on hopper works correctly.
```
INFO 09-21 11:29:57 [__init__.py:90] [vllm_hopper_mega_moe] registered SM90 MegaMoE backend (DeepGemmSm90MegaMoEBackend) for DeepSeek V4.
INFO 09-21 11:29:57 [__init__.py:90] [vllm_hopper_mega_moe] registered SM90 MegaMoE backend (DeepGemmSm90MegaMoEBackend) for DeepSeek V4
```

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Drop -1 sentinels when building the ragged sparse-MLA indices
body:
## Purpose
The sparse MLA kernel (pa_sparse_prefill_opus) currently seg. faults when -1 sentinels happen within accessed region as there is no check for it.

 `combine_topk_swa_indices` reserves top-k columns from a position-derived count and writes `-1` wherever a candidate fails its validity test, and `build_ragged_indices_from_dense` copies the row prefix verbatim, sentinels included.
 
 ## The fix

Make the ragged index stream sentinel-free at the point it is built, so no consumer can dereference one. `build_ragged_indices_from_dense` now keeps only valid entries per row, and `indptr` counts those. Semantically identical, skipping an index and masking it out give the same attention result.

This is layout-agnostic: it does not matter whether the sentinels are leading, interior or trailing. Getting rid of 
"-1" indices should not cause any side-effects as they are supposed to be masked out anyway.

## Tests

GSM8K 5-shot shares a few-shot prefix, so with prefix caching on (the default)
it generates partial hits:

| build | aiter | GSM8K (full 1319, 5-shot) |
|---|---|---|
| without the fix | ToT | **engine crashes mid-eval**, 4x `Memory access fault`, lm_eval aborts |
| with the fix | ToT (`tot_main`, 93 commits past v0.1.22) | **0.9750** strict / **0.9742** flexible, 1319/1319 |
| with the fix | **v0.1.22.post1**, vLLM's pin (`docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base`) | **0.9727** strict / **0.9719** flexible, 1319/1319 |

## Performance

This function is already almost invisible e2e as it is called few times:

For dsv41 flash:

| phase | calls | vs the model's 40 sparse-attention layers |
|---|---|---|
| **prefill** | **40 per chunk** | one per layer, not shared |
| **decode** | **~3 per step** | already shared across layers |

I still did a unit-benchmark to show the fixes do not make this kernel expensive, and kernel count goes from 4 to 3 as no need for clamping (in kernel logic now) and torch zeros is folded into the newly created kernel.

| topk | sliding_window | width | C | upstream | this fix | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | 128 | 640 | 1 | 7.2 us (4 kernels) | 6.3 us (3 kernels) | -0.9 us |
| 512 | 128 | 640 | 64 | 7.4 us (4) | 9.4 us (3) | +2.0 us |
| 512 | 128 | 640 | 128 | 7.6 us (4) | 9.6 us (3) | +2.0 us |
| 512 | 128 | 640 | 1024 | 9.0 us (4) | 10.9 us (3) | +1.9 us |
| 512 | 128 | 640 | 8192 | 32.6 us (5) | 28.4 us (4) | -4.2 us |
| 512 | 128 | 640 | 16384 | 52.7 us (5) | 43.3 us (4) | -9.4 us |
| 1024 | 128 | 1152 | 1 | 7.2 us (4) | 7.3 us (3) | +0.1 us |
| 1024 | 128 | 1152 | 64 | 7.6 us (4) | 11.0 us (3) | +3.4 us |
| 1024 | 128 | 1152 | 128 | 7.5 us (4) | 11.0 us (3) | +3.5 us |
| 1024 | 128 | 1152 | 1024 | 10.8 us (4) | 13.1 us (3) | +2.3 us |
| 1024 | 128 | 1152 | 8192 | 48.2 us (5) | 41.3 us (4) | -6.9 us |
| 1024 | 128 | 1152 | 16384 | 78.2 us (5) | 67.4 us (4) | -10.8 us |
| 2048 | 128 | 2176 | 1 | 7.4 us (4) | 8.6 us (3) | +1.2 us |
| 2048 | 128 | 2176 | 64 | 7.5 us (4) | 12.8 us (3) | +5.3 us |
| 2048 | 128 | 2176 | 128 | 8.1 us (4) | 12.6 us (3) | +4.5 us |
| 2048 | 128 | 2176 | 1024 | 13.9 us (4) | 15.8 us (3) | +1.9 us |
| 2048 | 128 | 2176 | 8192 | 71.6 us (5) | 55.5 us (4) | -16.1 us |
| 2048 | 128 | 2176 | 16384 | 164.1 us (5) | 91.2 us (4) | **-72.9 us** |

E2E runs with dsv41 flash:

ISL=1024, OSL=1024, C=1 with NP=10 and C=32 with NP=320.
Speculative decoding and prefix caching both off, to keep the comparison simple.

(The bug doesnt trigger without prefix caching, no perf delta as expected since this module has very little part in e2e in terms of perf)

| | | upstream | with this fix | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **C=1** | output tok/s | 95.15 | 95.59 | +0.5 % |
| | TTFT mean | 142.14 ms | 142.06 ms | -0.1 % |
| | TPOT mean | 10.38 ms | 10.33 ms | -0.5 % |
| | duration | 107.62 s | 107.12 s | -0.5 % |
| **C=32** | output tok/s | 1885.15 | 1881.40 | -0.2 % |
| | TTFT mean | 894.94 ms | 891.07 ms | -0.4 % |
| | TPOT mean | 16.11 ms | 16.15 ms | +0.2 % |
| | duration | 173.82 s | 174.17 s | +0.2 % |


## Duplicate check

I searched vLLM PRs and issues for `pa_sparse_prefill_opus`, `build_ragged_indices_from_dense`, and "Memory access fault" with DeepSeek V4 sparse attention. No other PR fixes this crash. Related work that is not a duplicate:

- #52628 and #58352 (draft) add `build_ragged_indices_from_dense_out`, which writes ragged decode metadata straight into caller-owned CUDA graph buffers. They don't touch the prefill crash, but they build on `_pack_dense_prefix_to_ragged_kernel`, which this PR replaces. Whichever lands second needs to keep the sentinel-free behaviour, or decode rows will carry `-1` again.
- #55695 hardens the same DSv4 prefill path against chunks with zero query tokens. That's a different failure.
- #48266 is a memory fault on gfx942 (MI325X). It predates the OPUS routing added in #54855, and gfx942 never takes the OPUS path, so it isn't this crash.

## AI assistance

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). I used it to trace the root cause through #54855 and #56228, to help write the kernel changes and the unit test, and to address review comments. I reviewed every changed line and understand the change end to end.

title: [Spec Decode] Enable async scheduling for DFlash
body:
## Scope

Adds `dflash` to the async-scheduling allowlist in `VllmConfig`, on both the explicit `--async-scheduling` path (previously a hard `ValueError`) and the default auto-enable path (previously force-disabled with a warning). The V2 model runner's async machinery (async output copies, GPU-side draft-token buffers) is method-agnostic, and the DFlash speculator consumes the same GPU tensors (`num_sampled`, `num_rejected`, `last_sampled`) as the DSpark one, so no engine changes beyond the allowlist are needed.


## Configuration

No new configuration. With default settings, async scheduling now stays enabled for `--speculative-config '{"method":"dflash", ...}'` instead of being silently disabled. `--no-async-scheduling` still forces it off.

## Launch command

<details>
<summary>vllm serve command used for validation (GB200, TP4)</summary>

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 -tp 4 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --language-model-only \
  --compilation-config '{"pass_config": {"fuse_allreduce_rms": false}}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"TRITON_ATTN"}'
```

(The `fuse_allreduce_rms` workaround is unrelated to this PR: the DFlash2 candidate selector trips a piecewise-compile assert when the allreduce-RMS fusion splits compile ranges at TP4. The TRITON_ATTN draft backend is used because the FLASH_ATTN path is broken for this draft/target pair — FA4-hd256 page-size clash with the hybrid target's mamba-forced KV block size.)

</details>

## Validation

- New unit test `test_dflash_allows_async_scheduling` in `tests/test_config.py`: builds a minimal DFlash2 draft config and asserts async scheduling stays enabled (previously force-disabled). Run: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -k "dflash or async_scheduling" -q` → 5 passed. `pre-commit run --files vllm/config/vllm.py tests/test_config.py` → all passed (ruff check + format included).
- E2E correctness on 4xGB200 TP4, Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B + z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 draft (7 speculative tokens, standard rejection, greedy draft, async scheduling on): GSM8K 5-shot flexible-extract 0.9708 / strict-match 0.9704, matching the no-spec baseline 0.9719/0.9716 and the DSpark draft 0.9708/0.9712. Measured acceptance length 5.96 on GSM8K traffic. Repeated with prefix caching enabled (default): 0.9735 / 0.9735 — the hybrid-mamba + prefix-cache + spec-decode path is also correct.

## Performance

Same-build A/B, bs=1 pure-decode (ISL=1, OSL=1000, 2 warmup + 4 requests, `vllm bench serve`, 4xGB200 TP4, DFlash2 with TRITON_ATTN draft backend fully CUDA-graphed, synthetic acceptance length 6):

| async scheduling | TPOT (mean) | decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| off (`--no-async-scheduling`) | 2.127 ms | 470.2 |
| on (default with this PR) | 1.510 ms | 662.3 |

**+41% decode throughput (1.41x lower TPOT) at bs=1** with DFlash2 enabled.

## Notes

AI assistance was used for this change (code, tests, and validation); all quoted results were produced by actually running the commands above.

Duplicate-work check: `gh pr list --search "dflash async"` and `gh search prs "async scheduling" "dflash"` over vllm-project/vllm return no open or merged PR enabling async scheduling for DFlash; the allowlist in `vllm/config/vllm.py` on master still excludes it. The sibling DSpark was allowlisted in its original PR (#46995); nothing since covers DFlash.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Restore KVCR construction through the secondary-tier factory
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58087.

A standard `type="kvcr"` secondary tier fails to initialize because `SecondaryTierFactory` passes `backpressure_detector=None` even when backpressure is not configured, while `KVCRSecondaryTierManager` does not accept that argument. Consequently, the server exits before it can serve a request.

Accept the optional detector in the KVCR constructor and forward it to `SecondaryTierManager`. Keep the parameter at the end of the existing signature to preserve existing positional arguments. Route the existing KVCR test helper through the production factory and exercise request/load behavior with both default and explicitly configured backpressure.

This restores the constructor contract introduced by [#50045](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50045) after the KVCR adapter landed in [#53624](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53624). Default configurations retain a `None` detector; explicitly configured detectors are preserved rather than silently discarded.

Duplicate checks on 2026-09-22 found no existing issue or PR addressing this constructor mismatch. [#57500](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57500) concerns buffer lifetime after a native startup failure and leaves this signature unchanged.

## Test Plan

Run the focused suites with the optional KVCR package installed:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_kvcr_tier.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_factory.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_backpressure.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py -q
```

The adapted KVCR tests use the real factory with the existing recording backend. They cover construction, configured detector retention, request hints, key/descriptor translation, load completion, and request cleanup.

Changed-file checks:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/kvcr/manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_kvcr_tier.py
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/kvcr/manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_kvcr_tier.py
```

For serving validation, repeat the accompanying issue's Qwen3-0.6B startup command on the same RTX 3090 and send three deterministic `/v1/completions` requests. Compare their generated token IDs with the primary-only reference. Run the repository's required checks on the changed files.

## Test Result

The published fix is commit `ab62868f6f16b4b21ced4655150833100a07cb83`. Its patch is byte-for-byte identical to the validated two-file patch.

Before the production fix, on vLLM source `c723a831a81cb4ff89ea6d61b2d15109306ed1bc`:

- The KVCR suite with its helper routed through the production factory failed all 21 cases with the constructor keyword error.
- The generation-only GPU reproduction with real Qwen3-0.6B weights exited during startup with the same `TypeError`.
- The primary-only control started successfully and returned HTTP 200 for all three completion requests, each generating `[7407, 304, 279, 3283, 315, 12095, 13, 362]`.

Environment: KVCR `0.1.0` at `317e62f301300c101bf9c911e020fb89b35f1583`, NIXL `1.3.2`, Python 3.12.14, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu132`, Transformers `5.16.1`, RTX 3090, FP16. The editable vLLM checkout uses the official cu130 native artifacts from `e9f169d16b9408bb9ae44f75072b91a5521d733c`; the changes between that revision and the tested source contain no C/C++/CUDA source changes. Distribution metadata still reads `0.1.dev648+g1fee69838.precompiled`, while Python source is the `c723a831` checkout plus this patch.

After the fix:

- All six related suites above: **229 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** in 85.55 seconds, including all 21 KVCR cases. There were 14 existing PyTorch deprecation warnings.
- The same real-weight GPU configuration started successfully with the real KVCR/NIXL UCX backend. All three completion requests returned HTTP 200; generated token IDs, corresponding per-token logprobs, prompt token IDs, and finish reasons matched the primary-only reference exactly.
- All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks passed. The manual Python 3.12 mypy check passed as well. `git diff --check` passed.

At submission, the affected constructor, factory, base class, and KVCR tests remain unchanged at upstream `496c6472cb70d5eb8681dadae238d160f5086454`. The test results above use the stated `c723a831` baseline plus this patch.

The single-GPU serving check measures startup and generation. It does not establish cross-node transfer correctness or a broad model-quality evaluation.

---

OpenAI Codex assisted with the investigation, implementation, and execution of the validation reported above.

title: [Model] Decoder-side SWA bounded replay for DeepSeek-V4.1
body:
## Purpose

Decoder-side SWA bounded replay for DeepSeek-V4.1, on top of the encoder side (#56227). The layers past the last KV-source layer (21-39 of 40 on V4.1-Flash) own only sliding-window KV, so in eager prefill steps they run on each request's last 128 tokens, cold prefills included. Simplified re-submission of #56752 (closed); no other open PR implements this.

- `DeepseekV41ModelState.prepare_attn` prepares the kept rows as a sub-batch, the way a microbatch is prepared: one Triton kernel gathers rows, positions, slot mappings and the replay-layer KV start, and the sub-batch gets attention metadata and a forward context of its own. DP ranks agree on whether any rank trims and on every rank's replay token count.
- `DecoderReplayLayers` gathers the layer inputs by those rows, runs the replay layers under that context and scatters the outputs back.
- Only eager steps trim. A step that fits a CUDA graph (up to 1024 tokens by default) keeps the replay layers on its whole batch inside the graph: such steps are launch-bound, so the graph is worth more than the trim. `prepare_attn` already gets the step's graph mode, which DP ranks share, so there are no nested captures, no eager breaks and no runner changes; the diff is confined to `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/`, a config docstring and the CI job list.
- With the fused MoE finalize of #58586, a decode step's cut layer hands its unfinalized `MoEOutput` to the replay layers unchanged, and layer 21's first boundary finalizes it. A trimming step holds a prefill longer than the window, more tokens than any step that defers its finalize, so the trim path only sees tensors.
- Stays off, with a warning, when the PP stage does not hold every layer after the cut, under sequence-parallel MoE, PCP or microbatching, with an Engram layer after the cut, or with a drafter window wider than the target's. `--no-swa-bounded-replay` turns off both sides. A no-op on ROCm.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py
```

- Accuracy: gsm8k 5-shot, n=1319, two passes against one server (pass 2 is all full-prompt prefix hits).
- Performance: `vllm-bench`, random token-id prompts, prefix cache reset before every point.
- Both on V4.1-Flash, TP4 and DP4 x TP1 x EP4 (DEP4), decoder side on vs off with the encoder side on in both (off via a local patch, not in this PR).

## Test Result

Unit tests cover the replay rows and sub-batch metadata (adaptive verification, prompt-logprobs requests, DP agreement), graph steps getting no replay batch, and the gather/scatter with the indexer buffers. pre-commit and mypy are clean.

### Accuracy (GB200, V4.1-Flash)

| arm | pass 1 (cold) | pass 2 (prefix hits) |
|---|---|---|
| TP4, decoder replay on | 0.9249 | 0.9234 |
| TP4, decoder replay off | 0.9303 | 0.9249 |
| DEP4, decoder replay on | 0.9333 | 0.9287 |
| DEP4, decoder replay off | 0.9257 | 0.9181 |

`exact_match/flexible-extract`; one standard error is 0.0072. 0 request errors. On TP4 the fused MoE finalize of #58586 is active, so every decode step passes the cut layer's unfinalized MoE output through the replay layers.

### Performance (GB200, V4.1-Flash)

Saturated prefill throughput with decoder replay stays at 83K-86K tok/s on TP4 and 199K-228K on DEP4 at every prompt length, against 68K-54K and 134K-120K without. From 16K up, prefill TTFT drops 25-36% on TP4 and 37-45% on DEP4 at any concurrency, and TPOT drops up to 29% and 39% at high concurrency.

Decoder replay on / off. TTFT is the prefill-only p50. Each point is one run of 4 x concurrency prompts with the default `max_num_batched_tokens` 16384 (per rank on DEP4) and max CUDA graph size 1024; each arm runs on its own GB200 node, in parallel.

**Regressions.** Only prompts of 8K or less at concurrency 64 or less; the table has every such point on either setup, with decoder replay on vs off.

- A single 1K prompt runs the same code as the baseline, inside the CUDA graph: TP4 matches (55 / 55 ms); DEP4 measures within 1-6%. Trimming such steps, as the previous revision did, took TP4's TTFT from 56 to 110 ms.
- Single 4K-8K prompts cost ~2.7 ms of CPU per eager step: 0.2 ms preparing the sub-batch, ~2 ms building its attention metadata with the same builders the main batch runs every step, 0.5 ms of gather/scatter. Those steps are launch-bound (~175 ms of kernel launches with the GPU waiting on the CPU), so the trim saves no time there. With both TP4 arms on one node the gap is 0-3%; across nodes in the main runs it measures up to +21% on TP4 and +7% on DEP4, with throughput within 5%.
- The larger TTFT p50 swings at concurrency 4-64 change sign between points and setups, with throughput between -5% and +13%.

title: [Bugfix] Preserve padding token types for cross encoders
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58138.

`padding="max_length"` currently extends `token_type_ids` with the last real token's type, so right-padded BERT pairs assign type 1 to padding even when the tokenizer's `pad_token_type_id` is 0. The existing scalar compression also cannot represent the correct `0*1*0*` shape.

This change:

- pads with `tokenizer.pad_token_type_id`;
- compresses token types as the document segment's half-open `(start, end)` range;
- reconstructs that range in both pooling worker paths; and
- adds regressions for padded pairs and invalid disjoint type-1 ranges.

Unpadded `0*1*` inputs retain the same reconstructed token types.

AI assistance was used for implementation and validation.

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py

ruff check --ignore UP038 \
  vllm/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/io_processor.py \
  vllm/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/utils.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/encoder_only.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py

ruff format --check \
  vllm/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/io_processor.py \
  vllm/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/utils.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/encoder_only.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py
```

## Test Result

The source-level reproducer showed the bug before the change:

```text
actual=[0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]
expected=[0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0]
compressed=3
```

After the change:

```text
actual=[0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0]
expected=[0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0]
compressed=(3, 5)
reconstructed=[0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0]
```

The targeted tests pass: `4 passed`. Ruff check and format check pass on the touched files. `UP038` is ignored because `gpu_model_runner.py` has five pre-existing findings outside this diff.

## Real BERT cross-encoder comparison (H200, 2026-10-13)

Executed the actual Python source from main `816173ca9d9256f85c36d09d133a7ed219ccbd8e` and PR branch `13a08eb29f8d3ffd32ecc98aa24a31e715a8504b`, using the same isolated runtime and three query/document pairs. The fixed checkpoint is `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2`, revision `233902d25c440f23af6f7d6e94d2946bac0bee0a`, architecture `BertForSequenceClassification`.

Configuration: H200, FP16 model weights, raw logits (`PoolingParams(use_activation=False)`), eager execution, TP=1, and `attention_config={"backend": "FLASH_ATTN", "flash_attn_version": 2}`.

### Matching padding and masking

HF tokenization used `padding="max_length", max_length=128` for the padded case. vLLM used `tokenization_kwargs={"pad_prompt_tokens": 128}` and produced the same right-padded 128 input IDs on main and branch. Unpadded input lengths were 17, 22, and 18; all six main/branch ID arrays matched exactly.

`pad_prompt_tokens` supplies padding IDs as visible sequence positions in this vLLM path. Therefore the matching padded HF reference explicitly uses an all-ones attention mask and the tokenizer's padding token type 0. This is not conflated with standard HF masked padding. No production attention-mask behavior was changed.

| Pair | Input | Main | Branch | HF matching mask |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | unpadded | 9.265308 | 9.265308 | 9.265625 |
| 2 | unpadded | 7.329526 | 7.329526 | 7.328125 |
| 3 | unpadded | -7.128927 | -7.128927 | -7.128906 |
| 1 | padded to 128 | 7.273251 | 3.266776 | 3.265625 |
| 2 | padded to 128 | 7.249307 | 4.620015 | 4.621094 |
| 3 | padded to 128 | -8.581070 | -3.295383 | -3.294922 |

Unpadded main-versus-branch maximum absolute difference: `0`. Unpadded branch-versus-HF maximum absolute difference: `0.001400948`.

Padded main-versus-HF maximum absolute difference: `5.286148071`; padded branch-versus-HF: `0.001150846`. These are observed numerical differences, not a substituted or loosened test assertion.

As a separate mask control, standard HF masked padding returns `9.265625`, `7.328125`, and `-7.12890625`, matching its unpadded scores. Those masked-padding scores are not claimed to match vLLM's visible-padding requests.

### Runtime and validation boundary

Both source checkouts ran with PyTorch `2.11.0+cu130`, Transformers `5.19.0`, humming `0.1.16`, actual CuTe DSL `4.8.0`, and matching FlashInfer Python/cubin `0.7.0.post1`. No mocks or disabled FlashInfer version checks were used.

The existing vLLM `0.25.1` native extensions were reused for both Python checkouts. This is an actual H200 source-level model comparison, not a fresh build of all native extensions or validation of the main branch's declared PyTorch 2.13 dependency matrix. HF goldens were obtained with the same PyTorch/Transformers versions and fixed checkpoint.

AI assistance was used for environment preparation, execution, and reporting.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] Enable DSpark adaptive verification
body:
## Purpose

Enable confidence-scheduled adaptive verification for `DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` on ROCm.

This PR extends the existing validated ROCm flattened-query mechanism to V4.1 and adds adaptive-only graph-support declarations for the two builders. Fixed-width DSpark behavior is unchanged.

AI assistance was used for this PR.

## Implementation

- Allow the V4.1 indexer backend to use the ROCm device/CPU query-length mismatch capability.
- Extend ROCm flattened device-query handling to `DeepseekV41ForCausalLM`.
- Report `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS` for the V4.1 ROCm compressed sparse-MLA and sparse-SWA builders only when adaptive verification is enabled.
- Add focused policy coverage, a fixed-K regression test, and a gfx950 graph-replay test for changed device query boundaries and stable persistent metadata buffers.

## Validation stack

- 4x MI355X (gfx950), TP=4, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`; expert parallel enabled for baseline and disabled for the matched mono-off/on (referring to #60397) comparison
- ROCm nightly `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-7d0b4e57aac4c4323225b0eee9ae960ce75ffffe` (vLLM `0.31.1rc1.dev253+g7d0b4e57a.rocm723`)
- nightly source `7d0b4e57aa` plus this PR's exact four-file patch
- Matched EP-off accuracy and throughput tests were run with `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=0` and `1`, and the EP-on baseline used mono decode off
- #60397's mono path does not support EP, so mono's direct effect is measured by the matched EP-off pair

The primary validation matrix below used standard rejection sampling. With the adaptive block-rejection out-of-bounds fix now merged in [#60945](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60945), block rejection matched standard rejection on GSM8K accuracy and TP4 throughput.

<details>
<summary>vLLM server command and environment</summary>

The adaptive arm used the following effective command inside the vllm container (the fixed-K=5 arm changed only `enable_adaptive_verification` to `false`; the no-speculation arm omitted `--speculative-config`; `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE` was set to `0` or `1`). The EP-on baseline additionally passed `--enable-expert-parallel` and used `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=0`:

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=7200 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=<0|1> \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 64 \
  --moe-backend aiter \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","max_cudagraph_capture_size":2048}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","enable_adaptive_verification":true}' \
  --language-model-only \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41
```

</details>

## Test results

### Focused tests

- 156 passed on gfx950: the PR's CPU policy tests, the fixed-K regression test, `test_dsv41_adaptive_mla_swa_metadata_graph_replay`, and the shared adaptive-verification tests.
- Changed-file pre-commit: passed.

### Accuracy

GSM8K 5-shot, 1,319 samples per arm, concurrency 16, standard rejection sampling:

| EP | Mono decode | Arm | Strict exact match | Flexible exact match |
|:---:|:---:|---|---:|---:|
| On | Off | No speculation | 0.9265 ± 0.0072 | 0.9272 ± 0.0072 |
| On | Off | Fixed K=5 | 0.9325 ± 0.0069 | 0.9325 ± 0.0069 |
| On | Off | Adaptive K<=5 | 0.9219 ± 0.0074 | 0.9227 ± 0.0074 |
| Off | Off | No speculation | 0.9310 ± 0.0070 | 0.9303 ± 0.0070 |
| Off | Off | Fixed K=5 | 0.9249 ± 0.0073 | 0.9265 ± 0.0072 |
| Off | Off | Adaptive K<=5 | 0.9189 ± 0.0075 | 0.9189 ± 0.0075 |
| Off | On | No speculation | 0.9204 ± 0.0075 | 0.9204 ± 0.0075 |
| Off | On | Fixed K=5 | 0.9287 ± 0.0071 | 0.9287 ± 0.0071 |
| Off | On | Adaptive K<=5 | 0.9212 ± 0.0074 | 0.9219 ± 0.0074 |

All arms completed every sample. Every within-configuration and same-arm topology difference is within 1.2 combined standard errors.

<details>
<summary>GSM8K command</summary>

```bash
lm_eval \
  --model local-completions \
  --model_args 'model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=16,tokenizer_backend=none,tokenized_requests=False' \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --batch_size 1 \
  --seed 42
```

</details>

RULER `niah_single_2`, 500 samples per length, TP4 with EP on and mono decode off, standard rejection, concurrency 32, greedy decoding with thinking disabled. The server used `--max-model-len 131072` and `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`:

| Arm | 16K | 64K |
|---|---:|---:|
| Fixed K=5 | 0.970 | 0.980 |
| Adaptive K<=5 | 0.980 | 0.988 |

<details>
<summary>RULER NIAH command</summary>

```bash
lm_eval \
  --model local-chat-completions \
  --tasks niah_single_2 \
  --metadata '{"max_seq_lengths":[16384,65536]}' \
  --batch_size auto \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --gen_kwargs '{"chat_template_kwargs":{"thinking":false}}' \
  --seed 1234 \
  --model_args '{"model":"deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash","tokenizer":"deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash","base_url":"http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions","num_concurrent":32,"tokenized_requests":false,"timeout":7200}'
```

</details>

### SPEED-Bench throughput

All 880 qualitative prompts in original order, 512 forced output tokens, a distinct cache salt per concurrency. Each arm and mono mode used one fresh server and one 64-request C32 warmup. Output tokens per second:

Baseline, EP on and mono decode off:

| Arm | C4 | C16 | C32 | C64 | C128 | C256 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| No speculation | 446.5 | 1,346.4 | 2,317.4 | 3,753.6 | 5,832.9 | 8,297.5 |
| Fixed K=5 | **822.3** | 2,188.0 | 3,404.2 | 4,824.2 | 6,579.9 | 8,487.3 |
| Adaptive K<=5 | 806.5 | **2,265.7** | **3,588.4** | **5,331.0** | **7,448.9** | **9,475.1** |

Matched mono comparison, EP off and mono decode off:

| Arm | C4 | C16 | C32 | C64 | C128 | C256 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| No speculation | 463.5 | 1,338.2 | 2,299.4 | 3,713.1 | 5,688.8 | 8,017.0 |
| Fixed K=5 | **821.1** | 2,154.7 | 3,345.7 | 4,760.2 | 6,527.9 | 8,031.1 |
| Adaptive K<=5 | 802.8 | **2,255.6** | **3,522.4** | **5,273.2** | **7,136.3** | **9,235.4** |

Matched mono comparison, EP off and mono decode on:

| Arm | C4 | C16 | C32 | C64 | C128 | C256 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| No speculation | 818.0 | 2,063.0 | 2,975.1 | 3,755.8 | 5,751.0 | 8,106.8 |
| Fixed K=5 | **1,111.4** | 2,177.5 | 3,325.4 | 4,700.0 | 6,530.2 | 8,243.4 |
| Adaptive K<=5 | 1,093.8 | **2,277.1** | **3,558.0** | **5,251.0** | **7,262.4** | **9,210.9** |

All 54 cells completed 880/880 requests with zero failures. In the EP-on baseline, adaptive relative to fixed K=5 was -1.9% at C4 and +3.5% to +13.2% from C16 to C256; it beat no speculation by 27.7% at C128 and 14.2% at C256. In the matched EP-off comparison, adaptive relative to fixed was -2.2% at C4 and +4.7% to +15.0% from C16 to C256 with mono off; with mono on it was -1.6% at C4 and +4.6% to +11.7% from C16 to C256. Adaptive beat no speculation at every measured concurrency in all three configurations.

The mono launches were confirmed active in all three mono-on server logs. Their direct performance effect matched #60397's scope: at C4 mono improved no speculation by 76.5%, fixed K=5 by 35.4%, and adaptive by 36.3%. Above C4 the fixed/adaptive mono-on/off difference was mostly within about 2%, because a full K=5 verify reaches the mono path's 48-row ceiling at eight requests.

<details>
<summary>SPEED-Bench commands</summary>

Each arm used one server and a 64-request C32 random warmup before the measured loop:

```bash

ARM=<nospec|fixed_k5|adaptive>

for c in 4 16 32 64 128 256; do

    --temperature 1.0 \

    --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \
    --extra-body "{\"cache_salt\":\"speedbench-tp4-${ARM}-c${c}\"}" \

done
```

title: [Bugfix]Fix FlashInfer warmup crash: autotune(tuning_buckets=...) must round M up, not down (Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic with spec-decode)
body:
## Fix FlashInfer warmup crash: `autotune(tuning_buckets=...)` must map runtime M **up**, not down

Fixes the engine crash-loop at startup for SM100/SM103 block-scaled cute-dsl linear kernels (`mm_mxfp8` / `mm_fp4`) when speculative decoding is enabled.

### The crash

`kernel_warmup` runs dummy forwards inside `fi_utils.autotune(tuning_buckets=tuning_buckets)`. With spec-decode, the DSpark draft model forward runs at M = `max_num_seqs × k` = e.g. 8 × 3 = **24** — not a bucket value. Boot dies:

```
ValueError: Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic: ((128, 16), (1, 1), True, False, 4)
```

at `flashinfer/gemm/gemm_base.py:5327` (`CuteDSLMxfp8GemmRunner.forward`), reached from the draft model's `fused_wqa_wkv` GEMM.

Reproduced on DGX Station GB300 (SM103) with vLLM nightly + DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + dspark k=3; standalone FlashInfer-only repro at https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5450.

### Root cause

`mm_mxfp8`'s own tuning config maps runtime M to buckets with `map_to_hybrid_bucket_uncapped`, which rounds **up**, and the cute-dsl split-K MMA tile is likewise chosen by rounding M up (`mma_tiler_mn_for_m`: 8/16/32). A tactic tuned at bucket b is therefore valid for every M ≤ b — tune space and apply space agree.

But inside `autotune(tuning_buckets=...)` the autotuner **replaces the op's mapper** with `make_bucket_mapper(buckets, round_map=round_up)` and `round_up` **defaults to False** (floor). So the warmup dummy run at M=24 looks up the **bucket-16** tactic — tile (128,16), split_k=4 — and `forward()` rejects it because `mma_tiler_mn_for_m(24)` is (128,32).

Outside the context (serving, CUDA-graph capture) the op's own round-up mapper is restored, so **only the warmup pass ever crashes**: the engine can never boot, while the identical weights, tactics, and cache would serve fine.

Standalone repro (no vLLM, one process, same cache — all three regimes):

```
inside autotune(tuning_buckets=..., round_up=False [default]):
  M=24 FAILED -> Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic: ((128, 16), (1, 1), True, False, 4)
  M=12 FAILED -> Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic: ((128,  8), (1, 1), True, False, 4)
  M=40 FAILED -> Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic: ((128, 32), (1, 1), True, False,  2)
outside any autotune context (op mapper, rounds up):
  M=24 OK / M=12 OK / M=40 OK
inside autotune(tuning_buckets=..., round_up=True):
  M=24 OK / M=12 OK / M=40 OK
```

### The fix

One line: `round_up=True` on the warmup `autotune()` call, making tune-context mapping equal serving-time mapping. Every cached tactic at bucket b is then applied only to M ≤ b — exactly the envelope both the split-K validator and the small swap-AB base tactics guarantee.

Profiling is per bucket, so tactic choices and the cache file are unchanged; only the dummy run's execution path changes. Verified live on GB300: the crash-looping boot (identical config) boots clean with this change and serves with full CUDA graphs; warmup passes on the pre-existing cache.

### Broader hazard (why this should land even before any FlashInfer-side change)

The base (non-split-K) candidate tactics include swap-AB tiles (128, 8/16/32) whose persistent-kernel `can_implement` requires `kernel_n ≤ tile_n` (kernel_n = token count in swap-AB) — and those tactics get **no apply-time check**. Under floor mapping, a bucket-16 winner applied at M=24 runs silently outside its envelope. The same tactic generator serves `mm_fp4`, so NVFP4 + spec-decode is exposed too. The split-K `ValueError` is just the one place that notices. Filed upstream with full analysis: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5450

### Notes for reviewers

- The change is one argument on one line (plus the explanatory comment); the diff is intentionally minimal.
- If maintainers prefer the fix inside FlashInfer (honor the op's mapping direction under bucket override, or size small tiles against `DynamicDim.max`), this line remains a correct, self-contained fix on the vLLM side and can be revisited later.

title: [KV Offload] Expose OffloadingManager.lock()/unlock() and service the tiering control plane off the scheduler thread
body:
## Purpose

Two things, in priority order.

**1. Expose exclusive access to an `OffloadingManager` as a public API.** `lock()` / `unlock()`, plus a `locked()` helper, guard a manager's whole state subtree: the manager, the tiers it composes, and any front-end state those tiers own. Manager methods never acquire it themselves, so a caller holds it across as many operations as its own invariants need. That property is the point — several manager operations only make sense in sequence. `prepare_load()` documents that its keys are offloaded, a fact `lookup()` established one hook earlier, so a caller has to be able to span both. Internal per-method locking cannot offer that.

**2. Use it for the first case that needs it** (#55179). The `p2p` secondary tier answers a remote peer, which the engine does not drive, so its control plane only advanced from `on_schedule_end`. A peer's lookup or fetch therefore waited for a model-step boundary — seconds on a saturated rank, gating a transfer of well under one. Tiers now opt in with `needs_control_plane_thread`, and `TieringOffloadingManager` runs one thread that polls them and lets them serve between steps.

## Not a duplicate of the open PRs on #55179

This overlaps open work and I want that on the record rather than buried.

| PR | Author | Driver | Locking |
|---|---|---|---|
| **this** | me | thread owned by `TieringOffloadingManager` | **public `lock()`/`unlock()` on `OffloadingManager`, held by callers** |
| #58113 | me | same thread, same sweep | private `_enter_step`/`_exit_step`/`_observation_lock` + `*_unlocked` variants |
| #57165 | @nilig | `EngineCore` poller thread | new `KVConnectorBase_V1.poll_pending_work` |
| #55962 | @Etelis | `EngineCore` + connector base API + executor changes | new base-API hook |
| #57139 | me | — | the separate async peer-registration half, not this |

**This supersedes my own #58113, which I will close.** The difference is not cosmetic:

- **#58113 does not expose an API.** It takes the lock inside the manager's public methods, which forces a `*_unlocked` variant of every method `_SecondaryTierFacingParent` can re-enter (`lookup`, `on_new_request`, `create_store_job`, `on_request_finished`, `reset_cache`) because the parent handle's caller already holds it. That duplication is most of its `+393` lines in `manager.py`, and it is precisely what prevents an outside caller from saying "hold this across several operations." Moving the lock to the caller removes every one of those variants.
- **#58113 releases at `on_schedule_end`, which is not the end of the step.** `build_connector_meta` called `on_schedule_end` ~40 lines early, before `_build_store_jobs` → `prepare_store` (which evicts) and before `on_request_finished`. So its `prepare_store` re-acquired via `_enter_step()` and nothing released it: on every step that builds store jobs — the common case under load — the lock was held across `future.result()`, starving the control thread in exactly the window the change exists to exploit. That plausibly explains #58113's own "parity-within-noise" result, which was measured through the bug, and that conclusion should be re-tested.

Relative to #57165 / #55962: same goal, but no new `KVConnectorBase_V1` hook and no `EngineCore` or executor changes. In #55179 @nilig asked for a read on "a thread touching the connector from inside `EngineCore`, even phase-exclusive, versus a control thread owned by the tier" — this is a working implementation of the second option, offered as input to that question. If maintainers prefer either existing PR, close this one.

## Changes

Commit 1, **`on_schedule_end` runs last** — independent of all locking, reviewable on its own. Its docstring already claimed "called once at the end of each scheduler step"; it was called ~40 lines early. Moving it makes the contract true and gives callers a sound release point. Two ordering consequences, both handled: `prepare_store`'s poll becomes unconditional (the per-step gate was previously reset mid-`build_connector_meta`, which is where its fresh completion data came from — without this, eviction decisions would run on data up to a step stale), and `_flush_pending_cascades` now re-parks keys this step parked, which is safe because `_maybe_finalize_request` holds off while `pending_cascade_keys` is non-empty.

Commit 2, **the API and its consumer**.

`OffloadingConnectorScheduler` holds one region per engine step, opened by the first manager-touching hook and closed at the end of `build_connector_meta`, so the manager is free while the engine runs the model. Hooks outside `schedule()` take a short region.

Two placements are load-bearing and easy to get wrong:

- **`has_pending_push_work` must use the short region.** `EngineCore.step()` returns early at `core.py:597` when `has_requests()` is false, so a step-scoped acquire there would never reach the release and would hold the manager for good — the state an idle engine settles into. It does still need the lock: `has_pending_work()` iterates `_req_state` while the control thread may insert or delete via `parent.on_new_request` / `on_request_finished`.
- **`take_events` drains inside the region.** `manager.take_events()` is a generator whose backing list is cleared once exhausted, so iterating it lazily both pinned the manager for the consumer's duration and discarded events a concurrent `complete_write` appended, unpublished. It stays a generator so the caller's truthiness check at `sched/scheduler.py` is unchanged.

The thread yields unconditionally *after* `unlock()`, which is what bounds the scheduler's wait to one round — Python locks are not fair, so a release-then-reacquire loop could starve it. A failed round is logged, not fatal, and `on_schedule_end` still serves every tier, so the fallback is per-step servicing. `_process_finished_jobs` takes a tier filter so a round does not drag tiers that expect the scheduler thread. `shutdown()` stops and joins the thread before any tier teardown, since closing a transport under a live round can end the process rather than raise.

Config: `control_plane_interval_s` in `kv_connector_extra_config`, default 1 ms, `0` disables the thread and restores per-step servicing.

Docstrings that claimed single-threaded tier access are corrected, including the eviction-race argument in `_pin_and_register_hits` — which still holds, now because `serve_external_requests` runs inside one hold of the lock. `async_lookup.py`'s "owned exclusively by the scheduler thread" claim was outright false once `parent.lookup` can fan out to `fs.lookup` from the control thread.

## Test results

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ -q
  901 passed, 12 skipped in 295s      (baseline on this tree: 889 passed, 12 skipped)

pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/ -q
  217 passed in 66s                   (subset of the above; re-run on its own)

pre-commit: all hooks pass, including ruff, ruff-format, mypy, and check-test-tethering.
```

Note for reviewers: a whole-directory run of `tests/v1/kv_offload/` produces a large number of CUDA IMA errors that are **pre-existing and unrelated** (`tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/` poisons the rest of the session). Run the subdirectories separately.

12 new tests. The two that matter most were both verified to fail without the change, not just to pass with it:

- `test_on_schedule_end_is_the_last_manager_call_of_a_step` — without the reorder it observes `['on_schedule_end', 'prepare_store']`. This is the check #58113's suite lacks, because its `_step()` helper drives `on_schedule_end` with no following `prepare_store`.
- `test_control_thread_and_scheduler_never_overlap` — with `lock()`/`unlock()` stubbed to no-ops it detects 86 overlaps. It also asserts both threads made progress, so neither a thread that never runs nor one that starves the scheduler passes it.

I wrote and then **deleted** a third test ("no eviction between a served lookup and its pin") after finding it still passed with the lock neutered: LRU keeps evicting the fresh keys rather than the constantly-looked-up hit keys, so it could never fail. The overlap test is the real guard for that property, and a test that cannot fail is worse than no test.

## Model evaluation — the 4-case matrix from #55179

Run on two H200 pods, Llama-3.2-1B, `--enforce-eager`, `--block-size 16`, 96 GiB CPU
primary tier, `secondary_tiers: [{"type": "p2p"}]`, `max-model-len 32768`.

**Topology.** Source = the pod holding the KV in its CPU offload tier. Consumer = the
other pod, which probes the source over P2P (`remote_kv_source`) and fetches. Every
measured fetch uses a freshly generated ~27k-token prompt that is populated on the source
first, so nothing hits a GPU prefix cache and the fetch is real work: each one moved
**~1720 chunks** (`kv_offload_tiering_chunk_hits` delta), i.e. the full prefix.

**Busy** = source saturated with 8 concurrent ~27k-token prefills. That took its
request latency from **0.018 s idle to 1.40 s**, so the control plane really is gated
behind ~1.4 s of model work — the same regime as the issue's report.

**Cold** = no P2P session yet. A session lives as long as the engine, so only the first
fetch after a restart is genuinely cold; both pods were restarted between every phase and
the cold fetch measured first.

**Signal** = the consumer's `vllm:kv_offload_lookup_async_delay_seconds` delta for the
measured request (one observation per fetch). Warm figures are the mean of 3 reps.

| case | A: baseline (`7b077f36a8`) | B: #58113 | C: this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| idle, cold | 0.177 s | — | **0.133 s** |
| idle, warm | 0.0455 s | — | **0.0457 s** |
| busy, cold | 0.440 s | 0.289 s | **0.155 s** |
| busy, warm | 0.220 s | 0.129 s | **0.0534 s** |

**The per-step gating penalty, which is what this PR removes:**

| arm | idle-warm | busy-warm | penalty |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: baseline | 0.0455 s | 0.2196 s | **4.83x** |
| C: this PR | 0.0457 s | 0.0534 s | **1.17x** |

Saturating the source costs baseline 4.8x on the consumer's lookup delay. With the control
thread it costs 1.17x — the stall is essentially gone, and a busy source now behaves like
an idle one.

Supporting numbers on busy-warm: per-chunk tiering delay
(`kv_offload_tiering_lookup_async_delay_seconds`) 0.100 s → 0.0174 s (5.8x), and end-to-end
TTFT for the fetch 0.310 s → 0.144 s (2.2x). Idle is parity within noise in every metric,
as expected — there is no model step to hide behind.

Per-rep spread, busy-warm: baseline `0.1929 / 0.2532 / 0.2127`, this PR
`0.0388 / 0.0427 / 0.0786`. The distributions do not overlap — the worst rep here is still
better than the best baseline rep.

**No source-side slowdown.** The concern that holding the manager lock slows the scheduler
does not show up: on the busy source, request latency was 1.4174 s (baseline) vs 1.4039 s
(this PR), and the populate-request mean 1.7056 s vs 1.7100 s. The background load
generator completed 158 vs 153 requests over comparable windows, a ~3% difference that is
within single-run noise and not corroborated by either latency measure. A dedicated
`vllm bench serve` throughput comparison is still worth running before merge; I did not
run one.

### On #58113

Arm B is #58113 at `b8ea135c71`, measured on the same pods in the same session. It lands
**between** baseline and this PR: busy-warm 0.129 s vs baseline 0.220 s vs 0.0534 s here.

That is what the release-point bug predicts. #58113's thread is not dead — on steps that
build no store jobs the lock is released normally, so it recovers some of the win (1.7x
over baseline). But on any step that does build store jobs, `prepare_store` re-acquires
after `on_schedule_end` released and nothing releases it again, so the lock is held across
`future.result()` and the thread is shut out for exactly that step. Under load most steps
build store jobs, which is why it recovers only about a third of what is available (4.1x
over baseline here, 2.4x over #58113).

I am reporting this as *consistent with* the bug rather than as direct proof of the
mechanism; the mechanism itself is demonstrated by the unit test, which observes the call
order `['on_schedule_end', 'prepare_store']` without the reorder in commit 1.

### Caveat on absolute magnitudes

These numbers are much smaller than the issue's 13.6 s, and deliberately so: this is
Llama-3.2-1B on a single H200 per side, not GLM-5.2-FP8 on DP8. What reproduces here is the
**mechanism and its scaling** — the consumer's lookup delay is proportional to the source's
step time under baseline, and roughly independent of it with the control thread. The issue's
13.6 s came from a far slower source; the ratio, not the absolute, is what transfers.

Raw per-rep JSON for all six runs is available on request.

## NIXL thread-safety: checked, and it holds

Checked against the **NIXL 1.4.1** sources (`ai-dynamo/nixl` at tag `v1.4.1`), which is the
deployed version. **This corrects an earlier version of this description**, which said
`NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_RW` does not exist and that the config offers no way to request a sync
mode. Both statements were true of 0.6.0, which is what I had installed; neither is true of
1.4.1.

**Serialized use from a second thread is supported.** `makeMtType`
(`src/plugins/ucx/ucx_utils.cpp:383-392`) returns only `WORKER` or `SINGLE`, never
`CONTEXT` -- and `mt_mode_t::CONTEXT` is the only value that maps to
`UCS_THREAD_MODE_SINGLE` (`ucx_utils.cpp:476-492`), the one UCX mode with creator-thread
affinity. Grepping confirms `CONTEXT` never appears as a produced value, only in switch
arms. So the weakest mode NIXL ever requests is `UCS_THREAD_MODE_SERIALIZED`, which UCX
documents as *"Multiple threads can access, but only one at a time"* -- precisely this
design. And because `enable_prog_thread` defaults on for this transport, it actually gets
`UCS_THREAD_MODE_MULTI`, with a hard library-support check that throws if unavailable.

**The manager lock is load-bearing, not redundant.** With `syncMode = NONE` -- which is what
this transport gets, since it sets neither `enable_listen` nor `sync_mode` -- NIXL's internal
agent lock compiles to no-ops (`src/core/sync.h:36-39`), leaving ~23 agent entry points
unguarded over shared, non-atomic containers. The external mutex is therefore the only
protection, and it must cover every entry point plus the lifetime of handles passed between
calls. It does.

Two caveats worth recording:

- NIXL binds a shared UCX worker per calling thread (`tlsSharedWorkerMap`,
  `ucx_backend.cpp:821-825`). That is harmless only while there is exactly one shared
  worker, which holds for this configuration (`num_workers` unset ⇒ `numSharedWorkers_ == 1`,
  so every thread maps to worker 0) but would not if a `num_workers` UCX backend param were
  ever set. The chosen worker also travels on the request handle rather than being
  re-derived per call, so a transfer prepped on one thread and polled on another still uses
  the same worker.
- 1.4.1 *does* accept an explicit `sync_mode` (including `NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_RW`, value 2),
  which would make NIXL's own locking real as belt-and-braces, and is what every upstream
  multi-threaded test uses. I have not added it, because the parameter does not exist on
  0.6.0 and passing it unconditionally would break older environments; it needs the same
  kind of version gate `capture_telemetry` already needs. Worth a follow-up.

Honest limit: `~/nixl` is a 1.4.1 source checkout, not a build, and only 0.6.0 is installed
locally, so every 1.4.1 claim above is static source reading rather than runtime
introspection. A runtime confirmation (log the thread mode `ucp_worker_query` actually
grants, or run the two-thread pattern under TSan) would close the remaining gap. The
end-to-end matrix above ran on the deployed 1.4.1 across ~14k P2P chunk fetches with no
transfer failures, which is evidence but not a substitute.

pyzmq is fine under strict serialization: libzmq permits migrating a socket between threads
given a full memory barrier, which lock acquire/release provides, and nothing is bound
thread-locally at socket creation. The one hazard is `zmq_ctx_destroy` racing a socket call,
which the shutdown ordering handles.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change (Claude Code): the code-path analysis, the implementation, and the tests. I am reviewing every changed line. The two items that were blocking this leaving draft are now done: the 4-case matrix has been run on H200 hardware (results above) and the NIXL question has been checked against 1.4.1. title: [Bugfix][Sampler] Fix split top-p masking every token for huge logits (thinking_token_budget + spec decode emits token 0)
body:
## Purpose

This affects `thinking_token_budget` with speculative decoding (MTP, on both the V1 runner and Model Runner V2) and any `top_p < 1`, including a model's `generation_config` default. When the budget is reached, the request emits token id 0 (`<unk>` for NemotronH) until `max_tokens` instead of the forced `</think>`. Greedy requests and `top_p=1.0` are not affected.

**Root cause.** The bug is in the split-row top-p pipeline (#54651), not in the thinking-budget code. `_topp_sb_mask_kernel` in `vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_triton.py` runs on CUDA for batches of 64 rows or fewer, for rows with top-p and without an active top-k. It finds its pivot in probability space but masks in logit space:

```python
pivot_logit = tl.log(pivot) + logZ + M
keep = x > pivot_logit
```

Thinking-budget forcing writes `1e9` into the end-of-reasoning logit. The V1 `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder` and the MRV2 `_thinking_budget_kernel` both do this, so `M = 1e9`. fp32 spacing at 1e9 is 64. The term `log(pivot) + log(Z)` (about -7.7) is lost in the addition, so `pivot_logit == M`. No token passes the strict `>`, and the whole row becomes `-inf`. From there:
- In the V1 rejection sampler, `softmax` gives NaN, the draft is rejected, and `sample_recovered_tokens_kernel` falls back to `recovered_id = 0`.
- In the MRV2 verifier (`_resample_kernel`), argmax over an all `-inf` row returns index 0.

Token 0 is sampled, the budget is still exceeded, forcing runs again, and the loop never ends. Throughput also drops about 3x because every draft is rejected.

Spec decode exposes the bug because the forced verification rows go through `apply_top_k_top_p`: V1 via `apply_sampling_constraints`, MRV2 via `SamplingStates.apply_top_k_top_p`. Non-spec decoding is safe only in the default configuration, where the fused FlashInfer sampler is used. If processed-logprobs mode is on, or the FlashInfer sampler is unavailable, non-spec sampling goes through the same Triton path and hits the same bug.

The monolithic `_topk_topp_kernel` (batches over 64) is left alone on purpose. Its `max_sample` estimate (avg + 10·std of a sample block) is far below 1e9, so `sum_exp` overflows to inf and the pivot becomes NaN. Its `not (final_pivot < max_logit)` guard then disables top-p for that row. Sampling stays correct because the 1e9 logit dominates the softmax.

**Fix.** Mask with the same probability-space predicate the step kernels used to measure the mass: `exp(x - M) / Z > pivot`. This matches `pivot` and `dup` bitwise against the values the search produced. Tie handling reuses the same `prob`; it already compared in probability space for exactly this precision reason. The row max is also kept as a backstop. For ordinary logits the kept set does not change: 24 of 24 randomized rows were identical before and after under `TRITON_INTERPRET=1`.

This is not a duplicate of #54906 or #39573. Those were reported on v0.28.1 and v0.19, which predate the split pipeline (#54651, 2026-09-03), and they describe the budget being ignored rather than token-0 output. No open PR or issue covers split top-p masking with large logits. #55414 touches the same kernel, but only to precompile variants.

## Known related follow-ups (out of scope)

- The monolithic `_topk_topp_kernel` has the same logit-space round trip (`final_pivot = log(p_pivot * sum_exp) + max_*`, `duplicate_logit = ...`). Today it fails open through the guard described above, so it does not produce wrong tokens.
- Thinking-budget forcing uses a `1e9` sentinel logit. Masking every other token to `-inf` and keeping the forced logit ("mask-and-bump") would stop producing extreme values that downstream sampling ops must tolerate.
- The `nomask = pivot * Z >= 1` guard in `_topp_sb_combine` is stale: pivots are always strictly below `hi = 1/Z`.
- Duplicate matching uses inconsistent tolerances: `abs(a - b) < 1e-9` in the step/combine kernels versus exact equality in the mask kernel.

## Test Plan

- New regression test `TestTritonTopkTopp::test_topp_keeps_forced_huge_logit` in `tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py`:
  - batch sizes 4 and 64, both on the split path (64 is its maximum batch size);
  - forced logits `1e9` and `1e9/0.6` (the latter models temperature 0.6);
  - `p = 0.95`.
  
  It asserts that the forced logit survives, that every other token is masked (exactly one kept per row), that the softmax has no NaN, and that the argmax is the forced token.
- `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py -v`
- CPU kernel repro under the Triton interpreter:
  - Harness: `topp_split_interp_harness.py`. It loads the kernel file with vLLM imports stubbed and drives `_topp_sb_stats_kernel`, `_topp_sb_step_kernel` and `_topp_sb_mask_kernel` exactly as `_apply_topp_split` does, with `num_sm=108` for A100.
  - Command:
    ```
    docker run --rm -v $PWD:/src python:3.12-slim sh -c "pip install -q --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu torch numpy && pip install -q triton==3.8.0 && mkdir -p /work && cp /src/topp_split_interp_harness.py /work/harness.py && TRITON_INTERPRET=1 V=131072 python /work/harness.py /src/vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_triton.py"
    ```
- End-to-end repro setup:
  - model: NemotronH-30B-A3B BF16 on 1x A100;
  - server flags: `--reasoning-parser nemotron_v3 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'`;
  - request: chat completion with `thinking_token_budget: 300`, `temperature: 1.0`, `logprobs: true`, `skip_special_tokens: false`.

## Related issues

- Related to #54906, but a different bug. #54906 reports the budget being ignored (reasoning continues) on MRV2 only, with `top_k=20` set. Rows with an active top-k go through the monolithic `_topk_topp_kernel`, not the split top-p path fixed here, so this PR is not expected to fix #54906.
- Same symptom family as #39573 (closed), which was reported on v0.19, before the split top-p pipeline (#54651) existed.

## Test Result

- CPU kernel under `TRITON_INTERPRET=1` (vocab 131072, p=0.95):
  - Before the fix, `forced 1e9` gives `kept=0`: the whole row is `-inf`, and sampling returns token 0 via NaN.
  - After the fix, `kept=1` (the forced token), and the sampled token is 13 (`</think>`).
  - Normal rows: 24 of 24 are identical to the pre-fix kernel, and within 1 token of the PyTorch sort reference.
- End-to-end on unpatched v0.30.0 (V1 runner + MTP5):
  - `top_p=0.95`: the budget is reached, then every remaining token is `<unk>`.
  - `top_p=1.0` or `top_k=50`: `</think>` is forced at the budget and a normal answer follows.
  - Greedy: works.
- GPU pytest (1x A100-SXM4-80GB, v0.30.0 with this fix applied, `--noconftest`):
  - `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py -k test_topp_keeps_forced_huge_logit -v`: 4 passed (`split` and `split-boundary`, each with `1e9` and `1e9_over_temp0.6`).
  - `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py`: 135 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed. This includes the existing Triton and FlashInfer distribution and reference tests; `scipy` is needed for the FlashInfer distribution tests.
- Patched end-to-end run (MRV2, Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B + MTP `num_speculative_tokens=5`, 1x A100, default sampling `top_p=0.95`):
  - Raw `/v1/completions`, `thinking_token_budget=300`, `skip_special_tokens=false`: 0 `<unk>` tokens. `</think>` is forced at the budget and a valid JSON answer follows (`finish_reason=stop`). Checked on BF16 weights and on FP8 weights.
  - Chat, `thinking_token_budget=1000`: 212 tok/s (the unpatched run collapsed to 65 tok/s), `finish_reason=stop`, valid answer.
  - Not re-run on the V1 runner with the patch applied. The fix is in the shared Triton kernel that both runners call.

## AI assistance

This change was investigated and drafted with AI assistance (Claude). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests listed above.

Signed-off-by: Gilad Zamoscinski <gilad.z@taboola.com>

title: [XPU][MLA] Integrate XPU MLA support into the existing FLASH_ATTN_MLA backend
body:
## Summary

Integrate XPU MLA support into the existing `FLASH_ATTN_MLA` backend, following the same platform-specific integration pattern used by `FLASH_ATTN`.

This PR:

- Adds an XPU-specific FlashAttnMLA backend while keeping the shared MLA implementation in the existing `flashattn_mla.py` module.
- Routes `FLASH_ATTN_MLA` to the XPU-specific backend through XPU platform backend selection, without rebinding `FlashAttnMLABackend` at module scope.
- Uses the `flash_attn_varlen_func` implementation from `vllm-xpu-kernels` for MLA paged decode on XPU.
- Packs the query as `q = [q_nope, q_pe]`, uses the latent cache as K, and passes a narrowed V view to match the MLA value dimension.
- Keeps the existing CUDA FlashAttnMLA behavior unchanged, including FA3 decode and LSE handling.
- Fixes XPU varlen output allocation so that, when `out` is omitted, the output tensor uses the V head dimension instead of the Q head dimension.

The output-allocation fix is required for MLA because its packed Q/K head dimension is 576 while its V head dimension is 512. It preserves the existing behavior for regular attention, where `q.shape[-1] == v.shape[-1]`.

## Validation method

Run from a vLLM checkout on an Intel XPU machine with `vllm-xpu-kernels` installed or on `PYTHONPATH`.

1. End-to-end test

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

tmp_script="$(mktemp /tmp/vllm_xpu_mla_validate.XXXXXX.py)"
trap 'rm -f "${tmp_script}"' EXIT

cat >"${tmp_script}" <<'PY'
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

def main():
    llm = LLM(
        model="deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite",
        tensor_parallel_size=2,
        dtype="bfloat16",
        attention_backend="FLASH_ATTN_MLA",
        block_size=64,
        max_model_len=512,
        trust_remote_code=True,
        enforce_eager=True,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.80,
    )

    prompts = [
        "Hello, my name is",
        "The capital of France is",
        "The future of AI in 2030 will be",
    ]
    sampling_params = SamplingParams(
        temperature=0.0,
        max_tokens=64,
        repetition_penalty=1.1,
    )
    outputs = llm.generate(prompts, sampling_params)
    for output in outputs:
        print("=" * 60)
        print("PROMPT:", output.prompt)
        print("OUTPUT:", output.outputs[0].text)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
PY

python "${tmp_script}"
```

Expected result:
- Logs show `Using Flash Attention MLA backend on XPU.`
- Generation reaches `Processed prompts: 100%` and prints outputs for all prompts.

This was validated locally on 2x Intel Arc Pro B60; the run logged `Using Flash Attention MLA backend on XPU.`, completed `Processed prompts: 100%`, and generated coherent outputs for all three prompts (e.g. "Hello, my name is" -> "John. I am a 20 year old male...", "The capital of France is" -> "Paris.").

2. Compile check

```bash
python -m py_compile vllm/_xpu_ops.py vllm/platforms/xpu.py vllm/v1/attention/backends/fa_utils.py vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashattn_mla.py vllm/v1/attention/backends/test_mla_backends.py
```
All 5 changed files compile cleanly with no errors.

3. Accuracy

Ran `lm_eval` with `--model vllm` against DeepSeek-V2-Lite on Intel Arc Pro B60 with `attention_backend=FLASH_ATTN_MLA`:

- TP=2, `dtype=bfloat16`, `max_model_len=4096`, `enforce_eager=True`:
  - GSM8K (5-shot): `exact_match,strict-match` = 0.3723, `exact_match,flexible-extract` = 0.3783
  - MMLU: overall `acc` = 0.5895 ± 0.0277 (humanities 0.5846, other 0.5538, social_sciences 0.7667, stem 0.5053)
- DeepSeek-V2-Lite GSM8K with `ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASH_ATTN_MLA`, TP=4, `APPLY_CHAT_TEMPLATE=0`, `NUM_FEWSHOT=5`, `MAX_MODEL_LEN=2048` completed successfully; 300-sample result was strict-match 0.3800 / flexible-extract 0.3833, consistent with the base model's expected GSM8K range.

Ran `lm_eval` with `--model vllm` against DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat on local Intel Arc B580 with `attention_backend=FLASH_ATTN_MLA`:

- TP=4, `dtype=bfloat16`, `max_model_len=2048`, `enforce_eager=True`, `trust_remote_code=True`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.85`, `block_size=64`:

- GSM8K (5-shot, 300-sample subset): `exact_match,strict-match` = 0.6633, `exact_match,flexible-extract` = 0.6700

Both are consistent with DeepSeek-V2-Lite's published reference numbers.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend][Rust Frontend] Update DeepSeek V4.1 Flash reasoning effort mappings
body:
## Purpose

This PR updates the reasoning effort mappings of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash to align with the official implementation.

Current mappings are:

```python
REASONING_EFFORT_MAPPINGS: Dict[str, int] = {
    "low": 25,
    "high": 50,
    "xhigh": 75,
    "max": 100,
}
```

The DeepSeek V4.1 Flash repo on Hugging Face updated them in [commit df42c10](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/commit/df42c109f1defefcbfcedbe7d905718a12266e40), to:

```python
REASONING_EFFORT_MAPPINGS: Dict[str, int] = {
    "low": 50,
    "high": 75,
    "max": 100,
}
```

The [Technical Report](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/blob/dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277/DeepSeek_V41_Tech_Report.pdf) (page 30) and [deepseek-recipe](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-recipe/blob/8cadfede7063c896b944e7bae05daa3549ae97ea/deepseek-recipe-encoding/src/v4/dsv41.rs#L6-L15) both use this low -> 50, high -> 75 mapping.

This PR updates the Python encoder, Rust renderer and the relevant tests and fixtures.

To maintain backwards compatibility, I've kept the xhigh -> 75 mapping. [DeepSeek API Docs](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode/) mentioned they map xhigh to high, so the current behaviour should be appropriate.

## Test Plan

Run the updated Python and Rust tests and linter tests.

```bash
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py -v
$ cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-chat --locked renderer::deepseek
$ pre-commit run
$ cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-chat --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
```

## Test Result

All tests passed.

## AI Assistance Clarification

Claude found this bug, and I verified it by reading through the code. I made the code changes, ran the tests and wrote this PR message; Claude reviewed the diff and the description.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Drop two dead per-step ops from the AITER sparse MLA metadata build
body:
## Purpose

`ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadataBuilder.build()` runs once per KV-cache group per scheduler step and launches two GPU ops whose results are not needed:

1. **Unused `query_lens`.** `build()` computes `query_start_loc[1:] - query_start_loc[:-1]`, but `generate_sparse_seqlen_triton` only reads its size and device; the kernel derives per-request lengths from `cu_query_lens`. The parameter is dropped and `num_seqs` is taken as `cu_query_lens.size(0) - 1`.
2. **Self-aliasing `fill_`.** `paged_kv_indptr[n + 1:].fill_(paged_kv_indptr[n])` passes a view of the tensor being filled, so ATen clones the value first. A broadcast `copy_` from the same element writes the same values without the clone.

| op | aten ops | GPU kernels |
|---|---|---|
| `x[n+1:].fill_(x[n])` | `fill_` → `clone` (`empty_strided` + copy) → `copy_` | 2 |
| `t.copy_(x[n].expand_as(t))` | `copy_` | 1 |
| `qsl[1:] - qsl[:-1]` | `sub` (+ alloc) | 1 |

Each `build()` launches two fewer kernels and makes two fewer device allocations, with no change in output. #57885 removed a similar dead op from the DSA indexer builder.

On ROCm, sparse-MLA layers that do not bring their own backend select `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`. Of 18 current checkpoints probed on main (dummy weights, 8 layers, TP=1), three reach this `build()`:

| model | binding | `build()` per decode step |
|---|---|---:|
| GLM-5.3 (`glm_moe_dsa`) | `DeepseekV32MLAAttention` → `ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend` | 2 |
| GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 (`glm_moe_dsa`) | same | 2 |
| GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`, DSA every 4th layer) | `MLAAttention` → `ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend` | 1 |

DeepSeek-V4-Flash/Pro and V4.1-Flash use their own builders, and the other 12 have no sparse MLA. CUDA never selects this backend.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py`. The new `test_build_fills_paged_kv_indptr_tail` poisons the `paged_kv_indptr` tail and checks that it reads as the running total; it fails if the tail copy is removed.
- Output equivalence: every benchmark run hashes the full `paged_kv_indptr` buffer (tail poisoned first), the returned metadata tensors and the AITER work/reduce metadata.
