title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Restore prompt-tail prefix-cache hits with MTP
body:
Regression introduced in #55390.
Affects hybrid Mamba/GDN models with MTP, prefix caching, `--mamba-cache-mode align`, and `hash_block_size` smaller than the Mamba `block_size`.

| Model                                          | Prefix-cache hit (%): before → main → fix | Output TPS/GPU: before → main → fix |
|------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| [Nemotron 3.5 Lightning NVFP4][l] (Mamba, TP1) | 95.72 → 92.02 → **95.71**                 | 2846 → 2228 → **2833**              |
| [Qwen3.5-122B NVFP4][q] (GDN, TP2)             | 95.47 → 89.80 → **95.57**                 | 687 → 480 → **688**                 |

[l]: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4
[q]: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4

- AIPerf: 50K-token shared prefix, 20 turns of 2K in / 1K out, concurrency 32.
- GSM8K is on par across the three builds (1319 questions, temperature 1.0): Lightning 91.7±0.6%, Qwen3.5 80.4±0.2%.

<details>
<summary>Full results, images, and commands</summary>

#### Full results

| Model        | vLLM          | Prefix-cache hit | Uncached prompt tokens | Output TPS/GPU | Gen TPS/user | GSM8K  |
|--------------|---------------|------------------|------------------------|----------------|--------------|--------|
| Lightning    | Before #55390 | 95.72%           | 2.25M                  | 2846           | 108.7        | 91.05% |
|              | Main          | 92.02%           | 4.19M                  | 2228           | 88.9         | 91.81% |
|              | Main + fix    | 95.71%           | 2.26M                  | 2833           | 109.4        | 92.27% |
| Qwen3.5-122B | Before #55390 | 95.47%           | 2.35M                  | 687            | 48.9         | 80.29% |
|              | Main          | 89.80%           | 5.27M                  | 480            | 34.1         | 80.67% |
|              | Main + fix    | 95.57%           | 2.29M                  | 688            | 49.4         | 80.21% |

Gen TPS/user is the mean of `1 / inter-token latency` per request.

#### Images

- Before #55390: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-3df4ae153eb385e27b52f26c81f8edb9e20b9984`
- Main: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-e9757321527ca1ecd514c07c1418dd2c53da3d19`
- Main + fix: the main image with this PR's `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` mounted over the installed one.

#### AIPerf

Server environment: `VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY=uniform_random`.

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4 --trust-remote-code --max-num-seqs 32 --max-model-len 114688 --async-scheduling \
  --enable-prefix-caching --block-size 64 --prefix-match-unit 64 --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --mamba-backend flashinfer --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 --enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding --mamba-cache-philox-rounds 5 \
  --speculative_config.method mtp --speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens 3 \
  --speculative_config.rejection_sample_method synthetic --speculative_config.synthetic_acceptance_length 3.0
```

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --quantization modelopt_fp4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --language-model-only \
  --trust-remote-code --max-num-seqs 32 --max-model-len 114688 --async-scheduling \
  --enable-prefix-caching --block-size 64 --prefix-match-unit 64 --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --speculative_config.method mtp --speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens 3 \
  --speculative_config.rejection_sample_method synthetic --speculative_config.synthetic_acceptance_length 3.0
```

```bash
aiperf profile --model $MODEL --tokenizer $MODEL --tokenizer-trust-remote-code --url http://0.0.0.0:30000 \
  --endpoint-type chat --streaming --use-server-token-count --random-seed 42 \
  --concurrency 32 --num-conversations 32 --request-count 640 --warmup-request-count 16 \
  --shared-system-prompt-length 51200 --isl 2048 --isl-stddev 0 --osl 1024 --osl-stddev 0 \
  --conversation-turn-mean 20 --conversation-turn-stddev 0 --conversation-turn-delay-mean 0 \
  --extra-inputs temperature:0 --extra-inputs ignore_eos:true
```

#### GSM8K

Same `vllm serve` commands as above, without the two `synthetic` flags and without `VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY`. [NeMo-Skills](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Skills) at `467b057372`:

```bash
python -m nemo_skills.inference.generate \
  ++server.server_type=vllm ++server.base_url=http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 ++server.model=$MODEL \
  ++input_file=$GSM8K_TEST_JSONL ++eval_type=math ++eval_config.split=test ++prompt_config=generic/math \
  ++inference.endpoint_type=chat ++inference.tokens_to_generate=4096 ++inference.temperature=1.0 \
  ++inference.top_p=0.95 ++inference.random_seed=0 ++chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=True \
  ++inference.extra_body.skip_special_tokens=False ++max_concurrent_requests=512 ++output_file=output.jsonl
```

</details>

## Explanation of regression

Example: `hash_block_size = 64`. Prompt A has 1600 tokens. Prompt B starts with A. With MTP, the prefix-cache lookup drops the last 64 matched tokens, so B can reuse at most 1536. [The scheduler](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9ed8158/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L479-L486) ends a prefill chunk of A at 1536 to compute the Mamba state there. But [`_cache_partial_tail_block`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9ed8158/vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py#L2078-L2086) saves the state at 1536 only if the Mamba group has `use_eagle`. Otherwise, it saves at 1600.

The Mamba group got `use_eagle` only from **the all-groups fallback** in [the coordinator](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9ed8158/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py#L108-L110):

```python
if use_eagle and not self.eagle_group_ids:
    self.eagle_group_ids = set(range(len(kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups)))
```

#55390 marks the MTP group, so the all-groups fallback no longer runs. The Mamba state is saved at 1600, and B reuses 0 tokens instead of 1536.

## Fix
`_cache_partial_tail_block` checks `drop_eagle_checkpoint_block` instead of `use_eagle`. [The coordinator](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9ed8158/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py#L153-L156) sets it on every Mamba manager exactly when the scheduler shifts the chunk end:

```diff
-if self.use_eagle:
+if self.drop_eagle_checkpoint_block:
     latest_prompt_hash_boundary = max(
         latest_prompt_hash_boundary - hash_block_size, 0
     )
```

#### Tests

`pytest tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_mamba_eagle_resume_checkpoint.py`: the new `annotated-draft` cases fail on main and pass with this change.

#### AI assistance

AI assistance was used.

title: [ROCm][DSv4][Perf] Use the shared prefill chunk plan in the ROCm sparse prefill
body:
## Purpose

`DeepseekV4ROCMAiterMLAAttention._forward_prefill` splits prefill requests into fixed groups of `PREFILL_CHUNK_SIZE = 4` and sizes the bf16 gather workspace from the static worst case (`N = ceil(max_model_len / compress_ratio)`, `M = N + window_size + max_num_batched_tokens`). The NVIDIA FlashMLA path already uses `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadata.get_prefill_chunk_plan()` (#45061), which packs requests by workspace area and returns each chunk's real widths.

This PR drives the ROCm prefill loop from the same plan. The loop allocates the workspace per chunk as `(chunk_size, chunk_M, head_dim)` and passes `chunk_N` / `chunk_M` to the SWA gather and `combine_topk_swa_indices`, matching the NVIDIA V4 path. Steps with more than 4 prefill requests now run as fewer, larger chunks. Peak memory is unchanged: the plan's area bound equals the worst case that `forward_mqa()` already reserves during warmup. Decode is unchanged, and steps with at most 4 prefills still run as a single chunk.

`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py` has the same loop and is not changed here.

## Test Plan

MI355X (gfx950), TP=1, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, main `4fb767ff0a`.

- Micro: time `_forward_prefill` on live model inputs for main vs. this PR, in interleaved blocks within one process. Each scenario is one prefill step, summed over 43 layers.
- e2e: a fresh server per run, 4 runs per arm per block with the first discarded, one server on the host at a time.

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 65536 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len 307 --random-output-len 23 --random-range-ratio 0.25 \
    --num-prompts 1021 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1234
```

- Accuracy: `lm_eval --model vllm --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto`, greedy, `max_model_len=4096`, `seed=1234`. The base arm was run twice.

## Test Result

**Micro** (median of 3 runs; noise floor ≤ 1.1 %):

| prefill step | chunks main → PR | main (ms) | PR (ms) | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 × 11777 tokens | 1 → 1 | 84.6 | 84.8 | −0.2 % |
| 7 × 400–1800 | 2 → 1 | 43.6 | 40.5 | +7.8 % |
| 13 × 700–1100 | 4 → 1 | 70.5 | 58.5 | +20.9 % |
| 29 × 170–430 | 8 → 1 | 67.5 | 41.4 | +63 % |
| 53 × 90–250 | 14 → 1 | 105.0 | 37.7 | +182 % |

On gfx950, part of the gain comes from larger chunks crossing the 1024-query threshold that sends them to AITER OPUS (#54855). With routing pinned to Triton, the gains are +3.9 / +5.0 / +17 / +62 %, and outputs are bit-identical.

**e2e**, 1021 prompts in 307 / out 23 (9 base / 7 patched warm runs, ranges disjoint):

| metric | main | PR | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total tok/s | 27218 | 29075 | +6.8 % |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 5812 | 5401 | −7.1 % |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 5706 | 5328 | −6.6 % |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 272.6 | 254.9 | −6.5 % |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 275.8 | 256.5 | −7.0 % |

No regression under `--max-concurrency` 96, 48 and 3 (Δ of medians, PR vs main):

| workload | warm runs | Total tok/s | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | Mean TPOT | Median TPOT |

| in 1033 / out 131, 61 prompts, concurrency 3 | 6 / 6 | +0.5 % | +0.0 % | −3.4 % | −0.7 % | −0.5 % |

**GSM8K** (strict-match):

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Treat padded prompt tails as spec-decode rows for hybrid models
body:
The scheduler pads a one-token prompt tail over prior state (e.g. a P/D decode-node arrival) with K placeholder drafts to keep the K+1 spec-decode shape (#45237). For recurrent-state layers these rows must run the spec-decode kernels, which keep the running state and roll the rejected placeholders back; the prefill kernels store only the state after all K+1 tokens (#55178).

#52988 changed the hybrid model state to classify spec-decode rows by request state (not prefilling) instead of num_scheduled_tokens, which adaptive verification rewrites. That sent every padded tail's draft count to -1, so Mamba's padded-tail handling no longer fires and GDN/KDA build the row as a prefill, folding the placeholder tokens into the request's recurrent state.

Also count prefilling rows with exactly one remaining prompt token and prior state as decodes, still using request state only.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Emit MXFP8 from the sparse decode reduce and run wo_a as a grouped FP8 GEMM
body: ## Purpose Follow-up to #57435. That PR moved the inverse RoPE into the sparse-decode reduce epilogue, but the reduce still writes the attention output as bf16 `[T, H, 512]` and `wo_a` then reads it back through a bf16 hipBLASLt einsum (`Cijk_Alik_Bljk_BBS_BH_Bias...`) on a dequantized bf16 copy of the weight. `wo_a` is weight-bandwidth bound at decode, so it pays for twice the bytes the checkpoint actually stores. This PR takes the rest of the chain the way the SM100 path does: the reduce epilogue also emits `wo_a`'s MXFP8 input directly, and `wo_a` runs as a grouped FP8 GEMM on the checkpoint's MXFP8 weight. ``` before: sparse partial -> reduce + inv RoPE -> bf16 [T,H,512] -> bf16 einsum (dequantized W) -> wo_b after: sparse partial -> reduce + inv RoPE + MXFP8 quant/scales -> grouped MXFP8 GEMM -> wo_b ``` ## What changes - **Reduce epilogue (`_sparse_attn_decode_reduce_kernel`, `QUANT_OUT`)**: after the inverse RoPE, the fp32 row is MXFP8-quantized in registers (one E8M0 scale per 32 lanes, the `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` rounding) and stored as e4m3 plus scales. There is no bf16 write, no read-back and no standalone quant launch. - **Grouped MXFP8 `wo_a` GEMM (`rocm_mxfp8_wo_a_bmm`)**: a Triton `tl.dot_scaled` kernel for `[T, G, 4096] x [G, 1024, 4096]` on the CDNA4 MX matrix cores. It reads the e4m3 weight and per-row E8M0 scales exactly as the ROCm MXFP8 linear leaves them after loading, with no scale re-layout and no dequantized copy (the cached bf16 `wo_a` is no longer built: ~33.5 MB/layer at TP2). Tile tiers are keyed on `T * G`, tuned under HIP graphs with a cold weight. It is registered as a custom op, because the tile choice branches on the token count and `_o_proj` runs compiled. - **Prefill rows (`rocm_inverse_rope_mxfp8_rows`)**: sparse prefill still writes bf16, into a workspace slice requested together with the prefill KV gather. One pass then rotates and quantizes it into the same MXFP8 buffer, so a mixed step feeds a single `wo_a` GEMM. - **Layer (`DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention`)**: on gfx950 (`on_gfx950()`), `_alloc_attn_out` returns a `QuantizedActivation` (same contract as the SM100 mega-attention layer), and `_o_proj` runs the FP8 GEMM then `wo_b`. This replaces the bf16 path on gfx950. The bf16 path remains only for archs without MX matrix cores (gfx942), where `wo_a` is BF16-emulated anyway. ## Not a duplicate - **#57081** (open) also targets FP8 `wo_a` on MI355X, but it fuses less. It runs a standalone `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` pass over the bf16 attention output and feeds AITER's `batched_gemm_a8w8_mxscale` after re-laying the 32x32 scales into 128x128. That keeps the bf16 global-memory round trip and adds a launch per layer. It also predates #57435: it targets `vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/`, which no longer exists on main, and is marked as conflicting. This PR fuses more ops into the current path instead. The quant and scale generation live inside the #57435 reduce epilogue, and the GEMM consumes the loaded weight layout directly. The only standalone pass left is for prefill rows, which never had a fused epilogue. - **#57977** chains MXFP8 activations between DeepGEMM kernels on NVIDIA; this PR is the ROCm counterpart for the attention -> `wo_a` hop. - **#57435** is the base this builds on (merged). ## Kernel performance (MI355X, gfx950) The measured unit is the reduce plus `wo_a`. **Before:** reduce + inverse RoPE writes bf16, then the bf16 einsum. **After:** reduce + inverse RoPE + MXFP8 quant, then the grouped FP8 GEMM. Times are in µs, shown as before → after (speedup). Everything is replayed from HIP graphs, and the weight rotates across >1 GB of copies so every call is cold, as in a real step. Note that DeepSeek's reference `inference/model.py` runs `wo_a` on bf16 activations, which is why the end-to-end accuracy eval below matters. Kernel parity, from the new tests: - The reduce's MXFP8 epilogue is **bit-exact** (data and scales) against `_mxfp8_e4m3_quantize_torch` applied to the reduce's fp32 output, with and without adaptive splits. - The prefill rotate+quant pass matches inverse RoPE + MXFP8 in fp32: scales are exact and every element is within half an e4m3 step. - `rocm_mxfp8_wo_a_bmm` matches an fp32 einsum of the dequantized operands across every tile tier and partial M tiles. - The real split-K decode with `out_mxfp8` dequantizes to its bf16 output within e4m3 rounding. ## Test Plan / Results ``` $ pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py -q # MI355X 86 passed in 58.38s ``` New tests: - `test_sparse_attn_decode_reduce_mxfp8_epilogue`: bit-exact against `_mxfp8_e4m3_quantize_torch`. - `test_inverse_rope_mxfp8_rows` - `test_sparse_attn_decode_mxfp8_output`: the real decode launcher with `out_mxfp8`. - `test_rocm_mxfp8_wo_a_bmm[one case per tile tier]` The existing #57435 epilogue tests pass unchanged. `pre-commit run` (including mypy) is clean. ## Accuracy (GSM8K) DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MI355X, TP4, DSpark spec decode (5 tokens). title: [Spec Decode] Remove eager metadata rebuild during MTP fused multi-step decode
body: ## Context https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46849 added the infrastructure to fuse last N-1 draft steps into a single cudagraph for models with attention backends that support it. Currently DeepSeek V4 satisfies the conditions to enable this, when using MTP > 1. ## This PR It turns out we can remove the first attention metadata build before drafting the last N-1 speculative tokens in a fused loop. In this PR, I make the necessary changes to `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadataBuilder.update_draft_decode_metadata` and refactor `AutoRegressiveSpeculator` so that the first draft metadata build can be safely skipped during FULL cudagraph replay. With these changes, DSV4 + MTP no longer rebuilds metadata during proposal, resulting in a correctness-preserving removal of about 1ms of host work per decode step. No significant throughput improvement was observed from these changes. ## Profile Captured while serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP=3 on 4xGB200: **Before** **After** In the decode step above, `propose`'s CPU time shrinks by an entire millisecond. ## Benchmarks / Evals **Setup.** DeepSeek-V4-Flash, MTP with `num_speculative_tokens=3`, 4x GB200 (TP4), `--block-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --moe-backend deep_gemm --no-enable-prefix-caching`, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. Baseline is `main` at `34b069080d`; PR is `cfb93dedca`. One server per arm; trace, benchmark and eval share it. ### Speed-Bench 2K/2K (`throughput_16k`, `low_entropy`, temperature 0) Prompts scaled 8x concurrency (min 16), seed 0. Greedy decoding keeps acceptance deterministic, so ITL p50 is the step-time metric. | Concurrency | ITL p50 base (ms) | ITL p50 PR (ms) | Δ | TPOT p50 base (ms) | TPOT p50 PR (ms) | Output tok/s base | Output tok/s PR | Δ | Accept. len base | Accept. len PR | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 8.97 | 8.97 | 0.0% | 3.41 | 3.42 | 290.3 | 288.3 | -0.7% | 2.705 | 2.685 | | 16 | 19.13 | 19.15 | +0.1% | 8.71 | 8.57 | 1806.7 | 1819.4 | +0.7% | 2.664 | 2.717 | | 64 | 22.96 | 22.96 | 0.0% | 14.52 | 14.58 | 4415.5 | 4380.6 | -0.8% | 2.693 | 2.693 | Step time is unchanged at every concurrency. The ~1 ms of host work removed per step is not on the critical path for this model at TP4; throughput deltas track the small acceptance-length differences and are within noise. ### AIME25 (MQA, 2 epochs x 30 problems, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, max 98304 tokens, 64 concurrent) | Arm | Exact match | pass@2 | Samples | Request errors | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | base | 0.9333 | 0.9667 | 60 | 0 | | PR | 0.9333 | 0.9333 | 60 | 0 | Mean accuracy identical. pass@2 differs by one problem in 30, which is expected sampling variance at temperature 1.

title: [KV Connector] Fix DecodeBench fp8 fill values and add a startup fill mode
body:
## Purpose

Two changes to `DecodeBenchConnector`, one commit each:

- **Fix fp8 fill values.** fp8 KV caches are stored as `uint8`, and the fill used `torch.full(fill_mean, dtype=uint8)`, which truncates to 0. So the dummy prompt KV was all zeros, and random fill (`fill_std > 0`) raised.
  - Plain fp8 `uint8` caches now get the fill encoded in their fp8 dtype (platform e4m3, or e5m2 for `fp8_e5m2`).
  - Random values are sampled in float32 and clamped to the finite range.
  - Packed `uint8` layouts with scales or metadata (e.g. `fp8_ds_mla`, NVFP4) keep the zero fill, now with a one-time warning.
- **Add an opt-in `startup_fill` option** (`kv_connector_extra_config`).
  - Today's per-request fill runs inside the decode steps that admit new requests. For every layer it copies block IDs to the device, filters them with a boolean mask (a device sync) and builds a temporary tensor.
  - With `startup_fill`, the worker fills the KV cache once in `register_kv_caches` and skips the per-request fill.
  - Circular-buffer groups, and attention groups whose new blocks the engine zeroes (hybrid Mamba, mixed precision), keep the per-request fill, so the dummy KV is never left as zeros.
  - The fill isn't redone after sleep mode. The default behavior is unchanged.
- No open PR covers either change. #57751, which fixes Mamba state filling in the default mode, is complementary.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_decode_bench_connector.py`. New tests:
  - read-back as fp8 for `fp8` / `fp8_e5m2` `uint8` caches and a `float8_e4m3fn` cache, with constant and random fill;
  - a packed layout stays zero;
  - startup fill of strided, padded and fp8 caches;
  - no per-step fill;
  - circular-buffer and engine-zeroed groups keep the per-request fill.
- KV read-back on the workers, in the default mode and with `startup_fill`:
  - `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`;
  - `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` TP4 with fp8 main KV and fp8 indexer KV.

title: [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Keep pinned PLE prefetch ids out of the CUDA graph pool
body:
## Problem and fix

Fixes #58441. With `engram_config.cpu_offload=True`, `Qwen4ExpPLEPinnedHostEmbedding.start_prefetch` launches the PLE lookup on a side stream and returns; `_finalize_prefetch` joins it one decoder layer later. Qwen4Exp defaults to breakable CUDA graphs, so for PIECEWISE batches (prefill/mixed batches up to the capture size, or every batch with `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`) `start_prefetch` is an eager break and its arguments are replaced by `weak_ref_tensor`s. Two things then combine:

- `gathered_ids.record_stream(prefetch_stream)` is a no-op: with `etp_data_parallel_size == 1`, `gathered_ids` is the weak ref itself, and the caching allocator skips `recordStream` for storage it does not own.
- The only strong reference to the ids is the local `ngram_ids` in `Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding.start_prefetch`, which drops as soon as it returns, while the next segment is already being captured. The graph-pool block goes straight back to the free list and the rest of the preceding decoder layer can be captured on top of it.

At replay the side stream reads the ids while the main stream may be overwriting them, so greedy outputs silently stop being reproducible.

The fix computes the prefetch ids into a persistent per-layer buffer through the existing `output=` argument of `compute_ngram_ids`. This mirrors the persistent `_prefetch_buffer` already used for the lookup output, adds no kernel or copy, and costs `max_num_batched_tokens * ngram_heads * 8` bytes per PLE layer. FULL graphs and eager runs were already safe (the argument stays a real tensor there), and ETP spanning DP is unaffected (the ids are re-gathered into a fresh tensor inside the eager break).

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py
```

- **51 passed** on GB200. The new `test_ngram_prefetch_ids_outlive_start_prefetch` reproduces the lifetime bug without a full graph capture: the prefetch stub keeps a weak ref to the ids, as the eager break does, and a fresh `MemPool` makes the next same-size allocation reuse freed storage, as a later graph segment would. On main the weak ref reads the overwritten `-1`s (3/3 runs); with this change it reads the reference ids.
- Pre-commit passed.
- No model eval: the ids are produced by the same kernel into a different buffer, so outputs only change where the race corrupted them. The reporter's cold/warm greedy table in #58441 (8/8 identical once the ids are in a persistent buffer) covers the end-to-end effect.

## Related work and AI assistance

Open-PR search found no equivalent fix. #57785 joins side-stream work during breakable capture and does not affect replay (row 2 of the table in #58441); #57497 and #58439 move or add PLE backends without changing this lifetime.

Claude Code assisted with root-causing, implementation and validation; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

title: [BUG] Fix KV offload shared-memory slot selection using worker rank
body:
# KV offload selects the wrong shared-memory slot when device index differs from worker rank

## Description

CPU and Tiering KV offload select a worker's shared-memory slot using the
physical device index modulo the worker world size. The device index is not
necessarily the worker's rank, so this can select the wrong slot in a
non-replicated layout.

For example, with `world_size=4`, `rank=1`, and `device_index=6`, the current
calculation selects slot `6 % 4 = 2` instead of slot `1`. Workers can therefore
read or write a different slot from the one assigned to their rank.

## Expected behavior

Non-replicated layouts should select the shared-memory slot using the worker
rank. Replicated layouts should continue to use slot `0`.
~

title: [Bugfix][DSV4.1] Avoid host sync in ViT CUDA graph replay metadata
body:
## Purpose

`(H200 MIG 35GB) Multimodal Models (Extended Generation 1)` has failed on every main build since 2026-09-20 (first failure: build 90097). The failing test is `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py::test_vit_cudagraph_image[deepseek_v41]`. Example: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90589#01a0ccda-d883-4363-b95b-3c0434c9726e

```
encoder_cudagraph.py _run_budget_graph -> model.prepare_encoder_cudagraph_replay_buffers
deepseek_v41/common/vl_cudagraph.py -> build_packed_vit_metadata
deepseek_v4/common/vision.py:282   cos = torch.cat(cos_list).to(device)
gpu_sync_debug.py:81 RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected - avoid it or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()
```

CI runs with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. The encoder CUDA graph path added in #56625 syncs the host in two places. The `deepseek_v41` test entry has no `core_model` mark, so it only runs in the Extended lane, not on the PR.

1. `build_packed_vit_metadata` / `build_packed_merge_metadata` copy host tensors to the GPU with pageable `.to(device)` / `torch.tensor(..., device=...)`. The eager `DeepseekV4ViT.forward` RoPE tables do the same.
2. After (1) is fixed, `postprocess_encoder_output` fails next. It copies `types` with a pageable `.to()`, then builds the span with boolean-mask assignment (`index_put_` calls `nonzero`, which syncs).

## Changes

- `vision.py`: use `async_tensor_h2d` (pinned staging, `non_blocking`) for cos/sin, `cu_seqlens`, `merge_idx`, `merge_mask`, and the eager RoPE tables. `max_seqlen` stays on CPU.
- `vl_cudagraph.py::postprocess_encoder_output`: build the gather index on the host from `types`, which is a CPU tensor, and copy it with `async_tensor_h2d`. The span is then assembled with a single index into `[aligner rows, image_start, image_newline, image_end]`. The result is still a freshly allocated tensor, so later replays cannot overwrite it. I checked on CPU that this matches the old masked-fill output bit for bit, across several grids.

I left the eager `_build_image_span` unchanged. I also did not add `core_model` to the test entry: several other entries (step3_vl, ernie45_vl) are also Extended-only, and adding it would put a DSV4.1 model build into the per-PR Standard 4 lane. Reviewers can decide whether to promote it.

## Not a duplicate

On 2026-09-23 I searched open PRs for `deepseek v4 vision`, `vit cudagraph deepseek`, `56625`, `vl_cudagraph` and `deepseek gpu sync`. None of the results touch these code paths. The closest one, #57898, changes DSV4.1 profiling in `mm_preprocess.py` only.

## Test Plan / Results

I ran this on an H200 using the CI image `vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:e9f167129c09` (main), with the patched files bind-mounted over the installed package:

```
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest -v -s models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -k deepseek_v41
```

- Before (unpatched image): `1 failed, 1 skipped`. It fails with the same `GPU<->CPU sync detected` in `build_packed_vit_metadata`, matching CI.
- With only the `vision.py` change: still fails, now at `postprocess_encoder_output` (`types.to(...)`).
- With both changes: `1 passed, 1 skipped` (video is skipped for this model). The log shows the encoder CUDA graph was captured and used, with no sync errors.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes (ruff, mypy).

I have not run model evals. The span-assembly change is an exact rewrite, confirmed by the bit-for-bit CPU check. The H2D changes affect only how the copies are made, not the values.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change. @khluu will review every changed line before merge.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Use the shared prefill chunk plan in the ROCm sparse prefill
body:
## Purpose

`DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention._forward_prefill` splits prefill requests into fixed groups of `PREFILL_CHUNK_SIZE = 4` and sizes the bf16 gather workspace from the static worst case (`N = ceil(max_model_len / compress_ratio)`, `M = N + window_size + max_num_batched_tokens`). The NVIDIA V4.1 paths already use `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadata.get_prefill_chunk_plan()`, which packs requests by workspace area and returns each chunk's real widths.

This PR drives the ROCm V4.1 prefill loop from the same plan. As on NVIDIA, it passes `has_compressed=not swa_only`, because ratio-1 layers carry a compressed region. Each chunk's KV is a `(chunk_size, chunk_M, head_dim)` view of the single prefill workspace, which also holds the MXFP8 staging rows, and `chunk_N` / `chunk_M` go to the SWA gather and `combine_topk_swa_indices`.

The ROCm V4.1 combine runs two `torch.repeat_interleave` calls per chunk, each forcing a host sync, so steps with more than 4 prefill requests gain the most. Peak memory is unchanged: the plan's area bound equals the worst case that `forward_mqa()` already reserves during warmup. Decode is unchanged, and steps with at most 4 prefills still run as a single chunk.

The same change for DeepSeek-V4 is #58405. #56720 touches this loop and composes with it.

## Test Plan

MI355X (gfx950), `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `kv_cache_dtype=fp8`, main `bbd7c24d6e`.

- **Micro:** time `_forward_prefill` on live model inputs for main vs. this PR, in interleaved blocks within one process. Each scenario is one prefill step. The model is DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash truncated to 6 layers with dummy weights (compress ratios 0, 0, 2, 2, 1, 1), TP=1, `max_model_len=65536`, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`.
- **Reach:** under the default serving config, where main selects `CompilationMode.NONE` with FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs for V4.1, `_forward_prefill` runs on every prefill step on all layers.
- **e2e:** real-weight DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP=2, a fresh server per run, 4 runs per arm per block with the first discarded, one server on the host at a time.

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash -tp 2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 65536 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len 307 --random-output-len 23 --random-range-ratio 0.25 \
    --num-prompts 1021 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1234
```

- **e2e at TP=4, 1k/1k:** one server per arm (warmed, prefix caching off), `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536 --max-num-seqs 512`, `--num-prompts` = 10 × concurrency, 3 runs per point.

```bash
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio <0|0.25> \
    --num-prompts <10 x conc> --max-concurrency <512|128|32> --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1234
```

- **Accuracy:** `lm_eval --model vllm --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto`, greedy, `max_model_len=4096`, `seed=1234`, on real-weight DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP=2. Main was run three times and this PR twice.

## Test Result

**Micro:** sum over 6 layers, median of 3 runs, noise floor ≤ 0.9 %.

| prefill step | chunks main → PR | main (ms) | PR (ms) | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 × 11777 tokens | 1 → 1 | 18.5 | 18.5 | −0.0 % |
| 7 × 400–1800 | 2 → 1 | 16.6 | 11.6 | +43 % |
| 13 × 700–1100 | 4 → 1 | 29.8 | 15.0 | +99 % |
| 29 × 170–430 | 8 → 1 | 45.3 | 11.2 | +305 % |
| 53 × 90–250 | 14 → 1 | 74.6 | 10.3 | +621 % |

On gfx950, part of the gain comes from larger chunks crossing the 1024-query threshold that sends them to AITER OPUS (#54855). With routing pinned to Triton, the gains are +24 / +51 / +189 / +411 %, and outputs are bit-identical.

**e2e**, 1021 prompts in 307 / out 23 (6 warm runs per arm, ranges disjoint):

| metric | main | PR | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total tok/s | 14563 | 22407 | +53.9 % |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 11678 | 7359 | −37.0 % |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 11677 | 7282 | −37.6 % |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 502.4 | 327.9 | −34.8 % |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 499.0 | 329.0 | −34.1 % |

With `--max-concurrency 3`, no step carries more than 3 prefills, so every step runs as one chunk on both sides (Δ of medians, PR vs main):

| workload | warm runs | Total tok/s | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | Mean TPOT | Median TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| in 1033 / out 131, 61 prompts, concurrency 3 | 6 / 6 | −0.9 % | +2.0 % | +2.4 % | +0.8 % | +0.7 % |

The two arms' ranges overlap (p = 0.07), and within-block drift is ±1 %.

**e2e at TP=4, 1k/1k** (median of 3 runs, Δ PR vs main):

| range ratio | concurrency | Total tok/s | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | Mean TPOT | Median TPOT |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 512 | +6.9 % | −19.4 % | −19.9 % | −4.7 % | −4.5 % |
| 0 | 128 | +3.4 % | −16.9 % | −43.0 % | −1.6 % | +2.5 % |
| 0 | 32 | +2.6 % | −22.4 % | −24.0 % | −0.6 % | −0.1 % |
| 0.25 | 512 | +0.0 % | −15.8 % | +0.7 % | +0.3 % | +0.3 % |
| 0.25 | 128 | +0.5 % | −12.0 % | −0.3 % | −0.3 % | −0.2 % |
| 0.25 | 32 | −0.1 % | −6.9 % | +0.7 % | +0.2 % | +0.3 % |

With fixed lengths (ratio 0), finished requests are replaced together, so every wave of admissions is a prefill step with dozens of requests. Throughput ranges are disjoint at each concurrency, and the gain is mostly in TTFT.

With ratio 0.25, completions spread out and later steps rarely carry more than 4 prefills. Throughput and median latency are unchanged; only the opening burst gets faster, which shows up in mean TTFT.

**GSM8K** (strict-match):

| model | main | main (repeats) | PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | 0.9318 | 0.9310 / 0.9310 | 0.9272 / 0.9295 |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (does not reach this path) | 0.7013 | 0.7081 | 0.7028 / 0.7089 |

title: [ROCm][MLA] Route gfx942 DCP causal multi-token verify to Triton split-KV decode
body:
## Purpose

On gfx942, `ROCM_AITER_MLA` has no kernel for DSpark/MTP target verify under DCP
(causal qlen > 1 on a sharded KV cache): no ASM heuristic, no cprr kernels, and
AITER segmented MLA exceeds gfx942's 64 KiB LDS (`OutOfResources: Required:
131072`) for bf16 KV at TILE-128 and for fp8 KV with 128 heads.

This PR adds a `TRITON` DCP route for that shape only. It runs the existing
split-KV `decode_attention_fwd` over the rank-local verify rows, and the MLA
layer merges the per-rank fp32 LSEs as before. Empty shards return LSE = −inf
and get zero weight, so no masking is needed.

The split count is capped by batch occupancy. Without the cap, max-batch scratch
is 8–16 GiB and overflows the kernel's int32 offsets; with it, 0.25 GiB and
equal or faster.

Unchanged: qlen == 1, non-causal, replicated-KV DSpark, gfx950, and TRITON_MLA
(its `forward_mqa` moves into the shared helper with the same behaviour).

Serve command that fails:
```
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
    --served-model-name kimi-k3 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
    --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
    --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
    --max-model-len 135168 \
    --max-num-seqs 8 \
    --max_num_batched_tokens 4096 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --quantization-config '{"moe":{"weight":"int4_per_group_32"}}' \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", "model": "Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark", "num_speculative_tokens": 5, "attention
_backend": "TRITON_MLA", "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic", "rejection_sample_method": "block"}' \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000
```

## Test Plan

pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_{dcp_cprr,fp8_decode_routing,mtp_split,dcp_cprr_numerics,dcp_verify_gfx942}.py

`test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_verify_gfx942.py` is the regression test. It runs the
real AITER builder and `forward_mqa` for all 8 DCP ranks and checks the merged
output against causal attention:

| Case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Kimi-K3: 96 heads, bf16 KV, qlen 6, 768-token blocks | `OutOfResources` | pass (Triton) |
| DeepSeek-V3: 128 heads, fp8 KV, qlen 2, 16-token blocks | `OutOfResources` | pass (Triton) |
| 96 heads, bf16 KV, 64-token blocks | pass | pass (segmented, unchanged) |

`test_segmented_lds_gate_matches_the_kernel` compiles the AITER kernel at the
boundary shapes and checks the gate against the actual compile result.

## Test Result

- [X] MI325X: 559 passed, 4 skipped (gfx950-only).
- [X] MI325X DSpark only: still ASM
- [X] MI325X DCP only (no drafter): still ASM
- [X] MI325X DSpark+DCP (this PR): target verify (qlen>1) + later qlen==1 decode

ons", "num_concurrent": 32, "max_retries": 10, "max_gen_toks": 2048, "tokenizer_backend":"None","tokenized_requests":"False" }' --tasks gsm8k --b

title: [ROCm][CI] Mirror the DSv4-Flash disaggregated DP EP group on MI355
body:
## Purpose

**Split out of #50519.** That PR mirrors the H200 DSv4-Flash P/D accuracy group
(#42310) on eight MI355X: a TP=4 prefiller against a DP=4 EP decoder over
NixlConnector. It comes along here because the fix below has nothing to
exercise it without a group.

**The mirror repeats the parent env**, which it does not inherit, and two of
the entries have to be written even though they are empty.
`run_accuracy_test.sh` defaults the two KV layouts to HND when they are unset,
and DeepSeek-V4 packs its indexer pages beside the MLA latent pages inside each
block, so `DeepseekV4IndexerBackend` accepts only the block-outermost BLHNC and
BLNHC. With HND both engines die before they load a single weight.

**What it exposed: NIXL cannot register a padded KV allocation.** #53698 rounds
the shared allocation up to a 4096-byte page so MoRIIO can register the whole
backing as one RDMA memory region, and #54247 narrowed that to ROCm.
`register_kv_caches` decides a cache is block-major by comparing
`num_blocks * block_stride` against the registered length exactly, so a padded
allocation fails the test and falls into the segmented branch, where
`cache.nbytes % segment_bytes` kills the engine during initialization. Here the
sliding-window layer misses by a 2816-byte tail. #54021 hardened the block-copy
path against the same padding and #53974 documented the regression; NIXL was
never fixed. The path is entirely on `main`.

**The fix widens the test by one block.** The tail is shorter than a page, so
shorter than a block: it cannot hold another block and cannot make block-major
storage segmented. `storage_block_len` then comes from `block_stride`, which is
what dividing the registered length evaluated to whenever the old equality held
and which stays exact once a tail is present. Registration still uses the whole
registered length, so a connector that needs the padded allocation in one
memory region still gets it.

## Test Plan

`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`, with a new case that
registers the same two overlaid MLA layers on an exact and on a padded
allocation and requires identical descriptor geometry, and the new group on
8x MI355X (gfx950).

## Test Result

Unit tests go from 210 to 212 passed. The group goes from an engine that dies
in `register_kv_caches` to 2 passed with accuracy 0.9568.

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Keep the compressor ring out of the null block
body:
## Purpose

`_ring_slot_mapping_kernel` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/compressor.py`) maps each token to `block_table[req, 0] * capacity + pos % capacity`. Warmup and CUDA-graph capture run dummy batches whose block tables are zeroed, so their compressor state rows are written into **block 0**. That is the null block, and every KV-cache group shares it. The fp32 state bytes therefore land in other layers' pages. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, layer 2's ring overlaps the sliding-window KV of layers 0–13, and layer 8's overlaps layers 0–27.

Why it matters: sparse MLA decode kernels gather the null block for masked candidates and weight it by zero. When the bytes decode to a non-finite value, 0 × NaN is still NaN. On sm_120 (FlashInfer's DSv4 sparse decode) with DSpark speculative decoding and FULL CUDA graphs, this produced wrong outputs on the first request (0 accepted drafts), then `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` / Xid 31 MMU faults on the next prefill.

The bug is latent without DSpark too: block 0 still ends dirty (we measured 29 NaN bytes). It used to be masked because `warmup_kernels` ran after `capture_model`, and that warmup zeroed block 0 again. `gpu_worker.py` now runs `warmup_kernels` before `capture_model`, so the bytes survive into serving.

The fix maps tokens whose ring block is 0 to PAD (`-1`), which the ring consumers already skip. Real requests never own block 0, so their mapping is unchanged.

## Test Plan

- New `test_v41_compressor_ring_never_writes_the_null_block`, next to the existing `test_v41_compressor_metadata_maps_tokens_to_their_ring`: a dummy request on block 0 must map to PAD, and a real request next to it must keep its ring slots.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on the touched files.

## Test Result

- Both tests pass with the fix. As a control, the new test fails without it: `assert [0, 1, 25, 26] == [-1, -1, 25, 26]`, i.e. the dummy tokens are written to slots 0 and 1 of the null block. This ran on an RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120) in the `nightly-e9757321` image with the patched `compressor.py`, using the two test functions verbatim (the full test file imports modules newer than that nightly).
- End-to-end on 8× RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP8, DSpark (`num_speculative_tokens=5`), FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs, prefix caching, v0.30.0 plus our sm_120 page-geometry patch (needed to serve this model on sm_120 at all, and unrelated to this change):
  - without the fix: block 0 of every sliding-window layer is non-finite after capture, the first request decodes garbage, and the next ~1.6k-token prefill raises Xid 31;
  - with the fix: all 13 block-0 views stay clean through capture and 11,000 decode steps (including c16 load); needle retrieval 9/9, greedy determinism and shared-prefix divergence checks pass; 0 Xid; c1 131 tok/s, c16 672 tok/s, DSpark acceptance 0.38.
- Not verified: an end-to-end run on current `main`, and GPUs other than sm_120.

A related robustness point, arguably for FlashInfer: its SM120 DSv4 sparse decode is only correct while slot 0 is finite, because masked candidates still contribute 0 × V.

AI assistance was used to find this bug and write the patch and test. The tests above were run as described.

title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Remove redundant copy after ragged sparse MLA
body:
## Purpose Avoid an extra copy by storing the sparse prefill output in place. This is a **tiny** perf improvement (5us per MLA layer), meaning a total of ~55us per forward. With ~13ms per forward this means it's not quite measurable within the noise from vllm bench serve. Hence will skip full perf sweep and only provide correctness results and simple non-regression benchmark. ## Why - The attention output has shape `[s, h, kv_lora_rank]`, i.e. without the rope dim - The kernel's output is sized like the query, i.e. `[s, h, kv_lora_rank + rope_dim]` - Once the kernel completes, it slices out the first `:kv_lora_rank` part of the head dimension. We delegate this last part to triton instead. title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] BF16 splitk kernel for sparse MLA decode
body:
## Purpose Decode rows in the bf16 sparse MLA path go through the ragged **prefill** kernel, whose grid is `(q_len, heads_blocks)`. GLM-5.3-Flash at TP8 has one head block, so during decode with concurrency 4 launches only 4 workgroups on 256 CUs. Clearly underutilized. This new kernel instead uses splitK+reduce over the context dim, i.e. with a grid `(q_len, num_kv_splits, heads_blocks)`. DSv4 has a similar one. Enabled if topk>=512, as microbenchmarks suggest (GLM uses topk=2048). **Perf: e2e -5-15% ITL. title: [Kernel][DSV4.1] Fuse MoE finalize into the TP all-reduce + mHC boundary
body:
## Purpose

DSV4.1 decode (TP4, `0 < M <= 16`, FULL CUDA graphs) closes every sublayer with a fused TP all-reduce + mHC kernel. After an MoE, that boundary is preceded by FlashInfer's MoE finalize (top-k weighted sum) and a separate shared-expert add. This PR folds the finalize and the shared add into the boundary:

- **Vendored FlashInfer LL kernels.** `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/cute_dsl/` copies FlashInfer's CuTe DSL low-latency MNNVL all-reduce (`flashinfer/comm/mnnvl_cutedsl/kernel_ll`, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer@139af6f6, the H5120 presets):
  - `_SharedOnlyPublishDeviceKernel` and `_group_leader_block_sum` are byte-identical to upstream.
  - `_QuadFinalizePublishDeviceKernel` is upstream's plus an `fp32_weights` option. DSV4.1's router emits FP32 top-k weights with the routed scaling folded in; FlashInfer loads BF16.
  - `_LamportMHCDeviceKernel` is upstream's `_LamportResidualRMSNormDeviceKernel`. Its residual add and copy are replaced by the mHC post-mix of the hc streams (stored as the new residual) and their pre-mix collapse, which the unchanged RMSNorm then normalizes. This replaces `torch.ops._C_custom_ar.all_reduce_mhc` (#57643) on the overlap path. That CUDA kernel has no other user, so this PR deletes `csrc/libtorch_stable/all_reduce_mhc.cu` and its CMake entry. #57643's boundary wiring (`reduce_results`, `fuse_mhc_all_reduce`, `supports_mhc_all_reduce`) is kept and reused.
- **MoE left unfinalized, via #58635.** For layers whose experts are the modular TRTLLM MXFP4 ones, DSV4.1 requests deferral once at model build with `moe_config.defer_moe_finalize(MHC_OVERLAP_MAX_TOKENS)`. Per call, `should_defer_moe_finalize(M)` picks the path, and the experts return a single `UnfinalizedMoEOutput`. This PR touches no fused-MoE code.
- **DSV4.1 wiring (model file only, no new runner).**
  - A layer defers when its successor opens with the fused boundary: 37/40 layers on DSV4.1-Flash. The last layer and the layers before an engram layer finalize as before.
  - `DeepseekV4MoE.forward_unfinalized` runs the runner's `_forward_impl` directly, since the custom op returns tensors only. It hands `MoEOutput(routed=UnfinalizedMoEOutput, shared_output=...)` to the next layer.
  - `mhc_shifted_post_pre` calls `AllReduceMHC.finalize`, so top-k reduce, shared add, all-reduce and mHC post/pre run as two PDL-chained kernels.
  - Outside FULL graphs (eager/PIECEWISE), the next mixes run inline instead of on the side stream.
  - `MHC_OVERLAP_MAX_TOKENS` (16), the side-stream design and the M > 16 path are unchanged.

Duplicate check: #58635 (merged) supplies the modular-path deferral this builds on. #52601 (MoE tail all-reduce fusion for MiniMax-M3, last updated 2026-09-02) targets a different model and kernel. No open PR fuses the DSV4.1 MoE finalize into the mHC boundary.

## Test Plan

Unless noted, everything below is on main 378504a544 (includes #58635) plus this change, with main's pins: flashinfer 0.7.0, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1, torch 2.13.0+cu130. Hardware is DSV4.1-Flash on TP4 GB300.

- Kernel regression test: `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py::test_all_reduce_mhc_matches_unfused_path`, which replaces #57643's CUDA-kernel test. It checks against the unfused math in torch (FP32 rank sum → BF16, mHC post FMA chain → BF16, collapse → BF16, RMSNorm). Run as `pytest -v -s tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py` with ray workers; all 51 tests in the file passed on 4× GB300. It covers M in {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 12, 16}, visited in shrinking and growing order, ±0 sentinel inputs, CUDA graph replay with mutated inputs, and the finalize path with padded/permuted rows and an invalid (−1) route.
- `pre-commit run` (ruff, typos, SPDX, forbidden imports, test tethering, mypy 3.10) and `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual` on the changed files.
- In-engine numerical check (ad-hoc patch, not in this PR) under FULL CUDA graphs.
- E2E perf, `vllm bench serve`: random 1024 in / 256 out, `--ignore-eos`, concurrency 1/4/8/16.
- Accuracy with mqa, using the eval config of this model's existing recipes. GPQA-Diamond runs at concurrency 16 so decode batches take the fused path.

Server: `vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 128 --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192`. GPQA used `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --max-model-len 65536 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384` instead. The baseline arm is the same tree with deferral disabled, so both arms share the new all-reduce + mHC kernel and differ only in the MoE finalize.

## Test Result

**Correctness**
- Regression test: PASSED.
  - Post-mixed hc streams: bit-identical to the torch reference.
  - Fused-finalize path: bit-identical to an FP32 FMA-chain reference fed through the same collective.
  - Normalized layer input: within 1 BF16 ULP of the torch reference. The RMSNorm is FlashInfer's, which sums the squares in another order and uses an approximate rsqrt.
  - Before the CUDA kernel was deleted, an earlier revision of this test compared against it directly: the hc streams were bit-identical and the normalized input was within 1 ULP.
- In-engine, FULL graphs: on each rank, the fused boundary was compared against the plain collective run on a torch finalize of the same buffers, inside the same graphs. Over a GSM8K run, 51,393 fused boundaries ran per rank, of which 1,295 were host calls (eager or capture) and the rest graph replays. Both the post-mixed hc streams and the normalized input matched bit-for-bit: 0 of 1.6e10 elements differed, on every rank.
- Before the rebase, an eager check over 55,500 deferred MoE calls found the deferred GEMM2 rows plus an FP32 top-k sum bit-identical to FlashInfer's own finalized output.

**E2E decode.** Random 1024/256:

| concurrency | median ITL base → PR (ms) | median TPOT base → PR (ms) | output tok/s base → PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.14 → 5.03 | 5.15 → 5.05 | 174.7 → 177.8 (+1.8%) |
| 4 | 5.71 → 5.56 | 5.71 → 5.58 | 581.7 → 591.7 (+1.7%) |
| 8 | 6.30 → 6.17 | 6.30 → 6.15 | 1069.7 → 1089.8 (+1.9%) |
| 16 | 7.19 → 7.13 | 7.36 → 7.64 | 1818.6 → 1817.6 (flat) |

At concurrency 16, TPOT moves with prefill interference, so median ITL is the steadier number. Over every c=16 sweep in this work, base median ITL ranged 7.19–7.39 ms (4 sweeps) and fused-finalize 7.13–7.24 ms (5 sweeps, including kernel iterations before the mirror). The pre-rebase sweep measured c=16 at +3.0% throughput.

**Kernel level** (before the rebase; the kernel file is unchanged). One decoder layer, two boundaries each followed by a sublayer, in µs. Each arm is timed as the slope between CUDA graphs of 8 and 40 calls, max over ranks, median of 50 replays:

| M | sublayers only | before (CUDA all_reduce_mhc, MoE finalizes itself) | CuTe LL, MoE finalizes itself | this PR (fused finalize) | Δ vs before |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 38.19 | 48.59 | 48.15 | 45.28 | −3.31 |
| 4 | 70.91 | 82.50 | 81.43 | 79.22 | −3.28 |
| 8 | 105.36 | 117.61 | 116.34 | 111.61 | −6.00 |
| 16 | 171.30 | 186.22 | 184.91 | 180.26 | −5.96 |

**Accuracy**

| eval | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K (5-shot completions, greedy, n=1319, concurrency 16), 3 runs each | 0.9295 / 0.9287 / 0.9272, mean 0.9285 | 0.9249 / 0.9287 / 0.9265, mean 0.9267 |
| GPQA-Diamond (chat, thinking, temp 1.0, top_p 0.95, 57344 tokens, 4 epochs), exact match / pass@4 | 0.9040 / 0.9545 | 0.9066 / 0.9444 |

- Two GSM8K runs of the same code differ on about 46 of 1319 questions, so a single run has an SD of about 0.35 pt.
- Before the rebase, 13 base runs and 20 runs across fused-finalize variants averaged 0.9275 vs 0.9238. A control whose finalize rounds exactly like the unfused path (bit-identical per-rank contribution) trailed by the same amount. The per-question shift was diffuse (net about 5 of 1319, none consistently broken). So that gap was not the fused arithmetic; my best guess is timing-dependent batching, but it is unexplained. On this rebase it is 0.18 pt over 3 runs each.
- GPQA-Diamond: 0 request errors and no empty answers in either arm; 6 (base) and 1 (PR) of 792 generations hit the token cap. pass@4 differs by 2 of 198 questions. The pre-rebase pair was 0.904 vs 0.904. This model's dashboard history for the same config (4-epoch runs) has median 0.909 and IQR 0.906–0.913.

## Notes

- Like upstream, `_QuadFinalizePublishDeviceKernel` reads the routing metadata before `griddepcontrol.wait`. That is safe only if the preceding GEMM2 triggers its dependents after its own wait. The graph-mode check saw no mismatch; a wait-first variant measured about 0.08 ms/step slower at concurrency 1 (on a different node) with no accuracy difference.
- Moving the prenorm GEMM + Sinkhorn onto the critical path instead of the side stream was measured: +17–20 µs per decoder layer at M = 1–32, with the mixes inline or with TileLang's fused post + prenorm GEMM. So the side stream stays.

title: [Perf][DSv4] Fuse inverse RoPE + FP8 quant into FlashInfer sparse MLA
body:
## Purpose

FlashInfer 0.7.0 (already pinned) ships the TRTLLM-GEN DSv4 sparse-MLA **RopeQuant** epilogue (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4918): the kernel applies the inverse RoPE to the attention output and casts it to FP8 with packed UE8M0 scales, in the layout DeepGEMM's `fp8_einsum` consumes. This PR uses it on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` for DeepSeek V4, so `wo_a` reads the kernel's FP8 output directly instead of a bf16 `[T, 128, 512]` output plus a separate `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` pass.

It mirrors the pattern the DSv4.1 FlashMLA mega-attention layer already uses (`_alloc_attn_out` returning a `QuantizedActivation` that `_o_proj` consumes whole).

### Changes
- `DeepseekV4Attention` gets an `_alloc_attn_out` hook. The default stays the padded bf16 buffer (still head-sliced before `_o_proj`), so the FlashMLA, SM120, ROCm, XPU and CPU layers are unchanged.
- `DeepseekV4FlashInferMLAAttention` allocates RopeQuant's buffers. `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` now also takes a `QuantizedActivation`: it skips `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` and feeds the kernel's FP8 output and scales straight to `fp8_einsum`.
- The launcher requires the output's group stride to equal `sum_q` (it has no stride field for O), so a token slice of a shared buffer is rejected. Both the decode and prefill calls therefore span the full, CUDA-graph-padded buffer and select their tokens through `cum_seq_lens_q`; the prefill call's offsets are not rebased. Rows outside `cum_seq_lens_q` are never read or written (checked with garbage pad rows under `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`).
- `build_flashinfer_mixed_sparse_indices` gains `num_rows` so it can size its outputs for those rows while computing only the real tokens.
- **DSpark non-causal decode (bugfix, affects the unfused path too).** The kernel treats every entry of its active index ranges as a key: the first `min(128, pos + 1)` columns (the query's causal SWA window) and `[128, sparse_topk_lens)`. `-1` is not skipped. DSpark's non-causal decode rows were copied in as one contiguous run with `sparse_topk_lens` set to the full row width. So the `-1` padding past the run was attended as keys, and with fewer than 128 context tokens the causal window also cut out the later block tokens. The builder now fills each row's causal window with the first visible entries, puts the rest from column 128 on, and sets `sparse_topk_lens` to exactly that. Every draft token then sees the whole block at any context length. Because the decode call passes real `seq_lens`, RopeQuant's derived positions match `positions` for the draft too. This is the DSv4 counterpart of #57432, which fixed the same two problems for DSv4.1 only; DSv4 reads neither of the metadata fields it added. #57432 presents each draft token as its own sequence with the full request length. RopeQuant cannot use that, because it derives RoPE positions from `seq_lens`. So this change keeps the real `seq_lens` and lays out each row around the query's causal window instead.

### When it is on
Automatically, with no flag, when all of these hold:
- exactly 128 local query heads (DSv4-Pro at TP1 or with DP attention). The kernel has one fixed 128-head schedule; padding fewer heads up to 128 measured slower;
- per-tensor FP8 KV cache;
- FP8 `wo_a`.

DSv4 has 8 heads per `wo_a` group at every TP size, so 128 local heads always means the kernel's 16 × 8 layout. That is DSv4-Pro at TP1 or with DP attention; Pro at TP2–16 and Flash have fewer heads and keep the existing path.

This includes the non-causal DSpark draft. The one inexact case is a draft block running past `max_model_len`: the draft clamps its positions there and RopeQuant does not reproduce the clamp, which only affects those drafts.

Everything else keeps the existing path.

## Not a duplicate
I searched open and closed PRs for RopeQuant, `dsv4_inv_rope_cos_sin_cache`, flashinfer#4918, and fused inverse-RoPE/FP8 on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`. No PR wires this epilogue into vLLM. The nearby DSv4 PRs (#57679 query RMSNorm+MXFP8, #57977 MXFP8 activations between DeepGEMM kernels, #55459 indexer Hadamard) touch different paths. #57432 (merged) fixed the DSpark non-causal FlashInfer layout for DSv4.1 only; the DSv4 fix here is the counterpart, done differently so RopeQuant can apply (see Changes).

## Test Plan
- **Unit (new):**
  - `test_flashinfer_rope_quant_matches_unfused_o_proj` runs one mixed step (two decodes, a three-token prefill, and three CUDA-graph pad rows) through the real `_forward` + `_o_proj`, fused and unfused, and compares the `wo_a` output.
  - `test_flashinfer_dspark_noncausal_block_sees_future_tokens[0|20|127|900]` runs a DSpark non-causal block (q_len 4) through the DSv4 layer. It checks each draft token against a reference over its full visible set (context window plus the whole block), then checks that the fused output projects like the unfused one. Without the fix it fails at both contexts it was run at (20, 900); the kernel probe below shows the old layout off at every context tried.
- **Existing suites:**
  - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py`
  - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py`
  - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py`
  - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py`
- **Kernel microbenchmark** (standalone script, not included): decode under CUDA graphs, fused vs bf16 attention + `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant`, on 1×GB300.
- **E2E accuracy A/B**, as described in the results below.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files, including mypy.

## Test Result
**Tests:** all pass on GB300. `test_flashmla_sparse` 19/19, `test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla` 33 passed and 8 skipped, `test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible` 28/28, `test_fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` 82/82 (on the first commit). pre-commit passes. The suites ran on a checkout of the parent commit (09fe178dba) plus this change; none of the 12 commits between it and the branch base touch these files.

**Kernel probe for the index layout:** FlashInfer called directly with a 4-token block per request, compared with a torch reference over the full visible set. With per-token split rows the max error is 0.008–0.029 at contexts 0, 1, 20, 100, 126, 127, 128 and 900, the same level as ordinary causal rows (0.008–0.02). The old contiguous rows are off by 0.09–0.6 at every context.

**E2E accuracy** (first commit; no DSpark), DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, DEP8 over 2×4 GB300 (tp 1 per rank, so 128 local heads), `--attention-config.backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8`, MegaMoE. The two arms are identical except that the baseline loads a clean worktree of the same HEAD. The fused arm logged `fuses the inverse RoPE and FP8 quant` on every node; the baseline did not.

| | fused (this PR) | baseline |
|---|---|---|
| gsm8k 5-shot greedy, completions (n=1319), flexible / strict | 0.9530 / 0.9538 | 0.9545 / 0.9553 |
| aime25 ×4, temperature 1.0, max_tokens 98304 (n=120), exact_match | 0.9667 | 0.9833 |
| aime25 pass@4 | 1.0 | 1.0 |
| request errors | 0 | 0 |

The gsm8k gap is 2 of 1319 questions, inside greedy batching noise. The aime25 gap is 2 of 120 samples at temperature 1.0, and both arms solve every problem at least once.

**E2E with DSpark** (the index-layout fix plus RopeQuant on the draft), same setup plus `--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}'`. The baseline is the same clean worktree (old layout, unfused). Acceptance comes from `vllm:spec_decode_*` snapshots on both nodes around each eval, and per-position acceptance from the whole run.

| | fused (this PR) | baseline |
|---|---|---|
| gsm8k flexible / strict | 0.9538 / 0.9545 | 0.9553 / 0.9560 |
| gsm8k acceptance length (rate) | **4.42** (0.489) | 3.70 (0.386) |
| aime25 ×4 exact_match, pass@4 | 0.9917, 1.0 | 0.9833, 1.0 |
| aime25 acceptance length (rate) | **3.83** (0.405) | 3.31 (0.330) |
| whole-run per-position acceptance, 0 → 6 | 0.796, 0.632, 0.490, 0.371, 0.276, 0.189, 0.115 | 0.774, 0.585, 0.402, 0.264, 0.168, 0.096, 0.044 |

- Acceptance length rises 19.5% on gsm8k and 15.9% on aime25, in line with the +20% #57432 measured for the same fix on DSv4.1.
- Every draft position gains, and the gain grows with depth, from +3% at position 0 to 2.6× at position 6.
- Accuracy is unchanged within noise: gsm8k differs by 2 of 1319, and aime25 by 1 of 120 at temperature 1.0.

**Serving perf, 8k in / 1k out**: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, DEP4 on one GB300 node (4 DP ranks at tp 1, so 128 local heads), `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, FP8 KV, MegaMoE, no speculative decoding. The two arms run the same config and differ only in the vLLM tree. The benchmark is a closed-loop `vllm-bench` sweep: exact token ids, `--ignore-eos`, 10 requests per slot, prefix cache reset between points. The arms ran concurrently on two different nodes, so low-concurrency TTFT is not comparable; ITL p50 is.

| concurrency | output tok/s/GPU, fused / base (Δ) | TPOT p50 ms (Δ) | ITL p50 ms (Δ) | TTFT p50 ms | ITL p99 ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 19.0 / 19.4 (−1.9%) | 12.73 / 12.43 (+2.5%) | 12.70 / 12.39 (+2.5%) | 494 / 549 | 13.1 / 12.7 |
| 2 | 34.7 / 35.2 (−1.3%) | 13.38 / 13.09 (+2.2%) | 13.31 / 13.02 (+2.2%) | 597 / 1050 | 13.7 / 13.4 |
| 4 | 63.3 / 63.9 (−0.8%) | 14.64 / 14.37 (+1.8%) | 14.24 / 13.94 (+2.2%) | 1108 / 1212 | 14.7 / 14.4 |
| 16 | **213.3 / 183.8 (+16.0%)** | 17.57 / 19.19 (−8.4%) | 16.99 / 17.12 (−0.7%) | 1370 / 2631 | 17.8 / 18.0 |
| 64 | **444.7 / 417.5 (+6.5%)** | 33.28 / 35.29 (−5.7%) | 23.80 / 24.42 (−2.5%) | 3468 / 3649 | 68.0 / 490.5 |
| 256 | **853.3 / 783.3 (+8.9%)** | 70.50 / 77.70 (−9.3%) | 34.94 / 35.56 (−1.8%) | 3597 / 4329 | 909.5 / 1180.2 |

- **One request per rank (c1–c4):** the decode step is 2–2.5% slower. This is the kernel's fixed cost at batch 1 per rank with long KV, the same corner as in the kernel table below.
- **c16 and up:** most of the gain is in prefill, not the decode step (ITL p50 improves only 0.7–2.5%).
  - With 8k prompts, the unfused path writes and re-reads a bf16 `[8192, 128, 512]` attention output per layer before quantizing it; RopeQuant removes that.
  - Prefill interruptions shrink accordingly (ITL p99 68 vs 490 ms at c64).
  - TPOT improves by 6–9% and throughput by 6.5–16%.

**Kernel time** (µs, current path / fused), 128 heads, decode (q_len=1), full SWA window. "KV len" is the sequence length; C4A attends 128 + min(L/4, 512) entries, C128A 128 + L/128.

| layer, KV len | bs 1 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 | 128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C4A, 1k | 11.5/11.7 | 0.98× | 1.08× | 1.29× | 1.76× | 1.46× | 1.64× |
| C4A, 4k–40k | 12.5/13.5 | 0.98–0.99× | 1.03–1.04× | 1.22–1.23× | 1.61–1.62× | 1.41–1.42× | 1.55–1.58× |
| C128A, 64–16k | 11.3–11.7 / 10.1–11.5 | 1.04–1.10× | 1.15–1.20× | 1.34–1.44× | 1.77–1.87× | 1.49–1.55× | 1.66–1.82× |
| C128A, 40k | 12.6/12.7 | 0.98× | 1.16× | 1.26× | 1.69× | 1.44× | 1.59× |
| SWA-only (1 of DSv4-Pro's 61 layers) | 8.8/10.4 | 0.84× | 0.84× | 1.09× | 1.22× | 1.54× | 1.82× |

- With MTP (q_len=2), fused is 1.01–2.13× faster on every layer type and KV length.
- The fused kernel's cost is nearly flat (10–13.5 µs up to batch 32).
- The one slower corner is single-token decode at batch ≤ 8 with long KV: about 1 µs per C4A layer, about +35 µs per DSv4-Pro step at batch 1 and 40k KV. That is well under 0.1% of a step.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- **DSv4.1:** its MXFP8 `wo_a` expects per-32 activation scales, and the shipped RopeQuant cubins emit only per-128.

## AI assistance
This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code): code, tests, benchmarks and the eval setup. The test and eval results above come from those runs.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Count reasoning tokens for Harmony, DeepSeek-V3 and Step3 parsers
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

  ## Purpose

`/v1/chat/completions` always reports `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens: 0` for gpt-oss, even though `message.reasoning` is populated. `/v1/responses` reports the count correctly for the same prompt.

Chat Completions gets the count from `parser.count_reasoning_tokens(token_ids)` (added in #45802). `HarmonyParser` doesn't override it, so the call falls through `DelegatingParser` to `GptOssReasoningParser`. That parser only detects reasoning boundaries, so it inherits the base `ReasoningParser.count_reasoning_tokens`, which returns `0`. `HarmonyParser.process_chunk()` already counts reasoning tokens for the Responses API, but Chat Completions never used that count.

The same always-zero result affects two other parsers with no open fix:

  - **`deepseek_v3` / `holo2`**: `DeepSeekV3ReasoningParser` passes every method to its wrapped R1/identity parser except `count_reasoning_tokens`, so it always returns 0.
  - **`step3`**: `Step3ReasoningParser` never implemented counting.

  ### Changes

  - `HarmonyParser.count_reasoning_tokens`: counts with a fresh `StreamableParser`, so the instance's streaming state is untouched. This matters because Chat Completions calls it after `parse()` (non-streaming) and after each chunk with the
  cumulative token IDs (streaming).
  - The channel rule (`analysis`, or `commentary` with a recipient) moves into `_is_reasoning_token`, shared by `process_chunk()` and `count_reasoning_tokens()`, so Chat Completions and Responses report the same number.
  - Harmony control tokens (`<|message|>`, `<|end|>`, …) are no longer counted as reasoning. This matches #45802, where engine parsers exclude `<think>`/`</think>` boundary terminals. **Behavior change:** Responses API `reasoning_tokens`
  for gpt-oss drops by about 1 per reasoning message or tool call (previously `<|message|>` was counted).
  - `DeepSeekV3ReasoningParser.count_reasoning_tokens` passes the call to the wrapped parser. With the R1 template the `<think>` start token is in the prompt, so a non-zero count for that case also depends on #49743.
  - `Step3ReasoningParser.count_reasoning_tokens` counts the tokens before the first `</think>` (all tokens if it's absent), matching its existing `extract_reasoning`.

  ### Why this is not a duplicate

  - #56914 (per-request reasoning/content token metrics, +1186/-37, open, awaiting review) also adds `HarmonyParser.count_reasoning_tokens`, as part of a larger opt-in metrics feature. This PR is the small, standalone bug fix for the
  user-visible usage field, so it can land independently. If #56914 merges first, I'll rebase onto it or close this in its favor.
  - Other open PRs cover different parsers: #58372 (Kimi K3), #54091 / #54238 / #54585 (Muse Glimmer), #50240 (Poolside), #49743 (base thinking parser without a start token). None touch Harmony, `deepseek_v3` or `step3`.
  - Out of scope: `granite`, `hunyuan_a13b` and `olmo3` detect markers in decoded text rather than by token ID, so counting needs a text-to-token mapping. `minimax_m2_append_think` intentionally returns reasoning inside `content`.

  ## Test Plan

  Unit tests (CPU, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty`, tokenizers only):

  ```bash
  pytest tests/parser/test_harmony.py \
         tests/reasoning/test_deepseekv3_reasoning_parser.py \
         tests/reasoning/test_step3_reasoning_parser.py \
         tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_context.py \
         tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py -q

  New tests:
  - TestCountReasoningTokens in tests/parser/test_harmony.py:
    - the count matches process_chunk().reasoning_token_count for analysis plus a tool call
    - a final-only output gives 0
    - control tokens are excluded (the count equals the analysis text's token count)
    - counting doesn't disturb the streaming parser's state
  - test_count_reasoning_tokens_delegates in tests/reasoning/test_deepseekv3_reasoning_parser.py: thinking on/off.
  - New tests/reasoning/test_step3_reasoning_parser.py. Step3 had no test file; test_step3p5_reasoning_parser.py covers a different parser.

  End-to-end check with openai/gpt-oss-20b:

  vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b
  curl localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
    "model": "openai/gpt-oss-20b",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
    "reasoning_effort": "high"
  }' | jq .usage

  Test Result

  Unit tests: 150 passed, 1 xfailed. Without the source changes, the 4 new tests that expect a non-zero count fail (Harmony test_matches_process_chunk, DeepSeek-V3 thinking=True, both Step3 tests).

  ruff check / ruff format --check: pass.

  End-to-end, gpt-oss-20b, same prompt:

  ┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬──────────────────┐
  │                           │ completion_tokens │ reasoning_tokens │
  ├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼──────────────────┤
  │ Before (Chat Completions) │ 93                │ 0                │

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Fuse small-batch WO-A with inverse RoPE and MXFP8 quant on SM100/SM103
body:
## Purpose

On SM100/SM103, the DSv4.1 O-projection runs four kernels per layer. At decode batch sizes the first three are latency-bound and together take 11-12 µs on GB200 (DSv4.1-Flash, TP=4):

```
before: attn_out ─▶ [Triton] inverse RoPE + per-32 FP8 quant ─▶ [DeepGEMM] fp8_einsum wo_a ─BF16─▶ [FlashInfer] MXFP8 quantize ─▶ [FlashInfer CuTe-DSL] wo_b
after:  attn_out ─▶ [FusedWoAKernel] inverse RoPE + quant + wo_a + MXFP8 quant ──────────────────────────────────────────▶ [FlashInfer CuTe-DSL] wo_b
```

This PR adds `FusedWoAKernel`, a CuTe-DSL kernel that replaces the first three and hands `wo_b` a pre-quantized `QuantizedActivation`, so `wo_b` skips its own quantize. Each cluster owns 128 `wo_a` output rows and each of its CTAs one head of K (split-K by heads per group); at TP=4 that is 128 CTAs per token tile in clusters of 8:

1. **Weight prefetch under PDL:** before `griddepcontrol.wait`, each CTA TMA-loads its 64 KiB FP8 weight slice and TMA-loads its packed weight scales, overlapping the attention kernel. The MMA warp transposes the scales into the `tcgen05.cp` layout before use. TMEM is allocated after the wait, since a PDL predecessor may still hold it.
2. **Inverse RoPE + quant into SMEM:** the CTA reads its head of the BF16 attention output, applies inverse RoPE to the last 64 dims, quantizes per 32 elements with UE8M0 scales, and writes straight into the swizzled SMEM MMA operand, with no global round trip.
3. **Pipelined block-scaled MMA:** `tcgen05` MXFP8 MMA with the weight as the 128-row operand and tokens as N, accumulating in TMEM. Each 128-wide K stage has its own mbarrier, so the MMA starts on a stage once its weights land and its activations are quantized; the last stage triggers `griddepcontrol.launch_dependents` for `wo_b`.
4. **Split-K reduce + output quant:** partials are reduced over DSMEM (each CTA reduces a subset of tokens), rounded to BF16 like the unfused `z`, and quantized to MXFP8 in FlashInfer's F8_128x4 scale layout, including the zero padding FlashInfer's quantizer writes.

The latest kernel update preloads the RoPE coefficients across tokens to overlap global loads, narrows two CTA barriers to the 128 TMEM readers, and uses `redux.sync.max.abs.f32` for output amax. Explicit `mul.rn.f32` / `fma.rn.f32` preserves the prior RoPE rounding order; split-K accumulation and BF16 rounding are unchanged.

`dsv41_o_proj(layer, attn_out, positions)`, which the FlashMLA and FlashInfer backends call directly, takes the fused path on SM100/SM103 when each group has at most 8 local heads (one portable cluster), `o_lora_rank` is a multiple of 128, `wo_a` is per-32 FP8 and `wo_b` is FlashInfer CuTe-DSL MXFP8. The pushed head supports 1–32 tokens. The local extension measured below supports 1–96 when `n_local_heads * (o_lora_rank // 128) <= 128` (DSv4.1-Flash TP4/TP8), retaining 1–32 for TP1/TP2. Other batches and unsupported layouts use `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`. Mega Attention retains its own output-projection path.

The extension keeps each compute tile at most 32 tokens and adds token tiles in the launch grid. For T65–96 it balances three tiles in multiples of four (24/28/32 tokens per tile). Scale stores use the global token row within the existing 128-row F8_128x4 layout; the extension preserves split-K accumulation and BF16 rounding.

The kernel follows the `VllmCuTeDSLJitKernel` warmup contract. The FlashMLA and FlashInfer SM100/SM103 backends register it at construction, and warmup compiles every token count accepted by dispatch: 32 on the pushed head, and 96 for eligible shapes in the local extension (all 96 TP4 keys compiled in 54.11 s in the earlier extension check): target graphs, DSpark draft graphs and eager batches land on different counts, so covering the whole range keeps runtime compile-free. `_wo_b_proj` keeps pre-quantized activations off GEMM-RS, which only runs from 128 tokens.

The kernel binds `amax`, `exponent` and `inv` before its output stage. vLLM imports `quack`, which rewrites `if const_expr(S) or D:` process-wide into a constexpr if; without the binding, token counts whose input stage takes the dynamic path (3, 5, 6, 7, 9, ...) fail warmup with `TYPE_UNSTABLE_JOIN` inside a server even though they compile in isolation.

Why not DeepGEMM: its 26/09 release lets `fp8_einsum` emit FP8 with packed UE8M0 scales from the GEMM epilogue, which covers only the third kernel and can only feed a DeepGEMM `wo_b`. It has no hook on the A-operand side, so the inverse RoPE + quant cannot be fused into it.

Duplicate check: searched open PRs for `wo_a`, `fused wo_a`, `DSv4.1 o_proj`, `inverse RoPE MXFP8`, `fused_inv_rope` and `o_proj cutedsl`. #57977 (draft) also targets the `wo_a` to `wo_b` handoff, but keeps `fp8_einsum`, has it emit MXFP8, and moves `wo_b` to DeepGEMM; this PR instead collapses the whole pre-`wo_b` chain into one kernel for small batches. Both touch the same call sites; if #57977 lands first, the fused kernel could emit DeepGEMM's packed scale layout for that `wo_b` instead. #58621 changes DSv4, not DSv4.1.

## Validation

The fused kernel should cut decode latency at small batch sizes without changing what the model produces. The kernel microbenchmark below was rerun on the local 96-token extension based on `4f59bdde4b`, against the unfused path unchanged from merge-base `e33de821c0`; rows 97–128 were added on the PR head `813bcd4042`. The serving benchmark, the DSpark GSM8K run 3 and the concurrency-16 GSM8K run 4 were run on the PR head `813bcd4042`; the other acceptance, GSM8K and GPQA results are retained from the earlier PR revision, before the latest kernel optimization and token-range extension.

### Serving / model evaluation setup

- **Hardware / software:** 4× GB200, FlashInfer 0.7.0, CuTe DSL 4.7.1; both sides share one venv built from the merge-base's precompiled wheel and the same kernel caches.
- **Model:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`).
- **Topology:** TP4 (no expert parallel), `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41` attention.

### Kernel microbenchmark

One NVIDIA GB200; DSv4.1-Flash TP=4 per-rank shape, BF16 `[T,16,512]` with token stride 32768 elements, FP8 weights `[2,1024,4096]`. FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, CuTe DSL 4.7.1, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132, CUPTI 13.3.1. The unfused and fused production kernel entry points run in the same process with default PDL settings. CUPTI measures the span from first kernel start to last kernel end, using CUDA graphs and cold L2. Every token count uses 7 alternating rounds × 500 iterations per path; each value is the median of the round medians. Compilation and warmup precede timing. The timed chain includes inverse RoPE, per-32 FP8 input quantization, WO-A GEMM, and MXFP8 output quantization; WO-B is excluded. This is a single-GPU measurement of the TP4 rank shape, not a distributed serving benchmark.
