### Acceptance and GSM8K accuracy

Each run uses the full GSM8K test set (1,319 identical 5-shot completion prompts) with greedy decoding, concurrency 32, a 1,024-token output cap, and strict answer extraction, served with the benchmark configuration above. Runs 1 and 2 are two passes on one server; run 3 is one pass on a later head (DSpark: `813bcd4042`; no speculative decoding: `2ea0e22a47`). At concurrency 32, DSpark verifies 6 × 32 = 192 target tokens (and drafts 5 × 32 = 160) per step, past the 96-token fused limit, so DSpark runs 1–3 reach the fused kernel only in the last requests. Run 4 is one pass on `813bcd4042` at concurrency 16, where every decode-only step takes the fused path (6 × 16 = 96). DSpark uses 5 speculative tokens, and acceptance is read from the engine's `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters over each run.

| Configuration | GSM8K strict (run 1 / run 2 / run 3 / run 4) | Acceptance length, incl. bonus |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Base, DSpark | 93.03% / 92.57% / - / - | 3.470 / 3.473 / - / - |
| PR, DSpark | 93.03% / 93.33% / 93.33% / 93.86% | 3.469 / 3.477 / 3.472 / 3.475 |
| PR, no speculative decoding | 93.03% / 92.42% / 92.95% / 93.10% | - |

- Acceptance matches the base within 0.007 and the per-position curves coincide (run 1: base 0.796 / 0.655 / 0.462 / 0.341 / 0.217, PR 0.797 / 0.657 / 0.462 / 0.338 / 0.215; run 3: PR 0.796 / 0.654 / 0.461 / 0.341 / 0.220; run 4: PR 0.798 / 0.655 / 0.462 / 0.342 / 0.218).
- Every PR run at concurrency 32 is within 0.61 points of a base run, the largest spread between two repeats on the same server; run 4 at concurrency 16 scores 0.83 points above the best base run. These results establish parity with the base; they do not claim an accuracy improvement.

### GPQA Diamond

PR, TP4 without speculative decoding, `--max-model-len 1048576`; 198 problems, 0-shot chat completions, thinking on with the default (high) reasoning effort, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, 262,144-token output cap. Score **91.92%** from a single run (standard error about ±1.9 points); all 198 responses finished with `stop`, with a median of 2,134 and a maximum of 53,922 completion tokens.

### Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py -q
```

Earlier validation: 106 passed, both as is and with quack's preprocessor patch active (`-p quack.dsl`). The new test checks the fused kernel against the unfused Triton + DeepGEMM + FlashInfer reference at T in {1, 3, 6, 8, 12, 16, 18, 32} (every guard and tile size), with padded and unpadded attention output and all-zero input, under CUDA graph replay, including the scale padding. The fused FP8 data and scales are bit-identical to the unfused path in most cases; otherwise split-K accumulation order flips rare values (relative L2 up to 6.7e-4 after `wo_b`).

Latest kernel optimization (`e63dfaec75` → `4f59bdde4b`):

- The pytest command above: **90 passed**; all applicable pre-commit hooks passed.
- **704 additional CUDA graph cases** compare FP8 output and every scale byte against the previous fused kernel, including all token counts 1–32, multiple group/head layouts, padded and offset buffers, zero inputs and varied magnitudes. All are bit-identical; 192 cases run with quack's preprocessor active.
- Compute Sanitizer racecheck at T = 3, 8, 31, 32: **0 errors, 0 warnings**.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Uncount stop-trimmed spec tokens from num_computed_tokens
body:
## Purpose

When a speculative decode step stops on an accepted draft (EOS, a stop token, or `max_tokens` reached before the bonus token), `_update_request_with_output` trims the step's later tokens, but `num_computed_tokens` keeps counting them. Rejections are rolled back in `update_from_output`; trimmed tokens are not.

Ordinary requests are freed right after the stop, so the count is never read again. A resumable (streaming-input) request continues: `_update_request_as_session` uses `num_computed_tokens` as the fold boundary, so the next chunk starts "already computed" over positions whose KV belongs to the trimmed drafts.

Prompt `[1, 2, 3]`, `max_tokens=2`, k=2. The prefill samples `10`; a step with drafts `[11, 12]` returns `[11, 12, 13]` (both accepted) and stops at `11`. Folding in the next chunk `[7, 8]`:

| | `all_token_ids` | `num_computed_tokens` | next step computes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main | `[1, 2, 3, 10, 11, 7, 8]` | 6 | `8` only; `7` reuses draft `12`'s KV |
| this PR | `[1, 2, 3, 10, 7, 8]` | 4 | `7, 8` |

The fix uncounts the trimmed tokens, so `num_computed_tokens` again covers all new tokens but the last kept one. The fold then drops that token exactly as it drops the final sampled token of a non-speculative turn, which is what makes a session's output identical with and without speculative decoding (see the GPU check below).

Under async scheduling the trimmed tokens' placeholders were never released either (`num_output_placeholders` was decremented by the post-trim count), so they are released too. `num_computed_tokens - num_output_placeholders` is unchanged, so neither the async `cache_blocks` frontier nor the `C - P` frontier from #58259 moves.

This count is also what stale block-hash truncation keys on (#52806, and the `del session.block_hashes[num_computed_tokens // hash_block_size:]` suggested on #58259): with the overshoot, the cut point lands too late and leaves stale hashes behind.

Diffusion schedulers inherit the change; resumable diffusion requests were not exercised.

## Not a duplicate

- #44526 clamps `num_computed_tokens` to `num_prompt_tokens` after the fold. That catches only an overshoot past the whole new chunk (`num_new_tokens <= 0`); in the example above it is a no-op and `7` is still skipped. This PR fixes the count where it goes wrong.
- #58259 (merged) fixed the async handoff race. Its `C - P` frontier also covers this case under async scheduling, but not under sync scheduling, where `num_output_placeholders` is always 0. This PR keeps `C - P` unchanged, so the two compose.
- #54979 caps its terminal `cache_blocks` call at `request.num_tokens` to work around the same overshoot; the cap stays correct.
- Searched open and closed PRs and issues for streaming input + speculative decoding, `num_computed_tokens` trimming, and `_update_request_as_session`; no other PR fixes this.

## Test Plan

```bash
# CPU
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py -q
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core tests/v1/streaming_input -q

# GPU (GB200)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py::test_with_ngram_gpu_spec_decoding -v
```

New test: `test_next_chunk_fully_computed_after_stop_on_accepted_draft` (scheduler, sync and async scheduling): after the trimmed stop, the fold drops the last kept token and the next chunk is scheduled in full.

GPU check, run manually and not kept in CI: a 6-chunk streaming session (opt-125m, fp32 + FLEX_ATTENTION, greedy, `max_tokens=2` per chunk) must produce the same tokens and logprobs with and without ngram speculative decoding (k=4), with drafts accepted. The greedy tokens of this repetitive prompt do not change with the context, so logprobs are what catch the difference.

## Test Result

- Scheduler test: the sync case fails on main and passes with the fix. The async case passes on main since #58259 and is kept to check that this PR's `C`/`P` accounting still composes with it.
- `test_scheduler_streaming.py` + `test_scheduler.py` + `test_async_scheduler.py`: 221 passed.
- `tests/v1/core` + `tests/v1/streaming_input` (CPU): 797 passed. The 1 failure and 6 errors (`test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e`, `test_scheduler_e2e`) need a GPU and are identical on main.
- GPU on GB200:
  - Streaming session check, main: diverges from the second chunk on, e.g. logprobs `[-0.3593, -0.5455]` with ngram vs `[-0.3427, -0.7063]` without.
  - Streaming session check, this PR: tokens match and logprobs agree to ~1e-5; `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py` passes.
  - Async spec-decode regression check (the placeholder accounting change applies to every async spec request, not only streaming): `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py::test_with_ngram_gpu_spec_decoding` passes, all 6 configs (sync/async, preemption, chunked prefill, mp/uni executor) match the non-speculative baseline in outputs and logprobs.
  - `ngram` is not yet supported by Model Runner V2, so the streaming session check uses the V1 model runner. The fix is in the scheduler and runner-independent. Async scheduling is covered by the scheduler test only.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find, reproduce and fix this. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] Paged MXFP4 sparse indexer on aiter's MQA-logits kernel
body:
## Summary

Adds a ROCm (gfx950) path for DeepSeek V4.1's indexer with an MXFP4 K cache, built on aiter's paged MXFP4 MQA-logits Gluon kernel. The CUDA path is unchanged. There are two modes:

- **Regular MXFP4** (`indexer_kv_dtype="mxfp4"`): dense logits over the whole context, read straight from the paged K cache.
- **Sparse MXFP4** (opt-in, also set `indexer_sparse_logits=True`): the candidate source takes block maxima from the same pass that writes its logits, and the consumer layers score only the candidate pool instead of the whole context. Steps whose contexts are too short for the pool to pay off keep the regular pass, so it helps mainly at long contexts.

Both modes:

- The logits kernel reads the preshuffled paged K cache in place, so no K gather is needed, prefill included.
- K is written to the cache by aiter's `k_norm_rope_mxfp4_cache`, and Q is quantized by `q_rope_mxfp4_quant`.
- Each prefill chunk is packed into one launch through `query_start_loc`. Uniform spec-decode steps run as `next_n`-row sequences, with the decode schedule built once per step.
- 128-token KV pages are preferred.

In sparse mode, the candidate pool is resolved once per step and shared by every consumer layer.

Requires aiter with the paged MXFP4 MQA-logits kernel and the cache ops (merged to aiter main) (https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5834)

## Tests

- `tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py`
- `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py`

## Performance

## Benchmark: C=32, 128 prompts of 350K tokens, 350 out, spec. decoding = 5+1

| metric | tot_baseline | mxfp4_dense | Δ | mxfp4_sparse | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| total tok/s | 19,225 | 22,796 | +18.6% | 24,863 | +29.3% |
| output tok/s | 19.21 | 22.77 | +18.6% | 24.84 | +29.3% |
| requests/s | 0.0549 | 0.0651 | +18.6% | 0.0710 | +29.3% |
| duration s | 2,333 | 1,967 | -15.7% | 1,804 | -22.7% |
| TTFT mean s | 378.2 | 319.4 | -15.5% | 292.3 | -22.7% |
| TTFT median s | 400.8 | 339.3 | -15.4% | 309.0 | -22.9% |
| TTFT p99 s | 556.9 | 473.2 | -15.0% | 436.7 | -21.6% |
| TPOT mean ms | 490.8 | 412.1 | -16.0% | 380.5 | -22.5% |
| TPOT median ms | 513.8 | 429.9 | -16.3% | 399.1 | -22.3% |
| TPOT p99 ms | 638.6 | 525.8 | -17.7% | 467.4 | -26.8% |
| ITL median ms | 816.2 | 695.0 | -14.8% | 638.7 | -21.7% |
| E2E mean s | 549.5 | 463.3 | -15.7% | 425.1 | -22.6% |
| spec acceptance length | 1.64 | 1.65 | +0.9% | 1.64 | +0.3% |

Note, since this is done on artificial data, AL is lower (1.65) compared to more realistic 3.5.

8k/1k, NP=10*C, TP4, using mxfp4 dense path (too short kv for sparse), no spec decoding:

| C | FP8 output tok/s | MXFP4 output tok/s | Δ | FP8 mean TTFT | MXFP4 mean TTFT | Δ | FP8 mean TPOT | MXFP4 mean TPOT | Δ |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 102.0 | 109.3 | **+7.2%** | 291 ms | 290 ms | -0.3% | 9.53 ms | 8.88 ms | **-6.8%** |
| 16 | 1027.9 | 1061.0 | **+3.2%** | 1611 ms | 1580 ms | -1.9% | 14.00 ms | 13.55 ms | **-3.2%** |
| 64 | 2005.7 | 2065.9 | **+3.0%** | 2048 ms | 2025 ms | -1.1% | 29.92 ms | 29.01 ms | **-3.0%** |
| 128 | 2485.5 | 2564.0 | **+3.2%** | 2835 ms | 2798 ms | -1.3% | 48.73 ms | 47.18 ms | **-3.2%** |


## Accuracy

| check | tot_baseline | mxfp4_sparse | mxfp4_dense |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K flexible-extract | 0.9651 ± 0.0051 | 0.9613 ± 0.0053 | 0.9598 ± 0.0054 |

### Long context accuracy check

- **The text:** the first 131,072 tokens of *War and Peace* (Project Gutenberg), tokenized with the model's own tokenizer. The token ids are saved, so every run scores exactly the same sequence.
- **One request** to the running server: `/v1/completions` with the ids as the prompt, `max_tokens=1`, `temperature=0`, `prompt_logprobs=0`. For every position the server returns the log-probability the model gave to the token that actually comes next, given everything before it. Nothing is sampled; it is one teacher-forced pass over the whole book.
- **The score:** NLL per token is minus that log-probability, averaged in four position buckets: 0-16K, 16K-32K, 32K-64K and 64K-128K.
- **Two runs per configuration** on the same server.


| run | 0K-16K | 16K-32K | 32K-64K | 64K-128K |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| tot_baseline run1 | 0.0710 | 0.1302 | 0.1323 | 0.1460 |
| tot_baseline run2 | 0.0717 | 0.1293 | 0.1332 | 0.1484 |
| mxfp4_sparse run1 | 0.0709 | 0.1274 | 0.1334 | 0.1465 |
| mxfp4_sparse run2 | 0.0711 | 0.1269 | 0.1300 | 0.1449 |
| mxfp4_dense run1 | 0.0715 | 0.1313 | 0.1353 | 0.1489 |
| mxfp4_dense run2 | 0.0721 | 0.1302 | 0.1330 | 0.1494 |

## Not a duplicate

#57517 and #56834 also add a ROCm MXFP4 indexer K cache, with dense scoring. The main
addition here is sparse MXFP4 (`indexer_sparse_logits=True`): the candidate source takes
block maxima from the same pass that writes its logits, and the consumer layers score only
the candidate pool, read in place from the paged MXFP4 cache. Neither PR supports this
(#56834 rejects candidate blocks outright). For the dense path, this PR uses aiter's paged
MXFP4 MQA-logits kernel (ROCm/aiter#5834, in aiter v0.1.23) and leaves vLLM's shared Q/K
kernels untouched.

Follows the main idea from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56254 while going direct to the paged K for prefill.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Shard the Engram wkv projection across TP ranks
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1's two Engram layers (1 and 14) project the looked-up n-gram rows with `wkv` (6144 → 25600, MXFP8 `[32, 32]` blocks). `wkv` is a `ReplicatedLinear`. Without sequence parallelism, every TP rank runs the full projection on every token. This covers plain TP and TP + EP with DP = 1, the single-node Hopper layouts in the recipe (H100 TP8, H200 TP4). Per Engram layer that is 315 MFLOP per token, plus a 157 MB weight read per step, repeated on each of the TP ranks.

This PR makes `wkv` a `ColumnParallelLinear` with `gather_output=True`. Each rank computes 25600 / TP output columns, and one all-gather rebuilds the full `kv` that `_fused_engram_post_wkv_kernel` already consumes, so nothing downstream changes.

The replicated layout is kept in two cases, so their behavior is unchanged:
- Under sequence parallelism each rank already projects only its own tokens, so `disable_tp=use_sequence_parallel` keeps the replicated layout there.
- TP = 1 behaves as before.

Model loading per GPU drops by 0.28 GiB at TP8 (61.63 → 61.35 GiB), which goes to the KV cache.

**Duplicate check.** `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "engram"` and `--search "wkv"` show no PR touching this projection.

## Test Plan

**Setup**
- Hardware: 8× H20 (SM90, 96 GB, NVLink).
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (HF revision `dba1be0a`).
- vLLM: nightly `0.30.1rc1.dev85+g8b84e1506`, with this diff applied as a Python overlay. `engram.py` is identical between that nightly and current `main`.

**Server.** TP8 + EP8, DSpark with the synthetic acceptance length 3.51 (InferenceX's golden AL), so both arms decode the same number of tokens per step:

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --max-model-len 262144 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.51,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
```

The default Engram placement (`cpu_offload=true`, the same command without `--engram-config`) was measured as well.

**Load.** One `vllm bench serve` call per point:

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len <ISL> --random-output-len <OSL> --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency <C> --num-prompts <N> --num-warmups <C> --seed 1
```

**Arms.** Run in the order main (A1), this PR (B1), main (A2), this PR (B2), each on a fresh server. B1 used an earlier revision of this diff with the same runtime behavior (`ColumnParallelLinear(gather_output=True)` for TP > 1 without sequence parallelism); B2 is the final code.

**Accuracy.** Full GSM8K (1,319 questions), 5-shot multi-turn chat, thinking off, greedy, `max_tokens` 1024. Real DSpark block verification (`rejection_sample_method: block`).

## Test Result

**Engram tables on GPU.** The last column compares this PR's mean with main's mean:

| Point | Metric | main A1 | this PR B1 | main A2 | this PR B2 | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT, 8K prompt, C1 | ms | 1223.2 | 1169.9 | 1220.9 | 1172.4 | **−4.2%** |
| TTFT, 32K prompt, C1 | ms | 4922.1 | 4740.4 | 4922.7 | 4731.5 | **−3.8%** |
| TTFT, 128K prompt, C1 | ms | 21359 | 20571 | 21261 | 20550 | **−3.5%** |
| 1K in / 1K out, C1 | output tok/s | 314.5 | 319.8 | 314.8 | 318.9 | **+1.5%** |
| 1K in / 1K out, C64 | output tok/s | 1940.3 | 2004.3 | 1939.5 | 2004.1 | **+3.3%** |
| 8K in / 1K out, C16 | output tok/s | 569.6 | 588.7 | 568.9 | 589.3 | **+3.5%** |
| 8K in / 1K out, C64 | output tok/s | 661.4 | 688.2 | 662.7 | 688.3 | **+4.0%** |
| 8K in / 1K out, C64 | median ITL (ms) | 85.4 | 82.7 | 84.9 | 82.8 | −2.8% |

The two arms of each side agree within 0.5%, and no point regresses. Mean TTFT under load (C ≥ 16) moves with queueing (±15% between main's own runs), so it is left out.

**Default Engram placement (`cpu_offload=true`).** One more pair of fresh servers, main then this PR, with the same command minus `--engram-config`:

| Point | Metric | main | this PR | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT, 8K prompt, C1 | ms | 1227.2 | 1175.9 | **−4.2%** |
| TTFT, 32K prompt, C1 | ms | 4938.5 | 4730.3 | **−4.2%** |
| 1K in / 1K out, C1 | output tok/s | 314.4 | 318.1 | **+1.2%** |
| 1K in / 1K out, C64 | output tok/s | 1935.1 | 1997.0 | **+3.2%** |
| 8K in / 1K out, C64 | output tok/s | 660.8 | 686.9 | **+3.9%** |

The gains match the GPU placement, since `wkv` stays on the GPU either way.

**Accuracy**

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K, 5-shot chat, greedy (1,319 questions) | 96.97% | 96.74% |
| DSpark acceptance length (same run) | 3.863 | 3.864 |

The 3-question difference is within greedy BF16 run-to-run variation. Acceptance is unchanged. The "this PR" column comes from the B1 revision; its runtime path is identical to the final code.

**Tests.**
- `test_engram_constructor_honors_offload` in `tests/kernels/test_engram.py` stubs the `wkv` constructor. It now stubs `ColumnParallelLinear` instead of `ReplicatedLinear`; that rename is the only change to the test file.
- The other tests in that file set `module.wkv` to `nn.Identity`.
- `tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py` builds `Engram` inside real TP groups of size 1 and 2, so it constructs the new `ColumnParallelLinear`, but it checks only the table lookups, never `wkv`.
- Results with this diff: `tests/kernels/test_engram.py` gives 83 passed and 1 skipped (it needs two GPUs) on one H20; `tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py` gives 26 passed on four H20s.
- The pinned `ruff` (0.14.0) and `typos` checks pass on the changed files.

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py
```

AI assistance: Claude Code helped profile this version and run the benchmarks. I reviewed every changed line and checked the results above.

title: [Perf][Attention] Remove D2H sync from FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA plan under async scheduling
body:
## Purpose

With async scheduling, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` did a blocking D2H copy on every metadata build. FlashInfer bakes each row's `kv_len` into its schedule on the host, and `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` is optimistic under async spec decode, so the builder copied `positions` / `seq_lens` back to get exact lengths. With MTP that happens on every draft step too. On GLM-5.3-Flash this made async scheduling *slower* than `--no-async-scheduling` (11.1 vs 7.7 ms TPOT at c=1).

How it works:

1. **Plan on the CPU with the upper bound plus slack.** The host bound, padded by 32 tokens and capped at the max valid count, is available without touching the GPU, so there's no sync.
2. **Clamp on the GPU.** FlashInfer keeps the plan in its int workspace as a list of work items with `kv_start`/`kv_end`. A small Triton kernel (`_clamp_work_kv_end`) computes each row's exact valid count on device from `seq_lens` / `query_start_loc` / `req_id_per_token` (same formula as before) and clamps every work item's `kv_end` to it. The FA3 kernel never reads past `kv_end`, so the slack (and the `-1` tail of the index buffer) is never touched.
3. **Reuse the plan across steps.** Contexts grow by a few tokens per step and the slack absorbs that, so while the new bounds still fit, `wrapper.plan()` is skipped and only the clamp runs. This is also why no-async gets slightly faster.

```
before:  GPU seq_lens --(blocking D2H)--> CPU exact lens --> plan --> run
after:   CPU upper bound + 32 --> plan (usually reused)
         GPU: clamp kv_end to exact lens (Triton, no sync) --> run
```

Notes:
- This reads `wrapper._plan_info` and the planned int workspace (the `MLAPlanInfo` layout from `scheduler.cuh`). The plan-info length is asserted, and the per-work capacity is read from the layout rather than hardcoded.
- With adaptive verification the host query split may not match the device one, so the host bound falls back to the batch max for every row.
- The exact (syncing) path is only used when there's no host upper bound.
- Only affects `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (Hopper; the default sparse backend for NoPE models such as GLM-5.3-Flash).

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs touching this backend. #55222 fixes the fp8 plan dtype and indexer workspace sizing, and #58260 chunks plan/run for >16k-row steps. Neither addresses the sync. #58260 does touch `plan()` / `build()`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase; I'm happy to do it.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests: `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py` on H100. I updated the existing tests to the new `plan()` signature and added two GPU tests against real FlashInfer. One checks that an upper-bound plan plus the device clamp matches an exact plan (including MTP-style multi-query rows around `index_topk` and a batch spanning several clamp blocks). The other checks that the plan is reused across growing contexts without replanning.
- E2E: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, TP8 on H100, fp8 KV cache, MTP with 5 speculative tokens, `max-model-len 32768`. Benchmark: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 --ignore-eos` at concurrency 1/8/32, at least 32 prompts, each point run twice, no profiler.
- Accuracy: `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` (1319 questions, 5-shot).
- Syncs: a torch profiler trace on the patched server shows no blocking sync left in the draft-step metadata build (before: 13 per ~5 steps, ~79 ms total, at `_kv_lens_host`).

All E2E runs, baseline included, have the fp8 plan-dtype fix from #55222 applied locally, since fp8 KV on this backend fails without it.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 18 passed.

Mean TTFT / median TTFT / mean TPOT (ms), average of 2 runs:

| | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, async | 136.6 / 138.8 / 11.09 | 226.2 / 188.6 / 21.87 | 338.2 / 319.9 / 45.04 |
| **this PR, async** | 128.1 / 126.9 / **6.86** | 188.0 / 152.7 / **17.36** | 283.7 / 251.5 / **37.04** |
| main, no-async | 129.8 / 128.8 / 7.70 | 189.2 / 157.8 / 18.20 | 258.9 / 175.5 / 42.71 |
| this PR, no-async | 124.2 / 123.8 / 7.47 | 177.2 / 152.0 / 17.95 | 254.7 / 170.6 / 41.72 |

With async scheduling, TPOT drops 38% / 21% / 18%, and async is now faster than no-async at every concurrency.

GSM8K is unchanged: 0.913 → 0.921 (async), 0.911 → 0.917 (no-async). MTP mean acceptance length stays ~4.2. The random-token bench has ~no draft acceptance, so its TPOT is close to the worst case for spec decode.

---

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] Disambiguate ROCm attention class names
body:
## Purpose

This is a small, focused naming cleanup of DeepSeek V4.1 ROCm attention classes and their selector. It preserves runtime behavior and compatibility with existing configurations.

DeepSeek V4.1 ROCm attention defined its own SWA metadata, SWA metadata builder, and sparse-MLA backend under the same class names as the DeepSeek V4 ROCm implementations. The ROCm SWA metadata builder is a distinct type. It subclasses `DeepseekV41SparseSWAMetadataBuilder`, which handles V4.1's 0/1/2 compression topology.

Rename those V4.1-local classes so they cannot be confused with `vllm.models.deepseek_v4.amd.rocm`:

- `DeepseekV41ROCMAiterSparseSWAMetadata`
- `DeepseekV41ROCMAiterSparseSWAMetadataBuilder`
- `DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend`

`DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention` now uses the renamed sparse-MLA backend, while its SWA backend returns the renamed metadata builder. The canonical V4.1 selector is `ROCM_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41`; V4.1 continues to accept `ROCM_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4` as a legacy alias for backward compatibility. DeepSeek V4 behavior is unchanged.

## Test Plan

- `git diff --check`
- Changed-file pre-commit
- Focused registry and backend-selection tests
- Start `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` with TP=4 using both `ROCM_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4` and `ROCM_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41`, and send a completion request to each server.

## Test Result

- Changed-file pre-commit passed (ruff, mypy 3.10–3.13, SPDX, test tethering).
- Focused tests passed for the distinct V4/V4.1 registry paths and for selecting the V4.1 implementation through both the legacy and canonical selectors.
- TP=4 serve smokes passed on four MI355X GPUs with both selectors. Each server returned HTTP 200 and generated `42` for the completion request.

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] SM90 sparse MLA: index_kpool mismatch leads to corruption via unread query token
body:
## Purpose

Another corruption fix found while on the hunt that started in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58454. _Partial_ fix for #56868 and #56605. These both help, but there will likely be one or two more PRs with followups.

Partial fix for GLM-5.3-Flash corruption at medium length context. This is a source for minor corruption: the query token and up to two before it are unread by attention on three of four positions past 2048 tokens.

This was contributing to a failed tool call in ~1 of 8 34k sample sessions and ~1 of 2 42k sample sessions, both with heavy tool calling. Note that the proportion is highly variable depending on workload/tokens/etc, but fixing it shows improvement in corrupted toolcalls at these lengths and others.

The fix is to read index_kpool from the model config, defaulting to 1 for DeepSeek-V3.2.

## Test Plan

Test included.

## Test Result

Passes with fix in `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py`, failed without.

title: [ROCm][CI] Test AMD DeepSeek V4 MoE routing against a PyTorch reference
body:
## Purpose

**Split out of #50519** and carried over unchanged in intent. Test only, no pipeline change.

Nothing checked that the AMD V4 MoE computes the right thing. The ten existing tests in `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_vl_rocm.py` only verify wiring, so a wrong expert selection or a dropped swiglu clamp would pass unnoticed.

## What changed

One test with four cases, regular and hash routing each with and without vision. It builds a small `DeepseekV4MoE` on the Triton path and compares it against a reference written in plain PyTorch.

**Routing is compared exactly.** Expert ids and routing weights are checked at `rtol=1e-5`, covering the `sqrtsoftplus` scoring, the correction bias, hash routing through `tid2eid`, and the vision re-routing through `bias_vl`.

**The full layer output is compared within a tolerance**, which exercises the clamped experts and the shared expert on top of routing.

**The vision boundary is covered**: tokens are placed at both ends of the five-token sentinel interval and at the first ordinary id above it.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_vl_rocm.py
```

## Test Result

On gfx942, `4 passed` for the new cases and `14 passed` for the file as a whole, so the ten existing tests are unaffected.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep resumable sessions that stop while preempted
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58776.

With async scheduling, a resumable (streaming-input) request can be preempted while a step is still in flight. That step's output is delivered as stale output, and if it hits a stop condition the request stops in `PREEMPTED` state. Two things then go wrong:

1. **The session drops out of every queue.** `_handle_stopped_request` re-enqueues the resumable request, but the stopped-while-preempted cleanup in `update_from_output` removes it from `waiting`, `kv_holding_waiting` and `deferred_waiting`, including that new entry. The session is then in no queue and is never scheduled again. (Still the case after the queue rework in #58947 and the handoff fix in #58259.)
2. **The fold deletes the prompt.** `_update_request_as_session` keeps `all_token_ids[num_prompt_tokens:num_computed_tokens]` and deletes the rest. After preemption `num_computed_tokens == 0`, so it deletes the whole list, while `prompt_token_ids` (a separate list) is only extended; `num_prompt_tokens` then no longer matches `all_token_ids`, and the previous turn's output is lost.

Changes:

- After the stopped-while-preempted cleanup, re-enqueue requests that did not finish, so each ends up in exactly one queue.
- In the fold, keep up to `max(num_computed_tokens, num_tokens - 1)`. On a normal stop `num_computed_tokens == num_tokens - 1`, so nothing changes; after preemption the session keeps all but the final sampled token, and `num_computed_tokens` stays 0 so everything is recomputed.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open and closed issues and PRs for this path (`stopped_preempted_reqs`, streaming/resumable + preempt, `_update_request_as_session`, session hang symptoms); none found. #58668 fixes a different case where `num_computed_tokens` is wrong at the fold (a speculative step stopping on an accepted draft). Both PRs append a test to `tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py`, so whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase.

## Test Plan

```bash
# CPU
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py -k stop_while_preempted
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core tests/v1/streaming_input -q

# GPU (GB200)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/streaming_input \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler_e2e.py tests/v1/core/test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py -v
```

New tests in `tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py`, using a real `AsyncScheduler`:

- `test_session_resumes_after_stop_while_preempted` (next chunk queued before / after the stop) reproduces #58776. It asserts that the session is scheduled again, that `all_token_ids` and `prompt_token_ids` both hold the old prompt, the kept output and the new chunk, and that everything is recomputed.
- `test_non_resumable_request_stays_dequeued_after_stop_while_preempted` guards the re-enqueue: a request that finishes while preempted must stay out of the queues. It passes on main and fails if the `is_finished()` check is dropped.

## Test Result

`test_session_resumes_after_stop_while_preempted`, with each half of the fix:

| scheduler | result |
| --- | --- |
| main | both cases fail: tokens are `[20, 21]` (prompt and output lost) |
| re-enqueue fix only | both fail: same token loss |
| fold fix only | both fail: `KeyError`, the session is never scheduled |
| this PR | both pass |

- CPU, `tests/v1/core` + `tests/v1/streaming_input`: 806 passed with this PR vs 804 on main. The only difference is the two cases above; the remaining 1 failure and 6 errors need a GPU and are identical on main.
- GPU (GB200), `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py`: 14 passed.
- GPU (GB200), `tests/v1/streaming_input` + the GPU-only core tests above: 19 passed, 2 errors. The errors are `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler_e2e.py`, which fails identically on main: engine profiling hits `assert prefill_query.shape[0] == num_prefill_tokens` in the FlashInfer backend with `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM` on this machine.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find, reproduce and fix this. I reviewed every changed line.

---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)



## Impact (update)

Besides the client-visible hang, the parked variant leaks scheduler capacity. When the session stops while preempted with no continuation queued, it is parked as `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` and `num_waiting_for_streaming_input` is incremented — and the queue cleanup then drops the session from every queue. If no continuation ever arrives, the counter is never decremented: each occurrence permanently consumes one `max_num_active_reqs` admission slot (the `num_running = len(self.running) + self.num_waiting_for_streaming_input` accounting in `schedule()`), so repeated occurrences silently shrink admission capacity. Verified locally on main: after the preempted stop, the parked case leaves `num_waiting_for_streaming_input == 1` with the session in no queue; if a continuation later arrives the counter rebalances in `_update_request_as_session`, but the session itself is already lost.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2][Spec Decode] Reject draft slots that were never proposed
body:
## Purpose

On a P/D decode instance, Model Runner V2 verifies draft slots its drafter never proposed. After the remote KV load the request resumes with one token left, and the scheduler pads that step with `k` placeholder drafts of `-1` (#45237, #55126). MRV2 fills those slots from `req_states.draft_tokens`, which are still zeros, so the rejection sampler verifies `k` real token-0 drafts against a stale draft distribution. With probabilistic drafting at T > 0 and block verification all `k` are accepted: on main, 71/80 MT-Bench responses through 1P1D start with at least 8 NUL tokens (`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` + `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-DSpark`, `k=8`). MRV1 is not affected (#47029).

Fix: `RejectionSampler` gathers the verified tokens and positions with a Triton kernel that sets the draft rows of any step starting within the prefill (first position < `prefill_len`) back to `-1`, which the rejection kernels already reject. Drafts are only proposed after sampling past the prefill, so these rows are always placeholders. No new request state, and `input_ids` is unchanged.

#54102 (open) also restores these placeholders, via scheduler-side counts; this PR is a standalone runner-side fix with no scheduler changes. #58434 assumes these placeholders are rejected.

## Test Plan

- New `test_verify_rejects_unproposed_drafts`. Also ran the rejection-sampler, spec-decode and MRV2 worker suites, and `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k spec_decode_padding`.
- E2E on GB300, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, DSpark with `num_speculative_tokens=8`, `draft_sample_method=probabilistic`, `rejection_sample_method=block`. Topologies: 1P1D (TP4 + TP4, `NixlConnector`) and co-located TP4. Workloads: 80 MT-Bench prompts at T=1 (count responses starting with NUL), the same prompts greedy (byte-compared with main), and GSM8K 5-shot.

## Test Result

| | NUL-prefixed (T=1) | Greedy vs main | GSM8K strict |
|---|---|---|---|
| P/D, main | 71/80 | – | – |
| P/D, this PR | 0/80 | 80/80 identical | 0.9545 |
| co-located, main | 0/80 | – | – |
| co-located, this PR | 0/80 | 80/80 identical | 0.9575 |

Unit tests pass.

AI assistance was used. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [ROCm] gfx1250 optimizations and model enablement
body:
## Purpose

  Enables and optimizes gfx1250 (ROCm) for gpt-oss-120b, DeepSeek-R1-0528, DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiniMax-M3 (MXFP4). Every change is limited to gfx1250; other ROCm and CUDA paths behave as
  before.

  - **MoE:** new AITER Triton/Gluon W4A4 MXFP4 expert (`aiter_mxfp4_w4a4_moe.py`), with its own backend enum so the oracle picks it only on gfx1250 (MI300/MI355 defaults unchanged). gfx1250
  MX-scale swizzle and weight prep for W4A16/W4A8, router-logit sanitization and an fp32 routing bias, and routing-replay plumbing.
  - **Linear:** AITER preshuffled block-FP8 GEMM, used when a tuned config exists.
  - **Attention / sampling:** gfx1250 paths in the AITER unified-attention backend and an AITER fused sampler (`sampler.py`, `topk_topp_sampler.py`).
  - **Models:** DeepSeek-V4 AMD fixes and gpt-oss MXFP4 stride fix. gpt-oss RMSNorm+pad fusion uses the existing `fuse_act_padding` pass,
  not a model-specific op.
  - **Docker:** gfx1250 base/image updates (ROCm SDK, Triton and AITER pins).

  Not a duplicate: no other open PR targets gfx1250 enablement for these models. Kimi-K3 gfx1250 support was split out to be upstreamed separately.

  ## Test Plan

gsm8k (lm-eval) for all models along side the normal server benchmarks

  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58800#issuecomment-5902957137

title: [CI] Stabilize batch submission in full CUDA graph tests
body:
- Pause scheduling at level 0 while queueing the complete prompt batch for each engine.
- Resume scheduling in a `finally` block so an enqueue error cannot leave the engine paused.
- Collect typed `RequestOutput` results through `wait_for_completion`.
- Assert that both response counts match `batch_size` while retaining the exact output comparison.

This addresses the intermittent MI250 failure in [Buildkite build 91284](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91284#01a0da17-1395-4ad9-ad6f-b63ce962165a) while testing [#56679](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56679). Tracing showed that the nominal 64-request batch arrived as 1 + 63 requests in one engine and 1 + 34 + 29 in the other; replaying those splits reproduced the mismatch within either graph mode, motivating explicit batch submission.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, and validation, and the repository pre-commit checks passed.

title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Refresh DSpark context KV cache pointers after the KV cache is re-bound
body: ##Purpose Fixes a GPU memory fault and silent memory corruption in the Kimi-K3 DSpark draft, introduced by #57632. ``` 21:05:36 JIT kernel warmup finished (all 8 ranks) Warning: Queue error - HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT Memory access fault by GPU node-14 ... on address 0x7ec3c95b0000. Reason: Unknown. 21:15:38 [Rank 0..7] Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: _ALLGATHER_BASE ... 600000 ms RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed ``` K3DSparkModel caches the per-layer KV cache base pointers, and the block-layout flag, on first use and never rebuilds them. Since #57632 captures the context K/V precompute in the draft CUDA graph, that first use now happens during the CUDA graph memory-profiling capture. That capture runs against a temporary KV cache that is freed afterwards. The real KV cache is then allocated at different addresses, but the draft keeps the stale pointers, so every later context K/V insert writes into freed memory. This change keys both cached values on the live kv_cache.data_ptr() tuple and rebuilds them when it changes. The pointer array is updated in place, so captured graphs keep reading live pointers. The rebuild only runs on eager calls; an assert guards against it running during capture. kimi_k3/nvidia/dspark_mla.py is the only K3 DSpark implementation and is used on every platform, so this also applies to CUDA. It was only tested on ROCm. ##Test Plan - 8x MI355X, Kimi-K3 TP8 + DSpark (ROCM_AITER_MLA, fp8 KV cache), nightly 29468dde (which contains #57632). - Recipe config for the conc-4 cell: --max-num-seqs 8, K=5, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, 8k/1k random prompts. ##Test Result

title: [ROCm][Perf] Add opt-in a4w4 (FP4 activation) MoE for DeepSeek V4.1 on AITER
body:
## Purpose

Adds an opt-in AITER a4w4 (FP4-activation) MXFP4 MoE path for DeepSeek
V4.1 on ROCm, gated by `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4` (unset/`"0"` =
a8w4, the existing default and behavior; `"1"` = a4w4, only for validated
model types — see commit 5 below).

- Commit 1 forces a4w4 via AITER's `_q_dtype_a` override but keeps vLLM's
  existing `GateMode.INTERLEAVE` weight shuffle. AITER's INTERLEAVE stage-1
  GEMM has no tuned FlyDSL config for fp4x2 activations at this shape and
  silently falls back to a heuristic kernel that produces degenerate output
  end-to-end — AITER's own `op_tests/test_moe_2stage.py` cosine-similarity
  check (used to validate this commit) does not catch this, but real-model
  GSM8K does (near-chance accuracy, garbled reasoning traces).
- Commit 2 fixes that by switching a4w4 to ATOM's `GateMode.SEPARATED`
  gate/up weight layout instead, which AITER validates for fp4x2
  activations on this checkpoint. It's a single `is_guinterleave=False`
  flag flip in AITER's own `shuffle_weight`/`shuffle_scale` — no new
  shuffle function needed — gated on the same
  `FusedMoEConfig.use_mxfp4_w4a4_dsv4` flag that already gates the forced
  a4w4 activation dtype. a8w4 (default for every other MXFP4 model on this
  code path) is untouched.
- Commit 3 scoped the (then auto-detect-on) behavior to DeepSeek V4.1
  (`deepseek_v41`/`deepseek_v41_text`) model types, since DeepSeek V4
  shares the same MoE shape/dispatch path but had not been validated yet.
- Commit 4 dropped model-type auto-detection and made a4w4 a plain,
  explicit opt-in env knob instead of a default. The AgentX numbers below
  show a4w4 is -1.0% at c1, parity at c8, and only clearly wins at c64
  (+10.5% tok/s) — a perf knob with that profile should not silently
  change default behavior for every DeepSeek V4.1 deployment.
- **Commit 5 restores a model-type check, but as a hard guard instead of
  silent auto-detection or silent allow-anything.** `use_mxfp4_w4a4_dsv4`
  doesn't just pick an activation dtype — it also flips the MXFP4
  weight-shuffle layout at load time (`is_guinterleave` in
  `oracle/mxfp4.py`), and that shuffle call runs for *any* MXFP4 W4A16
  model (e.g. gpt-oss), not just DeepSeek V4.1. Setting
  `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4=1` while serving an unvalidated model
  would silently reproduce the exact garbled-output bug commit 2 already
  fixed once — just on a different model. `FusedMoEConfig.__post_init__`
  now raises a clear `ValueError` instead if the env var is set for any
  `hf_config.model_type` outside the validated DeepSeek V4.1 set. This also
  means #58869 (which extended the old auto-detection to DeepSeek V4) no
  longer applies; closing that PR in favor of this design.

## Test Plan & Result

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py -v
pre-commit run --files vllm/envs.py vllm/_aiter_ops.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/config.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/mxfp4.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.13 --files vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/config.py --hook-stage manual
```
45 passed, 1 pre-existing failure (`test_aiter_fused_moe_fake_tensor_support`,
missing AITER JIT module, unrelated, reproduces on unmodified `main`).
New tests added for the opt-in behavior (unset/"0"/"1" x validated model
types).
pre-commit: clean.

Real-model validation on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP2, AITER `MXFP4_BF16` backend
(a4w4 = `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4=1` vs a8w4 = default):

- **GSM8K** (`lm_eval`, DSpark w/ real `block` rejection sampling): a4w4 and
  a8w4 both score `exact_match,strict=0.9712` / `flexible=0.9704` — identical.
- **AgentX** (`aiperf` `inferencex-agentx-mvp`, DSpark synthetic-AL=3.51
  rejection, settings matched to the public InferenceX dashboard run
  [`36101751233` attempt 2](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/36101751233/attempts/2),
  3600s each, 0 errors):

  | Concurrency | Output tok/s (a4w4 vs a8w4) | Inter-token latency |
  |---|---|---|
  | c1  | 142.7 vs 144.1 (**-1.0%**) | 3.46 vs 3.37ms (+2.7%) |
  | c8  | 404.1 vs 404.5 (parity) | 4.39 vs 4.40ms (parity) |
  | c64 | 303.4 vs 274.5 (**+10.5%**) | 138.8 vs 149.0ms (**-6.9%**) |

  a4w4's fixed fp4-activation-quantization overhead isn't amortized at
  batch=1 (c1), reaches parity at c8, and wins clearly at c64 once the
  halved weight-read bandwidth dominates — consistent with a genuine
  compute/bandwidth crossover, not noise. This crossover behavior is
  exactly why the flag is opt-in rather than default: it is a net win at
  high concurrency but not universally so.

## Duplicate-work check

Same as prior commits on this PR; no other open PR touches this heuristic or
gate-mode path. #58869 previously extended the auto-detection this PR is
now removing; closed as no longer applicable.

## AI-assistance disclosure

Drafted with Cursor (Claude Sonnet 5): the AITER `GateMode`/shuffle
investigation, GSM8K root-cause debugging (INTERLEAVE+fp4x2 vs
SEPARATED+fp4x2), the AgentX perf sweep, the DeepSeek V4.1-only scoping,
the opt-in redesign (commit 4), the follow-up hard model-type guard
(commit 5, prompted by checking whether Kimi K3's MoE path was affected —
it isn't, since its SITU activation branch short-circuits before this
flag is read in the forward pass, but the weight-loading shuffle path
turned out to apply the flag unconditionally to any MXFP4 W4A16 model),
and this PR description. I (the submitting human) reviewed every changed
line and ran the test/eval commands above.

title: [Model] DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 VL: stream language-model weights instead of sorting the checkpoint
body:
## Purpose

The DeepSeek-V4 VL wrapper and the NVIDIA DeepSeek-V4.1 VL wrapper sort the whole mapped weight stream so that the `language_model.` group reaches the child loader contiguously. The NVIDIA children finalize fused expert weights inside `load_weights`, so the group must not be interleaved. `sorted()` materializes the iterator, so every tensor the loader yields is alive before the first copy:

- **Loaders that yield materialized tensors** (`--safetensors-load-strategy eager`, or `--load-format fastsafetensors`, which yields a separate tensor per weight): nearly the whole checkpoint is held at once (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is 475 GiB). #58782 reports host OOM from the same sort on the AMD V4.1 wrapper.
- **The default mmap views**: this costs no extra anonymous memory. But every shard stays mapped for the whole load and name order jumps between shards. In our runs that meant ~20–30 GiB more mapped page cache per rank, more storage reads and a slower load (below).

Contiguity needs only a non-interleaved group, not a total order. This PR adds `stream_language_model_first`, which yields `language_model.*` as it arrives and defers the rest (vision tower, aligner), cloned in case the loader reuses its buffers. Both wrappers use it.

**Not a duplicate:** #58782 applies the same idea to the AMD V4.1 wrapper as one part of a ROCm fix, and could reuse this helper. This PR covers the V4 wrapper and the NVIDIA V4.1 wrapper. #57733 keeps the in-load finalize, so the contiguity requirement stays.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_vl_stream_weights.py
```

The test is parametrized over both wrappers and uses the real `AutoWeightsLoader` with a language model that finalizes in `load_weights`. It asserts that a weight is loaded before the stream is drained, that the child is called once, and that it finalizes after all of its weights. It is registered in the Basic Models (Other) CUDA step.

## Test Result

Both cases pass on current main (GB10, torch 2.13.0+cu130). Without the change, both cases fail at the mid-stream assertion: the stream is drained before anything loads.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 on 4x DGX Spark with `--load-format auto`, page cache dropped before each boot. These runs used a 0.28.1-based build with the same change minus the clone. Two nodes had `read_ahead_kb=1024` and two had 128, the same in both arms, which is why reads vary by rank:

| | boots | read per rank | load, slowest rank |
|---|---|---|---|
| sorted | 1 | 179–357 GiB | 248 s |
| streamed | 2 | 158–265 GiB | 202 s, 212 s |

With `--load-format fastsafetensors`, #55985 and some fastsafetensors fixes that are not upstream yet, streaming is what lets this model load on a 121.7 GiB node at all: ~88 s, against 202–212 s for `auto` above.

This changes only the order in which weights reach the loader. The child's per-tensor loaders don't depend on order, and it still finalizes once, after all of its weights.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the change, the tests and the measurements. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and boots.

title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Reject structural_tag and unhandled specs in backend validation
body:
## Purpose

With the `outlines` or `lm-format-enforcer` structured-output backend, `structural_tag` requests currently pass validation even though neither backend supports them. They then fail in the engine with `ValueError` and finish as `FINISHED_ERROR` instead of being rejected with a 400. This can also affect requests that do not explicitly specify `structural_tag`, since vLLM can construct these constraints internally (e.g. tool parsers using `structural_tag_model` and the Responses API).

This adds a `structural_tag` rejection to both validators, consistent with the existing `grammar` rejections.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Split fused_wqa_wkv by token across TP ranks on SM90
body:
## Purpose

Without sequence parallelism, every TP rank computes DeepSeek-V4.1's `fused_wqa_wkv` (5120 → 1280 + 512) for all tokens, so all ranks do the same work. The checkpoint stores this weight as FP8 with UE8M0 block scales, which vLLM runs through its MXFP8 path. On SM90 that path is a W8A16 Marlin GEMM: on H20 it takes 1.79 ms per layer for an 8192-token prefill chunk, 72 ms per chunk over the 40 layers.

This PR splits the projection by token for batches of at least 2048 tokens. Each rank projects its token shard (`sp_shard`), and `sp_all_gather` rebuilds `qr_kv`. The change is confined to `DeepseekV4Attention._fused_wqa_wkv_gemm`:
- `_run_parallel_input_projections` is unchanged, so the multi-stream decision is the same as on main.
- The all-gather is issued on the current stream, right after the GEMM that produces its input.

`_shard_fused_wqa_wkv` in the NVIDIA decoder layer enables the split only when all of the following hold:
- **SM90.** On SM100, `fused_wqa_wkv` runs as a native MXFP8 GEMM, far cheaper than W8A16 Marlin, so the gather would be a much larger share of the cost. I have not measured SM100, and the H20 results below do not carry over to it.
- **No sequence parallelism.** There the hidden states are already sharded, and #57257 splits this projection for that case.
- **No LoRA.** The LoRA wrapper maps every token of the batch.
- **No micro-batching.** Two micro-batches would share the custom all-gather buffer.
- **No batch invariance.** Whether a token takes the split depends on the batch size.
- **The custom all-reduce is enabled and fully connected.** This serves only as a proxy for NVLink between all TP ranks. From 6144 tokens at TP8, the shard exceeds the custom all-gather's 2 MiB limit, so the gather itself runs on NCCL.

TP4 and TP2 take the same gate but were not measured. On Hopper they need pipeline parallelism to hold the checkpoint.

The compressor's `fused_wkv_wgate` and the indexer's `weights_proj` stay replicated, and `_run_parallel_input_projections`, which can run them on separate streams, is unchanged. They appear in only a few layers:
- the compressor in the 4 KV-source layers (2, 8, 14, 20);
- the indexer in the 8 index-source layers, which are those four plus 24, 28, 32 and 36.

At 8192 tokens, splitting them as well would save at most another 457 µs in a KV-source layer (last column of the second table; layer 20's compressor is half as wide). In the four indexer-only layers the projection is only 5120 → 32. This PR saves about 1.45 ms in each of the 40 layers, so it limits the split to this dominant projection.

**Why 2048 tokens.** On H20 the split is faster from 48 tokens (first table below). H100 and H200 have about 6.7 times H20's dense throughput with the same 900 GB/s NVLink, so the replicated GEMM costs much less there while the gather costs the same.

I have no H100 or H200 to measure on, so I scaled the H20 numbers pessimistically:
- a GEMM of 1024 rows or more runs 6.7 times faster than on H20;
- one of 512 rows runs 3.7 times faster, and one of 256 rows or fewer only twice as fast;
- the gather runs no faster.

Under these assumptions the break-even is about 1450 tokens, and 2048 is the next power of two. A measurement on H100 or H200 would confirm or retune it.

**Related work.** I found no upstream PR for the case without sequence parallelism. The fork commit bytedance-iaas/vllm@383776ac20 splits `fused_wqa_wkv` the same way, but behind an environment variable that is off by default, and not when speculative decoding is on.

## Test Plan

**Kernel benchmark.** Setup:
- Hardware: 8× H20 (SM90, 96 GB, NVLink), TP8.
- Software: torch 2.13.0+cu130, NCCL 2.29.7, vLLM nightly `0.30.1rc1.dev85+g8b84e1506` with this diff applied as a Python overlay.
- What it runs: `fused_wqa_wkv` is built as the model builds it, with random weights and the checkpoint's quantization, so SM90 runs Marlin. The second table times `_run_parallel_input_projections` from this branch, which calls `_fused_wqa_wkv_gemm`, with the model's projection shapes and three aux streams.

Timing follows `.agents/skills/kernel-microbenchmark`:
- One CUDA graph per candidate.
- Before every measured replay, an L2 flush (twice the L2 size) and a device-side barrier, both outside the timed interval.
- The time of a replay is the CUPTI span of its kernels. Each sample is the maximum over the 8 ranks, and the tables report the median of 50 samples.
- Candidates alternate within every round, and correctness is checked before timing.

The benchmark script is not part of this PR; I can add it under `benchmarks/kernels/` if that helps.

**Serving.** TP8 without expert parallelism. DSpark uses synthetic acceptance with a mean acceptance length of 3.51, the same distribution in both arms:

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --revision dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --max-model-len 262144 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.51,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
```

One `vllm bench serve` call per point:

| Point | ISL | OSL | C | N |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8K / 32K / 128K prompt TTFT | 8192 / 32768 / 131072 | 1 | 1 | 5 / 3 / 2 |
| 1K in / 1K out, C1 | 1024 | 1024 | 1 | 6 |
| 1K in / 1K out, C64 | 1024 | 1024 | 64 | 192 |
| 8K in / 1K out, C16 | 8192 | 1024 | 16 | 48 |
| 8K in / 1K out, C64 | 8192 | 1024 | 64 | 128 |

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len <ISL> --random-output-len <OSL> --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency <C> --num-prompts <N> --num-warmups <C> --seed 1
```

Each arm ran on a fresh server, in the order this PR (B1), main (A1), main (A2), this PR (B2).

**Accuracy.** Full GSM8K (1,319 questions) through `/v1/chat/completions`, with real DSpark verification (`rejection_sample_method: block`) instead of synthetic acceptance:
- 5-shot multi-turn chat with thinking off (`chat_template_kwargs: {"thinking": false}`);
- temperature 0, seed 123, `max_tokens` 1024, 32 concurrent requests;
- each reply is scored by the number after `####`, or else by its last number.

## Test Result

**`fused_wqa_wkv`, split vs replicated** (µs per call, TP8, every batch size split so the crossover is visible):

| Tokens | Rows per rank | Replicated | Split + all-gather | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 6 | 1 | 14.1 | 23.2 | 0.61x |
| 12 | 2 | 14.6 | 23.1 | 0.63x |
| 24 | 3 | 19.2 | 21.1 | 0.91x |
| 48 | 6 | 25.9 | 20.3 | 1.28x |
| 96 | 12 | 49.6 | 21.5 | 2.31x |
| 384 | 48 | 99.7 | 35.8 | 2.78x |
| 1024 | 128 | 239.4 | 66.8 | 3.58x |
| 2048 | 256 | 458.5 | 99.7 | 4.60x |
| 4096 | 512 | 903.6 | 173.3 | 5.22x |
| 8192 | 1024 | 1794.7 | 346.9 | 5.17x |
| 16384 | 2048 | 3570.8 | 635.4 | 5.62x |

Up to 4096 tokens the gather is the custom all-reduce's all-gather; from 6144 tokens it is NCCL. From 4096 tokens on, the replicated Marlin GEMM runs at 83–84 TFLOPS.

**Input projections of one attention layer, main vs this PR** (µs; only this stage is timed, not the whole layer):

| Tokens | Layer without compressor or indexer (32 layers): main | This PR | Speedup | Layer with compressor and indexer (layers 2, 8, 14): main | This PR | Speedup | If compressor and indexer were also split |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 236.7 | 236.5 | same code | 337.6 | 337.7 | same code | 337.5 |
| 1536 | 351.1 | 348.8 | same code | 478.5 | 480.6 | same code | 481.1 |
| 2048 | 458.1 | 99.9 | 4.59x | 660.4 | 301.8 | 2.19x | 198.3 |
| 4096 | 903.0 | 172.7 | 5.23x | 1276.2 | 545.9 | 2.34x | 343.5 |
| 8192 | 1794.2 | 346.0 | 5.19x | 2473.9 | 1028.4 | 2.41x | 571.6 |
| 16384 | 3569.4 | 635.6 | 5.62x | 4902.1 | 1976.6 | 2.48x | 1052.3 |

- **Estimate per 8K prefill chunk:** this stage gets about 1.45 ms faster in every layer, about 58 ms over the 40 layers. The serving results below are the measurement.
- **Correctness:** `qr_kv` differs from the replicated projection by at most 0.031 across two sweeps with different inputs. That is bf16 rounding from Marlin's M-dependent tiling. `kv_score` and `indexer_weights` are bitwise identical to main.

**Serving and accuracy.** The serving numbers are a sanity check with two servers per arm, not a precise measurement. Lower TTFT and higher output throughput are better, and Change compares the means of the two arms.

| Point | Metric | main A1 | main A2 | this PR B1 | this PR B2 | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT, 8K prompt, C1 | ms | 1117.8 | 1117.8 | 1066.5 | 1075.2 | −4.2% |
| TTFT, 32K prompt, C1 | ms | 4535.6 | 4559.3 | 4320.5 | 4322.3 | −5.0% |
| TTFT, 128K prompt, C1 | ms | 19648 | 19680 | 18859 | 18807 | −4.2% |
| 8K in / 1K out, C16 | output tok/s | 601.1 | 602.1 | 621.4 | 620.8 | +3.2% |
| 8K in / 1K out, C64 | output tok/s | 709.9 | 709.4 | 739.0 | 739.4 | +4.2% |
| 1K in / 1K out, C64 | output tok/s | 1983.8 | 1987.6 | 2014.9 | 2010.1 | +1.4% |
| 1K in / 1K out, C1 | output tok/s | 335.2 | 335.2 | 338.0 | 334.1 | +0.2% |

At 1K in / 1K out, C1, no batch reaches 2048 tokens, so both arms run main's kernels. The two servers of this PR differ by 1.2% there, more than the gap between the arms.

| GSM8K, 5-shot chat, greedy (1,319 questions) | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Accuracy | 96.59% (1274) | 96.97% (1279) |
| DSpark acceptance length | 3.867 | 3.863 |

In three runs of main on the same nightly, one of them the run above, GSM8K accuracy ranged from 96.36% to 96.97%.

title: [Perf][MoE] Cheaper triton_kernels 3.8 routing build in the OAI Triton MoE
body:
## Purpose

On triton_kernels 3.8, which every ROCm build ships since #50605, the MoE routing metadata is rebuilt in torch with an int64 stable `argsort` and a `scatter_add_` histogram, costing 31–178 µs per MoE layer per step on MI355X / MI325X.

- `make_routing_data` sorts the ids in their own dtype and reads per-expert counts off the sorted keys with `searchsorted` instead of an atomic histogram. This path runs under expert parallelism and in `UnfusedOAITritonExperts`, which DeepSeek-V4 uses whenever AITER's MXFP4 MoE does not apply — on gfx942 that includes `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`.
- `routing_data_from_sparse_topk` (gpt-oss without EP) reuses the `col_sum` / `col_sorted_indx` of the `SparseMatrix` that `triton_kernels.topk` already returned, as the 3.6 path does since #45457.

The routing metadata is identical to main's. CUDA is unaffected: it pins triton_kernels v3.5.1, and only the 3.8 branches change.

## Tests

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_gpt_oss_triton_kernels.py tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_oai_triton_moe.py
```

44 passed on both main (`74f4404f58`) and the PR, on MI325X. The new `test_make_routing_data_tk38_matches_reference` checks the 3.8 build against a stable sort plus `bincount`, including `-1` slots, and fails if the `-1` clamp is removed while every other test still passes; `test_routing_data_from_sparse_topk_parity` no longer skips on 3.8.

## Measurements

Routing call under CUDA-graph replay, 1000 rows, µs (MI355X / MI325X):

| path | main | PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash rebuild | 104 / 142 | 61 / 80 |
| gpt-oss-120b `topk` + routing | 132 / 176 | 32 / 44 |

e2e, TP=1, `vllm bench serve`, Δ of medians vs main:

| model | GPU | concurrency | total tok/s | mean TPOT | median TPOT | median TTFT |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | MI355X | 37 | +2.2 % | −2.6 % | −2.5 % | −0.3 % |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (AITER on) | MI325X | 37 | +1.4 % | −1.9 % | −1.7 % | −0.2 % |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (AITER on) | MI325X | 101 | +2.0 % | −1.7 % | −1.7 % | −0.1 % |
| gpt-oss-120b | MI355X | 61 | +9.7 % | −10.5 % | −11.1 % | −0.5 % |
| gpt-oss-120b | MI325X | 61 | +6.0 % | −5.8 % | −6.0 % | −1.2 % |

Throughput and TPOT ranges are disjoint in every row except MI325X DeepSeek-V4-Flash at concurrency 37, where they touch at the edges. TTFT is flat, so the gain is in decode.

GSM8K strict-match (5-shot, 1319 questions), PR vs main runs: DeepSeek-V4-Flash 0.9522 vs 0.9538 / 0.9522 (MI355X) and 0.9538 vs 0.9560 / 0.9500 (MI325X); gpt-oss-120b 0.2782 vs 0.2881 / 0.2691 (MI355X) and 0.2654 / 0.2737 vs 0.2547–0.2805 (MI325X). title: [Bugfix][Compile] Replace Transformers AOT caching with graph caching
body:
## Purpose

Fix compilation caching for the Transformers backend by running Dynamo tracing on each startup while reusing PyTorch graph caches.

Decorated HF `forward` methods can fail model-AOT serialization. Disabling model AOT alone is insufficient: direct artifact lookup can reuse stale compiled code when decorator state changes between processes.

Following the review suggestion, HF opts out through `support_torch_compile(..., use_aot_compile=False)`. The option is passed explicitly through `init_backend` to the backend, compiler manager, and adaptors:

- Skip model AOT, mega artifacts, and direct artifact loading/saving, including existing cache-index lookup.
- Retain PyTorch graph caching and initialize persistent Inductor/Triton cache directories.
- Preserve native AOT caching, including native EAGLE3 drafts under an HF target.

This replaces the earlier `CompileCachePolicy`, owner ContextVar, and loader changes. The opt-out applies in `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`; cache-disable settings remain respected. HF does not attempt forced model-AOT loading when opted out.

Related to #50128, specifically compilation caching. Follows the graph-caching recommendation in #53295 and preserves the cache-relocation behavior from #52142. This addresses HF cache routing rather than the cache-key API migration in #39517 or empty-artifact validation in #56879.

## Test Plan

- Fresh-process regression for changed decorator closure state, warm graph-cache hits, and repeated forward calls, covering both Inductor adaptors.
- Native AOT save/load after an opt-out module runs under the same configuration.
- Functorch configuration restoration on normal/exceptional exit and hash calculation; bypass of existing direct-cache metadata and handles.
- Three HF models and a native control under two cache-persistence protocols; real TP=2 and full HF-target/native-EAGLE3 generation.
- Full Qwen3-0.6B GSM8K evaluation under the batch-invariant compilation configuration described below.

## Test Results

### Warm startup: 8.9%–10.5% less time with persistent caches

Before is main at `9f3d70e08157a95911f15809f2f1446424825ea7`; After is the smaller implementation described above.

Single L20, TP=1, BF16. Each model/backend/version/protocol has **1 cold + 5 fresh-process warm runs**, alternating A/B order. Values are `LLM(...)` initialization **median [min, max] in seconds**, excluding imports.

For the primary protocol, both versions receive persistent Inductor/Triton cache-directory settings. Caches are isolated by model/backend/version, and each process has private HOME/TMPDIR/XDG directories. Worker paths are verified because vLLM may redirect Inductor to its own persistent subdirectory.

| Model / backend | Before warm, s | After warm, s | Time reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 20.344 [20.105, 20.953] | **18.204 [17.595, 18.343]** | **10.52%** |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 15.570 [15.160, 16.111] | **14.121 [13.734, 14.297]** | **9.31%** |

| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 11.857 [11.723, 11.978] | 11.719 [11.659, 12.030] | Ranges overlap |

The HF results are consistent in magnitude with the earlier 8–10% observation. No native speedup, throughput improvement, or TTFT improvement is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Supplement: only VLLM_CACHE_ROOT persists</summary>

Inductor/Triton directory overrides are unset; each process has private HOME/TMPDIR/XDG directories. This measures the case where only the vLLM cache root persists, rather than ordinary same-user restarts.

| Model / backend | Before warm, s | After warm, s | Time reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 30.274 [30.041, 31.056] | **18.180 [17.794, 18.358]** | **39.95%** |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 25.188 [24.725, 25.983] | **14.109 [13.875, 14.304]** | **43.98%** |

| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 11.909 [11.545, 12.693] | 11.958 [11.618, 12.532] | Ranges overlap |

The **34.2%–44.0%** reduction is specific to this protocol. Compared with explicit lower-level caches, HF Before is 9.62–9.93 s slower; After differs by 0.011–0.545 s. Worker paths and cache counters support a cache-persistence explanation, without establishing per-kernel attribution. Independently compiled caches and shared-host load also limit cross-protocol attribution.

Native median changes are −1.17% with explicit caches and +0.41% with root-only persistence. Ranges overlap in both protocols; no consistent native regression or speedup is established.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Cold timings and reproducibility</summary>

| Model / backend | Explicit Before / After, s | Root-only Before / After, s |
|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 46.855 / 44.519 | 47.267 / 45.283 |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 37.518 / 35.636 | 37.459 / 36.782 |
| Qwen3-14B / HF | 56.375 / 54.423 | 56.104 / 52.939 |
| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 51.503 / 51.999 | 52.575 / 51.835 |

- **96/96 starts completed; all 96 cache checks passed.** No samples were discarded. These are new measurements of the smaller implementation, not reused smoke timings.
- Baseline: `9f3d70e08157a95911f15809f2f1446424825ea7`.
- Measured patch SHA256: `5edec6ae4c933e25df921c1c1d045b2ff277c0d8c56ed473ac12f99a2b2bf4eb`.
- Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu129, Transformers 5.15.1, Triton 3.7.1. A/B use identical hashes for the five rebuilt dense-runtime extensions.
- BF16, FlashAttention, seed=0, max model length=512, max batched tokens=512, max sequences=8, memory utilization=0.8, CUDA graph sizes `[1,2,4,8]`, four CPU/compilation threads.
- Raw AOT/mega/standalone flags are enabled; cache-disable and force-load are disabled. No batch invariance or additional deterministic controls are enabled. All workers use `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`.
- Fixed physical L20 GPU 4, checked idle before every start. Runs were serial within the task; the host was not CPU-exclusive. A/B never share compiled artifacts; remote graph caches are disabled.
- Cold means an empty compilation cache. OS page caches were not cleared; model-file verification may warm them. Single cold observations and five warm samples do not establish statistical significance.
- Qwen3-0.6B revision: `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`. TinyLlama and Qwen3-14B snapshots are identified by per-file SHA256.

</details>

### Correctness and cache behavior

- **HF:** all After warm performance runs hit FX/AOTAutograd caches; model-AOT/direct-artifact save/load counts remain zero.
- **Native:** all cold runs save AOT; all five warm runs per version/protocol load it with zero model-AOT recompilations. Separate forced-load checks also pass.
- **TP=2:** Qwen3-0.6B HF completes cold/warm initialization and generation on both versions. Both After ranks record three FX and three AOTAutograd hits on warm start, with separate rank cache directories.
- **EAGLE3:** full generation with Qwen3-0.6B HF and `Nicolassuez/Qwen3-0.6B-eagle3` completes across cold/warm processes. The HF target uses graph caching; the native draft saves AOT on cold start and loads it on warm start.
- **Cache disable:** separate HF cold/warm checks retain compilation while recording zero FX/AOTAutograd cache hits and zero model-AOT/direct-artifact saves or loads.

Performance runs generate the same 32 prompts after initialization, using batch sizes 1/4/8, greedy decoding, and up to 64 tokens. **All 128 comparisons pass the existing repository helper without relaxed tolerances; 124/128 contain token-sequence differences.** Each comparison covers 32 prompts; this count is not a prompt failure rate or an accuracy measurement.

| Model / backend | Explicit: comparisons with token differences | Root-only: comparisons with token differences | Helper failures |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 16/16 | 16/16 | 0 |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 16/16 | 15/16 | 0 |
| Qwen3-14B / HF | 16/16 | 15/16 | 0 |
| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 14/16 | 16/16 | 0 |

Each group includes ten within-version cold/warm comparisons and six corresponding A/B comparisons. The helper checks first-divergence tokens against the other output's top-5; it does not establish full-sequence or accuracy equivalence.

### Qwen3-0.6B GSM8K

All **1,319 questions**, 5-shot, greedy decoding, 256-token generation limit. Before cold, After cold, and After warm each score **519/1319 (39.35%)**, with **identical per-question answers and complete token sequences**. Each run has 3 invalid answers and generates 132,670 tokens. After warm records **29 FX graph hits and 29 AOTAutograd hits**.

This uses batch invariance with compilation enabled, max model length=4096, max batched tokens=2048, and max sequences=8. Batch invariance disables model AOT upstream; mega/standalone remain enabled. This evaluation does not establish quality equivalence under the default AOT-enabled configuration or for Qwen3-14B. Evaluation timings are excluded from the performance results.

<details>
<summary>Numerical diagnostics and coverage limits</summary>

Default runs contain token differences across versions and between cold/warm starts within a version, despite passing the repository helper. Separate smaller-implementation smoke comparisons also pass the helper, with these token-sequence differences among 32 prompts:

| Path | Before cold → Before warm | Before cold → After cold | After cold → After warm |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| HF | 4/32 | 6/32 | 3/32 |
| Native | 4/32 | 1/32 | 4/32 |
| HF TP=2 | 7/32 | 5/32 | 6/32 |
| EAGLE3 | 2/32 | 2/32 | 3/32 |

These smoke comparisons are separate from the 128 performance-run comparisons above. Cache-disabled HF runs also differ on 5/32 prompts, showing that cache hits are not necessary for output variation; this does not rule out all effects of the patch.

The largest common-prefix logprob difference in the performance matrix is **4.312496** for Qwen3-14B: an unselected token has logprobs −13.250004 and −17.5625, while both runs select the same token at that position. This is not evidence of an incorrect selected token, but the differences should not all be described as negligible rounding. Operator-level attribution has not been established.

The batch-invariant GSM8K result is separate evidence with its own configuration limits. Full Qwen3-14B quality evaluation has not been repeated for this implementation. Earlier implementation-specific numerical controls and quality results are not counted as current validation.

Testing covers the recorded dependency environment and L20 GPUs. Required dense-runtime components were rebuilt from pinned source, but this is not a full wheel/Rust build, every optional extension, or full upstream CI. ROCm execution and a separate real `model_impl=auto` → HF resolution check remain unverified. The independent TinyLlama breakable-CUDA-graph issue is outside this patch.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Per-module LM heads for multi-layer MTP on Model Runner V2
body:
## Purpose

Fix two issues with multi-layer MTP on Model Runner V2 (MRV2):

1. **Multi-module MTP samples every draft step with module 0's LM head.**
   `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator` runs step `i` through MTP module `i` (`spec_step_idx=step`), but `DraftModelSpeculator.sample_draft` calls `self.model.compute_logits(hidden_states)` without `spec_step_idx`. MTP drafters whose `compute_logits` selects the module's own `shared_head` by `spec_step_idx` (Step3.5/3.7, DeepSeek MTP, GLM MTP, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3, ...) therefore use module 0's head/norm for all steps. The same applies to the `use_local_argmax_reduction` path (`get_top_tokens`).
   Fix: `sample_draft` goes through two `DraftModelSpeculator` hooks, `compute_draft_logits` and `get_draft_top_tokens`, which ignore the step by default. `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator` overrides them to pass `spec_step_idx`, so other drafters (EAGLE, DFlash, ...) are untouched.

2. **Step-3.x MTP cannot run on MRV2** (needed to reproduce 1 end-to-end):
   - The drafter read `vllm_config.model_config.hf_config`, which for the Step-3.7 VLM target is the top-level `Step3p7Config` (`AttributeError: ... 'vocab_size'`), and used the target's quant config (`output_partition_size = 24 is not divisible by block_n = 128`). It is now built from its own text config and draft quant config, as the V1 `Step3p5MTPProposer` does.
   - `load_eagle_model` replaced every MTP layer's `shared_head.head` with the target `lm_head` because `Step3p5MTP` has no top-level `lm_head`. Step-3.7's three MTP heads differ from the target `lm_head` (checked in the checkpoint), so this collapsed position-0 acceptance from 0.93 to 0.06. `Step3p5MTP` now declares `has_own_lm_head = True`, and `_should_share` keeps a declared-own copy that has no top-level module.

## Relation to existing PRs

Item 2's config part overlaps #49490 by @chanh, credited as co-author on that commit. This PR additionally fixes the per-step LM head selection (item 1) and the per-layer LM head overwrite, without which the drafter loads but barely accepts anything.

## Test Plan

E2E on 4×GB200, `stepfun-ai/Step-3.7-Flash-FP8`, TP4, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, GSM8K 500 questions 5-shot, temperature 0. Acceptance from the `/metrics` counters.

## Test Result

| MRV2 | GSM8K | pos 0 | pos 1 | pos 2 | mean acceptance length |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Item 2 only (per-step head bug present) | 0.910 | 0.934 | 0.743 | 0.526 | 3.20 |
| This PR | 0.902 | 0.931 | **0.786** | **0.592** | **3.31** |

Position 0 (always module 0's head) is unchanged, while positions 1 and 2, the steps affected by the bug, improve by 4.3 and 6.6 points (~16k drafts per run). GSM8K differences are within noise. Before item 2, main fails to start with this model on MRV2.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; all changes were reviewed and tested by the submitter.
