title: [Bugfix] Terminate streaming sessions on ABORT/ERROR and prevent zombie sessions
body:
## Purpose

Split out from #53861 (bugs 2 and 3 of the 4 streaming-input session lifecycle fixes there), with the original author included as co-author — this is a carve-out for independent review/merge, not duplicate work. Bugs 1 (collector merging across chunk boundaries) and 4 (zero-chunk streams / DP sticky routing) are being split separately.

**Bug 2 — engine-side ABORT/ERROR treated as a normal chunk boundary.** `OutputProcessor.process_outputs` treated any `finish_reason` on a streaming-input request as "chunk done, wait for next chunk". ABORT and ERROR end the whole session, so treating them as a chunk boundary left `generate()` waiting forever and desynced the frontend/scheduler chunk queues. Fix: only non-terminal finish reasons are chunk boundaries (`streaming_chunk_boundary`); ABORT/ERROR finish the request state and also send an abort back to the engine (see below).

**Bug 3 — a chunk sent after the session finished resurrects it as a zombie.** If a chunk ADD reaches the engine after the session was aborted/finished, the scheduler sees an unknown resumable id and admits it as a new session. That session then sits in `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` forever, holding KV blocks, with no frontend state left to abort it. Fix (reworked per review, no new request fields):
- `handle_inputs` checks `output_processor.has_request()` before each non-first chunk and before the final empty request, and stops if the session is gone. There is no `await` between this check and the ADD send, and `AsyncLLM.abort()` removes frontend state before sending ABORT on the same socket, so any chunk that passes the check is ordered before the abort. This holds for every abort path, including direct `abort()` calls (e.g. realtime `cleanup()`).
- For the engine-finished race (engine finishes the session with ABORT/ERROR while a chunk sent before the frontend saw that finish is in flight), the output processor always re-sends an abort for a terminally-finished streaming session. That abort is ordered after any such chunk, so a re-created session is cleaned up.
- `DPLBAsyncMPClient.abort_requests_async` broadcasts aborts for ids with no routing entry to all engines, since the routing entry is dropped when the engine reports the request finished.

## Test Plan

```
ruff check / ruff format --check (ruff 0.14.0) on changed files
pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/test_async_llm_streaming.py \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py -k "streaming or abort or chunk"
```

New coverage: `test_streaming_input_stop_is_chunk_boundary`, `test_streaming_input_abort_error_is_terminal[abort|error]` (bug 2); `test_handle_inputs_stops_after_session_finished[True|False]`, `test_dplb_abort_of_finished_request_goes_to_all_engines[1|2]` (bug 3).

## Test Result

- ruff check / format: pass.
- On macOS CPU: all streaming-input and output-processor tests above pass. `test_abort_requests[*]` errors only because the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` tokenizer cannot be downloaded here (same on main).
- `test_engine_core_client.py` is skipped on non-CUDA platforms, so `test_dplb_abort_of_finished_request_goes_to_all_engines` was run standalone: it passes with this change and fails against the previous `abort_requests_async`.
- Not yet validated end-to-end against a realtime model on GPU.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (split and adaptation onto latest main). The bug-3 approach was reworked following @njhill's review suggestion. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [ROCm][Refactor] Move DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 multi-stream overlap gate to ROCm platform
body:
## Purpose

The multi-stream overlap gate `_enable_multi_stream_overlap` was implemented identically in the ROCm MLA attention layers of DeepSeek V4 (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/rocm.py`) and DeepSeek V4.1 (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py`). It decides whether the aux-stream fork/join may run: only when aux streams exist and the current region is inside graph capture or uses non-dict attention metadata (no eager breaks, where runtime HIP event sync is unreliable).

This PR hoists that gate into a `RocmPlatform` classmethod, following the existing platform capability-method convention (`supports_fp8`, `is_fp8_fnuz`, etc.): the base `Platform` provides a safe `False` default and `RocmPlatform` overrides it with the gate logic. Both models now decide via `current_platform.enable_multi_stream_overlap(aux_stream_list, attn_metadata)`, deleting the duplicated private methods.

The gate logic itself is unchanged, so this is a behavior-neutral refactor.

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Avoid target request padding in DP drafter
body:
## Purpose

When a target FULL CUDA graph pads its request count, `DPSyncState.num_reqs` describes graph capacity rather than the number of scheduled requests. Reusing that capacity for uniform drafter steps makes active DP ranks select larger draft graphs than needed.

This PR keeps the DP-wide maximum real request count alongside graph capacity and uses it for uniform drafter dispatch. It also shrinks online dummy-rank DFlash batches coherently across input preparation, graph dispatch, attention metadata, EPLB preparation, and draft generation. Startup graph capture retains its required capacity.

## Test Plan & Result

The performance validation below uses the official nightly build at the PR base. This PR uses the same nightly plus only the four Python files changed by this PR; the runtime SHA-256 values were verified after the overlay was applied.

### GPU environment

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
- Hardware: two non-production nodes, one arm per node, with 8x NVIDIA H20 96GB per arm.
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-77154ca6116ae34cbfe314beef1016bde9b63989`
- Baseline: the official nightly without a source change.

### vLLM Startup Command

```bash
vllm serve /data00/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8010 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 131072 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[16,32,64,128,256,512]}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":true}' \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log
```

### Performance Test

```bash
# Concurrency 64 example.
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai \
  --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8010 \
  --model deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --tokenizer /data00/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 3500 \
  --random-output-len 1500 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --num-prompts 640 \
  --request-rate inf \
  --max-concurrency 64 \
  --seed 42 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --extra-body '{"seed":42}' \
  --ignore-eos \
  --num-warmups 64 \
  --save-result \
  --save-detailed
```

All 890 requests completed in each arm without failures or Pod restarts.

Each point uses `num-prompts = 10 * concurrency`, random input 3500, output 1500, and seed 42. Both arms receive byte-identical input and output token arrays at each point.

| Concurrency | Output TPS Baseline -> This PR | Mean TPOT Baseline -> This PR | Acceptance Baseline -> This PR | Mean TTFT Baseline -> This PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 84.42 -> 86.09 (+1.98%) | 11.32 -> 11.15 ms (-1.57%) | 94.22% -> 85.63% (-8.58pp) | 795.0 -> 716.5 ms (-9.88%) |
| 8 | 471.97 -> 539.51 (+14.31%) | 15.23 -> 13.72 ms (-9.94%) | 84.54% -> 88.38% (+3.84pp) | 1339.1 -> 1271.8 ms (-5.02%) |
| 16 | 775.13 -> 842.71 (+8.72%) | 18.71 -> 17.01 ms (-9.06%) | 80.29% -> 82.97% (+2.68pp) | 1179.1 -> 1089.1 ms (-7.63%) |
| 64 | 1341.96 -> 1356.23 (+1.06%) | 44.55 -> 43.89 ms (-1.47%) | 81.09% -> 76.13% (-4.97pp) | 2306.4 -> 2371.9 ms (+2.84%) |

Acceptance varies between the two arms, but This PR improves output throughput and mean TPOT at every measured concurrency. This consistent end-to-end benefit across C1/C8/C16/C64 supports the optimization in this PR.

### GSM8K Test

Both arms were evaluated simultaneously with EvalScope 1.9.1 using the full 1319-sample zero-shot GSM8K test split and identical generation parameters.

```bash
evalscope eval \
  --eval-type openai_api \
  --api-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 \
  --api-key EMPTY \
  --model deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --model-id deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --datasets gsm8k \
  --dataset-args '{"gsm8k":{"few_shot_num":0}}' \
  --eval-batch-size 8 \
  --generation-config '{"temperature":0.2,"top_p":0.95,"max_tokens":8192,"timeout":3600,"seed":0,"reasoning_effort":"high"}' \
  --work-dir ./gsm8k-results \
  --no-timestamp
```

- Baseline: 1270/1319 (96.29%).
- This PR: 1264/1319 (95.83%).
- Paired outcomes: 1257 both correct, 13 baseline-only correct, 7 This PR-only correct, and 42 both wrong.
- Exact two-sided McNemar test: `p=0.26318`; no statistically significant difference.
- API errors: zero in both arms. Baseline had three and This PR had five outputs reach the 8192-token limit.
- EvalScope performance: mean latency 7.58 -> 7.13 s (-5.90%); average output throughput 52.17 -> 56.16 tok/s (+7.65%).

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to instrument the DP drafter path, identify the online dummy-rank graph mismatch, implement the follow-up optimization, run GPU validation, and summarize the results.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Requeue encoder-stalled waiting requests
body:
## Purpose

A waiting request can end a scheduling pass with `num_new_tokens == 0`: its encoder inputs do not fit the cache or the compute budget, or the prefill-lookahead reserve consumes the tokens. The waiting loop `break`ed there, so the request kept its head-of-queue position and every request behind it went unscheduled for that step — repeating on every step while the resource condition holds.

It is now requeued with `skip_request()`, which preserves the drain-first priority of requests holding KV blocks (async KV-load resumes) and the `deferred_waiting` accounting.

The self-pinned encoder-cache release from the earlier revision is dropped here; #60553 proposes that.

### Duplicate-work check

Searched open issues and PRs for waiting-queue requeue / head-of-line blocking and encoder cache stalls. No open PR touches this path; the nearest matches are #56826 and #57368 (encoder input lifetimes across steps — different concern), #40707/#40709 (mamba split deadlock — different path), and umbrella EPD tracker #52409.

## Test Plan

```bash
ruff format --check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py
ruff check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py -q
```

## Test Result

- `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` clean.
- 248 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `test_encoder_cache_embed_count_mismatch_restores_prior_hit_state`: the mismatch path also returns zero tokens, so the `encoder_cache_manager.free(request)` added in d12809f1 drops the prior-hit references that test guards. It fails at 5219f995 as well, so it is not introduced by this drop.
- 3 tests in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` cover the requeue: queue head-of-line starvation, `deferred_waiting` accounting, drain-first queue membership.
- No model eval: the change only alters failure-path control flow, no logits-affecting code.

## AI Assistance

AI assistance was used (pi coding agent): analysis, draft and test runs. The human author reviewed every changed line, ran the checks above, and defends the change end-to-end.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Enable decoder SWA bounded replay
body:
## Summary

#58132 added decoder-side SWA bounded replay for the CUDA model. This PR enables it on ROCm. During eager prefill, layer 20 writes its KV for every token, then layer 20 and layers 21–39 run on each request's last 128 tokens. The final `mhc_post` runs on that replay batch. Decode graphs stay on the full batch. #59532's replay graphs are already used: the AMD model uses `DeepseekV41ModelState`.

The AMD attention class does not override `forward_kv`. Replay calls `DeepseekV4Attention.forward_kv`, which writes the uint8 SWA cache through `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert`.

## What changed

- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py`: `write_kv` on the last KV source, then `DecoderReplayLayers` from that layer. Pass `write_kv`, the attention metadata prefixes, and that layer's SWA prefix. `mhc_post` runs inside the replay batch. The return is `(hidden_states, pre_mix, *aux)`. The aux state at the cut is captured on the trimmed rows.
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py`: no `forward_kv` override. The shared method calls `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert` and then the compressor insert and indexer K write.
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/vl_model.py`: forward `decoder_replay_layers` from the language model.
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model_state.py`: when decoder replay layers exist and the prefix-cache window is 0, build `replay_start` and warm the gather kernel. The pad kernel stays on the prefix-cache path.
- Tests cover a 300-token forward (trim, both `mhc_post` calls, the cut-aux capture, the prefix set from the cut, and the SWA insert) and window 0 warming gather without the pad kernel.

## Gating

On when `cache_config.swa_bounded_replay` is set and the v2 model runner is in use. Off with `--no-swa-bounded-replay`. The last KV source must have `compress_ratio <= 1`, and no Engram layer may sit at or after it. ROCm does not read `swa_cache_layer.bounded_replay`; that flag is the prefix-cache path, and attention forces it off. CUDA still requires it. Replay graphs follow `compilation_config.cudagraph_decoder_replay` (default on) and `decoder_replay_trim_threshold` (default 768).

## Depends on

#59894 is in this base. It replaced the row buffers with `write_kv` and `first_swa_prefix`, and replay starts at the last KV source. #56638 is in this base. It replaced #59136 and bounds the ROCm prefill SWA indices at the replay start. #59532 is in this base and supplies the replay graphs. None of the three are in this diff.

## Performance

4× MI325X (gfx942), TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, spec decode off, prefix cache off, HIP INT4 QuickReduce, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. `max_num_seqs` left at the default. Head `bf6a231a018d`, rebased onto main `c75cb63cd2bb`. The bench, GSM8K, and NIAH below were measured before that rebase and were not re-run. The extension is the installed ROCm nightly `0.31.1rc1.dev1+gbb87d227d`.

Serve log: `Decoder SWA bounded replay: in eager prefill steps, layer 20 writes its KV for every token, and the rest of it and layers 21-39 run on each request's last 128 tokens only.` Also `cudagraph_decoder_replay: True` and `Capturing decoder replay CUDA graphs (PIECEWISE): 4/4`.

4 prompts, 16384 in, 128 out, concurrency 1, seed 7. Both arms completed 4 requests.

| Metric | Replay off | Replay on |
|---|---:|---:|
| Median TTFT | 1176.37 ms | 629.97 ms (−46.4%) |
| Mean TTFT | 1176.09 ms | 629.65 ms (−46.5%) |
| Median TPOT | 10.59 ms | 10.58 ms |
| Mean TPOT | 10.59 ms | 10.58 ms |
| Output throughput | 50.75 tok/s | 64.87 tok/s (+27.8%) |

## Accuracy

RULER `niah_single_2` was not re-run after this drop. On the previous head, 500 samples at 16384 tokens scored 1.0 off and 1.0 on. 65536 was not run.

The 300-token forward wrote the same uint8 SWA cache as `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert`. That write covers full blocks and a 12-token tail, and the spare block stayed at the poison value.

GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 questions, concurrency 8, spec decode off, prefix cache off, `max_num_seqs` at the default:

| Metric | Replay off | Replay on |
|---|---:|---:|
| strict-match | 0.9287 ± 0.0071 | 0.9257 ± 0.0072 |
| flexible-extract | 0.9280 ± 0.0071 | 0.9257 ± 0.0072 |

## Test result

```
11 passed, 14 warnings in 8.17s
```

`test_deepseek_v41_amd_replay_forward.py` and `test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py`, on GPU 4, after the rebase.

title: [Perf][MoE] Skip padded work in SM100 FP4 DeepGEMM experts
body:
## Purpose

Avoid computing with padding in the Blackwell FP4 DeepGEMM MoEs layers. Currently we are doing so in both GEMMs and activations.  This mainly affects the decoder when running DeepEPv2+ DeepGEMM. This PR updates the grouped GEMMs to use DeepGEMM's prefix-sum scheduler, and changes the packed SiLU+mul+FP8-quantization kernel to use those endpoints to process only live rows.

Each endpoint is the aligned expert start plus its actual token count; the next expert starts at the preceding endpoint rounded up to the GEMM alignment. No count readback, additional launch, or DeepGEMM source change is required. Activation workspaces keep their allocated capacity. The per-row layout metadata shrinks from 112 KiB to 128 bytes for 32 local experts and 28,672 allocated rows.

The quantization metadata is optional. Calls without it retain the original dense launch configuration, and the metadata loads compile out. SM120 and FP8 expert callers retain their existing path. Padding outputs are left unwritten; the down GEMM uses the same bounds to identify live rows. `mk_alignment_scope` and `ensure_zero_padding=True` remain in place.

The new activation masking also differs from #51332/#51217 (shared masked activation/Humming paths) and #53911 (Humming indexed metadata preparation): `DeepGemmFP4Experts` directly calls the packed-UE8M0 fused activation kernel. Those changes do not pass this caller's expert endpoints into that kernel. Open-PR searches for DeepGEMM prefix sums and SiLU padding found no implementation of this change. No associated issue is being closed.

## Test Plan

Conflict-resolution update (2026-10-06): merged upstream main `5ab4e4445b` in `e704a97688`. Resolved the graph-replay test conflict by retaining upstream packed/float32/ceil-UE8M0 scale-format coverage and this PR's `is_cuda_alike()` CUDA/ROCm guard. Applicable pre-commit hooks (including mypy 3.10), mypy 3.12, syntax checks for the five affected Python files, and `git diff origin/main --check` passed. GPU tests and model evaluations were not rerun: the local machine has no CUDA GPU. The GPU results below describe the earlier validated revision.

Validation used 8×GB200, DeepSeek-V4-Flash revision `60d8d70770c6776ff598c94bb586a859a38244f1`, EP8/DP8/TP1, DeepEP V2 + DeepGEMM. Both nodes shared one ready NVLink ComputeDomain; all eight ranks passed peer-memory and NCCL checks.

- 69 activation tests passed on GB200, including the corrected benchmark rerun. New cases check bitwise live FP8 values and packed scales, poisoned alignment gaps and unused capacity, empty experts, all-empty counts, clamping, and changing counts on CUDA-graph replay.
- Interleaved CUDA-graph kernel benchmarks used five warmups and 25 samples, with 16 calls per graph. The old packed quantization functions were loaded as the control; ten cases cover padded and fully populated buffers.
- Full FFN comparison uses the same saved real inputs on both variants: layer 10, 512 tokens/GPU, five warmups and 25 unprofiled graph replays per rank. A device all-reduce precedes the timed interval. Three separate outer profiles per rank provide kernel timings. Untimed audits verify both GEMMs' scheduler selection and the activation's actual expert bounds.
- Paired full-model GSM8K: all 1,319 questions, five-shot, greedy, seed 42, maximum output 256 tokens, concurrency 64, FP8 KV, no MTP, eager prefill and full decode graphs.

Commands executed in the validation environment:

```bash
/tmp/check/.venv/bin/python -m pytest /bundle/test_padding.py -q --disable-warnings
/tmp/check/.venv/bin/python /bundle/benchmark.py --baseline /bundle/baseline.py --output "$out/benchmark.json"
/tmp/validation/.venv/bin/python /bundle/worker.pyz \
  --spec /bundle/$backend.json --job-id "$backend" \
  --output-dir "$out" --node-count 2 --local-world-size 4 \
  --node-rank-env JOB_COMPLETION_INDEX \
  --rendezvous-host "$head" --rendezvous-port 29500
/tmp/validation/.venv/bin/python -u /bundle/serve_and_evaluate.py
```

`test_padding.py` is an unchanged copy of `tests/kernels/moe/test_silu_mul_per_token_group_quant_fp8_colmajor.py`; `benchmark.py` is the standalone script included below (removed from the repository). The FFN and GSM8K orchestration uses an external experiment harness.

All relevant pre-commit hooks, including mypy, and `git diff --check` passed.

## Test Result

The latest paired run compares this PR's prefix-sum GEMMs with and without activation masking:

| Measurement | Prefix sums only | + activation masking |
|---|---:|---:|
| Full FFN, unprofiled | 425.5 µs | 385.7 µs |
| SiLU+mul+quant, separately profiled | 76.0 µs | 20.7 µs |
| Standalone quantization: 3,072 live / 28,672 allocated rows, hidden 2,048 | 63.984 µs | 10.510 µs |

Full FFN latency fell 9.36% (1.103× speedup); outputs match bit for bit on all eight ranks, including eager versus graph execution. Both projections used prefix sums in both variants; only the masked variant supplied expert bounds to activation. The median profiled activation saving is larger than the FFN saving because ranks carry different amounts of expert work and meet again at combine. Main activation workspaces are unchanged.

**Dense-path control:** calls without metadata preserve the original launch and differed by 0.20% faster to 0.39% slower across ten controls in the corrected rerun. At 28,672×2,048, the old and new dense paths measured 64.082 and 64.020 µs; at 28,672×7,168, 217.796 and 217.814 µs. No extra kernel or GPU-to-host count synchronization is introduced.

Supplying metadata for an already full buffer does have a small checking/scheduling cost in some shapes: 64.082→64.822 µs for the fully populated 28,672×2,048 case, and approximately 0.15–0.32 µs for the tested smaller group-128 cases. The ordinary dense path does not pay this cost. The 28,672×7,168 metadata-aware case improved from 217.796 to 212.236 µs. The benchmark includes these full-buffer cases rather than measuring padded buffers alone.

| Paired GSM8K | Prefix sums only | + activation masking |
|---|---:|---:|
| Correct / questions | 1,253 / 1,319 | 1,259 / 1,319 |
| Accuracy | 94.996% | 95.451% |
| Configured 95% threshold | Did not pass | Passed |
| HTTP errors | 0 | 0 |

All prompts and labels matched. There were three control-only correct answers and nine masked-only correct answers. This is an accuracy check, not evidence that masking improves model quality: repeating the unchanged control also produced 16 correctness flips while retaining the same total score. The previous and repeated controls used identical MoE sources.

The earlier scheduler-only validation, before this activation update, measured stock versus prefix sums at 717.4 versus 428.7 µs for the same FFN setup, also with bitwise-identical outputs. Those are from a separate paired run. Stock GSM8K was 1,255/1,319 (95.148%), versus prefix sums at 1,253/1,319 (94.996%).

The runtime image was pinned at `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:f29125bcc6d276ed38a67c9dfd4e51ccbaba09ad92847a0913c0df38d9c05c71` (vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev422+gd05da62e9`). The experiment overlaid the two MoE Python files and only the two packed-quantization functions in `fp8_utils.py`; installed hashes were checked on both nodes. DeepGEMM headers were unmodified. These results are not from a rebuild of all of current main.

AI assistance: Codex helped implement the change, run validation, and prepare this description. This remains a draft pending human review and verification before marking ready.

## Standalone activation benchmark

<details>
<summary>Benchmark script, reproduction command, and recorded output</summary>

Save the following script as `benchmark.py`. It replays all three captured graphs and synchronizes before checking live FP8 values and packed scales. This fixes the pre-replay comparison of uninitialized captured scale tensors.

```python
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project

"""Compare dense and expert-aware packed quantization with CUDA graph timing."""

import argparse
import importlib.util
import json
import statistics
from pathlib import Path

import torch

from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils import (
    silu_mul_quant_fp8_packed_triton,
)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--baseline", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("baseline", args.baseline)
    assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    baseline = module.silu_mul_quant_fp8_packed_triton
    warmups, iterations, graph_calls = 5, 25, 16
    results = []
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    cases = [
        (128, 1, 128, 256, 128),
        (512, 4, 128, 2048, 128),
        (4096, 32, 128, 2048, 128),
        (28672, 32, 896, 2048, 128),
        (28672, 32, 96, 2048, 128),
        (28672, 32, 1, 2048, 128),
        (28672, 32, 0, 2048, 128),
        (28672, 32, 896, 7168, 128),
        (28672, 32, 96, 7168, 128),
        (4096, 32, 128, 2048, 32),
    ]
    for capacity, experts, live_per_expert, hidden, group in cases:
        x = torch.randn((capacity, hidden * 2), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
        starts = torch.arange(experts, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
        starts *= ((live_per_expert + 127) // 128) * 128
        ends = starts + live_per_expert
        graphs = {}
        for name, fn, kwargs in [
            ("baseline", baseline, {}),
            ("dense", silu_mul_quant_fp8_packed_triton, {}),
            (
                "expert",
                silu_mul_quant_fp8_packed_triton,
                {"expert_ends": ends, "expert_alignment": 128},
            ),
        ]:
            output = torch.empty(
                (capacity, hidden), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn
            )

            def invoke(fn=fn, output=output, kwargs=kwargs, x=x, group=group):
                return fn(
                    x, group_size=group, output_q=output, clamp_limit=10.0, **kwargs
                )

            for _ in range(warmups):
                invoke()
            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
            graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
            with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
                for _ in range(graph_calls):
                    q, s = invoke()
            graphs[name] = (graph, q, s)

        for graph, _, _ in graphs.values():
            graph.replay()
        torch.accelerator.synchronize()

        live = torch.zeros(capacity, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bool)
        for start in starts.tolist():
            live[start : start + live_per_expert] = True
        for name in ("dense", "expert"):
            torch.testing.assert_close(
                graphs[name][1].view(torch.uint8)[live],
                graphs["baseline"][1].view(torch.uint8)[live],
                rtol=0,
                atol=0,
            )
            torch.testing.assert_close(
                graphs[name][2][live], graphs["baseline"][2][live], rtol=0, atol=0
            )
        samples = {name: [] for name in graphs}
        for iteration in range(iterations):
            order = list(graphs)
            if iteration % 2:
                order.reverse()
            for name in order:
                begin, end = (torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(2))
                begin.record()
                graphs[name][0].replay()
                end.record()
                end.synchronize()
                samples[name].append(begin.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / graph_calls)
        result = dict(
            capacity=capacity,
            experts=experts,
            live_rows=experts * live_per_expert,
            hidden=hidden,
            group_size=group,
            samples_us=samples,
            median_us={k: statistics.median(v) for k, v in samples.items()},
        )
        results.append(result)
        print(json.dumps(result), flush=True)
    args.output.write_text(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
                "warmups": warmups,
                "iterations": iterations,
                "graph_calls": graph_calls,
                "results": results,
            },
            indent=2,
        )
        + "\n"
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

title: [Bugfix][Engram] Keep THP tables private when resolving shared memory
body:
## Purpose

`use_thp` is silently ignored under DP. It is only validated against `dp_shared_memory` at construction, where the field is still unset. The DP default from #57651 then resolves sharing on for any CPU-offloaded, non-elastic run with DP > 1, and the table allocator takes the shared branch before the THP branch added in #56926:

```python
config = EngramConfig(use_thp=True)  # dp_shared_memory=None
config.resolve_dp_shared_memory(ParallelConfig(data_parallel_size=2))
config.dp_shared_memory  # True on main; the tables are never THP-backed
```

This PR leaves automatic sharing off when THP is requested (one added predicate, `and not self.use_thp`). That is what both fields already document: sharing defaults on "whenever the other settings allow it", and `use_thp` "requires cpu_offload without dp_shared_memory".

Effect on a DP > 1 run with `use_thp=True`: instead of one `/dev/shm` table shared by the node-local replicas, the tables are private, THP-backed and head-sharded across the node-local Engram DP group, which is the existing non-shared path. Host memory stays at one table per node (without co-located replicas, sharing was not possible anyway); lookups use the per-step Engram DP collectives that sharing avoids. THP versus shared-table performance under DP has not been measured here. Users who prefer sharing can leave `use_thp` unset.

Unchanged: every configuration without `use_thp`, explicit `dp_shared_memory=False`, and the construction-time rejection of explicit `use_thp=True, dp_shared_memory=True`.

Not a duplicate: open PR searches for `use_thp`, `dp_shared_memory`, `resolve_dp_shared_memory` and Engram THP found no fix for this interaction. #58439 adds a `checkpoint_mapped` predicate to the same expression for a different option; whichever lands second needs a one-line rebase.

## Test Plan

The existing resolver test matrix now also covers implicit THP, explicit private tables and elastic EP. A new test checks that explicit shared memory plus THP is still rejected. Both are pure config tests and use the existing `skip_global_cleanup` marker, so their teardown does not need an accelerator.

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/test_config.py \
  -k 'engram_dp_shared_memory_defaults or engram_thp_rejects_explicit_shared_memory'
```

## Test Result

Against main `6b24bd8e75a3e465083e8a131968915bc00efaf4`, running the new tests on the original and on the fixed `vllm/config/engram.py`:

```text
Original: 1 failed, 6 passed   (only the implicit THP case fails)
Fixed:    7 passed
Both:     0 errors, 0 skips
```

The tests ran in a CPU-only container (Python 3.12.13, pytest 9.1.1), with no config mocks or custom pytest plugin. Ruff 0.14.0 check and format passed.

No model evaluation: the change only selects which existing storage path holds the tables and does not change lookup results. The THP storage path and its exact-row lookups are covered by #56926's tests.

AI assistance was used: the initial fix was prepared with Claude, and Codex assisted with review, test preparation and validation.

title: [ROCm][MLA] Keep DCP prefill context in FP8 through AllGather
body:
## Overview

Keep ROCm MLA's cached DCP context in FP8 through AllGather, then use AITER's fused gather/projection kernel to expand it into K/V. This removes the BF16 communication payload and separate reorganization, dequantization, projection and packing operations for supported configurations.

```diff
 local cached context
-  gather/dequant → BF16 AllGather → reorg → kv_b_proj → K/V pack
+  gather bytes → FP8 AllGather → fused reorg/dequant/kv_b_proj/K/V pack
```

## Claims

- Halves AllGather bytes for the same padded row count, preserving the existing FP8 cache bytes, workspace capacity, chunking and merge plan.
- Falls back to the original path for unsupported cache formats, dimensions, dtypes or projection layouts. The optional upstream K/V concatenation callback is forwarded on that fallback.
- Historical full-model K3 measurements below show unchanged aggregate GSM8K accuracy and lower cached-prefix TTFT with **both this PR and #59069**. Those measurements do not isolate this PR's end-to-end contribution or validate the current rebased head.

## Validation

### Full-set K3 GSM8K (2026-10-12)

| Full GSM8K | Original context path | Fused context path |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Strict match | **1264/1319 (95.8302%)** | **1263/1319 (95.7544%)** |
| Flexible extract | **1264/1319 (95.8302%)** | **1263/1319 (95.7544%)** |
| HTTP success | 1319/1319 | 1319/1319 |
| Output-cap hits | 0 | 0 |
| Natural DSpark token acceptance | 96567/121728 (79.3301%) | 96818/122628 (78.9526%) |

### End-to-end K3 serving performance

Historical paired run on **8 × MI355X, TP8/DCP8**, complete Kimi-K3, FP8 KV, DSpark3 with natural/standard rejection, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, 80 max sequences, 16,384 batched tokens and 1,048,576 context. Candidate includes **#59069 + #59070**. These are full-model, single-instance serving measurements, not PD throughput measurements.

Each row reports server TTFT in **milliseconds, median [min, max] over three unprofiled repetitions** of the same prefix chain. All 24 first-token outputs, cache-hit counts and computed-token counts match between baseline and candidate.

| Request | Baseline TTFT | Candidate TTFT | Median change |

| Exact 32K repeat | 83.37 [82.56, 83.38] | 77.13 [77.05, 77.41] | −7.49% |
| Append 1,024 tokens | 290.44 [288.19, 297.70] | 291.09 [288.70, 294.20] | +0.22% |
| Fork at token 12,032 | 1114.15 [1114.11, 1114.24] | 1091.69 [1090.71, 1091.89] | −2.02% |
| Repeat fork | 69.97 [69.47, 72.26] | 64.42 [64.28, 64.70] | −7.94% |

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Do not let mark_miss() flip a pending or in-flight async lookup probe
body:
## Purpose

When a slow KV offload tier (the filesystem or object-store tier) fails to load a block, it records "this block is not really there" so the scheduler stops retrying it. That note is written against whatever lookup currently exists for the block. If the request that started the load was cancelled in the meantime, and another request has since asked about the same block, the note lands on the newer, unfinished lookup, and the engine crashes on an internal consistency check. The trigger is ordinary traffic: a client disconnects while its cached prefix is being loaded, and another request shares that prefix. The result is that the whole engine goes down, not just one request. This PR makes the note apply only to lookups that have already finished.

Concretely, `AsyncLookupManager.mark_miss()` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/async_lookup.py:216-224`) forces a cached lookup entry to `RESOLVED`/`False` without checking its phase. If the entry belongs to a newer probe that is still `PENDING` or `IN_FLIGHT`, that probe's own result later trips the phase asserts on the scheduler thread (`drain_results()` at `:204`, or `flush()` at `:181`), and the engine core dies.

How it happens with the FS tier (the OBJ tier calls `mark_miss` the same way, `obj/manager.py:400`):

1. Request A looks up key K and gets a hit. The tier starts a promotion (load job) for K.
2. A is aborted or finishes while the load is still in flight. `on_request_finished` calls `cleanup("A")`, which deletes the `RESOLVED` entry for K.
3. Request B looks up K. This creates a new `PENDING` entry, and `flush()` at the end of the step moves it to `IN_FLIGHT`.
4. A's load fails (file evicted, truncated or unreadable). `get_finished_jobs()` calls `mark_miss([K])` (`fs/manager.py:306`), which flips B's `IN_FLIGHT` entry to `RESOLVED`/`False`.
5. B's next `lookup()` drains the probe result and hits `assert state.phase is LookupPhase.IN_FLIGHT`. If step 4 lands while the entry is still `PENDING`, `flush()` asserts instead.

Needed: a client disconnect during a promotion, a failed load, and another request that shares the prefix.

**Fix:** `mark_miss()` now overrides only `RESOLVED` entries. A `PENDING` or `IN_FLIGHT` entry belongs to a newer probe, and that probe returns its own verdict. The #49176 livelock guard is unchanged: if the block is still bad, the next failed load marks the resolved entry `False` exactly as before, and the request stops re-issuing the promotion. One side effect: a newer probe that read the file before the failure can still return `True` once, which costs one more failed load. It does not loop.

**Not a duplicate:** I checked the open PRs that touch `async_lookup.py`: #57474 (draft, per-request-group result publishing), #58168 (draft, manager `lock()`/`unlock()`) and #52103 (draft, provenance). None of them changes `mark_miss` or the phase handling. `mark_miss` itself came in with #49328; #55823, #54872 and #55075 are the neighbouring merged fixes.

## Test Plan

```
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_async_lookup.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_fs_tier.py -q -k "mark_miss or failed_load"
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ -q
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
```

New tests:

- `test_async_lookup.py::test_mark_miss_skips_newer_unresolved_probe[in_flight|pending]`: the unit sequence above, for both phases.
- `test_fs_tier.py::test_failed_load_after_abort_does_not_break_newer_probe`: the same sequence end to end on `FileSystemTierManager`, with a load that really fails.

## Test Result

With the fix (macOS arm64, CPU, rebased on `32cc3f1ea`):

```
tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_async_lookup.py + test_fs_tier.py -k "mark_miss_skips_newer or failed_load_after_abort" ... 3 passed
tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ ... 436 passed, 1 skipped
```

On `main` (fix reverted, new tests kept): all 3 new tests fail on the engine asserts:

```
vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/async_lookup.py:204: AssertionError   (in_flight)
vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/async_lookup.py:181: AssertionError   (pending)
vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/async_lookup.py:204: AssertionError   (FS tier end to end)
3 failed
```

pre-commit (`--from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD`) and `mypy-3.12` (manual stage): clean.

This is a scheduler-side control-path change; model outputs are unaffected, so no evals are needed.

**Related:** one of a few independent fixes from an audit of the KV transfer paths (CPU offload, NIXL, P2P): #59099, #59102, #59325, #59329. None depends on another; they can be reviewed and merged in any order.

## AI assistance

I used an AI coding assistant (Claude) to audit this code path, write the fix and write the tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above myself. The commit carries a `Co-authored-by` trailer, as `AGENTS.md` asks.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Reserve the bonus KV slot for fill-in DSpark
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59104. DSpark with `sample_from_anchor=false` writes a bonus query plus N draft queries, but reserves only N lookahead slots. At a KV-block boundary, the extra write can use a stale block-table entry and corrupt another request's target KV.

Reserve N+1 slots for this layout. Anchor-sampling DSpark and DFlash behavior remain unchanged.

Related PR #48909 addresses the same mismatch with a broader four-file change, including a shared query-width property and the older runner's max-length guard. This PR is a smaller two-file alternative limited to lookahead reservation and its regression test.

## Tests

The commits are ordered test-first, fix-second:

1. `58eff92e7`: adds a plain regression test with loops and asserts; no pytest import or decorators.
2. `a26af2d9d`: fixes lookahead reservation.

```sh
python -m pytest --noconftest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_lookahead.py -k dspark_lookahead_covers_query_window -q
```

**Before: 1 failed. After: 1 passed.** The test covers 12 combinations of true/false/missing anchor flag, N=1/7 and block sizes 16/32, with prompt lengths spanning two blocks. Validation used the exact test file in an isolated pinned-nightly environment with the source fix applied; the full repository suite was not run. Ruff and `git diff --check` passed.

Standalone [synthetic CUDA reproducer](https://gist.github.com/notimesea/7de52434b9ef659e1ae6a6aab4d201b7) exercises the actual draft slot-preparation kernel without model weights or user prompts. It fails before the fix and passes after it; instructions and expected output are included in the gist.

## GPU validation

Gemma4-31B-it + RedHatAI DSpark on one H200, BF16, FA4, V2 runner, eager, synchronous scheduling, prefix caching off, no LoRA; vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev284+gbeef814e1`.

- Before: deterministic malformed output on batch 9; instrumentation confirmed two draft writes into target-owned blocks.
- After: three cold starts × 20 batches × 16 requests (**960 responses**), no observed corruption; identical output tokens across the three runs. On the originally failing batch, no invalid draft writes or target-KV mutations were observed.

This is bounded regression validation, not a full quality benchmark or a claim of bitwise equivalence to non-speculative decoding.

AI assistance: Codex assisted with debugging, implementation and tests.

title: [DSv4.1] Avoid runtime recompiles of _ring_slot_mapping_kernel
body:
## Summary

`_ring_slot_mapping_kernel` builds the compressor ring slot mapping in `CompressorMetadataBuilder.build()` and runs on every step. Its int args `num_tokens` and `num_actual_tokens` change from step to step, and Triton specializes int args by value (`== 1`, `% 16 == 0`, or neither), so each new combination compiles a new variant while serving. These compiles are not covered by startup warmup because the triggering combinations depend on the live batch (for example, a real token count that is a multiple of 16 padded to one that is not). Under DP/EP, a rank that stops to compile stalls every other rank at the next collective.

This PR marks `block_table_stride`, `num_actual_tokens` and `num_tokens` as `do_not_specialize`, so one variant is compiled at startup and reused for every batch. These args only feed address and mask arithmetic; dropping their divisibility hints narrows some loads/stores, but the kernel is latency-bound on its dependent loads and performance is unchanged (see below).

Evidence from a DSv4.1-Flash DEP4 AgentX run on GB200: a new variant of this kernel was compiled 46 min after the server was healthy, in the middle of a benchmark, and the Triton cache holds 6 variants of it.

This does not overlap with #58560, which changes the kernel's store mask (null block), not its specialization.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py`
- Kernel microbenchmark: main (bare `@triton.jit`) vs this PR on GB200, FlashInfer `bench_gpu_time_with_cupti` (CUPTI), `block_table_stride=1` and `CAPACITY=8` (5 draft tokens) as in serving. 37 token counts from 1 to 8192, exact and padded; outputs match exactly.

## Test Result

- 136 passed, 13 skipped.
- Performance is unchanged. PR / main geomean over the 37 shapes is 1.005 with cold L2 (range 0.99–1.02) and 0.98 with warm L2 (noise at ~1.5 us). Compiled variants over the sweep: main 5, PR 1.

| 1 / 1 | 2.11 | 2.14 |
| 42 / 48 | 1.98 | 2.02 |

| 366 / 368 | 1.70 | 1.73 |

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Fix inaccurate proportional store dropping
body:
## Purpose

`ThrottledDropPolicy` calculates what fraction of store attempts should be dropped based on pressure. This PR fixes how it applies that fraction.

For a calculated drop rate of 75%, the expected result over 20 store attempts is 15 drops and 5 allowed stores.

- Before: 10 dropped, 10 allowed. Only 50% are dropped.
- After: 15 dropped, 5 allowed. The calculated 75% rate is honored.

The old implementation rounds the rate into a "drop every N attempts" interval, which cannot represent rates such as 75%. The replacement carries fractional drops between decisions, keeping the cumulative drop count within one store of the calculated target.

This corrects application of the existing rate; it does not change how pressure determines that rate. Pressure detection and cooldown behavior are unchanged. These decisions control optional writes to secondary cache tiers, not inference-request admission.

Related to #50045. Duplicate-work checks found no open PR implementing this arithmetic correction. #51576 adds admission-policy infrastructure without changing this calculation; #51240 tracks the broader admission/backpressure work.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used to implement and test this change.

title: [Feature] Offload KV-init runtime state on sleep
body:
Based on main, which now includes #59156 (merged). The runner-construction part (former #59162) has moved to a separate follow-up; this PR covers only the state built in `initialize_kv_cache()`.

## Purpose

`/sleep` releases the weights and the KV cache, but not the other persistent GPU state built during KV-cache initialization. On DeepSeek-V4-Flash with TP4 on GB300 that state is about 4.6 GiB per GPU:

| Buffer | Size |
|---|---:|
| V2 block tables (staged + input) | 3.3 GiB |
| DSV4 sparse-MLA metadata | 1.0 GiB |
| Indexer metadata | 0.25 GiB |
| Sampler state and similar | small |

These buffers are allocated in `Worker.initialize_from_config`, but only the KV cache inside that call uses a sleep-mode pool.

This PR:
- Runs `model_runner.initialize_kv_cache(...)` inside a new cumem tag, `runtime`. That is where block tables and attention metadata are built. The KV cache keeps its own nested `kv_cache` pool.
- Needs no KV-connector exception. What in-tree connectors allocate on the GPU in `register_kv_caches` is scratch or pointer tables (e.g. the HF3FS staging buffers), which the offload restores at the same address with the same contents. The memory connectors register with a transport (NIXL, Mooncake, MoRIIO, LMCache-MP IPC) is the KV cache, which keeps its own `kv_cache` (or connector) pool. The aux-output connector's `RoutedExpertsCapturer.device_buffer` is likewise a plain tensor. XPU is the one exception, below.
- Has `CuMemBackend.suspend` offload `runtime` to host memory at every sleep level. These buffers hold live state, so they are copied rather than discarded. Wake copies them back to the same addresses, so captured CUDA graphs stay valid.
- Needs no wake-side change: since #59156 any wake, selective or not, restores every tag other than `weights` and `kv_cache`, so `runtime` comes back automatically, for example `wake_up(["weights"])` → `reload_weights` → `wake_up(["kv_cache"])`.
- Model Runner V1: with CUDA graphs, the memory profiler runs `initialize_kv_cache()` outside any pool, and for MLA, hybrid and multi-group models it rebuilds the `InputBatch` there. The real `initialize_kv_cache()` then saw matching sizes and kept that `InputBatch`, so the live block tables stayed in the default pool. `_cleanup_profiling_kv_cache()`, which already undoes the rest of the profiling KV init, now also resets `_init_block_sizes`, so the real call rebuilds the `InputBatch` under `runtime`, as it already does without CUDA graphs. Model Runner V2 needs no change: its `initialize_kv_cache()` always builds new `BlockTables`, inside the `runtime` pool for the real call.
- Leaves behavior unchanged when the sleep-mode allocator is off. On XPU the KV-init state stays outside `runtime` (see the XPU note below); CPU (no sleep mode) is unchanged.

Cost: sleep and wake copy the `runtime` bytes over the host link, about 4.6 GiB in the case above.

#59156 (merged) covers the workspace scratch.

## Test Plan

- New GPU unit test `test_runtime_state_survives_sleep[sleep-1|sleep-2]`:
  - `runtime` with a nested `kv_cache` pool keeps the tags separate;
  - a sleep at either level releases everything;
  - `wake_up(["weights"])` restores the runtime contents;
  - `wake_up(["kv_cache"])` restores the KV cache.
- End-to-end on 4× GB300 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash (TP4 + EP4, MTP, CUDA graphs):
  - memory after `/sleep`;
  - prompt logprobs before sleep and after each wake (level 1 twice, then level 2);
  - sleep and wake time.

## Test Result

**Current head `658bdd4b52` (on main with #59156 merged), H200, CI image `deb148e730`:** `test_cumem.py` 19, `test_sleep_mode_backend.py` 9, `test_gpu_worker.py` 20 passed. Model Runner V1, DeepSeek-V2-Lite with FlashMLA (block size 64, so the profiling pass rebuilds the `InputBatch`): with the `_cleanup_profiling_kv_cache()` reset the live block table is in `runtime`, without it the block table, slot mapping and sampling tensors of the `InputBatch` are not. Model Runner V2: the block tables are built in `initialize_kv_cache()` and are in `runtime`. opt-125m + `ExampleConnector` (kv_both), V1 and V2: outputs equal the awake run after level-1 and level-2 (+ `reload_weights`) wakes. An allocation audit of everything `initialize_kv_cache()` allocates under `runtime` (V1 and V2, FlashMLA, Triton MLA, FA3, FlashInfer, draft-model and ngram speculation, LoRA, a GDN hybrid) found no memory that is registered with a transport or exported, and no allocation or free in `runtime` after startup.

Earlier measurements. The re-validation sections from head `b0a91fd8f8` on were measured with heads that also built the model runner under `runtime`, which this PR no longer does: with a speculator, those asleep numbers are lower than this PR's by the MTP hidden-states buffer (512 MiB on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 192 MiB on GLM-5.3); without one the difference is negligible (DeepSeek-V4.1: 18583 MiB either way).

TP4 + EP4, auto MoE. Memory per GPU after `/sleep`:

| | Unpatched | Patched |
|---|---:|---:|
| Residual | 15178 MiB | **10487 MiB (−4691 MiB)** |
| Block tables / sparse-MLA / indexer metadata | 3361 / 1024 / 257 MiB | 0 |
| `runtime` tag (offloaded at level 1 and level 2) | — | 4704 MiB |

- **Correctness:** prompt logprobs are bit-identical to before sleep after both level-1 wakes. The level-2 round completes without errors; its output is garbage only because weights are discarded, same as unpatched.
- **Timing:** sleep 9.2–11.3 s (unpatched 9–11 s). Wake 1.0 s (unpatched 0.7 s); the extra ~0.3 s is copying the `runtime` bytes back.
- **Unit tests** pass. Pre-commit passes.

**Re-validation of the combined PR (head `b0a91fd8f8`), DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP4 + MTP, 4× GB300.** Gated bit-exact harness (553 requests per round, batch composition fixed by `/pause` gating; tokens, output logprobs and prompt logprobs compared with the first awake round):
- Asleep: **9977 MiB** on two GPUs / 10103 MiB on the other two, same after a second sleep (the PR2 + #59162 measurement was 9975 MiB).
- Every round is 553/553 bit-identical: after a level-1 full wake and after a level-1 selective wake (`weights`, then `kv_cache`).
- Sleep 1.2–1.3 s, wake 0.95 s.
- Unit tests `test_cumem.py` and `test_sleep_mode_backend.py`: 24 passed.
- With #59156 and #59160 merged on top: 6313 MiB asleep (6439 on one GPU), every round 553/553 bit-identical after full and selective wakes; merged unit tests 29 passed.

**Re-validation stacked on #59156 (head `0354f3d8a9`, #59156 at `21c7a0be4c`), DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP4 + MTP, 4× GB300, same image, another rack.** Gated bit-exact harness, 553 requests per round:
- Model Runner V2 (default): asleep **8775–8781 MiB** per GPU (15181 unpatched on these nodes; 9165–9293 with the previous heads). Every round 553/553 bit-identical after two level-1 full wakes and two level-1 selective wakes, plus 4 more sleep/wake cycles exact. KV cache 202.31 GiB / 13,036,348 tokens (unpatched 202.44 GiB / 13,044,408).
- Model Runner V1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`): asleep **7507 MiB** with the V1 `InputBatch` fix vs 9187 MiB without it (−1680 MiB: the block tables), same KV cache (12.26 M tokens). Both arms give the same 552/553 in every round, including the awake-only rounds, so the one differing request is V1 run-to-run variation, not sleep.
- V1 probe (Qwen3.5-0.8B, hybrid, 1 GPU, in-process): the live block tables move from the default pool to `runtime`; KV blocks equal unpatched (34471); full and selective wakes exact. Qwen3-8B (geometry matches the placeholder): identical with and without the fix, block tables already in `runtime`.
- Unit tests: `test_cumem.py` 15, `test_sleep_mode_backend.py` 11, `test_workspace.py` 11 passed.

**Large model accuracy (GLM-5.3, TP8 over 2 GB300 nodes, `mp` backend, MTP on).** GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0. Each cell is accuracy, and every run had 0 invalid answers. The unpatched numbers come from the same nodes and image (see #59156).

| State | Unpatched | Patched |
|---|---:|---:|
| Awake | 0.914 | 0.914 |
| Level-1 sleep, full wake | 0.914 | 0.913 |
| Level-1 sleep, selective wake (weights, then kv_cache) | 0.918 | 0.917 |
| Level-2 sleep, `reload_weights` | 0.911 | 0.911 |

- **Memory while asleep, per GPU:** 9449 MiB unpatched, 8847 MiB patched, so the runtime state saves 602 MiB. The level-2 sleep saves the same amount, and the state comes back correctly after `reload_weights`.
- **Timing:** sleep and wake timings are unchanged.
- **Errors:** no errors on either node.

**Large model accuracy (DeepSeek-V4.1, TP8 over 2 GB300 nodes, `mp` backend).** GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0. Each cell is accuracy / invalid rate.

| State | Unpatched | Patched |
|---|---:|---:|
| Awake | 0.892 / 0.002 | 0.906 / 0.001 |
| Level-1 sleep, full wake | 0.899 / 0.002 | 0.905 / 0.002 |
| Level-1 sleep, selective wake | 0.902 / 0.003 | 0.896 / 0.002 |
| Memory while asleep, per GPU | 21035 MiB | 18583 MiB (**−2452 MiB**) |

- `reload_weights` after a level-2 sleep produces garbage for this model with or without this PR: 172 "Failed to load weights" warnings from `layerwise.py` for `DeepseekV4MegaAttnAttention`, `DeepseekV4ScalingRotaryEmbedding` and `NgramHashState`. It is a separate, existing layerwise-reload gap, so level-2 accuracy is not compared here.

**Other model families (with #59156, TP4, 4× GB300).** In every phase, every request matches the first awake run exactly, text and all logprobs. The phases are level-1 full wake, level-1 selective wake, and level 2 + `reload_weights`. Level 2 + reload being exact confirms the runtime state comes back.

| Model | Asleep MiB/GPU, unpatched → patched |
|---|---:|
| Qwen3-8B | 4019 → 3605 |
| Llama-3.1-8B NVFP4 | 3949 → 3535 |
| Qwen3-VL-8B (text + image) | 4045 → 3629 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B (MLA + KDA) | 4809–4937 → 4733 |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B FP8, EP | 7363–7491 → 6829 |

- **GSM8K, Qwen3-8B** (awake / full wake / selective / level 2 + reload): 0.888 / 0.886 / 0.887 / 0.885.

**Lifecycle edge cases (with #59156, DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4):** all pass, bit-exact after each.
- 300 consecutive sleep/wake cycles with all sleep-mode PRs (alternating full and selective wake): every cycle bit-exact (34,140/34,140 requests), memory after wake equal to before sleep on every GPU, device-memory slope 0.000 MiB/cycle. Host RSS grows by about +5 MB/cycle over the first ~50 cycles of every launch, unpatched too; later slopes change sign between launches of the same configuration in both arms (patched −1.8 to +3.6, unpatched −0.5 to +0.6 MB/cycle) and the shared-memory backup stays byte-for-byte constant.
- Sleep right after startup.
- A request sent while asleep, or after a weights-only wake: it is queued and completes after the full wake.
- Double sleep and double wake: no-ops.
- Level 1 followed by level 2 without a wake: ignored.
- 256 concurrent mixed-length requests right after wake: no errors, no NaN.

**Configuration variants (with #59156, DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4).** Every post-wake round is bit-identical to the awake reference: 553 requests, tokens plus output and prompt logprobs.

| Variant | Asleep MiB/GPU, unpatched → patched | `runtime` tag |
|---|---:|---:|
| Default (MTP) | 15181 → 9293 | 4.59 GiB |
| MTP off | 13593 → 7589 | 4.57 GiB |
| Model Runner V1 | 12641 → 10083 | 1.31 GiB |
| `--enforce-eager` | 9851 → 3827 | 4.59 GiB |
| Chunked prefill, `--max-num-batched-tokens 2048` | 13561 → 8841 | 3.45 GiB |
| `--max-num-seqs 8` | 6973 → 4391 | 1.33 GiB |
| Qwen3-8B TP1 / TP2 (incl. level 2 + `reload_weights`) | 3123 → 2069 / 4133 → 3725 | 1.03 / 0.53 GiB |

- **KV connector (earlier heads, which skipped the KV-init `runtime` pool with a connector):** Qwen3-8B TP2 + `ExampleConnector`, asleep memory equal to unpatched. The current head drops that exception; see the current-head results above. DeepSeek-V4-Flash + `ExampleConnector` fails to start on unpatched vLLM too (`MLAAttentionSpec ... 'bounded_replay'`), so it is not covered.
- **Scaling:** the runtime state scales with `max_num_seqs` × `max_model_len`, as expected for block tables.

**Review:** three rounds of adversarial review (Codex, Kimi K3). The final round found no blocker or major issue.

---
This PR contains AI-assisted code (Claude Code); commits carry a `Co-authored-by` trailer.

### AMD MI355X (ROCm)

Works on ROCm unchanged, stacked on #59156 (vLLM ROCm nightly `e975732152`). Nested pools behave as on CUDA: the innermost pool wins, so the KV cache and the runtime state land in separate tags. Additional saving over #59156, memory per GPU while asleep (level 1): DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP1 −104, TP2 −110, DP2 −92 MiB; DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 −143 MiB. Outputs are bit-identical after full and selective wake.

AMD 50-cycle leak test (DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP1 / TP2 / DP2, DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4; with #59156): device-memory slope 0.00 MiB/cycle, 50/50 cycles bit-exact, no host-RSS growth over level-1 cycles, in-process memory after wake equal to before sleep. GSM8K on V4-Flash TP4 (1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0), awake R1 / R2 → full wake / selective wake / +10 cycles: unpatched 0.949 / 0.945 → 0.948 / 0.944 / 0.945; with #59156 0.947 / 0.948 → 0.949 / 0.948 / 0.947.

XPU: the XPU caching allocator allocates from the outermost active pool (`get_pool()` walks the active pools FIFO; CUDA uses LIFO since pytorch/pytorch#168382), so the nested `runtime`/`kv_cache` pools would share one pool there. On XPU the KV-init state therefore stays outside the `runtime` pool, as on main. A hardware check is requested in the comments.

title: [Bugfix][XPU] Make DeepSeek V4 FP8 sparse decode graph-capturable
body:
## Purpose

Fix DeepSeek-V4-Flash failing to start on XPU with graph capture enabled:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'level_zero backend failed with error: 44 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE)'
```

**Root cause:** `xpu_sparse_decode_fp8` used `.item()` host syncs, data-dependent tensor shapes, and a per-token Python loop. Level Zero graph capture doesn't support any of these.

**Changes:** Rewrite `xpu_sparse_decode_fp8` to use static shapes and vectorized index construction without host syncs, making it graph-capture safe to fix this bug.


## Test Plan

Start a DeepSeek-V4-Flash server on XPU with graph capture. The test cmds are as follows:

```
# EP4xDP2
ACC_LIMIT=256 VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1  VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH=1 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 DISABLE_EAGER=True   python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
--model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --port 8123 --host localhost --trust-remote-code --gpu-memory-util=0.85 \
--max-model-len=8192   --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 2 --enable-expert-parallel  --data-parallel-size 2     -tp=4  
# TP4xPP2
ACC_LIMIT=256 VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1  VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH=1 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 DISABLE_EAGER=True   python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
--model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --port 8123 --host localhost --trust-remote-code --gpu-memory-util=0.85 \
--max-model-len=8192   --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 2 -pp 2     -tp=4
# TP8
ACC_LIMIT=256 VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1  VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH=1 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 DISABLE_EAGER=True   python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
--model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --port 8123 --host localhost --trust-remote-code --gpu-memory-util=0.85 \
--max-model-len=8192   --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 2     -tp=8
```

## Test Result

- **Before:** server fails to start with the errors above.
- **After:** server starts normally and serves requests, the server hits another startup failure under pipeline parallelism:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error '', please check the stack trace above for the root cause
```
