title: [Feature] Release the CUDA graph pool on sleep
body:
## Purpose

With sleep mode on, CUDA graphs keep their private tensor pools resident after `sleep()` has unmapped weights and KV cache. On large MoE deployments this is GiBs per GPU that sleep cannot release. This PR adds an opt-in, `sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph` (off by default), that captures CUDA graphs into a dedicated cuMem-backed pool, so sleep releases their physical memory and wake remaps the same virtual addresses. Graphs are not recaptured. With the option off, behaviour is identical to main: plain graph pools, custom allreduce registers graph buffers, `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` is untouched.

The design follows SGLang's `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH` (off by default; sgl-project/sglang#7873, #32718, #40648); the table below compares the two item by item.

It is based on the graph-pool design from aoshen02/vllm#50 (same author), ported to current main, plus two fixes needed on multi-GPU deployments.

**Based on main, which now includes #59156 and #59158 (both merged)**: per-tag pool lists in `CuMemAllocator.allocator_and_pools`, and the rule that any wake restores every tag other than `weights` and `kv_cache`. With #59158's `runtime` tag, `CuMemBackend.suspend()` offloads `("weights", "runtime", "cudagraph")` at level 1 and `("runtime", "cudagraph")` at level 2.

**Must merge after #59228** (free-while-asleep fix in `csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp`). Without it, tearing down a cuMem graph pool while asleep (for example deleting the engine during sleep) double-unmaps it and leaves a sticky CUDA error. The weights and KV pools already have this failure on main; this PR extends it to the graph pool.

### Enabling it

```python
llm = LLM(model, enable_sleep_mode=True, sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph=True)
```

```bash
vllm serve <model> --enable-sleep-mode --sleep-mode-offload-cudagraph
```

`sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph` is a `ModelConfig` field next to `enable_sleep_mode` and `sleep_mode_backend` (the name keeps their `sleep_mode_` prefix and says what it does to graphs). It reaches `ModelConfig` through `EngineArgs` like its neighbours, with the CLI flag `--sleep-mode-offload-cudagraph` next to `--enable-sleep-mode`.

The pool is active when the option is on, `enable_sleep_mode` is on, the sleep backend is `cumem`, CUDA graphs are on and the platform is CUDA (`VllmConfig.use_cumem_cudagraph_pool`, the single predicate that the capture routing, `CudaCommunicator` and the NCCL default all read). If the option is on but another requirement is not met, the pool is simply not used and startup logs one warning saying which requirement is missing.

**Benefit when on:** graph memory is released while asleep at both levels (DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP: 2.3 GiB/GPU; DeepSeek-V4.1 TP8: 7.43 GiB/GPU; Qwen3-8B TP1: 332 MiB). **Cost when on:** pinned host memory for the pool's backup, also at level 2; about +3 % decode TPOT at concurrency 1 from the custom-allreduce copy (within noise at concurrency 16 and above); 0.05–0.1 s more per sleep.

### SGLang parity

| Item | SGLang | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Switch | env `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH`, default off | config field `sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph`, default off |
| Preconditions unmet | pool not used, silently | pool not used; one startup warning naming the missing requirement |
| Graph pool across sleep | backed up and restored (#32718, #40804) | backed up at both levels, restored by any wake |
| `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` | defaulted to `0` when active (#40648) | `setdefault("0")` when active; an explicit value wins with a warning |
| Custom allreduce | unregistered capture (#7873), keyed on the env alone | unregistered only when the pool is active (same predicate) |
| Runners | single runner | Model Runner V2 capture sites; on V1 see the limitation below |
| Recapture | n/a | elastic EP releases the pool before recapture |

### Scope

- Runner-agnostic predicate; the capture sites and tests are those of Model Runner V2, and V1 code is unchanged. Covered capture paths all go through one helper, `use_cudagraph_pool()` in `vllm/compilation/cudagraph_pool.py` (next to the capture sites, which keeps the NCCL `set_graph_pool_id` coupling at the compilation layer). It gets the allocator through `get_mem_allocator_instance()`; the predicate already requires CUDA, so that is `CuMemAllocator` (a narrow cast at the call site rather than new `MemAllocator` protocol methods, which XPU's allocator would not implement):
  - V2 FULL graphs (`CudaGraphManager.capture`, including DBO microbatch capture on the ubatch capture stream);
  - compiled PIECEWISE graphs (`CUDAGraphWrapper`);
  - breakable CUDA graph segments (`BreakableCUDAGraphWrapper`);
  - speculator graphs (autoregressive/EAGLE/MTP, DFlash, DSpark), which subclass `CudaGraphManager` and reuse its `capture()`.
- Memory profiling is deliberately *not* routed through cuMem: V2's `profile_cudagraph_memory()` captures inside `plain_cudagraph_capture()` (a `ContextVar`), so destroying the profiling graphs frees their pool as before.
- **V1 limitation:** with the option on under Model Runner V1, V1's profiling graphs stay in the cuMem pool (awake +326 MiB on Qwen3-8B, +1.6 GiB on DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4, not counted in the KV-cache estimate) and V1 DBO microbatch graphs stay in the plain pool; outputs are unaffected.
- Out of scope: encoder CUDA graphs (the encoder runner keeps its own `graph_pool_handle()`), and the Gemma4 centroids graphs in the V1 spec-decode path.

### Design

- **One graph pool, tagged `cudagraph`.** All routed captures share the process's single graph pool, as they share the global graph pool without sleep mode. `CuMemAllocator.use_cudagraph_pool()` creates one pluggable-allocator `MemPool` on the first capture, keeps it as a one-entry `cudagraph` list in `allocator_and_pools`, and yields its id for `torch.cuda.graph(pool=...)` while the allocator tags allocations `cudagraph`. There is no `use_mem_pool` (`capture_begin` routes allocations itself) and no trim loop, so reusing the pool is safe. The module-level `use_cudagraph_pool()` also points NCCL's graph allocator (`set_graph_pool_id`) at whichever pool is used, so the capture sites need no separate call.
- **CPU-backed at level 1 and level 2.** A captured pool is not only scratch activations. It can hold values written once at capture time (constants, persistent kernel or attention state) that replay reads but never rewrites. Discarding the pool corrupts those graphs. SGLang hit this and moved to backing up the graph pool across pause/resume (sgl-project/sglang#32718) and to keeping DSA graph state and the pool intact (sgl-project/sglang#40804). The pool is therefore always backed up to host memory, at level 2 as well. This costs pinned host RAM at level 2 as well: the pool is 2.3 GiB/GPU on DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 and 7.43 GiB/GPU on DeepSeek-V4.1 TP8 (about 60 GiB per 8-GPU node), in addition to the level-1 weight backup. Discarding the pool was also bit-exact on DeepSeek-V4-Flash (TP2 and TP4, full and selective wakes), but it is not safe in general, so the default stays offload.
- **Sleep policy lives in `CuMemBackend`; the allocator is mechanism only.** `suspend()` offloads `cudagraph` at both levels; like every tag other than `weights` and `kv_cache`, it is restored automatically by any wake, selective or not. The RL flow `wake_up(["weights"])` → update → `wake_up(["kv_cache"])` has graphs replayable once both are awake.
- **Pool lifetime.** The graph `MemPool` is kept together with its pluggable allocator wrapper and released by `release_pools()` like every other pool. Freeing an allocation while asleep (e.g. a graph pool at teardown) needs no spare VRAM and no Python remap: **this PR depends on #59228**, which makes the C++ `my_free` skip unmapping an allocation that `sleep()` already released and only free its address reservation (ROCm already skipped via an empty chunk list).
- **Recapture (elastic EP).** Elastic EP is the only runtime path that drops and recaptures graphs (on every scale). Each capture runs on a new stream (`graph_capture()`), and the caching allocator reuses a freed block of a live pool only on the stream that freed it, so recapturing into the kept pool grew it: DeepSeek-V2-Lite DP2↔4 with sleep mode went from 586 to 5098 MiB of graph pool on rank 0 over five scale cycles. Elastic EP now calls `release_cudagraph_pool()` (a no-op unless the pool is active) right after `release_graphs()` on the V2 path; the V1 path is as on main. Once no graph uses the pool, it is dropped, its segments are unmapped through the free callback, and the next capture starts a fresh pool. It refuses while the pool is asleep (freeing would unmap a second time) or while something still references it, and the message counts the other references and names the possible holders (live graphs, or a capture-time pool reference taken without a release, as NCCL symmetric memory did). That check found that graph release left the PIECEWISE graphs alive in the compiled model's wrappers until the recompile replaced them; `CudaGraphManager.release_graphs()` now clears them too, as profiling teardown already does. No other runtime path releases or recaptures graphs: LoRA and weight updates replay the existing graphs, and profiling captures into a throwaway plain pool.

### Custom allreduce fix

Custom allreduce IPC-registers the buffers that captured graphs read (`register_graph_buffers`). `cudaIpcGetMemHandle` rejects cuMem memory, so capture fails with `csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:164 'invalid argument'` and the worker exits. This was reproduced on GB300 with Qwen3-8B TP4, `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0` and `--compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"fuse_allreduce_rms":false}}'`.

When the cuMem graph pool is active, custom allreduce captures with `registered=False`: it copies the input into the pre-registered IPC buffer, which is `cudaMalloc` memory. SGLang does the same (sgl-project/sglang#7873), keyed on its env alone; here it follows the same predicate as the pool. `CudaCommunicator` reads `use_cumem_cudagraph_pool` from the current config once at construction (workers build communicators under `set_current_vllm_config`; without a config there is no sleep-mode policy, so graph buffers stay registered) and passes `register_graph_buffers=False` to `CustomAllreduce`, which itself reads no config and does not look at allocator state during capture. Custom all-gather and reduce-scatter always copy into the pre-registered buffer already, so they need no change. The cost is one device-to-device copy per captured allreduce, the same path eager mode uses, and only when the pool is active. Measured on GB300 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP, MTP, sleep mode on and awake): over five server restarts per build (four of them with a warmup), median decode TPOT at concurrency 1 is about +3 % for the whole PR (5.35 vs 5.21 ms) and +3.6 % for a control that only forces the copy (no cuMem pool), so the cost is the copy; the cuMem pool itself adds nothing measurable. Main's own restart-to-restart spread is 2.4 %. `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=0` alone costs nothing measurable. At concurrency 16 and above the difference is within run-to-run noise. On MI355X (#59523) the same copy costs +3.4 % (vLLM custom allreduce) and +2.7 % (AITER).

### NCCL graph registration

With `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` enabled, NCCL registers graph-captured user buffers and retains their cuMem handles. That pins about 400–510 MiB/GPU through sleep. After wake remaps new physical memory at the same address, NCCL also keeps stale registrations; in SGLang this caused hangs and wrong results (fzyzcjy/torch_memory_saver#88, sgl-project/sglang#40648). As in #40648, startup (`VllmConfig.__post_init__`, `_verify_cumem_cudagraph_pool`) sets `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=0` when the pool is active and it is unset, before any worker or communicator exists (workers inherit the environment; Ray copies `NCCL_*`). An explicit value is kept, with a warning giving the reason. An earlier revision also refused `TORCH_NCCL_USE_TENSOR_REGISTER_ALLOCATOR_HOOK`. On GB300 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP and DP4 + EP, hook=1 with that check removed, `NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=REG`), NCCL logged no buffer registration, memory while asleep and after each wake matched hook=0, and outputs matched hook=0, so the check was removed.

### What is not released

Graph executables (`cudaGraphExec_t`) and the driver memory they own are not released. They live outside any PyTorch pool. On DeepSeek-V4-Flash DP4, about 1944 MiB of graph-exec memory plus 1142 MiB charged during capture stay resident per GPU after sleep. Releasing them would require destroying and recapturing graphs, or checkpointing the CUDA process.

### Related work

- #47700 captures CUDA graphs into the `weights` cuMem pool. Graph memory then follows the weights policy: it is discarded at level 2 and restored only with weights. This PR gives graphs their own tag with an always-backup policy, so level-2 sleep and selective wake cannot corrupt captured state. It also covers FULL, compiled PIECEWISE, breakable and speculator capture in both runners.
- #56373 (closed) used CUDA checkpoint of the whole process. That releases everything, including graph executables and the context, but it supports a single GPU only. This PR works with TP/DP and keeps communicators alive, at the cost of the resident graph executables described above.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py -k cudagraph_pool
pytest -v tests/basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py -k cudagraph_pool  # TP=2 case needs 2 GPUs
pytest -v tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py -k cumem_cudagraph_pool
```

- `test_cudagraph_pool_sleep_and_release[sleep-1|sleep-2]` (allocator level): captures are not routed with the policy off or under `plain_cudagraph_capture()`, and are routed with NCCL's graph pool id following the pool. A captured graph that reads a pool-resident constant survives `suspend(level)` → `resume(["kv_cache"])` (which already restores the pool at the same addresses) → `resume(["weights"])` and replays correctly. Release is refused while asleep and while the graph is alive; afterwards the pool is empty and a recapture on a new stream refills it to the same size.
- `test_sleep_cudagraph_pool[...]` (engine level, tiny Llama): for each Model Runner V2 capture site (FULL, PIECEWISE, breakable) graph memory carries the `cudagraph` tag, `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` defaults to `0`, and greedy output is exact after level-1 and level-2 selective wakes; on V2, elastic EP's sequence (`release_graphs()`, `release_cudagraph_pool()`, `capture_model()`) empties the pool and refills it to the same size, twice. The TP=2 case forces the legacy custom allreduce. The `off-by-default` case checks that without the option there is no cuMem graph memory and `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` is untouched.
- `test_cumem_cudagraph_pool_startup_checks[...]`: active pool → `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=0`; an explicit value wins with a warning; not opted in → untouched, no log; opted in but inactive → one warning, env untouched.

## Test Result

**Opt-in and runner-agnostic revision (h200, Qwen3-8B TP1, sleep mode on, this branch on the CI image):**

| Runner | `sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph` | Awake MiB | KV cache tokens | `cudagraph` tag | Asleep MiB | GSM8K awake / after wakes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| V1 | off | 122379 | 731,296 | 0 | 1741 | 0.8832 / 0.8832 |
| V1 | on | 122705 | 731,296 | 658 MiB | 1411 | 0.8832 / 0.8817 |
| V2 | off | 120437 | 729,808 | 0 | 1555 | 0.8832 / 0.8840 |
| V2 | on | 120437 | 729,808 | 332 MiB | 1223 | 0.8825 / 0.8825 |

- V1 (code as on main): KV cache size is the same with the option on and off, but awake memory is +326 MiB and peak during GSM8K +266 MiB (124913 vs 124647 MiB), because V1's profiling graphs stay in the pool; outputs after full, selective and level-2 wakes are 16/16.
- Probe outputs (16 prompts, greedy) after three rounds of full, selective and level-2 wakes are 14–16/16 in all four arms, the same as three awake repeats without sleep (13–15/16 against the first run), so the differences are run-to-run batching variation, not the option.
- With the option off: no `cudagraph` tag, `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` untouched (engine-level `off-by-default` test).

**Current head (GB300 rack 4, nightly `0cbac6cd1` + #59158 + this PR per file; DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP, MTP, V2):**
- GSM8K awake / full wake / selective wake: 0.944 / 0.945 / 0.946 vs 0.947 / 0.951 / 0.941 without this PR (level 2 + reload is broken on V4 either way). Asleep 8945 → 6379 MiB/GPU; `cudagraph` tag 2342 MiB.
- 21-cycle soak (full, weights-first and kv-first selective wakes): memory flat, every probe exact, sleep about 1.0 s and wake 0.6–1.7 s per cycle.
- KV cache size matches the unpatched build to 0.01 %; the profiling graphs are released.
- TP2: exact after full and selective wakes. Qwen3-VL-2B (encoder graphs on) and a Qwen3-0.6B LoRA: exact after every wake order (h200).
- Elastic EP (h200, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, DP2↔4 ×5 with a level-1 sleep/wake after each cycle, Ray backend): the `cudagraph` tag stays at 586 MiB on every scale (it grew to 5098 MiB before the fix). Awake memory on rank 0 after each scale-down is 117341–117355 MiB, versus 117321–117325 MiB for the same build without sleep mode and 118135–118143 MiB on main with sleep mode. The 0.8 GiB below main comes from clearing the previous PIECEWISE graphs in `release_graphs()`, which the build without sleep shows too. Asleep: 6845 MiB vs 8219 MiB on main. Probe outputs match main in every arm (4/4 at DP2; 2/4 at DP4 in every arm, including main, from DP batching nondeterminism).
- Dual batch overlap could not be run on the current GB300 image: Model Runner V2 rejects `--enable-dbo` with speculative decoding, microbatching without MTP needs the DeepEP or NIXL EP all2all backend, and DeepEP low-latency fails at startup on that image (`cudaErrorSymbolNotFound` in `internode_ll.cu`) on main as well. The DBO capture path is covered by code review only.
- Unit tests on h200: `test_cudagraph_pool_policy.py`, `test_cumem.py`, `test_sleep_mode_backend.py`, `test_workspace.py`, the capture-site and TP2 custom-allreduce sleep tests: all pass.

- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass (ruff check/format, mypy, typos, SPDX, forbidden imports, torch.cuda API check, test tethering). `python -m py_compile` passes.
All runs are on GB300 with the nightly image, torch 2.13.0+cu130. The branch also needs the C++ fix from #59228.


**Re-validation after the restructure (head `d5f3bd94fb`, with #59156 underneath), nightly image, GB300.**
- **Unit tests:** `test_cumem.py` + `test_sleep_mode_backend.py`: 26 passed (single GPU). The graph-pool tests also pass with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`, so the capture path needs no expandable-segments toggle.

The TP=2 pytest regression needs hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM, which is not in the offline cache there, so the TP2 check used Qwen3-8B.
- **All sleep PRs merged** (#59156 + #59158 + this PR): asleep **6313 MiB/GPU**, 553/553 bit-identical after full and selective wakes; merged unit tests 29 passed.

- **Unit tests:** `test_cumem.py` 14/14, including both `test_cudagraph_pool_survives_sleep` cases; `test_sleep_mode_backend.py` 9/9.
- **TP=2 custom allreduce regression test:** passed, not skipped. Custom allreduce was active and graph memory carried the `cudagraph` tag.
- **Qwen3-8B TP4 with custom allreduce forced** (FlashInfer/symm-mem allreduce and allreduce+RMSNorm fusion off):

- **DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP4, MTP, bit-exact:** 553 deterministic requests (batch sizes 1–256) per round.
  - 13 rounds are identical to the awake baseline: 3× full wake, 3× selective wake weights-first, 3× selective wake kv_cache-first, plus awake rounds.
  - Level 2 + `reload_weights` is broken for DeepSeek-V4 on unpatched vLLM as well.
- **Memory while asleep, level 1, per GPU:**

  | Model / setup | Unpatched | This PR | `cudagraph` tag (backed up) |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4 + EP4, MTP | 15178 MiB | 12839 MiB (−2339) | 2.29 GiB |

- **Other model families (all sleep PRs combined, TP4):** level-1 full wake, level-1 selective wake and level 2 + `reload_weights` are all bit-exact against the first awake run. The engine used Model Runner V2 on every model.

  | Model | Asleep MiB/GPU, without → with this PR | `cudagraph` tag |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | Qwen3-8B | 3605 → 3561 | 0.04 GiB |
  | Llama-3.1-8B NVFP4 | 3535 → 3491 | 0.04 GiB |
  | Qwen3-VL-8B (text + image) | 3629 → 3573 | 0.05 GiB |
  | Kimi-Linear-48B (MLA + KDA), EP | 4733 → 4505 | 0.23 GiB |
  | Qwen3-235B-A22B FP8, EP | 6829 → 6585 | 0.24 GiB |

  GSM8K on Qwen3-8B across awake / full wake / selective wake / level 2 + reload: 0.885 / 0.882 / 0.892 / 0.885.
- **Sleep/wake latency:**
  - V4-Flash TP4: first sleep 3.09 s, later sleeps 1.2 s, wake 0.8 s. That is 0.05–0.1 s more than discarding the pool.
  - V4.1: the first level-1 sleep is about 1.7 s slower, because it backs up 7.4 GiB/GPU. Wake time is unchanged.
- **GSM8K on V4.1:** 0.897 / 0.901 / 0.899 for awake / full wake / selective wake, against 0.892 / 0.899 / 0.902 unpatched. Level 2 + reload is broken upstream for DeepSeek-V4.
- **GSM8K on GLM-5.3** (1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0):

  | Build | Awake | Level-1 full wake | Level-1 selective wake | Level 2 + `reload_weights` |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | Unpatched | 0.914 | 0.914 | 0.918 | 0.911 |
  | This PR | 0.910 | 0.916 | 0.915 | 0.917 |

- **NCCL guards:**
  - `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=1` fails at startup with a clear error (the register-hook check was removed, see "NCCL graph registration").
  - With sleep mode off, `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` is left unset and graph pools stay plain PyTorch pools.
- **Teardown while asleep with the freed VRAM taken by another process** (this PR + #59228): no error, no OOM.

---

AI assistance (Codex, Claude Code) was used for the implementation, porting, review and drafting of this PR. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing the changes and owns them end to end.

### AMD MI355X (ROCm)

This PR is gated on `current_platform.is_cuda()`, so it is inert on ROCm (verified: memory matches #59156 within 6 MiB). Enabling it on ROCm was tried as a local patch, not included here:
- `is_cuda()` → `is_cuda_alike()` alone fails at the first capture: a blocking `hipMemset` in `csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp` makes the legacy stream depend on the capturing stream. Running it as `hipMemsetAsync` on a private non-blocking stream fixes it.
- vLLM custom allreduce needs the same unregistered capture path as on CUDA (`hipIpcGetMemHandle` fails on cuMem memory). QuickReduce needs no change. RCCL honours `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER`, so the existing guard applies.
- With that patch, DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 stays bit-exact over 10 cycles plus a level-2 reload, but the graph pool is only 72–244 MiB per GPU: most graph memory (0.95–1.7 GiB) is held by the HIP runtime outside torch pools. Unlike CUDA, ROCm returns it when graphs are destroyed, so destroy-and-recapture would be the better option there (9–50 s per wake).

ROCm support is left for a follow-up.

title: [Bugfix] Fix DSpark graph-padding handling in the DeepSeek-V4.1 MoE fused top-k
body:
## Purpose


FIx https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56389
 ## Test Plan

  Hardware: 8× NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.2. TP=4, EP, DSpark with 5 speculative tokens,
  `max_num_seqs=1024`, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` CUDA graphs,
  `--moe-backend humming`.

  ```bash
.venv/bin/vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --seed 0 --port 8011 --max-model-len 500000 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  ```

``` python
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Concurrent traffic driver to force adaptive draft-budget trimming."""
import json
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

PORT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "8002"
N = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 16
MAXTOK = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 8

URL = f"http://localhost:{PORT}/v1/completions"
PROMPTS = [
    "Explain the theory of relativity in simple terms.",
    "Write a poem about a rainy day in the city.",
    "Summarize the history of the Roman Empire.",
    "Describe how a neural network learns.",
    "List five facts about the human brain.",
    "Tell a short story about a lost dog.",
    "Explain photosynthesis to a child.",
    "What are the causes of climate change?",
    "Describe the water cycle step by step.",
    "Write about the importance of sleep.",
    "Explain how the internet works.",
    "Give a recipe for chocolate chip cookies.",
    "Describe the life cycle of a butterfly.",
    "Explain the stock market in simple words.",
    "Write about the benefits of exercise.",
    "Describe the process of making coffee.",
]


def one(i):
    body = json.dumps({
        "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash",
        "prompt": PROMPTS[i % len(PROMPTS)],
        "max_tokens": MAXTOK,
        "temperature": 0.7,
        "seed": i,
    }).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(URL, data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=1800) as r:
            d = json.load(r)
        return i, d.get("usage", {}).get("completion_tokens"), time.time() - t0
    except Exception as e:
        return i, f"ERR {type(e).__name__}: {e}", time.time() - t0


with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=N) as ex:
    for i, ntok, dt in ex.map(one, range(N)):
        print(f"req {i}: tokens={ntok} in {dt:.1f}s", flush=True)
print("DONE")
```

title: [Config] Remove Engram CUDA-alike device restrictions
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59169.

Remove the CUDA-alike device restriction from Engram model validation and automatic config resolution. Hardware plugins implementing Engram can then reuse the native configuration without patching validation or recreating defaults in their platform hook. Supported-model, non-empty-layer and parallel-config checks remain unchanged.

This unblocks https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/17427 once Ascend updates its vLLM pin to include this change. Configuration acceptance does not itself add an Engram implementation to a backend.

Duplicate-work checks found no equivalent open PR. Prepared with AI assistance.

## Test Plan

Update the two existing CPU cases in `test_engram_model_support` to expect successful configuration. The test covers explicit validation and automatic defaults; existing cases retain unsupported-model and empty-layer coverage. No new test cases or platform interfaces are added.

```bash
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' \
  PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -k engram -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/config/engram.py vllm/config/vllm.py tests/test_config.py
```

## Test Result

43 passed, 367 deselected. Pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.

No hardware serving or model evaluation was performed; this changes configuration acceptance, not kernels or model execution.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Skip SWA bounded replay for KV loads that carry the window
body:
Also credit to @wangyicong52 who originally reported the issue and helped test the PR.

## Purpose

SWA bounded replay (#56227) replays the last window of every prefix hit, including KV loaded by P/D connectors, which transfer the request's own sliding-window KV. P/D decode on DeepSeek-V4.1 therefore recomputed the last 128 prompt tokens of every request. The whole-block rounding that replay applies to external hits also shrinks decode's allocation below what prefill exports, so NIXL's end-aligned pairing puts prefill block k + 1 into decode block k for the MLA groups whenever N % 128 != 0 (found with a CPU probe of the real scheduler and NIXL code).

## Changes

- The scheduler takes a load that restores every replayed group (`get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids`, added by #59504) as is: no replay, no whole-block rounding, and no dropping of hits no longer than the window. Async loads record the decision at admission and apply it when the KV arrives; failed loads and store / offloading loads still replay.
- Without the replay, decode relies on the transferred window as laid out, so NIXL and Mooncake now back off the last prompt token for models with bounded replay, as they already do for Mamba: prefill stops at N - 1, decode loads N - 1 tokens and computes the last one. Loading all N tokens and rewinding one after laying the window out for N dropped the block holding position N - W when N % block_size == block_size - 1, and the recomputed token attended to the null block, which DeepSeek-V4.1 does not keep zero.

- The prompt cut keeps two prompt-indexed features working (they were already broken for Mamba P/D): a request with prompt logprobs (e.g. completions with echo and logprobs) is not cut, since it skips reading the prefix cache and the decoder never loads its KV; before, the prefiller returned prompt logprobs for one token fewer than the prompt and the frontend failed. The routed-experts (R3) start is clamped to the prompt length; a start equal to the original length lay past the cut prompt and made the scheduler assert.

This PR stands alone. #59330 is the general fix: it applies the backoff to every model (a sliding window has the same rewind problem everywhere, it is only masked by a zero null block) and handles the prompt shapes that only Mamba used to reach (mixed token-id / embeddings prompts, a cut inside a multimodal item, push and Mooncake zero-token loads). DeepSeek-V4.1 is text-only and needs none of those.

## Not a duplicate

#59142 (draft, opt-in, Mooncake only) moves replay to prefill and certifies checkpoints; this PR drops the replay of KV that P/D already transfers, for any connector that declares it, with no new config. #58504 keeps partial external hits exact by retaining the boundary block; loads carrying the window skip the rounding here.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/{test_nixl_connector_hma,test_nixl_connector,test_nixl_push_connector,test_mooncake_connector,test_mooncake_connector_hma,test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba,test_multi_connector,test_remote_prefill_lifecycle,test_invalid_blocks_correctness,test_kv_load_failure_recovery}.py`: `test_kv_load_carrying_window_does_not_replay` (sync/async, window-long and unaligned hits), the NIXL backoff tests extended to bounded replay and prompt-logprob requests, and the aux output connector test extended to a start past the cut prompt.
- `pre-commit`
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D (NIXL, 1P1D TP4 + TP4), two-pass GSM8K 5-shot, concurrency 512; pass 2 re-sends the prompts so decode gets local prefix hits.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 754 passed.
- GSM8K flexible-extract. "N%32==31" counts pass-2 errors on prompts with N % 32 == 31 (the rewind case); "t < 16" pass-2 errors elsewhere with (N - 1) % 128 < 16, where the kept window lies almost entirely below a decode-side prefix hit (the zeroing race #59504 fixed). title: [Model][GLM-5.3-Flash] Support DCP for the kpool sparse indexer
body:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash cannot run with decode context parallelism. Its kpool sparse indexer compresses the indexer KV (`index_kpool=4`), and the indexer metadata builder rejects DCP whenever `compress_ratio > 1`. This check does not depend on the platform or the attention backend:

```
NotImplementedError: DCP is not supported with sparse indexer KV compression (compress_ratio=4)
```

This PR shards the kpool indexer across DCP ranks by pool:

- `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size` must be a multiple of `index_kpool` (e.g. 4), so each compressed pool lives entirely on one rank. The builder now raises a clear error when this does not hold.
- `CompressedSlotMappingKernel` is DCP-aware. Each rank writes only the compressed states it owns, at rank-local positions. Prefill chunk metadata uses the interleave measured in compressed units.
- Each rank scores its local pools, takes a local top-k, and merges it across ranks with the existing DSA DCP global top-k merge (`_merge_dcp_topk_global`), using the interleave in pool units. The result is global token ids, which the sparse MLA backend already filters and localizes under DCP.
- The CuteDSL DCP merge warmup keys use pool-level top-k and interleave for kpool models.
- The raw kpool tail ring (`KpoolTailSpec`) stays replicated on every DCP rank, like Mamba state. Its pages are self-addressed (`uses_slot_mapping=False`), so `resolve_kv_cache_layout` no longer treats it as a replicated draft group that requires a block-outer layout.
- Unchanged: DeepSeek-V4 compressed KV stays unsupported under DCP, and ROCm kpool raises explicitly.

## Repro

On `main`, this fails at engine startup with the error above. On Blackwell, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` supports DCP; the indexer builder check applies on any platform.

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash -tp 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8
```

With this PR, set the interleave to a multiple of `index_kpool`:

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash -tp 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
    --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4
```

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py \
    tests/models/glm5next/test_sparse_indexer_topk_dispatch.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py \
    tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
```

New tests:
- `test_compressed_slot_mapping_dcp_uses_rank_local_state_positions`: each DCP rank writes only its own compressed states, at rank-local slots.
- `test_dcp_replicated_kpool_tail_keeps_block_interior_layout`: a replicated kpool tail does not force a block-outer layout.

E2E: GSM8K (1319 questions) at 5, 25, 50 and 100 shots with `vllm serve` at TP8 + DCP8 + `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4`, compared with TP8 alone (bf16 KV, no MTP).

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 309 passed on 1×H100. The 2 failures are `test_get_kv_cache_config_mamba_hybrid_sharing_pp_*`, which need more than 1 GPU for their PP config and are unrelated to this change.
- E2E was run on 8×H100 together with a separate local SM90 attention-backend change that Hopper needs for DCP at head_dim 512 (out of scope here). I did not have Blackwell hardware to run this PR on its own.

| Config | GSM8K accuracy |
|---|---|
| TP8 | 0.911 – 0.922 |
| TP8 + DCP8 (interleave 4) | 0.916 |

5-shot GSM8K prompts are shorter than `index_topk` (2048 tokens), so that eval only lightly exercises the cross-rank top-k selection. To cover longer contexts, I raised the shot count. Both configs ran on the same build:

| Shots | Prompt tokens | TP8 | TP8 + DCP8 (interleave 4) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | ~650 | 0.916 | 0.913 |
| 25 | ~4.3k | 0.909 | 0.917 |
| 50 | ~8.5k | 0.920 | 0.920 |
| 100 | ~16.9k | 0.926 | 0.922 |

Accuracy matches TP8 at every length, including 100 shots (about 8× `index_topk`). Prefix caching was on, so the shared few-shot prefix is mostly a cache hit, while decode and the question chunks run the top-k selection over the full context.

## Duplicate check

I searched open PRs and issues for GLM-5.3-Flash / kpool / sparse-indexer DCP and found none that enables DCP for compressed indexer KV. #57161 reworks kpool compression and scheduling but does not touch DCP.

## AI assistance

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed the changes and ran the tests above.

title: [CI][Kimi-K3] Test prefix cache reuse with KV offload, P/D and DCP
body:
## Purpose

Kimi-K3 has no end-to-end prefix-cache coverage. FlashKDA exports Mamba prefill checkpoints, a path the Qwen3.5-based `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` never takes, so regressions such as the dropped prompt-end checkpoint fixed by #59146 / #59175 reach users unnoticed. KV offload, P/D and DCP are not tested with K3 at all.

This adds `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_prefix_cache.py`. It serves [`riverclouds/Kimi-K3-8L-dummy`](https://huggingface.co/riverclouds/Kimi-K3-8L-dummy) (the official Kimi-K3 config with 8 layers and no weights) with `--load-format dummy`, and runs 3 turns where each turn extends the previous prompt. Each turn must:

- hit at least the previous prompt's end checkpoint (`cached_tokens`), and
- produce the same greedy tokens as a recompute of the same prompt under a fresh `cache_salt` (`check_logprobs_close`). This catches restored state that is wrong even though the hit count looks right.

With offloading, GPU prefix caches are reset before each turn, so the hit has to come back from CPU.

Every deployment runs in 4 modes:

- `block`: Mamba-block granularity.
- `partial`: `--prefix-match-unit 128`, i.e. partial hits.
- `block-dspark` and `partial-dspark`: the same, plus DSpark speculative decoding as in the recipe. The draft is [`riverclouds/Kimi-K3-DSpark-for-8L-dummy`](https://huggingface.co/riverclouds/Kimi-K3-DSpark-for-8L-dummy), which is `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` with `target_layer_ids` remapped to the 8-layer target and no weights. With EAGLE-style block drop, the expected hit is one unit lower.

| deployment | GPUs |
|---|---|
| plain | 1 |
| SimpleCPUOffloadConnector (config from the [Kimi-K3 recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/moonshotai/Kimi-K3?kv_offload=simple)) | 1 |
| DCP2 | 2 |
| DCP2 + SimpleCPUOffloadConnector | 2 |
| P/D (NIXL) TP1 → TP1 | 2 |
| P/D TP2 → DEP2 (decode: DP2 + EP, TP1 per rank; prefix caching on P only, since NIXL rejects it on a hybrid decoder with a different TP) | 4 |
| P/D + SimpleCPUOffloadConnector (MultiConnector) | 2 |

CI: a new `(4xB200) Kimi K3 Prefix Cache Shard %N` step runs the file in 2 shards. It installs NIXL with `.buildkite/scripts/install-kv-connectors.sh` first, because the CI image does not include it. It is triggered by `vllm/v1/core/`, `vllm/v1/spec_decode/`, the NIXL and SimpleCPUOffload connectors, `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/` and `vllm/models/kimi_k3/`. The existing 1xB200 Kimi K3 step ignores this file.

### Known failures (strict xfail)

- `dcp2-*-dspark`, `dcp2-offload-*-dspark`: FlashInfer MLA DCP decode crashes on ragged spec-decode batches (`causal_seqlens_kv_global must have shape (9,), got (2,)`). This is fixed by #59392.

### Not covered

P/D + DCP: NIXL with DCP sets `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` to the block size (`vllm/config/vllm.py`), but FlashInfer MLA native DCP requires 1, so the server fails to start. A P TP → D DCP case can be added once that is fixed.

### Depends on #59146 or #59175

On current `main`, every block-granularity case fails at turn 1 with `cached=0 expected=17280`, which is the bug those PRs fix. Partial cases pass on `main`. This PR stays a draft until one of them lands.

### Not a duplicate

There are no open PRs adding Kimi-K3 prefix-cache, offload, P/D or DCP tests. #59146 and #59175 fix the scheduler bug and add unit tests only.

## Test Plan

On GB200 (SM100), with #59146 cherry-picked onto main (`379e9a1`):

```
pytest -v -s tests/models/kimi_k3/test_prefix_cache.py
pre-commit run --files tests/models/kimi_k3/test_prefix_cache.py .buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml
```

## Test Result

On main + #59146, one 4xGB200 node. The full run predates two changes: `pd-tp1-tp2` was replaced by `pd-tp2-dep2`, and `pd-dcp2` was dropped. It ran 32 cases: `24 passed, 4 failed, 4 xfailed in 5136.53s (1:25:36)`. The 4 failures are the `dcp2*-dspark` cases, marked xfail after the run started. The 4 xfails were `pd-dcp2`. The `pd-tp2-dep2` cases were run separately on this branch at `c2a0aaa` (merged with main): `4 passed in 1138.28s (0:18:58)`.

| deployment | block | partial | block-dspark | partial-dspark |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| plain, offload | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| dcp2, dcp2-offload | pass | pass | xfail (#59392) | xfail (#59392) |
| pd, pd-offload | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| pd-tp2-dep2 | pass | pass | pass | pass |

Each case prints its turns. For example, `dcp2-offload-partial`, with GPU prefix caches reset before every turn:

```
turn  prompt  cached  expected  matches_recompute
   0    8869       0         0  True
   1    9646    8832      8832  True
   2   10423    9600      9600  True
```

With DSpark (`pd-offload-partial-dspark`), the expected hit drops by one 128-token unit:

```
turn  prompt  cached  expected  matches_recompute
   0   18469       0         0  True
   1   19246   18304     18304  True
   2   20023   19072     19072  True
```

On main without the fix, `plain-block` fails at turn 1 (`cached=0 expected=17280`) and `plain-partial` passes. Each server start takes about 70–90 s.

With `OffloadingConnector` instead, DCP2 hits CPU only when the prompt-end checkpoint lands on a multiple of the DCP-scaled MLA chunk. That connector is not in the recipe, so it is not covered here.

No model outputs change (test and CI only), so no eval was run.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this test.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Resolve MTP verification rows with a union residency kernel
body:
## Purpose

Resolve all of a request's MTP verification rows with one union residency kernel, on every sparse MLA backend, and drop the fragile routing that worked around the old kernel.

The old `hisparse_resolve_residency_kernel` ran one block per row, but `device_global_indices` and the LRU are per request, so two rows of one request in one launch could claim the same free slot and read each other's KV. Callers avoided that by resolving verification one step per launch (FlashMLA, FlashInfer TRTLLM) or by treating it as prefill (backends without `hisparse_supports_multi_token_decode`). On FlashAttn sparse MLA a FULL CUDA graph froze that prefill path's residency check at capture, so replays with spilled pages still hit the race. Found via #59036's CI failure (`test_hisparse_spill_and_prefix_restore`).

## Changes

- **Union kernel.** Each request's first-row block resolves all its rows: one hash-table union of host misses, one LRU walk, eviction slots in deterministic (row, top-k) order, one LRU rewrite. Each host row is copied once per request; a reused slot counts as a hit. The table is sized from `max_decode_query_len * index_topk` (~90 KB for GLM-5.3 + MTP3, MTP ≤ 9 at `index_topk=2048`), checked at startup; a union past that bound traps.
- **One routing path.** Verification resolves in one `swap_in` per layer, and `hisparse_supports_multi_token_decode` is removed, so every backend keeps verification as decode. Request ids (with CUDA-graph padding rows masked) live in a group-owned buffer, since the resolver reads them on the copy stream.

## Test Plan

- New `test_hisparse_speculative_rows_resolve_host_misses_consistently` (disjoint, overlapping, and multi-pass rows) plus unit tests for hit counting, union-bound sizing, the startup check, spec-as-decode, and padding/request-id handling.
- HiSparse kernel, sparse MLA backend, and e2e tests; #59036 applied on top.
- GLM-5.3-NVFP4 + MTP3 on B200 (FlashInfer TRTLLM, HiSparse under spill pressure), and a layer-level benchmark on H100.

## Test Result

- Race test fails 30/30 on main's kernel and passes with this PR; HiSparse tests pass (H100, H200, B200); `test_hisparse.py` passes, also with #59036.
- GLM-5.3 B200: MTP acceptance in line with main (1.06–1.32 vs 1.19 per window on random prompts); a shrunk GLM-5.3 config matches main's tokens and drafts exactly under FULL graphs.

Decode residency per layer, µs (H100, MTP3, `index_topk=2048`, main → this PR). **Bold** = faster by >5%.

| Mode | Regime | 1 req | 8 reqs | 32 reqs | 64 reqs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CUDA graph | steady | 155 → **64** | 185 → **87** | 264 → **167** | 373 → **268** |
| | cold | 189 → **129** | 582 → **539** | 2119 → 2174 | 4213 → 4139 |

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; the root cause was reproduced and validated on H200, H100, and B200.

title: [Spec Decode][MRV2] Warm up top-k/top-p and greedy rejection kernels for speculative decoding
body:
## Purpose

With speculative decoding, Model Runner V2 compiles sampling kernels in the first verification steps instead of at startup, so the first requests stall.

- **Commit 1:** register the native top-k/top-p warmups on CUDA when speculative decoding is configured. #58465 limited them to ROCm, but verification always masks top-k/top-p with these kernels, never with FlashInfer's fused sampler. Target-only CUDA engines are unchanged.
- **Commit 2:** when a rejection sampler exists, run the scheduler warmup a second time with greedy requests. All-greedy batches skip logits processing, so the rejection kernels see BF16 logits, a variant the warmup never compiled. Fixes #54455.

Not a duplicate: #56654 and #58465 removed CUDA sampler registration for its startup cost; this re-enables only what speculative decoding needs. #54630 (open) targets #54455 with mixed warmup configs, but on current main it calls `Sampler.add_request` with the signature from before #56497.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_mixed_warmup_gate.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py tests/model_executor/test_jit_warmup*.py`, and pre-commit including mypy.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark (5 speculative tokens), TP4 on one GB300, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. Main, commit 1 and this PR were started interleaved on one node with a fresh Triton cache per start (4 starts each; other caches warm). After `/health`, each server got one streaming request (top-p 0.9 or greedy), then 64 concurrent mixed requests. Compiles were counted with `--jit-monitor-verbose`.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 219 passed, 1 skipped on main and on this PR. pre-commit and mypy pass.

| | main | + commit 1 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| First top-p request, 2nd token | 2.07 / 2.09 s | 0.45 / 0.44 s | 0.43 / 0.45 s |
| First greedy request, 2nd token | 1.58 / 1.50 s | 1.47 / 1.62 s | 0.42 / 0.42 s |
| Compiles in the 64-request burst | 27 | 0–5 | 0 |
| Warmup time¹, cold Triton cache | 37.2 s | 52.9 s | 55.0 s (greedy pass 2.0 s) |
| Warmup time¹, warm Triton cache | 26.6 s | 26.1 s | 27.0 s (greedy pass 1.0 s) |

¹ JIT kernel warmup plus `warmup_kernels`. Commit 1 adds 22.1 s of registry warmup (120 more keys) and saves 6.5 s in `warmup_kernels`, which on main compiled these kernels itself.

TTFT doesn't change (0.40–0.57 s on all builds); the first token comes from prefill. The stall was in the first verification step, before the 2nd token. Greedy outputs are byte-identical across the three builds, and acceptance length is unchanged (2.84).

Limits: target-only batches that can't use the fused sampler still compile on first use, as on main. Seeded requests (#54425) aren't covered. Only tested on GB300 with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark; ROCm and pipeline parallelism are untested.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Qualify Transformers backend attention layer names with the model prefix
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59292.

`method="draft_model"` speculative decoding fails at engine start-up when both the target and the drafter run on the Transformers modeling backend. One example is OLMo-2, which has been served through `TransformersForCausalLM` since v0.26.0:

```text
ValueError: Duplicate layer name: 0.attn
```

`Base._create_attention_instances` named every attention layer `f"{i}.attn"` and ignored the `prefix` passed to `Base.__init__`. The drafter is built in the same engine with `prefix="draft_model"`, in both the V1 proposer and the model runner V2 speculator. Target and drafter therefore registered the same layer names.

This PR passes the model prefix through and names each layer `maybe_prefix(prefix, f"{attn_prefix}.{VLLM_ATTN_ATTR}")`, where `attn_prefix` is the attention module's qualified name inside the model:

- The drafter's layers now sit under `draft_model.`, so they no longer collide with the target's.
- Layer names follow the module path, which is how native models already name their attention layers. This also changes the names of a model built with an empty prefix, from `0.attn` to the module path.
- The new argument is optional, so direct callers of `Base._create_attention_instances` are unaffected.

**Update after review.** My original commit named the layers `maybe_prefix(model_prefix, f"{i}.attn")`. The review commit 9bef685 by **hmellor** switched to the qualified module name, renamed the loop variable to `attn_prefix` so the parameter can be called `prefix`, and removed a unit test that only restated the naming formula with mocks. The description above reflects the final code.

## Test Plan

- End-to-end (1 GPU): `pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_draft_model.py::test_draft_model_transformers_backend`. OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct drafts for itself with greedy sampling, so acceptance should be close to 1.
- The issue's minimal reproduction, on model runner V2 (default) and V1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`), before and after the change.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`
- Full CI on the final commit.

## Test Result

**Final commit (`de4e6c4`).** [Buildkite CI #92113](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/92113) passed, including the `spec-decode-draft-model` jobs on NVIDIA and AMD.

**Local runs.** These were done on my original commit (`d544cff`), before the review changes. I have not repeated them on the final commit.

Before (`main` at `cb4f016c5`), the minimal reproduction from the issue fails on both model runners:

```text
ValueError: Duplicate layer name: 0.attn
```

The new end-to-end test fails the same way (`1 failed … RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed`, root cause `Duplicate layer name: 0.attn`).

After:

- Reproduction: the engine starts and generates on model runner V2 (default) and on V1. Greedy output is identical on both: `' Paris, and the largest city in France is Lyon. Lyon is known for its'`.
- A realistic pairing, `OLMo-2-1124-7B-Instruct` as target with `OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct` as drafter: fails with `Duplicate layer name: 0.attn` before the change; after it, the engine starts and generates.
- End-to-end: `test_draft_model_transformers_backend` gives `1 passed in 200.68s`, with `acceptance_rate=0.99, acceptance_len=3.98` (K=3, so at most 4.0), as expected when a model drafts for itself.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks passed, including ruff, typos, mypy and the Buildkite test-wiring check.

Environment: NVIDIA RTX 5090, torch 2.13.0+cu130, Python-only build (`VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`). This machine has no CUDA toolkit, so FlashInfer's JIT sampler cannot build here. I ran the V1 reproduction and the end-to-end test with `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`; that setting is unrelated to this change.

---

AI assistance: this change was prepared with help from Claude (Anthropic). I reviewed every changed line and ran the local tests above. My commit carries a `Co-authored-by: Claude` trailer and my DCO sign-off.

title: [Misc] Remove tool name from warn logs
body:
## Purpose

Tool names are user input and must be kept private. 

Previously, WARN logs for malformed tool calls did include tool names, e.g.:
```
Tool call 'my_tool' has arguments that are not valid JSON (420 chars); coercing to an empty object so the conversation can continue.
```

After this change, the WARN log does no longer print sensitive information:
```
Tool call has arguments that are not valid JSON (420 chars); coercing to an empty object so the conversation can continue.
```

Upside: vllm can be used in privacy-relevant applications without custom patches
Downside: debugging is more complex in case of malformed tool calls. We could add DEBUG logs that include the tool name, if strongly desired.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Fix MTP acceptance collapse under FULL graphs with a saturated GPU pool
body:
## Purpose

Fixes MTP acceptance collapsing with HiSparse + speculative decoding under FULL CUDA graphs once the HiSparse GPU pool saturates. Two independent causes; both are needed on current main.

**1. Draft rows mirrored before the drafter writes them.** The MTP layers are HiSparse layers too, and HiSparse marks a page clean and releases it for all of its layers, target and draft, at once. Each step does:

```
start_step → target forward → finish_forward → propose (drafter writes its rows)
```

`finish_forward` mirrored *all* layers to host, including draft layers whose rows `propose` had not written yet, and then reported the step's pages clean. The drafter's own per-layer mirror is skipped under FULL graphs, so the fresh draft rows never reached host. When the page's GPU block was reused, the drafter read stale host rows.

**2. The residency resolver can read stale request ids** (regression from #59235). The resolver runs on the HiSparse copy stream, which outside PIECEWISE graphs waits only on `logical_topk_ready`, recorded right after the indexer. #59235 writes the masked request ids later, on the compute stream, so the resolver can read the previous call's ids. The MTP layer alternates four rows per request (draft prefill) with one (draft decode), so stale ids resolve draft rows against other requests' KV.

## Changes

- The speculator tags its draft attention layers (`AttentionLayerBase.is_draft_layer`); HiSparse binding marks their cache handles as draft layers.
- `finish_forward` mirrors only target layers.
- The next step's `start_step` first mirrors the previous step's draft-layer rows (the drafter has run by then), then submits that step's page transfers behind them on the same DMA stream, so a page is only reported clean after its draft rows are queued. They are queued before the step swaps host write events, so the new step's forward and host copies wait for them: by then the scheduler may have handed a finished request's GPU and host blocks to another request. No connector API changes (`wait_for_save` stays a no-op).
- Build the resolver's masked request ids on the copy stream after its wait, into buffers owned by the HiSparse index group (moved from the generic `SparseMLAIndexGroup`); `swap_in` now requires the valid-row count.

**Why not just move `finish_forward` after `propose`?** Outside FULL graphs the drafter re-prepares the draft handles with its own (decode-shaped) metadata, so a combined end-of-step mirror hits HiSparse's metadata consistency checks (`RuntimeError`) for every target/drafter graph-mode mix except FULL/FULL. Target and draft layers need to be mirrored at different points, which requires knowing which layers are draft layers.

**Known limitation (follow-up).** A host block freed after step N (finished or preempted request) can be reallocated to a P/D import before step N's deferred copies land; NIXL writes are not ordered against the copy stream, so an imported request could, rarely, receive stale draft-layer rows (or, with the non-default lazy mirror mode, stale rows for all layers of a preempted request's spilled page). GPU writes and host copy-on-write are ordered: the next step waits for the deferred copies before its forward and host copies. The follow-up holds freed host blocks until the step's deferred writes are reported done.

## Test Plan / Results

**Unit:**
- `test_draft_layer_rows_mirrored_after_drafter[FULL|NONE]` drives the real worker and checks that host draft rows equal the drafter's writes, with exactly one draft-layer copy and the page reported only after it. On main the FULL case fails.
- `test_hisparse_resolver_reads_current_request_ids` (GPU) stalls the compute stream between `logical_topk_ready` and attention, then resolves four rows per request followed by one row per request plus a padding row. It fails on main and passes here.
- H100: `test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "hisparse or index_group"` 40 passed; HiSparse connector/worker tests pass.
- `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: the FULL-graph host-mirror check now verifies MTP rows when the next step's start mirrors them (it compared them right after `finish_forward`, before the drafter writes them) and requires the MTP layer to be detected as a draft layer. 4 passed (H100); fails if the speculator stops tagging its layers.

**E2E, cause 1 (on the pre-#59235 base):** H200 2×8, GLM-5.3 TP8/EP8 HiSparse decoder, MTP3, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, NIXL P/D from a PCP8/DCP8 prefiller; Agent X workload at concurrency 48 (HiSparse GPU pool ≥95%).

| | MTP acceptance | per position | output tok/s | ITL p50 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | 0.248 | 0.46/0.19/0.09 | 438* | 66.0 ms |
| cause 1 fixed | **0.503** | 0.68/0.48/0.35 | **727.7** | 50.1 ms |
| before, PIECEWISE only (per-layer mirror active) | 0.471 | 0.66/0.45/0.30 | 664.6 | 51.8 ms |

\* includes debug-counter overhead; the pre-fix sweep peaked at ~500 tok/s.

- Host-vs-GPU audit of sealed MTP-layer pages: 98.7% mismatch before, 60.3% after, in line with the target layers' 58.6% (the audit also samples pages that are still being written).
- gsm8k (5-shot, 500) through P/D: 0.928 (0.920–0.936 before).

**E2E, current main:** B300 ×4, GLM-5.3 FP8 TP4, MTP3, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, GPU KV capped at 8 GiB (pool saturated), 40 code prompts × ~16k in / 512 out.

| | acceptance length | output tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | 1.37 | 113–138 |
| cause 1 fix only | 1.31–1.48 | 123–138 |
| cause 2 fix only | 1.37 | 133 |
| **both (this PR)** | **2.68** | **295** |

PIECEWISE on main under the same pressure: 2.29. The cause-2-only row used an earlier variant of the same fix (re-recording the event after the write).

Mirroring draft rows at the next `start_step` instead of in `wait_for_save` (B300, same setup, `--async-scheduling`, 2 runs each): acceptance length 2.80/2.72 vs 2.78/2.70, median ITL 33.6/34.0 ms vs 33.3/33.8 ms; throughput differences are within run-to-run noise.

Cost of the copy-stream build, per resolving layer in a CUDA graph (H100, 32 reqs × 4 rows, top-k 2048, all hot hits): 132.5 µs → 134.1 µs (+1.2%); with host misses the difference is within noise.

No other open PR addresses this. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; changes reviewed and tested by the submitters.

title: [Rust Frontend] Add per-request timing metrics to chat and completions
body:
Implements the per-request `metrics` (`--enable-per-request-metrics`) roadmap item in #44280. Speculative-decoding acceptance stats remain a separate checklist item.

## Summary

- Accept `--enable-per-request-metrics` in the Rust frontend and reject it alongside `--disable-log-stats`.
- Carry the engine's queue, schedule, first-token, and last-token timestamps through decoded text and chat output.
- Return Python-compatible timing fields in non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` responses. For streaming, attach them to the final usage chunk when `stream_options.include_usage` is enabled.
- Serialize unavailable timing fields as `null` in non-streaming responses and omit them from streaming usage chunks, matching Python's recursive `exclude_none=True` behavior.

## Implementation detail

Each engine output carries the current request-timestamp snapshot. This is required because the Rust text decoder can terminate a request locally after matching a stop string, before the engine emits a terminal output. Keeping the snapshot with the current output lets that path report valid metrics; limiting timestamps to engine-terminal outputs caused the Rust frontend to panic in Buildkite CI. The snapshot is four `f64` values and does not add GPU synchronization.

## Scope

Speculative-decoding acceptance metrics are intentionally not included in this PR. `GenerateOutput` already carries terminal `spec_decode_metrics`, but mapping those values into the OpenAI `PerRequestMetrics.speculative_decoding` response field is separate follow-up work.

## Duplicate-work check

- #44280 tracks this Rust frontend gap.
- #36383 is a Python frontend draft. #42198 concerns response headers. #56914 concerns reasoning/content token metrics in Python. None adds this Rust frontend response-body implementation.
- Rechecked open PRs and #44280 comments before branch upload; no Rust timing-metrics duplicate was found.

## Tests

- `cargo fmt --all` — passed.
- `cargo test -p vllm-llm -p vllm-text -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd --quiet -- --test-threads=1` — passed (1,019 tests passed, 1 ignored). An earlier parallel rerun intermittently missed an unrelated `preprocess_audio_secs` snapshot key in `vllm-chat`; that test passed in isolation and in the serial suite.
- `cargo check --workspace --tests` — passed after the review updates.
- After rebasing onto current `main`: `cargo test -p vllm-text` passed (105 passed, 1 network test ignored), `cargo test -p vllm-llm --test generate` passed (12 passed), and `cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib` passed (355 passed).
- Focused `vllm-server` metric, completion, and streaming tests — passed.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Faster Engram host lookups: sorted rows, inline big lookups
body:
## Purpose

Speed up DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram lookups from CPU-offloaded tables. On GB200 they are bound by GPU address translation, not bandwidth: each row misses the TLB on the small pages that back the table.

- **Sorted host lookups.** Large lookups from small-page host tables (pinned or `/dev/shm`) sort their rows by table offset, so neighboring rows share page walks. THP tables skip it, and so do lookups below the sort threshold.
- **Inline big lookups.** From the inline threshold (tokens, max over DP ranks), the lookup runs on the main stream at full width instead of the prefetch stream. Persistent main-stream kernels (MegaMoE, mHC, block-scaled GEMMs) cannot co-reside with lookup CTAs, so a background lookup stalls them anyway, and EP collectives then wait on the slowest rank.

`_engram_lookup_thresholds` picks both thresholds per GPU family: 36864 rows and 4096 tokens on Blackwell (measured on GB200). Other GPUs, including ROCm, keep both paths off and behave as before.

All Engram logic now lives in `common/engram.py`, so NVIDIA and AMD share one implementation and `nvidia/engram.py` is removed.

Also fixed along the way:

- DP replicas share the tables only if `/dev/shm` has enough free space (it used to check the total size). The Engram DP leader decides and broadcasts, so replicas always agree, and peers do not hang if the space query raises.
- The lookup kernel no longer ties the output row index to the id dtype, so int64 ids compile.

## Kernel microbenchmark

Kernel only, single GB200 bound to its NUMA node, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash table sizes (24 heads x 16M rows, 94.4 GiB), uniform random ids, CUPTI median of 3 runs rotating 16 id sets. Grid as in production: 76 CTAs below 4096 tokens, 152 from there. HEAD, new unsorted and new sorted outputs are bitwise identical, and from 64 tokens up the new kernel is never more than 1.5% slower than HEAD below the sort threshold.

DEP2/DEP4 (24 heads per rank, `/dev/shm` table shared across DP replicas):

| tokens/rank | before (us) | after (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 90.1 | 88.1 | 1.02x |
| 512 | 620.5 | 620.6 | 1.00x |
| 1024 | 1236.0 | 1237.0 | 1.00x |
| 2048 | 2463.7 | 2163.7 | 1.14x |
| 4096 | 4621.3 | 3773.7 | 1.22x |
| 8192 | 9243.6 | 5925.9 | 1.56x |
| 16384 | 18476.0 | 8174.7 | 2.26x |
| 32768 | 36963.3 | 9905.1 | 3.73x |

TP2/TP4 (per-rank pinned tables):

| tokens | TP2 before (us) | TP2 after (us) | TP4 before (us) | TP4 after (us) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 1791 | 834 | 440 | 447 |
| 8192 | 3578 | 1846 | 877 | 160 |
| 16384 | 7162 | 3457 | 1745 | 232 |
| 32768 | 14319 | 4291 | 3481 | 396 |

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -q
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files <changed files> --hook-stage manual
```

New coverage: the sorted lookup reconstructs the checkpoint under TP padding; a `/dev/shm` that is too small or cannot be queried falls back to sharding, and the leader still broadcasts that decision.

## Test Result

117 passed on 4x GB200. Ruff, format and mypy pass.

## E2E prefill (DEP4)

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (DP4 x TP1 + EP) on one GB200 node: DeepGEMM mega MoE, FlashMLA mega attention, fp8 KV cache, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, prefix caching off. `vllm bench serve` on random prompts with one output token, so every request is a single prefill. Base (5e887a078b) and this PR ran in the same job on the same node; each point is the median of 3 repeats with unique seeds after a warmup pass. No timed run saw a runtime compile.

| prompt | concurrency | base TTFT p50 (ms) | PR TTFT p50 (ms) | speedup | base tok/s | PR tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4k | 1 | 126 | 128 | 0.99x | 31,961 | 32,060 |
| 8k | 1 | 166 | 160 | 1.04x | 49,498 | 51,176 |
| 16k | 1 | 321 | 295 | 1.09x | 51,265 | 55,732 |
| 32k | 1 | 597 | 548 | 1.09x | 54,845 | 59,752 |
| 4k | 64 | 1059 | 863 | 1.23x | 222,676 | 270,319 |
| 8k | 64 | 2107 | 1721 | 1.22x | 236,670 | 282,490 |
| 16k | 64 | 4239 | 3472 | 1.22x | 236,677 | 283,612 |
| 32k | 64 | 8620 | 7056 | 1.22x | 233,837 | 284,409 |

At concurrency 64 every step prefills the 16384-token budget on all four ranks, so those rows share one step shape and differ in context length; their repeat spread is under 4%. At concurrency 1 the spread is up to 11%. Concurrency 4 and 16 are left out: their TTFT depends on arrival order and repeats spread up to 40%.

Where the time goes at concurrency 64 (estimated from the throughput and the microbenchmark, not profiled): a step takes about 280 ms on base and 230 ms with this PR. Sorting saves about 20 ms of it: each step looks up 16384 tokens x 24 heads in each of the two Engram layers, which drops from 18.5 ms to 8.2 ms per layer. The other ~30 ms comes from running those lookups inline, so they no longer stall the persistent MoE, mHC and GEMM kernels on every rank. At concurrency 1 only one rank is busy and the gain (about 24 ms per 16384-token step) is close to the sorting saving alone.

## Accuracy (DEP4, this PR)

GSM8K: 1319 problems, 5-shot completions, temperature 0, 4096-token cap, concurrency 32. Strict match 92.49% (flexible 92.49%), no request errors.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for Engram storage and lookup work. #58766 (FP8 rows into `wkv`) edits the same lookup kernel, #58310 (reject tables larger than host memory) adds a host memory check, and #57195 shares host tables across SP ranks. None sorts lookups or runs big lookups inline, but they touch the same files.

## AI assistance

Written with AI assistance (Claude Code). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Drop a timed-out store job's blocks from the round's parked supply
body:
## Purpose

In the symmetric P2P KV offload tier, a decode instance asks a peer whether it holds a prompt's KV, and the peer pins the matching blocks in its own cache until the fetch arrives. If the fetch is late, the pin times out and the peer's engine frees those cache slots for reuse, but the round still advertises the blocks as available. A fetch that arrives after the timeout then RDMA-reads slots that may already hold another request's KV, and reports success. The decode instance would continue generating from someone else's cache. This PR withdraws the advertised blocks when their pin times out, so the late fetch fails fast and the request prefills locally.

Concretely, in `vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/session/server.py`:

- Answering a lookup, the server pins the blocks through a store job and parks them in the fetch round: `add_stored_blocks` (`:94`) records them in `available` and the job in `pending_job_ids`.
- `_timeout_pending_store_jobs` (`:1121`) fails a job older than `_STORE_TIMEOUT_S` (`:40`, 30 s) with `StoreResult(success=False)`. The tiering manager maps that to a failed `JobResult` (`p2p/manager.py:859`), and the engine unpins the slots.
- The round's `available` entries and `pending_job_ids` are left as they were. A late `FetchMsg` matches them in `on_fetch` and submits the transfer.

**Fix:** when store jobs time out, remove their entries from every round's `available` map and `pending_job_ids`. The late fetch then has unmatched demand and takes the existing fail-fast path for symmetric rounds (`server.py:372`): `TransferDoneMsg(success=False)`, and the consumer prefills locally. The PD case where the prefiller finishes first has the same problem when its store stays parked longer than `_STORE_TIMEOUT_S` before the fetch arrives, and this fix covers it too: `finish()` has already set `finishing`, so `on_fetch` fails the round (thanks @liranschour for pointing this out and for reproducing the bug).

**Not a duplicate:** #53453 added a one-round-trip rejection of a late fetch for stores the *manager* reaps while still unbound (`_reaped_stores`). This PR covers the other case: a store job already bound to a session that `_timeout_pending_store_jobs` fails. #58168 (draft) edits `server.py` elsewhere and does not reference these identifiers. No open PR touches `_timeout_pending_store_jobs`.

## Test Plan

```
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py -q -k symmetric_supply_timed_out
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ -q
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
```

New test, `TestServerFlows::test_fetch_after_symmetric_supply_timed_out_reads_nothing`: a lookup pins block `hA` (slot 7); the store job is aged past `_STORE_TIMEOUT_S` and reported failed; then a `FetchMsg` for `hA` arrives. It checks that no transfer is submitted and the round ends with `TransferDoneMsg(success=False)`.

## Test Result

With the fix (CPU, macOS arm64, on main `4e0a414c4`):

```
-k symmetric_supply_timed_out ... 1 passed
tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ ... 434 passed, 1 skipped
```

On `main` (fix reverted, test kept):

```
E   AssertionError: assert {0: ('peer:8000', [7], [20])} == {}
    (the late fetch RDMA-reads the unpinned slot 7)
1 failed
```

pre-commit (`--from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD`) and `mypy-3.12` (manual stage): clean.

This only changes a failure path (a fetch after its pin timed out now fails instead of reading a possibly reused slot); no evals are needed.

**Related:** one of a few independent fixes from an audit of the KV transfer paths (CPU offload, NIXL, P2P): #59096, #59099, #59102, #59325. None depends on another; they can be reviewed and merged in any order.

## AI assistance

I used an AI coding assistant (Claude) to audit this code path, write the fix and write the test. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above myself. The commit carries a `Co-authored-by` trailer, as `AGENTS.md` asks.

title: [Core] Include the LoRA path in prefix-cache block hashes
body:
## Purpose

Prefix-cache block hashes identify a LoRA adapter only by its name. If a name is
re-pointed at a different adapter (unload then load under the same name, or
`load_inplace` with a new path), requests for that name can reuse KV computed with the
previous adapter until those blocks are evicted. See #42125 and #30931.

This adds the adapter path to the LoRA extra key: `("lora", name, path)`.

- Re-pointing a name at an adapter stored elsewhere no longer reuses the old blocks.
- Hashes stay deterministic across instances: no file I/O, no per-process counter.
- Connectors and offload tiers keyed by block hash pick the change up automatically.
- KV events are unchanged: they publish only the LoRA name for this key.

An in-place reload from the same path with changed files still cannot be detected
without hashing the adapter's contents, so that case now logs a warning suggesting a new
path. Content-based versioning (as proposed in #48352) could be added on top of this key
later.

## Why this is not a duplicate

#48352 versions the LoRA key with a digest of the adapter's files. That handles
same-path content changes for local absolute paths, but it adds about 190 lines of file
hashing that runs on the API server's request path. This PR is the minimal,
deterministic fix for re-pointed names and is compatible with #48352 as a follow-up.

## Compatibility

Prefix-cache and external-store hashes change for LoRA blocks, so KV stored by an
earlier version for LoRA requests misses once after upgrade. Instances that serve the
same adapter from different absolute paths no longer share LoRA blocks with each other.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache tests/v1/simple_kv_offload \
  tests/distributed/test_kv_cache_events.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/entrypoints/serve/lora \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/sagemaker/test_sagemaker_lora_adapters.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_lora_resolvers.py
```

## Test Result

- New `test_lora_path_change_changes_block_hashes` fails without the change (2 failed)
  and passes with it.
- On 4x GB200, the command above gives 1013 passed, 8 skipped.
- The KV event tests are unchanged and pass, so the event format is unchanged.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, run the tests and draft this
description.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][Mooncake] Suppress completion for empty pulls
body:
## Purpose

Mooncake can issue a pull with no local destination blocks only to notify the Prefill side that its producer blocks may be released. The Decode request does not wait for remote KV in this case.

`MooncakeConnectorWorker.process_pulling_result` currently reports every successful pull as `finished_recving` after its worker tasks drain. For an empty pull, this sends a completion for a request that is not in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` and can trip the scheduler's request ownership/status assertion.

Empty pulls are reachable both during early-abort cleanup and when a remote prefix hit is reduced to no transferable local blocks.

## Change

Report a successful receive completion only when the pull contains at least one local destination block:

```python
if pull_meta.pull_tasks_count == 0 and any(pull_meta.local_block_ids):
    self.finished_recving_reqs.add(pull_meta.d_req_id)
```

The producer notification and pull-task accounting are unchanged. This also matches the existing failed-receive path, which already skips scheduler notification when the pull has no local blocks.

## Relationship to other work

#50565 addresses the early-abort cleanup variant by adding an explicit `notify_scheduler` flag. Its current version intentionally still reports completion for an ordinary empty-block full-prefix pull. That does not cover the case where Decode does not enter `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` after the connector returns no transferable blocks.

This PR applies the check at the worker completion sink, covering both cleanup-only and full-prefix empty pulls while preserving completion for every pull with real local destinations.

## Test Plan


The regression test covers:

- `local_block_ids=[]`: no scheduler completion;
- `local_block_ids=[[]]`: no scheduler completion;
- a non-empty pull: normal scheduler completion.

- Runtime: Mooncake RDMA, 64-token blocks, prefix caching, and SWA bounded replay.

title: [Feature][Spec Decode] Support sampling mask replay for MRV2 MTP
body:
## Purpose

Add sampling-mask replay for fixed-boundary speculative decoding in Model Runner V2, on top of the compact sampling-mask representation.

The implementation preserves the ordinary single-token fast path and exact packed-mask fallback, and returns one processed-target support set for each emitted accepted, recovered, or bonus token. Output D2H is scheduled before postprocessing and the next proposal.

## Supported configuration and boundaries

The merged implementation does **not** restrict replay to `method="mtp"` or standard rejection sampling. Configuration tests accept MTP, EAGLE/EAGLE3, dFlash, dSpark and draft_model, and accept standard, block and synthetic rejection configurations. Configuration acceptance is not a claim that every combination has GPU E2E coverage.

Replay requires Model Runner V2, fixed verification boundaries (adaptive verification disabled), `logprobs_mode="processed_logprobs"`, no diffusion model and no custom logits processors. NGRAM GPU replay validation is not established by the test results below.

The original description incorrectly said non-MTP methods and block/synthetic rejection were rejected. This description is corrected to match the merged code.

## Duplicate check

At implementation time, open PRs were searched using sampling-mask, replay, MTP and speculative-decoding keywords; no overlapping fixed-boundary replay implementation was found.

## Validation recorded during development

- Ruff check/format, mypy, test tethering, configuration validation and `git diff --check` passed on the refreshed branch.
- On the Windows development host, hooks requiring `/bin/bash` could not run; focused pytest did not start because its virtualenv lacked test dependencies.
- Earlier GPU validation: 30 focused tests passed per arm.
- TP1 MTP replay-off/on: 512 tokens and selected processed logprobs matched exactly, with zero membership, alignment or mass failures.
- TP2 MTP replay-on: 512 output rows with zero membership, row-alignment or support-alignment failures; captured-input oracle exact in 5/5 repetitions.
- dFlash/dSpark **replay-off** regressions showed no token or selected-logprob differences; these are not replay-on coverage.
- GPU environment: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu129, CUDA 12.9, Triton 3.7.1.

These earlier GPU results were not rerun against the refreshed base by the description correction. The PR is merged; no new test success is claimed here.

title: [BugFix][Multimodal] Pick worst-case DeepSeek-V4 VL dummy image size (#59271)
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59271.

`DeepseekV4VLProcessingInfo.get_image_size_with_most_features` assumed a square maximizes ViT patches within the token budget. Because each aligner row costs an extra `IMAGE_NEW_LINE`, a wide grid (`1932x336`) produces more placeholder tokens and patches than the previous `756x756` dummy, so memory profiling under-estimated peak multimodal usage.

Search budget-feasible LLM grids (respecting `vision_max_wh_ratio`) and pick the one with the most ViT patches, breaking ties by sentinel-block length. For the default config this returns `1932x336`.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_deepseek_v4_vl.py -q
```

Also re-ran the issue reproducer against the local CPU editable install.

## Test Result

```
2 passed
```

Issue reproducer after fix:

```
dummy ImageSize(width=1932, height=336) (378, 3312)
1932x336 (378, 3312)
```

## Duplicate-work check

- `gh issue view 59271 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments` — no claims
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "59271 in:body"` — none
- Keyword searches (`DeepseekV4VLProcessingInfo`, `DeepSeek-V4 VL dummy`, `vision_max_wh_ratio`, `mm_preprocess most features`) — no open PR for this fix
- Note: `deepseek_v41` already searches non-square grids; only `deepseek_v4` had the square assumption

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to reproduce the bug, apply the grid search described in the issue, and add regression tests. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.
