title: [Bugfix][Watermarking] Keep draft prompt lengths valid under CUDA graphs
body:
## Overview

Fix stale prompt lengths in the draft watermark deduplication mask under CUDA graphs. The bug came in with #56807. I found it while reviewing #59554, which would expose DFlash to it too.

## Claims

- With `dual_key_gumbel` and the default `deduplicate_contexts="single_turn"`, draft sampling under FULL CUDA graphs (default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`) read prompt lengths from a stale UVA buffer after new requests arrived. This affects EAGLE3, MTP and DSpark (reproduced; EAGLE shares the autoregressive path). Some drafts were sampled without key A where they should carry it, and some repeated contexts were not deduplicated. Graph and eager mode now agree.
- No host sync, and no end-to-end change I can separate from run-to-run noise (see Performance). The fix adds one async copy of `max_num_reqs` int32 values per propose. The captured dedup kernel then reads device memory instead of pinned host memory, which is faster in a microbenchmark.

## Validation

Engine harness: Qwen3-4B targets (Qwen3.5-0.8B for MTP) with dedup `single_turn`. It compares the dedup mask each draft row actually used against a CPU reference built from the true prompt lengths. Compared with the engine-level script under Reproduction, it also covers Poisson arrivals, MTP and DSpark. λ is arrivals per engine step.

| Workload | Before (FULL graph) | After (FULL graph) | Eager |
|---|---|---|---|
| EAGLE3 K=3, crafted (one request at a time, prompt-copying) | 576/1905 mask rows wrong; 536 accepted drafts lacked key A | 0/1896 | 0/1896 |
| EAGLE3 K=3, online Poisson (λ=0.2, mean concurrency 12) | 43/23178 mask rows wrong (41 falsely skipped, 2 missed dedup) | 0/23178 | 0/23325 |
| MTP K=3, crafted / online λ=0.02 | 32.6% / 2.06% of accepted drafts falsely skipped; online also 74 rows with missed dedup | n/a / 0 | 0 / n/a |
| DSpark K=7, crafted / online λ=0.02 | 39.5% / 2.05% of accepted drafts falsely skipped; online also 74 rows with missed dedup | n/a / 0 | 0 / n/a |

The MTP and DSpark "after" numbers come from the harness's patched `prepare()`, not from a commit tree. The EAGLE3 online "after" rows used the first revision of this fix, which differed only in copying into a `[:num_reqs]` slice. The EAGLE3 crafted "after" and eager runs use this commit.

Host sync: `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, EAGLE3 under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, 12 staggered admissions and 98 `prepare()` calls: clean. A deliberate `.item()` in `prepare()` trips the check, so the check does cover this path.

Unit test:

```bash
pytest tests/watermarking/test_watermarking.py -k reads_current_prompt_lens   # fails on main, passes with the fix
pytest tests/watermarking/                                                    # 148 passed (B300)
```

The test is CUDA-only. CI runs `tests/watermarking` only in the CPU "V1 Others" step, where it is skipped. I ran it locally on a B300: it fails on main and passes with the fix, and the suite passes (148).

About 1-2% of accepted drafts are affected at low traffic (EAGLE3 0.98%, MTP 2.06%, DSpark 2.05%) and 0.54% when busy (EAGLE3). Per-category detection rates in paired runs are identical for EAGLE3 and within noise for MTP and DSpark: at most 2 of 19-20 requests differ. The bug still breaks the watermark's own contract, and graph and eager runs diverge.

### Performance

Setup: B300, Qwen3-4B with EAGLE3 (`AngelSlim/Qwen3-4B_eagle3`, K=3, probabilistic), `dual_key_gumbel`, temperature 1.0, random 1024 in / 256 out with `--ignore-eos` (64 prompts at c=1 and c=8, 256 at c=64), default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. Main and fix servers ran in parallel on two GPUs, swapped each round, for 10 rounds of 2 passes. Δ is the mean of the per-round paired change, ± the 95% CI. A/A is the same comparison of main against main (4 rounds).

| Concurrency | Output tok/s (main → fix) | Δ tok/s | Δ mean TPOT | Δ mean TTFT | Acceptance length | A/A Δ tok/s | A/A Δ TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 464.7 → 462.3 | −0.5% ± 0.6 | +0.5% ± 0.6 | +1.8% ± 2.0 | 1.632 → 1.632 | −0.4% ± 0.6 | +0.6% ± 3.4 |
| 8 | 3032 → 3012 | −0.6% ± 0.8 | +0.4% ± 0.9 | +2.3% ± 1.7 | 1.658 → 1.662 | −0.3% ± 3.3 | −1.2% ± 5.6 |
| 64 | 10543 → 10495 | −0.4% ± 0.8 | +0.3% ± 0.9 | +0.8% ± 1.5 | 1.533 → 1.533 | +0.3% ± 1.2 | −0.7% ± 4.1 |

Throughput and TPOT change by less than 1%, with CIs that include zero. The A/A differences are of similar size.

Mean TTFT is 0.35-0.65 ms (0.8-2.3%) higher. Only the c=8 CI excludes zero (+0.7% to +4.0%). Between two identical main servers, per-round TTFT differences range from −6% to +3%, and one A/A CI (c=64 acceptance length) also excludes zero. I read the TTFT difference as noise, but these runs cannot rule out a TTFT cost of a few percent at c=8.

`prepare()` alone, with a UVA-backed prompt-length source and the speculator's two gathers: host time goes from 48.4-48.9 µs to 51.4-52.1 µs (+3 µs for one more copy launch). The copy itself takes 4.2 µs on the GPU at `max_num_reqs=1024` and 0.9 µs at 256. The dedup kernel runs once per draft step, so three times per propose at K=3. Replayed in a CUDA graph, those three steps get faster because the kernel reads device memory instead of pinned host memory: 12.3 → 8.7 µs with 1 request and 30.2 → 17.0 µs with 1024 requests (`max_num_reqs=1024`).

### Reproduction

A standalone script shows the bug without a model. It captures the draft dedup mask in a CUDA graph, admits a request (which moves `prompt_len.gpu` to the next pool buffer), and compares the replayed graph with eager mode. Run it on a CUDA GPU with `python repro_stale_prompt_len.py`.

<details>
<summary>repro_stale_prompt_len.py</summary>

```python
# Draft watermark dedup mask under a CUDA graph reads a stale prompt length.
import torch

import vllm
from vllm.v1.watermarking.gumbel import GumbelWatermarker
from vllm.v1.watermarking.spec_decode import DraftWatermarker
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.buffer_utils import UvaBackedTensor

print("vllm from", vllm.__file__)
dev = torch.device("cuda")
wm = DraftWatermarker(GumbelWatermarker(key=42, context_width=2), max_num_reqs=1,
                      device=dev, num_speculative_steps=1,
                      deduplicate_contexts="single_turn",
                      deduplicate_contexts_max_history=None)
prompt_len = UvaBackedTensor(1, dtype=torch.int32)  # like req_states.prompt_len
# Request in slot 0: prompt [5, 6, 9], generated [5, 6], next draft context
# [5, 6]. The context repeats only inside the prompt, so with single_turn the
# draft must use key A. Read with prompt length 0, it looks like repeated
# generated text and the draft skips key A.
tokens = torch.tensor([[5, 6, 9, 5, 6]], device=dev)
total_len = torch.tensor([5], device=dev)
ctx = torch.tensor([[5, 6]], device=dev)
enabled = torch.tensor([True], device=dev)
logits = torch.zeros(1, 8, device=dev)
idx = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
temp, draft_step = torch.ones(1, device=dev), torch.tensor(0, device=dev)

def prepare():  # the speculator calls this on every propose()
    wm.prepare(ctx, enabled, tokens, prompt_len.gpu, total_len)

def uses_key_a():  # per-row mask that draft sampling uses for key A
    return wm._sampling_state(logits, idx, temp, draft_step, ctx)[1]

prepare()  # capture time: slot 0 has prompt length 0
uses_key_a()  # warm up outside capture
graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
    graph_out = uses_key_a()
# A step that admits a request runs copy_to_uva(), which moves
# prompt_len.gpu to the next buffer of its round-robin pool.
prompt_len.np[0] = 3
prompt_len.copy_to_uva()
prepare()
eager = uses_key_a().item()
graph.replay()
replayed = graph_out.item()
print(f"eager: key A={eager}  graph: key A={replayed}  ->",
      "OK" if eager == replayed else "STALE prompt length in graph")
```

</details>

Main:

```
eager: key A=True  graph: key A=False  -> STALE prompt length in graph
```

With the fix:

```
eager: key A=True  graph: key A=True  -> OK
```

An engine-level script runs EAGLE3 with `dual_key_gumbel` through `LLM`, admits 24 requests one at a time, and counts draft rows whose dedup mask differs from the mask built from the current prompt lengths. Run `python engine_repro.py` for the default CUDA graph mode and `python engine_repro.py eager` for eager mode (30-45 s each on a B300).

<details>
<summary>engine_repro.py</summary>

```python
# EAGLE3 + dual_key_gumbel: compare the dedup mask each draft row used with the
# mask recomputed, in the same CUDA graph, from the current prompt lengths.
import os
import sys

import torch

os.environ.update(VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER="1", VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING="0")
import vllm  # noqa: E402
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams  # noqa: E402
from vllm.v1.watermarking.spec_decode import DraftWatermarker as DW  # noqa: E402
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.watermark import draft_watermarking_mask  # noqa: E402

print("vllm from", vllm.__file__)
orig_init, orig_prepare, orig_state = DW.__init__, DW.prepare, DW._sampling_state
instances = []

def __init__(self, wm, max_num_reqs, device, *args):
    orig_init(self, wm, max_num_reqs, device, *args)
    self.true_pl = torch.zeros(max_num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    self.stats = torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)  # rows, wrong, skip
    instances.append(self)

def prepare(self, ctx, enabled, tokens, prompt_lens, total_lens):
    orig_prepare(self, ctx, enabled, tokens, prompt_lens, total_lens)
    self.true_pl.copy_(prompt_lens)  # current prompt lengths

def _sampling_state(self, logits, idx, temps, step, ctx):
    steps, mask = orig_state(self, logits, idx, temps, step, ctx)
    ref = draft_watermarking_mask(
        self.all_token_ids, idx, self.true_pl, self.total_lens, self.prior_contexts,
        ctx, steps, self.enabled[: len(ctx)] & (temps != 0),
        self.deduplicate_contexts_max_history, False)
    self.stats += torch.stack(
        [torch.ones_like(ref).sum(), (mask != ref).sum(), (ref & ~mask).sum()])
    return steps, mask

DW.__init__, DW.prepare, DW._sampling_state = __init__, prepare, _sampling_state
wm = {"algorithm": "dual_key_gumbel", "key": 42, "context_width": 4}
spec = {"method": "eagle3", "model": "AngelSlim/Qwen3-4B_eagle3",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic"}
llm = LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-4B", speculative_config=spec, watermark_config=wm, seed=0,
          max_model_len=4096, gpu_memory_utilization=0.5,
          enforce_eager=sys.argv[1:] == ["eager"])
(dw,) = instances
dw.stats.zero_()  # drop warmup and capture rows
text = ("The committee met on Tuesday to review the annual budget. The members agreed "
        "to fund the public libraries, repair the old bridge near the river, and hire "
        "two more nurses for the clinic. The mayor promised a full report next month.")
for i in range(24):  # one request at a time; each admission rotates the UVA pool
    ask = f"Repeat exactly, word for word:\n{text}" if i % 3 == 1 else "Say hi."
    llm.chat([{"role": "user", "content": f"[{i}] {ask}"}],
             SamplingParams(temperature=1.0, seed=i, max_tokens=96), use_tqdm=False,
             chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False})
rows, wrong, skipped = dw.stats.tolist()
print(f"draft rows={rows}  mask rows wrong={wrong}  wrongly skipped key A={skipped}")
```

</details>

| Run | Output |
|---|---|
| Main, CUDA graphs (2 runs, identical) | `draft rows=714  mask rows wrong=129  wrongly skipped key A=129` |
| Fix, CUDA graphs | `draft rows=720  mask rows wrong=0  wrongly skipped key A=0` |
| Main, eager | `draft rows=720  mask rows wrong=0  wrongly skipped key A=0` |
| Fix, eager | `draft rows=720  mask rows wrong=0  wrongly skipped key A=0` |


## Details

**Root cause:** `req_states.prompt_len` is a `UvaBackedTensor`. `copy_to_uva()` runs from `apply_staged_writes` on steps that add requests, and it moves `.gpu` round-robin across the buffer pool. `DraftWatermarker.prepare()` stored that reference, so a captured `draft_watermarking_mask` kept reading the capture-time buffer. Newly admitted requests then see the previous occupant's prompt length until the pool comes back around:
- If the stale length is shorter than the real one, prompt n-grams count as generated history and the draft skips key A.
- If it is longer, real repeats are missed.

**Fix:** `DraftWatermarker` owns an int32 `[max_num_reqs]` buffer, and `prepare()` copies into it. This follows the existing `contexts` and `enabled` copies in the same method. It is also the principle MRV2 states for fused draft decoding: replayed tensor state must live in persistent storage.

I found no other inputs to captured draft sampling that go stale:
- `all_token_ids` and `total_len` are `StagedWriteTensor`s whose `.gpu` never moves.
- `contexts` and `enabled` are already copied into owned buffers.
- Other UVA-backed inputs to the draft path (temperature, seeds) are already copied into speculator-owned buffers. The remaining readers run eagerly.

**Unchanged behavior:** eager mode and the watermark-off path are unaffected. By code inspection, dedup modes `none` and `all` do not depend on prompt lengths: `none` returns before the mask is built, and `all` searches from position 0. The copy still runs in those modes; its cost is negligible.

**Alternatives:**
- Making `RequestState.prompt_len` a stable `StagedWriteTensor` would fix this for every future graph reader. It touches the penalties, bad_words, trace_replay and model_runner readers, and the `LogitsProcessor` interface types `prompt_len` as `UvaBackedTensor`, so it is better done as a separate refactor.
- A persistent device mirror inside `UvaBackedTensor` would cost a copy for every user.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Keep store pins and AbortAck until NIXL transfers stop
body:
## Overview

The P2P producer released store pins, and sent `AbortAck` to the consumer, while its NIXL WRITEs could still be running. Neither cancelling the handle nor removing the remote peer stops a running WRITE with the UCX backend. This PR keeps the pins, and holds back `AbortAck`, until NIXL reports each transfer terminal. Addresses #59569 and the review on this PR. The consumer-side counterpart is tracked in #61532.

## Claims

- `NixlTransport.cancel(mode="wait")` releases only transfers that are no longer `PROC`/`PEND`. Previously it reported running WRITEs as cancelled, because `release_xfer_handle` never fails for an in-progress UCX request.
- A round whose store timed out, or which the consumer aborted, fails its jobs but keeps the pins of jobs that inflight transfers still read, until those transfers are terminal. Late completions settle each job exactly once, and new supply cannot restart such a round.
- The abort drain no longer falls back to `cancel(mode="immediate")` + `AbortAck` after `_CANCEL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S`. Past the timeout it logs once and keeps retrying. `AbortAck` is sent only when no transfer of the round can still write to the consumer.
- Wait-mode cancel retries are paced to one attempt per round per 100 ms, shared by the store-timeout sweep and the abort drain.
- When one transfer of a round fails, the round's other transfers are no longer cancelled with `mode="immediate"`. The round is marked cancelled instead: their pins and the round's `TransferDoneMsg(success=False)` wait until they are terminal.
- `nixlRemoteDisconnectError` from `check_xfer_state`, which NIXL raises when the peer process is gone, is treated as a terminal failure, so a dead peer no longer pins its transfers until the session closes.

## Validation

Real NIXL 1.4.1, UCX over TCP, CPU DRAM. This is not RDMA hardware.

| scenario | result |
|---|---|
| 512 MiB WRITE, old `cancel(mode="wait")` | returned `[]` while `PROC` in 5/5 runs; all bytes landed afterwards |
| 512 MiB WRITE, new `cancel(mode="wait")` | returned the tid as still inflight in 5/5 runs; `poll()` reported DONE only after all 512 MiB landed |
| 512 MiB WRITE, `remove_remote_peer` | returned with 14–392 MB landed in 5/5 runs; the rest still landed, and the handle then raises `nixlNotFoundError` |
| 1 GiB WRITE stalled by SIGSTOPping the target, then `cancel(mode="immediate")` + `remove_remote_peer`, then resume | 64/64 blocks still landed |
| stalled WRITE, target left stopped | stays `PROC` for 60 s, no timeout of its own |
| stalled WRITE, target SIGKILLed | `check_xfer_state` raises `nixlRemoteDisconnectError` |

Unit tests use the fake transport in `test_sessions.py` and a mocked NIXL agent in `test_data_transport.py`. The new behavior tests fail on the respective previous logic and pass now.

```sh
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ -q
# head 387b0ba092 (agent-run):  486 passed, 1 skipped
# head 84ec0d792f (I ran it myself, and the agent independently): 484 passed, 1 skipped, 14 warnings in 78.57s
```

ruff 0.14.0 and mypy 1.20.2 (`tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.12`) are clean.

Not done: RDMA/InfiniBand hardware, GPU memory, serving load or model evaluation.

## Details

**Root cause.** `NixlTransport.cancel(mode="wait")` relied on `release_xfer_handle` raising for a transfer that is still running. With UCX it never raises: `nixlUcxBackendReqH::release` calls `ucp_request_cancel`, which does nothing for an RMA PUT, then frees the request and returns success. The producer therefore treated running WRITEs as cancelled, released their store pins, and acked aborts while bytes were still landing. `remove_remote_peer` → `invalidateRemoteMD` only drops the connection entry, and the endpoint is later closed in flush mode, so outstanding writes complete rather than stop. That rules out the suggested "tear down the peer, then ack" fallback.

**Abort flow after this change.**
1. The consumer sends `AbortFetchMsg`.
2. The producer marks the round cancelled, fails the jobs no transfer reads, and keeps the rest pinned. A failed transfer takes its round down the same path.
3. It retries `cancel(mode="wait")` at the paced rate. A transfer leaves only when NIXL reports it terminal, or the peer is gone.
4. When no transfer of the round remains, the producer releases the remaining pins and sends `AbortAckMsg`. An aborted round sends no `TransferDoneMsg`.

**Tradeoff.** There is no hard deadline on the producer side. If a peer stays alive but the WRITE never progresses, the pins stay held, with one warning after `_CANCEL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S`. A bound would need a transport primitive that guarantees a running WRITE has stopped. An awaited forced endpoint close (`UCP_EP_CLOSE_FLAG_FORCE`) might be one, but NIXL does not expose it. The consumer still gives up after `_ABORT_ACK_TIMEOUT_S` and frees its slots; that is the open issue #61532.

The `store_timed_out` flag on a round is renamed `cancelled`, because it now covers aborts and failed transfers as well. All three paths share it: jobs no transfer reads fail at once, and the others keep their pins until their transfers are terminal.

The remote-disconnect check matches the binding's class name or the `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT` status code, so the NIXL bindings are not imported in this module. An error it does not recognize keeps the transfer inflight, which is the conservative side.

The shutdown drain in `manager.py` still falls back to `mode="immediate"` after `_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S`, because the engine is exiting. Only its docstring is updated.

This is distinct from #59329, which withdraws timed-out parked supply before Fetch. Its withdrawal set must be derived from the results actually emitted (`{r.job_id for r in results}`), so that unconfirmed inflight jobs are not removed from the round's pending jobs. Whichever PR merges second needs that adjustment.

AI assistance was used for the investigation, implementation, tests and this description.

---

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] Design Fit: reuses the transport cancellation contract and the existing store-timeout path; no new abstractions.
- [x] Testing and Validation: unit tests for each behavior, real-NIXL probes over TCP; RDMA/GPU/serving not covered, as documented.
- [x] Code Quality and Style: ruff 0.14.0 and mypy clean.
- [x] Pull Request Contents: root cause, abort flow, tradeoffs and scope documented.

title: [Quantization] Support compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE with FP8 activations via Mxfp4MoEMethod
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Load compressed-tensors checkpoints with MXFP4 weights and dynamic FP8 activations (e.g. `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MXFP4-DSFP8`, `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-MXFP4xFP8_BLOCK`, `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-MXFP4xFP8_BLOCK`, DeepSeek-V4-Flash converted to CT) and run them with the FP8 activations the checkpoint declares. Alternative to #59376 (cc @kylesayrs).

**Depends on #61556.** Humming 0.1.16, which `main` pins today, rejects FP8 (GS128) activations with MXFP4 weights, so these checkpoints fail to load with `--moe-backend humming` until #61556 lands.

## Claims

- MoE experts: `CompressedTensorsW4A8Mxfp4MoEMethod(Mxfp4MoEMethod)` only handles the `*_weight_packed` checkpoint naming and the declared activation scheme. Backend selection, weight conversion, size round-up, monolithic kernels and EPLB are inherited from the native MXFP4 method.
- The checkpoint's FP8 activation key reaches the Humming MoE backend. Before, it was dropped and Humming ran BF16 activations (W4A16) unless `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` was set.
- Dense linears with MXFP4 weights and FP8 inputs (GLM-5.3's dense MLPs target `Linear`) use a new `CompressedTensorsW4A8Mxfp4` scheme that requests FP8 activations, instead of the W4A4 scheme requesting MXFP4 activations.
- `get_moe_method` looks up the expert scheme with the layer's `ckpt_*_proj_name`, and DeepSeek-V4 (NVIDIA) passes `ckpt_names=("w1", "w2", "w3")`, so name-based targets such as `re:.*experts\.\d+\.w\d+$` match.

## Validation

H200 (SM90), `--moe-backend humming`, checked by inspecting the loaded layers.

| Model | Config | Dense MXFP4 linear | MoE experts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MXFP4-DSFP8 (real weights) | TP1 | n/a (FP8 block) | Humming, FP8 GS128 (W4A16 before this PR's 2nd commit) |
| GLM-5.3-MXFP4xFP8_BLOCK (dummy weights, 5 layers) | TP1, TP2, TP2+EP | Humming, FP8 GS128 (FP8 per-token before) | Humming, FP8 GS128 (BF16 before) |

These runs used the v0.32.0 release branch with #61556, and `main` with #61556 applied. With `main` alone, the Humming 0.1.16 schema check rejects the combination. EP selects `HummingGroupedExperts` and TP selects `HummingIndexedExperts`. Greedy outputs match between TP2 and TP2+EP.

GSM8K, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 1x H200 (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --use-chat-completions --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' --temperature 0 --max-tokens 1024`, 1319 questions, 5-shot):

| Checkpoint / activations | Accuracy |
|---|---|
| `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` BF16 | 0.956 |
| MXFP4-DSFP8, MoE W4A16 (previous behavior) | 0.958 |
| MXFP4-DSFP8, MoE W4A8 (this PR) | 0.961 |

Tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py -k mxfp4 -v  # 4 passed (H200, main)
pre-commit run --files <changed files>  # incl. mypy
```

The original commit was also validated on B300 (SM103): a layer harness loading a real `RoutedExperts` with random MXFP4 weights was bitwise equal to native `Mxfp4Config` across the default, monolithic TRTLLM, unaligned-shape, `triton_unfused`, `marlin`, `deep_gemm`, `flashinfer_cutlass` and `flashinfer_trtllm` backends. Converted DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 generated the same token ids and logprobs as the original checkpoint on 8 prompts.

## Details

**Root cause of the BF16 fallback.** For `Mxfp4MoeBackend.HUMMING`, the MoE conversion built Humming's input schema only from `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` (`TODO: read input_quant_config from quant_config`), so an unset env meant BF16. With schema fallback enabled, Humming also demotes group-scaled FP8 to A16 (`prefer wna16 for groupwise weight or groupwise input`). Output still looked correct, so the slower path went unnoticed. `Mxfp4MoEMethod` now takes an optional `activation_key`. The HUMMING conversion uses it with fallback disabled, unless the env override is set. Other backends ignore the key.

**Performance.** At the GLM-5.x expert GEMM shapes (N/K 4096/6144 and 6144/2048, 32 experts, top-8; `benchmarks/bench_humming.py` at the #61556 Humming pin), W4A8 is 1.4-1.8x faster than W4A16 for M >= 256. End to end, the small Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 1x H200 is 3-8% slower with W4A8 than with W4A16 across prefill- and decode-heavy runs (hidden 2048, expert intermediate 512, so the per-layer activation quantization is not amortized). This PR follows the checkpoint's declared scheme. `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` still overrides it.

**Limitations**
- ROCm, XPU and CPU have no MXFP4 linear kernel for FP8 activations, so MXFP4 x FP8 dense layers keep the previous MXFP4-activation path there, with a warning. MI300 CI hit this; the linear test is CUDA-only.
- Blackwell: dense linears now use Humming FP8, which is slower than FlashInfer W4A4 on SM100 but matches the checkpoint. The MoE still picks its Blackwell backend without the activation key, so it uses MXFP8 or BF16 activations instead of `DEEPGEMM_MXFP4` (FP8 GS128 x MXFP4). Hooking that up is left for a follow-up issue.
- The AMD, XPU, CPU and V4.1 DeepSeek model variants still need the same `ckpt_names` one-liner; untested here.
- The rename breaks the pre-processed weight cache, so `supports_pre_processed_weights` is off for this method.
- Converting DeepSeek-V4-Flash with vllm-project/compressed-tensors#902 also emits `shared_experts.w\d+` targets, while vLLM names that layer `shared_experts.down_proj`; that needs a fix in the converter or model.

**Not a duplicate:** #59376 targets the same scheme with a different design; only one should merge. #58714 adds a separate CT -> `HummingMoEMethod` route for the same checkpoints; this PR covers that path through the native MXFP4 method. #56523 and #56306 migrate the W4A4 method to the oracle and do not touch this scheme.

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Support DSpark adaptive verification on MI355X
body:
**Requires #55504 and #56831.** Both are open, and this branch carries them as separate commits until they merge.
> - **#55504** "Preserve GDN recurrent state on zero-draft speculative decode steps". Without it, the 1-token-per-request varlen capture dummies record the non-spec KDA path, which trimmed verify batches then replay. This PR also contains the fix I'm proposing for #55504: a row is a spec-decode row only if it is no wider than k+1.
> - **#56831** "Synchronize adaptive DSpark decisions across TP ranks". Without it, rank-local confidences can choose different draft budgets or request boundaries on different TP ranks, which leaves the collectives mismatched and can hang. Kimi-K3 runs at TP8, and trimming happens on ~97% of steps at conc ≥ 8.

### Purpose

`speculative_config.enable_adaptive_verification` (#47808) trims each verify request to 1..k+1 tokens on the device, using the DSpark confidence head. #52988 enabled it for Kimi-K3 on NVIDIA only. On ROCm, Kimi-K3 is refused at engine start:

1. `KimiK3ROCmKDABackend` inherits GDN's `is_ssm()`, so `supports_device_cpu_query_lens_mismatch()` returns `False`.
2. The ROCm KDA builder is `UNIFORM_BATCH` and declares no varlen bound.
3. `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder` is `UNIFORM_BATCH` and declares no varlen bound.

This PR removes those three gates. It also fixes two bugs that showed up once adaptive verification actually ran on a hybrid model.

### Changes

**ROCm KDA** (`models/kimi_k3/amd/kda_metadata.py`)
- The backend accepts a CPU/device query-length mismatch. The spec path plans from `spec_query_start_loc` and `num_accepted_tokens` on the device.
- `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len` returns k+1 under adaptive verification. The builder keeps `UNIFORM_BATCH`, because FULL capture is decode-only.
- Under adaptive verification, the builder drops the host-derived `uniform_spec_sequence_length`. The fixed-length recurrent kernel places sequence *i* at `i * L` and bakes `L` in at graph capture. Varlen graphs are captured with an even split (e.g. 2×4) and replayed with ragged batches (e.g. 1×8), so keeping it corrupts KDA state: acceptance length fell from about 3.8 to 2.0 when we kept it.

**AITER MLA** (`v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py`)

These changes apply under adaptive verification only, with DCP=1 and causal batches:
- Every decode batch runs as uniform k+1 blocks. That is the width the FULL graph's ASM kernel variant was captured at.
- Real tokens are left-aligned in their block, and the kernel's KV length is extended by the pad. Each real token keeps its exact causal window, and no row gets an empty window. Right-alignment faulted the ASM kernel (`HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_APERTURE_VIOLATION`) on contexts shorter than k+1.
- The appended page-list entries repeat the request's first page (`CLAMP_TAIL` in `_expand_page_indices_kernel`), so they stay in bounds.
- q is gathered into the blocks and the output is gathered back using index maps built on the device from `query_start_loc`. This adds no host sync.
- `query_len_support` becomes `VARLEN`, and `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len` returns k+1.
- Causality is decided per batch, not from the group spec. Kimi-K3 DSpark draft layers share the target's MLA group, and `MLAAttentionSpec.merge` sets `non_causal_multi_token_decode` on the whole group. Non-causal draft batches keep the existing path.
- No aiter change is needed: the kernels only ever see uniform blocks.

**Adaptive-verification cost profiling** (`v1/worker/gpu/input_batch.py`, `v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`, `v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py`)

With the default `VLLM_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT_LEN=8192`, profiling faulted on the second prefill-shaped dummy batch ("Write access to a read-only page"). Two causes:
- `compute_num_decode_draft_tokens` (from #55504) made every non-prefilling row without drafts a spec row, including the dummy run's 12-token rows. Those rows carry no prefill flag. The recurrent kernel then walked 12 tokens through an 8-wide state-index row. Now only rows no wider than k+1 are decode rows. Before this fix, running without the fabricated context avoided the crash but silently corrupted memory: acceptance dropped about 10% at conc 1, and recovered fully once the bug was fixed.
- `set_dummy_context` gave every KV cache group the same `arange` block ids, including the recurrent-state groups. Hybrid models back all groups with the same tensors, so KDA wrote fp32 state over blocks the MLA layers read as fp8 KV. Context blocks now count up from the first block past the null block, and state slots count down from the top of the pool.

### Dependencies

Both are required for adaptive verification to run correctly on Kimi-K3. Until they merge, this branch carries them as separate commits, and they will be dropped on rebase.

| PR | Status | Commit here | Why it is required |
|---|---|---|---|
| #55504 | open | `83f1d05dd4` (unchanged backport, original author) | Zero-draft decode rows, including the 1-token varlen capture dummies, must take the GDN/KDA spec path that applies `num_accepted_tokens`. Without it, the FULL varlen graphs record the plain decode kernel. |
| #56831 | open | `2a4a548fd6` (cherry-pick) + `7777ad03c3` (test adapted to this base's `async_tensor_h2d`) | Rank 0's draft budget and per-request capacities are broadcast, so all TP ranks build the same verify layout. |

The width check in `compute_num_decode_draft_tokens` (commit `843d1663e8`) fixes #55504 itself. I've also proposed it on #55504; if it lands there, it will drop from this PR.

### Test Plan

One new test per fix, plus the updates existing tests need:
- `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py::test_adaptive_varlen_decode_correctness` (GPU, 2 cases at 16 heads). Ragged device query lengths (1..k+1) are run against an even host split and checked against an SDPA reference. The two cases are fp8 KV, and bf16 with contexts shorter than k+1 (the left-alignment case).
- `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py`: `test_varlen_cudagraph_bound_follows_adaptive_verification` (on/off, DCP, and a draft group that shares the target's spec) and `test_varlen_rows_left_align_each_request_in_its_block`.
- `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_adaptive_verification.py`: the backend/builder opt-in, and dropping the uniform length under adaptive verification (with a control case without it).
- `tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py::test_rows_wider_than_a_verify_block_keep_the_sentinel`.
- `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py::test_dummy_context_keeps_state_slots_apart_from_context_blocks`.
- End to end: Kimi-K3 FP4, TP8, MI355X (vLLM nightly 36768d1b plus this branch). DSpark K=7 with block (real) acceptance, adaptive verification on vs off, measured on fresh servers.

### Test Result

**Unit tests**
- All of the new tests above pass on MI355X.
- The touched files pass in full: AITER MLA mtp_split 67/67, the new KDA file, pcp manager, and mamba_hybrid model state.
- KDA/GDN/adaptive-verification suites (`tests/models/kimi_k3/test_*kda*`, `test_amd_mla_direct_return.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py`, `test_mamba_update_block_table.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py`, `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py`): 263 passed, 31 skipped, 0 failed on this branch, vs 233 passed and 31 skipped on base main. The difference is the new tests from this PR, #55504 and #56831.

**Kimi-K3 end to end**

| | adaptive off (static K=7) | adaptive on |
|---|---|---|
| Startup with default 8192 profiling context | – | passes (faulted before the fix) |
| conc 1, AL @32k / @128k | 3.68–3.88 / 2.91–3.15 (2 runs) | 3.82 / 3.00 (no trimming at conc 1) |
| conc 10, out tok/s | 453.4 | 485.5 (+7.1%, 1 run) |
| conc 12, out tok/s | 499.3 | 510.9 (+2.3%, 1 run) |
| conc 14, out tok/s (3 runs) | 515.1 | 529.7 (+2.8%; pairs +3.8 / +2.9 / +1.8) |
| Drafts actually verified, conc 10 / 12 / 14 | 100% | ~59% / 54% / 49% |
| KV cache capacity | 3.31M tok | 2.99M tok (−9.8%) |
| Engine init | – | +76 s (cost profiling) |

- conc 10–14 used 16k-token code prompts, 1024 output tokens, and a warmup phase before the timed phase.
- No faults or hangs across 10 on/off runs. With #56831, all 8 TP ranks logged identical draft budgets.

**Not covered yet**
- No accuracy eval (e.g. GSM8K) with adaptive verification on.
- No long-context (>16k) runs at conc ≥ 8.
- conc 4 / FULL_AND_PIECEWISE mixed batches and async scheduling are untested.
- DCP>1 is gated off.
- The gains above are against static K=7. They have not been measured against the best static K for each concurrency.

### Notes

- Related, not required: #57942 (AMD DSpark MLA module) currently maps `confidence_head` to `None`. Once ROCm routes K3 DSpark to that module, enabling adaptive verification would fail at load with `AttributeError` on `model.model.confidence_head`, so the head needs to be kept there. Today ROCm uses the NVIDIA module, which keeps it.
- `vllm:spec_decode_num_draft_tokens` counts proposed drafts, so it reads K even when adaptive verification trims on the device. The "verified" figures above come from instrumentation in the adaptive-verification manager. The scheduler metric still needs fixing

title: [Perf][KV Connector][Mooncake] Send the KV layout once per peer
body:
## Overview

`MooncakeConnector` now sends the decode KV layout to each prefill worker once, instead of on every pull. Later pulls carry only block ids and a `layout_id`, and decode stops attaching the layout only after prefill echoes that id back. This is the exchange-once, cache-per-peer model `NixlConnector` already uses for its handshake. Follows the packed-region work in #57952.

## Claims

- On DeepSeek-V4-Flash 4P4D (146 registered regions), each later pull is **9184 B smaller per rank**: 9500 B → 316 B at ~8k tokens. The saving is the same at 508 and 8008 tokens.
- Prefill-side control-plane time per pull drops from **0.078 ms to 0.014 ms** (steady-state P50). The absolute saving is ~0.06 ms, so **TTFT does not change** (1.10 s at ~8k tokens on both sides).
- Mixed versions stay correct in both directions. A prefill without this change never receives a layout-less pull; a decode without this change keeps today's behavior.
- No accuracy change on gsm8k (Qwen3-0.6B 1P1D; DeepSeek-V4-Flash 4P4D vs. single node).

## Validation

**Unit tests**: 123 passed.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py
```

The environment was `uv venv --system-site-packages`, with the default test model `facebook/opt-125m`. The cu129 precompiled wheel for the base commit returned 404, so this is not a `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1` install.

New tests cover:
- layout-less pulls after the echo;
- a `LAYOUT_MISS` resend;
- a prefill that never echoes (old peer);
- a reused layout arriving under a new id;
- LRU eviction.

`pre-commit` passes: `ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `typos`, and `mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual`.

**Version matrix** (Qwen2.5-0.5B, greedy, TP=1, RDMA). "Old" is `origin/main` (`4e4d75c459`). The `MooncakeXferMetadata to <addr> is N bytes (layout|blocks)` line is a DEBUG log (`VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`). These runs used an earlier revision that logged the same line once per address at INFO.

| Prefill | Decode | PP (P/D) | Decode log | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| new | new | 1/1 | `1615 B (layout)`, then `256 B (blocks)` | same output, 100% external prefix hits |
| old | new | 1/1 | `(layout)` only, never `(blocks)` | same output |
| old | new | 2/1 | `(layout)` only for both prefill addresses; no `no matching consumer` on prefill | same output |
| new | old | 1/1 | (old decode has no size log) | same output |

The old/new-PP 1/1 and new/old rows were run on the pre-rebase commit; the Mooncake code is identical. The LRU commit does not touch the code those two rows run: an old prefill never executes it, and an old decode sends `layout_id=0`, which the new prefill never stores.

**Bytes and TTFT** (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP=4, EP, fp8, block 256, 4P4D on one node). Each TTFT row is 8 streamed requests with `max_tokens=1`, after warmup.

| | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Metadata per pull, per rank, ~8k tokens | 9483 B every pull | 9500 B first pull, then 316 B |
| Prefill control plane, steady-state P50 / P99 | 0.078 / 0.099 ms (n=44) | 0.014 / 0.029 ms (n=24) |
| TTFT, ~8k tokens | 1.092–1.097 s | 1.096–1.099 s |

The control-plane time was measured from `send_kv_to_decode` entry to the end of region-length validation, on all 4 ranks, dropping the first pull. The timing code was temporary and is not part of this PR.

**Accuracy** (gsm8k, `exact_match,strict-match`, 1319 questions).

| Setup | Score |
|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B 1P1D, `tests/v1/kv_connector/mooncake_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh` | 0.422 (expected 0.41 ± 0.05) |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash 4P4D | 0.951 (1255/1319) |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash single node, TP=4, same eager / fp8 / `max_num_seqs=8` | 0.951 (1254/1319) |

Both P/D runs had 100% external prefix hits and 0 failed transfers.

**Not covered end to end.** Prefill side-channel ports come from `bind_to_random_port`, and decode RPC ports from the transfer engine, so a restarted peer always comes back at a new address. Three paths therefore have unit coverage only:
- the `LAYOUT_MISS` resend;
- the same address reusing a layout under a new id;
- LRU eviction followed by a resend.

Prefill and decode restarts were run end to end; they re-sent the layout to the new address, with unchanged output.

## Details

**Why.** Every pull sends the whole registered layout in `MooncakeXferMetadata`: base addresses, block lengths, layer names, group ids and row offsets. On a 146-region model that is ~9 KB per rank per pull, mostly layer names. Prefill then builds and hashes a tuple of all of it on every batch, just to hit `_prepared_transfer_regions`. Both costs grow with the number of registered regions, not with the request.

**Prior art: `NixlConnector`.** NIXL already exchanges the KV layout once per remote engine and keeps the per-request message small:

| | `NixlConnector` (pull mode) | `MooncakeConnector`, this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Data direction | Decode reads from prefill, so **decode** caches the prefill layout | Prefill writes into decode, so **prefill** caches the decode layout |
| When the layout is exchanged | Once per remote engine, in `_ensure_handshake`; concurrent requests to the same engine share one handshake future | Once per decode worker address, piggybacked on the first pull |
| Where it is cached | `add_remote_agent` stores `kv_caches_base_addr[engine_id][tp_rank]`, block lengths, and region metadata | `_layout_by_peer`, keyed by decode host, port, ranks, and `layout_id` |
| Per-request message | `RemoteMeta`: block ids, host, port, `engine_id`, request id | `req_blocks` and `layout_id` |
| How a new layout is detected | The cache is keyed by `engine_id`; a restarted engine has a new id and is handshaken anew, and the replaced engine is cleaned up (`_track_remote_engine_replacement`) | Each `register_kv_caches` mints a new `layout_id`; an unknown id gets `LAYOUT_MISS` and a resend |

Mooncake has no separate handshake round trip; decode simply sends its pull to the prefill side channel. So instead of adding a handshake, this PR makes the first pull carry the layout. Prefill's echo of `layout_id` then plays the part of NIXL's handshake response: decode treats the layout as delivered only after it sees the echo, so a peer that never echoes keeps getting the full layout. NIXL's compatibility hash (`NixlHandshakePayload.compatibility_hash`) is out of scope here.

**Protocol.**
- `register_kv_caches` draws a random nonzero 63-bit `layout_id`. A counter would restart at 1 in every process, so a restarted decode at the same address could match a stale prefill entry and be written with the old layout.
- Prefill stores aligned regions by `(decode host, port, tp_rank, pp_size, tp_size, layout_id)`. It stores them on both a fresh alignment and a `_prepared_transfer_regions` hit. A hit can carry a new id for a layout prefill has already seen.
- Prefill echoes `layout_id` in `MooncakeXferResponse` once it holds that layout. Decode omits the layout for a worker address only after seeing the echo.
  - A plain `FINISH` is not enough. A prefill without this change ignores the new field and answers `FINISH`. With equal PP it would then reject every layout-less pull. With different PP, `allow_partial_layers` would align zero regions, transfer nothing, and report success.
- A layout-less pull whose id prefill does not hold gets the new `LAYOUT_MISS` status. Decode resends with the layout once; a second miss fails the request normally. Only layout-less pulls can receive `LAYOUT_MISS`, and only a new decode sends those, so an old decode never sees the new enum value.
- `_layout_by_peer` is an LRU capped at 1024 entries, because every decode re-registration mints a new id. Eviction is always safe: the evicted decode gets `LAYOUT_MISS` and resends.

**Tradeoff.** About 130 net lines in the connector, for ~9 KB and ~0.06 ms per pull, with no TTFT change on DeepSeek-V4-Flash. The case for the change is that this overhead is fixed per pull and grows with the region count and layer-name length, so it grows with deeper and multi-cache models. It is not a latency win at today's scale.

**Limitations (pre-existing, unchanged here).**
- `_prepared_transfer_regions` is still unbounded. Its key includes decode base addresses, so it grows on every decode restart. Its entries could take the same LRU in a follow-up.
- After a prefill restart, the proxy must be restarted too. Otherwise decode keeps the old `engine_id` and requests stall instead of failing.
- A pull with empty `req_blocks` gets no response.

**Related PRs.**
- #59592 adds `remote_block_size` to `MooncakeXferMetadata`, in code this PR moves into `_build_pull_metadata`. Whichever lands second should set it on both full and layout-less pulls.
- #59625 (draft, sleep mode over RDMA) re-registers KV caches on wake-up. Here that mints a new `layout_id` and clears the caches, so a woken peer re-sends or re-receives the layout. That PR also restructures `send_kv_to_decode`, so expect a textual conflict.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR sends the Mooncake layout once or caches it per peer. Searched `mooncake layout`, `mooncake handshake` and `mooncake metadata` with `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search ...`.

**AI assistance.** This PR was written with AI assistance (Cursor). I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

title: [Feature][PCP] Add DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash support
body:
## Overview

Add text-only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Prefill Context Parallelism (PCP) support on NVIDIA CUDA to Model Runner V2 with FlashMLA sparse attention.

This PR intentionally targets a colocated single-model instance only. P/D disaggregation and KV transfer are not supported in this initial scope. The implementation keeps compressed KV, indexer, SWA, Engram lookback, MoE routing inputs, and padding consistent across PCP ranks while closing ratio-2 pairs split across PCP chunks with gathered predecessor rows.

Related to #25749 and #49109. This PR targets the DeepSeek-V4.1 ratio-1/2 cache path and does not add the V4 C4/C128 or MegaMoE work from #43809.

## Supported Scope

- NVIDIA CUDA only: text-only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Model Runner V2 with `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41`.
- One colocated model instance with PP=DP=DCP=1.
- Prefill PCP with arbitrary PCP chunk boundaries, including ranks with no local decode requests.
- Tensor parallelism and PCP can be composed; the validation below covers TP8/PCP1, TP4/PCP2, and TP2/PCP4 on an 8-GPU node.
- Expert parallel execution with the `allgather_reducescatter` all-to-all backend.
- Eager execution with synchronous scheduling.

## Not Supported Yet

- P/D disaggregation or any KV connector.
- ROCm.
- Pipeline parallelism, data parallelism, decode context parallelism, or microbatching with PCP.
- Prefix caching or SWA bounded replay with PCP.
- Speculative decoding, CUDA graphs, or MegaMoE with PCP.
- Multimodal inputs, encoder-decoder models, or LoRA with PCP.
- Attention backends other than the DeepSeek-V4.1 FlashMLA sparse path.

These constraints are deliberate so the first upstream step establishes standalone PCP correctness without mixing in KV handoff or replay semantics. Follow-up work will expand one boundary at a time: first standalone cache/replay behavior, then additional single-instance parallel topologies and runtime features, and finally P/D disaggregation with a minimal direct connector before layering prefix caching, bounded replay, and speculative Decode support.

## Implementation

- Compress ratio-2 groups on each rank's local token rows. Gather only the last FP32 row of each local chunk to close cross-rank pairs and keep the open ring rows consistent.
- Keep PCP linkage in model-specific compressor metadata; `InputBatch` and `PCPManager` remain unchanged relative to `main`.
- Gather BF16 compressor latents in one cache-insert path shared with ratio 1, then use the aligned gathered positions and slots for main KV and Indexer K writes.
- Keep Engram lookback, MoE routing token IDs, padding, compressed KV, indexer keys, and SWA metadata aligned across PCP ranks.
- Keep PCP collectives ordered consistently across ranks, including empty local shards and requests with no local decode rows.

Engram embeddings remain TP-sharded, so increasing PCP can increase host memory requirements.

## Rank-local Compressor Revision

Following LucasWilkinson's review, this revision adopts [wangyicong52/vllm#1](https://github.com/wangyicong52/vllm/pull/1), authored by Lucas Wilkinson, at `b06bea7abc4eb5cf6965fe704d16257ac7c70697`. It removes the `InputBatch.pcp_metadata` / `PCPBatchMetadata` plumbing and the global FP32 `kv_score` gather.

Local validation of this revision: 101 passed, 6 CUDA-only skipped; applicable pre-commit hooks, mypy 3.10/3.12, syntax and diff checks passed. Additional CPU regressions cover PCP2/4 predecessor linkage, replicated short prefills, empty ranks, request isolation and newest open ring rows.

The GPU/model measurements below belong to the preceding global-order compressor implementation. They have not been rerun for this revision. The rank-local kernel, GSM8K and Prefill benchmark require renewed validation on the target H20 configuration before these historical results can support claims about this version.

## Validation Environment

- Hardware: one node with 8x NVIDIA H20 (96G, SM90) GPUs.
- SM100 was not validated in this PR.
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-92044241a02f05de51420d654daf669de20b4691`.

## vLLM Launch Arguments

Only the TP/PCP pair changed across the accuracy arms: `TP_SIZE=8, PCP_SIZE=1` for TP8/PCP1, `TP_SIZE=4, PCP_SIZE=2` for TP4/PCP2, and `TP_SIZE=2, PCP_SIZE=4` for TP2/PCP4. PP, DP, and DCP remained 1.

```bash
vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 18001 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --block-size 64 \
  --tensor-parallel-size "${TP_SIZE}" \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size "${PCP_SIZE}" \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter \
  --moe-backend marlin \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-swa-bounded-replay \
  --enforce-eager \
  --no-async-scheduling
```

## Validation

```bash
evalscope eval \
  --eval-type openai_api \
  --api-url http://<HOST>:18001/v1 \
  --api-key EMPTY \
  --model deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --model-id deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --datasets gsm8k \
  --dataset-hub modelscope \
  --dataset-args '{"gsm8k":{"few_shot_num":4}}' \
  --seed 42 \
  --eval-batch-size 64 \
  --generation-config '{"temperature":0.0,"top_p":1.0,"max_tokens":65536,"reasoning_effort":"high","seed":42,"timeout":10000}' \
  --timeout 10000
```

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Release pending CPU lookup pins on cache reset
body:
## Overview

Release SimpleCPUOffload lookup-only CPU block references during cache reset. A request waiting for GPU allocation can otherwise prevent `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)` from succeeding even after GPU blocks and in-flight transfers have drained.

## Claims

- Reset releases temporary CPU lookup pins and invalidates their saved lookup state.
- Existing in-flight DMA references remain protected until completion.
- A deterministic regression covers eager/lazy modes and one/two cache groups.

## Validation

Validated against upstream `5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c`, using its matching precompiled native extensions.

| Check | Unpatched + regression | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| New reset regression | 4 assertion failures (`reset()` returns False) | 4 pass within the full scheduler suite |
| Scheduler, KV events, connector and metrics suites | — | 92 passed |
| CUDA worker suite, RTX 4090 | — | 21 passed |
| Real Scheduler allocation-pressure diagnostic | Reset fails after GPU blocks are released | Reset succeeds; retry has no stale CPU hit |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct GPU diagnostic | 16 lookup references prevent reset | References released; reset and subsequent generation pass |

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py -k test_reset_releases_pending_cpu_hits
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_metrics.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py
```

All applicable changed-file hooks, mypy 3.10/3.12 and `git diff --check` passed. The existing Buildkite KV Offload suite collects the new test; test tethering passed. Upstream CI has not run for this candidate.

The GPU diagnostic used MRV2, FP16, TP=1, eager execution and 128 MiB each of GPU/CPU KV cache. After a real CPU store/load round trip with 256 cached tokens, it explicitly paused a queued request after the production CPU lookup. Baseline reset returned False; the patch released all 16 lookup pins, reset successfully and generated the same token `[19]` with zero cached tokens. Actual allocation pressure is covered separately by the real Scheduler diagnostic, whose worker token output is synthetic. This is a focused correctness check, not a performance or broad model-quality claim. Multi-node, disk/GDS and other GPU backends were not validated.

## Details

`get_num_new_matched_tokens()` pins matching CPU blocks until `update_state_after_alloc()` consumes the lookup. Failed GPU allocation leaves that lookup in `_pending_cpu_hits`. Reset already abandons transfers safely but omitted these pre-allocation references.

Reuse `_free_pending_cpu_hit()` before clearing the pending lookup map. These references have no associated worker DMA; submitted transfers retain their separate pins and existing completion-based cleanup. A waiting request performs a fresh lookup when scheduling resumes. No API, storage format or normal scheduling policy changes are introduced.

Duplicate screening on 2026-10-03 covered open/closed/merged PRs, related issues, recent commits and the contributor's existing PRs. [#42289](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42289) introduced temporary lookup pins; [#39726](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39726) introduced reset support. Both are merged. The active [#57816](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57816) addresses eager-store placement after MRV2 preemption, a different state transition. No active implementation of this lookup-pin reset fix was found. This draft does not claim to close an existing issue.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex performed investigation, implementation, local/remote validation and drafting. The human contributor has confirmed review of the final change and authorized submission. The reported validation was performed with Codex; independent human reruns have not been confirmed.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix speculative block reservations across KV cache groups
body:
## Overview

Fix speculative decode block reservations for asynchronous KV loads with
multiple KV cache groups. Under KV memory pressure, under-reserving these
blocks can leave a request admitted for an asynchronous KV load but unable
to start decoding once the load completes.

## Claims

- Account for every KV cache group using its actual allocation block size.
- Extend the existing promotion-margin regression test to cover single-group,
  multi-group, and mixed-block-size configurations.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_decode_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py
```

**32 passed.** Pre-commit checks and manual Python 3.12 mypy passed.

Regression controls replace only the reservation method in the test process:

| Implementation | Single group | Multiple groups | Different block sizes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Original | Pass | Fail | Fail |
| Original × group count | Pass | Pass | Fail |
| This fix | Pass | Pass | Pass |

The broader scheduler/decode/recovery run showed no additional failures:
both the patched implementation and the original reservation method produced
171 passes and the same 46 failing test IDs. Observed environment limitations
included unavailable offline model configurations and insufficient visible
GPUs for parallel tests.

Validation exercises the scheduler and KV allocation paths with simulated
remote completion. Live NIXL P/D and model-level evaluations were not run.

## Details

The existing calculation converts the speculative token margin to blocks
using the scheduler block size once. However, each KV cache group allocates
independently from the shared block pool, and groups may use different
allocation block sizes.

Sum the reservation across cache managers using each manager's block size.
Simply multiplying the old result by the group count is insufficient for
mixed-block-size configurations. The existing conservative reservation
approach is preserved.

The regression test checks admission and subsequent scheduling rather than
asserting the helper's arithmetic directly.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Trim the last KV-source layer in decoder replay
body:
## Purpose

In decoder replay steps, the last KV-source layer (layer 20 on DSV4.1-Flash) still ran on every row, though for the trimmed rows only its KV (SWA, compressed, index K) is read. Its indexer scoring and top-k, sparse MLA, wo and MoE feed only the replay layers.

- The cut layer now writes its KV for every row (`DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.write_kv` → `DeepseekV4Attention.forward_kv`), then runs as the first replay layer (`decoder_replay_start = cut`) on the replay rows, in the replay batch and its CUDA graphs. Its sliding-window metadata keeps the batch's window starts, so it stays exact. The indexer row-buffer compaction goes.
- PIECEWISE graphs now decide the replay break (and `write_kv`) by graph size (`DecoderReplayLayers.replays()`) instead of `replay_batch is not None`, which is unset at capture: before, the break was never captured and PIECEWISE steps did not trim.

## Results

title: [Bugfix] Drop enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce from FlashInfer CuteDSL MegaMoE config
body:
## Overview Fixes #59887. `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` (added in #54049) passes `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce` to FlashInfer's CuTeDSL MegaMoE config. The pinned FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 calls that field `in_kernel_fc2_reduce`, so the backend raises `TypeError` while the layer is built. This PR drops the kwarg and adds a regression test that doesn't need SM100. `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` is unaffected. ## Claims - With the pinned `flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1`, `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` no longer raises `TypeError` when the layer is built. Behavior is as intended: `False` is the field's default in every FlashInfer release from v0.7.0 through v0.7.1. - The fix doesn't depend on the FlashInfer version: 0.7.1 (released 2026-10-09; #60948 bumps the pin) renames the field but keeps its `False` default, and the new test passes against 0.7.1's config types (constructor check only; the backend itself was not run on 0.7.1). With 0.7.1, `main`'s current kwarg becomes valid too; this PR keeps 0.7.0.x working and adds the drift test. - On 4× GB200 at current `main`, with `nvshmem4py` installed and #61041's decoder-replay fix copied in, the backend serves DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with default CUDA graphs (FULL and PIECEWISE captured). GSM8K is 0.891 (one run), vs 0.901 for `deep_gemm_mega_moe` and 0.910 for the default MoE backend on the same image. - New test `test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer`: it builds the adapter against the installed FlashInfer's real config types, without SM100 or multiple GPUs (it also passes with no GPU visible). It lives in `tests/kernels/moe`, which the L4 `kernels-moe-test` job runs; no Buildkite job has run on this PR yet. - **What it catches:** a renamed or removed kwarg in FlashInfer's MoE-EP config types, or removal of the deprecated `Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig`/`DeepGemmMegaMoeConfig` aliases. Before, these only failed at model load on SM100. - **What it doesn't cover:** `MoEEpTensors` and the megakernel layer's own methods. Only the SM100 e2e test covers those. ## Validation ### Retest at current `main` (3c062d391d) `main` was merged into this branch (no conflicts); the PR still changes only `flashinfer_moe_ep.py` (the kwarg) and its test. All runs were on 4× GB200 (docker, with the Slurm job's IMEX channel) in `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` arm64 `sha256:f853a683…`, built from 7d0b4e57aa. That image's `flashinfer_moe_ep.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py`, `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/` and `vllm/config/kernel.py` are identical to `main`'s. - **base:** the image as is. - **fix:** the image with this PR's `flashinfer_moe_ep.py` copied over the installed one. - Tests ran from this branch's `tests/` tree. The CuTeDSL path also needs `nvshmem4py` (#59903, installed by #59912), so `nvshmem4py-cu13` (0.4.0) was installed in the container. | Check | base | fix | |---|---|---| | `pytest kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py -k test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer` | `[cutedsl]` ❌ `TypeError: Sm100_Nvfp4_Nvfp4_Bf16_Cutedsl_MegaMoeConfig.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce'`; `[deep_gemm]` ✅ | ✅ 2/2; also 2/2 with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=` | | Same, with `flashinfer-python==0.7.1` installed (constructor check only; run with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=`, and with `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1` because the image's `flashinfer-cubin` is 0.7.0.post1) | ✅ 2/2 | ✅ 2/2 | | `pytest kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py -k "test_init_warmup and cutedsl"` (2 and 4 GPUs, 4 geometries) | ❌ same `TypeError` (ran the 2-GPU dsv4-flash case) | ✅ 8/8, run twice | | DEP=4 serve, `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`, default CUDA graphs | all 4 DP ranks raise the same `TypeError` right after the checkpoint loads; the server exits about 2 minutes in | serves (FULL and PIECEWISE graphs captured); answers correct; GSM8K **0.891** | - **Serve command:** `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` (revision `2cba9e42`, pre-downloaded; containers run with `--ipc=host` so the DP replicas share the Engram tables through `/dev/shm`). Startup takes about 10 minutes, which can exceed the default 600 s engine-ready timeout. - **GSM8K:** `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-concurrency 128`, one run. For reference, on the same image the default MoE backend scored 0.910 and `deep_gemm_mega_moe` 0.901 (#61041's validation). One run's standard error is about 0.008 (about 0.012 for a two-run difference), so the gap to the default is about 1.6 SE; other runs of this backend scored 0.888–0.899 (#59912's retest, #61041). The fix run also had #61041's one-file decoder-replay fix copied in: without it, every FlashInfer MegaMoE backend crashes under GSM8K load on current `main` (#61040), independent of this PR. - **Also covered:** #59912's retest, on images built from `main` c41b2639e2 + #59912 + this PR, passed the kwargs test (2/2) and the CuTeDSL e2e tests (8/8) on GB200, GB300 and B200, and, with the same decoder-replay fix, served DEP=4/8/16 with GSM8K 0.888–0.897. - **pre-commit:** `pre-commit run --files tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/flashinfer_moe_ep.py` passes. - **pytest:** run from `tests/` with `-v -rs --timeout=900`.
Earlier validation (at 7712663, on main 84bcbc6264; locally built images) All runs were on 4× GB200. Images were built from `docker/Dockerfile` with the arm64 CI build args, with these deviations: `torch_cuda_arch_list=10.0`, no sccache, `RUN_WHEEL_CHECK=false`, local `max_jobs`/`nvcc_threads`, and an added `vllm-openai` target. **fix** from this branch at 7712663 (35b3ca5 only edits a comment and docstrings), **base** from `main` @ 84bcbc6264. | Test | base (main) | fix | |---|---|---| | `test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer[cutedsl]` | ❌ `TypeError: Sm100_Nvfp4_Nvfp4_Bf16_Cutedsl_MegaMoeConfig.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce'` | ✅ | | `test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer[deep_gemm]` | ✅ | ✅ | | `test_init_warmup_forward_is_exact_on_grid_inputs[*-cutedsl-*]` (2 and 4 GPUs, 4 geometries) | ❌ same `TypeError` in every worker | ✅ 8/8 (one case hung once and passed on retry) | Serving DEP=4: base, with the default cudagraph mode, crashed on every DP rank with the `TypeError` before graph capture. Fix, with `--compilation-config.cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` (full-graph capture failed in that environment), served, answered correctly, and scored GSM8K 0.898 (`flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`) vs 0.901 for the default backend with the same flag. `nvshmem4py-cu13==0.4.0` was installed in a test-only layer, and containers got the Slurm job's IMEX channel (without it NVSHMEM's fabric `cuMemCreate` fails with `CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED`).
## Details **Root cause.** FlashInfer renamed `in_kernel_fc2_reduce` to `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce` in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4604, first shipped in v0.7.1rc1 and now in v0.7.1. The adapter was written against the new name while vLLM still pins 0.7.0.post1 (`requirements/cuda.txt`). Every other kwarg and method the adapter uses on FlashInfer's MoE-EP types is present in both 0.7.0.post1 and 0.7.1, so this was the only mismatch. **Why CI missed it.** The only test that constructs the adapter, `test_init_warmup_forward_is_exact_on_grid_inputs`, needs SM100 and 2+ GPUs. `kernels-moe-test` runs on L4, so it always skips there, and no B200 job runs this file. The new test fakes four things: - `flashinfer.moe_ep.MoEEpMegaLayer`, which allocates symmetric memory; - the EP group; - the device index; - `_expose_deep_gemm_to_flashinfer`, which imports DeepGEMM. Everything FlashInfer receives is its own config dataclasses plus a real `MoEWeightPack`. **Relation to #60948 (FlashInfer 0.7.1).** #60948 bumps the pin to 0.7.1 and doesn't touch `flashinfer_moe_ep.py`; the two PRs don't conflict and pass in either order. After #60948, `main`'s explicit `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce=False` would be valid; dropping it still gives the same `False` default (0.7.1 documents the flag as an opt-in to nondeterministic accumulation), keeps the backend working on 0.7.0.x, and the new test guards both versions. **Alternatives considered.** *Version-gate the kwarg name:* unnecessary, since the value equals the default. **Related, found while validating.** - **`nvshmem4py` packaging:** vLLM's images don't ship `nvshmem4py`, so without it `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` fails at FlashInfer's runtime bootstrap. Tracked in #59903, fixed by #59912. - **Decoder replay under load:** on current `main`, DeepSeek-V4.1 with either FlashInfer MegaMoE backend crashes under GSM8K load in the decoder-replay CUDA graph. Tracked in #61040, fixed by #61041. - **Earlier limitations that no longer reproduce at current `main`:** full CUDA-graph capture with this backend (FULL graphs captured above), and the DeepGEMM "type Runtime is already registered" import error (#59904; the vendored DeepGEMM moved to `TORCH_LIBRARY` in #48962). The one-off 2-GPU e2e hang did not recur in 16 cases. - The adapter still imports FlashInfer's deprecated `Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig`/`DeepGemmMegaMoeConfig` aliases, which FlashInfer has scheduled for removal. Switching to the `Sm100_*` names is a follow-up; the new test would flag the removal. **Duplicate check.** Apart from #59887, which I filed for this bug, no open or closed issue or PR mentions `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce`, `in_kernel_fc2_reduce`, `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` or `Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig` as a fix for it. #60948 (FlashInfer 0.7.1 bump) makes `main`'s kwarg valid but leaves 0.7.0.x broken and adds no test. ---

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Exchange packed FP8 Engram rows across DP and feed wkv MXFP8
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1's Engram tables are already MXFP8 (FP8 rows with one ue8m0 scale per 32 values) and `wkv` is an MXFP8 GEMM, but the lookup dequantizes each row to BF16, DP replicas all-gather those 512-byte rows layer by layer, and `wkv` quantizes them right back. This PR keeps rows packed from the host table to `wkv`.

- **Packed rows, direct MXFP8.** The lookup copies each row's 256 FP8 bytes and 8 scale bytes as they are, and one unpack kernel writes them in FlashInfer's MXFP8 activation layout (F8_128x4 scales). `wkv` takes them as a `QuantizedActivation`, so both the dequant and the requant are gone, and the output is bit-identical.
- **One all-to-all per prefill step.** `EngramBatch` looks up every local Engram layer into one packed buffer and exchanges it with a single all-to-all, which sends each rank only its own tokens (264 instead of 512 bytes per head row, 1/DP of an all-gather), then unpacks all layers in one launch.
- **Peer exchange for decode.** Below 128 tokens per rank, `EngramPeerExchange` replaces the hash all-gather and the per-layer row all-gathers: ranks publish ids in symmetric memory, look up their head shard for every peer's tokens, and read their own tokens back from the peers after a barrier. All layers share one lookup and one unpack launch.

The batched path serves DP-sharded tables (`embedding_across_dp` without DP-shared memory) with TP = 1, `head_dim % 128 == 0`, no LoRA (it wraps `wkv` after construction), and a `wkv` kernel that takes F8_128x4 scales (reusing `can_fuse_query_quant`). The peer exchange also needs SM100, CPU offload, and 2/4/8 fully connected GPUs; without it every slot uses the all-to-all, which on DEP4 HBM tables at 1–127 tokens per rank is 19–58 us faster than the BF16 path. Everything else, including TP, DP-shared tables, single replicas and ROCm, keeps the existing BF16 path unchanged. Communication stays on the current stream and `wkv` still runs in `Engram.forward`.

Also changed along the way:

- `EngramBatch` is an `nn.Module`, so the peer exchange's pointer tables are model buffers that level-2 sleep restores.
- `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm_quant` and the Engram unpack kernel share the F8_128x4 scale offset and size helpers.

## Kernel microbenchmark

The benchmarks, E2E runs and the first accuracy table were measured on d593d7f5df. 3724967bb9 only drops paths that DEP + THP never takes and keeps its `wkv` outputs bitwise identical (see Test Result).

Engram only, two layers (lookup, exchange, and anything needed to reach the MXFP8 `wkv` input), 4 x GB300 in one node. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash table sizes (24 heads x 16M rows, 94.4 GiB per layer) as DP-shared `/dev/shm` tables or private THP shards, uniform random ids rotating 3 sets, 256 MiB L2 flush per sample, full CUDA graph replay, median of 40 samples of the slowest rank, best of 2 rounds. Since this PR's output is already the `wkv` input, the BF16 columns include their activation quantization (17 us for decode, 203 us at 32K tokens).

DEP4:

| tokens/rank | DP-shared (us) | THP + all-gather (us) | this PR (us) | vs THP + all-gather |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 34 | 80 | 36 | 2.22x |
| 8 | 34 | 81 | 38 | 2.13x |
| 32 | 38 | 93 | 40 | 2.33x |
| 64 | 44 | 106 | 43 | 2.47x |
| 127 | 136 | 136 | 50 | 2.72x |
| 128 | 140 | 136 | 72 | 1.89x |
| 1024 | 2442 | 315 | 179 | 1.76x |
| 4096 | 5326 | 1097 | 534 | 2.05x |
| 8192 | 8224 | 2087 | 1010 | 2.07x |
| 16384 | 11854 | 4047 | 1954 | 2.07x |
| 32768 | 16008 | 7860 | 3800 | 2.07x |

DEP2:

| tokens/rank | DP-shared (us) | THP + all-gather (us) | this PR (us) | vs THP + all-gather |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 34 | 73 | 38 | 1.92x |
| 8 | 34 | 74 | 40 | 1.85x |
| 32 | 35 | 81 | 43 | 1.88x |
| 64 | 41 | 90 | 44 | 2.05x |
| 127 | 66 | 107 | 49 | 2.18x |
| 128 | 62 | 107 | 71 | 1.51x |
| 1024 | 2015 | 228 | 168 | 1.36x |
| 4096 | 4629 | 754 | 507 | 1.49x |
| 8192 | 6873 | 1407 | 970 | 1.45x |
| 16384 | 9511 | 2709 | 1879 | 1.44x |
| 32768 | 12389 | 5268 | 3672 | 1.43x |

DP-shared tables need no exchange, so at 1–64 tokens they are at most 8 us faster than this PR; from 1024 tokens this PR is 3.4–13.6x faster than them. The 127 → 128 step is the switch from the peer exchange to the all-to-all.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py tests/kernels/core/test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm.py -q
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files <changed files> --hook-stage manual
```

New coverage: the packed lookup output, and a 4-GPU check of the batched staging across peer and all-to-all slots, uneven and idle replicas, and full and breakable CUDA graph replays. The peer path needs SM100, so other GPUs only cover the all-to-all path.

## Test Result

On 3724967bb9, 202 passed on 4x GB200 (102 Engram kernel, 27 distributed, 73 `test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm.py`). Ruff, format and mypy pass.

Also checked locally, without adding tests:

- The staged MXFP8 bytes equal the table rows byte for byte on DEP2 and DEP4 with 22 and 24 heads, 1–3 layers starting at a non-zero hash index, pinned, THP and HBM tables, 1–4096 tokens around the 127/128 boundary (sorted lookups included), and 24 unsynchronized steps that switch between peer exchange and all-to-all.
- Real layer 1 and 14 checkpoint rows and `wkv` weights: the `wkv` output is bitwise identical to the BF16 path at 129, 1024 and 4096 tokens, with CuTe-DSL and CUTLASS.
- DEP4 `Engram.forward` through the peer exchange and the all-to-all in eager mode and full and breakable graph replays: bitwise identical to the BF16 path.
- 3724967bb9 vs d593d7f5df on DEP4 (24 heads x 256, 2 layers, 10% dead ids, idle ranks; pinned tables at 1–512 and HBM tables at 128–512 tokens per rank): staged MXFP8 values and `wkv` outputs (CuTe-DSL and CUTLASS) are bitwise identical; only the scales of padding and unowned rows change from 127 to 0.
- After a simulated level-2 sleep the peer exchange's pointer tables are restored and its lookups stay exact.

## E2E prefill (DEP4)

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (DP4 x TP1 + EP) on one GB300 node: DeepGEMM mega MoE, FlashInfer sparse MLA, fp8 KV cache, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, prefix caching off. Offline `LLM` per DP rank, one prompt per rank (nominal length minus 7 tokens per rank), `max_tokens=1`; TTFT is `scheduled_ts` to `first_token_ts` on the slowest rank, median of 3 repeats after a warmup repeat. Measured on top of #59532 with `max_cudagraph_capture_size=8192` (default size list, so 1K–8K prefills run in PIECEWISE graphs) and `max_num_seqs=64`. Prompts are uniformly random token ids; a repeated sentence keeps the few distinct n-gram rows in cache and hides Engram entirely.

| tokens/rank | DP-shared TTFT (ms) | THP + all-gather TTFT (ms) | this PR TTFT (ms) | vs DP-shared | vs THP + all-gather |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 60.2 | 61.7 | 60.5 | 0.99x | 1.02x |
| 4096 | 129.7 | 128.0 | 127.2 | 1.02x | 1.01x |
| 8192 | 220.2 | 214.2 | 213.9 | 1.03x | 1.00x |
| 16384 | 248.1 | 242.6 | 240.5 | 1.03x | 1.01x |
| 32768 | 466.0 | 447.4 | 446.5 | 1.04x | 1.00x |

Repeat spread is under 2.5 ms (5 ms for DP-shared at 32K). The gain over DP-shared tables matches the microbenchmark: at 8K the two Engram layers take 7.2 ms less, close to the 6.3 ms measured end to end. Against THP tables with all-gather it is about 1 ms per step, within noise end to end.

## E2E decode (DEP4)

Same setup on `main` (default capture sizes up to 512, `max_num_seqs=128`), short prompts, 64 output tokens with the decode token fixed to hold MoE routing constant. Mean request TPOT of the slowest rank, median of 3 repeats after a warmup repeat.

| batch/rank | DP-shared TPOT (ms) | THP + all-gather TPOT (ms) | this PR TPOT (ms) | vs DP-shared | vs THP + all-gather |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6.072 | 6.128 | 6.082 | 1.00x | 1.01x |
