title: [Model][DeepSeek-V4] Make MegaMoE shared-expert finalize independent of linear post-load order
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

MegaMoE fuses the DeepSeek-V4 shared expert using the shared linears' block-FP8 UE8M0 scales. Those linears' own DeepGEMM post-load hook repacks the same scales into int32, in place.

`_finalize_shared_expert_weights` only converted scales that were still in checkpoint layout, and passed packed scales straight to MegaMoE. So it was only correct when it ran **before** that hook:
- Real loads finalize inside `load_weights`, before the hook, so they are fine.
- A dummy load never calls `load_weights` and finalizes **after** the hook. With DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MegaMoE + EP, DeepGEMM then asserts at startup (`layout.hpp:114`).

The packed layout already stores one UE8M0 byte per (row, k-block), four k-blocks per int32. `_prepare_shared_expert_scale` now reads per-row exponents from either layout and builds the same 1x32 MegaMoE scale. The rest of the path is unchanged, including the existing shape check and the fallback to the serial shared MLP.

This removes the ordering constraint that keeps DeepSeek-V4 finalizing inside `load_weights`. #57733 builds on it.

## Test Plan / Results

`tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py::test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe_finalizes_native_shared_expert_weights` gains two `-packed` cases. Their scales are packed by the real linear-hook packer (`deepgemm_post_process_weight_scale_block`) before finalize runs. Results on GB200:
- With this PR: 7 passed.
- On `main`: both `-packed` cases fail at the check that the scale reaching MegaMoE equals the checkpoint scale.
- The rest of the file has 14 failures, identical on `main`. They are V4.1 / hash-routing tests that need a DeepGEMM build with `bf16_mega_gate`.

GPU checks with real DeepGEMM. Setup: the vLLM image `nightly-dev-arm64-cu130-ac9126e58aa7` plus this commit, overlaid file by file with SHA-256 gates.

| check | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Fused shared scale from checkpoint scales vs from hook-packed scales. Shapes (4096, 4096), (4096, 2048), (6144, 7168), (7168, 3072). | packed scales not converted | **bitwise identical** |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash 4-layer config (FP4 experts), MegaMoE + EP, TP1, `load_format="dummy"` | startup crash, DeepGEMM `layout.hpp:114` | starts; shared expert **fused** on all 4 layers; finite logprobs |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, real weights, `vllm serve` DP4 / EP4, MegaMoE (shared expert fused); greedy decoding, top-5 logprobs | baseline | **bit-identical** tokens and logprobs, 4/4 prompts |

`pre-commit` passes.

## Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for `MegaMoE shared expert`, `_finalize_shared_expert_weights`, `transform_weights_for_mega_moe` and `deepseek v4 dummy load mega moe`. None of them changes how the shared-expert scales are read.

title: [MRV2][Spec Decode] Quantized draft lm_head for drafters that share the target head
body:
## Overview **Decode at c=1 on SPEED-Bench goes from 39.4 to 46.5 tok/s (+18%) with average AL unchanged (-0.4%)** with an NVFP4 draft head, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 + MTP (k=3), one DGX Spark, measured on three nodes with the SM121 skinny-GEMM plans from #59753. An MTP or EAGLE drafter that shares the target's lm_head reads the whole head once per draft token; on a 248k x 2560 BF16 head that is the largest kernel in a draft step. A new opt-in key gives the drafter a private quantized copy of the head. The target still verifies with its own BF16 head, so outputs are unchanged; only the acceptance length can move. ```bash vllm serve --speculative-config \ '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "draft_lm_head_quantization": "nvfp4"}' ``` ## Claims - `"nvfp4"`: E2M1 weights with an E4M3 scale per 16 values, weight-only on the platform's W4A16 kernel, chosen by `init_nvfp4_linear_kernel` (Marlin on SM12x; activations stay BF16/FP16). `"fp8"`: per-row FP8 weights and per-token FP8 activations, reusing the existing online `Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod` on the platform FP8 kernel (`CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` on GB10). CUDA graphs and TP work (each rank quantizes its own shard). - Decode on GB10: +17.5% to +18.4% at c=1 and +9% to +11% at c=4 (NVFP4, three nodes), +10.8% / +6.5% (FP8, one node). AL within run-to-run noise, including multilingual (every row of the head stays available). GSM8K unchanged (earlier run, below). - Probabilistic drafting stays exact: the quantized logits are both sampled and used as q. - Extra memory: about 0.35 GiB (NVFP4) or 0.6 GiB (FP8) for a 248k x 2560 head, created inside model loading, so profiled KV sizing accounts for it. With `--kv-cache-memory-bytes`, leave room for it. ## Validation SPEED-Bench qualitative (11 categories at c=1 and c=4, greedy, 256 output tokens), Flash-Next, MTP k=3, real AL from the spec-decode counters, full vocabulary. Each node ran stock and the quantized head back to back; vLLM nightly `0cbac6cd1` with the skinny-GEMM plans of #59753 applied, plus this PR. ``` decode tok/s per user stock c=1 NVFP4 c=1 stock c=4 NVFP4 c=4 p4242-0121 39.42 46.63 (+18.3%) 26.61 29.46 (+10.7%) p4242-0547 39.45 46.69 (+18.4%) 26.54 29.44 (+10.9%) p4242-0122 39.36 46.24 (+17.5%) 26.55 28.95 (+9.0%) p4242-0122, FP8 head 43.61 (+10.8%) 28.28 (+6.5%) AL, mean of 3 nodes stock 2.670 NVFP4 2.658 (-0.4%) multilingual 2.799 / 2.845 ```
Earlier measurement, before #59753 (ABBA, larger gain) Without the skinny-GEMM plans the BF16 head GEMV is slower, so the same change measured +27%. Stock and NVFP4 ran in ABBA order (stock, nvfp4, nvfp4, stock) on one GB10 node (p4242-0073, median SM clock 2242 MHz); numbers are the mean of the two runs per arm. | vs. BF16 head | AL (avg) | AL (multilingual) | decode c=1 | decode c=1 (multilingual) | decode c=4 | step, forced AL 3, c=1 | GSM8K (256) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | BF16 head (stock) | 2.673 | 2.859 | 35.6 tok/s | 36.9 tok/s | 27.2 tok/s | 73.7 ms | 243 | | NVFP4 draft head | 2.664 (-0.3%) | 2.851 (-0.3%) | **45.2 tok/s (+27.1%)** | 46.7 tok/s (+26.7%) | 30.4 tok/s (+11.7%) | 58.2 ms | 243 | | FP8 draft head (separate node, own stock) | +0.2% | -0.6% | **+21.0%** | +19.1% | +9.7% | 61.6 ms | 247 vs 244 | The FP8 serving row comes from a second GB10 node (p4242-0067, 2496 MHz, 7G KV) against its own stock arm (36.1 tok/s c=1, AL 2.664); the forced-AL step times and GSM8K for stock and NVFP4 are from an earlier same-node run (p4242-0074, 2489 MHz). Forced AL 3, c=4 per-user step: 114.2 / 102.4 / 104.1 ms (stock / NVFP4 / FP8).
Kernel choice, draft head GEMV only (248320 x 2560, CUDA graph, cold L2, median of 3 x 100 replays): ``` GB200 (SM100) GB10 (SM121, M>=4) BF16 (cuBLAS) 191 to 196 us 5.50 to 5.58 ms FP8 W8A8 (selector) 111 to 113 us 2.80 to 2.84 ms <- used for "fp8" FP8 W8A16 Marlin 145 to 153 us 2.80 to 2.82 ms NVFP4 W4A16 Marlin 133 to 149 us 1.60 to 1.64 ms <- used for "nvfp4" ``` FP8 reuses the online PTPC method (platform W8A8 kernel, needs SM89+): 1.3x faster than Marlin on GB200, parity on GB10. NVFP4 picks its kernel with `init_nvfp4_linear_kernel(use_a16=True)`, so `--linear-backend`, `linear_backend_per_quant` and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` apply as for any NVFP4 linear layer. On SM100/103 the default is the CuTe DSL W4A16 kernel, which measured 1.42x slower than Marlin at M=16 on GB200; `linear_backend_per_quant={"nvfp4_w4a16": "marlin"}` selects Marlin there. Independent reproduction at TP2 on 2x DGX Spark (earlier revision, MTP k=4, [#56577 comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56577#issuecomment-5994233686)): +18.5% (fp8) and +19.5% (nvfp4) decode at c=1, greedy outputs byte-identical across arms. Disclaimers: - Greedy decoding on this model is not bit-reproducible run to run; per-category AL moves up to about 3% in either direction for stock as well. Across the three nodes above stock varies by 0.2% and NVFP4 by 1.0%. Absolute tok/s also varies across Spark nodes and recipes, so compare arms only within one node. - The gain shrinks with concurrency, where more tokens share each head read. ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_draft_lm_head.py # all passed (GB10) pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py -k draft_lm_head # 2 passed (GB10) ```
Setup Setup: vLLM nightly `0cbac6cd1` with #59753 applied (not in the earlier ABBA run), this PR and two Flash-Next serving prerequisites (#59309, #56273); `local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` @ada4da32, FP8 KV cache, `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 7G` (8G in the earlier ABBA run), `--max-model-len 49152`, `--max-num-seqs 8`, MTP drafter MoE on Marlin. Every arm used the same settings.
## Details - Design: the quantization lives with the other online quantization methods, in `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/lm_head.py`. `quantized_lm_head_copy()` builds a plain `ParallelLMHead` with that quant method and quantizes it straight from this rank's shard of the target head, so no bf16 copy is made and the target head is unchanged. FP8 reuses the existing `Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod`; NVFP4 adds a small weight-only method (`_LMHeadNvfp4Method`) that quantizes the head and hands it to the selected W4A16 kernel. `ParallelLMHead` gains an optional `quant_method` argument, which `VocabParallelEmbedding` already has. vllm-ascend overrides `ParallelLMHead.__init__` without this argument, so the soft-fail Ascend NPU interface check flags it; on Ascend, `draft_lm_head_quantization` needs the override updated. `"nvfp4"` needs a CUDA W4A16 kernel, so on ROCm only `"fp8"` is available and the tests skip the nvfp4 cases there. - Hook: `load_eagle_model` gives the drafter that head instead of the shared target head, including the MTP per-layer `shared_head.head`. - Derived state: the copy is kept out of layerwise reload and re-derived in place from the target head whenever the target's weights are replaced (`reload_weights`, weight transfer), so sleep mode, weight reload and weight transfer keep working. During a draft-only weight update the drafter shares the target head again, as on main, and the copy is re-derived when the update finishes. - Scope: MRV2 drafters loaded through `load_eagle_model` (EAGLE, EAGLE3, MTP) that share an unquantized fp16/bf16 lm_head running in the model dtype; other cases are rejected at config validation or load. Gemma-4 MTP is excluded because it scores a subset of its tied embedding rows directly and has no shared lm_head. DFlash and DSpark can call the same helper in a follow-up. - Not a duplicate: #56577 (Qwen4Exp only, env var, eager only) and #47584 (DSpark only, env var) add an FP8 draft head for one model or method; this is the generic version behind one config key, with CUDA graphs and NVFP4. #59740 (reduced draft vocabulary) composes with it; both add a draft-head key to `speculative_config` and hook the same place in `load_eagle_model`, so whichever lands second will reuse this quantizer for the list rows (as `draft_token_map_quantization` there) rather than add a second one. #41000, #42124 and #58343 concern heads quantized in the checkpoint, and the online quantization framework (#51285) covers linear and MoE layers but not `ParallelLMHead`. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the code, tests and benchmark harness; I reviewed every changed line and ran the measurements above.
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
**Reproduction on upstream main (DGX Spark, GB10)** Upstream main 02b83919aa with the heads of #59958, #59973, #59740, #60068 and #54614 merged, no other runtime patches. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4, MTP 6 with confidence stop 0.6, sparse draft head via `draft_token_map` (32k ids, 16384 dynamic rows at rank 256, `draft_token_map_quantization: nvfp4`), FP8 KV, `host_file_gather` PLE tables. SPEED-Bench throughput 2K in / 1K out, fixed OSL, c=1, n=20: | Build | tok/s/user | AL | GSM8K-256 | |---|---|---|---| | upstream main + these PRs | 49.94 | 2.68 | 249/256 | | our internal stack, same node | 49.73 | 2.65 | 245/256 | The PR route reproduces the internal stack result within noise.

title: [Bugfix] Fix Mamba page size AssertionError with spec decoding on GraniteMoeHybrid, FalconH1 and Zamba2
body:
## Overview

This fixes the `AssertionError` in `MambaSpec.page_size_bytes` that stops the engine at startup. It happens when `GraniteMoeHybridForCausalLM` (for example `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny`) runs with speculative decoding and `num_speculative_tokens=2`. The config-time Mamba state shape now counts the speculative tokens, the same way the layer does. `FalconH1ForCausalLM` and `Zamba2ForCausalLM` had the same one-line gap and get the same fix.

Fixes #57721

## Claims

- `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny` with ngram speculative decoding and `num_speculative_tokens=2` now starts. Before this fix, it failed during KV cache setup with `AssertionError` at `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py:1075`.
- `GraniteMoeHybridForCausalLM`, `FalconH1ForCausalLM` and `Zamba2ForCausalLM` now pass `num_spec=vllm_config.num_speculative_tokens` in `get_mamba_state_shape_from_config`. `Mamba2ForCausalLM` and `NemotronHForCausalLM` already do this.
- A new unit test checks the config-time shape of these three models when speculative tokens are set.

## Validation

Setup: 1 × NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3. vLLM at commit `18f8f96025b556071eb627076f94df560fbd3a22` (`0.30.1rc1.dev630+g18f8f9602`), editable install. This PR is one commit on top of that commit.

Reproducer (`repro.py`), from the issue:

```python
from vllm import LLM
print('=== Starting LLM with num_speculative_tokens=2 ===')
llm = LLM(
    model='ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny',
    max_model_len=4096,
    speculative_config={
        'method': 'ngram',
        'num_speculative_tokens': 2,
        'prompt_lookup_max': 4,
        'prompt_lookup_min': 2,
    },
)
print('=== LLM started successfully ===')
```

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 python repro.py
```

| Tree | Runs | `AssertionError` | Engine started | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `18f8f96` (before) | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| this PR (after) | 2 | 0 | 2 |

The same crash also happens with the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image at the same commit.

Before:

```
(EngineCore pid=217923) INFO 10-04 21:20:48 [interface.py:970] Setting attention block size to 400 tokens to ensure that attention page size is >= mamba page size.
(EngineCore pid=217923) INFO 10-04 21:20:48 [interface.py:994] Padding mamba page size by 1.59% to ensure that mamba page size and attention page size are exactly equal.
...
  File ".../vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py", line 1075, in page_size_bytes
    assert self.page_size_padded >= page_size
AssertionError
...
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}
```

After (exit code 0):

```
(EngineCore pid=225256) INFO 10-04 21:36:57 [interface.py:970] Setting attention block size to 416 tokens to ensure that attention page size is >= mamba page size.
(EngineCore pid=225256) INFO 10-04 21:36:57 [interface.py:994] Padding mamba page size by 3.94% to ensure that mamba page size and attention page size are exactly equal.
(EngineCore pid=225256) INFO 10-04 21:37:28 [core.py:373] init engine (profile, create kv cache, warmup model) took 31.43 s (compilation: 0.61 s)
=== LLM started successfully ===
```

Unit test: `test_mamba2_config_state_shape_includes_speculative_tokens` in `tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends_selection.py`.

- With the fix: 3 passed.
- With the three model lines reverted: 3 failed, each with `assert ((3, 288), (8, 32, 16)) == ((5, 288), (8, 32, 16))`.

The test was run with `--noconftest`, because the local env had no `tblib` and could not load `tests/conftest.py`. The test uses no fixtures. `pre-commit run --files` passes on the four changed files, including `mypy` and the check that new tests are wired into Buildkite CI.

## Details

Root cause: vLLM plans the Mamba page size at config time and checks it against the real page at runtime. For these models, the planned page and the real page used different conv state shapes.

- `Platform._align_hybrid_block_size` (`vllm/platforms/interface.py`) sizes the padded Mamba page from `get_mamba_state_shape_from_config`. That function did not pass `num_spec`, so the planned conv state for granite-4.0-h-tiny was `(3, 3328)`.
- At runtime, each `MambaMixer2` layer builds its spec from `get_state_shape()`, and that function does pass `num_spec`. So the real conv state is `(5, 3328)`.
- The real page is 13312 bytes bigger than the planned page (3328 × 2 tokens × 2 bytes). Rounding up the attention block size only leaves 12800 bytes of slack. So the real page (819712 bytes) is bigger than the padded page (819200 bytes), and `assert self.page_size_padded >= page_size` fails. With 1 speculative token the gap is only 6656 bytes and fits in the slack. This is why the crash starts at 2 tokens.

Temporary debug prints of the planned shape and the real shape confirmed this. They also showed that the padding arithmetic was correct for the shape it was given: 400 × 2048 = 819200 ≥ 806400. The prints are not in this PR.

#33726 added `num_spec` to `MambaMixer2.get_state_shape` and to the config-time shapes of `Mamba2ForCausalLM` and `NemotronHForCausalLM`. It did not add it to the other three models that use `MambaMixer2`. Only these five models use `MambaMixer2`, so with this PR all five plan the same shape that the layer builds. The assert, the padding logic and the layer are not changed. Now the planner sees the real page size, so it picks an attention block size of 416 tokens (3.94% Mamba padding) instead of 400 tokens (1.59%).

Limitations:

- FalconH1 and Zamba2 get the same one-line fix, but only the unit test checks them. They were not run end to end.
- The reproducer only starts the engine. No generation was run.
- The config-time shape in `vllm/model_executor/models/lfm2.py` does not pass `num_spec`, but `ShortConv.get_state_shape` does. This may be the same kind of mismatch. It is outside this PR and was not tested.

title: [Bugfix] Keep force-killing the process tree when a child exits mid-walk
body:
## Overview

Fix a regression from #52314: `kill_process_tree` stops early, leaving the rest of the tree and the target alive, when a child exits between `parent.children()` and `child.name()`.

## Claims

- `kill_process_tree` now SIGKILLs every remaining descendant and the target pid even if a child is reaped while it walks the tree.
- Before this change, `psutil.NoSuchProcess` escaped the function. Callers such as `vllm/v1/utils.py::shutdown()` then abandoned their loop over the remaining processes, so EngineCores, API servers or workers that were meant to be force-killed survived.

## Validation

The new test `tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py::test_kill_process_tree_skips_child_that_exits_mid_walk`:
- starts four real processes and makes `children()` report three of them as the target's children;
- ends one of the three with SIGTERM and reaps it before `kill_process_tree` runs, so psutil's own `name()` raises `NoSuchProcess` for it;
- asserts that this child exited from that SIGTERM, and that the other two children and the target exit with SIGKILL.

Results on Linux (base `04462732a4`, Python 3.12):

| psutil | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 6.1.0 (pinned in vLLM's CUDA/CPU test requirements) | fails: `NoSuchProcess: process no longer exists`, from `child.name()` | passes |
| 7.2.2 (latest; pinned in vLLM's ROCm/XPU test requirements) | fails: same | passes |

- `pytest tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py`: 5 passed with each psutil version. The new test also passed 30 runs in a row with each.
- `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual` (the stage CI runs) passes on the changed files, including ruff, typos and mypy.

## Details

**Root cause.** #52314 added `logger.warning(..., child.name(), child.pid)` inside the existing `contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError)`. On Linux, `psutil.Process.name()` re-reads `/proc/<pid>/stat` on every call; only Windows caches it. Once the child has been reaped it raises `NoSuchProcess`, which is not a `ProcessLookupError`. Before #52314 the loop only read `child.pid`, which only returns the stored pid, so this path could not raise.

**Why the window is real.** The force-kill path runs when a process did not exit within its grace period. Typically that process is still tearing down and reaping its own children, for example EngineCore joining its workers after SIGTERM, so a child listed by `children()` can be gone by the time `name()` runs.

**Fix.** Also suppress `NoSuchProcess` for that child. The child is already gone, so it needs no SIGKILL, and skipping it avoids signalling a pid that may have been recycled. This matches the existing `psutil.NoSuchProcess` guard at the top of the same function and `vllm/entrypoints/launchers/dp_supervisor.py`.

**Affected callers.**
- `vllm/v1/utils.py::shutdown()`, used by `CoreEngineProcManager`, `APIServerProcessManager` and the DP coordinator.
- `vllm/v1/utils.py::_shutdown_subprocesses()`, used by `RustFrontendProcessManager`.
- `dp_supervisor.py` already suppresses the exception, but before this fix it silently skipped killing the rest of the tree.

**Not a duplicate.** I found no issue or PR that reports or fixes this. I searched `kill_process_tree`, `NoSuchProcess` and "force killing sub process" for anything after #52314 was merged on 2026-09-30.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find this, write the patch and the test, and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: [Bugfix] Keep GateLinear batch invariant under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
body:
## Overview

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, MoE models whose gate uses `GateLinear`'s specialized router GEMM tiers are not batch invariant. I found this while validating models for #27433 on NVIDIA GB300: `zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air`, `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2` and `baidu/ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B-PT` all fail the batch-invariance suite. This PR makes `GateLinear` use the batch-invariant linear path in that mode.

## Claims

- GLM-4.5-Air, MiniMax-M2 and ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B pass the full batch-invariance suite on GB300 (22/22 each). Without the fix they fail 12, 16 and 6 of the 22 tests.
- New regression test `tests/v1/determinism/test_gate_linear_batch_invariant.py` fails without the fix on both Blackwell and Ampere and passes with it.
- No change when `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is off.

## Validation

NVIDIA GB300 (SM 10.3), driver 580.167.08, CUDA toolkit 13.1, torch 2.13.0+cu130, vLLM `f590eb2448` (`gate_linear.py` is unchanged between that commit and this PR's base).

**Model level.** Each test id of `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py` run in its own process:

```bash
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=<model> VLLM_TP_SIZE=<tp> VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=<tp> \
  pytest -p no:rerunfailures "tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::<test id>"
```

| Model | GPUs (TP) | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air` | 2 | 12 failed, 10 passed | 22 passed |
| `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2` | 2 | 16 failed, 6 passed | 22 passed |
| `baidu/ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B-PT` | 1 | 6 failed, 16 passed | 22 passed |

What fails without the fix:

- All three: the 6 needle tests (`Nondeterministic outputs detected`, 2 to 5 of 5 trials).
- GLM-4.5-Air and MiniMax-M2: the 6 `bs1_vs_bsN` bitwise tests (`Batch invariance violated` in 30 to 32 of 32 prompts).
- MiniMax-M2 only: the 3 ragged chunked-prefill tests and the decode/prefill logprob test (49 mismatches).

GLM-4.5-Air also fails the needle test at TP=1 (4 of 5 trials), so this is not a tensor-parallel effect. MiniMax-M2 used `VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.9`. For MiniMax-M2 and ERNIE the before and after runs were on two identical GB300 nodes at the same commit, one unmodified and one with this change.

Models whose results do not change: `Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B` passes the suite without the fix (its gate does not use the specialized tiers). `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1` pass the needle and bitwise tests with and without it.

**Unit level.** `pytest tests/v1/determinism/test_gate_linear_batch_invariant.py`:

| GPU | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA GB300 (SM 10.3) | 10 failed, 2 passed | 12 passed |
| NVIDIA A10 (SM 8.6) | 6 failed, 6 passed | 12 passed |

**No regression with the mode off.** `tests/kernels/test_ll_bf16_gemm.py` and `tests/kernels/test_gate_linear_rocm_dispatch.py` give 19 passed, 136 skipped both before and after (A10). `pre-commit` passes.

## Details

**Root cause.** `UnquantizedLinearMethod.apply` is where `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is honored for linear layers (it calls `linear_batch_invariant`). `GateLinear.forward` returns from tiers 1 to 4 before reaching it. Those tiers also dispatch on the number of tokens:

- tier 1 (`ll_bf16_gemm`) is used for `M <= 16`, otherwise the cuBLAS `out_dtype` tier;
- tier 2 (fp32 kernel) is used for `M <= 32`, otherwise BF16x3 or `F.linear`;
- tier 3 (BF16x3) picks its tile size and split-K from the token count in `_pick_tile_config`.

So the router logits of one row can come from a different kernel, or a different K-reduction order, depending on how many tokens share the batch. A small difference in the logits can change the selected experts, which then changes logprobs and tokens. GLM-4.5-Air and ERNIE-4.5 have fp32 gates that take the BF16x3 tier on Blackwell; MiniMax-M2's gate shape (3072 x 256) also has the fp32 kernel, so it switches kernels at `M = 32`.

To localize it I compared the same prompt alone and inside a mixed batch on GLM-4.5-Air. Disabling fused grouped top-k did not restore bitwise-equal logprobs; disabling the `GateLinear` tiers did.

These tiers were added between June and September (#46385, #42562, #47973, #55899), and #58234 moved all MoE models to `GateLinear`, after most of the batch-invariance model validation was done.

**Fix.** The tier eligibility flags are now false when `envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is set, so `forward` falls through to tier 5 (`ReplicatedLinear`), which uses the batch-invariant matmul. The flags are also what `set_out_dtype` and the kernel warmup read, so warmup for the unused kernels is skipped too.

**Cost.** In batch-invariant mode the gate no longer uses the specialized kernels. Median time of one `GateLinear.forward` call on GB300 (bf16 input, 200 iterations after warmup):

| Gate (hidden x experts) | M | Specialized tiers | Batch-invariant path |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| fp32, 3072 x 256 | 1 | 54 us | 139 us |
| fp32, 3072 x 256 | 1024 | 134 us | 145 us |
| fp32, 4096 x 128 | 1 | 105 us | 146 us |
| fp32, 4096 x 128 | 1024 | 98 us | 155 us |
| bf16 with fp32 output, 7168 x 256 | 1 | 73 us | 131 us |
| bf16 with fp32 output, 7168 x 256 | 1024 | 72 us | 133 us |

That is 1.1x to 2.7x per call, between 10 and 90 microseconds, and only when the mode is on. I disabled all four tiers because that is the configuration I validated. If a tier can be shown to be batch invariant on its own, it could be re-enabled separately.

**CI.** The new test is added to the H100 and B200 Batch Invariance jobs, where the specialized tiers exist.

**Related.** #57016 and #57092 are about batch invariance of the MoE experts, a different component.

**AI assistance.** Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). I reviewed every changed line and the test logs.

title: [Model][GLM-5.3-Flash] Warm up the DCP top-k merge kernels for the kpool indexer
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #59211 (now merged; this branch is rebased on main).

Under DCP, the GLM-5.x kpool indexer merges the per-rank top-k with `_merge_dcp_topk_global`, which runs `PackDCPTopkCandidatesKernel` and `StableTopKFromGatheredCandidatesKernel`. Only `SparseAttnIndexer.__init__` registers these kernels for JIT warmup, so with the kpool indexer they were compiled on the first long-context request:

```
WARNING [jit_monitor.py:140] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: PackDCPTopkCandidatesKernel.kernel. This causes a latency spike; consider extending warmup to cover this shape/config.
```

This PR registers them from `SparseAttnIndexerKpool.__init__` under the same conditions: DCP > 1, JIT warmup enabled, CUDA, and CuteDSL available. #59211 already makes the warmup keys use pool-level top-k and interleave for kpool models.

## Test Plan

`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` on 8×H100 with `vllm serve`, bf16 KV cache, no MTP. TP8 + DCP8 with `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4`, compared with TP8. GSM8K (1319 questions) at 5, 25, 50 and 100 shots, i.e. prompts from about 650 to about 17k tokens. Checked the server log for JIT monitor warnings.

## Test Result

`PackDCPTopkCandidatesKernel` no longer compiles during inference under DCP8. Without this change, it compiled during inference in the same setup. The other JIT warnings in the log (`fused_moe_kernel`, kpool compress kernels) also appear without DCP and are unrelated.

| Shots | TP8 | TP8 + DCP8 |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 0.918 | 0.920 |
| 25 | 0.914 | 0.917 |
| 50 | 0.911 | 0.911 |
| 100 | 0.917 | 0.921 |

The E2E runs used the same local SM90 FlashMLA bf16 DCP change as #59211, which Hopper needs for DCP at head_dim 512.

## Duplicate check

I searched open PRs for kpool / `SparseAttnIndexerKpool` / `PackDCPTopkCandidates` warmup and found none. #54345 deals with prefill metadata JIT, not the DCP top-k merge kernels.

## AI assistance

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed the change and ran the tests above.

title: [Core][Mamba] Remove leftovers of mamba_cache_mode="all"
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Follow-up to #58997. Removes what was left of `mamba_cache_mode="all"` and deprecates `--mamba-cache-mode`, which no longer has any effect.

## Changes

- **KV cache manager:** `MambaManager` asserts that prefix caching runs only with `mamba_cache_mode="align"`. A `"none"` group under a caching manager used to silently run all-mode dense caching. Production never pairs them: `MambaModelConfig` ties `"align"` to prefix caching on and `"none"` to off.
- **CLI:** deprecated `--mamba-cache-mode`. `MambaModelConfig` already overwrote any user value (`"align"` iff prefix caching is on), so the flag is now ignored with a warning and will be removed in v0.33.0. ReplaySSM/RecoverSSM errors, config docstrings, docs, CI configs and e2e tests now refer to prefix caching instead of the flag.
- **Kernels:** dropped the APC per-block state inputs from Triton `causal_conv1d_fn` / `causal_conv1d_update`. No caller used them, and the non-APC path is unchanged. XPU is untouched.
  - Two all-mode leftovers are kept on purpose:
    - SSD's `return_intermediate_states`: #57329 uses it for Mamba2 internal prefill checkpoints.
    - CUDA `selective_scan_fwd`'s per-block state outputs: Mamba1 internal checkpoints will need mid-prefill state output from that kernel.
  - Conv-window checkpoints do not need the `causal_conv1d` inputs, because they are written from the pre-conv input.
- **Models:** removed the `supports_mamba_prefix_caching` flag. Its only reader was the all → align fallback deleted in #58997. Dropped the `SupportsMambaPrefixCaching` base from hybrid models, since `IsHybrid` already declares `get_mamba_state_copy_func(s)`. Only attention-free `Mamba`/`Mamba2` keep it.
- **Docs/comments:** fixed stale all-mode descriptions.
- **Tests:**
  - Mamba prefix-caching tests use `"align"`. `req0` is split so align keeps a state at the shared prefix.
  - Dropped `test_mamba_shared_prefix_survives_zero_retention`. Its flow is covered by `test_mamba_shared_prefix_reuse_under_zero_retention`.
  - The simple-offload DCP geometry test uses a replicated attention group.
  - `test_p_side_chunked_prefill_mamba` runs without prefix caching.
  - Fixed `test_mixer2_gated_norm_multi_gpu`, which also failed on `main`: its spawned workers had no vLLM config.

## Compatibility

- `ModelConfig.supports_mamba_prefix_caching` is removed. A leftover `supports_mamba_prefix_caching` class attribute is ignored.
- `--mamba-cache-mode` / `EngineArgs.mamba_cache_mode` is deprecated: ignored with a warning, removed in v0.33.0. Behavior is unchanged for Mamba models, since the value was already overwritten. `CacheConfig.mamba_cache_mode` stays and is still derived from `enable_prefix_caching`.

## Validation

GB200:

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py   # 560 passed, 2 skipped
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k mamba     # 18 passed
pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py tests/test_config.py   # 546 passed, 5 skipped
```

`EngineArgs(model="Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B", ...).create_engine_config()`: no flag → `align`; `mamba_cache_mode="none"` with prefix caching → deprecation warning, `align`; `mamba_cache_mode="align"` without prefix caching → `none`.

Not a duplicate: no open PR covers these #58997 leftovers.

title: [Model][DeepSeek-V4.1] Permute mega-attention wq_b / wo_a while loading
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

DeepSeek-V4.1's FlashMLA mega attention (the SM100 default) permutes `wq_b` rows and `wo_a` columns into the kernel's layout as a post-load step. That step is only correct when it runs before the linear quant hooks. This PR does the permutation in the weight loaders instead, so it no longer depends on post-load order. It is a prerequisite for #57733.

## Claims

- Fixes the DSv4.1 dummy-load startup crash on SM100 (DP4: `IndexError: index 1280 ...`; TP4: a size-mismatch `RuntimeError`).
- Fixes `reload_weights` (layerwise reload) for mega attention. On `main` the reloaded `wq_b` / `wo_a` are written in checkpoint order and `_fused_layouts_ready` skips the permutation, so accuracy collapses. Layerwise reload replays the loaders recorded at model init, so with this PR the reloaded shards are permuted again.
- Real loads are unchanged: after a TP4 cold load, checksums of every parameter and buffer (1605 per rank, after the quant hooks) match `main` on all 4 ranks.
- Removes `finalize_loaded_weights`, `_fused_layouts_ready`, `finalize_mega_attn_weights` and DSpark's `_finalize_attn` (+62 / −94).

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, real weights, `vllm serve`, GB200, mega attention (`FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41`, confirmed in the logs). GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy. MegaMoE unless noted.

| config | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| DP4 / EP4, mega attention | 0.892 | 0.896 |
| TP4 / EP4, mega attention | 0.910 | 0.911 |
| TP4 / EP4, default MoE backend: GSM8K, `reload_weights`, GSM8K | 0.897 → **0.000** | 0.906 → **0.898** |
| DP4 / EP4 + DSpark k=5: GSM8K, draft acceptance | 0.892, 51% | 0.896, 51% |
| DP4 / EP4, `--load-format dummy` | startup crash: `IndexError: index 1280 is out of bounds for dimension 0 with size 1280` | starts, serves a completion |
| TP4 / EP4, `--load-format dummy` | startup crash: `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (327680) must match the size of tensor b (1280)` | starts, serves a completion |

With MegaMoE, `reload_weights` collapses on both arms for a separate reason: the model-level post-load step (MegaMoE and mHC state) is not rerun after the layerwise reload finishes. #57733 reruns it; with #57733 and this PR, the same TP4 MegaMoE reload measures 0.901 → 0.898, while #57733 without this PR measures 0.900 → 0.002. The DP4 reload is not measurable on any arm: layerwise reload re-materializes the CPU-offloaded Engram table on the GPU and runs out of memory (pre-existing).

`tests/kernels/test_dsv41_mega_attn_layouts.py`: 2 passed. It loads `wq_b` / `wo_a` and their MXFP8 scales through the permuting loader and checks the permuted GEMMs against a reference that permutes the activation instead.

`pre-commit` passes.

Setup: the vLLM image `nightly-dev-arm64-cu130-ac9126e58aa7` plus this commit, overlaid file by file with SHA-256 gates.

## Details

**Root cause.** `permute_wq_b_` derives `head_dim` from `weight.shape[0]`. After the CuteDSL linear hook, `wq_b` is transposed to `[K, N]`, so `head_dim` is wrong and `q_fused_permutation` indexes out of bounds. The `wo_a` BMM hook likewise reshapes `wo_a` to 3D and packs its scales. A real load calls the permutation from inside `load_weights`, before the hooks, so it works there. A dummy load never calls `load_weights`. The model-level `process_weights_after_loading` then runs after the hooks and crashes.

**Fix.** `permute_on_load(param, perm, dim)` wraps the parameter's `weight_loader` with `composed_weight_loader`, so each loaded shard is gathered into the fused layout right after it is written. The wrapping happens in `DeepseekV4MegaAttnAttention.__init__`, for `wq_b.weight`, `wq_b.weight_scale`, `wo_a.weight` and `wo_a.weight_scale`. Each of these tensors is loaded by a single `weight_loader` call (no stacked mapping), so the whole local shard is present when the permutation runs. The quant hooks then see already-permuted tensors, exactly as `main`'s real load does.

The permutations are computed from the module's own `n_local_heads` / `head_dim` instead of tensor shapes. `n_local_heads // n_local_groups == WV_GROUP_SIZE` is already enforced in `__init__`.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs for `mega attention wq_b`, `DeepSeek-V4.1 dummy load`, `fused_layout permute`, `finalize_loaded_weights` and `V4.1 mega attn`. #57977 touches `flash_mla_mega_attn.py` for MXFP8 activations but does not change the weight permutation.

**AI assistance.** Written with Claude Code. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and GPU checks above.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Honor speculative cacheability in SimpleCPU
body:
## Overview

Fix lost CPU prefix-cache reuse during speculative decoding with eager `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`. Share the GPU coordinator's per-group cacheability rule with CPU store selection, and pass the configured prefill lookahead to the CPU coordinator.

Related: #54736, which is already merged and provides the underlying per-group offload geometry.

## Claims

- Prevent the CPU store cursor from permanently skipping blocks whose trailing KV is still re-prefillable during multi-module MTP.
- Preserve the extra cached draft block required by hybrid speculative prefix lookup.
- Preserve existing GPU cache-publication behavior by extracting its eligibility calculation into a shared helper.

## Validation

[Complete public reproducer, exact model config, patches, commands, and structured before/after records](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217).

Both GPU A/B cases use native `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM` with a reduced config and **dummy weights**, three MTP modules, BF16, TP2/DCP2, model runner V2, a 64-token prefill budget, and real GPU/CPU transfers. The before/after columns compare separate unpatched and patched engines. Full reuse means matching that prompt's GPU-reusable prefix; block alignment and speculative cache-safety rules leave a suffix to recompute.

### Serial: the missing block persists across two CPU replays

Run one prompt at a time (`max_num_seqs=1`). For each prompt, clear both caches initially, then run **cold → reset GPU cache only → CPU replay 1 → reset GPU cache only → CPU replay 2 → GPU-hot control**. CPU caching survives both intermediate resets.

| Prompt tokens | CPU replay | GPU-hot reuse, both arms | CPU before | CPU after |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8,257 | 1 | 8,064 | 8,064 | 8,064 |
| 8,257 | 2 | 8,064 | 8,064 | 8,064 |
| 8,321 | 1 | 8,192 | **8,064** | **8,192** |
| 8,321 | 2 | 8,192 | **8,064** | **8,192** |

Both CPU replays have **zero local GPU-cache hits** in both arms. The unpatched 8,321-token case stays one effective 128-token block short on the second CPU replay; the later 8,192-token GPU-hot hit is a separate local-cache control. Output token IDs match across all four phases and both arms (16 request outputs).

Raw records and checked summary: [`serial-before.jsonl`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-serial-before-jsonl), [`serial-after.jsonl`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-serial-after-jsonl), and [`serial-comparison.json`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-serial-comparison-json).

### Concurrent: uneven prefill chunks can eliminate CPU reuse

Submit both prompts together (`max_num_seqs=2`). They share the 64-token prefill budget with `long_prefill_token_threshold=63`, allowing uneven 63/1-token chunks. Each arm runs **cold → reset GPU cache only → CPU replay → GPU-hot control**. Each row below identifies a different prompt in the same concurrent batch.

| Prompt tokens | GPU-hot reuse, both arms | CPU replay before | CPU replay after |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8,257 | 8,064 | 8,064 | 8,064 |
| 8,321 | 8,192 | **0** | **8,192** |

The 8,257-token prompt is an unaffected control: its 8,064-token CPU hit already matches its full GPU-reusable prefix. The 8,321-token prompt reproduces the bug: CPU reuse is zero before the fix and reaches its full 8,192-token reusable prefix afterward.

CPU replay has **zero local GPU-cache hits** in both arms. Output token IDs match across all three phases and both arms (12 request outputs). The later GPU-hot control cannot warm the earlier CPU replay.

Raw records and checked summary: [`concurrent-before.jsonl`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-concurrent-before-jsonl), [`concurrent-after.jsonl`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-concurrent-after-jsonl), and [`concurrent-comparison.json`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-concurrent-comparison-json).

### Environment and additional checks

- **GPU environment:** 2× B200, driver 580.126.20; public image `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:584c6bc58f76411936e0f22a37039e436019e155ae144c017b7eebbe2edc1d4e`; vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev648+g92044241a`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`. Only the two production files in this PR are patched in the fixed arm. They are identical at the image's source revision and the PR base `30d4032363d4a1f6412d9a235049673b41309f98`.
- **New CPU regression on the PR base:** baseline **12 failed / 6 passed**; patched **18 passed**, included in the **78/78** passing offload scheduler tests. The matrix covers replicated SWA, replicated full-attention, and sharded full-attention drafts; dense/latest-only retention; small/large chunks and multi-token prefill lookahead. It checks GPU/CPU hit equivalence and the loaded block hashes using real cache managers with simulated transfer completion.
- **Existing prefix-cache coverage:** **31 passed**, selecting EAGLE, cache publication, retention, and per-group DCP tests.
- **Code checks:** all applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy 3.10, and CI test tethering; the additional mypy 3.12 check and `git diff --check` passed.
- The added cases extend the existing offload scheduler suite already run by `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`.

The tables report one serial A/B and one concurrent A/B. They establish cache/transfer consistency, not trained-model accuracy or production throughput. Elapsed times include warmup effects and are not used to claim a speedup. Both cases exercise sharded MTP; replicated SWA is covered by the CPU matrix. A trained-model accuracy evaluation is not included.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

Download the linked gist into a fresh directory for each case. This command selects the concurrent case:

```bash
mkdir -p models/tiny_mtp
cp config.json models/tiny_mtp/config.json
docker run --rm --gpus '"device=0,1"' --ipc=host \
  -e REPRO_CASE=concurrent \
  -v "$PWD:/repro" --entrypoint bash \
  vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:584c6bc58f76411936e0f22a37039e436019e155ae144c017b7eebbe2edc1d4e \
  -lc 'REPRO_ROOT=/repro bash /repro/run_in_container.sh'
```

For the serial case, run the same command in another fresh gist directory with `-e REPRO_CASE=serial`. It runs both CPU replays with a GPU-only reset before each. Each invocation uses a fresh container so the baseline starts from the stock package.

The measured run used this image through Enroot; the equivalent Docker launcher above has not itself been run. The scripts and comparison logic are the measured versions. No checkpoint download is required. The wrapper enables serialization for its own offline layout-inspection RPC and starts no HTTP server.

CPU commands run on the PR checkout (`GIST_DIR` points to the downloaded gist containing the upstream logging fixtures; dependencies and the public OPT-125M config used by the existing test fixture are already installed):

```bash
# Run with only regression.patch applied to reproduce the baseline failures.
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" VLLM_PLUGINS='' HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py -q \
  -k test_dcp_draft_offload_preserves_prefix --tb=short
# Baseline: 12 failed, 6 passed.

# Run with the full fix applied.
PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$GIST_DIR" VLLM_PLUGINS='' HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \

```

Code checks (with the three changed files staged):

```bash

  mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \

  vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py \
  vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py
git diff --check
```

</details>

## Details

Eager CPU selection currently rounds confirmed tokens to a common alignment. This can disagree with GPU cacheability in two ways:

1. Multi-module MTP keeps `num_prefill_lookahead - 1` trailing tokens re-prefillable. A block can fall inside the CPU scan before the GPU has hashed it. Selection skips it as not hashed but advances the persistent store cursor, so it is never revisited after finalization. A missing early block can collapse the reusable CPU prefix to zero.
2. Hybrid speculative lookup matches an extra draft block and then drops it. GPU publication already allows this block past the aligned boundary, but CPU selection truncates it away, losing otherwise reusable prefix length.

`get_num_cacheable_tokens()` extracts the existing GPU eligibility calculation. GPU publication and eager CPU selection now use it, including the per-group draft-block rule. The CPU coordinator also receives `num_prefill_lookahead_tokens`, so both sides agree on finalization. This adds no GPU synchronization and does not change model computation.

**Duplicate-work check:** #54736 fixes geometry/fine-grained offload support, not this speculative eligibility mismatch. #58413 changes align-mode Mamba chunks in the separate `OffloadingConnector`; #54979 concerns terminal GPU cache registration; #50897 proposes a broader successor-aware hash/publication protocol. None implements this `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` store-boundary fix. Searches for open SimpleCPU/speculative offload fixes found no equivalent PR.

title: [Model][MoE] Load MegaMoE experts directly into the DeepGEMM layout
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE (also used by Kimi-K3) loads the routed experts into loader-side parameters, then `finalize_weights` asks the `DeepGemmMegaMoEBackend` (#58053) to transform them into DeepGEMM's layout and drops the loaded parameters, so any later `load_weights` has nowhere to write. The fused shared expert is built the same way, from a shared MLP whose weights the fusion then takes over.

This PR moves the layout into load time. The backend is selected when the experts are constructed, registers the kernel-layout tensors as the parameters (`create_weights`), and writes each checkpoint shard straight into them (`load_weight`). Whether the shared expert is fused is also decided at construction. Loading, reloading and updating weights then write into the tensors the kernel reads, and there is no MegaMoE post-load step left: `finalize_weights`, `finalize_mega_moe_weights` and the post-load hooks that only called them are removed (DeepSeek-V4 keeps its mHC hook).

## Claims

- `reload_weights` works with MegaMoE. DeepSeek-V4-Flash GSM8K after a reload: `main` 0.948 → 0.008, this PR 0.951 → 0.948.
- DeepSeek-V4.1 (MXFP8 shared expert) keeps its fused shared expert across a reload: `main` 0.898 → 0.010, this PR 0.904 → 0.901.
- An identity reload changes no parameter and moves no storage (0 of 1588 per-rank checksums, DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP2).
- The shared expert has no second copy: its four kernel tensors are the parameters (DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP2: 76.6 GiB, same as `main`).
- Kimi-K3 drops its `finalize_weights` override and the `_mega_l*` buffers.

## Validation

GB200, real weights, `vllm serve`, `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, EP. GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy.

| model, parallelism | `main`: GSM8K → `reload_weights` → GSM8K | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP2, MTP k=2 | 0.948 → **0.008** | 0.951 → 0.948 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4 | 0.898 → **0.010** | 0.904 → 0.901 |
| Kimi-K3 (1.5T MXFP4), 4 nodes, TP4 × DP4, EP16 | 0.944 → 0.950, 137.52 GiB | 0.949 → 0.937 and 0.945 → 0.954 (two runs), 137.52 GiB |

The `main` column was measured before #58053; #58053 moved the transform into the backend but kept the post-load transform that drops the loaded parameters. On `main`, Kimi-K3 survives this reload only because the checkpoint is the same: its `finalize_weights` returns early once transformed experts exist, so reloaded expert weights never reach the kernels.

Neither DeepSeek run logs the shared-expert fusion fallback warning, so both keep the fused shared expert.

`tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py` (68 passed on GB200):
- Shuffled, per-shard routed loads (with EPLB replicas) are compared against DeepGEMM's batched transform, including the real DeepGEMM CUDA transform.
- A second routed load updates the kernel tensors in place.
- Shared-expert shards (gate, up, down; weights and 1x32 scales, both `.w2.` and `.down_proj.` names) land where DeepGEMM's transform puts them; reloading one shard overwrites in place and leaves the other half alone; the returned names are the registered parameters (for `enable_weights_track`).
- The fusion decision at construction: fused for DeepSeek-V4-Flash (e8m0 128x128) and V4.1 (uint8 1x32) scales; not fused for an older DeepGEMM, BF16 shared experts, non-UE8M0 scales or scales that do not tile to 1x32.

`tests/models/kimi_k3/test_weight_loading.py` is removed: it only checked that the removed Kimi-K3 finalize ran once.

`pre-commit` passes.

Setup: the vLLM image `nightly-dev-arm64-cu130-ac9126e58aa7` plus this change, overlaid file by file with SHA-256 gates.

Reviews: Codex (gpt-6-astra), Kimi K3 and Claude Fable 5.1 audited this change. The two Codex should-fix findings (backend chosen for GPU 0 when the model is built on `meta` under `ipc_cache`; fused shared parameters reported under checkpoint names to weight tracking) are fixed and re-verified by Codex.

## Details

**Backend interface.** #58053's `transform_weights` / `transform_shared_expert_weights` / `supports_shared_experts(deep_gemm)` become:
- `create_weights(layer, ...)`: register the routed (and fused shared) parameters in the kernel layout, indexed by local expert on dim 0 (EPLB moves experts along it);
- `load_weight(dst, src, shard_id, is_scale)`: write one checkpoint shard into one expert slice or a shared parameter;
- `supports_shared_experts(shared_experts)`: decide fusion at construction.

A post-load transform cannot coexist with in-place weight updates, because it replaces the storage the loaders write into. A backend with a different layout (e.g. an SM90 plugin) expresses it in `create_weights` and `load_weight`. Out-of-tree backends written against #58053 need this migration.

**SM100 layout.** DeepGEMM's `transform_weights_for_mega_moe` interleaves gate/up rows in groups of 8 and permutes scale rows for UTCCP; the L2 weight is unchanged. Each row of each shard lands at a fixed position, so `load_weight` copies a shard into a strided view of its final location:
- L1 gate row `r` → `(r // 8) * 16 + r % 8`, up row `r` → `(r // 8) * 16 + 8 + r % 8`.
- Scales are the UE8M0 bytes expanded to one per 1x32 block, packed four along K per int32, stored MN-major, with the UTCCP row map `128b + 32j + i → 128b + 4i + j`.

Routed FP4 parameters are int8 (the kernel's dtype) instead of uint8; loads reinterpret the bytes.

**Shared expert.** Fusion requires FP8 shared weights with UE8M0 scales that tile to 1x32 (checked on the shared MLP's parameters, which its quant method creates at init) and a DeepGEMM with the shared-expert API. Otherwise it warns once and keeps the separate shared MLP, as on `main`, but at construction instead of after loading, so the layout never changes after load. When fused, `DeepseekV4MoE.shared_experts` is `None` and `load_weights` routes `shared_experts.*` tensors to the experts' four kernel-layout parameters.

**Backend selection.** The backend is selected for the device the model is built on, or for the worker's current GPU when that is `meta` (`--load-format ipc_cache`).

**Scope.** EPLB with a reload after a rebalance is broken on `main` and is not addressed. XPU keeps its own implementation.

**Not a duplicate.** #59003 (draft, stacked on #53509) also targets MegaMoE reload, but by staging new checkpoint sources and re-packing into buffers through a reload lifecycle. This PR removes the packed copy: the parameters are the kernel tensors, so there is nothing to stage or rebuild.

**AI assistance.** Written with Claude Code. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and GPU checks above.

title: [Bugfix][KVConnector][NIXL] Size per-region replicate flags by each region's block count
body:
## Background

With P_TP > D_TP (e.g. PCP8/DCP8 prefill → DP8 decode), each decoder rank reads a block from several prefill ranks. Each local descriptor gets a replicate flag: full-attention regions are **SPLIT** (each rank fills its head slice), MLA regions are **REPLICATE** (whole block read once).

`_fa_desc_replicated` assumed every region holds the same number of blocks. HiSparse breaks this: host-resident MLA regions hold `hisparse_host_num_blocks`, GPU regions hold `num_blocks`. Every P_TP > D_TP handshake into a HiSparse decoder failed with `AssertionError: FA desc flags N != num_fa_descs M`.

## Fix

Build the flags the same way `_build_fa_local` builds the descriptors: same region order, `region_num_blocks[i] * block_size_ratio` per region. Companion fix for the same topology: #60108. No other open PR touches this function.

## Validation

**main vs. this PR**, checked against the descriptors `_build_fa_local` emits:

| Region layout | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Equal block counts | OK | OK |
| HiSparse, unequal block counts | assert | OK |
| Unequal counts that divide evenly | flags silently wrong | OK |
| Layer-name routing, region listed twice | flags silently wrong | OK |

**Unit:** `test_tp_mapping.py` + `test_nixl_connector_hma.py`: 121 passed.

**E2E** (GLM-5.3, 2 × 8 H200, PCP8/DCP8 prefill → DP8 HiSparse decode, with #60108): main asserts on the first request. With both fixes, 8 one-hour agentic benchmark points ran with 0 errors and a 100% decoder prefix-cache hit rate. That run used an earlier revision of this fix that produces identical flags for this topology.

title: [Bugfix][KVConnector][NIXL] Return NumPy descriptors from mixed-memory local registration
body:
## Overview

With mixed DRAM/VRAM registration (HiSparse host-resident regions), `register_local_xfer_handler` returned the local descriptors as a list of tuples instead of its annotated `np.ndarray`. The P_TP > D_TP split path (`_build_local_splits_from_plan`) calls `.tolist()` on them, so a PCP8/DCP8 prefiller feeding a HiSparse decoder failed the NIXL handshake with `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'tolist'`. Companion fix for the same topology: #60107.

**Fix:** keep the Nx3 `uint64` array in the mixed-memory path. DRAM rows get device 0 via `blocks_data[desc_is_dram, 2] = 0`, and the DRAM/VRAM subsets are array slices.

## Validation

**Unit:** `test_mixed_memory_local_descriptors_split_by_memory_type` now asserts the returned descriptors are an `np.ndarray` (fails before the fix). `test_tp_mapping.py`, `test_nixl_connector.py`, `test_nixl_connector_hma.py`, `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`: 498 passed (3 GPU e2e tests left to CI).

**End to end**, GLM-5.3 on 2 × 8 H200, PCP8/DCP8/EP8 prefill → DP8/EP8 HiSparse decode, MTP3:

| vLLM | Result |
|---|---|
| main + #60107 | decoder fails in `_build_local_splits_from_plan` on the first request; no KV transferred |
| main + #60107 + earlier revision of this fix | 8 one-hour Agent X points (142K cap c8–64, 1M cap c4–32): 0 errors, 100% external prefix-cache hit rate on the decoder |

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] MegaAttn: wo_a writes wo_b's MXFP8 input
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

MegaAttn's (`FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41`) `wo_a` einsum now writes `z` directly as MXFP8, together with the F8_128x4 UE8M0 scales that `wo_b`'s FlashInfer MXFP8 GEMM reads. `wo_b` therefore no longer quantizes a BF16 `z`, at any token count. It uses vllm-project/DeepGEMM#40 (merged), which adds the 128x4 scale layout to DeepGEMM's FP8 einsum epilogue. This PR bumps the DeepGEMM pin to it.

## Claims

- `_o_proj` drops the standalone `mxfp8_quantize` kernel. On GB200 it is 0.4-2.0 us per layer faster in decode (1-256 tokens) and 2.8-141 us faster in prefill (512-32768 tokens). The one regression is +0.6 us at 384 tokens (see Details).
- `wo_b` receives byte-identical FP8 data and scales, so model outputs do not change.
- Only `flash_mla_mega_attn.py` changes (+33/-5 lines vs main). Shared o_proj code and other backends are untouched.

## Validation

`_o_proj` alone (`wo_a` einsum, then `wo_b` CuTe-DSL MXFP8 GEMM) at DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP1 shapes: 8 groups x 4096 -> 1024, `wo_b` 8192 -> 5120. Setup: 1 x GB200, CUPTI, full CUDA graph, cold L2, median of 3 rounds, both arms in one process. Software: torch 2.13.0+cu132, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, DeepGEMM a7a9277 + DeepGEMM#40. Outputs are bitwise identical at all 20 sizes measured.

| tokens | main (us) | this PR (us) | delta (us) | main: einsum BF16 + quant (us) | PR: einsum FP8 (us) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 26.2 | 24.9 | -1.3 | 10.9 + 2.4 | 11.2 |
| 4 | 25.5 | 23.8 | -1.7 | 10.9 + 2.4 | 11.2 |
| 16 | 26.1 | 24.1 | -2.0 | 11.0 + 2.5 | 11.3 |
| 64 | 29.9 | 28.1 | -1.8 | 12.4 + 2.7 | 13.0 |
| 128 | 29.3 | 28.8 | -0.5 | 13.3 + 2.9 | 14.8 |
| 256 | 46.8 | 45.1 | -1.7 | 14.3 + 3.6 | 14.5 |
| 384 | 42.3 | 42.9 | +0.6 | 17.9 + 4.6 | 22.3 |
| 512 | 58.5 | 55.6 | -2.8 | 20.0 + 4.9 | 20.7 |
| 1024 | 77.7 | 73.2 | -4.5 | 33.4 + 7.7 | 34.1 |
| 4096 | 250.1 | 229.8 | -20.3 | 105.4 + 20.6 | 104.5 |
| 8192 | 497.4 | 454.5 | -42.9 | 216.8 + 36.2 | 210.5 |
| 16384 | 1010.0 | 906.5 | -103.5 | 439.5 + 68.2 | 430.4 |
| 32768 | 2127.5 | 1986.9 | -140.6 | 936.5 + 129.8 | 903.3 |

The previous revision of this PR wrote MN-major scales, swizzled them with a separate Triton kernel (1.6-5.2 us per call), and was gated to 1024+ tokens. The E2E prefill (DEP4) and accuracy results below were measured on that previous revision and were not re-run. This revision only removes the swizzle kernel from the same prefill path, and it hands `wo_b` the same bytes. Decode E2E has not been measured.

<details>
<summary>Previous revision: E2E prefill (DEP4, GB300) and accuracy</summary>

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (DP4 x TP1 + EP) on one GB300 node. Default config: SWA bounded replay on, MegaAttn, DeepGEMM mega MoE, fp8 KV cache, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, prefix caching off. Offline `LLM` per DP rank, one random-token prompt per rank, `max_tokens=1`. TTFT is measured from `scheduled_ts` to `first_token_ts` on the slowest rank; median of 3 repeats after a warmup.

| tokens/rank | base run 1 (ms) | base run 2 (ms) | PR (ms) | vs base mean |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 58.7 | 56.4 | 57.9 | +0.5% (noise) |
| 4096 | 93.1 | 92.9 | 91.4 | -1.7% |
| 8192 | 134.7 | 135.0 | 133.5 | -1.0% |
| 16384 | 229.1 | 227.9 | 227.4 | -0.5% |
| 32768 | 421.1 | 421.9 | 419.5 | -0.5% |

| eval | setup | score |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K | lm-eval 0.4.13, 1319 problems, 5-shot, temperature 0, 4096-token cap, concurrency 32 | strict match 92.80%, flexible extract 92.72% (±0.7) |
| GPQA Diamond | gpt-oss `GPQAEval`, 198 problems, 0-shot chat, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 | 89.90% (±2.1) |

</details>

Tests:
- vllm-project/DeepGEMM#40: all 7 tests in `tests/test_einsum.py` pass, including the new bitwise check of the 128x4 scales against the MN-major path.
- `tests/kernels/test_dsv41_mega_attn_layouts.py::test_quantized_o_proj_matches_quantized_bf16` now covers 1, 129 and 8193 tokens (decode, partial and multiple 128-row tiles), including CUDA graph capture and replay. It checks that `_o_proj`'s FP8 data and valid-row scales are byte-identical to `wo_b` quantizing the BF16 `z`. All 5 tests in the file pass on 1 x GB200 (torch 2.14.0+cu132, DeepGEMM with #40): `pytest tests/kernels/test_dsv41_mega_attn_layouts.py -v`.
- `pre-commit` (ruff, format, typos, shellcheck, mypy) passes.

## Details

- **Why the gate is gone.** DeepGEMM's einsum could only write MN-major packed scales, so `wo_b` needed a separate swizzle kernel. Below about 1024 tokens, that launch cost about as much as the quantization it saved. vllm-project/DeepGEMM#40 changes only the scale address in the einsum epilogue, so no extra kernel is left.
- **Gate conditions (unchanged).** The path runs when the einsum uses the per-32 recipe, `o_lora_rank % 128 == 0`, and `wo_b` is an MXFP8 kernel that accepts F8_128x4 scales (`can_fuse_query_quant`). It also requires no GEMM-RS, because the fused GEMM + reduce-scatter takes a BF16 `z` only.
- **Padded scale rows.** Rows past the last token in the final 128-row tile are not written. They only feed `wo_b` output rows that are never stored, so the test compares valid rows only.
- **384 tokens.** At 128-384 tokens (and at 2048 tokens), DeepGEMM's FP8-output einsum is slower than its BF16-output einsum, for example 17.9 -> 22.3 us at 384. The old MN-major scales show the same slowdown, so it is independent of this change. It is a DeepGEMM kernel-selection issue that can be fixed there.
- **DeepGEMM pin.** The pin points at `727f847`, the merge commit of DeepGEMM#40 on the fork's `dev` branch. The einsum selects the 128x4 scales with `use_128x4_sfd_layout=True`, which an older externally installed `deep_gemm` (vLLM prefers site-packages) does not accept.
- Merged `main` to resolve conflicts.

title: [UX] Skip checkpoint shards an MTP head does not load
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

MTP heads load from their target's checkpoint, so loaders that read whole files (InstantTensor, fastsafetensors, multi-thread, eager/prefetch) read the entire checkpoint a second time, only for the head's `load_weights` to drop almost all of it. This PR lets a model say which checkpoint weights it does not load, and `DefaultModelLoader` drops the safetensors shards that hold nothing else before any loader opens them.

Related: #58016 adds a similar model hook for per-tensor skipping in the lazy safetensors path (see Details).

## Claims

- With `--load-format instanttensor`, the MTP drafter no longer re-reads the target checkpoint: 704 G → 20 G on GLM-5.3, 149 G → 3.35 G on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 61.3 G → 10.2 G on Nemotron-3.5-Lightning.
- Total model load time drops accordingly: 226.5 s → 127.5 s (GLM-5.3, TP=8), 56.5 s → 36.6 s (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP=2), 22.8 s → 14.9 s (Nemotron, 1 GPU).
- Generated text and draft acceptance are unchanged.
- Opted in: DeepSeek-V4 (NVIDIA), DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.2 / GLM-5.3 (NVIDIA and ROCm), Nemotron-H, Qwen3.5, Qwen3-Next MTP heads. Models without the hook are unaffected.

## Validation

End to end on 8x H200, local XFS, InstantTensor 0.2.0, one run per configuration:

```bash
vllm serve <model> --load-format instanttensor --max-model-len 4096 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}' [--tensor-parallel-size N]
```

| Model | Drafter read, before → after | Shards read | Drafter load | Total model load | Draft tokens accepted, before / after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `zai-org/GLM-5.3`, TP=8 | 704 G → 20.0 G | 4 of 141 | 109.9 s → 3.4 s | 226.5 s → 127.5 s | 54 of 65 / 54 of 65 |
| `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, TP=2 | 149 G → 3.35 G | 1 of 46 | 25.7 s → 0.9 s | 56.5 s → 36.6 s | 60 of 60 / 60 of 60 |
| `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16`, 1 GPU | 61.3 G → 10.2 G | 3 of 14 | 10.1 s → 2.2 s | 22.8 s → 14.9 s | 59 of 61 / 59 of 61 |

Acceptance is a smoke check from one 120-token greedy completion per run, not an accuracy evaluation; the completions matched before and after.

A separate-repo drafter is unaffected: `zai-org/GLM-5.3` with `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-speculator.dspark` on this branch loads the 2.3 G speculator in 0.5 s (total 116.9 s) and generates correctly.

For each opted-in head, the new rule was compared with the original filtering on every weight name of a real checkpoint (GLM-5.2, GLM-5.2-FP8, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Nemotron-3.5-Lightning, Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.5-27B): zero mismatches. Scanning the 141 GLM-5.3 shard headers takes 0.12 s.

Tests and linters:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_filter_duplicate_safetensors.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_mm_encoder_only_weight_filter.py   # 51 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>                                      # passed
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <changed files>        # passed
```

Not validated:

- GLM-5.2 itself was not run end to end; GLM-5.3 uses the same `glm_moe_dsa` architecture and the same MTP head. From the published index, GLM-5.2 keeps 6 of 282 shards (29.9 of 1,403 GiB) and GLM-5.2-FP8 keeps 4 of 141 (20.0 of 704 GiB).
- The ROCm DeepSeek-V3.2 head has the same edit as the NVIDIA one but was not run on AMD hardware.
- Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next were not run end to end.
- Only InstantTensor was run end to end. The other safetensors load formats share the code path (the filter runs before the format is chosen) and are covered by the loader unit test only.

## Details

**Design.** A model may define `is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name) -> bool`, returning True for checkpoint weights it does not load. `DefaultModelLoader` passes it through a new `Source.is_unused_weight` field, and `filter_safetensors_files_by_weight_name` reads each shard's header and keeps only shards with at least one wanted tensor. Each opted-in head's `load_weights` calls the same rule, so the filter and the loader cannot drift apart. If the rule rejects every shard, the file list is left unchanged so the head's own missing-weight error still fires.

**Why shard level.** Whole-file loaders cannot skip single tensors, so the file list is the only lever vLLM has for them. MTP weights sit in a few shards, which is why this is enough.

**Relation to #58016 (not a duplicate).** #58016 adds an equivalent hook (`skip_checkpoint_weight`) and `Source` field but applies it per tensor inside `safetensors_weights_iterator`, which only helps the lazy safetensors path, and opts in only the DeepSeek-V4 DSpark drafter. This PR covers the whole-file loaders and the MTP heads. The two are complementary (drop shards, then skip tensors inside the kept ones), but the hooks are named differently, so whichever lands second should adopt the other's name and rebase the few shared lines in `default_loader.py`. Open PRs and issues were also searched for "MTP checkpoint load weights", "MTP shards skip", "draft model load entire checkpoint" and "MTP double load"; nothing else overlaps.

**Limitations.**

- Kept shards are still read in full. Qwen3.5 gains little: its head also loads `embed_tokens` and `lm_head`, which are spread across shards (Qwen3.5-27B keeps 5 of 11, Qwen3.5-9B keeps 4 of 4).
- Other MTP heads (DeepSeek V3, GLM-4, Kimi, Inkling, the ROCm/XPU V4 variants and others) are not opted in and behave as before.
- This does not help the EP weight filter under InstantTensor. On DeepSeek-V4-Flash, V4-Pro and Nemotron every shard holds at least one local expert at EP sizes 2, 4 and 8, so that needs per-tensor skipping inside InstantTensor itself.
- Loaders outside `DefaultModelLoader` (Run:ai streamer, tensorizer, sharded state, IPC weight cache) are untouched.

title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Register HiSparse host pool under single TP Rank
body:
When HiSparse uses its **shared host pool**, all local TP ranks share one `/dev/shm` mmap per DP rank. Even so, every TP rank registers the whole pool with NIXL, and every TP rank READs the same host-pool KV into the same pages. With UCX this means `ibv_reg_mr` of the full pool on every NIC, twice per NIC when relaxed ordering is on. At TP8 with 8 NICs, the pool is registered **128 times per node**, and each request's host-pool KV is pulled **8 times** into identical memory.

This PR adds an opt-in flag, `VLLM_NIXL_HISPARSE_DRAM_RANK0_ONLY=1`, which makes TP rank 0 the only rank that registers the shared pool and pulls into it. The other ranks:

- keep the DRAM regions in their metadata, so the prefill handshake still sees identical region lists;
- skip the DRAM `register_memory`;
- skip the DRAM transfer dlist;
- skip the DRAM part of each READ.

The GPU-resident part (the indexer cache) is still read by every rank, and every rank still notifies the producer.

Completion and ordering need nothing new:

- A request finishes only when all TP ranks report it done.
- HiSparse restores from the shared pool on the next step.
- The `cudaHostRegister` pin of the pool on every rank is unchanged, because each rank's GPU still reads from it.

### Changes

- `vllm/envs.py`: adds `VLLM_NIXL_HISPARSE_DRAM_RANK0_ONLY` (default off).
- `nixl/base_worker.py`:
  - `_leaves_dram_xfer_to_rank0()` decides whether a rank skips. That requires the flag, mixed DRAM/VRAM regions, `tp_rank != 0`, and `use_shared_hisparse_host_pool()`. Private (non-shared) pools are never affected.
  - Skipping ranks:
    - do not register DRAM ranges;
    - store `None` instead of preparing DRAM dlists, in both the local path and the split path;
    - leave zeroing of clipped shared-pool pages to rank 0.
  - Shutdown ignores the `None` handles.
- `nixl/pull_worker.py`: `_read_blocks_mixed()` drops the DRAM descriptors on skipping ranks and keeps the device part. It registers the request even when nothing is left to read, so it still completes and notifies.
- `NixlPushConnector` already rejects mixed-memory KV caches, so it is unchanged.
- Tests (`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py`):
  - **The rank decision:** flag on/off × rank 0 vs non-zero × shared vs private pool.
  - **No DRAM dlist on skipping ranks:** descriptor positions still cover the DRAM regions, so ids stay aligned with the remote side.
  - **A READ that keeps only the device part** still notifies.
  - **A READ left with no descriptors** still completes and notifies.
  - Existing `object.__new__` fixtures initialise the new attribute.

### Why: VM freezes on cloud RoCE VFs

On Cloud VPC instances (QEMU/KVM guests with ConnectX-7 SR-IOV VFs over RoCE, UCX 1.21 via NIXL 1.3.2), a GLM-5.3 HiSparse decode froze **both VMs** during NIXL registration with a 384 GiB pool. There was no guest panic, no guest log and no watchdog output; the nodes had to be reprovisioned. The same configuration passes on bare-metal H200 with InfiniBand.

Guest-side sampling explains the scale of the problem:

- **Pins per page:** `nr_foll_pin_acquired − released` measured exactly **8 + ranks × NICs × 2** (relaxed ordering) per page of pool.
- **Registration metadata:** the VFs' `fw_pages_total` stayed flat at 4 per VF throughout, so the registration metadata is not taken from guest memory.
- **Freeze point:** the freeze appeared between 36.9 TiB (passed) and 49.2 TiB (froze) of NIC-registered memory per VM.

### Results (llmd-roce cluster, GLM-5.3, DeepEP LL decode, 8 NICs, relaxed ordering on unless noted)

**Registration footprint per VM**, from a 2-node decode (DP2 × TP8). These numbers are measured with a startup patch equivalent to this PR on vLLM `87ecf7dbb`.

| Host pool | Stock: pins/page | Stock: NIC-registered | This PR: pins/page | This PR: NIC-registered | This PR: rank-0 registration |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 GiB | 136.1x | 12.5 TiB | **24.2x** | **1.58 TiB** | ~28 s (ranks 1–7 < 1 s) |
| 288 GiB | 136x | 36.9 TiB | **24.05x** | **4.51 TiB** | ~80 s |
| 384 GiB | 136x | 49.2 TiB, **both VMs froze** | **24.04x** | **6.01 TiB, passes** | 43–52 s |
| 384 GiB, relaxed ordering off | — | — | 16.02x | 3.01 TiB, passes | 21 s |

Startup is not faster per node: rank 0 does the same per-rank work as before. What drops 8x is the number of registrations, the pinned memory and the NIC metadata.

**P/D correctness**, using a separate prefill and greedy decoding:

- **Results:** P/D output matched the prefill-only reference for 18-, 28.7k- and 250k-token prompts, at pool sizes 100, 288 and 384 GiB. The short prompt shows the usual small numerical divergence between prefill and decode kernels; the 28.7k answer is identical; the 250k answer is the same sentence, differing in one word ("at" vs "in").
- **Transfer count:** each request takes **9** NIXL transfers (rank 0 host + 8 device) instead of 16.
- **Failures:** 0 failed transfers.

**End-to-end benchmark**, 4P/4D, 64 H100:

- **Prefill:** DP4 × PCP8/DCP8.
- **Decode:** DP4 × TP8 with a 288 GiB shared pool.
- **Load:** cc_traces 256k, constant load, 900 s per level.
- **Fairness:** both arms ran on the same 8 nodes, and both roles were re-created between arms.

| Concurrency | Out tok/s (PR vs stock) | TTFT p99 | ITL p50 | ITL p99 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | **602 vs 503 (+19.7%)** | **21.6 vs 89.0 s** | 20.9 vs 23.3 ms | 116 vs 167 ms |
| 64 | 547 vs 563 | 98.2 vs 87.5 s | 19.2 vs 21.6 ms | 33.3 vs 46.6 ms |
| 128 | 482 vs 520 | 194 vs 183 s | 18.2 vs 20.7 ms | 36.5 vs 65.6 ms |

- **ITL improves at every level:** p50 by 10–12%, p99 by 28–44%.
- **At c64 and c128 both arms are prefill-bound:** request rate is equal within 2%, and the tok/s gap follows output length.

**Transfer totals over the sweep:**

| Metric | This PR | Stock |
|---|---|---|
| NIXL bytes pulled | 5.35 TB | 31.3 TB |
| Average transfer time | 30.8 ms | 122 ms |
| p90 transfer time | 63.7 ms | 318 ms |
| CPU time posting transfers | 472 s | 3,657 s |
