title: [WideEP] Explain how to fix a too-old NCCL for DeepEP v2
body:
## Overview

Make a too-old NCCL for DeepEP v2 self-explanatory on pip/uv installs. PyTorch pins an NCCL older than the 2.30.4 that `--all2all-backend deepep_v2` needs (PyTorch 2.13 pins `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.29.7`). The Docker images override it since #45321, but installs outside the images fail with a message that states the requirement and not the fix. This does not change any dependency.

## Claims

- The startup log line and the `DeepEPV2All2AllManager` assertion now name the cause and the upgrade command for the installed CUDA major.
- `tools/ep_kernels/install_python_libraries.sh` warns, before and after the build output, when the installed NCCL is too old for DeepEP v2. It does not fail, so DeepEP v1 builds are unaffected.
- `tools/ep_kernels/README.md` reflects the current PyTorch pin, explains that later `uv pip install` runs restore it without `UV_OVERRIDE`, and that DeepEP must be rebuilt after upgrading NCCL.

## Validation

On an environment with torch 2.13.0, `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.29.7`, and DeepEP 2.0.0:

```console
$ python -c "from vllm.utils.import_utils import deep_ep_v2_unavailable_reason as r; print(r())"
DeepEP v2 requires NCCL >= 2.30.4 but found 2.29.7. PyTorch pins an older NCCL; upgrade it with `pip install "nvidia-nccl-cu13>=2.30.4" --no-deps` and rebuild DeepEP against it. See tools/ep_kernels/README.md.
```

The NCCL check from the install script, run in isolation against the same environment:

```console
WARNING: nvidia-nccl-cu13 2.29.7 is installed, but the deepep_v2 backend
requires NCCL >= 2.30.4 when DeepEP is built and when it runs. To use deepep_v2, run
    uv pip install "nvidia-nccl-cu13>=2.30.4" --no-deps
and then run this script again. See tools/ep_kernels/README.md.
```

pre-commit (including shellcheck and markdownlint) and `mypy-3.12` pass on the changed files.

Not validated: the full install script was not re-run end to end, the Docker build was not run (it sets `UV_OVERRIDE`, so the warning should not trigger there), and the available path (NCCL >= 2.30.4) was not exercised on a real environment. No tests were added; the change is message text plus a shell warning.

## Details

`has_deep_ep_v2()` now delegates to a new `deep_ep_v2_unavailable_reason()`, so the log line and the assertion share one message. One behavior difference: an environment with a pre-v2 DeepEP installed now also gets the one-time INFO line saying `deepep_v2` is unavailable.

The alternative of forcing a newer NCCL through `[tool.uv] override-dependencies` in `pyproject.toml` was left out on purpose to avoid changing dependencies.

Not a duplicate: searches for `deepep_v2 NCCL` and `nccl install_python_libraries` found no open PR addressing this.

AI assistance was used to investigate and implement this change.

title: [Feat] Add text-only OpenAI Decisions API
body:
## Overview

Adds a text-only `/v1/decisions` endpoint following the [OpenAI API format](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions).

Builds on #59299 and #60677, now merged into `main`.

## Claims

Supports predicate, choice, and score questions using shared label reads under `vllm/entrypoints/openai/decisions`. `/v1/decisions` is available by default on supported generation models and returns 501 when no generation read strategy is available. `/v1/systemone` also supports Clef-Omni pooling models from #61064. The new endpoint accepts text strings or user messages and returns ordered answers with probabilities and token usage.

## Validation

- 137 CPU tests passed on the rebased commit, including Clef-Flash, Liquid d1, and Clef-Omni strategy coverage, DiffusionGemma, launcher routing, cache-salt/tracing behavior, HTTP error handling, logging, limits, Qwen tokenization, and shared generative scoring. All-files pre-commit with the CI manual stage passed.
- Local SDK/schema checks passed without model inference. The OpenAPI schema test collects after extending the existing SmolVLM 501 handling to `/v1/decisions`; its live GPU case runs in Buildkite.
- Qwen3-0.6B GPU end-to-end tests on a DGX Spark: all 15 endpoint tests passed without an endpoint flag before this rebase and the test relocation. The run used `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.35` to share the device. The current checkout could not rerun GPU tests because its NVIDIA driver is unavailable.
- A small balanced Qwen3-0.6B factual eval through `/v1/decisions` scored 8/16: 6/12 predicates and 2/4 choices. All six true predicates received probabilities below 0.5. Direct Chat Completions with the same predicate prompt also returned `false` for a true case, so this result needs a stronger-model follow-up. Live OpenAI comparison remains pending.

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_strategies.py \
  tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_decisions.py \
  tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_question_types.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/test_factories.py \
  tests/entrypoints/generate/generative_scoring/test_generative_scoring.py -q
# 137 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/test_openai_schema.py --collect-only -q
# 1 test collected; GPU server unavailable locally

UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/uv-cache .venv/bin/pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage manual
# passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -o addopts='' \
  -o cache_dir=/tmp/decisions-pytest-cache \
  tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_structured_decisions_e2e.py -q
# 15 passed with Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, before the test relocation

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/decisions/test_decisions_e2e.py --collect-only -q
# 2 tests collected in the current location; GPU server unavailable locally
```

The CPU HTTP tests use a test engine and a cached Qwen tokenizer. The worktree used existing precompiled CUDA extensions for model registry inspection; this PR changes no C/CUDA code. The earlier GPU run used a temporary copy of this PR's Python source with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.35`. The 16-case factual eval was a temporary script with six true and six false predicates and balanced choice positions, also before this rebase.

</details>

## Details

For this MVP: no images or refusal scoring, and at most 64 questions and 26 choices. Confidence is not calibrated to OpenAI's models.

Duplicate checks found no other open PR for this endpoint. #59299 added the shared backend and #60677 ungated `/v1/systemone`; this PR moves shared modules under `openai/decisions` and adds the OpenAI-format endpoint. Built with Codex assistance.

title: [Perf] Warm up DeepGEMM MegaMoE kernels before serving
body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution -->
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The DeepGEMM warmup covers `fp8_gemm_nt` and the grouped MoE GEMM. It does not cover `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` or the `bf16_mega_gate` that routes into it. With `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, DeepSeek-V4 and Kimi K3 therefore JIT-compile these kernels on the first request at each new prefill size. This PR adds them to `deep_gemm_warmup.py`, following the structure of the two existing DeepGEMM warmups there.

## Claims

- No serving-time compiles of the MegaMoE kernels: `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`, `bf16_mega_gate` and the Triton input-staging kernel. Before: 60 DeepGEMM compiles in one DeepSeek-V4 benchmark run. For Kimi K3, the 2 SiTU `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` compiles during serving that cost 2.6-2.9 s of TTFT each go to 0, at about +10 s of startup.
- MTP speculative decoding needs nothing extra. The DeepSeek-V4 MTP drafter's MegaMoE layer uses the same kernels as the target's, and there were 0 DeepGEMM compiles during serving with MTP on.
- DeepSeek-V4: the first request at a new prefill size no longer stalls for 3.5 to 6 s. It now takes about the same time as a repeat. The exception is a one-time 60-85 ms communication-buffer setup on the server's first large prefill, which is not a compile (see Details).
- Cost: for DeepSeek-V4, the first startup on a cold DeepGEMM cache takes about 4 to 5 min longer (+247 to +299 s on fully empty caches). A warm restart takes the same time as before. For Kimi K3, it is about +10 s.

## Validation

**Setup (DeepSeek-V4).** DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 2x B300, TP2 + EP2, `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, `max_num_batched_tokens` 16384, `--max-model-len 16384`, prefix caching off, Model Runner V2. vLLM precompiled wheel `3ca00a82` (cu130) with its bundled DeepGEMM.

Each run used a fresh `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` seeded with every non-mega DeepGEMM kernel, so only the mega kernels start cold.

**Workload.** One request at a time: token-ID prompts to `/v1/completions`, `max_tokens` 4, streamed time to first token (TTFT).
1. Six fixed lengths (100 to 8000 tokens). Each gets a first request, then 3 repeats with new random tokens.
2. 40 seeded random lengths from 51 to 15504 tokens. The warmup did not pick these.
3. 32 concurrent requests.

**JIT compiles during serving.** Counted as new entries in the DeepGEMM cache dir between "Application startup complete" and the end of the workload, across all kernel families. Triton, CuTeDSL and TileLang compiles were counted with `--jit-monitor-verbose`.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `sm100_bf16_mega_gate` | 58 | 0 |
| `sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe` | 2 | 0 |
| other DeepGEMM families | 0 | 0 |
| Triton `_prepare_megamoe_inputs_kernel` | ≥1 (see note) | 0 |

On main, the Triton row comes from the default (non-verbose) JIT monitor, which logs only the first compile per kernel, so the true count is unknown. The previous revision of this PR, which warmed without a padding mask, compiled 3 variants for just three prompt lengths in a verbose run.

A separate single-GPU check called both kernels for every per-rank token count from 1 to 8192 after the warmup's representative sizes. It produced 0 new cache entries. An independent rerun of the patched server, with 20 prompt lengths, 16 of them chosen to give unaligned per-rank chunks, saw 0 JIT events.

**TTFT, first request vs median of 3 repeats (ms):**

| prompt tokens | main, first | main, repeat | this PR, first | this PR, repeat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 36 | 36 | 36 | 36 |
| 2000 | 3503 | 106 | 112 | 103 |
| 4000 | 5913 | 119 | 178 | 117 |
| 8000 | 3489 | 136 | 141 | 136 |

- 40 random lengths: 24 of the 40 requests on main took 3.5 to 6.0 s. The slowest on this PR took 0.27 s. Total TTFT went from 90.1 s to 6.1 s.
- 32 concurrent requests: worst TTFT went from 8.33 s to 1.47 s.

**Startup, `init engine` (profile, KV cache, warmup, graph capture):**

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| cold mega-kernel cache (all other kernels cached) | 141 s | 428 s |
| fully empty caches, no MTP (separate tester run) | 444 s | 691 s (+247 s) |
| fully empty caches, with MTP (separate tester run) | 406 s | 705 s (+299 s) |
| warm restart, same cache dir | 63 s | 63 s |

KV cache sizing is unchanged: 163.13 GiB and 465,145 tokens in both.

**MTP (DeepSeek-V4, `--speculative_config.method=mtp --speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens=2`, same setup and workload):**

| MegaMoE compiles during serving | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| seeded cache (mega kernels cold), 1 run | not run | 0 |
| fully empty caches, 1 run (separate tester) | 2 `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`, 10 `bf16_mega_gate`, 6 Triton staging | 0 |

On this PR's commit with MTP: the server was healthy, GSM8K (200 questions, 5-shot) scored 0.970, and mean MTP acceptance length was 2.62 on GSM8K. On the random-token benchmark, acceptance was 1.61, against 1.55 on the previous revision. DeepGEMM compiles during serving: 0.

The drafter needs no extra warmup. Its MegaMoE layer reuses the target's kernels, and the tester's tracer saw no DeepGEMM compile in the drafter during serving on either build.

**Kimi K3 (`mgoin/Kimi-K3-pruned75`, a pruned checkpoint):** 4x B300, TP4 + EP4 with sequence parallelism, `max_num_batched_tokens` 8192 (2048 per rank), fp8 KV, no prefix caching, no spec decode.
- Each run started with empty DeepGEMM, Triton, Inductor and vLLM caches. One run per build.
- Workload: one 3000-token request, a second 3000-token request with new tokens, then 137, 1500, 5000 and 8000 tokens.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| DeepGEMM compiles during serving | 2 (`fp8_fp4_mega_moe` SiTU, `block_m` 128 and 192) | 0 |
| Triton `_prepare_megamoe_inputs_kernel` compiled during serving | yes (ranks 1-3, first request) | no |
| TTFT at 1500 / 5000 tokens | 2734 / 3139 ms | 153 / 244 ms |
| `init engine` | 46 s* | 56-57 s |

\*The main run had a warm FlashInfer JIT cache from an earlier run. The PR runs had one too, so the +10 s compares like with like.

On both builds, two non-MegaMoE kernels still compile during serving: the Inductor kernel `triton_poi_fused_mul_sigmoid_0`, on the first prefill above the capture sizes, and the KDA gated RMSNorm Triton kernel `layer_norm_gated_fwd_kernel`. They are outside this PR.

**Fully cold cache.** With every DeepGEMM and Triton cache empty (not just the mega kernels), three other DeepGEMM kernel families still compile on first use with this PR. They are outside MegaMoE and left for follow-ups:
- `fp8_einsum` in `o_proj` (`sm100_fp8_gemm_1d1d`): 2 kernels.
- `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`: 8 kernels without MTP, 6 with MTP.
- The sparse indexer's `sm100_mqa_logits`: 1 kernel.

With MTP, the spec-decode rejection-sampler Triton kernels also compile on first use on both builds. That is unrelated to this PR.

**Tests.** `tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py` adds two CPU tests:
- The layer predicate is False for other models, and neither model module is imported. It is True only for DeepSeek-V4 and Kimi K3 MegaMoE layers.
- The warmup sizes for each `bf16_mega_gate` config are above the gate's token threshold, so the forward reaches the kernel.

All 8 tests pass.

**CI gap.** This path needs SM100 GPUs, DeepSeek-V4 or Kimi K3 with the native MegaMoE backend, and expert parallelism. CI has no such setup, so the validation above was run by hand.

<details>
<summary>Repro commands</summary>

```bash
# server (baseline: same command on main)
export VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1 DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR=<fresh dir>
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype=mxfp4 \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --max-model-len 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching --jit-monitor-verbose --port 8234

# client: fixed lengths x (1 first + 3 repeats), 40 random lengths, 32-request burst;
# records TTFT and the new DeepGEMM cache entries per request
SWEEP=40 python bench.py 8234 $DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR results.json
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>bench.py</summary>

```python
"""First-hit benchmark. Phase 1 (fixed): for each prompt length, one request
at a time: a first hit, then REPEATS more with fresh random tokens. Phase 2
(sweep, optional): random lengths the warmup did not pick, then a concurrent
burst (mixed prefill + decode). Records TTFT and every DeepGEMM JIT cache
entry created during serving, per kernel family."""
import collections, concurrent.futures as cf, json, os, random, re, sys, time
import requests

port, dgdir, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
LENGTHS = [int(x) for x in os.environ.get("LENGTHS", "100,400,1000,2000,4000,8000").split(",")]
REPEATS = int(os.environ.get("REPEATS", "3"))
SWEEP = int(os.environ.get("SWEEP", "0"))
URL = f"http://localhost:{port}/v1/completions"
MODEL = "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash"
cache = os.path.join(dgdir, "cache")

def entries():
    return set(os.listdir(cache))

def family(e):
    m = re.match(r"(?:kernel\.)?(.+?)\.[0-9a-f]{32}$", e)
    return m.group(1) if m else e

def fam_count(es):
    return dict(collections.Counter(family(e) for e in es))

def ttft(prompt_ids, max_tokens=4):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    r = requests.post(URL, json=dict(model=MODEL, prompt=prompt_ids, max_tokens=max_tokens,
                                     temperature=0, stream=True, ignore_eos=True),
                      stream=True, timeout=3600)
    first = None
    for line in r.iter_lines():
        if line and line.startswith(b"data: ") and line != b"data: [DONE]" and first is None:
            first = time.perf_counter() - t0
    return first, time.perf_counter() - t0

rng = random.Random(0)
def prompt(L):
    return [rng.randrange(1000, 100000) for _ in range(L)]

start = entries()
print(f"entries at ready: {len(start)} {fam_count(start)}", flush=True)
rows = []
ttft(prompt(8))  # HTTP/tokenizer warm; 4 per-rank tokens -> no mega gate
for L in LENGTHS:
    for i in range(1 + REPEATS):
        before = entries()
        t, e2e = ttft(prompt(L))
        new = entries() - before
        rows.append(dict(phase="fixed", prompt_len=L, rep="first" if i == 0 else f"repeat{i}",
                         ttft_s=t, e2e_s=e2e, new=fam_count(new)))
        print(json.dumps(rows[-1]), flush=True)
after_fixed = entries()
sweep_lengths = []
if SWEEP:
    srng = random.Random(1)
    sweep_lengths = sorted(srng.randrange(17, 16380) for _ in range(SWEEP))
    for L in sweep_lengths:
        before = entries()
        t, e2e = ttft(prompt(L))
        rows.append(dict(phase="sweep", prompt_len=L, rep="first", ttft_s=t, e2e_s=e2e,
                         new=fam_count(entries() - before)))
        print(json.dumps(rows[-1]), flush=True)
    # concurrent burst: 32 requests, mixed lengths, 64 output tokens -> prefill + decode mix
    burst = [prompt(srng.randrange(17, 6000)) for _ in range(32)]
    before = entries(); t0 = time.perf_counter()
    with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(32) as ex:
        res = list(ex.map(lambda p: ttft(p, 64), burst))
    rows.append(dict(phase="burst", prompt_len=-1, rep="32 concurrent", ttft_s=max(r[0] for r in res),
                     e2e_s=time.perf_counter() - t0, new=fam_count(entries() - before)))
    print(json.dumps(rows[-1]), flush=True)
end = entries()
summary = dict(rows=rows, entries_at_ready=fam_count(start), new_during_fixed=fam_count(after_fixed - start),
               new_during_serving=fam_count(end - start), new_entries=sorted(end - start),
               sweep_lengths=sweep_lengths)
json.dump(summary, open(out, "w"), indent=1)
print("new during serving:", summary["new_during_serving"])
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** Both kernels choose a JIT config from the per-rank token count:
- `bf16_mega_gate`: block tokens, MMA CTAs, split-K, expert groups and stages (`heuristics/mega_gate.hpp`). That is 87 configs for per-rank sizes 17 to 8192.
- `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`: `block_m` in {16, 32, 64, 128, 192, 240}.

Startup only compiles the sizes that the profile run and CUDA graph capture hit, here 512 or fewer tokens per rank. Every other prefill size compiles on first use, about 1.7 s per kernel. DeepSeek-V4 needs two gate kernels per size, because hash-routed and bias-routed layers pass different optional inputs.

**Design.** The warmup lives in `deep_gemm_warmup.py`, with the same parts as the existing DeepGEMM warmups:
- A layer predicate that matches DeepSeek-V4's `DeepseekV4MoE` and Kimi K3's `KimiMoE` when they use the native MegaMoE backend.
- A cache constant.
- `_get_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_m_values`: for every per-rank size, it asks DeepGEMM for the `block_m` and, for DeepSeek-V4, the gate config. It keeps the largest size of each distinct config (95 sizes for DeepSeek-V4 here), because DeepSeek-V4 only calls `bf16_mega_gate` above a small token threshold and a config's largest size is always above it. The configs come from DeepGEMM's own getters, so the dedup is exact and `VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=full` would add nothing.
  - Kimi K3 routes with its `GateLinear`, which the bf16x3 router warmup already covers, so for Kimi only `block_m` matters.
  - Kimi's experts call the SiTU variant of `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`, which picks `block_m` with the same heuristic.
- A private worker and a public loop, an `elif` branch in `_count_warmup_iterations`, and calls in `deep_gemm_warmup`.

The worker runs the whole MoE layer at each size, not the raw kernels:
- The gate gets the same optional inputs it gets in serving.
- Every EP rank runs the same sizes in the same order, which the collective MegaMoE kernel needs.
- It runs under a minimal forward context with a padding mask, because the layer reads `is_padding` from the forward context. This makes the Triton input-staging kernel compile the variants serving uses.
- Under sequence parallelism with `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` on (the default), ranks above 0 get mask slices at any alignment, so each size runs once with an aligned slice and once with an unaligned one.

The predicate looks the model modules up in `sys.modules`, as other model-specific warmups in this package do (`kimi_k3_triton_warmup.py`, `qwen4_exp_qsa_warmup.py`), so other models import neither model. The cache key reads two DeepSeek-V4-only attributes (`tid2eid`, `image_sentinel_lo`) with `getattr`, because they do not exist on Kimi K3. The two config getters are reached through `_import_deep_gemm`, as in the model code.

`models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py` gains one line, which stores `use_sequence_parallel` on `KimiMoE` as `DeepseekV4MoE` already does. The warmup needs it to compute the per-rank token count.

<details>
<summary>Startup trade-off: where the cold warmup time goes</summary>

- About 84% of the cold warmup is serial `nvcc` time for 136 gate kernels (1.7 s each).
- About 14% is about 24 Triton staging variants.
- About 3% is 3 MegaMoE kernels.
- The layer forwards and the size search take under 1 s.

Compiling in parallel threads crashed inside DeepGEMM's JIT, which has no locking and no compile-only API. Parallel compilation would need DeepGEMM changes. vLLM keeps the DeepGEMM cache in `~/.cache/vllm/deep_gemm`, so the cold cost is paid once per machine and DeepGEMM version.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Remaining one-time first-request cost</summary>

The first eager prefill whose reduce-scatter falls in the MNNVL multimem size range sets up a symmetric-memory buffer (`_init_mnnvl_multimem_reduce_scatter_buffer`). This adds 60-85 ms to that one request (+61, +66 and +83 ms in three runs). CUDA graph capture skips this setup. It is paid once per server and is not a compile. A torch profile and a request-order test confirm both points.
</details>

**Limitations.** DeepSeek-V4 was validated only on 2x B300 with TP2 + EP2 and Model Runner V2, with and without MTP. Kimi K3 was validated only with a pruned checkpoint on 4x B300, TP4 + EP4, Model Runner V2.
- Not run: Model Runner V1, DP > 1, other EP sizes, EPLB, and routed-experts capture. With EPLB or routed-experts capture on, the warmup forwards would pass dummy tokens to the load recording and the capture hook.

---

title: [Bugfix] Keep compressed-tensors wNa16 linear layers batch invariant
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Follow-up to #60479. With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the compressed-tensors `pack-quantized` linear scheme (`CompressedTensorsWNA16`, W4A16 and W8A16) still runs the Marlin GEMM, whose tiling and K-split depend on the number of tokens, so logprobs change with the batch size. This PR applies the same fix as #60479 to that scheme: in batch-invariant mode skip the Marlin kernel selection and repacking, keep the checkpoint layout, unpack the weight in `apply_weights()` and call `matmul_batch_invariant`. Without the flag nothing changes.

## Claims

- On `main`, `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py` fails for `RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-quantized.w4a16` (dense), `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-quantized.w4a16` (MoE; its dense layers use this scheme) and `RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-quantized.w8a16`. With this PR all ids pass, on an A10 and on a B300.
- Accuracy is unchanged (`lm_eval` gsm8k, batch-invariant path versus Marlin), and the Marlin path is still selected when the flag is unset.
- Throughput cost of the batch-invariant path on these models is in the blocks below.

## Details

**Root cause.** `CompressedTensorsWNA16.create_weights` always builds a Marlin `MPLinearKernel` (`choose_mp_linear_kernel`), and `apply_weights` runs it. Marlin's results depend on the number of rows, so batch-invariant mode is silently violated; the determinism suite fails for every pack-quantized checkpoint tried, on A10 and B300, while the needle test often passes (greedy outputs usually survive the logprob differences).

**Change** (`compressed_tensors_wNa16.py` only). With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`: no Marlin kernel is created, `process_weights_after_loading` keeps `weight_packed` / `weight_scale` / `weight_zero_point` in the checkpoint layout, and `apply_weights` unpacks the weight with `compressed_tensors.compressors.pack_quantized.helpers.unpack_from_int32` (and the zero points for asymmetric checkpoints), dequantizes in the scales dtype and calls `matmul_batch_invariant`. The log line becomes `Using dequantize + batch-invariant matmul for CompressedTensorsWNA16`.

**Trade-offs and limitations.**
- The weight is unpacked on every forward in batch-invariant mode (same choice as #60479: keeping a dequantized copy would need the memory of the unquantized model). The cost is in the benchmark blocks above.
- Symmetric W4A16 and W8A16 checkpoints and an asymmetric W4A16 checkpoint were validated (blocks above).
- The MoE expert path of compressed-tensors (`CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod`) is not touched: on the MoE model tested the experts run through the Triton WNA16 MoE backend and the violation disappears once the dense layers are fixed.

title: [Feature][MoRIIO] Support hybrid WRITE transfers with DSpark
body:
## Overview

Enable MoRIIO WRITE for hybrid attention and Mamba/KDA models, including DSpark. This extends the hybrid READ support in #51052 and #57700 using existing transfer plans and post-draft save finalization.

## Claims

- Transfer attention KV, convolution and SSM state with per-group identity and completion accounting.
- Resolve the live final prefill state, exclude speculative scratch slots and publish matching N-1 token accounting.
- Use native `wait_all` with a finite deadline and a bounded fallback for older MoRI versions; nonblocking progress is unchanged.

## Validation

Rebased onto `642c18d64c`. The complete MoRIIO suite passed **274 tests**, followed by **3** block-state and **12** adjacent scheduler tests (**289 passed**). Changed Python files pass Ruff check and formatting. Full pre-commit installation was blocked by a certificate error while fetching actionlint.

```bash
uv run --no-project python -m pytest -q -o addopts='' tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_*.py
uv run --no-project python -m pytest -q -o addopts='' tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_scheduler_kv_connector_override.py
uv run --no-project python -m pytest -q -o addopts='' tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k 'hybrid or mamba or remote_kv or async_load or pending_push'
```

Real-weight GSM8K uses all 1,319 questions, concurrency 64, 5-shot, temperature 0, seed 42 and at most 256 output tokens.

| Validation | Control | Hybrid WRITE |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current revision: Kimi-K3, TP8/DCP8, DSpark K4, block verification | Direct decode: 1,244/1,319 (94.31%) | Two runs: 1,232/1,319 (93.40%) and 1,253/1,319 (95.00%) |
| Previous revision: Kimi-Linear, TP2/DCP2, no speculation | READ: 1,167/1,319 (88.48%) | 1,171/1,319 (88.78%) |

Current K3 runs use connector revision `70c6fbfff9` on runtime `0.32.0rc1.dev190+g3f1bcfd82`, FP8 KV, FP32 recurrent state, A8W4, align-mode caching, GMU 0.90 and explicit P16/D40 GiB KV budgets per rank. The first full WRITE run imported 836,896 prompt tokens and recorded 67.86% real draft acceptance. Each full evaluation had one empty answer; the measurements show run-to-run variation, not bit-exact equivalence or a performance comparison. The previous Kimi-Linear evaluation used runtime `43b4aaea3`; it has not been repeated after this rebase.

```bash
uv run --no-project python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64 --num-shots 5 --temperature 0 --seed 42 --max-tokens 256 --request-timeout-seconds 3600
```

The existing connector CI suite covers the unit tests. Distributed model evaluations were run separately.

Serving completed without engine termination or RDMA transfer failures. Prefill logged recoverable hipBLASLt fallback warnings; these runs are not a warning-free runtime qualification.

## Details

The three commits separate bounded completion waiting, grouped hybrid WRITE and DSpark support. Changes are confined to MoRIIO, its tests and its usage guide; no scheduler, model-runner, sampler or router implementation changes are needed.

1. Decode advertises allocated block IDs in transfer-group order.
2. Prefill resolves the live final slots and writes attention KV plus convolution and SSM state for the N-1 prompt.
3. Decode waits for all transfers before consuming the imported state and recomputing the final prompt token. A complete coupled local hit releases the producer without an empty remote load.

Set `read_mode: false` in both roles' `kv_connector_extra_config`, use matching cache layouts and TP sizes, and enable `--mamba-cache-mode align`. For DSpark, configure the same draft model on both roles. Sliding-window WRITE and other hybrid speculative methods remain unsupported. READ and plain-attention WRITE wire formats are preserved.

This adds hybrid recurrent-state WRITE, rather than duplicating attention registration work in #58585 or READ lifecycle work in #58968. The rebase retains upstream #57705 local-hit release and failure routing, per-layer registration geometry and one-shot receive guards.

title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Fix encoder cache deadlock with drafter look-ahead
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes the encoder-cache deadlock with a drafter look-ahead (EAGLE / MTP) reported in the second half of #40707 ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40707#issuecomment-5760731067)). When two multimodal items only fit in the encoder cache one at a time and the gap between them is smaller than `2 * num_prefill_lookahead`, the request hangs forever, getting 0 scheduled tokens on every step with no error or log. The Mamba-alignment half of #40707 was already fixed by #51603.

## Claims

- A request with adjacent multimodal items that can't share the encoder cache now finishes under speculative decoding instead of hanging. Before this change it hung whenever `gap < 2 * L`, where `L = num_prefill_lookahead`.
- Output doesn't change. With temperature 0 the text matches the no-spec baseline exactly, and no `Encoder cache miss` was observed.

## Validation

**E2E** (1x GB200, MRV2, async scheduling on, prefix caching off): `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`, MTP with `num_speculative_tokens=1` (L=1). Each request has two 3008x4032 images of 11844 tokens each; the encoder cache is 16384, so only one image fits at a time. I used raw prompts to control how many tokens sit between the two `<|image_pad|>` runs, and confirmed the placeholder offsets in the scheduler (gap=0 gives `[(4, 11844), (11848, 11844)]`).

| | gap=0 | gap=1 | gap=2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, MTP | **hang** (no completion in 300 s) | **hang** | OK |
| this PR, MTP | OK (2 runs) | OK | OK |
| main, no spec (baseline) | OK | OK | OK |

At temperature 0, every OK run with this PR produces the same text as the no-spec baseline for the same prompt: "The first image contains a red circle, and the second image contains a blue rectangle." MTP acceptance was 9/9 drafts in all spec runs.

<details>
<summary>Scheduler-level sweep (L x gap; image=600 tokens, cache=900)</summary>

| L \ gap | 0 | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (main) | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok |
| 1 (main) | hang | hang | ok | ok | ok |
| 3 (main) | hang | hang | hang | hang | ok |
| 1, 3 (this PR) | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok |

#59030 at `17d95d3eb8` gives the same results as main in this sweep.
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** Two places offset by the drafter look-ahead `L`, in opposite directions:

1. `_free_encoder_inputs` keeps item 1 until `num_computed_tokens >= end1 + L`. This was added in #46315.
2. When item 2 can't be allocated, `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` stops the chunk at `start2 - L`.

If `start2 - L < end1 + L`, then `num_computed_tokens` can never reach the point where item 1 is freed, so item 2 is never allocated.

**Fix.** Remove the `L` offset in both places:

- **Free** once `end <= num_computed_tokens - num_output_placeholders`, as without spec decode. Both the V1 and V2 gathers read the drafter window `[c + 1, c + k + 1)`, which is ahead of `num_computed_tokens`. Once the target has passed an item, neither the target nor the drafter reads it again. Rejection rollback is still covered by `num_output_placeholders`. Async scheduling has the same timing as the existing non-spec path.
- **Stop at `start2`** instead of `start2 - L`, and only in the `can_allocate` failure branch. The drafter's read-ahead then lands on the item that isn't encoded yet. Both runners already handle that case: they fall back to token embeddings via the `start_pos >= computed + scheduled` check added in #46315. The `disable_chunked_mm_input` rollback still applies the shift.

Both changes are needed. Either one alone only narrows the hang condition from `gap < 2L` to `gap < L`.

**Tradeoff.** When the cache is full, the drafter uses token embeddings instead of image embeddings for up to `L` positions at that chunk boundary. This can slightly lower acceptance for one step. Requests whose items fit in the cache are unaffected.

**Relation to #59030.** #59030 adds a mid-schedule release of a request's consumed inputs, but it keeps the `+L` retention margin (its last commit re-added it). That release can never fire at this deadlock point, which is why its results match main in the sweep above. This PR instead argues that the margin isn't needed. The requeue half of #59030 is independent of this PR and complementary to it.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for analysis, the patch, tests, and running the validation. I reviewed every changed line and the results above.

title: [Model][Qwen4Exp] FP8 QSA main KV cache on Ampere (sm_80, sm_86)
body:
## Summary

`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` crashes for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on Ampere (sm_80, sm_86): the QSA Triton kernels use an `fp8e4nv` pointer, which Triton supports only from sm_89. Below sm_89 this PR reads the e4m3 cache as bytes and decodes it exactly with a bit cast. Same flag and cache format; BF16 and sm_89+ do not change.

**Why Ampere:** vLLM already enables an FP8 KV cache on sm_80 for other backends (FlashInfer, #24577); this model's QSA path is the gap. We serve Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on 8× A100, where FP8 doubles the KV capacity, and @nkuhn-vmw runs it on 4× RTX 3090 (sm_86).

## Results (8× A100-40GB, TP8 + EP)

- Fixes the crash: 4 FP8 attention tests that fail on `main` at sm_80 now pass.
- KV cache capacity ×1.83 (1.16M → 2.13M tokens). sm_86 (4× RTX 3090, by @nkuhn-vmw): ×1.87, GSM8K unchanged.
- Attention kernel time, FP8 vs BF16 cache: 0.92–1.14×. End to end at concurrency 8, client TPOT p50 is 6 % higher with FP8 (see "Decode cost").
- Prompt-logprob difference FP8 vs BF16 is close to BF16 run-to-run noise (σ 0.115 vs 0.111 nats, 150k tokens).
- Serving the full MLPerf agentic dataset (multi-turn coding, prompts up to ~200k tokens), 3 runs per row:

| Concurrency | KV cache | Requests/s | TTFT p95 (s) | Prefix-cache hit | Prompt tokens received / computed in prefill, per run (M) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | BF16 | 1.15–1.24 | 1.1–1.3 | 97–98 % | 301–319 / 5.0–7.8 |
| 8 | FP8 | 1.20–1.23 | 1.2 | 98.5 % | 322–326 / 4.7–4.9 |
| 12 | BF16 | 0.96–1.09 | 18–27 | 90–92 % | 235–277 / 21–23 |
| 12 | FP8 | **1.59** | **1.5** | 98.5 % | **457–462 / 6.8–7.1** |
| 16 | BF16 | 0.58–0.64 | 73–83 | 73–77 % | 126–143 / 32–33 |
| 16 | FP8 | **1.58–1.63** | **7.5–10.4** | 96–97 % | **426–445 / 14–15** |

At concurrency 16, FP8 serves 2.7× the requests with ~9× lower p95 TTFT: it receives 3.4× more prompt tokens but computes less than half as many in prefill, because more prefixes stay cached. At concurrency 12, FP8 serves 1.5–1.6× the requests with 12–18× lower p95 TTFT and computes about a third as many prompt tokens in prefill. No preemptions in either arm. Pending: a prefix-caching-off control, and a run without our scheduler hook.

## Changes

- `ops/qsa.py`: one Triton helper, `_maybe_dequant`, chooses the decode by the cache tile's dtype: BF16 passes through, native e4m3 (sm_89+) upcasts to fp16, and `uint8` (the same e4m3 cache read as raw bytes below sm_89) is decoded with a bit cast (`2⁸` folded into the K/V scales on the host). Each K/V tile is decoded right after its load. On sm_80 FP8, 128-column / 4-warp tiles.
- `qsa.py`: on sm_89+ the uint8 cache is viewed as e4m3 once in `forward_qsa`; below sm_89 it stays `uint8`. Below sm_89 with FP8, skip the fused prepare/cache-write kernel (also an FP8 pointer); use the separate path.
- Byte decode: all 254 finite codes decode exactly (checked on A100, below). There is no CI test for it: CI has no sm_80 runner.

**Maintainer refactor (13 Oct, @gau-nernst, `a76baf2fd`…`3327e9bf1`), checked on A100.** It replaced the architecture flags with the dtype dispatch above, dropped the sm_80-only `[N, D]` + transpose K/V load, and interleaved load and dequant. On 1 × A100-SXM4-40GB, with the same synthetic reader inputs (2,048 selected tokens, TP8 geometry), the FP8 output is bitwise identical to the previous head at every row count, and all 254 finite codes decode exactly (the 2 NaN codes read as ±480, as before). | 8 | 0.156 | 0.148 | 0.150 | 0.96 |
| 32 | 0.179 | 0.171 | 0.171 | 0.95 |

<details>
<summary>NaN handling</summary>

**What this PR does.** Below sm_89, the decode places the e4m3 sign, exponent and mantissa bits into an fp16 and folds `2⁸` into the scales. All 254 finite codes are exact. The two NaN codes (0x7F, 0xFF) decode to ±1.875 · 2⁸ = ±480. The cache can only hold a NaN code if a NaN was written: the CUDA cache writer uses `__nv_cvt_float_to_fp8(..., __NV_SATFINITE, ...)`, which saturates finite overflow to ±448.

**Merged vLLM precedents with the same behaviour:**

| Path | How FP8 is decoded | NaN codes become |
|---|---|---|
| Marlin FP8, Ampere weights (#5975, `csrc/.../marlin/dequant.h`) | bits placed into fp16/bf16 fields, bias by one multiply | finite (±480) |
| CPU FP8 KV attention, AMX/AVX-512 (#39445, `cpu_attn_amx.hpp`) | payload placed into a bf16 field, bias `2¹²⁰` folded into the K/V scales on the host, as here | finite (±480); its writer also clamps NaN input to ±448, so no NaN code is stored |
| ROCm FP8 weights (`w8a8_utils.py`, `fp8_utils.py`) | e4m3fn → e4m3fnuz | the fnuz NaN pattern is set to 0 |

TurboQuant (#38479) handles Ampere differently: it stores keys in Triton's `fp8e4b15`, so its cache format depends on the architecture. This PR keeps one e4m3 format on all architectures.

**What this kernel does with NaN today, on every architecture** (from the code): a NaN value element makes only that output element NaN. A NaN key makes the row's softmax normalizer NaN; `has_values = normalizer > 0` is then false and the row is written as zeros. So a NaN key is already not propagated on sm_89+.

**NaN-preserving decode, measured and not included.** We tried two variants on one A100 against this PR's kernel, on the same inputs:

| Variant | FP8 kernel time vs this PR (8 / 32 / 80 / 128 / 512 / 1,024 / 2,048 rows) |
|---|---|
| per-tile check of `byte & 0x7F` over K and V, NaN row at the end | 1.02 / 1.22 / 1.59 / 1.69 / 2.03 / 2.15 / 2.19 |
| branch-free decode (`(low + 1) & 0x80` sets the top fp16 exponent bit) | 1.00 / 1.26 / 1.62 / 1.86 / 2.26 / 2.25 / 2.35 |

**Question for reviewers:** is ±480 acceptable under the precedents above, or should NaN handling for this kernel be addressed for all architectures in a follow-up?

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the accuracy trace</summary>

Each server runs alone on the 8 GPUs, one after another (BF16, BF16 again, FP8):

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --served-model-name flash-fp8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --enforce-eager --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}' --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "bf16"}' \
  --mamba-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32 \
  --kv-cache-dtype {bfloat16 | fp8}
```

Client steps (script below, sha256 `e8a77f55c7053dca05e7af47c0597c97b2feb96a3797f112900a6be271d957a2`):

```
python3 logprob_trace.py build   http://127.0.0.1:8000 out mlperf_agentic_inference_dataset.jsonl   # once, on the first BF16 server
python3 logprob_trace.py run     http://127.0.0.1:8000 out bf16_a    # then bf16_b and fp8, each on its own server
python3 logprob_trace.py compare out bf16_a bf16_b fp8
```

- `build` tokenizes through the server's `/tokenize` and fixes the prompt token ids once. Every server then gets the same ids, and `compare` checks their hashes.
- Prompt sources: the official MLPerf agentic dataset (sha256 above), and the Python standard library inside the vLLM image (`/usr/lib/python3.12/*.py`, sorted) for the code prompt and the needle haystack.
- `run` sends each prompt to `/v1/completions` with `max_tokens: 1, temperature: 0, prompt_logprobs: 1`. It keeps the logprob of the actual next prompt token at each position, and fails on a missing or non-finite value.
- `compare` reports, per prompt, the standard deviation and mean of the per-position difference, and the share of positions that differ by more than 1 nat.

```python
"""Per-position prompt-logprob trace and needle check against one running vLLM server (upstream #60602 evidence).

Method of vllm-project/vllm#55557: send identical prompt token ids with prompt_logprobs=1 at temperature 0, keep the
logprob of each actual next prompt token, and compare FP8-KV against BF16 with the BF16-vs-BF16 run-to-run noise as the
floor. Prompt ids are fixed once (build) and reused verbatim by every arm; each arm records the prompt hash it served.

This is a numerical diagnostic of the KV-cache dtype only (prefix caching and MTP off, eager). It is not a task-quality
or serving result. Every step fails loudly: a short source, a missing position or a non-finite logprob is an error.

  logprob_trace.py build   <base_url> <out_dir> <dataset.jsonl>
  logprob_trace.py run     <base_url> <out_dir> <arm>
  logprob_trace.py compare <out_dir> <arm_a> <arm_b> <arm_fp8>
"""
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

MODEL = "flash-fp8"
TARGETS = {"agentic_150k": 150_000, "code_30k": 30_000, "text_8k": 8_000}
NEEDLE_TOKENS = 125_000
NEEDLE_DEPTHS = (0.1, 0.5, 0.9)
NEEDLE = "The secret passphrase for the archive is amber-falcon-42."
NEEDLE_ANSWER = "amber-falcon-42"
QUESTION = "\n\nQuestion: What is the secret passphrase for the archive? Answer: The secret passphrase is"
CODE_ROOT = Path("/usr/lib/python3.12")
METADATA_TYPE = "dataset_metadata"  # the full dataset's header row, skipped as MLCommons Endpoints does
REQUEST_SECONDS = 1500


def post(base, path, body):
    request = urllib.request.Request(base + path, json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=REQUEST_SECONDS) as response:
        return json.loads(response.read())


def tokenize(base, text):
    return post(base, "/tokenize", {"model": MODEL, "prompt": text, "add_special_tokens": False})["tokens"]


def ids_sha256(ids):
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(ids).encode()).hexdigest()


def write_private(path, value):
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value))
    os.chmod(path, 0o600)


def code_text(limit_chars):
    parts, size = [], 0
    for path in sorted(CODE_ROOT.glob("*.py")):
        text = path.read_text(errors="replace")
        parts.append(text)
        size += len(text)
        if size >= limit_chars:
            return "\n".join(parts)
    raise ValueError(f"code source has {size} characters, fewer than {limit_chars}")


def agentic_text(dataset, limit_chars):
    """Messages of the longest conversations, as role-tagged text, until limit_chars."""
    conversations = {}
    for line in open(dataset):
        row = json.loads(line)
        if row.get("_type") == METADATA_TYPE:
            continue
        text = " ".join(str(row.get(key) or "") for key in ("content", "reasoning_content", "tool_calls"))
        conversations.setdefault(row["conversation_id"], []).append(f"[{row['role']}] {text}")
    parts, size = [], 0
    for conversation in sorted(conversations.values(), key=lambda c: -sum(map(len, c))):
        for message in conversation:
            parts.append(message)
            size += len(message)
            if size >= limit_chars:
                return "\n".join(parts)
    raise ValueError(f"dataset text has {size} characters, fewer than {limit_chars}")


def exactly(ids, count, name):
    if len(ids) < count:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: source gives {len(ids)} tokens, fewer than {count}")
    return ids[:count]


def build(base, out, dataset):
    out = Path(out)
    sources = {"agentic_150k": agentic_text(dataset, 1_200_000), "code_30k": code_text(300_000),
               "text_8k": agentic_text(dataset, 80_000)}
    prompts = {name: exactly(tokenize(base, sources[name]), TARGETS[name], name) for name in TARGETS}
    needle, question = tokenize(base, " " + NEEDLE + " "), tokenize(base, QUESTION)
    body = NEEDLE_TOKENS - len(needle) - len(question)
    haystack = exactly(tokenize(base, code_text(1_200_000)), body, "haystack")
    needles, positions = {}, {}
    for depth in NEEDLE_DEPTHS:
        name, at = f"needle_{int(depth * 100)}", int(body * depth)
        needles[name] = haystack[:at] + needle + haystack[at:] + question
        positions[name] = at
    write_private(out / "prompts.json", {"trace": prompts, "needle": needles})
    summary = {"lengths": {k: len(v) for k, v in {**prompts, **needles}.items()}, "needle_positions": positions,
               "sha256": {k: ids_sha256(v) for k, v in {**prompts, **needles}.items()}}
    write_private(out / "prompts-summary.json", summary)
    print(json.dumps(summary["lengths"]))


def trace(base, ids, name):
    result = post(base, "/v1/completions", {"model": MODEL, "prompt": ids, "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0,
                                            "prompt_logprobs": 1})
    choice, usage = result["choices"][0], result.get("usage") or {}
    rows = choice["prompt_logprobs"]
    if len(rows) != len(ids) or usage.get("prompt_tokens") != len(ids):
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: {len(rows)} logprob rows, usage {usage.get('prompt_tokens')}, sent {len(ids)}")
    values = []
    for position in range(1, len(ids)):
        chosen = (rows[position] or {}).get(str(ids[position]))
        if chosen is None or not math.isfinite(chosen["logprob"]):
            raise ValueError(f"{name}: no finite logprob for the prompt token at position {position}")
        values.append(chosen["logprob"])
    return values, {"usage": usage, "finish_reason": choice.get("finish_reason")}


def run(base, out, arm):
    out = Path(out)
    prompts = json.loads((out / "prompts.json").read_text())
    record = {"arm": arm, "trace": {}, "needle": {}, "seconds": {}, "api": {}, "sha256": {}}
    for name, ids in prompts["trace"].items():
        start = time.time()
        record["trace"][name], record["api"][name] = trace(base, ids, name)
        record["seconds"][name], record["sha256"][name] = time.time() - start, ids_sha256(ids)
    for name, ids in prompts["needle"].items():
        answer = post(base, "/v1/completions", {"model": MODEL, "prompt": ids, "max_tokens": 16, "temperature": 0})
        choice = answer["choices"][0]
        record["needle"][name] = {"text": choice["text"], "found": NEEDLE_ANSWER in choice["text"],
                                  "finish_reason": choice.get("finish_reason"), "usage": answer.get("usage")}
        record["sha256"][name] = ids_sha256(ids)
    write_private(out / f"{arm}.json", record)
    print(json.dumps({"arm": arm, "needle": {k: v["found"] for k, v in record["needle"].items()},
                      "seconds": record["seconds"]}))


def spread(first, second, name):
    if len(first) != len(second):
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: {len(first)} and {len(second)} positions differ")
    diffs = [b - a for a, b in zip(first, second)]
    mean = sum(diffs) / len(diffs)
    sigma = math.sqrt(sum((d - mean) ** 2 for d in diffs) / len(diffs))
    return {"positions": len(diffs), "sigma_nat": round(sigma, 4), "mean_nat": round(mean, 5),
            "share_over_1_nat": round(sum(abs(d) > 1 for d in diffs) / len(diffs), 5)}


def compare(out, arm_a, arm_b, arm_fp8):
    out = Path(out)
    a, b, f = (json.loads((out / f"{x}.json").read_text()) for x in (arm_a, arm_b, arm_fp8))
    if not a["sha256"] == b["sha256"] == f["sha256"]:
        raise ValueError("arms served different prompt ids")
    table = {name: {"bf16_noise": spread(a["trace"][name], b["trace"][name], name),
                    "fp8_vs_bf16": spread(a["trace"][name], f["trace"][name], name)} for name in a["trace"]}
    table["needle"] = {arm["arm"]: {k: v["found"] for k, v in arm["needle"].items()} for arm in (a, b, f)}
    write_private(out / "compare.json", table)
    print(json.dumps(table, indent=1))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    {"build": build, "run": run, "compare": compare}[sys.argv[1]](*sys.argv[2:])
```

```
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}' --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "bf16"}' \
  --mamba-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32 \

```

- Environment: `VLLM_ENABLE_CUDA_COMPATIBILITY=1`, `VLLM_CUDA_COMPATIBILITY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.9/compat` (host driver older than the image CUDA).
- **Not stock vLLM, in both arms:**
  - A `sitecustomize` hook replaces `EngineCore._should_throttle_prefills`: with DP1, new prefills are admitted only on every 16th scheduler step while requests are running, unless a prefill chunk is already running. Continuing prefill chunks are not delayed. It changes no model or kernel code.
  - The image's `torchcodec/__init__.py` raises `ImportError`, because torchcodec in the cu129 image needs `libnvrtc.so.13` and crashes vLLM start-up (#60406). Only text requests are served.
- The two arms differ only in `--kv-cache-dtype` and in this PR's two files.

</details>

Received = computed + reused.

| Concurrency | KV cache | Received (M), run 1 / 2 / 3 | Computed in prefill (M) | Reused from cache (M) | Computed per completed request |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | BF16 | 301 / 315 / 319 | 7.8 / 5.7 / 5.0 | 294 / 309 / 314 | 1.1k–1.9k |
| 8 | FP8, this PR | 322 / 324 / 326 | 4.7 / 4.9 / 4.9 | 317 / 319 / 321 | 1.1k |
| 12 | BF16 | 235 / 270 / 277 | 22.7 / 21.7 / 21.4 | 213 / 248 / 255 | 5.3k–6.5k |

Ranges are over the three runs. Requests/s and output tokens/s are whole-run averages (completed work ÷ tracked duration; see "Reproduce the serving runs"), not sampled rates. Latencies are the client's native per-request values. Prefix-cache hit and preemptions come from vLLM's `/metrics`, scraped about every 5 s and counted over each run's measurement window, located from the client's session markers (approximate); no counter reset occurred.

- **Concurrency 8:** the BF16 cache does not limit anything, and throughput is the same. FP8 median TTFT and TPOT are 3–7 % higher (the byte decode); its p99 range across runs is narrower.
- **Concurrency 12 and 16:** BF16 throughput goes down as load goes up (1.2 → 1.0 → 0.6 requests/s), and its prefix-cache hit falls (98 → 91 → 75 %). With FP8 the hit stays at 98.5 % at concurrency 12 and 96–97 % at 16. At 12, FP8 completes 1.5–1.6× the requests of BF16, with p95 TTFT 1.5 s instead of 18–27 s. At 16, FP8 completes 2.8× the requests and output tokens per second of BF16, with about 9× lower p95 TTFT. Neither arm preempts.
- Our reading: with BF16, the cached prefixes of conversations that are idle during a tool call are evicted and then computed again. This fits the data but is not proven by a direct eviction count.
- **Pending:** both arms at concurrency 20.
- An earlier edge-set pair (20 conversations, concurrency 16) ran an earlier version of this change on the 5 Oct nightly. The full-set runs above, with this PR's exact code, supersede it.

4. Metrics, as Endpoints `594612e6` computes them (`metrics/report.py`, `metrics_table.py`):
   - **Requests/s** = completed requests ÷ tracked duration. **Output tokens/s** = sum of output tokens of the completed requests ÷ the same duration. Output tokens are counted by the client's tokenizer on the streamed text.
   - The tracked duration runs from `session.start_performance_tracking` to the completion of the last tracked request: the 1-hour issue phase plus the drain (3,613–3,740 s in these runs). It is one value per run, not a sampled rate. The legacy LoadGen window applies only to Poisson load and is not used here. Example: BF16, concurrency 8, run 1: 4,156 requests ÷ 3,612.9 s = 1.150 requests/s.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Make AITER FlyDSL GDN prefill default on gfx942/gfx950
body:
## Overview

Under `--gdn-prefill-backend auto`, use the AITER FlyDSL GDN prefill backend from #57560 on gfx942 and gfx950, as agreed in that PR's review. It applies only to BF16 models with 128-dim linear-attention heads, and only when AITER is enabled and the build ships the FlyDSL kernels. Not a duplicate: `gh pr list --state open --search "gdn prefill flydsl"` finds no other PR that changes the default; #57560 added the opt-in backend, and #60659 changes the prefill kernels' internals, not which backend `auto` picks.

## Claims

* Lower time to first token by default for GDN models on MI300X and MI355X: −2.7% geomean on Qwen3-Next-80B (MI300X), −3.6% on Qwen3.8-2.4T (MI355X). Decode is unchanged.
* GSM8K is unchanged on Qwen3-Next (0.9606 → 0.9606).
* Anything FlyDSL cannot serve (other architecture, missing kernels, other head dims or dtype) stays on Triton/FLA under `auto`. `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` opts out.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_rocm_layout_dispatch.py
```

The new `test_auto_defaults_to_aiter_flydsl` fails against the old resolver and passes with this change. In a ROCm container without a GPU, `tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py` gives 12 passed, 2 skipped. The two skips are the on-device FlyDSL-vs-Triton numerics test from #57560, which this PR does not change. `ruff check` and `ruff format` (0.14.0) pass.

TTFT with FlyDSL (default) vs Triton, from this PR's earlier run and the opt-in runs in #57560:

| Hardware | Model | Mean TTFT | Accuracy, Triton → FlyDSL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MI300X, TP2 | `Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct` | −2.7% geomean over 4 points, ISL/OSL 8k/1k at c=4/16/64 and 60k/600 at c=4 | GSM8K flexible-extract 0.9606 → 0.9606 (8 fixed, 8 broken, McNemar p = 1.00) |
| MI355X, TP8 | `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4` | −3.6% median geomean over 16 cells | GPQA-Diamond 0.9192 → 0.9343; GSM8K 0.9787 → 0.9825 |
| MI300X, TP2 | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` | −1.9% geomean over 4 cells | GSM8K 0.9697 → 0.9712 |

## Details

One new `auto` branch in `_resolve_gdn_prefill_backend` returns `aiter_flydsl` when `on_mi3xx()` and the same conditions an explicit request must meet hold. Those conditions now live in one helper, `_aiter_flydsl_unsupported_reasons`. An explicit request still raises when the kernels are missing, and warns before falling back to Triton/FLA when the model is outside the gate. `test_gdn_rocm_layout_dispatch.py` pins `triton`, since it checks the Triton path and `auto` would now route it to FlyDSL.

The gain depends on the model: about −1% TTFT on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, against −3.6% on Qwen3.8-2.4T.

title: [Attention] Fetch MLA prefill workspace at use instead of init
body:
## Purpose

The TRTLLM-ragged and FlashInfer MLA prefill backends keep a view of the shared workspace from `__init__`. When a later user, such as the sparse indexer's profile, grows the workspace, that view keeps the old buffer alive as an orphan. On GLM-5.3 on B200 that's 394 MB of GPU memory nobody uses.

Both backends now reserve their size at init without keeping a view, and fetch it in `prepare_metadata`, once per step. FlashInfer rebuilds its wrappers if the workspace has moved. The builder runs outside the DBO micro-batch threads, so both still use the micro-batch 0 slot, as on main.

Sharing the workspace is safe: TRTLLM ragged runs with multi-CTA KV off and uses it only for per-launch softmax stats, and FlashInfer cutlass prefill never touches it (it has its own 32 MB buffer).

## Test Result

Memory: 1×B200, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 cut to 4 layers with dummy weights, fp8 KV, `--max-model-len 1048576`, TRTLLM-ragged prefill:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Available KV cache | 138.64 GiB | 139.02 GiB |
| GPU KV blocks | 861,476 | 863,866 |
| Orphaned 0.38 GiB block from `trtllm_ragged.py` `__init__` | present | gone |

- Greedy token ids and logprobs are bit-identical to main, with chunked-context prefill, on GLM-5.3 (TRTLLM-ragged) and DeepSeek-V2-Lite (FlashInfer prefill forced). FlashInfer wrappers are built once per backend instance, as on main.
- GSM8K, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 TP4: main 0.906, this PR 0.908.
- `tests/v1/attention/`: `test_mla_prefill_selector`, `test_mla_prefill_registry`, `test_mla_prefill_quant_output`, `test_mla_noncausal`, `test_sparse_mla_backends`, `test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla` and `test_mla_backends` all pass on B200.

- New CPU test `test_prefill_backend_does_not_pin_grown_workspace` (both backends) fails on main and passes here.
- Results above re-checked at 82731e58f4 (fetch in `prepare_metadata`): same memory, outputs bit-identical, `test_mla_backends.py` 1793 passed. DBO not run (needs a DeepEP / NIXL-EP all2all build); the workspace slot it uses matches main.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

Main is d80ddaac73; this PR is 82731e58f4.

```bash
VLLM_DEBUG_WORKSPACE=1 vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --load-format dummy --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": 4}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 16
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 4 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --enforce-eager --block-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 --max-concurrency 32 --seed 42
```
</details>

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Route by swap-row capacity, not the index-group workspace
body:
## Overview

HiSparse crashes when a batch has exactly `max_num_seqs * max_decode_query_len + 1` tokens. With `max_num_seqs=1` the engine fails at startup, and with `max_num_seqs=2` a 3-token prompt crashes at runtime:

```
ValueError: HiSparse swap rows exceed the configured speculative decode capacity: stop=2, capacity=1.
```

Part of #60072.

## Claims

- HiSparse now routes a batch to `swap_in` only when the batch fits the swap rows that `swap_in` consumes. Larger batches take the existing all-resident fallback.
- No performance impact: the change is a Python-side routing comparison against a fixed size. Batches up to the swap capacity take the same path as before; only the single size that crashed changes path.

## Validation

1×H200, upstream `main` 242e4213fc. Repro (tiny DeepSeek-V3.2, dummy weights):

```python
import sys
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.config import AttentionConfig, HiSparseConfig, KVTransferConfig

llm = LLM(
    "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2", load_format="dummy",
    hf_overrides={"num_hidden_layers": 8, "hidden_size": 256, "intermediate_size": 512,
                  "num_attention_heads": 8, "num_key_value_heads": 1, "n_routed_experts": 8,
                  "num_experts_per_tok": 2, "index_topk": 128},
    max_model_len=320, block_size=64, max_num_seqs=int(sys.argv[1]),
    enable_prefix_caching=False, gpu_memory_utilization=0.3,
    kv_transfer_config=KVTransferConfig(kv_connector="HiSparseConnector", kv_role="kv_both",
                                        kv_connector_extra_config={"host_pool_gib": 1}),
    attention_config=AttentionConfig(hisparse_config=HiSparseConfig()),
)
for n in (2, 3, 200):
    llm.generate([{"prompt_token_ids": list(range(100, 100 + n))}],
                 SamplingParams(max_tokens=8, ignore_eos=True))
```

| Command | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `python repro.py 1` | Startup fails during piecewise CUDA-graph capture at size 2: `stop=2, capacity=1` | All 3 prompts complete |
| `python repro.py 2` | Startup succeeds; the 3-token prompt crashes: `stop=3, capacity=2` | All 3 prompts complete |
| 61-layer DeepSeek-V3.2 (8 experts, dummy weights), `max_num_seqs=1`, 16k context, 256 output tokens, `host_pool_gib=32` | Startup fails: `stop=2, capacity=1` | Runs; TPOT 18.4 ms over 3 reps |

Tests on this PR (each command run separately):

- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "hisparse or index_group"`: 40 passed. The regression case `test_hisparse_resident_prefill_uses_attention_block_stride` fails on `main` and passes with this PR.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py`: 9 passed
- `pytest tests/v1/core -k hisparse`: 72 passed
- `pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: 4 passed

## Details

**Root cause.** `HiSparseMLAIndexGroup.convert_logical_to_physical_topk` sends a batch to `swap_in` whenever the batch fits `physical_topk_indices`. That index-group workspace is allocated with one spare row (`max_decode_rows + 1`). `swap_in`, however, writes into the HiSparse runtime's shared swap rows, which hold exactly `min(max_num_batched_tokens, max_num_seqs * max_decode_query_len)` rows. A batch one token larger than the swap capacity therefore passes the routing check and then overflows in `_step_rows`.

With `max_num_seqs=1`, the CUDA-graph capture sizes are `[1, 2]`. The 2-token piecewise capture follows the all-resident prefill path into this conversion, so the engine fails at startup. With `max_num_seqs=2`, capture sizes `[1, 2, 4]` skip 3 tokens, so the failure only appears when a real 3-token batch arrives.

**Fix.** Route on `HiSparseRuntime.max_swap_rows`, the capacity that `swap_in` actually consumes. The non-HiSparse `SparseMLAIndexGroup` does not change.

title: [Perf][MiniMax-M3] MSA prefill attends with the E4M3 query; bump fmha_sm100 to 968061a
body:
## Overview With CUTLASS MSA sparse decode on (an NVFP4 KV cache, or an FP8 E4M3 cache with the `CUTLASS_MSA` decode backend), the fused QK-norm/RoPE/insert kernel writes MiniMax-M3's query only in E4M3. `MiniMaxM3SparseMSAImpl` then dequantized it back into the BF16 query buffer before every prefill. Both `fmha_sm100` prefill kernels take an E4M3 query natively, so prefill now passes it through as is. The PR also bumps `fmha_sm100` (vllm-project/MSA) from `be4a52a` to `968061a`. The new pin includes MSA's Blackwell prefill port, which now serves an E4M3 query over vLLM's packed K|V pages (vllm-project/MSA#32). ## Claims - MSA prefill attention is **26–37% faster with an FP8 KV cache** and **8–13% faster with an NVFP4 KV cache** than on main (per layer on GB300; table below). - Prefill no longer makes a BF16 copy of the query. Only the Triton decode fallback still reads the dequantized query. - BF16 caches and the default Triton decode backend for FP8 caches still pass a BF16 query, so their path is unchanged. ## Validation **Tests:** on GB300 (SM103, CUDA 13.4, `fmha_sm100` built from the new pin), `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_msa_cutlass_sparse_decode.py tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_fp8_triton_indexer.py tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py tests/kernels/test_minimax_m3_sparse_attn_fp8_scale.py tests/kernels/test_fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py` gives **240 passed, 45 skipped**. All skips are ROCm-only tests. The MSA test file runs in CI on B200. - New `test_msa_prefill_reads_query_fp8_over_fp8_cache[tp1|tp4]` covers FP8-cache prefill, including chunks over cached context, with CUTLASS decode on. It checks that `sparse_atten_func` receives the E4M3 query and that the output matches Triton on the dequantized query. - `test_msa_prefill_nvfp4_matches_triton_on_dequantized_cache` now checks that `sparse_atten_nvfp4_kv_func` receives the E4M3 query. Its reference is now the cache as an E4M3-query kernel reads it (see Details). - Both prefill tests require all but 1e-4 of the elements within atol/rtol 0.05 and bound the rest at 0.25. The E4M3 probabilities are rounded per split, and splits follow the SM count, so a rare element lands just past 0.05: 1 of 4.1M on B200 CI. On GB300 over 16 seeds the worst case is 2.4e-7 of the elements and 0.07 max abs error. - On the old code, all four prefill cases fail with `[torch.bfloat16] == [torch.float8_e4m3fn]`. **Performance:** `MiniMaxM3SparseMSAImpl.forward` on prefill-only batches (`build_k2q_csr` + attention + combine, plus the dequant where the query is BF16). GB300, one request, top-k 16, page 128. Each value is the median of 3×50 iterations after warmup; spread ≤1%, except ±5% on the first FP8 row of the main run. | KV cache | Q heads / KV heads | Query tokens @ cached context | main (MSA `be4a52a`, BF16 q) | pin bump only (BF16 q) | this PR (E4M3 q) | |---|---|---|---:|---:|---:| | FP8 | 16 / 1 (TP4) | 8k @ 0 | 411 µs | 368 µs | 303 µs (-26%) | | FP8 | 16 / 1 | 8k @ 32k | 462 µs | 439 µs | 314 µs (-32%) | | FP8 | 16 / 1 | 16k @ 112k | 801 µs | 754 µs | 530 µs (-34%) | | FP8 | 64 / 4 (TP1) | 8k @ 0 | 1423 µs | 1320 µs | 891 µs (-37%) | | FP8 | 64 / 4 | 8k @ 32k | 1498 µs | 1423 µs | 985 µs (-34%) | | NVFP4 | 16 / 1 | 8k @ 0 | 379 µs | 375 µs | 342 µs (-10%) | | NVFP4 | 16 / 1 | 8k @ 32k | 457 µs | 458 µs | 420 µs (-8%) | | NVFP4 | 16 / 1 | 16k @ 112k | 798 µs | 795 µs | 695 µs (-13%) | | NVFP4 | 64 / 4 | 8k @ 0 | 1411 µs | 1395 µs | 1255 µs (-11%) | | NVFP4 | 64 / 4 | 8k @ 32k | 1491 µs | 1491 µs | 1317 µs (-12%) | Percentages are relative to main. With the new pin, a BF16 query over the FP8 cache also reaches the Blackwell port, but with BF16 MMAs. The E4M3 query gives the bulk of the FP8 gain at either pin: on main's pin alone it is 13–24% (411 → 356, 462 → 367, 801 → 623, 1423 → 1083, 1498 → 1162 µs).
Benchmark script (run from the repo root with PYTHONPATH=.) ```python """Per-layer MSA prefill attention (impl.forward) with an E4M3 query.""" import math from types import SimpleNamespace import torch import tests.kernels.attention.test_minimax_m3_msa_cutlass_sparse_decode as t from vllm.forward_context import ForwardContext, override_forward_context from vllm.models.minimax_m3.common.sparse_attention import ( MiniMaxM3SparseMetadata, MiniMaxM3SparsePrefillMetadata) BLK, TOPK = 128, 16 def case(q_len, seq_len, hkv, g): pos = torch.arange(seq_len - q_len, seq_len, device="cuda") visible = pos // BLK + 1 vmax = int(visible.max()) r = torch.rand(q_len, hkv, vmax, device="cuda", generator=g) ar = torch.arange(vmax, device="cuda") r = torch.where(ar < visible[:, None, None] - 1, r, -1.0) r = torch.where(ar == visible[:, None, None] - 1, 2.0, r) k = min(TOPK, vmax) val, idx = r.topk(k, dim=-1) topk = torch.where(val >= 0, idx, -1).int() if k < TOPK: topk = torch.cat([topk, topk.new_full((q_len, hkv, TOPK - k), -1)], -1) pages = math.ceil(seq_len / BLK) block_table = torch.randperm(pages, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")[None] seq = torch.tensor([seq_len], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") cu_q = torch.tensor([0, q_len], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") cu_k = torch.tensor([0, seq_len], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") p = MiniMaxM3SparsePrefillMetadata( cu_seqlens_q=cu_q, cu_seqlens_k=cu_k, seq_lens=seq, context_lens=seq - q_len, block_table=block_table, max_query_len=q_len, max_seq_len=seq_len, total_kv_blocks=pages) md = MiniMaxM3SparseMetadata( seq_lens=seq, max_seq_len=seq_len, slot_mapping=torch.empty(q_len, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda"), num_actual_tokens=q_len, num_decodes=0, num_decode_tokens=0, num_prefills=1, num_prefill_tokens=q_len, prefill=p) return md, topk, pages def bench(fn, iters=50): for _ in range(10): fn() torch.cuda.synchronize() s, e = torch.cuda.Event(True), torch.cuda.Event(True) s.record() for _ in range(iters): fn() e.record() torch.cuda.synchronize() return s.elapsed_time(e) / iters * 1e3 g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0) for kv_dtype in ("fp8", "nvfp4"): for hq, hkv, q_len, ctx in ((16, 1, 8192, 0), (16, 1, 8192, 32768), (16, 1, 16384, 114688), (64, 4, 8192, 0), (64, 4, 8192, 32768)): md, topk, pages = case(q_len, ctx + q_len, hkv, g) k_scale = torch.tensor(1.0, device="cuda") v_scale = torch.tensor(1.0, device="cuda") if kv_dtype == "nvfp4": kv_cache, _ = t._make_nvfp4_kv_cache(pages, hkv, "nvfp4", k_scale, v_scale) else: kv_cache = (torch.randn(pages, hkv, BLK, 256, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn) layer = SimpleNamespace(layer_name="l", topk_indices_buffer=topk, _q_scale_float=0.5, _k_scale=k_scale, _v_scale=v_scale) qf = torch.randn(q_len, hq * 128, device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn) query = torch.empty(q_len, hq * 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") out = torch.empty_like(query) impl = t.MiniMaxM3SparseMSAImpl( num_heads=hq, head_size=128, scale=t.SM_SCALE, num_kv_heads=hkv, kv_cache_dtype=kv_dtype, topk_blocks=TOPK, sparse_block_size=BLK, msa_decode_backend="cutlass") assert impl.use_cutlass_decode with override_forward_context(ForwardContext(no_compile_layers={}, attn_metadata={"l": md}, slot_mapping={})): bench(lambda: impl.forward(layer, query, kv_cache, out, query_fp8=qf), iters=200) ts = [bench(lambda: impl.forward(layer, query, kv_cache, out, query_fp8=qf)) for _ in range(3)] print(f"{kv_dtype} H{hq}/{hkv} q{q_len} ctx{ctx}: " + " ".join(f"{x:.1f}" for x in ts) + " us") ```
**No end-to-end accuracy eval or serving benchmark** is included; validation is the kernel-level numerics and per-layer timings above. ## Details **Kernel capability (MSA `968061a`; same at `be4a52a` except the Blackwell port):** - `sparse_atten_func` accepts an FP8 E4M3 query over FP8 E4M3 K/V and runs FP8 QK/PV MMAs, on the Blackwell port when eligible. The BF16-Q × FP8-K/V mode stages K/V up to BF16 instead. - `sparse_atten_nvfp4_kv_func` accepts a BF16 or E4M3 query. With E4M3 it dequantizes each NVFP4 `code × block_scale` to E4M3 instead of BF16, and applies the K global scale to the scores and the V global scale in the combine. **Scales:** `q_scale` folds into `softmax_scale`. The FP8 cache is written with unit scales and the NVFP4 global scales are passed as before, so K/V scale handling is unchanged. **Numerics:** the E4M3-query kernels round the softmax probabilities to E4M3. The NVFP4 kernel also rounds K/V to E4M3. On the NVFP4 test (TP1): - Against the E4M3-staged cache: max abs error 0.06, and 0 of 4.1M elements outside atol/rtol 0.05. - Against the exact BF16 dequantization: max 0.14, with 122 of 4.1M elements outside that tolerance. This is why the test's reference changed. On the FP8 test the max abs error is ≈0.03. **Limitations:** validated on SM103. SM100 is covered by the CI kernel job. The E4M3-query NVFP4 kernel is untested on SM107 here. **MSA pin bump (`be4a52a` → `968061a`):** - The functions vLLM calls keep their signatures: `fmha_sm100`, `fmha_sm100_plan`, `_fmha_sm100(_plan)`, `sparse_topk_select`, `sparse_atten_func`, `sparse_atten_nvfp4_kv_func` and `nvfp4_head_slot_views`. - vLLM's decode plans still pin `decode_backend="kv_mode3"`. The new `prefill_backend` plan option only routes sparse-prefill plans built through `fmha_sm100_plan`, which vLLM does not use. - The cmake install list adds the files the package now imports: `_jit_cache.py`, `msa_warmup.py`, `q8kv4_prefill_adapter.py` and `prefill_q8kv4/`. **Duplicate check:** no open PR touches the MSA prefill query or `fmha_sm100.cmake`. Open MiniMax-M3 MSA PRs (#55838, #56932, #59979) change decode or indexer metadata only. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, implement, test and benchmark this change. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

title: [Spec Decode] Skip metadata build for dflash/dspark when all model backends support it
body: # Context Continuing the effort from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58463 to remove unnecessary attention metadata rebuilds before FULL cudagraph replays for draft model-based speculators. I found an opportunity to use the same `supports_draft_decode_metadata_update` flag to gate updating the metadata within the captured decode step for DFlash/DSpark, reducing GPU kernel launch overhead. # This PR Adds support for skipping the full attention metadata rebuild before replaying the uniform decode cudagraph. Previously, only the `TargetDependentARSpeculator` was leveraging the `update_draft_decode_metadata` operations for its attention backends to update the attention metadata in a cudagraph-safe way. In this PR, I move that logic for deciding draft model eligibility (`supports_update_decode_metadata`) for this optimization to the base class `DraftModelSpeculator`, and then i have both `TargetDependentARSpeculator` and `DFlashSpeculator` check this eligibility. If True, capture the `_update_draft_decode_metadata` op in the graph before the draft model forward. Otherwise, rebuild the attention metadata eagerly via `_build_uniform_attn_metadata` before replaying the graph. This optimization has been enabled for DeepSeek V4.1 + DSpark, as verified below. ## Profile Captured while serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark on 4xGB200: **Before** **After** ## Benchmarks / Evals **Setup (both subsections).** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DSpark with `num_speculative_tokens=5`, 4x GB200 (TP4), `--max-model-len 102400 --max-num-seqs 128 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --no-enable-prefix-caching`, `--attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}'`, adaptive verification off, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. Speed-Bench is 2K/2K (`throughput_16k`, `low_entropy`), with prompts scaled 8x concurrency (min 16), seed 0, and a fresh server per arm. In both subsections the PR server logged no "cannot update draft decode metadata" warning, so the in-graph metadata update was active. ### Greedy draft sampling Baseline is `main` at `b6d8e8afd9`; PR is `1abc890148`. **Speed-Bench, temperature 0.** Each value is the mean of repeated runs: 3 runs at concurrency 1, 2 runs at 16 and 64. | Concurrency | ITL p50 base (ms) | ITL p50 PR (ms) | Δ | TPOT p50 base (ms) | TPOT p50 PR (ms) | Output tok/s base | Output tok/s PR | Δ | Accept. len base | Accept. len PR | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 6.96 | 6.94 | -0.3% | 1.91 | 1.90 | 521.2 | 520.7 | -0.1% | 3.760 | 3.747 | | 16 | 16.11 | 16.04 | -0.4% | 4.92 | 4.91 | 3144.3 | 3113.5 | -1.0% | 3.775 | 3.755 | | 64 | 30.37 | 30.36 | 0.0% | 9.88 | 9.94 | 6249.0 | 6250.2 | 0.0% | 3.795 | 3.795 | Step time is unchanged at every concurrency. As with MTP in #58463, the host work this removes is not on the critical path for this model at TP4. Acceptance length differs between arms by at most 0.02, while runs of the same arm vary by up to 0.16 at concurrency 1. **AIME25** (MQA, 2 epochs x 30 problems, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, max 98304 tokens, 64 concurrent): | Arm | Exact match | pass@2 | Samples | Request errors | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | base | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 60 | 0 | | PR | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 60 | 0 | Accuracy is identical. Every sample includes reasoning, with median completion lengths of 5.3k tokens (base) and 4.9k (PR). ### Probabilistic draft sampling `--speculative-config` adds `"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"`. Baseline is `main` at `240785b82c`; PR is `6065f7c37c` (this branch rebased onto that baseline). **Speed-Bench, temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0.** Each value is the mean of 2 runs. Individual acceptance lengths are in brackets. | Concurrency | ITL p50 base (ms) | ITL p50 PR (ms) | Δ | TPOT p50 base (ms) | TPOT p50 PR (ms) | Output tok/s base | Output tok/s PR | Δ | Accept. len base | Accept. len PR | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 6.89 | 6.86 | -0.4% | 1.95 | 1.86 | 505.1 | 514.8 | +1.9% | 3.60 [3.68, 3.52] | 3.66 [3.71, 3.61] | | 16 | 16.05 | 16.02 | -0.2% | 5.01 | 5.06 | 3051.8 | 3046.9 | -0.2% | 3.64 [3.65, 3.62] | 3.65 [3.65, 3.65] | | 64 | 30.51 | 30.50 | 0.0% | 10.28 | 10.43 | 6061.4 | 5972.4 | -1.5% | 3.66 [3.65, 3.67] | 3.67 [3.66, 3.68] | Median ITL matches within 0.03 ms. The -1.5% throughput at concurrency 64 comes from a single PR run (5930 vs 6015 tok/s for the other); output lengths vary between runs at temperature 1.0. Acceptance length is equal or higher for the PR at every concurrency, and the largest gap (+0.06 at concurrency 1) is smaller than the baseline's own run-to-run spread (0.16). **gsm8k** (1319 questions, 5-shot `/v1/completions`, temperature 1.0, max 512 tokens, 64 concurrent). Acceptance is computed from the server's spec-decode counters over the eval: | Arm | Accuracy | Invalid | Accept. len | Per-position acceptance (0-4) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---| | base | 0.838 | 1.1% | 3.296 | 0.779 / 0.605 / 0.423 / 0.298 / 0.190 | | PR | 0.835 | 1.1% | 3.299 | 0.782 / 0.603 / 0.421 / 0.298 / 0.195 | Accuracy is within 4 questions, and per-position acceptance shows no drop at later draft positions, which is where a stale non-causal window would show up first.
