title: [ROCm][Qwen4Exp] Remove the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next TEP8 MXFP4 emulation guard
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Removes `_requires_qwen38_tep8_emulation`, which forces OCP MX emulation for Qwen3.8 Flash Next's (`amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`) routed experts at TEP8 on gfx950 when the fused shared expert is off. The guard was added because AITER padded the MoE width from 640 to 768 for that shape and the native W4A4 kernel lost accuracy. Since #55104 aligns the W4A4 intermediate to 128, Flash Next's width stays at 640 with no pad, and the native kernel is as accurate as emulation and about twice as fast.

Existing work:
* #55104 removed the pad that the guard worked around, and on its own fixes Flash Next's accuracy at EP4 and TEP8 (measured below) and at TP1 (0.9651, #55104 on `nightly-43b4aaea`).
* The first revision of this PR also changed the pad rounding at MoE `tp_size == 1`. With #55104 merged, that is a no-op for Flash Next, so it is dropped here.

## Claims

- At TEP8 with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0`, the only configuration where the guard fires, the native AITER W4A4 kernel matches emulation's accuracy (GSM8K 0.9651 vs 0.9629) at 2.3x the output throughput at 8k/1k concurrency 4 (362 vs 158 tok/s) and 1.9x at concurrency 32 (1399 vs 741).
- No change for the checkpoint card's recipe: with the fused shared expert each rank holds 65 local experts, the guard requires exactly 64, so it never fired there.
- No change for any other shape: the guard matched only `E=512, H=2560, N=640` at EP8 on gfx950.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (MI355X, gfx950, `nightly-5555a2d8` with this PR): 5 passed.

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/quantization/test_gfx950_moe.py
```

`test_qwen38_tep8_selects_native_aiter` replaces the guard's two tests: the TEP8 shape now selects `AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4` under both `auto` and `aiter`.

**Accuracy**, GSM8K 5-shot, all 1319 questions, MI355X, the checkpoint card's recipe, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-5555a2d8` vs the same image with this PR, one run per cell. Exact match, higher is better:

| config | stock | this PR |
| ------ | ----- | ------- |
| TEP8, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0` | 0.9629 (emulation, guard hit) | 0.9651 (native) |
| TEP8, the card's recipe | 0.9644 (native, guard not hit) | unchanged |
| EP4 (TP4 + `--enable-expert-parallel`) | 0.9636 (native) | unchanged |

Flexible-extract; strict-match for the first row is 0.9636 → 0.9659. Standard error is about 0.005.

**Throughput**, TEP8 with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0`, emulation (stock) vs native (this PR), random dataset, one run per cell. Output tok/s is higher-is-better, mean TPOT lower-is-better:

| ISL / OSL | Conc | Output tok/s, emulation → native | Mean TPOT (ms), emulation → native |
| --------- | ---- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| 8192 / 1024 | 4 | 158 → 362 | 24.2 → 9.5 |
| 8192 / 1024 | 32 | 741 → 1399 | 38.7 → 20.0 |
| 128 / 8 | 1 | 40 → 90 | 21.2 → 7.2 |

**Reproduce:**

```bash
# plus the checkpoint card's ROCm environment, identical in both arms
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0 \
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 262144 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template \
  --model_args model=amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,max_gen_toks=2048,num_concurrent=32
```

## Details

* **Why the guard is stale.** Its docstring says AITER pads `N` to 768 for this shape. Since #55104 the W4A4 intermediate is aligned to 128, so 640 is stored as is, with no pad. The native kernel at 640 is accurate (first accuracy row), so CK-Tile's `inter_dim % 256` scale issue does not show up for this shape.
* **When the guard fired.** It matches `num_local_experts == 64`. The fused shared expert adds one local expert per rank (`ExpertMapManager`), so with the card's recipe the count is 65 and the native kernel already ran; only `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0` hit the guard.
* Only the ROCm MXFP4 oracle changes; nothing changes on CUDA.

**Limitations and CI gaps.**

* gfx950 only. The W4A4 MXFP4 MoE path does not run on gfx942.
* The end-to-end image applied the previous revision of this PR, which also changed the pad rounding at MoE `tp_size == 1`. With #55104, Flash Next's pad there is 0, so that part did nothing in these runs; the guard removal is the same code.
* The unit tests run in the AMD kernels CI job. The accuracy and throughput runs happened outside CI.

title: [Chore] Port more vendored configs and processors to upstream Transformers
body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #60623. Ports the vLLM code for 6 more models to the upstream Transformers 5.16.1 schemas, and deletes their vendored configs and processors (9 files). Also fixes registry entries that kept models out of CI.

Related PRs:
- **#61392:** the DeepSeek-V4 part of this PR, split out.
- **#61813:** the MiniMax-M3 part of this PR, split out.
- **#61883:** the Inkling part of this PR, split out.
- **#47438:** a stale draft (last updated 2026-07-16) with a partial OpenCUA fix. This PR supersedes it.

## Claims

- Deletes the vendored configs for `step3p5`, `muse_glimmer`, `cosmos3_edge`, `colpali`, `colmodernvbert` and `qianfan_ocr`. It also deletes the vendored `cosmos3_edge` and `muse_glimmer` processors, and the model code now reads the upstream fields:
  - **Step3p5:** reads `layer_types` / `mlp_layer_types` / per-type `rope_parameters`. Upstream `Step3p7TextConfig` is registered in `_CONFIG_REGISTRY`, because the hub remote code fails validation.
  - **MuseGlimmer and Cosmos3-Edge:** they consume upstream processor outputs. Cosmos3-Edge reorders upstream's merge-window patches back to raster order before SigLIP2.
  - **ColPali:** reads PaliGemma from `vlm_config`.
  - **Qianfan-OCR:** a small adapter maps the upstream vision fields onto InternViT's.
  - **ColModernVBERT:** `ModernVBertModel` is mapped to `ColModernVBertForRetrieval`.
- **Fixes:**
  - **ColModernVBERT:** the vendored config dropped the checkpoint's sliding-window `rope_theta` (160000 → 10000). vLLM now matches the HF reference.
  - **Step-3.5-Flash MTP:** built with an `IndexError` before; it now builds.
  - **InternS1-Pro:** failed to initialize (`model_config` was not set).
  - **OpenCUA:** Transformers v5 builds a processor's sub-processors from its `__init__` signature, which here only exposed `tokenizer`, so the processor had no `image_processor`. Fixed by overriding `get_attributes`.
  - **Kimi-K2.5:** the spec-decode image token is now read from `image_token_id`. `ModelConfig.is_quantized()` now uses the arch config, so it sees quantization configs nested in `text_config`.
- Renames the vendored `InternVL{,Image,Video}Processor` to `InternVLChat*`, so they stop shadowing the upstream classes.
- **Registry entries CI was skipping:**
  - FireRedASR2, FunASR and InternS1 caps removed; they work on Transformers v5.
  - Isaac and InternS1-Pro caps narrowed to the HF comparison.
  - Phi-4-reasoning-vision and OpenCUA pinned to the compatible `refs/pr/8` and `refs/pr/10` (OpenCUA's cap narrowed to the HF comparison).
  - Cohere2-MoE switched to the renamed `CohereLabs/North-Mini-Code-1.0`.
- **Kept vendored:**
  - `qwen3_asr`: upstream silently loads the original nested checkpoints with default sizes.
  - Step3p7 and MiniMax-M3 processors: upstream tiles differently, or lacks the opt-in resize modes.

## Validation

`main` vs this branch on CPU, `transformers` 5.19.0. Each checkpoint's config and meta-device model build were dumped with `.agents/skills/transformers-upgrade/scripts/` and diffed.

| Checkpoint | Model diff vs `main` |
|---|---|
| Step-3.5-Flash, Step-3.7-Flash (+ MTP drafts) | 0 |
| Cosmos3-Edge | 0 params and modules. `num_layers` goes 56 → 28: the attention layers only, as Nemotron-H no longer counts MLP blocks. |
| Muse-Glimmer-30B (+ DFlash drafter) | 0 params. Constant `use_qk_norm` / `use_output_gate` flags dropped. |
| colpali-v1.3-hf, Qianfan-OCR | 0 |
| colmodernvbert-merged | sliding-window `rope_theta` 10000 → 160000 (the fix above). vs HF fp32: max abs diff 0.39 → 8e-5. |

Processor outputs, bit-identical to `main` unless noted:
- **Cosmos3-Edge:** pixels are identical after the raster reorder.
- **Qianfan, ColPali, ColModernVBERT:** identical.
- **Muse-Glimmer:** upstream's torchvision LANCZOS differs from PIL by at most 1 uint8 level on about 0.3% of pixels.

```bash
pytest tests/transformers_utils tests/config tests/models/test_registry.py tests/tokenizers_ tests/test_config.py  # failures identical to main (environment: no Ray/CUDA on the test host)
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k "<touched models>"  # 96 passed, 9 skipped
```

Pending on GPU:
- **Evals:** ColModernVBERT (`tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_colmodernvbert.py`) and Muse-Glimmer image/video.
- **Smoke tests:** Step-3.5-Flash with MTP.
- **`tests/models/test_initialization.py`** for the touched architectures.

title: [Bugfix][EC Connector] Don't create hash directories on cache-miss lookups in ECExampleConnector
body:
## Purpose

`ECExampleConnector.has_cache_item()` resolves the safetensors path via
`_generate_filename_debug()`, which auto-creates the `<mm_hash>/` directory.
Since `has_cache_item()` is called from the scheduler's encoder-input
admission check and from `update_state_after_alloc()` on every multimodal
allocation, **every probed-but-missed hash leaves an empty directory in
shared storage**. On a long-lived deployment the EC storage root accumulates
one empty directory per unique missed hash, making the cache impossible to
inspect and polluting any listing-based tooling/backup jobs.

Fixes #60820

## Approach

Keep auto-creation on the **save** path (where the directory is actually
needed) and disable it on the **lookup** path:

- `_found_match_for_mm_data()` now passes `create_folder=False` to
  `_generate_filename_debug()`.
- `_generate_filename_debug()` gains a `create_folder: bool = True`
  parameter, forwarded to `_generate_foldername_debug()`. Defaults are
  unchanged, so `save_caches()` / `start_load_caches()` behavior is
  identical.

No behavioral change beyond the filesystem side effect.

## Testing

- Added `test_has_cache_item_miss_creates_no_folder` to the existing
  `tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_ec_example_connector.py`: a cache-miss
  lookup leaves no empty folder in shared storage.
- Also verified on a live A100 EPD testbed against a producer-role
  connector: `VERIFY-OK`.

## Notes

- Observed on a live deployment; the same code paths exist on current main.
- `start_load_caches` is untouched: it only loads hashes that
  `has_cache_item()` has already confirmed to exist.

title: [HiSparse] Prefault the shared host pool in parallel

Related to #60072.

Earlier tests on 4 H200s with a 128 GiB pool showed about 35% faster pool setup. Validation at `0db43832fa` on 2 H100s: 123 worker, shared-region, and KV-layout tests passed, along with two-worker failure, GPU-copy, and cleanup checks.

Full GLM startup time has not been measured.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix][MLA] Fix FP8 MLA prefill unpad for interleave-padded heads
body:
## Overview
The gfx950 FP8 asm MLA prefill pads heads to a multiple of 16. When the target is a multiple of the real head count (8 → 16, e.g. Kimi-K2.x at TP8), `get_mla_padded_q` uses `repeat_interleave`, but the output was sliced back as `[:, :num_heads]`, which is only correct for tile padding. The model then attends with the wrong heads and produces garbage. Introduced by #51040.

## Claims
- Restores accuracy for interleave-padded head counts: Kimi-K2.6 MXFP4 TP8 GSM8K 0.027 → 0.933.
- No performance change: same kernels; the unpad copy is still one kernel at the same cost.
- Adds the 8-head (interleaved) case to `test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_prefill.py`.

## Validation
Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4, TP8, MI355X, fp8 KV cache. GSM8K 5-shot, `lm_eval --model local-completions ... --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5`, num_concurrent=64:

| | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| Before (upstream main) | 0.0273 ± 0.0045 | 0.0235 ± 0.0042 |
| After (this PR) | 0.9333 ± 0.0069 | 0.9333 ± 0.0069 |

Torch profiler, random 1024/1024, 64 prompts, concurrency 64: 40 kernels per prefill MoE layer before and after.

Unit test on MI355X: `pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_prefill.py`

| Code under test | Result |
|---|---|
| This PR | 12 passed |
| Upstream unpad, with the new test cases | 2 failed, 10 passed: only `test_fp8_prefill_matches_reference[128-8]` and `[512-8]` fail |

<details>
<summary>Failure details on the upstream unpad</summary>

- `[128-8]`: mismatched elements 81,670 / 131,072 (62.3%), greatest absolute difference 4.5 (atol 0.1)
- `[512-8]`: mismatched elements 230,240 / 524,288 (43.9%), greatest absolute difference 4.5 (atol 0.1)
- All tile-padded (12, 24) and unpadded (16) cases pass on both versions.
</details>

## Details
Real heads sit at stride `nhead // num_heads` after `repeat_interleave` and at `[0:num_heads]` after tiling; the fix selects accordingly. Existing test head counts (12, 16, 24) only exercised tile padding.
No duplicate: no open issue or PR addresses this; #59966 changes `get_mla_padded_q` but keeps `repeat_interleave` for the divisor case.
AI assistance was used to prepare this change and description; I reviewed every changed line.

title: [Attention] Set ALWAYS cudagraph support for FA4
body:
# Summary
This PR enables `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS` cudagraph support for Flash Attention 4. The primary motivation is to enable adaptive verification (AV) with MiMo-V2.5-Pro-FP4 + DFlash using the default attention backend (`FLASH_ATTN_DIFFKV`) on GB200.

`AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS` means a FULL cudagraph captured for one batch layout can be replayed for any other layout with the same token count, including mixed prefill+decode batches and variable per-request query lengths. That holds for FA4 for three reasons:

1. No host-side scheduling state. Unlike FA3, FA4 builds no AOT scheduler metadata (aot_schedule is gated on fa_version == 3). All per-batch tiling is derived on device from cu_seqlens_q/seqused_k inside the captured kernels, so replays with a different layout recompute it correctly.
2. The grid does not depend on per-request lengths. The varlen tile scheduler sizes its grid from total_q (the padded token count, fixed per graph) and the batch size, not from max_seqlen_q.
3. Host-side specializations are conservative under an upper bound. FA4 does specialize on the host max_seqlen_q: it selects q_stage and, when max_seqlen_q * qhead_per_kvhead <= q_stage * tile_m, a static persistent scheduler that assumes at most one M-block per request. These are correct for any replay whose real query lengths do not exceed the captured max_seqlen_q. The runners guarantee that: mixed FULL graphs are captured with max_query_len = num_tokens, the worst case for the token count (MRV2 prepare_inputs_to_capture, V1 _dummy_run); decode and varlen-decode graphs are captured with the decode width and only replay batches within it; and dispatch matches a graph only when its max_query_len covers the batch.

FA2 still needs `AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_BATCH` because of its packed-GQA special case for max_query_len == 1 captures.

# Test Plan
- Kernel-level graph-replay checks, FA4 on GB200, MiMo-V2.5-Pro TP4 attention geometry (32/2 heads, head dims 192/128, SWA 128 with sinks, page sizes 16/64):
  - Varlen-decode replay (42 configs) and mixed prefill+decode full-graph replay (18 configs) both match eager bit-for-bit, including captures with tiny max_seqlen_k.
  - A negative control that captures with max_seqlen_q below the replayed lengths fails (max abs error 2.05), so the checks detect a broken replay.
- Without AV: Qwen3-8B gsm8k with FLASH_ATTN + cudagraph_mode=FULL, main vs PR: 88.48% vs 88.55%, within noise.
- With AV: MiMo-V2.5-Pro-FP4 + DFlash gsm8k (full 1319 questions), AV off vs on: 95.83% vs 96.29%, within noise. It also starts and serves coherent output with no attention overrides.

title: [Bugfix][PCP] Align MoE routing padding with gathered tokens
body:
## Purpose

The non-all-to-all PCP path gathers hidden states and router logits across PCP ranks, but the router still reads the rank-local padding mask. With N local rows and P PCP ranks, routing processes P*N rows while the mask still has N entries. CUDA top-k checks that the mask length matches the token count and can raise an `is_padding` size mismatch.

This PR aligns the MoE padding mask with the PCP-gathered token rows and restores the original rank-local mask in a `finally` block. The dispatch/combine interfaces and PCP1/all-to-all paths remain unchanged. Regression tests cover PCP1/2/4, the all-to-all bypass, per-forward caching, and exception cleanup.

A search of open PRs covering PCP padding, PCP MoE, and the relevant padding-cache key found no equivalent fix. Nearby PRs #53639, #60049, and #56258 address different paths.

## Implementation

- Non-all-to-all PCP routing receives a padding mask with the same rank-major layout and row count as the gathered hidden states.
- The original local padding mask is restored on normal and exceptional exits.
- The gathered mask is cached per forward context and reused across MoE calls.

## Validation

### Environment

- Model: official `mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603` native FP8 checkpoint.
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93`.
- Hardware: two nodes, each with 4x NVIDIA H20 GPUs.

### vLLM startup arguments

```bash
# Set MASTER_ADDR to the reachable IP address of the master node.
vllm serve /models/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 19180 \
  --served-model-name mistral-small4-pcp-ab \
  --config-format mistral \
  --load-format mistral \
  --tokenizer-mode mistral \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --master-addr "${MASTER_ADDR}" \
  --master-port 29511 \
  --language-model-only \
  --enforce-eager \
  --attention-backend TRITON_MLA \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --block-size 64 \
  --kv-cache-dtype auto \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-async-scheduling
```

### Result

**Without this fix** (baseline): 
With the unmodified image and model, all seven native weight shards loaded (29.34 GiB per rank). The unpatched run then failed during vLLM's standard startup memory profiling, before the API server became ready:

```text
RuntimeError: .../topk_softmax_kernels.cu:785, is_padding size mismatch, expected: 4096
```

**With this PR**:
Applying the `_sequence_parallel_context` change from this PR at startup allowed the TP2/PCP2 deployment to start and generate successfully. It passed all five chat smoke requests, including a 2,235-token input and concurrent requests of different lengths.

Using the official `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` scoring logic, we evaluated all 1,319 test examples with 5-shot prompts, temperature=0, seed=42, `max_tokens=256`, and concurrency=4. Results:

| Run  | GSM8K | Invalid answers | Runtime result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Baseline + TP4/PCP1 | 1191/1319 (90.2957%) | 0 | Full evaluation completed; 0 API errors and 0 Pod restarts |
| Baseline + TP2/PCP2 | Could not run | — | Failed during startup profiling with the padding-size mismatch above |
| This PR applied + TP2/PCP2 | 1197/1319 (90.7506%) | 0 | Full evaluation completed; 0 API errors and 0 Pod restarts |

AI assistance was used to extract the change, prepare regression tests and run the validation described above. The human submitter retains responsibility for line-by-line review and final sign-off.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MiniMax-M3] Reject unbuilt index-head counts in the AITER indexer
body:
## Overview

The MiniMax-M3 AITER indexer selector now rejects index-head counts AITER has no kernels for. At attention TP=1 (4 index heads per rank), the server now fails at load with a clear error instead of crashing on the first decode step.

## Claims

- `aiter_indexer_unsupported_reason` accepts only 1 or 2 index heads, the counts AITER builds its MSA score kernels for (`SPARSE_DECODE_TABLE`/`SPARSE_PREFILL_TABLE`, unchanged from the `v0.1.24.post1` pin through AITER main).
- A new regression test in `test_minimax_m3.py` fails without the fix and passes with it.

## Validation

MI355 (gfx950). At TP=1, `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4` crashed before the fix at the first forward with `pa_sparse_block_score_decode: no build for num_idx_heads=4`. With the fix it refuses to start with a configuration error. `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py` passed 10/10 runs.

At TP=2 the same AITER kernels run before and after. I ran 5 interleaved runs per column, each with a fresh server, using `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` and the fp8 index cache. Values are mean ± sd.

| `vllm bench serve` (4096 in / 256 out, conc 16) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Request throughput (req/s) | 2.366 ± 0.007 | 2.365 ± 0.009 |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 18.83 ± 0.73 | 18.53 ± 0.86 |

| gsm8k (5-shot, n=1319) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| strict-match | 0.8799 ± 0.0089 | 0.8708 ± 0.0089 |

The gsm8k difference is not significant (Welch p ≈ 0.14).

## Details

The selector only rejected head counts above the 16 MFMA columns, so 4 heads got through and failed inside AITER's kernel dispatch. A rejected config falls back to the platform-neutral indexer, which turns this case into a load-time error. TP ≥ 2 still gives each rank 1 or 2 heads, so it keeps the AITER path. The test asks the selector instead of naming an architecture, so it keeps working as more CDNA targets are added. No open PR fixes this. If #57909 (which moves this selector to `indexer_msa.py`) lands first, the guard belongs there.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [ROCm][DSv4] Fuse the shared expert into AITER MegaMoE
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds an opt-in env var, `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`. With it set, `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe` (#59685) runs DeepSeek-V4's shared expert inside AITER MegaMoEV2, as one extra local expert per EP rank, instead of as a separate FP8 MLP after the MoE. This is the ROCm counterpart of the DeepGEMM MegaMoE shared-expert fusion (#53040), using the same extra-slot scheme as sglang on ROCm (sgl-project/sglang#35619).

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4-Pro on MI355X (DEP8): decode **ITL drops 4–9%** at concurrency 1–64 and **2–5%** at 128.
- **Output throughput rises 3–8%** at concurrency 1–64. At concurrency 128 the gain is small (+1–2%).
- Accuracy is unchanged:
  - Thinking mode: GPQA-Diamond 0.894 → 0.899 (official Think High 89.1) and MMLU-Pro 0.852 → 0.854, both within 1σ.
  - GSM8K stays within stderr, and NIAH is 1.00 from 4k to 128k context.
- With the env var unset, behavior is unchanged.

## Performance

**Setup**
- Hardware and model: MI355X ×8, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`.
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-7d0b4e57…`, the merge base of this PR, with the PR files mounted.
- Serving flags, aligned with the AgentX DEP8 recipe:
  - `--data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput --moe-backend aiter_mega_moe`
  - `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --async-scheduling --gpu-memory-utilization 0.86 --no-enable-prefix-caching`
- Benchmark: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --ignore-eos --num-prompts max(16, 4×conc)`.
- Baseline and fused ran on the same node with identical flags; only the env var differed.

**ISL 1024 / OSL 1024**

| Conc | Output tok/s | Median TPOT (ms) | Median ITL (ms) | P99 ITL (ms) | Median E2EL (s) | Median TTFT (ms) |
|:-:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 37.9 → **40.6 (+7.0%)** | 26.2 → **24.5 (−6.4%)** | 26.2 → **24.5 (−6.5%)** | 26.8 → **24.9 (−6.9%)** | 27.0 → **25.3 (−6.4%)** | 181 → 180 |
| 32 | 1002 → **1044 (+4.1%)** | 30.8 → **29.1 (−5.6%)** | 30.3 → **29.0 (−4.5%)** | 32.7 → **31.3 (−4.3%)** | 32.7 → **31.3 (−4.2%)** | 1166 → 998 |
| 64 | 1911 → **1974 (+3.3%)** | 32.2 → **30.9 (−4.1%)** | 32.1 → **30.7 (−4.3%)** | 34.6 → **33.3 (−3.8%)** | 34.3 → **33.0 (−3.7%)** | 1117 → 1146 |
| 128 | 3358 → 3380 (+0.7%) | 36.4 → **35.4 (−2.7%)** | 35.8 → **34.9 (−2.4%)** | 38.8 → **37.6 (−3.0%)** | 39.1 → 38.7 (−1.0%) | 1765 → 2194 |

**ISL 8192 / OSL 1024**

| Conc | Output tok/s | Median TPOT (ms) | Median ITL (ms) | P99 ITL (ms) | Median E2EL (s) | Median TTFT (ms) |
|:-:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 16 | 445 → **471 (+5.7%)** | 32.2 → **29.7 (−7.8%)** | 29.1 → **27.3 (−6.1%)** | 32.4 → **30.4 (−6.1%)** | 36.7 → **34.9 (−5.0%)** | 4080 → 3792 |
| 64 | 1487 → **1600 (+7.6%)** | 38.8 → **36.0 (−7.3%)** | 32.1 → **29.2 (−8.9%)** | 35.6 → **32.9 (−7.6%)** | 44.2 → **41.1 (−7.0%)** | 4574 → 4262 |
| 128 | 2478 → 2518 (+1.6%) | 47.4 → 46.7 (−1.5%) | 34.6 → **32.7 (−5.4%)** | 1020 → 1015 | 52.7 → 52.2 (−1.1%) | 4138 → 4175 |

Each point is a single run. In an earlier same-node session, two baseline runs differed by ≤0.6% in median ITL; with default flags that session also showed −4% to −7% ITL and +4% to +8% throughput at concurrency 1–128. TTFT is prefill/queue dominated and noisy at these prompt counts; the 1k/1k conc-128 TTFT increase did not reproduce at 8k/1k.

## Accuracy

All runs use the AgentX DEP8 server flags from the Performance section; baseline and fused differ only in the env var.

**Thinking mode, official sampling settings** (vLLM's default `reasoning_effort=high`, `temperature=1.0, top_p=1.0`, `--reasoning-parser deepseek_v4`, chat completions)

| Eval | Baseline | Fused | Official V4-Pro (Think High / Max) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| GPQA-Diamond (official `Idavidrein/gpqa`, 198 q, 0-shot, 128k output cap) | 0.8939 ± 0.0219 | **0.8990 ± 0.0215** | 89.1 / 90.1 |
| MMLU-Pro (12,032 q, 0-shot, 64k output cap) | 0.8524 ± 0.0032 | **0.8536 ± 0.0032** | 87.1 / 87.5 |

- **Prompt:** the simple-evals format, ending in `Answer: $LETTER`; the score is the `Answer:` line of the final content. Choices are shuffled with a fixed seed, so both arms see identical prompts.
- **Arms:** baseline and fused are within 1σ on both evals. GPQA-Diamond matches the official Think High score.
- **Truncation:** responses still thinking at the output cap are scored wrong:

  | | Baseline | Fused |
  |---|--:|--:|
  | GPQA-Diamond | 9/198 (4.5%) | 7/198 (3.5%) |
  | MMLU-Pro | 450/12,032 (3.7%) | 425/12,032 (3.5%) |

  Excluding them, MMLU-Pro is **0.886** (baseline) vs **0.885** (fused), so the ~1.7-point gap to the official number is the output cap, not the fusion. The official Think Max setting recommends a ≥384K context.

**Non-thinking / short-budget A/B** (same node and image for both arms)

| Eval | Baseline | Fused |
|---|--:|--:|
| GPQA-Diamond (InferenceX prompt, greedy, 16k output cap) | 0.6717 ± 0.0335 | 0.6768 ± 0.0333 |
| GSM8K (5-shot, flexible / strict) | 0.9575 / 0.9568 | 0.9477 / 0.9484 |
| NIAH 4k (RULER, 8 tasks × 100) | 1.00 (single_1: 0.99) | 1.00 |
| NIAH 16k (8 tasks × 100) | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| NIAH 64k (8 tasks × 50) | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| NIAH 128k (8 tasks × 25) | 1.00 | 1.00 |

- **GPQA at 16k is truncation-limited:** about half the responses hit the 16k cap mid-reasoning. On the ones that finished, accuracy is 96% in both arms. The row is only an A/B comparison; use the thinking-mode table above for absolute scores. Its data is the ungated `fingertap/GPQA-Diamond` mirror of the same 198 questions.
- **NIAH:** lm-eval's RULER needle tasks (`niah_single_{1,2,3}`, `niah_multikey_{1,2,3}`, `niah_multiquery`, `niah_multivalue`), one run per context length.
- **GSM8K:** `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5`. The difference is about 1.2σ; #59685 reported 0.9484 for the unfused MegaMoE path.
- **MMMU / MMMU-Pro:** not applicable, because DeepSeek-V4-Pro is text-only (`DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`, no vision encoder).

## Details

- **Routing:** each rank holds 48 routed + 1 shared expert, so the kernel runs with `experts=392, topk=7`. A small Triton kernel remaps routed id `e → e + e // 48` and appends `ep_rank * 49 + 48` with weight 1.0. The routed weights already include `routed_scaling_factor`. The shared route always stays on the token's own rank, so it adds no all-to-all traffic.
- **Weights:** the shared MLP loads as usual. When MegaMoE weights are finalized, its block-FP8 weights are requantized to MXFP4 (`scaled_dequantize` + `mxfp4_quantize`, i.e. aiter `dynamic_mxfp4_quant`) into the shared slot, and the MLP is dropped. MTP and DSpark layers go through the same finalize path.
- **Tradeoffs:**
  - The shared expert runs at MXFP4 instead of FP8 (about 12% relative weight error), the same format the routed experts use.
  - `topk=7` needs a larger MoRI heap, so its default rises from 8G to 16G when the flag is on.
- **Known issue, not introduced by this PR (ROCm hipBLASLt):** with the default `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, startup can hang in the profile run on MI355X, with or without this flag, on the unmodified image too.
  - **Root cause:** hipBLASLt 1.2.2 (ROCm 7.2.3) keeps Stream-K fixup flags in one per-handle `Synchronizer` that every stream shares. DSv4's CSA layers run the two compressor `torch.mm` calls (N=2048 and N=512, fp32 out) concurrently on two aux streams with the same torch handle. At ≥12288 tokens per rank, the N=512 GEMM picks a Stream-K remainder kernel (`…SK3_SKFTR0_SKXCCM8`). One kernel can then clear a flag the other is waiting on, and that workgroup spins in `label_SK_Fixup` forever (seen with rocgdb). The other ranks then wait in the MegaMoE collective. It is not a MegaMoE bug.
  - **Fix:** ROCm/rocm-libraries#10951 (per-stream Stream-K flags) and #11691 (gfx950 cross-XCD flag coherence). Neither is in ROCm 7.2.3 or 7.2.4.
  - **Workaround until a ROCm release includes them:** `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` (the AgentX recipe). At that size the N=512 GEMM never takes the remainder path, and every run started reliably.

**Tests:** `pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_aiter_mega_moe.py` passes on MI355X (6 passed). The new `test_shared_expert_route_appended` covers the id remap, `-1` padding routes, and the appended shared route. The end-to-end EP8 path needs 8× gfx950 and the DSv4 checkpoint, so it is validated outside CI (results above).

**Not a duplicate:** the existing MegaMoE shared-fusion PRs are NVIDIA DeepGEMM (#53040, #56568, #59927) or Kimi K3 (#53556). #53847 targets the non-mega AITER fused-MoE path.

title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Use the EAGLE replay boundary when retaining sliding-window tails
body:
## Purpose

`MooncakeStoreCoordinator.store_mask` mirrors the core's sparse sliding-window retention (`SlidingWindowManager.reachable_block_mask`) so the store keeps the same tails the local prefix cache does. It passed the non-EAGLE replay boundary, `(num_prompt_tokens - 1,)`, while masking with `use_eagle=True`. Under EAGLE the lookup matches one block past the hit and drops back from it, so the core's `replay_boundaries` places the boundary one scheduler block lower; the store did not. For a prompt that is not block-aligned the retained tail therefore ended one block too high, the saved prefix held `need - 1` of the `cdiv(sliding_window - 1, block_size) + 1` contiguous blocks the lookup requires, and the joint hit collapsed to 0. Only block-aligned prompts hit.

Affected layout: a full-attention target group plus a sliding-window EAGLE drafter group (DFlash-style, e.g. window 2048 / block 64) with `prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`. Same family as #57610 (sparse sliding-window retention keeping a tail exactly `need` blocks long), but on the store side and with a different cause; #57613 composes with this change.

The fix extracts the core rule into a module-level `replay_boundaries()` in `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py` (called directly from `KVCacheCoordinator.cache_blocks`, behaviour unchanged) and calls it from `_reachable_masks`, so the two sides cannot drift again. The non-EAGLE path still yields `(num_prompt_tokens - 1,)`. On a block-aligned prompt the store now also keeps the core's lower "resend" tail: one extra sliding-window tail per aligned prompt, identical to what the local cache retains.

Not a duplicate: #56615 pairs Mamba and attention boundaries for partial-tail handoffs and does not touch the retention boundary; #57444 changes the core boundary alignment for fine-grained hits (same function, orthogonal change; trivial rebase whichever lands first); #46906 sidesteps by making store retention dense; #57613 fixes #57610 inside `reachable_block_mask`.

## Test Plan

- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py`: `test_store_mask_retention_interval_zero_eagle_keeps_lookup_tail` (the mask keeps the `need`-block tail at the lowered boundary, for an unaligned and an aligned prompt) and `test_store_mask_retention_interval_zero_eagle_round_trip` (save through `store_mask`, then the EAGLE lookup hits).
- Existing Mooncake coordinator, worker and scheduler unit tests, and `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py` + `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache` for the core refactor.

## Test Result

- Direct-call cleanup validation: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q -k "mooncake or retention or eagle or replay"` — 62 passed, 147 deselected. All pre-commit hooks passed on the three changed files. This cleanup used OpenAI Codex assistance.

- On B300: 677 passed across the suites above. The two `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate` cases error identically on `main` in that environment (the test server cannot fetch its Hub model there) and are unrelated.
- On `main` the new tests fail for the unaligned prompt (mask mismatch; hit 0); with this change they pass.
- Lint: ruff check / format and mypy pass.
- Model output is unaffected: retention only decides which already-computed blocks the store keeps.

AI assistance: this change was developed with Claude (Anthropic) under human direction; every changed line was reviewed by the submitter, who ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Keep input_ids on later PP stages for raw-token models
body:
## Overview

Model Runner V2 drops `input_ids` on every pipeline stage after the first, so models that set
`requires_raw_input_tokens` (they read token ids inside their decoder layers) cannot run with
`--pipeline-parallel-size > 1`. This keeps `input_ids` on later stages for those models, as Model Runner V1
already does. Fixes #55515.

## Claims

- MRV2 with pipeline parallelism works for models that set `requires_raw_input_tokens` (DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1
  vision variants, Qwen4Exp with N-gram PLE, Voxtral realtime): later stages receive `input_ids` in the execute
  path and in CUDA graph capture.
- Other models are unchanged: later stages still get `input_ids=None`.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4 x PP2 + EP, 8x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120), max-model-len 1M, CUDA graphs,
no speculative decoding. Same image both times; only the two files in this PR differ.

| | Startup | Smoke (25k- and 60k-token prompts) | Needle at 20/50/90% of a 22.5k-token prompt | ITL p50, bs1 / bs16 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| upstream main | fails: every PP rank 1 worker raises `ValueError: DeepSeek V4 vision MoE routing requires input_ids.` | – | – | – |
| this PR | serves (health OK after 250 s) | pass | 3/3 found | 11.1 / 17.7 ms per token |

<details><summary>Build and reproduction</summary>

Base: vLLM nightly image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-7d0b4e57aac4c4323225b0eee9ae960ce75ffffe` with FlashInfer
0.7.1 (for the sm_120 sparse-MLA decode shapes). DeepSeek-V4.1 on sm_120 with PP also needs fixes that are not on
main yet, so the validation build is our fork branch
[`quettaflop/vllm:sm120-dsv41-main`](https://github.com/quettaflop/vllm/tree/sm120-dsv41-main) on that commit. It
includes per-stage KV tensor placement (same fix as #60569) and 64-row sparse-MLA/indexer pages on sm_120 (same
issue as #60762 / #56509), plus other DeepSeek-V4.1 changes. Between the two runs only the two files in this PR
differ.

    vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
      --enable-expert-parallel --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 64 --block-size 64 \
      --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41"}' \
      --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41

</details>

`pre-commit run` passes on the changed files. CI test: `test_distributed_oot_pp_raw_input_tokens` in
`tests/distributed/test_distributed_oot.py` serves a dummy OPT from the `vllm_add_dummy_model` plugin that sets
`requires_raw_input_tokens = True` and asserts `input_ids` is not None, with PP=2 on MRV2, eager and with CUDA
graphs, in the 2×L4 plugin step. Without the fix both cases fail on the PP rank 1 worker; reverting only the
`cudagraph_utils.py` change fails the CUDA-graph case during capture. It passes in
[Buildkite build 94033](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94033). A dummy model is used because DeepSeek
V4/V4.1's sparse MLA kernels need sm90+ and the step runs on L4.

## Details

Root cause: `GPUModelRunner.execute_model` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`) and
`ModelCudaGraphManager.capture` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`) set `model_inputs["input_ids"] = None`
on every non-first PP rank. Every rank still prepares the same input batch, so the ids are already in the input
buffer there; MRV1 passes them to all ranks (the text-only branch of `gpu_model_runner.py`). The new condition
reuses `requires_raw_input_tokens`, the check MRV2 already applies on the first rank when it passes
`inputs_embeds`.

Relation to open PRs: #55520 (DeepSeek V4) and #56444 (Qwen4Exp) relay `input_ids` through `IntermediateTensors`
per model, and #60234 forbids PLE layers on later ranks. This change fixes the runner once, with no extra
inter-stage transfer and no per-model code; the input_ids relays in those PRs become unnecessary, while their
other fixes (KV allocation, MTP drafter) are independent.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to prepare this change and this description; the commit carries a
`Co-authored-by` trailer.

title: [Attention] Make the sparse MLA prefill workspace size configurable
body:
## Overview

Adds `AttentionConfig.sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor`. It replaces the fixed `5 * max_model_len` FlashMLA sparse prefill workspace and the `40 * max_model_len` DSA indexer prefill buffer sized from it. Unset, `VllmConfig` resolves it to 5 up to a 256K `max_model_len` and to 2 above. At a 1M `max_model_len` the fixed reservations hold several GiB per GPU that a long-context deployment can return to the KV cache.

Related: #60874 (right-sizes the DeepSeek-V4.1 copies of these buffers), #42856 (fixed lower factors on SM120 only), #59319 (skips the FlashMLA workspace on the fp8 mixed-batch path).

## Claims

- Up to a 256K `max_model_len` the default keeps every size identical to main.
- Above 256K the default is 2: workspace `2 * max_model_len`, indexer `16 * max_model_len`. `--attention-config.sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor=5` restores the main sizes.
- The default resolves once, in `VllmConfig.__post_init__`. KV cache auto-fit can lower `max_model_len` after the workspace is reserved, so a factor derived later could switch from 2 to 5 and size a step past the reservation.
- One knob sizes both buffers. The indexer buffer stays `(576 * 2 // 132) * factor` rows, so it still fits inside the FlashMLA workspace.
- Both chunkers keep each request's context in one gather, so a lower factor changes only how many requests share a gather.
- The floor is 2 (`ge=2`). Under PCP+DCP the per-rank budget is `factor * max_model_len // dcp`, and a full-length request's shard can round up past `max_model_len // dcp`, which `split_prefill_chunks` asserts against.
- GLM-5.3 FP8 on H100 at a 1M `max_model_len` (PCP8, DCP8, TP1): factor 2 raises available KV cache from 9.07 to 18.36 GiB per GPU.

## Validation

**Default, CPU.** On 06a24c32f, a real `VllmConfig` (`Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B`, CPU device) resolves the factor and both buffer sizes as follows:

| `max_model_len` | factor | workspace | indexer |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 163840 | 5 | 5x | 40x |
| 262144 | 5 | 5x | 40x |
| 262145 | 2 | 2x | 16x |
| 1048576 | 2 | 2x | 16x |

An explicit factor of 3 at 1M is kept, and `AttentionConfig(sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor=1)` raises a validation error. `test_indexer_prefill_budget_matches_compressed_workspace` reads the resolved factor through `create_vllm_config`; it needs a GPU, so CI runs it in the `v1/attention` job. pre-commit (ruff, mypy, `validate-config`, test tethering) passes on the changed files.

**GLM-5.3 on H100, same sizes.** We run GLM-5.3 FP8 in production with these exact sizes (workspace 2x, indexer 16x) applied to the same two functions on our vLLM build. The prefill engines are PCP8, DCP8, TP1, `--max-model-len 1048576`, `fp8_ds_mla`, block size 64, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.93`.

| | factor 5 | factor 2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Available KV cache per GPU | 9.07 GiB | 18.36 GiB |
| KV cache tokens per 8-GPU engine | 1.40M to 1.42M | 2.63M to 2.88M |
| 1M-token code-recall prompt | passes, 120.5 to 122.0 s | passes, 122.6 s |

All 28 production prefill engines have run factor 2 since 2026-10-10 18:08 UTC, and every one booted without OOM.

**This branch on GPU: not run.** The production numbers come from the same sizes on our build.

## Details

- **Why a config field.** The neighbouring sparse-MLA and indexer knobs (`sparse_mla_force_mqa`, `indexer_kv_dtype`, `hisparse_config`) live in `AttentionConfig`. `get_prefill_workspace_size` now takes the `VllmConfig`, like `get_max_prefill_buffer_size` already does.
- **Scope.** The FlashMLA workspace part applies to `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` with a quantized DS-MLA cache. `get_max_prefill_buffer_size` also sizes the indexer in `deepseek_v2` (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x), `deepseek_v32`, `deepseek_v4`, `deepseek_v41`, `hy_v4` and `glm5next`, so the factor applies there too. The DeepSeek-V4.1 FlashMLA workspace is sized in `models/deepseek_v41` and does not read it.
- **Cost.** A step gathers in more passes only when its prefill requests hold more than `factor * max_model_len` context tokens in total. At the default above 256K (factor 2), that takes three or more concurrent near-full-length prefills.
- **Not a duplicate.** Open PRs found with `gh pr list --state open --search` for "sparse prefill workspace", "prefill workspace size configurable", "flashmla sparse workspace", "indexer prefill buffer" and "workspace factor":
  - #42856 lowers the factors to 2 and 8 on SM120 only, stacked on #41834.
  - #60874 changes only the DeepSeek-V4.1 builders.
  - #59319 drops the reservation on the mixed-batch path. On the separate prefill path this knob still sizes it, and the two PRs touch one shared call line in `FlashMLASparseImpl.__init__`.
  - None makes the size configurable.

title: [NIXL] Prepare KV transfer descriptors as NIXL 1.5 strided lists
body:
NIXL 1.5 accepts a compressed Nx5 descriptor list in `prep_xfer_dlist`: each `(addr, len, dev_id, stride, count)` row stands for `count` blocks of `len` bytes whose starts are `stride` bytes apart. The connector built one `(addr, len, dev_id)` row per block per region instead, so a large KV pool meant millions of descriptors materialized in NumPy and copied into NIXL at startup and again on every handshake.

Emit one strided row per region:
- `_build_fa_local`, `_build_fa_remote` and the Mamba/PLE builders return Nx5 rows. Padded blocks split by a block-size ratio get one row per block.
- Local, per-source split and remote dlists are prepared directly from the Nx5 arrays with an explicit memory type; `get_xfer_descs` is no longer used. Descriptor ids are unchanged because NIXL indexes a strided list by flat block index.
- Split handles (P_TP > D_TP) slice each row's length and address, and the REPLICATE/SPLIT flag is computed once per row from the region owning its first block, honoring per-region block counts, instead of once per block.
- Mixed DRAM/VRAM registrations split rows by memory type; the per-block maps used by the READ path are unchanged.
- The worker refuses to start with NIXL < 1.5.

The transfer path is unchanged: request descriptors are built from the same flat indices, and NIXL 1.5 already compresses flat lists internally.

## Performance

Qwen3-8B P/D on one GB300 node, NIXL 1.5.0, `main` (f2376cdc4d) vs this PR. Each decode rank has a ~1.48M-token KV pool (~3.3M per-block descriptors before this change). Method timings come from a wrapper around `register_local_xfer_handler` / `add_remote_agent`; request times are end-to-end through the toy proxy (`max_tokens=1`, ~700-token prompt). Medians of 3 rounds with alternating run order, ranges in brackets.

**Prefill TP1 → decode TP1**

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Local descriptor setup (`register_local_xfer_handler`, startup) | 52 ms | 0.2 ms |
| Handshake (`add_remote_agent`) | 156 ms [153–162] | 109 ms [108–113] |
| Cold first request (includes the handshake) | 307 ms [299–341] | 259 ms [255–296] |
| Warm requests | 65–77 ms | 64–73 ms |

**Prefill TP2 → decode TP1** (decode builds per-source split handles and handshakes with two prefill ranks)

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Prefill local descriptor setup (twice the tokens per rank) | 107–112 ms | 0.1–0.2 ms |
| Handshake with first prefill rank | 2,255 ms [2,242–2,258] | 118 ms [113–118] |
| Handshake with second prefill rank | 145 ms | 42 ms |
| Cold first request | 2,656 ms [2,625–2,661] | 425 ms [415–444] |
| Warm requests | 76–89 ms | 77–99 ms |

On `main`, building the split handles looped in Python over every per-block row, costing ~2.1 s on the first handshake; it now operates on a handful of strided rows. The gain grows with KV pool size and with the prefill/decode TP ratio. The remaining ~110 ms of handshake is NIXL loading remote metadata and connecting, which this change doesn't touch. Warm request latency is unchanged, as expected, since transfer-time descriptor lookup is the same.

Ports https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55157 to current main and addresses its review feedback.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Length-aware candidate block selection in the decode indexer
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1's decode indexer writes its logits into a `[rows, max_model_len]` buffer, a width that must stay static for CUDA graphs (1M with the default `max_model_len`). Each row only holds its own context, but `select_candidate_blocks` scored every block of the full width and then ran `torch.topk(2048)` over all of them. At 1M that costs about 850 us per decode step, whatever the actual context length. This PR makes candidate selection length-aware.

- **Score only valid blocks.** `_block_scores_kernel` now runs a fixed `(rows, 32)` grid that walks each row's tiles only up to the row's end, and it writes each row's valid block count.
- **DeepSelect instead of `torch.topk`.** On the DeepSelect path, the block count is passed as DeepSelect's per-row `end`. Short rows are padded with -1. Candidate order does not matter, because the sparse expansion sorts. The full-width `torch.topk` path stays as the fallback for no DeepSelect, non-contiguous output, `topk > 4096` and narrow logits, and its behaviour is unchanged.
- **NaN rows.** DeepSelect leaves NaN rows only partly written, which can happen during warmup or capture on an uninitialized KV cache. On the DeepSelect path, NaN blocks are pinned like the newest block, as `torch.topk` ranks NaN first. NaN rows therefore still get complete, in-range candidates.
- **bf16 decode logits.** The decode indexer now asks DeepGEMM for bf16 logits when the top-k backend is `deep_select` and DCP is off. This halves the bytes that the top-k and candidate passes read. The logits kernel still accumulates in fp32 and only rounds the output, which is byte-identical to `bf16(fp32 logits)`. The other top-k backends and the DCP merge still get fp32.
- **Footprint.** `candidate_blocks.py`, the decode call in `sparse_attn_indexer.py`, and a `logits_dtype` passthrough on `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` (default fp32). The DeepSelect availability check reuses `has_deep_select()`.

## Kernel microbenchmark

`select_candidate_blocks` alone, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode shapes: 384 rows (64 requests x 6 tokens), logits width 1,048,576 (default `max_model_len`, ratio-1 candidate-source layer), 2048 candidate blocks of 8. 1 x GB300, FlashInfer CUPTI timing with CUDA graph replay and cold L2, median. Logits are continuous random values; random FP4 inputs give heavily tied logits, which is pathological for radix selection and does not match the model.

| context (tokens) | main, fp32 logits (us) | this PR, fp32 logits (us) | this PR, bf16 logits (us) | speedup (bf16 vs main) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 131,072 | 847.8 | 77.0 | 42.9 | 19.8x |
| 176,000 | 861.2 | 116.8 | 62.2 | 13.8x |
| 400,000 | 884.0 | 205.9 | 119.9 | 7.4x |
| 1,048,576 | 939.0 | 408.2 | 254.9 | 3.7x |

main's cost is flat because it always scores and sorts the full width. This PR scales with the context and is still faster at the full 1M.

The dense indexer top-k reads the same logits, so the bf16 switch also speeds it up. DeepSelect top-512 at 131K context, ratio-2 layer (65K keys) / ratio-1 layer (131K keys): fp32 42.2 / 62.7 us, bf16 28.8 / 45.4 us. The logits kernel itself takes the same time with fp32 and bf16 output (93.0 vs 94.2 us, 180.6 vs 181.5 us).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py -q -k "candidate or sparse_topk_remap"
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py
```

Also checked locally, without adding tests:
- Against the previous implementation, on 384-row decode inputs (1M width, random ends, `row_repeat=6`, rows shorter than 2048 blocks, empty rows, ends past the width), prefill rows with starts, and the fallback path: the selected candidate sets are identical. The only exception is an exact score tie at the 2048th block, where either choice is valid.
- The fallback path forced on is identical to the previous implementation (fp32). With bf16 logits, the DeepSelect path and the fallback select the same blocks, compared by score so ties do not count.
- NaN rows (fully NaN, and partly NaN) on the DeepSelect path: every id is in range and unique, nothing stale is left, and the NaN blocks are selected.
- bf16 paged MQA logits are byte-identical to the fp32 output rounded to bf16.

## Test Result

On 1 x GB300: 6 passed (the four `test_candidate_kernels_preserve_packed_bounds_and_padding` cases, including `out[:, ::2]` at 32768 columns, `test_select_candidate_blocks_tolerates_empty_rows`, and `test_sparse_topk_remap_bounds_nan_rows`). Pre-commit (ruff, format, typos, mypy) passes.

## E2E decode (DEP4)

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (DP4 x TP1 + EP) on one GB300 node. `FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41` with the MXFP4 indexer cache and sparse indexer logits, DeepGEMM mega MoE, `--sparse-indexer-topk-backend deep_select`, DSpark (5 tokens, synthetic acceptance), `max_num_seqs=64`, default `max_model_len` (1M), `DecodeBenchConnector`. 256 random-token requests with 125,000 input and 8,000 output tokens, all admitted at once. The nsys window opens about 40 s in, at a context of about 131K. GPU time is per decode step and GPU, averaged over all GPU-steps in the window. The E2E runs used a DSv4.1 development tree whose `candidate_blocks.py` and `sparse_attn_indexer.py` are identical to main's, with and without this patch; the unit tests ran on this branch.

| | base | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| indexer + candidate selection (us/step) | 1698 | 886 |
| `_block_scores_kernel` (us/step) | 208 | 26 |
| `torch.topk` kernels (`computeBlockDigitCounts`, `gatherTopK`, sort, ...) (us/step) | 619 | 0 |
| target forward GPU busy (ms/step) | 24.11 | 23.36 |
| median ITL (ms) | 26.52 | 25.65 |

A rerun with the final code gives the same 886 us.

## Accuracy

GSM8K with lm-eval 0.4.13 on this PR: 1319 problems, 5-shot completions, temperature 0, 1024-token cap, concurrency 32, one DEP4 `vllm serve` (MegaAttn, MXFP4 indexer cache with sparse logits, DeepGEMM mega MoE, `deep_select` top-k, so the decode indexer runs with bf16 logits and the new selection path). DSpark used 5 speculative tokens with standard rejection sampling and adaptive verification off. Acceptance comes from the `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters over the eval.

| | strict match | flexible extract | acceptance length, incl. bonus | per-position acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR | **92.57%** | 92.49% (±0.7) | **3.423** | 0.790 / 0.646 / 0.452 / 0.329 / 0.205 |
| #59923 (DSpark, adaptive verification on) | 92.57% | | 3.398 | 0.795 / 0.644 / 0.446 / 0.319 / 0.194 |
| #59511 base (DSpark, adaptive verification on) | 92.57% | | 3.365 | 0.792 / 0.641 / 0.441 / 0.310 / 0.181 |

GSM8K contexts are short (under 16K tokens), so the candidate-source layer keeps every valid block either way. Here the bf16 logits mainly feed the dense top-512. No accuracy or acceptance change is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve <model> --served-model-name DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --language-model-only \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --sparse-indexer-topk-backend deep_select --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"embedding_across_dp":true,"dp_shared_memory":true,"use_thp":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"standard","enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[6,12,...,384],"max_cudagraph_capture_size":384}'

lm-eval run --model local-completions \
  --model_args "model=DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8010/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None" \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs "max_gen_toks=1024,temperature=0"
```

</details>

## Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for `select_candidate_blocks`, `candidate_blocks`, `candidate blocks DeepSelect`, `indexer candidate topk` and `DSv4.1 indexer bf16 logits`. #59668 fuses the ROCm candidate mask (`rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`) and does not touch candidate selection.

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write and benchmark this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and benchmarks above.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Match decoder-replay input_ids dtype for FlashInfer MegaMoE
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61040. DeepSeek-V4.1 served with `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` or `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` crashes in the decoder-replay CUDA graph once it serves long prompts or batched prefills (e.g. GSM8K at concurrency 128) (`RuntimeError: Expected out tensor to have dtype int, but got long int instead`), because the replay graph's `input_ids` buffer is int64 while the model passes int32 ids for these backends. This PR sizes the buffer to match what the model passes.

## Claims

- **Bug fix:** with either FlashInfer MegaMoE backend, the replay graph's `input_ids` buffer is now int32, matching the ids `DeepseekV4Model.forward` passes. GSM8K serving no longer crashes. `deep_gemm_mega_moe` keeps its int64 buffer, and the default backend keeps int32, so neither changes.
- **Test:** `test_replay_graph_matches_eager` now sweeps the MoE backends and feeds `input_ids` in the dtype the model passes, instead of the buffer's own dtype. Without the fix both FlashInfer cases fail; run on its own, each fails at the line that crashes in serving.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (1× GB200, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` arm64 `sha256:f853a683…`, built from 7d0b4e57aa, which includes #59532; the fix installed by copying this PR's `decoder_replay_cudagraph.py`, the PR's only non-test change, into the image):

```bash
cd tests && pytest -v -rs models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py \
  models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_start.py
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| without the fix | 16 passed, 2 failed: `test_replay_graph_matches_eager[flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl-torch.int32]` fails at `decoder_replay_cudagraph.py:95` with `RuntimeError: expected scalar type Long but found Int`; `[flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm-torch.int32]` fails the same way when run on its own (after the first failure in the same process it fails during capture instead) |
| with the fix | **18 passed** |

**Serving** (4× GB200, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `2cba9e42`, `vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --moe-backend <backend>`, default CUDA graphs; GSM8K via `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-concurrency 128`, one run each):

| `--moe-backend` | Image | without the fix | with the fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` | nightly above | serves and answers short prompts, then the engine dies under GSM8K load with `RuntimeError: Expected out tensor to have dtype int, but got long int instead` at `decoder_replay_cudagraph.py:95`: GSM8K **0.027** (97% invalid) | GSM8K **0.899**, no errors |
| `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` | `main` c41b2639e2 + #59912 + #59900 | same crash: GSM8K 0.070 (earlier run, same image) | GSM8K **0.899**, no errors |
| `deep_gemm_mega_moe` (int64 path, unchanged) | nightly above | — | GSM8K 0.901 |
| default (`FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`; int32 path, unchanged) | nightly above | — | GSM8K 0.910 |

Every run in this round logged `Decoder SWA bounded replay` and captured all 8 decoder replay CUDA graph sizes, so the replay path was active. The earlier CuTeDSL "without the fix" run's server log was not kept, but its crash was in the replay graph's own `run()`. Short prompts ("capital of France", "17 * 23", a `fib(n)` function, "why is the sky blue") were answered correctly in every run.

The `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` row needs `nvshmem4py` (#59912) and the FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 kwarg fix (#59900), both still open, so it uses an image built from `main` c41b2639e2 + #59912 + #59900, with this PR's file copied in the same way.

**pre-commit:** `pre-commit run --files tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/decoder_replay_cudagraph.py` passes.

## Details

**Root cause.**
- `DecoderReplayCudaGraphManager.__init__` sized its `input_ids` buffer as int64 when `kernel_config.moe_backend in MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS` (`decoder_replay_cudagraph.py:59-60`). `MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS` is `NATIVE_MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS | FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_BACKENDS` (`vllm/config/kernel.py`).
- `DeepseekV4Model.forward` casts `input_ids` to int64 only when `use_native_mega_moe` (`moe_backend in NATIVE_MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS`, `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py:671-673`, `:929-930`); the runner's ids are int32 (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/input_batch.py:25`).
- So for both FlashInfer backends `run()` copies int32 ids into the int64 buffer with `torch.index_select(..., out=buf[:num_rows])` (`decoder_replay_cudagraph.py:95`), which requires matching dtypes.
- It needs a large enough step, not concurrency as such: `run()` is reached only when a replay batch dispatches to a replay graph (a PIECEWISE step of at least `decoder_replay_trim_threshold` = 768 padded tokens, or an eager step with a prefill chunk longer than the 128-token window; `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model_state.py:456-501`), so by the code a single prompt of 768 or more tokens hits it too. Capture feeds the buffers directly and the eager fallback has no `out=`, so startup and short prompts work.
- The two checks diverged when #54049 narrowed the model's cast (and the other native-only paths) to `NATIVE_MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS` while #59532 was in flight with the wider `MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS` check.

**Fix.** Key the buffer dtype on `NATIVE_MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS`, with a comment pointing at the cast in `DeepseekV4Model.forward`. The FlashInfer backends don't need int64 ids: the router accepts int32 (`fused_topk_bias` only casts when a hash table exists; `dsv4_topk` widens the ids to int64 after loading them, and the CUDA fallback accepts int32 or int64 ids), the FlashInfer experts never see `input_ids`, and the non-replay layers already run with int32 ids on these backends.

**Alternatives considered.** Deriving the dtype from one shared helper on `vllm_config`, called from both `DeepseekV4Model.__init__` and `DecoderReplayCudaGraphManager.__init__`, would stop the two from drifting again; this PR keeps to the minimal fix. Removing the native backend's int64 cast (a DSv4 hash-routing leftover; DSv4.1 has no hash layers) would need native MegaMoE revalidation. Both are possible follow-ups.

**CI.** The test runs in `:nvidia: (H200 MIG 35GB) Basic Models (Other)` and its `:amd: (MI355) Basic Models (Other)` mirror (`.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml`); it needs one GPU but no weights or FlashInfer kernels.

**Duplicate check.** `gh issue list` / `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm` searches for `decoder replay`, `decoder_replay`, `MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS`, `NATIVE_MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS`, `Expected out tensor to have dtype int` and `59532` found no issue or PR that fixes this bug. The only hit that describes it is #59912 (nvshmem4py), whose validation notes record this crash and leave the fix to a separate PR (this one); it does not change `decoder_replay_cudagraph.py`. Open #59039 (ROCm decoder replay) doesn't touch `decoder_replay_cudagraph.py`'s dtype logic, and the AMD model has no native MegaMoE.

---

title: [Sleep] Retain draft-private weights with existing parameter selector
body:
## Overview

The existing `sleep_preserve_parameter_names` API preserves frozen Engram table weights and scales across level-2 sleep, without retransmitting them during target weight updates (#57891). Extend the same API to draft-private weights for target-only updates; both use cases are documented. Related: #52479.

## Claims

- Select draft-private parameters with `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names 'draft.*'`, or individual `draft.<name>` patterns.
- Reuse existing CPU snapshots and in-place restoration; exclude target-shared `Parameter` identities.
- Allow an empty `draft.*` selection (no draft, or no private parameters). Other unmatched patterns still raise.
- No new switch, runner hook, RPC, inference-loop work, or graph recapture. Core diff: two files, 17 additions / 3 deletions.
- Document both the original frozen Engram table use case and `draft.*` in the existing Sleep Mode section; preserve the distinction between retention and Engram inference-time CPU offload.

## Validation

Changed-file pre-commit passes. Focused CPU regression command:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/worker \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py -k sleep_preservation -v
```

The tests check shared ownership, in-place restoration, an absent/all-shared draft, and unmatched target names: baseline **3 failed**, simplified pinned candidate **3 passed**, main-based candidate **3 passed**. Current-main base: `3c062d391d15cfa41d3f321cad24f3030c892a97`. Tests used the experimental container's dependencies with current-main Python source; no kernels were exercised by these CPU tests.

H200 model evaluation on the earlier equivalent nonempty-selection implementation, based on `43b4aaea` with the composed Vime patches:

| Qwen3.8-27B, TP4, MTP3 | Accepted draft tokens | Private parameters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before sleep | 498/813 (61.25%) | 48 fingerprints recorded |
| Level-2 sleep, staged wake, target-only reload | 499/816 (61.15%) | All 48 values and addresses unchanged |
| Retention disabled, isolated baseline | 0/2286 | Private values lost |

Six requests per phase; temperature 1, top-p 0.95, context 65,536, eager execution; model revision `1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0`. This is not an otherwise-unpatched current-main GPU result. No throughput improvement or ROCm/CPU/XPU/all-drafter validation is claimed.

The graph-enabled eight-GPU Agent training/rollout E2E also passes on the earlier `2ec58c52` implementation in the installed experimental image: two training steps, maximum observed MTP acceptance 87.6%, mean acceptance length up to 3.63. This does not substitute for a clean current-main GPU test.

## Details

Level-2 sleep discards target and draft weights. Reloading only the target leaves draft-private storage undefined: verification still works, but speculative acceptance can disappear. This opt-in extension saves the current draft before sleep and restores it at weight wake, using the existing narrow no-grad restore helper. Draft-buffer handling is unchanged.

This is distinct from #52487 (restore a configured disk checkpoint during `reload_weights`) and #60139 (explicitly load a new draft checkpoint). Neither retains the current draft across target-only IPC/NCCL updates. Those disk APIs remain useful and unchanged.

The measured snapshot is approximately 203 MiB per rank for this model; CPU storage and copies occur only at sleep/wake. Retained parameters must not also be supplied by the weight-update sender, as with the existing retention API.

AI assistance was used for implementation, investigation, and validation. Submitted at the human maintainer's explicit request; kept as a draft for human line-by-line review, which is not asserted complete.

title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Register packed MLA KV rows as a single region
body:
## Purpose

With a block-outermost KV cache layout (`VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC`), all layers' pages of a block sit in one contiguous row. 
NIXL still registers one region per layer, so each block moves as one descriptor per layer (effectively rendering BL* useless). 

This PR registers the row once, fixing registration back to its intended use.

Example: GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4, BLHNC. Input to `register_kv_caches` on rank 0 is 99 views over one 43.8 GB storage:

```
model.layers.0.self_attn.indexer.k_cache  (14323, 1, 64, 132)  stride(0)=3059712  offset 0
model.layers.0.self_attn.attn             (14323, 1, 64, 576)  stride(0)=3059712  offset 177408
...

row b: [ idx L0 | idx L1 | ... | mla L0 | mla L1 | ... | mla L77 ]   3059712 B
```

**Before** (`elif storage_is_block_major:` branch), each view is its own region:

```
region 0:  base S + 177408, block_len 36864, stride 3059712   # layers.0.attn
region 1:  base S + 0,      block_len 8448,  stride 3059712   # layers.0.indexer
...
-> 99 regions, 99 x 14323 = 1.42M descriptors; a 2-block request = 198 descriptors
```

**After** (the existing whole-row branch, previously push-only), every view emits the same region and dedup folds them into one:

```
region 0:  base S, block_len 3059712, stride 3059712           # whole row, all layers
-> 1 region, 14323 descriptors; a 2-block request = 2 descriptors
```

### HiSparse

A HiSparse decoder can't register rows: its MLA cache is in host DRAM and its indexer on GPU, so it keeps per-layer regions LB*. 
P can still advertise each layer's `(offset, page_size)` within the row (BL*).
When the peer is per-layer, `_split_remote_packed_rows` (added with this PR) maps P's row onto the peer's per-layer regions.
 
BLHNC P + HiSparse D therefore works as before, with the same descriptor count as `main`.
cc @LucasWilkinson the alternative is to enforce P also uses LB* here, not sure if there's disadvantages (considering .

Out of scope: GQA spec-decode drafts under an MLA target, deferred to #60564.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py test_nixl_connector.py test_nixl_connector_hma.py test_nixl_push_connector.py`
  - `test_packed_mla_pp1_transfers_whole_rows` now covers pull and push and asserts 1 region / 1 descriptor per block, guarding against falling back to per-layer regions again.
  - New tests for the row split and for the mismatched-rows error.
- E2E, GLM-5.3-NVFP4, P TP4 -> D TP4 on 8xB200, NixlConnector pull, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 500` (5-shot) through `toy_proxy_server.py`.

## Test Result

- Unit: 593 passed across the four suites. On `main`, the new pull-mode cases of `test_packed_mla_pp1_transfers_whole_rows` fail (per-layer regions); with this PR they pass.

| P -> D | regions P / D | gsm8k | NIXL transfers | avg descriptors / transfer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BLHNC -> BLHNC | 1 / 1 (99 / 99 on main) | 0.912 | 1040, 0 failed | 1.2 |
| BLHNC -> HiSparse D (default layout) | 1 / 99 | 0.918 | 685, 0 failed | 45.9 |

## Related PRs

#60851 and #60564 target the same descriptor blow-up. #60564 puts whole rows behind an opt-in `whole_row_regions` flag that must be set on both P and D, and rejects HiSparse. Here it is the default for BLHNC, needs no flag, and HiSparse decoders keep working. 

#60564 also handles GQA draft head-sharding, which this PR leaves to it.

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Restore MTP index sharing across draft iterations
body:
## Overview

GLM-5.3-Flash's checkpoint sets `index_share_for_mtp_iteration: true`: the MTP head computes the sparse indexer top-k on draft step 0 and reuses it on the later steps. Since #57387 the flag is no longer visible on the draft config, so sharing has been silently off. This restores it.

Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs for `index_share_for_mtp_iteration`, `share_mtp_topk_indices`, `glm5_next_mtp` and GLM-5.3-Flash MTP and found nothing covering this.

## Claims

- With MTP on GLM-5.3-Flash, draft steps 1+ reuse step 0's top-k again, as before #57387.
- Accepted tokens per draft step go from 3.28 to 3.42 on GSM8K (MTP 5), and decode throughput is +2.7% at a fixed acceptance length.

## Validation

4x B200, nightly `8cbd5d03`, TP1 x DP4 with expert parallel and #60895's MegaMoE path, MTP 5, one run each.

| | sharing off (main) | sharing on |
|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K (lm-eval, 5-shot, 1,319 questions) | 0.9704 ± 0.0047 | 0.9750 ± 0.0043 |
| draft steps for that GSM8K run | 58,471 | 56,072 |
| accepted tokens per draft step | 3.28 | 3.42 |
| random 1024 in / 1024 out, concurrency 128, output tok/s | 11,639 | 11,952 |
| mean TPOT | 10.13 ms | 9.90 ms |

The GSM8K rows use real acceptance; the throughput rows fix it with `synthetic_acceptance_length` 3.61.

The GPU runs switched the same proposer flag (`share_mtp_topk_indices`) through a local patch that read it from `text_config`. With this PR's code I ran:

- `tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py`: 17 passed; the new test fails without the change. Run against nightly `8cbd5d03`, whose `speculative.py` is identical to `main`'s.
- `SpeculativeConfig.hf_config_override` on the real checkpoint config: `index_share_for_mtp_iteration` is `True` (missing before).
- pre-commit on the changed files.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --language-model-only --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true,"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97

lm_eval run --model local-chat-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 \
  --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=2048 temperature=0.0
# accepted per draft step = vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens / vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts

# throughput rows: same server with
#   "rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.61
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --num-prompts 512 --num-warmups 64 --max-concurrency 128 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos \
  --temperature 0 --seed 42
```

The remaining serve flags (CUDA graph sizes, KV offload, `--prefix-match-unit 16`) are the ones listed in #60895.
</details>

## Details

- Root cause: the MTP proposers read the flag from the draft config (`mtp/speculator.py`, `llm_base_proposer.py`). The in-tree `Glm5NextConfig` forwarded `text_config` attributes to the top level; the upstream Transformers config that #57387 switched to does not. That PR moved `num_nextn_predict_layers` to `get_text_config()` but not this flag.
- Fix: promote the flag onto the draft config in the `glm5_next` override, as the Qwen4-Exp override already does. An explicit `index_share_for_mtp_iteration` in `--speculative-config` still takes precedence.
- The GSM8K difference is within one standard error; I read it as no regression, not as an accuracy gain.
- Limitations: validated on NVIDIA SM100 only, not on ROCm. Acceptance was measured on GSM8K only.
