title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono decode on every backbone layer
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Follow-up to #60397. The DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash mono decode kernels (MI355X, `--monokernel`) now run all 40 backbone layers whole as K1 + K2. Before, 30 layers ran whole and the other 10 kept vLLM's attention plus the FFN launch: layer 0, the Engram layer 1, and the index sources 2, 8, 14, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36. The switch is now `--monokernel` (`KernelConfig.monokernel`, per RFC #60904), replacing the `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE` environment variable from #60397.

## Claims

- AgentX at TP4, concurrency 1, 3,600 s, Rust frontend, against `main` with mono on: P90 interactivity goes from **541.6 to 562.6 tokens/s/user** (+3.9%), P50 from 569.8 to 595.5 (+4.5%), and ITL p50 from 1.760 to 1.680 ms.
- Accuracy is unchanged. GPQA-Diamond and AIME25 pass@1, mono on against off on this branch, differ by +0.1 ± 0.7 and +1.7 ± 1.2 points, both within noise. RULER NIAH scores 1.00 with mono on and off at 32K, 128K and 256K.
- Nothing changes with the switch off, and the 30 standard layers build the same kernels as before.

## Validation

**Performance.** MI355X, TP4, DSpark with 5 drafts and synthetic acceptance 3.51 (InferenceX#3690's TP4 recipe), AgentX at concurrency 1. Each arm is one 3,600 s run, and both arms ran at the same time on GPUs 0–3 and 4–7.

| | P90 interactivity | P50 interactivity | ITL p50 | TTFT p50 | requests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` (7d0b4e57aa), mono on | 541.6 | 569.8 | 1.760 ms | 0.200 s | 328 |
| this PR, mono on | **562.6** | **595.5** | **1.680 ms** | 0.201 s | 332 |

The `main` arm reproduces InferenceX's sweep point for this config (543). A 900 s run of each arm on the Python frontend gave +6.2% on P90 (503.5 to 534.5).

**Accuracy.** TP2, this branch, mono on against off, 4 seeds each, thinking on, DSpark with block rejection. Each mono-on server logged every backbone layer running whole.

| | mono on | mono off | on − off (paired by question) |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPQA-Diamond pass@1 | 85.0 ± 2.2 | 85.0 ± 2.2 | +0.1 ± 0.7 |
| AIME25 pass@1 | 100.0 ± 0.0 | 98.3 ± 1.2 | +1.7 ± 1.2 |

**Long context.** RULER NIAH, TP2, this branch, mono on against off: single-1, multikey-2 and multikey-3 at 32K, 128K and 256K, 40 samples each, greedy. All 9 points score 1.00 on both arms (360 samples per arm).

**Tests**, all run locally on MI355X:

- `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` at TP2 and TP4: passed. Its 5-layer model now covers every variant: the first layer, a ratio-2 KV and index source, a ratio-2 consumer with an Engram, a ratio-1 KV, index and candidate source, and a ratio-1 index source over layer 3's candidates. Every layer has to take the whole-layer path on every rank at every decode step.
- `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` at TP2 and TP4, including the 300-replay CUDA-graph stress: passed.
- `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`: 37 passed.
- `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` on the 5-layer model with CUDA graphs: no sync in steady-state decode. The runner's one-time setup on the first decode step syncs, as on `main`.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py -v
# AgentX: InferenceX#3690 dsv41flash TP4 c1 recipe with --monokernel, `infx.bench agentic`, DURATION=3600
# Evals: lm-eval local-chat-completions on GPQA-Diamond / AIME25, temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, 4 seeds, mono on vs off
# NIAH: lm-eval RULER niah_single_1 / niah_multikey_2 / niah_multikey_3 (chat), max_seq_lengths 32768 / 131072 / 262144, --limit 40
```
</details>

## Details

- **Settled residual (layers 0, 1, 14).** K1 gets a `fold` build flag. Without it, the seam slice takes the residual as it arrives instead of folding the previous layer's output in. Layer 0's residual is the embedding broadcast to the 4 streams, with an identity incoming pre-mix. The mix projection uses `hc_attn_fn` over the broadcast, which equals vLLM's folded `hc_attn_fn_broadcast` up to summation order. On an Engram layer, `mhc_post` and the Engram write run in torch before K1, as on vLLM's path.
- **Index sources (layers 2, 8, 14, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36).** K1 gets an `index` build flag.
  - K1 also stores its normed input and its bf16 qr (the q_norm output). It skips the key-table stage, because the top-k does not exist yet.
  - Between the two launches, `_select` runs vLLM's own modules: the compressor and its cache insert, the indexer K write, `weights_proj`, `forward_q` and `indexer_op`.
  - K2 then builds the key table on its last CTAs. Each attention split task waits on its token's flag, and the table goes through device scope, since the same launch reads it.
- **Tradeoffs.**
  - The compressor and indexer now run serially between the kernels. vLLM's path overlapped them on side streams, which the persistent kernels can't do, since they need every CU.
  - The indexer's `wq_b` quantizes the bf16 qr itself, where vLLM's fused q-norm hands it fp8 qr. The model-level test bounds the difference.
  - `_select` restates the module call sequence of `_forward_csa2_full` and `_forward_csa2_reindex` without their stream forks.
- **Not covered.** The DSpark draft layers still take vLLM's path. A layer outside the kernels (an MXFP8 KV cache, another indexer type) still takes the FFN launch, and the model-level test no longer exercises that launch; the numerics test does.
- **Model-level test bounds.**
  - Layer 0 now runs whole, so its output is held to 3% at every token. The old 1.5% at a request's first decode token was written for the FFN launch.
  - The near-tie exemption past layer 0 widens from 5e-3 to 1e-2. Every layer's input now carries the earlier layers' kernel differences (0.4–0.7%). One TP4 token flipped an expert at a gap of 0.0072 while every other token stayed near 4%.
- **Relation to other PRs.** #60731 ports the mono kernels to gfx942 and touches the same files. The two don't overlap in function, but whichever merges second needs a rebase.
- **Remaining gap.** On the formal sweep, ATOM's P90 at this point is 574. Moving the indexer's scoring and top-k, and the draft layers, into the kernels are the next steps.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix EXAONE-4.5 image inputs: ViT received un-normalised pixels
body:
## Overview

EXAONE-4.5 (`Exaone4_5_ForConditionalGeneration`) produces garbage for any request that contains an image on every release since #50411 (v0.29.0, v0.30.0, v0.31.0, main). Text-only requests are unaffected.

Root cause: the class inherits `supports_mm_device_do_normalize = True` from `Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration`, so `mm_device_do_normalize` defaults to on and the HF processor is told `do_rescale=False, do_normalize=False`. But `EXAONE4_5_VisionTransformer` is constructed without `input_norm`, so the inherited `Qwen2_5_VisionTransformer` uses `IdentityInputNorm` and the ViT receives raw 0–255 pixels.

Two smaller issues in the same constructor are fixed alongside, since they are the same missing wiring relative to the parent class:

- `self.model_config` and `self.video_pruning_rate` are never set, but the inherited `embed_multimodal` / encoder-CUDA-graph paths read them (`AttributeError` with `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true}'`).
- The MTP drafter (`Exaone4_5MultiTokenPredictor`) builds its `Exaone4DecoderLayer` without `cache_config`, so the drafter's attention ignores `--kv-cache-dtype`.

## Claims

- With the fix, image requests give coherent answers and are identical to the pre-#50411 behaviour (processor-side normalisation); text-only outputs and MTP acceptance are unchanged.
- No API change: the device-side normalisation feature stays on by default for this model, now with the correct normalisation module (`build_mm_input_norm(model_config)`), exactly as `Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration` does.
- Users on affected releases can work around it with `--no-mm-device-do-normalize`.

## Validation

`LGAI-EXAONE/EXAONE-4.5-33B-FP8`, TP=2, 2× A100-SXM4-40GB, greedy, thinking off, image = the model card's `assets/exaone45_input1.jpg` (a bowl of kimchi):

| | "Describe this image in one sentence." | gsm8k-50 (text only) |
|---|---|---|
| main (default flags) | `The\n</think>\n</think>one\n</think>…/or/or/or/or/or…` | 0.90 |
| this PR (default flags) | `A person in a light blue shirt is serving freshly made kimchi from a large black bowl into a smaller black dish, …` | 0.90 |

Second prompt ("What objects are in this image? List them.") shows the same pattern: `/or/or/or…` before, a correct itemised list (kimchi, dark ceramic bowl, …) after.

- `pre-commit` passes (ruff, mypy, typos).
- CI: the model is 33B and not in the multimodal generation test lists; the processing test (`tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py`) already covers it and still passes.

## Details

- `exaone4_5.py`: `EXAONE4_5_VisionTransformer.__init__` gains `input_norm` and forwards it to `Qwen2_5_VisionTransformer`; `Exaone4_5_ForConditionalGeneration.__init__` passes `input_norm=build_mm_input_norm(self.model_config)` and sets `self.model_config` / `self.video_pruning_rate` like the parent.
- `exaone4_5_mtp.py`: pass `cache_config=vllm_config.cache_config` to the MTP decoder layer.

Not in this PR (follow-ups): `Exaone4Model` lacks `EagleModelMixin` although the VLM advertises `SupportsEagle3` (asserts at load); `EXAONE4_5_VisionTransformer` builds and discards the full Qwen2.5 MHA block stack in `super().__init__` before replacing it with GQA blocks.

title: [Model] Support EAGLE3/DFlash aux hidden states for GraniteMoe and GraniteMoeShared
body:
## Overview

Implement `SupportsEagle3` for `GraniteMoeForCausalLM` and `GraniteMoeSharedForCausalLM` (which also serves `GraniteMoeSWAForCausalLM`), so Granite MoE models can serve as targets for aux-hidden-state speculative decoding (EAGLE3, DFlash, DSpark) and for `extract_hidden_states`. Follow-up to #60855, which did the same for dense `GraniteForCausalLM`.

## Claims

- Granite MoE targets (`GraniteMoeForCausalLM`, `GraniteMoeSharedForCausalLM`, `GraniteMoeSWAForCausalLM`) can now attach aux-hidden-state drafters and run `extract_hidden_states`. Previously, engine init rejected them because `supports_eagle3` was absent.
- The captured hidden states match HF `output_hidden_states` at the requested layers.
- No behavior change when no aux layers are requested: the models return `hidden_states` exactly as before.

## Validation


title: [Model Loader] Make dummy weight init dtype-aware
body:
## Overview

Make `--load-format dummy` produce non-degenerate quantized weights by picking dummy values per dtype in `initialize_single_dummy_weight`. Today, dummy-loaded MXFP4 MoE experts are entirely zero and FP8 weights are ~98% zero. That skews performance measurements with dummy weights (e.g. MoE routing and kernels see all-zero experts).

Related: #54958 bounds the memory of the FP8 dummy path. It's complementary (how values are generated vs. which values), and this PR keeps that code path intact so the two compose.

## Claims

- uint8 / int8 / `float4_e2m1fn_x2` params (packed FP4, int8 weights and zero points) get deterministic random bytes instead of being left as zeros or uninitialized memory. Every FP4 code is finite.
- E8M0 scales (`float8_e8m0fnu`, or uint8 params named like a scale, e.g. MXFP4 `w13_weight_scale`) get a fixed 2**-7 instead of arbitrary tiny exponents.
- 8-bit floats default to the range ±1 instead of ±1e-3, which mostly underflows in FP8 (E4M3's smallest normal is 2**-6).
- Wider integer params (int32/int64, e.g. `g_idx`) are untouched, since random values could be out-of-range indices. Explicit `low`/`high` and `dummy_weight_value` still take precedence.

## Validation

Weight statistics after `LLM(model, load_format="dummy")` (after `process_weights_after_loading`) on GB200, measured with `llm.apply_model`:

| Model | Param dtype | Zero fraction before | Zero fraction after | Non-finite |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RedHatAI/gpt-oss-20b` (MXFP4 experts) | uint8 (packed FP4 + scales) | 1.0 | 0.0039 (≈1/256) | 0 |
| `RedHatAI/gpt-oss-20b` | float8_e4m3fn (backend-converted) | 1.0 | 0.0 | 0 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8` | float8_e4m3fn | 0.977 | 0.001 | 0 |

Both models generate with finite logprobs before and after.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script</summary>

```python
import sys, torch
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

def weight_stats(model):
    stats = {}
    for _, p in model.named_parameters():
        if p.dtype in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16, torch.float32):
            continue
        s = stats.setdefault(str(p.dtype), [0, 0])
        raw = p.data.view(torch.uint8) if p.dtype in (torch.uint8, torch.int8) else p.data.float()
        s[0] += int((raw == 0).sum()); s[1] += p.numel()
    return {k: round(z / n, 4) for k, (z, n) in stats.items()}

llm = LLM(sys.argv[1], load_format="dummy", enforce_eager=True, max_model_len=1024,
          gpu_memory_utilization=0.5, skip_tokenizer_init=True)
print(llm.apply_model(weight_stats)[0])
print(llm.generate([{"prompt_token_ids": [785, 6722, 315, 9625, 374]}],
                   SamplingParams(max_tokens=8, temperature=0, logprobs=1))[0].outputs[0].logprobs)
```

Run with `VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1`.
</details>

Unit tests (run in CI by `.buildkite/test_areas/model_executor.yaml`):

```
pytest tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py -q
42 passed
```

New tests cover the FP8 range, fixed E8M0 scales (both dtypes), deterministic random bytes for uint8/int8/FP4, and wide integer params left untouched.

No model evaluation: real checkpoint loading is unaffected. Only `--load-format dummy` values change.

## Details

- **Identifying uint8 E8M0 scales by name.** Several quant methods (MXFP4, Quark OCP-MX, ModelOpt MXFP8) store E8M0 scales as uint8, which is indistinguishable from packed weights by dtype. `DummyModelLoader` now passes each tensor's attribute name, and uint8 tensors whose name contains `scale` get the E8M0 fill. Quant methods can still override per param with `dummy_weight_value`.
- **Magnitudes.** 2**-7 keeps dequantized weights small and finite: |FP4| ≤ 6 gives ≤ 0.047; FP8 ±1 gives ≤ 0.008. FP8 weights with float32 scales (dummy ±1e-3) end up around ±1e-3, matching bf16 dummies.
- **ROCm** previously zeroed all integer params for cross-process reproducibility. 8-bit integer params are now filled from the seeded generator, which is also reproducible.
- **Limitation.** GGUF block formats are uint8 with embedded fp16 scales, so random bytes can decode to large or non-finite values. That's no worse than the uninitialized memory they got before.
- **Behavior change.** Benchmarks run with dummy weights on FP8 / MXFP4 / int8 models may shift, because their quantized weights are no longer zero.

---

title: [Kernel][Build] Bump DeepGEMM to the 26/09/30 release and adapt the sparse indexer
body:
## Overview

Bump the vendored DeepGEMM pin to the tip of `vllm-project/DeepGEMM` `dev` (`6ce1c5e`): upstream's 26/09/30 public release (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#30, deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#462) plus vendoring import fixes (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#31, vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32) and a relaxed paged sparse MQA page-stride guard (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#33). Adapt vLLM to the breaking MQA-logits API.

## Claims

- vLLM builds, vendors and imports DeepGEMM 2.8.1.
- The DSA sparse indexer (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, HY-V4) keeps working on SM90/SM100/SM120 with the new MQA-logits API.
- On SM100 the FP8 indexer cache stays numerically identical: same FP8 values and the same per-token power-of-two scale, now stored as four packed UE8M0 bytes (a valid MXFP8 encoding) because SM100 MQA kernels only take MX scales.

## Breaking changes in DeepGEMM `1e1842a` → `6ce1c5e`

| Change | vLLM impact | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| `deep_gemm/__init__.py` imports a new `deep_gemm/locality_domain.py` | not vendored → `import vllm.third_party.deep_gemm` fails | install it in `deepgemm.cmake` |
| `_C.py` registered the locality-domain shim as `deep_gemm._C.locality_domain` | relative import fails when vendored as `vllm.third_party.deep_gemm`, and vLLM then silently treats DeepGEMM as unavailable | fixed in vllm-project/DeepGEMM#31 (in the pin); `tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py` now imports the package so CI catches this |
| The C++ MLOPart bridge imported `deep_gemm.utils.mlopart` and the epilogue module was named `deep_gemm.epilogue` | `localize()` (not called by vLLM) would fail when vendored | fixed in vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32 (in the pin): `_C.py` passes its `__package__` to the new `init(library_root_path, python_package_name)` |
| `fp8_fp4_paged_sparse_mqa_logits` page-stride guard lowered from 512 to 256 B (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#33) | DeepSeek-V4.1's sparse-logits block stride stays 512-aligned, which still satisfies it | none |
| `fp8_mqa_logits`, `fp8_paged_mqa_logits`, `fp8_gemm_nt_skip_head_mid`, `get_bf16_mega_gate_config` removed | unused by vLLM | none |
| `clean_logits` / `logits_dtype` removed from `fp8_fp4_(paged_)mqa_logits`; `max_seqlen_k` now required (> 0) | wrapper signatures | `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py`; prefill chunk metadata carries a host `max_seqlen_k` bound (no device sync) |
| `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` returns **compressed** logits `[M, max_seqlen_k]` (row `i` starts at K position `ks[i]`) on every arch | prefill top-k / candidate-block / DCP consumers indexed absolute columns | consumers run on row starts `0`, ends `ke - ks`; output indices are unchanged (already relative to `ks`) |
| SM100 MQA kernels take only MXFP8/MXFP4 with packed UE8M0 scales, **BF16 weights**, return **BF16 logits**; paged is varlen-only | FP8 indexer (fp32 per-token scale, scale folded into fp32 weights) rejected | see below |
| `bf16_mega_gate` default `scoring_func` → `'sqrtsoftplus'` | vLLM always passes it | none |
| FP8×FP4 / BF16 Mega MoE assert DeepGEMM's SM count equals the device's | only DBO + DeepEP-HT lowers it (`ubatch_utils.py`), not combined with Mega MoE today | none (noted) |
| Epilogue classes (`epilogue=` kwarg), locality domains, `shutdown` | additive | none |

### SM100 FP8 indexer

Every CUDA FP8 indexer writer already stores an exact power-of-two scale `2^ceil(log2(amax/448))` per 128-wide token. On SM100 (`mqa_logits_use_mx_scales()`) the writers store that scale's exponent as four equal UE8M0 bytes instead of the fp32, which is an exact MXFP8 encoding of the same values (same cache size, same FP8 bytes):

| Writer | Models |
|---|---|
| C++ `indexer_k_quant_and_cache` (`scale_fmt="mxfp8"`) | DeepSeek-V2-class `Indexer` (V3.2 via that class, DeepSeek MTP), HY-V4, DeepSeek-V3.2 under PCP |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 fused norm/RoPE (`_fused_norm_rope_kernel`) | DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5/5.2 (`GlmMoeDsa`), Dots3Note, V3.2 MTP |
| DeepSeek-V4 compressor (Triton; the CuTeDSL compressor is head-512 MLA only) | DeepSeek-V4 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 `indexer_k_norm_rope_store` | DeepSeek-V4.1 |
| GLM-5.3 kpool prefill compress + decode update | GLM-5.3 |

Readers need no change: `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache` (prefill, all of the above) and the DCP/PCP gathers copy the 4 scale bytes verbatim, and DeepGEMM reads the paged cache directly. The 512-wide MLA caches, MXFP4 caches, and the MiniMax-M3 / Qwen4 indexers are untouched.

FP8 Q keeps folding its per-(token, head) power-of-two scale into `weights`; `mqa_logits_mx_inputs` passes unit MX Q scales (exact, since `relu(s·x) = s·relu(x)` for `s > 0`) and casts weights to BF16. The BF16 logits are upcast to FP32 for the existing FP32-only top-k kernels (`as_fp32_logits`); routing BF16 logits straight to a BF16-capable top-k (DeepSelect / LiteTopK, #59921/#59922) is a follow-up.

SM90 and SM120 keep the FP8 format, FP32 weights and FP32 logits. Consequently the FP8 indexer cache's scale bytes now differ between SM100 and other architectures: moving that KV cache between SM100 and non-SM100 nodes (cross-generation PD disaggregation, shared KV offload) is not supported for these models. Same-architecture setups are unaffected.

## Validation

All on 4x GB200 (SM100), CUDA 13, torch 2.13; baseline = `main` with the old pin `1e1842a`, same build otherwise.

**GLM-5.3-Flash** (FP8, TP4 + EP, MTP=3, `--max-model-len 131072 --max-num-batched-tokens 131072 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --reasoning-parser glm47`, `reasoning_effort=low`), on the rebased branch vs `main` bfa7e5b7af. MRCR prompts are far longer than the indexer's coverage (2048 pools × 4 = 8K tokens), so they exercise top-k selection; long prefills also engage the TP prefill row sharding from #54951 (confirmed with a temporary log, e.g. 129K-row steps split `[47458, 18791, 42577, 19957]` across ranks):

| | `main` + `1e1842a` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| MRCR, 60 samples of 16K–32K tokens (`tests/evals/mrcr`), match ratio (2 / 4 / 8 needles) | 0.794 (0.823 / 0.798 / 0.760) | 0.810 (0.904 / 0.791 / 0.735) |
| MRCR, 24 samples of 57K–66K tokens, match ratio | 0.578 (4 runs hit max_tokens) | 0.665 |
| GSM8K (1319, 5-shot) | 90.8% | 91.6% |
| Serving, 4 runs of 128 × (4096 in / 512 out) at concurrency 32, output tok/s | 1492 / 1544 / 1491 / 1471 | 1484 / 1476 / 1337 / 1501 |
| Median ITL | 19.85 ms | 19.9 ms |

GLM-5.3 serving throughput tracks the MTP acceptance length, which varies per run (the 1337 tok/s run had 1.31 vs ~1.7–1.8 elsewhere); runs with matching acceptance agree (1476 @ 1.70 vs 1471 @ 1.71).

**DeepSeek-V4-Flash** (before the rebase onto current `main`; baseline 26a488ad93), TP2 + EP, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`, `--max-model-len 8192`; GSM8K via `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` (1319 questions, 5-shot, 2 rounds). GSM8K prompts fit inside the indexer's coverage (512 × 4 = 2K tokens), so this checks the SM100 path end to end rather than top-k selection:

| indexer cache | `main` + `1e1842a` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| fp8 | 95.5% / 94.6% | 94.8% / 94.6% |
| mxfp4 | 94.9% | 94.7% |

**Serving** — same server, `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 512 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos`, one warm-up + 3 runs each, sequential on the same GPUs:

| | output tok/s | mean TPOT | median ITL |

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Avoid reusing random draws across block verification rounds
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61114. Give block verification fresh acceptance and draft random draws when an uncommitted position is revisited in a later round.

## Claims

- Removes the cross-round sampling bias for deterministic and probabilistic drafts in Model Runner V2.
- Preserves seeded repeat, request-order and batch-splitting behavior in both verification modes. Standard probabilistic token sequences change, but their target distribution is retained.
- Uses a shared step-seed helper without new forwarding parameters, round-position tensors, scheduler state, host synchronization or sampling kernel launches.
- Covers ordinary draft sampling, the shared DFlash2/LiLiCorr candidate walk, DSpark and ordinary watermark fallback.

## Validation

Real V2 generation with one-layer, context-independent Llama target/draft models, TP=1, float32, two speculative tokens and 10,000 requests per configuration:

| Draft | Verification | Expected P(third token = 0) | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Deterministic | standard | 0.5000 | 0.5039 | 0.5039 |
| Deterministic | block | 0.5000 | 0.4171 | 0.4989 |
| Probabilistic | standard | 0.3000 | 0.3083 | 0.3055 |
| Probabilistic | block | 0.3000 | 0.3558 | 0.2898 |

All six output marginals pass in each updated configuration; both original block cases fail. Worker types and nonzero acceptance metrics confirm the real V2 draft-model path. All four updated configurations pass seeded repeat, reordered requests and split batches. Standard deterministic output retains its original hash; standard probabilistic output does not. The probabilistic block run also passes with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Before-fix values are the retained original model measurements; the updated four-case matrix was rerun after this review.

The official multi-round regression fails before the fix. Disabling only the acceptance step helper fails the deterministic block distribution assertion. Disabling only the cached draft step helper while retaining the acceptance repair also fails the probabilistic distribution assertion. Disabling only the candidate-walk helper fails both FP32/FP64 parity cases. These negative controls contain actual assertion failures, not setup errors or skips. The mixed watermark test covers the fused ordinary fallback and unchanged raw-logit caching.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_synthetic_rejection_sampler_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_i64.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_gumbel_sample.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_profile.py tests/watermarking --ignore=tests/watermarking/test_engine_compatibility.py --ignore=tests/watermarking/test_watermarking_e2e.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler_utils.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/gumbel.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/watermark.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash2/speculator.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py tests/watermarking/test_gumbel.py
git diff --check
```

Results: 350 official tests pass in the CUDA run, with three existing skips; all applicable native hooks pass. Separately, 175 CPU controls pass, with 76 accelerator-dependent skips. Five supplemental CUDA controls cover signed seeds, scalar/per-token cache columns, padding, graph replay and ordinary watermark fallback. Model tests use Triton attention and a bounded KV cache because this host's driver cannot run the reused CUDA 13 FlashAttention wheel. The candidate-walk tests cover FP32/FP64 step-seed parity and retain the existing conditional proposal-cache, padding and graph-replay checks. No AMD, full-runner CUDA graph, adaptive-policy model evaluation or throughput claim is made.

## Details

Block verification reads uniforms for draft positions past the finally accepted prefix. Reusing `(request seed, position)` in the next round reuses randomness conditioned on the preceding decision. Probabilistic drafting has the same problem with its position-keyed Gumbel noise.

Following review, `spec_step_seed(seed, step)` mixes the draft step into the seed's upper 32 bits. Cached Gumbel sampling uses its existing cache column; the DFlash2/LiLiCorr walk uses its loop step. A request's `(position, step)` pair does not repeat across rounds. Block acceptance calls the same helper with `i` inside its verification loop, always starting from the original request seed. No new flag is needed, including in DSpark and the watermark adapters. The fused ordinary watermark fallback uses the same cached step seed; context-keyed watermark draws are unchanged.

Cached draft seeding now applies under standard verification too. This changes standard probabilistic seeded sequences, not their target distribution; the updated implementation remains reproducible. This is distinct from #59355/#60945's residual lookahead bounds and #60652's grammar-invalid drafts, and complements #54282's within-round draft/target stream separation.

Related PR #61153 addresses the same bug with an explicit round-position tensor and a different seed mixer. This implementation instead uses the existing draft step inside the kernels. Both implementations passed the earlier shared four-case CUDA distribution comparison on #61153 at `170dcc217`; that comparison predates this reviewer-requested simplification. This is an alternative implementation of the same repair, not a claim that #61153 is incorrect.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Clear stale shared block-table rows
body:
## Overview

A larger MTP decode graph can read stale shared block-table rows after the target batch shrinks, allowing padded work to address another request's cache or state.

Move shared-row cleanup into `BlockTables`, as suggested in review.

## Claims

- Clear previously active rows during gather and dummy preparation, using the existing buffers and gather kernel.
- Preserve active rows, returned views, and independent PCP output buffers.
- Remove the MTP caller workaround without changing model math.

## Validation

Base: `92dc3dd39332`, H20.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New regressions without the fix | 7 failed |
| BlockTables, speculator, PCP suites with the fix | 140 passed |
| Model/cache/offload compatibility suites | 656 passed |
| Pre-commit, including mypy and CI test tethering | Passed |
| BlockTables with strict GPU sync checking | 17 passed |
| GLM-5.3-Flash TP8/MTP3, stream=true | 47/47 correct, no truncation |

Serving used CUDA Graphs and native CPU offload on H20×8: cold requests, GPU cache hits, forced CPU restores, branched prefixes, and mixed concurrency (8/5/2/8/3), with 1,281–32,769 input tokens and a 1,024-token output cap. CPU restore phases recorded 56,960 external cache-hit tokens; MTP accepted 1,549 of 1,573 draft tokens. This is correctness validation, not a throughput comparison.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py -q
```

<details>
<summary>Compatibility checks</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_state_dtype.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_attention_warmup.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py -q
```

</details>

## Details

`BlockTables` tracks potentially dirty shared rows. Gather clears through `max(num_reqs_padded, previous_dirty_rows)`; dummy preparation follows the same rule and tracks rows that profiling may populate. External `out` buffers leave shared tracking unchanged.

Regressions cover real/dummy transitions, shrink/grow/empty batches, independent outputs, and physical KPool slots under eager execution and CUDA Graph replay. PCP has unit coverage; distributed PCP serving was not tested.

The full serving run used sync-check `warn`: strict mode reports a separately reproduced, unchanged SM90 MLA metadata copy. The affected BlockTables methods passed all 17 tests under strict checking.

Duplicate checks found no other shared-row lifecycle fix: #45005 handles legacy slot mappings; #60767 handles sliding-window columns.

AI assistance was used for code and tests.

title: [Core][Refactor] Move KV cache planning logic to kv_cache_planning.py
body:
## Overview

Move the KV cache grouping, sizing, and capacity-planning logic from `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` into a new module, `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_planning.py`. This is a pure code move with no behavior change.

Split out from #53558 so the large move can be reviewed separately from the pluggable `KVCacheConfigBuilder` change.

## Claims

- `kv_cache_utils.py` goes from about 2.8k to about 1.2k lines. It keeps the block, hash, and free-queue utilities, plus the helpers that consume a finished `KVCacheConfig`: `get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config`, `generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config`, `get_kv_cache_capacity`, and `update_kv_cache_capacity`.
- `kv_cache_planning.py` holds the planning path: `get_kv_cache_configs`, `get_kv_cache_groups`, `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups`, page-size unification, packed/hybrid grouping, memory and max-model-len estimation, auto-fit, and TP-replica helpers (38 functions).
- Function names and bodies are unchanged. No compatibility re-exports are left in `kv_cache_utils.py`; all in-tree callers are updated.

## Validation

- Every moved function is byte-identical to `origin/main`. This was checked by comparing each top-level definition with the AST. Reviewers can confirm with:
  ```bash
  git diff --color-moved=dimmed-zebra origin/main...HEAD -- vllm/v1/core/
  ```
- `pre-commit` passes (ruff, mypy, typos, and the test-tethering checks).
- Ran the affected unit tests on CPU, on both this branch and `origin/main`. Both give the same result: **294 passed, 19 skipped**.
  ```bash
  pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
    tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py \
    tests/v1/engine/test_init_error_messaging.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py \
    tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hidden_states_connector.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_dsv4_packed_zeroer_geometry.py
  ```
- `tests/models/test_initialization.py`, `tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py`, and `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py` import and collect cleanly. They need a GPU, so they are left to CI.

## Details

Besides the move itself, these updates keep behavior and CI coverage the same:

- **Imports:** updated in `v1/engine/core.py`, `v1/hisparse/layout.py`, `v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`, `v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`, and the affected tests.
- **Monkeypatch targets:** the `get_hisparse_host_pool_bytes` patches and the `max_memory_usage_bytes` patch string now point at `kv_cache_planning`. Patching the old module would silently stop taking effect.
- **Subprocess test:** the import embedded in the script string of `test_is_kv_cache_spec_uniform` now uses the new module.
- **Buildkite:** wherever `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` and `.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml` list `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` as a source dependency, `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_planning.py` is now listed too. Changes to the moved code still trigger the same jobs.

Out-of-tree code that imports planning functions from `vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils` needs to switch to `vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_planning`.

Follow-up: #53558 can rebase on top of this, so its diff only contains the builder changes.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Kimi-K3] Stage fused KDA decode weights after loading
body:
## Overview

The ROCm Kimi-K3 fused KDA decode read uninitialized memory as its conv1d and gated-norm weights whenever weight loaders were skipped, as with `--load-format dummy`. This intermittently produced NaN logprobs. Those copies are now built from the final parameters after loading.

## Claims

- `process_weights_after_loading` stages `decode_conv1d_weight` and `decode_norm_weight` from `conv1d.weight` and `o_norm.weight`, and the two side-effect weight loaders are removed.
- This fixes the intermittent HTTP 400 (`Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan`) in `test_prefix_cache.py` on MI355.

## Validation

MI355 (gfx950), `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. In `test_prefix_cache.py[offload-partial]`, NaN runs went from 5 of 21 to 0 of 20. The new `test_decode_weights_staged_after_loading` fails before (18432/18432 elements are NaN) and passes after. `models/kimi_k3` passes: 311 passed.

The perf runs used `riverclouds/Kimi-K3-8L-dummy` at TP1, 5 interleaved runs per column, each with a fresh server. Values are mean ± sd.

| `vllm bench serve` (4096 in / 256 out, conc 16) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Request throughput (req/s) | 7.687 ± 0.025 | 7.672 ± 0.009 |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 634.4 ± 6.5 | 633.5 ± 2.5 |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 5.434 ± 0.004 | 5.454 ± 0.017 |

No real-weight Kimi-K3 checkpoint was available for an accuracy run. With real weights, the buffers receive the same values the loaders wrote before.

## Details

The fp32 copies from #50654 are non-persistent `torch.empty` buffers that were written only inside the conv1d and o_norm weight loaders. `DummyModelLoader` skips both, so the fused decode used whatever the allocator returned: usually zeros, sometimes NaN. That poisoned the recurrent state from the first decode step. The post-load hook runs for every loader, including layerwise reload (the buffer storage is reused, so CUDA graphs stay valid). It skips weights that arrive already processed. The NVIDIA `KimiK3DeltaAttention` has the same latent issue and is left for a follow-up. #59245 reads these buffers and will need a rebase.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

---

title: [Perf] Improve `_topk_topp_kernel()` for masked logits
body:
* **Problem:** the `_topk_topp_kernel()` kernel wastes work searching for a top-k cutoff even when the input logits have less than `k` finite logits (the rest are `-inf`).
* **Solution:** Skip the search when `num_finite_total <= k`, preserving the existing top-p path.
* Does this make sense to the kernel authors & reviewers? @cakeng @njhill 

## Benchmarks

Using the `benchmark_topk_topp.py` script on an H100 80GB. CUPTI, 5 warmups and 20 measured iterations, cold L2, no CUDA graphs, Triton only.

### Table 1: Masked Logits

We observe multi-ms savings for `num_finite_logits <= k`. The runtimes below are a single call to `apply_top_k_top_p_triton()` plus `logits.clone()`, averaged over 20 measurements. All logits are `-inf` except for `num_finite_logits`. The scenario uses bsz=1024 and vocab=131072. This bsz happens e.g. with concurrency=64, DFlash K=15 (64 * 15+1 = 1024). The speedups are probably larger because the timings include cloning a 512 MiB logits tensor (1024 × 131072 × 4 bytes). At peak H100 SXM memory bandwidth, that copy alone takes about 320 µs (read and write).

| `num_finite_logits` | Top-k | Top-p | Main (ms) | Branch (ms) | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | 50 | Disabled | 6.672 | 0.863 | 7.74× |
| 49 | 50 | Disabled | 7.029 | 0.862 | 8.15× |
| 50 | 50 | Disabled | 7.074 | 0.862 | 8.21× |
| 51 | 50 | Disabled | 3.094 | 3.076 | 1.01× |
| 8 | 100 | 0.9 | 10.151 | 4.221 | 2.40× |
| 99 | 100 | 0.9 | 12.145 | 5.907 | 2.06× |
| 100 | 100 | 0.9 | 12.411 | 6.176 | 2.01× |
| 101 | 100 | 0.9 | 4.331 | 4.315 | 1.00× |

### Table 2: No regression

This table follows the original one in [PR #33538](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33538). All logits are finite. Across 168 cases, branch runtime changes by -1.5% to +3.3%, with a median change of +0.6%. These small differences may be measurement noise.

title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Fix MultiConnector stats and proxy SSE responses
body:
## Overview

Using direct Mooncake with Mooncake Store can fail in MultiConnector's metrics handler, and the Mooncake example proxy labels SSE responses as JSON, causing clients such as AIPerf to reject them. Fix both integration issues by respecting optional metrics exporters and returning the correct streaming Content-Type.

## Claims

- Skip children without Prometheus exporters while continuing to forward supported metrics and `engine_idx`.
- Return `text/event-stream` for streaming requests on `/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions`; preserve JSON responses for non-streaming requests and forward response bytes unchanged.

```diff
 P transfer stats -> MultiConnector metrics
-  require an exporter for every child with stats
+  forward stats only to registered exporters

 D SSE frames -> Mooncake proxy -> client
-  Content-Type: application/json
+  Content-Type: text/event-stream
```

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_proxy.py \
  -k 'TestMultiConnectorStats or test_mooncake_proxy' -q
```

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stats-only child, with empty or mixed exporter registry | Both regression cases fail on main `c75cb63cd2bb` | All 17 stats cases pass |
| Real ASGI routes, completion/chat × streaming/non-streaming | 2 streaming cases fail on main `258b97ff6bc1`; 2 non-streaming cases pass | All 4 cases pass |
| Combined PR branch, based on `258b97ff6bc1` | — | **21 passed, 15 deselected** |

The metrics regression also checks that the supported child's payload reaches its exporter with `engine_idx=2`. The proxy regression mocks only the remote P/D calls and checks the actual response headers and bytes. In Buildkite, the V1 KV Connectors step runs the metrics regression. The proxy regression is CPU-only, so it is marked `cpu_test` and runs in the CPU V1 Others step, which also lists the proxy as a source dependency so proxy-only changes still trigger it.

Changed-file pre-commit checks pass:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  .buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml \
  examples/disaggregated/mooncake_connector/mooncake_connector_proxy.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_proxy.py
```

Earlier ROCm end-to-end validation used integration commit `b41cf676db9cc124fffbcf305f7fa8c8d2f895b8`, containing the identical proxy file and metrics `observe()` implementation:

- [Before the proxy fix](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38169410559): AIPerf attempted JSON parsing of SSE frames; all 13 sampled warmup responses were rejected.
- [C16 serving](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38174661539): Kimi-K3 + DSpark3, 1P1D/16 MI355X, Mooncake RDMA + TCP Store completed a 3600-second performance window with 2006 successes and 4 errors. The workflow later failed while importing the separate GSM8K evaluator.
- [Natural GSM8K](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38203116096): flexible extraction 1269/1319 (96.21%).

GPU evidence belongs to that integration revision; the current main-based PR branch has local regression coverage. Store lease timeouts and empty-response failures remain separate limitations. No additional GPU experiment was dispatched for this PR.

## Details

**Metrics:** `KVConnectorBase_V1.build_prom_metrics()` may return `None`. MultiConnector's metrics factory already excludes null exporters, while stats collection independently includes stats-only children. Direct Mooncake provides stats without an exporter, so its worker stats trigger the assertion in the API output handler. A conditional exporter lookup follows the existing optional-interface contract. Stats collection is unchanged; missing exporter IDs are skipped, so this assertion no longer detects inconsistent IDs in the metrics path.

**HTTP:** `_handle_completions` already forwards the request's streaming mode to D. Use the same flag to select the response media type. KV transfer and generation logic are unchanged.

The metrics portion follows up the **same fix proposed in #43836 for #43828**, adapted to the current flat stats payload with regression coverage. That PR remains open; this is not a distinct solution. The submitting operator explicitly requested including it here to cover both direct-Mooncake integration failures. Searches found no overlapping proxy SSE-header fix.

Both changes are reversible and scoped to metrics forwarding and the example proxy. AI assistance (Codex) was used; this remains a draft submitted at the human operator's request.

title: [Security] Bound decoded and downloaded media per request
body:
## Overview

Bound the total downloaded and decoded media in one multimodal request. The same patch was reviewed and approved in the private security fork before public submission.

## Claims

- Enforce one decoded-byte budget across images, audio, and video frames, including direct PIL chat inputs.
- Enforce one streamed HTTP download-byte budget across all media URLs in a request, while retaining the per-response limit.
- Reject requests that exceed either budget and document both configuration controls.

## Validation

- `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /Users/jperezde/Documents/Dev/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_unprocessable_entity_error.py tests/test_connections.py tests/test_audio_media_size_precheck.py tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py -q` — 44 passed.
- `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /Users/jperezde/Documents/Dev/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_audio.py tests/multimodal/media/test_video.py -q -k 'request_budget_rejects_second_decoded_audio_clip or video_request_budget_counts_torch_frames'` — 2 passed.
- `/Users/jperezde/Documents/Dev/vllm/.venv/bin/pre-commit run` — passed on all staged files, including Ruff and mypy.
- `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /Users/jperezde/Documents/Dev/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_audio.py tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py tests/multimodal/media/test_video.py tests/multimodal/media/test_unprocessable_entity_error.py -q -m skip_global_cleanup` — 34 passed, 62 deselected after the audio reservation follow-up.
- `/Users/jperezde/Documents/Dev/vllm/.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/multimodal/media/base.py vllm/multimodal/media/audio.py tests/multimodal/media/test_audio.py` — passed, including Ruff and mypy.
- The initial public commit has the same stable patch ID as the approved private commit.

An unrestricted run of those media files on this macOS host segfaulted in `torch.accelerator.memory.empty_host_cache` during the global cleanup fixture after the first test. The selected tests above skip that cleanup.

No model evaluation was run. Accepted inputs follow the same decode and serving paths; requests above the new resource limits are rejected by design.

## Details

Previously, a request could pass every per-item media check while still scheduling and retaining many compressed media items before prompt-length admission. The change shares request-scoped budgets across the synchronous and asynchronous chat media paths. HTTP responses are charged as bytes stream in; decoded images are charged before raster allocation, audio decoders reserve capacity before decoding and settle their actual decoded bytes afterward, and video frames are charged during extraction or before JPEG decoding as appropriate. In-flight audio reservations count against the budget for other media. The existing per-item limits remain in effect.

The default decoded budget is 715827880 bytes and the default aggregate HTTP download budget is 256 MB. Operators can configure either limit through the documented environment variables. Requests above a limit now fail rather than consume unbounded frontend resources.

Coverage includes chat completions, messages, and responses that use the Python multimodal tracker; HTTP URLs, `data:` URLs, allowed local files, direct PIL inputs, and video frames. The opt-in Rust frontend and offline user-code helpers are outside this Python parser change.

Duplicate-work check: I searched open and merged upstream PRs for request-wide media budgets, decoded media limits, and HTTP download limits, and inspected the related media PR diffs. The related Rust frontend, audio preprocessing, and Pillow error-handling PRs do not close this Python request-wide path.

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Cursor and OpenAI Codex). The human submitter is responsible for reviewing the diff and validating the change.

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Slice expert LoRA by the unpadded per-rank size under TP
body:
## Overview

Expert LoRA factors are sliced at the wrong offset under TP > 1 when the MoE backend pads the expert intermediate dimension (e.g. Marlin / FlashInfer TRTLLM MXFP4). Every rank except rank 0 silently applies the wrong LoRA rows.

## Claims

- `FusedMoEWithLoRA` and `FusedMoE3DWithLoRA` shard an adapter along the intermediate dim by the unpadded per-rank size, matching how the base expert weights are sharded.
- No behavior change when the backend does not pad.
- No dependency on a FlashInfer version.

## Validation

CPU-only check of the slicing (TP 2 and 4, every rank, per-expert and both 3D layouts, padded and unpadded), run locally and not added to the test suite:

| `vllm/lora/layers/fused_moe.py` | passed | failed |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 6 (unpadded cases) | 6 (padded cases) |
| this PR | 12 | 0 |

`ruff check` and `ruff format --diff` are clean on the changed file.

End-to-end on `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, TP 2, `moe_backend="marlin"` (per-rank intermediate size 1440 padded to 1536), random expert-only LoRA (rank 8, seeded; `gate_up_proj` and `down_proj`). Reference: the same model at TP 1 with `triton_unfused`, which does no TP slicing. 16 prompts x 200 tokens, teacher-forced `prompt_logprobs`. Nightly arm64 image at `af7f9488c` (the changed file is byte-identical to `ffec22127` there), one run per row:

| TP 2 marlin | adapter | MAE vs ref | effect projection | effect correlation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | none | 0.150 | – | – |
| `main` | small | 0.444 | 0.38 | 0.47 |
| `main` | large | 1.682 | 0.53 | 0.50 |
| this PR | none | 0.157 | – | – |
| this PR | small | 0.139 | 0.76 | 0.82 |
| this PR | large | 1.013 | 0.83 | 0.77 |

`triton_unfused` at TP 2 is affected as well (1440 padded to 1472): small adapter 0.444 on `main`, 0.144 with this PR (no-adapter floor 0.137).

The no-adapter rows are the Marlin-vs-Triton floor (Marlin differs from itself by 0.09 across two runs). With this change the small adapter is back at that floor; the projection of the adapter effect (logprob with adapter minus base) on the reference effect goes from 0.38 to 0.76. The large adapter degrades the model itself (Marlin self-difference 0.69), so only the direction is meaningful there.

The same on/off contrast on DeepSeek V4.1 (TP 4, 576 padded to 640, FlashInfer TRTLLM experts with a prototype LoRA path, change backported to an older dev build): MAE against the unpadded Triton backend 0.028 -> 0.014 for a small adapter (no-adapter floor 0.014) and 0.73 -> 0.31 for a large one.

## Details

Root cause: `_slice_w13_b` / `_slice_w2_a` use `moe_config.intermediate_size_per_partition` as the per-rank stride. `RoutedExperts.__init__` overwrites that field with the result of `maybe_roundup_sizes()`, so it is the padded size (MXFP4 rounds up to 128 for Marlin / TRTLLM / DeepGEMM / CUTLASS and to 64 for Triton). The base weights are sharded by `loaded_weight.shape[shard_dim] // tp_size` in `RoutedExperts._load_w13` / `_load_w2`. With 576 padded to 640, the base weight of rank `r` holds rows `[576 r, 576 (r + 1))` while the adapter slice is `[640 r, 640 (r + 1))`. Nothing raises because the slice is copied into the head of a zero buffer. We first observed this on DeepSeek V4.1 (TP 4, padded MoE backends).

Fix: use `moe_config.intermediate_size_per_partition_unpadded` as the stride. Buffers keep the padded size with a zero tail. For the concatenated `(gate, up)` layout of the 3D class, the up half is placed at the allocated per-rank size, where the base `w13` has it.

Not addressed: GPT-OSS MXFP4 uses a block-aligned shard stride in its own loader (`cdiv(intermediate_size / 32, tp_size) * 32`), which differs from `intermediate_size // tp_size` at TP 4 / 8.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs and issues for `_slice_w13_b`, `intermediate_size_per_partition LoRA padded`, `fused_moe LoRA TP slice`; nothing addresses this. #61164 and #61165 touch other parts of the MoE LoRA path and do not overlap.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Stop re-parsing the whole GLM tool argument per chunk
body:
## Overview

Streaming a GLM tool call re-parses the whole argument on every chunk, so a long argument (for example a 100 KB file `Write`) costs quadratic CPU on the API server. This PR streams the open argument value with work proportional to each chunk.

Related: #51141 fixes the same pattern for the Inkling parser only (compared under Details).

## Claims

- Parser cost per streamed GLM argument chunk no longer grows with argument length: 6.4 ms at 100 KB and 12.7 ms at 200 KB become 7 us at every size (M4 Pro, table below).
- Streamed deltas are unchanged, including schema type coercion and the held-back trailing value for non-string keys.
- Opt-in per parser through a new `ParserEngineConfig.arg_value_extender`. Only `glm47_moe` (GLM-4.7 and later, including GLM-5.x) sets it. Every other parser keeps its current path.
- Model evaluation does not apply, since model output and streamed tool-call text are unchanged.

## Validation

Tests on `691b6c37c`:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/parser/engine` | 5869 passed |
| `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_glm4_moe_tool_parser.py tests/reasoning/test_glm4_moe_reasoning_parser.py` | 39 passed |
| pre-commit on the changed files | passed |

New tests in `tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py`:
- `test_long_call_streams_non_streaming_arguments`: a 26 KB GLM call with escapes, non-ASCII and tag-like text, streamed in 7-character chunks through `parse_delta`, gives the same arguments as `extract_tool_calls`. Runs with no schema and with a schema that coerces an integer key.
- `test_conversions_do_not_grow_with_argument_length`: counts streaming calls to the arg converter. With this PR the count is 23 for both 40 and 400 lines of content. On `main` it is 547 and 5,227, so the test fails there.
- Two small tests for the GLM extender: a closing tag split across chunks, and the cases where no extender is created.

**Same output as `main`.** A local differential test streamed 15,000 random GLM tool calls through `main`'s parser and this branch. It used random chunk sizes; schemas with string, integer, object, array, boolean and nullable keys; repeated keys; truncated calls; and tag fragments inside values. Every per-chunk `DeltaMessage` was identical. Both new paths ran: per 3,000 cases, about 100K chunks extended a streamed string value and about 57K extended a held-back value. The same check passed on 6,000 more cases with the GLM regexes from #54971 applied to both sides.

**Per-chunk cost.** The script below streams a GLM `Write` call through `Glm47MoeParser.parse_delta` in 8-character chunks. Each row is the mean cost per chunk since the previous row. Apple M4 Pro, Python 3.12, 3 runs each, range across runs.

| Argument size | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 25 KB | 1.04-1.06 ms | 6.9-7.1 us |
| 50 KB | 3.11-3.17 ms | 7.0-7.1 us |
| 100 KB | 6.37-6.44 ms | 6.9-7.0 us |
| 200 KB | 12.68-12.79 ms | 6.8-7.0 us |

`_compute_arg_delta` alone, timed with a script that drives the extracted parser functions, goes from 6.7 ms to 0.9 us per chunk at 100 KB and from 13.3 ms to 0.95 us at 200 KB, with byte-identical streamed arguments.

**Replay at serving step rate.** A 115 KB Python-file `Write` call, tokenized with the GLM-5.3 tokenizer, replayed through the streaming lexer and `_compute_arg_delta` at 22.4 decode steps/s and 2.8 tokens per step (the rate measured on a GLM-5.3 decode server). Parser CPU per 30 s of stream climbs from 0.008 to 0.20 cores on `main` over the 6.3-minute stream. With this PR it stays between 0.00006 and 0.00008 cores. The streamed arguments are byte-identical.

<details>
<summary>Reproducer</summary>

Run from the root of a vLLM checkout:

```python
import time
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

from tests.parser.engine.conftest import make_mock_tokenizer
from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
from vllm.parser.glm47_moe import Glm47MoeParser

vocab = {"<think>": 1, "</think>": 2, "<tool_call>": 3, "</tool_call>": 4}
request = MagicMock(spec=ChatCompletionRequest)
request.tools, request.tool_choice, request.include_reasoning = [], "auto", True
parser = Glm47MoeParser(make_mock_tokenizer(vocab))

head = (
    "</think><tool_call>Write<arg_key>file_path</arg_key>"
    "<arg_value>/repo/app.py</arg_value><arg_key>content</arg_key><arg_value>"
)
body = (open("vllm/sampling_params.py").read() * 10)[:200_000]
parser.parse_delta(head, [], request, finished=False)

marks, elapsed, chunks = [25_000, 50_000, 100_000, 200_000], 0.0, 0
for i in range(0, len(body), 8):
    start = time.perf_counter()
    parser.parse_delta(body[i : i + 8], [], request, finished=False)
    elapsed += time.perf_counter() - start
    chunks += 1
    if marks and i + 8 >= marks[0]:
        print(f"{marks.pop(0) // 1000} KB: {elapsed / chunks * 1e6:.1f} us per chunk")
        elapsed, chunks = 0.0, 0
```

</details>

## Details

**Trigger.** Any streamed GLM tool call with a long argument, for example a coding agent writing a file.

**Mechanism.** `_compute_arg_delta` runs once per `ARG_VALUE_CHUNK`. Each run works on the whole argument received so far:
- joins `slot.args`;
- runs `_glm47_arg_converter`: three regex passes and `json.dumps`;
- runs `_fix_arg_types`: `json.loads`;
- runs `_safe_arg_prefix`: a Python character loop over the whole JSON, 89% of the time under cProfile.

GLM sets `stream_arg_deltas=True` and no `arg_structural_chars`, so every chunk takes this path.

**Effect.** Cost per chunk grows linearly with the argument, so one tool call costs quadratic time. It runs inside `parse_delta` on the API server's event loop, so it also delays other requests on that server.

**Why the fix is in `engine/`.** The full conversion per chunk lives in `ParserEngine._compute_arg_delta`. Every parser that sets `arg_converter` and streams deltas without `arg_structural_chars` runs it on every chunk: GLM-4.7, Granite, Inkling, MiniMax-M2, Nemotron-v3, Qwen3 and Step-3.5. The engine part is a generic opt-in hook, and the format knowledge stays in each parser's file. This PR wires GLM only.

**Fix.**
- After a full conversion, once the safe prefix is sent, the engine calls `arg_value_extender(slot.args)`. It returns an extender for the open trailing value, or `None`.
- For each later chunk, the extender returns the JSON text the chunk appends to that value, or `None` when the chunk may change anything else. On `None`, the engine runs the full conversion as today, which may create a new extender.
- `_safe_arg_prefix` also reports whether the open value streams. If it does, the engine sends the extender's text. If the value is held back (non-string key), it sends nothing, as today.
- `ToolCallSlot.streamed_json` keeps its parts in a list and joins them on read, like `args`, so the fast path does no work proportional to the argument.

Full conversions now happen only around argument boundaries.

**Why the GLM extender gives the same output.**
- The open value runs to the end of the raw arguments, and the converter emits it as a JSON string with `json.dumps`. JSON string escaping maps each character on its own, so a chunk appends `json.dumps(chunk)[1:-1]`.
- A chunk can only change the parse by completing `</arg_value>`. The extender keeps the last 11 raw characters, so it also sees a closing tag split across chunks.
- The extender is only created when the open key is the last key of the parsed arguments. A repeated earlier key updates an earlier position, so that case falls back to the full conversion.
- Schema coercion leaves string keys alone and coerces earlier values the same way every time, so the JSON before the open value stays the same.

**Overlapping PRs** (checked 2026-10-12).
- #51141 (Inkling) caches the wrapper offset, scans the safe prefix incrementally, and sets `arg_structural_chars`. Its scan resumes from the previous end of the JSON. That fits Inkling, whose converter returns a growing slice of the raw text. The GLM converter closes the JSON (`"}`) again on every chunk, so it needs a different approach. I think Inkling could implement `arg_value_extender` too, so both parsers share one mechanism; we can align with #51141 on the order.
- #54971 changes only the GLM key regexes. The extender reuses `_ARG_RE` and `_PARTIAL_ARG_RE`, and its close check depends only on `</arg_value>`, so it works with either version (differential above).
- #53739 and #58780 also edit `_compute_arg_delta` or `_safe_arg_prefix`, so whichever lands second needs a rebase.

**Limitations.** All measurements drive the parser code directly. There is no end-to-end run on a GPU serving deployment.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used for the implementation, tests and measurements.

---

title: [ROCm][DSv4] AITER MegaMoE Fixed-Slot Dispatch For DeepSeek-V4
body:
AITER MegaMoEV2 (initially integrated in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59685) has two dispatch schemes:
1. Compact: a separate megamoe_prepare_compact kernel packs tokens before dispatch.
2. Fixed-slot: each token writes straight into a per-rank slot, with no prepare kernel.

AITER takes fixed-slot only when the runtime's max_tok_per_rank is at most FIXED_SLOT_MAX_MTPR. That limit is 255 by default and can be raised with AITER_MEGA_FIXED_SLOT_MAX_MTPR. In the initial integration, we built a single runtime with the compact path, so decode always pays for the compact prepare step.

This PR builds a second runtime and picks between the two paths at each decode step.

The decode runtime is sized `max_tok_per_rank = prev_power_of_2(FIXED_SLOT_MAX_MTPR)`, which ends up being 128 by default. It's only built when AITER's bundle plan says that size actually uses fixed-slot. Otherwise behavior is unchanged. The fused shared expert makes 49 experts per rank, so no decode runtime is built with FSE enabled.

### Perf and Accuracy

#### Without MTP
| Concurrency | Tokens/rank/step | main TPOT p50 | This PR TPOT p50 | main tok/s | This PR tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | 4 (fixed-slot) | 40.1 ms | **34.5 ms (−14%)** | 775 | **894 (+15%)** |
| 128 | 16 (fixed-slot) | 49.1 ms | **43.3 ms (−12%)** | 2490 | **2827 (+14%)** |
| 2048 | 256 (compact) | 121.3 ms | 121.9 ms | 14456 | 13934 |
#### With MTP (DSpark, 3 draft tokens)
| Concurrency | Tokens/rank/step | main TPOT p50 | This PR TPOT p50 | main ITL p50 | This PR ITL p50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | 16 (fixed-slot) | 15.4 ms | **14.0 ms (−9%)** | 50.6 ms | **44.9 ms (−11%)** |
| 128 | 64 (fixed-slot) | 23.0 ms | **22.0 ms (−4%)** | 67.6 ms | **58.1 ms (−14%)** |
| 512 | 256 (compact) | 45.8 ms | 45.5 ms | 113.9 ms | 113.7 ms |

At 2048 without MTP and 512 with MTP, both builds use the compact runtime, so they run the same kernels. So it is expected that there is no diff from the current main.
### Accuracy (gsm8k 5-shot, flexible / strict, ±0.006)
| | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Without MTP | 0.9530 / 0.9538 | 0.9545 / 0.9538 |
| With MTP | 0.9538 / 0.9538 | 0.9515 / 0.9515 |

MTP acceptance rate is 91–92% on both.

**Edit**: A useful note from @benenzhu 
>One note from that setup: with K6 drafts each decode request carries 7 tokens, so at concurrency 128 a rank holds 112+ tokens per step, about 143 on average in our runs because of uneven load. With the default FIXED_SLOT_MAX_MTPR=255 the decode runtime holds 128 tokens, and those steps fall back to the compact path. We ran with AITER_MEGA_FIXED_SLOT_MAX_MTPR=511, which gives a 256-token decode runtime. It may be worth mentioning this knob in the description.

title: [Bugfix] Preserve independent tokenizer code_revision in snapshot resolution
body:
## Overview

Preserve an independent Hugging Face tokenizer `code_revision` when resolving a Hub ID to a local data snapshot. This applies the same guard the processor path already has (introduced in #60825) to the tokenizer resolver.

## Claims

- Before this change, `resolve_tokenizer_args` rewrote `tokenizer_name` to a data-revision snapshot unconditionally. Transformers reads dynamic tokenizer code from a local directory as-is, so a `code_revision` distinct from the data revision was silently shadowed: the code from the data snapshot was loaded, and invalid/older code revisions were silently accepted instead of rejected.
- After this change, default and matching code/data revisions keep the snapshot optimization (byte-identical token IDs vs direct Transformers loading in the regression fixture), while a distinct code revision is passed to Transformers with the Hub ID intact.

## Validation

Linux x86_64 container (Ubuntu, Python 3.12.13, Torch 2.13.0+cpu, Transformers 5.19.0, HF Hub 2.2.0), native source build of this branch (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, editable install). Normal production imports and `get_tokenizer` were exercised; no AST extraction or tokenizer stubs.

Pinned fixture: `hf-internal-testing/test_dynamic_tokenizer` at data revision `08a35780b7a78794436d8654aafa26ee0165c149` (repo has exactly two commits; `73293ac504e43f4a895688b57c65cebe24f01a38` predates the tokenizer code and contains only `.gitattributes`).

- With the fix: `pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py -q -p no:cacheprovider` → **10 passed** (6 pre-existing + 4 new: 2 parametrized rejection cases, matching/default control pair, and a resolver-contract test).
- A/B discriminative check: reverting only the `code_revision` guard in `vllm/tokenizers/registry.py` and re-running → **3 failed** (`test_tokenizer_code_revision_rejects_missing_code[unknown-revision]` and `[revision-without-code]` both `DID NOT RAISE OSError`; `test_tokenizer_code_revision_distinct_from_revision` assertion on kept Hub ID), 2 passed (matching/default controls). Guard restored, 10 passed again.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/tokenizers/registry.py tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py`: passed (Ruff, mypy, SPDX, test tethering included).
- `git diff --check`: passed.

### How to test

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py -k code_revision -q -p no:cacheprovider
pre-commit run --files vllm/tokenizers/registry.py tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py
```

Manual reproduction: call `get_tokenizer` with `tokenizer_mode="hf"`, `trust_remote_code=True`, the pinned data revision above, and either `code_revision="never"` or the older code commit. Before this fix both calls load code from the data snapshot (no error); after the fix both fail with the Transformers missing-revision/missing-code error. With omitted or matching `code_revision`, encoding `"hello world"` remains equal to direct `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained`.

## Details

`resolve_tokenizer_args` previously resolved every HF tokenizer to a directory pinned to the data `revision`. Dynamic code cannot be re-selected against a local directory, so forwarding `code_revision` in kwargs cannot restore the requested code selection. The fix preserves the Hub ID when the two revisions differ, mirroring the processor path from #60825. This deliberately gives up the snapshot request reduction for independently versioned code, as the processor path already does.

The tests extend the existing tokenizer suite and use its supported `skip_global_cleanup` marker (tokenizers only, no GPU models). They remain wired into the existing tokenizer CI area.

Scope is direct `get_tokenizer(..., code_revision=...)` loading. No `vllm serve --code-revision` regression, inference accuracy improvement, or performance gain is claimed. Full tokenizer-suite, serving E2E, GPU and model evaluations were not run; the targeted validation above must not be read as those results.

Duplicate-work searches covered #60825 references, open PRs matching `code_revision` + tokenizer keywords, and `get_non_weight_snapshot_path`. No open PR for this tokenizer guard was found at the time of checking; nearby #54780 addresses a different caller. AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, tests and review (Hermes Agent); the submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Quantization] Auto-disable DeepGEMM for Kolibri 1 on SM12x
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Auto-disable DeepGEMM for Kolibri 1 on SM12x, next to the existing Qwen3.5 exclusions, and apply the exclusions to automatic FP8 MoE backend selection. Follow-up to #60827; 

## Claims

- On B200, Kolibri 1 FP8 is faster at the defaults than with `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`., no claimed accuracy issues could be found
- On SM12x, FP8 MoE layers of excluded models select Triton instead of DeepGEMM. SM90 and SM100 selection is unchanged.
- On DGX Spark, Kolibri 1 and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B FP8 now run as fast at the defaults as with `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`, with GSM8K unchanged.

## Validation

Kolibri 1 FP8 on B200, TP=1, nightly `253e02b95e` + #60827 (identical to main `0838cd6593` in all files this PR or kernel selection touches). Two runs per arm, interleaved; latency uses 512 input / 256 output tokens, throughput 256 requests of 1024 / 256 after a full-batch warmup.

| Kolibri on SM100 | Dense / MoE | Batch 1, s | Batch 32, s | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Not excluded (main, this PR) | DeepGEMM / TRTLLM | 1.295 | 2.208 | 5562 |
| Excluded | CUTLASS / TRTLLM | 1.487 | 2.409 | 5014 |

The excluded arm selects the same kernels as `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`, so Kolibri is listed for SM12x only.

DGX Spark (GB10), TP=1, main `61d9c777bf` (Kolibri + #60827), same timing protocol, one run per arm:

| GB10 | Dense / MoE | Batch 1, s | Batch 32, s | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Kolibri 1, main | DeepGEMM / DeepGEMM | 6.258 | 37.782 | 213 |
| Kolibri 1, this PR | CUTLASS / Triton | 5.567 | 27.063 | 248 |
| Kolibri 1, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` | CUTLASS / Triton | 5.518 | 27.243 | 247 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, main | CUTLASS / DeepGEMM | 5.631 | 32.574 | 411 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, this PR | CUTLASS / Triton | 5.067 | 23.049 | 494 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` | CUTLASS / Triton | 5.012 | 22.601 | 499 |

GSM8K (all 1319 questions; `tests/evals/gsm8k` 5-shot, plus sampled zero-shot chat), paired by question: this PR vs main and vs `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` is unchanged for both models (every 95% CI includes 0). The Qwen3.5 exclusion is still needed: with the list emptied, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B FP8 drops from 79.4% to 71.0% on the 5-shot eval (95% CI −10.5 to −6.2 pt), below its CI threshold of 0.76.

<details>
<summary>Test commands and results</summary>

Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy, passed.

Per-run B200 results (batch 1 / batch 32 s, output tok/s): main 1.257 / 2.184 / 5707 and 1.333 / 2.232 / 5417; excluded 1.491 / 2.417 / 5062 and 1.483 / 2.400 / 4967.

GB10 build: main's Python tree on the aarch64 nightly wheel `0fae39a014` (`0fae39a0..61d9c777` is Python-only), torch 2.13.0, flashinfer-python 0.7.0.post1. Repeat runs of the `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` arms: timing within 2.1% (Kolibri) and 0.6% (Qwen3.5); Kolibri 5-shot outputs identical.

| GSM8K, % | main | this PR | `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` | list emptied |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Kolibri 1, 5-shot | 85.97 | 86.28 | 86.13 | |
| Kolibri 1, chat | 92.68 | 92.97 | 92.70 | |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, 5-shot | 78.92 | 79.91 | 79.42 | 71.04 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, chat | 95.53 | 95.28 | 95.17 | 95.09 |

</details>

## Details

The exclusions only reached the dense DeepGEMM kernel; `select_fp8_moe_backend` checked only the environment variables. On SM12x, block-FP8 MoE has no TRTLLM or FlashInfer CUTLASS backend, so DeepGEMM was selected. With E8M0, `TritonOrDeepGemmExperts` then runs DeepGEMM for every shape, including the N ≤ 512 experts it otherwise leaves to Triton; Kolibri 1 and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B both use 512. On SM100 these models select TRTLLM ahead of DeepGEMM, so only the dense kernel is affected there.

Kolibri's entry is for latency, so the warning no longer cites accuracy. An explicit `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1` still selects DeepGEMM for MoE.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Use AITER tuned configs to select a4w4 gemm kernel instead of env var
body:
## Purpose

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM` is currently used to select the weight layout (preshuffled vs plain) for every layer. With preshuffled layout, ASM gemm is used for prefill and preshuffled Triton gemm for decode. 

In previous PRs, attempted to remove the environment variable altogether and default to on, but caused regressions because various models (Kimi, DS) do not have tuned preshuffled Triton decode kernels. Ideally we would like to have this active for the models that it helps (Llama, mostly) without the environment variable. 

This PR removes the environment variable and decides per layer at weight-load time. A layer takes the preshuffled (ASM) layout only when aiter has tuned configs for both the ASM and Triton preshuffled kernels. 

## Testing

### Unit tests

```
python -m pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py
59 passed
```

### Serving setup

MI350X ×8, fresh server per arm, two restarts per arm. "Before" is `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=0` on main.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve $MODEL -tp $TP --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 16384 --load-format dummy

vllm bench serve --model $MODEL --trust-remote-code --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --max-concurrency $C --num-prompts $((4 * C))
# C = 1 4 8 16 32 64 128 for Llama-3.3-70B (min 8 prompts); C = 1 (8 prompts) and 32 (192 prompts) for the other models
```

### Serving: Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-MXFP4 (change vs. today's default)

Layers on ASM: TP1 4/4 shapes, TP2 1/4 (aiter has no a4w4 tuned rows for the other three), TP4 4/4, TP8 4/4.

| 4 | 1 | 77 → 50 ms (−36%) | −9.8% | −10.0% | +11.1% |
| 4 | 4 | 189 → 137 ms (−28%) | −10.2% | −10.5% | +11.8% |
| 4 | 8 | 353 → 266 ms (−24%) | −10.0% | −10.6% | +11.8% |
| 4 | 16 | 678 → 534 ms (−21%) | +1.9% | +0.2% | −0.2% |

### Serving: other models (TP8, change vs. today's default)

| Model | layers on ASM | c1 TTFT | c1 E2EL | c32 TTFT | c32 E2EL | c32 tok/s | ASM forced for comparison |

title: [Attention][DCP] Support a2a DCP comm backend for FlashMLA sparse
body:
## Purpose

`FlashMLASparseMetadataBuilder` rejects any DCP comm backend other than `ag_rs`. 
The mixed-batch fp8 path already returns `(out, lse)` for every MQA token, with packed heads and with rows that have no local top-k candidates set to `(0, -inf)`. That is the input `MLADCPManager`'s `a2a` combine expects, both the direct symmetric-memory kernel and the NCCL all-to-all fallback for batches larger than the direct workspace. This PR removes the guard.

PCP + DCP still requires `ag_rs`. The MRV2 PCP manager enforces that (`MRV2 PCP + DCP requires dcp_comm_backend='ag_rs'`), and PCP is MRV2-only.

With `ag_rs`, each layer's combine is an NCCL all-gather of the LSEs plus a reduce-scatter of the outputs, which means many small NCCL kernels per decode step. With `a2a` it is one exchange per layer.

There is also a side effect for GLM-5.x: `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` defaults DCP to `a2a`, so with this change it no longer fails at startup when FlashMLA sparse serves DCP (`--attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, or SM90).

## Not a duplicate

Searched open and merged PRs for `dcp a2a flashmla`, `dcp_comm_backend`, `FlashMLA sparse DCP`, `decode context parallel symmetric memory`, `dcp a2a`, `flashmla sparse a2a`:
- #59310 fixes the same startup failure from the other side: it keeps GLM DSA's DCP defaults on `ag_rs` wherever FlashMLA sparse serves DCP. Its description mentions lifting the guard as the alternative but leaves it alone because it was not validated. This PR is that alternative, with validation below. If this PR lands, #59310's Hopper/forced-backend fallback is no longer needed.
- #54472 and #60373 change direct-A2A layout handling (strided output and LSE). FlashMLA sparse already hands the combine packed heads (the fp8 kernel's LSE is token-major; checked on SM100), so this PR does not depend on either one.
- #46514 added the guard. Nothing else touches it.

## Test Plan / Results

Unit tests (GB300):
```
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k dcp     # 7 passed (incl. new test_fp8_dcp_accepts_comm_backend[ag_rs|a2a])
pytest tests/distributed/test_dcp_a2a.py tests/distributed/test_dcp_direct_a2a_lse_reduce.py
# 44 passed, 12 failed -- the same 12 fail on unmodified main (test-side dtype/mock/query_start_loc issues), unrelated to this change
```

Combine precision check (4x GB300, 64 heads, D=512, T=40, rows empty on some ranks set to `(0, -inf)`), measured against an fp32 LSE-weighted reference: the direct a2a combine has max error 0.010-0.013 and mean 0.0009. The ag_rs path (correct_attn_out followed by a bf16 reduce-scatter) has max error 0.026-0.032 and mean 0.0015. No NaNs in either.

End-to-end setup: `zai-org/GLM-5.3` (FP8) on 2x4 GB300, TP8, `--attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 65536 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192`. Default runner (MRV2), FULL_AND_PIECEWISE CUDA graphs. The DCP runs add `--decode-context-parallel-size 8 --no-dcp-q-replicate` and either `--dcp-comm-backend ag_rs` or `--dcp-comm-backend a2a`. The log confirms `Using direct symmetric-memory DCP A2A for MLA.`

GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --max-tokens 512`, 5-shot):

| config | accuracy |
|---|---|
| TP8 | 0.918 |
| TP8 + DCP8 ag_rs | 0.917 |
| TP8 + DCP8 a2a | 0.914 |

Prompt logprobs on 3 fixed texts (115 positions, mean abs diff): a2a vs TP8 0.065, ag_rs vs TP8 0.058. For comparison, TP8 against itself under different concurrent load gives 0.073. Greedy outputs are identical run to run for a given config.

`vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos`, a different seed per point, mean TTFT/TPOT in ms:

| point | TP8 | DCP8 ag_rs | DCP8 a2a | a2a vs ag_rs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prefill 8k, c1 (TTFT) | 541 | 923 | 867 | -6% |
| prefill 32k, c1 (TTFT) | 2193 | 3653 | 3433 | -6% |
| decode 1k/256, c1 (TPOT) | 9.50 | 15.17 | 13.45 | -11% |
| decode 1k/256, c16 (TPOT) | 15.71 | 23.28 | 20.84 | -10% |
| decode 1k/256, c64 (TPOT) | 27.35 | 38.83 | 34.97 | -10% |
| decode 32k/256, c1 (TPOT) | 9.59 | 14.84 | 13.10 | -12% |

DCP8 holds 21.95M KV tokens versus 2.75M for TP8 (8x).

title: [Bugfix] Accept whole-number floats for integer tool arguments in the response parser
body:
When tool schemas are passed to the response parser, an `integer` argument written as a whole-number float like `"3.0"` is now cast to `3` instead of being left as the raw string.

- JSON Schema (draft 6 onward, including 2020-12) defines `integer` as any number with a zero fractional part, so `3.0` is a valid `integer` value. `jsonschema` (Draft 7 and 2020-12 validators) and Pydantic v2 both accept it, and Pydantic returns `3`.
- Models do sometimes write integer arguments this way, and the tool then receives a string where its schema declares an integer.
- Values with a fractional part (`"3.5"`), `inf` and `NaN` still fail the `integer` cast, so they fall through to the next declared type or stay raw, as before.
- Adds a unit test next to the existing argument coercion tests.
- Same change as in Transformers: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49547.
