title: [Rust Frontend] Accept whole-number floats for integer tool arguments
body:
Schema-typed tool arguments in the Rust frontend now accept an `integer` written as a whole-number float like `"3.0"` and convert it to `3`, instead of falling back to the raw string.

- JSON Schema (draft 6 onward, including 2020-12) defines `integer` as any number with a zero fractional part, so `3.0` is a valid `integer` value. `jsonschema` (Draft 7 and 2020-12 validators) and Pydantic v2 both accept it, and Pydantic returns `3`.
- The fallback only applies to schema-driven conversion, so it covers the response-template parser and the other tool parsers that use `ToolSchemas` (`qwen_coder`, `glm_xml`, `minimax_m2`, `minimax_m3`, `deepseek_dsml`, `hy`). The `int` content parser keeps its strict behavior.
- Values with a fractional part (`"3.5"`), non-finite values and floats outside the `i64` range still fail the `integer` conversion, so they fall through to the next declared type or stay raw, as before.
- Matches the Python response parser change in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61297 and the same change in Transformers: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49547.

title: [Model] Add Clef-Flash support
body:
## Overview

Add native support for [Cloudflare/clef-flash](https://huggingface.co/Cloudflare/clef-flash) through `/v1/systemone`, reusing the Qwen3.5 backbone and the joint schema head introduced for Clef-Omni in #61064.

## Claims

- Automatically detect and load the separate joint schema head, scoring `choice`, `noul`, and `score` questions in one pooling request.
- Support text/JSON, images, and videos sampled at 2 fps. Match the release's fixed prompt, media separators, schema spans, and 16K truncation.
- Share the head/pooler between Clef-Flash and Clef-Omni. Flash rejects audio inputs and ignores video soundtracks.

## Validation

Compared the full checkpoint at revision `8b2e5fd17c09fd49bc2880b805d5323ec7ff4ff3` against the release's `joint_schema_model.py` in BF16. Ten model inputs covered invoice decisions, Unicode/empty instructions, a state truncated to 16K, one/two images, video, and image+video. Prompt token IDs and question/option spans matched the reference exactly in all ten cases.

Each mode ran the ten inputs once sequentially and twice at concurrency 4:

| Mode | Requests | Highest-probability option matches | Max absolute probability difference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Eager | 30 | 57/57 | 0.001508 |
| Default compile | 30 | 57/57 | 0.000863 |

The four invoice threshold labels were correct in every repetition (12/12 per mode). These are synthetic model correctness checks. Probability normalization and input-token counts also matched; output-token counts were zero.

The reference evaluation used `encode_record`, `collate_records`, and `load_release_model(..., attn_implementation="sdpa")`, comparing each question's softmax probabilities against `/v1/systemone` responses. Serve the model with:

```bash
vllm serve Cloudflare/clef-flash \
  --served-model-name clef-flash --dtype bfloat16 \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 --max-num-seqs 8
# Add --enforce-eager for the eager comparison.
```

## Details

The checkpoint advertises `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` and supplies `joint_head_config.json` plus `joint_head.safetensors`. Architecture conversion detects that head, and the Flash wrapper uses the output embedding table for lexical option features, matching the reference implementation.

The existing Clef head/pooler is moved unchanged into `clef_joint_schema.py`. Flash shares the joint schema strategy's typed answers and span/truncation logic, with its own media rendering for adjacent placeholders and a single trailing newline.

Duplicate checks found no open Clef-Flash support PR. #61064 supports Clef-Omni; the other open Clef-related PRs concern API/frontend behavior.

Model comparisons cover BF16 with TP=1. Multi-GPU configurations, quantization, and the full Clef checkpoint were not evaluated.

AI assistance (Codex) was used to implement and validate this model support.

title: [Model Loader] Keep norm layers neutral under dummy weight init
body:
## Overview

Keep normalization layers neutral under `--load-format dummy`: `RMSNorm`, `LayerNorm`, `RMSNormGated` and `GemmaRMSNorm` tag their parameters with `dummy_weight_value` (their identity value), so dummy init no longer fills them with ±1e-3. Follow-up to #61134 (dtype-aware dummy init).

## Claims

- Dummy-loaded norms are identity-like (weight 1, bias 0; Gemma's `1 + w` weight 0) instead of random ±1e-3.
- Activations then keep a realistic scale, so data-dependent kernels time like they do with real weights. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill, the sparse indexer's `topKPerRowPrefill` takes 27.8 ms per forward with dummy weights on `main`, 10.7 ms with this PR, and 10.6 ms with real weights.
- Only dummy initialization changes; checkpoint loading is unaffected.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (40 layers), TP4 + EP on 4x GB200, MegaMoE, FlashInfer sparse MLA, MXFP4 indexer cache. One prefill step: 8 requests x 1024 new tokens at ~100K context each. GPU kernel time per forward from a profiled CUDA-graph replay of the model forward (3 replays):

| Weights | `topKPerRowPrefill` (ms/forward) | Forward (ms, median of 100 replays) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dummy, `main` (norms ±1e-3) | 27.84 | 136.0 |
| dummy, this PR | 10.68 | 120.3 |
| real checkpoint | 10.64 | 124.1 |

The remaining forward gap to real weights is MoE routing (real routing from random token IDs vs. a balanced fixture), not this change. All other kernels differ by under 1 ms between this PR and real weights.

These numbers come from an exact-shape forward benchmark that isn't upstream yet; the per-kernel effect can also be seen in an `nsys` profile of any long-context DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill with `--load-format dummy`.

Unit test (in `.buildkite/test_areas/model_executor.yaml`):

```
pytest tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py -q
43 passed
```

`test_dummy_norm_weights_are_neutral` fails on `main` (`RMSNorm` weight stays random) and passes with this PR.

No model evaluation: only `--load-format dummy` values change.

## Details

- **Root cause.** With norm weights in ±1e-3, every normalized sublayer input shrinks by ~1000x and loses structure. DeepSeek-V4.1's indexer query ends up near zero, and after FP8/MXFP4 quantization its logits collapse onto a few values with many exact ties. `topKPerRowPrefill` is a data-dependent radix select, so these degenerate logits are its slow case; real models never produce them.
- **Mechanism.** Reuses the existing `dummy_weight_value` hook in `initialize_single_dummy_weight`, as DeepSeek-V4.1's engram already does for its own weights. Each norm declares the value its constructor already uses.
- **Limitation.** Model-local norm classes that don't build on these four layers keep random dummy values.
- **Behavior change.** Dummy-weight benchmarks of models with data-dependent kernels (sparse top-k, etc.) shift toward their real-weight timings.

title: [Frontend] Let an unset `--tool-strict-level` fall back to the tool parser's default
body:
## Overview

An unset `--tool-strict-level` now falls back to the tool parser's default level, while an explicit value, `auto` included, always wins. Both frontends resolve the level the same way, and the Rust frontend gains the per-parser default that #56403 added on the Python side for `glm47`.

## Claims

- Resolution on both frontends: explicit `--tool-strict-level` > the tool parser's default level > `auto`.
- `--tool-strict-level auto` now overrides a parser default. Before, it could not be told apart from an unset option, so it left GLM-4.7 at `function`.
- Rust: `ToolParser::default_tool_strict_level` / `UnifiedParser::default_tool_strict_level` (default `Auto`; `CombinedParser` forwards its tool parser's), and `glm47` defaults to `Function` like its Python counterpart. Rust `glm47` therefore now constrains non-strict `tool_choice="auto"` requests by default.
- No change when the option is unset, except that Rust `glm47` now follows Python.

## Validation

```bash
cd rust && cargo nextest run -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py tests/parser/test_abstract_parser.py tests/parser/test_harmony.py tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_registry_and_args.py
```

- Rust: 1505 tests pass; Clippy and rustfmt are clean. The new `unset_tool_strict_level_falls_back_to_the_parser_default` covers `glm47` unset/`function`/`auto` and `qwen3_coder` unset; CLI snapshots now show `tool_strict_level: None` when unset.
- Python: the new `test_glm47_default_level_applies_only_when_the_level_is_unset` goes through `ParserManager.get_parser` and fails for both cases without the Python change. Locally, 29 tests in these files fail identically on `main` and on this branch because my environment has xgrammar 0.2.2 instead of the pinned 0.2.8 (missing `mimo` / `deepseek_v4_1` builtins); everything else passes. `tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_cli_args.py` was not runnable in my environment, so CLI parsing was checked directly: unset → `None`, `function`/`auto` parse, unknown values are rejected.
- Render check with `zai-org/GLM-4.7` (engine-free render servers, one non-strict tool), whether the request gets a grammar:

  | Server | `tool_choice="auto"` | `tool_choice="required"` |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `vllm-rs render`, `glm47`, unset | grammar | grammar |
  | `vllm-rs render`, `glm47`, `--tool-strict-level auto` | none | grammar |
  | `vllm-rs render`, `glm47`, `--tool-strict-level function` | grammar | grammar |
  | `vllm-rs render`, `qwen3_coder`, unset | none | grammar |
  | `vllm launch render`, `glm47`, unset | grammar | grammar |
  | `vllm launch render`, `glm47`, `--tool-strict-level auto` | none | grammar |

- Not run: GPU serving or model evaluation. The change only selects which existing grammar a request gets.

## Details

- Python: `FrontendArgs.tool_strict_level` defaults to `None` and is passed through the serving layers as `str | None`. `Parser.tool_strict_level` is `None` when unset, and `_apply_structural_tag` falls back to `ToolParser.default_tool_strict_level`, which is now `AUTO` by default instead of `None`.
- Rust: the CLI and bootstrap JSON arg (`vllm serve` forwards only non-default args, so an unset option arrives absent) are `Option<ToolStrictLevel>`, as are `ChatRequestProcessor`, `NewChatOutputProcessorOptions`, and the server/render configs. `DefaultChatOutputProcessor` resolves the level once the parser is chosen, mirroring the Python fallback.
- At `function`, Rust `glm47` uses the xgrammar `glm_4_7` builtin with broad arguments, while Python uses its shallow argument tag (#56403). That difference predates this PR; this PR only aligns when the level applies.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR touches `--tool-strict-level` resolution or Rust parser default levels (searched open PRs for `tool-strict-level`).

title: [CPU] Fix underflow in FP8 AMX attention
body:
## Overview

Fix underflow in CPU FP8 AMX attention with BF16 exponent lifting and delayed scale compensation, plus cache writes that avoid tiny FP32 intermediates. Follow-up to #39445.

## Claims

- AMX decoding retains FTZ with **four instead of six** vector conversion instructions per 32 values.
- E4M3/E5M2 attention latency: **5.4% lower** than the original decoder across six workloads per format.

## Validation

### Model evaluation

GSM8K results are from earlier decoder comparisons; FTZ rows precede delayed scaling (`da46b8b`).

RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-quantized.w8a8, BF16 compute, all 1,319 GSM8K questions, 5-shot, chat template, seed 42, greedy decoding, maximum 512 generated tokens, batch size 32, prefix caching disabled.

| KV format / decoder | Flexible extract | Strict match |
|---|---:|---:|
| E4M3, original underflow-prone | 77.786% | 73.995% |
| E4M3, exact-subnormal alternative | 83.245% | 81.804% |
| E4M3, FTZ before delayed scaling | 83.017% | 79.757% |
| E5M2, proper-subnormal integer alternative | 80.667% | 78.772% |
| E5M2, FTZ before delayed scaling | 81.804% | 78.999% |

All runs passed sample-count validation; prompt, target, and document hashes match within each comparison.

```bash
MODEL=RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-quantized.w8a8
KV_DTYPE=fp8_e4m3  # Repeat with fp8_e5m2.
MODEL_ARGS="pretrained=$MODEL,dtype=bfloat16,kv_cache_dtype=$KV_DTYPE,seed=42"
MODEL_ARGS+=",max_model_len=4096,max_num_seqs=32,max_num_batched_tokens=8192"
MODEL_ARGS+=",enable_prefix_caching=false,enforce_eager=true,kv_cache_memory_bytes=17179869184"

VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 lm_eval run \
  --model vllm --model_args "$MODEL_ARGS" \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 32 \
  --apply_chat_template --seed 42 \
  --gen_kwargs temperature=0,max_gen_toks=512 \
  --log_samples --output_path "gsm8k_$KV_DTYPE"
```

### Kernel validation and performance

- Full CPU build and pre-commit passed.
- Eight targeted attention regressions passed, covering encoded subnormals, split reduction, and large cache scales.
- 28 attention behavior checks passed, including split/unsplit, sliding window, softcap, ALiBi, sinks, and VEC.
- All 256 byte encodings of each format were checked against the selected conversion contract with FTZ/DAZ enabled and disabled.

Production assembly confirms four vector conversion instructions per 32 values for E4M3/E5M2 at head sizes 128 and 256.

Three balanced rounds; five repetitions of 20 timed calls per workload. Workload medians pool 15 repetitions; ratios are geometric means across six workloads per format.

| Attention comparison | E4M3 | E5M2 | Combined |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| This PR / original underflow-prone decoder | 0.9525 | 0.9402 | 0.9463 |
| This PR / delayed scaling without FTZ | 1.0248 | 1.0019 | 1.0133 |

Combined ratios by round were 0.9570/0.9435/0.9415 versus original and 1.0222/1.0039/1.0043 versus delayed scaling without FTZ. BF16 controls were within 0.2% overall; the small latter gap is subject to timing variation. These are kernel timings, not end-to-end serving speedups.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu uv pip install -e . -v --no-build-isolation

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py \
  -k 'fp8_qk_covers_full_64_token_group or fp8_large_prefill_amx' -q

# Representative large-prefill benchmark.
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/cpu/benchmark_cpu_attn.py \
  --isa amx --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2 \
  --batch-size 1 --q-len-min 512 --q-len-max 512 \
  --kv-len-min 4096 --kv-len-max 4096 \
  --head-size 128 --num-query-heads 32 --num-kv-heads 8 \
  --block-size 128 --num-blocks 32 --iters 20
```

The existing pytest selection above passed one case and skipped one. The additional reproducers and conversion checks were run locally; no new tests or benchmark files are added to CI.

## Details

The old decoder scaled BF16 values by `2^-120`/`2^-112`; AMX flushed small operands/products before the later scale correction could recover them.

Both AMX decoders lift normal values by `2^8`/`2^16`, compensated in K/V scales, and flush encoded FP8 subnormals to zero. NaN/Inf correction is omitted because the cache writer saturates inputs to finite FP8 codes.

Open-PR searches for CPU FP8 attention and AMX underflow found no overlapping fix.

AI assistance was used for implementation, validation, source and assembly review, and drafting.

title: [Benchmark] Add vllm bench forward: exact-shape forward timing
body:
> Commits: *[Benchmark] Add vllm bench forward*, the *model-microbenchmark* agent skill, and *Support DCP*. No changes to the model runner or model code.

## Overview

Add `vllm bench forward`: time the model forward of an **exact** batch (prefill, chunked prefill, prefix hit, decode, spec-decode verify, or any mix), built without the scheduler and run through the real `execute_model`, captured as a one-shot CUDA graph. Works single-GPU and with DP/TP/EP/DCP across nodes via `torchrun`.

```bash
vllm bench forward --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --case decode=64*1@8192 --case prefill=8192 --case mix=4096,32*1@8192
torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward \
  --model ... -dp 4 --enable-expert-parallel --shapes shapes.json
```

## Claims

- Exact shapes: requests are `[N*]Q[@K][c][:D]` (query length, KV length including the query, draft tokens). A prefill's prefix is a prefix-cache hit (SWA bounded replay on DeepSeek-V4.1) unless `c` marks a chunked prefill. Every run checks that the runner built exactly that batch.
- Accurate GPU time: one-shot FULL graph even for prefill (host-side plans are correct by construction, since the graph only replays the batch it captured). Rendezvous and timing events live inside the graph, so rank skew and launch gaps are excluded; each replay is reduced with MAX over ranks; per-replay jitter is reported (sample spread) and flagged above 0.5%.
- Realistic defaults for dummy weights: KV lengths vary +-50% (same on every DP rank, `--kv-len-jitter`); MoE routing is balanced per EP rank (`--routing auto`), replacing the degenerate routing of dummy gates.
- Matches independent references (below).

## Validation

GB200. CLI and unit tests (Benchmarks CLI job runs `tests/benchmarks/`):

```
pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py   # 3 passed
```

Against serving (decode, same model/config, `vllm bench latency` per-step time from 65- vs 1-token runs, FULL decode graph):

| Model | bench forward | serving step | gap (sampler, LM head, step overhead) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B, 32 x 4K context | 3.48 ms | 3.69 ms | 0.21 ms |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (43 layers, 1 GPU), 32 x 4K | 7.94 ms | 8.93 ms | 0.99 ms |

Against a standalone DeepSeek-V4.1 forward harness (recorded Sept 16; same shapes and config: DEP4, MegaMoE, FlashInfer sparse MLA, fp8 KV; ~100K KV, decode):

| batch | harness | bench forward |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 6.39 ms | 6.31 ms |
| 8 | 9.97 ms | 9.85 ms |
| 32 | 15.77 ms | 15.58 ms |
| 128 | 20.07 ms | 19.97 ms |

DCP: Kimi-K3 (9 layers, MLA) TP4 with DCP1 vs DCP4 on decode, chunked prefill and prefix hit: the runner builds the expected batches, DCP4 allocates the scheduler's block count (`block_size * dcp` tokens per block for DCP-sharded specs), and replays are deterministic.

Also run: DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 DEP4 (1 node) and DEP8 (2 nodes, MNNVL), TEP4, prefix hits, verify. Median run-to-run reproducibility within ~0.3%; sample spread mostly 0.01-0.4% (higher on V4.1 DEP prefill, from MegaMoE cross-rank sync and host engram reads).

## Details

- **Flow per case:** build `SchedulerOutput` (disjoint block IDs across KV groups) -> zero the case's KV blocks -> `execute_model` twice: eager warmup (JIT, autotune), then capture/validate/time. For those two steps the bench shadows `runner.prepare_inputs` (to check the batch the runner built) and `model.forward` (to take over the eager model call) with instance attributes, then deletes them; the runner itself is unchanged. Requests are re-added on the second call; `sample_tokens` is never called, so the pending step state is dropped.
- **State restore:** the KV blocks a step writes are snapshotted and restored inside the graph before each replay, so in-place state (e.g. DeepSeek-V4.1's compressor) is identical across replays.
- **KV init:** zeros only for now (`--kv-init zeros`). Random KV was measured within 3% on DeepSeek-V4.1 at ~100K context, so its per-layout model code isn't worth it yet.
- **Routing:** forward hooks on `GateLinear` replace gate logits with a balanced fixture; this covers backends that route from logits, including monolithic FlashInfer TRTLLM (verified on Kimi-K3) and modular (verified on DeepSeek-V4: router top-k equals the fixture). Models that compute top-k themselves (e.g. MegaMoE's fused gate on DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 and Kimi-K3) instead get the fixture's `topk_ids` through a forward pre-hook on any experts module whose `forward` takes `topk_ids`; on DeepSeek-V4.1 DEP4 this matches the earlier model-local override within run-to-run noise (+0.05% to +0.8%). Grouped top-k is rejected; layers the fixture can't reach fail loudly.
- **Model code:** none.
- **Dependencies / limitations:**
  - Dummy-loaded DeepSeek-V4.1 loses MegaMoE shared-expert fusion (fixed by #60096); the bench's dummy loader finalizes early as a temporary workaround (TODO to remove).
  - Data-dependent kernels need realistic activations: #61323 keeps dummy norms neutral (e.g. V4.1 sparse top-k 27.8 ms -> 10.7 ms, real weights 10.6 ms).
  - The batch builder mirrors scheduler semantics (block counts, prefix-hit replay); the unit test and the per-run layout check guard against drift.
  - Model branches on `is_current_stream_capturing()` (e.g. DeepSeek-V4 short-context top-k, V4.1 mHC overlap) make small batches' graph output differ slightly from eager; reported, not asserted.
- **Agent skill:** `.agents/skills/model-microbenchmark` documents usage and pitfalls (dummy-weight artifacts, torch.compile models, timing spread) for agents.
- **Size:** ~1,050 non-test lines, isolated under `vllm/benchmarks/forward/` plus the CLI entry, docs and agent skill.

title: [Tests][Mamba] Wait for accepted counts in fake MTP proposer
body:
## Overview

Fix `test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv1` / `_mrv1_async`, failing on `main` since #61134 on H200 MIG and MI250 (e.g. [main build #94362](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94362#01a1333b-d247-49be-b767-84df48ec72c7)): `ValueError: Mamba state is not equal for key: 576 at index 0`. Test-only change.

## Claims

- The test's fake MTP proposer read `num_accepted_tokens_cpu` before the same-step non-blocking D2H copy finished, so a GPU lagging behind the host fed off-by-one draft tokens. It now waits on `num_accepted_tokens_event` first.
- No runner change: the real proposer uses GPU tensors, and the runner already synchronizes that event in `_prepare_inputs` before reading the CPU counts.

## Validation

The failure does not reproduce on GB200 as-is (fast GPU hides the race), so I injected GPU lag with a `sitecustomize.py` that runs `torch.cuda._sleep(20_000_000)` (~10 ms) at the start of every `GPUModelRunner.execute_model`:

| GB200, `-k test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv1*` | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no injected lag | pass | pass |
| injected GPU lag, sync | **fail** (`key: 576 at index 0`, same as CI) | pass |
| injected GPU lag, async | — | pass |

```bash
pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py -k "test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv1" -s
```

`pre-commit` passes.

## Details

- In `accept_2_1`, the mismatching conv state at token 576 differed only in row 0 (the token carried over from the previous step); rows 1-2, computed in the current step, matched the reference bit-exactly. That row was produced from a wrong draft token: the fake proposer computed its offset from a stale `num_accepted_tokens_cpu` (still the value written before `postprocess_mamba_align_gpu`'s non-blocking D2H landed).
- Why now: before #61134, FP8 dummy weights were ±1e-3 (mostly rounded to 0 in E4M3), so conv states were ~0 regardless of the input token and the comparison passed vacuously. With ±1 FP8 dummy weights the states are meaningful, and slow CI GPUs (16-SM H200 MIG slice, MI250) expose the race. `main` passed this test at c6566bb9f6 and fails from the next build onward; the other commits in that window only touch DSv4.1/ROCm or Intel CI yaml.
- Related but distinct: #51571 (row-ownership race of the same CPU tensor under async scheduling, fixed in the runner by #51599/#53919). This PR touches neither; the test runs a single request and fails without async scheduling too.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR touches `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py`.

title: [Perf] per_token_group_quant_8bit: multiply by reciprocal instead of dividing per element
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Speed up FP8 per-token-group quantization by computing the per-group scale reciprocal once and multiplying, instead of dividing per element. This covers both CUDA group-quant kernels: `per_token_group_quant_8bit` (smem and register-resident schedules) and the fused RMSNorm+group-quant kernel (`layernorm_utils.cuh`), so that all CUDA fp8 group-quant paths share the same reciprocal-multiply numerics. ~1.2-1.3x kernel speedup on GB300 across M=1..32768; ~1-2% e2e TPOT improvement on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 (TP4).

## Claims

- 1.15-1.29x faster `per_token_group_fp8_quant` CUDA kernel on GB300 across M=1..32768 (details below).
- All CUDA fp8 group-quant paths (unfused kernel, fused RMSNorm+quant kernel, Triton fallback, UE8M0 path) now use the same reciprocal-multiply numerics; previously the fused and unfused kernels could disagree by 1 fp8 ulp on ~0.05% of elements.
- ~0.6-2.0% e2e TPOT improvement on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, 8k input / 1k output, at concurrency 1-64.
- Accuracy-neutral: GSM8K / GPQA-Diamond deltas within noise (details below).

## Validation

### Correctness

- `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_per_token_group_quant.py`: 848 passed, including `test_per_token_group_quant_fp8_register_matches_smem` (bitwise register-vs-smem equality; both schedules are changed identically, so the invariant is preserved).
- Scale outputs are bit-identical to main; quantized values can differ by 1 fp8 ulp on ~0.05% of elements (randn data) when a quotient lands within 1 fp32 ulp of an fp8 rounding boundary.

### Microbenchmarks

GB300, K=4096, group=128, bf16 -> fp8e4m3 + fp32 scales. FlashInfer CUPTI with CUDA graph and cold L2; median of interleaved rounds. Both columns are standalone same-toolchain builds (nvcc 13.1) of the register-resident kernel; repro harness: `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_per_token_group_quant.py`.

| M | main (us) | this PR (us) | speedup | achieved BW (this PR) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 2.30 | 1.92 | 1.20x | 6 GB/s |
| 4 | 2.34 | 1.92 | 1.22x | 26 GB/s |
| 16 | 2.56 | 2.14 | 1.20x | 93 GB/s |
| 64 | 2.69 | 2.27 | 1.19x | 350 GB/s |
| 256 | 3.20 | 2.78 | 1.15x | 1.14 TB/s |
| 1024 | 6.14 | 5.02 | 1.22x | 2.53 TB/s |
| 4096 | 15.23 | 12.19 | 1.25x | 4.17 TB/s |
| 16384 | 52.35 | 41.09 | 1.27x | 4.95 TB/s |
| 32768 | 101.25 | 78.34 | 1.29x | 5.19 TB/s |

The kernel is memory-bound (~2 FLOPs/element; TFLOPS is not the meaningful metric here). This PR lifts achieved bandwidth from 4.0 to 5.2 TB/s at M=32768. A flat-index Triton variant we prototyped reaches 6.7 TB/s at M=32768 but loses at small M; modifying the existing CUDA kernel is the lower-risk change.

### E2E perf

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, 8k input / 1k output, vllm bench serve; median TPOT. main (`c077dc663d`) and the branch (`1aca0a263f`) ran sequentially on the same GB300 node:

| Concurrency | main (ms) | this PR (ms) | Change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6.27 | 6.23 | -0.6% |
| 4 | 8.30 | 8.14 | -1.9% |
| 16 | 12.06 | 11.82 | -2.0% |
| 64 | 24.98 | 24.67 | -1.2% |

Request throughput +1.2% at concurrency 64. Note: the e2e delta includes a toolchain effect (branch built from source with local nvcc 13.1; baseline is the nvcc 13.0 wheel, whose stock quant kernel is mis-scheduled -- see Details), so it mildly overstates the pure source-change effect. The same-toolchain kernel numbers above are the honest claim.

### Accuracy

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, identical server flags on the same GB300 node:

| Task | main | this PR | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K flexible-extract (n=1319) | 0.8211 | 0.8112 | -0.99pp |
| GSM8K strict-match (n=1319) | 0.8158 | 0.7991 | -1.67pp |
| GPQA-Diamond (n=198) | 0.8586 | 0.8687 | +1.01pp |

Mixed and within noise (binomial std error ~1.06pp per arm at n=1319), but GSM8K drifts down directionally; consistent with the ~0.05% of elements whose fp8 rounding flips under reciprocal-multiply.

## Details

- Root cause: `div.rn.f32` is a multi-instruction slow sequence, and the kernel issued it once per *element* when one division per *group* suffices. The kernel's own UE8M0 path already uses reciprocal-multiply (a power-of-two scale makes the reciprocal exact); this PR applies the same transform to the fp32-scale path.
- The per-element division was inherited from the SGLang kernel this file was ported from (#21083); the register-resident path (#55330) kept it so the new schedule stayed bit-exact with the smem one. That invariant is a test convenience, not an accuracy requirement, and is preserved by changing both schedules identically.
- Numerics: this is the same rcp-mul numerics class already shipped by this kernel's UE8M0 path, vLLM's Triton fallback (`_per_token_group_quant_fp8`), and SGLang's production quant kernel.
- Scope: no Python/dispatch changes. The file is also hipified into ROCm builds; the change uses only portable float ops, so ROCm gets the same numerics (not separately benchmarked there).
- Related work: #60903 adds a separate Triton row kernel for prefill-sized inputs (large M only); this PR instead speeds up the existing CUDA kernel at all M and is complementary. No open PR duplicates this change.
- Consistency: the fused RMSNorm+group-quant kernel (`layernorm_utils.cuh`, the target of `RMSNormQuantFusionPass` for block-FP8 models, on both CUDA and ROCm via hipify) is switched to the same reciprocal-multiply. Without this, fused and unfused paths diverge by 1 fp8 ulp on ~0.05% of elements (caught by `test_fused_quant_layernorm` and `test_mamba_prefix_cache`). The fused kernel also drops 4 div.rn per vec4. Per-token fp8 keeps exact per-element division for FBGemm parity; int8 paths are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Toolchain note: nvcc 13.0 x sm_100 mis-schedules the stock kernel</summary>

All official artifacts (release pipeline nvcc 13.0.2, Dockerfile CUDA_VERSION=13.0.3) target `... 10.0 ...` (no sm_103). nvcc 13.0 targeting sm_100 mis-schedules this kernel's div.rn slow paths: 864 instructions / 3095 static stall cycles vs 568 / 1655 under nvcc 13.1; the shipped wheel runs the stock kernel at 167.6us vs 101.2us for a 13.1 rebuild at M=32768 (sm_100 SASS loads natively on sm_103; verified with CUDA_DISABLE_PTX_JIT=1). This PR's variant is insensitive to the compiler (78.3us on nvcc 13.0 vs 78.1us on 13.1) because it removes the per-element div.rn entirely. Worth a separate build-toolchain discussion; out of scope here.
</details>

title: [ROCm][DSv4] Require explicit MXFP4 opt-in for MegaMoE shared-expert fusion
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Follow-up to #61004. Fusing DeepSeek-V4's shared expert into AITER MegaMoE requantizes it from FP8 to MXFP4. With this PR, that requires an explicit opt-in through the online quantization API instead of a dedicated env var, and it goes through the shared fused-shared-expert (FSE) helpers.

## Claims

- Removes `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS`. Under `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe`, the existing `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` requests the fusion.
- The shared expert is fused only when it is explicitly requantized to MXFP4:
  ```bash
  VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro --moe-backend aiter_mega_moe ... \
      --quantization-config.targets '{"*shared_experts*": "mxfp4"}'
  ```
  Without that target, a warning is logged and the shared expert stays unfused in checkpoint precision (FP8).
- No model-specific logic:
  - The decision goes through `resolve_layer_fused_shared_expert` / `is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible`, which now take a `moe_backend` argument.
  - The requantization reuses `get_and_maybe_dequant_weights` and the `ONLINE_SHARED_EXPERT_QUANTIZERS` from #55686.
- Kernel, routing and performance are unchanged from #61004.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MI355X, DEP4, `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe`. GSM8K: lm-eval, 5-shot.

| `--quantization-config.targets` | Shared expert | GSM8K (strict) |
|---|---|--:|
| `{"*shared_experts*": "mxfp4"}` | fused, MXFP4 | 0.9469 ± 0.006 |
| none | unfused, FP8 + warning | 0.9545 ± 0.006 |

```
INFO  Quantizing 122 layers of types: ffn.shared_experts.down_proj: 61 (from targets: *shared_experts*, mxfp4); ffn.shared_experts.gate_up_proj: 61 (...)
WARNING  VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS is enabled but cannot be enabled - skipping for this layer: AITER MegaMoE fuses the shared experts only when --quantization-config.targets requantizes them to MXFP4.
```

Unit tests:
- `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_aiter_mega_moe.py` covers `is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible` with the MegaMoE backend.
- `tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py::test_online_mxfp4_shared_expert_rejects_quark_weight_only_mxfp4_fse` keeps Quark weight-only routed experts incompatible with an `mxfp4` shared-expert target.

## Details

- **Activation key.** MegaMoE (a8w4) quantizes every slot's activations to MXFP8 itself. A `"mxfp4"` target cannot express "MXFP4 weights, MXFP8 activations", so for MegaMoE only the weight key is compared. Other backends still compare both keys: Quark weight-only routed experts have no activation key (BF16 activations), which an `mxfp4` target does not match.
- **Why the shared expert is not built with `Mxfp4OnlineLinearMethod`:**
  - `Fp8LinearMethod` has no `dequantize_weight`, so it can't serve as the source for requantization.
  - `AiterMxfp4LinearKernel` pre-shuffles the weights into a layout MegaMoEV2 can't use.

  Instead, the fused shared expert keeps the checkpoint quant config, minus online quantization. MegaMoE then dequantizes it with `get_and_maybe_dequant_weights` and quantizes it with the registered quantizer.
- **Config class.** On CUDA and ROCm, `deepseek_v4_fp8` resolves to the v4.1 `DeepseekV4FP8Config`, so the check accepts both the v4 and v4.1 classes.
- **Breaking:** `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS`, added in #61004 and present in v0.32.0rc0–rc2, is removed without a deprecation period. Setting it afterwards triggers vLLM's "Unknown vLLM environment variable" warning (an error with `--fail-on-environ-validation`), and the shared expert stays unfused in FP8. If preferred, I can keep it as a deprecated no-op with a warning for one release instead.
- **Out of scope:** making MegaMoE a generic MoE backend in the oracle.

title: [Perf] Tune Triton GDN decode tiles on SM100-family GPUs
body:
## Overview

Tune the existing Triton packed GDN decode launch on SM100-family GPUs. Smaller value tiles improve utilization at small batches and reduce per-CTA work with FP32 recurrent state.

## Claims

- **1.34–1.74× faster kernel** at B=1–64 for the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next TP4 layout with FP32 state on GB300; **1.21–1.34×** at B=1/2/4 with BF16 state.
- **1.0–2.2% higher output throughput** in Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 serving, with unchanged full GSM8K and C=8 check scores.
- A 12-line dispatch change; existing kernel math and interfaces are preserved. FlashInfer is benchmarked as a comparison candidate only and is **not integrated by this PR**.

## Validation

### Microbenchmarks

GB300 (152 SMs), BF16 QKV, `(H, HV)=(4, 12)`, `K=V=128`, Q/K normalization enabled. FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. CUPTI kernel time with CUDA graphs and cold L2; medians of seven shuffled rounds, 40 samples per call. Main uses BV32; PR uses the tile selected by the heuristic.

**FlashInfer is an ideal-input comparison:** `gated_delta_rule_decode_pretranspose(backend="flashinfer")` with contiguous Q/K/V prepared outside the timed call. These numbers exclude layout-conversion/copy costs and do not represent an integrated vLLM serving path. The E2E results below compare main against tuned Triton only.

**FP32 recurrent state**

| Batch | Main (µs) | PR (µs) | Speedup | FlashInfer, not integrated (µs) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 5.36 | 3.09 | 1.74× | 4.22 |
| 2 | 5.60 | 3.30 | 1.70× | 4.43 |
| 4 | 6.08 | 3.78 | 1.61× | 4.93 |
| 8 | 7.14 | 5.09 | 1.40× | 5.73 |
| 16 | 8.99 | 6.56 | 1.37× | 7.18 |
| 32 | 15.65 | 11.07 | 1.41× | 11.78 |
| 64 | 24.21 | 18.06 | 1.34× | 19.54 |

**BF16 recurrent state**

| Batch | Main (µs) | PR (µs) | Speedup | FlashInfer, not integrated (µs) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4.00 | 3.10 | 1.29× | 3.36 |
| 2 | 4.19 | 3.12 | 1.34× | 3.36 |
| 4 | 4.38 | 3.62 | 1.21× | 3.71 |
| 8 | 4.85 | 4.85 | 1.00× | 4.11 |
| 16 | 6.05 | 6.05 | 1.00× | 6.08 |
| 32 | 8.19 | 8.19 | 1.00× | 9.09 |
| 64 | 14.14 | 14.14 | 1.00× | 12.72 |

For BF16 state at B≥8, the PR selects unchanged BV32; the main and PR columns therefore use the same measured launch.

Triton output and recurrent state matched the baseline bit-for-bit in these checks. FlashInfer is not bit-identical: output checks used `atol=rtol=1e-3`; FP32-state checks used `atol=rtol=1e-5`, while BF16-state checks required `atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-2` after ten recurrent updates. No FlashInfer model-accuracy claim is made.

<details>
<summary>TP generalization</summary>

GB300, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next local head layouts `(H, HV)`, BF16 activations and FP32 state. Speedup is main / PR kernel time; median of five shuffled rounds with 40 CUPTI samples each. Eager execution and ten recurrent CUDA-graph updates matched bit-for-bit.

| Batch | TP1 (16, 48) | TP2 (8, 24) | TP4 (4, 12) | TP8 (2, 6) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.56× | 1.69× | 1.80× | 1.87× |
| 2 | 1.40× | 1.57× | 1.74× | 1.77× |
| 4 | 1.38× | 1.36× | 1.62× | 1.75× |
| 8 | 1.41× | 1.41× | 1.37× | 1.63× |
| 16 | 1.33× | 1.40× | 1.39× | 1.47× |
| 32 | 1.19× | 1.30× | 1.40× | 1.36× |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Microbenchmark reproduction</summary>

Run from the feature checkout in an installed CUDA development venv with FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 and `cupti-python`. The script loads the baseline kernel from upstream commit `28d679e762`, uses the checkout's PR dispatch, and prepares the FlashInfer inputs before timing. Save as `bench_gdn.py` and run `.venv/bin/python bench_gdn.py`.

```python
import importlib.util
import json
import random
import statistics
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from flashinfer.gdn_decode import gated_delta_rule_decode_pretranspose
from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti
from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops.fused_recurrent import (
    fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode as tuned,
)

BASE = '28d679e762a0b6ed560d767a76ebe02699bf5c46'
FILE = 'vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/fused_recurrent.py'
source = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', f'{BASE}:{FILE}'], text=True)
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / 'baseline.py'
    path.write_text(source)
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        'vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops._gdn_baseline', path
    )
    baseline = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(baseline)

    generator = torch.Generator(device='cuda').manual_seed(1234)
    order_rng = random.Random(1234)
    for state_dtype in [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16]:
        for batch in [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64]:
            mixed = torch.randn(batch, 2560, device='cuda',
                                dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=generator) * .1
            a = torch.randn(batch, 12, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16,
                            generator=generator)
            b = torch.randn(batch, 12, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16,
                            generator=generator)
            al = torch.zeros(12, device='cuda')
            dt = torch.zeros_like(al)
            ids = torch.arange(1, batch + 1, device='cuda', dtype=torch.int32)
            initial = torch.randn(batch + 1, 12, 128, 128, device='cuda',
                                  dtype=state_dtype, generator=generator) * .1
            # FlashInfer ideal case: Q/K/V layout conversion is outside timing.
            q = mixed[:, :512].view(batch, 1, 4, 128).contiguous()
            k = mixed[:, 512:1024].view(batch, 1, 4, 128).contiguous()
            v = mixed[:, 1024:].view(batch, 1, 12, 128).contiguous()
            states = {name: initial.clone() for name in ['main', 'PR', 'FI']}
            outputs = {name: torch.empty(batch, 1, 12, 128, device='cuda',
                                        dtype=torch.bfloat16) for name in states}
            calls = {}
            for name, fn in [('main', baseline.fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode),
                             ('PR', tuned)]:
                calls[name] = lambda fn=fn, name=name: fn(
                    mixed, a, b, al, dt, 128**-.5, states[name], outputs[name], ids, True
                )
            calls['FI'] = lambda: gated_delta_rule_decode_pretranspose(
                q=q, k=k, v=v, state=None, A_log=al, a=a.view(batch, 1, 12),
                dt_bias=dt, b=b.view(batch, 1, 12), scale=128**-.5,
                output=outputs['FI'], use_qk_l2norm=True,
                initial_state=states['FI'], initial_state_indices=ids,
                backend='flashinfer',
            )
            for call in calls.values():
                for _ in range(10):
                    call()
            torch.testing.assert_close(outputs['PR'], outputs['main'], atol=0, rtol=0)
            torch.testing.assert_close(states['PR'], states['main'], atol=0, rtol=0)
            torch.testing.assert_close(outputs['FI'], outputs['main'], atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-3)
            tol = (1e-5, 1e-5) if state_dtype == torch.float32 else (1e-3, 1e-2)
            torch.testing.assert_close(states['FI'], states['main'], atol=tol[0], rtol=tol[1])
            times = {name: [] for name in calls}
            for _ in range(7):
                order = list(calls)
                order_rng.shuffle(order)
                for name in order:
                    states[name].copy_(initial)
                    for _ in range(30):
                        calls[name]()
                    times[name].append(statistics.median(bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(
                        calls[name], dry_run_iters=5, repeat_iters=40,
                        use_cuda_graph=True, cold_l2_cache=True,
                    )) * 1000)
            print(json.dumps(dict(batch=batch, state=str(state_dtype),
                                  us={name: statistics.median(t) for name, t in times.items()})))
```

</details>

### E2E performance

 Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, revision `236dfdf285828023ca3bcd3f37366c58a3469b13`; four GB300s on the same node, TP4 with expert parallelism, MRv2, no speculative decoding, prefix caching disabled, NUMA binding enabled, FP8 main KV and FP8 indexer caches. Model activations are BF16; the checkpoint's default recurrent state is FP32. Both arms use FlashInfer autotuning, `max_num_batched_tokens=32768`, and `max_num_seqs=256`.

Real NVIDIA SPEED-Bench `throughput_8k` prompts, dataset revision `454f88454792dfa3ccfd7ef15fff248efde44cd1`, capped at 8192 raw prompt tokens; 1024 output tokens with `ignore_eos`. Closed-loop concurrency sweep, five warmup requests per point, `max(32, 10 × concurrency)` measured requests, fixed seed 0. One serial sweep per arm. Output tokens/s covers the full benchmark window.

| Concurrency | Baseline output tok/s | Tuned output tok/s | Change | Baseline TTFT P50/P95 (ms) | Tuned TTFT P50/P95 (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 246.1 | 249.5 | +1.4% | 173.1 / 180.2 | 172.6 / 178.6 |
| 2 | 416.7 | 424.9 | +2.0% | 250.5 / 329.4 | 249.3 / 331.4 |
| 4 | 714.7 | 730.4 | +2.2% | 477.5 / 670.1 | 474.4 / 492.1 |
| 8 | 1200.1 | 1217.8 | +1.5% | 586.6 / 878.3 | 586.6 / 876.0 |
| 16 | 1943.3 | 1967.9 | +1.3% | 993.7 / 1651.9 | 985.3 / 1646.6 |

| 64 | 3970.6 | 4014.4 | +1.1% | 3395.5 / 6092.3 | 3361.7 / 6029.8 |

All 1304 measured requests per arm succeeded and produced exactly 1024 output tokens.

### Accuracy

| Configuration | Questions | Baseline flexible / strict | Tuned flexible / strict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| C=1, full test set | 1319 | 97.04% / 97.12% | 97.04% / 97.12% |
| C=8, concurrency check | 64 | 98.44% / 98.44% | 98.44% / 98.44% |

No per-question scores changed. Both arms had zero request errors, null answers, or empty responses. The same two questions hit the output cap in the full run; neither arm truncated at C=8. Generated text was not bit-identical for every question: three responses differed at C=1 and twenty at C=8, without changing their scores.

### Tests

- Focused GPU reference suite: **14 passed on GB300**, covering BV4/BV8/BV32, independent activation/state dtypes, contiguous/strided QKV, and padded/null state slots. Reproduce with `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/fla/test_fused_recurrent_packed_decode.py -q`.
- Wrapper validation: **136 FP16/BF16-activation cases** using this dispatch matched output and updated state bit-for-bit. Broader sweeps covered Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8 head layouts, TP settings, uneven batches, and normalization on/off on GB200 and GB300. 148-SM green contexts covered the occupancy boundary relevant to B200; this is not a physical B200 performance measurement.
- Natural MRv2 graph capture exercised BV4 and BV8 on all four ranks. The existing B200 CI job `kernels-fla-ops-test-b200` runs the updated reference suite.
- Post-rebase changed-file pre-commit passed, including ruff, mypy, and test tethering; `git diff --check` passed.

<summary>Serving, accuracy, and lint reproduction</summary>

## Details

For `K=V=128` on CUDA SM100-family GPUs, select BV4 when `B × HV <= 64`, BV8 otherwise for FP32 recurrent state, and retain BV32 otherwise. Warps and stages stay at 1 and 3. The baseline launches `4 × B × HV` CTAs; BV4 provides eight times as many at small batches. Larger batches with 16-bit state keep BV32 because smaller tiles regressed those workloads in tuning.

The capability query uses the input tensor's device. Existing MRv2 warmup/graph capture compiles the reachable variants; no extra warmup, GPU synchronization, or online autotuning is introduced. Prefill and speculative verification use separate paths.

The serving A/B used baseline `28d679e762` and the PR's GDN module in fresh processes on the same node, with identical diagnostics. GPU validation was collected before rebasing onto `e2ad0ce5f5`; all three patches and the changed GDN source/test files are unchanged. Post-rebase lint passed; no further serving sweep was run.

Duplicate checks found no open PR implementing this SM100-family policy. Related [#54181](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54181) tunes SM120, [#60400](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60400) tunes ROCm, and [#60403](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60403) adds opt-in FlashInfer decode; their hardware/backend scope differs.

title: [Kernel][DSv4.1] Bump FlashMLA to the 2026.09.30 release and its interleaved V4.1 KV cache
body:
# Overview

Bump FlashMLA to vllm-project/FlashMLA@5dceadb (vllm-project/FlashMLA#30), which syncs upstream's 2026.09.30 release (deepseek-ai/FlashMLA#229). Upstream changed the DeepSeek-V4.1 KV cache records to an interleaved layout, so this moves vLLM's V4.1 cache writers and readers to it and aligns the packed DSv4.1 block to the new decode kernels.

## Claims

- vLLM builds against FlashMLA 5dceadb. V4.1 records (528 B MXFP8, 288 B NVFP4) written by vLLM now use the interleaved layout, and FlashMLA's V4.1 decode kernels and vLLM's own gathers read back exactly what the writers stored.
- DeepSeek-V4.1 serves end to end on SM100 with both FlashMLA backends; GSM8K is in the table below.
- KV capacity: a packed DSv4.1 block now has to hold whole rows of both V4.1 records. Relaxing the indexer's DeepGEMM alignment to 256 B (possible since #61149) keeps the loss at 9.5% instead of 24.6% on DSv4.1-Flash with MegaAttention.
- V3.2, V4.0, NVFP4 (V3.2 geometry) and SM90 keep FlashMLA's legacy kernels; their layouts and code paths are unchanged.

## Validation

GB200 (SM100), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (DP4 x TP1 + EP), DeepGEMM mega MoE, MXFP4 indexer cache with sparse logits, DSpark (5 tokens), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 8192`. GSM8K: lm-eval, 1319 problems, 5-shot completions, temperature 0, 1024-token cap, concurrency 32.

| | block (B) | KV memory (GiB/GPU) | GPU KV cache (tokens) | GSM8K strict-match |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| MegaAttention (`nvfp4_ds_mla`), main | 114,688 | 63.81 | 2,307,478 | |
| MegaAttention (`nvfp4_ds_mla`), this PR | 126,720 | 63.69 | 2,084,294 | 92.87% (±0.71) |
| MegaAttention, this PR with the indexer kept at 512 B | 152,064 | 63.81 | 1,740,323 | |
| `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` (`fp8_ds_mla`), this PR | 194,304 | 59.32 | 2,457,007 | 92.87% (±0.71) |
| `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41`, this PR with the indexer kept at 512 B | 202,752 | 59.78 | 2,372,929 | |

The main and 512 B rows ran on the base before #61149; KV memory per GPU differs slightly between the two bases. At equal KV memory, MegaAttention has 9.5% fewer KV tokens than main (24.6% with the indexer at 512 B), and `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` has 4.3% more than with the indexer at 512 B. Every bound KV view had `stride(0)` equal to the block, CUDA graph capture passed, and all 1319 requests succeeded.

Unit tests, with the vendored DeepGEMM on `PYTHONPATH` so the `importorskip("deep_gemm")` cases run:

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py   # 374 passed, 19 skipped (ROCm-only)
pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py   # 47 passed
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py   # 511 passed, 1528 skipped (Hopper-only or other backends)
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_native_next_n.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_tp_row_shard.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py   # 370 passed
```

New and updated tests:
- `test_v41_cache_writers_match_flashmla_decode` (SWA MXFP8, compressed MXFP8, compressed NVFP4): a token written mid-page into a padded block reads back identically through FlashMLA's V4.1 decode and both vLLM gathers.
- `test_sparse_mqa_logits_paged_matches_dense_masked[page_pad=256]`: the paged sparse indexer decode with a page stride that is 256 B- but not 512 B-aligned, as in a packed DSv4.1 block.
- The existing V4.1 record tests now check the interleaved offsets.

DeepGEMM 6ce1c5e's own `test_sparse_mqa_logits` also passes on the vendored build (644/644, including 196 paged cases with 256 B- but not 512 B-aligned page strides).

CI runs FlashMLA's legacy SM90 kernels in the H100 MLA kernel job. It has no SM100 job for the V4.1 records, so that path is validated only by the runs above.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe","enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"enable_adaptive_verification":true}' \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":"VLLM_COMPILE","cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[6,12,18,24,30,36,48,60,72,96,120,144,192,240,288,384,480,576,768,1020,1536,2046,3072,4092,6144,8190]}' \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 8190 --numa-bind
# FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41: same command with "backend":"FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41"

lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,base_url=http://localhost:8123/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs temperature=0,max_gen_toks=1024
```

</details>

## Details

**Layout.** Upstream's V4.1 records used to put a page's data rows first and all its scale rows after. They are now interleaved, so token `i` sits at `i * 528` (512 fp8 values, then 16 UE8M0 scales) or `i * 288` (256 Bof e2m1 pairs, then 32 e4m3 scales). The writers (`fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert`, `rope_quant_insert`, the MXFP8 quantize-and-insert in `cache_utils.py`) and readers (the Triton MXFP8 / NVFP4 gathers and the CuTeDSL dequant gather) only change their offsets. The V4.0 record (584 B, separate scale region) is untouched.

**Block stride.** The new decode kernels gather tokens with TMA as rows of a 2D view over the whole cache, so they require `k_cache.stride(0) % bytes_per_token == 0`. DSv4.1 packs every layer's page (SWA, compressed, indexer, compressor state) into one physical block, so each view's `stride(0)` is the whole block. `DeepseekV4SWACache` therefore takes `packed_block_stride_alignment`, and V4.1 sets it to `lcm(528, compressed record)`: 528 with `fp8_ds_mla`, 3168 with `nvfp4_ds_mla`. The KV cache planner already rounds the block up to the lcm of every spec's `block_stride_alignment`.

**Indexer alignment.** DeepGEMM's paged sparse MQA logits address pages as `base + page * stride` with 16 B loads; since #61149 (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#33) its guard is 256 B instead of 512 B. main still aligned the indexer to 512 B, which with V4.1 records would round the block up to `lcm(512, 528, 288) = 50,688` B (152,064 B, -24.6%). With 256 B it is `lcm(256, 528, 288) = 25,344` B (126,720 B, -9.5%). With V4.1 records the indexer leaves its page alignment out of that lcm, since the SWA spec now carries the record stride; with the V4 record it keeps the 576 B TMA stride in it.

**Compatibility.** The V4.1 KV cache bytes change layout, so V4.1 KV caches transferred or offloaded between builds before and after this PR are not interchangeable. Decode kernel speed is not claimed here; the V4.1 kernels are upstream's.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs for `bump FlashMLA`, `FlashMLA pin`, `flashmla.cmake`, `interleaved KV FlashMLA` and `FlashMLA 5dceadb`; none bumps the FlashMLA pin or changes the V4.1 record layout.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Enqueue the default chain first in CSA/HCA at small batch sizes for DeepSeek-V4
body:
## Overview

#57407 added a `default_first` option to `execute_in_parallel` (`vllm/utils/multi_stream_utils.py`). When it is set, the default-stream chain is enqueued before the aux-stream chains. The aux streams still wait only on `start_event`, which marks the default-stream work before the fork, so they keep overlapping the default chain.

The DeepSeek-V4 ROCm multi-stream paths still enqueue the aux chains first:

- HCA dual-stream, from #56853: the main compressor runs on aux stream 0.
- CSA three-stream, from #51794: the main and indexer compressors run on aux streams 0 and 1.

On the default stream, both paths run fused `wq_a`/`wkv` GEMM → split + norm → `wq_b` → q-norm/RoPE/KV insert. This is the **longest** chain in the fork. Starting it first shortens the tail of the step when the device is underfilled.

Benchmarks show that this is not true for every batch size. Default-first is faster at small token counts and slightly slower once the batch saturates the device. This PR therefore enables `default_first` only when the step has at most `_DEFAULT_FIRST_TOKEN_THRESHOLD = 96` tokens.

### Changes

All changes are in `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/rocm.py`:

- Add the module-level constant `_DEFAULT_FIRST_TOKEN_THRESHOLD = 96`.
- In `DeepseekV4ROCMAiterMLAAttention._prepare_and_attn`, compute `default_first = hidden_states.shape[0] <= _DEFAULT_FIRST_TOKEN_THRESHOLD` and pass it to the HCA and CSA `execute_in_parallel` calls.

```python
default_first = hidden_states.shape[0] <= _DEFAULT_FIRST_TOKEN_THRESHOLD
...
execute_in_parallel(..., enable=True, default_first=default_first)
```

**Notes:**

- **No runtime cost.** On ROCm, the multi-stream path only runs inside CUDA graph capture or with full-cudagraph metadata (`RocmPlatform.enable_multi_stream_overlap`). `hidden_states.shape[0]` is a concrete Python int at capture time, so each capture size bakes in its own launch order.
- **No change to correctness.** Every aux chain only reads `hidden_states` and its own compressor state, both produced before the fork. The join, where the `done_events` are waited on before returning, is unchanged.
- **Scope.** The threshold is a hard-coded constant, not an env var. It only affects the DeepSeek-V4 ROCm attention class, so DeepSeek-V4.1, CUDA, and other models are untouched. DeepSeek-V4-Flash shares this class and is also gated by the threshold.

### Choosing the threshold

The tests ran with MTP and `num_speculative_tokens=2`, so each decode step runs `3 × conc` tokens. With MTP, capture sizes are rounded to multiples of 3, and both 96 and 144 are capture sizes.

| Conc | Tokens / step | TPOT vs. main | Throughput vs. main |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 3 | -7.26% | +7.22% |
| 4 | 12 | -1.26% | +2.99% |
| 16 | 48 | -0.21% | +0.40% |
| 32 | 96 | -0.73% | +0.92% |
| 48 | 144 | +0.65% | -0.49% |
| 64 | 192 | +0.69% | -0.26% |

The sign flips between 96 and 144 tokens. The threshold is set to 96, the last measured point with a gain. The range from 99 to 141 tokens was not measured.

## Claims



## Validation

### Performance

Benchmark with SA InferenceX `8k1k` workload with server launch commands below:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export AITER_LOG_LEVEL=WARNING

vllm serve /shared/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
    --port 8333 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --data-parallel-size 1 \
    --max-model-len 9472 \
    --max-num-seqs 512 \
```

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Restore TP-sharded routed-expert capture for DP=1
body:
## Overview

Restore complete routed-expert rows when model-level sequence parallelism shards tokens across TP ranks and DP=1 has no DP metadata. Related platform-specific work: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18502.

## Claims

- Identify TP shards using the existing `BatchDescriptor.num_tokens` (or `DPMetadata` for multi-DP), gather in rank order, and trim SP padding.
- Reuse the descriptor in eager, graph, microbatch and decoder-replay contexts; no extra `ForwardContext.num_tokens` field or count-only caller arguments.
- Preserve multi-DP layout priority and reject malformed shard grouping explicitly, including under optimized Python.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py
pre-commit run --files tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py vllm/forward_context.py vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts_capturer.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model_state.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/ubatch_utils.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu_ubatch_wrapper.py
git diff --check
```

- **62 pytest cases passed** on GB200, using isolated test-root collection (`--confcutdir`) against a nightly-image overlay. Includes real `sp_padding_mask` mutation and compact V4.1 replay contexts. A mask-length implementation fails both new TP-rank regressions.
- Real NCCL/CUDA-graph layout checks passed for **TP2/DP1, TP4/DP1 and TP2/DP2**: 36 cases per rank, including odd/empty counts, unequal DP counts and buffer reuse.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks (including mypy and test tethering) and diff checks passed.
- Final helper cleanup: **51 capture tests passed** locally, with **30 targeted cases** rerun during review. **89,469 CPU layout cases** compared the previous and simplified production helper in both normal and optimized Python: identical rows, strides, exception types and collective calls. Collective outputs were simulated in this differential check; the GPU/model results below precede this cleanup.
- Historical CPU checks: 25 isolated capture cases (also 25 under `optimize=1`) and 96,203 multi-DP differential cases passed. Earlier model reproducer and commands: [discussion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61388#issuecomment-6148311175).

### Real-weight DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash A/B

Control: `fe18b045fd`; candidate: this descriptor simplification. GB200, TP2/DP1/EP, `deep_gemm_mega_moe`, default padding skipping, async scheduling, prefix caching, chunked prefill, SHM/value delivery. Both eager and `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` were exercised.

- Five model runs, including a control reload: **41,315 returned rows / 9,915,600 expert IDs**, with no missing or mismatched IDs. Compare raw per-rank routes to capture snapshots and HTTP outputs; prefix hits use the existing first-published immutable Store values. Multi-chunk prefill, decode, a measured cache hit and actual graph replays were verified.
- Fixed-token scoring: three sequences (33/257/1025 tokens), three uncached repeats each. Short-sequence logprobs were exactly equal. The long sequence varies even across control runs: same-GPU control/candidate mean absolute logprob difference **0.05360**, versus **0.05179** between control initializations. Mean NLL shift was **0.00174**, versus control-reload shift **0.00459**. No clear additional degradation in these bounded checks; **not** a claim of bitwise equivalence or broad benchmark accuracy. R3-disabled serving smoke checks also passed.
- **DBO is not fixed:** real V2 UBatchRunner/TP collectives/graph checks reproduce the same existing microbatch overwrite in both variants. V4.1 Engram itself rejects DBO, so these are separate checks, not a claimed V4.1+DBO model pass. Offset repair remains outside this PR (#57184).

Environment: official nightly `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:a7deff2c216def98c193352aca50fb03a2ee29231355b3033dc3789009f6d23e`, V4.1 snapshot `2cba9e42aa026125f3ed06c6d98c1db82f7ca027`. Only the affected production Python files were overlaid per variant; **not a full checkout rebuild**. Model runs used `--max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --max-num-seqs 16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`, concurrent prompt lengths 33/1024/2051/4096 and 8 output tokens, then repeated the 1024-token prefix. `VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip` bypassed an existing image warmup API mismatch; normal JIT and graph capture still ran. Correctness instrumentation makes these runs unsuitable for throughput claims.

## Details

The previous DP=1 path wrote only the received TP shard, leaving later routing rows stale. Restore the local token axis before buffer assignment. Layer bounds are checked before collectives and gather inputs are contiguous.

The pre-SP count must survive model-level sharding: `is_padding` can itself become a TP shard and is not a reliable count source. The existing batch descriptor retains the original size, including in compact decoder-replay contexts. Creating that descriptor for eager execution removes duplicate state and three count-only caller edits (production diff for this refinement: net -11 lines).

This updates the existing TP fix rather than opening a duplicate. Microbatch write offsets (#57184) and decoder-replay row retention (#61643) remain separate concerns, unchanged here. The restoration helper shares one layout error, reads the declared `DPMetadata.local_sizes` field directly, and retains the existing layout priority. Tests use actual `DPMetadata` objects.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review and validation.

title: [Chore] Use upstream Transformers DeepseekV4Config
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Split from #60823: deletes the vendored `DeepseekV4Config` and ports the DeepSeek-V4 code to the upstream Transformers 5.16.1 schema. Also updates the `transformers-upgrade` skill.

Related PRs:
- **#60823:** the larger unvendoring PR this is split from; DeepSeek-V4 has been dropped from it.
- **#43443:** patches one reader of the popped `compress_ratios` (`attention.py`). This PR covers every reader, so it supersedes #43443.

## Claims

- Deletes `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/deepseek_v4.py`. Upstream folds `compress_ratios` and `num_hash_layers` into `layer_types` / `compress_rates` / `mlp_layer_types`:
  - V4-only code (attention, decoder, CPU/XPU/NVIDIA MoE, the C4/C128 CuTe DSL kernels) reads the upstream fields directly.
  - Code that also sees DeepSeek-V4.1 configs (the shared MLA backends, `mla_attention`, the arch convertor, the spec-decode proposer and the warmup kernels) uses `get_compress_ratios`. That helper returns V4.1's legacy field, or derives it from the upstream fields with the MTP layers appended. V4.1 can't move to the upstream schema: it uses compress ratios 1 and 2, which have no upstream layer type.
- `mm_prefix_span_leading_pad_modulus` moves from the config onto `DeepseekV4ForConditionalGeneration`, where the model runner already looks for it. The sparse-SWA image-span widening is now keyed on an upstream `DeepseekV4Config` with `vision_n_layers > 0`, matching what the vendored config set.
- `is_rope_parameters_nested` accepts V4's `{"main", "compress"}` rope layout.
- No numerics change for DeepSeek-V4-Flash: greedy outputs are bit-identical to `main`, and GSM8k, GPQA Diamond and MTP acceptance match.
- **`transformers-upgrade` skill:**
  - Models in `vllm/models/` must run GSM8k and GPQA Diamond against `main`, and these evals should disable FlashInfer autotuning.
  - Adds two hazards: undeclared fields with no default, and top-level configs that no longer forward reads to `text_config`.
  - Adds a re-grep for old field names after rebasing.
  - Drops the PR and issue numbers from the skill.

## Validation

`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` on 8x B200, `main` (`bc3ddb198a`) on GPUs 0-3 vs this branch on GPUs 4-7, TP4 each, `transformers` 5.19.0.

| Check | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8k, 5-shot, 1319 questions, autotune off | 0.944, 0.944 | 0.937, 0.947 |
| GSM8k with MTP (1 token), autotune off | 0.947 | 0.946 |
| MTP draft acceptance | 95.5% (57174 / 59896) | 95.4% (57041 / 59771) |
| GSM8k with MTP, rerun on 84f38ff455 | 0.948 | 0.949 |
| MTP draft acceptance, rerun on 84f38ff455 | 95.4% (57236 / 59977) | 95.5% (57494 / 60209) |
| GPQA Diamond, 8 repeats, reasoning effort high | 0.538 | 0.534 |
| Greedy decode, 4 short prompts x 64 tokens, autotune off | | bit-identical logprobs |

FlashInfer re-tunes its FP4 MoE tactics on every server start, even when given a cache. With autotuning on, the two servers picked different tactics and GSM8k drifted by about 1 point (0.947-0.951 vs 0.939-0.941). With `--kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": false}'` greedy outputs match exactly, so the drift is tactic selection, not this change.

Config dumps for Flash, Flash-Vision-Exp and Pro, using the skill's scripts: `get_compress_ratios`, the per-layer upstream reads, the hash-layer count and the C4/C128 kernel flags all reproduce each checkpoint's legacy values exactly; the mm-prefix clamp is on only for Vision-Exp, as before; and the DeepSeek-V4 RoPE `cos_sin_cache` is bit-identical for sliding, CSA and HCA layers. Vision-Exp and Pro were not served (not enough disk on the host); Vision-Exp's `config.json` sets every `vision_*` field the processor reads.

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-model-len 65536 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": false}' \
  [--speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}']
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port <port> --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 512
OPENAI_API_KEY=EMPTY python tests/evals/gpt_oss/run_gpqa_eval.py --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --reasoning-effort high --base-url http://localhost:<port>/v1 --n-threads 128 --max-output-tokens 32768
```

```bash
pytest tests/transformers_utils tests/config tests/tokenizers_ \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_deepseek_v4_vl.py \
  "tests/test_config.py::test_draft_inherits_ep_only_for_moe"
# main: 1 failed, 1137 passed; this PR: 1 failed, 1139 passed

```

title: [ROCm][CI] Drop the -inf padding check from the AITER MQA logits test
body:
## Purpose
`test_unpaged_mqa_logits_preserves_intervals_and_scale_layout` fails on MI355 in `(MI355 DPX) Attention Kernels Shard 1` for both scale layouts:
```text
FAILED test_unpaged_mqa_logits_preserves_intervals_and_scale_layout[vector]
FAILED test_unpaged_mqa_logits_preserves_intervals_and_scale_layout[column]
>       assert torch.equal(torch.isneginf(actual), ~valid)
E       AssertionError: assert False
```
Failing run: <https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14534/list?jid=01a1347e-aad0-4a29-9623-d798e9c54fad&tab=output>

#58724 added the test while `rocm_fp8_mqa_logits` used AITER's default `clean_logits=True`, which fills positions outside `[start, end)` with `-inf`. #51314 switched the dispatch to `clean_logits=False`, so those positions are now unspecified.

This PR removes the `-inf` padding assertion. The top-k consumers only read the ragged interval, so the test now compares just the values inside it. The AITER dispatch and scale-layout checks are unchanged. No production code changes.

## Test Plan
MI355X (gfx950):
```bash
cd tests
pytest -v -s kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py
```

## Test Result
Before:
```text
FAILED kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py::test_unpaged_mqa_logits_preserves_intervals_and_scale_layout[vector] - AssertionError: assert False
FAILED kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py::test_unpaged_mqa_logits_preserves_intervals_and_scale_layout[column] - AssertionError: assert False
```
After:
```text
129 passed
```

title: [Perf] Share Triton JIT warmup compilation pool across registered kernels
body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #58582. Eligible Triton kernels now share one `AsyncCompileMode` pool during startup warmup, instead of each kernel draining its own pool in turn.

## Claims

- Compilation now overlaps across kernels, not just within one kernel. Single-key kernels previously always compiled serially.
- 9–12% faster cold JIT warmup at default threads, 23–28% at 16 threads, when several Triton warmup kernels are registered (MRV1 sampler/spec-decode kernels, DSv4, GLM-5 Next).
- No change for ROCm, autotuned kernels, non-Triton owners, or configs with a single registered kernel.

## Validation

`pytest tests/model_executor/test_jit_warmup_triton_launcher.py`: 15 passed. The updated test (two single-key kernels must compile concurrently) fails on the base commit.

Cold-cache `JIT kernel warmup finished in …s` on H100, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, mean of 3 runs per arm:

| Config | Threads | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gemma 4 31B + EAGLE3, TP=8 (12 kernels) | 4 | 20.72s | 18.86s (−9%) |
| | 16 | 15.25s | 11.69s (−23%) |
| Qwen3-0.6B-FP8 + ngram (9 kernels) | 4 | 17.99s | 15.89s (−12%) |
| | 16 | 11.55s | 8.37s (−28%) |

Gemma 4 on default MRV2 registers only the FA4 kernel, so there's nothing to overlap: 5.74s → 5.73s. No model evals: only compile scheduling changes, not the compiled kernels.

<details>
<summary>Repro</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 VLLM_TRITON_JIT_WARMUP_NUM_THREADS=16 \
TRITON_CACHE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=$(mktemp -d) python -c "
from vllm import LLM
LLM('google/gemma-4-31b-it', tensor_parallel_size=8, max_model_len=8192,
    kernel_config={'enable_flashinfer_autotune': False},
    speculative_config={'method': 'eagle3', 'num_speculative_tokens': 3,
                        'model': 'RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-speculator.eagle3'})
" 2>&1 | grep 'JIT kernel warmup finished'
```

</details>

## Details

`JitWarmupRegistry.warmup()` runs all kernels with `supports_parallel_compile` inside one `compile_triton_warmup()` pool, then the rest serially. A ContextVar stops `compile_many` from nesting pools; called directly, it still creates its own pool. Dispatch stays on the calling thread, as in #58582.

Limitations:
- The tqdm bar advances on dispatch, so it jumps ahead and then waits for the pool to drain.
- Compile errors surface when the shared pool exits, not inside the failing kernel's `compile_many`.

Not a duplicate: no open PR shares a pool across kernels. #56154 (compile-key derivation) and #56761 (TileLang) are the closest.

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Skip bonus-logit reduction for short drafts in rejection sampling
body:
## Overview



Identify the bonus logit in the V2 rejection sampler by request boundary rather than `local_pos >= num_speculative_steps`, so the full-vocab reductions are skipped on the bonus row of requests verified with fewer drafts than `num_speculative_steps`.
Follow-up to #60945.

## Claims



- A bonus logit helper `_is_bonus_logit` is added. The bounds check introduced by #60945 is now part of `_is_bonus_logit`, and `num_speculative_steps` triton kernel arg is replaced with `num_logits`.
- `_compute_local_logits_stats_kernel` and `_compute_local_residual_mass_kernel` no longer run full-vocab max/sum-exp (target and draft) or residual-mass reductions on the bonus row of a request with `num_drafts < num_speculative_steps`. Previously that work was done and never read.

## Validation



**bonus oracle unit test**

```shell
python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py -k adaptive_draft_lengths -v

# To run OOB detection, wrap with compute-sanitizer
PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1 compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py -k adaptive_draft_lengths -x
```

```text
==================================================================================== 4 passed, 59 deselected, 14 warnings in 8.40s =====================================================================================
```

(if reverted to pre-#60945, the test result above is the same `Invalid __global__ read of size 4 bytes` error at `_compute_local_residual_mass_kernel`)

**Speed boost benchmark**

H100, vocab size 151936, K=7, median of 500 repetitions.

| type | requests | logits | block_verify | main (us) | this PR (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| full | 64 | 512 | False | 218.7 | 220.6 | 0.99x |
| full | 64 | 512 | True | 342.7 | 341.9 | 1.00x |

## Details



The added test is an adaptation from the removed unit test in #60945. If the OOB detector is too verbose, can be remove here as well.

title: [Qwen4Exp] Clean up HC and PLE implementations for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
body:
## Overview

Clean up Qwen4Exp HC/PLE implementations and refine PLE quantization selection, with regression coverage for the affected paths.

## Claims

- **Remove redundant custom-op registrations,** dispatcher wrappers, and fake implementations for NVIDIA HC operations and the shared PLE gate. Call the existing Triton kernel launch functions directly.
- **Move checkpoint shard overlap and copy helpers** into `PLEVocabParallelEmbedding`, using the embedding's own TP shard metadata.
- **Rename HC** `lora_rank` to `hc_lowrank` and local `lora` **variables** to `lowrank` on NVIDIA and AMD. **Use clearer names** for token counts and tensor dimensions in HC and PLE launch functions.
- **Reuse `round_up`** for PLE vocabulary padding, QSA RoPE-position alignment, QSA ring capacity, and prefill logits alignment.
- **Refine PLE quantization selection**: honor ModelOpt layer exclusions, retain serialized FP8 support, **warn and fall back to unquantized PLE for unsupported global configurations**, and reject unsupported explicit ModelOpt per-layer algorithms, embedding dtype overrides, and nonserialized `Fp8Config` usage.

## Validation

**Correctness tests:**

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_hc_ops.py -q
```

Result: **123 passed, 2 skipped**. The skipped cases require ROCm. Coverage includes HC and PLE kernel correctness, checkpoint shard loading, FP8 handling, pinned-host lookup and prefetch, and quantization selection.

**Static checks:** Ruff lint and formatting checks passed for all 12 changed files. `git diff --check` also passed.

**Serving smoke validation:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next started and served HTTP 200 requests with BF16, TP2/DP1, CPU-offloaded PLE, and MTP with 3 speculative tokens. The run recorded nonzero MTP acceptance.

**CI coverage:** Existing CPU CI covers PLE quantization selection and shard-loading tests. The H200 job covers HC operations and PLE convolution correctness.

End-to-end model accuracy evaluations and before/after performance benchmarks were not run. ROCm hardware execution and quantized-checkpoint serving validation remain pending.

## Details

The unquantized PLE fallback assumes the checkpoint contains an unquantized embedding table. NVFP4 PLE decoding and format conversion remain outside this change.
