title: [Core][Spec Decode] Replace EAGLE group heuristics with explicit draft-layer tags
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`is_eagle_group` decides which KV cache groups take the EAGLE last-block drop. The planner used to guess these groups from `non_causal_multi_token_decode` and from "the group holding the last registered layer" (MTP, DeepSeek-V4), and only on some grouping paths. This PR replaces the guesses with an explicit per-layer tag that the runners report, so a group is flagged iff it holds a draft layer. Supersedes #41640 (closed; its compared per-model field changed grouping) and #56026 (adds another guessing rule).

## Claims

- DFlash / DSpark drafters on hybrid models no longer make every group take the drop, so Mamba groups keep their prefix-cache reuse (#57032, #54360).
- A drafter spanning several groups (e.g. DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 DSpark) gets every one of its groups flagged, not only the group holding the last layer.
- Gemma4 MTP no longer flags an unrelated target group. Its drafter shares the target's KV, so no group holds draft-owned KV and the coordinator's existing "flag all" fallback applies.
- The flags survive pipeline parallelism. Before, the scheduler config (worker 0's projection) cleared the flag of every group with no layers on worker 0, so with PP >= 2 the draft groups on the last stage were never flagged and the coordinator flagged every group.
- New draft models need no planner code to be identified. Out-of-tree runners must tag draft specs to benefit; untagged runners keep the conservative "flag all" fallback.

## Validation

Unit tests (CPU; the only failures need a GPU and fail the same way without this PR):

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py
```

`test_mtp.py` and `test_attn_utils.py` also pass in full on one GB200 (84 passed). `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit` gives identical results with and without this PR (1843 passed, 10 skipped; the same 97 GPU-only failures on CPU).

`test_eagle_groups_are_the_groups_holding_draft_layers` checks, through `get_kv_cache_configs` and `generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config`, that the scheduler flags exactly the groups holding draft layers for a uniform model, a Qwen3.5-like GDN hybrid with MTP, and an MLA + SWA-MLA drafter spanning two groups, with pp=1 and pp=2. Reverting the PP projection fix makes the pp=2 case fail.

End-to-end, Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B with `{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}`, prefix caching on, one GB200, main (`ae8f41238c`) vs this PR. The workload is 8 prompts sharing a ~2.2k-token prefix, sent in two waves, greedy, 128 output tokens:

| Metric | main | PR | PR repeat |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prefix hit rate, wave 1 / wave 2 | 0.4409 / 0.5039 | 0.4409 / 0.5039 | 0.4409 / 0.5039 |
| Mean acceptance length | 3.3065 | 3.3065 | 3.3065 |
| Wave-2 outputs equal wave-1 outputs | yes | yes | yes |
| GSM8K-250 flexible-extract | 0.760 | 0.764 | 0.752 |

The GSM8K delta (1/250) is below the PR repeat spread (3/250). Commands: `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 8192 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, then `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --limit 250 --gen_kwargs temperature=0.0`.

The DFlash-on-hybrid case could not be run end to end: the local Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B DFlash2 draft sets `sample_from_anchor: true`, which DFlash rejects at startup on main and on this PR alike.

## Details

- Speculators set `AttentionLayerBase.is_draft_layer` on their layers at load time (V2 already did; V1 now does too). Both runners copy it onto `KVCacheSpec.is_draft`.
- `KVCacheSpec.is_draft` describes ownership, not cache format, so it uses `compare=False`: it never changes equality, hashing, grouping, or the cross-worker spec check. The `merge` assertions skip `compare=False` fields, because a group can mix target and draft layers (Qwen3.5 MTP). The field is only meaningful on per-layer specs; groups expose `KVCacheGroupSpec.is_eagle_group`.
- `get_kv_cache_configs` sets `is_eagle_group` after `get_kv_cache_groups_from_builder`, so it also covers groupings from a model's `SupportsKVCacheGrouping` or a platform builder. Flags are only set when `use_eagle_block_drop()` is true.
- `_project_kv_cache_groups_to_worker` now keeps the global flag. Every `is_eagle_group` consumer (coordinator, OffloadingConnector scheduler, Mooncake store coordinator) runs on the scheduler side.
- Behavior change: on uniform models the OffloadingConnector now drops the tail chunk like the GPU coordinator. Newly flagged groups recompute one tail chunk on external hits; this is a performance cost, not a correctness one.
- HiSparse resident/hot specs are not tagged; their groups are not prefix-cacheable, so no hit lookup reads the flag.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Capture DCP FULL cudagraphs with KV context
body:
## Overview

On MRV2, GQA models with DCP produce garbage under the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` cudagraph mode, including the Qwen3-235B `-tp 8 -dcp 2` example in `docs/serving/context_parallel_deployment.md`. This PR captures DCP FULL graphs with KV context, as V1 already does (`get_dcp_dummy_context_len`).

## Claims

- Fixes GQA + DCP + FULL cudagraphs on MRV2. Qwen3-235B at TP=8 DCP=2: needle retrieval 0/9 → 9/9.
- No regression for MLA + DCP (DeepSeek-V2-Lite).

## Validation

8x H100, `main` @ de8291e24f, default settings. Needle: 6-digit code at depths 0.1/0.5/0.9 of ~8k/~31k/~100k-token prompts, greedy. gsm8k: 5-shot, chat template.

| Model | Build | Needle | gsm8k flex / strict | KV tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8, TP=8 DCP=2 | `main` | **0/9** | garbage | 1,851,136 |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8, TP=8 DCP=2 | this PR | **9/9** | 91.66 / 80.74 | 1,846,080 |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8, TP=8 DCP=1 | this PR | 9/9 | 92.80 / 81.50 | 925,920 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B, TP=4 DCP=2 | `main` | **0/6** | | |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B, TP=4 DCP=2 | `main`, PIECEWISE | 6/6 | | |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B, TP=4 DCP=2 | this PR | 6/6 | | |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite (MLA), TP=4 DCP=4 | `main` | 6/6 | 53.83 | 8,634,624 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite (MLA), TP=4 DCP=4 | this PR | 6/6 | 54.89 | 8,634,624 |

gsm8k stderr is ±0.7–1.1 (Qwen3) and ±1.4 (DeepSeek).

Zero-context batches (64 concurrent one-token prompts after a long request, FA3): first-token logprobs at DCP=2 match DCP=1 exactly (64/64).

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-FP8 -tp 8 -dcp 2 --max-model-len 131072
pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py  # new test fails on main
```

## Details

**Root cause.** For DCP, the FlashAttention metadata builder skips context attention on the host when no request has context (`should_skip_dcp_context_attention`, #40996). MRV2 captures FULL graphs from a dummy batch with `seq_lens == query_lens`, so every FULL graph records the skip path and replays ignore the KV cache. Piecewise and eager rebuild metadata each step and are unaffected.

**Fix.** On FULL capture with `cp_size > 1`, give the dummy batch `cp_size * cp_interleave` tokens of context through the existing `set_dummy_context`. Applied on both FULL capture paths, normal and DBO. Capture-time only.

**Limitations.**
- The FA2 decode/prefill split (`should_split_fa2_dcp_context_attention`) is still decided at capture; unchanged by this PR.
- `set_dummy_context` clamps context to `max_model_len - max_query_len`, so a capture size within `cp_size * cp_interleave` of `max_model_len` still gets zero context.
- The DBO path is not tested end-to-end (needs DeepEP).

**Alternative.** Forcing `skip_dcp_context_attention=False` in the FlashAttention builder during capture. The runner-side fix matches V1 and is backend-agnostic.

No existing PR or issue covers this; nearest are #59951 and #54300 (different code paths).

title: [Frontend] Accept `--reasoning-parser none` as the unset default
body:
## Overview

`vllm serve --reasoning-parser none` (any case) now disables reasoning parsing instead of raising `KeyError`, matching `vllm-rs serve --reasoning-parser none`. Follows the per-launcher parser semantics from #46359.

## Claims

- `--reasoning-parser none` / `None` / `NONE` parses to the unset default (`""`) on every Python entrypoint, instead of failing at engine config with `KeyError: "Reasoning parser 'none' not found. Available parsers: ..."`.
- Under `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, the normalized value is the argparse default, so it is not forwarded to the bootstrapped Rust frontend, which keeps its `none` default (#46359).
- Named parsers are unchanged.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_cli_args.py`: 64 passed. The new parametrized test fails on `main` with `assert 'none' == ''` for each `none` spelling.
- CLI → engine config → Rust bootstrap, through the real `make_arg_parser`:

  | `--reasoning-parser` | `EngineArgs` | `StructuredOutputsConfig` | forwarded to Rust frontend |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `none` | `''` | `''` | not forwarded (Rust keeps `none`) |
  | `NONE` | `''` | `''` | not forwarded |
  | `deepseek_v41` | `deepseek_v41` | `deepseek_v41` | `deepseek_v41` |

- `pre-commit run --files <changed>`: all hooks pass, including mypy for the oldest supported Python.
- End-to-end `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --enforce-eager --max-model-len 4096` on one RTX 6000 Ada. This used the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-21d93d0d8c0e9627900020382bfce4730e61cab7` image (`0.30.1rc1.dev709`), with this diff applied in the container via `patch -p1`. Each running server got one chat request, `"What is 2+3? Answer in one word."`, at temperature 0:

  | Launcher | `--reasoning-parser` | Before | After | Response (after) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve` | `none` | `KeyError: "Reasoning parser 'none' not found..."` | serves; Rust frontend logs `reasoning parsing disabled` | no reasoning field; `<think>...</think>` stays in `content` |
  | `vllm serve` | `None` | `KeyError: "Reasoning parser 'None' not found..."` | serves | no reasoning field; `<think>...</think>` stays in `content` |
  | `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve` (control) | `qwen3` | serves | serves | reasoning split out (624 chars); `content` is `five` |

## Details

**Root cause.** The Rust frontend's `ParserSelection` accepts `auto | none | <name>`, case-insensitively. `vllm-rs serve` defaults to `auto`, and `none` is the only way to turn parsing off. Python's `--reasoning-parser` is a plain string that `ReasoningParserManager` looks up by exact name, so Python has no way to spell "disabled" other than omitting the flag. A launcher that starts some workers with `vllm-rs serve` and others with Python `vllm serve` therefore cannot share one setting that disables the parser. Multi-node hybrid-DP currently has to go through the Python-supervised Rust frontend. We hit this in Dynamo + vLLM disaggregated deployments, which need vLLM's own reasoning parser off: single-node prefill (`vllm-rs serve`) required `none`, while multi-node decode (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve`) crashed on it.

**Design.** Normalization happens in the `--reasoning-parser` argparse `type`. That single point covers `EngineArgs`, `StructuredOutputsConfig`, `ReasoningConfig`, entrypoints that read `args.reasoning_parser` directly, and the Rust bootstrap, which only forwards non-default args.

**Limitations.**
- `none` means "unset", so model defaults for an unset parser still apply (gpt-oss → `openai_gptoss`). That is what the engine already receives under `vllm-rs serve --reasoning-parser none`, which forwards no parser to Python.
- `--structured-outputs-config '{"reasoning_parser": "none"}'` and programmatic `EngineArgs(reasoning_parser="none")` are not normalized.
- `auto` stays unsupported in Python. Supporting it would mean Python resolving parsers from model IDs, which only Rust does today.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open vLLM PRs and issues for `reasoning-parser none` and `reasoning parser none` / Rust frontend; none address CLI parsing of `none`.

title: [MoE] Unify DeepGEMM MegaMoE experts behind one feature-matrix layer; add NVFP4
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Folds the three DeepGEMM MegaMoE expert implementations into one `DeepGemmMegaMoEExperts` layer. The three are DeepSeek V4/V4.1's `DeepseekV4MegaMoEExperts`, Kimi K3's `KimiK3MegaMoEExperts`, and the `DeepGemmMegaMoEBackend` pair under both. The new layer is driven by a feature matrix: routed precision × activation × fusable shared-expert precision. The PR also adds NVFP4 routed experts (DeepGEMM `nvfp4_mega_moe`) as a new row. It keeps the procedure from #60096: weights load straight into the DeepGEMM layout, with no post-load transform.

**Draft:** the end-to-end eval has not been run yet (see Validation).

## Claims

- **One layer.** Every DeepGEMM MegaMoE caller uses `forward(hidden_states, topk_weights, topk_ids, shared_experts=None)`.
- **Fusion decided at construction.** Fusion of the shared expert is decided once, from the shared MLP's weights, and never changes at runtime.
- **Supported matrix.** It covers every routed precision and activation that the pinned DeepGEMM exposes:

  | routed | kernel | dispatch | fusable shared | activations |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | mxfp4 | `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` (fp8xfp4) | MXFP8 | MXFP8 | swiglu, situ |
  | mxfp8 | `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` (fp8xfp8) | MXFP8 | MXFP8 | swiglu, situ |
  | nvfp4 | `nvfp4_mega_moe` | NVFP4, one scale per token | MXFP8, BF16 | swiglu |
  | bf16 | `bf16_mega_moe` | BF16 | BF16 | swiglu |

  `swiglu` takes optional `clamp`, `alpha` and `beta`. `situ` (Kimi K3) takes `alpha` and `beta`.
- **Existing models unchanged.** DeepSeek V4/V4.1 and Kimi K3 still build the MXFP4 row and pass the same kernel arguments as before. The mxfp8, nvfp4 and bf16 rows have no model caller yet.
- **Size.** Code under `vllm/` is +360 lines net. The refactor commit is −120, the NVFP4 commit is +472, and the two follow-up commits are −15 and +23.

## Validation

GB200 (SM100), vendored DeepGEMM at the current pin:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py \
    tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py \
    tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py
# 138 passed in 67s
```

**Kernel numerics.** The real kernel is compared against an fp32 reference that runs on the same quantized weights and activations. The reference covers dispatch quantization, the activation, the L2 activation quantization and the shared expert. The metric is DeepGEMM's `calc_diff`; the test requires < 1e-3 and cosine > 0.99. The table shows the worst case over the activations each format supports:

| routed | unfused shared | fused MXFP8 shared | fused BF16 shared |
|---|---|---|---|
| mxfp4 | 2.9e-5 | 1.8e-4 | – |
| mxfp8 | 3.1e-5 | 1.8e-4 | – |
| nvfp4 | 1.8e-6 | 1.6e-4 | 1.4e-6 |
| bf16 | 2.1e-6 | – | 1.7e-6 |

**Negative controls.** Each of these deliberate breaks made the expected cases fail:

| break | cases that failed |
|---|---|
| wrong weight layout, activation or shared input (MX) | the affected cases |
| drop NVFP4 per-token `x_scales`, `l1_alpha` or `l2_alpha` | all 9 NVFP4 cases |
| drop the shared-expert input | all 6 fused cases |
| wrong shared `BLOCK_M` | the 3 fused-MXFP8 cases |

**Input staging.** The Triton staging kernels match DeepGEMM's reference quantizers (`per_token_cast_to_fp8`, `per_token_cast_to_nvfp4`) bit for bit. This covers values, scales, shared-expert inputs, unrouted padding and the zero-token case.

**Not yet done:**
- [ ] End-to-end DeepSeek-V4.1 gsm8k A/B against main: TP4, `--enable-expert-parallel`, `--kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'`. The main baseline is 92.65% flexible / 92.57% strict.
- [ ] End-to-end Kimi K3 with `moe_backend=deep_gemm_mega_moe`.
- Only single-rank kernel numerics have been run; there is no multi-rank EP numerics test.

## Details

**Feature matrix.**
- Each `MegaMoEWeightFormat` row declares five things: the MMA type, the kernel entry point, the routed weight spec (dtype, packing, scale group, scale dtype), the dispatch quant key, and the fusable shared-expert specs.
- The layer validates its `MegaMoEActivation` against the row at construction.
- A new precision is a new row plus whatever staging it needs. It needs no new expert class.

**Shared-expert fusion.**
- The layer fuses the shared expert when two conditions hold. First, the shared MLP's weight dtype, scale dtype and shape match one of the row's shared specs. Second, the installed DeepGEMM exposes the shared-expert buffer and kernel API.
- Otherwise `forward` adds `shared_experts(hidden_states)` once.
- A fused layer raises if it is still handed a shared module.

**Input staging.**
- `prepare_megamoe.py` moved from `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/` to `fused_moe/`. The old location caused an import cycle through `vllm.models.deepseek_v4`.
- It gained a BF16 passthrough and an NVFP4 kernel.
- Shared Triton helpers were factored out of the MX kernel, which is still bit-exact.

**NVFP4.**
- Dispatch quantizes hidden states with one NVFP4 scale per token, computed at runtime. The checkpoint's `w1`/`w3` `input_scale` are therefore unused. A model that wires NVFP4 must skip them.
- The kernel takes a single scalar L2 activation scale. The layer uses the largest `w2` `input_scale` across all experts. Every rank reads every expert's scale tensors during loading, so all ranks agree and EPLB expert moves stay valid.
- `l2_alpha` (the per-expert `w2` global scale × the L2 activation scale) is computed inside the staging kernel. This avoids an extra launch and stays correct after EPLB moves or a weight reload.
- The kernel takes one `l1_alpha` per expert, so the loader raises if `w1` and `w3` `weight_scale_2` differ (relative tolerance 1e-5, as in ModelOpt's `allclose` check). It compares the two shards of the same load, not the live slot, so a reload that changes the scale does not trip it. ModelOpt's and Quark's NVFP4 MoE only warn here; they also use one scale.
- Meta tensors, which reload dry runs pass, skip this host-side scale state.
- The L2 activation scale is a host scalar in DeepGEMM's API, so CUDA graphs capture its value. A weight reload that changes the `w2` input scales needs a graph recapture. In eager mode the layer recomputes the max on reload. Passing it as a device tensor needs a DeepGEMM change and a pin bump, so it is left for a follow-up.

**Behaviour changes for existing models:**
- DeepSeek V4/V4.1 now also run Kimi K3's one-time first-launch barrier: a device sync plus a gloo barrier on the EP CPU group. It runs on the first forward, which is the eager profile run before graph capture.
- `get_deep_gemm_mega_moe_backend()` and the backend classes are removed. Their docstring named them as the override point for plugins and SM90. The extension point is now a new `MegaMoEWeightFormat` row, plus `check_deep_gemm_mega_moe_supported`.

**CI.** The new test file and the moved sources are added to the B200 "DeepSeek V4 Kernels" step. Before this PR the SM100 numerics ran only from `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py`. The staging-kernel tests are gated to SM100, where those kernels run. The L4 "MoE Kernels" shards also collect `tests/kernels/moe/`, and on SM89 Triton casts fp32 to fp8 through fp16 (`cvt.rz.f16.f32`). That rounds the NVFP4 block scales twice, so the bit-exact test failed there. The loader and fusion-selection tests in the file still run on L4.

**Unchanged:** the XPU `DeepseekV4MegaMoEExperts`, which uses a different kernel.

**Related PRs:**
- Not a duplicate: no open PR unifies the MegaMoE expert classes or wires `nvfp4_mega_moe`.
- #60096 (merged): the load-into-kernel-layout procedure this PR keeps.
- #60895 (GLM-5.3 block-FP8 MegaMoE): edits the backend classes this PR removes, so the two conflict. After this PR lands it fits the mxfp8 row, plus a load-time block-scale requant.
- #59003 (weight reload for packed MegaMoE buffers): also targets the removed classes. #60096 already writes checkpoint shards in place.
- #53556 (Kimi K3 BF16 shared-expert fusion into the latent tail) and #40833 (modular-kernel MegaMoE integration, stale draft) take different approaches.

title: [CI] Run 4xB200 steps nightly only
body:
## Overview

Run the two remaining per-PR 4xB200 steps only on nightly builds: `(4xB200) Kimi K3 Prefix Cache` (2 shards) and `(B200) Distributed MooncakeConnector PD accuracy` (4 GPUs). The other 4xB200 steps (LM Eval HiSparse, PCP, Spec Decode, Qwen3.8 accuracy) are already `optional`.

## Claims

- On PR and main builds these steps are skipped unless someone requests them. Nightly and daily Full CI builds still run them.
- The `:amd: (MI355) Distributed MooncakeConnector HIP PD accuracy` mirror stays per-PR (`optional: false`, as kernels.yaml and distributed.yaml already do).

## Validation

- ci-infra `_step_should_run` returns True for every step on nightly builds, and False for `optional` steps otherwise. So these steps now run only on nightly/daily builds, or when requested explicitly.
- The mirror's `optional` comes from `amd.get("optional", step.optional)`, so the explicit `false` keeps the AMD job's current behavior.
- pre-commit passes, including the step-key and test-tethering checks.

## Details

**Why.** A read-only look at the b200-k8s cluster (01:35Z Oct 14) showed 6 schedulable nodes with 47 GPUs, all in use, and **22 pods pending, every one asking for 4 GPUs**. Some had waited about 3 hours, for example build 94519's Kimi K3 Prefix Cache shard. Freed GPUs go to 1- and 2-GPU pods first, so a node rarely has 4 free GPUs at once. Pods that wait too long are failed by agent-stack-k8s as `stack_error`. This is the same pattern seen on main's daily builds since Oct 5.

**Tradeoff.** PRs touching `vllm/models/kimi_k3/`, the Mooncake connector, or the other source dependencies of these steps no longer get these tests per PR. Regressions show up on the next nightly instead. Authors can still request the steps explicitly.

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs for these step keys and found none.

title: [Docs] Add train-inference consistency agent skill
body:
## Overview

Adds the `train-inference-consistency` agent skill under `.agents/skills/` (symlinked from `.claude/skills/`). It guides an agent through making RL training and vLLM rollout produce bitwise identical logprobs (true on-policy RL) while keeping rollout throughput close to the high-performance baseline.

## Claims

- A C0–C10 workflow with explicit pass criteria per gate, from module inventory and proxy model through inference batch / prefill-decode invariance, training forward and backward alignment, two-step RL acceptance, and delivery.
- Guides for the problems that come up on that path: mismatch localization and bisect, training forward and backward validation, which batch-invariant kernel each operator uses and what it costs, quantization conversion chain and QAT, rollout engine behavior (sampling seeds, prefix cache, MTP, R3), performance A/B, exact checkpoint resume, runtime provenance, and paired acceptance.
- The rules come from the DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Nemotron-3.5-Lightning NVFP4 consistency work, where `actor/ppo_kl` and rollout/training logprob diff are 0 at every step.

## Validation

Docs only, no code change.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Pin AITER back to v0.1.24.post1 for DSv4.1 mono decode numerics
body:
## Overview

Pin the ROCm base image back to AITER `v0.1.24.post1`. With AITER `v0.1.25` (#61230), the gfx950 MXFP4 fused-MoE reference selects different kernels and repeatedly fails `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py::test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm[4]`. Because that step's `source_file_dependencies` do not include the ROCm base image, the regression is invisible on `main` and only surfaces as a permanently red step on every PR that touches `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/`.

## Claims

- Restores the `AMD: (MI355) DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics` step to green.
- Makes an AITER / ROCm base-image change re-run that step, so the next bump cannot land without exercising this test.

## Validation

### Historical CI comparison

| Build | PR commit | `aiter` in the image | DSv4.1 Mono Decode Numerics |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [94372](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94372) | `05f5e3fdd3` | `v0.1.24.post1` | **passed** (`exit 0`), whole build 213 finished / 0 failed |
| [94644](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94644) | `a145d106ea` | `v0.1.25` | **failed** (`exit 1`), 11/11 runs |

The two commits carry the same attention-sink change but different upstream revisions, so this is not a strict single-variable experiment. The narrower passing-to-failing window is described below. Both base images report their dependency versions explicitly:

```
# build 94372, "AMD: :docker: refresh ROCm base"
Dependency summary: base=rocm/dev-ubuntu-22.04:7.2.3-complete,rocm=7.2.3,python=3.12,
pytorch=733fca1,...,flash-attn=0e60e394,aiter=v0.1.24.post1,mori=v1.2.3.post1,...

# build 94644, same step
Dependency summary: ...,aiter=v0.1.25,mori=v1.2.3.post1,...
```

Repeated attempts fail at the same TP4 assertion:

```
FAILED tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py::test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm[4]
AssertionError: ratio 1, 1 x 6
  File "tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py", line 471, in _check_layers
    assert _cos(o[0], same_in) > 0.9999 and _rel(o[0], same_in) < 0.015, tag
= 1 failed, 1 passed  (tp=2 passes, tp=4 fails)
```

Latest head: `259a66489693`, after merging current upstream `main`. Validation is pending in [upstream CI #94692](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94692), requested with `/ci run`. The target step is defined in `.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml`; the AMD-only `/amd-ci run` pipeline reads `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` and does not contain this step. A passing AMD bootstrap or other AMD jobs does not establish that the TP4 reproducer passed.

Local validation: `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed. With `PYTHONUTF8=1`, `uv run --no-project --python <repo-root>/.venv/Scripts/python.exe python tools/pre_commit/check_test_tethering.py .buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml` passed. YAML inspection confirmed four MI355 devices, the test-file command, the new source dependency, and the image-build dependency. No local GPU test was run; the reproducer requires CDNA4 (gfx950).

## Details

**Failure mechanism.** The mono path runs vLLM's own FlyDSL kernels; the reference uses `DeepseekV4MoE` with `moe_backend="aiter"`. In build 94372, the TP4 shape (model_dim=5120, padded inter_dim=640, token bucket=8) uses the heuristic `flydsl_moe1_afp8_wfp4_bf16_t32x128x256_w2_gui` / `flydsl_moe2_afp8_wfp4_bf16_t32x128x128_atomic_bnt2` pair. In build 94644, AITER selects `..._w2_gui_fp8` / `flydsl_moe2_layout_afp8_wfp4_bf16_t32x256x128_reduce_sbm32`, changing intermediate quantization and reduction. This agrees with TP2 passing and TP4 failing. It does not prove which implementation is more accurate. The failed assertion combines cosine similarity and relative L2 error without printing either value, so exceeding the 1.5% relative threshold specifically is not established. The duplicate-tuning warning also appears in the old passing log and is not evidence of a newly introduced defect.

The regression window is narrow. Between the last green run and the first red run, the only change to the branch was merging `main`; within `main` commits `c19c263ac8` (2026-10-13 20:06 UTC, proven green for this exact step by [94594](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94594)) and `4e0681ed56` (2026-10-14 00:24 UTC, the merge point), `7a9d3db896` (#61230) is the only commit touching anything this step executes. The other MoE-facing commit in that window, `ad8d39cbab`, wires padding into `fused_topk_bias`'s **non**-AITER branch, which this test does not take; `e90158d912` touches the batched Triton MoE, which `moe_backend="aiter"` does not use.

**Why the step never caught it.** The step's dependencies are `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/` and the two DSv4.1 mono test files. An AITER bump touches none of them, so the step is created but stays `blocked` on every `main` build. That is why the regression sat unnoticed and then blocked unrelated PRs (e.g. #57797) that happen to touch that directory.

**Tradeoff.** This reverts an intentional periodic bump, so AITER `v0.1.25` is not re-landed until the DSv4.1 mono numerics are understood — either the AITER kernels regressed accuracy on gfx950, or the new numerics are acceptable and the test's contract needs revisiting. ROCm/aiter has no newer tag than `v0.1.25`, so there is nothing to bump forward to. `docker/Dockerfile.rock_base` is pinned too, to keep the two base images on the same AITER.

**Not covered.** No full-model accuracy evaluation and no MI355 run outside CI. Whether `v0.1.25`'s numerics are wrong or merely different is not established by this PR.

**Duplication.** Checked: no open PR reverts the AITER pin or references #61230.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** three-line change; reverts a dependency pin and closes the CI dependency gap that let the regression land, without touching model or kernel code.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** await the latest upstream CI's TP2/TP4 reproducer result; historical evidence and passing local configuration checks are linked above. No local gfx950 hardware is available.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** comment-free, minimal diff; `git diff --check` clean; the edited Buildkite YAML parses and the step resolves with the new dependency.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** summary, root cause, evidence, tradeoffs and limitations above.
</details>

title: [Bugfix][MRV2][Spec Decode] Honor EAGLE3 single-state draft configuration
body:
## Overview

Fix Model Runner V2 startup for the GPT-OSS-120B EAGLE3 [short-context](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/gpt-oss-120b-Eagle3-short-context) and [throughput](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/gpt-oss-120b-Eagle3-throughput) drafts, which set `use_aux_hidden_state=false`.

## Claims

- Single-state EAGLE3 drafts receive the target's final hidden state.
- EAGLE3's default auxiliary-state path and other speculative methods keep their existing behavior.

## Validation

CPU: 32 tests passed, including nine new configuration cases; pre-commit passed, including mypy. Tested on `2521446` plus this patch.

GPU: B200 x1 / TP1, GPT-OSS-120B MXFP4, vLLM `c19c263` plus this patch, CUDA 13, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. Context 131072, GMU 0.90, max sequences 8, prefix caching off.

| Draft | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Throughput, k=1 | V2 startup fails: 2880/8640 width mismatch | Generates in eager and non-eager modes; natural acceptance in both |
| Short-context, k=3 | Not run | Generates in eager and non-eager modes; natural acceptance in both |
| Long-context, k=3 (multi-state reference) | Generates | Generates; auxiliary capture retained |

Eight fixed math/coding prompts, greedy decoding, normal EOS, 128-token cap; batches 1 and 8, one warmup and three measured repeats each.

<details>
<summary>Timings and output comparisons</summary>

Multi-state reference, identical rendered prompts and input token IDs:

| Batch | Before tok/s | After tok/s | Change | Before / after repeat ranges |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 | 547.840 | 537.452 | -1.90% | 544.820–549.704 / 535.911–538.325 |
| 8 | 1897.596 | 1900.161 | +0.14% | 1892.264–1906.589 / 1894.052–1906.894 |

Throughput is total output tokens divided by total wall time, including prefill and decode. Three repeats per case; before and after used separate GPU allocations. These measurements do not establish performance improvement or non-regression.

Some batch-8 outputs were not bit-identical. The unmodified baseline also varied across repeated runs, and the target-only/speculative differences started at near-tied token choices.

</details>

<details>
<summary>CPU test commands</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py -q

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/eagle/eagle3_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py
```

</details>

## Details

GPT-OSS-120B has [`hidden_size=2880`](https://huggingface.co/openai/gpt-oss-120b/blob/b5c939de8f754692c1647ca79fbf85e8c1e70f8a/config.json): 2880 elements per token's hidden-state vector. Three-state EAGLE3 concatenates three target-layer vectors to width `3 × 2880 = 8640`, then projects them to the draft's hidden size.

These two drafts instead consume only the final target hidden state and have no auxiliary-state projection. V2 still captures three states, and [`combine_hidden_states`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c19c263ac8ea3fd6e1d2d689f0e4e725855d89cf/vllm/model_executor/models/llama_eagle3.py#L397) passes the 8640-wide tensor through unchanged. Copying it into the draft's 2880-wide input buffer fails.

The fix honors the flag during runner initialization, so the existing proposer uses the final hidden state instead.

Related: [#40656](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40656) proposed this fix but is closed and unmerged. [#50170](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50170) addresses fallback warnings, not this configuration bug. No equivalent open PR was found.

AI-assisted implementation and testing using Codex.

title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Mask grammar-invalid implicit reasoning ends
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With an engine-based reasoning parser, a structured-output request fails with "grammar rejected tokens" and HTTP 500 when the model samples an implicit reasoning end, such as GLM's `<tool_call>`, that the request's grammar cannot start with. Reasoning rows of the bitmask are unconstrained, so the token can be sampled, and since #59627 it is fed to the grammar. This masks those tokens while the request reasons. Implicit ends the grammar accepts stay allowed.

Related: #60722 (RFC; this is the "remaining issue" it describes, using its first option restricted to grammar-rejected tokens), #59627 (feeds the implicit end to the grammar), #59608 (`required`/named tool calls, which must keep `<tool_call>` allowed), #61456 (open; also edits `_fill_bitmasks`).

## Claims

- A request whose grammar rejects an implicit reasoning end as its first token (a JSON schema, `tool_choice="none"` with `response_format`) can no longer sample that token while reasoning, so it no longer ends in "grammar rejected tokens".
- Requests whose grammar accepts the implicit end are unchanged: `tool_choice` `required`, named, and `auto` with tools (with or without `response_format`).
- The explicit end (`</think>`) and every other token stay allowed while reasoning. Draft and bonus rows under speculative decoding are masked the same way.

## Validation

**Unit, CPU.** `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, xgrammar and guidance:

```text
python -m pytest tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py
# main source + these tests: 181 passed, 8 failed, 1 xfailed
# this branch:               189 passed, 1 xfailed
```

The 8 that fail on main: `test_real_flow[implicit_end_rejected-*]` (pattern `RRUUU`; main gives `UUUUU`), `test_reasoning_rows_mask_grammar_invalid_implicit_end[json-*]`, `test_parallel_fill_masks_grammar_invalid_implicit_end[*]`, and the two `TestReasoningEndTokenIds` cases for the new property. `test_reasoning_rows_mask_grammar_invalid_implicit_end[regex_starts_with_marker-*]` passes on both: a grammar that starts with the marker keeps it allowed and consumes it.

Wider run on this branch: `tests/v1/structured_output`, `tests/parser` (without `tests/parser/cohere`, which needs `cohere_melody`), `tests/reasoning/test_glm4_moe_reasoning_parser.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py`, `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py`: 6636 passed, 1 xfailed. `tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py`: 19 passed on both. `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: the same 48 multimodal tests fail on main and on this branch, because this kernel-less install cannot inspect the Llava architecture.

**Real components, no model.** GLM-5.3 tokenizer, `--reasoning-parser glm45` (`Glm47MoeParserReasoningAdapter`), xgrammar, prompt ending in `<think>`. Bitmask rows while reasoning, then `accept_tokens([<tool_call>])` as the scheduler would call it:

| constraint | main: `<tool_call>` allowed / masked bits | this branch | `accept_tokens` |
|---|---|---|---|
| JSON schema, no spec | yes / 0 | no / 1 (`<tool_call>` only; `</think>` allowed) | False |
| JSON schema, 3 draft rows + bonus | yes / 0 in all 4 rows | no / 1 in all 4 rows | False |
| `required` structural tag | yes / 0 | yes / 0 | True |
| named structural tag | yes / 0 | yes / 0 | True |

**End to end, CPU server.** arm64 CPU image of main `206e45d47`, whose four changed files are identical to `a2fb48273`, with the structured-output backends from `a2fb48273` mounted in both arms and this branch's four files in the second. A 2-layer Llama with the GLM-5.3 tokenizer and vocabulary, `--reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice`, xgrammar, greedy, 3 runs per case. `logit_bias` makes `<tool_call>` (154843) the top token.

| request | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `json_schema`, bias `<tool_call>` | 500 x3, "grammar rejected tokens [154843]" | 200 x3, no `<tool_call>` in reasoning |
| `json_schema` + tools + `tool_choice="none"`, same bias | 500 x3 | 200 x3 |
| `json_schema`, bias `<tool_call>` 100, `</think>` 50, answer tokens 30 | 500 x3 | 200 x3, `{"answer": "yes"}`, finish `stop` |
| `json_schema` + tools + `tool_choice="auto"`, same bias | 200 x3, tool call | 200 x3, same tool call |
| `tool_choice="required"` / named / `auto` without `response_format` | 200 x3 each, tool call | 200 x3 each, same tool call |
| `json_schema`, no bias | 200 x3 | 200 x3 |

Every request that returns 200 on main returns the same response on this branch. The engine log on main has one `Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [154843]` per 500 (12 of 12); the branch logs have none.

<details>
<summary>Raw request and responses (third row)</summary>

```json
{"model": "glm-tiny", "max_tokens": 96, "temperature": 0,
 "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Is the sky blue? Reply as JSON."}],
 "response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "a", "schema": {
   "type": "object", "properties": {"answer": {"type": "string", "enum": ["yes", "no"]}},
   "required": ["answer"], "additionalProperties": false}}},
 "logit_bias": {"154843": 100, "154842": 50, "4913": 30, "9214": 30, "788": 30, "330": 30,
                "9689": 30, "9204": 30, "154820": 30}}
```

main, 3 of 3:

```text
HTTP 500 {"error":{"message":"Internal server error","type":"InternalServerError","param":null,"code":500}}
(EngineCore pid=131) ERROR 10-14 06:31:44 [scheduler.py:2189] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [154843] for request chatcmpl-8bf78d42551e682d-8a4ad66a. Terminating request.
```

this branch, 3 of 3 (fields from the response):

```text
HTTP 200  finish_reason=stop  reasoning="" (no <tool_call>)  content={"answer": "yes"}  tool_calls=[]
```
</details>

**Speculative decoding, end to end.** `logit_bias` is rejected with speculative decoding, so these runs use fixed weights instead: layer outputs are zero and the LM head prefers `<tool_call>`, then ` the`, at every position. ngram, 3 speculative tokens, `json_schema`, 96 tokens:

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `json_schema` | 500 x3 | 200 x3, 96 reasoning tokens, all ` the` |
| `json_schema` + tools + `tool_choice="none"` | 500 x3 | 200 x3 |
| drafts accepted (`json_schema` only) | | 207 of 225 |
| `required`, `auto` + tools | tool calls | same tool calls |

Each accepted draft position used a masked row; an unmasked draft row would have sampled `<tool_call>` and failed the request.

<details>
<summary>CPU harness note</summary>

On main the CPU stand-in `_compute_slot_mapping_kernel_impl` (`vllm/utils/cpu_triton_utils.py`) takes its arguments in an order that no longer matches `ComputeSlotMappingKernel.kernel`, so the dispatcher passes `slot_mapping` as `block_size` and the first forward fails. These runs mount a copy of that one function, with the kernel's parameter names, in both arms. Separate from this change.
</details>

**GPU, end to end.** @simon-veitner-redhat ran main `a2fb482732` against this branch `6d144d6478` on H200 ([results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61574#issuecomment-6163972357)): GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4, TP2, `glm47` tool and reasoning parsers, xgrammar, 8 seeds per row. "Tagged" means a tool result in the conversation quotes GLM's own tags (`<tool_call>`, `<arg_key>`, `<arg_value>`), followed by a `json_schema` request.

| request, no spec decode | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| tagged, `json_schema`, no tools | 7/8 500s, 0/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 4/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `json_schema`, `tool_choice: "none"` | 5/8 500s, 3/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 7/8 valid JSON |
| `logit_bias` forcing `<tool_call>`, blocking `</think>` | 8/8 500s | 0 500s, empty content |
| untagged, `json_schema` | 8/8 valid JSON | 8/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `tool_choice: "required"` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` |

| request, MTP 3 tokens, Model Runner V2, async scheduling | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| tagged, `json_schema`, no tools | 6/8 500s, 2/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 6/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `json_schema`, `tool_choice: "none"` | 2/8 500s, 6/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 8/8 valid JSON |
| untagged, `json_schema` | 8/8 valid JSON | 8/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `tool_choice: "required"` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` |

Main logs one `Failed to advance FSM` per 500; this branch logs none. The remaining invalid JSON on this branch is a separate frontend issue: the token stream is valid JSON, but the model quotes `<tool_call>` inside a JSON string and `content` is cut there. The CPU runs above use the V1 model runner, so both runners are covered.

**Motivation.** A GLM-5.3 deployment (MTP with 3 tokens, Model Runner V2, xgrammar, `glm45`) logged 649 "grammar rejected tokens" terminations in 8 hours; 625 of them ended on `<tool_call>` (154843). A non-streaming request terminated this way returns HTTP 500.

## Details

Path of the failure, `enable_in_reasoning=False`:

1. A request with a JSON schema is reasoning. `_get_constraint_bounds` puts `constraint_start` past every scheduled row, so `grammar_bitmask` fills each row with the full mask.
2. The model samples `<tool_call>`, which `Glm47MoeParser` treats as an implicit reasoning end: it ends reasoning and starts a tool call.
3. `accept_tokens` finds that end and, since #59627, sets `grammar_start` to its offset, so `<tool_call>` is fed to the grammar. A JSON grammar rejects it and `accept_tokens` returns False.
4. The scheduler logs "Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens" and finishes the request with `FINISHED_ERROR`.

The change, in `StructuredOutputManager`:

- `ParserEngine.implicit_reasoning_end_token_ids`: reasoning-end tokens other than the explicit end, the same split `find_reasoning_end` uses to report an implicit end. Exposed through `ParserEngineReasoningAdapter`. This only adds a read-only property, so no parser changes behavior.
- `_masked_reasoning_ends`: the implicit ends the grammar rejects as its first token (`validate_tokens([t])`, non-mutating in every backend). The grammar does not advance before reasoning ends, so the set is computed once per request and cached on `StructuredOutputRequest`.
- `_fill_bitmasks`: a row the grammar does not constrain allows every token except those ids. Only rows before `constraint_start` (including the bonus row while reasoning) get them, in both the serial and the parallel fill. Constrained rows and rows after padding are unchanged.

Tradeoffs and limits:

- This changes the reasoning distribution only by removing tokens whose sampling makes the output invalid under the request's own constraint. The model keeps reasoning or ends with the explicit end. The alternative outcome is an error, so there is no flag.
- Same scope as #59627: engine-based parsers and single-token implicit ends. Multi-token or text-only ends (`deepseek_v4`, `inkling`) are not covered.
- Cost: one `validate_tokens` call per implicit end per request, and a bit clear per masked id on reasoning rows. No device work and no host sync.
- #61456 replaces the guidance path of `_fill_bitmasks` with a batch fill. Whichever lands second has to keep the reasoning-row mask.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Make the query contiguous for TRTLLM ragged MLA prefill
body:
## Overview

`TRTLLM_RAGGED` MLA prefill passes the query straight to FlashInfer's `trtllm_ragged_attention_deepseek`, whose launcher forwards K/V strides but not Q strides, so a strided query is read as if it were packed and prefill attention is silently wrong. This makes the query contiguous at both call sites (a no-op for callers that already pass a contiguous query, such as native models).

The Transformers modeling backend hits this because it hands MLA a transposed query (`[1, heads, tokens, dim] -> [tokens, heads, dim]`), and `TRTLLM_RAGGED` is the default MLA prefill backend on Blackwell.

## Claims

- Fixes MLA prefill for strided queries with `TRTLLM_RAGGED`, which broke every MLA model on the Transformers backend on Blackwell (e.g. GLM-4.7-Flash gsm8k 0.8% -> 83.5%, native 83.6%).
- No change for contiguous queries.

## Validation

GLM-4.7-Flash, gsm8k (5-shot, 1319 questions), 1x B200:

| Config | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---|---|
| Native | 83.6% | 0.1% |
| Transformers backend, `main` | 0.8% | 31.8% |
| Transformers backend, this PR | 83.5% | 0.0% |

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash --max-model-len 8192 [--model-impl transformers]
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000
```

On a small random-weight GLM-4.7-Flash-architecture checkpoint, the first generated token's logprob vs HF eager (same prompt, teacher-forced) went from 0.19 off to 0.00 with `TRTLLM_RAGGED`. Other MLA backends were already correct with the strided query: `FLASH_ATTN` prefill, and `FLASHINFER_MLA` / `CUTLASS_MLA` / `TRITON_MLA` decode.

Tests on B200:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_registry.py tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_selector.py  # 47 passed
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -k TRTLLM_RAGGED  # 580 passed
```

title: [Perf][MRV2] Skip empty draft-token resets on request admission
body:
## Overview
On GH200, short-input embedding inference at high concurrency is **CPU-bottlenecked by the EngineCore main thread**, with GPU SM utilization only **~9–18%**. Skip unnecessary per-request draft-buffer indexing and zeroing when Model Runner V2 has zero speculative steps, improving throughput by **~11–28%** in the measured workload while preserving the stale-slot reset from [#39833](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39833) for nonempty buffers. The improvement is largely due to reduced GIL contention.



## Claims
- Remove unnecessary PyTorch operations from request admission for pooling and ordinary non-speculative generation.
- Preserve draft-token clearing on slot reuse whenever the buffer has columns, including speculative decoding and diffusion models.
- The PyTorch operation releases the GIL, leading to the main thread being unnecessarily preempted by other threads that could do their work while the main thread waits for the GPU instead.
- Existing pinned GH200 embedding benchmarks report +10.6% request throughput for short inputs at concurrency 512 and +25.0–28.2% at concurrency 2048 for this guard alone.


## Validation
Checks run for this change:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py -v -rs
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/states.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py
git diff --check
```

With short inputs on GH200, throughput plateaus at roughly **5–6k requests/s (~85–100k tokens/s)** while the EngineCore main thread is CPU-saturated and GPU SM utilization remains **~9–18%**. For comparison, 1024-token inputs reach roughly **400k tokens/s** on the same server. These observations identify per-request work on the engine's main thread as the short-input throughput bottleneck.

| Concurrency | Stock throughput | With guard, pass 1 / pass 2 (estimated) | Gain, pass 1 / pass 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | ~4.66k req/s | ~5.15k / ~5.15k req/s | +10.6% / +10.6% |
| 2048 | ~5.57k req/s | ~6.96k / ~7.14k req/s | +25.0% / +28.2% |

Configuration: `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16`, FP8 quantization, v0.31.0 aarch64 container, one GH200, MRV2 with synchronous scheduling, 16 API servers, and unique random short text inputs. Two reverse-order benchmark passes used six runs per configuration. Engine cores 4–5, API-server cores 8–39, and client cores 40–71 were pinned on GPU 0's NUMA node. Stock pinning-validation repeats spanned 4741–4965 req/s; per-patch raw variability is unavailable here.

Server flags:

```text
--max-num-batched-tokens 65536 --max-model-len 32768
--max-cudagraph-capture-size 32768
--api-server-count 16 --chat-template-content-format openai
```



## Details
`RequestState` allocates `draft_tokens` with shape `[max_num_reqs, num_speculative_steps]`. Admission previously evaluated `self.draft_tokens[req_idx].zero_()` even when the row had zero elements. The guard tests the configured width before indexing.

**Why such a large improvement:** The reason seems to be GIL contention. The pytorch op releases the GIL and then the main thread spends time waiting in pthread_cond_timedwait to reacquire it. If GIL is not released at that point, other threads will acquire it when the main thread waits for the GPU instead, leading to better overlapping GPU and CPU work.

**Why short inputs matter for embedding models:** semantic search commonly embeds a short question or a few keywords to retrieve much longer passages. Short-query embedding is therefore a core online serving workload, even when the indexed documents are long.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Keep routing rows during DeepSeek V4.1 decoder replay
body:
## Overview

Keep every prefill routing row when DeepSeek V4.1 decoder replay runs with returned routed experts enabled. Extracted from #61388 as a standalone fix based on `main`.

## Claims

- R3 requests use the existing prompt-logprobs keep-row mechanism so decoder replay does not omit their routing computations.
- Cover eager and PIECEWISE replay in the existing replay-batch suite.
- The diff contains the request row-retention policy and its regression coverage in two files.

## Validation

- **20 isolated CPU policy cases passed** using the actual request-admission, graph-selection, and replay row-selection methods with real CPU tensors. The same checks against unmodified `main` reproduce **6 failures / 14 passes**, including a 300-row prefill incorrectly reduced to 128 rows.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy and Buildkite test tethering, and `git diff --check`: passed with local UTF-8/Git Bash interpreter adaptations.
- The pre-split #61388 validation recorded real-weight DeepSeek-V4.1 TP1/DP2/EP, 300/301-token prefill: late layers previously executed only 128 rows; the keep-row fix retained all rows in all 40 layers. The request-retention change is preserved from that combined revision.

GPU/model runs were not repeated for the split. CPU checks stop at the row-selection boundary and substitute configuration/base-state/input-gather fixtures; they do not validate CUDA kernels or attention numerics. The GPU regression remains in the existing CI-tethered suite:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py
```

## Details

Decoder replay can normally skip older prefill rows when only final logits are needed. Returned routing needs every accepted token's decisions; scattering the remaining rows cannot recover computations that never ran. Mark R3 requests as requiring every row when admitted, using the existing keep-row policy.

R3-enabled replay therefore retains prefill work that could otherwise be trimmed. No throughput measurement is claimed.

Duplicate-work checks refreshed open PR searches for `61388 in:body`, routed-expert capture, and decoder replay. #52902 adds API consistency tests, #57184 handles DBO staging/offsets, and #56778 implements terminal transport; they do not implement this NVIDIA V4.1 admission policy. The same fix has been removed from #61388, so this is its single review location.

AI assistance was used to split and validate the existing fix.

title: [Bugfix] Engage indexer TP row sharding on total rows, not per-rank rows
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

> This PR description was written by @ZJY0516.

## Overview

Follow-up to #54951, addressing https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54951#discussion_r4267244007: gate the sparse-indexer TP row sharding on **total** scheduled prefill rows instead of per-rank rows, so the 8xH100 TP8 recipe can actually engage it. The floor becomes `AttentionConfig.indexer_tp_shard_min_rows` (default 65536).

Not a duplicate: no other open PR changes how this floor scales with TP. #60601 lowers the same floor on ROCm only; whichever lands second needs a rebase.

## Claims

- TP8 engages row sharding at `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536`; before, it needed 131072, which OOMs on 80 GB Hopper.
- −34.1% mean TTFT on a 1.02M-token prompt at TP8 under an H100-equivalent memory budget.
- TP4 engagement point unchanged (64K total rows). TP2 moves from 32K to 64K total rows by design.
- The floor is configurable, e.g. `-ac '{"indexer_tp_shard_min_rows": 131072}'`.

## Validation

**Problem reproduced** on 8xH200 with an 80 GB-equivalent budget (`--gpu-memory-utilization 0.56`, TP8, BF16 KV, merged-commit build `3e8e1364`):

| Config | Result |
|---|---|
| `--max-num-batched-tokens 131072` | engine init fails: `Available KV cache memory: -6.94 GiB` |
| `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536` | server healthy, but a 70K-token request schedules `num_rows=65536 < threshold=131072` on every chunk → **0 engagements** |

**TTFT at the H100 budget** (8xH200, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.568` ≈ 81,662 MiB/card vs H100's 81,559 MiB), TP8, `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536`, `--max-model-len 1048576`, FP8 KV, `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE`, streaming completions with one request in flight; only the floor differs between arms:

| Prompt | row-sharded (default) | replicated (floor = 2,000,000) | Δ mean TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.02M tok (n=2) | **31.57 s** | 47.92 s | **−34.1%** |

The replicated arm was measured with an earlier revision's `VLLM_INDEXER_TP_SHARD_MIN_ROWS=2000000`; the equivalent now is `-ac '{"indexer_tp_shard_min_rows": 2000000}'`. The gain grows with context depth (0.48 s saved at 255K vs 16.35 s at 1.02M): per-row indexer cost ramps with causal depth while the per-row exchange cost stays constant.

**Tests**

- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_tp_row_shard.py`: 12 passed (TP8 parametrization, total-not-per-rank floor, TP2 32K–64K window stays replicated, floor never below `tp_size`).
- End-to-end serve + long-context completions on TP8 at the H100-equivalent budget; engagement verified via NCCL coll logging, outputs sane.

## Details

Per rank, the saved replicated indexer work (`~ (1 - 1/tp) * rows`) and the `all_gatherv` index traffic (`~ (tp - 1)/tp * rows * topk * 4B`) both scale with `(tp - 1)/tp`, so the engagement crossover in total rows is tp-independent to first order. The old per-rank floor grew the total requirement linearly with `tp`. 65536 is the TP4-calibrated total floor from #54951.

- TP2 now engages later (64K instead of 32K total rows); the exchange's fixed latency term is largest at small `tp`.
- `balanced_prefill_row_shard` takes the floor as an argument and clamps it to at least `tp_size`, so every rank always gets at least one row.
- The floor was calibrated on H200 with NVSwitch; other interconnects were not measured. Startup auto-calibration is a possible follow-up.

title: [Bugfix][CI] Fix renderers tests broken by tool name removal from warn logs
body:
## Overview

[#59294](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59294) removed the tool name from the two malformed-`arguments` warnings in `vllm/renderers/chat_utils/chat_message.py`, but did not update `tests/renderers/test_chat_utils.py`, which still asserts the name appears in the emitted record. Seven tests have failed on `main` since it merged.

That PR's own `:computer: (CPU) Reasoning + Renderers` job failed for this reason ([build 94769](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94769)) and it was merged red, so the breakage landed on `main` and now fails for every PR that touches a `cpu-async-engine-deps` path.

## Fix

Drop the four tool-name assertions and keep each test asserting the part of the message that still exists. The tool name was the only thing distinguishing `test_tool_call_arguments_malformed_json_large` from the small-payload case, so it asserts on the logged length instead, which is what actually covers the point of having a large case: an 18 KB payload is summarised by length rather than logged.

The source change in #59294 is left alone: not logging the tool name is the intended behavior.

## Validation

```
$ pytest -q tests/renderers/test_chat_utils.py -k tool_call_arguments
12 passed
```

Failing tests before this change, all with the same shape:

```
FAILED renderers/test_chat_utils.py::test_tool_call_arguments_malformed_json_small
  assert 'exec' in 'Tool call has arguments that are not valid JSON (54 chars);
  coercing to an empty object so the conversation can continue.'
```

- `test_tool_call_arguments_malformed_json_small`
- `test_tool_call_arguments_malformed_json_large`
- `test_tool_call_arguments_valid_json_non_object[[]]`
- `test_tool_call_arguments_valid_json_non_object[42]`
- `test_tool_call_arguments_valid_json_non_object[true]`
- `test_tool_call_arguments_valid_json_non_object["hello"]`
- `test_tool_call_arguments_multiple_independent`

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Don't read W_UK_T before weight loading in the MLA wrapper
body:
## Overview

Fixes a Kimi-K3 startup crash on ROCm (`'MLAAttention' object has no attribute 'W_UK_T'`) that appears once #53123 turns AITER FP8 BMM off by default.

## Claims

- `KimiK3MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper._fused_qk_prep_supported()` no longer reads `attn.W_UK_T` in `__init__`.
- The fused decode Q-prep path stays enabled when neither AITER BMM is on, instead of being silently disabled.

## Validation

- CI failure: MI355 LM Eval Spec Decode (Fixed-length FP8), `Kimi-K3-pruned75-DSpark-AITER-TP4`, [amd-ci #14622](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14622#01a13ad1-6ae5-4cca-85f2-e72e6996548a).
- Called `_fused_qk_prep_supported` against an `nn.Module` fake MLA attention in that build's CI image (includes #53123):

| FP4 BMM | FP8 BMM | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| off | off | `AttributeError: W_UK_T` | True |
| off | on | False | False |
| on | off | True | True |

- Not run end to end locally: the 475 GB checkpoint doesn't fit on my box. CI's MI355 Spec Decode job covers it.

## Details

`_fused_qk_prep_supported()` runs in `__init__`, but `MLAAttention.W_UK_T` is only created in `process_weights_after_loading`. Before #53123, FP8 BMM was on by default, so the expression short-circuited and never read it. `process_weights_after_loading` always creates `W_UK_T` when FP4 and FP8 BMM are both off, so the check isn't needed. Using `getattr(..., None)` instead would have turned the fused path off for every such config. No open PR fixes this; #60110 edits `_fused_decode` but not this gate.

title: [Bugfix] Don't crash DeepGEMM MegaMoE warmup when get_bf16_mega_gate_config is missing
body:
**Before:** A server started with `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` on a model whose MoE layers use the bf16 mega gate crashes during kernel warmup with `AttributeError: module 'deep_gemm' has no attribute 'get_bf16_mega_gate_config'`.

**After:** Warmup completes. When DeepGEMM does not export `get_bf16_mega_gate_config`, the MegaMoE warmup buckets M values by `block_m` only.

## Overview

#60468 made `_get_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_m_values` call `dg.get_bf16_mega_gate_config` to pick one warmup M per gate config. #61149 moved the DeepGEMM pin to `6ce1c5ec`, which no longer exports that op. Every MegaMoE warmup that uses the mega gate now fails:

```
kernel_warmup.py:244 -> deep_gemm_warmup.py:511 -> :504 -> :366
AttributeError: ... has no attribute 'get_bf16_mega_gate_config'
```

This PR checks `hasattr(dg, "get_bf16_mega_gate_config")` and uses an empty gate config when the op is missing.

## Claims

- MegaMoE warmup no longer crashes when the installed DeepGEMM lacks `get_bf16_mega_gate_config`.
- Behavior is unchanged when the op is present.

## Validation

Existing unit tests:

```
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e .
pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py
# 8 passed
```

Real module, with the vendored DeepGEMM from the precompiled wheel (`vllm.third_party.deep_gemm`): `hasattr(dg, "get_bf16_mega_gate_config")` is `False`, and `_get_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_m_values` (EP=4, 256 experts, top-k 6, 8192 tokens, mega gate on) now returns `[106, 256, 602, 2565, 7901, 8192]` instead of raising.

End to end on 4x B300: a DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint with `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192` finishes DeepGEMM warmup (1254/1254), passes `/health`, and answers a completion request ("The capital of France is" -> " Paris.").

No open PR fixes this: searching open PRs for `get_bf16_mega_gate_config` finds none, and #61538, which edits the same function, keeps the call.

## Details

Coverage trade-off: without gate configs, warmup no longer picks one M per distinct bf16 mega gate config. Gate configs that do not line up with a `block_m` bucket are not warmed and will JIT on the first request that hits them. This costs first-request latency, not correctness.

## Follow-up

A follow-up PR will reintroduce `get_bf16_mega_gate_config` in vllm-project/DeepGEMM and bump the vLLM pin, which restores full warmup coverage for the mega gate. This guard can stay afterwards so a mismatched external `deep_gemm` install does not crash the server.

title: [Perf][HiSparse] Reuse pinned host pool after graph profiling
body:
HiSparse allocates and pins its host KV pool during profiling, then repeats that work for serving. Keep one engine-scoped pool, keyed by `instance_id`, and reuse its backing for the real KV cache.

Profiling teardown detaches temporary layer caches; connector shutdown or failed initialization releases the pool. This removes the per-layer ownership and preservation flags, leaving CUDA-graph teardown unchanged from main.

Adopts Matthew’s approach in [Etelis/vllm#9](https://github.com/Etelis/vllm/pull/9). Refs #60072; complements #60869.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Allow explicit SimpleCPUOffload block counts
body:
## Overview

Allow `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` users to set a shared `num_cpu_blocks` so uneven pipeline stages use the same offload pool size. This implements the explicit-count alternative [suggested in the review of #52921](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52921#pullrequestreview-5449639086).

## Claims

- The scheduler and workers honor the configured count for CPU or disk offload.
- Startup rejects nonpositive/noninteger counts and counts exceeding the local byte-derived capacity, before allocating offload buffers.
- Omitting the option retains automatic sizing. No engine-core changes, collectives, or runtime synchronization are added.

## Validation

- **116 scheduler/worker tests passed**, including 15 added regression cases. Tested current-main Python sources on a B200 using the deployed v0.30.0 compiled extensions; this was not a full current-main native build.
- **All pre-commit hooks passed**, including mypy, formatting, and CI test tethering.
- **End-to-end A/B serving:** Kimi K3, two nodes with 8 B200 GPUs each, TP8/DCP8/PP2, fp8 KV, TOKENSPEED MLA, MRV2, RDMA, no speculative decoding, 128 MiB CPU budget per rank. The same connector change was backported to the deployed v0.30.0 image for serving validation.

| Observation | Automatic sizing | Explicit `num_cpu_blocks: 23` |
|---|---:|---:|
| Scheduler / PP0 / PP1 block counts | 25 / 25 / 23 | 23 / 23 / 23 |
| Highest CPU destination ID | 24 | 22 |
| Out-of-bounds native copy calls | 40, across all 8 PP1 ranks | 0 across 1,088 copy calls |
| Nonempty streaming responses with `[DONE]` | 34/34 | 35/35 |
| Forced CPU reload after GPU prefix-cache reset | Not requested | All 16 ranks; identical 16 output tokens |

The baseline reproduced invalid copy IDs and completed its responses without a model segfault. These results establish the sizing/copy defect; they do not attribute every historical crash to it. No throughput or broad model-accuracy improvement is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Test commands and serving exercise</summary>

The GPU test environment put the current-main source tree at `/tmp/upstream-vllm` and used a `uv` virtualenv with the deployed wheel's compiled extensions:

```bash
/tmp/offload-test-venv/bin/python -I -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp/upstream-vllm"); import pytest; sys.exit(pytest.main(["tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py", "tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py", "-v"]))'
```

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/simple_cpu_offload_connector.py \
  vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py \
  vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/worker.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py \
  docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md
```

Baseline transfer configuration:

```json
{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":134217728,"lazy_offload":false}}
```

Add `"num_cpu_blocks":23` for the patched run. Both runs use `--enable-prefix-caching --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-backend TOKENSPEED_MLA`. The tested model's stage allocations contain 12 and 13 block-strided tensors, respectively, with 442,368 bytes per tensor block. Other models/layouts need a different count.

Exercise `/v1/completions` with `stream:true`, `stream_options:{"include_usage":true}`, `return_token_ids:true`, `temperature:0`, `seed:42`, `ignore_eos:true`, and `max_tokens:16`. Send one approximately 11k-token prefix twice, then 32 different approximately 3.7k-token prefixes to cycle the CPU pool. Check positive usage and `[DONE]` for every response.

In the patched run, enable `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1` and POST `/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=false` after the cold prefix stores drain. Require `success:true`, repeat the prefix, and compare output text and token IDs with the cold result. Reset the GPU cache every four unique prefixes. Instrument `cuda_mem_ops.build_params`/`copy_blocks` to record tensor allocation limits, copied block-ID ranges, and actual CPU-to-GPU copies; successful API responses alone do not establish that offload was exercised.

Baseline trace excerpt:

```json
{"event":"copy_params","layers":13,"source_blocks":10844,"destination_blocks":23,"source_order":1}
{"event":"out_of_bounds_copy","source_max":27,"destination_max":24,"source_limit":10844,"destination_limit":23}
```

Patched trace excerpts (same allocation limits on both stages):

```json
{"event":"copy_enter","blocks":3,"destination_min":20,"destination_max":22,"destination_limit":23,"source_order":1}
{"event":"copy_enter","blocks":5,"source_min":1,"source_max":5,"source_limit":23,"source_order":3}
```

</details>

## Details

Automatic sizing divides the byte budget by each stage's cache geometry independently. With uneven PP stages, the scheduler can assign IDs beyond a heavier worker's allocation; the DMA implementation forms pointers from those IDs without a bounds check. An explicit shared count limits both the scheduler's pool and each worker's allocation, with worker validation based on live tensor strides. For the disk backend, the bound is `disk_capacity_bytes`.

This is materially different from the open #52921: that PR automatically aligns counts using worker collectives and engine RPC. This PR provides the reviewer's smaller configuration-based alternative and leaves engine core untouched. It requires operators to choose a count that fits every worker and configure it identically on every rank. Recalculate it when model layout, parallelism, or speculative decoding changes; unspecified automatic sizing is not repaired by this option.

## Claims

It ran an early `process_weights_after_loading()` so dummy-loaded DeepSeek-V4.1 could fuse its MegaMoE shared experts. #60096 loads MegaMoE experts directly into the DeepGEMM layout, so the CUDA models no longer have `finalize_mega_moe_weights` and the workaround was already a no-op.

- The model-microbenchmark skill drops its caveat about degenerate dummy norm weights, fixed by #61323.

title: [CI/Build] Fix test_deepseek_v41_mxfp8_scale_loading after #57797
body:
#57797 removed `get_tensor_model_parallel_rank` from `vllm.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.model`, since attention sinks now load through their `weight_loader`. `test_deepseek_v41_mxfp8_scale_loading` still monkeypatches it there, so all 4 cases fail with `AttributeError` ([build 94813](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94813), H200 Quantization shard 3/4). The model only reads the world size now, and TP slicing happens in the linear layers, so the rank is patched on `linear` only.

The Quantization step's `source_file_dependencies` don't include `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py`, so #57797's CI did not run this test.

Test: `pytest tests/quantization/test_fp8.py -k test_deepseek_v41_mxfp8_scale_loading` on DGX Spark (GB10), upstream main 47232f3c7f: 4 failed before the fix, 4 passed after (all 17 `-k deepseek_v41` tests pass).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; I reviewed the change and ran the test above.

title: [Benchmark] Add per-case kernel profiles to vllm bench forward
body:
## Overview

Add `--profile-dir` to `vllm bench forward` (#61339): a per-kernel GPU time breakdown of each benchmarked batch, in a form an agent or a script can read and compare directly.

## Claims

- `--profile-dir DIR`: after timing, each case's graph is replayed 3 more times under `torch.profiler`. Every rank writes `DIR/<case>.rank<r>.trace.json.gz` (Perfetto) and `DIR/<case>.rank<r>.kernels.json` (GPU time per kernel per forward, sorted, with call counts and one full name per group). Rank 0's top kernels are printed and included in `--output-json`.
- Only the timed forward is counted: the in-graph KV restore and rank rendezvous that precede it in each replay are left out (reported as `pre_forward_us`), so the profile accounts for the same interval as `median_us`.
- `python -m vllm.benchmarks.forward.profile A.kernels.json [B.kernels.json]` prints one summary, or a per-kernel diff of two (e.g. before/after a change) sorted by the largest change.
- Nsight Systems: each case's 3 profiled replays always run between `cudaProfilerStart`/`Stop` in an NVTX range `forward/<case>`, so `nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --capture-range-end=repeat --cuda-graph-trace=node` records just them, one small report per case (and per rank with `torchrun --no-python nsys ...`). `--profile-dir` and nsys can't share CUPTI; combining them fails with a clear message.
- Timing runs before profiling, so reported latencies are unchanged; without a profiler the extra 3 replays per case are the only cost.

## Validation

```
pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py   # 4 passed (GB200): new summary unit test; the end-to-end test now also runs --profile-dir
```

Llama-3.2-1B, 1 GPU: profiled forward span vs timed median: decode 1291 vs 1265 us, prefill 4755 vs 4498 us, prefix hit 1782 vs 1770 us (profiler overhead; prefill's own sample spread was 1.75%). Decode excluded 512 restore copies per replay (~830 us), as intended.

Nsight Systems (2025.5), Llama-3.2-1B: one ~680 KB report per case; `nsys stats --report nvtx_sum` shows the `forward/<case>` range and `cuda_gpu_kern_sum` matches the JSON summary (48 calls = 16 layers x 3 replays). DP2 via `torchrun --no-python nsys`: one report per rank per case. `--profile-dir` under nsys: fails with the CUPTI message.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (1 GB200 node), ~100K KV: all 4 ranks wrote traces and summaries; span vs median: decode b32 15731 vs 15734 us, b128 20087 vs 19975 us, prefill 16K 204.2 vs ~202 ms. Example (prefill 16K, rank 0):

```
        us      %  calls  kernel
   62146.8  30.35     40  deep_gemm::sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_impl
   22000.9  10.74    131  kernel_cutlass_kernel_flashinfergemmkernelsdense_blockscaled_gemm_sm100Sm100BlockScaledPersistentDenseGemmKernel
   20274.8   9.90     40  fmhaSm100fKernel_QkvE4m3OBfloat16H512PagedKvDenseDynamicTokenSparseP1VarSeqQ64Kv128PersistentKeepsAbForGen
   19139.9   9.35      2  _engram_lookup_kernel
   10378.6   5.07     23  vllm::topKPerRowPrefill
```

## Details

- Each replay's GPU activities are split into the `len(state_views)` restore copies (one copy each), the rendezvous all-reduce (multi-rank), and the forward. The summary checks that the activities divide evenly into replays and raises otherwise.
- Kernel names are grouped without return type, template and function arguments (`void ns::foo<T>(...)` -> `ns::foo`); generic launchers keep their first template argument (`cutlass::device_kernel<Op>`), CuTe DSL names drop their per-shape suffix. Non-kernel activities (memcpy/memset) keep their names.
- `span_us` is first-to-last forward activity and should track `median_us`; `busy_us` sums kernel durations and can exceed it with multi-stream overlap.
- Why both: `torch.profiler` needs no extra tooling, is scoped per case in-process, and is tested in CI, so it backs the agent-facing JSON summary and diff. Nsight Systems adds NVTX, NCCL, CPU-side and GPU-metric views that many users reach for; the capture range makes it record only the benchmarked replays instead of the whole process (load, JIT, warmup, timing).
- The model-microbenchmark skill gets a short "Kernel breakdown" section on both workflows (including keeping `--capture-range-end=repeat`, since nsys's default stops after the first case and leaves the bench hanging).
- Size: `profile.py` ~200 lines plus ~40 lines of wiring; tests and docs ~60.

title: [Spec Decode] Remove Medusa and MLP speculator support
body:
## Overview

Removes Medusa and MLP speculator support and simplifies the code paths, configs, tests, docs, and CI rules that existed only for them. Net −858 lines, no new code.

## Claims

- `method="medusa"` and `method="mlp_speculator"` are removed. They are now rejected by `SpeculativeConfig` validation, which lists the valid methods.
- The MLP speculator was already dead code: its registry entry was commented out ("temporarily disabled") until V1 support, which never landed. Medusa is not supported by Model Runner V2, and EAGLE/MTP/DFlash/DSpark cover its use case.
- Other spec-decode methods are unchanged.

## Validation

- `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy, Buildkite/autolabel rule checks) passes.
- `pytest tests/models/test_registry.py tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py`: **504 passed, 11 skipped, 2 failed**. The 2 failures (`test_registry_imports[Dots3Note*]`) are unrelated: my local DeepGEMM build is older than the tag bump in #61491 (`cannot import name 'get_block_m_for_nvfp4_mega_moe'`).
- E2E smoke on the V1 model runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, GB200, 16 prompts, greedy, 128 tokens). Results are identical before and after:

| Method | drafts | accepted | mean accept len |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ngram (k=3) | 151 | 192 | 2.27 |
| eagle3 (k=3, yuhuili/EAGLE3-LLaMA3.1-Instruct-8B) | 1480 | 568 | 1.38 |

No model eval is needed: no surviving method's output changes.

## Details

Removed:
- `vllm/model_executor/models/{medusa,mlp_speculator}.py`, `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/{medusa,mlp_speculator}.py`, `vllm/v1/spec_decode/medusa.py`, and their registry and config-map entries.
- In `SpeculativeConfig`:
  - the `medusa`/`mlp_speculator` method literals and their auto-detection;
  - the old-format Medusa checkpoint workarounds (`model_type` hf_override injection and vocab-size patching);
  - the `mlp_speculator` draft-TP=1 override, including the now-unused `draft_hf_config` parameter of `_verify_and_get_draft_tp`;
  - the `hf_config.num_lookahead_tokens` sync (only Medusa/MLP speculator configs defined that attribute).
- The `MedusaProposer` branches in the V1 `gpu_model_runner.py`.
- The `T`/`T_co` generic on `VllmModel`/`VllmModelForTextGeneration`/`VllmModelForPooling`. It existed only for Medusa's `list[torch.Tensor]` hidden states; the default was already `torch.Tensor`, so typing for every other model is unchanged.
- `MedusaModelArchConfigConvertor`, plus the `check_head_size` escape hatch in `tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py`, which only existed for Medusa's zero head size.
- The Medusa e2e acceptance test, MLP docs page, MRV2-unsupported-method entries, Buildkite source deps, mergify/autolabel rules, and docs table rows.

Breaking change: users still passing `method="medusa"` or a Medusa/MLP-speculator draft checkpoint will get a config validation error.

Duplicate check: no open PR removes these. Draft #61357 migrates Medusa to the flat model layout; this PR would make it unnecessary.
