title: [Perf][Core] Skip the null head of sliding-window block tables
body:
## Purpose

A sliding-window KV group keeps one null block per out-of-window block, so a long request's block table is almost all null (8,183 of 8,192 entries for a 128K-token prompt with a 128-token window and 16-token blocks). `KVCacheBlocks.get_unhashed_block_ids_all_groups` and `SingleTypeKVCacheManager.free` walked every entry in Python. This PR skips that null head.

* `null_head_len()` finds the leading null run by binary search and checks it with one `list.count` of the shared null block. If the null blocks are not one contiguous head, it falls back to a scan.
* `get_unhashed_block_ids_all_groups` and `pop_blocks_for_free` (so both `free` and the deferred-free path) start after the head. `free_blocks` skips any other null blocks; the null block's `ref_cnt` is not maintained (see `BlockPool.__init__`).
* No behavior change: the same block ids are collected, and the same blocks reach the free queue in the same order.

Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs for `null block sliding window free`, `null_block free_blocks`, `sliding window null blocks` and `get_unhashed_block_ids`. vllm-project/vllm#42276 and #55818 change SWA eviction and allocation, not these walks.

## Where it matters

The cost is paid per sliding-window group, on the scheduler's critical path, each time a request is admitted with async KV loads or freed. It shows up when GPU steps are short and requests turn over quickly, as in **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, WideEP DEP16 decode** (GB300, 64 requests/rank, 169.5K-token prompts):

* A decode step takes ~22 ms on the GPU, and all 16 DP ranks wait for the slowest rank's scheduler.
* Each rank admits and frees ~9 long requests per second.
* Each request has 8 sliding-window groups x 5,298 blocks, 5,292 of them null.

| Scheduler CPU per request | main | PR |
| -- | --: | --: |
| free | 2.0 ms | 0.5 ms |
| async-KV admission (135K prompt) | 0.73 ms | 0.47 ms |

End to end, output throughput went from 8,892 to 9,025 tok/s/GPU **(+1.5%).** 

## Microbenchmark

One request on one sliding-window group (window 128, block size 16): `KVCacheBlocks.get_unhashed_block_ids_all_groups` (collect) and `SlidingWindowManager.free` (free). Median of 300 calls on a Grace CPU, main (`8530aed2b7`) vs this PR, consistent across two runs.

| Prompt tokens | Blocks (null) | Collect, main / PR (us) | Free, main / PR (us) |
| -- | -- | --: | --: |
| 32K | 2,048 (2,039) | 54.1 / 9.7 | 92.9 / 10.8 |
| 128K | 8,192 (8,183) | 214.9 / 34.8 | 370.6 / 35.8 |
| 512K | 32,768 (32,759) | 867.5 / 135.9 | 1471.7 / 137.5 |

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

New test `test_null_head_len`: empty, no-null, all-null, contiguous-head and non-contiguous tables, plus `get_unhashed_block_ids_all_groups` on two groups.

## Test Result

312 passed. Pre-commit (ruff, format, typos, mypy) passes.

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write and benchmark this change.

title: [CI] Use an ungated model as the attention test config default
body:
## Overview

`create_vllm_config()` in `tests/v1/attention/utils.py` defaults to the gated `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B`, so every test that relies on the default fails on agents and machines without access to that repo. As suggested in #61416, this defaults it to `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, the default model of `vllm serve`, and switches the explicit Llama-3-8B uses in `tests/v1/attention/` to it as well.

## Claims

- Tests that build their config through the default, and the attention tests that named Llama-3-8B, no longer need access to the meta-llama repo.
- Results do not change for the CUDA tests that use the default or the replaced model.

## Validation

On SM80 with FlashInfer 0.7.1 and an offline HF cache, `main` against `main` + this PR, for every CUDA test file that uses the default or the replaced model:

| Test file | `main` and this PR |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py` | 88 passed, 60 failed, 10 skipped |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py` | 30 passed, 1 failed |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_dcp_spec_reorder.py` | 1 passed |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_mm_prefix.py` | 13 passed, 22 skipped |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py` | 32 passed, 1 skipped |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_linear_attention_metadata_builder.py` | 4 passed |
| `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py` | 111 passed, 60 skipped |

The failing tests are the same on both sides and fail for reasons unrelated to the model: FP8 KV caches the Triton backend rejects below SM89, and FlashMLA not being built for SM80. The ROCm test files that use the default were not run.

## Details

Llama-3-8B stays where a test is about that model itself (`tests/test_config.py`, `tests/models/registry.py`) and in the spec decode test that uses the Instruct variant.

title: [Bugfix] Honor OPT token embedding width for prompt embeddings
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61709. Use OPT's token embedding width for prompt embedding validation and runner buffers so `facebook/opt-350m` works with `--enable-prompt-embeds`.

## Claims

- Accept OPT-350m's 512-wide prompt embeddings and reject its incompatible 1024-wide hidden states.
- Allocate 512-wide input buffers for both model runners, matching `embed_input_ids()` and the decoder's `project_in` input.
- Preserve CLIP/SigLIP text embedding validation when their projection width differs from their hidden size.

## Validation

Review follow-up: CI scripts are unchanged. OPT-350m retains GPU generation coverage and is omitted from the offline CPU model matrix, whose cache lacks its weights; existing OPT-125m CPU coverage remains. The completion-renderer mock exposes the text config, and tokenizer setup uses the existing bounded retry helper. Follow-up checks: 57 renderer/width tests passed; both OPT-350m GPU cases remain selected, and neither is selected by `-m cpu_model`. Earlier CI-fix validation also passed 148 renderer/validation tests and 12 GPT-J streaming tests (4 skipped).



Tested in WSL on an RTX 3050 (8 GiB), Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132, and Transformers 5.19.0. **202 pytest cases passed**, plus live HTTP and baseline reproduction checks.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original OPT-350m config and validation | 512-wide inputs rejected; incompatible 1024-wide inputs accepted; buffer width 1024 |
| Fixed OPT-350m config and validation | 512-wide inputs accepted; 1024-wide inputs rejected; buffer width 512 |
| Prompt payload, sparse tensor, and completion validation | 113 passed |
| Chat prompt embedding parsing and GPU overlay kernels | 85 passed |
| OPT-350m generation evaluation, V2 runner | 2 passed, prompt embeddings enabled/disabled |
| OPT-350m generation evaluation, legacy runner | 2 passed, prompt embeddings enabled/disabled |
| Live HTTP completions | Single/batched embeddings match token-ID generation; streaming matches; wrong width returns 400; server remains healthy |
| Pre-commit hooks and whitespace | Passed, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX, and test CI tethering |

Generation evaluations use the existing Hugging Face/vLLM greedy generation and top-5 log-probability comparison over 32 generated tokens. With prompt embeddings enabled, they also compare token-ID and embedding generation. Both runners were tested with compilation/CUDA graphs; HTTP validation additionally exercised eager mode and chunked prefill.

<details>
<summary>Test commands and local configuration</summary>

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/renderers/test_prompt_embeds_payload_validation.py \
  tests/renderers/test_sparse_tensor_validation.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_prompt_validation.py \
  -k 'not empty_prompt and not out_of_vocab' --tb=short -q

PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/renderers/chat_utils/test_prompt_embeds.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_prompt_embeds_state.py --tb=short -q

PYTHONPATH=. VLLM_PLUGINS= .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/language/generation/test_common.py -k opt-350m --tb=short -xv

PYTHONPATH=. VLLM_PLUGINS= VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 \
  VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/language/generation/test_common.py -k opt-350m --tb=short -xv

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only HEAD^ HEAD)
git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD
```

For the local 8 GiB GPU, a pytest plugin set `VllmRunner` defaults to `gpu_memory_utilization=0.65`, `attention_config={"backend": "TRITON_ATTN"}`, and `max_num_batched_tokens=1024`; the evaluation commands above require equivalent overrides on similarly constrained GPUs. Legacy runner testing used the supported PyTorch sampler because FlashInfer sampling warmup requires `nvcc`, which is absent from this WSL environment. Compiled libraries and the wheel-supplied FlashMLA interface were reused from the existing installation. No CUDA/C++ sources changed.

The HTTP server used `--enable-prompt-embeds --dtype float16 --enforce-eager --gpu-memory-utilization 0.65 --max-model-len 128 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 16 --enable-chunked-prefill --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN`.

</details>

## Details

OPT-350m embeds tokens at `word_embed_proj_dim=512`, then projects them to `hidden_size=1024` inside the decoder. Buffer allocation and request validation previously used 1024, causing startup/input-copy failures and accepting embeddings that `project_in` cannot consume.

Add `word_embed_proj_dim` to the input-buffer size lookup and use it for request validation when present. Validation otherwise retains `get_hidden_size()`: using the buffer accessor wholesale would change CLIP/SigLIP validation to their projection width. Both runners share the corrected buffer accessor; no runner-specific branches or inference synchronization are added.

Regression coverage extends existing suites with actual OPT-350m/OPT-125m/CLIP/SigLIP configurations and adds OPT-350m to the model registry and generation comparison matrix. Duplicate searches for `61709 in:body` and `word_embed_proj_dim` found no open PR addressing this fix.

title: [CI] Pin DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 eval to its FP8-Engram revision
body:
## Overview

Pin `tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4-DSpark-TP4.yaml` to HF revision `3431dde3` of `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4`, the last revision before the checkpoint stored its Engram tables as MXFP4. This is a stopgap until #61530 adds MXFP4 Engram support; revert the pin when #61530 merges.

## Claims

- `(B200) LM Eval Spec Decode` stops failing at weight loading with `AssertionError: engram shard (…, 128) does not fit param (…, 256)`. Example on the v0.32.0 release branch: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94968. Main's last pass (94756, 10:00Z Oct 14) predates the checkpoint change, so main fails the same way on its next run.
- CI only. No vLLM code changes.

## Validation

- `config.json` at the pinned revision has no `engram_embed_*` fields, which is the FP8 Engram layout the current loader expects. Revision `main` has `engram_embed_quant: mxfp4`, `engram_embed_block_size: 32`, `engram_embed_scale_dtype: ue8m0` and `engram_embed_layers: [1, 14]`.
- `--revision <sha>` in `server_args` is already used by `DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8-TP1-PCP2-ROCm.yaml`, and the YAML still parses.
- Not run: the full 4xB200 GSM8K eval. 4-GPU B200 capacity is scarce right now, and this step's CI run on this PR is the end-to-end check.

## Details

**What changed upstream.** At 16:40Z on Oct 14, HF PR #2 on `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4` ("Store Engram lookup tables as MXFP4", commit `c48dca0146`) merged. It rewrote shards 47 and 48 and `config.json`, and the checkpoint shrank from about 491 GiB to about 400 GiB. vLLM support for that format is #61530, which is still in review. Every vLLM version without #61530 fails on the current `main` revision. This PR only keeps CI testing the format vLLM currently supports.

**Tokenizer and remote code.** HF PR #2 touched only shards 47/48, `config.json` and the README, so the tokenizer and `trust_remote_code` files are identical at both revisions.

**Release branch.** This also needs a cherry-pick to `releases/v0.32.0` if v0.32.0 ships without #61530.

Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs for this checkpoint and for revision pins and found nothing.

title: [Perf] Low-latency CPU all-reduce for DP metadata syncs
body:
This is a refactored version of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60267 from @hjjq.

Main changes from that PR:
- Move out of MRV2 since it's a generic collective, make compatible with elastic ep
- Don't use `batch_isend_irecv` which is actually slower with gloo
- Generalize to any DP size (not just power of 2)
- Also use for the post-step DP state sync
- Remove the env var, just use it unconditionally

---

Gloo's all_reduce on the small CPU tensors used for DP synchronization is latency-bound and grows roughly linearly with the DP size. Add `cpu_all_reduce_()` to `vllm.distributed.utils`: recursive doubling within power-of-two blocks of ranks, then one concurrent exchange between blocks, so any group size completes in log2(largest power-of-two factor) + 1 rounds. Block sums are added in a fixed order, so results are bitwise identical across ranks.

It calls `ProcessGroup.send/recv` with group-local ranks, so it also works with stateless (unregistered) groups such as the engine-core DP group and elastic EP's DP group.

It is used automatically (no env var) for:
- the V2 worker's DP padding/cudagraph sync, via `GroupCoordinator.cpu_all_reduce_()`
- the engine-core DP state sync, `ParallelConfig.sync_dp_state()`

### Performance

Standalone microbenchmark: p50 latency (µs) of an in-place SUM all-reduce of a 6×N int32 CPU tensor (the V2 DP metadata shape) over gloo, one process per rank, on GB200 nodes with gloo over the nodes' Ethernet NIC. Each method was run for 5,000 calls, interleaved in random order; the value is the median across ranks of per-rank p50.

- **gloo**: `dist.all_reduce` (current main)
- **#60267**: the original PR (`VLLM_DP_METADATA_TRANSPORT=gloo-tree`); power-of-two sizes only
- **this PR**: `cpu_all_reduce_`

| nodes | ranks | gloo | #60267 | this PR | speedup vs gloo |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 2 | 161 | 121 | **99** | 1.6× |
| 1 | 3 | 326 | n/a | **175** | 1.9× |
| 1 | 4 | 780 | 265 | **224** | 3.5× |
| 1 | 5 | 566 | n/a | **266** | 2.1× |
| 1 | 6 | 695 | n/a | **252** | 2.8× |
| 1 | 7 | 850 | n/a | **365** | 2.3× |
| 1 | 8 | 1690 | 377 | **326** | 5.2× |
| 1 | 9 | 1094 | n/a | **459** | 2.4× |
| 1 | 11 | 2379 | n/a | **695** | 3.4× |
| 1 | 12 | 2749 | n/a | **400** | 6.9× |
| 1 | 15 | 3920 | n/a | **1042** | 3.8× |
| 2 | 2 | 308 | 146 | **129** | 2.4× |
| 2 | 4 | 845 | 271 | **234** | 3.6× |
| 2 | 6 | 1366 | n/a | **344** | 4.0× |
| 2 | 8 | 1977 | 413 | **362** | 5.5× |
| 2 | 10 | 2563 | n/a | **444** | 5.8× |
| 2 | 12 | 3005 | n/a | **536** | 5.6× |
| 4 | 4 | 1114 | 281 | **267** | 4.2× |
| 4 | 8 | 2560 | 459 | **409** | 6.3× |
| 4 | 12 | 3806 | n/a | **482** | 7.9× |
| 4 | 16 | 5354 | 604 | **546** | 9.8× |

Where #60267 applies (power-of-two sizes), this PR has 5–18% lower latency. Gloo's latency grows roughly linearly with the number of ranks, while this PR adds about one round per doubling plus one round for the odd factor.

Correctness: `tests/distributed/test_cpu_all_reduce.py` (sizes 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12; exact match vs `dist.all_reduce`, bitwise-identical float results across ranks, and a stateless process group). `tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py` with DP=4 passes with the multiprocessing backend (ray backend not tested).

title: [Perf][MoE] Skip the TRTLLM fp8-block activation-scale transpose copy
body:
## Overview

Skip the per-layer `a1q_scale.t().contiguous()` copy between per-token-group FP8 quantization and the FlashInfer TRTLLM fp8-block MoE experts by emitting the scales in the layout the experts consume. This is pure plumbing on top of the quant kernel's existing `column_major_scales` mode — no kernel changes. ~2% TPOT improvement at concurrency 4 on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (TP4+EP).

## Claims

- Removes one `direct_copy_kernel` per MoE layer per decode step (24/step -> 0 on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) from the critical path.
- ~2% TPOT p50 improvement at concurrency 4 on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP4+EP on 4xGB300; parity at concurrency 1 (details below).
- Bitwise-identical expert inputs: the scale bytes are the same values, just allocated in the final physical layout, so there is no accuracy impact.
- Python-only change (+77/-14 across 5 files, mostly the test).

## Validation

### Correctness

- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer.py`: 49 passed (+2 mxfp8 skips), including the new `transposed` arm of `test_trtllm_fp8_block_moe_deferred_finalize`, which builds the quant config through the production oracle + `no_dp_ep` path, asserts the prepared activation scale is column-major (`a1q_scale.t().is_contiguous()`), and asserts bitwise-equal expert output against the non-transposed baseline.
- No new test for the `column_major_scales` wrapper mode itself: it is a pre-existing feature already exercised by the CUTLASS/DeepGEMM/FlashInfer/PyTorch scaled-mm kernels on every CUDA run and by existing fusion/eplb tests.

### Profiler evidence

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP4+EP, decode step trace:

| | main | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `per_token_group_quant` launches / step | 24 | 24 |
| `direct_copy_kernel` launches / step | 24 | 0 |

### E2E perf

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP4+EP on 4xGB300, `vllm bench serve`, 2048 input / 256 output, `--ignore-eos`. main (`f46021a7fa`) and the branch (`9f75804588`) ran sequentially on the same node, two server instances each:

| Concurrency | main TPOT p50 (ms) | this PR TPOT p50 (ms) | Change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 3.92-3.93 | parity (see below) | ~0% |
| 4 | 5.11-5.12 | 4.98-5.00 | -2.3% |

TPOT p99 at concurrency 4 improves from 5.67-6.04 ms to 5.57-5.58 ms. Concurrency-1 serve numbers were noisy across instances, so c=1 was A/B'd with interleaved `vllm bench latency` (bs=1, 2048/128): 0.756/0.704 s (this PR) vs 0.756/0.800 s (main) — no regression, as expected since the eliminated copies are nearly free inside a bs=1 CUDA graph.

## Details

- Root cause: the TRTLLM fp8-block kernels consume activation scales in the physical `[K/128, M]` (scale-major) layout, while the MoE per-token-group quant emits `[M, K/128]` row-major, so every layer paid a transpose copy between the quant kernel and the experts.
- The quant kernel's existing `column_major_scales=True` mode already allocates the scale buffer as a contiguous `[G, M]` tensor viewed as `[M, G]`, so on that buffer the experts' `.t().contiguous()` is a no-op returning the same tensor. The change just threads a new `FusedMoEQuantConfig.is_scale_transposed` flag — set by the fp8 oracle only for `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` + `[128, 128]` blocks — through `no_dp_ep` into `moe_kernel_quantize_input`. TRTLLM expert code is unchanged.
- Scope: only `no_dp_ep` forwards the flag; dispatch-based paths (deepep, naive-dp, fi-nvl) keep row-major scales since their scales cross an all2all dispatch. Other MoE backends are unaffected.
- No accuracy eval: the scale bytes handed to the experts are bitwise-identical (same values, different physical layout), so outputs cannot change; the e2e runs above exercised the modified path at c=1-4.
- Duplicate-work check: nearest open PRs inspected — #59564 (value-only amax reduction inside the quant kernel, orthogonal), #53345 (deepep ep_scatter scale-stride bugfix), #44034 (XPU quant fallback); none touch the MoE activation-scale layout.

AI assistance: Kimi Code helped develop, benchmark, and validate this change.

title: [CPU] Keep the hybrid block size across the engine core's config rerun
body:
## Overview

On the CPU platform, prefix caching never hits for hybrid (Mamba / GDN) models when a prompt's prefill fits in one chunk: the block size the workers raise to fit the Mamba state pages is reset to the CPU default in the engine core, so Mamba prefill checkpoints are aligned to 128 tokens instead of the block size.

## Claims

- A repeated prompt on a hybrid model hits every full block on the CPU platform (Qwen3.5-0.8B: 640 of 960 tokens, previously 0), with one or more ranks.
- The CPU default block size (128, or what the attention backends prefer, e.g. 16 for CPU MLA) is applied in `update_block_size_for_backend()`, as on the other platforms, instead of in `check_and_update_config()`.

## Validation

Real forward, dummy weights, CPU build (x86, AVX-512), `max_num_batched_tokens` large enough for one prefill chunk, prompt of 4.5 blocks, sent twice:

| | TP=1 | TP=2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | hits `[0, 0]` | hits `[0, 0]` |
| this PR | hits `[0, 2560]` | hits `[0, 2560]` |

New test `test_prefix_cache_hit_reaches_last_full_block` in `tests/v1/e2e/test_cpu_linear_attn_chunked_prefix.py` (run by the CPU CI's `cpu_model` job): fails on main with `assert [0, 0] == [0, 640]`, passes with this PR.

```bash
pytest tests/platforms/test_cpu.py tests/v1/e2e/test_cpu_linear_attn_chunked_prefix.py tests/v1/e2e/test_cpu_spec_decode.py tests/quantization/test_cpu_w8a8.py
# 22 passed; test_v2_speculator_smoke[eagle3] fails on main too here (gated model repo, no access)
```

Block sizes resolve as on main: Qwen3-0.6B 128; DeepSeek-V2-Lite 128 with AMX MLA and 16 with the reference CPU MLA backend.

## Details

**Root cause.** `CpuPlatform.check_and_update_config()` set the default block size whenever it was not user-specified:

1. The workers build the model and `update_block_size_for_backend()` raises the block size so an attention page fits a Mamba state page (640 tokens for Qwen3.5-0.8B).
2. The engine core takes that size from the KV cache groups.
3. After its handshake the engine core reruns `VllmConfig.__post_init__()`, which reruns `check_and_update_config()` and resets `cache_config.block_size` to 128. The scheduler and KV cache manager keep 640.
4. In `align` Mamba cache mode, `Scheduler._mamba_block_aligned_split()` reads `cache_config.block_size`, so it ends the prefill at the last 128-token boundary instead of the last 640-token one, and no Mamba state is cached at a block boundary. The next request finds full-attention hits but no Mamba hit, so the hybrid hit is 0.

When a prefill spans several chunks, a chunk boundary can land on a block boundary by chance, which is why `test_prefix_cache_hit_matches_cold_cache` (which asserts `num_cached_tokens > 0` without forcing one chunk) did not catch it.

**Fix.** Other platforms set the default block size in `update_block_size_for_backend()`, which runs once after the model is built; the CPU platform now does the same, taking the backends' preferred size for 128 (`_preferred_block_size_for_backends`). `check_and_update_config()` keeps only what is idempotent: the sizes CPU MLA and DeepSeek-V4 force, and the multiple-of-32 warning for a user-specified size.

**Found while** running vLLM's simulated execution (#61506) on the CPU platform; this fix is independent of it.

title: [Bugfix] Fix Apertus streaming scientific notation
body:
## Overview

Fix corrupted scientific-notation arguments in Apertus streaming tool calls.

## Details

The parser could emit incomplete numbers before receiving their exponents. Since streamed arguments cannot be retracted, a value such as `-2e-3` could produce invalid arguments like `-20.002`.

Exclude `Allow.NUM` during incremental parsing to avoid emitting incomplete numeric values. Final parsing and incremental string streaming remain unchanged.

Numbers may be delayed until a terminating delimiter arrives.

## Validation

Added three regression cases covering positive and negative exponents, including numbers inside arrays.

- Before: **3 failed**.
- After: **22 passed** in the Apertus parser suite.
- All applicable pre-commit checks passed, including Ruff, mypy, and test coverage checks.

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \

title: [ROCm][DSv4] Overlap the unfused shared expert with AITER MegaMoE
body:
## Overview

With `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe` and an unfused shared expert, DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm ran the shared expert after the router and MegaMoE, on the main stream. This PR runs it on the aux stream next to the router + MegaMoE through `maybe_execute_in_parallel`. It follows the existing `VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM` / `VLLM_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM_TOKEN_THRESHOLD` convention: the overlap applies to steps of at most 256 tokens by default, and `VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM=1` keeps the serial order. ATOM overlaps its shared expert with the routed experts the same way.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4-Pro, AgentX agentic workload: P90 interactivity +2.7% at concurrency 128 and +6.4% at concurrency 64.
- No accuracy change on gsm8k.
- Prefill-sized steps and the fused shared-expert path are unchanged.

## Validation

Setup:
- DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 8x MI355X, DP8 attention + EP8 AITER MegaMoE, shared expert unfused.
- AgentX agentic workload, 1200 s runs, requests counted in the 300-1200 s window.
- Single runs per configuration.

| | Without | With this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| c128 (same node, same job): P90 interactivity (tok/s/user) | 27.13 | 27.87 (+2.7%) |
| c128: output tok/s/GPU | 335 | 346 (+3.3%) |
| c128: total tok/s/GPU | | +1.4% |
| c64 (same node, separate jobs): P90 interactivity | 48.26 | 51.33 (+6.4%) |
| c64: P50 interactivity | 61.65 | 64.31 (+4.3%) |
| c64: total tok/s/GPU | | -1.5% |
| gsm8k 5-shot, real speculative decoding (flexible / strict) | 0.9697 / 0.9704 | 0.9727 / 0.9735 |

Unit tests and lint:
- `pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_aiter_mega_moe.py` on MI355X: 10 passed, against 6 on main. The 4 new cases run the shared expert on the aux stream.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks passed, mypy included. This was rerun on the current main, which includes #61262.

## Details

- When MegaMoE fuses the shared expert, `shared_experts` is `None` and the routed path runs alone, as before.
- `maybe_execute_in_parallel` falls back to sequential execution when the stream is `None` and during breakable CUDA graph capture.
- #61262's runtime selection runs inside the MegaMoE call on the main stream, so it is not affected.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR.

title: [BugFix][MyPy] Guard Linux-only mmap/fadvise calls with sys.platform
body:
## Purpose

`mmap.MADV_HUGEPAGE`, `os.posix_fadvise` and `os.POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED` are
Linux-only. On macOS, mypy fails with:

```text
vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py:923: error: Module has no attribute "posix_fadvise"  [attr-defined]
vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py:923: error: Module has no attribute "POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED"  [attr-defined]
vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py:911: error: Module has no attribute "MADV_HUGEPAGE"  [attr-defined]
```

At runtime the same lines raise `AttributeError`, which the surrounding
`except OSError` does not catch.

This PR adds a `sys.platform != "linux"` early return so that non-Linux
platforms take the existing fallbacks:

- `_allocate_huge_page_storage` returns `None`, so the caller falls back to
  pinned memory.
- `drop_checkpoint_cache` skips page-cache eviction.

mypy understands `sys.platform` checks, so the Linux-only code is no longer
type-checked on macOS. This follows the same approach as #41465.

Both call sites were introduced in #56926.

## Duplicate check

I searched open PRs for `posix_fadvise`, `MADV_HUGEPAGE` and `mypy sys.platform`.
None of the open PRs guards these calls or fixes the macOS mypy errors.

## Test Plan

On macOS (darwin, arm64):

```bash
pre-commit run mypy --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py
```

## Test Result

- Before: mypy reports the 3 `attr-defined` errors above.
- After: `Success: no issues found in 2 source files`. All other pre-commit
  hooks pass.

There is no behavior change on Linux, so model evaluation is not applicable.

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance. A human submitter reviewed every
changed line and ran the commands above.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Honor a prompt-closed reasoning block in non-streaming parse and reasoning token counts
body:
## Overview

With GLM-5.3 and `continue_final_message`, non-streaming Chat Completions return the continued answer as `reasoning` with `content: null`, and both streaming and non-streaming count every generated token as a reasoning token. This PR makes non-streaming parsing and `count_reasoning_tokens()` honor a prompt that already closes reasoning, as streaming `parse_delta()` already does.

## Design

Thanks to @bbrowning for catching that an earlier version leaked multi-turn reasoning into `content` for legacy parsers like `deepseek_r1`, and for suggesting moving the fix onto `ParserEngine`. This version follows his outline:

- `ParserEngine.set_prompt_token_ids()` uses the engine's turn-aware `is_reasoning_end` to start the parse in `CONTENT` when the prompt already closes reasoning. The engine's reasoning token count uses the same starting state.
- `ReasoningParser` gets a no-op `set_prompt_token_ids()`, so legacy reasoning parsers behave exactly as on `main`. `ParserEngineReasoningAdapter` and `DelegatingParser` pass the prompt through.
- The engine only uses the prompt when its config starts in `REASONING` and declares `turn_boundary_tokens`; without turn boundaries, a previous turn's `</think>` would count as closing reasoning in the new turn.

## Claims

- Non-streaming returns the continuation as `content` instead of `reasoning` when the prompt already closes reasoning.
- `reasoning_tokens` is 0 in that case, on both streaming and non-streaming. Before, it was the whole output (17 tokens in the example below).
- Normal reasoning turns are unchanged, and a previous turn's `</think>` doesn't count as closing reasoning in the new turn.

## Validation

**Dummy Reproduction** (CPU only) parser level:

```python
from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
from vllm.parser.parser_manager import ParserManager
from vllm.tokenizers import get_tokenizer

tok = get_tokenizer("zai-org/GLM-5.3")
msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": "Count from 1 to 10 separated by commas."},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": "1, 2, 3, 4,"}]
prompt = tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=False,
                                 continue_final_message=True)
prompt_ids = tok.encode(prompt, add_special_tokens=False)
out = " 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10"
out_ids = tok.encode(out, add_special_tokens=False)
req = ChatCompletionRequest(model="m", messages=msgs, add_generation_prompt=False,
                            continue_final_message=True)
parser_cls = ParserManager.get_parser(tool_parser_name="glm47", reasoning_parser_name="glm45",
                                      enable_auto_tools=True, tokenizer=tok)
print("prompt tail :", repr(prompt[-44:]))
print("model output:", repr(out))

# non-streaming, as chat_completion/serving.py does it
p = parser_cls(tok, None, chat_template_kwargs={}, model_config=None)
p.set_prompt_token_ids(prompt_ids)
reasoning, content, _ = p.parse(out, req, enable_auto_tools=True, model_output_token_ids=out_ids)
print(f"non-stream  reasoning={reasoning!r}  content={content!r}  "
      f"reasoning_tokens={p.count_reasoning_tokens(out_ids)}")

# streaming, one token at a time
p = parser_cls(tok, None, chat_template_kwargs={}, model_config=None)
r = c = ""
for i, t in enumerate(out_ids):
    d = p.parse_delta(tok.decode([t]), [t], req, prompt_token_ids=prompt_ids,
                      finished=i == len(out_ids) - 1)
    if d:
        r += d.reasoning or ""
        c += d.content or ""
print(f"stream      reasoning={(r or None)!r}  content={(c or None)!r}  "
      f"reasoning_tokens={p.count_reasoning_tokens(out_ids)}")
```

**Before** (`main` at `3dcfaeb4e8`, this branch's base):

```
prompt tail : 'mmas.<|assistant|><think></think>1, 2, 3, 4,'
model output: ' 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10'
non-stream  reasoning=' 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10'  content=None  reasoning_tokens=17
stream      reasoning=None  content=' 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10'  reasoning_tokens=17
```

**After** (this PR):

```
prompt tail : 'mmas.<|assistant|><think></think>1, 2, 3, 4,'
model output: ' 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10'
non-stream  reasoning=None  content=' 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10'  reasoning_tokens=0
stream      reasoning=None  content=' 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10'  reasoning_tokens=0
```

The "before" output matches what we saw in production on GLM-5.3: the API returned the continuation in `reasoning_content` with `content: null` and `reasoning_tokens: 17`.

Claude Code used to build up the test cases and validate the logic.

title: [Perf] Kimi K3 Specialized Decode: CuTeDSL Optimized GB300 (1.5-2x)
body:
## Overview (this PR description was manually written by me) This is an NVIDIA-developed specialized implementation of Kimi K3 for GB300 that achieves 1.5-2x decode speedups. It supports: - TP8 and TP16 on GB300 - NoSpec (up to B64) and DSpark verification with 3-7 draft tokens (up to 64 tokens -- B8 for DL7, B16 for DL3) - Decode context parallelism with DCP=TP (DCP-off also supported) It is enabled opt-in via `--additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}'`. All changes are localized to `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/`. ## Claims With FP8 KV Cache, FP32 SSM Cache, and model-provider weights: - TP16, ISL 1, no speculation: decode step **1.79-1.92x faster than stock at B1-B8** (3.90 vs 7.38 ms at B1). - TP16, DSpark DL7, synthetic acceptance 6: **1.53-1.71x decode tok/s at B1-B8**. - DL7, ISL 32k, DCP on: **1.36-1.50x (TP8)** and **1.53-1.75x (TP16)** decode tok/s. - AIME25, GPQA-Diamond and MRCR v2 8-needle match stock within about one standard error, with and without speculation. ## Validation ### Correctness Testing Evals for this branch ran with DCP = TP (TP8+DCP8 and TP16+DCP16); stock ran on TP8 without DCP, C2 and C8 pooled. Spec on = DSpark DL7 with probabilistic drafting and standard rejection sampling (no forced acceptance). Score ± standard error, n samples per cell; pooling ours' C2 and C8 cells gives AIME25 avg@4, GPQA-Diamond avg@2, GSM8k avg@2. MRCR v2: 8-needle, (128k, 256k] contexts, thinking on, 32k output cap. | Task | Spec | Stock TP8 | Ours TP8+DCP8 C2 | Ours TP8+DCP8 C8 | Ours TP16+DCP16 C2 | Ours TP16+DCP16 C8 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | AIME25 | off | 0.867 ± 0.033 (n=120) | 0.867 ± 0.048 | 0.917 ± 0.035 | 0.900 ± 0.037 | 0.900 ± 0.037 | | AIME25 | DL7 | 0.892 ± 0.032 (n=120) | 0.917 ± 0.042 | 0.900 ± 0.037 | 0.883 ± 0.052 | 0.950 ± 0.037 | | GPQA-D | off | 0.924 ± 0.011 (n=594) | 0.919 ± 0.019 | 0.914 ± 0.020 | 0.919 ± 0.019 | 0.929 ± 0.018 | | GPQA-D | DL7 | 0.916 ± 0.011 (n=594) | 0.939 ± 0.017 | 0.929 ± 0.018 | 0.919 ± 0.019 | 0.955 ± 0.015 | | GSM8k | off | 0.867 ± 0.009 (n=1319) | 0.856 ± 0.010 | 0.860 ± 0.010 | 0.864 ± 0.009 | 0.873 ± 0.009 | | GSM8k | DL7 | 0.863 ± 0.005 (n=5276) | 0.853 ± 0.010 | 0.854 ± 0.010 | 0.868 ± 0.009 | 0.865 ± 0.009 | | MRCR v2 | off | 0.282 ± 0.039 (n=100) | 0.334 ± 0.042 | 0.226 ± 0.036 | – | – | | MRCR v2 | DL7 | 0.343 ± 0.042 (n=100) | 0.339 ± 0.042 | 0.320 ± 0.042 | – | – | Sample counts: AIME25 n=60, GPQA-D n=198, GSM8k n=1319, MRCR n=100. Single MRCR runs swing by ~0.1 between repeats; a larger TP8 C8 matrix ({ours, stock} x {DCP on, off} x {spec off, DL7}, 750–900 samples per build) gives **0.296 (ours) vs 0.290 (stock)**.
Numerical validation and the MRCR output-length study - **Greedy logprobs, spec vs no-spec on the same build** (up to and including the first divergence): TP8 drift ≤ 0.50 vs stock's own 0.38, divergences only at near-ties (top-1/top-2 margin ≤ 0.50); TP8+DCP8 (~8k context) drift ≤ 0.38, margins ≤ 0.375, inside stock's B1-vs-B4 noise of 0.875. :heavy_check_mark: - **Greedy probes at 128k–256k context vs stock** (32 MRCR prompts, 4096 tokens, top-10 logprobs): every divergence is at an exact BF16 top-1/top-2 tie; ours-vs-stock |Δ logprob| (0.007–0.009, first divergence ~step 50–80) matches stock DCP-on vs DCP-off (0.014, ~59); no growth with position. Same with DL7. :heavy_check_mark: - **Per-step error vs a 1-ulp noise floor** (stock re-run with 1-ulp-perturbed embeddings on the same state), out to 245k context with and without DCP: KL, top-1 agreement, hidden-state, KDA-state and KV differences all equal the floor; accumulated drift over 1536 consecutive decodes equals the accumulated floor. Prefill is bit-identical to stock. :heavy_check_mark: - **Decode vs prefill rescoring** (CUDA graphs, sampling, 8192 tokens; the same server then rescores the text via prefill logprobs): per-token decode-minus-prefill logprob, stratified by confidence, is identical to stock's in all configs and flat with depth. :heavy_check_mark: - **Output length:** At low cap (32k), we see many truncations and slightly more for ours than baseline. This remains unclear, as there is very high variance and the mean OSL at 32k is a bit higher. With a 64k cap (100 samples per config), we see very few truncations and mean output length is comparable. : | build | config | mean | std | capped at 64k | |---|---|---|---|---| | ours | DCP, spec off | 8757 | 13515 | 3 | | ours | DCP, DL7 | 7540 | 12612 | 2 | | ours | no DCP, spec off | 6987 | 9577 | 0 | | ours | no DCP, DL7 | 11891 | 19250 | 9 | | stock | DCP, spec off | 9458 | 12858 | 1 | | stock | DCP, DL7 | 10634 | 16039 | 5 | | stock | no DCP, spec off | 9083 | 14634 | 4 | | stock | no DCP, DL7 | 10526 | 16881 | 5 |
### Performance Validation **TP16, no speculation, ISL 1, OSL 1024, greedy.** Decode step = median ITL at exactly B running requests (prefill excluded), cross-checked against nsys graph-replay time. 3 runs x 4 prompts per B. | | B1 | B2 | B4 | B8 | |---|---|---|---|---| | ours, step ms | 3.90 | 4.58 | 5.75 | 6.82 | | stock, step ms | 7.38 | 8.79 | 10.33 | 12.19 | | **speedup** | **1.89x** | **1.92x** | **1.80x** | **1.79x** | | decode tok/s, ours / stock | 255 / 135 | 439 / 227 | 695 / 387 | 1156 / 649 | **TP16, DSpark DL7, synthetic acceptance length 6, ISL 1.** Decode tok/s = decode steps/s x acceptance length x B. | | B1 (M8) | B2 (M16) | B4 (M32) | B8 (M64) | |---|---|---|---|---| | ours | 838 | 1361 | 2091 | 3094 | | stock | 489 | 847 | 1366 | 2014 | | **speedup** | **1.71x** | **1.61x** | **1.53x** | **1.54x** | **DSpark DL7, synthetic acceptance 3.78, ISL 32k (SPEED-Bench mixed prompts), DCP on.** Stock baseline with `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --dcp-comm-backend a2a --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`, same for ours. Decode tok/s excludes prefill; output tok/s and TPOT include the other requests' 16k prefill chunks, so their gains are smaller. TTFT is at parity. | B | TP8+DCP8 decode tok/s, ours / stock | output tok/s | TPOT ms, ours / stock | TP16+DCP16 decode tok/s, ours / stock | output tok/s | TPOT ms, ours / stock | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 374 / 249 (**1.50x**) | 1.32x | 2.68 / 4.02 | 483 / 276 (**1.75x**) | 1.49x | 2.08 / 3.63 | | 2 | 625 / 420 (**1.49x**) | 1.16x | 3.87 / 5.41 | 775 / 473 (**1.64x**) | 1.35x | 3.10 / 4.72 | | 4 | 875 / 625 (**1.40x**) | 1.18x | 7.14 / 8.91 | 1156 / 750 (**1.54x**) | 1.24x | 5.45 / 7.28 | | 8 | 1233 / 904 (**1.36x**) | 1.14x | 11.92 / 13.91 | 1667 / 1088 (**1.53x**) | 1.20x | 9.70 / 12.30 | ### Full matrix (nsys decode step, stock / ours) SPEED-Bench mixed prompts at ISL 8k / 32k / 100k; DSpark DL3 at forced acceptance 2.87, DL7 at 3.78.
TP8 (complete) and TP16 (partial) **TP8, no DCP, spec off** (step time ratio, B1/2/4/8/16/32/64): | ISL | B1 | B2 | B4 | B8 | B16 | B32 | B64 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 8k | 1.65x | 1.52x | 1.55x | 1.59x | 1.44x | 1.35x | 1.31x | | 32k | 1.65x | 1.52x | 1.57x | 1.45x | 1.42x | 1.33x | 1.32x | | 100k | 1.66x | 1.50x | 1.52x | 1.40x | 1.39x | 1.32x | (KV) | 8k step us, stock -> ours: 8673->5254, 9799->6434, 11663->7505, 15490->9745, 17373->12104, 23873->17648, 33664->25709. **TP8+DCP8, spec off, 100k:** 1.69 / 1.58 / 1.60 / 1.49 / 1.45 / 1.36 / 1.31x (step us 9387->5550 ... 34903->26638). **TP8, DL3 (AL 2.87), B1–B16 = M4–M64:** | ISL | B1 | B2 | B4 | B8 | B16 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 8k verify forward | 1.68x | 1.58x | 1.51x | 1.40x | 1.36x | | 8k step | 1.61x | 1.52x | 1.47x | 1.37x | 1.34x | | 32k step | 1.58x | 1.51x | 1.47x | 1.36x | 1.37x | | 100k step | 1.55x | 1.51x | 1.42x | 1.31x | 1.28x | 8k decode tok/s, ours vs stock: 373/619/977/1410/1931 vs 239/413/672/1009/1435. **TP8, DL7 (AL 3.78), B1–B8 = M8–M64:** | ISL | B1 | B2 | B4 | B8 | |---|---|---|---|---| | 8k verify forward | 1.62x | 1.52x | 1.41x | 1.41x | | 8k step | 1.57x | 1.47x | 1.38x | 1.38x | | 32k step | 1.45x | 1.47x | 1.39x | 1.37x | | 100k step | 1.44x | 1.45x | 1.34x | 1.34x | 8k step ms, ours vs stock: 9.6/11.5/16.4/23.2 vs 15.1/16.9/22.6/32.1.
## Details ### vLLM Integration No weight changes were made in this model implementation: it is fully compatible with Aggregated vLLM serving, and falls back to the default implementation for prefills, mixed batches, and large batches. The specialized decode runtime is implemented via _composition_: a SpecializedDecode object owned by the Kimi LLM model, built when supported (see `unsupported(...)`), and called during forward(). The runtime can opt-out of a batch (e.g. when it has too many tokens) by checking `decode.plan(...) is None`, and fall back to stock forward. I considered a few alternate designs but ultimately feel like this is the cleanest integration. It uses the ModelState protocol to build the runtime object and hook into initialize_kv_cache(). The rest of the integration is organized into subfolders, e.g. `vllm/models/kimi_k3/specialized_decode/nvidia/cutedsl/kda/` with the specialized implementation(s) for each component. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). (Omitted -- I reviewed all the code manually and did multiple cleanup passes internally before opening the PR here). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. **I am happy with the validation, but still unclear how much we want to put into CI. I may yet add a GSM8k sanity check to CI** - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

title: [Chore] Use upstream Transformers InklingProcessor
body:
## Overview

Split from #60823: deletes the vendored Inkling processor and builds Inkling's multimodal inputs with upstream Transformers `InklingProcessor`.

Related PRs:
- **#60823:** the larger unvendoring PR this is split from; Inkling has been dropped from it.
- **#61392** and **#61813:** the same split for DeepSeek-V4 and MiniMax-M3.

No other open PR touches `vllm/models/inkling/common/mm_preprocess.py` or the vendored processor.

## Claims

- Deletes `vllm/transformers_utils/processors/inkling.py` (504 lines). `InklingProcessingInfo.get_hf_processor` loads upstream `InklingProcessor` from the checkpoint, which ships in every Transformers version vLLM supports (>= 5.16.1).
- Images: the upstream image processor patchifies, but vLLM still does the 2x long-edge upscale with PIL LANCZOS, because upstream defaults to no rescale and torchvision LANCZOS does not match the reference.
- Audio: the upstream feature extractor computes the mel features and `InklingProcessor._extract_dmel_bins` (private) quantises them to dMel ids. The dMel parameters now come from the checkpoint's `preprocessor_config.json` instead of being copied from the vLLM config.
- The multimodal kwarg names are unchanged (`input_audio_features` stays), so the model code and the Rust frontend, which sends Inkling audio under that key, are untouched. The only output difference is that the dMel ids are int32 instead of float32 holding the same integers; the audio tower casts to int32 anyway.
- No numerics change: processor outputs and greedy decode are bit-identical to `main`.

## Validation

Processor outputs on CPU, `thinkingmachines/Inkling-NVFP4`, `main` vs this PR: 4 images (224x224 to 1920x1080, and 37x501), 3 audio clips at 16 kHz (1 s to 31 s), one 44.1 kHz clip, and a mixed image + audio prompt. Prompt token ids, `pixel_values` and `num_patches` are identical; the dMel ids have identical values.

Greedy decode, `thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4` on 2x B200 (TP2), `transformers` 5.19.0, FlashInfer autotuning off, 128 tokens with logprobs:

| Prompt | `main` run 1 vs run 2 | `main` vs this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Text only | identical | identical |
| 1 image (x2 prompts) | identical | identical |
| 2 images | identical | identical |
| 1 audio (x2 prompts) | identical | identical |
| Image + audio | identical | identical |

"Identical" means the same prompt token count, text and logprobs (max |Δ logprob| = 0). With FlashInfer autotuning on, two `main` launches already differ from each other, so it was turned off.

```bash
vllm serve thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4 --tokenizer-mode inkling --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 32768 --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 2, "audio": 1}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": false}'
```

```bash
pytest tests/renderers/test_inkling.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k "inkling or Inkling"
# main and this PR: 48 passed (includes 3 test_processing_correctness cases for Inkling-NVFP4)
```

title: [ROCm][Perf] Any-shape low-latency MoE router GEMM on MI355
body:
## Overview

On MI355 (gfx950), the MoE router GEMM now has a low-latency kernel for **any** router shape (fp32 or bf16 weights, fp32 output, M ≤ 32), matching the CuTeDSL `ll_fp32w` / `ll_bf16` router kernels from #44343 and #50174. Previously only five hard-coded `(hidden_size, num_experts)` shapes had a fast path; every other model paid 9–13 µs per MoE layer per decode step in `F.linear` / hipBLASLt.

## Claims

- **Decode 1–14% faster** on all 8 tested MoE models whose router path changes, largest at low concurrency.
- **No accuracy change**: GSM8K matches `main` on every model (paired McNemar p = 1.0 and 0.34 where runs varied most).
- **No regressions**: prefill, an unchanged-path control (Qwen3-30B-A3B) and the 5 previously tuned shapes stay flat; shapes where the kernel would lose keep today's path.
- **New MI355 CI job** mirroring `(B200) Gate Linear CuTeDSL Kernels`.

Changes:

- Generalize `rocm_fp32_router_gemm` to any shape: masked K tail, MI355-swept launch rule, bf16 weights, size guards
- `GateLinear`: enable the fp32 router tier on gfx950 for any shape and route bf16-weight fp32-logit gates (tier 6) through the same dispatch op
- Extend `test_rocm_fp32_router_gemm.py` and fix the now-outdated rejection test in `test_gate_linear_rocm_dispatch.py`
- Add `:amd: (MI355) Gate Linear Router Kernels` (B200 mirror + optional `test-amd.yaml` entry) and move the 3 ROCm router test files there from MI355 Misc

## Validation

`main` vs this PR, end to end on MI355 (decode TPOT Δ, + is faster; median of 5 reps):

| Model | Router | Decode Δ C1 / C8 / C32 | GSM8K main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B | fp32 2560×64 | **+14.1 / +3.4 / +2.1%** | 86.58 → 86.28 |
| Trinity-Nano | fp32 1024×128 | **+9.6 / +4.9 / +4.0%** | 79.08 → 79.00 |
| Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-FP8 | fp32 2688×128 | **+9.4 / +5.4 / +2.2%** | 90.96 / 90.69 (A/A) → 90.83 |
| Ling-mini-2.0 | fp32 2048×256 | **+7.7 / +4.6 / +2.5%** | 88.02 → 88.10 |
| GLM-4.5-Air-FP8 (TP2) | fp32 4096×128 | **+5.0 / +5.0 / +2.9%** | 72.33 → 72.02 |
| Step-3.5-Flash-FP8 (TP2) | fp32 4096×288 | **+4.7 / +3.1 / +2.7%** | 89.61 → 89.31 |
| Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | bf16 2816×128 | **+8.9 / +5.5 / +3.5%** | 94.31 → 94.39 |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (TP2) | bf16 4096×256 | **+2.0 / +1.2 / +1.0%** | 95.80 → 95.86 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B (control) | unchanged | −0.2 / 0.0 / +0.2% | 91.66 → 91.58 |

8K prefill TTFT is flat on every model (within ±0.7%).

<details>
<summary>Methodology and accuracy details</summary>

- `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, prefix caching off, 1–8 input / 256–512 output tokens. `main` and the PR were served at the same time on separate GPUs, alternating every run, with GPU load logged each rep.
- GSM8K: lm_eval 5-shot chat, median of 3+ runs.
- Nemotron and DeepSeek-V4 were re-run with `--log_samples` for a paired per-question test. Nemotron PR vs `main`: 9 / 9 discordant, McNemar p = 1.0; `main` vs `main` A/A: 9 / 6, p = 0.61. DeepSeek-V4: 3 / 7 in the PR's favor, p = 0.34. An earlier DeepSeek-V4 round read 96.06 → 95.53; the repeat did not reproduce it.
- ERNIE's −0.7% prefill is within the 0.3–0.5% spread between GPUs, which a GPU-swap A/B confirmed. Trinity's prefill TTFT ranges overlap.
- **Why decode improves:** one router GEMM per MoE layer per step drops from 9–13 µs (`F.linear`) or 5–11 µs (hipBLASLt) to 1.9–4.9 µs at ≤ 8 tokens, saving 0.2–0.6 ms per step. Prefill and large batches never reach the kernel.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Kernel benchmark</summary>

MI355, one idle GPU, median of 30 graph replays, 2 runs with ≤5% drift. M = 1–32.

| | Shapes | vs today's path |
|---|---|---|
| fp32, the 5 old shapes | 5 | 0.97–1.30× vs old tuned configs (median 1.07×) |
| fp32, new shapes (DeepSeek-V3, Kimi-K2, Qwen3, Qwen3.8, gpt-oss, Llama4) | 7 | **1.2–6.8×** vs `F.linear` (median 4.1×) |
| fp32, held out from the sweep (GLM-4.5, Ernie, 1000×100, 1024 experts, …) | 10 | **1.1–7.0×**; two 1024-expert M=32 cases keep `F.linear` |
| bf16 | 9 | **1.7–5.4×** vs hipBLASLt at M ≤ 8, 1.04–2.9× at 16–32; never slower |

Max relative error vs float64: 1.3e-7 (fp32 weights), 8.9e-8 (bf16 weights).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

- New CI command `pytest -v -s tests/kernels/test_rocm_fp32_router_gemm.py tests/kernels/test_gate_linear_rocm_dispatch.py tests/kernels/test_bf16x3_router_gemm_rocm.py`: 847 passed, 10/10 loops, ~5 min each.
- Each new test fails against a mutated kernel or dispatcher: no K-tail mask, the old shape list, a bypassed dispatcher, no bf16 cutoff, or no gfx950 tier-6 routing.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Design details, scope and related PRs</summary>

- **Launch rule:** one program computes `BLOCK_M` tokens for one expert. Narrow routers (< 64 experts) keep `BLOCK_M = 1`; wide routers grow it with the token count. Fitted on 12 shapes, checked on 10 held-out shapes: within 1.11× of the per-shape best and faster than the fallback everywhere.
- **Size guards:** at M·N·K ≥ 2^27 (fp32) or tokens × experts > 8192 (bf16) the fallback is faster, so the kernel declines and today's path runs.
- **Compile safety:** runtime branching stays inside the existing `fp32_router_gemm_dispatch` custom op.
- **Scope:** gfx950 only; gfx942, CUDA, biased/quantized gates and batch-invariant mode are unchanged.
- **Not covered end to end:** MiniMax-M2.5-MXFP4 decodes at ~196 ms/token on both `main` and the PR, so the difference is unmeasurable. Kimi-Linear-48B and LongCat-Flash-Lite-FP8 crash on unmodified `main`, unrelated to this change. Their router shapes are covered by the kernel tests.
- **Related PRs:** #59023 does the bf16 extension for Kimi-K3's 7168×896 gate only (this PR gives the same M ≤ 9 limit there, for any shape). #57626 forces fp32 weights for the 5 listed shapes instead; this PR runs bf16 weights directly with no fp32 copy. #61687 targets a separate AITER tier and is orthogonal.

</details>

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Keep the gate's hash_indices_table out of RoutedExperts parameters
body:
## Overview

Fixes `KeyError: "attribute 'hash_indices_table' already exists"` when building any DeepSeek-V4 MoE layer that uses hash routing. Main has hit it since #58800 merged (build 95246), on both NVIDIA and AMD. Example: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95273#01a14218-f99c-4f41-a508-15d43366b27e

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4 models with hash-routed MoE layers initialize again.
- Fixes on main:
  - `(MI355) DeepSeek V4 MoE Integration`: `test_deepseek_v4_vl_rocm.py::test_rocm_moe_routing_and_shared_experts_match_reference[text-hash, vision-hash]`
  - `(MI355 DPX) Basic Models (Extra Initialization) Shard 9`
  - `(H200 MIG 35GB) Basic Models (Extra Initialization) Shard 7`: `test_can_initialize_large_subset[DeepseekV4ForConditionalGeneration]`
- `hash_indices_table` stays out of `RoutedExperts`' registered parameters, as #60282 intended.

## Validation

Not run locally. The jobs listed above are the check: they fail on every main build since 95246 and should pass on this PR's CI.

## Details

**Root cause: two changes that conflict once both are on main.**
1. #60282 (merged 14:10Z Oct 15) gave `RoutedExperts` a class-level default `hash_indices_table = None`. It has `FusedMoEFactory` attach the gate-owned table with `object.__setattr__`, so the gate's `nn.Parameter` is not registered a second time under the experts module.
2. #58800 (merged 21:52Z Oct 15, branched before #60282) also passes `hash_indices_table` into `RoutedExperts.__init__` and assigns `self.hash_indices_table = hash_indices_table`.
3. The table is an `nn.Parameter`, so that assignment calls `register_parameter`. The class attribute from (1) already exists, so `register_parameter` raises `KeyError`.

Each PR passed CI on its own.

**Fix.** `RoutedExperts.__init__` stores the table with `object.__setattr__`, before `_get_quant_method` as #58800 needs, and `FusedMoEFactory` drops its now-redundant `object.__setattr__`. `hash_indices_table` is already in `NON_EXPERT_WEIGHTS` for EPLB and is never a registered parameter of `RoutedExperts`, so nothing else changes.

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs for `hash_indices_table` and found none. This affects main only: `releases/v0.32.0` predates both #58800 and #60282.

cc @jpvillam-amd @Rohan138

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Fix Triton MLA decode int32 overflow and logits workspace accounting
body:
Triton MLA models crash at their default context length on MI355: `vllm serve` with default settings for Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct, LongCat-Flash-Lite-FP8 and DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat dies with `Memory access fault by GPU ... Write access to a read-only page` during CUDA graph capture. Two bugs are involved, and the second only shows up once the first is fixed:

1. **int32 overflow in the decode kernels.** The split-KV logits offset `cur_batch * stride_mid_ob` is computed in int32. At ≥ 128K context, `_compute_num_kv_splits` picks 512 splits on MI355 (2 × 256 CUs), so with 32 heads one request's logits span 32 × 512 × 513 = 8.4M floats. From batch row 256 onward the offset passes 2^31, and FULL graph capture runs batches up to 512.
2. **The logits workspace is not counted by memory profiling.** #46819 reserves the worst-case logits workspace (32 GiB for LongCat at defaults: 1024 seqs × 32 heads × 512 splits × 513 × fp32) when the metadata builder is created, which happens after profiling. The KV cache is then sized as if that memory were free, and its allocation OOMs (`Tried to allocate 164.67 GiB`, 157.84 GiB free).

To resolve the above, this PR modifies:
- `triton_decode_attention.py`: compute `cur_batch * stride_mid_ob` in int64 at the six logits offsets (stage 1 normal/grouped stores and stage 2 loads), following #47671.
- `MLAAttentionImpl.reserve_profiling_workspace()`: a no-op hook called from the MLA profiling branch, next to the existing `kv_b_proj` scratch simulation.
- `TritonMLAImpl` overrides the hook to reserve the logits workspace at its upper bound (`max_num_seqs × max_decode_query_len`) during profiling. The builder keeps its reservation, which becomes a no-op.
- `test_triton_decode_attention.py`: a regression test whose logits exceed 2^31 elements, for the grouped (MLA) and normal kernels.

## Validation

MI355, TP1. `main` vs this PR:

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct, default 1M context | memory access fault | serves, GSM8K 87.34 |
| LongCat-Flash-Lite-FP8, default 320K context | memory access fault | serves, GSM8K 86.88 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, default backend (`TRITON_MLA`) and 160K context | memory access fault | serves |
| LongCat with only the overflow fix | — | OOM at KV cache allocation |
| LongCat with only the accounting fix | — | memory access fault |

Both models were also served at concurrency 384, where decode rows ≥ 256 run with 512 splits: 0 failed requests.

At 32K context, where `main` works (decode TPOT Δ, + is faster; median of 5 reps, repeated with GPUs swapped):

| Model | C1 | C8 | C32 | C128 | GSM8K main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct | +0.4 / +0.3% | +0.2 / +0.3% | −0.1 / +2.1% | +2.2 / +2.1% | 86.88 → 86.58 (McNemar p = 0.75) |
| LongCat-Flash-Lite-FP8 | +1.0 / +0.6% | +1.7 / +1.6% | +3.6 / +3.0% | +6.0 / +5.3% | 86.88 → 87.34 (p = 0.57) |

<details>
<summary>Why decode got faster</summary>

A rocprofv3 trace of the same LongCat decode workload (128 × 2048-token prompts, 256 output tokens, 32K context) shows all of the difference in `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1`: 6062 → 5230 ms (−13.7%), with identical grids and register counts. Every other kernel is within ±0.5%. In the stage-1 variants I inspected, the int32 offset lowers the logits stores to scalar `buffer_store_dword`, while the int64 base produces vectorized `global_store_dwordx3`. The kernel microbenchmark is neutral at long sequences (30 shapes, H 16–128, 4K–128K context: median 1.000×, range 0.990–1.005×, run-to-run drift ≤ 0.8%) and 15–17% faster at 512 splits with batch ≥ 128.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

- `test_decode_attention_int64_logits_offset` faults on `main` (both cases) and passes with this PR in 2.4 s. It uses ~8.6 GB of fp32 logits.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py` + `test_triton_mla_causal_verify_flatten.py`: 133 passed, 10/10 loops.
- `v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` + `test_sparse_mla_backends.py` (the CI command): 11 clean runs (751 passed), including all 6 with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`. The 7 other runs failed only in tests that behave the same on `main`:
  - The sparse `ROCMAiterMLA` decode test fails about 1 in 20 in isolation: 19/20 on both `main` and this PR.
  - HF API 429 rate limits, from four loops running in parallel.
  - `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness` failed only in runs that also hit 429s. It is 20/20 in isolation on both `main` and this PR.
  - One transient engine OOM, where device-wide free memory dropped during profiling.
- `v1/attention` (rest of the CI command, CI environment): 1972 passed.
- DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat on `ROCM_AITER_MLA` (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0`), where the hook is a no-op, serves normally. AITER MoE was turned off only because this image's AITER `topk_gating` rejects `num_shared_experts` on `main`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Design notes</summary>

- **Effect on KV cache size:** the KV cache now excludes the logits workspace. LongCat at 32K goes from 164.67 to 162.91 GiB (`main` over-commits there too, but its slack absorbs it). At 320K it is 134.86 GiB, where `main` cannot start.
- **Upper bound:** the profiling hook has no builder, so it sizes rows as `max_num_seqs × max_decode_query_len`. That matches the builder's `reorder_batch_threshold` except with DCP on a backend without varlen support, where the builder uses 1 and the profiled reservation is larger than needed.
- **Why the profiling forward:** the impl is built at model load, but the decode metadata builder only exists after profiling. Reserving in the profiling run follows the existing MLA `kv_b_proj` simulation and the sparse-indexer reservations, and avoids touching the worker's profiling code.
- **History:** #33529 made split counts up to 2 × compute units reachable, and #46819 moved the logits into a workspace reserved after profiling. #47671 fixed the same overflow class for page offsets in these kernels.
- **Duplicate check:** no open PR or issue covers this. #46728 (NVIDIA shared-memory OOR) and #57094 (NaN on empty `seq_len`) touch the same kernels for different bugs.

</details>

title: [ROCm][Perf] Use AITER top-k for the DeepSeek-V3.2/GLM-5 sparse indexer
body:
## Overview

On gfx950 with AITER enabled, the uncompressed sparse indexer of DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.x (`index_topk` 2048) now takes AITER's top-k for decode and for prefill chunks whose longest row reaches 32K tokens, through the adapters #52882 added for DeepSeek-V4. Related: #55327, #50470, #46172, #60012.

## Claims

- GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X, TP4, `--max-model-len 133120`: 128K/1K TPOT -7.0% / -4.6% / -3.0% at c1 / c8 / c16, MTP3 c8 -3.0%; 8K/1K within noise; gsm8k and passkey unchanged.
- DeepSeek-V3.2, TP4, default max_model_len (163840): 128K/1K c1 TPOT -15.6%, 4K/1K c16 -1.1%, 4K/1K c1 +0.7% (+0.085 ms); gsm8k unchanged.
- Compressed indexers, other `index_topk`, GLM-5.3-Flash kpool, gfx942, AITER off and non-ROCm are unchanged.

## Validation

- `test_top_k_per_row.py`, MI355X: 43 passed (8 new), 246 skipped, 1 failed as on main (pre-existing, see below). glm5next dispatch tests pass. pre-commit clean.
- AITER vs in-tree on FP8 scorer output: same selections on 29,934 rows (by value where scores tie).
- Serving, mean TPOT (ms), GLM-5.2-MXFP4 unless noted; main 2 runs / PR 3 runs (4 each with MTP3, 2 each for DeepSeek-V3.2), no failed requests:

| workload | main | PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128K/1K c1 / c8 / c16 | 14.73 / 45.05 / 78.94 | 13.70 / 42.97 / 76.60 | -7.0% / -4.6% / -3.0% |
| MTP3 128K/1K c8 | 34.84 | 33.79 | -3.0% |
| 8K/1K c1 / c8 / c16, MTP3 c8 | 13.48 / 17.37 / 22.66 / 9.06 | 13.45 / 17.39 / 22.54 / 9.16 | within noise |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 128K/1K c1 | 16.23 | 13.70 | -15.6% |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 4K/1K c1 / c16 | 12.81 / 22.86 | 12.90 / 22.61 | +0.7% / -1.1% |

- gsm8k 5-shot strict: GLM-5.2 0.9287 main, 0.9348 PR (stderr 0.007); DeepSeek-V3.2 0.9522 main, 0.9507 PR (stderr 0.006). MTP3 acceptance length 3.29 / 3.30.

<details>
<summary>Per-run numbers, kernel data and reproduction</summary>

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (AITER 0.1.25) running main at 7f730b4 and this branch from source, MI355X.

GLM-5.2-MXFP4, mean TPOT per run (ms). Order: main, PR, PR, main, PR. A further main run between the two PR sessions was dropped: another process held about 88 GiB per GPU while it started, so its KV cache was 1.23M tokens instead of 3.2M. MTP3 order: main, PR, PR, main, PR, PR, main, main.

| workload | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| 8K/1K c1 | 13.43, 13.53 | 13.44, 13.45, 13.46 |
| 8K/1K c8 | 17.27, 17.47 | 17.27, 17.51, 17.38 |
| 8K/1K c16 | 22.46, 22.86 | 22.44, 22.66, 22.52 |
| 128K/1K c1 | 14.72, 14.75 | 13.66, 13.67, 13.78 |
| 128K/1K c8 | 44.55, 45.56 | 42.95, 42.98, 42.98 |
| 128K/1K c16 | 78.89, 79.00 | 76.58, 76.62, 76.60 |
| MTP3 8K/1K c8 | 8.91, 9.16, 9.08, 9.10 | 9.14, 9.34, 9.08, 9.10 |
| MTP3 128K/1K c8 | 34.27, 35.52, 34.45, 35.12 | 33.96, 33.67, 34.17, 33.35 |

- Median ITL (ms): 128K c1 14.83 to 13.76, c8 18.22 to 17.01, c16 21.52 to 20.49, MTP3 128K c8 27.04 to 25.39. Output throughput at 128K: +5.8% / +3.7% / +2.8%. KV cache size and startup time match across arms.
- The 128K c1 ITL drop (1.07 ms) matches the kernel estimate of 21 indexer layers x 53 us (1.11 ms).
- gsm8k flexible: 0.9295 main, 0.9363 PR. MTP3 gsm8k, first 400 questions: 0.935 main, 0.9325 PR (stderr 0.012). Passkey at 32K / 64K / 120K: 12/12, 8/8, 6/6 in both arms.
- Operator check: decode logits from AITER's `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` (buffer poisoned past each row), prefill logits from `rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`, calls mirroring `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer`; widths 133120 and 1M, `next_n` 1 (1-D), 2 (native 2-D) and 4 (one row per token), packed multi-sequence prefill, and graph replay with new lengths. Every row has `min(L, k)` distinct indices in `[0, L)` followed by `-1`.

DeepSeek-V3.2 (FP8 checkpoint), TP4, same env and flags but no `--max-model-len` (163840), mean TPOT per run (ms), order main, PR, PR, main; median ITL and output throughput follow TPOT:

| workload | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| 4K/1K c1 | 12.83, 12.80 | 12.91, 12.89 |
| 4K/1K c16 | 22.84, 22.88 | 22.62, 22.60 |
| 128K/1K c1 | 16.24, 16.22 | 13.72, 13.69 |

- 4K/1K c16 mean TTFT: 2333, 2326 ms main, 2465, 2327 ms PR. 128K/1K c1 output throughput +10.0%. KV cache 2.07M tokens in every session. gsm8k flexible: 0.9530 main, 0.9507 PR.
- A static cut-off for 131072-200000 columns would put this deployment back on the in-tree kernel: it would recover the 0.085 ms at 4K c1 and lose the 128K gain (2.53 ms) and the 4K c16 gain. GLM-5.2 at 133120 would lose its 128K gains as well.

Decode top-k per indexer layer (us, in-tree to AITER), GLM-5.2 indexer (32 heads, k=2048); scoring and top-k for 21 layers captured in one graph, LLC flushed before each replay, median of 20:

| width | context | 1 row | 8 rows | 16 rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 133120 | 4K | 17.5 to 20.4 | 17.3 to 22.3 | 17.2 to 22.7 |
| 133120 | 32K | 34.0 to 22.2 | 34.9 to 22.8 | 34.7 to 23.5 |
| 133120 | 128K | 80.8 to 27.9 | 81.8 to 28.8 | 81.3 to 28.5 |
| 1M | 4K | 37.0 to 25.9 | 35.3 to 29.3 | 35.3 to 35.3 |
| 1M | 32K | 42.8 to 26.8 | 42.3 to 29.6 | 43.7 to 32.3 |
| 1M | 128K | 46.3 to 27.1 | 50.0 to 31.2 | 50.2 to 34.4 |

MTP1 (2-D bounds) and MTP3 (one row per token) follow the same pattern. At 262144 columns AITER wins at every measured context.

Prefill top-k GPU time per 16K-row chunk (us, in-tree to AITER): context 16K 304 to 370, 20K 426 to 469, 24K 568 to 558, 32K 757 to 680, 64K 1681 to 1320, 128K 4026 to 2635. 512-row chunks cross over near 20K. Host enqueue per call: in-tree 5-12 us, AITER 27-36 us.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0 \
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 133120 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9
# MTP3: --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# DeepSeek-V3.2: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2, same env and flags without --max-model-len.

# 128K/1K: num-prompts max(C, 3). 8K/1K: --random-input-len 8192,
# num-prompts max(3C, 6), --seed 42. MTP3 c8: 8 prompts at 128K, 24 at 8K.
# DeepSeek-V3.2 4K/1K: --random-input-len 4096, 6 prompts at c1, 48 at c16, --seed 42.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 \
  --num-prompts $N --max-concurrency $C --seed 43

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --model_args model=amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False

VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -v tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py \
  tests/models/glm5next/test_sparse_indexer_topk_dispatch.py
```

</details>

## Details

- Gate: compress ratio 1 and k=2048 only. Decode always takes AITER (FULL graphs are not keyed by context length); prefill when `chunk.max_seqlen_k`, a host int, reaches 32K.
- Cost: with max_model_len between 131072 and 200000 and up to 48 rows, AITER loses 3-6 us per layer below 8-16K context. DeepSeek-V3.2 (default 163840, 61 indexer layers) measures +0.085 ms TPOT at 4K/1K c1. Keeping the in-tree kernel for that width band would also give up the 2.53 ms gain at 128K on the same deployment, so the gate does not exclude it.
- Not measured end to end: GLM-5/5.1, TP8. CI (MI300, NVIDIA) runs only the new selection test; the GPU tests need gfx950.

<details>
<summary>Design notes, pre-existing failure and related PRs</summary>

- Cause: the in-tree decode kernel has gfx950 policies only for k=512 and k=1024 (#55327). At k=2048 its cost grows with context; AITER's stays near flat.
- Semantics come from #52882's wrappers. ROCm DSA decode carries `(B, next_n)` bounds for native MTP1 and one row per token otherwise, so `seq_lens.reshape(-1)` with `next_n=1` gives AITER each row's exact end. Prefill turns AITER's chunk-global indices into sequence-local ones and keeps `-1`.
- Decode is not split by context length because a FULL graph replays one kernel for every length. Eager decode could use the length, but would then pick a different kernel for the same shape depending on graph mode. AITER's extra host time per call only shows in eager steps.
- `test_aiter_decode_topk_matches_per_row_under_mtp` (from #58167, `requires_gfx950`, so not in CI) fails identically on main: it passes `(B, 1)` seq_lens with `next_n=4` to the in-tree k=512 gfx950 kernel, which reads any 2-D `seq_lens` per row, so its reference rows are wrong. It does not reach the code changed here.
- #60012 (open) tunes the in-tree k=2048 kernel above 200000 columns for #55327. With this PR it still serves AITER-off deployments and short prefill chunks; the gate should be re-measured if it lands. #57844 (open) edits the same selector. #59421 (draft, native MTP above `next_n=2`) is compatible because decode flattens the bounds.
- #50470 (draft) and #46172 also move the k=2048 decode top-k to AITER. Both have merge conflicts and no activity since 2026-08-22, and both swap the call unconditionally, passing vLLM's `next_n` with its 2-D MTP bounds. On both, the author of #52882 noted that AITER v0.1.19 needs those bounds adapted and asked to treat #52882 as the consolidated direction; #52882 then merged with AITER enabled for compressed indexers only. This PR applies its adapters to the k=2048 path, adds prefill and serving results, and leaves every other indexer unchanged. The `aiter.top_k_per_row_decode` entry point that #50470 waited for ships in AITER 0.1.25 and is the function called here.
- Duplicate search, `gh pr list --state all --search`: "aiter topk", "top-k ROCm", "topk ROCm", "indexer ROCm", "indexer aiter", "DeepSeek-V3.2 ROCm", "GLM-5 ROCm", "sparse indexer AMD", "top_k_per_row_decode", "top_k_per_row_prefill", "compress_ratio aiter topk".

</details>

Not a duplicate: #50470 and #46172 target the same decode call, have been inactive since 2026-08-22, and were marked superseded by #52882's author; #52882 left k=2048 on the in-tree kernel (details above). Thanks @JH-Leon-KIM-AMD for #50470.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the implementation, the measurements and this description.

---

title: [CI][AMD] Move 17 test groups from MI300 to MI355 and test large DeepSeek/Nemotron evals on AITER
body:
- Move 14 single-GPU groups from `mi300_1` to `mi355_dpx`, and LM Eval Large Models / ROCm Harness from `mi300_8` to `mi355_8` (`test-amd.yaml` + `test_areas` mirrors)
- Move LM Eval KV-Offload Large (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) from `mi300_4` to `mi355_4`
- Drop the MI300 copies whose MI355 twin already exists: Extended Pooling, Multimodal Extended Generation 1 / Extended Pooling, LM Eval Large Models
- Retire the MI300 DeepSeek R1 / V3.2 evals that ran on `TRITON_ATTN` (`models-mi3xx.txt`, `*_MI325.yaml`). Both models already run on MI355 with `ROCM_AITER_MLA(_SPARSE)` and AITER MoE
- Nemotron 3 Super (MI355): use `ROCM_AITER_FA` attention
- V1 E2E Hybrid Chunked Prefill: drop the stale `num_gpus: 4` (the test is TP1, and the mirror already used one GPU)

This is a subset of #60480, split out so these groups move first. DeepSeek R1, V3.2, V4 and Nemotron 3 Super should be gated on AITER on MI355 instead of Triton on MI300. R1, V3.2 and V4 already resolve to AITER on MI355, so for them this PR only removes the MI300 Triton runs and moves the V4 KV-offload eval. Nemotron 3 Super can only switch attention: AITER MoE rejects its non-gated ReLU² experts (`kernel does not support no act_and_mul MLP layer`), and there is no AITER Mamba backend. With `ROCM_AITER_FA`, the CI eval passes 10/10 for each Nemotron config on MI355 (TP4), and accuracy matches the default `ROCM_ATTN`:

title: [CI][ROCm][Bugfix] DeepSeek V4.1: don't pass expert intermediate padding to AITER
body:
AITER 0.1.25's FlyDSL MoE (ROCm/aiter#6125 configs) leaves the padded intermediate columns unwritten when told about the padding, so stage 2 reads stale memory and small decode batches (M <= 4 tokens) can come out NaN. This hits DeepSeek V4.1 at TP4, where the per-rank expert intermediate size is padded 576 -> 640.

Pass intermediate_pad=0 for V4.1's routed experts so AITER computes over the zero padding instead of skipping it, which is exact. DeepSeek V4 never pads the expert intermediate size and is unchanged. Revert once vLLM pins an AITER with the fix https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6598.

This hotfix was developed to resolve the flakiness in the newly added test group `(MI355) DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics`

#### lm-eval results:
| Run | Concurrency | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|---|
| DSv4.1-Flash TP4 + hotfix | 64 | 0.9242 ± 0.0073 | 0.9249 ± 0.0073 |
| DSv4.1-Flash TP4 + hotfix | 2 | 0.9375 ± 0.0121 | 0.9375 ± 0.0121 |
