title: [Feature][LoRA][MoE] Expert LoRA for FlashInfer TRTLLM MXFP4 experts
body:
## Overview

Add expert LoRA to the fused FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE kernel for MXFP4 expert weights with BF16 activations (`TrtLlmMxfp4LoRAExperts`, next to `TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts`). TP > 1 relies on #61235 (merged).

## Claims

- MXFP4 MoE models can serve expert LoRA adapters on `moe_backend="flashinfer_trtllm"` instead of falling back to Marlin / unfused Triton.
- Opt-in: `moe_backend="auto"` selects the same backend as before. `flashinfer_trtllm_afp8` (MXFP8 activations) with expert LoRA is rejected with an explicit reason.
- Requires FlashInfer >= 0.6.18 (`gemm1_lora_delta` on `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3987); vLLM pins 0.7.2.

## Validation

Environment: `vllm/vllm-openai` nightly arm64 image built from `af7f9488c` (flashinfer-python 0.7.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130), NVIDIA GB300, with the changed files of this PR and #61235 backported onto that commit and mounted over the image. Not run on the PR base itself; the changed files apply to it without conflicts.

**Kernel-level** — `pytest tests/lora/test_trtllm_mxfp4_lora_moe.py -v`: 9 passed. Random MXFP4 weights through vLLM's TRTLLM weight conversion, float64 reference from the dequantized weights, with and without an FC1/FC2 bias:

- delta in `[up | gate]` order: output and FC1 activation within 2% relative error of the reference; the swapped order is off by more than 30%;
- zero delta vs. the non-LoRA path: within 2%;
- the four incoming delta layouts are converted exactly;
- oracle: unchanged without LoRA, `TrtLlmMxfp4LoRAExperts` first with LoRA + BF16 activations, explicit error with MXFP8 activations.

**End-to-end** — `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, offline `LLM`, `enable_lora=True`, fixed-token logprobs (`prompt_logprobs`) of 16 prompts x 200 tokens. Adapters are seeded random expert-only LoRAs (rank 8, alpha 32, only `gate_up_proj` / `down_proj` nonzero; B std 0.01 = small, 0.05 = large). Reference: `moe_backend="triton_unfused"`, TP 1. On the reference the adapters move the logprobs by 0.53 (small) and 1.89 (large) mean abs. "Effect" is adapter minus base logprob per token; projection is `<new, ref> / <ref, ref>`.

| backend | TP | set | MAE vs ref | median abs | effect projection | effect correlation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer_trtllm` (this PR) | 1 | base | 0.136 | 0.038 | - | - |
| | 1 | small | 0.132 | 0.046 | 0.81 | 0.86 |
| | 1 | large | 0.963 | 0.629 | 0.84 | 0.79 |
| `marlin` | 1 | base | 0.126 | 0.040 | - | - |
| | 1 | small | 0.137 | 0.046 | 0.81 | 0.86 |
| | 1 | large | 0.973 | 0.621 | 0.82 | 0.79 |
| `flashinfer_trtllm` (this PR) | 2 | base | 0.149 | 0.044 | - | - |
| | 2 | small | 0.146 | 0.051 | 0.74 | 0.81 |
| | 2 | large | 1.023 | 0.665 | 0.81 | 0.76 |
| `flashinfer_trtllm`, without #61235 | 2 | small | 0.472 | 0.232 | 0.33 | 0.42 |
| | 2 | large | 1.703 | 1.193 | 0.54 | 0.49 |
| `triton_unfused` | 2 | base | 0.137 | 0.044 | - | - |
| | 2 | small | 0.144 | 0.051 | 0.80 | 0.84 |
| | 2 | large | 0.993 | 0.619 | 0.83 | 0.79 |

The base rows are the floor between two backends or TP sizes on this text (same size for Marlin and for Triton at TP 2 against Triton at TP 1; the mean is tail-heavy, see the median). With the small adapter the new backend stays on that floor; with either adapter it tracks the reference as closely as Marlin does. At TP 2 it needs #61235 (now on main). The large adapter breaks the model (mean logprob -4.6) and is only there to make the direction of the effect visible. Repeating a request gives identical logprobs on `flashinfer_trtllm` at TP 1 (Marlin: 0.07 MAE between two passes). One run per configuration.

**Throughput** — same model, TP 1, 64 concurrent requests, 256 output tokens each, output tokens/s (second of two passes):

| backend | base requests | with expert LoRA |
|---|---|---|
| `triton_unfused` | 5828 | 4593 |
| `marlin` | 10510 | 7047 |
| `flashinfer_trtllm` (this PR) | 13388 | 7699 |

Supplementary, on a 384-expert, top-6 MXFP4 MoE at TP 4 (prototype of this change on an older base, 128 requests of ~3.3k output tokens): with an expert adapter 1.5-1.65x the throughput of `triton_unfused` and 1.02-1.16x Marlin; base requests 2.5-2.7x `triton_unfused`.

Not validated: EP, `fully_sharded_loras`, per-expert (2D) adapters end-to-end, more than one loaded adapter, CUDA graph specialization per LoRA, GPT-OSS at TP 4 / 8. `ruff check` and `ruff format --diff` are clean on the changed files.

## Details

Design. `TrtLlmMxfp4LoRAExperts` subclasses `_TrtLlmLoRAExpertsBase` and reuses its flow unchanged: the gate/up delta is computed by punica and passed as `gemm1_lora_delta`, so the kernel adds it before the activation; the down delta is computed from the post-activation FC1 output the kernel returns, and the base finalize and the delta reduction happen in one FP32 pass. Kernel arguments (`gemm1_alpha/beta/clamp_limit`, unpadded hidden size) come from the existing `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsBase`.

Three things differ from the BF16 class, each behind the new `prepare_gemm1_lora_delta` hook or a small base change:

- FC1 bias. The kernel has one FC1 bias slot, used either by the static `gemm1_bias` or by the per-token delta. On the LoRA path the static bias (GPT-OSS has one) is un-shuffled to logical order and added to the delta; `gemm1_bias` is then not passed. The sum is rounded to BF16, the dtype the kernel takes for the delta.
- Delta layout. The kernel takes `[up | gate]` halves. Per-expert adapters already arrive that way (or as interleaved pairs for `SWIGLUOAI`); fused 3D adapters arrive in checkpoint row order. All four cases are converted.
- Hidden padding. MXFP4 TRTLLM pads the hidden size (2880 -> 3072 for GPT-OSS) and returns an unpadded output, so the shared finalize now writes `output.size(1)` columns instead of the padded width. No change for the BF16 class, where the two are equal. The modular kernel also sized its output from the padded input and asserted on the narrower result in the no-op finalize; it now asks the experts for the output hidden size (`FusedMoEExpertsModular.output_hidden_dim`, default: the input size; the TRTLLM MXFP4 experts return the unpadded size) and allocates `output` at that width up front, so the result is used without a copy on a single rank. This also applies to the non-LoRA `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular`. This was found by the end-to-end run, not by the kernel tests.

MXFP8 activations are not supported because the kernel then returns the FC1 activation as uint8 without block scales (observed with FlashInfer 0.6.18), so the down delta cannot be computed.

Limitations.

- DP is rejected (explicit `flashinfer_trtllm` + LoRA + DP raises, as before this PR): the inherited no-LoRA fast path reads the local batch's adapter flag, while under DP the experts see the gathered batch. `TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts` has the same gap; left for a separate fix.
- Top-1 routing with the weight applied on the input double-weights through the shared LoRA base (also `TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts`); fixed separately in #62019.
- The kernel tests need SM100, so the H200/L4 LoRA CI shards skip them; they were run on GB300 only.
- Not chunked, like `TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts`: the LoRA token mapping covers the whole batch. The TRTLLM-Gen grid limits one call to about `(65535 - num_experts) * 8 / top_k` tokens (~130k for GPT-OSS).
- `SITU` activation is not enabled for the LoRA class (untested).
- With a static FC1 bias, a delta far below the BF16 step of the bias is rounded away.

Related work, not duplicated: #47226 adds FlashInfer MoE LoRA for FP8 / MXFP8 / MxInt4 (not MXFP4, not updated since July) and uses the same opt-in rule; #34421 routes NVFP4 LoRA to Marlin; #61164 and #61165 fix other parts of the MoE LoRA path and do not overlap.

title: [Perf][Bugfix] Prefer MNNVL for single-node FlashInfer allreduce again
body:
## Purpose

Fixes a 3-5% decode regression in v0.32.0, caused by #56891.

#56891 changed automatic FlashInfer allreduce selection to use `trtllm` for every node-local process group. Before it, single-node runs used `mnnvl`, falling back to `trtllm` on nodes without NVSwitch multicast. The PR included no perf data, and on single-node NVSwitch systems `trtllm` is slower.

## Evidence

The perf-eval nightlies show a step in the 14 commits between the 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-04 nightlies, and #56891 is the only distributed change among them. Only TP>1 workloads moved:

| workload | before (10-03) | after (10-04 on) |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-397B NVFP4, 8xB200 | ~5650 tok/s, TPOT 20.8 ms | ~5460 tok/s, TPOT 21.6 ms |
| gpt-oss-120b TP4, H200 (same host) | 10883 tok/s, TPOT 11.20 ms | 10571 tok/s, TPOT 11.54 ms |
| GLM-5.3-Flash TP4, B200 | ~2770 tok/s | ~2650-2720 tok/s |
| MiniMax-M3 TP8, H200 | TPOT 35.9 ms | TPOT 36.8 ms |
| gpt-oss-120b TP1, B200 | unchanged | unchanged |

A/B on the v0.32.0rc2 image with `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND` forced:

| workload | default (`trtllm`) | `mnnvl` |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-397B NVFP4, 8xB200, 8k/1k conc 128 | 5462 tok/s, TPOT 21.78 ms | **5728 tok/s, TPOT 20.22 ms** |
| GLM-5.3-Flash TP4, B200, 3 repeats | 2533 / 2753 / 2771 tok/s | **2581 / 2811 / 2845 tok/s** |

## Change

For node-local groups, auto-selection goes back to `mnnvl` with `allow_trtllm_fallback=True`. The existing fallback still builds a `trtllm` workspace when `mnnvl` can't create one (no NVSwitch multicast). Multi-node selection from #56891 is unchanged: `mnnvl` on Blackwell, disabled on Hopper. The unit test's expectations are updated to match.

cc @elvircrn: is there a case where single-node `mnnvl` misbehaved that #56891 was fixing? The PR description only covers the multi-node cases.

## Test Plan

- `test_flashinfer_auto_backend_uses_group_topology` updated for the single-node cases.
- ruff check/format pass.
- Perf A/B above (perf-eval build 680).

title: [Perf][Sampler] Speed up the small-batch split top-p pipeline
body:
## Overview

The small-batch split top-p pipeline (#54651) caps its grid at one program per SM (`S * B <= num_SMs`), and at that occupancy its step kernels are latency-bound. On a 148-SM GPU S drops to 2 at 38 rows, so a top-p call at 38-64 rows (e.g. 8 requests x 8 spec-decode verify tokens) takes about twice as long as at 37 rows. This PR makes two changes:

1. It keeps splitting rows past one wave while each slice still spans at least 7168 vocab entries.
2. It lets MRV2 skip the split pipeline when no row is top-p-only. Today the pipeline is still launched in that case, as 7 kernels whose programs all exit immediately.

cc @njhill

## Claims

- With the `has_topp_only_rows` hint that MRV2 passes, `apply_top_k_top_p` on <= 64 rows is as fast or faster for every row mix measured: all top-p-only, half and half, and all top-k on both GPUs, plus 1, 10% and 25% top-p-only rows on B300. This holds on B300 (148 SMs) and H200 (132 SMs), across the vocab sizes of current models (120K-262K, plus 32K). Main -> this PR:
  - Top-p-only rows, where main is at S=2: 1.22-2.16x on B300 and 1.05-1.90x on H200.
  - Batches that mix top-k rows with top-p-only rows, B >= 32, V >= 120K: 1.43-2.70x. At 32K, where S changes only from B=38 on B300 and B=34 on H200, it is 1.00-1.62x. The fewer top-p-only rows, the bigger the win: with a single top-p-only row, up to 3.7x at V=151936 and 4.4x at V=262144 (B300).
  - Batches where every row has top-k (e.g. the Qwen3.8 and Gemma 4 defaults): 1.00-1.21x. MRV2 no longer launches the split pipeline for them.
  - The worst ratio, 0.97x, is in configs where nothing changes, within the A/A noise. Callers that do not pass the hint get the same gains, except that all-top-k batches run at 0.90-0.98x (see Change 2).
- Real MiMo-V2.6 spec-decode verify rows (top_p 0.95) on B300: 561 -> 219 us at B=38 (2.56x) and 565 -> 318 us at B=64 (1.78x).
- End to end on the Triton sampler path (B300):
  - Llama-3-8B-Instruct, seeded top-p, c=48: median ITL -5.1%.
  - MiMo-V2.6-Pro TP4 with DFlash K=7, c=8: top-p goes from 558 to 301 us per step, and GPU busy time excluding MoE GEMMs drops by 0.27 ms of a 22.7 ms decode step.

## Validation

**Tests**, on fa75d3456d + this PR:
- B300: `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py tests/v1/sample/test_sampler.py tests/v1/sample/test_rejection_sampler.py tests/v1/sample/test_sampling_params_e2e.py tests/model_executor/test_watermark_sample_warmup.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py`: 287 passed, 1 skipped (ROCm only).
- B300: `cd tests && pytest watermarking`, in its own session as CI runs it: 191 passed, 3 skipped. In a shared session, the default device that `test_topk_topp_sampler.py` sets leaks into these CPU tests; that is unrelated to this PR.
- H200: `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py`: 140 passed, 1 skipped. This ran on the revision before the new test gained its monkeypatch; the kernel code is the same.
- New tests:
  - B=48 in `test_topp_only` and `test_topk_and_topp`. On 128-152-SM GPUs this is the only tested size where main uses S=2.
  - `test_skip_split_without_topp_only_rows`: with `has_topp_only_rows=False` the split pipeline is not launched, and the result is bitwise identical, including for a grammar-masked row.
  - `test_has_topp_only_rows`: covers MRV2 `SamplingStates`, including top_k values that disable top-k.
- CI runs `tests/v1/sample` on H200 MIG and MI355.

**Microbenchmark setup.** Calls are to `apply_top_k_top_p_triton`, one CUDA graph per variant, with variants interleaved and capture order alternated between configs. Each number is the median of 100 replays with L2 hot. On an earlier revision without the hint, cold L2 agreed within 0.07x.
- "main" is this tree with `_topp_split_count` patched back and no hint.
- "PR" passes `has_topp_only_rows` computed from k and p, as MRV2 does.
- A second capture of "PR" (A/A) gives the noise floor: 95% of configs fall within +-1.5%, the worst at 0.96x/1.05x.
- Logits are randn x 3; p=0.95 and k=50 unless stated. The script is below.

V=151936, main -> PR:

| rows | GPU | B=16 | B=32 | B=38 | B=48 | B=64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| top-p only | B300 | 1.09x | 1.01x | 1.93x | 1.52x | 1.29x |
| | H200 | 1.16x | 1.06x | 1.69x | 1.38x | 1.05x |
| half top-k, half top-p only | B300 | 1.09x | 1.50x | 2.44x | 2.16x | 1.86x |
| | H200 | 1.08x | 1.51x | 2.06x | 1.92x | 1.66x |
| all top-k + top-p | B300 | 1.08x | 1.09x | 1.07x | 1.07x | 1.05x |
| | H200 | 1.06x | 1.07x | 1.04x | 1.07x | 1.07x |

S goes 8->16 at B=16 and 4->16 at B=32. It goes 2->16 from B=38 on B300 and from B=34 on H200; at B=34 the H200 speedups are 1.74x for top-p only and 2.13x for half top-k.

Popular models, with each model's vocab size and default sampling: generation_config, or the model card's recommendation when the repo sets none (*). B=38 (B300) and B=34 (H200) are the first sizes where main uses S=2. (†) gpt-oss sets no sampling defaults and OpenAI recommends top_p 1.0, which skips top-p entirely; the row shows a client that sends top_p 0.95.

| model | vocab | default sampling | B300 B=16 | B300 B=38 | B300 B=64 | H200 B=16 | H200 B=34 | H200 B=64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | 128256 | top_p 0.9 | 1.14x | 2.13x | 1.44x | 1.18x | 1.81x | 1.14x |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | 129280 | top_p 0.95* | 1.14x | 2.11x | 1.44x | 1.17x | 1.89x | 1.14x |
| Nemotron-3.5-Super | 131072 | top_p 0.95 | 1.13x | 1.77x | 1.24x | 1.16x | 1.73x | 1.11x |
| MiMo-V2.6-Pro | 152576 | top_p 0.95 | 1.11x | 1.88x | 1.30x | 1.15x | 1.78x | 1.06x |
| GLM-5.3 | 154880 | top_p 0.95 | 1.09x | 1.87x | 1.30x | 1.16x | 1.71x | 1.05x |
| Kimi-K3 | 163840 | top_p 0.95* | 1.09x | 1.98x | 1.38x | 1.15x | 1.79x | 1.16x |
| MiniMax-M3 | 200064 | top_p 0.95 | 1.06x | 1.85x | 1.27x | 1.13x | 1.76x | 1.13x |
| gpt-oss | 201088 | none; row uses top_p 0.95 (†) | 1.06x | 2.01x | 1.30x | 1.13x | 1.78x | 1.15x |
| Muse-Glimmer | 202048 | top_k 64, top_p 0.95 | 1.06x | 1.06x | 1.07x | 1.06x | 1.05x | 1.05x |
| Qwen3.8 | 248320 | top_k 20, top_p 0.95 | 1.05x | 1.07x | 1.05x | 1.05x | 1.03x | 1.04x |
| Gemma 4 | 262144 | top_k 64, top_p 0.95 | 1.04x | 1.04x | 1.00x | 1.04x | 1.04x | 1.04x |

Real MiMo-V2.6 verify-step logits on B300, top-p only, p=0.95. Rows are drawn from 1424 dumped verify rows (V=152576); the dump is not attached.

| B | 16 | 32 | 38 | 48 | 64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S main -> PR | 8 -> 16 | 4 -> 16 | 2 -> 16 | 2 -> 16 | 2 -> 16 |
| main (us) | 151.3 | 259.8 | 561.2 | 561.5 | 565.0 |
| PR (us) | 125.2 | 188.4 | 219.0 | 280.7 | 317.8 |
| speedup | 1.21x | 1.38x | 2.56x | 2.00x | 1.78x |

GB300 (152 SMs) shows the same picture at V=128K-262K: top-p only 1.18-1.94x where main is at S=2 (B >= 39), and mixed 1.43-2.55x at B >= 32. At 32K, where S changes, the numbers are 1.17-1.19x and 1.11-1.45x. These numbers come from an older vLLM tree with an earlier revision of this PR's `topk_topp_triton.py` swapped in. That revision used a 6144-entry floor, which picks the same S as 7168 at these vocab sizes, and predates the hint, so it covers only top-p-only and mixed rows.

**Serving on B300.** These runs used upstream 30e79c3a76, whose `topk_topp_triton.py` matches this PR's base, with the split-count change loaded in. Servers ran back to back on one node. Per-step times come from a 29-step torch-profiler window; ITL comes from the benchmark client.

| config | top-p per step | result |
|---|---|---|
| Llama-3-8B-Instruct TP1, T=1.0, top_p=0.95, per-request seed (keeps MRV2 on the Triton sampler), c=48 | 573 -> 166 us | GPU busy 5.80 -> 5.49 ms; median ITL 5.60 -> 5.32 ms (-5.1%) |
| same, c=64 / c=32 | 218 -> 126 us at c=32 | median ITL -4.7% / -0.7% |
| same, c=48, no seed (FlashInfer sampler; control) | not used | median ITL 5.11 -> 5.13 ms |
| MiMo-V2.6-Pro TP4, DFlash K=7, top_p=0.95, c=8 (64 verify rows) | 558 -> 301 us | GPU busy excluding MoE GEMMs (which vary with sampled content) 10.90 -> 10.63 ms; TPOT and ITL within sampling noise |

**Accuracy.** GSM8K 5-shot, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`, T=0.6, top_p=0.9, c=64, 6 runs per variant (2 servers x 3 seeds): main 73.25 +- 1.11, PR 73.82 +- 0.96.

<details>
<summary>Upstream benchmarks/benchmark_topk_topp.py (callers without the hint)</summary>

`benchmark_topk_topp.py` calls the op without `has_topp_only_rows`, so it shows what non-MRV2 callers get. Setup: B300, Zipf(1.1) logits, L2 flushed, no CUDA graph, input clone included, mean of 2 runs, us (main -> PR).

| scenario | V | B=38 | B=48 | B=64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| topp_whole (p=0.9) | 131072 | 522 -> 288 (1.81x) | 523 -> 344 (1.52x) | 526 -> 410 (1.28x) |
| topp_whole | 151936 | 711 -> 410 (1.73x) | 711 -> 483 (1.47x) | 715 -> 562 (1.27x) |
| topp_whole | 262144 | 1005 -> 552 (1.82x) | 1012 -> 667 (1.52x) | 1021 -> 846 (1.21x) |
| topp_partial (50% p=0.9) | 151936 | 710 -> 268 (2.65x) | 710 -> 272 (2.61x) | 715 -> 345 (2.07x) |

| topk_topp_whole | 262144 | 263 -> 268 (0.98x) | 275 -> 285 (0.96x) | 285 -> 296 (0.96x) |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script (bench_topp_split.py)</summary>

```python
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
"""Microbenchmark for the small-batch split top-p changes in topk_topp_triton.py.

Run from a checkout with the PR applied. "main" monkeypatches
_topp_split_count back to the rule on main (S * batch_size <= num_SMs) and
always launches the split pipeline, as main does; "pr" uses the module as is
and passes has_topp_only_rows computed from k and p, as MRV2 does.
Every config is captured once per variant as a CUDA graph on a scratch
copy of the logits; each rep restores the scratch copy outside the timed
region (and optionally flushes L2), then times one graph replay with CUDA
events. Variants are interleaved rep by rep, the
capture order alternates between configs, and the median is reported.
--aa adds a second capture of "pr" to show the noise floor.

    python bench_topp_split.py --vocabs 32000 128256 151936 262144 \
        --out results.json
"""

import argparse
import gc
import json

import torch

import vllm.v1.sample.ops.topk_topp_triton as tt

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--vocabs", type=int, nargs="+", default=[151936])
ap.add_argument("--bs", type=int, nargs="+",
                default=[1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 38, 48, 56, 64])
ap.add_argument("--modes", nargs="+", default=["p", "kp", "mixed", "k"])
ap.add_argument("--p", type=float, default=0.95)
ap.add_argument("--topk", type=int, default=50)
ap.add_argument("--reps", type=int, default=100)
ap.add_argument("--cold", action="store_true", help="flush L2 before each rep")
ap.add_argument("--real", help="optional .pt file with a [N, V] 'logits' tensor")
ap.add_argument("--aa", action="store_true", help="also time an A/A copy of pr")
ap.add_argument("--no-hint", action="store_true",
                help="pr does not pass has_topp_only_rows (non-MRV2 callers)")
ap.add_argument("--out")
args = ap.parse_args()

dev = torch.device("cuda")
props = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(dev)
NUM_SM = props.multi_processor_count
FLUSH = torch.empty(256 * 1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.int8, device=dev)
PR_RULE = tt._topp_split_count


def main_rule(batch_size: int, vocab_size: int, num_sm: int) -> int:
    splits = 1
    while splits < tt._SPLIT_MAX_SPLITS and splits * 2 * batch_size <= num_sm:
        splits *= 2
    return splits


VARIANTS = {"main": (main_rule, False), "pr": (PR_RULE, not args.no_hint)}
if args.aa:
    VARIANTS["pr_aa"] = (PR_RULE, not args.no_hint)


def make_inputs(mode, B, V, real):
    g = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(B * 7919 + V)
    if real is not None:
        cpu_g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(B * 7919 + V)
        idx = torch.randint(0, real.shape[0], (B,), generator=cpu_g)
        x = real[idx].to(dev).float().contiguous()
    else:
        x = torch.randn(B, V, device=dev, generator=g) * 3.0
    p = torch.full((B,), args.p if mode != "k" else 1.0, device=dev)
    k = None
    if mode != "p":
        k = torch.full((B,), args.topk, device=dev, dtype=torch.int32)
        if mode == "mixed":
            k[1::2] = V  # odd rows have no top-k
        elif mode == "onep":
            k[0] = V  # one row has no top-k
        elif mode.startswith("pfrac"):
            k[: max(1, round(B * int(mode[5:]) / 100))] = V
    if mode == "k":
        p = None
    return x, k, p


class Runner:
    def __init__(self, rule, hint, x, k, p):
        self.x, self.buf = x, x.clone()
        buf = self.buf

        def fn():
            tt._topp_split_count = rule
            tt.apply_top_k_top_p_triton(buf, k, p, has_topp_only_rows=hint)

        fn()  # compile and warm up outside capture
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        gc.collect()
        gc.disable()
        try:
            self.g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
            with torch.cuda.graph(self.g):
                fn()
        finally:
            gc.enable()
            tt._topp_split_count = PR_RULE
        torch.cuda.synchronize()

    def rep(self):
        self.buf.copy_(self.x)
        if args.cold:
            FLUSH.zero_()
        st = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        en = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        st.record()
        self.g.replay()
        en.record()
        return st, en


def bench(x, k, p, flip):
    items = list(VARIANTS.items())
    if flip:
        items.reverse()
    ponly = True
    if k is not None and p is not None:
        ponly = bool(((k >= x.shape[1]) & (p < 1)).any())
    runners = {
        n: Runner(rule, ponly if use_hint else True, x, k, p)
        for n, (rule, use_hint) in items
    }
    evs = {n: [] for n in runners}
    for i in range(args.reps + 5):
        for n, r in runners.items():
            e = r.rep()
            if i >= 5:
                evs[n].append(e)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    out = {}
    for n, lst in evs.items():
        ts = sorted(s.elapsed_time(e) * 1e3 for s, e in lst)
        out[n] = ts[len(ts) // 2]
    # Same kept sets? (they may differ only at exact ties at the threshold)
    masks = {}
    for n, r in runners.items():
        r.rep()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        masks[n] = r.buf != float("-inf")
    out["rows_diff"] = int((masks["main"] != masks["pr"]).any(-1).sum())
    return out


real = None
if args.real:
    real = torch.load(args.real, map_location="cpu")["logits"]
    args.vocabs = [real.shape[1]]

print(f"# {props.name}, {NUM_SM} SMs, torch {torch.__version__}, "
      f"{'cold' if args.cold else 'hot'} L2, p={args.p}, k={args.topk}, "
      f"median of {args.reps} graph replays (us)")
aa_hdr = (" A/A |", "---|") if args.aa else ("", "")
print("| vocab | mode | B | S main | S pr | main | pr | speedup | rows diff |" + aa_hdr[0])
print("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|" + aa_hdr[1])
results = []
for V in args.vocabs:
    for mode in args.modes:
        for B in args.bs:
            x, k, p = make_inputs(mode, B, V, real)
            r = bench(x, k, p, flip=len(results) % 2 == 1)
            s_main, s_pr = main_rule(B, V, NUM_SM), PR_RULE(B, V, NUM_SM)
            row = dict(gpu=props.name, sms=NUM_SM, vocab=V, mode=mode, B=B,
                       S_main=s_main, S_pr=s_pr, **r)
            results.append(row)
            print(f"| {V} | {mode} | {B} | {s_main} | {s_pr} | {r['main']:.1f} | "
                  f"{r['pr']:.1f} | {r['main'] / r['pr']:.2f}x | {r['rows_diff']} |"
                  + (f" {r['pr_aa'] / r['pr']:.3f} |" if args.aa else ""),
                  flush=True)
if args.out:
    with open(args.out, "w") as f:
        json.dump(results, f, indent=1)
```

```bash
BS="1 8 16 32 34 38 39 48 64"
python bench_topp_split.py --aa --bs $BS --modes p kp mixed --p 0.95 --topk 50 \
    --vocabs 32000 120832 128896 129280 131072 151936 152576 154880 163840 200064 201088
python bench_topp_split.py --aa --bs $BS --modes p kp mixed --p 0.9 --topk 50 --vocabs 128256
python bench_topp_split.py --aa --bs $BS --modes p kp mixed --p 0.95 --topk 20 --vocabs 248320
python bench_topp_split.py --aa --bs $BS --modes p kp mixed --p 0.95 --topk 64 --vocabs 202048 262144
# share of top-p-only rows; add --no-hint for callers that do not pass the hint
python bench_topp_split.py --aa --vocabs 128256 151936 262144 --bs 16 32 38 48 64 \
    --modes kp onep pfrac10 pfrac25 mixed p
python bench_topp_split.py --aa --real <logits.pt>   # [N, V] "logits" tensor
```
</details>

## Details

**Why more than one program per SM.** Each split program sweeps a `V/S` slice serially, so at small B the call time follows S, not B. I forced S to 1..128 on B300 over 425 top-p-only configs: 6 synthetic logit kinds x 4 vocab sizes plus real MiMo rows, B=1-64. Regret is time over the time at the best S <= 32:

| rule | configs > 5% slower than main | worst vs main | regret, geomean / max |
|---|---|---|---|
| main: `S * B <= num_SMs` | - | - | 1.24 / 2.95 |
| `S * B <= 2 * num_SMs` | 20 | 0.72x | 1.10 / 2.00 |
| `S * B <= 4 * num_SMs` | 69 | 0.59x | 1.07 / 1.87 |
| this PR | 0 | 0.96x | 1.02 / 1.26 |

Pure occupancy targets shrink slices down to 1000 entries at V=32K. Raising `_SPLIT_MAX_SPLITS` would not help at B=38-64, where the one-wave cap is what binds.

**Change 1: split count.** `_topp_split_count` keeps doubling S, still a power of two capped at 32, while either main's condition holds or the doubled S leaves slices of at least `_SPLIT_MIN_SLICE = 7168` entries. The value sits between two measured regimes:
- Around 200K vocab (gpt-oss, MiniMax, Muse), a forced S sweep shows S=32 (about 6.3K-entry slices) 3-24% slower than S=16 for top-p-only rows at B=16-64. S=32 wins only at B=8-24, by up to 20% for half-top-k batches at B=16. So the floor must be above 6314 to exclude it.
- At 256K-262K, S=32 (8.0-8.2K entries) is faster than S=16 in most configs, and at most 4% slower at V=256000 (9% at 262144). So the floor must be at most 8000 to allow it.

Qwen3.8 (248K) lands on S=32 with 7.8K-entry slices. I measured it against main, not against a forced S=16.

S never drops below main's value, and the workspace size is unchanged. The set of S values per vocab can only shrink: at V >= 120K it becomes {32, 16} or just {32}, instead of {32, 16, 8, 4, 2}. The warmup providers already push every B through the same dispatch functions, so no runtime JIT is added.

**Change 2: skip the idle split launch.** `apply_top_k_top_p` gains `has_topp_only_rows: bool = True`. False means no row has p < 1 together with k >= vocab_size. In that case the monolithic kernel already masks every row, including grammar rows whose top-k is a no-op, and the split pipeline is not launched. MRV2's `SamplingStates.has_topp_only_rows()` computes the flag from host-side numpy state, with no sync, and the MRV2 call sites pass it: verification and logits processing via `apply_sampling_params`, non-fused random sampling, and the watermark sampler. So does diffusion_gemma, which uses the MRV2 sampling state. The flag is computed only when both top-k and top-p are active, since it matters only then. MRV1 keeps the default: it gets the new split count but still launches the split pipeline. All-top-k batches there run at 0.90-0.98x (+2 to +23 us) at B=32-64 in the graph-captured microbenchmark (B300 and GB300, V=128K-262K; the "none, without the hint" row below), and at 0.96-0.99x (+2 to +11 us) in the upstream benchmark above.

A cutoff on the share of top-k rows would not work. The gain is largest when only a few rows are top-p-only, and only zero top-p-only rows lose (B300, V=151936):

| top-p-only rows | B=32 | B=38 | B=64 |
|---|---|---|---|
| none, without the hint | 0.97x | 0.95x | 0.91x |
| none, with the hint | 1.09x | 1.07x | 1.05x |
| 1 row | 1.96x | 3.68x | 3.66x |
| 25% | 1.60x | 3.00x | 2.83x |
| 50% | 1.50x | 2.44x | 1.86x |
| all | 1.01x | 1.93x | 1.29x |

**Unchanged: the split/monolithic handover at B=64.** On peaked logits (real MiMo rows, Zipf) the monolithic kernel at B=65 is still faster than the split pipeline at B=64, even with this PR: 318 vs 193 us on MiMo rows. On flat logits the order flips. Where to hand over depends on the distribution, so `_SPLIT_MAX_BATCH` is left alone here.

**Output changes.** S only changes how rows are partitioned, and it already varies with B on main. Kept sets differ only at the p boundary:
- On real (bf16-valued) MiMo logits, every differing token is an exact tie with the boundary logit; this affects 19% of row evaluations.
- On continuous fp32 logits (synthetic flat, peaked and Zipf), 3671 of 41424 row evaluations differ. 2536 of them are not boundary ties and come from fp32 summation order, with kept mass differing by at most 1.1e-4.
- Against a float64 reference, rows below p are unchanged (6 vs 6 over 33776 real-row evaluations). Rows that over-keep boundary copies drop from 6698 to 2445 and rows that under-keep rise from 6 to 30, mostly because the mask kernel's tie count restarts at every 8192-entry block, which shorter slices hit less often. That restart is a pre-existing bug, separate from this PR.

**Scope and limits.** Only the Triton sampler path is affected:
- Spec-decode verification, for any model.
- Non-spec batches that cannot use the fused FlashInfer sampler: per-request seeds, greedy rows in the batch, processed logprobs, or FlashInfer disabled.
- ROCm takes the split path too, and S changes there as well; for example, at V ~152K S becomes 16 from B=20 on MI300X (304 CUs). I have no AMD hardware to measure it.
- GPUs with fewer than 132 SMs were not measured either.

**Related PRs.** No open PR changes the split count for performance.
- #55414 (@njhill) buckets B before the same one-wave rule, to bound the precompiled variants. Since #56323 the warmup dispatcher enumerates every B, so I think its goal is covered. If you still plan to land it, the two compose.
- #56154 (draft) carries a copy of the same dispatchers with the 2-argument `_topp_split_count`.
- #58231, #59540, #59804 and #60104 touch other code in these files. #60104 adds tests right above the `test_topk_and_topp` parametrize line edited here.

title: [MRV2] Collect KV transfer results before the drafter runs
body:
With a speculator, collect the KV connector's transfer results right after sampling and defer only `wait_for_save()` and `clear_connector_metadata()` until after the drafter, via a new `finalize_step()`. Finished loads are then reported without waiting for the drafter, and async loads start before it.

Note this doesn't involve any changes to the KVConnector interface itself.

title: [Kernel] Add router GEMM kernels for (5120, 256) and BF16 output to ll_bf16_gemm
body:
## Overview

First, low-risk slice of #61978 (Reflection Beam): kernel coverage for Beam's router shape and a BF16 output for `ll_bf16_gemm`. Nothing here selects Beam-specific code, and existing shapes, dtypes and dispatch are unchanged. This does not enable the model end to end.

## Claims

- `fp32_router_gemm` supports `(hidden=5120, experts=256)` for up to 48 tokens, with a Blackwell-tuned launch geometry. `GateLinear` uses it for that shape: on SM100 with BF16 input, up to 48 tokens when the count is a multiple of 8, otherwise up to 16. Larger batches go to BF16x3.
- `ll_bf16_gemm` accepts `output_dtype=torch.bfloat16`. It still accumulates in FP32 and only the epilogue changes. This PR also adds tuned split-K configs for K=5120, N∈{1792, 3584}. FP32 output stays the default, and both dtypes keep separate compile-cache entries.
- BF16x3 router GEMM fixes:
  - It raised `KeyError` when a shape had overrides but none for the current token bucket; it now falls back to the heuristic.
  - It returns early for zero tokens.
  - It adds a `(5120, 256)` tile override.
- `grouped_topk` returns empty outputs for zero tokens, e.g. on an idle DP rank, instead of launching the kernel.

## Validation

GB200, run on this branch:

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_fp32_router_gemm.py tests/kernels/test_ll_bf16_gemm.py tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py
```

| Test file | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_fp32_router_gemm.py`: all M in 1..48 for the new shape, range errors per shape, `GateLinear` FP32 precision and top-k with CUDA graph replay | 278 passed |
| `test_ll_bf16_gemm.py`: BF16 output next to FP32 in the cache, CUDA graph replay | 144 passed |
| `test_routing.py`: zero-token `grouped_topk` | 509 passed |

## Details

- The new router GEMM instantiations cover M=1..48 for `(5120, 256)` only. The other shapes keep their limit of 32.
- An existing model would also switch to the FP32 kernel if it has an FP32 router weight, hidden size 5120 and 256 experts, since that pair is now in `GateLinear.FP32_SUPPORTED_SHAPES`.
- Beam's remaining pieces will follow in separate PRs: MegaMoE deferred finalize, parsers and the model itself.
- Not a duplicate: open PRs that touch the router GEMMs (#61903, #50177, #60681) cover other shapes, architectures or compile behavior.

title: [Frontend] Add the Beam reasoning and tool parsers
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Second slice of #61978 (Reflection Beam), after #62042: the `beam` reasoning and tool parsers, in Python and in the Rust frontend. They take effect only with `--reasoning-parser beam` or `--tool-call-parser beam`. This does not enable the model end to end.

## Claims

- **New parsers:** `--reasoning-parser beam` and `--tool-call-parser beam` parse output with the checkpoint's `response_template` metadata, as `hf` does. They also derive a structural-tag grammar from the template, which constrains:
  - strict tools;
  - required and named tool choice;
  - structured outputs;
  - by default, every other request, so output follows the template's format. `VLLM_BEAM_ALWAYS_CONSTRAIN_OUTPUT=0` turns this off.
- **Docs:** `docs/features/tool_calling.md` documents the parser.

## Validation

Results on this branch next to upstream main (fa75d3456d), on the same machine:

| Command | This PR | main |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest tests/parser tests/reasoning tests/tool_parsers --ignore=tests/parser/cohere` | 8267 passed | 8064 passed |
| `cargo test -p vllm-parser` | 578 passed | 561 passed |
| `cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib` | 357 passed | 356 passed |

- **Same failures on both trees, all from this machine's setup:**
  - Python: 10 failed and 117 errors in `tests/parser/mistral` and the Step-3.5 parser tests, because their tokenizers can't be downloaded into the read-only shared HF cache.
  - Rust: the `vllm-chat` `roundtrip` and `grammar_replay` tests, because they need write access to a lock file or that same HF cache.
- **Not run:** `tests/parser/cohere` needs the optional `cohere_melody` package, which isn't installed here.

## Details

- **Shared code touched:**
  - `ParserManager` now picks any response-template parser, not just `hf`. A parser opts in through `unified_parser_cls()`. The `hf` behavior is unchanged except for error messages, which now name the selected flags.
  - `OnlineRenderer` passes the prompt token IDs to the parser before `adjust_request`. Beam needs this to see whether the prompt already opened reasoning or an answer. Only the response-template parsers (`hf`, `beam`) override `set_prompt_token_ids`; for all other parsers the base class method does nothing.
  - `ResponsesRequest` gets two private attributes, so a parser-built grammar can replace `text.format` without changing the request's public fields.
- **Response-template parser fixes**, which also apply to `hf`:
  - When output stops inside a closer whose last part is the next message's start anchor, the parser completes the closer instead of reporting it as malformed.
  - Reasoning tokens are counted incrementally from the template.
- **Size:** about 2.3k non-test lines. Most of it is the grammar builder (`vllm/parser/response_template_grammar.py`) and the Rust `beam` parser.
- **Not a duplicate:** no open PR adds a Beam parser.

title: [Attention] Add CuTe DSL backend selection for MLA context prefill
body:
## Overview

Add an opt-in CuTe DSL kernel for MLA attention over cached context. Default dispatch and new-token prefill remain unchanged.

```bash
--attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"TRTLLM_RAGGED","use_prefill_query_quantization":true,"trtllm_ragged_backend":"cute-dsl"}'
```

For Kimi K3, this requires FP8 KV cache.

## Claims

- Enable CuTe context prefill without changing the default TRTLLM path.
- Align packed indptrs on the CPU, avoiding additional GPU copies.
- Reject unsupported dimensions and dtypes before kernel launch.

This is separate from #56784, which adds CuTe decode selection.

## Validation

Validated on GB300 with FlashInfer 0.7.1: **76 passed, 49 skipped** across kernel correctness, chunk metadata, and prefill selector/registry tests.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py \
  -k test_chunked_context_backend_correctness
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_registry.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_selector.py
```

CUDA-graph microbenchmarks with Kimi's 12 local heads, FP8 Q/K/V, BF16 output, and packed V:

| Query tokens | Cached-context tokens | TRTLLM µs | CuTe µs | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,024 | 8,192 | 71.8 | 56.2 | 1.28× |
| 8,192 | 8,192 | 221.0 | 184.8 | 1.20× |
| 16,384 | 8,192 | 467.2 | 369.8 | 1.26× |

Times are medians of three CUDA-graph timing rounds. These measure context attention, not whole-model throughput.

### End-to-end GSM8K

Validated on 8 GB300 GPUs (two 4-GPU nodes)

Kimi K3 MXFP4 target weights, DSpark draft weights, FlashInfer Python/cubin 0.7.1 and JIT-cache 0.7.1+cu130, TokenSpeed MLA 2.0.3, and PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132.

**`max-num-batched-tokens=256` forces chunked prefill for the GSM8K prompts.** A short trace of a cold 775-token GSM8K prompt before evaluation confirmed **72 CuTe context-attention kernel launches on rank 0** (`kernel_cutlass_kernel_cuteblackwellkernelattentionfmhafmhaBlackwellFusedMultiHeadAttentionForward…`). Profiling was stopped before the full evaluation.

| Task | Questions | Few-shot | Flexible-extract exact match | Strict-match exact match |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K | 1,319 | 5 | **96.36%** (1,271/1,319) | **96.29%** (1,270/1,319) |

Server configuration (run on each node; `NODE_RANK` is 0 or 1, and rank 1 also passes `--headless`). `TARGET_MODEL` and `DRAFT_MODEL` point to the local target/draft checkpoints:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0
export VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=1
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=8

vllm serve "$TARGET_MODEL" \
  --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --nnodes 2 --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --master-addr "$MASTER_ADDR" --master-port 29547 \
  --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
  --trust-remote-code --language-model-only \
  --load-format fastsafetensors --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 256 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 32 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --profiler-config "{\"profiler\":\"torch\",\"torch_profiler_dir\":\"$TRACE_DIR\",\"torch_profiler_with_stack\":false}" \
  --enable-prefix-caching --prefix-match-unit 128 \
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --attention-backend TOKENSPEED_MLA \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"TRTLLM_RAGGED","use_prefill_query_quantization":true,"trtllm_ragged_backend":"cute-dsl"}' \
  --speculative-config "{\"model\":\"$DRAFT_MODEL\",\"attention_backend\":\"TOKENSPEED_MLA\",\"method\":\"dspark\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":4,\"draft_sample_method\":\"greedy\",\"rejection_sample_method\":\"block\"}"
```

No online weight quantization, EP/SP, Mooncake, Dynamo, or synthetic speculative acceptance was enabled. Decode uses TokenSpeed MLA; CuTe is selected only for cached-context prefill. A cached-prefix extension smoke test passed before evaluation.

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args 'base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,max_length=8192,max_gen_toks=256,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None,num_concurrent=32' \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs temperature=0 \
  --seed 42 --log_samples --output_path "$OUTPUT_DIR/gsm8k"
```

## Details

- CuTe requires FP8 queries for head dimension 192 and does not support dimension 256. Runtime validation and test skips share one compatibility helper until FlashInfer exposes a public API.
- CuTe requires packed V. Generic MLA's strided V is copied only when CuTe is selected; already-contiguous V incurs no copy.
- That copy can erase or reverse the speedup on small workloads, so CuTe remains opt-in.

title: [Model] Add Reflection Beam
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add day-0 support for Reflection's Beam-1.0 (`BeamForCausalLM`), a 501B-parameter MoE with 23B active parameters, and its DFlash2 drafter (`DFlash2BeamDraftModel`). This is the model slice of #61978.

Builds on #62042 (merged). This PR doesn't need FlashInfer nightly. The `beam` reasoning and tool parsers are in #62052. The fused MNNVL all-reduce (with Beam's norm and MoE-finalize epilogue) is split out into a stacked follow-up PR. MegaMoE support (attention DP + expert parallelism on FlashInfer CuTeDSL), which does need FlashInfer nightly, follows in #62073.

## Claims

- **Architecture:**
  - hybrid sliding-window (RoPE) and full-attention NoPE layers with SSMax;
  - per-head Q/K norm and a sigmoid output gate;
  - DeepSeek-V3-style MoE with an FP32 router;
  - sandwich norms and depth-scaled residuals.

  It runs with tensor, data or expert parallelism. `BeamConfig` and the model follow the released `config.json` schema (`layer_types`, `mlp_layer_types`, per-type `rope_parameters`); behavior the release does not configure is fixed rather than switchable.
- **Fused kernels for Blackwell**, under `vllm/models/beam/nvidia`: attention, norm/residual boundaries, and DFlash2 context ops. TP all-reduce uses vLLM's standard path in this PR.
- **DFlash2 speculative decoding:** works with FP8 KV cache and adaptive verification. The Beam drafter is self-contained and does not subclass the Qwen3 DFlash classes.

## Validation

**Serving:** Beam-1.0 NVFP4 + DFlash2 (7 draft tokens), TP8 on GB200, SPEED-Bench `throughput_1k` low-entropy subset, greedy decoding. *Measured on the previous revision, which included the fused all-reduce; re-run on this revision pending.*

| Concurrency | Fixed draft (tok/s) | Adaptive (tok/s) | Acceptance length |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 708 | 707 | 3.71 → 3.61 |
| 128 | 15,012 | 16,632 | 3.68 → 3.23 |

```bash
vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4 -tp 4 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --reasoning-parser beam --tool-call-parser beam --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER"}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN"}'
```

**Unit tests** on this branch, GB200. These need no checkpoint: the construction test builds a small random-weight Beam and generates with it (TP/EP up to 4). The released `config.json` files for `reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B` and `-NVFP4` also load through `get_config` (9 NoPE layers, 3 dense layers).

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_beam_construction.py tests/models/test_beam_numerics.py \
  tests/models/test_beam_weight_mapping.py tests/transformers_utils/test_beam_config.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py tests/kernels/moe/test_trtllm_nvfp4_moe.py \
  "tests/test_config.py::test_dflash_candidate_draft_forces_v2_model_runner"
# 301 passed, 2 skipped
```

## Details

- **Shared code touched outside the model directory:**
  - `BeamForCausalLM` is added to `DEFAULT_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH_ARCHITECTURES`.
  - The DFlash2 speculator also selects `DFlash2BeamDraftModel`.
- **Packaging:** no `.cu` sources ship with the model; all kernels here are Triton or CuTeDSL.
- **Not a duplicate:** no other open PR adds Beam.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Fix speculative warmup deadlock with pipeline parallelism
body:
## Overview

Fix a pipeline-parallel startup deadlock in MRV2 speculative decoding introduced by [#59260](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59260).

## Claims

- Ensure all PP stages participate in the additional greedy warmup pass.
- Add regression coverage for matching warmup rounds across PP stages, with speculative decoding enabled and disabled.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mixed_warmup_gate.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py -q
```

- **34 passed** in 9.64 seconds. These suites are covered by the existing `V1 Executor + Worker` CI job.
- **GLM-4.7-Flash smoke test passed**: MRV2, TP=2, PP=2, BF16, MTP with one speculative token, JIT warmup and CUDA graphs enabled.
- Warmup completed and generation produced exactly **1,024 tokens** using `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=1024`, and `ignore_eos=True`. Recorded 532 draft tokens and 492 accepted tokens; process exited successfully.
- Ruff lint and formatting checks passed.

The model run validates startup and generation; no accuracy benchmark was performed.

## Details

Only the last PP stage owns a rejection sampler. Previously, the additional greedy warmup pass was gated on its presence, so earlier stages skipped the pass while the last stage waited for their activations.

Gate this pass on `speculative_config` instead, ensuring every PP stage executes matching forwards. The change is limited to the warmup condition and regression tests.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono decode for the DSpark draft layers
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

DSv4.1-Flash mono decode (MI355X, `--monokernel`): the DSpark draft's three layers now run on the mono K1 / K2 kernels too, as ATOM's `DraftMonoRunner` does, instead of vLLM's per-op path. Follow-up to #60397 and #61082; they follow `--monokernel` like the target's layers, with no new switch. Overlaps files with #60731 (gfx942 port), so whichever merges second needs a rebase.

## Claims

- The draft's three layers cost about 227 us of kernel time per step on mono, in place of about 640 us on the original path (graph profile, TP4 c1): about 414 us less GPU time a step.
- AgentX at c1, per-request ITL p50 is 0.030 ms (1.8%) lower than InferenceX's run with `--monokernel`, at TP4 (1.646 against 1.678 ms) and at TP2 (1.970 against 2.000 ms).
- Draft quality is unchanged: DSpark mean acceptance length 3.889 / 3.935 (TP4) and 3.917 (TP2) against 3.899 / 3.896 without, and GSM8K 0.975 / 0.972.
- Target layers' kernels are untouched: their ISA is identical to `main`'s.

## Validation

All on MI355X, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, the InferenceX #3690 recipe, `main` at `ce49c47cbb` plus this PR unless a row says otherwise. "Off" is the same build with the draft layers on vLLM's path (a throwaway env switch for the A/B, not in this PR).

**Layer level.** The draft layers against the original layers on real eager decode steps (TP4 c1 and TP2 c1, 5- and 10-row steps), same inputs: x output cosine >= 0.99975 (relative L2 up to 2.3%, the MoE's top-3 routing near-ties), residual, post / comb / pre mixes >= 0.9999 cosine.

**Acceptance and accuracy** (real block rejection, GSM8K as in InferenceX's DSv4.1-Flash eval: custom `gsm8k` task, chat, 5-shot multiturn, `max_tokens` 12288, 64 requests in flight, full 1,319):

| | draft on mono: GSM8K strict / flexible; mean acceptance length | draft off |
|---|---|---|
| TP4 | 0.9750 / 0.9742; 3.889 (3.935 on the final rebase) | 0.9750 / 0.9742; 3.899 |
| TP2 | 0.9719 / 0.9712; 3.917 | 0.9727 / 0.9719; 3.896 |

**AgentX, c1, 3,600 s** (InferenceX's `infx.bench agentic` client, the #3690 recipe with `--monokernel`, DSpark with synthetic acceptance 3.51, the Rust frontend). Reference: InferenceX's run [38377181342](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38377181342) (same recipe, nightly 5555a2d8, its own node). TP4 and TP2 ran at the same time on one node. The confidence intervals are bootstrap over the per-request ITL of the profiling phase (about 330 requests an arm).

| | TP4 PR | TP4 ref | TP2 PR | TP2 ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ITL p50 (ms), from the summary | 1.650 | 1.680 | 1.970 | 2.000 |
| per-request ITL p50 (ms), diff [95% CI] | 1.646 | 1.678: -0.032 [-0.034, -0.027] | 1.970 | 2.000: -0.030 [-0.034, -0.026] |
| per-request ITL p90 (ms), diff [95% CI] | 1.690 | 1.757: -0.068 [-0.189, +0.012] | 2.053 | 2.178: -0.125 [-0.292, +0.196] |
| interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 607.6 / 591.8 | 596.1 / 569.1 | 507.6 / 487.1 | 499.9 / 459.1 |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (s) | 0.170 / 0.247 | 0.245 / 0.336 | 0.183 / 0.293 | 0.210 / 0.383 |
| E2E p50 (s) | 1.85 | 1.93 | 2.14 | 2.18 |
| requests completed | 335 | 331 | 318 | 316 |

The p50 gain is outside the noise at both TP sizes; the p90 interactivity gain (+4.0% and +6.1%) is not (its interval spans zero), and the TTFT difference is the node, not this PR (prefill is untouched). The reference is not a same-node baseline, so the p50 difference also includes any difference of node, image and commit; an earlier run on the same node of `main` plus only #61934's change (a different kernel change) gave ITL p50 1.670 / 2.000 ms (per-request 1.675 / 1.998).

**Kernel time** (graph-mode torch profile, TP4 c1, draft on mono): K1 about 20 us and K2 about 56 us a layer for the three draft layers (227 us a step); the non-target kernels of a step total 1.76 ms against 2.17 ms with the draft off (excluding all-reduce spin-waits).

**Tests.** `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`: 41 pass, 3 new (the draft layer takes the mono path on its own runner, its first layer takes the broadcast embedding, a layer takes only its own SWA row width). The K1 / K2 ISA of the target builds at TP4, M=6 is identical to `main`'s (`FLYDSL_DUMP_IR` diff: 0 lines).

**Accuracy** (RFC #59665 protocol, as in #60397: thinking on, `reasoning_effort` high, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, 8 requests in flight a server, DSpark with block rejection, `--monokernel` so the draft layers run on mono; pass@1, ± is the standard error across questions). The baselines are #60397's numbers; no reference arm of this build was rerun.

| | this PR | #60397 |
|---|---|---|
| TP2 GPQA-Diamond (8 samples a question) | 84.8 ± 2.2 | 85.3 ± 2.2 reference, 85.1 ± 2.2 mono |
| TP2 AIME25 (16 samples a problem) | 98.3 ± 0.9 | 99.4 ± 0.3 reference, 98.3 ± 0.8 mono |
| TP4 GPQA-Diamond (4 samples a question) | 84.5 ± 2.3 | 85.2 ± 2.2 mono |
| TP4 AIME25 (8 samples a problem) | 98.8 ± 0.7 | 100.0 mono (240/240) |

AIME25's wrong samples: 8 of 480 at TP2 (3 empty, out of the 64K budget; 4 on one hard problem) and 3 of 240 at TP4 (1 empty).

**RULER NIAH** (lm-eval, prefix-free chat copies, thinking on, greedy, 40 samples a cell): `niah_single_1`, `niah_multikey_2` and `niah_multikey_3` at 32K, 128K and 256K score 40/40 in every cell at both TP2 and TP4, as in #60397.

## Details

The draft layers are `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer`s with window-only attention (compress ratio 0, no indexer), so the kernels need no new stage. What differs is carried by the build and the step's integers:

- **Routing:** 128 routed experts, top-3 (`dspark_n_routed_experts` / `dspark_num_experts_per_tok`) and one FP4 group per ug task. `MoeBuild` already took these; `MonoBuild` now carries `experts`, `topk`, `ug_groups` and `swa_width` into the MoE stage and the scratch layout.
- **SWA rows:** the draft's metadata is non-causal, with rows `get_dspark_swa_index_width(window, num_speculative_tokens)` wide (192 for window 128 and 5 drafts). K1's key-table stage read the row width as the constant 128; it reads it from the build now.
- **First layer:** the draft hands it the embedding already repeated to the hc copies, `[rows, hc, dim]`; K1 takes it as the settled residual (`fold=False`), as for the target's layer 0.
- **Its own runner:** the scratch layout depends on the number of experts, and a mailbox word must never be a tag to one launch and data to another, so the draft's layers share a second `DSV41MonoLayer` (epoch, scratch, peer buffers) as in ATOM. Every rank creates it at the same layer of the same eager step, like the target's.

Target builds are unchanged: every new field defaults to the target's value, the kernel symbols gain no suffix for them, and the ISA diff above is empty.

Limitations: MI355X (CDNA4), TP2 / TP4, steps of at most 48 rows (the draft's are 5 per request, so up to 8 requests); the layer comparison is on eager steps only. The draft's remaining per-step cost is outside its layers: `_prepare_dflash_inputs` (3 launches of 113 us), the six skinny head GEMMs (279 us), and about 75 small elementwise and copy kernels. I found no open PR doing this. Developed and measured with Claude Code; the submitter's line-by-line review is still pending.

title: [Feature][PCP] Support APC and encoder-side SWA bounded replay for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
body:
## Overview

Follow up on #59857 to enable automatic prefix caching (APC) together with encoder-side SWA bounded replay for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash under PCP in a colocated model instance. The initial PCP implementation rejected APC; this change enables the PCP + APC + encoder-side replay combination.

## Claims

- Enable local APC prefix hits under PCP and rebuild the SWA tail through encoder-side bounded replay while preserving cached compressed KV and indexer keys across ranks.
- Decoder-side tail trimming remains disabled under PCP; scheduled rows execute the normal decoder layers.

## Validation

### Environment

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
- Hardware: two separate nodes, each with 8x NVIDIA H20 97,871 MiB; driver 535.161.08
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294`
- Baseline: the image + prerequisite #59857
- Candidate: the same image and prerequisite + This PR; APC and bounded replay were enabled.
- Common topology: TP2/PCP4, PP1, DCP1, Humming MoE, eager execution, and synchronous scheduling.

Candidate launch command:

```bash
python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 18001 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --block-size 64 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --moe-backend humming \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --swa-bounded-replay \
  --enforce-eager \
  --no-async-scheduling
```

Baseline used the same command except:

```bash
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-swa-bounded-replay
```

### Prefix-repetition performance

Both arms ran concurrently with byte-identical deterministic inputs:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai \
  --base-url http://<HOST>:18001 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --tokenizer /tmp/dsv41-tokenizer \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --dataset-name prefix_repetition \
  --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 1024 \
  --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 128 \
  --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 10 \
  --prefix-repetition-output-len 1 \
  --num-prompts 80 \
  --num-warmups 8 \
  --request-rate inf \
  --max-concurrency 8 \
  --seed 42 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --ignore-eos \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,e2el \
  --disable-tqdm
```

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Successful requests | 80/80 | 80/80 | - |
| Mean TTFT | 640.73 ms | 386.73 ms | **-39.64%** |
| Median TTFT | 570.56 ms | 346.28 ms | **-39.31%** |
| P99 TTFT | 907.04 ms | 712.10 ms | **-21.49%** |
| Effective input throughput | 13,837.87 tok/s | 22,499.21 tok/s | **+62.59%** |
| Request throughput | 12.01 req/s | 19.53 req/s | **+62.59%** |
| Prefix-cache token hit ratio | disabled | 80,384/101,376 (79.29%) | - |

Every measured request had exactly 1,152 input tokens and one output token. There were no failed requests or Pod restarts.

### Full GSM8K

Both arms ran the same full 1,319-sample ModelScope test split:

```bash
evalscope eval \
  --eval-type openai_api \
  --api-url http://<HOST>:18001/v1 \
  --api-key EMPTY \
  --model deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --model-id deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --datasets gsm8k \
  --dataset-hub modelscope \
  --dataset-args '{"gsm8k":{"few_shot_num":4}}' \
  --seed 42 \
  --eval-batch-size 64 \
  --generation-config '{"temperature":0.0,"top_p":1.0,"max_tokens":8192,"reasoning_effort":"high","seed":42,"timeout":10000}' \
  --timeout 10000
```

EvalScope version: 1.11.1.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Accuracy | 1279/1319 (96.97%) | 1284/1319 (97.35%) |
| API errors | 0 | 0 |

Paired outcomes were 1,277 both correct, 33 both wrong, 7 candidate-only correct, and 2 baseline-only correct. The exact two-sided McNemar p-value was `0.1797`, so the observed `+0.38 pp` accuracy difference is not statistically significant. Candidate GSM8K traffic recorded 674,816/803,206 local prefix-cache hit tokens (84.02%).

## Details

Reuse the existing scheduler replay boundary and padding kernel, stage replay starts per local PCP segment, mask each rank's own cacheable slots, and gather those slots back in the same rank-major order as KV publication. All ranks participate even when a peer has no replay rows; SWA and compressor scratch mappings stay unchanged. The additional slot metadata collective applies only to PCP batches with encoder replay enabled. Production changes are confined to DeepSeek-V4.1 files, with the existing non-PCP path and other PCP restrictions retained.

This does not duplicate #61554, which targets cold-prefill decoder trimming with prefix caching disabled. Enable APC and encoder-side replay with `--enable-prefix-caching --swa-bounded-replay`. The supported scope is NVIDIA CUDA, MRV2, eager execution, synchronous scheduling and PP=DP=DCP=1. KV connectors, speculative decoding, microbatching and MegaMoE remain unsupported with PCP. AI assistance was used for implementation and Codex CLI review; human line-by-line review remains pending, while GPU/model validation is documented above.

## Overview

Match the Python DeepSeek V4.1 encoder to the updated reference [`encoding/`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017/tree/main/encoding). Rust counterpart: #62200.

Affects both V4.1-Flash checkpoints (launch and 1017). DeepSeek fixed the turn handling in both repos ([launch `314113f`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/commit/314113f8a7dadb388215396ba5fbee2c610a04d6), 1017 release); their `encoding/` is now identical. The image-token check has been in the reference since launch.

## Claims

- Tool results alone no longer start a new user turn, so reasoning before a tool call is kept.
- Literal `<｜deepseek_image｜>` in message text or reasoning returns 400.
- All five reference golden prompts match. V4 is unchanged.

## Examples

**1. Tool call in thinking mode, with no `tools` field in the request**

```python
[{"role": "user", "content": "What's the weather in Paris? Answer in Fahrenheit."},
 {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "reasoning": "Tool returns Celsius; convert to Fahrenheit.",
  "tool_calls": [{"id": "c1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "arguments": "{\"city\": \"Paris\"}"}}]},
 {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "c1", "content": "{\"temp_c\": 20}"}]
```

Before (reasoning dropped):
```
<｜User｜>What's the weather in Paris? Answer in Fahrenheit.<｜Assistant｜></think>

<｜DSML｜ calls>...
```
After (reasoning kept, same as the reference encoder):
```
<｜User｜>What's the weather in Paris? Answer in Fahrenheit.<｜Assistant｜><think>Tool returns Celsius; convert to Fahrenheit.</think>

<｜DSML｜ calls>...
```

**2. Literal image token in text**

```python
[{"role": "user", "content": "hi <｜deepseek_image｜>"}]
```

Before: accepted, so the prompt has an image placeholder with no image. After: 400.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py`: 84 passed. The new tests fail on main.
- E2E on 8x H100 (TP8, recipe H100 flags, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017): the prompt keeps the tool-call reasoning and matches the reference encoder; the literal image token returns 400.
- GSM8K (chat, thinking off, 1319 questions): 0.970.

## Details

Not a duplicate: #60792 (image order) and other open V4.1 tokenizer PRs don't change turn boundaries or placeholder validation. Fixtures are copied from the 1017 repo (MIT).

title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep the EAGLE-reachable SWA tail at a shared-prefix junction
body:
## Overview

This PR fixes cross-request prefix reuse for sliding-window groups under EAGLE/MTP with sparse prefix-cache retention. The shared-prefix junction pin from #47782 kept a sliding-window tail one block too high, so requests that share only a prefix got no prefix-cache hit at all. The fix also pins the tail one block lower, which is where an EAGLE sibling's hit actually lands.

## Claims

- Under sparse retention, a sibling request that shares only a prefix now gets a prefix-cache hit when the drafter's groups are sliding-window and the full-attention groups are not EAGLE groups. On Step-5-Preview with MTP, the GSM8K 5-shot prefix goes from 0 hit tokens to a hit on every request after the first two.
- Nothing changes without EAGLE, or when every group is flagged as an EAGLE group. In those cases the junction already sits one block lower, because the full-attention group drops its block too.
- The cost is one extra cached block per sliding-window group for each request that registers a junction.

## Validation

**Unit test.** `test_swa_shared_prefix_reuse_under_zero_retention` gets a `use_eagle` case that flags only the SWA group, as https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61455 does for drafters. It fails on main (0 instead of 48 hit tokens) and passes with the fix.

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/prefix_cache \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py
620 passed, 2 errors
```

The 2 errors are `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate`, which needs a GPU and a model checkpoint (the run was CPU-only). On a wider set (`tests/v1/core`, Mooncake Store and offloading connector unit tests), the failure set with and without this PR is identical (GPU- or model-dependent tests), apart from the new case.

**End to end.** Step-5-Preview (MTP layers are sliding-window, the target also has full-attention DSA layers), 4x GB300, TP4 + EP, MTP k=3. Prefix caching runs with `--prefix-cache-retention-interval 1024`. The test runs on the Step5 preview branch of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61727, with this change applied.

12 GSM8K 5-shot prompts are sent one at a time. They share a 565-token prefix, and every prompt is shorter than 1024 tokens.

| | request 1 | request 2 | requests 3–12 |
|---|---|---|---|
| no MTP | 0 | 0 | 560 each |
| MTP k=3, without this PR | 0 | 0 | **0** |
| MTP k=3, this PR | 0 | 0 | 544 each |

Request 2 detects the junction, so later requests can hit. 544 is one block below the 560-token junction, which is the deepest hit an EAGLE lookup can verify.

Full GSM8K (1319 questions, concurrency 64, MTP k=3, Mooncake Store connector on):

| | without this PR | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| local prefix-cache hit tokens / queried | 0 / 839,793 | 737,520 / 839,793 (87.8%) |
| accuracy | 0.933 | 0.935 |
| Mooncake Store replay vs GPU-cache replay | 64/64 bit-identical | 64/64 bit-identical |

## Details

**Root cause.**
1. Request A runs alone.
2. Request B shares a prefix with A, but under sparse retention only A's full-attention blocks are still cached. `get_computed_blocks` reports the junction J as the full-attention hit length (B's shared prefix floored to a block), and B pins J.
3. The sliding-window mask keeps the `need`-block tail at J. Under EAGLE, that tail is shifted one block right, to include the block past J as the lookahead (#44082). This is right for a replay of the same prompt.
4. The block past J holds B's own tokens, so for request C it is not shared. C's SWA lookup must verify one block past its hit, so its best hit is J − block_size. That hit needs the window one block lower than the pinned tail, and the lowest block was never kept.
5. C gets no hit and pins the same J again, so no later request ever hits.

When every group takes the EAGLE drop (no group flagged), the full-attention hit is already one block lower, so J lands where the SWA hit can verify. The bug therefore shows only when a sliding-window group is an EAGLE group and the full-attention group that reports the junction is not. Step5 MTP already met this under the older "group holding the last registered layer" rule. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61455 makes per-group flags the general rule: drafters whose layers are sliding-window now flag only those groups.

**Fix.** Under EAGLE, `cache_blocks` registers both J and J − block_size as reachable boundaries. The masks overlap, so this keeps one extra block. Replay boundaries are unchanged, because they already account for the EAGLE drop (#54713, #61012). Mamba checkpointing reads `shared_prefix_boundary` directly and is unaffected.

**Not covered.** `OffloadingConnector` builds its own reachable boundaries from `shared_prefix_boundary` and is not changed here.

title: [Bugfix][DeepSeek V4.1] Inject Engram at pipeline stage entry
body:
## Overview

DeepSeek-V4.1 applies trained Engram modules at configured transformer layers. If a pipeline partition starts a non-initial stage on one of those layers, the stage-entry control-flow branch calls mHC pre directly and bypasses the normal Engram branch. Certain valid PP partitions can therefore silently skip an Engram operation for every request. The real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash configuration triggers this at layer 14 with `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=14,26`.

This PR restores the missing NVIDIA operation by applying the local stage-entry Engram after receiving the previous stage's completed residual stream and before mHC pre.

**AMD is affected by the same issue. We currently only have access to NVIDIA hardware, so this PR fixes only the NVIDIA implementation for now.**

## Claims

- Restore Engram when its layer is the first layer of a non-initial pipeline stage.
- Preserve the incoming `pre_mix`, selected Engram hash column, mask, and existing no-hash behavior.
- Add a non-identity regression test to the NVIDIA model CI job.

## Validation

### Environment

- Hardware: two 8 x NVIDIA H20 96GB nodes.
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294`.

### vLLM launch

Both arms used identical arguments:

```bash
VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=14,26 \
VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1 \
vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 18001 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --block-size 64 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --moe-backend humming \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-swa-bounded-replay \
  --enforce-eager \
  --no-async-scheduling
```

### Verify Engram execution at the pipeline boundary

This check verifies that layer 14 executes its trained Engram module before mHC pre when it is the first layer of a pipeline stage.

We compared three configurations using the real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash checkpoint:

- **Without this PR, PP=1:** the reference configuration. Layer 14 runs within the same pipeline stage as the preceding layers.
- **Without this PR, PP=2 (`14,26`):** the configuration that exposes the bug. The first stage contains 14 layers, so the second stage starts at layer 14.
- **With this PR, PP=2 (`14,26`):** the same pipeline partition with the fix applied, tested independently on both H20 nodes.

Each configuration received the same fixed 256-token prompt and generated two tokens, each constrained to a single allowed token ID. This kept the token sequence fixed across configurations. Each configuration was run twice in eager mode.

#### Was layer 14's Engram actually executed?

| Configuration | Layer 14 Engram executed? | Input passed to layer 14's mHC pre |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Without this PR, PP=1 — reference | Yes | Engram output |
| Without this PR, PP=2 (`14,26`) | **No** | Tensor received from the previous stage, without applying Engram |
| With this PR, PP=2 (`14,26`) — both nodes | **Yes** | Engram output |

The unpatched PP=2 configuration had valid Engram hashes and masks available at layer 14, but never called its Engram module. The missing operation was therefore caused by the stage-entry control flow.

#### Did mHC receive the correct tensor?

We recorded SHA-256 checksums of the full tensors at the pipeline handoff, Engram input/output, and mHC pre input. These checksums track tensor contents; they are separate from the token hashes used by Engram.

For every TP rank, measured step, and repeat, the checks confirmed these paths:

- **Without this PR, PP=2:** the tensor sent by the previous stage was passed directly to mHC pre. Engram was skipped.
- **With this PR, PP=2:** the received tensor was passed to Engram, and Engram's output was passed to mHC pre.
- **PP=1 reference:** Engram's output was also passed to mHC pre.

These comparisons verify the data flow within each run; they do not require bitwise-identical outputs between PP=1 and PP=2.

#### Did Engram make a measurable change?

For runs that executed Engram, we measured the difference between its input and output at layer 14:

| Step | RMS of the Engram update | Tensor elements whose stored values changed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Prefill | 0.03445–0.03557 | 67.22%–67.82% |
| Decode | 0.05899–0.06505 | 81.83%–83.14% |

The update RMS is `RMS(Engram output − Engram input)`. These nonzero differences confirm that skipping this trained Engram module changes the tensor passed to mHC pre.

**This check confirms that the affected PP partition skips a trained Engram operation and that this PR restores it before mHC pre on both tested nodes.** It does not establish an accuracy improvement: captured logits varied across repeated runs and nodes by an amount comparable to the patch effect. The GSM8K results below report the separate end-to-end accuracy evaluation.

### Full GSM8K comparison

Both configurations used PP=2 (`14,26`) with identical evaluation settings: 4-shot, temperature 0, seed 42, and a maximum of 8,192 output tokens.

```bash
evalscope eval \
  --eval-type openai_api \
  --api-url http://<node-ip>:18001/v1 \
  --api-key EMPTY \
  --model deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --model-id deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --datasets gsm8k \
  --dataset-hub modelscope \
  --dataset-args '{"gsm8k":{"few_shot_num":4}}' \
  --seed 42 \
  --eval-batch-size 64 \
  --generation-config '{"temperature":0.0,"top_p":1.0,"max_tokens":8192,"reasoning_effort":"high","seed":42,"timeout":10000}' \
  --timeout 10000 \
  --no-timestamp
```

| Configuration | Correct / Total | Accuracy | API errors | Pod restarts |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Without this PR | 1283 / 1319 | 97.27% | 0 | 0 |
| With this PR | 1283 / 1319 | 97.27% | 0 | 0 |

Seven questions were correct only without the patch, and seven only with it; aggregate accuracy was unchanged.

**We have not observed an end-to-end accuracy loss in this GSM8K evaluation. However, the confirmed omission of a trained Engram operation remains a correctness bug with potential model-quality impact that this benchmark has not demonstrated.**

The focused regression test and full pre-commit suite also passed.

## Details

At the end of a pipeline stage, the previous rank completes its final mHC post and sends the full 3-D residual stream together with `pre_mix`. The next stage starts with `residual=None`, assigns that received stream to `residual`, and calls mHC pre directly. Because normal Engram injection lives in the following `elif`, an Engram on the stage's first layer is silently skipped.

This change injects the local Engram after accepting the completed stream and before mHC pre. It does not repeat the previous stage's post or alter first-layer embeddings, in-stage Engram execution, or batches without Engram hashes.

The real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash configuration has Engram layers 1 and 14. A pipeline partition beginning its second stage at layer 14 can therefore reach this path. Open PR searches for the same Engram pipeline-stage fix found no direct duplicate; related PCP work such as #62183 does not implement this injection.
