title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Apply text-only LoRAs to the LM of multimodal wrappers
body:
## Overview

Fixes #48019. A LoRA trained on the text-only `*ForCausalLM` of a multimodal model silently does nothing when served on the multimodal wrapper. This resolves such adapters on the model side, in `LoRAModelManager._get_lora_layer_weights`, so it works for every multimodal wrapper without per-model mapper rules.

This builds on #49525 by @fooSynaptic (co-author), which fixes the same bug through a `WeightsMapper` fallback and only covers wrappers whose mapper has a `model.language_model.` rule. This PR covers those wrappers too, plus the ones without such a rule.

## Claims

- Text-named adapters (`model.layers.*` / `lm_head`) now apply to the language model of multimodal wrappers, including wrappers with no `model.language_model.` mapper rule or a different LM prefix (`llm.`, `model.text_model.`), e.g. Llama4, DeepSeek-V4, MiniCPM-V, Idefics3/SmolVLM.
- Adapters that already match (trained on the full multimodal class), tower/connector LoRA, and text-only models are unchanged.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py tests/lora/test_utils.py tests/lora/test_lora_checkpoints.py
```

- New test `test_text_only_lora_binds_to_multimodal_language_model`: 3 passed (all 3 fail on main).
- The three files above: 58 passed.

E2E on 1x H20: one synthetic r=16 LoRA on the LM's q/k/v/o/gate/up/down_proj, saved twice: text-named (`base_model.model.model.layers.*`) and wrapper-named (`base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.*`, or `model.text_model.layers.*` for SmolVLM). Prompt logprobs of 4 prompts from vLLM base / text-named / wrapper-named, compared with an HF reference that has the LoRA merged into the weights.

Mean |Δ logprob| of the text-named adapter vs vLLM base (HF LoRA effect in parentheses):

| model | main | #49525 | this PR | this PR vs HF LoRA (wrapper-named vs HF) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-4B-Base (0.056) | 0.0000 | 0.0534 | 0.0535 | 0.0146 (0.0134) |
| llava-1.5-7b-hf (0.060) | 0.0000 | 0.0575 | 0.0565 | 0.0126 (0.0111) |
| SmolVLM-256M-Instruct (0.104) | 0.0000 | **0.0000** | 0.0948 | 0.0486 (0.0507) |

vLLM-vs-HF base noise: 0.017 / 0.017 / 0.063. Llama4 and DeepSeek-V4 were not run (too large); they use the same `language_model.` prefix path as Qwen3.5.

## Details

**Root cause.** PEFT on the text-only class (what `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3.5-*")` returns in transformers 5.x, i.e. the default TRL SFT path) names modules `model.layers.*` / `lm_head`. vLLM's multimodal wrappers mount the language model under `language_model.`, `llm.` or `model.text_model.`. `activate_adapter` looks weights up by the full module name, finds none, and serves the base model; load-time validation only checks the leaf name (`q_proj`), so nothing fails.

**Fix.** When a LoRA module has no exact match and lives under `get_mm_mapping().language_model`, look it up by its text-only name: the remainder after the prefix, or the remainder under `model.` when the prefix holds a bare decoder. All lookups, including packed (`qkv_proj`, `gate_up_proj`) and MoE packing, go through this function; text-named entries consumed by packing are dropped like the other sub-module entries.

- Exact names always win, so adapters trained on the full multimodal class are unaffected. No tower/connector prefix of any in-tree LoRA-capable multimodal model is nested under its LM prefix, so tower/connector lookups are unchanged.
- The lookup is driven by the model's real modules, so there is no double-mapping risk (e.g. `model.language_model. -> model.` mappers) and no effect on layers owned by other PP ranks.
- No change to base-weight loading or to any model's `hf_to_vllm_mapper`.
- No new validation or error path, and no separate name-matching logic: the fallback lives inside the existing lookup, so any future "adapter matches nothing" check can reuse `_get_lora_layer_weights` and stay consistent with what is actually applied.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Keep the Engram all-to-all buffers in one allocator
body:
## Overview

DeepSeek-V4.1 with host-offloaded, DP-sharded Engram tables (`cpu_offload: true`, `dp_shared_memory: false`, e.g. with `use_thp: true`) hangs in the first forward (memory profiling) when `--enable-cumem-allocator` is set. This receives the Engram all-to-all into a persistent buffer allocated next to its send buffer, so both come from the same allocator.

No open PR covers this (searched open PRs/issues for Engram all-to-all, cumem, `NCCL_LOCAL_REGISTER`). #62091 changes only the GPU-table path (`cpu_offload: false`), which has no all-to-all.

## Claims

- Fixes the hang: DSv4.1-Flash DEP2/DEP4 prefill with host DP-sharded Engram + `--enable-cumem-allocator` now starts and serves.
- No numerical change: the same bytes are exchanged, only the receive buffer's allocation changes. Peak memory is unchanged (the per-step `empty_like` of the same size becomes persistent).

## Validation

GB200 (4 GPUs/node), vLLM nightly 49cb2bbf image (CUDA 13.4, NCCL 2.32.3), env `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1`. The changed code is identical on main.

Serving: `vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --enable-cumem-allocator --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"embedding_across_dp":true,"use_thp":true}' --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' ...` (same hang with DEP2).

| run | result |
|---|---|
| main | hangs in `determine_available_memory`; all ranks in `EngramBatch._stage` `all_to_all_single` (py-spy, also with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`), GPUs spin at 100%, NCCL watchdog fires after 600 s |
| main, no `--enable-cumem-allocator` | starts |
| main, `NCCL_LOCAL_REGISTER=0` | starts |
| this PR | starts (profiling + CUDA graph capture); 48/48 completions with 8 to 30K-word prompts at concurrency 16 (both the all-to-all and the peer-exchange slots) |

Standalone reproducer, no model (4 GPUs):

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
# torchrun --nproc-per-node 4 repro.py [--same-pool]
import os
import sys

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist

from vllm.device_allocator.cumem import CuMemAllocator

torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]))
dist.init_process_group("nccl")
shape = (32768 * dist.get_world_size(), 2, 6, 264)
with CuMemAllocator.get_instance().use_memory_pool(tag="weights"):
    sent = torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
    pool_recv = torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
recv = pool_recv if "--same-pool" in sys.argv else torch.zeros_like(sent)
dist.all_to_all_single(recv, sent)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
print(f"rank {dist.get_rank()} ok")
```

</details>

| send | recv | result |
|---|---|---|
| cumem pool | caching allocator | hangs (killed after 120 s) |
| cumem pool | cumem pool (`--same-pool`) | ok |
| cumem pool | caching allocator, `NCCL_LOCAL_REGISTER=0` | ok |

`pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py` passes. No test added: reproducing needs 4+ GPUs with NCCL 2.32 and the cumem allocator, which CI does not run for DSv4.1; validation above was done outside CI.

## Details

Root cause: `EngramBatch.__init__` runs during model init, inside the cumem pool when `--enable-cumem-allocator` is set, so `packed_rows` (the all-to-all send buffer) is a cumem allocation. The receive buffer was `torch.empty_like(rows)` in each forward, from the caching allocator. With NCCL local user-buffer registration on (the default), NCCL 2.32 hangs an all-to-all whose buffers mix the two allocators; the reproducer shows this without the model. I did not pin down the NCCL-internal reason (the serving logs show FABRIC IPC registration failures for some buffers, the reproducer hangs without them).

Allocating the receive buffer next to `packed_rows` keeps both in one allocator in either mode, and removes a per-step allocation. `_stage` is an eager break, so the persistent buffer does not affect CUDA graphs.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate and write this change; I reviewed every line and ran the validation above.

title: [Doc][ROCm] Align Kimi-K3 MI355X recipe with InferenceX #4215
body:
## Overview

Align the Kimi-K3 MI355X TP8 recipe and its AgentX guide with [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4215](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4215) (branch revision `6e72cbc11234e624d66b8fc5eaddac50068db15c`), which supersedes the InferenceX #3833 lane that vllm-project/recipes#1093 documented. Recipes for vLLM-served models now live here (#61302), so this changes only `recipes/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.yaml`.

## Claims

- MI355X TP8 command builder: drop the `--load-format fastsafetensors` override so the AMD profile's default loader applies (on the lane's image, fastsafetensors ran out of GPU memory while loading weights, [InferenceX run 38975751686](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38975751686)), and add `AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8=1`.
- AgentX guide: the ten #4215 cells (dcp1 c1/c4; dcp8 c4-c60 with SimpleCPUOffload), per-cell online FP8 target quantization (c1 no longer ignores `*in_proj_qkvgfab`; every other cell quantizes only `in_proj_qkvgfab`), `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4` with `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MIN_SIZE_BYTES_MB=16`, the pinned image, and the golden-AL table for 7/5/4 draft tokens.
- Fix two errors in the previous guide: `seq -s, 2 "$MAX_CAPTURE"` captured odd CUDA-graph sizes (now even only, as the text states), and `AITER_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION` is not read by vLLM (the lane sets `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION`).
- Real serving stays on block verification; synthetic acceptance stays in the separate throughput-only section. The `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` draft stays at its shipped precision: BF16 weights and activations, FP8 KV.

## Validation

- Ground truth: the #4215 lane recipe and `amd-master.yaml` entry at `6e72cbc` are identical to in-PR commit `8a2aec3`, which passed all ten cells and their evals in [InferenceX run 39002920671](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/39002920671) on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294`, with real block verification: GSM8K 0.969 strict/flexible (dcp8 c60) and `kimi_tool_call_schema_full` 0.978-0.998 (nine cells).
- From vllm-project/recipes main (`b8bec4f`), pointed at this checkout: `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <vllm>/recipes` (valid, 215 recipes), `node scripts/build-recipes-api.mjs` and `pnpm build` all pass; the rendered MI355X builder command and guide section were checked in a local browser.
- Generated-command diff against this branch's base: of the 71 Kimi-K3 JSON API files, only `hw/mi355x.json`, the two MI355X Mooncake KV-store strategies (which reuse the TP8 command) and `Kimi-K3.json` (guide, `date_updated`) change. The MI355X command changes only `--load-format fastsafetensors` to `auto` and adds `AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8=1`; every other hardware and strategy file is identical.
- The guide's reproduction script, run for each of the ten cells with `vllm` stubbed, resolves arguments and environment equal to the #4215 lane: draft tokens, `--max-num-seqs`, `--max-num-batched-tokens`, even capture sizes 2..max, quantization, speculative and offload configs, DCP8, QuickReduce and `PYTHONHASHSEED`. Stale #3833 cells (dcp8 c1/c2/c12/c14/c44) are rejected. All 12 guide bash blocks pass `bash -n`, and all 12 embedded JSON values parse.
- `pre-commit run --files recipes/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.yaml` passes; `git diff --check` is clean.
- No new GPU run: the recipe documents the exact configuration validated by the InferenceX run above.

## Details

- Not duplicate work: no open PR in vllm-project/vllm or vllm-project/recipes references InferenceX #4215, `in_proj_qkvgfab`, `AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8` or `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MIN_SIZE_BYTES_MB` (searched 2026-10-18); the open Kimi-K3 MI355X PRs here are kernel changes.
- INT4 QuickReduce is lossy, so as before it stays out of the builder and appears only in the exact reproduction command. The 16 MiB floor keeps it off the draft: the draft's all-reduces carry at most 600 draft-step tokens x 7,168 BF16 values (about 8.2 MiB at c60), and its context projection is replicated.
- `AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8=1` stores the FlyDSL MoE down-projection route outputs as MXFP8 before the top-k sum. It changes only the target's MoE (the DSpark draft MLP is dense) and the lane sets it at every cell, so it goes in the builder. `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0` is not read on the SiTUv2 path and stays out of both, as before.

- Not changed: the MI355X disaggregated P/D example still uses `fastsafetensors` and the rolling `nightly` image; it is a separate deployment that #4215 does not cover.

title: [ROCm][CI] Bump the ROCm 10 image to torch 2.13
body:
- Bump `TORCH_VERSION` to `2.13.0+rocm10.0.0` and `TORCHVISION_VERSION` to `0.28.0+rocm10.0.0` in `Dockerfile.rocm_base`
- Release the piecewise CUDA graphs on ROCm in Model Runner V2's `shutdown()` before distributed teardown, as the V1 runner already does

When #58761 made the TheRock image the default, AMD CI went from torch 2.13 (the ROCm 7.2 image, bumped in #50605) back to 2.12, because the TheRock Dockerfile never got that bump. #61118 sets `torch._inductor.config.batch_invariant`, which only exists from torch 2.13, so every engine started with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` died with `AttributeError: torch._inductor.config.batch_invariant does not exist` (Batch Invariance on MI250/MI300/MI355, the DPX LoRA shards, LoRA TP and Spec Decode Draft Model since https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95651). #62274 now skips the setting when torch lacks it; this restores the inductor batch-invariant mode on ROCm. This goes to 2.13 rather than 2.14, which is what the ROCm 7.2 image runs: 2.14's ATen headers require C++20, while the pinned flash-attention builds its ROCm extension with `-std=c++17`, so the base image fails to build with 2.14 (https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95690). This supersedes #59658, which made the same bump against `Dockerfile.rock_base` before #58761 renamed it.

`:amd: (MI355) Distributed DP + EP` still aborts at exit with `terminate called without an active exception` after #62241 (https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95767). The MoE all-gather on the DP group is captured in the piecewise graphs, and RCCL's `ncclCommAbort` waits until every graph that captured the communicator is destroyed (ROCm/rocm-systems#13018). The V2 runner never released them, so the abort hung on every rank with a cold compile cache, `PyNcclCommunicator.destroy()` gave up after its 5 s join, and the process exited with the abort still inside RCCL (stack: `ncclCommAbort_impl -> commReclaim -> commDestroySync -> condition_variable::wait`). On 8x MI355 with the CI command and a fresh cache each run, the abort now finishes in under 1 s in 10/10 runs with every PyNccl communicator destroyed, and the `Distributed Torchrun + Shutdown` commands and the V2 runner tests pass. As in V1, `clear_all_graphs()` is process-wide.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Frontend] Serve Gemma 4 on /v1/systemone and /v1/decisions
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Serve the Gemma 4 family on `/v1/systemone` and `/v1/decisions` by mapping its architectures to the existing `NextTokenStrategy`. This addresses #62096 with the alternative the issue suggests, adding Gemma 4 to the supported list. A default for every generation model is left to RFC #59365.

```bash
vllm serve google/gemma-4-12B-it
```

## Claims

- `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` (E2B, E4B, 26B-A4B, 31B), `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` (12B) and `Gemma4ForCausalLM` (text-only exports) now serve both endpoints. Before this change, both returned 501.
- With thinking off, each Gemma 4 chat template ends where the label is the reply's first token. All 38 labels (A–Z, yes/no, 0–9) are one token there. A CPU test pins both template variants.
- Other generation models stay unsupported. This widens the allowlist and adds no default.

## Validation

**Templates and labels (CPU).** `test_gemma4_labels_start_the_reply` builds `NextTokenStrategy` from the `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` and `google/gemma-4-12B-it` tokenizers. Construction fails unless every label is one distinct token at the start of the reply. The E2B/E4B prompt ends at `<|turn>model\n`. The 12B/26B/31B prompt ends with a closed empty thought, `<|turn>model\n<|channel>thought\n<channel|>`.

**End to end.** I ran main at `3c13653738` with this patch, installed with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`. Each model ran the existing `/v1/systemone` e2e suite (`test_structured_decisions_e2e.py`) with `MODEL_NAME` swapped and `--max-model-len 4096`. Each model also answered the first 200 AG News test rows as a 4-way `choice`, with the article as the state; that sample has about ±6% error at 95%. Before the patch, `vllm serve google/gemma-4-E2B-it` returns 501 on both endpoints.

| Model | Served as | GPU, weights | e2e suite | AG News acc. | mean `label_mass` | `argmax_is_label` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` | `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` | L4, bf16 | 13/13 | 0.790 | 0.729 | 0.775 |
| `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` | `Gemma4ForCausalLM` (via `--hf-overrides`) | L4, bf16 | 13/13 | 0.790 | 0.728 | 0.770 |
| `google/gemma-4-E4B-it` | `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` | A100, bf16 | 13/13 | 0.830 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| `google/gemma-4-12B-it` | `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` | A100, bf16 | 13/13 | 0.865 | 0.990 | 0.990 |
| `google/gemma-4-12B-it` | `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` | L4, fp8 | 13/13 | 0.860 | 0.991 | 0.995 |
| `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` | `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` | A100, fp8 | 13/13 | 0.815 | 0.985 | 0.985 |
| `google/gemma-4-31B-it` | `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` | A100, fp8 | 13/13 | 0.865 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` (already supported) | `Qwen3ForCausalLM` | L4, bf16 | 13/13 | 0.795 | 0.638 | 0.730 |

The A100 was the 40 GB model, so 26B-A4B and 31B ran with `--quantization fp8`. `/v1/decisions` returned 200 for the docs example on every run.

**Tests.**

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_strategies.py
# 55 passed (macOS CPU and L4)
pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_decisions.py tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_question_types.py
# 49 passed
```

Without the `strategies.py` change, `test_strategy_selection` fails with "does not support Gemma4ForCausalLM". A template that leaves `<|channel>thought\n` open still constructs `NextTokenStrategy`, so the test's prompt-ending assertion is what catches that.

**Not covered in CI.** No Gemma 4 checkpoint runs in CI, as in #60676 and #61064. The CPU test downloads two Gemma 4 tokenizers (31 MB each).

## Details

- **Why not a default for every generation model.** Review on #59299 asked that models opt in once their read is known to work, after a DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash read came back wrong. At startup the server only checks that each label is one token after the generation prompt. It cannot tell whether the reply starts with the answer, so a template that opens a thought or a channel returns 200 with noise. RFC #59365 proposes a next-token fallback behind a strategy registry, and this PR leaves that open.
- **Why no new strategy.** Each checkpoint's own template already ends where the answer starts, and it should not be swapped. Serving E2B with the 12B template, whose only difference is the empty thought, drops `argmax_is_label` from 0.77 to 0.00 and AG News accuracy from 0.79 to 0.30.
- **E2B.** Its misses are a preamble, not a thought: in 45 of the 46 non-label reads the top token is `The`. `label_mass` reports this. E4B uses the same template and lands every read on a label.
- **`Gemma4ForCausalLM`.** No Google checkpoint declares it, but text-only exports do. For example, `LilaRest/gemma-4-31B-it-NVFP4-turbo` has 147k downloads, and its template also closes an empty thought. I also checked this architecture by serving E2B with `--hf-overrides '{"architectures": ["Gemma4ForCausalLM"]}'`.
- **Startup.** A Gemma 4 checkpoint without a chat template, such as the base `google/gemma-4-E2B`, fails `NextTokenStrategy` with a `ValueError`. The server still starts, and both endpoints return 501 as before.
- **Speculative decoding.** With MTP, `logprob_token_ids` reads can return 500 when they share a batch with draft requests, until #42592 is fixed (#44727 and #61219 are open). This affects every next-token model, and Gemma 4 is often served with MTP.
- **Media.** `NextTokenStrategy` takes no media yet, so Gemma 4 reads are text-only until #62181.
- **Not a duplicate.** No open PR adds Gemma 4 to `NextTokenStrategy`. I searched for 62096 and for keywords such as `READ_STRATEGIES`, `NextTokenStrategy`, systemone, decisions and gemma. Related PRs:
  - #60713 (Winnow) picks its own strategy from an explicit `decision_read_strategy` override before this lookup, so it still works. Its test asserts that a plain `Gemma4ForCausalLM` is unsupported, so whichever PR lands second updates that line.
  - #61251's splice test would need Gemma 4 entries in `SPLICE_MODELS`.

title: [PCP] Allow decode-only full CUDA graphs for DSv3.2/GLM-5.2/5.3 sparse MLA with DCP=1
body:
## Overview

Allows decode-only full CUDA graphs (`FULL_DECODE_ONLY` / `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`) under MRV2 PCP with DCP=1 for sparse-MLA models on the DeepSeek-V3.2 attention path (DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.2/5.3: `deepseek_v32`, `glm_moe_dsa`). In that mode, decode requests are round-robin sharded across PCP ranks. These models previously had to run with `cudagraph_mode=NONE`, but the pure-decode full-graph path from #53867 already handles them. Other `index_topk` models (DSv4/V4.1, MiniMax-M3, ...) still require `NONE`, because they need model-specific work (see #61555 for DSv4.1).

## Claims

- GLM-5.3 with TP1 × PCP4 + EP captures and replays decode-only full CUDA graphs.
- On GSM8K, that is 2.6× faster than eager, with matching accuracy (0.9083 vs 0.9075).

## Validation

Tested with GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on 4×B300: `-tp 1 -pcp 4 --enable-expert-parallel --kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64`:

| cudagraph_mode | GSM8K accuracy | Wall time | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| NONE | 0.9075 | 379.5 s | 330 |
| FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | 0.9083 | 145.9 s | 859 |

Every rank captured 11 FULL and 19 PIECEWISE graphs.

`pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py`: passes.

## Details

- Pure FULL mode is still rejected, so prefills under PCP keep running piecewise.
- DeepSeek-V3.2 shares GLM-5.3's attention/indexer code but was not run end-to-end.
- Not validated yet with MTP.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] persistent_topk: don't select float4 tail lanes past the row length
body:
## Overview

FIX #62466

`histogram_2048_topk` in `csrc/persistent_topk.cuh` can return indices `>= seq_len`. This happens when the row length is not a multiple of 4 and the top-k threshold lands in the fp16 `-inf` bin. This PR skips lanes past `seq_len` in the collection loop and adds a regression test.

## Claims

- `persistent_topk` no longer returns indices past the row length on the `histogram_2048_topk` path (k < length <= 8192, at most 32 rows).
- The out-of-bounds reads of `logits` in the refinement pass are gone.
- Rows with length % 4 == 0 and rows whose threshold is above the `-inf` bin are unchanged. The guard only drops lanes that were never real elements.

## Validation

GPU: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (sm_103), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu130. `_C_stable_libtorch` rebuilt from this branch; main measured with the precompiled wheel for 3e96f9cf6.

New test, `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py::test_persistent_topk_masked_row_tail`. It covers k in {512, 1024, 2048}, length = k + {1, 2, 3, 4}, 0 or 100 finite scores, and in-row fill of `-inf` or `-1e30`:

```text
pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k masked_row_tail
main:     36 failed, 12 passed   (every length % 4 != 0 case fails; % 4 == 0 passes)
this PR:  48 passed
```

Sample failure on main: `AssertionError: row 0: indices outside [0, 513): [513, 514, 515]`.

Op-level repro (1 row, k = 512, stride 516, every in-row score `-inf`, padding 0.0):

```text
            main                      this PR
len=513:    [513, 514, 515]           []
len=514:    [514, 515]                []
len=515:    [515]                     []
len=516:    []                        []
```

compute-sanitizer memcheck, one row of length 513 that is also the tensor width, `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1`:

```text
main:     3 x "Invalid __global__ read of size 4 bytes" in histogram_2048_topk<512>, kernel aborts
this PR:  ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors
```

Full file with this PR: `pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py` gives 294 passed, 44 skipped (platform-gated cases).

No end-to-end serving repro: no shipped model reaches this path (see Details). CI runs this test file on Blackwell (`.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`).

## Details

Root cause. The last float4 load of a row (`load_float4_predicated`) fills the lanes past `seq_len` with `-inf`. They are binned like real elements. The collection loop gates candidates only on `vec_valid = i < n_vec`. When fewer than k in-row scores are above the `-inf` bin, the threshold is that bin, so the tail lanes become "equal" candidates. Refinement then reads `logits[idx]` for them and can output them.

Fix. Add `in_range = vec_valid && elem_idx < seq_len` and use it for `is_above` and `is_equal`. Tail lanes still count in the histogram, but that does not move the threshold. They only add to the `-inf` bin, the lowest non-NaN bin, so the counts above it are unchanged. And since `seq_len > k`, the in-row elements alone already reach k at the `-inf` bin.

Reachability, and why there is no end-to-end repro. The kernel path needs a decode row with k < length <= 8192, at most 32 rows, and the persistent backend. The persistent backend is picked by `--sparse-indexer-topk-backend persistent`, by `auto` on SM12x and pre-SM90 GPUs, or by `auto` when the logits row stride is not divisible by 4. The bug also needs fewer than k in-row scores above the fp16 `-inf` bin. I checked every in-tree caller:

- DeepSeek V3.2 / GLM-5 style DSA decode (`sparse_attn_indexer`): in-row scores come from `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` and are finite. Prefill uses `top_k_per_row_prefill`, not this kernel.
- Qwen4-exp QSA: scores are sums of ReLU terms, so they are finite and >= 0.
- Step5 rejects the persistent backend.
- DeepSeek V4.1 `apply_candidate_mask` does write `-inf` inside decode rows. But the shipped DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash config keeps 2048 candidate blocks of 8 tokens (16384 positions) on full-length (`compress_ratio` 1) layers. Every row on this path (<= 8192) is therefore fully covered.

So no shipped model reaches the bug with default or near-default flags. Reaching it needs a config with `candidate_topk_blocks * candidate_block_size < index_topk`, or more than `length - k` scores at or below about -65504. The layer-level script in the issue shows the V4.1 composition (`apply_candidate_mask` then `SparseIndexerTopk("persistent")`) with such a candidate set. If the bug were hit, `triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index` only drops `tok < 0`, so the result would be wrong KV slots with no error.

`cooperative_topk`, `histogram_256_topk` and the radix path are not affected. I checked lengths 8193 to 70001 with all-`-inf` rows on main and saw no bad indices.

Performance: one extra compare per element in the collection loop. No measurable change expected; not benchmarked.

title: [Bugfix][AuxOutput] Send routed-experts block hashes only for computed or scheduled blocks
body:
## Purpose

Split from #62044 (by @faresobeid): only the scheduler-side hash fix. The store eviction fix is #62392.

The scheduler sent a request's block hashes to the worker as soon as they existed. A prompt's hashes all exist before its first chunk runs, so with chunked prefill the worker pinned one store object for every prompt block, including blocks whose KV had not been computed yet. When those objects were still stored from an earlier turn, the extra pins could push the KV-sized store over capacity and make `put()` raise `BlockObjectStoreError` in the writer thread.

`AuxOutputSchedulerConnector` now sends only the hashes of blocks covered by `num_computed_tokens + num_scheduled_tokens` (or `num_computed_tokens` for hash-only updates and finished requests). It takes the hash block size from the scheduler to do that.

As a side effect, when a request finishes and its last sampled token completes a block, that block's hash is no longer sent unless a step that computes that token is already in flight: otherwise the token's KV is never computed, so the worker held a reference to a key with no stored object.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/distributed/aux_output_connector
```

- `test_routed_experts_hashes_follow_scheduled_tokens` runs a 160-token prompt with a 64-token budget and 20 decode steps through the real scheduler, and checks the number of hashes sent after each step against fixed values: 4, 8 and 10 during prefill, then 11 once the decode tokens complete the next block.
- `test_scheduler_connector_sends_only_computed_hashes_off_schedule` (hash-only update, finish) schedules a request's first 4-token block, then lets a settled token complete a second hash block while only 7 tokens are computed. Neither a hash-only update nor the terminal event may send the second hash; the hash-only update sends it once the eighth token is computed.
- `test_worker_does_not_pin_unscheduled_prompt_blocks` drives the scheduler connector and the worker with a 4-object store. A first request stores 4 prompt blocks and finishes. A second request with the same prompt runs its first 4-token chunk next to a request that stores a new block.

## Test Result

- With this change: the new tests pass; `test_scheduler.py` and `tests/distributed/aux_output_connector` pass (288 tests).
- On `main`, with the new constructor argument removed from the tests, all new tests fail:
  - the scheduler sends all 10 prompt hashes at the first step (`[10, 10, ...] != [4, 8, ...]`);
  - after the first block is sent, the hash-only update and the terminal event both send the second hash although only 7 of its 8 tokens are computed;
  - the worker pins all 4 stored prompt blocks, so storing the new block raises `BlockObjectStoreError: auxiliary output store cannot retain the requested batch: limit=4 objects`, the writer-thread failure seen in production.
- Reverting only one of the three bounds to "send every hash" fails only the tests for that path: the scheduled-step bound fails the scheduler and worker tests, and the hash-only and terminal-event bounds each fail their case of `test_scheduler_connector_sends_only_computed_hashes_off_schedule`. The scheduler test cannot see the terminal-event bound, because its request finishes with 179 computed tokens and 11 complete hash blocks either way.

title: [ROCm][perf] Use workspace manager for sparse indexer allocations
body:
Replace dynamic per-call allocations in the ROCm sparse attention indexer with a workspace manager.
This eliminates caching allocator bloat that caused OOM crashes under sustained MTP load.

## Purpose

With MTP speculative decoding enabled on ROCm, the sparse attention indexer dynamically allocates temporary buffers
(`k_fp8, k_scale` per prefill chunk; `out_qk` per decode call) on every invocation.
These varying-size allocations cause PyTorch's caching allocator to retain large amounts of unused memory (reserved >> allocated), eventually exhausting GPU memory available to the HIP runtime for kernel scratch space.
This manifests as non-deterministic memory access faults or `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES` errors.

## Solution

- **Prefill path:** Replace per-chunk `torch.empty` for k_fp8/k_scale with a single `workspace_manager.get_simultaneous()` call, slicing per chunk. Matches the existing CUDA path in `sparse_attn_indexer.py`.
- **Decode path:** Replace `torch.full` for `out_qk` in `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` with a workspace manager view filled with -inf.
- **Memory profiling path**: Reserve workspace for both prefill and decode buffer sizes in the real impl's early-exit path (not the fake impl, which runs under FakeTensor mode during torch.compile).

## Test Plan

image: vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-3e802e8786e05ba94e8a585630f14c86f83b8ad4

```
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8004 \
    --seed 4321 \
    --dtype auto \
    --gpu_memory_utilization 0.75 \
    --max_num_seqs 256 \
    --max_model_len 16384 \
    --max_num_batched_tokens 4096 \
    --no_enable_prefix_caching \
    --profiler-config '{"profiler": "torch", "torch_profiler_dir": "/tmp/traces", "torch_profiler_with_stack":"False"}' \

title: (alternative to #37891) [ROCm] Fix rocm allreduce rmsnorm fusion for Deepseek models
body: ## Depends on #37646 ## Summary Fix allreduce+rmsnorm fusion pattern matching for DeepSeek V2/R1 MoE layers on ROCm. PR #37646 adds `RocmAiterAllReduceFusionPass` which fuses `all_reduce → rmsnorm` sequences using AITER's fused kernel. This works for attention layers but **fails for MoE layers** in DeepSeek because the model inserts a no-op `view(num_tokens, hidden_dim)` between all_reduce and rmsnorm ([`deepseek_v2.py:398`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py#L398)), breaking the pattern match. ### Root cause In the compiled FX graph, DeepSeek MoE layers produce: all_reduce_1: "bf16[s72, 7168]" = torch.ops.vllm.all_reduce(...) view_3: "bf16[s72, 7168]" = all_reduce_1.view(s72, 7168) ← identity-shaped, breaks pattern rocm_aiter_rmsnorm2d_fwd_with_add_1 = ...(view_3, ...) The `view` is a no-op (same shape in/out) from `final_hidden_states.view(num_tokens, hidden_dim)` in the MoE forward path. It creates an intermediate node that prevents the `all_reduce → rmsnorm` pattern from matching. ### Fix Add a graph pre-processing step (`_bypass_noop_views_after_allreduce`) to `RocmAiterAllReduceFusionPass.__call__` that removes identity-shaped `aten.view.default` / `aten.reshape.default` nodes after `all_reduce` before pattern matching runs. This exposes the direct `all_reduce → rmsnorm` sequence for the standard patterns to match. After the fix: all_reduce_1: "bf16[s72, 7168]" = torch.ops.vllm.all_reduce(...) rocm_aiter_rmsnorm2d_fwd_with_add_1 = ...(all_reduce_1, ...) ← fused This is an alternative to #37891 which achieves the same goal via model-level changes. This approach addresses the [reviewer feedback on #37891](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37891#discussion_r2117282974) requesting a pattern matching mechanism instead. ## Changes on top of #37646 | File | What | |------|------| | `vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/allreduce_rms_fusion.py` | Add `_bypass_noop_views_after_allreduce()` to `RocmAiterAllReduceFusionPass` (+55 lines) | ## Test plan Tested with DeepSeek-R1-0528 FP8, TP=8 on 8x MI355X (gfx950): - [x] All `all_reduce → rmsnorm` pairs fused (attention + MoE layers) - [x] `rocm_aiter_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm` confirmed in Inductor-generated runtime code (`kernel_5.py`) - [x] Server starts and serves inference without errors - [x] Graph dumps (`after_split.0.py`) confirm no-op view elimination ## How to test This PR is based on top of #37646. To get a working branch: ```bash # Fetch and checkout PR #37646 gh pr checkout 37646 --repo vllm-project/vllm # Cherry-pick this fix on top git fetch https://github.com/rbrugaro-amd/vllm.git fix/rocm-allreduce-rms-deepseek-view-bypass git cherry-pick FETCH_HEAD Then run with graph dump to verify: VLLM_DEBUG_DUMP_PATH=/tmp/graph_dump \ vllm serve \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --quantization fp8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"fuse_allreduce_rms":true}}' ``` Verify fusion is applied: after_split.0.py: no view between all_reduce and rmsnorm2d_fwd_with_add kernel_*.py: rocm_aiter_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm calls present in the decoder loop

title: [Bug][ROCm] GLM-5 MXFP4 sparse MLA decode crash on MI355x
body:
## Summary

GLM-5 (GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM) with MXFP4 quantization crashes during the **decode** phase on ROCm MI355x (gfx950) with 8 GPUs. The model loads and prefills successfully, but decode consistently fails with either `ZeroDivisionError` or `Memory access fault`.

## Root Cause

GLM-5 has 64 attention heads and 32 sparse indexer heads (`index_n_heads=32`). At TP=8, the MLA decode kernel receives 8 heads per GPU, but AITER's sparse MLA kernels require `num_heads >= 16`:

1. **MLA decode kernel**: `mla_decode_stage1_asm_fwd` only supports `gqa >= 16`. With TP=8, `gqa=8` triggers `RuntimeError: get_heuristic_kernel_mla: cannot get heuristic kernel! gqa:8`
2. **FP8 paged MQA logits (indexer)**: `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1` computes `TileQCount = heads // ChunkQ` with default `ChunkQ=64`. When `heads < 64`, `TileQCount=0` causes `ZeroDivisionError` at `SplitKV = (max(1, TotalCuCount // TileQCount) + 4) // 5 * 5 * WavePerEU`

Even with TP=4 (16 heads per GPU, satisfying the `>= 16` requirement for the MLA kernel), a `Memory access fault` persists during decode, suggesting additional issues in the sparse attention indexer's forward_hip path.

## Environment

- **GPU**: 8x AMD MI355X (gfx950)
- **ROCm**: 7.2.1
- **vLLM**: main branch (latest)
- **Model**: GLM-5-MXFP4 (`zai-org/GLM-5-MXFP4` or equivalent Quark checkpoint)
- **Config**: `num_attention_heads=64`, `index_n_heads=32`, `kv_lora_rank=512`, `n_routed_experts=256`

## Reproduction

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1

vllm serve /path/to/GLM-5-MXFP4 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --block-size 1 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --enforce-eager
```

Then send any chat completion request - prefill succeeds but decode crashes.

## Error Traces

### ZeroDivisionError (TP=8, indexer path)
```
File "aiter/ops/triton/attention/pa_mqa_logits.py", line 198, in deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1
    SplitKV = (max(1, TotalCuCount // TileQCount) + 4) // 5 * 5 * WavePerEU
ZeroDivisionError: integer division or modulo by zero
```

### Memory access fault (TP=4 or TP=8, during decode)
```
Memory access fault by GPU node-X (Agent handle: ...) on address ...
```

## Related

- PR #36855 - Fix for head repeat in sparse MLA (addresses the `gqa:8` crash)
- https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/726 - Upstream feature request for native nhead=8 support
- https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/2563 - Upstream issue for ZeroDivisionError in paged MQA logits
- Issue #34553 - GLM-5 FP8 on H200 OOM in sparse_attn_indexer (CUDA, different issue)
- Issue #36220 - GLM-5 quantized serving failure (AWQ/INT4, different quantization)

## Proposed Fix

Two complementary approaches (both needed):
1. **MLA decode kernel**: Head repeat padding from 8->16 (temporary workaround in PR #36855) until AITER supports nhead < 16 natively
2. **Indexer MQA logits**: Fall back to PyTorch reference implementation when `heads < 16` (implemented in `fix/rocm-glm5-mxfp4-optimizations` branch)

title: [ROCm][Perf] Add AITER MLA prefill kernel for dense MLA backend
body:
## Summary

Integrate AITER's `mla_prefill_fwd` assembly kernel into vLLM's dense MLA backend (`AiterMLAImpl`), replacing the base class's chunk-by-chunk prefill context path with a single kernel call that avoids expensive KV expansion.

### What this changes

The base class (`MLACommonImpl._compute_prefill_context`) computes context attention by:
1. Gathering cached KV per chunk
2. Expanding through `kv_b_proj` to materialize full K/V heads
3. Running `flash_attn_varlen` per chunk
4. Merging chunk results

This is expensive because `kv_b_proj` expansion materializes `O(context_len * num_heads * head_dim)` intermediate tensors.

The new path instead:
1. **Absorbs Q** through `W_UK^T` (extracted from `kv_b_proj` weights) to produce compressed queries in the latent space `[T, N, L+R]`
2. **Runs `mla_prefill_fwd`** directly against the paged KV cache in a single assembly kernel call — no KV expansion needed
3. **Projects output** through `W_UV` to recover full V dimensions

This eliminates the per-chunk KV expansion loop and replaces it with a single kernel dispatch.

### Fallback behavior

- **FP8 prefill**: Falls back to base class (AITER `mla_prefill_fwd` does not yet accept `q_scale`/`kv_scale`)
- **AITER unavailable**: Falls back to base class via `ImportError` guard

### Part of the GLM-5 on ROCm performance series

This PR is part of a series of optimizations to bring GLM-5 inference on ROCm (MI355X) closer to ATOM performance:

| PR | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|
| #38665 | Dual-stream shared experts + Quark MXFP4 + GLM-5-FP8 weight loading fix | Open |
| #36855 | Sparse MLA head repeat for < 16 heads + FP8 KV cache support | Open |
| **This PR** | MLA prefill kernel integration (eliminates KV expansion) | **New** |

Related upstream:
- [ROCm/aiter#2563](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/2563) — AITER sparse MLA ZeroDivisionError with < 16 heads
- [ROCm/aiter#2577](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/2577) — AITER MLA decode nhead < 16 pad-to-16 support

### Context

Reference: [ATOM GLM-5 recipe](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/blob/main/recipes/GLM-5.md)

AI assistance (Claude) was used. The submitting human has reviewed all changed lines.

**Not duplicating existing PRs**: No existing vLLM PR integrates `mla_prefill_fwd` for the dense MLA backend.

## Test plan

- [ ] Serve DeepSeek-V3 / GLM-5 on MI355X (TP=8) and verify prefill context path uses AITER kernel (check logs)
- [ ] Compare prefill throughput with and without this change
- [ ] Verify FP8 prefill falls back correctly to base class
- [ ] Verify CUDA path is unaffected (AITER import guard)

title: Request for triage permission — active ROCm contributor
body:
Hi maintainers,

I'm requesting **triage** permission on this repository. I'm an active ROCm/AMD contributor with 12+ open PRs covering AITER integration, MLA attention backends, MXFP4 quantization, and GLM-5 model support on MI355X.

### Why triage permission?

title: [ROCm] Fixing GLM-5.1, DeepSeek-V3.2, DeepSeek-V4 on gfx942 and gfx950
body:
* An in-tree Triton paged MQA kernel.  It is required unconditionally for DeepSeek V4 (Flash and Pro): V4 shares KV-cache blocks between the indexer and the main MLA cache, so its indexer cache is a non-contiguous strided slice of a larger per-block record written in plain pos-major layout, whereas aiter assumes a contiguous 16×16-preshuffled cache. It is also required when speculative decoding is enabled, because the current AITER implementation of paged_mqa_logits does not work correctly in these cases (the exact cause is yet to be determined).
* Periodically synchronizing the device during FP8-BMM precompilation. Without it, vLLM emits a flood of short kernel launches that sometimes ends in a segfault. 
* A fix to cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache for unaligned block_stride.

Test results, MI325 and MI355, AITER 0.1.21 branch (2026/Aug/28) + the fix from https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5202, https://github.com/ekuznetsov139/llm-comprehension/ (average errors per iteration in a 190 multiple-choice question corpus, lower is better, sigma ~ 0.8 in all cases):

Model               | Upstream  | Upstream + init fix  | Upstream + init fix + spec   |    PR     |    PR + spec
--------------------|-----------|-----------|------------|-----------|----------
GLM-4.7, MI325      |          |   3.2       |  4.4   | 4.6  |    4.2
GLM-5.1, MI325      | crash     |    2.8    |  9.0+1.2   |   2.8     |    3.0
GLM-5.2, MI325      |               |     1.6  |            |   1.0     |    1.6
GLM-5.3, MI325      |              |     1.4      |  10.0+3.6   |   2.2     |    1.2
DS3.2, MI325        | crash       |    5.0    |  10.6+3.8   |   3.0     |    3.0
DS4-Flash, MI325    | junk      |           |            |   3.6     |    4.0
DS4-Pro, MI325      | junk      |           |            |   3.4     |    3.2
GLM-5.1, MI355      |   1.8     |           |   7.2+1.0  |     |  2.8
DS4-Flash, MI355    | junk      |           |            |     |  5.2
DS4-Pro, MI355      | junk      |           |            |     |  3.2

As a reference: 

Model                  | Error rate
------------------------------------------|-------------------
Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8           | 7.2
Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-FP8-KV | 9.6
gpt-oss-120b  | 16.0

* Entries with '+' (e.g. 9.0+1.2): the value after "+" is the average number of unparseable responses, expected to be 0 in healthy models.
* "junk" = runs, emits locally coherent sequences of tokens that have only a tenuous connection to supplied text, error counts of 50+ and large numbers of unparsed responses.


The two optimization commits previously in the PR have been broken out into a separate PR.

title: Fix engine_id collision + MoRIIO robustness for multi-node disagg DP
body:
## Summary

### 1. Engine_id collision fix (`core.py`, `utils.py`)

Use global `dp_rank` instead of `local_dp_rank` when generating the engine_id suffix for KV transfer in data-parallel deployments. In multi-node DP with `--headless` child nodes, using `local_dp_rank` causes master and child nodes to produce identical engine_ids, routing all data to whichever engine registered first.

### 2. MoRIIOConnector fixes (`moriio_connector.py`, `moriio_common.py`)

**Fix A -- Cache `kv_transfer_params` across scheduler steps:** Snapshot into `_req_kv_params` dict at allocation time; use cached copy in `build_connector_meta`. Handles chunked prefill correctly: params are retained for requests moved to `_reqs_need_pending_save` and only cleaned up when the final chunk is processed.

**Fix B -- Handle attention backend `block_size` overrides:** FlashMLA silently overrides `block_size` to 64 for MLA models. Trust the actual tensor shape instead of asserting against the CLI config value.

**Fix C -- Default values for MORI-IO-specific ports:** `remote_handshake_port` and `remote_notify_port` now use `.get()` with `MoRIIOConstants` defaults, preventing `KeyError` from external coordinators (e.g., NIXL sidecar in LLM-D).

**Fix D -- Multi-node DP sizing and ranking:** Use `data_parallel_size_local` and local `dp_rank` (`global % local_size`) so port offsets stay in 0..N range per node. Applied to both `MoRIIOConfig.from_vllm_config` and `MoRIIOConnectorScheduler`.

**Fix E -- Prevent child nodes from sending block notifications:** Added `_is_kv_master` flag to guard `send_notify_block` calls.

### 3. MoRIIO robustness fixes (`moriio_engine.py`, `moriio_connector.py`)

**Fix F -- Timeout-guarded transfer completion:** Replace blocking `status.Wait()` with a polling loop bounded by `VLLM_MORIIO_TRANSFER_TIMEOUT_S` (default 120s).

**Fix G -- Failure detection in `_pop_done_transfers`:** Check `Failed()` status and implement age-based timeout for pending RDMA reads.

**Fix H -- Deferred task timeout:** Expire write tasks stuck waiting for remote block allocation after `VLLM_MORIIO_DEFERRED_TIMEOUT_S` (default 300s).

**Fix I -- ZMQ notification retry:** Non-blocking send with 3 retries and exponential backoff for transient ZMQ failures.

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `VLLM_MORIIO_TRANSFER_TIMEOUT_S` | 120 | Max seconds to wait for a single RDMA transfer |
| `VLLM_MORIIO_DEFERRED_TIMEOUT_S` | 300 | Max seconds a deferred write task waits for remote block allocation |

## Files Changed

| File | Lines | Change |
|------|-------|--------|
| `core.py` | +4/-3 | engine_id: local_dp_rank -> dp_rank |
| `utils.py` | +4/-3 | engine_id: local_index -> index |
| `moriio_common.py` | +11/-4 | Fix C (default ports), Fix D (local dp_size/dp_rank) |
| `moriio_connector.py` | +71/-17 | Fix A-E + Fix G (failure detection + timeout) |
| `moriio_engine.py` | +60/-21 | Fix F (transfer timeout), Fix H (deferred timeout), Fix I (ZMQ retry) |

## Test Plan

The plan is to evaluate the performance improvements and accuracy impact on:

title: [Bug]: aiter.ops.triton.attention.pa_mqa_logits.deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1` returns random topk for `context_len > 2048` on ROCm (gfx950), breaks GLM-5.1-FP8 decode
body:
## Summary
Investigations done with Claude Code on a mi355 mode.

On the `rocm/vllm-dev:nightly` image bundled with vLLM `0.19.1rc1.dev83+g83d09d36b`, the aiter sparse-MLA **paged decode** kernel `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1` produces correct top‑k indices for `context_len <= 2048` but essentially random results (≈0.3 % topk-set match against its own bf16 torch reference) the moment `context_len` crosses 2048. The transition is exact: `ctx=2048 → 100 %`, `ctx=2049 → ~0.5 %`.

This is invoked on every decode step through `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py::rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits`, so any model with the `glm_moe_dsa` architecture (GLM-5, GLM-5-FP8, GLM-5.1-FP8) collapses to token salad as soon as its running (prefill + decode) context exceeds ~2048 tokens. Short-context generation looks coherent; then it degrades to repeated punctuation, random code fragments, or non-whitespace Unicode. On an older nightly (vLLM `0.18.2rc1.dev55+g9bd723110`, image id `d9863fe6ff74`, 2026-04-03), the same model ran correctly on long context, so this is a regression within the 2026-04-03 → 2026-04-08 window.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Image | `docker.io/rocm/vllm-dev:nightly` |
| Image id | `45a197521fa0` (pulled 2026-04-08) |
| vLLM | `0.19.1rc1.dev83+g83d09d36b` |
| Model | `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8` (`glm_moe_dsa`, 754 B, FP8 E4M3) |
| Hardware | 8× AMD Instinct MI355X OAM (`gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-`) |
| Runtime | Podman 4.7.1, ROCm |
| Relevant env | `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` |
| Serve flags | `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --trust-remote-code --dtype auto --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45` (chunked prefill on, default `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`) |

TP=4 is forced by a separate constraint (aiter MLA ASM kernels only exist for `gqa ∈ {1,16,32,64,128}` on `gfx950`; GLM-5.1 has `num_attention_heads=64` so TP=4 → `gqa=16`). TP=8 crashes at graph capture and TP≤2 is memory-infeasible. Attempts to change tensor parallelism were therefore not a workaround.

## Minimal reproduction (runs inside the running container)

The reproducer calls the kernel with synthetic random inputs, compares its output against the bf16 torch reference that lives in the same file (`fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch` in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`), and reports the per-row top‑k set-match ratio. No GLM weights, no server, no vLLM engine required.

```python
# repro_pa_mqa_ctx2048.py — run inside rocm/vllm-dev:nightly (image 45a197521fa0)
import torch
from aiter.ops.triton.attention.pa_mqa_logits import (
    deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1,
)


def torch_ref(q, kv_cache, weights, context_lens, block_tables, max_model_len):
    """Bf16 reference. Matches `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch` in
    vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py."""
    bs, next_n, heads, hd = q.size()
    fp8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn
    kv_cache_v, scale = kv_cache[..., :hd], kv_cache[..., hd:]
    scale = scale.contiguous().view(torch.float32)
    kv_cache_v = kv_cache_v.view(fp8).float() * scale
    _, block_size, _, _ = kv_cache_v.size()
    logits = torch.full(
        [bs * next_n, max_model_len], float("-inf"),
        device=q.device, dtype=torch.float32,
    )
    q_f = q.float()
    for i in range(bs):
        ctx_len = context_lens[i].item()
        q_offsets = torch.arange(ctx_len - next_n, ctx_len, device="cuda")
        weight_slice = weights[i * next_n:(i + 1) * next_n, :].transpose(0, 1).contiguous()
        for blk in range((ctx_len + block_size - 1) // block_size):
            blk_id = block_tables[i][blk]
            qx, kx = q_f[i], kv_cache_v[blk_id]
            k_offsets = torch.arange(blk * block_size, (blk + 1) * block_size, device="cuda")
            mask = (k_offsets[None, :] < ctx_len) & (k_offsets[None, :] <= q_offsets[:, None])
            s = torch.where(
                mask[None, :, :],
                (qx.transpose(0, 1) @ kx.transpose(0, 1).transpose(1, 2)).to(logits.dtype),
                float("-inf"),
            )
            s = (torch.relu(s) * weight_slice[..., None]).sum(dim=0)
            logits[i * next_n:(i + 1) * next_n, blk * block_size:(blk + 1) * block_size] = \
                torch.where(k_offsets[None, :] <= q_offsets[:, None], s, float("-inf"))
    return logits


def test(ctx_len):
    torch.manual_seed(42)
    bs, next_n, heads, hd = 1, 1, 32, 128
    block_size = 1  # DeepseekV32IndexerCache uses block_size=1
    max_blocks = ctx_len + 16
    max_model_len = 202752  # GLM-5.1-FP8 config value
    kv_cache = torch.randint(
        0, 256, (max_blocks, block_size, 1, hd + 4),
        dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda",
    )
    q = torch.randn(bs, next_n, heads, hd, device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    weights = torch.randn(bs * next_n, heads, device="cuda")
    context_lens = torch.full((bs,), ctx_len, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    block_tables = torch.arange(
        max_blocks, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda",
    ).unsqueeze(0).expand(bs, -1).contiguous()
    out = torch.full(
        (heads, bs * next_n, max_model_len),
        float("-inf"), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32,
    )

    deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1(
        q, kv_cache, weights, out, context_lens, block_tables, max_model_len,
    )
    a = out.sum(dim=0)
    r = torch_ref(q, kv_cache, weights, context_lens, block_tables, max_model_len)

    a2 = torch.where(torch.isfinite(a), a, torch.full_like(a, -1e30))
    r2 = torch.where(torch.isfinite(r), r, torch.full_like(r, -1e30))
    k = min(2048, ctx_len)
    a_set = torch.topk(a2, k=k, dim=1).indices.sort(dim=1).values
    r_set = torch.topk(r2, k=k, dim=1).indices.sort(dim=1).values
    match = (a_set == r_set).float().mean(dim=1)
    print(f"ctx={ctx_len:5d}  topk_set_match={match.mean().item():.4f}")


for ctx in [1024, 2048, 2049, 3000, 4096, 8192]:
    test(ctx)
```

Run it in the container:

```bash
podman exec <container> python repro_pa_mqa_ctx2048.py
```

## Expected output

All `topk_set_match` values near `1.0` (bf16 reference and FP8 kernel should disagree only at precision boundaries, not at entire topk sets).

## Actual output

```
ctx= 1024  topk_set_match=1.0000
ctx= 2048  topk_set_match=1.0000
ctx= 2049  topk_set_match=0.0049
ctx= 3000  topk_set_match=0.0015
ctx= 4096  topk_set_match=0.0039
ctx= 8192  topk_set_match=0.0029
```

At `ctx >= 2049` the kernel selects essentially random positions — the 0.2–0.5 % match is just the baseline `2048 / ctx` collision rate you would get from sampling uniformly.

The *absolute* values it writes are also implausible. Running the same reproducer with

```python
finite = torch.isfinite(a) & torch.isfinite(r)
print("max_abs_diff:", (a[finite] - r[finite]).abs().max().item())
```

at `ctx=4096` gives `max_abs_diff ≈ 4.9e34`, i.e. the kernel is not "noisy but close", it is writing garbage floats into `out_qk` for the past‑2048 positions.

## Downstream impact

The broken kernel is on the decode path of `SparseAttnIndexer.forward_hip → rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer → rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` (lines ~600–680 on this nightly). Each generated token of a `glm_moe_dsa` model calls this once per sparse‑indexer layer. Once the running context grows past 2048, the topk picks ~random positions, the sparse MLA attention attends to those positions, and generation collapses. Concretely, serving `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8`:

- Prompt ≈ 1 k tokens → coherent reasoning and answer.
- Prompt ≈ 2 k tokens → first few tokens coherent, then token salad (`1.1.1.0px solid #endregion...`, mixed scripts).
- Prompt ≈ 4 k–60 k tokens → garbage from the first generated token.

The threshold depends only on how fast the decode context crosses 2048, not on prompt content or prompt shape. Chunked prefill scheduling (`max_num_batched_tokens=8192`) does not affect it.

The same model on the prior nightly (image id `d9863fe6ff74`, vLLM `0.18.2rc1.dev55+g9bd723110`, pulled 2026-04-03) generated coherent long-context output under the same deploy flags, so this is a regression introduced between the 2026-04-03 and 2026-04-08 `rocm/vllm-dev:nightly` image rebuilds.

## Observations while narrowing it down

- Bug is **on N (key / context length)**, not M (query length). `M=4096, N=2048` → 100 % match. `M=128, N=4096` → broken. Chunking the query dimension does not help.
- Bug is **in the decode kernel**, not in the prefill indexer kernel. A parallel reproducer against `aiter.ops.triton.attention.fp8_mqa_logits.fp8_mqa_logits` (the prefill path) at `num_heads=32, head_dim=128` produces `max_abs_diff ≈ 0.5` across the full tested range up to `N=8192` — normal FP8-vs-bf16 precision noise. Only the paged (decode) kernel misbehaves.
- Bug is **not** a `ChunkQ` issue caused by GLM-5.1's `index_n_heads=32 < default ChunkQ=64`. Padding `q` heads from 32 to 64 and calling with `ChunkQ=64` (the DeepSeek‑V3.2 tested configuration) reproduces the identical failure past 2048. The wrapper patch required to avoid the `heads // ChunkQ == 0` ZeroDivisionError during CUDA‑graph capture
  ```python
  if heads < ChunkQ:
      ChunkQ = heads
  TileQCount = max(1, batch_size * next_n * (heads // ChunkQ))
  ```
  is orthogonal — the correctness regression happens with or without it.
- `block_size > 1` is **not** a workaround. The indexer cache (`DeepseekV32IndexerCache`) uses `block_size=1` and the kernel only has working template instantiations for that case on this image; passing `block_size ∈ {16, 64, 256}` raises `hipErrorIllegalAddress (700)`.
- `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch` (the torch fallback in the same file) is numerically correct but takes ~1 s per call at `ctx=4096`, i.e. ≈ 60 s per generated token across all indexer layers — not viable as a production shim.
- `index_n_heads`, `index_head_dim`, `index_topk`, `max_position_embeddings` are identical between `zai-org/GLM-5-FP8` and `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8` (32 / 128 / 2048 / 202752), so this is not a GLM-5.1-specific config issue — the older GLM-5-FP8 would hit the same kernel regression on this image.

## Where I think the bug lives

The kernel in question is
`/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/aiter/ops/triton/_triton_kernels/attention/pa_mqa_logits.py::_deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1`

dispatched from the wrapper at
`/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/aiter/ops/triton/attention/pa_mqa_logits.py::deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1`.

Since M does not matter and only N > 2048 is affected, the regression is almost certainly in how the kernel walks the KV / `block_table` dimension — either an off-by-one in the per‑split KV range computation, a missing mask on a tail load past the 2048‑position `SplitKV` boundary, or stale shared‑memory / register state carried across `SplitKV` shards. Given that `SplitKV` is computed as
```python
TileQCount = batch_size * next_n * (heads // ChunkQ)                 # = 1 for decode
SplitKV    = (max(1, TotalCuCount // TileQCount) + 4) // 5 * 5 * WavePerEU   # ≈ 160 on 80 CUs
```
the kernel is running ~160 KV‑dimension shards per query even for decode, and with `block_size=1` each shard covers a very small KV span. The threshold at exactly 2048 strongly suggests a per‑shard shared buffer sized for the previous worst-case workload (DeepSeek‑V3.2 with `index_topk=2048`) being reused as a hard N upper bound.

## Ask

1. Can the aiter team confirm / bisect this against the aiter changes that landed between the 2026-04-03 and 2026-04-08 `rocm/vllm-dev:nightly` rebuilds?
2. Pending a proper fix, can `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` gate the aiter path on `max_model_len <= 2048` and fall back to `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch` otherwise? That will be slow but at least it will produce correct output for users who need to run GLM-5 family models on MI300X / MI350X in the interim.
3. Is there a tag of the previous aiter build that we can pin `rocm/vllm-dev:nightly` against to get a known-good GLM-5/5.1 deploy while the kernel is under investigation?

title: [Performance] DSV3.2 Indexer: Overlap indexer op || q_b_proj + MLA RoPE on separate CUDA streams
body: ## Motivation In the DeepSeek-V3.2 attention layer, `q_b_proj` + `MLA RoPE` and the full indexer (projections + op) execute sequentially on the same CUDA stream despite having no data dependency. This is complementary to the multi-stream overlap of the indexer k+w path || q path (separate issue): see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39309 ## Current Execution ``` #4 QKV A Proj (fused_a_gemm) 7.7us #8 q_a_rmsnorm + split qkv_lora 2.3us #9 kv_a_rmsnorm + split kv_lora 2.5us ↓ #14 Q B Proj (q_b_proj) 15.1us → reads q_c #15 MLA RoPE (Q RoPE + KV RoPE) 2.0us → reads q + k_pe ↓ Full indexer (self.indexer(hidden_states, q_c, ...)): #5 wk_weights_proj (splitK) 4.8us #6 splitKreduce 2.8us #7 k_norm (LayerNorm) 2.2us #10 wq_b 7.2us #11 Indexer RoPE (q+k) 2.0us #12 FP8 quant 2.3us #13 W scale 1.4us #16 Indexer Cache (k_quant_and_cache) 2.5us #17 fill 1.1us #18 Indexer MQA (paged_mqa_logits) 4.5us #19 Logits Top K (topk_kernel) 1.4us ↓ #20 concat_and_cache_mla 2.0us ← start of mla_attn ... MLA attention continues ... ``` ## Proposed Standalone Execution Run the full indexer on the default stream and `q_b_proj + MLA RoPE` on an aux stream in parallel. In the current code, `q_b_proj` is already called outside the indexer — no changes to `Indexer.forward()` needed. The sync point is before `mla_attn()`, which needs both `MLA q` (from q_b_proj) and `topk_indices` (from the indexer): ``` #4 QKV A Proj 7.7us #8 q_a_rmsnorm + split 2.3us #9 kv_a_rmsnorm + split 2.5us ┌──────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┐ Default stream (full indexer): Aux stream (q_b_proj + MLA RoPE): ────────────────────────── ──────────────────────────── #5 wk_weights_proj 4.8us #14 Q B Proj (q_b_proj) 15.1us #6 splitKreduce 2.8us #15 MLA RoPE (Q+KV) 2.0us #7 k_norm 2.2us → MLA q ready #10 wq_b 7.2us (17.1us total) #11 Indexer RoPE 2.0us #12 FP8 quant 2.3us #13 W scale 1.4us #16 Indexer Cache 2.5us #17 fill 1.1us #18 Indexer MQA 4.5us #19 Logits Top K 1.4us → topk_indices ready (32.2us total) └──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┘ sync (mla_attn needs both MLA q + topk_indices) ↓ #20 concat_and_cache_mla 2.0us #21 kv_b_proj (W_UV) 5.9us ... sparse FlashMLA ... ``` ## Combined with https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39309 (k+w path || q path overlap) If implemented together with the k+w path || q path multi-stream overlap (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39309), the aux stream is reused across two fork/sync phases. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39309 shortens the indexer's critical path, making the two streams more balanced: ``` AR + Add + RMS → hidden_states ready ↓ fork #1 (issue 1) Default: QKV A Proj → q_a_rmsnorm → kv_a_rmsnorm → wq_b Aux: wk_weights_proj → reduce → k_norm ↓ sync #1 (before Indexer RoPE) Default continues: Indexer RoPE → FP8 quant → W scale ↓ fork #2 (issue 2 — aux stream reused) Default: Indexer Cache → fill → MQA logits → TopK Aux: Q B Proj → MLA RoPE ↓ sync #2 (before mla_attn) MLA attention → MoE → ... ```

title: fix: Fallback to torch for context_len > 2048 to bypass aiter kernel bug
body:
## Summary

Fixes vllm-project/vllm#39303

The aiter deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1 kernel returns random results when context_len > 2048. Added a check to use the torch fallback implementation when max context_len exceeds 2048.

This is a workaround until the aiter team fixes the kernel bug. The torch implementation is slower but produces correct results.

## Changes

- Modified ocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits() in llm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py to check max(context_lens) and fall back to torch implementation when it exceeds 2048

## Testing

This fix was verified by reviewing the code logic. The fallback uses the existing  p8_paged_mqa_logits_torch function which is a validated reference implementation.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: Add tokens-per-expert threshold for DeepGemm vs Triton MoE dispatch
body:
### Summary

DeepGemm's persistent kernel pads each expert's token batch to `BLOCK_M` (128). When experts receive fewer tokens than this — which happens at decode batch sizes — the padding wastes up to 94% of compute. This PR adds a runtime check in `TritonOrDeepGemmExperts._select_experts_impl` that falls back to Triton when `tokens_per_expert = M * top_k / E < BLOCK_M`.

For Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 (E=256, top_k=8), the threshold is M >= 4096:
- **Prefill** (M >> 4096): uses DeepGemm (faster for large GEMMs)
- **Decode** (M = 256): uses Triton (avoids DeepGemm padding waste)

### Change

Single file: `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/triton_deep_gemm_moe.py`
- Import `get_mk_alignment_for_contiguous_layout` to get `BLOCK_M`
- Before returning `self.experts` (DeepGemm), check if `tokens_per_expert < block_m` and fall back to `self.fallback_experts` (Triton) if so

### Benchmark results

**Hardware:** 1x NVIDIA H100 NVL (96GB), CUDA 13.0, Driver 580.95.05
**Model:** Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 (E=256 experts, top_k=8, FP8 quantized)
**vLLM:** v0.19.0, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1`
**Note:** All benchmarks run with `--attention-backend FLASHINFER`. The default auto-selected backend (FlashAttention v3) has a separate performance issue on this model that is being tracked independently.

#### `vllm bench latency` (offline, deterministic, BS=256, input_len=4096)

| Output tokens | Baseline (s) | + Threshold (s) | Speedup |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 10 (prefill-heavy) | 22.29 | 18.42 | **1.21x (−17.4%)** |
| 256 (decode-heavy) | 34.08 | 30.10 | **1.13x (−11.7%)** |

#### `vllm bench serve` (server mode, 256 prompts, request_rate=inf, input_len=4096)

**Prefill-heavy (output_len=10):**

| Metric | Baseline | + Threshold | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Benchmark duration (s) | 24.36 | 21.41 | −12.1% |
| Request throughput (req/s) | 10.51 | 11.96 | +13.8% |
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 43,144 | 49,093 | +13.8% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 12,454 | 10,968 | −11.9% |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 179.07 | 156.78 | −12.4% |
| Mean ITL (ms) | 179.07 | 156.78 | −12.4% |

**Decode-heavy (output_len=256):**

| Metric | Baseline | + Threshold | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Benchmark duration (s) | 39.53 | 36.41 | −7.9% |
| Request throughput (req/s) | 6.48 | 7.03 | +8.5% |
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 1,658 | 1,800 | +8.6% |
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 28,181 | 30,598 | +8.6% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 14,421 | 12,847 | −10.9% |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 92.07 | 86.05 | −6.5% |
| Mean ITL (ms) | 92.07 | 86.05 | −6.5% |

### Threshold derivation

DeepGemm's persistent kernel operates on tiles of size `BLOCK_M` (128 on H100, queried at runtime via `get_mk_alignment_for_contiguous_layout()`). Each expert receives, on average:

```
tokens_per_expert = M * top_k / E
```

where `M` is the total number of tokens in the batch, `top_k` is the number of experts each token is routed to, and `E` is the total number of experts.

When `tokens_per_expert < BLOCK_M`, DeepGemm pads each expert's batch up to 128. The wasted compute fraction is:

```
waste = 1 - tokens_per_expert / BLOCK_M
```

For **Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8** (E=256, top_k=8, BLOCK_M=128):

| Phase | M | tokens_per_expert | Waste | Winner |
|-------|---|-------------------|-------|--------|
| Decode (BS=256) | 256 | 256 × 8 / 256 = **8** | 93.8% | Triton |
| Chunked prefill | 16,384 | 16384 × 8 / 256 = **512** | 0% | DeepGemm |

The crossover point where DeepGemm breaks even is `M * top_k / E >= BLOCK_M`, i.e.:

```
M >= BLOCK_M * E / top_k = 128 * 256 / 8 = 4096
```

Below M=4096 the kernel falls back to Triton. Above it, DeepGemm's persistent kernel is used. The threshold is computed at runtime from the model's actual `E`, `top_k`, and the hardware's `BLOCK_M`, so it generalizes across MoE architectures.

### Why this matters in practice

With chunked prefill (default in v0.19.0, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`), vLLM interleaves prefill chunks and decode batches in the same forward pass. The decode batches consistently hit the small-M regime where DeepGemm wastes compute on padding. Since decode steps dominate wall-clock time in generation-heavy workloads, the cumulative overhead is significant.

The prefill chunks have large M (up to 16384), so DeepGemm's persistent kernel continues to be used where it provides its advantage over Triton.

AI assistance was used in developing and benchmarking this change. The change was largely automatically discovered using the nCompass Performance Optimization Agent.

title: DSA module construction corrupts CUDA RNG state (Offset increment outside graph capture)
body:
## Bug: DeepseekV2MLAAttention construction leaves CUDA graph RNG offset tracking active

### Description

Constructing a `DeepseekV2MLAAttention` module for DSA (DeepSeek-V3.2 sparse MLA) leaves the CUDA graph RNG offset tracking in an active state. Any subsequent RNG operation (`normal_()`, `uniform_()`, `torch.randn()`, `torch.randint()`, etc.) on the same device fails with:

```
RuntimeError: Offset increment outside graph capture encountered unexpectedly.
```

This happens outside vLLM's model runner — we construct standalone modules for kernel benchmarking. Regular (non-DSA) MLA modules do not trigger this.

### Reproduction

```python
import torch
from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
from vllm.model_executor.models.deepseek_v2 import DeepseekV2MLAAttention

vllm_config = ...  # VllmConfig with DeepSeek-V3.2 model

with set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config):
    attn_module = DeepseekV2MLAAttention(
        vllm_config=vllm_config,
        config=hf_config,
        # ... DSA-specific config
        prefix="model.layers.0.self_attn",
    )

attn_module = attn_module.to("cuda:0")

# This crashes:
torch.randn(1, device="cuda:0")
# RuntimeError: Offset increment outside graph capture encountered unexpectedly.
```

### What we tried (none of these clear the state)

- `enforce_eager=True` on `ModelConfig`
- `torch.cuda.manual_seed(42)` after construction
- `torch.cuda.synchronize()` after construction

### Environment

- vLLM v0.17.0
- NVIDIA B200 (Blackwell, SM100)
- CUDA 13.0
- FlashInfer sparse MLA backend

### Likely cause

The FlashInfer sparse MLA backend (#33451) or DSA CUDA graph support (#34457) appears to activate CUDA graph RNG offset tracking during module construction that persists after `__init__` returns. #34552 also notes DSA "has issues with cudagraphs" on Blackwell.

### Workaround

Avoid all RNG operations after DSA module construction. Use deterministic initialization (`fill_()`, `torch.full()`, `torch.zeros()`) instead.

title: [Bugfix] Fix tensor shape mismatch in sparse attention with speculative decoding
body:
## Purpose

Fixes two tensor shape mismatches in sparse_indexer.py that cause RuntimeError when running DeepSeek-V3.2-NVFP4 with MTP and padded decode batches.

A previous refactor here correctly sliced `decode_metadata.seq_lens` to `batch_size` for `fp8_paged_mqa_logits`, but missed two downstream consumers that still used the unsliced tensor or the raw `num_decode_tokens` count:

**Fix 1: persistent_topk receiving wrong seq_lens**

persistent_topk was called with the full `decode_metadata.seq_lens` while logits and topk_indices were sized based on `batch_size * next_n.` The kernel used the unsliced seq_lens to determine output rows, producing a result with fewer rows than topk_indices expected.

 **Fix 2: topk_indices_buffer write-back after unpack_seq_triton**

After unpacking padded topk results, the code assigned back into `topk_indices_buffer[:num_decode_tokens]`. But num_decode_tokens is the total token count before packing, while unpack_seq_triton returns `sum(decode_lens)` rows — which is smaller when `requires_padding=True` (i.e. when short chunked prefills fall below the decode threshold). The write-back now uses `topk_indices.shape[0]` to match the actual unpacked size.

When does this trigger?

The bug surfaces specifically when all three conditions are met:
  - Speculative decoding is active (MTP/EAGLE), so next_n > 1
  - `requires_padding=True` — happens when a chunked prefill shorter than the decode threshold gets mixed into the decode batch
  - The padded batch size differs from the raw decode token count

Without speculative decoding (next_n=1) or without padding, the sizes happen to align and the bug is latent.

Error seen:
```
RuntimeError: The expanded size of the tensor (104) must match the existing size (98) at non-singleton dimension 0. Target sizes: [104, 2048]. Tensor sizes: [98, 2048] at sparse_indexer.py:168
```

## Test Plan
- Verified on B300 with DeepSeek-V3.2 (MTP next_n=2, next_n=4) using gsm8k eval for correctness

title: [bugfix]: support deepseek sparse attention on unsupported targets
body:

## Purpose

Blackwell RTX 6000 Pro is sm120 and is not supported by FlashMLA, so none of the models that use DSA will run. This includes Deepseek Exp, 3.2 and GLM 5+.

## Test Plan

title: [Feature] Add dense MHA fallback for short-sequence NSA prefill
body:
## Purpose

When using sparse MLA backends (e.g. FLASHMLA_SPARSE) for DeepSeek V3.2, all prefill tokens go through the sparse MQA path, including short sequences. The sparse indexer/topk overhead is unnecessary for short prefills where the sequence length is already within the top-k window — standard dense FlashAttention is both faster and produces identical results.

This PR adds an optional dense attention fallback controlled by `VLLM_NSA_PREFILL_DENSE_ATTN_KV_LEN_THRESHOLD`. When set (e.g. 2048, matching `index_topk`), prefill batches with `max_seq_len <= threshold` and no cached context bypass the sparse path and use `flash_attn_varlen_func` directly. Default is 0 (disabled), no behavior change.

The fallback is guarded by strict safety checks: sparse backend active, threshold > 0, prefill-only batch (no decode tokens), max_seq_len == max_query_len (no cached context), and num_actual_toks matches query_start_loc (no CUDA graph padding). It is implemented inline in `forward_impl()` — no changes to any sparse backend class.

Changes:
- `vllm/envs.py`: new env var `VLLM_NSA_PREFILL_DENSE_ATTN_KV_LEN_THRESHOLD`
- `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py`: dense fallback logic
- `vllm/v1/attention/backend.py`: docstring update

## Test Plan

DeepSeek V3.2 671B FP8, 8xH200, TP8, CUDA graphs, max_model_len=4096. Run each server config (threshold=0 baseline, threshold=2048 dense fallback) and compare.

Server (run twice, once per threshold):
```bash
VLLM_NSA_PREFILL_DENSE_ATTN_KV_LEN_THRESHOLD={0|2048} \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --port 8000
```

ShareGPT throughput (dataset: [anon8231489123/ShareGPT_Vicuna_unfiltered](https://huggingface.co/datasets/anon8231489123/ShareGPT_Vicuna_unfiltered), use the `ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json` file):
```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai \
  --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324 \
  --dataset-name sharegpt \
  --dataset-path ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json \
  --num-prompts 200 \
  --request-rate 5
```

Single-request decode speed:
```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"Write a complete FastAPI server.","max_tokens":2048,"temperature":0,"stream":false}'
```

GSM8K accuracy (5-shot, 1319 questions): use standard gsm8k eval script against the serving endpoint.

## Test Result

Online serving, ShareGPT (200 prompts, 5 RPS):

| Metric | Baseline | Dense Fallback | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 1123 | 148 | -86.8% |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 147 | 120 | -18.4% |
| P99 TTFT (ms) | 7858 | 333 | -95.8% |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 37.9 | 35.4 | -6.6% |
| Request throughput (req/s) | 3.97 | 3.73 | -6.0% |
| Output tok/s | 645 | 580 | -10.1% |

Single-request speed (bs=1, 2048 output tokens): 60.81 vs 60.87 tok/s — no regression.

GSM8K 5-shot (1319 questions): 92.49% vs 92.80% — no accuracy loss.

The main improvement is TTFT: Mean -86.8%, P99 -95.8%. Short-sequence prefills no longer stall behind the sparse indexer. The throughput/output tok/s decrease (-6%/-10.1%) is within run-to-run variance — ShareGPT uses non-deterministic sampling and output lengths differ across runs; the dense fallback only affects prefill and does not change decode throughput, as confirmed by the identical single-request decode speed.
