This directly isolates the contribution of this PR. **Results:** | Metric | Baseline (fusions off) | F2+F3 (fusions on) | Delta | |---|---|---|---| | Request throughput (req/s) | 5.91 | 6.18 | **+4.6%** | | Output tok/s | 591 | 618 | **+4.5%** | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 986 | 898 | **−9.0%** | | P99 TTFT (ms) | 8,997 | 7,927 | **−11.9%** | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 16.73 | 16.46 | **−1.6%** | | P99 TPOT (ms) | 35.54 | 32.75 | **−7.8%** | | P99 ITL (ms) | 92.96 | 88.35 | **−5.0%** | **QPS at 1s TTFT budget:** At this concurrency level, baseline mean TTFT is 986 ms — right at the 1s SLA boundary. F2+F3 mean TTFT drops to 898 ms, comfortably within the 1s budget, while delivering **+4.6% higher QPS** (5.91 → 6.18 req/s). This confirms that the fusions directly expand the operating headroom at the 1s TTFT SLA. All metrics improve with fusions enabled. Native MXFP4 is fully supported on MI350X (gfx950).
### Multi-seed variance (concurrency=16, ISL=1000, OSL=100, TP=8, 8×MI350X) | Seed | Output (tok/s) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Mean TTFT (ms) | |---|---|---|---| | 1234 | 904.7 | 14.10 | 368 | | 5678 | 1040.1 | 13.37 | 208 | | 9012 | 921.2 | 13.97 | 349 | | **mean** | **955.3** | **13.8 ± 0.4** | — | TPOT coefficient of variation < 3% — results are stable across seeds. ### F2 — FX graph op counts (synthetic 1-layer fixture, `hidden_size=7168`) *(From `test_functional_pattern_fires_no_residual` / `test_functional_pattern_fires_with_residual`, verified on 8×MI350X. No env var needed — patterns fire via `has_fused_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant()`.)* No-residual path (`rms_norm → dynamic_mxfp4_quant`): | FX node | w/o fusion | with F2 | |---|---:|---:| | `vllm_ir.rms_norm` (standalone) | 1 | 0 | | `rocm_aiter_dynamic_mxfp4_quant` (standalone) | 1 | 0 | | `rocm_aiter_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant` **(fused)** | 0 | **1** | | `matched_count` | 0 | **1** | With-residual path (`fused_add_rms_norm → dynamic_mxfp4_quant`): | FX node | w/o fusion | with F2 | |---|---:|---:| | `vllm_ir.fused_add_rms_norm` (standalone) | 1 | 0 | | `rocm_aiter_dynamic_mxfp4_quant` (standalone) | 1 | 0 | | `rocm_aiter_rmsnorm_add_mxfp4_quant` **(fused, with residual)** | 0 | **1** | | `matched_count` | 0 | **1** | Pattern registration confirmed via `VLLM_DEBUG_DUMP_PATH` on 8×MI350X (gfx950): `patterns.RocmAiterRMSNormQuantFusionPass.0.py` written for all 8 TP ranks, 16 patterns registered (2 epsilon variants × 4 shapes). --- ## Test Plan ```bash # F2 — unit + functional (GPU required for functional subset) pytest tests/rocm/test_mxfp4_fusion_patterns.py \ tests/compile/passes/test_mxfp4_quant_fusion.py \ -v --noconftest --override-ini="addopts=" # F3 — probe + dispatch tests pytest tests/rocm/aiter/test_f3_mla_fused_dispatch.py \ -v --noconftest --override-ini="addopts=" ``` Results on 8×MI350X (gfx950, vllm 0.20.2, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`): ``` tests/rocm/test_mxfp4_fusion_patterns.py 4 passed, 0 skipped tests/compile/passes/test_mxfp4_quant_fusion.py 35 passed, 1 skipped (aiter-absent probe skip) tests/rocm/aiter/test_f3_mla_fused_dispatch.py 6 passed, 9 skipped (MLA dispatch tests need PR3 impl) ``` Total: **45 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed** across 55 collected tests. **Models tested:** `amd/DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4` (quark, TP=8, torch.compile) — target model; `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` (BF16, TP=1, eager) — regression check confirming guard does not break non-MXFP4 models. --- ## Debugging Fusion Patterns vLLM provides several debugging aids for post-grad fusion passes: | Tool | How to enable | What you get | |---|---|---| | FX graph dumps | `VLLM_DEBUG_DUMP_PATH=` | Per-rank `patterns.{Pass}.py` + pre/post-pass graphs | | Match counting | Built-in | `matched_count` logged at INFO after each compiled graph | | Per-pass graph logging | `TORCH_LOGS="+post_grad_graphs"` | FX graph after each pass | | Pattern-match debug | `VLLM_PATTERN_MATCH_DEBUG=1` | Forwards to `TORCHINDUCTOR_PATTERN_MATCH_DEBUG=1` | --- ## Model Applicability and Benefit ### F3 — Immediate production benefit (all MLA models on ROCm) F3 fuses RoPE application and MLA KV-cache write into a single Triton kernel. It fires automatically via `has_fused_rope_mla_kv_cache()` — no user action, no env var. Any model using MLA attention on ROCm with AITER benefits immediately on upgrade. **What changes per decode step per layer:** | | Before this PR | After this PR | |---|---|---| | RoPE | `rotary_emb(q_pe, k_pe)` — separate kernel, round-trips through HBM | Fused into cache-write kernel — `q_pe`/`k_pe` stay in registers | | KV-cache write | `concat_and_cache_mla(kv_c, k_pe, kv_cache)` | `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla(...)` + one redundant write (removed in follow-on PR) | | Net HBM traffic | `k_pe` written out after RoPE, read back for cache write | `k_pe` never leaves registers between RoPE and cache write | The duplicate `do_kv_cache_update` call inside `mla_attn` still fires on this PR (correct but redundant — see Notes). Full kernel-launch reduction is tracked in the follow-on PR. **Models that benefit automatically:** | Model | vLLM arch file | F3 fires | |---|---|---| | `amd/DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4` | `deepseek_v2.py` | ✓ TPOT 13.8 ± 0.4 ms (measured, 3 seeds) | | `amd/DeepSeek-V3-MXFP4` | `deepseek_v2.py` | ✓ same `MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper` | | `amd/DeepSeek-V3-0324-MXFP4` | `deepseek_v4.py` | ✓ same `MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper` | | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1` (BF16) | `deepseek_v2.py` | ✓ all 61 layers — 488 F3 log lines (8 workers × 61) | | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3` (BF16) | `deepseek_v2.py` | ✓ all 61 layers — 488 F3 log lines (8 workers × 61) | | `moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Instruct` | `kimi_linear.py` | ✓ same `MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper` | Verified on 8×MI350X: `has_fused_rope_mla_kv_cache=True`, `is_mla_enabled=True`, `_f3_fusion_enabled=True` — fires for any model routed through `MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper` (`deepseek_v2.py`, `deepseek_v4.py`, `kimi_linear.py`, and 4 others in the vLLM model registry). **Models unaffected (no MLA):** Llama, Mistral, Qwen, Gemma — use GQA/MHA, never enter the MLA code path. This change is a no-op for them. --- ## Notes - **No env vars added.** F2 and F3 both activate automatically via `has_fused_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant()` and `has_fused_rope_mla_kv_cache()` respectively. This follows PR#42864's pattern: `RocmAiterAllReduceFusionPass` uses `get_aiter_allreduce_max_size()` as its runtime guard — no env var. - **F2 targets dynamic-activation MXFP4**, not the weight-static OCP MX GEMM path (`gemm_with_dynamic_quant`) used by `amd/DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4`. Because `dynamic_mxfp4_quant` is currently disabled in `QuarkConfig` (overhead of per-token dynamic quant can negate kernel speedup pending benchmarking), F2 patterns are verified through synthetic unit tests. The follow-on PR will re-evaluate and, if benchmarks confirm a net gain, enable the path. **The serving numbers above reflect F3 gains only.** - **AR+MXFP4 fusion** (`rocm_aiter_fused_allreduce_*_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant`) is deferred to a follow-on PR — the AITER kernel does not exist yet. This covers the dominant decode-phase chain (`all_reduce → rms_norm → mxfp4_quant`, 61× per decode step at TP=8). - **`do_kv_cache_update`** still runs after the F3 kernel (redundant but correct). The duplicate write will be removed in the follow-on PR. - **`RocmAiterRMSNormQuantFusionPass`** logs at INFO level when MXFP4 patterns are registered (count + epsilon variants), making fusion activity visible in server logs without setting any env var. - **FX graph dumps** use `VLLM_DEBUG_DUMP_PATH=` (not `VLLM_TORCH_COMPILE_DUMP`). Per-rank subdirectories `rank_N_dp_0/` contain `patterns.RocmAiterRMSNormQuantFusionPass.0.py` (registered patterns) and `__compiled_fn_*.py` (pre/post-pass graphs). --- ## AI Assistance Disclosure Developed with GitHub Copilot assistance. title: [2/N][KV-Cache Layout Refactor] Pack K/V into the content dim across attention backends
body:
PR #42374 (first part of RFC #42082) has been split into 4 PRs:

#44454 [1/N][KV-Cache Layout Refactor] Refactor DSV4 KV cache config
-> #44455 [2/N][KV-Cache Layout Refactor] Pack K/V into the content dim across attention backends
#44456 [3/N][KV-Cache Layout Refactor] Standardize Mamba cache; drop `get_transfer_cache_regions`
#44458 [4/N][KV-Cache Layout Refactor] Standardize KV cache layout

## Summary

Packs K and V into the content dimension across attention backends, changing the KV cache shape from `(num_blocks, 2, block_size, num_kv_heads, head_size)` (separate leading K/V dim) to `(num_blocks, num_kv_heads, block_size, 2*head_size)`. Backends recover K/V via `kv_cache.transpose(1, 2).split(head_size, dim=-1)`. This removes the need for `get_kv_cache_stride_order()` in most paths and is a major diff reduction toward #42374.

Stacked on top of #44454 (land that first)

## Testing

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py -v
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -v
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -v
```

Most backend paths require specific GPUs (ROCm, nvfp4/flashinfer); the submitter will run the relevant subset on appropriate hardware before merge.

title: [6/N][KV-Cache Layout Refactor] Standardize KV cache layout
body:
PR #42374 (first part of RFC #42082) has been split into 4 PRs:

#44454 [1/N][KV-Cache Layout Refactor] Refactor DSV4 KV cache config
#44455 [2/N][KV-Cache Layout Refactor] Pack K/V into the content dim across attention backends
#44456 [3/N][KV-Cache Layout Refactor] Standardize Mamba cache; drop `get_transfer_cache_regions`
-> #44458 [4/N][KV-Cache Layout Refactor] Standardize KV cache layout

## Summary

Final step of the KV-cache layout standardization ladder. Introduces standardized layout resolution and `reshape_kv_cache`, removes the legacy `get_kv_cache_shape` / `get_kv_cache_stride_order` APIs, and removes the remaining cross-layer block machinery from connectors. RFC #42082.

Stacked on top of #44456 (`bind_kv_cache`); the chain is #44454 → #44455 → #44456 → this PR. This is the restacked remainder of #42374, not a duplicate implementation of another open PR.

The rebase audit also fixed layout-sensitive regressions in compressed MLA allocation, CPU and XPU attention, NIXL, Mooncake, Mooncake Store, simple CPU offload, and in-place block copying. Coverage now includes layer-compact, cross-layer, separate-head-group, virtual-block-splitting, shared-storage, and host-buffer cases.

## Testing

Passed locally:

```bash
# All hooks on changed files, including ruff and mypy
pre-commit run --files <changed files>

# KV allocation and compressed-MLA coverage
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py
# 70 passed

# Copy/offload layout coverage
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py
# 22 passed

# Mooncake, Mooncake Store, and standardized Mamba registration
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py
# 115 passed

# CPU layout and XPU sparse-MLA interface regressions
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/attention/test_cpu_kv_cache_layout.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_xpu_mla_sparse.py \
  -k 'split_cpu_kv_cache or flattens_standard_cache'
# 6 passed

# NIXL registration across all layouts and separate head groups
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  -k test_register_kv_caches
# 16 passed

VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -x \
  tests/compile/passes/test_fusion_attn.py
# 24 passed, 36 skipped

VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BHLNC .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -x \
  tests/compile/passes/test_fusion_attn.py
# 24 passed, 36 skipped
```

The full NIXL unit file completed with 77 passed and 2 environment-only failures because NIXL is not installed in the local environment; all modified NIXL registration/handshake tests passed.

Model evaluations were not run locally because this is a cache-layout refactor with no intentional model-output change. GPU/XPU and multi-node accuracy coverage is delegated to CI and must be reviewed before merge.

title: [KV Connector][Mooncake] Pipeline-parallel support for PD-disaggregated serving with Mooncake connector
body:
## Purpose

This PR adds Mooncake-specific support for pipeline-parallel prefill in PD-disaggregated serving. It is intended for long-context workloads where the prefill side needs PP to fit or run efficiently on H20-class devices.
Decode-side PP is intentionally not part of this PR.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

Run the Mooncake unit suites from a Kubernetes validation pod using the PR source checkout:

```bash
python3 -m pytest -v --tb=short \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_stats.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py
```

### GLM-5.1-FP8 E2E smoke

title: [ROCm][MLA] AITER FP8 persistent ASM prefill backend
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

**Needs: AITER v0.1.22**.

Add a new `ROCM_AITER_ASM` MLA prefill backend. It's the first ROCm backend that supports fp8 prefill. It's the new default on gfx950 when using FP8 KV.

**Perf diff:** 8k/1k ISL/OSL: **7-9% lower TTFT**, **2-6% higher QPS** (tested at 32-128 concurrency). 1k/1k no visible diff

**Note**: previously ROCM_AITER_MLA dispatched to this asm kernel during **causal** prefill, but never during chunked prefill due to the **non-causal** kernel producing numerically incorrect LSE. https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/3606 fixed this inaccuracy, so we can now run this kernel also during chunked prefill. Thus removed the fp8 asm invocations in ROCM_AITER_MLA.

<details> <summary> Technical details </summary>

## Details

Note on changes made in the shared mla backend code:
- Previously, ROCm didn't have a prefill backend supporting fp8. That means that when using fp8 KV, those would be dequantized to bf16 before proceeding to the rest of the computation 
- In Dsv3 with FP8 KV, the compressed KV `kv_c` is stored as fp8 and subsequently up-proj'd by `kv_b_proj` as `kv_b_proj(kv_c)`
- On ROCm the `kv_b_proj` on fp8 DSv3 is a Fp8LinearMethod whose GEMM runs an fp8 quant on its input. It expects the input to not be quantized already
- Hence we need to upcast this `kv_c` to the model dtype. We do this in inside `_get_kv_b_proj_input_dtype`

</details>

## Test Plan

Bench sweep + gsm8k:

```shell
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9
```

title: [MegaMoE] Support external DP load balancing with DeepGEMM MegaMoE
body:
When the launcher masks CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to a single GPU per process (e.g. when using external external DP load balancing), every rank reports device index 0. The CUDA symmetric memory allocator rejects the rendezvous as "overlapping devices from different ranks."

Before fork/CUDA init in the multiproc executor, detect this case when moe_backend is deep_gemm_mega_moe, expand device visibility to all GPUs, and pass the physical GPU ID to workers via _VLLM_MEGAMOE_GPU_ID. Workers read this env var to pin to the correct device instead of relying on CVD masking.


This PR is a very ugly hack :-(
Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44556

title: [Bug]: External DP Load Balancing plus DeepGEMM MegaMoE
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

When the launcher masks CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to a single GPU per process (e.g. when using external external DP load balancing), every rank reports device index 0. 

Then, when using DeepGEMM MegaMoE, the CUDA symmetric memory allocator then rejects the rendezvous, and vLLM will fail during the profile run with:
```tms-wide-ep-prefill-0 vllm (EngineCore_DP0 pid=3060)     raise RuntimeError(
tms-wide-ep-prefill-0 vllm (EngineCore_DP0 pid=3060) RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'CUDASymmetricMemoryAllocator::rendezvous: detected allocations from overlapping devices from different ranks.', please check the stack trace above for the root cause
```

I put up a PR to address it here: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44555 but I do not like it.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Derive num_speculative_tokens from a speculators draft config
body:
## Purpose

Refs #40382. The primary issue there, no Ampere attention backend for a non-causal `head_dim=256` draft, is already resolved on current main by #40394. This PR fixes the remaining `num_speculative_tokens` auto-detect gap.

Serving a speculators-format draft (Eagle3, DFlash, PEAGLE, ...) through `--speculative-config` with the target as the top-level `--model` fails to start unless the user also restates `num_speculative_tokens`, even though the draft config already declares it under `speculators_config.proposal_methods[0].speculative_tokens`.

The existing auto-detect path only runs when the speculator repo itself is the top-level `--model` and `maybe_override_with_speculators` handles it. With the target as `--model` and the draft supplied via `--speculative-config`, `SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__` loads the draft as a `SpeculatorsConfig` built from `transformer_layer_config`, so the proposal-method `speculative_tokens` count is dropped before `num_speculative_tokens` can default from it.

This carries the speculators proposal count into the draft config and defaults `num_speculative_tokens` from that count when the user did not provide an explicit value. A user-provided value still takes precedence. Otherwise, non-DSpark drafts prefer `n_predict`, then `num_lookahead_tokens`. DSpark keeps its existing `block_size` / `dspark_block_size` defaults.

## Test Plan

Validated `EngineArgs.create_engine_config()`, the shared config-build path used by `vllm serve` and offline `LLM(...)` before engine startup. The repro uses target model `unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`, speculators draft `nm-testing/Llama3_2_1B_speculator.eagle3`, and omits `num_speculative_tokens`.

## Test Result

After merging main `2067297b2f15`, the current candidate passes 47 CPU tests and the scoped pre-commit hooks:

title: Add DeepSeek-V4  DCP decode support

## Summary

This PR adds decode context parallel support for DeepSeek-V4 Flash.

Main changes:
- Add DCP-aware FlashMLA decode output/LSE merge.
- Add DCP-aware compressor stats merge and compressed KV cache write.
- Add DCP local KV/index mapping for DeepSeek-V4 sparse decode paths.
- Keep existing PCP/prefill behavior unchanged.

### How you are installing vllm

## Summary

When installing vLLM on an AMD/ROCm host running Python 3.11 via the `--extra-index-url` method from the [vLLM release page](https://vllm.ai/releases), the resolver silently installs the **CUDA** wheel instead of failing or installing a ROCm artifact.

Root cause: the ROCm index at `https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/vllm/` currently provides only **cp312** wheels:
```text
vllm-0.22.1+rocm722-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_34_x86_64.whl
vllm-0.22.1rc2+rocm722-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_34_x86_64.whl
```

Because there is no `abi3` / `cp311` / `cp313` ROCm wheel, a resolver running on Python 3.11 rejects the `cp312` ROCm artifact on ABI grounds. Since `--extra-index-url` *merges* the custom index with PyPI (rather than replacing it), the resolver then falls back to the standard PyPI release, `vllm-0.22.1-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl`. Its `cp38-abi3` tag is a valid match for Python 3.11, so it installs cleanly, but vLLM's PyPI wheels are compiled for **CUDA**, so an AMD host silently ends up with a CUDA build.

Net effect: users on AMD hardware running the distro-default Python (e.g. Python 3.11 on Debian 12 Bookworm) who omit the strict `+rocm722` local version string unknowingly install a CUDA wheel that cannot load on their GPU. Pinning `vllm==0.22.1+rocm722` instead produces a clear `No matching distribution found` on Python 3.11 i.e. the failure is silent only because the local-version tag was omitted.

## Evidence

Running

```bash
pip install vllm==0.22.1 --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/0.22.1/rocm722
```

on Python 3.11 installs `vllm-0.22.1-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl` (note: no `+rocm` local version tag). Its bundled `.so` files expose it as the CUDA build:

```text
_C.abi3.so
_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so
_flashmla_C.abi3.so
_flashmla_extension_C.abi3.so
_moe_C.abi3.so
cumem_allocator.abi3.so
spinloop.abi3.so
```

There is **no `_rocm_C.abi3.so`**. On a ROCm host, importing the platform module shows the CUDA extensions failing to load and the ROCm extension missing entirely:

```text
WARNING [rocm.py:44] Failed to import from vllm._C with ImportError('libcudart.so.13: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory')
WARNING [rocm.py:50] Failed to import from vllm._C_stable_libtorch with ImportError('libcudart.so.13: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory')
WARNING [rocm.py:55] Failed to import from vllm._rocm_C with ModuleNotFoundError("No module named 'vllm._rocm_C'")
```

Downstream, `LLM('facebook/opt-125m')` fails at device-config init with `RuntimeError: Device string must not be empty`, a symptom of the missing ROCm extension.

Consistent with being the CUDA build, the wheel's dependency closure pulls in the CUDA stack (`torch==2.11.0` plain, `nvidia-*-cu13`, `flashinfer`) rather than the ROCm equivalents.

## Why this matters

The `rocm/` segment of the URL path implies a ROCm install, but because of the Python version mismatch and PyPI fallback, users on AMD hardware end up with an incompatible CUDA artifact and no error. It also blocks Debian Bookworm (Python 3.11) and Debian Trixie (Python 3.13) users from using the prebuilt ROCm wheels at all unless they construct a custom Python 3.12 environment, for which the base images have no precedent.

## Questions

1. Is there a plan to publish an `abi3` (cp38–cp313) **`+rocm`** wheel, the way the standard CUDA `abi3` wheel covers all Python versions in one artifact? Currently the only genuine ROCm wheels in `rocm/vllm/` are cp312-only.

2. Can the docs / release pages warn that ROCm wheels are currently cp312-only, and that omitting the exact `+rocm722` local version flag on a non-3.12 interpreter causes a silent fallback to the CUDA wheel rather than an error?

## Environment

- vLLM: 0.22.1 (attempted install from `https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/0.22.1/rocm722`)
- ROCm: 7.2.2 (path suffix `rocm722`, installs to `/opt/rocm-7.2.0`)
- torch: 2.12.0+rocm7.2, `torch.version.hip = 7.2.53211`, `torch.version.cuda = None`
- GPUs: 2× AMD Instinct MI210 (gfx90a), visible via `torch.cuda.device_count()` = 2
- OS / Python: Debian Bookworm, Python 3.11

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fix mHC fused-RMSNorm big-fuse miscompile for hidden_size != 4096
body:
## Purpose

`mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang` (the RMSNorm-fused mHC pre big-fuse used
by DeepSeek-V4 when `norm_weight` is supplied) pipelines its fused-RMSNorm pass
at `num_stages=3`. Combined with the loop-carried `sumsq` reduction and the
persistent `output_shared` staging buffer written at per-iteration offsets, the
TileLang software pipeliner miscompiles the loop. The result is **silently wrong
`layer_input`** for every hidden size except 4096:

| hidden_size | trip count (`H // 1024`) | result vs fp32 reference |
|---|---|---|
| 2048 | 2 | **NaN** |
| 3072 | 3 | **NaN** |
| 4096 | 4 | correct (1.66e-3) |
| 5120 | 5 | 0.55 |
| 6144 | 6 | 0.23 |
| 7168 (DSv4) | 7 | 0.17 |
| 8192 | 8 | 0.36 |

It is occupancy-dependent (at H=7168 it is correct for ≤256 tokens, breaks at
≥512) and slightly non-deterministic run-to-run — the signature of a pipeline
prologue/epilogue codegen issue, not an arithmetic one. The path was evidently
only validated at `hidden_size=4096`.

## Fix

Drop the fused-RMSNorm pass to `num_stages=2`, matching the correct no-norm
sibling kernel `mhc_pre_big_fuse_tilelang` (which already uses depth 2). One line.

Root cause is in the pipeliner, not the algorithm: forcing the no-norm kernel
(no loop-carried state) to `num_stages=3` stays correct, so depth-3 alone is
fine — it only breaks when combined with the loop-carried reduction + persistent
shared buffer. Depth-2 handles that combination correctly.

## Not a duplicate

Checked open mHC PRs (#42735 bf16 shared staging, #44144 XPU fused_post_pre,
#43950 ROCm aiter default, #42893 / #41834 DSv4 platform fixes). None touch the
`num_stages` / fused-norm correctness. #42735 is a separate float32→bf16 staging
perf change and already uses `num_stages=2` in its variants.

## Test

Verified on GB200 (CUDA 13, TileLang) against an fp32 RMSNorm reference built on
top of the existing `mhc_pre_ref` in `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py`:

- Before: `hidden_size` 2048/3072 → NaN; 5120/6144/7168/8192 → rel-err 0.17–0.55; only 4096 correct.
- After: all hidden sizes 2048–8192 match to ~1.6e-3 (bf16 floor), deterministic, across token counts 1..16384.
- Full op path `torch.ops.vllm.mhc_pre_tilelang(..., norm_weight, norm_eps)` (deep_gemm + kernel) at H=3072/7168: 1.67e-3, all finite.
- The non-fused paths (`mhc_pre`, `mhc_post`) are unchanged and unaffected.

> AI assistance (Claude) was used to diagnose and write this change; the author reviewed every line and ran the verification above.

title: [Opt] Optimize rotary embedding cache length
body:
## Description

This PR reduces RoPE `sin/cos` cache memory usage when the runtime
`max_model_len` is smaller than the model config's maximum RoPE position.

when vllm server use `--max-model-len 32768`
**DeepSeek-V4 saves 248MB, Qwen3-VL saves 224MB, gemma-4 saves 336MB**

Some recent long-context models define very large `max_position_embeddings`.
Before this change, vLLM precomputed RoPE caches for the full configured length
even when users explicitly ran with a smaller `--max-model-len`. This can waste
a large amount of memory, especially on large models and mixed-attention
architectures where multiple RoPE instances may be created and their
`sin/cos` caches cannot always be reused.

This change clamps the RoPE cache length in `get_rope()` for RoPE variants
where `max_position` only controls cache size and does not affect frequency
computation. DeepSeek YaRN-style RoPE is handled separately: the original max
position is still preserved for scaling math, while only the actual cache length
is limited.

The optimized cache keeps the same valid prefix values as the original full
cache, while avoiding allocation for positions beyond the runtime
`max_model_len`.

## Testing

Ran a remote-config smoke test comparing the optimized cache prefix against the
original full cache use --max-model-len 32768:
[test_remote_rope_configs.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28667583/test_remote_rope_configs.py)
``` python test_remote_rope_configs.py  --compare-prefix  # --max-model-len 32768 as default```

title: perf: port push-based 2-buffer allreduce from SGLang
body:
## Summary

Port SGLang's push-based 2-buffer allreduce protocol into vLLM as a new collective communication backend for small tensor reductions. The push protocol eliminates 2 explicit NVLink barrier round-trips per allreduce call by using a push-based data arrival detection mechanism (positive-zero sentinel) with a 2-buffer epoch alternation scheme.

The new `PushAllReduce` communicator is inserted into `CudaCommunicator`'s dispatch priority above the existing barrier-based `CustomAllreduce` for messages below a configurable size threshold (720 KB for TP=8 on B200). For DeepSeek-V4-Pro decode (BS=1, TP=8, 8x B200), all 122 allreduce calls per forward pass (14,336 bytes each) use the push protocol.

This implements improvement plan step I2 from cross-trace analysis comparing vLLM and SGLang allreduce performance on DeepSeek-V4-Pro with 8x NVIDIA B200 GPUs.

### Key Design Decisions
- CUDA kernel vendored from SGLang with minimal macro substitutions (no SGLang dependencies)
- No modification to existing `CustomAllreduce` code paths
- CUDA graph safe: epoch counter in device memory, fixed grid size = SM count
- No `cudaMemcpy` in eager mode (performance advantage over barrier-based approach)
- PDL (`griddepcontrol`) runtime dispatch for sm90+ GPUs (Blackwell/Hopper)
- Out-of-place semantics matching vLLM convention

### Files Changed
- **New** (6): `push_all_reduce_kernel.cuh`, `push_all_reduce.cuh`, `push_all_reduce.cu`, `push_all_reduce.py`, `test_push_all_reduce.py`, `_test_push_ar_worker.py`
- **Modified** (5): `CMakeLists.txt`, `torch_bindings.cpp`, `_custom_ops.py`, `cuda_communicator.py`, `parallel_state.py`

## Performance Results

Benchmarked on DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 8x NVIDIA B200 (TP=8), BS=1, ISL=4, OSL=33024:

| Metric | Patched (enabled) | Baseline (disabled) | Delta | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Throughput (tokens/s) | 84.060 | 82.301 | +1.759 | **+2.14%** |
| Output tokens/s | 84.05 | 82.29 | +1.76 | **+2.14%** |
| Elapsed time (s) | 392.912 | 401.308 | -8.396 | **-2.09%** |
| Derived TPOT (ms/token) | 11.897 | 12.152 | -0.255 | **-2.09%** |

TTFT is not separately reported; with ISL=4 (single prefill step), TTFT is negligible (~10-20 ms) and identical between runs.

The baseline uses the same patched code with the feature disabled via env var (`VLLM_DISABLE_AUTO_PERF_PLAN_2=1`), falling back to barrier-based `CustomAllreduce`.

## Correctness (lm_eval)

lm_eval gsm8k 5-shot (1319 prompts), DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP=2 (identical architecture):

| Metric | Enabled | Disabled | Delta | Within Tolerance? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| flexible-extract exact_match | 0.9530 | 0.9515 | +0.0015 | YES (< 0.005) |
| strict-match exact_match | 0.9538 | 0.9515 | +0.0023 | YES (< 0.005) |

**VERDICT: PASS** -- No correctness regression. Deltas are within 1 standard error (~0.0058), statistically indistinguishable.

## Feature Toggle

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Env var | `VLLM_DISABLE_AUTO_PERF_PLAN_2` |
| Enable (default) | Do not set the env var |
| Disable | `export VLLM_DISABLE_AUTO_PERF_PLAN_2=1` |
| Startup log (enabled) | `[AutoPerf] Plan step 2: AllReduce push-based 2-buffer protocol is ENABLED` |
| Startup log (disabled) | `[AutoPerf] Plan step 2: AllReduce push-based 2-buffer protocol is DISABLED (env override)` |

When disabled, `PushAllReduce.__init__` returns immediately with no resource allocation. The existing barrier-based `CustomAllreduce` is used as the fallback.

## Test Coverage

24 tests, **all passing** (138s on 2x B200):

| Category | Count | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Unit Tests (UT-1 to UT-16) | 16 | Build verification, init, should_use, correctness (int/float), sentinel, epoch alternation (1000 iters), thread count, threshold, out-of-place, dtype, multilayer (366 ARs), lifecycle, warmup, asymmetric data, identical values |
| Integration Tests (IT-1, IT-4, IT-10) | 3 | Dispatch priority routing, coexistence with CustomAllreduce, interleaved push AR + NCCL |
| CUDA Graph Tests (CG-1) | 1 | Graph capture + 10 replays with varying data |
| E2E Tests (E2E-4) | 1 | Transformer block simulation (61 blocks x 2 ARs x 2 steps) |
| Feature Toggle Tests (FT-1 to FT-3) | 3 | Enabled/disabled/not-disabled env var semantics |

title: [KV Connector] Mooncake store: prefix-cache retention interval for sparse attention
body:
Follow-up of #43447.

## Summary

Adds prefix-cache retention support to the Mooncake KV store's `store_mask`, so the store writes exactly the blocks a future local prefix-cache hit can actually consume — and no more.

Previously `store_mask` computed a per-lcm-region template (via a dummy-hash pass through `find_longest_cache_hit`) and tiled it across the request. This refactor instead reuses the engine's own `SingleTypeKVCacheManager.reachable_block_mask`, the same logic the local prefix cache uses to decide block reachability. As a result:

- For full-attention groups the mask is unchanged (every chunk is stored).
- For sparse / sliding-window-attention (SWA) groups, the retained tail blocks now honor `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL`. Instead of keeping an SWA tail at *every* lcm boundary, the store keeps one tail per `retention_interval`-token segment, plus the latest replay-boundary tail derived from the request's prompt length (`num_prompt_tokens`). This significantly reduces store writes for sparse-attention models (e.g. DSV4-style SWA checkpointing) while preserving cache-hit reachability.

`num_prompt_tokens` is plumbed from the request tracker (`prefill_end_tokens`) through `ReqMeta` into the sending thread so the coordinator can compute the replay boundary.

## Behavior

- `retention_interval=None` (default): keeps the SWA tail at every lcm boundary — matches prior behavior.
- `retention_interval=K`: keeps one SWA tail per K-token segment.
- `retention_interval=0`: drops all segment tails; only the latest replay boundary (capped at `num_prompt-1`, aligned down to lcm) is retained.

Configured via the existing `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL` env var, mirroring vLLM core's `KVCacheCoordinator.retention_interval`.

## Testing

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py -q
# 26 passed
```

Added 4 new tests covering the dense default, interval-based sparsification, the `retention_interval=0` replay-only case, and coexistence of segment + replay tails. Lint clean (`ruff check`, `ruff format`, `mypy`).

## Notes

- Not a duplicate: no open PR addresses Mooncake store retention; searched `vllm-project/vllm` open PRs for "mooncake store retention" and this branch head.
- AI assistance was used in preparing this change; the human submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above.

title: [Bug] ValueError: Following weights were not initialized from checkpoint (Gemma 4 models with KV sharing)
body:
### Describe the bug

When serving Gemma 4 models (specifically `google/gemma-4-E2B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized`) that leverage Key-Value (KV) cache sharing (`num_kv_shared_layers > 0`), the vLLM engine initialization crashes with a `ValueError` during weight validation.

vLLM's `Gemma4Attention` class unconditionally instantiates `self.k_norm` and `self.v_norm` for all 35 layers in its constructor. However, the last 20 layers are KV-shared layers which omit KV projections and normalization, and therefore correct model checkpoints do not contain weights for `k_norm` and `v_norm` in these layers.

Since the parameters are registered in PyTorch but missing from the checkpoint, `track_weights_loading` triggers a validation failure and crashes.

### Environment

* **vLLM Version:** 0.22.1
* **Model:** `google/gemma-4-E2B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized`
* **Architecture:** `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` / `Gemma4ForCausalLM`

### Steps to Reproduce

Run the following server command:
```bash
vllm serve google/gemma-4-E2B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized
```

### Full Server Console Output & Traceback


title: [Bugfix] Replace sequential port scan with atomic port=0 in get_open_ports_list
body:
Fixes part of #28498 — eliminates the sequential scan TOCTOU race in `get_open_ports_list()`.

## Purpose

`get_open_ports_list()` scanned ports sequentially from `VLLM_PORT`, making
assignments predictable across concurrent processes. Multiple processes would
all pick the same ports, causing `zmq.error.ZMQError: Address already in use`
in multi-node DP deployments.

This replaces the sequential scan with OS-assigned port=0 binding, which is
atomic (the OS guarantees the port is free at discovery) and unpredictable
(random ephemeral port assignment). When `VLLM_PORT` is set, it acts as a
minimum port bound, preserving backward compatibility for deployments
with port range restrictions (firewall rules, k8s policies, Docker mappings).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/utils_/test_network_utils.py -v
```

## Test Result

**16/16 pass** (15 existing + 1 new concurrent regression test).

The new test `test_get_open_ports_list_no_collisions_across_processes` spawns
5 concurrent processes each calling `get_open_ports_list(5)`:

**Before fix** (old code):
```
Total ports: 25, Unique: 6
FAIL: 19 collisions detected
```

**After fix** (this PR):
```
Total ports: 25, Unique: 25
PASS: No port collisions across 5 concurrent processes
```

Note: this fixes `get_open_ports_list()` callers (`core_client.py:1573`,
`parallel.py:815`). Other `get_open_port()` sites (e.g., `utils.py:1040` when
`defer_api_server_ports=False`) remain vulnerable and require Rust front-end
or Ray changes, documented as known limitations.

## AI disclosure

This PR was developed with AI assistance (DeepSeek V4 Pro, OpenCode).
All code has been reviewed and understood by the human submitter.

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

title: [Bug][DeepSeekV4-MTP] DeepSeekV4MultiTokenPredictorLayer.e_proj/h_proj constructed without prefix=, breaks compressed-tensors quant matching
body:
## Summary

`vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v4_mtp.py`'s `DeepSeekV4MultiTokenPredictorLayer.__init__` constructs `e_proj` and `h_proj` (both `ReplicatedLinear`) **without passing a `prefix=` kwarg**. When `compressed_tensors` is the active quant_config, `get_scheme(layer_name="")` then fails with:

```
ValueError: Unable to find matching target for  in the compressed-tensors config.
```

(Note the empty module name in the error — that's the empty prefix.)

## Reproduction

Any DeepSeek-V4 W4A16+FP8 artifact that retains a BF16 MTP draft block, served with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`, on stock upstream vLLM. Concrete example:

```bash
vllm serve canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-W4A16-FP8-MTP \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}' \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  ... (other flags)
```

Without `--speculative-config`, the model loads cleanly (the main model's `AutoWeightsLoader` uses `skip_substrs=["mtp."]`, so MTP weights stay on disk untouched). The error only fires when the spec-decode path constructs the draft model.

## Stack (truncated)

```
File "vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v4_mtp.py", line 81, in __init__
    self.e_proj = ReplicatedLinear(
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py", line 274, in __init__
    elif quant_method := quant_config.get_quant_method(self, prefix=prefix):
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py", line 818, in get_scheme_dict
    matched_target = find_matched_target(...)
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/utils.py", line 154, in find_matched_target
    raise ValueError(
ValueError: Unable to find matching target for  in the compressed-tensors config.
```

## Why this can't be fixed artifact-side

The matched layer_name is the empty string. Any ignore regex that matches `""` (e.g. `re:^$` or `re:.*`) would also match every other module — including the routed experts that should remain quantized. There's no way to disambiguate from the artifact.

## Proposed fix — surgical, two lines

In `deepseek_v4_mtp.py`'s `DeepSeekV4MultiTokenPredictorLayer.__init__`:

```python
self.e_proj = ReplicatedLinear(
    config.hidden_size, config.hidden_size,
    bias=False, return_bias=False,
    quant_config=quant_config,
    prefix=f"{prefix}.e_proj",     # ← ADD
)
self.h_proj = ReplicatedLinear(
    config.hidden_size, config.hidden_size,
    bias=False, return_bias=False,
    quant_config=quant_config,
    prefix=f"{prefix}.h_proj",     # ← ADD
)
```

With proper prefixes, the ignore patterns `re:^model\.mtp\..*` and `re:^mtp\..*` (which W4A16+FP8 MTP artifacts already need anyway) will match and skip quantization for the BF16 MTP draft block correctly.

## Alternative: revive the artifact-aware skip path

@yangsiqt2's [#43893](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43893) skipped MTP quant_config when no MTP-specific quantization tensors exist on disk. That approach was closed as "the quantizer should configure their quant_configs accordingly." That redirect is partially correct (we **did** fix the main-model side at the artifact: [canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-W4A16-FP8-MTP @ 289254e7](https://huggingface.co/canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-W4A16-FP8-MTP/tree/fix-ignore-runtime-names)), but for the MTP draft the artifact has no way to match an empty layer_name. Either the prefix-propagation fix above, or restoring #43893's intent, will close this. The prefix fix is smaller and more aligned with the rest of the codebase, so I'd lean that way.

## Affected artifacts

Any `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-*-MTP` checkpoint where the MTP draft is BF16 on disk and the main model is compressed-tensors-quantized. Includes `canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-W4A16-FP8-MTP`, `canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4-FP8-MTP`, and likely the V4-Pro siblings.

## Environment

- vLLM: `0.1.dev297+gc05638d70.d20260506.cu132` (jasl/vllm ds4 fork derivative; the upstream `main` is also affected per static reading of `deepseek_v4_mtp.py`)
- Hardware: 2× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM 12.1a), TP=2, QSFP RoCE between nodes
- Reproduced 2026-06-07

Happy to send a PR with the two-line fix if it's wanted.

title: [Kernel][Perf] Add moe_sum_kernel specializations for topk=5-8
body:
### Purpose

This PR addresses a performance regression in MoE (Mixture of Experts) models with top-k > 4 (e.g., Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with top-8, DeepSeek-V4 with top-6). Previously, the `moe_sum()` CUDA kernel only had specialized implementations for topk=2, 3, and 4. For topk=5 through 8, it fell through to `at::sum_out()` — PyTorch's generic reduction kernel — which is significantly slower on H20 GPUs.

The fix adds compile-time template specializations for topk=5, 6, 7, and 8 to the existing `moe_sum_kernel` template, ensuring all common topk values use the optimized VLLM_LDG-based CUDA kernel with coalesced memory access and no PyTorch fallback.

### Changes

**File: `csrc/moe/moe_align_sum_kernels.cu`** (lines 653–686)

Added four new cases to the `moe_sum` switch statement, each instantiating `moe_sum_kernel<scalar_t, TOPK>` with compile-time unrolling:

```cpp
case 5:
  VLLM_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES(input.scalar_type(), "moe_sum_kernel", [&] {
    vllm::moe::moe_sum_kernel<scalar_t, 5><<<grid, block, 0, stream>>>(
        output.data_ptr<scalar_t>(), input.data_ptr<scalar_t>(), hidden_size);
  });
  break;
// ... cases 6, 7, 8 follow the same pattern
```

Each case uses the same efficient pattern as the existing topk=2/3/4 kernels:
- Compile-time constant `TOPK` enables full loop unrolling
- `VLLM_LDG` read-only cache hints for coalesced memory access
- Single kernel launch (vs. PyTorch fallback's less optimal reduction)
- CUDA Graph capture compatible (kernel launches are deterministic)

The default case (`topk > 8`) remains `at::sum_out()` for rare configurations.

### Test Plan

1. **Build**: Verify CUDA kernel compiles without errors
   ```bash
   python -m pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto
   ```

2. **Unit tests**: Run MoE kernel tests
   ```bash
   .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/ -v -k "moe_sum or topk_weight"
   ```

3. **Benchmark**: Profile Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (top-8, 256 experts) on H20
   - Measure decode phase GPU time for `moe_sum` operations
   - Compare throughput (tokens/sec) and TPOT (time per output token)
   - Verify `at::native::reduce_kernel` no longer appears in profiling

### Test Result

**Benchmark configuration:**
- Model: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (top-8 MoE, 256 experts)
- Hardware: NVIDIA H20
- Batch: Continuous batching with varying sequence lengths

**Results:**

| Metric | Before (topk=8) | After (topk=8) | Δ |
|--------|----------------|----------------|-----|
| Throughput | 204.6 tok/s | 209.6 tok/s | **+2.4%** |
| TPOT | 4.885 ms | 4.772 ms | **-2.4%** |
| `at::native::reduce_kernel` | 3.6% GPU time (6.11ms) | ~0% | **-3.6%** |
| Elementwise `MulFunctor` | ~1.8% GPU time | N/A (eliminated by fused path) | — |

**Profiling observations:**
- The `moe_sum` kernel now appears in the CUDA trace for topk=8 (previously absent)
- No PyTorch `at::sum_out` fallback observed for topk ≤ 8
- CUDA Graph capture/replay works correctly (kernels are deterministic)
- Memory access patterns show improved coalescing via `VLLM_LDG` hints

**Net impact:** ~3.5-5% GPU time savings on decode-heavy MoE workloads with topk > 4, matching the expected improvement from eliminating the PyTorch generic reduction fallback.

title: [Bugfix][DeepSeekV4 MTP] Pass prefix= to e_proj/h_proj in MTP draft
body:
## Summary

In `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/{nvidia,amd,xpu}/mtp.py`, the `DeepSeekV4MultiTokenPredictorLayer.__init__` creates `e_proj` and `h_proj` (both `ReplicatedLinear`) **without an explicit `prefix=`**. The resulting modules end up with `prefix=""`, and when `compressed_tensors` is the active quant_config, `get_scheme(layer_name="")` raises:

```
ValueError: Unable to find matching target for  in the compressed-tensors config.
```

(The blank module name in the error message is the empty prefix.)

Filed as [#44817](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44817). Related (closed): [#43893](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43893) — @yangsiqt2 proposed an alternative skip-path approach. This PR takes the smaller route — propagate the prefix the parent layer already receives — which is consistent with how the rest of the main DSV4 model passes `prefix=` throughout.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

- **#43893** (closed, by @yangsiqt2): proposed skipping `quant_config` when no MTP-specific quant tensors exist on disk. Reviewer feedback was to fix at the quantizer side. That artifact-side fix is necessary (we shipped it on the model repo) but is **insufficient on its own** — even with correct ignore patterns, an empty layer_name can't be matched. This PR is the complementary vLLM-side change.
- **#44817** (open): the issue this PR closes. No PR currently attached.
- A subsequent BF16-`wo_a` runtime fallback in `nvidia/ops/o_proj.py` (described by @dnhkng on a related HF discussion) is also needed for full end-to-end MTP serve on stock vLLM. That's a separate change (different file, different code path), not addressed here.

## Why this can't be fixed at the artifact

Any ignore regex that matches `""` would also match every other module in the model, including the routed experts that should remain quantized. There is no way to disambiguate from the metadata side; the model code has to pass a non-empty prefix.

## The fix — 6 lines, 3 files

```diff
         self.e_proj = ReplicatedLinear(
             config.hidden_size, config.hidden_size,
             bias=False, return_bias=False,
             quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.e_proj",
         )
         self.h_proj = ReplicatedLinear(
             config.hidden_size, config.hidden_size,
             bias=False, return_bias=False,
             quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.h_proj",
         )
```

Applied identically to `nvidia/mtp.py`, `amd/mtp.py`, and `xpu/mtp.py`.

## Tests run + results

Reproduced verbatim and patched on 2× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM 12.1a, ARM64/CUDA 13.2), TP=2, with the [`canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-W4A16-FP8-MTP`](https://huggingface.co/canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-W4A16-FP8-MTP/tree/fix-ignore-runtime-names) artifact (`fix-ignore-runtime-names` branch, an artifact-side companion fix for `shared_experts` / `attn.compressor` runtime-vs-on-disk name mismatch).

**Before this PR:**
```
ValueError: Unable to find matching target for  in the compressed-tensors config.
```

**After this PR:** module construction proceeds past `e_proj`/`h_proj` into the MTP block's `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer`. The remaining failure (a separate `wo_a` BF16 path issue at runtime, described in @dnhkng's [HF discussion #8](https://huggingface.co/canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-W4A16-FP8/discussions/8) — confirmed independently on GH200 TP=2) is out of scope for this PR and will follow up.

Existing non-MTP DSV4 W4A16+FP8 serve paths are unaffected — this change only adds a `prefix=` kwarg already accepted by the parent constructor; non-MTP serve doesn't construct `DeepSeekV4MultiTokenPredictorLayer` at all.

## AI-assistance disclosure

This PR was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter (@pasta-paul, Canada Quant Labs) verified the diagnosis end-to-end on hardware — including reproducing the exact `ValueError` on stock vLLM, applying the patched code, and confirming module construction progresses past the prior failure point. The fix is a 6-line mechanical change to propagate an already-received kwarg; the human submitter understands and defends the change.

## Affected artifacts

Any `DeepSeek-V4-*-MTP` checkpoint where the MTP draft tower is intended to be served via `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp",...}'` with a compressed-tensors quantized main model. Includes the canada-quant `W4A16-FP8-MTP`, `NVFP4-FP8-MTP`, and Pro variants.

## Credit

@yangsiqt2's analysis in #43893 is what first pinned the root cause; this PR is the more surgical version of that fix. @dnhkng's independent reproduction (HF link above) confirmed it.

title: [Bug]: Mistral Small 4 EAGLE drafter crashes at init — EagleMistralLarge3Model missing use_mha (skips DeepseekV2Model.__init__)
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Versions</summary>

- vLLM: `0.22.1rc1.dev259+g303916e93` (nightly wheel) — also reproduced on the vendor `mistralllm/vllm-ms4` image
- transformers: `5.10.0.dev0` (main)
- mistral_common: `1.11.3`
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120), single GPU, TP=1

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Serving **Mistral Small 4** (`mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-NVFP4`) with its official EAGLE draft head (`mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-eagle`, `method: "eagle"`) crashes `EngineCore` during `profile_run`. The target model loads fine and `SpeculativeConfig(method='eagle', ...)` is created; the crash is in the **drafter**.

The eagle head resolves to **`EagleMistralLarge3Model`**. Its `__init__` calls `nn.Module.__init__(self)` directly — it does **not** call `DeepseekV2Model.__init__` — and only sets a curated subset of attributes. But `EagleMistralLarge3Model.forward` calls `super().forward(...)` into `DeepseekV2Model.forward`, which reads attributes that the bypassed parent `__init__` would have set. Those attributes are therefore missing:

- `self.use_mha` — set in `DeepseekV2Model.__init__` (computed from `qk_nope_head_dim`/`qk_rope_head_dim`) and read in `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer.forward`. **Missing on current `main`.**
- `self.aux_hidden_state_layers` — was the same class of failure earlier; it has since been added to `EagleMistralLarge3Model.__init__` (`= ()`), but `use_mha` was not.

So this is a recurring incomplete-init problem: the eagle subclass manually re-implements a subset of `DeepseekV2Model.__init__` and drifts out of sync with what `DeepseekV2Model.forward` requires.

### Serve command

```bash
vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-NVFP4 \
  --quantization compressed-tensors --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --attention-backend TRITON_MLA --max-model-len 16384 \
  --tool-call-parser mistral --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mistral \
  --speculative_config '{"model":"mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-eagle","num_speculative_tokens":3,"method":"eagle","max_model_len":"16384"}'
```

### Traceback (abridged)

```
EngineCore ... profile_run -> _dummy_run -> self.drafter.dummy_run(...)
  File ".../models/mistral_large_3_eagle.py", line ~91, in forward
    output = super().forward(...)
  File ".../models/deepseek_v2.py", line ~1378, in forward   # DeepseekV2DecoderLayer
    if not self.use_mha:
AttributeError: 'EagleMistralLarge3Model' object has no attribute 'use_mha'
...
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed.
```

(On the older `mistralllm/vllm-ms4` snapshot the same path raised `AttributeError: 'EagleMistralLarge3Model' object has no attribute 'aux_hidden_state_layers'` instead.)

### Suggested fix

Have `EagleMistralLarge3Model.__init__` either call `DeepseekV2Model.__init__` (so all attributes its `forward` depends on are set), or explicitly set every attribute `DeepseekV2Model.forward` / `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer.forward` reads — `use_mha` is the one currently missing. An audit for any further such attributes would prevent the next whack-a-mole.

The target model itself (NVFP4 + `TRITON_MLA`) loads and serves correctly without the drafter; only the EAGLE path is affected.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Searched existing issues; this is a distinct `EagleMistralLarge3Model` init gap (not the NVFP4 `#40260` shape error, which did **not** reproduce on sm_120 here).

title: [Bugfix][DeepSeekV4] Add BF16 MTP O-proj fallback for unquantized draft weights
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a NVIDIA DeepSeek V4 O-projection fallback for MTP draft blocks whose `wo_a` projection is BF16/unquantized while the target model is FP8/compressed.

Some compressed-tensors DeepSeek V4 artifacts keep the MTP draft tower unquantized. After the draft layer constructs successfully, the current NVIDIA O-proj path assumes `wo_a.weight_scale_inv` exists and always enters the FP8 `fp8_einsum` path. For BF16 MTP draft weights, no FP8 scale tensor is present, so execution fails before generation.

The fix keeps the existing FP8 path when scale metadata exists, and adds a BF16 fallback when it does not:

- detect `weight_scale_inv` / `weight_scale`, returning `None` when neither exists;
- apply inverse RoPE in BF16 for the unquantized fallback path;
- reshape flat grouped `wo_a.weight` into grouped form when applicable;
- run grouped BF16 matmul and continue through `wo_b`.

## Relationship to existing work

This is not intended to duplicate the MTP `prefix=` construction fix in #44837 / #44817. That PR fixes an earlier failure where MTP `e_proj` / `h_proj` are constructed with an empty prefix and compressed-tensors cannot match them.

This PR handles the next failure point after construction succeeds: executing the BF16/unquantized MTP O-proj path on NVIDIA.

Related:

- #44837
- #44817
- #43893
- HF discussion with GH200 validation and Canada-Quant artifact context: https://huggingface.co/canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-W4A16-FP8/discussions/8

I searched for existing open work around `DeepSeekV4`, `MTP`, `o_proj`, `wo_a.weight_scale_inv`, and BF16 draft weights. I found the prefix/construction PR above, but not an existing PR for this O-proj execution fallback.

## Tests

```bash
/home/grace/vllm-build/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v4/test_nvidia_o_proj.py -q
# 6 passed, 16 warnings in 1.13s

uvx ruff check vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/o_proj.py tests/models/deepseek_v4/test_nvidia_o_proj.py
# All checks passed!

uvx ruff format --check vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/o_proj.py tests/models/deepseek_v4/test_nvidia_o_proj.py
# 2 files already formatted

git diff --check
# clean
```

## Hardware validation

Locally validated end-to-end on a dual GH200 system with TP=2 using the Canada-Quant `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-W4A16-FP8-MTP` artifact plus the needed artifact/prefix fixes. The BF16 fallback allowed MTP generation to run; best measured point in that setup was MTP3 at ~193 output tok/s versus ~106 output tok/s without MTP.

These benchmark numbers are included only as validation context; this PR is a compatibility bugfix, not a general performance claim.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to prepare this patch and PR text. The submitting human should review every changed line and validate the behavior before opening/merging, per `AGENTS.md`.

title: [Feature]: Streaming parser engine for tool/reasoning parsers
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Streaming parser engine for tool/reasoning parsers

### Problem

vLLM has dozens of model-specific streaming tool-call and reasoning parsers, each implementing its own incremental tokenization, state tracking, and argument buffering. That's thousands of lines of structurally similar but independently maintained streaming logic, which makes adding new model formats expensive and bugs hard to fix consistently.

Reasoning and tool-call parsing are also handled by separate parser instances stitched together at the serving layer - the reasoning parser runs first, then its leftover content is fed to the tool parser. Getting this handoff right is tricky, and the existing parsers handle it inconsistently across model formats. Many of the existing parsers also assume single-token deltas. They can produce incorrect results or degrade to O(n²) when deltas contain multiple tokens, as happens with speculative decoding, MTP, or `stream_interval > 1`.

### Solution

Replace the hand-rolled parsers with a declarative, state-machine-based engine where O(n) complexity, multi-token delta correctness, and unified reasoning+tool parsing are properties of the engine itself instead of things each parser has to implement correctly on its own.

The key properties every parser config gets for free from the engine:

- **O(n) streaming** - the engine processes each token/character exactly once. No per-parser state machine tuning required to avoid O(n²).
- **Chunk-size invariance** - correct output regardless of whether deltas arrive as single tokens or multi-token chunks (speculative decoding, MTP, `stream_interval > 1`). The engine's incremental lexer handles prefix buffering and boundary conditions in one place.
- **Token ID + text hybrid parsing** - models increasingly use special tokens to delineate sections (reasoning, tool calls) with text-based content inside. The engine matches on token IDs where available and falls back to text lexing, rather than forcing everything through text.
- **Unified reasoning and tool-call parsing** - a single state machine handles the full output format, eliminating the fragile two-pass split where reasoning and tool parsing run as separate stages.

The engine is a 4-layer pipeline:

```
TokenIDScanner → IncrementalLexer → StreamingParserEngine → ParserEngine
```

- **TokenIDScanner** - pre-lexes special token IDs before they hit the text lexer
- **IncrementalLexer** - converts text deltas into terminal tokens with prefix buffering
- **StreamingParserEngine** - drives the state machine, emits semantic events
- **ParserEngine** - integrates with vLLM's serving layer (DeltaMessage, tool calls, reasoning)

Each model format provides a config (state machine transitions + terminal definitions) and, for non-JSON tool formats, an argument converter. Models that use JSON tool arguments (e.g. Qwen3) need only the config; models with custom formats (e.g. Gemma4's `<|"|>`-delimited args, DeepSeek V4's DSML attributes) also supply a converter function.

### Alternatives

One alternative considered was not consolidating into an engine - just fixing each parser independently. That's our current status quo, but it's leading to overwhelming numbers of issues, PRs, and user frustration as they try to use agentic workflows with advanced reasoning and tool call models alongside spec decoding or multi-token prediction to get faster inference throughput. The growing backlog of PRs with varying approaches to address these problems is evidence this doesn't scale.

Another alternative considered was using more formal grammar and/or parsing libraries. But, the challenging parts are the streaming complexity. Formal grammar tools don't natively support streaming parsing (with prefix buffering, partial delimiters across streaming deltas, etc) or mixed token id + text parsing. The actual grammars we're parsing are relatively simple - the challenge is in getting all the streaming mechanics right in a low latency and performant way.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Spec Decode] Adaptive verifier step-length for DFlash/PARD (D-Cut-style)
body:
## Purpose

Add **adaptive verifier step-length** for parallel speculative decoding (DFlash, PARD / `draft_model` + `parallel_drafting`). The drafter still proposes the full `num_speculative_tokens` every step, but the verifier dynamically shortens the next step's `query_len` based on drafter softmax probabilities and a profiled ITL cost table.

### Motivation

- [PR #32374](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32374) shows that at high concurrency, truncated verifier shapes are more likely to run under PCG than FCG. The PCG–FCG latency gap at high batch sizes can be outweighed by the end-to-end gain from adaptive step-length pruning (less verify work on positions likely to be rejected).
- Core algorithm follows [D-Cut: Adaptive Verification Depth Pruning for Speculative Decoding](https://angelslim.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/dcut.html): hardware-profiled cost table + draft-confidence prefix-product scores + batch-wide global top-K allocation to maximize `expected_accepted_tokens / verifier_ITL`.

### Runtime flow

```text
Step N
  execute_model start
    → read cached draft_len[req] from step N-1
    → truncate scheduled_spec_decode_tokens
      (draft_len=0 removes the spec entry for that request)
  verifier forward (truncated query lengths)
  propose_draft_token_ids
    → drafter still drafts full num_speculative_tokens
    → selected_probs[B, T] (softmax prob of each sampled draft token)
  sample_tokens (after _bookkeeping_sync)
    → choose_query_lens_discrete → cache draft_len[req] for step N+1

Step N+1
  execute_model start applies the cached draft_len …
```

`probs(N)` only affects `verifier(N+1)` (strict one-step lag).

### Core algorithm (D-Cut-style)

Verifier cost is profiled as `cost = ITL(batch_size, sum_query_len)`, where
`sum_query_len = B + Σ_i draft_lens[i]` (each sequence always contributes one
anchor token).

Per decode step, for active (post-prefill) sequences:

- **Input**: `probs[i][t]` — accept-probability proxy (softmax at the sampled
  draft token); `B` — full batch size; candidate `Q` — profiled `sum_query_len`
  keys for `bs_key` (ceil of `B` on the batch axis).
- **Marginal gain**: `m[i,t] = p[i,1] * … * p[i,t]`. Within each sequence `m`
  is non-increasing, so a global top-`S` pick satisfies the prefix constraint.
- **Score each candidate Q**: `S = Q - B`, `score = (B + sum(top-S gains)) / cost_table[(bs_key, Q)]`.
- **Output**: pick best `Q`, map top-`best_S` marginals to per-request
  `draft_len[i]`, cache for next-step truncation. Drafter still drafts full
  `num_speculative_tokens`; only verifier `query_len[i] = 1 + draft_len[i]` is
  adapted (0 to `num_speculative_tokens`).

### Implementation notes

- Probs transfer and CPU-side decision still add overhead; we avoid an extra
  blocking GPU sync on the critical path by piggybacking the D2H copy on the
  existing default-stream sync in `RejectionSampler.parse_output`.
- TP-safe: broadcast rank-0 `cost_table` after warmup profiling to avoid
  divergent `draft_lens`.

### Performance bottlenecks and outlook

**1. Low-concurrency overhead (~10%)**

At concurrency 1, enabling adaptive verify still shows a measurable throughput
drop vs static full-step verify (observed ~370 vs ~410 tok/s in internal runs;
exact numbers depend on model / GPU). The main suspected bottleneck is
`selected_probs` GPU→CPU transfer and the CPU-side marginal-gain decision — not
the extra softmax in the drafter itself (`needs_draft_probs` alone without the
controller is much cheaper).

Current mitigation (not zero-cost):
- Queue a **non-blocking** D2H copy of `selected_probs` to **pinned CPU memory**
  on the default CUDA stream in `_copy_draft_token_ids_to_cpu`.
- **Piggyback** on the existing default-stream sync in
  `RejectionSampler.parse_output` (inside `_bookkeeping_sync`), so we do not add
  a separate blocking `.cpu()` on the hot path.
- Run `choose_query_lens_discrete` at the end of `sample_tokens`, after
  bookkeeping, when the GPU is otherwise idle.

This removes the worst-case standalone D2H stall, but residual cost remains:
extra drafter logit/prob work, pinned-memory copy bandwidth, and NumPy decision
latency. **~10% low-concurrency regression is still expected today** and should
be called out in benchmarks.

**2. Complementary control with [PR #32374](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32374)**

This PR and PR #32374 target different levers and are intended to compose:

| | PR #32374 | This PR (adaptive verify) |
|---|---|---|
| When | **Prior** — at / around draft time | **Posterior** — after draft, before next verify |
| Signal | Draft-side scheduling / shape control | Draft confidence (`selected_probs`) |
| Effect | Better draft–verify shape alignment (e.g. PCG-friendly buckets) | Shorter verifier `query_len` on low-confidence tails |

Together: PR #32374 improves the drafting / graph-shape side; this PR prunes
verify depth from measured draft quality. At high concurrency the verify savings
can dominate; at low concurrency the combined story is still being evaluated.

**3. Async scheduling**

This change is developed and validated primarily on the **synchronous** DFlash
path (`use_gpu_toks`, drafter before `_bookkeeping_sync`). Async scheduling
(`async_scheduling=True`) uses a different draft / bookkeeping ordering and may
skip or defer `_copy_draft_token_ids_to_cpu`; the adaptive hooks are not yet
fully adapted to that pipeline. Follow-up work: relocate prob capture / consume
to the async-specific draft sync points without breaking the one-step-lag
correctness guarantee (`probs(N)` → `verifier(N+1)`).


## Changes

### New modules

| File | Summary |
|------|---------|
| `vllm/v1/spec_decode/verify_adaptive_config.py` | JSON-backed config dataclass: profiling grid (batch / query_len axes), `warmup_seq_lens`, measurement iters, validation. |
| `vllm/v1/spec_decode/verify_adaptive_controller.py` | Core controller: `profile_cost_table`, NumPy `choose_query_lens_discrete`, per-request `draft_lens` cache, TP broadcast of cost table. |
| `vllm/v1/spec_decode/verify_adaptive.md` | Feature doc: enablement, runtime flow, cost model, code map. |

### Config & CLI

| File | Summary |
|------|---------|
| `vllm/config/speculative.py` | Add `speculative_adaptive_verify_config` field and `supports_adaptive_verify()` (DFlash or parallel `draft_model` only). |
| `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py` | Add `--speculative-adaptive-verify-config` CLI flag and speculative-config JSON key wiring. |

### Drafter: draft-token probability collection

| File | Summary |
|------|---------|
| `vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py` | Add `needs_draft_probs`, `_last_selected_probs`, `take_last_selected_probs()`, `_gather_selected_probs()` (logsumexp, no full-vocab softmax). Extend `_sample_draft_tokens` to return `selected_probs` for parallel and serial draft paths. |

### Runner integration

| File | Summary |
|------|---------|
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` | Init controller + pinned CPU buffer; truncate `scheduled_spec_decode_tokens` at `execute_model` start; non-blocking D2H in `_copy_draft_token_ids_to_cpu` (residual CPU/numpy cost remains); consume probs in `sample_tokens` after `_bookkeeping_sync`; `invalidate` on request finish; `_adaptive_profile_run` + `profile_adaptive_cost`. |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py` | Call `profile_adaptive_cost()` at end of `compile_or_warm_up_model` (after CUDA-graph / JIT warmup). |

## Test Plan

- [x] **Qwen3-8B, 2× RTX 4090, TP=2**: compare AR baseline vs DFlash/PARD static
  (full verify) vs dynamic (adaptive verify) at concurrency 4 / 16 / 32 / 48.
- [x] Enable adaptive verify on DFlash and confirm `adaptive:` debug logs appear
  after warmup.
- [x] TP=2 sustained load: no NCCL / RPC timeout observed.
- [x ] Verify correctness lag: step-N `selected_probs` only changes step-(N+1)
  verifier length (inspect per-step `draft_lens` logs).

Example serve command (DFlash + adaptive verify):

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --spec-method dflash \
  --spec-model <dflash_draft_model> \
  --spec-tokens 15 \
  --speculative-adaptive-verify-config /path/to/verify_adaptive_config.json
```

## Test Result

**Setup**: Qwen3-8B, 2× RTX 4090, TP=2, `output_throughput` (tok/s).

| Concurrency | 4 | 16 | 32 | 48 |
|-------------|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **DFlash — AR baseline** | 331.68 | 967.21 | 1794.32 | 1612.29 |
| **DFlash — static** (full verify) | 1057.60 | 1896.82 | 2347.33 | 2451.30 |
| **DFlash — dynamic** (adaptive verify) | 926.87 | 2141.59 | 2784.74 | 2638.20 |

| Concurrency | 4 | 16 | 32 | 48 |
|-------------|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **PARD — AR baseline** | 335.68 | 883.11 | 1479.43 | 1703.14 |
| **PARD — static** (full verify) | 891.91 | 1589.51 | 2001.02 | 2197.50 |
| **PARD — dynamic** (adaptive verify) | 643.67 | 1454.21 | 2517.18 | 2715.72 |

**Observations**

- **Low concurrency (bs=4)**: dynamic is below static for both DFlash (−12%) and
  PARD (−28%), consistent with the residual probs D2H / CPU-decision overhead
  discussed above.
- **Mid–high concurrency (bs≥16)**: dynamic overtakes static; largest gain at
  bs=32 (DFlash +19%, PARD +26% vs static). At bs=48, dynamic still leads static
  on both methods.
- **vs AR baseline** (DFlash): at bs=32 dynamic **1.55×** / static **1.31×**; at
  bs=48 dynamic **1.64×** / static **1.52×**. Adaptive verify extends the
  high-concurrency advantage of parallel speculative decoding.

title: perf: add push-based allreduce for small tensor reductions
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a push-based 2-buffer allreduce protocol to vLLM, targeting small-message reductions during decode (e.g., the per-layer attention and MoE allreduces in DeepSeek-V4 models). The existing barrier-based `CustomAllreduce` uses two explicit cross-GPU NVLink barrier round-trips per call, which dominate latency for small tensors. The push protocol eliminates these barriers entirely by having each rank push its data to all remote GPUs via NVLink volatile stores and then polling locally for arrival using a positive-zero sentinel mechanism with double-buffered epoch alternation.

The new `PushAllReduce` communicator is inserted into the `CudaCommunicator` dispatch chain above the existing `CustomAllreduce` for messages below a dynamic size threshold (~720 KB at TP=8 on B200). Messages above this threshold continue to use the barrier-based path. No existing `CustomAllreduce` code is modified. The implementation includes a consolidated CUDA kernel header vendored from SGLang's proven push kernel with minimal macro substitutions (namespace, C++17 compatibility, AOT compilation guards), a C++ host-side manager class following vLLM patterns, torch custom op bindings, and a Python communicator wrapper with CUDA graph support.

The kernel uses all available SMs (vs 2 CTAs in the barrier-based approach), supports PDL (`griddepcontrol`) overlap on sm_90+ architectures, and avoids the `cudaMemcpy` to IPC staging buffer required by the barrier-based path in eager mode. CUDA graph safety is ensured by placing the epoch counter in device memory (read live during replay) with a fixed grid size equal to the SM count.

## Performance Results

| Configuration | Metric | Baseline | Patched | Delta | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro (8xB200, TP=8) | Throughput (tok/s) | 82.301 | 84.060 | +1.759 | **+2.14%** |
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro (8xB200, TP=8) | TPOT (ms/tok) | 12.152 | 11.897 | -0.255 | **-2.09%** |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (2xB200, TP=2) | Throughput (tok/s) | 127.035 | 130.905 | +3.870 | **+3.05%** |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (2xB200, TP=2) | TPOT (ms/tok) | 7.873 | 7.640 | -0.233 | **-2.96%** |

Workload: decode, BS=1, ISL=4, OSL=33024, KV cache FP8. Baseline = same patched code with push allreduce disabled via env var (falls back to barrier-based `CustomAllreduce`).

Per-call improvement on V4-Pro (122 allreduce calls per forward pass across 61 layers): ~2.09 us/call.

## Correctness (lm_eval)

| Configuration | Metric | Baseline | Patched | Delta | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro (8xB200, TP=8) | flexible-extract exact_match | 0.9515 | 0.9530 | +0.0015 | PASS |
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro (8xB200, TP=8) | strict-match exact_match | 0.9515 | 0.9538 | +0.0023 | PASS |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (2xB200, TP=2) | flexible-extract exact_match | 0.9598 | 0.9530 | -0.0068 | PASS |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (2xB200, TP=2) | strict-match exact_match | 0.9606 | 0.9530 | -0.0076 | PASS |

Benchmark: gsm8k 5-shot (1319 prompts). All deltas are within 1 standard error (~0.006) and statistically indistinguishable (z-scores < 1.96). The sign reversal between configurations confirms random variance, not a systematic shift.

## Feature Toggle

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Environment variable | `VLLM_DISABLE_PUSH_ALLREDUCE` |
| Disable command | `VLLM_DISABLE_PUSH_ALLREDUCE=1` |
| Startup log (enabled) | `AllReduce push-based 2-buffer protocol is ENABLED` |
| Startup log (disabled) | `AllReduce push-based 2-buffer protocol is DISABLED (env override)` |

When disabled, `PushAllReduce.__init__` returns immediately without allocating any GPU resources. `should_use()` returns `False` for all inputs, and `CudaCommunicator` falls through to the barrier-based `CustomAllreduce`.

## Test Coverage

24 tests included in the patch, all passing on 2x NVIDIA B200:

- **Unit tests (16):** build verification, initialization/IPC exchange, `should_use()` predicate logic, bit-exact integer correctness vs NCCL, float correctness, positive-zero sentinel handling, 1000-call epoch alternation, thread count selection, threshold boundary, out-of-place semantics, dtype coverage (fp16/bf16/fp32), multi-layer simulation (122 ARs x 3 steps), lifecycle/cleanup, warmup path, asymmetric rank data, identical-values edge case
- **Integration tests (3):** dispatch priority routing (small->push, large->fallback), coexistence with existing allreduce backends, interleaved push AR + NCCL operations
- **CUDA graph test (1):** graph capture + 10 replays with varying data, epoch counter correctness
- **E2E test (1):** transformer block simulation (61 blocks x 2 ARs x 2 decode steps)
- **Feature toggle tests (3):** enabled default, disabled via env var, non-"1" values do not disable

title: [ROCm][gpt-oss] Pass GateMode.INTERLEAVE for MXFP4 W4A16 fused MoE
body:
## Summary

Fixes gpt-oss-120b accuracy=0 on AITER ≥0.1.14 and the gpt-oss-20b-w-mxfp4-a-bf16 CK2stages JIT crash: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/3586

`oracle/mxfp4.py` shuffles MXFP4 W4A16 weights with `shuffle_weight_a16w4` (interleaved gate/up), but the call into `aiter.fused_moe` was using the default `GateMode.SEPARATED`.

Before [ROCm/aiter#3123](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/3123) the aiter dispatcher tolerated this; #3123 added gate-mode-sensitive dispatch branches that now either silently corrupt outputs or fall through to CK2stages which has no SwiGLU+MXFP4 kernel and crashes.

This PR mirrors the fix in [sgl-project/sglang#25580](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25580)) i.e. pass `GateMode.INTERLEAVE` for MXFP4 W4A16 so the dispatcher takes the matching path.

## Impact on other paths (verified non-affected)

- gpt-oss W4A8 (`amd/gpt-oss120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8`) goes through `aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe.py`, not touched by this PR (but please see [#44804](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44804)).
- Other W4A4/W8A8 MoE's e.g. DSR1, DSV4 going through `rocm_aiter_ops.fused_moe`: Unaffected, only `use_mxfp4_w4a16 == True` flips to `INTERLEAVE`.

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950), `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, gsm8k flex-extract (n=200, fewshot=5):

| vLLM | aiter | TP | unpatched | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| vllm@main + PR base | aiter@main `6aeba41` | 1 | **0.000** ❌ | **0.905** ✓ |
| vllm@main + PR base | aiter@main `6aeba41` | 8 | **0.000** ❌ | **0.905** ✓ |
| vllm-rocm:nightly | aiter 0.1.13.post1 | 1 | n/a | **0.910** ✓ (backward-compat: kwarg silently dropped) |
| vllm-rocm:v0.22.0 | aiter@main `6aeba41` | 1 | n/a | **0.895** ✓ |

Quark `amd/gpt-oss-20b-w-mxfp4-a-bf16` TP=2 enforce-eager: previously
crashed in CK2stages JIT; with this PR serves at 79 tok/s.

Throughput (W4A16, MI355X, 1k/1k random, ignore_eos), vllm@main + PR + aiter@main:

| TP | mc=1 | mc=8 | mc=32 | mc=64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 240 | 1334 | 3498 | 5454 |
| 8 | 272 | 2033 | 6991 | 12238 |

## AI-assistance disclosure

AI-assisted (Claude Sonnet 4.6 via Claude Code). I have read every
changed line, run the validation matrix above, and am responsible for
the change end-to-end.

title: [Mooncake] Auto-discover compatible RDMA devices for Mooncake Connector
body:
## Purpose
The PR supports auto-discovery for compatible and mutually routable RDMA devices for use by the Mooncake connectors (e.g., `MooncakeConnector`, `MooncakeStoreConnector`) when no device names are specified. The existing device selection in mooncake can use all devices in `/sys/class/infiniband` as candidates, which can lead to errors:
- devices that have `node_type=7: unspecified` and `link_layer=Unknown` are not usable
- devices with limited membership (`pkey0=0x7fff`) can cause transfer failure, despite successful startup.
- some devices are not mutually routable - leading to certain transfer to succeed while others fail

Example (B300, 16 RNICs):

title: [EPLB] Reject NCCL-based EPLB communicators with async EPLB
body:
NCCL is fundamentally incompatible with async EPLB due to multi-stream conflicts (see pytorch/pytorch#174288). Previously, the auto-selection logic avoided torch_nccl for async EPLB, but users could still explicitly set communicator="torch_nccl" or communicator="pynccl" and hit hangs. This PR adds explicit validation to catch these invalid combinations early


The DeepEP low-latency + async EPLB case that previously needed the NCCL_MAX_CTAS workaround in `eplb_utils.py` can no longer occur because NCCL-based communicators are now rejected at config validation when async EPLB is enabled. The workaround is simplified to only cover the DeepGEMM Mega MoE case.
