title: [Kernel] Resurrect rotted gather-cache OOB test + defensive block-table bound-checks
body:
## Purpose

Restore a dead regression test and add two defensive bound-checks in the CP gather cache kernels (`csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu`).

1. **Resurrect a dead regression test (the substantive fix).** `tests/kernels/test_cache_kernels.py::test_gather_cache_oob` (the #27909 sanitizer-mode regression test) still called the op without the since-added `token_to_seq` argument and **fails with a binding error on current `main`** (`Expected a value of type 'Tensor' for argument 'token_to_seq' but instead found type 'int'`). The only sanitizer-mode coverage for this kernel family has been dead since the signature changed; updated to the current signature.

2. **Defensive bound-checks for two malformed-index paths (#45380, #45377).** Both kernels index `block_table[...]` with a computed offset that isn't range-checked:
   - `gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache`: `block_table_id` can exceed the table width if `seq_starts` pushes a token past the block table's coverage (#45380). The kernel now receives `block_table.size(1)` and `continue`s past out-of-range indices.
   - `cp_gather_and_upconvert_fp8_kv_cache`: the ownership binary search floors `req_id` at 0, so a nonzero `workspace_starts[0]` would drive `token_offset` negative and underflow the read (#45377). Early-return on a negative offset (warp-uniform).

   **Reachability (honest):** I could not establish that either input occurs in production. For **#45377** I traced the callers — `flashmla_sparse.py` builds `workspace_starts` as `zeros()` then `cumsum()` into `[1:]`, with the per-chunk adjustment zeroing each chunk slice's first entry, so `workspace_starts[0] == 0` always and `token_offset >= 0` by construction. For **#45380** the chunked-context caller (`mla_attention.py`) sizes the block table to the full sequence, so a well-formed config keeps `block_table_id` in range. The sanitizer evidence below is from feeding the issues' constructed inputs directly. So these are defensive guards against malformed indices into `block_table`, not fixes for demonstrated production failures — happy to drop either if you'd prefer not to guard a currently-unreachable path.

## Test Plan / Result

- `tests/kernels/test_cache_kernels.py` — `2 passed` (previously `1 failed` on `main` from the signature rot). Against the prebuilt binary these exercise the op bindings; CI's source build + sanitizer covers the guards.
- Standalone compute-sanitizer (`--tool memcheck`, sm_120, CUDA 13.0) on a replica of the kernels' indexing logic (payload simplified to plain copies; the indexing under test preserved verbatim), fed the issues' constructed trigger inputs:

| build | constructed trigger inputs | valid inputs |
|---|---|---|
| pre-fix logic | 4161 invalid global reads | 0 errors |
| with guards | 0 errors | 0 errors |

The guards are pure bound checks, so behavior on well-formed input is unchanged.

## Duplicate check

No open PR addresses either issue: searched `45380`, `45377`, `gather_and_maybe_dequant`, `cp_gather_and_upconvert`; both issues have zero comments; reporter has no authored PRs; file history on `main` shows no fix since the libtorch_stable migration. Related but distinct: #45384 fixes an int32 overflow in `concat_mla_q` in the same file (different function; no textual overlap).

## AI assistance disclosure

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude); reviewed, compiled, and sanitizer-validated by the submitter.

title: [Frontend] Add Streaming Parser Engine and new Qwen3 Parser
body:
## Purpose

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44873

Introduce a declarative, config-driven streaming parser engine that replaces hand-rolled per-model streaming logic with a shared state machine. The engine handles reasoning/content/tool-call transitions, incremental JSON argument extraction, and detokenizer hold-back recovery through a single ParserEngineConfig.
    
This wires up Qwen3 as the first model, with engine adapters registered alongside existing parsers for side-by-side coexistence. Includes comprehensive replay tests, token-ID scanner tests, and DelegatingParser integration tests.

~~This PR does not remove the old reasoning / tool call parser files because I haven't yet audited all semi-common parsers in the wild for models that ship their own parser plugins to ensure nothing depends on these.~~

[Edit: After discussion with some other maintainers, removing the old Qwen 3 reasoning/tool call parsers as part of this PR to clean up legacy and confuse contributors/maintainers less when applying fixes. A search of HuggingFace and GitHub didn't show any popular external models or projects that depending on those.]

I have additional parser implementations for Nemotron v3, Gemma 4, and DeepSeek v4 that have been in testing and should be close to ready, pending some final rebasing after this merges with any reviewer feedback / changes to the engine itself.

The primary goal of this rewrite was to unify the hard parsing logic around the boundary transition, handle large multi-token deltas (speculative decoding, diffusion models), and unify logic between non-streaming and streaming paths within the parsers so that we don't have drift between the two.

AI assistance was used, especially to help with continual rebasing to latest main the last few weeks while I tested and refined this.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

This runs the existing Qwen3 reasoning and tool parser tests plus lots of new ones for the parser engine.

```
pytest \
  tests/parser/engine/ \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_qwen3coder_tool_parser.py \
  tests/reasoning/test_qwen3_reasoning_parser.py
```

### Integration tests

These are existing integration tests that touch qwen3 models.

```
pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_completion_with_function_calling.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_thinking_token_budget.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_simple.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_parsable_context.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/test_return_tokens_as_ids.py
```

### Manual testing

Running vLLM with various stream interval settings and pointing Codex CLI Claude Code, OpenCode, etc at it to do PR reviews and similar. The large stream intervals consistently broke the agentic loops before with failed tool parses, reasoning leaks, etc.

Tested on 2xH100 with the command below.

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --stream-interval 251
```

## Test Result

### Unit tests

```
505 passed, 2 warnings
```

### integration tests

```
65 passed, 3 skipped, 16 warnings
```

### Manual testing

Repeated agentic loops where the harnesses spin out subagents, execute dozens of tool calls, and long context scenarios. These are more of a "vibe" check, where everything seems to work.

title: [Bug]: Silent output corruption: MTP + DCP + FULL_AND_PIECEWISE cudagraphs when the attention backend lacks varlen-decode support under DCP
body:
## Your current environment

4×H200 NVL (SM90), vLLM v0.22.1 (also reproduced with the sparse-MLA DCP
patch ported onto current main), CUDA 12.x, GLM-5.1-NVFP4
(`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, sparse MLA, `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache).

## 🐛 Describe the bug

When all three of the following are combined:

- speculative decoding (MTP, `{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}`),
- decode context parallelism (`--decode-context-parallel-size 4`),
- the **default** cudagraph mode (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`),

the model **silently produces corrupted output**: generations truncate
after 1–2 characters or degenerate into repetition loops. There are no
errors or warnings in the logs — the server looks perfectly healthy.

Any one of the following makes the same setup fully correct:

- `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "PIECEWISE"}'` (correct, but
  roughly halves single-stream decode throughput vs full graphs),
- `--enforce-eager` (correct, much slower),
- disabling MTP (DCP without MTP is correct **with** full graphs),
- disabling DCP (MTP without DCP is correct with full graphs).

## Mechanism (analysis)

Under DCP, `AttentionMetadataBuilder._init_reorder_batch_threshold` forces
`reorder_batch_threshold` back to 1 for backends that do not declare
`supports_dcp_with_varlen` (vllm/v1/attention/backend.py). With MTP
enabled, spec-decode verify rows have q_len = 2, so after the forcing they
are classified as **prefills** at metadata-build time. The full-cudagraph
decode capture, however, is built around the assumption that uniform
spec-decode batches go down the decode path. The result is a mismatch
between captured and replayed work for the verify rows — and silent
garbage instead of a crash.

The dangerous part is the failure mode: an unsupported combination
degrades to *silent corruption* rather than an init-time error or an
automatic downgrade of the cudagraph mode. A user enabling MTP + DCP on
such a backend with default settings gets a healthy-looking server that
emits broken text.

Related precedent: #39635 fixed a same-shaped MTP×DCP problem for the
FlashInfer MLA decode path on SM120.

## Reproduction

```bash
vllm serve <DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.x class model> \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 4 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --enable-expert-parallel
# (sparse MLA under DCP needs the patch from #45426; the corruption
# itself is reproducible on any backend that reaches this combination
# without supports_dcp_with_varlen)
```

Then any short chat completion (`temperature 0`, e.g. "Capital of
Australia?") returns a truncated or looping answer; the same request with
`cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` or `--enforce-eager` is correct.

## Suggested resolution

Either (a) reject or downgrade at init: if `dcp_world_size > 1`, the
effective `reorder_batch_threshold` was forced to 1, spec-decode is
enabled and the cudagraph mode has full decode capture — fall back to
PIECEWISE with a warning (mirroring other cudagraph fallbacks), or
(b) teach the affected backends varlen decode under DCP
(`supports_dcp_with_varlen=True` + per-token local lengths) so the
combination is genuinely supported. #45426 does (b) for the FlashMLA
sparse backend; (a) would still protect every other backend from the
silent-corruption failure mode.

title: [Attention][MLA] FlashMLA sparse: enable DCP on the fp8 mixed-batch path and MTP with full cudagraphs
body:
## Purpose

Enable `--decode-context-parallel-size > 1` for sparse MLA models
(DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.x class, e.g. `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) with the
`fp8_ds_mla` KV cache on the mixed-batch fp8 path.

Today the FlashMLA sparse backend cannot run under DCP at all: the impl
never returns the softmax LSE, so the cross-rank merge has nothing to work
with, the indexer builds its metadata from global sequence lengths (while
each DCP rank only owns an interleaved shard of the KV cache), and the MLA
layer hard-asserts `not fp8_attention` under DCP. For long-context
multi-user serving this leaves sparse-MLA deployments stuck with the
TP-only KV pool.

This PR closes those gaps:

- **flashmla_sparse**: set `can_return_lse_for_decode = True` and plumb the
  softmax LSE from `flash_mla_with_kvcache` through
  `_forward_fp8_kv_mixed_batch` for **all** tokens. The kernel returns LSE
  in `(B, H, S)` layout (heads before seq) and in base *e* — matching the
  FlashMLA decode API contract (`softmax_lse: (batch_size, num_heads_q,
  seq_len_q)`), and additionally verified on H200 against a bf16 reference
  (matches after transpose to the `(tokens, heads)` layout the cp merge
  expects, max diff ~1e-4). Rows
  where a rank owns none of the selected tokens (all converted top-k
  indices are −1 — routine for the first tokens of a request under DCP) are
  neutralized to the LSE-merge identity `(out=0, lse=−inf)`. LSE is sliced
  together with the output on head padding. Unsupported combinations (bf16
  KV cache, the separate prefill/decode fp8 path, head envelopes that
  change after the DCP gather) raise `NotImplementedError` at init instead
  of corrupting output at runtime.
- **mla_attention**: relax the `assert not fp8_attention` in the DCP branch
  for sparse impls. Their q stays a bf16 `(nope, pe)` tuple
  (`supports_quant_query_input` is `False`), so the cat + all-gather over
  the head dim remains valid; dense fp8 paths stay unsupported.
- **indexer**: build decode metadata from this rank's
  `dcp_local_seq_lens` (mirroring the dense MLA builder), and make the
  prefill metadata kernel compute per-token causal bounds with the
  interleaved-ownership formula equivalent to `get_dcp_local_seq_lens`
  (`local_ctx(p)` = number of global positions ≤ p owned by this rank).
  Gather sizes and CPU bounds come from local lengths. Everything is an
  identity when `dcp_world_size == 1`.

### Relation to PR #34429

#34429 attempted the same feature on the separate prefill/decode path and
was closed unmerged. This PR differs in: (1) LSE is returned for every
token (the merge needs all tokens, not only decode rows); (2) the kernel's
LSE layout is handled as `(B, H, S)` per the FlashMLA API; (3) the LSE is
sliced together with the output when query heads are padded for the fp8
decode kernel (h_q 64/128).

### Top-k semantics under DCP (explicit design point)

Each rank selects top-`index_topk` (2048) tokens from **its own KV shard**;
the LSE merge then combines the partial attentions. The effective attention
support is the union of per-rank top-k — a superset of the global top-2048
(up to `dcp_world_size × 2048` tokens). Current behavior: each rank
selects top-k independently (no cross-rank index exchange; the support is
a superset that always contains the global top-k). The alternative — a
cross-rank exchange to reproduce the exact global top-2048 — costs an
extra collective on the hot path. Quality of the union semantics is
validated empirically below; open to guidance on whether this should be
the default, sit behind a flag, or move to the exchange-based scheme.
Note it only engages when DCP is explicitly requested for a sparse model,
which does not work upstream at all today.

### Spec-decode (MTP) under DCP with full cudagraphs (3rd commit)

Without varlen support, DCP forces `reorder_batch_threshold` back to 1,
so MTP verify rows (q_len=2) are classified as prefills — which breaks
the full-cudagraph decode capture and silently corrupts output
(issue #45425; users had to fall back to `PIECEWISE` at roughly
half the single-stream decode throughput). The third commit makes the
sparse stack handle multi-token decode rows under DCP:

- the sparse builder declares `supports_dcp_with_varlen` (gated on
  `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size == 1`, mirroring FlashAttn MLA); its fp8
  mixed-batch kernel metadata is shape-only, so no attention-side change
  is needed;
- the indexer keeps feeding its decode expansion global lengths, then
  reduces the resulting **per-token** global causal bounds to this rank's
  local counts with the interleaved-ownership map (equivalent to
  `get_dcp_local_seq_lens`). The map must run per token after the
  expansion: ownership of consecutive positions alternates between ranks,
  so `localize(L) - k != localize(L - k)`. Elementwise ops in-place into
  the persistent decode buffers — CUDA-graph safe, no device syncs.

### Known limitations (honest scope)

- Only the **mixed-batch fp8 path** (`num_heads < 32` per rank with
  `fp8_ds_mla`); the separate prefill/decode and bf16 paths raise
  `NotImplementedError` under DCP. Extending them needs hardware
  validation — proposed as follow-up.
- `compress_ratio == 1` only (not DeepSeek-V4 indexer compression — that
  territory belongs to #44573; the indexer asserts at build time).
- The silent-corruption failure mode of MTP×DCP×full-graphs for backends
  **without** varlen support remains reachable for other backends —
  issue #45425 proposes an init-time downgrade/reject as a
  generic guard (cf. the related FlashInfer fix #39635).
- Validated with the default `ag_rs` DCP comm backend
  (`cp_lse_ag_out_rs`); `--dcp-comm-backend a2a` is rejected at init
  with `NotImplementedError` until validated.

## Test Plan

Hardware: 4×H200 NVL (SM90), GLM-5.1-NVFP4 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`,
16 q-heads per rank at TP=4), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`.

Server (DCP config; baseline drops `--decode-context-parallel-size`):

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.1-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --max-model-len 202752 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill
```

- `lm_eval` (gsm8k, num_fewshot=5, local-completions) on DCP=4 vs TP-only
  stock on the same nightly base.
- Determinism/quality probes: 10 temp-0 prompts; needle-in-haystack at
  ~164K tokens (5 facts); 40K/120K-token prefill smoke with 4 concurrent
  mixed-length requests.
- A 16-task agentic coding eval (pass@3) against the TP-only baseline.
- Kernel-level GPU probes for the empirical claims: LSE layout/base,
  behavior of the kernel on all-(−1) index rows, and top-k kernels on
  zero-length local context (do not touch the −1 fill).

## Test Result

### lm_eval gsm8k (num_fewshot=5)

| Config | gsm8k strict-match | flexible-extract |
|---|---|---|
| TP=4 (stock nightly, dcp=1) | 0.9469 ± 0.0062 | 0.9424 ± 0.0064 |
| TP=4 / DCP=4, no MTP (this PR) | 0.9447 ± 0.0063 | 0.9447 ± 0.0063 |
| TP=4 / DCP=4 + MTP, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE (this PR) | 0.9401 ± 0.0065 | 0.9401 ± 0.0065 |

### MTP × DCP × full cudagraphs (3rd commit)

| Config | decode 1 seq (tok/s) | correctness |
|---|---|---|
| DCP=4 + MTP, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, before | — | silent corruption |
| DCP=4 + MTP, PIECEWISE (workaround) | 54.0 | correct |
| DCP=4 + MTP, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, after | 81.3 (median of 3) | correct: gsm8k above, needle 164K 5/5, temp-0 probes clean |

### Capacity / performance (validated on v0.22.1 + this diff, same hardware)

| Config | KV pool (tokens) | decode 1 seq (tok/s) | 4×512 aggregate | 40K cold prefill (tok/s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP=4 baseline | 217,664 | 98.2 (with MTP) | 278.9 | 4,412 |
| TP=4 / DCP=4 (no MTP) | **1,053,184** (×4.8) | 47.9 | 156.4 | **9,164** |

DCP overhead itself is ≈0 (47.9 tok/s with DCP vs 47.3 without, both no
MTP). On the current-main validation build the pool scales with
`--gpu-memory-utilization`: 591,872 tokens @0.92 → 977,664 @0.96
(TP4/DCP4 + MTP), 1,443,840 @0.96 without MTP.

- Needle 164K: 5/5 on every config (stock, DCP, DCP+MTP+full graphs).
- 16-task coding eval (pass@3): 16/16 on the final DCP=4 + MTP +
  full-cudagraphs build; the earlier DCP run and the TP-only baseline
  both scored 15/16 with the same single failure (a model refusal, not
  a patch artifact).
- temp-0 outputs are not byte-identical (expected: different reduction
  order + union-of-top-k support) but semantically equivalent 10/10 with
  matching factual answers.
- 4 concurrent users × ~136K-token unique prefixes (546K KV tokens, 2.5×
  the TP-only pool) served fully resident.

---

- [x] DCO sign-off on all commits

title: [Draft][Rust Frontend] Use Dynamo parser for DeepSeek V4
body:
# Use Dynamo Rust parser for DeepSeek V4

Linear: https://linear.app/nvidia/issue/DIS-2218

## What changed

- Adds a vLLM Rust adapter for Dynamo-owned `dynamo-parsers-v2::DeepSeekV4ToolStreamParser`.
- Registers that adapter only for `deepseek_v4`, and only when `VLLM_USE_EXPERIMENTAL_DYNAMO_RUST_PARSER=1` is set.
- Keeps every other vLLM Rust tool parser on the native vLLM implementation.
- Adds `VLLM_USE_EXPERIMENTAL_DYNAMO_RUST_PARSER` to `vllm/envs.py`; this is meaningful only with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`.
- Pins the Dynamo crate dependency for safety: `dynamo-parsers-v2` from `ai-dynamo/frontend-crates` at rev `8065db48ec557709e94dab487d346c68161bc28d`, version `=0.1.0`.

## Why

DIS-2218 is evaluating whether vLLM Rust can consume Dynamo frontend-crates parser implementations instead of carrying a separate parser surface. DeepSeek V4 is the first narrow test case because Dynamo has the DSv4 streaming parser in the v2 parser crate, and vLLM Rust already has a small parser trait that Dynamo intentionally mirrors.

This PR keeps the integration behind an explicit experimental env var so the default vLLM behavior is unchanged.

## How to use locally

Build or run vLLM with the Rust frontend enabled and the Dynamo parser flag enabled:

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 \
VLLM_USE_EXPERIMENTAL_DYNAMO_RUST_PARSER=1 \
vllm serve <DeepSeek-V4-model> \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4
```

Without `VLLM_USE_EXPERIMENTAL_DYNAMO_RUST_PARSER=1`, `deepseek_v4` still uses the native vLLM Rust parser. Non-DSv4 parser names are not changed by this branch.

## How to merge / review

- First review the dependency policy: this branch uses a pinned git dependency on `ai-dynamo/frontend-crates`. If upstream prefers crates.io-only dependencies, the follow-up is to publish `dynamo-parsers-v2` and switch this dependency to that published crate.
- Review the adapter boundary in `rust/src/tool-parser/src/dynamo.rs`; it only converts between equivalent vLLM and Dynamo parser structs and maps Dynamo errors into vLLM parser errors.
- Review the registration point in `rust/src/chat/src/parser/tool/mod.rs`; the experimental flag swaps only the `deepseek_v4` parser implementation.
- After human review and CI, remove draft status and merge normally through vLLM GitHub review. This branch is intentionally small so it can also be rebased onto current vLLM `main` if needed.

## Validation

Local checks run from `~/dynamo/vllm-0.22.0/rust`:

```bash
cargo fmt --check
cargo test --locked -p vllm-tool-parser dynamo -- --nocapture
cargo test --locked -p vllm-chat parser::tool::tests -- --nocapture
cargo test --locked -p vllm-tool-parser -- --nocapture
```

Results:

- `cargo fmt --check`: passed
- `cargo test --locked -p vllm-tool-parser dynamo -- --nocapture`: 2 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test --locked -p vllm-chat parser::tool::tests -- --nocapture`: 8 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test --locked -p vllm-tool-parser -- --nocapture`: 203 passed, 0 failed

Python env smoke note: direct `vllm.envs` import was not runnable in this local environment because local dependencies such as `torch` / test deps were not installed. The env parser itself was smoke-tested by loading `vllm/envs.py` by file path.

## Duplicate-work check

Before opening this draft, I searched open upstream vLLM PRs for `dynamo-parsers-v2`, `VLLM_USE_EXPERIMENTAL_DYNAMO_RUST_PARSER`, and `DeepSeek V4 Rust parser`. No overlapping open PR was found. PR #41834 is related to DeepSeek V4 enablement, but it does not integrate Dynamo frontend-crates parsers.

## AI assistance disclosure

This PR was prepared with AI assistance. The human submitter should review every changed line and validate the approach before marking the PR ready for review.

title: [Draft][Rust Frontend] Route top-N tool-call families through the Dynamo parser
body:
# Route top-N tool-call families through the Dynamo parser

Experimental, opt-in path to route tool-call parsing through the Dynamo-owned `dynamo-parsers-v2` crate instead of vLLM's native Rust parsers, for every family the crate implements.

Linear: https://linear.app/nvidia/issue/DIS-2218

## What changed

- `rust/src/parser/src/tool/dynamo_adapter.rs`: one shared adapter over the Dynamo crate's `create_tool_parser_for_family` dispatch. The family name is passed as data, so all families route through the same code (no per-family copy).
- Under `VLLM_USE_EXPERIMENTAL_DYNAMO_RUST_PARSER=1`, the factory overrides every native parser the Dynamo v2 crate implements: `deepseek_v4`, `qwen3_coder`, `glm47`, `kimi_k2`, `minimax_m2`, `minimax_m3`, `gemma4`. Registration is by name, so the flag re-registers each name in place; without it, behavior is unchanged.
- `gemma4` is a unified-only dummy in the native factory (errors on direct tool-parser creation); the flag turns it into a real parser.
- Exposes the Dynamo parsers through the PyO3 test binding (`vllm_parser::tool`) so the path is reachable from Python.
- Pins `dynamo-parsers-v2 = "=0.1.22"` at `ai-dynamo/frontend-crates` rev `a948ebc`.

## How to use

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 \
VLLM_USE_EXPERIMENTAL_DYNAMO_RUST_PARSER=1 \
vllm serve <model> \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser <deepseek_v4|qwen3_coder|glm47|kimi_k2|minimax_m2|minimax_m3|gemma4>
```

## Validation

Run from `rust/`:

- `cargo fmt --check`: passed
- `cargo test --locked -p vllm-parser`: 361 passed (adapter tests included)
- `cargo test --locked -p vllm-chat`: 234 passed — includes `factory_routes_all_dynamo_families_when_enabled` (all 7 families construct through the Dynamo adapter), `factory_gemma4_is_dummy_until_dynamo_enabled` (dummy without the flag, real parser with it), and the native-vs-Dynamo behavioral gates for `deepseek_v4` and `qwen3_coder`
- `cargo build --locked -p vllm-tool-parser-py`: clean (PyO3 binding compiles with the Dynamo parsers registered)

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open vLLM PRs for `dynamo-parsers-v2`, `VLLM_USE_EXPERIMENTAL_DYNAMO_RUST_PARSER`, and Dynamo Rust parser integration; no overlapping open PR.

## Disclosure

Prepared with AI assistance. A human must review every line and run the tests before this is marked ready for review.

title: Hardware-agnostic model definition for DeepSeek V4
body:
## Purpose

> Scope of this PR: A work in-progress sketch of how a hardware-agnostic
> model definition could look in-tree, using DeepSeek V4 as the case study.
> Feedback and discussion are highly appreciated.

vLLM has recently moved toward hardware-specific model definitions:
[#42770](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42770) split DeepSeek V4 into per-platform branches (`nvidia/`, `amd/`, `xpu/`), each owning the kernels that are fastest on that hardware. The follow-up [#44219](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44219) proposed extending this with a dedicated *hardware-agnostic* sibling so out-of-tree accelerators have a working path to deployment.

Three principles guided the structure:

1. **Strict isolation from vendor branches.** 
 `hw_agnostic/` never  imports from `nvidia/`, `amd/`, or `xpu/`.
  It only relies on shared infrastructure in `hw_agnostic/ops/`, `common/ops/`, `compressor.py`, `sparse_mla.py`'s V4 backend and the `model_executor` with core layers / activations / quantization.
2. **Full-graph `torch.compile` support.** 
  It allows the use of `@support_torch_compile`
3. **Pluggability for OOT vendors.**
  It leverages the infrastructure of `CustomOps` and `PluggableLayers` to enable OOT vendors to replace specific components. For the attention, the MLA wrapper `DeepseekV4MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper` is a `PluggableLayer`, which can also be overridden.

In particular this PR introduces a new `hw_agnostic` folder, next to the hardware-specific folders, containing a hardware-agnostic implementation of the DeepSeek V4 model. The implementation is isolated from the hardware-specific implementations such as `nvidia`, `amd` or `xpu` and does not interfere with them.
It subclasses `DeepseekV4FlashMLABackend` and the four perf-critical attention kernels live in hw_agnostic/ops/ (adapted from XPU); Furthermore, it employs the existing `FusedMoE` rather than NVIDIA's SM100-only MegaMoE. 

Points that potentially require further discussion:

- What should be a proper selection mechanism for this code path? Currently it is handled via an environment variable `VLLM_USE_HW_AGNOSTIC`. 
- What is the right level of pluggability? For example, in the current approach, the entire attention wrapper `DeepseekV4MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper` is a `PluggableLayer` an would need to be overridden by an OOT plugin.
- How should the testing look like and where should it take place?

cc @tdoublep @zou3519 

## Test Plan

In the future, we might need to have dedicated tests for the hardware-agnostic models, see last point for discussion above. Currently we only performed rudimentary verification tests, i.e., serving the model via

and then prompting the model via

```
VLLM_USE_HW_AGNOSTIC=1 vllm serve \
    deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --data-parallel-size 8 \
    --data-parallel-size-local 8 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --block-size 256 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --max-model-len 4096 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \
    --enforce-eager
```

```
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base","prompt":"What is vLLM?","max_tokens":13,"temperature":0}'
```

title: [Bug]: Engine core dies on KV-connector load failure for hybrid-KV models — `_update_requests_with_invalid_blocks` assumes a single KV cache group
body:
## Summary

When a KV connector reports failed loads (invalid blocks) for a model with
multiple KV cache groups (hybrid attention, e.g. **DeepSeek-V4-Flash**: CSA +
HCA + sliding-window layers), the scheduler's recovery path crashes and takes
the whole engine down:

```
File "vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", in _update_requests_with_invalid_blocks
    (req_block_ids,) = self.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(req_id)
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 1)
```

`get_block_ids()` returns one list per KV cache group; for DSv4-Flash that is
multiple groups, and the single-element unpack — marked with
`# TODO (davidb): add support for hybrid memory allocator` — raises, which
propagates through `update_from_output` and kills the EngineCore
(`EngineDeadError` for every in-flight request). A recoverable connector blip
becomes a full engine outage.

Still present on `main` as of 2026-06-13 (same TODO + unpack).

## Environment

- vLLM 0.22.1 (also inspected `main`), CUDA 13.0, 2x H200, TP=2
- Model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`
- KV connector: MooncakeStoreConnector (`kv_role: kv_both`) — but any
  connector that yields invalid blocks triggers it

## Reproduction

1. Serve DSv4-Flash with any KV connector configured.
2. Induce load failures (we hit it organically under 200-session concurrency
   when the store's TCP transport saturated; killing the store process
   mid-load also works).
3. First scheduler step that processes the invalid blocks raises the
   ValueError above; engine core exits.

## Workaround we are running

Conservative local patch: when `len(get_block_ids(req_id)) > 1`, treat any
invalid block as invalidating the entire request (reset
`num_computed_tokens = 0`, evict all the request's blocks across groups,
reschedule). Wasteful on failure but keeps the engine alive; single-group
behavior unchanged. Happy to send this as a PR if the approach is acceptable —
though we noticed #42461 proposes removing per-block transfer error handling,
which may subsume this; flagging the hybrid-model angle so the rework covers it.

## Related

- #45138 (load-failure request hangs), #45146, #34484 — adjacent failure-path
  bugs, all single-group scenarios; this report adds the multi-group crash.

title: [Bug]: `cudaErrorLaunchFailure` in worker under concurrent native KV offloading with DeepSeek-V4-Flash (frequency depends on kv-cache dtype)
body:
## Summary

With native CPU KV offloading enabled (`--kv-offloading-size 300
--kv-offloading-backend native`) and DeepSeek-V4-Flash under concurrent load
(~100 simultaneous prefill-heavy requests per node), workers intermittently
die with:

```
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure
  (cudaErrorLaunchFailure)
```

EngineCore then exits (`RuntimeError: cancelled` via shm_broadcast as the
worker disappears).

A diagnostic data point: the crash frequency depends strongly on
`--kv-cache-dtype`:

- `fp8`: both nodes' engines crashed within the first ~200 requests
- `fp8_ds_mla`: one of two nodes crashed after ~800 requests

This suggests the offload data-movement path makes layout assumptions that
only `fp8_ds_mla` satisfies for this hybrid-KV model (consistent with the
LMCache recipe's note that `fp8_ds_mla` is "required for hybrid KV storage"),
but even with the correct dtype a race or bounds issue remains under
concurrency. Notably the connector advertises `SupportsHMA` and works
functionally — when the engine survived, prefix-cache hit rates were 79–87%.

## Environment

- vLLM 0.22.1, CUDA 13.0 driver (580.159.03), 2x H200 (TP=2 per engine)
- Model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash, `--block-size 256`,
  `--max-model-len 131072`, `--prefix-caching-hash-algo sha256`
- `--kv-offloading-size 300 --kv-offloading-backend native`

## Reproduction

1. Serve DSv4-Flash with the flags above.
2. Drive ~200 concurrent multi-turn sessions with 4–6K-token prompts
   (prefill-heavy; sessions extend their prefix each step).
3. Worker dies with cudaErrorLaunchFailure within the first few hundred
   requests (`fp8`) or within ~1000 (`fp8_ds_mla`).

We can share full logs and the replay harness if useful.

title: [Model][Quant] compressed-tensors WNA16 input embeddings + tied embedding (lm_head) support
body:
## Purpose

compressed-tensors supports weight-only WNA16-INT quantization of the input embedding (`CompressedTensorsEmbeddingWNA16Int`, added in #44340), but the model-side plumbing was incomplete, so the feature silently failed on real models. This PR makes it work for both **untied** and **tied** embeddings.

### 1. Input-embedding plumbing (untied)

A `VocabParallelEmbedding` is only quantized if the model passes `quant_config` (and, for name-based targets, `prefix`) to it.

- **GPTNeoX** passed neither → quantized `embed_in` silently fell back to unquantized → `KeyError: 'embed_in.weight_packed'`.
- **Llama** passed `quant_config` but not `prefix` → name-based targets (e.g. `re:.*embed_tokens$`) could not match → same fallback: `KeyError: 'embed_tokens.weight_packed'`.
- **LFM2** passed neither → same as GPTNeoX.

Fix: pass `quant_config`/`prefix` to these input embeddings.

### 2. Tied embeddings reused as `lm_head` (new)

For tied models (common in small SOTA models like **Qwen3-0.6B** and **LFM2.5-350M**, where the embedding/`lm_head` dominates size), the shared matrix is used both for the input lookup *and* the output logits. Two things blocked quantizing it once and reusing it:

- `CompressedTensorsEmbeddingWNA16Int.apply()` raised `NotImplementedError`, so a quantized embedding could not serve the logits matmul.
- The tie paths assumed a plain `.weight` tensor, which a packed embedding does not expose (`AttributeError`), affecting the `tie_weights()` idiom (LFM2) and the direct `.weight`-assignment idiom (GPTNeoX).

Working around this by *untying* materializes a full fp16 head and **inflates** the checkpoint instead of shrinking it (e.g. Qwen3-0.6B: a 311 MB shared fp16 table becomes 82 MB packed **+ 303 MB fp16 head**). Instead, this PR quantizes the single shared matrix and reuses it for both paths:

- `compressed_tensors_embedding.py`: implement `apply()` (dequantize the packed table, `F.linear`).
- `vocab_parallel_embedding.tie_weights()`: when the embedding exposes no plain `weight` (packed/quantized), return the embedding module directly, mirroring the existing GGUF path.
- `gpt_neox.py`: route the tie through `tie_weights()`.

### 3. Extending the plumbing across the model zoo

The `quant_config`/`prefix` gap from section 1 was not unique to GPTNeoX/Llama/LFM2 — most models never passed them to their input embedding, so a WNA16-quantized checkpoint silently fell back to an unquantized embedding (or `KeyError` on the packed weight). This PR threads `quant_config`/`prefix` into the remaining input embeddings uniformly (~75 sites): dense and MoE decoders, MTP/eagle/speculator draft models (which source `quant_config` from `vllm_config`), and the BERT/RoBERTa/ModernBERT encoder families (threaded through their embedding helper classes, applied to the word/token embedding only). Position/token-type embeddings, CLIP/SigLIP vision embeddings, and non-token embeddings (gemma3n modality embedder, qwen3_dspark markov head) are intentionally left untouched — quantizing them is not a supported path.

Passing `quant_config` is inert unless the checkpoint actually targets the embedding (as proven by Llama/Qwen2, which already do this across every quant backend), so unquantized model loads are unchanged. Construction across these architectures is covered by `tests/models/test_initialization.py`; the WNA16 dispatch and kernel themselves are exercised by the GPTNeoX fixtures in the test below.

**Not a duplicate:** related embedding-quant PRs exist (#42791 ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4 embedding methods, #41365 opt-in FP8 vocab embedding) but none addresses compressed-tensors WNA16 input-embedding plumbing or tied-embedding reuse as `lm_head` for these models.

## Test Plan

`tests/quantization/test_quantized_embedding.py` loads tiny GPTNeoX checkpoints whose `embed_in` is WNA16-INT quantized (W4 group64), asserts dispatch to `CompressedTensorsEmbeddingWNA16Int`, and smoke-tests generation — one untied (`kkothuri/pythia-70m-emb-w4g64-ct`) and one tied (`kkothuri/pythia-70m-tied-W4g64-ct`, which additionally asserts the head reuses the quantized embedding so `apply()` is exercised).

```
pytest tests/quantization/test_quantized_embedding.py
```

## Test Result

- **Before:** GPTNeoX/Llama WNA16-embedding checkpoints fail to load with the `KeyError` above; tied quantized embeddings fail with `NotImplementedError`/`AttributeError`.
- **After:** both tests pass; all loads/generates work.
- **Accuracy (lm-eval, arc_easy + wikitext):**
  - *Untied input embedding (pythia-1.4b):* ~lossless — W8-channel wikitext ppl 14.733 → 14.732 (arc 0.6048 → 0.6052); W4-group64 ppl → 14.752 (arc → 0.6061).
  - *Tied shared matrix (fp16 → quant), wikitext bits-per-byte ↓:*

    | model | fp16 | **W8 tied** | W4 tied |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | Qwen3-0.6B | 0.9119 | **0.9119 (−0.0%)** | 0.9228 (+1.2%) |
    | LFM2.5-350M | 1.6525 | **1.6599 (+0.45%)** | 1.7254 (+4.4%) |

    arc_easy flat for both. W8 tied is near-lossless while halving the shared table; W4 is heavier on these compression-sensitive models because it also lowers the logits precision.
- `pre-commit run` on changed files is clean (incl. mypy).

> [!NOTE]
> Test fixtures are currently hosted under a personal HF account (`kkothuri/pythia-70m-emb-w4g64-ct`, `kkothuri/pythia-70m-tied-W4g64-ct`); happy to re-host under `nm-testing` if maintainers prefer.

> [!NOTE]
> The companion llm-compressor change (keep tied models tied when quantizing the embedding, and drop the redundant fp16 head at save) that *produces* tied quantized checkpoints whose on-disk size actually shrinks has landed in [llm-compressor#2835](https://github.com/vllm-project/llm-compressor/pull/2835). Runtime VRAM is already correct here regardless, since vLLM ties the head to the packed table at load.

---

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). All changed lines were reviewed by the submitter.

title: fix: remove nonexistent parse_chat_messages_async import (closes #44949)
body:
## What
The renderer `DeepseekV4Renderer` in `vllm/renderers/deepseek_v4.py` attempts to import `parse_chat_messages_async` from `vllm.entrypoints.chat_utils`, which no longer exists in the current codebase, causing a `ModuleNotFoundError` or an import error depending on the exact build.

Additionally, the `render_messages_async` method uses this non-existent function, so any async rendering attempt will crash.

## Fix
- Remove the import of `parse_chat_messages_async`.
- Replace the async usage in `render_messages_async` with the synchronous `parse_chat_messages`, which is already imported and works correctly as the base class handles threading.

Closes #44949

title: fix(deepseek_v4): recover tool calls trapped by a dangling </think>
body:
DeepSeek-V4-Flash occasionally omits the closing `</think>` before emitting a `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` block. This is a model bug: the chat template / encoder explicitly instructs it to output its complete reasoning inside `<think>... </think>` BEFORE any tool calls or final response, and the model intermittently fails to follow that instruction. Reasoning extraction is gated on `</think>`, so when it is missing the entire tool-call block stays in the reasoning channel, the tool parser never sees it, and the call is silently lost (finish_reason=stop, empty content). This is malformed model output, not a parser/template bug: it reproduces on the upstream DeepSeek API for V4-Flash and is invariant to MTP/cutlass/concurrency. DeepSeek's own encoding README notes the model can emit malformed output and that production needs "additional error handling". See bench/dangling-think/ for the full investigation and repro tooling.

Workaround: a narrowly-scoped, opt-in recovery in DelegatingParser that promotes a tool-call block trapped in reasoning to a real tool call, framed explicitly as malformed-output recovery (NOT making the tool-call token a reasoning terminator).

- ToolParser gains tool_call_start_token / tool_call_end_token and an opt-in recovers_tool_calls_in_reasoning flag, so the generic composition code keys off the declared interface instead of sniffing subclass internals. DeepSeekV32ToolParser (and thus V4) opts in.
- Non-streaming: when auto tool-choice parsed zero tool calls and produced no content, and the reasoning tail contains a *balanced* start/end tool-call block, re-run the tool parser over it and keep the preceding prose as reasoning. The balance requirement avoids promoting half-formed output or a marker the model merely mentioned.
- Streaming: watch the reasoning stream for the start marker, buffering partial markers across chunks so they never leak as reasoning; on a full marker, end reasoning right before it and route the remainder to the tool-call phase.
- Tests exercise the composed reasoning+tool DelegatingParser (CPU-only, stub tokenizer) for both the non-streaming and streaming dangling-`</think>` shapes.

title: [Bug]: NVFP4 fused MoE has no backend for SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE + SwiGLU clamp (blocks MiniMax-M3 NVFP4)
body:
### Your current environment

vLLM mainline (verified at HEAD / v0.23.0) and the day-0 `vllm/vllm-openai:minimax-m3`
build. NVFP4 fused-MoE path on Blackwell (sm_100/sm_103).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**No NVFP4 fused-MoE backend supports `SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE` together with the SwiGLU
clamp (`swiglu_limit`).** This blocks serving ModelOpt **NVFP4 MiniMax-M3** checkpoints,
whose experts use `hidden_act="swigluoai"` with the gate/up packed *uninterleaved*
(`[all gates; all ups]`) and a `swiglu_limit` clamp.

At engine warmup the model dies with:
```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE requires clamp_limit'
```

#### Root cause (file references at HEAD)
`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/nvfp4.py`:
- `NVFP4_BACKENDS_WITH_CLAMP = {FLASHINFER_TRTLLM}` — when `swiglu_limit` is set, available
  NVFP4 MoE backends are filtered to **trtllm only**.

But across the three NVFP4 MoE experts kernels:
- `experts/trtllm_nvfp4_moe.py::_supports_activation` → `{SILU, RELU2_NO_MUL, GELU, GELU_TANH}`
  — **no swigluoai of any kind**.
- `experts/flashinfer_cutlass_moe.py::_supports_activation` → includes `SWIGLUOAI` (interleaved)
  and *does* carry `gemm1_clamp_limit`, but cutlass is **not** in `NVFP4_BACKENDS_WITH_CLAMP`,
  and it does **not** list `SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE`.
- `experts/marlin_moe.py` → supports the swigluoai activations, but applies the clamp **only for
  SILU**: `if clamp_limit is not None and activation == MoEActivation.SILU:`. With
  `VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN=1` the kernel also receives `clamp_limit=None` because the MoE
  method reads `getattr(layer, "swiglu_limit", None)` on the `RoutedExperts` submodule (built
  inside `FusedMoE.__init__`), which never receives the `swiglu_limit` that the model passes to
  `FusedMoE(...)`.

Net: with `swiglu_limit` set + `swigluoai_uninterleave`, the oracle keeps only trtllm, which
rejects the activation → `select_nvfp4_moe_backend` finds no backend / the clamp is never wired.

#### Working contrast (confirms it's activation-specific, not a clamp problem)
`nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4` uses `hidden_act="silu"` + `swiglu_limit=10.0` and serves fine —
because `silu` is in trtllm's supported set and trtllm is clamp-capable. The gap is specifically
the **`swigluoai_uninterleave`** activation in a clamp-capable NVFP4 MoE kernel.

#### Suggested fix (either/both)
1. Add `SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE` (and ideally `SWIGLUOAI`) to a clamp-capable NVFP4 MoE backend —
   extend `flashinfer_cutlass`/`flashinfer_trtllm` activation support and/or add `MARLIN` to
   `NVFP4_BACKENDS_WITH_CLAMP` with clamp applied for the swigluoai variants (not only SILU).
2. Thread `swiglu_limit`/`swiglu_alpha`/`swiglu_beta` from `FusedMoEConfig` through to the
   `RoutedExperts`/NVFP4 MoE method so the apply path receives `clamp_limit` (today the methods
   read `getattr(layer, "swiglu_limit", None)`, which is unset on `RoutedExperts`).

#### Repro
Serve a ModelOpt NVFP4 MiniMax-M3 checkpoint with
`--block-size 128 --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 --tool-call-parser minimax_m3
--kv-cache-dtype fp8 -tp 8 --enable-expert-parallel` (± `VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN=1`).

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Searched existing issues / read docs.

title: [BugFix] Support MLA model identification for draft models Kimi(deepseek v2 structure)
body:
[BugFix] Support MLA model identification for draft models Kimi(deepseek v2 structure)

## Purpose
Currently, vLLM fails to correctly identify and initialize Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) for certain speculative decoding configurations when using the newly released Kimi draft models. 
Fix issue: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45760

**Root Cause:** The draft model `lightseekorg/kimi-k2.6-eagle3-mla` specifies `kimi_k2` as its `model_type` in `config.json`. However, `kimi_k2` is missing from the whitelist when going to the eagle branches inside the `is_deepseek_mla()` function. 

**Impact:** Because `is_deepseek_mla()` incorrectly evaluates this model as a non-MLA architecture, downstream components and optimization paths are misdirected. This either causes fallback to standard attention (leading to high memory usage/failures) or throws initialization errors during speculative decoding setup.

**Solution:** This PR adds `kimi_k2` to the `is_deepseek_mla()` detection logic, ensuring that these Kimi-based Eagle draft models are properly recognized as MLA-capable, enabling seamless speculative decoding.

* **Target Eagle Models:** 
  * HuggingFace: [lightseekorg/kimi-k2.6-eagle3-mla](https://huggingface.co/lightseekorg/kimi-k2.6-eagle3-mla)
  * ModelScope: [lightseekorg/kimi-k2.6-eagle3-mla](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/lightseekorg/kimi-k2.6-eagle3-mla)

title: [AuxOutput] Add block-keyed storage for routed-expert outputs
body:
# AuxOutput Connector: block-keyed storage for routed-expert outputs

## Summary

This PR introduces the first **AuxOutput Connector** implementation for vLLM.
The first supported auxiliary output is routed-expert output (R3): the expert IDs selected for
every token executed by an MoE model.

R3 cannot remain a request-local GPU buffer when prefix caching and async
scheduling are enabled:

- a prefix-cache hit skips model execution, so cached tokens produce no new R3;
- physical GPU/KV slots are reused and are not stable object identities;
- speculative decoding can execute rows that are later rejected;
- one result may contain cached blocks, new blocks, and a partial tail.

The connector stores immutable R3 blocks using KV-compatible block hashes. KV
and R3 for the same prefix can therefore be reused together. This PR provides a
bounded local SHM backend; distributed storage and more auxiliary output types are
follow-ups.

## Why an AuxOutput Connector?

The model capture hook only obtains a tensor from the current forward pass. A
separate lifecycle layer must decide:

- which logical tokens are accepted;
- which blocks are reusable across requests;
- when temporary GPU/CPU buffers can be released;
- where immutable blocks are stored; and
- how cached and new blocks form one ordered result.

These responsibilities also apply to future DSA and logprobs auxiliary outputs. The
connector keeps them out of the model runner and gives storage backends one
common object lifecycle. It is not a second KV Connector or a generic Scheduler
sidecar.

## Architecture

```text
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| API / OutputProcessor                                             |
| Current: return complete R3                                       |
| Follow-up: return ordered auxiliary output keys                           |
+-------------------------------+-----------------------------------+
                                |
                                v
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| EngineCore                                                        |
| Scheduler -> AuxOutputSchedulerConnector                           |
|              - logical request progress                           |
|              - KV-compatible hashes                              |
|              - terminal events                                   |
+-------------------------------+-----------------------------------+
                                | per-step metadata
                                v
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU Worker                                                        |
| Model Runner -> router capture -> async GPU-to-CPU copy            |
|              -> AuxOutputWorkerConnector                           |
|                 - accepted-row assembly                           |
|                 - block publication/materialization               |
+-------------------------------+-----------------------------------+
                                |
                  +-------------+-------------+
                  |                           |
                  v                           v
     +--------------------------+  +--------------------------+
     | Current                  |  | Follow-up                |
     | Bounded local SHM        |  | Mooncake distributed     |
     | background publication   |  | immutable objects        |
     +--------------------------+  +--------------------------+
```

The Scheduler connector owns logical progress and hashes, not payloads. The
Worker connector owns accepted R3 rows and publication. `BlockObjectStore` owns opaque
immutable blocks and retention, but knows nothing about tokens or speculative
decoding.

## Auxiliary output types

An execution auxiliary output is an auxiliary model output that is aligned to a stable
logical coordinate and may need to outlive the worker step that produced it.

| Auxiliary output | Coordinate | Reuse | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Routed experts (R3) | Executed token | Prefix block | This PR |
| DSA routing/index data | Executed token | Prefix block | Follow-up |
| Logprobs/prompt logprobs | Predicted token | Prefix block | Follow-up |
| Multimodal auxiliary data | Request/object | Request only | Exploratory |
| Sampling candidate IDs | Sampling step | Request only | Exploratory |

Prefix-block auxiliary outputs are content-addressed and reusable with a matching
prefix. Request-only auxiliary outputs use the same storage contract but do not
participate in prefix hits. Reward values, tool results, finish reasons, and
Scheduler status remain normal request/control-plane metadata.

## Current PR scope

This PR implements:

- Model Runner V2 R3 capture;
- block-keyed SHM publication and prefix materialization;
- async scheduling, chunked prefill, speculative rejection, and preemption;
- background publication, bounded capacity, and KV-aligned retention;
- terminal-only R3 delivery for streaming output;
- fail-closed checks for unsupported configurations.

It does not implement Mooncake, public auxiliary output keys, additional auxiliary output
fields, PD disaggregation, or new parallel topologies.

When disabled, no auxiliary output capture buffer, Store, per-step metadata, or R3 copy
is created on the normal serving path.

The existing `--enable-return-routed-experts` flag and `routed_experts` response
field are unchanged. The new optional configuration is exposed as
`--aux-output-config` (`AuxOutputConfig` in Python).

## Follow-ups

```text
This PR
  R3 lifecycle + local SHM
        |
        v
Unified object/profile contract + ordered keys
        |
        v
Direct Mooncake backend
        |
        v
Joint KV + mandatory-auxiliary output prefix readiness
        |
        v
DSA, logprobs, and additional topology support
```

The main planned work is:

1. define a backend-independent object/profile contract and ordered key output;
2. add a direct Mooncake backend for external trainer/JAX consumers;
3. admit remote prefix hits only when KV and mandatory auxiliary outputs are ready;
4. add DSA and logprobs through small field adapters, not new lifecycle code;
5. validate CPU KV offload, PD, PP/DCP/PCP, and multi-writer deployments before
   enabling them.

## Validation

Naming-update validation: **96 passed, 1 skipped** across configuration, store,
capture, Scheduler, output, and Ray tests. An AST comparison verified that all
24 renamed files preserve the original logic, allowing renamed identifiers,
messages, and sorted imports. Additional smoke checks passed for the existing
R3 flag, the new JSON/Python configuration, compilation hashes, serialization,
object keys, and R3 bytes. The latest naming-only update was also exercised on GB200; results and
limitations are below.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py \
  tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py \
  tests/v1/executor/test_ray_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py \
  -k 'aux_output or routed_experts or pending_output or store or worker or detach_zero_copy'
pre-commit run
```

### GB200 rename A/B (2026-09-08)

Compared `85f100032e` (before rename) with `f99d53b521` (after rename) on the
same two GB200 nodes (8 GPUs), using the locally cached DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base
FP8 weights. Both arms enable R3, MRV2, MP, TP1/DP8/EP8, async scheduling and
prefix caching. They use identical native libraries/dependencies; Python source
injection was verified by per-file SHA checks.

Workload: 64 concurrent requests, each with 262,144 input tokens and one output
token; synthetic token IDs, with output constrained to token 42. GPU memory
utilization is 0.90, max batched tokens 16,384, block size 256, and batch-invariant
mode is off. This is a serving/R3 regression test, not a model-quality evaluation.

| Measurement | Before rename | After rename |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Total throughput (input + output tokens/s) | 82,741.42 | 82,568.30 |
| Total duration | 202.768 s | 203.193 s |
| Preemptions | 0 | 0 |
| Prefix-hit tokens in the timed workload | 0 | 0 |

Throughput changed by **−0.21%** in this single A/B: no obvious regression, not a
statistical significance claim. Startup and warmup are excluded. Both arms still
reported the same first-long-request `CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel.kernel` JIT
warning, so this is not a strictly all-kernels-warm measurement.

Correctness checks:

- All 128 long responses passed token-count, R3 row-count, shape and dtype checks.
- Separate cold/hot tests cover eight 1K-prompt/16-decode requests and eight
  64K-prompt/1-decode requests per version. The latter exercises multi-step
  chunked prefill. All requests' reused-prefix R3 SHA hashes match exactly:
  768 rows/request for the short case and 65,280 rows/request for the long case.
- All eight short cold requests have identical full R3 hashes across versions.

**Limitation: long-context full-output bitwise equivalence did not pass.** None
of the 64 full 256K R3 hashes matched across the two server runs. In the saved
request-0 sample, differences begin at row index 2051 and affect 55.38% of
elements. The same candidate version also differs when comparing the identical
first 64K input prefix in 256K versus 64K cold requests (first difference at
2051; 46.44% of elements). Recomputed decode R3 can differ between cold/hot runs
as well, already before the rename. These observations do not establish the
underlying cause or prove long-output equivalence; they must not be presented
as a full R3 correctness pass.

This run validates the response structure, exact cached-block reuse and short
cross-version outputs. It does not add new forced-preemption, speculative
decoding or free-generation quality coverage. Slurm job `24176` completed with
exit code 0; test containers and node allocations were released.

Development validation covers focused unit tests, async scheduling, forced
preemption, chunked prefill, speculative rejection, cold/hot prefix reuse,
streaming aggregation, SHM capacity/LRU behavior, pre-commit, and GB200/H200
throughput experiments reported in the PR discussion.

The latest update also moves R3 GPU-to-CPU transfer onto the existing async
output copy stream, avoiding a synchronous copy on the model execution critical
path.

AI assistance was used for implementation, testing, performance experiments,
and review. The submitting human reviewed the accepted changes and validation.

title: [Feature][ROCm] Add flydsl_intranode MoE expert-parallel backend
body:
Wire FlyDSL intranode dispatch/combine as an all2all backend alongside MoRI, reusing the existing aiter fused_moe expert GEMM path. Requires mori (shmem), flydsl/mori.ir.flydsl, and FlyDSL dispatch kernels via pip or FLYDSL_REPO.




## Purpose

Wire FlyDSL intranode dispatch/combine as a new `--all2all-backend flydsl_intranode` option alongside MoRI, reusing the existing aiter `fused_moe` expert GEMM path (same as the MoRI EP integration). This adds FlyDSL PR#522-style intranode EP communication without changing the MoE compute backend.

**Requirements:** mori (shmem, ≥1.2 with `mori.ir.flydsl`), FlyDSL dispatch kernels (`pip install flydsl` or `FLYDSL_REPO` pointing at the FlyDSL repo root).

**Note:** This is distinct from the existing `moe_backend=flydsl` / `fused_flydsl_moe.py` path (W4A16 GEMM). This PR only replaces EP dispatch/combine; expert GEMM stays on aiter.

## Test Plan

- [x] Build FlyDSL from source + mori 1.2 on 8× MI355X (gfx950), integrate vLLM FlyDSL EP backend
- [x] MoE layer microbench: comm-only and full-layer E2E (`bench_dsv4_moe_e2e.py`, fp8 dispatch, EP8, DSv4-Pro shapes)
- [x] Full-model vLLM serve + bench serve: MORI EP vs FlyDSL EP, same aiter fused_moe, `--no-enable-prefix-caching`, `--num-warmups 5`, isolated docker runs per backend
- [ ] Upstream CI (gfx950 EP tests) — pending maintainer review

**Serve command (FlyDSL EP):**

```bash
export FLYDSL_REPO=/path/to/FlyDSL   # if flydsl not pip-installed
export MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE=32G
vllm serve /models/deepseek-v4-pro \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend flydsl_intranode \
  --moe-backend aiter \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

**Baseline:** same flags with `--all2all-backend mori_high_throughput`.

## Test Result

Platform: 8× MI355X (gfx950), DSv4-Pro MoE (hidden=7168, topk=6, 384 experts, EP8).

### 1) Comm-only (fp4→bf16, zero-copy=false, eager / no CudaGraph)

| tokens | fly comm (µs) | mori comm (µs) | speedup | PR speedup | PR fly (µs) | PR mori (µs) |
|--------|---------------|----------------|---------|------------|-------------|--------------|
| 4 | 156 | 157 | 1.01x | 1.37x | 27 | 37 |
| 8 | 142 | 214 | 1.51x | 1.46x | 26 | 38 |
| 16 | — | — | failed | 1.48x | 27 | 39 |
| 32 | 249 | 257 | 1.03x | 1.34x | 31 | 42 |
| 64 | 254 | 267 | 1.05x | 1.05x | 45 | 47 |
| 128 | 294 | 324 | 1.10x | 1.11x | 73 | 82 |
| 256 | 309 | 378 | 1.22x | 1.17x | 116 | 135 |
| 4096 | 3842 | 4244 | 1.10x | 1.19x | 1530 | 1819 |
| 8192 | 7622 | 8414 | 1.10x | 1.19x | 3050 | 3640 |

Speedup trend at large tokens is close to the PR reference (~1.10x vs ~1.19x), but absolute latency is still ~2–2.5× higher than PR numbers (likely due to eager vs CudaGraph and `zero_copy=false` in this bench setup).

### 2) Full MoE layer E2E (flydsl/mori dispatch + aiter fused_moe, fp8 dispatch)

| tokens | mori total (µs) | flydsl total (µs) | E2E speedup |
|--------|-----------------|-------------------|-------------|
| 4 | 496 | 263 | 1.89x |
| 8 | 648 | 500 | 1.29x |
| 16 | 745 | 666 | 1.12x |
| 32 | 895 | 852 | 1.05x |
| 64 | 1259 | 1152 | 1.09x |
| 128 | 1199 | 1126 | 1.07x |
| 256 | 1390 | 1266 | 1.10x |
| 4096 | 6398 | 5949 | **1.08x** |
| 8192 | 12495 | 11593 | **1.08x** |

### 3) Full-model vLLM prefill TTFT (EP8, bs=4, output=1, num-warmups=5, no prefix cache)

| input tokens | MORI TTFT (ms) | FlyDSL TTFT (ms) | speedup (mori/flydsl) |
|--------------|----------------|------------------|------------------------|
| 4096 | 794.5 | 777.8 | **1.021x** |
| 8000 | 1739.4 | 1720.4 | **1.011x** |

End-to-end full-model speedup is **~1–2% (~1.02x at 4096)**, consistent with microbench comm savings (~1.08x at 4096/8192 tokens) being a small fraction of total prefill time (attention + dense layers + 58× MoE layers).

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR: add `flydsl_intranode` all2all backend for MoE EP dispatch/combine on ROCm, reusing aiter fused_moe GEMM.
- [x] The test plan: microbench (comm + layer E2E) and vLLM serve TTFT A/B on DSv4-Pro EP8.
- [x] The test results: comm ~1.08–1.10x, layer E2E ~1.08x, full-model TTFT ~1.02x vs MoRI baseline.
- [ ] Documentation update: optional follow-up for ROCm EP docs / `--all2all-backend` help text.

</details>

title: [Bug]: OOM in sparse_attn_indexer (fp8_fp4_mqa_logits) when KV offloading + DeepSeek-V4 is used with long contexts
body:
### Your current environment

Title: [Bug] OOM in sparse_attn_indexer (fp8_fp4_mqa_logits) when KV offloading + DeepSeek-V4 is used with long contexts

Bug Description

When using KV cache CPU offloading (--kv-offloading-size) together with DeepSeek-V4's sparse MLA attention (Lightning Indexer), the engine crashes with OOM after a few requests once the context length grows sufficiently large. Without KV offloading enabled, the same configuration runs stably.

The crash occurs inside sparse_attn_indexer.py → fp8_fp4_mqa_logits → _fp8_fp4_mqa_logits_impl, where a temporary buffer for computing FP8 MQA logits over all candidate KV blocks is allocated. The size of this buffer grows proportionally with the number of active KV blocks, which can grow unboundedly when CPU offloading allows contexts far exceeding the GPU KV cache capacity.

After the initial OOM, a secondary cascading error occurs:

CUDA error: Invalid access of peer GPU memory over nvlink or a hardware error (cudaErrorContained)

This is not a real hardware failure — it is triggered because the OOM corrupts the CUDA context on affected GPUs, and the offloading connector's get_finished() then tries to query in-flight GPU→CPU transfer events on a corrupted context.

Environment

Item | Value -- | -- vLLM version | v0.23.0 Model | DeepSeek-V4-Pro Hardware | 2 nodes × 8 × H100 80GB SXM (16 GPUs total) Interconnect | NVLink (intra-node), NCCL (inter-node) Parallelism | PP=2, TP=8, EP=8 KV cache dtype | fp8 Quantization | deepseek_v4_fp8 (FP4 MoE via MARLIN)

Launch Configuration

Key flags involved (abbreviated):

--pipeline-parallel-size 2
--tensor-parallel-size 8
--enable-expert-parallel
--block-size 256
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95
--kv-cache-dtype fp8
--enable-prefix-caching
--kv-offloading-size 100.0      # 100 GB CPU offload
--max-model-len 1000000
--max-num-batched-tokens 8192
--max-num-seqs 16
--enable-chunked-prefill

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Launch vLLM with the flags above on a 2-node H100 cluster.
  2. Send a few sequential requests with moderate output length (e.g., max_tokens=100).
  3. The first 1–2 requests complete successfully.
  4. After the context of a running request grows to approximately 120K+ tokens (accumulated across turns or long input prompts), the engine crashes with OOM.

The scheduler output at crash time shows:

num_computed_tokens=[120064]
total_num_scheduled_tokens=8192

At block_size=256, this corresponds to ~470 KV blocks in flight per layer. The sparse attention indexer attempts to allocate a single contiguous tensor covering all 470 blocks' logits, which requires ~496 MiB — exceeding the remaining GPU free memory (~422 MiB).

Expected Behavior

The engine should either:

  • (a) handle long-context attention computation without exceeding GPU memory, by chunking the fp8_fp4_mqa_logits computation over KV blocks, or
  • (b) account for the peak memory required by the sparse indexer during memory profiling, and reduce the allocated KV cache pool accordingly, so this situation never arises.

Actual Behavior

OOM crash on GPU 2, 4, 6 (and others due to cascading), followed by full engine death:

File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py", line 478, in forward_cuda
    return torch.ops.vllm.sparse_attn_indexer(...)
File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py", line 233, in sparse_attn_indexer
    logits = fp8_fp4_mqa_logits(...)
File ".../vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py", line 377, in fp8_fp4_mqa_logits
    return _fp8_fp4_mqa_logits_impl(...)
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 496.00 MiB.
GPU 2 has a total capacity of 79.18 GiB of which 422.25 MiB is free.
Including non-PyTorch memory, this process has 78.74 GiB memory in use.
Of the allocated memory 75.23 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, with 92.00 MiB
allocated in private pools (e.g., CUDA Graphs), and 1.05 GiB is reserved
by PyTorch but unallocated.

Followed by cascading NVLink errors on all workers:

torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: Invalid access of peer GPU memory
over nvlink or a hardware error
Search for `cudaErrorContained' in https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/...

Root Cause Analysis

There are two related issues:

Issue 1 — Missing memory budget for sparse indexer scratch buffer

gpu_worker.py memory profiling accounts for model weights, CUDA graph pools, and the KV cache pool, but does notaccount for the peak scratch memory required by fp8_fp4_mqa_logits in sparse_attn_indexer.py. This function allocates a logit matrix proportional to:

scratch_size ≈ num_kv_blocks × num_q_heads × head_dim × sizeof(dtype)

Without KV offloading, GPU memory limits the number of KV blocks, so this buffer stays small and never causes problems. With KV offloading enabled, num_kv_blocks can grow far beyond what GPU memory alone would permit (since most blocks live in CPU RAM), making the scratch buffer unboundedly large at inference time.

Issue 2 — fp8_fp4_mqa_logits is not chunked over KV blocks

The current implementation materializes the full logit matrix for all KV blocks in one allocation. For long contexts under CPU offloading, this single allocation can exceed available GPU memory. The computation should be reformulated to iterate over KV blocks in smaller chunks, maintaining only top-k scores in GPU memory at any point.

Relevant source locations:

  • vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py — line 233 (fp8_fp4_mqa_logits call)
  • vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py — line 377 (_fp8_fp4_mqa_logits_impl)
  • vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py — memory profiling / KV cache budget calculation

Issue 3 — Both features are new in v0.23.0 and have never been co-tested at long context

KV CPU offloading (OffloadingConnector, CPUOffloadingSpec) and DeepSeek-V4 Lightning Indexer are both introduced or significantly reworked in v0.23.0. Their interaction at context lengths beyond GPU KV cache capacity appears to have never been validated.

Suggested Fix Direction

Option A (preferred): Chunked computation in fp8_fp4_mqa_logits

Process KV blocks in chunks of a configurable size (e.g., 64 blocks), accumulating only top-k scores:

# Pseudocode — instead of materializing all logits at once:
topk_indices = []
for block_chunk in chunk(all_kv_blocks, chunk_size=64):
    chunk_logits = fp8_fp4_mqa_logits(q, k[block_chunk])  # small allocation
    topk_indices.extend(topk(chunk_logits))
# Final top-k selection from accumulated candidates

Peak GPU memory would then be O(chunk_size) rather than O(total_kv_blocks).

Option B: Account for scratch buffer in memory profiler

Estimate the maximum scratch buffer size based on max_model_len / block_size and subtract it from the available KV cache budget during memory profiling in gpu_worker.py. This prevents the scheduler from ever allocating enough KV blocks to trigger the OOM.

Option C (minimal): Document the limitation and add a guard

If neither A nor B is immediately feasible, add a runtime check that raises a clear error (not an OOM crash) when kv_offloading_size is set and the estimated scratch buffer exceeds available headroom, with a recommendation to reduce max_model_len.

Workaround

Reducing --max-model-len to a value where (max_model_len / block_size) × per_block_logit_size fits in remaining GPU memory prevents the crash. A value of 131072 (128K) is stable in our testing with the above hardware configuration.

This is a workaround only — the root cause remains and will affect any deployment that genuinely requires long-context inference with CPU offloading.

Additional Notes

  • The secondary cudaErrorContained / NVLink errors are not real hardware faults and should disappear once the primary OOM is fixed.
  • The OffloadingConnector is correctly marked as experimental in the logs. However, a clear error message rather than a hard crash would significantly improve debuggability for users who encounter this combination.

title: [MSA] Tune Triton indexer score decode for spec-decode
body:
## Purpose

Currently, to support spec-decode case, we simply launch extra CTAs for each decode token. This is simple, because the kernel remains mostly unchanged. However, it is not good because we could have batched multiple Query tokens together for QK MMA to improve efficiency. This PR does exactly just that.
- Before: launch 1 CTA per **token** across all heads. Each CTA loads `num_idx_heads` Query tokens. For TP=4, this is just 1 token
- After: launch 1 CTA per **request** across all heads. Each CTA loads `decode_query_len x num_idx_heads` Query tokens. For TP=4 and spec-decode=3, this is 4 tokens. Crucially, when there is no spec-decode, this kernel should behave exactly like the old kernel.

Other design considerations:
- In spec-decode, the max number of decode tokens per request is `1 + num_spec_tokens`. But the scheduler can pass fewer tokens too. To avoid recompilation, we use an extra metadata `max_decode_query_len`, which stays constant throughout the lifetime of a vLLM worker, as the constexpr for the kernel.
- To keep the kernel simple, we don't introduce extra tiling over `num_idx_heads` nor `decode_query_len`. This is because at the worst case, TP=1 and 3 spec-tokens, we only have `num_idx_heads x decode_query_len = 16` Query tokens. This is still a small number that the kernel works just fine. I did some extra `num_warps` and `num_stages` tuning for this case though.
- Also reduce `TARGET_GRID` to 512 since 4096 was too much
- Also remove `sm_scale` since it doesn't affect the subsequent topk

title: [ROCM] [Communication] Add INT3 quantization method for quickreduce
body: 1.According to our kernel experiments, INT3 demonstrated better performance under TP2 (see figure below), but under TP=4 and TP=8 conditions, the performance of INT3 and INT4 was very close. This is likely because, as TP increases, the number of GPUs that need to communicate with each other grows exponentially, thereby requiring more synchronization and scheduling time; In this scenario, synchronization and latency overhead—rather than the amount of data being transferred—gradually become the bottleneck. Consequently, the proportion of total time saved by further bit-width compression (INT3) decreases, and its benefits diminish accordingly. 2.On accuracy, INT3 preserves accuracy well across the MoE models and the stronger dense model; the only model with a clearly visible drop is Qwen3-32B. Our analysis is as follows: On one hand, compared to INT4, INT3 has fewer quantization levels (8 vs 16) and therefore injects more quantization noise. The three MoE models (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, MiniMax-M2.5, and Qwen3-235B-A22B) are the most robust — each retains at least 99% of its baseline accuracy (Accuracy Recovery 0.9922, 0.9953, and 1.0055, respectively). For MoE models, the output is a weighted sum of multiple experts, and combined with their larger parameter redundancy and hidden dimension, the quantization noise is further diluted and averaged out during computation, making them less sensitive. On the other hand, the determining factor is the strength of the baseline rather than the Dense-vs-MoE distinction. Qwen3-32B is the only model with a notable drop (Accuracy Recovery 0.9462), and it already has a low GSM8K baseline (0.62), indicating limited inherent capability: many problems sit near the decision boundary, so the extra noise introduced by INT3 can easily flip their conclusions. By contrast, the other dense model, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, has a stronger baseline (0.712) and is essentially unaffected (Accuracy Recovery 1.0122). For models that are inherently strong and have high baseline scores, most problems are answered with high confidence, and 3-bit noise is not enough to change the correct outcome. **kernel test** title: [kv_offload] Use Hugepages for kv_offload tiering setup
body:
## Purpose

Add an opt-in hugepage-backed host-memory backend for the V1 KV offload `TieringOffloadingSpec` CPU primary tier.

Now you can specify to use hugepages instead of the old shared memory in the configuration:

```
{
  "kv_connector": "OffloadingConnector",
  "kv_role": "kv_both",
  "kv_connector_extra_config": {
    "spec_name": "TieringOffloadingSpec",
    "cpu_memory_backend": "hugetlbfs",
    "cpu_memory_path": "/dev/hugepages/vllm",
    "cpu_hugepage_block_size": "2MB",
    "cpu_bytes_to_use": 10737418240,
    "block_size": 256,
    "eviction_policy": "lru",
    "offload_prompt_only": true,
  }
}
```

New `kv_connector_extra_config` keys introduced:
- `cpu_memory_backend`: `default`, `shm`, or `hugetlbfs`
- `cpu_memory_path`: directory for shared mmap files, required for `hugetlbfs`
- `cpu_hugepage_block_size`: `2MB` or `1GB`

The implementation adds shared-memory backend parsing/validation, maps hugetlbfs files with hugepage-aligned size while exposing only logical KV capacity, threads the selected backend through scheduler and worker `SharedOffloadRegion` creation, keeps creator/joiner cleanup semantics, and documents setup/verification guidance.

AI assistance was used in preparing this change.

## Test Plan

- Run focused KV offload unit tests, including config parsing, shared mmap allocation, spec wiring, GPU-worker handler wiring, and tiering manager coverage.
- Run the optional real hugetlbfs smoke test with `VLLM_TEST_HUGETLBFS_PATH=/mnt/huge` (requires hugepages setup)
Set up a hugepages directory: 
```
sudo sysctl -w vm.nr_hugepages=10000

sudo mkdir -p /mnt/huge

sudo mount -t hugetlbfs nodev /mnt/huge

```

Set up permissions so the test user can read write and execute on the /mnt/huge directory

- Run CPU-only hardware-gating coverage for GPU transfer tests.
- Run relevant ruff hooks and documentation/example validation.

## Test Result

Passed:

```bash
VLLM_TEST_HUGETLBFS_PATH=/mnt/huge .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_config.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_spec_memory_config.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py -q
Result: 100 passed on a host with one visible CUDA device and /mnt/huge mounted as hugetlbfs.
Passed:
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py -q
Result: 1 passed, 24 skipped in a CPU-only environment.
Passed:
pre-commit run ruff-check --files \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_config.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py
Also passed:
.venv/bin/python -m json.tool examples/features/kv_offloading/doca_memos/kv_transfer_config.doca_memos_hugepages.json
