title: [Bug]: KV offload prefix reuse never hits when MTP/Eagle is on
body:
# [Bug]: KV offload prefix reuse never hits when MTP/Eagle is on

## Environment

vLLM `0.23.1rc1.dev301+g04c2a8dea`; same code is on current `main`. Model
`nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` (DeepSeek-V3.2 sparse MLA), 4×H200, TP4 + DCP4,
`fp8_ds_mla`, prefix caching + chunked prefill (`max-num-batched-tokens 8192`),
MTP (`num_speculative_tokens: 1`), and CPU offload via `OffloadingConnector`
(`block_size 256`, 800 GB).

## What happens

With MTP on, the offload connector stores KV to CPU fine, but reloading an
evicted prefix almost never hits. Re-sending a long prompt that fell out of the
GPU prefix cache recomputes the whole prefill instead of pulling it back from
CPU. `External prefix cache hit rate` sits at 0%.

Repro: prime a 200k prompt (offloads ~10.6 GiB to CPU), evict it with unrelated
traffic past the pool size, re-send it. TTFT ~47.7 s (full recompute), only
~0.42 GiB read back from CPU, and `get_num_new_matched_tokens` returns an
`offload_hit` of 7680 tokens no matter how long the prefix is.

## Why

In `offloading/scheduler.py`, `_build_store_jobs` computes `num_blocks` twice.
The key-collection loop applies the Eagle trailing-block exclusion
(`if is_eagle_group: num_blocks = max(0, num_blocks - 1)`), but the job-build
loop recomputes `num_blocks` without it and then advances
`next_stored_block_idx` to that larger value (`advance_stored_idx` has the same
gap). So the excluded trailing block is jumped over and never stored on the next
chunk. With an 8192-token chunk and 256-token offload blocks, that drops offload
block 31, 63, 95, … — one per chunk. `_maximal_prefix_lookup` stops at the first
gap (block 31), capping reuse at ~7680 tokens regardless of prefix length.

The Eagle flag here comes from the `from_spec` fallback that marks every group
Eagle when no group is explicitly tagged (DeepSeek-V3.2's MLA group isn't tagged
by `_annotate_eagle_groups_deepseek_v4`, which only handles `deepseek_v4`).
Excluding the one genuinely volatile final block is correct; applying it per
chunk is the bug.

Introduced in #44784 (2026-06-16, the cuMemcpyBatchAsync segfault fix). The
existing Eagle store tests are single-chunk, so they never hit this.

## Fix

Advance `next_stored_block_idx` by the Eagle-decremented count consistently in
all three spots (both `_build_store_jobs` loops and `advance_stored_idx`). Only
the true final block of the range is held back then, interior blocks store
normally. After the fix, same repro: TTFT 0.5 s, 10.9 GiB read back,
`offload_hit` 199424 (780/781 blocks, final volatile block still excluded), and
greedy output matches the freshly-computed reference token for token. All 78
existing offloading-connector scheduler tests still pass. PR with the fix and a
multi-chunk regression test to follow.

Checked open/closed issues and PRs first — no existing report; nearest ones
(#46960, #46139, #46082, #39021) touch different paths.

---
*Investigated and written with AI assistance.*

title: [Bugfix][KV offload] Store interior chunk-boundary blocks under MTP/Eagle
body:
## Summary

Fixes #46971.

With MTP/Eagle speculative decoding, `OffloadingConnector` stored KV to CPU but
prefix reuse almost never hit: re-sending an evicted long prompt recomputed the
whole prefill instead of loading it from CPU, and `External prefix cache hit
rate` stayed at 0%.

`_build_store_jobs` computes `num_blocks` twice. The key-collection loop applies
the Eagle trailing-block exclusion (`num_blocks - 1`), but the job-build loop
recomputes `num_blocks` without it and advances `next_stored_block_idx` to that
larger value (`advance_stored_idx` has the same omission). So the excluded
trailing block of every chunked-prefill chunk is jumped over and never stored —
offloaded block 31, 63, 95, … with an 8192-token chunk and 256-token blocks.
`_maximal_prefix_lookup` stops at the first gap, capping reuse at the first
chunk.

This pulls the exclusion into a single `storable_blocks()` helper used in all
three places, so only the one genuinely-volatile tail block of the range is held
back (the invariant #44784 added) and interior blocks store normally.

## Test

`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py` — full
offloading-connector scheduler suite plus a new `test_multichunk_store_no_interior_holes`
that drives a >1-chunk prefill and asserts the stored blocks are contiguous (no
boundary gap). The new test fails on the current code (gap at block 249) and
passes with the fix; the existing 78 tests still pass (80 passed total).

```
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q
# 80 passed
```

Verified end to end on GLM-5.2-NVFP4 (DeepSeek-V3.2 sparse MLA), TP4 + DCP4,
fp8_ds_mla, MTP, CPU offload. Prime a 200k prompt, evict it, re-send:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| re-send TTFT | 47.7 s (recompute) | 0.5 s |
| reloaded from CPU | 0.42 GiB | 10.9 GiB |
| `offload_hit` tokens | 7680 (30 blocks) | 199424 (780/781 blocks) |

Output is unchanged: on a deterministic prompt the greedy continuation served
from offload reload matches both a fresh prefill and a GPU-prefix-cache hit token
for token, and the volatile tail block is still excluded.

## Notes

Checked open/closed issues and PRs before filing — no existing fix; nearest PRs
(#46960, #46139, #46082, #39021) touch other paths. AI assistance was used to
investigate the bug and prepare this change; every line was reviewed.

title: [Performance]: Audit RoPE + KV-cache fusion coverage for GQA, MLA, and SparseMLA on CUDA
body:
## Summary

I audited whether RoPE + KV-cache fusion is observed across:

- GQA x BF16/FP8
- MLA x BF16/FP8
- SparseMLA x BF16/FP8

The audit used targeted runtime instrumentation around vLLM fused custom-op
paths and the DeepSeek V4 fused insert path.

## Environment

- vLLM: 0.23.0
- PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130
- CUDA: 13.x
- Hardware:
  - 1x H100 80GB for GQA and MLA
  - 2x H200 140GB for SparseMLA

## Results

| Configuration | Model | Hardware | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| GQA BF16 | `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` | 1x H100 | Ran successfully; generic GQA fused op marker count: `0` |
| GQA FP8 | `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` | 1x H100 | Ran successfully; generic GQA fused op marker count: `0` |
| MLA BF16 | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite` | 1x H100 | Ran successfully; generic MLA fused op marker count: `0` |
| MLA FP8 | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite` | 1x H100 | Ran successfully; generic MLA fused op marker count: `0` |
| SparseMLA BF16 | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` | 2x H200 | Unsupported for this path: FlashMLA fp8 layout only supports FP8 KV cache |
| SparseMLA FP8 | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` | 2x H200 | DeepSeek V4 fused insert path observed; marker count: `85` |

## Instrumented Paths

To check whether each fusion path was actually executed, I temporarily added print markers around the following vLLM functions/operators.

For GQA, I instrumented the generic RoPE + KV-cache fusion implementation:

  ```text
  vllm.compilation.passes.fusion.rope_kvcache_fusion
  fused_rope_and_unified_kv_cache_update_impl
```

  For MLA, I instrumented the generic MLA RoPE + KV-cache fusion implementation:

```
  vllm.compilation.passes.fusion.mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion
  fused_rope_unified_mla_kv_cache_update_impl
```

  For SparseMLA / DeepSeek V4, I instrumented the DeepSeek V4 fused insert operators:

```
  vllm.models.deepseek_v4.attention
  torch.ops._C.fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_quant_insert
  torch.ops._C.fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_full_cache_bf16_insert
  torch.ops._C.fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_full_cache_fp8_insert
```

If a marker appeared in the logs, that path was executed. If the marker count was 0, that specific instrumented path was not executed.

## SparseMLA FP8 Evidence

  Run config:

  ```python
  LLM(
      model="deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash",
      dtype="bfloat16",
      kv_cache_dtype="fp8",
      max_model_len=128,
      gpu_memory_utilization=0.65,
      tensor_parallel_size=2,
      trust_remote_code=True,
      enforce_eager=True,
  )
```

  I temporarily instrumented the DeepSeek V4 attention path immediately before the call to:

  ```text
  torch.ops._C.fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_quant_insert
```

The instrumented log line appeared 85 times in the runtime log, so the DeepSeek V4 fused quantized RoPE + KV-cache insert path was executed.

## SparseMLA BF16 Evidence

Using default/BF16 KV cache failed during initialization with:

```text
AssertionError: DeepseekV4 FlashMLA fp8 layout only supports fp8 kv-cache, got auto
```

So I classified SparseMLA BF16 as unsupported for the tested
DeepSeek-V4-Flash FlashMLA path.

## Caveat

The GQA/MLA results show that the targeted generic vLLM fused custom-op paths were not hit in these runs. They do not rule out backend-specific fused CUDA kernels because I did not have kernel-evel profiling available.

### Report of performance regression

_No response_

### Misc discussion on performance

_No response_

The output of `python collect_env.py`
```

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix] Prevent padding placeholders from reaching embeddings
body:
## Summary

Fix a CUDA device-side assert that can occur when speculative padding placeholders are scheduled as draft tokens.

Scheduler-side speculative padding uses `-1` draft token IDs to keep the first decode step at the uniform `1 + num_spec_tokens` shape. Those placeholder IDs should be visible to rejection sampling so they are never accepted, but they must not be fed into the model embedding lookup.

## Environment

Nightly image:

```text
vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-a65f93fb2e295e501b929df3c291ec89c27d39e8
```

Model and hardware:

```text
DeepSeek-V4-Flash on H800
```

## Reproduction

Start the prefill worker:

```bash
MODEL_NAME=/model/DeepSeek-V4-Flash

vllm serve "$MODEL_NAME" \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 256 \
  -tp 4 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer"}' \
  --enforce-eager \
  --profiler-config '{"profiler": "torch", "torch_profiler_dir": "/vllm-workspace/pro"}' \
  --port 8001
```

Start the decode worker:

```bash
export MODEL_NAME=/model/DeepSeek-V4-Flash

VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5561 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7 \
vllm serve "$MODEL_NAME" \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 256 \
  --block-size 256 \
  -ep \
  -dp 4 \
  -tp 1 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --profiler-config '{"profiler": "torch", "torch_profiler_dir": "/vllm-workspace/pro"}' \
  --port 8002
```

Start the proxy:

```bash
python3 toy_proxy_server.py \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8000 \
  --prefiller-hosts localhost \
  --prefiller-ports 8001 \
  --decoder-hosts localhost \
  --decoder-ports 8002
```

Run the benchmark:

```bash
export MODEL_NAME=/model/DeepSeek-V4-Flash
export TOKENIZER="$MODEL_NAME"
export PORT=8000

vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai-chat \
  --model "$MODEL_NAME" \
  --tokenizer "$TOKENIZER" \
  --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port "$PORT" \
  --dataset-name random \
  --num-prompts 2048 \
  --random-input-len 128 \
  --random-output-len 128 \
  --random-range-ratio 0.5 \
  --num-warmups 512 \
  --request-rate 40 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \
  --metric-percentiles 50,90,95,99,99.5,99.9 \
  --save-result
```

## Error

The decode worker crashes after serving a request with a CUDA embedding/index assert:

```text
/pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Indexing.cu:1515: indexSelectSmallIndex: block: [9,0,0], thread: [126,0,0] Assertion `srcIndex < srcSelectDimSize` failed.
/pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Indexing.cu:1515: indexSelectSmallIndex: block: [9,0,0], thread: [127,0,0] Assertion `srcIndex < srcSelectDimSize` failed.
(EngineCore_DP1 pid=19511) INFO 06-29 06:08:27 [multiproc_executor.py:426] [shutdown] Executor: waiting for worker exit count=1
(EngineCore_DP3 pid=19513) INFO 06-29 06:08:27 [multiproc_executor.py:426] [shutdown] Executor: waiting for worker exit count=1
WARNING 06-29 06:08:28 [utils.py:624] [shutdown] Process manager: force killing remaining processes count=3
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/bin/vllm", line 10, in <module>
    sys.exit(main())
             ^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/entrypoints/cli/main.py", line 95, in main
    args.dispatch_function(args)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/entrypoints/cli/serve.py", line 144, in cmd
    run_multi_api_server(args)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/entrypoints/cli/serve.py", line 373, in run_multi_api_server
    wait_for_completion_or_failure(
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/utils.py", line 569, in wait_for_completion_or_failure
    raise RuntimeError(
RuntimeError: Process ApiServer_3 (PID: 19517) died with exit code None
```

With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, the failing path points to the model embedding lookup:

```text
vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:4332 execute_model
  _model_forward(...)
  DeepSeekV4 model forward
  embed_input_ids(input_ids)
vllm/model_executor/layers/vocab_parallel_embedding.py:486
  F.embedding(input_, layer.weight)
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
```

The GPU coredump also shows the failing kernel as a bf16 embedding/index select:

```text
Assertion failed.
#0  0x00007f6a283f83f0 in void at::native::(anonymous namespace)::indexSelectSmallIndex<c10::BFloat16, long, unsigned int, 2, 2, -2>(...)
```

title: [Bug][ROCm] GLM-5.2-FP8 sparse MLA decode degenerates at long context on gfx942 (MI325X)
body:
### Summary

On ROCm gfx942 (AMD MI325X, 8x, TP8), `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` (sparse MLA / DSA) produces correct output at short context but degenerates during decode at long context. Beyond roughly 20k tokens the model stops following the task and collapses into repetition or verbatim echoing of the input, and it fails to retrieve information that is present in the prompt. The same build is correct at short context.

### Environment

- GPU: 8x AMD MI325X (gfx942), `--tensor-parallel-size 8`
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-3f5a1e1733200760169ff31ebe60a271072b199e`
- Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`
- AITER enabled (the sparse MLA decode path under suspicion is the AITER one). `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` is off by default, so it has to be set explicitly.

### Server

```
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_CAST_BF16_TO_FP16=0

vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 131072 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --reasoning-parser glm45
```

### Reproduction

This is a needle-in-a-haystack test. The prompt is a list of common filler words with 10 animal names inserted at even spacing. The model is asked to return the animals. The script runs the same task at growing context lengths with greedy decoding, and counts how many of the planted animals appear anywhere in the response (final answer plus reasoning).

```python
import random, requests

URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8100/v1/chat/completions"
MODEL = "zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8"

FILLER = (
    "table chair window bottle pencil garden river mountain coffee planet "
    "engine guitar pillow ticket basket candle market silver button orange "
    "rocket napkin ladder pepper carpet helmet jacket mirror anchor pocket "
    "branch copper saddle tunnel violin wallet zipper meadow cactus pebble"
).split()
ANIMALS = ["elephant", "giraffe", "kangaroo", "penguin", "dolphin",
           "tiger", "rhinoceros", "octopus", "crocodile", "panda"]

def make_haystack(n_words, seed=0):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    words = [rng.choice(FILLER) for _ in range(n_words)]
    step = max(n_words // (len(ANIMALS) + 1), 1)
    for i, animal in enumerate(ANIMALS):
        words[min((i + 1) * step, len(words) - 1)] = animal
    return " ".join(words)

SYSTEM = (
    "You read a word list and pick out the animals. Reply with a single "
    "comma-separated list of lowercase animal names. Output nothing else."
)

def run(n_words):
    body = {
        "model": MODEL,
        "messages": [
            {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM},
            {"role": "user", "content": "Find the animals in this list:\n\n" + make_haystack(n_words)},
        ],
        "temperature": 0.0,
        "max_tokens": 2048,
    }
    msg = requests.post(URL, json=body, timeout=1800).json()["choices"][0]["message"]
    text = ((msg.get("content") or "") + " " + (msg.get("reasoning_content") or "")).lower()
    found = sorted(a for a in ANIMALS if a in text)
    print("words=%6d  found=%2d/10  %s" % (n_words, len(found), found))

for n in (2000, 8000, 20000, 35000):
    run(n)
```

### Observed

- About 2k tokens: all 10 animals returned, on every run.
- About 20k tokens and above: the model frequently returns few or no animals, and the output degenerates into repetition or verbatim echoing of the filler list. At about 35k tokens it failed on every attempt in our runs.

### Expected

Retrieval quality should not collapse with context length up to the advertised `--max-model-len`. Short and long context should both return the planted animals.

### Additional observations

- The failure reproduces with both `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` and `--kv-cache-dtype auto` (bf16).
- Adding a repetition or frequency penalty does not fix it.
- Greedy decoding (`temperature=0`) is not reproducible run to run at long context. The same prompt returns a different number of retrieved animals across identical requests, which points at nondeterministic numerics in the long-context decode path.
- The sparse top-k selection looks correct during the collapse. Instrumenting the decode indexer shows the instruction tokens and the planted needle tokens stay in the selected set while the output is already degenerate. This points at the decode attention compute rather than the index selection.

title: Fix plain FP8 MLA KV cache page size
body:
## Summary

This PR is for the bug #46985

Fix plain FP8 MLA KV cache page-size accounting for `MLAAttentionSpec` and `SlidingWindowMLASpec`.

Plain FP8 MLA cache formats (`fp8`, `fp8_e4m3`, `fp8_e5m2`) store one combined MLA KV vector per token using one byte per FP8 element. The per-tensor scales are stored outside the KV cache tensor, so they should not be included in the KV page-size calculation.

Previously, these formats fell through to the generic dtype-based formula. That can overestimate KV cache memory when the semantic/cache dtype is not already a 1-byte dtype, causing vLLM to reserve fewer usable blocks or mis-size memory for plain FP8 MLA variants.

## Changes

- Add explicit plain FP8 MLA handling in:
  - `MLAAttentionSpec.real_page_size_bytes`
  - `SlidingWindowMLASpec.real_page_size_bytes`
- Preserve existing `fp8_ds_mla` custom-layout handling.
- Add regression coverage for plain FP8 MLA and sliding-window MLA page sizing.

## Tests

Passed:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m py_compile vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py tests/v1/test_kv_cache_interface.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
git diff --check
.venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-check --files vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py tests/v1/test_kv_cache_interface.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
```

Also passed via commit hooks:

- ruff check
- ruff format
- typos
- mypy
- SPDX header check
- forbidden imports check
- torch.cuda API check
- config validation
- Attention backend documentation check
- sign-off commit hook

Blocked:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/test_kv_cache_interface.py -v
```

The existing `.venv` does not have vLLM runtime dependencies installed, including `torch`.

Update:
  - The PR now covers both the KV-cache accounting fix for plain FP8 MLA and the runtime memory issue for fp8_ds_mla.
  - Specifically, `FlashMLASparseImpl` no longer eagerly reserves the large BF16 prefill workspace in `__init__`; it is allocated lazily when prefill actually
  needs it.

  Why this PR is not duplicative:
  - The earlier change fixed accounting.
  - This follow-up fixes the actual reserved memory overhead that was causing the OOM concern for fp8_ds_mla.

title: [Model Runner V2][Spec Decode] Fix stale values in idx_mapping from CG num reqs padding

# Context
During full cudagraphs, num_reqs can be padded up to the next capture size. Currently, the speculators can run `sample_draft` as part of a cudagraph, using the padded num_reqs first dimension size for `idx_mapping`. This is problematic because stale values in the `idx_mapping` within the padding region can be used during gumbel sampling to write to the `draft_logits` tensor. The consequence is that when running with the `probabilistic` draft sampling method during full cudagraphs, we can get incorrect/gibberish outputs.

# This PR

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Fix LSE log-base mismatch in DCP + FlashInfer MLA decode
body:
## Purpose

FlashInfer's trtllm-gen MLA decode kernel returns LSE in **log2** (per flashinfer's own reference at `flashinfer/trace/templates/attention.py:81`: `logsumexp / log(2.0)`), but `MLAAttention`'s DCP combine in `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py` hard-codes `is_lse_base_on_e=True` when calling `cp_lse_ag_out_rs` / `dcp_a2a_lse_reduce`, asserting natural log. The mismatch makes the per-shard re-weighting use the wrong base when combining DCP partial attention outputs, producing incorrect softmax denominators and corrupted attention values.

This is the residual bug after #43729 ("Support DCP with FlashInfer MLA") merged: that PR wired LSE *return* through `FlashInferMLAImpl` (so DCP combine now runs), but left the combine assuming natural-log LSE.

**Symptom** on Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 + FP8 KV + DCP=4 + `FLASHINFER_MLA`:
- Same prompt sent twice within one run produces different argmax tokens at 24/32 positions (vs ~4/32 noise floor on the no-DCP baseline with the same backend).
- Argmax tokens diverge from the no-DCP baseline on every test prompt.
- `TRITON_MLA`, FlashAttention MLA, FlashMLA, and Cutlass MLA are unaffected — their kernels emit LSE in natural log, matching the old hard-coded assumption.

**Fix:** declare each backend's LSE base as a capability flag (`lse_base_on_e`) on `AttentionImplBase` (default `True` / natural log), override it to `False` on `FlashInferMLAImpl`, and thread it through the DCP combine. The kernels already support both bases natively via their `IS_BASE_E` constexpr (`tl.exp/tl.log` vs `tl.exp2/tl.log2`), so there is no FP multiply or rounding loss — and adding another log2-emitting backend later is a one-line `ClassVar` instead of a call-site edit.

## Not a duplicate

- **#43729** (merged) added FlashInfer MLA + DCP support and the LSE-return plumbing, but not this log-base reconciliation.
- **#47074** ("Use larger workspace size for Flashinfer MLA LSE") touches the same file but fixes an orthogonal issue — a `trtllm_gen_softmax_workspace` allocation overflow — not the LSE base. The two are complementary.

## Test Plan & Results

Verified end-to-end on Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 + DCP=4 + FP8 KV (Blackwell GB200) against a TEP4 (no DCP, same FlashInfer backend) baseline:

- **5-prompt greedy-decode refcomp** (max_tokens=32, top_p=1): **0 token mismatches** after fix vs `28+24+24+4+0` before; within-run stability `24/32 → 5/32` (matches baseline `4/32`).
- **5-shot GSM8K** (full 1319-problem set): baseline `0.9356 / 0.9363` vs DCP4-FI `0.9363 / 0.9371` (flexible / strict) — delta `+0.07% / +0.08%`, well under run-to-run variance.

Kernel-level equivalence test added (`tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_decode.py` was part of the original branch; this PR contains the core fix — happy to fold the test/CI-trigger commits back in if reviewers prefer).

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude) was used to diagnose and patch this issue end-to-end. The submitting author has reviewed every changed line.

title: [XPU][Bugfix] Do not transpose weight_scale_inv at load time
body:
## Summary

The MLA attention's `_o_proj` path (via `_get_cached_wo_a_bf16` in `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`) directly reads `weight_scale_inv` and assumes the original `[N/128, K/128]` checkpoint layout for manual dequantization.

Pre-transposing to `[K/128, N/128]` in `process_weights_after_loading` caused `_expand_2d_block_scales` to apply wrong scale values (row/col blocks swapped), silently degrading GSM8K accuracy from 96.5% to 89% on DeepSeek-V4-Flash.

## Root Cause

`_get_cached_wo_a_bf16` reshapes the scale tensor:
```python
wo_a.weight_scale_inv.view(n_local_groups, -1, wo_a.weight_scale_inv.shape[-1])
```

With original `[4, 48]` layout: view -> `[1, 4, 48]` -> row_block=128, col_block=128 (correct)
With transposed `[48, 4]` layout: view -> `[1, 48, 4]` -> row_block=11, col_block=1536 (wrong)

The `.view()` succeeds in both cases (same total elements), but the semantic meaning is completely wrong when transposed - each weight element gets multiplied by a scale from the wrong block position.

## Fix

Remove load-time transpose of `weight_scale_inv` entirely. Transpose the scale to `[K/128, N/128]` (oneDNN expected layout) at runtime in `apply_block_scaled_mm` instead. The cost is negligible (~3.5KB scale tensor transpose per GEMM call).

With original `[4, 48]` layout (`wo_a`: N=512, K=6144):
- view -> `[1, 4, 48]` -> row_block=128, col_block=128 ✓

With transposed `[48, 4]` layout:
- view -> `[1, 48, 4]` -> row_block=11, col_block=1536 ✗

The `.view()` succeeds in both cases (same total elements), but the semantic meaning is completely wrong when transposed — each weight element gets multiplied by a scale from the wrong block position.

## Fix

Remove load-time transpose of `weight_scale_inv` entirely. Transpose the scale to `[K/128, N/128]` (oneDNN expected layout) at runtime in `apply_block_scaled_mm` instead. The cost is negligible (~3.5KB scale tensor transpose per GEMM call).

title: [Spec Decode] Add D-cut: Adaptive Verification Depth Pruning for Batched Speculative Decoding
body: ## Purpose This PR adds **D-Cut**, a confidence-based draft-pruning policy for the DFlash parallel drafter, that trims the per-step draft width *after* drafting and *before* target verification. By dropping low-confidence draft tokens, it cuts the number of tokens the target model must verify per step while keeping acceptance length almost unchanged — improving TPOT and end-to-end throughput, especially at higher batch sizes and on harder prompts where the draft is less likely to be accepted. D-Cut is disabled by default (`dflash_dcut=0`); existing DFlash behavior is unchanged unless the option is set. The implementation is small and contained — **+367/-12 across 7 files** (only 12 lines of existing code touched), plus a ~270-line test file. The technique is documented by the AngelSlim team: . ### Why this is not a duplicate of existing dynamic-SD work Dynamic speculative-decoding work in flight operates on **autoregressive** drafters and decides *before/during* drafting: - **DSL (#35301)** early-exits the draft loop at a confidence threshold — requires a step-by-step drafter to "stop early". - **DSD (#32374 family, e.g. #45953, #45963, #46399)** picks the runtime draft length `k` from batch size *before* drafting. DFlash is a **parallel** drafter: it emits all `num_speculative_tokens` in one shot, so there is no draft loop to exit early and no per-step `k` to lower. D-Cut targets exactly that gap — it prunes the already-produced draft based on per-token confidence, reducing **target-side verification** cost rather than draft-side compute. The `auto` policy selects how many drafts to keep per batch size from a warmup-profiled cost table, which none of the above provide. This PR **reuses** the DSD compatibility scaffolding (the `_maybe_override_dynamic_sd_cudagraph_mode` full→piecewise fallback and the v2-unsupported-features list) rather than conflicting with it. ## Design Three policies, selected by a single `dflash_dcut` field on `SpeculativeConfig`: | `dflash_dcut` | Policy | Behavior | |---|---|---| | `0` (default) | `off` | No pruning; standard DFlash. | | float in `(0, 1]` | `fixed_ratio` | Keep a fixed fraction of target-forward query tokens (global top-K by draft score). **Hardware-independent.** | | `"auto"` | `selector` | Keep length chosen at runtime from a warmup full-cost table. **Hardware-dependent.** | The pipeline is intentionally split into a **method-agnostic** transport/apply path and a **DFlash-specific** selection path, so the option can later be extended to other parallel-drafting methods: 1. **Select** (DFlash proposer): from the draft logprobs, compute per-request keep lengths. For `fixed_ratio` the budget is `ceil(value * batch_size * (num_draft + 1)) - batch_size`; `auto` looks the batch size up in a cost table profiled during warmup. 2. **Transport**: keep lengths ride on `DraftTokenIds.dcut_keep_lens`. 3. **Apply** (scheduler): truncate each request's spec tokens to its keep length (the reserved bonus token is always retained), and record kept vs. total draft tokens. 4. **Observe**: `SpecDecodingStats`/`SpecDecodingLogging` report a D-Cut keep ratio alongside the existing acceptance metrics. ### Compatibility D-Cut runs on the V1 model runner with piecewise CUDA graphs. To avoid silent misconfiguration it is gated the same way dynamic SD is: - **Async scheduling**: hard-errors if explicitly enabled, otherwise disabled with a warning (async SD currently assumes a fixed draft width). - **CUDA graphs**: full-graph mode falls back to piecewise (reusing the existing dynamic-SD override). - **Model Runner V2**: listed as an unsupported feature so config resolution falls back to V1. ### Usage ```bash # auto policy (recommended): keep length chosen from a profiled cost table vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash", "model":"", "num_speculative_tokens":7, "dflash_dcut":"auto"}' # fixed-ratio policy: keep ~50% of the draft width vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash", "model":"", "num_speculative_tokens":7, "dflash_dcut":0.5}' ``` Setting `dflash_dcut=0` (default) restores standard DFlash. ## Benchmark **Setup.** 5 target models (dense + MoE), 5 datasets, greedy decoding, 8×H20, serving concurrency swept {4,8,16,32,64}, results reported at **concurrency 32**. The primary metric is **output-token throughput speedup over autoregressive (AR) decoding** — under batched serving a longer draft raises mean accepted tokens (τ) but also enlarges the verification batch, so a higher τ does not necessarily mean higher throughput. `D-Cut (16)` is the `auto` policy on a block-16 drafter; `DFlash (16)` is the same drafter with no pruning. D-Cut keeps **92% of DFlash's τ on average** (85–97%) — it trims the low-confidence tail, not the useful prefix — so the throughput gains below come almost free of accepted-length loss. Speedup vs. AR (AR = 1.00× reference; higher is better; **bold** = best per row). Averaged over the 5 datasets: | Model | EAGLE-3 / MTP † | DFlash (16) | D-Cut (16) | |---|---|---|---| | Llama-3.1-8B | 1.03× | 0.67× | **1.12×** | | Qwen3-4B | 1.29× | 0.98× | **1.35×** | | Qwen3-8B | 1.11× | 0.80× | **1.21×** | | Qwen3.5-27B | **1.31×** | 0.94× | 1.25× | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (MoE) | 1.75× | 2.36× | **2.50×** | † EAGLE-3 for Llama-3.1-8B / Qwen3-4B / Qwen3-8B; MTP for the Qwen3.5 models. `D-Cut (16)` is the `auto` policy on a block-16 drafter; `DFlash (16)` is the same drafter unpruned. D-Cut beats unpruned DFlash on average throughput for **every** model, and beats the EAGLE-3/MTP baseline on 4 of 5. ### Scaling with concurrency The figure below shows absolute output-token throughput as concurrency grows 4→64 (rows = datasets, columns = models; green = D-Cut, blue = DFlash; solid = block-16, dashed = block-8). Throughput rises with concurrency for both, but they diverge at the high end: on dense targets DFlash (16) gains the least from batching (verifying long drafts cancels the accepted-token benefit), while D-Cut sustains the highest throughput, with the gap widening as load grows. Under **temperature-1 sampling** (Qwen3-8B, H20), stochastic decoding shortens accepted drafts and penalizes long fixed-depth proposals: DFlash falls below AR at high concurrency, while D-Cut (auto) sustains a 1.15× speedup over AR (1.68× relative to DFlash — a *larger* relative gain than under greedy decoding, since harsher sampling leaves more low-utility suffix to prune). ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dcut.py -v ``` 26 unit tests covering: keep-count arithmetic and bonus-token accounting, `dflash_dcut_mode` derivation and config validation (including the non-`dflash` method gate), keep-ratio stats accumulation/logging, and the scheduler-side truncation. All pure-logic (no GPU). ## Test Result - `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dcut.py`: **26 passed**. - End-to-end on H20 (Qwen3-4B + DFlash-B16, `num_speculative_tokens=7`, `dflash_dcut=auto`, piecewise CUDA graph, prefix-cache and async scheduling disabled): server boots, warmup cost table builds, inference correct, and the D-Cut keep-ratio metric is reported in the SpecDecoding logs. The three compatibility gates (async, cudagraph, MRv2) trigger as designed. - Benchmark numbers above collected on H20. --- *AI assistance was used in preparing this change (code migration, test authoring, and this description). All changes have been reviewed line-by-line and validated end-to-end on GPU by the submitter.*

title: ds-v4-nvfp4 support v1
body:
## Purpose

This PR adds ROCm support fixes for serving DeepSeek V4 Pro NVFP4 checkpoints in vLLM.

The main purpose is to make DeepSeek V4 Pro NVFP4 checkpoints load and run correctly on AMD ROCm with tensor parallelism, expert parallelism, FP8 KV cache, and the DeepSeek V4 AMD model path.

The change set covers:

- Add Quark full NVFP4 dense linear support.
- Add Quark NVFP4 MoE expert support.
- Add FP8 block-scaled W8A8 Quark linear support for selected DeepSeek V4 attention projections.
- Add DeepSeek V4 AMD loader compatibility for checkpoint scale names such as `.input_scale -> .input_scale_2`.
- Add ROCm-compatible NVFP4 MoE EMULATION backend support.
- Fix DeepSeek V4 attention input-shape handling for ROCm fused attention paths.
- Improve parameter loading robustness for already TP-sharded tensors.
- Avoid ROCm graph-capture failures from GPU-to-CPU debug synchronization in DeepSeek V4 MoE diagnostics.
- Document the NVIDIA ModelOpt NVFP4 runtime workaround for ROCm expert parallelism.

This PR intentionally removes the earlier experimental weight-only NVFP4 code path. The current DeepSeek V4 NVFP4 checkpoints are treated as full NVFP4 configurations with activation input scales.

## Test Plan

| **CUDA** | 13.0 (toolkit & runtime) |
| **Python** | 3.12 |
| **OS** | Ubuntu 24.04 |

---

## What happened

Launching with the default `--kv-cache-dtype auto` (or omitting the flag entirely, which is
equivalent) crashes vLLM during model initialisation:

```
AssertionError: DeepseekV4 fp8_ds_mla layout only supports fp8 kv-cache, got auto
```

The HuggingFace model page shows:

```bash
vllm serve "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash"
```

…with no `--kv-cache-dtype` flag. This works on H100/SM100 but silently fails on
Blackwell SM120 — there is no hint in the error message that `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`
is required on this architecture.

### Workaround

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --kv-cache-dtype fp8
```

vLLM then auto-upgrades `fp8` → `fp8_ds_mla` internally.

---

## Root cause

Two separate places in the codebase reject `auto` for SM120 without providing
an auto-resolution path.

### 1. `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py` — backend validator

```python
# SM10x (H100 / Hopper): "auto" is explicitly accepted
if kv_cache_dtype not in (None, "auto", "bfloat16", "fp8", "fp8_e4m3"):
    return "kv_cache_dtype not supported"
return None   # ← "auto" passes ✓

# SM12x (Blackwell): "auto" is NOT in the allowed set — no auto-resolution
if kv_cache_dtype not in ("fp8", "fp8_e4m3", "fp8_ds_mla"):
    return "kv_cache_dtype not supported"  # ← "auto" rejected ✗
```

### 2. `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py` — dtype resolver

```python
# DeepseekV4FlashInferSM120Attention sets use_fp8_ds_mla_layout = True (class-level hardcode)
def _resolve_dsv4_kv_cache_dtype(use_fp8_ds_mla_layout, kv_cache_dtype, cache_config):
    if use_fp8_ds_mla_layout:
        assert kv_cache_dtype.startswith("fp8"), (   # "auto" hits this assert
            f"DeepseekV4 fp8_ds_mla layout only supports fp8 kv-cache, "
            f"got {kv_cache_dtype}"
        )
        ...
    # The auto/bfloat16 fallback path is only reachable when use_fp8_ds_mla_layout=False
    return kv_cache_dtype, torch.bfloat16
```

On SM10x, `auto` falls through to the bfloat16 path. On SM120,
`use_fp8_ds_mla_layout` is always `True`, so `auto` hits the assertion before
any fallback is attempted.

---

## Expected behaviour

On SM120, `auto` should be silently resolved to `fp8_ds_mla`, parallel to how
`auto` resolves to bfloat16 on SM10x. The user shouldn't need to know about
SM120-specific memory layout internals to run a supported model on supported hardware.

---

## Suggested fix

In `_resolve_dsv4_kv_cache_dtype` (`attention.py`):

```python
if use_fp8_ds_mla_layout:
    if kv_cache_dtype in ("auto", "bfloat16"):
        # SM120 fp8_ds_mla layout requires fp8; silently upgrade (same as SM10x
        # automatically selecting bfloat16 for "auto").
        logger.info_once(
            "Blackwell SM120 fp8_ds_mla layout: auto-selecting kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla."
        )
        kv_cache_dtype = "fp8_ds_mla"
        cache_config.cache_dtype = "fp8_ds_mla"
    assert kv_cache_dtype.startswith("fp8"), (
        f"DeepseekV4 fp8_ds_mla layout only supports fp8 kv-cache, got {kv_cache_dtype}"
    )
    ...
```

And in the SM12x branch of the validator (`flashinfer_sparse.py`), allow `auto`
(or resolve it to `fp8_ds_mla` before the check):

```python
if device_capability.major == 12:
    resolved = kv_cache_dtype if kv_cache_dtype not in (None, "auto") else "fp8_ds_mla"
    if resolved not in ("fp8", "fp8_e4m3", "fp8_ds_mla"):
        return "kv_cache_dtype not supported"
    ...
```

---

## Additional context

- There is a related issue: `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1` (default) crashes during
  FP8 GEMM warmup on Blackwell for both DeepSeek-V4 and Qwen3.5 models. The
  workaround is `export VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`. Separate report filed at
  [mix-labs/BUG-Report-vLLM-DeepGemm-Warmup.md](./BUG-Report-vLLM-DeepGemm-Warmup.md).
- Tested on vLLM 0.24.0. The SM120 validator was introduced in 0.23.0 and the
  auto-resolution gap was not addressed in 0.24.0.

PYTORCH_HIP_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=112 TORCH_BLAS_PREFER_HIPBLASLT=1 PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx90a;gfx942;gfx950;gfx1100;gfx1101;gfx1200;gfx1201;gfx1150;gfx1151 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug On **gfx942 (MI300X)**, serving `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8` with **MTP speculative decoding** under **torch.compile / CUDA-graph** intermittently crashes the engine with a GPU memory access fault: ```text Memory access fault by GPU node-N (Agent handle: ...) on address 0x... . Reason: Unknown. ... Worker proc VllmWorker-N died unexpectedly ... vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError ``` **Only `--enforce-eager` (cudagraph=NONE) is immune** — the crash occurs in both `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` and `PIECEWISE`. ### Reproduce ```bash VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --block-size 1 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --max-model-len 200000 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}' # Send a few ~8K-token requests at concurrency 1. ``` Containerized launch we used (public base image + the still-unmerged #45324 sparse-attn masking patch applied on top): ```bash # Base: vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.23.0 + #45324 applied on top docker run -d --name glm5_server \ --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --group-add video --group-add render \ --ipc host --network host -v $CACHE_DIR:/model \ -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 -e HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1 -e NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=112 \ -e TORCH_BLAS_PREFER_HIPBLASLT=1 -e PYTORCH_HIP_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \ -e HF_HOME=/model -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 -e TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 \ vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.23.0 \ --model zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --block-size 1 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 200000 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}' ``` ### Root cause In `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`, the sparse-MLA backend uses persistent work-split metadata buffers (`_mla_work_*`) that are allocated once and reused. They are **written host-asynchronously in `build()` by `get_mla_metadata_v1(...)` outside the captured graph**, but **read by the decode kernel inside the captured CUDA graph**. With no ordering between the write and the graph replay, the kernel can read stale/partially-written metadata and go out of bounds → GPU memory fault. Evidence: serializing kernels (`AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3`) avoids the crash for n=1/n=3, and `work_indptr` values are in-bounds at the fault — i.e. an ordering/race, not bad metadata values. Eager is immune because it uses dynamic per-call buffers. ### Fix A one-line current-stream host sync in `build()` (after the metadata recompute) that orders the write before the graph-captured read eliminates the crash; it is performance-neutral (it runs before the heavy forward, waiting only on the tiny metadata write). Validated across 100+ requests at n=2/n=3 with fault=0 and unchanged TPOT. **I will open a PR with this fix.** ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode][V1] Guard stale async spec prev rows
body:
## Purpose

Fix an async speculative decoding batch-change failure mode where stale previous-batch row indices can outlive the tensors they index.

In async scheduling, `prev_positions` maps current request rows to rows from the previous worker batch. The existing code handled `-1` for new requests, but it did not guard positive stale indices when the previous sampled-token/count tensors are shorter than the old batch mapping. That can misattribute sampled counts or index out of bounds during input staging / token-count correction.

This PR makes those paths treat out-of-range previous rows the same way as new or non-participating rows.

## Summary

- Bounds-check `prev_positions` against `valid_sampled_token_count` before gathering accepted-token counts in `update_num_computed_tokens_for_batch_change`.
- Handle the empty valid-count tensor case explicitly.
- Bounds-check `prev_positions` against `prev_sampled_token_ids` in `GPUModelRunner._prepare_input_ids`.
- Add focused regression tests for stale positive previous positions and the empty valid-count edge case.

## Why this is a draft

The original failure was observed in a DGX Spark deployment running DeepSeek V4 Flash DSpark, while this PR currently contributes focused CPU-runnable regression tests for the worker/spec-decode bookkeeping paths. I am opening this as a draft to get early maintainer feedback on whether this should remain a separate worker-side guard or be folded into adjacent async-spec scheduling work before marking it ready for review.

## Scope and non-duplicate framing

This is narrower than #40768. That PR addresses `-1` placeholder materialization at the scheduler boundary. This PR addresses stale positive previous-row indices inside V1 worker/spec-decode bookkeeping after async batch changes.

This is also distinct from #41481, which warms spec-decode helper kernels and touches `update_num_computed_tokens_for_batch_change` for startup latency, not for stale-row correctness.

An adversarial placement review considered moving the guard into `_compute_prev_positions`, but the consumers have different validity bounds: input staging is bounded by `prev_sampled_token_ids`, while token-count correction is bounded by `valid_sampled_token_count`. Guarding at each consumer keeps the invariant local to the tensor being indexed.

## Files changed

- `vllm/v1/spec_decode/utils.py`
  - Guard previous-row gathers with `0 <= prev_position < valid_count_len`.
  - Avoid indexing empty `valid_sampled_token_count`.

- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`
  - Guard deferred correction lookup by sampled-count length.
  - Guard async input staging lookup by `prev_sampled_token_ids` length.

- `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_async_batch_change.py`
  - Regression tests for stale positive `prev_positions` and empty valid counts.

- `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py`
  - Regression tests for bounded sampled-count lookup and async input staging.

## Test Plan

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_async_batch_change.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py \
  -k 'async_batch_change or valid_sampled_count_for_prev_index or prepare_input_ids_skips_stale_positive_prev_position' -q

uvx ruff format --check \
  vllm/v1/spec_decode/utils.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_async_batch_change.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py
```

## Test Result

```text
4 passed, 35 deselected, 16 warnings in 10.42s
4 files already formatted
```

DGX Spark smoke against the deployment that motivated this patch:

- `spark-01:8888/v1/models` reports served model `deepseek-v4-flash-dspark`.
- `max_model_len`: `1048576`.
- Short chat completion finished normally.
- 4-way concurrent burst completed without transport failure.
- Recent service logs showed no engine death, CUDA assert, illegal memory access, or out-of-bounds errors after the smoke.

## AI assistance disclosure

This change was developed with AI assistance. The submitting author reviewed the changed lines, ran the test commands above, and kept this PR in draft for maintainer feedback before requesting review.

title: fix(deepseek_v4): resolve auto kv-cache-dtype to fp8_ds_mla on SM120
body:
Fixes #47174

On SM120 the fp8_ds_mla layout has no non-fp8 variant, but the default `auto` hit an assert in `_resolve_dsv4_kv_cache_dtype` instead of resolving. So `vllm serve <dsv4-model>` with no flag (as on the HF model card) crashed on Blackwell:

```
AssertionError: DeepseekV4 fp8_ds_mla layout only supports fp8 kv-cache, got auto
```

Map `auto`/`None` to `fp8` so it flows through the existing `fp8 -> fp8_ds_mla` upgrade (which also writes the canonical string back onto cache_config), and accept them in the SM120 backend validator so selection isn't rejected first. Explicit `bfloat16` on this layout still errors; the plain-row (SM10x) path is untouched.

Added a CPU unit test covering both layouts. Ran ruff clean; can't run the full test locally (no GPU box for the full vllm import) so leaving the suite to CI.

title: [XPU]add sycl path for Mhc
body:
## Purpose
This PR replaces the native/Triton-based fallback implementations in the forward_xpu methods of the MHC (Multi-Head Chunking) layer with dedicated SYCL kernel calls for the DeepSeek V4 (DSv4) model on Intel XPU.

Specifically, it:

Replaces self.forward_native(...) calls with optimized SYCL kernel ops:
- torch.ops._xpu_C.mhc_pre (in MHCPreOp.forward_xpu)
- torch.ops._xpu_C.mhc_post (in MHCPostOp.forward_xpu)
- torch.ops._xpu_C.mhc_fused_post_pre (in MHCFusedPostPreOp.forward_xpu)

Replaces the torch.ops.vllm.hc_head_triton(...) call with torch.ops._xpu_C.hc_head_fused(...) (in HCHeadOp.forward_xpu)
Removes parameters that are no longer needed by the new SYCL kernel interfaces: n_splits, tile_n, norm_weight, norm_eps

(will attach full `collect_env.py` output — pod was recycled, regenerating)
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Running DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 4x H20 with TP=4 and long context. After ~16h of serving the engine died and took all in-flight requests with it (`EngineDeadError`). Spent a while digging through the log and I'm fairly sure the trigger is a runtime TileLang recompile blocking one rank long enough to break TP sync, but wanted to report it since the failure mode is pretty opaque (the worker that actually dies leaves no traceback).

Here's what I pieced together.

The crash sequence:

```
11:18:28  Engine: Avg prompt throughput 49877 tok/s, Running: 3 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 4.7%
11:18:24  (Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=1237) TileLang begins to compile `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang`
              <- no matching "completes" line for this one
11:18:32  (EngineCore pid=975) Worker proc VllmWorker-2 died unexpectedly, shutting down executor.
11:18:32  (Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=1237) Parent process exited, terminating worker queues
11:18:36  [shutdown] workers still running after grace period; SIGTERM count=3
11:18:40  [shutdown] workers still running after SIGTERM; SIGKILL count=3
11:18:40  (EngineCore pid=975) EngineCore encountered a fatal error.
              ... mq.dequeue -> acquire_read -> raise RuntimeError("cancelled")
11:18:40  (APIServer pid=1) EngineDeadError
```

A few things that stood out:

- The worker that dies is **rank 2 (VllmWorker-2)**, and it prints nothing — no exception, no stack. Given that, I don't think it's a Python-level error; looks like the process got killed at the collective/comm layer.
- **rank 0** is sitting at `TileLang begins to compile mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang` with no `completes`. Every other compile of this kernel in the log finishes in ~8s and prints a `completes` line, so this one was mid-flight when the shutdown hit.
- The final `RuntimeError: cancelled` comes from the main process waiting on `mq.dequeue -> acquire_read`, i.e. it's just waiting for a worker reply that never arrives after rank 2 is gone.

I don't think it's OOM or a bad kernel:

- GPU KV cache usage was 4.7% at crash time, so no memory pressure.
- Grepped the whole log — no `CUDA error`, no `illegal memory access`, no `Xid`, no `segfault` anywhere.

What was in flight when it died (from the SchedulerOutput dump): 3 concurrent requests, two of them long-context with `num_computed_tokens=[510296, 460200]` (~510k / ~460k tokens), plus MTP spec-decode tokens and an active KV-offload `store_job`. So it's the long-context + chunked-prefill + MTP + offload mix, which is exactly where new shapes keep showing up and re-triggering TileLang compiles.

And the recompiles are not a one-off — `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang` gets recompiled during inference repeatedly over the run:

```
09:23:33 begins -> 09:23:41 completes  (8s)
09:24:13 begins -> 09:24:21 completes  (8s)
09:25:48 begins -> 09:25:56 completes  (8s)
09:27:43 begins -> 09:27:51 completes  (8s)
11:09:36 begins -> 11:09:45 completes  (9s)
11:18:24 begins -> (crash)
```

(same for `mhc_post_tilelang` and `hc_head_fuse_tilelang` earlier in the run). Each one is ~8-9s. Any of them landing during active multi-rank serving looks like a desync window waiting to happen — 11:18:24 is just the one that finally hit.

One more thing worth flagging: the `jit_monitor` warnings only cover Triton kernels. In this run it warned about 9 of them (`_compute_slot_mapping_kernel`, `eagle_prepare_inputs_padded_kernel`, `_mtp_shared_head_rmsnorm_kernel`, etc.), but none of the TileLang mHC kernels. So the monitor is flagging millisecond Triton JITs as latency spikes while staying blind to the ~8s TileLang JITs that are actually dangerous.

### Expected behavior

A runtime TileLang compile shouldn't be able to desync the TP group and hard-kill a worker. Ideally the mHC TileLang kernels get compiled/cached at warmup so nothing compiles during serving; failing that, the compile should at least be visible (jit_monitor) and the worker-response timeout should tolerate a slow rank instead of killing it.

### Questions

- The config shows `cache_dir=''` and `local_cache_dir=None` — is the TileLang mHC kernel cache persisted anywhere? If it's not on disk and shapes vary under 1M context, these recompiles will keep recurring. Any guidance on where the TileLang cache lives / how to warm it would help a lot.
- `compile_sizes=[]`, `compile_ranges_endpoints=[256, 8192]`, capture sizes up to 96 — the mHC TileLang kernels clearly aren't in warmup and compile lazily. Is there a way to force them into warmup?
- Can jit_monitor be extended to TileLang JIT? These are much longer than the Triton ones it tracks.

### Things I'm planning to try (would appreciate a steer on which is actually recommended)

- `--enforce-eager`
- `disable_custom_all_reduce=True` (pure NCCL — may not hard-kill on desync?)
- turning off MTP
- bumping collective / worker-response timeouts to cover the ~8s compile
- persisting the TileLang cache + warming the mHC shapes

Happy to attach the full engine log (~34k lines) or pull any specific section.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

[65162ed143e94524878c2c02f0fe1ddd.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29535986/65162ed143e94524878c2c02f0fe1ddd.txt)

PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1
TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1
TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_sdi2sh

### 🐛 Describe the bug

# vLLM 0.24.0 on Blackwell SM120 (RTX PRO 6000) — Comprehensive Compatibility Report

**Repository:** https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm  
**Target:** Full compatibility with SM120 (compute capability 12.0) for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Qwen3.6-27B-FP8

---

## Executive Summary

vLLM 0.24.0 runs on **2× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation (96 GB each, SM120, compute capability 12.0)** but requires **9 workarounds** (5 env vars, 4 code patches) and **2 major features disabled** (CUDA graphs, speculative decoding) to serve `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` at TP=2.

**The recurring root cause:** Most SM120-specific code paths assume "Blackwell = SM100" (B100/B200, `major == 10`). SM120 (workstation Blackwell, `major == 12`) is a different ISA target with different kernel support. Several features ship SM100 kernels only, then assert or mis-launch on SM120.

### Impact on user experience

| Feature | Status on SM120 | Root cause |
|---------|----------------|------------|
| Model loading (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) | ✅ works (with patches) | 5 kernel compatibility fixes needed |
| Model loading (Qwen3.6-27B-FP8) | ✅ works (1 env var) | DeepGemm warmup ignores auto-disable |
| **CUDA graphs** | ❌ **disabled** | 3 independent capture-unsafe code paths |
| **Speculative decoding (MTP)** | ❌ **disabled** | Requires CUDA graphs; also broken by eager-mode overhead |
| FP8 kernel tuning | ⚠️ sub-optimal | No tuned configs for Blackwell workstation GPU |
| Cooperative kernel launch | ⚠️ fallback | `cooperative_topk` cluster launch rejected |

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| **vLLM** | 0.24.0 |
| **Models tested** | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8` |
| **Hardware** | 2× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (96 GB each), TP=2 |
| **GPU architecture** | SM120 / compute capability 12.0 (`cap.major == 12`) |
| **Driver** | 595.71.05 (open kernel module) |
| **CUDA** | 13.0 (toolkit & runtime) |
| **PyTorch** | 2.11.0+cu130 |
| **Triton** | 3.6.0 |
| **flashinfer-python** | 0.6.14 (git `main`, not released) |
| **Python** | 3.12 |
| **OS** | Ubuntu 24.04 |

---

## All Issues (chronological by discovery)

### [Generic] Issue 1 — DeepGemm warmup ignores auto-disable flag

**Affects:** All models on Blackwell where DeepGemm is auto-disabled (Qwen3.6-27B, possibly others)

**Symptom:** Server crashes during DeepGemm warmup despite auto-disable being triggered:
```
RuntimeError: Assertion error (.../deepgemm-src/csrc/apis/../jit_kernels/impls/../heuristics/../../utils/layout.hpp:76): Unknown recipe
```

**Root cause:** vLLM correctly detects the model/hardware combo and sets `quant_config.use_deep_gemm = False`, but the warmup code checks `envs.VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM` (env var, defaults to `True`) instead of the config flag.

**Workaround:** `export VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`

**Code paths:**
- `vllm/config/vllm.py:925` — sets config flag
- `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py:33` — auto-detection logic
- `vllm/model_executor/warmup/deep_gemm_warmup.py` — only checks env var

---

### [DeepSeek-V4] Issue 2 — `--kv-cache-dtype auto` not auto-resolved on SM120

**Symptom:** Crash with unhelpful assertion:
```
AssertionError: DeepseekV4 fp8_ds_mla layout only supports fp8 kv-cache, got auto
```

**Root cause:** SM120 path in `flashinfer_sparse.py` validator rejects `"auto"` (SM100 accepts it). Then `attention.py` asserts `kv_cache_dtype.startswith("fp8")` without auto-resolving `"auto"` → `"fp8_ds_mla"` first.

**Workaround:** `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`

**Code paths:**
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py` — SM120 validator
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py` — dtype resolver

---

### [DeepSeek-V4] Issue 3 — CUTLASS `CutlassFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` is SM90-only

**Symptom:**
```
RuntimeError: CUTLASS C3x block-scaled FP8 GEMM requires SM90 (got SM120)
```

**Root cause:** The FP8 block-scaled kernel selector picks the CUTLASS c3x kernel (SM90 only) on SM120.

**Workaround:** `export VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=CutlassFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`

**Code path:** `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py` — kernel selector

---

### [DeepSeek-V4] Issue 4 — Triton FP8 fallback missing `float8_e8m0fnu` dtype mapping

**Symptom (after Issue 3 workaround):**
```
KeyError: 'float8_e8m0fnu'
  at vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py
```

**Root cause:** Triton block-scaled FP8 fallback has a dtype lookup dict missing `torch.float8_e8m0fnu` (the E8M0 scale dtype used by Blackwell FP8 block-scale).

**Workaround (patch):** Add `float8_e8m0fnu` mapping to dtype dict in `fp8_utils.py`.

---

### [DeepSeek-V4] Issue 5 — DeepGEMM `fp8_einsum` for `o_proj` asserts on SM120

**Symptom:**
```
Assertion error ... Unsupported architecture (DeepGEMM fp8 einsum) — SM120
```

**Root cause:** `o_proj` uses DeepGEMM `fp8_einsum` kernel (SM90/SM100 only).

**Workaround (patch):** Pure-torch FP8→bf16 einsum fallback on SM120 in `o_proj.py`.

---

### [DeepSeek-V4] Issue 6 — DSA indexer DeepGEMM MQA-logits kernels assert on SM120

**Symptom:**
```
Assertion error ... deepgemm-src/.../attention.hpp:219 — Unsupported architecture
```

**Root cause:** `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` / `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` kernels only support SM90/SM100.

**Workaround (patch):** Route SM120 (`cap.major == 12`) to pure-torch reference implementations in `deep_gemm.py`.

---

### [DeepSeek-V4] Issue 7 — FlashInfer separated sparse-MLA API not in released version

**Symptom:**
```
TypeError: trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4() got an unexpected keyword argument 'swa_topk_lens'
```

**Root cause:** vLLM 0.24.0's SM120 DeepSeek-V4 path was written against unreleased flashinfer `main`. Released versions (0.6.12, 0.6.13, all nightlies) lack the separated API (`swa_topk_lens`, `extra_sparse_indices`, etc.).

**Workaround:** Install flashinfer from git `main` (0.6.14) + `export FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1`

**Code path:** `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py`

---

### [DeepSeek-V4] Issue 8 — `cooperative_topk` cluster launch rejected on SM120

**Symptom:**
```
RuntimeError: launch_cooperative_cluster, cooperative_topk launch failed: invalid argument
```

**Root cause:** Thread-block-cluster (cooperative launch) kernel in `cooperative_topk.cu` is rejected on SM120.

**Workaround (patch):** Exclude SM120 from `use_cooperative_topk` gate → falls back to `persistent_topk`.

**Code path:** `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py`

---

### [DeepSeek-V4 / General] Issue 9 — CUDA graph capture broken on SM120 (3 independent blockers)

**Symptom:** All attempts to capture CUDA graphs on SM120 fail with cascading errors. Three independent blockers must be resolved before graphs work:

#### 9a. Custom all-reduce kernel crash (first blocker)
```
Failed: Cuda error /workspace/csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:455 'invalid argument'
```
The custom TP all-reduce kernel uses IPC memory handles that fail on SM120. Workaround: `--disable-custom-all-reduce` (forces NCCL). **This alone does not resolve the issue.**

#### 9b. `breakable_cudagraph.py` has host sync during capture (second blocker)
```
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation not permitted when stream is capturing
  at vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py:383
     seq_len = int(context_lens[i].item())
```
Even with `--disable-custom-all-reduce`, the **breakable CUDA graph capture code itself** contains a `.item()` host sync during capture, which is illegal. This is in `breakable_cudagraph.py`, **not** in the model-specific attention code.

#### 9c. DSA indexer torch fallback not capturable (third blocker)
```
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation not permitted when stream is capturing
  at vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py:290
     seq_len = int(context_lens[i].item())
```
The DSA indexer's pure-torch fallback (used on SM120 since DeepGEMM kernels aren't available) has a per-batch `.item()` GPU→CPU sync that is illegal during capture.

**Workaround:** `--enforce-eager` (disables CUDA graphs entirely)

**Impact without CUDA graphs:**
- No decode graph replay → full kernel launch overhead every step
- No MTP speculative decoding (see Issue 10)
- Reduced decode throughput by ~30-50%

**Code paths:**
- `vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py:383` — capture-unsafe `.item()` call
- `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py:290` — DSA indexer `.item()` call
- `vllm/custom_all_reduce.cuh:455` — SM120-incompatible IPC kernel

---

### [DeepSeek-V4] Issue 10 — MTP speculative decoding unusable without CUDA graphs

**Symptom:** MTP degrades throughput by ~60% (14 tok/s → ~5 tok/s) with `--enforce-eager`.

**Root cause:** MTP requires CUDA graph capture for efficiency (multiple tiny forward passes per step). Without graphs, each draft step pays full kernel launch overhead, making verification more expensive than greedy decoding.

**This is a downstream consequence of Issue 9.** MTP would likely work correctly once CUDA graphs are fixed for SM120.

**Workaround:** MTP disabled (commented out in launch config)

---

### [DeepSeek-V4] Issue 11 — Single request OOM crashes entire EngineCore

**Symptom:** One request's CUDA OOM crashes the whole server:
```
(Worker) OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 7.16 GiB.
(EngineCore) KeyError: 'chatcmpl-8fdb9f0ace8bc10f-a4e2d759'
```

**Root cause:** When a worker fails a request (OOM or other error), `scheduler.update_from_output` looks up the request ID and raises `KeyError` because it was already removed/aborted. The unhandled `KeyError` kills EngineCore.

**Workaround (mitigates trigger, not fix):** `export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` + `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`

**Code paths:**
- `vllm/v1/engine/core.py:605` — `step_with_batch_queue`
- `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` — `update_from_output` request lookup

---

### [Performance] Issue 12 — No tuned FP8 kernel configs for Blackwell workstation

**Symptom:** Warning on every FP8 GEMM shape:
```
Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config. Performance might be sub-optimal!
Config file not found at .../configs/N=1536,K=4096,device_name=NVIDIA_RTX_PRO_6000_Blackwell_Workstation_Edition,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128,128].json
```

6 shapes have no tuned config for RTX PRO 6000. vLLM falls back to a conservative default tiling.

**Impact:** ~5-10% prefill throughput loss (decode impact lower since MoE experts use FP4/MARLIN).

**Workaround:** None currently — requires running Triton kernel benchmarking on the target hardware.

**Code path:** `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py` → `get_w8a8_block_fp8_configs()`

---

### [System] Issue 13 — Orphaned child workers after parent `vllm serve` death

**Symptom:** After an abrupt vLLM shutdown or crash, child worker processes (`VLLM::Worker_TP0`, `VLLM::Worker_TP1`, `VLLM::EngineCore`) get re-parented to init (PPID=1) and continue holding ~38 GiB VRAM per GPU. The next launch fails with:
```
Free memory on device cuda:0 (56/95 GiB) ... less than desired GPU memory utilization
```

**Root cause:** `pkill -f "vllm serve"` only kills the parent API server. Worker processes have different cmdline patterns and are not killed by the model-specific grep.

**Workaround:** Custom teardown script that (1) kills parent, (2) reaps orphaned workers (PPID=1), (3) waits for VRAM to drop, (4) escalates to SIGKILL.

**Expected:** vLLM should register process group cleanup handlers or use SIGTERM/SIGKILL propagation via process groups.

---

## Summary of all workarounds required

### Environment variables (5)
```bash
# Skip DeepGemm warmup for models where it's auto-disabled
export VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0

# Disable SM90-only CUTLASS kernel
export VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=CutlassFp8BlockScaledMMKernel

# Reduce CUDA allocator fragmentation
export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True

# Use flashinfer git main (unreleased) for separated sparse-MLA API
export FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1

# Compile settings for torch.compile (32-core CPU)
export TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=32
export PYTORCH_TENSOREXPR_THREADS=32
```

### Code patches (4)
1. **`fp8_utils.py`** — Add `float8_e8m0fnu` dtype mapping for Triton fallback
2. **`o_proj.py`** — Pure-torch einsum fallback on SM120
3. **`deep_gemm.py`** — Route SM120 DSA indexer to torch reference implementations
4. **`sparse_attn_indexer.py`** — Exclude SM120 from `use_cooperative_topk`

### Launch flags required
```bash
--kv-cache-dtype fp8          # Issue 2
--enforce-eager               # Issue 9 (all three sub-issues)
# MTP NOT usable: requires CUDA graphs (Issue 10)
```

### What's disabled
- ❌ CUDA graphs (all three sub-issues in #9)
- ❌ MTP speculative decoding (Issue 10, requires CUDA graphs)
- ❌ Custom all-reduce (Issue 9a, uses NCCL fallback)
- ⚠️ FP8 kernel tuning (Issue 12, uses conservative defaults)

---

## What works (with workarounds)

With all workarounds applied, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` serves successfully on 2× RTX PRO 6000 at TP=2:
- ✅ Model loading (FP4 MoE + FP8 attention)
- ✅ Inference with coherent output
- ✅ Prefix caching
- ✅ Tool calling and reasoning parser
- ✅ DeepSeek Sparse Attention (via torch fallback)
- ✅ 256K context length
- ✅ Multi-user concurrency (max-num-seqs 4+)
- ✅ FlashInfer FP8 indexer cache

**Achieved throughput:** ~14 tokens/sec per stream (decode, 256K context, max-num-seqs 4)

**Expected with CUDA graphs:** ~20-30+ tokens/sec (estimated based on H100/SM100 graphs vs. no-graphs overhead)

---

## Patched files (diff summary)

| File | Env | Changes |
|------|-----|---------|
| `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py` | vllm-dsv4 | Added `float8_e8m0fnu` Triton dtype mapping |
| `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py` | vllm-dsv4 | SM120 excluded from `use_cooperative_topk` |
| `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/o_proj.py` | vllm-dsv4 | Pure-torch einsum fallback on SM120 |
| `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py` | vllm-dsv4 | SM120 routed to torch reference MQA logits |
| `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` | vllm-dsv4 | DSA indexer compatibility fixes |

### Before submitting a new issue...

title: [Model] Add support for OpenPangu V2 model
body:
## Summary

This PR adds OpenPangu V2 support on vLLM, including model registration, OpenPangu V2-specific MLA/static-sink attention paths, MoME short-convolution state handling, mHC execution support, OpenPangu MTP3 speculative decoding, and OpenPangu V2 tool/reasoning parsers.


## Major Changes

### OpenPangu V2 model support

- Registers `OpenPanguV2ForCausalLM` in the text generation model registry and supported model docs.
- Extends `vllm/model_executor/models/openpangu.py` with OpenPangu V2 execution paths:
  - `OpenPanguV2ForCausalLM` model class.
  - MLA attention path with static sink token support.
  - Optional MoME short-convolution modules on Q, compressed KV, and attention output.
  - Pangu sparse indexer integration based on DeepSeek indexer behavior.
  - mHC module support for multi-stream pre/post mixing and final head merge.
  - Weight-loading remaps for MoME convolution weights and indexer FP8 weights.
- Adds model config validation for OpenPangu V2 sliding-window alignment by computing `max_sliding_window` from `sliding_window` and `sliding_window_list`.
- Adds `openpangu_v2` / `openpangu_mtp` handling in model architecture conversion and speculative decoding config.

### OpenPangu MTP3 / multi-head speculative decoding

- Adds `OpenPanguV2MTPProposer` for OpenPangu MTP speculative decoding.
- Supports multi-head MTP when the draft config has `n_predict > 1`, including MTP3-style `num_speculative_tokens > 1` decoding.
- Dispatches each speculative step to the corresponding OpenPangu MTP layer and computes logits with the matching `spec_step_idx`.
- Supports MTP layers that span multiple KV cache groups. The proposer tracks per-group block tables, slot_mappings, and meatadata builders so each draft layer uses the correct KVcache group.
- Adds `multi_mtp_target_tokens_ids_cache` and `multi_mtp_target_hidden_states_cache` for the multi-head MTP path.
  - These caches are used to preserve the corrected target token ids and hidden states after draft-token rejection. Without them, later MTP heads may continue from stale target inputs, causing draft KV cache misalignment and lower acceptance rate.
- Corrects positions, slot mappings, sequence lengths, accepted-token metadata, and MoME draft metadata after rejected speculative tokens.
- Adds dummy-run support for multi-head MTP CUDAGraph capture.
- Prepares padded next-token inputs for multiple MTP heads using current sequence lengths.
- Updates speculative config so `num_speculative_tokens > 1` no longer emits the generic slow-path warning when the MTP draft config exposes `n_predict > 1`.

### MoME KV cache and metadata support

- Adds `SlidingWindowMomeSpec`, a sliding-window MLA-compatible KV cache spec for three MoME state components: Q state, compressed-KV state, and output state.
- Registers `SlidingWindowMomeSpec` with the `SlidingWindowManager`.
- Updates GPU model runner KV-cache tensor initialization so MoME state tensors are handled like Mamba-style multi-state caches while still being excluded from normal attention cache setup.
- Adds `MomeAttentionBackend` and `MomeAttentionMetadataBuilder` for:
  - decode-only, prefill-only, and mixed decode/prefill batches;
  - single-token prefills with prior state;
  - speculative decoding accepted-token metadata;
  - draft-mode accepted-token metadata for OpenPangu multi-head MTP;
  - decode-side computed-token and first-scheduled-block metadata needed by MTP KV correction;
  - full CUDAGraph decode padding;
  - block table updates after scheduling changes.
- Registers `vllm::mome_attention` as a splitting op for compilation.

### Static sink attention refactor

- Refactors static sink attention to use backend implementation overrides instead of a dedicated `SinkFullAttentionSpec` / `SinkFullAttentionManager`.
- Removes the old `SinkFullAttentionSpec` and `SinkFullAttentionManager`.
- Adds `StaticSinkMLAAttention` for MLA static sink use cases.
- Adds static-sink implementations for:
  - FlashAttentionDiffKVBackend;
  - FlashAttnMLABackend;
  - FlashMLASparseBackend.
- Merges sink-token attention results with normal attention results using LSE-aware state merging, supporting dense and sparse MLA paths, sliding-window paths, and chunked context paths where implemented.

### Kernel and indexing fixes

- Extends `causal_conv1d_fn` with `zero_initial_state_output` so MoME prefill output can zero the warmup region when there is no prior convolution state.
- Clamps DeepSeek V3.2 indexer decode sequence length offsets to avoid negative values.

### Tool and reasoning parser support

- Adds `OpenPanguV2ToolParser` and registers it as `openpangu_v2`.
- Supports OpenPangu V2 tool call tags:
  - `<|tool_call_start|>`
  - `<|tool_call_end|>`
- Handles non-streaming and streaming tool call extraction, including multiple tool calls and partial JSON streaming.
- Adds `OpenPanguV2ReasoningParser` and registers it as `openpangu_v2`.
- Selects DeepSeek R1-style reasoning parsing when `chat_template_kwargs.think` is enabled, otherwise uses identity parsing.

## Tests

New or updated tests cover:

- OpenPangu V2 tool parser registration, non-streaming extraction, malformed tool calls, and streaming edge cases.
- `MomeAttentionMetadataBuilder` behavior for decode, prefill, mixed batches, speculative decoding, CUDAGraph padding, and block table updates.
- `SlidingWindowMomeSpec` validation, cache-state shapes/dtypes, registry mapping, and uniformity behavior.
- `causal_conv1d_fn(zero_initial_state_output=True)` behavior against reference output.
- Model registry entry for `OpenPanguV2ForCausalLM`.

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

title: [Bug]: IndexError in DeepSeek-V4 MTP module when using TP=16
body:
### Your current environment

### Issue

**Title:** [Bug] IndexError in DeepSeek-V4 MTP module when using TP=16

**Description:**
I am encountering a crash when loading the DeepSeek-V4 model with speculative decoding enabled in a 16-card H100 (multi-node) setup with `tensor-parallel-size=16`.

**Environment:**

* vLLM version: 0.24.0 (latest)
* Model: DeepSeek-V4
* Hardware: 2 nodes, 16x H100 GPUs
* Configuration: `tensor-parallel-size=16`, `enable-chunked-prefill=True` (or standard decoding), speculative decoding enabled.

**Error Log:**
The error occurs during `load_weights` in `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/mtp.py`.

```text
  File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/mtp.py", line 397, in load_weights
    weight_loader(param, loaded_weight, shard_id)
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py", line 905, in weight_loader_v2
    param.load_merged_column_weight(...)
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/parameter.py", line 172, in load_merged_column_weight
    loaded_weight = loaded_weight.narrow(...)
IndexError: start out of range (expected to be in range of [-24, 24], but got 26)
# OR
RuntimeError: start (24) + length (2) exceeds dimension size (24).

```

**Context:**
The issue appears to be a logic error in the MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) weight sharding implementation. It seems the code fails to correctly calculate the tensor dimensions when the model is sharded across 16 GPUs, leading to an index out of bounds during the `narrow()` operation. It likely assumes a fixed dimension size that is incompatible with the TP=16 split.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

1. Setup a multi-node environment with 16x H100 GPUs.
2. Launch vLLM with `tensor-parallel-size=16` and a target DeepSeek-V4 model.
3. Enable speculative decoding.
4. Model fails to initialize during the weight loading phase.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

.

title: [Feature] implement return indexer topk of sparse attention

## Purpose
Add an `--enable-return-indexer-topk` flag to vLLM that surfaces per-token
sparse-attention top-k indices (the KV slots selected by the indexer layer)
back to the client alongside generated tokens. This mirrors the existing
`--enable-return-routed-experts` flag and follows the same capture →
D2H → slot-indexed-persist → API-encode pipeline.

please see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47280， new PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49555
## Test Plan

```bash

    --enable-return-indexer-topk ...
```

```python
class SamplingParams:
    indexer_topk_prompt_start: int = 0
    # Skip the first N prompt tokens from the returned topk. In multi-turn
    # agent scenarios, set to the length of the already-returned prefix to
    # avoid duplicating topk for prompt tokens covered by earlier turns.
```

}
