title: [Bugfix] DeepSeek V3.2/V4: drop whitespace content deltas around too…
body:
[Bugfix] DeepSeek V3.2/V4: drop whitespace delta.content around tool_calls in streaming

  ▎ Suggested branch: bugfix/deepseek-tool-parser-whitespace-content
  ▎ Target branch: main
  ▎ PR title (≤ 70 chars): [Bugfix] DeepSeek V3.2/V4: drop whitespace content around tool_calls

  Summary

  When streaming tool calls with the DeepSeek V3.2 / V4 tool parser
  (DeepSeekV32EngineToolParser / DeepSeekV4EngineToolParser), the parser
  engine can emit whitespace-only delta.content chunks immediately before
  and after the tool_calls delta:

  delta.content       = "\n\n"
  delta.tool_calls    = [...]
  delta.content       = "\n"
  delta.finish_reason = "tool_calls"

  The OpenAI streaming contract expects content to be null in any chunk
  associated with tool_calls. Downstream routers that translate OpenAI
  streams into Anthropic Messages streams (e.g. claude-code-router) reject
  these chunks with:

  API Error: Content block is not a text block

  because the active content block has already switched to tool_use, and
  a text-content delta cannot be appended to it.

  Reproduction

  - vLLM serving deepseek-v4 with --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 and
  streaming enabled.
  - Client: claude-code + claude-code-router proxying to vLLM.
  - Prompt: any tool-using turn (e.g. "看下今天的天气" with a get_weather tool).
  - Observed: plain-chat turns succeed; the first tool-using turn fails with
  Content block is not a text block because the vLLM stream contains
  delta.content = "\n\n" ahead of delta.tool_calls = [...] and
  another delta.content = "\n" immediately after.

  Minimal Python reproducer using the mock-tokenizer test fixture:

  chunks = [
      "Sure, let me check.",                    # legitimate text
      "\n\n",                                   # whitespace right before tool
      "<｜DSML｜tool_calls>...</｜DSML｜tool_calls>",
      "\n",                                     # whitespace right after tool
  ]
  # On main, deltas[1].content == "\n\n" and deltas[3].content == "\n"

  Root cause

  In vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine.py::_events_to_delta the streaming
  path uses _content_has_nonws as a fast-path guard: once any
  non-whitespace content has been emitted, the whitespace-drop / deferral
  logic is skipped for the rest of the stream:

  if self._content_has_nonws:
      pass                              # <-- whitespace slips through here
  elif content_str:
      stripped = content_str.strip()
      if stripped:
          self._content_has_nonws = True
      elif self._tool_slots:
          if self._drop_ws_only_content_before_tools:
              content_str = ""
      elif not finished:
          self._deferred_content = content_str
          content_str = ""

  DeepSeek V3.2/V4 reliably emit \n\n before <｜DSML｜tool_calls> and
  \n after </｜DSML｜tool_calls>. As soon as the model has produced any
  real content (or a chat template surfaces some), _content_has_nonws
  becomes True and those trailing/leading whitespace fragments are
  forwarded as delta.content — some of them landing in the same delta as
  tool_calls, and some landing after the tool_use block has already been
  opened downstream.

  Fix

  Add an opt-in config knob and use it only for DeepSeek V3.2 / V4:

  1. ParserEngineConfig — new field, default False, no effect on
  any existing parser:
  drop_whitespace_only_content_after_nonws: bool = False
  2. ParserEngine._events_to_delta — when the flag is True, keep
  applying the whitespace drop/defer step even after
  _content_has_nonws has flipped:
    - if _tool_slots are already populated → drop the whitespace
  (reuses drop_whitespace_only_content_before_tools);
    - else if not yet finished → defer via _deferred_content so that
  legitimate text arriving in a later chunk still preserves its
  leading whitespace, while tool_calls arriving instead will cause
  the deferred whitespace to be dropped.
  3. vllm/parser/deepseek_v32.py / vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py —
  set the new flag to True in deepseek_v32_config() and
  deepseek_v4_config().

  Non-streaming (extract_tool_calls) was already correct and is
  untouched.

  Scope

  Intentionally minimal and DeepSeek-only:

  - The new config flag defaults to False, so every other parser
  (Kimi K2, Qwen3, Gemma4, MinimaxM2, Mistral, Hermes, Llama, GLM,
  Granite, …) sees zero behavior change.
  - DeepSeek V3 and V3.1 use their own non–ParserEngine implementations
  and are not touched.
  - Only V3.2 and V4 configs opt in.

  Verified via config introspection:

  kimi_k2                              drop_whitespace_only_content_after_nonws=False
  qwen3                                drop_whitespace_only_content_after_nonws=False
  gemma4                               drop_whitespace_only_content_after_nonws=False
  minimax_m2                           drop_whitespace_only_content_after_nonws=False
  deepseek_v32                         drop_whitespace_only_content_after_nonws=True   <-- fix active
  deepseek_v4 (thinking=False)         drop_whitespace_only_content_after_nonws=True   <-- fix active
  deepseek_v4 (thinking=True)          drop_whitespace_only_content_after_nonws=True   <-- fix active

  A structurally similar issue may exist in ~27 other Python tool parsers;
  they are out of scope for this PR to keep the diff reviewable. A
  follow-up issue can enumerate them so the cleanup can be split into
  per-parser PRs.

  Duplicate-work checks

  gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open \
    --search "deepseek tool parser whitespace"
  gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open \
    --search "Content block is not a text block"
  gh issue list --repo vllm-project/vllm \
    --search "tool_calls content whitespace"

  Tests

  Added regression tests that fail on main and pass on this branch:

  - tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py — new class
  TestStreamingWhitespaceAroundToolCalls:
    - test_no_whitespace_content_before_tool_call
    - test_no_whitespace_content_after_tool_call
    - test_no_whitespace_content_around_tool_call_chunked
    - test_tool_calls_chunk_has_no_content — asserts the OpenAI
  contract: chunks carrying tool_calls have content=None or
  non-whitespace content.
    - test_real_text_before_tool_call_still_streamed — regression
  guard: legitimate leading text is preserved.
  - tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py:
    - test_streaming_no_whitespace_content_around_tool_call
    - test_streaming_no_ws_content_when_tool_starts_no_prior_content
    - test_streaming_ws_content_dropped_when_all_in_one_chunk
    - test_streaming_real_text_around_tool_call_preserved
    - test_streaming_trailing_whitespace_preserved_in_plain_chat —
  regression guard: trailing whitespace in a plain chat (no tool
  call) is still flushed on finish.

  Commands run:

  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py -v
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py -v
  pre-commit run --files \
    vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine_config.py \
    vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine.py \
    vllm/parser/deepseek_v32.py \
    vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py \
    tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py \
    tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py

  Results (locally, with mock tokenizer):

  tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py   48 → 53 passed
  tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py    11 → 16 passed

title: Add FP8 W8A8 Block kernel configs for NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090D
body:
# Add FP8 W8A8 Block Kernel Configs for NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090D

## Problem

RTX 4090D is the most widely adopted 48GB AI accelerator in the Chinese market, yet vllm currently has **zero** tuned FP8 kernel configs for this GPU. Every 4090D user sees:

```
Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config. Performance might be sub-optimal!
```

## Solution

This PR adds **13 pre-tuned W8A8 Block FP8 kernel configs** for `NVIDIA_GeForce_RTX_4090_D`, autotuned on 4× RTX 4090D hardware.

### Config Coverage

| N | K | M-dimensions tuned |
|---|---|---|
| 256 | 7168 | 2048, 3072, 4096 |
| 576 | 7168 | 2048, 3072, 4096 |
| 1536 | 1536 | 2048, 3072, 4096 |
| 1536 | 7168 | 2048, 3072, 4096 |
| 2048 | 512 | 2048, 3072, 4096 |
| 2304 | 7168 | 2048, 3072, 4096 |
| 7168 | 128 | 2048, 3072, 4096 |
| 7168 | 1024 | 2048, 3072, 4096 |
| 7168 | 1152 | 2048, 3072, 4096 |
| 7168 | 16384 | 2048, 3072, 4096 |
| 7168 | 18432 | 2048, 3072, 4096 |
| 24576 | 7168 | 2048, 3072, 4096 |
| 32768 | 512 | 2048, 3072, 4096 |

Key shapes covered:
- **N=7168, K=16384** — DeepSeek V4 attention projections
- **N=24576, K=7168** — Large MLP intermediate projections
- 7 of 13 (N,K) combinations are **entirely new** to vllm's config directory

## Verification

- Generated via SGLang/KT autotune on 4× RTX 4090D
- Each config file matches vllm's expected format: `N={N},K={K},device_name=NVIDIA_GeForce_RTX_4090_D,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128,128].json`
- Config loading path: `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/configs/`
- Device name matches `torch.cuda.get_device_name()` output: `NVIDIA_GeForce_RTX_4090_D`

title: [Bugfix] Fix ZeroDivisionError when Dynamic SD schedule includes K=0 for DSpark draft cudagraph capture
body:
## Purpose

Dynamic Speculative Decoding (DSD) allows `num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size` entries with `K=0`, meaning no draft tokens at high concurrency. When initializing CUDA graph candidates, `CudaGraphManager._init_candidates()` expands each schedule entry into a decode query length via:

`decode_query_len = K + (manager.decode_query_len - config.num_speculative_tokens)`

For **DSpark with anchor-as-first** (DeepSeek V4 default), the draft `DFlashCudaGraphManager` passes `decode_query_len = num_query_per_req = K_max`, so the recovered bonus term is **0**. A schedule entry with `K=0` therefore yields **`decode_query_len = 0`**, and `round_up(num_tokens, 0)` raises `ZeroDivisionError` during worker startup (e.g. `DFlashCudaGraphManager` init for DSpark).

This does not affect DFlash / 1+N layouts, where the bonus term is 1 and `K=0` maps to `qlen=1`.

**Fix:** Skip DSD schedule entries whose computed decode query length is `<= 0`. `K=0` disables drafting, so no draft FULL decode graph is needed for that shape. Target-model capture is unchanged (`K=0` still maps to `qlen=1` there).

**Test:** Add `test_dynamic_sd_skips_zero_draft_tokens_in_cudagraph_schedule` covering the DSpark anchor-as-first case with a schedule containing `[97, 128, 0]`.
## TEST

Environment: 4× H100
Test set: HumanEval
Command:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7 \
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
vllm serve /models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark/ \
--trust-remote-code \
--tensor-parallel-size 4 \
--kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
--max-num-batched-tokens 10240 \
--max-num-seqs 128 \
--block-size 256 \
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
--max-model-len 32768 \
--speculative-config '{
  "method": "dspark",
  "num_speculative_tokens": 16,
  "num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size": [
   xxxx
  ]
}'
```


Benchmarked decode under three Dynamic SD schedules (`num_speculative_tokens=16`, `max-num-seqs=64`), sweeping batch size 1 vs 64:

**Schedule A — fixed K=16**

```json
"num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size": [
  [1, 32, 16],
  [33, 64, 16]
]
```

| batch | output_throughput | mean_TPOT | mean_ITL |
|------:|------------------:|----------:|---------:|
| 1     | 325.88            | 2.44      | 11.95    |
| 64    | 381.04            | 148.34    | 526.32   |

**Schedule B — K=16 low concurrency, K=6 high concurrency**

```json
"num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size": [
  [1, 32, 16],
  [33, 64, 6]
]
```

| batch | output_throughput | mean_TPOT | mean_ITL |
|------:|------------------:|----------:|---------:|
| 1     | 314.33            | 2.49      | 11.88    |
| 64    | 525.50            | 107.42    | 346.51   |

**Schedule C — K=16 low concurrency, K=0 high concurrency**

```json
"num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size": [
  [1, 32, 16],
  [33, 64, 0]
]
```

| batch | output_throughput | mean_TPOT | mean_ITL |
|------:|------------------:|----------:|---------:|
| 1     | 307.23            | 2.57      | 11.95    |
| 64    | 882.42            | 43.54     | 51.24    |

title: [Bugfix] Disable custom all-reduce on consumer Blackwell (sm_12x)
body:
## Purpose

Auto-disable vLLM's custom all-reduce on **consumer Blackwell (sm_12x)** and fall back to NCCL all-reduce.

The custom all-reduce CUDA kernels are only built and tuned for sm_90 / sm_100 (see `CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES`, which lists 9.0/10.0/10.3 but no 12.x). On consumer Blackwell (sm_120 / sm_121 — RTX PRO 6000, RTX 50-series, GB10/DGX Spark) the kernel's IPC / peer-mapping path aborts with `custom_all_reduce.cuh:455 'invalid argument'` during cudagraph capture, killing the TP worker.

The existing topology guards don't catch this: they only disable custom all-reduce for **more than two** PCIe-only GPUs, so a 2-GPU tensor-parallel setup passes the checks, enables the kernel, and then crashes at capture. Today users must pass `--disable-custom-all-reduce` manually.

This gates on the whole 12.x family via the existing `current_platform.is_device_capability_family(120)` helper (extracted into `CustomAllreduce._is_unsupported_arch()` for testability). sm_100 (datacenter Blackwell), Hopper, Ada, and Ampere are unaffected.

Fixes the "Issue 9a — Custom all-reduce kernel crash" blocker reported in #47266. (That report also lists 9b/9c as further, independent cudagraph-capture blockers on sm_120; this PR addresses 9a only.)

## Test Plan

- Unit test (no GPU required): `pytest tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py -k is_unsupported_arch` — asserts the sm_12x family is disabled, other CUDA archs stay enabled, and non-CUDA platforms are not gated.
- End-to-end on 2× RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120), TP=2, **without** `--disable-custom-all-reduce`:
  `vllm serve <model> --tensor-parallel-size 2` and confirm the warning fires, FULL cudagraph capture completes without the `custom_all_reduce.cuh:455` crash, and the server serves.

## Test Result

- `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean (v0.14.0, repo config); `mypy` (3.10 and 3.12) pass.
- Unit test: 3/3 pass.
- End-to-end (2× RTX PRO 6000, sm_120, TP=2, no manual flag; `disable_custom_all_reduce=False` in engine config):
  - Warning fired on both TP workers: `Custom allreduce is disabled because it is not supported on consumer Blackwell (sm_12x ...); falling back to NCCL all-reduce.`
  - `Capturing CUDA graphs (mixed prefill-decode, PIECEWISE)` and `(decode, FULL)` both completed; `Graph capturing finished` — **no `custom_all_reduce.cuh:455` crash** (the failure this PR fixes).
  - `Application startup complete`; `/health` → 200; a `/v1/completions` request returned a correct response over the NCCL fallback path.

## Notes

- **AI assistance:** this change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.
- **Not a duplicate:** no open PR modifies `custom_all_reduce.py` for sm_12x (the SM12x enablement PR #41834 does not touch it); this is orthogonal to the DeepSeek-V4 `fp8_ds_mla` work in #47716.

title: [ROCm][MLA][Perf] Fuse decode QK-RoPE + Q-concat + KV-concat + KV-cache write for sparse MLA
body: ## Summary On ROCm, the sparse-MLA decode path currently runs the per-layer Q/KV preparation as several back-to-back ops: main RoPE on `q_pe`/`k_pe`, the query concat (`ql_nope` + RoPE'd `q_pe`), the KV concat, and the fp8 KV-cache write. This PR collapses all of them into the single AITER kernel `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla`. The fusion is implemented at the **model level** (eager op dispatch from the MLA layer), **not** as an FX graph-rewrite pass since vLLM is moving away from the graph-pass fusion mechanism, and several models already adopt the model-level eager approach. Implementing it this way keeps this change aligned with the current direction, and makes it easily portable to that new model-level mechanism. The fusion is gated and falls back cleanly to the existing split-kernel path when it is not applicable (non-ROCm, non-gfx9, no AITER, non-fp8 KV cache, the `fp8_ds_mla` layout). Before: After: Three coordinated decision sites, all keyed off one impl flag (`ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl.use_fused_qk_rope_cache`): 1. **Wrapper (`mla.py`)** — when fusing, skip the in-place main RoPE and pass raw (pre-RoPE) `q_pe`/`k_pe` down, threading `positions` as a real argument. 2. **KV write (`ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl.do_kv_cache_update`)** — no-op when fusing (the write is folded into the fused kernel; the sparse path routes *all* tokens through `forward_mqa`, so `num_mqa_tokens == q.size(0)` and the fused call writes the full batch's KV, prefill included). 3. **Decode (`MLAAttention.forward_impl`)** — after the `W_UK` bmm, call the fused kernel to produce the pre-fused `q` and write the cache. ### Why `positions` is a real argument (not a forward-context stash) `positions` is threaded through `MLAAttention.forward` → the opaque custom op (`unified_mla_attention_with_output`) / direct `forward_impl` → the fused kernel, as an optional trailing tensor argument. An earlier stash into `forward_context.additional_kwargs` inside the wrapper's `forward` proved **not** to be torch.compile / CUDA-graph safe. ## Compatibility / no-effect cases - **deepseek-v4** is unaffected: it uses its own standalone stack (`DeepseekV4ROCMAiterMLAAttention` / `DeepseekV4ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend`, registry tag `ROCM_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4`) with its own `forward_mqa` and cache write — it never touches `MLAAttention`, `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl`, `do_kv_cache_update`, or the fused flag. - **deepseek-v3.2 / GLM sparse** on ROCm run through the shared, modified path and are the intended beneficiaries. - **DeepseekV32Attention (nvidia)** fully overrides `forward`; base MLA path untouched. - **Dense MLA / CUDA / non-fp8 / `fp8_ds_mla`** all miss the gate → byte-for-byte unchanged. - **Spec-decode / MTP drafters** reuse the same `MLAAttention` layers, so the `positions` argument covers them too. - **`positions`** added as an optional trailing param (`Tensor?`) on `MLAAttention.forward`, `forward_impl`, and `unified_mla_attention_with_output` — backward compatible for every existing caller. - **Off-ROCm**: `_aiter_ops.py` registration is `@if_aiter_supported` (no-op); title: Fix KV offloading GSM8K eval: prefix caching, CPU reload verification, device fit
body:
Fixes for #46893 — addresses @orozery's review and the failing `lm-eval-kv-offload-*` steps.

- Enable prefix caching and reset the GPU prefix cache between passes (`POST /reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=false`) so pass 2 must reload KV from CPU. Without it, hybrid models crash at startup and `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` silently disables itself.
- Wait for `BlockStored(medium="CPU")` KV events before the reset so pass 2 never races the async offload (`OffloadingConnector`).
- Assert `vllm:external_prefix_cache_{queries,hits}` deltas to verify loading actually occurred (both connectors).
- Fix device fit: Qwen3.5-35B → 2xH100 (TP=2), DeepSeek-V4-Flash → 4xH100 (TP=4); both OOMed on the current devices.
- Widen `source_file_dependencies` to cover `vllm/v1/kv_offload/` and the simple connector.

Qwen's 0.75 threshold needs a baseline from the first green run.

title: [Bug]: MXFP4 MoE Marlin fallback crashes with illegal memory access on Hopper (DeepSeek V4, TP+EP) — non-tile-aligned intermediate size
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ### **Describe the bug** Serving DeepSeek V4 with tensor + expert parallelism on Hopper GPUs crashes during weight loading with a CUDA illegal memory access. The error surfaces asynchronously (at the next `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` call inside `DeviceMemoryProfiler`), meaning the traceback line is not the true fault site. The actual out-of-bounds access occurs earlier during the Marlin weight/scale repacking for the MoE layer (`ops.gptq_marlin_repack` or the scale permutation in `prepare_moe_mxfp4_layer_for_marlin`). ### **Traceback / Logs** ```text (Worker_TP7_EP7 pid=3823) ERROR ... torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered ... File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/marlin_utils_fp4.py", line 617, in prepare_moe_mxfp4_layer_for_marlin File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/marlin_utils_fp4.py", line 611, in permute_scales marlin_scales = mxfp4_marlin_process_scales(...) File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/marlin_utils_fp4.py", line 120, in mxfp4_marlin_process_scales marlin_scales = marlin_scales.view(-1, 4)[:, [0, 2, 1, 3]].view(...) torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered ``` ### **Root cause** 1. **Fallback Path:** Because Hopper GPUs lack native MXFP4 tensor-core support, `_get_priority_backends()` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py` falls through DeepGEMM/FlashInfer (which require SM100+) down to the `MARLIN` weight-only fallback for MXFP4 MoE. 2. **Alignment Requirement:** The Marlin GEMM/repack kernels require `N`/`K` dimensions to be tile-aligned (multiples of 64 or 128). 3. **Missing Padding:** Under expert parallelism (EP), the per-rank intermediate size (`intermediate_size_per_partition`) is not guaranteed to satisfy this alignment. However, `prepare_moe_mxfp4_layer_for_marlin` performs no padding before calling `ops.gptq_marlin_repack` / `marlin_permute_scales`—unlike its NVFP4 sibling. A recent fix, **#45295** *("[Kernel] Consolidate Marlin thread-tile padding across all dense Marlin paths")*, successfully added this zero-padding to: * `prepare_fp4_layer_for_marlin` (dense/linear NVFP4) * `prepare_nvfp4_moe_layer_for_marlin` (NVFP4 MoE) However, it did **not** update `prepare_moe_mxfp4_layer_for_marlin` (the MXFP4 MoE variant). The code still assumes the incoming weight shape is already tile-aligned per its own comments: > *"Derive dimensions from actual weight shapes to handle rounded/padded sizes correctly... e.g. Mxfp4MoEMethod rounds up hidden_dim"* For DeepSeek V4 under EP, that assumption does not hold, and the unaligned repack triggers the illegal memory access. This belongs to the same bug class as **#38022** *("Marlin MoE kernel fails with MXFP4-quantized GPT-OSS 20B — Invalid thread config for non-aligned dimensions")*. ### **Expected behavior** `prepare_moe_mxfp4_layer_for_marlin` should zero-pad the per-rank intermediate size to the nearest Marlin-tile-aligned boundary before repacking—exactly how `prepare_nvfp4_moe_layer_for_marlin` handles it. This will prevent MXFP4 MoE + Marlin fallback + EP setups from crashing on non-tile-aligned shard sizes. ### **Reproduction** Not easily reproducible with a minimal script as it requires an 8x Hopper GPU cluster and the DeepSeek V4 checkpoint. I am happy to help test and verify a fix against the original environment if a PR is put together. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [ROCm] Cache fp32 upcast of static e8m0 weight scale in AITER scaled_mm
body:
## Purpose

The e8m0 weight scale in the AITER block-scaled GEMM path is static, but
`apply_block_scaled_mm` re-runs the `<<23` bit-shift fp32 upcast plus
`.contiguous()` on it **every decode step, for every layer**, even though the
value never changes.

On DeepSeek-V4 FP4 (MI355X / gfx950) this shows up in profiles as ~3.5% of GPU
time split across `aten::__lshift__` and `direct_copy`.

This PR overrides `process_weights_after_loading` in `AiterFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`
to convert the e8m0 weight scale to fp32 once at model load time via
`replace_parameter`. The per-step activation scale (`As`) is dynamic and remains
handled in `apply_block_scaled_mm` unchanged.

## Test Plan

- DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4, TP8, MI355X, 1024/1024 decode sweep (conc 16–128).
- gsm8k 5-shot (full 1319 samples) accuracy parity check.
- Verify `__lshift__` / `direct_copy` ops disappear from the decode profile.

## Test Result

### Throughput / latency (8× MI355X, DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4)

8× MI355X (gfx950), TP=8 · DeepSeek-V4-Pro (FP4 MoE + FP8 attention), KV-cache fp8 · default fused AITER MoE · random ISL/OSL 1024/1024, num-prompts = 10×concurrency. Off → on = same base without / with this patch.

**Performance**

| concurrency | output tok/s (off → on) | Δ | mean TPOT ms (off → on) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16  | 542.48 → 590.22  | +8.8% | 28.10 → 26.02 | −7.4% |
| 32  | 937.39 → 1006.73 | +7.4% | 34.06 → 30.74 | −9.7% |
| 64  | 1504.27 → 1591.14 | +5.8% | 42.30 → 39.10 | −7.6% |
| 128 | 2295.98 → 2392.37 | +4.2% | 55.92 → 53.22 | −4.8% |

Note: median TTFT at c16 is dominated by request-queue scheduling noise (±38% run-to-run with no code change, confirmed via 3-pass repeatability on a warm server); TPOT and throughput are stable across repetitions.

**Accuracy — gsm8k 5-shot, full 1319 samples (exact_match)**

| | off | on |
|---|---|---|
| strict-match     | 0.9500 | 0.9484 |
| flexible-extract | 0.9500 | 0.9477 |

title: [ROCm] Use AITER topk_softplus for non-hash sqrtsoftplus MoE routing
body:
## Purpose

aiter's `topk_softplus` is a faster drop-in for the non-hash sqrtsoftplus
routing path (bias + sqrt(softplus) + top-k + optional renorm + scaling)
currently handled by `ops.topk_hash_softplus_sqrt` in
`vllm_topk_softplus_sqrt`.

It does **not** support hash routing (`input_tokens` / `hash_indices_table`),
so those layers fall through to the existing vLLM kernel unchanged. The fast
path is guarded on `rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled()`, int32 indices, and the
absence of hash-routing inputs.

## Test Plan

- DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4, TP8, MI355X decode.
- Numerical equivalence check vs. `ops.topk_hash_softplus_sqrt` for the
  non-hash case.

## Test Result

Numerically identical to the existing kernel for the non-hash case:
index match 100%, max top-k weight diff ~1.8e-7. gsm8k accuracy unchanged.

---
Draft — opened for early review. Part of a DeepSeek-V4 FP4 ROCm optimization set.

title: [Bug]: HY V3 (hy_v3) allocates router expert_bias in serving dtype, silently downcasting the checkpoint's float32 selection bias (DeepSeek models pin it to fp32)
body:
### Your current environment

Found by code inspection; the relevant logic is dtype-only and does not require a runtime environment to verify. Present on `main` @ 567a78432d8e (checked today) and in `v0.24.0`. Checkpoint-side evidence reproduced against `tencent/Hy3` on the HF Hub (header-only range request, snippet below).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`HYV3MoEFused` allocates the router selection bias without an explicit dtype:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/567a78432d8e/vllm/model_executor/models/hy_v3.py#L180

```python
self.expert_bias = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(config.num_experts))
```

Model construction runs under `set_default_torch_dtype(model_config.dtype)`, so in bf16/fp16 serving this parameter is allocated in the **serving dtype**. `load_weights` has no special handling for it — it falls through to `default_weight_loader` (hy_v3.py#L644), whose `param.data.copy_(loaded_weight)` **silently downcasts** the checkpoint tensor. There is also no `process_weights_after_loading` in `hy_v3.py` to fix it up afterward.

The checkpoint stores this tensor in float32 — it is the only non-BF16 weight in `tencent/Hy3`. Verified directly from the safetensors shard header:

```python
import json, urllib.request, struct
idx = json.load(open("model.safetensors.index.json"))
shard = idx["weight_map"]["model.layers.1.mlp.expert_bias"]  # model-00036-of-00099.safetensors
req = urllib.request.Request(f"https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy3/resolve/main/{shard}",
                             headers={"Range": "bytes=0-262143"})
data = urllib.request.urlopen(req).read()
hdr = json.loads(data[8:8 + struct.unpack("<Q", data[:8])[0]])
# → every 'model.layers.N.mlp.expert_bias' is ('F32', [192]); all 136 other tensors in the shard are BF16
```

This bias is DeepSeek-V3-style aux-loss-free balancing: it is added to the sigmoid scores **for top-k selection** (`e_score_correction_bias` in `GroupedTopKRouter`), so its exact bits decide which experts win near top-k ties. bf16 has ~2⁻⁸ relative precision; rounding the bias measurably flips the selected expert set for boundary tokens (in a synthetic check at realistic shapes — 4096 tokens × 192 experts, top-8, sigmoid — flips were 50/48/32 tokens per 4096 at bias scales 0.05/0.01/0.005; scales assumed, not measured from the checkpoint, but the effect persists across an order of magnitude).

vLLM already handles this correctly for the same tensor in the DeepSeek family:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/567a78432d8e/vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py#L314-L316

```python
self.gate.e_score_correction_bias = nn.Parameter(
    torch.empty(config.n_routed_experts, dtype=torch.float32)
)
```

HF transformers likewise pins it: `HYV3PreTrainedModel._keep_in_fp32_modules_strict = ["e_score_correction_bias"]`. And the rest of the hy_v3 gate path is already fp32-aware — the gate GEMM itself is built with `params_dtype=torch.float32` — which makes the bias allocation look like an oversight rather than a choice.

The MTP draft model (`hy_v3_mtp.py`) reuses the same MoE module, so speculative decoding inherits the same downcast.

### Expected behavior

`expert_bias` allocated as `torch.float32` regardless of serving dtype (matching `deepseek_v2.py` and the checkpoint), so routing decisions match the reference implementation bit-for-bit. One-line fix:

```python
self.expert_bias = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(config.num_experts, dtype=torch.float32))
```

(plus, if needed, the same ROCm post-load dtype handling deepseek_v2 applies at L390-392).

Happy to send a PR if the fix direction looks right to maintainers.

### Impact beyond serving accuracy

For RL pipelines that push trainer weights into vLLM for rollouts, the trainer routes with the true fp32 bias while vLLM routes with the bf16-rounded copy — a small systematic train/rollout routing mismatch that no amount of care on the trainer/export side can remove, since `copy_` re-rounds on ingest.

title: [Bugfix][SM120][MLA] Enable DCP for FlashInfer sparse MLA decode
body:
## Purpose

Enable decode context parallelism for the SM120 FlashInfer sparse MLA decode backend (`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`).

The generic FlashInfer sparse MLA backend already participates in DCP by filtering sparse top-k indices to the local DCP rank, passing valid per-row counts as `seq_lens`, requesting decode LSE, normalizing the LSE shape, and masking empty DCP rows before returning `(out, lse)` to the shared DCP reducer.

The SM120 packed sparse MLA wrapper still followed the simpler non-DCP path: it converted sparse indices without DCP filtering, passed `seq_lens=None`, did not request/return LSE, and allocated the output buffer from `self.num_heads`. On RTX PRO 6000 / SM120 GLM-5.2-NVFP4 serving with DCP this prevented startup and/or DCP reduction correctness. One concrete failure from hardware validation was:

```text
ValueError: Invalid shape of out: expected (32, 1, 32, 512), got torch.Size([32, 1, 8, 512])
```

This PR ports the existing sparse FlashInfer DCP wrapper behavior to the SM120 variant while preserving the SM120-specific packed `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache path, BF16 query input, `bmm2_scale=1.0`, and `kv_scale_format` plumbing.

Specifically, it:

- marks `FlashInferMLASparseSM120Impl` as able to return decode LSE;
- uses `triton_filter_and_convert_dcp_index` when DCP is enabled;
- passes compacted valid counts to FlashInfer as `seq_lens`;
- requests `return_lse` when the shared DCP reducer needs it;
- normalizes FlashInfer LSE to `(num_tokens, num_heads)`;
- masks empty DCP rows with `out=0` and `lse=-inf`;
- sizes the FlashInfer `out` buffer from the query head count actually passed to FlashInfer.

Dependency note: this patch applies cleanly to current `main` and does not require rebasing on another vLLM PR. Runtime validation below used FlashInfer 0.6.14. If `main` still pins 0.6.13 when this is reviewed, full SM120 GLM validation may be easier after #47669 lands.

AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI Codex was used to port the locally validated production patch into upstream form, add the focused unit test, run local checks, and draft this PR description. I reviewed the changed lines and own the submission.

## Test Plan

Local static/unit checks available in this environment:

- `python3 -m py_compile vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm120.py tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py`
- `python3 -m ruff check vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm120.py tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py`
- `python3 -m ruff format --check vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm120.py tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py`
- `git diff --check`

Targeted pytest attempted:

- `python3 -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py`

Production hardware validation performed separately on an 8x RTX PRO 6000 / SM120 system using `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`, vLLM V1, FlashInfer 0.6.14, packed sparse MLA, TP=8, EP enabled, `max_model_len=131072`, FP8 KV cache, DCP=4, and MTP=2.

## Test Result

Local:

- `py_compile`: passed
- `ruff check`: passed
- `ruff format --check`: passed after formatting the touched files
- `git diff --check`: passed
- targeted pytest: not runnable in this local checkout because the Python environment does not have `torch` installed (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'torch'` while importing `tests/conftest.py`)

Production SM120 validation summary:

- DCP=4 startup succeeded after this wrapper fix.
- vLLM reported `GPU KV cache size: 2,096,896 tokens` and `Maximum concurrency for 131,072 tokens per request: 16.00x` for DCP-only.
- With DCP=4 + MTP=2, vLLM reported `GPU KV cache size: 1,757,952 tokens` and `Maximum concurrency for 131,072 tokens per request: 13.41x`.
- 10 parallel chatbot-style requests completed successfully.
- Sustained 3 waves x 10 requests completed 30/30 HTTP 200 with about 239 output tok/s aggregate throughput.
- A near-128K request completed HTTP 200 with about 125K prompt tokens.

Follow-up validation that would be useful from maintainers with matching hardware:

- Run the new unit test in the normal CUDA CI/dev environment.
- Re-run GLM-5.2-NVFP4 on SM120 with DCP=2 and DCP=4.
- Compare DCP output against non-DCP output on deterministic prompts.
- Confirm FlashInfer SM120 sparse MLA LSE base remains `log2`, matching the generic FlashInfer sparse MLA backend.

title: [Bug]: DSV4 sparse MLA emits garbage (gsm8k ~0%) with the packed KV layout from #44577
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py - vLLM `0.23.1rc1.dev713+gd63c8e944` (`main` @ `d63c8e944`); regression bisected to `01192139b` (#44577), good parent `b9a7cd464` - PyTorch `2.11.0+cu130`, FlashInfer `0.6.13`, CUDA 13 (nvcc 13.3), Python 3.12.13 - 4× NVIDIA GB300 (sm100, driver 610.43.02, 280 GB), TP=4, DeepSeek-V4-Pro - KV dtype fp8, block-size 256, decode backend `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`
### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary On `main`, DeepSeek-V4 with the `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` decode backend produces token-soup output — gsm8k collapses from ~95% to ~0% (both strict- and flexible-match). Bisected to [#44577](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44577) ("Pack KV caches into contiguous per-block allocations for DeepSeek V4"); good parent `b9a7cd464`, first bad `01192139b`. It is a base-model correctness bug, independent of spec-decode (reproduces with MTP off). ## Reproduction Single node, TP=4. Real weights (this is an accuracy check, not a bring-up smoke test). ### 1. Launch server ```bash export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --port 8000 \ -tp 4 \ --trust-remote-code \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --block-size 256 \ --max-model-len 131072 \ --max-num-seqs 256 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --attention-config '{"backend": "FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4", "use_fp4_indexer_cache": true}' \ --enforce-eager \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune ``` Trigger-relevant flag: the `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` backend. The packed KV layout is auto-enabled for DeepSeek-V4 (no flag), so simply serving the model on `main` exercises it. The rest are performance/limit knobs and are not required to reproduce. ### 2. Verify with gsm8k ```bash lm_eval --model local-completions \ --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=256,tokenized_requests=False \ --tasks gsm8k \ --num_fewshot 5 \ --batch_size 256 \ --log_samples \ --output_path ./gsm8k-results ``` ## Result | | strict-match | flexible-extract | |---|---|---| | parent `b9a7cd464` (pre-#44577) | ~0.95 | ~0.95 | | `main` (#44577) | ~0.00 | ~0.01 | `--log_samples` shows the generations are degenerate token soup, not a parsing artifact. ## Root cause #44577 coalesces DeepSeek-V4's KV components (compressed-KV, sliding-window, indexer) into one shared per-block allocation and exposes each to the backend as a strided view, so per-component `stride(0)` becomes the full per-block span (larger than `page_size * per_token_stride`). The cache-store op honors this stride (it stores block `b` at `b * stride(0)`), but the `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` decode path does not: its call into FlashInfer's `trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4` passes `page_size = 1` and `batch_stride = per_token_stride`, so it addresses token `i` at `base + i * per_token_stride` and never reads `stride(0)`. Store and load agree only within block 0; every token in block ≥ 1 loads from the wrong offset → corrupted attention. The layout is otherwise valid — the `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4` backend, which decomposes the index by `page_block_size` and honors `stride(0)`, decodes the same packed cache correctly. The gap is specific to the FlashInfer sparse decode kernel (tracked upstream as a FlashInfer feature request to honor `stride(0)`). ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [ROCm][DSV4][Perf] Step 1/N: Port ATOM attention into vLLM: port single-node single-token-prediction case
body: ## Purpose Step 1/N of porting AMD **ATOM**'s DeepSeek-V4 hybrid attention into vLLM on ROCm. This step vendors the ATOM DeepSeek-V4 attention subsystem and wires it into the existing in-tree ROCm DeepSeek-V4 model as an **env-gated** alternative (`VLLM_DSV4_USE_ATOM`, default on) to the current ROCm MLA attention path. **Scope of this step** (kept deliberately small; more to follow): - Single node, **TP=8 / EP=1** with DP-attention, gfx950, fp8 KV cache. - **Single-token prediction only** — no MTP / speculative decode, no prefill/decode disaggregation, no prefill context parallelism. **Integration.** The ATOM attention runs as a single vLLM proxy `AttentionBackend` / `AttentionLayerBase`: vLLM's pager owns the classical KV storage (via a `FullAttentionSpec`), and the bridge slices ATOM's unified SWA-ring + CSA/HCA compressed views out of that storage, re-deriving ATOM's V4 attention metadata from vLLM's `CommonAttentionMetadata` each forward. Only the per-layer attention module is swapped — vLLM's embeddings / MoE / head / weight loading are reused as-is. The vendored code is kept ATOM-native (imports repointed to the vendored root, not rewritten to vLLM conventions) so it can track upstream ATOM. Dead-for-this-scope paths (PCP, dual-stream MoE, other-model norm/linear variants) were trimmed. ## Test Plan The main env switch for ATOM attention path: `export VLLM_DSV4_USE_ATOM=1` - Model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`, TP=8, fp8 KV cache, gfx950; served via the OpenAI-compatible server with `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` and async scheduling. - `lm-eval` GSM8K, comparing the ATOM path against the in-tree ROCm MLA path (`VLLM_DSV4_USE_ATOM=0`). ## Test Result

title: refactor: streamline DeepSeek V4 mHC warmup and remove token-size cap
body:
co-author：@[chungen04](https://github.com/chungen04) @SyaOtiLan 

## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4 inference suffers from multi-second latency spikes caused by TileLang JIT compilation of mHC (multi-head-compression) kernels when the scheduler encounters token sizes that were not warmed up. The existing warmup only covers a fixed set of power-of-two token sizes up to 16,384, leaving all other prefill shapes uncompiled.

kernel `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang` cost about 10s+, log info
'''

(Worker_TP0 pid=1098) 2026-07-06 16:03:24  [TileLang:tilelang.jit.kernel:INFO] (kernel.py:133): TileLang begins to compile kernel `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang` with `out_idx=None`

(Worker_TP0 pid=1098) 2026-07-06 16:03:34  [TileLang:tilelang.jit.kernel:INFO] (kernel.py:141): TileLang completes to compile kernel `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang`
(Worker_TP2 pid=1100) 2026-07-06 16:03:34  [TileLang:tilelang.jit.kernel:INFO] (kernel.py:141): TileLang completes to compile kernel `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang`
(Worker_TP3 pid=1101) 2026-07-06 16:03:34  [TileLang:tilelang.jit.kernel:INFO] (kernel.py:141): TileLang completes to compile kernel `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang`
(Worker_TP1 pid=1099) 2026-07-06 16:03:48  [TileLang:tilelang.jit.kernel:INFO] (kernel.py:133): TileLang begins to compile kernel `mhc_post_tilelang` with `out_idx=None`

(Worker_TP2 pid=1100) 2026-07-06 16:03:49  [TileLang:tilelang.jit.kernel:INFO] (kernel.py:133): TileLang begins to compile kernel `mhc_post_tilelang` with `out_idx=None`

'''


This PR removes the hard `16_384` auto-warmup cap and instead warms up **every token size from 1 to `max_num_batched_tokens`**, ensuring that any shape the scheduler may produce is compiled before serving traffic.

## What Changed

`vllm/model_executor/warmup/deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup.py`

- Removed `_AUTO_WARMUP_MAX_TOKENS` and `_DEFAULT_TOKEN_SIZE_CANDIDATES`.
- `_select_mhc_warmup_token_sizes` now generates a contiguous range `[1, max_tokens]` instead of a sparse list.
- `_warmup_layer_mhc` now uses real `attn_norm`/`ffn_norm` weights and `variance_epsilon` so norm-fused TileLang kernels are exercised with runtime tensors.
- Added progress logging every 1,000 token sizes.
- Added warmup for the fused `mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang` post+pre variant used after the first layer.
- Simplified verbose comments.

title: [Bug]: Cutlass C3X `dispatch_scaled_mm` crashes on SM120 Blackwell (RTX PRO 6000) with FP8 block-scaled model (DeepSeek-V4-Flash)
body:
### Your current environment

- **vLLM**: v0.23.0 / nightly (both reproduced)
- **GPU**: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition ??compute capability 12.0 (SM120)
- **Driver**: 580.159.03
- **CUDA**: 13.0, **PyTorch** 2.11.0+cu130
- **NCCL**: 2.28.9
- **TP**: 2 (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=6,7`, same PCIe Switch group, PIX topology)

### Describe the bug

Loading **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** (FP8 block-scaled, `quant_method: fp8`, `fmt: e4m3`, ~149 GB) on SM120 Blackwell crashes during the first simulated forward pass (`profile_run -> _dummy_run`). Weights load successfully (~74.05 GiB per GPU), but the Cutlass C3X dispatch table lacks an SM120 registration for FP8 block-scaled matrix multiplication, causing an immediate crash:

```
RuntimeError: dispatch_scaled_mm,
  /workspace/csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/c3x/scaled_mm_helper.hpp:17
```

This is **not** a NUMA/NCCL/hardware topology issue ??GPU6 and GPU7 are on the same NUMA node with PIX (direct PCIe Switch) connectivity. NCCL handshake completes normally. The error is purely in the Cutlass C3X static dispatch path.

### Verification

- SM120 is correctly identified (`CC = (12, 0)`)
- vLLM's `_C.abi3.so` contains many `sm_120.cubin` entries (via `cuobjdump --list-elf`), confirming partial Blackwell support
- Error is deterministic: always crashes at the same line after successful weight loading

### Attempts to work around

| Attempt | Result |
|---------|--------|
| Single GPU (`--tensor-parallel-size 1`) | OOM (96G VRAM < 149G model), crashes before reaching dispatch |
| Remove `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` | `AssertionError: DeepseekV4 FlashMLA fp8 layout only supports fp8 kv-cache, got auto` ??FP8 KV cache is mandatory for this model |
| Upgrade to `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` | Weights load successfully (10.12s), but same `dispatch_scaled_mm` crash at `profile_run` |

### Related but distinct issues

- **#47436**: Same SM120 + FP8 area, but crashes on **DeepGEMM** path (`layout.hpp:59: Unknown SF transformation`). Their workaround `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` falls back to the Cutlass path ??which is exactly where *this* issue lives. So that workaround does not help here.
- **#47130**: Also DeepGEMM SM120 regression, different code path.

### Suggested fix

Either add the missing SM120 case to the Cutlass C3X `dispatch_scaled_mm` dispatch table in `scaled_mm_helper.hpp`, or provide a fallback to Triton/runtime-compiled kernels when the static Cutlass path doesn't cover the current architecture.

### Potential workarounds (untested)

- `VLLM_USE_V1=0` ??disable V1 engine, fall back to V0
- `--linear-backend triton` ??bypass C++ static dispatch entirely

### Hardware topology (`nvidia-smi topo -m`)

```
        GPU0    GPU1    GPU2    GPU3
GPU0     X      PIX     NODE    NODE
GPU1    PIX      X      NODE    NODE
GPU2    NODE    NODE     X      PIX
GPU3    NODE    NODE    PIX      X
```

Platform: MSI CG480 workstation.

Image: `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:bf52bc37dccb4ba7c06053fe4c6e5e8fec2aa8e471f683d8a18b11e8402377f9` (= `nightly-aarch64`, `0.23.1rc1.dev799+g69715823d`, pushed 2026-07-06). Also reproduces on `0.23.1rc1.dev193+gecf9d8352` (which additionally has a since-fixed 2048-onset top-k bug, see below).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Serving **`nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`** (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, DSA sparse attention, `index_topk=2048`, modelopt FP4) on GB300, generations **corrupt mid-stream once total sequence length (prompt + decoded tokens) crosses ~4096**: token-repetition loops, digit/tag noise with control characters, or near-empty max-length responses. Below ~3.6k total sequence, output is consistently clean. Failure is stochastic per request (~40–60% at 4k–10k ctx for the full model) and reproduces at **concurrency 1**.

Sample mid-stream corruption:

```
...The log directory and file format have been993126089/8/2 3<5<7/5?<<3<0<2<1<0<<response>...
```

**Onset tracks the 4096 boundary during decode**, not prompt length: with a 3,644-token prompt the response degrades only after ~450 generated tokens; with a 4,043-token prompt it degrades almost immediately.

Sweep results (8 samples/size, concurrency 1, greedy-default sampling, MTP off, dev799):

```
ctx=851:   corrupt=0/8 near_empty=0/8
ctx=1782:  corrupt=0/8 near_empty=0/8
ctx=2580:  corrupt=0/8 near_empty=0/8   <- 2048-onset bug fixed vs dev193
ctx=3245:  corrupt=0/8 near_empty=0/8
ctx=3644:  corrupt=0/8 near_empty=1/8   <- onset
ctx=4043:  corrupt=3/8 near_empty=2/8
ctx=6038:  corrupt=3/8 near_empty=1/8
ctx=10161: corrupt=3/8 near_empty=1/8
```

### What we ruled out (single-variable A/B, each verified with the same sweep)

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| MTP speculative decode off | still corrupt |
| `use_index_cache: false` | still corrupt |
| `--kv-cache-dtype auto` (bf16 KV) | still corrupt |
| sampling (temp 0.6, repetition_penalty 1.05) | still corrupt |
| all-F `index_topk_pattern` (indexer on all layers) | worse (corrupt at short ctx too) |
| bypass compiled `persistent_topk` → triton `top_k_per_row_decode` | still corrupt ⇒ bug is upstream of top-k selection |
| REAP-pruned GLM-5.2 checkpoint (168 experts, cpu-offload 55 GiB vs 215 GiB) | identical ~4096 onset, lower incidence (~25%) ⇒ checkpoint- and offload-independent |

### Localization

- Top-k selection kernels exonerated (two different kernels produce the same corruption).
- Wrong values therefore enter at the **decode indexer logits**: `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` (imported via `vllm.utils.deep_gemm`), consuming the paged fp8 KV/index cache.
- The indexer backend logs `Setting kv cache block size to 64 for DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER backend`; **4096 = 64 tokens/block × 64 blocks**, i.e. the onset coincides with the request's KV crossing the second page group / schedule window of the paged-logits kernel on sm_103.
- Decode path per logs: `use_flattening=False (next_n=1, use_fp4_indexer_cache=False)`.
- Prefill appears fine: ≤3.6k prompts give clean prefill and clean early decode; corruption begins only when decode crosses the boundary.
- Related earlier bug, already fixed between dev193 and dev799 (thanks!): unguarded cooperative/persistent radix-topk in `sparse_attn_indexer.py` produced a hard onset at exactly `index_topk=2048`; the added `num_rows <= 32` / TMA-alignment guards resolved it. This issue is the *remaining* 4096-onset corruption.

### Serving command

```bash
vllm serve /model \
  --served-model-name glm52-full --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001 \
  --trust-remote-code --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.99 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --cpu-offload-gb 215 --cpu-offload-params experts \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --linear-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": false}' \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm47 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8,16,32]}' \
  --hf-overrides '{"index_topk_pattern":"FFFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSS","use_index_cache":true}'
```

(env: `VLLM_WEIGHT_OFFLOADING_DISABLE_PIN_MEMORY=1`, `VLLM_NVFP4_GEMM_BACKEND=flashinfer-trtllm`, `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`; corruption also reproduces with MTP `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'` on.)

### Reproducer

Stdlib-only script; point it at the OpenAI endpoint. Any output with long repetition loops / digit-tag noise, or empty text at `finish_reason=length`, counts as corrupt.

<details>
<summary>ctx_sweep.py</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Context-length corruption sweep against the local glm52 vLLM server.

Sends single-request (c1) chat completions at increasing context lengths and
scores outputs for token-corruption (repetition loops / digit-tag noise) and
near-empty responses. Onset at ~2048 ctx implicates the DSA sparse indexer
(index_topk=2048). Usage: ctx_sweep.py [samples_per_size]
"""

import json
import os
import re
import sys
import urllib.request

SIZES = [1000, 1800, 2600, 4000, 6000, 10000]
N = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 8
MODEL = os.environ.get("SWEEP_MODEL", "glm52-full")
# SWEEP_MAX_CTX: skip sizes above this (e.g. 3644 while the known >4096
# DeepGEMM indexer bug is outstanding and serving is capped below it).
_max_ctx = int(os.environ.get("SWEEP_MAX_CTX", "0"))
if _max_ctx:
    SIZES = [s for s in SIZES if s <= _max_ctx]

SYS_P = (
    "You are an AI assistant operating a terminal. Respond with an XML "
    "<response> block containing <analysis>, <plan>, and <commands> with "
    "<keystrokes>."
)
FILLER = """$ pdflatex main.tex
Overfull \\hbox (12.4pt too wide) in paragraph at lines 5--9
[]\\OT1/cmr/m/n/10 The ex-plorer was cu-ri-ous about the weath-er-beaten path-finder
Output written on main.pdf (1 page, 45631 bytes).
"""


def build(target_tok):
    msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": SYS_P}]
    n = max(1, (target_tok - 100) // 130)
    for i in range(n):
        msgs.append({"role": "user", "content": f"Output {i}:\n{FILLER}"})
        msgs.append(
            {
                "role": "assistant",
                "content": f"<response><analysis>Attempt {i} still failing."
                "</analysis><plan>Retry.</plan><commands><command>"
                "<keystrokes>make check\n</keystrokes><duration>2.0"
                "</duration></command></commands></response>",
            }
        )
    msgs.append({"role": "user", "content": "Still failing. What next?"})
    return msgs


def bad(text):
    flat = text.replace(" ", "").replace("\n", "")
    if re.search(r"(.{1,6})\1{7,}", flat):
        return True
    noise = len(re.findall(r"\d<|<\d|>\d\n|\d\n\d", text))
    return noise >= 5


for target in SIZES:
    msgs = build(target)
    d = e = 0
    ptok = None
    for i in range(N):
        body = {"model": MODEL, "messages": msgs, "max_tokens": 600}
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            "http://localhost:8001/v1/chat/completions",
            data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
        )
        r = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=900).read())
        ptok = r["usage"]["prompt_tokens"]
        m = r["choices"][0]["message"]
        text = (m.get("content") or "") + (m.get("reasoning_content") or "")
        if bad(text):
            d += 1
        elif len(text) < 20:
            e += 1
    print(f"ctx={ptok}: corrupt={d}/{N} near_empty={e}/{N}", flush=True)
```

</details>

### Impact

Any agentic or long-context use breaks (conversations trivially exceed 4k). Throughput-only validation (e.g. ISL/OSL 1024 benchmarks) never crosses the boundary and cannot see this — recommend a correctness sweep in serving validation for DSA models.

Possibly related: #35288 (MTP corrupt output at c≥4), #40018 (DSA sparse prefill garbage on ROCm), #40756 (MTP illegal memory access on long sequences) — none match this exact c1 / 4096-boundary signature.

title: [RFC]: Packed Variable Length Speculative Decoding
body:
### Motivation.

In speculative decoding, we can save verification cost by selectively verifying a different number of draft tokens per request in each step. There are various techniques of selecting and tuning which / how many tokens to submit for verification, but all share a common benefit: reducing verification overhead with per-request variable-length query lengths in a batch.



### Proposed Change.

We will support verification input batches with heterogeneous query lengths for each decode request. We will separate the concerns of total verification token budget and allocation of that budget among the draft tokens. The scheduler chooses a host-visible total token budget, and the worker distributes that budget across requests entirely on-device, avoiding serialization of the query lengths to/from the host. This allows us to maintain asynchronous scheduling and CUDA graph compatibility.

This will involve changes to the scheduler, model runner input preparation, cuda graph management, and speculator-scheduler implementations (for the actual logic to decide which tokens to propose).

I propose to build off of the [batch-level Dynamic Speculative Decoding](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45953) support (which already has full-graph compatibility) in ModelRunnerV2.

### Feedback Period.

_No response_

### CC List.

@TheEpicDolphin @WoosukKwon @LucasWilkinson @mgoin @ekagra-ranjan @simon-mo @zyongye 

### Any Other Things.

## Challenges

### Varlen kernel support

Attention kernels take as input the number of *requests* in addition to the query offset pointers.
For decoding, many attention kernels omit the latter and simply assume either 1 (autoregressive) or N (uniform speculative) query lengths per request.

Many, but not all, attention kernels already support variable length queries per request:
- FlashAttention Decode (Hopper/Blackwell GQA): supports varlen queries via `flash_attn_varlen_func` arguments `max_seqlen_q` and `cu_seqlens_q`. (Definitely FA3, not sure about varlen full-graph for FA4)
- FlashInfer TRTLLM-Gen Decode (Blackwell GQA): supports varlen queries via `max_q_len` and `cum_seq_lens_q`, but not plugged into vLLM yet
- FlashInfer TRTLLM-Gen MLA Decode (Blackwell MLA): no support
- FlashAttention MLA: Currently uniform-query CG compatibility, but supports varlen Q, might be compatible
- DeepSeek V4 Indexed attention: Underlying Sparse MLA kernel supports varlen, but seems to need some plumbing to fully support varlen
- MiniMax M3 Sparse attention: no support
- FlashMLA (Hopper MLA): no support
- GDN: seems possible with some extra work on the metadata builder
- Mamba/Mamba2: seems possible with a bit of plumbing

Thus we will have to gate support to only the attention backends which have varlen support implemented, and it'll take quite a bit of follow-up work to enable this for most backends.

### CUDA Graph Compatibility

We currently have support for FULL CUDA Graphs with different query lengths for different batch sizes.
This is done by keying the graphs by `num_reqs` _and_ `num_tokens` _and_ `uniform_token_count`.

We can extend this: for each `num_reqs` (binned to powers of 2 / multiples of 8 / etc.) from `1` up to `max_num_seqs`, 
we record a separate set of graphs for each `num_query_tokens_per_request` from `1` (no spec tokens) up to (1 + max_num_speculative_tokens).

To unlock true dynamism, we break the connection between `num_query_tokens_per_request` and `max_q_len`: we always permit up to `max_num_speculative_tokens` for a single request, a pass `max_q_len=max_num_speculative_tokens` in every attention kernel invocation,
and thus allow some requests to have fewer than `num_query_tokens_per_request` and some to have more. This means that the scheduler
effectively is only deciding `mean_num_query_tokens_per_request` (and will likely use heuristics from the workers to make that decision, see below).

Then all we need to do is leverage `cu_seqlens_q` to have variable query start locations within the block, mark the remaining tokens in the suffix with `is_padding`, and pad `num_reqs` to `num_reqs_padded` by appending to `cu_seqlens_q` with 0-query-length requests which are ignored by the kernel.

Thus, the attention kernel is, for a given `num_reqs_padded` and `num_tokens = int(mean_num_query_tokens_per_request * num_reqs_unpadded)`, always invoked with inputs of consistent shape and address.

Note, that we can support non-integer `mean_num_query_tokens_per_request` as long as we record more graphs for `num_tokens` values in between `num_reqs * i` and `num_reqs * (i + 1)`, though they will not be perfectly uniform; we will have to support some extra padding or handle this specifically when doing capture.

### Supporting mixed batches

Supporting mixed batches with FULL CUDA Graphs is appealing as host-overhead in short prefills is a real concern, but this is out-of-scope for this RFC.
For PIECEWISE graphs, this is simpler. The main remaining consideration is compatibility with the `is_padding` optimization, which allows some kernels (e.g. MoE kernels) to skip work on graph-padding tokens. With variable query lengths in the decode, we may end up with some decode padding (to match the number of actual query tokens with the number of expected query tokens) in addition to graph padding. This should be avoided, either by packing the decodes tightly in the batch or reordering prefills and extends to the front of the batch, to share the query padding with the graph's total-token-count padding. It's unclear to me if it will be easy to implement the former, as the total number of used query tokens need not be known on the host, but either solution seems feasible here.

The easiest short-term solution seems to be to **enforce no padding in the query block**. Since we always have more draft tokens than we will need to admit in our budget, we can just fill all allocated slots with draft tokens even if our performance model might indicate it's favorable to skip them. Even though they might be skippable via `is_padding`, there are still some attention and constant overheads to be paid, so the price shouldn't be too extreme here.

### Supporting Data Parallelism

Some coordination across workers will be necessary to synchronize which graph is being executed, i.e. which (`num_reqs_padded` x `num_tokens_padded`) pair is active. Seems like this should fit naturally with our existing DP sync, but I'm not an expert in this area.

### Scheduler-Speculator awareness

In vLLM, our scheduler lives in a separate process; yet I propose to let it decide `mean_num_query_tokens_per_request` when scheduling.
In order to have the scheduler make decisions about how many total query tokens to permit, it will need some information from the model runner.
I propose to extend the Speculator interface to allow the scheduler to "query" for "hints" such as how many query tokens should be issued on average per request.

It is important to maintain asynchronous scheduling support here; in the DSpark report, they suggest using information delayed by 2 engine iterations in order to schedule the next step. This seems very reasonable, as acceptance rates over batches generally have significant temporal locality over multiple steps (reasoning v.s. final response, conversation domain, blocks of code/math/formatted output, etc).

This would probably be easier to implement if the scheduler was replicated into each worker, so we don't need to cross an IPC boundary, but this is what we have today.

I'm not certain that the scheduler needs to know about this at all. Conceptually I feel like it's the role of the scheduler
to be choosing how many tokens to put in the batch, but besides allocating KV slots and selecting which requests to run
(both of which are pretty agnostic to the variable-length decode tokens, the scheduler can just allocate the slots optimistically), I'm not sure why the current scheduler would need to be involved.

title: [Bug]: OffloadingConnector: DSpark draft-model KV-cache group's sparse storage causes external_prefix_cache_hits_total to be permanently 0
body:
## Summary

When serving **DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark** (`--speculative_config '{"method": "dspark", ...}'`) with the native `OffloadingConnector` (`--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector",...}'`), the external (RAM-tier) prefix cache **never records a hit**, even under sustained real load with GPU eviction happening (`kv_cache_usage` >95%, `vllm:kv_offload_store_bytes_total` growing steadily into the hundreds of GB). `vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total` stays at exactly `0` for the lifetime of the server, while `vllm:external_prefix_cache_queries_total` grows into the millions.

Root cause: DSpark adds 3 extra decoder layers purely for speculative drafting (`DSparkDeepseekV4Model`, `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/dspark.py`). vLLM correctly classifies this layer group's `GroupOffloadConfig.is_eagle_group = True`. `OffloadingConnectorScheduler._lookup()` (`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py`) requires **every** KV-cache group to independently report a nonzero hit; any single group reporting `num_hit_blocks == 0` immediately short-circuits the **entire request's** lookup to `0` (`if num_hit_blocks == 0: return 0`, inside the per-group loop).

The DSpark group's own store IS occurring (verified via `vllm:kv_offload_store_bytes_total`), but its stored blocks are **sparse and discontinuous**: added per-key debug instrumentation confirmed real `HIT` results scattered among mostly `MISS` results (e.g. `[MISS, MISS, HIT, MISS, MISS]` scanning newest-first), never forming the consecutive run `_sliding_window_lookup` requires (`sliding_window_size_in_blocks + 1` for eagle groups, to account for the "trailing volatile block" compensation). Because this specific group can essentially never satisfy the consecutive-hit requirement for DSpark's block-based drafting pattern, it permanently poisons the AND-combination for the whole request: even though the model's *real* KV-cache groups (SWA, compressed C4A/C128A, indexer) independently measured a working 88.9%–100% hit rate once isolated from this effect.

## Related issues (different code path, same root pattern)

This looks superficially similar to a well-known family of bugs where an eagle/draft
KV-cache group breaks multi-group cache-hit coordination, but all of those live in the
**GPU-side** `HybridKVCacheCoordinator`/`find_longest_cache_hit()` radix-cache path
(`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py`), not in the **CPU-offload** `OffloadingConnector`
path this issue is about:

- #32802: GPT-OSS 0% prefix cache hits with hybrid attention + EAGLE (the original
  "EAGLE spiral block-dropping" report; GPU hybrid coordinator).
- #33524: partial fix for #32802 via an `is_simple_hybrid` guard (`len(attention_groups) == 2`).
- #40624: Gemma4 + DFlash hits the same spiral because it has 3 groups, not 2, so the
  `is_simple_hybrid` guard from #33524 doesn't cover it.
- #42948: DeepSeek-V4-Flash (no speculative decoding) loses first-block GPU cache
  entries on reassignment; same "eagle/multi-group intersection" family, again GPU-side.

I confirmed (by reading `kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py` directly and by
reproducing on this exact model/config) that this issue's bug is **not** the same code
path as any of the above: `OffloadingConnectorScheduler._lookup()` has its own,
separate AND-combination logic for the CPU/RAM tier, with no interaction with
`HybridKVCacheCoordinator`. I could not find an existing issue covering this specific
code path, hence filing separately, but flagging the connection since whoever
reviews this may recognize the general pattern from the issues above.

## Repro

- Model: `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark` (43 hidden layers + 3 DSpark draft layers + 1 MTP layer), `--tensor-parallel-size 4`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--block-size 256`, `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`.
- `--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":<N>}}'`
- `--speculative_config '{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 4, "draft_sample_method": "greedy"}'`
- vLLM: nightly build `cu129-nightly-09663abde0f50944a8d5ea30120666024b503faa` (`0.23.1rc1.dev714+g09663abde`)
- Workload: real multi-turn conversational replay (SWE-agent-style sessions), concurrency=64, sustained load causing genuine GPU KV eviction (`kv_cache_usage_max` ~99%).
- Observed: `vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total` = `0` for the entire run; `vllm:external_prefix_cache_queries_total` in the millions; `vllm:kv_offload_store_bytes_total` in the hundreds of GB.

## Diagnostic evidence

Added temporary debug logging to `_lookup()` printing per-group `group_idx`, `sliding_window_blocks`, `offloaded_block_size`, `num_hit_blocks`, and `is_eagle_group`. Sample from a live run:

```
group_idx=0 sliding_window_blocks=None offloaded_block_size=256 is_eagle=False: 279/2514 miss  (88.9% hit)
group_idx=1 sliding_window_blocks=2    offloaded_block_size=64  is_eagle=False: 0/2235 miss    (100% hit)
group_idx=2 sliding_window_blocks=2    offloaded_block_size=64  is_eagle=True:  66/66 miss     (0% hit, always)
group_idx=4 sliding_window_blocks=16   offloaded_block_size=8   is_eagle=False: 0/2235 miss    (100% hit)
```

Per-key trace for group_idx=2 (the DSpark draft group), confirming data exists but is non-consecutive:

```
required_window=3 per_key(newest-first)=[MISS, MISS, HIT, MISS, MISS]  RESULT=0
required_window=3 per_key(newest-first)=[MISS, HIT, MISS, MISS]        RESULT=0
```

## Suggested fix

**Scoping note**: `is_eagle_group` is a generic vLLM flag set for *any* model using
an EAGLE-family draft attention group (standard EAGLE/EAGLE3, MTP, DFlash, DSpark,
...), not something DSpark-specific. The existing `TestEagle` suite in
`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py` shows the
current "pop one volatile trailing block" mechanism (query one extra block,
subtract 1 from the hit count once verified) works correctly and provides real
cross-request reuse for well-behaved EAGLE/MTP/DFlash models: it's not itself
broken. DSpark's draft-layer KV is architecturally different: it's recomputed from
the target model's real hidden state every step
(`DSparkDeepseekV4Model.precompute_and_store_context_kv`), so its stored content has
*no* reuse value at all, not merely "one volatile tail block": that's why its
lookup is sparse/discontinuous throughout rather than just failing at the boundary.

Patch (`_lookup()` in `OffloadingConnectorScheduler`): when a group flagged
`is_eagle_group` reports `num_hit_blocks == 0`, drop *that one group* from the rest
of the current lookup call instead of returning 0 for the whole request, but only
when `speculative_config.use_dspark()` is true (`SchedulerOffloadConfig.is_dspark`,
computed once from `spec.vllm_config.speculative_config.use_dspark()`). The excluded
set is tracked on the request's state (`RequestOffloadState.lookup_excluded_groups`)
so `update_state_after_alloc` skips `prepare_load` for those specific groups (to
avoid `assert block is not None` in `CPUOffloadingManager.prepare_load`, since their
keys were never confirmed present for the boundary the surviving groups settled
on). `_build_store_jobs` is untouched entirely: storage keeps the existing "pop one
trailing block" behavior for every eagle-family method, including DSpark.

- For EAGLE, EAGLE3, MTP, and DFlash: `is_dspark` is always False, so the new branch
  is **unreachable**: `_lookup()` takes the exact original `return 0` path,
  byte-for-byte identical to before this change.
- For DSpark: a 0-hit draft group is excluded from the current lookup call instead
  of zeroing out co-existing non-eagle groups' real, reusable hits.
- Small diff: only `_lookup()`, `update_state_after_alloc()`, and one new field each
  on `SchedulerOffloadConfig` (`is_dspark`) and `RequestOffloadState`
  (`lookup_excluded_groups`). `__init__`'s group classification and
  `_build_store_jobs` are untouched.

**Verification**:
- Unit tests: added 3 tests to `TestEagle` (`test_sparse_eagle_group_does_not_poison_other_groups_lookup`, `test_non_dspark_eagle_group_miss_still_zeros_whole_request`, `test_sparse_eagle_group_load_excludes_only_the_failing_group`), covering the DSpark-sparse-storage lookup/load path and explicitly proving the branch is unreachable when `is_dspark=False`. Ran the full `TestEagle` class (21 tests: 18 pre-existing + 3 new) against this exact vLLM build: all pass, confirming no regression to the existing EAGLE/MTP/DFlash "pop one trailing block" tests.
- Production validation: 600s sustained load, concurrency=64, real multi-turn conversational replay, 100% request success rate (0 failures), zero crashes. `external_prefix_cache_hits_total`/`queries_total` recovered to **~83.7%** combined hit rate (up from a permanent 0%), consistent with the GPU-side prefix cache hit rate (83.3%) measured in the same run.
- Correctness: the "same prompt, different completion" variance I initially suspected as a correctness bug turned out to be a pre-existing property of DSpark speculative decoding under concurrent batched serving (reproduced identically on a baseline server with *no* KV-transfer connector at all, i.e. unrelated to this change).

I initially prototyped a simpler, blanket "exclude every `is_eagle_group` group
unconditionally" version (no `is_dspark` check, touching `__init__` and
`_build_store_jobs` too) and load-tested it successfully as well, but did not pursue
it further once I realized it would silently disable the *working* "pop one
trailing block" reuse for every other eagle-family method, not just DSpark: the
`is_dspark`-gated version above is what I'd like feedback on / propose as the actual
fix.

Happy to open a PR with this change (patch + the 3 regression tests) if the
approach looks right: flagging as an issue first since this touches shared logic
used by every eagle-family speculative-decoding + KV-offloading combination, not
just DSpark, and I'd like a scope sanity-check before submitting.

## Environment

- vLLM: `0.23.1rc1.dev714+g09663abde` (image `vllm/vllm-openai:cu129-nightly-09663abde0f50944a8d5ea30120666024b503faa`)
- GPUs: 4x (TP=4)
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark`
