body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

### Your current environment

Inference Framework: vllm-ascend 0.24.0
LLM: DeepSeek-V4 (Flash & Pro)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Overview

This issue proposes a systematic improvement: add an **automated request body validation and normalization module** at the very upstream of vLLM's request processing pipeline (e.g., API gateway or `/v1/chat/completions` entry point). This module upgrades the current "soft interception" (relying on system prompts) to a **hard interception** based on Python hard-coded logic, fundamentally eliminating DSML leakage, tag corruption, empty outputs, and other issues caused by illegal request bodies.

---

## Background and Problem Statement

### Case 1: Non‑standard Request Body Format Leading to DSML Leakage

**Case Link**: [Detailed analysis of Case 1](https://3ms.huawei.com/km/groups/3959141/blogs/details/22374443?l=zh-cn&moduleId=1047283487341719552) *(internal link)*

**Root Cause**: The request body does not follow the vLLM official Tool Calling standard format – the functions to be called are not registered in the `tools` dictionary.  
- The model cannot recognize the tool call format and fails to generate structured outputs via constrained decoding.  
- DSML tags (e.g., `<| DSML |>`) leak into the `content` field.  
- Function calls are missed, causing the expected tool invocation functionality to fail.

**Solution**: Manually normalize the request body according to the official standard, i.e., correctly place function definitions into the `tools` array.

### Case 2: Fundamental Defects of the System Prompt “Soft Interception”

**Case Link**: [Detailed analysis of Case 2](https://3ms.huawei.com/km/groups/3959141/blogs/details/22379454?l=zh-cn&moduleId=1047283487341719552) *(internal link)*

**Root Cause**: Currently, the industry (including DS official APIs) commonly uses system prompts as a “soft interception” for illegal requests. However, this approach has fatal flaws:  
1. **Instruction Priority Conflict**: When the request body contains `response_format={"type": "json_object"}` or `tool_choice: "auto"`   with thinking mode or other unknown illegal requests, the structured decoding constraint or tool invocation directive takes higher priority than the system prompt, causing the validation logic in the system prompt to be overridden or “swallowed”.  
2. **Inability to Cover All Bad Cases**: For some extreme illegal request bodies (e.g., combinations of multiple high‑priority parameters), the system prompt fails to intercept, and the illegal request reaches the core inference engine, leading to tag leakage, empty outputs, etc.  
3. **Extra Token Overhead**: The system prompt occupies context length and computational resources as part of the input.

**Experimental Verification**: Local reproduction using a system prompt successfully intercepted most illegal request bodies, but failed on a few extreme cases – exactly matching the behavior of the DS official API. This confirms that the DS official API uses a similar system prompt mechanism and also exposes its fundamental limitation.

---

## Proposed Improvement: From “Soft Interception” to “Hard Interception”

### Core Idea

Add a **Python‑hardcoded request body validation and normalization module** at the very upstream of vLLM’s request processing pipeline (e.g., API gateway or `/v1/chat/completions` entry). Before the request enters the inference chain, the module performs the following:

1. **Legality Validation**: Detect whether the request body conforms to the OpenAI‑compatible `/v1/chat/completions` interface standard.  
2. **Automatic Normalization**: Automatically fix non‑standard request bodies, including but not limited to:  
   - Check whether the `tools` field exists and is correctly formatted; if missing, attempt to extract function call information from `messages` and auto‑populate.  
   - Check the combination of `response_format` and `tool_choice`; if conflicting, adjust according to priority rules.  
   - Filter or escape illegal characters, empty characters, or unregistered DSML tags.  
   - Check each `content` field in `messages` for emptiness, garbled text, or excessive length.  
3. **Reject Irreparable Requests**: For extreme illegal requests that cannot be automatically fixed, directly return `400 Bad Request` to prevent them from entering the inference pipeline (exactly what  the DS offical API does).

### Three Core Advantages

#### 1. Cost Reduction (Reduce Token Overhead)
- **Current Solution**: The system prompt occupies extra context as a pre‑processing instruction, consuming tokens for every request.  
- **Improved Solution**: Request body validation and normalization are performed by Python code outside the inference pipeline, **zero token overhead**.

#### 2. Efficiency Increase (Improve Inference Throughput)
- **Current Solution**: The system prompt forces the model to process additional validation logic, consuming model computational resources; the KV cache generated by the system prompt also occupies GPU memory.  
- **Improved Solution**: Validation logic is executed efficiently on CPU, **consuming no manual efforts or GPU compute resources or memory**, thus improving overall hardware utilization. Moreover, normalized request bodies are more uniform, leading to higher inference efficiency.

#### 3. Quality Assurance (Fundamental Solution)
- **Current Solution**: The system prompt risks being overridden or “swallowed” by illegal requests (e.g., `response_format` or `tool_choice` high‑priority parameters), causing validation failure.  
- **Improved Solution**: Validation occurs **outside the inference pipeline**; every input is processed **before** entering the formal inference chain. This fundamentally prevents the validation logic from being overridden or skipped. All illegal requests are intercepted or fixed before reaching the model, **completely eliminating DSML leakage, garbled output, empty responses, etc.**

---

### Alternatives

## Technical Implementation Suggestions

### Module Location

Add a pre‑processing hook in the request handler of vLLM’s `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint. For example:

```python

```

   - If function definitions in `tools` do not conform to JSON Schema, auto‑fix or reject.

   - Detect and filter empty characters, garbled text, or overly long content.  
   - Check if `system` role messages have been overridden or tampered with by user messages.

   - If both thinking mode (e.g., `thinking: true`) and `tool_choice: "auto"` are enabled, return an error instructing the user to select only one mode.

I initially noticed that the crash could not be reproduced with `--enfroce-eager` or `--async-scheduling` args.

However, the root cause is that in the traditional non-async scheduling mode, `_prepare_inputs()` copies `num_computed_tokens` from CPU to GPU using `non_blocking=True`. This copy is then immediately read by the GPU to compute positions:

```
self.num_computed_tokens[:num_reqs].copy_(..., non_blocking=True)
self.positions[:N] = self.num_computed_tokens[req_indices_gpu] + ...
```

For LLMs, `_to_list()` syncs the GPU every step. However, for pooling models, intermediate prefill-only chunks return a plain `ModelRunnerOutput` (as no requests are considered 'finished' since `not any(finished_mask)` is True) and so it returns with no GPU sync. The next step's `_update_states()` then overwrites `num_computed_tokens_cpu_tensor` while the GPU is still reading it via the async H2D copy, producing stale values that cause positions to exceed `max_position_embeddings`.

Rerun the script from above with the changes in this PR.

Does not crash!

title: DSpark speculative decoding incompatible with NIXL P/D disaggregation and Hopper FA3
body:
## DSpark + NIXL P/D disaggregation: KV layer count mismatch and Hopper FA3 crash

**vLLM**: `v0.23.1rc1.dev1000+g95ed0feaa` (nightly)
**Model**: `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`, **Draft**: `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark` (7 spec tokens)
**Hardware**: 2x H200 nodes, 8 GPUs each, EP16, DP8 per node
**KV transfer**: `NixlConnector`, `kv_role=kv_both`

### Issue 1: NIXL handshake fails with decode-only DSpark

DSpark enabled on decode only. Prefill has no DSpark. NIXL connector rejects the connection:

```
AssertionError: Number of KV layers must match between producer and consumer
```

DSpark adds `is_eagle_group=True` KV cache layers for the draft model attention. Prefill has fewer KV layers than decode.

### Issue 2: Hopper FA3 crash with DSpark on prefill

Enabling DSpark on both sides to match layer counts. Server starts (health returns 200). Crashes on first request:


title: [ROCm] [CI] Keep original layer count for Eagle3DeepseekV2 init test
body:
## Purpose

`test_can_initialize_large_subset[Eagle3DeepseekV2ForCausalLM]` fails in the AMD
ROCm CI (basic models init tests) with:

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 6056, in _dummy_run
    hidden_states, _ = outputs
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)
```

The Eagle3 draft (`AQ-MedAI/Kimi-K25-eagle3`) requests auxiliary hidden states
from target layers `(2, 30, 58)` (log: `Using auxiliary layers from speculative
config: (2, 30, 58)`). The initialization test's default `dummy_hf_overrides`
collapses the target model (`moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5`) to a single hidden layer, so
layers 2/30/58 don't exist. In `DeepseekV2Model.forward` no layer index then
matches, `aux_hidden_states` stays empty, and the model returns a bare
`hidden_states` tensor instead of the `(hidden_states, aux_hidden_states)` tuple:

```python
# vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py
if len(aux_hidden_states) > 0:
    return hidden_states, aux_hidden_states
return hidden_states
```

Because Eagle3 sets `use_aux_hidden_state_outputs=True`, `_dummy_run`
unconditionally unpacks two values (`hidden_states, _ = outputs`). Unpacking a
bare tensor iterates its first dim (num tokens > 2), raising
`too many values to unpack (expected 2)`.

This is the same class of issue as `Eagle3Qwen3vlForCausalLM`: with reduced
layers the configured aux layers are absent.

### Changes

- Set `use_original_num_layers=True` for `Eagle3DeepseekV2ForCausalLM` in
  `tests/models/registry.py`, so the target keeps its full layer count during
  initialization. Layers 2/30/58 then exist, aux hidden states are collected,
  the model returns the `(hidden_states, aux_hidden_states)` tuple, and the
  unpack succeeds. This matches the existing pattern used by the other Eagle3 /
  speculative entries.
- Also set `max_model_len=8192`. With the full layer count the target
  (`Kimi-K2.5`) is large (~169 GiB of dummy weights), and the default
  `max_model_len` (262144) sizes a KV cache too big to fit alongside the weights,
  causing a `torch.OutOfMemoryError` during KV cache allocation. Reducing
  `max_model_len` shrinks the KV cache so the test fits in CI VRAM (same approach
  already used by other heavy entries in this registry).

## Test Plan

Environment: AMD MI300 (gfx942), ROCm, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` unset (default
`False` → `ROCM_ATTN` backend), matching the AMD CI configuration.

```bash
pytest -x -s "tests/models/test_initialization.py::test_can_initialize_large_subset[Eagle3DeepseekV2ForCausalLM]"
```

## Test Result

- `test_can_initialize_large_subset[Eagle3DeepseekV2ForCausalLM]`: **1 passed**
  (~288 s), previously failed with
  `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)`.


---

- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

I noticed that when I server models with 2048 context window traffic I always get crashes. I never get crashes when serving traffic with 1500 context window.

Memory access fault by GPU node-5 (Agent handle: 0x216a7480) on address 0x76e1b9159000. Reason: Unknown.
GPU core dump failed
(EngineCore pid=1419) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:284] Worker proc VllmWorker-3 died unexpectedly (exit code: None), shutting down executor.


Claude observes the following:
In both crash dumps (dump_input.py), the scheduler state at the moment of death shows a batch of requests at exactly 2050–2051 computed tokens, i.e. the fault fires within 1–2 decode steps of crossing 2048:

Crash 1 (dev245, GPU node-3, VllmWorker-1):

num_computed_tokens=[1901 x5, 1833 x8, 2051 x8]
num_output_tokens=[82 x5, 28 x8, 2 x8]

Crash 2 (dev1000, GPU node-5, VllmWorker-3):

num_computed_tokens=[2051, 2051, 2051, 2051, 2051, 2051, 2050, 2050, 1887 x8, 1893 x8, 1989 x8, 1194 x8, 2044 x8]

Both crashes occurred during pure decode (all scheduled requests at 1 token). KV cache usage was ~0.3–1.3%, so this is not memory pressure. Two different physical GPUs and worker ranks faulted, so it does not appear to be a hardware issue.

title: TRITON_MLA_SPARSE fallback crashes on SM80 during CUDA graph capture
body:
**Title:** TRITON_MLA_SPARSE fallback crashes on SM80 during CUDA graph capture

**vLLM version:** v0.24.0

**Backend:** `TRITON_MLA_SPARSE` (PR [#38476](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38476), head `3740c02`)

**Hardware:** NVIDIA A100 SM80 (12 GPUs, TP=4, PP=3)

**Model:** FenomAI/GLM-5.2-AWQ-INT4 (uses `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend` / DSA sparse attention)

---

PR [#38476](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38476) added `TRITON_MLA_SPARSE` as a sparse attention backend for SM80/SM121, including a Triton fallback in `sparse_attn_indexer.py` when `is_deep_gemm_supported()` returns False. **Two bugs in the decode-path Triton fallback cause engine crashes on SM80:**

### Bug 1: `seq_lens` passed as 2D `[B, next_n]` but Triton expects 1D `[B]`

**Location:** `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py`, decode branch

The DeepGEMM call passes `seq_lens` which is 2D `[B, next_n]`. DeepGEMM's C++ code handles both shapes. But the Triton fallback calls `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_triton()` which expects 1D `context_lens [B]` (see `mqa_logits_triton.py` docstring and kernel launch).

**Fix:**
```python
seq_lens_1d = seq_lens.squeeze(dim=1) if seq_lens.ndim == 2 else seq_lens
# pass seq_lens_1d to fp8_paged_mqa_logits_triton()
```

### Bug 2: Triton fallback uses `active_max_model_len` instead of `max_model_len` — breaks CUDA graph capture

**Location:** same decode branch in `sparse_attn_indexer.py`

The Triton fallback currently passes:
```python
active_max_model_len = attn_metadata_narrowed.max_seq_len  # per-batch, variable
max_model_len=active_max_model_len
```

While DeepGEMM uses:
```python
max_model_len=max_model_len  # configured constant
```

This produces **different tensor shapes** across the `if use_deep_gemm` / `else` branches. During CUDA graph capture with `torch.compile`, the shape mismatch causes downstream ops to fail with:

```
Failed: Cuda error /workspace/csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:455 'an illegal memory access was encountered'
```

**Fix:** Use `max_model_len=max_model_len` in the Triton fallback so both branches produce consistent tensor shapes. The downstream top-k reads only up to `seq_lens` per row, so the padded `-inf` entries are harmless with `clean_logits=False`.

---

**Reproduction:**

Deploy any GLM-DSA model (GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V3.2) on SM80 with:
```yaml
extraEnv:
  - name: VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND
    value: TRITON_MLA_SPARSE
```

Engine crashes during `profile_cudagraph_memory()` phase with the error above. Both bugs must be fixed together — fixing only `seq_lens` leaves the shape mismatch in `max_model_len`.

**Workaround:** Set `VLLM_DISABLE_SPARSE_ATTN=1` to fall back to dense MLA (significantly slower for long context).

title: DeepseekV32IndexerBackend requires --block-size 64 — not documented or auto-detected
body:
**Title:** `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend` requires `--block-size 64` — not documented or auto-detected

**vLLM version:** v0.24.0

**Backend:** `TRITON_MLA_SPARSE` / `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend` (PR [#38476](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38476))

---

`DeepseekV32IndexerBackend` (used by GLM-DSA models via `TRITON_MLA_SPARSE` backend) only supports block size `[64]`:

```python
SUPPORTED_BLOCK_SIZES = [64]
```

However, the KV cache manager defaults to block size `16`. When these don't overlap, `select_common_block_size()` in `vllm/v1/worker/utils.py` raises:

```
ValueError: No common block size for 16 between kv_manager=[16] and backend=[64]
```

This error is opaque and doesn't point users to the solution (`--block-size 64`).

**Proposed fix:** Either:
1. Auto-set block size to 64 when `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend` is selected (similar to how other backends constrain block sizes), OR
2. Add a clear error message: `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend requires --block-size 64, but got --block-size 16`, OR
3. Document the `--block-size 64` requirement in the TRITON_MLA_SPARSE / DSA model deployment guide.

**Affected models:** Any GLM-DSA variant (GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V3.2, etc.) when using `VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=TRITON_MLA_SPARSE`.

title: add pad-aware swiglu limit kernel
body:
## Purpose
When serving with expert-parallelism enabled, the MoE inputs and intermediate states are padded along the token dimension to handle the worst case (i.e. all tokens routed to a single rank; see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py#L32-L33). 

Most MoE kernels have internal logic to ignore such padding tokens during GEMM execution; however, the MoE activation kernels do not currently ignore padding tokens. This PR introduces a padding-aware variant of the swiglu limit activation.

## Test Plan

### Kernel-level Benchmarks 

<details>
<summary> Benchmarking Script </summary>

```python
import itertools

from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

from vllm.benchmarks.lib.utils import default_vllm_config
from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.utils import (
    _swiglu_limit_pad_aware,
    _swiglu_limit_torch,
)
from vllm.triton_utils import triton
from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_random_seed

num_tokens_range = [16, 32, 64, 128, 512, 2048]
hidden_size_range = [7168]
pad_fraction_range = [0.0, 1/2, 3/4, 7/8]
configs = list(
    itertools.product(num_tokens_range, hidden_size_range, pad_fraction_range)
)
SWIGLU_LIMIT = 10.0
TOPK = 6

def _reference(inp: torch.Tensor, limit: float) -> torch.Tensor:
    """High-precision fp32 SwiGLU-limit reference: silu(clamp(gate)) * clamp(up)."""
    d = inp.shape[1] // 2
    gate = inp[:, :d].float().clamp(max=limit)
    up = inp[:, d:].float().clamp(min=-limit, max=limit)
    return F.silu(gate) * up


@default_vllm_config()
def verify_correctness() -> None:
    """Check that routed (non-`-1`) rows match a fp32 reference across all
    providers, and that the pad-aware kernel leaves padded rows untouched.

    Uses an aligned and a non-multiple-of-1024 hidden size to exercise the
    pad-aware kernel's column-masking path.
    """
    device = "cuda"
    set_random_seed(42)
    torch.set_default_device(device)
    dtype = torch.bfloat16
    atol, rtol = 2e-2, 1e-2

    for hidden_size in (4096, 1536):
        num_tokens = 128
        num_rows = num_tokens * TOPK
        inp = torch.randn(num_rows, 2 * hidden_size, dtype=dtype, device=device) * 4

        topk_ids = torch.randint(
            0, 32, (num_tokens, TOPK), dtype=torch.int32, device=device
        )
        pad_idx = torch.randperm(num_rows, device=device)[: num_rows // 2]
        topk_ids.view(-1)[pad_idx] = -1
        routed = topk_ids.view(-1) != -1

        ref = _reference(inp, SWIGLU_LIMIT)

        SENTINEL = 1234.0
        out_pad = torch.full((num_rows, hidden_size), SENTINEL, dtype=dtype)
        _swiglu_limit_pad_aware(out_pad, inp, topk_ids, SWIGLU_LIMIT)

        out_torch = torch.empty(num_rows, hidden_size, dtype=dtype)
        _swiglu_limit_torch(out_torch, inp, SWIGLU_LIMIT)

        out_cuda = torch.empty(num_rows, hidden_size, dtype=dtype)
        torch.ops._C.silu_and_mul_with_clamp(out_cuda, inp, SWIGLU_LIMIT, 1.0, 0.0)

        for name, out in (
            ("pad_aware", out_pad),
            ("torch", out_torch),
            ("cuda", out_cuda),
        ):
            got = out[routed].float()
            want = ref[routed]
            ok = torch.allclose(got, want, atol=atol, rtol=rtol)
            max_abs = (got - want).abs().max().item()
            assert ok, (
                f"[H={hidden_size}] {name} routed rows mismatch: "
                f"max abs diff {max_abs:.3e} > atol {atol}"
            )


@default_vllm_config()
def benchmark_swiglu_limit(
    num_tokens: int,
    hidden_size: int,
    pad_fraction: float,
    provider: str,
):
    device = "cuda"
    set_random_seed(42)
    torch.set_default_device(device)
    dtype = torch.bfloat16

    num_rows = num_tokens * TOPK
    inp = torch.randn(num_rows, 2 * hidden_size, dtype=dtype, device=device) * 4
    output = torch.empty(num_rows, hidden_size, dtype=dtype, device=device)

    topk_ids = torch.randint(
        0, 32, (num_tokens, TOPK), dtype=torch.int32, device=device
    )
    num_pad = int(num_rows * pad_fraction)
    if num_pad:
        pad_idx = torch.randperm(num_rows, device=device)[:num_pad]
        topk_ids.view(-1)[pad_idx] = -1

    if provider == "pad_aware":
        fn = lambda: _swiglu_limit_pad_aware(output, inp, topk_ids, SWIGLU_LIMIT)
    elif provider == "torch":
        fn = lambda: _swiglu_limit_torch(output, inp, SWIGLU_LIMIT)
    elif provider == "cuda":
        fn = lambda: torch.ops._C.silu_and_mul_with_clamp(
            output, inp, SWIGLU_LIMIT, 1.0, 0.0
        )

    torch.cuda.profiler.start()
    times_ms = bench_gpu_time(
        fn,
        use_cuda_graph=True,
        cold_l2_cache=False,
    )
    torch.cuda.profiler.stop()

    ms, min_ms, max_ms = torch.quantile(
        torch.as_tensor(times_ms, dtype=torch.float64, device="cpu"),
        torch.tensor([0.5, 0.2, 0.8], dtype=torch.float64, device="cpu"),
    ).tolist()

    return ms * 1e3, max_ms * 1e3, min_ms * 1e3


if __name__ == "__main__":
    verify_correctness()

    perf_report = triton.testing.perf_report(
        triton.testing.Benchmark(
            x_names=["num_tokens", "hidden_size", "pad_fraction"],
            x_vals=configs,
            line_arg="provider",
            line_vals=["pad_aware", "torch", "cuda"],
            line_names=[
                "Persistent pad-aware (Triton)",
                "Torch",
                "CUDA",
            ],
            styles=[
                ("blue", "-"),
                ("green", "-"),
                ("red", "-"),
            ],
            ylabel="us",
            plot_name="swiglu-limit-performance",
            args={},
        )
    )

    df = perf_report(
        lambda num_tokens, hidden_size, pad_fraction, provider: benchmark_swiglu_limit(
            num_tokens, hidden_size, pad_fraction, provider
        )
    ).run(print_data=False, return_df=True)

    persistent = df["Persistent pad-aware (Triton) (us)"]
    cuda = df["CUDA (us)"]
    df["Persistent speedup vs CUDA"] = (cuda / persistent).round(2)
    df["Persistent speedup vs Torch"] = (df["Torch (us)"] / persistent).round(2)
    print("swiglu-limit-performance:")
    print(df.to_string())

```

</details>

| Padding Proportion | Tokens | Pad-Aware Kernel µs | Torch Kernel µs | CUDA Kernel µs |
| ------------------ | ------ | ------------------- | --------------- | -------------- |
| 0                  | 16     | 2.36                | 4.00            | 3.08           |
|                    | 64     | 4.36                | 10.65           | 5.88           |
|                    | 128    | 6.68                | 20.11           | 10.09          |
|                    | 512    | 33.77               | 74.95           | 38.71          |
|                    | 2048   | 133.34              | 292.81          | 149.17         |
| 1/2                | 16     | 2.37                | 4.00            | 3.10           |
|                    | 64     | 3.71                | 10.64           | 5.85           |
|                    | 128    | 5.08                | 19.99           | 10.16          |
|                    | 512    | 18.54               | 74.98           | 38.67          |
|                    | 2048   | 68.10               | 306.08          | 164.76         |
| 3/4                | 16     | 2.21                | 3.92            | 3.14           |
|                    | 64     | 3.21                | 10.63           | 5.85           |
|                    | 128    | 4.29                | 20.11           | 10.07          |
|                    | 512    | 10.27               | 75.02           | 38.68          |
|                    | 2048   | 39.12               | 294.86          | 150.12         |
| 7/8                | 16     | 2.04                | 3.95            | 3.11           |
|                    | 64     | 2.71                | 10.61           | 5.87           |
|                    | 128    | 3.29                | 19.92           | 10.05          |
|                    | 512    | 7.32                | 74.97           | 38.67          |
|                    | 2048   | 26.37               | 294.90          | 148.95         |


### End-to-End benchmarks

Benchmarked `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro` on 4 nodes with 8xH200 each (EP=32)

1k/1k conc=512
|                 | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT |
| --------------- | ------------ | --------- | --------- |
| Before          | 5566.2       | 9081.7    | 83.13     |
| After (this PR) | 5660.9       | 8982      | 81.66     |

Benefits is more pronounced in decode-only workloads:

| --------------- | ------------ | --------- | --------- |

| After (this PR) | 6635.7       | 251.8     | 75.68     |

**After:** flexible-extract=0.9454 | strict-match=0.9447

title: [Bugfix] DeepSeek V3/V3.1 tool parsers: emit tool calls that arrive in a single streaming delta
body:
## Purpose

When an entire tool call arrives in one streaming delta, the DeepSeek V3 and V3.1 tool parsers emit nothing — the call is silently lost. Their streaming state machines advance at most one state per invocation, gated on begin/end token counts: with a complete call in one delta, `start_count == end_count`, so the "starting a new tool" branch never fires (`current_tool_id` stays `-1`) and the closing branch bails at `len(self.prev_tool_call_arr) == 0`. Single-delta delivery is real in production: speculative decoding accepts multiple tokens per step (DeepSeek's MTP is a mainstream deployment), and the reasoning→tool transition re-delivers all accumulated text as one delta (`vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py:862`).

Rather than patching the count gates, this replaces the state machine with the reparse-and-drain shape used by the parsers that don't have this bug (`pythonic`, `hermes`): every invocation re-parses all tool-call blocks from the accumulated text — complete blocks and the trailing in-progress one — and streams whatever hasn't been sent yet for every call, however many arrived in this delta. Names are emitted once (with the first argument diff, if any); argument diffs keep the existing `streamed_args_for_tool` prefix accounting, so the finalize flush (`get_remaining_unstreamed_args`) stays consistent. Token-by-token behavior is unchanged: with small deltas the drain loop visits one call at a time, matching the old emission order. Net −209 lines per parser.

Same bug class as #47907, fixed for granite/gigachat3 in #47955; the DeepSeek parsers are not covered by any open PR.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv3_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv31_tool_parser.py
```

## Test Result

```
22 passed, 1 xfailed (xfail pre-existing)
```

New regression tests: single tool call in one delta and two parallel tool calls in one delta, for both parsers. A CPU harness comparing streaming reconstruction against non-streaming ground truth: before, all four single-delta cases streamed `[]`; after, all match, and incremental multi-chunk streaming matches ground truth (one pre-existing v3.1 quirk where a chunk boundary splits a marker mid-token is unchanged — impossible in production since markers are atomic special tokens, and the old code corrupted that case worse).

No open PR or issue covers this (searched deepseek tool parser/streaming; #48001/#47704/#47503 touch other aspects). Written with AI assistance; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Model] Add LongCat-2.0 (LongCat Sparse Attention + MTP)
body:
## What

Support for [meituan-longcat/LongCat-2.0-FP8](https://huggingface.co/meituan-longcat/LongCat-2.0-FP8) (arch `LongcatCausalLM`): the LongCat-Flash-Lite backbone (dual-attention MLA, zero-expert MoE, n-gram embedding) plus a DeepSeek-V3.2-style sparse attention indexer, reusing vLLM's existing DSA infrastructure (`Indexer`, shared `topk_indices_buffer`, `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`/`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`).

Not a duplicate: no open PR or issue covers LongCat-2.0 (the open LongCat PRs are a Rust tool parser, #45773, and the unrelated LongCat-Next multimodal model, #46623). Reference implementation is sgl-project/sglang#30275; there is no HF `modeling_*.py`.

### Model wiring
- The checkpoint ships `model_type: null` with no remote code, so the arch resolves to a registered `LongcatFlashNgramConfig` (subclass of transformers' `LongcatFlashConfig`) that aliases the `oe_*` n-gram fields.
- Cross-Layer Indexing (`cli_factor=2`): only the first attention of each layer computes DSA top-k indices; the second reuses them through the shared buffer. `DeepseekV2MLAAttention` gains a generic `skip_topk: bool | None` override; the schedule itself lives in `longcat_flash.py`.
- Streaming-aware indexing: the first `index_init_tokens` and last `index_local_tokens` positions are forced into the top-k set (config-driven, inert for other models).
- MTP speculative decoding: the checkpoint has one MTP module applied for up to `mtp_num_layers=3` draft steps, with plain token embedding (`mtp_disable_over_tokenizer`) and FP8 indexer weights (incl. an FP8 `weights_proj`, which the main model stores in BF16).
- `--reasoning-parser longcat` for the `<longcat_think>` tags (the chat template pre-appends the start token, DeepSeek-R1 style). `--tool-call-parser longcat` already existed.

### Bug fixes (also affect merged LongCat-Flash-Lite)
- The post-load `mla_scale_q_lora/kv_lora` fold silently dropped the scales when `load_weights` ran incrementally (AutoWeightsLoader splits the stream per child prefix): the first call folded still-default layernorm weights and set the reapplication guard, the second call overwrote them with raw checkpoint values. Fold at weight-load time instead (order-independent). Lite only worked by weight-file ordering luck.
- N-gram left-context is now rebuilt each step from the runner's accepted-token history instead of rolled incrementally, so rejected speculative-draft tokens never pollute it (found as a 5.7-sigma GSM8K regression, 0.901 -> 0.854, when MTP was first enabled; fixed back to 0.905).
- EOS-position n-gram hashing now matches the HF reference: an EOS current token hashes with its full look-back; only later positions' look-back stops at the EOS boundary. Matters for any prompt containing EOS (multi-turn chat). Unit test included (`tests/kernels/test_ngram_embedding.py`).
- LongCat model types added to `_DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL_EXCLUDED_MODEL_TYPES` (non-ue8m0 block scales; SGLang applies the same guard). On vLLM's stack we measured DeepGEMM-linear as GSM8K-neutral (0.908 vs 0.901 full set), so this is precautionary steering, not a correctness requirement.

## Tested (8xB300, TP8)

```bash
vllm serve meituan-longcat/LongCat-2.0-FP8 -tp 8
# with speculative decoding:
vllm serve meituan-longcat/LongCat-2.0-FP8 -tp 8 \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
    --reasoning-parser longcat
# eval:
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319
# unit test:
pytest tests/kernels/test_ngram_embedding.py  # 1 passed
```

| Config | GSM8K (1319q) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| TP8 | 0.901 | 731 |
| TP8 + MTP k=3 | 0.905 | 1662 (2.3x, 82.5% draft acceptance) |
| TP8 + EP8 + MTP k=3 | 0.910 (200q) | 1748 |
| SGLang (same harness, sglang#30275 branch) | 0.900 (100q) | — |

Also verified: 5K-token needle retrieval exact (exercises real sparse top-k selection past the 2048 window), greedy outputs match SGLang, LongCat-Flash-Lite regression outputs unchanged, MTP outputs byte-identical to non-speculative greedy.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for this PR; every change was reviewed and all tests/evals above were run on real hardware.

title: [Bugfix] Honor DeepSeek V4 checkpoints' MTP-layer compress_ratio entry (unscaled draft rope)
body:
## Purpose

The released DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark config has `num_hidden_layers=43` and additional `compress_ratios` entries, including zero-valued draft entries. `DeepseekV4Attention` currently ignores every entry at `layer_id >= num_hidden_layers` and uses ratio 1 with YaRN rope.

This change honors an in-range draft entry, clamps its operational cache ratio to at least 1, and uses a zero entry to select default rope. Draft layers beyond the list retain the existing ratio-1/YaRN fallback.

It also copies `rope_parameters` before per-layer updates and requests an FP32 rope cache; DeepSeek V4 kernels read that cache directly as FP32.

## Duplicate check

#41834 carries this change within a broad SM12x enablement branch. This PR isolates the three DeepSeek V4 source files and focused tests on main.

## Tests

`pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_rope.py`: 12 passed in the SM120 serving image. The tests are CPU-only.

## Model evaluation

In a matched TP=2 DSpark MTP:2 serving A/B, mean draft acceptance changed from 57% to 69%, and position-2 acceptance changed from 0.275 to 0.50. Rope selection and the FP32 cache change were tested together.

Created with AI assistance.

title: [RFC] Training-Inference Consistency for RL
body:
# [RFC] Training-Inference Consistency for RL

**Anchors**: [#42259](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42259) (Logprobs), [#39568](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39568) (R3), [#45221](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45221) (Data Plane)

## Problem

RL training correctness requires that for the same sample, weights, and routing strategy, the trainer and rollout engine observe identical results. Eight consistency dimensions:

1. **Numerical consistency** — batch shape must not introduce avoidable numerical differences in inference; batch invariance is one component, not a complete trainer–inference parity guarantee.
2. **Logprobs & token-ID replay** — logprob mismatch → importance sampling ratio corruption → noisy policy gradient. `trace_decode_token_ids` ([#46701](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46701)) enables replaying a fixed token sequence while computing real logprobs.
3. **R3 routing replay** — MoE expert routing must be captured during inference and replayed during training. Mismatch → gradients computed on wrong experts.
4. **DSA index replay** — DeepSeek V3.2+ dynamic sparse attention indices must match between inference and training.
5. **Data plane** — logprobs, routed_experts, and DSA indices must be transported from inference GPU workers to trainer efficiently, bypassing the EngineCore/API Server bottleneck.
6. **Hidden states replay** — OPD requires exporting intermediate-layer hidden states from teacher to student, avoiding full `[tokens, vocab]` logit transfer.
7. **Dtype (logits precision)** — Inference must match training's fp32 precision for lm_head to maintain train-inference consistency.
8. **Per-request weight provenance** — each output token and its logprob must identify the model weight version that actually produced it, including requests that span an update boundary.

## Subsections

### 3.1 Numerical Consistency

Current batch-invariance tracker: [#27433](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/27433). Batch invariance is one component of training–inference numerical consistency, not a full parity guarantee.

### 3.2 Logprobs & Token-ID Replay

Full tracker: [#42259](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42259). Exit: #47680 + #42245 merged; #46701 accepted.

### 3.3 R3 Routing Replay

- [ ] [#44214](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44214): FlashInfer + R3
- [ ] [#45419](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45419): P/D disagg + R3
- [ ] [#45635](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45635): KV offload + R3
- [ ] [#37094](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37094): Align routed_experts with streamed output spans

Exit: R3 works on FlashInfer + P/D + KV-offload; R3 correctness test in RL CI.

### 3.4 DSA Index Replay

- [ ] [#47280](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47280): RFC — `--enable-return-indexer-topk`
- [ ] [#47279](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47279): Implementation

No downstream demand yet. Forward-looking for DeepSeek V4+ RL adoption. Exit: RFC accepted.

### 3.5 Data Plane

- [ ] [#47809](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47809): Artifact transfer connector (bypasses EngineCore/API Server bottleneck)
- [ ] [vime#320](https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/pull/320): TransferQueue trajectory ingestion for closed-loop training

Exit: at least one data plane backend merged; R3 transport E2E verified.

### 3.6 Hidden States Replay

- [ ] [#37002](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37002): Observation Plugin — register plugins to intercept layer outputs via PyTorch hooks (Phase 1: API; Phase 2: model runner integration)

Exit: Observation Plugin Phase 2 merged.

### 3.7 Dtype Replay

- [x] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48390

### 3.8 Per-Request Weight Provenance

Merged [#49040](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49040) adds an EngineCore weight-version label and query/update APIs. It does not bind a version to a request or token: querying the current version after generation cannot identify which weights produced earlier output.

Detailed design and background: [#54443](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54443), which defines per-output token spans and their capture, delivery, and boundary semantics.

- [ ] Return `weight_versions` as contiguous generated-token ranges `[start, end)` for each output sequence, with `model_id` at the sequence level; the ranges must cover every output token and its logprob exactly once.
- [ ] Stamp the version used by the target model step, not the version at response assembly or query time. A kept request that crosses a committed version change must return separate ranges for each version.
- [ ] Define the contract for streaming, speculative decoding, and DP replicas; test single-version output, a request crossing a successful update, and a failed update.

The version is caller-managed metadata, not proof that the supplied weights match a checkpoint. A metadata-only update must not be presented as evidence of a weight transfer.

## Feedback Period

Two weeks from posting.

title: [XPU] FP8 o_proj with fp8_bmm and load-time scale transpose
body:
## Summary

Replace the BF16 reference `_o_proj` path (`rocm_inv_rope_einsum`) in XPU DeepSeek-V4 attention with a native FP8 BMM path using `fp8_bmm`, and optimize scale handling by moving transpose+reshape to load time.

## Changes

**`vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/xpu.py`**
- Restore `process_weights_after_loading` in `XPUFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`:
  - Transpose `weight_scale_inv` from checkpoint layout `[N/128, K/128]` to oneDNN layout `[K/128, N/128]` at load time (reverts PR #47116 runtime transpose)
  - For BMM layers (`wo_a` with `is_bmm=True`), precompute 3D scale `[n_groups, K/bs, lora_rank/bs]` as `layer.bmm_scale`
- Remove runtime `Bs.t().contiguous()` in `apply_block_scaled_mm` — scale is already transposed

**`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/xpu/xpu_sparse.py`**
- Replace BF16 `rocm_inv_rope_einsum` with FP8 path:
  - Use `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` for fused inverse RoPE + FP8 quantization
  - Use `torch.ops._xpu_C.fp8_bmm` for batched FP8 GEMM across `n_groups`
- Use precomputed `self.wo_a.bmm_scale` instead of per-call reshape/permute/contiguous
- Read `weight_block_size` from model config instead of hardcoded constant

**`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py`**
- Fix `launch_pdl` kwarg passing for XPU Triton compatibility

## Performance

- Eliminates per-call `Bs.t().contiguous()` in `apply_block_scaled_mm` (all block FP8 linear layers)
- Eliminates per-call scale reshape + permute + contiguous in `_o_proj` (precomputed at load time)
- Replaces BF16 dequant+einsum `wo_a` path with native FP8 BMM

## Testing

GSM8K accuracy on DeepSeek-V4-Flash (8x Intel B70, TP=8, FP8 KV cache): 0.952.

title: [Bugfix] Disable FA3 AOT scheduling for spec-decode proposer
body:
## Summary

Fixes [this](https://gist.github.com/elvircrn/70adb4b040fe9f6dca38a3116986d18c.).

- Pass `fast_build=True` from the speculator through `build_attn_metadata()` so FA3 skips AOT scheduling for draft model attention
- `get_scheduler_metadata` hardcodes `is_varlen=true` while `mha_fwd` derives it from actual tensor shapes — this divergence causes `metadata_size` mismatch and a `CHECK_SHAPE` crash on Hopper GPUs with spec-decode
- `fast_build=True` makes `scheduler_metadata=None` so `mha_fwd` allocates its own internally, avoiding the mismatch

Fixes #48221

## Test plan

- [x] `pre-commit run ruff-check --all-files` passes
- [ ] Verify DSpark spec-decode with FA3 on Hopper no longer crashes with `scheduler_metadata must have shape (metadata_size)`

AI assistance was used. Not duplicating an existing PR — no open PRs address this specific crash path.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek V3 streaming tool parser truncates final arguments not ending with '"}' when the end token shares the delta
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

Pure-Python logic bug in the DeepSeek V3 streaming tool parser, reproducible on current `main` on any hardware — no GPU needed.

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

In `DeepSeekV3ToolParser.extract_tool_calls_streaming` (`--tool-call-parser deepseek_v3`), when the final characters of the tool arguments arrive in the **same streamed delta** as the `<｜tool▁call▁end｜>` token (which happens with async scheduling / `stream_interval > 1`), the "tool call is being closed" branch reconstructs the unstreamed tail with a hard-coded `"}` heuristic:

```python
if '"}' not in delta_text:
    return None
end_loc = delta_text.rindex('"}')
diff = delta_text[:end_loc] + '"}'
```

This assumes arguments always end with a quoted string. Consequences:

- Arguments ending with a **number, boolean, null, or array**: the tail is dropped entirely (`return None`), so the client receives invalid truncated JSON. Example: deltas `['...get_code\n```json\n', '{"code": 1', '23}\n```<｜tool▁call▁end｜>']` stream as `{"code": 1` while non-streaming correctly returns `{"code": 123}`.
- Arguments ending with a **nested object**: `rindex('"}')` cuts at the inner `"}`, dropping the outer closing braces. Example: `{"a": {"b": "x"}}` streams as `{"a": {"b": "x"}`.
- Control: arguments ending with a quoted string (`..."Tokyo"}`) stream correctly, confirming the bug is specific to the `"}` assumption.

There is also dead code in the same branch: `diff.encode("utf-8").decode("unicode_escape") if diff is str else diff` compares against the *type object* (`is str`), which is always `False`.

The existing tests stream strictly one token per delta, so this multi-token-delta path is untested (with per-token deltas, all argument characters are streamed before the end token arrives and the closing branch has nothing to flush).

Note: the V3.1 parser (`deepseekv31_tool_parser.py`) shares this heuristic; it is partially reworked by open PR #38866 (for the `"` / `}`-in-separate-deltas case), so this issue is scoped to the **V3** parser, which no open PR touches.

Fix (PR incoming): extract the completed arguments from the full tool-call text with the existing `stream_tool_call_portion_regex` and emit exactly the not-yet-streamed part, instead of guessing the tail from `delta_text`.

title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] DeepSeek V3: don't truncate final streamed tool arguments that don't end with '"}'
body:
FIX #48342

## Purpose

When the final characters of tool arguments arrive in the same streamed delta as the `<｜tool▁call▁end｜>` token (async scheduling, `stream_interval > 1`), the DeepSeek V3 parser's closing branch reconstructed the unstreamed tail from `delta_text` assuming arguments always end with `"}`:

- arguments ending with a **number/boolean/null/array** → the tail was dropped entirely, clients received invalid truncated JSON (`{"code": 1` instead of `{"code": 123}`);
- arguments ending with a **nested object** → cut at the inner `"}`, dropping outer braces (`{"a": {"b": "x"}` instead of `{"a": {"b": "x"}}`);
- arguments ending with a quoted string worked, confirming the heuristic's exact boundary.

Instead of guessing from `delta_text`, this PR extracts the completed arguments from the full tool-call text with the existing `stream_tool_call_portion_regex` and emits exactly the not-yet-streamed part (`expected_args[len(already_streamed):]`). It also removes the dead `diff is str` branch (comparison against the type object, always `False`).

**Scope / duplicate check:** the V3.1 parser shares this heuristic but is partially reworked by open PR #38866, so this PR intentionally touches only the V3 parser (`deepseekv3_tool_parser.py`), which no open PR modifies. Also checked #47704 (V3.2/V4 whitespace deltas — different files) and #48001/#48006 (different layers).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv3_tool_parser.py
```

New parametrized streaming test places the final argument characters and the end token in one delta, covering number/boolean/nested-object tails plus a quoted-string control. The existing common tests (one token per delta) cover the unchanged paths.

## Test Result

On the parent commit, the three non-control cases fail exactly as described; the control passes. With this change:

```text
20 passed, 1 xfailed in 24.59s
```

(The xfail is a pre-existing, documented malformed-input case.) Linux/CPU, Python 3.12, real DeepSeek-V3 tokenizer. `pre-commit` (ruff check/format, mypy, typos) passes on the changed files.

title: [Bug]: xpu_mla_sparse NaN-poisons attention output when a row's leading topk index chunk is fully masked
body:
### Your current environment

The defect is in device-agnostic Triton source (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/xpu_mla_sparse.py`), analyzed on vLLM main @ `54503ec`. Reproduced with Triton 3.7.1 — the repro below runs on any GPU, and even under `TRITON_INTERPRET=1` on CPU, since it is a pure numerics bug, not a device one.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`_bf16_mla_sparse_kernel` NaN-poisons its output whenever the **first `BLOCK_N` (=16) topk index entries of a row are all masked** (`-1` padding or `>= seq_kv`), even though valid keys follow later in the index list.

**Mechanism** (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/xpu_mla_sparse.py`):

- L76: the running max starts at `-inf`: `e_max = tl.zeros([BLOCK_H], dtype=tl.float32) - float("inf")`
- L125: a fully-masked chunk sets every logit to `-inf`: `qk = tl.where(mask, qk, -float("inf"))`
- L139–141:
  ```python
  n_e_max = tl.maximum(tl.max(qk, 1), e_max)   # max(-inf, -inf) = -inf
  re_scale = tl.exp2(e_max - n_e_max)          # exp2(-inf - -inf) = exp2(nan) = nan
  p = tl.exp2(qk - n_e_max[:, None])           # nan
  ```
  `acc *= re_scale` and `e_sum = e_sum * re_scale + tl.sum(p, 1)` are then permanently poisoned — `nan × 0 = nan`, so no later valid chunk can rescue the accumulator. The NaNs flow silently into the attention output.

A row with **no valid key at all** likewise returns NaN (`0/0` at the epilogue), where the in-tree reference (`reference_mla_sparse_prefill` in `tests/kernels/attention/test_xpu_mla_sparse.py`, L67–69) explicitly defines the output of such rows as **zeros**.

**Blast radius** — every caller of `triton_bf16_mla_sparse_interface`:
- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/xpu_mla_sparse.py` L219 (XPU_MLA_SPARSE backend forward)
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/xpu/xpu_sparse.py` L342 (DSA prefill)
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/xpu/xpu_sparse_decode_fp8.py` L282 (fp8 decode wrapper)

**Why the existing test doesn't catch it:** `test_bf16_triton_sparse_mla` writes valid indices at the *front* of each row and pads with `-1` at the *back* (L98–102), so a leading chunk is never fully masked. Trailing padding is benign (by then `e_max` is finite). The newer sparse-MLA kernel from #47629 already avoids this exact pattern with a finite sentinel; this kernel predates that.

### Minimal repro

```python
# Run on any GPU; runs on CPU too via the Triton interpreter (auto-enabled).
import os
import torch
if not torch.cuda.is_available():
    os.environ["TRITON_INTERPRET"] = "1"
from vllm.v1.attention.ops.xpu_mla_sparse import triton_bf16_mla_sparse_interface

torch.manual_seed(0)
dev = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
T, HQ, DQK, DV, TOPK = 2, 16, 576, 512, 64        # TOPK % BLOCK_N(16) == 0
q  = torch.randn(T, HQ, DQK, device=dev)
kv = torch.randn(T, 1,  DQK, device=dev)          # seq_kv = 2
idx = torch.full((T, 1, TOPK), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
idx[0, 0, 16] = 0   # token 0: its only valid index sits AFTER the first BLOCK_N chunk
idx[1, 0, 0]  = 0   # token 1: valid index inside the first chunk (control)

out, max_logits, lse = triton_bf16_mla_sparse_interface(q, kv, idx, sm_scale=DQK ** -0.5)
print("token0 finite:", bool(out[0].isfinite().all()))   # False  <-- BUG
print("token1 finite:", bool(out[1].isfinite().all()))   # True
```

Output on main @ `54503ec`:

```
token0 finite: False   # all-NaN output despite a valid attention target
token1 finite: True
```

### Fix

Replace `-inf` with a finite sentinel (`-1.0e30`) for the running-max init and the masked logits — the same approach the newer sparse-MLA kernel in #47629 uses. Mixed chunks are unaffected (`exp2(-1e30 - m)` is exactly `0.0` in fp32); leading fully-masked chunks get rescaled away exactly; rows with no valid key produce zeros, matching the reference. Two lines, no perf change. PR with a regression test incoming.

title: [Bugfix] Prevent NaN poisoning in xpu_mla_sparse for fully-masked index chunks
body:
FIX #48364

## Purpose

`_bf16_mla_sparse_kernel` (the XPU sparse-MLA kernel behind `XPU_MLA_SPARSE`, DeepSeek-V4 XPU prefill, and the fp8 decode wrapper) NaN-poisons its output whenever the first `BLOCK_N` (=16) topk index entries of a row are all masked, even though valid keys follow later:

- the running max starts at `-inf`, and a fully-masked chunk sets every logit to `-inf`;
- `re_scale = exp2(-inf - -inf) = NaN` then poisons `acc` and `e_sum` permanently (`nan * 0 = nan`), so later valid chunks cannot recover the row.

A row with no valid key at all likewise returns NaN (`0/0`), where the in-tree reference (`reference_mla_sparse_prefill`) explicitly defines zeros.

The fix replaces `-inf` with a finite sentinel (`-1.0e30`) for the running-max init and the masked logits — the same approach the newer sparse-MLA kernel in #47629 uses. Two lines, no perf change:

- chunks mixing valid and masked keys are unaffected: `exp2(-1e30 - m)` is exactly `0.0` in fp32;
- leading fully-masked chunks are rescaled away exactly once a valid chunk arrives;
- rows with no valid key produce zeros, matching the reference semantics.

The existing test never catches this because it writes valid indices at the front of each row and pads with `-1` at the back — trailing padding is benign. The added regression test covers leading + trailing masked chunks and a fully-masked row.

## Test Plan

- Minimal repro in #48364 (runs on any GPU, or CPU via `TRITON_INTERPRET=1` — it is a pure numerics bug).
- New `test_bf16_triton_sparse_mla_masked_chunks`: verified bidirectionally on the kernel via the Triton interpreter — it FAILS (NaN) on the unfixed kernel and passes on the fixed one, with `out`/`max_logits`/`lse` matching `reference_mla_sparse_prefill` within the file's existing tolerances.
- `test_bf16_triton_sparse_mla` (existing) is unaffected: for any row containing at least one valid key in its first chunk, the sentinel path computes bit-identical `p`/`re_scale` values.

## Test Result

```
[broken] out finite: False            # regression test catches the bug
[fixed]  out finite: True
[fixed]  out[:2]  allclose vs reference: True  (max |d| = 0.0075, bf16 store rounding)
[fixed]  max_logits allclose: True  (max |d| = 2e-6)
[fixed]  lse        allclose: True  (max |d| < 1e-6)
[fixed]  fully-masked row == zeros: True
```

title: [Bugfix] Handle malformed DeepSeek V3 tool calls
body:
## Summary

Fix the DeepSeek V3 non-streaming tool parser fallback when model output contains the outer tool-call marker but no complete tool-call match.

Previously, `tool_call_regex.findall()` could return no matches while the parser still returned `tools_called=True` with an empty `tool_calls` list. This violated the extraction invariant that `tools_called` should reflect whether any tool calls were successfully parsed.

The parser now:

- returns `tools_called=False`;
- returns an empty `tool_calls` list;
- preserves the complete original model output as content.

The stale non-streaming expected failure was removed, and a focused regression test was added for the no-match case.

## Testing

title: [RFC]: fp8 KV cache for the Ampere sparse-MLA path (TRITON_MLA_SPARSE) via software dequant
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

**`TRITON_MLA_SPARSE` (#47629) is bf16-KV-only, and on 24 GB cards that is the binding constraint.** I have a working sm_80/sm_86 fp8 KV path and would like to know whether the project wants it before I polish it into a mergeable PR.

#### The gap, in the PR's own words

`TritonMLASparseBackend` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/triton_mla_sparse.py`):

```python
supported_kv_cache_dtypes: ClassVar[list[CacheDType]] = ["auto", "float16", "bfloat16"]
```

its decode entry point is literally `_forward_bf16_kv`, and the base it inherits refuses quantized KV outright (`xpu_mla_sparse.py:238`):

```python
if is_quantized_kv_cache(self.kv_cache_dtype):
    raise NotImplementedError("FP8 kv is not supported with XPU MLA Sparse yet")
```

The stated reason fp8 is excluded on Ampere is that Triton cannot handle `fp8e4nv` there. That is true for **native** fp8 — and irrelevant for fp8 **as storage**.

#### The technique is already in this very PR

`vllm/v1/attention/ops/mqa_logits_triton.py:191`, added by #47629 itself:

```python
# Kernel decodes FP8 from uint8 via LUT (SM80 Triton can't load fp8e4nv).
```

The indexer already reads fp8 pages on SM80 by loading them as `uint8` and decoding in-register. **The KV path simply hasn't had the same treatment.** (`models/deepseek_v4/xpu/xpu_sparse_decode_fp8.py` does the same thing for XPU: *"dequantize FP8 KV cache pages to BF16 on the fly, then reuse the BF16 sparse MLA attention kernel"*.) So the precedent is accepted in-tree, twice, and neither conflicts with #43914 / #47060's "native FP8 requires SM89+" — software dequant is a different mechanism.

#### What I did

An `IS_FP8: tl.constexpr` branch inside **your own** `_sparse_mla_compute_tile` — the single function through which both `_sparse_mla_kernel_final` and `_sparse_mla_kernel_split` load KV — so fp8 inherits your split-KV, your merge kernel, your autotune and your masking for free. The standard 656-byte `fp8_ds_mla` page is loaded as raw `uint8` and decoded with bit-math that is **bit-exact vs `torch.float8_e4m3fn` over all 256 byte values**. Nothing about the cache layout changes; the existing C++ `concat_and_cache_ds_mla` writer already runs on sm_86 unmodified (`ENABLE_FP8` is CUDA-version-gated, not arch-gated — verified by execution).

Patch (224 lines, applies to `bbe2ab4d6`, one flag / one branch / one dispatcher arg): https://github.com/nickus/vllm-fp8kv/blob/main/patches/triton_mla_sparse_fp8.patch

#### Measured on RTX 3090 (sm_86) — including the part that is not good news

| | |
|---|---|
| fp8 dequant, all 256 byte values | **bit-exact** vs `torch.float8_e4m3fn` |
| Decode vs fp32 reference, through vLLM's **own C++ `ds_mla` writer** and **own `triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index`** | **cosine 0.999996** |
| KV pool capacity | **1.756×** (656 B vs 1152 B/token); **~1.63×** effective once the indexer's own K-cache is counted |
| Decode speed vs bf16, same kernel, bs=8 / topk=2048 | **0.92×** |
| Decode speed vs bf16, same kernel, bs=32 / topk=2048 | **0.45×** |

**So this is a capacity-for-speed trade, not a free win**, and I would rather say so up front than have it found in review. At bs=32 fp8 decode is currently ~2.2× slower. My working hypothesis is that the autotune *config lists* (`_FINAL_AUTOTUNE_CONFIGS`: `BLOCK_N=16` only; `_SPLIT_AUTOTUNE_CONFIGS`: `BLOCK_N=32` only) are tuned for bf16's 1152 B rows and that fp8's 656 B rows plus a scale load want larger blocks — but **I have not measured that on the real kernel yet**, so I am flagging it as a hypothesis, not a finding. On a 24 GB card the 1.76× capacity may well be worth the decode cost; on an A100 it plainly is not, which is an argument for keeping this opt-in.

#### What is NOT done

* The patch above is **kernel-only** and therefore inert on its own: the backend still declares bf16-only dtypes, `get_kv_cache_shape` returns a 576-wide row for every dtype (fp8_ds_mla needs 656 — `flashmla_sparse.py` already handles this), and `_canonicalize_sparse_mla_kv_cache_dtype` maps `fp8_e4m3 -> fp8_ds_mla` only for FLASHMLA_SPARSE / SM120. I have that wiring working out-of-tree; it is ~40 more lines.
* **No engine-level boot yet.** All correctness numbers above are kernel-level. I have not yet run `LLM(..., kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3")` end-to-end and compared logits against a bf16 run.

#### The questions

1. Does the project **want** fp8 KV on the Ampere sparse-MLA path, given it buys ~1.76× KV capacity at a decode cost that is currently significant at larger batch?
2. If yes: kernel-only PR first (the diff above, dispatch dormant until the backend declares the dtype), or one PR including the backend wiring?
3. Any objection to the fp8-as-storage / software-dequant approach in the shared `_sparse_mla_compute_tile`, given `mqa_logits_triton.py` already does exactly this on SM80?

Happy to do the engine boot + logits parity and the config-list measurement before opening the PR — I just want to know the feature is wanted first.

---

*Unrelated bug found while working on this path, already filed: #48364 / #48366 (fully-masked leading index chunks NaN-poison `xpu_mla_sparse`).*

### Alternatives considered

* **Native fp8 (`fp8e4nv`) on Ampere** — impossible; that is the constraint the PR itself documents.
* **Dequantize whole pages to bf16 before the kernel** — what the XPU path does; costs a full bf16 materialization of the gathered KV, which throws away the bandwidth saving that is the entire point on a 24 GB card.
* **Keep bf16 KV and shrink the model instead** — what 3090/4090 owners do today; it is why GLM-5.2-class DSA models are effectively unusable at long context on consumer Ampere.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/vllm) users if needed.

title: [BugFix] Honor drop_eagle_block in MambaManager
body:
## Purpose

On a hybrid model (full-attention + Mamba/GDN layers, e.g. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B), enabling MTP/EAGLE
speculative decoding together with prefix caching corrupts the recurrent state, and the server
serves wrong answers. #43559 reports tool-eval accuracy dropping from ~90% to ~50%. Nothing raises
an exception and nothing shows up in the logs, so an operator has no signal that anything is wrong,
and prefix caching then spreads it, because the corrupted state is hash-reachable and every later
request sharing that prefix restores from it.

The root cause is the `find_longest_cache_hit` method on `MambaManager`, at
`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1049` on `main`, which takes `drop_eagle_block` in its
signature and never acts on it. Its body searches right-to-left for the last cached block, builds
`[null]*i + [cached]`, and breaks, referencing neither `drop_eagle_block` nor `.pop(`.

Every other manager that can receive the flag handles it:

| Manager | Behavior on `drop_eagle_block` |
|---|---|
| `FullAttentionManager` (:603) | `if drop_eagle_block and computed_blocks[0]: computed.pop()` |
| `SlidingWindowManager` (:763) | pops |
| `ChunkedLocalAttentionManager` (:936) | asserts `drop_eagle_block is False` rather than mishandle it |
| `MambaManager` (:1049) | **accepts the flag and silently ignores it** |

EAGLE/MTP requires the final matched block of a cache hit be dropped and recomputed, because it can
hold state written over draft positions that verification later rejects. Full-attention honors that.
The Mamba group keeps its final block, whose recurrent-state snapshot was taken over those
unverified positions. The one-block length mismatch between the two groups is how the bug is
detected; the harm is that the retained snapshot is restored and reused.

It propagates rather than getting masked. The coordinator's fixed-point loop only shrinks the
candidate length when a group reports a *shorter* hit. Mamba reports a *longer* one, so nothing
converges downward, and the final `hit_length` is the un-dropped mamba length
(`kv_cache_coordinator.py:732`).

The configuration that triggers this is the only one Qwen3.6 can be in. `is_eagle_group = True` is
set in exactly one place, `kv_cache_utils.py:1715`, inside `_annotate_eagle_groups_deepseek_v4`,
which early-returns
unless a spec's `model_version == "deepseek_v4"` (:1705). For any non-deepseek_v4 model, no group is
flagged, so `HybridKVCacheCoordinator` takes its "conservatively fall back to flag all groups when no
group is flagged" path (`kv_cache_coordinator.py:103-104`) and the mamba group is included. With MTP
on, Qwen3.6 is *guaranteed* to hand the mamba group `drop_eagle_block=True` (:710) and to have it
ignored.

### The fix

A nine-line change to `MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit`: when `drop_eagle_block` is set, lower
the search ceiling by one page (`max_num_blocks -= 1`) so the rightmost retained page is the one
before the eagle lookahead block.

It is deliberately **not** a literal `.pop()` mirroring `FullAttentionManager:603`. Mamba's hit list
is null-padded with the single real state block at the *end*: `[null, null, null, null, REAL]`. A
literal pop removes the real block and leaves an all-null hit claiming N-1 pages computed with no
state to restore from, which is worse than the bug it fixes. Lowering the ceiling instead lands on a
real earlier snapshot, `[null, null, null, REAL]`, which is what the coordinator's `_max_length`
peek-bump (`kv_cache_coordinator.py:712-720`) was set up to allow.

### Cost

This recomputes one mamba page per eagle cache hit, and a mamba page is 1000+ tokens of recurrent
state. That is expensive, and it is what EAGLE correctness requires.

The cheaper fix is on the write side: stop caching the lookahead block at all (the `_max_length` bump
plus the align-mode snapshot in `MambaManager.cache_blocks` / `reachable_block_mask`), so nothing
needs recomputing. That is the better long-term answer, and it is what the existing drafts (#43650,
#45477, #46281, and #47861 from @yanghui1-arch) are working toward. That change is larger and
subtler, and none of the drafts has merged yet.

This PR is the minimal correctness fix. Serving correct answers slower beats serving fast wrong ones,
and the write-side optimization can land on top of it without conflict. Scope is the aligned-block
case that align-mode prefix caching already guarantees.

Fixes #43559.

## Test Plan

`test_mamba_honors_drop_eagle_block` in `tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`,
alongside the existing manager tests. It is a `cpu_test`: no GPU, no model weights, no server, no
monkeypatching, using the real `BlockPool`, real specs, and the real classmethod. `block_size ==
alignment_tokens`, so the alignment loop is a no-op in both managers and the eagle drop is the only
behavior under test.

It carries a positive control (`drop_eagle_block=False`, both managers must see the full 5-block
prefix) so a passing result cannot come from a broken fixture, then asserts that with
`drop_eagle_block=True` the mamba hit matches full-attention's.

The bug also reproduces one level up, through `get_kv_cache_coordinator` ->
`HybridKVCacheCoordinator`: unpatched, the coordinator adopts the un-dropped mamba length and
returns `hit_length=80` where full-attention dropped to 64. I have that repro as well and am glad to
add it as a second test if you want the coverage at that layer.

## Test Result

Before, the new test fails on the parity assertion:

```
drop_eagle_block=False -> full-attn 5 blocks, mamba 5 blocks   (control passes)
drop_eagle_block=True  -> full-attn 4 blocks, mamba 5 blocks   (mamba retained the final block)
AssertionError: MambaManager ignored drop_eagle_block ...
```

After:

```
drop_eagle_block=False -> full-attn 5 blocks, mamba 5 blocks   (control unchanged)
drop_eagle_block=True  -> full-attn 4 blocks, mamba 4 blocks   (parity)
```

At the coordinator level, `hit_length` goes from 80 tokens (the un-dropped mamba length) to 64,
matching what full-attention dropped to.

One note on how this was validated. The bug was found and the fix exercised against v0.24.0, where I
could run the code with its compiled extensions: RED before, GREEN after, with the installed tree
left byte-identical and the change applied to a copy. The same change applies cleanly to `main`
(offset only), `MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` on `main` still takes `drop_eagle_block` and
still never reads it, and every API the test touches is unchanged there. I do not have a `main`
source build locally, so CI is the first execution of this test against `main`.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM DSA with --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla crashes at engine init: KV-cache reshape sizes view by head_size (576) while pages are 656B/token
body:
### Summary

On current main / nightly (`0.25.1.dev37+g3d99b0499`, also reproduced on `1ef1c7ebb`), any DSA-family model (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.2 / `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla` fails during engine core initialization:

```
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 7259, in _reshape_kv_cache_tensors
    kv_caches[layer_name] = _reshape_attention_kv_cache(
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py", line 251, in _reshape_attention_kv_cache
    kv_cache = kv_raw_tensor.view(dtype).view(permuted_kv_cache_shape)
RuntimeError: shape '[512, 64, 576]' is invalid for input of size 21495808
```

21495808 / (512·64) = 656 — the raw tensor is correctly allocated with the fp8_ds_mla 656-byte-per-token layout, but the target view shape was computed from `head_size` = 576.

### Root cause

`MLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec` constructs `MLAAttentionSpec` without `kv_quant_mode`, so it stays at the `KVQuantMode.NONE` default. The reshape helpers added for `--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers` treat `kv_quant_mode == NONE` as "this layer is skipped from quantization" and pass `cache_dtype_str="auto"` to `attn_backend.get_kv_cache_shape(...)`, which then returns the unquantized `(num_blocks, block_size, head_size)` shape instead of the 656-byte layout. The same pattern exists in both model runners (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py` and `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`).

The DeepseekV4-specific spec constructor was already fixed this way in #47716 (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py` passes `kv_quant_mode=get_kv_quant_mode(self.kv_cache_dtype)`), which is why DSv4 works while the generic MLA path (V3.2 / GLM DSA) crashes. Adjacent but non-overlapping open PRs: #47309 (per-layer `cache_dtype_str`), #47776 (preserves `kv_quant_mode` through the SWA-MLA spec merge) — neither touches the generic constructor.

### Repro

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --max-model-len 131072
```

No DCP or spec-decode needed; the crash is in `initialize_kv_cache` → `_reshape_kv_cache_tensors`.

### Fix

Mirror #47716 on the generic MLA path — pass `kv_quant_mode=get_kv_quant_mode(self.kv_cache_dtype)` in `MLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec`. Verified on 4×H200: GLM-5.2-NVFP4 + fp8_ds_mla + TP4 (and TP4/DCP4/EP + MTP) boots, cudagraph capture completes, output coherent, 198k-token needle retrieval exact. PR incoming.

*AI assistance (Claude) was used to bisect and draft this report; the repro and numbers were verified by the submitter on 4×H200.*

title: [Bug]: DSpark/DFlash speculative decoding fails to load with --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla: draft inherits an MLA-only cache layout
body:
### Summary

Launching a DSA-family target (GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V3.2) with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla` and a DSpark speculator fails during draft-model load:

```
ValueError: No valid attention backend found for cuda with
AttentionSelectorConfig(head_size=64, dtype=torch.bfloat16,
kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla, use_mla=False, use_non_causal=True, ...).
Reasons: {FLASH_ATTN: [kv_cache_dtype not supported], FLASHINFER: [kv_cache_dtype
not supported], TRITON_ATTN: [kv_cache_dtype not supported], FLEX_ATTENTION:
[kv_cache_dtype not supported], TURBOQUANT: [kv_cache_dtype not supported,
non-causal attention not supported]}
```

The DSpark draft is a dense (non-MLA) Qwen3-style transformer, but `load_dspark_model` builds the draft's `VllmConfig` with the target's `cache_config`, so the draft's attention layers try to use the MLA-only `fp8_ds_mla` layout, which no dense backend accepts.

Related but distinct from #47934 (FP4 target on B300, crashes later in FlashInfer draft attention) and #47626 (H20 fp8): the underlying issue — the draft inheriting a target-only kv-cache dtype — looks common to this family.

### Repro

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7}'
```

Needs the fix from #48378 to get this far on current main (fp8_ds_mla does not boot at all otherwise).

### Fix

In `load_dspark_model`, fall back to the model dtype for the draft's cache config when the target uses an MLA-only layout. With that one change the server boots and DSpark produces coherent output end-to-end on 4×H200 (GLM-5.2-NVFP4 target, TP4): 95 tok/s N=1, mean accepted length ~2.4.

The accompanying PR also adds a config-validation fail-fast for DCP>1 + dflash/dspark: the draft slot mapping is DCP-blind, so acceptance silently collapses to ~0% (as reported in the #46514 discussion).

*AI assistance (Claude) was used to bisect and draft this report; the repro and numbers were verified by the submitter on 4×H200.*

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] DSpark: store draft KV cache in model dtype for MLA-only cache layouts; fail fast on DCP
body:
FIX #48380

Two DSpark fixes for DSA-family targets:

1. **Draft cache dtype.** With `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla` the DSpark draft — a dense (non-MLA) Qwen3-style transformer — inherited the target's `cache_config` and tried to use the MLA-only fp8_ds_mla layout, which no dense attention backend accepts (`ValueError: No valid attention backend found for cuda ...`). `load_dspark_model` now falls back to the model dtype for the draft's KV cache; the draft cache is a few dense layers, so the memory cost is negligible.
2. **DCP fail-fast.** The DFlash/DSpark draft slot mapping is DCP-blind (`ctx_pos // block_size`), so with `decode_context_parallel_size > 1` the draft reads wrong KV blocks and acceptance silently collapses to ~0% (reported by @Leoyzen in #46514). Config validation now rejects the combination instead of degrading silently.

**Not a duplicate:** #47934 (FP4 target on B300) and #47626 (H20 fp8) crash later, in FlashInfer draft attention; no open PR touches the draft cache-config inheritance or adds a DCP guard for dflash/dspark.

**Testing** (4×H200, GLM-5.2-NVFP4 target, RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark):
- Before: the repro from #48380 fails at draft load with the ValueError above.
- After: server boots, output coherent end-to-end; 95 tok/s N=1, 341 tok/s aggregate N=8, mean accepted length ~2.4 (metrics: 4065 accepted / 2999 drafts / 20993 draft tokens).
- DCP guard: same command + `--decode-context-parallel-size 2` now fails at config validation with a clear NotImplementedError (previously: silent ~0% acceptance).

AI assistance was used for this change (Claude); the submitter reviewed every line and ran the tests above.

title: add pad-aware reduce path
body:
## Purpose
Adds a padding-aware reduce function for marlin MoE. When serving with expert-parallelism enabled, the MoE inputs and intermediate states are padded along the token dimension to handle the worst case (i.e. all tokens routed to a single rank; see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py#L32-L33).

The moe_sum reduce kernel currently includes padding tokens in its computation. This does not cause any accuracy problem currently because the moe output buffer is re-initialized to zeros on each invocation. Both of these (the zeroing out of the buffer and the iteration over padding tokens in the reduce kernel) degrade performance.

This PR adds a padding-aware reduce kernel (enabled only when expert parallelism is enabled) and removes the zeroing out of the moe output buffer.

## Test Plan

### Benchmark Results

Benchmarked `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`  on 8xH200 (EP=8) with 1k input / 1k output workload:
| Concurrency | Metric           | Before  | After (this PR) |
| ----------- | ---------------- | ------- | --------------- |
| 16          | Median TPOT (ms) | 25.06   | 19.61           |
|             | Median TTFT (ms) | 543.62  | 545.95          |
|             | Output tok/s     | 631.73  | 817.46          |
| 64          | Median TPOT (ms) | 34.05   | 34.36           |
|             | Median TTFT (ms) | 1010.58 | 938.73          |
|             | Output tok/s     | 1763.51 | 1808.16         |
| 256         | Median TPOT (ms) | 68.72   | 67.3            |
|             | Median TTFT (ms) | 2078.52 | 1889.58         |
|             | Output tok/s     | 3522.35 | 3602.23         |

### gsm8k Result
- Before: flexible-extract=0.9447 | strict-match=0.9462
- After: flexible-extract=0.9522 | strict-match=0.9522
