title: [Spec Decode] DFlash/DSpark draft support under decode context parallelism
body:
### What

Make dense (GQA/MHA) DFlash/DSpark drafts work under `decode_context_parallel_size > 1`
by caching the whole DCP group's KV heads on every rank.

Rebased on `main` after #52188. That PR landed the DCP-aware draft slot mapping this
branch used to carry (`cp_local_slot` / `prepare_dcp_local_seq_lens` in
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cp_utils.py`), and its version is strictly better: it also handles
the null block and the rejected context suffix. That commit is dropped here in favour
of upstream's, leaving the part #52188 does not cover.

#52188 enables the MLA draft path (Kimi-K3, one latent KV head, no head-gather). This
PR enables the dense path, where the head-gather is exactly what breaks.

### Why (root cause)

Reported by @Leoyzen in #46514: DFlash/DSpark acceptance collapses to ~0% under DCP.

The dense flash DCP path (`_forward_with_dcp`: all-gather query heads across the DCP
group, attend against the rank-local KV shard, LSE-merge) is only correct when a rank's
KV shard holds the KV heads for all gathered query heads, i.e. KV heads replicated
across the DCP group. `verify_with_parallel_config` enforces this for dense *targets*;
nothing checked the *draft*. The GLM-5.2 DSpark draft is MHA (64q/64kv), so under TP4
each rank has a 16-head shard and the gathered 64 query heads are GQA-remapped 4:1 onto
the wrong KV heads.

### How

Cache the whole DCP group's KV heads on every rank (replicated) for that rank's
interleaved positions:

- `cache_num_kv_heads` decouples the KV-cache spec from the impl's head count
  (`Attention.__init__`, defaults to `num_kv_heads`, only larger for this case).
- The draft precompute all-gathers K/V across the DCP group in the same rank order the
  query gather uses, so MHA maps 1:1 and GQA stays contiguous.
- The query block's K/V is not slotted into such a cache: the DCP path attends it
  against the freshly computed K/V, and at input-prep time the rank holds only its
  local heads, so writing them would corrupt the replicated layout.
- `vllm/config/vllm.py` fails fast on the layouts that are still wrong (partial
  replication, a dense draft whose architecture does not implement the replication, a
  quantized draft cache where the per-head descale is not wired for the decoupled head
  count).

Per-rank memory stays at the DCP=1 level because `AttentionSpec` already divides
blocks-per-request by the DCP size.

Behaviour change against the previous revision of this PR, worth calling out for
reviewers who saw it before: query slots used to be forced to PAD for *every* DCP run.
That is now conditional on the draft cache actually being head-replicated
(`PAD_QUERY_SLOTS_UNDER_CP`, derived from the draft attention layers). The
unconditional form would have broken the Kimi-K3 path from #52188, which writes real
query slots under DCP.

### Not a duplicate / related

No open PR implements DCP KV-head replication for the draft cache (checked
`gh pr list --search`). #52188 is complementary, not overlapping, after this rebase:
MLA draft there, dense draft here, sharing upstream's slot mapping.

The DCP change itself is independent of target/KV-cache dtype. Reproducing the GLM-5.2
numbers below (an `fp8_ds_mla` MLA target) also needs the draft-cache-dtype fallback
from #48381: without it the dense draft inherits the MLA-only `fp8_ds_mla` layout and
fails to load (bug #48380), before DCP is reached. DCP support for non-MLA targets does
not depend on #48381.

### Tests

The DCP slot-mapping tests this branch added are gone with the commit they covered.
The two behaviours specific to a head-replicated cache, plus a cross-rank partition
check, now extend upstream's suite:

```
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py -v
```

### Model evaluation (acceptance, the metric this change affects)

GLM-5.2-NVFP4 + `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark`, TP4/DCP4, 4xH200,
`vllm:spec_decode_num_*_total`:

| config | mean acceptance length |
|---|---|
| DCP=1 (baseline) | 2.40 |
| DCP=4, before this change | 1.10 (collapse) |
| **DCP=4, this change** | **2.63** |
| DCP=4, this change + CPU KV offload | 2.54 |

Per-position acceptance is a healthy monotone curve (pos0 54% to pos6 8%). Starts
cleanly under FULL-decode CUDA graphs; the OffloadingConnector draft-group exclude
(#47891) still fires correctly with the larger draft page.

A second run on the same hardware, GLM-5.2-NVFP4 + DSpark k=7, TP4 + EP, `fp8_ds_mla`,
`max_model_len` 131072, `max_num_seqs` 8:

| | GPU KV cache | N=1 | N=8 | mean accepted length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **DCP=4** (this PR) | 449,792 tok | 94 tok/s | 318 tok/s | **2.75 / 2.91** |
| DCP=1 (baseline) | 205,312 tok | 135 tok/s | 395 tok/s | 3.01 / 2.89 |
| DCP=4 before this PR | | | | **1.10** |

DCP=4 is slower than DCP=1 on short contexts, which is the expected DCP overhead, and
it buys ~2.2x the KV cache (450k vs 205k tokens), which is the point of enabling DCP.

Both runs predate the rebase and were measured on the revision that carried its own
slot mapping. The mechanism under test (KV-head replication) is unchanged by the
rebase, but the numbers have not been re-measured on top of #52188 yet.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for this change. The submitting human reviewed every

title: [Spec Decode][V1] Warm all spec-decode helper kernel specializations at startup (stacked on #41481)
body:
## Summary

Complements #41481 by warming `_mtp_shared_head_rmsnorm_kernel` at startup, **and** exhaustively covering all Triton specialization combinations for the eagle helper kernels.

### Problem

Triton specializes integer arguments whose runtime value is 1 into compile-time constants, producing a separate cubin per "which params are 1" combination. The existing single-shape warmup from #41481 only covers the production shape (`num_reqs=1`, `num_sampled>1`). The first request with a different combination (e.g. `num_reqs>1`, or `num_sampled=1` when `draft_tokens=0`) still triggers JIT during inference, causing latency spikes.

### Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

- #41481 covers `eagle_prepare_next_token_padded_kernel`, `eagle_prepare_inputs_padded_kernel`, `copy_and_expand_eagle_inputs_kernel`, and async-spec `@torch.compile` correction. It explicitly excludes `_mtp_shared_head_rmsnorm_kernel`.
- No other open PR addresses `_mtp_shared_head_rmsnorm_kernel` warmup or exhaustive specialization coverage.

### What this PR adds

1. **`_mtp_shared_head_rmsnorm_kernel` warmup** (commit `20c99b418`): A ~15-line addition to `LLMBaseProposer.dry_run_helper_kernels()` that calls `mtp_shared_head_rmsnorm(dummy_hidden, dummy_weight, eps)` once at startup, gated on `method == "mtp"`.

2. **Exhaustive specialization coverage** (commit `04c0a98ab`): Enumerate all (1, non-1) combinations for the three integer params (`num_sampled_tokens_per_req`, `num_reqs`, `stride_sampled_token_ids`) × all relevant `BLOCK_SIZE_TOKENS` values, so every cache entry is pre-compiled at startup.

   For `eagle_prepare_next_token_padded_kernel`:
   - 2³ int combos × len(block_sizes) entries (e.g. 8×4=32 for `num_speculative_tokens=4`)
   
   For `eagle_prepare_inputs_padded_kernel`:
   - 2 entries (`num_reqs=1` vs `num_reqs>1`)

   `vocab_size` is never 1 (model constant ≥ thousands) so it is never specialized and omitted from the enumeration.

### Why one warmup call is sufficient for `_mtp_shared_head_rmsnorm_kernel`

`_mtp_shared_head_rmsnorm_kernel` has only `tl.constexpr` parameters:
- `HIDDEN` — model constant (DSv4 fixed value)
- `BLOCK_SIZE = next_power_of_2(HIDDEN)` — derived from HIDDEN

The grid dimension (`num_tokens`) is NOT a specialization key in Triton, so a single warmup with `(1, HIDDEN)` covers all prefill/decode shapes. The runtime float `eps` is also not constexpr.

### Commits

This PR is stacked on #41481:
1. Commit `e34bedea1` — import #41481 verbatim (base dependency, by @li-xinwei)
2. Commit `20c99b418` — add `_mtp_shared_head_rmsnorm_kernel` warmup
3. Commit `04c0a98ab` — exhaustive specialization coverage for eagle helper kernels

### Test commands

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_helper_kernel_warmup.py -v
```

Ran `ast.parse` on all changed files: OK. `ruff-check`/`ruff-format` via pre-commit: Passed. (Other pre-commit hooks failed due to local Python version incompatibility — `itertools.pairwise` needs 3.10+; not a code issue.)

### AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (opencode). Every changed line was reviewed by a human.

title: [Bugfix] Size the sparse-indexer expanded block table from the runner's block-table width
body:
## Purpose

The DSA indexer's decode path preallocates `expanded_block_table_buffer` with
`cdiv(max_model_len, block_size * get_total_cp_world_size())` columns (per-rank,
CP-divided), but the `block_table` the runner hands in does not apply the CP
divisor: its width comes from the placeholder `InputBatch` built before KV-cache
init (`cdiv(max_model_len, block_size)`, `gpu_model_runner.py:688`), which is
only rebuilt when the block-size lists change. On TP8 / DCP2 / 1M the two widths
differ by 2× (buffer 8192 vs table 16384):

- the **variable-length** path raises `RuntimeError: The expanded size of the
  tensor (8192) must match the existing size (16384) at non-singleton dimension 1`;
- the **uniform** path is worse — `_prepare_uniform_decode_kernel`'s copy loop is
  bounded by the destination stride, so it silently truncates/mixes rows instead
  of raising.

Kernel-block splitting and `MultiGroupBlockTable` alignment padding are a second,
independent source of the same mismatch. The path is reachable without #46514
(the FlashInfer sparse DCP builder shares the buffer), hence a standalone fix.

## Fix

`_expanded_block_table(width)` matches the buffer to the block-table width
actually presented, reallocating at most once during the first (warmup) build —
before CUDA-graph capture, so the address stays stable across capture/replay.
Both decode use-sites go through it.

## Not a duplicate

Distinct root cause from the other open block-table-width fixes; none close the
CP-divisor gap:

- **#46787 / #46794 / #46884** (`max_model_len` auto-reduced after `InputBatch`
  creation): the widths come from two different `max_model_len` values and are
  fixed by rebuilding `InputBatch`. Here `max_model_len` is unchanged, and the
  divisor-less formula would not close the gap on rebuild.
- **#43970** (MTP alignment, 1669 vs 1670): pads to a 128-element boundary but
  keeps `* get_total_cp_world_size()`, so on DCP the buffer stays 8192.

Adapting to the delivered width also covers those triggers, but the change is
scoped to the indexer and composes with those PRs. The two width formulas could
instead be reconciled at the source (CP divisor on the placeholder `InputBatch`);
happy to move it there if preferred.

## Testing

Reported and validated by @rikki on 8×H200 — TP8 / DCP2 / EP8 / MTP=5,
`fp8_ds_mla`, 1M max-len, image `pr46514-fresh-20260712-idxfix`:

- variable-length: 4 concurrent requests, divergent `max_tokens`, ~524K context
  — 0 errors (previous image crashed in ~12 min with `[8, 8192] vs [8, 16384]`);
- uniform: 4×`max_tokens=512`, UUID needle in ~524K context — 4/4 retrieved
  verbatim.

Table + raw JSON: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46514#issuecomment-4950836862

Local CPU: `tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py` +
`test_sparse_mla_backends.py` → 15 passed / 18 skipped (parity with base); full
GPU run left to CI.

AI assistance was used (Claude); the submitter reviewed every line.

Tested-by: @rikki

title: [KV Connector] Canonical CPU layout for parallelism-agnostic KV offload
body:
Stacked on #48408. Stores offloaded KV in the canonical (parallelism-free) layout
described by the refs' page mappings: each worker scatters its page fragments to
their canonical positions in a CPU area shared by the whole worker group.

```
legacy row:     [worker0: T0|T1][worker1: T0|T1]...   per-worker slots
canonical row:  [T0 canonical page][T1 canonical page]  full heads + tokens, one copy
```

MLA latent and replicated GQA heads are stored once instead of once per rank
(empty store runs on non-writers). Copy expansions are precomputed per ref at
init; per-block placement is one vectorized base + offsets sum, with no
parallelism inputs anywhere in the transfer path.

## Configuration

`kv_connector_extra_config: {"canonical_layout": true}` on `TieringOffloadingSpec`
(requires the shared mmap). Requesting it on an uncertifiable config fails at
startup instead of silently downgrading. The persisted format identity
(`v1-nhd` / `v1-hnd`) joins the FileMapper namespace so canonical, legacy, and
cross-family bytes can never resolve to the same files; the `parallel_agnostic`
gate now also excludes replicated GQA heads, per-token-head scales, and CP.

## Test plan

`pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_canonical_layout.py tests/v1/kv_offload/test_file_mapper.py`
(no GPU): expansion offsets, empty store runs, per-tensor areas, namespace
separation, parallel_agnostic gates. Cross-topology byte semantics are covered by
the schema tests in #48408.

E2E on 4x H100 (eviction-forced CPU reloads, block-aligned prompts, greedy
token comparison against a GPU-cached baseline, lookup hits verified in logs):

| case | model | tokens exact | ranks certified |
|---|---|---|---|
| tp1 legacy | Qwen2.5-0.5B | yes | - |
| tp1 canonical | Qwen2.5-0.5B | yes | 1 |
| tp2 canonical | Qwen2.5-0.5B | yes | 2 |
| tp4 + dcp2 canonical | Qwen2.5-1.5B | yes | 4 |

Note for reviewers: `reset_prefix_cache` also resets the offload manager, so
reload tests must evict via cache pressure instead.

title: [Bugfix] Fix fp8_ds_mla config leak in DSpark speculative decoding
body:
Description

When an MLA model (like GLM-5.2 or DeepSeek) is initialized with `--kvcache-dtype fp8`, the `MLAAttention` and `DeepseekV4Attention` constructors secretly mutated the globally shared `cache_config` instance to force `cache_config.cache_dtype = "fp8_ds_mla"`. 

When running speculative decoding (like dspark) alongside it, the draft model uses standard attention layers that read this poisoned global config. Standard backends (FlashAttention, Triton) do not support the DeepSeek-specific MLA memory layout, causing the `AttentionSelector` to immediately crash with an unhandled `ValueError`.

Changes

* Single files modified: `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py` and `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py`
* Removed the global `cache_config.cache_dtype = "fp8_ds_mla"` assignments.
* `MLAAttention` now isolates `"fp8_ds_mla"` strictly to its internal `self.kv_cache_dtype` state.
* Leaves the global config untouched so standard draft models can boot up normally.

Related Issue

Closes #48406


Test Results

**Legacy (Without patch):**
```text
[FAILED] Standard Attention crashed: No valid attention backend found for cuda with AttentionSelectorConfig(... kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla ...). Reasons: {FLASH_ATTN: [kv_cache_dtype not supported]...
```

**Fixed (With patch):**
```text
INFO: Using fp8 data type to store kv cache.
[INFO] After MLA model load, global cache_config.cache_dtype = fp8
[SUCCESS] Standard Attention initialized successfully using TRITON_ATTN.
```

title: [Bugfix] Support heterogeneous per-layer attention geometry in Transformers backend
body:
### Summary
Fixes #44494.

The Transformers backend (`--model-impl transformers`) builds every `Attention` instance from the global config head count and head size. Models with heterogeneous per-layer attention geometry crash at the first forward pass. In Gemma 4 Unified, sliding layers use `head_dim=256` with 8 KV heads while full-attention layers use `head_dim=512` with a single shared KV head, so the attention output width does not match `o_proj` and serving fails with:

```
RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (8192x8192 and 4096x3840)
```

(With quantized checkpoints the same mismatch surfaces in the quantized GEMM instead, e.g. `marlin_gemm ... Shape mismatch: a.size(1) = 8192, size_k = 4096`.)

As requested in review, this now builds on huggingface/transformers#47384, which ports Gemma 4 to the heterogeneous config mechanism (`per_layer_config`, transformers ≥ 5.14.0) — so vLLM reads the per-layer geometry generically instead of special-casing Gemma 4 attribute names.

### Changes
- **`vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py`** — in `create_attention_instances`, when the text config declares `head_dim` or `num_key_value_heads` in `per_layer_attributes`, read them from `config.per_layer_config[i]` (the same reads the Transformers modeling code does). Homogeneous configs keep the global values, so existing models are unaffected.
- **`vllm/transformers_utils/config.py`** — heterogeneous configs raise `AmbiguousGlobalPerLayerAttributeError` if a per-layer attribute is read from the global config, and vLLM's engine initialization does such reads before the model exists; without a fix, Gemma 4 cannot even reach model construction on transformers with huggingface/transformers#47384 (`ModelConfig` creation dies in `Gemma4ModelArchConfigConvertor.get_head_size`). `get_config` now sets `allow_global_per_layer_attribute_access` on heterogeneous configs (root, text config and sub-configs) so those legacy reads return the global value, with a transformers warning.
- **`vllm/transformers_utils/model_arch_config_convertor.py`** — with the flag alone, `Gemma4ModelArchConfigConvertor.get_head_size` would silently return the global (sliding) `head_dim` instead of its deliberate max-over-layers, and attention backends size shared buffers with it (e.g. `TritonAttentionMetadataBuilder` preallocates the split-softmax output with it — an undersized buffer means out-of-bounds writes for the 512-wide layers). It now takes the max over `per_layer_config` when `head_dim` is per-layer.
- **`vllm/model_executor/models/config.py`** — same silent degradation in `Gemma4Config.verify_and_update_config`: the guard that forces a uniform attention backend for dual head dimensions (FA4, or Triton fallback) keyed off the removed `global_head_dim` and would stop firing. It now detects heterogeneity via `per_layer_config` too, keeping the guard (and the MTP spec-decode backend carry-through that depends on it) working.

With released transformers (Gemma 4 configs not yet heterogeneous) all four changes are inert; Gemma 4 through the Transformers backend starts working once huggingface/transformers#47384 lands.

**Known limitation:** the native Gemma 4 implementations (`gemma4.py`, `gemma4_mtp.py`, `gemma4_dspark.py`) still read the removed `global_head_dim`/`num_global_key_value_heads` keys, so with post-#47384 configs the native path (default `model_impl=auto`) builds projections with sliding geometry and fails at weight loading with a shape mismatch. Porting the native implementations to `per_layer_config` is left for a follow-up (happy to take it) — it needs its own weight-loading and accuracy verification.

### Tests

Mock-based so they run on the CI-pinned transformers 5.13.1, which predates the heterogeneity mechanism. Pass with the fix, fail without it.
- `pytest tests/transformers_utils/test_config.py::test_allow_global_per_layer_attribute_access` and `pytest tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py::test_gemma4_head_size_heterogeneous_config` — exercise the flag helper and the max-over-layers head size against the real transformers heterogeneity mechanism (auto-skip on transformers < 5.14).

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Preserve async load reservations
body:
## Summary

Async KV loads reserve the blocks they still need to finish, but the scheduler only honored that reservation when admitting another async load. Ordinary local admissions and subsequent running chunks could consume the reserved headroom. The full-sequence admission check also ignored `reserved_blocks`.

This change:

- applies in-flight prefill reservations to both waiting and running allocations;
- excludes the request that owns the reservation when it resumes;
- includes reserved blocks in the full-sequence fit check; and
- adds a regression test where a local request would otherwise consume an async load's remaining capacity.

The reservation is only nonzero while async loads or chunked prefills are in flight, so normal scheduling is unchanged.

## Why this is not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for async KV reservation, scheduler deadlock, and `reserved_blocks`.

- #44560 introduced reservation-based admission between async loads. This PR closes the remaining gap where non-async allocations ignore that reservation.
- #42568 changes `max_num_seqs` accounting for async loads; it does not protect block reservations.
- #45406 scans past an unschedulable queue head to promote a completed parked load; it addresses a different post-admission queue-stranding state.

## Validation

Focused lifecycle test file:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py -q
```

```text
10 passed, 17 warnings in 6.82s
```

Repository hooks on the modified files:

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py
```

All hooks passed.

I also ran a local two-GPU DSv4-Pro-shaped stress test with DP=2, EP=2, DeepGEMM MegaMoE, dummy weights, a deliberately small KV pool, one delayed async external-KV load, and heavily imbalanced requests. All 8 requests completed without a collective stall. On the original target branch, the same-config A/B reduced peak logical KV usage from 94.2% to 87.2% and completion time from 28.91s to 20.82s. Current upstream `main` with this patch completed in 20.78s with 87.8% peak KV usage.

This test validates the reservation-pressure behavior; it does not claim that every production collective hang has the same root cause.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex was used to investigate the scheduler path, draft the patch and regression test, and run the validation. I reviewed every changed line and am responsible for the change.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Keep TP all_gather on base-class collective
body:
## Summary

PR #40996 (DCP supports hybrid attention) changed `CudaCommunicator.all_gather` to bypass the base-class collective (`all_gather_into_tensor`) and instead run an inline pynccl path that allocates a fresh output tensor with `torch.empty` and then does `movedim` + `reshape` on every call:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/cuda_communicator.py

This is on the hot path for every tensor-parallel `all_gather` (e.g. sequence-parallel gather-before-GEMM), so it runs on every step.

On **ROCm** the inline path is slower than the base-class collective: the extra per-call output allocation and (for `dim != 0`) an extra copy add measurable per-step overhead. On DeepSeek-V4 with TP=8 this regresses decode throughput by ~22%.

This PR routes ROCm back to the base-class `all_gather` while leaving the CUDA / NVLS symmetric-memory path untouched. DCP itself is unaffected because it uses its own process group, not this method.

## Measurements

DeepSeek-V4, MI355X, TP=8, fp8 KV, 8k input / 1k output, concurrency 4 (mean TPOT):

| Build | mean TPOT |
|---|---|
| Before #40996 | 26.4 ms |
| After #40996 (current main) | 32.5 ms |
| With this fix | 26.4 ms |

Bisected to a single file: reverting only `cuda_communicator.py` to the pre-#40996 version restores the baseline, and this targeted ROCm guard reproduces that recovery on top of the full current tree.

## Test plan

- [x] CI (distributed / TP tests)
- [x] DeepSeek-V4 TP=8 decode throughput restored to pre-#40996 baseline on ROCm (MI355X)
- [x] Confirm no change on CUDA (path is unchanged for non-ROCm)

cc @vllm-project maintainers of #40996

title: [ROCm][Perf] Add gfx942 Gluon fp8_mqa_logits kernel for DSA sparse-ML…
body:
…A indexer

The DSA sparse-MLA "lightning indexer" scoring (fp8_mqa_logits) is a top prefill cost for DeepSeek-V3.2-architecture models (GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V3.2) on MI300X. On gfx942 vLLM currently forces the generic-Triton fp8_mqa_logits_gfx942 fallback, because AITER's optimized Gluon kernel is gfx950-only.

This ports AITER's gfx950 Gluon fp8_mqa_logits kernel to gfx942 (CDNA3): the gfx950-only mfma_scaled microscaled MMA is replaced with cdna3.mfma plus FNUZ fp8 operands (emitting the native v_mfma_f32_32x32x16_fp8_fp8 instruction, 2x the K-rate of the f16-upcast generic path); the LDS async-copy staging is replaced with direct cdna3.buffer_load of each KV tile, with Q and weights hoisted out of the loop (LICM).

The kernel is opt-in via VLLM_ROCM_MQA_LOGITS_GLUON=1 (default off, no behavior change), and falls back to the generic kernel when disabled or when the KV / logits tensors exceed the 2 GiB buffer-op resource-descriptor limit.

Correctness: rel_max ~1.8e-7 vs an fp32 dequant oracle across M in {64..8192}, N in {40..36000} on a co-located MI300X microbench, including causal, dense, and partial-tile windows. Perf: ~5.3x the generic fallback at the GLM-5.2 indexer shape (H=32 query heads); end-to-end on GLM-5.2-FP8 8xMI300X TP8, TTFT -20.8% at concurrency 1.

title: HybridKVCacheCoordinator: DSpark draft-model KV-cache group's ephemeral content incorrectly vetoes GPU-tier prefix cache reuse
body:
## Summary

`HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit()` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py`) requires every KV-cache group of a hybrid model to independently report a nonzero hit before confirming any prefix reuse for a request, on the GPU tier, independent of any KV connector. When serving DeepSeek-V4 with DSpark speculative decoding, the draft-model KV-cache group can never satisfy this, so it incorrectly vetoes reuse of the target model's own KV-cache groups (SWA, compressed C4A/C128A, indexer) even when those groups genuinely still hold valid, resident GPU blocks for a matching prefix.

Concretely, this means: a follow-up request sharing a prefix with GPU blocks still resident from a previous request (shared system prompt, multi-turn conversation), or a request resumed after preemption, gets treated as having zero reusable prefix and is fully recomputed from scratch, even though the target model's real cache groups could have served part or all of that prefix.

## Root cause

Same underlying issue as #47890, at a different layer. `OffloadingConnectorScheduler._lookup()` and `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit()` independently reimplement the same iterative AND-convergence lookup algorithm, one for the RAM-tier offloading path, one for the GPU tier. #47890 covers the RAM-tier symptom (`external_prefix_cache_hits_total` stuck at 0). This issue is the same defect on the GPU-tier side of that same algorithm.

`find_longest_cache_hit()`'s per-group loop calls `manager_cls.find_longest_cache_hit(...)` for every group and treats any group's `0`-block result as authoritative, truncating the confirmed hit length for the whole request to that group's result. DSpark's draft-model KV-cache group can never contribute a meaningful nonzero result here: `DSparkDeepseekV4Model.precompute_and_store_context_kv` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/dspark.py`) derives that group's context KV directly from the target model's own auxiliary hidden states at each drafting round and overwrites it every round, so its content has no request-independent, stable meaning across a lookup boundary. It is a write-then-immediately-consume-within-round buffer, not an incrementally accumulated, reusable cache, unlike EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP's draft KV, which is genuinely reusable because the draft model attends over its own previously drafted tokens the same way the target model attends over its own history.

## Scope

Same two boundaries as #47890's fix:

- Speculative method: DSpark specifically. DFlash's drafter shares the same ephemeral-context property but is a separate, unvalidated case.
- Model architecture: this only affects DeepSeek-V4-family models (Flash, Pro, and any other size variant), since the draft-model KV-cache group is only ever distinguished from other groups (`is_eagle_group`) for `model_version == "deepseek_v4"`. Other architectures are unaffected.

## Status

Identified via code inspection while working on #47891 (the OffloadingConnector-side fix for the same root cause), not yet backed by a live before/after benchmark isolating the GPU-tier-only prefix caching path (all live validation done so far had the OffloadingConnector enabled). Flagging this as its own issue per maintainer request on #47891, since the core coordinator fix should be reviewed on its own merits before the connector is aligned to match it.

Related: #47890, #47891

title: [Bugfix] Exclude DSpark draft-model KV-cache group from core prefix-cache lookup veto
body:
Fixes #48455

### Purpose

Split out from #47891 per review feedback there: this PR is the core-only
half of that fix, the offloading connector's PR will be rebased to align
with this once it merges.

`HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit()`
(`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py`) requires every KV-cache group of a
hybrid model to independently report a nonzero hit before confirming any
prefix reuse for a request, on the GPU tier. When serving DeepSeek-V4 with
DSpark speculative decoding, the draft-model KV-cache group can never
satisfy this, so it incorrectly vetoes reuse of the target model's own
KV-cache groups (SWA, compressed C4A/C128A, indexer) even when those groups
genuinely still hold valid, resident GPU blocks for a matching prefix. A
follow-up request sharing a prefix with GPU blocks still resident from a
previous request, or a request resumed after preemption, gets treated as
having zero reusable prefix and is fully recomputed from scratch.

### What this PR changes

- `SpeculativeConfig.has_ephemeral_draft_context()` (new,
  `vllm/config/speculative.py`): a predicate on the speculative method
  itself, following the same pattern as the existing `use_dflash()` and
  `use_dspark()`. Returns `True` for `"dspark"`. Identifies methods whose
  draft-model KV-cache group is rebuilt from the target model's auxiliary
  hidden states at generation time, rather than accumulated incrementally
  through the draft's own attention (EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP).
- `KVCacheGroupSpec.eagle_group_is_veto_exempt` (new,
  `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`): a plain boolean field, computed once
  from the predicate above wherever `is_eagle_group` is already set
  (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`).
- `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit()`
  (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py`, the primary fix): when a
  veto-exempt eagle group reports zero hit blocks in a round, that group is
  dropped from the round instead of zeroing the whole request's confirmed
  hit length. It still participates normally in every other round,
  including any round where it reports a nonzero hit.

Neither `find_longest_cache_hit()` nor `find_longest_cache_hit_per_group()`
contains a single method-name string comparison; the exemption is derived
once from `KVCacheGroupSpec.eagle_group_is_veto_exempt` and consumed as a
plain boolean.

### `eagle_group_is_veto_exempt` does not mean "excluded from the lookup"

A veto-exempt group's hit length is still computed every round exactly like
any other group's. The exemption only changes what happens when that
computed hit length is zero: normally a zero from any group vetoes
(truncates to zero) every other group's independently confirmed hit; for a
group whose KV has no request-independent, stable meaning, a zero is not
informative about whether the target model's own groups have a real,
reusable hit, so it is left unconfirmed for that round instead of zeroing
everyone else. A nonzero hit from the same group participates in the
AND-convergence exactly like before, with no special casing.

### Why this has no downside for DSpark, unlike EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP

EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP's draft model runs its own causal self-attention over
tokens it has itself drafted. Once a draft token's KV is computed, it stays
valid for the rest of the request and is genuinely reusable across requests
that share a prefix.

DSpark's draft context KV works differently.
`DSparkDeepseekV4Model.precompute_and_store_context_kv`
(`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/dspark.py`) derives each draft layer's
context KV directly from the target model's own auxiliary hidden states at
that exact decode step, and writes it into that layer's context slots. This
runs once per drafting round: the target produces real hidden states,
DSpark writes fresh context KV from them, the draft model attends over that
freshly written context to produce this round's speculative tokens, and the
next round overwrites those same slots again from the target's next hidden
states. It is a write-then-immediately-consume-within-round buffer, not an
incrementally accumulated cache. There is no window in which reusing it
would be meaningful, so this PR does not forfeit any reuse opportunity
DSpark had. It never had one to begin with.

### Scope

Two independent scope boundaries.

**Speculative method: DSpark only, DFlash is a follow-up.** DFlash's
drafter builds its context KV from the target model's auxiliary hidden
states the same way DSpark's does, so `has_ephemeral_draft_context()` could
mechanically be extended to cover `"dflash"` with a one-line change. This
PR deliberately does not do that: DFlash has not been validated end to end
in a live server (blocked on an unrelated attention-backend /
KV-cache-dtype compatibility gap for the DeepSeek-V4 target, plus a
checkpoint-architecture mismatch for the specific community DFlash
checkpoint available), so claiming the fix for DFlash here would be a claim
without evidence.

**Model architecture: the whole DeepSeek-V4 family (Flash, Pro, and any
other size variant), not size-specific.** `eagle_group_is_veto_exempt` is
only ever set inside `_annotate_eagle_groups_deepseek_v4` (pre-existing
code, `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`), which is itself hard-scoped to
`model_version == "deepseek_v4"`. That value is set in exactly one place,
`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py`, shared by the whole
`DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` architecture regardless of size variant. Every
other model architecture falls back to a different, pre-existing path that
flags all groups as `is_eagle_group` uniformly and never touches this new
field, so this PR has no effect there.

Live serving validation of this mechanism, via #47891 which shares the
same core fix, was on the Flash size variant.

### Testing

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py` | included in full run below |
| `tests/v1/core/` (full directory, 2 GPUs) | 423 passed, 0 failed |

Run inside an isolated throwaway container (source `.py` tree synced over
an installed `vllm` build to avoid needing a full rebuild), on this

title: [Feat][Spec Decode] Add DFlare support for Qwen3 series
body:
## Summary

Adds **DFlare** (per-layer adaptive fusion speculative decoding, built on DFlash) for **Qwen3**-series models, for the `DFlareQwen3Model` checkpoint family (e.g. `AngelSlim/Qwen3-4b-dflare`). Following the DFlash / DSpark review pattern, this is a **thin subclass reuse** of the existing DFlash stacks, not a standalone model.

## Design

DFlare extends DFlash with two key innovations over the baseline DFlash (single `fc` fusion + shared KV projections):

### 1. Per-layer adaptive hidden-state fusion

- **`layer_fusion_weights`**: a learnable \([D, T]\) matrix (softmax-normalized) replaces DFlash's single `fc` (ReplicatedLinear). Each of the \(D\) draft decoder layers receives an independently fused context signal:
  ```
  fused = layer_fusion_weights @ RMSNorm(concat(aux_hidden_states))
  ```
  rather than a single weighted sum shared by all layers.
- The `combine_hidden_states` method on `DFlareQwen3ForCausalLM` handles this fusion; the result is a \([N, D, H]\) tensor stored in a persistent `per_layer_hidden_states` buffer.

### 2. Heterogeneous KV projections for context precompute

- Each draft attention layer has its own **`k_proj_target` / `v_proj_target`** weights (packed as `kv_target_proj` via `QKVParallelLinear` with Q-section=0), independent of the query-time `k_proj` / `v_proj`.
- `_build_context_kv_buffers` stacks all layers' `kv_target_proj.weight` into `_kv_target` \([D, H, 2 \times \text{kv\_size}]\) and all `k_norm.weight` into `_k_norm_weights` \([D, \text{head\_dim}]\).
- `_project_context_kv` uses a **batched matmul** (`bmm`): \([D,N,H] \times [D,H,2\times\text{kv}] \rightarrow [D,N,2\times\text{kv}]\) — one projection per layer per token, since each layer has a different projection matrix.
- RoPE + K-norm reuse the same vLLM fused kernels (`ops.rms_norm` with per-layer weight broadcast, `ops.rotary_embedding`).

### Architecture inheritance

```
DFlashQwen3ForCausalLM          DFlashQwen3Attention
        ▲                               ▲
        │                               │
DFlareQwen3ForCausalLM    DFlareQwen3Attention (+ kv_target_proj)
        │                               │
        ├─ combine_hidden_states (override: per-layer fusion)
        └─ load_weights           (override: k/v_target weights + layer_fusion_weights)

DFlashSpeculator
        ▲
        │
DFlareSpeculator (+ per_layer_hidden_states buffer, override propose & load_draft_model)
```

- **Attention / decoder-layer forward**: fully inherited from DFlash (`DFlashQwen3Attention.forward`). Only `__init__` is overridden to add `kv_target_proj`.
- **CUDA graph manager**: aliased directly from DFlash (`DFlareCudaGraphManager = DFlashCudaGraphManager`), since the query-only draft forward is identical.
- **Speculator kernel** (`_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel`): fully reused from DFlash.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflare.py` (new) | `DFlareQwen3Attention`, `DFlareQwen3DecoderLayer`, `DFlareQwen3Model` (per-layer fusion + heterogeneous KV precompute), `DFlareQwen3ForCausalLM` |
| `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py` | Register `QwenDFlareDraftModel` → `DFlareQwen3ForCausalLM` |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflare/` (new) | `speculator.py` (extends `DFlashSpeculator` with per-layer buffer), `utils.py` (model loader), `cudagraph.py` (alias to DFlash CG manager) |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/__init__.py` | Wire `method="dflare"` → `DFlareSpeculator` |
| `vllm/config/speculative.py` | Add `"dflare"` to `SpeculativeMethod`, auto-detect from model name, set `parallel_drafting=True`, wire aux hidden states |
| `vllm/config/vllm.py` | Whitelist `dflare` for V2 engine, parallel drafting check |
| `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/speculators/algos.py` | `update_dflare`: set architectures to `Qwen3DFlareModel`, map `aux_hidden_state_layer_ids` → `target_layer_ids` (i-1 indexing), configurable `causal` for SWA |
| `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` | Extra lookahead slot for DFlare context KV (same as DFlash) |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` | Route `dflare` to aux hidden state collection |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` | Whitelist `dflare` for speculative method checks |

## Test Plan
Serving Command(DFlash as baseline)
```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "dflash", "model": "z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16", "num_speculative_tokens": 16}' \
    --attention-backend flash_attn \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
    --max-model-len 4096 \
    --max_num_seqs 128

vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "dflare", "model": "AngelSlim/Qwen3-4b-dflare", "num_speculative_tokens": 16}' \
    --attention-backend flash_attn \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
    --max-model-len 4096 \
    --max_num_seqs 128
```

| Dataset | DFlash Acceptance Rate | DFlare Acceptance Rate | Rate Improvement (Percentage Points) | DFlash Acceptance Length | DFlare Acceptance Length | Length Improvement |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Alpaca** | 6.80% | 8.90% | **+2.10** | 2.09 | 2.42 | **+0.33** |
| **ShareGPT** | 7.72% | 9.90% | **+2.18** | 2.24 | 2.58 | **+0.34** |
| **Human Eval** | 10.53% | 11.55% | **+1.02** | 2.69 | 2.85 | **+0.16** |
| **Math500** | 11.52% | 13.45% | **+1.93** | 2.84 | 3.15 | **+0.31** |

## Design decisions & trade-offs

1. **Reuse over rewrite**: The implementation reuses DFlash's attention forward, CUDA graph manager, speculator kernel, and weight loading patterns. DFlare only overrides the context-fusion and context-KV-projection paths where its architecture actually differs.

2. **`layer_fusion_weights` normalization**: Weights are softmax-normalized once after weight loading (`_build_fused_kv_buffers`), not per-step. This is a static learned matrix.

### 🐛 Describe the bug When running vLLM with tensor parallelism and CUDA Graph enabled, the server can hang after starting CUDA profiling through the `start_profile` API under Nsight Systems. The hang disappears when PyTorch symmetric-memory all-reduce is disabled via: ```bash VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0 ``` This keeps CUDA Graph enabled and forces TP all-reduce to use PyNCCL. Based on the experiments below, the issue appears to be related to: CUDA Graph replay + PyTorch symmetric-memory all-reduce + Nsight/cudaProfilerStart ```bash nsys profile \ -o /workspace/nsys_reports/vllm_serve_batch32 \ --force-overwrite=true \ --trace=cuda,nvtx \ --nccl-trace=none \ --sample=none \ --cpuctxsw=none \ --backtrace=none \ --python-backtrace=none \ --cudabacktrace=none \ --cuda-memory-usage=false \ --cuda-event-trace=false \ --cuda-trace-all-apis=false \ --cuda-graph-trace=node:host-only \ --resolve-symbols=false \ --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi \ --capture-range-end=stop \ --duration=200 \ vllm serve /home/models/ \ --disable-custom-all-reduce \ --trust-remote-code \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --block-size 256 \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --attention_config.use_fp4_indexer_cache=True \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --profiler-config '{"profiler":"cuda"}' ``` With symmetric-memory all-reduce enabled, TP uses: Using ['SYMM_MEM', 'PYNCCL'] all-reduce backends ... group 'tp:0' After calling start_profile, the process can hang during CUDA Graph replay. With symmetric-memory all-reduce disabled: VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0 TP uses only PyNCCL: Using ['PYNCCL'] all-reduce backends ... group 'tp:0' Using ['PYNCCL'] all-reduce backends ... group 'ep:0' In this configuration, the same workload is stable. When TP dispatches to PyTorch symmetric-memory all-reduce, CUDA Graph replay can hang after cudaProfilerStart / Nsight capture begins. Suspected Root Cause The issue appears to involve PyTorch symmetric-memory all-reduce being captured/replayed inside CUDA Graphs while Nsight Systems profiling is active via cudaProfilerStart. This does not appear to be caused by custom all-reduce, host NCCL launch order mismatch, rank-divergent collective sequences, or multi-stream GEMM. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: feat(mxfp4): add MXFP4 expert cache support to DeepSeek V4
body:
## Summary

Adds MXFP4 (Microscaling FP4) expert weight support to `--moe-expert-cache-size`,
enabling DeepSeek V4 Flash and PRO to run on GPU nodes with limited VRAM by
storing MoE expert weights in CPU pinned memory and caching only hot experts on GPU.

This PR extends the existing expert LRU cache infrastructure (PR #37190) to support
MXFP4 quantization, used by DeepSeek V4 Flash and PRO.

## Changes

**Cache infrastructure fixes (2 commits):**
- Accept multi-dimensional scale tensors (1D per-tensor, 2D FP8, 3D MXFP4 block)
- Warn instead of raising ValueError when MoE layers have bias terms

**MXFP4 backend support (3 commits):**
- `prefer_modular` parameter: selects modular kernel classes (accept external `topk_ids`)
- Cache init in `Mxfp4MoEMethod`: auto-detects monolithic kernels, re-selects with `prefer_modular=True`
- Apply wiring: reads `expert_weight_provider` at runtime, uses cache-provided weights

## Key design

DeepSeek V4's default MXFP4 kernel is **monolithic** (internal routing).
The expert cache remaps expert IDs to slot indices, incompatible with monolithic routing.
When `--moe-expert-cache-size` is set, the backend auto-switches to a modular kernel
(e.g. `OAITritonExperts` for TRITON, `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular` for FLASHINFER).

## Verification

All levels pass on H100 NVL:
- 3D MXFP4 block scales preserved through cache
- `prefer_modular=True` correctly selects modular kernel classes
- Cache wiring complete (supports_expert_lru_cache, _maybe_init, apply provider)
- Full inference + tool calling verified on real DeepSeek V4 Flash model
- FP8/BF16 cache regression tested (no breakage)

title: [BugFix] Add SM120 fallback for DeepSeek sparse indexer logits
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek sparse MLA on SM120 already selects the dedicated FlashInfer attention backend, but the sparse indexer still calls DeepGEMM for MQA logits and paged scheduler metadata. Those DeepGEMM paths reject SM120 with an unsupported-architecture error.

This PR:

- routes FP8 prefill and paged-decode indexer logits through a Torch/BF16 compatibility implementation on SM120;
- avoids generating DeepGEMM scheduler metadata that the SM120 fallback does not consume;
- fails explicitly for FP4 Q, which this compatibility path does not support.

This is a correctness fallback for the indexer stage. The optimized SM120 sparse-attention stage remains handled by FlashInfer.

Related to #47266 and #47818.

## Test Plan

```bash
uvx ruff format --check   vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py   vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_indexer_sm120.py   vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py   tests/kernels/test_sparse_attn_indexer_sm120.py

uvx ruff check   vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py   vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_indexer_sm120.py   vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py   tests/kernels/test_sparse_attn_indexer_sm120.py

pytest -q tests/kernels/test_sparse_attn_indexer_sm120.py
```

Manual DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP=8 serving smoke test on 8x NVIDIA RTX 6000D (SM120), including a short chat request and a 12K-token prompt.

## Test Result

- Ruff format and lint checks passed.
- GPU unit tests: `2 passed in 6.64s`.
- Service health check returned HTTP 200.
- Short chat: HTTP 200, 13 prompt tokens + 32 completion tokens, coherent output.
- Long-context smoke: HTTP 200, 12,006 prompt tokens + 2 completion tokens.
- No Traceback, OOM, or unsupported-architecture errors in the service log.

The end-to-end smoke used the exact PR fallback implementation mounted into the available NGC 26.06 runtime, with a thin call-signature adapter for that image's older indexer API.

No documentation update is needed because this change does not alter the public API or backend-selection behavior.

title: [Kernel] MXFP4 indexer cache for GLM-5.2 / DSA (glm_moe_dsa)
body:
# [Kernel] MXFP4 indexer cache for GLM-5.2 / DSA (glm_moe_dsa)

## What

Adds **MXFP4 (4-bit) support for the DSA lightning-indexer K-cache** and wires it into
GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, `deepseek_v2` `Indexer`). Gated by the existing
`--attention-config '{"use_fp4_indexer_cache": true}'` (default off, behavior unchanged).

Upstream shipped the FP4 indexer **read** path (mqa_logits) for DeepSeek-V4 in #40860, but
the **insert** path is still blocked — `assert not use_fp4_cache, "Unfused FP4 Insert is not
supported yet"` — and `indexer_k_quant_and_cache` is FP8-only. This PR fills that gap.

## Changes (3 files, +122 / −3)

- **`csrc/.../cache_kernels.cu`** (new kernel): `indexer_k_quant_and_cache_mxfp4_kernel`
  writes the indexer K-cache as MXFP4 (E2M1 values + UE8M0 block-32 scales, software E2M1
  encode for sm_100a). Dispatched from `indexer_k_quant_and_cache` when `scale_fmt=="mxfp4"`.
- **`sparse_attn_indexer.py`**: drop the "not supported yet" assert; pass `"mxfp4"` scale_fmt.
- **`deepseek_v2.py`** (`Indexer`): allocate the fp4-shaped K-cache, MXFP4-quantize the
  indexer query, disable the fused FP8 indexer-q path.

## Benefit

Indexer K-cache: **132 → 68 B/token/head (~1.94×)**. Measured on 4×B200 (GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4):

| metric | FP8 indexer | MXFP4 indexer | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPU KV cache size | 1,143,808 tok | 1,184,192 tok | **+3.5%** |
| max concurrency @131K | 8.73× | 9.03× | **+3.4%** |
| TTFT / TPOT (conc1 prefill 8K–122K; conc16 grid; conc48–64 long-ctx) | — | — | neutral |

It's a **memory-efficiency** feature (more KV headroom at long context), not a latency win —
the indexer is a small fraction of prefill vs MLA attention.

## Accuracy

passkey 8K / 32K / 64K = 3/3 · 3/3 · 3/3, identical to FP8. No regression.

## Testing

- Kernel + wiring validated end-to-end on 4×B200 (SM100) serving GLM-5.2-NVFP4: fp4 indexer
  cache active (KV size 1.18M tok), coherent generation, passkey 3/3.
- The `use_fp4_indexer_cache=true` flag was exercised on current-`main` Python (fp4 K-cache
  allocated, 9.09× concurrency). The modified C++ TU (`cache_kernels.cu` = `main` + this diff)
  **compiles clean against `main`'s headers** with CUDA 13.0 / sm_100 (exit 0, no warnings;
  see the compile-verification comment below). Full multi-arch build + link across all TUs is
  still what upstream CI does — a `ready` label would run it.
- Requires SM100 datacenter Blackwell (B200/GB200) — same constraint as the existing
  `use_fp4_indexer_cache` backend assert.

## Notes

- MXFP4 q-quant is done in PyTorch (indexer q is tiny vs attention); a fused q-rope-mxfp4
  kernel could follow.
- GLM's `index_n_heads=32` drives the paged MQA-logits reader at `N=16`; the vendored
  deep_gemm needs `N∈{8,16}` TMEM loaders (a 1-line assert/loader extension, tracked
  separately from this vLLM change).

title: [Perf][ROCm] Optimize DSA lightning-indexer fp8_mqa_logits scoring kernel on MI300X (gfx942)
body:
### Motivation

For DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.2 sparse attention (DSA), the lightning-indexer `fp8_mqa_logits` scoring kernel dominates prefill. On an 8x MI300X (gfx942) TP8 serve it is ~28% of GPU busy time during prefill, and its share grows with the prefix-cache hit rate (most GPU work becomes scoring a large fixed context against a few new query tokens).

Today gfx942 (CDNA3) falls back to a generic Triton stopgap (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_fp8_mqa_logits.py`), while NVIDIA uses DeepGEMM and gfx950 (CDNA4) uses an optimized AITER gluon kernel. So MI300X runs the indexer well below peak.

### Proposal

Port the gfx950 AITER gluon `fp8_mqa_logits` kernel to gfx942:
- CDNA4 async-copy loader -> CDNA3 `buffer_load` into registers
- CDNA3 MFMA layout (native `v_mfma_f32_32x32x16_fp8_fp8`), with the `transposed=True` output layout that keeps the per-row head-reduction in-lane

Gate it behind an env flag (default off) with a shape/backend guard that falls back to the current stopgap, so no default behavior changes.

### Results (8x MI300X, GLM-5.2-FP8, TP8, serve-validated)

- Microbench: ~5.3x over the shipped gfx942 stopgap on the hot prefill shapes.
- E2E: ~-20.8% prefill TTFT on a ~37K-token single-stream prompt, coherent output confirmed in serve (matches the Amdahl prediction for a ~28%-of-prefill kernel at 5.3x).

I have a working patch and will open a PR.

title: [DeepSeek-V4] Handle 3-D packed hidden states in attention forward
body:
## Summary
This PR adds handling for 3-D packed hidden states in the DeepSeek-V4
attention forward path.
It is split out from #47972 ("Support DeepSeek-V4 AMD Quark NVFP4 with
emulation kernel", https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47972). During
review of that PR it was pointed out that this attention/MTP change is
orthogonal to the NVFP4/Quark mixed-quant work there, so it is moved here to
keep both changes focused and easier to review. #47972 has been updated to
drop this change accordingly.
## Motivation
HC/MTP passes a packed hidden-state buffer of shape
`[num_tokens, num_slots, hidden_dim]`, where slot 0 is the target token used
for attention and the remaining slots hold auxiliary (multi-token) predictions.
The attention input GEMMs and the attention op should only operate on the
target token.
## Changes
- In `DeepseekV4Attention.forward`, when `hidden_states` is 3-D, select slot 0
  (`hidden_states[:, 0, :]`) as the attention input; 2-D inputs are passed
  through unchanged.
- Use this selected tensor for both `attn_gemm_parallel_execute` and the
  attention op.
## Compatibility
Fully backward compatible: the 2-D path is unchanged and slot selection only
triggers for 3-D inputs, so there is no behavior change for existing
(non-HC/MTP) callers.
## Related
- Split out from #47972 ("Support DeepSeek-V4 AMD Quark NVFP4 with emulation
  kernel"): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47972

title: [Bug]: #47327 dense-MHA split breaks FlashMLA sparse: OOB write in top-k index conversion, corrupted fp8_ds_mla context gather
body:
### Summary

#47327 (`c4f5cd60d`, "[1/N] Add dense MHA path for sparse MLA short sequences") routes short prefills (`prefill_max_seq_len <= topk_tokens`) to a dense-MHA path, so `forward_mqa` now receives only the leading `num_decode_tokens` tokens of the batch instead of all of them. Two parts of the FlashMLA sparse backend were not updated for that new contract:

1. an **out-of-bounds write** in the top-k index conversion whenever the split is active (any kv-cache dtype);
2. the dense-MHA path gathers cached context in a way that does not understand the **`fp8_ds_mla`** cache layout — silently wrong K/V without DCP, hard error with DCP.

Both are regressions from #47327: before it, every token went through the MQA path. cc @MatthewBonanni

### Repro

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla
```

**Bug 1 (OOB).** Send concurrent traffic so that a scheduler step holds at least one running decode plus a new short prompt (total seq len ≤ `index_topk` = 2048). The dense-MHA split activates, `forward_mqa` gets only the decode tokens, and the index-conversion kernel writes past the end of its output buffer: non-deterministic corruption of neighbouring GPU allocations, or `CUDA error: an illegal memory access`. Also reproduces with `--kv-cache-dtype auto` (bf16 cache).

**Bug 2 (context gather).** Multi-turn chat or any prefix-cache hit, i.e. a prefill that arrives with computed context, total sequence ≤ 2048. Without DCP the request completes but its context K/V is garbage, so the output is silently wrong. With DCP it raises `RuntimeError: src_cache and dst must have the same dtype`.

### Root cause 1 — unsliced `req_id_per_token`

`FlashMLASparseImpl.forward_mqa` slices `topk_indices = self.topk_indices_buffer[:num_actual_toks]` with `num_actual_toks = q.shape[0]` (the MQA subset), but all three forward paths pass the **full-batch** `attn_metadata.req_id_per_token` to `triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index`:

- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py:602` (`_forward_bf16_kv`), `:643` (`_forward_fp8_kv_separate_prefill_decode`), `:741` (`_forward_fp8_kv_mixed_batch`)

The converter sizes its grid by `req_id.shape[0]` but allocates `out = torch.empty_like(token_indices)` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_utils.py:168,176`), so rows `[num_mqa_tokens, num_batch_tokens)` are written **past the end of `out`**.

The MQA subset is exactly the leading `num_decode_tokens` tokens (the runner reorders decodes first, `reorder_batch_to_split_decodes_and_prefills`), so the fix is the same slice the FlashInfer and FlashAttn sparse backends already do (`flashinfer_mla_sparse.py:397`, `flashattn_mla_sparse.py:227`).

### Root cause 2 — `fp8_ds_mla` context gather on the dense-MHA path

When the prefill has context (`prefill.chunked_context is not None`), `forward_mha` gathers cached KV (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py:2349,2377-2393`). The `fp8_ds_mla` entry is 656B — 512B fp8 NoPE quantized with **per-128-tile** scales, 4×fp32 inline scales, 64×bf16 RoPE (see the writer, `concat_and_cache_ds_mla_kernel`, `csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu:447`) — and neither gather understands it:

- **DCP** (`_context_parallel_compute_prefill_context`, `mla_attention.py:2216-2241`): the dequant branch explicitly excludes `fp8_ds_mla`, so it falls through to raw `ops.cp_gather_cache`, which requires equal src/dst dtypes (`cache_kernels.cu:1363-1364`) — uint8 cache vs bf16 workspace → `RuntimeError`.
- **non-DCP** (`_compute_prefill_context`, `mla_attention.py:2102-2112`): `gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache(kv_cache_dtype="fp8_ds_mla")` dispatches `fp8_ds_mla` as plain E4M3 (`csrc/attention/dtype_fp8.cuh:28-30`) and dequantizes the **first 576 bytes** of each 656B entry element-wise with a single global scale (`cache_kernels.cu:1032-1051`): the NoPE bytes get the wrong scale, the inline scale words and part of the bf16 RoPE bytes are decoded as fp8 values, and the RoPE tail is never read. **Nothing raises — the context K/V is silently corrupted.**

Short **no-context** prefills — the case #47327 optimizes and benchmarks — never read the cache, so they are unaffected and should keep the fast path.

### Additional fallout found while triaging

With `fp8_ds_mla` and ≥32 heads per rank (e.g. DSV3.2 at TP1/2/4), FlashMLA takes `_forward_fp8_kv_separate_prefill_decode`, whose FP8 metadata is still built for the **full batch** (`_build_fp8_separate_prefill_decode`, `flashmla_sparse.py:353-494`). Under the dense-MHA split it allocates a full-batch output and iterates prefill chunks whose `tokens_slice` lies beyond the decode-only `q` → shape-mismatch `RuntimeError`, even without context. Making that path subset-aware (or gating `use_mha` for it) needs its own change; noting it here so it is not lost.

### Environment

Found on vLLM `main` (`793cf79c8`) while rebasing #46514. Analysis is static plus code reading; a GPU repro of the OOB with `compute-sanitizer` is the obvious confirmation and we are running it tonight.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for this analysis; the submitter reviewed every claim against the source.

title: [BugFix] Sparse MLA: fix req_id_per_token OOB write and fp8_ds_mla context-prefill routing after the dense-MHA split
body:
FIX #48611

## Purpose

Two regressions from #47327 (dense-MHA path for sparse-MLA short sequences). Full root-cause analysis with `file:line` is in the linked issue; the short version:

**1. OOB write in the FlashMLA sparse index conversion.** After #47327, `forward_mqa` receives only the MQA subset (the leading decode tokens), but all three FlashMLA forward paths still passed the full-batch `req_id_per_token` to `triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index`, whose grid is sized by `req_id` while the output is allocated like `token_indices` — the extra rows were written past the end of the output buffer. Fixed by slicing `req_id_per_token[: topk_indices.shape[0]]` at the three call sites, exactly as the FlashInfer and FlashAttn sparse backends already do, plus a length-invariant assert in the shared converter so a future mismatch fails loudly instead of corrupting memory.

**2. `fp8_ds_mla` context gather on the dense-MHA path.** When a short prefill carries cached context, `forward_mha` gathers it with kernels that do not understand the 656B `fp8_ds_mla` entry layout: raw `cp_gather_cache` rejects the uint8/bf16 dtype mismatch under DCP, and `gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache` otherwise dequantizes the raw bytes as flat fp8 with a single global scale, silently corrupting the context K/V. Fixed by keeping such prefills on the top-k MQA path, gated on `kv_cache_dtype == "fp8_ds_mla"` **and** `prefill.chunked_context is not None`.

Short **no-context** prefills — the case #47327 optimizes and benchmarks (DeepSeek-V3.2 short prompts) — never read the cache, so they keep the new dense-MHA fast path. kv-cache-dtype aliases cannot bypass the gate: `fp8`/`fp8_e4m3` are canonicalized to `fp8_ds_mla` before the layer stores `kv_cache_dtype`.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR addresses either regression (searched `req_id_per_token`, sparse-MLA / `fp8_ds_mla` dense-MHA). #34744 is the masked-MHA follow-up to #47327; #45537 is an unrelated `cp_gather_cache` bounds fix.

## Test plan

New regression tests in `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py`:

- `test_triton_convert_rejects_req_id_longer_than_token_indices` — the converter rejects the full-batch/subset length mismatch instead of writing OOB, and the sliced call matches the reference.
- `test_flashmla_forward_bf16_kv_slices_req_id_to_mqa_tokens` — call-site regression: `_forward_bf16_kv` with full-batch metadata and a subset `q`/`topk_indices` converts exactly the MQA rows (fails before the fix).
- `test_fp8_ds_mla_context_prefill_stays_on_mqa_path` — the dense-MHA path is blocked precisely for `fp8_ds_mla` + chunked context and stays available with no context; covers dtype-alias canonicalization.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -v \
  -k "triton_convert or forward_bf16_kv_slices or fp8_ds_mla_context"
```

## Test result

- `ruff check` / `ruff format` on all touched files: clean.
- **GPU suite (4×H200, CUDA 12.9):** `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py` → **111 passed, 422 skipped, 0 failed** (8 min). The three new regression tests pass by name:
  - `test_triton_convert_rejects_req_id_longer_than_token_indices` PASSED
  - `test_flashmla_forward_bf16_kv_slices_req_id_to_mqa_tokens` PASSED
  - `test_fp8_ds_mla_context_prefill_stays_on_mqa_path` PASSED
- **End-to-end:** both fixes are running in our production deployment (GLM-5.2-NVFP4, 4×H200, TP4 / DCP4 / EP, `fp8_ds_mla`, MTP, prefix caching + CPU KV offload). Multi-turn chat with prefix-cache hits — the exact case that hits the broken `fp8_ds_mla` context gather — returns correct output; a 4×551k-token concurrent stress run retrieved all 4 needles with no crash.
- No model-eval delta expected on supported paths: the change only restores pre-#47327 routing for the broken cases and leaves the new fast path in place for short no-context prefills.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude) was used for this change. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: Port DeepGemm MHC Kernel to CuTeDSL
body:
## Motivation

In the long run we want to port [Hopper and Blackwell Kernels to CuTeDSL])(https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47334).
This PR ports [the following DeepGemm Kernel](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/main/deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/impls/sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm.cuh) used for DeepSeek MHC to `CuTeDSL`.
I choose DeepGemm implementation as default because the CuTeDSL Kernel is basically on par.
I still believe this Kernel is valuable because it can serve in cases where DeepGemm is not available on B200s and can furthermore be seen as a best practice example of implementing CuTe Kernels. Furthermore we can extend it in the future to support further configurations without much developer cost.

## Current performance numbers

DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP=8 on 8 x NVIDIA B200 GPUs, FP8 KV cache, 1,024
requests at concurrency 128.

| Input / output | DeepGemm tok/s | CuTeDSL tok/s | CuTeDSL delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8192 / 128 | 56,352 | 55,923 | -0.76% |
| 2048 / 2048 | 10,515 | 10,493 | -0.21% |
| 128 / 8192 | 5,812 | 5,814 | +0.04% |

CuTeDSL is at end-to-end performance parity with DeepGemm across all three
workloads. All 6,144 benchmark requests completed successfully.


## Next steps

Port further DeepGemm kernels to CuTeDSL to reach above RFC. Improve performance of this kernel further (it is relatively untuned).
