title: [KV Offload] Enable single-copy MLA layout for CPUOffloadingSpec
body:
## Purpose

Enable the single-copy (replicated) MLA layout for the default KV-offload backend `CPUOffloadingSpec`, closing out the plan in #47929. After #50094 moved the default backend's worker CPU buffer onto the shared `SharedOffloadRegion` (on CUDA/ROCm), the default backend can now deduplicate the per-TP-rank-replicated MLA KV the same way `TieringOffloadingSpec` already does — but only on deployments that actually allocate on the shared region.

MLA latent KV is logically replicated across TP ranks (expected to be byte-identical in homogeneous TP without context parallelism), so storing one copy instead of `world_size` copies is safe under the existing `replicated_layout` gate (pure-MLA single group, TP>1, `PP=PCP=DCP=1`, `world==tp`, single-node mp).

Maintainer context (upstream reviewers do not see the issue thread):

- The two-PR plan (allocation swap in #50094, then this dedup), proposed and +1'd by @orozery: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47929#issuecomment-5096162285
- @orozery confirmed an independent PR is fine: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47929#issuecomment-4921375612
- Prerequisite (merged): #50094 (`CPUOffloadingSpec` → `SharedOffloadRegion`).

## What changes

- `replicated_layout` is gated by a new per-spec hook `_uses_shared_region()` — `current_platform.is_cuda_alike()` for the default spec, `True` for `TieringOffloadingSpec`. It is the **single source of truth** used by both the replicated-layout sizing (`num_copies`) and the `create_worker` allocation path, so the two cannot drift. This replaces the static `SUPPORTS_REPLICATED_LAYOUT` capability flag, which is removed: now that the default spec can deduplicate on the shared region, that flag was `True` for every in-tree spec and carried no information.
- `CPUOffloadingSpec.create_worker` now maps every rank to slot 0 under replicated layout (single MLA copy) and otherwise folds the physical device index into `[0, world_size)` — mirroring `TieringOffloadingSpec.create_worker`.
- `TieringOffloadingSpec` overrides `_uses_shared_region()` to `True` (it always allocates on the shared region, on every platform), so its behavior is unchanged.

## Why the platform gate is load-bearing (fail-closed)

The `replicated_layout` config gate has no platform clause, and #50094 intentionally kept non-CUDA-alike platforms (currently XPU) on a per-rank **private** pinned tensor. Enabling dedup there would be a correctness bug, not a perf trade-off: the connector's rank-0 writer gate (`offloading/worker.py`, `not spec.replicated_layout or rank == 0`) would ack rank>0 stores without performing the D2H copy, leaving those private buffers empty and corrupting later loads. Gating the flip on `_uses_shared_region()` makes non-shared-region deployments fail closed to the existing private, per-rank layout; a dedicated test pins this.

## Behavior changes

- Replicated-MLA deployments on the default backend: one host copy instead of `world_size` — cache capacity scales ×TP for the same `cpu_bytes_to_use`, and D2H store traffic drops to `1/TP` (only rank 0 writes). Store-throughput metrics become writer-only, same as the tiering spec's existing disclosure.
- Non-CUDA-alike platforms: unchanged (private per-rank tensor, per-rank sizing).
- `TieringOffloadingSpec`: unchanged.
- Deduplication rests on the existing gate's premise that the per-rank MLA KV is logically replicated (expected byte-identical in homogeneous TP without context parallelism) — the same assumption `TieringOffloadingSpec` already relies on; this PR stores one copy instead of `world_size`. The default backend has no persistent tier, so there is no cross-version on-disk compatibility concern.

## Not in this PR

- No change to the `replicated_layout` config gate predicate, the transfer protocol, or the tiering spec.
- XPU pinning is not addressed (#50094 already scoped around it; this PR inherits that boundary).
- Multi-group / non-MLA uniform-layout extensions remain future work (tracked with #48408).

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs (`SUPPORTS_REPLICATED_LAYOUT`, `CPUOffloadingSpec replicated`, `47929 in:body`) and the touched-path history — no open PR enables dedup for the default CPU offload backend. Nearest neighbor: #48414 (@Etelis) works the parallelism-agnostic canonical **allocation** layout (the #50094 area); it does not touch the replicated-layout gate, so there is no overlap with this PR.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Unit (offloading spec gating + sizing + create_worker)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/spec.py vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/spec.py tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py
```

A100 TP=2 end-to-end (MLA model to exercise `replicated_layout`): serve DeepSeek-V2-Lite with `-tp 2` and the OffloadingConnector, before (no dedup) vs after (dedup), and compare the connector's D2H store bytes and greedy output.

## Test Result

Unit (NVIDIA L4, torch 2.13.0+cu130): `tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py` — **38 passed**. Covers the platform × config truth matrix, shared-region single-copy sizing (`num_copies=1`), the non-shared-region **data-loss guard** (replicated stays off, per-rank sizing preserved), and the replicated `create_worker` (rank 0). `pre-commit` (ruff, ruff-format, mypy, SPDX, `torch.cuda`-API guard) all pass.

A100 TP=2 E2E (2× A100-SXM4-80GB, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, `--load-format dummy --seed 0 -tp 2`, `cpu_bytes_to_use=4 GiB`, image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-6f91edf96d` whose `v1/kv_offload/` is byte-identical to this PR's base — only the two changed spec files were overlaid for the "after" run):

| | connector D2H `store_bytes_total` | greedy output |
|---|---|---|
| before (no dedup, `world_size` copies) | 24.8832 MB | reference |
| after (dedup, single copy) | 12.4416 MB | **identical** |

The store bytes drop to exactly `1/TP` — only rank 0 performs the D2H copy under the writer gate — confirming `replicated_layout` engages for the default backend on an MLA model. Greedy generation is unchanged for this deterministic dummy-weights run. (This run exercises the D2H store side; it does not force a CPU→GPU reload and is not itself a per-rank KV byte-equality proof.) The capacity ×TP effect is the `num_copies=1` sizing, covered by the unit tests; the byte-exact GPU↔shared-region transfer is covered by #50094's `test_transfer[use_shared_memory=True]` and the tiering suite.

---

This PR was developed with AI assistance (implementation and tests). Unit tests and lint were run on the submitter's NVIDIA L4 workstation; the A100 TP=2 E2E was run on 2× A100-80GB.

title: [CI] Organize speculative decoding E2E tests by coverage
body:
## Summary

- Split the monolithic speculative-decoding E2E suite into feature directories that match CI ownership.
- Make Buildkite run directory scopes instead of keyword/file allowlists, so tests added to an existing area are discovered by default.
- Restore nightly DFlash and DSpark acceptance/accuracy coverage, using `poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-NVFP4` to keep Laguna practical on smaller GPUs.
- Fix the Gemma4 DSpark causality metadata and isolate the draft quant config from an NVFP4 target, both exposed by activating the existing Gemma test.

This is intentionally opinionated: directory boundaries are the CI contract. The three high-footprint Eagle cases and the four-GPU job remain intentionally removed; this change does not reintroduce them.

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/pre-commit run` — passed
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py` — 10 passed

Model checks: Laguna accuracy `0.905`, acceptance length `3.84`; Qwen DSpark accuracy `0.804`, acceptance length `4.04`; Gemma4 DSpark accuracy `0.920`, acceptance length `5.02`. DFlash reference-acceptance thresholds also passed.

## Duplicate work

Searched open PRs for the spec-decode test split and CI coverage; no PR duplicates this reorganization. #49133 is related but targets DeepSeek DSpark quant dispatch. This PR's loader hardening covers the newly active Gemma4 NVFP4-target/BF16-draft case and preserves the target `model_config` used for DSpark target-layer metadata.

AI assistance was used. The submitter reviewed the changed lines and ran the validation above.

title: [Bug]: DeepGemm accuracy auto-disable (_DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL_EXCLUDED_MODEL_TYPES) does not apply to the FP8 MoE path
body:
### Your current environment

- Hardware: NVIDIA GB10, **SM121 / compute capability 12.1** (also relevant to SM120 generally)
- vLLM **0.26.0** (standard PyPI wheel, aarch64), torch 2.11.0+cu130, `--enforce-eager`, TP=1
- Model: `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` — `model_type: **qwen3_5_moe_text**`, 256-expert FP8 MoE

### 🐛 Describe the bug

vLLM correctly identifies that DeepGemm is inaccurate for this model type and logs so at startup:

```
WARNING [vllm.py:1008] Auto-disabled DeepGemm for model_type=qwen3_5_moe_text on Blackwell.
  DeepGemm E8M0 scale format causes accuracy degradation for this architecture.
  Falling back to CUTLASS. To disable DeepGemm globally, set VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0.
```

…and then **selects DeepGemm anyway for the MoE layers**:

```
INFO [fp8.py:405] Using DEEPGEMM Fp8 MoE backend out of potential backends:
  ['AITER', 'FLASHINFER_TRTLLM', 'FLASHINFER_CUTLASS', 'DEEPGEMM', 'TRITON', 'MARLIN', ...]
```

The auto-disable sets `quant_config.use_deep_gemm = False` (`vllm/config/vllm.py`), and
`qwen3_5_moe_text` **is** present in `_DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL_EXCLUDED_MODEL_TYPES`
(`vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py`) — so the denylist is doing its job. But `use_deep_gemm` appears to have
**no references anywhere under `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/`**; the FP8 MoE backend
selector honors only the `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM` / `VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM` env vars. Net effect: the
denylist covers dense linear layers only, and the MoE layers — where the accuracy concern for an MoE
model actually matters most — still run DeepGemm.

So the warning is truthful about dense layers and silently wrong about MoE.

### Why this surfaced now

**PR #43477** ("Enable DeepSeek V4 and GLM-5.1 on SM120", shipped v0.24.0) added
`is_device_capability_family(120)` to `deep_gemm.py`. Prior to that, the SM100-family gate meant
DeepGemm was never *eligible* on SM121, so this gap was latent. The FP8 MoE backend priority list
itself is unchanged — DeepGemm simply became eligible and started winning.

Consistent with this, the original accuracy fix **#37804** reasoned that "MoE layers are unaffected
(already use FLASHINFER_TRTLLM)" — which holds on SM100 but **not** on SM121, where
FLASHINFER_TRTLLM is gated out (#43906).

### Impact

1. **Accuracy** — the exact degradation #37804 set out to prevent still applies to this model's MoE
   layers on SM120/121.
2. **Performance** — measurable on our hardware. Forcing Triton MoE (matching what vLLM 0.20.1
   selected) recovered most of a regression vs 0.20.1: median TPOT went 37.3 → 34.9ms at
   concurrency 1 and 43.7 → 39.3ms at concurrency 4 for this model.

### Expected behavior

The `_DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL_EXCLUDED_MODEL_TYPES` denylist should gate the FP8 **MoE** backend
selection as well as dense linear layers — i.e. `Fp8MoeBackend` selection should consult the same
`use_deep_gemm`/model-type exclusion rather than only the env vars.

### Workaround

`--moe-backend triton` (or `VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`). We shipped `--moe-backend triton`.

### Related

- **#47169** (open) is the *same gap in the warmup path* ("DeepGemm warmup ignores auto-disable"),
  reported on SM120 with a GB10/SM121 reproducer in the comments — likely the same fix area.
- **#37804** (closed) — origin of the denylist.
- **#43477** — made DeepGemm SM120-family eligible.
- **#41306** (open) — maintainer-confirmed MoE backend-selection perf regression of a similar shape.

### Note on SM121 specifically

On SM121 the alternatives to Triton for FP8 MoE all appear unusable, which is why `--moe-backend
triton` is the only workaround we found: FLASHINFER_TRTLLM gated to SM100 (#43906), VLLM_CUTLASS has
no SM120/121 CollectiveBuilder (#43507), MARLIN produces corrupt output on GB10 (#49546), HUMMING
crashes at startup (#49554).

title: [Bug][ROCm][MI355X] Kimi-K3 TP8 crashes in ROCM_AITER_MLA with HIP Code 700
body:
### Your current environment

- GPU: 8x AMD MI355X (gfx950)
- Container: vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k3
- vLLM: 0.1.dev19253+g5f76ae224.d20260727
- Target model: moonshotai/Kimi-K3
- Draft model: Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark
- Parallelism: TP8 / PP1
- Quantization: MXFP4
- dtype: bfloat16
- Execution: enforce eager
- Full collect_env.py output: pending; can provide from a follow-up reproduction run.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Summary

Kimi-K3 with DSpark crashes during AgentX warmup on 8x AMD MI355X with:

```text
RuntimeError: Triton Error [HIP]: Code: 700, Message: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

The target model automatically selects `ROCM_AITER_MLA`. The synchronous traceback points to:

```text
vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py::forward_mqa
→ aiter/ops/triton/gluon/mla_gluon.py::mla_gluon
→ _mla_gluon
```

The DSpark draft model separately uses `TRITON_MLA`. The crash occurs in the Kimi-K3 target-model attention path.

## Configuration

```text
Hardware: 8x AMD MI355X (gfx950)
Container: vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k3
vLLM: 0.1.dev19253+g5f76ae224.d20260727
Target model: moonshotai/Kimi-K3
Draft model: Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark
Parallelism: TP8 / PP1
Concurrency: 1
Quantization: MXFP4
dtype: bfloat16
```

Relevant server arguments:

```bash
export AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3

vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --language-model-only \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --speculative-config \
  '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"method":"dspark","attention_backend":"TRITON_MLA","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.84}'
```

## Observed behavior

The server loads the 1.45 TiB target checkpoint successfully and begins serving requests. During AgentX warmup, 12 requests complete successfully before multiple TP workers fail with HIP Code 700.

Relevant traceback:

```text
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py", line 895, in forward_impl
  attn_out, lse = self.impl.forward_mqa(...)

File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py", line 1044, in forward_mqa
  mla_gluon(...)

File "aiter/ops/triton/gluon/mla_gluon.py", line 937, in mla_gluon
  _mla_gluon[grid](...)

RuntimeError: Triton Error [HIP]: Code: 700,
Message: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

After one worker fails, the TP8 EngineCore terminates and the client receives HTTP 500.

## Isolation performed

- Reproduced with concurrency 1.
- Reproduced without `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` using GPU-only KV cache.
- Reproduced by the real block-rejection eval path.
- `AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3` reproduction points to the same MLA call path.
- This is TP8/PP1, so it is not a pipeline-parallel failure.
- The DSpark draft uses `TRITON_MLA`; the target model still automatically selects `ROCM_AITER_MLA`.

A control run forces the target model to `TRITON_MLA` to bypass `ROCM_AITER_MLA`:

https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/30501609272

## Expected behavior

Kimi-K3 TP8 should complete warmup and inference on MI355X without an illegal memory access when using `ROCM_AITER_MLA`.

## References

- InferenceX PR: https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/2403
- Failed AgentX sweep: https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/30496771349
- GPU-only serialized reproduction: https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/30499842314
- TRITON_MLA control run: https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/30501609272

title: [K3] Enable DS align state copies with speculative decoding
body:
## Summary

This is a focused follow-up to #50000 that enables the DS convolution-state
layout with Model Runner V2, align-mode Mamba prefix caching, asynchronous
scheduling, and speculative decoding.

The fused pre-copy and postprocess kernels already support DS state by shifting
along the state-length axis using per-row count and stride metadata. The
remaining blocker was a stale assertion in `MambaHybridModelState` based on the
older contiguous `MambaCopySpec` path, which cannot represent a strided DS
slice.

- Remove the stale DS plus speculative-decoding guard from the MRV2 align path.
- Clarify that DS offsets are handled by both fused state-copy kernels.
- Extend the existing fused pre-copy equivalence test across SD and DS layouts,
  request counts 1/4/16, and token offsets 0/1/7.
- Add an MRV2 DS plus asynchronous-scheduling prefix-cache test case.

Related issue: #38897.

## Duplicate-work check

The required searches were run:

```bash
gh issue view 38897 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open \
  --search "38897 in:body"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open \
  --search "DS conv state layout speculative decoding mamba align"
```

No open PR references #38897, and the area search found no direct duplicate.
The nearest open work is materially different:

- #49436 optimizes state-copy kernel tiling; it does not remove the DS/spec
  guard or add DS MRV2 coverage.
- #46912 is a broader, draft pre-copy-free redesign of align-mode prefix
  caching.
- #42792 provides the broader MRV2 speculative-decoding align implementation.
  This patch uses that implementation already present in the `kimi-k3` base
  and narrowly unblocks and validates DS.

This PR is stacked on #50000 and is intended to target its `kimi-k3` branch.

## Testing

### Focused CUDA correctness

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/mamba/test_precopy_mamba_align.py -v
```

Result: 18 passed. The matrix covers both layouts, 1/4/16 requests, offsets
0/1/7, fresh requests, same-block no-ops, cross-block convolution-state
shifts, and temporal-state copies. State comparisons use zero tolerance.

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  tests/kernels/mamba/test_precopy_mamba_align.py \
  tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_utils.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py
git diff --check origin/kimi-k3...HEAD
```

Result: all applicable pre-commit hooks passed; `git diff --check` produced no
errors.

### E2E and model evaluation

The run served `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` as one TP8 replica on two GB300 nodes with:

- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`
- `VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS`
- align-mode Mamba prefix caching
- automatically enabled asynchronous scheduling
- dSpark speculative decoding with 7 draft tokens
- `max_num_seqs=256` and `max_num_batched_tokens=32768`

Five full GSM8K 5-shot evaluations ran at concurrency 512, with 1,319 samples per run:

| Run | Strict exact match | Flexible exact match |
| ---: | -----------------: | -------------------: |
| 1 | 0.9629 | 0.9629 |
| 2 | 0.9613 | 0.9613 |
| 3 | 0.9613 | 0.9613 |
| 4 | 0.9621 | 0.9621 |
| 5 | 0.9613 | 0.9613 |

The output scanner checked all 6,595 generations and reported 0 garbage
responses.

An additional held-server probe exercised exact Mamba block boundaries, shared
prefixes, and full scheduler occupancy under the same configuration:

- 510/510 requests succeeded; the cumulative prefix-cache hit rate was 65.1%
  (810,240 of 1,244,567 queried tokens).
- Repeated 1,537/2,303/2,305/3,071/3,073-token prompts produced identical
  outputs and hit 768/768/1,536/1,536/2,304 prefix tokens, respectively.
- A repeated 6,789-token chat completed 16/16 requests, with all 8 replays
  matching and 5,376 cached tokens per replay.
- A 256-request concurrent wave completed 256/256 requests with unique response
  IDs and no garbage output.
- dSpark accepted 14,101 of 27,174 drafted tokens. Health remained HTTP 200,
  with no queued requests or live engine/CUDA/NCCL failures after the probes.

## AI assistance and human accountability

OpenAI Codex was used for implementation support, test authoring, log analysis,
and drafting this description.

title: [DCP] Default query replication for GLM sparse attention
body:
## Summary

- add `--dcp-q-replicate` and `--no-dcp-q-replicate` as explicit CLI options;
- preserve `VLLM_DCP_Q_REPLICATE` as the highest-precedence override;
- enable query replication automatically for `glm_moe_dsa` models when decode DCP is enabled and PCP is not enabled;
- keep query replication opt-in for other MLA model families.

The automatic default removes GLM's decode query all-gather at the cost of replicating the query projection weights across DCP ranks. Explicit CLI or environment selections still override the model default.

## Performance and memory

GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP=4, DCP=4, 32K input tokens, 128 output tokens, batch 8, two warmups, five measured iterations:

- QREP off: 20.1777 s
- QREP on: 19.7426 s
- delta: -0.4351 s (-2.16%)

With QREP enabled, a fresh DCP backend comparison measured:

| DCP backend | Average latency |
| --- | ---: |
| `ag_rs` | 19.7636 s |
| `a2a` | 18.0213 s |

For the matched 32K benchmark configuration, model-loading memory increased from 110.37 GiB/rank to 114.94 GiB/rank with QREP, approximately +4.57 GiB/rank.

## Model evaluation

GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP=4, DCP=4, GSM8K 5-shot, 300 questions:

- automatic GLM QREP default: 94.0% accuracy, 0% invalid outputs;
- explicit QREP off: 95.0% accuracy, 0% invalid outputs.

The QREP-off evaluation used `max_num_seqs=32` because FlashInfer's sparse-MLA workspace overflowed when all prompts were scheduled concurrently. Both runs evaluated the same 300 questions with the same decoding settings. The one-point difference is not significant at this sample size.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, benchmarking, profiling analysis, and drafting this description. The human submitter has reviewed.

title: [RFC]: Support Speculative Decoding with Decode Context Parallelism
body:
### Motivation. vLLM currently does not support using speculative decoding together with Decode Context Parallelism (DCP). This limitation applies to all DCP configurations, including both `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size = 1` and larger interleave sizes. DCP shards KV-cache tokens across ranks according to their global positions. For a global sequence length `L`, DCP size `D`, interleave size `I`, and rank `r`, the rank-local KV length is: ```text local_len(r, L) = floor(L / (D * I)) * I + clamp(L % (D * I) - r * I, 0, I) ``` During speculative verification, one request contains multiple query tokens. Query token `j`, with historical context length `H`, must see: ```text local_len(r, H + j + 1) ``` KV tokens on rank `r`. These boundaries differ across queries and ranks and cannot in general be inferred from the final rank-local KV length. DCP also affects the proposer. After speculative acceptance or rejection, the global sequence length changes, but the corresponding rank-local sequence length cannot be updated by directly adding or subtracting the number of accepted or rejected tokens. It must be derived again from the corrected global length and DCP topology. The goal of this RFC is to add complete DCP and speculative-decoding compatibility for: 1. autoregressive speculative proposers; 2. multi-token target verification in attention backends; 3. different context lengths, DCP ranks, interleave sizes, and acceptance results; 4. eager execution and CUDA Graph replay. ### Proposed Change. ### 1. Speculative decoding proposer The proposer must generate DCP-aware attention metadata for every autoregressive draft step. After speculative rejection is applied, the proposer has a corrected global sequence length. Before building the next draft attention metadata, it must recompute the corresponding rank-local sequence length from: ```text global sequence length DCP size DCP rank KV-cache interleave size ``` The proposer must not update rank-local length using: ```python local_seq_len += 1 local_seq_len -= num_rejected ``` Consecutive global tokens may belong to different DCP ranks, including when `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size = 1`. #### Draft metadata update Before building attention metadata for every draft decode step, the proposer should populate a persistent DCP local-length buffer: ```python prepare_dcp_local_seq_lens( input_buffers.dcp_local_seq_lens, input_buffers.seq_lens, num_reqs, dcp_size, dcp_rank, cp_interleave, ) ``` The resulting tensor must be passed to the attention metadata builder: ```python build_attn_metadata( ..., seq_lens=input_buffers.seq_lens, dcp_local_seq_lens=input_buffers.dcp_local_seq_lens, ) ``` The draft-step metadata flow is: ```text Apply rejection to global sequence length ↓ Prepare the absolute draft position ↓ Prepare DCP-aware slot mapping ↓ Recompute rank-local sequence length ↓ Build draft attention metadata ↓ Run proposer attention ↓ Advance global state for the next draft step ``` Rank-local sequence length must be recomputed after every global sequence-length change. ### 2. Attention backend strategies #### Problem For a target verification request with historical length `H` and `N` query tokens, the final local KV length on rank `r` is: ```text local_len(r, H + N) ``` However, query token `j` may only attend to: ```text local_len(r, H + j + 1) ``` local KV tokens. A conventional causal attention kernel generally derives all query boundaries from the final KV length. Under DCP, this may expose future speculative KV or hide valid KV, producing incorrect verifier logits and acceptance decisions. For example:
Example: DCP=2, MTP=3, context length=5 Assume: - `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size = 1` - MTP3 produces a target decode query length of 4 - `Q0–Q3` are at global positions `5–8` - `1` means visible and `0` means masked The global KV ownership is: | Global position | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 (Q0) | 6 (Q1) | 7 (Q2) | 8 (Q3) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | DCP owner | R0 | R1 | R0 | R1 | R0 | R1 | R0 | R1 | R0 | #### Rank 0 The final local KV sequence is `[k0, k2, k4, k6, k8]`. | Query | k0 | k2 | k4 | k6 | k8 | Visible local KV length | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Q0, global position 5 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 3 | | Q1, global position 6 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 4 | | Q2, global position 7 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 4 | | Q3, global position 8 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 5 | #### Rank 1 The final local KV sequence is `[k1, k3, k5, k7]`. | Query | k1 | k3 | k5 | k7 | Visible local KV length | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Q0, global position 5 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 3 | | Q1, global position 6 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 3 | | Q2, global position 7 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 4 | | Q3, global position 8 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 4 | A conventional bottom-right causal mask derives visibility only from the local KV length and query length. It would produce: | | Rank 0 | Rank 1 | |---|---|---| | Correct per-query visibility | `[3, 4, 4, 5]` | `[3, 3, 4, 4]` | | Bottom-right causal visibility | `[2, 3, 4, 5]` | `[1, 2, 3, 4]` | The mismatch occurs because advancing one global query token does not necessarily increase the local KV length on every DCP rank. Therefore, the backend needs per-query rank-local KV boundaries, a rank-specific mask, or a context/current split implementation.
The following strategies can implement the required per-query rank-local visibility. #### Strategy A: Direct CP-aware attention The attention kernel receives the information required to convert global causal boundaries into rank-local KV boundaries: ```text DCP size DCP rank interleave size global query positions global sequence lengths ``` For FlashAttention, this strategy can be used when the selected kernel interface supports CP rank, CP world size, and KV-cache interleave. Flow: ```text Q[N] + rank-local paged KV + global positions and DCP topology ↓ CP-aware attention ↓ partial output + LSE ↓ DCP output/LSE reduction ``` Performance impact: - one main attention call; - no custom dense mask; - no virtual batch expansion; - lowest dispatch and metadata overhead; - requires backend-specific kernel support; - every supported interleave configuration must be validated. This provides the highest expected performance but has the highest kernel implementation cost. #### Strategy B: Split context and current KV Historical KV and the current speculative KV block are computed separately. Historical path: ```text Q[N] × rank-local paged historical KV non-causal ``` Current path: ```text Q[N] × current K/V[N] causal ``` The two attention states are merged using their output and LSE. This can be implemented using a chunked-prefill-style flow: the paged cache represents historical context, while raw current K/V represents the speculative token block. Flow: ```text Q × local paged history ↓ history output + LSE \ → LSE/state merge → DCP reduction / Q × current K/V ↓ causal output + LSE ``` Performance impact: - supports arbitrary DCP ranks and interleave layouts; - does not require a rank-specific dense mask; - requires two attention calls and one state merge; - introduces additional workspace and launch overhead; - MLA implementations may require context chunk gathering or reconstruction. This provides a portable implementation when direct CP-aware attention is not available. #### Strategy C: Custom mask The backend constructs a rank-specific attention mask that explicitly describes the visible local KV range for every speculative query. For query token `j` on DCP rank `r`: ```text local_boundary[j] = local_len(r, H + j + 1) mask[j, k] = k >= local_boundary[j] ``` Each DCP rank generates a different mask because its local KV length and per-query visibility boundaries are different. Flow: ```text Global history and query positions ↓ Compute rank-local boundary for every query ↓ Construct rank-specific custom mask ↓ Q[N] × rank-local paged KV ↓ partial output + LSE ↓ DCP output/LSE reduction ``` Performance impact: - supports arbitrary DCP sizes, interleave configurations, and variable query lengths; - retains a single main attention call; - requires `O(batch × N × local_KV)` mask memory; - introduces device-side or host-to-device mask construction overhead; - increases CUDA Graph input and persistent-buffer sizes; - mask generation cost grows with context length; - **may disable optimized causal kernels and force the backend to use a more generic masked-attention kernel**. This is suitable for backends with efficient custom-mask support. #### Strategy D: Expand N tokens into N virtual requests One request containing `N` speculative query tokens is represented as `N` virtual single-query attention rows. Virtual row `j` uses: ```text query position = H + j global sequence length = H + j + 1 local sequence length = local_len(r, H + j + 1) query length = 1 ``` Each virtual row reuses the original request's KV-cache block table while providing an independent context length. Flow: ```text One request with N query tokens ↓ N virtual q_len=1 rows ↓ Duplicate block-table references and sequence metadata ↓ Batched single-token DCP decode ↓ Restore the original token order ``` Performance impact: - reuses single-token DCP decode kernels; - supports arbitrary DCP layouts without a custom mask; - expands the logical batch size by up to `N`; - duplicates block-table and sequence metadata; - increases scheduling and metadata-processing overhead; - reduces batching efficiency; - requires larger CUDA Graph batch dimensions. This provides a correctness-oriented fallback but is expected to have the largest overhead as `N` grows. #### Strategy comparison | Strategy | Attention calls | Extra metadata | Kernel changes | Expected performance | |---|---:|---:|---:|---| | Direct CP-aware | 1 | Low | High | Best | | Context/current split | 2 + merge | Low | Medium | Good and portable | | Custom mask | 1 | `O(B×N×local_KV)` | Low/Medium | Context and kernel dependent | | Virtual single-query rows | 1 expanded batch | Block-table duplication | Low/Medium | Lower for larger `N` | ### Feedback Period. _No response_ ### CC List. @LucasWilkinson @GirasoleY @ZJY0516 ### Any Other Things. Related Links 1. PR #39632 introduces DCP-aware attention metadata reuse across MTP draft steps. It is related to the proposer changes in this RFC, while this RFC additionally defines how context lengths must be updated consistently across draft iterations and acceptance outcomes. 2. Issue #45425 reports incorrect results when a backend without DCP variable-length decode support executes MTP verification under full or piecewise CUDA graphs. It demonstrates why this RFC requires explicit backend handling of per-query rank-local KV boundaries instead of relying on conventional multi-token decode metadata. 3. PR #45426 computes per-token rank-local causal boundaries for the FlashMLA sparse path and enables DCP variable-length decode when the KV-cache interleave size is one. It provides a backend-specific implementation of the local-boundary approach considered by this RFC, while this RFC targets a backend-neutral design without assuming a particular interleave size. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Kernel][MoE] Add VMM-backed SharedEP for native FP4 decode on SM100
body:
# [Kernel][MoE] Add VMM-backed SharedEP for native FP4 decode on SM100

## Summary

This adds a `shared_ep` all-to-all backend for low-latency MoE decode on peer-accessible SM100 GPUs.

The conventional dispatch/combine path materializes both communication
boundaries:

```text
router
  -> pack and dispatch routed activations
  -> materialized expert-rank input
  -> expert W1/W2
  -> materialized rank-partial output
  -> combine and reduce
  -> owner output
```

SharedEP publishes persistent, peer-addressable objects instead:

```text
router
  -> owner quantizes into fixed VMM rows and publishes routes
  -> expert rank gathers NVFP4 rows into the local layout required by W1
  -> unchanged native W1/W2
  -> W2 writes directly into canonical owner/token/top-k VMM slots
  -> owner-local top-k reduction
```

The backend creates persistent rank-major CUDA VMM objects during model setup. Each rank owns one physical allocation per object, exchanges its POSIX allocation handle once over the CPU process group, and maps every owner allocation into a stable rank-major virtual address range. Typed owner views and persistent device pointer tables are also created once during setup.

There is no allocation, handle exchange, VMM mapping, pointer-table construction, or peer-tensor initialization in the model forward path. Runtime execution consists of native quantization, direct peer loads/stores, and system-scope GPU release/acquire epochs.

The selected backend fails closed. In particular, NVFP4 requires the exact
FlashInfer direct-output API and refuses to materialize a rank-partial W2
fallback. It does not switch to another EP backend, expert kernel, or
quantization path.

## Native GB200 paths

- GLM-5.2: BF16 owner input is quantized to native NVFP4, fixed owner-reserved rows are gathered through the VMM peer view into the contiguous local-HBM layout required by FlashInfer CuTeDSL, local experts execute, and the W2 finalize epilogue stores every expanded token/top-k contribution directly into its canonical owner VMM row.
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash: owner input is quantized to native MXFP8 with UE8M0 scales, the same fixed owner-reserved rows are gathered, FlashInfer TensorRT-LLM MXFP4/MXFP8 experts execute, and partial outputs are directly scattered into owner slots.

After all source ranks publish their output epoch, an NVFP4 owner reduces only
its local top-k slots. This removes the W2 output memset, rank-partial W2
tensor, remote output scatter, peer pull of four rank-partial tensors, and
world-rank output reduction. MXFP8 retains its existing rank-partial
scatter/reduction path.

This is adapted from SGLang PR #32482 with source attribution. That source PR was tested on H20, which has no native NVFP4 hardware path. This port intentionally uses the native NVFP4 and MXFP4/MXFP8 paths available on GB200 and in the local checkpoints.

## Scope and admission

`shared_ep` currently requires:

- one peer-accessible SM100 NVLink domain with native peer atomics;
- `TP=1`;
- DP/EP greater than one, with every DP/EP rank local to that domain;
- at most 32 scheduled tokens per rank;
- chunked prefill;
- no DBO/ubatching, EPLB, elastic EP, fault tolerance, or multi-node execution;
- the exact native NVFP4/CuTeDSL or MXFP4/MXFP8/TRT-LLM expert backend selected by the checkpoint.

Unsupported configurations raise an admission error.

## Relationship to #50009

vLLM PR #50009 owns the reusable `RankMajorPeerView` and `create_rank_major_peer_view` CUDA VMM implementation. This feature branch is stacked directly on that PR and imports those helpers; the generic VMM implementation is not duplicated in this feature diff.

The current feature commit is `35395b1d0b345fafea6b5640ac7750bb5cee7d9a`. Its local dependency base `a3400f39a` merges #50009 head `f5c8cc4c1` with vLLM main `e04a30a77`. The feature-only range is 21 files, 2,020 insertions, and 9 deletions. GitHub displays the unmerged #50009 stack in this draft as well, so the complete PR view is currently 39 files.

#50009 is the deliberate infrastructure dependency; no generic CUDA VMM implementation is duplicated here.

## Validation

Current-base CPU and four-GPU GB200 coverage:

- focused vLLM suite: 40 passed, 14 warnings in 40.68 s;
- same-allocation owner-pull distributed control: 2 passed, 14 warnings in 21.78 s;
- current FlashInfer direct-owner test: 1 passed, 380 deselected in 6.37 s after its one-time build;
- applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed in both repositories.

The strict GLM-shape EP4 matrix used 20 warmups, 100 captured iterations per
trial, five trials, and T=1/4/16/32. Direct W2 measured
`55.303/65.721/105.230/151.178 us` versus paired same-VMM-allocation
owner-pull `57.443/67.922/107.438/154.044 us`, saving
`2.141/2.201/2.209/2.866 us` or `3.73/3.24/2.06/1.86%`. Independent-reference
maximum absolute error remained `0.25`; eager repeat, graph replay, and
graph-versus-eager checks were exact.

## Model correctness and performance

Hardware: four NVIDIA GB200 GPUs in one NV18 peer-accessible domain.

The request-level protocol is EP4, batch one per rank, exactly 128 input and
128 greedy output tokens with `ignore_eos`, three warmups, five measured
trials, full/piecewise CUDA graphs with capture sizes 1/4/16/32, and
maximum-rank aggregation.

| GLM-5.2 backend/output boundary | Median TTFT | Median TPOT | Median elapsed | Rank-0 consumed memory | Rank-0 KV tokens |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SharedEP direct W2 | 139.513 ms | 14.305 ms/token | 2361.013 ms | 130.62 GiB | 725696 |
| SharedEP owner-pull control | 137.187 ms | 14.740 ms/token | 2424.229 ms | 132.24 GiB | 706368 |
| DeepEP low latency | 139.657 ms | 17.193 ms/token | 2811.797 ms | 133.93 GiB | 669760 |

Direct W2 versus owner-pull saves `0.435 ms/token` (`2.95%`) and `63.216 ms`
elapsed (`2.61%`), while TTFT is `2.327 ms` slower. The complete SharedEP path
versus DeepEP low latency saves `2.888 ms/token` (`16.80%`) and `450.783 ms`
elapsed (`16.03%`); TTFT differs by `0.144 ms`.

Maximum-rank TPOT trial vectors:

- direct W2: `14.3023/14.3077/14.3045/14.3052/14.3049 ms/token`;
- owner-pull: `14.7377/14.7355/14.7400/14.7449/14.7497 ms/token`;
- DeepEP low latency: `17.1884/17.1918/17.1933/17.1927/17.1905 ms/token`.

Every backend produced the same 128 greedy tokens on every rank and trial: the
sequence `[576, 6722, 315, 9621, 374, 12089, 13, 220]` repeated 16 times.

The owner-pull control uses the same direct-output VMM allocation but executes
FlashInfer's ordinary atomic finalize path. Its activation and CUDA-graph
accounting is therefore higher; "same allocation" does not mean identical
whole-engine memory use.

Current-base DeepSeek-V4-Flash SharedEP versus DeepEP-v2 timing is WIP. The
installed vLLM environment carries NCCL 2.29.7, so the DeepEP-v2 arm uses an
isolated `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.30.7` package. DeepEP 2.0 imports with its
duplicate-runtime check enabled, vLLM reports runtime NCCL 2.30.7,
`has_deep_ep_v2()` passes, and `/proc/self/maps` contains only the isolated
2.30.7 library. The first current-base DSV4 arm was interrupted before
measurement when four unrelated GPU occupier jobs began using every GPU; no
timing from that attempt is accepted.

Reproduction:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
PYTHONPATH=$PWD \
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/benchmark_shared_ep.py \
  --model /path/to/model \
  --backend shared_ep \
  --world-size 4 \
  --input-len 128 \
  --output-len 128 \
  --warmup 3 \
  --repeats 5 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8
```

Use `--backend deepep_low_latency` for the GLM-5.2 baseline and `--backend deepep_v2` for the DeepSeek-V4-Flash baseline. GLM-5.2 does not require `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`.

Greedy-ID agreement is a bounded correctness gate, not a full accuracy
evaluation. Full model accuracy evaluation and the current-base DSV4 pair
remain WIP.

## Bounded optimization decisions

The PR keeps one fixed owner-reserved input layout and one local-HBM
gather. Eliminating that final input materialization requires a separate
owner-aware indexed NVFP4 W1 kernel that pipelines peer loads with tensor-core
work. That larger kernel project is intentionally not hidden inside this first
SharedEP PR.

## Dependencies

This change depends on vLLM PR #50009 for the generic rank-major CUDA VMM
peer-view abstraction and FlashInfer PR
https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4268 for CuTeDSL NVFP4 direct
owner output. Both dependencies must land or be pinned before SharedEP NVFP4
can be enabled.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to port, implement, test, benchmark, and prepare this change. The submitting human must review every changed line, rerun or independently accept the validation, and be able to explain and defend the VMM lifetime, owner layout, GPU epoch protocol, native kernel selection, and fail-closed admission behavior before publication.

title: GSM8K accuracy regression: nightly (0.26.1rc1.dev77) drops ~5% vs latest (0.26.0) on GLM-5.2-FP8 P/D
body:
## Summary

GSM8K accuracy drops ~5 percentage points when moving from `vllm/vllm-openai:latest` (v0.26.0) to `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` on the same cluster, same config, same benchmark command.

## GSM8K Results

### Setup

- **Benchmark**: [GSM8K](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/gsm8k) (grade school math, 1319 test examples)
- **Evaluator**: `lm_eval` v0.4.x, `local-chat-completions` model type
- **Few-shot**: 5-shot (`fewshot_as_multiturn=True`, default for chat completions)
- **Thinking**: Disabled (`enable_thinking: false` via `chat_template_kwargs`)
- **Sampling**: Greedy (`temperature=0.0`, `do_sample=False`)
- **Stop tokens**: `['Question:', '</s>', '<|im_end|>']`
- **Tokenizer**: HuggingFace backend

### Raw results

**`vllm/vllm-openai:latest`** (v0.26.0, commit [`ffd46bfab`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ffd46bfab2128bb84146050e98b51a617c6575ab)):

```
|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr|
|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9447|±  |0.0063|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9386|±  |0.0066|
```

Tested across concurrency 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384 — all consistently ~94.5%.

**`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`** (0.26.1rc1.dev77, commit [`6f91edf96`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/6f91edf96d3f3272945809c04702380053bff4de)):

```
|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr|
|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.8931|±  |0.0085|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.8855|±  |0.0088|
```

At 512 concurrency. 377 commits between the two versions.

### Regression summary

| Metric | latest (0.26.0) | nightly (0.26.1rc1.dev77) | Delta |
|--------|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| flexible-extract | 94.47% ± 0.63 | 89.31% ± 0.85 | **−5.16%** |
| strict-match | 93.86% ± 0.66 | 88.55% ± 0.88 | **−5.31%** |

### Null content warnings

The nightly run produced 3 instances of this warning (not seen on `latest`):

```
WARNING  [models.api_models:546] API returned null content. Content filled with
`LMEVAL_MODEL_NONE_ANSWER_PLACEHOLDER = `. Check reasoning_content field or generation limits.
```

These empty completions count as incorrect answers and partially contribute to the score drop.

### Benchmark command

```bash
lm_eval \
  --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args "model=zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8,base_url=http://localhost:8081/v1/chat/completions,tokenizer_backend=huggingface,num_concurrent=512,timeout=120" \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --gen_kwargs '{"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false}}'
```

Accessed via `kubectl port-forward svc/llm-d-inference-gateway-istio 8081:80`.

## Hardware & Topology

- **GPU**: 8× NVIDIA H100 SXM per node
- **Prefill**: 1 replica × 4 nodes (32 GPUs total, expert-parallel across nodes)
- **Decode**: 1 replica × 4 nodes (32 GPUs total, expert-parallel across nodes)
- **Orchestration**: LeaderWorkerSet (LWS) on Kubernetes, P/D disaggregation with NixlConnector

## Prefill vllm serve command

```bash
vllm serve \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 \
  --port 8000 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --disable-access-log-for-endpoints=/health,/metrics \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb \
  --data-parallel-supervisor-port=8208 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 32 \
  --data-parallel-size-local 8 \
  --data-parallel-address ${LWS_LEADER_ADDRESS} \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port 5555 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \
  --data-parallel-start-rank $START_RANK \
  --kv_transfer_config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector",
                          "kv_role":"kv_both",
                          "kv_load_failure_policy":"fail",
                          "kv_connector_extra_config":{
                              "connectors":[
                              {"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"},
                              {"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
                               "kv_connector_extra_config":{
                                 "spec_name":"TieringOffloadingSpec",
                                 "cpu_bytes_to_use":107374182400,
                                 "eviction_policy":"lru"
                            }}]
                            }}' \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput
```

### Prefill environment variables

```

ENABLE_KV_OFFLOADING=1
KV_OFFLOAD_CPU_BYTES=107374182400
ENABLE_DSPARK=0
VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=1
VLLM_RANDOMIZE_DP_DUMMY_INPUTS=1
DP_SIZE_LOCAL=8

VLLM_SKIP_P2P_CHECK=1
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1
NVIDIA_GDRCOPY=enabled
NVSHMEM_REMOTE_TRANSPORT=ibgda
NVSHMEM_IB_ENABLE_IBGDA=true
VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS=1
VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=120
VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=INFO
PYTHONHASHSEED=0
VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1
```

## Decode vllm serve command

```bash
# MAX_TOKENS = MAX_TOKENS_PER_NODE(32) * LWS_GROUP_SIZE(4) = 128
# NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH = (128 + 1) * 2 = 258

vllm serve \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 \
  --port 8200 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --disable-access-log-for-endpoints=/health,/metrics \
  --data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb \
  --data-parallel-supervisor-port=8208 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 128 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --data-parallel-size 32 \
  --data-parallel-size-local 8 \
  --data-parallel-address ${LWS_LEADER_ADDRESS} \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port 5555 \
  --data-parallel-start-rank $START_RANK \
  --kv_transfer_config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector",
                          "kv_role":"kv_both",
                          "kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}' \
  --all2all-backend deepep_low_latency \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

### Decode environment variables

```
HF_HOME=/mnt/hf-cache
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
ENABLE_DSPARK=0
VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=1
MAX_TOKENS_PER_NODE=32
DP_SIZE_LOCAL=8
TP_SIZE=1
TRITON_LIBCUDA_PATH=/usr/lib64
VLLM_SKIP_P2P_CHECK=1
VLLM_RANDOMIZE_DP_DUMMY_INPUTS=1
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1
NVIDIA_GDRCOPY=enabled
NVSHMEM_REMOTE_TRANSPORT=ibgda
NVSHMEM_IB_ENABLE_IBGDA=true
VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS=1
VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=120
VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=INFO
```

### Decode sidecar (routing-proxy)

```
ghcr.io/llm-d/llm-d-router-disagg-sidecar:v0.9.0
  --port=8000
  --vllm-port=8200
  --data-parallel-size=8
  --kv-connector=nixlv2
  --zap-log-level=1
  --secure-proxy=false
  --enable-prefiller-sampling
```

## Notes

- The **only** change between the two runs was the image tag (`latest` → `nightly`). All YAMLs, env vars, hardware, namespace, and benchmark command were identical.
- `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS=1` was enabled — no NaN logit warnings appeared in either run, so this is not a NaN issue.
- Model: [zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8) — MoE with 256 experts, uses FlashMLA + DeepEP.

title: [RFC]: Lookahead-aware prefix-cache hashing for EAGLE-style draft models
body:
### Motivation.

vLLM groups speculative methods that consume target-model hidden states under `SpeculativeConfig.use_eagle()`. For prefix-cache lookup, all of these EAGLE-style draft methods conservatively drop the last matched unit and recompute it.

This behavior is necessary with the current cache key. The reusable draft cache at a boundary depends on the finalized target token immediately following that boundary. The dependency is easiest to see in the autoregressive EAGLE/MTP input shift. For target tokens

```text
x0 x1 x2 x3 | x4
```

the draft inputs corresponding to target positions `0..3` contain the shifted token IDs

```text
x1 x2 x3 x4
```

as well as target-derived hidden states at positions `0..3`. A normal prefix-cache key for the first four-token block only proves equality of `x0..x3`. It does not prove equality of `x4`, even though `x4` is part of the draft input that produces the final cache entry at that boundary.

For example, both of these requests have the same current block hash:

```text
request A: a b c d | e
request B: a b c d | f
```

However, their draft input at the boundary is different (`e` versus `f`). Therefore, reusing the final matched draft block based only on the current block tokens would be unsafe. The current last-block drop makes the reuse safe by recomputing the boundary.

The cost is significant for hybrid full-attention + Mamba/GDN models. Their aligned cache unit can contain hundreds or thousands of tokens, so a one-unit drop can erase a large part of the prefix-cache benefit. This behavior is reported in:

- <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/38182>
- <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44858>

One Qwen3.6 report on vLLM 0.20.1 measured the hit rate dropping from 87.3% to 69.9%, with 1,056 fewer hit tokens per request—approximately one 1,072-token aligned block: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/38182#issuecomment-4498973050>. This is historical evidence from vLLM 0.20.1. Current `main` includes partial prefix-hit changes, so the remaining recomputation cost—including the Mamba align-mode backoff—must be measured again.

This RFC proposes making the boundary dependency part of the cache key. If the cache key proves that the token immediately following a block is also equal, then the target-derived state and boundary-token inputs used by the EAGLE-style drafter are equal. The final matched block can then be reused without the conservative drop.

The lookahead token in this proposal is the finalized prompt/target token immediately following a hash boundary. It is not one of the `K` unverified draft tokens. vLLM currently applies the same final-match drop policy to every `use_eagle()` method. This RFC proposes one finalized boundary token as the shared hash dependency, independently of `num_speculative_tokens`. The one-token contract must be validated for each current implementation—`eagle`, `eagle3`, `mtp`, `dflash`, and `dspark`—before its pop is disabled.

#### Goals

- Safely retain the final matched prefix-cache unit when its EAGLE-style draft boundary input is proven to match.
- Avoid the EAGLE-style last-block drop for colocated serving.
- Avoid the corresponding one-block Mamba align-mode backoff.
- Preserve the current conservative behavior when the next token is unknown or different.
- Build on the prefix-match and hybrid-cache behavior already present on current `main`.

#### Non-goals

- P/D disaggregated serving or any external KV connector.
- KV-cache event consumers.
- Speculative decoding methods for which `use_eagle()` is false.
- Resumable/streaming-input requests whose finalized tail can be replaced.
- Changing Mamba state checkpointing or retention policy.
- Fixing every correctness issue tracked in <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43559>. This proposal is an efficiency optimization with an explicit cache-key safety condition.

### Proposed Change.

#### 1. Include one following token in each EAGLE-style block hash

Let the prefix-match unit be `B`, and let block `i` cover the half-open token range `[s, e)`, where:

```text
s = i * B
e = (i + 1) * B
```

The current chained block hash is conceptually:

```text
H_i = hash(
    H_(i-1),
    token_ids[s:e],
    extra_keys[s:e],
)
```

For colocated EAGLE-style draft models, compute:

```text
H_i_eagle = hash(
    H_(i-1)_eagle,
    token_ids[s:e+1],
    extra_keys[s:e+1],
)
```

`token_ids[e]` is the lookahead token. The overlap is intentional:

- it is the lookahead token of block `i`;
- it is also the first regular token of block `i + 1`.

Existing cache salt, LoRA identity, and multimodal extra-key semantics remain part of the hash chain. If a multimodal placeholder starts at the lookahead position, its identity is included in both the preceding block's lookahead proof and the following block's regular content.

#### 2. Delay publishing a block until its lookahead token is known

A full block is not hash-ready until `B + 1` relevant tokens are available. Therefore:

- if a request ends exactly on a hash boundary, its final block remains pending;
- after the target model produces and finalizes the next token, the pending hash can be computed;
- the block becomes publishable only after the draft-cache entry at position `e - 1` has been materialized or overwritten from target-derived states together with the finalized `token_ids[e]`;
- cache managers must never publish a full or partial cache entry beyond the number of available request block hashes.

Observing `token_ids[e]` in the request is necessary but not sufficient. The scheduler/model-runner ordering must guarantee that the corresponding draft-cache write has completed before the cache manager registers the block.

This does not make the no-lookahead case worse. Today the final block may match and then be dropped. With the proposed key, that block is not considered a hit until its boundary dependency is known.

#### 3. Use a successful lookahead-aware match as proof that no pop is needed

For the new mode, a hit on `H_i_eagle` proves:

1. the target token prefix through the block is the same;
2. the target-derived hidden, auxiliary, or context states used by the drafter for the block are therefore the same;
3. the finalized boundary token used by the drafter is also the same, because `token_ids[e]` is part of the hash;
4. the cached boundary entry was published only after the corresponding draft-cache write completed.

The scheduler and KV-cache coordinator can consequently skip the EAGLE-style last-block drop for these hashes.

The expected behavior is:

| Incoming request state | Final lookahead hash | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The following token is not known | Not available | Do not reuse the final block |
| The following token is known and equal | Matches | Reuse the final block without a pop |
| The following token is known and different | Does not match | Fall back to the longest earlier cache hit |

For dense/full-attention cache groups, a next-token mismatch naturally loses the final match unit. For hybrid sparse-retention groups, the reconciled result is the longest earlier prefix jointly available across all cache groups; this proposal does not guarantee that every Mamba retention policy has an earlier checkpoint exactly one unit back.

#### 4. Remove the corresponding Mamba align-mode backoff

The current Mamba align scheduler backs `last_cache_position` off by one aligned block when EAGLE-style prefix lookup drops the final full-attention block. In lookahead-aware EAGLE mode, the full-attention drop is disabled, so the matching Mamba backoff should also be disabled.

This does not change how Mamba states are materialized or retained. It only removes the scheduler backoff that existed to stay consistent with the speculative-decoding cache pop.

#### 5. Enable the mode for every colocated EAGLE-style drafter

The first version should be selected only when all of the following are true:

```text
prefix caching is enabled
AND speculative_config.use_eagle() is true
AND no kv_transfer_config is present
AND KV-cache events are disabled
```

At the time of writing, `use_eagle()` covers `eagle`, `eagle3`, `mtp`, `dflash`, and `dspark`. The implementation should use the capability predicate rather than duplicate this method list. All five methods are in the target scope, but the no-pop path should be enabled for each implementation only after its one-token dependency and cache-publication ordering have been validated.

The speculative configuration is immutable for an EngineCore, so every request using a local prefix cache follows one consistent hash mode. No user-facing flag is required for the initial implementation, although an explicit cache-key mode is listed as an open design question below.

The absence of `kv_transfer_config` is intentionally a conservative gate. It excludes both P/D disaggregation and other external KV connector/offload cases until their transfer contracts are considered.

Resumable/streaming-input requests should remain on the current behavior for the first version. Their tail token may be replaced, so safely enabling this mode would require hash invalidation or delayed publication rules for mutable tails.

### Why P/D Disaggregation Is Out of Scope

P/D introduces more than a configuration check:

- P and D may learn or consume the boundary token at different times.
- Both sides must agree on the cache-key mode.
- Transferred block metadata must identify whether a hash includes a lookahead dependency.
- Remote block trimming must distinguish a cached prefix at the front from an extra lookahead allocation at the back.
- Cache events and external stores may need a versioned key/payload contract.

Issue <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43996> demonstrates a concrete failure caused by P and D having different lookahead/block-allocation behavior. For that reason, this RFC proposes a colocated-only first phase. P/D support should be a follow-up design after role negotiation, transfer ranges, and key semantics are explicit.

### Compatibility and Safety

#### Cache-key isolation

Local block hashes are process-lifetime data. A colocated EngineCore does not mix normal and lookahead-aware EAGLE hashes. External connectors and KV events are excluded, so the first version does not require a cross-process migration or compatibility protocol.

#### Hash collisions

The proposal keeps the configured hash function and its existing collision assumptions. It only adds one token and the corresponding existing extra keys to the hashed payload.

#### Hashing overhead

The additional input is one overlapping token per hash unit. The expected CPU hashing overhead is approximately proportional to `1 / B` of token payload processing and should be negligible compared with avoiding model recomputation. This still needs to be measured.

#### Correctness invariant

A cache block may be reused without the speculative-decoding pop only if the hash key proves equality of every target-derived and boundary-token input needed to construct the reusable draft-model cache entries in that block, and the corresponding draft-cache write is known to have completed before the block is published.

If this invariant cannot be established for a model or speculative method, the existing pop remains the fallback.

### Implementation Outline

A prototype on current `main` uses the following structure:

1. Extend the request block hasher with a configurable lookahead-token count.
2. Select one lookahead token for every local `use_eagle()` prefix-cache path.
3. Compute hashes only for blocks whose lookahead token is available.
4. Ensure the target-derived boundary draft-cache write completes before its hash-ready block is published.
5. Cap cache publication at hash-ready boundaries.
6. Disable speculative last-block popping in the coordinator for this mode.
7. Keep EAGLE-style scheduling behavior, lookahead-slot allocation, and draft input handling unchanged.
8. Disable the Mamba align-mode one-block backoff for this mode.
9. Keep the old behavior for non-EAGLE speculative methods, KV connectors, KV events, and resumable requests.

The prototype does not add a new public CLI option.

### Test and Evaluation Plan

#### Unit tests

- Text block hashing includes exactly one following token.
- The final exact-boundary block stays pending until the following token is appended.
- A matching following token reuses the final block without a pop.
- A different following token falls back to an earlier hash boundary.
- Multimodal extra keys include a lookahead placeholder correctly.
- Cache publication waits for the target-derived boundary draft-cache write.
- Hybrid full-attention + Mamba align mode reuses the same exact prefix length across groups.
- Configuration tests verify that `eagle`, `eagle3`, `mtp`, `dflash`, and `dspark` enable the mode, while P/D, other KV connectors, KV events, non-EAGLE speculative methods, non-speculative serving, and resumable requests do not.

The current local prototype passes the relevant CPU prefix-cache, partial-hit, hashing, and streaming scheduler tests.

#### End-to-end correctness

Before opening the implementation PR, run deterministic output comparisons with prefix caching enabled/disabled and with the optimization enabled/disabled:

- Qwen3.5 or Qwen3.6 hybrid full-attention + GDN/Mamba, `mamba_cache_mode=align`;
- EAGLE/EAGLE3 and MTP, with `num_speculative_tokens` equal to 1 and greater than 1;
- DFlash and DSpark on supported models/configurations;
- identical continuation, changed boundary token, and no-known-lookahead cases;
- A -> B -> A cache perturbation;
- multi-turn tool-use and long-context recall workloads;
- chunked prefill and supported async-scheduling configurations.

Prefix caching must remain behavior-preserving. Any deterministic output divergence is a release blocker.

#### Performance

Measure:

- cached-token count at each request;
- number of tokens recomputed after a cache hit;
- TTFT and prefill latency;
- end-to-end throughput;
- draft acceptance length/rate;
- CPU block-hashing time.

The expected result is to recover one speculative drop unit when the boundary token matches, with no hit-rate regression when it does not. On hybrid models, avoiding one drop may also avoid a much larger aligned Mamba recomputation.

GPU/model evaluation results will be added before the implementation PR is submitted.

### Alternatives Considered

#### Keep the current unconditional drop

This is conservative and simple, but it permanently sacrifices one match unit. The cost is especially visible when hybrid alignment makes that unit large.

#### Skip the drop based on prefill/decode phase

<https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44986> proposes skipping the drop during prefill because draft tokens are generated during decode. That is a smaller change and addresses the same performance symptom.

This RFC uses a different safety condition: it makes the cache key prove equality of the EAGLE-style boundary input. The decision to retain the block is content-based rather than phase-based. This distinction is useful when a cache entry was produced by an earlier request and is later consumed during a new request's prefill.

The RFC requests maintainer feedback on whether the phase-based rule is sufficient for every EAGLE-style cache lifecycle, or whether the stronger key invariant is preferable.

#### Drop or rewind a Mamba state correctly

The following work focuses on correctness when hybrid cache groups disagree or when Mamba must honor the speculative boundary:

- <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43650>
- <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45614>
- <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46281>
- <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48375>

Those approaches preserve or repair the backoff. This proposal is materially different: it strengthens the cache key so the backoff can be skipped when the boundary input actually matches. The approaches can remain complementary as a safe fallback.

#### Do not cache the speculative boundary block

Avoiding publication of the boundary block is safe, but it gives up the same reuse opportunity. Delaying publication until the finalized lookahead token is known retains safety while allowing later continuations to reuse it.

#### Cache additional target hidden states

Persisting the target hidden states required by the drafter could avoid recomputation, but it adds a separate cache payload and lifecycle. Encoding the shifted-token dependency in the existing key is smaller and keeps the current KV/state storage model.

### Related Work and Non-Duplication

- Hybrid prefix caching tracking: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26201>
- Original EAGLE prefix-caching integration and final-block drop: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/17137>
- Earlier discussion of approximate EAGLE/MTP draft KV and hidden states: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/14649>
- Partial cache hits for hybrid models: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45702> and <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46384>
- MTP prefix-cache hit-rate regression: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/38182>
- Prefill-phase pop optimization: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44858> and <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44986>
- Hybrid MTP prefix-cache correctness tracking: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43559>
- P/D lookahead allocation and trimming: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43996>

The open work above establishes both the correctness problem and the cost of the conservative drop. The proposed contribution is not another unconditional “skip pop” patch and not another Mamba rewind patch. Its distinct contribution is a cache-key contract that includes the finalized boundary token, allowing the cache hit itself to prove that the final EAGLE-style draft block is reusable. Although several motivating reports use MTP models, the cache contract and proposed scope cover every method represented by `use_eagle()`.

### Open Questions

1. Should this be an internal `use_eagle()` policy, or should vLLM introduce an explicit cache-key/hash mode?
2. Should a discriminator such as `eagle_lookahead_v1` be included in the initial hash payload even though the first version is process-local?
3. Should the `use_eagle()` contract explicitly guarantee one finalized-token boundary dependency, or should each drafter report its required cache-key lookahead count?
4. What method-specific validation should accompany the shared invariant for EAGLE3 auxiliary hidden states and DFlash/DSpark parallel drafting?
5. What metadata and versioning would be required before enabling KV events or external KV connectors?
6. For future P/D support, should P compute/publish the lookahead-aware hash, should D do so after transfer, or should the hash mode be negotiated and carried in transfer metadata?

### Feedback Period.

At least one week.

### CC List.

@ivanium @ZJY0516 @tdoublep @benchislett @njhill

### Any Other Things.

A local prototype and CPU regression tests exist. GPU model evaluation and performance measurements are intentionally required before an implementation PR is submitted.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [ROCm][CI] AITER MLA Kernel Test Coverage Tracker
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
AITER will be the default attention backend for vLLM on ROCm, and its MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention) paths are the critical decode path for models on MI300/MI355 hardware. Today, there are no kernel-level tests validating accuracy, determinism, or `torch.compile` compatibility for these paths meaning regressions can silently corrupt inference output with no CI signal. This issue tracks doing it properly: covering FP8 detection, dense MLA decode, sparse MLA kernels, and backend contract validation.  

## Test Groups

### 1. FP8 Support Detection 

Runtime detection of whether the installed AITER version supports FP8 KV caches.

- [x] Positive detection — FP8 signature present → returns `True`
- [x] Negative detection — FP8 params absent → returns `False`
- [ ] Error handling — 5 exception types all fail closed
- [ ] Caching — `inspect.signature` called exactly once across repeated calls

### 2. Dense MLA Decode Kernel 

The `rocm_aiter_mla_decode_fwd` custom op — the core decode kernel for absorbed MLA on MI300/MI355.

- [ ] Custom op registered and callable in `torch.ops.vllm`
- [ ] Fake-tensor support via `torch.library.opcheck` (for `torch.compile`)
- [ ] Environment gating — `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` × `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA` matrix
- [ ] BF16 decode smoke test — correct shape, dtype, finite, non-zero
- [ ] Accuracy vs PyTorch reference (absorbed MLA formulation)
- [ ] FP8-capable hardware BF16 path verification
- [ ] Bitwise determinism across N runs
- [ ] Parametrized sweep — `nhead ∈ {16, 128}`, `batch ∈ {1, 4, 16}`, `seq ∈ {16, 256}`
- [ ] Unsupported `nhead` raises `RuntimeError` from ASM kernel selector

**Requires MI3xx hardware** for kernel execution tests.
### 3. Sparse MLA Kernels

Sparse MLA selects top-k KV tokens per query for long-context efficiency.

- [ ] `triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index` matches Python reference
- [ ] `fetch_id_to_ragged_triton` packs valid top-k IDs contiguously
- [ ] Sparse forward smoke test — BF16, finite, non-zero output
- [ ] Sparse forward accuracy vs `reference_mla_sparse_prefill`
- [ ] Sparse forward bitwise determinism across N runs

**Triton helpers run on any GPU; forward requires MI3xx.**

---

### 4. MLA Variant Backend Contracts

The `AiterTritonMLABackend` and `ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend` must maintain API contracts that vLLM's attention infrastructure depends on.

- [ ] `AiterTritonMLABackend` — `is_mla()`, impl class, shared dtype/block-size/builder contract with dense
- [ ] `ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend` — `is_mla()`, `is_sparse()`, `accept_output_buffer`
- [ ] Sparse backend — impl/metadata/builder class wiring correct
- [ ] Sparse backend — static dtype, kv_cache_dtype, block-size contracts
- [ ] `get_kv_cache_shape()` returns token-level shape

**No hardware required** — pure class metadata checks.

title: # Bug: `Maximum concurrency` startup log contradicts `/metrics` endpoint due to premature `block_size` resolution
body:
## Bug: Startup log `Maximum concurrency` contradicts `/metrics` `kv_cache_max_concurrency`

### My current environment

```text
vLLM version: 0.26.0
Model: nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 (284B MoE, DeepseekV4ForCausalLM)
Hardware: 2× Blackwell (SM120), 96 GB each
TP=2, EP enabled
KV cache dtype: fp8
KV connector: SimpleCPUOffloadConnector (50 GiB CPU per rank)
Max model len: 262,144
Block size: 256
Prefix caching: enabled
```

### How to reproduce

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 262144 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.936 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":53687091200}}'
```

### The problem

The `Maximum concurrency` value printed in the startup log disagrees with the `kv_cache_max_concurrency` label in the `/metrics` endpoint.

**Startup log:**
```
GPU KV cache size: 302,945 tokens
Maximum concurrency for 262,144 tokens per request: 1.16x
```

**`/metrics` endpoint:**
```
vllm:cache_config_info{
  kv_cache_max_concurrency="0.47086269282041515",
  kv_cache_size_tokens="123433",
  num_gpu_blocks="14835",
  ...
} 1.0
```

| Source | kv_cache_size_tokens | Concurrency |
|---|---|---|
| Startup log | 302,945 | 1.16x |
| `/metrics` | 123,433 | 0.47x |

Both use the same formula (`num_blocks / sum(blocks_per_group)`) but with different inputs — the startup log is computed during `get_kv_cache_configs()` on a per-worker config, while `/metrics` reflects a later config sent via `EngineCoreReadyResponse`. It is unclear which value corresponds to the config the scheduler actually enforces.

### Expected behavior

The two values should agree. Whichever config the scheduler actually runs with should be used for both the startup log and the `/metrics` label.

### Root cause

`get_kv_cache_configs()` in `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` (line ~2197) computes and logs the concurrency **per-worker** using each worker's full `available_memory`:

```python
for kv_cache_config in kv_cache_configs:
    kv_cache_config.num_blocks = min_num_blocks
    ...
    num_tokens, max_concurrency = get_kv_cache_capacity(vllm_config, kv_cache_config)
    logger.info_once("GPU KV cache size: %s tokens", f"{num_tokens:,}")
    logger.info_once("Maximum concurrency for %s tokens per request: %.2fx",
                     f"{max_model_len:,}", max_concurrency)
```

The `EngineCoreReadyResponse` sent to the API server carries a different `KVCacheConfig` with `num_blocks=14835`, which is what `/metrics` exposes. The log message is emitted on the first config and never updated to match the final one.

### Suggested fix

Ensure the startup log and the `/metrics` label are computed from the same `KVCacheConfig` — either log after finalization, or log both values.

title: [Model Runner V2] batch-sharded sample
body:
# Summary
Currently before sampling, the full target logits are materialized, allocating memory of size `O(batch_size * (num_spec_tokens + 1) * vocab_size)`. This PR reduces that per-step memory allocation by a factor of `1/P` during tensor parallelism by sharding the logits and sampler inputs along the batch dimension, and sampling in parallel on a subset of the batch.

Sharding the sampler inputs (`InputBatch`) was straightforward, and is handled by `BatchSharder.shard_sampler_inputs`. Requests are assigned to ranks by partitioning the request state index mapping (using `idx_mapping % tp_size`) in a deterministic way. From there, we derive the new sharded input batch CPU arrays & GPU tensors for the local rank, based on the requests that it "owns".

Sharding the logits along the batch dimension is accomplished by having the model compute logits for only its slice of the vocab size by implementing the `compute_logits_local` method. After that, each rank has a `[num_tokens, vocab_size // P]` slice of the full logits. However, instead of all-gathering to get the full `[num_tokens, vocab_size]`, we instead all-to-all along the batch dimension, so that each rank ends up with `[num_tokens // P, vocab_size]`.

In summary, this PR (1) reduces peak target logits memory from `O(batch_size * (num_spec_tokens + 1) * vocab_size)` => `O(batch_size * (num_spec_tokens + 1) * vocab_size / P)`, and (2) parallelizes the sampling operation, which can be particularly beneficial for TPOT whenever heavy sampling operations (e.g. top-k, top-p, block verification, etc) are performed. No changes had to be made to the `Sampler` or `RejectionSampler` because they work perfectly fine with smaller batch sizes as long as we shard the `InputBatch` properly, which we do.

NOTE: A big motivation for this PR is to enable sharding of the draft logits. The cached draft logits from the speculator forward pass(es) are preallocated in memory for the worst case, with a size of `O(max_num_reqs * num_spec_tokens * vocab_size)`. We can reduce that by a factor of `1/P` as well, but sharded sampling is a prerequisite.
