title: [ROCm] Route sparse-indexer decode top-k through AITER dispatcher
body:
## Purpose

The DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5 sparse attention indexer calls decode top-k on every
decode step. On the ROCm path that call is hardwired to
`torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode` — a HIP radix kernel whose cost grows
~linearly with context width (~15× slower than NVIDIA B200's context-independent
`persistent_topk_kernel`; ~78 calls/step make it the dominant single-kernel gap
at long context).

This routes the call through `aiter.top_k_per_row_decode` instead, which gates a
**context-length-independent FlyDSL kernel** onto the arch/shape window where it
wins and keeps HIP everywhere else. vLLM adds **no gfx950 logic** — all
arch/shape routing and the HIP fallback live in AITER.

- Depends on the AITER decode-top-k dispatcher (ROCm/aiter, follow-up to
  https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4355). Until an aiter exposing
  `top_k_per_row_decode` is installed, this path is a **no-op** and the native
  kernel runs unchanged.
- Ticket: SILOTIGER-699 (epic SILOTIGER-606, GLM-5 MI355X perf uplift).

**What changes** — one file, `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`:

1. `_aiter_top_k_per_row_decode()` — cached resolver returning
   `aiter.top_k_per_row_decode` when importable, else `None`.
2. The decode call site calls the resolved op when present, else falls back to
   the existing `torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode`.

Signatures are positionally identical, so the call is drop-in. Behavior when
aiter is absent or predates the dispatcher: resolver returns `None` → native
`_C` kernel, i.e. a no-op on current deployments.

## Test Plan

Tested on **gfx950 (MI355X)** against the AITER dispatcher branch,
`torch 2.10+rocm7.1`:

- AITER dispatch-gate unit tests (`op_tests/test_topk_decode_dispatch.py`)
- FlyDSL decode GPU correctness (`op_tests/flydsl_tests/test_flydsl_topk_per_row_decode.py`)
- End-to-end through vLLM's resolver (`_aiter_top_k_per_row_decode`) → AITER gate
  on 7 shapes, results compared to `torch.topk`
- Fallback path with aiter absent (resolver returns `None`)
- Kernel + per-step A/B, FlyDSL vs HIP, gate toggled via
  `AITER_DISABLE_FLYDSL_TOPK_DECODE`; each arm proves which kernel ran via an
  opt-in dispatch counter (FlyDSL arm flydsl>0, HIP arm flydsl=0)

## Test Result

**Correctness**
- Dispatch-gate unit tests: 34/34 pass
- FlyDSL decode GPU correctness: 99/99 pass
- vLLM resolver → gate, 7 shapes: in-gate route FlyDSL, out-of-gate
  (rows=2, width<131072, k=512) route HIP, all **set-equal to `torch.topk`**
- Fallback: aiter absent → resolver `None` → native `_C` path unchanged

**Kernel-level A/B** (same op, gate toggled), 200 calls/shape,
`hip/flydsl` ratio (>1 = FlyDSL faster):

| rows | width | FlyDSL µs | HIP µs | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 131072 | 40.7 | 47.0 | 1.16 |
| 8 | 131072 | 40.6 | 52.9 | 1.30 |
| 16 | 131072 | 48.7 | 52.2 | 1.07 |
| 1 | 163840 | 31.2 | 37.3 | 1.20 |
| 4 | 163840 | 41.2 | 50.8 | 1.23 |
| 8 | 163840 | 44.6 | 51.7 | 1.16 |
| 16 | 163840 | 51.9 | 53.6 | 1.03 |

**Per-decode-step** (indexer calls decode top-k ~78×/step), in-gate widths,
ms/step (gate faster = >1×):

| rows | width | gate ms | HIP ms | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 131072 | 2.93 | 3.67 | 1.26× |
| 8 | 131072 | 3.17 | 4.18 | 1.32× |
| 16 | 131072 | 3.95 | 4.10 | 1.04× |
| 1 | 163840 | 2.42 | 2.53 | 1.05× |
| 4 | 163840 | 3.20 | 3.98 | 1.24× |
| 8 | 163840 | 3.42 | 4.04 | 1.18× |
| 16 | 163840 | 4.06 | 4.18 | 1.03× |

FlyDSL faster on all in-gate cells, best in the realistic rows 4–8 band
(1.2–1.32×). Using the ticket's top-k ≈ 12.2% step share, cutting per-step
top-k ~20% projects **~2.4–2.5% TPOT** at width ≥131072 (a kernel-share
projection, not a live serving TPOT — see below).

**Pending (needs the serving cluster):**
- vLLM-side unit test asserting the resolver returns `None` without aiter and the
  callable with it (patchable, no GPU).
- End-to-end serving A/B (GSM8K + long-context TPOT) on GLM-5.2-MXFP4 TP4 at
  ISL 60k/120k, `--max-model-len ≥ 131072`, toggling
  `AITER_DISABLE_FLYDSL_TOPK_DECODE`. Kernel wins convert to TPOT only when top-k
  is a real share of step time (long context); a 1k/8k comparison shows flat and
  must not be read as a regression.

## Not a duplicate

No open vLLM PR wires AITER's top-k into the sparse indexer: `_aiter_ops.py`
registers no `top_k` op and the decode call site still uses
`torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode`. Recent PRs in this file (#49714, #48788,
#44527) are DSV4 bugfixes/perf, none routing decode top-k to AITER.

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; the submitter has reviewed every line and
run the tests above. Commit is DCO signed-off.

title: [Kimi-K3] DCP support
body:
Co-authored-by: @foraxe

## Summary

Follow-up to #50000 adding decode context parallelism for Kimi-K3:

- direct symmetric-memory DCP A2A output/LSE reduction, including empty-KV-shard masking
- DCP support for the fused Kimi-K3 MLA layer
- NVLS-multicast direct query gather and multimem chunked-context KV gather
- direct publication of query shards into the consumer-final buffer, removing the staging-to-final materialization by @foraxe

This replaces #50055.

## Query-buffer lifetime

The direct query gather returns a view of its persistent symmetric buffer. Reuse is ordered by the mandatory post-attention DCP combine:

1. query gather publishes the current epoch and waits for every rank
2. attention consumes the gathered query on the same CUDA stream
3. every combine implementation introduces a cross-rank dependency after attention
4. the next gather cannot execute until all ranks have passed the preceding attention read

DBO microbatches use independent workspace slots.

## Accuracy

`.buildkite/kimi-k3/rack5/gsm8k.yaml`:

| Arm | exact_match | Correct/N | Request errors |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TP8 | 96.21% | 1269/1319 | 0 |
| DCP8 | 96.97% | 1279/1319 | 0 |

## Performance

120k regression workload: 114k shared prefix + 6k suffix, 400 output tokens, Mooncake disabled.

| Arm | Conc | TPOT p50/p90/p99 | HBM use mean/peak |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TP8 | c1 | 13.806/13.831/13.857ms | 4.93%/7.17% |
| DCP8 | c1 | 10.544/10.574/10.597ms | 0.64%/1.10% |
| TP8 | c2 | 16.192/23.591/34.101ms | 9.18%/14.11% |
| DCP8 | c2 | 11.828/19.437/27.562ms | 1.30%/2.37% |

HBM KV capacity per GPU:

- TP8: 1.933M tokens / 25.12 GiB
- DCP8: 19.752M tokens / 34.28 GiB

On 4x GB200 at matched Kimi-K3 geometry, the direct-to-final query path improved query-exchange latency by 10.4%-29.9%. Correctness and changing-input CUDA-graph replay passed.

## Scope and overlap

This PR subsumes the direct symmetric-memory MLA A2A work in #48897 and extends it with Kimi-K3 fused MLA DCP, direct query gather, chunked-context KV gather, and the direct-to-final query optimization.


## CUDA-graph padding follow-up

Commit `76b2e9d45e` makes empty-shard LSE masking tolerate CUDA-graph padding rows.

Validation:
- `tests/distributed/test_dcp_a2a.py::TestLSEWeightedCombine::test_ag_rs_masks_empty_shard_and_padded_lse`: 1 passed on GB300.
- DCP2 partial-prefix reuse versus TP2 on 2x GB300, with direct A2A, query gather, and KV gather selected: 1 passed; 256 cached tokens, exact generated-token match, finite logprobs, and drift <= 1e-2.
- Pre-commit hooks on both changed files: passed.
- An exploratory full-file GB300 run had 25 passes and 7 return-LSE dtype assertion failures (float32 actual versus fp16/bf16 expected); those cases pass no masking metadata and do not execute this change.

AI assistance was used to diagnose, implement, and validate this follow-up fix.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Launch KV block zeroing on a 3-D grid
body:
# [Bugfix][ROCm] Launch the KV block zeroing kernel on a 3-D grid

## Purpose
`_zero_kv_blocks_kernel` flattens `(block, segment, chunk)` into a single grid dimension. On AMD that dimension is capped (limit is `(2^32 - 1) / WG size`), so on models with many segments and large pages the launch is rejected, and every worker dies on the first request.

It leads to the following error when running DSV4 on MI355, TP8:
```
gpu_model_runner.py:1222  _zero_block_ids(scheduler_output.new_block_ids_to_zero)
worker/utils.py:199       _zero_kv_blocks_kernel[grid](...)
RuntimeError: Triton Error [HIP]:  Code: 1, Messsage: invalid argument
```
HIP code 1 is `hipErrorInvalidValue`.

This PR changes the flattened 1d grid to explicit 3d grid to resolve this problem.

## Test Plan

`test_many_blocks_exceed_flat_grid_limit` in `tests/v1/worker/test_kv_block_zeroer.py`.

This test designed to create a grid that leads to a failure in old version but passes with 3d grid.

## Test Result

Added tests pass and server starts and processes requests successfully and after the fix.

title: [RFC]: Per-request scheduling for MLA chunked context (prefill)
body:
## Motivation

MLA prefill with existing context gathers paged latent KV into a fixed workspace, up-projects it, attends, and merges the partial into the running output. The schedule is **batch-column shaped** — the workspace is divided evenly across all prefills, and every iteration processes the same context window of **every** prefill (`build_mla_chunked_context_metadata()`, `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/[mla_attention.py](https://github.com/home/LucasWilkinson/.t3/worktrees/vllm/t3code-da61773b/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py)`):

```python
max_context_chunk = workspace_size // num_prefills_with_context   # even split
max_context_chunk = round_down(max_context_chunk, block_size)     # gather kernel requirement
assert max_context_chunk > 0
num_chunks        = cdiv(max_context_len, max_context_chunk)      # longest request drives it
```

That bought two nice properties: workspace size is bounded and predictable, and since every chunk spans the whole prefill batch, the context partial is shaped exactly like the new-token (suffix) partial, so merging is one whole-batch `merge_attn_states` with no index bookkeeping. It's now causing problems on two fronts.

**1. Poor scheduling on heterogeneous batches.** With a 64k workspace and contexts `[60k, 1k × 7]`, `mcc = 8k` and we run 8 iterations; iterations 2–8 gather only the long request's rows — ~12% workspace utilization per launch. Every iteration also runs attention over *all* prefill queries, merges over *all* prefill tokens, and pays a `mask_empty_context` Triton kernel to neutralize requests whose context is already exhausted. And `mcc = W / num_prefills` means chunks shrink as the batch grows.

**2. Workspace memory is coupled to `max_num_seqs × block_size`.** Since every prefill needs its own slice, `determine_chunked_prefill_workspace_size()` floors the workspace at `max_num_seqs * block_size`, overriding the deliberate 64k cap (documented in-code as ≈144 MB workspace + ≈3 GB transient up-projected context). This is being hit on **Kimi K3** (reported by @wzhao18): HMA raises the attention block size to cover the KDA state page size, giving `block_size = 1536` @ TP8 and ~11000 @ DEP16 — at DEP16 with `max_num_seqs=32` the floor demands ~352k rows, **5.5× the cap**, forcing users to hand-tune `max_num_seqs` down for reasons unrelated to the scheduler. 

## Proposed Change.

Replace the `[num_chunks × num_prefills]` grid with a **flat list of per-request chunks**, matching the indexer / sparse-MLA shape:

```python
@dataclass
class ContextChunk:
    req_start, req_end: int        # prefill-local request range
    token_start, token_end: int    # query tokens of those requests
    starts, seq_lens: Tensor       # per-request context offset / rows this chunk
    cu_seq_lens, token_to_seq, cu_seqlens_q: Tensor
    is_continuation: bool          # first request was already partially processed
    # + DCP: per-rank local starts / padded lens
```

**Policy:** greedily pack whole requests until the workspace is full; split a request only when it doesn't fit.

- **Phase 1** — split only when a request alone exceeds the workspace (indexer-identical). A request is then either wholly inside one chunk (single init write, no merge) or alone across N sub-chunks (init + N−1 merges over just its own tokens).
- **Phase 2** — also split the tail request to fill the workspace, giving optimal chunk count `ceil(Σ context / W)`. Chunks are emitted in request order, so only a chunk's *first* request can be a continuation: one request-slice merge plus one bulk init.

The cost is the index bookkeeping, chunks no longer align with the suffix partial so context writes/merges become per-token-slice. In exchange:

- Full workspace per launch regardless of batch composition; attention/up-projection/merge charged only to the chunk's requests. Merge work drops from `num_chunks × all_prefill_tokens` to `Σ chunk tokens`.
- `has_empty_context` / `mask_empty_context` deleted — empty spans can't occur by construction.
- **Workspace floor drops from `max_num_seqs × block_size` to one page**, making workspace memory independent of `max_num_seqs` (~5.5× less for Kimi K3 @ DEP16). Huge pages degrade gracefully: a chunk just covers fewer requests instead of asserting.
- Workspace stays independent of `max_model_len`; a long request's context is still processed in workspace-sized pieces.

### Feedback Period.

_No response_

### CC List.

_No response_

### Any Other Things.

_No response_

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: (feat): optionally disable lookup on PD decode
body:
The original implementation is done by @ivanium .

## Summary
This PR introduces the `enable_lookup` flag for `MooncakeStoreConnector`, to be added in `kv_connector_extra_config` with `kv_consumer` role. This flag is for a PD setup where decode instance doesn't read from or write to the Mooncake, and only contributes its segment for extending prefill worker KV cache capacity. e.g.
```
--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"},{"kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"enable_cross_layers_blocks":false,"enable_lookup":false}}]}}'
```
- This avoid the potential overhead brought by the useless lookup, e.g. DSV4
- This also allows enabling a naive heterogeneous TP Mooncake PD setup for not yet compatible models, e.g. K3

## Test
### Unit

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py
22 passed
```

New `test_disabled_lookup_reports_no_hit_without_querying_client`, 21 are pre-existing.

### End to end

Kimi-K3 1P1D on 6x GB300 nodes / 24 GPUs: prefill TP8 across 2 nodes (prefix caching on,
mamba align mode, `MultiConnector` = Nixl + MooncakeStore), decode DEP16 across 4
nodes (`--no-enable-prefix-caching`, store child as in the Summary above). Mooncake 
 `enable_lookup: false`, `global_segment_size: 100GB` per rank.

With the flag, all 16 decode ranks start and report the mode, once each:

```
[worker.py:1279] Mooncake store in capacity-only mode: segment mounted
(global_segment_size=107374182400), KV transfer disabled.
```

The master shows all 24 ranks joining the pool. Before traffic, then at peak:

```
Mem Storage: 0 B / 2.34 TB (0.0%)      | Keys: 0     | Clients: 24
Mem Storage: 2.11 TB / 2.34 TB (90.0%) | Keys: 90357 | Clients: 24
```

The pool is 24 x ~97.5 GB usable, of which prefill owns only 8 x ~97.5 GB = 0.78 TB, so at
least ~1.3 TB of prefill's offloaded KV is resident in decode-owned segments. Decode itself
issues no put/get.

AA-LCR (100 long-context samples, concurrency 8) was run twice back to back against
the same deployment: once against an empty store, then again with the first run's blocks resident.

| | cold store | warm store |
|---|---|---|
| score (llm_judge) | 0.78 | 0.78 |
| samples / request errors | 100 / **0** | 100 / **0** |
| eval duration | 343.85 s | 307.57 s |
| master `Get` | `Item=0.00` for the whole run | up to 906 items/s |
| prefill external prefix cache hit | 6.7% peak | 44.2% peak |

The score is unchanged, validated as e2e correctness. Note the store was already ~86% full
when the warm run started (evictions 1 -> 3 during it), so some cold-run blocks were dropped
before they could be re-read. 

### AI
Claude code was used.

title: [Feature]: Allow an explicit expert override of the startup KV capacity check
body:
### Motivation

`_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` currently raises unconditionally when the configured maximum sequence length is calculated to require more memory than the profiled KV-cache budget.

That is the right default for supported model/backend combinations. It becomes hard to work with, however, while validating a downstream or custom hybrid attention backend whose KV-cache specs or grouping may not yet match the generic admission estimate. The engine exits before the backend can build its actual cache layout, so operators cannot deliberately accept the OOM risk and observe the resulting capacity.

This came up while running DeepSeek V4 Flash through Lvllmds4 with CPU MoE offload on a single 96 GiB GPU. One configuration reported:

```text
max seq len: 128000
calculated KV requirement: 14.17 GiB
available KV cache memory: 2.59 GiB
estimated maximum model length: 6148
```

The downstream work is not evidence that current vLLM lacks DeepSeek V4 accounting: the DeepSeek V4 `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` special case is already present from #40860. The request here is specifically about providing a controlled path for experimental/downstream backends when maintainers or operators need to validate the calculation itself.

### Proposed behavior

Would vLLM accept an explicit expert-only opt-in that changes this one startup failure into the existing detailed warning and continues?

For example, a CLI option or environment variable with these properties:

- off by default;
- prints the full calculated required/available/estimated-capacity diagnostic;
- clearly warns that startup or a later request may OOM;
- affects only the maximum-sequence-length KV admission check;
- does not suppress the `available_memory <= 0` failure;
- does not change scheduler admission policy.

A downstream implementation is available for discussion in guqiong96/Lvllmds4#33. It adds `VLLM_ALLOW_INSUFFICIENT_KV_CACHE=1`, preserves the default hard error, and includes a focused test.

### Alternatives considered

`--num-gpu-blocks-override` is useful when the desired block count is already known, but it requires selecting a concrete allocation up front. It does not provide a simple “use the profiled remainder, warn, and continue” path while debugging a model/backend capacity estimate.

Correcting the backend's KV-cache specs and capacity calculation remains the proper final fix whenever the estimate is wrong. This escape hatch would only make that investigation possible without maintaining a local patch to the generic startup check.

title: [Bug]: Inkling tool call leaks as content in multi-turn streaming (turn-initial tool call, tool_calls empty)
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>vLLM version</summary>

- vLLM `0.26.1rc1.dev30+g5773c4e60` (nightly, 2026-07-28)
- Model: `thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4` (also reproduces conceptually on any Inkling)
- Flags: `--tokenizer-mode inkling --reasoning-parser inkling --tool-call-parser inkling --enable-auto-tool-choice`
- The bug is in the streaming parser path, so it should be hardware-independent.

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Summary:** In **streaming** mode, when an assistant turn in a **multi-turn** conversation begins *directly* with a tool call (no leading text), the Inkling tool-call block leaks into `delta.content` as raw markers and `tool_calls` stays empty:

```
<|content_invoke_tool_json|>{"name":"search_notes","args":{"query":"..."}}<|end_message|>
```

**Deterministic trigger matrix** (same model, same request otherwise):

| scenario | result |
| --- | --- |
| single-turn, streaming | ✅ tool_calls parsed |
| multi-turn, **non**-streaming | ✅ tool_calls parsed |
| **multi-turn + streaming** | ❌ tool block leaks as content, `tool_calls == []` |

It is **independent of `reasoning_effort`** — reproduces at both `none` and `max`, including when the model emits no reasoning at all. (Possibly related to #49865, but that is non-reasoning-mode `<|end_message|>` leakage; this one specifically drops whole tool calls only in the multi-turn streaming path.)

This matters a lot for agent frameworks (e.g. Open WebUI): they stream and are inherently multi-turn (tool → result → next call), so the model frequently opens a turn with a tool call and the call is silently lost.

#### Minimal reproduction

```python
import json, urllib.request

URL = "http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions"
TOOLS = [{"type": "function", "function": {
    "name": "search_notes", "description": "Search the user's notes.",
    "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}}}}}]

# multi-turn: prior assistant tool call + tool result, then a follow-up
messages = [
    {"role": "user", "content": "Search my notes for DSpark."},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": None, "tool_calls": [
        {"id": "c1", "type": "function",
         "function": {"name": "search_notes", "arguments": "{\"query\": \"DSpark\"}"}}]},
    {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "c1", "content": "Found 2 docs."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Now search my notes again for MTP."},
]

def run(stream):
    body = {"model": "thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4", "messages": messages,
            "tools": TOOLS, "tool_choice": "auto",
            "temperature": 1.0, "top_p": 1.0, "max_tokens": 500, "stream": stream}
    req = urllib.request.Request(URL, data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    if not stream:
        d = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))
        m = d["choices"][0]["message"]
        print("non-stream: tool_calls=", [t["function"]["name"] for t in (m.get("tool_calls") or [])],
              "content=", repr(m.get("content")))
        return
    content, names = "", []
    for raw in urllib.request.urlopen(req):
        ln = raw.decode("utf-8", "ignore").strip()
        if not ln.startswith("data:"):
            continue
        data = ln[5:].strip()
        if data == "[DONE]":
            break
        delta = json.loads(data)["choices"][0].get("delta", {})
        if delta.get("content"):
            content += delta["content"]
        for tc in (delta.get("tool_calls") or []):
            if (tc.get("function") or {}).get("name"):
                names.append(tc["function"]["name"])
    print("stream:     tool_calls=", names, "content=", repr(content))

run(stream=False)   # -> tool_calls=['search_notes'] content=None      (correct)
run(stream=True)    # -> tool_calls=[]  content='<|content_invoke_tool_json|>{...}<|end_message|>'  (BUG)
```

#### Expected

Streaming multi-turn should parse the tool call identically to non-streaming: `tool_calls=[search_notes]`, no marker text in `content`.

#### Actual

Streaming returns `tool_calls == []` and the raw `<|content_invoke_tool_json|>{...}<|end_message|>` block as `content`.

#### Root-cause notes

The chat-completion server streams via `DelegatingParser.parse_delta` (`vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py`); the tool-call block leaks through as `DeltaMessage.content`. In the failing case the model's turn starts directly with `<|content_invoke_tool_json|>` (the generation prompt already ends with a primed `<|message_model|>`), and the streaming reasoning→tool handoff drops the content-kind marker that should start the tool block. `InklingParser.inkling_config` already carries a comment about this class of problem ("the reasoning pass can hand the tool pass reconstructed text whose token-id slice no longer contains the content-kind marker that starts the tool block") and sets `token_id_terminals={}` to mitigate it, but the mitigation does not cover the turn-initial tool call in multi-turn streaming. The non-streaming single-pass path (`_single_pass_parse`) receives the full text and parses it correctly, which is why only streaming is affected.

Happy to help test a fix.

title: [Bugfix][Core][Spec Decode] Exclude scheduler padding from draft metrics
body:
## Purpose

Related to #45237.

Uniform speculative batches use trailing `-1` placeholders on the first decode step to preserve the fixed `1 + num_spec_tokens` execution and graph shape. These placeholders must still reach the forward/rejection path, but they are not logical draft proposals. Counting them in speculative-decoding statistics makes P/D disaggregated serving report lower acceptance metrics even when its real drafts behave like colocated serving.

This PR tracks the trailing padding count per request in `SchedulerOutput` and separates the two meanings of draft length:

- scheduler rejection rollback continues to use the physical execution length;
- speculative-decoding statistics use only the valid draft prefix;
- a full-padding frame contributes no logical draft round;
- deferred draft-frame updates preserve other requests' padding metadata and clear stale metadata when a complete frame replaces padding.

The implementation does not inspect token values, so opaque async draft IDs remain valid. It also keeps all public metrics names and formulas unchanged.

## Duplicate check

I searched open issues and PRs for speculative-decode padding, acceptance metrics, and #45237. No open PR addresses scheduler padding in draft statistics.

- #45237 introduced optional first-step padding for P/D decode graph uniformity; this PR preserves that execution behavior and fixes only its statistics.
- #47029 prevents placeholder IDs from reaching embedding lookup; it does not change metric accounting.
- #47464 skips this padding for diffusion models; autoregressive speculative decoding must retain it.
- Open PR #43114 pads variable-length suffix proposals with real EOS IDs inside the proposer, so it has a different source and token semantics.

## Test Plan

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  -k "spec_decoding_stats or spec_decode_padding"
```

The scheduler tests cover prefix-cache and remote-KV first-decode padding, mixed full/partial suffix padding, stale invalid-metadata replacement, and per-position statistics.

## Test Result

- Changed-file pre-commit suite: passed, including Ruff check/format and mypy.
- Targeted scheduler suite: `11 passed, 127 deselected, 14 warnings in 31.66s`.
- The targeted suite used a node-local DeepSeek V4 model redirect with Hugging Face and Transformers offline modes; it did not download a test model.
- `git diff --check github/main..HEAD`: passed.

Two controlled Mix/P/D runs used the same 48 prompts, concurrency 12, greedy sampling, `ignore_eos=true`, and exactly 700 output tokens per request (`num_spec_tokens=7`):

| Run | Deployment | Draft rounds | Accepted / drafted | Acceptance length |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | Mix | 7,483 | 26,218 / 52,381 | 4.5037 |
| 1 | P/D | 7,466 | 26,216 / 52,262 | 4.5114 |
| 2 | Mix | 7,394 | 26,293 / 51,758 | 4.5560 |
| 2 | P/D | 7,330 | 26,340 / 51,310 | 4.5935 |

For all four windows, `drafted == 7 * draft_rounds`: first-step graph padding still executed but no longer entered the public draft counters. The previous P/D-only acceptance-length deficit was not reproduced in either post-fix run.

No documentation update is needed because this corrects internal accounting without changing configuration or the public metrics schema.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance. I reviewed and understand the changed lines, ran the tests and controlled model evaluation above, and am responsible for the contribution.

---

<summary>Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist</summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR.
- [x] The test plan.
- [x] The test results and model evaluation.
- [x] Documentation impact considered.

</details>

title: [ROCm][CI] Add missing test coverage for upstream parity
body:
- Extend ROCm CI coverage for the portable portions of upstream CUDA test groups while keeping NVIDIA-only or unsupported selectors out of the ROCm contract.
- Add MI355 coverage for DSv4-Flash disaggregated DP/EP, DiffusionGemma TP2, and fixed-length FP8 DSpark.
- Extend the existing ROCm compilation suites with AITER-MLA static-FP8 and supported AITER AR+RMS selectors.
- Add Qwen3.5 FP8 evaluation and the fused AMD Kimi K3 decode test to their existing ROCm groups.
- Broaden source dependency filters so shared evaluation helpers, distributed paths, and KDA bindings trigger the relevant jobs.

The partial DSpark job is deliberately labeled `Fixed-length FP8`: it does not claim parity with CUDA's Blackwell MXFP4 indexer and adaptive-verification payload. LM Eval PCP is not added because the native ROCm TP2 x PCP2 candidate reproducibly hit AITER memory-access faults during warmup.

The Medusa/Gemma4/Eagle3 acceptance group and its supporting graph-stream changes were split into #53399.

This PR also adds 13 AMD mirrors for its newly enabled coverage in upstream CI.

### `mi300_1`

- Torch Stable ABI Audit (CPU only)
- LM Eval TurboQuant KV Cache
- LM Eval KV-Offload
- Quantized Fusions
- Kimi K3

### `mi300_2`

- LM Eval KV-Offload Medium
- NixlConnector PD edge case

### `mi300_4`

- LM Eval KV-Offload Large
- Push NixlConnector PP prefill PD accuracy

### `mi355_1`

- Inkling
- Miscellaneous Kernels

### `mi355_2`

- Fusion E2E TP2 Quick (AITER subset)

### `mi355_8`

- DSv4-Flash Disaggregated DP EP

The existing Small Models Distributed mirror gains the DiffusionGemma TP2 payload while retaining FP8/mixed evaluations; the existing Spec Decode mirror adopts the fixed-length FP8 label, dependencies and timeout. Native runtime, AMD hardware allocations and supported selectors follow the AMD jobs; gating follows each upstream parent.

This extends the existing parity PR rather than duplicating Stage G (#50922), whose current 12 new mirror entries cover separate groups. The Stage G patch applies cleanly with these additions.

title: [Bugfix][Gemma4] Keep image bidirectional attention within the sliding window on the V2 model runner
body:
## Purpose

#47217 fixed Gemma4 vision models silently falling back to **causal-only** image
attention whenever a single image's soft-token span exceeded the text sliding
window (e.g. ~1120 soft tokens at `max_soft_tokens=1120` vs
`sliding_window=1024`). The runner was dropping the *entire* bidirectional
`mm_prefix` range for such an image; the fix gated that skip on a model
capability flag, `mm_prefix_clamp_sliding_window`, so models that bound
`mm_prefix` **in-kernel** keep the full range and let the kernel clamp it
per-query — matching HF's `(causal OR blockwise) AND sliding_window` on local
layers.

That fix only landed in the **V1** `GPUModelRunner`. The V2 model runner has its
own copy of the range-building logic in
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py::compute_mm_prefix_ranges`, which still drops
oversized ranges unconditionally:

```python
for r in mm_feature.mm_position.extract_embeds_range():
    if sliding_window is not None and (r[1] - r[0] + 1) > sliding_window:
        continue  # <- no opt-out, unlike V1
```

So the original defect is still reachable today on `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`.
This matters more than it did at the time of #47217, because V2 is no longer
opt-in for these configs — `VllmConfig.use_v2_model_runner` force-enables V2 for
DSpark speculative decoding and for hybrid DFlash drafters, both of which are
used with Gemma4. A user who serves Gemma4 with images and DSpark drafting gets
the degraded mask with no warning and no error.

The kernel-side clamp (`flash_attn.py`, `triton_attn.py`,
`triton_unified_attention.py`) is already shared by both runners and needs no
change — V2 simply never delivers the range to it.

### Fix

- `compute_mm_prefix_ranges` gains a `clamp_in_kernel: bool = False` parameter
  that gates the oversized-range skip, mirroring V1's `_clamps_in_kernel`. The
  default preserves current behavior for every other PrefixLM model.
- `DefaultModelState.build_attn_metadata` reads
  `mm_prefix_clamp_sliding_window` off the model and forwards it, exactly as
  `GPUModelRunner` does.

No behavior change for V1, for non-Gemma4 models, or for images that already fit
within the sliding window.

### Not a duplicate

Checked before opening, per `AGENTS.md`:

```bash
gh search issues "compute_mm_prefix_ranges" --repo vllm-project/vllm --include-prs   # 0 results
gh search issues "mm_prefix_clamp_sliding_window" --repo vllm-project/vllm --include-prs  # only #47217
gh search issues "mm_req_doc_ranges" --repo vllm-project/vllm --include-prs
```

No open issue or PR covers the V2 side. The nearest open PRs touch adjacent code
but not this logic: #47646 (revert of an FA4 mm_prefix *kernel* mask change,
`flash_attn.py` only), #46558 (FlashInfer mm-prefix, `flashinfer.py` only), and
#48907 / #46963 (V2 `attn_utils.py`, but KV-cache reshape). #47217 is the V1 fix
being ported here — its changed-file list contains no V2 file.

## Test Plan

Added four unit tests to `tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py` covering
`compute_mm_prefix_ranges` (previously untested):

- `test_compute_mm_prefix_ranges_skips_oversized_range_by_default` — default
  path still drops an oversized span (regression guard for other models).
- `test_compute_mm_prefix_ranges_keeps_oversized_range_when_clamped_in_kernel` —
  the fix: an oversized span survives when the model clamps in-kernel.
- `test_compute_mm_prefix_ranges_keeps_fitting_range_either_way` — spans within
  the window are unaffected by the flag.
- `test_compute_mm_prefix_ranges_ignores_non_visual_modalities` — audio is
  still skipped.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -q
```

## Test Result

All tests pass with the fix:

```
........                                                            [100%]
8 passed, 14 warnings in 4.15s
```

Reverting only the two source files and re-running (tests kept) fails, confirming
the tests exercise the fixed behavior rather than passing vacuously:

```
FAILED tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py::test_compute_mm_prefix_ranges_keeps_oversized_range_when_clamped_in_kernel
FAILED tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py::test_compute_mm_prefix_ranges_keeps_fitting_range_either_way
FAILED tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py::test_compute_mm_prefix_ranges_ignores_non_visual_modalities
3 failed, 5 passed
```

`ruff format --check` and `ruff check` are clean on all three changed files (the
one remaining `UP038` in `attn_utils.py` is pre-existing on `main`, in
`build_attn_metadata`, and untouched here).

### Model evaluation

This change affects generated output for one narrow case: Gemma4 vision requests
under the V2 model runner where a single image's soft-token span exceeds
`sliding_window` (i.e. `max_soft_tokens=1120` against `sliding_window=1024`; the
default `num_soft_tokens=280` on the released checkpoints is unaffected, so most
serving configurations see no change at all). The expected effect is the one
measured in #47217 — restoring blockwise-bidirectional image attention instead of
causal-only — with V1 as the reference implementation.

I have not re-run the end-to-end vision eval from #47217 under V2; I don't have a
Hopper box free for it right now. Flagging that gap explicitly rather than
implying coverage I don't have. If a reviewer wants those numbers before merging,
say so and I'll get them.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude) was used on this PR: tracing the V1/V2 divergence,
drafting the patch and tests, and drafting this description. The commit carries a
`Co-authored-by:` trailer. I have reviewed every changed line, run the tests and
linters reported above, and can defend the change end-to-end.

## Related

- #47217 — the V1 fix this ports (merged)
- #42175 — introduced Gemma4 FA4 + FlashAttention `mm_prefix` support

title: [ROCm][Performance] Eliminate per-decode allocations and output copy …
body:
### Summary
  
  Reduce decode latency for DeepSeek V4 sparse MLA attention on ROCm by removing redundant memory allocations and a device-to-device copy on every decode forward pass.
  
  ### Changes
  
  **1. Eliminate output tensor allocation + copy** (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`)
  
  Previously, `rocm_sparse_attn_decode()` allocated a fresh bf16 output tensor inside `_rocm_sparse_attn_decode_ragged_triton`, then copied it back to the caller's `output`
  buffer via `output.copy_(attn_out.to(output.dtype))`. Since both tensors are bf16 with identical shape and the Triton kernel uses explicit stride parameters, the caller's
  output buffer is now passed directly to the kernel, removing one `torch.empty_like` + one `.copy_()` per decode step.
  
  **2. Pre-allocate split-K partition buffers** (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/rocm.py` + `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`)
  
  On gfx942/gfx950, the split-K decode path allocates three scratch tensors (`part_m`, `part_l`, `part_acc`) on every forward call. These are now lazily allocated once at
  maximum size (`[max_num_batched_tokens, 16, n_local_heads, ...]`) and sliced per-call, eliminating 3× `torch.empty` per decode step.
  
  ### Backward Compatibility
  
  All new parameters (`out`, `split_k_buffers`) are `Optional` with `None` defaults. When `None`, the functions allocate internally as before. Existing tests and callers are
  unaffected.
  
  ### Testing
  
  - Verified buffer stride semantics and Triton kernel correctness on AMD MI210 (gfx90a)
  - Existing unit tests (`test_sparse_attn_decode_ragged_kernel`, `test_sparse_attn_decode_split_k_kernel`) pass unchanged (new parameters are optional)
  
  ### Expected Impact
  
  - Eliminates 4 `torch.empty` allocations per decode forward (1 output + 3 split-K)
  - Eliminates 1 D2D `.copy_()` per decode forward
  - Estimated ~50–150 μs/step savings on DeepSeek V4 with TP8 decode

title: [Feature]: SM8x (Ampere A100/A800) support for DeepSeek-V4-Flash / DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 DSpark
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

DeepSeek released [DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731) today (same `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` architecture as DeepSeek-V4-Flash). Neither checkpoint currently runs on SM8x (Ampere: A100/A800, RTX 30xx) — #40851 tracks the (substantial) user demand; this issue proposes and tracks a concrete contribution.

I have a working prototype on 8x A800 80GB (vLLM main @ `a074fd564` + a rebased community kernel set + fixes below): **40.6 tok/s single-stream decode** with cudagraphs, batch-8 at ~115 tok/s aggregate, boots at `max_model_len=1,048,576`, and retrieves a needle exactly from a 200k-token context. Quality validated (multi-step arithmetic, code generation, needle retrieval). So SM8x support is feasible with Triton/PyTorch fallbacks at usable speeds — no new CUDA required.

**Verified blocker chain on SM8x (main, empirical):**
1. Triton on SM80 cannot emit `fp8e4nv`: hits `_fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant_per_head` (o_proj path) and every fp8 KV-cache write kernel; fp8 KV is mandatory for DSv4. (Workaround exists: manual e4m3 bit manipulation, proven in the community fork.)
2. `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` is SM90a/SM100f-only; DSv4 decode additionally needs the dual-cache (`extra_k_cache`) + `attn_sink` + per-token-topk variant. A portable Triton bf16 sparse-MLA path works (community fork).
3. DeepGEMM `fp8_einsum` (o_proj) and MegaMoE are Hopper+; bf16 reference path (`rocm_inv_rope_einsum`, already in-tree for ROCm/XPU) works.
4. `wo_a` (`is_bmm` layer) gets Marlin-repacked to int32 while the DSv4 o_proj consumes the raw block-fp8 weight — needs a repack exclusion.

Already working on SM8x with no changes: the indexer Triton fallbacks (`fp8_mqa_logits_triton` / `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_triton`), MXFP4 experts via MarlinExperts, fp8 linear via Marlin.

**Bugs found while prototyping (arch-independent, will send as a separate small PR):**
- **int32 pointer-arithmetic overflow in `_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_kernel`** (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/mqa_logits_triton.py`): `block_idx` (int32, from the block table) is multiplied by the KV-pool block stride without an int64 cast. With the unified KV pool the per-layer view stride is ~1e6 elements, so the product wraps for `block_idx ≥ ~2065` → illegal memory access, or **silent corruption** when the wrapped address lands in mapped memory. Every other pool-accessing Triton kernel in-tree already casts (`.to(tl.int64)`). This affects **any model using the SM80/SM121 indexer fallback** (DSv4 and GLM DSA alike) once the pool exceeds ~2k blocks — i.e. exactly under long-context or concurrent load.
- Same kernel's tail store is masked only by `mask_n`, not `k_offset < context_len` (writes past the row for tail blocks).
- `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang` calls DeepGEMM `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` unconditionally — its siblings guard on `is_deep_gemm_supported()` and fall back to `_tilelang_hc_prenorm_gemm`; the broadcast variant missed the guard. This is the `hyperconnection.hpp:56 Unsupported architecture` error reported in #40851.
- `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant`: `launch_pdl` is a declared kernel parameter but the non-PDL branch omits it → `TypeError` on every pre-Hopper arch.

**Proposed contribution plan:**
1. **PR A (small, immediate):** the arch-independent fixes above (int64 cast + tail-store mask; DeepGEMM guard; `launch_pdl`). These fix real crashes/corruption independent of any new backend.
2. **PR B:** SM8x enablement for DeepSeek-V4 — an `ampere/` hardware backend under `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/` mirroring the existing `xpu/` layout (portable Triton bf16 sparse-MLA decode/prefill, manual-e4m3 cache writes, bf16 o_proj, Marlin repack exclusion for `is_bmm`, fused Triton MHC gates+sinkhorn for the hyperconnection layers), gated on `capability.major == 8`. This builds on the kernels from the community fork [Lasimeri/vllm-dsv4-ampere](https://github.com/Lasimeri/vllm-dsv4-ampere) (with credit), rebased onto current main, plus the fixes and the MHC fusion.

I'm aware of the sentiment that SM<90 for DSv4 "better lives in a fork" (PR #40906 discussion). Given the fleet sizes reported in #40851 and that this is all Python/Triton behind an arch gate (no new build targets, no impact on SM90+ paths), I'd like to ask maintainers whether a gated `ampere/` backend PR would be considered. If the answer is fork-only, PR A still stands on its own.

### Alternatives

- Keep SM8x support in out-of-tree forks (status quo): fragments quickly against main; the corruption-class bug above still needs an in-tree fix either way.
- llama.cpp `dsv4` branch: works but lacks vLLM's serving stack (continuous batching, prefix caching, OpenAI API parity).

### Additional context

Hardware: 8x NVIDIA A800 80GB PCIe (SM80), single node. All findings verified empirically on this machine against main @ `a074fd564`; happy to share full logs/repros. Analysis and prototyping were AI-assisted; I have validated every change and result end-to-end on the target hardware and will own the PRs.

Related: #40851 (user demand thread), PR #38476 / #47629 (GLM DSA SM8x sparse-MLA, same indexer fallback infrastructure).

title: [Bugfix][Model] Kimi-K3 NVIDIA: delegate regular FusedMoE padding to the selected quantization backend
body:
### Purpose

Kimi-K3 applies a model-level minimum MoE intermediate partition, while regular `FusedMoE` quantization backends also apply their own alignment. On NVIDIA MXFP4 Marlin at TP32, the logical global intermediate size is 3072, the raw local partition is 96, and Marlin requires 128. Passing the model-padded global size of 8192 instead makes regular `FusedMoE` allocate a local partition of 256.

This PR changes the NVIDIA regular non-EP ownership boundary:

```text
3072 logical global -> 96 raw TP32 local -> 128 Marlin-padded local
```

The regular `FusedMoEFactory` receives the logical intermediate size. The selected quantization backend owns the physical padded layout.

### Overlap with related work

#51131 fixes the expert-parallel path by skipping model-level padding when EP is enabled.

#50928 proposes retaining model-level padding and computing it from the effective shard count, including non-EP DP/PCP topologies and AMD.

This PR addresses the overlapping NVIDIA regular non-EP case with a different ownership model: regular `FusedMoE` receives the logical intermediate size, and the selected quantization backend applies its own required alignment.

The PR is therefore narrower than #50928: it does not change AMD, AITER, DP/PCP shard-count calculation, or MegaMoE behavior.

### Changes

- Pass `moe_intermediate_size` to the NVIDIA regular `FusedMoEFactory`.
- Retain the upstream model-level padding calculation, including the #51131 EP condition. MegaMoE remains the only consumer of the model-level padded value.
- Remove the NVIDIA post-construction model-level weight zeroing, packed-weight fallback, and `intermediate_size_per_partition_unpadded` fixup.
- Add focused NVIDIA regular-path, backend-sizing, MXFP4 allocation, and generic routed-expert loading coverage.

Because regular `FusedMoE` no longer consumes the model-level padded size, the associated model-level weight zeroing and `intermediate_size_per_partition_unpadded` fixup are removed as well. Backend allocation and generic routed-expert loading own the physical padded layout.

There is no CLI or kernel API change. The NVIDIA regular non-EP path no longer uses the model-level minimum partition as its allocation size. `min_moe_intermediate_per_partition` and the model-level padding structure are retained.

The production-code change is intentionally small: regular FusedMoE receives the logical intermediate size, and the obsolete model-level zero/fixup is removed. Most added lines are focused regression tests for backend sizing and padded weight loading.

### Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=tests/models/kimi_k3 \
  -q \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_moe_intermediate_padding.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_moe_padded_weight_loading.py

uvx ruff check \
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_moe_intermediate_padding.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_moe_padded_weight_loading.py

uvx ruff format --check \
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_moe_intermediate_padding.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_moe_padded_weight_loading.py

git diff --check 821717118fc26667dd474b9b0ab81d29259dfc5c...HEAD
git diff --exit-code 821717118fc26667dd474b9b0ab81d29259dfc5c -- \
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/linear.py
```

Results:

```text
pytest:                  31 passed
ruff check:              all checks passed
ruff format --check:     3 files already formatted
git diff --check:        passed
AMD unchanged check:     passed
```

The unit tests verify:

- TP8/TP16/TP32 NVIDIA regular factories always receive 3072, while the retained model-level value is 3072/4096/8192 respectively;
- no model-level weight `zero_()` or MoE-config fixup occurs;
- Marlin partitions are `384 -> 384`, `192 -> 256`, and `96 -> 128`;
- the existing raw-96 backend oracle matrix;
- TP32 rank 0/rank 31 weight and scale placement;
- all 32 ranks cover each checkpoint element exactly once without overlap or omission;
- only the valid 96-wide region is loaded into the 128-wide allocation and the padded tail remains zero;
- TP8 unpadded loading is unchanged.

### Historical end-to-end evidence and validation scope

The original problem was reproduced on a 4-node, 32x NVIDIA H20 deployment with EP disabled, MXFP4 quantization, and the Marlin MoE backend. On the old base, the backend-owned sizing scheme exercised the intended `3072 -> raw local 96 -> Marlin 128` path: all 32 ranks loaded all 96 checkpoint shards, KV-cache creation completed, and `/v1/chat/completions` returned HTTP 200. The baseline failed during expert-weight allocation with a local partition of 256.

That result is historical end-to-end evidence for the original bug and for the backend-owned sizing approach on the old base. It is not a complete hardware validation of this rebased commit, and this PR does not claim that the rebased files are byte-for-byte identical to the historical experiment. No new H20 integration test is added because the required topology is not available in the current environment.

No separate accuracy evaluation was run. The change does not alter kernels, logical weights, routing, or numerical computation; it changes allocation ownership and removes a redundant model-level fixup. The historical serving run provides forward-path evidence, subject to the scope above.

AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI Codex assisted with the implementation and tests. I reviewed the final diff and validation results.

title: [Bugfix] Honour VLLM_MQ_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES_MB at every MessageQueue call site
body:
## Purpose

`VLLM_MQ_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES_MB` exists to bound the `/dev/shm` ring buffers, but only `rpc_broadcast_mq` reads it. `worker_response_mq` falls back to the 24 MiB signature default in both the multiproc and Ray v2 executors — and that queue is created once **per worker**, so at TP=2 it requests `2 × 24 MiB × 10 chunks = 480 MiB` regardless of the env var.

On the common 64 MiB `/dev/shm`, the knob therefore cannot bring total usage under the limit. Since #48879 added `check_shm_free_space`, this is now a hard startup failure rather than a latent SIGBUS:

```
File "vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 585, in _init_message_queues
    self.worker_response_mq = MessageQueue(1, 1)
RuntimeError: Insufficient space in /dev/shm: 240 MiB required, 64 MiB free.
```

Setting `VLLM_MQ_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES_MB=4` moves the broadcast queue from 160 → 40 MiB but leaves the 480 MiB untouched, so the boot still fails:

| `VLLM_MQ_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES_MB` | `rpc_broadcast_mq` | `worker_response_mq` × 2 | total | fits 64 MiB? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 (default) | 160 MiB | 480 MiB | 640 MiB | no |
| 4, before this PR | 40 MiB | 480 MiB | 520 MiB | no |
| 4, with this PR | 40 MiB | 80 MiB | 120 MiB | no |
| 1, with this PR | 10 MiB | 20 MiB | 30 MiB | **yes** |

This matters most where `/dev/shm` cannot be resized. A plain Kubernetes Pod needs an `emptyDir{medium: Memory}` mount to raise it, and some managed platforms do not expose that. #49568 makes it configurable in the Helm chart; this change gives deployments that *cannot* mount volumes a way to fit inside what they have.

Reducing the chunk size is safe for these queues: an oversized message is not fatal, `shm_broadcast` sets an overflow flag and falls back to a local socket. The 24 MiB default is sized (per the comment on `MessageQueue.__init__`) for grammar bitmask tensors at 1024 requests, which is a property of the *broadcast* queue rather than the per-worker response queue.

Discovered while running DeepSeek-V4 at TP=2 on a platform with a fixed 64 MiB `/dev/shm`. Note this over-commit predates `check_shm_free_space` — it only ever worked because tmpfs allocates lazily, exactly the failure mode #48879 set out to make visible.

## Alternative considered

Making `MessageQueue.__init__` default `max_chunk_bytes` to the env var would guarantee no call site can bypass the cap, at the cost of changing the effective default for `worker_response_mq` from 24 → 16 MiB. I went with explicit pass-through to keep the change minimal and behaviour-preserving at default settings, but I'm happy to switch if maintainers prefer the stronger guarantee.

## Duplicate check

Searched issues and PRs for `worker_response_mq`, `max_chunk_bytes`, `VLLM_MQ_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES_MB`, `shm_broadcast`, `dev/shm` and the error string before writing this. #48879 added `check_shm_free_space` (its discussion does not raise the per-worker queue) and #49568 makes `/dev/shm` configurable in the Helm chart, which helps deployments that *can* mount volumes. Nothing merged or open addresses the env var being ignored at these two call sites, and `worker_response_mq = MessageQueue(1, 1)` is still unbounded on `main` today.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_mq_max_chunk_bytes.py -v
```

New test asserts the per-worker response queue picks up `VLLM_MQ_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES_MB` (parametrised over 1 and 4 MiB) by recording the kwargs passed at construction, plus a guard that a smaller chunk size actually shrinks `total_bytes_of_buffer` — the assumption the fix depends on.

Manual reproduction: `--tensor-parallel-size 2` in a container with `--shm-size=64m`. On `main` this fails with the error above (confirmed); with this change and `VLLM_MQ_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES_MB=1` the requested buffers total 30 MiB, which should clear the check — confirmation pending, see Test Result.

## Test Result

**Unit tests: not yet run.** I have no built vLLM/torch in my environment, so I am not pasting results I have not seen. CI is the gate for those.

**End-to-end: confirmed.** On the affected deployment (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP=2, fixed 64 MiB `/dev/shm`):

*Before* — fails at `_init_message_queues`, after a ~32 minute weight load:

```
Model loading took 79.03 GiB and 1904.426086 seconds
RuntimeError: Insufficient space in /dev/shm: 240 MiB required, 64 MiB free.
```

*After* (same base, this change, `VLLM_MQ_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES_MB=1`) — both queues initialise and startup proceeds past them:

```
Loading safetensors using Runai Model Streamer: 100% Completed | 72317/72317 [16:08<00:00, 74.68it/s]
INFO [dspark.py:465] DSpark draft model loaded: 96 params
INFO [model_runner.py:328] Model loading took 79.03 GiB and 1916.294725 seconds
INFO [topk_topp_sampler.py:62] Using FlashInfer for top-p & top-k sampling.
```

Startup then reached memory profiling and kernel warmup. (That run later failed for an unrelated reason in the draft model's attention — no message queues involved. Reporting it for completeness rather than claiming a fully clean boot.)

Intermediate evidence that isolates the cause: with `VLLM_MQ_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES_MB=4` and *without* this change, the first failure moved from `multiproc_executor.py:151` (160 MiB) to `:585` (240 MiB) — the env var works where it is read, and is ignored where it is not.

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance (Claude) was used to develop this change, and the commit carries a `Co-authored-by:` trailer accordingly.

Per the "Be involved" requirement: the submitting author has reviewed every changed line, and the fix is validated end-to-end on the affected deployment (see Test Result). The unit tests added here have not yet been executed locally — that is the one outstanding item, and CI is the gate for it.

title: [Attention][MLA] Per-request scheduling for MLA chunked context
body:
## Summary

Implements #50497. MLA prefill chunks are fit into the available workspace rather than forced to be the same size. This can reduce the overall number of chunks and improve prefill latency.

## Validation

### Correctness

`pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py -q` passes

title: [Bug]: DSpark spec decode dies in profile_run — forward_mqa warmup asserts topk_indices_buffer, which a drafter never has (regression from #50298)
body:
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Could not be captured: the crash happens inside EngineCore during profile_run, so the API server never starts and the pod has no shell. Environment facts taken from the boot log: vLLM version : 0.26.1rc1.dev77+g6f91edf96 (also reproduces on 0.26.1rc1.dev181+g0f1739456) Docker image : vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-0f17394564fa2fccd332cf63321314884c15ee37 Python : 3.12 PyTorch/CUDA : as shipped in the above image NCCL : 2.28.9 GPU : 2 x NVIDIA H100 NVL (93.09 GiB each, reported total_memory=99949805568) Platform : CUDA (auto-detected), Linux container on Kubernetes Parallelism : tensor_parallel_size=2, distributed_executor_backend=mp Model : deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 Model runner : V2 (VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1) ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `forward_mqa`'s warmup branch in `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py` unconditionally asserts `self.topk_indices_buffer is not None`. The DSpark drafter has no sparse indexer and therefore no such buffer, so **any DeepSeek-V4 + DSpark deployment dies during `profile_run`** — after the model has fully loaded. This is a regression introduced by #50298. The assert does not exist in `v0.26.0`, and `git log v0.26.0.. -- vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py` shows #50298 as the only commit touching that file in between. **Reproduce** ```bash vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --block-size 256 \ --max-model-len 262144 \ --max-num-seqs 4 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 \ --speculative-config='{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7}' ``` Any `--speculative-config` with `method: dspark` should be sufficient; the rest of the flags are from our deployment. **Traceback** ``` (Worker_TP1 pid=1852) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:1024] WorkerProc hit an exception. (Worker_TP1 pid=1852) ERROR ... Traceback (most recent call last): File "vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 1016, in worker_busy_loop output = func(*args, **kwargs) File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 504, in determine_available_memory self.model_runner.profile_run() File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 718, in profile_run hidden_states, sample_hidden_states = self._dummy_run( File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 655, in _dummy_run self.speculator.propose( File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py", line 361, in propose self._generate_draft( File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/speculator.py", line 162, in _generate_draft head_hidden = self._run_model( File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py", line 236, in _run_model last_hidden_states = self.model( File "vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/dspark.py", line 327, in forward return self.model(input_ids, positions, inputs_embeds) File "vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/dspark.py", line 180, in forward hidden_states, residual, post_mix, res_mix = layer( File "vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py", line 933, in forward x = self.attn(positions, x, None) File "vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py", line 378, in forward self.attention_impl( File "vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py", line 535, in attention_impl self.forward_mqa(q, kv, positions, out) File "vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py", line 99, in forward_mqa assert self.topk_indices_buffer is not None AssertionError ``` `EngineCore` then reports `RuntimeError: Worker failed with error ''` — the `AssertionError` carries no message, so the surfaced error is empty. **Root cause** `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py`, current `main`: ```python 87 if attn_metadata is None: 88 # Warmup dummy run: no real metadata. Reserve the same bf16 89 # gather workspace _forward_prefill would; the dequantize / topk 90 # / sparse_fwd kernels are skipped this step. 91 swa_only = self.compress_ratio <= 1 ... 99 assert self.topk_indices_buffer is not None 100 top_k = 0 if swa_only else self.topk_indices_buffer.shape[-1] ``` Two separate problems here: 1. **The assert is unconditional, but the value is only needed when `not swa_only`.** Line 100 already short-circuits to `top_k = 0` for the SWA-only case and never reads the buffer — yet line 99 rejects `None` before that check runs. So even an SWA-only layer with no buffer crashes. 2. **A drafter legitimately has no `topk_indices_buffer`.** `topk_indices_buffer` is populated from `indexer.topk_indices_buffer` in `sparse_mla_attention.py`; the DSpark draft model has no indexer, so it is `None` by construction, not by mistake. Only the warmup path is affected. The three pre-existing asserts on this buffer (lines ~166/268/278 in `v0.26.0`) live in real-metadata paths where a target model is guaranteed to have one, which is presumably why this went unnoticed — #50298's new early-return branch is the first place the buffer is touched during `profile_run`. **Suggested fix** At minimum, reorder so the buffer is only required when it is actually read: ```python if swa_only: top_k = 0 else: assert self.topk_indices_buffer is not None top_k = self.topk_indices_buffer.shape[-1] ``` That is behaviour-preserving for every configuration that works today. Whether that is sufficient depends on whether a DSpark drafter is ever `not swa_only` — if it is, the deeper question is whether drafters should share the target's `topk_indices_buffer`. #41212 reports that this share is already a silent no-op in the V1 proposer path for MTP, so the two may be worth looking at together. **Workaround** Pin to a base predating #50298 (e.g. `nightly-6f91edf96d3f3272945809c04702380053bff4de`, 2026-07-29) — or don't use DSpark. Worth noting the cost of the failure mode: the assert fires in `profile_run`, which runs *after* the full weight load. On a 155 GiB checkpoint that is ~30 minutes before an unmessaged `AssertionError`. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Densify strided activations for wvSplitKQ
body:
## Purpose

Prevent ROCm skinny GEMMs from reading past a packed activation view.
`wvSplitK` and `wvSplitKrc` do not consume strides, so their dispatch now
materializes the activation only when its 2-D layout is not exactly dense
row-major.

Kimi-K3 KDA projects several outputs into one row and passes the 128-element
`f_a` slice to `f_b_proj`. Under TP8 that view has `stride=(6288, 1)` and
`storage_offset=6144`. The skinny kernel preloads a flat span; the view is valid
for PyTorch indexing but the preload extends 12,288 bytes past it.

| Rows | `is_contiguous()` | Available | Flat preload | Over-read |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | `True` | 288 B | 12,576 B | 12,288 B |
| 4 | `False` | 38,016 B | 50,304 B | 12,288 B |

The singleton case is why `is_contiguous()` is insufficient: PyTorch ignores
singleton-dimension strides. Dense inputs, fallback GEMMs, NVIDIA, HIP kernel
code, and dispatch thresholds are unchanged.

## Test plan

Tested on 8x MI355X (`gfx950`) with the public Kimi-K3 image. Models:
`moonshotai/Kimi-K3@9f62e4e9` and `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark@cf6b8244`.
The command below pins the control and PR source revisions.

Fetch and verify the candidate:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git vllm
git -C vllm fetch origin refs/pull/50618/head:pr-50618
test "$(git -C vllm rev-parse pr-50618)" = \
  aa780f0db6e5f467378856dffda1e939bca53604
git -C vllm checkout --detach 9a7ae4b80866a322678ece31ca2854d9a174ab8d
git -C vllm diff 9a7ae4b80866a322678ece31ca2854d9a174ab8d..pr-50618 \
  --binary | git -C vllm apply -
git -C vllm diff --check
```

Use the complete verified vLLM tree as an overlay on the public image; do not
copy individual files. Verify `import vllm, vllm._C` before testing. Run:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_rocm_unquantized_gemm.py
```

Launch TP8 with both exact model revisions:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM=1 AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 \
AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 \
vllm serve /model --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --trust-remote-code --moe-backend auto \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-model-len 1048576 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,4,64]}' \
  --speculative-config \
  '{"method":"dspark","model":"/draft","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"TRITON_MLA"}'
```

The focused test injects packed singleton and multi-row views into both skinny
dispatches and asserts that the native kernels receive dense `(128, 1)`
activations. The real-workload layout can also be proved without issuing the
unsafe read by logging shape, stride, storage offset, remaining storage bytes,
and `stride(0) * rows * element_size()` immediately before dispatch.

## Test results

- Pinned-public focused suite: **4/4 passed in 4.46 s**.
- Native MI355X B1/B4 checks reached `wvSplitK` with dense activations and
  matched `torch.nn.functional.linear` exactly (`max_abs_error=0`).
- TP8 loaded 96/96 target shards and the draft; graph capture completed at
  1/4/64 tokens; health and generation passed with no memory-access fault.
- Full source-isolated GSM8K from the preceding runtime revision: control
  **1274/1319**, candidate **1276/1319**, zero invalid responses, 13 wins/11
  losses (`p=0.8388`). The final commit changes only the stride predicate and
  singleton test coverage; the full run was not repeated at that final head.
- Changed-file pre-commit, `git diff --check`, and DCO passed.

## Limits

The unpatched fault is allocator-layout dependent: the unsupported read faults
only when it crosses an unmapped page. The deterministic stride/storage probe
establishes the over-read even when a serving run happens not to fault.

## Tool assistance

Claude Opus and OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, tests, log/source
analysis, and drafting this description.

---

## Update 2026-08-18 — rewritten after re-checking against current upstream

**The original bug no longer reproduces.** #50907 densifies both skinny call sites
in `layers/utils.py`, covering what this PR fixed plus the `LLMM1` path it missed.
Checked over 139 layouts, including the single-row cases a contiguity flag cannot
express: zero over-read in all of them.

**The same defect is live in `wvSplitKQ`, which is what this PR now fixes.**
Identical staging bound (`Kap * N`, `Kap = in_a.stride(0)`), and its call site
`scaled_mm/rocm.py` never densifies.

There is a reachable in-tree path to it, and it runs entirely through
`is_contiguous()` reporting True for a single-row view:

| step | what happens |
|---|---|
| `x` is a single-row activation whose row stride exceeds K | `x.is_contiguous()` is **True** — PyTorch ignores the stride of a size-1 dim |
| `QuantFP8.forward_hip` | gates the aiter path on exactly that flag (`input_quant_fp8.py:144`), so it is taken |
| `rocm_aiter_ops.per_tensor_quant` | allocates with `torch.empty_like(x, dtype=...)`, which **preserves the row stride** |
| `ScaledMMLinearKernel` | `x_data.view(-1, shape[-1])` is a no-op on an already-2-D tensor |
| `wvSplitKQ` | receives stride(0) > K and stages past the extent |

Measured: at 1 row the stride survives `empty_like` as `(6288, 1)`; at 2 and 4 rows
`is_contiguous()` is False, the aiter gate rejects it, and the output comes back
dense. So the exposure is specifically single-row decode — which is what this
dispatch is for (`A.shape[0] <= 4`).

Config required: fp8 W8A8 with **per-tensor** activation and weight scales,
`VLLM_ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM` (default on), `B.shape[0] % 16 == 0`,
`B.shape[1] % 16 == 0`.

```python
# repro.py -- MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2, torch 2.11.0
import torch, vllm._custom_ops as ops

K, MULT = 1024, 8192
cu = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).multi_processor_count
fp8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn

wide = torch.randn(1, K * MULT, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda").to(fp8)
act = wide[:, K * (MULT - 1):]      # tail slice: valid data ends at the storage end
w = torch.randn(64, K, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda").to(fp8)
s = torch.ones(1, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")

print(f"act{tuple(act.shape)} stride={act.stride()} "
      f"-> kernel walks {act.stride(0)} elems, {K} valid")
ops.wvSplitKQ(w, act, torch.bfloat16, s, s, cu, None)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
```

```console
$ PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1 python repro.py
act(1, 1024) stride=(8388608, 1) -> kernel walks 8388608 elems, 1024 valid
Memory access fault by GPU node-3 (Agent handle: 0x3ce8f1c0) on address 0x7090fb800000
```

The env var only makes the fault visible: pooled allocations leave the bytes past a
tensor mapped, so the over-read normally reads a neighbour instead of faulting.
Staging bounds by the stride, compute bounds by `K`, so results stay correct and no
`allclose` test can catch this. Shrinking the stride so the over-read is 256 /
16,128 / 1,047,552 elements instead, it does not fault at all and the results are
correct — in production that makes it an occasional crash unrelated to its cause.

### Changes

- `scaled_mm/rocm.py`: densify before `wvSplitKQ`. Tests the stride explicitly
  rather than calling `.contiguous()`, which is a no-op on a single-row view.
- `skinny_gemms.cu`: state the contract `wvSplitKQ` already depends on, so a future
  call site fails at the boundary instead of over-reading.

### Test plan / results

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_rocm_scaled_mm_strided.py -q
```

Six tests, none vacuous: the four strided cases and the kernel-contract case fail
without this PR (the last as `DID NOT RAISE RuntimeError`); dense passthrough passes
either way. `ruff check`/`format` clean at the pinned v0.14.0.

The kernel-contract test needs the rebuilt extension, so I built it: with the
`TORCH_CHECK` compiled in it passes, and against a build without it the same test
reports `DID NOT RAISE RuntimeError`.

Tool assistance: analysis, repro and this description produced with Claude Code; I
reviewed every changed line and ran the above on MI355X.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Spec Decode] Fix defects on the Kimi-K3 DSpark decode path
body:
## Purpose

Two defects on the Kimi-K3 DSpark decode path:

1. The draft model turns cudagraphs off for the whole target model.
2. The multi-token verify is split into one decode per token, which costs two waits on the GPU every forward.

### (1) A draft's attention decides the target's cudagraph mode

Before it captures anything, vLLM asks every attention group whether it can be graphed and takes the lowest answer. Groups that belong to a spec-decode draft are asked too:

```python
for group in groups:
    cg_support = builder.get_cudagraph_support(vllm_config, group.kv_cache_spec)
    if cg_support.value < min_cg_support.value:
        min_cg_support = cg_support          # draft-owned groups included
```

That lowest answer then decides the mode for the *target*:

```python
if (cudagraph_mode.decode_mode() == CUDAGraphMode.FULL
        and uniform_decode_query_len > 1
        and min_cg_support.value < AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_BATCH.value):
    cudagraph_mode = CUDAGraphMode.NONE      # PIECEWISE only if splitting_ops
```

Kimi-K3 meets all three conditions. The target runs AiterMLA, which reports `UNIFORM_BATCH`, and the recipe puts the draft on TritonMLA, which reports `UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE`. The draft's answer is the lower one, so **5 draft layers turn cudagraphs off for all 93 target layers**. The draft never needed that help: `init_cudagraph_manager` already looks at its own support level and runs the draft eagerly when it cannot be graphed.

**Fix: leave a draft that already checks itself out of the target's decision, and keep a second minimum for the check that still needs every group.**

Some drafts do not check themselves. Eagle, mtp and gemma4 (`AutoRegressiveSpeculator`), and `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator`, simply use whatever mode the target ended up with. For those the downgrade is doing real work: take it away and they would capture in a mode their own backend cannot run. So the test is a flag on the speculator, not its class:

```python
if isinstance(speculator, DraftModelSpeculator) and speculator.sizes_own_cudagraph_mode:
    return speculator.draft_attn_layer_names
```

`init_attn_backend` now takes two minimums instead of one. The old `min_cg_support` still covers every group, and adaptive verification reads it, so that check is unchanged. The new `graph_min_cg_support` leaves out groups made up entirely of draft layers, and only the cudagraph decision reads it. A group that mixes target and draft layers stays in both. Today only `DFlashSpeculator` and `DSparkSpeculator` set the flag.

### (2) The verify block is split into one decode per token

The draft proposes several tokens at once and the target checks them in one block — 8 of them with the `num_speculative_tokens=7` this recipe uses. Each token in the block may only look at the text before it, not after it. In bf16 there is no asm kernel for fewer than 16 heads with more than one query token, so a 12-head rank sends this block to Gluon instead. (With an fp8 cache the q-row fold — folding query rows into the head dimension — does give it an asm kernel, so only bf16 comes here.)

The old code faked the "look backward only" rule by issuing one single-token decode per verify token, each with its own slice of the KV list. Building those slices meant rewriting the paged-KV table on every forward, and twice asking the GPU for a value and waiting for it:

```python
new_indptr = torch.cat([old_indptr.new_zeros(1), row_len.cumsum(0)]).to(torch.int32)
total = int(new_indptr[-1].item())                  # host sync
...
new_indices = decode.paged_kv_indices[src]          # gather over the whole batch
mla_gluon(..., page_table=new_indices, seq_info=new_indptr,
          min_kv_seq_len=int(row_len.min()))        # host sync
```

**Fix: give Gluon the whole block at once, which it already accepts, and delete the splitting.**

Gluon takes a `[batch, qlen, nhead, dim]` query and applies the backward-only rule itself, so reshaping the query is all that is needed. The page table goes through untouched:

```python
q_nope = q_nope.view(batch_size, qlen, num_q_heads, self.kv_lora_rank)
q_pe = q_pe.view(batch_size, qlen, num_q_heads, self.qk_rope_head_dim)
mla_gluon(..., page_table=decode.paged_kv_indices, seq_info=decode.paged_kv_indptr,
          min_kv_seq_len=decode.min_kv_seq_len)
```

Net −71 lines in `rocm_aiter_mla.py`.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py                       # 8, CPU only

pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_causal_verify_mask.py   # 2, ROCm + AITER
```

The first needs no GPU: it drives `init_attn_backend` with stubs. The second builds
the real AITER backend and metadata on device and replaces the Gluon kernel with a
spy, so it skips off ROCm.

End to end on 8x MI355X, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-aa9903490c616dc6871e5acc62cec7bb1e5e9434`, with `/model` = `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` and `/draft` its DSpark draft. Serve flags follow #51253:

```bash
vllm serve /model --served-model-name k3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.93 --block-size 128 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --load-format auto --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \
  --compilation-config '{"custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"/draft",
                         "num_speculative_tokens":7,
                         "attention_backend":"TRITON_MLA"}' \
  --port 8000
```

Run it twice: as written for the fp8 numbers, then with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` dropped for the bf16 numbers. That one flag is what sends the verify to the padded asm decode or to Gluon.

```bash
for C in 1 8; do
  vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
    --model k3 --tokenizer /model --trust-remote-code --port 8000 \
    --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 \
    --ignore-eos --max-concurrency $C --num-prompts $((C == 1 ? 16 : 48))
done

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=k3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 32 \
  --apply_chat_template --gen_kwargs temperature=0
```

`--apply_chat_template` and `tokenized_requests=False` are both needed against a chat endpoint. `--gen_kwargs temperature=0` matters because this model's `generation_config.json` sets no temperature, so the default is 1.0 and the run would otherwise be sampled.

## Test Result

Unit tests: **10 passed** (8 without a GPU, plus the 2 ROCm ones). For the end-to-end runs the control is this branch's base and the patched side is its head, in the same container, against the same aiter build.

Both dtypes are here because the KV cache dtype picks the decode kernel, and only one of them reaches the kernel (2) changes.

**fp8 sends the verify to the aiter asm decode**, and that is the production setup — the Kimi-K3 recipe runs `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`. Both of Gluon's checks turn a quantized cache away, so the verify falls through to the padded asm path: `get_mla_padded_q` pads 12 heads to 16, then `mla_decode_fwd`. That run covers (1), and the asm decode is the kernel that restored capture now has to hold.

**bf16 sends the verify to Gluon**, and it is the only setup that does, so it is the one that covers (2).

| KV cache | decode kernel | conc. | base | patched | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fp8 | aiter asm (padded) | 1 | 14.82 tok/s, TPOT 66.09 ms | **67.41 tok/s, TPOT 13.44 ms** | **4.5x** |
| fp8 | aiter asm (padded) | 8 | 108.49 tok/s, TPOT 66.72 ms | **291.06 tok/s, TPOT 23.96 ms** | **2.7x** |
| bf16 | Gluon | 1 | 15.01 tok/s, TPOT 65.00 ms | **72.22 tok/s, TPOT 12.24 ms** | **4.8x** |
| bf16 | Gluon | 8 | 102.57 tok/s, TPOT 68.88 ms | **309.07 tok/s, TPOT 22.37 ms** | **3.0x** |

Both control runs report `cudagraph_mode=NONE`, 8 downgrade warnings and 0 captures. Both patched runs report 0 warnings and 8 captures, with the draft eager on all 8 ranks.

Accuracy, on the full GSM8K test set (1319 questions), 5-shot, greedy, fp8 KV:

| | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| base | 0.9613 ± 0.0053 | 0.9598 ± 0.0054 |
| patched | 0.9651 ± 0.0051 | 0.9644 ± 0.0051 |

Operator benchmark for (2), against Gluon directly: 12 heads, kv_lora 512, rope 64, bf16 KV. The splitting work is inside the timed region, because the old code did it on every forward. Over batch 8-32, qlen 2-8 and ctx 8k-32k, sending all the tokens at once is **1.52-4.07x faster** — 383.8 us down to 148.0 us at batch 8, qlen 8, ctx 8192. Outputs agree to 1.5e-05.

---

Written with AI assistance (Claude Code); the commits carry `Co-authored-by: Claude`. I reviewed every changed line, ran the unit tests and the end-to-end runs above myself, and am responsible for the result.
