title: [Feature] Enable AITER MXFP4 MoE on gfx942 and optimize tile configurations for MI325X Target Kimi K3 running on MI325X
body:
## Summary

Makes Kimi-K3 run on AMD MI325X (gfx942 / CDNA3). The model loaded but
aborted in MLA decode; once past that it fell back to a dequantise-to-BF16
MoE emulation path. Both are fixed, and a third change addresses AITER MoE
tile shapes being sized for CDNA4 on all architectures.

Measured on 8x MI325X with the real 2.75T-parameter MXFP4 checkpoint:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kimi-K3 decode (TP=8, CUDA graphs, warm) | 4.27 tok/s | **99.67 tok/s** (23x) |
| Prefill throughput (36k prompt) | 3,522 tok/s | **6,537 tok/s** (1.9x) |
| MLA decode at 12 heads/rank | `AssertionError` | works, bit-exact |

## Motivation

Three independent blockers, in the order they surfaced.

**1. MLA decode aborted on any model with <16 heads per rank.**

```
AssertionError: mla_gluon requires gfx950 (CDNA4), got gfx942
```

AITER's small-head MLA decode kernel asserts CDNA4, but the backend selected
it on head count alone. Kimi-K3 has 96 attention heads, so TP=8 gives 12 per
rank — and TP=8 is the *only* viable parallelism: 1.5 TB of weights against
2 TB of HBM rules out TP=6 (260 GB/GPU, and 7168 % 6 != 0) and TP=4 (390
GB/GPU).

The existing pad-to-16 fallback only handled head counts dividing 16;
`repeat_interleave(16 // num_heads)` is a silent no-op for 12, leaving q at
12 heads while the output was allocated for 16.

**2. MXFP4 MoE fell through to BF16 emulation on gfx942.**

AITER's CK MXFP4 kernel needs CDNA4 native FP4 MFMA, so gfx942 landed on
`OCP_MXQuantizationEmulationTritonExperts`, which dequantises the *entire*
weight tensor every forward:

```python
w1_dequant = self._dequantize_weights(w1, ...)   # all 896 experts
w2_dequant = self._dequantize_weights(w2, ...)   # 16 are routed to
```

That is 56x the required work. For K3: 896 experts x 33.0M params / 8 GPUs
x 2 bytes ~= 7.4 GB per layer, x 93 layers ~= 688 GB materialised per token,
written then read back ~= 1.4 TB of HBM traffic, / ~6 TB/s ~= 229 ms/token.
Predicted ~4.4 tok/s; measured 4.27. That was the entire performance story.

AITER *does* ship a Triton `moe_gemm_a16w4` kernel which dequantises
in-register during the GEMM. It runs correctly on gfx942 — the arch gate
simply never admitted it. The ROCm base image already builds AITER with
`AITER_ROCM_ARCH="gfx942;gfx950"`, so these kernels were compiled and
present all along.

**3. AITER MoE tile selection is architecture-blind.**

`get_kernel_config` hardcodes `block_k=256`, `block_n=512`, `num_stages=1`
for every AMD part. Those suit CDNA4's 160 KiB LDS; CDNA3 has 64 KiB.
`arch_info._LDS_CAP_BYTES` already records the per-arch capacity and is
consulted by `pa_decode_sparse`, `gemm_config_utils` and
`sparse_attention_dsv4` — the MoE GEMM is the one kernel that skips it.

## Changes

### MLA small-head decode (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py`)

- Add `AiterMLAHelper.gluon_decode_available()` (gfx950) and require it in
  `use_gluon_decode()` and in the multi-token verify branch, so non-CDNA4
  falls through to the padded path instead of asserting.
- `get_mla_padded_q` / `get_mla_unpadded_o` keep whole-repeat expansion where
  the head count divides 16, and zero-pad the head dimension otherwise.

Zero-padding is exact, not approximate: the decode kernel treats query heads
independently, so filler heads cannot perturb retained ones. The new test
pins that property — running 16 real heads, then the same tensor with heads
>= N zeroed, gives **bit-identical** outputs for heads 0..N-1.

### MXFP4 MoE on gfx942

- `mxfp4_utils.py`: new `use_aiter_mxfp4_triton_moe()` — a single predicate
  for "AITER MXFP4 runs the Triton kernel", replacing scattered `on_gfx1250()`
  checks that independently decided weight-preparation format. It also
  requires `has_triton_kernels()`, so a build without that package falls
  through to previous behaviour instead of asserting at weight load.
- `aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe.py`: admit gfx942 in
  `AiterW4A16ExpertsMonolithic._supports_current_device`.
- `oracle/mxfp4.py`: split the `AITER_MXFP4_BF16` weight-prep branch — the
  Triton path swizzles and returns `PrecisionConfig`s, the CK path keeps the
  de-interleave plus aiter shuffle.
- `quantization/mxfp4.py`: route parameter-vs-wrapped-tensor assignment, the
  `is_shuffled` marking, and the quant-config scale source through the same
  predicate.

The **de-interleave of w13 gate/up pairs is CK-only.** A first attempt applied
it to the Triton path and produced uncorrelated output (cosine 0.034 vs the
TRITON backend). The Triton kernel consumes the checkpoint's interleaved
layout like every other Triton backend.

### SiTU activation support

K3's MoE uses SiTU — `beta*tanh(gate/beta)*sigmoid(gate)*up` — which cannot
be expressed through the a16w4 kernel's `alpha`/`limit`/`add_residual` knobs.

`aiter_triton_kernel_w4a16_moe_forward` now runs gemm1 unfused for SiTU and
applies the existing compiled `torch.ops._C.situ_and_mul` between the two
GEMMs. Only activations round-trip through HBM (a few hundred KB); weights
never do. K3 already stores w13 as `[gate_all, up_all]`, exactly what
`situ_and_mul` splits on, so no reshuffling is needed.

`_setup_kernel_k3_situ` emits the Triton layout on gfx942 rather than the CK
shuffle, and drops the registered Parameters before rebinding since the
swizzled tensors are `triton_kernels` wrappers.

### Tooling and CI

- `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe_a16w4_tiles.py` — sweeps MoE tile shapes
  and reports the best against stock. Overrides only tiles at/above
  `--min-block-m` (default 64), leaving decode alone.
- `tools/vllm-rocm/patch_aiter_cdna3_moe_tiles.py` — LDS-aware override for
  AITER's tile selector on gfx942, with `--revert`.
- `tools/vllm-rocm/README_kimi_k3_mi325x.md` — serving recipe and two
  operational traps (below).
- `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` — add
  `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/third_party/kda/` to the KDA job's source
  dependencies; edits to the AMD kernel copies did not trigger the AMD job.
- `kimi_k3/amd/.../kda/__init__.py` — correct a provenance note claiming
  byte-identity with a NVIDIA copy that has since diverged.

## Results

All on 8x MI325X (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.3 container, AITER v0.1.19, real
`moonshotai/Kimi-K3` weights, TP=8, CUDA graphs, `max_num_seqs=512`,
`gpu_memory_utilization=0.97`.

**Decode**

| backend | tok/s |
| --- | --- |
| EMULATION (before) | 4.27 |
| Triton a16w4 + SiTU, cold | 65.66 |
| Triton a16w4 + SiTU, warm | **99.67** |

Cold carries ~18 Triton JIT compilations inside the timed window.

**MoE GEMM tile shapes** (4096 tokens; stock = `block_n=512 block_k=256
warps=8 stages=1`)

| GEMM | stock | best gfx942 | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gemm1 K=3584 N=768 | 8.208 ms | 1.303 ms (`bn=128 bk=128 s=1 w=4`) | 6.30x |
| gemm2 K=384 N=7168 | 8.019 ms | 1.701 ms (`bn=512 bk=128 s=2 w=8`) | 4.72x |

`block_k` is the dominant variable — halving it shrinks both LDS tiles at
once. Triton names the constraint when it does not fit:
`OutOfResources: shared memory, Required: 100352, Hardware limit: 65536`.

**End-to-end prefill**

| prompt tokens | before | after | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3,697 | 2,268 tok/s | 4,459 | 1.97x |
| 14,497 | 3,156 tok/s | 5,910 | 1.87x |
| 36,097 | 3,522 tok/s | 6,537 | 1.86x |
| 72,098 | 3,427 tok/s | 6,585 | 1.92x |

Smaller than the kernel-level 5-6x because prefill also pays for MLA, 69 KDA
layers, norms and TP collectives.

## Testing

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_small_head_pad.py
# 11 passed

VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
  pytest -v -s tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py -k test_rocm_mxfp4_moe_oracle
# 3 passed, 1 skipped (AITER_MXFP4_FP8 still requires gfx950)

VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
  pytest -v -s tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py \
              tests/kernels/moe/test_mxfp8_aiter_backend_selection.py
# 22 passed, 117 skipped, 0 failed

pytest -v -s tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_attn_res.py
# 4 passed

pytest -v -s tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py
# 45 passed, 6 skipped
```

Additional verification beyond the suites:

- Isolated a16w4 kernel vs dequantised reference GEMM: max rel err **5.7e-4**
- Full MoE vs the trusted TRITON backend, identical weights: cosine **0.999906**
- MLA head padding: **bit-identical** outputs for retained heads

## Model evaluation

Greedy decode (`temperature=0`) through the OpenAI-compatible server on real
weights returns identical text to the EMULATION baseline, including
`17 * 23 = 17 * 20 + 17 * 3 = 340 + 51 = 391`. Post-tile-patch spot checks:
4/4 correct, including `4839 * 271 = 1311369`.

I did **not** run a formal lm-eval / gsm8k harness. Given the change is
kernel-path only and matches the reference backend to cosine 0.999906, I
consider that proportionate, but I will run one if a reviewer wants it.

## Not included / known limitations

- **The AITER tile fix is a runtime patch**, not a vLLM change. It modifies a
  third-party package and does not survive an AITER upgrade. The durable fix
  is upstream in ROCm/aiter, deriving `block_k` from `_LDS_CAP_BYTES`. Its
  constants are tuned to K3's two GEMM shapes; the `n <= 1024` split is a
  coarse proxy that lands on both measured optima but is not a general
  autotuner.
- **Speculative decoding on gfx942 with <16 heads is untested.** Gating the
  Gluon multi-token branch means that case now falls through to the padded
  path. It is dormant for K3 (`num_nextn_predict_layers=0`), but anyone
  enabling MTP/EAGLE3 would be on an unvalidated causality path.
- **`AITER_SITUV2_A8W4` is ignored by the new Triton path.** The CK branch
  reads it to select a gate/up-interleaved layout; the Triton path always
  assumes separated. Default-off, but a silent trap if set.
- **No tuned MoE configs for MI325X** at K3's shapes
  (`E=896,N=384,device_name=AMD_Instinct_MI325X.json` is absent).
- `AITER_MXFP4_FP8` (W4A8) remains gfx950-only — it needs the CDNA4 swizzle.

## Operational notes for anyone serving Kimi-K3 on MI325X

Two traps that look like model corruption and are not:

- **`max_num_seqs` must stay below the Mamba/KDA state block count.** K3 has
  69 KDA layers and needs one state block per concurrent decode sequence, so
  the default 1024 fails CUDA graph capture at 854 available blocks.
- **The `kimi_k3` reasoning parser strips the think channel on its closing
  marker.** If `max_tokens` truncates before that marker, raw chain-of-thought
  is returned as `content` instead of an answer. Combined with the template's
  `thinking_effort=max` default this reads as garbage output.

Measured tool-call emission, 6 trials per cell:

| schema | default (max) | low | high | thinking off |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1-param | 6/6 | 6/6 | 6/6 | 0/6 |
| 2-param | 3/6 | 6/6 | 6/6 | 3/6 |
| 3-param | 6/6 | 6/6 | 6/6 | 0/6 |

`thinking_effort: low` is 18/18 and ~3.5x cheaper in tokens than the default.
`thinking: false` must not be used with tools.

title: [Bugfix] Shard UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs block table width under DCP
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #50825.

`UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` never overrode `max_num_blocks_per_req`, so it used the base `cdiv(max_len, block_size)` while `AttentionSpec` divides by `decode_context_parallel_size`. The two sides that must agree read different specs:

- the runner sizes the block table from the **group** spec (`gpu_model_runner.py`, `may_reinitialize_input_batch`), which for DSA models is `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` — not DCP-sharded;
- metadata builders are constructed from the **per-layer** spec (`worker/utils.py`, `create_metadata_builders` → `get_block_table_width`), which is `MLAAttentionSpec` — DCP-sharded.

Under DCP the block table is therefore `dcp_world_size` times wider than the indexer's `expanded_block_table_buffer`, and decode dies in `mla/indexer.py`:

```
RuntimeError: The expanded size of the tensor (8192) must match the existing size (16384)
at non-singleton dimension 1.  Target sizes: [30, 8192].  Tensor sizes: [30, 16384]
```

Reported by @Leoyzen on GLM-5.2, TP8/DCP2, `fp8_ds_mla`, MTP: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50302#issuecomment-5161430855

The gap predates #50302 and is not the alignment part it fixed: before #50302 the indexer buffer was sized with `get_kv_cache_shard_count()`, which is also DCP-sharded, so the same asymmetry existed. The new `gpu/model_runner.py` divides by `dcp_size` explicitly and is unaffected; only the classic runner path hits this. #48404 worked around the symptom by reallocating the buffer.

Delegating to the merged specs fixes the crash and also stops the runner from allocating a block table `dcp_world_size` times wider than needed.

Not a duplicate: #46794 fixes the same symptom from a different cause (`InputBatch` not rebuilt after `max_model_len` is auto-reduced), #43970's alignment part is superseded by #50302, and neither touches the DCP sharding of the group spec.

## Test

`tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_uniform_type_spec_block_table_width_is_dcp_sharded` — asserts the group spec and the per-layer spec return the same DCP-sharded width.

Verified fail→pass on an 4×H200 box (CPU-only test, run inside a vLLM container):

```
python3 -m pytest test_uniform_type_spec_block_table_width_is_dcp_sharded -q
# before: AssertionError: assert 64 == 32
# after:  1 passed
```

This change is config-level only and does not affect model output; no eval run.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for this work; all changes reviewed.

title: [Bug]: expanded_block_table_buffer width mismatch in the DSA indexer under DCP
body:
### Your current environment

GLM-5.2, TP8, `--decode-context-parallel-size 2`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, MTP. Reported by @Leoyzen on 0.26.1rc1 (post-#50302): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50302#issuecomment-5161430855

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Decode crashes in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`:

```
RuntimeError: The expanded size of the tensor (8192) must match the existing size (16384)
at non-singleton dimension 1.  Target sizes: [30, 8192].  Tensor sizes: [30, 16384]
```

`UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` does not override `max_num_blocks_per_req`, so it falls back to `cdiv(max_len, block_size)` while `AttentionSpec` divides by `decode_context_parallel_size`. The runner sizes the block table from the group spec (`may_reinitialize_input_batch`), the metadata builders are constructed from the per-layer spec (`create_metadata_builders`), so under DCP the block table is `dcp_world_size` times wider than the indexer's buffer. DSA models are affected because their indexer and MLA layers merge into one uniform-type group.

Predates #50302 and is a separate issue from the alignment it fixed. The new `gpu/model_runner.py` divides by `dcp_size` explicitly and is not affected. Same symptom, different causes: #46794 (InputBatch not rebuilt after `max_model_len` is auto-reduced), #43970 (alignment, superseded by #50302).

Fix: #50823.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the docs chatbot in the [vLLM documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/) for help.

title: [Bug]: DSpark speculative decoding causes FlashMLA kernel assertion errors on DeepSeek-V4-Pro with both TP=8 and DP=8+EP
body:
# [Bug]: DSpark speculative decoding causes FlashMLA kernel assertion errors on DeepSeek-V4-Pro with both TP=8 and DP=8+EP

## Your current environment

- **vLLM version**: 0.26.0
- **GPU**: 8× NVIDIA H200 (275GB each)
- **Model**: DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1.6T parameters, FP8 quantized, DSpark variant)
- **OS**: Linux
- **Python**: 3.12
- **PyTorch**: 2.x with CUDA

## 🐛 Describe the bug

When deploying DeepSeek-V4-Pro with DSpark speculative decoding, the server crashes with **FlashMLA kernel assertion errors** during prefill. We observed **two distinct FlashMLA errors** across different parallelism configurations:

### Error 1: DP=8+EP — tensormap creation failure

With `--data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel`, the crash occurs at `host.h:140`:

```
Failed to create tensormap
Dim: 5
Assertion `false` failed (/workspace/.deps/flashmla-src/csrc/kerutils/include/kerutils/host/host.h:140)
```

**Stack trace:**
```
Worker_DP4_EP4 pid=XXXXX ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1007]
  File "vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py", line 333, in __call__
  File "vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py", line 423, in _replay
  File "vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py", line 214, in replay
  File "vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py", line 115, in <lambda>
```

After the assertion failure, rank4 crashes, causing NCCL TCPStore broken pipe errors across all ranks:
```
[rank4]:[W] ProcessGroupNCCL.cpp:1826 Failed to check the "should dump" flag on TCPStore,
  (maybe TCPStore server has shut down too early), with error: Broken pipe
```

### Error 2: TP=8 — TMA descriptor initialization failure

With `--tensor-parallel-size 8` and DSpark, the crash occurs at `phase1.cuh:651` in the sparse prefill path:

```
Error: Failed to initialize the TMA descriptor
Assertion `res == CUresult::CUDA_SUCCESS` failed
  (/workspace/.deps/flashmla-src/csrc/sm100/prefill/sparse/fwd/head64/instantiations/../phase1.cuh:651)
```

**Stack trace:**
```
Worker_TP2 pid=101592 ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1007]
  File "vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py", line 126, in forward_mqa
  File "vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py", line 339, in _forward_prefill
  File "vllm/third_party/flashmla/flash_mla_interface.py", line 217, in flash_mla_sparse_fwd
RuntimeError: Assertion error (...phase1.cuh:651): Assertion `res == CUresult::CUDA_SUCCESS` failed.
```

Multiple workers (TP2, TP6, etc.) crash simultaneously.

### Common pattern

Both errors:
- Occur in the **FlashMLA sparse prefill** path (`flash_mla_sparse_fwd`)
- Are triggered by **DSpark speculative decoding**
- Are **deterministic** — prefill=256 and prefill=512 work fine, but prefill=1024 always crashes
- **Do not occur** without DSpark (non-DSpark mode with prefill=1024 works correctly)

## To Reproduce

### Configuration 1: DP=8+EP

```bash
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE", "custom_ops":["all"]}' \
  --attention_config.use_fp4_indexer_cache=True \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}'
```

### Configuration 2: TP=8

```bash
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE", "custom_ops":["all"]}' \
  --attention_config.use_fp4_indexer_cache=True \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}'
```

### Trigger the crash

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "/path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "<1024+ tokens of text>"}],
    "max_tokens": 128
  }'
```

## Expected behavior

DSpark speculative decoding should work with prefill sequences >= 1024 tokens without crashing, same as non-DSpark mode.

## Benchmark Results

### dp8_ep (without DSpark) — all configs pass ✅

| Config | TTFT P50 | TBT P50 | E2E P50 | Success |
|--------|----------|---------|---------|---------|
| prefill=256, QPS=2 | 54.5ms | 17.8ms | 88.3ms | 20/20 |
| prefill=512, QPS=1 | 61.7ms | 18.3ms | 95.8ms | 10/10 |
| prefill=512, QPS=2 | 53.9ms | 18.0ms | 87.8ms | 20/20 |
| prefill=512, QPS=5 | 71.5ms | 16.0ms | 103.4ms | 30/30 |
| prefill=1024, QPS=2 | 82.0ms | 14.9ms | 113.5ms | 20/20 |

### dp8_ep_dspark (with DSpark) — crashes on prefill=1024 ❌

| Config | TTFT P50 | TBT P50 | E2E P50 | Success |
|--------|----------|---------|---------|---------|
| prefill=256, QPS=2 | 173.6ms | 21.5ms | 195.2ms | 20/20 |
| prefill=512, QPS=1 | 556.3ms | 21.8ms | 577.6ms | 10/10 |
| prefill=512, QPS=2 | 229.8ms | 23.3ms | 253.5ms | 20/20 |
| prefill=512, QPS=5 | 93.6ms | 22.6ms | 121.6ms | 30/30 |
| prefill=1024, QPS=2 | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | 0/20 |

## Additional context

- The crash is specific to **DSpark + prefill >= 1024**. Without DSpark, prefill=1024 works fine in both TP and DP configurations.
- **Error 1** (`host.h:140`): `Failed to create tensormap, Dim: 5` — tensormap creation fails when the tensor dimension is 5, likely due to an unsupported shape combination from DSpark speculative tokens + MLA attention.
- **Error 2** (`phase1.cuh:651`): `Failed to initialize the TMA descriptor` — TMA descriptor initialization fails in the sparse prefill kernel, suggesting the kernel doesn't handle the input shape produced by DSpark's speculative token expansion.
- Both errors occur in `flash_mla_sparse_fwd`, indicating the sparse attention path in FlashMLA is incompatible with DSpark's speculative decoding for longer prefill sequences.
- The crash likely relates to the combination of DSpark's speculative tokens (7) + long prefill (1024) + FP8 quantization + MLA attention with FP4 indexer cache.
- The model uses Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) architecture with hybrid attention (CSA/HCA/Sliding Window), which may interact with the FlashMLA kernel in unexpected ways when combined with speculative decoding.

title: [Bugfix] Bound tile-local argmax to vocab_size in samplers
body:
## Summary

The sampling kernels reduce over a `BLOCK_SIZE`-wide tile of the logits row and
form the token id as `block_idx * BLOCK_SIZE + idx`. The out-of-vocab tail lanes
of the last tile are loaded as `-inf`, so when every in-vocab lane of that tile
is also `-inf`, the reduction can settle on a tail lane and emit
`token_id >= vocab_size`.

Nothing downstream bounds a sampled token id.

Three sites share the pattern:

| Site | Path |
|---|---|
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/gumbel.py` | non-greedy sampling |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler_utils.py` (`_compute_local_logits_stats_kernel`) | greedy |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler_utils.py` (resample) | recovered-token resampling |

## Impact

On most models the bad id is absorbed by `VocabParallelEmbedding`, which masks
out-of-range ids to a zero embedding — so it degrades silently into a garbage
output token rather than failing loudly.

On DeepSeek-V4 it is fatal. The hash-MoE router indexes
`tid2eid[token_id * topk]` directly; an out-of-vocab id reads past the
`[vocab_size, topk]` table and the resulting garbage expert id faults the
context on **every** rank with a Warp MMU fault.

## Evidence

Reproduced in production on DeepSeek-V4-Flash (TP2, expert parallelism,
speculative decoding) under bursty concurrency, in 90 s – 5.5 min.

`vocab_size` is 129280, which is not a multiple of the 8192 tile, so the last
tile has 1792 masked lanes. The emitted id was exactly

    15 * 8192 + 6400 == 129280

i.e. the first out-of-vocab lane of the last tile. A check on `input_ids` right
after `combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens` reported this on real scheduled rows
(not cudagraph padding) at ~78 occurrences/minute; after the fix, 0 over a
40-minute run at the same load.

**What I could not reproduce synthetically.** I have not built a minimal input
that makes the argmax select a tail lane. Feeding a fully `-inf` row, or a fully
NaN row, does not do it (they select lane 0 and the last lane of tile 0
respectively). So the exact condition that steers `idx` onto the first
out-of-vocab lane is not established, and I would rather say so than invent a
mechanism.

What is established is the causal link, via a clean A/B under identical
production load:

| Clamped sites | out-of-range `input_ids` |
|---|---|
| none | ~78/min |
| `gumbel.py` only | 4 over ~15 min |
| all three | **0 over 30 min** (1322 requests) |

The middle row is what identified the greedy rejection-sampler site as the
active path.

## Fix

Clamp the tile-local argmax to `vocab_size - 1`. In a fully `-inf` tile no
in-vocab lane is a valid answer anyway, so any index is equally arbitrary — the
clamp only guarantees the result is addressable.

## Test

No unit test: as noted above I could not construct a synthetic input that
reproduces the tail-lane selection, and I did not want to ship a test that passes
with and without the fix. Validation is the end-to-end A/B table above, plus a
30-minute randomized-concurrency run with zero faults where the same load
previously killed the engine in 90 s - 5.5 min.

If a reviewer knows the condition that steers the tile argmax off the end, I am
happy to add a focused test for it.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4] Bound token_id before the tid2eid gather in hash-MoE routing
body:
## Summary

DeepSeek-V4's hash-MoE routing kernels read a token's expert ids straight out of
the lookup table:

```cpp
const int64_t token_id = load_index_as_int64(input_ids, warp);
...
expert = static_cast<int>(tid2eid[token_id * 6 + lane]);
const float x = input[warp * num_experts + expert];
```

`token_id` is data, not a loop bound, and `tid2eid` is `[vocab_size, topk]`.
There is no bound on it. An out-of-range token id gathers outside the table,
yields a garbage expert id, and that id is then used to index the gating logits
and is stored into `topk_ids` for the downstream MoE kernels — an illegal access
that takes down every TP rank.

## Evidence

Hit in production on DeepSeek-V4-Flash (TP2 + `--enable-expert-parallel`).
CUDA core dump, both ranks:

```
CUDA Exception: Warp MMU Fault
errorpc  vllm::moe::dsv4HashTopkSoftplusSqrt<int,int>
```

SASS at `errorpc` shows the chain explicitly:

```
LDG.E R7,[R10.64]        ; R7 = tid2eid[token_id*6 + lane]  -> "expert"
IMAD  R13,R2,UR6,R7      ; R13 = warp*num_experts + expert
IMAD.WIDE R8,R13,0x4,R8  ; addr = input + R13*4
*> LDG.E R8,[R8.64]      ; <-- FAULT

R7 = 0xD9E366E0 = 3655558880
```

`R7` is the value that came *out of* `tid2eid` — i.e. the table was read out of
bounds, and the "expert" is the bit pattern of a neighbouring tensor.

The out-of-range `token_id` came from the sampler emitting an id equal to
`vocab_size`, fixed separately in the sampler by bounding the tile-local argmax (#50843).

## Fix

Bound `token_id` against the table's row count, threaded from `tid2eid.size(0)`,
in both kernels that perform the gather (`dsv4HashTopkSoftplusSqrt` and the
generic `topkGatingSoftplusSqrt` `USE_HASH` path). Out-of-range ids fall into the
existing `is_pad_row` path, so the token routes to nothing rather than to a
garbage expert.

This is worth keeping independently of the sampler fix: `prompt_token_ids` arrive
from the API, so the kernel should not assume a token id is in range.

## Test

Covered end-to-end: with the sampler fix reverted, this bound converts a
guaranteed engine kill into a skipped token slot. A focused unit test needs a
`tid2eid` fixture and is easier to add alongside the DSv4 kernel tests — happy to
add one if reviewers prefer.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Bound expert_map gathers on data-derived expert ids
body:
## Summary

Four MoE kernels index `expert_map` with an expert id taken from `topk_ids`,
guarding the gather with a sign check only (`expert_id >= 0` / `expert_id < 0`).
`topk_ids` is data, not a loop bound: the routers allocate it with
`torch.empty` and do not always overwrite every slot, so a stale slot can hold
an arbitrary positive value. When that happens the gather reads far past the
end of `expert_map` and the context dies with a Warp MMU fault on **every** rank.

`get_local_expert_id()` in `csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/moe_align_sum_kernels.cu`
already applies exactly the missing bound:

```cpp
int expert_id = topk_ids[idx];
if (expert_id >= num_experts || expert_id < 0) {
  return -1;
}
```

This PR makes the other four consumers consistent with it. Out-of-range ids
fall out as not-routed, so a producer bug degrades one token slot instead of
killing the engine.

## Relationship to the root cause

These gathers were the *victims*, not the cause. The garbage expert ids
originated upstream: the sampler could emit a token id equal to `vocab_size`,
and DeepSeek-V4's hash-MoE router turned that into a garbage expert id by
gathering past its lookup table. Both are fixed separately in #50843 (sampler) and #50844 (DSv4 hash router). This PR is the
defence-in-depth layer — it keeps a producer bug anywhere upstream from
escalating into an engine kill, and it fixes one gather that was unguarded
outright.

## Evidence

Hit in production on DeepSeek-V4-Flash (TP2 + `--enable-expert-parallel`,
so `expert_map` is non-null), reproducible under bursty concurrency in
90 s – 5 min. CUDA core dump, both TP ranks:

```
CUDA Exception: Warp MMU Fault
errorpc  _swiglu_limit_pad_aware_kernel
         vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/utils.py:545
```

SASS at `errorpc` is the `expert_map` gather, and the index register holds the
bad id:

```
IMAD.SHL.U32 R6,R4,0x4,RZ     ; expert_id * 4
IADD.64      R6,R6,R8         ; expert_map_ptr + expert_id*4
@!P0 BRA ...                  ; skip if !(expert_id >= 0)
*> LDG.E R8,desc[UR10][R6.64] ; <-- FAULT

R4 = 0x66E65F78 = 1726373752
R4 = 0x3F988A43 = 1066961475   (as float32: 1.1917)
```

The model has 256 experts. Both observed ids are float bit patterns — the
allocation's previous tenant — which is what an unwritten `torch.empty` slot
looks like.

Bounding only the Triton kernel moved the fault to `moe_sum_vec_kernel`
(`moe_sum_pad_aware_skip`, same unguarded pattern), which is why all four
sites are fixed together.

Note `moe_fused_mul_sum_kernel`'s gather was not merely missing an upper
bound — it was entirely unmasked, with no sign check either, so it would also
fault on the ordinary `-1` unrouted sentinel on any model taking that path.

## Changes

- `csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/moe_align_sum_kernels.cu` — `moe_sum_pad_aware_skip()`
  bounds `expert_id` against `num_experts`, threaded through the vec / dynamic /
  scalar `moe_sum` kernels from `expert_map->numel()`.
- `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/utils.py` — `_swiglu_limit_pad_aware_kernel()`
  and `_count_expert_num_tokens()` bound the gather.
- `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/moe_fused_mul_sum.py` —
  `moe_fused_mul_sum_kernel()` bounds the gather (it was previously entirely
  unmasked).

No legitimate id is rejected: valid ids live in `[0, expert_map.numel())` by
construction, which is the new bound.

`gpt_oss_triton_kernels_moe.py` already clamps its gather and is unchanged.

## Test

Three regression tests, each feeding the observed `0x3F988A43` bit pattern and a
generic far-out-of-range id through the guarded path:

- `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py::test_moe_sum_pad_aware_bounds_expert_map_gather`
- `tests/kernels/core/test_activation.py::test_swiglu_limit_pad_aware_bounds_expert_map_gather`
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_count_expert_num_tokens.py::test_count_expert_num_tokens_bounds_expert_map_gather`

Without the fix these fault the CUDA context; with it they assert the
out-of-range slots are skipped and the in-range results are unchanged.

title: [Bug][Spec Decode] DSpark speculative decoding broken on H200 nightly
body:
## Summary

DSpark speculative decoding (`method: "dspark"`) is non-functional on current main. Multiple code paths assume only `"dflash"` when DSpark reuses the same proposer/speculator infrastructure (`DSparkSpeculator` extends `DFlashSpeculator`, both use `DFlashProposer`). The result is that DSpark either crashes at startup or produces wrong results at inference time.

Tested on GLM-5.2-FP8 (753B MoE) with `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark` on multi-node Wide-EP H200 clusters.

## Bugs

### 1. `use_dflash()` excludes DSpark — model runner never creates `DFlashProposer`

**File:** `vllm/config/speculative.py` (line ~1395)

```python
def use_dflash(self) -> bool:
    return self.method == "dflash"  # BUG: excludes "dspark"
```

`use_dspark()` exists (line ~1398) but is never checked in the model runner's drafter initialization elif chain (`gpu_model_runner.py`). DSpark falls through without getting `DFlashProposer` or `use_aux_hidden_state_outputs = True`, so the target model doesn't extract multi-layer aux hidden states.

**Fix:** `return self.method in ("dflash", "dspark")`

### 2. `DFlashProposer.__init__` asserts `method == "dflash"`

**File:** `vllm/v1/spec_decode/dflash.py`

```python
assert vllm_config.speculative_config.method == "dflash"
```

Even after fixing #1, this assert rejects DSpark at proposer creation time.

**Fix:** `assert method in ("dflash", "dspark")`

### 3. `llm_base_proposer.py` missing "dspark" in method lists

**File:** `vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py`

Three locations where DSpark needs to be included alongside DFlash:

- **`model_returns_tuple()`** (~line 1015): exclusion list `("mtp", "draft_model", "dflash")` missing `"dspark"` → `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)` at line ~591
- **`combine_hidden_states` gate** (~line 526): inclusion list `("eagle3", "dflash")` missing `"dspark"` → aux hidden states not combined for the drafter
- **`parallel_drafting_token_id` ValueError** — raises for unknown method instead of setting a default for DSpark

### 4. FA3 AOT scheduler head count mismatch (separate PR)

Already addressed in #50694 — the FA3 AOT scheduler reads head counts from the target model config, but the draft model may have a different GQA ratio.

## Error Traces

### Without any hotfixes — `model_returns_tuple` crash:
```
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)
  File "vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py", line 591
```

### After adding "dspark" to `model_returns_tuple` but not fixing routing — `combine_hidden_states` dimension mismatch:
```
ValueError: DFlash drafter expects 30720 concatenated aux hidden features but received 6144
  File "vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py", line 761
  File "vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py", line 536
```
(30720 = 5 layers × 6144 hidden_size — target model only outputs last hidden state because `use_aux_hidden_state_outputs` was never set)

## Environment

- vLLM nightly (`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`, v0.26.1rc1.dev255)
- Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` + `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark`
- Config: `--speculative-config {"model":"...","num_speculative_tokens":5,"method":"dspark"}`
- Multi-node Wide-EP with H200 GPUs, DP=16, EP enabled

title: [RFC]: Complete Model Runner V2 pipeline parallelism: scheduling, speculative decoding, and PP-first DP/EP topology
body:
### Motivation.

> [!NOTE]
> This RFC expands the original request-admission proposal into an end-to-end plan for Model Runner V2 (MRV2) pipeline-parallel feature composition. The original proposal remains Workstream A below, with its prototype in #50410.

MRV2 pipeline parallelism (PP) already overlaps multiple batches to reduce pipeline bubbles (#42187). With asynchronous scheduling, it keeps `pp_size + 1` batch slots in flight, while a decode request becomes eligible again after a `pp_size`-step cadence.

That foundation works for basic generation, but the surrounding features do not yet compose cleanly with PP:

| Area | Current state | Gap addressed by this RFC |
|---|---|---|
| Request scheduling | Basic MRV2 PP works | A burst can fill the global request slots in one batch and leave later PP batches empty |
| MTP speculative decoding | Work is in progress | Drafts produced and applied locally on the last rank must be published to non-last ranks and restored for the still-live rows of the stored step-`T` feedback slot |
| EAGLE3, DFlash, and DSpark | Explicitly rejected with PP in MRV2 today | Auxiliary hidden states may be produced on earlier ranks but are consumed by the proposer on the last rank |
| Index-sharing models | Rank-local buffers work when producer and consumer are colocated | A PP cut may fall between an index producer and a layer that reuses its top-k indices |
| PP + DP/EP topology | Current deployments commonly place complete DP replicas contiguously | On multiple nodes this tends to keep PP local while DP/EP groups cross nodes; a PP-first placement should keep EP/TP inside a node and move PP traffic across nodes |

The common theme is that PP is not only a partition of model layers. It also creates two state-transfer paths with different direction and lifetime:

1. **forward state**, sent from one PP rank to the next for the current microbatch; and
2. **deferred result state**, applied locally on the last rank and published to non-last ranks, which consume the stored `PPHandler` FIFO slot `pp_size` local feedback-ring steps later.

Adding each new tensor with one-off communication code would make ordering, CUDA-graph capture, request-slot reuse, and multi-node topology assumptions increasingly fragile. This RFC therefore proposes both the missing feature support and a small declarative PP transport abstraction that can carry future optional state without redesigning the execution loop each time.

#### Goals

- Balance request admission across concurrent MRV2 PP batches.
- Define correct MRV2 PP composition with MTP, EAGLE3, DFlash, and DSpark speculative decoding.
- Carry auxiliary hidden states and cross-partition index-sharing state when a model partition requires them.
- Define a PP-first multi-node placement in which each node hosts one complete PP stage's DP/EP domain, keeping EP/TP communication intra-node and PP communication inter-node.
- Keep optional communication absent when a model or configuration does not need it.
- Preserve static, graph-friendly buffer schemas and minimize extra collectives.

#### Non-goals

- Changing Model Runner V1.
- Introducing a new speculative decoding algorithm.
- Redesigning DP request routing, real/dummy execution cadence, or wave draining, or migrating live request/KV state between DP lanes.
- Introducing a new pipeline schedule such as interleaved 1F1B.
- Requiring every model to emit auxiliary hidden states or index buffers.
- Enabling adaptive verification with PP in the first rollout; it needs a separate protocol for trimmed shapes, confidence/cost state, and rank agreement.
- Supporting a PP-stage DP/EP footprint that cannot fit in a node-local topology domain in the first rollout.

### Proposed Change.

Implement the RFC as four independently reviewable workstreams over one set of communication and correctness invariants.

```text
                    current-microbatch forward plane
  scheduler  ->  PP rank 0  ->  ...  ->  PP rank N (sample + propose)
                    | IntermediateTensors | aux hidden states | shared indices |
                    |
                    +<---------- deferred result plane ----------+
                       sampled/count metadata and optional drafts
                       (queued in the worker-side PPHandler feedback FIFO)

  PP-first multi-node placement:

  node 0 / PP stage 0: [DP0 ... DPN]  <- EP/TP stays node-local
                              |  PP lanes  |
  node 1 / PP stage 1: [DP0 ... DPN]  <- EP/TP stays node-local
```

#### Workstream A: balance request admission across PP batches

Within each scheduler/DP replica, the scheduler currently applies `max_num_seqs` as one global running-request limit and greedily fills a batch until an existing token, sequence, KV-cache, or model-specific constraint is reached. A burst of short, uniform requests can therefore consume all local request slots before the pipeline has formed multiple useful batches.

For example:

```text
pipeline_parallel_size = 2
max_num_seqs = 25
50 short requests arrive together
```

The current scheduler can produce `25, 0, 25, 0` scheduled requests over four steps. The prototype in #50410 instead caps the next batch at:

```python
num_requests = min(
    max_num_running_reqs,
    get_num_unfinished_requests(),
)
max_num_scheduled_reqs = ceil(num_requests / pp_size)
```

The prototype applies the cap to both requests already in `RUNNING` and admissions from `WAITING`, while all existing token, KV-cache, priority, preemption, structured-output, and model-specific constraints remain authoritative. In the example, the first two useful batches become approximately `13, 12` instead of `25, 0`.

The divisor is `pp_size`, not `pp_size + 1`: the additional asynchronous queue entry covers result propagation and scheduler/worker overlap rather than an additional compute stage. Non-final chunked-prefill chunks remain eligible in adjacent steps because they do not depend on sampled-token feedback.

This is intentionally a PP batch target, not a claim that request count always equals compute. Request count is a useful decode proxy; scheduled tokens are a better prefill proxy.

The proposed MVP differs from the current prototype in one important respect: already-eligible `RUNNING` decode keeps its existing scheduling behavior, while the balance target is a soft cap on **new/resumed admission from `WAITING`**. The target may be exceeded when later phases have no runnable work, at low concurrency, at a KV/capacity boundary, or to prevent priority starvation. This preserves work conservation and avoids delaying active decode solely to make phase widths look uniform.

Every DP replica computes this target locally. Evaluation should decide whether the final policy is request-count based, token based, or hybrid, and whether a persistent phase assignment is worth its complexity around completion, abort, preemption, resume, and priority changes.

#### Workstream B: make PP state transport extensible

Refactor PP state ownership into a small declarative module. `PPTransport`, `ForwardPayload`, and `DeferredResultPayload` below are conceptual names, not a required public API.

One ownership module describes two independent schemas and communicators:

**1. Forward payload: adjacent rank -> adjacent rank, current microbatch**

- opaque model `IntermediateTensors` such as `hidden_states` and `residual`;
- namespaced sidecars for auxiliary hidden states keyed by a global activation-boundary ID and configured slot;
- a namespaced active top-k/index sidecar when the partition boundary crosses an index-reuse dependency.

**2. Deferred result payload: last PP rank -> every non-last PP rank, delayed receiver slot**

- sampled tokens;
- sampled/rejected-token counts;
- optional next-step draft tokens;
- local queued request mappings and generation metadata that associate the received rows with still-live request slots (these do not need to be network fields).

Each adjacent forward edge has its own field/liveness plan; the existing `PPHandler` sibling broadcast has one group-consistent feedback plan. They share descriptor and lifecycle machinery but not communicator, stream, cadence, or participant set. A conceptual field descriptor is:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PPTensorSpec:
    name: str
    plane: Literal["forward", "deferred_result"]
    boundary_id: int | None
    slot: int | None
    dtype: torch.dtype
    trailing_shape: tuple[int, ...]
    tp_policy: Literal["replicated", "sharded", "direct"]
    carry: Literal[
        "one_edge", "until_last", "until_consumed", "feedback_group"
    ]
    lifetime: Literal["forward_execution", "delayed_request_state"]
```

The exact fields can differ. The correctness MVP should run the declared plan over the existing tensor-dict path:

- namespace and split opaque model tensors from optional sidecars;
- keep each edge's field presence, key, dtype, slot ordering, carry policy, and TP policy deterministic after initialization;
- export/import sidecars through model-specific adapters;
- retain current tensor-dict metadata and allocation behavior where required for backend compatibility;
- stream/event ownership and buffer reuse centralized in the transport module;
- request generation/slot checks retained for delayed feedback, so an aborted or replaced request cannot consume stale state;
- group-identical feedback row order, row count, dtype/shape, collective order, and whole-collective skip decisions; no branch on rank-local optional-field presence;
- optional fields disabled add no bytes or collectives beyond the existing forward and sampled/count feedback paths.

For forward sidecars, `N` means the execution row count after padding (`num_tokens_after_padding` / the batch execution descriptor), not only logical scheduled tokens. Buffers and wire shapes use `N`; adapters separately track which rows contain real tokens.

For the initial models in this RFC, auxiliary hidden states are TP-replicated, and shared top-k is TP-replicated `[N, index_topk]` `torch.int32`. Existing model tensors such as sequence-parallel residual state retain their direct/sharded policy. Because the current tensor-dict path may automatically slice/all-gather based on tensor size, sidecar policy must be explicit rather than inferred from divisibility.

Model-specific adapters should declare which sidecars a partition boundary needs, export locally produced fields, and import received fields into the correct persistent model buffer. The communication layer should not interpret EAGLE, DSpark, or model-specific index semantics. Namespaced wire keys such as `model/*`, `spec/aux_hidden_states`, and `model/shared_index_topk` can avoid collisions while keeping ordinary model tensors opaque.

A later performance phase may compile a static wire schema, use persistent graph-address-stable receive buffers, and remove per-step CPU metadata. That requires explicit lower-level `GroupCoordinator`/backend protocol work and is not implied by adding the correctness wrapper.

Compatible small fields should be packed when doing so removes latency-sensitive collectives, following the direction explored in draft #47686. Large auxiliary tensors should not be blindly packed with token metadata: grouping must respect direction, dtype, destination, lifetime, TP layout, and performance. The abstraction is unified at the ownership/schema layer, while the two data planes remain separate internally.

#### Workstream C: compose PP with speculative decoding

##### C1. Base MTP draft-feedback synchronization

Under MRV2 asynchronous scheduling, scheduler-side speculative token IDs are shape placeholders: their authoritative values remain in per-worker GPU request state. The speculative proposer runs on the last PP rank. Every stage's sampled/draft/sequence bookkeeping must nevertheless describe the same logical token sequence: the first stage materializes the correct sampled-plus-draft token IDs, while later stages consume the corresponding forward activations and attention metadata.

Here `pp_feedback_step` means a local worker execute/control step that advances the `PPHandler` FIFO. It is not an EngineCore asynchronous batch-queue slot and is not advanced by a MoE DP dummy forward.

#52295 implements the narrow synchronization piece. The last rank applies sampled state locally in feedback step `T`, runs proposal, retains its new draft state, and then publishes one feedback record to non-last ranks. The token wire payload is fixed at `[B, (K + 1) + K] = [B, 2K + 1]` (`int64` sampled plus draft columns), while the existing `[2, B]` (`int32`) sampled/rejected count collective remains. Draft synchronization therefore adds `K` token-ID columns per request but no new collective.

Each non-last rank posts the matching receive in feedback step `T`, queues it with the saved row mapping, need mask, and slot-generation snapshot, and applies the surviving rows at feedback step `T + pp_size`. Sampled and draft rows use the same liveness/generation decision; invalid draft rows are compacted before index-copy because a `-1` destination is not valid for that operation. The association comes from FIFO feedback-step order and the saved step-`T` metadata, not from the composition of the current batch at `T + pp_size`.

The required invariant is:

> The last stage applies its sampling outcome and derived next-step drafts locally in feedback step `T` and publishes them as one causally consistent record. Every non-last stage posts the matching receive in step `T` and applies the stored live rows at feedback step `T + pp_size`, before that request's next verification input is prepared.

#52295 should be treated as the base transport/state-synchronization change, not as the complete enablement of every MTP model. Its transport gate is PP plus any speculative configuration that has already passed validation, so this feedback mechanism should not be duplicated per speculative method. Broader model-specific work in #46994 includes PP capability declarations, model-specific projection paths, weight/embedding ownership, and a same-rank stale sparse-MLA buffer-reference fix. Those requirements should either land with the affected model or be guarded by an explicit support check; the same-rank buffer fix is distinct from the cross-rank dependency in C3.

Fixed wire width also needs an explicit validity/padding protocol for a normal `[B, 1]` no-draft or prefill sampler source; `num_sampled` determines which sampled columns are valid. Existing #52295 coverage consists of two CPU/mock tests for payload splitting/event waiting and draft slot writeback. Real multi-rank communication, fixed-width send/receive, `T -> T + pp_size`, partial abort/reuse, and mixed prefill/decode are merge/enablement criteria, not established behavior. Delaying broadcast until after proposal may also change overlap, so validation must include TPOT and proposer latency.

##### C2. EAGLE3, DFlash, and DSpark auxiliary hidden states

These methods require auxiliary target-model hidden states during proposal. MRV2 currently rejects EAGLE3, DFlash, and DSpark with PP before execution. If those guards were simply removed, each rank would capture only its local auxiliary outputs and a non-last rank would return ordinary `IntermediateTensors` without carrying those outputs, so the proposer on the last rank would still see incomplete state.

For a configured set of auxiliary layers:

1. normalize each capture point to a global **activation-boundary ID** (`0` for the state before the first layer and `layer_idx + 1` for the state after that layer), including method-specific `+1` conversions;
2. map boundary IDs to the draft configuration's fixed slot order rather than numerically sorting IDs;
3. when an auxiliary state is produced, add it to the forward payload;
4. carry it through subsequent PP boundaries with `until_last` liveness;
5. combine upstream and last-rank-local states in configured slot order;
6. pass the ordered states to the proposer on the last PP rank.

Auxiliary states are forward dependencies of the current microbatch, not delayed sampled-token feedback. They should therefore use the adjacent-rank forward plane and must not be added to the last-rank-to-non-last-ranks feedback broadcast.

The schema must support zero, one, or multiple auxiliary tensors, and partition tests must cover auxiliary boundaries on the first, middle, and last PP ranks. Implementations that pack compatible states may use a stable `[N, slots, hidden]` layout where `N` is the padded execution row count, but correctness must not depend on all states having identical shapes. Persistent receive/pack buffers are a performance-phase optimization for avoiding per-step allocation and address changes under CUDA graphs.

Transport is necessary but not sufficient to remove the current PP guards. Model-specific enablement must also normalize activation-boundary IDs and target layer counts to global (not stage-local) coordinates, validate draft embedding/head ownership on the last rank, and remove loader-level PP rejections only after the corresponding model path is tested.

##### C3. Index-sharing state across a PP cut

Some models compute top-k routing/index information in one layer and reuse it in later layers. For example, an index-sharing pattern may contain one producing layer followed by layers that skip top-k computation and read a persistent buffer.

If PP cuts between that producer and a consumer in the same reuse interval, a rank-local buffer on the downstream rank has not been populated for the current microbatch. The forward schema must then carry the active top-k buffer across one or more reuse-only stages until it is consumed or overwritten.

At model/partition initialization, dependency analysis should determine whether a boundary crosses an index-reuse interval:

- if it does not, no extra tensor is registered;
- if it does, register the current contract—TP-replicated `[N, index_topk]` `torch.int32`, where `N` is the padded execution row count—and copy it into the downstream persistent shared buffer before model/graph execution;
- tie buffer validity and lifetime to the forward microbatch/transport handle so data cannot leak between in-flight batches;
- allow future model adapters to declare other trailing dimensions or dtypes without weakening this RFC's concrete acceptance contract.

This cross-rank dependency is distinct from the stale-buffer-reference issue addressed by parts of #46994 when draft and target models share an indexer on the same rank. Both must be correct, but only the former requires PP-boundary transport.

As an initial safety fallback, unsupported partitions may fail early with a precise error. The intended final behavior is to transport the dependency rather than permanently constraining PP cuts to index-reuse boundaries.

#### Workstream D: PP-first DP/EP topology for multi-node serving

This workstream is about **physical partition and placement order**, not a new DP load-balancing, dummy-forward, or drain protocol. Each request remains sticky to one logical DP lane, and that lane still traverses one complete PP pipeline. The proposal first assigns nodes to PP stages, then places the stage's DP/EP (and TP, when used) ranks inside that node.

##### D1. Background: why DP-first placement is suboptimal for multi-node MoE

With a conventional DP-first placement, complete DP replicas are packed before moving to the next node. Consider two 8-GPU nodes with `PP=2`, `DP=8`, and `TP=1`:

```text
default physical placement

node 0: DP0{PP0,PP1} DP1{PP0,PP1} DP2{PP0,PP1} DP3{PP0,PP1}
node 1: DP4{PP0,PP1} DP5{PP0,PP1} DP6{PP0,PP1} DP7{PP0,PP1}
```

This keeps several PP pipelines entirely inside a node, but the fixed-PP DP/EP domain spans both nodes. For MoE models, expert dispatch/combine is an all-to-all or all-gather/reduce-scatter style hot path repeated throughout the model. Sending that traffic across the inter-node fabric is substantially more topology-sensitive than keeping it on NVLink/NVSwitch.

PP communication has a different shape: each logical DP lane sends activations across an ordered stage boundary, with small sampled/draft feedback in the reverse PP direction. This traffic is point-to-point or PP-scoped, regular, and can be overlapped with pipeline execution. It is therefore the preferable communication dimension to place across nodes.

##### D2. Proposed PP-first placement

Place one complete PP stage's `DP x PCP x TP` footprint in a node-local topology domain before allocating the next PP stage:

```text
PP-first physical placement

node 0 / PP0: DP0 DP1 DP2 DP3 DP4 DP5 DP6 DP7
                    |   |   |   |   |   |   |   |
                    +--- matching cross-node PP lanes ---+
node 1 / PP1: DP0 DP1 DP2 DP3 DP4 DP5 DP6 DP7
```

The resulting communication placement is:

- `EP(pp)` stays inside the node containing that PP stage;
- `TP(pp, dp, pcp)` also stays inside that stage's node-local domain;
- `PP(dp, pcp, tp)` connects matching coordinates across nodes in stage order;
- PP forward activations, optional sidecars from Workstream B, and small sampled/draft feedback are the steady-state model data that crosses nodes;
- control-plane coordination may still cross nodes and is not the optimization target of this workstream.

The physical placement can be PP-first without changing the logical identity of a DP lane. Scheduler, request, KV-cache, sampling, and speculative state remain owned by that lane; no request or KV state is migrated between DP lanes.

##### D3. Topology contract and scope

The first rollout should target a uniform topology with one complete PP stage per node. Its contract is:

- the stage footprint `DP x PCP x TP` fits completely in one node-local communication domain;
- every EP and TP group is node-local;
- each PP group contains matching `(dp, pcp, tp)` coordinates in increasing stage order;
- every logical worker is placed exactly once, with no duplicated or missing device;
- a requested placement that would spill an EP group across nodes fails before model execution;
- disabling PP-first placement preserves the existing topology.

Multiple complete stage blocks may share a node in a future extension, provided no EP/TP group is split across nodes. A stage footprint larger than one node, heterogeneous partial-stage placement, PCP+DP combinations that are otherwise unsupported, and elastic-EP composition are outside the initial scope.

The existing DP/EP execution-order rules remain unchanged: ranks in a coupled EP domain must still enter model collectives consistently, and an idle logical DP lane still follows the existing dummy-execution behavior. These are compatibility requirements, not the feature proposed here.

#### Cross-cutting correctness invariants

1. **Verification-state agreement:** every PP stage agrees on ordered request rows and logical token/position/spec-verification metadata; the first stage materializes the correct token IDs and downstream stages consume the corresponding stage-local forward state.
2. **Forward-dependency completeness:** the consumer of an auxiliary state or shared index sees the value produced for the same microbatch.
3. **Slot safety:** aborted, preempted, or replaced requests cannot consume delayed state from an earlier slot generation.
4. **Placement completeness:** every logical `(pp, dp, pcp, tp)` worker maps to exactly one physical device, and every selected device has exactly one owner.
5. **Topology locality:** in PP-first mode every EP/TP group is contained in one node-local communication domain, while PP groups connect matching coordinates in stage order.
6. **PP-lane isolation:** PP P2P and optional sidecars stay inside one logical DP lane and follow the per-edge transport plan.
7. **Feedback collective agreement:** every feedback participant uses group-identical row ordering, row count, dtype/shape, collective order, and whole-collective skip decisions for a feedback step.
8. **DP/EP execution compatibility:** changing physical placement does not change existing collective-order, dummy-execution, or execution-shape rules for a coupled EP domain.
9. **State isolation:** request, KV, sampling, and speculative state remain inside one sticky DP lane; PP transfer is not DP migration.
10. **Work conservation:** a soft balance target cannot indefinitely create empty PP phases while runnable work exists, and scheduler safety/fairness constraints take precedence.
11. **Feature transparency:** optional fields disabled add no bytes or collectives beyond the existing PP forward and sampled/count feedback paths; disabling PP-first placement preserves current topology.
12. **MRV1/non-PP compatibility:** this RFC does not change their scheduling or communication semantics.

#### Rollout plan

1. Adapt the request-balancing prototype and scheduler tests from #50410 to the soft, work-conserving `WAITING`-admission MVP, then validate its policy/performance.
2. Introduce the ownership/adapter layer over the existing tensor-dict forward path and `PPHandler` feedback path without changing basic-generation behavior.
3. Land the base MTP draft-state synchronization from #52295, plus model-specific enablement or guards identified by #46994.
4. Add auxiliary-hidden-state descriptors and enable EAGLE3, DFlash, and DSpark model by model.
5. Add partition dependency analysis and cross-rank top-k/index transfer for index-sharing models.
6. Validate the PP-first multi-node topology contract, including node-local EP/TP groups and cross-node PP lanes.
7. Independently evaluate the static-wire/persistent-buffer transport performance phase.

Steps that are independent may proceed in parallel, but every step should preserve the invariants above and keep unsupported combinations behind an early, actionable validation error.

#### Compatibility and initial support limits

- Target and draft model paths must explicitly satisfy PP capability, loader, projection, embedding/head ownership, and partition checks before their guard is removed.
- Adaptive verification plus PP remains unsupported in the initial rollout.
- Existing restrictions such as MRV2 PP with an external launcher, elastic EP with PP, and `PCP > 1` with `DP > 1` remain unchanged unless a separate RFC/PR addresses them.
- `max_num_seqs` remains a per-EngineCore/per-DP-replica limit.
- A draft model without its own embedding/head must either have a validated last-rank loading/aliasing path or fail early when the corresponding target component is a `PPMissingLayer`.
- Initial PP-first support requires a uniform topology in which one complete `DP x PCP x TP` stage footprint fits inside one node-local communication domain.

#### Alternatives considered

1. **Add model-specific tensors directly to each send/receive call.** This is smaller initially but duplicates buffer, ordering, and lifecycle logic and does not scale to the next optional state.
2. **Put every optional tensor in one always-present payload.** This simplifies branching but wastes memory/bandwidth and makes high-volume forward state share an unsuitable lifetime with small delayed token metadata.
3. **Use a separate collective for every field.** Simple semantically, but latency grows with features; #47686 shows why packing small PP feedback fields can matter.
4. **Force PP cuts to dependency boundaries.** Useful as a temporary guard, but reduces partition flexibility and can produce poor memory/compute balance.
5. **Send auxiliary hidden states directly from their producer to the last rank.** This creates a variable communication graph; forwarding through adjacent boundaries keeps ownership and ordering aligned with the existing pipeline.
6. **Keep DP-first physical placement.** This preserves current deployment behavior but can force EP traffic across nodes while underusing PP as the inter-node communication dimension.
7. **Use hierarchical cross-node EP collectives.** This may reduce the penalty but does not provide the same hard node-local EP/TP boundary and remains backend/topology dependent.
8. **Allow arbitrary heterogeneous stage placement immediately.** More flexible, but substantially harder to validate and reason about than a uniform one-stage-per-node first rollout.

#### Evaluation plan

**Correctness matrix**

- PP sizes 2 and 4; DP sizes 1, 2, 4, and 8; TP 1/2 and representative EP configurations;
- synchronous and asynchronous scheduling; eager and compiled/full-CUDA-graph execution;
- no speculation, MTP, EAGLE3, DFlash, and DSpark;
- speculative widths 1, 2, and 3, including no-draft/prefill feedback rows;
- auxiliary layers before, on, and after PP boundaries;
- PP cuts outside and inside an index-reuse interval;
- burst admission, mixed prefill/decode, chunked prefill, preemption, abort storms, pause/resume, and request-slot reuse;
- two 8-GPU nodes with `PP=2, DP=8, TP=1`;
- two 8-GPU nodes with `PP=2, DP=4, TP=2`;
- a representative `PP=4` topology;
- both default DP-first and proposed PP-first physical placements.

The model-level acceptance set should include:

- Llama/Qwen EAGLE3 for global activation-boundary ID and configured-slot ordering;
- DeepSeek V3.2 with a forced PP cut inside a producer-to-reuse interval;
- DeepSeek V4 DSpark for post-mHC-mean auxiliary state;
- Kimi K3 DSpark/EAGLE3 for model-specific attention-residual auxiliary state;
- a draft model without its own embedding/head, covering either the validated last-rank loading path or the expected fail-fast error.

Use synthetic/unit tests for exact transport contents, schema validation, boundary liveness, activation-boundary slot ordering, request generations, and topology membership. Add real multi-rank tests for `T -> T + pp_size` feedback cadence, abort/reuse filtering, fixed-width payloads, forward sidecars, and collective traces. Multi-node tests must collect actual node identities for every PP/DP/EP/TP group and prove that PP-first mode keeps EP/TP node-local. Representative end-to-end models should cover output parity and speculative acceptance; supported configurations should be compared with PP=1 using deterministic inputs where possible. Require no deadlock or collective-order mismatch under timeout/failure-injection tests.

**Performance metrics**

- requests and scheduled tokens per PP batch;
- per-stage idle time and pipeline bubbles;
- throughput, TTFT, and TPOT;
- speculative acceptance rate and proposer latency;
- PP bytes, collective/P2P count, and communication overlap;
- CUDA-graph memory and capture/replay stability;
- inter-node bytes attributed to PP forward/feedback versus EP/TP collectives;
- EP all-to-all latency, PP overlap, node-local GPU utilization, and topology-induced idle time;
- preemption count and KV-cache utilization.

Optional transport disabled should have no material regression against current basic PP. Enabled configurations should be compared both before/after packing so communication optimizations remain evidence-driven.

#### Related work

- MRV2 pipeline bubble reduction and current PP/DP foundation: #42187
- Request-admission balancing prototype: #50410
- Isolated MTP draft-token synchronization: #52295
- Broader MTP-over-PP enablement and model-specific fixes: #46994
- Packed PP sampled/count/draft feedback draft experiment: #47686
- Async scheduling plan: #27679
- Persistent batch redesign: #23446
- Long-context optimized PP RFC: #41685
- Chunked pipeline parallel RFC: #33914

The long-context and chunked-PP RFCs focus on splitting long-context work, asynchronous P2P, and dynamic chunking. This RFC focuses on composing the existing MRV2 PP execution model with scheduler admission, speculative state, index-sharing dependencies, and a PP-first multi-node DP/EP topology.

#### Open questions

1. Should the transport API extend `PPHandler` and `IntermediateTensors`, or should both become clients of a new internal `PPTransport` owner?
2. Which small fields should be packed, and what static layout/versioning is needed for full CUDA graphs?
3. Should auxiliary hidden states remain individually keyed by activation-boundary/slot or use one packed tensor plus offsets?
4. Should cross-boundary index state be transported for all supported models, or should the first rollout reject unsafe partition cuts?
5. Should PP admission balance requests, tokens, estimated compute, or a hybrid, and should it be opt-in initially?
6. Should PP-first placement be explicit-only at first, or selected automatically when the stage footprint matches node capacity?
7. Must the initial topology require exactly one PP stage per node, or may a node host multiple complete stage blocks?
8. If an EP domain cannot fit in one node, should configuration fail, fall back to DP-first placement, or require an explicitly selected hierarchical EP mode?
9. Which feature combinations are required before removing the current PP validation guards for EAGLE3, DFlash, and DSpark?

### Feedback Period.

2026-08-18 through 2026-09-01.

### CC List.

@njhill @WoosukKwon @robertgshaw2-redhat @heheda12345 @youkaichao @eastwood-c @ChihayaK @yewentao256

### Any Other Things.

The author can provide scheduler traces, device profiles, representative PP partition layouts, and acceptance-rate results for the proposed combinations. Feedback is especially welcome on the transport ownership boundary, the minimum support matrix for the first rollout, and whether index-sharing dependencies should initially be transported or guarded by partition validation.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Coerce non-dict tool_call arguments to `{}` and return 400 on malformed JSON
body:
## Purpose

We've observed 500 errors in production caused by requests where `tool_calls[].function.arguments` contains non-dict JSON values. A minimal reproducer:

```bash
curl http://<host>/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "deepseek-v4-flash",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "How is the weather today?"},
      {"role": "assistant", "content": null, "tool_calls": [
        {"id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "arguments": "[]"}}
      ]},
      {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": "Sunny 25°C"}
    ]
  }'
```

When `tool_calls[].function.arguments` is a JSON string that does not decode to a dict (e.g. `"[]"`, `"null"`, `"42"`), `_postprocess_messages` passes the decoded non-dict value downstream, causing an unhandled exception and a 500 response. Similarly, malformed JSON (e.g. `"{invalid"`) triggers an uncaught `json.JSONDecodeError` that also results in a 500.

This PR fixes the argument parsing logic to:
1. Coerce any parsed non-dict value to `{}`.
2. Raise `VLLMValidationError` (HTTP 400) on invalid JSON instead of surfacing an internal 500.

## Test Plan

Added unit tests in `tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_chat_utils.py` covering:
- `"[]"` → coerced to `{}`
- `"{invalid"` → raises `VLLMValidationError`
- `"42"`, `'"hello"'`, `"true"` → coerced to `{}`
- `{"key": "value"}` (already dict) → passthrough
- `'{"a": 1}'` (valid dict string) → parsed normally

## Test Result

```
tests/.../test_chat_utils.py::test_postprocess_messages_null_arguments_string PASSED
tests/.../test_chat_utils.py::test_postprocess_messages_list_arguments_string PASSED
tests/.../test_chat_utils.py::test_postprocess_messages_invalid_json_arguments PASSED
tests/.../test_chat_utils.py::test_postprocess_messages_non_dict_parsed_arguments PASSED
tests/.../test_chat_utils.py::test_postprocess_messages_dict_arguments_passthrough PASSED
tests/.../test_chat_utils.py::test_postprocess_messages_valid_json_dict_string PASSED
```

title: [ROCm][Refactor] Split multi-stream launch/sync into CUDA and ROCm platform methods
body:
## Purpose

> Part of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/41820, continue working on https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43718.

Split multi-stream launch and sync semantics out of `vllm/utils/multi_stream_utils.py` into platform-specific `launch_multi_stream()` implementations on `CudaPlatformBase` and `RocmPlatform`. This addresses [#43718 comment by @zyongye](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43718) to avoid embedding CUDA/ROCm divergence in shared utility code.

- **CUDA** (`CudaPlatformBase.launch_multi_stream`): Uses standard `Event.wait()` / `Event.record()` with configurable launch ordering via `queue_aux_before_default`. `execute_in_parallel` queues aux work before the default callable (preserving the original DeepSeek-V4 input-GEMM overlap pattern); `maybe_execute_in_parallel` runs the default callable first (LoRA / two-way overlap pattern).
- **ROCm** (`RocmPlatform.launch_multi_stream`): Uses `Stream.wait_stream()` fork-join instead of CUDA Event-based cross-stream ordering. This follows the validated ATOM DeepSeek-V4 CSA pattern (`maybe_compressors_async`, `dual_stream_moe_forward` in `atom/models/deepseek_v4.py`), which avoids deadlocks/hangs observed with bare `Event.wait()` / `Event.wait_event()` on HIP during DSV4 multistream decode ([#41820](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/41820)). `start_event` and `done_events` are kept for a uniform platform API but are unused on ROCm.

This PR is a **platform refactor only**; it does not re-enable DSV4 ROCm multistream in `deepseek_v4/amd/model.py` (follow-up PR).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -sv tests/utils/test_multi_stream_utils.py
pytest -sv tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py::test_eager_attention_inside_multistream_overlap
```

## Test Result

```bash
# tests/utils/test_multi_stream_utils.py
2 passed, 14 warnings in 1.51s

# tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py::test_eager_attention_inside_multistream_overlap
1 passed, 14 warnings in 1.19s
```
