title: [Bug] fastsafetensors ParallelLoader broadcasts on group.WORLD; PP-scoped draft loads deadlock
body:
# Draft: upstream issue — fastsafetensors loader hard-codes the WORLD process group and deadlocks PP-scoped draft loads

**Repo:** vllm-project/vllm
**Title:** [Bug] fastsafetensors ParallelLoader broadcasts on group.WORLD; draft-model load under pipeline parallelism deadlocks

## What happened

Serving Kimi-K3 with speculative decoding (DSpark) under pipeline parallelism (TP8 × PP2, 2×8 B200, EFA) fails deterministically at engine init on current main. The drafter is instantiated only on the last PP stage (correct per #50514's design). Its weight load goes through `--load-format fastsafetensors`, which uses

```python
# vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py (fastsafetensors_weights_iterator)
if torch.distributed.is_initialized():
    pg = torch.distributed.group.WORLD
else:
    pg = SingleGroup()
```

and then broadcasts every tensor on that group (`fastsafetensors/frameworks/_torch.py:138/143/147`).

The 8 ranks on the last PP stage (global ranks 8-15) enter `ParallelLoader`'s per-tensor broadcast chain, while the 8 ranks on PP0 never call it — so the **first mismatched WORLD-group broadcast hangs without error** until the 600 s watchdog:

```
[rank11] Watchdog caught collective operation timeout:
WorkNCCL(SeqNum=497221, OpType=BROADCAST, NumelIn=1, NumelOut=1, Timeout(ms)=600000)
```

Python stack at the hang (from the doomed worker):

```
.../v1/executor/ray_executor_v2.py initialize_worker
   multiproc_executor.py:648 __init__
   gpu_worker.py:442 load_model
   model_runner.py:362
   speculator.py:160
   dspark/speculator.py load_draft_model
   dspark/utils.py load_dspark_model
   model_loader/__init__.py:140 get_model
   model_loader/base_loader.py load_model
```

## Why nobody hits this so far

- Target-model loads happen on **all** ranks, so WORLD-group broadcasts always pair.
- The DSpark×PP code path is brand new (#50514) and its validation used the default `--load-format auto` (plain safetensors, no broadcasts). The overlap — spec × PP × `--load-format fastsafetensors` — is unreachable shipped product today, but the Kimi-K3 recipe pins `--load-format fastsafetensors` on Blackwell for load speed, so this is on the vendor-sanctioned path.

## Suggested fix

Scope `pg` to the weight-loading *participants*, not the world. At the draft load site the natural choice is the drafter's own TP group (`get_tp_group()` or the parallel-config-sized group for the sub-engine), falling back to WORLD when the load is genuinely engine-wide. If scoping is unavailable at this layer, a defensive alternative is to refuse fastsafetensors for sub-engine (draft) loads with a clear error, and let vLLM select plain safetensors there on its own.

## Repro

- vLLM main @ e578de311 (cu130 wheel `0.26.1rc1.dev292`), Kimi-K3 MXFP4 + Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark, TP8 x PP2, 2x8 B200,
- exact serving flags: `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --distributed-executor-backend ray --load-format fastsafetensors --speculative-config '{"model":"...","num_speculative_tokens":7,"method":"dspark",...}'` plus #50514 applied (spec under PP).
- With `LOAD_FORMAT` flipped to `auto` the same boot proceeds past draft loading (falsification of the causal chain).

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Fall back to torch for unsupported expert counts in topk_softplus_sqrt
body:
## Summary

Fixes the load-time crash hit by pruned/REAP DeepSeek-V4-Flash checkpoints (e.g. `0xSero/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-REAP`, `n_routed_experts=160`):

```
RuntimeError: topkGatingSoftplusSqrtKernelLauncher, topk_softplus_sqrt_kernels.cu:747, Unsupported expert number: 160
```

## Root cause

The CUDA kernel `topkGatingSoftplusSqrtKernelLauncher` (in `csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/topk_softplus_sqrt_kernels.cu`) only instantiates a fixed set of expert counts — `{1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 192, 256, 320, 384, 448, 512, 576}` — and any other count falls into the `default:` branch, which calls `STD_TORCH_CHECK(false, "Unsupported expert number: ...")`. REAP/pruned checkpoints keep a non-instantiated `n_routed_experts` (160 for `0xSero/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-REAP`), so the router kernel crashes at load.

## Fix

In `vllm_topk_softplus_sqrt` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/fused_topk_bias_router.py`), route any `gating_output.shape[-1]` outside the kernel's instantiated set to the existing `_topk_softplus_sqrt_torch` fallback — the same pure-PyTorch implementation already used for XPU. The `is_xpu` check is untouched and still first; XPU keeps its current behavior of always using the torch fallback. The supported set is a module-level `frozenset` constant with a comment pointing at the C++ switch.

## Tests

Added `test_fused_topk_softplus_sqrt_unsupported_experts` to `tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py`, parametrized over expert counts `[160, 100, 200, 1000]` (plus token count, renormalize, dtype), verifying:
- no crash, and
- output matches the file's existing `_torch_topk_softplus_sqrt` reference (sorted-index comparison, weight `atol=2e-5`), mirroring `test_fused_topk_softplus_sqrt`.

## Related

- Issue #50576 — this crash is documented in MidasMining's comment: the REAP checkpoint itself ships this exact fix as a runtime patch; routing non-standard counts to `_topk_softplus_sqrt_torch` in `vllm_topk_softplus_sqrt` is the in-tree equivalent.
- Issue #47141 (open, XPU/SYCL-only, adds a SYCL path for topk_softplus_sqrt) — **does not overlap**: we do not touch the `is_xpu` branch.
- PR #50759 (open, touches the same file for padding handling) — this change is additive and minimal; no conflict with the padding path.

## Verification status (honest)

- `python3 -m py_compile` passes on both changed files.
- A standalone numpy script replicating `_topk_softplus_sqrt_torch`'s math (softplus→sqrt→bias-for-selection-only→topk→renormalize→routed_scaling_factor) for a 160-expert synthetic gating output confirms finite outputs, valid top-k indices, correct renormalization, and true top-k selection.
- **CUDA test execution on A10 (sm_86)**: `tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py` run on vLLM release-0.26.0 with the two changed files applied — `test_fused_topk_softplus_sqrt_unsupported_experts[160/100/200/1000]` and `test_supported_experts_use_kernel_path[8/64/256/384]` all pass; the fallback matches the `_torch_topk_softplus_sqrt` reference (sorted-index comparison, weights `atol=2e-5`).

## Implementation notes

- **Single fast-path branch.** The dispatcher was restructured from the original two-branch shape (separate `is_xpu` early-return, then a whitelist check) into one condition: `not is_xpu AND num_experts in _SOFTPLUS_SQRT_SUPPORTED_EXPERTS` → CUDA kernel; everything else (including XPU and all non-instantiated counts) → the existing pure-PyTorch `_topk_softplus_sqrt_torch`. Same math, not bit-exact, slower. Semantically identical to the previous two-branch version.
- **The set is pinned by a drift guard.** New test `test_supported_experts_use_kernel_path` monkeypatches `_topk_softplus_sqrt_torch` to `boom` and asserts that supported counts `[8, 64, 256, 384]` reach the kernel. It catches both failure directions: a missing count in the Python whitelist (fallback called → boom fires) and a dropped count in the C++ switch (kernel raises "Unsupported expert number").
- **Honest perf note.** Pruned/REAP checkpoints (e.g. K160) route through the PyTorch fallback — ms-scale per routing call vs the kernel's µs-scale. This is the price of correctness until the kernel gains a 160 path; it is exactly the trade-off the reference torch implementation already carries on XPU.
- **Upstreaming the checkpoint author's runtime patch.** The REAP checkpoint ships this workaround as `runtime/patch_vllm_router_k160.py`, which hardcodes the tuple `(16, 32, 64, 128, 192, 256, 320, 384, 512)` — **not** the kernel's real set (it omits `1, 2, 4, 8, 448, 576`). This PR instead uses the kernel's actual instantiation set `{1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 192, 256, 320, 384, 448, 512, 576}`, kept in sync by the drift-guard test above.

title: [Bugfix][DeepSeek V4] Fix fused MTP RMSNorm dtype mismatch
body:
## Summary

- cast both fused MTP RMSNorm input paths to FP32 before the runtime branch merges
- keep position-zero masking and RMSNorm arithmetic in the existing FP32 compute type
- add a kernel correctness test covering the masked enorm path and both hnorm slots

## Why

The two runtime branches previously assigned different inferred types to `x`: the masked `tl.where` path promoted it to FP32 while the hnorm path kept the input dtype. Triton requires local variables to have a consistent type when control-flow branches merge, so mixed-precision inputs could fail kernel compilation with a branch dtype mismatch.

Explicitly converting both loads to FP32 matches `_rmsnorm_row`, which already performs RMSNorm arithmetic in FP32. Results are still converted to the output pointer dtype at store time, so the output dtype and numerical behavior are preserved.

## Duplicate-work check

I searched open vLLM PRs for `fused_mtp_input_rmsnorm`, `MTP RMSNorm`, and the dtype mismatch. PR #45240 introduced the shared fused kernel but does not contain this dtype fix or a standalone correctness test. I found no open PR addressing this issue.

## Testing

- added `tests/kernels/test_fused_mtp_input_rmsnorm.py` to compare both fused outputs against a PyTorch RMSNorm reference
- `python -m py_compile vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/fused_mtp_input_rmsnorm.py tests/kernels/test_fused_mtp_input_rmsnorm.py`
- `git diff --check`

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to investigate the Triton type mismatch, prepare the patch, and draft the test and PR description. I reviewed the changed lines and test coverage.

title: [Bugfix][Build] Fix DeepGEMM CUDA 12.9 FP8 header visibility
body:
## Purpose

Fix the CUDA 12.9 release build failure in DeepGEMM's host extension while preserving the exact DeepGEMM `f5a76426` code baseline.

The pinned `mqa_logits.cuh` directly names `__nv_fp8_e4m3`, but it does not include the CUDA header that declares the type. CUDA 12.9 host compilation therefore fails with:

```text
deep_gemm/layout/mqa_logits.cuh:16:61: error: '__nv_fp8_e4m3' was not declared in this scope
```

This updates both synchronized vLLM DeepGEMM pins from `f5a76426` to `e21c821f`. The new commit has `f5a76426` as its sole parent and adds exactly one line:

```cpp
#include <cuda_fp8.h>
```

DeepGEMM branch: https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/tree/codex/f5a-cuda-fp8-include

DeepGEMM commit: https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/commit/e21c821f39a2056d68067a466c64ddc942200106

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR references `e21c821f`, `mqa_logits.cuh`, or the missing `cuda_fp8.h` declaration.

PR #50796 is related but not a duplicate. It replaces `f5a76426` with the broader `5f33a180` SM120+SITU merge to restore scale-factor layout support on SM120. This change deliberately preserves the existing `f5a76426` dependency content and adds only the missing CUDA FP8 declaration needed by the CUDA 12.9 host compiler. The PRs touch the same two synchronized pin files, but they test different dependency changes and address different failures.

## Validation

Baseline release-v2 build 4680 pinned `f5a76426`; its two CUDA 12.9 wheels and four CUDA 12.9 release images failed in the DeepGEMM host extension.

Release-v2 build 4684 used this exact vLLM commit and pinned `e21c821f`. All six CUDA 12.9 targets passed:

| Target | Result |
| --- | --- |
| x86_64 wheel | Passed |
| aarch64 wheel | Passed |
| x86_64 release image | Passed |
| aarch64 release image | Passed |
| x86_64 Ubuntu 24.04 release image | Passed |
| aarch64 Ubuntu 24.04 release image | Passed |

Build: https://buildkite.com/vllm/release-v2/builds/4684

The x86 and aarch64 logs both checked out `e21c821f` and advanced through the DeepGEMM host-extension builds without the prior `mqa_logits.cuh` error. The overall pipeline is marked failing only because of the unrelated macOS arm64 CPU wheel job.

Additional checks:

```bash
git diff --check
bash -n tools/install_deepgemm.sh
```

Applicable pre-commit hooks, including shell lint, dependency-graph validation, configuration validation, and commit sign-off, passed.

No model evaluation was run because this changes dependency header visibility during compilation and does not change model output or serving behavior.

---

AI assistance was used for root-cause analysis, branch preparation, CI orchestration, and PR drafting with OpenAI Codex. This draft requires the human submitter to review every changed line and the validation evidence before marking it ready for review.

title: [Rocm] Fix LMcache support issues for the kimik3-dspark model
body:
## Summary

- Fix Kimi-K3 DSpark multi-token verification on ROCm by expanding causal paged-KV metadata from the real per-request query offsets, caching the expansion across MLA layers, and keeping the small-head Gluon verification path single-split to avoid repeated allocations and GPU faults.
- Add a reproducible launcher for Kimi-K3 + DSpark with either native CPU offload or LMCache MP offload. The validated LMCache path uses FP8 KV, Mamba alignment, prefix caching, and an L1 pool sized to 60% of available `/dev/shm`.

### Install the ROCm dependencies

```bash
VERSION=v0.5.3rc2
pip install lmcache==${VERSION#v} --no-deps \
  --find-links https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/releases/expanded_assets/${VERSION}-rocm
pip install cupy-rocm-7-0 --no-deps
```

LMCache 0.5.3rc2 provides the unified Mamba-state and subpaged-MLA cache views required by Kimi-K3. CuPy is required by LMCache's ROCm GPU cache-registration path.

### Start the LMCache server

The LMCache connector option below requires this server. `LMCACHE_L1_SIZE_GB=906` was validated on a host with about 1512 GiB free in `/dev/shm`; adjust it to no more than roughly 60% of the free shared-memory capacity.

```bash
LMCACHE_L1_SIZE_GB=906
lmcache server \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 5555 \
  --http-host 127.0.0.1 \
  --http-port 8080 \
  --l1-size-gb "$LMCACHE_L1_SIZE_GB" \
  --l1-init-size-gb 20 \
  --l1-read-ttl-seconds 7200 \
  --chunk-size 1536 \
  --max-workers 8 \
  --eviction-trigger-watermark 0.85 \
  --eviction-ratio 0.10 \
  --eviction-policy LRU
```

### Run vLLM with `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`

This option does not require the LMCache server:

```bash
vllm serve /models/huggingface_hub/ \
  --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8888 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 3000 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":2,"method":"dspark","attention_backend":"TRITON_MLA","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":299875000000,"lazy_offload":true}}'
```

### Run vLLM with `LMCacheMPConnector`

Start the LMCache server first, then run:

```bash
vllm serve /models/huggingface_hub/ \
  --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8888 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 3000 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":2,"method":"dspark","attention_backend":"TRITON_MLA","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"LMCacheMPConnector","kv_connector_module_path":"lmcache.integration.vllm.lmcache_mp_connector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"lmcache.mp.host":"tcp://127.0.0.1","lmcache.mp.port":5555}}'
```

The complete LMCache setup is also available as:

```bash
examples/online_serving/start_kimik3_dspark_lmcache.sh
```

## Test plan

- [x] Python syntax compilation for `rocm_aiter_mla.py`
- [x] Shell syntax validation for the launcher
- [x] Two-prompt serving benchmark on 8x MI355X with 8192 input and 1024 output tokens
- [x] 2/2 requests completed successfully; speculative acceptance rate was 98.98%

  --backend vllm \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8888 \
  --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --tokenizer /models/huggingface_hub/ \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 \
  --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts 2 \
  --request-rate inf \
  --ignore-eos

title: [KV Offload] Support out-of-tree secondary tier managers via `module_path`
body:
## Purpose
- Add config-driven out-of-tree loading to `SecondaryTierFactory`, matching the pattern already used by `OffloadingSpecFactory` (`spec_module_path`) and `CachePolicyFactory` (`cache_policy_module_path`)
- Users can now specify custom `SecondaryTierManager` implementations purely via config without forking vLLM or running `register_tier()` before engine init
- Document the feature in the usage guide

### Example config

```json
{
  "spec_name": "TieringOffloadingSpec",
  "cpu_bytes_to_use": 10737418240,
  "secondary_tiers": [
    {
      "type": "MyCustomTier",
      "module_path": "my_package.my_module",
      "custom_param": "value"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Test Plan

title: [Bug] (SUPERSEDED 2026-08-06): MTP proposer eager GDN hypothesis — **overturned by 2nd-round attribution**
body:
> ⚠️ **Correction history (2026-08-04/05, after on-box instrumentation):** the original diagnosis
> claimed MTP makes per-seq `query_len` non-uniform (`{2,3,4}`) so the FULL decode graph "almost
> never hits" and PIECEWISE "deliberately keeps GDN eager" — **that premise was falsified**.
> A follow-up "eager only in prefill-mixed steps" was also an instrument artifact: it missed that
> PIECEWISE graph *replays* re-execute the GDN eager-break in Python on **every** step. The
> confirmed finding is below; the microbench table and torch.compile result remain valid.
>
> ## ⚠️⚠️ 2026-08-06 2nd-round attribution: the "every-step eager GDN" core claim is OVERTURNED
>
> Precise per-step attribution (80k-line phase0 log, pairing each `gdn_build` shape
> `(num_reqs, num_actual_tokens)` with the eager counter delta) + source check:
>
> 1. **Uniform decode steps run GDN with 0 eager invocations.** All 5859 eager events are
>    non-uniform shapes: `(0, nonuniform)`=4324 (prefill steps), `(1, nonuniform)`=1535
>    (non-uniform/mixed steps); **`uniform` (na == nr×4) = 0**. The main forward's 48 GDN layers
>    are captured in the FULL graph; uniform FULL steps replay them (10万+ builds, delta=0).
> 2. **The MTP proposer is an EagleProposer path and does NOT re-run the 48-layer GDN model.**
>    `use_eagle()` returns True for method in ("eagle","eagle3","mtp","dflash","dspark") → the
>    proposer is `EagleProposer` with `pass_hidden_states_to_model=True` (`spec_decode/eagle.py`),
>    i.e. it runs the MTP head on the **main forward's hidden states**. The earlier claim that
>    "proposer forwards run 48 layers of GDN eager every step" is wrong — the proposer does not
>    execute the GDN model at all. Consequently **the proposed fix "let the proposer hit FULL"
>    is a dead end** (there is no eager GDN in the proposer to eliminate).
> 3. **The baseline profiler trace cited below is a NON-uniform/mixed step**, not p50: it shows
>    65 `cudaGraphLaunch` (a uniform FULL step has ~1) + 48 eager GDN. Its "~16 ms/step idle,
>    GPU idle ~85%" is the cost of a non-uniform step, not the steady-state p50. **p50=33 ms
>    composition is not yet measured** and is NOT GDN-eager-driven.
> 4. **What still stands**: `query_len == 1+num_spec` constant (finding 1); the main forward is
>    FULL-captured on uniform decode (GDN already in graph, cost 0); the standalone microbench
>    (one eager 48-layer GDN pass ≈ 15.4 ms CPU, torch.compile −1.7×) quantifies what a GDN
>    eager step *would* cost, but its prevalence is only the non-uniform/mixed minority.
>
> **Net**: GDN eager is a secondary lever for non-uniform/mixed steps (~4.5% share to quantify),
> NOT the p50 lever. Sections below that assert "every step" / "proposer runs GDN" are
> superseded by this block.

## Description

**One-line summary:** Under MTP speculative decoding, Qwen3.6-27B's 48 GDN layers run eager
Python `_forward_core` **every step**. MTP runs **3 model forwards per scheduler step**; the two
PIECEWISE proposer passes are forced to PIECEWISE because the proposer dispatch omits the
`uniform_decode` decision (`llm_base_proposer.py:1776`), and a PIECEWISE graph *replay* executes
the GDN eager-break (`qwen_gdn_attention_core`) as Python on every replay — so the proposer
forwards pay 48 layers of Python host orchestration every step, regardless of step type.
Prefill-mixed steps additionally run the main forward (PIECEWISE) eager. Profiler-confirmed cost:
**~16 ms/step of GDN CPU orchestration (~50% of the ~33 ms step wall), with the GPU idle ~85% of
the main stream waiting on it** (the GDN kernels themselves are <1 ms of GPU time).

### Environment

- 4× RTX 5090 (sm_120, no NVLink, PCIe P2P, Ice Lake root port)
- Host CPU: Intel Xeon Platinum 8368Q (Ice Lake-SP, PCIe Gen4), 1 socket × 38 cores / 76 threads, base 2.6 GHz / boost 3.7 GHz — the bottleneck is serial Python dispatch on each TP worker's main thread (the 4× `VLLM::Worker_TP` main threads + the `VLLM::EngineCore` thread are the 5 saturated cores), so per-step time scales with per-core IPC, not core count
- vLLM v0.26.0 (V1 engine), image `vllm-openai:v0.26.0-cu129-fastokens` (stock v0.26.0 + fastokens *tokenizer* plugin; fastokens does not modify any vLLM source, so this is upstream behavior)
- Model: [Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B) ([ModelScope](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B)), Apache-2.0, BF16 ~55.6 GB. Qwen3.5 arch (`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`), 64 layers = 48 GDN linear-attention + 16 full-attention, hidden 5120, native context 262144
- TP=4, max-model-len 131072, chunked prefill, max-num-batched-tokens 32768, `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`
- Speculative decoding: `--speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}` (**note: 3, not 2** — `uniform_decode_query_len = 1 + 3 = 4`)
- Load: ~30 concurrent requests, ~400 input / 20 output tokens

### Symptoms

- 5 CPU cores saturated: 4× `VLLM::Worker_TP` main threads at ~70–100% + `VLLM::EngineCore` spinning on shm_broadcast `sched_yield`
- `nvidia-smi` reports SM 100%, but GPM counters show **SM activity 29%, SM occupancy 3%, tensor 11%, DRAM 8%**
- ITL 60–190 ms, aggregate gen ~255 tok/s. (The ~16 ms/step cost quantified below is **CPU dispatch overhead, not GPU execution** — the GDN kernels themselves are tiny, well under 1 ms of GPU time per step; per-step `torch.cuda.synchronize` ≈ no sync in the microbench confirms the GPU work is not the cost.)
- Microbenchmark: NCCL allreduce is only 40–60 µs/call — communication is **not** the bottleneck

## Corrected findings (Phase-0 instrumentation) — ⚠️ findings 2–4 superseded by the 2026-08-06 block above

Instrumentation on the exact production setup, with per-step counters in
`gdn_attn.build()`, `cudagraph_dispatcher.dispatch()`, and a GDN eager counter in
`qwen_gdn_linear_attn._forward_core`. Full report: `metrics_log/phase0/phase0_report.md`.

1. **`query_len` is constant, never `{2,3,4}`.** Every pure spec-decode step has
   `query_len == 1 + num_spec` (== 4 with num_spec=3). The rare `query_len=2` slots
   (870 across the window) are **prefill chunks**, not spec sequences. The original
   assumption `query_len = num_accepted + num_spec` is wrong: vLLM schedules a fixed
   1 base + `num_spec` draft positions per spec seq; the accepted count only advances
   KV/conv state and does not change this step's query_len.
2. **Pure spec-decode *main* forwards hit FULL 100%** (GDN captured in the graph), but the
   two **proposer** forwards are PIECEWISE and run GDN eager **every step**. (The earlier
   "frozen eager counter → zero eager" reading was an instrument artifact — a PIECEWISE
   graph replay re-runs the GDN eager-break as Python on every replay.)
3. **GDN `_forward_core` runs eager every step, ~16 ms/step of CPU orchestration.** A
   `torch.profiler` trace (concurrency 12, pure decode) shows 48 `qwen_gdn_attention_core`
   eager invocations/step, each layer doing ~120 small aten ops + ~40 tensor allocations;
   that host orchestration is ~16 ms/step (backed out from ITL p50=33 ms; profiler
   self-amplifies 2–6×), with the GPU main stream idle ~85% waiting on it. Prefill-mixed
   steps additionally run the main forward (PIECEWISE) eager, on top of the always-eager
   proposer passes. (The 48 invocations/step correspond to one of the two proposer
   forwards — the 1-token/seq draft-loop pass does not re-execute the 48-layer GDN
   eager-break, and the main forward is FULL-captured — otherwise 2×48 layers would
   exceed the ~33 ms step wall.)
4. **MTP runs 3 model forwards per scheduler step.** Each step: 1× FULL (uniform) main
   sampling forward + 1× PIECEWISE proposer main pass + 1× PIECEWISE proposer draft loop
   (1 token/seq). The proposer path calls `_determine_batch_execution_and_padding` →
   `dispatch(num_tokens)` **without passing `uniform_decode`** (`llm_base_proposer.py:1776`),
   so the proposer forwards are forced to PIECEWISE even when the batch is uniform — the
   proposer main pass has the same batch shape as the FULL-captured main forward and could
   otherwise hit FULL.

## Measured CPU floor of one eager GDN step (standalone microbenchmark, real Triton kernels, no serving)

`bench/gdn_decode_cpu_bench.py`, replicating the spec-decode branch of `_forward_core`
(48 GDN layers, num_reqs=30, query_len=4):

| Item                                                              | ms/step        | share |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ----- |
| Total real-kernel time                                            | **15.4** | 100%  |
| 96 Triton launches (2 kernels/layer)                              | 8.2            | 53%   |
| Python orchestration (slicing/rearrange/lookups/arg construction) | 5.5            | 35%   |
| Mock-kernel torch ops (reference only)                            | 1.76           | 11%   |

- `--sync` (per-step GPU sync) ≈ no sync (14.7 vs 14.4 ms) → **pure CPU bound, not an async-overlap issue**.
- **torch.compile is a net loss**: 24.8 ms compiled vs 15.4 ms baseline (~1.7× slower). Each layer's 2 opaque Triton kernels (`causal_conv1d_update` + `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update`) break the graph naturally; Inductor cannot fuse across kernels and only adds compile/dispatch overhead. **This explains why vLLM keeps GDN in `splitting_ops` — please do not suggest torch.compile as a fix.**

**Prevalence**: ~~this ~16 ms of GDN dispatch applies to **every** MTP step~~ — **⚠️ SUPERSEDED
2026-08-06**: eager GDN only occurs on non-uniform/mixed steps (uniform steps = 0; the proposer
does not run GDN). The standalone microbench measures one eager 48-layer GDN pass at 15.4 ms —
its *prevalence* is the non-uniform/mixed minority, not every step.

## Expected behavior — ⚠️ point 1 superseded (2026-08-06: proposer does not run GDN)

- ~~The MTP proposer main pass should be able to hit a FULL decode graph when its batch is
  uniform... this alone removes the every-step eager GDN from 2 of the 3 per-step forwards.~~
  **Dead end**: the EagleProposer path runs the MTP head on hidden states and does not execute
  the 48-layer GDN, so there is no proposer eager GDN to remove.
- More broadly, GDN should not be re-executed as a Python eager-break on PIECEWISE graph
  replays; it should be captured into the graph — **but this only helps non-uniform/mixed
  steps, not the p50 lever**.

## Suggested directions (for upstream consideration)

1. ~~**Let the MTP proposer main pass hit FULL**... This removes 1 of the 3 forwards per step
   and its eager GDN.~~ **⚠️ Superseded 2026-08-06**: the proposer (EagleProposer) does not run
   the 48-layer GDN, so this eliminates no eager GDN.
2. **Capture GDN on PIECEWISE replays instead of re-running the eager-break in Python** — the
   root of the every-step cost. Note this is the reason vLLM keeps GDN in `splitting_ops`;
   capturing it requires handling `_forward_core`'s data-dependent branches and host-side
   state access.
3. **Cross-layer batching (orthogonal, ~90% ceiling)**: stack the 48 GDN layers' decode
   states/weights along a leading dim — 96 Triton launches → 2 batched kernels, orchestration
   48× → 1×, ~15 ms → ~1–2 ms/step. Precedent: `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode`
   (already used by `_forward_core_decode_non_spec`).
4. **Remove per-step `.item()` CPU syncs in the GDN metadata build** (GPU-side reduction + async readback).

> **Verified and ruled out: torch.compile** — ~1.7× slower (see the measurement table above). Not a viable route.

## Steps to reproduce

Full serving command (MTP + chunked prefill, the combination that triggers the behavior):

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len 131072 --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --enable-prefix-caching --disable-custom-all-reduce
```

Then, under load (~30 concurrent, ~400-in / 20-out tokens):

- Instrument `gdn_attn.build()`, `cudagraph_dispatcher.dispatch()`, and a counter in
  `_forward_core` (see `phase0_instrumentation_checklist.md`) and log per-step
  `query_len` histogram, `num_prefills`, dispatch mode, and the eager counter.
- Expected: **⚠️ 2026-08-06 SUPERSEDED — do NOT expect +48 every step.** Measured reality:
  uniform decode steps (main forward FULL-captured) show **0** eager; +48 eager only on
  non-uniform/mixed steps. Pure decode steps show constant `query_len` (== 1+num_spec); the
  MTP proposer (EagleProposer) does not re-run the 48-layer GDN at all.
- `py-spy dump --pid <worker>` during load: `_forward_core` on the main-thread stack every
  step (proposer pass), more frequently during prefill-mixed steps.
- `nvidia-smi dmon --gpm-metrics 2,3,5,10` for real GPU activity (smutil/smocc/mmaact/dram) — `nvidia-smi` SM% is misleading.
- `bench/gdn_decode_cpu_bench.py` (standalone, real Triton kernels) quantifies the per-step
  GDN CPU floor (~16 ms); available on request.

## Related issues / PRs

- #50623 — `gdn_attn`: cudagraph padding branch guards on `num_decodes` but slices by `batch_size` (fixed by PR #50680)
- #50780 — CUDA graph memory profiler charges an mnbt-linear profiling transient as "graph memory" → KV cache pool −18–24% on hybrid GDN models since v0.26.0 (fixed by PR #50848)
- #45258 — RFC: FULL cudagraph support for spec-decode drafter chain steps (currently PIECEWISE-only)

### 🐛 Describe the bug # DSpark speculative decoding: acceptance collapses after position 0 on DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 **vllm version**: 0.26.1rc1.dev255+g5e35a6f4f (nightly image built 2026-08-03) **Model**: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (fp8 weights, ue8m0 scales, fp4 experts, sparse MLA / DSA indexer) **Hardware**: 2x NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, compute capability 12.1 / SM121a), TP=2 across nodes, aarch64, CUDA 13.0.88 **Stack**: flashinfer-python 0.6.15.post1, deep_gemm 2.5.0 (rebuilt from deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM@a6b593d against this torch), ray 2.55.1 ## Problem DSPark speculative decoding has near-normal acceptance at position 0, but the chain collapses at position 1+ (~25% conditional continuation per step), leaving average acceptance at 9-25% depending on request. Mean acceptance length 1.46 with 5 speculative tokens. ### Per-position acceptance rates temperature=0 (greedy target): ``` Position 0: 85.7% Position 1: 42.9% (conditional ~50%) Position 2: 14.3% (conditional ~33%) Position 3: 0.0% Position 4: 0.0% ``` draft_sample_method=probabilistic, server-default temperature (best window): ``` Position 0: 92.9% Position 1: 64.3% Position 2: 57.1% Position 3: 35.7% Position 4: 21.4% Avg 54.3%, Mean acceptance length 3.71 ``` vllm bench serve (random input 8192/512, ignore-eos, no temperature override → server default ~1.0): ``` Acceptance rate: 9.20%, Acceptance length: 1.46 Position 0: 34.29% Position 1: 8.57% Position 2: 2.57% Position 3: 0.57% Position 4: 0.00% ``` ## Launch config ```bash vllm serve /data/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/ \ --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --distributed-executor-backend ray --enable-prefix-caching \ -tp 2 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 --kv-cache-memory=11305291674 \ --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 10 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' \ --attention-config '{"use_fp4_indexer_cache": false}' ``` Reproduce: run the above, then `vllm bench serve --model --dataset-name random --tokenizer --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 512 --num-prompts 1 --trust-remote-code --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --port 8000` and inspect the SpecDecoding metrics. ## What has been verified (ruled out) 1. **Markov head weights ARE loaded** — instrumentation after `load_dspark_model`: `model.markov_head.markov_w1.weight dtype=bfloat16 shape=(129280,256) mean=-0.00068 std=0.50132 absmax=17.125` (not default init: std≈1.0) 2. **Target model output is correct** — coherent generation, no garbage. 3. `precompute_and_store_context_kv` runs every propose step (non-dummy path). 4. Draft-attention topk dispatch issue worked around: flashinfer sm120 dsv4 decode only has kernel instances for topk ∈ {128,512,1024}; the draft uses topk=256 → we pad indices to 512 in `_forward_decode`. Verified numerically safe (padded vs native output identical, diff 0.0) — padding is NOT the cause. 5. Same behavior on vllm 0.25.0 (separate issue there: garbage outputs, resolved by moving to 0.26.1rc1 nightly) and across flashinfer 0.6.13 / 0.6.15.post1 / 0.6.16.post1. ## Suspected area Position 0 works (anchors + markov bias from the last real token), but every subsequent chain step degrades to ~25% conditional acceptance. Suspects, for the maintainers: - The parallel backbone's multi-position predictions for positions 1+ (are later positions conditioned on intermediate draft tokens at all, or are they "blind" parallel outputs?). - The sequential markov sampling (`_sample_sequential`): the `prev` token / `map_draft_to_target` mapping feeding the markov head at positions 1+. - Possible interaction between the draft model (mtp blocks) fp4-expert handling and this checkpoint's mtp weight layout (`mtp.{0,1,2}.*` at top level; `model.layers.43.mtp_block.*` naming mismatch already observed for the MTP path in vllm 0.25.0). Happy to run any additional experiments / provide logs. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [CI] Stabilize GLM-5.2 PCP evaluation
body:
## Summary

- enable PyTorch expandable CUDA allocator segments for the GLM-5.2 TP1/PCP4 GSM8K evaluation;
- keep `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`, which is needed to exercise the large-batch PCP path;
- scope the allocator change to the memory-tight TP1/PCP4 case; TP2/PCP2 is unchanged.

## Root cause

The pytest-level error in [Buildkite #81913](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/81913#019fca13-8131-4f3f-bcfa-6636b1022f66) is only a 20-minute server-start timeout. The worker log shows the actual failure during the profile run:

```text
CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 24.43 GiB.
15.36 GiB is free
23.97 GiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated
```

The allocation comes from FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE's `FusedMoeRunner::getWorkspaceInfo`. The same signature is present in [Buildkite #80082](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/80082#019f95ee-f9e7-4318-b8c8-1b9d66c30436), before the recent Kimi/K3 changes, so this is not a recent model-runner regression or a bad B200 node.

The TP1/PCP4 configuration became memory-tight when `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768` was added in #49294. Successful runs such as [Buildkite #80689](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/80689#019fa750-64e9-4fea-a523-627445bed59c) show that the workload's real peak fits: 159.66 GiB total non-KV memory on a 178.35 GiB B200. The intermittent OOM occurs because a roughly 24 GiB cached allocator segment cannot satisfy the next slightly larger 24.43 GiB FlashInfer workspace request. Expandable segments let that reserved memory grow/reuse instead of requiring a second contiguous allocation.

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR was found for the GLM-5.2 PCP FlashInfer MoE startup OOM using searches for `GLM-5.2 PCP OOM`, `lm-eval-pcp-4xb200`, and `expandable_segments GLM`.

- #50791 sizes a different FlashInfer sparse-MLA attention workspace for DCP.
- #49196 is an automated draft revert for an older PCP accuracy regression, not this profile-run MoE OOM.
- #34553 concerns a GLM-5 sparse-attention indexer OOM under serving load, not the startup MoE workspace failure here.

## Testing

- `git diff --check`
- parsed the YAML and verified both the allocator setting and retained 32K batch limit with Ruby's YAML parser
- repository pre-commit hooks run by `git commit`: passed
- GitHub pre-commit workflow: passed
- [Buildkite #82253 — LM Eval PCP (4xB200)](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/82253#019fcc6a-d072-4725-be6e-5a78fc7a6367): passed on `dgxB200-14` with exit status 0
  - unchanged TP2/PCP2 control: GSM8K passed
  - TP1/PCP4 with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`: profile run passed with 130.49 GiB of weights and a 28.33–30.23 GiB torch peak, the server started, and all 1,319 GSM8K examples passed

The allocator-only change does not alter model inputs, kernels, or numerics. The B200 model evaluation passed on the first validation iteration.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for Buildkite log analysis, root-cause isolation, implementation, and drafting this description.

- [ ] The human submitter has reviewed the changed line and CI evidence before marking this PR ready.

title: feat: add SSE keep-alive comments for idle streaming responses
body:
## Purpose

Add an SSE keep-alive mechanism for idle streaming responses on the `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` endpoints.

Reverse proxies and tunnels (Cloudflare Tunnel, NGINX `proxy_read_timeout`, AWS ALB, ...) close a streaming connection when no bytes are sent for a while. For SSE responses this happens during three idle phases:

1. **Queue wait** - the request is queued behind other requests for GPU.
2. **Prefill** - a long input prompt is processed before the first token.
3. **Decode gaps** - preemption or a slow span between tokens.

All three look identical at the network boundary: the generator yields nothing for a while. So a single idle timer around the final SSE generator covers them uniformly, without touching the scheduler, prefill, or engine.

A new `--sse-keep-alive-interval` CLI flag (integer seconds, default `0` = disabled) emits a spec-compliant SSE comment line `": keep-alive\n\n"` whenever the streaming generator has been idle for that many seconds. Comments are ignored by SSE clients but still count as bytes for proxy read-timeout logic, so they keep the connection alive during long queue/prefill/idle periods.

**Production context:** we are hitting this timeout issue on several vLLM servers at work. The proxy read timeouts close long-idle streaming responses (especially while queued or during long prefill), which is a pressing operational problem for us. So I implemented this feature and we are already running it in production against our serving stack, where it resolves the problem. This PR upstreams that validated implementation.

## Current solution

`with_sse_keep_alive(generator, interval)` wraps the SSE generator just before it is handed to FastAPI's `StreamingResponse`. It forwards every chunk unchanged and, whenever the generator is idle for `interval` seconds, yields a comment line `": keep-alive\n\n"`.

```python
return StreamingResponse(
    content=with_sse_keep_alive(generator, keep_alive_interval),
    media_type="text/event-stream",
)
```

When disabled (`interval <= 0`), the function returns the original generator unchanged, so the default path is byte-identical to vanilla vLLM and has zero overhead.

## Why this design

### Wrap the generator rather than an independent timer or middleware

An SSE response is a single ordered byte stream with exactly one producer. A background task emitting keep-alives would still have to write to that body, so it must serialize with the real chunks anyway, which is the wrapper with extra indirection and a race risk. A middleware would apply to every response, not just the two SSE endpoints, hiding the behavior. Wrapping at the router keeps it explicit and scoped.

### Retained `anext()` task, not `asyncio.wait_for`

`asyncio` forbids concurrent `__anext__` calls on a generator, and `asyncio.wait_for` cancels the awaited coroutine on timeout, leaving the generator partially advanced and corrupted. Instead, one retained `anext()` task owns the generator and `asyncio.wait(timeout=...)` lets us observe both an idle timeout and the next chunk without cancelling the task mid-advance. This mirrors the existing `merge_async_iterators()` in `vllm/utils/async_utils.py`.

### A comment, not an empty `data:` event

An empty `data:` event is valid SSE but dispatches an empty message to the client. A comment line is the spec-blessed mechanism that is guaranteed to be ignored, which is what a transparent keep-alive needs.

### One global CLI flag, no second timeout

`--sse-keep-alive-interval` (an integer number of seconds) controls the idle interval. We deliberately add no server-side timeout: a hung engine and a slow engine are indistinguishable at the SSE boundary, and a timeout would kill exactly the long queue/prefill cases this feature protects. A request-level timeout belongs client-side. vLLM has no such timeout, so we add none.

### Scope: chat and completions only

The first PR wires `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions`. `/v1/responses` and other SSE endpoints are deferred to keep the diff focused; they can be added later with the same one-line wrap.

## Edge cases and how they are handled

| Case | Handling |
|------|----------|
| Disabled (`0`, negative) | `with_sse_keep_alive` returns the generator unchanged; no task, no wrapper. |
| Silent start (queue/prefill) | Comment emitted before the first real chunk. |
| Fast streaming | No comments; all chunks forwarded in order. |
| Idle gap between chunks | Comment emitted; chunk order preserved, none dropped. |
| Empty generator | Returns immediately, no hang. |
| Upstream exception | Re-raised in the consumer's task. |
| Upstream `CancelledError` | Propagates to the consumer, not swallowed into endless comments. |
| `aclose()` / client disconnect | `finally` cancels the pending `anext()`, then closes the upstream generator so its cleanup (engine abort) runs deterministically. |
| Custom app without `app.state.args` | Routers read the option via `getattr` with a `0` default, so no `AttributeError`. |

## Cleanup guarantee

On normal completion, error, upstream cancellation, direct `aclose()`, or the disconnect path used by the pinned Uvicorn (ASGI 2.3, where Starlette cancels the streaming task), the wrapper's `finally` cancels the pending `anext()` task and explicitly closes the upstream generator. This matches `merge_async_iterators()` and gives deterministic engine-request cleanup instead of relying on garbage collection.

An ASGI 2.4 `send()`-failure window (where Starlette does not close the body iterator) is not reached by the pinned Uvicorn; if vLLM later adopts an ASGI 2.4 server, that window should be revisited separately.

## No existing PR (duplicate-work check)

Searched `vllm-project/vllm` for open PRs covering "keep-alive" / "sse-keep-alive" and for the author who offered an implementation in [#47647](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47647). No open PR implements this feature; the commenter (Sammy-Dabbas) described a similar approach but has not opened a PR. This PR is the one addressing the issue.

## Test Plan

```bash
# repo uv build + unit tests
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/test_sse_keep_alive.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/test_cli_args.py -k sse_keep_alive -v
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

## Test Result

- `tests/entrypoints/openai/test_sse_keep_alive.py`: **11 passed** (disabled identity, silent start, inter-chunk gaps, empty generator, exception propagation, cancellation, `aclose()`, and two real `StreamingResponse` integration tests).
- `tests/entrypoints/openai/test_cli_args.py -k sse_keep_alive`: **10 passed** (default `0`, positive parse, negative rejection, non-integer rejection).
- `ruff`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy`, and `git diff --check`: all clean.
- **Live production validation:** ported onto our production vLLM 0.26.0 serving stack (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731) with `--sse-keep-alive-interval 15`. A streaming `/v1/completions` request that waited idle in the queue emitted a `: keep-alive` comment exactly every 15 seconds for ~3 minutes, then produced its real tokens with correct ordering and terminated with `[DONE]`. No data dropped or reordered.

## AI assistance disclosure

This contribution was developed with assistance from GitHub Copilot (running DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731) and GPT5.6-Sun. I, Dieter Schwarzmann (fuzzifikation), reviewed every changed line, ran the tests, and am responsible for the change end-to-end. I corrected issues and worked through several approaches until I was happy with simplicity, edge-cases, and minimal impact to the codebase.

- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4 sparse-decode MLA kernel wedges in a spin loop with no timeout and no diagnostic (device-level capture on sm_103; surfaces 300 s later as an unrelated DeepGEMM assert)
body:
### Your current environment

```text
- Hardware: 8× NVIDIA B300 SXM6 (sm_103), single node, NVLink
- vLLM: official image vllm/vllm-openai:v0.26.0, built from ffd46bfab212 (two commits
        behind the v0.26.0 tag 568afb3a1380; both are CI/release-pipeline only, no
        runtime code), plus upstream commit de6ec294ef07 cherry-picked.
        No other source changes.
- FlashMLA: vllm-project/FlashMLA @ a8f794d1251cbfd88a5011445dd5582289c727e4
            (the GIT_TAG pinned by cmake/external_projects/flashmla.cmake)
- CUTLASS:  NVIDIA/cutlass @ 147f5673d0c1c3dcf66f78d677fd647e4a020219
            (FlashMLA's csrc/cutlass submodule)
- Model: DeepSeek-V4-Pro (DSpark), FP8/MXFP4
- Parallelism: EP4/DEP4, PD disaggregation (prefill and decode as separate instances)
- Executor: multiproc (NOT Ray)
- cudagraph_mode: FULL_AND_PIECEWISE; VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH auto-enabled
  for DeepseekV4ForCausalLM
- Attention backend: FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4
```

### What this report is

This is **not** a root-cause report. It is an evidence dump plus one narrow,
self-contained request:

> The spin loops in the TMEM allocation path of the sparse-decode MLA kernel have
> **no timeout and no diagnostic**. When they stall, the only surviving evidence is an
> unrelated assert 300 s later, in a different library.

That request stands on its own, independent of everything else below.

### Describe the bug

Under sustained serving, roughly **once every few hours**, one rank wedges. Externally
it looks like a DeepGEMM failure:

```text
DeepGEMM NVLink barrier timeout (300s): rank=3, counter=60086137, signal=3, target=4, phase=0, sign=0, tag=1
Assertion failed: .../deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/comm/barrier.cuh:72, condition: false and "NVLink barrier timeout"
DeepGEMM NVLink barrier timeout (300s): rank=0, counter=60086137, ...
DeepGEMM NVLink barrier timeout (300s): rank=1, counter=60086137, ...
```

All three surviving ranks report the **same** `counter` and `signal=3, target=4`: the
missing signal is from the wedged rank, which never got that far. **This is a downstream
symptom.** We captured a live wedge with `cuda-gdb`; the relevant excerpts are below.

### Device-level evidence

The wedged GPU sits at **100 % utilization but at idle-level power**. Measured on this
box, same stack, same session:

| state | utilization | power |
| --- | --- | --- |
| idle | 0 % | 233 W |
| loaded (16 concurrent requests) | 37–100 % | 328–435 W |
| **wedged** | **100 %** | **234 W** |

So it is not power that identifies a wedge, it is *utilization pinned high while power
stays at idle level* — a resident kernel spinning without doing work.

```text
Kernel 0, grid 559302, device 2, Active
GridDim (2,74,1) = 148 blocks   BlockDim (512,1,1)   cluster dim (2,1,1)
SMs Mask -> only SM 56 and SM 57
sm100::fwd_for_small_topk::head128::flash_fwd_splitkv_mla_fp8_sparse_kernel<
    sm100::fwd_for_small_topk::head128::KernelTemplate<(SparseAttnFwdMode)1, 512> >
```

`SparseAttnFwdMode` is `{Prefill = 0, DecodeWithSplitKV = 1}` (`csrc/params.h:171`), so
this is the **decode** specialization (`instantiations/phase1_decode_k512.cu`), reached
via `flash_mla_with_kvcache(topk != None)` → `flash_mla_cuda.sparse_decode_fwd`.

146 of the 148 blocks retired normally. The two that remain are `(0,31,0)` and
`(1,31,0)` — exactly **one thread-block cluster**.

```text
Device 2 SM 57  block (1,31,0)     (= CTA 1 of the cluster)
Wp  ActiveLanes  Divergent   ActivePC     First active threadIdx
*0  0xfffffffe   0x00000001  0x...4a20    (65,0,0)   -> threadIdx 65 => warp_idx == 2
 1..15  0xffffffff  0x0      0x...4b80    UCGABAR_WAIT

Device 2 SM 56  block (0,31,0)     (= CTA 0)
 all 16 warps at 0x...4b80  UCGABAR_WAIT (no divergence)
```

Lane 0 of that warp (threadIdx 64) is alone at a different PC, in this loop:

```text
   SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P0, [R5+0x8], R4
   @!P0 NANOSLEEP.SYNCS 0x989680        ; 10 ms backoff
=> @!P0 SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64 P0, [R5+0x8], R4
   @!P0 BRA <loop>                      ; no timeout, no escape path
```

The kernel contains exactly **two** `UCGABAR_WAIT` sites, at `+0x0f00` and `+0x16c10`,
matching the two `ku::barrier_cluster_arrive_relaxed(); ku::barrier_cluster_wait_acquire();`
pairs in `phase1.cuh` (lines 88-89 and 923-924). The 31 waiting warps are at `+0x0f00`,
i.e. the **prologue** cluster barrier, so the wedged lane is stuck *before*
`phase1.cuh:88`.

### The allocation protocol, read from the shipped cubin

The shipped `_flashmla_C.abi3.so` (fatbin `arch = sm_100f`, **no PTX embedded**, so no
JIT is involved) disassembles to an **asymmetric CTA-pair protocol** for
`cute::TMEM::Allocator2Sm().allocate(512, smem.tmem_start_addr.data())`:

```text
/*0910*/ LDS.U8 R4, [R5+0x1c]      ; per-CTA "alloc permit relinquished" flag
/*0950*/ @P0 BRA <trap>            ; if != 0 -> __cuda_sm10x_tcgen05_guardrail_trap_phase_invalid
/*09a0*/ @!P1 BRA 0xbf0            ; cta_id==1 skips allocation entirely and only waits
/*09b0*/ ELECT P0                  ; compiler-generated
/*0a00*/ UTCATOMSWS.2CTA.FIND_AND_SET.ALIGN UP0, UR4, UR4   ; only CTA 0 allocates
/*0a30*/ NANOSLEEP 0x64 ; /*0a60*/ retry ; /*0a80*/ BRA.U !UP0, 0xa30
                                   ; CTA 0 retry loop -- no timeout
/*0ad0*/ SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P0, [R5+0x8], R8    ; CTA 0 waits on its own barrier
/*0b70*/ SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED RZ, [R11+URZ], R16=4      ; arrive on the PEER's barrier
/*0ba0*/ STAS [R10.64], R6                                  ; push result into peer's DSMEM
/*0bf0*/ <- where CTA 1 lands
/*0c10*/ ELECT P0
/*0c50*/ SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P0, [R5+0x8], R4    ; CTA 1 waits here
/*0c80*/ @!P0 BRA <cold spin loop>                          ; <- where we are wedged
/*16cf0*/ BRA 0xc90                                         ; on success, jump back
/*0c90*/ LDS R4, [R15+0x36d30]                              ; ...and read smem.tmem_start_addr
```

Address encoding (from `LEA R5, SR_CgaCtaId, 0x40, 0x18`): **`R5 = (cta_id << 24) | 0x40`**,
i.e. these are DSMEM addresses whose high byte is the CTA index. The live capture read
`R5 = 0x1000040`, which independently confirms the wedged CTA is **CTA 1**.

`PRMT R11, R7(=cta^1), 0x654, R14(=R5+8)` evaluates to `((cta^1) << 24) | 0x48`, so CTA 0's
`ARRIVE` targets `0x1000048` — **exactly** the address CTA 1 is waiting on. The address
pairing is exact.

### The `-lineinfo` rebuild and its self-check

vLLM's CMake compiles the vendored FlashMLA sources itself
(`set_gencode_flags_for_srcs`) and **drops the `-lineinfo`** that FlashMLA's own
`setup.py` would pass, so the shipped `.so` carries no line information. We rebuilt
`phase1_decode_k512.cu` with `-lineinfo` (nvcc 13.0.88, `sm_100f`, otherwise FlashMLA's
own nvcc flags) and cross-checked four anchors against the shipped cubin:

| offset | rebuilt | shipped | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `+0x0DA0` | `WARPSYNC.ALL` | `WARPSYNC.ALL` | match |
| `+0x0EC0` | `UCGABAR_ARV` | `UCGABAR_ARV` | match |
| `+0x0F00` | `UCGABAR_WAIT` | `UCGABAR_WAIT` | match |
| `+0x16CD0` | `IMAD.MOV.U32 R9,RZ,RZ,-0x1` | `@!P0 SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64` | **mismatch** |

The cold-block region shifted. Structural counts are identical
(`UCGABAR_ARV` 2/2, `UCGABAR_WAIT` 2/2, `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64` 104/104,
`UTCATOMSWS` 3/3) and the hot path is byte-identical, so we mapped by symbol/structure
rather than by offset.

**What the line info does establish** (in the equivalent build):

- `UTCATOMSWS.2CTA.FIND_AND_SET` comes from
  `cute/arch/tmem_allocator_sm100.hpp:141` — the operand line of the
  `tcgen05.alloc.cta_group::2.sync.aligned.shared::cta.b32` asm in
  `Allocator2Sm::allocate()`;
- `UTCATOMSWS.AND` comes from `:166` (`free()`), enclosing source `phase1.cuh:394`;
- `release_allocation_lock()` = `:176`, which writes 1 to the `[R5+0x1c]` flag;
- the `BPT.TRAP` site = `phase1.cuh:65`
  (`KU_TRAP_ONLY_DEVICE_ASSERT(tmem_start_addr == 0)`);
- `UCGABAR_ARV` = `kerutils/.../intrinsics.cuh:58`, confirming `+0x0EC0/+0x0F00` is the
  **prologue** cluster barrier.

**What it does NOT establish**: because the `+0x16CD0` anchor did not match, the claim
that *the live `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64` is the allocation completion wait* remains a
strong structural / dataflow inference (its exit branch returns to the basic block that
reads `tmem_start_addr`) — **not** an offset-based proof. We are deliberately not
upgrading it.

### What we could and could not determine about the stall

| check | result |
| --- | --- |
| CTA 1 expected phase vs its local phase byte | `R4 = 0` and `[R5+0x10] = 0`; `R4 = [R5+0x10] << 31` — **internally consistent** |
| CTA 0's phase byte | **not captured** — the container was gone before we thought to read it |
| barrier address pairing | **exact** (see above) |
| transaction/count matching | **undetermined** — CTA 0 arrives with `R16 = 4`; CTA 1's expectation is encoded in the mbarrier word `0x7ffff800001ffffe`, whose field layout we will not guess at |
| guardrail branch taken? | **no evidence** — `guardrail` / `tcgen05` / `phase_invalid` / `trap` all have 0 hits in the container log; the `[R5+0x1c]` byte itself was not captured |

So we cannot presently distinguish between a phase mismatch, a peer DSMEM write that
never became visible, and hardware state that never advanced. A phase mismatch is **one**
candidate, noted only because the guardrail trap path at `[R5+0x1c] != 0` bypasses the
`ATOMS.XOR` that toggles the phase byte — we have **no** evidence that path ran, and CTA 0's
phase byte was never captured.

### What we ruled out

- **Not NCCL.** PyTorch's NCCL watchdog never fired — 26 minutes after the wedge, with
  the default 600 s timeout. The stuck kernel is a compute kernel, not a NCCL kernel.
- **Not Ray.** multiproc executor; no Ray Compiled-DAG in this stack.
- **No local source changes beyond cherry-picking `de6ec294ef07`.** We verified that our
  two local kernel patches were *not* applied to this image.
- **Not JIT.** The shipped `.so` embeds no PTX; the `sm_100f` cubin runs directly.
- **Not a source-level misuse of `Allocator2Sm`.** We verified the source-visible/static
  preconditions: both CTAs pass an identical `dst_ptr` (we computed
  `SharedMemoryPlan`'s layout by hand and it lands on `0x36D30`, matching the
  `STS`/`LDS` targets in the SASS, with the barrier region at `0x36C20` also matching),
  both use `warp_idx == 2` for `allocate` and `warp_idx == 0` for `free`, and the column
  count is a constant 512 on both sides. (We have **not** observed the runtime
  preconditions — the active mask at the moment of issue, and the absence of a
  concurrently issuing warp.)
- **Not thermal / clocks.** 30–38 °C, clocks at max, all throttle reasons Not Active.
- **No Xid** in `dmesg`.

### What we are asking for

Both spin loops in this path — CTA 0's `FIND_AND_SET` retry loop and CTA 1's completion
wait — carry **no timeout and no diagnostic**. Once the protocol stalls, the kernel hangs
forever, and the only evidence that survives is an unrelated assert 300 s later in a
different library.

⚠️ These loops are **generated by ptxas** when lowering
`tcgen05.alloc.cta_group::2.sync.aligned`; they are **not** hand-written loops in vLLM,
FlashMLA or CUTLASS, so "add a `printf`" is not something any of those layers can simply
do. We are therefore asking for guidance rather than proposing a patch:

> **Could maintainers advise the correct owner and the supported diagnostic path for a
> stalled `tcgen05.alloc.cta_group::2` protocol? If a source-level mitigation or
> instrumentation is possible in FlashMLA or CUTLASS, we can build and test it — we have
> the hardware, the workload, and a capture procedure that has already produced one live
> `cuda-gdb` session on a wedged rank.**

For calibration of the *user-visible impact* only — not as an implementation template,
since it sits at a different layer — DeepGEMM (**a different dependency**, unrelated to
FlashMLA's source tree) does time out its own `nvlink_barrier` after 300 s and prints the
rank/counter/signal state. That printout is what eventually gave us a thread to pull; the
TMEM allocation stall gave us nothing.

Secondary question: has anyone seen a `tcgen05` TMEM allocation stall on Blackwell? Our
searches of this repo, FlashMLA and CUTLASS turned up no publicly indexed report of the
same shape — which of course only means there is no indexed precedent.

### Relationship to #49922 (closest neighbour — please read this first)

Issue #49922 is the nearest report: same hardware class (B300), same model
(DeepSeek-V4-Pro), same vLLM 0.26 line, and it touches the same file (`phase1.cuh`).
`de6ec294ef07` is the fix discussed there.

The relationship is:

- `de6ec294ef07` **removed the failure mode reported in #49922** for us as well — the
  `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` / tensormap assertions are gone from our runs.
- **This report is a different observation captured on top of that commit**: a silent
  device-side wedge with **no error, no assertion and no CUDA error** from the kernel
  itself, in the same kernel family.
- **Whether the two share a cause is not established.** We are not claiming #49922 is
  unfixed, and we are not claiming this is a regression of that fix. If maintainers
  believe they are the same underlying issue, we are happy to move this evidence there.

### Other related reports

- #40969 — same external symptom (100 % SM utilization, zero throughput, no NCCL timeout,
  no OOM). That thread contains reports later attributed to Ray Compiled-DAG / NCCL
  2.30.4 NVLS (NVIDIA/nccl#2167), **but it also contains unresolved reports under
  different controls** (including one under `enforce_eager=True`). Our capture differs
  materially: single node, no Ray, NCCL watchdog silent, and a device-level capture
  pointing at a compute kernel.
- #50774, #50842 — related reports in the same backend / kernel family
  (`FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, DSpark spec decode). Listed for context only; we are **not**
  suggesting a shared mechanism.
- NVIDIA/cutlass#2230 — TMEM races in the CuTe tutorials; the maintainer notes that
  `ptxas --g-tensor-memory-access-check` performs **runtime** TMEM access checks.
  Different failure mode (access violation vs. allocation stall), but the flag may help
  others.

### Reproduction

We do not have a reliable reproducer. The rate is roughly one wedge per several hours of
sustained benchmarking at concurrency 32–96; ~20 consecutive benchmark rungs can pass
cleanly in between. We are currently running a burst/idle cycling harness to try to raise
the rate (130 cycles / 144 minutes so far with no hit).

If maintainers can suggest instrumentation, we can carry it in our image and report back
— we have the hardware, the workload, and a capture procedure that has already produced
one live `cuda-gdb` session on a wedged rank.

title: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731: KV cache holds only 150K tokens in 7.7 GiB (56 bytes/token), max_model_len capped at ~121344 on H20 TP=2
body:
# DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731: KV cache holds only 150K tokens in 7.7 GiB (56 bytes/token), max_model_len capped at ~121344 on H20 TP=2

## Summary

`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` uses **~8× more KV cache per token** than `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` (preview), despite both checkpoints having identical `compress_ratios` / `sliding_window` / `num_hidden_layers`. This caps `max_model_len` at ~121344 on H20 TP=2, vs 912128 for the preview.

## Environment

- vLLM: 0.26.0
- GPU: 2× H20 (SM90, 95 GiB), TP=2
- `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --tensor-parallel-size 2` (MTP speculative, not DSpark)

## Measured per-token KV (both public checkpoints, same hardware/vLLM)

| | `DeepSeek-V4-Flash` (preview) | `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` |
|---|---|---|
| KV pool | 7.01 GiB | 7.71 GiB |
| GPU KV cache size | **1,009,661 tokens** | **150,992 tokens** |
| max_model_len that fits | 912,128 (1.11x concurrency) | 121,344 (1.24x concurrency) |
| **per-token KV** | **~7.2 bytes** | **~56 bytes (8× larger)** |

Both use `fp8_ds_mla` KV format, `DEEPSEEK_SPARSE_SWA` backend, block_size 256, 43 layers.

## Config comparison

Both configs contain `compress_ratios`, `sliding_window: 128`, `expert_dtype: "fp4"`. The `compress_ratios` pattern is identical (`[0, 0, 4, 128, 4, 128, ...]`); 0731 has 2 extra trailing zeros.

The **only** structural difference: 0731 adds DSpark fields (`dspark_target_layer_ids: [40, 41, 42]`, `dspark_block_size`, `dspark_markov_rank`, `dspark_noise_token_id`). Preview has none of these.

## What I've checked in source (vLLM 0.26.0)

- `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py:188`: `compress_ratio = max(1, config.compress_ratios[layer_id])` — ratio 0 → 1, and `get_kv_cache_spec` returns `None` for `compress_ratio <= 1` (SWA, allocated separately). Both models should produce identical KV specs for layers 0–42.
- Both checkpoints have identical weight keys (incl. `layers.*.attn.compressor.*`, `layers.*.attn.indexer.*`).
- 0731 uses 5 KV cache groups (per #50700): full MLA/indexer, C4, C128, two SWA groups.

## Questions

1. Is **56 bytes/token** the expected per-token KV cost for 0731's 5-group hybrid cache, or is the hybrid KV cache manager over-allocating (padding waste across groups)?
2. The paper (arXiv 2606.19348) states V4-Flash uses ~7% of V3.2's KV cache at 1M context. 56 bytes/token caps `max_model_len` at ~121K on H20 TP=2 — is there a way to reduce per-token cost?
3. Why do two checkpoints with identical `compress_ratios` produce 8× different per-token KV (7.2 vs 56 bytes)? Could the DSpark config fields cause vLLM to allocate extra KV even when running MTP (not DSpark)?

## Attempted workarounds (all failed on 0731)

- `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`: passes max_len check but OOMs during `profile_cudagraph_memory` (SWA → full MLA conversion increases KV).
- `--kv-cache-memory 11.44GiB` (vLLM's "fully utilize" suggestion): OOMs (skips profiling, no activation headroom).
- `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.97`: still OOMs during profiling.

Related: #50700 (5-group KV connector), #50774 (compress_ratio=1 SWA crash).

title: [Bugfix] Propagate decode SWA index width for DSpark + FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4
body:
DSpark non-causal draft batches allocate `decode_swa_indices` with
`noncausal_index_width` (wider than `window_size`). FlashInfer DSV4 sparse
MLA still reshaped / passed `self.window_size` into
`build_flashinfer_mixed_sparse_indices`, which crashes those drafts, e.g.:

```
RuntimeError: shape '[7, 128]' is invalid for input of size 1792
(at `flashinfer_sparse.py` `_build_sparse_index_metadata` when reshaping
`decode_swa_indices`).
```

- Add `decode_swa_width` to `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadata` and set it in the SWA
  builder (`window_size` or `noncausal_index_width`).
- Use that width in FlashInfer `_build_sparse_index_metadata` and the ROCM
  ragged conversion path.

## Test Plan
- [x] `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py`
- [x] Manual: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark with `attention_backend: FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`

title: [Bugfix][MLA] TritonMLA: fix illegal memory access on causal multi-token decode
body:
## Purpose
`TritonMLA` declared single-token decode support, so a speculative-decode verify block reached `forward_mqa` unflattened: `query_len * num_reqs` query rows against `num_reqs` rows of `block_table` / `seq_lens`. `decode_attention_fwd` launches one program per query row and indexes `tl.load(B_Seqlen + cur_batch)`, so every row past `num_decodes` is an out-of-bounds read.

Reaching it takes a group whose reorder threshold is raised past 1. Ordinary MLA spec decode does not qualify: `TritonMLAMetadataBuilder` inherits `query_len_support = SINGLE_ONLY`, so multi-token queries route to prefill. The threshold is raised by the non-causal route (DSpark draft) which sets its flags after the base `__init__` has asserted `SINGLE_ONLY ⇒ threshold == 1`.
`build()` then splits a *causal* batch with the raised threshold, and `forward_mqa` expands tables only under `if not causal`. Where that happens there is no fallback on either affected platform:

- **NVIDIA sm_86** — `triton_mla` is the only MLA backend whose   `supports_compute_capability` admits `major == 8` (CUTLASS/FlashInfer require 10,   FlashAttn 9, FlashMLA 9 or 10). Reported as `Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal   memory access` (#51848).
- **ROCm without AITER MLA** — `rocm.py` falls back to `[TRITON_MLA]` alone.

Fixes #51848.

On Kimi-K3 + DSpark, TP8, MI325: (18.01 → 45.00 tok/s), no quality regression (verified on gsm8k: **95%**)

## The fix
`decode_attention_fwd` has no causal flag, but it reads each row's KV extent from `seq_lens`. A uniform verify block is a contiguous suffix, so intra-block causality is expressible as per-row extents: flatten to one decode row per query token and give row `t` extent `seq_len - (query_len - 1 - t)`.

1. `forward_mqa`: derive `query_len` from `q.shape[0] // seq_lens.shape[0]` and    expand `block_table` / `seq_lens` to match, causal or non-causal.
2. `_cudagraph_support` → `UNIFORM_BATCH`, `query_len_support` → `UNIFORM`, so the    reorder threshold admits `query_len > 1`. `attn_logits` workspace grows to match  (workspace locks after capture).
3. `MLAAttentionSpec.merge()` asserts layers agree on  `non_causal_multi_token_decode` instead of `any()`, so a non-causal draft group cannot be merged with a causal target group.

## Testing

Validated on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (`ba07e4a48f`), gfx942. Rebased onto `origin/main` `9fd750f00d`

### Unit tests

`tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_mla_causal_verify_flatten.py` (new, 15) plus `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py` (87): **102 passed**. The new file replaces the kernel with a spy and asserts on the `block_table` and `seq_lens` the backend actually submits, so it needs no GPU or Triton runtime.

### The decode path actually taken

`tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` already covers this: `spec_decode_small` (4x4) and `spec_decode_medium` (6x8) install an ngram `SpeculativeConfig`, with `torch` SDPA as reference. `decode_attention_fwd` was instrumented to confirm which path runs.

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0 \
  pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -q -k "1.0-1.0-auto-1-"
```

| | result | TritonMLA decode launches |
|---|---|---|
| before, spec_decode only | 4 passed, 16 skipped | 0 (routed to prefill) |
| after, spec_decode only | 4 passed, 16 skipped | 4, causal staircase |
| before, all batch specs | 24 passed, 96 skipped | 12 (single-token) |
| after, all batch specs | 24 passed, 96 skipped | 16 (12 + 4 causal) |

The "after, all batch specs" row re-verified on 2026-08-21 against the final tree, with 16 launches and the same shapes:

```
x2  q_rows=1   bt_rows=1   seq_lens[:8]=[1024]
x4  q_rows=2   bt_rows=2   seq_lens[:8]=[32, 40]
x2  q_rows=3   bt_rows=3   seq_lens[:8]=[512, 1024, 2048]
x2  q_rows=8   bt_rows=8   seq_lens[:8]=[128, 256, 512, 1024]
x2  q_rows=16  bt_rows=16  seq_lens[:8]=[125, 126, 127, 128, 253, 254, 255, 256]
x2  q_rows=32  bt_rows=32  seq_lens[:8]=[2048]
x2  q_rows=48  bt_rows=48  seq_lens[:8]=[505, 506, 507, 508, 509, 510, 511, 512]
```

Extents match `seq_len - (query_len-1-t)`. The 12 single-token launches are unchanged in count and shape, so the ordinary decode path does not regress. 
`bt_rows == q_rows` throughout, confirming the `block_table` expansion tracks the flatten. Skips are prefill-backend unavailability on this platform, not decode skips.

## Model evaluation

GSM8K, all 1,319 questions, greedy (`temperature=0`, `seed=42`), `max_tokens=1024`, 8 concurrent clients, raw completions:

| | |
|---|---|
| accuracy | **0.9507** (1254 / 1319) |
| mean acceptance length | **3.279** of max 4.0, 40,823 drafts |
| throughput | 0.449 q/s, 46.0 tok/s, 135,175 output tokens |
| wall | 2,936 s |
| worker faults / NaNs | none |

Configuration: gfx942, 8x MI325X, TP8 + EP, target `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` on `ROCM_AITER_MLA`, drafter `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` on `TRITON_MLA` via `--attention-backend`, `dspark` method with 3 speculative tokens, 32,384 ctx. 

```bash
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel  --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors   --enable-auto-tool-choice   --tool-call-parser kimi_k3   --reasoning-parser kimi_k3   --enable-prompt-tokens-details   --mm-encoder-tp-mode data   --max-model-len 32384 --max-num-seqs 8  --speculative-config '{ "model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark", "num_speculative_tokens":3, "method": "dspark", "attention_backend": "TRITON_MLA", "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic", "rejection_sample_method": "block"}'
```


Spec-Bench:
```bash
---------------Speculative Decoding---------------
Acceptance rate (%):                     63.11     
Acceptance length:                       2.89      
Drafts:                                  16798     
Draft tokens:                            50394     
Accepted tokens:                         31804     
Per-position acceptance (%):
  Position 0:                            81.74     
  Position 1:                            61.65     
  Position 2:                            45.94     
==================================================
```
**The drafter is on TRITON_MLA precisely because this is the path the PR fixes.**

**There is no same-flags unpatched baseline.** Without this patch the above configuration is the crash the PR fixes, so "unpatched, same flags" does not produce a number. This run is evidence that the causal flatten is correct under sustained load, not a before/after comparison.

Independently corroborated by @maeehart on gfx942, 8x MI325X, TP8+EP, 7 spec tokens, same target/draft backend pairing, 262144 ctx: **GSM8K 95.6% strict and flexible over all 1,319 questions**, needle retrieval passed at 65K/131K/250K, 98.26% prefix-cache hit, no faults or NaNs. Their run bundles #50578 and AITER
fixes, so it is integration evidence rather than an isolated measurement. 

@reger-men's gfx950 throughput numbers were obtained with a different implementation and are explicitly **not** a measurement of this PR.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| cudagraph mode | PIECEWISE (downgraded) | **FULL + PIECEWISE** |
| throughput | 13.01 tok/s | **61.3 tok/s (4.0×)** |
| per-step latency | 233.9 ms | **50.4 ms** |

Removing per-launch overhead also removed cross-rank arrival skew that had been making TP collectives spin-wait: `vllm::all_reduce` 2.157 s (60.8% of Self CUDA) → 0.061 s (2.85%), arrival spread 313.8 µs → 7.1 µs.

## Correctness

Same config (61.3 tok/s, including two unrelated tuning changes not in this PR):

| benchmark | result |
|---|---|
| GSM8K, full test set (1319) | **97.2%** (1282/1319), 95% CI [96.3, 98.1] |
| GPQA Diamond, 0-shot CoT (198) | **90.9%** flexible / **90.4%** strict |

Hardware:

- [x] Boots with FULL cudagraph capture, no downgrade message
- [x] GSM8K 97.2%, GPQA Diamond 90.9%
- [x] Concurrency sweep 1→128, zero errors across 100 800 generated tokens
- [x] Causal-tail A/B showing acceptance is unaffected
- [x] NVIDIA sm_86 — [nickus](https://github.com/nickus) on 4x RTX 3090: illegal memory access without the patch, serves with it


## AI assistance

AI assistance was used. The submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above.

## Related work
- [#47310](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47310)  predates this PR and proposes the `query_len_support` half of this change and diagnoses the same flag coupling — credit there for that analysis. It has gone stale: Unmodified since 2026-07-09.
-  [#51171](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51171)  (open, 2026-08-05) also corrects cudagraph support reporting for  non-causal draft groups, but keys a conditional `get_cudagraph_support`   override on `non_causal_multi_token_decode`. That leaves the *causal* path   still declaring single-token support — which is this bug. Causal is the base   case, so the flag pair is set unconditionally here. The two changes are   compatible; #51171 additionally moves an AITER host sync out of `forward_mqa`,   which this PR does not touch.
- [#51685](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51685) (open, 2026-08-10) reworks the same decode path for a native fp8 KV cache (`triton_mla.py` +97/-33). Different purpose, no overlap in intent.
-  [#51705](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51705)  (open, 2026-08-10) is a Kimi-K3 DSpark decode-context-parallelism  feature (+760/-107) that happens to carry this PR's `MLAAttentionSpec.merge()`
  fix verbatim — the same `any()` → set-and-pop rewrite under a byte-identical   assertion message, differing only in a local variable name. This PR is six days   earlier and is scoped to the bug; #51705 needs the same correction as a   prerequisite for its own grouping work. 
- [#51848](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51848) is an issue, not a PR, and was closed on 2026-08-11. It is the independent sm_86 report of this bug. Its reporter confirmed there that this PR supersedes it and declined to open a competing one.
- [#50911](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50911) is complementary: the non-causal draft path on TokenSpeed/NVIDIA. No file overlap. 
- [#52218](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52218) (draft, opened 2026-08-13) — *"[Attention] Support speculative decode in Triton MLA"*. Same fix, same mechanism: uniform multi-token query support, the verify block flattened to decode rows, causal prefix lengths per row, padding rows clamped, split-KV workspace grown. This PR predates it by nine days and is a superset: #52218 is a draft touching only `triton_mla.py`, and does not correct `MLAAttentionSpec.merge()`, so a non-causal draft group can still be merged into a causal target group.

title: [Bug]: CPU offload cannot pin regions of 512 GiB or more (single cudaHostRegister call)
body:
### Your current environment

GLM-5.2 on 4×H200 NVL, TP4/DCP4, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, vLLM `0.26.1rc1.dev255+g5e35a6f4f`, with CPU offload:

```
--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"block_size":256,"cpu_bytes_to_use":600000000000}}'
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`pin_mmap_region` registers the whole offload region with one `cudaHostRegister` call ([`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py:136`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py#L136)). A single registration of 512 GiB or more fails with `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` regardless of free memory, so any `cpu_bytes_to_use` at or above ~550e9 never gets pinned.

Bracketed with a standalone script (mmap in `/dev/shm` + `posix_fallocate` + `cudaHostRegister`), one process, 1.3 TB host RAM free, no model loaded:

| region size | result |
|---|---|
| 20 / 300 / 400 / 500 GB | success, ~0.1 s per GB |
| 549.0e9 (511.29 GiB) | success, 55.3 s |
| 549.7e9 (511.96 GiB) | success, 55.4 s |
| 549.9e9 (512.15 GiB) | **fails, code=2** |
| 551e9 / 600e9 | fails, code=2 |

So the ceiling is 512 GiB = 549,755,813,888 bytes per call. Rank count is irrelevant — one process reproduces it with 809 GB still available. I could not find this documented; NVIDIA forum reports mention other, lower ceilings in other setups (DAX-mapped memory, older drivers), so treating any single large registration as safe looks wrong in general.

This became reachable with #50094: before it each rank pinned its own `cpu_bytes_to_use / world_size` buffer (150 GB here) through torch's pinned allocator, all far below the ceiling; after it one shared region is registered in full by every rank.

Until #50070 lands, the failure is also mis-reported: the failed registration latches an error that the next kernel launch picks up, so the engine dies in `warm_v1_block_table_kernels` with `AcceleratorError: CUDA error: out of memory` on a 64-byte `torch.arange` while GiBs are free.

Workaround: keep `cpu_bytes_to_use` under 512 GiB.

AI assisted.
