title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Fall back when MADV_POPULATE_WRITE is unsupported
body:
Fixes #44888

## Why this PR

`SharedOffloadRegion.__init__` unconditionally issues `madvise(MADV_POPULATE_WRITE, …)` on its shared mmap. On Linux < 5.14 (RHEL 8 ships 4.18) the syscall returns `EINVAL`, so any vLLM startup that touches `TieringOffloadingSpec` aborts before KV offloading can register.

This PR probes the advice once after mmap creation and falls back to a no-mutation NumPy read-modify-write (`|= 0`) that triggers the same page fault without altering any existing bytes. Other `OSError`s (e.g. `EIO`) propagate.

## Changes

`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/shared_offload_region.py` (+32 / -6):

- Module-level helpers `_madvise_populate_write` / `_fallback_populate_write` are the test seams (`mmap.mmap` is an immutable C type on Python 3.12+ and cannot be subclassed/patched).
- `_get_populate_write_fn(mmap_obj)` probes once via `_madvise_populate_write(mmap_obj, 0, PAGESIZE)`. On `OSError(EINVAL)`, logs once and returns `_fallback_populate_write` (which uses `arr[::PAGESIZE] |= 0` — no byte mutation, still faults in the page). Other `OSError`s propagate.
- The ranked and unranked call sites in `__init__` now invoke the returned helper instead of `mmap_obj.madvise(...)` directly. Behaviour on kernels ≥ 5.14 is unchanged.

`tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py` (+107 / -6):

- `test_madvise_success_selects_madvise_population` — spies on both helpers; asserts 1 probe + N populate calls, fallback 0 times.
- `test_madvise_einval_smoke` — constructor completes when the probe raises `EINVAL`.
- `test_fallback_populate_write_preserves_existing_bytes` — plants non-zero sentinels at each page head, drives `_fallback_populate_write` directly, asserts the sentinels survive. This is the test that distinguishes `= 0` from `|= 0`.
- `test_madvise_unexpected_oserror_propagates` — non-`EINVAL` `OSError`s propagate out of `__init__`.

`#44913` (guygir, OPEN since 2026-06) targets the same bug but was stalled on pre-commit / CI failures caused by `mmap.mmap` subclassing. The three commits on top of its merged base (`5031c2e`) — `990b8d6` (Python 3.12+ test rewrite), `10f7bfb` (`|= 0` per @orozery's review), `3233a6f` (route the probe through `_madvise_populate_write` so the module-level test seam actually intercepts it) — address those root causes.

## Test results

The submitter ran `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py -v` on two kernel versions:

- **Linux 5.14+** (development host, kernel accepts `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE`): 32 passed in 16.11s. Confirms the probe succeeds and the native path is selected.
- **Linux 5.4.0-155-generic** (Ubuntu, kernel rejects `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE` with `EINVAL`): 32 passed in 26.94s. Confirms end-to-end that the probe routes through `_madvise_populate_write`, the kernel returns `EINVAL`, and the `|= 0` fallback path executes without altering existing bytes.

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
    vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/shared_offload_region.py \
    tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py
# 12 hooks PASSED
```

No model-evaluation results are reported because this change does not affect model output, accuracy, or serving throughput — it only adds a fallback for the mmap pre-fault on kernels that lack the advice.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with the assistance of Claude (Anthropic). All code changes were reviewed line-by-line by the human submitter and the relevant tests were run on a Linux runner before submission, per the project's contribution policy.

title: [ROCm] Enable shared-expert multi-stream overlap on ROCm
body:
# [ROCm] Enable shared-expert multi-stream overlap on ROCm

## What this PR does

1. `current_platform.is_cuda()` -> `is_cuda_alike()` in
   `SharedExperts._determine_shared_experts_order`, so ROCm can take the
   `MULTI_STREAM_OVERLAPPED` path. Today the aux stream is allocated on ROCm and
   never used, and the shared expert always runs serially with the routed
   experts.

## Dependencies

**This must land on top of #52033.** The flip on its own is not safe on a tree
that predates #48223: it enables the aux stream over the old raw `wait_stream`
fork/join, and Kimi-K3 at TP=8 dies during warmup on all 8 ranks. #48111 already
flagged the one-liner as insufficient. #52033 supplies the event-based fork/join,
launch-before-dispatch, and the input clone — and it contains this same
`is_cuda_alike()` flip, so **if #52033 lands as written this PR is fully
subsumed and should simply be closed.**

**It also needs #50618** (`[ROCm][Bugfix] Fix wvSplitK OOB reads on strided
activations`), for the reason below.


The defect is in `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms.cu`. `wvSplitK` bounds its LDS
activation preload by `Kap * N` (**stride** × rows) instead of
`(N-1)*Kap + K`. For a dense, offset-0 tensor those are equal, so the bug is
invisible. For a **strided view of a wider buffer it over-reads by exactly
`storage_offset` elements**. Kimi-K3's KDA fuses several outputs into one row and
hands the 128-element `f_a` slice to `f_b_proj`; at TP=8 that view is
`stride=(6288,1)`, `storage_offset=6144`, so the preload runs **12,288 bytes past
the end of the parent allocation**.

Whether those bytes are mapped is a matter of allocator layout. Enabling the aux
stream adds a second per-stream allocator pool, which moves that tensor to the
tail of a 2 MiB segment — which is why an unrelated feature appeared to cause a
memory fault, and why the fault addresses are 2 MiB-aligned
(`0x…200000`, `0x…600000`).

Single-variable arms on 8× MI355X, Kimi-K3 TP=8, boot-only, ladder `1,2,4,8`:

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| overlap off (control) | clean |
| overlap on | **fault** |
| + ROCm/aiter#4715 (capture-safe split-K workspace) | fault |
| + fresh `torch.cuda.Event` per call | fault |
| + `AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3` (rules out kernel co-residency) | fault |
| + shared-expert output into a main-stream static buffer | fault |
| + aux-stream drain before capture | fault |
| + shared-expert GEMMs moved back to the main stream | fault |
| `VLLM_ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM=0` | **clean** |
| only `wvSplitK`/`LLMM1` disabled, `wvSplitKrc` left on | **clean** |
### One caveat about #52033's `dp_size > 1` gate

#52033 gates the ROCm overlap behind
`self._moe_config.moe_parallel_config.dp_size > 1`, on the basis that "only DPA
deployments benefit". **Every number below is TP=8 / DP=1**, i.e. exactly the
configuration that gate excludes, and the overlap is a solid win there. If the
gate lands as written, TP deployments get none of this by default.

I did not touch the gate in this PR, because it does not exist in `main` — it
arrives with #52033. For measurement I bypassed it locally with an env escape
hatch:

```python
 if not current_platform.is_rocm():
     return True
+if envs.VLLM_ROCM_FORCE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM:
+    return True
 return self._moe_config.moe_parallel_config.dp_size > 1
```

The right place to settle this is #52033 itself. My suggestion there would be to
either relax the heuristic now that there is TP data, or keep it but make it
overridable, so TP users are not silently opted out.

## Superseded results (2026-08-13) — kept for the record, do not cite

Kimi-K3 MXFP4, 8x MI355X, TP=8, EP=1, DSpark MTP (`num_speculative_tokens=2`),
kv-cache fp8, `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, capture ladder `seq 1..60`,
floor 61. Median generation throughput, matched request load per pair, zero
faults in every arm:

| conc | baseline | overlap | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 86.40 tok/s | 98.40 | **+13.9%** |
| 4 | 266.10 tok/s | 295.15 | **+10.9%** |
| 8 | 462.00 tok/s | 498.70 | **+7.9%** |

Control: with the patch applied but the overlap forced never to fire, throughput
returns to baseline (93.90 vs 93.30 on an earlier config), so the gain is the
overlap and not the restructuring.

title: [Bug]: Kimi-K3 MoE padding floor scales with TP - crashes `deep_gemm_mega_moe` at TP>=16 and pins per-GPU weight memory at ~120GB
body:
### Your current environment ### Summary `KimiMoE.__init__` pads `moe_intermediate_size` up to `min_moe_intermediate_per_partition * tp_size`. Because the pad target scales *with* `tp_size`, `padded // tp_size` is identically `min_moe_intermediate_per_partition` — the per-partition size saturates and stops decreasing as GPUs are added. This has two consequences for `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`, both of which only appear at TP >= 16: 1. An unguarded attribute write crashes model init when `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` is used. 2. Per-GPU MoE weight memory is pinned at ~120 GB regardless of TP, so adding nodes does not reduce it. Neither is hardware-specific. The published recipe is TP=8 on 8x GB300, which is exactly the case that skips the padding branch — which is likely why this hasn't surfaced. ### The code — `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py:493-502` ```python self.padded_moe_intermediate_size = moe_intermediate_size min_moe_intermediate_per_partition = getattr( config, "min_moe_intermediate_per_partition", 256 ) if self.tp_size > 1: moe_intermediate_per_partition = moe_intermediate_size // self.tp_size if moe_intermediate_per_partition < min_moe_intermediate_per_partition: self.padded_moe_intermediate_size = ( min_moe_intermediate_per_partition * self.tp_size ) ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug The padded value is what is actually handed to the experts (`model.py:600` for MegaMoE, `model.py:612` for `FusedMoEFactory`), so the memory is genuinely allocated; the pad region is only zeroed afterwards. ### Symptom 1 — AttributeError with `deep_gemm_mega_moe` `model.py:634-647` runs whenever padding engaged: ```python if self.padded_moe_intermediate_size != moe_intermediate_size: w13_weight = getattr(self.experts, "w13_weight", None) if w13_weight is None: w13_weight = getattr(self.experts, "w13_weight_packed", None) ... self.experts.moe_config.intermediate_size_per_partition_unpadded = ( # <-- unguarded moe_intermediate_size // self.tp_size ) ``` With `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, `self.experts` is a `KimiK3MegaMoEExperts`, which extends `DeepseekV4MegaMoEExperts(nn.Module)` — `moe_config` does not exist anywhere in that class. Every rank dies during `load_model`: ``` File "vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py", line 593, in __init__ self.experts.moe_config.intermediate_size_per_partition_unpadded = ( File "torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1967, in __getattr__ raise AttributeError( AttributeError: 'KimiK3MegaMoEExperts' object has no attribute 'moe_config' ``` (Line 593 is from the `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k3` image; the same statement is at line 645 on `main` as of d31de3c421.) Incidentally, this traceback is itself proof that the padding branch engaged: the statement only executes inside `if self.padded_moe_intermediate_size != moe_intermediate_size`. So in this run `moe_intermediate_size // self.tp_size < 256`, i.e. `self.tp_size > 12`, confirming that `tp_size` is the full 32 here and is not reduced to 1 by expert parallelism. **This reproduces with `--load-format dummy`** — the checkpoint is never read, so no 1.6 TB download is needed to verify it. On 4x8 H100 it fails in about 70 seconds, on all 32 ranks: ``` --load-format dummy --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --enable-expert-parallel \ --tensor-parallel-size 32 --nnodes 4 --node-rank <0..3> --enforce-eager \ --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 1 ``` **This is not a Hopper-only report.** The MegaMoE *kernels* are SM100, but this crash happens in `KimiMoE.__init__` during module construction, before any kernel launches. `use_mega_moe` is set purely by `vllm_config.kernel_config.moe_backend == "deep_gemm_mega_moe"` (`model.py:765`) with no SM or platform check on that path — reaching this traceback on H100 at all demonstrates there is no such gate. The trigger is `3072 // tp_size < 256`, i.e. `tp_size >= 13`, so a 16x B200 DEP deployment at TP=16 (`3072/16 = 192`) should hit the identical crash. I don't have Blackwell hardware to confirm that, so it's worth a check. The weight lookups immediately above use `getattr` with fallbacks precisely because the two expert implementations name things differently, so the direct `moe_config` access looks like an oversight. Note that `DeepseekV4MegaMoEExperts` stores only `self.intermediate_size` and has no padded/unpadded distinction — DeepSeek-V4 always passes an unpadded size, so Kimi-K3 is the first caller to hand MegaMoE a padded one. A `getattr` guard stops the crash, but it's worth confirming whether MegaMoE needs the unpadded size for correctness or whether zeroed padding is sufficient. ### Symptom 2 — per-GPU memory does not scale with TP From `config.json`: `moe_intermediate_size=3072`, `routed_expert_hidden_size=3584`, `num_experts=896`, `num_hidden_layers=93`, `first_k_dense_replace=1` (92 MoE layers), mxfp4 4-bit + uint8 scale per group of 32 = 0.53125 bytes/param. `min_moe_intermediate_per_partition` is absent from the config, so the default 256 applies. MoE weight bytes/GPU = `3 * (padded // tp) * 3584 * 896 * 92 * 0.53125`: | TP | padded_I | per-partition I | MoE weights/GPU | |----|----------|-----------------|-----------------| | 8 | 3072 | 384 | 180.8 GB | | 16 | 4096 | 256 | **120.5 GB** | | 32 | 8192 | 256 | **120.5 GB** | | 64 | 16384 | 256 | **120.5 GB** | The identity holds under expert parallel too: each rank holds `896/ep` experts at the full padded size, and `padded/ep` is the same constant. Practical effect: 80 GB GPUs cannot run this model at any TP (TP=8 needs 180.8 GB, TP>=16 needs 120.5 GB), and there is no reachable value in between — TP must divide both `num_attention_heads=96` and `vocab_size=163840`, whose common divisors are only powers of two up to 32. The failure surfaces as a bare CUDA OOM inside `Mxfp4MoEMethod.create_weights` with nothing indicating padding as the cause. Observed with `--moe-backend marlin --load-format dummy` at TP=32, identically on 24 of 32 ranks (the other node was claimed by an unrelated job mid-run): ``` File "vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py", line 550, in __init__ # experts construction (image numbering) File "vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py", line 622, in create_weights torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 392.00 MiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 79.18 GiB of which 260.19 MiB is free. Of the allocated memory 77.40 GiB is allocated by PyTorch ``` Note this is a *lower* bound, not a measurement of the total: allocation was still in progress when the GPU filled, so it establishes >77.4 GB/GPU rather than confirming the predicted 120.5 GB. The prediction is falsifiable by anyone running TP=32 on >=128 GB GPUs. On Blackwell this is not a fit problem (120.5 GB fits in 180 GB), but it still means scaling past TP=16 buys no additional weight-memory headroom for KV cache or batch size. This also matches an independent report of ~130 GB/rank persisting across both TP=16 and TP=32 on 16x H200, described there as weights being "replicated rather than sharded" (https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3/discussions/136). The padding floor explains that without any replication bug. As a cross-check, SGLang serves the same checkpoint at TP=EP=32 on 32x H100-80GB with a marlin W4A16 runner and reports 59.6 GB/GPU resident weights. Unpadded, the MoE term at TP=32 would be `3 * 96 * 3584 * 896 * 92 * 0.53125 = 45.2 GB`, leaving ~14 GB for the non-MoE stack — which is the right order for it, given the replicated latent up/down projections alone are about 9 GB (`2 * 3584 * 7168 * 2 bytes * 92`) on top of the TP-sharded attention, embeddings and shared experts. So the unpadded shape appears servable on this hardware, and the floor is what makes it not fit. ### Questions 1. Is the floor a hard kernel requirement or a performance heuristic? DeepGEMM's expert path checks `intermediate_size % 128 != 0` (`deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py:318`), which suggests the real constraint is 128-alignment rather than a magnitude of 256. At TP=32 the natural per-partition size is `3072/32 = 96`, which is not 128-aligned, so *some* padding is needed — but a floor of 128 would give 60.3 GB/GPU instead of 120.5 GB. 2. Should the pad be capped at one alignment step rather than growing without bound with `tp_size`? 3. `min_moe_intermediate_per_partition` is read off the model config via `getattr` and isn't settable from the CLI. If a smaller floor is valid, exposing it would let 80 GB GPUs serve this model. 4. Independently of the above: could the padded size be logged, and a clear error raised when the padded footprint provably exceeds device memory? ### Environment - 4 nodes x 8x H100-80GB (32 GPUs), image `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k3`, which reports vLLM `0.1.dev19262+gb6bbf29dd.d20260727` (git sha `b6bbf29dd`, 2026-07-27). Note the image is built for Hopper: `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.7 8.9 9.0 10.0+PTX 12.0 12.1`. - Repro: `--tensor-parallel-size 32 --enable-expert-parallel --nnodes 4 --node-rank <0..3> --enforce-eager --load-format dummy` - Symptom 1 with `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`; symptom 2 with `--moe-backend marlin`. - Source line numbers are from `main` at d31de3c421; line numbers inside tracebacks are from the image (sha `b6bbf29dd`), where the `moe_config` write sits at 593 rather than 645. - I checked this file's history through d31de3c421: the recent memory work (#50656 shared-expert sharding, #50383 latent up-proj sharding) reduces the non-MoE term but does not touch the padding floor or the unguarded `moe_config` write.

title: [Rust Frontend] Support dynamic tools from developer messages
body:
## Purpose

The Rust frontend already carries message-scoped function tools on developer messages, but tool choice resolution, parser activation, and structural-tag generation only used request-level tools. Dynamic-only declarations therefore reached some renderers without becoming available to downstream tool handling.

This PR adds a request-scoped `ResolvedToolContext` that resolves request-level and developer-message tools once and exposes their ordered union as `effective_tools`. Tool-choice defaulting and validation, structural-tag generation, parser construction, parallel-call handling, and response assembly now consume the same resolved state.

- Kimi K3 continues to render request-level tools before the conversation and dynamic declarations at their original message positions.
- The generic Hugging Face renderer exposes effective tools to templates while preserving developer-message tools.
- DeepSeek V3.2/V4, Harmony, and Inkling retain their reference-owned prompt projections.

The public system-message DTO remains content-only in this scope. Callers using the vendor `system.tools` shape can map it to a developer message with empty content.

## Test Plan

- Add resolver unit coverage for default choice, ordering, duplicate names, and named choice membership.
- Add Kimi K3 prompt fixtures for a dynamic-only declaration and explicit `tool_choice=none`.
- Add structural-tag coverage for dynamic-only tools and the ordered union of request-level and dynamic tools.
- Add Hugging Face and model-specific renderer coverage for developer-message tools.
- Run the Rust chat and server test suites, excluding the network-dependent Nemotron tokenizer test.

## Test Result

- `cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server -E 'not test(roundtrip_nemotron_v3)'`: 625 passed, 1 skipped.
- `cargo clippy -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

- [x] The test results are provided.

### 🐛 Describe the bug AMD CI involving AITER started to fail after the seemingly harmless https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50879, due to a **previously global `from .prepare_finalize.mori import MoriPrepareAndFinalize` import being moved to lazy import**. HIP used to load rightful `/opt/rocm/lib/libamdhip64.so.7` first with RTLD_GLOBAL in https://github.com/ROCm/mori/blob/0cc74439d82e231ad12674c4db2240a612b57cb1/python/mori/cpp/__init__.py#L39. Removing this `mori.cpp` initialization, instead: 1. We run into the call stack: ``` vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/__init__.py:116 from vllm.models.deepseek_v4 import DeepseekV4FP8Config └─ vllm/models/deepseek_v4/__init__.py:18 from .amd.dspark import ... └─ vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/dspark.py:40 from vllm.model_executor.layers.mhc import HCHeadOp └─ vllm/model_executor/layers/mhc.py:28 HAS_TILELANG_MHC = _has_tilelang_mhc() └─ vllm/model_executor/layers/mhc.py:15 if not has_tilelang(): └─ vllm/utils/import_utils.py:406 importlib.import_module("tilelang") # <-- trial import ``` that is https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/beca88e59ea75a7aa1af72a5ae50188fa91d4e3d/vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang_kernels.py#L16 and `importlib.import_module(module_name)` call https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/beca88e59ea75a7aa1af72a5ae50188fa91d4e3d/vllm/utils/import_utils.py#L406 `tilelang/__init__.py:173` does `import tvm`, which reaches https://github.com/tile-ai/tvm/blob/8df8ebd61659505dd7005f4820b030e983e2c005/python/tvm/base.py#L51-L53: ```python _LIB_RUNTIME = libinfo.load_lib_ctypes( "tvm", "tvm_runtime", "RTLD_GLOBAL", extra_lib_paths=_extra_lib_paths ) ``` libhip_stub.so` is a `DT_NEEDED` dependency of `libtvm_runtime.so` (and of `libtilelang.so` / `libtvm_compiler.so`). `RTLD_GLOBAL` propagates to dependencies, so the stub's 35 exported HIP symbols — including `hipMalloc`, `hipFree`, `hipGetDevice`, `hipGetDevicePropertiesR0600`, `hipModuleLaunchKernel` — land in the process-wide global symbol scope and win `dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "hipMalloc")`. AITER's JIT modules are `dlopen`ed later, and use wrong symbols then. ## CI reproduction See failures: - https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11701/list?sid=019fd126-db3f-4316-8fb3-04b9b28e096c&tab=output - https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11696/canvas?sid=019fcffa-7ecb-4330-bdaa-cf90089914fd&tab=output Also e.g. ```bash VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_quantization[True-fp8_per_tensor-None-Fp8PerTensorOnlineLinearMethod-Fp8PerTensorOnlineMoEMethod] -s -vvvvv ``` started failing locally after https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50879: ``` (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] File "/felmarty/repos/vllm/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py", line 1167, in _allocate_buffers (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] common_workspace, workspace2 = current_workspace_manager().get_simultaneous( (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] File "/felmarty/repos/vllm/vllm/v1/worker/workspace.py", line 110, in get_simultaneous (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] current_workspace = self._ensure_workspace_size(total_bytes) (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] File "/felmarty/repos/vllm/vllm/v1/worker/workspace.py", line 176, in _ensure_workspace_size (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] self._current_workspaces[ubatch_id] = torch.empty( (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] ^^^^^^^^^^^^ (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid configuration argument ``` ## Minimal reproduction ```python import ctypes import sys mode = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "broken" import torch # noqa: E402 if mode == "fixed": # What the eager Mori import used to do by accident: get the real HIP # runtime into the global scope before tilelang can put the stub there. ctypes.CDLL("/opt/rocm/lib/libamdhip64.so", mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL) import tilelang # noqa: E402,F401 -> libtvm_runtime.so RTLD_GLOBAL -> libhip_stub.so import aiter # noqa: E402 -> JIT .so files bind to whatever is global from aiter import topk_softmax # noqa: E402 torch.cuda.init() dev = "cuda" num_tokens, num_experts, topk = 16384, 32, 8 gate = torch.randn(num_tokens, num_experts, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev) # Primes AITER's cached device properties (multiProcessorCount == 1 via stub). topk_softmax( torch.empty(num_tokens, topk, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev), torch.empty(num_tokens, topk, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev), torch.empty(num_tokens, topk, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev), gate, False, ) torch.cuda.synchronize() # Sizes its grid from those properties -> invalid launch configuration. from aiter.fused_moe import moe_sorting # noqa: E402 topk_weights = torch.softmax(gate, -1)[:, :topk].contiguous() topk_ids = torch.topk(gate, topk, dim=-1)[1].to(torch.int32) try: moe_sorting(topk_ids, topk_weights, num_experts, 1024, torch.bfloat16) torch.cuda.synchronize() except Exception as exc: print(f"[{mode}] RESULT: FAIL -- {type(exc).__name__}: {str(exc).splitlines()[0]}") raise SystemExit(1) print(f"[{mode}] RESULT: PASS") ``` giving: ``` [aiter] WARNING: NUMA balancing is enabled, which may cause errors. It is recommended to disable NUMA balancing by running "sudo sh -c 'echo 0 > /proc/sys/kernel/numa_balancing'" for more details: https://rocm.docs.amd.com/en/latest/how-to/system-optimization/mi300x.html#disable-numa-auto-balancing [aiter] import [module_aiter_core] under /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/aiter/jit/module_aiter_core.so [aiter] import [module_moe_asm] under /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/aiter/jit/module_moe_asm.so Traceback (most recent call last): File "/felmarty/repos/vllm/_debug_mori/minimal_repro.py", line 90, in topk_weights = torch.softmax(gate, -1)[:, :topk].contiguous() ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid configuration argument Search for `hipErrorInvalidConfiguration' in https://rocm.docs.amd.com/projects/HIP/en/latest/index.html for more information. CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call, so the stacktrace below might be incorrect. For debugging consider passing AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3 Device-side assertion tracking was not enabled by user. ``` `python _debug_mori/minimal_repro.py fixed` gives: ``` [aiter] WARNING: NUMA balancing is enabled, which may cause errors. It is recommended to disable NUMA balancing by running "sudo sh -c 'echo 0 > /proc/sys/kernel/numa_balancing'" for more details: https://rocm.docs.amd.com/en/latest/how-to/system-optimization/mi300x.html#disable-numa-auto-balancing [aiter] import [module_aiter_core] under /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/aiter/jit/module_aiter_core.so [aiter] import [module_moe_asm] under /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/aiter/jit/module_moe_asm.so [aiter] import [module_moe_sorting_opus] under /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/aiter/jit/module_moe_sorting_opus.so [fixed] RESULT: PASS ``` ## Root cause - `has_tilelang()` should not load tilelang symbols. - tilelang loads broken symbols, with `hipDeviceProp_t` filled with the wrong ABI layout. The stub *exports* `hipGetDevicePropertiesR0600` (ROCm 6 ABI) but internally resolves the old `hipGetDeviceProperties` (ROCm 5 / R0000 ABI), so every field of the returned struct is read at the wrong offset. ## Hotfix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51110 works, but does not fix the root cause. Root cause is `has_tilelang()` and `tilelang` imports loading wrongful shared objects ## Root cause and suggested fixes In decreasing order of correctness: 1. **tilelang (upstream)** — fix `hip.cc:121` to resolve the same ABI it exports, e.g. look up `"hipGetDevicePropertiesR0600"` (with a fallback to `"hipGetDeviceProperties"` for ROCm 5). This is the actual defect: the stub silently mis-reports every device property to ROCm 6 callers. Arguably `libtvm_runtime.so` should also not be `dlopen`ed with `RTLD_GLOBAL` when it exports HIP symbols, since that makes it interpose on unrelated libraries in the same process. 2. **vLLM** — stop `_has_module()` from doing a trial import for tilelang, or skip the probe entirely on arches where the feature is disabled. Importing a large native package as a side effect of an availability check is surprising and, as here, can have process-wide consequences. `_has_tilelang_mhc()` already returns `False` on gfx942 — the probe should never have loaded anything. 3. **AITER** — explicitly load/`dlopen` the HIP runtime it needs rather than relying on whatever happens to be in the global scope. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: cache_config_info reports block_size=4 despite --block-size 256, and num_gpu_blocks × block_size ≠ kv_cache_size_tokens (DeepSeek-V4, fp8_ds_mla)
body:
### Summary

On DeepSeek-V4-Flash with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, `vllm:cache_config_info`
reports **`block_size="4"`** while `--block-size 256` was passed and is visible in
the process command line, and `user_specified_block_size="True"`. Separately,
`num_gpu_blocks × block_size` does not equal `kv_cache_size_tokens` for **any** of
the candidate block sizes.

The three numbers cannot all be correct, whichever block size is the real one.

### Observed

Two independent serves, different commits and different configs, both reproduce it:

| | serve A | serve B |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--block-size` passed | 256 | 256 |
| `block_size` reported | **4** | **4** |
| `user_specified_block_size` | True | True |
| `num_gpu_blocks` | 17,903 | 20,377 |
| `kv_cache_size_tokens` | 1,394,221 | 1,179,770 |
| implied tokens/block | **77.9** | **57.9** |
| `sliding_window` | 128 | 128 |

Neither 77.9 nor 57.9 matches the reported `4` or the passed `256`, and neither is
an integer.

Raw metric line from serve B:

```
vllm:cache_config_info{_block_size_resolved="True",block_size="4",cache_dtype="fp8_ds_mla",
enable_prefix_caching="True",gpu_memory_utilization="0.85",kv_cache_size_tokens="1179770",
num_gpu_blocks="20377",sliding_window="128",user_specified_block_size="True",...} 1.0
```

And the flag as actually received by the process (read from `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`):

```
--block-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --max-model-len 500000
```

### Why it matters

`cache_config_info` is what you reach for when sizing KV by hand or building
capacity dashboards. Right now a user cannot derive KV capacity from it: the
reported block size contradicts the configured one, and the block/token arithmetic
is self-inconsistent regardless of which you believe. It also makes
`user_specified_block_size="True"` misleading — it is true that the user specified
one, but not the one being reported.

### Environment

- 2× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), TP=2
- `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, `--max-model-len 500000`,
  `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`
- vLLM `20260805.dev1+g4eedf4876.d20260805`, built from the SM12x enablement branch
  in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834 (jasl/vllm @ `4eedf48765`)

### Caveat on scope

We can only observe this on the PR-41834 branch, because `DeepSeek-V4-Flash` does
not load on sm12x without it — so we cannot say whether this is branch-specific or
general to the DSv4 / `fp8_ds_mla` path on `main`. The metric itself
(`cache_config_info`) is generic, and the DSv4 packed KV layout is reported to use
64-token pages independent of the logical block size, which may be part of the
explanation but does not account for the non-integer ratios.

Filed separately at the request of @jasl in
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834 — it is orthogonal to the
corruption discussion in that thread.

title: [ROCm][MLA] Dispatch gfx942 verify to Gluon
body:
## Summary

Dispatch validated gfx942 Kimi-K3 multi-token verification shapes to the graph-safe CDNA3 Gluon MLA kernel from [ROCm/aiter#4582](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4582).

The dispatch is limited to 12 BF16 query heads. QLEN=4 is enabled through request batch 16, while other validated multi-token lengths remain single-request only. The backend passes existing ragged token metadata directly and flattens the physical KV cache before applying token-level indices, so the path remains capture-safe.

Single-token decode remains on persistent ASM for gfx942. Unsupported shapes also use ASM with 12 heads padded to 16. Existing gfx950 Gluon behavior is unchanged.

## Dependencies and scope

This draft depends on the gfx942 graph kwargs in `mla_decode_fwd` from [ROCm/aiter#4582](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4582) (`maeehart/gfx942-gluon-mla`, commit `62dbc1af`).

The non-divisor padding and CDNA4 architecture gate from merged [#50578](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50578) are now consumed directly from current `main`. This PR only adds the gfx942 graph dispatch.

Full Kimi-K3 DSpark graph validation uses the causal Triton MLA support from [#51065](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51065).

The dispatch feature-probes `mla_decode_fwd` for graph kwargs (`q_nope`, `q_pe`, `page_table`, `seq_info`), so older AITER versions retain the existing path. This PR remains draft until ROCm/aiter#4582 is available in the tested AITER dependency and #51065 is available for full causal DSpark validation.

## Test plan

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_gfx942_gluon.py

python -m pytest -q \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_causal_verify_mask.py

python -m ruff check \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_gfx942_gluon.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_causal_verify_mask.py
```

Serving validation uses Kimi-K3 TP8 with DSpark k=3 on 8 MI325X GPUs, BF16 KV, expert parallelism, and `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` graph capture. The workload uses 1,024 input tokens, 128 output tokens, and greedy target sampling.

## Results

The focused dispatch suite passes:

```text
20 passed
```

The dependent AITER gfx942 suite passes 12 tests covering graph replay, ragged paging, 768-token physical blocks, fused QLEN/head rows, and large-cache addressing.

Captured QLEN=4 kernel time on MI325X:

| Request batch | Persistent ASM | gfx942 Gluon | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 29.81 us | 18.87 us | 1.58x |
| 4 | 34.16 us | 22.89 us | 1.49x |
| 16 | 34.64 us | 33.04 us | 1.05x |

Full serving results:

| Concurrency | Persistent ASM | Candidate |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 60.02 output tok/s | 62.14 output tok/s |
| 16 | 299.42 output tok/s | 300.54 +/- 4.61 output tok/s |

The concurrency-16 candidate value is the mean of three runs: 295.35, 302.15, and 304.13 output tok/s. The end-to-end difference from persistent ASM is small relative to run variation, while the kernel path removes 16-head padding for the selected shapes.

Full graph capture completes without a downgrade or memory fault. A 200-question greedy GSM8K serving check scored 192/200, or 96.0%, matching the persistent ASM reference.

title: [Perf] Add an adaptive prefill delayer for data-parallel serving
body:
## Purpose

  When a large prefill is scheduled on only one DP engine, that engine performs a
  much longer model iteration while the other engines wait for it to finish. This
  creates uneven iteration times and delays ongoing decode requests.

  This PR adds an optional adaptive prefill delayer. It coordinates large prefill
  work onto the same engine steps across DP ranks, reducing iterations where one
  rank is doing prefill while others are decoding. Decode continues while prefill
  is delayed, with bounded fail-open and recovery behavior to guarantee progress.

  ## Test Plan

  Tested DeepSeek-V4 using:

  ```bash
  vllm serve "$MODEL" \
      --trust-remote-code \
      --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
      --block-size 256 \
      --no-enable-prefix-caching \
      --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
      --data-parallel-size 8 \
      --enable-expert-parallel \
      --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
      --prefill-schedule-interval 1 \
      --enable-adaptive-prefill-alignment \
      --prefill-alignment-max-delay-passes 30 \
      --prefill-alignment-target-step-lead 2 \
      --max-model-len 16384 \
      --max-num-batched-tokens 2048
  ```

  Added unit tests for coordinated release, delay limits, capacity release,
  missing acknowledgments, and DP-wave resets.

  ## Test Result

  ```text
  10 passed in 9.68s
  Ruff checks passed
  All changed files are formatted
  ```

title: fix: Skip empty DeepSeek-V4 FlashInfer attention slices
body:
## Purpose

Update `DeepseekV4FlashInferSM120Attention._forward_sparse_impl` to dispatch prefill and decode only when their corresponding actual token counts are positive, preventing empty tensor views from crossing the FlashInfer API boundary. Preserve the current slicing and ordering for mixed batches so nonempty decode tokens remain first and nonempty prefill tokens continue to use the existing metadata and cache paths. Extend the nearby sparse-attention tests with a lightweight constructed SM120 attention object and mocked forward methods, following the file's existing object-construction pattern, to cover both the empty-prefill regression and a mixed batch where valid work must still dispatch.

Fixes #51106

## Test Plan

Not applicable to this change.

- With `num_prefills` greater than zero but `num_prefill_tokens` equal to zero, verify the SM120 dispatcher does not invoke `_forward_prefill`, so no empty query or sparse-index tensor reaches FlashInfer. - With a mixed batch containing decode tokens and zero prefill tokens, verify `_forward_decode` still runs once with only the decode slice while prefill remains skipped. - With positive prefill and decode token counts, verify both paths run with the expected token slices, guarding against an over-broad early return.

title: [Feature] IndexCache for DeepSeek-V4 (validated on V4-Flash-0731, including DSpark on to accelerate on top of
body:
## Summary:

This work is built to support Dspark + IndexerCache to achieve best deepseek v4 flash serving performance.

## Purpose

Adds DSA IndexCache support to DeepSeek-V4, so C4A layers marked shared reuse the top-k the previous C4A layer left in the shared `topk_indices_buffer` instead of running their own indexer. Same config surface as the DeepSeek-V3.2 feature (`use_index_cache` / `index_topk_freq` / `index_topk_pattern`, see [docs/features/index_cache.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/features/index_cache.md)); addresses #45350.

The indexer dominates decode KV traffic on this model at long context: per decode token per C4A layer it reads `(S/4) x 132 B` of its own K cache, while the main sparse MLA reads only `index_topk x 576 B`. Across DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731's 21 C4A / 20 C128A / 44 SWA caches that is ~65% of decode KV traffic at 32K and ~81% at 128K, and the indexer is TP-replicated so every rank pays it in full.

### Relationship to #49085

#49085 implements the same feature for Hopper and is the earlier work; its authors (@wangyicong52, @zzz3bbb3) got there first on the two non-obvious points — per-PP-rank handling, and keeping skipped indexers' KV-cache specs registered while parking their linear weights on the meta device. 

Two behavioural differences worth a maintainer decision:

1. This PR gates on `use_index_cache`, matching the documented V3.2 surface. #49085 activates on `index_topk_freq > 1` alone, which would make `--hf-overrides '{"index_topk_freq": 4}'` silently enable on V4 while silently doing nothing on V3.2.
2. This PR uses `c4a_idx % index_topk_freq`; #49085 keeps V3.2's `index_skip_topk_offset` (default 2), so its first two C4A layers always compute. Theirs is more faithful to V3.2 and I am happy to switch.

## Design notes

Only C4A layers (`compress_ratio == 4`) carry an indexer in V4, so **the frequency and pattern are indexed over the C4A layers, not over all layers**. Applying the V3.2 absolute-`layer_id` formula to DeepSeek-V4-Flash marks *every* C4A layer as shared (they are all even), so nothing populates the buffer and every layer reads stale contents — silently, with no error. A regression test pins this.

Three further constraints, each covered by a test:

- `topk_indices_buffer` is rank-local, so the first C4A layer **of each pipeline stage** computes its own top-k (derived from the same `get_pp_indices` split `make_layers` uses).
- `compress_ratios` can be longer than `num_hidden_layers` (44 entries on V4-Flash, 46 on V4-Flash-0731, for the MTP/draft slots), so selection slices to `num_hidden_layers`.
- A pattern is one `F`/`S` character per C4A layer — 21 on V4-Flash-0731, not 43 — and may not start with `S`. Wrong-length patterns raise rather than silently applying a prefix.

Skipped layers keep their indexer allocated and simply never run it, so the change is confined to `attention.py` and needs no KV-cache-grouping or weight-loading changes. Memory savings are left to a follow-up.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_index_cache.py -v
```

E2E hardware: single node, 8xH100 80GB, TP=8, upstream vLLM 0.26.0 with this patch, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`.

```bash
# long context / frequency sweep
vllm bench latency --model <0731> --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 -tp 8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --max-model-len 33792 \
  --input-len 32768 --output-len 128 --batch-size 2 \
  --hf-overrides '{"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": N}'

# quality: GSM8K 200q 5-shot, MMLU 500q 5-shot, greedy
# throughput: short prompt + 512 output tokens at fixed concurrency
```

## Test Result

14/14 unit tests pass.

### Frequency sensitivity

32768-token input x batch 2, and MMLU 500 questions 5-shot. All arms are the same build with only `index_topk_freq` varying, so `freq=1`/off is a true no-skip control (confirmed by the log line firing only on freq>1 arms):

| freq | indexers run | 32K latency | Δ | MMLU |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| off / 1 | 21/21 | 3.004 s | — | 85.4% |
| 2 | 11/21 | 2.890 s | -3.8% | 85.6% |
| 3 | 7/21 | 2.842 s | -5.4% | 85.0% |
| 4 | 6/21 | 2.831 s | -5.8% | 84.8% |
| 6 | 4/21 | 2.808 s | -6.5% | 85.0% |

The latency curve saturates quickly — freq=2 captures most of the win, and skipping three times as many indexers (freq=6) only reaches -6.5%. MMLU spans 84.8-85.6%, within the ~1.6pp binomial noise at n=500. vLLM 0.25.1 and the older `DeepSeek-V4-Flash` checkpoint reproduce the freq=2/3 numbers within noise.

### Quality and throughput matrix (GSM8K, 200q 5-shot, best of 3 timed passes)

| cell | DSpark | IndexCache | accuracy | throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c4 | off | off | 96.0%, 96.5% | 4087, 4525 tok/s |
| c2 | off | **on** | 96.0%, 96.0% | 4322, 4081 tok/s |
| c1 | **on** | off | 96.0%, 97.0% | 3449, 3742 tok/s |
| c3 | **on** | **on** | 97.0% | 3873 tok/s |

IndexCache changes neither accuracy nor throughput here. Note this shape is ~91% prefill tokens (180K prefill vs 17K decode) and saturates the GPU, so it is not informative about speculative decoding; the concurrency sweep below is.

### Throughput vs concurrency (short prompt, 512 output tokens)

| concurrency | c4 baseline | c1 DSpark | c3 DSpark + IndexCache |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 560 tok/s | **1419** | 1201 |
| 16 | 1670 tok/s | 3289 | **3419** |
| 64 | 4910 tok/s | 6975 | **7187** |

The two features are complementary and stack: at the concurrencies that matter for serving, DSpark + IndexCache is the fastest configuration. Draft acceptance is 63-69% (mean accepted length 4.2-4.5 of 5) with IndexCache both on and off, so IndexCache does not measurably degrade the draft.

### Long-context correctness

A needle-in-a-haystack probe (18,930-token prompt, needle at depth 0.15 / 0.5 / 0.85, greedy) retrieves correctly with IndexCache off, at freq=2, and at freq=3.

### DSpark interaction

DeepSeek-V4's DSpark draft builds its decoder layers with `topk_indices_buffer=None` and layer ids >= `num_hidden_layers`, so draft layers resolve to `compress_ratio == 1` and never construct an indexer; the two features are structurally orthogonal. Enabling both is exercised end to end at every concurrency above.

## Notes

Not covered, stated rather than implied: no Blackwell run (#49085 hard-rejects non-SM90 for this feature; this PR does not gate, which may be wrong); no PP>1 e2e run (the per-stage rule is unit-tested only);

Meanwhile, if B200 number testing needed, I will provide later follow up test in NVFP4. 

AI Assistance are used for this development. 


---

## Full measurement set (AIPerf)

Everything below is `aiperf profile` against `vllm serve` on the same node: single 8xH100 80GB, TP=8, upstream vLLM 0.26.0 + this patch, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, AIPerf 0.12.0. Output length is pinned with `ignore_eos:true` + `min_tokens` (without it the model stops early and throughput deltas measure differing OSL, not speed), `--request-count` = 16x concurrency, `--warmup-request-count` = concurrency.

`ISL x concurrency` is chosen to fit the ~108K-token KV pool at each point; beyond that requests queue and the run becomes a scheduling test rather than a throughput test.

### Controls

Two arms exist purely to bound what a real effect must beat:

- **`freq=1`** enables IndexCache but skips nothing, so it must land on top of `off`. It does, everywhere.
- **`off` re-run** gives the run-to-run noise floor.

| control | throughput delta vs `off` |
|---|---|
| `freq=1`, all five workloads | -0.1% .. +0.1% |
| `off` re-run, 3 workloads | -0.1% .. +0.0% |

TTFT is the exception: identical configs vary by up to 5.8% on the 4K point, so no TTFT claim below ~6% is meaningful there.

### Output token throughput, delta vs `off`

| workload | ISL/OSL | conc | freq=1 | freq=2 | freq=3 | freq=4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| summarisation (prefill-heavy) | 32K / 16 | 3 | -0.0% | +3.3% | +5.2% | **+5.6%** |
| long chat | 32K / 256 | 3 | +0.1% | +3.5% | +4.9% | **+5.2%** |
| mid chat | 16K / 256 | 6 | +0.0% | +2.8% | +3.9% | **+4.2%** |
| RAG | 7K / 172 | 12 | +0.1% | — | **+3.2%** | — |
| short chat | 4K / 256 | 24 | -0.1% | +2.0% | +2.8% | **+3.1%** |

Absolute baselines: 13.63, 146.34, 285.82, 466.5, 1057.42 out tok/s respectively.

### Latency, delta vs `off` (freq=4; freq=3 for RAG)

| workload | e2e | TTFT | ITL |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32K / 16 | -5.3% | -5.1% | — |
| 32K / 256 | -5.0% | -5.1% | -4.8% |
| 16K / 256 | -4.0% | -4.6% | -3.7% |
| 7K / 172 | -3.1% | -2.7% | — |
| 4K / 256 | -3.0% | -1.9% | -3.2% |

### Accuracy per frequency

| freq | GSM8K (200q, 5-shot) | MMLU (500q, 5-shot) |
|---|---|---|
| off | 96.0% | 85.4% |
| 1 (control) | 96.0% | 85.0% |
| 2 | 95.5% | 85.4% |
| 3 | 96.0% | **86.2%** |
| 4 | **96.5%** | 85.0% |

No trend: the best GSM8K score is at freq=4 and the best MMLU at freq=3, and the `freq=1` control differs from `off` by 0.4pp on MMLU while being semantically identical to it. All deltas sit inside that noise.

**This is a no-harm result, not proof of quality preservation.** Both benchmarks' prompts (~900 and ~500 tokens, i.e. ~225 and ~125 compressed) are below `index_topk=512`, so every layer selects the whole compressed sequence and IndexCache is mathematically a no-op. Long-context quality evidence is limited to the needle probe (retrieved at all three depths with IndexCache off, freq=2 and freq=3); a RULER/LongBench run at 32K is still owed.

### Where the time actually goes

A torch-profiler run (eager, prefix caching off, conc 12 at 8K) attributes GPU kernel time as:

| bucket | freq=0 | freq=6 |
|---|---|---|
| TP all-reduce + other | 6176 ms | 5254 ms |
| MoE | 1003 ms | 980 ms |
| norm/rope | 395 ms | 394 ms |
| **indexer** | **91.7 ms (1.2%)** | **30.4 ms (0.4%)** |
| compressor | 43 ms | 42 ms |

The indexer is 1.2% of kernel time; the single largest kernel is `cross_device_reduce_1stage` (TP all-reduce) at ~69%. Removing 81% of the indexer work saves 61 ms directly, yet wall-clock improves several percent — the rest comes from ranks spending less time waiting inside the all-reduce. This configuration is communication-bound, which is also why the gain saturates between freq=3 and freq=4 (+0.3-0.4pp) and why a faster indexer kernel would not help much.

### Interaction with DSpark speculative decoding

Decode-heavy (short prompt, 512 output tokens, `ignore_eos`), output tok/s:

| concurrency | baseline | DSpark | DSpark + IndexCache |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 560 | **1419** | 1201 |
| 16 | 1670 | 3289 | **3419** |
| 64 | 4910 | 6975 | **7187** |

At serving concurrencies the two stack and DSpark + IndexCache is the fastest configuration. Draft acceptance is 63-69% (mean accepted length 4.2-4.5 of 5) with IndexCache both on and off, so IndexCache does not measurably degrade the draft.

### Honest summary of magnitude

**+3% to +5.6%** depending on shape and frequency, saturating at freq=3-4, free at inference time, with no measurable accuracy cost in the regimes tested. That is smaller than the 7-8% reported for vllm-ascend in #45350. On this hardware the gap is explained by the profile above (communication-bound, indexer at 1.2%), by the KV pool capping `ISL x concurrency` so the indexer's share cannot grow, and by Hopper reading an FP8 indexer cache at 132 B/token where `use_fp4_indexer_cache` would halve it.

### Measurement caveats

- The e2e numbers were produced by the 0.26.0-based build; upstream restructured `attention_impl` in #51430 after 0.26.0, so the rebased branch carries the same gates at the new call sites but has not itself been re-run on GPU.
- One RAG data point initially showed +9.8%; its `freq=1` control read +6.6%, which flagged the baseline as un-warmed. A repeat with two independent baseline arms put the true figure at +3.2%. The table above uses the corrected value.
- Single node only: no Blackwell run, and no PP>1 run (the per-stage rule is unit-tested only).

title: [ROCm][AMD] Enable preshuffled sparse indexing for 16-token blocks
body:
## Purpose

Allow ROCm sparse MLA indexer backends to use KV-cache block sizes aligned to 16 tokens. Previously, `--block-size 16` selected kernel block size 1, disabling AITER’s preshuffled FP8 paged-MQA path. The preshuffled AITER kernel was more performant than the non-shuffled variant so we were leaving some performance on the table. This PR fixes that.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -k select_common_block_size
ruff check tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py
```

Profile GLM-5.2 MXFP4 with TP4, concurrency 4, block size 16, and a 50k-input/1k-output workload on four MI355X GPUs.

### pre-commit checks
```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py
```

## Test Result

Unit tests: **4 passed**. Ruff: **passed**.

Both profiles ran on the same node with identical workload settings and completed all 40 requests.

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Paged-MQA kernel | Normal | Preshuffled | |
| Kernel time | 28.53 µs | 7.84 µs | **3.64× faster** |
| Output throughput | 207.01 tok/s | 212.23 tok/s | **+2.52%** |
| Median TPOT | 16.10 ms | 15.62 ms | **-2.98%** |
| Median E2E latency | 17.95 s | 17.44 s | **-2.86%** |

title: [MoE] Generalize masked activation for padded layouts
body:
## Summary

- add one shared count-aware MoE activation entry point for a flat valid prefix (`[T, D]`) and per-expert valid prefixes (`[E, T, D]`)
- support the gated and non-gated activation set explicitly, with a fail-closed `NotImplementedError` when a future activation lacks a masked implementation
- route Humming, batched Triton, and batched Marlin through `ApplyMoEActivationConfig` instead of backend-specific SITU/clamped-SiLU branches
- select Humming GEMM layout automatically: `indexed` without EP, `grouped_contiguous` with EP, and `grouped_masked` for batched experts; environment overrides remain available but are validated choices
- pass DeepEP v2's cudagraph valid-prefix metadata into Humming so activation skips padded receive rows
- validate padded/invalid expert IDs before indexing `expert_map` in the Humming permute path

## Why

DeepEP v1 and v2 expose different padded layouts. Legacy/batched execution has one valid prefix per expert, while DeepEP v2 has one valid prefix in a flat cudagraph receive buffer. Backend-specific activation branches had diverged and made SITU especially expensive in Kimi K3.

The shared op makes the layout contract explicit and specializes the flat versus batched branch at compile time. The Kimi investigation also found a correctness issue before activation: DeepEP v2 uses `-1` for padding, but Humming's permute preprocessing read `expert_map[topk_id]` before checking the ID. Invalid IDs now become the expert sentinel before any map access. The regression covers both `-1` and a positive out-of-range ID.

## Model validation

The final branch state was retested after the latest merge from `main`. No `VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE` override was set in these runs.

### DeepSeek-V4 Flash

Tested `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` in eager mode with FP8 KV cache:

- DP=1, no DeepEP: Humming selected `indexed`; the server reached healthy state and a deterministic arithmetic request returned the correct answer (42)
- DP=2 / EP=2 with `--all2all-backend deepep_v2`: vLLM used NCCL 2.30.7, selected `DeepEPV2All2AllManager` and Humming `grouped_contiguous`, reached healthy state, and returned the same correct answer
- earlier GSM8K 100 evaluation: DP=1 scored **0.96 accuracy / 0 invalid**; DP=2 / EP=2 scored **0.95 accuracy / 0 invalid**

The close DP1/DP2 evaluation scores and the final post-merge serving smoke test provide the model-level control for the DeepEP v2 layout. The earlier standalone DSV4 topology test was removed when this PR was refocused on the shared DP/EP activation contract, so it is not claimed as current CI coverage.

### Kimi K3

Served `mgoin/Kimi-K3-pruned75` on four B300 GPUs with:

```bash
chg run -g=4 -- env EP_DISABLE_GIN=1 vllm serve mgoin/Kimi-K3-pruned75 \
  --tokenizer-mode kimi_k3 --trust-remote-code --dtype bfloat16 \
  --language-model-only \
  --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend deepep_v2 --moe-backend humming \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \
  --max-num-seqs 16
```

- DP=4 / EP=4 used NCCL 2.30.7 and selected `DeepEPV2All2AllManager` and Humming `grouped_contiguous`
- the default non-eager server captured exactly **7 PIECEWISE + 5 FULL** breakable CUDA graphs; this model's V2 runner reports compilation mode `NONE`, so this validates CUDA graphs rather than TorchInductor
- the server reached healthy state and deterministic arithmetic requests returned coherent, correct output containing 42, with none of the prior repeated-`@` corruption

Before the invalid-ID guard, the same run emitted repeated `@` tokens; GSM8K 100 was 0% accurate with 100% invalid responses and every request exhausted 256 tokens. After the guard, chat-mode GSM8K 100 was **15% accuracy / 33% invalid** with 18,611 output tokens. Inspection showed the remaining invalid responses were mostly coherent but unfinished reasoning from this 75%-pruned checkpoint; a 10-question diagnostic at 1,024 tokens improved to 30% / 20% invalid. The latter small sample is not treated as a model-quality result. The relevant correctness signal is the disappearance of repeated-token corruption together with the focused native regressions.

Kimi required the 512-token batch cap on four B300s. A 2,048-token cap OOMed because DeepEP v2's worst-case receive/permute scratch must cover `max_tokens * dp_size * topk` rows.

### Runtime and shutdown notes

The final DeepEP v2 tests used the shared development `.venv` with `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.30.7` and `EP_DISABLE_GIN=1`. The runtime reported NCCL 2.30.7 and DeepEP v2 available. NCCL 2.29.7 is too old for the DeepEP v2 GIN API; vLLM requires NCCL >= 2.30.4 for this backend.

Stopping the multi-rank model servers with the default `--shutdown-timeout 0` force-killed peer processes and DeepEP subsequently reported `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` while destroying an elastic buffer. This happened after successful health checks and generation requests and was not observed on the inference path. Clean, draining multi-rank shutdown was not validated by these runs.

## Coverage and intentional exclusions

- flat masked activation: DeepEP v2 cudagraph padding
- batched masked activation: Marlin, batched Triton, and Humming `grouped_masked` GPU correctness tests
- standard unmasked activation: unchanged shared `apply_moe_activation` path
- invalid expert IDs: negative and positive out-of-range IDs are converted to the sentinel before `expert_map` indexing
- DeepEP low-latency + Humming: intentionally rejected with a clear reason because low-latency dispatch does not support Humming's deferred input quantization contract

The full-model DSV4 and Kimi runs exercise DeepEP v2 `grouped_contiguous`. There is no fresh full-model run of `BatchedExperts -> grouped_masked` after the final merge from `main`; that layout is covered at the kernel/backend-test level. Legacy DeepEP v1 was tested earlier during development, while the final validation round focused on v2 because it is the important new layout.

## Tests

After the final merge from `main`:

- focused PR test suite: **57 passed**
  - 17 activation tests
  - 10 Humming tests
  - 6 batched-expert tests
  - 24 permute/SITU tests
- current two-GPU DeepEP v2 smoke case: **1 passed**

```bash
chg run -g=2 -- env EP_DISABLE_GIN=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  'tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_moe.py::test_deep_ep_v2_moe[world_dp_size0-6-32-3-1024-2048-dtype0]' \
  -q -s
# 1 passed
```

Also completed:

- incremental CUDA/C++ native rebuild after the final merge from `main`
- pre-commit hooks on all 15 changed files
- `git diff origin/main...HEAD --check`

## Duplicate-work check

Open-PR searches for `masked MoE activation Humming`, `SITU Humming`, and `apply_moe_activation batched` found only this PR, so this does not duplicate another open change.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to develop and test this change. The human submitter reviewed the changed lines, understands the implementation and validation, and is responsible for defending the change end to end.

title: [Feature]: DeepSeek V4: option to preserve <think>/</think> markers in chat completion content
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

### Environment
- vLLM v0.25.1
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash
- Startup: --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice
  (--reasoning-parser is NOT configured)

### Repro
POST /v1/chat/completions with:
{
  "chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking": true},
  "return_token_ids": true,
  "return_prompt_text": true
}

### Observed
- prompt_text ends with `<think>` and prompt_token_ids ends with 128821, so `</think>` is 128822.

- Generated token_ids contain 128822 `</think>`, but content no longer contains
  `<think>/</think>`. Reasoning text is still concatenated into content.

### Expected
Same as v0.23/v0.24 when --reasoning-parser is not set: raw model text,
including `<think>/</think>`, is returned in content. Or at minimum a
request-level option to restore that behavior.

### Root cause
PR #45877 ported DeepSeek V4 to the streaming parser engine:
- vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py:43-44 defines `<think>/</think>` as terminals
- vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py:151-155 absorbs `</think>` in CONTENT state with no event
- vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine.py:696-740 only puts TEXT_CHUNK into content
- ParserEngineToolAdapter.extract_tool_calls -> extract_tool_calls_from_content
  (vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine.py:543) parses the full output from CONTENT state

The legacy regex parser returned content=model_output unchanged when no DSML
block was found (v0.24 vllm/tool_parsers/deepseekv32_tool_parser.py:189).

### Suggested solution
Add a request-level opt-in, e.g. chat_template_kwargs={"keep_thinking_tags": true},
honored by DeepSeekV4Parser, that removes THINK_START/THINK_END from the engine
terminals so the markers are emitted as plain TEXT_CHUNK. Default stays current.

### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Rocm] Fix AITER_MLA issues for the kimik3-dspark model with Agentic workload
body:
## Summary

Kimi-K3 DSpark fails to start on 8x AMD Instinct MI355X when AITER MLA is enabled with FP8 KV cache, TP8, LMCache MP offload, and the AgentX concurrency-2 workload configuration.

Kimi-K3 has 96 MLA query heads, so TP8 gives 12 local heads per rank. The current non-divisor small-head path pads 12 heads to 16 and routes single-token decode (`qseqlen=1`) to AITER ASM persistent MLA. AITER then cannot select a gfx950 kernel for the resulting BF16-query/FP8-KV configuration. Every rank fails with the same deterministic error before the server becomes ready.

Running Issues:
****************
(Worker_TP1 pid=1389918) [aiter] [fused_moe] using 2stage (kernelName1='flydsl_moe1_afp8_wfp4_bf16_t32x64x256_w4_gui_kw2_fp8', kernelName2='flydsl_moe2_afp8_wfp4_bf16_t32x256x256_reduce_persist') for ('gfx950', 256, 2, 3584, 384, 896, 16, 'ActivationType.Situv2', 'torch.bfloat16', 'torch.float8_e4m3fn', 'torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2', 'QuantType.per_1x32', True, False) 
[AITER] /app/aiter/aiter_meta/csrc/py_itfs_cu/asm_mla.cu:193 get_heuristic_kernel_mla: cannot get heuristic kernel! q_type:bf16 kv_type:fp8 gqa:16 ps:0 prefill:0 causal:0 qseqlen:1 lse:0 cprr:0
[AITER] /app/aiter/aiter_meta/csrc/py_itfs_cu/asm_mla.cu:193 get_heuristic_kernel_mla: cannot get heuristic kernel! q_type:bf16 kv_type:fp8 gqa:16 ps:0 prefill:0 causal:0 qseqlen:1 lse:0 cprr:0
(EngineCore pid=1389568)     return future if non_block else future.result()
(EngineCore pid=1389568)                                     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
(EngineCore pid=1389568)   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 91, in result
(EngineCore pid=1389568)     return super().result()
(EngineCore pid=1389568)            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
****************
Failed InferenceX job: https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/31077120323/job/92537712903

## Test environment

- Hardware: 8x AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`)
- Host ROCm driver: 6.16.6
- Container: `haihub007/hc-gpu:kimik3-dspark-lmcache-pr50618-pr51040-aiter4474-20260806-shadowfix1`
- Container digest: `sha256:7f1c79836ecf99b121741a19db8fc35e384d4eaba43a688d09348f6e8fb3cddb`
- vLLM: `0.26.1rc1.dev229+g124154a88`
- PyTorch: `2.11.0+gitd0c8b1f`
- HIP runtime reported by PyTorch: `7.2.53211`
- LMCache: `0.5.3rc2`
- AITER: image includes ROCm/AITER PR https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4474
- Model: `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (96 MLA query heads)
- Draft model: `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark`
- Tensor parallel size: 8 (12 local query heads per rank)
- KV cache dtype: FP8
- AgentX session concurrency: 2 (`max-num-seqs=4`)
- Speculative tokens: 3

The container also includes vLLM PRs #50618, #50619, and #51040.

## Reproduction

### Pull the image

```bash
docker pull haihub007/hc-gpu:kimik3-dspark-lmcache-pr50618-pr51040-aiter4474-20260806-shadowfix1
```

### Environment

```bash
export PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1
export PYTHONHASHSEED=42
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM=0
export AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1
export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0
export VLLM_ENABLE_K3_LATENT_MOE_TAIL_FUSION=1
export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1200
export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=7200
export HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1
export SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1
```

### Start the LMCache server

`LMCACHE_L1_SIZE_GB=906` was used on the failing host, which had sufficient `/dev/shm` capacity. Adjust this value for the host being used.

```bash
LMCACHE_L1_SIZE_GB=906
lmcache server \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 6000 \
  --http-host 127.0.0.1 \
  --http-port 8080 \
  --l1-size-gb "$LMCACHE_L1_SIZE_GB" \
  --l1-init-size-gb 20 \
  --l1-read-ttl-seconds 7200 \
  --chunk-size 1536 \
  --max-workers 8 \
  --eviction-trigger-watermark 0.85 \
  --eviction-ratio 0.10 \
  --eviction-policy LRU
```

### Start vLLM

```bash
vllm serve /models/huggingface_hub/ \
  --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8888 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --moe-backend auto \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --load-format auto \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 3000 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 \
  --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"method":"dspark","attention_backend":"TRITON_MLA","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"LMCacheMPConnector","kv_connector_module_path":"lmcache.integration.vllm.lmcache_mp_connector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"lmcache.mp.host":"tcp://127.0.0.1","lmcache.mp.port":6000}}'
```

The server fails during startup, before the AgentX coding trace replay can begin.

## Actual behavior

All TP ranks report:

```text
get_heuristic_kernel_mla: cannot get heuristic kernel!
q_type:bf16 kv_type:fp8 gqa:16 ps:0 prefill:0 causal:0 qseqlen:1 lse:0 cprr:0
```

The padded local head count appears as `gqa:16`; the model's actual local head count is 12 (`96 / TP8`). No matching AITER MLA kernel is selected on gfx950, the engine core exits, and vLLM never becomes ready.

## Expected behavior

vLLM should select a supported AITER/Gluon MLA implementation for Kimi-K3's 12 local heads at TP8, or fall back cleanly, allowing the server to start and serve the AgentX workload with FP8 KV cache and LMCache MP offload.

## Suspected dispatch issue

The non-divisor small-head logic introduced for 12 heads pads the query to 16. For `max_qo_len == 1`, `use_gluon_decode()` returns false when 12 does not divide 16, so execution reaches the ASM persistent decode path. That path asks AITER for the unsupported configuration shown above.

Potential fixes include:

- Keep single-token non-divisor small-head decode (12 heads at TP8) on the Gluon path.
- Add and tune the missing gfx950 AITER MLA kernel-table entry for BF16 Q, FP8 KV, GQA 16, `qseqlen=1`.
- Add a capability check and safe fallback when the padded ASM configuration has no matching kernel.

## Related work

- Kimi-K3 DSpark + LMCache support: #51004
- FP8 MLA prefill for non-divisor small head counts: #51040
- DSpark verification fix: #50619
- Strided wvSplitK fix: #50618
- Large MLA KV-offset fix: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4474

title: [WIP][Model] Add upcoming XingChen4 model support
body:
## Summary

This PR adds native vLLM support for the upcoming **XingChen4** MoE causal model.

XingChen4 reuses the DeepSeek-V2/V3 backbone (MLA attention, MoE block, optional DSA indexer) and replaces the standard residual connection with **Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC)**: the residual stream is expanded into `num_residual_streams` parallel streams mixed by input-dependent, doubly-stochastic matrices produced via Sinkhorn-Knopp projection. The mHC math matches the shared ops in `vllm.model_executor.layers.mhc`, so no private kernels are introduced.
Additionally, this PR enables optional FlagOS/FlagGems acceleration for TeleChat4: it enables the hot-path kernels (MoE, attention, softmax, topk, etc.) and brings measurable end-to-end inference speedups — up to 19.87% TTFT and 26.32% TPOT reduction on high-concurrency long-prompt workloads (H100 benchmark), opt-in and disabled by default.

> **Status: Draft.** Model weights are not yet public on Hugging Face Hub. This PR is opened for early code review. Once weights are released, I will:
> 1. add a test entry in `tests/models/registry.py`
> 2. update `docs/models/supported_models.md`
> 3. mark the PR ready for review.

## Changes

1. `vllm/model_executor/models/telechat4.py`: full model implementation (`TeleChat4ForCausalLM`), including forward pass, mHC adapter, and tensor-parallel `load_weights()`.
2. Register `TeleChat4ForCausalLM` in `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py` and related `__init__.py`.
3. Reasoning parser (`vllm/reasoning/xingchen4_reasoning_parser.py`) for reasoning-capable variants.
4. Tool parser (`vllm/tool_parsers/xingchen4_tool_parser.py`) for auto tool calling.
5. Register `telechat4` in `vllm/config/speculative.py`, `vllm/transformers_utils/model_arch_config_convertor.py`, and `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py`.

## Optional FlagGems acceleration (opt-in)

An optional acceleration path is gated behind the env var `USE_FLAGOS=1` (disabled by default). When set, it enables a curated subset of FlagGems kernels via `flag_gems.only_enable(include=[...])`.

> **Scope note:** The acceleration is only enabled from the TeleChat4 model path — the flag_gems.only_enable(...) call lives exclusively inside telechat4.py and is gated behind the env var, so no other model load path triggers it. The whitelist is intentionally narrow (...), and with the env var unset the behavior is fully unchanged. 
 For completeness: only_enable substitutes operators at the PyTorch dispatch level, so once enabled the kernels apply to any op in the same process that matches the whitelist — we therefore consider this an acceleration prototype and welcome feedback on a more scoped kernel backend.

```bash
pip install flagtree==0.6.1 flag-gems==5.3.4 -i https://resource.flagos.net/repository/flagos-pypi-nvidia/simple            # see version constraints in the PR discussion
USE_FLAGOS=1 vllm serve ${model_path} \
    --chat-template ${model_path}/chat_template.jinja \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name $mode_name \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dtype bfloat16 \
    --nnodes 1 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --max-model-len 262144 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \

```

All TeleChat4 hot-path tests below run with FlagGems **disabled**.

## Benchmark method (H100 × 1)

- Framework: this branch vs. vanilla vLLM baseline (same branch, env var unset).
- Metric: **TTFT** (time to first token) and **TPOT** (time per output token).
- Workload: cold cache for each (input tokens + output tokens) pair.
- Each run: 5 repetitions, report the **median**; standard deviation in parentheses when ≥ 1%.
- No kernel warmup excluded; results reflect end-to-end served latency.

| input+output | concurrency | vanilla TTFT (ms) | flaggems TTFT (ms) | TTFT Δ | vanilla TPOT (ms) | flaggems TPOT (ms) | TPOT Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50K+500 | 1 | 3965 | 3971 | ~0% | 10 | 10 | ~0% |
| 50K+500 | 10 | 23827 | 23050 | 3.26% | 60 | 62 | ~0% |
| 10K+500 | 1 | 486 | 483 | 0.62% | 8 | 8 | ~0% |
| 10K+500 | 10 | 1439 | 1153 | 19.87% | 38 | 28 | 26.32% |
| 1K+500 | 1 | 98 | 98 | ~0% | 8 | 7 | 12.50% |
| 1K+500 | 10 | 185 | 189 | ~0% | 17 | 17 | ~0% |

**Reading:** gains concentrate in the high-concurrency long-prompt case (10K+500, concurrency=10): ~19.87% TTFT / ~26.32% TPOT. Low-concurrency and short-prompt cases are neutral. The benefit is workload-specific, not universal.

## Test plan (internal non-public checkpoint)

1. Single-GPU: init, weight loading, text generation.
2. Tensor-parallel size=2: weight loading and inference.
3. Generation outputs and logits aligned with the Hugging Face transformers reference implementation (layer-wise comparison, reported in the accompanying notes).
4. FlagGems dual-path: default path (env unset) and accelerated path (env set) both produce consistent outputs/logits.

## Usage
```bash
vllm serve ${model_path} \
    --chat-template ${model_path}/chat_template.jinja \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name $mode_name \

    --max-model-len 262144 \

    --enable-log-requests \
    --disable-custom-all-reduce
```

## Known limitations / open items for review

- **mHC checkpoint biases** (`bias_pre` / `bias_post` / `bias_res`) and the `h_res` clamp: currently merged/omitted to match the shared `MHCPreOp` signature. **Please review whether the folded formula is equivalent to the official checkpoint** — this is the main correctness item I need confirmed.
- `_telechat4_transpose_contiguous` custom op exists to keep `comb_mix` C-contiguous for the TileLang `mhc_post` kernel that torch.compile cannot prove. Happy to simplify if reviewers prefer.
- Pipeline parallelism is not supported in mHC mode (n_streams > 1); tensor parallelism is.
