```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: ./send_request.sh [timestamp]
set -euo pipefail

HOST="http://127.0.0.1:8000"
TIMESTAMP="${1:-$(date +%s)}"
NUM_TOKENS="${NUM_TOKENS:-8000}"

if ! [[ "$TIMESTAMP" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
  echo "Error: timestamp must be an integer, got '$TIMESTAMP'" >&2
  exit 1
fi

MODEL="${MODEL:-$(curl -sS "$HOST/v1/models" | jq -r '.data[0].id')}"

RANDOM=$TIMESTAMP
WORDS=(alpha bravo charlie delta echo foxtrot golf hotel india juliet kilo lima
       mike november oscar papa quebec romeo sierra tango uniform victor
       whiskey xray yankee zulu river mountain forest ocean desert canyon
       galaxy nebula photon quantum vector matrix cipher signal packet
       server kernel thread mutex socket cluster shard replica ledger)

PROMPT_FILE="$(mktemp)"
PAYLOAD_FILE="$(mktemp)"
TOKENIZE_PAYLOAD_FILE="$(mktemp)"
TOKENIZE_RESP_FILE="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$PROMPT_FILE" "$PAYLOAD_FILE" "$TOKENIZE_PAYLOAD_FILE" "$TOKENIZE_RESP_FILE"' EXIT
build_prompt() {
  local n_words="$1"
  {
    printf 'Timestamp:%s ' "$TIMESTAMP"
    for ((i = 0; i < n_words; i++)); do
      printf '%s_%s_%d ' "${WORDS[RANDOM % ${#WORDS[@]}]}" "$TIMESTAMP" "$i"
    done
    printf 'Question: summarize the above in one sentence.'
  } > "$PROMPT_FILE"
}

tokenize_count() {
  jq -n --arg model "$MODEL" --rawfile prompt "$PROMPT_FILE" \
    '{model: $model, prompt: $prompt}' > "$TOKENIZE_PAYLOAD_FILE"
  curl -sS -X POST "$HOST/tokenize" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --data-binary "@$TOKENIZE_PAYLOAD_FILE" > "$TOKENIZE_RESP_FILE"
  jq -r '.count' "$TOKENIZE_RESP_FILE"
}
# Grow the word count until the prompt tokenizes to >= NUM_TOKENS.
n_words=$(( (NUM_TOKENS / 2) + 1 ))   # rough starting guess, refined below
while true; do
  build_prompt "$n_words"
  count=$(tokenize_count)
  if (( count >= NUM_TOKENS )); then
    break
  fi
  n_words=$(( n_words * 2 + 1 ))
done

# Truncate to exactly NUM_TOKENS real token ids and send those ids directly
# as the prompt -> exact count, no re-tokenization ambiguity.
token_ids_json=$(jq -c ".tokens[0:${NUM_TOKENS}]" "$TOKENIZE_RESP_FILE")

jq -n --arg model "$MODEL" --argjson prompt "$token_ids_json" \
  '{model: $model, prompt: $prompt, max_tokens: 32, temperature: 0}' > "$PAYLOAD_FILE"

echo "timestamp=$TIMESTAMP target_tokens=$NUM_TOKENS model=$MODEL" >&2

curl -sS -X POST "$HOST/v1/completions" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary "@$PAYLOAD_FILE"
echo




echo "Sleeping before prefix-cache reset ..."
sleep 10
set -x
curl -sS -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8000/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true"
```

title: Bound generation inputs before expensive work
body:
# Bound generation inputs before expensive work

## What this fixes

Five ordinary request values could make vLLM perform work far larger than the JSON body
before an effective limit ran. Examples included tokenizing 50,000 bad words before a
later rejection, scanning 500,000 stop strings after every generated token, and scanning
an entire DeepSeek message history again for every message.

Before this change, a request such as `{"stop":["x", ... 500000 entries ...]}` could
add about 54 seconds to an otherwise identical completion. After this change, public
stop lists are limited to four entries at request parsing. The other affected inputs are
similarly bounded, deduplicated, or processed in one pass before costly work begins.

## Why it matters

An authenticated client could consume frontend CPU or memory out of proportion to the
request size and slow other users. These paths do not expose data or run code; their
impact is reduced service availability.

## The change

| Commit | Input/path | What it now does |
|---|---|---|
| `ec52561` | Streaming beam `n`/width | Enforces `VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES` before per-choice allocation. |
| `c875867` | `bad_words` | Caps the list at 128 before tokenizing every entry. |
| `d343767` | DeepSeek V3.2/V4 histories | Finds the last user message once per conversation. |
| `92daff3` | Public `stop` arrays | Limits Python and Rust request models to four strings. |
| `a1a82f0` | `stop_token_ids` | Removes duplicates while preserving order. |

## How it was tested

All five focused suites show RED-to-GREEN behavior:

| Site | Without the fix | With the fix |
|---|---:|---:|
| Beam sequence cap | 2 failed, 1 passed | 3 passed |
| Bad-word cap | 2 failed | 2 passed |
| DeepSeek history scan | 2 failed, 2 passed | 4 passed |
| Stop-string cap | 4 failed, 4 passed | 8 passed |
| Stop-ID deduplication | 1 failed | 1 passed |

## Reference

Advisory: GHSA-4c3x-h2r4-j55f

Track B: this is a public PR against `vllm-project/vllm@main`.

## Credit

- @KernelClint (Clinton Thomas) and @dhalf (Lucas Bourtoule)
- Patch the Planet (Trail of Bits + OpenAI collaboration); discovered using GPT-5.5-Cyber

All commits include DCO `Signed-off-by` trailers.

title: [Performance] DP8 vs TP8 for single-KV-head MLA: 7.7x KV, 3.4x faster 1M TTFT at c=8 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, 8x B200, vLLM v0.25.0)
body:
### Summary

On a single 8x NVIDIA B200 node, `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.0` serves `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (304B total / 13B active, MLA, 1M context, FP4 experts + FP8 KV) with measured multi-session 1M-context concurrency that has not been published before for this model class.

The headline finding: **parallelism shape matters more than any tuning knob for this model.** The recipes-page default (TP8) reports a startup-log KV budget of 20.43x maximum concurrency for 1,048,576-token requests, i.e. KV capacity for ~20 simultaneous 1M-token sessions ("c" throughout this report = concurrent requests). Switching to `--data-parallel-size 8` reports **156.9x**, a 7.7x improvement, because MLA's single KV head cannot be sharded across tensor-parallel ranks, so TP8 replicates the KV cache 8x; under DP8 (with `--enable-expert-parallel`) each GPU holds an independent KV pool for the data-parallel attention path, while the MoE experts remain sharded EP8 across GPUs (not replicated). For scale: V4-Pro's startup log on the same host class reported 2.0x for the same 1M request shape (vllm-project/vllm#43753; same startup-log KV-budget figure, different model). Both DP8 figures are KV-budget capacity, validated empirically to c=16 in this report, not to c=156.

Measured envelopes (cache-busted real-prose token IDs from the public-domain Federalist Papers corpus, 3 reps per cell, `max_tokens=64`, streaming, 600s client timeout on all cells):

| Parallelism | 1M c=8 TTFT p50 | 1M c=8 ok rate | 1M c=16 ok rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TP8 (recipes default) | 314.6s | 24/24 (100%) | 27/48 (56%) |
| **DP8 (recommended)** | **84.7s** | **24/24 (100%)** | **48/48 (100%)** |

(Same-node controlled follow-up, posted as a comment on this issue: TTFT p50 ratio 3.44x; a fair statement of the DP8 advantage at 1M c=8 is 3.2-3.7x depending on metric and run.)

Additional findings:
- **DSpark speculative decoding at 1M context delivers 4.1x decode-window speedup (matched 0.85/0.85 util), and it exposes a metrics problem**: at 1M c=1 with `max_tokens=512`, DSpark decode-window TPOT is 2.08ms vs vanilla 8.44ms (both at 0.85 util, real Federalist prose, 3 reps; decode-window TPOT = `(wall - TTFT) / (completion_tokens - 1)`). But streaming inter-arrival TPOT reports 11.18ms, 5.4x higher than the decode-window TPOT, because 512 tokens arrive in ~96 stream chunks under 5-token speculation, and the inter-arrival mean divides by chunks not tokens. Vanilla streaming TPOT (8.97ms) closely matches its decode-window TPOT (8.44ms) because tokens arrive individually (details in the DSpark section). Crossover: tail-latency collapse at c>=4 on the tested 8K TP8 cells (mean TPOT explodes while p50 stays single-digit).
- **Prefix-cache warm-document: 22x speedup**: first question on a 1M-token document in 66s, every follow-up in ~3s.
- torch.compile is not supported for this model on v0.25.0; the auto-disable via `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` appears intentional (vLLM warns the model does not support it; confirmation requested in ask 2).
- Increasing `--max-num-batched-tokens` beyond 8192 yields no TTFT improvement and costs 32% of KV capacity.

Context for why this model matters: DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 is currently the #3 open-weights model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (retrieved 2026-08-07) at very low per-task cost; this report adds a measured 1M-context concurrency envelope for it on a single node.

Prior art: vllm-project/vllm#43753 (DeepSeek-V4-Pro 1M on 8x B200, same host class). V4-Pro's startup log reported 2.0x max concurrency at 1M and our testing there topped out at "1M c=2, isolated queue." V4-Flash-0731 on DP8 serves 1M c=16 with 100% success.

**Updates** (body revised with follow-up work; the linked comments are the audit trail):

- 2026-08-07: DP8/EP8 mechanism wording corrected (attention/KV data-parallel; experts EP-sharded, not replicated); focused recipes proposal filed as vllm-project/recipes#762.
- 2026-08-08: same-node TP8-vs-DP8 bridge posted (closes the cross-node limitation); title and headline restated to the controlled 3.4x figure, range 3.2-3.7x.
- 2026-08-08: measured DP8 mitigation for ask 4 (single-1M mixed workload, same node: short TTFT p50 63.9s to 0.57s, ~112x, 1M unchanged); ask 4 narrowed to TP8 deployments and the all-replicas-busy case ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51454#issuecomment-5229675310)).

### Maintainer asks

1. **DP8 vs TP8 for MLA models**: The recipes-page B200 profile uses `--tensor-parallel-size 8`, but `--data-parallel-size 8` delivers 7.7x more total KV capacity and 3.4x faster TTFT at 1M c=8 for this model (same-node controlled measurement; 3.7x in the original cross-node ladder, see the follow-up comment). Should the recipes page recommend DP8 as the default for concurrency- and long-context-oriented serving of single-KV-head MLA models, keeping TP8 for latency-critical single-stream (c=1-2; our measured break-even is c=3)? Is this a known property that could be surfaced more prominently?

2. **torch.compile auto-disable**: `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` is auto-set for this model, disabling torch.compile (`mode=NONE`). Forcing `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` turns on `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`, but vLLM warns "the model does not support it." Is this intentional, and is torch.compile support planned for DeepSeek-V4-Flash on a future tag?

3. **Speculative-decode metrics on stable**: streaming inter-arrival TPOT is not interpretable under speculative burst delivery: our matched-util A/B shows it reporting 11.18ms (5.4x higher than the true decode-window TPOT of 2.08ms) because 512 tokens arrive in ~96 stream chunks under 5-token speculation, and the inter-arrival mean divides by chunks not tokens. Decode-window TPOT `(wall - TTFT) / (completion_tokens - 1)` is the correct metric but requires `max_tokens` large enough for a measurable decode window. Acceptance-rate fields (`verifier_accept_len`) are nightly-only, so on v0.25.0 stable there is no built-in way to quantify spec-decode speedup from the serving API. Ask: would you accept exposing acceptance-length and decode-window metrics on stable, or documenting that TPOT metrics are burst-artifacted under spec decode? We are happy to file this as a separate metrics issue if preferred.

4. **Mixed-workload scheduler knobs**: `--long-prefill-token-threshold` and `--scheduling-policy priority` (with per-request priorities) have no effect on short-request TTFT beside a 1M prefill on v0.25.0. `--max-num-partial-prefills > 1` raises `NotImplementedError`. Is improved prefill preemption planned for a future release? This is the most operationally important gap: serving 1M-context requests alongside short requests without queue isolation currently starves the short requests for the full prefill duration (~65s). Follow-up (2026-08-08): monolithic DP8 avoids this for the single-long-prefill case via replica isolation (~112x short-TTFT improvement at p50, same-node A/B; [details](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51454#issuecomment-5229675310)), so this ask now primarily concerns TP8 deployments and the case where long prefills occupy all DP replicas.

5. **DSpark stable-vs-nightly knob gap**: `verifier_accept_len` and `dspark_block_size` are nightly-only speculative-config fields (pydantic rejects them on v0.25.0). The recipes-page B200 cell pins a nightly tag. Is there a timeline for these knobs to reach stable?

6. **`draft_sample_method` discrepancy**: The HF model card says `greedy`; the vLLM recipes page emits `probabilistic`. We A/B tested both on real prose (7 cells, 3 reps each): no significant difference (greedy 0-16% slower at c=1, identical at c=2+). Ask: align the recipes page with the HF card (or document why `probabilistic` is emitted); this is a one-line recipes-repo fix and we can file it there if preferred.

Note on routing: asks 1 and 6 may belong on the recipes repo and ask 3 could be a standalone metrics issue; we kept them here for context and will split on maintainer preference.

### Environment

| Component | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Cloud / instance | Nebius AI Cloud, two preemptible 8-GPU nodes. Node 1: correctness suite, real-prose ladder, TP8 concurrency envelope, tuning sweeps, first DSpark probe. Node 2: DP8 1M ladder, KV-eviction probe, scheduler-knob experiment, DSpark crossover. Same image + model snapshot on both; KV capacity verified identical. |
| GPUs | 8x NVIDIA B200 SXM6 |
| GPU architecture | SM100 |
| VRAM | 183,359 MiB per GPU |
| Driver | 580.126.09 (node 1) / 580.173.02 (node 2) |
| Model | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, snapshot `7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062` |
| Model on disk | 155.4 GiB, 48 safetensors shards |
| Serving image | `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.0`. Hub amd64 digest `sha256:e1c1ff1af9a15921bfa11d1d95047258c1797392cdbfa296e7639da446b23f97`; pull manifest digest `sha256:fc56161ee42a`; local image ID `sha256:d5219758abb3` (same image, three identifier forms) |
| vLLM version | 0.25.0 (V1 engine), build commit `dd10e03f95f94edbea1975c67ace3a35ec9a8a40` |
| Python | 3.12 |
| CUDA / PyTorch | CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130 |
| NCCL | 2.28.9 |
| Triton | 3.6.0 |
| FlashInfer | 0.6.13 |
| DeepEP | 1.2.1+73b6ea4 |
| Transformers | 5.13.0 |
| Accelerate | 1.14.0 |
| huggingface_hub | 1.23.0 |

Provenance: all version rows captured from in-container `pip freeze`, `torch.cuda.nccl.version()`, `nvidia-smi`, and vLLM startup logs. Full 262-package pip freeze available with proof artifacts on request.

### Launch command (TP8, recipes-page default)

```bash
docker run -d --name v4flash0731 --gpus all --ipc=host --shm-size 32g \
  --ulimit nofile=1048576:1048576 \
  -v /data/hf-cache:/root/.cache/huggingface -p 8000:8000 \
  vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.0 \
  /root/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--deepseek-ai--DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/snapshots/7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4-flash-0731 --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --attention_config.use_fp4_indexer_cache=True \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 \
```

The speedup factor grows with both context length and concurrency, because DP8 distributes prefill across 8 independent GPU replicas rather than sharing one request across all 8 GPUs. The trade-off: 1M c=1-2 is comparable or slightly slower under DP8 (single-GPU prefill vs 8-GPU TP prefill). Break-even at c=3.

Root cause of the KV capacity delta: MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention) uses 1 KV head. Under TP8, the KV cache cannot be sharded across tensor-parallel ranks and is replicated 8x. Under DP8 with `--enable-expert-parallel`, the attention/KV path is data-parallel: each GPU holds its own independent KV pool and runs the full attention stack, while the MoE expert weights remain sharded EP8 across all GPUs (not replicated); expert traffic crosses GPUs via EP all-to-all. So "independent" applies to the attention/KV state, not the whole model. The per-GPU KV pool is 20.6M tokens (vs TP8's 21.4M, slightly less due to per-GPU overhead), and 8 independent pools sum to 164.6M.

Tested whether vLLM v0.25.0 scheduler knobs can fix short-request starvation beside a 1M prefill. Scenario: 1x 1M request + 8x 8K requests (max_tokens=64), 3 reps each.

\* The streaming-TPOT values at this cell (0.25ms mean) are a burst-delivery measurement artifact, withdrawn to prevent out-of-context quotation; the valid decode-window measurement is 2.08ms (matched-util re-measurement below). ** Throughput not meaningful for a TTFT-dominated cell (65.7s prefill, ~64 output tokens). The 8K c=1 TTFT mean (5.8s vs 0.4s at c=2) includes a first-request cold-start; p50 was 0.26s.

**Streaming-TPOT measurement caveat (resolved by the matched-util re-measurement below).** The 0.25ms mean (0.24ms p50) above is streaming inter-arrival TPOT, and under 5-token speculation it is **not a valid per-token decode latency**: tokens arrive in bursts of up to 6, so the inter-arrival mean divides by the number of stream chunks (~96 for 512 tokens at max_tokens=512), not the number of tokens. The vanilla comparison was additionally unmatched (util 0.95 vs 0.85; vanilla 1M TPOT from a random-token-ID ladder). The matched-util re-measurement below re-measures at max_tokens=512 with decode-window arithmetic on a matched-util A/B, yielding a defensible **4.1x multiplier** at 1M c=1.

**Tail-latency collapse at c>=4**: the mean TPOT explodes (7.8ms at c=3 to 64.2ms at c=4) while p50 stays single-digit (6.3ms at c=3 to 9.9ms at c=4). The mean inflation is driven by straggler requests, not uniform degradation. Under the tested 8K TP8 workload, SLO-bound serving should switch DSpark off at c>=4; treat c>=4 with caution on other workloads until higher-concurrency long-context cells are measured. Regime rule (8K TP8): DSpark on for c=1-3 (interactive), off for c=4+ (batch throughput). This matches the recipes-page guidance ("low latency & small batch size") and the SGLang pattern of dropping MTP at saturation.

#### Matched-util decode-window re-measurement

The crossover table above uses streaming inter-arrival TPOT at `max_tokens=64`, which is not a valid per-token metric under speculative burst delivery (the 1M c=1 row is artifacted; see caveat above). This subsection re-measures DSpark decode speedup with a method that is valid: decode-window TPOT = `(wall - TTFT) / (completion_tokens - 1)`, at `max_tokens=512`, on a matched-util A/B (both legs at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`, identical cache-busted Federalist real-prose prompts, temperature=0, streaming, 3 reps per cell). `min_tokens=512` is set because the model naturally generates <15 tokens at 1M context before EOS.

| Cell | Leg | Decode-window TPOT (mean) | Decode window (mean) | Streaming TPOT (mean) | Stream chunks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1M c=1 | Vanilla 0.85 | 8.44ms | 4.31s | 8.97ms | ~482 |
| 1M c=1 | DSpark 0.85 | 2.08ms | 1.06s | 11.18ms | ~96 |
| 8K c=1 | Vanilla 0.85 | 7.82ms | 4.00s | 7.82ms | 512 |
| 8K c=1 | DSpark 0.85 | 4.97ms | 2.54s | 9.71ms | ~262 |

**Decode-window multiplier (matched 0.85/0.85 util):** 1M c=1 = **4.1x** (8.44/2.08); 8K c=1 = **1.6x** (7.82/4.97). The multiplier is context-dependent: at 1M, each verify pass is amortized over more attention computation; at 8K, the decode is cheaper and the draft-model overhead is proportionally larger.

**Streaming-artifact contrast (side-by-side):** DSpark streaming TPOT (11.18ms at 1M) is 5.4x higher than its decode-window TPOT (2.08ms), because 512 tokens arrive in ~96 stream chunks (5.3 tokens/chunk); the inter-arrival mean divides by ~95 instead of ~511. Vanilla streaming TPOT (8.97ms) closely matches its decode-window TPOT (8.44ms, 1.06x) because tokens arrive individually (482 chunks for 512 tokens). This demonstrates that streaming TPOT is not a valid per-token metric under speculative burst delivery; decode-window TPOT correctly accounts for the burst structure by dividing by the actual token count.

```python
@dataclass
class RequestSpec:
    label: str
    role: str
    context: str
    max_tokens: int
    delay_s: float = 0.0


def gpu_snapshot() -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    cmd = [
        "nvidia-smi",
        "--query-gpu=index,memory.used,memory.total,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,pstate",
        "--format=csv,noheader,nounits",
    ]
    try:
        out = subprocess.check_output(cmd, text=True, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    except Exception as exc:
        return [{"error": str(exc)}]
    rows = []
    for line in out.strip().splitlines():
        parts = [p.strip() for p in line.split(",")]
        if len(parts) == 6:
            rows.append(
                {
                    "index": parts[0],
                    "memory_used_mib": parts[1],
                    "memory_total_mib": parts[2],
                    "utilization_gpu_pct": parts[3],
                    "temperature_c": parts[4],
                    "pstate": parts[5],
                }
            )
    return rows


def metrics_snapshot(base_url: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        resp = requests.get(f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/metrics", timeout=5)
        text = resp.text
    except Exception as exc:
        return {"error": repr(exc)}
    keep = {}
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("#") or not line.startswith("vllm:"):
            continue
        name, _, raw_value = line.partition(" ")
        metric = name.split("{", 1)[0]
        if any(key in metric for key in ("num_requests", "gpu_cache_usage", "kv_cache", "request")):
            try:
                value: Any = float(raw_value)
            except ValueError:
                value = raw_value
            keep.setdefault(metric, []).append(value)
    return {"selected": keep}


def cleanliness(text: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    non_ascii_count = sum(1 for ch in text if ord(ch) > 127)
    cjk_count = sum(1 for ch in text if "\u4e00" <= ch <= "\u9fff")
    de_count = text.count("\u7684")
    return {
        "text_len": len(text),
        "non_ascii_count": non_ascii_count,
        "non_ascii_ratio": (non_ascii_count / len(text)) if text else 0,
        "cjk_count": cjk_count,
        "ascii_clean": non_ascii_count == 0,
        "corruption_clean": cjk_count == 0 and de_count == 0,
        "clean": bool(text) and non_ascii_count == 0 and cjk_count == 0 and de_count == 0,
    }


def percentile(values: list[float], pct: float) -> float | None:
    if not values:
        return None
    ordered = sorted(values)
    idx = min(len(ordered) - 1, max(0, round((pct / 100.0) * (len(ordered) - 1))))
    return ordered[idx]


def build_base_prompt(context: str, federalist: str, variant: int, repeat: int = 0) -> str:
    cfg = CONTEXTS[context]
    n_reps = int(cfg["repeats"])
    ts = time.time_ns()
    parts = []
    for i in range(n_reps):
        parts.append(f"[Segment {repeat}-{variant}-{i}-{ts}]")
        parts.append(federalist)
    base = "\n\n".join(parts)
    return (
        "Continue the following public-domain prose in plain ASCII English.\n\n"
        f"{base}"
    )


def stream_completion(args: argparse.Namespace, spec: RequestSpec, prompt: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    url = f"{args.base_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/completions"
    body = {
        "model": args.model,
        "prompt": prompt,
        "max_tokens": spec.max_tokens,
        "temperature": 0,
        "stream": True,
        "stream_options": {"include_usage": True},
    }
    timeout_s = int(CONTEXTS[spec.context]["timeout_s"])
    started = time.time()
    first_token = None
    last_token = None
    chunks = 0
    text_parts: list[str] = []
    usage = None
    error = None
    status_code = None
    try:
        with requests.post(url, json=body, stream=True, timeout=(30, timeout_s)) as resp:
            status_code = resp.status_code
            if resp.status_code >= 400:
                error = f"HTTP {resp.status_code}: {resp.text[:1000]}"
            else:
                for line in resp.iter_lines():
                    if not line:
                        continue
                    if line.startswith(b"data: "):
                        data = line[6:].strip()
                    else:
                        data = line.strip()
                    if data == b"[DONE]":
                        break
                    try:
                        obj = json.loads(data)
                    except json.JSONDecodeError:
                        continue
                    if obj.get("usage"):
                        usage = obj.get("usage")
                    for choice in obj.get("choices", []):
                        delta = choice.get("text") or ""
                        if delta:
                            now = time.time()
                            if first_token is None:
                                first_token = now
                            last_token = now
                            chunks += 1
                            text_parts.append(delta)
    except Exception as exc:
        error = repr(exc)
    finished = time.time()
    text = "".join(text_parts)
    clean = cleanliness(text)
    return {
        "label": spec.label,
        "role": spec.role,
        "context": spec.context,
        "max_tokens": spec.max_tokens,
        "prompt_chars": len(prompt),
        "status": "ok" if error is None else "error",
        "status_code": status_code,
        "error": error,
        "started_at_utc": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime(started)),
        "finished_at_utc": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime(finished)),
        "wall_sec": finished - started,
        "ttft_sec": (first_token - started) if first_token is not None else None,
        "decode_sec": (last_token - first_token) if first_token is not None and last_token is not None else None,
        "stream_chunks": chunks,
        "usage": usage,
        "cleanliness": clean,
        "text_first_240": text[:240],
        "text_last_240": text[-240:],
    }


def run_specs(args: argparse.Namespace, name: str, specs: list[RequestSpec], federalist: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    cell_dir = args.out_dir / name
    cell_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for spec in specs:
        (cell_dir / f"{spec.label}.request.json").write_text(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    "label": spec.label,
                    "role": spec.role,
                    "context": spec.context,
                    "max_tokens": spec.max_tokens,
                    "delay_s": spec.delay_s,
                },
                indent=2,
            )
        )

    all_repeat_results = []
    for rep in range(1, args.repeats + 1):
        rep_name = f"rep{rep}" if args.repeats > 1 else "rep1"
        prompts = {
            spec.label: build_base_prompt(spec.context, federalist, idx, rep)
            for idx, spec in enumerate(specs, start=1)
        }
        print(f"=== {name}/{rep_name} start requests={len(specs)} ===", flush=True)
        before_gpu = gpu_snapshot()
        before_metrics = metrics_snapshot(args.base_url)
        start_wall = time.time()
        barrier = threading.Barrier(len(specs))

        def worker(spec: RequestSpec, _prompts: dict[str, str] = prompts) -> dict[str, Any]:
            barrier.wait()
            if spec.delay_s:
                time.sleep(spec.delay_s)
            return stream_completion(args, spec, _prompts[spec.label])

        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(specs)) as pool:
            rows = list(pool.map(worker, specs))

        end_wall = time.time()
        after_gpu = gpu_snapshot()
        after_metrics = metrics_snapshot(args.base_url)
        rep_result = {
            "rep": rep,
            "started_at_utc": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime(start_wall)),
            "finished_at_utc": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime(end_wall)),
            "cell_wall_sec": end_wall - start_wall,
            "gpu_before": before_gpu,
            "gpu_after": after_gpu,
            "metrics_before": before_metrics,
            "metrics_after": after_metrics,
            "requests": rows,
            "summary": summarize_requests(rows),
        }
        (cell_dir / f"{rep_name}.result.json").write_text(json.dumps(rep_result, indent=2))
        all_repeat_results.append(rep_result)
        rep_summary = rep_result["summary"]
        print(
            f"{name}/{rep_name} done wall={rep_result['cell_wall_sec']:.1f}s "
            f"ok={rep_summary['ok']}/{rep_summary['requests']} "
            f"clean={rep_summary['clean']}/{rep_summary['requests']} "
            f"ttft_p50={rep_summary['ttft_p50_sec']} ttft_p99={rep_summary['ttft_p99_sec']} "
            f"wall_p50={rep_summary['wall_p50_sec']} wall_p99={rep_summary['wall_p99_sec']}",
            flush=True,
        )
        if rep_summary["ok"] < rep_summary["requests"]:
            print(f"  WARNING: {rep_summary['ok']}/{rep_summary['requests']} ok -- errors present", flush=True)

    cross_rep_rows = [row for rep in all_repeat_results for row in rep["requests"]]
    for row in cross_rep_rows:
        (cell_dir / f"{row['label']}.response_excerpt.txt").write_text(row.get("text_first_240", ""))
    cross_summary = summarize_requests(cross_rep_rows)
    result = {
        "name": name,
        "repeats": args.repeats,
        "all_reps": all_repeat_results,
        "summary": cross_summary,
    }
    (cell_dir / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    print(
        f"=== {name} ALL REPS done: "
        f"ok={cross_summary['ok']}/{cross_summary['requests']} "
        f"clean={cross_summary['clean']}/{cross_summary['requests']} "
        f"ttft_p50={cross_summary['ttft_p50_sec']} ttft_p99={cross_summary['ttft_p99_sec']} "
        f"wall_p50={cross_summary['wall_p50_sec']} wall_p99={cross_summary['wall_p99_sec']} ===",
        flush=True,
    )
    return result


def summarize_requests(rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    ok = [row for row in rows if row.get("status") == "ok"]
    clean = [row for row in ok if row.get("cleanliness", {}).get("clean")]
    ttfts = [row["ttft_sec"] for row in ok if row.get("ttft_sec") is not None]
    walls = [row["wall_sec"] for row in ok if row.get("wall_sec") is not None]
    decode = [row["decode_sec"] for row in ok if row.get("decode_sec") is not None]
    return {
        "requests": len(rows),
        "ok": len(ok),
        "clean": len(clean),
        "all_clean": len(rows) > 0 and len(clean) == len(rows),
        "ttft_mean_sec": statistics.mean(ttfts) if ttfts else None,
        "ttft_p50_sec": percentile(ttfts, 50),
        "ttft_p95_sec": percentile(ttfts, 95),
        "ttft_p99_sec": percentile(ttfts, 99),
        "wall_mean_sec": statistics.mean(walls) if walls else None,
        "wall_p50_sec": percentile(walls, 50),
        "wall_p95_sec": percentile(walls, 95),
        "wall_p99_sec": percentile(walls, 99),
        "decode_mean_sec": statistics.mean(decode) if decode else None,
        "errors": [row for row in rows if row.get("status") != "ok"],
    }


def make_concurrency_specs(cell: dict[str, Any]) -> list[RequestSpec]:
    return [
        RequestSpec(
            label=f"{cell['cell']}_r{i}",
            role="long",
            context=cell["context"],
            max_tokens=int(cell["max_tokens"]),
        )
        for i in range(1, int(cell["concurrency"]) + 1)
    ]


def make_mixed_specs(name: str) -> list[RequestSpec]:
    specs = []
    for group in MIXED_SCENARIOS[name]:
        for i in range(1, int(group["count"]) + 1):
            specs.append(
                RequestSpec(
                    label=f"{name}_{group['role']}_{group['context']}_{i}",
                    role=group["role"],
                    context=group["context"],
                    max_tokens=int(group["max_tokens"]),
                    delay_s=float(group["delay_s"]),
                )
            )
    return specs


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--base-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:8000")
    parser.add_argument("--model", default="deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731")
    parser.add_argument("--haystack", type=Path, default=Path("/data/work/haystack-federalist.txt"))
    parser.add_argument("--out-dir", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--mode", choices=["concurrency", "mixed"], default="concurrency")
    parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=3, help="Repeats per cell (for p50/p99 stability)")
    parser.add_argument("--only-cells", help="Comma-separated concurrency cell names")
    parser.add_argument("--mixed-scenarios", help="Comma-separated mixed scenarios")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    federalist = args.haystack.read_text()
    all_results = []
    if args.mode == "concurrency":
        cells = CONCURRENCY_CELLS
        if args.only_cells:
            wanted = {item.strip() for item in args.only_cells.split(",") if item.strip()}
            cells = [cell for cell in cells if cell["cell"] in wanted]
            if not cells:
                raise SystemExit(f"no cells selected by --only-cells={args.only_cells!r}")
        for idx, cell in enumerate(cells):
            if idx > 0:
                time.sleep(5)
            all_results.append(
                run_specs(args, cell["cell"], make_concurrency_specs(cell), federalist)
            )
    else:
        names = list(MIXED_SCENARIOS)
        if args.mixed_scenarios:
            wanted = {item.strip() for item in args.mixed_scenarios.split(",") if item.strip()}
            names = [name for name in names if name in wanted]
            if not names:
                raise SystemExit(f"no scenarios selected by --mixed-scenarios={args.mixed_scenarios!r}")
        for idx, name in enumerate(names):
            if idx > 0:
                time.sleep(5)
            all_results.append(run_specs(args, name, make_mixed_specs(name), federalist))

    summary = {
        "mode": args.mode,
        "repeats": args.repeats,
        "model": args.model,
        "results": [
            {
                "name": row["name"],
                **row["summary"],
            }
            for row in all_results
        ],
    }
    (args.out_dir / "t1-summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    (args.out_dir / "t1-results.json").write_text(json.dumps(all_results, indent=2))
    print("=== SUMMARY ===", flush=True)
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2), flush=True)
    return 0 if all(row["summary"]["all_clean"] for row in all_results) else 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

title: [CI] Fix and extend PR/issue auto-labeling
body:
## Purpose

Auditing the labeling setup against the actual repo turned up rules that had stopped matching the code they were written for, plus issue-side labeling that covered only 6 of 62 labels.

### Rules that were missing real work

- **`deepseek` missed the `vllm/models/` tree.** Newer models live in `vllm/models/<model>/` rather than `vllm/model_executor/models/`. The rule only knew the old location, so only the title match applied — **64 of 99 PRs** touching `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/` went unlabeled. Same gap for `deepseek_v32`.
- **`speculative-decoding` missed the Model Runner V2 subtree.** `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/` has seen 94 PRs in 6 months, more than the original `vllm/v1/spec_decode/` at 81. This also folds `dflash` and `dspark` under the umbrella label, per review feedback that both are spec decoding techniques.

### Rules that could never fire

Four conditions used `files=` (exact match) with regex syntax, or carried a doubled backslash that YAML passes through literally:

```yaml
- files=^examples/features/speculative_decoding/    # never matches
- files~=^\\.buildkite/intel_jobs/                  # never matches
```

A further 13 conditions pointed at files that have since moved or been deleted — `harmony` moved to the Rust frontend, `pallas` is gone. Repointed where the code moved, removed where it is gone.

### Retired: `new-model`

The rule fired on any PR touching a model file **and** `registry.py`. `registry.py` is edited for renames, aliases, refactors and removals, not just additions.

Of the 25 most recent PRs carrying the label, 10 added a model. The rest included:

- `[Model] Remove Ouro`, `[Model] Remove Plamo2`, `Remove PersimmonForCausalLM and FuyuForCausalLM` — PRs that **delete** models
- `[model registry] some simple typos`
- `[Perf] Optimize clamp to clamp_`, `[Kernel] ReplaySSM: cache SSM inputs`, `Revert "Blackwell decode optimizations"`

Whether a new architecture was registered depends on what changed *inside* `registry.py`. Mergify matches file paths, not diff contents, so this rule cannot be made accurate — tightening the paths does not help. 111 open PRs currently carry the label.

The label remains on issues, applied by the New Model template, where the requester states the intent explicitly.

### Rule that fired too often

`nvidia` matched `requirements/cuda.txt`, so dependency bumps were tagged as NVIDIA backend work. Measured across 200 merged PRs, 17 carried the label and this was the one clear miss.

### New rules

`scheduler`, `kv-cache-manager`, `glm`, `minimax`, `inkling`, `DSv4`, `dflash`, `torch.compile`, `ray`, `vllm-ir`.

### Issue labeling

Extended from 6 labels to 31. Terms match **titles only** by design: issue bodies carry pasted `collect_env` output that names unrelated hardware and libraries, which tags the reporter's environment rather than the topic.

### Guard against recurrence

`tools/pre_commit/check_label_rules.py` fails when a file condition matches nothing in the tree, and runs via pre-commit when `mergify.yml` changes. It caught two bugs in this change while it was being written.

### Also removed: the New Model issue template

`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/600-new-model.yml` is deleted.

- Usage fell from 155 issues in 2025 to 30 in 2026, only 3 since July
- It applied a label named `new model`, but the label is `new-model`. GitHub silently skips a label that does not exist, so requests went untagged from the March rename onward — five months, unnoticed
- 292 of the 304 ever filed are closed
- Model support arrives as planned work rather than as community requests

`blank_issues_enabled` is `false`, so model requests route to Feature Request.

**Nothing applies `new-model` after this change.** The label is left in place so it stays on the 917 PRs and 304 issues carrying it; deleting the label itself is a separate call.

## Before merging

**The five new labels must be created first** — `scheduler`, `kv-cache-manager`, `glm`, `minimax`, `inkling`. Mergify errors on a label that does not exist.

Two related items a PR cannot do:
- `mrv1-only`'s description currently reads "apply only to Model Runner V2 (not applicable to Model Runner V2)" — says V2 twice.
- `DSv4` has a rule here mirroring the `kimi`/`k3` split, but whether to keep it as a distinct label is a maintainer call.

## Test Plan

Rules were validated against the real file tree and against real issues and PRs, rather than by inspection.

```bash
# every file condition in mergify.yml matches at least one tracked file
python tools/pre_commit/check_label_rules.py

pre-commit run check-label-rules --files .github/mergify.yml
pre-commit run ruff-check  --files tools/pre_commit/check_label_rules.py
pre-commit run ruff-format --files tools/pre_commit/check_label_rules.py
```

## Test Result

```
tracked files: 6430   rules: 44
file conditions matching >=1 file: 154
file conditions matching NOTHING:  0

Check auto-label rules still match real files............................Passed
ruff check...............................................................Passed
ruff format..............................................................Passed
```

Negative test: injecting a condition pointing at a nonexistent path makes the check exit 1 and name the offending rule.

New rules were spot-checked against the tree — `glm` matches 21 files and correctly ignores `midashenglm.py`, which contains the substring "glm" but is an unrelated model. Issue rules were replayed over 600 real issues: 43% now receive at least one label, and the existing rules agreed with hand-applied labels (`kimi` 35 fires / 31 already labeled, `rocm` 34 / 33, `k3` 27 / 26).

No model evaluation is included because this change touches only CI labeling configuration. It does not affect inference, model output, accuracy, or serving.

## Note on AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to audit the existing rules, measure PR and issue volumes, and draft these changes. Every measurement quoted above is reproducible with the commands shown. I have reviewed each changed line.

title: [Bugfix] Install the weight offloader in the V2 model runner
body:
Fixes #50672

`set_offloader(create_offloader(...))` is only called from the V1 GPU model runner.
The V2 runner never installs an offloader, so `make_layers()` gets the process-global
default `NoopOffloader` and `--cpu-offload-gb` is silently a no-op.
`KimiK3ForConditionalGeneration` is in `DEFAULT_V2_MODEL_RUNNER_ARCHITECTURES`, and
`_is_default_v2_model_runner_model()` also returns True for any dense model, so this
hits Kimi K3 and most non-MoE models.

The fix mirrors the V1 wiring: create the offloader in `__init__` before the model is
built, and call `post_init()` at the end of `load_model()`. Nothing else was missing,
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py` already calls `get_offloader().sync_prev_onload()`
and `join_after_forward()`.

The existing `test_cpu_offload` only compares outputs with and without offloading, and
not offloading produces identical outputs, so it passed vacuously on V2. Added
`test_cpu_offload_is_applied`, which asserts the offloader actually ran, parametrized
over both runners.

**Tested** on 8x A40 (sm_86), driver 560.35.03, built from source against CUDA 12.6 /
torch 2.13.0+cu129, TP=1:

- `test_cpu_offload_is_applied`: fails on `[1]` (V2, `NoopOffloader`) and passes on `[0]`
  (V1) without the patch; both pass with it.
- `tests/basic_correctness/test_cpu_offload.py::test_cpu_offload`: 4 passed. This now
  runs with real UVA offloading on V2, with and without CUDA graphs, and still matches
  the non-offloaded baseline.
- `tests/v1/streaming_input/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_streaming.py`: 2 passed.
- The patch also switches on the prefetch backend for V2, so I checked it by hand:
  `--offload-group-size 2 --offload-num-in-group 1` on V2 with CUDA graphs gives
  byte-identical greedy output to the baseline.
- `pre-commit run --files` on both touched files: all hooks pass, mypy included.

**Not verified:** Kimi K3 itself. It needs sm_90+ FP8 MegaMoE kernels and far more
memory than this box has, so the Kimi K3 part of the diagnosis is from reading
`vllm/config/vllm.py` and `vllm/models/kimi_k3/`, not from a run. Also untested here:
multi-GPU / TP / PP / EP, multimodal offload, `--cpu-offload-params`, and quantized
checkpoints (`tests/quantization/test_cpu_offload.py` needs FP8 or Marlin, which do
not run on sm_86).

The reporter's issue body was an empty template, so I could not reproduce their exact
run. I reproduced the defect its title describes. Thanks to @ee-redbull for filing it.

AI assistance was used to write this patch.

File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 951, in sample_tokens return self.model_runner.sample_tokens(grammar_output) File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 1392, in sample_tokens sampler_output, num_sampled, num_rejected = self.sample(...) File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/structured_outputs.py", line 35, in apply_grammar_bitmask bitmask = async_copy_to_gpu(...) RuntimeError: Engine core process EngineCore died unexpectedly. ``` ### Additional observations [full_error.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30848763/full_error.txt) - Reproduces on both `v0.25.0` and `v0.26.0-cu129`. - Reproduces with `thinking` enabled, with `thinking` disabled, and with `--default-chat-template-kwargs` removed entirely → the bug is in the structured-output/grammar path, not the reasoning path. - Even a bare `json_object` request (no JSON schema, no regex) crashes it. - Plain (non-structured) chat completions work fine, so this is specific to structured output. - The 4040-vs-4041 tensor shape mismatch looks like a buffer-size/layout mismatch in the grammar bitmask path ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Perf] Use the fused rotary_embedding kernel in DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding without FlashInfer
body:
## Purpose

Without FlashInfer, `DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding.forward_cuda` fell back to the eager `forward_native` decomposition — ~8 kernel launches (index, cat, chunk, rotate, mul, add) per attention layer per step. The fused in-place `ops.rotary_embedding` CUDA kernel already serves this exact pattern: the plain `RotaryEmbedding.forward_cuda` uses it, and `DeepseekV4ScalingRotaryEmbedding` wired it up (with a `rope_dim_offset` for its tail-aligned layout). YaRN scaling only changes the precomputed cos/sin cache, so the base class can call the same kernel with `rope_dim_offset=0`.

This affects DeepSeek-V2/V3-family models (and other users of `deepseek_yarn` rope: openpangu, sarvam, AXK1) on CUDA deployments where FlashInfer is unavailable — the `use_flashinfer` gate also excludes fp32 models and head sizes outside {64,128,256,512}. As a side effect the fallback now supports `key=None` (MLA q-only paths), which the eager path rejected with an assertion.

Microbenchmark, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.11, DeepSeek-V2 rope shape (`qk_rope_head_dim=64`, 16 heads, bf16, YaRN factor 40; median of 5×200 iters):

| shape | eager fallback | fused kernel | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| decode, batch 8 | 120.5 µs | 11.8 µs | 10.2× |
| decode, batch 64 | 120.7 µs | 8.0 µs | 15.1× |
| prefill, 4096 tokens | 123.4 µs | 9.3 µs | 13.3× |

Correctness on the same config:

- fp32: kernel vs native max diff < 5e-7, both neox styles.
- bf16/fp16: the kernel computes in fp32 internally, so it lands closer to the fp32 ground truth than the eager path it replaces (mean |err| 0.00186 vs 0.00218 for bf16; the two differ from each other by bf16 rounding only).
- Strided MLA-style slice inputs (`q_pe = q[..., 128:]`) verified: rope region matches, untouched `nope` region preserved.

The FlashInfer branch is unchanged and stays first preference.

Related: the V4 subclass added this wiring in #40860; #30729 added the FlashInfer branch here but left the else-branch on eager. The closed vLLM-IR ports (#39488/#41773/#42264) were a different abstraction-layer effort. No open PR touches this fallback.

## Test Plan

New test (fails before this change — the 6 `key=None` cases hit the eager path's assertion — passes after):

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/core/test_pos_encoding.py::test_deepseek_scaling_rotary_embedding_cuda_kernel
```

Full file regression:

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/core/test_pos_encoding.py
```

## Test Result

- New test: 12 passed (fp32 strict compare; bf16/fp16 vs fp32 ground truth; key=None; both neox styles).
- Full file: `397 passed` on SM120.
- pre-commit (ruff, mypy) clean.

Not verified locally: Hopper/ROCm runs (no hardware; ROCm keeps its own `forward_hip` path, untouched).

title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4 sparse prefill crashes (FlashMLA/SM90, phase1.cuh:614) on 0-token KVTransfer prefill requests
body:
## Environment
- Hardware: NVIDIA H100 (SM90), TP=4, EP on, DP=2
- vLLM version: current main at time of report
- Relevant flags:
  ```
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":236223201280,"lazy_offload":false}}'
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}'
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
  --max-num-seqs 80 --max-model-len 393216 --enable-chunked-prefill --enable-prefix-caching
  ```

## Symptom
During a mixed decode/prefill step, the worker aborts with:
```
Assertion `res == CUresult::CUDA_SUCCESS` failed (/workspace/.deps/flashmla-src/csrc/sm90/prefill/sparse/instantiations/../phase1.cuh:614):
```
The preceding CDA wrapper dump shows the output TMA descriptor was built from an empty tensor:
```
format 9 / gmem_address 0 / globalDim (512, 64, 0) / boxDim (64, 16, 1)
Error: Failed to initialize the TMA descriptor
```
i.e. `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` received `q`/`out` with `s_q == 0`.

The abort happens at `flash_mla_interface.py:217` (`sparse_prefill_fwd`), called from `_forward_prefill` in `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py` with an empty chunk:
```
chunk=[73,77) q[69:69] q_total=72 num_decodes=3 num_decode_tokens=24 num_prefill_tokens=72
```

## Root cause
1. With `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` (`kv_role="kv_both"`), a request whose KV is being reloaded from CPU is scheduled by the scheduler **with 0 tokens** for the load step (`scheduler.py` `load_kv_async` branch sets `num_new_tokens = 0`). It still occupies a request slot in the batch.
2. Such requests are prefill-phase, so they land in the batch's prefill region with `query_len == 0` (and `seq_len > 0`). In the failing step there were ~70 such requests, so `num_prefills` (≥77) far exceeds `num_prefill_tokens` (72).
3. `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadata.get_prefill_chunk_plan` does not exclude zero-query-len requests, so it can emit a chunk covering only `query_len == 0` requests → `query_start == query_end` → `_forward_prefill` slices `q[query_start:query_end]` / `out[query_start:query_end]` to an empty tensor.
4. FlashMLA's `sparse_prefill_fwd` has no `s_q > 0` guard and fails to build the output TMA descriptor for the empty tensor.

## Impact
- Any DeepSeek-V4 serving deployment using CPU/remote KV offload (disaggregated prefill or `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`) can crash during mixed decode/prefill steps, independent of workload size. It reproduces whenever several prefill-phase requests are concurrently in the `load_kv_async` state.

## Related work
- #49059 "[Bugfix][DSv4][SM120] Skip empty sparse-MLA prefill chunks" fixes the **same root cause** (an empty prefill chunk with `query_start == query_end`) for the **FlashInfer / SM120** path. This issue is the **FlashMLA / SM90** manifestation of the same bug (different backend, different error: FlashMLA TMA-descriptor assert at `phase1.cuh:614` vs FlashInfer reshape error).

## Proposed fix (summary)
- `get_prefill_chunk_plan`: skip zero-query-len prefill requests when advancing chunk boundaries so they never form their own chunk.
- `_forward_prefill`: skip chunks with `query_end <= query_start` (defensive), and return early when the chunk plan is empty.

## Observed log (failing step, all TP/EP workers)
```
(Worker_TP0_EP0) chunk=[73,77) q[69:69] q_total=72 num_decodes=3 num_decode_tokens=24 num_prefill_tokens=72
(Worker_TP6_EP6) chunk=[31,77) q[69:69] q_total=72 num_decodes=3 num_decode_tokens=24 num_prefill_tokens=72
```
`num_prefills >= 77` while `num_prefill_tokens == 72` ⇒ the prefill region contains dozens of `query_len == 0` requests (KVTransfer / CPU-offload load placeholders).

title: [Bugfix][DSv4] Skip zero-query-len prefill chunks in FlashMLA sparse prefill (complements #49059)
body:
## Why

[Fixes #51486] DeepSeek-V4 sparse prefill crashes with `Assertion res == CUresult::CUDA_SUCCESS failed (.../phase1.cuh:614)` when KVTransfer / `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` schedules prefill requests with 0 tokens while their KV is being loaded.

When such a request sits in the batch's prefill region with `query_len == 0`, `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadata.get_prefill_chunk_plan` can emit a chunk covering only zero-query-len requests, so `query_start == query_end`. `_forward_prefill` then slices `q`/`out` to an empty tensor and passes it to `flash_mla_sparse_fwd`, which fails to build the output TMA descriptor (`s_q == 0`) and aborts.

This is not a FlashMLA kernel bug — it is a missing invariant in the DeepSeek-V4 sparse-prefill chunking: it assumed every prefill-region request has ≥ 1 query token, which the scheduler (KVTransfer async load) does not guarantee.

## What

1. `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_swa.py` — `get_prefill_chunk_plan` now skips zero-query-len prefill requests when advancing chunk boundaries, so they never form their own (empty) chunk.
2. `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py` — `_forward_prefill` computes the chunk's query range before any KV gather, skips chunks with `query_end <= query_start` (defense in depth), and returns early when the plan is empty (all placeholder requests).
3. `tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py` — two unit tests covering the chunk planner with zero-query-len requests (skipped/never-empty) and the all-zero → empty-plan case.

Behavior of the existing chunk planner is unchanged when there are no zero-query requests (existing test `test_deepseek_v4_prefill_chunk_planning_expands_for_short_sequences` still passes).

## Why not duplicating an existing PR

- #49059 "[Bugfix][DSv4][SM120] Skip empty sparse-MLA prefill chunks" addresses the **same root cause** (empty prefill chunk with `query_start == query_end`) but only for the **FlashInfer / SM120** path (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py`). It does **not** touch the FlashMLA path (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py`) or the shared chunk planner (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_swa.py`).
- This PR is the **FlashMLA / SM90** complement: same `query_start == query_end` empty-chunk bug, manifesting as a FlashMLA TMA-descriptor assert at `phase1.cuh:614` instead of FlashInfer's reshape error.
- Verified with `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "..."` on 2026-08-08: no PR other than #49059 addresses this. If maintainers prefer, these two changes can be consolidated into #49059.

## Test plan

- [x] `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py -v -k "chunk_plan"` — **passed** (3 tests: the existing chunk-plan test + the 2 new ones).
- [x] pre-commit — **passed** (the `mypy` `var-annotated` error on `covered` from the first run was fixed with `covered: list[int] = []`).

## Model evaluation

This change only skips chunks that produce **zero output tokens** (placeholder requests); it does not alter the computation or output of any real prefill token, so no numerical/accuracy change is expected.

Real smoke test: served DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with the reproduction config below (the same one that previously crashed with the `phase1.cuh:614` TMA-descriptor assert) and completed mixed decode/prefill requests without the crash:

```bash
  --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --enable-prefix-caching --data-parallel-size 2 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 80 --max-model-len 393216 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":236223201280,"lazy_offload":false}}' \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 128
```

then load-tested with:

```bash
evalscope perf \
      --parallel 48 \
      --api openai \
      --min-tokens 1024 \
      --max-tokens 1024 \
      --prefix-length 0 \
      --min-prompt-length 32768 \
      --max-prompt-length 32768 \
      --number 100 \
      --tokenizer-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct \
      --name $result_name
```

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek V4 FULL_AND_PIECEWISE capture fails with CUDA error 700
body:
### Your current environment

## Description

Serving `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` with `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` fails during the first PIECEWISE CUDA Graph capture, typically at capture size 128:

```text
DeepseekV32IndexerMetadataBuilder.build
-> get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata
-> CUDA error 700: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

`FULL_DECODE_ONLY` can run.

Environment: vLLM `0.26.1rc1.dev512+g44351f81d`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu132`, 8 × H20-3e, TP=8, DeepGEMM `2.6.1`.

## Reproduction

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --max-model-len 65536 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 128 \
  --compilation-config \
  '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \
  --speculative-config \
  '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
```

Minimal DeepGEMM reproduction:

```python
import torch
from vllm.utils.deep_gemm import get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata

context_lens = torch.zeros((128, 1), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata(context_lens, block_size=64, num_sms=78)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
```

## Root cause

The PIECEWISE capture creates 128 one-token dummy requests. With `compress_ratio=4`, their compressed context lengths are all zero.

The vllm's DeepGEMM paged-MQA scheduler does not handle an all-zero workload. Its binary search can produce `q_idx == batch_size` and read `prefix_sum[batch_size]` out of bounds.

This issue has already been fixed upstream in:

- https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/353

However, the fix is absent from vLLM’s DeepGEMM commit: https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM

## Suggested fix

Update or cherrypick the DeepGEMM revision to include https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/353.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

see above

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Stream Inkling plain-text answers incrementally
body:
The follow-up @bbrowning asked for in #49876: the no-tools plain-text
streaming-latency half, split out of that PR. Rebased onto current `main` as a
single commit, and narrowed to `vllm/parser/inkling.py` plus its tests.

## Purpose

With no tools and a `reasoning_effort` of `none` or `minimal`, Inkling answers
in bare text with no `<|content_text|>` marker. Seeded into the message-header
state, that text is buffered until a closer proves it was not the optional
function name. Final content is already correct on `main`; what is left is
latency. Feeding `the answer is 42` one token at a time through `parse_delta`
on current `main` yields `['the answer is 42']`, a single final delta.

## Modification

When the prompt ends in `<|message_model|>` at those efforts and declares no
tools, `adjust_initial_state_from_prompt` starts in `CONTENT` instead of
`MESSAGE_HEADER`, so the text streams as it arrives.

"Declares no tools" is read from the prompt token ids rather than from
`request.tools`. The Inkling renderer emits every tool source (request tools,
`chat_template_kwargs["tools"]`, developer-message tools) as one
`<|content_xml|>` block (`vllm/renderers/inkling_encoding.py`), so its absence
proves no function name can follow. This keeps the change inside the model's
parser file, with no serving or renderer plumbing, and it covers every caller
that seeds the parser from the prompt. If the marker cannot be resolved in the
vocab, message-header parsing is kept, which is today's behaviour.

Only the named `none` / `minimal` efforts are handled; the numeric forms are
left alone.

Compared with the previous revision of this PR, this drops
`prompt_declares_tools`, the `_vllm_prompt_has_tools` kwarg, the
`chat_completion/serving.py` changes, the `Parser.__init__` typing change, and
the `inkling_config(plain_text_mode=...)` transition rewrite.

## Duplicate check

No other open PR addresses Inkling plain-text streaming latency
(`gh pr list --state open --search inkling`). #52392 makes message-level tools
visible downstream of the renderer; this change does not depend on it, since it
reads the rendered prompt.

## Test Plan

`TestPlainTextStreaming` in `tests/parser/engine/test_inkling.py`:

- `test_bare_text_streams_incrementally`: no tools, `reasoning_effort` of
  `none` and `minimal`, bare text fed one token per `parse_delta` call, with
  both an explicit `<|end_message|>` and EOS without a closer. Asserts one
  content delta per token, not only the concatenation.
- `test_otherwise_keeps_message_header_parsing`: a prompt that declares tools
  (at `none` and `minimal`), and a no-tools prompt at `low`, keep
  message-header parsing, so the function name stays hidden.

```
pytest -q tests/parser/engine \
  tests/reasoning/test_deepseekv3_reasoning_parser.py \
  tests/reasoning/test_gemma4_reasoning_parser.py \
  tests/reasoning/test_glm4_moe_reasoning_parser.py \
  tests/reasoning/test_minimax_m2_reasoning_parser.py \
  tests/reasoning/test_qwen3_reasoning_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_gemma4_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_minimax_m2_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_qwen3coder_tool_parser.py \
  tests/renderers/test_inkling.py
```

## Test Result

- The four incrementality cases fail on `main` with `['the answer is 42']` and
  pass here.
- With tool detection forced off, the two tools-declared cases fail, so they
  guard the leak.
- Checked separately that `render_inkling_messages` emits `<|content_xml|>` for
  request tools and developer-message tools, and not for a tool-free prompt.
- The selection above: **6239 passed**.
- pre-commit (ruff, mypy 3.11, typos, test tethering) passes.

No live model evaluation was run: this is a parser-level change verified with
deterministic CPU-only tests, and an Inkling model was not available here.

## AI assistance

The human submitter selected the issue, controlled the scope, reviewed the
root cause and implementation, reviewed every changed line, and approved
publication. AI-assisted tooling supported implementation, test authoring and
validation.

title: MooncakeConnector P/D: NVLink fallback transfer fails "Requested address not found" (fp8 MLA, v0.25.0)
body:
### Summary

Same-node P/D disaggregation of DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with the MooncakeConnector fails at the first KV transfer on `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.0`, on an 8x B200 SXM node, in every configuration tested; each transport fails differently, and none fails at startup.

The primary case: when the engine containers are launched without `--device=/dev/infiniband` (no RDMA devices visible in-container; the host's IB ports are ACTIVE), mooncake falls back to its NVLink transport, and the fallback is only visible in mooncake's own logs: the vLLM connector layer reports `The Mooncake Transfer Engine is using rdma as its protocol`, while mooncake-transfer-engine logs `No RDMA devices found` and selects `cross-node NVLink transport (MC_FORCE_MNNVL or no HCA detected)`. Both vLLM processes initialize and accept the routed request, prefill executes, and the transfer then fails: every producer TP worker's transfer-engine thread logs `nvlink_transport.cpp:497 Requested address 0x... not found`, the consumer's pull returns -1, and with `kv_load_failure_policy: fail` the request dies and the proxy stream hangs.

With the RDMA devices mapped in (variant 6), mooncake selects the rdma path (`Device mlx5_0 port 1 is available`) and the transfer fails differently: every slice reports `worker_pool.cpp:307 ... transport retry counter exceeded` (zero successful transfers; not root-caused, and consistent with same-host IB loopback not being routable on this fabric, so this leg may be environmental). After the failed pulls, the decode engine process exited on its own, which reads as a robustness gap: `kv_load_failure_policy: fail` is documented to fail the request, not the engine. The tcp protocol fails at engine init (not root-caused; see matrix). Net: no tested Mooncake P/D configuration produced a working transfer on this node, and no failing configuration was rejected at startup.

The image carries PR #46807's MLA support for this model (merge commit `0feca7f`, included in v0.25.0), and PR #39548 previously fixed NVLink transfers for this same connector-plus-MNNVL-transport combination, so this path is intended to work. The failing span is 8,640 bytes, equal to the `layer_spec.page_size_bytes` value described for this model in PR #46807, which suggests a possible interaction with the packed MLA registration on this path; controls that would separate a layout-specific failure from a general NVLink registration failure on this node (different block size, non-MLA model, standalone transfer bench) have not been run. Filing here because the integration contract is the question: does the connector hand the NVLink transport a layout it cannot support, or does the transport mis-register it? Happy to cross-file in [kvcache-ai/Mooncake](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake) if triage believes the root cause is in the transport layer.

### Expected behavior

1. If the NVLink fallback and this same-node topology are supported for MLA models: the address-resolution failure (variant 1/5) is the bug to investigate.
2. If a container without RDMA device access, or this topology, is outside the supported envelope: reject the configuration at startup with a clear error. The fallback is already logged inside mooncake; today the stack comes up, accepts traffic, and fails on the first transfer with a hung stream.
3. Separately, the decode engine exiting after failed pulls in variant 6 looks like a robustness gap regardless of transport: `kv_load_failure_policy: fail` is documented to fail the request, not the engine.

### Environment

| Axis | Value |
|---|---|
| Hardware | 8x B200 SXM (Nebius, single node), driver 580.173.02, CUDA 13.0; `nvidia-smi topo -m`: NV18 full mesh across all 8 GPUs; 4x mlx5 HCAs (PIX to each other, SYS to all GPUs), IB ports ACTIVE at 100 Gb/s (2X HDR) on the host, IPoIB netdevs down |
| Image | `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.0`, digest `sha256:e1c1ff1af9a15921bfa11d1d95047258c1797392cdbfa296e7639da446b23f97`, vLLM build `dd10e03f95f94edbea1975c67ace3a35ec9a8a40` |
| Mooncake | `mooncake-transfer-engine 0.3.10.post2` (bundled in the image) |
| Model | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, snapshot `7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062` |
| KV config | `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` (fp8_ds_mla), `--block-size 256`, hybrid KV cache manager on, fp4 indexer cache on |
| P/D placement | P: TP4 on GPUs 0-3, `kv_producer`; D: TP4 on GPUs 4-7, `kv_consumer`; toy proxy `examples/disaggregated/mooncake_connector/mooncake_connector_proxy.py`; engine containers `--ipc=host --network=host`, launched WITHOUT `--device=/dev/infiniband` in variants 1-5 and WITH it in variant 6 |

Monolithic TP8 and DP8 launches of the same model on the same node, image, and weights serve 1M-token requests cleanly, so the node, image, and model recipe are healthy on the monolithic paths; the disagg transfer path has no independent baseline on this node (see Not tested).

<details>
<summary>Launch commands (producer, consumer, proxy)</summary>

Producer (consumer is identical except `--gpus '"device=4,5,6,7"'`, `--port 8020`, and `"kv_role":"kv_consumer"`):

```bash
docker run -d --name v4flash0731-prefill --gpus '"device=0,1,2,3"' \
  --ipc=host --network=host --shm-size 32g --ulimit nofile=1048576:1048576 \
  -e VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT=8998 \
  -v /data/hf-cache:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.0 \
  /root/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--deepseek-ai--DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/snapshots/7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4-flash-0731 --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --attention_config.use_fp4_indexer_cache=True \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log \
  --port 8010 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_buffer_device":"cuda","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma"},"kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}'
```

Proxy (note `--entrypoint python3`; the image ENTRYPOINT is the vLLM CLI, which otherwise consumes the script path as a model argument):

```bash
docker run -d --name v4flash0731-proxy --network=host \
  --entrypoint python3 \
  -v /data/bin/mooncake_connector_proxy.py:/root/mooncake_connector_proxy.py \
  vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.0 \
  /root/mooncake_connector_proxy.py \
  --prefill http://0.0.0.0:8010 8998 --decode http://0.0.0.0:8020 --port 8000
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Verbatim log excerpt (transport selection at init, then first-transfer failure)</summary>

Primary-case logs below are from variant 5 (same-container colocation); variant 1's failure signature is identical. The final excerpt is from variant 6.

Init (consumer side shown; producer identical). vLLM's connector believes it is on rdma; mooncake detects no RDMA devices and selects the NVLink transport:

```text
(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=2342) INFO 08-08 19:29:44 [mooncake_connector.py:934] The Mooncake Transfer Engine is using rdma as its protocol.
W0808 19:29:44.334410  2342 topology.cpp:156] No RDMA devices found, check your device installation
I0808 19:29:44.334455  2342 transfer_engine_impl.cpp:301] Using cross-node NVLink transport (MC_FORCE_MNNVL or no HCA detected)
W0808 19:29:44.490669  2186 nvlink_transport.cpp:347] Memory region 0x71036a000000 is not allocated by cuMemCreate, but it can be used as local buffer
```

First request (2K-token smoke), producer side (all four TP workers emit the same pair; TP0 shown):

```text
E0808 19:34:55.902447 19738 nvlink_transport.cpp:497] Requested address 0x7fc3ea0fdd40 to 0x7fc3ea0fff00 not found!
(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=2184) WARNING 08-08 19:34:55 [mooncake_connector.py:1643] Sending to <consumer-ip>:15653 failed (ret=-1) after 0.001339847000053851 (1029 descriptors, 27478080 bytes)
```

Consumer side:

```text
(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=2342) ERROR 08-08 19:34:55 [mooncake_connector.py:1899] pulling kv_caches for ['chatcmpl-e7e14ef6-...-b4574823'] failed: Mooncake transfer engine returned -1
```

Variant 6 (RDMA devices mapped): mooncake stays on rdma at init, then the transfer fails at the transport level (producer side; representative slices):

```text
I0808 20:51:20.334829  1121 topology.cpp:124] Device mlx5_0 port 1 is available
E0808 20:57:16.498456  3892 worker_pool.cpp:307] Worker: Process failed for slice (opcode: 1, source_addr: 0x7a610a3f7500, length: 8640, dest_addr: 0x79b48a3f7500, local_nic: mlx5_1, peer_nic: <consumer-ip>:16504@mlx5_2, dest_rkey: 2213058, retry_cnt: 0): transport retry counter exceeded
(APIServer pid=1) INFO 08-08 20:57:18 [metrics.py:103] KV Transfer metrics: Num successful transfers=0, ... Num failed transfers=4, ...
```

</details>

### Observed

- Both P/D engines initialize; Mooncake registers KV regions (`use_mla: True`), the bootstrap on :8998 answers `/query`, the proxy routes the request, prefill executes.
- On the first transfer, all four producer TP workers report `Sending ... failed (ret=-1)` for 1,029 descriptors / 27,478,080 bytes each; the logged failing span `0x...fdd40` to `0x...fff00` is 0x21c0 = 8,640 bytes, equal to the `layer_spec.page_size_bytes` value described for this model in PR #46807. The descriptor population mixes span sizes (27,478,080 / 1,029 is not a multiple of 8,640); a per-descriptor breakdown was not captured.
- All four consumer TP workers report `pulling kv_caches ... failed: Mooncake transfer engine returned -1`; `kv_load_failure_policy: fail` kills the request and the proxy stream hangs.
- Reproduction count: one clean-start run per variant, with the primary failure hitting the first transfer attempted in each of variants 1 and 5.

### Failure matrix (same node, same image, all variants)

| # | Variant | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `"mooncake_protocol": "rdma"`, two containers (P: GPUs 0-3, D: GPUs 4-7) | Engines healthy; transfer fails: `nvlink_transport.cpp:497` address not found |
| 2 | `"mooncake_protocol": "tcp"` | `TransferEngine.initialize` fails at engine boot (`RuntimeError: Mooncake Transfer Engine initialization failed`); engines never start. Not root-caused; included for completeness |
| 3 | `MC_INTRANODE_NVLINK=0` (standalone/scratch `TransferEngine.initialize` probe, not a full P/D launch) | Init returns -1: "Unsupported transport nvlink_intra, please rebuild Mooncake"; the toggle is unavailable on the bundled build. `nvlink_intra` appears to be a distinct Mooncake transport from the cross-node NVLink/MNNVL one selected in variant 1 |
| 4 | rdma + `MC_USE_NVLINK_IPC=0` | Init OK; transfer fails differently: `cudaIpcOpenMemHandle failed: invalid argument` (nvlink_transport.cpp:421) |
| 5 | Same-container colocation (one container, `--gpus all`, two `vllm serve` processes on CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES 0-3 / 4-7) | **Identical** failure to #1; a separate Docker container/IPC namespace is not required to reproduce |
| 6 | rdma + `--device=/dev/infiniband` mapped into both engine containers | Mooncake selects the rdma path (`Device mlx5_0 port 1 is available`, no fallback); every transfer slice fails `worker_pool.cpp:307 ... transport retry counter exceeded` (KV Transfer metrics: 0 successful, 4 failed); the decode engine process then exited on its own. Not root-caused; possibly environmental (same-host IB loopback routability) |

Both engine containers run `--ipc=host` (the proxy container does not; it holds no GPU memory). Variant 5's identical in-container failure shows the primary error is not an IPC-namespace artifact; variant 4's distinct `cudaIpcOpenMemHandle` error may be environment-sensitive and I would not lean on it.

### Localization

- Transport selection is evidenced at init: `No RDMA devices found` followed by `Using cross-node NVLink transport (MC_FORCE_MNNVL or no HCA detected)`, while the vLLM connector layer reports rdma. The failure is downstream of a fallback the connector layer does not surface.
- The producer-side prefill, bootstrap handshake, and request routing all succeed; the failure is isolated to the KV block transfer.
- Variant 5 shows a separate container/IPC namespace is not required to reproduce; variant 3 shows the `nvlink_intra` toggle is unavailable as a workaround on the bundled build; variant 4 changes but does not fix the failure.
- The 8,640-byte failing span equals the packed MLA block payload that PR #46807's layout handling addresses on the RDMA registration path. This is consistent with, but does not prove, a layout-specific registration or resolution failure on the NVLink path; the discriminating controls (different block size, non-MLA model, standalone transfer bench) have not been run. I have not verified the registration code paths at source.
- Variant 6 shows the rdma path also fails on this node, with a different, transport-level signature that is not root-caused and may be environmental. It does not isolate the NVLink finding, but it removes "map the RDMA devices in" as a known workaround here, and it produced the engine-exit robustness observation.

### Scope

- Tested: the six variants above; monolithic TP8/DP8 baselines on the same node (healthy); 2K-token smoke as the failing transfer (the failure precedes any long-context work).
- Not tested: cross-node RDMA between two hosts (variant 6 exercised only same-host IB loopback, and its failure is not root-caused); a newer or nightly mooncake-transfer-engine wheel; `kv_buffer_device: cpu` staging; a different `--block-size` (to confirm the failing span tracks the per-block MLA payload); standalone mooncake `transfer_engine_bench` on this node (would isolate transport vs. KV-layout registration for both the NVLink and rdma legs); non-MLA models over the same NVLink fallback.

Closest prior reports found: #39548 fixed a thread-local CUDA context bug in the connector's NVLink `_send_blocks` path (so NVLink transfer is an intended connector path, not an unsupported mode), and kvcache-ai/Mooncake#546 addressed missing receiver-side address validation. Neither covers address resolution failing on this packed MLA layout.

### Potential next checks

- Whether the NVLink/MNNVL transport path is expected to support the packed fp8 MLA layout at all on mooncake-transfer-engine 0.3.10.post2. If not, failing fast at startup (the fallback is already logged) would save users the diagnosis; today the stack comes up, accepts traffic, and fails on the first request.
- Whether same-node P/D over the rdma protocol (variant 6) is expected to work when both engines sit on one host's HCAs, or whether the `transport retry counter exceeded` leg is a fabric/environment issue on our side.
- Rerun with a newer mooncake-transfer-engine wheel or vLLM nightly. I can run specific variants on this hardware if useful.

Available on request: full engine logs for producer/consumer/proxy across all six variants, the exact 2K-token smoke request payload, and pip freeze from the image. Reporter context: independent benchmarking on Nebius B200 hardware (prior same-node results for this model in #51454).
