title: [Bugfix] Raise ValueError instead of bare assert for expert-parallel divisibility check
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52435.

`DeepseekV4MoE._init_mega_moe_experts` / `_init_fused_moe_experts` used a bare
`assert n_physical_experts % ep_size == 0` (and the `tp_size` equivalent) to
validate that the physical expert count divides evenly across the
expert/tensor-parallel size. This crashes every worker process with an
unhandled `AssertionError` when serving DeepSeek V4 with
`--enable-expert-parallel` and a routed-expert / redundant-expert
configuration that isn't evenly divisible by the parallel size (e.g. 256
experts, `ep_size=3`, `num_redundant_experts=0`).

This PR converts both checks to `if ...: raise ValueError(...)`, preserving
the exact same message, so the check (a) isn't stripped under `python -O`
and (b) surfaces as `ValueError`, matching the validation convention already
used elsewhere in this class for user-facing config errors.

Also wires the new regression test into the CPU-only
"Basic Models Test (Other CPU)" Buildkite job so it actually runs in CI.

## Test Plan

```
pytest -v tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_expert_divisibility.py
```

Two new CPU-only unit tests construct `DeepseekV4MoE` directly (mocking the
expert-parallel group, mirroring the existing pattern in
`test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py`) and assert `ValueError` is raised for both
the mega-MoE and fused-MoE init paths when experts aren't evenly divisible.
No GPU/distributed process group needed.

## Test Result

```
tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_expert_divisibility.py::test_mega_moe_experts_raises_value_error_when_not_divisible_by_ep_size PASSED
tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_expert_divisibility.py::test_fused_moe_experts_raises_value_error_when_not_divisible_by_tp_size PASSED
2 passed
```

`ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on all changed files.

---

## AI assistance disclosure

Per [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/AGENTS.md):

- **AI assistance was used** to help write this change and its regression test. The commits carry a
  `Co-authored-by:` trailer accordingly.
- **Not a duplicate.** Checked before opening via
  `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "52435 in:body"` and a search for
  `n_physical_experts` — no other open PR addresses this.
- **Tests run:** `pytest -v tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_expert_divisibility.py` → 2 passed;
  `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on all changed files. Results in the Test Result
  section above.
- **Model evaluation:** not applicable — this changes only the exception *type* raised by an
  existing config-validation guard on a startup path. It cannot affect model output, accuracy, or
  serving behavior; the condition and message text are unchanged.
- **Human accountability:** I have reviewed every changed line and understand and stand behind the
  change end-to-end.

### Scope note

To be explicit about what this does and does not fix: this does **not** make
`--tensor-parallel-size 3` work for DeepSeek V4. That configuration is independently blocked by the
attention-head check (`total_num_attention_heads=64` is not divisible by 3, and
`ModelConfig.get_num_attention_heads` divides evenly with no padding), which is architectural and
out of scope here.

What it fixes is the guard itself: a bare `assert` is stripped under `python -O`, so in an optimized
deployment this check silently disappears and the invalid configuration proceeds into incorrect
expert-index arithmetic instead of failing fast. Converting it to `raise ValueError` makes the guard
unconditional and matches the validation convention already used for user-facing config errors
elsewhere in this class.

title: [Feature]: Support NVFP4 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with FP4 KV cache + DSpark speculative decoding on SM121 (DGX Spark)
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Summary

Requesting first-class support for serving **NVFP4** DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 checkpoints (e.g. `Rarri/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-NVFP4`) with **FP4 KV cache** (`nvfp4` / `nvfp4_ds_mla`) **and DSpark speculative decoding** on SM121 (NVIDIA GB10 / DGX Spark, 2-node TP=2).

Today this combination does not work on vLLM main. We currently run it on a fork of jasl's branch (PR #41834) which serves the NVFP4 checkpoint but **cannot** do DSpark speculative decoding with it (draft loader fails with `KeyError: 'layers.0.ffn.experts.routed_experts.w13_input_scale'`). vLLM main v0.27.1 fails earlier at startup on SM121 with the DeepGEMM "Unknown SF transformation" error (see #51884).

## Environment

- **Hardware**: 2× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10), compute capability 12.1 / SM121, Linux ARM64, two-node TP=2
- **Model (NVFP4)**: `Rarri/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-NVFP4`
  - ModelOpt mixed-precision conversion: `producer: dsv4-nvfp4-experts-mtp-fallback`
  - `quant_method: fp8`, `quant_algo: MIXED_PRECISION`, `moe_quant_algo: NVFP4`, `group_size: 16`, `format: e4m3`
- **Model (FP8)**: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`
- **vLLM versions tested**:
  - v0.27.0 / v0.27.1 (main) — fails at startup on SM121 (DeepGEMM "Unknown SF transformation")
  - jasl fork branch `codex/ds4-sm120-min-enable` (PR #41834), image `vllm-jasl-41834:latest` — serves NVFP4 but no DSpark
- **KV cache dtypes**: `fp8`, `fp8_ds_mla`, `nvfp4`, `nvfp4_ds_mla`
- **Speculative decoding**: DSpark, 5 speculative tokens, `--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'`
- **Serving config**: `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`, `--block-size 256`, `MTP_NUM_TOKENS=5`, `MAX_MODEL_LEN=131072`, `MAX_NUM_SEQS=4`

## What we want

1. Serve the **NVFP4** DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 checkpoint on SM121 with **FP4 KV cache** (`nvfp4` / `nvfp4_ds_mla`).
2. Enable **DSpark speculative decoding** on top of that NVFP4 target (MTP draft), without the draft loader failing on missing NVFP4 scale tensors.
3. Have the DSpark draft built under its **own model/quant config** so an NVFP4 target does not corrupt the MXFP4 draft experts (see abandoned PR #49133).

## What fails today

### On vLLM main (v0.27.1, official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1-aarch64-cu129`)

Startup fails on SM121 with the DeepGEMM scale-layout error:

```
RuntimeError: Assertion error (/workspace/.deps/deepgemm-src/csrc/apis/layout.hpp:60): Unknown SF transformation
```

This is the same class of failure as #51884 / #51758 (DeepGEMM SM120/121 regression). Full report: #51884.

### On jasl's fork (PR #41834) — NVFP4 serves, but DSpark fails

The NVFP4 checkpoint loads and serves, but enabling DSpark fails during draft weight loading:

```
KeyError: 'layers.0.ffn.experts.routed_experts.w13_input_scale'
```

The draft loader expects a scale tensor that is absent from the NVFP4 draft params, so speculative decoding cannot be enabled for the NVFP4 target.

## Related issues / PRs

- **#51884** — DeepGEMM "Unknown SF transformation" on SM120/121 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash FP8 + DSpark (blocker on main)
- **#51758** — v0.26→v0.27 DeepSeek-V4-Flash load regression (DeepGEMM SM120)
- **#50720** — DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 + DSpark fails on SM120 (FlashInfer sparse MLA topk=256 dispatch)
- **#49133** (PR, closed/abandoned) — "DSpark: build draft under its own model/quant config (NVFP4 target corrupts MXFP4 draft experts)". Closed by author with note: *"we have nvfp4 drafter for dsv4-nvfp4 now"* — but that drafter does not work for this checkpoint on SM121.
- **#51835** (PR, open) — "Restore DeepSeek-V4 DSpark draft quantization" (restores `deepseek_v4_fp8` for the draft)
- **#41834** (PR) — "Add SM12x support for DeepSeek V4 Flash with essential fixes" (jasl's branch we currently run)
- **jasl/vllm#43** — our original issue on jasl's fork for this exact scenario

## Request

Please add/validate end-to-end support for **NVFP4 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 + FP4 KV cache + DSpark speculative decoding** on SM121, including:

- Making the DSpark draft loader work with NVFP4 targets (missing `w13_input_scale` / NVFP4 scale tensors).
- Building the DSpark draft under its own model/quant config (revive #49133) so NVFP4 targets don't corrupt MXFP4 draft experts.
- Confirming the `nvfp4` / `nvfp4_ds_mla` KV cache path works with DSpark on SM121.

Happy to test any branch / provide logs.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4-Flash think-until-cap / empty turn under concurrent DSpark + breakable CUDA graphs
body:
## Summary

On **DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731** with the official DSpark recipe, concurrent `/v1/chat/completions` requests (same greedy tool-calling turn) intermittently **never leave the reasoning channel**. Generation runs to `max_tokens` with:

- `finish_reason: "length"`
- empty `message.content`
- **no** `tool_calls`
- `reasoning_content` is a tight loop (never emits a think-end token), repeating e.g.  
  `Wait, the user wants to upgrade XEHM4B to business, then cancel it.`

This is a **real decode loop**, not only a parser mis-bucket. Healthy replies on the same prompt are short tool-calls (~181 tokens). Failed replies burn the full cap (`max_tokens=16384` in the numbers below).

The high-rate failure needs **all three**:

1. **DSpark** speculative decoding
2. **Breakable CUDA graphs** (this nightly auto-enables `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`)
3. **In-flight concurrency ≥ 10**

`--enforce-eager` does **not** reproduce. The same prompt at the same concurrency is **0/1024** on SGLang (DSPARK) and TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc23 / 1.3.0rc25 (DSpark).

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|------|--------|
| Image | `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-acb0f1dcdb668d90bbbf50e57552d2f6f0987c87` |
| Digest | `sha256:6b084be85c1806afcb69df24d853ebf240b9f0dfca3eaa2252d0096a46a12c58` |
| Version | `0.27.2rc1.dev110+gacb0f1dcd` |
| Hardware | 2× NVIDIA B200, TP=2 + expert parallel |
| Model | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` |
| HF snapshot | `7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062` |
| Startup log | `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` auto-enabled; `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`; separate DSpark CUDA-graph capture |

Hub image `ENTRYPOINT` is `["vllm","serve"]`.

## Serve command (repro / default recipe)

Flags follow [recipes.vllm.ai DeepSeek-V4-Flash](https://recipes.vllm.ai/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash), adapted to TP2.

```bash
# SNAP = local HF snapshot of deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731
#         (7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062)

docker run --gpus '"device=0,1"' --network=host --ipc=host --shm-size=32g \
  -v "$HF_HOME:$HF_HOME" -e HF_HOME -e PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
  vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-acb0f1dcdb668d90bbbf50e57552d2f6f0987c87 \
  "$SNAP" \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}' \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-model-len 70000 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune
```

## Payload + curl

Multi-turn airline tool-calling conversation (tau2-style): system policy, prior `get_reservation_details` / `get_flight_status` / `get_user_details` results, last user turn:

> Upgrade XEHM4B to business first, then cancel it. Use the card ending in 2135. Also, do I have any other upcoming flights? What’s the total cost of those?

Full body: **17 messages, 14 tools**, `temperature: 0`. Gist: **https://gist.github.com/dsingal0/8973a0fb9166beb38e6aaf1fb1df20e9**

```bash
# force the length-cap path
curl -sS -L -o payload.json https://gist.githubusercontent.com/dsingal0/8973a0fb9166beb38e6aaf1fb1df20e9/raw/deepseek_v4_flash_airline_toolcall.json
jq '.max_tokens=16384 | .temperature=0' payload.json > /tmp/req.json

# single request
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @/tmp/req.json | jq '{
    finish: .choices[0].finish_reason,
    content: .choices[0].message.content,
    n_tools: (.choices[0].message.tool_calls|length),
    reasoning_len: (.choices[0].message.reasoning_content|length),
    completion: .usage.completion_tokens
  }'
```

**Hit** = `finish_reason=="length"` AND empty/whitespace `content` AND no `tool_calls`.  
**Healthy** = `finish_reason=="tool_calls"`, ~181 completion tokens.

A hit’s `reasoning_content` never contains a think-end token; it loops the upgrade/cancel sentence until the cap.

Concurrent repro (need **≥ 10** in flight; **32** is reliable). Fire N identical POSTs, then repeat sequential waves:

```bash
# example: 8 sequential waves of 32 in-flight
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions"
payload = json.load(open("/tmp/req.json"))
payload["max_tokens"] = 16384
payload["temperature"] = 0

def one(i):
    t0 = time.time()
    req = Request(url, data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
                  headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST")
    body = json.loads(urlopen(req, timeout=7200).read())
    ch = (body.get("choices") or [{}])[0]
    msg = ch.get("message") or {}
    content = (msg.get("content") or "").strip()
    tools = msg.get("tool_calls") or []
    finish = ch.get("finish_reason")
    hit = finish == "length" and not content and not tools
    return {"i": i, "finish": finish, "hit": hit,
            "n_tools": len(tools), "sec": round(time.time() - t0, 2),
            "completion": (body.get("usage") or {}).get("completion_tokens")}

for wave in range(8):
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=32) as ex:
        rows = [f.result() for f in as_completed(ex.submit(one, i) for i in range(32))]
    hits = sum(1 for r in rows if r["hit"])
    print(f"wave {wave}: {hits}/32 hits")
PY
```

## Conditions required

| Condition | Needed for high-rate repro? |
|-----------|-----------------------------|
| Greedy (`temperature=0`) | Yes (all numbers below) |
| Tools + this multi-turn prompt | Yes |
| `max_tokens` large enough (4096 often misses; **16384** used) | Yes |
| In-flight concurrency **≥ 10** | Yes |
| DSpark `num_speculative_tokens: 7`, greedy draft | Yes for ~30% rate |
| Breakable CUDA graphs (default on this nightly) | Yes for ~30% rate |
| Prefix caching | On in all runs (not ablated) |
| `--enforce-eager` | **Suppresses** the bug |
| `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` | **Almost suppresses** |

Serial (`c=1`) after a polluted server: rare (1/16). Cold start + high concurrency: the first ~256 requests can be clean, then the rate climbs.

## Observed frequencies

Same image, same weights, same payload, `max_tokens=16384`, `temperature=0`.

**Default recipe (DSpark + breakable graphs), 64 in-flight, 1024 requests: 298 / 1024 (29.1%)**  
`finish`: 697 `tool_calls`, 309 `length`, 18 `stop`. All 298 hits used the full 16384 tokens.  
By 64-id bucket: first 256 requests **0%**, then 23% → **67%** on the last bucket.

**Default recipe, sequential waves of 32 (already-warm server), 256 req: 103 / 256 (40%)**

| Wave | Hits | Local slots that hit |
|------|------|----------------------|
| 0–3 | **6/32 each (18.75%)** | **always 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31** |
| 4 | 11/32 | spreading downward |
| 5–7 | 21–24/32 (66–75%) | high slots dominate |

**Concurrency threshold** (3 waves each, polluted default server):

| In-flight | Hits | Rate |
|-----------|------|------|
| 4 | 0/12 | 0% |
| 7 | 0/21 | 0% |
| 8 | 0/32 | 0% |
| 9 | 0/27 | 0% |
| **10** | **4/30** | **~13%** (first consistent hits) |
| 12 | 9/36 | 25% |
| 16 | 21/48 | 44% |
| 24 | 49/72 | 68% |
| 26 | 55/78 | 71% |
| 28 | 61/84 | 73% |
| 32 | 103/256 | 40% (escalating across waves) |

**Ablations** (same prompt/cap; 8×32 waves = 256 unless noted):

| Setup | Hits | Rate |
|-------|------|------|
| DSpark + breakable graphs (**default**) | 298/1024 | **29.1%** |
| DSpark + `--enforce-eager` (`cudagraph_mode=NONE`) | **0/256** | **0%** |
| DSpark + `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` | 2/256 | 0.8% |
| **No** `--speculative-config` (graphs still on) | 10/512 | 2.0% |
| SGLang nightly + DSPARK, same payload, 64 in-flight | 0/1024 | 0% |
| TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc25 + DSpark, same payload | 0/1024 | 0% |
| TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc23 + DSpark, same payload | 0/1024 | 0% |

DSpark without breakable graphs ≈ 0–2%; graphs without DSpark ≈ 2%; **both + c≥10 ≈ 30% and climbing**. The last-6-of-32 slot pattern on early waves is deterministic enough that this is unlikely to be sampling noise (`temperature=0`).

## Notes

- `ParserEngine.adjust_initial_state_from_prompt` is a no-op in this build. Empty `content` here is because generation never leaves reasoning, not only a CONTENT↔REASONING flip.
- Think-parser `initial_state` issues (e.g. #51296) can also empty `content` when think-end is missing; they do **not** explain the 16k self-loop or the CUDA-graph / batch-index dependence.
- Workarounds that held here: `--enforce-eager`, or `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`, or keep concurrency ≤ 9. Eager is the only config that was **0/256**.

## Expected

The same greedy prompt should keep producing the ~181-token tool-call path at c=32, as SGLang and TensorRT-LLM do, and as vLLM does under `--enforce-eager`.

title: [Bugfix][Structured Output][Spec Decode] Validate accepted blocks before commit
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #43338.

Structured-output requests using speculative decoding must satisfy this commit
invariant:

> Request history and grammar state advance through the same longest
> grammar-valid token prefix. Any rejected suffix remains schedulable for
> resampling.

At `main@4666a8ba9ed5d271bf751cf1384cab2d2dcc0cfa`, the scheduler appends the
verifier's accepted token block to request history before
`StructuredOutputGrammar.accept_tokens()` checks the block. Prospective grammar
masks reduce the chance of an invalid token, but they cannot establish the
commit invariant when one accepted block crosses either of these state
transitions:

1. deferred grammar activation at the end of model reasoning;
2. grammar termination before the final accepted token in the block.

The invalid suffix is therefore already visible in request state when
`accept_tokens()` rejects it. Depending on the serving path, that produces an
invalid structured response or terminates the request with `FINISHED_ERROR`.

This PR validates accepted multi-token structured-output blocks before
`Scheduler._update_request_with_output()` mutates request history. It uses the
non-advancing `StructuredOutputGrammar.validate_tokens()` interface, commits
only the valid prefix, and leaves the existing post-commit path as the sole
grammar-state advancement operation.

### Resulting behavior

- Reasoning content through a deferred end marker remains unconstrained.
- Tokens after the marker must form a valid grammar prefix.
- Blocks sampled after reasoning has ended are validated in full, including
  suffixes that follow grammar termination.
- Rejected suffix tokens decrement `num_computed_tokens` and asynchronous
  output placeholders so they can be sampled again.
- Speculative metrics count only committed draft tokens. Rejecting only the
  target-sampled tail does not reduce the accepted-draft count.
- Unstructured requests, stale outputs, non-speculative output, and
  single-token output blocks retain their existing fast paths.

Reasoning-boundary detection exposes prior request tokens through a read-only
concatenated `Sequence`; it does not copy the committed history. A block that
does not contain a boundary requires one parser call. A block that contains a
boundary is scanned through cumulative delta prefixes, which supports
single-token markers, multi-token markers, and markers split across scheduler
steps. Each detection call uses an isolated copy of the request-scoped parser,
so a stateful parser cannot consume its transition before the standard
post-commit path observes it.

## Provenance and related work

The state boundary is produced by the composition of two supported features,
not by a single isolated regression:

- #14702, merge commit
  `34120f5acd693924cc783dfaa33733afbe9ae8b0`, enabled structured output with
  speculative decoding and introduced per-position grammar-mask simulation.
- #16577, merge commit
  `2fc9075b82e05007f460992b3f9d42d2746c41cb`, deferred structured-output
  grammar activation while a request is reasoning.

Several changes cover narrower parts of the lifecycle:

- #36138, head commit
  `94f4dc2e98d63dc1a3ff7cca2b35a9235df667e1`, detects reasoning activation
  inside a speculative window but does not establish pre-commit validation.
- #44297, merge commit
  `e7c9df944969c251bdceed7b9d7bbcc7fec3639b`, constrains scheduled rows after
  a reasoning boundary, including the bonus row. It operates prospectively on
  scheduled draft candidates, not on the authoritative verifier result.
- #44993, merge commit
  `0416dab275d51327b331a1c6baaec754a68d7764`, advances grammar state across an
  accepted reasoning boundary. The accepted block is still appended before
  grammar acceptance.
- #45560, merge commit
  `dc818c198d3ff50a16f38eba567da006478239c8`, constrains GPT-OSS through a
  Harmony structural-tag grammar active from token zero. It is specific to the
  GPT-OSS path and does not cover deferred reasoning parsers or grammar
  termination for other models.
- #43424, commit
  `4e96809853442f1cf9dacf83f166fc32482b6632`, supplies the pre-commit design
  used for the reasoning-boundary case. This PR credits its author and extends
  the contract to every accepted structured speculative block, avoids copying
  committed history, isolates stateful reasoning probes, updates speculative
  metrics, and covers grammar termination. A boundary-only build still fails
  the qualified runtime test.
- #51870, commit
  `c3573d92f69cda2d42d3e74f80f00d0e932e5010`, replaces a mutating operation
  during draft-window mask simulation. It intentionally does not alter accepted
  output or scheduler accounting.
- #48200, commit
  `21265a9a4841812b5088cb062fc5356abcb979d9`, refactors structured-output
  management. Its scheduler still appends `new_token_ids` before accepting them
  into the grammar, so the commit invariant remains separate from that
  refactor.

The scope difference from #43424 is also recorded in #43338:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43338#issuecomment-5302532715

## Compatibility and limitations

- The patch changes Python scheduler and grammar-management code only. It does
  not change model kernels, sampling distributions, API schemas, or compiled
  components.
- XGrammar and Guidance have direct backend tests. Outlines and
  LM Format Enforcer implement the same non-advancing, longest-prefix
  `validate_tokens()` interface but do not have model-serving qualification in
  this PR.
- Runtime qualification uses XGrammar 0.2.5 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 and
  DSpark K5. Other speculative methods exercise the same scheduler interface,
  but their model-serving behavior was not separately benchmarked.
- The additional work is bounded by the accepted speculative block length. The
  reasoning-only path performs one parser check, and request history is not
  copied by the manager.
- A direct Step3.5 parser test verifies that pre-commit boundary detection does
  not consume the parser's pending-transition state.

## Test Plan

```bash
uvx --from pre-commit pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_reasoning_structured_output.py
```

The tests cover:

- XGrammar and Guidance rejection at a reasoning boundary;
- rejection after grammar completion;
- multi-token markers within a block and across committed/new token storage;
- constant-history sequence access and one-check reasoning-only behavior;
- preservation of request-local state in a Step3.5 reasoning parser;
- synchronous and asynchronous rollback for bonus-only, partial-draft, and
  complete-block rejection;
- speculative acceptance totals and per-position metrics;
- scheduler commit, emitted output, and grammar advancement through one
  identical filtered prefix;
- bypass behavior for unstructured requests.

## Test Result

### Source qualification

- Repository pre-commit hooks: passed, including Ruff, formatting, typos,
  mypy, SPDX, forbidden imports, and configuration checks.
- Four relevant pytest modules: `211 passed` in 170.56 seconds.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Negative control at
`main@ac2ae8798c7ef59c1924d5c0447a4279fa645770`:

- four XGrammar/Guidance boundary and termination tests fail because accepted
  blocks have no pre-commit validation;
- the scheduler behavior test commits `[10, 11, 12]` instead of the valid
  prefix `[10, 11]`.

The same five discriminator cases pass with commit
`fa0777ff775a870a5d6a6ff187f769e50b38c4ad`.

### Model-serving qualification

Runtime conditions:

```text
model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731
topology: TP2 / DCP1
target backend: B12X W4A8
speculative decoding: fixed probabilistic DSpark K5
structured-output backend: XGrammar 0.2.5
scheduler: asynchronous
CUDA graph row cap: 48
concurrency: 8
```

The runtime branch contains #44297 and #44993. The accepted-block validation is
the source change in local-inference-lab/vllm#320.

- Unfiltered source fails the deterministic growing strict-tool test by round
  11.
- A boundary-only filter fails at round 29 when a speculative suffix follows
  grammar termination.
- Complete-block validation finishes 32 rounds and 256 HTTP requests at up to
  225,634 prompt tokens per request. Of those responses, 255 contain one
  schema-valid tool call. One response reaches its configured 768-token output
  limit while still reasoning and reproduces that output-limit result on retry.
- The committed source composition passes 24/24 deterministic strict-tool
  requests: eight buffered or streaming requests at C1 and 16 requests at C8.
- An independently supplied 282,817-byte request payload returns one valid JSON
  tool call in each of eight concurrent replays.
- Ordinary no-tool C1 decode measures 194.3 tok/s. Same-host controls with the
  same launch profile measure 194.02-194.81 tok/s, so no throughput regression
  is measurable at the precision of those runs.

Reproducible image:

```text
tag: voipmonitor/vllm:infernal-invocation-vllm91e2adf-b12xec2f97d-fi1ac6942-cu133-torch213-20260815-r14
digest: sha256:9fe1d1b0e8370df578f92c6431af41a9fc36076ccbebac18c77a8ae99a3454e3
```

Detailed serving evidence:

- https://github.com/local-inference-lab/vllm/pull/320
- https://github.com/local-inference-lab/rtx6kpro/blob/master/models/ds4dspark-infernal-invocation-r14.md
- https://github.com/local-inference-lab/rtx6kpro/issues/67

## AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex assisted with source analysis, implementation, tests, negative
controls, and PR drafting. The submitted patch is supported by the source and
model-serving qualification documented above.

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] Purpose and affected invariant are specified.
- [x] Test commands and results are included.
- [x] Model-serving evaluation is included because output correctness changes.
- [x] Related and partially overlapping PRs are distinguished.
- [x] No user documentation change is required; the patch preserves the public
  API and corrects an internal commit invariant.

</details>

title: [Bug]: 0.27.1 crashes in custom_all_reduce (illegal memory access) during CUDA graph capture on Hopper TP=4; identical config works on 0.26.0
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```text
vLLM (failing)    : 0.27.1+cu129
vLLM (working)    : 0.26.0+cu129
PyTorch           : 2.13.0+cu129   (0.26.0 env: 2.11.0+cu129)
CUDA (torch built): 12.9
Python            : 3.10.12
OS                : Linux-5.15.0-94-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35
GPU               : NVIDIA H800, compute capability 9.0 (Hopper / SM90)
Driver            : 575.57.08
Parallelism       : TP=4, single node, no PP, no DP, no EP
Model             : deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (FP8 checkpoint)
KV cache dtype    : fp8
```

The two vLLM versions are installed in **separate virtualenvs** on the same
host, so the comparison below changes exactly one variable: the vLLM version.

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

A TP=4 configuration that has been serving reliably on **0.26.0** for weeks
fails to start on **0.27.1**. The engine dies during CUDA graph capture with an
illegal memory access originating in the custom all-reduce kernel:

```
Failed: Cuda error /workspace/csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:164 'an illegal memory access was encountered'
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

Immediately before the crash, 0.27.1 logs:

```
Auto-enabling VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1. Set VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 to opt out.
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH is set, disabling vLLM's torch.compile pipeline. Equivalent to -cc.mode=none.
```

followed by `Capturing CUDA graphs (PIECEWISE): 0%| | 0/51` and then the fault
on all four ranks.

#### Reproduction

The command line is **copied verbatim** from the working 0.26.0 systemd unit —
same model, same `--tensor-parallel-size 4`, same `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, same
`--gpu-memory-utilization`, same environment variables. Only the interpreter
(virtualenv) differs:

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \
    --served-model-name deepseek-v4 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8012
```

- On **0.26.0**: starts normally, serves traffic.
- On **0.27.1**: crashes as above, reproducibly, every attempt.

#### What I ruled out

I ran this twice with different configurations to isolate the cause:

| Run | Config | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.27.1 **with** `--speculative-config` (DSpark), `gpu-mem-util 0.88`, `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"}'`, `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` | illegal memory access |
| 2 | 0.27.1 **without** speculative decoding, no `expandable_segments`, parameters byte-for-byte identical to the working 0.26.0 unit | **same crash**, `custom_all_reduce.cuh:164` |

So the failure is **not** caused by speculative decoding, not by the lowered
memory utilization, and not by `expandable_segments` — run 2 has none of them
and still crashes. The only remaining variable is the vLLM version itself.

#### Possibly relevant

`csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh` was heavily refactored between the two releases —
`git diff v0.26.0..v0.27.1` shows **+20 / −296** for that file, with the
implementation moved into a new `custom_collective_common.cuh`. Given the crash
site, that refactor seems like a plausible place to look.

#### Not a duplicate of

I checked the closest-looking existing reports; none match this configuration:

- **#51758** — same headline symptom ("upgrade 0.26.0 → 0.27.0, DeepSeek V4
  Flash error"), but that environment is **RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) +
  CUDA 13.0**, and the comments trace it to a DeepGEMM scale-factor layout
  regression missing the `arch_major == 12` branch. This report is **Hopper
  SM90 / cu129**, and the fault is in the all-reduce kernel, not DeepGEMM.
- **#46253** — illegal memory access under `breakable_cudagraph`, but that is a
  **cross-node** GB10 setup where NCCL falls back to a host-staged transport
  without GPUDirect. This is a **single-node** TP=4 case.
- **#45604** — same file, 4 GPUs, but the reported fault is `invalid argument`
  in the FlashInfer AllReduce **norm fusion** path with MXFP8.
- **#42609** — `custom_all_reduce` IPC handles vs `expandable_segments`,
  requires DP>1 **and** TP>1; here DP=1, and run 2 does not set
  `expandable_segments` at all.

#### Happy to help

I have both versions installed side by side on the same host and can run
additional diagnostics (`CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, `--enforce-eager`,
`VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`, `--disable-custom-all-reduce`, compute-sanitizer)
if that would help narrow it down — just say which would be most useful.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lengthy documentation-related questions.

title: [Bugfix] Fall back Mamba cache 'all' mode to 'align' on Model Runner V2 (#52317)
body:
## Purpose
Fixes #52317

When running hybrid Mamba models like `nvidia/Nemotron-H-4B-Base-8K` with prefix caching and `--mamba-cache-mode all` under configurations that trigger Model Runner V2 (such as DSpark/DFlash speculative decoding or Context Parallelism), vLLM crashes on startup during warmup:

```
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py", line 990, in _forward_core
    assert block_idx_last_scheduled_token_prev_step_d is not None
AssertionError
```

### Why this happens
- In Model Runner V1, Mamba prefix caching in `"all"` mode works by having the runner allocate and pass `block_idx_last_scheduled_token_prev_step_d` down to the mixer layers.
- Model Runner V2 (`GPUModelRunnerV2`) only implements `_align_mode` Mamba state tracking (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py`) and does not construct `block_idx_last_scheduled_token_prev_step_d`.
- In `MambaModelConfig.verify_and_update_config`, we only checked if the model architecture supported prefix caching (`model_config.supports_mamba_prefix_caching`). Since Nemotron-H supports it on MRv1, it passed validation, but when MRv2 was selected by the engine, the missing tensor caused an assertion failure at runtime.

### What this PR does
1. **Fallback in `MambaModelConfig`**: In `vllm/model_executor/models/config.py`, check `vllm_config.use_v2_model_runner`. When MRv2 is active and `mamba_cache_mode == "all"`, fall back to `"align"` mode with a warning. On MRv1, `"all"` mode is preserved for supported models.
2. **Unit test suite**: Added unit tests in `tests/test_config.py` verifying MRv2 fallback, verification idempotency, and MRv1 preservation.

---

### Update
- **MRv2 Behavior**: Automatically falls back `mamba_cache_mode="all"` → `"align"` mode (logging an informative warning) since MRv2 only implements `_align_mode` state tracking and does not construct `block_idx_last_scheduled_token_prev_step_d`.
- **MRv1 Behavior**: Retains `"all"` mode behavior as-is for supported hybrid models (e.g. `Nemotron-H`), keeping existing V1 prefix caching fully intact.

## Test Plan

- **Unit tests**:
  ```bash
  pytest tests/test_config.py -k "test_mamba_cache_mode or test_validate_mamba" -v
  ```
- **Linting**:
  ```bash
  pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/config.py tests/test_config.py --hook-stage manual
  ```
- **End-to-End Verification (4x A100 GPUs)**:
  Reproduced the crash and verified the fix by starting `nvidia/Nemotron-H-4B-Base-8K` with DSpark speculative decoding:
  ```bash
  vllm serve nvidia/Nemotron-H-4B-Base-8K \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --mamba-cache-mode all \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark", "draft_model":"nvidia/Nemotron-H-4B-Base-8K", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4
  ```

## Test Result

- `pytest tests/test_config.py -k "test_mamba_cache_mode or test_validate_mamba"`:
  ```
  tests/test_config.py::test_validate_mamba_align_subblock_prefill PASSED
  tests/test_config.py::test_mamba_cache_mode_all_fallback[mrv2_falls_back] PASSED
  tests/test_config.py::test_mamba_cache_mode_all_fallback[mrv1_supported_keeps_all] PASSED
  tests/test_config.py::test_mamba_cache_mode_all_fallback[mrv1_unsupported_falls_back] PASSED
  ================ 4 passed, 188 deselected in 4.18s ================
  ```
- `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual` on both changed files: all hooks pass, including `ruff check`, `ruff format`, `typos`, and `mypy` for Python 3.10–3.13.
- End-to-end server: confirmed warning `Model Runner V2 only supports Mamba cache 'align' mode for prefix caching: falling back to 'align' mode.` is logged and server finishes warmup and handles inference without crashing.

---

title: [Bug][DP] Tie-break rotation from #47420 degrades prefix-cache locality for multi-turn traffic under internal DP LB
body:
### Your current environment

vLLM nightly `ac7509e2b1db` (also reproduced on the latest release build), 8×H100 SXM (one node), `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, `--data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --api-server-count 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 1000000 --block-size 256`, prefix caching enabled (default).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**#47420 ("Rotate load-balancer tie-break to avoid systematic engine bias") degrades prefix-cache locality for multi-turn / shared-prefix traffic under internal DP load balancing.**

`DPLBAsyncMPClient.get_core_engine_for_request` resolves score ties by scanning from `eng_start_index`, and since #47420 that start index rotates after every decision. A multi-turn conversation at low load is exactly a stream of tied decisions, so consecutive turns rotate across DP ranks — and every turn misses the prefix its previous turn left in that rank's KV cache. Before #47420 the fixed scan start accidentally pinned each frontend client's tied decisions to one rank, which is what kept sessions cache-local.

Measured with an aiperf mooncake-trace replay matched to production shape (multi-turn sessions, ~34k-token prompts, trace designed for **81.7%** prefix reuse), identical client and trace on both engines:

| | prefix-cache hit rate (c=1 … c=128) | designed |
|---|---|---|
| v0.23.0 (pre-#47420) | **81.6%** measured run-wide | 81.7% |
| current main (`ac7509e2b1db`) | **37.6% / 52.9% / 20.0% / 16.0% / 10.9% / 7.8%** | 81.7% |

Per-rank counters confirm the mechanism: at c=1 (strictly sequential turns), `vllm:prefix_cache_queries` spreads *evenly* across all 4 DP ranks (~350k each) while hits concentrate on the ranks that happened to repeat.

**On attribution.** The mechanism is confirmed directly: #47420's only behavioral change to `get_core_engine_for_request` is rotating `eng_start_index` per decision, and a tie-break-only A/B on a single nightly (nothing else changed) moves the c=1 hit rate 37.6% → 61.5%. The 81.6% row above is v0.23.0 — a version-level baseline spanning many commits, not a single-commit revert — so it *bounds* rather than *isolates* #47420's exact share; reverting only #47420 on the current nightly would isolate it cleanly. Either way the `--api-server-count` / SO_REUSEPORT factor noted below is an independent contributor.

End-to-end cost on this workload: **−2% to −13% per-user output throughput vs v0.23.0** despite main being +6–17% faster on a cache-defeating random-token ladder (same hardware, same recipe) — the re-prefill of ~34k-token prompts swamps the decode-side wins.

#47420's own benchmark ran with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`, so the fairness fix never saw this cost. The fairness problem it fixed was real; the tie-break just shouldn't rotate *related* requests away from their cache.

### Partial mitigation (PR incoming) and why the full fix needs a design decision

PR from this account: remember which engine served a prompt's first-block prefix (small LRU keyed on `cache_salt` + LoRA id + first `block_size` prompt token ids) and prefer that engine **only when scores tie**. Load-aware decisions are unchanged; unrelated tied requests still rotate, preserving #47420's fairness.

A/B on the hardware above (same trace, same engine, only the tie-break differs): c=1 hit rate 37.6% → **61.5%** (+6% per-user throughput), c=32 16.0% → 23.2%. It does **not** restore the 81.6% baseline, for a structural reason: with `--api-server-count N`, each frontend process has its own `DPLBAsyncMPClient` (and now its own affinity map), and SO_REUSEPORT spreads one session's connections across processes — client-side affinity can only see the requests that land on its process. The pre-#47420 behavior dodged this by pinning *every* client's ties to a per-client rank, at the cost of the fairness bias #47420 fixed.

A complete fix needs prefix-awareness at a shared layer — the DP coordinator, or a shared affinity table across frontend processes — which is a design decision for the maintainers. Filing this issue so the tie-break mitigation and that larger conversation have a home.

title: [Core][DP] Prefix-affinity tie-break in the internal DP load balancer
body:
## Purpose

Partial mitigation for #52463: the tie-break rotation added in #47420 degrades prefix-cache locality for multi-turn / shared-prefix traffic under the internal DP load balancer. Consecutive turns of one conversation are tied decisions at low load, so they rotate across DP ranks and every turn misses the prefix its previous turn cached.

This PR remembers which engine served a prompt's first-block prefix (LRU of 16k entries, keyed on `cache_salt` + LoRA id + first `block_size` prompt token ids) and prefers that engine **only when scores tie**:

- Load-aware decisions unchanged — a lower-scored engine always wins.
- Unrelated tied requests still rotate — #47420's fairness fix is preserved (regression-tested).
- Explicit `data_parallel_rank` and late-interaction routing bypass affinity, unchanged.
- Stale entries from elastic-EP scale-in are discarded; sub-block prompts (which cannot hit the cache) are exempt.

## Test Plan

- `tests/v1/engine/test_dp_lb_prefix_affinity.py` — 8 CPU-only unit tests driving `get_core_engine_for_request` directly: session stickiness across turns, tied-unrelated rotation preserved, load-beats-affinity, sub-block exemption, cache_salt separation, explicit-rank bypass, scale-in staleness, LRU bound.
- Hardware A/B on 8×H100 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, DP=4+EP, `--api-server-count 4`, fp8 KV, aiperf mooncake trace designed for 81.7% prefix reuse — full methodology in #52463): identical runs, only this patch differs.

## Test Result

Unit: 8/8 pass (run inside `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image).

Hardware A/B (prefix-cache hit rate, per-user output tok/s):

| conc | hit rate before → after | tok/s/user before → after |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | 37.6% → **61.5%** | 69.5 → 73.6 (+6%) |
| 4 | 52.9% → 53.5% | 47.2 → 45.1 (−4%) |
| 16 | 20.0% → 21.9% | 16.3 → 12.6 (−23%)* |
| 32 | 16.0% → **23.2%** | 9.7 → 9.6 (−1%) |
| 64 | 10.9% → 11.1% | 5.0 → 4.8 (−5%) |
| 128 | 7.8% → 8.8% | 2.6 → 2.7 (+4%) |

\* hit rate unchanged while throughput moved — consistent with run-to-run variance at 160 requests/level, not a cache effect; happy to re-run if reviewers want more samples.

**Known limitation (why this is a mitigation, not the full fix):** with `--api-server-count N` each frontend process has its own client and affinity map, and SO_REUSEPORT spreads one session's connections across processes — client-side affinity only sees its own process's requests (this bounds the c=1 recovery at 61.5% vs 81.6% measured on v0.23.0, a pre-#47420 release — a version-level baseline, not a single-commit revert of #47420). The complete fix needs prefix-awareness at a shared layer (DP coordinator or a shared affinity table); #52463 is the home for that design discussion.

FIX #52463

title: [Core] Keep client stop strings dormant inside the reasoning segment
body:
FIX #52393

## Problem

When a model emits reasoning inline in the same text stream (think-in-prompt deployments, e.g. DeepSeek-V4 with `--reasoning-parser deepseek_v4`), client-supplied `stop` strings are evaluated against the reasoning text too. A stop string that legitimately appears while the model is thinking (restating the user's question, quoting a delimiter) truncates the response inside the reasoning segment — the reasoning parser then never sees the end-marker, and the API returns `content: None` with the visible answer lost. Details and reproduction in #52393.

## Fix

`BaseIncrementalDetokenizer` now arms a per-request guard (`reasoning_stop_guard`) when the request carries stop strings and the deployment has a reasoning parser with a known end marker. While armed:

- stop strings stay dormant until the reasoning end marker (`</think>`) has been observed in the output stream;
- once the marker lands, stop evaluation resumes from the character offset immediately after the marker (handles the marker and post-marker content arriving in one decode step, e.g. under speculative decoding);
- requests without stop strings, or deployments without a reasoning parser, take the existing code path unchanged.

`min_tokens` and EOS/token-id stopping are unaffected; only client stop-string matching is deferred.

## Testing

- 4 new tests in `tests/v1/engine/test_stop_in_reasoning.py` (dormant-in-reasoning, one-chunk marker+content close, non-reasoning requests unchanged, marker split across decode steps) — all pass.
- Logic additionally validated end-to-end against a GB10 two-node DeepSeek-V4-Flash deployment where the truncation reproduces; with the guard, hostile stop strings inside reasoning no longer truncate, and stops still fire in the visible answer.

title: [Bugfix] Reload speculative draft weights after Level 2 sleep wake
body:
Addresses #52479

## Problem

After the documented Level 2 sleep/wake sequence, MTP speculative decoding
silently stops helping: every drafted token is rejected
(`Mean acceptance length: 1.00`, `Accepted throughput: 0.00`) and decode
throughput falls to approximately the no-speculation rate. Target-model outputs
remain correct, so the failure appears only as a large performance regression.

Level 2 sleep discards draft parameters together with the target parameters.
`wake_up()` restores the saved draft buffers, but the documented subsequent
`reload_weights()` call reloaded only the target model. The drafter is a
separate module and therefore continued with discarded parameter storage.

## Fix

Put the disk-backed draft reload in `GPUModelRunner.reload_weights`
(`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`), on the existing
`weights_iterator is None` path, before the target load:

- Resolve the draft through the existing `get_draft_model()` accessor.
- Read the configured draft checkpoint with its model loader. MTP configurations
  without a separate `draft_load_config` use the target load configuration.
- Load in place through `initialize_layerwise_reload` /
  `finalize_layerwise_reload`, preserving the parameter addresses captured by
  the compiled runtime.
- Invoke the helper unbound (`GPUModelRunner._reload_draft_weights_from_disk(self)`)
  because Model Runner V2 already delegates this method with a V2 `self` and
  does not inherit the helper.
- During that draft load, temporarily unbind any draft submodule that is the
  same object as a target module. A discard dummy swallows checkpoint tensors
  for those aliases so layerwise reload and `load_weights` cannot shape-mismatch
  or rewrite live target storage (Gemma4 MTP after `_maybe_share_embeddings`).
  The exemption is checkpoint-free-subtree only: a shared module with no
  parameters **and** no persistent buffers anywhere in its subtree (the
  `get_rope`-cached rotary embedding) is left attached, because the draft's
  `load_weights` may still read it (dflash/dspark read `rotary_emb.head_size`
  while rebuilding fused KV buffers) and it receives no checkpoint tensors.
  Each buffer is checked against the persistence set of the module that
  registers it, so a shared module carrying a persistent buffer (direct or
  nested) is still detached — `AutoWeightsLoader` loads persistent registered
  buffers, so leaving such a module attached would let the draft checkpoint
  write into the target's buffer. This covers registered checkpoint state; a
  custom `load_weights` that consumes tensors into unregistered state is out of
  scope.
- If a detached `embed_tokens` keeps the same vocab-axis width as the draft
  `lm_head` but differs on the hidden axis (the Gemma4 MTP tied-placeholder
  layout), load those embed tensors into the still-live `lm_head`. Heads that
  differ on the vocab axis (EAGLE3 low-rank heads) are real projections with
  their own checkpoint entries and take the discard path; same-width shared
  embeds are discarded and restored by the target reload.
- After `finalize_layerwise_reload`, re-run the drafter's fused-buffer rebuild
  (`_build_fused_kv_buffers`) if it defines one. The dflash/dspark drafters
  rebuild derived state (a stacked copy of layer weights plus a cached
  rotary-embedding reference) at the end of `load_weights`; inside the layerwise
  window that rebuild captures the temporarily meta-derived rotary buffer, so
  it is re-run after finalization restores the real buffers. No-op for
  drafters without the builder.
- Reload the target last so same-width shared storage (typical Qwen MTP /
  EAGLE) is restored from the target checkpoint.
- Leave iterator-based reloads unchanged; those weights are supplied by their
  caller and are not assumed to contain a second draft checkpoint.

Model Runner V2 keeps its existing one-line delegate into that method. There is
no V2 wrapper and no production-file diff under `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/`.

This mirrors Level 1 sleep semantics: both paths restore the existing target
and draft modules in place. Level 1 restores their tagged allocations from host
RAM, while Level 2 restores saved buffers during `wake_up()` and reloads model
parameters from their disk checkpoints during `reload_weights()`.

### Why not `start_draft_weight_update()`?

The draft weight-update API added by #46725 selects the draft as the destination
of an already-configured `WeightTransferEngine`. Its built-in NCCL and IPC
backends receive weights supplied by an external trainer; they do not accept a
checkpoint path or read weights from disk. The API also requires the server to
start with `weight_transfer_config`. It remains the correct path for runtime
trainer/RL weight transfer; this PR does not replace it.

The failing workflow is the separate, documented disk-restore path and does not
require a trainer or weight-transfer engine:

```python
llm.sleep(level=2)
llm.wake_up(tags=["weights"])
llm.collective_rpc("reload_weights")
llm.wake_up(tags=["kv_cache"])
```

This change reuses #46725's `get_draft_model()` accessor and the same layerwise
reload lifecycle used by checkpoint-format transfer engines, while keeping the
checkpoint source appropriate to this workflow.

This is not a duplicate of #46725: that change added externally supplied
runtime draft updates, while this PR completes the separate documented
disk-backed `reload_weights()` recovery path.

## Live evidence

### Qwen3.8 MTP (same-checkpoint, same-width share)

Measured on an earlier MRV2-wrapper revision of this PR (same disk draft
loader, layerwise lifecycle, and draft-first / target-last order) on 2x RTX
5090, TP=2, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=2`, with sleep mode
enabled. Each throughput entry is the median of three 256-token HTTP
generations.

| State | Throughput | Mean acceptance length | Reload RPC |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Cold baseline | 109.4 tok/s | not recorded | — |
| L2 wake cycle 1 | 108.9 tok/s (100% of baseline) | 2.17 | 4.18 s |
| L2 wake cycle 2 | 104.9 tok/s (96% of baseline) | 2.43 | 4.11 s |

Unpatched reproduction on that stack: 51.8 tok/s, acceptance length 1.00, zero
accepted draft tokens.

### Gemma4 E2B MTP (dim-mismatched shared embeddings)

Measured on this branch (identity detach + tied-embed sink) on the same
2x RTX 5090, TP=2, `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` + `google/gemma-4-E2B-it-assistant`,
MTP `num_speculative_tokens=1`, sleep mode enabled. Each throughput entry is
the median of three 64-token HTTP generations. Assistant `hidden_size=256`,
`backbone_hidden_size=1536`.

| State | Throughput | Mean acceptance length | Reload RPC |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Cold baseline | 297.5 tok/s | 1.50 | — |
| L2 wake cycle 1 | 293.0 tok/s (98% of baseline) | 1.50 | 1.15 s |
| L2 wake cycle 2 | 304.6 tok/s (102% of baseline) | 1.50 | 1.08 s |

Both models used the documented staged sequence plus a prefix-cache reset.
Outputs were coherent. No shape-mismatch traceback. A discard-only detach
avoided the crash but left acceptance at 1.00 (tied `lm_head` never refilled);
the sink is what restored 1.50.

### EAGLE3 (separate draft checkpoint, low-rank draft head)

Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct + yuhuili/EAGLE3-LLaMA3.1-Instruct-8B, 2x RTX 5090,
TP=2, `num_speculative_tokens=3`, sleep mode enabled, `--enforce-eager`,
median of three 64-token generations. The head ships no `embed_tokens`
tensors, so the target's embedding module is installed in the draft (one
detached alias at reload); it keeps its own low-rank `lm_head` (draft vocab
32000).

| State | Throughput | Mean acceptance length | Reload RPC |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Cold baseline | 93.9 tok/s | 2.17 | — |
| L2 wake cycle 1 | 94.1 tok/s | 2.17 | 2.8 s |
| L2 wake cycle 2 | 97.1 tok/s | 2.17 | 2.8 s |

No draft parameters remain on meta after the reload; outputs coherent. On the
pre-guard revision used for this validation the tied-embed sink engaged on the
vocab-axis mismatch but consumed no tensors (the checkpoint ships none); the
hidden-axis guard added in a follow-up commit now sends this layout directly to
the discard path.

With CUDA graphs enabled (default), the same cycle instead fails at the first
post-wake step with a CUDA illegal memory access that under
`CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` raises synchronously inside the draft speculator's
fused multi-step decode CUDA-graph replay. This failure is reproduced without
this PR on the stock nightly (identical synchronous site, same machine), so it
was not introduced by this change; eager mode with this PR fully works. The
specific stale pointer inside the captured graph is not identified here.

### DSpark (draft ships neither embed nor lm_head)

Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 + its DSpark drafter (checkpoint of 62 tensors, no
`embed_tokens`/`lm_head` — both modules are the target's and are the two
detached aliases at reload), TP=2, `num_speculative_tokens=7`, median of three
64-token generations. The drafter rebuilds fused buffers at the end of
`load_weights`; inside the layerwise window that rebuild captured the
temporarily meta-derived rotary buffer while finalization restored the real
one, crashing the first fused RoPE dispatch. The follow-up commit re-runs that
rebuild after finalization.

| State | Throughput | Mean acceptance length | Reload RPC |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Cold baseline | 86.6 tok/s | 2.26 | — |
| L2 wake cycle 1 | 84.9 tok/s | 2.26 | 4.6 s |
| L2 wake cycle 2 | 85.4 tok/s | 2.26 | 4.6 s |

Zero draft parameters on meta after the reload; outputs coherent; clean worker
logs.

## Tests

Eleven focused unit tests cover:

1. A disk-backed reload restores the draft through its configured loader and
   the layerwise lifecycle before reloading the target.
2. The same disk path through Model Runner V2's existing
   `GPUModelRunnerV1.reload_weights(self, ...)` delegate.
3. A disk-backed reload without a draft still reloads the target normally.
4. A caller-supplied weight iterator does not trigger an implicit draft reload.
5. A dim-mismatched aliased `embed_tokens` (same vocab width, differing
   hidden) is not written; the tied draft-dim `lm_head` still receives the
   embed checkpoint tensor.
6. A same-width shared embed is discarded; a distinct `lm_head` is not filled
   from `embed_tokens`.
7. A vocab-mismatched shared embed (low-rank draft head) is discarded, and the
   head still loads from its own checkpoint entry.
8. A drafter whose `load_weights` rebuilds fused state mid-lifecycle has that
   rebuild re-run after finalization.
9. The same target `lm_head` aliased at `draft.lm_head` and every
   `shared_head.head` is detached (`named_modules(remove_duplicate=False)`).
10. A parameterless shared module (the `get_rope`-cached rotary embedding)
    stays attached and readable during the draft load, while a shared
    parameter-bearing module is still detached; both are restored afterward.
11. A shared module carrying a persistent buffer (direct or nested) is
    detached during the draft load, while a shared module with only a
    non-persistent buffer stays attached; all aliases are restored afterward.

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::TestReloadDraftWeights -q
# 11 passed
```

## Scope and limitations

- The serving path of interest is Model Runner V2. The implementation lives in
  the shared `GPUModelRunner.reload_weights` that V2 already calls, so a
  legacy V1 engine using that method also gets the disk draft reload.
- Live validation covers Qwen3.8 same-checkpoint MTP, Gemma4 E2B MTP with a
  separate assistant checkpoint, EAGLE3 under `--enforce-eager`, and DSpark
  end-to-end, all TP=2. Graphed-mode EAGLE3 fails at the first post-wake step
  inside the draft's multi-step CUDA-graph replay; that failure is reproduced
  without this PR on the stock nightly and is not addressed here. Independent
  drafts are unbound only when a module is the same object as the target:
  EAGLE3 shares the target's embedding, DSpark shares both the embedding and
  the output head, and both detach as expected.
- Downstream validation (reported by @colinasmith, pinned to the revision
  tested — `main@4e4d75c45` + this PR, before the checkpoint-free-subtree
  narrowing): MTP Qwen3.6-27B FP8 and DFlash muse-glimmer-30B both reload
  correctly across L2 sleep/wake cycles on a single RTX PRO 6000 (SM120),
  with acceptance preserved and 141/141 requests OK behind a sleep/wake
  model-switching gateway. The DFlash rotary-alias crash found there is fixed
  by the checkpoint-free-subtree exemption above; that downstream result does
  not itself validate the final narrowed stack.
- The configured draft checkpoint remains the source of draft weights. This
  change does not redefine draft selection during `weights_path` model swaps.
- Draft formats whose loaders do not implement `get_all_weights` raise
  `NotImplementedError`, matching the existing target-model disk reload.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, review-response
analysis, and test orchestration. The submitter reviewed the changes and the
live validation described above.

title: [ROCm] Keep DeepSeek V4 on MRV1 with the wide eager attention region
body:
## Summary

- On ROCm only, restore the DeepSeek V4 defaults that [#52093](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52093) and [#52094](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52094) revert globally: MRV1 as the default runner, and the wide eager attention region MRV1 needs.
- CUDA keeps MRV2 and the narrow eager region from [#51430](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51430) / [#51768](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51768).
- MRV1 wraps `_prepare_and_attn` in `_prepare_and_attn_eager`; MRV2 keeps the narrow `_sparse_indexer_and_attn` break. Drop the MRV1+PIECEWISE rejection once the wide region is restored for MRV1.

## Why this is not a duplicate of #52093 / #52094

Those PRs revert [#51430](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51430) and [#51768](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51768) on every platform. This PR scopes the same performance recovery to ROCm. CUDA is unchanged.

[#52401](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52401) already takes this same runner-gated approach. This PR is the AMD-fork replacement for #52093/#52094 so those global reverts can close. If #52401 lands first, this PR can close as a duplicate.

## Test plan

- [x] `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py::test_rocm_defaults_deepseek_v4_to_mrv1 tests/test_config.py::test_is_default_v2_model_runner_model tests/test_config.py::test_v2_model_runner_env_tri_state -v --noconftest` — 23 passed
- [x] Pre-commit on commit: ruff, format, mypy 3.10, SPDX, config validation passed

- [x] Non-thinking gsm8k on the new ROCm default. MRV2 clamp-only on this box was 0.9568 / 0.9575; MRV1 + wide eager previously scored 0.9591 / 0.9598.

## Contribution notes

- Duplicate check: #52093/#52094 are global reverts; #52401 is the same ROCm-scoped approach. This PR exists to supersede the global reverts from this fork.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Count SWA in-flight KV once per pool, not per request (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 #51041)
body:
Fixes #51041

## Summary

`get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config()` divided the KV cache pool by each group's **full per-request admission cap**, which includes the `max_in_flight_tokens` allowance inside `SlidingWindowSpec.max_admission_blocks_per_request()`. But in-flight tokens are bounded **system-wide** by the scheduler's token budget across *all* requests — at most `max_in_flight_tokens` tokens are unsettled at any moment, regardless of concurrency. Multiplying a global bound by max concurrency over-reserves the pool by `(max_concurrency − 1) × transient` blocks per SWA-class group.

On DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (H20 TP=2, `fp8_ds_mla`, block size 256, `max_num_batched_tokens` 8192, doubled under async scheduling) the four SWA-class groups of the 5-group hybrid layout each charge in-flight tokens at tiny compressor block granularity (`cdiv(16384, 4) = 4099` pages, `cdiv(16384, 8) = 2065` pages …), inflating the per-request footprint from ~3.6 KiB/token to ~53.5 KiB/token and capping `max_model_len` at ~121K instead of ~1M. This matches every datapoint in the issue (Burlesque1's 53.5 KiB H20 TP=2, kezboard233's V100 α/β regression, @CHNtentes' healthy 10.07 KiB DSpark run).

### The change

- `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`: add `steady_memory_usage_bytes()` / `transient_memory_usage_bytes()` to `KVCacheSpec` with the exact identity `admission == steady + transient`. Defaults preserve byte-identical behavior for every other spec type; overridden only in `SlidingWindowSpec`, `ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec`, and `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` (the DSv4 aggregated worker-config shape).
- `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`: reserve the transient part once per pool instead of per request:

  ```
  N_max = (num_blocks − Σ_g transient_g) / Σ_g steady_g
  ```

The runtime per-request admission gate is unchanged, so startup sizing and runtime admission stay consistent: `N × steady + transient ≤ num_blocks`. Pool sizing (`_max_memory_usage_bytes_from_groups`, the `max`-based conservative bound) is untouched.

### Note on 0731 vs preview

The checkpoint config delta (2 trailing zeros in `compress_ratios`, `dspark_*` fields) is a red herring — layer indices ≥ `num_hidden_layers` are clamped and every `dspark_*` consumer is gated behind `use_dspark()`. The regression tracks the **vLLM version**, not the checkpoint: the admission formula was introduced by #40946 and widened to `max_in_flight_tokens` by #47728 (2026-07-08, shortly before 0.26.0). The preview checkpoint's older config format simply doesn't form the 5-group hybrid layout on 0.26.0, so it never hits the SWA-group overcharge.

### Not duplicating existing PRs

Checked open PRs referencing #51041 / KV-cache accounting — none. This PR is distinct from:
- #37584 (auto-revert of #36030) — concerns the pool-sizing **sum** in `_max_memory_usage_bytes_from_groups`, untouched here; the #48317/#36030 per-group sums are preserved for the steady part.
- #40694 — fixes the capacity **log** for Qwen3.5 hybrid, log-only.
- #41834 — SM12x enablement, no accounting changes.

## Behavior change

Capacity/concurrency **reporting and admission headroom only** — no attention kernels, no KV layout, no numerics. Model outputs are unchanged, so no model evals were run.

## Test Plan / Results

All on CPU (no GPU on the dev machine — GPU test suites were **not** run):

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py                                        # 78 passed
pytest tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
       tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py                                        # 100 passed
pytest tests/v1/test_kv_cache_spec_registry.py \
       tests/v1/engine/test_init_error_messaging.py                                # 45 passed
pytest tests/v1/core/                                                              # 496 passed; 3 e2e tests fail
                                                                                   # engine init identically on
                                                                                   # the base commit (GPU-less host,
                                                                                   # pre-existing, not a regression)
pre-commit run --files <changed files>                                             # all passed (ruff, format, mypy-3.10)
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files <changed files> --hook-stage manual               # passed
```

New regression test `test_dsv4_flash_0731_kv_capacity` builds the real 0731 architecture (43 layers, `compress_ratios = [0, 0, (4, 128)×20, 0]`, real per-layer spec shapes from `deepseek_v4/attention.py` / `compressor.py`) through the actual grouping → packed-layout → concurrency pipeline, and asserts:
1. the 5-group hybrid layout forms with 20/20 compressor layers,
2. `steady + transient == max` holds per group,
3. per-token cost < 10 KiB at 1M context (pre-fix ~53 KiB),
4. the new formula strictly beats the pre-fix per-request-peak formula.

Four existing assertions in `test_get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config` / `test_get_max_concurrency_packed_kv_cache_config` were updated to the new (documented-in-comment) expected values.

## AI-assistance statement

**The code, tests, and this PR description were entirely generated by an AI agent (Claude); the change was reviewed line-by-line by the human submitter (@volkermauel), who also ran the full CPU test suites and lint/mypy checks listed above and verified the root-cause analysis against the numeric evidence in the issue thread.**

title: [Bugfix][Hardware][NVIDIA] Fix DSV4 sparse MLA spec-decode shapes on SM120 FlashInfer path
body:
## Purpose

Fix DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA speculative decoding (DSpark) on SM120/SM121 (GB10 / DGX Spark) with the `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` backend.

FlashInfer's `trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4` API disambiguates decode-vs-prefill by query rank. With speculative decoding (`next_n > 1` tokens per request), `DeepseekV4FlashInferSM120Attention` passes a flattened 3-D `[tokens, heads, 512]` query, which FlashInfer's normalizer misroutes to the varlen prefill kernel. The SM120 prefill build asserts `num_tokens > 64` and the server crashes with the cryptic `"Decode ... must go through sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4"` assertion.

Four related fixes, all confined to `DeepseekV4FlashInferSM120Attention`:

1. **4-D spec-decode query**: pass `[batch, next_n, heads, 512]` query (and matching output view) for spec decode batches so FlashInfer routes them to the decode kernels.
2. **Companion index reshape**: reshape sparse indices/lens to `[batch, next_n, ...]` alongside the 4-D query (FlashInfer validates their layout against the query).
3. **≤64-token prefill segments**: route them through per-request decode-form `[1, q_len, ...]` calls (the DSpark draft's k-token pass and short chunked-prefill tails hit the same `num_tokens > 64` prefill assert).
4. **Empty prefill chunks**: skip zero-token spans in `query_start_loc` — the FlashInfer sparse kernel crashes reshaping 0 elements. (FlashMLA-side counterpart of the same class of bug: #51489.)

Not a duplicate: #51538 (merged) fixes the SM120 top-k specialization selection and adds an init-time check, but the decode call on `main` still passes flat 3-D queries for spec batches, and the prefill chunk loop still has neither the ≤64-token routing nor the empty-chunk skip. #41834 (SM12x DSV4 enablement) does not touch `flashinfer_sparse.py` spec-decode shapes.

## Test Plan

- `python -m py_compile vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py`
- End-to-end: 2× DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), TP=2, serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with DSpark speculative decoding enabled; mixed short/long prompt load including chunked prefill.

## Test Result

- Before: server crashes on the first spec-decode batch with the SM120 prefill `num_tokens > 64` assertion.
- After: DSpark spec decode serves stably on 2× DGX Spark GB10 TP=2 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731); draft k-token passes, short chunk tails, and empty chunks all handled; output spot-checked against non-spec decoding.

---

AI assistance was used for this PR (rebasing/porting the fixes from a v0.26.0-based production branch onto `main`); every changed line was reviewed and validated end-to-end by the submitter on the hardware above.

title: [Bugfix] Detect unloaded NVFP4 weight scales with a NaN sentinel
body:
## Purpose

Fail during loading when a ModelOpt NVFP4 linear layer's `weight_scale` was not fully populated, instead of producing NaN outputs later. This can happen when a mixed-precision checkpoint stores the layer as BF16 but the layer is not excluded from NVFP4 quantization.

Initialize per-block `weight_scale` values to NaN, then check for remaining NaNs in `KNvfp4Static.process()` after casting to FP32 for backend compatibility. If any remain, raise a `RuntimeError` identifying the layer and suggesting that it be excluded from quantization. This detects skipped or partial scale loading without relying on the contents of `torch.empty()` memory.

This complements #45320, which checks missing per-expert scales in the MoE path. This PR covers per-block scales in the linear path. #42601 addresses activation-scale clamping for dead experts, a separate NaN source.

## Validation

- Current rebase: `.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --all-files --hook-stage manual --show-diff-on-failure` — all hooks passed, including Ruff, clang-format, and mypy for Python 3.10–3.13.
- `git range-diff` confirms all three reviewed patches are unchanged by the rebase onto `6fbb00b18`.
- Previously validated the NaN-sentinel check on GB10/CUDA with completely unloaded and partially loaded scales; casting to FP32 preserved detection in both cases.
- The original guard was validated while serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on 2× DGX Spark (GB10), TP=2: the affected checkpoint failed during startup with the offending layer identified, while a fully FP4 checkpoint loaded successfully.
- The GB10/model checks were not rerun for this rebase.

The rebase includes upstream #55630, which fixes the unrelated CUDA comment formatting that failed the previous pre-commit run.

AI assistance was used to prepare and rebase this PR. The hardware and model validation above was previously reported by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][Hardware][NVIDIA] Add VLLM_DISABLE_CUTEDSL kill-switch for CuTeDSL kernels
body:
## Purpose

Add a `VLLM_DISABLE_CUTEDSL` environment kill-switch for CuTeDSL kernels.

On GB10 (SM12.1), CuTeDSL kernels fail with internal compiler errors (e.g. the DSV4 `fused_indexer_q_cutedsl` indexer kernel), while the non-CuTeDSL fallbacks work fine. Today there is no way to opt out of CuTeDSL when the `cutlass` package is installed — availability probes only check importability, so every affected code path has to be patched by hand.

Changes:

- `vllm/envs.py`: register `VLLM_DISABLE_CUTEDSL` (default off), documented as an escape hatch for platforms where CuTeDSL kernels fail to compile.
- `import_utils.has_cutedsl()`: return `False` when the switch is set — single central gate.
- DSV4 compressor: fall back to the Triton two-stage compressor for `head_dim=512` on CUDA when CuTeDSL is unavailable/disabled (it is the only non-CuTeDSL compressor for that head dim).
- `cute_dsl/ll_bf16.is_available()`: consult `has_cutedsl()` before probing the `cutlass` import, so the cached probe honors the switch.

Not a duplicate: no open PR adds a CuTeDSL opt-out (searched `cutedsl disable`, `VLLM_DISABLE_CUTEDSL`); existing `VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS` only filters quantization kernel classes by name and does not gate CuTeDSL availability probes.

## Test Plan

- `python -m py_compile` on all four touched files.
- End-to-end: 2× DGX Spark (GB10, SM12.1), TP=2, serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with `VLLM_DISABLE_CUTEDSL=1`: verify the Triton two-stage compressor is selected, `ll_bf16` reports unavailable, and no CuTeDSL compilation is attempted.
- Default-path regression: without the env var, behavior is byte-identical (`has_cutedsl()` still just probes the `cutlass` module).

## Test Result

- Before: DSV4 startup on GB10 dies in CuTeDSL internal compiler errors with no opt-out.
- After: `VLLM_DISABLE_CUTEDSL=1` serves DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 stably on 2× DGX Spark GB10 TP=2 via the non-CuTeDSL fallbacks; unset, nothing changes.

---

AI assistance was used for this PR (rebasing from a v0.26.0-based production branch onto `main`, plus moving the env read into `vllm/envs.py` per project convention); every changed line was reviewed and validated end-to-end by the submitter on the hardware above.

title: [Bug] Cross-node TP CUDA-graph replay deadlocks with NCCL 2.28.9 (fixed by NCCL 2.30.4) — watchdog "RPC call to sample_tokens timed out"
body:
### Your current environment

2× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM12.1), connected back-to-back over 200G RoCE. vLLM TP=2 across the two nodes, `mp` distributed executor backend. NCCL 2.28.9 (as shipped). DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With CUDA graphs enabled, serving deadlocks within the first 2–3 requests: a CUDA-graph replay containing NCCL collectives hangs on the cross-node link. The engine watchdog eventually fires with:

```
RPC call to sample_tokens timed out
```

after which the server must be killed. With `--enforce-eager` the identical setup serves indefinitely, which isolated the hang to captured-graph NCCL collectives (not the collectives themselves — eager NCCL is fine under the same traffic).

**Root cause / resolution data point:** upgrading NCCL 2.28.9 → **2.30.4** fixes the deadlock with graphs re-enabled; nothing else changed. So this is the NCCL graph-capture bug class, not a vLLM logic bug — but vLLM can save users days here.

Related: #41725 (same watchdog signature).

### Suggestion

- Document the NCCL ≥2.30.4 requirement for multi-node CUDA-graph capture over RoCE (or gate/warn: if `torch.cuda.nccl.version() < (2,30,4)` and world spans nodes and cudagraphs enabled, log a prominent warning suggesting `--enforce-eager` or an NCCL upgrade).
- The watchdog message could surface "likely collective hang inside CUDA graph replay; try --enforce-eager" as a hint — `sample_tokens timed out` sends users to the sampler, which is innocent.

_Checked before filing: #41725's thread has no NCCL-version discussion; this adds the missing root-cause data point. NCCL versions verified on both nodes: deadlock on 2.28.9, clean on 2.30.4._

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Do not use Dense MHA for GLM-5.2
body:
## Purpose

Fix incorrect short-prefill dispatch in the NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 attention
wrapper.

The generic sparse-MLA metadata path may select dense MHA when a prefill's
sequence length is at most `index_topk`. It then allows the sparse indexer to
skip top-k scoring. `DeepseekV32Attention`, however, only invokes
`forward_mqa`; it does not execute the dense-MHA backend. For a pure prefill
above the backend's decode-like threshold, MQA therefore consumed the cleared
all-`-1` top-k buffer and GLM-5.2 output degenerated into repeated tokens.

This change adds a model-layer dense-prefill capability in addition to the
backend capability. The NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 wrapper declares that it is
MQA-only, so sparse MLA keeps its prefill on top-k MQA and the indexer does not
advertise the dense-MHA scoring skip.

This does not duplicate the open related work:

- #51395 disables dense prefill only for the SM120 sparse-MLA backend.
- #52046 adds a dense branch for the PCP path; the reproduced failure is the
  non-PCP SM100 path.
- #49790 routes DSA architectures to the NVIDIA implementation but does not
  resolve this dispatch mismatch.

Issue #46715 reports a different GLM-5.1 failure at a 65,536-token scheduler
budget and multi-thousand-token prompts on the registered model path.

## Test Plan

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py -q

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v32/attention.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py
```

Real-model validation uses `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`, TP=4, the explicit NVIDIA
DeepSeek-V3.2 class override, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, eager execution, FP32 indexer
logits, GVR disabled, and FlashInfer autotuning disabled. It serially probes
the 128/129-token routing boundary without setting
`sparse_mla_force_mqa=true`.

## Test Result

- Focused pytest: `7 passed`.
- Pre-commit on all three changed files: all hooks passed.
- `compileall` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Before this change, the real model passed through 127 actual prompt tokens
  and failed at 129 and every tested larger prompt through 1,001 tokens. Adding
  only `sparse_mla_force_mqa=true` made all 19 boundary cases pass, causally
  confirming the routing mismatch.
- Patched real-model result: all 19/19 cases passed exact retrieval without the
  force-MQA workaround, spanning 97, 101, 122, 127, 129, 130, 131, 132, 162,
  191, 192, 193, 194, 196, 202, 257, 301, 502, and 1,001 actual prompt tokens.

AI assistance was used to diagnose, implement, test, and draft this change.
The human submitter must review every changed line and understand and defend
the change end-to-end before marking the PR ready for review.
