title: [Feature] Batch-invariant support for speculative decoding
body:
## 1. Summary

This PR extends batch invariance to stochastic speculative decoding. A seeded
request now follows the same sampling and speculative-decoding path when batch
size, request order, or scheduling changes, including KV-cache preemption.

The implementation has two main parts:

~~1. Independent deterministic RNG streams for proposal sampling, acceptance,
   and residual sampling.~~
**Update on 8.27:** RNG-stream separation is handled separately in woosuk/mrv2-draft-gumbel-decouple branch. In particular, [commit 214a205](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/woosuk/mrv2-draft-gumbel-decouple) separates draft Gumbel noise from acceptance/recovery noise. Since that issue is orthogonal to speculative batch invariance, I’ve removed the RNG-domain changes from this PR.

2. Preemption recovery that reconstructs the discarded proposal at the same
   logical boundary before verification.

The validated methods are EAGLE3, DFlash, and DSpark with probabilistic draft
sampling and standard rejection sampling. I didn't find a proper model with MTP to
test, because GDN hasn't been supported with batch-invariance now.

An exact open-PR search for speculative batch invariance found no duplicate.
Related issue: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/27433. Broader searches 
found adjacent batch-invariance and speculative-decoding work,
but none covering this proposal RNG and preemption-recovery design. No issue
number was provided for an issue-specific duplicate check. AI assistance was
used for implementation, review, testing, and documentation. The human
submitter remains responsible for reviewing every changed line and reproducing
the reported tests before submission.

## 2. Method

~~### 2.1 Independent deterministic RNG streams~~

~~Proposal, acceptance, and residual sampling use separate RNG domains. Each draw
is derived from the request seed and its logical token position, so unrelated
requests cannot change its random sequence through batching or scheduling. The
bonus target token continues to use the normal target-sampling stream.~~

### 2.2 Preemption recovery and KV-cache boundary

A speculative proposal spans two scheduler steps: one step creates `K` draft
tokens, and the next verifies those tokens plus one bonus target token. If the
request is preempted between these steps, retaining only the request tokens is
not enough: the proposal and the worker-side hidden state used to create it have
been released.

For example, let the request contain `L = 4` committed tokens:

```text
A B C D
```

Before preemption, the proposal is produced as follows:

```text
execute C -> target hidden state h_C
sample D from h_C
draft from (h_C, D) -> P1 P2
```

The logical state is therefore:

```text
computed tokens:       A B C
sampled next token:          D
pending proposal:              P1 P2
```

On preemption, the scheduler records only the proposal length (`K = 2`) and
uses the normal cleanup path to release KV-cache blocks and worker state. On
recovery it performs:

```text
prefix-cache hit:      A B       # at most L - 2 tokens
replay:                    C     # reconstruct h_C
known next token:             D
regenerate:          (h_C, D) -> P1 P2
verify atomically:               P1 P2 + bonus token
```

An `L - 1` hit would cache `A B C` and skip the forward pass for `C`. Its KV
entries are available, but `h_C`, which the drafter needs, is not. Executing
`D` instead would advance to `h_D` and build the proposal for the next logical
position. Limiting the hit to `L - 2` therefore recreates the same `(h_C, D)`
input and, with the position-based draft RNG stream, the same proposal as the
non-preempted execution. Scheduling the subsequent `K + 1` verification as one
unit prevents another partial boundary from being introduced.

## 3. Evaluation

### 3.1 Serving configuration

The two runs for each method use the same target/speculative model pair and
change only `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`.

| Method | Target model | Speculative model | Speculative tokens |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| EAGLE3 | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` | `RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3` | 3 |
| DFlash | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` | `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16` | 16 |
| DSpark | `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-FP8` | `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7` | 7 |

The command below uses placeholders so that the same serving setup can be
reused for each row.

```bash
export TARGET_MODEL="TARGET_MODEL_ID"
export DRAFT_MODEL="DRAFT_MODEL_ID"
export SPEC_METHOD="eagle3"       # eagle3, dflash, or dspark
export SPEC_TOKENS="3"            # 3, 16, or 7 respectively
export SPEC_CONFIG="{
  \"model\": \"${DRAFT_MODEL}\",
  \"method\": \"${SPEC_METHOD}\",
  \"num_speculative_tokens\": ${SPEC_TOKENS},
  \"draft_sample_method\": \"probabilistic\",
  \"rejection_sample_method\": \"standard\",
  \"enable_adaptive_verification\": false
}"

# BI off
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0 \
vllm serve "$TARGET_MODEL" \
  --max-model-len 2048 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --async-scheduling \
  --speculative-config "$SPEC_CONFIG"

# BI on
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 \
vllm serve "$TARGET_MODEL" \
  --max-model-len 2048 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --async-scheduling \
  --speculative-config "$SPEC_CONFIG"
```

For DSpark, the evaluation added `"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN"` to
`SPEC_CONFIG`. DFlash used `--max-num-seqs 128` for model warmup.

### 3.2 GSM8K end-to-end results

All 1,319 GSM8K test examples were served twice per configuration: concurrency
32 in natural order and concurrency 64 in reverse order. Every request used a
stable unique seed with temperature `0.6`, top-k `20`, top-p `0.95`, and at most
256 output tokens. Exact BI requires identical token IDs, text, and finish
reason between the two phases. Accuracy and throughput below are from the
concurrency-64 phase.

| Method | BI | Exact BI | Mismatches | Accuracy | Req/s | Output tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| EAGLE3 | off | FAIL | 401 | 88.32% | 28.92 | 3468.76 |
| EAGLE3 | on | PASS | 0 | 88.02% | 21.68 | 2614.11 |
| DFlash | off | FAIL | 187 | 87.79% | 11.08 | 1335.24 |
| DFlash | on | PASS | 0 | 87.79% | 10.50 | 1270.43 |
| DSpark | off | FAIL | 118 | 83.17% | 42.67 | 5398.54 |
| DSpark | on | PASS | 0 | 82.94% | 41.28 | 5169.72 |

| Method | Accuracy delta | Req/s delta | Output tok/s delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| EAGLE3 | -0.30 pp | -25.03% | -24.64% |
| DFlash | +0.00 pp | -5.22% | -4.85% |
| DSpark | -0.23 pp | -3.26% | -4.24% |

These throughput runs validate invariance across concurrency and request order;
they did not trigger KV-cache preemption. The focused E2E test below uses a
small KV-cache allocation and asserts that preemption occurred before comparing
serial and batched token IDs.

### 3.3 Minimal tests

The first test checks independent RNG domains, batch splitting, and the target
bonus-token stream. The second forces speculative decoding and KV-cache
preemption, then checks exact batch invariance.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py::test_spec_rng_streams_are_batch_invariant \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_stochastic_batch_invariance.py::test_spec_batch_invariance_with_preemption
```

The E2E test requires one CUDA GPU with at least 32 GB of memory and access to
the configured public model artifacts.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary We found a numerical determinism issue in the Marlin MoE WNA16 path while investigating DeepSeek-V4-Flash. `moe_align_block_size()` may produce different legal orderings of `sorted_token_ids` within blocks assigned to the same expert. Those orderings are semantically equivalent: the same routed tokens are processed by the same experts. However, we observed that Marlin's W13 GEMM can produce slightly different BF16 outputs depending on that within-expert ordering. The numerical differences are very small, but they can propagate through subsequent transformer layers and eventually alter autoregressive generation. ### Isolation We isolated the behavior using a same-forward A/B experiment. Two calls to `moe_wna16_marlin_gemm` used identical: - hidden-state / A input - quantized weights and scales - `expert_ids` - `num_tokens_post_padded` - top-k weights - launch parameters Each call used separately zeroed output and workspace buffers. The only changed input was `sorted_token_ids`: 1. the raw legal ordering produced by the alignment path 2. a deterministic canonical ordering containing the same routed tokens within each expert Across 3 requests and 2 TP ranks, all 6 raw-vs-canonical comparisons produced different W13 output tensors. The geometry where we originally isolated the issue was: ```text M = 8192 K = 4096 N = 2048 top_k = 6 block_size_m = 64 global_num_experts = 256 local_num_experts = 128 ``` ### Numerical magnitude Further experiments localized the permutation sensitivity to the multi-threadblock split-K region. One representative raw-vs-canonical comparison produced: ```text differing BF16 values: 26 max BF16 ULP distance: 4 max absolute difference: 0.0078125 RMS difference: ~1.50e-5 non-finite values: 0 ``` A direct split-K comparison produced: ```text differing BF16 values: 20 max BF16 ULP distance: 4 max absolute difference: 0.00390625 RMS difference: ~6.81e-6 non-finite values: 0 ``` This does not appear to be memory corruption or a gross numerical correctness failure. The magnitude is consistent with ordinary floating-point reduction-order effects. The issue is that two semantically equivalent routed layouts can select different floating-point reduction orderings inside Marlin because their physical block positions differ. ### Expected behavior Equivalent within-expert routed layouts should either: 1. produce a stable result independent of their physical block ordering, or 2. be canonicalized before entering an execution path whose reduction tree depends on that ordering. ### Validated workaround We tested deterministic canonicalization of `sorted_token_ids` within each contiguous expert region after `moe_align_block_size()` and before invoking Marlin. With canonicalization: - expert assignment is unchanged - `expert_ids` are unchanged - `num_tokens_post_padded` is unchanged - expert-map semantics are unchanged - the captured W13 numerical divergence disappears - the downstream layer-0 divergence disappears We have also validated this workaround in our serving environment. We do not think the right characterization is that the split-K scheduler is broken. Our current interpretation is a determinism/contract gap between legal MoE alignment ordering and Marlin's reduction behavior. We can prepare a focused regression test and PR if this interpretation matches the intended Marlin contract. ### AI assistance disclosure AI tools were used during investigation and debugging. The experiments, measurements, and production patch described above were executed and validated on the target hardware. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Summary

Serving Kimi-K3 with TP16 across two 8× B200 nodes (EFA, no NVSwitch/MNNVL),any form of CUDA graph capture produces wrong output or crashes. enforce_eager is correct 100% of the time. Unlike #50147, this reproduces at batch=1 on the first request, with prefix caching disabled and no concurrency. I also tried TP=8 and PP=2, the issue persists

Critically, the FlashInfer fused all-reduce path is disabled on this topology, so the latent-MoE stale-residual fix in #50386 cannot apply here (details below).

Configuration

vllm serve flags:

  • -tensor-parallel-size 16 --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors
    --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA
    --disable-custom-all-reduce --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune
    --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90

env: VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0
VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=0 NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0
VLLM_ENABLE_K3_LATENT_MOE_TAIL_FUSION=0

Prefix caching is OFF. All tests below are single-stream, temperature=0, max_tokens=64, identical prompt.

Failure matrix

cudagraph config | result -- | -- enforce_eager: true | Correct output, every time, across many deploys (TP16 and TP8+PP2) default (FULL_AND_PIECEWISE) | Fluent but semantically random multilingual text; host SIGSEGV in cuGraphLaunch / at::cuda::CUDAGraph::replay() on the 3rd request cudagraph_mode: PIECEWISE | No crash. Deterministic collapse to a single repeated token (@ @ @ ...) from the first request VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 | AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered, surfaced at torch.cuda.set_rng_state during Dynamo tracing

Performance impact

Eager decode is ~2.6 tok/s at batch=1 (64 tokens in ~25 s), closely matching the ~2.7 tok/s eager figure in #50147 against ~85 tok/s with graphs. DSpark speculative decoding recovers this to ~10 tok/s, still far below the graph-enabled figure. Eager is therefore not a viable workaround for latency-sensitive serving, which makes graph capture on this topology effectively blocking.

Questions

  1. Is CUDA graph capture expected to be supported for Kimi-K3 on multi-node TP without NVSwitch, where the FlashInfer fused all-reduce path is inactive and collectives fall back to NCCL over EFA? But I tried TP=8 and PP=2 the issue still persist.
  2. Are there other buffers allocated outside capture in the K3 MoE/KDA paths, analogous to the one fixed in #50386, that would be reached on the non-FlashInfer path?

Reproduction

Serve:

vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 --nnodes 2 --node-rank $RANK \
  --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors \

from openai import OpenAI

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="moonshotai/Kimi-K3",

title: [Bugfix][Core] Make the attention-head / TP divisibility error actionable
body:
## Purpose

Make the attention-head / tensor-parallel divisibility error actionable.

Serving e.g. `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` with `--tensor-parallel-size 3` fails with:

```
Value error, Total number of attention heads (64) must be divisible by tensor parallel size (3).
```

The message states the constraint but not *why* or *what to do instead*, which is what caused the
confusion reported in #52435: users assume the expert-count check is the real blocker, when in fact
64 attention heads simply cannot be sharded across 3 TP ranks.

**Scope note:** this is a different code path from #52446. #52446 fixes the *expert-parallel*
divisibility assert (`n_physical_experts % ep_size`) in `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py`;
this PR only improves the attention-head message in `ModelConfig.verify_with_parallel_config`.

## Change

`vllm/config/model.py::ModelConfig.verify_with_parallel_config` now raises an error that:

- explains that tensor parallelism shards attention heads across ranks,
- lists the valid `--tensor-parallel-size` values (the divisors of the head count),
- and, when the model supports pipeline parallelism, suggests `--pipeline-parallel-size`
  (which shards by layers and has no head-divisibility constraint).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/config/test_head_divisibility_error.py -v
```

## Test Result

<!-- TODO: paste local pytest output -->

## Notes

- Complements the earlier expert-parallel fix (#52446); does not replace it.
- AI-assisted; reviewed by me. DCO `Signed-off-by:` present.

title: [Feature] Allow random dataset to use --dataset-path for realistic token sampling
body:
## Motivation

When benchmarking speculative decoding, the acceptance rate of draft tokens depends heavily on the token distribution of the input. Currently, the `random` dataset in `vllm bench serve` generates purely random token IDs, which do not represent real-world text distributions. This can understate the effectiveness of speculative decoding in production.

On the other hand, the `sharegpt` dataset uses real conversation prompts but does not support `--input-len` to control input length, making it impossible to run benchmarks with a fixed input length using real text.

SGLang's benchmark tool already supports this via `--dataset-name random --dataset-path <sharegpt.json> --random-input-len 8192`, which samples tokens from ShareGPT and truncates/repeats them to the requested length.

## Proposal

Allow `--dataset-name random` to accept `--dataset-path`. When provided, the random dataset samples token IDs from the file and truncates/repeats them to fill `--random-input-len`. File format is auto-detected from the extension:

- `.json` → ShareGPT format (conversations array)
- `.jsonl` → one JSON object per line with a "prompt" field
- `.txt` → plain text, one line per entry

No new CLI arguments are needed. When `--dataset-path` is not provided, the random dataset behaves exactly as before (purely random token IDs).

### Usage

```bash
vllm bench serve \
    --dataset-name random \
    --dataset-path /data/ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json \
    --random-input-len 8192 \
    --random-output-len 1024 \
    --max-concurrency 32 \
    --num-prompts 32
```

### Why not use existing options?

- `--dataset-name random`: supports fixed length but uses purely random tokens, not realistic for speculative decoding benchmarks
- `--dataset-name sharegpt`: uses real text but doesn't support `--input-len`
- `--dataset-name custom`: requires pre-processing ShareGPT into a JSONL file with truncated/padded prompts, which is inconvenient
- `--dataset-name sonnet`: requires a chat template, not compatible with all tokenizers (e.g. DeepSeek-V4)

title: [Spec Decode] Add graph-aware adaptive K for DFlash
body:
## Purpose

Addresses the throughput degradation reported in #49730 when a fixed DFlash
draft length remains enabled after target verification becomes more expensive
than ordinary decoding at larger batches.

This change extends `enable_adaptive_verification` to DFlash and selects a
batch-level K from graph-compatible candidates (`0, 1, 3, 7, 15` for K15).
The policy combines startup-measured drafter/target costs, CUDA graph coverage,
an EMA of accepted-prefix survival, and calibrated shared runtime overhead.
K=0 skips the drafter and trims the current target verification batch to
ordinary decode immediately.

The current PR intentionally does not optimize sampling, the non-causal
drafter, or fuse Qwen3.5 hybrid-GDN/FP8 target verification. H200 profiling
showed target verification is the dominant cost; that kernel-fusion work is a
separate follow-up.

This is not a duplicate of #52522. That PR makes stochastic speculative
decoding batch-invariant and recovers proposals after preemption; it does not
choose K from runtime costs or disable speculation when it is predicted to be
slower. Searches for `49730 in:body`, `DFlash adaptive K`, and `DFlash
performance` found no open PR implementing this policy.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review, testing, and documentation.
The human submitter reviewed the changes and remains responsible for them.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --noconftest \
  tests/test_config.py \
  tests/test_sampling_params.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd_cug.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py \
  -k 'adaptive or dflash or dspark'

SKIP=shellcheck .venv/bin/pre-commit run
```

H200 serving A/B:

- Target: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`, FP8 target path
- Drafter: `z-lab/Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash`, K15
- CUDA graph capture sizes: 1 through 512
- Dataset: GSM8K, 256 prompts, 32 warmups, temperature 0
- Concurrency: 1, 8, 32
- Arms: ordinary decode, fixed K15, automatic K
- Gate: 256/256 complete and zero failures. Fixed K15 must exactly match
  ordinary decode; automatic K must retain at least 99% exact full-text matches
  under the FP8 target path, with the mismatch count reported.

## Test Result

- Focused pytest: `37 passed`
- Staged pre-commit: passed
- H200 A/B (output tokens/s):

  | Concurrency | Ordinary | Fixed K15 | Automatic K |
  |---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | 1 | 340.84 | 583.96 | 557.78 |
  | 8 | 2331.09 | 2387.12 | 2392.29 |
  | 32 | 6863.32 | 4505.21 | 4528.87 |

- At concurrency 32 the policy moved from K15 to K7. Automatic K was 0.53%
  faster than fixed K15, instead of the previous false K0 fallback, while all
  256 outputs exactly matched ordinary decoding.
- All nine cells completed 256/256 requests with zero failures. Automatic K
  exact full-text match rate was 100% at concurrency 1, 8, and 32.
- Ordinary decoding remains faster at concurrency 32. This isolates the next
  optimization to the hybrid-GDN/FP8 target verification path rather than
  sampling or the non-causal drafter.
- Durable H200 result:
  `/threed-code/mokashliu/h200/vllm-dflash-adaptive-k/dflash-adaptive-k-h200-20260817-r30`

title: fix: avoid overlapping stores in XPU KV cache kernel
body:
## Summary

Fix overlapping stores in the DeepSeek V4 XPU qnorm/RoPE KV kernel.

The KV branch previously performed a bulk store across all 512 KV
elements before separately storing the rotated RoPE region. These
stores overlap in the RoPE region and can result in nondeterministic
KV cache contents.

The bulk store is now masked to `NOPE_DIM`, matching the existing
Q-branch pattern:

```python
tl.store(kv_out_base + offs, kv_full, mask=offs < NOPE_DIM)

title: [Bug]: Kimi-K3 silent output corruption in 1P1D NIXL Direct-PD disaggregated deployment
body: ### Summary I am seeing intermittent silent output corruption / garbled generation when serving Kimi-K3 with TP=8 in a 1P1D disaggregated Prefill/Decode deployment using MooncakeStoreConnector together with NixlConnector through MultiConnector. The important A/B observation is: - **NIXL-only PD**: stable, no garbled output observed. - **NIXL + MooncakeStoreConnector through MultiConnector**: garbled output reproducibly appears under sustained load. - **Mooncake enabled + DSpark/speculative decoding disabled**: corruption still reproduces. - **Mooncake disabled**: corruption has not reproduced in my testing. Therefore speculative decoding does not appear to be required to trigger the corruption. The corrupted requests can generate long sequences of nonsensical mixed-language/repeated tokens, for example repeated words such as `Effective/effective` mixed with unrelated English/Chinese fragments. Some affected streams eventually surface at the application layer as HTTP 502 / `7104_UPSTREAM_STREAM_INTERRUPTED`. This looks like a correctness issue rather than a crash-only issue: the engine can continue running while individual outputs are already corrupted. ### Deployment topology Two-node 1P1D deployment: ``` Prefill node Kimi-K3 TP=8 | | NIXL PD transfer v Decode node Kimi-K3 TP=8 ``` Failing configuration additionally uses: ``` Prefill | +-- MultiConnector | +-- NixlConnector | kv_role=kv_producer | +-- MooncakeStoreConnector kv_role=kv_both load_async=true lookup_async=true ``` The Decode node remains a NixlConnector consumer. ### Environment - **Model**: Kimi-K3 - **Tensor parallel size**: 8 - **PD topology**: 1 Prefill + 1 Decode - **KV transfer**: NIXL - **Prefix caching**: enabled - **KV cache dtype**: fp8 - **MLA prefill backend**: FLASHINFER - **VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT**: DS - **vLLM version**: Latest main / nightly - **vLLM commit**: Latest main - **GPU**: 8x NVIDIA B300 - **CUDA**: CUDA 12.8 - **OS / container image**: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 / Container) Relevant upstream fixes included: - #48425: yes (tested on latest main) - #49499: yes (tested on latest main) - #49502: yes (tested on latest main) - #50344: yes (tested on latest main) ### Failing Prefill configuration Relevant environment: ```bash export VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS export VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL=4608 ``` KV connector: ```json KV='{ "kv_connector": "MultiConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "connectors": [ { "kv_connector": "NixlConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail" }, { "kv_connector": "MooncakeStoreConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "load_async": true, "lookup_async": true } } ] } }' ``` Relevant server arguments: ```bash vllm serve /modules/Kimi-K3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config \ '{"mla_prefill_backend":"FLASHINFER","use_prefill_query_quantization":true}' \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --enforce-eager \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --kv-transfer-config "$KV" ``` *(For minimal reproduction, run without `--speculative-config`, as the corruption reproduces without DSpark).* ### Decode configuration The Decode side uses NIXL only: ```bash vllm serve /modules/Kimi-K3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config \ '{"mla_prefill_backend":"FLASHINFER","use_prefill_query_quantization":true}' \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --kv-transfer-config \ '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}' \ --compilation-config \ '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \ --max-num-seqs 32 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 ``` ### Stable control configuration If I remove `MooncakeStoreConnector` / `MultiConnector` and use only: ```json --kv-transfer-config \ '{ "kv_connector": "NixlConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail" }' ``` on the Prefill side, the same Kimi-K3 TP8 PD setup is stable in my testing. The control setup still uses: - Kimi-K3 - TP=8 - prefix caching enabled - FP8 KV cache - FLASHINFER MLA prefill - NIXL PD transfer I have also tested DSpark/speculative decoding in the NIXL-only configuration without observing the same corruption. ### Reproduction A minimal A/B reproduction: 1. **Test A — Control**: - Start Kimi-K3 TP8 Prefill with NixlConnector only. - Start Kimi-K3 TP8 Decode with NixlConnector. - Enable prefix caching. - Run sustained concurrent traffic, including repeated/shared prefixes. - Confirm prefix-cache activity. - **Result**: No corrupted output observed. 2. **Test B — Failing**: - Keep the same model and PD topology, but replace the Prefill connector with `MultiConnector` (`NixlConnector` + `MooncakeStoreConnector`). - Run the same traffic and make sure Mooncake external cache hits are occurring. - **Result**: Intermittent silent output corruption / garbled text. 3. **Test C — DSpark disabled**: - Repeat Test B without any `--speculative-config`. - **Result**: Corruption still reproduces. (Speculative decoding is not the primary trigger). ### Actual behavior Affected generations suddenly degrade into nonsensical output containing repeated and unrelated multilingual tokens. Example pattern: ``` ... effective ... Effective ... effective ... ... random unrelated English words ... ... Chinese fragments ... ... repeated/degenerate text ... ``` The server does not necessarily crash immediately. At the upper service layer, affected streams can end as: ``` HTTP 502 7104_UPSTREAM_STREAM_INTERRUPTED ``` ### Attachments I can provide: - screenshot of a corrupted generation; - Prometheus graphs from the failing run; - Prometheus graphs from the stable/control run; - complete Prefill/Decode logs around an affected request; - Mooncake hit/load metrics; - exact request ID / prompt and response if needed. ### Additional observation about speculative decoding When DSpark is enabled, I have also observed abnormal MTP/spec-decode acceptance behavior during some bad runs. However, I currently consider this a secondary symptom, because the output corruption can still reproduce after DSpark is completely disabled. Therefore this report is specifically about the Mooncake/external hybrid-cache path, rather than the DSpark rejection sampler. ### Expected behavior Loading a prefix from MooncakeStore should be correctness-equivalent to either: 1. recomputing the prefix, or 2. serving the same prefix from local GPU prefix cache. For Kimi-K3, all cache/state groups required to resume generation should represent the same safe token boundary. Enabling Mooncake external caching should not change model output correctness. ### Suspected area The A/B result suggests the issue is somewhere in the interaction between: - Kimi-K3 hybrid cache - `MooncakeStoreConnector` + `MultiConnector` - external prefix cache lookup/load - KDA recurrent state / attention KV reconciliation A possible failure mode would be a resume boundary where the attention KV and KDA recurrent state do not correspond to the same token position. I am particularly interested in whether the following invariant is always guaranteed for Mooncake external hits: ``` reported reusable prefix <= safe Full-Attention/MLA prefix <= valid boundary with corresponding KDA recurrent state ``` and whether all hybrid cache groups are invalidated/reconciled together if one external group is unavailable or has a shorter valid hit. ### Possibly related issues / PRs - #48425 — per-group prefix-hit divergence for hybrid models with KV connector - #49499 — Mooncake TP-sharded Mamba/linear-attention state corruption - #49502 — reliable partial-tail KV offload for sub-block prompts - #50344 — divergent hybrid cache hits scoped to capable connectors / MultiConnector behavior - #47812 — group-aware recovery for KV load failures on hybrid models - #50630 — hybrid recurrent-cache correctness / hit-boundary coordination discussion If my commit already contains them, this may indicate a remaining Kimi-K3-specific or MooncakeStore/MultiConnector-specific correctness path.

title: [ROCm] Enable fused AR draft metadata updates for DeepSeek V4
body:
Builds on vLLM PR #46849, which restores fused multi-step draft decode graphs for autoregressive speculative decoding when every attention backend can update step-dependent draft metadata in place. That PR left DeepSeek V4 ROCm sparse SWA disabled because the AMD path also materializes ROCm-specific ragged SWA indices and indptrs.

Enable the ROCm DeepSeek V4 AITER SparseSWA metadata builder for fused draft decode by refreshing its ragged SWA representation after the generic dense SWA update. The refresh writes directly into the persistent metadata buffers returned by build(), avoiding temporary ragged flat/indptr allocations so captured HIPGraph replay keeps stable tensor storage addresses. Add focused tests for the direct-to-buffer helper and in-place metadata update.

Validation used TP4 on MI355X against patched and control images built from vllm/main@c4e9692. Runtime logs confirmed the patched image used the fused speculator graph path, while control logged fallback because DEEPSEEK_SPARSE_SWA did not support fused multi-step draft decode metadata updates. Smoke, GSM8K, c16, and c128 runs completed with no HIPGraph/cudagraph replay errors, illegal memory access, stale metadata symptoms, or failed benchmark requests.

Serve command shape:
  VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 \
  vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --attention_backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
    --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN"}' \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --distributed-executor-backend mp \
    --max_model_len 4096 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
    --max_num_seqs 256 \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --trust-remote-code

Accuracy command shape:

    --tasks gsm8k \
    --num_fewshot 8 \
    --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash,base_url=http://localhost:<PORT>/v1/completions,num_concurrent=16,tokenized_requests=False

Accuracy results, full GSM8K 8-shot, no limit:
  patched flexible/strict: 0.9492 / 0.9500
  control flexible/strict: 0.9416 / 0.9424

title: [Feature]: Optional content fallback policy for length-truncated reasoning responses
body:
#### Summary

When a DeepSeek V4 generation reaches `max_tokens` before its reasoning block closes, the Chat Completions response has `finish_reason: "length"`, `message.content: null`, and non-empty `message.reasoning`.

vLLM preserves the generated text, so this is not token loss. However, OpenAI-compatible clients that read only `content` present an empty assistant response.

Could vLLM provide a documented, explicit opt-in policy for deployments that prefer non-empty standard content on this path?

The default behavior can remain unchanged. An opt-in is important because copying incomplete reasoning into content can expose chain-of-thought text and can misrepresent an unfinished analysis as a final answer.

#### Relationship to existing work

- #48645 covers naturally completed replies that omit `</think>` and are misclassified as reasoning.
- #50753 proposes `force_nonempty_content` for that natural-stop case and deliberately excludes streaming responses with `finish_reason: "length"`.
- This request concerns whether deployments should have a separate explicit compatibility policy for the length-truncated case.

#### Environment

- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813`
- vLLM release: `0.27.1`
- vLLM nightly: `0.27.2rc1.dev122+g8efa13b70`, commit `8efa13b700f1836657699cae2503dc2feab27fa0`
- Hardware: Linux arm64, 4 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs
- Endpoint: `/v1/chat/completions`
- Parser: `deepseek_v4`
- Direct `vllm serve`, with no proxy or separate response assembler

Material server arguments:

```bash
vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --max-num-seqs 36 \
  --trust-remote-code
```

#### Reproduction

```bash
curl -sS http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813",
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": "Rank these by acidity and justify each comparison from first principles, considering inductive effects, resonance stabilisation, and hybridisation: phenol, ethanol, acetic acid, water, trifluoroacetic acid. Think step by step, then finish with \"the answer is (X)\"."
      }
    ],
    "max_tokens": 256,
    "temperature": 0,
    "chat_template_kwargs": {
      "enable_thinking": true
    }
  }' \
  | jq '.choices[0] | {finish_reason,content:.message.content,reasoning:.message.reasoning}'
```

Observed response shape:

```json
{
  "finish_reason": "length",
  "content": null,
  "reasoning": "<non-empty generated text>"
}
```

#### Results

For vLLM 0.27.1, all 48 requests capped at 256 through 2,048 tokens ended inside reasoning, returned null content, and returned non-empty reasoning.

For nightly `8efa13b70`, all 60 requests capped at 256 through 4,096 tokens had the same result.

At 4,096 tokens on vLLM 0.27.1, every response crossed the reasoning boundary and produced non-empty content. Ten later ended by length and two stopped normally. This shows that the condition is truncation inside reasoning, not any response with `finish_reason: "length"`.

Streaming reproduced the split in both builds. At 256 tokens, 12 of 12 streams per build emitted non-empty reasoning deltas and no non-empty content delta.

With thinking disabled on nightly, 12 of 12 requests at 256 tokens returned non-empty content and empty reasoning.

#### Requested behavior

Please consider one of these outcomes:

1. Document that length-truncated reasoning is available only in `reasoning`, and document that content-only clients must handle this response shape.
2. Add an explicit opt-in compatibility policy that copies or moves length-truncated reasoning into `content`.
3. Expose a terminal indicator that lets clients distinguish an empty answer from a response whose entire generation remains in the reasoning channel.

The option must behave consistently for streaming and non-streaming responses. It must not silently expose incomplete reasoning by default.

#### Duplicate check

I searched the current issue tracker. #48645 and #50753 are related but focus on naturally completed replies that omit the reasoning close marker. This request is limited to an explicit compatibility policy for responses that end by length while still reasoning.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary Running DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 with MRV2 on ROCm with graph mode "FULL_DECODE_ONLY" will cause significant accuracy drop, compared with eager mode / PIECEWISE. ### Environment vLLM version: The lastest upstream vLLM has moved DSv4 back to MRV1, so please use this commit (commit 1f7427bc0ad31fdad1b0933c77ea5acae15da2e0) and apply this PR(#52426) to enable DSv4 with MRV2 on MI350. Start vLLM: ``` VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve /data/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --dtype auto \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --max-num-seqs 512 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --trust-remote-code \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --compilation-config '{"mode": 3, "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' ``` lm_eval command: ``` lm_eval --model local-completions \ --model_args model=/data/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813/,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=128,max_retries=10,max_gen_toks=2048,timeout=60000 \ --batch_size auto \ --tasks gsm8k \ --num_fewshot 8 \ --output_path . ``` **_Please note_**: This lm_eval doesn't disable the default "thinking"=True setting for DSv4, so it may not reflect the real accuracy, but with the same lm_eval command but different server settings (FULL_DECODE_ONLY vs. eager/PIECEWISE), users can observe significant accuracy drop, indicating something bad happening with FULL_DECODE_ONLY. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Recover DeepSeek V4 tool calls with malformed DSML wrappers
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #51914.

DeepSeek V4 can intermittently emit an otherwise complete DSML `<｜DSML｜invoke ...>` block while the outer `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` opener is missing or malformed. One observed `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` variant changes `tool_calls` to `toolcalls`. The current `DeepSeekV4Parser` only enters the tool-call state machine from `CONTENT` or `REASONING` when the exact outer opener is recognized, so the invoke is otherwise returned as text and the structured tool call is lost.

## Relationship to #49117

This PR is a current-`main`, DeepSeek V4-only refinement derived from the orphan-invoke recovery direction developed in #49117. It is not an unrelated competing implementation.

- #49117 covers both DeepSeek V4 and V3.2, foreign-wrapper handling, and additional cross-dialect behavior.
- This PR extracts only the V4 behavior needed for #51914 onto the current ParserEngine implementation.
- It validates names against tools declared by the current request.
- It holds the complete provisional invoke, not only the name, and commits only on the configured `</｜DSML｜invoke>` transition.
- It restores incomplete or rejected candidates to their original content or reasoning state unchanged.
- The normal correctly wrapped path, including its existing compatibility behavior, remains unchanged.

This narrower scope keeps the current-main patch to the parser engine and DeepSeek V4 parser tests.

## Fix

- Add opt-in provisional-start and provisional-commit markers to parser transitions.
- Let DeepSeek V4 treat a bare `<｜DSML｜invoke name="...">` seen from `CONTENT` or `REASONING` as a provisional recovery candidate.
- Buffer its semantic events and raw text instead of emitting a tool call immediately.
- Validate the completed function name against tools declared by the current request.
- Commit only after the DeepSeek V4 `INVOKE_END` transition.
- After committing a recovered invoke, return to `CONTENT` so ordinary suffix text is preserved and any following bare invoke must pass provisional validation again.
- Still absorb an optional outer `TOOL_END` after a recovered invoke.
- Drop unconfigured special tokens before provisional recovery buffering, so EOS and other parser-level drop tokens cannot leak into rolled-back content.
- Preserve provisional recovery while the reasoning adapter is running with `skip_tool_parsing=True`; only a completed, validated invoke ends reasoning and is handed off to the tool parser.
- Synchronize the current request's tools and `tool_choice` into the reasoning-side parser engine before recovery validation, so undeclared tools and `tool_choice="none"` still roll back correctly.
- If `TOOL_END` arrives without `INVOKE_END`, the request has no tools, uses `tool_choice="none"`, names an undeclared tool, or generation ends early, restore the full candidate to its original content or reasoning state.
- Keep the normal wrapped DSML state-machine path unchanged.

The patch deliberately does not normalize specific misspelled wrapper spellings. Recovery anchors on the inner invoke structure, so the same conservative path covers missing and malformed outer openers without expanding a typo allowlist.

## Regression coverage

Recovery coverage is integrated into the existing `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py` suite:

- missing outer start wrapper
- corrupted `tool_calls` to `toolcalls` opener from #51914
- undeclared tool name
- requests with no tools
- parser reuse followed by a request with no tools
- `tool_choice="none"`
- truncated candidate before the tool name completes
- declared tool name with no closing `</｜DSML｜invoke>`
- truncated provisional invoke followed by an EOS drop token
- `</｜DSML｜tool_calls>` without a preceding invoke close
- streaming with the invoke marker split across chunks
- streaming rollback when only the outer tool-call closer arrives
- ordinary trailing content after a recovered invoke with no outer closer
- multiple bare invokes with every declared tool name validated
- an undeclared second invoke remains content instead of bypassing validation through the parallel-call path
- a complete declared bare invoke before a missing `</think>` commits and is handed off to the tool parser
- undeclared, truncated, and `tool_choice="none"` bare invokes before a missing `</think>` remain reasoning instead of becoming user-visible content

## Validation

Parser tests and changed-file checks were run on commit `94ceafb1e7` before the follow-up review fixes:

```text
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py
75 passed

VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/parser/engine
3802 passed

pre-commit run ruff-check --files <changed Python files>
Passed

pre-commit run ruff-format --files <changed Python files>
Passed

pre-commit run typos --files <changed Python files>
Passed

pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <changed Python files>
Passed
```

Follow-up commit `35af231a99` addresses the suffix-preservation and parallel-name-validation review findings and adds focused regression cases to the existing DeepSeek V4 test suite. Commit `c848ab5aa4` addresses the subsequent `DROP_TERMINAL` rollback finding and adds an EOS-leak regression case. Commit `4f2aae22cd` addresses the reasoning-adapter rollback finding and adds serving-style `DelegatingParser` coverage for a valid committed invoke plus undeclared, truncated, and `tool_choice="none"` rollback cases.

The follow-up commits have not yet received upstream code-check results. On the upstream PR, the `pre-commit` workflow stops at the repository contributor gate before code checks run: it requires a `verified`, `ready`, or `ready-run-all-tests` label, or at least four merged PRs by the author. The actual `pre-commit` job is therefore skipped until that gate is opened.

Real-environment validation was also completed on the affected DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 plus DSpark serving stack for the original reported failure family. The original production prompt and tool payload remain private; validation used a sanitized equivalent and confirmed structured tool-call recovery in the affected serving path.

## Scope and tradeoff

A fully formed DSML invoke using a real declared tool name is intentionally recoverable even if the outer wrapper is absent. Prose that reproduces an entire valid invoke for a declared tool is fundamentally ambiguous. Requiring a current-request tool match and a complete invoke bounds the recovery without broad regex repair.

Unknown malformed wrapper text emitted before the inner invoke is not guessed or retracted. The parser recovers the structured invoke while preserving text it cannot safely classify.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to analyze the parser state machine, prepare the implementation, review the provisional-commit conditions, and write regression tests. The affected serving behavior was validated in the reporter's real environment, and the original parser tree was checked with the commands and results above.

title: [Perf] Avoid FlashInfer MLA prefill GPU sync
body:
## Purpose

Avoid a GPU-to-CPU synchronization in FlashInfer MLA prefill planning. FlashInfer's ragged prefill planner needs `qo_indptr` on the host and otherwise calls `.to("cpu")` on the CUDA `query_start_loc` tensor.

Thread the existing host-side prefill query offsets through `MLACommonPrefillMetadata` and pass them as `qo_indptr`. This keeps the values and planner behavior unchanged while avoiding the device-to-host copy and its synchronization.

This does not duplicate an existing PR. Searches for `FlashInfer MLA qo_indptr sync` and `GPU CPU sync FlashInfer prefill` found no matching fix. #51540 addresses a different synchronization in KDA/FLA chunk-index construction.

AI assistance was used to trace the synchronization, implement the change, and prepare tests. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and can explain and defend the change.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py -q

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_mla_prefill_context.py -q

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_mla_prefill_context.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/sparse_mla_attention.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/flashinfer.py
```

## Test Result

- Nearby MLA chunk tests: **11 passed**.
- Kimi-K3 CUDA-only MLA tests: **9 skipped** because no CUDA device is available locally.
- All pre-commit hooks on changed files: **passed**.
- Model evaluations were not run because this changes only the device placement of planner metadata, not model execution or output values.

title: [Rust Frontend] Add Hunyuan A13B reasoning parser
body:
## Purpose

Adds the `hunyuan_a13b` reasoning parser to the Rust frontend, from the parser parity checklist in
#44280. Claimed in-thread before starting.

Hunyuan A13B frames its output differently from every reasoning family already ported here — the
content is wrapped in a section of its own:

```
<think>\n REASONING \n</think>\n<answer>\n CONTENT \n</answer>
```

This is an adaptation of `vllm/reasoning/hunyuan_a13b_reasoning_parser.py` rather than a line-by-line
port, as #44280 asks for. Two findings drove the design.

**1. The delimiters are not vocabulary tokens.** Verified against `tencent/Hunyuan-A13B-Instruct`
(127,957-entry byte-level BPE, empty `added_tokens_decoder`):

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("tencent/Hunyuan-A13B-Instruct", trust_remote_code=True)
print(t.convert_tokens_to_ids("<think>"))   # None — not a vocab token
print(t.tokenize("<think>\n"))              # ['<th', 'ink', '>Ċ']
```

`</think>`, `<answer>` and `</answer>` are all absent too. That is why the Python parser hardcodes
`think_start_ids = [14023, 771, 397]` and eight more literal ID sequences, and it means
`DelimitedReasoningParser::new` cannot construct here at all: it resolves both delimiters through
`token_to_id` and returns `MissingToken` when either is missing.

So `delimited.rs` makes the resolved delimiter IDs `Option<u32>` and adds a `new_text_only`
constructor that skips resolution. `new` and all seven existing callers are untouched and keep passing
real IDs, so no existing parser changes behaviour. This is the same class of problem @rabrooks raised
for `hy_v3` in #44280 — that one was resolvable by reusing the plain `<think>`/`</think>` parser, which
is not an option here (aliasing Hunyuan to `qwen3` yields reasoning `\nR\n` and content
`\n<answer>\nC\n</answer>`, i.e. wrong against the Python spec).

Text matching is not merely a workaround for the missing IDs; it removes a class of upstream
fragility. The Python parser carries `think_start_ids_fast`, `response_start_ids_fast` and
`fast_think_ids` — *parallel* ID sequences for the very same strings — purely because BPE merges
differ by context (`>Ċ` vs `>ĊĊ`). Matching text makes all of that disappear, and it survives tokenizer
revisions, where nine pinned literal IDs would not.

`delimited.rs` gains one other opt-in, `strip_framing_newlines()`, described under "Framing newlines"
below.

Both `delimited.rs` changes are additive and default to the existing behaviour, but I'm happy to take
a different approach if you'd rather not touch that file — the parser is the part that matters.

**2. Prompt-boundary initialization is impossible here, and unnecessary.**
`last_reasoning_boundary` compares token IDs, so with no IDs there is nothing to inspect. It is also
not needed: the model's own `chat_template` has no thinking logic, and
`examples/tool_chat_template_hunyuan_a13b.jinja` prefills `<think>\n\n</think>\n` **only** when
`enable_thinking is false`. With thinking on, the prompt prefills nothing and the model emits
`<think>\n` itself, so text matching with `default_in_reasoning = false` is the faithful behaviour.
`preserve_special_tokens` stays `false` — these are ordinary text, not special tokens.

### Notes for review

- **Delimiter choice.** The parser uses `<think>` and `\n</think>\n<answer>`, stripping the single
  framing newline that opens each section. The obvious alternative — folding the
  newlines into the delimiters as `<think>\n` and `\n</think>\n<answer>\n` — does not work: the shared
  machine's `partial_suffix_len` holds back any buffered suffix that could complete *either*
  delimiter, regardless of which one it is currently looking for. A completed `<think>\n` therefore has
  its trailing newline held back as a possible start of `\n</think>`, and `<think>` alone is emitted as
  content, so reasoning is never entered. It reproduces only when a chunk boundary lands on the
  delimiter, which is why the tests re-feed every case at several chunk sizes. Ending both delimiters
  on `>` avoids the overlap entirely. No existing delimiter pair has it.
- **Framing newlines are stripped inside the shared machine**, via a new opt-in
  `DelimitedReasoningParser::strip_framing_newlines()` that defaults to off, so no existing parser is
  affected. Doing it in the wrapper instead is wrong, and there is a test for why: `ReasoningDelta`
  concatenates every run parsed out of one push, so once two `<think>`->`<answer>` round trips land in
  a single push the per-section boundaries are gone and only the first section's newline is reachable.
  That made `<think>\na\n</think>\n<answer>\nb\n</answer><think>\nc…` yield reasoning `"a\nc"` in one push
  but `"ac"` at every chunk size — a genuinely split-dependent result. Python's state machine cycles
  `response -> idle -> think`, so repeated round trips are a shape it supports and worth getting right.
  Stripping where the boundaries are still visible fixes it, and made the wrapper smaller.
- **Auto-detection is deliberately narrow.** `resolve_name_for_model` is a case-insensitive substring
  scan, so a bare `hunyuan` pattern would also claim `HunyuanOCR` and the dense `Hunyuan-7B-Instruct`,
  which has no thinking mode. `hunyuan-a13b` / `hunyuan_a13b` match the target and nothing else, which
  is the convention the registry already uses (`deepseek-v4`, `step-3p5`, `seed-oss`, `minimax-m3`,
  `kimi-k2`). A test asserts both the match and the two non-matches. My claim comment said I would add
  no matcher at all; on reflection the concern I had there was the bare substring, and a narrow pattern
  avoids it while letting `--reasoning-parser auto` work out of the box.
- **`\n</answer>` handling.** Only the marker is suppressed; a stream that opens another `<think>`
  section afterwards keeps parsing. An incomplete tail such as `\n</ans` at end of stream is emitted as
  content rather than swallowed.
- **One deliberate divergence from Python, on this roadmap's own terms.** With
  `enable_thinking is false`, `tool_chat_template_hunyuan_a13b.jinja` prefills `<think>\n\n</think>\n`
  and stops there, so the model body opens with a bare `<answer>` that is never part of a delimiter.
  Python leaks it into content (`content = "<answer>\nC"`) — its regex makes the `<think>` group
  optional and its token state machine starts in `idle`, so the opener falls through as content in
  both paths. This parser drops it: `reasoning: None, content: "C"`.

  #44280 says it may skip "options that mainly reflect Python frontend implementation details or
  Python-side workarounds", and prefers "adapting the current Rust design over line-by-line Python
  ports". This is that case. It also costs nothing in spec parity: **every case in
  `tests/reasoning/test_hunyuan_reasoning_parser.py` begins with `<think>\n`, or is the bare
  `"This is content"` case — none starts at `<answer>`**, so the prefill path is untested upstream and
  every ported case is byte-identical either way. Tests cover the fix, the split-across-pushes
  hold-back it needs, and content that merely looks like the opener (`<abc>…` passes through).

- **Text after a complete `\n</answer>` keeps streaming as content**, matching Python's streaming path.
  Python's non-streaming regex discards it instead, so the two Python paths disagree with each other;
  streaming is the right match for this trait. Pinned by a test.
- `rust/src/chat/src/lib.rs` is also touched by #52133 (the tool half). Different snapshot line, so a
  textual conflict is unlikely, but it is the one file both PRs edit.
- **`delimited.rs` cannot be split into a commit of its own.** I tried: `new_text_only` and
  `strip_framing_newlines` are `pub(crate)` with no non-test caller until the parser lands, so such a
  commit fails `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` on `dead_code` — `--all-targets` still builds the lib
  without `cfg(test)`, so the tests do not rescue it. The shared-machine change and its only caller
  therefore arrive together.
- **Slightly more permissive than Python at the delimiters.** Python's regexes require the newline —
  `<think>\n` and `\n</think>\n<answer>\n` — whereas this matches `<think>` and `\n</think>\n<answer>`
  and strips the following newline only when it is actually there. So `<think>reason` enters reasoning
  here and does not upstream. Every Python test case carries the newlines, so this changes no ported
  expectation; I preferred the lenient reading because a missing framing newline should not silently
  turn a whole reasoning block into content.
- Python's `is_reasoning_end` and `extract_content_ids` are not ported — the Rust `ReasoningParser`
  trait has no equivalent hooks. Flagged with a `TODO`, matching the existing note in
  `minimax_m2_append_think.rs`.

## Test Plan

```bash
cd rust
cargo nextest run -p vllm-parser
cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat
cargo clippy -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

The Python suite's 18 parametrizations reduce to seven distinct outputs, five of them behaviourally
distinct; the new tests port those five. The two left out are literal variants of ported cases —
`COMPLETE_REASONING_WITH_SYMBOL` only appends `!` to `COMPLETE_REASONING`, and `REASONING_WITH_THINK`
is `MULTIPLE_LINES` on a single line. The Rust tests add streaming coverage that suite lacks: every
case is re-fed at chunk sizes 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11 and must produce the identical reasoning/content
split, plus a delimiter split mid-sequence across pushes, an incomplete `\n</answer>` tail released at
`finish()`, and a prompt-boundary call that must not flip the initial state.

## Test Result

All on `origin/main` @ 8bdc70ec7 plus this branch, CPU-only, macOS aarch64.

```
$ cargo nextest run -p vllm-parser
     Summary [   0.403s] 435 tests run: 435 passed, 0 skipped

$ cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat
     Summary [   7.712s] 310 tests run: 310 passed, 0 skipped

$ cargo clippy -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2.56s

$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
    (no output)
```

Baselines on `origin/main` @ 8bdc70ec7 are 422 (`vllm-parser`) and 308 (`vllm-chat`), so this adds 13
parser tests and 2 registry tests. I also ran the same four commands with the three `vllm-chat` files
reverted, leaving only the parser side: 435 / 308, clippy and fmt clean — `vllm-chat` back at its
baseline, which confirms no existing parser is affected by either `delimited.rs` change.

### Also green on a second platform

Same four commands on `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` (NVIDIA DGX Spark, GB10), measured before the
rebase, on base `49905ad94` (429 / 300 against that base's 416 / 298):

```
$ cargo nextest run -p vllm-parser
     Summary [   0.133s] 429 tests run: 429 passed, 0 skipped

$ cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat
     Summary [   9.899s] 300 tests run: 300 passed, 0 skipped

$ cargo clippy -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 13.84s

$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
    (no output)
```

Identical counts on macOS aarch64 and Linux aarch64 at that revision.

## Not a duplicate

- **`hy_v3` (#53054) is a different parser for a different model.** It landed after this PR opened
  and touches four of the same files, hence the rebase. HY3 is Tencent Hunyuan **v3**: a *unified*
  reasoning+tool parser whose delimiters are tokenizer-derived `<think{suffix}>` / `</think{suffix}>`,
  registered as `hy_v3` via `register_unified_dummy` on the pattern `hy3`. Hunyuan-**A13B** is an
  earlier generation with a different wire format — `<think>\n…\n</think>\n<answer>\n…\n</answer>` —
  a standalone `register_parser`, and the patterns `hunyuan-a13b` / `hunyuan_a13b`. Neither routes
  the other's models, and neither parser's tests change. The rebase adopts #53054's widened
  `DelimitedReasoningParser::new` signature (`&'static str` -> `impl Into<String>`) and threads it
  through the `new_text_only` / `with_token_ids` helpers this PR adds.
- `#44280` — read all 28 comments. No claim on `hunyuan_a13b`; mine is the only one.
- Searched open PRs for `hunyuan` (83 results across all states, 19 open). The only Hunyuan A13B parser
  work is #52133, the **tool** parser. I checked its file list: `parser/src/tool/json/hunyuan_a13b.rs`,
  `parser/src/tool/{json/,}mod.rs`, `chat/src/parser/tool/{mod,tests}.rs` and `chat/src/lib.rs` —
  nothing under `rust/src/parser/src/reasoning/`. The two are complementary halves.
- `grep -ri hunyuan rust/src/` on `origin/main` returns a single hit, an embedded template filename in
  `renderer/hf/format.rs`. No reasoning parser is registered.
- No other open PR touches `rust/src/parser/src/reasoning/delimited.rs`.

## Model evaluation

Not applicable, stated explicitly rather than omitted: this is a CPU-only text state machine in the
frontend's output path. It does not touch model execution, logits, sampling or kernels, and cannot
change generated tokens — it only decides how already-generated text is split between the `reasoning`
and `content` fields of the response. The behavioural contract is pinned by the ported Python test
cases above. **No live Hunyuan A13B serve was run, and I am not claiming one** — the model is 160.8 GB
and I do not have the hardware budget for it.

### Live serving check, with an explicitly labelled stand-in

I did run the parser end to end against a real engine, using **Qwen3-0.6B as a stand-in generator, not
Hunyuan A13B**. vLLM 0.27.1 engine, Rust frontend built from this branch, single GB10:

- `--reasoning-parser hunyuan_a13b` is accepted end to end — Python's `ReasoningParserManager` validates
  the name first, then the Rust registry constructs the parser and the server reaches ready.
  `/version` reports `{"version":"0.27.1","rust_frontend_version":"0.1.0"}` and `/v1/models` reports
  `"owned_by":"vllm-frontend-rs"`, so it is the Rust frontend answering.
- Startup logs `Auto-initialization of reasoning token IDs failed…`. **This is expected and benign** —
  the parser resolves no delimiter token IDs by design, which is the whole point above. The existing
  `minimax_m2_append_think` parser logs the same line for the same reason.
- A request carrying a `tools` array returns 200, so registration does not disturb tool parsing.

The one behaviour a stand-in can exercise is the `<answer>`-opener case from the divergence note, since
a small model will emit that shape on request. Same messages, `temperature 0`, 9 completion tokens in
both runs — only `--reasoning-parser` differs:

| | `qwen3` (control) | `hunyuan_a13b` |
|---|---|---|
| `reasoning` | `null` | `null` |
| `content` | `"<answer>\n4\n</answer>"` | `"4"` |

The control shows what the model actually generated; this parser strips the bare opener, the framing
newline and the trailing `\n</answer>`, which is the documented divergence from Python behaving as
described.

**What the stand-in cannot show:** Qwen3 emits `</think>\n\n<answer>` with two newlines, so it cannot
produce Hunyuan's single-newline frame, and the reasoning/content split for a complete
`<think>…</think><answer>…</answer>` response is covered by the unit tests only — including the
chunk-size sweep, which is stricter than a single live generation would be.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change (Claude Code): to locate the relevant files, draft the parser
and its tests, and draft this description. I ran the verification commands under Test Result myself,
and I also checked that the new tests fail when the behaviour they pin is broken: folding the framing
newline into the `\n</think>\n<answer>` delimiter fails three of them, removing the shared state
machine's newline stripping fails four, and dropping the `hunyuan-a13b` auto-detection pattern fails
exactly one registry test. The second-platform run and the serving check above were run with AI
assistance on my own machines. I reviewed every changed line and can explain and defend the design —
in particular the two findings in the review notes that shaped it: the `partial_suffix_len` delimiter
overlap, which surfaced as a real test failure and drove the delimiter choice, and the
multi-round-trip framing-newline bug, which surfaced as a chunk-size-dependent result and is why
newline stripping ended up in the shared machine rather than in this parser.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Widen eagle lookup query for non-sliding-window groups
body:
> **Draft — scope corrected after further investigation.** This is offered as an *internal
> consistency* fix, not as the cause of any particular symptom. An earlier revision of this
> description overstated the production evidence; corrections are at the bottom.

## The asymmetry

In `OffloadingConnectorScheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens`, an eagle group's hit count is
decremented **unconditionally** once the group is verified:

```python
if is_eagle_unverified:
    num_hit_chunks -= 1
    eagle_verified.add(group_idx)
```

but the compensating query widening — whose own comment says it exists so that extra chunk
*can* be popped — is applied **only to sliding-window groups**:

```python
# For eagle groups, query one extra chunk that will be popped.
# We only need to increase the query size for sliding window groups.
query_max = max_hit_size_tokens
if is_eagle_unverified and sliding_window_size_in_chunks is not None:
    query_max = min(max_hit_size_tokens + tokens_per_chunk, ...)
```

For a **full-attention** eagle group the query is never widened, yet the pop still happens, so
the group returns one chunk fewer than it actually matched.

This is reachable in ordinary configurations, not just DeepSeek-V4. `is_eagle_group` has one
real writer (`_annotate_eagle_groups_deepseek_v4`, gated on `model_version == "deepseek_v4"`),
but when that produces nothing the fallback flags **every** group:

```python
if use_eagle and not eagle_groups:
    eagle_groups = set(range(len(kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups)))
```

and `use_eagle()` is true for `method="mtp"`. So on any MTP model the full-attention group is
an eagle group, takes the non-widened path, and still pays the pop.

## The change

Make the widening unconditional so it matches the unconditional pop, and tie the two sites
together in the comment so they are less likely to drift apart again.

## Scope — what this does NOT claim

The decrement applies to an already-non-zero hit. A total backend miss returns earlier:

```python
if num_hit_chunks == 0:
    return 0          # this precedes the eagle pop
```

So this defect can cost a real hit one chunk, but it cannot turn a zero into a zero. I am
**not** claiming it explains any specific case of "loads never happen" — including our own,
where a simpler explanation is in play (see below).

## Corrections to the first revision of this description

- I wrote that `kv_offload_cpu_cache_usage_perc` "reads 0.0 across 1353 samples". **That was
  wrong.** Re-measured across all four workers: 1873 samples, **177 non-zero** (values around
  0.0008–0.009). I had read the last value and misreported it as the whole series. The gauge
  also nets out evictable blocks, so a low reading is expected for a healthy cache and is not
  evidence of anything.
- I implied this defect was the likely cause of `CPU_to_GPU == 0` on our deployment. That is
  not established. A simpler, MTP-independent explanation fits our numbers: with
  `--kv-offloading-size 128` per engine against 4x62–147 GiB of per-rank GPU KV, our CPU tier
  holds roughly 0.2–0.5x the tokens of the GPU tier in front of it — and the CPU tier is only
  ever queried about chunks the GPU tier missed. Under LRU that region is precisely what it
  cannot hold. We also see zero `lookup_async_delay` samples, consistent with a hard first-key
  miss rather than a clamped hit.

Happy to close this if the intended direction is to handle it via #50507's partial-tail path
(which currently excludes EAGLE with the note "EAGLE and DCP need additional hand-off
semantics"), or to add a test if you can point me at the right harness for multi-group
offload lookups.

title: [ROCm][CI] Handle tied experts in softplus sqrt top-k test
body:
- Uses a stable descending sort in the shared PyTorch reference so equal scores resolve to lower expert IDs, matching the CUDA/ROCm and DeepSeek-V4 kernels.
- Makes top-k cutoff ties an explicit regression case by setting the first real gating row to all zeros instead of relying on accidental low-precision collisions.
- Leaves hash routing unchanged and preserves the existing exact expert-ID, weight, padding, and NaN assertions.

[`torch.topk`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.topk.html) does not guarantee which indices it returns for tied elements, while the vLLM kernels deterministically prefer lower expert IDs. The padding test can therefore report a false expert-ID mismatch when BF16 routing scores tie at the top-k cutoff. The failure has consistently appeared in 384-expert BF16 cases as a single mismatched expert ID with an absolute delta of 115:
- [AMD CI #11834, MI355 MoE Test 3](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11834#019fdfcf-a69f-439e-a7bf-a35ce8955218)
- [AMD CI #11845, MI355 MoE Test 2](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11845#019fe374-ac4a-4f92-bad5-9620658cf9a5)
- [AMD CI #11862, MI355 MoE Test 3](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11862#019fe4e5-8e16-4f8e-b421-bd548b93dcf5)
- [AMD CI #12302, MI355 MoE Kernels Shard 2](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12302#01a0225d-3661-44c5-bae3-ed570d36a9a2)
- [AMD CI #12307, MI355 MoE Kernels Shard 2](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12307#01a02500-419a-4007-b963-dcc3114443cc)

Using `torch.argsort(..., descending=True, stable=True)` makes the reference follow the kernels' intentional tie-break and keeps exact routing validation rather than treating tied experts as interchangeable.
