title: [Performance][MLA] Use FP16 logits for sparse indexer
body:
## Summary

- make the sparse-attention indexer request FP16 logits by default on CUDA,
  with an explicit `float16`/`float32` engine override
- keep DeepGEMM output, local DCP top-k, and every vLLM selector on native FP16
  without widening the materialized logits tensor
- convert two packed FP16 score encodings to ordered keys at once, use exact
  native FP16 refinement, and retune persistent/decode crossover tiers
- remove the experimental BF16 indexer/top-k surface and add rejection,
  correctness, engine-policy, DeepGEMM, DCP, and odd-length coverage
- resolve the configured logits dtype during module construction so worker
  warm-up and inference do not depend on a thread-local config context
- cover DeepSeek-V4 Flash's 64-head MXFP4 indexer in FP16 for both prefill and
  paged MTP decode with exact packed-cache-layout correctness tests

## Why

GLM-5.2's sparse indexer materializes a large logits tensor before selecting
top-k indices. Keeping the tensor and selection native FP16 reduces memory
traffic. `--attention-config.indexer_logits_dtype` accepts `auto`, `float16`,
or `float32`; `auto` chooses FP16 on CUDA and FP32 elsewhere.

The final kernel transforms both packed halves with one 32-bit operation and
reuses the exact keys in histogram and scatter. This reduced the unified
FP16 kernel from 57 to 32 registers/thread at 1,024 rows and raised measured
occupancy from 49.7% to 94.9%.

The dtype is passed as a constant custom-op argument. Resolving it in the
operator body originally failed during real-model warm-up because the worker
callback does not run inside `set_current_vllm_config`; resolving it when the
`SparseAttnIndexer` module is constructed fixes eager warm-up and graph replay.

DeepSeek-V4 Flash's optional MXFP4 indexer cache uses the same FP16 logits path.
The model-specific tests exercise 64 indexer heads, the packed 68-byte cache
layout, and `next_n=3` (MTP=2), comparing both prefill and paged decode against
dequantized MXFP4 references.

## Performance

All selector measurements use captured real-model GLM logits, top-k 2,048,
warmed CUDA graphs, and the repository `.venv`. CUDA events bracket graph
replays and are not captured in the graph. Both the custom top-k and reference
`torch.topk` run on CUDA; CPU transfers occur only in separate pytest failure
diagnostics. Every result was checked against `torch.topk` before timing.

### Production-style fixed 256K decode graph

The logits row stride and captured `max_seq_len` remain 256K while only the
live KV length changes, matching reuse of a maximum-length graph. Entries are
`FP16 us / FP32 us (FP32 / FP16 speedup)`:

| Rows | 10K KV | 50K KV | 100K KV | 200K KV | 256K KV |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4.242 / 4.609 (1.087x) | 7.527 / 9.742 (1.294x) | 8.144 / 10.485 (1.287x) | 9.383 / 12.028 (1.282x) | 9.820 / 12.383 (1.261x) |
| 8 | 4.732 / 5.069 (1.071x) | 7.628 / 10.008 (1.312x) | 8.941 / 11.507 (1.287x) | 11.562 / 14.032 (1.214x) | 12.573 / 15.349 (1.221x) |
| 32 | 4.838 / 5.242 (1.084x) | 9.639 / 12.419 (1.288x) | 13.138 / 16.068 (1.223x) | 18.901 / 22.429 (1.187x) | 21.295 / 25.228 (1.185x) |
| 128 | 5.323 / 5.549 (1.042x) | 17.500 / 19.292 (1.102x) | 27.604 / 29.836 (1.081x) | 47.513 / 66.983 (1.410x) | 56.910 / 85.397 (1.501x) |
| 1,024 | 23.967 / 33.269 (1.388x) | 94.387 / 139.846 (1.482x) | 153.163 / 221.120 (1.444x) | 271.360 / 470.133 (1.733x) | 334.933 / 574.720 (1.716x) |

FP16 is faster in all 25 production-style shapes: 1.042x-1.733x.

### Exact-stride matrix

FP16 speedup over FP32 after retuning the selector:

| Rows | 10K KV | 50K KV | 100K KV | 200K KV |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 1.087x | 1.276x | 1.271x | 1.270x |
| 8 | 1.062x | 1.300x | 1.290x | 1.214x |
| 32 | 1.088x | 1.294x | 1.240x | 1.191x |
| 128 | 1.051x | 1.084x | 1.048x | 1.387x |
| 1,024 | 1.389x | 1.472x | 1.492x | 1.763x |
| 8,192 | 1.528x | 1.627x | 1.628x | 1.839x |
| 16,384 | 1.542x | 1.638x | 1.635x | 1.832x |

FP16 is faster in all 28 exact-stride shapes: 1.048x-1.839x. The packed-key
change invalidated the old decode crossover: persistent now wins through 32K,
and measured row thresholds are 768 for 32K-64K, 512 for 64K-100K, and 1,024
for 100K-131K.

## Accuracy

### End-to-end long-context recall

The final PR code was evaluated with the real `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`
checkpoint and the standard Paul Graham NIAH corpus. The paired runs used TP4,
greedy decoding, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, 2,048-token chunked prefill, one sequence
at a time, eager execution, disabled prefix caching, disabled FlashInfer
autotuning, and no GVR. The only changed engine setting was
`--attention-config.indexer_logits_dtype=float32` versus `float16`.

Each context used needle depths 10%, 50%, and 90%, with two independently
generated seven-digit keys per cell:

| Context | FP32 exact | FP16 exact | Paired identical responses |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 50K | 6/6 | 6/6 | 6/6 |
| 100K | 6/6 | 6/6 | 6/6 |
| 200K | 6/6 | 6/6 | 6/6 |
| 250K | 6/6 | 6/6 | 6/6 |
| **Total** | **24/24** | **24/24** | **24/24** |

Server-reported prompt lengths were 50,000-50,002, 100,001-100,002,
200,002, and 250,001-250,002 tokens. This is deterministic single-needle
retrieval coverage, not a claim that every downstream task is unchanged.

### DeepSeek-V4 Flash FP4 indexer-cache NIAH

The real `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` checkpoint was evaluated with TP4,
MTP=2, FP8 main KV cache, FP16 indexer logits, eager execution, disabled
prefix caching, and disabled FlashInfer autotuning. Both arms used the same
ordinary fused-MoE backend because the local mega-MoE extension has a stale
ABI. The only paired change was an FP8 indexer cache versus
`use_fp4_indexer_cache=true`, which startup resolved to `mxfp4` and
confirmed with `Using MXFP4 indexer cache for Lightning Indexer`.

The standard Paul Graham NIAH corpus used one deterministic seven-digit key
per cell and greedy decoding:

| Context | FP8 indexer exact | FP4 indexer exact | Paired identical responses |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 50K | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| 100K | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| 200K | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| 250K | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| **Total** | **12/12** | **12/12** | **12/12** |

Needle depths were 10%, 50%, and 90%. Server prompt-token counts matched
between paired arms for all 12 cells and ranged from 49,983 to 249,984, so no
prompt was truncated. This is deterministic single-needle retrieval coverage,
not a claim that every downstream task is unchanged. Request latency is not
reported because the control arm absorbed first-use JIT compilation.

### Real-input top-k set recall

To isolate selector-set changes, FP32 logits captured from real GLM decode
for BEAM documents were rounded to FP16 and exact top-2,048 was recomputed.
Recall is `|topk(FP16) intersect topk(FP32)| / 2048`.

Two layer-74 snapshots with 1,024 real rows each and 199,401-199,481 live KV
tokens produced:

| Rows | Mean recall | Median | 1st percentile | Worst row | Mean / max changed indices |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2,048 | **99.9313%** | 99.9512% | 99.8047% | 99.7070% | 1.41 / 6 |

A separate context sweep used two selector positions and 64 real rows per
length:

| Live KV | Mean recall | Worst row | Mean changed indices |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 10K | 100.0000% | 100.0000% | 0.00 |
| 50K | 99.9496% | 99.9023% | 1.03 |
| 100K | 99.9733% | 99.9023% | 0.55 |
| 200K | 99.9428% | 99.8535% | 1.17 |
| **Overall** | **99.9664%** | **99.8535%** | **0.69** |

This recall measurement isolates FP16 score rounding on real distributions;
the end-to-end NIAH table above measures the actual native FP16 DeepGEMM and
top-k execution path.

## Validation

- `cmake --build build/gvr_native_fp16 --target _C_stable_libtorch -j16`
- 65 workspace/backend correctness cases passed, including FP16 odd lengths
- 20 indexer dtype and retuned-selector policy cases passed
- real TP4 GLM launch and warm-up passed for explicit FP32 and FP16 engine
  settings after moving dtype resolution to module construction
- full 1,024-row FP16 equality with CUDA `torch.topk` at 10K, 50K, 100K,
  200K, and 256K with a fixed 256K stride
- all 56 exact-stride and all 50 fixed-stride dtype/shape cells passed
  correctness before CUDA-graph timing
- packed transform exhaustively matched the scalar ordered-key transform for
  all 65,536 FP16 encodings
- real DSV4 TP4 NIAH passed 12/12 with the FP8 indexer cache and 12/12
  with `use_fp4_indexer_cache=true`; all 12 paired responses were identical
- all 12 DeepGEMM attention cases passed on GB200, including 64-head DSV4
  MXFP4-to-FP16 prefill and paged `next_n=3` decode against dequantized
  references; 2 full DCP FP16/FP32 decode-parity cases passed earlier
- `SWEEP_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1,8,32,256 SWEEP_NUM_PROMPTS_FACTOR=3 bash
  ../glm_bench.sh` and a matched concurrency-1,024 factor-1 run completed
  1,915 requests per dtype with no failures
- all applicable pre-commit hooks on the PR changes passed

`uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto` was attempted. The full editable
build is currently blocked on unmodified current-main QUTLASS code including
ATen extension headers while `TORCH_TARGET_VERSION` is defined; both changed
CUDA targets build successfully.

## Duplicate-work check

This does not duplicate #52149, which fixes persistent top-k candidate
overflow, or #48726, which adds an opt-in fused DSA indexer/top-k path. This PR
changes dtype production and native selection for the existing materialized-
logits path, including DeepGEMM and DCP.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to implement and benchmark this change. Before this
draft is marked ready, the submitting human must review every changed line,
reproduce the relevant validation, and be prepared to explain and defend the
change end-to-end.

title: Integrate DeepGEMM NVFP4 MegaMoE with fused shared experts
body:
## Summary

Add a ModelOpt NVFP4 MegaMoE path backed by DeepGEMM, including fused BF16 shared-expert execution.

- Quantize NVFP4 activations and stage activation/scales/top-k directly into the symmetric buffer in one Triton launch.
- Transform routed NVFP4 weights/scales into the DeepGEMM layout.
- Fuse compatible BF16 shared experts; keep the ordinary shared path for unsupported modules.
- Keep symmetric-buffer allocation/rendezvous outside forward and CUDA Graph capture.
- Fail closed for unsupported router semantics, dtype, bias, LoRA, alignment, platform, DBO, or missing DeepGEMM APIs.
- Preserve the existing ModelOpt path unless `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` is selected.

Requires a DeepGEMM build containing the NVFP4 MegaMoE APIs from the merged [deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#409](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/409).

### Why this is not a duplicate

The related open Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4 changes target model-specific paths; this PR is the only open change integrating NVFP4 MegaMoE with the ModelOpt/RoutedExperts path used by GLM-5.2.

### Design and review fixes

- Replaced `scaled_fp4_quant` plus temporary tensors and four `copy_` calls with direct-to-symmetric-buffer NVFP4 staging.
- Folded FP4 quantization, E4M3 scale packing, top-k conversion, and padding masking into one launch.
- Cached the reciprocal activation global scale outside forward.
- Added fail-closed handling for `apply_router_weight_on_input` and other unsupported configurations.
- Restricted shared fusion to modules whose semantics are preserved; otherwise shared execution remains unfused.
- Fixed the real startup contract found on GB300: router IDs may be `int32` or `int64`, while the symmetric `topk_idx` output is `int64`.
- Expanded contract, padding, dtype, H=6144, and CUDA Graph replay tests.

## Test Plan

### Environment

- 8x GB300, two hosts x four GPUs, DP8/EP8 and TP1.
- Model: `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`.
- CUDA 13, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, FlashInfer `0.6.15.post1`.
- vLLM V2 model runner with compilation mode 0 (no `torch.compile`).
- FULL CUDA Graph requested; sparse MLA selects `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` at runtime.
- Maximum sequences per rank: 1024; maximum batched tokens: 16,384; prefix caching disabled.
- Performance revision: `8d37d14`; current PR head: `70a04c5`. The later commits update tests, the runtime output-dtype contract check, and add a fail-closed guard for TP-sharded shared experts; they do not change the timed DP8/EP8, TP1 path.
- DeepGEMM revision: `0c067ed4` from the dependent PR.

### Serve recipe

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --max-num-seqs 1024 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL"}'
```

For the FlashInfer baseline, replace `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` with `--moe-backend auto --all2all-backend flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided`.

### Workload and measurement

- [NVIDIA SPEED-Bench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/SPEED-Bench) `throughput_16k`, `low_entropy` category. Download it with:

  ```bash
  curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Skills/refs/heads/main/nemo_skills/dataset/speed-bench/prepare.py | \
    python3 - --config throughput_16k --output_dir ./speed-bench
  ```

- Deterministically sample exact 128-token windows across source rows without replacement. Each point uses `8 * M` distinct prompts.
- ISL `128`, OSL `256`, `temperature=0`, `ignore_eos=true`.
- M/rank: `1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024`; global request concurrency is `8 * M`.
- Send exactly M requests directly to each rank endpoint. Warm each point with one short request per rank, then run two formal repeats. The final DeepGEMM M1024 point uses three repeats.
- For each repeat, measure the common steady-decode interval from the latest first-token timestamp to the earliest request-completion timestamp. Count streamed output tokens in that interval and report aggregate throughput across all eight ranks. The table reports the median repeat.
- Model loading, JIT compilation, backend autotuning, CUDA Graph capture, prefill, first-token latency, and drain are outside the measured window.

## Test Results

### D-only: SPEED-Bench low entropy, 128 input / 256 output, DEP8

| M/rank | FlashInfer baseline (tok/s) | DeepGEMM fused (tok/s) | Change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 532 | 560 | **+5.12%** |
| 2 | 982 | 1,030 | **+4.84%** |
| 4 | 1,778 | 1,860 | **+4.61%** |
| 8 | 3,227 | 3,404 | **+5.49%** |
| 16 | 6,182 | 6,533 | **+5.67%** |
| 32 | 11,787 | 12,422 | **+5.38%** |
| 64 | 22,040 | 23,606 | **+7.10%** |
| 128 | 41,878 | 44,571 | **+6.43%** |
| 256 | 68,145 | 76,152 | **+11.75%** |
| 512 | 96,883 | 108,828 | **+12.33%** |
| 1024 | 104,228 | 117,379 | **+12.62%** |


### P-only: random prompts, OSL=1, GB300 PCP8/EP8

| ISL | FlashInfer req/s | DeepGEMM req/s | Throughput gain | FlashInfer p50 TTFT | DeepGEMM p50 TTFT | p50 TTFT |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1K | 39.601 | 55.249 | **+39.51%** | 402.807 ms | 288.575 ms | **-28.36%** |
| 2K | 27.004 | 37.990 | **+40.68%** | 592.267 ms | 421.739 ms | **-28.79%** |
| 4K | 20.329 | 26.193 | **+28.84%** | 776.873 ms | 604.094 ms | **-22.24%** |
| 8K | 10.089 | 12.815 | **+27.01%** | 1539.304 ms | 1221.353 ms | **-20.66%** |

Every point completed all formal requests with zero failures. The initial sweep showed +38.12%/+41.91%/+29.93%/+28.72% throughput for 1K/2K/4K/8K; the repeat preserved the direction and magnitude at every point. Because `long_prefill_token_threshold=4096`, the 8K prompts were chunked; this flag was identical in both arms.

#### P-only serve recipe

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --enforce-eager \
  --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --max-model-len 9216 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --long-prefill-token-threshold 4096 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

For the FlashInfer baseline, replace `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` with `--moe-backend auto`; all other serving flags are identical.

### Routing-imbalance sensitivity

The imbalance factor `x` is the busiest destination rank's received routed slots divided by the mean received slots across the eight destination ranks:

```text
x = max(slots_received_by_rank) / mean(slots_received_by_rank)
```

Thus, `1x` is perfectly balanced, while `2x`, `4x`, and `7x` mean that the busiest rank receives 2, 4, or 7 times the average routed slots. 
| Destination imbalance | DG gain at M32 | DG gain at M64 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1x | **+18.26%** | **+19.95%** |
| 2x | **+17.61%** | **+19.53%** |
| 4x | **+4.83%** | **+7.82%** |
| 7x | **-25.76%** | **-28.36%** |

## Accuracy

| Validation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| B300 dense PyTorch-reference UT | **PASS** on all eight ranks; relative output differences `1.49e-6` to `2.16e-6` with finite outputs and per-expert alpha/A2 scale paths |
| B300 full-size fusion-order test | Fused versus unfused output was exactly identical; deliberately wrong `(routed + shared) * 2.5` ordering differed by `0.2979`, validating `routed * 2.5 + shared` |
| Targeted GB300 integration smoke | **PASS**: M=1 `int32` IDs, M=8 `int64` IDs, and semantic guards |
| Targeted vLLM GPU tests | **16/16 passed** |
| DeepGEMM boundary/adversarial | **42/42 passed**, M/rank 1-2048, max rel-L2 `0.005421` |
| DeepGEMM random fuzz | **22/22 passed**, M/rank 3-3073, max rel-L2 `0.002655` |
| DeepGEMM shared-only | **10/10 passed**, max rel-L2 `0.001134` |
| Real GLM-5.2 MoE layer replays | **75/75 passed**; fused was closer to FP32 in 69/75 layers |
| Deterministic E2E prompts | **16/16 exact** for each arm across two runs |
| 700-repeat long-context probe | All three arms produced the same token sequence and content |
| Initial paired GSM8K canary, fixed 100 questions, 5-shot | FI **93%**, DG fused **93%**; invalid responses **0%** in both arms |
| GSM8K, 100 questions, 5-shot | FI **95%**, DG unfused **94%**, DG fused **95%**; invalid responses **0%** |


<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR.
- [x] The test plan and commands.
- [x] The model-evaluation and performance results.
- [ ] (Optional) Documentation updates.
</details>




## Contribution notes

- AI assistance was used during implementation, debugging, review, benchmark analysis, and preparation of this PR description. The human submitter must review and understand every changed line and verify the final commands and results before merge.

title: [Bugfix][Optimization] Zero packed KV blocks once from the backing sorage base
body:
## Problem

`KVBlockZeroer` builds one segment per aliased layer view of a packed
block-first KV cache (e.g. DeepSeek V4). Each segment starts at the layer
view's `data_ptr()`. Packed views are created by `_reshape_attention_kv_cache`:

    kv_cache = kv_raw_tensor.view(-1, block_stride)[:, offset : offset + page_bytes]

For such a view:

- `kv.data_ptr()` includes the layer's per-block byte `offset`
- `kv.stride(block_dim) * element_size()` is the whole slab's per-block
  stride, not this layer's page size

Starting a segment at `data_ptr()` therefore zeroes:

    backing_base + layer_offset + block_id * block_stride

which has two failure modes:

1. **Out-of-bounds write** — for `layer_offset > 0`, the last blocks walk past
   the end of the backing allocation (CUDA illegal memory access), reproduced
   as `block_id = num_blocks - 1` failing while `num_blocks - 2` is safe.
2. **Cross-layer stomp** — even in bounds, the cleared range is shifted by
   `layer_offset`, overwriting a neighbouring layer's KV (session corruption).

## Fix

Root every segment at the backing storage base and deduplicate on the storage
pointer so each packed slab is zeroed exactly once, and make the cleared span
cover the whole block stride:

1. `dp = kv.untyped_storage().data_ptr()` — strips the per-block layer offset.
2. deduplicate on `dp` (storage base) — one segment per packed slab.
3. `seg_page_sizes` uses `block_stride_bytes` instead of the single-layer
   `kernel_page_bytes` — a single segment clears every interleaved layer.

All three changes are required together: starting at the storage base without
widening the span would clear only the first layer, and widening the span
without rooting at the storage base would shift the cleared region.

## Correctness

| layout | storage base | span | dedup | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| packed block-first | != data_ptr | whole block | 1 seg / slab | clears all layers, no OOB |
| standalone allocation | == data_ptr | == page size | 1 seg / layer | unchanged |
| K/V-first (block_dim=1) | == data_ptr | == page size | K/V segments | unchanged |
| page-aligned (ROCm) | == data_ptr | == page size | unchanged | unchanged |

The key invariant is that `kv.stride(block_dim) * element_size()` always equals
the full byte span of one logical block: the sum of all layer pages for packed
views, and the single-layer page size for standalone allocations. Setting
`seg_page_sizes == seg_block_strides == block_stride_bytes // 4` therefore clears
exactly one whole block per segment.

## Performance

The kernel grid becomes `(n_blocks, n_segs, max_chunks)` where `max_chunks` grows
from `single_layer_page / blk_size` to `block_stride / blk_size`. Total kernel
programs are unchanged (`N_layers x small` -> `1 x large`), but the number of
kernel launches per zeroing step drops from `N_layers` to 1.

## Test

- `test_packed_slab_dedup_clears_whole_block` — two layers sharing a packed
  backing yield a single segment rooted at the storage base with `block_stride`
  as the cleared span; zeroing the last block clears the whole block.
- `test_packed_segment_zeros_whole_block_from_storage_base` (replaces
  `test_packed_segment_zeros_only_its_last_block_page`) — verifies a packed
  segment rooted at the storage base clears the full block stride, not a single
  layer's page.

## Relationship to #50276

#50276 (already merged) splits block stride from page span but keeps per-layer
segments starting at `data_ptr()`. This PR is a complementary alternative: it
collapses the per-layer segments of a packed slab into one whole-block segment
rooted at the storage base. This both removes the offset-based OOB/stomp hazard
and reduces zeroing launches from `N_layers` to 1. The two approaches are
mutually exclusive for packed views; this PR does not layer on top of #50276 but
replaces the per-layer segment construction for the packed case.

title: [Bug]: Missing `has_cutedsl()` guard in `DeepseekCompressor` (head_dim == 512 path)
body:
### Your current environment

cant share this at the moment.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Summary
In the DeepSeek V4 `DeepseekCompressor` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/compressor.py`), the CuTe DSL kernel path for `head_dim == 512` is selected without checking `has_cutedsl()`. Every other DeepSeek V4 CUDA/DS kernel selection site in the repo gates on `has_cutedsl()`, so this looks like an inconsistency that was missed in one spot.

### Where the guard is already established
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/cache_utils.py:412` -> `if has_cutedsl():`
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/fused_indexer_q.py:353` and `:422` -> `if has_cutedsl():`
- `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py:57` -> `if not has_cutedsl():`
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/__init__.py` explicitly documents that leaf modules must only be imported under a `has_cutedsl()`/`is_cuda()` gate.

### The missing guard
`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/compressor.py` currently uses:

```python
if current_platform.is_cuda() and self.head_dim == 512:
```

which unconditionally selects the CuTe DSL compressor (`compress_norm_rope_store_cutedsl`), even when the optional `cutlass` (CuTe DSL) package is not importable.

### Suggested change
```python
if current_platform.is_cuda() and self.head_dim == 512 and has_cutedsl():
```

with the existing import (`from vllm.utils.import_utils import has_cutedsl`) added if not already present.

### Why it matters
- On builds where `cutlass`/CuTe DSL is not available, the `head_dim == 512` compressor path currently fails at kernel dispatch even though the framework already supports a graceful Triton fallback and the rest of the DSv4 ops check `has_cutedsl()`.
- Consistent with the established pattern in the same feature area.

### Environment (for reference)
This was found while building/running vLLM 0.26 for an H200 (sm_90a) target where the optional CuTe DSL package is not shipped.

title: [Bug] DeepseekV4 cannot start on sm_121 (GB10): DeepGEMM assumed available, with no working fallback path
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `0.26.1rc1.dev608+g99a10304d` (container image, aarch64)
- 2× NVIDIA GB10 (**sm_121**, 121 GiB unified memory each), CUDA 13.0, driver 580.173.02
- Two-node TP=2 via the built-in multi-node `mp` executor (`--nnodes 2 --node-rank {0,1} --master-addr … --distributed-executor-backend mp`, rank 1 `--headless`)
- Model: `MJPansa/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-NVFP4` (mixed precision: routed experts NVFP4, attention / shared experts / head not quantized)
- `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` and `VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` are set

Other models start and serve fine on the same two-node setup with the same image (Qwen3-235B-A22B-NVFP4, Mistral-Small-4-119B, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8), so the cluster wiring itself is good.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

DeepseekV4 cannot start on sm_121. There are two separate architecture gates that report "supported" and then fail inside compiled kernels.

**1. `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang` calls DeepGEMM unconditionally**

`vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang.py` has three call sites for `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`. Two of them are guarded:

```python
use_deep_gemm = is_deep_gemm_supported()
...
if use_deep_gemm:
    tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm(...)
else:
    _tilelang_hc_prenorm_gemm(...)
```

The third one, inside `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang` (the first-layer 2-D input path taken from `models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py`), is not:

```python
from vllm.utils.deep_gemm import tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm

tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm(
    residual_flat, fn_broadcast, gemm_out_mul, gemm_out_sqrsum, n_splits,
)
```

On sm_121 this aborts during `determine_available_memory`:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'Assertion error
(/workspace/.deps/deepgemm-src/csrc/apis/hyperconnection.hpp:56): Unsupported architecture'
```

The shipped DeepGEMM extension only contains kernels for two architectures:

```
$ strings vllm/third_party/deep_gemm/_C.cpython-312-aarch64-linux-gnu.so | grep -oE 'sm[0-9]{2,3}' | sort -u
sm100
sm90
```

Note this happens **even with `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`**. That env var does work — `is_deep_gemm_supported()` returns `False` with it set and `True` without it — but this call site never consults it.

A fix that works: guard the call and fall back to `_torch_hc_prenorm_gemm`, which already exists in the same file and implements exactly this contract (`out[0] = x.float() @ fn.t()`, `sqrsum[0] = x.float().square().sum(-1)`); the broadcast shapes line up as-is. It requires a single split, so `n_splits` has to be forced to 1 on the fallback path before the output tensors are allocated. With that patch the model loads all 48 shards and gets past this point.

**2. `CutlassScaledMM.is_supported()` ignores compute capability**

Past the first issue, DeepseekV4's attention input projections fail:

```
File "vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py", line 493, in _run_parallel_input_projections
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py", line 461, in apply
File "vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/BlockScaledMMLinearKernel.py", line 132, in apply_weights
File "vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/cutlass.py", line 320, in apply_block_scaled_mm
RuntimeError: dispatch_scaled_mm,
/workspace/csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/c3x/scaled_mm_helper.hpp:17
```

The selection gate in `kernels/linear/scaled_mm/cutlass.py` is:

```python
@classmethod
def is_supported(cls, compute_capability: int | None = None) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
    if not current_platform.is_cuda():
        return False, "requires CUDA."
    return True, None
```

`compute_capability` is accepted and never used, so the CUTLASS c3x kernel is selected on any CUDA device and then rejects sm_121 in the C++ dispatcher. A Triton implementation exists in the same directory, but `use_triton` on `BlockScaledMMLinearKernel` only affects the input-quantisation step, not the matmul, and there is no env var to override the backend choice.

### Suggested fix

Both gates should consult compute capability rather than assuming Hopper/datacenter-Blackwell:

- `CutlassScaledMM.is_supported()` should return `False` on architectures without the compiled c3x kernels so selection can fall through to the Triton kernel.
- `is_deep_gemm_supported()` should reflect the architectures actually compiled into the extension (currently sm90/sm100), not just the env var — otherwise every DeepGEMM call site needs to be individually correct.
- `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang` should be guarded like its two siblings regardless.

Happy to open a PR for the `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang` guard if that shape of fix is acceptable.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Guard DeepSeek V4 compressor CuTe DSL dispatch
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52710.

The DeepSeek V4 compressor imported the optional CUDA CuTe DSL implementation
unconditionally for `head_dim == 512`. Builds without CuTe DSL therefore failed
at dispatch.

The fallback must also respect the cache layout. The Triton compressor writes
the packed `fp8_ds_mla` representation (`torch.uint8`); it is not compatible
with FlashInfer's plain BF16 or per-tensor FP8 cache rows. This change therefore:

- uses CuTe DSL when it is available on CUDA;
- permits the Triton fallback only for packed `torch.uint8` cache rows; and
- raises a clear error for plain BF16/per-tensor FP8 rows without CuTe DSL.

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR addresses this issue.

## Test Plan

- Execute `DeepseekCompressor.forward` with CuTe DSL unavailable for packed
  `uint8`, plain BF16, and plain FP8 E4M3 cache rows.
- Assert the plain layouts fail before the Triton callable can launch.
- Assert the packed layout dispatches to Triton.
- On SM89+, execute the real packed Triton writer against a 584-byte cache row
  followed by a sentinel guard region and verify the guard is unchanged.
- Run the Python-specific pre-commit lint and formatting hooks.

## Test Result

- RTX 3050 (SM86), driver 610.88, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130:
  - plain BF16 forward rejection: **passed**
  - plain FP8 E4M3 forward rejection: **passed**
  - packed `uint8` forward dispatch: **passed**
  - real packed FP8 write with overrun sentinel: **skipped**, because native
    FP8 E4M3 conversion requires SM89+
- Focused pytest result: **3 passed, 1 skipped**
- Kaggle probe: Tesla P100 (SM60), also below the SM89 requirement
- `pre-commit run ruff-check --files ...`: **passed**
- `pre-commit run ruff-format --files ...`: **passed**
- `git diff origin/main...HEAD --check`: **passed**

The SM89+-gated sentinel test is included for Ada/Hopper/Blackwell CI.

## Model evaluation

Not run. This change does not modify model math, kernels, output values, or model
loading. It restricts dispatch according to the existing cache representation
and prevents an incompatible writer from receiving plain cache rows.

No documentation update is needed because this fixes internal optional-kernel
dispatch without changing the public interface.

AI assistance was used for the implementation. I reviewed every change.

title: [5/N] Share HiSparse host cache across TP ranks
body:
## Summary
This PR optimizes #51324 with the following improvements:
- Resolve shared/private Host pool mode in the KV cache planner.
- Fall back to private pools when the Indexer block layout cannot be represented
  by the shared mmap layout.
- Propagate the resolved mode and physical Host block stride through
  `KVCacheConfig`.
- Roll back the shared Host region when GPU KV allocation or HiSparse worker
  initialization fails.
- Check physical Host RAM only in the shared mmap creator process.
- Fail joiners promptly when the creator fails and unlinks an incomplete mmap.
- Add real multiprocess same-slot visibility coverage.
- Clarify logical versus physical `host_pool_gib` capacity and startup logging.

This is intentionally based on `feat/hisparse-metrics` so it remains the [6/N] change in the HiSparse stack.

cc @MatthewBonanni

title: [Feature][KV Offload] Add capacity-bound LRU eviction to FileSystemTierManager
body:
## Motivation

The `FileSystemTierManager` secondary tier currently grows without bound: every completed KV block is written to disk on store and **no code path ever deletes a block file**. On long-running servers, multi-turn sessions, or shared `root_dir` deployments this means stale blocks accumulate until the filesystem fills up.

Two concrete scenarios hit this:

1. **Context compaction**: when a client compacts a long conversation (e.g. summarizes and drops earlier turns), the KV blocks for the discarded tokens become permanently unreachable — no future prompt can hit them (blocks are content-addressed by hash), yet they stay on disk forever. This is not recoverable by the engine itself, since a request finishing only clears the *lookup index*, not the files.
2. **Shared PVC / multi-instance**: with a shared `root_dir` (documented cross-process sharing), instances keep adding blocks over time with no reclamation.

There is prior art in the ecosystem (LMCache has LRU/LFU eviction on its disk backend; Mooncake has capacity-driven SSD offload), but vLLM's native fs tier has no equivalent. A previous attempt (#43725, "Toy Evictors for FS Offloading") was closed by the author without merging.

## What this PR does

Adds an optional **`capacity_bytes`** config key to the fs tier. When set:

- **LRU tracking**: the tier maintains insertion order per stored block; `lookup()` hits, `touch()`, and completed promotions (`submit_load` completions) move a block to the MRU end.
- **Bounded eviction**: after each completed store job, if total on-disk usage exceeds `capacity_bytes`, the least-recently-used block files are deleted until usage drops to **90% of the bound** (hysteresis avoids thrashing at the boundary).
- **Startup indexing**: existing block files left by previous runs sharing `root_dir` are scanned and counted at construction, so capacity accounting covers the full on-disk state — not just blocks this process wrote. Files are ordered by mtime so old blocks evict first.
- **Safety**: blocks with an in-flight load (`_in_flight_loads`) are never evicted. Deletion is idempotent (`delete_block` ignores missing files), and eviction races with concurrent `os.path.exists` lookups are harmless (a miss just triggers recomputation).
- **Observability**: evictions emit the existing `OffloadingEvent(removed=True)` payload when KV events are enabled, and log the count/bytes freed.

Default remains `None` (unbounded), so existing deployments are unaffected.

## Design rationale

- **Why LRU, not reference counting?** Disk blocks are content-addressed: a block's usefulness is "how likely is the same token content to appear again", which is not tied to any single request's lifecycle. Compacted-away blocks die by *never being looked up again*, so LRU-by-last-access is the natural fit; hot shared prefixes (system prompts) stay resident.
- **Why a watermark (90%) instead of evicting to exactly the bound?** Avoids repeated eviction of the boundary block when stores trickle in.
- **Why track bytes in-process instead of `du`?** `du` is O(files) on every store; an in-process counter with `os.path.getsize` only at store/evict time is O(1) per block and stays consistent with the filesystem because `store_block`/`batch_store_block` skip already-existing files (so size is added once per key).

## Config example

```json
{
  "kv_connector": "OffloadingConnector",
  "kv_role": "kv_both",
  "kv_connector_extra_config": {
    "spec_name": "TieringOffloadingSpec",
    "cpu_bytes_to_use": 68719476736,
    "secondary_tiers": [
      {
        "type": "fs",
        "root_dir": "/mnt/kv_cache",
        "n_read_threads": 32,
        "n_write_threads": 16,
        "capacity_bytes": 107374182400
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Verification

- **Unit tests** (`tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_fs_tier.py`):
  - `test_capacity_evicts_oldest_blocks`: stores 5 blocks with capacity for 3, asserts only the 3 newest remain on disk; then `touch()`es one and asserts it survives the next eviction while the untouched ones are evicted down to the 90% watermark.
  - `test_capacity_indexes_existing_files`: writes 2 blocks with one tier instance (no bound), then constructs a second instance with a 1-block bound over the same `root_dir` and asserts the pre-existing files are counted and evicted on the first store.
- **End-to-end** (local, vLLM 0.26.0 + Qwen3.8-27B, 2 GB bound): a burst of long-context requests produced 41 block files / 2.0 GB on disk with usage clamped at the 90% watermark:
  ```
  FileSystemTierManager: evicted 7 block(s) (359661568 bytes); usage now 1901068288 / 2147483648 bytes
  FileSystemTierManager: evicted 8 block(s) (411041792 bytes); usage now 1901068288 / 2147483648 bytes
  ```
  Without a bound, the same workload accumulated blocks monotonically; with the bound, disk usage stayed flat at ~1.9 GB while requests kept succeeding.

## Notes / follow-ups

- The eviction policy is a fixed LRU. A custom policy hook (mirroring the primary tier's pluggable `CachePolicy`) could be a follow-up if needed.
- `capacity_bytes` is a soft bound: because stores are async, a burst can overshoot by one in-flight job's worth of blocks before eviction catches up (bounded by `blocks_per_chunk` per job).
- Per-run digests (model/config hash) already isolate eviction to the correct run directory.

title: [Feature][DSpark]: Enable varlen for GLM-5.x/DSV3.2 (Sparse MLA)
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Adaptive verification has a firm requirement that the attention backend must not use the CPU-side query lengths as a source-of-truth, instead using the GPU tensors (so that we can run the confidence-based assignment on the GPU without synchronizing the CPU).

Additionally, kernels must be able to support decode batches where requests have different query lengths per request.

GLM-5.x models using DSV3.2-style sparse MLA should be compatible through FlashInfer's SM100 TRT-LLM sparse-MLA kernel. vLLM currently derives the sparse token-to-request mapping from CPU query boundaries, and the target capability check also includes draft attention that is captured by a separate graph manager. We should wire up the device-length path, validate correctness, evaluate performance, and merge support.

PROPOSED IN https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52783

DEPENDS ON https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47808

title: fix(deepseek_v4): gate head_dim==512 compressor path on has_cutedsl()
body:
Fixes vllm-project/vllm#52710

## Summary
`DeepseekCompressor`'s `head_dim == 512` CuTe DSL kernel path was selected unconditionally on CUDA:

```python
if current_platform.is_cuda() and self.head_dim == 512:
```

...which imports `sparse_attn_compress_cutedsl` even when the optional `cutlass` (CuTe DSL) package is not importable, failing at kernel dispatch on builds that don't ship it — e.g. an H200 (sm_90a) target. Every other DeepSeek V4 CUDA/DS kernel selection site gates on `has_cutedsl()` (cache_utils.py:412, fused_indexer_q.py:367/440), and `nvidia/ops/__init__.py` documents that leaf modules must only be imported under a `has_cutedsl()`/`is_cuda()` gate.

Added `has_cutedsl()` to the guard and the import, matching the established pattern, so the Triton fallback is used when CuTe DSL isn't available.

## Verification
- `has_cutedsl()` exists at `vllm/utils/import_utils.py:578` and is used the same way at the three sibling call sites.
- `compressor.py` parses cleanly (the module-level import is unconditional at line 24, consistent with how the other DSv4 files import it).
- Signed-off-by included.

title: [Bug][ROCm] Kimi-K3 (KimiLinear/GDN hybrid) + ngram spec-decode: GPU memory access fault on concurrent mixed spec/non-spec batches (single-stream works after fixing a strided `state_indices` slice)
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>collect_env output (summary; full output attached)</summary>

- vLLM: `0.1.dev19253+g5f76ae224.d20260727` — the official ROCm Kimi-K3 image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k3`, with aiter built from source at `ROCm/aiter@e8f438a748d27d5350b9a2d63c8e1cffc2626f52` (2026-08-17)
- PyTorch: 2.11.0+gitd0c8b1f (ROCm 7.2.53211), Python 3.12.13, Ubuntu 22.04.5
- Hardware: 8× AMD Instinct MI300X (gfx942), single node, TP=8
- Model: `nota-ai/Kimi-K3-Nota-Global-Pruned-25` (MXFP4). Note: expert-pruned K3 variant — the pruning affects MoE expert counts only; the KDA/GDN and MLA attention layers are architecturally identical to stock Kimi-K3, and the files involved in this bug (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/third_party/kda/fused_recurrent.py`, `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/kimi_gdn_linear_attn.py`, `vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py`) were verified byte-identical to the image's stock copies before testing.

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Enabling ngram speculative decoding on Kimi-K3 (KimiLinear hybrid: 69 KDA/GatedDeltaNet recurrent layers + 24 MLA layers) produces **two distinct failures** on the ROCm build:

**Failure 1 (root-caused, workaround proven): strided `state_indices` rejected by the KDA single-token decode kernel.**

The first decode request after enabling `--speculative-config '{"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":6,"prompt_lookup_max":4,"prompt_lookup_min":2}'` dies on every TP worker:

```
File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/kimi_gdn_linear_attn.py", line 609, in _forward
    core_attn_out_non_spec, _ = fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode(
File ".../vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/third_party/kda/fused_recurrent.py", line 564, in fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode
    raise ValueError("`state_indices` must be contiguous and one-dimensional.")
```

Diagnostics show `state_indices` arrives as **ndim=1, shape=(1,), stride=(7,)** — a strided column-slice of the block table (`block_table_tensor[~spec_mask, 0]`, row-stride = num_speculative_tokens+1 = 7). Without spec-decode the mask is all-true and the slice comes out contiguous, which is why only the spec path trips it. The data itself is correct (one read-only state-slot index per request); only the layout is strided, so a compacting copy is lossless:

```python
# fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode, before the strict guard:
if state_indices.ndim != 1 or state_indices.stride(0) != 1:
    if state_indices.ndim == 1:
        state_indices = state_indices.contiguous()   # <- fix
    else:
        raise ValueError("`state_indices` must be contiguous and one-dimensional.")
```

With this in place, **single-stream ngram spec-decode works and is a large win**: mean acceptance length 5.45/5.41/4.80 (num_spec=6), accepted throughput up to **33.8 tok/s** vs 25.7 tok/s baseline on retrieval-shaped prompts, output exactness verified at temp=0 against a 200k-context needle suite (50/50 facts, identical to non-spec).

**Failure 2 (the blocker, unresolved): GPU memory access fault under concurrent mixed spec/non-spec batches.**

With the workaround in place, running **≥8 concurrent requests** through the same server GPU-faults all 8 devices within ~a minute:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-7 (Agent handle: 0x15c8c3d0) on address 0x73862f600000. Reason: Unknown.
Memory access fault by GPU node-9 (Agent handle: 0x170d4d00) on address 0x7210ff200000. Reason: Unknown.
... (all 8 GPUs)
GPU core dump failed
(EngineCore pid=543) ERROR ... Worker proc VllmWorker-2 died unexpectedly (exit code: None), shutting down executor.
```

The fault correlates with batches that mix spec-accepted and non-spec requests (the spec-decode metrics immediately before the fault show acceptance collapsing as the batch mixes). Our read: the concurrent spec+non-spec KDA recurrent-state indexing walks state out of bounds — the single-request `.contiguous()` read is benign, but the multi-request spec path has a deeper state-indexing bug. We deliberately stopped patching at this point (GPU-fault-class bugs are yours to own, not something downstream should whack-a-mole).

### Repro

```bash
# image: vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k3  (+ aiter main built from source, see env)
python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model nota-ai/Kimi-K3-Nota-Global-Pruned-25 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 655360 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --max-num-seqs 64 --block-size 128 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --language-model-only --trust-remote-code \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":6,"prompt_lookup_max":4,"prompt_lookup_min":2}'
# env: VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=0 HSA_ENABLE_IPC_MODE_LEGACY=0
#      VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=FP NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0
#      PYTORCH_HIP_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:False
```

1. Single `/v1/completions` request → Failure 1 (ValueError) on stock code; works with the `.contiguous()` workaround at 33.8 tok/s accepted throughput.
2. 8+ concurrent `/v1/completions` requests (mixed lengths) → Failure 2 (GPU memory access fault, all devices) within ~1 minute.

### The question for maintainers

Since our image was built (2026-07-27), this exact path has been reworked on main: #50649 *"Fix KDA NaN on mixed batches and racy autotune config"*, #50654 *"Fused kernel for KDA decode"*, #51862 *"Remove prefill pipeline stall in chunk KDA"* — and `kimi_gdn_linear_attn.py` now materializes the non-spec batch via `index_select` (which would also fix Failure 1 by construction).

- **Does the current main/next kimi-k3 ROCm image fix the concurrent mixed spec/non-spec KDA fault (Failure 2)?** #50649's NaN fix touches mixed batches but the symptom we see is an OOB fault, not NaN.
- If it's believed fixed, we're happy to validate a new `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k3` (or nightly rocm) image on our 8×MI300X node and report back — ngram spec is worth ~30% end-to-end on this model and is currently the only spec-decode path that works on gfx942 (draft-model/DSpark and aiter-MLA paths are gfx950-only).

Full logs available: complete ValueError traceback (all 8 workers), the strided-shape diagnostic, spec-decode metrics leading into the fault, and the GPU-fault log. Full bundle (secret gist): https://gist.github.com/skimanwhite/135d50e01ce9da029ba01bdaa4d10ba0

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Normalize FlashInfer prefill LSE before merging
body:
## Purpose

Prefix-cache hits could produce different logits from a cold prefill and
eventually lead to repetitive output. This was initially observed with GLM-5.2
in a disaggregated prefill/decode deployment.

KV cache digests matched before and after transfer, and the issue also
reproduced with BF16 KV cache. A local prefix-cache cold/warm comparison then
reproduced the logits divergence without KV transfer, narrowing the issue to
the cached-context attention path.

A cold prefill computes attention in one operation. On a prefix-cache hit,
vLLM computes attention over the cached context and new suffix separately, then
combines the two partial states with `merge_attn_states`.

FlashInfer prefill kernels, including the TRT-LLM ragged kernel, return base-2
log-sum-exp values. vLLM's CUDA and Triton `merge_attn_states` implementations
use natural `exp` and `log`. Passing base-2 LSE values directly therefore
produces incorrect context/suffix weights.

This PR:

- adds a shared `log2_lse_to_ln` conversion helper;
- converts LSE returned by the FlashInfer MLA prefill backend;
- converts LSE returned by the TRT-LLM ragged MLA prefill backend;
- converts generic FlashInfer DCP prefill LSE after the base-2 cross-rank
  reduction and before the natural-log attention-state merge.

The conversion is performed at the external kernel boundary so the rest of
vLLM continues to use the natural-log LSE contract.

### Duplicate-work check

No open PR currently fixes the MLA prefill paths changed here.

PR #36503 previously experimented with scaling generic FlashInfer prefill LSE
in an older commit (`f10579e`), but that change is not present in its current
diff. Its current scope is persistent buffer management for FlashInfer DCP
decode. This PR fixes the missing conversions on current main and additionally
covers both FlashInfer MLA prefill and TRT-LLM ragged MLA prefill.

PR #47779 concerns SM120 sparse MLA decode DCP and does not modify these
prefill merge paths.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -rs \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py \
  -k 'test_chunked_context_backend_correctness and \
      (FLASHINFER or TRTLLM_RAGGED)'

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/flashinfer.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/trtllm_ragged.py

git diff --check
```

Before/after error measurements used the same B300 GPU, test selection, and
random sequence. The old behavior was simulated by replacing the conversion
helper with an identity function at runtime.

## Test Result

Affected auto/FP8 matrix:

- 6 passed
- 2 skipped because FlashInfer does not support the tested GLM dimensions

Maximum absolute output error against the SDPA reference:

| Prefill path | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| FlashInfer / DeepSeek | 0.236328 | 0.0078125 |
| TRT-LLM ragged / DeepSeek | 0.228516 | 0.0078125 |
| TRT-LLM ragged / GLM | 0.265625 | 0.0078125 |

The results were identical across CUTLASS_MLA, FLASHINFER_MLA, and TRITON_MLA,
which is consistent with the error originating in the shared context/suffix
merge.

Pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.

The complete `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness` matrix produced 10
passed, 8 skipped, and 2 failures. Both failures are in the unchanged
FlashAttention FA4 path because the local extension does not accept the
`fp8_kv_dequant` keyword. They occur before LSE merging.

### AI assistance

AI assistance was used.

---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR is described.
- [x] The test plan and commands are included.
- [x] Local test results and the environment-specific failures are included.
- [ ] Model evaluation results must be added before submission.

</details>

title: [ROCm][AMD] Kimi-K3 gfx942 / MI325X Gap and Roadmap
body:
Sibling of [#50682](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50682). That tracker is the general Kimi-K3 ROCm roadmap. Most of it is gfx950 / MI355X. This issue is the gfx942 / MI325X (and MI300X) plan on top of current `vllm-project/vllm` main.

gfx942 is already listed as a one-line gap in #50682, with [#50817](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50817) as the enablement PR. The work below should land as stacked PRs on main, not as a private fork.

CC:

- [@xaguilar-amd](https://github.com/xaguilar-amd)
- [@hissu-hyvarinen](https://github.com/hissu-hyvarinen)
- [@jhartika-amd](https://github.com/jhartika-amd)
- [@hongxiayang](https://github.com/hongxiayang)
- [@tjtanaa](https://github.com/tjtanaa)
- [@seanfilimon](https://github.com/seanfilimon)
- [@mpashkovskii](https://github.com/mpashkovskii)
- [@LucasWilkinson](https://github.com/LucasWilkinson)
- [@fxmarty-amd](https://github.com/fxmarty-amd)

## Why gfx942 is a separate plan

Kimi-K3 is 93 layers, 69 KDA + 24 gated MLA, 96 heads. TP8 is 12 heads per rank. The day-0 image and [recipes.vllm.ai Kimi-K3](https://recipes.vllm.ai/moonshotai/Kimi-K3?hardware=mi355x&features=reasoning) target MI355X.

On gfx942 today:

- [#50516](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50516) makes the MXFP4 checkpoint constructible via lossless EMULATION. That path is about 9x to 15x slower than a real quantized MoE kernel, and it does not survive CUDA-graph capture. See the gfx942 measurements on #50682.
- The fused KDA decode kernel from [#50654](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50654) is still gfx950-only in current main. Runtime gate is `on_gfx950()` in `is_fused_kda_decode_supported`. CMake only adds `fused_kda_decode_kernel_rocm.cu` when `gfx950` is in the arch list.
- Gluon MLA decode asserts `mla_gluon requires gfx950` for the 12-head TP8 shape unless the asm pad-to-16 path is used.

## KDA decode fallback is still on main

This is not leftover fork code. On gfx942, current main still runs the unfused KDA decode path: `causal_conv1d_update` + `fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode` + `FusedRMSNormGated.forward_native`. The native gated RMSNorm is `pow` / `mean` / `rsqrt` / `sigmoid` as separate ATen launches. Inductor does not fuse this on ROCm.

Measured on MI325X, TP8, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`, one representative KDA+MoE decode layer. CUDA-graph replay, so these are real launches inside the graph.

KDA decode block only (conv + recurrent + gated output RMSNorm), 16 launches, 74.9 us:

| Step | Launches | Time (us) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `causal_conv1d_update` | 1 | 4.7 |
| `fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode` | 1 | 10.8 |
| `FusedRMSNormGated.forward_native` (`aten::pow`, `mean`, `rsqrt` path, `sigmoid`, copies) | 14 | 59.4 |
| **KDA decode fallback total** | **16** | **74.9** |

That is about 17% of this KDA+MoE layer. There are 69 KDA layers. [#52293](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52293) collapses the same block to one kernel at 7.8 us on gfx942. End-to-end TPOT barely moves until MoE is no longer the emulation path. The fusion is still required. The 14 ATen launches sit on the ~4 us launch floor and will not get cheaper by themselves.

The rest of a KDA+MoE layer is MoE routing, expert GEMM, TP all-reduce, and AttnRes. Those are later waves. The table above is the KDA fusion case.

## Wave 0: make gfx942 a real upstream baseline

Nightly is not a gfx942 baseline until a real MoE kernel and a small-head MLA route exist on main.

1. **AITER pin that includes [ROCm/aiter#4646](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4646).** [#51728](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51728) bumps to `v0.1.19.post2`. That tag is 2026-08-05. aiter#4646 (FlyDSL a16wi4) merged 2026-08-13, so it is not in post2. #51728 is still open, so including 4646 in this bump is still doable. Either retarget #51728 at a SHA after `4bbc57db`, or land post2 and follow immediately with a pin that contains 4646. #50682 already lists 4646 under the AITER docker upgrade. gfx942 should not wait for a later release if this pin can take it now.
2. **[#50817](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50817).** Native MXFP4 Triton `moe_gemm_a16w4` on gfx942, plus pad-to-16 MLA for 12 heads at TP8. This is the default enablement path. It does not depend on aiter#4646. Reported decode went from the emulation baseline to about 100 tok/s.
3. **Recipes and CI.** A gfx942 recipe on recipes.vllm.ai, and a gfx942 gsm8k / serve job on the public ROCm image. Without that, gfx942 keeps regressing silently.
4. **Load-time INT4 through the online-quant RFC, not extra checkpoints.** See the quantization section below.

## Wave 1: KDA fusion on gfx942

All of this is on top of #50654 / [#52606](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52606), not a second KDA stack.

1. **[#52293](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52293).** Enable the existing fused KDA decode kernel on gfx942. This is the PR that removes the 16-launch block in the table. Do not open a competing o_norm fusion PR.
2. **[#51183](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51183).** Write KDA decode into the layer buffer.
3. **KDA prefill on gfx942.** #52606 is the fused prefill work, currently gfx950-gated. After it lands, a small gfx942 gate PR, same shape as #52293.

## Wave 2: MLA (blocked on open AITER)

K3 MLA is dense gated MLA, NoPE, QK 192 / V 128, 12 heads per rank at TP8. Pad-to-16 in #50817 / [#50578](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50578) is the bridge.

1. [ROCm/aiter#4582](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4582) then draft [#51195](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51195) (native CDNA3 Gluon decode for measured verify shapes).
2. [ROCm/aiter#4645](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4645) then draft [#51551](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51551) (opt-in FP8 D192/V128 prefill).
3. A durable sub-16-head gfx942 decode in AITER, so we do not pad 12 heads to 16 forever.

DSA sparse-MLA kernels (indexer + top-k) do not apply here. K3 is hybrid KDA + dense MLA.

## Wave 3: after MoE is not emulation

Only after Wave 0. Otherwise the e2e signal is noise.

- Latent-MoE all-reduce overlap: draft [#51437](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51437)
- AttnRes follow-ups on top of [#50593](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50593)
- GEMM / FlyDSL tile work that #50817 still has to runtime-patch

[#52190](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52190) (`torch.compile` for `fused_qk_rmsnorm`) is not the gfx942 KDA o_norm fix.

## Load-time INT4 belongs in the online quantization RFC

[#52167](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52167) item 4 is "Requantize already-quantized layers to different precision." It already cites draft [#51274](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51274). That is the right place.

I think that we should not keep publishing extra Hugging Face checkpoints every time a new MXFP4 MoE model needs a gfx942 kernel. That is a bottleneck, and the models will keep coming. Kimi-K3, Qwen3.8, and likely more upcoming MXFP4 MoE models can use one opt-in at-load conversion onto an INT4 expert kernel that AITER already has (groupwise INT4 / a16wi4 once aiter#4646 is in the pin).

#51274 is a Kimi-K3 prototype of that: `--quantization-config.moe.weight int4_per_group_32`, default path unchanged, lossy and explicit. It should be generalized under #52167 rather than cloned per model. It stays draft until the AITER pin contains [ROCm/aiter#4646](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4646).

#50817 remains the native MXFP4 gfx942 path. Load-time INT4 is the opt-in when that kernel is missing or slower, not a silent default.

## How to use this issue

Stack PRs on main. For each PR: full gsm8k if it can change text, and `vllm bench serve` with `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` if it claims perf. Same bar as #50682.

Please comment here with gfx942 PRs so they do not only land on the gfx950 tracker.

AI assistance was used to draft this tracker. I reviewed the plan, the public PR list, and the kernel table.

title: [BugFix] Cache Hit Rate with KIMI + RHAI Dspark
body:
Keep KV cache group block sizes commensurate when unifying page sizes

For a hybrid target (e.g. MLA + linear attention, block size aligned to the mamba state page, 1536 tokens) plus a draft model whose layers have a different per-token KV footprint (e.g. an SWA DSpark drafter), unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size scaled the draft layers' block size by the byte ratio to make pages exactly equal. The resulting block size (e.g. 3456 tokens) is generally neither a multiple nor a divisor of the other groups' block sizes, so scheduler_block_size — the LCM of all group block sizes and the prefix-cache hit alignment — exploded (e.g. lcm(1536, 3456) = 13824 tokens). Every prefix-cache hit then rounds down to a 13824-token boundary, costing ~7K reusable tokens per request at 70K ISL (~10-15pp hit rate).

Fix: when byte-exact scaling would break token commensurability and the layer's backend tolerates padded pages (indexes_kv_by_block_stride), pick the largest block size that divides the max-page groups' block-size LCM instead and pad the page to the shared page size. The scheduler block size then stays at the target's block size (1536), matching the behavior of an architecture-matched (e.g. MLA-native) drafter. Backends without padded-page support keep the byte-exact behavior; a new warning in resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes flags incommensurate group block sizes so the hit-granularity cost is visible.

title: [Bug]: PD Multi Tier supplies nothing when the producer already holds the blocks
body:
### Summary

In the PD Multi Tier flow (`remote_decoder` / `remote_prefiller`, secondary tier
of `type: p2p`),
a producer that **already holds the requested blocks** supplies nothing to the
consumer. The consumer's fetch demand parks unsatisfied, waits out
`_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S = 30.0`, aborts, and recomputes the prompt locally.

The effect is inverted from the intent: the better the producer's prefix cache
works, the more often the Multi Tier path fails to deliver.

### Environment

- vLLM `v0.27.1`, stock `docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1`
- `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, TP=1, `--block-size 128`,
  `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` on all instances
- 2x H200, RDMA between pods
- Connector on both instances:

```
--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
  "kv_load_failure_policy":"recompute",
  "kv_connector_extra_config":{"spec_name":"TieringOffloadingSpec",
    "cpu_bytes_to_use":107374182400,"block_size":128,"eviction_policy":"lru",
    "offload_prompt_only":false,
    "secondary_tiers":[{"type":"p2p","host":"$(POD_IP)","port":7777}]}}'
```

Two files (`tiering/p2p/session/server.py`, `.../client.py`) carried added
`logger.info` counters only, no behavioural change; the timings and byte counts
below come from vLLM's own metrics and logs.

### Reproducer

Two instances, A (producer) and B (consumer). No P/D topology, router or proxy
required — three HTTP calls.

1. **Producer leg** on A: `POST /v1/completions`, `max_tokens=1`,
   `kv_transfer_params={"remote_decoder":{"kv_request_id":ID}}`
2. **Consumer leg** on B: `POST /v1/completions`,
   `kv_transfer_params={"remote_prefiller":{"kv_request_id":ID,"remote_host":A,"remote_port":7777}}`

Run that pair twice with a **unique prompt each time** (so the consumer is always
cold). Before the second pair, send the prompt to A once on its own with no
`kv_transfer_params`, so A already holds the blocks.

Prompt ~8K tokens. Watch `vllm:kv_offload_load_bytes_total` on B.

### Observed

| case | producer leg | consumer leg | consumer bytes loaded |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| A cold for the prefix | 0.20 s | 0.16 s | +268,959,744 (256 MiB) |
| A pre-warmed | 0.03 s | **32.9 s** | **0** |

Identical with a real P/D pair (prefill producer, decode consumer):
0.086 s / +256 MiB cold vs 30.2 s / 0 bytes warm. Reproduces every time.

Consumer log for the warm case:

```
P2PSession <A>:7777: <id> round=0 timed out, sending abort
P2PSession <A>:7777: load request <id> (job_id=N) timed out; load job completed
with failure. If this recurs, ensure PYTHONHASHSEED is set to the same value on
all nodes.
```

`PYTHONHASHSEED=0` was set and verified identical on every instance, so that
hint is misleading for this failure mode.

### Analysis

Supply for a PD round can only come from that request's store jobs
(`session/server.py` `_OutboundRequestState.add_stored_blocks`). A warm producer
creates no store job, so demand parked in `demanded`
(`key -> remote_block_idx: blocks peer wants, awaiting supply`) is never matched.

Two gates prevent the blocks from being offered:

1. `distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py` (~L941):

```python
# Skip prefix-hit chunks for block-level policy; for
# request-level, next_stored_chunk_idx stays at 0 so all
# chunks (including hits) are offloaded.
if req_status.offloading_context.policy == OffloadPolicy.BLOCK_LEVEL:
    group_state.next_stored_chunk_idx = num_chunks
```

`P2PTierManager.on_new_request` returns a bare `RequestOffloadingContext()`,
which defaults to `BLOCK_LEVEL`. `grep -c REQUEST_LEVEL` is **0** for every tier
(`p2p`, `fs`, `obj`, `example`) at `v0.27.1` **and on `main`**, so
`request_level_tiers` is always empty and
`TieringOffloadingManager._cascade_existing_blocks_to_request_level_tiers` never
runs.

2. Forcing `REQUEST_LEVEL` for producer-side requests clears gate 1 — verified,
the request then reaches the store path with `next_stored_chunk_idx=0` and 56
storable chunks — but the keys are then dropped by `if block_id == 0: continue`,
since a prefix-hit request has no GPU block ids recorded for those blocks
(measured: 55 keys dropped). `new_offload_keys` empties, `prepare_store` is
skipped, and with it the cascade.

### Why symmetric (non-PD) Multi Tier is unaffected

`session/server.py`:

> `# Supply came from inbound lookup pins (symmetric): no late submit_store can arrive, so unmatched fetch demand fails fast. PD rounds park demand for stores instead.`

`session/client.py`:

> `PD-only loads leave probes/unsent empty ... PD clients never probe and stay on round 0.`

The symmetric path supplies from tier lookups and pins, which need neither a store job
nor GPU block ids, so a warm producer is its best case. PD has no equivalent
route.

### Impact at scale

Shared-prefix workload, 8 producers + 8 consumers, 10,800 requests. Supply match
rate tracks producer cache warmth:

| | cold | warming | warm |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| fetch demand matched | 93.8% | 51.5% | **36.7%** |

6,083 load timeouts were logged against 10,800 requests. End to end this made
PD Multi Tier slower than plain NIXL P/D on the same hardware (1571 s vs
1032 s to completion; mean TPOT 92 ms vs 10.7 ms).

### Question

Should the PD Multi Tier path gain a lookup/pin supply route like the symmetric one, or should
the p2p tier declare `REQUEST_LEVEL` (and the store path then be able to offload
prefix-hit blocks that have no GPU block id)? The second looks like it fights both
the `BLOCK_LEVEL` optimisation and the missing block-id constraint, so the first
seems closer to the existing design — but that is your call.

cc @liranschour

title: [RFC]: Hybrid SSM models and last-block-replay with SpecDec and APC enabled
body:
### Motivation.

Long name, I know, but it should explain the issue we're facing.
Currently, when running a model with EAGLE-like speculative decoding (EAGLE/MTP/DFlash/DSpark) and APC enabled, on prefix cache match, vLLM needs to re-run the last full block of the cached prefix, as the drafter needs access to the first uncached token's EAGLE intermediate states.
This is usually fine for pure attention models, where a block consists of ~16 tokens. For hybrid SSM/attention models, however, each block may contain thousands of tokens (for Nemotron 3 Nano in TP1 it's 4224 tokens per block), and re-running a block can really hurt performance.

This RFC aims to offer a few different possibilities for properly solving this issue.

### Proposed Change.

We came up with three different ideas, and have working prototypes of them, and are actively working on a fourth one, initially rejected as too wasteful, but it might turn out to be the simplest. The ideas can potentially compliment each other, too, and work in unison, which may lead to better performance. We'll validate that once we land on an agreed path forward. The exception here are the last two ideas, both looking at caching the intermediate EAGLE states, just in differing ways.

From least to most involved, the ideas are:

- Partial match block promotion
  - Building on top of @ZJY0516 's work in [#45702](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45702).
  - First prefix cache hit will re-run last full block, up to `prefix-match-unit` tokens from the end of the block.
  - The SSM state at that point will get promoted, and saved to the prefix cache as a new block.
  - Subsequent matches can match on the new block, and only re-run the last `prefix-match-unit` tokens, with COW so that the prefix cache remains valid in the partial block.
  - Partial block granularity is not limited to "`prefix-match-unit` tokens from the end", specifically, but rather any multiple of `prefix-match-unit` can become a promotion junction.
- Next-token receipt on cached blocks
  - Each cached block will store additional information on the token that was generated following it.
  - If the prefix cache is hit, with the uncached token matching the first token that will be computed, the full prefix cache can be used, without any re-computation needed.
  - Still not sure on this point, but we're working to verify it as well.
- Cache boundary EAGLE states
  - After determining an SSM cache block's size, it is rounded up in number-of-tokens terms for the KV cache, and any diff is used as padding in the SSM view of the block.
  - We can take advantage of that, and before rounding up, append enough memory to the SSM cache for a single token's worth of EAGLE states.
    - For Nemotron 3 Nano in TP1, for example, 5,376 bytes are needed for the EAGLE states, which fits inside the existing `all`-mode APC's padding.
  - These states can then be used in conjunction with the cache, and eliminate the need to re-compute that block altogether.
  - This solution can add quite a lot of code complexity, surrounding different parallelization schemes.
    - With PP, for example, the SSM cache the EAGLE states are written to might belong to a rank that doesn't hold the drafter model.
- Sparse EAGLE cache
  - This is the newly revived idea, and is not fully fleshed or tested yet.
  - Building on top of the existing `HiddenStateCacheSpec`, adapting it for our needs.
  - Only cache states at block boundaries, packing multiple such states into a single cache page and sharing them across requests.
  - Requires somewhat complex bookkeeping:
    - Coupling states with the right prefix
    - Evicting states only when corresponding prefix cache blocks are evicted
    - Consolidating sparse pages as states get evicted

### Feedback Period.

_No response_

### CC List.

@benchislett @ZJY0516 @yewentao256 @Naveassaf @amitz-nv @amirkl94 @shaunkotek 

### Any Other Things.

_No response_

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek V4 buffers long string tool arguments until </parameter>
body:
### Your current environment

This is reproducible in the parser without a model or accelerator.

- Reproduced on vLLM `v0.25.1` (`752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34`).
- Confirmed by source inspection on current `main` at `f1178f3a06fa30a0cc282376924210cedad08c44`: `deepseek_v4_config()` still sets `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")`, and `_compute_arg_delta()` still skips converter calls when a raw delta does not contain one of those characters.
- Python 3.12.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

DeepSeek V4 tool calls do not incrementally stream the body of a single long string parameter. The stream emits the function name and the opening JSON prefix, then remains silent for the entire parameter body. When the DSML `</parameter>` closing tag arrives, the accumulated body is emitted as one large `delta.tool_calls[0].function.arguments` fragment.

This is the same user-visible failure mode discussed in #43267, but it affects the DeepSeek V4 parser added in #45877 after #43267 was closed. #46351 added schema-aware support for streaming prefix-stable string values in the shared ParserEngine, but the DeepSeek V4 configuration prevents that path from running for ordinary parameter-body deltas.

#### Minimal parser-only reproduction

The following uses no model weights or accelerator:

```python
import json
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import (
    ChatCompletionToolsParam,
    FunctionDefinition,
)
from vllm.tool_parsers.deepseekv4_engine_tool_parser import (
    DeepSeekV4EngineToolParser,
)

tokenizer = MagicMock()
tokenizer.get_vocab.return_value = {}
tool = ChatCompletionToolsParam(
    type="function",
    function=FunctionDefinition(
        name="emit_text",
        parameters={
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"text": {"type": "string"}},
            "required": ["text"],
        },
    ),
)
request = MagicMock()
request.tools = [tool]
request.tool_choice = "auto"
parser = DeepSeekV4EngineToolParser(tokenizer, tools=[tool])

header = (
    '<｜DSML｜tool_calls>\n'
    '<｜DSML｜invoke name="emit_text">\n'
    '<｜DSML｜parameter name="text" string="true">'
)
body = "A" * 4096
tail = (
    '</｜DSML｜parameter>\n'
    '</｜DSML｜invoke>\n'
    '</｜DSML｜tool_calls>'
)
chunks = [header] + [body[i : i + 32] for i in range(0, len(body), 32)] + [tail]

previous = ""
argument_deltas = []
for index, delta_text in enumerate(chunks):
    current = previous + delta_text
    delta = parser.extract_tool_calls_streaming(
        previous_text=previous,
        current_text=current,
        delta_text=delta_text,
        previous_token_ids=[],
        current_token_ids=[],
        delta_token_ids=[1],
        request=request,
    )
    previous = current
    if delta:
        for tool_call in delta.tool_calls:
            if tool_call.function and tool_call.function.arguments is not None:
                argument_deltas.append((index, tool_call.function.arguments))

print([(index, len(value)) for index, value in argument_deltas])
print("pre-close non-empty deltas:", sum(
    bool(value) for index, value in argument_deltas if index < len(chunks) - 1
))
print("valid reconstruction:", json.loads("".join(
    value for _, value in argument_deltas
)) == {"text": body})
```

Observed output:

```text
[(0, 10), (129, 4104)]
pre-close non-empty deltas: 1
valid reconstruction: True
```

The only pre-close fragment is the JSON prefix `{"text": "`. All 4096 body characters are withheld and emitted with the closing tag.

Expected behavior: multiple non-empty `function.arguments` deltas should contain parameter body text before `</parameter>`, while their concatenation remains valid JSON after the tool call completes.

#### Root cause

`vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py` configures:

```python
arg_converter=_dsml_arg_converter,
arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">"),
```

`ParserEngine._compute_arg_delta()` then returns early for every body-only delta:

```python
structural = self._arg_structural_chars
if structural is not None and structural.isdisjoint(raw_delta):
    return None
```

The opening parameter tag contains `>`, so the converter emits `{"text": "`. Typical string body deltas contain no `>`, so they are accumulated without conversion. The closing tag contains `>`, which finally triggers conversion of the full accumulated body.

As a diagnostic control, setting `arg_structural_chars=None` for the same parser input produces 130 non-empty argument deltas (maximum 32 characters) before/finally at close, with exact JSON reconstruction. That demonstrates the filtering condition is the immediate cause, although simply removing it may make the regex-based converter repeatedly scan the full accumulated argument and should be evaluated for long-argument complexity.

#### Real endpoint confirmation

A deterministic `stream=true`, `tool_choice="auto"` request to a DeepSeek V4 Flash service produced:

```text
2.433s  function name: emit_text
2.531s  arguments: {"text": "        (10 characters)
12.893s arguments: <entire body>       (861 characters)
12.942s arguments: "}                  (2 characters)
12.992s finish_reason: tool_calls
```

There were no argument-body deltas for 10.36 seconds. The reconstructed arguments were valid JSON. `tool_choice="auto"` is intentional so the request exercises the DeepSeek V4 parser rather than the generic required/named-tool path.

A regression test should specifically assert that a single long schema-typed string parameter emits more than one body delta before `</parameter>`. The existing mixed-parameter incremental test can pass because each subsequent parameter header contains `>` and flushes the preceding value.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I searched open and closed issues for DeepSeek V4 tool-call argument streaming and reviewed the related #43267, #45877, and #46351 history.
