title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix eagle draft sharing with a quantized lm_head
body:
## Purpose

`_should_share()` in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/eagle/utils.py` reads `draft.weight` unconditionally to decide whether the draft can adopt the target's `lm_head`:

```python
w = draft.weight
if w.is_cuda and torch.accelerator.get_memory_info(w.device)[0] < w.numel() * 2:
    return torch.equal(w.cpu(), target.weight.cpu())
return torch.equal(w, target.weight)
```

A quantized `ParallelLMHead` registers packed weights (`weight_packed`, `qweight`, ...) and no `weight`, so this raises and aborts engine startup:

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/eagle/utils.py", line 22, in _should_share
  w = draft.weight
AttributeError: 'ParallelLMHead' object has no attribute 'weight'
```

This is a guard that already exists in V1 and was lost in the V2 rewrite. `LLMBaseProposer._maybe_share_lm_head` gates the same comparison on the attribute being present:

```python
elif (
    hasattr(target_language_model, "lm_head")
    and hasattr(target_language_model.lm_head, "weight")
    and hasattr(self.model.lm_head, "weight")
    and isinstance(target_language_model.lm_head.weight, torch.Tensor)
    and isinstance(self.model.lm_head.weight, torch.Tensor)
    and torch.equal(...)
):
    share_lm_head = True
else:
    # "Detected EAGLE model with distinct lm_head weights.
    #  Keeping separate lm_head weights from the target model."
```

When the attribute is missing, V1 falls through to the `else` and keeps the draft's own head. This PR restores that behaviour in the V2 helper.

## Why the draft keeps its own head

Not sharing is the correct answer, not merely the safe one. Without a plain `weight` on both sides there is no way to prove the two copies match, and adopting the target's head would silently change the draft's output.

For eagle3 drafts with a reduced `draft_vocab_size` the decision is unchanged: the shapes differ, so `torch.equal` already returned `False`. Those models get the same answer they did before — without raising.

The helper is shared, so this also covers the dflash and dspark drafters.

## Scope — please read

I could not find a public checkpoint that reproduces this. I scanned 880 eagle3/speculator repos and 429 quantized-target candidates on the Hub, reading safetensors tensor names; none carries a quantized `lm_head` or `embed_tokens`. The closest public eagle3 drafts (`nm-testing/Speculator-*-Eagle3-converted-*-quantized-w4a16`) quantize the transformer layers and leave `lm_head.weight` in place.

So this is a supported-but-uncommon configuration. Quantizing the `lm_head` is first-class in vLLM — `ParallelLMHead` takes a `quant_config`, and `CompressedTensorsConfig.get_quant_method` has a dedicated `isinstance(layer, ParallelLMHead)` branch — it is just rarely shipped. We hit it with internal compressed-tensors checkpoints that quantize the head (`lm_head.weight_packed` / `weight_scale` / `weight_shape`, no `lm_head.weight`), which made some of our models fail.

I am raising it because the V1/V2 divergence is a real inconsistency regardless of how many checkpoints exercise it today, not because of the number of users affected. Happy to publish a small reproducer checkpoint to the Hub if a maintainer wants one.

## Not a duplicate

Could not find any.

## Test plan

```
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_spec_decode_eagle_utils.py    # 5 passed
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py  # 2 passed
```

Reverting the fix fails the two quantized-head cases with the exact `AttributeError` above; the three unquantized cases pass either way, confirming the sharing policy is unchanged.

End-to-end on gfx1151 with an internal `Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct-AWQ` target and an eagle3 draft whose `lm_head` is int8 compressed-tensors.

`pre-commit` (ruff, mypy) clean.

AI assistance was used for this change.

title: [CI/Build][ROCm] Run the TileLang HIP symbol checks in their own interpreter
body:
The test belongs to the Kernels Root Misc Test group, which AMD CI does not run yet.
This fix should land before the PR that enables that group (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50519).

## Purpose

`test_deepseek_v4_import_and_jit_monitor_do_not_hijack_hip_symbols` asserts two
things about process-global state: that importing DeepSeek V4 and activating the
JIT monitor leaves TileLang out of `sys.modules`, and that `hipFree` in the
global symbol table still resolves to `libamdhip64.so` rather than the
`libhip_stub.so` TileLang ships.

On its own the test holds. In a whole-directory run it does not, because the
sibling `test_mhc_kernels.py` imports TileLang on purpose to exercise those
kernels. By the time this test runs, TileLang is already in `sys.modules` and
its stub is already loaded, so the test fails on suite-wide state rather than on
anything about the code it is guarding.

Move the two checks into `tests/kernels/scripts/check_no_tilelang_hijack.py` and
have the test run it with `sys.executable`. In a fresh interpreter the
assertions mean what they say no matter what the rest of the suite imports, and
the test reports the script's output when it fails.

## Test Plan

Run the two files together, in the order a whole-directory collection gives
them:

```
pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py tests/kernels/test_mhc_tilelang_jit.py
```

## Test Result

On MI355 (gfx950, ROCm 7.2.3), before the change, the sibling import is enough
to take the test down:

```
FAILED kernels/test_mhc_tilelang_jit.py::test_deepseek_v4_import_and_jit_monitor_do_not_hijack_hip_symbols
E       assert not True
1 failed, 54 passed, 39 warnings in 21.65s
```

After:

```
55 passed, 39 warnings in 77.35s
```

The check still bites when the symbols really are taken over. Running the script
in an interpreter that has TileLang loaded fails it, as it should:

```
AssertionError: TileLang was imported: ['tilelang.env', 'tilelang.libinfo', ...]
```

title: [Bug][KVOffload] PD Multi Tier discards parked KV after a fixed 60s, so a queued consumer recomputes
body:
### Your current environment

vLLM `main` (nightly `5a4c8d99`), plus #52912 applied. Two instances,
prefill and decode, each running `OffloadingConnector` with
`TieringOffloadingSpec` (CPU primary + `p2p` secondary tier).

### Describe the bug

A PD Multi Tier producer discards stored KV 60 s after `submit_store` when no
`FetchMsg` has bound the `kv_request_id` yet, so a consumer whose fetch is
issued later finds nothing, burns its own 30 s load deadline, and recomputes
the prompt.

`_UNBOUND_STORE_TIMEOUT_S = 60.0` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/manager.py`)
is a fixed timer counted from store time. Nothing ties it to whether the
consumer's request still exists or is merely queued behind other work, so the
reap can fire while the request it belongs to is perfectly alive. When the
late fetch arrives, the consumer waits out `_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S = 30.0`
(`.../p2p/session/client.py`) before falling back to recompute.

This is separate from #52808 and is not addressed by #52912; that fix makes a
warm producer cascade its blocks, this is about how long those blocks survive
while the peer has not asked for them yet.

Reproduced with two vLLM instances and three curls - no router, no proxy, no
scheduler involved. The only difference between the two cases is how long the
consumer waits before fetching:

| case | consumer fetch delay | consumer leg | bytes pulled |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| control | 5 s (inside the park) | 0.30 s | 580,962,816 |
| late | 65 s (past the park) | 38.31 s | 0 |

Producer log for the late case:

```
P2P <producer-ip>:7777: unbound store kv_request_id=park-late-39 timed out
after 60s without a fetch - failing 1 job(s)
```

### Why this fires in practice

The 60 s clock does not start when prefill completes - it starts at the
producer's FIRST stored chunk. `_build_store_jobs` iterates
`scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens` (in-flight requests), `complete_store`
cascades each finished store job to the secondary tiers every step, and
`_reap_unbound_stores` keys off `batches[0].submitted_at`, the oldest batch,
then pops the whole `kv_request_id`.

Measured on an idle H200 with a 98 K-token producer leg: HTTP returned in
6.7 s, the first batch parked at +1 s, and with no fetch sent the reap fired
at first-park + 60 s rather than completion + 60 s (the two predictions
differ by 6 s in that setup; the log lands on the former).

So the failing condition is not decoder queueing. The real budget is
first-chunk-to-fetch < 60 s, where the fetch only happens after the remaining
prefill, the producer's HTTP return, proxy dispatch, decode admission, and
the decode scheduler's lookup/flush. The producer's own prefill spends the
budget first: 6.7 s of it idle at 98 K tokens, 13.3 s under mild concurrent
load on the same GPU. At real concurrency on long prompts the sum passes
60 s with the decoder never queueing at all. Each occurrence costs a 30 s
stall plus a full prompt recompute, which feeds back into the load that
caused the delay.

Both leg-dispatch orders lose, so this cannot be fixed by the caller:

- dispatch the legs concurrently and the fetch can arrive **before** the
  store, so demand parks and the consumer burns its 30 s deadline. This is
  what llm-d/llm-d-router#2451 fixes on the routing-proxy side, by running
  the prefill leg to completion before dispatching decode
- dispatch them sequentially, as that PR does and as the NIXL path already
  did, and the fetch can arrive **after** the 60 s reap - this issue

A post-reap fetch is also not rejected: the reap adds the id to
`_failed_req_ids`, but the fetch-bind path never consults that set (it feeds
only the consumer-side `lookup()` and dead-session teardown, despite the
reap docstring saying otherwise). The late fetch binds, finds nothing, and
parks silently until the consumer's 30 s deadline.

### Steps to reproduce

Two instances, `PF` = producer, `DE` = consumer, both with the tiering spec
and a `p2p` secondary tier.

```sh
M=<model>; ID=park-$$
PROMPT=$(awk 'BEGIN{p="unique-'$ID' ";for(i=0;i<900;i++) p=p "alpha bravo charlie delta echo ";print p}')

# producer leg: stores KV under ID, parks it (no peer has fetched yet)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'producer http=%{http_code} t=%{time_total}\n' \
  -X POST "http://$PF:8000/v1/completions" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"model\":\"$M\",\"prompt\":\"$PROMPT\",\"max_tokens\":1,\"temperature\":0,\"kv_transfer_params\":{\"remote_decoder\":{\"kv_request_id\":\"$ID\"}}}"

sleep 65     # 5 reproduces the working control

curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'consumer http=%{http_code} t=%{time_total}\n' \
  -X POST "http://$DE:8200/v1/completions" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"model\":\"$M\",\"prompt\":\"$PROMPT\",\"max_tokens\":4,\"temperature\":0,\"kv_transfer_params\":{\"remote_prefiller\":{\"kv_request_id\":\"$ID\",\"remote_host\":\"$PF\",\"remote_port\":7777}}}"

# watch vllm:kv_offload_load_bytes_total on the consumer across the pair
```

With `sleep 5` the consumer pulls the blocks in ~0.3 s. With `sleep 65` it
transfers nothing and returns after ~38 s.

### The NIXL path already solves this

`NixlConnector` faces the same question - how long does P hold blocks that D
has not read yet - and answers it with a renewable lease rather than a fixed
timer:

- `_kv_lease_duration` (`nixl/base_scheduler.py`), default **30 s**,
  configurable via `kv_lease_duration`
- `_heartbeat_interval = _kv_lease_duration // 6`, and D sends periodic
  lease-renewal heartbeats to P for every request it still intends to read
- `decoder_kv_blocks_ttl`, default 480 s, for the client-driven turn-2 case

So NIXL's nominal pin is *shorter* than the tier's 60 s, yet a queued consumer
never loses its blocks: the lease is tied to consumer liveness, and only a
consumer that has actually gone away lets it lapse. The p2p tier has no
equivalent - no renewal, no way for the consumer to signal intent, and no
config knob - so it cannot distinguish "the peer is still queued" from "the
peer will never come".

### Suggested direction

Tie the parked store's lifetime to the consumer's liveness instead of a fixed
interval from store time. A few shapes that would work:

- adopt the NIXL contract: let the consumer renew the parked store the way D
  renews P's lease, so a queued request keeps its KV and a dead one releases
  it promptly
- failing that, let the consumer register intent for a `kv_request_id` before
  it is admitted, so the producer knows a peer is coming
- at minimum make the interval configurable like `kv_lease_duration` is,
  since the right value depends on the deployment's admission latency

Worth surfacing the reap as its own counter either way - today it is only a
warning line, so operators see the consumer's recompute without the producer
side that explains it.

cc @liranschour

title: Add multi-path sharding and aligned direct I/O to FS offloading
body:
## Purpose

  The filesystem KV offloading tier currently uses a single storage path and assumes direct I/O can be selected for an entire batch. This PR adds two capabilities to the filesystem KV offloading tier:

  - Optional whole-block sharding across an ordered, comma-separated list of storage paths using `path_sharding: "by_block_hash"`. Blocks assigned to different paths are processed in parallel, while existing single-path behavior remains unchanged.
  - Safe O_DIRECT selection based on per-path support and per-operation buffer and length alignment. Unaligned operations fall back to buffered I/O.

Documentation is included for the new configuration and block-placement behavior.

  ## Test Plan

  Focused unit tests:

  ```bash
  python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_fs_tier.py
  ```

  Multi-path filesystem KV offloading configuration:

  ```bash
  kv_transfer_config='{
    "kv_connector": "OffloadingConnector",
    "kv_role": "kv_both",
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
      "spec_name": "TieringOffloadingSpec",
      "cpu_bytes_to_use": 34359738368,
      "block_size": 1024,
      "eviction_policy": "lru",
      "secondary_tiers": [{
        "type": "fs",
        "root_dir": "/mnt/ps-1/kv-cache,/mnt/ps-2/kv-cache,/mnt/ps-3/kv-cache,/mnt/ps-4/kv-cache",
        "path_sharding": "by_block_hash",
        "n_read_threads": 64,
        "n_write_threads": 64
      }]
    }
  }'

  vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --max-model-len 262144 \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --kv-transfer-config "$kv_transfer_config"
  ```
  
 ## Test Result

  The native extension was rebuilt from source against CUDA 13 on H100 using an editable installation. The focused unit tests were rerun against the rebuilt extension.

  Runtime validation used four filesystem paths with TP=4 and a 128K-token request. Three storage-hit reads retrieved all `126/126` requested blocks without short-I/O or backend errors.

  The four-paths configuration reduced mean storage-hit TTFT by **41.1%**. Mean filesystem-to-CPU transfer time decreased from `1.404 s` to `0.671 s` (`52.2%`).

title: [Bug]: DC unavailable for GlmMoeDsa (GLM-5.2 FP8) on SM90 — sparse MLA backend lacks decode-LSE support
body:
### Your current environment I am working on Air gapped environment, that is why I am posting it here ### 🐛 Describe the bug

Environment

  • vLLM: 0.26.0

  • Hardware: 8× NVIDIA H200 (SM90)

  • Model: GLM-5.2-FP8

  • Resolved architecture: GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM

  • Tensor parallelism: --tensor-parallel-size 8

  • Expert parallelism: --enable-expert-parallel

  • Decode context parallelism: --decode-context-parallel-size 8

  • KV cache dtype: fp8_ds_mla

  • Maximum model length: 131072

Full vllm collect_env output is attached.

Summary

DCP=8 cannot currently be enabled for GLM-5.2 (GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM) on Hopper/SM90 when using the required fp8_ds_mla KV-cache dtype.

The currently available sparse-MLA attention backends appear to have mutually incompatible capabilities:

As a result, there does not currently appear to be a selectable sparse-MLA backend satisfying all of:

SM90 + fp8_ds_mla + decode-LSE + DCP

Reproduction

Using the default sparse MLA backend:

--tensor-parallel-size 8 \
--decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla

the server fails during initialization with:

RuntimeError: DCP requires attention impls to return the softmax lse for decode,
but the impl FlashMLASparseImpl does not return the softmax lse for decode.

When forcing:

--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE

backend selection fails with:

ValueError: Selected backend AttentionBackendEnum.FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE is not valid
for this configuration. Reason: [
    'kv_cache_dtype not supported',
    'compute capability not supported',
    'FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE SM10 does not support fp8_ds_mla kv-cache dtype'
]

Why this matters

GLM-5.2 uses sparse MLA with a single latent KV head. With TP=8, the KV cache is replicated across the tensor-parallel ranks.

For our workload, this significantly limits long-context decode concurrency.

At a 262,144-token request length, the measured maximum concurrency is approximately 1.50×, corresponding to roughly 393K KV tokens per GPU against approximately 20 GB of available KV-cache memory.

DCP would allow the decode attention workload to be distributed across the 8 GPUs, which is important for our long-context serving workload.

Question for maintainers

Is decode-LSE support planned for FLASHMLA_SPARSE on SM90?

FLASHMLA_SPARSE appears to be the only currently available backend that satisfies both:

  1. SM90 support

  2. fp8_ds_mla KV-cache support

However, DCP currently rejects it because:

can_return_lse_for_decode = False

The underlying flash_mla_sparse_fwd operation appears to expose LSE as an output already. Is the remaining blocker primarily in the vLLM integration layer, or does making FLASHMLA_SPARSE DCP-compatible also require changes to the sparse MLA/indexer path?

In particular, does DCP require the sparse MLA index/top-k selection to be coordinated across DCP ranks, rather than only exposing the decode LSE?

If so, what is the intended implementation path for making FLASHMLA_SPARSE DCP-compatible on SM90?

Related issues

This appears related to the existing GLM-5.2 / DCP work in #50095, as well as earlier sparse-MLA/DCP issues such as #45425 and #48611.

The specific capability gap I'm tracking is:

SM90 + fp8_ds_mla + decode-LSE + DCP=8

At present, no available sparse-MLA backend appears to satisfy all four requirements.

Attachments

  • Full python -m vllm.collect_env output

  • nvidia-smi output

  • Full traceback using default FLASHMLA_SPARSE

  • Full traceback when forcing FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE

  • Full vLLM serving command/configuration

title: [ROCm][DSv4] Enable aux-stream for c4a/c128a compressor overlap
body:
Enable aux_streams[0] on ROCm to overlap the main KV compressor (c4a/c128a layers) with Q/KV projections, matching ATOM alt_stream. Slots [1],[2] (indexer streams) remain None.

maybe_execute_in_parallel BreakableCUDAGraphCapture guard ensures the aux-stream path is disabled during piecewise graph capture.

NOTE: Initial measurement on MI355X (ISL=8k/OSL=1k) showed a 2-4% throughput regression across conc=1..64, likely due to HIP inter-stream event synchronization overhead exceeding the overlap benefit at these batch sizes. Keeping enabled for further investigation on longer contexts where the compression kernel is heavier.

title: vLLM v0.26.0 + Ray TP8: intermittent wedge, `RayWorkerProc rank=[0] died unexpectedly` after `shm_broadcast` block starvation; API stays up but generation is dead
body:
## Summary

On an 8-rank tensor-parallel deployment of GLM-5.2-FP8, vLLM v0.26.0 intermittently
wedges during bring-up. ~60 s of shared-memory broadcast block starvation is followed
by `RayWorkerProc rank=[0] died unexpectedly`, `RuntimeError: cancelled` from
`shm_broadcast.acquire_read`, and `EngineDeadError`. **Rank 0's own reason for dying
is never surfaced** - the executor reports only that it died.

**Observed in 5 of 7 startup attempts.** When a start does survive, the server is
stable — one surviving instance served 40 consecutive authenticated generation
requests over 2 hours with zero failures. So this is a startup-time race, not
runtime decay.

**Most damaging detail:** in 2 of 3 controlled trials the HTTP server still came up
and answered `GET /v1/models` with 200 while generation was already dead. Any
readiness check based on the models endpoint reports a healthy start for a wedged
engine. Only an authenticated completion request detects it.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| vLLM | 0.26.0 |
| Hardware | 8 × NVIDIA GB10, compute capability 12.1 (SM121), 128 GB unified LPDDR5X per node |
| Driver / CUDA | 580.173.02 / 13.0 |
| OS / kernel | Ubuntu 24.04.4, 6.17.0-1029-nvidia, aarch64 |
| Model | `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` |
| Executor | Ray, `distributed_executor_backend=ray` |
| Topology | TP8, PP1, DP1, expert-parallel off, speculative decoding off |
| Attention backend | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` |
| KV cache dtype | `fp8_ds_mla` |
| CUDA graph | `NONE` |
| Interconnect | RoCEv2, dual 200 Gb/s ConnectX-7 rails, NCCL over IB |

Serve arguments (constant across all trials):

    --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 8 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.83 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120 \
    --enable-chunked-prefill --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}'

## Observed sequence

Timestamps from two independent trials. The starvation warning precedes the worker
death by ~60 s in both.

That warning is the reader-side long-wait message from `acquire_read`, logged by the
EngineCore while it waited on rank 0's response, and it repeats at
`VLLM_RINGBUFFER_WARNING_INTERVAL` (default 60 s). It is a periodic warning, not a
deadline, and nothing is cancelled by it. So it does not show that the block starvation
caused anything; it shows that **rank 0 had stopped answering at least 60 s before its
actor task ended**. The `RuntimeError: cancelled` that follows is raised because
`shutting_down` was set during executor shutdown, so it is downstream of the rank-0
death rather than its cause.

Trial A:

    13:11:01 INFO  [shm_broadcast.py:705] No available shared memory broadcast block
                   found in 60 seconds. This typically happens when some processes
                   are hanging or doing some time-consuming work...
    13:12:05 ERROR [ray_executor_v2.py:514] RayWorkerProc rank=[0] died unexpectedly,
                   shutting down executor.
    13:12:05 ERROR [core.py:1332]   File ".../shm_broadcast.py", line 779, in dequeue
    13:12:05 ERROR [core.py:1332]   File ".../shm_broadcast.py", line 701, in acquire_read
    13:12:05 ERROR [core.py:1332] RuntimeError: cancelled
    13:12:05 ERROR [async_llm.py:704] vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError:
                   EngineCore encountered an issue.

Trial B (same signature, 59 s gap):

    13:35:55 INFO  [shm_broadcast.py:705] No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds
    13:36:54 ERROR [ray_executor_v2.py:514] RayWorkerProc rank=[0] died unexpectedly
    13:36:54 ERROR [core.py:1332] RuntimeError: cancelled
    13:36:54 ERROR [async_llm.py:704] EngineDeadError

Full call path captured on an earlier occurrence:

    core.py:136 __init__
      -> core.py:324 _initialize_kv_caches
        -> abstract.py:124 initialize_from_config
          -> multiproc_executor.py:405 collective_rpc
            -> multiproc_executor.py:91 result
              -> multiproc_executor.py:95 _wait_for_response
                -> multiproc_executor.py:390 get_response  ->  mq.dequeue
                  -> shm_broadcast.py:779 dequeue
                    -> shm_broadcast.py:701 acquire_read
                      -> RuntimeError("cancelled")

**Correction (2026-08-21).** That call path is from the earlier occurrence on a
different configuration (speculative decoding enabled). It is *not* the path Trials A
and B took. Trials A and B died on the first scheduled completion after the engine had
already reported READY:

    core.py:1364 run_busy_loop
      -> core.py:1403 _process_engine_step
        -> core.py:693  step_with_batch_queue
          -> model_output = future.result()

    ... SchedulerOutput(scheduled_new_reqs=[NewRequestData(req_id=cmpl-<id> ...
    "POST /v1/completions HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error

Both phases have been observed: KV-cache initialisation on the earlier occurrence, and
the first request after READY in the two controlled trials. The common element is not
the phase - it is that rank 0 goes silent and then dies, with no cause recorded
anywhere in vLLM's own logs.

## Reproduction

1. Deploy `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` across 8 GB10 nodes with the arguments above.
2. Start the server; wait for the API to bind.
3. Issue an **authenticated completion** request (not `/v1/models`).
4. Repeat the full stop/start cycle.

Roughly 5 of 7 cycles fail. Weight load is ~15 min per cycle, so failures are
expensive to reproduce.

## Expected vs actual

**Expected:** engine start either succeeds or fails loudly; a bound HTTP server
implies a functional engine.

**Actual:** rank 0 dies and the engine core follows it, yet the API server can remain
bound and answer `/v1/models` with 200. `POST /v1/completions` returns no tokens, or
500. A readiness probe on the models endpoint therefore reports success.

## What was ruled out

- **Speculative decoding / MTP** — reproduced with MTP fully disabled.
- **Context length** — reproduced at 16384 after 16384 had previously succeeded;
  also seen at 32768.
- **Kernel OOM** - none on any rank; engine reports 88.73 GiB weights, 1.4 GiB peak
  activation, 2.3 GiB non-torch against a 101.0 GiB budget, and separately advertises
  ~18 GiB of unused headroom. Note that this excludes a *kernel* OOM only. A kill by
  Ray's own memory monitor is **not** excluded: that is recorded in `raylet.out`, which
  we did not have (see "Evidence"). These are unified-memory nodes, and the node hosting
  rank 0 also runs the API server, the engine core, the GCS and the raylet.
- **Interconnect** — NCCL reports `ncclCommInitRank ... Init COMPLETE` on all 8 ranks
  across both IB devices with ECE negotiated in ~2.3 s. Fabric counters show zero
  discards, zero retransmits and zero link events across the affected windows.
- **KV dtype support** — `FlashInferMLASparseSM120Backend` declares
  `fp8_ds_mla` among its `supported_kv_cache_dtypes`.

## Patched-build isolation

This runs on an image with local patches layered on v0.26.0, so the obvious question
is whether those patches are implicated. They are not: **every file in the failure
path is byte-identical between the patched build and an unpatched v0.26.0 build of
the same base.**

| file | unpatched | patched |
|---|---|---|
| `vllm/distributed/device_communicators/shm_broadcast.py` | `7ff67c2ef6b8a33a` | `7ff67c2ef6b8a33a` |
| `vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py` | `fb279ff0e0a08681` | `fb279ff0e0a08681` |
| `vllm/v1/engine/core.py` | `3ae1381a6af841e2` | `3ae1381a6af841e2` |
| `vllm/v1/executor/abstract.py` | `419002195d13cf05` | `419002195d13cf05` |
| `vllm/v1/executor/ray_executor_v2.py` | `5920e5924bd74b85` | `5920e5924bd74b85` |
| `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse.py` | `550079022e858952` | `550079022e858952` |
| **aggregate of all `vllm/**/*.py`** | `af932612311083bf` | `8d3fa2ce4a73bcc0` |

(sha256, first 16 hex chars.) The aggregate row differs, confirming the two images
are genuinely distinct — the patches exist, they simply do not touch any module the
traceback passes through. The local patch set targets speculative-decoding/MTP paths
(`dsa_mtp_index_sharing`, `mtp_compact_shared_topk`, `glm52_mtp_indexer_correctness`),
and this issue reproduces with **speculative decoding disabled**.

## Workaround

Retry the start. Surviving instances are stable. At the observed rate this needs
3–4 attempts (~25 min each), which is not viable for production bring-up, so we
have reverted to vLLM v0.23.0 with `TRITON_MLA_SPARSE` and `bfloat16` KV. That
combination has started reliably every time.

Note the cost of the workaround: v0.23.0's `TRITON_MLA_SPARSE` does not support any
fp8 KV dtype, so reverting forfeits the `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache. Measured on identical
context and utilisation, `fp8_ds_mla` on v0.26.0 gave **152,000 KV tokens / 9.28x max
concurrency** versus **61,184 / 3.73x** on v0.23.0 — a 2.5x capacity difference.

## Suggested follow-up

1. A timeout is probably not the fix. `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` governs the
   frontend's wait for the EngineCore READY message, and in these trials READY had
   already been sent; the 60 s line is `VLLM_RINGBUFFER_WARNING_INTERVAL`, a warning
   interval rather than a deadline. The missing piece is the worker's exit reason (2).
2. Rank 0's own termination reason is not surfaced — the executor reports only
   "died unexpectedly". Propagating the worker's exit cause would make this
   diagnosable in one cycle rather than seven.
3. Consider having the API server refuse to bind, or report unready, when
   `EngineCore` has died, so that `/v1/models` cannot answer 200 for a dead engine.

## Evidence available

Per-rank engine captures from 3 controlled trials (all 8 ranks each), full
orchestration run logs, and fabric counter deltas across each window.

What is **missing** is Ray's own logs. Ray writes them inside the container
(`/tmp/ray/session_*/logs`), and the teardown after each failed trial removed the
containers, so `raylet.out`, `gcs_server.out` and rank 0's `worker-*.err` /
`python-core-worker-*.log` were never captured - which is why this report can say that
rank 0 died but not why. That is now fixed on our side (host-persistent Ray log
directory, plus an all-rank capture that runs before teardown), and rank 0's exit type
and death cause will be posted here once the wedge is reproduced.

title: [Perf][ROCm][Attention] Fuse Kimi-K3 MLA chunked-context gather on AITER
body:
## Purpose

The dense-MLA prefill spends four kernels per context chunk in
`_compute_prefill_context`:
- `vllm::gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache<bf16,bf16,(0),576,64>`
- `Cijk_…MT192x160x64` (`kv_b_proj` expansion)
- `at::native direct_copy` (`k[..., :128] = k_nope`)
- `at::native direct_copy` (`k[..., 128:] = k_pe`)

AITER ships `gather_kv_b_proj`, which does all four in one launch. `AiterMLAImpl._compute_prefill_context`
now calls it per context chunk, with the per-token KV indices built once per step in the metadata builder.
The fused gather runs only without decode context parallelism (`dcp_world_size == 1`); DCP > 1 keeps
main's DCP prefill path.

`AiterMLAImpl._concat_k_nope_k_pe` now calls the already-merged `fused_kimi_k3_mla_kv_concat` (#51772)
instead of two slice-assign copies, gated on the MLA dims that kernel asserts (`STD_TORCH_CHECK` on
128-wide NoPE / 64-wide rope).

## Test Plan

Unit tests: `tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_prefill_fusions.py` (11 cases: fused vs unfused

title: [glm] [pcp] fuse norm rope with pcp cache gather
body:
## Summary

Fuse PCP Q/K preparation, cache quantization, and NVLS publication into one dispatch kernel plus one combine kernel for prefill, mixed, and decode batches.

* Old: bf16 norm/RoPE: output kv_c, k_pe, indexer_k → 3 all-gathers → quantize + cache-insertion 
* New: fused dispatch + NVLS multicast → local cache combine/scatter


### Dispatch

It launches one 256-thread CTA per local token and performs:

- Q RMSNorm, keeping Q local because each rank already holds the query rows it computes.
- KV RMSNorm.
- RoPE on `k_pe`.
- For sparse layers, indexer-K LayerNorm and RoPE.
- Packing directly into a cache-ready representation and NVLS multicast to every PCP rank.

For static E4M3, the fixed transport row is:

```text
| kv_c E4M3: 512 B | k_pe E4M3: 64 B | indexer K E4M3: 128 B | index scale FP32: 4 B | alignment: 12 B | = 720 B/token
```

For `fp8_ds_mla`, the fixed transport row is:

```text
| kv_c E4M3: 512 B | KV tile scales FP32: 16 B | k_pe BF16: 128 B | indexer K E4M3: 128 B | index scale FP32: 4 B | alignment: 12 B | = 800 B/token
```

Full workspace

```text
workspace[double_buffer_index][src rank][max_num_tokens][payload]
```

### Combine

The second kernel reads the received rank-major rows and scatters them into each rank's local paged caches:
- Prefill: tokens from every PCP rank are inserted.
- Decode: tokens are replicated, so they are inserted once from rank 0.

### Scope and limitations

- Requires CUDA and NVLS symmetric-memory multicast.
- Specialized for the GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek-V3.2 MLA dimensions above.
- Each rank retains a persistent double-buffered staging allocation of approximately `2 * num_ubatches * PCP_world_size * max_local_tokens * packed_row_bytes`.

## Performance

GLM-5.2 PCP8 on one 8×B300 node, TP1/PCP8/EP8, BF16 activations, static E4M3 KV cache, a 32K batched-token limit, and a 32K long-prefill threshold.

Default portable PCP pipeline (historical stage profile):

| Stage | Time |
| --- | ---: |
| Fused Q/K norm + K RoPE | 1.441 ms |
| Indexer-K all-gather | 2.064 ms |
| Indexer-K quantization/insertion | 0.423 ms |
| MLA `kv_c` all-gather | 11.044 ms |
| MLA `k_pe` all-gather | 2.349 ms |
| MLA quantization/insertion | 6.931 ms |
| **Total** | **24.252 ms** |

Final fused NVLS pipeline (latest two-run mean):

| Stage | Time |
| --- | ---: |
| Fused norm/RoPE + FP8 quantization + NVLS multicast | 8.228 ms |
| Cache combine/scatter | 0.898 ms |
| **Total** | **9.127 ms** |

Controlled current-stack full-forward A/B from the Kineto `execute_context_1(32768)_generation_0(0)` GPU annotation:

| Metric | Default portable PCP | Final fused NVLS | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Mean across PCP ranks | 357.781 ms | 343.875 ms | **−3.89%** |
| Slowest PCP rank | 357.933 ms | 344.109 ms | **−3.86%** |

Each value is the arithmetic mean of two fresh-process runs. The portable baseline and pre-optimization fused path were measured in one current-stack ABBA; the final fused kernel was then measured in a second ABBA against that fused control. All runs used the same B300 node, model snapshot, source tree, eager-mode configuration, exact 32K input, warmup, and profiler procedure. The second ABBA measured the slowest-rank fused forward at 345.069 ms before these cache-overhead changes and 344.109 ms after them (−0.960 ms, −0.28%). "Default portable PCP" means the Triton fused norm/RoPE + PCP gather + cache-insert path.

## Relationship to existing work

- #52046 supplies the DeepSeek-V3.2 PCP gather-and-insert baseline now on `main`.
- #52839 moved the PCP attention helpers into `vllm/v1/attention/ops/pcp.py`; this branch is ported onto that layout.
- #52863 writes final rows directly into symmetric persistent cache replicas through P2P peer pointers.
- #49517 has the same replicated-KV-update goal using CUDA VMM peer mappings and direct peer stores.

This PR uses a different design from #52863/#49517: NVLS multicast into transient symmetric staging followed by a receiver-local paged-cache combine. It keeps cache tensors, allocation, and ownership ordinary and receiver-local, supports PCP2/4/8, and integrates with the common DeepSeek-V3.2 PCP path.

title: [RFC]: Experimental Recirculation for causal decoder models
body:
## Motivation

[Recirculation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17981) improves a pretrained decoder without changing weights by norm-matching a deep residual-stream activation, mixing it into an earlier residual boundary, and rerunning the upper layers. The first pass supplies the current token's logits; the rerun overwrites its upper-layer KV entries so later tokens attend to the recirculated representation.

This RFC proposes experimental vLLM support for that execution pattern. A working implementation is available at [mihir-s-05/vllm@`e32222290`](https://github.com/mihir-s-05/vllm/commit/e3222229016064f47b47b43d2234bc56a0498923).

## Proposed change

### Configuration

Accept a validated `recirculation_config` through `--hf-overrides`:

```json
{
  "source_layer": 11,
  "destination_layer": 4,
  "alpha": 0.15,
  "beta": null,
  "ramp_tokens": 10,
  "wavefront": true
}
```

The parser is engine-level, validates the full grammar before deciding whether a configuration is an identity, and supports both ordinary `[tokens]` positions and text-token `[dimensions, tokens]` MRoPE positions.

### Model capability boundary

The scheduler, pending recurrent-state buffer, KV-slot remapping, and CUDA-graph specialization are shared engine features. Residual-decoder implementations opt in with a capability interface and a common decoder mixin. This prevents an unreviewed model subclass from inheriting support accidentally while allowing family-specific state snapshot/restore logic.

The current adapters cover:

- serial and wavefront: Gemma 3/4, Llama/Llama 4, Mistral/Mixtral, Qwen 2/3/3 MoE, GLM-4 MoE, MiniMax-M2, MiMo-V2, Step-3.5;
- serial only: DeepSeek V2/V3/V3.2, GLM-4.7-Flash, GPT-OSS, MiniMax-M3, Qwen3-Next, and Qwen 3.5 dense/MoE.

DeepSeek-V4 hyperconnections, multimodal wrappers, diffusion/non-causal backbones, pipeline parallelism, and Model Runner V2 are not enabled.

### Execution semantics

Serial execution runs the normal decoder stack, returns its final hidden state for logits, mixes the source and destination residuals, restores family-specific recurrent state where needed, and reruns layers above the destination. The rerun overwrites upper-layer KV state.

Wavefront execution preserves the same token dependency while batching the previous token's recurrent upper stack with the current token's normal upper stack. After a one-token warmup, each upper attention layer overwrites the previous token's KV entry before the current token consumes it. The current implementation limits this path to one sequence and one scheduled token, FlashAttention, no prefix caching, and no DP/DCP/SP/PP.

Prefill with a one-token threshold is exact tokenwise recurrence. Larger chunks are an explicit blockwise quality/throughput approximation.

### Recurrent and MoE families

MoE routing remains part of each rerun: Recirculation changes the residual entering the upper stack, so experts may be selected differently. No model-specific expert script is required.

Qwen3-Next and Qwen 3.5 need an additional rule because their convolution/GDN states update in place. Their adapters snapshot active state slots before the normal upper pass and restore them before the recurrent rerun. They remain serial-only because the current two-token FlashAttention wavefront cannot represent those recurrent state transitions.

All speculative configurations, including EAGLE/DFlash auxiliary hidden-state extraction, are rejected initially. Supporting them requires an explicit definition for draft-token recurrence and auxiliary-state ownership.

## Validation

All results below were collected on an RTX 3080 10 GB after rebasing onto current `main`.

- Focused regression suites: 76 passed.
- Repository pre-commit stack passed, including Ruff, formatting, Markdown, mypy 3.10, import rules, SPDX, and CUDA API checks.
- No-download GPU matrix: all 20 documented families generated with four-layer BF16 dummy models through real attention/MoE/recurrent kernels.
- MRoPE ramping: Qwen 3.5 dense and MoE passed with `ramp_tokens=10`.
- Compiled Gemma 3 dummy comparison:
  - no-op was bit-identical to baseline;
  - serial and wavefront produced identical token IDs;
  - maximum serial/wavefront selected-token log-probability difference was `1.235e-4`.
- Real `google/gemma-3-1b-pt`, compiled BF16, the same 16 fixed C4 windows (16,368 scored tokens):
  - baseline perplexity 19.1576, mean prefill latency 7.9496 s;
  - wavefront perplexity 16.9613, mean prefill latency 8.4007 s;
  - 11.46% lower perplexity and 5.67% higher mean prefill latency on this small sample.

The branch contains the commands, harnesses, model/config revisions, window hashes, and a compact RTX 3080 result table. Dummy elapsed times are treated only as compatibility evidence because they include startup and JIT work.

## Alternatives considered

- **Gemma-only implementation.** Simpler initially, but duplicates identical residual-stack logic across families and cannot coordinate scheduling/KV semantics centrally.
- **Automatic support for every decoder subclass.** Rejected because recurrent state, hyperconnections, per-layer embeddings, and attention backends require explicit capability review.
- **Serial execution only.** Correct but leaves avoidable upper-stack launch/dispatch overhead; retained as the compatibility path while wavefront is opt-in.
- **Speculative decoding with undefined auxiliary semantics.** Rejected until recurrence over draft blocks and auxiliary hidden states is designed and tested.

## Feedback period

At least one week. The main questions are:

1. Is a model capability interface plus shared residual-decoder mixin the right abstraction boundary?
2. Should experimental Recirculation remain an `hf_overrides` feature or gain a first-class engine argument?
3. Are the initial restrictions appropriate for an experimental merge?
4. What additional real-weight model-family evidence should be required before broadening the opt-in list?

## AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, review fixes, regression harnesses, and benchmark analysis. The reported results were measured on the stated hardware, and the branch includes reproducible commands and tests.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Searched for relevant issues and pull requests using `recirculation`, `residual stream recurrence`, `looped transformer`, and `recurrent depth`; no duplicate proposal was found.
- [x] Reviewed the project documentation and contribution requirements.

title: [Core][Model] Add experimental Recirculation support
body:
## Purpose

Add experimental [Recirculation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17981) execution for causal residual-decoder models.

Recirculation feeds a norm-matched deep residual activation into a shallower boundary, returns logits from the normal pass, and reruns the upper stack so later tokens attend to recirculated KV state. The implementation provides:

- an engine-level, fully validated `recirculation_config` parser;
- explicit model capability negotiation and a shared residual-decoder execution mixin;
- correct serial execution plus an optimized two-token wavefront;
- scheduler state, KV-slot remapping, and dedicated CUDA-graph handling;
- recurrent-state snapshot/restore for Qwen3-Next and Qwen 3.5;
- adapters for 20 current dense, MoE, MLA, and recurrent model families;
- reproducible real-weight and no-download GPU validation harnesses.

Architecture discussion: [RFC #53178](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53178).

### Configuration

```bash
vllm serve google/gemma-3-1b-pt \
  --hf-overrides '{
    "recirculation_config": {
      "source_layer": 11,
      "destination_layer": 4,
      "alpha": 0.15,
      "ramp_tokens": 10,
      "wavefront": true
    }
  }' \
  --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --long-prefill-token-threshold 1 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

An identity configuration (`alpha=0`, with convex/default `beta`) is validated and then becomes a true no-op.

### Current restrictions

- Model Runner V1 only; Recirculation automatically selects it.
- Speculative decoding and auxiliary hidden-state extraction are rejected.
- No pipeline parallelism, multimodal wrappers, non-causal diffusion backbones, or DeepSeek-V4 hyperconnections.
- Wavefront currently requires one sequence/one scheduled token, FlashAttention, no prefix cache, and no DP/DCP/SP/PP.
- Qwen3-Next/Qwen 3.5 and other incompatible attention/recurrent backends use serial execution.
- MiniMax-M3 sparse attention was disabled in the tiny fixture, so its optional custom sparse-attention kernel is not covered by this PR's GPU matrix.

## Test Plan

Focused regression tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/model_executor/test_recirculation.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_gemma3_recirculation.py \
  tests/benchmarks/test_recirculation.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_jit_warmup_migration.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_hybrid_block_table_initialization \
  tests/transformers_utils/test_minimax_m3_config.py

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_config.py -k recirculation
```

Repository checks:

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  benchmarks/benchmark_recirculation.py \
  benchmarks/validate_recirculation_adapters.py \
  docs/features/recirculation.md \
  tests/benchmarks/test_recirculation.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_gemma3_recirculation.py \
  tests/test_config.py \
  vllm/config/__init__.py \
  vllm/config/recirculation.py \
  vllm/config/vllm.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_next.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/recirculation.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py
```

GPU validation uses `benchmarks/validate_recirculation_adapters.py` in separate processes for baseline/no-op/serial/wavefront and every documented family. It creates four-layer local configs with dummy weights and downloads no weights or tokenizer.

Real-weight quality uses `benchmarks/benchmark_recirculation.py` with the pinned Gemma 3 1B revision and the same pre-tokenized 16-window C4 file for both arms.

## Test Result

- Focused regressions: **73 passed**.
- Recirculation configuration tests: **3 passed**.
- Full pre-commit stack over all changed files: **passed** (Ruff, format, typos, Markdown, mypy 3.10, SPDX, import/config/CUDA API checks).
- `git diff --check`: **passed**.
- DCO: all seven commits signed off.
- No-download RTX 3080 matrix: **20/20 families passed** through real GPU engine paths.
- Qwen 3.5 dense and MoE MRoPE ramping: **passed** with `ramp_tokens=10`.
- Compiled Gemma 3 dummy:
  - baseline and no-op token IDs/log probabilities: **bit-identical**;
  - serial and wavefront token IDs: **identical**;
  - max selected-token log-probability difference: **1.235e-4**.
- Real compiled BF16 `google/gemma-3-1b-pt`, 16 fixed C4 windows / 16,368 scored tokens:
  - baseline: perplexity **19.1576**, mean prefill **7.9496 s**, decode **194.97 tok/s**;
  - wavefront: perplexity **16.9613**, mean prefill **8.4007 s**, decode **181.90 tok/s**;
  - wavefront: **11.46% lower perplexity**, **5.67% higher mean prefill latency**, and **6.70% lower decode throughput** on this small sample.

The documentation includes the full 20-family result table, methodology, revision behavior, benchmark beta support, memory-measurement fallback, and interpretation caveats.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open issues and all PRs for `recirculation`, `residual stream recurrence`, `looped transformer`, `recurrent depth`, this branch name, and the proposed title. No duplicate implementation or RFC was found.

## AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, code review fixes, test/harness development, and benchmark analysis. Results in this PR were produced by the committed harnesses on the stated hardware; the branch was also independently reviewed before these follow-up fixes.

title: [Doc] Fix local input path in run-batch examples across docs
body:
## Purpose

Fix the local input path in `vllm run-batch` examples across multiple docs.

Affected files:
- `docs/cli/README.md`
- `examples/features/openai_batch/README.md`

The examples use `-i features/openai_batch/openai_example_batch.jsonl` (or `cat`, `aws s3 cp` with the same path), but the actual file is at `examples/features/openai_batch/openai_example_batch.jsonl`. There is no `features/` directory at the repo root, so running the commands from the root directory fails with `FileNotFoundError`. The remote-file example in the same docs already uses the `examples/` prefix, making the inconsistency obvious.

## Why not duplicating an existing PR

Searched `gh issue list` / `gh pr list` for "run-batch" / "openai_batch" path issues: no open issue or PR addresses this. Related PRs are code changes (#47697, #12430) not documentation.

## Test Plan

Run the old command from the repo root:

    vllm run-batch -i features/openai_batch/openai_example_batch.jsonl ...

This fails with:

    FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'features/openai_batch/openai_example_batch.jsonl'

After correcting the path to `examples/features/openai_batch/openai_example_batch.jsonl`, the file is read successfully.

## Test Result

Verified on Ubuntu 24.04 with vLLM 0.27.1 — the path issue is resolved after the fix.

## AI Assistance

This PR was drafted with AI assistance; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Description of the bug

Streaming tool calls (`stream: true`) on DeepSeek-V4-Pro with the `deepseek_v4` tool call parser leak raw DSML markup into tool call arguments. Non-streaming mode works correctly.

## Reproduction

### Hosted
```python
import json, requests

BASE = "http://<server>:8000/v1"
MODEL = "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro"

tools = [{
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
        "name": "get_weather",
        "description": "Get weather for a location",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "location": {"type": "string"},
                "date": {"type": "string"}
            },
            "required": ["location"]
        }
    }
}]

messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "What's the weather in Paris and Tokyo tomorrow?"}]

resp = requests.post(f"{BASE}/chat/completions", json={
    "model": MODEL,
    "messages": messages,
    "tools": tools,
    "tool_choice": "required",
    "stream": True,
}, stream=True, timeout=120)

for line in resp.iter_lines():
    if not line: continue
    line = line.decode("utf-8")
    if line.startswith("data: "):
        data = line[6:]
        if data == "[DONE]": break
        chunk = json.loads(data)
        delta = chunk["choices"][0].get("delta", {})
        if delta.get("tool_calls"):
            print(json.dumps(delta["tool_calls"]))
```
**Expected**: clean argument deltas like `{"location": "Paris"}`

**Actual**: DSML markup leaks into arguments:
```json
{"tool_calls": [{"index": 0, "function": {"arguments": "{\"location\": \""}}]}
{"tool_calls": [{"index": 0, "function": {"arguments": "Paris</\uff5cDSML\uff5cparameter"}}]}
{"tool_calls": [{"index": 0, "function": {"arguments": "\", \"date\": \""}}]}
```
### Regex-level reproduction (no model, GPU, or server required)

```python
import re, json

_DSML = "｜DSML｜"
_ESCAPED_DSML = re.escape(_DSML)

_PARAM_RE = re.compile(
    rf'<{_ESCAPED_DSML}parameter\s+name="([^"]+)"\s+string="(true|false)">'
    rf"(.*?)</{_ESCAPED_DSML}parameter>",
    re.DOTALL,
)
_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE = re.compile(
    rf'<{_ESCAPED_DSML}parameter\s+name="([^"]+)"\s+string="(true|false)">'
    rf"(.*)$",
    re.DOTALL,
)

def _dsml_arg_converter(raw_args, partial):
    params = {}
    last_end = 0
    for m in _PARAM_RE.finditer(raw_args):
        name, is_str, value = m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)
        params[name] = value if is_str == "true" else value
        last_end = m.end()
    if partial:
        pm = _PARTIAL_PARAM_RE.search(raw_args, last_end)
        if pm:
            params[pm.group(1)] = pm.group(3)
    return json.dumps(params, ensure_ascii=False)

# slot.args with a partial closing tag (missing final >)
raw = "<｜DSML｜parameter name=\"location\" string=\"true\">Paris</｜DSML｜parameter"
print(_dsml_arg_converter(raw, partial=True))
# Output: {"location": "Paris</｜DSML｜parameter"}
# Expected: {"location": "Paris"}
```
## Possible root cause

PR #45877 (commit `fb5291b35b`, July 3 2026) ported DeepSeek V4 from the hand-written `DeepSeekV32ToolParser` to the generic `StreamingParserEngine` framework. The new code introduced `_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE` with `(.*)$` to capture in-progress parameter values during streaming.

## Impact

- `stream: true` with `tool_choice: required`: DSML markup leaks into argument JSON
- `stream: true` with `tool_choice: auto`: tool calls emitted with empty `{}` arguments (no arg deltas streamed)
- `stream: false`: works correctly (unaffected)
- Agent harnesses (e.g. opencode, Claude Code) that use streaming mode fail to execute tool calls

## Proposed fix

Change `_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE` to use a negative lookahead that stops at DSML tag prefixes instead of greedily capturing everything:

```python
_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE = re.compile(
    rf'<{_ESCAPED_DSML}parameter\s+name="([^"]+)"\s+string="(true|false)">'
    rf"((?:(?!</?{_ESCAPED_DSML}).)*)",
    re.DOTALL,
)
```

## Related issues
- #40800 (closed), but the parser has changed since then

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Fix DeepSeek V4 DSML markup leaking into streaming t…
body:
## Purpose

Fixes streaming tool call argument corruption in the DeepSeek V4 parser where DSML closing tag fragments leak into tool call arguments.

`_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE` used a greedy `(.*)$` capture that swallowed partial DSML closing tags (e.g. `Paris</｜DSML｜parameter` without the final `>`) into parameter values during streaming. Replaced with a tempered greedy token using a negative lookahead that stops at DSML tag prefixes:

```python
# Before
rf"(.*)$"
# After
rf"((?:(?!</?{_ESCAPED_DSML}).)*)"
```

This preserves literal `<` in values (the concern from #46047) while preventing partial closing tags from leaking into arguments.

## Root cause

Introduced in #45877 which ported DeepSeek V4 to the `StreamingParserEngine`. The old hand-written parser (`DeepSeekV32ToolParser`, #42879) used a buffer-and-split approach that never ran a regex on partial args.

## Verification

Tested on a live 8xH200 deployment (vLLM v0.27.1, dspark speculative decoding):
- `stream: true, tool_choice: required`: DSML markup no longer leaks into arguments (3/3 runs clean)
- `stream: true, tool_choice: auto`: tool calls now stream proper incremental argument deltas (previously emitted empty `{}`)
- `stream: false`: unchanged (always worked)

## Test plan

Added two regression tests in `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py`:
- `test_partial_does_not_capture_closing_tag_prefix` — partial closing tag in a single parameter
- `test_partial_with_complete_param_and_partial_closing_tag` — complete parameter followed by a partial closing tag

AI assistance was used. Every changed line was reviewed and tested.

Closes #53227

body:

title: [Performance] MooncakeConnector emits one RDMA descriptor per (layer, block) — but with the unified paged KV layout a block's layers are contiguous; page-level descriptors give up to 19x faster PD transfers
body:
## Summary

On vLLM ≥0.26 the KV cache pool is a **single unified allocation** (`num_segments=1`):
every layer's cache tensor is a strided view over one storage, with block stride equal
to the pool page size, and **one physical block's data for all layers lives contiguously
inside one page**.

`MooncakeConnector`'s sender, however, still iterates **per layer region**, emitting one
transfer descriptor per `(layer_region, block)`. For a hybrid-attention model
(DeepSeek-style, 43 layers / 5 KV groups) this shreds a physically contiguous page into
~61 tiny descriptors (avg ~16 KB, compressed layers contribute sub-KB fragments), and a
1M-token prompt produces **254k descriptors per rank**. Transfer throughput then becomes
descriptor-count-bound and collapses with prompt length, while the underlying data was
contiguous all along.

The existing coalescing path (`_can_coalesce_block_transfers`) can never fire on this
layout: its gate requires `transfer_len == region.block_len`, but with the unified pool
`block_len` is always the full page (~1.04 MB here) while a single layer's per-block
payload is 0.8–100 KB. We instrumented the gate in production: **668/668 evaluations
returned False for exactly this reason** (block-id runs themselves were nearly perfectly
contiguous, offsets all zero).

## Environment

- vLLM 0.26.0, TP=4 (symmetric PD), `--block-size 256`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`
- Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash (43 layers, 5 KV cache groups: full-attention + MLA
  compressed + sliding-window + GDN state)
- `MultiConnector` with `MooncakeConnector` (kv_producer/kv_consumer), RDMA (RoCE,
  2×200 Gbps bond per GPU, GPU↔NIC PIX)
- Engine: `Available KV cache memory: 84.49 GiB`, `num_blocks: 87,253` per GPU
  → page = 84.49 GiB / 87,253 ≈ 1.0397 MB; all 167 registered layer regions report
  `block_len == 1,039,680`

## Measured impact (before)

Single cold request, per-rank connector stats (`Avg xfer time` = wall clock of
`batch_transfer_sync_write`):

| ISL | MB/rank | descriptors | xfer avg | GB/s/rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16K | 81 | 4.6K | 4.9 ms | 16.8 |
| 64K | 263 | 16.4K | 19.6 ms | 13.4 |
| 256K | 996 | 64K | 155 ms | 6.4 |
| 1M | 3,929 | 254K | **1,867 ms (P90 3,179)** | **2.1** |

Bare TransferEngine on the same NIC pair sustains ~44-45 GB/s flat, so the gap is
entirely descriptor-side. (The per-descriptor cost also degrades superlinearly at depth
due to a hot-spin O(N) status poll in Mooncake's sync wrapper — filed separately against
kvcache-ai/Mooncake.)

## Root cause (code)

1. Region iteration & per-block emission: `mooncake_connector.py::_build_transfer_params`
   — per `(region, block)` pointer append; regions come from `_expand_transfer_regions`
   (one per layer, two for split-K/V layers).
2. Coalescing gate: `_can_coalesce_block_transfers` requires
   `transfer_len == local/remote region.block_len` with zero offsets. With the unified
   pool, `block_len = cache.stride(0) * esize = page`, while `kv_block_len`
   (`layer_spec.page_size_bytes` for MLA, `block_len // 2` for split-KV) is a small
   fraction of it — the gate is structurally unsatisfiable, and per-layer cross-block
   merging is impossible anyway (a layer's consecutive blocks are 1 page apart).
3. The correct merge axis is the **page**: a block's all-layer data is contiguous, and
   physically-consecutive block ids form contiguous multi-page spans.

## Proposed fix (working patch, results below)

When (a) all of a KV group's registered regions share `block_len == page`, (b) layer
offsets fit within the page, and (c) the remote layout is isomorphic (same tp_size,
same page, same offset multiset — exchanged via the existing `MooncakeXferMetadata`),
emit descriptors per **(group, contiguous block run) × whole pages**:

```
src = page_origin + run_start * page ; len = run_len * page
```

Safety: a physical block id is exclusively owned by one (request, group), so writing the
full page (including other layers' unused slots) into the remote block's page cannot
clobber live data (vLLM never zero-initializes blocks anyway). NULL block id (0) pairs
are dropped; any precondition failure falls back to the existing per-layer path
(asymmetric/heterogeneous TP unaffected).

### Results with the patch (same hardware/model)

| ISL | descriptors | xfer avg | GB/s/rank | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64K | 16,425 → 237 | 7.4 ms | 37.4 | 2.6× |
| 256K | 63,979 → 355 | 29.6 ms | 35.1 | 5.2× |
| 1M | 254,195 → 3,148 | **185 ms** | 22.1 | **10.1×** |

With `MC_SLICE_SIZE=256KB` on top (Mooncake-side knob), the curve is flat
**41.6–42.3 GB/s for 16K→1M** (92-94% of the bare-metal ceiling); 1M transfer is
98.7 ms (P90 100.8) — **18.9× total**, and byte inflation from page padding is only
4-6% in practice (block runs are long).

Correctness validated by: needle-in-haystack retrieval at 5 depths × 32K/128K (5/5),
concurrent seeding + retrieval (16/16 across two rounds, no cross-request bleed),
D-side full/partial prefix-hit paths (delta tail-alignment preserved), zero
failed/expired transfers throughout.

## Ask

Is there interest in upstreaming a page-level transfer path for the unified layout
(gated + fallback as above)? We're happy to open a PR with the patch and benchmarks.
Related but distinct: the same per-(layer,block) shredding presumably affects other
connectors that iterate `kv_caches` per layer for RDMA transfer.

title: [Bugfix][R3] Unwrap UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs when selecting the routed-experts KV group
body:
## Purpose --enable-return-routed-experts` crashes at worker init on DeepSeek-V4: ``` ValueError: Routed-experts capture requires a full-attention KV cache group. ``` `get_routed_experts_attn_gid` scans groups with `isinstance(group.kv_cache_spec, FullAttentionSpec)`, but `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` subclasses `KVCacheSpec` directly, so no group matches. This hits DeepSeek-V4 (`group_and_unify_kv_cache_specs` wraps every group) and the `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs.from_specs` path. Worker-side only — the scheduler gets an unwrapped config from `generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config`. Regression from `42ab184ea7` (#50721), which merged the scheduler and worker gid lookups and replaced the worker's `return 0` fallback with a raise. The scan never handled the wrapper, but the fallback had been masking it — and masking it correctly, since group 0 is the MLA group in every wrapped layout. Fix: unwrap the wrapper, requiring *all* wrapped layers to be full attention. Mixing can't happen via `is_uniform_type` today, but the wrapper is also built directly (`_project_kv_cache_groups_to_worker`), and a group with a recycling sliding-window layer has no stable slot layout to key routing data by — so fail closed. ## Test Plan New test `test_routed_experts_attention_group_unwraps_uniform_type_specs` builds a DeepSeek-V4-shaped layout from real `MLAAttentionSpec` / `SlidingWindowMLASpec` (SWA wrapper at gid 0, MLA wrapper at gid 1). The existing test monkeypatches a stub `FullAttentionSpec` and never constructs a wrapper. Both suites are `cpu_test`-marked. ```bash python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py -q python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_routed_experts_capture_monolithic.py \ tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py -q pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts_capturer.py \ tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py ``` End to end tests on verl for DeepSeek V4 RL training. ## Test Result All test cases and e2e passes without any error now. ---

title: [Bug]: extract_hidden_states overestimates DeepSeek-V4 KV cache memory
body:
## Your current environment

The failing baseline and patched run used the same image, model, hardware, and
serving configuration. The patched run replaced only the vLLM wheel.

```text
Base image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.26.0-cu129-ubuntu2404
Baseline vLLM: 0.26.0+cu129
Fix validation vLLM: 0.26.1rc1.dev657+g793ca6998.cu129
Fix source commit: 793ca6998adfa5a3ab22d6012dee78044b8ba901
OS: Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS (x86_64)
Python: 3.12.3
PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu129
CUDA runtime: 12.9.86
NVIDIA driver: 580.159.03
GPU: 4 x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3
Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash
Tensor parallelism: TP=4
Hidden-state layers: 40, 41, 42, and the final layer 43
Hidden-state dtype and size: bf16, 4096
KV cache dtype: fp8
Cache block size: 256
Maximum model length: 8192
Prefix caching: enabled
CUDA Graph mode: FULL_DECODE_ONLY
```

## 🐛 Describe the bug

Enabling hidden-state extraction on DeepSeek-V4 causes the KV-cache capacity
calculation to overestimate the required memory and reject engine startup after
the model has loaded successfully.

With TP=4 on four H100 80GB GPUs, the model uses approximately 38.87 GiB per
GPU. The subsequent KV-cache validation incorrectly reports that an 8,192-token
request requires 581.48 GiB of KV-cache memory:

```text
ValueError: To serve at least one request with the model's max seq len (8192),
(581.48 GiB KV cache is needed, which is larger than the available KV cache
memory (21.61 GiB). Based on the available memory, the estimated maximum model
length is 288.
```

On the same model and hardware, disabling hidden-state extraction allows a
maximum model length of 256,000. The failure is therefore specific to the
hidden-state cache being included in capacity accounting.

### Root cause

Hidden-state extraction registers a `CacheOnlyAttentionLayer` backed by
`HiddenStateCacheSpec`. Because `HiddenStateCacheSpec` inherits from
`MLAAttentionSpec`, DeepSeek-V4's model-specific grouping path classifies it as
a regular MLA layer.

For four bf16 hidden states with hidden size 4096 and block size 256, the
hidden-state page is approximately 8 MiB:

```text
256 * 4 * 4096 * 2 bytes = 8 MiB
```

This page is included in DeepSeek-V4 MLA packing and causes the compressor and
sliding-window cache pages to be padded to 8 MiB. The generic logic that
separates `HiddenStateCacheSpec` is not reached because the DeepSeek-V4 branch
returns earlier. The affected grouping and early-return logic remained
unchanged in the subsequent release inspected during this investigation, so
the bug persists wherever this original code path is present.

### Expected behavior

The hidden-state cache should be excluded from DeepSeek-V4 MLA/SWA tuple
grouping, restored exactly once as an independent cache group, and accounted
for using its own page geometry. Enabling hidden-state extraction should not
inflate the page sizes or memory estimates of the attention cache groups.

With the hidden-state cache isolated, the same startup reaches KV-cache
initialization and reports:

```text
Available KV cache memory: 21.61 GiB
GPU KV cache size: 6,199 tokens
Maximum concurrency for 8,192 tokens per request: 0.76x
```

The incorrect 581.48 GiB estimate is no longer produced, and the engine
continues past the KV-cache validation that previously raised the exception.

### Additional context

- A fix and regression tests are available in
  [#53074](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53074).
- [#39949](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39949) added generic
  hidden-state cache isolation for hybrid-attention models, but that logic is
  below DeepSeek-V4's model-specific early return.
- [#50894](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50894) addresses a separate
  tensor-parallel page-size alignment issue.
- [#49811](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49811) adds Model Runner V2
  support for `extract_hidden_states`; it does not change DeepSeek-V4 KV-cache
  grouping.

## Before submitting a new issue

- [x] Searched open and closed vLLM issues for the DeepSeek-V4-specific
  `HiddenStateCacheSpec` grouping failure and found no existing report.
- [x] Asked the chatbot on the vLLM documentation site; it identified this as a
  known issue and pointed to the open fix in #53074.
- [x] Added the exact image, runtime, hardware, and serving configuration used
  for the failing baseline and patched validation run.
- [x] Checked the report for tokens, credentials, private URLs, internal model
  paths, and confidential data.

Set `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=900` for the release-branch DSv4-Flash disaggregated CI step. title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Flash: non-deterministic output at temperature=0, rate scales with concurrency
body:
### Your current environment

```
vLLM       : 0.27.1 (installed from PyPI wheel, verified unmodified —
                     all 4735 .py files hash-match the wheel)
Model      : nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-nvfp4-DSpark  (NVFP4, DSpark draft head)
GPU        : NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, 1x, TP=1  (compute capability 10.3)
Driver     : 580.126.09
torch      : 2.13.0+cu132   (CUDA 13.2)
OS         : Ubuntu 24.04
```

Serve command:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-nvfp4-DSpark \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --trust-remote-code --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' \
  --attention-config '{"use_fp4_indexer_cache":true}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 128
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Summary:** with `temperature=0`, the same prompt returns **different completions**
depending only on how many requests are in flight. Greedy decoding should be
reproducible, so any variation is a bug. The rate rises with concurrency.

#### Reproducer

`repro.py` — sends the identical greedy request N times and counts distinct completions:

```python
import concurrent.futures as cf, json, sys, time, urllib.request
from collections import Counter

URL   = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions"
MODEL = "nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-nvfp4-DSpark"

IDS = [
    "c_mhw9v76obuh72x98f4pb8xr3",  "o_ftcj97ua0p5heapj5fpng02e",
    "c_3exww35axs739igmh42hvph1g", "c_8oold74tm25kw4uag86kyj16z",
    "c_6adnmt0f3gs4xfl4ne2x5zkjo", "c_z72re6iq4gltfujr1zrwll11y",
    "o_9klm2xr7ta4bnvq8wsdf31hgc", "c_pw4nz8tqm6ykxj02hcv5rb7ed",
]
PROMPT = ("Echo each of these identifiers back to me, one per line, prefixed "
          "with 'ECHO: '. Do not modify any character. Do not add commentary.\n\n"
          + "\n".join(IDS))
BODY = {"model": MODEL, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": PROMPT}],
        "temperature": 0.0, "max_tokens": 2000}

def call(_):
    req = urllib.request.Request(URL, data=json.dumps(BODY).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    return json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=600).read()
                      )["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]

n, conc = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2])
if conc == 1:
    outs = [call(i) for i in range(n)]
else:
    with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=conc) as ex:
        outs = [f.result() for f in cf.as_completed(
            [ex.submit(call, i) for i in range(n)])]

v = Counter(outs)
minority = sum(c for _, c in v.most_common()[1:])
print(f"n={len(outs)} conc={conc} DISTINCT={len(v)} "
      f"minority={minority} ({100*minority/len(outs):.2f}%)")
print("EXPECTED at temperature=0: DISTINCT=1")
```

```bash
python repro.py 500 32
```

#### Results — stock 0.27.1, 10/10 runs non-deterministic

Each row is an independent run against the same server.

| concurrency | n | runs | minority-output rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8  | 400 | 2 | 0.25%, 0.50% |
| 16 | 400 | 3 | 2.25%, 1.75%, 1.75% |
| 32 | 500 | 5 | 2.40%, 1.00%, 0.40%, 1.20%, 0.80% |

`DISTINCT` was >1 in **every** run (up to 8 distinct completions in 500 requests).
"minority" = responses differing from the modal completion.

A typical divergence — one identifier comes back altered, the rest of the
completion is byte-identical:

```
majority: ...ECHO: c_6adnmt0f3gs4xfl4ne2x5zkjo...
variant : ...ECHO: o_9klm5t0f3gs4xfl4ne2x5zkjo...
```

#### This is not float non-determinism from reduction order

Requesting `top_logprobs=20` at the divergent position:

```
conc=1  (correct):        conc=32 (corrupt):
  '2'    0.000000           '5'   -1.377942
  'x'  -18.375000           '7'   -2.252942
  '3'  -20.250000           '6'   -2.377942
  '27' -21.125000           '8'   -2.502942
  '22' -21.125000           '4'   -2.627942
```

The correct arm is maximally confident: an **18-logprob** gap between top-1 and
top-2 (~1e8 probability ratio). The corrupt arm collapses to a near-uniform
distribution over digits, margin **0.1–2.0**.

Batched-reduction float noise perturbs logits on the order of 1e-3 and could
only flip a near-tie. Turning an 18-logprob margin into a coin flip means the
**attention output feeding that position differs**, not that a tie broke the
other way. The divergence also lands at a consistent token index across runs.

#### Notes

- Reproduced on **unmodified** 0.27.1 from PyPI (hash-verified against the wheel).
- Also reproduces with `--enforce-eager` (4/5 runs non-deterministic), so it is
  not CUDA-graph capture/replay.
- Not `seed`-related: at `temperature=0`, `SamplingParams.sampling_type` returns
  `GREEDY` before `seed` is consulted (`sampling_params.py`), and passing a seed
  changes nothing.
- Requests were verified to complete successfully; runs with any transport error
  were discarded rather than counted.

The flags above are the standard serving configuration for this model
(sparse-MLA block size, fp8 KV cache, FP4 indexer cache, DSpark draft head).

I have not isolated the mechanism and don't want to speculate. Happy to run
further diagnostics on this hardware — e.g. with speculative decoding or prefix
caching disabled, or with different `num_speculative_tokens` — if that helps.

title: [7/N][KV Connector][NIXL] Stage host KV reads through device memory
body:
## Summary

- Stage same-node NIXL reads into registered device buffers when every destination region is host memory.
- Pipeline the completed device-to-host copies without reporting a request complete until both transfer legs finish.
- Bound shutdown and retain staging slots through asynchronous copy completion, including failure and abort paths.

This avoids UCX's slow TCP-loopback path for direct device-to-host NIXL reads while leaving device-resident and mixed layouts on their existing path.

## Duplicate check

Open-PR searches found no other PR implementing same-node NIXL host-read staging. This is a generic NIXL prerequisite used by the HiSparse stack, rather than a HiSparse-specific path.

## Tests

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py -k host_stager -q
```

Result: 4 passed. Changed-file pre-commit hooks also passed.

## Evaluation

title: [Bugfix][KV offload] Validate computed device pointers before copy
body:
## Problem

`compute_sub_block_ptrs()` in `vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py` derives raw
device addresses from `data_ptr()`, `stride(0)` and `shape[1]`:

```python
base_ptr = tensor.data_ptr()
row_stride = tensor.stride(0)
block_page_size = tensor.shape[1] // blocks_per_chunk
all_ptrs = (base_ptr + block_ids * row_stride) + sub_offsets
```

Those addresses are handed to the swap kernel, which dereferences them as
`int64*`:

```python
src = tl.load(src_addrs + job).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64))
words = tl.load(sizes + job) // 8
data = tl.load(src + idx, mask=idx < words, other=0)
```

The `mask` bounds the copy against the *declared* size, not against the
allocation, and nothing validates the pointers themselves. The arithmetic
assumes a flat, unpadded row layout; a cache whose pages carry alignment
padding produces addresses that walk off the buffer.

### Reproduction

Enabling `OffloadingConnector` with a `fs_python` tier on DeepSeek-V4, whose MLA
pages are padded to 576B (`fp8_ds_mla`) or 584B, kills the worker during
startup:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'CUDA error: an illegal memory access
was encountered'
```

Reproduced on v0.27.1 with and without the b12x attention backend, so it is not
backend-specific.

An IMA is the *lucky* outcome. Because the kernel masks against the declared
size rather than the allocation, the same mismatch can instead copy the wrong
bytes successfully and corrupt KV silently.

## Change

Adds a host-side bounds check on the computed pointer array, on both exit paths
of `compute_sub_block_ptrs()`. One `min`/`max` over the array per batch, which
is negligible next to the transfer itself.

On violation it raises a `ValueError` naming the offending range, the tensor
shape, dtype and `stride(0)`, and points at the likely cause, instead of
faulting inside the kernel.

## Scope

This does **not** add MLA/padded-page support to the offload path. It makes the
unsupported case fail diagnosably rather than dangerously. Supporting padded
layouts would additionally require deriving per-block offsets from
`MLAAttentionSpec.page_size_bytes`/`alignment` rather than `tensor.shape[1]`,
and handling multiple KV cache groups with differing geometry.

## Test

Logic verified for in-bounds, out-of-bounds and empty pointer arrays. Happy to
add a unit test under `tests/v1/kv_offload/` if you would like it in this PR;
I did not want to guess at the preferred fixture style.
