title: [RFC]: Experimental Recirculation for causal decoders
body:
### Motivation.

[Recirculation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17981) is an inference-time method
that changes a pretrained causal decoder's effective depth without changing
its weights. A normal pass produces logits and a deep residual-stream state.
That state is norm-matched, mixed into an earlier residual boundary, and the
upper stack is run again. The rerun overwrites upper-layer KV entries so later
tokens attend to the recirculated representation.

The design question for vLLM is broader than adding a branch to one model's
`forward`: cache ownership, scheduler behavior, CUDA-graph shapes, model
capability negotiation, and recurrent state must agree on the same semantics.
This RFC asks whether vLLM wants that behavior as an experimental engine
feature with explicit model-family opt-in.

This proposal supersedes author-closed RFC #53178. That issue was closed before
feedback and received no maintainer comments; it should not be interpreted as
either approval or rejection. This proposal narrows the initial code review to
the core engine and Gemma 3, with other model families reviewed separately.

### Proposed Change.

### Algorithm and cache invariant

For destination layer `d` and source layer `s`, where
`0 <= d < s < num_hidden_layers`, one scheduled token block executes as:

```text
normal pass: layers 0 ... d ... s ... N
                  |       |
                  |       +-- source residual
                  +---------- destination residual

mix: norm_match(source, destination) * alpha + destination * beta

rerun: mixed residual -> layers d+1 ... N
```

The normal pass's final hidden state supplies logits. The rerun replaces the
block's upper-layer cache state; lower-layer cache entries are unchanged. A
one-token block implements tokenwise Recirculation. Larger prefill blocks are
an explicit blockwise approximation: their logits come from the normal pass,
and their recirculated cache affects later blocks.

### Experimental configuration and capability boundary

The initial implementation accepts a validated dictionary through
`--hf-overrides`, avoiding a stable public CLI contract while the feature is
experimental:

```json
{
  "recirculation_config": {
    "source_layer": 11,
    "destination_layer": 4,
    "alpha": 0.15,
    "beta": null,
    "ramp_tokens": 10,
    "wavefront": true
  }
}
```

Validation covers unknown or missing fields, layer ordering, coefficient
ranges, identity configurations, ramping, and both ordinary and MRoPE token
positions. An open question is whether maintainers prefer a first-class
configuration object before merge.

Engine code detects an explicit `SupportsRecirculation` capability. Models opt
in through a shared residual-decoder mixin and declare the modes they support;
unreviewed subclasses and wrappers fail closed. Families may override layer
execution, residual materialization, finalization, or non-KV state handling
without duplicating the scheduler and cache protocol.

### Execution paths

The serial compatibility path runs the normal stack, records the source and
destination boundaries, returns the normal final state for logits, and reruns
the upper stack from the mixed residual. Ordinary attention KV entries are
overwritten at the same token positions. Hybrid recurrent models must instead
snapshot and restore affected convolutional or recurrent state before the
rerun.

An optional two-token wavefront batches the previous token's recirculated
upper pass with the current token's normal upper pass after a one-token warmup:

```text
row 0: previous token's recirculated upper pass
row 1: current token's normal upper pass
```

At every upper attention layer, row 0 first replaces the previous token's KV
entry and row 1 then consumes the same effective cache as serial execution.
The engine owns the pending residual, positions, attention metadata, remapped
slot mappings, and a dedicated two-row upper-stack CUDA graph.

The first wavefront implementation is limited to one sequence, one scheduled
token, FlashAttention, and no prefix caching or distributed parallel modes.
Other compatible configurations use the serial path.

### Safety boundary

The initial implementation targets Model Runner V1 and rejects explicit V2
selection. It also rejects speculative decoding and auxiliary hidden-state
extraction, pipeline parallelism, non-causal or diffusion backbones,
DeepSeek-V4 hyperconnection state, unreviewed wrappers, and parallel modes
whose state ownership has not been defined. Speculative decoding would need a
separate definition of which pass owns draft blocks, cache writes, and
auxiliary states.

MoE routing is recomputed during the upper rerun. A mixed residual may select
different experts; the proposal does not replay fixed routing decisions.

### Staged rollout

Implementation is split into dependent, scoped PRs:

1. Core engine/configuration and Gemma 3.
2. Ordinary residual dense and MoE adapters.
3. DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM DSA adapters.
4. Qwen3-Next and Qwen 3.5 recurrent-state adapters.
5. MiniMax-M3 sparse-attention adapters.
6. Kimi Linear and reviewed wrapper delegation.

Each family opts in only after its residual, cache, and non-KV state semantics
are reviewed and tested; support is not inferred from model configuration.
Kimi-K3 AttnRes is excluded because its residual-bank mapping requires a
separate design decision.

Serial Recirculation intentionally adds upper-stack compute and cache writes.
Wavefront execution reduces dispatch overhead, not mathematical work. No
universal quality or performance claim is proposed: each adapter must provide
correctness tests and appropriate real-model evidence.

### Feedback Period.

Fourteen calendar days, with no code PR until a maintainer indicates that the
core direction is worth reviewing. Main questions:

1. Is explicit capability negotiation plus a shared residual-decoder mixin the
   right boundary?
2. Should Llama and Mistral accompany Gemma 3 in the core PR or follow it?
3. Is V1-only experimental support acceptable, or should this wait for V2?
4. Are the wavefront invariant and initial restrictions convincing?
5. Should configuration use `hf_overrides` or a first-class interface?
6. What real-model evidence should be required for later adapter classes?

### CC List.

_No response_

### Any Other Things.

- Paper: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17981>
- Superseded author-closed RFC: #53178
- Superseded author-closed draft PR: #53179

The local prototype has exercised baseline, identity, serial, and wavefront
generation on an RTX 3080 using dummy weights through eager and compiled engine
paths, FlashAttention 2, CUDA graphs, and slot mapping. A cached Gemma 3 1B
sanity check over 1,020 scored tokens measured compiled perplexity `36.9618`
for baseline, `32.5482` for serial, and `32.2460` for wavefront. This was a
small fixed sample, not a standardized benchmark, and must be rerun on the
final rebased PR head.

Core acceptance requires parser and mixing tests, adapter cache/state tests,
serial/wavefront equivalence tests, direct runner and slot-mapping coverage,
and at least one real-weight comparison on the final PR head. Large Kimi,
MiniMax-M3, GLM-5, and similar checkpoints have not received local real-weight
validation; synthetic tests are not a substitute, so those follow-up PRs need
fresh model evidence or maintainer-approved provider validation.

### AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex provided non-trivial assistance with implementation, code review,
test development, local validation, branch decomposition, and this RFC draft.
The human submitter remains responsible for reviewing, understanding, and
defending every proposed change and reported result.


### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [deepseek-v4-flash-sm86 fork] PP8 + DSpark: recurring deadlock in the V2-runner PP sampled-token/draft broadcast protocol (PPHandler)
body:
# PP8 + DSpark: recurring deadlock in the V2-runner PP sampled-token/draft broadcast protocol (`PPHandler`)

Recurrent, reproducible deadlock on the `deepseek-v4-flash-sm86` fork (commit ccfeb3a8, vLLM 0.11.2.dev278 base) when serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with pipeline parallelism (PP=8) + DSpark speculative decoding. Filed as a tracking issue with the evidence we were able to gather on-device.

## Environment

- Fork: `LimeChain/vllm`, branch `deepseek-v4-flash-sm86`, commit `ccfeb3a8baac21d7e1364c609dfa88f2e0230cfd`
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (embedded DSpark drafter)
- Hardware: 8× RTX 3090 (PCIe only, no P2P/NVLink), Threadripper PRO 7965WX, Ubuntu 24.04, driver 595.84
- Relevant config: `--pipeline-parallel-size 8 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --distributed-executor-backend mp --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}' --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 --max-num-seqs 12 --max-num-batched-tokens 256 --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY",...}' --enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 327680`. Env: `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`.

## Symptom (recurs after minutes-to-tens-of-minutes of real agentic traffic)

- One streaming chat request in Running state; generation token counter frozen
- GPUs 0–6: 100 % util busy-spin (~160–180 W); GPU 7 (PP7, the final 2-layer + lm_head + DSpark stage per partition 5,6,6,6,6,6,6,2): 0 % util, worker process alive, threads in futex/epoll waits, zero I/O progress
- EngineCore first logs repeated "No available shared memory broadcast block found" (shm_broadcast reader-or-writer side), then — with timeouts enabled — aborts with `TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out` or `EngineDeadError`
- SIGTERM teardown hangs (NCCL groups stuck); recovery requires `kill -9` on vllm processes
- After each restart the same config serves normally (~59–91 tok/s) and then wedges again under the same workload class (long agentic sessions, growing context ~190-230K tokens, DSpark active, prefix-cache hit ~94 %)

## NCCL watchdog evidence (60 s timeouts enabled)

Every rank in the pipeline times out on the same stuck collective, named repeatedly across occurrences:

```
[PG ID 8 PG GUID 85(pp_broadcast) Rank R] failure detected by watchdog at work sequence id: 40427
  PG status: last enqueued work: 40432, last started work: -1, last completed work: 40426
Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL(SeqNum=40427, OpType=BROADCAST, NumelIn=6, Timeout(ms)=60000)
```

A later occurrence timed out instead on the PP activation pair (`OpType=RECV, NumelIn=98304`) on the default group, consistent with the same upstream stall cascading into the activation p2p.

The repeated `NumelIn=6` on the `pp_broadcast` group does not match the three payload shapes the protocol broadcasts per step (sampled `[12,i64]`, combined `[2,12,i32]`, draft `[12,5,i64]`), which this fork comments on as a cross-step FIFO mismatch signature.

## Trace level points at `PPHandler` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/pp_utils.py`)

The protocol is timeout-free with data-dependent send/skip gating and no rendezvous validation:

- Non-last ranks post three NCCL broadcast recvs per step whenever their own `compute_need_sampled_mask()` is non-None (pp_utils.py:227-238)
- The last rank sends two broadcasts in `broadcast()` gated by its own mask (pp_utils.py:277-279); the third (draft) broadcast is a **separately gated** call executed only after `speculator.propose()` succeeds (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:1664`)
- The recv is consumed pp_size=8 steps later via a FIFO (pp_utils.py:136-138), so one mismatched broadcast poisons the main stream 8 steps later
- Sender-side draft broadcast ends with `main_stream.wait_stream(broadcast_stream)` (pp_utils.py:324), so a stuck side stream gates the PP7 main stream too

Whether the mask can actually diverge cross-rank could not be proven from source — but the protocol has zero defense if it does, and the aggregated evidence (all 8 ranks parked on one collective, PP7 stage idle, PP activation RECV also subsequently orphaned) is consistent with a step-count divergence rather than payload corruption.

## Why PP7 specifically

Structural: PP7 owns the sampler, rejection sampler, and the entire DSpark draft model (`model_runner.py:244-250`), is the broadcast src (pp_utils.py:291), and is the only rank whose response the engine awaits (`multiproc_executor.py:515-528`). It also has the smallest layer slice (partition ends with `..2`), so when its CPU stalls its GPU drains to 0 % while every other rank sits in an orphaned NCCL recv spinning at 100 %.

## Secondary hazards flagged (may be related)

- Warmup is deliberately skipped for DSpark+PP (`gpu_worker.py:795-802` → `warmup.py:30-39`), so all runtime Triton JIT happens on first real traffic; `jit_monitor` hooks are post-compile, so a wedged compile is silent
- Engine async scheduling allows `max_concurrent_batches = pp_size+1 = 9` in-flight steps (`vllm/config/vllm.py:540-547`); the deferred structured-output path (`vllm/v1/engine/core.py:718-763`) can reorder `sample_tokens` vs `execute_model` RPCs, which would also break `PPHandler`'s FIFO-slot accounting

## Attempted fix that did not work

A local patch made the broadcast schedule data-independent (always post all three payload broadcasts on every step on every rank, plus a per-step sequence number + mask-hash wire header, plus zeroed/–1 sentinel payloads when the mask is None or the proposal failed, and a matching consume-side None-safe mask filter). It still wedged on the first real request with the identical signature — the EngineCore blocked in `acquire_read` and PP0 stuck in `update_pp_decode_requests` → `get_prev_sampled_outputs`. The validation header either never gets far enough to raise a named desync, or the divergence is deeper than the payload-count asymmetry (e.g. a step-count or ordering divergence in the scheduler/async layer crossing into `PPHandler`). Rolled back.

## Ask

Is the `PPHandler` broadcast protocol designed to tolerate the async-scheduling 9-deep in-flight window and the DSpark proposal-failure path? If so, which invariant is actually being violated? We can reproduce the hang reliably under long-context DSpark agent traffic and capture additional traces (NCCL flight recorder dumps, iteration-details logs, py-spy/faulthandler stacks if needed) — happy to send whatever would be most diagnostic.

title: fix(parser): stop leaking partially delivered DSML tags into streamed tool arguments
body:
## Purpose

While streaming DeepSeek V4 tool calls (`stream: true` + `tool_choice: required`), an in-progress parameter value can be followed by the *beginning* of its closing tag `</｜DSML｜parameter>`, because a chunk boundary may land anywhere inside that tag. The partial matcher in `_dsml_arg_converter` used a greedy `(.*)$`, so the truncated tag fragment was captured into the argument value:

```
{"location": "Paris</｜DSML｜parameter"}
```

This corrupts streamed tool arguments for every agent harness consuming them.

## Changes

- Add `_TAG_PREFIXES`, the set of all non-empty prefixes of `</｜DSML｜parameter>` and of `<｜DSML`.
- Add `_strip_partial_dsml_tag()`: trim the partial value at the earliest offset where the remainder is one of those prefixes. Applied only in the partial branch; the complete-parameter path is untouched.
- Three regression tests in `TestArgConverter`, including truncation in the middle of the closing tag.

### Why prefix trimming instead of a tempered regex

A tempered pattern such as `(?:(?!</?｜DSML｜).)*` only stops when it can see the full `｜DSML｜` sequence. Streaming truncation can land earlier than that — e.g. a value ending in `y</｜DSM` still leaks under that approach (verified experimentally). Checking whether any suffix of the value is a prefix of a DSML tag handles every truncation point exactly, and leaves ordinary angle brackets in values (`a<b`) untouched.

## Test Plan

- [x] New unit tests: partial closing tag missing final `>` (the issue's repro), closing tag truncated midway (`y</｜DSM`), invalid in-progress JSON plus close remnant stays omitted.
- [x] Full `TestArgConverter` class passes against the patched converter (20/20), and plain `<` values keep working via the existing angle-bracket tests.

Fixes #53227

title: [Bugfix] DeepSeekV4MTP: implement SupportsPP so the draft can start under PP
body:
## Summary

`DeepSeekV4MTP` (all three of `nvidia/amd/xpu`) inherits from `nn.Module` only. The moment `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1` is combined with an MTP/DSpark speculative config, `SpeculativeConfig._verify_args` runs `draft_model_config.verify_with_parallel_config(draft_parallel_config)` — `draft_parallel_config.pipeline_parallel_size` is copied from the target — and the draft trips `is_pp_supported_model()`:

```
NotImplementedError: Pipeline parallelism is not supported for this model.
Supported models implement the `SupportsPP` interface.
```

Server never starts. Repro from #52761:

```
vllm serve /path/to/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 3 \
  --speculative-config '{\"method\":\"dspark\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":7,\"draft_sample_method\":\"greedy\"}' \
  ...
```

## Fix

Add `SupportsPP` to `DeepSeekV4MTP` in each of the three platform variants and wire `self.make_empty_intermediate_tensors` from `utils.make_empty_intermediate_tensors_factory`.

The MTP draft only ever runs on the last PP stage — `gpu/model_runner.py` gates `init_speculator` on `is_last_pp_rank` — so the factory exists to satisfy the `SupportsPP` protocol and is never actually consumed at forward time. Same pattern as `NemotronHMTP` on `main` and `DeepSeekMTP` in the in-flight #46994.

`forward()` on the DSv4 MTP wrapper takes an extra positional `hidden_states` that the parent protocol doesn't have, so mypy needs a `# type: ignore[override]` — commented in place so it doesn't look like a stray silencer.

## Related

- #52761 — this specific error, DeepSeek-V4-Flash + PP + DSpark.
- #52069 — the systemic version (\"MTP draft models don't declare `SupportsPP`\").
- #46994 — the analogous fix for DeepSeek base MTP + Qwen3.5 (in review, doesn't touch DSv4).

## Test plan

- [x] `pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/mtp.py vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/mtp.py vllm/models/deepseek_v4/xpu/mtp.py` (ruff / mypy-3.10 / typos / DCO all pass locally)
- [ ] `vllm serve <DSv4-Flash-model> --pipeline-parallel-size 3 --speculative-config '{\"method\":\"dspark\", ...}'` — needs someone with the model + 3 GPUs; the failure this fixes is a pre-model-load config check, so \"server startup completes past speculative-config verification\" is sufficient signal.

AI assistance was used to locate the missing mixin and mirror the existing pattern; every changed line was reviewed and the mypy signature-override was verified against the pre-existing `NemotronHMTP` precedent.

This affects the next-token probability distribution, which can harm model performance depending on sampling parameters. To isolate the defect, we ran reproductions on SGLang (v0.5.14), where agreement was high. We believe this failure is unique to UE8M0 block-scale checkpoints. added --hf-overrides ‘{“swiglu_limit”: null}’ which reproduces this issue, so it seems like the serving path is at least protected now through this ValueError. title: [Bug]: GLM-5.2 FP8 on 8×H200 dies with runtime CUDA OOM in sparse_decode_fwd
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

   ## Summary

   On the FlashMLA sparse **fp8 mixed-batch** path, the sparse decode kernel allocates a workspace that
   scales linearly with `--max-num-batched-tokens` and is **not bounded by any workspace limit and not
   accounted for during startup memory profiling**. The server starts fine, serves for days, then dies
   with a runtime `torch.OutOfMemoryError` inside `flash_mla_cuda.sparse_decode_fwd` the first time a
   batch gets large enough. The OOM kills EngineCore, so every in-flight request fails with
   `EngineDeadError` and the process exits.

   This is not KV-cache pressure: **GPU KV cache usage was 2.0–5.4%** in the minute before the crash,
   with at most 8 concurrent requests.

   The mixed-batch path is selected automatically whenever per-rank head count < 32, i.e. exactly the
   common high-TP configurations. 

   ## Repro

   ```bash
   vllm serve /models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \
     --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
     --enable-expert-parallel \
     --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
     --max-model-len 262144 \
     --max-num-seqs 32 \
     --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
     --speculative-config.method mtp \
     --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 5
   # NOTE: --gpu-memory-utilization left at its 0.90 default
   ```

   Then drive mixed prefill+decode traffic until a step fills the token budget. In our case it ran
   ~61 hours before dying during a burst (prompt throughput ~3.6k tok/s, 8 running requests).

   ## Error

   All 8 workers hit it in the same step:

   ```text
   (Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=751) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1000] Traceback (most recent call last):
   ...
     File "vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py", line 812, in forward_impl
       attn_out, lse = self.impl.forward_mqa(mqa_q, kv_cache, attn_metadata, self)
     File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py", line 886, in forward_mqa
       attn_out = self._forward_fp8_kv_mixed_batch(
     File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py", line 772, in _forward_fp8_kv_mixed_batch
       _attn_out, _ = self._fp8_flash_mla_kernel(
     File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py", line 803, in _fp8_flash_mla_kernel
       out, lse = flash_mla_with_kvcache(
     File "vllm/third_party/flashmla/flash_mla_interface.py", line 158, in flash_mla_with_kvcache
       out, lse, new_tile_scheduler_metadata, new_num_splits = flash_mla_cuda.sparse_decode_fwd(
   torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 8.00 GiB.
   GPU 0 has a total capacity of 139.80 GiB of which 6.40 GiB is free.
   Including non-PyTorch memory, this process has 133.39 GiB memory in use.
   Of the allocated memory 124.39 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, with 3.23 GiB allocated in
   private pools (e.g., CUDA Graphs), and 5.01 GiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated.

   (EngineCore pid=614) ERROR [core.py:1233] EngineCore encountered a fatal error.
   (APIServer pid=1) ERROR [serving.py:812] vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError:
       EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause.
   ```

   The 8.00 GiB is exactly `max_num_batched_tokens x index_topk x index_head_dim`

   ```
   32768 x 2048 x 128 x 1 byte = 8,589,934,592 B = 8.00 GiB
   ```

 
  ### Root cause: the mixed-batch path bypasses the workspace bound that the separate path uses

   `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py` (line numbers from `main` @ `a014e35f38`):

   ```python
   MIN_HEADS_FOR_BF16_PREFILL = 32                                      # L63
   self.fp8_use_mixed_batch = self.num_heads < MIN_HEADS_FOR_BF16_PREFILL  # L307

   def get_prefill_workspace_size(max_model_len: int):                  # L221
       # Memory usage: 5 * max_model_len * 576 * 2 bytes
       # This fits nicely below the typical MoE workspace size of >2GB so this is "free"
       return max_model_len * 5
   ```

   * The **separate prefill/decode** path is bounded — it computes `max_prefill_buffer_size` from
     `get_prefill_workspace_size(...)` and *"Chunk[s] prefill requests to fit within workspace size"* (L451-456).
   * The **mixed-batch** path is not. Its own docstring says it *"treats all tokens as one batch"*, and
     `_forward_fp8_kv_mixed_batch` does `q.unsqueeze(0)` / `topk_indices.unsqueeze(0)` over the full
     flattened token count with no chunking and no reference to the workspace manager.

   So the one path that has no memory bound is the one selected for every config with < 32 heads/rank.

   Additionally, this allocation appears not to be captured by startup memory profiling: `profile_run`
   executes a dummy prefill before the KV cache exists, so the fp8 sparse **decode** kernel never runs
   and its workspace is never reflected in the `gpu_memory_utilization` budget. (Inferred from the
   failure timing — I have not traced `profile_run` directly.) The practical effect is that
   `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90` is unsafe here even though vLLM's own accounting says it fits:
   PyTorch took 124.39 GiB of its 125.82 GiB budget, leaving 6.40 GiB against an 8.00 GiB request.

   MTP compounds it: `num_speculative_tokens 5` puts 6 query tokens per sequence into each decode step,
   so mixed batches reach the token cap much sooner than `max_num_seqs` alone suggests.

### Environment
   ```text
   vLLM:      0.24.0
   PyTorch:   2.11.0+cu130   (CUDA 13.0)
   GPU:       8x NVIDIA H200 (sm_90), 139.80 GiB each
   Driver:    580.126.20
   Python:    3.12.13
   Image:     vllm/vllm-openai:v0.24.0
   Model:     GLM-5.2-FP8  (GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM, model_type=glm_moe_dsa)
   ```

   Relevant model config:

   ```json
   {
     "num_attention_heads": 64,
     "num_hidden_layers": 78,
     "kv_lora_rank": 512,
     "index_topk": 2048,
     "index_head_dim": 128,
     "index_n_heads": 32
   }
   ```

title: fix(parser): prevent DSML markup leak in DeepSeek V4 streaming tool calls
body:
### Description
Fixes #53227.

Streaming tool calls on DeepSeek-V4-Pro leak raw DSML markup into tool call arguments when using the `deepseek_v4` tool call parser. This happens because `_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE` uses a greedy `(.*)$` match that captures trailing DSML tags (like `</｜DSML｜parameter`) when they are only partially received or processed during streaming.

### Changes
- Updated `_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE` in `vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py` to use a non-greedy match with a negative lookahead `((?:(?!</?{_ESCAPED_DSML}).)*)`. This ensures the parser stops capturing argument content as soon as it encounters the start of any DSML tag.

### Testing
Verified with a standalone reproduction script that simulates partial streaming chunks:
```python
raw = '<｜DSML｜parameter name="location" string="true">Paris</｜DSML｜parameter'
# Before: {"location": "Paris</｜DSML｜parameter"}
# After: {"location": "Paris"}
```
Confirmed that the fix correctly handles both complete and partial DSML tags without leaking markup into the argument JSON.

title: [Feature] Add PCP O-Proj tensor parallelism
body:
This PR adds an opt-in `--enable-pcp-o-proj-tp` path that shards the resident MLA O-Proj parameter across the combined PCP-by-TP rank grid while preserving the existing TP reduction semantics.

## Summary

The feature further partitions each TP-local O-Proj input shard across the PCP group, reducing the resident O-Proj parameter on each rank to `1 / PCP` of its standard TP layout. Execution requires `decode_context_parallel_size=1` and eager mode.

Supported architectures are DeepSeek V2, V3, and V3.2, plus GLM-4 MoE Lite and the GLM-5 family MLA architecture. Supported O-Proj representations are `UnquantizedLinearMethod` and ModelOpt W4A4 NVFP4 with a CUTLASS-compatible post-load layout. The NVFP4 adapter is an implementation example for quantized methods; its packed weight and swizzled block scale are handled explicitly. Other post-load layouts fail during post-load processing.

## Runtime behavior

The model runner records the logical, pre-partition batch type and propagates it consistently to every PCP rank. This keeps the collective decision identical even when PCP token partitioning gives different local batch shapes to different ranks.

- For prefill or mixed batches, generic MLA starts an asynchronous O-Proj weight all-gather after Q/KV normalization and before the remaining Q projection, RoPE, indexer, and main attention work. O-Proj waits for the gather only when the full TP shard is needed, then runs the normal TP-local O-Proj computation.
- For decode-only batches, each rank slices the TP attention output to its local PCP feature shard, computes a partial O-Proj result with the resident weight, and all-reduces that result over PCP.
- The existing TP reduction behavior remains unchanged, including paths where TP reduction is handled outside O-Proj.

## Implementation

- Adds a reusable `TPWeightSwitchMixin` with opt-in tensor/method specifications, asynchronous gather and wait handling, local/full tensor alias switching, and representation-specific prepare/finalize hooks.
- Reuses shared full-weight and assembly buffers across compatible layers.
- Adds a ModelOpt W4A4 NVFP4 adapter for native CUTLASS and FlashInfer kernels that use the CUTLASS packed-weight and 128x4 swizzled block-scale layout. Block-scale payloads are gathered through `uint8` views, then assembled into the complete kernel layout after the asynchronous handle completes. Replicated global scales remain unchanged.
- Validates the concrete NVFP4 kernel representation and local input padding. Marlin, TensorRT-LLM shuffle, Humming, FBGEMM, and other post-load layouts remain fail-closed until they receive layout-specific adapters.
- Adds an explicit attention hook so the gather can overlap with the remaining attention work and O-Proj cannot consume an incomplete shared buffer.
- Adds configuration and post-load checks for supported execution settings and O-Proj representations.

## Accuracy validation

Online accuracy used four NVIDIA H20 GPUs with GLM-4.7-Flash BF16, eager execution, DCP1, the full 1,319-question GSM8K test set, 5-shot prompting, concurrency 32, `temperature=0`, seed 42, and `max_tokens=4096`. These results cover the unquantized O-Proj path.

| Topology | 32-question output gate | Correct | Accuracy | Failed requests | Invalid answers |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TP4 baseline | 25/32 | 1129/1319 | 85.5951% | 0 | 0 |
| PCP4TP1 | 25/32 | 1135/1319 | 86.0500% | 0 | 0 |
| PCP2TP2 | 24/32 | 1131/1319 | 85.7468% | 0 | 0 |

## Process memory

The following measurements used the same four-H20 setup and a fixed 32 GiB KV cache. `Model-load allocation` is the model runner allocation reported after loading and post-load processing; `Ready HBM` is per-rank process HBM after engine initialization.

| Topology | Metric | Disabled | Enabled |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| PCP4TP1 | Model-load allocation | 17.02 GiB/rank | 16.58 GiB/rank |
| PCP4TP1 | Ready HBM | 59,461 MiB/rank | 60,021 MiB/rank |
| PCP2TP2 | Model-load allocation | 15.15 GiB/rank | 15.17 GiB/rank |
| PCP2TP2 | Ready HBM | 56,541 MiB/rank | 57,140 MiB/rank |

The resident parameter layout is smaller, but that saving is not equivalent to a total process-HBM reduction. Ready HBM also includes the fixed KV cache, CUDA context, communication buffers, the shared one-layer full-weight buffer, persistent staging, runtime workspaces, and allocator effects. In these measurements, PCP4TP1 reduced model-load allocation while ready HBM increased; PCP2TP2's local parameter saving was offset at model load and ready HBM also increased.

## Serving performance

Serving used four H20 GPUs, GLM-4.7-Flash BF16, random 32,768-token inputs and 1,024-token outputs, `ignore_eos`, `temperature=0`, seed 12345, prefix caching disabled, and a fixed 32 GiB KV cache. Each row is one controlled completed run; all runs had zero failed requests. Throughput is output-token throughput. These results cover the unquantized O-Proj path.

| Topology | Feature | Concurrency | TTFT (ms) | TPOT (ms) | Output throughput (tok/s) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PCP4TP1 | disabled | 1 | 2027.49 | 82.33 | 11.87 |
| PCP4TP1 | enabled | 1 | 2030.59 | 86.39 | 11.33 |
| PCP4TP1 | disabled | 8 | 9368.98 | 89.98 | 80.51 |
| PCP4TP1 | enabled | 8 | 9402.45 | 94.69 | 76.84 |
| PCP4TP1 | disabled | 16 | 17376.00 | 97.19 | 139.50 |
| PCP4TP1 | enabled | 16 | 17438.39 | 104.49 | 131.04 |
| PCP2TP2 | disabled | 1 | 2091.03 | 89.73 | 10.91 |
| PCP2TP2 | enabled | 1 | 2151.26 | 95.16 | 10.29 |
| PCP2TP2 | disabled | 8 | 9008.10 | 95.98 | 76.17 |
| PCP2TP2 | enabled | 8 | 8968.01 | 103.23 | 71.27 |
| PCP2TP2 | disabled | 16 | 16404.51 | 103.03 | 133.75 |
| PCP2TP2 | enabled | 16 | 16417.18 | 108.64 | 127.70 |

## Validation

The branch is rebased onto upstream `main` at `bfa7e5b7afe40ebe48288801a2baf5c1135cd881`. The GLM-5 family architecture gate and regression test incorporate the contributor change from [pisceskkk/vllm#7](https://github.com/pisceskkk/vllm/pull/7), commit `0174b10c522b7b5ac06654df3492143732bf87a5`, in this existing feature PR.

- Repository pre-commit checks over all 15 PR files passed, including Ruff, mypy, Markdown, configuration validation, and Buildkite test tethering. Subsequent runtime fixes and documentation updates also passed their commit hooks.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -v tests/model_executor/layers/test_pcp_o_proj_tp.py tests/test_config.py -k pcp_o_proj`: **16 passed**, 439 deselected. The existing image's matching FlashInfer Python overlay was used; there were no dependency stubs or version-check overrides.
- All 2,637 Python source-file checksums were verified in an isolated source overlay. Image-built native artifacts and their third-party Python bindings were retained.

The four-layer GLM-5.2-FP8 crop retained original attention dimensions and all 256 routed experts. Its O-Proj weights were dequantized to BF16 using the checkpoint's 128x128 scales, then excluded from FP8 weight quantization. Both arms used the same crop on two H20 GPUs with TP1/PCP2/DCP1/EP2, eager mode, FP8 KV cache, a fixed 1 GiB KV cache, and prefix caching disabled.

Code commit `eb04a107090e4eab5f20ecc43ed2e8c5272869f2` passed baseline and enabled runs; the subsequent commit only adds validation documentation. Each arm completed six requests across short and mixed chunked-prefill workloads. Every O-Proj call was compared with a full-weight BF16 GEMM on the actual layer input.

| Phase | Enabled calls across ranks | Maximum relative L2 error | Maximum scaled error |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Prefill | 16 | 0 | 0 |
| Mixed | 96 | 0 | 0 |
| Decode | 160 | 0.003212 | 0.007752 |

All outputs were finite and stayed within the predeclared 0.01 relative-L2 and 0.02 scaled-error bounds. Five of six continuations matched the baseline exactly. The crop provides execution and per-layer numerical evidence; it does not establish full-model dataset accuracy or serving performance. Native NVFP4 GEMM remains untested on this H20 run.

The O-Proj resident parameter total across four layers decreased from 768 MiB to 384 MiB per rank. Before the validation oracle was installed, ready tensor allocations were 11.0743 GiB/rank disabled and 11.2618 GiB/rank enabled. Reconstruction/staging offsets the parameter reduction in this small crop.

The runtime checks exposed and verified fixes for two current-upstream interactions:

- Dummy warmup uses its own batch metadata because PCP global-batch state may be unset or stale.
- Enabling PCP O-Proj TP replicates decode queries across PCP ranks. Ordinary PCP decode ownership is retained when the feature is disabled; reducing feature-sharded outputs requires identical query rows on all ranks.

The full-model accuracy, process-memory and serving-performance tables above are historical evidence from feature head `74167404613af2261fc0613d9e3347ad33c981ef` and preceding implementation revisions. They have not been rerun on the current branch.

## Documentation

`docs/design/pcp_o_proj_tp.md` documents the design and constraints, the validation evidence, the NVFP4 mixin example, and PCP8 parameter-layout projections for GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4 checkpoints.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for the implementation and rebase.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4] SM12x FlashInfer sparse MLA kernel block size 64
body:
## Purpose

FlashInfer SM120 DSV4 decode is compiled for 64-token pages (`_DECODE_DSV4_PAGE_BLOCK_SIZE = 64` on flashinfer main). `DeepseekV4SparseMLABackend` / `DeepseekV4IndexerBackend` still advertised `[256]`, so `select_common_block_size` could not split manager `--block-size 256` into kernel pages. Isolated page-64 cosine vs torch on GB10 was 0.99966; listing 256 skipped the specialized decode kernel.

Keep `--block-size 256` (C128 storage is `block_size/128 = 2`; SWA pages are already 64). On capability family 120 return `[64]`. SM100 stays `[256]`.

`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` inherits the base method (it was a hard-coded `[256]` override).

Not a duplicate of:
- #52499 (spec-decode query rank / `num_tokens > 64`)
- #41834 (does not change these kernel block sizes)
- flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4380 (TOPK 192/256 dispatch, already merged)

Rebased onto current main. DCO sign-off added.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_dsv4_kernel_block_size.py -q
```

## Test Result

2x DGX Spark GB10, TP=2, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, DSpark k=5, manager `block_size=256`, kernel page 64. Greedy `"The capital of France is"` (`temperature=0`, 32 tok): `" Paris. The capital of Spain is Madrid..."`. First token `' Paris'` logprob -0.244. KV 561,703 tokens at util 0.81.

title: [Core][Spec Decode] Opt-in skip of the K=0 draft sync forward (MTP + DFlash, default off)
body:
**Stacked on #51575** — this branch contains rebased equivalents of its
two commits until that PR merges; please merge #51575 first.
Implements the opt-in option discussed in #53420.

## Purpose

When Dynamic Speculative Decoding resolves K=0 for a step, vLLM still
runs one draft-model forward per step — the prefill inside
`AutoRegressiveSpeculator.propose()` (and equivalently in
`DFlashSpeculator.propose()`), deliberately kept as per-step draft
KV-state sync (#51510/#51575 lineage). On K=0-resolving batch sizes
this is measurable overhead (+4–11% decode in our MTP measurements),
but skipping it is only safe for some drafter architectures: drafters
whose proposals depend on their own full-attention KV history (the
EAGLE family) lose nearly all speculative acceptance after unsynced
K=0 steps, at every K tested.

Because safety is a property of the drafter's internal architecture —
which cannot be reliably predicted for unmeasured models — this PR
exposes the skip as an **explicit opt-in, default off**. The operator
decides. The option is accepted when the method resolves to `mtp` or
`dflash`: EAGLE-family methods are refused as measured-unsafe (one
EAGLE3 checkpoint collapsed; `eagle` shares the full-attention risk);
methods whose speculators override `propose()` without the skip
(`dspark`, multi-module-MTP) are refused rather than silently ignoring
the option; other variants (e.g. `gemma4`) are refused as unmeasured.
Default off.

**Where the overhead lands: the high-concurrency serving regime.**
Dynamic spec tables deliberately resolve K=0 at exactly the batch
sizes where speculation stops paying — high concurrency, vLLM's core
serving workload. Every step of that regime still pays the draft sync
forward, for every concurrent request, for as long as traffic stays
high. This option removes that per-step tax precisely where DSD
deployments spend most of their time. Two scoping notes: (a)
measurements below cover c=1 through c=16; (b) K=1 steps are
unaffected — at K≥1 the drafter is genuinely proposing, and the skip
fires only on resolved-K=0 steps.

## Measurements behind the flag — MTP

RTX 5090 ×2, nightly `0.26.1rc1.dev926+gb05ae5dc0`, greedy, TP=2.
Full methodology and limitations in the companion issue #53420.

Benefit (sync forward skipped via the same early return this PR adds):

| model / drafter | workload | stock | skipped | time reduction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (1-layer hybrid-GDN MTP) | dynamic `[[1,2,2],[3,16,0]]`, c=1 — K=2 region, skip must not fire (control) | 5210 µs/step | 5303 µs/step | −1.8% (noise) |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | **dynamic `[[1,2,2],[3,16,0]]`, c=8 — K=0 (serving regime)** | 11121 µs/step | 10075 µs/step | **9.4%** |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | **dynamic `[[1,2,2],[3,16,0]]`, c=16 — K=0 (serving regime)** | 13606 µs/step | 12495 µs/step | **8.2%** |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | K≡0 table `[[1,16,0]]`, c=1 | 6585 µs/step | 6317 µs/step | **4.1%** |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | K≡0 table `[[1,16,0]]`, c=2 | 6778 µs/step | 6015 µs/step | **11.3%** |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct + EAGLE3 drafter | 950-token solo K=0 phase | 6.78 s | 6.33 s | **6.6% (7.1% throughput)** |

The c=1–16 rows ran the real flag through `speculative_config` parsing
(end-to-end for this implementation; single boot per arm; walls
include identical prefill per cell; artifacts available). The c=1
control confirms no effect where K>0.

Risk when enabled on a drafter that needs the sync (same request
resuming K>0 after K=0 steps; per-request streamed-output proxy):

| drafter | resume K | acceptance-like ratio vs control |
|---|---|---|
| MTP (tested checkpoint) | 2 | 0.985× (batch-aggregate proxy, joiner-diluted; worst round 0.97×) |
| MTP (tested checkpoint) | 8 | 0.84–0.88× (streamed proxy, two boots) |
| EAGLE3 | 2 and 8 | **collapse to ~zero, non-recovering** (streamed proxy) |

Context on the K=8 row: stress configuration, not a realistic
production setting — in the healthy control arms of the K=8
experiments the drafter accepted only ~2 of 8 proposals per step
(streamed-output proxy), so deep-K MTP is already past its
efficiency point at this checkpoint; the dynamic tables in our
measurements use K=2. The row bounds the skip cost at depths where
the rollout leans hardest on the drafter's own state.

Output token identity as recorded: full-stream identity in the K=8
experiments, first-40 identity in the K=2 MTP experiment, and as
persisted in the K≡0 comparisons (greedy; target verification is
lossless — the risk is spec-efficiency only, which is why the flag is
opt-in rather than forbidden outright where untested).

## Measurements behind the flag — DFlash (this update)

Same hardware/wheel, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 target (hybrid GDN) + DFlash2
drafter (`z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, 2B conv + candidate selector),
TP=2, dynamic `[[1,2,7],[3,16,0]]` (K=7 is the drafter's trained
block width: `block_size = 1 + K`).

- **Skip fires where it must**: at c=8, the tiered boot ran 25–51
  draft steps per full workload leg vs 3,119 for a static-K=7 boot on
  identical traffic — the residual is the brief c≤2 completion tails
  where the K=7 rung correctly re-engages (same signature as the MTP
  option).
- **Resume behavior on the tested checkpoint**, two distinct cases:
  same-request recovery (requests that lived through a K=0 phase and
  resumed K=7 mid-request) accepted ~3.0 tokens/step on the resumed
  steps; a new-request c=1 workload run immediately after two K=0
  phases measured acceptance 2.87 vs 3.36 on a static-K reference
  boot — 14.6% lower, but with no EAGLE-style collapse (new requests
  rebuild drafter state via their own prefill+decode). The docstring
  records the caveat: DFlash's context-KV is per-step, so resume
  acceptance after unsynced K=0 phases is checkpoint-dependent and
  must be validated per deployment.
- **End-to-end (aggregate t/s, exact-32k chat, 4 rounds, temp 0.7)**,
  DFlash tiers with the skip vs MTP `[[1,2,2],[3,16,0]]` with the
  skip: c=1 (decode-only) 135.6 vs 133.7; c=4 168.9 vs 140.9; c=8
  232.2 vs 193.2. Scoping note, kept honest: a no-spec engine at
  c≥4 is still faster than either spec arm (202.6 / 331.2 t/s) —
  resolved-K=0 steps route through the spec-decode step machinery
  even with drafting skipped. That machinery overhead is pre-existing
  (we measured MTP-K0 at 30–42% below no-spec at batch, DFlash-K0 at
  17–30%) and out of scope for this option, which removes the draft
  forward only.

## Changes

- `vllm/config/speculative.py`: new `skip_draft_when_k0: bool = False`
  field on `SpeculativeConfig` with a docstring carrying the measured
  trade-offs and the #53420 reference; `_validate_skip_draft_when_k0()`
  called twice — early in construction (before any draft-config/model
  access, deferring the `draft_model` inference placeholder) and at
  the end of `__post_init__` (after method inference, where the
  resolved draft config is available) — resolving the ACTUAL
  speculator via the same predicates `init_speculator` uses
  (`use_gemma4_mtp()`, `use_multi_module_mtp()`), not just the method
  string: refusing `eagle`/`eagle3` (measured collapse), `dspark` and
  multi-module-MTP drafts (own `propose()` overrides — the option
  would be silently ignored) and gemma4-MTP drafts (unmeasured), and
  warning when no dynamic schedule is configured (static-K never
  resolves K=0). Accepted for `mtp` and `dflash`.
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py`:
  `AutoRegressiveSpeculator.__init__` reads the flag; `propose()`
  returns `draft_tokens[:num_reqs, :0]` before any hidden-state copy,
  input preparation, CUDA-graph dispatch, or draft forward when the
  resolved `num_speculative_tokens == 0` and the flag is on. The
  buffer is allocated in `__init__`, so the pre-prefill return is
  safe; downstream `active_width == 0` handling already exists from
  the K=0 fix.
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py` (this update):
  the same mechanism in `DFlashSpeculator` — flag read in `__init__`,
  early return after the count locals in `propose()`, before the
  hidden-state copy / context-KV preparation / CUDA-graph dispatch /
  draft generation. Capture and profiling paths cannot fire it (dummy
  and capture calls resolve `num_speculative_tokens=None`, and the
  DFlash drafter's graph capture path bypasses `propose()`).
- **Fixed-width tier validation for dflash (this update)**:
  `_validate_dflash_dynamic_schedule()` — DFlash proposes a fixed
  `1 + num_speculative_tokens` block width regardless of the per-step
  schedule, so `num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size` rungs must
  resolve (via the scheduler's `min(k, num_speculative_tokens)`
  clamp) to the full width, or be `0` with this flag. Without this, a
  K=0-resolving step would draft the full block against a 0-draft
  step — a shape mismatch, not just a wrong value; and below-max rungs
  would be silently ignored. Fail at config time instead.
- Method resolution: the flag requires the method to resolve to `mtp`
  or `dflash` — explicit method, or a draft model whose config infers
  it. The `draft_model` placeholder (method=None) defers the check to
  final validation (nothing is silently ignored, and inference is
  never blocked early).

```python
# propose(), first statements after the count locals (both speculators):
if self.skip_draft_when_k0 and num_speculative_tokens == 0:
    return self.draft_tokens[:num_reqs, :0]
```

## Tests

New `tests/config/test_skip_draft_when_k0.py` (20 tests) + a 6-line
update to `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py`
(existing K=0 prefill test now pins `skip_draft_when_k0 = False` and
the multimodal stub provides the config attribute).

- Default off; flag accepted for `mtp` and `dflash`.
- `eagle`/`eagle3` refused at construction with a bogus draft path —
  proving the rejection fires before any model/download access.
- Support matrix at validator level: `mtp` and `dflash` accepted;
  `eagle`/`eagle3` refused (unsafe); `dspark` refused (would be
  silently ignored); other method strings refused (out of scope).
- REAL-ROUTING construction tests (no mocks): method=`mtp` with a
  callable target override routing the draft to (a) a single-module
  MTP draft — accepted, flag on; (b) a multi-module draft
  (`num_nextn_predict_layers=4`) — rejected, own-propose override;
  (c) a `gemma4_mtp` draft — rejected, unmeasured. These resolve the
  same predicates `init_speculator` uses, closing the silent-ignore
  gap a method-string check misses.
- Inference deferral: the `draft_model` placeholder (method=None) is
  NOT rejected by the early validation; at validator level the final
  call accepts a resolved `mtp` and rejects a resolved `eagle`
  (simulated method assignment; construction-time inference coverage
  is provided by the REAL-ROUTING tests below).
- Real construction (no mocks) with the flag on and an unresolved
  method: defers early, rejects at final validation with the clear
  message.
- Real CLI path via `EngineArgs.create_speculative_config`: JSON to
  hyphen-normalized dict to constructor; flag typed bool; `false`
  constructs cleanly.
- Warning when enabled without a dynamic schedule.
- K=0 + flag on: `propose` returns `[num_reqs, 0]` and the prefill
  path is never entered — proven by a sentinel on the first
  prefill-path helper (`_copy_request_inputs`), which sits before both
  the eager prefill and the FULL-graph dispatch, so neither path can
  be reached without tripping it.
- K=0 + flag off: sentinel fires (existing sync behavior preserved).
- K=2 + flag on, and K unresolved (`None`) + flag on: no early return
  (sentinel fires) — the skip is K=0-specific.
- CLI JSON round-trip preserves the flag type.
- DFlash tier-rung validation (this update): a `0` rung accepted with
  the flag, rejected without it; an over-max rung (8 with max 7)
  accepted — it clamps to the full width in the scheduler; a
  below-max rung rejected with the fixed-width rationale.
- DFlash speculator (this update, bare-instance sentinel style
  mirroring the AutoRegressive set): K=0 + flag on returns
  `[num_reqs, 0]` without entering the forward path; flag off, K>0,
  and K unresolved each proceed (sentinel on the first stateful
  access after the branch).

Local run (source tree, CPU, rebased on current main): **20/20 new +
23/23 speculator+EPLB tests passed; ruff clean on all touched files.**

## Non-duplication / relation to neighbors

- #51575 (stacked here): propagates dynamic K=0 from the scheduler to
  `AutoRegressiveSpeculator` — the bugfix that makes K=0-resolving
  steps correct at all; it contains no skip option, no config flag,
  and nothing for DFlash.
- #52816 (merged): added the DFlash/DFlash2 drafter — without a K=0
  skip (its `propose()` runs the sync forward on K=0 steps) and
  without fixed-width tier validation.
- No other open or recent PR adds a `skip_draft_when_k0` option or
  DFlash dynamic-schedule validation (checked before opening).

## Test commands (source tree, CPU)

```
pytest tests/config/test_skip_draft_when_k0.py                          # 20 passed
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py \
       tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_eplb.py                 # 23 passed
```
Ruff clean on all touched files.

## Why a knob instead of auto-enabling at provable K≡0

The structurally safe auto case (spec table resolves K=0 for every
reachable batch size) is worth having, but it cannot serve dynamic
tables — which are the real DSD deployment pattern (K>0 rows at low
concurrency, K=0 rows at high concurrency, requests crossing between
them). For those, the trade-off is genuinely model-dependent and the
operator is the right decision-maker; the flag carries the measured
evidence in its docs. Auto-enable-at-provable-K≡0 composes with this
flag and is a natural follow-up if maintainers want it. (Dynamic K is
disabled under DP today, so the early return cannot diverge DP ranks.)

## Notes

- Extends the #51510/#51575 K=0-respect lineage (same reporter/author;
  the sync remnant was deliberate insurance — this makes it optional
  where measurements justify it).
- The DFlash addition is the same mechanism applied to the second
  speculator that runs the K=0 sync forward, plus the config-time
  fixed-width tier guard its proposer needs. DSpark still refuses the
  option (its proposer override has no skip; identical reasoning to
  multi-module MTP).
- Long-term generalization path (catch-up state reconstruction on
  K=0→K>0 resume) tracked in #53420; would let the flag's
  restriction be lifted family-wide.
- AI assistance: **this PR includes AI-generated code**, authored
  with Claude (ZCode) under human direction; every line reviewed,
  tests run, and measurements human-verified from saved artifacts
  (per the vLLM AI contribution policy; commit carries the
  Co-authored-by trailer).

*(v1 quarantine banner and misattribution audit trail retained in git
history / `codex-review-pr-draft.md`.)*

title: [PCP][Spec Decode] Prefer sharded MTP with replicated draft fallback
body:
## Summary

Extend the PCP speculative-decoding support already merged in [#56107](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56107) with backend-aware draft execution:

- Prefer the upstream PCP-sharded draft prefill for single-module MTP when the selected draft attention backend supports PCP.
- Fall back to a global replicated drafter when the selected backend does not support PCP, while keeping the target model PCP-sharded.
- Keep DSpark on its existing replicated path.

This allows PCP-capable and non-PCP-capable draft backends to coexist without disabling the upstream sharded implementation.

## Implementation

Draft mode is resolved before model construction from the effective draft attention backend, including `attention_backend` from the speculative config and `backend_per_kind` precedence:

- Automatic backend selection remains shard-first because the selector receives `use_pcp=True` and considers PCP-capable candidates.
- An explicitly selected backend with `supports_pcp() == false` builds the drafter with `prefill_context_parallel_size=1`.

The two runtime contracts remain separate:

| Draft mode | Hidden states | Prefill metadata | Input/capture buffers |
|---|---|---|---|
| PCP sharded | Rank-local target states | Reuse rank-local target metadata | PCP local buffers |
| Replicated fallback | PCP-restored global states | Rebuild from global positions, sequence lengths, and block tables | Drafter-owned global buffers |

For PIECEWISE graphs, replicated drafting captures with drafter-owned attention groups and buffers. Runtime graph-padding rows receive zero hidden states and the global `is_padding` mask.

Warmup follows the same selection: sharded MTP stays rank-local, while replicated drafters restore the global batch before `propose()`.

## Validation

Current commit:

- Ruff check passed on all changed files.
- Ruff format check passed on all changed files.
- Python bytecode compilation passed on all changed files.
- Unit coverage added for automatic shard preference, explicit backend capability selection, per-KV-kind precedence, config isolation, and global replicated metadata construction.

The available 5090 development container did not have a main-compatible Python/test environment, so model execution for this rebased commit remains to be rerun on the H20 environment.

### Replicated-mode model evidence

The following full GSM8K results were collected on the earlier global-replicated implementation using 4x NVIDIA H20, `/home/weight/GLM-4.7-Flash`, `FLASH_ATTN_MLA`, EP4, MTP3, all 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, seed 42, max output tokens 4096, and concurrency 32. They are retained as reference evidence for the replicated execution contract; they are not reported as a rerun of this rebased commit.

| Configuration | Correct | Accuracy | Invalid | Errors | Acceptance rate | Acceptance length |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP4 + greedy fixed K | 960/1319 | 72.7824% | 0 | 0 | 0.409285 | 2.227856 |
| PCP4 + greedy fixed K | 933/1319 | 70.7354% | 0 | 0 | 0.410057 | 2.230170 |
| PCP4 + greedy fixed K + PIECEWISE | 949/1319 | 71.9484% | 1 | 0 | 0.409514 | 2.228542 |
| PCP4 + probabilistic fixed K | 932/1319 | 70.6596% | 0 | 0 | 0.407958 | 2.223873 |
| PCP4 + probabilistic dynamic K | 967/1319 | 73.3131% | 1 | 0 | 0.920441 | 1.929728 |

Dynamic K used K=3 for batch sizes 1-8, K=2 for 9-16, and K=1 for 17-32. Its raw acceptance rate is not directly comparable with fixed K.

The fixed-K PCP and TP acceptance metrics were aligned (acceptance-rate delta 0.000771; acceptance-length delta 0.002314). PIECEWISE was also aligned with the eager PCP reference (acceptance-rate delta 0.000543; acceptance-length delta 0.001628).

## Scope

- Single-module MTP uses capability-selected sharded or replicated draft prefill.
- DSpark remains replicated as implemented by #56107.
- PCP continues to support PIECEWISE CUDA graphs; full graph modes remain outside the current PCP contract.
- Existing PCP+DCP restrictions are unchanged.

AI assistance was used for implementation and validation. The human submitter reviewed the changes.

title: [Bug]: DFlash2 draft models fail to load on main — #52560 reverted the `decoder_layer_cls` indirection added by #52816
body:
### Your current environment

```
vLLM: 0.26.1rc1.dev1117+g30b34171b (built from main, VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1)
GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell (sm_120, 48GB)
torch 2.13.0+cu132, flashinfer-python 0.6.17 + flashinfer-cubin 0.6.17
Target: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (NVFP4, compressed-tensors), --kv-cache-dtype fp8
Draft:  incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2
```

### Describe the bug

Any `DFlash2DraftModel` checkpoint fails to load on current `main`. The DFlash2 decoder layers are never constructed, so the checkpoint's convolution weights have no destination:

```
ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'layers.0.attention_conv' in DFlash2Qwen3Model.
The available parameters belonging to layers.0 (DFlashQwen3DecoderLayer) are:
{'layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj.weight', 'layers.0.self_attn.k_norm.weight',
 'layers.0.self_attn.o_proj.weight', 'layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight',
 'layers.0.self_attn.q_norm.weight', 'layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight',
 'layers.0.input_layernorm.weight', 'layers.0.post_attention_layernorm.weight'}
```

Note the reported layer type: `DFlash2Qwen3Model` built `DFlashQwen3DecoderLayer` layers instead of `DFlash2Qwen3DecoderLayer`.

### Root cause

#52816 ("[Spec Decode] DFlash2: local convolution + candidate selector") introduced two parallel extension points in `qwen3_dflash.py` so the DFlash2 subclasses could override them:

- `DFlashQwen3ForCausalLM.model_cls`
- `DFlashQwen3Model.decoder_layer_cls`

**#52560 ("[Model] Add Qwen3-Omni DSpark support") reverted the second one.** Per `git log -L442,443:vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py`:

```
2f55ef254 [Model] Add Qwen3-Omni DSpark support (#52560)
-                self.decoder_layer_cls(
+                DFlashQwen3DecoderLayer(

b389ac294 [Spec Decode] DFlash2: local convolution + candidate selector (#52816)
-                DFlashQwen3DecoderLayer(
+                self.decoder_layer_cls(
```

`2f55ef254` landed after `b389ac294`, and also dropped the `decoder_layer_cls` class attribute from `DFlashQwen3Model`. `model_cls` survived, which is why `DFlash2Qwen3Model` is instantiated correctly and the failure looks confusing -- only the layer class is wrong.

`qwen3_dflash2.py` still sets `decoder_layer_cls = DFlash2Qwen3DecoderLayer` (line 236), so the override is now dead code. A code search for `decoder_layer_cls` on the default branch returns exactly one file -- the consumer, with no definer.

This looks like a merge-resolution mistake rather than an intentional revert: #52560 is about Qwen3-Omni DSpark and has no reason to change how DFlash layers are constructed.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7}'
```

### Fix

Restoring the two lines #52816 added is sufficient:

```diff
 @support_torch_compile
 class DFlashQwen3Model(nn.Module):
+    decoder_layer_cls = DFlashQwen3DecoderLayer
+
     hf_to_vllm_mapper = WeightsMapper(
@@
         self.layers = nn.ModuleList(
             [
-                DFlashQwen3DecoderLayer(
+                self.decoder_layer_cls(
                     current_vllm_config,
```

With that applied, DFlash2 loads and runs correctly. Measured on one RTX PRO 5000 (sm_120), Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 target, fp8 KV cache, `--max-model-len 262144`, single stream, 5 fixed prompts, thinking disabled:

| spec method | decode | prefill @18.7K | KV pool |
|---|---|---|---|
| MTP spec=3 | 112.5 tok/s | 6,288 tok/s | 515,501 tok |
| **DFlash2 spec=7** | **203.0 tok/s** | 6,516 tok/s | 359,511 tok |
| DSpark spec=7 | 141.4 tok/s | 6,440 tok/s | 304,558 tok |

Decode-only mean acceptance length for DFlash2 was 4.71, and output was correct on inspection -- so the regression is purely the missing extension point, not a deeper problem with the DFlash2 path.

Happy to open a PR with the two-line restore, plus a small regression test asserting that a `DFlash2DraftModel` config actually builds `DFlash2Qwen3DecoderLayer` layers, if that's wanted.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I have searched existing issues and read the documentation. The three open DFlash2 issues (#53323 ROCm acceptance collapse, #53063 RoPE layout, #53031 capture logging) are unrelated to this load failure.

title: [Bug]: Run-to-run performance non-determinism with speculative decoding at temperature=0 (fixed seed) on DeepSeek-V4-Flash / Blackwell SM120
body:
## Summary

With `temperature=0` (greedy) and a **fixed seed**, repeating the *exact same* request produces the **same output text** but a **large run-to-run variance in decode throughput** (output tok/s), concentrated at low concurrency. The most likely mechanism (see root-cause probing below) is that speculative-decoding **acceptance varies between otherwise-identical runs**: since accepted-tokens-per-forward-step sets the decode speed, a shift in acceptance moves throughput while leaving the finally-emitted greedy tokens unchanged.

Root-cause probing (details below) points to the **target-model forward pass not being bit-reproducible run-to-run**: for the same prefix and the same proposed draft tokens, the target logits differ between runs. Because acceptance at `temperature=0` is exact-equality verification, tiny (near-tie) logit differences can flip individual accept/reject decisions, changing tokens-per-forward-step and therefore throughput — without changing the finally-emitted argmax token, which is why the output text stays identical.

This is a performance-stability bug, **not** an output-corruption bug: final text is stable, throughput is not.

The acceptance-rate link is directly measured (via vLLM's own `spec_decode` Prometheus counters, per run): acceptance varies run-to-run at fixed seed and correlates with throughput at **Pearson r = 0.98** (data in the "Acceptance-rate correlation" section below).

## Environment

- vLLM: `0.1.dev20005+g75c2eef60` (V1 engine)
- Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash (sparse MLA), `--trust-remote-code`
- Speculative decoding: `--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}'`
- GPU: 4× NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 (Blackwell, compute capability 12.0 / SM120), 72 GB
- FlashInfer: `0.6.18.dev20260811` (SM120 sparse-MLA path, `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache)
- torch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA 13.0
- Attention backend selected at runtime: FlashInfer MLA sparse SM120
- MoE backend: DEEPGEMM_MXFP4

This is an 8-GPU host; the vLLM server under test runs on GPUs 0–3, and a SGLang server (used only as a same-hardware reference point in the tables below) runs on GPUs 4–7. Full launch command as run:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server --model /model \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30013 \
  --trust-remote-code --served-model-name DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
  --max-model-len 33792 --max-num-batched-tokens 8448 --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --seed 0 --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

Note `--seed 0` is the server-side seed; the `--seed 42` referenced throughout Reproduction is the *benchmark client's* request seed — two independent knobs. `--no-enable-prefix-caching` is set so caching cannot mask the effect.

Reference SGLang server (same model weights, same host, GPUs 4–7, port 30012), for the comparison tables only:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /model \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30012 --tp 4 --trust-remote-code \
  --attention-backend flashinfer --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8448 --max-running-requests 32 \
  --disable-radix-cache
```

## Reproduction

Fixed request shape (`input_len=8192`, `output_len=1024`, `random-range-ratio=1.0` so every prompt is identical length), `temperature=0`, **fixed `seed=42`**, one warmup run (discarded) then **10 measured repeats** per concurrency level, sweeping `max_concurrency ∈ {1,2,4,8,16,32}`. Output text is identical across repeats; only decode throughput moves.

**Important methodological note:** with only 3 repeats the jitter frequently hides — the samples happen to land close together and vLLM looks stable (<1% CV). It only shows up reliably at **10 repeats**. Anyone trying to reproduce should not conclude "stable" from a handful of runs.

### Raw `output_tok/s`, 10 repeats each, seed=42

vLLM (this build, dspark N=5):

| conc | raw output tok/s (10 runs) | mean | min→max | **CV** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 170.97 153.19 133.80 123.13 133.72 127.97 130.32 136.81 133.25 149.84 | 139.3 | 123.1→171.0 | **9.85%** |
| 2 | 336.79 197.29 238.78 249.91 276.31 210.06 329.29 216.14 340.48 237.18 | 263.2 | 197.3→340.5 | **19.65%** |
| 4 | 430.38 503.23 509.25 528.60 494.89 504.92 544.35 452.88 550.84 548.15 | 506.7 | 430.4→550.8 | **7.50%** |
| 8 | 682.05 680.84 684.95 684.48 685.68 686.93 686.94 686.96 681.80 689.71 | 685.0 | 680.8→689.7 | 0.39% |
| 16 | 814.76 820.47 819.76 814.43 819.95 817.43 816.92 812.62 812.13 818.54 | 816.7 | 812.1→820.5 | 0.36% |
| 32 | 972.30 972.28 965.99 971.36 972.66 956.32 957.94 971.34 971.01 959.99 | 967.1 | 956.3→972.7 | 0.64% |

SGLang, same model, same FlashInfer 0.6.18.dev family, same 8× RTX PRO 5000 host (GPUs 4–7), for reference:

| conc | raw output tok/s (10 runs) | mean | min→max | **CV** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 250.45 249.39 251.27 250.18 250.19 251.71 251.62 249.99 250.49 250.42 | 250.6 | 249.4→251.7 | 0.28% |
| 2 | 343.46 344.34 344.17 344.52 346.22 344.79 342.85 344.30 345.56 344.30 | 344.5 | 342.9→346.2 | 0.26% |
| 4 | 463.15 460.50 460.84 463.28 461.47 463.24 460.25 463.61 461.94 461.98 | 462.0 | 460.3→463.6 | 0.26% |
| 8 | 523.31 522.46 522.11 522.72 521.71 522.98 522.45 521.68 521.84 521.66 | 522.3 | 521.7→523.3 | 0.11% |
| 16 | 631.87 633.42 633.33 634.19 633.45 632.17 631.10 632.24 633.95 632.44 | 632.8 | 631.1→634.2 | 0.15% |
| 32 | 507.06 534.79 529.92 503.55 538.76 528.49 523.68 514.37 499.80 531.74 | 521.2 | 499.8→538.8 | 2.54% |

### CV comparison (vLLM vs SGLang, same host)

| conc | vLLM CV | SGLang CV | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **9.85%** | 0.28% | **35×** |
| 2 | **19.65%** | 0.26% | **75×** |
| 4 | **7.50%** | 0.26% | **29×** |
| 8 | 0.39% | 0.11% | 3.6× |
| 16 | 0.36% | 0.15% | 2.4× |
| 32 | 0.64% | 2.54% | 0.3× |

**The jitter is concentrated at low concurrency (1/2/4), peaking at conc=2 with a 54% peak-to-peak spread (197→340 tok/s) on identical, fixed-seed input.** At conc≥8 vLLM converges to <0.7%. SGLang on the identical host stays <0.3% at low concurrency, so this is not a hardware / clock-jitter artifact of the box. (SGLang's own 2.54% at conc=32 is a separate, unrelated effect.)

The mechanism is that per-run speculative-decoding **acceptance varies**: when more draft tokens are accepted, tokens-per-forward-step is higher, so output tok/s is higher. This is directly measured below (not merely inferred), and is consistent with the variance vanishing as concurrency rises (at higher concurrency each forward step is dominated by batch width rather than by per-request accepted-token count).

### Acceptance-rate correlation (directly measured)

To confirm the mechanism I read vLLM's own speculative-decoding counters from `/metrics` (`vllm:spec_decode_num_draft_tokens_total`, `vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total`, `vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total`) immediately before and after each run, and paired the per-run delta with that run's throughput. Same fixed request, `seed=42`, `temperature=0`, `conc=2`, 10 runs (1 warmup discarded):

| run | output tok/s | acceptance rate (accepted/draft) | accepted tokens per draft step |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 207.86 | 0.2751 | 1.376 |
| 2 | 214.87 | 0.2716 | 1.358 |
| 3 | 217.90 | 0.2960 | 1.480 |
| 4 | 193.60 | 0.2214 | 1.107 |
| 5 | 202.21 | 0.2394 | 1.197 |
| 6 | 183.76 | 0.1989 | 0.995 |
| 7 | 190.75 | 0.2062 | 1.031 |
| 8 | 209.88 | 0.2620 | 1.310 |
| 9 | 204.22 | 0.2458 | 1.229 |
| 10 | 224.29 | 0.3140 | 1.570 |

- Acceptance rate is **not** stable run-to-run at fixed seed: it ranges 0.199 → 0.314 (**CV 14.2%**), despite identical input and greedy decoding.
- Throughput CV in this measurement run was 5.9% (the magnitude of the jitter itself varies between measurement sessions; see the 10-repeat sweep above for a larger spread).
- **Pearson correlation, acceptance rate vs. throughput: r = 0.98** (accepted-tokens-per-step vs. throughput: also r = 0.98).

This closes the causal chain: non-bit-reproducible target forward → run-to-run acceptance variation → throughput variation.

### Exact benchmark command

The benchmark client is SGLang's `bench_serving` in OpenAI-compatible mode, pointed at either running server (it speaks the OpenAI API, so it drives the vLLM server too). It therefore requires `sglang` installed in the client environment; the random dataset uses `ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json` (the standard SGLang/vLLM sample dataset, downloadable from the ShareGPT_Vicuna_unfiltered HF repo). Set `PORT` to `30013` for vLLM or `30012` for SGLang, `TOK` to the local tokenizer path, and `CONC` to the concurrency level:

```bash
PORT=30013           # 30013 = vLLM, 30012 = SGLang
CONC=2               # concurrency level under test
TOK=/path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-tokenizer
NP=$((CONC*2)); [ "$NP" -lt 4 ] && NP=4   # at least 4 prompts so the level is filled

python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang-oai \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:$PORT --model DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --dataset-name random --dataset-path ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json \
  --tokenizer $TOK \
  --num-prompts $NP --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --max-concurrency $CONC --temperature 0 --seed 42
```

### Full sweep script

<details><summary>repro_rep10.sh — 6 concurrency levels × 2 engines × (1 warmup + 10 measured), computes per-level CV</summary>

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Fixed seed=42, identical request, REP measured repeats per concurrency level.
# vLLM (port 30013) + SGLang (port 30012), conc in {1,2,4,8,16,32}. Read-only load test.
set -u
LOG=repro_rep10.log; : > $LOG
log(){ echo "[$(date +%T)] $*" | tee -a $LOG; }

export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1   # avoid ~15s HF retry per run
DS=ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json
TOK=/path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash
REP=10
INLEN=8192; OUTLEN=1024; SEED=42
CONCS="1 2 4 8 16 32"
mkdir -p rep10

# $1=port $2=tag $3=conc $4=nprompts $5=run
runbench(){
  python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang-oai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:$1 \
    --model DeepSeek-V4-Flash --dataset-name random --dataset-path $DS --tokenizer $TOK \
    --num-prompts $4 --random-input-len $INLEN --random-output-len $OUTLEN --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
    --max-concurrency $3 --temperature 0 --seed $SEED >rep10/${2}_c${3}_r${5}.txt 2>&1
}

engine_scan(){
  local port=$1 tag=$2
  log "############ engine=$tag port=$port REP=$REP ############"
  for C in $CONCS; do
    local NP=$((C*2)); [ $NP -lt 4 ] && NP=4
    rm -f rep10/${tag}_c${C}_tps.txt
    runbench $port $tag $C $NP warm     # warmup, discarded
    for r in $(seq 1 $REP); do
      runbench $port $tag $C $NP $r
      tp=$(grep -iE "Output token throughput" rep10/${tag}_c${C}_r${r}.txt | grep -oE "[0-9.]+" | head -1)
      echo "${tp:-0}" >> rep10/${tag}_c${C}_tps.txt
    done
    python3 - "$tag" "$C" <<'PY' 2>&1 | tee -a $LOG
import sys,statistics as st
tag,C=sys.argv[1],sys.argv[2]
v=[float(x) for x in open("rep10/%s_c%s_tps.txt"%(tag,C)) if x.strip() and float(x)>0]
m=st.mean(v); sd=st.pstdev(v) if len(v)>1 else 0
print("  %-7s conc=%-3s n=%d mean=%.2f CV=%.3f%% min=%.2f max=%.2f raw=%s"%(
   tag,C,len(v),m,(sd/m*100 if m else 0),min(v),max(v),["%.1f"%x for x in v]))
PY
  done
}

engine_scan 30013 vllm
engine_scan 30012 sglang
```

</details>

## Root-cause evidence

I instrumented the rejection sampler (read-only, at the point where target logits are materialized for verification) and dumped, per verify step: the logits tensor shape, a fingerprint of the draft tokens, and a bit-level SHA-256 of the target logits (fp32).

Running the identical request twice with the same seed and diffing the two aligned sequences:

- Draft-token fingerprints match step-for-step across the two runs (same proposals).
- Yet at some steps the **target-logits SHA differs between the two runs**, for identical prefix + identical draft input.

**Conclusion:** the target-model forward is not bit-reproducible run-to-run. At `temperature=0` this causes near-tie accept/reject flips, which change tokens-per-forward-step (throughput) without changing the finally-emitted argmax token. The accept/reject logic itself is deterministic (pure hard-equality at temp=0); the non-determinism enters upstream, in the forward pass. Both ends of this are directly measured: the target logits differ run-to-run (this section), and the resulting acceptance rate varies and tracks throughput at r = 0.98 (Acceptance-rate correlation section above).

(The probe methodology was validated with a positive control: the same instrumentation fires correctly — module-level load in all 4 TP workers, and 240 in-generation function calls for a 128-token request — so an empty result elsewhere is meaningful, not a broken probe.)

## Additional finding: the official determinism switch is unavailable on this hardware

`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (the documented batch-invariant / deterministic path) **fails at startup** on this configuration with:

```
NotImplementedError: No MXFP4 MoE backend supports the deployment configuration
```

So the standard remedy for run-to-run non-determinism cannot be enabled for DeepSeek-V4-Flash on Blackwell + MXFP4 MoE. This makes the above non-determinism currently unmitigable through the official switch on this class of hardware.

## Impact

- Benchmarking / capacity planning is unreliable at low concurrency: identical fixed-seed workloads report a run-to-run throughput CV up to ~19.7% (conc=2), with a 54% peak-to-peak spread.
- Speculative-decoding acceptance rate — a key tuning signal — is not reproducible between identical runs (measured CV 14.2% at fixed seed, conc=2).
- The documented determinism escape hatch (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`) is blocked on this hardware (see above).

## What I have NOT been able to pin down

I could not yet localize the non-determinism to a specific kernel (sparse-MLA attention vs. MXFP4 MoE). The decode hot path is captured under CUDA graph + torch.compile, and the `CudagraphDispatcher` used by the workers is instantiated in the engine-core process before the workers are spawned, so Python-source instrumentation of the dispatch layer does not reach the workers. Suggestions for a reachable instrumentation point (or confirmation of which kernel is expected to be non-deterministic here) would be very welcome.

## Questions for maintainers

1. Is target-forward run-to-run non-determinism expected on the FlashInfer SM120 sparse-MLA path and/or DEEPGEMM_MXFP4 MoE?
2. Is there a supported way to get batch-invariant / deterministic execution for MXFP4 MoE on Blackwell, given `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` currently raises `NotImplementedError`?
3. Would a fix on the acceptance side (e.g. tolerance-free but tie-stable argmax) be in scope, or is the intended fix to make the forward bit-reproducible?
