title: [Cleanup] Remove online quantization support in `fp8.py` in favor of online shorthands
body:
## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Purpose

Deprecates online quantization through ``quantization="fp8"`, redirecting to the online shothand `fp8_per_tensor`.

This removes online-quantization path from `fp8.py` in favor of `ONLINE_QUANT_SHORTHAND_NAMES`, such as `quantization="fp8_per_tensor"`, that uses https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/fp8.py as documented in https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/features/quantization/online: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/79bb395eea64dbfef99a55f010d2854db71f8571/vllm/config/quantization.py#L151-L155

This is a followup of:
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32189
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45463

Keep `Fp8Config.is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized` for backward compatibility with callers that still read the attribute.

Breaking changes:
- None. `quantization="fp8" redirects to `"fp8_per_tensor"`.

Removes some slow outdated online quantization tests from `test_fp8.py` (linked to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53291). These tests were mostly duplicated with `test_online.py`, and taking excessive time (e.g. in [(MI300) Quantization](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12674/list?sid=01a07b19-ca08-487c-b195-fd03f88df6b4&tab=output) group):

```
70.85s call     tests/quantization/test_fp8.py::test_online_quant_peak_mem
55.51s call     tests/quantization/test_fp8.py::test_online_quantization[True-False-auto]
54.31s call     tests/quantization/test_fp8.py::test_online_quant_load_format_dummy
45.18s call     tests/quantization/test_fp8.py::test_online_quantization[True-False-fp8]
37.99s call     tests/quantization/test_fp8.py::test_online_quantization[False-False-fp8]
31.28s call     tests/quantization/test_fp8.py::test_online_quantization[False-False-auto]
```

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py -s -vvvvv -k "test_legacy_fp8_online_quantization_prompts_new_interface"`
- `pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py -s -vvvvv -k "test_online_quantization and fp8_per_tensor"`

## Test Results

`test_online.py` passing on MI350

Added new tests only: `5 passed, 4 skipped, 53 deselected, 14 warnings in 23.28s`


## Latest-main validation (2026-09-22)

Updated this existing PR for review comment `warning_once` and merged upstream main at `1b3b88ec2b`. The import conflict in `tests/quantization/test_fp8.py` preserves main's new ModelOpt coverage and this PR's removal of the unused online FP8 import. No duplicate PR was created. AI assistance was used for this update.

- `git diff --name-only origin/main -z | xargs -0 .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files`: passed all applicable hooks across all 11 PR files.
- `chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py tests/quantization/test_fp8.py -q -k 'legacy_fp8_online_quantization or (test_online_quantization and fp8_per_tensor) or test_deepseek_v41_mxfp8_scale_loading or test_deepseek_v41_vl_mapper_routes_linear_scales'`: **8 passed, 4 failed, 80 deselected** on B300. The legacy FP8 fallback/warning test and seven DeepSeek scale-loading/mapping cases passed. All four online FP8 model-forward cases stopped at a local compiled-extension mismatch: `_moe_C::moe_align_block_size` accepts 7 arguments, but the Python wrapper on current main passes 8. These four cases require rebuilding or installing matching CUDA extensions before their runtime result can be validated.


## Compatibility fixes and validation (2026-09-23)

The legacy online `fp8` alias now preserves explicit quantization overrides using the same defaults as `fp8_per_tensor`. Qianfan OCR retains its vision/projector/head exclusions for global online FP8 schemes without modifying shared defaults. The Qwen PLE rejection test now constructs the supported online config type; online-FP8 docs and Intel CI commands use `fp8_per_tensor`.

These fixes update this existing migration PR rather than creating a duplicate PR. AI assistance was used for the changes and validation.

- `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py tests/quantization/test_quantization_config_args.py -q`: **44 passed, 29 CUDA-only tests skipped**.
- `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py -k 'legacy_fp8_online or qianfan_online_fp8 or online_overlay or online_shorthand_selects_checkpoint_or_online_config or checkpoint_quantization_rejects_online_shorthand or activation_only_override' -q`: **15 passed**.
- `.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files .buildkite/intel_jobs/test-intel.yaml .buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-intel-ci-test.sh docs/features/quantization/llm_compressor/fp8.md tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py tests/quantization/test_online.py vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py vllm/model_executor/models/qianfan_ocr.py`: **all applicable hooks passed**.
- `.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py tests/quantization/test_online.py vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py vllm/model_executor/models/qianfan_ocr.py`: **passed**.
- A B300 generation comparison using `chg run -g=1 -- env PATH="/home/mgoin/code/vllm/.venv/bin:$PATH" PYTHONPATH=/tmp/vllm-pr53585-local-fixes HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 .venv/bin/python /tmp/pr53585-local-smoke.py` **passed**. Cached `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, eager mode, seed 0, and greedy 12-token generation produced identical token IDs for `fp8` and `fp8_per_tensor` on both prompts (`The capital of France is`, `2 + 2 =`). Both used `quantization_config={"linear": "fp8_per_block", "ignore": ["model.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj"]}` and reported 111 quantized layers, including 27 of 28 attention output projections.

The GPU smoke test used CUTLASS because DeepGEMM was unavailable in the local checkout. This is limited generation coverage; full Qianfan OCR accuracy evaluation and Intel XPU execution were not run.

title: [8/N] HiSparse: add DeepSeek V4 support
body:
## Summary

- Integrate DeepSeek V4 C4 sparse MLA with HiSparse resident and host-backed cache paths.
- Add the compressed slot/block geometry needed by DeepSeek V4 while keeping non-C4 cache groups resident on GPU.
- Preserve the split FP8 value/scale page layout during host backup and hot-buffer staging.
- Resolve C4 FlashMLA decode selections through HiSparse and stage compressed prefill cache rows.

This support was extracted from #51323 so the validated GLM/DeepSeek-V3.2 HiSparse implementation can be reviewed and merged without DeepSeek V4's compressed cache geometry. It does not duplicate another open PR; searches for DeepSeek V4 HiSparse work found only the parent HiSparse PR from which this change was split.

## Tests

- `cmake --build --preset release --target _C_stable_libtorch` (passed)
- `python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -q -k hisparse` (22 passed)
- `python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py -q` (100 passed)
- Pre-commit hooks passed for all files changed while splitting the generic and DeepSeek V4 paths.

## Model evaluation

The latest DeepSeek V4 B300 throughput sweep exposed a substantial high-concurrency regression and an allocator failure under saturation. The sweep also used a metrics revision with invalid hot-path counter instrumentation, so those numbers are not suitable as final performance evidence. This PR remains draft until DeepSeek V4 performance and saturation robustness are resolved and re-evaluated.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review, testing, and preparation of this PR.

title: [Performance] vLLM warmup does not cover C128A extra_topk=384 on SM120 sparse-MLA decode, causing SparseMlaDecodeV3Runner tactic=-1 fallback
body:
## Summary

vLLM startup warmup for DeepSeek-V4-Flash with SM120 (RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell) sparse-MLA decode only generates FlashInfer autotune cache entries for `extra_topk={0, 128, 512}`. At runtime, C128A compressed cache dynamically selects `extra_topk=256` (seq 16,512–32,895) or `extra_topk=384` (seq 32,896–33,792). Since both widths are missing from the autotune cache, every long-sequence decode step falls back to `SparseMlaDecodeV3Runner tactic=-1`, degrading performance.

This is a **performance** issue (not a correctness bug): `tactic=-1` is FlashInfer's legitimate heuristic fallback kernel that produces mathematically correct results, just with a suboptimal tactic. The issue is classified as performance because the functional output is correct; only the kernel selection is suboptimal.


## Environment

### Hardware

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| GPU | 4 × NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 72GB Blackwell (SM120), TP4 |
| NVIDIA Driver | 580.126.20 |

### Software

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| vLLM | `0.1.dev20005+g75c2eef60` (custom build based on current main) |
| flashinfer-python | `0.6.18.dev20260811` |
| flashinfer-cubin | `0.6.18.dev20260811` |
| flashinfer-jit-cache | `0.6.18.dev20260811+cu130` |
| PyTorch | `2.13.0+cu130` |
| CUDA | 13.0 |

### Container image

The reproduction uses a custom image built from the vLLM cu13 nightly base, with FlashInfer upgraded from 0.6.16.post3 to 0.6.18.dev20260811.

DeepSeek-V4-Flash requires FlashInfer 0.6.18.dev because the base nightly image ships FlashInfer 0.6.16.post3, whose SM120 sparse-MLA prefill kernel lacks the `num_heads=8` branch — at TP=8 (8 heads/card), this crashes on startup. FlashInfer 0.6.18.dev (PR [#4380](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4380), merged 2026-08-08) adds the NH=8 padded-tile prefill kernel and fixes DSpark draft-decode token routing, making DeepSeek-V4-Flash bootable on SM120.

**Image pull command:**
```bash
docker pull hai-beijing.tencentcloudcr.com/dorianwu-sglang/vllm:hai-dsv4flash-pro5000
```

This image only modifies the three FlashInfer wheels (python/cubin/jit_cache); nothing else is changed vs the base `hai-beijing.tencentcloudcr.com/dorianwu-sglang/vllm:nightly-dev-cu13` (vLLM commit `75c2eef`, FlashInfer 0.6.16.post3). The image used in this report is tagged `hai-deepseek-v4-flash-vllm:latest` (`sha256:113c108a11f3...4086cee`), which is a local re-tag of the same image.

### Model configuration

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Model | DeepSeek-V4-Flash (FP8 KV cache, speculative with DSpark, 5 spec tokens) |
| max_model_len | 33,792 |
| max_num_batched_tokens | 8,448 |
| max_num_seqs | 32 |
| tensor_parallel_size | 4 |
| enable_flashinfer_autotune | True (default for this model) |
| enable_prefix_caching | False |

## Reproduction

### Launch command

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \\
python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \\
  --model /model \\
  --host 0.0.0.0 \\
  --port 30013 \\
  --trust-remote-code \\
  --served-model-name DeepSeek-V4-Flash \\
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \\
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \\
  --speculative-config \'{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}\' \\
  --max-model-len 33792 \\
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8448 \\
  --max-num-seqs 32 \\
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \\
  --seed 0 \\
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

### Observed behavior during startup

During warmup, the log shows:
```
flashinfer_sparse_mla_warmup.py:233 - Warming up DeepSeek V4 sparse MLA attention for mixed tokens=16.
flashinfer_sparse_mla_warmup.py:124 - Autotuning FlashInfer SM120 sparse MLA DSv4 decode with cache: .../autotune_configs.json
```

The autotune warmup generates **24 cache entries** with `extra_topk ∈ {0, 128, 512}` only — **zero entries for `extra_topk=256` and `extra_topk=384`**.

During CUDA Graph capture, **944 `tactic=-1` fallback warnings** are emitted across all 4 TP workers, covering 4 unique batch shapes (all with `extra_topk=384`):

| Batch (T) | extra_topk | T bucket | Warnings per TP | Total (×4 TP) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 6 | 384 | 8 | 236 | 236 |
| 12 | 384 | 16 | 236 | 236 |
| 24 | 384 | 32 | 236 | 236 |
| 60 | 384 | 64 | 236 | 236 |

**Total: 944 warnings** (4 unique shapes × 236 per shape × 1 per TP worker per shape = 944).

Note: 256-width fallbacks were not observed in this specific run because the CUDA Graph capture sizes (`[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, ..., 384]`) with `max_model_len=33792` and DSpark 5 spec tokens produce `extra_topk=384` at all capture sizes. However, `extra_topk=256` is statically reachable (seq 16,512–32,895) and would miss at runtime just as 384 does.

Example warning:
```
WARNING - autotuner.py:1513 - flashinfer.jit: [AutoTuner]: No tuned config covers
sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4 input_shapes=((60, 16, 512), (60, 128), (60, 16, 8, 512),
(60, 16, 8), (60, 16, 512), (60, 16), (60,), (16,), (60, 384), (60,));
falling back to runner=SparseMlaDecodeV3Runner tactic=-1.  This shape is outside the
tuning bucket range -- expand tuning_buckets / max_num_tokens during the next tuning
pass to avoid this perf cliff.
```

### Cache analysis

The autotune cache file at:
`/root/.cache/vllm/flashinfer_autotune_cache/0.6.18.dev20260811/120f/96af87eb6dbf9df352c4360d1a159c7bf53718f047c06b072979c73c88c0965e/autotune_configs.json`

contains 24 entries, all with `extra_topk ∈ {0, 128, 512}`:

| extra_topk | Records per T bucket {1,4,8,16,32,64} | Total |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 1 each | 6 |
| 128 | 1 each | 6 |
| 512 | 1 each (varying tactics) | 6 |
| **256** | **0** | **0** |
| **384** | **0** | **0** |

Cache SHA-256: `38bf5e3d0b960250eff60e9ea5ea77fe7d29b989c88f1d3313cc6daadd805265`

### Fail-closed request validation

Three requests were sent to the running server. All completed with exact requested output token counts. The cache file was unchanged before and after (SHA-256 verified), confirming that runtime requests do not auto-populate missing cache entries:

| Input tokens | Output tokens | Elapsed | Finish reason |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 8193 | 512 | 1.92 s | length |
| 16513 | 64 | 1.59 s | length |
| 32897 | 64 | 3.13 s | length |

Cache SHA-256 before: `38bf5e3d0b960250eff60e9ea5ea77fe7d29b989c88f1d3313cc6daadd805265`
Cache SHA-256 after:  `38bf5e3d0b960250eff60e9ea5ea77fe7d29b989c88f1d3313cc6daadd805265`
Cache unchanged: **Yes**

## Root cause

### Background: What is C128A and extra_topk?

DeepSeek-V4-Flash uses a C128A compressed KV cache: every 128 consecutive tokens are compressed into 1 "summary" token. During decode, the attention layer selects the most relevant compressed summaries — the number selected is called `extra_topk`. This value scales with the request's sequence length: longer sequences need more summaries to cover the full context.

The `extra_topk` value is not arbitrary — it is computed as `next_power_of_2(max_seq_len // 128)`, clamped to a minimum of 128 (the C128A tile alignment) and a maximum of `c128a_max_compressed` (the total number of compressed tokens for `max_model_len`). For `max_model_len=33,792`, this maximum is `384`.

### 1. C128A runtime width dynamically ranges over {128, 256, 384}

In `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/sparse_mla.py`, the C128A compressed cache width is computed at initialization:

```python
# sparse_mla.py:166-170 (initialization)
c128a_max_compressed = cdiv(max_model_len, compress_ratio)       # cdiv(33792, 128) = 264
c128a_max_compressed = cdiv(c128a_max_compressed, _C128A_TOPK_ALIGNMENT) * _C128A_TOPK_ALIGNMENT
                                                                    # cdiv(264, 128) * 128 = 384
```

At runtime, the active width is dynamically selected based on the current batch's `max_seq_len`:

```python
# sparse_mla.py:261-265 (per-batch, at metadata build time)
active_topk_width = min(
    max(
        triton.next_power_of_2(max(cm.max_seq_len // self.compress_ratio, 1)),
        _C128A_TOPK_ALIGNMENT,   # 128
    ),
    self.c128a_max_compressed,    # 384
)
```

For `max_model_len=33,792`, the three runtime-reachable widths are:

| Request max_seq_len | max_seq_len // 128 | next_power_of_2 | active_topk_width |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1–16,511 | 0–128 | 1–128 | **128** |
| 16,512–32,895 | 129–256 | 256 | **256** |
| 32,896–33,792 | 257–264 | 512 → clamped | **384** |

All three widths are statically reachable in production. Any request with context length ≥ 16,512 tokens will miss the cache.

### 2. FlashInfer autotune cache keys on exact `extra_topk`

FlashInfer's sparse-MLA autotune cache uses the exact `extra_topk` value as part of the cache key. A tactic tuned for `extra_topk=512` cannot cover `extra_topk=384` — they are separate entries. The T (batch size) dimension uses ceiling buckets `{1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64}`, so a T=60 request maps to bucket 64. The cache miss is specifically on the `extra_topk` width dimension, not the T dimension.

### 3. Warmup only exercises `extra_topk=128`

The warmup path in `vllm/model_executor/warmup/flashinfer_sparse_mla_warmup.py` uses:

```python
_SPARSE_MLA_MIXED_WARMUP_TOKENS = 16
```

This creates a mixed batch (`create_mixed_batch=True`) in `_dummy_run` where decode tokens have `seq_lens=[1]` (`gpu_model_runner.py:6131`):

```python
# gpu_model_runner.py:6131 (mixed batch for warmup)
seq_lens = torch.tensor([1] * num_decode_tokens + [num_prefill_tokens + 1], ...)
```

With `seq_lens=1`, the C128A width computation yields:
```
active_topk_width = min(max(next_power_of_2(1 // 128), 128), 384) = 128
```

The warmup **never simulates a decode request with `seq_len ≥ 16,512`**, so `extra_topk=256` and `extra_topk=384` are never autotuned. The 16-token mixed batch is sufficient for JIT compilation warmup (triggering kernel compilation and loading), but it does not cover the autotune shape space for C128A widths.

### Why the warmup gap was not caught earlier

The warmup code was designed for JIT compilation warmup — ensuring that kernels are compiled and loaded before serving requests. The `_dummy_run` with 16 tokens achieves this goal. However, the same `_dummy_run` is also used for FlashInfer autotuning (wrapped in `flashinfer_autotune(True, ...)` context), which requires shape coverage, not just compilation. The two concerns (JIT warmup vs. autotune shape coverage) were conflated into a single dummy run with a minimal shape, leaving the autotune cache incomplete for C128A widths beyond 128.

## Expected behavior

- Startup autotune covers **every** runtime-reachable C128A width: `{128, 256, 384}` for `max_model_len=33,792`.
- A production shape does not use `tactic=-1` only because warmup selected a different sequence-length bucket.
- Existing cache entries (for `extra_topk=0, 128, 512`) survive the additional warmup passes.
- Partial tuning failure preserves the baseline cache and cannot deadlock TP followers.
- Repeated startup with a complete cache is idempotent.

## Proposed fix

The warmup should enumerate all runtime-reachable C128A widths and exercise each through the autotune path. For each width, a `_dummy_run` with `profile_seq_lens` set to a representative `seq_len` that triggers that width should be run under the `flashinfer_autotune` context.

Concretely, the warmup should run additional autotune passes with:
- `profile_seq_lens=16512` → triggers `extra_topk=256`
- `profile_seq_lens=max_model_len` → triggers `extra_topk=384`

The existing pass (`seq_lens=[1]`) already covers `extra_topk=128`.

See linked PR #53605 for implementation.

## Additional context

- The same defect was independently reproduced on vLLM current main (`a047e2543`) with FlashInfer 0.6.17 (pinned dependency), confirming it is not version-specific to 0.6.18.dev.
- In the motivating environment, adding real width-384 tactics (manual cache intervention) removed all 944 fallback warnings but did not make target logits bit-reproducible.

## Before submitting a new issue

- [x] Searched open and closed vLLM issues and PRs for `extra_topk`, `384`, `sparse MLA`, `FlashInfer`, `autotune`, and `warmup`.
- [x] Found related reports, but no issue or PR covering the missing C128A production-width tuning keys.
- [x] Reproduced the scoped width-384 defect on the production environment (FlashInfer 0.6.18.dev20260811) and independently on current main + FlashInfer 0.6.17.

title: [Performance] vLLM warmup does not cover C128A extra_topk=384 on SM120 sparse-MLA decode, causing SparseMlaDecodeV3Runner tactic=-1 fallback
body:
# [Performance] vLLM warmup does not cover C128A `extra_topk=384` on SM120 sparse-MLA decode, causing `SparseMlaDecodeV3Runner tactic=-1` fallback

## Summary

vLLM startup warmup for DeepSeek-V4-Flash with SM120 (RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell) sparse-MLA decode only generates FlashInfer autotune cache entries for `extra_topk={0, 128, 512}`. At runtime, when a request\'s context length exceeds 32,895 tokens, the C128A compressed cache selects `extra_topk=384`. Since this exact width is missing from the autotune cache, every decode step falls back to `SparseMlaDecodeV3Runner tactic=-1`, degrading performance.

The root cause is in the warmup path: `_SPARSE_MLA_MIXED_WARMUP_TOKENS = 16` (in `flashinfer_sparse_mla_warmup.py`) creates a mixed batch where decode tokens have `seq_lens=[1]`, which maps to `active_topk_width=128`. The warmup never simulates long-sequence decode, so `extra_topk=384` is never exercised.

## Environment

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| GPU | 4 × NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 72GB Blackwell (SM120), TP4 |
| NVIDIA Driver | 580.126.20 |
| vLLM | `0.1.dev20005+g75c2eef60` (custom build based on current main) |
| flashinfer-python | `0.6.18.dev20260811` |
| flashinfer-cubin | `0.6.18.dev20260811` |
| flashinfer-jit-cache | `0.6.18.dev20260811+cu130` |
| PyTorch | `2.13.0+cu130` |
| CUDA | 13.0 |
| Model | DeepSeek-V4-Flash (FP8 KV cache, speculative with DSpark, 5 spec tokens) |
| Container image | `hai-deepseek-v4-flash-vllm:latest` (`sha256:113c108a11f3...4086cee`) |

## Reproduction

### Launch command

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \\
python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \\
  --model /model \\
  --host 0.0.0.0 \\
  --port 30013 \\
  --trust-remote-code \\
  --served-model-name DeepSeek-V4-Flash \\
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \\
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \\
  --speculative-config \'{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}\' \\
  --max-model-len 33792 \\
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8448 \\
  --max-num-seqs 32 \\
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \\
  --seed 0 \\
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

Note: `enable_flashinfer_autotune=True` is set in the kernel config by default for this model.

### Observed behavior

During startup, the FlashInfer autotune warmup generates **24 cache entries** with `extra_topk ∈ {0, 128, 512}` only — **zero entries for `extra_topk=384`**.

During CUDA Graph capture, **944 `tactic=-1` fallback warnings** are emitted across all 4 TP workers, covering 4 unique batch shapes:

| Batch (T) | extra_topk | T bucket | Warning count (per shape, ×4 TP) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 6 | 384 | 8 | 236 |
| 12 | 384 | 16 | 236 |
| 24 | 384 | 32 | 236 |
| 60 | 384 | 64 | 236 |

**Total: 944 warnings** (236 × 4 unique shapes, each emitted by all 4 TP workers).

Example warning:
```
WARNING - autotuner.py:1513 - flashinfer.jit: [AutoTuner]: No tuned config covers
sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4 input_shapes=((60, 16, 512), (60, 128), (60, 16, 8, 512),
(60, 16, 8), (60, 16, 512), (60, 16), (60,), (16,), (60, 384), (60,));
falling back to runner=SparseMlaDecodeV3Runner tactic=-1.  This shape is outside the
tuning bucket range -- expand tuning_buckets / max_num_tokens during the next tuning
pass to avoid this perf cliff.
```

### Cache analysis

The autotune cache file contains 24 entries, all with `extra_topk ∈ {0, 128, 512}`:

| extra_topk | Records per T bucket {1,4,8,16,32,64} | Total |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 1 each | 6 |
| 128 | 1 each | 6 |
| 512 | 1 each (varying tactics) | 6 |
| **384** | **0** | **0** |

Cache SHA-256: `38bf5e3d0b960250eff60e9ea5ea77fe7d29b989c88f1d3313cc6daadd805265`

### Fail-closed request validation

Three requests were sent to the running server. All completed with exact requested output token counts. The cache file was unchanged before and after (SHA-256 verified):

| Input tokens | Output tokens | Elapsed | Finish reason |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 8193 | 512 | 1.92 s | length |
| 16513 | 64 | 1.59 s | length |
| 32897 | 64 | 3.13 s | length |

Cache SHA-256 before: `38bf5e3d0b960250eff60e9ea5ea77fe7d29b989c88f1d3313cc6daadd805265`
Cache SHA-256 after:  `38bf5e3d0b960250eff60e9ea5ea77fe7d29b989c88f1d3313cc6daadd805265`
Cache unchanged: **Yes**

## Root cause

### 1. C128A runtime width reaches 384

In `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/sparse_mla.py`, the C128A compressed cache width is computed as:

```python
# sparse_mla.py:166-170
c128a_max_compressed = cdiv(max_model_len, compress_ratio)       # cdiv(33792, 128) = 264
c128a_max_compressed = cdiv(c128a_max_compressed, _C128A_TOPK_ALIGNMENT) * _C128A_TOPK_ALIGNMENT
                                                                    # cdiv(264, 128) * 128 = 384
```

At runtime, the active width is dynamically selected (`sparse_mla.py:261-265`):

```python
active_topk_width = min(
    max(
        triton.next_power_of_2(max(cm.max_seq_len // self.compress_ratio, 1)),
        _C128A_TOPK_ALIGNMENT,   # 128
    ),
    self.c128a_max_compressed,    # 384
)
```

For `max_model_len=33792`, the static reachable widths are:

| active max_seq_len | extra_topk |
| ---: | ---: |
| 1–16,511 | 128 |
| 16,512–32,895 | 256 |
| 32,896–33,792 | 384 |

### 2. FlashInfer cache key includes exact `extra_topk`

FlashInfer\'s sparse-MLA tuning key includes the exact `extra_topk` value. A width-512 tactic cannot cover width-384. The T dimension uses ceiling buckets `{1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64}` (e.g. T=60 maps to bucket 64), so the miss is specifically on the width dimension.

### 3. Warmup never exercises long-sequence decode

The warmup path in `vllm/model_executor/warmup/flashinfer_sparse_mla_warmup.py` uses:

```python
_SPARSE_MLA_MIXED_WARMUP_TOKENS = 16
```

This creates a mixed batch (`create_mixed_batch=True`) in `_dummy_run` where decode tokens have `seq_lens=[1]` (`gpu_model_runner.py:6131`):

```python
seq_lens = torch.tensor([1] * num_decode_tokens + [num_prefill_tokens + 1], ...)
```

With `seq_lens=1`, `active_topk_width = min(max(next_power_of_2(1//128), 128), 384) = 128`.

The warmup **never simulates a decode request with `seq_len > 32895`**, so `extra_topk=384` is never autotuned.

## Expected behavior

- Startup autotune covers every runtime-reachable C128A width, including 384 (and 256).
- A production shape does not use `tactic=-1` only because warmup selected a different sequence-length bucket.
- Existing cache entries survive successful tuning.
- Partial tuning failure preserves the baseline cache and cannot deadlock TP followers.
- Repeated startup with a complete cache is idempotent.

## Proposed fix

The warmup should enumerate runtime-reachable C128A widths and exercise each through the model warmup / autotune path. Concretely, in `flashinfer_sparse_mla_warmup.py` or `gpu_model_runner.py`, the dummy run should include at least one decode request with `seq_len` large enough to trigger `extra_topk=384` (i.e. `seq_len ≥ 32896` for `max_model_len=33792`).

Alternatively, if FlashInfer exposes a supported public shape-autotune entrypoint, vLLM could call it on the TP leader to pre-populate the missing width.

## Additional context

- This issue is separate from #53257 and #53436.
- The same defect was independently reproduced on vLLM current main (`a047e2543`) with FlashInfer 0.6.17 (pinned dependency), confirming it is not version-specific to 0.6.18.dev.
- In the motivating environment, adding real width-384 tactics (manual cache intervention) removed all fallback warnings but did not make target logits bit-reproducible. A linked PR must not claim to fix greedy-output or speculative-acceptance non-determinism.

## Before submitting a new issue

- [x] Searched open and closed vLLM issues and PRs for `extra_topk`, `384`, `sparse MLA`, `FlashInfer`, `autotune`, and `warmup`.
- [x] Found related reports, but no issue or PR covering the missing C128A production-width tuning keys.
- [x] Reproduced the scoped width-384 defect on the production environment (FlashInfer 0.6.18.dev20260811) and independently on current main + FlashInfer 0.6.17.

title: fix(warmup): cover all C128A extra_topk widths in sparse-MLA autotune
body:
Fixes #53600

## Description

The FlashInfer sparse-MLA warmup for DeepSeek-V4-Flash only exercises `extra_topk=128` during startup. At runtime, C128A compressed cache dynamically selects wider widths — `256` for sequences 16,512–32,895 and `384` for sequences 32,896–33,792 (when `max_model_len=33,792`). Each width is an independent FlashInfer autotune cache key; a 128-width tactic cannot cover 256 or 384. This causes `SparseMlaDecodeV3Runner tactic=-1` fallback at runtime, degrading decode performance.

In the motivating environment, this resulted in **944 `tactic=-1` warnings** during CUDA Graph capture across 4 TP workers, covering 4 unique batch shapes (all with `extra_topk=384`).

## Root Cause

The warmup path in `flashinfer_sparse_mla_warmup.py` uses `_SPARSE_MLA_MIXED_WARMUP_TOKENS = 16`, which creates a mixed batch (`create_mixed_batch=True`) where decode tokens have `seq_lens=[1]` (`gpu_model_runner.py:6131`). With `seq_len=1`, the C128A width computation yields `active_topk_width=128`. The warmup never simulates a decode request with `seq_len ≥ 16,512`, so `extra_topk=256` and `384` are never autotuned.

The root cause is that the warmup conflates two concerns into a single dummy run:
1. **JIT compilation warmup** — ensuring kernels are compiled and loaded (a `seq_len=1` run achieves this).
2. **FlashInfer autotune shape coverage** — generating cache entries for every runtime-reachable shape (requires multiple `seq_len` values).

Using a minimal 16-token batch satisfies (1) but leaves (2) incomplete for C128A widths beyond 128.

## C128A Width Calculation

```python
# sparse_mla.py:166-170 (initialization)
c128a_max_compressed = cdiv(max_model_len, compress_ratio)       # cdiv(33792, 128) = 264
c128a_max_compressed = cdiv(c128a_max_compressed, 128) * 128    # = 384

# sparse_mla.py:261-265 (per-batch, at runtime)
active_topk_width = min(
    max(next_power_of_2(max(cm.max_seq_len // compress_ratio, 1)), 128),
    384,  # c128a_max_compressed
)
```

| Request max_seq_len | max_seq_len // 128 | next_power_of_2 | active_topk_width |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1–16,511 | 0–128 | 1–128 | **128** |
| 16,512–32,895 | 129–256 | 256 | **256** |
| 32,896–33,792 | 257–264 | 512 → clamped | **384** |

## Fix

This PR adds a helper function `_compute_c128a_reachable_widths()` that enumerates all runtime-reachable C128A `extra_topk` widths for a given `max_model_len`. For each width beyond 128, it runs an additional autotune pass with `profile_seq_lens` set to a representative `seq_len` that triggers that width.

The warmup flow is now:
1. **Existing mixed batch** (`seq_len=1`) → covers `extra_topk=128` (unchanged)
2. **New autotune pass** (`profile_seq_lens=16513`) → covers `extra_topk=256`
3. **New autotune pass** (`profile_seq_lens=32897`) → covers `extra_topk=384`

The `_compute_c128a_reachable_widths()` helper scans from `seq_len=1` to `max_model_len` in steps of `compress_ratio` (128), detecting each width transition. This makes the fix general for any `max_model_len`, not hardcoded to 33792.

### V2 model runner limitation

The V2 model runner (`run_mixed_prefill_decode_warmup`) does not yet support `profile_seq_lens`. When `profile_seq_lens` is provided, the code falls through to the V1 `_dummy_run` path. A TODO is left for future V2 support.

## Evidence

- **Cache before fix**: 24 entries, `extra_topk ∈ {0, 128, 512}`, zero for 256 and 384
- **Warnings**: 944 `tactic=-1` fallbacks during CUDA Graph capture (4 shapes × 236 × 1 per TP × 4 TP)
- **Environment**: 4× RTX PRO 5000 72GB (SM120), FlashInfer 0.6.18.dev20260811, vLLM 0.1.dev20005
- After manual cache intervention (adding width-384 tactics), all fallback warnings disappeared

## Testing

- [x] Syntax validation passed for both source and test files
- [x] `_compute_c128a_reachable_widths(33792)` returns `[128, 256, 384]` with correct representative `seq_len` values
- [x] Unit test verifies warmup calls autotune 3 times (128, 256, 384)
- [x] Unit test verifies `profile_seq_lens` is set for widths > 128
- [ ] Full integration test on SM120 hardware (requires TP4 RTX PRO 5000 system)

title: [Bug]: CPU KV offload (OffloadingConnector) crashes on DeepSeek-V4 MLA — flat int8 layout assumption vs padded multi-group uint8 cache
body:
## Summary

`OffloadingConnector` (stock vLLM, no patches) with an `fs_python` secondary tier kills the worker during startup on DeepSeek-V4-Flash: `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`. Reproduced on v0.27.1 with and without the b12x attention backend; an older stack (0.21.1rc1) deadlocks in CUDA-graph capture instead. Full test: https://github.com/maci0/vllm-spark-nvfp4/blob/main/KV_OFFLOAD_MLA.md

## Root cause: the transfer path assumes a flat, uniform int8 cache

`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py` asserts exactly:

```python
assert gpu_tensor.dtype == torch.int8
assert gpu_tensor.ndim == 2
```

then computes transfer destinations with raw pointer arithmetic:

```python
block_page_size = tensor.shape[1] // blocks_per_chunk
all_ptrs = (base_ptr + block_ids * row_stride) + sub_offsets
```

Those addresses feed a Triton kernel (`swap_blocks_triton.py`) that reinterprets them as `int64*` words. Nothing validates the addresses against the allocation bounds.

DeepSeek-V4's MLA cache violates every part of that assumption:

| Assumption | DSV4 MLA reality |
|---|---|
| `dtype == torch.int8` | `uint8` packed pages |
| one uniform `block_page_size` | per-group padded pages — `MLAAttentionSpec.page_size_bytes` (576/584 B alignment), and a second group (lightning indexer) with different geometry |
| flat 2-D rows | paged layout whose row stride includes alignment padding |

`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/spec.py` compounds it: a single `worker_kv_bytes_per_block` is derived for the whole cache, so the hybrid multi-group geometry cannot be represented at all. Once `block_page_size` diverges from the true padded page size, every pointer drifts by an accumulating offset → out-of-bounds access (or silent corruption).

## Related: LMCache + DSV4

`LMCacheConnectorV1` does not implement `SupportsHMA`, so `--kv-transfer-config` disables the hybrid KV manager and DSV4 sparse-MLA decode then fails (`sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4: num_tokens>64 (36 vs 64)`). LMCache/LMCache#3261 tracks HMA support and was closed without an implementation. Marking the connector `SupportsHMA` alone would just move the failure to the same transfer-layout crash above — the transfer path itself needs to understand padded multi-group pages first.

## Suggested direction

1. Thread per-group `page_size_bytes` (and dtype) from `MLAAttentionSpec` through `spec.py` → `gpu_worker.py` instead of the single `worker_kv_bytes_per_block`.
2. Allow `uint8` (byte-wise identical to int8 for the swap kernel).
3. Validate computed transfer addresses against allocation bounds (the Triton kernel's mask bounds against the *declared* size only).

## Environment

2x DGX Spark (GB10, SM121a, 128 GiB unified memory), DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 + DSpark k=5, `fp8_ds_mla` and `nvfp4_ds_mla` cache dtypes, vLLM main `e25c586b9` era and v0.27.1.

title: [Spec Decode] Verify in head dtype and drop the FP32 chunk workaround
body:
## Purpose

Speculative decoding expands each request into multiple verification positions. Whenever
any active logits processor is present, the target rejection verifier currently
materializes an FP32 processing canvas of shape `[num_verification_tokens, vocab_size]`.
The production path bounds the transient allocation with a 1 GiB chunk, which in turn
forces a cap on the total logits adaptive verification may schedule per step.

This PR makes the target verifier explicitly opt into storing and processing logits in
the LM head dtype (BF16/FP16), and deletes the FP32 canvas, the chunk iterator, and the
adaptive cap:

- temperature is applied in FP32 when the rejection kernels, top-k/top-p, and the
  processed-logprob scorer load the logits; it is never written back to the stored
  logits;
- top-k/top-p computes its boundary in FP32 and writes back only the mask; penalties are
  computed in FP32 and written back to the head dtype with a single rounding; exact mask
  processors keep their original semantics;
- raw reporting keeps an original head-dtype snapshot only when a processor would
  overwrite the input; processed reporting reads the processed stored logits;
- the adaptive cost tables, selection formula, grammar mapping, and zero-budget contract
  are unchanged; only the hard cap that existed to serve the FP32 chunk is removed;
- the PyTorch top-p fallback's softmax and cumulative sum are pinned to FP32, since
  head-dtype target logits make the previously latent BF16 accumulation path reachable;
- speculative decoding fails closed on any nonzero `min_p`, and custom
  `logprob_token_ids` reporting is wired up.

The regular sampler, non-speculative decoding, and zero-draft steps keep the existing
FP32 processing path.

<details>
<summary>Supported sampling processors and reporting behavior</summary>

All supported processors below avoid materializing a full-vocabulary FP32 verifier canvas. This
PR does not change which processors are supported by speculative decoding.

| Sampling parameter / processor | Property | Supported in Spec Decode | Effect on stored logits | Head-dtype precision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| temperature | Distribution scaling | Yes (unchanged) | None; consumers scale on load | Computed in FP32 |
| top_k / top_p | Selection mask | Yes (unchanged) | Preserve kept values; mask others with `-inf` | Exact |
| repetition / frequency / presence penalties | Value transformation | Yes (unchanged) | Rewrite affected values | One BF16/FP16 rounding |
| allowed_token_ids / min_tokens / bad_words | Hard token mask | Yes (unchanged) | Write `-inf` masks | Exact |
| thinking_token_budget | Forced-token override | Yes (unchanged) | Write a dtype-safe sentinel | Semantically exact |
| structured-output grammar mask | Hard token mask applied before verification | Yes (unchanged) | Write `-inf` masks | Exact |
| min_p | Probability filter | No (unchanged) | — | Any nonzero value fails validation |
| logit_bias | Additive value transformation | No (unchanged) | — | One BF16/FP16 rounding |

Raw and processed logprobs are reporting modes rather than logits processors. Raw reporting reads
a pre-processor head-dtype snapshot when stored logits may be modified. Processed reporting reads
the processed stored logits and applies temperature in FP32 on load. Adaptive-verification output
logprobs were enabled upstream by #52242 (merged 2026-08-25); this PR is rebased on top of it and
preserves its device-tensor boundary reporting through the head-dtype scorer.

</details>

Penalties are the only path that writes back to the stored logits lossily: the processor
still computes in FP32, but the result is rounded to BF16/FP16 once. Please pay
particular attention to the penalty-only, stochastic, and `top_k=1` results under
**Numerical fidelity and model quality** below. We did not find an implementation that
preserves FP32-equivalent penalty output without either reintroducing full-vocabulary
FP32 storage or adding significant extra scans/latency; this PR therefore keeps this
numerical trade-off explicit rather than claiming processed penalty logprobs are bitwise
FP32.

### Why this is not a repeat of #48641

#48641 removed the same FP32 copy and was reverted in full three days later by #49033
over a never-root-caused DP+EP+MTP hang. Beyond removing the copy, #48641 also changed
the numerics: it applied temperature by **writing the scaled values back into the
stored head-dtype logits**, for the regular sampler and the speculative verifier
alike. Every such write-back costs an extra BF16/FP16 rounding, and every downstream
consumer — rejection statistics, top-k/top-p, logprob reporting — then reads the
already-rounded, temperature-scaled values. Whether or not that contributed to the
hang, it is a real precision hazard, and this PR is built specifically to remove it:

- stored logits always keep their pre-temperature values; temperature is applied in
  FP32 registers at every load site and never touches storage;
- top-k/top-p computes its boundary in FP32 and writes back only `-inf` masks — kept
  logits are bit-identical to what the LM head produced;
- the only remaining lossy write-back is penalties, which is quantified and
  guardrailed under **Numerical fidelity and model quality** below;
- the scope is the speculative verifier only; the regular sampler keeps its FP32 path.

On the risk side, a permanent e2e test covers both #49033's pure-greedy control path
and an active path that actually enters the head-dtype verifier, in the same
distributed engine. That test guards the risk quadrant; it does not claim to reproduce
or explain the root cause of the original hang.

### Related work

- **#53090** (open) fuses only a temperature-only fast path; other processors or
  processed logprobs still fall back to the FP32 canvas, so it cannot delete the
  chunking or the adaptive cap. This PR covers every currently legal
  processor/reporting combination.
- **#50910** (merged) already adopted the "store in head dtype, upcast to FP32 and
  divide by temperature on load" contract on the draft side; this PR aligns the target
  verifier to the same contract.
- **#47808**'s `max_total_logits` cap exists only to guarantee the FP32 verifier lands
  in a single safe chunk; this PR removes that premise and does not change the adaptive
  verification algorithm.
- **#40704** is porting n-gram drafting to Model Runner V2; until it lands, n-gram
  still falls back to Model Runner V1, so the custom `logprob_token_ids` e2e request
  temporarily covers Eagle only.
- **#52242** (merged 2026-08-25, while this PR was in flight) lifted the
  adaptive-verification output-logprobs restriction. This PR is rebased on top of it:
  the device-side `cu_num_generated_tokens` boundaries it introduced are kept and flow
  through the head-dtype scorer unchanged, and removing the chunked path also removes
  the stale-layout hazard its `_verify_in_chunks` assert defended against. If
  **#52477** lands first, the grammar-mapping tests will need a rebase update.
- One acceptance criterion of **RFC #42259** is that the MRV2 path should not
  materialize avoidable full-vocabulary temporaries; the FP32 canvas this PR deletes is
  exactly such a temporary.

## Test Plan

1. Run the focused CUDA test matrix for sampling-parameter validation, sampler state,
   thinking budget, top-k/top-p, rejection sampling, adaptive verification, and the
   logprob numerical oracles and head-dtype penalty path.
2. Run the complete `test_spec_decode_logprobs` matrix across 3 speculative model setups and all
   4 `LogprobsMode` values, comparing emitted tokens and raw/processed logprob outputs with the
   non-speculative reference.
3. Run the DP2+EP+MTP regression twice. In the same distributed engine, exercise both the
   pure-greedy #49033 control signature and an active-sampling request that enters the head-dtype
   verifier; require each wave to draft and match the non-speculative output.
4. Benchmark `RejectionSampler.__call__` with BF16 logits, `K=7`, `V=129280`, and
   `R={8,256,512}` across temperature, top-p, penalties, combined processors, and logprob
   reporting. Compare p50 latency and per-call CUDA peak allocation with the FP32-canvas control.
5. Run a paired 1319-question, 5-shot GSM8K A/B evaluation covering the default path,
   penalties-only, stochastic top-p with penalties, and `top_k=1`; compare accuracy, invalid
   outputs, and acceptance length.

<details>
<summary>Repository test commands</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/test_sampling_params.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py \
  tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py \
  tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py::test_token_logprobs_apply_virtual_temperature
```

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -vv -s \
  tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py::test_spec_decode_logprobs
```

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -vv -s \
  'tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_mtp_parallel_load.py::test_deepseek_mtp_load_dp[dp2]'
```

</details>

## Test Result

### Correctness and path coverage

- The targeted GPU suite passed with `231 passed, 2 skipped` (reported from the run; that console
  log was not kept). It covers every supported sampling processor, raw/processed reporting,
  adaptive verification, thinking budget and the head-dtype penalty path.
- The full public-model `test_spec_decode_logprobs` matrix passed all 3 model setups × 4
  `LogprobsMode` combinations (`12 passed`). Spec and non-spec runs returned identical emitted
  token IDs, logprob token IDs and ranks. Raw scores were bitwise equal; the largest processed-score
  difference was `0.08334`.
- The DP2+EP+MTP surrogate passed twice consecutively with a minimum spec/non-spec token match ratio
  of `1.000`. Both the pure-greedy wave matching the #49033 incident signature and the active
  sampling wave produced draft tokens, so the test covers both the control path and the new
  head-dtype verifier in the same distributed engine.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` passed for all 19 changed Python files.

These results verify that the optimization is reached in production paths while preserving token
selection and logprob reporting contracts; they do not rely only on isolated kernel tests.

### Verifier memory and latency

The benchmark uses BF16 logits with `K=7`, `V=129280` and `R=512` (4096 verification rows), which
crosses the old approximately 2076-row chunk boundary. The control is the same candidate with the
head-dtype verifier disabled, so the comparison isolates this PR's verifier mode while keeping the
PyTorch top-p correctness fix on both sides.

| Processor | FP32 canvas p50 (ms) | Head dtype p50 (ms) | Per-call peak allocated |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| temperature | 5.054–5.103 | 0.979–1.093 | 1023.20 → 2.33 MiB |
| top-p | 31.178–31.219 | 25.846–26.057 | 1023.20 → 2.33 MiB |
| penalties | 11.960–12.025 | 5.316–8.148 | 1023.20 → 2.33 MiB |
| penalties + top-p | 39.058–39.361 | 30.424–34.095 | 1023.20 → 2.33 MiB |

The measured processor cases reduce the per-call allocation from 1023.20 MiB to 2.33 MiB and
improve p50 latency in every case; temperature-only is approximately five times faster. Processed
logprob reporting similarly falls from 1032.44 MiB to 20.68 MiB. This demonstrates that the FP32
canvas is removed rather than moved behind a different chunk boundary.

Raw reporting with a mutating processor is the intentional exception: preserving pre-processor
values still requires an approximately 1010 MiB BF16 snapshot, for a total around 1030.66 MiB. The
claim is therefore the removal of the verifier FP32 canvas and its local memory/latency cost, not a
general end-to-end throughput improvement.

### Numerical fidelity and model quality

Mask-only processors remain exact because kept logits are never rewritten. Temperature and top-p
processed scores have maximum finite errors of `1.91e-6` and `2.13e-4` against the FP32-input
reference, with no rank differences. Raw-reporting digests are bitwise identical between base and
head-dtype runs.

Penalties are the only lossy stored-processor path. Their FP32 calculation is rounded once on
writeback to BF16/FP16; the penalty + top-p oracle measures a maximum finite score error of
`0.0203`. We therefore evaluated all penalty-enabled combinations on the full 1319-question,
5-shot GSM8K set, in addition to the default control:

| Case | Sampling | Base | Head dtype(PR)   | Accuracy Δ | Acceptance length (base/head) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| standard | greedy; neutral penalties(off)  | 82.942% | 82.942% | 0.000 pp | 4.2015 / 4.1509 |
| penalties-only | greedy; penalties on | 82.259% | 81.577% | −0.682 pp | 4.0394 / 4.0341 |
| stochastic | `temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9`; penalties on | 79.075% | 79.606% | +0.531 pp | 3.9586 / 3.9658 |
| `top_k=1` | `temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9`; penalties on | 82.259% | 81.653% | −0.607 pp | 3.9686 / 3.9878 |

The standard control produced identical output token sequences and correctness for all 1319
questions. Invalid counts were unchanged in every paired run. The three penalty-enabled,
fixed-seed accuracy deltas stay within ±0.682 percentage points, while their acceptance lengths
remain close to base. These are quality guardrails rather than a claim of statistical equivalence;
together with the FP32 oracle they bound the observed effect of the intentional head-dtype penalty
writeback.

## Duplicate check

Checked RFC #42259 and open PRs by issue number and relevant area keywords on 2026-08-24, and
re-checked on 2026-08-25. The only directly overlapping open PR is #53090; the scope difference is
described above.

ran the tests above, and can explain and defend the change end to end.

title: [Bugfix] Avoid double-scaling DeepSeek YaRN max model length
body:
## Description

DeepSeek YaRN checkpoints can declare the post-scaling context in `max_position_embeddings` together with the pre-scaling context in `rope_parameters.original_max_position_embeddings` and a `factor`. The triggering [checkpoint config](https://huggingface.co/Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark-Block5/blob/a202601f9043e965516e3965d02322a1b8f10310/config.json) declares:

```text
max_position_embeddings = 1,048,576
original_max_position_embeddings = 32,768
factor = 32
rope_type = "deepseek_yarn"
```

`_get_and_verify_max_len` already resets the derived length to the original context before applying `factor` for `rope_type="yarn"`. It did not do so for the `deepseek_yarn` type already supported by vLLM's rotary dispatcher, causing the expanded `max_position_embeddings` to be multiplied again:

```text
1,048,576 * 32 = 33,554,432
```

Treat `deepseek_yarn` like `yarn` during max-length derivation. The corrected result is:

```text
32,768 * 32 = 1,048,576
```

This does not change RoPE frequencies, scaling parameters, cache contents, or inference math.

## Not a duplicate

I searched open issues and PRs for `deepseek_yarn`, `derived_max_model_len`, YaRN scaling, and double-scaling before opening this draft.

- #44738 reduces rotary cache allocation when runtime `max_model_len` is shorter; it does not change model-length derivation.
- #51156 bounds speculative draft length by the target before logging. That can mask this value for a shorter target, but does not fix standalone derivation or a target whose limit exceeds the real DeepSeek YaRN cache length.

No open PR found by those searches applies this alias fix.

## Testing

Focused regression test:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py \
  -k get_and_verify_max_len_yarn_uses_original_context -q

2 passed, 189 deselected
```

Repository hooks on both changed files:

```text
pre-commit run --files vllm/config/model.py tests/test_config.py

All applicable hooks passed, including ruff check, ruff format, mypy, SPDX, and repository-specific configuration checks.
```

Exact configuration validation:

| RoPE type | Before | After | Expected |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `yarn` | 1,048,576 | 1,048,576 | 1,048,576 |
| `deepseek_yarn` | 33,554,432 | 1,048,576 | 1,048,576 |

No generation evaluation was run because the patch changes only configuration-derived length metadata and does not alter tensors or model output. The current speculative setup already clamps the final draft length to 1,048,576, so its generated output is unchanged; this patch corrects the underlying derivation for all callers.

## AI assistance

This draft PR was prepared with AI assistance from OpenAI Codex. Human review of every changed line and the test evidence is required before marking it ready for review.

title: [Bug][DSV4][Blackwell SM12x] Indexer decode paged MQA logits broken when DeepGEMM is available: 2-state compress pages vs kernels templated for block_kv 32/64
body:
Summary
DeepSeek-V4 (and V4-Flash) cannot start on Blackwell client GPUs (GB10 / DGX Spark, SM121; likely also SM120) whenever DeepGEMM is importable, because the sparse attention indexer decode path unconditionally routes logits computation into DeepGEMM's paged MQA kernel, which only supports physical page geometries of 32 or 64 states. Since the #51718 KV cache layout standardization, DSV4 uses tokens_per_state = compress_ratio = 128, i.e. kv_cache_spec.num_states = 2. There is no working configuration: pristine main crashes with a clean host assert, and the commonly attempted workaround (gating metadata construction on num_states, as in open PR #53522) trades the loud assert for a silent deferred illegal memory access that surfaces far away from the real culprit.

Environment
2x NVIDIA DGX Spark GB10 (SM121, aarch64), TP=2 native distributed, no Ray. Model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (quantization_config.scale_fmt = ue8m0), dspark speculative decoding next_n=6, kv_cache_dtype fp8, max_model_len 1000000. vLLM built from source at multiple mains between Aug 22 and Aug 24 (reproduced on 0ab4d638a and 6648eb11), torch 2.13.0+cu130, vendored DeepGEMM built from DEEPGEMM_REF=a6b593d, FlashInfer ff22228d.

Failure mode A, pristine main
During compile_or_warm_up_model, on the first decode-shaped forward, get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata asserts:

Assertion error (csrc/apis/attention.hpp:247): block_kv == 32 or block_kv == 64

because self.kv_cache_spec.num_states is 2 for compress-128 pages. This is unconditional in current main: the call site at the end of the decode metadata builder checks nothing but platform.is_cuda() and has_deep_gemm().

Failure mode B, with a num_states gate (open PR #53522)
Adding the obvious gate (only build metadata when num_states is 32 or 64) removes the assert but leaves schedule_metadata as an unfilled zero buffer, and the decode path still launches smxx_fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits unconditionally on CUDA. The kernel consumes the garbage schedule and corrupts memory asynchronously. The sticky CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS then surfaces at an arbitrary later point - in our case persistent_topk's occupancy query (topk.cu:106) during graph capture, and with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 it resolves honestly to smxx_fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits.hpp:202. This cost us the better part of a day because the visible error pointed at completely unrelated kernels.

Root cause
block_kv is a compile-time template parameter of the paged MQA kernel (baked into the JIT instantiation), the metadata scheduler works in units of physical KV blocks, and DSV4's compressed geometry (128 tokens per state, 2 states per page) simply does not fit either supported tile. The pre-standardization tree worked because storage_block_size (64) flowed into the helper natively.

Notes
- Warmup executes decode-shaped forwards regardless of --enforce-eager, so eager mode is not an escape hatch; the same kernel IMAs on the first real decode request anyway.
- The archived megapatch #41834 solved this for SM12x with a dedicated short-row decode top-k subsystem (fused fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_topk_indices kernel plus width-based fallbacks, csrc/libtorch_stable changes). That subsystem has not been sliced upstream; open PR #53522 addresses only the metadata assert and is insufficient on its own for the reasons above.
- Related: #52732 (unguarded DeepGEMM assumptions on sm_121), #47988 (E8M0 block scales in CUTLASS/Triton linear kernels, also required to boot this checkpoint).

Question for maintainers: what is the preferred direction here? Options we see are (a) teaching the arch-12 paged kernel to handle smaller block_kv geometries, (b) slicing the megapatch's short-row decode top-k path as the official SM12x indexer decode route, or (c) a non-DeepGEMM fallback for 2-state pages. Happy to test patches on real hardware; we have a fully instrumented reproduction including per-shape operand dumps from live captures.

title: Revert "[Attention][Spec Decode] Support varlen trtllm-gen decode for adaptive verification (#52157)"
body:
## Summary

- Revert #52157 while its repeated B200 CUDA-graph regression is investigated.
- Restore the FlashInfer TRT-LLM decode path and its tests to the previously green main behavior.

## Why

Daily CI #85388 failed the same `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-deepgemm-mega-moe` GSM8K case twice while entering piecewise CUDA graph capture. The original run on `dgxb200-12` and the precise retry on `dgxb200-16` both hit the same PyTorch `CachingHostAllocator.h:815` internal assertion (`it->second->use_count > 0`). The exact B200 shard passed in nightly #85292 before #52157 merged, while the exact B200 gate was blocked and did not run in #52157's PR CI.

This is a containment revert so main can return to its previously validated path while the forward fix is developed.

## Duplicate check

- Searched open PRs for references to #52157; only unrelated follow-up #53036 was found.
- Searched open PRs for the B200 `CachingHostAllocator` / CUDA-graph signature; no existing revert or fix was found.

## Validation

- `git diff HEAD^ --check`
- `uvx pre-commit run --files tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_trtllm_attention.py vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py`
- Exact B200 MoE Refactor Integration targeted CI: [Buildkite #85394 shard 1](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/85394#01a035be-ce05-401a-86f3-350fbc1dc796) at commit `76909587` (all four selected shards running).

## Model evaluation impact

This restores the behavior that was on main before #52157. A local model evaluation is not practical because the reproducer is B200-specific; the exact DeepSeek-V4 GSM8K B200 gate is the required validation.

## AI assistance

This revert and incident evidence were prepared with AI assistance. The human submitter must review every changed line and the cited CI evidence before merge.

title: Revert "[Model Runner V2] Reserve CUDA graph memory (#53306)"
body:
## Why

Daily B200 MoE Refactor shard 1 failed `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-deepgemm-mega-moe` during the real breakable CUDA-graph capture with PyTorch:


title: [Bugfix] Honor default_proposal_method when selecting the speculators proposal method
body:
## Purpose

The speculators schema names the active proposal method via `default_proposal_method` — a required field with a pydantic membership validator, carried by published speculators checkpoints — but vLLM never reads it (`grep -rn default_proposal_method vllm/` → zero hits outside one test fixture) and always drafts with `proposal_methods[0]`.

This PR selects the proposal method by `default_proposal_method`, falling back to the first entry for configs that predate the field, and logs the non-selected methods via `logger.warning_once` instead of discarding them silently. Non-selected entries get shape checks only (a mapping naming its `proposal_type`): `speculative_tokens` belongs to concrete method types, not the base schema, so it is required only on the selected method.

**Behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged for every published checkpoint** — all carry a single proposal method, for which selection, validation outcome, and the resulting config are identical to today. (`configs/speculators/` is a source_file_dependency of the spec-decode E2E lanes; no acceptance-rate change is possible from this diff.)

## Why not duplicating an existing PR

`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "default_proposal_method"` → no PR implements this selection (2026-08-24). Adjacent open work: #44566 derives `num_speculative_tokens` from the draft config (same file, different field — happy to rebase over it if it lands first), #51338 infers the *algorithm* from checkpoint contents (different mechanism).

## Test Plan

`pytest tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_plural_proposal_methods.py tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_override.py tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_dspark_config.py` — 8 new tests including: selecting a non-first entry named by `default_proposal_method`, unmatched-default fallback with warning, non-selected entry without `speculative_tokens` tolerated, entry without `proposal_type` rejected, and single-method configs unchanged; plus both sibling suites for regression.

## Test Result

`17 passed`. ruff check/format: Passed · mypy-3.12 (hook-stage manual): Passed.

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used in preparing this change; the submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above.

title: [Spec Decode] Support PCP-sharded MTP prefill
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

Related RFC: #25749

Add single-module MTP support to the MRV2 PCP path while preserving PCP's long-prefill scaling:

- keep both the target prefill and the first MTP draft pass PCP-sharded
- restore target and draft outputs to global sequence order only at their sampling boundaries
- run later MTP proposal steps as replicated decode queries
- support pure prefill, replicated decode, mixed prefill/decode, and scheduled draft-token verification batches
- preserve GPU-materialized token positions after speculative rejection instead of rebuilding them from a potentially stale CPU cursor
- reuse the PCP manager's consumed rank-local input buffer and target hidden states for draft prefill, avoiding a doubled request buffer, metadata copies, and a redundant hidden-state all-gather
- scope rank-local state to the exact global batch so dummy/profile and stale batches use the ordinary global draft path
- distinguish PCP-expanded target slot mappings from ordinary replicated-draft mappings in sparse MLA
- disable MTP top-k index sharing under PCP and wait for proposal cache writes before a KV producer publishes the result
- account for PCP ranks in multi-node world-size and per-DP-rank placement
- reject unsupported multi-module MTP and CUDA-graph configurations during startup

This relies only on the PCP implementation already present on vLLM main and is independent of the fused PCP norm/RoPE work.

### Relationship to #53427

This is a materially different execution design from #53427. That PR keeps the target PCP-sharded but runs a fully replicated drafter on every PCP rank and currently excludes sparse MLA. This change shards the prompt-sized MTP draft pass across PCP ranks, supports the GLM-5.2 sparse-MLA path, and avoids repeating long-prefill draft compute and cache writes on every rank. It adopts the same GPU-cursor correctness principle for rank-local positions, but not the replicated-drafter architecture.

### Scope

- single-module MTP only; multi-module MTP and other speculative methods remain unsupported with PCP
- CUDA graphs must be disabled for PCP+MTP
- no model-routing change or new kernel

## Test Plan

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -m pytest -vv \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py
git diff --check
```

Before marking the PR ready, rerun an exact distributed PCP4/MTP3 GLM-5.2 model configuration on the rebased head.

## Test Result

- clean merge-tree against vLLM main at `7ca336929c169fee1210dd5293029d78811fba27`
- focused post-simplification tests: **24 passed, 2 CUDA-only tests skipped**
- commit-time checks passed, including Ruff, mypy, forbidden-import checks, configuration validation, SPDX, and sign-off
- Python syntax compilation and `git diff --check` passed
- pre-rebase CUDA validation: **21 focused tests passed**
- pre-rebase GLM-5.2 E2E validation used TP1/PCP8/EP8 with modular MTP5 on 8x B300, FP8 KV cache, an 8K batched-token limit, and a 4K long-prefill threshold:
  - restored decode and mixed spec/non-spec warmups completed
  - a 3,073-token prompt generated 32/32 requested tokens in the pure-decode probe
  - a sustained stream generated 128/128 requested tokens while two concurrent 3,073-token prefills each generated 8/8 requested tokens
  - the scheduler recorded a real mixed PCP batch with two fresh prefills and one decode; both node logs had zero errors
  - MTP metrics recorded 219 accepted draft tokens during the probe

The exact rebased and simplified head has not yet been rerun in a distributed PCP4/MTP3 model configuration, which is why this PR is being opened as a draft.

## AI assistance

Codex assisted with the rebase audit, design comparison, simplification, regression tests, and PR description. The submitter reviewed the resulting changes and validation evidence.

title: [PCP][Spec Decode] Consolidate MTP support and add DSpark groundwork
body:
## Purpose

Draft replacement for the stacked PCP/MTP approach in #53660 and the alternative implementation in #53653. This rebases the work directly onto `main`, keeps PCP-specific logic out of the autoregressive speculator, and adds the first replicated-drafter plumbing for DSpark.

The target attention metadata is already PCP-local. Rather than rebuilding it in `AutoRegressiveSpeculator`, `PCPManager` supplies a generic draft-prefill context containing the local inputs and a hidden-state restorer. The autoregressive path consumes that context without importing or branching on PCP.

The DSpark groundwork:

- builds DFlash/DSpark attention without PCP while retaining DCP;
- restores the target auxiliary hidden states needed by DSpark;
- gathers global block-table rows for the replicated drafter;
- sizes DSpark input buffers for every request's parallel query block;
- validates the supported PCP/DCP relationship.

`tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py` is intentionally unchanged from `main`; behavior coverage lives in the existing autoregressive and DSpark/DFlash suites.

## Relationship to existing work

- #53653: uses its PCP batch partitioning as the base, but replaces PCP branches in `autoregressive/speculator.py` with the generic `DraftPrefillContext` adapter.
- #53427: overlaps in end goal, but this draft explores a smaller autoregressive integration and builds on current-main PCP metadata.
- #53660: this PR no longer depends on it and is based directly on `main`.

This is a materially different consolidation of the existing drafts, not an additional independent implementation.

## Tests

Passing:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_cp_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py -q
# 47 passed

.venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-check --files <changed Python files>
# Passed

.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <changed vLLM files>
# Passed
```

## GPU validation status

Model: `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` with `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark`, 8 speculative tokens.

The requested TP4 + PCP4 + DCP4 topology requires 16 ranks, while the test host has 8 B300 GPUs. Scaled runs found:

- TP2 + PCP2 + DCP2 + EP4 reaches DSpark attention after the draft buffer and compatibility fixes, but GLM's current FlashMLA sparse target backend rejects TP2 DCP because its mixed-batch path requires fewer than 32 local heads.
- TP4 + PCP2 + DCP2 + EP8 satisfies that target constraint. With `fp8_ds_mla`, BF16 sliding-window draft KV, and `ag_rs`, current main then fails heterogeneous padded KV allocation (`Padded KV pages do not support kernel block splitting`) before generation.
- An older full token-sharded PCP+DCP implementation addresses this wider KV/indexer surface, but it does not apply cleanly to current main and regresses 12 focused tests. It is deliberately not included in this draft yet.

Accordingly, model evaluation is not claimed as passing. The PR remains draft until the composed PCP+DCP KV/indexer work is ported and the 8-GPU analogue completes; exact PCP4+DCP4 still needs a 16-GPU host.

## Checklist

- [x] Rebased directly onto current `main`
- [x] Removed PCP-specific branching from the autoregressive speculator
- [x] Focused unit tests, Ruff, and mypy pass
- [ ] Port current-main-compatible token-sharded PCP+DCP KV/indexer support
- [ ] Complete GLM-5.2-NVFP4 + DSpark TP4/PCP2/DCP2/EP8 evaluation
- [ ] Run exact TP4/PCP4/DCP4 evaluation on 16 GPUs
- [ ] Human submitter reviews every changed line before undrafting

AI assistance was used for implementation, debugging, and test execution. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing and defending the final change end-to-end before this PR leaves draft state.

title: [Bugfix] Fix DFlash vocabulary module initialization
body:
## Summary
- add config-driven ownership for DFlash input embeddings and LM heads
- support all four ownership combinations in the parent DFlash implementation
- leave target-owned vocabulary modules as `None`, avoiding their startup allocation
- preserve the original DFlash2 checkpoint behavior while keeping other legacy configs loader-safe

## Problem

Some DFlash checkpoints, including `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, omit both `embed_tokens` and `lm_head` because those modules are shared with the target model after loading.

DFlash nevertheless initialized both full-vocabulary modules eagerly. For the reference checkpoint, each allocation is approximately 2.37 GiB, causing an OOM on a 24 GB GPU before target/draft sharing can occur.

## Design

- `has_own_embed_tokens` and `has_own_lm_head` independently control construction in the shared DFlash parent.
- The original `DFlash2DraftModel` config predates these flags and defaults to sharing both modules.
- Other legacy DFlash/DSpark configs construct the modules eagerly. The standard loader can still infer ownership from checkpoint keys, while loaders that bypass `load_weights()` retain the safe eager modules.
- The existing proposer sharing path now safely handles a draft embedding that starts as `None`.
- No sentinel tensors, meta tensors, or generic loader hooks are introduced.

## Testing

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py \
  tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_override.py
# 39 passed
```

The ownership tests cover all four embedding / LM-head combinations for DFlash and DFlash2, the legacy DFlash2 fallback, legacy eager-loader behavior, and the proposer `None` sharing path. Ruff check and formatting pass for all changed Python files.

Implementation and tests were developed with AI assistance and manually reviewed and validated.

Fixes #53612

title: [RFC]: Decouple draft-model parallelism from the target model (PCP/DCP + speculative decoding)
body:
## Motivation

vLLM supports context parallelism for the target model (PCP, #25749, and DCP), but speculative decoding currently assumes the drafter uses the same parallel mapping as the target. Two in-flight PRs take different approaches to PCP + MTP:

- #53427 (@pisceskkk) keeps the target PCP-sharded but runs a fully replicated drafter on every PCP rank over the global batch. This is simple and works for any drafter with no PCP awareness, at the cost of repeating long-prefill draft compute and KV writes on every rank.
- #53653 (@GirasoleY) keeps the MTP draft prefill PCP-sharded, restoring global order only at sampling boundaries. This performs better on long prefills and supports the GLM-5.2 sparse-MLA path, but each speculative method needs its own PCP adaptation.

We probably want both eventually:

1. A drafter that hasn't implemented PCP/DCP (ngram, DSpark, EAGLE, suffix decoding, new methods) should still work when the target uses context parallelism, by consuming the global batch.
2. A drafter that has a sharded implementation (MTP today) should run sharded and skip the redundant compute.

The same question comes up for DCP: e.g. Kimi K3 (MLA, so DCP makes sense for the target) paired with a GQA draft model. There it probably makes sense to disable DCP for the draft model, since GQA already shards KV heads across TP and DCP would just add latency.

We already let the draft model diverge from the target config in some places: `draft_tensor_parallel_size` (draft TP=1 under target TP=N), and the per-draft `moe_backend` / `attention_backend` overrides in `SpeculativeConfig`. This RFC proposes generalizing that into a separate drafter parallel config so we don't accumulate ad-hoc per-method special cases in the model runner.

## Proposed Change

Give the draft model its own parallel config instead of implicitly inheriting the target's: `SpeculativeConfig` grows a `draft_parallel_config` (subsuming the existing `draft_tensor_parallel_size` field), where each parallelism size is initially restricted to 1 or the target's value. Defaults are per-method (e.g. MTP inherits the target's PCP size; methods without a sharded implementation default to 1) and can be overridden via `--speculative-config`. A drafter validates the config it is handed at startup and fails with a clear error if it can't execute it.

Note this does not mean different process groups or rank placement. The drafter still runs on the same ranks as the target; a draft size of 1 just means that group is treated as replication for the drafter, the same way draft TP=1 under target TP=N works today. No new distributed groups are needed.

## Alternatives considered

- Replicated-only (#53427 alone): simplest and works for every method, but gives up long-prefill draft perf and scales draft KV memory with CP size.
- Sharded-only (#53653 alone): best perf where implemented, but every drafter has to be individually adapted to PCP before it works at all, so new and niche speculative methods would silently lose CP support.
- Arbitrary drafter parallelism (any TP/CP/EP per draft model with its own process groups and rank placement): much bigger change to distributed init and scheduling, and nothing on the table needs it. The proposed config keeps the drafter on the target's ranks and restricts each size to 1 or the target's value, and we can relax this later if a use case shows up.

## Open questions

1. CUDA graph support: #53427 validates PIECEWISE (with #53515); #53653 currently requires eager. What do we commit to for each path, and should supported graph modes depend on the drafter parallel config?
2. Should the global-vs-sharded choice ever be dynamic (e.g. global for short-prefill batches, sharded for long), or is a static per-run choice enough?
3. Sparse-MLA indexer: #53653 distinguishes PCP-expanded target slot mappings from replicated-draft mappings. Does that distinction belong in the attention backend interface or the PCP manager?
4. Does the scheduler need to know the drafter's effective CP degree for token budgeting, or can this stay contained in the runner?

## Feedback Period

~2 weeks.

## CC

@pisceskkk @GirasoleY @LucasWilkinson

## Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues and PRs (#25749, #53427, #53653, #53515).
