title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash — ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoints emit invalid UTF-8 byte tokens on SM120, while a compressed-tensors NVFP4 of the same model is clean
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```text
GPUs:     4x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GiB, SM120), PCIe, no NVLink
Image:    cstechdev/vllm:glm53-flash-nope-sm120-cu130-20260826-r1
          (a NoPE sparse-MLA overlay on vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash;
           github.com/chriswritescode-dev/glm-5.3-flash-sm120)
vLLM:     0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187
Model:    GLM-5.3-Flash (glm5_next), TP4
KV:       fp8_ds_mla (the only layout the SM120 sparse-MLA impl accepts)
MoE:      --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"marlin","enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}'
Other:    MTP off, --block-size auto (lands on 1792), --enable-prefix-caching
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Two ModelOpt-produced NVFP4 conversions of GLM-5.3-Flash emit **invalid UTF-8 byte-token
sequences** during generation on SM120. A compressed-tensors NVFP4 conversion of the *same*
model, served from the same image with the same kernel, KV layout, parallelism and sampling
settings, is clean. Only the checkpoint changes between these rows.

The failure is quiet: the server returns HTTP 200, throughput looks normal, English text is
mostly fine, and short prompts read correctly. It shows up as U+FFFD inside multi-byte
(here: Korean) text, which is easy to mistake for a rendering or client problem.

#### Result

Six generations per row — 3 at `temperature=0.0`, 3 at `0.7`, identical Korean prompt,
`max_tokens=4096`. The count is U+FFFD characters across `content` + `reasoning`.

| checkpoint | quant format | U+FFFD / 6 runs | degenerate loops |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `LibertAIDAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` | modelopt NVFP4 | **86** | 0/6 |
| `LibertAIDAI/...` @ rev `cf5434c00b` (43-entry ignore list) | modelopt NVFP4 | **62** | 1/6 |
| `dealignai/GLM-5.3-Flash-UNCENSORED-NVFP4` | modelopt NVFP4 | **94** | 0/6 |
| `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` | compressed-tensors NVFP4 | **0** | 0/6 |

Sample from a `temperature=0` generation on the LibertAI checkpoint — `퍼셉트론`
(“perceptron”) loses its middle syllable:

```
프랭크 로젠블랫(Frank Rosenblatt)의 퍼<?>트론(Perceptron, 1957)
```

#### This is not a detokenizer artifact

Requesting `return_token_ids: true` and decoding the returned ids offline with the
checkpoint's own tokenizer reproduces the same U+FFFD count as the API text (5 and 5 on the
sampled request), so the emitted token ids themselves do not form valid UTF-8. Byte-token
continuations are near-deterministic, so producing an invalid continuation under greedy
decoding points at the logits rather than at decoding.

#### Ruled out

Each of these was varied independently with everything else held fixed:

- **Context length** — a Korean prompt answered correctly at 62, 25 772, 103 040, 412 112 and
  1 030 162 prompt tokens, with both Korean and English filler. Corruption appears at
  **zero context** too, so it is not the sparse-MLA/long-context path.
- **Sampling** — present at `temperature=0.0`.
- **MTP** — `num_speculative_tokens` 5 and 0 behave the same.
- **PDL** — patching `CudaPlatformBase.is_arch_support_pdl` to exclude SM12x changes nothing.
- **Abliteration** — the guardrail-removed `dealignai` build and its un-abliterated
  `LibertAIDAI` sibling score the same (94 vs 86).
- **`quantization_config.ignore` completeness** — our LibertAI copy predated commit
  `cf5434c00b`, which grew the ignore list from 32 to 43 entries (fused attention
  projections, `q/k/v/qkv_conv1d`, `o_norm`, `visual.*`). Updating `config.json` to that
  revision — weights untouched — left corruption in place (86 → 62, within the run-to-run
  spread of 7–22 per generation).

#### Open question

The two checkpoint families differ in **loader path**, not only in file format: modelopt vs
compressed-tensors. So this data cannot distinguish

- (A) the two ModelOpt conversions carry damaged weights, from
- (B) vLLM's ModelOpt NVFP4 path is wrong here while the compressed-tensors NVFP4 path is
  correct.

If (B), every ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint is affected, not just this model. Someone able to
compare the two loaders' dequantized weights for the same tensor would settle it quickly;
we do not have a reference to diff against.

#### Side observation: NvFp4 MoE backend availability on SM120

While isolating the above, with the checkpoint held fixed:

| `moe_backend` | result on SM120 |
|---|---|
| `flashinfer_trtllm` | rejected — `kernel does not support current device cuda` |
| `flashinfer_cutedsl` | rejected — same |
| `flashinfer_cutlass` | **6/6 runs collapse into a repeated single token** (`locklocklock…`) |
| `cutlass` (VLLM_CUTLASS) | **6/6 collapse**, no `content` produced at all |
| `emulation` | collapses — 49 129 chars of `</arg_value>` repeats, 0 % Hangul |
| `marlin` | the only usable path |

The two CUTLASS failures line up with sgl-project/sglang#18954 (“NVFP4 models produce NaN
outputs on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120)”), which was closed on the FlashInfer side; this is
the same symptom reached through vLLM, and it reproduces on vLLM's own CUTLASS path as well.
That `emulation` also collapses is the part we cannot explain — a dequantizing reference path
should be the safe fallback.

#### Reproduction

```bash
docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host --shm-size 32g -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /data/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4:/model:ro \
  cstechdev/vllm:glm53-flash-nope-sm120-cu130-20260826-r1 /model \
  --served-model-name GLM-5.3-Flash --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-model-len 131072 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"marlin","enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' \
  --enable-prefix-caching --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45
```

Then ask for a long answer in a language with multi-byte characters and count U+FFFD:

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model":"GLM-5.3-Flash","temperature":0,"max_tokens":4096,
  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"인공지능의 역사를 1950년대부터 현재까지 시대별로 나누어 한국어로 자세히 설명해 주세요."}]
}' | python3 -c 'import json,sys; m=json.load(sys.stdin)["choices"][0]["message"]; t=(m.get("content") or "")+(m.get("reasoning") or ""); print("U+FFFD:", t.count("�"))'
```

Swapping `/model` to `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` with everything else identical returns 0.

title: [Kimi-K3] AG-GEMM for Sequence Parallelism
body:
## Purpose This PR implements overlapping AG-GEMM with CUDA streams pipelining: compute local shard while sending the local activation shard to neighboring remote rank, and continue the rotation until all shards are computed. No custom kernel required, and technically we can adapt to any quantization kernels in the future. Implementation details - Inter-GPU transfer is done in push mode using `cuMemcpyDtoDAsync` -> CopyEngine-based, no SM usage. Hence, this only requires P2P, no multicast is needed. - Synchronization is done via PyTorch's built-in `handle.put_signal(next_rank, channel=channel)` and `handle.wait_signal(previous_rank, channel=step)`. - We purposely **don't** have a cross-rank exit barrier, which is meant to prevent next invocation overrides recv buffers that previous GEMM might not have finished. Instead, we rely on the fact that there will be another collective between 2 consecutive AG-GEMM invocations acting as an implicit barrier. - For data push, we don't issue all push at once in the beginning. Instead, we only push to the receiver of the current round, and wait for the expected incoming data to arrive before pushing to the next receiver. In microbenchmarks, this design seems to be a bit faster, likely because we avoid transport contention. ### vLLM integration The AG-GEMM logic alone is very straight forward: `ag_gemm.py` only has 150 LOC. The rest of the changes target some refactoring of SP collective ownership and initialization logic. - KDA/MLA/MLP now owns SP collectives, regardless of whether the fused AG-GEMM/GEMM-RS are activated. This is more natural as the fusion boundary is within the same module, not leaking outside to `DecoderLayer`. When fused AG-GEMM and GEMM-RS are not used (either because it's not supported or disabled), KDA/MLA/MLP modules are now responsible to invoke the unfused AG/RS collectives. - For Kimi-Linear, DecoderLayer still executes SP collectives - GEMM-RS is also enabled by default now. Previously I left it off by default in #52079 because I don't know a reliable way to determine whether multicast memory is available. However, the check is actually quite simple: see if `multicast_ptr` is not None #53053 (thanks @wzhao18) - This PR also separate GEMM-RS and GEMM-AR. Previously #53053 combines them together since they share the same kernel code. However, separating them (i.e. initialization logic, dispatch logic) improves readability and logical flow: `use_sequence_parallel` now implies AG-GEMM and GEMM-RS, while `run_gemm_ar` controls GEMM-AR only - In the future, we may want to integrate GEMM-AR directly into `RowParallelLinear` so all models can benefit from it, and we don't need manual dispatch for each model. ## Microbenchmark title: [Hy4] support Hy4-preview model
body:
## Purpose

# Hy4 preview Usage Guide

  Hy4 preview is Tencent Hy's new-generation open-source Mixture-of-Experts language
  model. Its backbone has 770B total parameters with 49B activated per token across
  78 layers. The first layer uses a dense FFN; the other 77 layers use 256 routed
  experts (top-8) and 1 shared expert. A native MTP layer adds 10B total parameters
  (0.7B activated) for speculative decoding.

  On the architecture side, inspired by DeepSeek and GLM, the attention module employs Gated DeepSeek Sparse Attention (Gated DSA) with IndexCache for cross-layer sparse index reuse. The residual pathway uses iHC (identity Hyper-Connections) to expand inter-layer information flow.

  ## vLLM Setup

  Choose one of the following setup methods.

  ### Using Docker

  ```bash
  docker run --gpus all \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    --ipc=host \
    -e VLLM_ENABLE_HPC_OPS=1 \
    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
    vllm/vllm-openai:hy4-preview tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8 \
      --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
      --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":3,"method":"mtp"}' \
      --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE \
      --tool-call-parser hy_v4 \
      --reasoning-parser hy_v4 \
      --enable-auto-tool-choice \
      --port 8000 \
      --served-model-name hy4-preview
  ```

  Build vLLM from source:

  ```bash
  uv venv --python 3.12 --seed --managed-python
  source .venv/bin/activate
  git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git
  cd vllm
  uv pip install --editable . --torch-backend=auto
  ```

  ## vLLM Deployment

  Start the FP8 model with MTP enabled:

  ```bash
  export VLLM_ENABLE_HPC_OPS=1

  vllm serve tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":3,"method":"mtp"}' \
    --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE \
    --tool-call-parser hy_v4 \
    --reasoning-parser hy_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name hy4-preview
  ```

  ## OpenAI Client Example

  Tencent recommends `temperature=0.9` and `top_p=1.0`. Reasoning defaults to
  `high`, which is suitable for math, coding, and other complex tasks.

  ```python
  from openai import OpenAI

  client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")

  response = client.chat.completions.create(
      model="hy4-preview",
      messages=[
          {"role": "user", "content": "Hello! Can you briefly introduce yourself?"},
      ],
      temperature=0.9,
      top_p=1.0,
  )
  output_msg = response.choices[0].message
  print(output_msg.reasoning_content)  # chain-of-thought
  print(output_msg.content)             # final answer
  ```

  For a direct response without deep reasoning, pass `reasoning_effort="no_think"`:

  ```python
  response = client.chat.completions.create(
      model="hy4-preview",
      messages=[
          {"role": "user", "content": "Hello! Can you briefly introduce yourself?"},
      ],
      temperature=0.9,
      top_p=1.0,
      extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"reasoning_effort": "no_think"}},
  )
  print(response.choices[0].message.content)
  ```

  ### cURL Usage

  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
      "model": "hy4-preview",
      "messages": [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Hello! Can you briefly introduce yourself?"}
      ],
      "temperature": 0.9,
      "top_p": 1.0
    }'
  ```

  ## References

  - [Hugging Face: Hy4 preview](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4-preview)
  - [Hugging Face: Hy4 preview-FP8](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8)
  - [ModelScope: Hy4 preview](https://modelscope.cn/models/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy4-preview)
  - [GitHub: Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy4-preview](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy4-preview)
  - [GitCode: Hy4 preview](https://ai.gitcode.com/tencent_hunyuan/Hy4-preview)
  - [CNB: Hy4 preview](https://cnb.cool/ai-models/tencent/Hy4-preview)
  - [AngelSlim quantization toolkit](https://github.com/tencent/AngelSlim)


## Test Plan

## Test Result

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] DFlash/DSpark no longer drop the last prefix-cache block (mamba align context recompute)
body:
# PR: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] DFlash/DSpark no longer drop the last prefix-cache block (mamba align context recompute)

**Fixes**: #53477

## Summary

`SpeculativeConfig.use_eagle()` is a stand-in for "spec decode that reads target
hidden states" and returns `True` for `dflash`/`dspark` too. The scheduler used it
(via #53388's `use_eagle_block_drop()`) to back `last_cache_position` off by one
mamba block. But only **eagle-family** drafters (eagle/eagle3/mtp) actually pollute
the target's last matching full-attention block with the lookahead KV write;
**DFlash/DSpark draft via block diffusion from their own KV cache and never write
target blocks**. The spurious back-off made every prompt shorter than two mamba
blocks skip the final block-aligned chunk, so the mamba recurrent state never
materialized on a block boundary and the next turn's fixed-point prefix-cache
lookup converged to 0 → **the whole context was recomputed on every reply**.

## Root Cause

`SpeculativeConfig.use_eagle()` and the `use_eagle_block_drop()` built on it in
#53388 are stand-ins for "speculative decoding using target model hidden states":

```python
def use_eagle(self) -> bool:
    return self.method in ("eagle", "eagle3", "mtp", "dflash", "dspark")

def use_eagle_block_drop(self) -> bool:
    return self.use_eagle() and not self.disable_eagle_block_drop
```

Consequence chain for a prompt shorter than `2 * block_size` (block = mamba block,
e.g. 560 on Qwen3.5-4B, larger on 27B class models):

1. `last_cache_position == 0` → the whole prompt is one chunk whose end is **not**
   block-aligned.
2. Mamba "align" mode only materializes reusable recurrent state at block-aligned
   chunk ends; the prompt-tail state is advanced by decode steps but its running
   block is later nulled out (`remove_skipped_blocks`), so its hash is never
   published to the prefix cache.
3. The next request's `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit()` fixed
   point pulls the hit length to 0 → full context recompute every turn.

MTP (an eagle-family drafter) was also slightly affected, but the symptom was
masked because the reporter's comparison was "DFlash2 reprocesses vs MTP works".

## Changes

- `vllm/config/speculative.py`
  - Add `use_eagle_preserves_target_kv_cache()` → `method in ("eagle", "eagle3", "mtp")`,
    in the same style as the existing `use_multi_module_mtp()`. This is the precise
    capability bit for "the drafter shares (and pollutes) the target's KV cache
    groups".
  - Redefine `use_eagle_block_drop()` (introduced in #53388) to compose with that
    bit: `use_eagle_preserves_target_kv_cache() and not disable_eagle_block_drop`.
    #53388's opt-out flag still applies to the eagle family; DFlash/DSpark no
    longer drop the trailing block by default.
- `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`
  - No new attribute: the existing `use_eagle_block_drop` wiring (split back-off +
    `KVCacheManager(use_eagle=...)` and the offloading/mooncake call sites) now
    receives the precise value through the redefined method.
  - The "block dropping is disabled" warning is gated on eagle-family drafters
    only, so DFlash/DSpark do not log a misleading warning.
- `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py`
  - New regression test `test_dflash_does_not_back_off_last_cache_position`.
- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`
  - `test_mamba_align_eagle_schedules_encoder_at_boundary` sets the
    `use_eagle_block_drop` attribute.

No behavioral change for `eagle`/`eagle3`/`mtp`/`draft_model`/`ngram` paths
beyond #53388's flag semantics: `use_eagle()` (encoder shift, lookahead budget,
`num_prefill_lookahead`) is untouched; only the prefix-cache last-block drop is
scoped precisely.

## Test commands and results

Local reproduction (2×L40S, vLLM 0.26.0 layout, Qwen3.5-4B hybrid +
Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash draft, 3-turn conversation with a shared 30x system prefix):

| Configuration | Before fix | After fix |
|---|---|---|
| DFlash + mamba align | `cached=[0, 0, 0]` (full recompute every turn) | `[0, 560, 560]` |
| DFlash + mamba all | `[0, 0, 0]` | `[0, 560, 560]` |
| no spec + align/all | `[0, 1056, 1136]` | unchanged |
| MTP + align (regression) | no regression observed | no regression observed |

```bash
# CPU unit tests (no GPU needed)
python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py -q

# Existing scheduler tests (no regression)
python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q -k "mamba_align"
```

Independent validations since opening:

- dtandersen: Intel Arc B70, Qwen3.8-27B-INT4 + DFlash2 — token corruption with
  prefix cache resolved.
- vedcsolution: 4×DGX Spark GB10 (TP4), GLM-5.3-Flash + DFlash2 — identical-request
  prefix hits 0/12,552 → 4,608, TTFT 3.9s → 1.55s; capability bit also fixed an
  extra over-truncation on KDA groups (69-scenario tool-call suite 89 → 91).
- positive666 closed #54041 as superseded by this PR after validating both approaches.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

No open PR addresses #53477. Related work: #53388 (merged the
`disable_eagle_block_drop` switch; this PR makes the drop precise instead of
requiring the flag for DFlash/DSpark), #30877 (align prefix caching, which
introduced the `use_eagle` back-off), #42971, #44082 — none touch the
DFlash/DSpark misclassification.

## AI assistance disclosure

This fix was developed with AI assistance (static analysis, reproduction scripts,
test generation). All changes were reviewed and verified by a human.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Restore hybrid mamba align cache hits under spec decode with a KV connector (related to #53505)
body:
# PR: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Restore hybrid mamba align cache hits under spec decode with a KV connector (related to #53505)

**Related**: #53505 (scoped as related — see Scope below)

## Summary

Fix three deterministic defects on the spec-decode + hybrid-mamba + KV-connector
path. Two of them misclassify DFlash/DSpark as eagle-family drafters and corrupt
or degrade the mamba align prefix cache; the third hard-crashes the EngineCore
when a finer `prefix_match_unit` meets a sliding-window draft group.

Local reproduction uses the native `kv_offloading_size` OffloadingConnector (no
LMCacheMP server was available): output is clean before and after, and the
change restores the expected prefix-cache hits (`[0, 560, 560]`). It does not
reproduce the reporter's retrieve-ON LMCache corruption cell, so this PR is
declared **related to** #53505 rather than a full fix of that issue.

## Stack

This PR stacks on #54163 (commit `e1b29d5`). The shared capability-bit change
(`use_eagle_preserves_target_kv_cache()` and the scheduler/KV-cache-manager
wiring) is reviewed once in #54163; once that PR merges, the diff here shrinks
to the delta below (offloading fallback + sliding-window tolerance + regression
test).

## Root Causes

### 1. DFlash/DSpark get the EAGLE last-block drop (primary corruption source)

Same root cause as #53477: `use_eagle()` returns `True` for `dflash`/`dspark`,
so `_mamba_block_aligned_split()` backs `last_cache_position` off by one mamba
block. Prompts shorter than two mamba blocks never materialize a block-aligned
recurrent state; the next lookup converges to 0 and decode resumes from a wrong
boundary. With a connector attached, its `update_state_after_alloc` /
`build_connector_meta` bookkeeping and mamba partial-tail CoW paths amplify the
bad boundary into corrupted decode (the issue reporter's U+FFFD garbage /
runaway turns).

Fix: introduce `SpeculativeConfig.use_eagle_preserves_target_kv_cache()`
(`eagle/eagle3/mtp` only) and use it in the scheduler split + the KV cache
manager's `use_eagle` argument (see #53477 PR for the full chain).

### 2. Offloading connector marks every KV group as eagle under DFlash

`SchedulerOffloadConfig.from_spec()` fell back to

```python
use_eagle = (spec_config is not None and spec_config.use_eagle())
if use_eagle and not eagle_groups:
    eagle_groups = set(range(len(kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups)))
```

Under DFlash/DSpark this flags **all 38 groups — including the target's mamba
group — as volatile eagle groups**, so `storable_chunks()` excludes the trailing
chunk of every decode step from offloading and the store/lookup windows drift.
This matches the reporter's H12 instrumentation showing off-by-window store
ranges even with retrieval disabled.

Fix: use the precise capability bit here too, so only eagle-family drafters get
the fallback.

### 3. SlidingWindowManager assert-crashes on a finer prefix_match_unit

With a hybrid mamba target configured with `prefix_match_unit` finer than the
mamba block size, the coordinator's `alignment_tokens` becomes finer than the
draft model's sliding-window group block size, and
`SlidingWindowManager.find_longest_cache_hit()` hit:

```python
assert alignment_tokens % kv_cache_spec.block_size == 0
# 16 % 560 -> EngineDeadError, killing all in-flight requests
```

Fix: fall back to block-aligned hits for that group instead of crashing.
(Verified crash before fix, clean hit after fix.)

Reachability note: on current main the core coordinator guard (#51843) already
disables fine-grained hits when an incompatible sliding-window manager is
present, so this assert is not reachable on the native path; the fallback is
kept as defense-in-depth. The Mooncake store-side
`partial_hash_hits_enabled()` mirror does not include the same
unsupported-manager exclusion — a coordinator-level regression with real
fine-grained hashes is left for a separate follow-up.

## Scope / not covered

The reporter's corruption repro needs a running LMCacheMP server with retrieval
enabled and long (40 min) agent sessions; this PR restores cache hits under the
native OffloadingConnector path but does **not** reproduce or claim to close
the retrieve-ON LMCache corruption cell. The remaining suspect is the `assert
RequestStatus.is_finished(req.status)` in `_update_from_kv_xfer_finished`
(crashes the engine on a retrieve that finished after the request was dropped) —
kept out of this PR for a separate fix.

## Changes

- `vllm/config/speculative.py` — add `use_eagle_preserves_target_kv_cache()`.
- `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` — precise `drop_last_prefix_cache_block`;
  pass it as `KVCacheManager(use_eagle=...)`.
- `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py` —
  eagle-group fallback uses the precise capability bit.
- `vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` — SWA group falls back to
  block-aligned hits when the coordinator alignment is finer than its block size.
- `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py` — two new regression tests
  (`test_dflash_does_not_back_off_last_cache_position`,
  `test_sliding_window_group_tolerates_finer_alignment`); stub updates.
- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` — attribute update for the eagle encoder test.

## Test commands and results

Local reproduction (2×L40S, vLLM 0.26.0 layout, Qwen3.5-4B hybrid +
Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash draft, native `kv_offloading_size` connector):

| Configuration | Before fix | After fix |
|---|---|---|
| DFlash + align + offload 0/1/4 GB | clean, but boundary wrong | clean, hits restored `[0,560,560]` |
| DFlash + align + `prefix_match_unit=16` | **EngineDeadError (assert)** | hits `[0,560,560]` |
| 4 concurrent interleaved sessions + offload | clean | clean, identical output |

```bash
# CPU unit tests
python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py -q
python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q -k "mamba_align"
```

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

No open PR targets #53505. Overlapping/related work that touches the same files
or semantics and will need reconciliation:

- #54163 — this PR's stack base (the focused #53477 fix; same capability bit).
- #53479 — the same speculative back-off plus retained-boundary handling.
- #52771 — the same native-offloading fallback in `offloading/scheduler.py`
  under a different policy.
- #54076 — the splitter's mamba-group block-size source.
- #54041 — explicit DFlash draft-group annotation (closed).

Happy to reconcile or drop parts where the maintainer PRs cover the semantics.

## AI assistance disclosure

This fix was developed with AI assistance (static analysis, reproduction scripts,
test generation). All changes were reviewed and verified by a human.

title: [Feature][Spec Decode] Support sampling mask replay for MRV2 MTP
body:
## Summary

This updates sampling-mask replay for fixed-boundary MTP speculative decoding on
top of the compact sampling-mask implementation merged in #54901. It is not a
duplicate of #54901: that PR introduced ordinary compact masks, while this PR
adds emitted-token-aligned MTP replay and its validation.

The final head is `d121ee5513dbdbfda190ef7ee32fb5a0ba174a2e`, based on frozen
upstream `main` at `6fbb00b18874e27ba7d7adc0a3b8e93fee763ab1`. I did not
rebase solely to chase unrelated upstream commits. The final series is one
signed commit touching 13 files (`+601/-66`).

## Scope and design

- Reuse #54901's ordinary compact token-ID representation and exact packed
  bitmask fallback; do not introduce a second ordinary sampling-mask path.
- Preserve the ordinary single-row fast path and upstream generic
  batch-sharded-sampling validation.
- Extend the compact representation with fixed request-major MTP rows and
  explicit cumulative row boundaries.
- Skip the vocabulary loop entirely for inactive Triton programs after writing
  a zero count. Active-row token IDs, packed masks, and counts are unchanged.
- Package one processed target-logit support for each possible committed
  position in a fixed MTP verification chunk, then route exactly one support for
  every emitted accepted, recovered, or bonus token.
- Flatten chunk-local supports in output processing so completion output remains
  aligned one-to-one with emitted token IDs.
- Preserve upstream `AsyncOutput` construction before
  `postprocess_sampled()` and `speculator.propose()`. The complete output D2H,
  including replay masks, can therefore overlap proposal. There is no
  mask-specific deferred state, second production event, late mutation, helper,
  or delayed-output branch.
- Enable replay only for standard rejection sampling with fixed-boundary MTP.
  Adaptive verification, non-MTP draft methods, synthetic/block verification,
  diffusion/custom samplers, logprob-incompatible modes, and MRV2-incompatible
  modes remain rejected.

## AsyncOutput ordering audit and isolated A/B

The static data-flow audit found no dependency requiring delayed D2H:

- `Sampler.sample()` and `RejectionSampler._verify_in_chunks()` finish
  constructing replay masks on the main stream before `GPUModelRunner.sample()`
  returns.
- `AsyncOutput` enters its copy stream and calls
  `copy_stream.wait_stream(main_stream)`, ordering every copy after the mask
  packing already enqueued at its construction point.
- `AsyncOutput` retains the sampler output and source GPU tensor references
  until copy completion.
- `postprocess_sampled()` updates request/model state and
  `speculator.propose()` consumes sampling state and token/hidden-state inputs;
  neither receives or mutates the sampling-mask buffers.
- Previously observed TP2 rank-local LM-head drift occurs before mask packing
  and is not D2H/collective-conflict evidence.

I then compared OVERLAPPED against the DELAYED arm of this PR; this is not a
comparison against upstream or replay-off and does not claim a general
throughput gain. The worktrees' tracked source was byte-identical except for
`AsyncOutput` timing. Both used local Qwen3.5-9B, MTP K=3, temperature 0.8,
top-k 5, top-p 0.9, identical per-request seeds and prompts, and replay enabled.
The balanced order used 6 complete warm-ups and 10 measured full-workload pairs
at both c16 and c64 (20 independent pairs total). Bootstrap intervals use
50,000 paired resamples, pairing by shape and run ID.

Throughput is 1,024 completed output tokens divided by full-workload elapsed
time. Each run's mean engine-step latency is elapsed time divided by its actual
engine-step count (41 at c16, 11 at c64); the reported p95 is the nearest-rank
p95 across the 10 independent run means, which is the maximum with n=10.

| Shape | DELAYED median tok/s | OVERLAPPED median tok/s | Throughput delta (paired 95% CI) | DELAYED p95 run-mean step ms | OVERLAPPED p95 run-mean step ms | Step delta (paired 95% CI) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| c16 | 407.053 | 430.433 | +5.744% [+4.779%, +6.985%] | 62.449 | 59.135 | -5.306% [-6.240%, -4.230%] |
| c64 | 934.106 | 1035.080 | +10.810% [+9.430%, +12.073%] | 100.728 | 95.814 | -4.879% [-9.751%, -4.435%] |

The throughput runs carried no diagnostic instrumentation. CUDA event data came
from a separate run in detached diagnostic worktrees and is shown below.

<details>
<summary>Separate CUDA event diagnostics</summary>

| Shape | Proposal median ms D/O | Full output-copy median ms D/O | Copy completion relative to proposal end ms D/O | Median overlap ms D/O | Steps with overlap D/O |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| c16 | 5.658 / 5.650 | 0.096 / 0.097 | +0.109 / -5.577 | 0.000 / 0.072 | 0/490 / 488/490 |
| c64 | 5.841 / 5.833 | 0.161 / 0.162 | +0.180 / -5.706 | 0.000 / 0.129 | 0/190 / 189/190 |

Here, a negative copy-completion value means D2H completed before proposal
ended.

</details>

The isolated correctness gates passed for both arms, and neither c16 nor c64 has
a credible regression over 2%, so the final design is OVERLAPPED.

## TP2 nondeterminism boundary and exact oracle

The original TP2 cross-engine result is baseline-nondeterministic, so it is not
presented as replay-off/on exact evidence:

- Every fresh engine received its own identical, unmeasured 32-request x
  16-token warm-up covering the measured shape, prefill, decode, top-k/top-p,
  causal-conv, and Triton GDN paths.
- Five identical workloads in one initialized replay-off engine were not all
  exact (three distinct output digests). A fresh replay-off A/B pair had zero
  token mismatches but nine selected processed-logprob mismatches; this is not
  treated as a correctness pass.
- Detached instrumentation located all nine recurring first differences in
  rank-local LM-head logits before the TP collective, logits processing,
  rejection sampling, mask packing, and output D2H.
- Qwen3.5's selected GDN backend does not opt into
  `supports_batch_invariance`, so `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` was not enabled or
  bypassed.

Exact replay correctness instead uses a real TP2 production-call-path oracle.
From a measured MTP rejection call, it captured complete processed target
logits, draft tokens/probabilities, request boundaries, accepted-count inputs,
effective stateless RNG seeds/positions, and CUDA device generator state/offset.
With device RNG state restored before each replay-off/on arm, all 5/5
repetitions were exact for sampled token IDs, selected processed-logprobs and
ranks, accepted/recovered/bonus decisions, counts, post-call RNG state/offset,
and processed inputs. Input mutation, mask membership, row alignment, support
alignment, and exact probability-reconstruction failures were all zero.

## Final validation

All review-revision gates used the two isolated source arms derived from remote
head `f590870478adf4b895e56eb1361c2bb11c2b1449`. The local amended commit
contains the passing OVERLAPPED arm.

- Required focused suite: 30 passed per arm (60 executions total): 13 config,
  8 output/mask, 2 scheduler, 1 output-processor, and 6 GPU rejection/chunking
  tests. The inactive-row early return compiled and ran through the Triton mask
  tests in both arms.
- TP1 replay-off/on per arm, Qwen3.5-9B, K=3, 32 x 16: zero token or selected
  processed-logprob differences; zero mask membership/alignment failures;
  acceptance metrics exact (mean acceptance length 2.2278481013, draft
  acceptance rate 0.4092827004).
- TP2 replay-on per arm, Qwen3.5-9B, K=3, 32 x 16 after a complete identical
  warm-up: 512 output rows; zero membership, row-alignment, or support-alignment
  failures; captured-input oracle exact 5/5. There was no hang, timeout, NCCL
  collective sequence divergence, or rank-ordering failure.
- dFlash replay-off, Qwen3-8B with 16-token draft, 24 x 16: masks absent and
  DELAYED/OVERLAPPED token IDs, selected processed-logprobs, and acceptance
  metrics exact.
- dSpark replay-off, Qwen3-4B with block7 draft, 24 x 16: masks absent and
  DELAYED/OVERLAPPED token IDs, selected processed-logprobs, and acceptance
  metrics exact.
- `.venv/bin/python -m compileall`, `git diff --check`, every changed-file
  pre-commit hook, and
  `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual` passed.
- DCO: one commit; author, committer, and the single `Signed-off-by` trailer
  are `Cuiping Cheng <chengcuipingswu@163.com>`.

The host exposed 8 NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB GPUs. Formal A/B used two persistent
workers on host GPU 0 (UUID `GPU-1714bc68-6be5-ad06-8969-674ddc0dd73e`);
`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` mapped that device to `cuda:0` in each worker. TP1
used one GPU per run (host GPU 1 mapped to process-local `cuda:0`). TP2 used
two GPUs per run: `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3` mapped host GPUs 2 and 3 to TP
ranks' process-local `cuda:0` and `cuda:1`. Replay-off dFlash used host GPUs
0/1 for DELAYED/OVERLAPPED, and dSpark used host GPUs 4/5.

GPU validation used PyTorch `2.13.0+cu129`, CUDA 12.9, and Triton 3.7.1. The
Codex inner sandbox masked devices, so GPU commands ran in the existing
GPU-visible host context after repeating the device checks; no environment
reinstall or model download was performed.

## AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex assisted with upstream-diff analysis, semantic migration, test
development, static ordering audit, isolated performance/ordering diagnostics,
and validation orchestration. I reviewed and understand the final changes and
take responsibility for them.

title: [Kimi-K3][Kernel] Optimize the low-M fused latent MoE tail
body:
## Summary

This PR reduces the SM100 Kimi-K3 latent-MoE decode tail latency for low token counts while preserving the existing operator structure. Deferred BF16 top-16 finalization, routed AllReduce, RMSNorm, and shared-expert ReduceScatter remain fused in one CuTe DSL collective kernel; the following rank-sharded up-projection and Lamport consumer are made cheaper and are launched earlier with PDL.

The production path remains valid for `M <= 16` (and the existing larger capacities). The most aggressive static SIMT up-projection is deliberately limited to `M <= 5`; measurements show that the dynamic WGMMA path wins again from `M=6` onward.

## Optimization details

### 1. Specialize BF16 top-16 finalization inside the fused collective

The Kimi-K3 route contract on current `main` is BF16 top-16. The specialized path assigns one 16-byte latent fragment to each thread and uses inline PTX to:

- load all 16 route indices and 16 BF16 route weights with wide vector loads;
- predicate invalid/dropped routes before gathering their GEMM2 fragments;
- accumulate weighted BF16 inputs directly into eight FP32 registers with `fma.rn.f32.bf16`;
- round to packed BF16 once, immediately before NVLS publication.

This removes scalar metadata traffic and compiler-generated BF16-to-FP32 conversion sequences from the hot loop. FP32 is used for arithmetic accumulation, not for the communication buffers: multicast, Lamport storage, and the collective's configured internal wire format remain BF16 (`fp32_internal=False`).

### 2. Compact the fused collective's low-M launch

For the TP8 Kimi-K3 shape (`latent=3584`, `hidden=7168`), `M=1..4` now uses a seven-CTA cluster with 64 threads per CTA and exact one-cluster-per-token ownership. `M=1` gets its own specialization; `M=2..4` share the four-token specialization. The shared ReduceScatter uses one compact role instead of launching redundant destination roles.

The routed and shared roles call `griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()` immediately after publishing the data required by the successor. This lets the up-projection grid become resident while the collective completes its remaining reduction, normalization, flag rotation, and cleanup. The general schedule is retained for `M >= 5`, including multi-wave Lamport generation handling.

### 3. Use a one-pass skinny BF16 up-projection for `M <= 5`

The static SIMT kernel now uses:

- 224 threads per CTA;
- two output columns per CTA;
- 16 BF16 values (32 bytes) per thread;
- one K tile for `K=3584`;
- explicit `fma.rn.f32.bf16` into FP32 accumulators;
- a checked 32-byte alignment contract.

Compared with the prior eight-output/eight-BF16 geometry, this trades more output CTAs for a shorter, single-pass inner loop. The production WGMMA cluster shape remains `(1, 8)`; this PR does not change the dynamic GEMM cluster. The measured crossover keeps the static path at `M <= 5`: at `M=6` static/dynamic were `5.478/5.629 us`, but by `M=8` they were `7.193/5.794 us`, and the gap continued to grow through `M=16`.

### 4. Right-size and overlap the Lamport consumer

The copy/reset grid is selected at runtime as:

```text
min(32, ceil((M * 7168 / 8) / 128)) CTAs
```

For `M=1`, this is exactly seven 128-thread CTAs covering the 896 16-byte fragments, instead of 32 x 224 = 7,168 launched threads. Each polling iteration copies a ready fragment and resets its sentinel in the same pass. Because the Lamport marker itself is the data-readiness contract, the consumer no longer waits for ordinary producer-grid completion before polling, and it publishes its own PDL launch point early.

## Performance

Measured on 8x NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (driver 580.126.09), TP8, Kimi-K3 dimensions, BF16 tail inputs, and CUDA Graph replay. Isolated GEMV measurements rotate weights through a working set larger than L2. Values are medians.

| M=1 measurement | Before | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Exposed collective -> skinny GEMV -> Lamport chain in the packed Nsight trace | 12.096 us | 9.056 us | -25.1% |
| Skinny GEMV, rotating weights | 2.84-2.92 us | 2.51-2.52 us | -11% to -14% |
| Lamport copy/reset, standalone | ~4.77 us | ~1.25 us | -73.8% |
| Lamport copy/reset under packed overlap | ~4.77 us | ~1.95 us | -59.1% |

The decomposition shows that launch right-sizing of the Lamport consumer is the largest direct kernel reduction. In paired whole-tail replays holding the collective and copy fixed, the GEMV geometry reduced `16.512 -> 16.224 us` (~0.29 us). Moving the PDL point early reduced `16.576 -> 16.224 us` (~0.35 us).

The slowest-rank CUDA-event whole-tail sweep for `M=1..16` was effectively flat because that metric includes cross-rank graph scheduling and hides producer/consumer overlap; for example, `M=1` was `16.384 -> 16.352 us`. The 3.04 us improvement above is the exposed three-kernel critical chain in Nsight, excluding the region overlapped with its predecessor.

## Accuracy

### Kernel parity

The TP8 distributed tests compare the fused result with PyTorch collectives, RMSNorm, linear projection, and final add using `atol=8e-2`, `rtol=3e-2`:

- finalized input: `M = 1, 5, 8, 16, 33, 65, 5`, including two token waves, mailbox reuse, and CUDA Graph replay;
- deferred top-8 input: `M = 1, 5, 16, 33, 65`;
- specialized BF16 top-16 input: `M = 1, 2, 4, 5, 16`, including an invalid/dropped route and CUDA Graph replay.

All comparisons passed. The machine has eight GPUs, so the distributed TP16 pytest was not run; local TP16-shard up-projection parity passed during kernel tuning.

### Full-model evaluation

The modified production service was evaluated with `lm-eval 0.4.12` on the complete GSM8K v3 test split: 1,319/1,319 samples, 5-shot multi-turn chat-template prompting, greedy decoding, and seed 2026.

| Task | Filter | Correct | Exact match | Stderr |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K v3 | strict-match | 1267 / 1319 | 0.9606 | 0.0054 |
| GSM8K v3 | flexible-extract | 1273 / 1319 | 0.9651 | 0.0051 |

Serving used TP8, MXFP4 MoE, FP8 KV cache, a 16,384-token context limit, and 64 concurrent evaluation requests. No requests failed or retried.

Current `upstream/main` at `c01b50e390` has an unrelated Kimi-K3 startup issue where `_KimiK3LowLatencyApply` does not initialize the base method's `_gemm_impl`. For this evaluation only, startup used a local, uncommitted `super().__init__()` workaround. It does not touch the latent tail and was removed before the branch was pushed; it is not present in this PR.

## Tests run

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_latent_moe_tail.py \
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/cute_dsl/latent_moe_tail/allreduce_rmsnorm_reduce_scatter_early_exit.py \
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/cute_dsl/latent_moe_tail/fused_add_multicast_skinny_gemm.py \
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/cute_dsl/latent_moe_tail/lamport_copy.py \
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/cute_dsl/latent_moe_tail/primitives.py \
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/latent_moe_tail.py
# all hooks passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_latent_moe_tail.py \
  -k 'tp8_matches_native_path or deferred_finalize_matches_finalized' -v
# 2 passed, 2 deselected

.venv/bin/lm_eval run \
  --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=Kimi-K3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8100/v1/chat/completions,tokenizer=/path/to/Kimi-K3,tokenizer_backend=huggingface,trust_remote_code=true,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,timeout=900,max_gen_toks=1500,max_length=16384 \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template \
  --fewshot_as_multiturn true --log_samples --seed 2026
# 1319/1319 samples; strict 0.9606, flexible 0.9651
```

## Duplicate-work check

No issue number was provided, so there is no issue-number-specific PR query. Keyword searches found no PR implementing this low-M path.

- #53556 targets a different execution path: it moves BF16 shared-expert work into DeepGEMM MegaMoE, removes the standalone shared reduction, and optimizes the published-shared tail at `M=32/64`. This PR keeps the modular MXFP4 tail structure and optimizes its existing fused finalize + routed AR/RMSNorm + shared RS chain at `M=1..16`.
- #53202 changes the default unquantized BF16 linear implementation. The skinny kernel here is not that linear method: it fuses the shared-shard add, TP-local up-projection, and NVLS multicast publication.

## Contribution notes

AI assistance was used during implementation, source comparison, benchmarking, testing, and preparation of this PR description. The human submitter must review every changed line, understand and defend the change end-to-end, and verify the reported commands and results before submission.

title: [Model] Support Ling 3.0 D-Spark serving
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

> [!NOTE]
> This description was updated by @ZJY0516's AI agent (Claude Code) after addressing the latest review comments (f5b5b198b0) and merging main (12946cc1be). The original implementation is by @zexplorerhj.

## Overview

Add D-Spark speculative decoding for [Ling 3.0 Flash](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash) using the official [Ling D-Spark draft](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-dspark). The Ling draft is normalized onto the existing Qwen3 D-Spark runtime; no new drafter is added.

## Claims

- `LingDSparkModel` drafts are validated against a `BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM` target and mapped to `Qwen3DSparkModel`. The draft checks shared with Qwen3-Omni D-Spark now live in one helper (`_validate_qwen3_dspark_draft`).
- `BailingMoeV3` exposes the auxiliary hidden states D-Spark needs (`SupportsEagle3`).
- The draft's `block_size` is the default `num_speculative_tokens`; an explicit value still takes precedence.
- On hybrid MLA targets, a DFlash/D-Spark draft whose KV page would exceed the target page uses a smaller KV block that fits the target page, instead of inflating the target's MLA/KDA pages (or failing page-size unification).

## Validation

Unit tests:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py tests/model_executor/test_bailing_moe_v3.py \
  tests/test_config.py -k "dflash or dspark or bailing or eagle_aux"   # 50 passed
```

E2E on GB200, Ling 3.0 Flash BF16, TP=4, branch head `12946cc1be`. GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot chat completions, thinking off, temperature 0, concurrency 8.

| Configuration | GSM8K flexible / strict | Mean acceptance length | Eval wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Target only | 91.28% / 88.63% | - | 405 s |
| Ling D-Spark (`num_speculative_tokens=7`) | 91.58% / 88.78% | 6.02 | 269 s |

Per-position acceptance for positions 1-7: 93.9 / 86.4 / 79.1 / 71.9 / 64.5 / 57.3 / 49.1%. Eval wall time is a rough end-to-end signal, not a throughput benchmark.

<details>
<summary>Launch command</summary>

```bash
vllm serve inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --reasoning-parser ling3 \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7}'
```

`--moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass` is required on current main for both configurations, and it is unrelated to this PR. The auto-selected FlashInfer TRTLLM BF16 MoE fails in its routing kernel: Ling has 64 experts per group, and the kernel allows at most 32 (one warp).

</details>

CI cannot run the end-to-end path: the Ling checkpoints are registered with `is_available_online=False` because they are too large for CI. The unit tests above cover config normalization, aux hidden-state capture, and the draft KV block size selection.

## Details

**Draft KV block size.** Ling pairs an MLA/KDA hybrid target with a dense MHA draft. The hybrid alignment raises the global block size until the MLA page covers the KDA state, for example 512 tokens at TP=4. At that block size the draft's MHA page is about 3.6x the target page. MLA pages cannot be padded, so page-size unification fails.

`_DFlashAttention.get_kv_cache_spec` now picks the largest block size that meets three conditions:

- it divides the global block size, so the scheduler LCM is unchanged;
- the backend runs it directly, without splitting the block;
- its page fits in the target page (`cache_config.mamba_page_size_padded`).

Unification then pads the draft page up to the target page. For Ling 3.0 Flash this gives 128 tokens at TP=1/2/4/8, with 88.9% of each draft page used. No core KV-cache code is changed.

The E2E engine log confirms the geometry: target block 512, Mamba page padded by 0.70%, and an LCM of 512 across KV cache groups.

The draft's dense MHA KV (32 KV heads) is much larger per token than the target's MLA KV. Adding the draft reduces KV capacity from 13.9M to 3.1M tokens at TP=4. That cost comes from the draft architecture, not from the block size.

**Scope.** Only hybrid MLA targets use this path. Non-MLA hybrid targets with larger DFlash drafts, such as Qwen3.5 + DFlash, keep their current behavior.

**Duplicate check.** There is no other open PR for Ling D-Spark or BailingMoeV3 aux hidden states.

title: fix: enable ROCM_AITER_FA with Eagle3 spec decode
body:
Create patch file based on `releases/v0.27.1` (to be updated after each sync to `main`)
```
git diff b0224f9d2f~1 9e5b969005 -- vllm/ ':!README_ROCM_AITER_FA.md' | sed 's|a/vllm/|a/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/|g; s|b/vllm/|b/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/|g' > /tmp/rocm_aiter_fa_only.patch
```
Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.27.1`

## Problem

ROCM_AITER_FA + Eagle3 speculative decoding on MiniMax-M3 crashes at startup and is slower than TRITON_ATTN:

1. **`ValueError: No common block size for 128`** — MiniMax-M3 sparse attention requires page block size 128 for its indexer cache. `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes` returns `[16, 32]` (from [#32492](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32492)), overly restrictive now that [#24486](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24486) decoupled kernel block size from page block size.

2. **KV cache shape mismatch** — `get_kv_cache_spec` in AMD sparse attention and indexer cache used `cache_config.block_size` instead of the model's `sparse_block_size` (128).

3. **`AssertionError` on first verification step** — Hard-asserts `not is_shuffle_kv_cache_enabled()` in the `decode_max_query_len > 1` branch crashes when `VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1` is set.

4. **Performance: ROCM_AITER_FA was 24% slower than TRITON_ATTN** for spec decode due to the chunked extend loop (Python for-loop with gather+flash_attn+merge per chunk) and per-call temp tensor allocations in the attention kernel.

## Fix

**Correctness:**
- Widen `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes` back to `MultipleOf(16)`
- Use `sparse_block_size` from model config for both main attention spec and indexer cache spec
- Auto-disable shuffle KV cache layout when `speculative_config` is present (in `RocmPlatform.check_and_update_config`)
- Relax shuffle assertion: only raise for sliding window/sinks, not spec decode
- Prioritize ROCM_AITER_FA over ROCM_ATTN in backend selection order

**Performance:**
- **Unified fast-path**: route ALL tokens through a single `unified_attention` kernel call, bypassing the batch-split metadata computation and the chunked extend loop (which launched multiple gather + flash_attn + merge kernels per step)
- **Fast metadata build**: skip `split_decodes_prefills_and_extends` entirely when the unified path is taken — eliminates CPU-side tensor ops every step
- **Attention kernel**: the unified path uses vLLM's Triton `unified_attention` (2D kernel, no per-call allocations) rather than AITER's `unified_attention` (3D segmented path with per-call temp tensor allocations for long sequences). The ROCM_AITER_FA backend still provides AITER-accelerated ops that account for the +17% gain over TRITON_ATTN:
  - **FP4/FP8 GEMM** (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM`, `FP8BMM`) — MXFP4 MoE and linear kernels optimized for MI300X/MI355X
  - **Fused MoE** (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE`) — AITER fused mixture-of-experts dispatch+GEMM (128 experts in MiniMax-M3)
  - **Fused RMSNorm** (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM`) — fused add+RMSNorm, avoids extra kernel launch per layer
  - **Fused RoPE+KV cache write** — single kernel for rotary embedding + cache insert (vs separate RoPE then cache write)
  - **QK-Norm+RoPE+KV cache fusion** (`qk_norm_rope_kvcache` compilation pass) — fuses query/key normalization, RoPE, and KV cache write into one kernel
  - **Custom AllReduce** (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR`) — optimized TP allreduce for MI300X interconnect


# ROCM_AITER_FA Benchmark Results (MI350X gfx950, TP4, MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 + Eagle3)

## Key Flags

```
--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA
--block-size 128
--kv-cache-dtype fp8
--tensor-parallel-size 4
--speculative-config '{"method": "eagle3", "model": "Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'

VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=0
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA=1
VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
```

## Benchmark Parameters

```
--dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024
--random-range-ratio 0.8 --max-concurrency 8 --num-prompts 80
```

## Results

| Metric | ROCM_AITER_FA (block-128) | TRITON_ATTN baseline | Delta |
|--------|---------------------------:|---------------------:|------:|
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | **7659** | 6228 | **+23%** |
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | **843** | 685 | **+23%** |

## Analysis

The two critical flags for performance:
- `--block-size 128`: reduces block table lookups in the unified attention kernel, improves memory coalescing
- `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4`: compresses all-reduce communication to INT4, reducing inter-GPU bandwidth pressure on TP4

title: [Metrics] Export KV cache capacity in bytes
body:
## Review summary

- Adds startup-time `vllm:kv_cache_capacity_bytes`, preserving capacity per global DP rank.
- Counts device KV backing only; excludes HiSparse host pools and avoids counting aliased device descriptors twice.
- Rebased onto main `852989f580`; 111 CPU checks and changed-file pre-commit passed.

## Overview

Expose a KV-cache byte-capacity Gauge for device-memory dashboards and capacity
alerts, using post-profiling `KVCacheConfig` backing sizes summed across workers
in each DP engine.

This complements #42206's group-aware token capacity and maximum concurrency
in `vllm:cache_config_info`, rather than duplicating that work. The original
duplicate-work searches found no equivalent open byte-capacity PR.

## Claims

- Counts device backing allocations per worker, without double-counting
  aliased cache-group descriptors. Custom builders with multiple allocations
  use their declared total bytes per block. Host-resident pools are excluded.
- Initializes each `engine` Gauge from its matching global-DP-rank ready
  response, independent of response arrival order.
- Computes capacity at startup with no steady-state GPU work; the Gauge uses
  the existing model/engine labels.

## Validation

2026-10-19: **111 passed** on CPU across packing, builder resolution, planning,
and per-DP capacity propagation through msgspec, `MPClient`, and Prometheus Gauges.
Changed-file pre-commit passed, including mypy and Buildkite test tethering.

The HiSparse regression previously reproduced the failure before the fix. It
covers equal and unequal host/device pool sizes, aliased device descriptors,
the shared-host flag, and a host-only configuration. It uses the real config
producer, without allocating GPU buffers.

The October 19 rebase preserves upstream coordinator metadata in the ready-response
test and adds its required `parallel_config` field to the CPU DP fixture.

A new real-planner regression reproduced two incompatibilities with upstream
custom builders: unequal device allocation sizes raised an assertion, while
equal-sized independent allocations were undercounted. Both cases now pass,
including two workers converging from 10/20 blocks to 10 blocks each.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_config_builder.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py \
  tests/v1/metrics/test_kv_cache_capacity.py -q
git diff --name-only -z 852989f580820849113d67d13fd8053e279d0444..HEAD \
  | xargs -0 pre-commit run --files
```

These CPU checks are not a new full-serving/GPU or ROCm runtime validation.
The CUDA-alike-only engine-client test module was not rerun. The original
submission's serving metric inventory checks remain historical evidence.

## Details

Ready responses carry each EngineCore's capacity; the frontend stores it by
global DP rank and initializes the matching `engine` Gauge once.

HiSparse uses separate host and device backings. The old assertion incorrectly
required all descriptors to have the same size and could fail during EngineCore
initialization. Accounting now filters host-resident descriptors first, matching
the device allocator's input. Default layouts retain the device single-backing
invariant; an empty device descriptor list reports zero. Custom builders that
declare multiple allocations store their declared bytes per block times the
final worker block count, after cross-worker replanning. This does not change
allocation or model execution. Shared host memory is outside the metric's scope.

The value excludes allocator tail padding, including ROCm's 4096-byte rounding;
it is not total process/device memory usage. The configuration documentation,
Prometheus HELP, and `docs/design/metrics.md` use the same device-only definition.

OpenAI Codex assisted with code, tests, documentation, and rebase maintenance.
The October 19 validation above was agent-run; no new personal test execution
by the submitter is implied.

title: [Bug]: Out-of-vocab stop_token_ids crashes the whole engine on backends with bounds-checked index kernels (single-request DoS)
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`stop_token_ids` is not validated against the vocabulary size. An out-of-vocab token id in a request is accepted unchecked and is later used as a **logits index on the device** (e.g. min_tokens / EOS masking does `logits.index_put_((rows, all_stop_token_ids), -inf)` in `vllm/v1/sample/logits_processor/builtin.py`). On backends whose index kernels perform device-side bounds checking, a single such request crashes the entire engine with an unrecoverable device exception.

Reproduced end-to-end on vLLM 0.23.0 + vllm-ascend 0.23.0rc1, DeepSeek-V4-Flash (vocab 129280), PD-disaggregated deployment (MooncakeHybridConnector + MTP), CANN 9.1.0:

```
# request
{"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}], "stop_token_ids": [151645], "max_tokens": 300}

# device error (all 8 TP ranks die simultaneously)
Index out of range in dimension 1: index value 151645 exceeds bounds 129280!
[ASSERT] .../ascendc/index_check/index_check.h:130: Assertion `(idx < bound)' failed.
fault kernel_name=IndexCheck_int32_high_performance_1
RuntimeError: vector core exception, retCode=0x31
```

The prefill instance dies completely (HTTP 500 for all subsequent requests). 151645 is `<|im_end|>` of the older DeepSeek V3 tokenizer; DeepSeek-V4-Flash's vocab is 129280, so clients reusing stale token ids hit this trivially.

Trigger conditions (all verified experimentally):
1. `stop_token_ids` contains an id `>= vocab_size` — passes `_verify_common` which only checks the type (`vllm/sampling_params.py`)
2. The id reaches a device-side indexing path. This happens whenever `min_tokens > 0` (`MinTokensLogitsProcessor.apply` / `apply_with_spec_decode` register `params.all_stop_token_ids` and index logits with them). Note the PD proxy example scripts rewrite prefill requests to `max_tokens=1, min_tokens=1` (`load_balance_proxy_server_example.py`), which activates this path for **every** request going through the proxy
3. Backend performs bounds checking on index ops (Ascend CANN 9.1.x inserts IndexCheck kernels; older CANN 9.0.1 silently corrupts neighboring logits instead — arguably worse)

On CUDA the same request "works" only because out-of-bounds `index_put_` semantics are luck-dependent; on NPU with CANN 9.1 it is a guaranteed device-level crash. Either way the id can never match a sampled token, so rejecting it upfront loses nothing.

`logit_bias` and `allowed_token_ids` are already validated against the vocabulary in `SamplingParams.verify()`; `stop_token_ids` is the one unchecked entry point into `all_stop_token_ids`.

### Proposed fix

Add `_validate_stop_token_ids` to `SamplingParams` mirroring `_validate_logit_bias`, rejecting out-of-vocab ids with a 400 before the request reaches the engine. PR to follow.

Downstream issue: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/15200

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Validate stop_token_ids against vocab size
body:
### Description
Fixes #54195 (downstream: vllm-project/vllm-ascend#15200)

`stop_token_ids` was the only user-facing token-id parameter not validated against the vocabulary. Out-of-vocab ids are accepted and later used as logits indices on the device (min_tokens / EOS masking in `vllm/v1/sample/logits_processor/builtin.py` does `logits.index_put_((rows, all_stop_token_ids), -inf)`).

Impact, both verified on vLLM 0.23.0 / vllm-ascend 0.23.0rc1 / DeepSeek-V4-Flash (vocab 129280) / CANN 9.1.0:
- On backends with bounds-checked index kernels (CANN 9.1 inserts an `IndexCheck` kernel), a single request with `stop_token_ids: [151645]` crashes the whole engine with an unrecoverable vector-core exception (all TP ranks die; device context aborts).
- On backends without the check (CANN 9.0.1, and effectively any backend relying on UB), the OOB `index_put_` silently writes into logits rows of neighboring requests in the same batch.

This PR adds `SamplingParams._validate_stop_token_ids`, mirroring the existing `_validate_logit_bias` / `_validate_allowed_token_ids` pattern, so invalid requests are rejected with a 400 before reaching the engine.

### Proof of crash (before this fix)

Device log, all 8 TP ranks simultaneously:
```
Index out of range in dimension 1: index value 151645 exceeds bounds 129280!
[ASSERT] .../ascendc/index_check/index_check.h:130: Assertion `(idx < bound)' failed.
fault kernel_name=IndexCheck_int32_high_performance_1
```

Trigger chain (requires all three):
1. out-of-vocab id in `stop_token_ids` (151645 = stale `<|im_end|>` of the older DeepSeek tokenizer)
2. `min_tokens > 0` — note the PD proxy example scripts rewrite prefill requests to `max_tokens=1, min_tokens=1`, activating the device-indexing path for every proxied request
3. bounds-checking backend

### Testing
- New test `tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat_stop_token_ids_validation.py` following the existing `test_chat_logit_bias_validation.py` pattern: valid id accepted; out-of-vocab and negative ids rejected with 400.
- Verified the validator offline against `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct` (vocab 151936): `[vocab_size-1, 0]` passes, `[vocab_size, vocab_size+5]` and `[-2]` raise with a clear message.
- End-to-end on the repro environment: with this patch, the crashing request returns a 400 and the engine survives.

title: [Docs] Document DeepSeek-V4 reasoning_effort normalization
body:
## Purpose

`docs/features/reasoning_outputs.md` does not describe how DeepSeek-V4 resolves `reasoning_effort`, and one existing statement about it is inverted. This PR documents the actual behavior of `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py` and corrects the stale sentence.

Three changes, all in `docs/features/reasoning_outputs.md`:

1. **Corrects a false statement.** The "Automatic `enable_thinking` Activation" section lists DeepSeek-V4-Pro among the models that "require `enable_thinking: true` … without it, reasoning tokens are never generated regardless of other settings". The opposite has been true since #50580: when neither `thinking` nor `enable_thinking` is present, the tokenizer sets `thinking_enabled = True`.

2. **Adds DeepSeek-V4 to the defaults note**, alongside the existing Qwen3 / Granite / Gemma 4 / Holo2 entries, which is where a reader looks for a model's default thinking behavior.

3. **Adds a `DeepSeek-V4 Effort Normalization` subsection** with the mapping table. The normalization is model-specific and diverges from the generic `enable_thinking` injection documented just above it, so a reader following the generic rules currently gets the wrong answer.

The two behaviors that are most surprising, and the reason this is worth documenting rather than leaving to source reading:

- Omitting `reasoning_effort` is not neutral. With thinking on it resolves to `high`, which prepends the "Absolute maximum with no shortcuts permitted" prefix. A client that wants thinking *without* an effort directive has to pass `reasoning_effort="low"` explicitly.
- `minimal` / `low` / `medium` all collapse to `low` (no prefix), while unrecognized values go to `high`. The pre-#50580 mapping sent `minimal` / `medium` to `high`, so stale second-hand descriptions of this mapping are in circulation.

This exact gap produced #52083 ("massive spike in truncations and a drop in AL"), where the default change to `high` was only discovered by bisecting to #50580. The follow-up #52085 proposed a runtime warning and was closed as no longer needed now that DSV4-Pro-0813 shares the pattern — which settles the behavior as intended and stable, and therefore documentable.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Checked open PRs touching `docs/features/reasoning_outputs.md` and open PRs/issues matching DeepSeek-V4 + reasoning effort.

The closest is #52739 (`[Frontend] Map unsupported reasoning_effort to nearest supported level`), which also edits this file. It is a different concern and does not overlap: it adds a *serving-layer* opt-in flag (`--supported-reasoning-efforts`) that remaps values before rendering, and documents it in a new section appended near the end of the file. This PR documents the *model-side* normalization that DeepSeek-V4's tokenizer already applies unconditionally, and edits the defaults note and the auto-activation section. The two are complementary; the new subsection here is placed inside the existing "Automatic `enable_thinking` Activation" section, so the hunks do not collide.

#52085 (closed, unmerged) proposed a code-level warning for the same default. This PR takes the documentation route instead, which is what the closing rationale left open.

## Test Plan

Documentation-only change: no Python or Rust code paths are touched, so no test suite applies. Every claim in the added text was verified against source rather than against the PR descriptions that currently carry this information:

- `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py` — the `thinking_enabled` default and the `reasoning_effort` branch chain, checked on `main` and at tag `v0.28.0`.
- `tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py` — `test_deepseek_v4_defaults_to_thinking_with_high_effort` and the parametrized mapping cases (`minimal`/`low`/`medium` → `low`, `high`/`xhigh`/`unexpected` → `high`, `max` → `max`, `none` → chat), which match the table added here row for row.
- `encoding/encoding_dsv4.py` in `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` — `REASONING_EFFORT_PROMPTS` for the prefix texts (`low` maps to the empty string) and `DEFAULT_REASONING_EFFORT`.

## Test Result

No tests run — documentation only. Markdown rendering of the added table and section was checked locally.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to research the source files and issue history and to draft this change. The submitter has reviewed every changed line and verified each factual claim against the sources listed above.

title: [MoE] Re-enable TRITON_UNFUSED in the gpt-oss MXFP4 dispatch list
body:
## Purpose

Closes #49446.

`TRITON_UNFUSED` was taken out of `_get_priority_backends_for_gpt_oss()` in #40860 with a note about an MTP bug. MTP only exists in DeepSeek-V4, which selects through `select_deepseek_v4_mxfp4_moe_backend()`, and that function already auto-selects `TRITON_UNFUSED` on ROCm today. The gate sits on the list where MTP cannot occur and is absent on the one where it can. This restores it in the gpt-oss list only; the DeepSeek-V4 list keeps its gate, since I have no MXFP4 DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint to test MTP against.

The issue also asks for a warning that the backend ignores activation quantization. No warning can fire: `_filter_by_activation` drops it whenever an activation key is requested, and `BaseOAITritonExperts._supports_quant_scheme` accepts only `(kMxfp4Static, None)`. That is the difference from the fallback #46491 reverted, which sat after the filter. I pinned it with a test instead.

Only GELU and SWIGLUSTEP change backend, both off `MARLIN`, because `OAITritonExperts` accepts SWIGLUOAI alone while `UnfusedOAITritonExperts` covers the wider set. SWIGLUOAI stays on `TRITON`, SILU and SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE stay on FlashInfer CUTLASS. With fp8-static, mxfp8-dynamic or mxfp4-dynamic requested, selection raises `NotImplementedError` before and after, never `TRITON_UNFUSED`.

## Test plan

1x H100 80GB, `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, nightly `a9a17e709` with the patch overlaid.

```
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_oai_triton_moe.py
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py
```

## Test result

`test_modular_oai_triton_moe.py` 21 passed, including all 10 `unfused=True` cases and the DeepSeek-V4-Flash topology test. `test_ocp_mx_moe.py` 15 passed, 135 skipped (CUDA host, most cases are ROCm). The new test fails against unpatched main, and fails again if `_filter_by_activation` is stubbed out, so both halves are load-bearing.

gsm8k, full 1319 items, chat template, greedy: TRITON auto stock 93.78%, TRITON auto patched 94.84%, TRITON_UNFUSED forced 94.54%. Repeat runs of one config move about a point, so the kernels are equivalent here.

gsm8k 500 items under ngram speculative decoding, which is the multi-token-per-step decode shape MTP produces: TRITON 94.80%, TRITON_UNFUSED 95.20%, no errors on either.

I could not run TP=2 EP, NCCL fails to init on my cluster for unrelated reasons.

#41764 refactors this same function and carries the comment forward, so whichever lands first the other needs a trivial rebase. Neither it nor #52240 re-enables the backend, so this is not a duplicate.

AI assistance was used for this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and evals above myself.

title: [Bugfix] Keep ROCm out of the >=160GiB batched-token tier
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #53961. #51726 added a `device_memory >= 160GiB` tier targeting B200/B300, but it gates on raw capacity, so MI300X (192GB) and MI325X (256GB) fall into it as well. `OPENAI_API_SERVER` `max_num_batched_tokens` silently doubles (8192 → 16384), the activation peak during `profile_run` doubles with it, and DeepSeek-V4-Pro can no longer initialize its KV cache at 1M context on MI300X (`ValueError: 23.32 GiB KV cache is needed ... larger than the available 13.41 GiB`). The replaced 70GiB branch named MI300x explicitly. Gate the new tier to non-ROCm platforms so AMD devices stay on the branch they were on before #51726. No behavioral change for NVIDIA: H100/H200 stay under 160GB, B200/B300 remain in the top tier.

Not a duplicate: no open PR references #53961 or the tier gate; #51726 is the change being corrected, and the issue reporter's repro is ROCm-specific.

## Test Plan

```
ruff check / ruff format --check vllm/engine/arg_utils.py tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py  (repo-pinned 0.14.0, clean)
mypy 1.20.2 vllm/engine/arg_utils.py --python-version 3.10  (no issues)
python -m compileall  (ok)
```

Added `test_get_batch_defaults_160gib_tier_excludes_rocm` (parametrized: B200 keeps 16384, MI300X and MI325X stay at 8192, H100 unchanged). Local pytest execution is blocked on this machine by a broken torch build in the dev venv (native extension crash at import, unrelated to this diff), so the test runs on CI. Lint/type/syntax checks above were run locally; no GPU-dependent verification was claimed.

AI assistance: prepared with Kimi K3 assistance; the fix and test were reviewed line by line before submission.

title: [Bug]: Quark FSE compatibility check matches `shared_expert_gate`, silently disabling fused shared experts on Qwen MoE MXFP4
body:
## Summary

`is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible` decides whether AITER fused shared experts (FSE) may run by searching the **entire** Quark `exclude` list for the substring `shared_expert`:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/config_utils.py#L106-L111

```python
is_compatible = not any(
    "shared_expert" in str(entry)
    for entry in quant_config.quant_config["exclude"]
)
if not is_compatible:
    return False, f"Quark excludes shared experts at {shared_expert_prefix}"
```

That substring also matches `mlp.shared_expert_gate`, which is a **different module**: the `hidden_size -> 1` router gate that scales the shared expert's output. It is BF16 by design (quantizing a 1-column projection is pointless), so every Qwen MoE Quark checkpoint lists it in `exclude` — including checkpoints whose shared-expert projections are fully MXFP4.

The result is that FSE is refused on exactly the checkpoints it was enabled for. Nothing fails and accuracy is unchanged; the shared expert simply runs unfused, costing the FSE speedup on ROCm, with only a per-MoE-layer startup warning:

```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS is enabled but cannot be enabled:
Quark excludes shared experts at model.layers.0.mlp.shared_expert.
```

## Regression

Introduced in #51695, which moved Qwen off its own local check onto the shared helper. The previous Qwen check matched `"shared_expert."` **with the trailing dot**, which only matched real projections (`shared_expert.down_proj`) and correctly ignored the `shared_expert_gate` sibling:

```python
# removed in #51695, vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_next.py
return not any("shared_expert." in str(e) for e in exclude)
```

The dot appears to have been dropped so one substring could cover both the Qwen singular `shared_expert.` and the DeepSeek/GLM plural `shared_experts.`. The test added in that PR only exercises the plural naming and never a `shared_expert_gate` sibling, which is why CI did not catch it.

## Reproduction

No GPU needed — the check is a pure function of `config.json`. Using a public checkpoint:

```python
import json
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

path = hf_hub_download("amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MoE-MXFP4", "config.json")
exclude = json.load(open(path))["quantization_config"]["exclude"]

matches = [e for e in exclude if "shared_expert" in e]
print(len(matches), "entries match the current check, e.g.", matches[:2])
print("any real shared-expert projection excluded:",
      any("shared_expert." in e for e in exclude))
```

```
61 entries match the current check, e.g. ['model.layers.0.mlp.shared_expert_gate', 'model.layers.1.mlp.shared_expert_gate']
any real shared-expert projection excluded: False
```

Every match is the router gate; not a single shared-expert projection is excluded. The current check nevertheless reports incompatible and FSE is disabled.

## Impact

Evaluated by building a real `QuarkConfig` from each checkpoint (weights mapper applied, `packed_modules_mapping` populated as the loader does) and calling the gate:

| Checkpoint | before #51695 | current `main` | correct |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MoE-MXFP4` (public) | enabled | **disabled** | enabled |
| `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-MoE-MXFP4` | enabled | **disabled** | enabled |
| `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4` (public) | disabled | disabled | disabled — shared expert genuinely BF16 |

The last row is the true positive the check exists for, and it must keep working: that checkpoint really does exclude `shared_expert.{gate,up,down}_proj`.

## Proposed fix

Ask whether the shared expert's **own projections** are excluded, instead of substring-scanning the list. `should_ignore_layer` already answers exactly this question — it is what `QuarkConfig.get_quant_method` uses — and it handles exact names, `re:`/glob patterns, and expands fused names such as `gate_up_proj` into the `gate_proj`/`up_proj` shards the checkpoint stores. Being scoped to one module, a sibling cannot trigger it. This also matches the DeepSeek-V4 branch a few lines above, which already scopes with `startswith(shared_expert_prefix)`.

```diff
     if isinstance(quant_config, QuarkConfig):
+        from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.quark.utils import (
+            should_ignore_layer,
+        )
+
         # TODO: layer_type_quant_config is not taken into account here.
         assert "exclude" in quant_config.quant_config
         assert "global_quant_config" in quant_config.quant_config
 
-        is_compatible = not any(
-            "shared_expert" in str(entry)
-            for entry in quant_config.quant_config["exclude"]
-        )
-        if not is_compatible:
-            return False, f"Quark excludes shared experts at {shared_expert_prefix}"
+        # Ask whether the shared expert's own projections are excluded rather
+        # than searching the exclude list for the substring "shared_expert".
+        # Sibling modules contain that substring while saying nothing about the
+        # shared expert: every Qwen MoE checkpoint excludes
+        # `mlp.shared_expert_gate`, a 1-wide router gate that is BF16 by design.
+        excluded = [
+            projection_name
+            for projection_name in projection_names
+            if should_ignore_layer(
+                f"{shared_expert_prefix}.{projection_name}",
+                ignore=quant_config.quant_config["exclude"],
+                fused_mapping=quant_config.packed_modules_mapping,
+            )
+        ]
+        if excluded:
+            return False, (
+                f"Quark excludes shared-expert {', '.join(excluded)} at "
+                f"{shared_expert_prefix}"
+            )
```

`projection_names` is already a parameter and is already used further down, so this introduces no new inputs. With the patch applied, the three checkpoints above return enabled / enabled / disabled, and the refusal message becomes specific: `Quark excludes shared-expert gate_up_proj, down_proj at model.layers.0.mlp.shared_expert`.

Restoring the trailing dot would also work and is a one-character change, but it leaves the same trap for the next module named `shared_expert_*`, and it still relies on guessing names rather than asking whether a module is excluded.

I am happy to open a PR with this plus a regression test covering a checkpoint that excludes `shared_expert_gate` while quantizing the shared-expert projections.

## Environment

Working build (FSE enabled): `0.27.2rc1.dev150+g311b3513a`, ROCm, MI355X (gfx950), Qwen3.8/Qwen3.5 MoE MXFP4, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`. Regression confirmed present on `main` as of today.

cc @fxmarty-amd @mgoin @bnellnm @BowenBao — authored / reviewed / merged #51695.
