title: [Bugfix] Resolve --kv-cache-dtype auto to fp8_ds_mla for DeepSeek-V4 on SM120
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #47174

On SM120 (consumer/workstation Blackwell, e.g. RTX PRO 6000), the DeepSeek-V4 sparse-MLA attention path hardcodes the `fp8_ds_mla` KV block layout (`DeepseekV4FlashInferSM120Attention.use_fp8_ds_mla_layout = True`), which has no unquantized fallback. The default `--kv-cache-dtype auto` (i.e. the plain `vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` command from the model card) therefore crashed engine init with a bare assert:

```
AssertionError: DeepseekV4 fp8_ds_mla layout only supports fp8 kv-cache, got auto
```

This PR:
- resolves `auto` to `fp8_ds_mla` in `_resolve_dsv4_kv_cache_dtype`, mirroring the existing `fp8` → `fp8_ds_mla` upgrade (incl. the `cache_config` write-back that drives the 576B page-size specs), with the existing `info_once` log;
- replaces the bare assert with an actionable `ValueError` for genuinely unsupported values (e.g. `bfloat16`);
- accepts `auto`/`None` in the SM12x branch of `DeepseekV4FlashInferMLASparseBackend.supports_combination`, matching the SM10x branch.

Behavior on SM10x (H100 etc.) is unchanged: that path uses the plain KV row layout (`use_fp8_ds_mla_layout = False`) and `auto` still resolves to bf16 rows, covered by a new regression test.

**Duplicate-work check:** no open PR references #47174 (checked `gh pr list --search "47174 in:body"` on 2026-08-28); the issue has no linked fix.

## Test Plan

Hardware: 8× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, CC 12.0), driver 580.178.04, torch 2.13.0+cu132, FlashInfer 0.6.18rc10 (the SM120 sparse-MLA decode path requires a FlashInfer build containing flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4380; the current 0.6.17 pin refuses to start independently of this change).

Unit tests:
```
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py -v
```

E2E (repro of the issue, using a 4-layer DeepSeek-V4-Flash config with `--load-format dummy` on 1 GPU):
```python
from vllm import LLM
llm = LLM(model=<4-layer DSV4-Flash config>, load_format='dummy', enforce_eager=True, max_model_len=4096)  # kv_cache_dtype defaults to auto
llm.generate('Hello')
```

## Test Result

- Unit: **11 passed** (5 pre-existing + 6 new: `auto`/`fp8`/`fp8_e4m3` resolve to `fp8_ds_mla` + write-back, `bfloat16` raises actionable ValueError, plain layout keeps `auto` → bf16, SM12x `supports_combination` accepts `auto`).
- E2E before: `AssertionError: DeepseekV4 fp8_ds_mla layout only supports fp8 kv-cache, got auto` at `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py:105`.
- E2E after: boots with `INFO ... Using DeepSeek's fp8_ds_mla KV cache format.` and generates — identical behavior to the previous `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` workaround.
- Full-model sanity on the same machine (unrelated to this diff path, exercised via `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`): DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 serves coherent greedy output on current main.

This change only affects engine startup dtype resolution (crash → boot); it introduces no new numeric path: `auto` now takes exactly the code path `fp8` already took.

---

AI assistance was used for this change (Claude Code); the submitter has reviewed the diff and test results.

title: [Kernel] Warm up Qwen GDN gated RMSNorm
body:
## Purpose

Refs #49349.

Qwen3.5's GDN output projection calls the FLA `layer_norm_fwd_kernel` through
`RMSNormGated`. With cold Triton/vLLM caches, the first real request compiled
this specialization after the JIT monitor became active:

```text
ACTIVATION='silu', BLOCK_N=128, HAS_BIAS=False, HAS_Z=True,
IS_RMS_NORM=True, N=128, NORM_BEFORE_GATE=True, ROWS_PER_BLOCK=4,
X/Y/W/Z='*bf16'
```

This PR moves that compilation into startup warmup by:

- adding a shared `VllmJitKernel` wrapper for the FLA layer-norm forward kernel;
- using the same compile-key dispatch contract for runtime execution and
  compile-only warmup;
- enumerating the `M` specialization and `ROWS_PER_BLOCK` keys implied by the
  configured token limit and TP-local Qwen value-head count; and
- registering the Qwen GDN gated RMSNorm configuration with its actual dtypes,
  head dimension, activation, and gate ordering.

The warmup uses `TritonWarmupTensor` descriptors and does not allocate or launch
dummy inference tensors.

This does not duplicate #51134, which removes an obsolete FlashInfer startup
warning but does not warm this Triton kernel. It also does not overlap #50279,
which adds an SM103-specific fused kernel rather than general compile-key warmup
for the existing FLA implementation.

## Test Plan

Run focused key-coverage and kernel-correctness tests on an RTX 3090:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=5 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/kernels/test_fla_layernorm_guard.py::test_layer_norm_fwd_warmup_keys_cover_qwen_gdn \
  'tests/kernels/test_fla_layernorm_guard.py::test_layer_norm_fwd_with_gate[True-True-dtype1-128-1]' \
  'tests/kernels/test_fla_layernorm_guard.py::test_layer_norm_fwd_with_gate[True-True-dtype1-128-512]' \
  'tests/kernels/test_fla_layernorm_guard.py::test_layer_norm_fwd_with_gate[True-True-dtype1-128-8191]'
```

Run changed-file checks:

```bash
pre-commit run ruff-check --files \
  tests/kernels/test_fla_layernorm_guard.py \
  vllm/model_executor/warmup/qwen_triton_warmup.py \
  vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/layernorm_guard.py
pre-commit run ruff-format --files <same files>
pre-commit run typos --files <same files>
pre-commit run --hook-stage manual mypy-3.10 --files <same files>
git diff --check
```

Run Qwen3.5-0.8B E2E generation with fresh Triton/vLLM caches and
`--jit-monitor-mode error` for TP=1 and TP=2.

## Test Result

- Focused pytest: `8 passed, 14 warnings in 5.67s`.
- `ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `typos`, `mypy-3.10`, and `git diff --check`:
  passed.
- Cold-cache TP=1 E2E completed with `--jit-monitor-mode error`; no runtime JIT
  was reported.
- Cold-cache TP=2 E2E completed on two RTX 3090 GPUs with
  `--jit-monitor-mode error`; no runtime JIT was reported. Shutdown later emitted
  unrelated force-kill and leaked semaphore/shared-memory warnings after the
  successful result.
- One cold-cache TP=1 A/B measurement reduced first-request time from
  `0.2791 s` to `0.0933 s` (about 66.6%). Startup time was `124.117 s` before
  and `124.403 s` after. These are single-run latency observations, not a

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Fuse gated RMSNorm with per-token FP8 for KDA o_proj
body:
## Purpose

Depends on #54248 (K3 `o_proj` becomes `Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod`). Until this lands, this path is a no-op.

Kimi-K3 KDA is gated RMSNorm then `o_proj`. With PTPC that is `FusedRMSNormGated` plus standalone dynamic_per_token_scaled_quant` in the linear. Fuse them in one Triton kernel with per-token amax.

Wrap `(fp8, scale)` as `QuantizedActivation(kFp8DynamicTokenSym)` when `o_proj.input_quant_key` matches. Skip `o_norm` on that path so we do not double-norm.

`fused_kda_decode` (#50654) already applied gated RMSNorm on pure non-spec decode. Quantize that output with `per_token_fp8_quant` so we do not double-norm.

## Profile

8×MI355X, TP8, Kimi-K3 + DSpark, 50 decode steps. Overlay is `--quantization-config` PTPC `o_proj` only.

Kimi-K3 mix in this window: **69 KDA / 24 MLA** → 3450 KDA launches (`69 × 50`).

### Unfused

Gated RMSNorm and per-token quant are still two launches.

| Kernel | Calls | CUDA avg | CUDA total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `layer_norm_gated_fwd_kernel.kd` | 3450 | 4.375 µs | 15.094 ms |
| `dynamic_per_token_scaled_quant` | 4650 | 4.086 µs | 18.998 ms |

The 4650 quant launches are **3450 KDA + 1200 MLA**. KDA-only epilogue ≈ **8.5 µs** (4.4 + 4.1).

### Fused (this PR)

Gated RMSNorm and per-token quant are one launch.

| Kernel | Calls | CUDA avg | CUDA total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `_rmsnorm_gated_fp8_per_token_kernel.kd` | 3450 | 4.221 µs | 14.561 ms |
| `layer_norm_gated_fwd_kernel.kd` | **0** | — | — |
| `dynamic_per_token_scaled_quant` | **0** | — | — |

KDA epilogue **8.5 → 4.2 µs** (−4.3 µs / KDA layer, ~**0.30 ms/step** × 69 KDA).

## Accuracy

8×MI355X, TP8, DSpark MTP (`num_speculative_tokens=2`). Same recipe as the fused PTPC KDA `o_proj` path (this change). Full GSM8K, 1,319 examples, `lm_eval` 5-shot (`local-completions`). No unfused PTPC pair in this run.

| Tasks | Version | Filter | n-shot | Metric |  | Value |  | Stderr |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| gsm8k | 3 | flexible-extract | 5 | exact_match | ↑ | 0.9613 | ± | 0.0053 |
|  |  | strict-match | 5 | exact_match | ↑ | 0.9621 | ± | 0.0053 |

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 \
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8888 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --language-model-only \
  --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"FLASH_ATTN"}' \
  --quantization-config '{"linear":"fp8_per_channel","ignore":["re:(?!.*self_attn\\.o_proj$).*"]}' \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":2,"method":"dspark","attention_backend":"TRITON_MLA","kv_cache_dtype":"auto","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}'

pip install --quiet 'lm_eval[api]==0.4.12'
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1/completions,tokenized_requests=False,trust_remote_code=True,num_concurrent=8,max_gen_toks=8192,timeout=3600 \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --seed 1234
```

## Tests

- `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_oproj_ptpc.py` — fused vs sequential; `per_token_fp8_quant` vs already-normed (`fused_kda_decode` path).
- Overlay self-check (CPU torch fallback, no GPU): `rmsnorm_gated_fp8_per_token` matches sequential gated RMSNorm + per-token amax (`scale` exact, dequant atol/rtol 1e-3). All `self.o_norm(...)` sites stay behind `if not _o_proj_is_ptpc_fp8(...)` so PTPC does not double-norm.

title: [Perf][MLA Sparse] Pin req_id_per_token before non_blocking H2D on XPU and ROCm
body:
## Summary

Route the two `buffer.copy_(torch.from_numpy(...), non_blocking=True)` sites on the sparse-MLA metadata path through `np_to_pinned_tensor` so the copy source is pinned:

- `XPUMLASparseMetadataBuilder.build` `req_id_per_token_buffer`
- ROCm AITER sparse MLA metadata builder `req_id_per_token_buffer`

## Context

Same class of stall #53491 adds a stricter check for: `torch.from_numpy(...)` returns a pageable CPU tensor, and `buffer.copy_(src, non_blocking=True)` with a pageable source is silently staged by the CUDA driver and blocks the host. Continues the sweep in #54266, #54292, #54293.

## Note on the alternative approach

The CUDA sparse backends (flashinfer / flashattn / flashmla) already build `req_id_per_token` on device via `CommonAttentionMetadata.token_to_req_indices`, avoiding the numpy pipeline entirely. Converging XPU and ROCm onto the same path is the more principled fix but a larger refactor. This PR just pins the source of the existing H2D so it stays async; happy to follow up with the refactor if reviewers prefer.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs for `xpu_mla_sparse in:body`, `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse in:body`, `req_id_per_token pin`, and `#53491 in:body`. None open.

## Testing

- `.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/xpu_mla_sparse.py vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` — passed (ruff, mypy, typos, SPDX, etc.)

No available XPU or ROCm hardware to run the runtime path end-to-end; the change is a pattern swap to an existing helper with no semantic drift. Once #53491 lands its runtime checker, this becomes CI-enforced on any test that exercises these builders.

AI assistance was used for code search and drafting; every line was reviewed by the submitter.

(see "Works on 0.27" below). Hardware: 4x NVIDIA B200 (SM100), driver 580.x, CUDA toolkit 13.0. ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary On vLLM 0.28.0, serving a DSA sparse-attention model (GLM-5.3, `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) with `--decode-context-parallel-size > 1` crashes during engine startup with: ``` AttributeError: 'FlashInferMLASparseMetadata' object has no attribute 'decode' ``` at `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py:961` (`forward_impl`: `if attn_metadata.decode is not None`). **This is a regression from 0.27.** The identical model, hardware, and flags boot and serve correctly on vLLM 0.27.0, including with MTP speculative decoding. The same config family (MTP + DCP + fp8 KV) also ran in production for ~a month on GLM-5.2 (same `GlmMoeDsa` architecture) on the pre-0.28 lineage. The crash fires on the **first decode-shaped batch**, regardless of which subsystem builds it. I isolated it across three axes — none avoids it: | Variant | Result | |---|---| | DCP=4, **no speculative config**, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | crashes in target-model CUDA graph capture (`capture_model → _dummy_run`) | | DCP=4, MTP spec decode (`num_speculative_tokens=5`) | crashes in MTP draft step (`speculator.propose`) | | DCP=4, MTP, `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` | same crash | | DCP=4, no spec, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` (legacy runner) | same crash, via `determine_available_memory → profile_cudagraph_memory` | | **DCP removed** (everything else identical) | boots and serves correctly on 0.28 | | **vLLM 0.27.0**, DCP=4 + MTP (identical flags) | boots and serves correctly | So: not runner-specific, not cudagraph-mode-specific, not spec-decode-specific. Root cause appears to be that `FlashInferMLASparseMetadata` does not implement the unified MLA metadata interface (`.decode`) that the DCP branch of `mla_attention.forward_impl` requires. Prefill-shaped batches work (the initial profiling run completes); any decode-shaped metadata hits the missing attribute. Likely related: #50064 reports the sibling class `ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadata` missing `num_decode_tokens` on GLM-5.2/MI300X — same bug family (sparse-MLA metadata classes not implementing the unified MLA metadata interface). ## Reproduction Model: GLM-5.3 NVFP4 (ModelOpt) — I used `incoai/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`; the crash is in metadata handling, not weights, and #50064 suggests it reproduces with official checkpoints of any `glm_moe_dsa` model. ```bash vllm serve /path/to/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --decode-context-parallel-size 4 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --max-model-len 1048576 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --enable-chunked-prefill \ --enable-prefix-caching ``` (No speculative config needed — the target model's own warmup/graph capture is sufficient to crash. Adding `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'` crashes earlier, in the draft path, with the same error.) Remove `--decode-context-parallel-size 4` → boots and serves. title: [Bug]: Direct DCP A2A crashes on GLM sparse-MLA strided output
body:
### Your current environment
Relevant python vllm/collect_env.py output ```text OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : 13.3.0 Python version : 3.12.3 PyTorch version : 2.13.0 CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.3 CUDA runtime version : 13.3.73 Nvidia driver version : 595.58.03 GPU 0: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU 1: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU 2: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU 3: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition vLLM Version : 0.1.dev20111+g7f1e92bec.d20260827 NCCL version : 2.31.2 GPU topology : four PHB-connected GPUs, one NUMA node ``` The image was built from local-inference-lab/vllm `7f1e92bec`; I also confirmed that official `main` at `7fd9cc036` selects the direct workspace without checking the runtime output/LSE layout in `MLADCPManager._direct_workspace_combine`.
### 🐛 Describe the bug Automatic direct symmetric-memory DCP A2A selection crashes during CUDA-graph capture when an MLA attention backend returns a valid capacity-strided/head-major output view rather than packed token-major heads. The generic `dcp_a2a_lse_reduce` path supports this layout through its stride-aware pack kernel, but the direct path calls the C++ kernel unconditionally. Observed configuration: - GLM-5.3-Flash sparse MLA, BF16 output, NVFP4 MLA KV cache - tensor parallel 4, decode context parallel 4, A2A backend - 64 total attention heads, head dimension 512 - full and piecewise CUDA graphs; capture sizes through 32 - `VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A` unset, so automatic selection enables the direct workspace The launch fails while capturing the first graph: ```text RuntimeError: partial output must have packed heads and an aligned token stride ``` Instrumenting the Python dispatch immediately before the direct call showed: ```text output strides: (512, 1572864, 1) LSE strides: (64, 1) ``` The C++ operator requires `partial_output.stride(1) == head_dim` and `stride(0) >= total_heads * head_dim`, so this valid backend view cannot use the direct kernel. The generic A2A implementation accepts it because `_dcp_a2a_pack_send_kernel` receives and uses all output/LSE strides. Two workarounds both serve correctly: 1. `VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A=0`, which disables the direct path globally. 2. A Python layout gate that uses direct A2A only for its supported packed-head layout and otherwise calls `dcp_a2a_lse_reduce`. I validated workaround 2 on the same four-GPU server with direct selection still enabled. Startup completed, the log recorded the exact layout fallback above, and an end-to-end serving gate passed: - three short correctness probes - strict JSON-schema output with reasoning - exact 32,853-token prompt - 3/3 needle retrieval at depths 0.15, 0.55, and 0.90 Expected behavior: automatic direct selection should preserve correctness for attention backends whose output layout is unsupported by the direct kernel. It should fall back to generic NCCL A2A for that invocation, just as the current code already falls back when token count exceeds direct-workspace capacity. Proposed fix: mirror the direct C++ tensor shape/stride contract in a small allocation-free Python predicate inside `_direct_workspace_combine`; dispatch to the direct workspace only when both capacity and layout are supported. Add CPU dispatch tests for padded packed token-major input and capacity-strided head-major input. Duplicate search: I searched open and closed issues for the exact error and searched open PRs for direct-DCP layout fallback. I found the originating direct-A2A work (#48897 / merged #50484) and related KV-layout work (#52239), but no report or change covering output/LSE layout fallback.

title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash (glm5next) — recurring CUDA illegal memory access on 4xB200, surfacing in three unrelated kernels (KDA linear-attention, MHC TileLang, TRT-LLM fused MoE)
body:
### Your current environment

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash-x86_64-cu130` (`sha256:2e771fa615452282cc331eb418b3ef21636fce355bea0491fca89e6d362ab703`, published 2026-08-26 — the newest `glm53-flash` tag on Docker Hub)
- `vllm.__version__` = `0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187`
- tilelang 0.1.12
- 4x NVIDIA B200 (SM100), TP=4, driver healthy: 0 uncorrected ECC, no pending page retirement, no Xid, `Remapping Failure Occurred: No` on all 4 GPUs
- Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`)

Note this model is not upstream yet (#53906 is open), so this is filed against the day-0 image.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The engine dies with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` → `EngineDeadError`, repeatedly, under ordinary production chat traffic. Five crashes over ~6 hours, at 22 min / 10 min / 47 min / 2 h 34 min / 62 min of uptime. Before this the same box ran **15.5 h without a crash**, so it is load/state dependent rather than a startup or config error.

**The distinguishing detail: the fault surfaces in three completely unrelated kernel families, and different TP ranks of the same crash report different kernels.**

| Crash | Time (UTC) | Uptime | Faulting frame |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2026-08-28 22:48:48 | 22 min | `glm5next/nvidia/kda.py:581 _forward` → `flash_linear_attention/ops/kda.py:1576 chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` → `:1488 _fwd` → `ops/index.py:27 prepare_chunk_indices` |
| 2 | 2026-08-28 23:08:46 | 10 min | `glm5next/nvidia/model.py:558 hc_fused_post_pre` → `layers/mhc.py:409 forward_cuda` → `kernels/mhc/tilelang.py:635 mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang` → `tilelang/jit/kernel.py:202` |
| 3 | 2026-08-29 00:18:55 | 47 min | same as #2 (`mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang`) |
| 4 | 2026-08-29 02:58:08 | 2 h 34 min | **mixed per rank**: 3 ranks `mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang` / `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang` (TileLang, `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`); 1 rank `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` (`kda.py:581`, Triton) |
| 5 | 2026-08-29 05:04:08 | 62 min (PDL disabled — see below) | **mixed per rank**: TRT-LLM fused MoE `trtllm_fused_moe_dev_kernel.cu:991` on all 4 ranks; `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` (Triton) also reported |

Because the errors are asynchronous, we read these as *where the fault surfaced*, not where it originated — `prepare_chunk_indices` calls `.tolist()`, which forces the sync that reports crash #1. Two unrelated victims suggests a single upstream corrupter (most likely in the linear-attention/state path) that other kernels then trip over.

### Serve command

```
vllm serve /workspace/models/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --served-model-name glm-5.3-flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 524288 --max-num-seqs 1024 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.94 --enable-prefix-caching \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 --enable-prompt-tokens-details
```
`max_num_batched_tokens=16384` (default). No MTP, no LMCache, no `--mamba-cache-mode`.
Traffic is ordinary `/v1/chat/completions` (~95%) plus `/v1/responses` (~5%), 4–23 concurrent.

### What we ruled out

- **Hardware** — 0 ECC/Xid/page-retirement on all 4 GPUs.
- **Disk / JIT cache corruption** — 291 GB free.
- **Host RAM** — 48 of 1996 GB used.
- **A new client or changed workload** — same client IPs before and after the stable period.
- **`--mamba-cache-mode align`** — removed it (it is LMCache-only and LMCache was not running); crashed again at 47 min.
- **TileLang JIT-during-inference.** The JIT monitor does warn (`TileLang JIT compilation during inference: mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang`) and glm5next has **no mHC warmup module** — `model_executor/warmup/` covers DSv4, Kimi-K3, Qwen and MiniMax but not glm5next, so the DSv4 warmup work (#52941, #51802, #49707, #50178) does not cover this model. **But we correlated compile timestamps against all three crashes and found none nearby** — every compile happens in the first seconds after startup. So missing warmup is a real latency gap here, but it is not this crash.
- **`cu_seqlens` int32→int64 (`878631b60`, "normalize GDN sequence offsets")** — does not apply: that fix is in `fi_chunk_gated_delta_rule` (Qwen GDN + FlashInfer), and the glm5next KDA path is pure FLA Triton and never calls it. PR head's own `glm5next/nvidia/kda.py` has no such cast and `gdn_attn.py` remains int32.

### A failed workaround worth recording

Routing `MHCFusedPostPreOp.forward_cuda` to `self.forward_native(...)` — mirroring what `forward_hip` already does when `HAS_TILELANG_MHC` is false — **produces garbage output**, e.g.

```
', in inin fenslin green tit correct correctver in correctsenswald verververver that-n anglever thatv'
```

and runs ~6x slower. So on CUDA the torch decomposition in `MHCFusedPostPreOp.forward_native` does not appear to be numerically equivalent to `mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang`. That may be worth a separate look, given `forward_hip` relies on that same fallback for gfx942 (where TileLang MHC is already disabled for "incorrect results").

Also note `MHCFusedPostPreOp.enabled()` returns `True` unconditionally, so `-O.custom_ops=-mhc_fused_post_pre` cannot disable this op — there is no supported way to route around the TileLang kernel on CUDA.

### Code-review observation (mixed batches take the chunk path unpeeled)

`GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder` builds chunk metadata from a *prefill-only, rebased* `cu_seqlens`
and states the invariant explicitly (`gdn_attn.py`):

```python
# In a mixed non-spec batch, decodes are peeled off to the recurrent kernel (decode-first
# front slice), so build chunk metadata from the rebased prefill-only cu_seqlens; otherwise
# use the full non-spec one. _forward_core keys off the same condition, so they agree.
prefill_query_start_loc = non_spec_query_start_loc[num_decodes:] - num_decode_tokens
prefill_state_indices   = non_spec_state_indices_tensor[num_decodes:]
```

`Glm5NextKDA._forward` does **not** peel decodes. It branches `if num_prefills > 0: <chunk path>`
/ `elif num_decodes > 0: <recurrent path>`, so whenever a batch contains **both** decodes and
prefills, every non-spec token — including the 1-token decode sequences — goes through
`chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` with the **full, non-rebased** `cu_seqlens` and the full
`non_spec_state_indices_tensor`. `qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py`, which the builder was written
against, does peel them.

This is benign for the precomputed metadata itself: nothing in `glm5next/` reads
`chunk_indices`/`chunk_offsets`/`prefill_state_indices` (only `qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py` does), and
`chunk_kda_with_fused_gate_fwd` recomputes `prepare_chunk_indices(cu_seqlens, ...)` internally. So
the stale-metadata path is not the bug.

What we cannot rule out is the shape distribution: glm5next drives the chunked-prefill kernel with
batches containing many length-1 sequences interleaved with long prefills, which the builder's own
comment says should never reach that kernel. Is the unpeeled mixed batch intended for this model?

⚠️ To be clear about what this is NOT: we checked the base rate before reading anything into it.
Over 6,897 engine throughput samples on this box, prefill is active in **85.9%** of steps and
mixed batches (prefill AND decode both non-zero) are likewise **85.9%**. All four crashes occurred
during mixed batches, but at that base rate that is p ≈ 0.54 — no signal. Likewise both KDA
crashes landed in `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` (prefill) and neither in `fused_recurrent_kda`
(decode), but since glm5next takes the chunk path whenever `num_prefills > 0`, that kernel is live
in ~86% of steps versus ~14% for the recurrent one, so 2/2 is p ≈ 0.74 — also pure exposure.
**There is no prefill-vs-decode signal in our data.** The mixed-batch question above is raised on
the strength of the code divergence alone, not on any observed correlation.

(We also checked and ruled out a stale-`@tensor_cache` theory for `prepare_chunk_indices`: the
identity-keyed cache cannot go stale here because `input_batch.py` hands out
`input_buffers.query_start_loc[: num_reqs + 1]`, a fresh slice object each step.)

### Tested and falsified: PDL trigger-before-store in the mamba ops

Per PDL semantics, memory operations executed **after** `cudaTriggerProgrammaticLaunchCompletion`
are not guaranteed visible to a dependent grid past its `cudaGridDependencySynchronize`. The mamba
Triton ops fire the trigger at the **top of the kernel, before their loads and stores**:

```python
# gather_initial_states.py / scatter_states.py / causal_conv1d.py (launch_pdl=is_arch_support_pdl())
if launch_pdl:
    tl.extra.cuda.gdc_wait()
    tl.extra.cuda.gdc_launch_dependents()   # <-- trigger fired here
...
values = tl.load(...)                        # loads and stores happen AFTER the trigger
tl.store(...)
```

so a PDL-launched consumer can legally observe stale memory. (The MHC TileLang kernels do it
correctly — `T.pdl_sync()` at entry, `T.pdl_trigger()` after stores — but `mhc_pre_big_fuse`
reads its GEMM inputs immediately after `pdl_sync`, with the prenorm GEMM's trigger placement
inside the vendored library.) Since `is_arch_support_pdl()` is `major >= 9`, this code path is
live only on Hopper/Blackwell — consistent with a B200-only, intermittent, timing-dependent
fault whose reporters are simply the most frequently launched error-checking kernels (KDA chunk:
34/45 layers; MHC: every layer — matching the per-rank reporter mix with no phase signal). A related
latent defect: `_scatter_states_kernel` performs an unguarded `tl.store` at
`state_ptr + state_idx * stride`, with no NULL_BLOCK_ID check, where its decode-side counterpart
(`fused_recurrent.py`) explicitly guards `state_idx <= 0` on load and `> 0` on store.

**Tested: crash #5 occurred with `is_arch_support_pdl()` forced to `False`** (verified live in
the worker interpreter), at 62 minutes uptime, same `an illegal memory access`. Reporter this
time was the TRT-LLM fused MoE (`trtllm_fused_moe_dev_kernel.cu:991`, all 4 ranks) alongside KDA
on another rank — a third distinct reporting site, further confirming the fault is asynchronous
and upstream of every reporter. The trigger-before-store placement and the unguarded
`_scatter_states_kernel` store remain latent defects worth fixing, but they are not this bug.

### Structured output: present in all crash batches, but base-rate-neutral

All 3 crashes that produced a `dump_input` SchedulerOutput show
`has_structured_output_requests=true` with live xgrammar `json_object` requests — however we
then measured the base rate and **98.4% of this deployment's arrivals are structured**, so that
is exposure, not signal. One anomaly stands on its own: the only two
`backend_xgrammar.py:166 Failed to advance FSM ... tokens [154827]` errors in the log each
preceded a crash by 13–24 minutes; a grammar rejecting a token it should have masked to `-inf`
suggests the bitmask occasionally fails to apply — possibly the same corruption surfacing
non-fatally.

### Ask

Is there a known memory-safety issue in the glm5next KDA / mHC path on SM100? We have per-crash snapshots (full worker tracebacks, `nvidia-smi -q`, metrics, in-flight request shapes) and can run targeted instrumentation on the box — happy to attach anything useful.

title: [Prefix Cache] Support fine-grained SWA hits
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #53786 by allowing `SlidingWindowManager` to participate in fine-grained hybrid prefix-cache lookup when its physical KV page is larger than the configured hash unit.

The worker-facing block table remains physical-page based. This change only makes prefix endpoints hash-granular:

- register the producer's last prompt boundary inside an SWA page through the existing `BlockPool.cache_partial_block` primitive;
- scan sparse fine-boundary endpoints right-to-left, apply an EAGLE/MTP drop of one hash unit, and validate every physical page intersecting the resulting sliding window;
- return null-padded physical block lists, preserving global page indices;
- retain the exact reachable physical span under sparse retention, including the speculative endpoint page when EAGLE/MTP proves a boundary across a page;
- reuse the existing partial-hit copy-on-write path when resuming inside an SWA page;
- if fine cross-manager reconciliation loses a usable Mamba/EAGLE checkpoint,
  retry at the scheduler-page boundary and keep the longer reconciled result.

This is deliberately narrower than the adjacent work:

- #50457 represents an all-sliding DFlash group as full attention when prefix caching is enabled; this PR supports fine lookup in `SlidingWindowManager` itself.
- #53945/#53614 add Mamba resume checkpoints. They may still be required for a hybrid common hit to survive fixed-point reconciliation, but are not SWA page-table changes.
- #53670 and the DFlash/DSpark classification changes in #54165 concern whether/where the speculative last unit is dropped. This PR preserves the drop and reduces its unit to the shared hash boundary for fine-capable SWA.

No kernel/page-alignment workaround is needed: all returned block IDs and CoW
copies remain physical pages. The coarse fallback preserves checkpoint + tail
replay when Mamba state cannot resume at a fine boundary; internal Mamba
checkpoints remain separate follow-up work.

AI assistance was used to inspect related work, draft the implementation and tests, and prepare this description. The contributor must review every changed line and run the reported commands before submission, per `AGENTS.md`.

## Test Plan

```bash
uvx ruff format --check \
  vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py \
  vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py
uvx ruff check \
  vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py \
  vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core -q
```

Single-H20 validation performed:

- cold producer vs identical warm consumer at several prompt lengths;
- deterministic output-token comparison and cached-token/TTFT measurements;
- manager/CUDA smoke coverage for interior-page eviction, sparse retention,
  physical-page validation, and copy-on-write;
- resolved geometry: hash unit 16, SWA physical page 816 tokens, window 2048,
  with the target's auto-aligned Mamba checkpoint geometry.

Multi-GPU TP/DCP/PCP geometry is follow-up validation and is not inferred from a TP=1 run.

## Test Result

- Focused manager/prefix suite: **146 passed**.
- Ruff format/check and `git diff --check`: **passed**.
- Full `tests/v1/core` source-only run: **562 passed**, with one failure and
  five collection/setup errors. Three fixture errors pass when run with the
  repository root `conftest.py` (**3 passed**); the remaining failure and two
  errors are CPU engine E2E tests that cannot initialize because this checkout
  has no compiled `vllm._C` extension (`init_cpu_memory_env` is unavailable).
  None reaches the changed manager code.
- Single-H20 manager/CUDA smoke: **passed** on vLLM `0.28.0+cu129` and
  PyTorch `2.13.0+cu129`. This covered fine lookup, physical span validation,
  EAGLE cross-page fallback, interior-page eviction, sparse retention, and the
  actual CUDA physical-page CoW operation.
- Single-H20 serving completed with a Qwen3.8 FP8 target and a five-layer
  DFlash SWA draft geometry. The unpatched coarse path hit 4,896/6K tokens;
  fine-only reconciliation regressed to zero; the final fallback restored the
  4,896-token hit and matching output hash. This confirms that Mamba internal
  checkpoints are still required for finer end-to-end EAGLE hits.

title: [Bugfix][Speculative decoding] Name the controlling CLI flags in max_num_scheduled_tokens validation
body:
## What & why
Closes #50708.

When speculative decoding is enabled, `_set_max_num_scheduled_tokens` can
reject a config while only reporting a derived token count. A user hitting
this sees a negative/zero `max_num_scheduled_tokens` with no path back to the
knobs that produced it. This change makes the `ValueError`/warning report the
derived budget and name the user-facing CLI flags that control it
(`--max-num-batched-tokens`, `--num-speculative-tokens`), so the failure is
actionable.

Behavior is unchanged for valid configs; only the messages and the new
regression tests change.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR
I ran the mandatory duplicate-work checks:
- `gh issue view 50708 --comments` -> no linked/claimed fix.
- `gh pr list --state open --search "50708 in:body"` -> none.
- `gh pr list --state open --search "max_num_scheduled_tokens speculative error"` -> only unrelated PRs (#44566 derives num_speculative_tokens from a speculator draft config; #41834 is SM12x DeepSeek V4). Neither touches this validator.

No open PR addresses #50708, so this is not duplicate work.

## Tests
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the changed files: passed.
- New unit tests in `tests/test_config.py`:
  - `test_speculative_scheduled_tokens_error_names_flags`
  - `test_speculative_scheduled_tokens_warning_names_flags`

To run:
```
uv venv --python 3.12 && source .venv/bin/activate
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto
uv pip install -r requirements/test/cuda.in
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py::test_speculative_scheduled_tokens_error_names_flags tests/test_config.py::test_speculative_scheduled_tokens_warning_names_flags -v
```
Note: I could not run these locally (macOS, no CUDA; `flashinfer` CUDA-only
wheels). They are CPU-only config-validation tests and run in CI.

## Model evaluation
N/A — this only changes a config-validation `ValueError`/`warning` message.
No model output, accuracy, or serving behavior is affected, so no eval is
required.

## AI assistance
This change was produced with AI assistance (Open Discovery agent). I have
reviewed every changed line and the added tests.

title: [Bugfix] Stop advertising fp8_e5m2 where the KV writer stores e4m3
body:
## Overview

`triton_reshape_and_cache_flash` stores an e4m3 variant for every fp8 cache dtype, but
`TRITON_ATTN` and `ROCM_ATTN` advertise `fp8_e5m2`, and the readers decode that cache as
`torch.float8_e5m2`. The cache therefore holds e4m3 bits read back as e5m2, and the model
produces garbage with no error. This PR stops advertising `fp8_e5m2` on those two backends and
refuses it in the writer.

## Claims

- **Bug:** `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2` on `TRITON_ATTN` (any block size) and on `ROCM_ATTN`
  (block sizes other than 16/32) silently stores e4m3 bits. On `ROCM_ATTN` with block size
  16/32 the C++ writer refuses e5m2 with a `RuntimeError`, so the same request either fails or
  produces garbage depending only on the block size.
- **Root cause:** the writer stores `current_platform.fp8_dtype()`, which is `float8_e4m3fn`
  or `float8_e4m3fnuz` on every platform. `chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py` and
  `prefix_prefill.py` decode `fp8_e5m2` as `torch.float8_e5m2`.
- **Fix:** remove `fp8_e5m2` from `TritonAttentionBackend` and `RocmAttentionBackend`
  `supported_kv_cache_dtypes`, and return `False` for it in `_is_supported_kv_cache_dtype`.
  `fp8` and `fp8_e4m3`, the format the kernel actually stores, are unchanged.

## Validation

Unit test (CPU only):

```bash
pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_triton_kv_writer_fp8_format.py
```

| environment | without this PR | with this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.30.0`, MI250 (gfx90a) | 2 failed, 3 passed | 5 passed |
| vLLM nightly `0.28.1rc1.dev87`, RTX 4090 (SM89), 2026-08-29 | 2 failed, 3 passed | 5 passed |

On the v0.30.0 image the installed vLLM files were checked byte-identical to the `v0.30.0` tag,
then this PR's diff was applied to them for the "with this PR" column and removed again; the
reverted run returned to 2 failed, 3 passed.

The two failing tests are `test_e5m2_is_refused_by_the_writer` and
`test_backends_do_not_advertise_a_format_the_writer_refuses`. The three that pass on both sides
are controls: the kernel still stores an e4m3 variant, unquantized dtypes are unaffected, and
both backends still advertise `fp8` and `fp8_e4m3`.

End to end on the same image: Qwen3-0.6B, bfloat16, greedy, `max_tokens=16`, prompt
`"The capital of France is"`. The default selection picks `ROCM_ATTN` ("Overriding with ROCM_ATTN
out of potential backends: ['ROCM_ATTN', 'TRITON_ATTN']"), which uses the C++ writer for block
sizes 16/32 and the Triton writer otherwise.

| `--kv-cache-dtype` | block 64 (Triton writer) | block 16 (C++ writer) | with this PR, both block sizes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fp8_e4m3` | `' Paris. The capital of Italy is Rome. …'` | | unchanged |
| `fp8_e5m2` | **`' Parislocklocklocklocklocklock…'`**, no error | `RuntimeError` in `reshape_and_cache` | `ValueError: No valid attention backend found for rocm …` at startup |

<details>
<summary>Bytes in the cache, and the other cache dtypes (vLLM 0.26.0, gfx90a)</summary>

For the `fp8_e5m2` run, 0.0% of the stored bytes are non-finite when read as e4m3, and the
byte statistics match the `fp8_e4m3` run: the cache holds e4m3 values under an e5m2 label.
Read back as e5m2, `[1.0, 2.0, 3.5, 0.25]` becomes `[0.5, 2.0, 6.0, 0.03125]`.

All 15 `CacheDType` values were run at block 16 and block 64 with the same model and prompt.
`fp8_e5m2` is the only one whose result depends on the writer:

- correct at both writers: `auto`, `fp8`, `fp8_e4m3`, `turboquant_k8v4`, `int8_per_token_head`
- refused at both: `fp8_inc`, `fp8_ds_mla`, `nvfp4`, `nvfp4_4over6`
- the same quantisation loss at both: `turboquant_4bit_nc`, `turboquant_k3v4_nc`,
  `turboquant_3bit_nc`, `int4_per_token_head`, `fp8_per_token_head`
</details>

## Details

- **Why refuse instead of convert:** no e5m2 store exists in this kernel. Adding one is a
  larger change; #49077 shows the cost of a software fp8 conversion for one format.
- **#49077** (open) edits the same function and the same assert message to add an
  `fp8`/`fp8_e4m3` arm for pre-SM89 GPUs. It does not cover `fp8_e5m2`. The two PRs will
  conflict textually; whichever lands second keeps both arms.
- **Scope:** `_is_supported_kv_cache_dtype` gates only this writer. The per-token-head and
  DiffKV writers have their own paths, and neither DiffKV backend accepts `fp8_e5m2` on `main`.
- **Not a duplicate:** on 2026-10-03, and again on 2026-10-05, I searched open and merged PRs and issues for `fp8_e5m2`,
  `e5m2`, `triton_reshape_and_cache_flash` and `_is_supported_kv_cache_dtype`. #54811, #56198
  and #58128 each state in their descriptions that they do not cover this. `main`
  (`34051ad714`) and v0.31.0 still advertise `fp8_e5m2` on both backends.
- **Limitations:** end to end measured on gfx90a only; the unit test also ran on SM89.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change and to run the measurements above. I reviewed
every changed line.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Avoid prefill metadata JIT during inference
body:
## Purpose

Prevent `BuildPrefillChunkMetadataKernel` from compiling a new Triton variant during the first real sparse-MLA prefill.

The existing compile-only warmup leaves two gaps:

- request slice and decode-context-parallel scalar values are part of the compile key even though they do not change the algorithm;
- Triton's compile-only `kernel.warmup()` does not populate the in-process `JITFunction.run` cache used by the first real launch.

This change:

- marks `query_slice_start`, `query_slice_stop`, `DCP_RANK`, `DCP_WORLD`, and `DCP_INTERLEAVE` as non-specialized runtime scalars and removes them from `CompileKey`;
- includes the GLM pooled-selector `index_kpool` compression ratio in warmup keys;
- executes one valid metadata row for each compression-ratio and pointer-alignment key after compile-only warmup;
- lets an explicitly configured `B12X_MLA_SPARSE` backend select the early warmup even before attention groups are available, while preserving `DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER` selection.

Related to the broader warmup migration in #50175 and zero-runtime-JIT tracking in #49349. Field findings were first recorded in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50175#issuecomment-5461508640; this PR is a focused fix against current `main`.

## Test Plan

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_sparse_mla_triton_warmup.py
python3 -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py \
  -k 'indexer_warmup or metadata_runtime_scalars'
python3 -m py_compile \
  vllm/model_executor/warmup/sparse_mla_triton_warmup.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_sparse_mla_triton_warmup.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py
```

Run a fresh-cache four-worker sparse-MLA server with verbose JIT monitoring, then exercise deterministic short generation, strict structured output, a 32,933-token three-needle prompt, and 32K/128K prefill requests.

## Test Result

- Configured-backend warmup test: `1 passed`.
- Compression-ratio and scalar-specialization tests: `3 passed`.
- Python compilation and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Four RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell workers each logged four sparse-MLA metadata runtime variants warmed.
- Short generation, structured output, and all three long-context needles passed.
- 32K and 128K prefill requests completed.
- No `BuildPrefillChunkMetadataKernel` inference-time JIT warning appeared after the change.

title: [Kimi K3] Support sequence parallelism with pipeline parallelism
body:
## Purpose

Enable Kimi K3 model-level sequence parallelism (SP) when pipeline parallelism (PP) is also enabled. This lets the DeepGEMM MegaMoE path run with the production TP8/PP2/EP8 topology instead of disabling SP whenever PP > 1.

The implementation keeps tokens sequence-sharded across a PP boundary:

- Select SP for Kimi K3 when EP is enabled, TP > 1, and the MoE backend is `deep_gemm_mega_moe`, including PP > 1. Non-MegaMoE behavior is unchanged.
- The first PP stage shards the embedded tokens. Later PP stages consume the already-local `hidden_states` and `residual` rows instead of sharding them a second time.
- Add a model-specific PP transport override for `hidden_states` and `residual`. The default PP optimization assumes TP-replicated tensors and reconstructs them with a TP all-gather on the receiver. SP tensors are distinct across TP ranks, so matching TP ranks now send their shards directly without that all-gather.
- Preserve the received local leading dimension in the V2 and legacy GPU model runners. Full-sized persistent buffers are still used for profiling and CUDA graph capture, then narrowed exactly once inside the model.
- Record the non-last-PP output row count per CUDA graph descriptor so replay returns an SP-local `IntermediateTensors` view.
- Delegate the transport override through the multimodal Kimi K3 wrapper and add focused tests for backend selection, PP-stage shard handling, and PP transport behavior.

### Performance-sensitive details

- Attention still gathers the full token sequence at the start of each layer; the O-projection/GEMM-RS returns the local shard. MoE, shared-expert work, and PP activation transport remain sequence-sharded.
- Avoiding full-token reconstruction at the PP boundary removes an otherwise redundant TP all-gather and prevents a second SP split on the receiving stage.
- CUDA graph and runtime PP buffers use the actual local row count. Sending a full capture buffer would erase the communication benefit and break replay shapes.
- The first unseen short-prompt concurrency shape can incur a one-time 6--10-second MegaMoE preparation cost. The benchmark below warms at least one complete target-concurrency wave before collecting three measured waves.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

```bash
pytest -q tests/models/kimi_k3/test_sequence_parallel.py \
  -k "not sharded_sequence_parallel_mlp_matches_replicated"
```

Result: `30 passed, 1 deselected`. The nine newly added parameterized cases all pass.

### Two-node serving

Run the following command on both 8xB200 nodes. Set `NODE_RANK=0` on the first node and `NODE_RANK=1` plus `HEADLESS=--headless` on the second node.

```bash
export MODEL=/path/to/Kimi-K3
export MASTER_ADDR=<rank-0-host>
export HOST_IP=<this-host>
export NODE_RANK=<0-or-1>
export HEADLESS=<empty-or---headless>

PYTHONPATH=/path/to/DeepGEMM \
VLLM_HOST_IP="$HOST_IP" \
VLLM_KIMI_K3_SHARD_SP_SHARED_EXPERT=1 \
VLLM_KIMI_K3_GEMM_RS=1 \
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 \
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --served-model-name Kimi-K3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 1048576 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.84 \
  --load-format fastsafetensors \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --attention-config '{"use_prefill_query_quantization":true,"mla_prefill_backend":"flashinfer"}' \
  --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8691 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --nnodes 2 \
  --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --master-addr "$MASTER_ADDR" \
  --master-port 29991 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend deepep_v2 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 128 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' \
  $HEADLESS
```

For the FI+EP baseline, remove `--kernel-config`. For the FI/no-EP baseline, also remove `--enable-expert-parallel` and `--all2all-backend deepep_v2`. All other arguments remain identical.

### Prefill benchmark

Output length is fixed at one token, so total-token throughput is effectively prefill throughput.

```bash
run_point() {
  input_len="$1"
  concurrency="$2"
  warmups=4
  if ((concurrency > warmups)); then warmups="$concurrency"; fi

  vllm bench serve \
    --backend openai-chat \
    --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8691 \
    --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
    --model Kimi-K3 \
    --tokenizer "$MODEL" \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len "$input_len" \
    --random-output-len 1 \
    --random-range-ratio 0 \
    --num-prompts $((concurrency * 3)) \
    --num-warmups "$warmups" \
    --request-rate inf \
    --max-concurrency "$concurrency" \
    --ignore-eos \
    --temperature 0 \
    --percentile-metrics ttft,e2el \
    --metric-percentiles 50,90,95,99 \
    --seed 2026
}

for c in 1 8 32 64 128; do run_point 128 "$c"; done
for c in 1 2 4 8; do run_point 8192 "$c"; done
run_point 32768 1
```

## Test Results

Hardware: 2 nodes x 8 B200, TP8/PP2, EP8 where enabled. Serving limits are `max_num_seqs=128` and `max_num_batched_tokens=32768`. Every arm completed 747 measured requests with zero failures.

### Total token throughput

| Input | Concurrency | FI/no-EP tok/s | FI+EP tok/s | MegaMoE+SP tok/s | Mega vs FI+EP | Mega vs no-EP |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 128 | 1 | 962 | 1,025 | 1,381 | +34.7% | +43.5% |
| 128 | 8 | 3,529 | 3,791 | 4,840 | +27.7% | +37.2% |
| 128 | 32 | 12,401 | 12,963 | 20,346 | +57.0% | +64.1% |
| 128 | 64 | 19,472 | 18,044 | 26,332 | +45.9% | +35.2% |
| 128 | 128 | 22,291 | 21,757 | 31,118 | +43.0% | +39.6% |
| 8192 | 1 | 20,450 | 19,769 | 27,859 | +40.9% | +36.2% |
| 8192 | 2 | 22,518 | 21,658 | 30,634 | +41.4% | +36.0% |
| 8192 | 4 | 24,734 | 32,564 | 46,948 | +44.2% | +89.8% |
| 8192 | 8 | 35,767 | 34,268 | 49,473 | +44.4% | +38.3% |
| 32768 | 1 | 21,688 | 21,160 | 29,259 | +38.3% | +34.9% |

### Mean TTFT

| Input | Concurrency | FI/no-EP | FI+EP | MegaMoE+SP | Mega vs FI+EP | Mega vs no-EP |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 128 | 1 | 225.3 ms | 211.5 ms | 157.0 ms | -25.8% | -30.3% |
| 128 | 8 | 459.8 ms | 429.2 ms | 315.6 ms | -26.5% | -31.4% |
| 128 | 32 | 547.2 ms | 519.0 ms | 336.3 ms | -35.2% | -38.5% |
| 128 | 64 | 700.9 ms | 743.8 ms | 522.3 ms | -29.8% | -25.5% |
| 128 | 128 | 1,232.8 ms | 1,265.4 ms | 884.7 ms | -30.1% | -28.2% |
| 8192 | 1 | 404.7 ms | 418.7 ms | 297.0 ms | -29.1% | -26.6% |
| 8192 | 2 | 668.8 ms | 695.3 ms | 491.6 ms | -29.3% | -26.5% |
| 8192 | 4 | 1,254.9 ms | 920.0 ms | 638.4 ms | -30.6% | -49.1% |
| 8192 | 8 | 1,679.9 ms | 1,755.4 ms | 1,214.6 ms | -30.8% | -27.7% |
| 32768 | 1 | 1,541.2 ms | 1,579.6 ms | 1,142.3 ms | -27.7% | -25.9% |

The FI/no-EP 8192/c4 point has a repeatable scheduling/PP performance cliff when four chat-templated prompts cross the 32768-token step budget. A separate six-wave rerun measured 24,143 tok/s versus 24,734 tok/s in the paired three-wave run.

Accuracy results will be added after the full GSM8K evaluation completes.

title: [RFC]: Data integrity and I/O liveness for the filesystem KV offload tier
body:
### Motivation.

The filesystem secondary tier (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/fs/`) is a data path with no integrity verification and no bound on how long a single I/O operation may take. #49328 established the partial-keep contract this builds on: a failed load marks its own cached lookup verdict a miss and reports how many blocks loaded before the failure, so earlier blocks survive. Two gaps remain on top of that:

1. **No data integrity verification.** Block contents written to the filesystem tier are never checksummed. `_load_block` detects a file shorter than `block_size` and deletes it, so truncation is caught. What is not caught is content that is the right length and the wrong bytes: bit rot on the storage device, a partially rewritten file, or a block written by an instance whose layout differs in a way the `FileMapper` path hash does not capture. Such a block is copied into the primary tier and consumed as attention KV, producing wrong logits with no error signal anywhere in the system.

2. **No deadline on filesystem I/O.** `batch_store_block` and `batch_load_block` run as a single pool task per job with no deadline. A stalled NFS mount, hung FUSE filesystem, or a device in error recovery blocks that pool thread indefinitely. The pool is bounded at `n_read_threads` + `n_write_threads` (16 + 16 by default), and read-priority threads fall back to the store queue and vice versa, so ~32 stuck operations stall all tiering traffic in both directions. This is the tier-side half of the problem reported in #49829: that issue bounds how long the scheduler waits on a `HIT_PENDING` block, but nothing bounds the write it is waiting for.

Two smaller gaps follow from the same code path:

1. **Stale temporary files are never reclaimed.** `_store_block` writes to `<dest>_<random>.tmp` and `os.replace` it, cleaning up the temp file if the write raises. If the engine dies between the two (OOM kill, SIGKILL, node preemption), the temp file survives with nothing that will ever remove it. On a long-lived shared PVC these accumulate without bound.

2. **No errno-based error classification.** Both the C and Python I/O paths already surface `errno` (`PyErr_SetFromErrnoWithFilename` in `csrc/fs_io.cpp`), and partial progress is already reported (`exc.num_succeeded` -> `JobResult.successful_keys`, added in #49328). Nothing consumes the errno. A transient `ESTALE` on an NFS remount is treated identically to a permanent `ENOSPC`: the remaining keys in the batch are marked a miss and recomputed.

These matter most on shared or network filesystems (NFS, POSIX PVCs), which the tier explicitly supports: `FileSystemTierManager` documents cross-instance cache sharing over a common `root_dir`.

### Proposed Change.

Four changes, each independently. Every one of them touches both I/O implementations: `vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/fs/io.py` is a pure-Python fallback, and `csrc/fs_io.cpp` (built as `vllm.fs_io_C`) is the path actually taken whenever the extension imports. 

### 1. Block-level checksum validation
**What:** Compute a CRC32C over each block when storing it to the filesystem tier, persist it with the block, and verify it on load. A mismatch deletes the file and marks the key a miss rather than returning corrupt KV.
**Design:**
- **Placement, given O_DIRECT.** The tier prefers `O_DIRECT` and falls back to buffered I/O only where the probe fails, so block payloads must stay length- and offset-aligned. A 4-byte trailer appended to the payload breaks that alignment for every block. Two viable options, and choosing between them is the main open question for this item:
  - *Padded trailer:* store the checksum in a full logical block appended after the payload, keeping the payload aligned. Costs one extra device block (512 B or 4 KiB) per file, where a file holds `blocks_per_chunk` blocks. This overhead is the main argument for the sidecar.
  - *Sidecar directory:* keep checksums in a separate file keyed by the same hash. Preserves the payload byte-for-byte, but loses the single-rename atomicity that `os.replace` gives today.
- **Verification point.** `_load_block` reads via `os.readv` directly into the primary tier's memoryview slice, so a block cannot be verified before it lands there. Verification happens after the read and before the key is reported as a successful load, and a mismatch is reported through the existing `num_succeeded` partial-keep path so preceding blocks in the batch are still kept.
- **On-disk format versioning.** `FileMapper._compute_base_path` derives the storage directory from a SHA-256 of `FileMapper.fields`. Enabling checksums changes the on-disk format, so it must add a field there. Without it, a cache directory written before the upgrade is read as if it carried checksums, and every block fails verification. This is a one-line change and the reason the item touches `file_mapper.py`.
- **Algorithm.** CRC32C is hardware-accelerated on x86 (SSE 4.2) and ARM (CRC extension) and is straightforward to implement in `csrc/fs_io.cpp` alongside the existing I/O, which avoids adding a Python dependency for the fast path.
- **Config:** `checksum_blocks: bool = False` as a `FileSystemTierManager` kwarg, plumbed through the tier config dict that `SecondaryTierFactory.create_secondary_tier` splats into the constructor. Defaulting to off keeps the change inert until the storage-overhead and throughput numbers are on the table.
- **Metric:** `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_checksum_failures`, labeled by tier. Existing counters in this subsystem are unsuffixed (`..._cascade_job_failures`, `..._promotion_job_failures`); `vllm:kv_offload_cpu_evictions_total` is the sole `_total` user, so this follows the local majority.

### 2. I/O deadline for filesystem jobs
**What:** Give each enqueued filesystem job a deadline. When it expires, report the job as failed to the tiering manager so the scheduler stops waiting, and account for the fact that the worker thread may still be blocked.
**Design:**
- Add a monotonic deadline to `JobState` at enqueue time. A periodic check in `DualQueueThreadPool.get_finished()` (the pool's own method; the tier-level API is `get_finished_jobs()`) publishes expired jobs to `_finished_q`.
- **Reconciling a reaped job is the core problem, not the timer.** `JobState.task_done` publishes a job when `_completed == _n_tasks` and decrements `_inflight_jobs` there. If the reaper publishes a job and its stuck task later completes, the job is published twice and `_inflight_jobs` goes negative, which breaks the `wait_idle()` that `drain_jobs()` and `shutdown()` depend on. The proposal is a terminal flag on `JobState`: the first publisher wins, the second is dropped, and `_inflight_jobs` is decremented exactly once. Reviewers should push on this part first.
- **Interrupting the I/O.** A blocked `os.write`/`os.readv` cannot be interrupted from Python, and the C path releases the GIL for the entire batch with no cancellation check, so a flag polled between blocks only works if `csrc/fs_io.cpp` grows one. Even then it cannot preempt a syscall already blocked in the kernel. The honest scope is: the deadline unblocks the *scheduler* promptly; the thread stays stuck until the filesystem returns. `p2p/manager.py::_reap_unbound_stores` is the in-tree precedent for this shape.
- **Config:** `io_timeout_seconds: float | None = None` (off by default) as a `FileSystemTierManager` kwarg.
- **Metric:** `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_io_timeouts`, labeled by tier and direction.

### 3. Stale temporary file cleanup
**What:** Reclaim `*.tmp` files left behind by a crashed engine.
**Design:**
- **A blind sweep at startup is not safe.** `FileSystemTierManager` documents cross-process cache sharing over a common `root_dir`, and `FileMapper` is constructed with `parallel_agnostic=True`, which forces `rank` to 0 for qualifying models. Multiple live instances therefore write into the same directory. Deleting every `*.tmp` at init would delete another running instance's in-flight temp files. The temp suffix is `_<random>.tmp` with no owner encoded, so ownership cannot be recovered from the name.
- Proposal: delete only temp files whose mtime is older than a conservative threshold (default 1 hour), which no in-flight write can plausibly reach. The `.o_direct_probe_<random>.tmp` files from `probe_o_direct` are covered by the same rule.
- Alternative worth discussing: encode the writing instance's identity in the temp suffix so a sweep can skip files belonging to a live PID. More precise, but does not help across containers or nodes, which is the deployment this tier targets.
- **Config:** `cleanup_stale_tmp_after_seconds: float | None = 3600.0`.

### 4. Transient error classification and retry
**What:** Use the `errno` already surfaced by both I/O paths to distinguish retryable from terminal failures, and retry the retryable ones once or twice before falling back to the existing partial-keep path.
**Design:**
- Classify: `EAGAIN`, `EIO`, `ESTALE`, `ETIMEDOUT`, `EINTR` retryable; `ENOSPC`, `EPERM`, `EACCES`, `ENOENT` terminal. `ENOENT` on load is an ordinary miss, not an error, and must not be retried. The open PR #52838 takes the same shape one layer up, dropping a failed store but escalating a failed load, and is worth keeping consistent with.
- Retry the failing block only, not the batch. `exc.num_succeeded` already identifies where the batch stopped, so a retry resumes there.
- Bound retries so they cannot extend a job past the item 2 deadline; a retry budget without a deadline reintroduces the unbounded wait this RFC is trying to remove. This is why this item lands last.
- **Metric:** `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_io_retries`, labeled by tier, direction, and errno.

### Out of scope: tracked in other threads
The following are deliberately excluded so this RFC does not duplicate or pre-empt work already under discussion. All are open issues rather than merged or in-flight changes, so none of the four items above depends on any of them landing.
- **Tier health tracking and circuit breaking.** Two RFCs already build per-tier gating: #50031 detects saturation from an EMA of store completion rate and drops cascade stores; #51240 defines a `TieringAdmissionPolicy` ABC and ships `CascadeBackpressurePolicy`, detecting saturation from an EMA of submission-to-completion latency and rejecting jobs in `should_admit`. #53485 exists to reconcile the two and argues #51240's hook is the integration point, since it is already wired into `create_store_job()`. An error-rate breaker is a different *signal* — a tier failing fast with `EIO` is not saturated, and neither EMA would trip — but it is the same *decision*, and `TieringAdmissionPolicy.on_completed(job, result)` already receives `JobResult.success`. It therefore belongs as a policy implementation under #51240 once that lands, not as a separate `health.py` and not as a section of this RFC. Metrics from items 1, 2, and 4 are what such a policy would act on.
- **Bounding how long the scheduler waits on an in-flight write.** #49829: `TieringOffloadingManager.lookup()` returns `HIT_PENDING` with no deadline and the scheduler re-polls in a hot loop, so a stalled write defers requests until the client timeout. Item 2 bounds the write itself. The two are complementary and neither subsumes the other.
- **Reclaiming leaked shared-memory segments after a crash.** #54002: `SharedOffloadRegion` never unlinks `/dev/shm/vllm_offload_<engine_id>.mmap`, and on Kubernetes `/dev/shm` survives container restarts, so a crash wedges the pod in CrashLoopBackOff. Same failure class as item 3 (an artifact outliving the process that made it) but a different artifact, a different owner, and a much sharper impact.
- **Recovering primary-tier ref-counts after a crash.** Not needed, and worth stating so reviewers do not ask. `CPUPrimaryTierOffloadingManager` inherits its block index and `ref_cnt` bookkeeping from `CPUOffloadingManager`, built in memory in `__init__` with no restore-from-disk path, and `SharedOffloadRegion` keys its backing file on `engine_id`, so a restarted engine gets a fresh region rather than reattaching to the old one. In-flight transfer state is therefore gone, not stale. The old region itself does leak, but that is the memory-reclamation problem in #54002, not a ref-count problem.

### Summary table
items are numbered in the order they should be merged, and the motivation list above uses the same numbering.
| Item | Needs a `csrc/fs_io.cpp` change | Priority |
|------|-------------------------------|----------|
| 1. Checksum validation | Yes | High — silent corruption has no error signal today |
| 2. I/O deadline | Yes, for a cancellation point | High — pool starvation stalls both directions |
| 3. Stale tmp cleanup | No | Medium — unbounded growth on shared PVCs |
| 4. Transient retry | Yes | Low — needs item 2's deadline to bound the retry budget |

### Feedback Period.

_No response_

### CC List.

@varun-sundar-rabindranath 

### Any Other Things.

- Scope is the filesystem tier only. The P2P tier already has abort-on-timeout, abort-ack timeout, and `_reap_unbound_stores` in `p2p/manager.py`. The object store tier (`tiering/obj/`) would benefit from items 1 and 4 but is left out to keep each PR reviewable.
- Item 1 changes the on-disk format. Existing caches are not migrated: the `FileMapper` field change moves checksummed caches to a new directory, and operators enabling the flag start with a cold tier.
- Each PR adds unit tests for both the C and Python I/O paths. The existing `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_fs_tier.py` covers both and is the pattern to follow. Fault injection for items 2 and 4 needs a stub that blocks or returns a chosen errno, since a real stalled mount is not reproducible in CI.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Perf][ROCm] Sparse-MLA/kpool backends fall back to rebuilding attention metadata per draft step, capping useful MTP depth at k=4
body:
### Summary

On ROCm with GLM-5.3-Flash, vLLM logs at startup:

```
Fused multi-step draft decode is not supported by attention backend(s)
DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER, KPOOL_TAIL, ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE;
falling back to rebuilding attention metadata between draft steps.
```

Because the metadata is rebuilt between every draft step, the per-step cost of MTP speculation is high enough that deeper speculation stops paying for itself well before the draft quality runs out. Measurements below quantify the gap.

### Measurements

8x MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, TP8, GLM-5.3-Flash-FP8, `--max-model-len 1048576`, 2 000-token context, 256 output tokens, unique per-request prefixes (nothing hits the prefix cache), warmup round then median of 3-4 rounds.

| `num_speculative_tokens` | acceptance length | draft acceptance rate | 1 user | 16 users | 64 users |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 2.57 | 78.4 % | 155 tok/s | 1 432 | 3 012 |
| **4** | **3.36** | 58.9 % | **173** | **1 499** | **3 055** |
| 6 | 3.76 | 46.0 % | 175 | 1 367 | 2 874 |

The accepted length keeps climbing (2.57 → 3.36 → 3.76), i.e. the draft head still has useful signal at k=6. But throughput peaks at k=4 and *falls* at k=6, which is what you would expect when each additional draft step carries a fixed metadata-rebuild cost rather than being fused.

Note this model has `num_nextn_predict_layers = 1`, so every draft token is another autoregressive pass through the same MTP head — the per-step overhead is paid k times.

### Why this matters

For latency-sensitive single-stream use, speculation is the main lever (at high concurrency the GPU is compute-saturated and speculation contributes almost nothing — see the 64-user column). Being capped at k=4 by framework overhead rather than by draft quality leaves measurable throughput on the table.

### Ask

Is fused multi-step draft decode feasible for these backends (`ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`, `DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER`, `KPOOL_TAIL`), or is there a structural reason the sparse-indexer metadata cannot be built once for all draft steps? If it is mainly a matter of hoisting the metadata build, I am happy to test a patch on this hardware — I have the harness and the baseline numbers above.

Related: #54359 (a correctness bug in the same kpool indexer path on ROCm), #53906 (GLM-5.3-Flash support).

title: [Bugfix] DeepSeek-V3.2: render tools after the system prompt
body: ## Purpose Fixes #54911 When a request carries tools, `deepseek_v32.py` inserts a new **empty** system message to hold them instead of using the system message that's already there: ```python messages.insert(0, {"role": "system"}) messages[0]["tools"] = tools ``` That empty message renders as `""` + `"\n\n"` + the tools block, so the whole `## Tools` section ends up **in front of the system prompt**. Running the checkpoint's own `encoding/test_input.json` through the encoder and diffing against its `encoding/test_output.txt`, we diverge at token 1, the first token after BOS: DeepSeek's reference encoder attaches tools to the existing message ([`test_encoding_dsv32.py`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2/blob/main/encoding/test_encoding_dsv32.py) does `messages[0]["tools"] = test_dict["tools"]`), and the golden output starts with the system prompt, not the tools: ``` <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>You are a helpful Assistant. ## Tools ``` #52255 fixes this same pattern in `deepseek_v4.py`, but its diff only touches that file. V3.2 has the identical bug and nothing open covers it. This is the companion fix, kept deliberately identical to #52255 so the two wrappers don't drift. ## Changes - Attach request-level tools to the leading `system`/`developer` message, inserting one only when there's nothing to attach to. - Copy that message first, since `list(conversation)` is shallow and `messages[0]` is still the caller's dict. - Request-level tools now replace tools already on the message instead of rendering both, which emitted `## Tools` twice. - Add `tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v32.py`. This module had no tests at all, which is why the V4 version of this bug got caught and this one didn't. Four of the five tests follow #52255's shapes. Two needed different assertions because V3.2 isn't V4: `render_message` deliberately emits tools *before* `developer` content, and V3.2 doesn't render tool schemas as JSON. The fifth is new. It checks the caller's messages aren't mutated, which is what keeps the `dict()` copy from being deleted later as redundant. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v32.py -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py -v .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v32.py tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v32.py ``` ## Test Result Linux x86_64, Python 3.12.13, torch 2.13.0+cu132. ``` tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v32.py 5 passed tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py 35 passed (no regression) both together 40 passed ``` pre-commit clean, including `ruff check`, `ruff format`, `mypy` and `typos`. Two pre-existing issues turned up while testing, both reproducing on `main` and neither touched here: `TOOLS_SYSTEM_TEMPLATE` is 7 blank lines off from the golden, and a leading `developer` message crashes in thinking mode (`drop_thinking_messages` drops it while the render loop still iterates the original count). Happy to file the second separately. ## Note for reviewers This changes the prompt for every V3.2 request that passes tools, so it invalidates existing prefix caches and may move eval numbers. Same caveat #52255 carries for V4. AI assistance was used here. I've reviewed every line, reproduced the divergence against the checkpoint's golden files, and run the tests and lint myself.

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Avoid strided-view D2H stall on dynamic-K draft token copy
body:
## Summary

`self.draft_token_ids_cpu` is `[max_num_reqs, self.num_spec_tokens]` pinned. When DSD picks a runtime K smaller than the buffer's config K, `self.draft_token_ids_cpu[:num_reqs, :num_spec_tokens]` is a **gapped strided view** (row stride = config K, but only runtime K per row is data). `cudaMemcpyAsync` on a strided pinned destination falls back to pageable staging and blocks the host — exactly the class of stall the stricter check in #53491 catches, and it defeats the whole point of the `draft_token_ids_copy_stream` side stream.

Keep the fast path when `num_spec_tokens == self.num_spec_tokens` (the slice collapses to `[:num_reqs, :]` and is dense); otherwise split into per-row copies so each destination is a dense sub-view — same pattern as #53412 for XD-RoPE and njhill's original mrope fix in #51841.

## Context

Continues the sync-elimination sweep against the checker in #53491. njhill's #54299 covered a broad set of non-pinned H2D cases and the earlier merged PRs (#54266, #54292, #54293, #54295) pinned host tensors on the MM / KV connector / sparse MLA paths. This one is the DSD spec-decode D2H-strided case that was missed.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs for `draft_token_ids_cpu in:body`, `draft_token_ids_copy_stream`, and `#53491 in:body`. None cover this site.

## Testing

- `.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` — passed (ruff, mypy, typos, SPDX, etc.)

Static K workloads hit the fast-path branch and their behavior is byte-identical. Dynamic K workloads trade one strided `copy_` (which was silently blocking) for `num_reqs` per-row `copy_` calls on the same side stream — same pattern established in #53412.

AI assistance was used for code search and drafting; every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Feature] Support downloading models from AtomGit
body:
## Summary

Add **AtomGit** as a third model download source, alongside HuggingFace and ModelScope, mirroring the `VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE` UX:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_ATOMGIT=True
vllm serve hf_mirrors/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --served-model-name Qwen3.8-27B ...
```

- When `VLLM_USE_ATOMGIT=True`, redirects `HF_ENDPOINT` to `https://hub.atomgit.com` early at import time (`vllm/env_override.py`), matching what the `atomgit_hub` SDK does on import; vLLM's existing HuggingFace download paths (config / tokenizer / weights / processors) work unchanged.
- Repo ids with 3+ path segments (e.g. `hf_mirrors/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`) are normalized to the 2-segment form (`hf_mirrors-Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`) in `ModelConfig`, consistent with the atomgit SDK's `_normalize_repo_id`; 2-segment ids (e.g. `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`) are kept as-is.
- Reuses the token saved by `atomgit login` (`~/.atomgit/config.json`) as `HF_TOKEN`, exported only when the endpoint actually points at AtomGit so the credential is never sent to a third-party endpoint; robust against malformed config (non-dict JSON / non-string token) so `import vllm` never crashes.
- Normalization skips URLs, object-storage URIs (`s3://`, `gs://`, `az://`, `runai://`, ...) and absolute/relative paths, so existing features such as RunAI object storage are unaffected; when both `VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE` and `VLLM_USE_ATOMGIT` are set, AtomGit takes precedence.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Searched open PRs of vllm-project/vllm via the GitHub search API for `AtomGit`, `VLLM_USE_ATOMGIT`, `atomgit download` and `atomgit in:title` — all returned 0 results. No duplicate PR exists.

## Test commands run and results

- `uvx ruff check` (all changed files + test file): **all pass**
- New unit test `tests/transformers_utils/test_utils.py::test_normalize_atomgit_repo_id`: covers 1/2/3/4-segment ids and exclusion of URLs / object-storage URIs / absolute paths
- Verified against the real `hub.atomgit.com` endpoint:
  - `hf_mirrors/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` (3-segment → normalized `hf_mirrors-Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`): `list_repo_files` OK, `config.json` fetched (`model_type=qwen3_5`)
  - `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (2-segment, unchanged): `list_repo_files` OK, `config.json` fetched (`model_type=glm5_next`)
  - The un-normalized 3-segment id returns 404 on the endpoint, confirming that normalization is required

## Model evaluation

This change only affects the download source of model/weight files (HF → AtomGit); it does not change model output, accuracy, or serving behavior after loading, so no model evaluation is required.

## AI assistance statement

This PR was created with AI assistance (AtomCode / deepseek-v4-flash): implementation, code-review fixes, and verification were generated by AI; the submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the relevant tests.
