title: [Bug]: DeepSeek V4 DSpark TP=2 on 2× GB10 hits dual-rank Xid 31 at the inferred T=16 PIECEWISE warmup
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Sanitized environment snapshot</summary>

- Hardware: 2× ASUS GX10, one NVIDIA GB10 per node, compute capability 12.1, 121 GiB usable unified memory per node
- Architecture: aarch64
- Interconnect: direct ConnectX-7 RoCE
- Host OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Kernel: 6.17.0-1029-nvidia
- NVIDIA driver: 580.173.02
- Docker: 29.2.1
- Python: 3.12.3
- PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130
- CUDA reported by PyTorch: 13.0
- NCCL: 2.30.7+cuda13.3
- Triton: 3.7.1
- vLLM: 0.28.0 plus the exact source ports listed below
- FlashInfer: 0.6.16.post3 plus the exact source ports listed below
- B12X: 1.2.6
- Model repository at run: `drowzeys/keys-DeepSeekV4-Flash-GA-0731-Dspark-Abliterated-32-32`
- Current canonical repository: `drowzeys/keys-DeepSeekV4-Flash-GA-0731-Dspark-Abliterated-Anchored-Tensors` (the at-run slug now redirects here)
- Model revision: `6c47916f85e52b5e712223ca8f93952f90255714`

</details>

This is a sanitized, manually reconstructed host/container snapshot assembled from metadata-only checks of the tested image and both nodes. It is not presented as verbatim output from `collect_env.py` because repeating the full-model startup after a dual-GPU Xid was judged unsafe. The attached bundle contains `environment.json` with the same values and provenance caveat.

### Bug description

#### Summary

This is a one-shot evidence report, not a minimal runnable reproducer. The original run did not use `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG` or `VLLM_TRACE_FUNCTION=1`, and I did not repeat an unchanged startup after simultaneous GPU Xids solely to collect those diagnostics.

A two-node DeepSeek V4 + DSpark K=5 startup progressed through TP=2 initialization, model loading, KV profiling, and FlashInfer sparse-MLA autotuning, but failed before API readiness during PIECEWISE CUDA-graph warmup.

Both GB10 GPUs reported Xid 31 MMU virtual-write faults at the same wall-clock second. Rank 1's closest Python stack traversed the DeepSeek V4 attention path into FlashInfer's DSv4 SM120/SM121 sparse-MLA runner. CUDA explicitly warned that the error may have been reported asynchronously, so this stack identifies where the poisoned context surfaced, not necessarily the kernel that caused the write.

The failing graph size is inferred to be T=16: capture uses descending sizes; 36, 32, 30, and 24 completed (4/9) before the next pre-capture forward failed. T=16 was not directly instrumented in this run.

#### Expected behavior

PIECEWISE CUDA-graph warmup completes and the TP=2 API becomes ready.

#### Observed behavior

- TP=2/NCCL formed successfully.
- Target weights loaded successfully; the K=5 draft then loaded all 97 draft parameters. Total model loading reached about 79.48 GiB per rank.
- KV profiling completed.
- FlashInfer sparse-MLA autotuning loaded 24 cached configurations.
- PIECEWISE warmup reached 4/9 capture sizes.
- Both GPUs emitted Xid 31 `ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_WRITE` faults at 2026-08-29 06:34:18 UTC.
- Rank 0 surfaced `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` at a later FP8 allocation.
- Rank 1 surfaced `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` while constructing `_SparseMLAPagedAttentionRunner` after the stack passed through `flashinfer_sparse.py:857`.
- Rank 1 later emitted Xid 13 ×16 and Xid 109 ×1. TCPStore/NCCL errors occurred after rank 0 died and are treated as secondary fallout.
- The API never became ready. No correctness, throughput, or soak result exists.

The kernel journals also contained driver-level `NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY` allocation probes before the fault (135 on rank 0 and 42 on rank 1). These may be a pressure cofactor. There was no PyTorch OOM, Docker OOM kill, or container restart.

#### Why this appears distinct from existing reports

- #50720 remains open and covers a deterministic `num_tokens > 64` assertion caused by short-token DSpark routing. That failure class was separately cleared in a local v0.27.1 test by patching both source and the active precompiled FlashInfer module; TP=2 then reached readiness without Xid: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50720#issuecomment-5385709649
- The tested tree includes the exact #52499 head (`af2456b11328a15ea7f2f8e48aeb7ed30a61e32f`), covering flat 3-D speculative-decode queries and ≤64-token routing.
- The tested tree ports both changes from #53425 head (`ed71de505898e1c006de15958795c229c9f7e21f`) onto v0.28, covering SM12x FlashInfer kernel page size 64.
- vLLM 0.28.0 already includes #51538's DSpark CUDA-graph workspace-lifetime, graph-replay, and draft-KV-write safeguards. This failure persisted despite those adjacent protections.
- #53391 is the closest GB10 startup report: DSV4 + DSpark + TP=2 on two GB10s. It is a deterministic `ragged spec decode batch: 7 tokens over 2 requests` assertion during kernel warmup; this tested tree includes its separate query-offset-driven ragged-dispatch port and instead reaches graph capture before a GPU fault.
- #51499 and #51970 report DeepSeek V4 CUDA illegal-memory failures from all-zero indexer lengths reaching an out-of-bounds DeepGEMM paged-MQA metadata scheduler on H20/GH200. Their localized path and capture shapes differ from this two-GB10, PIECEWISE, inferred-T=16 sparse-MLA-adjacent observation. Because this run lacked synchronous launch localization, it does not rule out an earlier asynchronous fault in another path.
- FlashInfer #4802 head (`c2eec117219457e45126fa4fa87e7240dd4ea620`) directly refactors the same SM120 T≤64 sparse-MLA/CUDA-graph surface. It adds a persistent graph-safe runner and documents a lazy-allocation/free graph-memory-pool reuse hazard. This candidate did not include #4802, and its description does not diagnose this dual-rank Xid 31. I can validate a maintainer-specified #4802-head build if that is the preferred next check.

I searched open and closed vLLM issues for DeepSeek V4/DSpark + SM121/GB10 + TP=2 + T=16 + Xid 31 and did not find an equivalent report. The closest neighboring reports are distinguished above; #50189 and #53455 involve materially different models, execution paths, or configurations.

#### Exact source provenance

This was not stock vLLM 0.28.0 or stock FlashInfer 0.6.16.post3.

vLLM:

- Base tag/commit: `v0.28.0` / `2cf0a6915ce544dc493a0990f2ea38d81601128a`
- Tested local commit/tree: `9165323e2ebffbb0260d7df9feb955b87330f83b` / `7637f703bd2d9e94bb6a8f6516ef5ba7bb69685d`
- Included #52368, #52018, exact #52499 head, exact #53425 head, validated SM12x sparse-indexer fallbacks, contiguous/ragged speculative-decode fixes, and public SM12x Triton O-projection commit `409086a5f588d155ffbddd4bb7b917c96333ed3c`.

FlashInfer:

- Base tag/commit: `v0.6.16.post3` / `9dc1b2495b40314dec8a8cde8cd7faf5c5206702`
- Tested local commit/tree: `1fb01df312cefb0eaea004fd4c7e513848eb3952` / `62ef2a19f1b8ea4f21392eb9ae7d60d786c8f76e`
- Included the DeepSeek V4 H32/K192 support from #4380 and the narrow SM120/SM121 prefill-handshake fix associated with #4732.

The local replay commits are not publicly fetchable. The attached bundle therefore includes consolidated patches against the two stated base commits plus `source-lock.json`.

#### Launch configuration

Key observed vLLM settings were:

- tensor parallel size 2 across two nodes
- pipeline parallel size 1
- DSpark with five speculative tokens, probabilistic sampling, adaptive verification disabled
- FP8 KV cache
- block size 256
- maximum model length 532,288
- GPU memory utilization 0.810
- maximum sequences 6
- maximum batched tokens 8,192
- long-prefill threshold 1,024
- chunked prefill and async scheduling enabled
- FlashInfer autotuning enabled
- B12X linear and MoE backends
- PIECEWISE capture sizes `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 30, 32, 36]`

The bundle's `launch-observed.yaml` records a sanitized subset of the observed launch and container configuration. It is evidence, not a cutover script or minimized reproducer.

#### Primary error excerpts

Rank 1:

```text
compile_or_warm_up_model
  -> capture_model
  -> cudagraph_utils.py:337 forward_fn(CUDAGraphMode.NONE)
  -> deepseek_v4/attention.py
  -> flashinfer_sparse.py:857 _forward_decode
  -> flashinfer.mla._core._trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4_sm120
  -> _SparseMLAPagedAttentionRunner(...)
  -> torch.empty(...)
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call,
so the stacktrace below might be incorrect.
```

Kernel evidence, with hostnames, PCI addresses, process identifiers, GPU UUIDs, channels, and virtual addresses removed:

```text
2026-08-29T06:34:18Z rank0 NVRM: Xid 31, MMU Fault, FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_WRITE
2026-08-29T06:34:18Z rank1 NVRM: Xid 31, MMU Fault, FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_WRITE
2026-08-29T06:34:18Z rank1 NVRM: Xid 31, MMU Fault, FAULT_PTE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_WRITE
```

Sanitized rank excerpts and the compact kernel fault window are included in `logs/`.

#### Negative controls

The standalone controls did not reproduce the fault:

- The prior SM121 O-projection blocker passed eager execution plus CUDA-graph capture/replay at T=10, 96, and 8,192 on both nodes.
- Standalone FlashInfer sparse MLA at T=16, H=32, D=512, K=192 passed the heuristic and explicit tactics 1, 2, and 3.
- Corrected cached-shape tests passed K128/tactic 2, K128+512/tactic 8, and a 4,224-wide K128 buffer with 4,158 valid compressed entries/tactic 52, using eager/reference checks and alternating A/B/A/B graph replays.
- No Xid, illegal-memory event, OOM kill, or restart occurred in those controls.

The full-model warmup's exact T=16 metadata was not captured or reproduced. These controls also do not recreate full TP=2 allocation pressure, production tensor strides/buffer reuse, or stream ordering. They rule out a simple always-failing T=16 kernel/tactic explanation.

#### Reproduction status and limitations

- The full-model failure was observed once in one attended startup and was not repeated because it produced simultaneous GPU Xids.
- T=16 is inferred from capture order, not directly instrumented.
- Rank 1's sparse-MLA stack is the closest report, not proof of causation.
- Memory pressure may contribute, but this was not a framework/container OOM.
- The exact model is publicly listed but gated; no weights or cache content are in the bundle.
- `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG` and `VLLM_TRACE_FUNCTION=1` were not used in the original one-time failure. Repeating the same startup solely to collect them was judged unsafe.

#### Evidence bundle

The proposed compact source-and-evidence bundle is available at:

https://github.com/TurboTheTurtle/vllm-gb10-dsv4-xid31-evidence

It contains only source patches, sanitized excerpts, a sanitized configuration record, source locks, checksums, and the corrected cached-shape negative-control script. It excludes weights, caches, compiled modules, images, credentials, private networking, full service logs, and any host-control/rollback code.

#### Maintainer follow-up

I can run one maintainer-specified near-stock build or bounded diagnostic on the same two-GB10 cluster, provided the requested commit set and instrumentation are explicit. I would prefer not to repeat the unchanged startup because the first run faulted both GPUs.

### Before submitting a new issue

- [x] I searched open and closed issues for relevant reports and asked the documentation chatbot on the vLLM documentation site.

title: Revert "[Nixl][PD] DCP support for MLA models" (#50611)
body:
## Suggested narrower fix (preferred over this revert)

The regression is one gated assignment. In `SparseAttnIndexer.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size`, the memoization is conditional:

```python
if isinstance(get_forward_context().attn_metadata, dict):
    self._cp_kv_cache_interleave_size = value
return value
```

When `attn_metadata` is not a `dict`, the value is **never** cached, so every subsequent forward re-enters `get_current_vllm_config()`. Outside a `set_current_vllm_config()` context that raises. Caching unconditionally on first access — or resolving the value eagerly in `Worker.initialize_from_config`, as the docstring says already happens — should fix this without a revert. **If a maintainer lands that, please close this PR.**

## Root cause

#50611 replaced an eager `__init__`-time read:

```python
self.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size = parallel_config.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size
```

with a lazy `@property` that resolves `get_current_vllm_config()` at **model forward time**. DeepSeek-V4-Flash forwards then fail:

```
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py", line 849, in forward_cuda
    self.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size,
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py", line 791, in cp_kv_cache_interleave_size
    get_current_vllm_config().parallel_config.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size
AssertionError: Current vLLM config is not set.
```

EngineCore then fails to start and the server exits.

## Evidence

Build <https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/86170> (`Full CI run - daily`, commit 6cddad4). 3 newly-failing jobs, plus a 4th whose failure signature changed to this one:

| Job | Failing config |
|---|---|
| `(B200) LM Eval Spec Decode` | `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark-confidence-TP4` |
| `(B200) MoE Refactor Integration TEMPORARY Shard 1` | `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-deepgemm-mega-moe` |
| `(H100) LM Eval KV-Offload Large` | `offloading-deepseek-v4-flash`, `simple-deepseek-v4-flash` |
| `(H200) DSv4-Flash Disaggregated DP EP` | 22 occurrences of the same assertion |

Only DeepSeek-V4-Flash configs fail — both Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 configs in `MoE Refactor Shard 1` passed in the same job.

**Bisect:** all four jobs passed at build 86121 (commit d3d79ff) and failed at 86170 (6cddad4). `7f4793e` is the only commit in that range touching `sparse_attn_indexer.py`.

**No stacked dependents:** `7f4793e` is still HEAD on `sparse_attn_indexer.py`, `nixl/pull_worker.py`, and `config/vllm.py`, so this reverts cleanly (no conflicts; file set identical to the original PR).

title: [Bug]: PD-admitted Mamba request is spec-padded before prefill completes, then align split truncates the 8-token window to 5
body:
## Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment and topology</summary>

```text
vLLM: v0.27.1, tag commit 6e448d0ea9bf3d88d898b65449ca6dc2aec170ac
Relevant merged change: #51113
  release commit: 3f9fc83067cdd377c51d58ad949380a164bee260
  upstream commit: c56f169d9ae46ca420617e2cf5f0c9135da0f651

Backend: vLLM Ascend, source installation from main plus Kimi-K3 support
Python: 3.11.10
Device: Ascend NPU
Engine: V1 with async scheduling

Deployment:
  - disaggregated prefill/decode using MooncakeConnectorV1
  - 2 prefill instances and 2 decode instances
  - each instance: TP=16
  - each P/D group: DP=2, one local DP rank per node
  - enable_prefix_caching=true
  - mamba_cache_mode=align on both P and D
  - Mamba/scheduler block size=384
  - max_model_len=133120
  - max_num_batched_tokens=8192
  - max_num_seqs=16
  - speculative method=DSpark, K=7, parallel draft TP=16

Model: Kimi-K3 hybrid attention/Mamba target with a compatible DSpark draft model.
For this scheduling/metadata investigation only, the target was loaded in a
10/93-layer reduced debug mode. This makes generated text unsuitable for model
quality evaluation, but does not change the scheduler transition described
below: prompt length, external-computed-token count, Mamba block split,
scheduled token count, or speculative placeholder count.

The same scheduler ordering is still present on vLLM main at
1ebff996a118cdc6e831c521c839d29ffe47d30f (checked 2026-08-30).
```

The full `collect_env.py` output is not attached because the reproduction ran
on an isolated multi-node environment. The values above are taken from the
startup and engine logs. Private host addresses, model paths, engine IDs and
request IDs have been removed.

</details>

## Describe the bug

### Summary

On a PD decode worker, a newly admitted request may have all but the last prompt
token supplied by the KV connector. If running decode requests are already in
the batch, the waiting-request scheduling path treats the one remaining token
as a new decode and pads it from 1 token to `1 + K` tokens.

For a hybrid Mamba model in `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, #51113 correctly clips
a prefill-like span that starts mid-block so it cannot cross the next Mamba
boundary. In our case the padded 8-token span starts at 379 and is clipped at
384, leaving only 5 physical query tokens. However, `pad_spec_decode` remains
true and the scheduler still publishes 7 speculative placeholders.

This creates a request-local contract violation:

```text
logical speculative window: 1 target + 7 drafts = 8
physical target span after Mamba split:          5
speculative placeholders/rejection window:      7
```

The global flattened batch shapes remain valid. The failure occurs when the
proposer interprets the 5-token request row using a 7-token rejection window.
On the Ascend DSpark backend this produces an invalid request-local position and
slot mapping and terminates the engine.

This is not a request to revert #51113. Its Mamba boundary protection is
required to prevent recurrent-state cache poisoning. The missing invariant is
that a synthetically padded speculative window must either survive all later
scheduler limiters atomically, or the padding must be cancelled for that
request.

### Deployment/startup configuration

The actual deployment uses a small wrapper to start one local DP rank on each
node. The following is a sanitized equivalent of the startup strategy:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ROLE="$1"       # producer or consumer
DP_RANK="$2"    # 0 or 1 within the P group / D group
DP_ADDR="$3"    # shared coordinator address for that group
KV_PORT="$4"

export VLLM_USE_V1=1
export VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_MLAPO=1

SPEC_CONFIG='{
  "method": "dspark",
  "model": "<compatible-dspark-model>",
  "num_speculative_tokens": 7,
  "draft_tensor_parallel_size": 16,
  "max_model_len": 4096,
  "draft_sample_method": "greedy",
  "enforce_eager": true
}'

KV_CONFIG="{
  \"kv_connector\": \"MooncakeConnectorV1\",
  \"kv_role\": \"kv_${ROLE}\",
  \"kv_buffer_device\": \"npu\",
  \"kv_port\": ${KV_PORT},
  \"kv_connector_extra_config\": {
    \"prefill\": {\"dp_size\": 2, \"tp_size\": 16},
    \"decode\": {\"dp_size\": 2, \"tp_size\": 16}
  }
}"

vllm serve <kimi-k3-target-model> \
  --served-model-name kimi-k3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 \
  --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --data-parallel-rank "${DP_RANK}" \
  --data-parallel-address "${DP_ADDR}" \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --max-model-len 133120 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --speculative-config "${SPEC_CONFIG}" \
  --kv-transfer-config "${KV_CONFIG}"
```

The Ascend platform selects `mamba_cache_mode=align` when prefix caching is
enabled and resolves the common scheduler/Mamba block size to 384. P and D use
the same cache mode and logical KV-manager group topology.

### Trigger conditions

All of the following are needed for the observed frame:

1. A hybrid Mamba/GDN model with `mamba_cache_mode=align`.
2. Speculative decoding with a fixed `K` (`K=7` here).
3. A PD consumer request admitted with an unaligned external prefix. In the
   failing request, `num_prompt_tokens=380` and the D scheduler starts from
   `num_computed_tokens=379`.
4. At least one normal decode request is already scheduled in the same step,
   while no other prefill has yet been scheduled. This satisfies the
   waiting-request `pad_spec_decode` condition.
5. Padding creates an interval that crosses the next Mamba boundary:
   `[379, 379 + 1 + 7) = [379, 387)` crosses 384.
6. `_mamba_block_aligned_split()` clips the physical interval to `[379,384)`,
   but the scheduler retains 7 speculative placeholders.
7. The proposer subsequently applies the full 7-token rejection/proposal
   semantics to this 5-token request row.

A single 380-token request normally does **not** reproduce the failure. It first
schedules the one remaining prompt token alone and enters ordinary decode in
the next step. The mixed running-decode/new-PD-request batch is important.

### Workload used to trigger the mixed batch

The original fatal frame was observed during a concurrent GPQA workload. We
then reduced the traffic pattern to the following controlled case:

1. Use `/tokenize` to construct a prompt with exactly 380 tokens.
2. Start four long-running decode requests (`temperature=0`,
   `max_tokens=768`) so both D schedulers have running decode rows.
3. Wait two seconds.
4. Concurrently submit twelve identical 380-token completion requests through
   the 2P+2D proxy.

Sanitized client outline:

```bash
# Keep decode batches active.
for i in $(seq 1 4); do
  curl -sS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{
      "model":"kimi-k3",
      "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<long deterministic request>"}],
      "temperature":0,
      "max_tokens":768,
      "stream":false
    }' \
    http://<pd-proxy>/v1/chat/completions >"runner_${i}.json" &
done

sleep 2

# The prompt in exact_380.json was verified by /tokenize to contain 380 tokens.
for i in $(seq 1 12); do
  curl -sS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data-binary @exact_380.json \
    http://<pd-proxy>/v1/completions >"exact_380_${i}.json" &
done
wait
```

`exact_380.json`:

```json
{
  "model": "kimi-k3",
  "prompt": "<neutral repeated text tokenized to exactly 380 tokens>",
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 16,
  "stream": false
}
```

The controlled workload deterministically reaches the same scheduler state on
both D instances (`start=379, requested=8, result=5, end=384`). The fatal
unpatched metadata frame quoted below comes from the original concurrent GPQA
run; the controlled workload was also used for subsequent isolation and fix
validation.

### Exact scheduler transition

The relevant waiting-request path currently behaves as follows:

```text
request.num_prompt_tokens = 380
num_computed_tokens        = 379  # external PD prefix ends here
real remaining prompt      = 1
num_spec_tokens            = 7

padding before split:
  num_new_tokens = 1 + 7 = 8
  pad_spec_decode = true

Mamba align split (#51113):
  start               = 379
  next_block_boundary = 384
  requested           = 8
  returned            = 384 - 379 = 5

scheduler output:
  num_scheduled_tokens[request]          = 5
  scheduled_spec_decode_tokens[request] = [-1] * 7
```

The ordering is visible in `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`: the waiting path
sets `pad_spec_decode`, `_mamba_block_aligned_split()` is called later, and the
placeholder list is populated after slot allocation without checking whether
the padded width survived.

### Observed result

The failing batch contained 12 requests:

```text
num_scheduled_tokens = [5, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8]
total_num_scheduled_tokens = 93 = 5 + 11 * 8
query_start_loc.shape = [13]
input_ids.shape = [93]
```

Therefore the batch-level shapes are internally consistent. Only request row 0
is semantically invalid:

```text
prompt_tokens     = 380
computed_tokens   = 379
scheduled_tokens  = 5
num_ctx           = 5
seq_len           = 384
num_rejected      = 7
valid_ctx_end     = 5 - 7 = -2

expected query positions = [377, 378, 379, 380, 381, 382, 383]
actual query positions   = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
actual query slots       = [-1, -1, -1, -1, -1, -1, -1]
metadata_valid           = false
```

The first fatal error is:

```text
RuntimeError: Invalid DSpark input metadata; see DSPARK_METADATA_MISMATCH
for request index 0, kv-cache group 0.

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 1010, in worker_busy_loop
    output = func(*args, **kwargs)
  File "vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py", line 714, in sample_tokens
    return self.model_runner.sample_tokens(grammar_output)
  File "vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py", line 2380, in sample_tokens
    propose_draft_token_ids(sampler_output.sampled_token_ids)
  File "vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py", line 1708, in propose_draft_token_ids
    draft_token_ids = self.drafter._propose(...)
  File "vllm_ascend/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py", line 827, in _propose
    ... = self.set_inputs_first_pass(...)
  File "vllm_ascend/spec_decode/dspark_proposer.py", line 541, in set_inputs_first_pass
    raise RuntimeError(...)
```

Without the diagnostic guard, the invalid position/slot mapping would proceed
toward the device kernel. The guard turns it into a deterministic host-side
failure instead of a possible device-side out-of-bounds access.

### Isolation and validation results

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Small end-to-end PD request | HTTP 200; Mooncake transfer succeeds |
| One exact 380-token request without active decode traffic | Schedules 1 prompt token, then normal 8-token decode; no 5-vs-7 frame |
| Concurrent GPQA, mixed new PD admissions and running decode rows | Reproduces fatal `scheduled=5`, `num_rejected=7`, `valid_ctx_end=-2` frame |
| Controlled 4 long runners + 12 exact-380 requests | Reaches `start=379, requested=8, result=5, end=384` on both D instances |
| Temporarily restore the pre-#51113 `next_boundary <= last_cache_position` predicate | No 384 split and no metadata error, but reintroduces the prefix-cache poisoning fixed by #51113; not an acceptable fix |
| Keep #51113 and cancel/degrade speculative processing for the short request row | All requests return HTTP 200; no invalid metadata; subsequent scheduling continues from 384 |
| Keep #51113 and rebuild the DSpark anchor from the valid accepted end | All requests return HTTP 200; no invalid metadata; normal rows in the same mixed batch remain speculative |

The last two experiments confirm that the 384 stop itself is valid and that the
failure is the stale logical speculative width after the physical span is
shortened. They are backend-side experiments, not proposed as the preferred
upstream fix.

### Expected behavior

The last uncached prompt token on a PD consumer should remain a prefill token.
It should be scheduled alone, and speculative decode should begin on a later
step after the request has crossed the prefill/decode phase boundary.

More generally, when a scheduler marks a request as synthetically padded for
speculative decode, the final physical width after all limiters must be exactly
the padded width. If a Mamba split, token budget, encoder cap, long-prefill cap,
or any later limiter shortens it, the scheduler must cancel the synthetic
padding and not emit `K` placeholders for the shortened row.

### Suspected scheduler fix

The minimal phase guard is the same distinction discussed in #49495: do not
classify `num_new_tokens == 1` as a new decode solely by token count. Require
that prompt prefill has actually completed:

```diff
 if (
     (self.num_spec_tokens > 0 and self.dynamic_sd_lookup is None)
     and self.num_sampled_tokens_per_step > 0
     and num_new_tokens == 1
+    and num_computed_tokens >= request.num_prompt_tokens
     and (scheduled_running_reqs and not prefill_scheduled)
 ):
```

For the failing PD request, `379 < 380`, so it would schedule the one real prompt
token and would not advertise seven draft placeholders.

A defensive invariant should also be considered after all token-count limiters:

```text
if pad_spec_decode and final_num_new_tokens != padded_num_tokens:
    cancel speculative padding for this request
    schedule only its real remaining token(s)
    do not populate scheduled_spec_decode_tokens for this row
```

This would protect against future limiters that can shorten a padded window,
not only Mamba alignment.

Suggested regression test:

```text
hybrid Mamba align scheduler, block_size=384, K=7
one running decode request
one waiting request with prompt_tokens=380
connector reports external_computed_tokens=379

expected:
  num_scheduled_tokens[new_request] == 1
  new_request not in scheduled_spec_decode_tokens

must not produce:
  num_scheduled_tokens[new_request] == 5
  len(scheduled_spec_decode_tokens[new_request]) == 7
```

It would also be useful to parameterize this test for generic MTP/EAGLE. The
scheduler condition and window atomicity are not DSpark-specific, although the
exact error manifestation is backend/proposer-dependent.

### Related issues and PRs

- #51113 — required Mamba align boundary correctness; this report describes an
  interaction exposed by that fix, not a reason to revert it.
- #49495 — another case where a one-token prefill remainder is mistaken for a
  new decode by the padded waiting-request optimization.
- #53505 — related hybrid Mamba + KV connector + speculative-decoding family,
  but it reports recurrent-state corruption through connector prefix-cache
  reconciliation rather than this 5-token/7-placeholder mismatch.

### Before submitting a new issue

- [x] Searched existing open and closed issues, including #49495 and #53505.
- [x] Removed private hosts, credentials, paths, engine IDs and request IDs from
  the report.

title: [Perf][Attention][DSA] Shard prefill indexer rows across TP ranks
body:
## Summary

Fixes #53691.

The SM90 CUDA DSA prefill indexer currently recomputes the same logits and Top-K results on every tensor-parallel rank. This PR assigns each independent prefill query row to one TP rank, scores that row against its complete key interval, and reconstructs the original Top-K layout with one `all_gatherv` per indexer layer.

Only finished `int32` Top-K indices are exchanged. This is not an approximation or a merge of partial candidates: each row has exactly one writer, so there is no cross-rank score/tie merge and no index-only `MAX` reduction.

The implementation change is 184 additions / 23 deletions across two production files. The complete PR remains below 500 added lines, including a 314-line focused test file.

## Design and invariants

The partition is contiguous and balances the exact number of scored keys using replicated CPU scheduler metadata:

```text
cost(request, j) = (seq_len - query_len + 1 + j) // compress_ratio
```

A cumulative sum plus `searchsorted` produces a positive, exhaustive partition for any TP size without a device synchronization.

Five boundaries keep the change local and safe:

- **KV state stays replicated.** KV gathering runs before the row intersection on every rank, preserving the existing `skip_kv_gather` workspace-reuse contract across chunks.
- **Decode stays replicated.** Mixed-batch decode rows `[0, num_decode_tokens)` remain on the stock path. Ownership and `all_gatherv` cover only the following prefill slice.
- **All row-coupled operands stay aligned.** Q, weights, causal bounds, output rows, and DeepSeek-V4.1 candidate blocks use the same global row slice.
- **The collective decision is rank-consistent.** `row_shard_sizes` is derived from replicated metadata and static configuration; a rank-local runtime predicate cannot make only some ranks enter the collective.
- **Unsupported/small workloads fall back.** The existing replicated implementation remains unchanged and is selected conservatively.

The sharded path requires an SM90 CUDA GPU, TP > 1, sparse-MQA prefill, at least 1,024 scheduled prefill rows per rank, PyNCCL, no DCP/PCP, no NCCL symmetric-memory all-gather, no batch-invariant mode, and a mixed-batch CUDA Graph mode other than FULL.

## Performance

Unless noted otherwise: 4 × NVIDIA H20, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP=4, clean stock/patched processes.

### Indexer critical path

At a 4,098-row fresh prefill, measured across 21 DSA indexer layers with CUDA-event medians, the distributed critical path is the slowest rank rather than the rank average:

| Implementation | Critical indexer time | Delta | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Replicated | 0.229 ms | — | 1.00× |
| Balanced rows + `all_gatherv` | 0.173 ms | -24.5% | 1.32× |

The measured row split was `[2049, 849, 651, 549]`. On the patched critical rank, scoring took 0.069 ms and exchange/wait took 0.103 ms; communication is included rather than hidden.

### Why the activation floor is 1,024 rows/rank

A dedicated sweep used the production score/Top-K kernels and production PyNCCL `all_gatherv` (maximum per-rank median, 31 samples after 8 warmups):

| Rows/rank | Replicated | Sharded + exchange | Delta | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 0.0966 ms | 0.1666 ms | +72.5% | 0.58× |
| 1,024 | 0.2504 ms | 0.1860 ms | -25.7% | 1.35× |
| 2,048 | 0.7414 ms | 0.3531 ms | -52.4% | 2.10× |

512 rows/rank does not amortize the collective; 1,024 is the first measured profitable point and the benefit grows with work. The value is an internal conservative performance gate, not a correctness condition or public tuning knob. Because the exact crossover is model, kernel, collective, and hardware specific, the optimization is currently enabled only on the measured SM90 family; other architectures retain the replicated path until separately calibrated.

### End-to-end serving

Three repetitions per arm, prefix caching disabled:

| Workload | Stock tok/s | Patched tok/s | Throughput | TTFT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| C1, 4K | 8,622.8 | 8,643.7 | +0.24% | -0.24% |
| C2, ragged 8K total | 8,722.8 | 8,745.9 | +0.26% | -0.84% |
| C4, ragged 15.6K total | 9,048.6 | 9,090.3 | +0.46% | -0.34% |
| C2, ragged 16.3K total | 9,117.7 | 9,181.2 | +0.70% | -2.76% |
| C1, 16K | 8,981.7 | 9,158.5 | +1.97% | -1.91% |
| C1, 32K | 8,803.5 | 9,120.7 | +3.60% | -3.48% |

The long-context retrieval runs show the intended scaling regime:

| Prompt tokens, C4 | Stock median latency | Patched median latency | Delta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 65,377 | 36.972 s | 34.695 s | -6.2% |
| 130,402 | 78.822 s | 70.265 s | -10.9% |

KV gathering remains replicated and collective wait is fixed overhead, so the gain increases as the scored key history grows.

## Correctness and compatibility

| Gate | Stock | Patched |
|---|---:|---:|
| Needle retrieval, 65,377 tokens, 16 positions | 16/16 | 16/16 |
| Needle retrieval, 130,402 tokens, 16 positions | 16/16 | 16/16 |
| GSM8K, 1,319 questions, 5-shot | 93.9348% | 94.3897% |
| Native DSpark, accepted / draft tokens | 865 / 2,184 (39.61%) | 850 / 2,156 (39.42%) |

The DSpark comparison used TP=4, 7 draft tokens, three repetitions per arm, and four concurrent ragged/chunked-prefill requests per repetition. Mean acceptance length was 3.772 stock vs 3.760 patched. All 24 requests returned HTTP 200 with non-empty output and no CUDA/NCCL errors. The -0.18 percentage-point aggregate acceptance difference is smaller than run-to-run variation; this is compatibility/non-regression evidence, not a statistically powered quality claim. N-gram speculative decoding also completed with the row-sharding gate active.

PIECEWISE CUDA Graph captured 51/51 graphs and completed sharded prefill plus decode without a capture error. Explicit FULL captured and generated successfully while conservatively retaining the replicated prefill path.

For continuous random logits, three H20 actual-kernel replays found zero full-vs-sharded selected-set differences. Synthetic exact-tie differences were confined to zero-margin rows with identical selected-score multisets; unchanged stock and sharded launches both exhibit the existing kernel's tie nondeterminism. A deterministic kernel tie-break is orthogonal to this PR.

## Tests

- Latest-main targeted row-sharding suite — **57 passed**, including exact sparse-MQA routing boundaries, mixed decode/prefill with padded tails, repeated query ranges, alternating KV-gather reuse, DeepSeek-V4.1 candidate-row alignment, the measured-architecture gate, and all other enablement fallbacks
- Focused `pre-commit` — all hooks passed
- Service coverage — TP=4 concurrency 1/2/4, ragged/mixed requests, chunked prefill, 4K–130K contexts; TP=2 C1/C2 smoke tests
- Pure/simulated TP=2/3/4/8 partition and collective coverage

TP=8 hardware was unavailable. TP=8 partition/collective behavior is unit-tested, but its performance scaling remains unmeasured.

## Related work / non-duplication

- #46103 implements the same disjoint-row principle for ROCm/gfx950; this PR covers NVIDIA SM90/CUDA and adds scored-key balancing plus conservative KV-workspace handling.
- #54951 was opened after this PR and extends the pattern to GLM-5.3's k-pool indexer. The shared row-planner/scoring changes overlap; its k-pool-tail support can remain a model-specific follow-up. Its 16K rows/rank floor is a separate GLM/H200 policy, while this PR's 1K DSA/H20 floor is backed by the crossover measurement above.
- #48726 and #53563 optimize indexer kernels/materialization and are orthogonal to eliminating TP-replicated work.
- #50366 merges owner-sharded candidates for DCP. This PR owns complete rows, so it needs layout reconstruction rather than a `(score, global_id)` candidate merge.

## AI assistance

Parts of this change were drafted with AI assistance. The author reviewed the final diff, tests, and validation evidence before submission.

title: [Prefix Cache] Support fine-grained SWA hits
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #53786 by allowing `SlidingWindowManager` to participate safely in
fine-grained hybrid prefix-cache lookup when its physical KV page is larger
than the configured hash unit.

Previously, one SWA group with a larger physical page disabled
`enable_partial_hash_hits` for the entire hybrid coordinator. This forced full
attention and align-mode Mamba groups back to scheduler-page alignment even
when they could reuse a finer prefix.

This PR implements the three SWA semantics requested in the issue:

- map a hash-aligned candidate to the physical SWA pages intersecting its live
  window, with null block slots preserving global block-table indices;
- use a manager-specific EAGLE/MTP replay quantum so fixed-point reconciliation
  reaches a published SWA endpoint; and
- retain and revalidate every physical page needed to reconstruct the hit,
  including the proof page used by the EAGLE/MTP drop.

It reuses `BlockPool.cache_partial_block()` for sparse prompt-tail aliases and
the existing physical-page copy-on-write path. The same manager-specific replay
quantum is used by the core and Mooncake coordinators.

### Lookup and retention invariants

For a candidate hit `p`, the worker block table remains physical-page based.
The SWA lookup accepts `p` only if every page intersecting
`[max(0, p - (sliding_window - 1)), p)` is still cached. A live endpoint alias
alone is insufficient: an evicted interior page makes the candidate a miss and
the right-to-left search continues.

Sparse retention keeps both:

1. the deepest prompt-tail fine hit; and
2. the scheduler-aligned hit that was reachable before fine lookup was enabled.

The second boundary is a compatibility floor. Another hybrid group can rewind
the shared fixed point to that boundary; without retaining its SWA page span,
enabling fine lookup can turn an existing coarse hit into a zero-token miss.

For a prompt of length `N` and hash unit `H`, SWA publishes
`floor(N/H) * H` and, when distinct, `floor((N-1)/H) * H`. The first serves a
longer consumer. The second is reachable by immediate replay because cache
lookup is capped at `N-1`.

### Why the SWA EAGLE drop is one physical page

Fine lookup alignment does not imply that a reusable SWA alias exists at every
hash boundary: aliases are sparse prompt-tail entries, while full-page
endpoints are always published. Widening by one hash unit can therefore land
between aliases during hybrid fixed-point reconciliation and walk past an
otherwise valid Mamba checkpoint. Widening and dropping by one SWA physical
page reaches a guaranteed page endpoint; lookup then validates the complete
post-drop window.

The manager-level convergence test and an implementation mutation reproduce
the fixed point:

```text
H=2, SWA page=4, Mamba page=8, prompt=22, EAGLE enabled
hash-unit SWA drop: 22 -> 20 -> 6 -> 0
page-sized SWA drop: 22 -> 18 -> 8 -> 8
```

## Measured end-to-end change

Strict A/B was rerun on one H20 after #53614 merged, using
`origin/main` at `144e79c8106da23141ac010394b782f730cc7fe8` as the baseline and
the final production diff on top. The serving topology used a Qwen3.8 27B FP8
hybrid target plus a five-layer all-SWA DFlash
draft, hash unit 16, physical SWA/Mamba page 864, and sliding window 2,048.
Each entry is the median of three cold/warm pairs; all 32-token greedy outputs
were identical within and across versions.

| prompt | version | warm cached | warm TTFT | warm total | peak HBM |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 6,000 | current main | 5,184 | 238.945 ms | 308.693 ms | 77,307 MiB |
| 6,000 | this PR | 5,184 | 237.533 ms | 313.149 ms | 77,307 MiB |
| 6,001 | current main | 5,184 | 238.541 ms | 308.711 ms | 77,307 MiB |
| 6,001 | this PR | **6,000** | **66.324 ms** | **112.682 ms** | 77,307 MiB |

At the fine boundary, this PR reuses 816 additional tokens (+15.7% versus the
baseline hit), reducing median TTFT by 72.2% and total latency by 63.5%. The
6,000-token case is the compatibility control: align-mode Mamba cannot query
its prompt-tail endpoint because lookup is capped at `N-1`, so both versions
correctly fall back to 5,184 rather than the patched SWA path collapsing to 0.

To isolate #53786 from the independent DFlash/DSpark block-drop classification
tracked by #54163, the serving A/B used
`"disable_eagle_block_drop": true`. DFlash speculative decoding and its SWA KV
group remained active; only that unrelated target-KV drop policy was disabled.
EAGLE/MTP SWA drop behavior is covered directly by the manager fixed-point and
retention tests; reverting the SWA override to the base hash-unit drop was also
verified to collapse that fixed point to zero.

#53614 is included in both sides of this A/B. Its denser Mamba checkpoints do
not remove the SWA fine-hit veto: current main still stops at 5,184 tokens for
the 6,001-token replay, while this PR reaches the shared 6,000-token boundary.

## Scope

This PR fixes SWA participation in the existing fine-hit contract, whose
producer-side partial entries are prompt-tail aliases. It does not introduce a
new policy for publishing every generated-region boundary. Doing that naively
would conflict with partial-block hash promotion, multiply cache events, and
require local/remote agreement on alias lifetime; it is a separate BlockPool
and connector design rather than part of the three SWA manager semantics in
#53786.

`shared_prefix_boundary` is retained as a reachable boundary but is not itself
published as a new alias. Publishing it would similarly expand alias ownership
beyond prompt tails and is left as a follow-up design question.

Related work remains separate or complementary:

- merged #53614, now in this PR's base, publishes internal Mamba checkpoints;
- open #53945 concerns the EAGLE Mamba block-grid resume position;
- #54163 controls whether DFlash/DSpark should use the target-KV last-block
  drop; and
- #48435 concerns the broader reuse cliff under interleaved SWA eviction.

No commits from the open changes are included here.

## Duplicate-work check

The current #53786 discussion and open PRs were checked immediately before the
final update. `53786 in:body` returns only this PR. The closest open changes are
complementary: merged #53614 adds Mamba checkpoints but leaves the SWA veto in
place; #40156 optimizes coarse SWA search; #39171 addresses repeated EAGLE
drops; #50457 handles an all-sliding DFlash path with a broader model and
scheduler patch; and #53007 changes page-size selection. None implements fine
SWA prompt-tail lookup with physical-span validation, retention, and CoW.

## Test plan and results

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/core/

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files <all five changed files>
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <all five changed files>
```

- focused manager/prefix/Mooncake coordinator suite: **205 passed**;
- Mooncake coordinator/HMA/scheduler/worker suites: **251 passed**;
- full `tests/v1/core/`: **629 passed, 1 failed, 2 errors**. The three
  source-only macOS failures are E2E startup tests requiring the unavailable
  compiled `vllm._C.init_cpu_memory_env`; they do not execute changed manager
  logic;
- file-scoped pre-commit: **all hooks passed**;
- manual Python 3.12 mypy: **passed**; and
- `git diff --check`: **passed**.

AI assistance (Claude Code and OpenAI Codex) was used for review,
implementation iteration, tests, and this description. The contributor
reviewed the code and measurements as required by `AGENTS.md`.

body:
HY-V4's platform entry point from [#54160](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54160) rejects ROCm, causing the two HY initialization failures in [AMD build 12635](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12635/list?jid=01a06dbb-c994-4dda-9277-8d85dae8eecb&tab=output) and [build 12653](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12653/list?jid=01a070cd-0530-4d60-a5fd-a77dcc439bad&tab=output). title: [Bug][Feature][KV-offloading]: shared-mmap CPU region assumes all ranks on one host — multi-node engines hang at init; node-local disk tier reference implementation
body:
### Bug half

`SharedOffloadRegion` is one mmap file with a slot per rank. On a multi-node engine (mp executor with `--nnodes 2`, ranks on different hosts) the remote rank's slot is never written and startup dies after a multi-minute opaque wait:

```
TimeoutError: Timed out waiting for mmap file to reach 4144029696 bytes
```

`TieringOffloadingSpec` cannot avoid it: it overrides `_uses_shared_region → True` because the scheduler-side StoreController pushes L1 bytes to secondary tiers through a whole-region memoryview — single-host by construction. Plain `CPUOffloadingSpec` could fall back to private pinned tensors (which work fine multi-node), but has no gate either.

**Suggested minimal fix:** detect ranks-per-host at spec init and fail fast with an explicit "multi-node engines are not supported by the shared-region CPU tier" (or fall back to private tensors for the non-tiering spec). Related lifecycle work: #51317 / #52596 (leaked/unlinked regions — we added supporting evidence there from unified-memory hardware, where leaked regions silently shrink the next boot's profiled memory).

### Feature half: node-local tier for multi-node engines

For multi-node engines we built a working alternative worth considering in-tree: a spec where the scheduler keeps **metadata only** (persistent key index; per-key file paths derived from block hashes) and **each rank performs its own disk I/O against node-local storage** — shards never cross nodes and are never duplicated. ~450 lines over `CPUOffloadingSpec`, loaded via the existing `spec_module_path` hook, no core changes beyond the per-group geometry in #54413.

Production numbers (2× NVIDIA DGX Spark, GB10 unified memory, GLM-5.3-Flash EXL3 TP=2 with DFlash2 speculation): 155k-token session restored in 36.6 s vs 205 s recompute after a **full engine restart**; 10 *simultaneous* restores after restart, 10/10 needle-correct, TTFTs 18–164 s stacking gracefully.

Code: https://gist.github.com/hughmadden/03f369339b709a80fd594f4083702722

Hardening findings that generalize to any persistent tier (details in the gist):

- `PYTHONHASHSEED` must be pinned or block-hash-derived filenames change every restart → silent 0% hit rate (the fs manager documents this for cross-*process* sharing; it equally applies across restarts of one instance).
- Store completion must be decoupled from persistence (snapshot the bytes, complete the job, drain writes from private copies with a bounded backpressure queue) — otherwise long prefills stall on the block-reuse fence and the engine dies with `TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out`.
- Capacity-gated lookups race prepare-time allocation across requests within one scheduling step; a per-step committed-capacity counter (reset in `on_schedule_end`) closes it. Possibly relevant to #54363's I/O-liveness discussion.

Happy to contribute any of this as PRs if there's maintainer appetite.

title: [KV Connector] Support piecewise Store and P/D loading with Mooncake
body:
## Purpose

This PR depends on #54240.

This stacked PR implements the range-load API introduced by the preceding
`MultiConnector` framework PR for `MooncakeStoreConnector` and
`MooncakeConnector`.

With `load_policy=range_aware` and `MooncakeStoreConnector` configured before
`MooncakeConnector`, the Store connector can load `[0, S)` while
`MooncakeConnector` receives only the assigned P/D suffix `[S, N)`. For an
8192-token Store hit and a 9216-token prompt, the P/D transfer therefore
contains only `[8192, 9216)`.

`MooncakeStoreConnector` accepts explicit ranges, trims stale partial-hash tail
metadata when an aligned boundary shortens its load, and maps scheduler cache
groups to the worker's transferable-group indices. `MooncakeConnector` maps
the assigned suffix to the end-anchored destination blocks already allocated
for the request.
Both scheduler block lists and worker transfer regions use the same
transfer-enabled group order, so local-only groups are excluded without
shifting region indices.

The range-load path supports scheduler-block-aligned starts, partial final
ranges, DCP-scaled per-group block sizes, and attention-only hybrid KV caches
containing Full/MLA and sliding-window groups, including omitted
sliding-window padding blocks. `MooncakeConnector` does not advertise range
loading for recurrent-state groups such as Mamba/GDN; those models should use
the default single-source policy.

This PR also adds focused Mooncake and Mooncake Store scheduler tests, a
reusable in-tree launcher, and configuration documentation.

## Test Plan

### Unit and static checks

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  docs/features/mooncake_store_connector_usage.md \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/mooncake_integration/piecewise_store_pd_launcher.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/connector.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/data.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/scheduler.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/worker.py

python -W ignore::DeprecationWarning -m pytest -q \
  -W ignore::pytest.PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py
```

### RDMA cluster tests

The in-tree integration launcher is available at:

https://github.com/ScaleX-IO/vllm/blob/4d0c82af87/tests/v1/kv_connector/mooncake_integration/piecewise_store_pd_launcher.py

The standalone RDMA E2E scripts are available at:

https://github.com/ScaleX-IO/vllm/tree/decode-offloading-e2e-tests/examples/disaggregated/mooncake_store_connector/piecewise_prefix_cluster

The following scenarios were tested:

1. Single-node 1P1D functional serving.
2. Single-node 1P1D performance comparison.
3. Two-node 1P1D performance comparison.

Environment:

- Alibaba Cloud Linux 3, x86_64
- Python 3.12.13
- PyTorch 2.13.0 with CUDA 13.0
- NVIDIA driver 580.105.08
- Two compute nodes, each with 8 NVIDIA H20-3e GPUs and 192 logical CPUs
- RDMA-tested revision: `7bc12d5211c658238d36e12bf13a1759895d6097`
- RDMA transport over `mlx5_bond_0`
- `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, Prefill TP2 and Decode TP2
- FP8 KV cache, block size 256, DeepGEMM linear backend
- GPU memory utilization 0.82
- Standalone Mooncake Store on the Decode node
- Performance transfer settings: 32 QPs, 32 workers, 1 MiB slices, and one
  load-receive thread
- Functional E2E: one node, 4 GPUs, 64 CPUs, max model length 2048, eager
  execution, a 1024-token Store hit, a 32-token P/D suffix, and 8 output tokens
- Single-node performance E2E: one node, 4 GPUs, 64 CPUs, max model length
  10240, CUDA Graph, an 8192-token Store hit, a 1024-token P/D range, 1 output
  token, concurrency 1, 5 warmups, and 20 measured requests per arm
- Two-node performance E2E: Prefill on `vllm-h20-01` and Decode plus Store on
  `vllm-h20-02`, 2 GPUs and 64 CPUs per node, max model length 10240, CUDA
  Graph, the same prompt settings, 3 warmups, and 3 measured requests per arm

The performance workload used an 8193-token base plus a 1023-token delta. Each
arm used a separate Store namespace and seed pass, so Baseline and Piecewise
both had an 8192-token Store hit. Baseline disabled Decode-side Store lookup.
Piecewise loaded the Store prefix on Decode and received `[8192, 9216)` from
Prefill. Outputs were compared between the two arms.

## Test Result

### Unit and static checks

```text
All pre-commit hooks passed.
146 passed in 78.61s
```

### RDMA functional test

- Store supplied `[0, 1024)`.
- Mooncake P/D transfer supplied `[1024, 1056)`.
- The generated token IDs were
  `[16, 223, 1162, 45449, 344, 25126, 1353, 513]`.
- The continuation matched the single-source reference token for token.
- No Store, RDMA, scheduler, or serving error was observed.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Honor draft eager mode in MRV2
body:
## Purpose

`SpeculativeConfig.enforce_eager` is a draft-side override for the target model's execution mode. Model Runner V1 already uses it when initializing proposer CUDA graph keys, but Model Runner V2 passes the resolved target CUDA graph mode directly to every speculator.

This change adds a common speculator CUDA graph mode resolver. Draft-model speculators resolve the mode to `NONE` when their nested `enforce_eager` flag is enabled; otherwise they preserve the target mode. The default `None`/`False` path and target-model CUDA graph mode are unchanged.

Duplicate-work check: I searched open issues and PRs for `enforce_eager`, `speculator`, and MRV2 draft eager handling. The related open SpeculativeConfig refactor (#36979) changes configuration initialization but does not modify MRV2 speculator CUDA graph mode resolution.

This contribution was implemented with assistance from OpenAI Codex. I reviewed every changed line and validated the behavior described below.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py \
  -k draft_speculator -v

.venv/bin/ruff check \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py

.venv/bin/ruff format --check \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py
```

The unit test covers Eagle, multi-module MTP, and DFlash speculators with nested `enforce_eager=True`, `False`, and `None`.

Runtime validation used an equivalent DFlash/DSpark eager-mode resolution on an A2 8x910B3 system with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP8/EP8, target `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, and draft `enforce_eager=true`. Target FULL graphs remained enabled, draft graph capture was skipped, and all 8 requests in an 8K-input/4K-output concurrency-8 serving run completed successfully.

## Test Result

- Pytest: `9 passed, 3 deselected`
- Ruff check: passed
- Ruff format check: passed
- `py_compile`: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed

title: [ROCM] Enablement of Hy4-Preview on gfx950
body:
## Purpose

:construction: WIP: this PR is a draft as I self-review and polish these changes :construction: 

Add initial AMD ROCm/gfx950 support for Hy4-preview on top of #54160.

This change:

- Adds a self-contained `vllm/models/hy_v4/amd/` implementation for the model, MTP, attention, iHC, MoE, and ROCm backend.
- Dispatches `HYV4ForCausalLM` and `HYV4MTP` to the AMD implementation on ROCm.
- Keeps the NVIDIA implementation unchanged and prevents AMD code from importing NVIDIA-specific modules.
- Adds a Hy4 ROCm sparse-MLA backend that preserves learned attention sinks.
- Generalizes the ROCm Triton ragged sparse-attention kernel to support Hy4's absorbed 512 latent + 64 RoPE dimensions and a 512-wide value output, while preserving existing DeepSeek V4 behavior.
- Reuses the ROCm/AITER sparse indexer and portable eager iHC and gated-MLA paths.
- Enables Hy4 model-registry import tests on ROCm.

This is an initial correctness-oriented bring-up. 

- requires an unquantized FP16/BF16 KV cache
- FP8 KV cache is explicitly unsupported for now, but I plan to add support before I mark this as ready for review.

No documentation update is included because model registration and user-facing Hy4 documentation are provided by the parent Hy4 PR.

title: [Spec Decode][Perf] Support vocab-parallel DSpark top-k for DeepSeek V4
body:
# [Spec Decode][Perf] Support vocab-parallel DSpark top-k for DeepSeek V4

## Purpose

The existing `dspark_draft_topk` optimization limits each sequential DSpark
Markov projection to the top-k base-logit candidates, but it is currently
usable only by Qwen3's single-rank draft vocabulary. DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731
uses a full target vocabulary sharded across tensor-parallel ranks, so its
greedy DSpark path still all-gathers dense logits and evaluates the Markov
projection over the full vocabulary for every speculative step.

This change extends the opt-in path to DeepSeek-V4 DSpark:

- select top-k base logits locally on every vocabulary shard;
- all-gather only candidate values and global token IDs, then select the
  global top-k;
- gather the corresponding rows from the replicated Markov head and score
  only those candidates;
- sample the winning candidate sequentially, preserving the dependency on the
  previous draft token; and
- keep the existing dense path unchanged unless `dspark_draft_topk` is set.

For TP=8 and top-k=512, candidate communication is proportional to
`2 * k * TP` entries per row instead of the full 129,280-token vocabulary.
The new path is currently limited to greedy DeepSeek-V4 DSpark drafting; the
existing dense sampling path remains in use whenever draft logits are needed.

There is no linked issue.

## Duplicate-work check

Immediately before preparing this draft, open upstream PRs were searched for
`DeepSeek V4 DSpark topk`, `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, `DSpark speculative
decoding`, and `sparse top-k draft logits`. No open PR implements this
vocab-parallel DeepSeek path.

- #49969 is the merged Qwen3 top-k implementation that this change extends.
  Its PR explicitly scoped support to Qwen3 and its dense top-k path assumes
  locally materialized draft logits.
- #50737 optimizes the exact dense Markov projection with in-place `addmm`.
  It is complementary, though it overlaps several DSpark files and may require
  rebasing.
- #51209 reuses sparse-attention indexer results across DeepSeek-V4 layers. It
  does not change DSpark vocabulary scoring or Markov projection.
- #53972 optimizes the initial DSpark mHC projection. It does not change draft
  logits or Markov scoring.
- #52165 changes DeepSeek-V4 DSpark checkpoint detection and overlaps the
  speculative configuration file, but it does not add a top-k execution path.

## Test plan and results

Focused tests on the rebased branch:

```text
<active-env>/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/test_config.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py \
  -k 'draft_topk or gathered_markov or deepseek or vocab_parallel' -v

24 passed, 214 deselected
```

The tests cover configuration propagation, sparse scores versus dense scores,
the sequential previous-token dependency, and the case where top-k is larger
than one local vocabulary shard.

Relevant tests before the final rebase also passed:

```text
<active-env>/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -k dspark \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py \
  tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py -q

35 passed, 228 deselected
```

Applicable checks passed on all changed files:

```text
pre-commit run ruff-format --files <changed files>
pre-commit run ruff-check --files <changed files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <changed source files>
git diff --check
```

After rebasing to upstream commit `d1922cb5a7`, the exact model served on eight
H200 GPUs with TP=8, expert parallelism, FP8 KV cache, seven greedy DSpark
tokens, and `dspark_draft_topk=512`. A 32-request, 1024-input/128-output smoke
run completed 32/32 requests with no illegal memory access.

The submitted patch was also applied without conflicts to a local verification
branch at upstream commit `56058fd572`. Its stable patch ID exactly matches the
fork commit; the focused 24-test suite, mypy, commit hooks, and diff check were
rerun on that current-main verification head.

## H200 profile and serving A/B

The controlled A/B was collected on upstream commit `9236159bb6` before the
final rebase. Both arms used the same source and server configuration except
for `dspark_draft_topk=512` in the candidate:

```text
8 x NVIDIA H200, TP=8, expert parallelism
FP8 KV cache, DSpark with 7 speculative tokens, greedy drafting
max_num_batched_tokens=8192, max_num_seqs=256
1024 input tokens -> 128 output tokens
32 prompts, concurrency=32, ignore_eos, temperature=0
five steady-state measurements per arm
```

| Metric | Dense baseline | top-k=512 | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Output throughput | 830.80 token/s | 881.45 token/s | **+6.10%** |
| Per-run median TTFT | 493.38 ms | 461.62 ms | **-6.44%** |
| Per-run median TPOT | 23.50 ms | 23.02 ms | **-2.05%** |
| Draft acceptance | 47.66% | 51.36% | **+3.70 pp** |

For output throughput, an independent bootstrap with 200,000 resamples gave a
95% interval of `[+1.49%, +10.00%]`. The exact one-sided permutation p-value
was 0.01984 and the exact one-sided Mann-Whitney p-value was 0.04762.

This is an end-to-end result, not a pure kernel-time attribution. The candidate
also raised draft acceptance by 3.70 percentage points, so the measured gain
combines reduced computation/communication with the changed truncated proposal
distribution. A low-concurrency probe was noisy and did not establish a gain;
the feature therefore remains opt-in rather than becoming a default.

The TP8 trace attributed 59.71% of rank-0 GPU kernel time to communication and
showed 64 full-vocabulary all-gathers plus 224 sequential Markov projections in
the captured window. This optimization directly targets those two repeated
operations.

## Model evaluation

A paired GSM8K smoke evaluation used 100 questions, five-shot prompting,
greedy generation, at most 256 new tokens, and concurrency 32:

| Arm | Accuracy | Invalid rate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Dense baseline | 0.96 | 0.00 |
| top-k=512 | 0.96 | 0.00 |

Target-model verification remains unchanged, so speculative decoding preserves
the target distribution; this eval checks the concrete serving path for a
regression signal.

## AI-assistance and submitter review

AI assistance was used for profiling, implementation, testing, benchmarking,
statistical analysis, and drafting this description.

- [x] The human submitter reviewed every changed line.
- [x] The human submitter understands and can defend the implementation and
  all reported measurements.
- [x] Duplicate-work checks were rerun immediately before publication.
- [x] The final commit contains no private benchmark artifacts or generated
  files.

title: [Bug] hy_v4 (Hy4-preview): degenerate output with FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120 — the only available sparse backend on SM120
body:
**Summary**: On RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, CC 12.0), serving Hy4-preview (`hy_v4`, merged in #54160) produces degenerate output (`" of of of of…"` at temperature 0 from any prompt, including 5-token prompts) when using `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`. This is the only selectable sparse-MLA backend on SM120: the prescribed `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` gates to `major in [9, 10]`, and hy_v4 sparse layers correctly refuse dense fallback.

**Setup**: 2 nodes × 4× RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q 96 GB, TP8 over Ray, image `vllm/vllm-openai:hy4-preview` (+ ray), driver 595.71.05. Weights: an experts-only NVFP4 cast of the official MXFP8 checkpoint (produced locally to fit 768 GB VRAM; expert tensors validated against `nvfp4_emulation_utils.dequantize_to_dtype`, 0.094 rel err vs the MXFP8 reference). Server reaches HEALTHY at `--max-model-len 530000`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`.

**Elimination evidence** (all A/B on the same live cluster, identical degenerate output in every case):
- MoE expert backends ×3: `flashinfer_cutlass`, `marlin`, `emulation` — byte-identical output, so expert kernels/quant path exonerated.
- MXFP8 linear kernels ×2: `FlashInferCutlassMxfp8LinearKernel` and (via `VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS`) `MarlinMxfp8LinearKernel` — identical.
- Model-side code verified consistent with Tencent's reference implementation: elementwise sigmoid gate applied to decompressed attn_out; `is_neox_style=False`; sink params dumped from the checkpoint are modest (per-layer means 0.1–0.7, max 3.2), so the backend's warned sink-disable should be mild, not catastrophic.
- 5-token prompt repro ⇒ indexer *scoring* exonerated (top-k ⊇ all tokens).
- The backend rejects `bfloat16` KV (`kv_cache_dtype not supported`), so fp8-KV numerics cannot be ruled out by dtype A/B — fp8-class KV is mandatory on this path.

**Remaining suspects, in the backend**: fp8_ds_mla KV numerics on SM120, and/or the sparse kernel's handling of hy_v4's *gated* DSA / IndexCache (this backend was validated for DeepSeek/GLM shapes; hy_v4 is its first gated-MLA consumer). Possibly a FlashInfer-side issue — happy to re-file there if triage points that way.

**Ask**: (a) is hy_v4 × FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120 expected to work, or should SM120 be documented as unsupported for hy_v4? (b) If expected: full logs and configs available on request.

title: [Bugfix] Upcast E8M0 block scales on every platform, not just ROCm/XPU
body:
> This pull request was developed and reviewed with support from the Linux Club of Peking University (LCPU). For questions, please contact linuxclub@pku.edu.cn.

Fixes #47818


## Purpose

`w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` decodes exponent-only E8M0 block scales to fp32
before launching the Triton kernel, because Triton cannot bind an
`torch.float8_e8m0fnu` tensor as a kernel argument. That decode is currently
gated on the platform:

```python
# vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py
# Triton cannot currently bind E8M0 scale tensors directly. On ROCm,
# DeepSeek-V4 checkpoints store block scales in exponent-only E8M0 format,
# so decode them to fp32 before launching the kernel.
if current_platform.is_rocm() or current_platform.is_xpu():
    if As.dtype == torch.float8_e8m0fnu:
        As = _upcast_e8m0_to_fp32(As).contiguous()
    if Bs.dtype == torch.float8_e8m0fnu:
        Bs = _upcast_e8m0_to_fp32(Bs).contiguous()
```

The limitation is Triton's, not the platform's. The checkpoint format is also
not platform-specific: DeepSeek-V4-style checkpoints ship E8M0 block scales
regardless of which GPU loads them. On CUDA, any path that reaches this Triton
fallback with E8M0 scales therefore hands Triton a dtype it cannot bind.

This is what #47818 runs into on SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 / Blackwell), where the
CUTLASS C3X `dispatch_scaled_mm` path is unavailable and the Triton fallback is
taken.

## Change

Drop the platform condition; keep the dtype condition, which is the one that
actually decides whether work is needed. Scales that are not E8M0 are untouched,
so this is a no-op for every existing configuration.

Net: 11 lines in one file, plus a regression test.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py -k e8m0 -q
```

`test_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_e8m0_scales` runs the same matmul twice — once with
fp32 scales, once with the identical values as `torch.float8_e8m0fnu` — and
asserts the outputs are bit-identical. The scales are powers of two
(`torch.exp2(randint(-8, 0))`) so they round-trip E8M0 ↔ fp32 exactly and
`torch.equal` is the right assertion rather than a tolerance.

The module is skipped below SM90, so this needs an SM90+ device.

## Test Result

On an RTX 5090 (SM120, `torch.cuda.get_device_capability() == (12, 0)`), against
`main` @ `87b9b5b`:

Without the fix — the exact failure mode from #47818, surfacing as Triton
refusing to bind the dtype:

```
E       KeyError: 'float8_e8m0fnu'
.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/triton/_utils.py:119: KeyError
1 failed, 477 deselected in 1.22s
```

With the fix:

```
1 passed, 477 deselected in 1.20s
```

The rest of `test_block_fp8.py` is unaffected: no other test in the file uses
E8M0 scales, so the dtype condition is never true for them.

## AI assistance

This PR contains AI-generated code. The analysis and patch were produced with
Claude; the submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the test.

```

```

title: [Bugfix][PP] Never drop a decoding request from the sampled-token broadcast
body:
> This pull request was developed and reviewed with support from the Linux Club of Peking University (LCPU). For questions, please contact linuxclub@pku.edu.cn.

## Purpose

Under pipeline parallelism, `compute_need_sampled_mask` decides which rows of a
batch get their sampled token (and the draft block proposed from it) broadcast
back to the earlier PP stages. It currently excludes two kinds of row:

```python
# vllm/v1/worker/gpu/pp_utils.py
produces_sample = old_computed + input_batch.num_scheduled_tokens >= prefill_len
# Exclude requests that we know are finished.
not_finishing = np.maximum(old_computed, prefill_len) + 1 < max_seq_len
need_sampled_mask = produces_sample & not_finishing
```

The first exclusion is sound. A non-final prefill chunk provably produces no
sample, and both the last rank (`get_num_sampled_and_rejected` zeroes
`num_sampled`/`num_rejected`) and the earlier ranks
(`post_update_num_computed_tokens`) then advance `num_computed_tokens` by the
full query length, so the stages stay in step without a broadcast.

The second is not. Whether a request stops is only known *after* sampling, and
under speculative decoding `num_computed_tokens` advances several tokens per
step, so it can overrun `prompt_len + max_tokens` while the scheduler is still
running the request. `not_finishing` is then False for a row that is still
decoding, and its broadcast is skipped.

The consequence is permanent divergence, not a dropped token. The earlier
stages' `last_sampled_tokens` and `draft_tokens` freeze at their last received
values while the last rank keeps advancing its own. The earlier stage then
re-embeds the same token block at ever-advancing positions — degenerate,
repeating output — and writes KV at positions the last stage never used, so the
damage persists in the request's blocks.

Requests that really do finish are already handled downstream: the `req_idx_gen`
check in `get_prev_sampled_outputs` drops the update once the slot is freed. The
guard therefore buys nothing and costs correctness.

## Change

- `pp_utils.py`: drop the `not_finishing` exclusion; keep the prefill-chunk one.
  The docstring now states why the remaining exclusion is the only sound one, so
  the guard does not get reintroduced.
- `model_runner.py`: stop gathering `max_seq_len` per step under PP. Nothing
  reads `InputBatch.max_seq_len_np` once the guard is gone. (The field itself is
  left in place; removing it can be a separate cleanup.)
- `tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py`: new, four cases.

Net: 3 files, ~30 lines of production code changed, no behaviour change for any
row that was previously included.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py -q
```

Two of the four tests pin behaviour that must not change (a non-final prefill
chunk is still excluded; an all-prefill batch still returns `None`). The other
two are the regression:

- `test_keeps_decoding_request_past_its_length_cap` builds the exact shape the
  old predicate mishandled — `num_computed=14176`, `prefill_len=12175`,
  `max_seq_len=14175`, i.e. already overrun — and asserts the row stays in the
  mask.
- `test_does_not_depend_on_max_seq_len` asserts the mask is computable without
  `max_seq_len_np` at all.

## Test Result

Against `main` with the fix:

```
tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py ....                                    [100%]
4 passed in 1.67s
```

Against `main` without it, the two regression cases fail and the two
behaviour-pinning cases pass:

```
FAILED test_pp_utils.py::test_keeps_decoding_request_past_its_length_cap
FAILED test_pp_utils.py::test_does_not_depend_on_max_seq_len
2 failed, 2 passed in 1.70s
```

Beyond the unit tests, this fix has been running in production for weeks on a
2-node × 2-GPU deployment (`pipeline_parallel_size=2`, `tensor_parallel_size=2`,
DeepSeek-V4-Flash with `dspark` speculative decoding, K=7), where the symptom
was exactly the one described: a long-running request degenerating into repeated
output while its peers stayed healthy.

## AI assistance

This PR contains AI-generated code. The root-cause analysis and the patch were
produced with Claude; the submitter reviewed every changed line, ran the tests,
and validated the behaviour end-to-end on the deployment described above.

Commits carry:

```
Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
```
