title: [Bug]: structured output can sample unconstrained tokens when the draft hand-off goes stale (spec decode + async scheduling + PP)
body:
> This issue was investigated and reported with support from the Linux Club of Peking University (LCPU). For questions, please contact linuxclub@pku.edu.cn. ## Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ``` ```
## 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary The draft-token hand-off from the worker to the scheduler carries no identity: `DraftTokensHandler` holds a single slot that every `execute_model` overwrites. When a structured-output request's drafts are lost that way, its `-1` placeholders survive into `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask`, which then writes `_full_mask` — **every token in the vocabulary allowed** — at rows that are real sampling positions. The worker verifies the genuine drafts from its own GPU-resident copy, so acceptance can walk straight into those rows and emit up to `num_speculative_tokens` tokens with no grammar constraint at all. The failure is silent by construction: the mask fails **open**. When the emitted tokens happen to be grammar-legal the request is quietly corrupted and keeps generating from a poisoned context; when they are not, the request dies with ``` ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py] Failed to advance FSM for request for tokens . ERROR [scheduler.py] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [30, 128825, ...] for request . Terminating request. ``` **This is latent on `main` today** — see "Reachability" below. It becomes live the moment a pipeline-parallel-capable drafter lands, which is why it seems worth fixing before that happens rather than after. All line numbers below are `main` @ `87b9b5b`. ### The chain **1. The scheduler installs `-1` placeholders for the next step's drafts.** `vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py:42-44` ```python # Add placeholders for the new draft/spec tokens. # We will update the actual spec token ids in the worker process. request.spec_token_ids = self._spec_token_placeholders # [-1] * K ``` **2. They are back-filled from a single, unidentified slot.** The deferred-sampling branch (`vllm/v1/engine/core.py:678`, back-fill at `:736`) calls `take_draft_token_ids()`, which resolves to `DraftTokensHandler` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/utils.py:11`): ```python def set_draft_tokens(self, input_batch, draft_tokens) -> None: self.req_ids = input_batch.req_ids # :25 — overwritten every step self.num_draft_tokens = draft_tokens.shape[1] if not input_batch.has_structured_output_reqs: self.draft_tokens_np = None # and cleared by plain batches return ``` No step id, no batch id, no history. The slot is correct only when the batch that last reached the worker covers the same requests as the step being sampled. That holds at `pipeline_parallel_size == 1`, where `max_concurrent_batches` is 2 (`vllm/config/vllm.py:563`): the deferred branch pops one entry and blocks on it, and the slot ends up holding exactly the predecessor's drafts. Under pipeline parallelism it does not hold. `max_concurrent_batches` becomes `pp_size + 1`, and `next_decode_eligible_step = current_step + pp_size` (`async_scheduler.py:48`) alternates requests across microbatches, so the batch that wrote the slot is a *different request set* than the one being sampled. There is also a second, more direct path (`utils.py:48-51`): ```python else: # This case only happens when async scheduling is disabled. draft_token_ids = [[-1] * self.num_draft_tokens for _ in self.req_ids] ``` That comment is not accurate: the branch is taken whenever the last batch to reach `set_draft_tokens` had no structured-output requests, which a plain-only microbatch does routinely. **3. A surviving `-1` makes the bitmask fail open.** `vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py:301-306` ```python for i, token in enumerate(req_tokens): self._fill_bitmasks(((grammar, cumulative_index, apply_bitmask),)) # row i filled FIRST advance_grammar = apply_bitmask if token == -1: # :304 apply_bitmask = False # rows i+1.. get _full_mask advance_grammar = False ``` `_full_mask` is `torch.tensor(-1, dtype=torch.int32)` — 32 bits set (`:59`, applied at `:213`) — and `apply_grammar_bitmask` only writes `-inf` where a bit is **0**. "The mask could not be built" therefore renders as "every token is allowed". Note that row 0 is filled *before* `req_tokens[0]` is inspected, so it is always correct. Only rows `1..K-1` go permissive. **4. Meanwhile the model verifies the real drafts, not the `-1`s.** The `-1` exists only in the scheduler's copy. The worker builds `input_ids` from its own GPU-resident `req_states.draft_tokens` via `combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens`, so the rejection sampler verifies genuine draft tokens against rows whose mask allows everything. Accepting any of them emits a token the grammar never allowed. ### Reproduction on stock `main`, without a model `repro.py` below drives the two links directly. It needs a CUDA device (for the handler's copy stream) and the `gpt2` tokenizer; no model weights.
repro.py ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Reproduce the structured-output hole on stock vLLM main, without a model. The end-to-end symptom needs pipeline parallelism, and every draft head whose checkpoint is small enough to test with (Eagle3Llama, MiMoMTP, ...) refuses PP because it does not implement `SupportsPP`, while `create_draft_parallel_config` copies the target's pp_size verbatim. So drive the two links of the chain directly instead; together they are the whole bug. Link A `DraftTokensHandler` keeps ONE slot with no identity, so a batch that does not contain a request destroys that request's drafts. Link B the `-1` placeholders that therefore survive make `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` emit `_full_mask` -- every token allowed -- at rows that are REAL sampling positions, because the worker verifies the genuine drafts from its own GPU-resident copy. Run with the stock venv: .venv/bin/python stock_unit_repro.py """ import sys from types import SimpleNamespace import numpy as np import torch from transformers import AutoTokenizer from vllm.config import StructuredOutputsConfig, VllmConfig from vllm.config.model import ModelConfig from vllm.config.speculative import SpeculativeConfig from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams, StructuredOutputsParams from vllm.v1.request import Request from vllm.v1.structured_output import StructuredOutputManager from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.utils import DraftTokensHandler TOKENIZER = "gpt2" K = 4 ok = True def report(name, holds, detail=""): """Each assertion states an observed fact about the current code. `yes` means the fact holds, which for the Link A/B facts means the bug is present.""" global ok ok = ok and holds print(f" [{'yes' if holds else 'NO '}] {name}{(' ' + detail) if detail else ''}") # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Link A: the single slot has no identity. # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- def link_a(): print("\nLink A -- DraftTokensHandler keeps one unidentified slot") dev = torch.device("cuda:0") handler = DraftTokensHandler(dev) # Only `req_ids` and `has_structured_output_reqs` are read off the batch. def batch(req_ids, structured): return SimpleNamespace( req_ids=list(req_ids), has_structured_output_reqs=structured ) drafts_a = torch.arange(1, 1 + 2 * K, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev).reshape(2, K) drafts_b = torch.arange(101, 101 + 2 * K, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev).reshape(2, K) # Batch A carries the structured-output request. handler.set_draft_tokens(batch(["gA", "pA"], True), drafts_a) got = handler.get_draft_tokens() report( "drafts for 'gA' are available right after its own batch", "gA" in got.req_ids, f"req_ids={got.req_ids}", ) # Another microbatch runs. Under PP this is the other half of the requests. handler.set_draft_tokens(batch(["gB", "pB"], True), drafts_b) got = handler.get_draft_tokens() report( "after another batch runs, 'gA' can no longer be found", "gA" not in got.req_ids, f"req_ids={got.req_ids} -- gA's drafts are gone, with nothing recording that", ) # A batch with no structured-output request clears the payload entirely and # still overwrites req_ids. get_draft_tokens then returns all -1 for a set of # requests it was never asked about. handler.set_draft_tokens(batch(["p1", "p2"], False), drafts_b) got = handler.get_draft_tokens() all_minus_one = all(all(t == -1 for t in row) for row in got.draft_token_ids) report( "a plain-only batch makes get_draft_tokens return all -1", all_minus_one, f"req_ids={got.req_ids} drafts={got.draft_token_ids}", ) print( " (utils.py comment claims this 'only happens when async " "scheduling is disabled')" ) # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Link B: a surviving -1 turns the mask fully permissive at real positions. # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- def link_b(): print("\nLink B -- surviving -1 makes grammar_bitmask fail OPEN") tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(TOKENIZER) vllm_config = VllmConfig( model_config=ModelConfig(tokenizer=TOKENIZER), structured_outputs_config=StructuredOutputsConfig(backend="xgrammar"), speculative_config=SpeculativeConfig( model="[ngram]", num_speculative_tokens=K ), ) manager = StructuredOutputManager(vllm_config) sampling_params = SamplingParams( structured_outputs=StructuredOutputsParams(json='{"type": "object"}') ) sampling_params.structured_outputs._backend = "xgrammar" sampling_params.update_from_generation_config({}, tokenizer.eos_token_id) prompt = tokenizer.encode('{"a"') request = Request( "req", prompt_token_ids=prompt, sampling_params=sampling_params, pooling_params=None, ) manager.grammar_init(request) while not request.structured_output_request._check_grammar_completion(): pass grammar = request.structured_output_request.grammar assert grammar.accept_tokens(request.request_id, prompt) # This is what the scheduler holds when the back-fill missed: the whole # window is still placeholders. window = [-1] * K bitmask = manager.grammar_bitmask( requests={request.request_id: request}, structured_output_request_ids=[request.request_id], scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={request.request_id: window}, ) assert bitmask is not None and bitmask.shape[0] == K + 1 row0_constrained = not (bitmask[0] == -1).all() report("row 0 is constrained (filled before the -1 is inspected)", row0_constrained) permissive = [i for i in range(1, K) if (bitmask[i] == -1).all()] report( "rows 1..K-1 are fully permissive", permissive == list(range(1, K)), f"rows {permissive} allow every token in the vocabulary", ) # And those rows are real sampling positions: the worker verifies the drafts # from its own GPU copy, so acceptance can walk into them. vocab = tokenizer.vocab_size row = bitmask[1] allowed = int(np.unpackbits(row.view(np.uint8), bitorder="little")[:vocab].sum()) report( "a permissive row allows the entire vocabulary", allowed == vocab, f"{allowed}/{vocab} token ids allowed at a position the model will sample", ) # Contrast: a fully back-filled window keeps every row constrained. Pick the # drafts from the grammar itself -- `validate_tokens` reports the accepted # prefix without advancing -- so this cannot fail on hand-picked token ids # that simply are not legal here. grammar.reset() assert grammar.accept_tokens(request.request_id, prompt) candidate = tokenizer.encode(':"b"')[:K] real = grammar.validate_tokens(list(candidate)) if not real: report("contrast: could not build a legal draft window", False, str(candidate)) else: bitmask2 = manager.grammar_bitmask( requests={request.request_id: request}, structured_output_request_ids=[request.request_id], scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={request.request_id: real}, ) any_permissive = [ i for i in range(bitmask2.shape[0]) if (bitmask2[i] == -1).all() ] report( "with real drafts, no row is permissive", not any_permissive, f"window of {len(real)} real drafts, permissive rows: {any_permissive}", ) def main(): print(f"vLLM under test: {__import__('vllm').__version__}") link_a() link_b() print() if ok: print("BUG REPRODUCED on stock main: the draft hand-off carries no") print("identity, so a request loses its drafts silently, and the grammar") print("bitmask then fails OPEN at real sampling positions.") return 1 print("at least one link no longer holds -- bug not reproduced here") return 0 if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main()) ```
Output on `main` @ `87b9b5b`: ``` vLLM under test: 0.28.1rc1.dev118+g87b9b5b8d Link A -- DraftTokensHandler keeps one unidentified slot [yes] drafts for 'gA' are available right after its own batch req_ids=['gA', 'pA'] [yes] after another batch runs, 'gA' can no longer be found req_ids=['gB', 'pB'] -- gA's drafts are gone, with nothing recording that [yes] a plain-only batch makes get_draft_tokens return all -1 req_ids=['p1', 'p2'] drafts=[[-1, -1, -1, -1], [-1, -1, -1, -1]] (utils.py comment claims this 'only happens when async scheduling is disabled') Link B -- surviving -1 makes grammar_bitmask fail OPEN [yes] row 0 is constrained (filled before the -1 is inspected) [yes] rows 1..K-1 are fully permissive rows [1, 2, 3] allow every token in the vocabulary [yes] a permissive row allows the entire vocabulary 50257/50257 token ids allowed at a position the model will sample [yes] with real drafts, no row is permissive window of 3 real drafts, permissive rows: [] BUG REPRODUCED on stock main: the draft hand-off carries no identity, so a request loses its drafts silently, and the grammar bitmask then fails OPEN at real sampling positions. ``` ### Reachability: why this is latent upstream today The end-to-end symptom needs `pipeline_parallel_size >= 2`, and that is currently unreachable for any small public checkpoint: - `create_draft_parallel_config` copies the target's pp_size to the drafter verbatim (`vllm/config/speculative.py:1647`), and `verify_with_parallel_config` then rejects any drafter that does not implement `SupportsPP`. - Of the registered draft heads, only `Glm4MoeLiteMTP` and `BailingMoeV3MTPModel` implement it. `Eagle3LlamaForCausalLM`, `MiMoMTP`, `DeepSeekMTP` and `DeepSeekV4MTP` do not. - Relaxing that gate is not sufficient either: with the check bypassed, `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` + `RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3` at `pp=2` fails while *constructing* the drafter on a non-last rank (`llama_eagle3.py:166` → `llama.py:282`). We hit the symptom in production because our deployment carries a local relaxation for a side-model drafter (a DSpark head, which runs on the last stage rather than being partitioned across stages) plus the PP plumbing to broadcast draft tokens between stages. Any upstream change that makes a side-model drafter work under PP — which seems a natural thing to want — turns this from latent into live. ### Field evidence (from that deployment) 2 nodes x 2 GPUs, `pipeline_parallel_size=2`, `tensor_parallel_size=2`, DeepSeek-V4-Flash with `dspark` K=7, xgrammar backend. | probe | result | |---|---| | `tool_choice=required`, solo into an idle engine | passes 3/3 | | `tool_choice=required`, one other grammar request decoding | **fails 3/3** | | `json_schema` | **fails** | | `tool_choice=auto`, `json_object`, plain text | passes (permissive grammar hides it) | | `temperature=0` | passes (the resample kernel returns early on the masked argmax) | | speculative decoding disabled | passes | Permissive grammars pass because an unconstrained token is usually still legal, which is why this presents for a long time as "one agent out of six occasionally emits garbage" rather than as a hard error. Instrumenting `update_draft_token_ids_in_output` to classify each structured-output request in the deferred `SchedulerOutput` (6 concurrent `tool_choice=required` requests, 2400+ deferred steps): ``` MISSING (absent from draft_token_ids.req_ids) 100% ALL_MINUS1 (present, all drafts -1) 0% REAL ~0% ``` Retaining the last 4 snapshots and reporting at what depth the request's drafts would have been found: ``` MISSING@depth1 == MISSING 100% ``` The drafts are never actually unavailable — they are exactly one snapshot away, 100% of the time, which is the signature of a single slot under alternating PP microbatches. Solo, the back-fill succeeds ~85% of the time, which is why this only shows up under concurrency. Histogram of where the first `-1` lands in the K=7 window, same load: ``` first -1 at index -> {0: 2710, 1: 6, 2: 4, 3: 3, 4: 4, 5: 21, 6: 12, 7: 1309} ``` 66% of grammar rows had no usable draft at all, i.e. rows 1..7 permissive. ### Relationship to #44006 #44006 made the **bonus** row stay constrained after `-1` padding, and `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py:144` asserts exactly that: ```python assert not (bitmask[-1] == -1).all() ``` Rows `1..K-1` are deliberately left permissive, on the assumption that a `-1` means "this draft was rejected by `validate_tokens`, so the sampler will reject it too". That assumption is sound when the `-1` really is a rejection signal. It is violated here, where `-1` means "the drafts never reached the scheduler" — and no test covers those rows. `rejection_sampler_utils.py:767` already resamples a `-1` position straight from the target distribution and needs no change. ### Suggested fix Two independent pieces; the first is the correctness fix and stands alone. 1. **Fail closed.** When a structured-output request's scheduled spec tokens still contain `-1` at index `j`, mark drafts `j..K-1` invalid (`is_valid_draft = draft_sampled >= 0`) so the accepted length cannot run past the last row with a real mask. Rows `0..j` are correctly masked, so row `j` still supplies the step's token under the right constraint. Cost: that step gets no speculative speed-up. 2. **Give the hand-off an identity.** Snapshot `req_states.draft_tokens` where `prepare_inputs` feeds it into `input_ids` — at *consumption* time, not proposal time — tagged with the scheduler's step counter, and retain the last few. The scheduler then asks for the snapshot belonging to the step it is sampling, by equality, instead of taking whatever ran last. A miss falls back to (1), so the failure mode is the conservative one rather than a wrong mask. Both are implemented and running in our deployment. Measured effect of (2) on top of (1), 5 concurrent requests, aggregate decode throughput: | grammar + plain | (1) only | (1)+(2) | |---|---|---| | 1 + 4 | 235.6 | 256.0 | | 3 + 2 | 170.7 | 260.2 | | 5 + 0 | 111.9 | **276.8** | With (2), grammar requests decode at 52–58 tok/s against a 52.5 tok/s plain-text baseline — the speculative speed-up is fully recovered. Back-fill hit rate goes to 100%, and bitmask rows carrying a real mask from 32% to 96.5%. Happy to open PRs for both if this looks like the right direction. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Searched existing issues and asked the documentation chatbot.

title: [Bugfix] Don't let a structured-output request sample from an unmasked row
body:
> This pull request was developed and reviewed with support from the Linux Club of Peking University (LCPU). For questions, please contact linuxclub@pku.edu.cn. ## Purpose Part of #54437. `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` constrains a row only while `apply_bitmask` holds, and a `-1` placeholder in the scheduled draft window sets `seen_padding`, so every row after it is filled with `_full_mask` — every token in the vocabulary allowed: ```python # vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py for i, token in enumerate(req_tokens): apply_bitmask = not failed and not seen_padding and i >= constraint_start self._fill_bitmasks(((grammar, cumulative_index, apply_bitmask),)) if token == -1: seen_padding = True ``` That is sound when the `-1` means "`validate_tokens` rejected this draft": the first `-1` then sits at exactly the draft the grammar rejected, that draft's own row is still masked, so it is rejected and acceptance never reaches the permissive rows. It is not sound when the `-1` means "the drafts never reached the scheduler", which happens because the draft hand-off carries no identity — `DraftTokensHandler` keeps one slot that every `execute_model` overwrites (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/utils.py`), and it also clears the payload entirely for a batch with no structured-output requests. The worker meanwhile verifies the genuine drafts from its own GPU-resident `req_states.draft_tokens`, so acceptance can walk straight into rows that constrain nothing and the request emits tokens the grammar never allowed. #54437 has the full chain, a model-free reproduction on `main`, and field measurements. This PR is the fail-closed half: it makes the permissive rows unreachable regardless of why the drafts went missing. The identity fix for the hand-off is a separate change. **Not a duplicate of #56802.** That PR implements the other half of #54437 — identity for the hand-off, so the drafts are not lost in the first place. It is complementary: its lookup miss path falls back to exactly the invalidation this PR adds, so on a miss without this PR the bitmask still fails open. ## Change Carry, per structured-output request, how many leading drafts the bitmask actually constrained, and invalidate the drafts from that index on, so `is_valid_draft = draft_sampled >= 0` pins the accepted length before sampling can reach a permissive row. - `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`: `get_grammar_bitmask` fills `num_acceptable_drafts` with `len(strip_speculative_padding(window))`, reusing the helper #48200 introduced. - `vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py`: `GrammarOutput.num_acceptable_drafts`, a defaulted field, so existing constructors keep working. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/structured_outputs.py`: `grammar_invalid_drafts` turns that into a mask over logit rows, built on device: a draft is invalid when its local position exceeds its request's `num_acceptable_drafts`. The local position is `expanded_local_pos`, which `expand_idx_mapping` derives from the device `cu_num_logits` — the same (request, position) keying `apply_grammar_bitmask` uses, so it stays correct when adaptive verification trims drafts on device and `cu_num_logits_np` is only an upper bound. When every request's scheduled drafts are within its limit (fully back-filled, the normal case) it returns `None` on the CPU and launches nothing. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`: `sample()` calls it after applying the bitmask and hands the mask to the rejection sampler. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler.py`: verification runs against `draft_sampled.masked_fill(mask, -1)`. `apply_sampling_params` and the watermarking context still receive the real draft ids, so penalties and bad-words are unaffected. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/batch_shard.py`: shard the new per-request list the same way as the bitmask. No kernel change: `rejection_sampler_utils` already resamples a `-1` position straight from the target distribution rather than from the residual. That matters — `max(p - q, 0)` is the residual of a *genuine* rejection, and forcing one where `p ≈ q` collapses it across the vocabulary. When the drafts are fully back-filled nothing is invalidated and behaviour is unchanged. Absent the field — an older scheduler, or warmup — the whole window is invalidated, which is the conservative choice. Production diff is 85 added / 3 removed lines across those six files. ## Test Plan ```bash # Unit coverage for the new helper, plus the suites this PR's call paths touch. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py \ tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py -q ``` `tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py` — 5 cases covering `grammar_invalid_drafts`: whole window, partial window, nothing to do, per-request offset, and **adaptive verification with an uneven reallocation** (the device layout differs from `cu_num_logits_np`). **End-to-end reproduction.** Not committed, per review. Save the file below as `tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_fail_closed.py` and run it on `main` and on this branch: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_fail_closed.py -q ``` It drives the real `GPUModelRunner.sample()` → `apply_grammar_bitmask` → `RejectionSampler` path with a bitmask whose leading rows carry a real mask and whose later rows are `_full_mask`, and with the drafts the worker holds on the GPU disagreeing with the scheduler's padded copy, which is what a lost hand-off produces. Temperature 0, one request, four logit rows, so it is deterministic.
tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_fail_closed.py ```python # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project """Acceptance must stop at the last bitmask row that carries a real mask. `grammar_bitmask` stops constraining rows once it meets a -1 placeholder in the scheduled draft window, and the worker verifies the drafts it holds on the GPU rather than the scheduler's padded copy. When the two disagree -- the hand-off lost a step's drafts, see #54437 -- acceptance can walk into a row where every token is allowed. The grammar here admits only LEGAL. The scheduled window is back-filled one draft deep, so rows 0 and 1 carry a real mask and rows 2.. are `_full_mask`, while the drafts on the GPU would carry acceptance into row 2 and emit ILLEGAL. """ from types import SimpleNamespace import numpy as np import pytest import torch from vllm.platforms import current_platform from vllm.utils.math_utils import cdiv from vllm.v1.core.sched.output import GrammarOutput from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner import GPUModelRunner from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.states import NO_LOGPROBS from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.rejection_sampler import RejectionSampler from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.structured_outputs import StructuredOutputsWorker VOCAB = 128 K = 3 # drafts per step NUM_LOGITS = K + 1 # + the bonus row LEGAL = 7 ILLEGAL = 99 # Index of the first -1 in the scheduled window: rows 0..1 are masked. NUM_ACCEPTABLE = 1 def _bitmask() -> np.ndarray: """Rows 0..NUM_ACCEPTABLE constrained to LEGAL, the rest fully permissive.""" mask = np.zeros((NUM_LOGITS, cdiv(VOCAB, 32)), dtype=np.int32) for row in range(NUM_LOGITS): if row <= NUM_ACCEPTABLE: mask[row, LEGAL // 32] = 1 << (LEGAL % 32) else: mask[row, :] = -1 # every token allowed return mask def _input_batch(device: torch.device) -> SimpleNamespace: cu_np = np.array([0, NUM_LOGITS], dtype=np.int32) # draft_sampled = input_ids[logits_indices]; entry i + 1 is draft i, so the # drafts the GPU holds are [LEGAL, LEGAL, ILLEGAL]. input_ids = torch.tensor( [LEGAL, LEGAL, LEGAL, ILLEGAL], dtype=torch.int32, device=device ) return SimpleNamespace( num_reqs=1, req_ids=["g"], num_draft_tokens=K, num_draft_tokens_per_req=np.array([K], dtype=np.int32), input_ids=input_ids, logits_indices=torch.arange(NUM_LOGITS, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), positions=torch.arange(NUM_LOGITS, dtype=torch.int64, device=device), cu_num_logits_np=cu_np, cu_num_logits=torch.from_numpy(cu_np).to(device), idx_mapping_np=np.array([0], dtype=np.int32), idx_mapping=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), expanded_idx_mapping=torch.zeros(NUM_LOGITS, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), expanded_local_pos=torch.arange(NUM_LOGITS, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), seq_lens=torch.tensor([64], dtype=torch.int32, device=device), seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound=torch.tensor([64], dtype=torch.int32), ) def _logits(device: torch.device) -> torch.Tensor: """Every row prefers its own draft, so nothing but the mask can reject one.""" logits = torch.zeros(NUM_LOGITS, VOCAB, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) logits[0, LEGAL] = 10.0 logits[1, LEGAL] = 10.0 logits[2, ILLEGAL] = 10.0 # row 2 is permissive, so this wins there logits[3, LEGAL] = 10.0 return logits def _rejection_sampler(device: torch.device) -> RejectionSampler: sampler = object.__new__(RejectionSampler) sampler.num_speculative_steps = K sampler.enable_adaptive_verification = False sampler.use_block_verification = False sampler.synthetic_conditional_rates = None sampler.watermark_key = None zeros_f = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) # greedy sampler.sampler = SimpleNamespace( compute_nans=False, logprobs_mode="raw_logprobs", use_fp64_gumbel=False, apply_sampling_params=lambda logits, *args, **kwargs: logits, sampling_states=SimpleNamespace( temperature=SimpleNamespace(gpu=zeros_f), seeds=SimpleNamespace(gpu=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)), max_num_logprobs=lambda _: NO_LOGPROBS, ), req_states=SimpleNamespace( prefill_len=SimpleNamespace( gpu=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device) ) ), ) return sampler @pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="Requires CUDA") def test_acceptance_stops_at_the_last_masked_row(): device = torch.device("cuda") input_batch = _input_batch(device) logits = _logits(device) runner = object.__new__(GPUModelRunner) runner.device = device runner.vocab_size = VOCAB runner.batch_sharder = None runner.sampler = None runner.model = SimpleNamespace(compute_logits=lambda hidden: logits) runner.rejection_sampler = _rejection_sampler(device) runner.speculator = SimpleNamespace(draft_logits=None) runner.structured_outputs_worker = StructuredOutputsWorker( max_num_logits=NUM_LOGITS, vocab_size=VOCAB, device=device, mask_stride=NUM_LOGITS, num_bonus_tokens=1, ) grammar_output = GrammarOutput(["g"], _bitmask()) # The scheduler reports how many leading drafts the bitmask constrained. # Absent on an older scheduler, where the whole window is invalidated. grammar_output.num_acceptable_drafts = [NUM_ACCEPTABLE] hidden = torch.zeros(NUM_LOGITS, 8, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) sampler_output, num_sampled, _ = runner.sample(hidden, input_batch, grammar_output) accepted = int(num_sampled[0].item()) emitted = sampler_output.sampled_token_ids[0, :accepted].tolist() assert ILLEGAL not in emitted, ( f"emitted {emitted}: a draft verified against a permissive row was " f"accepted, so the request sampled with no grammar constraint" ) # Draft 0 may be accepted; draft 1 must not be, because accepting it moves # sampling into row 2, which constrains nothing. assert accepted == NUM_ACCEPTABLE + 1 assert emitted == [LEGAL] * accepted ```
## Test Result End-to-end reproduction on `main` @ `2798f668`: ``` E AssertionError: emitted [7, 7, 99, 7]: a draft verified against a permissive row was accepted, so the request sampled with no grammar constraint E assert 99 not in [7, 7, 99, 7] 1 failed, 14 warnings in 1.00s ``` Token 7 is the only token the grammar admits; token 99 is one it never admits. On this branch, same base: ``` 1 passed, 14 warnings in 1.26s ``` and the Test Plan selection is `71 passed, 1 xfailed`. ### Model evaluation One RTX 4090, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, Qwen3-8B + `Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3` (K=4), `--async-scheduling`, xgrammar. `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --limit 200`: | | exact_match, strict-match | exact_match, flexible-extract | |---|---|---| | `main` @ `0bfc7a15` | 0.925 ± 0.0187 | 0.925 ± 0.0187 | | this PR @ `ec112592`, same base | 0.925 ± 0.0187 | 0.925 ± 0.0187 | gsm8k carries no structured-output requests, so that is the "speculative decoding is untouched" half. For the structured-output half, a mixed grammar + plain load with every grammar response validated against its JSON schema (4 concurrency mixes, 49 grammar requests) gives 0 schema violations, 0 `grammar rejected tokens` and 0 `Failed to advance FSM` on both `main` and this PR — which is the expected result at `pipeline_parallel_size=1`, where the hand-off does not get clobbered. Both were measured at `ec112592`. The review round since changed only how the invalid drafts are located, and that code runs only for a batch that holds a structured-output request whose drafts were not fully back-filled — which neither gsm8k (no grammar requests) nor the `pp=1` load (always fully back-filled) produces. I have not re-run them for that reason; happy to if you want the numbers on the current head. Beyond that: both this change and the identity fix have been running in production on a 2-node x 2-GPU deployment (`pipeline_parallel_size=2`, `tensor_parallel_size=2`, DeepSeek-V4-Flash with `dspark` speculative decoding, K=7, xgrammar). Before them, `tool_choice=required` and `json_schema` failed 100% of the time whenever a second structured-output request was resident; after, 72/72 concurrent grammar requests complete with zero `grammar rejected` lines and zero engine errors. Independently, @xinli-sw [reports](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54442#issuecomment-5822629259) that this PR fixes a `pipeline_parallel_size=2` x `tensor_parallel_size=8` deployment with DSpark (K=3) on 16x B200. ## AI assistance This PR contains AI-generated code. The root-cause analysis, the instrumentation behind the numbers in #54437, and the patch were produced with Claude, with the consumption-time-snapshot idea and the fail-closed requirement contributed by GPT-5.6. The adaptive-verification issue in review was caught by an AI reviewer and fixed with Claude. The submitter reviewed every changed line, ran the tests and the evaluation above, and validated the behaviour end-to-end on the deployment described. Commits carry: ``` Co-authored-by: GPT-5.6 Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) ```

title: [RFC]: Weight version attribution for RL rollouts and Background survey
body:
_Revision 2 (2026-09-28): re-anchored on #48305 §3.8 after #48306 closed; spans are always returned; no request-level scalar; KV provenance is out of scope; corrected the `keep`/`clear_cache` description._

## Motivation

vLLM reports one engine-wide weight-version label (`/weight_info`, #49040), but it does not say which weights produced a given output.

#48305 §3.8 ("Per-Request Weight Provenance") asks for exactly that, at token granularity:
- contiguous `[start, end)` ranges of generated tokens;
- each range tagged with the version used by the model computation;
- together covering every output token and its logprob exactly once;
- a defined contract for streaming, speculative decoding and DP.

This RFC is the design for that item, and it asks for decisions on the points §3.8 leaves open.

### Requests straddle weight updates

`docs/training/async_rl.md` describes `pause(mode="keep")` → update → `resume` as the typical async RL flow. A kept request produces tokens from the old weights before the pause and from the new weights after it. `keep` has two KV variants:

| `pause(mode="keep", ...)` | Running requests after resume |
|---|---|
| `clear_cache=True` (default) | Preempted ([`_finish_pause` → `_reset_caches()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d6cce94fd4221e6f5547e1c00ca5e0c92ab52d6c/vllm/v1/engine/core.py#L874-L879)). On resume their KV is recomputed with the new weights, or loaded from a KV connector that kept an old copy (#57970). |
| `clear_cache=False` | The KV computed with the old weights is kept, and new tokens attend to it. |

The `/pause` docstring still says `clear_cache` is ignored under `keep`. #57970 (draft) fixes the docs, and #57810 fixes that docstring.

Nothing tells the caller where the boundary fell. The official example infers it by sleeping five seconds after pausing and then counting streamed tokens ([`rlhf_async_new_apis.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d6cce94fd4221e6f5547e1c00ca5e0c92ab52d6c/examples/rl/rlhf_async_new_apis.py#L111-L117)).

Requests admitted during the pause wait in the queue and are then served entirely by the new weights (#51476; #51488 keeps that behavior for `keep`).

prime-rl, SkyRL and PipelineRL use `keep` on their async update paths and retain KV by default, and so does NeMo-RL when in-flight weight updates are enabled. #58041 describes the same setup for GLM-5.3 with P/D.

### Existing signals are not enough

Take request R. It generates tokens `[0, 57)` under v7, the weights become v8, and it generates `[57, 128)` under v8.

- `/weight_info` returns v8, the engine's label at query time.
- Draft #53199 records v7, the label at admission. For a request that waited in the queue across the update, that label names weights that produced none of its tokens.
- The controller knows which version it dispatched. It does not know which version was live on a given replica when a token was sampled. Delayed or failed replica updates, DP, P/D and `keep` all break that link, and the fact is gone once the step is over.

Only the engine can record this. Today, token-level attribution requires patching vLLM, and each patch uses its own encoding:
- PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-rl#2957 (a closed prototype): version segments on the `/inference/v1/generate` choice.
- ServiceNow/PipelineRL#150 (`fast-llm` branch): a per-token version appended to each OpenAI chat logprob token string.
- OpenPipe/ART: its own `policy_token_spans`.

Other frameworks record coarser versions on the client side: request start and end versions on chat responses in NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4146 (draft), and a version-keyed `cache_salt` in SkyRL.

### What this is, and is not

The span shape is SGLang's `weight_versions` (sgl-project/sglang#35926, consumed by radixark/miles#1891), so frameworks can share one parser. On top of that shape, this RFC adds a native output-attribution contract to vLLM, with the capture point, the boundary definition, delivery (final output only, including aborts) and `n > 1` written down and tested.

The metadata is a filtering, masking and audit signal:
- **Freshness filtering by the oldest version.** GLM-5 records `(w0, …, wk)` per response and drops it when `current − w0 > τ`.
- **Token-level staleness masking**, as in DeepSeek-V4.1 §5.2.2 and areal-project/AReaL#1722.
- **Per-segment replay** of `routed_experts` and `sampling_mask` for samples that span checkpoints (DeepSeek-V4.1 §5.2.1). This needs the offsets, not just a list of versions.
- **Auditing** partial fleet updates.

It is not an off-policy correction; that stays on rollout logprobs, `routed_experts` and `sampling_mask`. Freshness thresholds, global version assignment and update coordination stay with the RL controller.

A span names the target weights that ran a step. It does not certify which weights computed the KV that the span's tokens attended to:
- With `keep` and `clear_cache=False`, the spans after a boundary attended to KV retained from the older version.
- Salting requests with the weight version (`cache_salt`) prevents new requests from reusing prefix-cache blocks across versions. It does not refresh KV that a kept request already holds.
- P/D version skew and external KV tiers belong to #48312 (cache coherence).

## Proposed Change

### Output

The final output of every output sequence carries `weight_versions`, a list of spans over its output tokens. There is one span per version, so the size grows with updates, not tokens:

```json
"weight_versions": [
  {"version": "v7", "start": 0,  "end": 57},
  {"version": "v8", "start": 57, "end": 128}
]
```

| Case | `weight_versions` |
|---|---|
| No update while the request ran | `[{v7, 0, n}]` |
| Running when a `keep` pause starts, like R (either `clear_cache` value) | `[{v7, 0, 57}, {v8, 57, 128}]` |
| Admitted during the pause | `[{v8, 0, n}]` |
| No output tokens | `[]` |

It is always returned on `CompletionOutput` and on `/inference/v1/generate` choices. OpenAI chat and completions return it on each choice only when the request asks for it, like `return_token_ids`.

### Contract

1. **Coverage.** Each output sequence, including each `n > 1` child, has its own list. Spans are half-open ranges over output-token indexes (prompt excluded), contiguous and in generation order, and together cover every returned token and logprob exactly once. Adjacent spans with the same label merge; A → B → A gives three spans. `routed_experts` rows use their own coordinates and must be converted before slicing.
2. **Capture.** `version` is the label of the target weights whose forward pass sampled the token: under DP, the label of the engine that ran the request; under P/D, the decode instance's label. It is stamped when the step is scheduled, so in-flight steps keep their label. It does not say which weights computed the KV that the token attended to.
3. **Boundaries.** A new span starts when the engine's committed label changes: after a successful update that carries a label, or after `update_weight_version`. The label changes in the same EngineCore call that finishes the update. Failed and draft-only updates leave it unchanged; keeping a partially updated model from serving is #48312's job. Any request that crosses a change gets one span per version, whatever the pause mode: `wait` drains running requests, not preempted ones. LoRA adapters swapped without a pause are not covered until adapters have versions (#48297).
4. **Delivery.** Only on the final output, including aborted ones. Streaming sends it on the last chunk, with offsets over the whole output; streaming-input sessions send it at the end of each input chunk.
5. **Labels.** Opaque strings set by the caller; vLLM never orders them. There is no request-level scalar: `[0]` is the first token's version and `[-1]` the last, and neither is necessarily the oldest. An engine argument sets the initial label; `"default"` means unknown. §3.8's `model_id` (the served model or LoRA adapter) cannot change within a sequence, so it stays at the sequence level.

### Implementation

EngineCore stamps its label on each scheduled step, and every finish path (Python, the Ray client, the Rust server) passes the new label into the finish call. The scheduler attaches the label to `EngineCoreOutput` only when it changes for a request, and `OutputProcessor` turns those change points into spans on the final output. The Rust engine-core client decodes `EngineCoreOutput` too, so its protocol struct changes in the same PR; Rust frontend responses and gRPC follow under #44280. This reuses the transport of #53199, but records the label of the step that ran rather than the label at admission, per `CompletionOutput` rather than per request.

## CC List.

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Core] Add XPress speculative decoding method
body:
## Purpose

Adds **XPress**, a causal refiner for block-diffusion drafters, as a V1 speculative decoding method alongside DFlash and DSpark. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02438

A block-diffusion drafter such as DFlash proposes a whole block in one forward pass, which makes drafting cheap, and decodes it from per-position marginals, which makes it inaccurate: token *k* is drawn without seeing what the drafter chose at *k-1*. The target verifies conditionally, so blocks that are individually plausible but jointly improbable are rejected early, capping acceptance length. 


## Design

XPress adds a small head that reads the drafter's per-position hidden state, a block-global summary and the previous token, fuses them into a rank-256 bottleneck, mixes across the block with a lower-triangular (causal) mixer, and reads back out as a bias on the base logits. Everything except the two vocabulary projections lives in the bottleneck (~80M params, 96% of
which are those two matrices).

Because the mixer is true causal rather than local smooth, the block is resolved by **Jacobi iteration** rather than a left-to right loop: the same call runs K times, each pass re-feeding the previous pass's argmax, so the serial depth is a constant K instead of the block size. Both stages are fixed-shape and loop-free, so the whole draft step is CUDA-graph capturable, which is what makes K passes cheap: they cost K matmuls, not K kernel launches. Two Triton kernels keep a pass at three launches (`xpress_latent_pass`, and a fused add+argmax that writes straight into the block buffer so the [N, B, V] sum is never materialized).

`XPressSpeculator` subclasses `DFlashSpeculator` and overrides only draft generation; attention, KV cache setup and weight sharing are inherited unchanged. Existing files gain **39 lines** of method registration; everything else is new files.

## Test Plan

```bash
# e2e (80GB GPU; public Qwen3-8B + XPress checkpoint pair): full GSM8K at temperature 0,
# accuracy and acceptance metrics against reference values -- same protocol as the
# DFlash and DSpark tests in acceptance_rates/
pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/xpress/test_xpress.py -s
```

The e2e test guards GSM8K accuracy and acceptance rate and length against references, with an upper bound on acceptance length. Note that acceptance length moves by about 0.5% with anything that changes the vLLM config hash, because the hash keys torch.compile's cache and autotuning then picks different kernels, shifting the floating-point reduction order so that near-tie draft tokens flip. Under `enforce_eager=True` the paths are identical. 

<details><summary>Serving and benchmark commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --speculative_config '{"method":"dflash","model":"UIUC-SSAIL/Qwen3-8B-XPress-b16","num_speculative_tokens":15}'

# optional: narrow each Jacobi pass to the drafter's top-C candidates
# (default 512; 0 scores the full vocabulary)
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --speculative_config '{"method":"dflash","model":"UIUC-SSAIL/Qwen3-8B-XPress-b16","num_speculative_tokens":15,"xpress_topc":256}'

# baselines
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --speculative_config '{"method":"dspark","model":"UIUC-SSAIL/Qwen3-8B-Markov-b16","num_speculative_tokens":15}'
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --speculative_config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16","num_speculative_tokens":15}'
```

</details>


## Test Result

On current main (merged, no conflicts), H200:

```
$ pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_xpress_head.py -q
3 passed in 17.52s

$ pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/xpress/test_xpress.py -s
XPress target=Qwen/Qwen3-8B, draft=UIUC-SSAIL/Qwen3-8B-XPress-b16:
    gsm8k_accuracy=0.889, acceptance_rate=0.310, acceptance_len=5.654
1 passed in 396.48s (0:06:36)

$ ruff check && ruff format --check
All checks passed!
```

The e2e acceptance length is measured under the 5-shot completion GSM8K protocol the DFlash and DSpark tests share, so it is comparable to their references on the same target (DFlash 3.5, DSpark ~4.0) and, like theirs, lower than the chat-template numbers below.

The benchmarks below were measured on vLLM `82ae4164`. This PR has since been merged with current main with no functional change to the XPress path; acceptance length is deterministic and unaffected, and absolute throughput moves with upstream scheduler and kernel work, so the paired ratios are what to compare.

Qwen3-8B on one H200, FlashAttention 3, CUDA graphs and prefix caching on, greedy, K=6, `num_speculative_tokens=15`, `max_model_len=8192`, up to 2048 new tokens. Seven benchmarks x five batch sizes (1/4/16/32/64), three-way against the Markov head and the bare drafter, two independent rounds for xpress and dspark.

`--max-samples 512` is a cap; a smaller dataset is used in full:

| dataset | gsm8k | math500 | aime25 | humaneval | mbpp | mt-bench | livecodebench |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| prompts | 512 | 500 | 30 | 164 | 257 | 80 | 512 |

aime25 (30) and mt-bench (80) finish in a single batch at 32/64, so those measurements run about five seconds and their throughput is correspondingly noisy. Acceptance length is not affected.

title: [ROCm] DFlash unusable for GLM-5.3-Flash: glm5next lacks SupportsEagle3, and ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE has no non-causal path
body:
### DFlash on GLM-5.3-Flash / ROCm: the target model interface is missing, and the sparse-MLA backend cannot do non-causal

Trying to run `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` as a drafter for `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` on 8x MI350X (gfx950, ROCm 7.2.3, TP8), I hit two separate walls. The first has a small fix; the second looks structural.

**1. `models/glm5next/` does not implement `SupportsEagle3`.**

```
RuntimeError: Model does not support EAGLE3 interface
```

DFlash needs the target model to expose auxiliary hidden states from the layers named in the drafter's `target_layer_ids`. `glm5next` implements neither `EagleModelMixin` nor `SupportsEagle3`. Wiring it the way `qwen3_moe.py` does works — with one GLM-specific caveat worth recording:

```python
class Glm5NextModel(nn.Module, EagleModelMixin):
    ...
        # residual=None: on GLM-5.3 `residual` is the mHC bundle of several
        # residual streams, not a single same-shaped residual, so the mixin's
        # default `hidden_states + residual` does not apply.
        aux_hidden_states = self._maybe_add_hidden_state(
            [], self.start_layer, hidden_states, None
        )
        for aux_idx, layer in enumerate(self._active_layers, start=self.start_layer):
            hidden_states, residual, post, comb = layer(...)
            self._maybe_add_hidden_state(
                aux_hidden_states, aux_idx + 1, hidden_states, None
            )
```

Passing `residual` as the mixin expects fails with `The size of tensor a (8192) must match the size of tensor b (4)` because of the manifold-constrained hyper-connections. With `None` the mixin stores the hidden state directly, which is what the drafter consumes.

**Verified harmless when unused**: with this in place and no drafter configured, throughput and acceptance are unchanged (2 773 tok/s, acceptance 3.06 at 96 concurrency, within the ±5 % run-to-run spread) — `_maybe_add_hidden_state` is a no-op while `aux_hidden_state_layers` is empty.

**2. After that, the drafter loads and then the GPU aborts.**

```
DFlash2Qwen3ForCausalLM loaded (0.21 s)
:0:rocdevice.cpp:3586: Callback: Queue aborting with error :
HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION: An HSAIL operation resulted in a hardware exception. code: 0x1016
```

No Python traceback — a kernel faults. The cause looks like the non-causal requirement from #41559/#40632. `DFlashSpeculator` passes `use_non_causal=self.requires_non_causal`, but grepping for `causal` across the backends:

| backend | occurrences of `causal` |
|---|---|
| `flash_attn` | 51 |
| `triton_attn` | 5 |
| `mla/indexer` | 1 |
| **`mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse`** | **0** |

`ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` — the only backend GLM-5.3-Flash can use on ROCm — has no notion of causality at all; it is causal-only by construction. The drafter's non-causal cross-attention then hands the kernel a shape it was not built for.

Things I ruled out along the way: it is not memory (`--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85` fails identically), not the fp8 KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16` fails identically, so #41559's bf16 restriction is not what is biting here), and not the `CandidateSelector`'s `@support_torch_compile` 4-D einsum (bypassing the decorator changes nothing).

#40632 was closed as "dflash is available now for both models functionally" for Kimi-K2.5 and Qwen3.5-27B — presumably on backends that do have a non-causal path. For sparse-MLA models on ROCm it does not appear to be reachable.

**Question:** is non-causal support in `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` on anyone's roadmap, or is DFlash structurally out of reach for GLM-5.3-Flash on AMD? Happy to send the `SupportsEagle3` wiring as a PR either way — it is useful on its own for any EAGLE3-family drafter, and it is measurably free when unused.

title: [Bug] [Portability][MSVC]: M_LOG2E is unavailable when building Flash Attention with NVCC and MSVC
body:
### Your current environment

### Environment

- Windows Server 2025
- Visual Studio Build Tools with MSVC
- CUDA/NVCC 13.2
- Python 3.12
- PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130
- SystemPanic/vllm-windows 0.25-based deployment
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731
- 4 x H200 NVL GPUs, SM90a

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Background

I encountered this issue while building vllm-project/flash-attention through SystemPanic/vllm-windows for a deployment serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on 4 x H200 NVL GPUs.

### Problem

Several Flash Attention CUDA source files use `M_LOG2E` in softmax and `exp2f` scale calculations:

    csrc/flash_attn/flash_api.cpp
    csrc/flash_attn/src/softmax.h
    hopper/flash_bwd_preprocess_kernel.h
    hopper/mainloop_fwd_sm80.hpp
    hopper/mainloop_fwd_sm90_tma_gmma_ws.hpp
    hopper/mainloop_bwd_sm80.hpp
    hopper/mainloop_bwd_sm90_tma_gmma_ws.hpp
    hopper/softmax.h

Examples include:

    params.scale_softmax_log2 =
        softmax_scale * M_LOG2E;

and:

    const float max_scaled =
        max(mi) == -INFINITY
            ? 0.f
            : max(mi) * (
                  Scale_max ? scale : float(M_LOG2E));

`M_LOG2E` represents `log2(e)` and is commonly available in GNU/Linux build environments. Its availability is implementation-specific, however, and MSVC normally exposes the `M_*` constants only when `_USE_MATH_DEFINES` is defined before the relevant math header is included.

I understand that native Windows may not be part of the supported build matrix. This appears to be a small source-portability issue rather than a request for broader Windows support.

### Tested workaround

The working downstream build replaces `M_LOG2E` with the corresponding float constant:

    - float(M_LOG2E)
    + 1.4426950408889634f

For example:

    - params.scale_softmax_log2 =
    -     softmax_scale * M_LOG2E;
    + params.scale_softmax_log2 =
    +     softmax_scale * 1.4426950408889634f;

The replacement preserves the intended `log2(e)` scale used by the float-based softmax and `exp2f` paths.

Applying the replacement to all affected occurrences allowed the Flash Attention extensions to build successfully with NVCC and MSVC.

### Related PyTorch-side solution

The discussion in: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54007

indicates that a PyTorch-side update may resolve this compatibility issue in the Windows build environment and perhaps could the same change be done here as well.

### Other possible solutions

The affected NVCC and MSVC targets could define:

    _USE_MATH_DEFINES=1

For example:

    target_compile_definitions(
        <target> PRIVATE _USE_MATH_DEFINES=1
    )

Alternatively, Flash Attention could use a project-owned `constexpr` value for `log2(e)` instead of depending on the host math-header configuration.

The source-level constant would be independent of PyTorch headers, build flags, and math-header include order.

### Repository context

Seven affected files are inherited from Dao-AILab/flash-attention.

The vllm-project fork additionally contains an affected occurrence in:

    hopper/softmax.h

I am reporting the complete set here because this is the Flash Attention fork built by vLLM.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
