title: [Bug]: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: greedy decoding is non-deterministic from persistent_topk in prefill when prompt length nears indexer_budget (sm121/GB10)
body:
## Summary

On `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`, five byte-identical requests at `temperature=0`
return five different completions — but only when the context exceeds
`indexer_budget`, the point at which Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA) switches from
attending densely to selecting a top-k subset.

Below the budget, output is byte-identical every time. Above it, greedy decoding
is not reproducible.

The user-visible symptom is silent text corruption. It is easy to miss in English
but severe in Thai, which uses ~3x more tokens per character and many
near-identical combining-mark tokens: tone marks get dropped, duplicated or
transposed, and Lao/Latin/CJK lookalike characters are spliced into Thai words
(`ความชื้่น`, `ตอนนนี้`, `อีก` -> `อกี`, `ปี` -> `ปื`). HTTP status stays 200.

## Environment

- **Official Qwen/vLLM image** `vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next`, per
  <https://recipes.vllm.ai/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next>
- vLLM `0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198` — verified identical in the official image and
  in the image actually used for these runs
- The image used adds **only** the InstantTensor fast weight loader on top of the
  official image; nothing else is patched. The loader is not implicated: the same
  behaviour occurs with `--load-format safetensors`.
- 2x NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, **sm121**), aarch64, driver 580.173.02
- `-tp 2` across two nodes
- Model `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` (`Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`)
- `--enforce-eager` (so this is **not** a CUDA-graph capture issue)

## Reproducer

`determinism.py` (attached below) sends the same prompt N times at
`temperature=0` and counts distinct completions. It is language-independent.

```
./determinism.py --base http://localhost:8000/v1 --model <served-name> --budget 8192
```

## Observed

Server run with `--hf-overrides '{"text_config": {"indexer_budget": 8192}}'`,
5 identical greedy requests per row:

| prompt tokens | vs `indexer_budget` (8192) | distinct completions / 5 |
|---:|:--|--:|
| 5629 | below | 1 |
| 6829 | below | 1 |
| 7629 | below | 1 |
| **8429** | **above** | **4** |
| 9629 | above | 3 |
| 12829 | above | 4 |

The transition tracks `indexer_budget`, not any absolute context length.

## Ruled out

- **Prefix caching** — reproduces identically with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`.
- **CUDA graphs** — `--enforce-eager` was set throughout.
- **Quantization** — FP8 and NVFP4 checkpoints both affected.
- **Weight loading** — `instanttensor` and `safetensors` both affected.
- **Sampling** — this *is* `temperature=0`; greedy is the failing case.
- **Chat template / tokenizer** — reproduces via `/v1/completions` with a
  pre-rendered prompt; tokenizer round-trips the text exactly.
- **The model weights** — static weights cannot yield different outputs for
  identical greedy input; this has to be in the execution path.

## Where we would look

`vllm/models/qwen3_8_flash_next/nvidia/qsa.py` -> `qsa_sparse_paged_attention`
(`.ops.qsa`), and the top-k selection in `indexer_qsa.py`
(`qsa_select_paged_tokens`). The `persistent_topk` CUDA kernel accepts only
`k in {512, 1024, 2048}` where `k = indexer_budget / indexer_compress_ratio`.
Non-deterministic ordering / tie-breaking in that selection would explain the
threshold behaviour exactly.

Possibly related: MiaAI-Lab's dual-DGX-Spark repo reports that "SM121 silently
corrupts long-context decode" on the sparse-attention path in **SGLang**, and
ships SM121-specific kernel patches for it. Different engine, same hardware,
same subsystem — so this may be an SM121 kernel issue rather than a vLLM-only one.

## Known gap

All determinism measurements above were taken with `indexer_budget` overridden to
8192. We did **not** verify the threshold at the model's default budget of 2048.
The finding predicts it reproduces there with the transition near ~2k of context
(i.e. more easily), but that specific run was not performed.


## `determinism.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal reproducer: greedy decoding is non-deterministic above indexer_budget.

Language-independent. Sends the SAME prompt N times at temperature=0 and reports
how many distinct completions come back. Expected: 1. Observed above
indexer_budget on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next / SM121: up to N.

  ./determinism.py --base http://localhost:8000/v1 --model <served-name>
  ./determinism.py --base ... --budget 2048      # sweep around a given budget
"""
import argparse, json, urllib.request

FILLER = ("The climate of Thailand is tropical with three seasons. The southwest "
          "monsoon brings heavy rain to the west coast from May to October. ")
TASK = "\n\nSummarise the text above in two sentences."

def complete(base, model, prompt, max_tokens):
    body = {"model": model, "prompt": prompt,
            "max_tokens": max_tokens, "temperature": 0.0}
    req = urllib.request.Request(base.rstrip("/") + "/completions",
                                 data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    r = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=900).read().decode())
    return r["choices"][0].get("text") or ""

def ntokens(base, model, prompt):
    root = base.rstrip("/").rsplit("/v1", 1)[0]
    req = urllib.request.Request(root + "/tokenize",
                                 data=json.dumps({"model": model, "prompt": prompt}).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    try:
        return len(json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120).read().decode())["tokens"])
    except Exception:
        return -1

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--base", default="http://localhost:8000/v1")
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--budget", type=int, default=8192,
                    help="indexer_budget the server runs with (sweep straddles it)")
    ap.add_argument("--runs", type=int, default=5)
    ap.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=300)
    a = ap.parse_args()

    # context sizes straddling the budget
    approx_tok_per_rep = 16
    targets = [int(a.budget * f) for f in (0.70, 0.85, 0.95, 1.05, 1.20, 1.60)]
    print(f"indexer_budget = {a.budget}; {a.runs} identical greedy requests each")
    print(f"{'tokens':>8s} {'vs budget':>10s} {'distinct':>9s}   verdict")
    bad = False
    for tgt in targets:
        reps = max(1, tgt // approx_tok_per_rep)
        prompt = FILLER * reps + TASK
        n = ntokens(a.base, a.model, prompt)
        outs = {complete(a.base, a.model, prompt, a.max_tokens) for _ in range(a.runs)}
        rel = "below" if n < a.budget else "ABOVE"
        verdict = "OK (deterministic)" if len(outs) == 1 else "*** NON-DETERMINISTIC ***"
        if len(outs) > 1:
            bad = True
        print(f"{n:8d} {rel:>10s} {len(outs):>6d}/{a.runs}   {verdict}")
    print("\nRESULT:", "BUG REPRODUCED" if bad else "not reproduced")

main()
```

title: Dcp sparse mla fix 0.23.1

title: Filter sparse MLA top-k indices per DCP rank, and fix decode LSE
body:
Backport onto the v0.28.0 release, which does not carry the upstream fix: vllm-project/vllm#46514 (63ff748f6, 2026-08-19) landed this on main, but the v0.28.0 release branch forked before it, so the released wheel still has the bug. flashmla_sparse.py is byte-identical from v0.26.0 through v0.28.0, so this applies unchanged across all three.

Under decode context parallelism each rank holds only its own shard of the KV cache, but the sparse FlashMLA path fed the top-k results - which are global token positions - straight into
triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index. That converter assumes every index is local, so it translated positions owned by other ranks through this rank's block table and read unrelated cache slots, corrupting decode output.

Use triton_filter_and_convert_dcp_index when dcp_world_size > 1: it drops the indices this rank does not own before converting the rest. Applied at all three call sites (bf16 KV, fp8 KV separate prefill/decode, fp8 KV mixed batch). Non-DCP runs keep the original converter unchanged. The helper is already in sparse_utils.py at this tag.

Ownership depends on the interleave stride, so plumb cp_kv_cache_interleave_size from parallel_config through the metadata rather than leaving the dataclass default of 1.

Two LSE fixes needed for the cross-rank reduction to be correct:

  - flash_mla_sparse_fwd returns (output, max_logits, lse), so read kernel_out[2]. The previous kernel_out[1] fed max_logits into the reduction. Upstream main expresses the same thing as 'output, _, lse = flash_mla_sparse_fwd(...)'.
  - flash_mla_with_kvcache returns LSE as (batch, num_heads, seq_len) while callers reshape assuming (batch, seq_len, num_heads); transpose it, and trim the padded head dim.

Also guard the two LSE reshape sites against a None lse.


Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01MYhgsjgQ2GQcpkXZfM3dec

title: [ROCm][MLA][DCP] Advertise Triton MLA non-causal multi-token DCP
body:
## Summary

Declare that Triton MLA can serve a non-causal multi-token decode block while the MLA KV cache is DCP-sharded, scoped to ROCm.

`forward_mqa` already flattens a non-causal block into one decode row per query token. Every row attends the same committed prefix, so a rank-local `seq_len` fully describes the row under DCP. Without this capability, backend selection rejects Triton MLA for this combination and pushes the multi-token block away from its decode path.

## Why this is separate

This is split out of #51705 on reviewer request. #51705 implements causal multi-token target verification in the ROCm AITER backend; this two-line capability is the only part that touches a backend shared with CUDA and XPU.

## Scope and behavior

`AttentionBackend.supports_non_causal_dcp()` is a backend-eligibility gate, and Triton MLA is selectable on CUDA, XPU, and ROCm. The flatten itself is platform independent, but this DCP configuration has only been validated on ROCm, so the capability remains `current_platform.is_rocm()`.

A single module-level constant feeds both read sites: the class capability and the `supports_dcp_with_varlen` builder argument. With DCP disabled, behavior is unchanged. With DCP enabled on ROCm, a non-causal multi-token group retains its decode reorder threshold instead of being forced back to single-token support. Only the affected KV-cache group is promoted to `UNIFORM_BATCH` graph support.

## Validation

Revision: `8474084088b12b7bc3ca35cf6d74f87cb7161f92`

```text
python3 -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_triton_mla_capabilities.py -v
3 passed, 14 warnings
```

The tests cover the ROCm-scoped capability, both read sites, the retained multi-token reorder threshold under DCP, and conditional graph-support promotion.

### Full-model stacked validation

This revision was cleanly stacked on #51705 at `e1843114b7c233a9c71ad44b28bf63426ad64836` and tested with real Kimi-K3 target and Kimi-K3-DSpark weights. Configuration: TP8/DCP8, A2A DCP, FP8 target KV, 1,048,576 maximum model length, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs through batch 32, two draft tokens, probabilistic draft sampling, block rejection sampling, and Triton MLA for the draft.

```text
combined focused tests:       543 passed, 14 warnings in 31.75s
GSM8K 5-shot:                 1319/1319 at concurrency 64
strict-match exact_match:     0.9628506444 +/- 0.0052095163
flexible-extract exact_match: 0.9636087945 +/- 0.0051581135
evaluation time:              353 seconds
mean acceptance length:       2.67-2.74 in the final 10 windows
server errors/tracebacks:     0/0
HSA memory-access faults:     0
```

The run selected Triton MLA for the non-causal draft and ROCm AITER MLA for the target, completed FULL graph capture, and remained healthy after evaluation.

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Codex). The human submitter has reviewed every changed line and is responsible for defending it.

title: [Feature]: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp (multimodal) — implementation ready, two design questions
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

[`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp) — DeepSeek's first multimodal V4 — has no vLLM support. Today the checkpoint cannot be loaded at all: it declares `architectures: ["DeepseekV4ForCausalLM"]`, so vLLM routes it to the text-only class, which then fails on the 316 tensors it has no destination for.

I have a working implementation and would like a maintainer steer on two design points **before** opening the PR, since both are project decisions rather than implementation choices.

Branch: https://github.com/tacos8me/vllm/tree/deepseek-v4-vision (1 commit, 8 files, +651). Verified on 2× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), TP=2: correct descriptions/counts/attributes on real images, image token counts matching the reference math exactly (313 and 109 for the two examples shipped in the repo), text generation and DSpark speculative decoding unaffected.

### What the model needs

The vision path is not a pure embedding splice. DeepSeek ships only a reference implementation (`inference/` in the repo, described in their own README as "a readable reference implementation rather than a production serving engine"), and it couples image tokens into the LM in four places:

1. **Out-of-vocabulary sentinel ids.** Each image expands to a block of ids `vocab_size + {0..4}`. They never index the embedding table — embeddings arrive via the multimodal path — but the LM reads them.
2. **Hash-routing guard.** The 3 hash-routed MoE layers index `tid2eid[input_ids]`, and that table is `[vocab_size, k]`, so the sentinels must be substituted before the lookup or it reads out of bounds. The reference substitutes id 0.
3. **Modality-forked expert selection.** Every gate carries a second bias `bias_vl [n_experts]`, used instead of `bias` for image positions in top-k selection only (routing weights still come from the unbiased scores).
4. **Input-id validation.** `v1/engine/input_processor.py` caps ids at `max(tokenizer.max_token_id, vocab_size - 1)` and so rejects the sentinels.

(2) and (3) must be branch-free: they run inside the `torch.compile` region, where `if mask.any()` is a data-dependent guard and `nonzero()` a data-dependent shape.

### Open question 1 — architecture selection

The vision checkpoint declares the **same** `architectures` string as the text model, `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`, with flat `vision_*` config keys (no `vision_config`/`text_config` nesting). So the vision class cannot be resolved from the checkpoint alone.

Options:

| | approach | cost |
|---|---|---|
| **a** | Separate `DeepseekV4VForConditionalGeneration`, selected with `--hf-overrides '{"architectures": [...]}'` | zero core change; poor UX, and every user must know the incantation |
| **b** | Conditional class: `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` grows vision when `vision_n_layers > 0` | works out of the box; makes `supports_multimodal` class-level for all V4 deployments |
| **c** | Arch remap during config normalization, keyed on `vision_n_layers` (`transformers_utils/config.py`) | works out of the box; needs a small hook, and I found no exact precedent for a same-arch-name fork |

**My branch implements (a)** because it needs no core change, but I think (c) is the right long-term answer and I'm happy to redo it. Worth noting DeepSeek may rename the arch in a later revision, which would make this moot.

### Open question 2 — position-dependent prompt expansion

The reference prepends `3 - start_pos % 4` pad tokens so an image's first grid token aligns to the C4 compressor block. That makes an image's token count depend on **its offset in the prompt**, which `_get_prompt_updates` cannot express — its replacement callables receive only `item_idx`.

**My branch's workaround:** do the whole tokenize-and-expand in `_call_hf_processor`, and override `_cached_apply_hf_processor` to force the uncached whole-prompt path (the per-item processing cache is unsound here, since the same image expands differently at different offsets). This is correct but gives up per-item caching for this model.

**What would be better:** giving prompt-update callables access to the running offset, so this can use the standard path. That's a small core extension; I did not want to propose one unilaterally. Is there an existing mechanism I've missed?

### Not included

The reference makes attention bidirectional **within** each `[IMAGE_START, IMAGE_END]` span across all layers (`get_image_visible`). vLLM builds `sparse_indices` as `[num_tokens, window_size + padded_topk]` with the first `window_size` columns as SWA slots, prefill windows derived from position inside a triton kernel; the reference needs `window_size + vision_max_n_token` (128 + 384) with per-token bounds. Closing it means widening the matrix for prefill rows, threading bounds into that kernel, and carrying an image mask on the attention metadata — `sparse_topk_lens` already supports variable attended lengths, so the design permits it.

Attention in my branch stays causal. Image understanding is accurate without it (counts, attributes and spatial relations check out against the source images), but it is a real fidelity gap and I'd rather state it than have it found in review. Happy to do it as a follow-up if wanted.

### Alternatives considered

Running DeepSeek's reference implementation instead — it requires per-TP-rank conversion via their `convert.py` and is explicitly not a serving engine (no OpenAI API, plain autoregressive sampling).

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I have searched for relevant issues and PRs — there are none for this model. `DeepseekV4V` and "deepseek v4 vision" return zero PR hits, a GitHub-wide code search for the arch name returns nothing, and no issue requests it. The only recent commit touching `vllm/models/deepseek_v4` is an unrelated SM120 topk-indices bugfix.

title: [Bugfix][SM120][MLA] Read fp8_ds_mla tile scales as arbitrary fp32
body:
## Purpose

The read format has to match the write format. The vLLM writers used with this backend store each tile scale as raw fp32 amax / 448 (concat_and_cache_ds_mla and the DeepSeek-V3.2 fused Triton path). However, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` asked FlashInfer for `pow2_fp32`, which extracts the exponent and reconstructs `2^floor(log2(scale))`. For a non-power-of-two scale written by vLLM, that is smaller by a factor in `(0.5, 1]`.

The format was chosen from a `model_type` allowlist that only sent `glm*` to the correct reader, so every other sparse model landing here reads its scales wrong: DeepSeek-V3.2 today, and HY V4 as soon as it can select this backend (it needs
the sink support in the stacked follow-up, since `learnable_sink` defaults to on). https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54434

FlashInfer supports both scale conventions for the same 656-byte physical layout, but vLLM's writer contract currently always stores arbitrary fp32 scales. Kimi-K3 demonstrates that this convention is not tied to the model label: its dense MLA path writes the same layout even though it never reaches this sparse backend. This backend accepts no other layout (it raises unless
`kv_cache_dtype == "fp8_ds_mla"`), so its reader format becomes a constant.

DeepSeek-V4 is not a counterexample. It reuses the `fp8_ds_mla` string for a different footer-scale layout: 576 bytes of per-token data plus 8 bytes of UE8M0 `2^(u8-127)` scales in the page footer, or 584 logical bytes per token.
That layout is written by DSv4's own CuteDSL/Triton insert rather than `concat_and_cache_ds_mla`, and DSv4 is rejected here: `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` is not a DSv4 backend; those models must use `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`. 

## Test Plan

Run on real SM120 hardware (AWS `g7.2xlarge`: RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell, sm_120, driver 595.91.07, CUDA 13.2, torch 2.13.0+cu132, flashinfer 0.6.17).

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -q
```

Because this patch changes how bytes are dequantized, the decisive test is a kernel-level A/B: pack a `fp8_ds_mla` cache exactly the way vLLM's writer does (`amax / 448` stored as raw fp32), call the same public FlashInfer decode API
this backend calls, once per `kv_scale_format`, and compare both against an fp32 dequant-then-attention reference computed from the same bytes.

## Test Result

Unit tests: **18 passed**.

Neighbouring suite `test_sparse_mla_backends.py`: 46 passed, 504 skipped, 4 failed — the same 4 `masked_mha` prefill cases fail on the unpatched base commit (`d3d79ffc1e`) on this GPU, so they are pre-existing and unrelated.

Scale A/B, 1024-token cache, 32 heads, top-k 2048. 4083 of 4096 stored tile scales are not powers of two (mean `pow2/true` factor 0.776, min 0.505), so the two readers genuinely disagree:

| reader | rel L2 vs writer reference | cos |
|---|---|---|
| `arbitrary_fp32` (this PR) | **0.0030** | 1.0000 |
| `pow2_fp32` (before) | 0.0213 | 0.9998 |

The gap widens with per-tile scale spread, which is what real K vectors look like (outlier channels in the nope tiles):

| log2 scale spread | `arbitrary_fp32` | `pow2_fp32` |
|---|---|---|
| 1.4 | 0.0030 | 0.0213 (7.0x) |
| 4.7 | 0.0032 | 0.0224 (7.0x) |
| 10.1 | 0.0062 | 0.0737 (11.9x) |
| 18.0 | 0.0196 | 0.1985 (10.2x) |

FlashInfer's own docstring confirms the two semantics: `"auto"`/`"pow2_fp32"` "select DSv3.2 power-of-2 FP32 inline scales", `"arbitrary_fp32"` "selects GLM-style arbitrary FP32 inline scales".

No end-to-end eval: every model that can reach this backend (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM, HY V4) is far larger than the biggest single SM120 (96 GB), so a serving eval is not reachable on this hardware. The A/B above measures exactly the quantity this patch changes, on the kernel this patch configures.

<details>
<summary>A/B harness (abridged)</summary>

```python
# pack the way vLLM's concat_and_cache_ds_mla does: raw fp32 amax/448
for ti in range(4):
    tile = kv[:, ti * 128 : (ti + 1) * 128].float()
    scale = (tile.abs().amax(-1).clamp(min=1e-4) / 448.0).to(torch.float32)
    packed[:, ti * 128 : (ti + 1) * 128] = (tile / scale[:, None]).to(
        torch.float8_e4m3fn
    ).view(torch.uint8)
    packed[:, 512 + ti * 4 : 512 + (ti + 1) * 4] = scale.view(torch.uint8).view(-1, 4)

for fmt in ("pow2_fp32", "arbitrary_fp32"):
    out = trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla(
        query=q.unsqueeze(1), kv_cache=kv_hnd, workspace_buffer=ws,
        qk_nope_head_dim=512, kv_lora_rank=512, qk_rope_head_dim=64,
        block_tables=indices.unsqueeze(1), seq_lens=None,
        max_seq_len=indices.shape[-1], sparse_mla_top_k=indices.shape[-1],
        bmm1_scale=sm_scale, bmm2_scale=1.0, backend="sparse",
        kv_scale_format=fmt,
    ).squeeze(1)
    report(fmt, out, reference_from_the_same_bytes)
```

</details>

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Checked per AGENTS.md:

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "pow2_fp32"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "arbitrary_fp32"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "kv_scale_format"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "SM120 sparse MLA"
```

No open PR changes the model-dependent `kv_scale_format` selection fixed here (both explicit format searches return nothing). #47527 wires the packed-cache arguments, including `kv_scale_format`, into the released FlashInfer API but
preserves the existing selection; this PR fixes the value passed through that API. #53969 adds NoPE support and validates the effective top-k buffer width. Both touch the same files, so textual conflicts are possible, but neither duplicates this change.

## AI assistance disclosure (per AGENTS.md)

AI assistance was used to cross-check the vLLM writer kernels against FlashInfer's reader paths, to run the SM120 hardware A/B above, and to write the test. The submitter reviewed every changed line.

title: [Bugfix][SM120][MLA] Forward attention sinks through sparse MLA
body:
FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120 never advertised sink support and dropped the per-head sink bias on the floor, so a sink model (HY V4) selecting this backend computed attention without its learned sinks. FlashInfer's SM120 sparse kernels take the bias as `attn_sink` on both the decode and the prefill path, and the impl already routes every prefill through sparse MQA (supports_dense_mha_prefill is False), so one plumbing point covers both.

Validate dtype and shape at construction: the kernel binding ICHECKs `attn_sink.size(0) == num_heads` and float32, which would otherwise abort at the first forward.

Measured on an SM120 (RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell, FlashInfer 0.6.17): on an 8-head TP shard, passing the sinks matched FlashInfer's documented `out *= sigmoid(lse - sink)` reference with 0.0153 relative L2 error and 0.9999 cosine similarity. Omitting the sinks changed the output by 0.2302 relative L2 at the sink magnitudes reported in #54434, confirming that silently dropping them materially changes attention.

AI assistance was used for the FlashInfer API cross-check, the hardware A/B and the tests.

Test: python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py


Co-authored-by: Cursor Claude Opus 5

title: [Sampling] Add Mirostat v2 sampling
body:
## Purpose

Add opt-in **Mirostat v2** sampling (`mirostat_mode` / `mirostat_tau` /
`mirostat_eta`) to the V1 sampler. Mirostat (Basu et al., 2020,
https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.14966) is a feedback controller that keeps the
per-token *surprise* (`-log2 p`, i.e. per-token cross-entropy in bits) near a
target `tau` by maintaining a per-request threshold `mu` updated every step:

```
mu <- mu - eta * (observed_surprise - tau)
```

This bounds the per-token surprise from above, which keeps decoding out of the
*confusion trap* — the incoherent, non-terminating output that plain
temperature/top-p sampling falls into at high temperature. Measured on
DeepSeek-V4-Flash at `temperature=1.8-2.0`, it cuts the share of requests that
run all the way to `max_tokens` by ~85% and halves generated tokens (numbers in
[Model evaluation](#model-evaluation)). At `temperature <= 1.5` it is inert by
design and leaves well-behaved decoding untouched.

**Default `mirostat_mode=0` is a no-op**, so existing behavior is unchanged.

Usage:

```python
SamplingParams(mirostat_mode=2, mirostat_tau=5.0, mirostat_eta=0.1,
               temperature=1.0, top_k=0, top_p=1.0)
```

Also exposed on the OpenAI `/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions` request
bodies as `mirostat_mode` / `mirostat_tau` / `mirostat_eta`.

Closes the long-standing request in #5209 (Mirostat), which was auto-closed for
inactivity, not rejected.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs/issues (`gh pr list --search "mirostat"`, `gh search issues
mirostat`). No open PR implements Mirostat. #5209 is a stale-closed feature
request with no implementation; this PR implements Mirostat v2 for the V1
sampler.

## Design notes (for reviewers)

- **State lives in the `Sampler`, not a `LogitsProcessor`.** The `mu` update
  needs the probability of the *sampled* token, which only exists after
  sampling; a pre-sampling logits processor cannot see it. This mirrors the
  existing `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder` pattern. `MirostatStateHolder`
  (`vllm/v1/sample/mirostat_state.py`) is created per `InputBatch`, synced via
  `BatchUpdate` (add/remove/move), attached to `SamplingMetadata`, and consumed
  in `Sampler.sample()`.
- **Truncation is argmax-invariant.** Mirostat v2 sets the logit of any token
  with surprise `> mu` to `-inf` and always keeps the argmax, so it composes
  with the rest of the random-sampling pipeline. It runs after temperature and
  the argmax-invariant logits processors (e.g. min_p), before top-k/top-p.
- **Decode throughput is unaffected (GPU-resident state).** `mu`/`tau`/`eta`
  are persistent device tensors; the per-step math (truncate + `mu` update) is
  fully on-device with **no host<->device sync**. Inactive rows carry
  `mu = +inf` / `eta = 0`, making the per-step math a masked no-op for them, so
  a single vectorized path covers the whole batch with static shapes (CUDA
  graph friendly). When no request uses Mirostat the holder short-circuits, so
  there is zero overhead on the common path.
- **Validation.** `mirostat_mode` must be `0` or `2`. When enabled it requires
  `temperature > 0`, `top_k in {0, -1}`, `top_p == 1.0` (Mirostat replaces
  top-k/top-p truncation), and finite `tau`/`eta > 0`. Because temperature is
  applied before Mirostat, the `mirostat_mode` docstring recommends
  `temperature ~= 1.0` (a much lower temperature drives surprise toward 0 and
  makes Mirostat approach greedy).

## Tests

- `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_mirostat.py -v` → **14/14 passed** (parameter
  validation; holder add/remove/swap/move bookkeeping; truncation keeps the
  argmax; `mu` updates in both directions).
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on all changed files (ruff
  0.14.0, the pinned CI version).

## Model evaluation

Measured on DeepSeek-V4-Flash (8xH20, TP=8).

**Repetition / degeneration** (HumanEval/132 `is_nested`, `think`-high,
N=20/config, `max_tokens=8192`; a "loop" = `finish_reason==length` with high
tail-repetition):

| config | loop rate |
| --- | --- |
| greedy (`temperature=0`) | 35% |
| plain sampling (`temperature=1.0`, `top_p=1.0`) | 0% |
| Mirostat v2 (`mode=2`, `tau=5`, `temperature=1.0`) | 0% |

Any `temperature > 0` already breaks the greedy repetition attractor, so
Mirostat is not what fixes greedy loops here. Being explicit about the scope:
with a fixed `seed`, Mirostat (`tau=5`) at `temperature <= 1.5` produces
**byte-identical** output to plain sampling. `tau=5` bits targets perplexity
`2^5 = 32`; below that temperature the observed surprise stays under `tau`, so
`mu` grows monotonically and the truncation is inert. That is the intended
behavior — Mirostat should not perturb well-behaved decoding. Its measurable
benefit shows up once the distribution is hot enough to enter the *confusion
trap*.

**High-temperature stability (confusion trap)** — this is the regime where
Mirostat is not substitutable by temperature tuning. Full HumanEval (164
problems, `think`-high, `top_p=1.0`, `max_tokens=8192`, 30 concurrent):

| temperature | config | pass@1 | truncated at `max_tokens` | mean out tokens | total out tokens |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.8 | baseline | 4.9% (8/164) | 135/164 (82%) | 7217 | 1.18M |
| 1.8 | Mirostat v2 (`tau=5`) | **12.2%** (20/164) | **20/164 (12%)** | **3018** | **0.49M** |
| 2.0 | baseline | 0.6% (1/164) | 146/164 (89%) | 7718 | 1.27M |
| 2.0 | Mirostat v2 (`tau=5`) | **1.2%** (2/164) | **24/164 (15%)** | **3335** | **0.55M** |

At `temperature >= 1.8` plain sampling degenerates into incoherence and burns the
entire budget — the *median* request hits `max_tokens`. Mirostat cuts the
truncation rate by ~85% (82% -> 12% and 89% -> 15%), reduces total generated
tokens by ~57%, and raises pass@1 by 2.5x / 2x respectively. End-to-end
wall-clock for the two sweeps dropped 43% and 46%.

Scope of the win, stated plainly: this is damage mitigation, not recovery.
`temperature=1.8` + Mirostat (12.2%) is still far below `temperature=1.0` plain
sampling (99.4% pass@1 on the same harness). The value is that workloads which
*must* run hot (diversity / creative sampling) get a bounded-surprise safety net
instead of unbounded degeneration, at roughly half the tokens.

**Decode throughput — lossless** (same engine, 30 concurrent, `max_tokens=3000`,
non-think, measured from `vllm:generation_tokens_total`):

| config | decode tok/s |
| --- | --- |
| baseline (no Mirostat) | 1902.3 |
| Mirostat v2 (enabled) | **1895.1** |

Δ = **-0.4%, within noise**. An earlier host-syncing prototype regressed decode
by ~16% at 30 concurrency; moving the `mu` state fully GPU-resident (no per-step
`.tolist()`/D2H) removed the regression.

## Limitations / follow-ups

- Only Mirostat **v2** is implemented (the common variant). v1 (which estimates
  the Zipf exponent per step) can be added later.
- Not validated with speculative decoding; the `mu` update assumes one sampled
  token per request per step. Recommend not combining with spec decode for now.
- Mirostat v2 cannot break a **high-confidence** repetition loop, and should not
  be advertised as a general anti-repetition fix. The repeated token is the
  argmax, which the truncation always keeps, and its surprise is near 0, which
  drives `mu` *upward* and loosens truncation further. The controller bounds
  surprise from above (confusion trap), not from below. For greedy-style loops,
  raise `temperature` or use a repetition penalty.

## Note

AI assistance was used to prepare this change. The submitter has reviewed every
line and is responsible for the change and its tests/evaluations.

title: [Attention][DeepSeek-V4] Add SM90 Q8KV8 sparse MLA prefill
body:
## Purpose

This PR adds an opt-in native SM90 Q8 x KV8 sparse MLA prefill path for
DeepSeek-V4 on the NVIDIA FlashMLA backend.

The existing prefill path gathers the packed DeepSeek-V4 FP8 KV cache into a
BF16 workspace before calling FlashMLA. The new path instead:

1. gathers and requantizes the UE8M0 paged cache directly to OCP E4M3;
2. converts the BF16 query to OCP E4M3 in a reusable workspace;
3. maps padded sparse indices to a zero sentinel row; and
4. runs a native SM90 Q8KV8 sparse MLA kernel with attention-sink and
   variable-top-k support.

The kernel is adapted from the SGLang/FlashMLA implementation with its source
license retained. It is registered through the libtorch stable ABI as
`torch.ops._C.sparse_mla_q8kv8_prefill_sm90` and is built only for `sm_90a`
with CUDA >= 12.3.

Runtime selection is fail-closed and default-off through
`AttentionConfig.use_deepseek_v4_q8kv8_prefill`. Enabling it requires:

- an exact SM90 NVIDIA GPU;
- BF16 model activations;
- the FlashMLA DeepSeek-V4 sparse backend; and
- the canonical `fp8_ds_mla` KV-cache layout.

The existing BF16 gather + FlashMLA path remains unchanged when the option is
disabled.

### Duplicate-work check

No open issue or PR contains `Q8KV8` in its title/body. The nearest open PRs
are materially different:

- #39941 adds a BF16 CUTLASS FA3 backend for small-batch decode.
- #41836 is a draft direct paged-KV FlashMLA prefill path validated on GB200;
  it does not add a native SM90 Q8KV8 kernel.
- #42504 adds a B200 BF16 sparse-gather kernel only and explicitly leaves
  runtime integration to follow-up work.

No tracking issue number was provided, so there is no issue-specific duplicate
PR search to link.

## Test Plan

All Python invocations used the repository `.venv` and all GPU work ran through
Slurm on NVIDIA H20-3e (`sm_90`, CUDA 13.0).

```bash
# Incremental CUDA build and stable-op registration check
.venv/bin/cmake --build cmake-build-q8kv8-gcc13 \
  --target _C_stable_libtorch --parallel 32
.venv/bin/cmake --install cmake-build-q8kv8-gcc13 \
  --component _C_stable_libtorch

# Native kernel/reference and sentinel tests
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py -k q8kv8 -vv

# Packed-cache BF16/direct-FP8 gather tests
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
  -k dequantize_and_gather_k_cache -vv

# Configuration parsing
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py::test_attention_config -vv

# Correctness-gated CUPTI microbenchmark
.venv/bin/python \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_q8kv8_sparse_mla_prefill.py --batch-size 4

# Repository checks
pre-commit run --all-files
pre-commit run --from-ref upstream/main --to-ref HEAD
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual
```

The benchmark uses CUDA graphs and CUPTI activity timing, performs warmup
outside the measured region, and fails closed when CUPTI is unavailable. Its
timed boundary includes packed-cache gather/requantization, query conversion,
and sparse attention for the Q8 path; the shared index-construction work is
excluded from both paths.

## Test Result

### Build and focused tests

- Incremental build succeeded; the SM90 op registration check returned `True`
  (Slurm job 2037).
- Native Q8KV8 tests: `3 passed` for 64/128 heads, partial top-k,
  attention-sink handling, finite statistics, and repeatability.
- Cache gather tests: `2 passed`; the direct OCP E4M3 output matches the
  reference conversion exactly on valid rows.
- AttentionConfig test: `1 passed`.
- Full pre-commit, rebased-diff pre-commit, manual mypy 3.12, `compileall`, and
  `git diff --check` passed.

### Production `_forward_prefill` A/B

The real DeepSeek-V4 FlashMLA `_forward_prefill` method was exercised on an
H20 with identical compressed/SWA paged caches, sparse indices, and metadata.
The baseline arm used BF16 gather + FlashMLA; the candidate arm used direct
E4M3 gather + sentinel + Q8KV8.

Configuration: query length 128, sequence length 192, 64 heads, top-k 64.

| Metric | Q8KV8 vs BF16 FlashMLA |
| --- | ---: |
| Mean absolute error | 0.00005155 |
| P99 absolute error | 0.00027466 |
| Max absolute error | 0.00070190 |

Both outputs were finite and the integration gate passed (Slurm job 2055).

### CUPTI performance

Hardware/software: NVIDIA H20-3e, PyTorch 2.13 + CUDA 13.0,
`cupti-python==13.0.1`, CUDA graph enabled (Slurm job 2040).

| Queries | KV/request | Heads | Top-k | BF16 (us) | Q8KV8 (us) | Speedup | Mean error | P99 error |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 128 | 1152 | 64 | 640 | 107.7 | 91.8 | 1.17x | 0.000024 | 0.000122 |
| 512 | 2176 | 64 | 640 | 370.1 | 313.0 | 1.18x | 0.000022 | 0.000107 |
| 512 | 2176 | 64 | 1152 | 635.5 | 470.7 | 1.35x | 0.000018 | 0.000092 |

### Full-model evaluation note

A deterministic DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 TP4 comparison was attempted with a
fixed 4096-token prompt, eight greedy output tokens, and chosen-token
logprobs. The shared `vllm-h20-02` node emitted NVIDIA Xid 13/43
`Out Of Range Address` faults on three devices during initialization. The Xid
records belonged to PIDs outside this evaluation's worker PID set, and the
engine exited before either arm produced tokens. Therefore this PR does not
claim generated-token/logprob parity or model-level latency from that run.

To avoid substituting an invalid result, correctness was instead verified on a
different, clean H20 through the production `_forward_prefill` A/B described
above. The full deterministic model comparison should be repeated when a clean
four-GPU node is available.

### AI assistance and accountability

AI assistance was used to research the SGLang implementation, prepare the
port, tests, and benchmark, and diagnose the shared-node evaluation failure.
The submitting human reviewed every changed line, understands the change
end-to-end, and ran/reviewed the tests and measurements reported above.

- [x] The test plan with commands that were run.
- [x] Test and benchmark results, including the model-evaluation limitation.
- [x] No documentation update is necessary because this is an experimental,

</details>

title: [ROCm] Optimize HY V4 graph inference on gfx942 and gfx950
body:
# [ROCm] Optimize HY V4 graph inference on gfx942 and gfx950

## Purpose

This PR remains stacked on #54405 (and therefore #54404). This update adds four
targeted changes to the HY V4 ROCm graph-mode serving path:

- use AITER's fused biased sigmoid top-k for HY V4's one-group routing shape;
- make the AITER MXFP8 routing buffers contiguous before fused MoE consumes
  them;
- fuse the BF16 elementwise MLA output gate into one graph-safe Triton op; and
- apply attention sinks with a grouped, graph-safe kernel that also repairs
  empty graph-padded rows.

Unsupported AITER sink layouts are now rejected during construction instead of
on the first request. The shared NVIDIA attention path retains the same eager
gate expression through a small subclass hook.

## Platform isolation

- The direct top-k route is guarded by the one-group sigmoid routing
  configuration and HY V4's measured hidden/expert/top-k shape.
- The fused MLA gate is in the ROCm subclass and requires matching contiguous
  BF16 CUDA tensors with the measured width; all other inputs use the existing
  eager expression.
- The attention-sink kernel remains inside the ROCm AITER sparse-MLA backend.
- NVIDIA still executes `attn_out * torch.sigmoid(gate_score)`.
- Model-class dispatch remains capability/platform based. The only gfx-specific
  branch in this update is the AITER sink compatibility check that rejects the
  unsupported gfx942 BF16 64-head bucket.

## Exact candidate and runtime

- Published optimization commit:
  `53abd3cac3e06993a8afae86b3246fa27d0ab1b1`

title: [Bugfix][Model] Read Eagle3 aux layer count from the top-level config key
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #54526.

Speculators-trained Eagle3 checkpoints declare their aux hidden layers as `eagle_aux_hidden_state_layer_ids` at the top level of the draft config, and vLLM's own speculators loader (`transformers_utils/configs/speculators/algos.py`) carries the key through unchanged. The fc width resolution in `LlamaModel.__init__` only looked at `num_aux_hidden_states` and the nested `eagle_config` layout, so any such checkpoint with a layer count other than 3 fell off the hard default of 3 and crashed on weight load: the reporter's head has 4 aux layers, the fc was built for 3, and the loader asserted on `4096x16384` vs `4096x12288`.

The fix reads the top-level key before defaulting, matching the precedence `_get_qwen3_dspark_value` in `config/speculative.py` already uses for the same pair of layouts (nested first, top-level as the modern fallback), and factors the resolution into a helper so the precedence is testable without a model init. Not a duplicate of #50170: that one warns about the aux-layer capture heuristic (silent acceptance collapse), this one is the fc width resolution (load-time crash).

## Test Plan

`tests/model_executor/test_llama_eagle3_config.py` covers all five branches: explicit `num_aux_hidden_states` wins, nested `eagle_config` layout, top-level Speculators layout, nested beats top-level, and the default of 3.

## Verification

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_llama_eagle3_config.py -q` -> 5 passed (run against the real module import on current main `e0d2704`).
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both files.
- Not run: GPU/model loading with a real 4-layer Speculators checkpoint (no such checkpoint or GPU here); the config-resolution change is exercised only at the unit level above.

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Kimi K3); the mechanism was verified by reading the full config path (Speculators' own schema, vLLM's speculators loader, and the fc construction) before writing the fix.

RecoverSSM adds two temporary workspace tensors after its two persistent states. These workspace tensors are rewritten during every speculative verification step and do not require state migration.

This PR fixes the issue.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Implement SupportsPP on more MTP drafters (Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3, GLM4-MoE)
body:
## Summary

Extends the SupportsPP treatment from #46994 (DeepSeek + Qwen3.5) and #53408 (DSv4) to five more MTP draft classes. Without it, running any of these models under `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1` with `--speculative-config method:mtp` fails in `create_engine_config` with:

```
NotImplementedError: Pipeline parallelism is not supported for this model.
Supported models implement the `SupportsPP` interface.
```

## Files

- `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/mtp.py` (`KimiK3MTP`)
- `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/mtp.py` (`KimiK3MTP`)
- `vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/mtp.py` (`MiniMaxM3MTP`)
- `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/mtp.py` (`MiniMaxM3MTP`)
- `vllm/model_executor/models/glm4_moe_mtp.py` (`Glm4MoeMTP`)

Same mechanical fix per class:
1. `SupportsPP` mixin on the outer MTP class.
2. `make_empty_intermediate_tensors_factory(["hidden_states", "residual"], self.config.hidden_size)` wired in `__init__`.
3. `# type: ignore[override]` on `forward` because MTP drafts take an extra positional `hidden_states` (Liskov violation vs the `SupportsPP` protocol).

The drafter is only ever built on the last PP stage (`is_last_pp_rank` guard in `model_runner.py`), so the SupportsPP-shaped `forward` is never called; the mixin and factory only satisfy the config verification path that copies `pipeline_parallel_size` from the target into `draft_parallel_config`. Same rationale as #46994 point (1).

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs for each target file and for `MTP SupportsPP`. Only #46994 (DeepSeek + Qwen3.5) and #53408 (DSv4) are in flight; both cover disjoint files.

## Testing

- `.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files <the five files>` — passed (ruff, mypy, typos, SPDX, etc.)

Mechanical, per-class mixin add; no behavior change on the actual per-request path (draft forward call site is untouched).

## Remaining MTP classes

Same audit turned up ~15 more MTP variants still missing SupportsPP (`ernie_mtp`, `exaone*_mtp`, `gemma4_mtp`, `hy_v3_mtp` / `hy_v4/nvidia`, `longcat_flash_mtp`, `mimo_mtp`, `mimo_v2_mtp`, `openpangu_mtp`, `step3p5_mtp`, `deepseek_v32/{amd,nvidia}`, `dots3_note/nvidia`, `inkling/{amd,nvidia}`). Happy to send a follow-up covering those if this shape is agreeable; kept the current batch to five popular families for a small first review.

AI assistance was used for code search and drafting; every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix] Add worker-side watchdog for wedged device kernels
body:
The FlashMLA sparse-decode MLA kernel can wedge silently: ptxas lowers `tcgen05.alloc.cta_group::2` into CTA-pair TMEM-allocation spin loops with no timeout, so a stalled rank spins at 100% SM utilization while the only error surfaces 300s later in an unrelated collective. The loops are ptxas-generated and cannot be bounded at source level, so this PR arms a worker-side watchdog around `execute_model` (reusing `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`) that logs a rank-local diagnostic, and compiles FlashMLA with `-lineinfo` so cuda-gdb captures map to source.

Closes #51035

title: [Bug]: Kimi-K3 DSpark/DCP illegal memory access
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Regression Introduced by vLLM commit 6d4562c59b / [PR #54277](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54277). ## Cause MLAAttentionSpec.merge() uses an assert to keep causal target and non-causal draft KV-cache specs separate. The nightly container runs optimized Python, which removes assertions. A subsequent set.pop() then nondeterministically selects the wrong metadata, eventually causing a CUDA-graph illegal memory access. ## Affected Kimi-K3, DSpark, DCP8, CUDA graphs. Both TokenSpeed MLA and FlashInfer MLA reproduce it, so changing attention backends does not help. ## Workarounds - Use the older pre-regression vLLM container. - Patch the merge back to any(spec.non_causal_multi_token_decode ...), which we validated end to end. - Eager mode avoids the graph failure but is not performance-representative. ## Correct upstream fix Preserve separate target/draft KV-cache groups, but implement the grouping condition with explicit runtime logic rather than assertion-dependent control flow. The merge should also fail deterministically if incompatible specs reach it—never use unchecked set.pop(). ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [RFC]: Per-KV-cache-group prefix-cache retention, with a hit-min exemption for hit-inert EAGLE sliding-window draft groups
body:
### Motivation.

**Summary.** On hybrid models that carry an EAGLE-style sliding-window draft group (DFlash/DSpark-shaped drafters), that group hashes `cdiv(sliding_window - 1, block_size) + 1` block ids at *every* prefix-cache boundary and frees them *cached* onto the protected tail of the one LRU that all groups share, while — once it is exempted from the hit `min` — contributing nothing to the reconciled hit length. On a GLM-5.3-Flash deployment this one group spends 87% of the prefix cache and caps coexisting conversations at ~50K tokens each. A per-group retention interval, combined with exempting such hit-inert groups from the hit `min`, restored ~4× the coexisting-conversation capacity with the fine hit grid kept for the target model's groups, and a third party reproduced 99.95% cached across alternating 120K conversations. All numbers below are **deployment evidence from a vLLM fork**, not upstream verification; the code reading is against upstream `main` @ `22df3a3`. This RFC asks for agreement on the policy before any code is posted as a PR.

**Where the cost comes from (upstream `main` @ `22df3a3`, verified).**

- `--prefix-cache-retention-interval` (`vllm/config/cache.py:156-158`, `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:530`) reaches the coordinator as one scalar, `KVCacheCoordinator.retention_interval` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py:158`), and is handed unchanged to every manager at both `cache_blocks` sites (`:306-326` base, `:740-768` hybrid).
- Everything below the coordinator is already per group: `SingleTypeKVCacheManager.cache_blocks(..., retention_interval=None)` (`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:432-436`), and each `reachable_block_mask` interprets it against its own block size and window (`:485-`, `:1010-`, `:1472-`).
- A sliding-window group needs `need = _contiguous_blocks_for_hit(window, block_size, use_eagle)` contiguous blocks at every retained boundary (`:898-908`, `:1028`); a full-attention group needs one block per boundary. Those SWA blocks are freed by `remove_skipped_blocks` -> `_remove_blocks_in_range` -> `BlockPool.free_blocks` (`:632`, `:605`), and because they are hashed they go to `blocks_to_evict_last` / `append_n`, the LRU *tail* (`vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py:723-747`). Full-attention blocks stay allocated until request end; Mamba align-mode state blocks may also be freed mid-request (`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1529-1557`), but a 3584-token Mamba group frees one id per segment where the draft group frees 33. The group with the least reusable state gets the most eviction protection.
- `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit` folds every attention group, EAGLE draft group included, into the reconciled hit (`kv_cache_coordinator.py:770-903`, `curr_hit_length = _new_hit_length` at `:871`). So giving the draft group a sparser retention on `main` today would shorten everyone's hit — which is why the fork below carries a `min` exemption first.

**Measured (deployment evidence: GLM-5.3-Flash, 2× DGX Spark, TP=2, DFlash2 draft k=7; vLLM fork `0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187`; GLM-5.3-Flash support upstream is #53906).** Groups: MLA block 3584, four Mamba "align" groups at 3584, one EAGLE sliding-window draft group with window 2048 / block 64, scheduler block 3584; one `BlockPool` of 643 block ids (642 usable; derived from the logged `max_concurrency`, see *Any Other Things*).

| group | block ids per cached 3584-token segment (dense retention) |
|---|---:|
| full attention (MLA) | 1 |
| Mamba × 4 | 4 |
| **draft sliding window** | **33** (`cdiv(2047, 64) + 1`) |
| total | 38 |

Two conversations of `S` segments coexist only while `642 >= 43·S` (each of B's segments pops 38 ids while A's cached draft tail contributes 33 back), i.e. `S <= 14.9`. Measured on a clean server: 14 segments OK / 17 evicting; pair ladders at 45K / 56K / 66K tokens hit 99% / 0% / 0%.

Raising the single global `--prefix-cache-retention-interval` to 14336 restored the ladder to 99 / 98 / 97 / 96% at 45K / 56K / 66K / 80K — but it bought that capacity by coarsening *everyone's* retention grid: a diverging sub-agent prefix then hit only 45% of a ~29K prompt instead of landing on the 3584 grid.

With per-group retention — retention `0` (reachable-boundary tails only) on the draft group, dense for MLA/Mamba — and the draft group exempted from the hit `min`, the per-segment cost drops to 5 ids (+33 per turn boundary), projected `S <= 54` (~195K tokens per conversation) with the 3584 hit grid kept. Independent reproduction by a third-party tester on a different 2× DGX Spark deployment (`max_model_len=524288`, `max_num_seqs=4`), two distinct 120K-token conversations alternated A -> B -> A -> B:

```
A cold             cached      0 / 119,995   TTFT 174.522s
A warm             cached 119,936 / 119,995   TTFT   0.581s
B cold             cached      0 / 119,995   TTFT 174.392s
B warm             cached 119,936 / 119,995   TTFT   0.590s
A return after B   cached 119,936 / 119,995   TTFT   0.567s
B return after A   cached 119,936 / 119,995   TTFT   0.567s
```

99.95% cached on every return, where the same shape previously evicted the parked conversation. Sources: https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-2x-DGX-Sparks/pull/83 (per-group retention; the tester's receipt above is in its comments) and https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-2x-DGX-Sparks/pull/84 (fine-grained hits, tested together). Those are recipe overlays on a fork; nothing there applies to `main` as-is.

### Proposed Change.

Three parts, in this order. The ask is agreement on 1 and 3 before any of the code is posted as a PR.

1. **Exempt hit-inert sliding-window groups from the reconciled hit `min`, with an explicit per-group lookup/consumption contract.** A sliding-window group is *hit-inert* when (a) it is EAGLE-annotated (`KVCacheGroupSpec.is_eagle_group`), so its hit length is not needed to bound the target's; (b) its window is shorter than `_cache_hit_alignment_tokens`, so its cached tail is only ever consultable at an alignment boundary; and (c) sparse retention is actually reachable for it: `need < alignment_tokens // block_size` (otherwise `reachable_block_mask` returns dense anyway, `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1027-1053`), `block_size` divides the alignment, and `extra_retained_tokens == 0` (it separately affects admission/retention sizing, `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py:694-730` / `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:888-895`; nonzero values require separate handling or exclusion).

   The group is still looked up. If its own hit reaches the candidate boundary, its blocks are consumed as today — that is how the retained boundary tail keeps a conversation's own follow-up turn warm. If its hit is *shorter*, it must neither shorten `curr_hit_length` nor inflate `longest_hit_length`, and its per-group result must be an explicit "no reusable blocks; allocate a fresh window", not the empty list the current lookup would return: today `find_longest_cache_hit` initialises empty per-group results (`kv_cache_coordinator.py:795-800`), fills them only for `attention_groups` (`:815-874`), and `KVCacheManager.get_computed_blocks` passes them straight to allocation (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py:228-294`), so an empty draft result cannot reuse a retained tail. This is the same per-group-boundary concern #53786 raises for SWA fine-grained hits, and it is the part that needs design agreement.

   **Unproven risk, stated plainly:** final outputs are protected by target verification, but the drafter's *acceptance* depends on the window's KV being valid. Whether a newly allocated window block is zeroed depends on `needs_kv_cache_zeroing` (`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:88-94`); the design must guarantee the window is recomputed during prefill of the uncached remainder rather than read stale, and the acceptance dip while it refills has only been measured on the fork (decode-rate control within noise), not upstream. It is free whenever the remainder is at least one window — the diverging-prefix / new-turn case. #50457 (all-sliding DFlash drafter with prefix caching, PR) is in this area and may be the right home.

2. **Resolve the retention interval per KV cache group.** `KVCacheCoordinator` gains `retention_interval_by_group: tuple[int | None, ...]`, resolved once in `__init__` and indexed at both `cache_blocks` sites. The manager API is untouched (already per call). With the identity resolution behaviour is byte-identical, which the accompanying tests pin. The seam patch is ready and rebased on `22df3a3` — `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py` +37/−4, tests +72: https://github.com/nood-co1/vllm/tree/feat/per-group-prefix-cache-retention (commit https://github.com/nood-co1/vllm/commit/b9f82ae0f946039be1e96084ef15399e8cf2e07c). It is deliberately *not* opened as a PR: on its own it is plumbing with no user-visible effect, and it is only safe to use once part 1 exists.

3. **Policy:** resolve `retention_interval = 0` for groups that satisfy part 1's predicate, i.e. cache only the reachable-boundary tails (`SlidingWindowManager.reachable_block_mask`, `retention_interval == 0` branch), and the configured value for every other group. A genuine SWA target model (window spanning the alignment, or a group still inside the `min`) is unchanged. A user override can come later if wanted; the default should not need one.

Offered as a follow-up PR (parts 1–3 together, or 2 first if maintainers prefer the decomposition) once the policy is agreed.

### Feedback Period.

One week.

### CC List.

@rchalamala (#50457), @RichApple123 (#54397), @Suppressor72 (#53786 has the same DFlash2 all-sliding drafter shape), @woosebastian (#48532, eviction order in the shared pool).

### Any Other Things.

**Related work, and why this is not a duplicate** (`gh pr list` / `gh issue list --state open --search` for "per-group retention", "retention interval", "sliding window prefix cache eviction", "EAGLE draft prefix cache", 2026-09-01; titles verified with `gh` the same day):

- Issue [#48435](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48435) — hybrid-SWA prefix caching collapses under multi-session round-robin on Gemma-4 (eager-freed SWA tails recycled tail-first). Same LRU mechanism seen from the other side: there the SWA group *is* the target's own attention, its tails are needed for the hit, and losing them zeroes the hit. This RFC targets the case where the SWA group is a drafter whose hit is not needed; the eviction-order remedy for #48435 is different and the two compose.
- PR [#50457](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50457) — all-sliding DFlash drafter with prefix caching (open). Part 1 belongs near it.
- PR [#54397](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54397) — fine-grained SWA hits (draft). Orthogonal (lookup granularity, not retention or eviction).
- PR [#51886](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51886) — retention interval for `OffloadingConnector`; PR [#52747](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52747) — docs for the existing flag; PRs [#53803](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53803), [#53479](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53479), [#53945](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53945) — which Mamba checkpoints are materialized. None make the coordinator's retention per group.
- Issues [#53670](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53670), [#53786](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53786) — EAGLE last-block drop and SWA fine-grained hits on Qwen3.8/3.5 hybrids with DFlash2 drafters; same deployment shape, different costs.
- PR [#48532](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48532) — per-group eviction order in deferred block free (same pool, different path).

**Caveats.** All measurements are deployment evidence from a fork on GLM-5.3-Flash, which is not yet in `main` (#53906); the block-id arithmetic uses code paths that exist unchanged on `main` (`SlidingWindowManager.reachable_block_mask`, `BlockPool.free_blocks`). The pool size (643 ids) is derived from the logged `GPU KV cache size` / `max_concurrency` figure rather than logged directly — filed separately as a small observability request. The ~195K-per-conversation projection is from the capacity model (`642 >= 2C − D`), which predicted every measured row's sign and order but ran ~25% optimistic at retention 7168; the 120K × 2 reproduction above is the measured point.

Submitted by nood-co1 on behalf of Blockbrain Labs (https://x.com/blockbrain_labs, GitHub org blockbrain-ai); drafted with AI assistance (Claude, with an independent adversarial review pass by OpenAI Codex folded in) and reviewed by the submitter, who checked every `file:line` against `22df3a3`.

title: [Feature]: Log block pool size and per-group blocks-per-request next to "GPU KV cache size: N tokens" (N is max_concurrency x max_model_len)
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

**Ask:** log the block pool size and the per-group blocks-per-request next to the boot line `GPU KV cache size: N tokens`, and label `N` as what it is. Small, log-only.

**What the line reports today** (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` @ `22df3a3`):

```python
# :2021-2031
def get_kv_cache_capacity(vllm_config, kv_cache_config) -> tuple[int, float]:
    """Get the group-aware KV cache token capacity and max concurrency."""
    max_model_len = vllm_config.model_config.max_model_len
    max_concurrency = get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config(vllm_config, kv_cache_config)
    return int(max_concurrency * max_model_len), max_concurrency

# :2034-2047
def update_kv_cache_capacity(vllm_config, kv_cache_config) -> None:
    num_tokens, max_concurrency = get_kv_cache_capacity(vllm_config, kv_cache_config)
    vllm_config.cache_config.kv_cache_size_tokens = num_tokens
    ...
    logger.info_once(
        "GPU KV cache size: %s tokens, "
        "Maximum concurrency for %s tokens per request: %.2fx", ...)
```

with `max_concurrency = kv_cache_config.num_blocks / num_blocks_per_request` and `num_blocks_per_request` a **sum over KV cache groups** of each group's admission blocks for one request, `cdiv(spec.max_memory_usage_bytes(vllm_config), spec.page_size_bytes)` (`:1047-1068`) — for sliding-window groups that depends on `max_in_flight_tokens`, the window and `extra_retained_tokens` (`vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py:704-740`), not just `max_model_len / block_size`. So `N` is `max_concurrency × max_model_len`: "how many max_model_len-sized requests fit", in token units. For a single-group model that equals the pool's token capacity up to rounding, which is what the label suggests. For a hybrid model it is not `num_blocks × block_size` of any group, and the reader cannot convert it back from this line: neither `num_blocks` nor `num_blocks_per_request` is included in the normal capacity boot line, `max_concurrency` is printed to two decimals, and only the ratio is recoverable. (`num_gpu_blocks` is logged on the `num_gpu_blocks_override` path, `:2318-2323`, and is in the engine-ready response, `vllm/v1/engine/core.py:1655-1668`; neither is a per-group breakdown, and neither is what a user pastes into an issue.)

**Why it matters.** The same number is exported as `kv_cache_size_tokens` (`:2039`, `vllm/v1/engine/core.py:1665`, the `cache_config_info` metric), and #51163 is a user trying to reconcile it with `num_gpu_blocks × block_size` on DeepSeek-V4 and finding no block size for which the arithmetic works — that is this quantity, not a wrong block size. On a 7-group GLM-5.3-Flash deployment (MLA + 4 Mamba + EAGLE sliding-window draft + one non-prefix-cacheable scratch group; a vLLM fork, GLM-5.3-Flash upstream is #53906) the boot line reads:

```
GPU KV cache size: 1,553,140 tokens, Maximum concurrency for 1,000,000 tokens per request: 1.55x
```

The pool behind it is 643 block ids (recovered by hand: `max_concurrency ∈ [1.553140, 1.553141)` has exactly one integer solution consistent with the physical bound, `num_blocks = 643`, `num_blocks_per_request = 414`), and a cached 3584-token segment costs 38 of those ids across the groups. Two people independently read the line as a ~1.5M-token prefix-cache pool before the arithmetic was redone; the actual coexisting-conversation capacity was ~50K tokens each. A per-group breakdown would have made that visible at boot.

**Proposal** (happy to send the PR):

1. Keep the existing line for compatibility but make the figure's meaning explicit, e.g. `GPU KV cache size: N tokens (max_concurrency × max_model_len)`.
2. Add one `info_once` with `num_gpu_blocks`, `num_blocks_per_request`, and per group `(spec type, block_size, admission blocks per request)`. `get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config` computes `num_blocks_per_request` locally and returns only the ratio, and `update_kv_cache_capacity` receives only `(num_tokens, max_concurrency)`, so the helper would need to return the breakdown (or it is recomputed once at the log site from the same per-group expression).

### Alternatives

Leave the line as is and document the semantics in `docs/` next to `kv_cache_size_tokens`. That fixes the metric's docs but not the boot log, which is what people paste into issues.

### Additional context

Related: [#51163](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51163) (`kv_cache_size_tokens` vs `num_gpu_blocks × block_size` on DeepSeek-V4). Checked `gh issue list --search` for "kv_cache_size_tokens", "max_concurrency log", "GPU KV cache size", "num_gpu_blocks log" (2026-09-01): I found no open issue in those searches asking for the pool size or a per-group breakdown to be logged.

Submitted by nood-co1 on behalf of Blockbrain Labs (https://x.com/blockbrain_labs, GitHub org blockbrain-ai); drafted with AI assistance (Claude, with an independent adversarial review pass by OpenAI Codex folded in) and reviewed by the submitter, who checked every `file:line` against `22df3a3`.

title: [Perf]: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 first-token latency regresses 6-13x from v0.26.0 to v0.28.0 on SM90/TP4 (constant ~1s/request prefill floor; knob sweep included)
body:
### Summary

Serving **DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731** on 4×H800 (SM90, TP4), upgrading **v0.26.0 → v0.28.0** improves decode throughput (+8–21%) but regresses **first-token latency ~6–20×**. There appears to be a **constant ~1s/request prefill overhead** in 0.28 that exists even for ~16-token prompts at concurrency 1, and compounds into severe admission queueing at moderate concurrency. We swept every knob we could find (details below) and could not recover 0.26-class TTFT.

### Environment

- 4×H800 80GB (SM90), single node, TP=4
- Driver 580.173.02 / CUDA 13.0
- `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0` official image (cu13 flavor), `--ipc=host --network host`
- Baseline: v0.26.0 (pip venv, torch cu129) on the same node, same weights, same flags
- Model: local `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (fp8), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, model-native max len (1M)
- Serve flags (both versions): `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-prompt-tokens-details` (variations noted per row)
- Load generator: async OpenAI-compat client, ~16-token prompts, 200–400 token outputs, temperature 0, concurrency 1 / 8 / 32
- All 0.28 runs use `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`. With the auto-enabled default (=1, which logs that it disables the torch.compile pipeline) we instead hit CUDA OOM: at init with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`, or on the first ~22k-token prefill with 0.90. This matches the throughput findings in #49370, so the whole sweep was done with `=0`.

### Numbers (TTFT p50 per request; decode tok/s per stream)

| Config | single TTFT | conc=8 TTFT | conc=32 TTFT | conc=32 decode/stream |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **v0.26.0** (MRV1, 8192, util 0.90) | **~52 ms** | **~183 ms** | **~330 ms** | 58.6 |
| v0.28.0, 8192, util 0.90, +kv-offloading 200GB | 681 ms | 1013 ms | **48.1 s** | (99.1, inflated by queueing) |
| v0.28.0, 8192, util 0.90 | n/a | 1188 ms | 7.10 s | 76.8 |
| v0.28.0, **16384**, util 0.85 (new default budget) | n/a | 1093 ms | **1.81 s** (best) | 63.4 |
| v0.28.0, MRV1 forced (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, cudagraph_mode FULL_DECODE_ONLY, 8192, 0.90) | n/a | 1172 ms | 2.34 s | 56.7 |
| v0.28.0, 16384, 0.85, `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB=4096` | n/a | 1254 ms | 2.16 s | 56.5 |
| v0.28.0, 16384, 0.85, `VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` | n/a | 981 ms | **49.3 s** | **15.4 (collapse)** |
| v0.28.0, MRV1 forced + 16384 + 0.85 | — | — | — | engine core init failure |

Observations:

1. **A constant ~1s/request first-token cost is present in every 0.28 config**, including single-stream with ~16-token prompts (681 ms vs 52 ms on 0.26 — 13×). It is not a long-prompt chunking effect: raising `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` 512→4096 changed nothing, and the tiny-prompt case shows the overhead too.
2. Raising `--max-num-batched-tokens` to the new 16384 default (#51726) recovers most of the *queueing* (48 s → 1.8 s at conc=32) but the per-request floor remains ~1 s (conc=8 is ~1.0–1.2 s in every configuration; 0.26 does 0.18 s).
3. Forcing Model Runner V1 (allowed per #51768 with non-piecewise graphs) improves conc=32 TTFT ~3× vs MRV2 at the same flags (7.1 s → 2.3 s), but is still ~7× off 0.26, and fails engine-core init when combined with 16384 + util 0.85.
4. The default sparse backend (FlashMLA family) is the better of the two on SM90: forcing `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` collapses conc=32 decode to 15 tok/s with ~49 s TTFT.
5. Decode throughput is genuinely better on 0.28 in clean configs (single 149.8 → 174.9, conc=8 100.6 → 122.3, conc=32 58.6 → 63.4 tok/s) — the regression is specific to the prefill/first-token path.
6. KV offloading (`--kv-offloading-size 200`) works functionally on 0.28 (≈258 GB written through, no crashes — thanks for the fixes that landed after 0.26), but under load it amplifies the TTFT problem (48 s at conc=32), presumably from transfer contention.

### Suspicion

The per-request floor smells like the new sparse MLA prefill path that became the default for this model in 0.27/0.28. Possibly related: #54179 and #52339 (FlashMLA sparse prefill assertions on H20 — same kernel family, adjacent SM90 hardware), and #51430/#52401 (eager cudagraph region reshuffling for this model, which is also what forces MRV2 by default per #51768).

### Questions

1. Is a ~0.7–1.2 s per-request first-token floor for DSV4 on SM90 known/expected on 0.28, or a regression worth bisecting?
2. Is there a supported way to select the 0.26-era (dense/older) prefill path for this model on 0.28+, to keep the decode gains without the TTFT floor?

Happy to run additional experiments or bisect specific PRs on this hardware — the node and the harness that produced the table are still available.

title: [Perf]: DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 on 4xH800: v0.28.0 needs ~4 GiB/GPU more non-KV memory than v0.26.0; my earlier TTFT-regression claim was caused by VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 on my side (retracted)

> ## ⚠️ Correction 2026-09-02 — the TTFT/throughput regression reported below was caused by my own configuration, not by vLLM
>
> All my v0.28.0 runs had `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` (set to work around an OOM at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`). For `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`, which has no `@support_torch_compile`, the breakable CUDA graph **is the only piecewise-graph path** (as the comment in `config/vllm.py` says), so `=0` made every prefill-containing step run fully eager. With the default (`=1`) and `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`, **v0.28.0 is faster than v0.26.0 on every arm** (TTFT 22/32/41 ms vs 49/58/68 ms at conc 1/8/32; conc-32 throughput +35%). Full data and profiler evidence in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54677#issuecomment-5504401811). What remains real: v0.28.0 needs ~4 GiB/GPU more non-KV memory than v0.26.0 on this model, which is why 0.92 OOMed for us. I am sorry for the noise; maintainers may retitle/close as they see fit.

> **Baseline figures corrected 2026-09-01** — the v0.26 conc=8 / conc=32 TTFT numbers first posted here (183 ms / 330 ms) were misquoted from a different run. Re-derived from the baseline CSV, they are **57 ms / 69 ms**, which makes the regression larger than originally stated (up to ~24× at conc=32), not smaller. All 0.28 figures are unchanged.

title: Fix DSML leaking for DeepSeek-v4 models
body:
## Purpose The tool-call reliability on DeepSeek V3.2/V4 has been reported continuously for several months. We deployed `DeepSeek-v4-Flash-0731` on a real production system. After serving billions of tokens, we find the bug actually is very severe for real production: Once DSML leaks happen around tool calls, the agent (in our case, claude code/codex) would probably loop itself correcting the tool calls and emitting more DSML. Therefore, I think the bug is worth a fix in the vLLM template parser. Agent reports: [hermes-agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/15453), [oh-my-pi](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/issues/1462), [opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/24566), [deepx-code](https://github.com/itmisx/deepx-code/issues/232), [HF discussion](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro/discussions/209), [NVIDIA DGX Spark forum](https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/deepseek-v4-flash-0731-dsml-tool-call-closers-leak-into-the-answer-after-latest-spark-vllm-b12x/381835) Related DSML leak issues in vLLM: #30541, #36654, #40800, #40801, #48089, #48931, #51914, #53227, #53831 Related PR: #53099 (this PR is based on it), #46149, #46632, #49117, #52645, #53228, #53405, #52865, #53752, #53764 Some downstream expect fixes from upstreams: [hermes-agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/15473), [oh-my-pi](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/1463) ### Leaks After serving billions of tokens, we sampled the different ways how `DSML` leaks. Surprisingly, with current vLLM template parsing, the `DSML` can actually leak anywhere =/. | model emits | tool call before this PR | tool call after this PR | what is wrong before | share of leaks | |---|---|---|---|---| | `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>`
`<｜DSML｜invoke name="record_item {`
`category: Dexes` | none; `content` = `first`
`<｜DSML｜parameter name="beta" string="true">second` | `record_item({"alpha": "first\n<｜DSML｜parameter name=\"beta\" string=\"true\">second"})` | `record_item({"beta": "second"})` | `alpha` runs past the mis-spelled closer to the next real one and swallows the whole `beta` parameter; both arguments lost | 49% | | `<｜DSML｜tool-calls`
`record_item`
`` | none; `content` = `""` | none; `content` = `<｜DSML｜tool-calls\nrecord_item\n` | the opener is not recognised, the block is consumed anyway and the whole response comes back empty | 21% | - Out of 9,500 sampled responses, 76 (0.80%) leaked DSML and leaks may happen at the same time. - Note the third class does not have reliable fixes and I can add to this PR if necessary. Or #49117/#52645 would help mitigate. ## Reproduction Deterministic at `temperature=0`. Serve with the documented flags, declare one tool, omit `tool_choice`, and leave `strict` unset (note it is the **behavior of most coding agents** and even setting `strict` does not fully resolve the leaks): ``` --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 ``` ```python import json, urllib.request BASE, MODEL = "http://127.0.0.1:8000", "deepseek-v4-flash" D = "｜DSML｜" TOOLS = [{"type": "function", "function": { "name": "record_item", "description": "Record one item.", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"alpha": {"type": "string"}, "beta": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["alpha", "beta"]}}}] # no "strict" key CASES = { "runaway_name": f'Reply with exactly this and nothing else:\n\n<{D}tool_calls>\n' f'<{D}invoke name="record_item {{\ncategory: Dexes', "mis_closed_parameter": f'Reply with exactly this and nothing else:\n\n<{D}tool_calls>\n' f'<{D}invoke name="record_item">\n' f'<{D}parameter name="alpha" string="true">first\n' f'<{D}parameter name="beta" string="true">second\n' f'\n', "undeclared_tool": 'Call a tool named "totally_undeclared_tool" with alpha="x". ' 'Do not write any other text.', "misspelled_opener": f'Reply with exactly this line and nothing else:\n\n' f'<{D}tool-calls\nrecord_item\n', "control": 'Call record_item with alpha="A" and beta="B". No other text.', } for name, prompt in CASES.items(): body = {"model": MODEL, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], "tools": TOOLS, "temperature": 0.0, "max_tokens": 600} req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + "/v1/chat/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) msg = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=300).read())["choices"][0]["message"] print(f"--- {name}") print(" content:", repr(msg.get("content") or "")[:120]) for c in msg.get("tool_calls") or []: print(f" call: {c['function']['name']!r} args={c['function']['arguments']!r}"[:200]) ``` (The script was adapted from [#52645](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52645#issuecomment-5332292216)) ## Test Plan CI. ## Test Result See above table. ## AI Tool Assistance The PR itself is handwritten but the code is largely assisted by Claude, as the commits already show. However, it is exactly adapted from our running production code. ---
