title: [Bug]: Speculative kv_cache_dtype=fp8 crashes startup on hybrid GDN models - FlashInfer "Unrecognized dtype: auto", then native crash on SM89 with explicit target dtype
body:
### Summary Setting a **draft-only** KV cache dtype via `--speculative-config '{"kv_cache_dtype": "fp8", ...}'` on a hybrid GDN model (Qwen3.5-family: full-attention + GDN layers) crashes engine startup in the FlashInfer attention metadata builder: ``` ValueError: Unrecognized dtype: auto ``` The identical launch **without** the speculative `kv_cache_dtype` field works fine (bf16 KV everywhere). Explicitly setting `--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16` on the target (so no group carries the raw `auto`) gets past this error, but the engine then dies with a **native crash** (no Python traceback) during attention init on SM89. Checked against current `main`: both `LLMBaseProposer._create_draft_vllm_config()` (kv_cache_dtype passthrough) and `FlashInferBackend.get_dtype_for_flashinfer()` (no `auto` mapping) are unchanged, so this should still reproduce on main. ### Environment
collect-env (abridged)
vLLM 0.28.0 (pip wheel)
PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12.3, Ubuntu 24.04
4x RTX 4090 (SM89, PCIe), TP4, CUDA runtime 12.8
Attention backend: FlashInfer (auto-selected; the drafter needs non-causal attention)
Target: Qwen3.5-family hybrid model (full-attn + GDN layers), INT8-W8A16
Draft: DFlash2 drafter (method="dflash")
Full `vllm collect-env` output available on request.
### Reproduction ```bash vllm serve \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --max-model-len 200000 \ --speculative-config '{"method": "dflash", "model": , "num_speculative_tokens": 4, "kv_cache_dtype": "fp8"}' ``` Any hybrid GDN target + draft-model-style speculative method should hit the same path; the draft does not need to be DFlash specifically. ### Actual behavior **Failure 1** - with only the speculative `"kv_cache_dtype": "fp8"`, every TP worker fails during `initialize_kv_cache`: ```python-traceback File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 680, in initialize_from_config self.model_runner.initialize_kv_cache(kv_cache_config) File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 532, in initialize_kv_cache self.attn_groups, attn_cg_support, self.kernel_block_sizes = init_attn_backend(...) File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py", line 156, in init_attn_backend group.create_metadata_builders(...) File "vllm/v1/worker/utils.py", line 275, in create_metadata_builders builder_cls(...) File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py", line ~840, in FlashInferMetadataBuilder.__init__ self.kv_cache_dtype = FlashInferBackend.get_dtype_for_flashinfer(...) File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py", line 514, in get_dtype_for_flashinfer raise ValueError(f"Unrecognized dtype: {kv_cache_dtype}") ValueError: Unrecognized dtype: auto ``` `get_dtype_for_flashinfer()` only maps `fp8`/`fp8_e4m3`/`fp8_e5m2`/`nvfp4*`. In the normal single-dtype flow the raw `auto` is resolved to the model dtype before attention init; with a speculative `kv_cache_dtype` set, at least one attention group of the hybrid model appears to receive the **unresolved** string. Likely suspects: the GDN KV group, or the target-side group of the multi-group KV config created alongside the draft config. **Failure 2** - adding `--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16` (target) so no group carries `auto`: ``` ERROR [core.py:1346] EngineCore failed to start. ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:311] Worker proc VllmWorker-3 died unexpectedly (exit code: None) ``` i.e. a native crash of one worker during (draft) attention initialization on SM89, no Python traceback. The FlashInfer fp8-KV path appears to be non-functional on Ada for this (draft, non-causal) configuration, and it takes the whole engine down instead of failing backend selection with a readable error. ### Expected behavior Either: 1. draft KV cache dtype is honored (draft fp8, target bf16), or 2. startup fails fast with a clear error, e.g. "fp8 draft KV cache is not supported with backend FlashInfer on SM89", instead of `ValueError: Unrecognized dtype: auto` / silent worker native crash. ### Related issues - #48380 / PR #48381 - same family (draft inheriting a target-only KV dtype), but for MLA `fp8_ds_mla` layouts; this report is the draft-only `fp8` path on a hybrid GDN target. - #44184, #48406 - fp8 KV cache crashes together with spec decode. - #49077, #52202 - fp8 KV support work for pre-SM89 GPUs. - #54341 - fp8_e5m2/e4m3 KV writer mismatches. Happy to test patches / provide full logs.

title: [ROCm][RDNA3] Fix W4A16 split-K accuracy and determinism
body:
## Problem

The RDNA3 (gfx11) W4A16 GPTQ kernels accumulate split-K partials in
bf16/fp16 via CAS atomics. The narrowing happens **before** accumulation,
and low-precision addition is not associative — so whichever split block
wins the CAS first changes the result. That numerical error is present on
**every affected forward pass**, in every decoding configuration.

Greedy decoding is merely where it becomes visible: at temperature 0 the
rounded logit wobble can flip `argmax` between repeated identical
generations (the trail in #50603). Under sampling (e.g. T=0.6) the same
error hides under the sampler's own noise while still sitting under every
reported metric.

## Root cause

```
FP32 per-block partial
  -> bf16/fp16 narrowing (8 / 11 mantissa bits)
  -> CAS-atomic accumulation in execution-dependent order
```

gfx11 has no packed bf16/fp16 atomic, so the epilogue emulated one with a
CAS retry loop — which also made the accumulation order scheduler- and
contention-dependent.

## Fix

Keep the compute kernels and dispatch unchanged; replace only the epilogue
on both paths:

```
FP32 per-split partials
  -> fixed ascending-z FP32 reduction
  -> one final bf16/fp16 cast
```

* Every path writes each output element exactly once; `k_split == 1`
  (WMMA) and `z_count == 1` (scalar) keep/store directly — no scratch, no
  reduce, no atomics.
* The FP32 partials scratch is `at::empty`: coverage is total by
  construction (every reducer-visible `(z, m, n)` slot has exactly one
  writer in all seven WMMA variants and the scalar kernel; the invariant
  is documented at `alloc_wmma_partials`), so there is no zero-fill pass.
* Scratch is per-call via the caching allocator, row-tiled so the bound is
  independent of the caller's M.

## Accuracy (W7900/gfx1100, FP32 dequantized reference)

Max abs error, synthetic uint4b8/group-128 weights, K=4096:

| path | dtype | legacy CAS | this PR | factor |
|------|-------|-----------:|--------:|-------:|
| scalar | bf16 | 0.24–0.37 | 0.0625 | 4–6x |
| WMMA | bf16 | 0.15–0.23 | 0.09–0.11 | ~2x |
| WMMA | fp16 | 0.024–0.038 | 0.011–0.018 | ~2x |
| scalar | fp16 | ~0.95 | 0.002-0.015 | **94-201x** (see 2026-10-01 update: exact factored dequant) |

bf16 is the headline; fp16 carried 11 mantissa bits so the removed CAS
rounding cost it ~8x less (as expected). The scalar-fp16 row was the
classic exllama bit-trick rounding the per-group offset constant to fp16
— fixed by the exact factored dequant in the 2026-10-01 update below
(now 0.002-0.015 on the same shapes).

The earlier "0.028 → 0.0061" measurement is the same bf16 improvement
factor on real Muse weights. bf16 residual error now sits at the final
output cast (1 ulp); WMMA at the B-tile narrowing.

## Determinism

Fixed inputs now produce bit-identical outputs on every call: 20/20
benchmark shapes repeatable; real Muse q_proj at M=1 gives 1 distinct
result / 100 calls (previously up to 200/200 distinct). Repeatability
alone is not correctness, so the tests also check values against the FP32
reference — a stale `at::empty` scratch slot would be bitwise-repeatable
and wrong, and is caught by the tolerance analysis in the test module.

## Performance (W7900/gfx1100, median of 100 CUDA-event timings)

Rows are **bf16**; fp16 differs in dispatch (bf16 reaches WMMA at
M ≥ 16, fp16 not until M ≥ 64 — at M=16 fp16 is still on the scalar path):

| M | N | K | path | k_split | scratch MB | before µs | after µs | Δ |
|--:|---:|---:|------|--------:|-----------:|----------:|---------:|---:|
| 1 | 4096 | 4096 | scalar | 16 | 0.25 | 44.5 | 39.7 | -10.8% |
| 8 | 4096 | 4096 | scalar | 16 | 2.0 | 61.8 | 57.2 | -7.5% |
| 16 | 4096 | 4096 | wmma 16x16_1w | 4 | 1.0 | 58.8 | 53.7 | **-8.7%** |
| 64 | 4096 | 4096 | wmma 64x64_4w | 4 | 4.0 | 120.5 | 112.0 | **-7.0%** |
| 128 | 4096 | 4096 | wmma 128x64_k32 | 4 | 8.0 | 123.5 | 114.7 | **-7.2%** |
| 512 | 4096 | 4096 | wmma 128x64_k32 | 4 | 32.0 | 378.4 | 350.8 | **-7.3%** |
| 512 | 4096 | 6656 | wmma 128x64_k32 | 4 | 32.0 | 554.7 | 527.4 | -4.9% |
| 512 | 25600 | 6656 | wmma 128x64_k32 | **1** | **0** | 3070.7 | 2894.2 | -5.8% |

(Historical W7900 campaign numbers; superseded WMMA-dispatch note: fp16
now reaches WMMA from M>=12, see the 2026-10-01 update.)
Full tables for both dtypes incl. N/K/k_split/scratch
per row: `05-benchmark.md` in the evidence package:
https://github.com/AIwork4me/vllm/tree/evidence/pr-54706-jartx-w7900/validation-54706-jartx-w7900
(immutable: same tree at commit
https://github.com/AIwork4me/vllm/tree/9bc79045c157dd12a2728cad4e52fd9b21b0ccc3/validation-54706-jartx-w7900)

Notes:
- "before" = this branch's original HEAD (zero-filled WMMA scratch);
  "after" = with the dead zero-fill removed (`at::zeros` → `at::empty`
  once total coverage was proven). Same-M/different-N matters: at M=512,
  N=4096 → k_split=4 (32 MB scratch) while N=25600 → k_split=1 (none).
- Versus a locally restored legacy-CAS control build, the deterministic
  epilogue is now at parity or **faster** for prefill shapes (bf16 M=16:
  53.7 vs 55.3 µs); only M=1 decode pays a residual ~4–10% (scratch
  round-trip at tiny output) — the price of bit-reproducibility.
- Numerics are bit-identical before/after the memset removal on all 20
  shapes (zero-init was dead traffic).
- A follow-up fix (CodeRabbit finding) gave the V7/V8 k_split==1 path
  the same direct-store branch the 64x64 path had: no scratch, no
  reduce, partials == nullptr. N=25600 row: bf16 3020.1 -> 2894.2 µs
  (-4.2%), fp16 2858.3 -> 2668.6 µs (-6.6%); split-K shapes unchanged
  within noise; numerics bit-identical.

## Why not FP32 atomics?

gfx11 does have `global_atomic_add_f32`; an FP32 scratch accumulated with
native atomics plus one cast pass would remove nearly all the rounding
error with no reduce kernel. We still chose the fixed-order reduce:
FP32 addition is also non-associative, so atomic accumulation remains
order-dependent — vastly better numerically, but not bit-reproducible.
Since bit-exact reproducibility is an explicit goal of this PR, the
fixed ascending-z reduction is the design that guarantees it.

## Tests

`tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna3_w4a16_determinism.py` — 24 tests:

* bit-repeatability through the public op (scalar/WMMA × bf16/fp16),
  with the scalar regression at K=4096 (16 concurrent writers — well
  inside the old failure regime, whose onset was 2–4 writers);
* FP32-reference correctness for scalar and WMMA, split-K and
  direct-store (k_split == 1 / z_count == 1) paths, both dtypes, with
  tolerances derived from each path's rounding structure;
* explicit V7/V8 (128x64) no-split coverage at M=512, N=25600, K=6656
  (repeatability + FP32 reference, both dtypes; routing asserted via a
  replica of the k_split heuristic);
* test hygiene: repo-standard `dist_init` fixture (no `__enter__` leak,
  no hardcoded MASTER_PORT).

On a locally restored legacy-CAS build, 8 tests fail (7 repeatability +
the scalar-bf16 reference check at max_abs 0.30 vs 0.10 tolerance,
measured on the then-20-test suite); on this PR, 24/24 pass.

## Validation

- W7900D / gfx1100, ROCm 7.14 runtime, torch 2.14; upstream base
  `40b2f62061575905aaac8bc360eaea62a4baeb67`
- targeted tests 24/24 PASS (bf16 + fp16, scalar + WMMA, incl. V7/V8
  no-split)
- FP32-reference correctness + A/B legacy control: see above
- benchmark matrix: dtype × M{1,8,16,64,128,512} × N{4096,25600} ×
  K{4096,6656} with path/k_split/scratch per row (full evidence package
  below)
- independent RX 7900 XT evidence from @cadamcat (A/B table in #50603)
- full W7900/gfx1100 reproducibility package (environment, correctness
  and A/B-control evidence, complete benchmark tables):
  https://github.com/AIwork4me/vllm/tree/evidence/pr-54706-jartx-w7900/validation-54706-jartx-w7900
- Muse eager ctx512: 1 unique / 8 greedy generations; 0
  same-input/different-output events across 16,640 intercepted W4A16
  GEMM calls

## Scope

gfx11 / RDNA3 W4A16 only; no attention-routing changes. The residual
Muse eager/8192 divergence after this fix was traced to ROCm paged
attention V-cache tail consumption and is fixed by #53856. Investigation
trail: #50603; full earlier evidence in the
`validation-50603/rdna3-w4a16-upstream-cleanup` tree linked there.

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used for code iteration, validation orchestration, and
drafting. I reviewed the final diff, kernel behavior, test results,
performance data, and evidence and can explain the change end to end.




---

## Rebase validation (2026-09-09, post-#54809)

Rebased onto upstream/main `385dce36` after #54809 (GPTQ act-order/g_idx
removal) and revalidated on gfx1100 (W7900D, torch 2.14.0+rocm7.14,
ROCm 7.2.1 toolchain — same environment as the original campaign):

- conflicts resolved semantically; the post-#54809 no-g_idx op contract
  (`gptq_gemm_rdna3(a, b_q_weight, b_qzeros, b_scales, use_v2_format)`)
  kept native — no `b_g_idx`/`b_q_perm`/`has_g_idx`/`w_gidx_param_name`
  anywhere in the PR
- gfx1100 build PASS; gfx942 (non-RDNA3 stub pass) compile guard PASS
- targeted determinism/FP32-reference suite: **24/24 PASS**
- upstream RDNA3 tests (`test_rdna3_w4a16`, `test_rdna3_compile_guards`,
  `test_rdna3_w4a16_selection`, `test_rdna3_moe_w4a16`): 148 passed,
  5 skipped (non-gfx1100 guards), 0 failed
- V7/V8 `k_split == 1` direct-store confirmed (no scratch, no reducer,
  profiler-verified); split-K control: deterministic FP32 reducer active,
  scratch 33.6 MB as designed; scalar z_count=1/z_count=16 paths verified
- performance within noise of the pre-rebase reference:
  no-split M=512 N=25600 K=6656 — bf16 2877 µs / fp16 2633 µs (was
  2894 / 2669); split-K M=512 N=4096 K=6656 — bf16 545 µs / fp16 507 µs
  (was ~528 / ~501); scratch 0 / 33.6 MB unchanged
- DCO green on all replayed commits; historical W7900 measurements above
  remain the pre-rebase evidence package (unchanged)

Note: the two commits added on top of the original six adapt the tests to
the post-#54809 API and apply the repo's current formatter pins
(ruff 0.14.0 / clang-format 21.1.2); no semantic changes.


## Update (2026-10-01): exact fp16 dequant, M>=12 WMMA dispatch, fused fp16 split-K reduce

Addressed @JartX's two review items (semantically ported from
dafcde3f8bb9 and 5e8db861e02 — neither cherry-picks cleanly) and rebased
onto current upstream/main `ccda9098`.

### 1. fp16 dequant is now exact (the "~0.95" row is gone)

The old bit-trick bakes `z = scale * (-1024 - zero)` into an **fp16**
constant; that representation rounding (~0.008 abs at scale≈0.02, repeated
for every weight of a group×column) was the error — not the epilogue. The
dequant now uses the exact factored form

```
sum_k a_k * w_k  =  y * sum_k a_k * (1024 + q_k)  +  z * sum_k a_k
```

with **fp32** (y, z) pairs per nibble slot and the z·sum_a correction
applied once per 32-K round (same structure the bf16 path already had).
Ported to the dense scalar kernel **and** the MoE kernel (its baked error
was previously masked by the dense reference being equally biased).

Accuracy vs the FP32 dequantized reference on gfx1100 (public op path,
100-repeat calls, K=4096–6656, M=1/4/8):

| path | dtype | before | after | factor |
|------|-------|-------:|------:|-------:|
| scalar | fp16 | 1.03–1.37 | 0.002–0.015 | **94–201x** |
| scalar | bf16 | 0.06–0.12 | 0.06–0.12 | bit-identical (unchanged) |

### 2. WMMA dispatch: both dtypes from M ≥ 12

Measured scalar/WMMA crossover on this gfx1100 (both ops timed directly,
identical inputs, median of 300; full table in the dispatch comment): at
M ≥ 12 WMMA wins or ties on every measured shape for both dtypes
(1.00–1.69x); below that scalar wins and is the more accurate path. fp16
previously stayed scalar until M=64 — that speed came with ~100x more
dequant error; with the exact dequant the crossover moved to 12, same as
bf16. An M=11 (scalar) / M=12 (WMMA) boundary test pins it via profiler
kernel names.

### 3. Split-K reduction fused into the fp16 kernel — with per-call state

The fp16 scalar path now reduces in the GEMM kernel: each block publishes
arrival on its tile's ticket; the last z block sums the z-slices in fixed
ascending order (batched loads) and rounds once — still bit-reproducible,
one launch fewer, partials read while L2-hot.

**The ticket array is per-call** (`at::zeros`, one int per tile,
re-armed in-kernel), **not** the device-global `g_w4_tickets` of the
reference: nothing in vLLM serializes quantized W4A16 GEMMs on one device
(DeepSeek V4/V4.1 aux-stream forks, LoRA dual-stream, and the
SharedExperts side stream all overlap quantized linears today), so
cross-launch global state would be a correctness hazard. Per-call tickets
from the stream-aware caching allocator keep concurrent invocations
independent by construction; verified by a two-stream concurrent-vs-serial
(bit-exact) test and CUDA-graph capture/replay tests.

The **bf16** path keeps the separate reducer: measured on gfx1100, fusing
it was neutral at M=1 and up to ~10% slower at M=4–8 (the fused reduce
serializes a multi-row tile's reduction into one block per tile), so bf16
behavior is unchanged.

Performance, interleaved A/B/C in one session (original baked / exact +
separate reduce / final; min of 4-rep medians × 3 rounds; public op):

| dtype | M | vs original | vs separate-reduce |
|-------|--:|------------:|-------------------:|
| fp16 | 1 | **−6.3 … −11.3%** | −8.1 … −8.8% |
| fp16 | 4 | −6.7 … −8.2% | −11 … −12% |
| fp16 | 8 | −2.2 … −7.6% | −6 … −16% |
| bf16 | 1–8 | −1.4 … +0.1% (noise) | — (unchanged path) |

i.e. the final fp16 kernel is both ~100–200x more accurate **and**
6–11% faster at decode than the pre-review state.

### Validation (gfx1100 / ROCm 7.2.1 toolchain, torch 2.13.0+rocm7.14, base `ccda9098`)

- targeted determinism/reference suite: **54/54 PASS** (fp16+bf16, scalar+
  WMMA, split-K z∈{2,16,17,26} incl. K%256≠0 clipped tails, no-split,
  G∈{32,64,128}, M_COUNT∈{1,2,4,8}, M=100 multi-row-tile, dispatch
  boundary, 100x repeats, two-stream, graph capture/replay)
- upstream RDNA3 suites (`test_rdna3_w4a16`, `_compile_guards`,
  `_selection`, `_moe_w4a16`): **151 passed, 5 skipped** (non-gfx1100
  guards), 0 failed
- gfx942 full build PASS; RDNA3 ops confirmed absent from the gfx942
  binary (compile guard)
- non-RDNA3 stub updated for the new kernel parameter

### Scope notes

- The MoE kernel gets the **exact dequant** (its tests compare against the
  dense op, which is now exact) but keeps its existing epilogue; making
  the MoE split-K deterministic is follow-up work.
- `groupsize % 32 == 0` is now stated where assumed and host-enforced
  (dense + MoE) — such configs were silently wrong before (the kernel
  checks group transitions at 32-K granularity); K % 32 ≠ 0 remains a
  pre-existing upstream limitation, unchanged here.
- The legacy CAS epilogues stay for A/B comparison, clearly marked; the
  shipped dispatch never selects them.

### 🐛 Describe the bug When serving Kimi K2 base or DeepSeek v3 base, with the default moe_backend selection of FlashInfer TRTLLM will cause hangs under DP/EP. On the other hand, TP with TRTLLM and DP/EP with triton moe_backend work. This issue was not present in 0.20.1. I bisected vLLM releases and found that 0.21.0 introduced this regression; all releases after seem to have this problem. Flashinfer was not bumped between those two versions, still at 0.6.8.post1, so it seems unlikely to be related. I dug into the code changes around the code listed in the py-spy output below, and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39917 touches related files, with https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4172 reading like a possibly related issue. (FP4 hangs under PDL; the suggestion in the issue is to disable PDL) When py-spying the stuck deployment, roughly 10 minutes into a prefill-heavy load (perplexity eval), it looks like flashinfer::trtllm_fp8_block_scale_moe is hung, either around or at execute_dummy_batch. title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix DFlash draft KV cache dtype isolation
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #54690.

When DFlash uses an explicit FP8 draft KV-cache dtype while the target keeps
`kv_cache_dtype=auto`, the shared cache configuration can expose the unresolved
target value to FlashInfer metadata construction. This causes startup to fail
with `ValueError: Unrecognized dtype: auto`.

This change:

- resolves the FlashInfer cache dtype from the layers in the actual attention
  group;
- keeps target and draft KV-cache dtypes isolated while preserving the shared
  `CacheConfig` layout lifecycle required by model loading; and
- restores the target dtype even when draft model construction fails.

This is not duplicating an existing PR. The closest open DFlash changes cover
RoPE cache reuse (#53251), draft weight-quantization mapping (#53122), fused
quantized context-KV projection (#51620), or DSpark-specific MLA cache handling
(#48381); none addresses the target/draft `CacheConfig.kv_cache_dtype` lifecycle
or per-attention-group FlashInfer dtype resolution.

AI assistance was used during implementation and validation. The submitting
human reviewed every changed line, understands the change end-to-end, and
confirmed the test evidence below.

## Test Plan

Run the focused regression and worker suites:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_model_loading.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_group_head_counts.py::test_kv_cache_dtype_comes_from_the_group \
  tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_dcp_spec_reorder.py::test_flashinfer_resolves_group_cache_dtype_without_mutating_config \
  tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py
```

Run the relevant pre-commit hooks for all six changed Python files, then perform
an exact-base before/after DFlash startup and generation check on CUDA.

## Test Result

- Focused pytest suite on RTX 3090 / SM86: `23 passed, 14 warnings in 9.84s`.
- Relevant pre-commit hooks passed: Ruff check/format, SPDX, typos, filename,
  forbidden-import, `torch.cuda`, boolean-context-manager, root-lazy-import, and
  Python 3.10 mypy checks.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Exact-base A/B at `4ac452ad9883864bb3ab0412a45a63cbf62d730a`:
  - Before: Qwen3-8B target with `auto` KV dtype plus Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16 draft
    with FP8 KV dtype fails in `FlashInferMetadataBuilder` with
    `ValueError: Unrecognized dtype: auto`.
  - After: the same configuration loads the target and draft, resolves the
    draft attention group to `torch.float8_e4m3fn`, allocates KV cache, warms
    up, and generates successfully.
- A TP=4 run initialized and loaded all four target/draft workers, but the
  environment then hit a stale native extension missing
  `_C.vocab_parallel_embedding`; this is not counted as a TP=4 pass.
- The reporter's native SM89 / 4x RTX 4090 path was not rerun because that node
  was unreachable. The separate explicit-target-dtype native crash described
  in the issue therefore remains unverified by this PR.
- A full all-hook pre-commit invocation was attempted but could not install an
  unrelated Go hook environment because `proxy.golang.org` timed out. No Go or
  GitHub Actions files are changed.
- No performance claim is made.

---

- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.

title: [Bugfix][DCP] Validate connector interleave capabilities
body:
# Summary

Add a connector capability for DCP KV-cache interleave alignment and use it for both adjustment and validation.

This includes the core behavior from #54457 and adds the missing validation/composition path:

- connectors that need block-aligned DCP interleave keep the existing automatic adjustment;
- `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, `OffloadingConnector`, and `DecodeBenchConnector` declare that they do not require block-aligned interleave;
- `validate_block_size()` uses the same connector capability predicate as `adjust_dcp_kv_cache_interleave_size()`;
- `MultiConnector` owns recursive child capability aggregation through the same connector classmethod, so mixed compositions remain conservative while all-local compositions keep valid custom interleave values.

# Why This Is Needed

With DCP enabled, the current config code always treats KV-transfer setups like block-oriented PD and widens `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` to the local KV block size. That is correct for connectors that move block-layout KV across DCP ranks, but it is unnecessarily restrictive for local/offloading connectors that operate within the same DCP rank. This breaks production-style Kimi-K3 local offload recipes such as:

```text
--decode-context-parallel-size 8
--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1
```

The #54457 behavior fixes the automatic adjustment for direct local/offloading connectors, but the capability has to be used consistently by validation as well. Otherwise an invalid local-offload config such as `block_size=16` with `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size=3` can skip the divisibility check. `MultiConnector` also needs to compose child capabilities explicitly; otherwise a local child can be hidden behind the wrapper, or a mixed local + PD composition can lose the stricter child requirement.

# Correctness Notes

The default capability remains conservative: connectors return `True` unless they explicitly opt out. A connector should only return `False` if it does not require DCP block-aligned KV transfer layout.

For `MultiConnector`, the composed result is `True` if any child requires block-aligned DCP interleave. Empty compositions also return `True`. This preserves correctness for mixed setups such as `MultiConnector(SimpleCPUOffloadConnector, NixlConnector)` while allowing all-local compositions to keep finer valid interleave values.

The capability is only queried on DCP paths. `adjust_dcp_kv_cache_interleave_size()` returns before connector resolution when `decode_context_parallel_size <= 1`, and `validate_block_size()` short-circuits the same way. For DCP-enabled KV-transfer configs, resolving the connector class follows the existing config-time connector validation pattern used by CUDA graph and HMA checks; unsupported or broken connector configs should continue to fail explicitly rather than being silently treated as a conservative layout.

# Relation To #53917

This PR is split out from the original full-stack #53917. The end-to-end Kimi-K3 SimpleCPU validation on #53917 used this capability behavior so the production recipe could preserve `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size=1`. This PR is still a config-contract change, not a SimpleCPU fine-grained cache-hit implementation.

# Relation To #54457

This PR carries #54457's original commit from @cjackal and adds the follow-up validation/MultiConnector handling. It also includes the later `DecodeBenchConnector` capability update with co-author attribution.

# Validation

Initial three-revision matrix before the classmethod cleanup:

```text
main:          3 passed, 4 failed
#54457 only:   5 passed, 2 failed
this PR head:  7 passed
```

The #54457-only failures were the two cases completed by the follow-up: invalid `interleave=3` was not rejected for `block_size=16`, and `MultiConnector(SimpleCPUOffloadConnector)` did not inherit the child's capability. A mixed `MultiConnector(SimpleCPUOffloadConnector, NixlConnector)` keeps the stricter block-aligned behavior.

Latest head after rebasing over the upstream Nixl-only interleave fix:

```text
head: 96d3bdac8a29025681c56c52bd1dd8171d748a48
pytest -q tests/test_config.py -k "pd_dcp_interleave or local_offload or simple_cpu_offload or multi_connector or empty_multi_connector"
result: 11 passed, 239 deselected
```

The latest focused tests include direct `DecodeBenchConnector`, nested all-local `MultiConnector`, upstream's Nixl/MultiConnector strict-alignment coverage, and invalid local-offload validation coverage.

A Kimi-K3 TP8/DCP8 startup and completion smoke test was also run with `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size=1`, FP8 KV cache, dummy weights, and eager execution. On the base, vLLM logged that it changed the requested interleave from `1` to `1536`. This PR preserved `1`; the server became healthy and completed the request successfully. The smoke test did not include DSpark because this PR only changes the DCP transfer-layout contract.

title: [Bug]: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next generates corrupted Thai orthography under vLLM; the same model under llama.cpp at the same QSA budget is clean
body:
### Summary

`Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` under vLLM produces systematically malformed Thai: single-character substitutions, displaced tone marks and doubled combining marks. The same model at the same effective QSA budget under llama.cpp is clean — 0 defects across 130 samples versus 12–18 per 1000 Thai characters across five vLLM configurations.

This was originally reported as part of #54521 (non-determinism from `persistent_topk`). It is a **separate defect**: I have since shown non-determinism is not its cause, and that QSA block selection is not either. Splitting it out so #54521 can stay scoped to determinism.

### Environment

- 2x DGX Spark GB10 (sm_121), `-tp 2`, aarch64, driver 580.159.03 / 580.95.05
- vLLM `0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198` (official `vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next` body)
- `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`, `--enforce-eager`, stock `indexer_budget=2048`
- Sampling: the model card's temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20. **Greedy is not usable for a quality measurement on this model** — it degenerates even at 105 prompt tokens — so every number below is a rate over 10 samples.

### What the corruption looks like

The probe is a Thai date-countdown answer, so the same words recur with unambiguous correct forms:

| correct | observed |
|---|---|
| `ปีใหม่` | `ปีใหม้` (mai tho for mai ek) |
| `สงกรานต์` | `สงกรานตค์์`, thanthakhat detached or missing |
| `ครับ` | `ครรับ` (doubled ro rua) |
| `คริสต์ศักราช` | `คริศต์ศักราช` (so sala for so suea) |
| `เช่น` | `เชน่` (tone mark displaced past the consonant) |
| `คำนวณ` | `คานวณ` (sara am lost) |
| `อีก` | `อีีก` (doubled sara ii) |

Thai is a sensitive detector rather than a special case: it runs ~3x more tokens per character than English, with many near-identical combining-mark tokens, so a perturbation surfaces as visibly broken text instead of a harmless paraphrase.

### Evidence

Prompt-length ladder built from a real captured agent request by dropping tool definitions and truncating the system prompt; the conversation itself is never touched, so every rung asks the identical question. N=10 per cell, corrupt / informative samples:

| prompt tok | 20394 | 16006 | 13369 | 9635 | 8556 | 6490 | 4675 | 2959 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vLLM stock | 6/10 | 10/10 | 10/10 | 9/9 | 9/10 | 10/10 | 7/9 | 7/10 |
| vLLM, no MTP | 7/10 | 7/10 | 7/10 | 9/9 | 7/10 | 6/8 | 6/9 | 6/8 |
| **llama.cpp** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** |

Five further rungs from 2631 down to 1720 tokens: vLLM 6–10/10, llama.cpp 0/10. **The corruption is not length-gated.**

A structural detector (stacked tone marks, doubled upper vowels, tone-then-vowel — independent of the word list above) over every sample collected:

| engine / configuration | samples | Thai chars | defects per 1k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| vLLM stock | 77 | 5981 | 16.55 |
| vLLM stock, short rungs | 113 | 9316 | 15.99 |
| vLLM without the sort patch | 78 | 6751 | 17.63 |
| vLLM `indexer_budget=8192` | 77 | 6486 | 14.96 |
| vLLM without MTP | 76 | 5737 | 12.90 |
| **llama.cpp UD-IQ4_XS** | **130** | **11085** | **0.00** |

### The llama.cpp comparison is matched, not approximate

llama.cpp build 10731, `unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF` UD-IQ4_XS, single GB10, `--jinja -c 32768`. It implements QSA itself and does not fall back to dense attention:

- `src/models/qwen4exp.cpp:423` — "QSA attends to a budget of whole blocks of compress_ratio tokens, plus the incomplete tail; one mean-pooled indexer key scores each block"
- `build_qsa_top_k` → `ggml_top_k(ctx0, expanded, width)` with `width = min(n_kv, indexer_top_k + r - 1)`, then the KQ mask is unmasked only at the selected cells

At the 20k rung that is **2051 attended tokens of 20343**. vLLM at stock `indexer_budget=2048` attends `k=512` blocks × `compress_ratio=4` = **2048 tokens**. Same algorithm, same budget, same ~10:1 sparsity, from GGUF metadata that is the model's own (`indexer.top_k = 2048`, `compress_ratios = [0,0,0,4,...]`, `full_attention_interval = 4`).

### Ruled out

- **QSA sparse block selection.** Density is `prompt_tokens <= indexer_budget` (the compress ratio cancels), so shortening the prompt reaches genuinely dense selection. Five dense cells — 4/8, 7/10, 9/10, 6/10, 8/10 — all corrupt at the sparse rate. Dense selection does not help.
- **Non-determinism.** A deterministic tie-break makes the real payload byte-identical across runs and leaves the Thai just as corrupt (#54521).
- **Speculative decoding.** `--speculative-config` removed: still 6–9/10 corrupt, 12.90 defects per 1k.
- **Quantization.** UD-IQ4_XS is a *coarser* quant than the FP8 used under vLLM, and the lower-precision weights are the clean ones.
- **The weights / the model / the QSA algorithm.** Clean under llama.cpp.
- Also eliminated earlier in #54521: prefix caching, chat template, `rows_per_chunk`, #53287, CUDA graphs (`--enforce-eager` throughout), the weight loader, and `indexer_budget` overrides.

### Not controlled

Two differences between the engines remain uncontrolled, and I would rather state them than argue them away.

**1. Chat template.** llama.cpp used the GGUF's built-in template; vLLM used a locally fixed jinja template. Prompt lengths differ by ~50 tokens per rung. The chat template was independently eliminated as a cause earlier in #54521, but it was not held identical across this particular comparison.

**2. Tensor parallelism.** llama.cpp ran single-GPU; vLLM ran `-tp 2`. I cannot close this on my hardware — FP8 is ~193 GiB (96.5 GiB per rank) and NVFP4 is 125.9 GiB, both above one GB10's ~121 GiB, so no vLLM variant of this model runs at `-tp 1` here.

**This is the most useful thing someone else could check:** does the Thai corruption reproduce on a single large-memory GPU at `-tp 1`, and on non-GB10 hardware? That would separate a tensor-parallel bug from something in the `qwen4exp` implementation generally.

### Reproduction

Any Thai generation task shows it; a short factual answer in Thai is enough, and it reproduces from 1720 tokens of prompt upward. Score with a stacked-mark detector (tone+tone, upper+upper, tone-then-vowel adjacency) rather than by eye — but note that detector is a **lower bound**, since it does not catch the substitution errors, which are the majority. Harness and all raw samples available on request.

title: [KV Offload] Scope offload group configs to prefix-cacheable KV cache groups
body:
# [KV Offload] Scope offload group configs to prefix-cacheable KV cache groups

## Purpose

`build_offloading_config` (`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/config.py`) builds an `OffloadingGroupConfig` for **every** `kv_cache_group` and then asserts, for all of them:

```
assert group.tokens_per_block % tokens_per_hash == 0, (
    f"tokens_per_block={group.tokens_per_block} not divisible by "
    f"tokens_per_hash={tokens_per_hash}. "
    f"Hybrid models (e.g. Mamba+Attention) need "
    f"--enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes."
)
```

But `tokens_per_hash` comes from `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`), which derives the hash granularity from **prefix-cacheable groups only** (`hashing_sizes = [... if group.kv_cache_spec.prefix_cacheable]`). The two sides disagree about which groups are in scope, so any hybrid model with a non-prefix-cacheable scratch group (`CircularBufferSpec.prefix_cacheable == False`) whose block size does not divide the cacheable groups' hash granularity crashes at boot the moment the OffloadingConnector is enabled:

```
AssertionError: tokens_per_block=4 not divisible by tokens_per_hash=16. Hybrid models (e.g. Mamba+Attention) need --enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes.
```

Enabling prefix caching does not help — the message's advice cannot be followed, because the scratch group is excluded from hash-size resolution *by design* and its ring capacity is set by compression/lookahead geometry, not by the cache block size.

Where this bites: sparse-MLA hybrids that keep a `CircularBufferSpec` ring of pre-compression keys. We hit it deploying GLM-5.3-Flash (support proposed in #53906) on DGX Spark: per rank the layout is MLA + 4 GDN mamba groups at block size 3584 and an SWA drafter group at 64 (all prefix-cacheable, gcd → `tokens_per_hash = 64`), plus a kpool-tail scratch group at block size 4 → `4 % 64 != 0` → boot crash with any `--kv-transfer-config` offloading setup. Any future DeepSeek-V4-style model with a scratch spec of block size not dividing the cacheable gcd hits the same wall.

## Fix

Scope the offload group list to prefix-cacheable groups — the same scoping commit e126687a (#53896) applied to the fine-grained prefix-cache-hit gate in `HybridKVCacheCoordinator` (our test-only PR #54663 pins that gate). Non-cacheable groups have no valid hash granularity, so they can never be keyed, looked up, stored, or loaded; building offload configs for them was never meaningful.

Mechanically:

- `OffloadingGroupConfig` gains a `group_idx` field holding the original index into `KVCacheConfig.kv_cache_groups`. `build_offloading_config` now emits configs only for prefix-cacheable groups, preserving those indices, and keeps the divisibility assert for them.
- The connector scheduler (`offloading/scheduler.py`) iterates the (now scoped) `kv_group_configs` and pairs them with per-request `group_states` via `group_idx` instead of positional `zip`. `group_states`, `GPULoadStoreSpec.group_sizes`, and `block_indices` stay sized by the **full** KV cache group count (new `SchedulerOffloadConfig.num_kv_cache_groups`), with zero entries for scratch groups — so the worker side (`CanonicalKVCaches.group_data_refs`, `gpu_worker`'s `len(group_sizes) == len(layer_refs_per_group)` invariant) is completely unchanged.
- `supports_partial_tail` additionally requires every KV cache group to be prefix-cacheable, keeping the partial-tail CoW hand-off semantics exactly as narrow as before.
- Net behavior for models without scratch groups: identical — every group is prefix-cacheable, so the scoped list equals the old list, indices included, and the on-disk namespace hash of `FileMapper` is untouched.
- Extension contract: `OffloadingSpec.tokens_per_block` stays aligned with `config.groups` and now covers prefix-cacheable groups only (documented at the attribute; original indices via `group_idx`). No existing backend or persistent fs-tier store can observe an index shift or a namespace change from this: any layout where the scoped list differs from the full list crashed on this very assert at boot, so no offloaded bytes or spec state for such layouts exist anywhere.
- Degenerate case: a config with no prefix-cacheable group at all (not constructible with in-tree models) yields an empty group list — the connector idles with no lookup groups and no keys, and passing the optional `block_size` extra config fails loudly on the reworded "at least one prefix-cacheable KV cache group" assert.

Not a duplicate: `gh pr list`/`gh issue list` sweeps for "offloading prefix_cacheable", "build_offloading_config", "tokens_per_hash divisible", "CircularBufferSpec offload", "offloading connector hybrid assert", "offloading eligible groups" surface no PR or issue addressing this boot assert. #53889 / #50883 touch the same function for DCP block-size scaling (orthogonal); #51886 adds retention to the connector (orthogonal); #54663 is our test-only pin of the e126687a coordinator gate and changes no behavior.

## Test Plan

New tests in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py`, following the file's existing `MagicMock`-config style:

- `test_scratch_group_does_not_crash_config_translation` — hybrid `KVCacheConfig` (full-attention 16 + `CircularBufferSpec` block 4 + mamba-align 16) previously tripped the assert; now translates, with `group_idx == [0, 2]` and `tokens_per_hash == 16`.
- `test_scratch_group_gets_no_offload_keys` — `SchedulerOffloadConfig.from_spec` spans only groups {0, 2} while `num_kv_cache_groups == 3`; `supports_partial_tail` is off; `OffloadingConnectorScheduler` boots and `_lookup_groups == (0, 2)`; `RequestOffloadState.update_offload_keys` emits keys whose embedded group indices are exactly {0, 2} and the scratch group's state holds none.
- `test_scratch_group_gets_no_load_slots` — `update_state_after_alloc` emits full-length `GPULoadStoreSpec.group_sizes`/`block_indices` (`[2, 0, 2]` / `[0, 0, 0]`, matching the worker's per-group layout) with the scratch entry zero, and no load key or destination block is drawn from the scratch group.
- `test_prefix_cacheable_misaligned_group_still_asserts` — a mamba group outside "align" mode backs the hash size off to the LCM, and the assert still fires for prefix-cacheable groups.

Constructor updates for the new field in `tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py`, `tests/v1/kv_offload/test_file_mapper.py`, and eligible-aware boot checks in the connector test harness (`utils.py`).

Environment: macOS arm64, Python 3.13, torch 2.13 CPU wheel, source tree on `PYTHONPATH` (no build). The repo root `tests/conftest.py` segfaults on macOS while importing multimodal assets, so runs use `--noconftest` (plus `-p tests.v1.kv_connector.unit.offloading_connector.conftest` where the `request_runner` fixture is needed).

```
$ python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py --noconftest -q
47 passed, 15 warnings in 2.84s

$ python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py --noconftest -q -k "scratch_group or misaligned"
4 passed, 43 deselected, 15 warnings in 2.83s

$ python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py tests/v1/kv_offload/test_file_mapper.py --noconftest -q
55 passed, 1 warning in 2.29s

$ python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ --noconftest -p tests.v1.kv_connector.unit.offloading_connector.conftest -q
82 failed, 234 passed, 2 skipped in 29.32s

$ python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/ --noconftest -q
33 failed, 472 passed, 21 skipped, 1 warning, 36 errors in 10.44s
```

The failures in the two directory-wide runs are pre-existing on this platform, not caused by this PR: the same commands on unmodified `origin/main` (4707679) produce the **byte-identical** sorted `FAILED`/`ERROR` sets (82 and 33+36 respectively; verified with `diff`; the passed counts differ only by this PR's 4 new tests). They are macOS/CPU environment limitations — `VllmConfig` rejects `disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager=False` on this platform, which every `RequestRunner`-based test needs, plus CUDA-dependent `kv_offload/cpu` worker tests.

Mutation check — reverting the `vllm/` changes while keeping the tests reproduces the original crash:

```
$ git stash push vllm/ && python -m pytest ... -k "scratch_group or misaligned"
E  AssertionError: tokens_per_block=4 not divisible by tokens_per_hash=16. Hybrid models (e.g. Mamba+Attention) need --enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes.
2 failed, 1 passed, 43 deselected
```

Lint: `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on all changed files; `uvx pre-commit run --files <changed files>` (repo hook config incl. mypy-3.10, typos, SPDX) exits 0.

## Related

- e126687a / #53896 — scoped the fine-grained-hit gate and `attention_groups` to `prefix_cacheable` groups; this PR applies the same predicate to the offloading boundary.
- #54663 — our test-only PR pinning that coordinator gate against scratch-group regressions.
- #54661 — RFC: per-group prefix-cache retention (the hybrid-offloading context this feeds into).
- #53906 — GLM-5.3-Flash support; with the OffloadingConnector enabled that model boots into this assert today.
- #53889, #50883 — open PRs to the same function for DCP scaling of uniform groups; no overlap with this scoping.
- #51886 — offloading-connector retention (not merged; unaffected).

title: [RFC]: The dynamic-SD K decision is a batch-keyed array index — agreeing on its shape before more signals arrive
body:
### Motivation.

On current `main` (`504bb8b0c3`) the dynamic-SD K decision is one array index:

```python
# vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:1321-1324
if self.dynamic_sd_lookup is not None and len(num_scheduled_tokens) > 0:
    num_spec_tokens_to_schedule = self.dynamic_sd_lookup[
        len(num_scheduled_tokens)
    ]
```

The key is batch size, and that choice is fixed in four places, not one:

- `validate_and_normalize_dynamic_sd_schedule` unpacks entries as
  `(range_start, range_end, num_speculative_tokens)` (`dynamic/utils.py:37`)
- `build_dynamic_sd_schedule_lookup` returns `list[int]`, a dense
  `batch_size -> K` table (`dynamic/utils.py:77-81`)
- the scheduler indexes it by `len(num_scheduled_tokens)` (`sched/scheduler.py:1322`)
- since #50488, two capture-planning sites read the same dense table
  (`worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py:219`, `config/vllm.py:2067`)

The decision site is not short of information — `schedule()` has the request set
in hand, so per-request `num_computed_tokens`, acceptance history and queue
depth are all in scope. They are simply not read. Whatever a proposal wants K to
depend on, it currently has to widen that tuple everywhere, or bypass the
schedule entirely.

**Six different signals are being proposed for this one decision right now.**
Batch size is what ships. Beyond it:

| signal | where |
|---|---|
| context length | #48944 (mine), widening the tuple to `(bs, ctx) -> K` |
| token entropy | #54082, gating K between 0 and K at runtime |
| marginal gain | LibraSpec, [2608.08721](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08721) |
| expert activation cost | EcoSpec, [2607.12696](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12696) |
| step-wise efficiency (entropy-controlled length) | SparseSpec-L, [2607.27735](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27735) |
| learned verification payoff | Hybrid Verified Decoding, [2606.01019](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.01019) |

Two of those papers converge on the same criterion. SparseSpec-L states it
directly: *"extending the speculation horizon can reduce rather than improve
speedup when the marginal acceptance probability falls below the relative
drafting cost."*

I am not asking for any of them to be adopted. I am asking whether the K
decision should keep being a batch-keyed array index, given that the next six
proposals all need it not to be.

> **Update, 2026-09-07 — prior art I should have cited, and a seventh signal.**
>
> **#38038** (`Dynamic SD scheduler decides`, draft, opened 2026-03-24) already
> answers the question this RFC asks, and I did not find it before posting. It
> adds `vllm/v1/spec_decode/dynamic/manager.py` —
> `DynamicSpeculativeDecodingManager`, which picks K by maximizing
> `goodput = acceptance_length / ITL` over a profiled `batch_stats[bs][K] -> ITL`
> table, refreshes its per-position acceptance rates from live
> `SpecDecodingStats` after a warmup period, and interpolates between measured
> batch sizes and K values. It is a policy object, not an array index, and it is
> the most developed K controller in the tree.
>
> It is also keyed on batch size alone: `step(batch_size) -> int`, and the
> companion `generate_config.py` sweeps `(batch_size, K)` on a fixed dataset to
> produce `{batch_size: {num_drafts: median_itl_ms}}`. ITL is context-dependent,
> so in that design context is a constant of the profiling run rather than an
> input to the policy.
>
> That is the sharpest form of what this RFC is asking about, and it points the
> question at the maintainers more than at me: the one component here that was
> built as a policy rather than a table still cannot express a context-dependent
> K, and it has been dormant since 2026-05-07. Whether that is the intended
> destination for this decision is exactly what I do not know.
>
> Separately, a seventh signal has since been proposed and implemented:
> **#54801** adds `num_speculative_tokens_per_seq_len` as a second table
> consulted only when the batch-size table is unset, prompted by **#54691**,
> which reports speculation becoming a net loss at 185k context and states that
> no per-sequence-length hook exists today. I have commented there rather than
> restate it here. That is two new entries to the table above in the six days
> since this was opened, which is the part I would ask maintainers to weigh.

### Evidence I can offer, with its limits.

I ran the (batch, ctx) case, so the numbers below are about that one signal.
Full provenance, including what I have withdrawn, is in a
[ledger](https://github.com/seongyun1104/depthchart/blob/931ff25/EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md);
the per-cell working is in a
[companion note](https://github.com/seongyun1104/depthchart/blob/931ff25/POLICY_INTERFACE.md).

**1. The win localises to a single cell.** Position-balanced 2 trials, cache
wiped per launch, cold-start burn, 3 warm-up discarded + 3 measured per cell,
c=256, per-arm stdev at most 1.72 %, Gemma-4-31B-it-QAT-FP8 with its assistant
drafter on one H100 NVL. A batch-only schedule `[[1,64,3],[65,128,1],[129,512,0]]`
against a (bs, ctx) schedule that differs from it in exactly one cell — at
bs ≥ 129 and ctx ≥ 769, K=3 instead of K=0:

| ctx | batch-only | (bs, ctx) | ratio |
|---:|---:|---:|:-:|
| 400 | 1875.6 | 1890.7 | 1.01× |
| 900 | 1453.5 | 1874.6 | 1.29× |
| 1900 | 1416.6 | 1848.2 | 1.30× |
| 4000 | 1232.8 | 1680.4 | 1.36× |

The ctx=400 tie is the design working: there both schedules select K=0. The
mechanism is narrow and worth stating plainly — **at high batch a batch-only
schedule has to turn speculation off, and context is what tells you when to turn
it back on.**

The distinct-K set is `{0, 1, 3}` for both schedules, so this costs no extra
CUDA graphs; graphs are keyed on K, and the K values are the same ones.

**2. A cost model over the same interface gets that cell wrong.** I also have a
producer that derives the schedule from a stated cost model rather than typing
it — `K* = argmax_K E_accept(K) / (F(ctx) + K·M(bs))`, the same marginal-utility
shape LibraSpec and SparseSpec-L arrive at. Run with the coefficients it ships,
sweeping only the acceptance prior across 0.35–0.75 (the campaign observed
44–47 % in the K=3 tier), it selects **K=0 at the high-batch tier at every
context**. It reproduces the batch-only schedule and would not have found the
cell worth 29–36 %.

That gap closes under recalibration — the per-context coefficient has to be
roughly an order of magnitude larger relative to the per-batch one — not under a
change of functional form. I am reporting it because it is the honest state of
that producer: a stated model, uncalibrated, currently disagreeing with my own
measurement.

**3. What I have not established.** One model pair, one hardware configuration,
one concurrency, four context points, one differing cell. I have not calibrated
the cost model on hardware. I have not attributed the DSD baseline tax to its
terms — the 2×2 design for that is written and unrun. And the sharpness of the K
optimum at low batch did not clear its own pre-registered bar (#48627, and see
the ledger); the result above is at c=256, which is a different regime.

### Proposed Change.

**None yet — this asks for a decision, not a design.** I have a stake here
(#48944 is the ctx-axis version) and I would rather the shape be agreed before
more signals arrive than argue for mine.

The question is where the K decision should live:

1. **Keep it batch-keyed** and let each new signal negotiate its own widening.
   Predictable, and the dense array stays trivially cheap. #50488 has just made
   this the assumption in two more places, so this is the status quo by default
   rather than by decision.
2. **Let the schedule declare its own key set**, so `(bs, ctx)` and any later
   key are the same kind of object to the consumers. This is what #48944 does
   for one extra key; generalising it is a small change to the validator, the
   lookup and the three read sites.
3. **Separate the decision from the schedule**, so that a table, a cost model,
   or a runtime controller are interchangeable producers of K. Two producers
   already exist behind one schedule in my branch, which is the minimum evidence
   for this being more than speculative generality — but two is also the
   minimum, and I would not argue for it on that basis alone.

What I think matters more than which option: **nothing in the engine currently
measures the quantity these policies need.** Acceptance is exported in aggregate,
but per-`(batch bucket, ctx bucket, K)` draft and verify latency, first-rejection
position, committed tokens per verification, and K-keyed graph hit/miss are not.
My cost model missed the cell above because its coefficients were guesses; there
is no way to stop them being guesses from inside vLLM today. If only one thing
comes out of this thread, that telemetry is the one I would pick, and it is
independent of which option above wins.

I have opened #54748 for the smallest piece of it, so this is not a request for
someone else to do the work: steps the schedule sends to K=0 build no
`SpecDecodingStats` at all, so a schedule that has correctly stopped speculating
under load is indistinguishable from speculative decoding not running. That PR
adds a step counter keyed on the selected K and is deliberately independent of
everything proposed here.

### Feedback Period.

No deadline. I will not open a PR against any of the three options without
agreement here first.

### Any Other Things.

Related: RFC #48627 (the ctx axis specifically, with its evidence section
corrected on 2026-09-01), PR #48944, #54082, #49986, #49548, #48494.

Prior art on the ctx dependence itself: MagicDec
([blog](https://infini-ai-lab.github.io/MagicDec-part1/), paper
[2408.11049](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11049)) proposes choosing speculation
amount as a function of sequence length; TurboSpec/SmartSpec
([2406.14066](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.14066)) is the batch-adaptive
predecessor of the schedule API this RFC is about.



> **Update, 2026-09-13 — this RFC left out the controller that actually shipped, and with it in view the question gets sharper.**
>
> My 2026-09-07 update said of #38038 that *"whether that is the intended destination for
> this decision is exactly what I do not know."* It is answerable, and I should have
> answered it here rather than leaving it open: the destination was **#47808**
> (`[Spec Decode] DSpark confidence-scheduled verification`, merged 2026-08-12), which
> added `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/adaptive_verification.py`. RFC #48627 cites it;
> this RFC does not, which makes the Motivation section above read as though the dense
> `batch_size -> K` array were the only controller in the tree. It is not, and the
> omission is mine.
>
> **#38038 and #47808 are the same author's two answers to this RFC's question.** Both are
> @LucasWilkinson's. Both choose a speculation budget by maximizing goodput. Both price
> context once, before serving, and then hold it fixed.
>
> | | #38038 (open, draft, dormant since 2026-05-07) | #47808 (merged 2026-08-12) |
> |---|---|---|
> | objective | `acceptance_length / ITL` | estimated accepted tokens / cost |
> | cost table keyed on | `batch_stats[bs][K] -> ITL` | `num_reqs`, `num_target_tokens` |
> | context | constant of the profiling run | constant of the profiling run |
>
> For #47808 that is visible in three places. The budget is a goodput argmax
> (`adaptive_verification.py:342`):
>
> ```python
> draft_budget = int(np.argmax(num_tokens_to_estimated_accepted_tokens / costs))
> ```
>
> `costs` is assembled from two profiled curves, neither of which carries a context axis —
> `set_initial_cost_curves` builds `draft_curve` keyed on `s.num_reqs` and `verify_curve`
> keyed on `s.num_target_tokens`:
>
> ```python
>         costs = (
>             draft_cost_ms[len(req_ids)]
>             + verify_cost_ms[
>                 num_non_draft_tokens_total : num_non_draft_tokens_total
>                 + max_draft_budget
>                 + 1
>             ]
>         )
> ```
>
> And context enters exactly once, in `batches_to_profile`, held fixed across every sample:
>
> ```python
>                 yield {
>                     "num_tokens": num_tokens,
>                     "context_len": envs.VLLM_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT_LEN,
>                 }
> ```
>
> That env var defaults to 8192. Its comment in `envs.py` states the consequence directly:
> *"Raise it for long-context deployments, where step cost is dominated by attention over
> a much larger KV cache than the default assumes."* The feature documentation says the
> same thing to operators: *"Deployments serving much longer contexts may want to raise it
> so the profiled step reads a more realistic amount of cache."*
>
> So context is not absent from the shipped controller. It is a **deployment-wide scalar
> set before serving**, not an input the policy reads per step — which is the distinction
> this RFC exists to ask about, and I had been asking it against the weaker example.
>
> To be precise about scope, since it would be easy to overstate: adaptive verification
> does not choose K. Drafting still happens at the scheduled length; it chooses how much
> of the already-drafted block to verify, scoring every (request, position) slot by
> survival probability and admitting the best until the budget is spent. So the array
> index above is still the K decision. But "should a table, a cost model, or a runtime
> controller produce the budget" is not an open question in the way I framed it — a cost
> model shipped in August, and 41 open PRs reference it today.
>
> **The question I would actually ask, now:** the person who owns this decision has
> implemented it twice, three months apart, in two subsystems, and both times context was
> priced once at startup rather than read as an input. @LucasWilkinson — is that a
> deliberate boundary?
>
> It is a real question and either answer is useful to me. If it is deliberate, then
> #48944 and #54801 are both arguing against a decision that has already been made twice
> by the person best placed to make it, and the honest thing is for me to say so on my own
> PR. If it is not deliberate, then the natural place for a context term is
> #47808's cost curves rather than the config tuple I have been widening — a smaller and
> better-located change than the one I have been proposing.
>
> I have no measurement on the adaptive-verification path and am not claiming one.
>
> ---
>
> Two smaller corrections while I am here.
>
> **Coordinates in the Motivation section have drifted.** Refreshed against `main`
> (`fa1b3b1922`): the scheduler index is now `sched/scheduler.py:1393-1397` (was
> `:1321-1324`); the capture-planning reads are `worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py:246` (was
> `:219`) and `config/vllm.py:2282` (was `:2067`). `dynamic/utils.py:37` and `:77-81` are
> unchanged, and the quoted block itself is unchanged.
>
> **One piece of external evidence has arrived.** In #54691, @hongboshi1234 measured a
> break-even acceptance surface on B300 / TP8 / DCP-8 with Kimi-K3 and a DFlash drafter —
> different vendor, model family and drafter from mine — by forcing every draft to be
> rejected and comparing per-token latency against no speculation. For any achievable
> accept length in (1.91, 3.51), the resulting pays / does-not-pay region cannot be
> produced by a context rule and a batch rule consulted separately: (2k, B=8) pays, so
> neither rule fires there; (32k, B=8) does not pay, so the context rule must fire at 32k;
> but then (32k, B=1) would be switched off, and it pays. My own result has the opposite
> sign — speculation switched back *on* at high batch when context is long — and the same
> non-separable shape. Two measurements is not many, but they are independent, and the
> second was not looking for this. I checked their proposed *mechanism* and it does not
> hold, which I have said in that thread; the surface stands, the explanation for its
> magnitude is open.


> **Update, 2026-09-20 — walking back one phrase, and a constraint that applies to either answer.**
>
> No answer yet on the question above, which is a fair outcome for a question nobody asked
> for. Two things are worth putting in the record regardless of who decides, because both
> narrow the decision rather than argue for a side.
>
> **First, a correction to my own 2026-09-13 update.** I wrote that a context term in
> #47808's cost curves would be *"a smaller and better-located change"* than widening the
> config tuple. I had not checked that, and having checked it, "better-located" holds but
> **"smaller" does not**. `self.cost_tables` is a pair of 1-D `np.ndarray`
> (`adaptive_verification.py:151`), built by `build_cost_tables_from_curves` (`:81-129`),
> which stitches three regimes together: a step function below the cudagraph capture limit
> where execution pads to the next captured size, linear interpolation above it where
> nothing pads, and linear extrapolation past the last profiled point. A context axis means
> reproducing all three per context slice, and the cudagraph discontinuity is a function of
> token count rather than context, so the axes do not separate cleanly. Profiling would
> also multiply: `batches_to_profile` currently yields
> `(capture_sizes + tail_sizes) × _PROFILE_REPLAYS`, with context pinned to one env value.
>
> **Second, the part that matters more, because it is not a preference.** Wherever the
> context term lives, the same question has to be answered, and I had not noticed that it
> is invariant to the choice.
>
> `get_num_tokens` computes one cost vector for the whole batch:
>
> ```python
>         draft_cost_ms, verify_cost_ms = self.cost_tables
>         costs = (
>             draft_cost_ms[len(req_ids)]
>             + verify_cost_ms[num_non_draft_tokens_total : ...]
>         )
> ```
>
> But a batch holds requests at many different context lengths. Indexing a context-keyed
> cost table requires collapsing them to a single number — and that is exactly the question
> benchislett put to me on #48944 on 2026-07-21:
>
> > *"It's not clear to me what is the right way to aggregate sequence length across a
> > batch. I feel like mean or max … makes more sense than median"*
>
> which #48944 currently exposes as `ctx_agg: Literal["median", "mean", "max"]`.
>
> So the aggregation question is **not** an artifact of the schedule-table design I have
> been proposing. It is a property of putting context into a per-batch budget decision at
> all, and it lands on the shipped controller identically. Whoever decides where the
> context term belongs — including deciding that it belongs nowhere — is deciding this too.
>
> I am noting it rather than answering it. My own answer to benchislett did not hold up:
> I retracted the benchmark evidence for the `mean` default on 2026-09-10 on #48944, because
> two of the four scenarios I had cited turned out to be controls. The knob names a real
> decision; the measurement I offered for its default does not survive, and I would not want
> that distinction lost if someone picks this up.
>
> **Third, a correction I owe on the telemetry ask above.** The Proposed Change section
> says *"nothing in the engine currently measures the quantity these policies need"* and
> picks that telemetry as the one thing worth taking from this thread. Half of that is
> wrong, and I should not have written it without looking harder.
>
> #50919 (`[MRV2] Worker-Level Timings`, open since 2026-08-03, +929/-7) exports exactly
> the latencies I said were missing:
>
> ```
> vllm:worker_spec_decode_proposer_time_seconds   labels: phase, num_requests
> vllm:worker_model_execute_time_seconds          labels: phase, num_model_tokens
> vllm:worker_step_time_seconds                   labels: phase, num_model_tokens
> ```
>
> So draft time and verify time are measured. What survives, and is sharper than what I
> originally wrote, is the **keying**. `WorkerTimingStats` carries `iteration_index`,
> `phase`, `num_model_tokens`, `num_requests`, and the prefill/decode token and request
> splits. It carries no KV context length and no selected K, and the `num_*_tokens` fields
> are query tokens for the step rather than cache depth.
>
> Those are the same two keys as the cost curves in #47808: `draft_curve` keyed on
> `s.num_reqs`, `verify_curve` on `s.num_target_tokens`. And #50919's own stated purpose
> is *"establish reliable statistics for introspective profiling-based tuning such as
> adaptive verification"* — so the instrument is being built to tune the policy, and the
> two share a key set that excludes context.
>
> That is the thing I would now put in place of my original ask. A profiling-driven policy
> cannot discover a dependence on an axis its instrumentation does not record. If context
> is deliberately out of scope for this decision, then this is all consistent and I should
> stop. If it is not deliberate, the cheapest place to find out is a context bucket on the
> proposer timing, long before anything needs to change in a schedule or a config tuple.
>
> I am not raising this on #50919 itself. It is a draft, and I have an open PR that
> benchislett holds review authority over, so a request there for the axis I happen to be
> arguing for would read as exactly what it would be.
>
> **Fourth, something merged after I drafted the rest of this, which changes the scope of
> the question rather than my answer to it.**
>
> #52228 (`[Model Runner V2] Acceptance estimation for adaptive verification`) merged on
> 2026-09-14 as `3bb0a03f35`. Two things about it are worth recording here.
>
> It removed the gate confining adaptive verification to DSpark. `SpeculativeConfig` used
> to raise `"Adaptive verification only supported with DSpark"`, and `DSparkSpeculator`
> additionally required a checkpoint with a trained confidence head. The new
> `OnlineAcceptanceEstimator` predicts per-position acceptance from draft logits that any
> drafter already materializes, so the trained head became an optimization rather than a
> precondition. The controller this thread has been asking about is therefore no longer a
> DSpark feature; on main it is the general adaptive-verification path.
>
> And it makes the shape of the decision visible in a way it was not before, because the
> two sides of the ratio in `get_num_tokens` are now keyed differently from each other.
>
> The benefit side is per-slot. `adaptive_verification.py:314, 326-328`:
>
> ```python
>         scores = np.sort(survival_probability[valid])[::-1]
>         ...
>         num_tokens_to_estimated_accepted_tokens = np.concatenate(
>             ([num_sampling_requests], num_sampling_requests + np.cumsum(scores))
>         )
> ```
>
> `survival_probability` is each request's own running product of per-position
> confidences, so the b-th admitted draft slot contributes `scores[b-1]` expected accepted
> tokens and that quantity belongs to an identifiable request.
>
> The cost side is not. Its marginal term is
> `verify_cost_ms[T+b] - verify_cost_ms[T+b-1]`, a function of the batch's total token
> count, identical no matter which request the slot belongs to. So the descending sort is
> the right admission order exactly when every draft slot costs the same to verify, which
> is what a table keyed on `s.num_target_tokens` encodes.
>
> This refines what I wrote above rather than repeating it. I said the batch-to-scalar
> aggregation question is invariant to where the context term lives. That still holds for
> a **batch-keyed** cost table, which is what both #48944 and #47808 have. What #52228
> shows is that the aggregation is forced by the table's keying and not by pricing context
> as such — because the benefit side prices per slot and never needs a batch reduction at
> all. I had been treating the aggregation as intrinsic. It is not; it is a consequence of
> the shape I picked, and of the shape the shipped cost table picked.
>
> One detail I want to state plainly because it removes the most reasonable objection.
> Per-request KV depth is not unavailable at this decision — it is already read there, at `:322-325`, above the cost expression at `:329`:
>
> ```python
>         num_sampling_requests = np.count_nonzero(
>             self.req_states.num_computed_tokens_np[slots] + num_non_draft_tokens
>             >= self.req_states.prefill_len.np[slots]
>         )
> ```
>
> `num_computed_tokens_np[slots]` is gathered for exactly the requests being priced, used
> to count how many have finished prefill, and not consulted again. So "context is not
> modelled in the cost table" is not a statement about what the scheduler can see.
>
> There is also a timing asymmetry now. The acceptance coefficients refit online every
> 100 steps for the life of the process (`acceptance_estimator.py:330`). The cost curves
> are fitted once, during startup capture — `set_initial_cost_curves` has a single caller,
> `model_runner.py:1044` — at one context length taken from
> `VLLM_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT_LEN`, whose own comment in `envs.py` reads:
>
> > Raise it for long-context deployments, where step cost is dominated by attention over
> > a much larger KV cache than the default assumes.
>
> I am quoting that because it states the dependence better than I have been stating it,
> and because it shows the current answer is not that context does not matter — it is that
> context is an operator-set constant. That is a coherent position. It is the position I
> am asking whether anyone intends.
>
> To be careful about what I am not claiming: the acceptance estimator is **not** context-
> blind. Its feature is computed from the drafter's forward pass over the real prefix, and
> the code says so — *"It scores the draft distribution, not the token drawn from it, so
> it is a function of the prefix alone."* Context reaches the benefit side implicitly,
> through the drafter's own confidence. What is pooled is the fit: one global slope, with
> intercepts keyed on draft position only. Whether that pooling holds across context
> regimes is a question I can state but have not measured, and I would rather leave it
> stated than dress it up.
>
> One note on that pooling, since it stopped being only my reading of the code. #57533
> was opened on 2026-09-18 against the estimator, from a different direction: request-
> specific sampling transforms are applied on the target but not on the draft, so
> accept/reject labels from those requests were being folded into worker-wide coefficients
> that then size verification for unrelated later requests. That is not my question and it
> does not answer it — it concerns which observations are admissible, not which regimes a
> single fit is expected to span. I raise it only because it establishes that the fit being
> shared across heterogeneous requests is load-bearing rather than incidental, which
> otherwise I would be asserting on my own.
>
> Absent a decision here I am going to go and measure the boundary rather than keep arguing
> its shape, and I will report what comes back whichever way it falls. This RFC does not
> need a reply for that to happen.

title: [Bug]: On ROCm, DCP and non-FP8 KV dtypes are unreachable, but the errors suggest fixes that don't exist there
body:
### Your current environment

8x AMD MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, vLLM with AITER. Model: GLM-5.3 (`glm_moe_dsa` → `deepseek_v32` → on ROCm the generic `deepseek_v2.GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), TP4, MXFP4 experts + FP8 attention, `fp8_e4m3` KV cache.

### Describe the bug

Two capabilities that would raise KV-cache capacity are reachable in the CLI but cannot work on ROCm, and the error messages point users toward a fix that does not exist on this platform.

**1. DCP: the error suggests switching backends, but no ROCm backend qualifies.**

`v1/worker/cp_utils.py:47`:

```
AssertionError: Decode Context Parallelism (DCP) requires attention implementations
to return the softmax LSE during decode, but ... does not.
Try a different backend by setting --attention-backend or disable DCP.
```

Counting `need_to_return_lse_for_decode` across all 22 files in `v1/attention/backends/mla/`:

| backend | LSE occurrences | ROCm/AITER/HIP mentions |
|---|---:|---:|
| `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse` | **0** | 53 |
| `rocm_aiter_mla` | **0** | 99 |
| `aiter_triton_mla` | **0** | 7 |
| `cutlass_mla` | 3 | 0 |
| `flashmla_sparse` | 3 | 0 |
| `flashattn_mla` | 2 | 0 |
| `flashinfer_mla_sparse` | 2 | 1 |
| `flashinfer_mla`, `flashmla`, `tokenspeed_mla` | 1 | 0 |

Every LSE-capable MLA backend is CUDA-only. And vLLM itself reports at startup:

```
Using ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE backend out of potential backends: ['ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE']
```

There is exactly one candidate on ROCm for this model, and it does not return LSE. So `--attention-backend` cannot resolve the assertion — the suggestion sends users looking for something that isn't there.

Before hitting this, there is a second, separate hurdle worth noting: the model requests `q_replicate=True` through `verify_and_update_config` (visible as `dcp_comm_backend=a2a` instead of the default `ag_rs`), and `mla_attention.py:1096` then raises `NotImplementedError: DCP query replication is not implemented for the aiter ...`. That one **is** avoidable with `VLLM_DCP_Q_REPLICATE=0`, per the comment in `deepseek_v2.py:1049` ("The env var predates the config field and still wins if set explicitly"). The LSE assertion is what remains.

**2. Non-FP8 KV cache dtypes fail with a generic message.**

`CacheDType` in `config/cache.py` lists 18 values. Three tried on this setup, all with the same result:

```
--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla           ValueError: No valid attention backend found for rocm with ...
--kv-cache-dtype int4_per_token_head  ValueError: No valid attention backend found for rocm with ...
--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_k8v4      ValueError: No valid attention backend found for rocm with ...
```

The message names neither which dtypes *are* supported on the platform nor that the limitation is platform-wide rather than model-specific.

### Suggestion

Not asking for the features themselves — this is about discoverability:

1. Make the DCP assertion platform-aware: when no LSE-capable backend exists for the current platform, say so instead of suggesting `--attention-backend`.
2. Have the KV-dtype validation list the dtypes the resolved backend actually accepts.

Both would have saved a couple of hours here, and the information is already available at the point where the errors are raised.

### Scope of what I verified

Verified: the counts above from the source tree, that `VLLM_DCP_Q_REPLICATE=0` clears the first hurdle, and that DCP=2 and DCP=4 both stop at the LSE assertion. Not verified: whether adding LSE to the ROCm backends is straightforward — I did not read the AITER kernels closely enough to judge that.

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Register Quark per-block FP8 scales as weight_scale
body:
## Summary
- Register Quark per-block FP8 linear scales as `weight_scale`, matching what Quark exports, instead of `weight_scale_inv` (DeepSeek-V3 `Fp8LinearMethod` convention).
- Drop the DeepSeek-V4 AMD mapper rewrite of non-expert `.weight_scale` → `.weight_scale_inv`. Loaders already alias to `_inv` only when that parameter is registered (`Fp8LinearMethod` / MXFP4 override).
- Read block scales through `get_fp8_block_weight_scale()` so DSV4 ROCm preshuffle and MLA `wo_a` dequant work with Quark layers.

This is the quant-method fix discussed on #54556 / #52263 / #47972, rather than another model-specific remap.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/quantization/test_quark.py::test_quark_w8a8_fp8_per_block_registers_weight_scale`
- [x] Load `amd/GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4` (or equivalent) without `KeyError` on `.weight_scale` — GSM8K 0.9158, see [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54770#issuecomment-5506943426)
- [x] Load DeepSeek-V4 AMD Quark NVFP4 (`QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock`) and MXFP4 (`Fp8LinearMethod` + `_resolve_param_name`) — NVFP4 verified (GSM8K 0.9507, see [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54770#issuecomment-5506943426)); MXFP4 still pending
- [x] Confirm native DeepSeek `.scale` → `weight_scale_inv` path is unchanged
