title: [Bug]: KDA/gated-delta-rule chunked-scan buffers are outside memory profiling — runtime OOM at large --max-num-batched-tokens
body:
### Summary

The chunked-scan buffers in the gated-delta-rule (KDA) path scale linearly with
`--max-num-batched-tokens`, are allocated transiently inside the forward pass, and are **not
covered by vLLM's startup memory profiling**. The KV cache is therefore sized as if that memory
were free, and above a certain chunk size the engine dies at runtime — mid-request, after having
served traffic.

### Observed

GLM-5.3-Flash (45 layers: 34 KDA linear-attention + 11 sparse MLA), 1× MI350X (gfx950),
ROCm 7.2.3, TP1, MXFP4 weights, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.93`.
16 concurrent requests of ~38k tokens each.

| `--max-num-batched-tokens` | successful | failed | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 192 … 65 536 | 16 / 16 | 0 | stable across 3 runs each |
| **81 920** | **5 / 16** | **11** | engine shut down |
| **131 072** | **4 / 16** | 12 | engine shut down |

```
(Worker) ERROR  File ".../flash_linear_attention/ops/chunk_delta_h.py", line 357,
                  in chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h
(Worker) ERROR    v_new = torch.empty_like(u) if save_new_value else None
(Worker) ERROR  torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.25 GiB.
                  GPU 0 has a total capacity of 287.98 GiB of which 0 [bytes is free]
(APIServer) INFO [shutdown] EngineCore process manager: using 15.0s ROCm cleanup grace
                  after immediate request abort
```

Startup reported no problem — `GPU KV cache size: 6,940,947 tokens` at 81,920, and the memory
profiling line looked healthy.

### Mechanism

`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` allocates two buffers proportional to the token count in the batch:

```python
B, T, Hg, K, V = *k.shape, u.shape[-1]
H  = u.shape[-2]
BT = chunk_size                      # FLA_CHUNK_SIZE = 64, hard-coded in ops/utils.py:31
...
N, NT = len(cu_seqlens) - 1, len(chunk_indices)
h     = k.new_empty(B, NT, H, V, K)          # NT = ceil(T / 64)  -> linear in T
v_new = torch.empty_like(u) if save_new_value else None   # linear in T
```

For this model (`linear_attn_config`: 64 heads, head_dim 128) at T = 81,920 with BT = 64:

```
NT     = 1280
h      = 1280 · 64 · 128 · 128 · 2 B  ≈ 2.5 GiB
v_new  = 81920 · 64 · 128 · 2 B       ≈ 1.25 GiB   <- the allocation that failed
```

That is ~3.75 GiB transient **per KDA layer invocation**, and there are 34 KDA layers per forward
pass. They are freed between layers, so the caching allocator mostly reuses the blocks — but the
peak is real, and it is not what the profiling run measured. Measured peaks from vLLM's own log,
same model, same everything but the chunk size:

```
chunk  8 192:  14.52 GiB peak activation   KV 9,578,037 tokens
chunk 65 536:  22.73 GiB peak activation   KV 7,512,186 tokens
```

The KV pool shrinks ~35 KV-tokens per extra chunk token, linearly, which is the profiler
*partially* accounting for this. But at 131,072 the loss jumps to ~60 KV-tokens per chunk token —
non-linear — and at 81,920 the runtime allocation no longer fits.

### Why it matters beyond this model

The failure mode is the bad one: **it does not fail at startup, it fails under load.** A
configuration passes a smoke test, serves requests, then the engine dies with requests in flight.
And it is silent in the metrics — `vllm bench serve` computes `Total input tokens` over
*successful* requests only, so throughput per second goes **up** as requests die. In my own sweep
81,920 initially looked like the fastest setting (+21 % over baseline) purely because 11 of 16
requests never completed.

Any model with gated-delta-rule / linear-attention layers goes through this path (GLM-5.x hybrid,
Qwen3-Next GDN, and others).

### Suggested directions

1. **Include the KDA path in the memory profiling run** at the configured
   `max_num_batched_tokens`, with a batch composition representative of chunked prefill
   (several sequences, not one), so the peak is measured rather than partly inferred.
2. **Or bound the buffers**: `FLA_CHUNK_SIZE` is a module-level constant
   (`third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/utils.py:31`). Making it configurable would let
   operators trade chunk-scan parallelism for memory — `BT = 128` halves `h`. `BT` is already a
   free `tl.constexpr` in the kernels (the `64` in the block pointers is the head-dim blocking,
   not the time chunk), so this looks mechanically possible, though I have not yet measured
   whether 128 is correct and faster.
3. **Or refuse the configuration at startup** rather than at runtime, if the peak can be
   computed analytically from `max_num_batched_tokens`, the head count and `FLA_CHUNK_SIZE`.

Happy to test a patch on this hardware.

**Unrelated but adjacent, in case it helps someone sizing a config:** the ~11.7 GiB left unused by
`--gpu-memory-utilization 0.93` on a 288 GiB part is *not* free headroom — it is where these
transient allocations land. vLLM's own log suggests `--kv-cache-memory=<the full amount>` to
"fully utilize gpu memory"; taking that suggestion at a large chunk size is what removes the room
this path needs.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Gemma4: parse tool calls whose opener omits the `call:` marker
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #53431.

Gemma 4 sometimes writes a tool call without the documented `call:` marker. When it does, the parser discards the entire span: no tool call, no content, no error and no metric. The reporter measured 386 lost turns over 21 days in production, about 0.4% of tool-calling requests.

`vllm/parser/gemma4.py` defines one route out of `TOOL_PREAMBLE` into `TOOL_NAME` and its literal is `"call:"`. Anything else leaves the FSM parked in `TOOL_PREAMBLE`, and that state has no entry in `content_events`, so `_emit_for_state` returns `[]` for every character until the closing tag. The missing transition is why it breaks. The missing `content_events` entry is why it is silent, and that is the more consequential of the two.

The same shape exists in `qwen3.py`, `deepseek_v32.py`, `deepseek_v4.py`, `minimax_m2.py` and `kimi_k2.py`. No config in the repo maps `TOOL_PREAMBLE` to a content event, so a stuck parse is silent everywhere, not only here.

### Why this does not add a terminal per variant

The issue describes two opener forms. The raw capture in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53431#issuecomment-5401799341), taken by bypassing the parser with `/tokenize` then `/v1/completions` at `skip_special_tokens: false`, contains three opener markers plus a separate variation in the arguments:

| Captured | What varies | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<\|tool_call>call:search_files` | the documented marker | parses today |
| `<\|tool_call>call:terminal(command:` | round bracket arguments | fixed by #53657, merged |
| `<\|tool_call>:search_files{pattern:` | bare colon | this issue |
| `<\|tool_call>- starting-task-overview` | dash | not covered by any open PR |

In this PR we take the following approach: let `TOOL_PREAMBLE` emit the text it is already consuming. `TOOL_PREAMBLE` gains a `content_events` entry, `OPEN_BRACE` and `OPEN_PAREN` gain transitions out of it so the name is bounded by the argument bracket, and a new optional `tool_name_normalizer` on `ParserEngineConfig` lets a grammar strip a marker the lexer did not consume.

Credit where it is due: #53444 by @wuhangxian correctly fixes the bare colon and its tests are sound. This separate approach however addresses other variations as well for Gemma4. 

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_gemma4_tool_parser.py
```

Plus the reproduction script from the issue body, run unmodified.

7 tests added in a new `TestOpenerVariants` class: the bare colon opener non-streaming and streaming, an unmarked opener, the documented opener unchanged, the bare colon with round bracket arguments, an empty tool call yielding nothing, and a colon in plain content that must not start or split a tool call. That last one guards the alternative fix.

## Test Result

```
61 passed
```

The 54 existing tests are unchanged and still pass.

The reproduction from the issue, run unmodified. Before:

```
--- DOCUMENTED  call: ---
  non-streaming  : {'tools_called': True, 'tool_calls': [('get_weather', '{"location": "London"}')], 'content': None}
--- BARE           : ---
  non-streaming  : {'tools_called': False, 'tool_calls': [], 'content': None}
  streaming      : {'tool_calls': [], 'content': ''}
```

After:

```
--- BARE           : ---
  non-streaming  : {'tools_called': True, 'tool_calls': [('get_weather', '{"location": "London"}')], 'content': None}
  streaming      : {'tool_calls': [('get_weather', '{"location": "London"}')], 'content': ''}
```

title: [Spec Decode] Enable fused draft metadata updates for sparse MLA backends under DCP
body:
## 🚀 Description

Fixes #54369 (CUDA side).

On CUDA, the sparse-MLA backends (`FlashMLASparse`, `DeepseekV32Indexer`) never declare
`supports_draft_decode_metadata_update`, so MTP draft decode falls back to rebuilding
attention metadata between every draft step (up to k=7 rebuilds per decode step at k=8,
per #54369). Under DCP, the indexer additionally could not participate at all: rank-local
sequence lengths must be re-derived from the speculator-advanced global lengths inside the
captured fused loop, and that path was not CUDA-graph-capture-safe.

This PR opts the two CUDA sparse backends into the fused framework from #46849:

- **FlashMLA sparse**: no-op update hook — the framework already advances positions,
  `seq_lens` and slot mappings in-graph, and the per-step topk indices are already
  rewritten in-forward on persistent buffers.
- **DSV3.2 indexer**: two-field in-place refresh — localized `decode.seq_lens`
  (recomputed via `get_dcp_local_seq_lens` from the advanced global lens, never an
  increment) and `deep_gemm` `schedule_metadata` (re-run into the same buffer slice; a
  stale captured schedule can deadlock the paged MQA logits kernel).
- **Capture-safety fix** in `get_dcp_local_seq_lens`: the rank offset was constructed as
  a CPU-scalar tensor on the caller's CUDA device, an illegal CPU→CUDA copy during graph
  capture (all TP workers died in `profile_cudagraph_memory`). It is now a Python scalar
  folded into the existing device arithmetic.
- **Eligibility guards**: the `advance_draft_positions=False` path no longer enables
  fused mode without declared backend support (previously a `NotImplementedError` crash
  at first propose); fused + MTP index sharing is rejected at startup for
  `num_mtp_layers > 1` (shared topk buffer aliasing).
- **Default-off opt-in**: `VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_DRAFT_SPARSE_MLA` (with
  `VLLM_DISABLE_FUSED_DRAFT_SPARSE_MLA` override). No env vars set → behavior identical
  to pre-change.

## Known limitations

- Feature is opt-in (default off): on a compute-bound GLM-MTP TP8/DCP4 serving sweep the
  throughput delta was within the ±3.6% run-to-run noise band at concurrency 2–16
  (+12.7% at C1, −12% at saturated C32), so we do not flip the default in this PR.
- FlashInfer sparse variants (sm90/sm120) are audited capture-safe but not enabled here;
  a follow-up can flip them the same way.

## 🧮 Test plan / results

- [x] `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py -q`
  → **38 passed** (12 new: DCP-localized refresh field equality, max-len clamp boundary
  propagation, env-gating matrix, index-sharing toggles, non-advancing fallback,
  capture/replay equality, producer-consumer ordering).
- [x] E2E, GLM-5.3 MTP, TP8 + DCP4, H200: feature enabled → server starts, FULL decode
  CUDA graphs capture cleanly (per-step-rebuild fallback warning gone); greedy
  acceptance counters identical to the pre-change baseline across 200-request runs × 3
  (8977/11319 accepted; one run bit-identical) — no acceptance drift.
- [x] Without the `get_dcp_local_seq_lens` fix, all 8 workers crash in
  `profile_cudagraph_memory` with "Cannot copy between CPU and CUDA tensors during CUDA
  graph capture" — reproduced and fixed.

## Related

- Fixes #54369 (CUDA + DCP side). The ROCm enablement is #52628 — complementary, no
  code overlap (different backends/arch); this PR covers FlashMLA-sparse + DSV3.2
  indexer + DCP-aware refresh, which no open PR addresses (checked before opening).
- Builds on the fused framework from #46849.

---

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (OpenCode / GLM-5.3). Every changed line was
reviewed and all listed tests were run by the submitter.

title: [ROCm] Avoid DSpark placeholder shared vocab allocations
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4 DSpark on ROCm was allocating draft-side placeholder `embed_tokens` and `lm_head` modules even though the AMD DSpark draft model does not own those weights in steady state.

For this model family, `load_dspark_model()` aliases the target model's shared vocab modules into the draft model. That means the placeholder allocations were only transient startup overhead. On the Strix Halo TP=2 bring-up that overhead was large enough to matter: about `0.863 GiB` per placeholder per rank, or about `1.73 GiB` per rank combined.

This also matches an existing DSpark pattern already in tree: `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/dspark_mla.py` <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/dspark_mla.py> sets `has_own_embed_tokens = False` and `has_own_lm_head = False`, keeps `embed_tokens` and `lm_head` as `None`, and relies on target-model aliasing after draft loading.

This PR narrows the fix to the ROCm implementation only:

- change `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/dspark.py`
- keep `embed_tokens` as `None` until `load_dspark_model()` aliases the target module
- keep `lm_head` as `None` until `load_dspark_model()` aliases the target module
- add defensive assertions before those modules are used
- remove now-unused placeholder allocation imports

## Test Plan

Validate this change on a 2-node Strix Halo TP=2 ROCm setup by applying the no-placeholder DSpark behavior and checking the following runtime outcomes:

- repeated DSpark server startup tests after removing the placeholder shared-vocab allocations, using `gpu_memory_utilization` values of `0.30`, `0.34`, `0.38`, `0.42`, `0.46`, `0.50`, `0.60`, `0.70`, `0.80`, `0.90`, `0.93`, `0.95`, `0.97`, and `0.99`
- offline DSpark-vs-baseline TP=2 comparison

## Test Result

On a 2-node Strix Halo TP=2 ROCm setup, applying the no-placeholder DSpark change removed the transient draft-side shared-vocab allocations and improved DSpark startup behavior.

Startup-memory impact:

- removed about `1.73 GiB` transient draft-side startup allocation per rank for the shared vocab placeholders combined; this savings comes from eliminating two fixed-size placeholder modules, so it is the same regardless of which `gpu_memory_utilization` setting was used in the startup tests
- after the no-placeholder patch, the old immediate DSpark startup-memory failure mode no longer reproduced in the startup sweep

Offline TP=2 DSpark benchmark summary (E2E latency per request):

| Input -> Output | Baseline E2E latency | DSpark E2E latency | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `1024 -> 128` | `178.63s` | `44.39s` | `~4.0x` |
| `4096 -> 256` | `608.98s` | `85.91s` | `~7.1x` |
| `8192 -> 256` | `375.22s` | `86.00s` | `~4.4x` |

---

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results

title: [Bugfix][Speculative Decoding] Fix Gemma4 MTP hidden-state buffer sizing
body:
Size the spec-decode hidden-state buffer by the target model's backbone_hidden_size for Gemma4 MTP. The Gemma4 assistant drafter has a decoder hidden_size smaller than the target's backbone hidden_size and consumes the target's backbone-dim hidden states, so the current draft_model_config.get_hidden_size() undersizes the buffer and engine initialization fails during profile_run/dummy_run with:

`RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (2048x6400 and 10752x1024)`

Mirrors the existing DeepSeek-V4 hc_mult special-case. Guarded with hasattr so it is a no-op for all non-Gemma4 models.

title: [Bug]: KV offloading impossible for GLM-5.3 (DSA indexer): tail_cache block_size=4 fails the hash-alignment assertion, --mamba-cache-mode align does not reach it
body:
### Summary

KV offloading (`OffloadingConnector`, and by extension LMCache) cannot be enabled for
GLM-5.3-Flash because one of its KV-cache groups — the sparse-MLA indexer's **`tail_cache`** —
has `block_size=4` and cannot be aligned to the prefix-hash granularity. The assertion in
`offloading/config.py:55` rejects the whole configuration, and `--mamba-cache-mode align` does
not help because it does not reach this group.

The error message points the operator at `--enable-prefix-caching`, which is a dead end: prefix
caching is on by default and enabling it explicitly changes nothing.

### Reproduction

1× MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, vLLM `glm-release`, GLM-5.3-Flash (MXFP4), TP1,
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`,
`--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
"kv_connector_extra_config":{"spec_name":"CPUOffloadingSpec","cpu_bytes_to_use":214748364800}}'`

```
AssertionError: tokens_per_block=4 not divisible by tokens_per_hash=8704.
  Hybrid models (e.g. Mamba+Attention) need --enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes.
```

Instrumenting `build_offloading_config` to print every group:

```
[GROUPS] tokens_per_hash=8704
[GROUPS]   UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs block_size=8704 -> tokens_per_block=8704  layers=24  first=...layers.3.self_attn.indexer.k_cache
[GROUPS]   UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs block_size=4    -> tokens_per_block=4     layers=12  first=...layers.3.self_attn.indexer.tail_cache
[GROUPS]   MambaSpec               block_size=8704 -> tokens_per_block=8704  layers=12  first=...layers.0.self_attn
[GROUPS]   MambaSpec               block_size=8704 -> tokens_per_block=8704  layers=11  first=...layers.1.self_attn
[GROUPS]   MambaSpec               block_size=8704 -> tokens_per_block=8704  layers=11  first=...layers.2.self_attn
```

Every group aligns to 8704 except `indexer.tail_cache`.

### Why `--mamba-cache-mode align` does not fix it

It does exactly what it promises, verified by instrumenting
`Platform._align_hybrid_block_size`:

```
[ALIGN] called. mamba_cache_mode='align' block_size=8704 mamba_block_size=16
[ALIGN] set: mamba_block_size=8704
```

`mamba_block_size` goes 16 → 8704 and the MambaSpec groups follow. But `tail_cache` is not a
Mamba group — it is a small per-sequence ring buffer holding recent raw K+gate to seed the
indexer's boundary pool (see the comment in `models/glm5next/nvidia/attention.py`: *"prefill
(seeds the boundary pool) and decode (per-step stash); read by the decode kernel to compress the
boundary pool"*). Nothing in the alignment path touches it, and semantically it has no
per-token block size to align.

With and without `--mamba-cache-mode align`, KV pool, timings and prefix-hit counts are
byte-identical (10,360,556 tokens; 2.25 s / 2.26 s / 0.75 s on a repeated 38k prompt), so the
flag is a no-op for this model apart from the mamba block size itself.

### Why this matters

Prefix caching on the GPU works well here — measured with a unique needle mid-context, hits read
from `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` (the API does not report `cached_tokens`):

| context | prefix hits from run 2 | share | needle |
|---|---|---|---|
| 60 000 | 147 968 → 513 536 | | 5/5 verbatim |
| 200 000 | 156 672 | 78 % | 5/5 verbatim |
| 600 000 | 478 720 | 80 % | 5/5 verbatim |

But it is bounded by GPU memory. The capacity argument for offloading is strong on this box:

| tier | capacity | 1M-token contexts |
|---|---|---|
| GPU (8 × 11.2M tokens) | 89.8M | 87 |
| host RAM (2 055 GB free) | 282M | 272 |
| disk (1.4 TB free) | 192M | 185 |

and a miss at 1M context costs **95.0 s** of prefill (measured, TP1) versus roughly 0.3 s to move
6.92 GB back over PCIe. That is the difference offloading would buy on long-context workloads.

### Suggested directions

1. **Let groups whose block size is smaller than `tokens_per_hash` opt out of offloading**
   rather than failing the whole configuration — but only if such a group can be *recomputed*
   rather than restored. For `tail_cache` that needs a maintainer's judgement: if the tail is not
   restored alongside the offloaded KV, the indexer's boundary pool is seeded from stale state
   and attention is silently wrong. **A blanket skip would trade a startup error for silent
   corruption, which is why I did not patch around it locally.**
2. **Fix the error message.** "need --enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes" sends the
   operator down a dead end when prefix caching is already enabled — which is the default. It
   would help to name the offending group and its layers.
3. If `tail_cache` genuinely cannot participate, it would be worth stating in the docs that
   KV offloading (and LMCache) is unavailable for DSA-indexer models, so operators do not spend
   time on it.

Happy to test a patch on this hardware — the setup above reproduces in one start.

title: [Bugfix] FlashInfer: read the KV cache layout from attention metadata
body:
## Purpose

`FlashInferImpl` reads `kv_cache_layout` from a `cache_config` captured at construction. #51718 resolves the layout after model load and records it on the worker's `CacheConfig`. A drafter with a `kv_cache_dtype` override (DFlash, EAGLE, DSpark alike) is built under a `replace()`d config, so its impls hold a copy that never sees the resolution, and the first draft forward during profiling raises "KV cache layout has not been resolved yet".

Carry the layout on `FlashInferMetadata` instead. The builder already reads it from the worker's config to plan the wrappers, and every impl-side read is in `forward()`, so the impl needs no config of its own. FlashInfer is the only backend whose impl read the layout this way.

Replaces the first revision, which propagated the layout into draft config copies from `worker_base.py`. No open PR touches drafter layout resolution.

## Test

`pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py -k "flashinfer or causal_backend_correctness"` - 110 passed on GB10 (sm_121).

2x DGX Spark (GB10), TP=2, FLASHINFER, target Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 with KV `auto`, DFlash2 drafter z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 with `kv_cache_dtype: fp8`, `--linear-backend flashinfer_cutlass`, 8 speculative tokens. `main` at 8f816a3f6 fails in memory profiling with the error above from `FlashInferImpl.kv_cache_layout`. With this commit it reaches READY (34 piecewise + 2 full target graphs, 12 DFlash2 full graphs) and serves the 12-scenario tool-calling suite 12/12 at 154 tok/s mean decode, 72% draft acceptance. A W4A16 drafter does not load on `main` for an unrelated reason (`_build_context_kv_buffers` reads `qkv_proj.weight` after Marlin repacks it), hence the bf16 drafter.

AI assistance was used; every line reviewed and the tests above run by me.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Bake real KV caches into captured fused_norm_rope under PIECEWISE (fixes silent garbage output for DSA models on multi-node TP)
body:
## Purpose

Fixes silent output corruption (garbage / repetition-loop "jibberish") when serving DeepSeek-V3.2-class DSA models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) with **PIECEWISE CUDA graphs** on multi-node TP where the KV-cache write is fused into a *captured* Triton kernel (`_fused_norm_rope_kernel`).

### Root cause

Under MRV2 PIECEWISE capture, the DSA eager-break python (`_sparse_indexer_and_attn` and the captured-region code feeding it) runs with **no attention metadata**: `prepare_inputs_to_capture` builds metadata with `for_capture=False` for PIECEWISE (per the known "brittle assumption" in `cudagraph_utils.py`), and at capture time the layer python observes `forward_context.attn_metadata is None`.

`DeepseekV32Attention.forward()` treated `attn_metadata is None` as "no KV cache" and passed:

- `mla_kv_cache = None` → `fused_norm_rope` substituted a **0-element dummy tensor** with `entry_stride == 0`
- `mla_slot = None` → `slot_mapping = None`

Those arguments were **baked into the captured graph**. At every decode replay the captured `fused_norm_rope` re-executes, but its fused cache-write path (pid 0: indexer-K FP8 cache write, pid 1: MLA latent concat-and-cache) early-returns on the baked dummy/None arguments — so **decode-time KV writes never happen**. Attention then reads latent rows that are stale from prefill (or garbage from a previous request), the indexer MQA logits go wrong, and the corruption cascades (finite-but-weak attention output at the first indexer-leader layer, NaN from the second onward). Prefill and the first generated token are unaffected because chunked prefill runs with real metadata — matching the classic "first token correct, then garbage" signature.

The same `attn_metadata is None` condition can also arise for any DSA model whose attention layer python executes during capture with no metadata, so the fix is written defensively rather than tied to one backend.

### Fix

Split the `attn_metadata is None` case from the `use_pcp` case. When there is no metadata but the layer has bound cache tensors and a persistent per-layer slot-mapping buffer (always true after `initialize_kv_cache`, including during capture):

- bake the **real** `self.kv_cache` / `self.indexer.k_cache.kv_cache` views and `self._k_scale` into the captured kernel launch, and
- keep `mla_slot` pointing at the **persistent slot-mapping buffer**.

Safety during capture: `get_dummy_slot_mappings()` fills the persistent buffer with `PAD_SLOT_ID = -1` and `_fused_norm_rope_kernel` returns early for `slot < 0`, so no cache write happens at capture time (verified: the dummy/capture path never writes any slot). At replay the same persistent buffer carries the real per-step slots, so the baked in-graph kernel writes the correct rows every step. Behavior with metadata present (eager, prefill, FULL-graph capture) is unchanged.

### Results

All serving on a 4-node AGX Thor (SM110) TP=4 cluster, `--attention-backend TRITON_MLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` (canonicalized to `fp8_ds_mla`), `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`, greedy decoding:

| Config | Behavior |
|---|---|
| main (80389cfedd) with PIECEWISE | jibberish: reasoning degenerates to `"1!!!"`-style repetition; ~0.1 tok/s decode |
| main + this fix | coherent: correct reasoning chains, clean final answers, ~10× faster decode |

Prompts validated end-to-end: arithmetic ("What is 2+2?" → `"2 + 2 = 4."` with a full reasoning chain), creative writing, multi-part instructions, and a 2000-token long-form technical generation that stayed coherent through the entire decode (previous corruption typically appeared within the first few decode steps). Runtime device-side probes confirmed that with the fix the per-replay `index_q_fp8`/`mqa_q` tensors are finite with sane magnitudes (previously NaN / 1e37 garbage), the indexer top-k valid count grows correctly with context (48 → 138+), and the first decode replay produces finite MLA outputs.

### Issues this may also address

The "silent corruption under PIECEWISE/FULL_AND_PIECEWISE with no errors" failure mode matches several open reports; those reporters should re-test with this fix:

- #45425 — Silent output corruption: MTP + DCP + FULL_AND_PIECEWISE cudagraphs (GLM-5.1 NVFP4, sparse MLA, fp8_ds_mla)
- #40969 — DeepSeek-V4-Flash hangs/corrupts with FULL_AND_PIECEWISE + chunked prefill on SM 12.x (GB10)
- #43631 — `enforce_eager=False` generates garbage tokens (InternVL2-8B; that one was root-caused separately in #43668, but the symptom class is the same)

(Note: #45425's own mechanism analysis points at a different trigger — varlen-decode reclassification under DCP — so this fix may be complementary rather than a complete fix there.)

## Test plan

- [x] 4-node SM110 cluster, GLM-5.2 NVFP4-AQLM-hybrid, TP=4, TRITON_MLA_SPARSE + fp8_ds_mla, PIECEWISE: server starts, greedy Q&A coherent across short/medium/2000-token generations (was: deterministic garbage within the first decode steps)
- [x] Capture-path safety: during capture the persistent slot buffer is `PAD_SLOT_ID=-1` and the kernel early-returns — verified no cache writes occur with dummy/capture inputs, and that capture-time slot values can never exceed the allocated cache blocks (dummy mappings are all `-1`; real slots come from the shared block pool, `block_id < num_gpu_blocks`)
- [x] Metadata-present paths (eager prefill, decode eager breaks, FULL capture) unchanged
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on the touched file

## AI assistance

This change was developed with the assistance of an AI coding agent (Hermes - using GLM-5.3-flash). The submitting author has reviewed all changed lines, ran the validation above on the target hardware, and understands the root cause end-to-end.

🤖 **Generated with AI assistance** — see the statement above.

<details>
<summary>Additional diagnostics that isolated the root cause (for reviewers)</summary>

- Device-side captures (copy kernels *inside* the captured region, so they hold replay-time data) showed `q_c` / `index_q_fp8` / `mqa_q` at the second indexer-leader layer were NaN or 1e37-magnitude garbage on most decode replays while the residual stream stayed finite — the signature of consumed buffers that their producer failed to rewrite.
- The MQA-logits/topk path itself is correct: the shared top-k buffer holds valid, context-growing indices every replay.
- A standalone capture+replay harness of the fused_norm_rope → fused_q chain reproduced 1e37 garbage deterministically when an out-of-bounds slot was fed by the harness; that OOB hole is real but **not** the server trigger (server slot mappings are always in-bounds or `PAD_SLOT_ID=-1`), so a separate defensive bounds-guard commit will follow.

</details>

title: DP engine startup stuck >50 min in MoE triton JIT warmup (MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModular) vs ~3 min single-node
body:
# Bug Report: vLLM 0.28 — DP engine startup stuck >50 min in MoE triton JIT warmup (`MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModular`)

## Describe the bug

With `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (MoE backend resolves to `DEEPGEMM_MXFP4`), launching with data parallelism (`--data-parallel-size 2`, TP=8 per node across 2 nodes) selects **`MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModular`** for the MoE prepare/finalize kernel. After weight loading completes (~13 s), all 16 workers sit at 100% GPU in a triton JIT compile loop and the engine never becomes ready — not within the default 600 s `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S`, nor within a raised 7200 s window (observed >50 min without completing).

The identical model + flags on a **single node** (TP=8) selects **`MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPModular`** and is ready in ~3 minutes.

## To Reproduce

1. **Single node (works, ~3 min to ready):**
```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --moe-backend auto --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
```
Log: `Using MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPModular` → engine ready ~3 min.

2. **Two nodes DP (hangs in warmup):** node 1 adds:
```bash
  --data-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size-local 1 \
  --data-parallel-address <node1_ip> --data-parallel-rpc-port 13345
```
node 2 same command plus `--headless --data-parallel-start-rank 1`.

Log: `Using MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModular` → weights load in 13 s → then all workers loop at 100% GPU. `py-spy dump` on any worker shows the same stack, cycling through shapes:
```
count_expert_num_tokens (vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/utils.py:106)
deepgemm_moe_permute      (vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/deep_gemm_utils.py:529)
apply                     (vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/deep_gemm_moe.py:579)
_fused_experts            (vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:1342)
...
_init_handles             (triton/compiler/compiler.py:469)   ← per-shape first-call JIT compile
```

3. Neither `--kernel_config.enable_jit_warmup False` nor `--enforce-eager` skips this warmup path — the warmup forward passes still compile the NaiveDPEP triton kernels.

## Expected behavior

- DP-mode startup warmup bounded and/or cached like the single-node path
- `enable_jit_warmup=False` should skip this loop (currently ignored for it)
- Ideally the DPEP module reuses the NoDPEP triton kernels/cache keys, or shares the triton cache

## Actual behavior

- Warmup compile loop >50 min at 100% GPU on every worker; engine killed by engine-ready timeout
- The triton cache built by the single-node path (~34 MB) is not reused by the NaiveDPEP kernel variants (different kernel signatures → full cold compile)

## Additional context

- **Per-GPU weight memory differs between the two paths for the same model/flags:** `Model loading took 13.09 GiB` (DP / NaiveDPEP) vs `21.3 GiB` (single node / NoDPEP) — suggests a different expert layout beyond just the prepare kernels, worth a look
- Module selection lines (same vLLM install):
  - DP: `INFO [mxfp4.py:1843] Using MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModular`
  - single: `INFO [mxfp4.py:1843] Using MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPModular`
- Speculative decoding (dspark, 7 tokens) was enabled in all runs above
- Same behavior with graphs enabled and with `--enforce-eager`

## Environment details

- vLLM 0.28.0 (pip venv), flashinfer 0.6.18
- 2 nodes × 8× NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (SM 12.0), driver 580.105.08
- Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8, CUDA 13.x
- Direct-attached 2×200G Ethernet (no switch); NCCL over RoCE — not relevant to the bug (no cross-node collectives in DP mode)

title: [Qwen3.8-Flash-Next] Improve QSA sparse GQA for prefill and short-ctx decode
body:
## Purpose

QSA sparse attention read topk indices from `[num_tokens, 2048+3]` buffer, where each token can attend up to 2048+3 past KV tokens. This number can be smaller when a new token's position is less than 2048, hence the indices buffer might be padded with -1. This is true for fresh prefill (causal attention) requests and short-context decode.

In the current code, sparse GQA always attend to the full 2048+3 indices (with appropriate masking of course). This is wasteful when there is a lot of padding like mentioned above. To fix this issue, we insert a variable `valid_counts`, representing the total number of valid, non-padding indices, at the **end** of the `logical_indices` table. Why this design?
- The valid counts always go together with the indices table. This can be seen as an encoding of variable length sequences with stable buffer size.
- This also works nicely with topk indices reuse in MTP `compact_topk_indices` -> we don't need to carry another tensor and ensure it's in-sync with the indices table

The key change in the kernel is basically this (notice the loop's upper bound is tightened by `valid_counts`)

```python
valid_count = tl.load(indices_ptr + row * stride_indices_row + TOPK)
tile_end = tl.minimum(NUM_TILES, tl.cdiv(tl.minimum(valid_count, TOPK), BLOCK_N))
for tile in range(split_id, tile_end, NUM_SPLITS):
   ...
```

Other features included in this PR
- Add proper warmup logic
- Add a tuned config for prefill case

title: [KV Connector][Mooncake] Support hybrid DCP direct transfer
body:
## Summary

- add Mooncake direct-PD transfer for hybrid MLA + Mamba models when the decode side uses native DCP
- scatter producer attention tokens into decoder DCP pages while preserving TP-sharded recurrent state and PP-aware rank mapping
- carry physical HMA/Mamba page-layout metadata and repack non-speculative producer state into the DSpark decoder layout
- preserve target-model cache-group semantics when speculative cache groups are also registered
- zero partially populated destination pages before async load so recycled block tails cannot leak stale KV data
- safely disable DSpark per request when Mooncake loaded the target prefix but no draft-model context was transferred

## PR scope

This is a clean, single-commit PR based directly on the current upstream `main`. It does **not** contain commits from #54347, #50514, or #54416.

The implementation intentionally validates the first hybrid-DCP topology:

- producer DCP = 1
- producer and consumer TP sizes match
- consumer DCP = consumer TP
- hybrid MLA + Mamba cache layout
- PP-aware direct transfer

## End-to-end validation

The full Kimi K3 deployment used for validation separately stacked #54347, #50514, and #54416 because those changes enable PP+SP and PP+DSpark; they are test-environment dependencies, not part of this PR.

Validated topology:

- P: TP8 + PP2 + EP + MegaMoE + SP
- D: TP8 + PP2 + DCP8 + DSpark
- 1P1D across nodes 1/2 and 14/21
- official nightly based on `55aa766dc`

Observed results:

- cold request plus five recycled-page requests
- all runs returned first token ID 1008 (`The`)
- observed first-token latency: 592-705 ms
- each request continued for 16 tokens without transfer or decode errors
- pre-commit ruff, formatting, and mypy checks passed
- targeted unit coverage is included; the full pytest suite was not run

## Known limitation

Mooncake currently transfers only the target-model cache. A producer without DSpark cannot provide draft-model context, so requests that load an external prefix take the safe non-speculative path on D. Target-model decoding and cache reuse remain enabled. Transferring draft context can be addressed separately.

## Review focus

This is a draft for early review. The main areas worth scrutinizing are the DCP token mapping, HMA physical-page layout metadata, Mamba state repacking, and the scheduler zeroing contract for partially loaded pages.

title: [Kernel][Spec Decode] Add hybrid NVFP4 LM-head sampling support
body:
## Purpose

  This Draft PR adds an opt-in hybrid NVFP4 LM-head sampling path for NVFP4-compatible Qwen
  models on SM120 GPUs.

  The implementation:

  - Uses NVFP4 coarse projection followed by BF16 candidate refinement.
  - Supports greedy, compact top-k, and Qwen MTP speculative sampling paths.
  - Adds compact rejection sampling and reduced TP synchronization.
  - Adds deterministic candidate selection and request-keyed RNG handling.
  - Adds presence-penalty handling and fail-closed fallback for unsupported penalty modes.
  - Adds compatibility gates for LoRA, added vocabulary, adaptive verification, incompatible
    `head_dtype`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, and `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS`.
  - Refreshes or releases derived NVFP4 state when model weights or runtime configuration change.
  - Adds bounded hybrid warmup and auxiliary-memory limits.
  - Adds unit tests, kernel tests, runner tests, rejection-sampler tests, and custom-op checks.

  The fast path is intentionally approximate: NVFP4 coarse candidate pruning can exclude the
  exact full-vocabulary winner. Unsupported or correctness-sensitive configurations fall back to
  the standard full-logits sampler.

  ## Test Plan

  For end-to-end validation:

  1. Start baseline and hybrid services with identical V2 Model Runner, TP=2, FlashInfer,
     Qwen MTP2, CUDA Graph, and cache settings. The only difference in hybrid enablement is
     `VLLM_HYBRID_NVFP4_LM_HEAD=0/1`. Both services explicitly pass
     `--no-enable-prefix-caching` to prevent cross-scenario KV reuse.

  2. Run fixed-seed random workloads with 3000 input tokens, 1000 output tokens, eight warmup
     requests, and 32 measured requests at BS=1 and BS=16.

  3. Test greedy, top-k (k=20), presence-penalty, and unsupported frequency-penalty requests.

  4. Compare TTFT, TPOT, ITL, and output throughput.

  ## Test Result

  ### Unit and Kernel Validation

  - CPU targeted suite: 56 passed, 8 skipped, 1 deselected.
  - SM120 CUDA targeted suite: 64 passed, 1 deselected.
  - Full CUDA suite including the FP32/NaN regression: 65 passed.
  - Custom-op and CPU sampler fallback regression: 3 passed.
  - Rejection-sampler chunking/layout regression: 7 passed.
  - compileall and git diff --check: passed.
  - Ruff was unavailable in the current environment.
  - Full repository mypy was not completed because the required Pydantic plugin dependency
    was unavailable.

  ### SM120 Service Validation

  - Qwen3.5-27B TP=2/MTP2 loaded and executed hybrid greedy and compact top-k paths.
  - Qwen3.5-35B TP=2/MTP2 loaded and executed hybrid greedy and compact top-k paths.
  - Unsupported frequency-penalty requests correctly used the standard full-logits path.
  - CUDA Graph capture and replay completed without CUDA, NCCL, or illegal-memory-access errors.
  - A short fixed prompt produced identical output and 16-token logprobs between baseline and hybrid.
  - Observed auxiliary hybrid memory was approximately 341 MiB per GPU for the 27B model and
    136 MiB per GPU for the 35B model.

title: [CI][ROCm] Prefetch safetensors weights in AMD CI
body:
- Use vLLM's existing safetensors prefetch strategy for the 8-GPU ROCm Llama 4 Maverick evaluation instead of forcing lazy loading.
- Add an optional safetensors loading strategy to the AMD weight-loading model lists and pass it through the existing test runner.
- Enable prefetching for the slow multishard Mixtral case and the AMD large-model weight-loading group.

AMD CI loads these large checkpoints from shared storage, where lazy mmap access can turn weight loading into many slow reads. vLLM already has a prefetch strategy that reads shards concurrently into the page cache, so this change opts in only the affected AMD jobs and leaves common model lists unchanged.

Local benchmark: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark, 155.43 GiB across 48 shards, TP4/EP4 on 4 x gfx950 GPUs with a cold page cache.

| Measurement | `lazy` before | `prefetch` after | Improvement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Checkpoint loading | 73.71 s | 26.17 s | 2.82x faster |
| End-to-end cold startup | 135.57 s | 76.62 s | 1.77x faster |

AI assistance was used for research, implementation, benchmarking, testing, and PR drafting. The submitter reviewed the resulting changes and benchmark results.

title: [Bug]: Request-level tools render ahead of the system prompt in DeepSeek-V3.
body:
### Your current environment

**Not applicable — this is a tokenizer encoding bug, not a runtime/GPU issue. The bug reproduces by calling `deepseek_v32_encoding.encode_messages` directly with the checkpoint's own test files**


### 🐛 Describe the bug

When a request carries tools, `deepseek_v32.py` inserts a new empty system message to hold them instead of attaching them to the existing system message. This causes the `## Tools` block to render **before** the system prompt, diverging
  from DeepSeek's reference encoder at token 1.

  **Affected file:** `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v32.py`

  Root cause:

  messages.insert(0, {"role": "system"})
  messages[0]["tools"] = tools

  This creates a new empty system message. The empty message renders as "" + "\n\n" + the tools block, so tools end up ahead of the system prompt.

  DeepSeek's reference encoder attaches tools to the existing leading message:

  messages[0]["tools"] = test_dict["tools"]

  Golden output confirms tools should come after the system prompt:

  <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>You are a helpful Assistant.

  ## Tools

  Reproduction:

  from vllm.tokenizers.deepseek_v32 import get_deepseek_v32_tokenizer
  from transformers import AutoTokenizer

  tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2")
  ds_tokenizer = get_deepseek_v32_tokenizer(tokenizer)

  messages = [{"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful Assistant."}]
  tools = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "test", "description": "test"}}]

  result = ds_tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
  {"messages": messages, "tools": tools, "add_generation_prompt": True}
  )

  # On main: tools render BEFORE the system prompt

  # Expected: system prompt first, then tools (matches DeepSeek's golden output)


  **Impact:**
  - Every DeepSeek-V3.2 request that passes tools gets a wrong prompt layout
  - Prefix caches built against the wrong token sequence
  - May affect model quality since the prompt doesn't match training

  **Related:**
  - PR #52255 fixes the identical bug in `deepseek_v4.py` but does not touch `deepseek_v32.py`
  - This is the V3.2 companion fix****

body:
### Your current environment

.


### 🐛 Describe the bug



### Description

After running successfully for several days, our vLLM cluster crashed with `EngineDeadError` due to a KV cache block not found during offloading load operation.

### Environment

- **Model**: DeepSeek-V4-Pro (custom, ~671B MoE)

title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3 accuracy collapses on ROCm (GSM8K 91.6% -> 14.9%) after #53155 forces MRV1
body:
## Your current environment

- vLLM: bisected across `44fe2a392..40824284b`, also reproduced on `main` @ `1b4b2a18b`
- Platform: ROCm, AMD MI350/MI355 (`gfx950`), TP=4
- Model: [`amd/GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`](https://huggingface.co/amd/GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8) (`architectures: ["GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM"]`)
- Env: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0`

## Describe the bug

`ce2e343be` ("[ROCm] Keep GLM-5.2 on MRV1 and disable default breakable cudagraph", #53155)
added `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` to `ROCM_DEFAULT_MRV1_ARCHITECTURES`:

```python
ROCM_DEFAULT_MRV1_ARCHITECTURES = frozenset(
    {"DeepseekV32ForCausalLM", "DeepseekV4ForCausalLM", "GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM"}
)
```

Since GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 share the same architecture string, this also switches
**GLM-5.3** from MRV2 to MRV1 on ROCm. MRV1 produces corrupted generations for this
architecture, and GSM8K 5-shot accuracy drops from **91.6% to 14.9%**.

The offending entry is still present on `main` (`1b4b2a18b`).

## Reproduction

```bash
MODEL=amd/GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8

VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0 \
python -m lm_eval --model vllm \
  --model_args "pretrained=$MODEL,tensor_parallel_size=4,dtype=auto,\
quantization=quark,max_model_len=32768,trust_remote_code=True,max_num_seqs=32" \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --batch_size auto
```

Adding `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` to the exact same command restores accuracy.

## Results

| Build | flexible-extract | strict-match | Runner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `40824284b` (default) | 0.1486 | 0.1418 | MRV1 |
| `40824284b` + `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` | **0.9158** | **0.9143** | MRV2 |
| `44fe2a392` (before the regression) | 0.9158 | 0.9151 | MRV2 |
| model card reference | 0.9128 | - | - |

The model card's own reproduction instructions pin the image to
`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-44fe2a392b71d52a8d72faf2f8278834379482c9` with
#54556 applied, i.e. exactly the third row above — so the reference 91.28 was
measured on a vLLM revision predating this regression, which landed 68 commits
later (`ce2e343be`; the last good commit is its parent `dc9114b20`).

All runs carry that same Quark FP8 block-scale naming fix (#54556 / #54770),
which this checkpoint needs in order to load at all; it is independent of the
regression and is present in both the good and the bad rows above.

The runner in use is visible in the logs: bad runs load via
`gpu_model_runner.py`, good runs via `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`.

## Bisect

91 commits in `44fe2a392..40824284b`, full GSM8K run at each probe:

| # | Commit | PR | flexible-extract | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 64 | `188716ace` | #53190 | 0.9098 | good |
| 65 | `e16b5e518` | #50175 | 0.9121 | good |
| 67 | `dc9114b20` | #50622 | 0.9083 | good |
| 68 | `ce2e343be` | **#53155** | 0.1638 | **bad** |
| 76 | `d0e695a91` | #53784 | 0.1440 | bad |

67 good / 68 bad are adjacent, so `ce2e343be` is the first bad commit.

## Corrupted output example

GSM8K doc 17, MRV1, `batch_size=1` — the generation degenerates into repeated
token garbage:

```
...total weekly pay: $700/week + $450/week = $<<700+450=1150>>1150/week
! = $30*15 hours2*15*15*15*0=<<15*30*15 hours3 30*15 hours/week1=<<302*15*30*30*15*15*15*15*30*151=<<1=<<1=<<1=<<1=7000=<<30*302*15=<<0>>302=9000. week = $<<30*15=450>>450/week
```

## Ruled out

These were each tested and are **not** the cause:

- **Quantization / AITER kernels** — `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0` and
  `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0` were already set in every run above; toggling
  them moves the score by ~1 point at most.
- **Breakable cudagraph** — the same PR also made
  `default_breakable_cudagraph_architectures()` return `frozenset()` on ROCm.
  Accuracy is ~91% both with it enabled (`e16b5e518`, 0.9121) and disabled
  (`40824284b` + MRV2 override, 0.9158), so this half of the PR is orthogonal.
- **CUDA graphs / torch.compile** — on a 20-doc subset, MRV1 scores 0.75 with
  `enforce_eager=True`, the same as with cudagraphs enabled.
- **Batch size** — on the same 20-doc subset, MRV1 scores 0.75 with
  `batch_size=1`, and the corrupted generation quoted above comes from that run.

MRV1 vs MRV2 is the only variable that changes the outcome. Note that the
20-doc subset (0.75) is much less severe than the full 1319-doc run (0.149),
so the degradation appears to grow as the run progresses.

## Related

#53155 belongs to a series of ROCm changes that deliberately pin DSA models to
MRV1 (#52488, #52866 for DeepSeek V4), motivated in part by MRV2 problems on
ROCm such as #52644 (DSv4 accuracy drop with MRV2 + `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` on
gfx950). #54197 separately reports that `GlmMoeDsa` on MRV2 silently falls back
to eager because the model lacks `@support_torch_compile`.

So the MRV1 preference is intentional, and the report above is not an argument
that MRV1 is generally wrong — only that for GLM-5.3 on ROCm it is currently
unusable.

## Suggested fix

The immediate problem is that `ROCM_DEFAULT_MRV1_ARCHITECTURES` keys off the
architecture string, and GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 share `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`
(`model_type: glm_moe_dsa`). The GLM-5.3 checkpoint carries no version field
that would let the two be told apart here, so the MRV1 preference intended for
GLM-5.2 cannot avoid also catching GLM-5.3.

Dropping `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` from the set restores GLM-5.3 and leaves the
breakable-cudagraph default from #53155 untouched; a patch doing that is
attached. If GLM-5.2 genuinely needs MRV1 on ROCm, a discriminator finer than
the architecture string would be needed instead.

Either way the underlying MRV1 correctness bug for this architecture is worth
fixing separately, since the corruption above is a silent wrong-output failure.

---

A patch implementing the suggested fix is up as a PR against `main`; branch: `jimmy-adams:fix-rocm-glm-dsa-mrv1-accuracy`.

title: [CI] Bump CUTLASS DSL to 4.7
body:
## Summary

- Bump `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]` from 4.6.2 to 4.7.
- flashinfer KDA prefill kernel and some future kernels need 4.7


## Duplicate-work check

Searched open vLLM PRs for `nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7`, `CUTLASS DSL 4.7`, `CuTeDSL 4.7`, and the pinned QuACK commit. No open PR implements this upgrade.

The closest results are not duplicates:

- #41834 is a broad DeepSeek V4 SM12x enablement branch and currently uses CUTLASS DSL 4.6.0.
- #47571 and #41609 only raise older QuACK minimum versions to 0.4.1.

## Tests

Dependency resolution:

```bash
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto --dry-run
```

Resolved 196 packages successfully.

FA4 coverage:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_mixed_causal_attn.py::test_flash_attn4_mixed_causal \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mm_prefix.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_quant_output.py \
  tests/models/inkling/test_fa4_rel_attention.py \
  tests/models/inkling/test_fa4_warmup.py
```

Result: `104 passed, 5 skipped`. Four skips require Hopper SM90, while the test host is GB200 SM100; the remaining head-dim 512 case is unsupported on Blackwell. The FA4 selector plus head-dim 256 coverage also passed separately: `34 passed, 44 deselected`, including a final `8 passed` head-dim 256 rerun with the pinned QuACK commit.

Additional CuTeDSL coverage:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_prefill_cutedsl.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_cutedsl_moe.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_cutedsl_layout.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_cutedsl_nvfp4_moe.py \
  tests/kernels/test_bf16x3_router_gemm_cutedsl.py \
  tests/kernels/test_flashinfer_bf16_gemm.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_flashinfer_nvfp4_scaled_mm.py::test_flashinfer_cutedsl_nvfp4_w4a16_linear \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py::test_decode_index_score_cutedsl_correctness \
  tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py::test_cutedsl_full_cache_store \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py::test_cutedsl_dcp_candidate_pack_and_select_matches_reference \
  tests/jit_monitor/test_hooks.py -k 'cutedsl or cute_dsl'
```

Result: `53 passed, 4 failed, 18 deselected`. The four failures are the gated activation variants in `test_flashinfer_cutedsl_nvfp4_moe.py`. They fail before CuTeDSL compilation in FlashInfer validation with `A K=256` versus `B K=128`. The existing test creates gated W1 rows and then unconditionally replaces the parametrized activation with `RELU2_NO_MUL`, producing the shape mismatch.

Other native CuTeDSL kernel coverage:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/kernels/test_ll_bf16_gemm.py \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_rope_quant.py
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k cute
```

Results: `176 passed`; and `2 passed, 138 skipped, 250 deselected`. The skinny GEMM kernel cases require SM90 or SM103, while the test host is SM100.

Lint:

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files requirements/cuda.txt
```

All applicable hooks passed.

## Model evaluation

Not applicable. This is a dependency-only compatibility upgrade and does not change model output or serving logic. Kernel correctness coverage is reported above.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to update the dependency pins, investigate QuACK compatibility, and execute and analyze the tests. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the reported test results before this PR was opened.

title: [Attention] Portable Triton sparse-MLA fallback for SM12x (consumer Blackwell)
body:
## Purpose

DSA models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.2) currently have **no working sparse-attention backend on
consumer Blackwell** (SM12x: RTX 5090, GB10): the native FlashMLA sparse kernels
(`vllm._flashmla_C`) only build for sm90/sm100, and the sole SM12x option,
`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`, livelocks under sustained load — GPUs pin at 100 % with zero
output until the NCCL watchdog kills the server. Fixes #51921 (on SM12x).

This makes the `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` backend work on SM12x by binding portable **Triton**
implementations of `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` / `flash_mla_with_kvcache` when the native extension
can't serve the device. The kernels are from #49026 (@marksunner, validated there on
sm_121/GB10) — this PR is that work rebased onto current main as a first-class code path
instead of that PR's runtime monkeypatch, with its model-side diffs dropped (main already has
that content). Supersedes/continues #49026 — happy to hand back or co-drive.

## Scope

This path covers **DeepSeek-geometry sparse MLA** — `qk_rope_head_dim = 64`, i.e. the
512 NoPE + 64 RoPE = **576** head layout: DeepSeek-V3.2/V4.1 and GLM-5.2. The Triton kernels
and the `fp8_ds_mla` 656-byte per-token entry are built around that 576 layout
(`get_supported_head_sizes() == [576]`).

**Not covered:** NoPE MLA models (`qk_rope_head_dim = 0`, `head_size = 512`) such as
GLM-5.3-Flash. Those are correctly rejected at the head-size gate and need the `pe_dim != 64`
work in #55277 / #53969 *in addition to* this PR. Thanks to @haqishen for confirming this
boundary on real SM120 hardware (see comments).

Changes:
- `ops/flashmla.py`: `_use_triton_sparse_mla()` (auto on SM12x; `VLLM_TRITON_MLA_SPARSE`
  forces on/off) selects the Triton binding; `is_flashmla_sparse_supported()` reports True
  there; `get_mla_metadata` returns `(None, None)` (the Triton kernels self-schedule).
- New files: `sm12x_sparse_mla_attn.py`, `sparse_mla_kernels.py`, `sparse_mla_env.py`,
  `ops/deepseek_v4_ops/*` — kernels + helpers from #49026, unchanged.
- `flashmla_sparse.py`: capability 12 allowed on the Triton path; %16 fp8-decode head padding
  there (64-head models at TP=8 have 8 heads/rank — 64-padding wastes 87 % of attention
  compute); b12x fused fast path with clean fallback.
- `sparse_attn_indexer.py`: DeepGEMM not hard-required on the Triton path (fallbacks exist).
- `envs.py`: `VLLM_TRITON_MLA_SPARSE*` registered.
- **Recommended runtime knob:** set `VLLM_SPARSE_MLA_SPLITK=32` on SM12x — it enables the
  split-K decode path and is a large single-stream decode win (see Test Result). The backend
  now logs a one-time hint when it is left unset.

**All changes are no-ops on sm90/sm100** unless `VLLM_TRITON_MLA_SPARSE=1` is set explicitly.

## Test Plan

End-to-end serving on 24× RTX 5090 (3 hosts, TP=8 × PP=3), GLM-5.2-NVFP4,
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, driven by `vllm bench serve`
(1K-in/256-out latency cell @ c1, then a c16 throughput cell; repeated full passes incl.
10K-token prompts). This load reproduces the #51921 livelock on stock v0.26.0/v0.28.0 within
minutes, so it discriminates cleanly between the two paths.

## Test Result

| | stock (`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`) | this PR's path (`FLASHMLA_SPARSE` + Triton) |
|---|---|---|
| latency cell (c1, n=8) | first request spins **660 s** (GPUs 100 %, zero output), engine dead before the next cell | **8/8** — TTFT 5.3 s, **TPOT 41 ms** |
| throughput cell (c16) | never reached | **64/64** in 136 s — 120 tok/s output |
| output quality | n/a | coherent, correct stop reasons, `glm47` reasoning/tool parsers intact |

Startup shows the Triton binding + backend selection on all 24 workers; KV cache
(`fp8_ds_mla`, 656 B/token layout) sizes as expected.

Note: the runtime validation above ran on this exact diff backported onto v0.28.0 (our
production pin). We are set up to re-validate a main build on the same cluster, and happy to
add unit tests in whatever shape maintainers prefer for device-gated kernels.

### Independent validation on 8× RTX PRO 6000 (SM120, GB202-class)

Separately from the 5090 gang, we ran **GLM-5.2 NVFP4** on a single 8× RTX PRO 6000 (96 GB)
node with this PR's path (`--attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla
--reasoning-parser glm47`, `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS`, `VLLM_SPARSE_MLA_SPLITK=32`), TP=8:

| cell (1K in / 256 out) | TP=8 |
|---|---|
| c1 TPOT median | 23.84 ms |
| c1 output tok/s | 36.3 |
| c16 output tok/s | 211.5 |
| KV pool | 480K tok (util 0.90) |

The 433 GB checkpoint fits one node (54.7 GiB weights/GPU at TP=8), serves coherently, and
single-stream decode (23.84 ms) approaches our 24×5090 gang's best (22.8 ms).

**On split-K:** with `VLLM_SPARSE_MLA_SPLITK` unset (the default), c1 TPOT was 44.9 ms;
setting it to 32 dropped it to 23.84 ms — the motivation for the one-time startup hint added
here.

Caveat (same as the 5090 result): this ran as this PR's files overlaid on a v0.28.0 image,
not a clean `main` build — a data point, not CI.

title: [Bug]: Explicit scalar CUDA graph maximum can drop a required uniform-decode shape
body:
### Your current environment

The configuration-level reproducer below does not require a GPU.

- vLLM `main`: `76ba32160a501e5e8aadb5e1820c51c765714220`
- Also observed with vLLM 0.28.0: `2cf0a6915ce544dc493a0990f2ea38d81601128a`
- Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130
- Runtime validation: two NVIDIA DGX Spark systems (GB10), driver 580.173.02,
  CUDA 13.0, Ubuntu 24.04.4 aarch64

### Describe the bug

When `CompilationConfig.max_cudagraph_capture_size` is set explicitly but
`cudagraph_capture_sizes` is left unset, `_set_cudagraph_sizes()` builds the
default stepped grid and silently truncates the scalar maximum to the largest
grid entry.

For static speculative decoding with `max_num_seqs=6` and six speculative
tokens, the widest uniform decode batch is:

```text
6 requests * (1 sampled token + 6 speculative tokens) = 42 tokens
```

Setting `max_cudagraph_capture_size=42` currently produces a capture list that
ends at 40 and changes the resolved maximum to 40. The model-runner-v2 CUDA
graph manager rounds the 40-token candidate to the seven-token query width,
gets 42, then rejects it because 42 exceeds the resolved maximum of 40. The C6
verification step therefore dispatches eager.

#### Minimal reproducer

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

from vllm.config import (
    CompilationConfig,
    CUDAGraphMode,
    ParallelConfig,
    SchedulerConfig,
    VllmConfig,
)

compilation_config = CompilationConfig(
    cudagraph_mode=CUDAGraphMode.FULL_AND_PIECEWISE,
    max_cudagraph_capture_size=42,
)
config = MagicMock(spec=VllmConfig)
config.compilation_config = compilation_config
config.scheduler_config = SchedulerConfig.default_factory(
    max_num_seqs=6,
    max_num_batched_tokens=8192,
)
config.parallel_config = ParallelConfig()
config.model_config = MagicMock(enforce_eager=False)
config.performance_mode = None
config.diffusion_config = None
config.speculative_config = SimpleNamespace(
    num_speculative_tokens=6,
    num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size=None,
    uses_dynamic_speculative_decoding=lambda: False,
)
config.num_speculative_tokens = VllmConfig.num_speculative_tokens.fget(config)
config.uniform_decode_query_len = VllmConfig.uniform_decode_query_len.fget(config)

VllmConfig._set_cudagraph_sizes(config)
print(compilation_config.max_cudagraph_capture_size)
print(compilation_config.cudagraph_capture_sizes)
```

Actual output on current `main`:

```text
WARNING ... Truncating max_cudagraph_capture_size to 40
40
[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40]
```

Expected output:

```text
42
[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 42]
```

The expectation is not that every scalar maximum must necessarily become a
capture size. It is that a schedulable uniform decode shape that fits within an
explicit scalar bound is not discarded merely because it is off the inferred
8/16-token stride. An explicit `cudagraph_capture_sizes` list should remain
authoritative.

### Measured serving impact

We reproduced this with DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision, DSpark static K=6,
`max_num_seqs=6`, and an otherwise matched two-node/two-rank configuration.
Five p256/C6 trials were run in each lane:

| C6 median | Inferred list ending at 40 | Exact 42 included |
|---|---:|---:|
| Decode/request | 30.4 tok/s | 27.0 tok/s |
| Aggregate throughput | 25.3 tok/s | 133.3 tok/s |
| TTFT | 26.016 s | 0.839 s |

Adding the 42-token capture removes the eager verification step, improving
aggregate throughput by 5.27x and reducing TTFT by 96.8%. Startup shape probes
also completed 47/47 in 30 seconds, compared with 85 seconds before the fix.

### Related work and duplicate check

- #50488 added uniform-decode shapes when vLLM computes the default scalar
  ceiling; #54418 subsequently kept those defaults within the platform memory
  ceiling. The explicit scalar branch still does not populate
  `uniform_decode_sizes`.
- Open PR #37865 addresses the same externally visible truncation by appending
  every explicit scalar maximum to the inferred grid. It is currently stale
  and conflicted. A narrower alternative is to append only the widest
  schedulable uniform-decode shape when it fits within the scalar maximum,
  leaving unrelated scalar bounds and explicit capture-size lists unchanged.

Because #37865 overlaps this bug, I am not opening a competing PR without
maintainer/author coordination. I have a rebased two-file patch and regression
test ready if the narrower semantics are preferred.

This investigation and candidate patch used OpenAI Codex assistance. The
reproducer and measurements were run on the systems described above.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and open PRs for
  `max_cudagraph_capture_size`, uniform decode, off-stride capture sizes, and
  speculative CUDA graphs.

title: [DeepSeek-V4][Preview][DO NOT MERGE] Batch-invariant kernels for 0-diff RL
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Preview only — DO NOT MERGE.**
>
> This draft collects the vLLM changes required for end-to-end DeepSeek-V4
> train/rollout alignment. It is intentionally larger than an upstreamable PR.
> After the preview is validated, it will be rebased onto current `main` and
> split by kernel, sparse attention, MoE/DeepEP, and reload support. Those
> focused PRs are the changes intended to merge. The verl production recipe
> will be updated after they land on official vLLM branches.

## Purpose

Make DeepSeek-V4 rollout execution independent of request batching so the same
vLLM kernels can be used by the mLite actor recomputation path and produce
exactly matching probabilities.

Preview source:

- head: `ISEEKYAN/vllm:ds4-v9-rc1`
- revision: `1a6542cdebbaabbf9972c358de8d6baa54e46b0c`
- tree: `df12131335d84e9848e188905449230902eaf7ca`
- fork point used by the image: `7aa248fcfef5ba7a6bfb0ce314e328ce63abb9f9`

Default vLLM behavior is unchanged. The aligned path is enabled only with
`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` and the required native libraries.

### Fused activation and FP8 quantization

`csrc/batch_invariant/` adds a standalone
`fused_silu_mul_per_token_group_quant` operator for contiguous and
expert-masked inputs.

- Fuses SiLU, multiply, and 128-element group quantization with fixed launch
  geometry rather than selecting a path from batch-local M.
- Supports FP32, ceil-UE8M0, and packed UE8M0 scales.
- Uses architecture-specific activation/rounding behavior for Hopper and
  Blackwell.
- Uses 64-bit group and output offsets, including tensors above `2**31`
  elements.
- Is wired into `deep_gemm_moe.py` and `batched_deep_gemm_moe.py`.

In batch-invariant mode, missing kernel support is a hard error rather than a
silent fallback to a numerically different implementation.

### Deterministic sparse top-k

`csrc/ds4_bi_topk_extension.cu` adds `ds4_bi.top_k_per_row_prefill`.

- Selects top-k from a composite score/index key with a stable tie-break.
- Uses the same selector for prefill and batch-invariant decode.
- Canonicalizes selected indices before FlashMLA so reduction order is fixed.
- Keeps persistent row-start buffers for CUDA graph replay.

This removes top-k set/order changes caused by equal scores, request offsets,
or decode-versus-prefill dispatch.

### Sparse MLA and FlashMLA

`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py` and the sparse-attention helpers
add `VLLM_DS4_DECODE_KERNEL=sparse`.

- Decode gathers compressed and sliding-window KV and calls
  `flash_mla_sparse_fwd`, matching the prefill attention path.
- Batch-invariant prefill chunks each request independently instead of using a
  grouped batch-local plan.
- C128 top-k width, gather capacity, and workspaces derive from model capacity,
  not neighboring sequence lengths.
- Graph-safe Triton helpers fill top-k and length buffers without host sync.

This makes sparse index selection, KV gather order, and attention reduction
independent of the other requests in the batch.

### DeepGEMM, MoE, and DeepEP

- `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py` probes and enables the batch-invariant DeepGEMM
  contract, failing closed when the installed fork does not support it.
- MoE backend selection requires a batch-invariant implementation and uses a
  fixed expert capacity instead of `expert_num_tokens.max()`.
- Router gate logits use a common FP32 `torch.mm` path rather than an
  M-dependent low-latency GEMM.
- DeepEP low-latency dispatch is staged at fixed capacity; empty ranks still
  join collectives and FP8 dispatch requests aligned quantization.
- Shared experts launch once across staged dispatch slices.

Together these changes fix route ordering, expert input quantization, grouped
GEMM geometry, and combine order across actor and rollout.

### MHC, CUDA graphs, and weight reload

- Batch-invariant DeepSeek-V4 uses explicit MHC pre/post operations instead of
  the batch-dependent fused path.
- MHC split count is fixed and multi-token inputs are processed in stable
  token order.
- Sparse-attention, top-k, and MHC buffers keep stable addresses across CUDA
  graph capture and replay.
- Layerwise actor-to-rollout reload calls
  `finalize_weights_after_layerwise_reload()` to refresh MHC broadcast weights.
- `attn_sink` loading preserves `-inf` padding through the model weight loader.

### Hopper and Blackwell

- Hopper keeps FP32 block scales and uses the compatible block-scaled
  projection path in batch-invariant mode.
- Blackwell keeps packed UE8M0 scales and the DeepGEMM einsum path.
- Both architectures use their validated SiLU and FP8 packing behavior rather
  than treating SM90 and SM100+ as numerically interchangeable.

## Test Plan

- Run the batch-invariant kernel contract and large-tensor offset tests.
- Run deterministic sparse top-k tie/order tests.
- Run sparse FlashMLA and DeepSeek-V4 sparse decode tests.
- Run batch-invariant DeepGEMM/MoE and router gate tests.
- Run MHC graph/refit and layerwise reload tests.
- Load both custom libraries on x86_64 and arm64 images.
- Run the companion verl `quick_alignment_test`, H100 aligned profile, and
  GB200 aligned profile.

## Test Result

- image digest: `TODO`
- verl recipe PR: `TODO_VERL_PR_URL`
- quick alignment test: `TODO`
- H100 64-GPU aligned run: `TODO`
- GB200 32-GPU aligned run: `TODO`

---

<details>
<summary>Essential PR description checklist</summary>

- [x] Purpose and non-merge preview status are explicit.
- [x] Test plan is listed.
- [ ] Test results are attached.
- [ ] Documentation and split PR ownership are finalized.

</details>

## Acknowledgements

The train/inference alignment strategy and deterministic kernel work are
informed by [THUDM/slime#2262](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/pull/2262)
and its SGLang/DeepGEMM/DeepEP alignment work led by
[@zhuzilin](https://github.com/zhuzilin).

## Contributors

- Yan Bai ([@ISEEKYAN](https://github.com/ISEEKYAN)) maintains the DS4 preview
  integration and the batch-invariant DeepSeek-V4 execution path.
- [@aoshen02](https://github.com/aoshen02) authored
  `36687196d62e0e26d4c29f19d505b1fc4e1df1e8`, which widened fused-SiLU
  group counts and output offsets to 64-bit. The fix came from three failed
  eight-node RL runs with long responses, added a `numel >= 2**31` regression,
  and verified chunked/full bitwise parity on GB200 without measurable
  regression.
- [@andakai](https://github.com/andakai) and
  [@zobinHuang](https://github.com/zobinHuang) optimized the performance of
  the batch-invariant vLLM execution path.

title: [Attention] Add B12X sparse MLA and DSA backends
body:
## Purpose

This PR extends the optional B12X attention backend on NVIDIA SM120 and SM121
GPUs with non-compressed sparse MLA and its DSA indexer. The existing `B12X`
selector chooses dense paged attention or sparse MLA from the model's attention
contract; users do not select separate B12X attention implementations.

The integration:

- Adds B12X sparse-MLA and paged-DSA backend implementations using B12X's
  `Caps -> plan -> bind -> run` APIs and caller-owned workspaces.
- Routes DeepSeek-V3.2-family sparse attention through the NVIDIA model hook,
  which also covers compatible GLM-5.2 and non-Flash GLM-5.3 configurations.
- Emits physical KV-cache slots directly from the DSA indexer.
- Supports decode context parallelism with rank-local selection and the existing
  LSE-based attention reduction, without adding global candidate reranking or
  model-specific DCP optimizations.
- Fuses BF16 absorbed query projection and RoPE assembly directly into the B12X
  query workspace when the selected attention implementation advertises that
  capability.
- Plans against the finalized KV-cache page geometry and warms the decode,
  extend, and indexer signatures needed by CUDA graph execution.

This does not duplicate #54929. That PR adds a portable Triton fallback behind
`FLASHMLA_SPARSE`; this PR integrates the separately packaged B12X sparse-MLA
and DSA implementations behind the existing optional `B12X` backend.

AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used while developing this PR. I reviewed
every changed line and am responsible for understanding and defending the
integration end-to-end.

## Test Plan

Run the focused attention tests against the B12X 1.4.0 API contract. The test
below used an editable checkout of the revision being released as 1.4.0:

```bash
uv run --with pytest --with tblib --no-sync python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_b12x.py -q
```

Run all configured checks over the changed files:

```bash
mapfile -t changed_files < <(git diff --name-only upstream/main...HEAD)
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files "${changed_files[@]}"
git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
```

Serve GLM-5.2-NVFP4 with TP=8 on eight RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs and verify
both DCP=1 and DCP=2. For the performance comparison, keep B12X linear and MoE
backends fixed and change only the attention stack between
`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` and `B12X`.

The pure-prefill workload uses four concurrent requests with 65,536 input
tokens and one output token. The pure-decode workload first primes the prefix
cache, then uses four concurrent requests with a cached 65,536-token context
and 1,024 output tokens. Each result is the mean of two repetitions.

## Test Result

Focused tests on the rebased PR head:

```text
55 passed, 15 warnings in 34.49s
```

All changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, formatting, mypy,
markdownlint, SPDX, forbidden-import, and CUDA API checks. `git diff --check`
and Python compilation/import checks also passed.

GLM-5.2-NVFP4 TP=8/DCP=2 started with the default collective implementation,
warmed the B12X MLA and DSA signatures, and completed `/v1/models` and a
20-token-input/32-token-output request successfully. DCP uses rank-local
physical selection and LSE reduction; no optimized DCP candidate exchange is
included.

End-to-end throughput; higher is better:

| Workload | FlashInfer MLA + stock DSA | B12X MLA + DSA | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Pure prefill | 4,147.89 input tok/s | 4,737.78 input tok/s | +14.22% |
| Cached 64K decode | 184.61 output tok/s | 194.89 output tok/s | +5.57% |

The B12X decode repetitions were 194.60 and 195.18 output tok/s, or
approximately 195 output tok/s. The comparison excludes the experimental CTA
redistribution because its end-to-end effect was within run noise.

---
