title: [Bug]: [Kimi-K3][Hopper] Low-M TP8 KDA projection fails CUTLASS DSL compilation for sm_90a
body:
### Your current environment

## Summary

Kimi-K3 fails to start on H100 when the low-M TP8 KDA projection-overlap path
introduced by #54697 is enabled. During CUDA-graph profiling,
`kda_skinny_gemm.run_n()` fails in the CUTLASS DSL compiler with
`NVVM_ERROR_COMPILATION` for `sm_90a`.

The failure has reproduced in two independent four-node launches. The same
deployment works on an older vLLM revision that predates #54697.

## Environment

- GPUs: 32 x NVIDIA H100 80 GB HBM3
- Topology: 4 nodes, TP8/PP4
- NVIDIA driver: 580.126.20
- CUDA reported by the driver: 13.0
- Model: `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`
- Model dtype/quantization: BF16 activations, MXFP4 weights
- vLLM image revision: `27a94d1ce4e3fc100c4732439ccec10f8246a804`
- vLLM version: `0.28.1rc1.dev337+g27a94d1ce`
- `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]`: 4.6.2, as pinned by this vLLM revision
- CUDA graphs: enabled (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`)
- Tensor parallel size: 8
- Pipeline parallel size: 4
- Maximum model length: 1024
- Maximum batched tokens: 8192
- Maximum sequences: 710
- Attention backend: `FLASHMLA`
- MoE backend: `marlin`
- FlashInfer autotuning: enabled

The local image also contains changes to pipeline-parallel communication, but
none of those changes modifies the Kimi-K3 KDA implementation,
`low_latency_gemm.py`, `kda_skinny_gemm.py`, or the CUTLASS DSL installation.

## Reproduction

The relevant server arguments are equivalent to:

```bash
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 1024 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 710 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --moe-backend marlin \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA \
  --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --language-model-only \
  --async-scheduling \
  --enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

Startup reaches model loading and then fails while profiling CUDA-graph
memory. No inference request is required to trigger the problem.

## Error

```text
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 577, in determine_available_memory
  cudagraph_memory_estimate = self.model_runner.profile_cudagraph_memory()
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 908, in profile_cudagraph_memory
  return _profile_cudagraph_memory(self)
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py", line 812, in profile_cudagraph_memory
  measured = int(runner.capture_model())
...
File "vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/low_latency_gemm.py", line 789,
  in run_kda_projection_overlap
  projected_fab = kda_skinny_gemm.run_n(...)
File "vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/cute_dsl/kda_skinny_gemm.py", line 343,
  in _compile_n
...
cutlass.base_dsl.compiler.CompilerDiagnosticError: error: NVVM backend compilation failed
  error: libNVVM failed while compiling generated device IR.
  note: target architecture: sm_90a
  note: backend log:
        NVVM backend compilation failed
  suggestion: check that CUDA_TOOLKIT_PATH is set correctly and that the CUDA
              toolkit supports target architecture sm_90a
```

The engine subsequently reports:

```text
EngineCore failed to start.
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'NVVM backend compilation failed ...'
```

Later NCCL/TCPStore errors are teardown effects after the worker failure.

## Regression range and suspected change

The working image is based on:

```text
ac7509e2b1db40fec2f03dde1ed4e9dfdc2338c9
```

The failing image is based on:

```text
27a94d1ce4e3fc100c4732439ccec10f8246a804
```

The failing source file and dispatch path were introduced between those
revisions by:

```text
3ba9907a1db20c085be5c2d3cfbbbd6ec4a182dc
[Kimi-K3] Overlap low-M TP8 KDA projections (#54697)
```

`kda_skinny_gemm.py` was introduced by that commit and has not changed between
the failing revision and the current main revision checked during this
investigation. The PR description reports hardware validation on B300/SM100;
this failure occurs on H100/SM90a.

## Expected behavior

Kimi-K3 should start on H100. If the specialized projection kernel cannot be
compiled for SM90a, vLLM should fall back to the previous sequential GEMM path
instead of aborting engine startup.

## Workaround under test

`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` causes `_enable_kda_projection_overlap()` to return
false and therefore avoids registering this specialized warmup. This is only a
diagnostic workaround because batch-invariant mode also changes unrelated
attention and collective paths.

A narrow environment gate or an SM90 capability guard around KDA projection
overlap would provide a safer fallback while the compiler failure is
investigated.

## Questions

1. Is the KDA projection-overlap path from #54697 intended to support
   H100/SM90a, or should it currently be restricted to SM100-class GPUs?
2. Would maintainers prefer an architecture fallback or a dedicated feature
   flag that preserves the prior sequential projection path?
3. Are there additional CUTLASS DSL IR-dump flags or environment details that
   would be useful for diagnosing the libNVVM failure?


### 🐛 Describe the bug

```

  cudagraph_memory_estimate = self.model_runner.profile_cudagraph_memory()
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 908, in profile_cudagraph_memory
  return _profile_cudagraph_memory(self)
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py", line 812, in profile_cudagraph_memory

...

  in run_kda_projection_overlap
  projected_fab = kda_skinny_gemm.run_n(...)
File "vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/cute_dsl/kda_skinny_gemm.py", line 343,
  in _compile_n
...
cutlass.base_dsl.compiler.CompilerDiagnosticError: error: NVVM backend compilation failed
  error: libNVVM failed while compiling generated device IR.
  note: target architecture: sm_90a
  note: backend log:
        NVVM backend compilation failed
  suggestion: check that CUDA_TOOLKIT_PATH is set correctly and that the CUDA
              toolkit supports target architecture sm_90a
```

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Allow num_speculative_tokens to default from draft config for MTP
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55323

When initializing speculative decoding with MTP (or DSpark) where `num_speculative_tokens` is not explicitly supplied by the user, `SpeculativeConfig` is intended to default `num_speculative_tokens` from the draft model config's `n_predict` attribute.

However, several issues previously blocked this path:
1. `SpeculativeConfig.num_speculative_tokens` was type-annotated as `int = Field(default=None, gt=0)`. In Pydantic v2, explicitly passing `num_speculative_tokens=None` triggered a `ValidationError: Input should be a valid integer`.
2. In `SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__`, draft model resolution (`self.model = self.target_model_config.model_weights or self.target_model_config.model`) was guarded by `if self.model is None and self.num_speculative_tokens is not None:`. When `num_speculative_tokens` was `None`, draft model derivation was skipped entirely.
3. In method auto-detection, the MTP check evaluated `if self.num_speculative_tokens > 1:`. When `num_speculative_tokens` was `None`, this raised `TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int'` before reaching where `self.num_speculative_tokens` is populated from `n_predict`.
4. When `num_speculative_tokens` was omitted, the multi-token warning check ran prematurely before `n_predict` defaulting occurred, missing the warning when `n_predict > 1`.
5. DSpark configurations specifying only `block_size` or `dspark_block_size` without an explicit `n_predict` could fail initialization with a missing-count error when `num_speculative_tokens` was omitted.

This PR:
- Changes `num_speculative_tokens` type annotation to `int | None = Field(default=None, gt=0)`.
- Allows draft model derivation when `self.method in ("mtp", "dspark")` even if `num_speculative_tokens` is initially `None`.
- Defers the MTP `num_speculative_tokens > 1` warning until after default token count resolution so omitted values resolving above 1 properly trigger the warning.
- Recognizes `block_size` and `dspark_block_size` as default sources of speculative count in the DSpark path.
- Adds comprehensive docstrings to all touched functions.

## Test Plan

- Added parameterized regression unit tests in `tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py`:
  - `test_mtp_num_speculative_tokens_default_from_n_predict` covering both `model=None` and explicit `model="draft_model"`.
  - `test_mtp_num_speculative_tokens_warning_when_defaulted_above_one` verifying warning emission when omitted tokens default to `n_predict > 1`.
  - `test_dspark_num_speculative_tokens_default_from_block_size` verifying default resolution from `block_size` and `dspark_block_size`.
- Tested with:
  `pytest tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py`
- Formatted and linted via `ruff check` and `ruff format`.

## Test Result

All 10 unit tests in `tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py` pass cleanly.

title: [6/N] HiSparse: support direct GPU landing for P/D transfers
body:
## Why

HiSparse P/D imports always land in the host tier today. That costs a host round trip even when the decoder has room to keep the whole prefix on GPU. This PR lands a NIXL import directly in resident GPU pages when it fits, and falls back to the host tier otherwise.

## Design

- **Landing choice:** `HiSparseCoordinator` tries GPU landing first. If that admission fails, the retry uses the host tier and keeps it. There is no length threshold, and the generic KV cache manager is unaware of the choice.
- **NIXL alias regions:** NIXL registers each source layer's resident pages as a local-only *alias region* of that layer's host source region. Aliases are not advertised in the handshake.
  - A GPU import sends its resident blocks as `ReqMeta.alias_block_ids`. The existing region-mapped pull then writes those regions into their aliases, and the mixed DRAM/VRAM split still applies.
  - A host import is unchanged from `main`.
- **Review follow-up:** this replaces `HiSparseNixlDestination`, which re-implemented NIXL's host registration, descriptor mapping and read submission ([review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55398#pullrequestreview-5190836165)). NIXL no longer has a second host path; the only HiSparse-specific input is the source-to-resident layer map from `vllm/v1/hisparse/layout.py`.
- **Not supported with aliases** (each raises `NotImplementedError`): host staging buffers, Mamba, layer-name routing, kernel block size ≠ logical block size, DCP, and more than one source rank.

## Validation

CPU unit tests (Mac; NIXL suite on H100 because it needs `ray`):
```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py \
  --deselect tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py::test_fewer_blocks_with_hma
```
All pass. `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma[gemma]` hangs on that H100 box on `main` too.
- `test_nixl_hisparse_gpu_import_pulls_into_resident_pages` registers a real worker and checks that a GPU import's NIXL read targets resident-page addresses. It fails if the alias remap is removed.
- Two scheduler tests cover GPU landing (alias IDs past the local prefix) and host fallback (source pages, no alias IDs).

**Tiny-model P/D, 1×H100.** DeepSeek-V3.2 with 8 layers and dummy weights. Prefill and decode share the GPU. Greedy, 48 tokens, prompts of 200–3000 tokens. Compared against a HiSparse-only, non-P/D server.

| Decoder pool | Path taken | Matches non-P/D |
|---|---|---|
| 2000 blocks | 5/5 GPU landing | 5/5 (48/48 tokens) |
| 800 blocks, concurrent | 4 GPU, 1 host fallback | 5/5 (48/48 tokens) |

0 failed NIXL transfers. The path taken was confirmed with a probe on `prepare_gpu_import`.

**GLM-5.3 FP8, 2×8 H200, earlier revision `431cf98763`.** That revision used `HiSparseNixlDestination`.
- Setup: prefill TP8 with no HiSparse; decode TP8 with HiSparse, 384 GiB host pool and 16384 GPU blocks; FP8 KV, eager.
- 8K/32K/60K needle-in-haystack retrieval over P/D: correct.
- `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT` did not reproduce: 0 failed transfers over ~150 requests.

Decode TTFT, median of 18 sequential requests each:

| Prompt | `main` (host) | PR | Path on PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8K | 0.210 s | 0.198 s | GPU |
| 32K | 0.335 s | 0.288 s (−14%) | GPU |
| 60K | 0.490 s | 0.499 s | host fallback (does not fit) |

TPOT is unchanged at ~144 ms.

**Fixed: garbled answers after GPU-landed imports.** That revision garbled two 60K answers deterministically under a fixed request history; `main` was clean.
- Cause: the default eager host mirror only records page write-backs as complete, but rows NIXL writes into resident pages were never mirrored. Those pages were still published as host prefix-cache entries, so a later request with a one-page prefix hit read an unwritten host page.
- Fix: the NIXL scheduler records the pages a GPU import writes, and those pages' write-backs now copy to host (`SparseKVPageTransfer.unmirrored`).
- Minimal repro (fresh decoder): three 32K needles that land on GPU, then the 61,193-token seed-10 60K needle.
- With the fix, the full 77-request history replay passes 77/77, including both previously garbled prompts.
- That replay ran on an equivalent fix that recorded the import from `HiSparseSourceManager`. The pushed version records it from the NIXL scheduler instead, leaving `vllm/v1/core` unchanged for this fix. A GLM rerun of the pushed head is pending.

AI assistance was used; the submitter reviews every changed line.

title: [Hybrid] Block priorities enabling opportunistic APC hits with sparse caching
body:
## Purpose
Recently `prefix_cache_retention_interval` has been introduced (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43447 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45845), affecting hybrid models such as DeepSeekv4, KIMI K3, Qwen 3.5, etc. When  `prefix_cache_retention_interval` is not `None`, cache entries with low matching probabilities are masked, skipped hash assignment, and evicted in FIFO manner rather than LIFO (LRU). Cache hits can only occur then at designated blocks and via specific mechanisms, such as Marconi shared prefix detection (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37898) that provides cache hits on 3rd appearance of shared prefix.

In this PR, we notice that **the masked blocks**:
- **have valid data that could potentially result in APC hits**
- **compute effort has been spent on them**

**Rather than completely discarding them, we enable opportunistic APC hits.** To achieve this the PR: 
- introduces Block priorities (currently NORMAL and LOW), where masked blocks are assigned LOW priority and still considered in the APC matching
- the eviction mechanism extends the free_blocks queue in the following manner:
  `[hash-less blocks | LOW PRIORITY | ... | NORMAL PRIORITY]`
- thus it retains the LIFO logic for normal blocks, and FIFO logic for masked blocks
- but if there is no memory pressure, the LOW priority blocks have a chance to be hit

The core logic is in `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` and `vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py` with around 20 lines of code touched. 

A synthetic test with truncated shared prefixes that simulates:
* 2nd appearance of shared prefix (not captured by Marconi shared prefix detection yet)
* user roll-back

demonstrates valid cache hits for masked blocks and **35% prefill time reduction** for `prefix_cache_retention_interval=0` with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`

AI assistance disclosure: development of the code in this PR (all tests, some parts of core logic) was assisted with AI. 

@tdoublep 

## Test Plan
```
if __name__ == "__main__":
    from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
    from vllm.distributed import cleanup_dist_env_and_memory
    import time, string
    # Should be even more visible for DeepSeekV4 and KIMI K3
    MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B"
    sampling_params = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=1)
    prefix1 = ( # examples/offline_inference/prefix_caching.py
        "You are an expert school principal, skilled in effectively managing "
        "faculty and staff. Draft 10-15 questions for a potential first grade "
        "Head Teacher for my K-12, all-girls', independent school that emphasizes "
        "community, joyful discovery, and life-long learning. The candidate is "
        "coming in for a first-round panel interview for a 8th grade Math "
        "teaching role. They have 5 years of previous teaching experience "
        "as an assistant teacher at a co-ed, public school with experience "
        "in middle school math teaching. ")
    prefix2 = ("Based on these information, fulfill "
                "the following paragraph: ")
    PROMPTS = []
    for i in range(10):
        PROMPTS.append(str(i) + prefix1 * 200 + prefix2)
        # Simulate partial match, e.g.:
        #  - user roll-back in conversation
        #  - 2nd system prompt appearance
        PROMPTS.append(str(i) + prefix1 * 190 + prefix2)

    for RET in [None, 0]:
        engine = LLM(prefix_cache_retention_interval=RET,
            model=MODEL, gpu_memory_utilization=0.4, disable_log_stats=False)
        print(f"Block size: {engine.llm_engine.vllm_config.cache_config.block_size}")
        # Measure:
        start_time = time.time()
        for prompt in PROMPTS:
            outputs = engine.generate(prompt, sampling_params)
            n_prefill = len(outputs[0].prompt_token_ids)
            print(f"Prefill tokens: {n_prefill} | Generated text: {outputs[0].outputs[0].text!r}")
        total_time = time.time() - start_time
        # Summary
        print('Execution with RET:', RET, "took --- %s seconds ---" % total_time)
        for m in engine.llm_engine.get_metrics():
            if 'vllm:prompt_tokens_cached' in m.name:
                print(m.name, m.value)
        del engine
        cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()
```
## Test Result
**Main:**
```
[...]
Execution with RET: None took --- 20.84550404548645 seconds ---
vllm:prompt_tokens_cached 158400
[...]
Execution with RET: 0 took --- 32.47444725036621 seconds ---
vllm:prompt_tokens_cached 0
```
**This PR:**
```
[...]
Execution with RET: None took --- 20.97832942008972 seconds ---
vllm:prompt_tokens_cached 158400
[...]
Execution with RET: 0 took --- 21.07378101348877 seconds ---
vllm:prompt_tokens_cached 158400
```
Executed on 1x A100.

title: [Bugfix] Pass CPU sequence lengths to TRT-LLM ragged prefill
body:
## Purpose

The B200 LM Eval PCP lane fails deterministically for both GLM-5.2 configs when the DeepSeek-v3.2 sparse-MLA prefill path calls FlashInfer's `trtllm_ragged_attention_deepseek`. Without trusted host sequence lengths, FlashInfer derives them from CUDA indptrs and evaluates `.any().item()`, which vLLM correctly rejects as a GPU-to-CPU synchronization.

This change:

- preserves the already-computed CPU query lengths in `MLACommonPrefillMetadata`;
- passes trusted CPU query/KV lengths to FlashInfer for new-token prefill;
- passes the corresponding host query/context lengths for context chunks.

This avoids the synchronization without disabling vLLM's sync guard or reverting PCP. It addresses the current synchronization failure in issue #49810; it does not claim to resolve every PCP issue tracked there.

Duplicate-work checks found no open PR referencing #49810 and no open PR matching the TRT-LLM ragged/CPU-sequence-length fix. The older PR #49196 is a much broader PCP revert and is not equivalent.

AI assistance was used to investigate the failure, prepare the code and tests, and draft this description. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and confirmed running the relevant tests before PR submission.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_registry.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/trtllm_ragged.py
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

Post-fix model evaluation requires B200 hardware and was not available locally. Request the exact `B200: LM Eval (PCP)` lane on this PR; the fix should not be considered proven until both GLM-5.2 PCP configs complete successfully.

## Test Result

- `test_mla_backends.py`: **42 passed, 292 skipped**
- MLA context-chunk and prefill-registry tests: **20 passed**
- Focused CPU-sequence-length regression test: **1 passed, 333 deselected**
- Pre-commit hooks on all changed files: **passed**
- `git diff --check`: **passed**

Pre-fix exact evidence: upstream main build #87024 failed the B200 PCP job on both the original and retry across two B200 hosts with the same FlashInfer `.any().item()` synchronization stack; builds #86943 and #86851 show the same failure family.

---

- [x] The test plan, including exact commands.
- [x] The local test results and required B200 model-evaluation follow-up.

title: [Spec Decode] Enable GLM-5.3-Flash DFlash2 end to end
body:
## Purpose

Enable the existing DFlash2 implementation to serve `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` with `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2`. Unpatched main fails after loading the weights with `Model does not support EAGLE3 interface`; auxiliary capture alone also leaves the GLM-specific cache allocator incompatible with the external drafter.

This narrows the existing draft to two required pieces:

- Expose completed auxiliary states through the EAGLE3 interface. Materialize and contract deferred mHC output without changing the target's state, preserve ordinary-layer semantics, and gather every selected activation under sequence parallelism.
- Allocate plain draft attention in a separate region using its native page geometry, independent block IDs, and explicit memory accounting. Honor the existing block-drop setting.

The previous draft/target slot-sharing and block-repacking optimization is removed from this PR. Capacity optimization and broader KV-management work are deferred. Main already includes the dense-draft EP inheritance fix from #56930.

## Related work and attribution

This updates existing draft #55423 rather than opening another implementation. Review of #55682 and #56983 informed the narrower scope:

- #55682 contributes auxiliary-capture work but leaves the cache startup blocker, adds an extra residual on ordinary layers, and omits early sequence-parallel gathers.
- #56983 supplies the separate draft-cache allocation adapted here and correct mHC semantics, but does not gather its selected auxiliary outputs under sequence parallelism.

This patch retains #55423's completed-state capture and selected-state gathers, adapts #56983's minimal cache allocation, and adds executable regression tests. Leoyzen and Shijin Zhang are both credited in `Co-authored-by` trailers. The sequence-parallel regression uses mocked collectives; distributed GPU validation remains outstanding.

## Validation

Base: `729ebac4983e1510e035bc579142b0fc210a49a3`.

```bash
HF_HUB_CACHE=/mnt/ceph/hf-models/hub HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/glm5next/test_eagle3.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py -q

uv run --no-project .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/models/glm5next/common/model.py vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/models/glm5next/test_eagle3.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
git diff --check
```

**131 tests passed.** All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff and mypy; diff checks were clean. Coverage includes completed mHC and ordinary-layer outputs, unchanged target state, capture disabled, sequence-parallel padding/gathers, wrapper layer selection, and independent draft allocation/accounting with FP8/BF16 cache specs and both block-drop settings.

### GPU E2E

Tested on four GB300 GPUs, TP4, max sequences 1, concurrency 1, maximum model length 16384, GPU-memory utilization 0.96, FP8 KV for target and draft, prefix caching, and CUDA graphs enabled. The tested DFlash configuration explicitly disables EAGLE block dropping.

Environment: Torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.1 native build, FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, Transformers 5.16.1, CUTLASS DSL 4.7.1. Native extensions built at `23e26e0588` were reused because native build inputs are unchanged through this base; the editable Python source is this patch.

- Target/draft loading, cache initialization, and CUDA graph capture passed.
- Cold/warm checks passed for identical 10240-token prompts and a shared 10000-token prefix. Both warm requests reused 9216 tokens and matched their cold 32-token greedy outputs.
- SpeedBench `throughput_16k/low_entropy`, 10240 input-token limit, 1536 output-token limit, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95: **32 successful requests, zero failures**, 48352 generated tokens in 118.277 seconds (**408.80 output tokens/s**), **49.086%** draft-token acceptance, mean acceptance length **4.436**. This is a serving smoke measurement, not a speedup comparison.

Matched GSM8K evaluation: first 128 test questions, 5-shot, greedy, seed 42, 256-token output limit, concurrency 1.

| Configuration | Correct | Accuracy | Invalid responses |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Target only | 115/128 | 89.84375% | 0 |
| DFlash2-7 | 115/128 | 89.84375% | 0 |

The equal aggregate score is a bounded model-quality check, not proof of token-for-token equivalence. Total generated tokens differed (11656 target-only, 11627 DFlash2).

### Reproduce serving and evaluation

With an installed editable checkout and sufficient GPU memory:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 \
VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \
uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve \
  zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --revision 690b705278a3a58e538fcb37c2ca8b5f9511213c \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --served-model-name glm53 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.96 --max-num-seqs 1 --max-model-len 16384 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2","revision":"bf582e4eacc1810f76656d1811693ff6c6737d2a","num_speculative_tokens":7,"disable_eagle_block_drop":true}' \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

Once healthy, run the bounded evaluation:

```bash
uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py \
  --port 8000 --num-questions 128 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 \
  --max-concurrency 1 --request-timeout-seconds 7200 \
  --save-results gsm8k-dflash.json
```

Restart with `--speculative-config null` for the matched target-only evaluation, retaining all other flags and using a separate result file. Greedy decoding and seed 42 are evaluator defaults. Development mode provides the localhost cache-reset endpoint used by prefix checks.

## Limits and AI assistance

This remains a draft. These bounded runs establish the tested Flash TP4 serving path; they do not certify exact speculative output equivalence, all cache behavior, distributed sequence parallelism, ROCm, pipeline parallelism, or the full GLM-5.3 model. Historical longer-continuation variability has not been isolated by this change. Full GLM-5.3 + DFlash2 is the next target after Flash support.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review, test execution, and this description. Human review of this revised patch and personal execution of the relevant tests are still required before marking it ready. Both contributing PR authors and AI assistance are credited in the commit, with the submitter's DCO sign-off.

title: [Bug]: VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC asserts in MLAAttention.bind_kv_cache for DeepSeek-V3.2 sparse MLA
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `0.28.1rc1.dev388+g8a728663c` (`vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:d996ae3a9dd3a77283177c7d660b8223be8e1ed707ae0264b65a1098349d7be0`, cu129, linux/arm64)
- NVIDIA GB200 (aarch64), NVL72
- Model: DeepSeek-V3.2-architecture MoE (GLM-5.3, NVFP4), 78 layers, `kv_lora_rank=512`, `qk_rope_head_dim=64`, `index_head_dim=128`
- Backends selected: `DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER` and `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`
- KV registration: `num_groups=1, num_segments=101, num_blocks=20307`, block size 64
- `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC` is **accepted by layout resolution and by `validate_kv_cache_layout`**, then asserts during engine initialization on every worker, so the engine crash-loops and never serves. The default resolution (`HND`) works fine on the same configuration.

```
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py", in bind_kv_cache
    assert self.kv_cache.stride(0) % row_width == 0
AssertionError
...
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above.
```

Call path: `multiproc_executor` → `gpu_worker.determine_available_memory` → `model_runner.profile_cudagraph_memory` → `_profile_cudagraph_memory` → `MLAAttention.bind_kv_cache`. Observed 25+ restarts per decode worker. No connector code is reached.

#### Why it gets that far

1. **Resolution accepts it.** Neither `FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMBackend` nor `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend` overrides `supported_kv_cache_layouts`, so both report "any layout" and an explicit `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT` is honoured. (`DeepseekV4IndexerBackend` does declare `(BLHNC, BLNHC)`, in the opposite direction.)

2. **Validation accepts it.** `validate_kv_cache_layout` returns early when page sizes are uniform, and otherwise only requires a *block-compact* layout:

   ```python
   if not layout.is_block_compact or (len(kv_cache_groups) > 1 and layout.is_layer_compact):
       raise ValueError(...)
   ```

   `is_block_compact` is `set(value[:2]) == {_DIM_L, _DIM_B}`, true for both `LBHNC = (0,1,2,3,4)` and `BLHNC = (1,0,2,3,4)`. This model has a single KV cache group, so the second clause never fires.

3. **The allocation becomes block-outermost**, so each layer's view has `stride(0)` equal to the whole packed block across all 101 KV segments rather than that layer's own page.

4. **The assert guards a real precondition** — the row-denominated stride handed to the sparse index kernel:

   ```python
   row_width = self.kv_cache.shape[-1]
   assert self.kv_cache.stride(0) % row_width == 0
   _CONVERT_REQ_INDEX_TO_GLOBAL_INDEX_KERNEL.register_warmup(
       self._vllm_config,
       block_stride_rows=self.kv_cache.stride(0) // row_width,
   )
   ```

5. **It fails because the segments are not uniform in width.** The MLA latent page is `kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim` = 576 elements per token; the DSA indexer page is `index_head_dim` = 128. Packed block-outermost, the block stride is a sum over segments of two different widths and is not a multiple of either. The failure is its own proof: if every segment had width `C`, the packed stride would be `n_segments × N × C`, which divides by `C`.

#### Relationship to #54465

`[Bugfix][MLA] Fix BLHNC addressing for FlashInfer sparse MLA` (#54465) threads `BLOCK_STRIDE_ROWS` through the forward path via `flat_kv_row_view`. The assertion here came from #50175 (`[1/N][warmup][DSv4] Migrate generic MLA metadata and indexing kernels`) and guards the warmup registration. Both express the block stride in whole content rows, so both inherit the same alignment precondition — with #54465 present you get past index conversion and land on this assert instead.

DeepSeek-V4 avoids it because `MLAAttentionSpec` carries V4-only `alignment` / `storage_block_size` fields and its indexer pages are designed to pack beside the MLA latent pages. V3.2 has neither.

#### Please do not work around this by disabling JIT warmup

The assert is gated on `vllm_config.kernel_config.enable_jit_warmup`. Disabling warmup removes the assert and lets the engine boot, with the sparse index kernel holding a `block_stride_rows` derived from a stride that is not a whole number of rows. That converts a loud startup failure into silently wrong addressing against real KV.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Serve a DeepSeek-V3.2-architecture model whose MLA latent width and DSA indexer width differ, so `DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER` and `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` are both selected.
2. Set `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC`.
3. Start the engine. It asserts in `MLAAttention.bind_kv_cache` during `profile_cudagraph_memory` on every worker.

Unset the variable and the same configuration starts and serves normally on `HND`.

### Expected behavior

Either:

1. **Fail fast and clearly.** Have the sparse-MLA / DSA-indexer backends declare `supported_kv_cache_layouts` excluding block-outermost for V3.2-style models, so resolution rejects `BLHNC` with a clear message — mirroring how `DeepseekV4IndexerBackend` already declares its requirement in the opposite direction. Or extend `validate_kv_cache_layout` to check the row-width divisibility the sparse kernels need, so this surfaces as a config-time `ValueError`.

2. **Support it.** Give `MLAAttentionSpec` the padding/alignment treatment V4 already has so segment widths become uniform under packing, or carry an element-accurate block stride through the sparse path so it tolerates non-uniform packed blocks.

At minimum, the current behaviour — accepted by two validators, then an unlabelled `AssertionError` during worker startup — is hard to diagnose.

### Why we were setting BLHNC

Block-outermost is the precondition for `_register_packed_kv_cache`, which would cut our NIXL descriptor count per transfer by ~71×. See #55434 for that performance problem; this bug blocks one of its candidate fixes.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find this reported (#54710 and #55312 concern layout resolution but different failures).

title: [Performance]: GLM-5.3 P/D on GB200 — NIXL issues up to ~112k KV descriptors per rank-transfer, making MNNVL/cuda_ipc slower than RDMA on this workload
body:
### Proposal to improve performance

Serving **GLM-5.3** (DeepSeek-V3.2 architecture: MLA + DSA indexer) with P/D disaggregation on GB200, NIXL KV transfer is dominated by **descriptor submission, not fabric bandwidth**. Under agentic load we observe **91,000–120,000 descriptors per TP-rank transfer** for a ~4.9 GB payload, and `cuda_ipc` spends **56.9% of transfer time posting them**.

The consequence: **for this workload shape, the documented GB-series MNNVL configuration is slower end to end than plain RDMA on the same hardware**, because `cuda_ipc` submission costs ~20× more per descriptor than `rc_x`. This is a statement about fragmented, descriptor-heavy transfers, not about the fabrics in general — with few descriptors we would expect MNNVL to win, and its post-submission movement rate is already the equal of IB's.

Descriptor count is not fixed by the model — it is the product of an architectural amplifier and workload-driven fragmentation. Measured below.

### Measurements

GLM-5.3 (NVFP4), DEP8 prefill + TP4 decode, AgentX C64. Deltas from vLLM's NIXL Prometheus histograms over each profile window. `postDuration` is synchronous submission; `xferDuration` is posting plus asynchronous movement/completion.

| Transport | Descriptors / transfer | Post mean | Total mean | Movement remainder | Payload / remainder | Post share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| RoCE `rc_x`, 1 rail | 91,262 | 32.1 ms | 517.4 ms | 485.2 ms | 6.45 GB/s | 6.2% |
| MNNVL `cuda_ipc` | 112,092 | **455.9 ms** | 800.8 ms | 345.0 ms | 14.16 GB/s | **56.9%** |
| Native IB `rc_x`, 4 rails | 119,984 | 24.4 ms | 350.8 ms | 326.4 ms | 15.11 GB/s | 7.0% |

Amortized submission cost per descriptor: `rc_x` IB **0.204 µs**, `rc_x` RoCE **0.352 µs**, `cuda_ipc` **4.067 µs**.

Two things to note:

- IB posted **more** descriptors than MNNVL and did it **18.7× faster**. The descriptor geometry was *comparable*, not identical (119,984 vs 112,092, within 7%), so the difference is in the submission path rather than in what was submitted.
- Their post-submission movement rates are comparable, 15.11 vs 14.16 GB/s. The NVLink data plane is healthy once the work is issued.

End-to-end, matched topology, budget, cache pool, concurrency and near-identical payload:

| Metric | MNNVL `cuda_ipc` | IB4 `rc_x` | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT mean / p50 / p95 / p99 | 5.240 / 3.079 / 14.412 / 37.930 s | 3.113 / 2.063 / 6.102 / 23.726 s | −41% / −33% / −58% / −37% |
| TPOT mean / p50 / p95 | 15.476 / 10.977 / 28.733 ms | 8.752 / 7.748 / 10.745 ms | −43% / −29% / −63% |
| Output tok/s/user mean / p50 | 102.68 / 91.10 | 136.77 / 129.06 | +33% / +42% |
| Decode output TPS | 1,444 | 2,093 | +45% |

We separately measured the same swap on a 6-decoder deployment: moving NIXL from RoCE onto MNNVL cut per-transfer wall time roughly in half and still made TTFT and ITL **worse** end to end, at both C48 and C64.

### The sensitivity is granularity, not bandwidth

A **direct PyTorch device-to-device peer-copy microbenchmark** between two GB200s on the same NVLink fabric — `torch.Tensor.copy_` on peer tensors, no NIXL or UCX involved — same total bytes, varying only how the copy is split:

| Transfer shape | Copies | Rate | Per-copy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| One contiguous 4.29 GB | 1 | **778.6 GB/s** | — |
| 45 KiB chunks | 93,206 | 2.4 GB/s | 19.31 µs |
| 180 KiB chunks | 23,301 | 9.5 GB/s | 19.36 µs |
| 1 MiB chunks | 4,096 | 53.1 GB/s | 19.74 µs |
| 16 MiB chunks | 256 | 416.8 GB/s | 40.25 µs |
| 256 MiB chunks | 16 | 740.9 GB/s | 362.31 µs |

Per-copy cost is flat from 45 KiB to 1 MiB and only becomes bandwidth-bound above ~16 MiB. At 45 KB granularity NVLink delivers 0.3% of what it does contiguously. Note this measures per-operation cost on the CUDA copy path, so the absolute 19.3 µs is not UCX's submission cost (measured separately above at 4.067 µs per descriptor); it is included to show that fine granularity, not fabric bandwidth, is what NVLink is sensitive to. An RDMA NIC is far more tolerant of the same shape: with these identical descriptors, RoCE sustained 43 GB/s, 86% of a 400 Gb/s link, because the NIC pipelines scatter-gather in hardware.

### Where the descriptor count comes from (measured)

`register_kv_caches` creates one NIXL region per distinct KV allocation. With a layer-outermost KV layout each layer owns its own allocation, so this model registers **101 regions**:

```
Registered KV caches: num_groups=1, num_segments=101, num_blocks=20307
```

Descriptors are coalesced spans, so a request whose blocks are contiguous needs only one descriptor per region. We measured the scaling directly on an otherwise idle deployment, reading `vllm:nixl_num_descriptors_sum` / `vllm:nixl_xfer_time_seconds_count` deltas:

| Condition | Prompt tokens | Payload / rank-transfer | **Descriptors / rank-transfer** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Idle pool, 2 sequential requests | 10.3k | 502 MB | **101** |
| Idle pool, 2 sequential requests | 41.1k | 1,990 MB | **101** |
| Concurrency 12, unique prompts | ~30.8k | 1,492 MB | **168** |
| AgentX C64 agentic load | ~90k, 88–92% prefix hit | 4.9 GB | **112,092** |

Two things follow:

1. **Context length alone does not drive it.** Quadrupling the prompt from 10.3k to 41.1k tokens quadrupled the payload and left the descriptor count at exactly 101 — one per region, because freshly allocated blocks are contiguous and coalesce.
2. **Block-pool fragmentation drives it, and 101 amplifies it.** Every non-contiguous run in a request's block list costs one descriptor *per region*. Under agentic load — long contexts assembled largely from prefix-cache hits scattered across the pool from many earlier requests — the block list is highly fragmented and the count rises three orders of magnitude.

So the architecture sets the multiplier (101 regions, from 78 layers of MLA plus the DSA indexer) and the workload sets how many spans that multiplier is applied to. Long-context, high-prefix-reuse serving is the worst case, and it is exactly the case P/D disaggregation exists for.

### Candidate directions

We are not attached to any particular one; the problem is the descriptor count.

1. **Packed region registration — removes the 101× amplifier.** vLLM already has `_register_packed_kv_cache`, which registers the whole cache as one region with one descriptor per block. It fires only when every layer view shares one backing storage, which needs a block-outermost KV layout. With one region, even a fully fragmented request costs one descriptor per block rather than 101, taking our worst case from ~112,000 to roughly 1,100 — a **~100× reduction** that does not depend on fixing fragmentation. Applying the measured submission costs, `cuda_ipc` posting would fall from 455.9 ms to roughly 4.5 ms. We could not test this: `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC` asserts at engine init for sparse MLA, filed separately as #55431.

2. **Reduce fragmentation, or coalesce better.** Coalescing clearly already happens (101 at idle proves it). Allocation policy that keeps a sequence's blocks contiguous, or a smarter merge when assembling prefix-cache-matched block lists, attacks the other factor. Related work appears on the `feat/nixl-per-region-geometry` branch.
3. **Investigate the `cuda_ipc` submission path** with NIXL/UCX. 4.067 µs per descriptor against 0.204 µs for `rc_x`, with comparable movement afterwards, suggests per-span submission rather than batched.

Things we ruled out, to save others the time:

- `--block-size` is already 64, and the `DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER` backend pins it there.
- A CUDA 13 rebuild is not the answer. We diffed the `nixl_cu12` and `nixl_cu13` UCX builds shipped inside nixl 1.3.2: their `cuda_ipc` symbol sets are identical (21 symbols, zero diff), both exporting `uct_cuda_ipc_ep_get_zcopy` and `uct_cuda_ipc_iface_get_max_get_zcopy`.

### Documentation note

`docs/features/nixl_connector_usage.md` recommends `--enable-cumem-allocator` + `UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_MNNVL=y` + `cuda_ipc` in `UCX_TLS` for GB-series GPUs. Until descriptor counts come down, that configuration is slower end to end than leaving `cuda_ipc` out, which is worth a caveat. NVIDIA's own GB200 vLLM recipe sets `UCX_TLS: '^cuda_ipc'`.

### Your current environment

| | |
|---|---|
| vLLM | `0.28.0+cu129` (transport measurements); `0.28.1rc1.dev388+g8a728663c` (layout attempt) |
| Model | DeepSeek-V3.2-architecture MoE (GLM-5.3, NVFP4), 78 layers, `kv_lora_rank` 512, `qk_rope_head_dim` 64, `index_head_dim` 128 |
| Backends | `DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER`, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` |
| KV registration | `num_groups=1, num_segments=101, num_blocks=20307`, block size 64 |
| Hardware | NVIDIA GB200 (aarch64), NVL72; 4 IB rails + RoCE |
| Serving | P/D disaggregation, `NixlConnector` pull, TP4 decode, nixl 1.3.2 |

Percentile caveats: NIXL latency percentiles are Prometheus histogram estimates with a 5 s top finite bucket; the descriptor histogram tops out at 50,000 while observed means are 91k–120k, so only descriptor **means** are valid. Metrics are per TP-rank transfer, and a TP4 decode request waits on the slowest of four.

### Related

- #55431 — `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC` asserts for sparse MLA. Blocks direction 1 above.
- #50913 — P/D TTFT RFC touching NIXL descriptor overhead; its `--block-size 16→64` advice does not apply here.
- #34054 / #36475 — same descriptor signature, different cause (CUDA context so UCX could select NVLink). MNNVL is already active for us.
- #42082 — Standardize KV-cache Layouts. #50714 / #50717 — packed cache, `num_regions=1`.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find this specific report.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Declare layer-compact KV layouts for V3.2 sparse MLA
body:
## Purpose

Fix #55431.

On a DeepSeek-V3.2-style sparse MLA model, `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC` passed both layout resolution and `validate_kv_cache_layout`, then asserted in `MLAAttention.bind_kv_cache` on every worker (`kv_cache.stride(0) % row_width == 0`), so the engine crash-looped and never served.

Root cause: none of the V3.2 sparse MLA backends overrode `supported_kv_cache_layouts`, so they reported "any layout" and the explicit env was honored. Their sparse top-k walk reads the bound cache as per-layer `[B, N, C]` rows, which only layer-compact layouts provide; a block-outermost layout packs every KV segment into one block-major slab and the per-layer row view falls apart. The SM90 sibling already declared `(LBHNC,)`, the V4 indexer declares its packing pair, these four were simply missing.

This declares the layer-compact layouts on `FlashMLASparseBackend`, the FlashInfer sparse TRTLLM/SM120 base, and `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend`, in the same relative order as the default preference. Resolution now fails fast:

```
ValueError: VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC does not satisfy every supported set; valid layouts: ['LBNHC', 'LBHNC']
```

Behavior for working configurations is unchanged: default resolution still lands on the same layout (mixed-HNC narrowing keeps the default-preference leader), explicit `LBNHC`/`LBHNC` are still accepted, the NIXL/HND pairing still resolves, `DeepseekV4IndexerBackend` keeps `(BLHNC, BLNHC)` and `KpoolTailBackend` keeps `(LBHNC,)`. All of this is pinned by the new tests.

Duplicate check: #54834 and #55384 change how an already-resolved layout propagates through config copies, not which layouts these backends accept. Nothing else open touches `supported_kv_cache_layouts` for sparse MLA (searched KV_CACHE_LAYOUT, BLHNC, supported_kv_cache_layouts).

No model eval: resolution output is bit-identical for every configuration that previously worked, so serving behavior is unaffected; only the previously crash-looping explicit setting changes, from assert at worker init to a clear error at engine core resolution.

AI assistance: this change was prepared with AI assistance (Kimi K3). The submitter-reviewed claims are the ones backed by the commands below: mechanism traced on current main, new suite red-green checked both directions, neighboring CPU suite run.

## Test Plan

New CPU suite `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py` (11 tests): the four backends declare only layer-compact layouts; the combined supported set for the reporter's pairing (TRTLLM + V32 indexer) excludes block-outermost; explicit BLHNC with mixed page sizes raises at resolution; default resolution and explicit LBNHC/LBHNC acceptance are unchanged; the SM90 pairing still resolves LBHNC; V4 indexer and KpoolTail declarations are untouched.

```
python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py -q
python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py -q
ruff check <touched files> && ruff format --check <touched files>
```

## Test Result

New suite: 11 passed. Red-green both directions: with the source edits stashed, the six bug-pinning tests fail (on main the BLHNC test resolves and returns BLHNC instead of raising) while the five preservation tests still pass; with the edits, all 11 pass. Neighboring kpool suite: 12 passed. ruff clean.

Local environment: torch 2.14.0 CPU, macOS, Python 3.12. The kpool file was run with `--noconftest` locally because the repo's global-cleanup teardown segfaults inside `torch.accelerator.empty_host_cache` on this platform; that is unrelated to this change and does not occur in CI. No GPU available here, so the sparse kernels themselves were not executed; per above, no configuration that previously resolved changes behavior.

title: [Attention] Use packed MLA sizes for hybrid block alignment
body:
## Overview `_align_hybrid_block_size` estimates the MLA page from `head_size`. Packed ds_mla caches store a different number of bytes per token (`fp8_ds_mla` 656, `nvfp4_ds_mla` 352), so the hybrid block size is computed for the wrong page. This is the second of two complementary PRs, stacked on #60967; only the top commit is new. #60967 stops padding Mamba pages for block-outermost layouts and changes plain fp8/bf16 MLA configurations; this PR corrects the block size for packed ds_mla configurations. Without #60967, the corrected size makes the KDA layers need a fourth group with MTP off: 80 of 384 configurations would be worse instead of 42. ## Claims - The hybrid alignment reads the packed width from `get_mla_state_content_bytes`, the lookup `MLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec` already used inline. - With #60967, GLM-5.3-Flash `fp8_ds_mla` at 8k–128k: median +10.7% max concurrency vs main, worse in 42 of 384 configurations (down to −8.3%). ## Validation GLM-5.3-Flash (real `config.json`), same CPU allocation harness as #60967, 384 reachable `fp8_ds_mla` configurations. #60967 leaves all of them identical to main, so these numbers hold against both: 340 better, 2 equal, 42 worse (−8.3% to +26.1%). The worse ones, TP8 with MTP at ≥ 32k and SM90 TP4 at 128k, keep their group count; the smaller block rounds up to a worse multiple of the packed block-stride alignment.
Max concurrency vs #60967 (e5b4c3c184 → 4b51580ae6, main ec8a372566), 8 GiB KV cache per GPU, 8k / 32k / 128k SM90 `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, prefix caching on: | TP | MTP off | MTP 1 | MTP 3 | MTP 5 | |---:|---|---|---|---| | 1 | +14.1 / +16.1 / +7.8 | +18.4 / +19.8 / +11.5 | +20.7 / +21.4 / +13.4 | +21.6 / +22.1 / +14.8 | | 2 | +16.6 / +13.7 / +3.6 | +16.2 / +13.2 / +6.9 | +23.0 / +19.9 / +10.7 | +18.3 / +15.7 / +8.9 | | 4 | +12.1 / +4.1 / −4.1 | +11.7 / +7.2 / +0.6 | +22.1 / +14.0 / +4.1 | +23.1 / +15.8 / +5.5 | | 8 | +26.1 / +16.3 / +10.7 | +6.6 / −2.0 / −7.4 | +8.7 / +0.0 / −6.5 | +10.1 / +1.7 / −5.7 | SM120 `--kv-cache-dtype auto` (→ `fp8_ds_mla`), prefix caching on: | TP | MTP off | MTP 1 | MTP 3 | MTP 5 | |---:|---|---|---|---| | 1 | +15.8 / +17.9 / +9.5 | +15.3 / +16.7 / +11.9 | +22.8 / +23.6 / +15.4 | +21.6 / +22.1 / +14.8 | | 2 | +16.6 / +13.7 / +3.6 | +10.7 / +7.8 / +3.9 | +21.4 / +18.4 / +9.0 | +22.6 / +19.9 / +10.7 | | 4 | +21.6 / +12.3 / +3.9 | +20.3 / +11.5 / +2.5 | +22.1 / +14.0 / +4.1 | +23.1 / +15.8 / +5.5 | | 8 | +25.9 / +14.2 / +9.1 | +8.8 / −1.0 / −6.1 | +10.0 / +0.8 / −5.2 | +10.7 / +2.2 / −4.5 | Prefix caching off and 40 GiB: same pattern. At 256k / 512k / 1M the median is +2.0% / +0.8% / −0.3%.
```bash pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -k "glm5_like_hybrid or hybrid_mla_block_alignment" ``` `test_hybrid_mla_block_alignment` fails on #60967 (block 4352 instead of 3328) and passes here. Not run on a GPU. ## Details - Among hybrid models, only GLM-5.3-Flash can select a ds_mla cache, and only `fp8_ds_mla`. - #60321 adds `mxfp4_mla` with its own inline width in both places; whichever PR lands second moves it into `get_mla_state_content_bytes`. title: [Bugfix][DSv4] Add missing Hadamard rotation to sparse indexer quant kernels
body:
## Problem

`DeepseekV4Attention` / `DeepseekV4Indexer` pass `rotate=True` to
`DeepseekCompressor`, but `DeepseekCompressor.rotate` is stored and never
read — a dead parameter. The fused Triton kernels
(`fused_indexer_q.py` fp8/mxfp4 Q, `fused_compress_quant_cache.py` fp8/mxfp4 K)
apply RoPE and then quantize directly, skipping the Hadamard rotation that the
official DeepSeek-V4 inference reference applies to the indexer path:

- `inference/model.py` in `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`:
  `rotate_activation(...)` (fast_hadamard_transform, scale = dim^-0.5, bf16)
  is applied to indexer Q and to the indexer K compressor (`rotate=True`).
  (The main-attention 512-dim compressor uses `rotate=False` and is untouched
  here.)
- SGLang's DSA indexer does the same (`_get_k_bf16` -> `rotate_activation` /
  `hadamard_transform`).

Because the rotation mixes each 128-dim vector before per-group quantization,
skipping it changes the quantized values themselves, not only their rounding —
the indexer top-k selection (and thus which tokens sparse attention attends
to) can diverge from the reference implementation.

## Fix

Apply the Sylvester Hadamard rotation (scaled by `head_dim**-0.5`) in all
four indexer kernels, after RoPE + bf16 round-trip and before quantization:

- Q kernels (`fused_indexer_q.py`): masked full-width GPT-J RoPE -> bf16
  round-trip -> rotate -> fp8 / mxfp4 (per-32-block e2m1) quantization.
- K kernels (`fused_compress_quant_cache.py`): same rotation inserted after
  RoPE + bf16 round-trip, before fp8 / mxfp4 cache quantization.

The rotation is orthogonal and applied to **both** Q and K, so indexer QK dot
products are preserved (a property test asserts this); only the quantized
representations change. Indexer cache contents change bit-wise for DSv4
deployments — that is the intended alignment with the reference
implementation.

**Dimension gating (no env, no opt-in).** The kernels take a `HADAMARD`
constexpr and the launchers set it when `head_dim == 128 and rope_dim == 64`
(the production DSv4 indexer config). Off-dims configs keep main's exact
behavior: the original Triton code paths are preserved (the 128/64
`static_assert`s are scoped to the `HADAMARD` branch) and the Q launcher's
cutedsl dispatch still serves the dims it served on main. Main's own
generality envelope is unchanged — its fp8 Triton kernel needs a power-of-2
nope dim, and its mxfp4 Q launcher needs `head_dim % 128 == 0` for the int32
scale view. (Note: the cutedsl indexer-Q kernels are effectively
production-dims only — at (96, 32) main's cutedsl fp8 path runs but diverges
from the unfused rope+quant reference; pre-existing on main, untouched here.)
Dimension-guard tests assert bit-exact parity with the unrotated reference
for off-dims configs (Q 96/32 fp8, Q 128/32 mxfp4, K 64/32 fp8+mxfp4).

## Implementation notes

- **Matrix-free fp32 butterfly, not a matrix multiply.** The rotation runs as
  7 fixed-order butterfly stages (`_hadamard_stage` x S=64..1 in
  `fused_indexer_q.py`), each a single elementwise fp32 add/sub, followed by
  the `128**-0.5` scale. Every step is reproducible with plain torch
  elementwise ops, so the unfused oracle in the tests matches the kernel
  bit-exactly at any token count and any `num_warps`. A broadcast-mul +
  `tl.sum` formulation is not bit-stable: torch eager switches reduction
  strategy with problem size, which broke oracle equality at large sizes
  (e.g. 257/1023 tokens x 64 heads). The full RoPE → bf16-roundtrip →
  rotation block is a single `@triton.jit` helper (`_rope_hadamard_full`,
  returning the rotated full-width vector) shared by all four indexer
  kernels, so the two Q and two K kernels cannot drift apart (post-review
  dedup; verified byte-identical before/after over 236M output elements).
- **Pinned FMA contraction.** The RoPE even/odd updates in all four indexer
  kernels now use explicit `tl.fma` on every platform, matching the
  contraction NVCC/HIP already apply in the unfused `rotary_embedding` flow.
  This removes the ROCm-only `USE_EXPLICIT_FMA` divergence and makes results
  independent of the `cos_sin_cache` dtype (bf16 vs fp32). The head=512
  kernels are not FMA-pinned (out of scope; their tests use `assert_close`).

## Scope and follow-ups

- **Only the head=128 indexer path rotates** (see Problem: reference uses
  `rotate=False` for the 512-dim compressor). The 512-wide kernels and the
  Triton/cutedsl 512 read paths are deliberately unchanged.
- **cutedsl**: the cutedsl indexer-Q kernels predate the rotation and would
  silently skip it, so for the rotated production dims (128/64) the launcher
  in `fused_indexer_q.py` always uses the Triton kernel (with a `NOTE` in
  code) until the cutedsl kernels implement the rotation; off-dims configs
  keep main's cutedsl dispatch (see "Dimension gating"). The cutedsl files
  themselves are untouched. Implementing the rotation there is a follow-up —
  it requires a cross-thread butterfly over the 8-thread subwarp that owns
  each 128-dim row, and bit-exact parity with the Triton path (their existing
  test asserts `torch.equal`).
- **XPU**: the closed-source
  `torch.ops.vllm.xpu_deepseek_fused_indexer_q_rope_{fp8,mxfp4}` ops still
  skip the rotation and need a follow-up from the XPU op owners. ROCm uses
  the Triton kernels and gets the rotation automatically.

## Test plan

Command (GB200, SM100; the `dsv4_hadamard_upstream_shim` conftest plugin only
redirects the dsv4 ops modules to this source tree):

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3 VLLM_DSV4_CUTEDSL_OPS="" \
  PYTHONPATH=<shim-dir> python -m pytest -p dsv4_hadamard_upstream_shim \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_hadamard.py \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_rope_quant.py \
  tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py -q
```

Test changes:

- `tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_hadamard.py` (new): bit-exact Q and K
  tests against unfused oracles — fp64 FMA emulation for RoPE, a butterfly
  oracle for the rotation, an independent per-row ue8m0 oracle for fp8 (not
  `per_token_group_quant_fp8`) — plus the orthogonality property test
  (H symmetric, H@H = 128*I exact, fp64 QK dot product preserved) and a
  quantization-quality property test: on outlier-heavy post-RoPE-like
  activations the rotated kernels' QK dot-product quant error is <0.5x the
  unrotated oracle's (measured 0.21 fp8 / 0.25 mxfp4; main's kernels are
  identical to that oracle, i.e. ratio ~1.0, so the test fails on main),
  and neutral (ratio in [0.8, 1.25], measured ~1.00) on iid Gaussian input. The Q-side
  oracle resolves the fp8 flavor at runtime via `current_platform.fp8_dtype()`
  (fnuz/224 on gfx942, e4m3fn/448 elsewhere), mirroring the launcher; the
  K-side oracle keeps e4m3fn/448 because the K kernels pin `tl.float8e4nv`
  on every platform.
- `tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_rope_quant.py`: oracle rewritten to
  rope -> bf16 round-trip -> Hadamard -> quant; the `use_cutedsl`
  parametrization is dropped since the launcher no longer dispatches to
  cutedsl for indexer Q.
- `tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py`: reference gains
  `rotate: bool` (fp64 FMA emulation + butterfly oracle); the indexer test
  passes `rotate=True` and launches with `num_warps=1` like the production
  launcher.

## Test result

**Kernel suites**: **82 passed, 11 skipped** (all skips are pre-existing
ROCm/gfx950-only gates). Breakdown: hadamard 15 + q_rope_quant 20 +
compressor 47. Lint: `ruff format --check` clean on all 5 touched files
(ruff 0.14.0).

**Quantization quality on real indexer activations** (why the rotation
matters). We captured the actual post-RoPE indexer Q and compressor-K
vectors from the official reference implementation (torchrun TP4, synthetic
8192-token input, layers 2/22/40) and measured quantization quality with and
without the rotation:

- Real indexer Q is firmly in the outlier regime the reference's rotation
  targets: per-vector kurtosis 17.5-44.9 (iid Gaussian = 3), top-8 channels
  carry 24-34% of channel energy. After rotation: kurtosis 4.5-5.7, top-8
  share 9-13% — near-incoherent.
- QK dot-product error (the quantity the indexer actually consumes) improves
  in **every** layer x format cell: fp8 mean 1.25-1.46x (max 2.0-2.6x);
  mxfp4 mean 1.18-1.66x (p99 up to 2.0x). Rotation exactness: max
  |dot(qH,kH) - dot(q,k)| = 1.6e-5.
- Post-rotation, real vectors quantize exactly like norm-matched iid Gaussian
  vectors (relL2 ratio 0.97-1.02 over all 12 layer x format cells) — the
  rotation closes the gap to the incoherent bound, which is the mechanism by
  which it stabilizes indexer top-k selection.
- fp8 per-vector relL2 is rotation-neutral (0.0264 vs 0.0264): expected for a
  floating-point format whose per-row scale absorbs outliers into the
  exponent — the fp8 gain appears in dot products (error deconcentration),
  not per-element MSE. mxfp4 (4-bit, 32-dim blocks, ~4.6-binade dynamic
  range per block) improves per-vector as well (layer-22 Q p99 relL2
  0.377 -> 0.288).

**E2E accuracy vs the reference implementation** (synthetic programmatic
8192-token technical document, identical raw token ids fed to both sides;
reference = official open-source `inference/` stack, torchrun TP4,
full-position top-20 logprobs; vLLM = this branch, TP4,
`/v1/completions?prompt_logprobs=20`, 8191 aligned positions): top-1
agreement 95.0%; on behavior-relevant tokens (reference logprob > -2) median
|dlogprob| 0.0000 nats, p95 0.114 nats; teacher-forced actual-token mean
|dlogprob| 0.013 nats. On bulk text the rotated and unrotated configs are
nearly indistinguishable end-to-end (top-1 agreement with the reference
95.04% vs 95.01%) — expected, since top-2048-of-8192 selection is permissive
and bulk argmax margins are large. The fix's value is algorithmic parity with
the reference (a dead `rotate` parameter is not merely suboptimal, it is
unimplemented behavior) plus the quantization-quality gains above, with no
e2e regression.

**Performance.** Kernel latency (GB200, median of 50 iters, committed
branch vs main): Q kernels within ±5% at all token counts (several faster,
e.g. fp8 @37 tokens -12.6%); K kernels within ±5% except mxfp4 @16384 tokens
+8.2% (absolute ~2-4 us per 16k tokens, ~0.2 ns/token — the intrinsic cost of
the added rotation in the mxfp4 kernel). E2E serving (TP4, spec decode,
synthetic 8k input): ITL 15.12 vs 15.15 ms/step (-0.18%, within run-to-run
jitter). The rotation itself is performance-neutral: an earlier revision that
also bumped the indexer kernels to num_warps=4 regressed K by +404% at 16k
tokens; the committed branch keeps num_warps=1 and matches or beats main.

## Why this is not a duplicate

Checked 2026-09-05 via the GitHub search API (`gh` CLI unavailable in this
environment) for open PRs in vllm-project/vllm: `hadamard indexer`,
`deepseek indexer rotate`, `rotate_activation`, `hadamard` (16 hits). No open
PR addresses this fix. The only nominal indexer hit is #41834 ("[New
Model][Nvidia] Add SM12x support for DeepSeek V4 Flash"), a different scope —
SM12x enablement for another DSv4 variant; its body contains no
Hadamard/rotation change to these kernels. All other `hadamard` hits are
unrelated quantization work (AutoRound MXFP4, humming, QuIP/hadacore,
TurboQuant, KVarN).

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (Kimi Code CLI): implementation,
test rewrites, and this description were authored by the agent and reviewed by
the human submitter.

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Recover locally invalidated pull peer metadata
body:
## Summary

Recover a pull peer whose **local NIXL metadata is missing while Prefill is still alive with the same engine ID**. Without recovery, vLLM's cached `_remote_agents` entry and prepared dlists can keep subsequent requests on the stale path.

A receive failure schedules a descriptor-free `check_remote_metadata(agent)` check. This queries **local metadata existence, not peer health**. Only confirmed absence makes the peer eligible for recovery; a transfer error or probe exception alone does not.

## Implementation

- Track failed and locally invalid peers in `NixlBaseConnectorWorker`. One `_cleanup_remote_engines()` pass handles both replacement and invalidation, reusing `_cleanup_remote_engine()` to release resources.
- Defer probes and cleanup while background handshakes are pending. For invalid peers, reject new reads and wait for all existing receive handles to settle before cleanup. Replacement cleanup retains its existing queued-request guard.
- Clear recovery state in the shared per-engine cleanup, including TTL eviction and shutdown. A peer that is both replaced and invalidated is cleaned once; the replacement's address mapping is preserved.
- Route new and handshake-ready requests through the pull worker's existing read entry point. After cleanup, a fresh request re-handshakes the unchanged engine ID and uses newly prepared descriptors. Failed requests are **not replayed with old remote block IDs**.

The production changes are in `nixl/base_worker.py` and `nixl/pull_worker.py`. Recovery remains **pull-only**, with an explicit push-mode TODO. There is no new router API, configuration, or metadata probe on successful transfers.

Following Yannik's review, tests reuse `TestPeerReplacement` and `FakeNixlWrapper` instead of a separate hand-built recovery fixture. The existing receive/HMA fixtures and push test stub initialize the new fields. Nick Hill's read/handshake simplification is retained with authorship preserved.

## Related Work and Scope

Related to #49238. This is a follow-up to merged #50047, not another replacement detector:

| Change | Trigger |
| --- | --- |
| #50047 | A new engine ID is confirmed at the same address. |
| This PR | The engine ID is unchanged, but NIXL has lost the decoder's local peer metadata. |

Both now use one base-worker cleanup pass, rather than separate replacement and recovery passes. The scope split was discussed in [#50047](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50047#issuecomment-5629552908).

#52232 addresses HMA failure propagation and is **not included here**. Recovering future requests does not by itself guarantee that the failed HMA request returns an error instead of invalid output. TTL policy and the native UCX race discussed in NIXL #1987 are also outside this patch's scope.

Stuck reads or handshakes defer recovery; this patch does not forcibly release active resources. Native cleanup exceptions propagate rather than being swallowed. Recovery is not a claim that every UCX failure is recoverable.

## Validation

### Refactor and CI

| Check | Result and revision scope |
| --- | --- |
| Local source-AST/mock regressions after the refactor and September 29 main merge | 32 passed: 20 previous recovery cases plus 12 existing receive-lifecycle cases. These external harnesses are not full-import vLLM tests. |
| Old-fixture negative control | The same 12 receive-lifecycle cases fail with the original missing-field fixtures. |
| Recorded-main behavioral negative control | 3 expected recovery assertion failures and 5 passing controls. |
| Local pre-commit, including Ruff and mypy; `git diff --check` | Passed on the September 29 merged revision. |
| [Buildkite #91865](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91865), September 29 merged revision | NVIDIA KV Connector shards **4/4 passed**; AMD KV Connector shards **4/4 passed**. The overall build reports "passed and blocked"; not every defined pipeline job was executed. |
| [Subsequent automatic main merge](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/8aba1056b6b811b4770fd6bba860b54835c84ca6), September 30 | Pre-commit and DCO passed. No full Buildkite result is attached to this new head at the time of this update; #91865 tested the preceding revision. |

The failures in earlier CI #91736 were missing recovery fields in fixtures that bypass the worker constructor. Those fixtures are now initialized, and the subsequent KV Connector shards pass.

Regression coverage includes confirmed-missing versus healthy/probe-error cases, same-ID re-handshake with fresh descriptors, pending-handshake gating, sibling-handle drain ordering, new-read rejection, healthy-peer isolation, replacement/invalidation overlap, notify-only requests, expiry accounting, cleanup exceptions, TTL eviction, and shutdown.

Local full-import pytest collection was blocked by missing `tblib` and the incomplete vLLM runtime environment; the 32 local cases are not a substitute for CI. There is **no new native NIXL/GPU or model-serving evaluation of the refactored revision**. Historical experiments below remain evidence only for their stated revisions and configurations.

### Reproduction Commands

From a vLLM checkout with the repository's test dependencies installed:

```bash
# Focused replacement and local-invalidation coverage.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  -m cpu_test -k TestPeerReplacement -v --tb=short

# Broader connector CPU regression suite.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py \
  -m cpu_test -v --tb=short

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/pull_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py
```

These commands select the current tests; they are not presented as the exact Buildkite shard commands. The old `-k peer_recovery` selector no longer describes the consolidated tests.

<details>
<summary>Historical native and serving evidence, before the current refactor</summary>

### September 23 H20 validation

Full vLLM Python imports in isolated H20 containers: **357 selected CPU tests passed**, including 18 recovery cases; the corresponding main-only selection passed 339. Eight selected baseline cases produced 3 expected recovery assertion failures and 5 passes.

Real NIXL/UCX probes passed with 1 MiB CPU and GPU buffers. With the peer still alive, the probe deliberately removed local metadata, observed the stale-read failure, invoked patched cleanup, and explicitly reloaded the same agent's metadata for a byte-checked read. Healthy-peer reads continued working. Automatic re-handshake was covered separately by pytest.

Runtime: NIXL 1.4.1, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12.3. The rebased Python source used native extensions from the existing vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev422+gd05da62e9` image, not a fresh CUDA build of main. No weights were loaded for this validation. This is not a model-serving, natural-disconnect, or NVLink/RDMA validation of the current revision.

[Exact commands, full selected logs, and native probe](https://gist.github.com/xijiaat/34c74ce35e1f68958e5881a1907bf84d).

### Original TP1 P/D serving experiment

The original implementation was tested with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, NIXL 1.3.2, fp8 HMA KV, eager mode, `UCX_TLS=tcp,cuda_copy`, and the existing TP1 packed-layout fix. With no active reads, a controlled hook removed only Decode's local remote metadata, retaining the Python cache. A real stale read failed with `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND`; fresh requests automatically re-handshook the unchanged Prefill engine ID and returned the expected short answers.

The **recovery-only failed request still emitted 32 invalid tokens**. Adding #52232 and an API terminal-error follow-up produced a passing 10-request scenario: two normal controls, four controlled failures across Chat/Completion and streaming/non-streaming, and four fresh Chat recoveries. The failed requests emitted no generated content. This combined result must not be attributed to the recovery-only diff. Attribution for the HMA change belongs to Tyler Michael Smith.

The original recovery-only CPU selections passed 353 distinct cases across two runs. The combined recovery/HMA/API experiment passed 425 selected tests, not 425 tests of this standalone patch. Full original logs retain earlier failures and an independently wrong pre-injection arithmetic control.

This is controlled failure-path evidence, not general accuracy, natural transport-failure reproduction, multi-rank native-race coverage, or a guarantee of production readiness.

[Selected raw logs, response bodies/SSE, commands and patches](https://gist.github.com/xijiaat/a975858a507d6c45fd394b3675cc0ab9). Internal addresses and paths are anonymized. The HMA/API evidence is also reported in [#52232](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52232#issuecomment-5552174526).

### Maintainer simplification

Nick Hill's [simplification](https://github.com/njhill/vllm/commit/7dc2a0eb49dbc62fdfc329885e663a672160cdec) was incorporated with authorship and sign-off preserved. It reuses main's in-flight-transfer guard rather than a second request-to-engine map: receive metadata remains available until the handles settle. The subsequent refactor retains that approach and moves cleanup into the base worker as suggested by Yannik Hinteregger.

</details>

## AI Assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, testing, and this report. The human submitter reviewed and approved the original contribution; subsequent compatibility adaptations remain subject to human review. Historical results and limited failure-path tests are not claims of comprehensive model evaluation or production readiness.

title: [Security] Time out DeepSeek tool-call regexes
body:
## Summary
The `deepseek_v3` and `deepseek_v31` tool parsers run multi-`.*` `regex` patterns on model output without a timeout. Sibling parsers already pass `timeout=VLLM_TOOL_PARSE_REGEX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` so a pathological completion cannot stall the API-server event loop. This applies the same limit and treats `TimeoutError` as "no tool call" / skip the stream delta.

This is not a duplicate of #54678 (poolside_v1 / dots regex rewrite) or other open timeout work: those do not cover these DeepSeek parsers.

## Changes
- `vllm/tool_parsers/deepseekv3_tool_parser.py`: pass the existing regex timeout on `findall` / both streaming `match` sites; catch `TimeoutError`.
- `vllm/tool_parsers/deepseekv31_tool_parser.py`: same for the sibling parser (greedy `.*` on the streaming patterns).

## Codepath coverage
- Non-streaming `extract_tool_calls` (`findall`) for both parsers.
- Streaming portion `match` and name `match` for both parsers.
- All HTTP/gRPC generate surfaces that select these parsers go through those two methods.

## Tests
- `test_regex_timeout_treated_as_no_tool_call` — timeout is fail-closed (content returned, no tool calls) and `timeout=` is passed.
- `test_streaming_portion_regex_timeout_skips_delta` — streaming portion match times out and skips the delta.
- `test_streaming_name_regex_timeout_skips_delta` — streaming name-regex fallback times out and skips the delta.

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv3_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv31_tool_parser.py -k "timeout" -v --noconftest
# 6 passed
```

Well-formed DeepSeek tool-call strings still parse after the timeout argument is added. No model-output change for valid completions; no eval rerun.

## AI assistance
This PR was developed with AI assistance.
