title: [Performance][Model] DeepSeek-V4: reuse fused post residual for aux hidden states
body:
## Performance (measured on 4×H20, sm_90)

Same machine / same recipe (TP4+EP, DSpark K=7 probabilistic + adaptive
verification, KV fp8, think=off, temperature=0), before vs after:

| Scenario | decode tok/s (median) | system tok/s (median) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| C4 (4 concurrent, 8 req) | 130.26 → 142.10 (**+9.1%**) | 342.66 → 381.24 (**+11.3%**) |
| C8 (8 concurrent, 16 req) | 109.45 → 114.07 (**+4.2%**) | 492.22 → 571.17 (**+16.0%**) |
| S1 (single, 8 req) | 221.60 → 207.73 (−6.3%) | 188.24 → 178.92 (−5.0%) |
| Long S1 (8k prompt, single) | 229.81 → 217.44 (−5.4%) | 160.07 → 155.24 (−3.0%) |

The win comes from removing per-step HBM traffic that scales with T:
two standalone `mhc_post_tilelang` runs with full `[T,4,H]` writes plus one
`[T,4H]` bf16 copy (~256 MiB of traffic at T=4096). Concurrent steps have
large T and tight HBM, so the wall-clock throughput gains the most (C8
system +16.0%); single-stream decode steps are only ~8 tokens wide, so
nothing is left to save and the small extra `mean` kernel noise shows up
(S1/Long S1 within run-to-run variance, 3 runs per scenario, not an SLA).
TTFT is unchanged (these paths are not on the first-token critical path).
Resident memory is unchanged (the buffer allocation is kept; only the copy
is skipped).

## Why

For DSpark, the aux hidden states (draft `main_proj` inputs) are the
mean-pooled post residuals `[T, hc, H] → [T, H]` of layers 40/41. The old
code ran a standalone `mhc_post_tilelang` for every aux layer even though
the next layer's fused post already produces the exact same post residual.
It also kept the full `[T, hc, H]` MTP buffer copy alive although DSpark
consumes aux states (which are `torch.cat` + `main_proj`), never that
buffer.

## What

- `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.forward` gains an optional `capture_previous_aux`
  flag; when the *current* layer is an aux layer, the `mean(dim=1)` of the
  fused post residual is captured instead of running a standalone
  `mhc_post_tilelang` for the previous layer.
- The last layer keeps its standalone `mhc_post_tilelang` because
  `hc_head` still needs the full `[T, hc, H]` residual (it also feeds the
  final aux entry).
- The `_mtp_hidden_buffer` copy and the runner's MTP-buffer read are
  skipped when aux hidden states are present (dummy run and real propose
  path).

## Tests

- `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py`: `.mean(dim=1)` of the fused-post
  residual now matches the reference (4 passed: T ∈ {1,4,8,128}).
- Stability on the internal 4×H20 deployment (v0.28 line): HTTP warmup
  failures=0, DSpark FULL CUDA-Graph captured (80 s, 11.34 GiB/rank),
  bench errors 0/11 runs after / 0/11 before.

> Baseline note: the numbers above were measured on the internal
> vLLM-MoE fork (v0.28 line); this branch is a source-level port to
> current main and GPU revalidation there is pending.

## Duplicate check

GitHub PR search (`aux hidden`, `mhc post`, `DeepSeek-V4`) returns no
existing PR addressing this change.

---
AI assistance was used in preparing this change (see Co-authored-by
trailer in the commit).

title: [ROCm][MLA] Serve non-causal multi-token decode on the AITER ASM path
body:
## Purpose

DSpark's draft emits a **non-causal** multi-token block: every query token in the block attends the same KV range. The AITER MLA backend had no way to express that, so such a block was refused and the group fell back to Triton.

### What changed since the first revision

The first revision of this PR threaded `is_causal=False` into `get_mla_metadata_v1`, on the theory that the decode kernel takes its causality from the work metadata. **It does not.** The persistent kernel masks causally whatever that flag says, so the block came back causally masked while the backend advertised non-causal support. I found this with a direct A/B against a plain-PyTorch reference and moved the PR to draft; that mechanism is gone now.

The smallest case where the two causalities differ visibly is `qlen=2`, `seq_len=10`, where causal gives row 0 nine KV positions and non-causal gives it ten:

| row 0 vs | `is_causal=True` | `is_causal=False` |
|---|---|---|
| causal reference | **2.32e-02** | **2.32e-02** |
| non-causal reference | 4.83e-01 | 4.83e-01 |

Both builds compute the causal answer. (This is also why an end-to-end run cannot catch it: at a 128k context the two differ by one KV position in 131072.)

### The mechanism now

Serve the block at `qseqlen=1`. `seq_lens` already spans the verify block, so a request's ordinary paged-KV view *is* exactly the range every row needs. Issuing one `qseqlen=1` decode per query position hands each row that untruncated range, and at `qseqlen=1` there is no intra-block position left to mask, so causality never enters the result — it is non-causal by construction rather than by asking the kernel for it.

Same harness, same references, this time on the `qseqlen=1` split:

| | vs non-causal reference | vs causal reference |
|---|---|---|
| rows 0 and 1 | **2.27e-02** | 4.77e-01 |

The cost is one pass over the KV range per query position, which is the traffic a per-row expanded page list would have moved, without needing a `qlen`-fold page-index buffer.

### Guards

- **Gluon small-head verify** and **segmented DCP verify** both apply their causal bound in-kernel and have no way to express the untruncated range. A non-causal block is now rejected on both — in the builder, and again in `forward_mqa`. Previously, enabling non-causal support silently routed such a block through the segmented DCP path, which builds causally bounded rows and calls the kernel with `causal=True`.
- Non-causal DCP stays off: `supports_non_causal_multi_token_dcp` is left `False`, so the shared layer refuses it with a clear error.
- `CommonAttentionMetadata.causal` is `bool | torch.Tensor` and is now reduced through a helper rather than tested directly — a tensor of all-false is truthy, and `bool()` on a multi-element one raises. The helper agrees with the shared MLA builder, which selects its non-causal route with `causal is False` and therefore never selects it for a tensor, and refuses a tensor that *does* ask for non-causal attention rather than quietly masking it.

## Test Plan

1. `tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_non_causal.py` (new) pins both halves of the mechanism on gfx950: that `is_causal` does not reach the mask, and that the `qseqlen=1` split produces non-causal attention.
2. End-to-end: Kimi-K3 (MXFP4, TP8) with the Kimi-K3-DSpark MTP draft on one MI355X node, concurrency 1, ISL 131072 / OSL 1024, fp8 KV on both target and draft. Only the draft's `attention_backend` differs between arms. Three repeats per arm, interleaved.

## Test Result

`test_rocm_aiter_mla_non_causal.py` passes on MI355X (gfx950), stable across repeated cold-container runs.

**End-to-end, 3 repeats per arm (`num_speculative_tokens=2`):**

| draft backend | p90 ITL (ms) | mean TPOT (ms) | output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TRITON_MLA` (before this PR) | 31.99 / 32.26 / 32.23 | 13.44 avg | 33.9 avg |
| `ROCM_AITER_MLA`, non-causal `qseqlen=1` | **29.43 / 29.44 / 29.48** | 12.24 avg | 35.6 avg |

**8.4% p90 ITL improvement** and **+5.1% output throughput**, with a spread of ±0.15 ms on the Triton arm and ±0.03 ms on the aiter arm, so the gap is far outside the noise.

**Where it comes from** (rank-0 torch trace, 6 decode passes, 5 draft layers), draft attention kernels plus their MLA reduce:

| draft route | launches / pass | ms / pass |
|---|---|---|
| Triton (`_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1` + `_fwd_kernel_stage2`) | 5 | 2.02 |
| asm `qseqlen=1` x2 (this PR) | 10 | 0.61 |
| asm `qseqlen=2` (the withdrawn causal mechanism) | 5 | 0.33 |

The ASM path is 3.3x cheaper than Triton on the draft even paying for one launch per query position. Note the last row: the withdrawn mechanism had the cheapest attention of the three and yet measured **32.49 ms p90 ITL** — no end-to-end gain over Triton at all. So the earlier 9.1% figure in this PR's original description does not reproduce, and the correct mechanism is also the faster one.

### Caveats I would not want a reviewer to miss

- **The gain depends on spec depth.** This replay issues one decode per query position, so its cost scales with the block length, while Triton reads the KV range once for the whole block. The numbers above are at `num_speculative_tokens=2`. At depth 6 the replay costs ~6 passes per draft layer and the win should shrink, possibly to nothing. Deep-spec deployments should measure before adopting.
- **Attribution is incomplete.** The attention saving I can account for in the trace is ~1.4 ms/pass, but the ITL improvement works out to ~3.4 ms/pass, and the withdrawn arm had cheaper attention with zero gain. The measurement is reproducible; my explanation of *why* is not complete, so I would treat the 8.4% as the result and not attach a mechanism claim to it.
- **Which code was measured.** The three-repeat A/B ran on a vendor image whose MLA backend predates this file's current layout, carrying an equivalent change that routes the same way (`qseqlen=1` per query position). This exact diff applies cleanly to a build tracking `upstream/main` and is running there now on 8x MI355X: patch applied, FULL cudagraph capture completed, server healthy, serving at `num_speculative_tokens=6` with no faults. I will follow up with that arm's numbers, which also settle the spec-depth question above.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Take the AITER MLA KV dtype from the group, not cache_config
body:
## Purpose

`AiterMLAMetadataBuilder` derives its KV dtype from the global `cache_config.cache_dtype`, but the cache dtype is a per-KV-cache-group property. A speculative draft model may run `kv_cache_dtype: "auto"` (so a bf16 cache) under a server started with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`.

The builder then normalizes that group to `"fp8"` and, from it, sizes the persistent work metadata via `get_mla_metadata_info_v1` and selects the fp8 asm decode kernels — against a cache that is actually bf16. The kernel reads the buffer at the wrong element size and the decode faults:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-N (Agent handle: ...) on address ...
Reason: Unknown.
```

This only reproduces once the persistent asm decode actually runs, i.e. under cudagraph capture. In eager the same group takes the Gluon path, so the mismatch stays hidden — which makes it awkward to diagnose: the model runs fine until graphs are enabled.

The fix defers to the group's own `kv_cache_spec.dtype` whenever it is unquantized, so the normalized string, `q_dtype`, `kv_dtype` and the metadata sizing all describe the buffer the kernel will actually read. A group whose cache really is fp8 is unaffected: its spec dtype is not a float type, so the new condition does not fire.

## Test Plan

MI355X (gfx950), Kimi-K3 + a DSpark MTP draft on `ROCM_AITER_MLA`, TP8, server started with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` while the draft's speculative config leaves `kv_cache_dtype: "auto"`. Started the server with `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` cudagraphs.

## Test Result

Before: every one of the 8 ranks hit a memory access fault during PIECEWISE capture, reproducibly at the same capture step.

After: PIECEWISE and FULL capture both complete to 100% with no faults, and the server serves normally.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

title: [Bug][Spec Decode] GLM-5.3 (non-Flash) MTP: draft acceptance ~1-2% pos-0 even on repetitive text — draft head effectively emits noise (2 nightlies, 2 backends, graphs+eager)
body:
## Summary

Enabling MTP speculative decoding for **zai-org/GLM-5.3** (non-Flash, official FP8 checkpoint) via `--speculative-config.method mtp` produces catastrophically low draft acceptance — **position-0 acceptance ≤2.4% on maximally-predictable repetitive text**, where a healthy MTP head scores 60-80%. Throughput drops 29-41% vs non-MTP. The draft head behaves like it is emitting noise.

## Environment

- 8x NVIDIA B300 (sm_103), driver 580.173.02 (CUDA 13.0), TP=8
- vLLM nightlies **0.28.1rc1.dev380+g25268f0c9** and **0.28.1rc1.dev455+gdd0760165** (identical results)
- torch 2.13.0+cu132, flashinfer 0.6.18
- Model: local snapshot of zai-org/GLM-5.3 (FP8, 141 shards). Arch resolves to `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`; with MTP the draft resolves to `DeepseekV32MTPModel`.
- Serve flags: `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 131072 --max-num-seqs 256` (+ variations below)

## Evidence matrix (all combinations broken identically)

| wheel | attention backend | graphs | num_spec_tokens | dataset | accept rate | pos-0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dev380 | FLASHMLA_SPARSE | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | 5 | random 8k/1k | 8.85% | 18.4% |
| dev380 | FLASHMLA_SPARSE | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | 5 | prefix_repetition | 0.94% | 2.3% |
| dev455 | FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | 5 | random 8k/1k | 8.69% | 18.6% |
| dev455 | FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | 5 | prefix_repetition | 0.62% | 1.68% |
| dev455 | FLASHMLA_SPARSE | **enforce-eager** | **1** | prefix_repetition | 2.41% | 2.41% |

Notes:
- Acceptance on **repetitive text is WORSE than on random tokens** — backwards for any functioning draft head.
- The eager + MTP-1 row eliminates CUDA-graph/dispatch effects and the multi-pass rerun of the single MTP layer: the corruption is present at the proposer level itself.
- Non-MTP output quality is normal in all configs (served + benchmarked extensively; e.g. 2030 tok/s output @128-concurrency on dev455).

## Checkpoint verification

- `config.json`: `num_nextn_predict_layers: 1`, `num_hidden_layers: 78`, **`index_share_for_mtp_iteration: true`**
- MTP tensors present in the checkpoint: `model.layers.78.eh_proj.weight`, `.enorm.weight`, `.hnorm.weight` (+ layer-78 block) in `model-00136-of-00141.safetensors`
- `index_share_for_mtp_iteration` is detected by `v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/mtp/speculator.py` / `v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py` in these wheels — but given the DSA sparse-indexer coupling, the non-Flash GLM-5.3 path is a prime suspect (indexer state for draft iterations, or draft-weight processing under FP8 block-scale).

## Related

- #55239 fixed the same *symptom class* for GLM-5.3-**Flash** on ROCm (spec verification rows mis-dispatched → corrupted output); after that fix they report **62.7% weighted acceptance** and MTP5 faster than baseline — a healthy reference this model family can reach. Our eager-mode result suggests the non-Flash NVIDIA issue is not (only) dispatch, however.
- #55357 reports another 0%-acceptance episode (Qwen family) on recent nightlies.

## Repro

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --speculative-config.method mtp --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 1 \
  --enforce-eager --max-model-len 131072
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --base-url http://localhost:8000 --model zai-org/GLM-5.3 \
  --dataset-name prefix_repetition --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 1024 \
  --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 512 --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 24 \
  --prefix-repetition-output-len 256 --num-prompts 96 --max-concurrency 16
# → Speculative Decoding block: acceptance ~2% at position 0
```

Happy to run further diagnostics on this hardware if useful.

title: [ROCm] Sparse-MLA decode top-k falls back to the vLLM kernel above 64k because of an aiter 0.1.19 limitation
body:
**[ROCm] Sparse-MLA decode top-k falls back to the vLLM kernel above 64k
because of an aiter 0.1.19 limitation**

`vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` disables the AITER top-k
kernel for decode:

```python
if not is_prefill:
    # AITER v0.1.19 decode is one-block only. This measured gfx950
    # FP32/k=1024 compressed-row boundary is independent of the native
    # split-count boundary in sampler.cu.
    if (
        num_rows <= _GFX950_C4A_NATIVE_MAX_ROWS            # 256
        and max_valid_seq_len > _GFX950_C4A_AITER_MAX_COMPRESSED_SEQ_LEN  # 64 KiB
    ):
        return None
```

The comment states the limitation is specific to **aiter v0.1.19**. On
**0.1.21.post1** the AITER kernel handles these shapes and is faster.

**Measured** (MI355X / gfx950, ROCm 7.2.3, aiter 0.1.21.post1, 40 rows —
that is 8 concurrent requests × MTP-5 — `topk=2048`, FP32 logits; three
repeats, median, 8 warm-up calls, synchronised timing windows):

| context | `torch.ops._C` (current path) | `aiter.ops.topk` | delta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 65 536 | 0.0505 ms | 0.0383 ms | **−24.1 %** |
| 131 072 | 0.0785 ms | 0.0624 ms | **−20.5 %** |

Both kernels select the **identical set** of indices — 100 % overlap on the
checked row, so this is not a precision trade-off.

Note the condition also has a somewhat counter-intuitive shape: it disables
AITER precisely for **small** batches (`num_rows <= 256`) at long context,
which is the low-concurrency long-context case — exactly where per-token
latency matters most to a user.

Suggestion: gate on the installed aiter version rather than unconditionally,
or drop the branch once 0.1.21 is the floor. Happy to run any variant on
gfx950.

For transparency about the size of the effect: in our deployment this kernel
accounts for ~1.1 % of decode TPOT, so the end-to-end gain is small. The
reason to fix it is that the stated justification no longer holds.

title: [Spec Decode][GLM-5.3] Expose auxiliary hidden states (EAGLE-3 / DFlash) from Glm5Next
body:
## Purpose

DFlash / DFlash2 drafters for GLM-5.3-Flash (e.g. `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2`, `dflash_config.target_layer_ids = [5, 14, 24, 33, 42]`) consume the target's residual stream at a handful of layers, but `Glm5NextForCausalLM` / `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` did not implement the EAGLE-3 auxiliary-hidden-state interface, so `--speculative-config '{"method": "dflash", ...}'` failed at init:

```
RuntimeError: Model does not support EAGLE3 interface but aux_hidden_state_outputs was requested
```

## Change

Implement `SupportsEagle3` / `EagleModelMixin` on `Glm5NextModel` and both model classes.

The value captured at index `i` is the stream **entering** layer `i` (HF `hidden_states[i]`), which is the convention the runner's `+1` mapping of DFlash's `target_layer_ids` expects. GLM-5.3's mHC layers defer the hyper-connection post-mix into the next layer's fused pre-op, so the plain stream is not materialized between layers: the capture applies the previous layer's post-mix (`hc_post`) and contracts the streams (`hc_contract`), exactly as the last layer does before the final norm. Non-mHC layers and the embedding already carry the summed stream. Sequence-parallel runs all-gather the captured value. No change when no aux layers are set.

## Test

2× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), `--tensor-parallel-size 2 --nnodes 2`, GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4, `fp8_ds_mla` KV, `--max-model-len 245760`, `--speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7}'`, together with the drafter KV dtype fix and the GLM-5.3 KV grouping fix (separate PRs, referenced below):

- init passes the interface check and the DFlash2 CUDA graphs capture
- arithmetic gate exact; per-request reasoning-effort levers unchanged
- single-stream decode 25.4 tok/s prose / 56.0 tok/s code (bare: 16.7; MTP ×3: 24.5 / 35.7); prefill 956 tok/s
- keyed long-context probe 15/22 at 8K, same as without a drafter

Related: #53906 (model), #55621 (drafter KV dtype), #55622 (GLM-5.3 KV grouping) — the three together enable DFlash on GLM-5.3-Flash.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Keep the model dtype for regular attention layers under kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla
body:
## Purpose

`fp8_ds_mla` is the packed DeepSeek-MLA cache layout and only MLA layers can use it. When a GQA drafter (EAGLE-3 / DFlash) is loaded next to a DS-MLA target served with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, the drafter's plain `Attention` layers inherit that cache dtype and backend selection fails:

```
ValueError: No valid attention backend found for cuda with AttentionSelectorConfig(head_size=128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla, block_size=256, ...)
```

## Change

In `Attention.__init__`, keep the model dtype for regular attention layers when the requested cache dtype is `fp8_ds_mla` (the same effect as `--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers`, applied automatically where the requested layout cannot apply), with a one-time log line. MLA layers are unaffected.

## Test

GLM-5.3-Flash (`fp8_ds_mla`, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`) + `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` (5 sliding-window GQA layers) on 2× DGX Spark, TP=2: the drafter's layers select FlashAttention with bf16 KV, the engine initializes, arithmetic gate exact, 25.4 / 56.0 tok/s prose / code single-stream decode with the drafter. Without this change the run fails at the selector as above.

Related: #55620 (GLM-5.3 aux hidden states), #55622 (GLM-5.3 KV grouping) — the three together enable DFlash on GLM-5.3-Flash.

title: [Core][GLM-5.3] Carry a GQA drafter's attention layers through the GLM-5.3-Flash KV cache layout
body:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash has a dedicated KV grouping/layout in `kv_cache_utils` (`_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` / `_glm5_next_tensor_layout`) that aliases the MLA, kpool-indexer, tail and KDA state pages into one block layout. It admits only those spec types, so loading a GQA drafter (EAGLE-3 / DFlash) next to the target makes it return `None`; the generic page unification then fails on the indexer cache, which that layout deliberately does not unify:

```
NotImplementedError: Layer language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.indexer.k_cache: page size is not divisible by the maximum page size and cannot be padded. Padding is only supported for non-MLA attention layers.
```

## Change

Carry the drafter's attention layers through the GLM-5.3 path as one more group: its block is shrunk to the largest kernel-granular (multiple of 16) size whose page fits under the MLA page **and that divides the model's block** — with a sliding-window group present the KV cache coordinator only does block-aligned prefix-cache lookups, and a non-dividing block never lines up with a cached prefix (measured: 0% hit rate, every request re-prefilled) — and the page is padded to exactly the MLA page; the layout recognizer returns the group, and the three consumers (bytes per block, tensor allocation, max-memory accounting) size, allocate and count it. No change without a drafter.

The drafter's group is flagged `is_eagle_group` when the speculative config uses the EAGLE last-block drop. Left unflagged, the KV cache coordinator flags **every** group, which widens the Mamba groups' lookup window past what align-mode checkpointing produces and silently drops prefix-cache reuse to zero (`_warn_if_unannotated_eagle_mamba` describes this) — measured as a 0% hit rate on a repeated 37K-token prefix before this flag. Foreign attention layers are only treated as a drafter when a speculative config is set; the padded-page fit is applied on CUDA only (backends with a fixed set of kernel block sizes cannot run a padded page without kernel block splitting); the fitted block is a multiple of the drafter spec's own block; a drafter group with no layers on a PP rank is not charged in the max-memory accounting.

## Test

GLM-5.3-Flash (`fp8_ds_mla`, kpool indexer, KDA) + `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` (5 sliding-window GQA layers) on 2× DGX Spark, TP=2, `--max-model-len 245760`: the engine initializes with 397,776 KV tokens (1.62× concurrency), DFlash2 CUDA graphs capture, arithmetic gate exact, keyed long-context probe unchanged, 25.4 / 56.0 tok/s prose / code single-stream decode. Without this change the run fails as above (and without a drafter the layout is byte-identical to before). A unit test in `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py` covers the grouping, the block fit/alignment, the tensor allocation and the memory accounting with a 5-layer GQA drafter next to the GLM-5.3-like fixture.

Related: #55620 (GLM-5.3 aux hidden states), #55621 (drafter KV dtype) — the three together enable DFlash on GLM-5.3-Flash.

title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash: CUDA illegal memory access in FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA backend under TP+EP and MTP decoding on H20 (vLLM nightly 260904)
body:
### Your current environment

- **GPUs**: 8x NVIDIA H20 (SM90)
- **vLLM**: nightly image `vllm-nightly-260904`
  - Custom image: `mirrors.tencent.com/abo/nvidia-serve:vllm-nightly-260904`
  - Base image: `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:f5df5cc3302b5f404848c4eca88d7bf7ed5226e151c056da22816d7734644d67`
  - Upstream commit: `8a728663c1c3eeace834a95f5654fa653cc1998c` (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/8a728663c1c3eeace834a95f5654fa653cc1998c)
- **Python**: 3.12.3
- **PyTorch**: 2.13.0+cu130
- **CUDA**: Toolkit 13.0.2, Runtime 13.0.96-1
- **Model**: GLM-5.3-Flash 

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Summary

Serving **GLM-5.3-Flash** on **8x NVIDIA H20** with vLLM nightly (`260904`). One engine worker (`Worker_TP2_EP2`) aborted with `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` while building attention metadata inside the **FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA** backend (`flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py`, called from `mamba_hybrid.py prepare_attn`). The fault is reported at a host-side sync point (`positions[:num_rows].cpu()`), so the actual faulting kernel is likely earlier in the async stream, not necessarily the FlashInfer path itself.

### Serving config (EXTRA_PARAMS)

```
--enable-expert-parallel
--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune
--tool-call-parser glm47
--enable-auto-tool-choice
--reasoning-parser glm45
--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'
```

Load: input/output length 65536, batch_size 32 (crash observed mid-serving on a normal chat completion request).

### Error / stack trace (worker log, 2026-09-04 15:47:46)

```
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
Search for 'cudaErrorIllegalAddress' in https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html
CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call, so the stacktrace below might be incorrect.
For debugging consider passing CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 1047, in _execute_worker_rpc
    output = func(*args, **kwargs)
  ...
  File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py", line 348, in _kv_lens_host
    ctx = positions[:num_rows].cpu().to(torch.int64) + 1
  File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py", line 378, in build
    num_rows, kv_lens = self._kv_lens_host(common_attn_metadata)
  File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py", line 336, in build_attn_metadata
    attn_metadata = build_attn_metadata(...)
  File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py", line 311, in prepare_attn
    attn_metadata = self.model_state.prepare_attn(...)
  File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 1677, in execute_model
    output = self.model_runner.execute_model(...)
  File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 1177, in execute_model
    output = self.worker.execute_model(scheduler_output)
  File "vllm/v1/worker/worker_base.py", line 375, in execute_model
    ...
```

### Expected behavior

No illegal memory access; engine keeps serving under TP+EP + MTP speculative decoding.

### Questions / info we can still provide

Happy to run with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, and to bisect with EP off / MTP off / prefix-caching off, and to report actual attention block size + kpool indexer page size. Please tell us what diagnostics would help most.

### Related issues checked (not duplicates)

- **#55221** – same backend file (`flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py`) on CUDA TP2, but different symptom (fp8 KV dtype rejected by `plan()` + indexer prefill workspace sizing), no runtime illegal memory access.
- **#55280** – GLM-5.3-Flash hybrid `block_size=1152` -> 32-entry paged-MQA GPU memory fault on MTP decode, but ROCm/gfx942 only; no CUDA reproduction reported. Possibly the same family of hybrid KV-geometry issue; we are checking our `block_size` / `index_kpool` geometry.
- **#53142** – hybrid Mamba align precopy illegal memory access on prefix-cache resume (`mamba-cache-mode=align`): demonstrates that an async CUDA fault can surface later inside an attention backend. We have not confirmed whether our deployment uses `--enable-prefix-caching` / align mode.
- **#55279** – deterministic CUDA IMA in DFlash2 spec decode; different decode method and GPU.

title: [Model] Mamba2: Bit-identical prefill and decode under batch-invariant mode
body:
> **Conflict synchronization — October 15, 2026:** Head `55528ee70602873dcd9a9183aaf0e76fa4cfd589`, tree `8f8cd97b30df4102b125cd175e295ad9352e4c15`, incorporates main `c5f8adc0` and the updated stack dependencies through merge commits. The Mamba checkpoint length fix from main is retained. Existing PR history is preserved. The maintainer's Mamba2 RFC/hold remains in effect; this update does not request re-review.
>
> Codex performed the synchronization and checks. Historical GB200/model results and first-person human statements below remain attributed to their original revisions. Fresh human review and personal test execution of this synchronization are not attested.

### October 15 validation

**This branch:** 10 existing exact-replay/attention tests passed, plus one audit-only assertion confirming `AttentionCGSupport.NEVER` (11 total).

The `False-0-64` emit failure was reproduced on the untouched original `fc697366` at the same position 180 (chunk 2, offset 52). The emit implementation, test and six supporting kernel/helper files are byte-identical between that original, pre-sync `cda097cb` and the synchronized downstream tree. Only this one failure has a before/after negative control; the other 16 failures are not declared pre-existing. Two downstream model determinism attempts failed during EngineCore initialization because this source-only checkout lacks the build-generated `vllm.third_party.flashmla.flash_mla_interface`; they did not reach numerical assertions.

All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks passed on 13 files, including mypy targeting the oldest supported Python version. Each run exited 0 with no source modifications or blocked hook environments. The newly triggered upstream pre-commit run remains blocked by contributor eligibility; these local results are independent of upstream CI. PR-scope whitespace, Python syntax and Ruff checks passed.

Focused pytest selections:

```text
tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_exact_replay.py
tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_ssd_emit.py
tests/v1/attention/test_mamba2_batch_invariant.py
tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_mixer2.py -k "batch_invariant or fallback"
tests/v1/determinism/test_mamba2_batch_invariance.py
```

Execution used `uv run --no-project ~/vllm-run/.venv/bin/python <audit>/run-native-overlay-tests.py --candidate <checkout> --report <report> -- <pytest selection>`, with `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1`, offline model cache and a strict native-only import finder propagated to subprocesses. Candidate Python source was verified with zero installed-source fallback. WSL2/Python 3.12.3, RTX 4060 Laptop (SM89, 8 GiB), Torch 2.13.0+cu132 and Triton 3.7.1 were used. Reused native extensions come from installed baseline `cb6458c5`; current main requires Torch 2.14.0. This is partial local regression evidence, not a current-main native build, final model-output validation, multi-GPU validation or an upstream CI success.

## Purpose

Second half of the split of this PR: #57539 adds the exact-replay SSD step and its metadata; this PR wires them into the Mamba2 backend. Tracked in #55524.

Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, a Mamba2 layer should produce the same bits for a token whether it is computed in prefill, in a chunked-prefill continuation or in decode. Today prefill runs the chunked scan and decode the single-token update, which round differently, so a token's logprob depends on how the scheduler split the sequence. That defeats the purpose of the mode for RL, where a trainer rescores the rollout through prefill.

With this PR, in batch-invariant mode:

- The SSM state is kept in fp32 and the layer state gains three per-sequence buffers with the inputs of the current partial chunk (x, dt, B), through the shared state shape and dtype calculators, so every model built on `MambaMixer2` gets it without per-model changes.
- The Mamba2 attention metadata builder produces the replay metadata for the prefill and decode rows of each step, and the mixer runs the replayed step from #57539 instead of the chunked scan and the single-token update.
- Unsupported settings are rejected at startup: prefix caching on the Mamba2 layers, PP > 1, speculative decoding, micro-batching, KV connectors and the non-Triton mamba backend. Tensor parallelism works; the gated RMSNorm's TP path for a single group reduces per-rank means in fp32, because batch-invariant mode overrides `mean` but not `sum` (#54993 touches the same lines).
- The Mamba2 layers run outside CUDA graphs in this mode; #55905 brings them back.

Default mode is untouched. Costs: each decode step runs the chunked-scan kernels over the partial chunk instead of the single-token update, the per-layer state grows from two tensors to five (about 43 MiB per sequence for a 27-layer, 32-head model at chunk size 256), and decode throughput on small models drops to roughly a tenth. #55905 recovers most of that, and #55895 pins the kernels' tiles so the bits also match across processes.

Not a duplicate: #54993 aligns the scheduler's chunking and replays the generated history through the SSU kernel on recovery, so it gives decode == recompute while decode stays on SSU. This PR gives decode == single-shot prefill.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mamba2_batch_invariant.py
pytest tests/v1/determinism/test_mamba2_batch_invariance.py
```

Engine-level oracle, out of tree: tokens are forced through a logits processor so every run realizes the same trajectory, then each generated token's raw logprob is compared bit for bit with its raw logprob in a single-shot prefill of prompt plus generation.

## Test Result

GB200, TP1 unless noted, on the final commit.

- Unit tests: 7 cases for the state layout and the startup checks, plus the engine-level determinism test.
- mamba2-130m, 8 concurrent requests, prompts of 37 to 1000 tokens, 60 to 300 generated tokens: 0 of 3666 prefill and 0 of 1190 decode positions differ, with and without `max_num_batched_tokens=100`, CUDA graphs on. With the mode off, 1182 of 1190 differ.
- granite-4.0-h-350m with `num_gpu_blocks_override=33`, so one request is preempted and recomputed: 0 of 1859 and 0 of 5750, with CUDA graphs and eager. Mode off: 5746 of 5750.
- Nemotron-H-8B-Base-8K: 0 of 1859 and 0 of 5750 at TP1 and at TP2.
- An earlier revision of this change also passed the determinism test on H100 NVL, posted in this thread.
- pre-commit passes on the changed files.

## AI assistance

AI tools assisted with the implementation, tests and documentation. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bug] DeepSeek V4 sparse MLA can index a nonexistent block-table row during CUDA-graph warmup
body:
### Summary

I found a separate DeepSeek-V4 sparse-MLA bounds bug while debugging a TP=2 CUDA illegal-address failure.

During CUDA-graph warmup, `CommonAttentionMetadata.token_to_req_indices()` can generate a request index that has no corresponding row in `block_table`. The downstream Triton mapper, `_compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens_kernel`, trusts `req_idx` and performs a block-table gather without checking `req_idx < block_table.shape[0]`.

In the captured failing state:

```text
block_table.shape[0] = 1
token_to_req_indices.min() = 0
token_to_req_indices.max() = 1
```

so request row `1` is invalid. In the full serving run this surfaced under `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` as `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` in `_compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens_kernel` on both TP ranks. A tiny standalone repro did not always fault: it returned a silent wrong KV slot instead, which makes this a correctness issue as well as a crash issue.

### Environment

- 2x NVIDIA DGX Spark / GB10, TP=2
- vLLM `0.25.2.dev0+g752a3a504.d20260714`
- Triton 3.6.0
- PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130
- CUDA driver 580.173.02
- DeepSeek-V4 Flash sparse MLA prefill path

I also checked current `vllm-project/vllm` main at `1f778486fc313f3599a6b59e67f65b1c186477fd`: the consumer path still has only the lower-bound validity check for `local_idx`; there is no request-row bound in the gather.

### Production failure

With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, the first synchronous failure was:

```text
Triton _compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens_kernel
vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/cache_utils.py
via sparse MLA prefill
Triton Error [CUDA]: illegal memory access
```

Both TP ranks failed at the same point. Vision/aligner/merge synchronization points had already passed, and NCCL only saw the sticky CUDA error afterward.

### Producer bug

The bad metadata comes from:

```text
vllm/v1/attention/backend.py
CommonAttentionMetadata.token_to_req_indices
```

The mapping is built from the request/query count (`arange(query_lens.shape[0])`) without proving that this cardinality matches `block_table.shape[0]` during synthetic CUDA-graph warmup.

Observed invariant break:

```text
query/request slots represented by token_to_req_indices: 2
block_table rows: 1
```

The prefill path then passes the unsliced block table into the sparse MLA global-top-k mapping.

The producer fix should preserve the logical request-row contract rather than clamp an invalid request index onto another request's KV row. Depending on CUDA-graph padding semantics, that likely means making the synthetic request metadata and block-table row count consistent, slicing to the real request count, and failing closed when the invariant is violated.

### Consumer memory-safety bug

The Triton consumer should defensively validate both dimensions before the block-table gather:

```text
0 <= req_idx < block_table_rows
0 <= block_indices < block_table_stride
```

Invalid entries should map to `-1` and be excluded from `topk_lens`.

There is related local hardening in `jasl/vllm@d64074e6f07250f6cd072861aa3c389a929befb9`, which adds the column bound:

```text
block_indices < block_table_stride
```

That is useful but insufficient for this case because it does not bound `req_idx`. With `rows=1, req_idx=1`, that patch alone still permits a read from a nonexistent request row.

### Minimal repro result

I built a standalone test with:

```text
block_table rows = 1
token_to_req_indices = [0, 1]
```

Results:

- safe reference implementation: detects row 1 as OOB
- stock Triton kernel: on the tiny synthetic case, no CUDA exception, but token 1 maps to a wrong slot instead of being rejected
- dual-bound hardened kernel: matches the reference, token 1 -> `-1`, invalid entry excluded from the length

So the same missing row bound can manifest as either silent wrong KV mapping or a hard illegal-address depending on geometry/runtime state.

### Regression coverage prepared

I have two focused regression tests ready:

1. metadata producer test for a CUDA-graph-warmup-like shape where query/request slots exceed block-table rows
2. Triton row+column bounds test covering both:
   - invalid `req_idx`
   - invalid `block_indices`

Both pass with the proposed producer + consumer hardening in a disposable GPU environment.

### Relation to #49896

Related but distinct from #49896.

#49896 demonstrated a different producer failure: bad/garbage local top-k indices can reach this same mapper and make it read past a block-table row. This report is the orthogonal dimension: an invalid **request row index** can make the mapper select a row that does not exist at all.

Both point to the same general requirement: the global-top-k mapper should defend both the request-row dimension and the block-within-row dimension.

I can submit the two-layer patch and regression tests if this direction looks right.

title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA can index past block-table rows during CUDA-graph warmup
body:
### Summary

We found a distinct DeepSeek-V4 sparse-MLA metadata bug where CUDA-graph warmup can produce a request index that is outside the number of rows in the block table. The downstream Triton mapper does not bound `req_idx`, so the same bad metadata can become either a silent wrong KV-slot mapping or, at full serving geometry, a CUDA illegal memory access that kills all TP ranks.

This is related to, but distinct from, #49896. That issue demonstrates bad local top-k indices reaching `compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens`; this report is about an out-of-range **request-row index**.

### Environment

Observed on:

- 2x NVIDIA DGX Spark GB10, TP=2
- vLLM `0.25.2.dev0+g752a3a504.d20260714`
- Triton 3.6.0
- PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130
- NVIDIA driver 580.173.02
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash Vision-Exp serving path
- sparse MLA prefill / `compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens`

Current vLLM `main` was also checked during preparation and still lacks a `req_idx < block_table.shape[0]` guard in this path.

### Production symptom

With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, the first synchronous failure was:

```text
Triton Error [CUDA]: illegal memory access
_compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens_kernel
vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/cache_utils.py
via sparse MLA prefill
```

Both TP ranks failed, followed by EngineCore/API death. Earlier synchronization points after the vision encoder, aligner, and merge path all completed cleanly, so this failure was localized to post-merge model execution.

### Proven invariant violation

Immediately before the failing Triton launch during CUDA-graph warmup:

```text
block_table.shape[0] = 1
token_to_req_indices.min = 0
token_to_req_indices.max = 1
```

Therefore valid request rows were only:

```text
0 <= req_idx < 1
```

but the metadata contained `req_idx = 1`.

The producer is `CommonAttentionMetadata.token_to_req_indices` in `vllm/v1/attention/backend.py`, which constructs request indices from `arange(query_lens.shape[0])` without proving that the number of query slots matches `block_table.shape[0]`. In the failing CUDA-graph warmup shape, those cardinalities diverged.

The sparse-prefill caller then passed the unsliced `attn_metadata.block_table` into `compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens`.

### Consumer safety bug

The downstream Triton kernel computes a block-table pointer from both a request-row selector and a column/block selector.

The effective safety contract needs both dimensions bounded:

```text
0 <= req_idx < block_table_rows
0 <= block_indices < block_table_stride
```

Existing local hardening such as `jasl/vllm@d64074e` adds only the second condition (`block_indices < block_table_stride`). That is useful but insufficient for this row-OOB case.

### Minimal repro result

A standalone disposable-GPU repro was built with:

```text
block_table rows = 1
token_to_req_indices = [0, 1]
```

Results:

- safe reference detects the out-of-range request row
- stock Triton did **not** throw on the tiny synthetic shape, but returned a silent wrong slot for the invalid token
- a dual-bound hardened kernel returned `-1` for the invalid request row and matched the safe reference
- the full serving workload produced `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` at the same kernel

So this is not only a crash-safety problem: depending on geometry, the same missing row bound can silently read the wrong KV mapping.

### Root cause

There are two separate defects:

1. **Producer correctness bug**: CUDA-graph warmup metadata can describe more request slots than there are block-table rows.
2. **Consumer memory-safety bug**: the Triton mapper trusts `req_idx` and does not bound the request-row dimension before the gather.

Clamping `req_idx` onto an existing row would be incorrect because it could map one request onto another request's KV row.

### Proposed fix direction

Producer side:

- make the request-slot count and block-table row count an explicit invariant
- construct `token_to_req_indices` from the real request-row count
- when CUDA-graph padding requires synthetic slots, pad/slice the block table and validity metadata consistently
- fail closed on impossible cardinality mismatches rather than clamping one request onto another row

Consumer side:

- pass the block-table row count to `compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens`
- require both:
  - `0 <= req_idx < block_table_rows`
  - `0 <= block_indices < block_table_stride`
- invalid entries should become `-1` and must not contribute to `topk_lens`

### Regression coverage prepared

We prepared separate tests for:

1. CUDA-graph-warmup-like metadata where query-slot count exceeds block-table rows
2. Triton request-row OOB (`req_idx >= block_table_rows`)
3. Triton block-column OOB (`block_indices >= block_table_stride`)

The draft fixes pass the prepared metadata tests and disposable-GPU Triton tests.

I can provide the minimal repro / patch draft if useful.

title: [Perf][DSpark] KV-only context insert and fused kv_norm
body:
## Summary

DSpark context-KV write is now 1× KV-only GEMM + 3× fused `kv_norm`+RoPE+quant+insert on the default `fp8_ds_mla` (uint8) path, instead of 3× Q+KV GEMM + 3× standalone `kv_norm` + dummy-Q insert. BF16 / e4m3fn caches also drop the dummy query and call the existing full-cache ops with `num_heads_q=0`. The path runs once per request (not serving tok/s).

**Perf (4×H20, Flash-0731, uint8 / fused WKV on):** kernel **4.7x–4.9x** at every N, including 512. Engine long-prompt write **~4.2x**.

| N | Before (ms) | After (ms) | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 128 | 0.540 | 0.112 | **4.83x** |
| 512 | 0.545 | 0.112 | **4.85x** |
| 2048 | 0.791 | 0.168 | **4.71x** |
| 8192 | 2.597 | 0.554 | **4.69x** |

Engine `precompute_and_store_context_kv` (TP4+EP, median of 8): 2048 → **4.19x**, 8191 → **4.17x**. Do not report engine N=512 as a speedup; that before-arm median is bimodal.

## Why

After target prefill, DSpark writes sliding-window context KV for every draft layer from the same `main_x`. Each layer today:

- runs fused `wq_a|wkv` and discards the Q slice;
- allocates a dummy query so insert can reuse the Q+KV fused kernel (65 warps/token instead of 1);
- launches a standalone `kv_norm` and materializes an `[N, 512]` bf16 buffer that insert immediately rereads.

None of that Q work is consumed on this path. `kv_norm` is also redundant with the insert kernel: the warp already holds the 512-d KV in registers.

## What

- Slice the existing block-FP8 `fused_wqa_wkv` weight/scale at `q_lora_rank`, cat the KV rows across draft layers, and run **one** KV-only GEMM. Compare `fp8_linear` by type (not object identity) so per-layer kernel instances still share that GEMM. Build the KV weight buffer in `process_weights_after_loading`. Incompatible layout falls back to per-layer `fused_wqa_wkv`.
- Add `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_quant_insert` (uint8, 1 warp/token, no dummy Q).
- Add `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_norm_rope_quant_insert`, folding RMSNorm into that kernel with a bf16 round-trip so RoPE sees the same intermediate rounding as the unfused pipeline.
- BF16 / e4m3fn: reuse the existing full-cache ops with `num_heads_q=0` and `apply_q_norm=False` (no dummy-Q allocation).
- Fallbacks: missing fused-norm op → external `kv_norm` + KV-only insert; projection mismatch → per-layer `fused_wqa_wkv`.

## Relationship to existing work

This is **V4-only**. I searched open PRs for `DSpark context KV`, `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_quant_insert`, `kv_norm` insert, and `stacked WKV`.

- [#56441](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56441) is **V4.1-only**: reuses the existing H=0 kernel across cache formats and does **not** change projection or `kv_norm`. Overlap is the uint8 “no dummy Q” goal. This PR additionally adds the fused-norm CUDA ops and the V4 fused-WKV GEMM. Happy to consolidate the overlapping uint8 API if both proceed.
- [#54674](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54674) stacks WKV via `MergedColumnParallelLinear` at load time and **does not change insert or `kv_norm`**. This PR keeps the existing `fused_wqa_wkv` modules, slices+cats their KV blocks for one GEMM, and adds the KV-only / fused-norm CUDA ops. The projection approaches can coexist.
- [#55573](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55573) / [#55575](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55575) touch DSpark/DSv4 logits and aux-hidden capture, not this context-KV write path.

## Tests

```text
python -m pytest --noconftest -v --tb=short \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py
# 181 passed (original suite)

python -m pytest --noconftest -v --tb=short \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py \
  -k "kv_only_insert or kv_norm_fused or h0_matches"
# 34 passed (includes 8 H=0 BF16/FP8 cases)
```

Default DeepSeek-V4 serve is `fp8_ds_mla` (uint8). The follow-up does not make that insert kernel faster; it makes fused WKV actually enable (type compare) and removes dummy-Q on BF16/e4m3fn.

AI assistance was used for implementation and local A/B. I reviewed every changed line and can defend the change end-to-end.

title: [WIP][Model] Add upcoming XingChen4 model support
body:
## Summary

This PR adds native vLLM support for the upcoming **XingChen4** MoE causal model.

XingChen4 reuses the DeepSeek-V2/V3 backbone (MLA attention, MoE block, optional DSA indexer) and replaces the standard residual connection with **Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC)**: the residual stream is expanded into `num_residual_streams` parallel streams mixed by input-dependent, doubly-stochastic matrices produced via Sinkhorn-Knopp projection. The mHC math matches the shared ops in `vllm.model_executor.layers.mhc`, so no private kernels are introduced.
Additionally, this PR enables optional FlagOS/FlagGems acceleration for XingChen4: it enables the hot-path kernels (MoE, attention, softmax, topk, etc.) and brings measurable end-to-end inference speedups — up to 19.87% TTFT and 26.32% TPOT reduction on high-concurrency long-prompt workloads (H100 benchmark), opt-in and disabled by default.

> **Status: Draft.** Model weights are not yet public on Hugging Face Hub. This PR is opened for early code review. Once weights are released, I will:
> 1. add a test entry in `tests/models/registry.py`
> 2. update `docs/models/supported_models.md`
> 3. mark the PR ready for review.

## Changes

1. `vllm/model_executor/models/xingchen4.py`: full model implementation (`XingChen4ForCausalLM`), including forward pass, mHC adapter, and tensor-parallel `load_weights()`.
2. Register `XingChen4ForCausalLM` in `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py` and related `__init__.py`.
3. Reasoning parser (`vllm/reasoning/xingchen4_reasoning_parser.py`) for reasoning-capable variants.
4. Tool parser (`vllm/tool_parsers/xingchen4_tool_parser.py`) for auto tool calling.
5. Register `xingchen4` in `vllm/config/speculative.py`, `vllm/transformers_utils/model_arch_config_convertor.py`, and `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py`.

## Optional FlagGems acceleration (opt-in)

An optional acceleration path is gated behind the env var `USE_FLAGOS=1` (disabled by default). When set, it enables a curated subset of FlagGems kernels via `flag_gems.only_enable(include=[...])`.

> **Scope note:** The acceleration is only enabled from the XingChen4 model path — the flag_gems.only_enable(...) call lives exclusively inside xingchen4.py and is gated behind the env var, so no other model load path triggers it. The whitelist is intentionally narrow (...), and with the env var unset the behavior is fully unchanged. 
 For completeness: only_enable substitutes operators at the PyTorch dispatch level, so once enabled the kernels apply to any op in the same process that matches the whitelist — we therefore consider this an acceleration prototype and welcome feedback on a more scoped kernel backend.

```bash
pip install flagtree==0.6.1 flag-gems==5.3.4 -i https://resource.flagos.net/repository/flagos-pypi-nvidia/simple            # see version constraints in the PR discussion
USE_FLAGOS=1 vllm serve ${model_path} \
    --chat-template ${model_path}/chat_template.jinja \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name $mode_name \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dtype bfloat16 \
    --nnodes 1 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --max-model-len 262144 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --reasoning-parser xingchen4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser xingchen4 \
    --uvicorn-log-level info \
    --enable-log-requests \
    --disable-custom-all-reduce
```

All XingChen4 hot-path tests below run with FlagGems **disabled**.

## Benchmark method (H100 × 1)

- Framework: this branch vs. vanilla vLLM baseline (same branch, env var unset).
- Metric: **TTFT** (time to first token) and **TPOT** (time per output token).
- Workload: cold cache for each (input tokens + output tokens) pair.
- Each run: 5 repetitions, report the **median**; standard deviation in parentheses when ≥ 1%.
- No kernel warmup excluded; results reflect end-to-end served latency.

| input+output | concurrency | vanilla TTFT (ms) | flaggems TTFT (ms) | TTFT Δ | vanilla TPOT (ms) | flaggems TPOT (ms) | TPOT Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50K+500 | 1 | 3965 | 3971 | ~0% | 10 | 10 | ~0% |
| 50K+500 | 10 | 23827 | 23050 | 3.26% | 60 | 62 | ~0% |
| 10K+500 | 1 | 486 | 483 | 0.62% | 8 | 8 | ~0% |
| 10K+500 | 10 | 1439 | 1153 | 19.87% | 38 | 28 | 26.32% |
| 1K+500 | 1 | 98 | 98 | ~0% | 8 | 7 | 12.50% |
| 1K+500 | 10 | 185 | 189 | ~0% | 17 | 17 | ~0% |

**Reading:** gains concentrate in the high-concurrency long-prompt case (10K+500, concurrency=10): ~19.87% TTFT / ~26.32% TPOT. Low-concurrency and short-prompt cases are neutral. The benefit is workload-specific, not universal.

## Test plan (internal non-public checkpoint)

1. Single-GPU: init, weight loading, text generation.
2. Tensor-parallel size=2: weight loading and inference.
3. Generation outputs and logits aligned with the Hugging Face transformers reference implementation (layer-wise comparison, reported in the accompanying notes).
4. FlagGems dual-path: default path (env unset) and accelerated path (env set) both produce consistent outputs/logits.

## Usage
```bash
vllm serve ${model_path} \
    --chat-template ${model_path}/chat_template.jinja \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name $mode_name \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dtype bfloat16 \
    --nnodes 1 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --max-model-len 262144 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --reasoning-parser xingchen4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser xingchen4 \
    --uvicorn-log-level info \
    --enable-log-requests \
    --disable-custom-all-reduce
```

## Known limitations / open items for review

- **mHC checkpoint biases** (`bias_pre` / `bias_post` / `bias_res`) and the `h_res` clamp: currently merged/omitted to match the shared `MHCPreOp` signature. **Please review whether the folded formula is equivalent to the official checkpoint** — this is the main correctness item I need confirmed.
- `_xingchen4_transpose_contiguous` custom op exists to keep `comb_mix` C-contiguous for the TileLang `mhc_post` kernel that torch.compile cannot prove. Happy to simplify if reviewers prefer.
- Pipeline parallelism is not supported in mHC mode (n_streams > 1); tensor parallelism is.

## Checklist

- [x] Model registers and loads (single + TP=2)
- [x] Logit alignment vs HF reference (documented)
- [ ] Test entry in `tests/models/registry.py` (pending weights release)
- [ ] Docs entry in `docs/models/supported_models.md` (pending weights release)
- [ ] CI green

title: [ROCm][CI] Add HY-V4 generation coverage
body:
HY-V4 initialization failed after [#54160](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54160), including in [AMD build 12653](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12653/list?jid=01a070cd-0530-4d60-a5fd-a77dcc439bad&tab=output). [#54404](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54404) supplies sparse-MLA support and [#54405](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54405) restores model initialization, but those initialization tests do not run generation.

- Check finite logprobs and batch/single token agreement, actual graph capture on both workers, and a positive MTP draft count.
- Add a standalone MI300 two-GPU HY generation job in the shared pipeline. Preserve the existing CUDA step exactly, including its commands and three-shard layout; the AMD job has its own key, image dependency and source filters.
- Append the HY TP2 command to the existing unsharded legacy AMD Distributed Models job. Retain its original label and command list, and run the four single-GPU cases only in AMD Basic Models (Other), with source filters covering the model and attention/configuration paths.
- Disable prefix caching so batch/single comparisons each execute prefill. Keep the suite to five cases.

Prepared with AI assistance (OpenAI Codex).

title: [Spec Decode] GLM-5.3-Flash DFlash2 aux hidden-state capture
body:
## Purpose

Enable DFlash2 speculative decoding for GLM-5.3-Flash by implementing aux hidden-state capture on the target model. Related: #55423 (same goal, different aux-materialization path — see below; comment posted there with the structural analysis).

## Problem

#55423 materializes aux states as `hidden + residual`. GLM's mHC residual is a deferred-fusion structure: at each layer boundary the decoder holds a 4-tuple `(x, residual, post, comb)`, and the layer-k output is only completed by `MHCPostOp` (`mhc.py`), whose mixing weights live inside the `post/comb` tensors. A plain `hidden + residual` therefore captures an intermediate state, not the completed output of layer k that the draft was trained against. We believe this may explain the unisolated output divergence reported in #55423.

## Solution

Capture before layer k+1, materializing aux via `hc_post(x, residual, post, comb)` followed by `hc_contract` — structurally identical to the last-layer epilogue. KDA/non-mHC boundaries fall back to `hidden + residual`. Sequence-parallel gather skips the dense stages. The multimodal wrapper (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`, the architecture of the official `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` checkpoint) declares `SupportsEagle3` and delegates to the inner text model, so the protocol unpack through `language_model.model` works natively.

Semantics adapted from SGLang `xinyuan/glm-5.3-flash-support` (#36507/#36708), Apache-2.0.

## Test plan

- [x] New suite `tests/models/glm5next/test_dflash2_aux_capture.py` (9 passed, 2 GPU-gated skipped): bit-exact vs independently materialized fp64 reference, KDA/residual-None fallback, adjacent-boundary enumeration, capture-on/off return shapes, next-layer tuple purity, wrapper `supports_eagle3` flag
- [x] Regression: `tests/models/test_registry.py` (379 passed), glm5next registry imports, `test_dflash_causality.py` (13 passed), mhc kernel + transformer-utils glm5next suites — all green
- [x] E2E on H200 (SM90) TP4: greedy DFlash2 K=7 with `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` is lossless vs non-spec decode reference (teacher-forced NLL parity worst |Δ| = 0.00000)
- [x] FULL_DECODE_ONLY cudagraph capture/replay passes on SM90
- [x] pre-commit hooks (ruff, mypy, spellcheck) all pass

## Known limitations

- DCP > 1 with the draft sliding-window groups is not yet supported (pre-existing coordinator assert)
- `supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp = False` (fails fast rather than silently mis-capturing under PP)
- The hybrid KV-cache layout needs a companion change for the draft SWA groups under `block_size=128` + `fp8_ds_mla` (draft logical block must shrink to fit one MLA slot) — will follow up separately or fold into #55423

title: [Bugfix][Kernel][DSv4/4.1] Bound sparse MLA block-table gathers
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55636.

DeepSeek V4 / V4.1 sparse MLA maps local top-k indices through a 2-D
block table. The gather currently trusts both selectors after checking only
`local_idx >= 0`. An invalid request row or logical block column can therefore
read outside the intended block-table view, producing a wrong KV slot or an
illegal memory access.

Current `main` already pads the producer-side block table consistently during
CUDA-graph capture, so this PR is intentionally limited to defensive consumer
hardening plus focused regression coverage.

## Change

For both current shipped paths:

- `vllm.models.deepseek_v4`
- `vllm.models.deepseek_v41`

the mapper now:

- passes the logical row and column counts from `block_table.shape`;
- requires `0 <= req_idx < block_table_rows`;
- requires `0 <= block_indices < block_table_cols`;
- includes `is_valid_token` in the gather mask;
- maps invalid entries to `-1`;
- compacts surviving valid entries into the prefix consumed by `topk_lens`;
- excludes invalid entries from `topk_lens`.

The regression is kept in the existing
`tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py` suite and covers both V4 and
V4.1, including a non-contiguous block-table view where `stride(0) > shape[1]`
and an invalid-before-valid ordering.

## Duplicate-work check

I checked the linked issue and open sparse-MLA bounds PRs before the current
update.

PR #55744 was opened later on 2026-09-07 and overlaps this bug, but it is not an
equivalent fix:

- its current column check uses `block_table_stride` rather than logical
  `block_table.shape[1]`; CodeRabbit flagged that as allowing padded-view
  columns outside the logical table;
- its current output is not left-compacted when an invalid entry precedes a
  valid entry, while downstream consumers use `topk_lens` as a prefix length;
- it currently changes the V4 implementation only, while this PR keeps V4 and
  current V4.1 (`deepseek_v41`) aligned;
- #55744 is currently conflicted/unmergeable and has unresolved review
  comments around its optional `num_reqs` override.

Related #49896 is also distinct: it exposed bad local top-k indices reaching the
same mapper, whereas #55636 is the orthogonal request-row failure. The common
hardening point is the same 2-D gather boundary.

## Validation

Current head:

`e02a24951128103af2cfcba78a83ecddf6b83a3e`

Built directly on upstream `main` at:

`82daf9f5756e1868be0aa751afaec4726beca12a`

Current upstream `main` is `db7f1f671419535b85fa73e29ff061e287e39459`; GitHub still reports this PR mergeable against it.

Current GitHub state:

- mergeable against `main`;
- CodeRabbit / Read the Docs checks are allowed to run normally;
- upstream full CI remains maintainer/trusted-contributor gated for this fork;
- no fresh full GPU run is claimed for this rebased head.

Previous GPU-certified candidate `6ec865827ef45baafe184e095a637939cd767162`
validated the same consumer safety behavior before the upstream V4.1 package
rename and later refactors:

- dual-axis consumer bounds + focused sparse-MLA bounds tests: 28/28 PASS twice
  on a disposable RTX 3090;
- original `rows=1, req_idx=1` mechanism on V4 and V4.1: PASS;
- invalid entries became `-1`, did not alias row 0, and were excluded from
  the returned length;
- invalid-before-valid ordering retained the valid survivor via left
  compaction.

Those results are retained as historical evidence only; they are not presented
as fresh certification of the current SHA.

AI assistance was used for source review, rebasing, and drafting. I reviewed
the resulting patch scope and kept the current PR limited to the consumer
hardening described above.

title: [ROCm] Harden DeepSeek-V4 sparse prefill against zero-query-token chunks
body:
`_forward_prefill()` can be handed a prefill chunk covering zero query tokens,
and `combine_topk_swa_indices()` cannot reshape that. This adds the missing
guard.

## How an empty chunk arises

`split_decodes_and_prefills()` returns `num_prefills` as a suffix,
`num_reqs - first_prefill`. Request slots with zero query tokens are never
themselves flagged as prefills, but any that trail the first real prefill fall
inside that suffix. Such slots are an intentional artifact of request-dimension
padding: `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/input_batch.py` writes
`query_start_loc[num_reqs + 1:] = num_tokens` and `seq_lens[num_reqs:] = 0`, and
`split_decodes_and_prefills()` documents them itself ("some requests may have a
query length of 0 but since they are padding ...").

Since #58405, `_forward_prefill()` chunks that range with the shared
`get_prefill_chunk_plan()`, which packs rows greedily until
`rows × widest row` exceeds the workspace. A padding row has zero width, but it
is still charged at the chunk's widest row. So once the chunk holding the last
real prefill is full by area, the padding opens a chunk of its own, that chunk
covers zero query tokens, and `topk_indices.reshape(topk_indices.shape[0], -1)`
becomes ambiguous.

## Change

Compute the chunk's query range first (it only reads `query_start_loc_cpu`) and
skip chunks with an empty range. This also drops the workspace request, two
`dequantize_and_gather_k_cache()` calls and one `rocm_sparse_attn_prefill()`
launch per padding-only chunk, which had nothing to compute.

## What I can show

On `main@72e7874fa6`: the real `split_decodes_and_prefills()` and
`get_prefill_chunk_plan()`, window 128, `max_model_len` 65536,
`max_num_batched_tokens` 8192, three decodes followed by `n` ∈ 1…12 chunked
prefills (query 37 or 509, context 32k or 64.5k) and 0/1/3/5 padded slots:

| compress ratio | shapes with a zero-query chunk |
| --- | ---: |
| 4 (C4A) | 56 / 192 |
| 128 (C128A) | 0 / 192 |
| SWA only | 0 / 192 |

The smallest case is a single C4A prefill at 64.5k context followed by 5 padded
slots: the plan is `[(0, 5), (5, 6)]`, and the second chunk is padding only.
Running the tree's real `_forward_prefill()` loop over that batch, with the GPU
kernels stubbed and the empty chunk handed to the real
`combine_topk_swa_indices()`:

| | `main` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| result | `RuntimeError: cannot reshape tensor of 0 elements into shape [0, -1]` | completes |
| real chunk | 2 gathers, 1 combine, 1 attention launch | identical |
| padding chunk | workspace + 2 gathers, then raises | skipped |

The earlier shape sweep from this description (`[1 + k, 256] + [0] * pad`) no
longer produces an empty chunk on `main` (0 / 126), because a short prefill
leaves room for the padding in its own chunk. The condition is now area-driven,
not a fixed count of padded slots, and it still does not depend on
`num_speculative_tokens`.

## What I cannot show

Reachability end to end on `main`. The state was hit for real on v0.26.0 (full
traceback, all four TP ranks, `EngineDeadError`). On `main` it needs padded
request slots in the same batch as a prefill; in the default configuration only
FULL-cudagraph batches are padded, and those carry no prefills. Two full DSpark
runs earlier produced zero empty chunks across 90,988 instrumented prefill-chunk
invocations:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55695#issuecomment-5578723131

So this is hardening a path that is reachable by construction, not a fix for an
observable regression. The suffix semantics and the padding convention are both
unchanged, and the guard removes work rather than adding it.

---

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom); reviewed and measured by hand.

title: [Bug]: `fuse_attn_quant` without `use_inductor_graph_partition` drops all piecewise cudagraphs on backends that cannot do FULL (-38 % on ROCm sparse MLA)
body:
On an attention backend whose cudagraph support is below `FULL`, enabling
`fuse_attn_quant` **without** `use_inductor_graph_partition` removes every
piecewise cudagraph and does not get full ones in return. On GLM-5.3
(`glm_moe_dsa`, `ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend`, gfx950, TP4, MTP k=4) it costs
**38 % throughput** and **+60 % TPOT**.

### The chain

`config/compilation.py:1257`:

```python
def set_splitting_ops_for_attn_fusion(self):
    assert self.pass_config.fuse_attn_quant
    if self.splitting_ops is None:
        self.splitting_ops = []
        if self.cudagraph_mode.has_piecewise_cudagraphs():
            logger.warning_once(
                "fuse_attn_quant is incompatible with piecewise cudagraph when "
                "use_inductor_graph_partition is off. In this case, splitting_ops "
                "will be set to empty list, and cudagraph_mode will be set to FULL."
            )
            self.cudagraph_mode = CUDAGraphMode.FULL
```

The backend then cannot honour `FULL`:

```
WARNING [compilation.py:1413] CUDAGraphMode.FULL is not supported with
ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend backend (support: AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_BATCH);
setting cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY
```

and the fallback picks the lossy branch:

```python
if self.splitting_ops_contain_attention():
    cudagraph_mode = CUDAGraphMode.FULL_AND_PIECEWISE   # would keep piecewise
else:
    cudagraph_mode = CUDAGraphMode.FULL_DECODE_ONLY     # loses piecewise entirely
```

`set_splitting_ops_for_attn_fusion` has just set `splitting_ops = []` and even
asserts that no attention op is in it, so `splitting_ops_contain_attention()`
is **always** False here. The `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` branch is unreachable for
this path.

Resulting config: `'splitting_ops': []`, `'cudagraph_mode': FULL_DECODE_ONLY`,
`54 Capturing CUDA graphs (FULL)`, zero piecewise captures. With chunked
prefill most steps are mixed prefill+decode, so they get no cudagraph at all.

### Measured

Same replica, env switches byte-identical between arms, only the compilation
config differs. Passes 2 and 3 of three, fixed dataset, 32 concurrent:

| arm | throughput | TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|
| baseline (no fusion flags) | 2118 / 2124 tok/s | 13.97 ms |
| `fuse_attn_quant=True` (no inductor graph partition) | 1152 / 1459 tok/s | 22.30 ms |

### Suggestion

When the resolved decode/attention backend cannot support `FULL`, either

* keep the piecewise splitting ops and skip the attention+quant fusion, or
* refuse `fuse_attn_quant` with a clear error instead of silently trading all
  piecewise cudagraphs for decode-only ones.

A related observation from the same run: `AttnQuantFusionPass` logged
`"no attention layers were found ... so no fusion patterns were registered"`
(it looks for `Attention`, this model uses `MLAAttention`), while
`MLAAttnQuantFusionPass` did register patterns. So on an MLA-only model the
whole cudagraph downgrade is paid for the MLA pass alone. See also #55720.

Happy to send a patch for whichever behaviour you prefer.

title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Decode hot-path cleanups: strided KDA recurrent inputs, NoPE MQA query without concat, no duplicate router GEMM
body:
## Purpose

One of three independent GLM-5.3-Flash perf PRs 

Three small, independent decode hot-path cleanups found while profiling GLM-5.3-Flash (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, FP8, TP4 on 4x GB300, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`):

1. **KDA decode: read token-strided q/k/v/beta in `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel`.** The decode path hands the recurrent kernel column slices of the merged `q|k|v` conv output and of the fused `qkvbfg_a` projection (beta); `fused_recurrent_kda` made each contiguous, i.e. 4 copy kernels per KDA layer per step (34 layers; ~11 us/layer at 64 requests, ~0.4 ms/step). The Triton kernel now takes explicit token strides; contiguous callers are unchanged. The stride check is pure integer arithmetic (no views) because the KDA forward is a CUDA-graph break and runs eagerly.
2. **MLA: write the absorbed MQA query token-major and skip the empty RoPE concat.** Without head padding the W_UK bmm now writes into a `(B, N, L)` buffer through a transposed `out` view (verified: one GEMM kernel, no copy, identical result). For NoPE models (`qk_rope_head_dim == 0`) the FlashInfer sparse backend then uses `ql_nope` directly instead of `torch.cat` with a zero-width `q_pe`, which took the slow `CatArrayBatchedCopy` path (13.7 us/layer at 256 decode tokens, ~0.75 ms/layer per 16k-token prefill chunk).
3. **Glm5NextMoE: do not compute the router logits twice.** `MoERunner` holds the gate (passed via `FusedMoEFactory`) and recomputes the logits (`moe_runner.py:897`), so the gate GEMM in `Glm5NextMoE.forward` was wasted (two bf16->fp32 GEMMs + reductions per MoE layer). Follows `DeepseekV2MoE` and passes a placeholder.

## Test Plan

- Unit / kernel tests listed under "Tests" below.
- Serving benchmark, all builds back-to-back in one session on 4x GB300 (SM100), TP4, prefix caching disabled:
  ```bash
  vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash -tp 4 --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE \
    --max-model-len 69632 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching
  vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model glm53-flash --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 0 \
    --ignore-eos --seed 0 --random-input-len <in> --random-output-len <out> --max-concurrency <c> \
    --num-prompts <n> --num-warmups <c> --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
  ```
  Points: 1k/512 at c=1/64/256; prefill-only 8x2048, 2x8192, 8x32768, 2x65536; 32k/256 at c=16. The prefix-cache hit rate in the server log was checked to be 0.0% for every run.
- Accuracy per build: `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs temperature=0`

## Test Result

### Performance of this PR alone

main `156050598` vs main + this PR, 4x GB300, TP4, `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE --max-model-len 69632 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, **prefix caching disabled** (hit rate 0.0% checked in the server log), `vllm bench serve` random dataset with warmups, both servers run back-to-back in the same session. Decode tok/s is the steady-state window value (full concurrency); TPOT is the per-request median.

| point | metric | main | +#55736 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1k/512 c=1 | decode tok/s | 144 | 146 | +1.8% |
| 1k/512 c=1 | median TPOT ms | 6.57 | 6.46 | -1.7% |
| 1k/512 c=64 | decode tok/s | 2964 | 3090 | +4.3% |
| 1k/512 c=64 | median TPOT ms | 20.02 | 19.26 | -3.8% |
| 1k/512 c=256 | decode tok/s | 7147 | 7367 | +3.1% |
| 1k/512 c=256 | median TPOT ms | 33.87 | 32.87 | -3.0% |
| prefill 8x2048 | mean TTFT ms | 461 | 449 | -2.5% |
| prefill 2x8192 | mean TTFT ms | 389 | 380 | -2.4% |
| prefill 8x32768 | mean TTFT ms | 5258 | 5108 | -2.8% |
| prefill 2x65536 | mean TTFT ms | 2738 | 2661 | -2.8% |
| 32k/256 c=16 | decode tok/s | 287 | 296 | +3.1% |
| 32k/256 c=16 | mean TTFT ms | 3883 | 3835 | -1.2% |
| 32k/256 c=16 | median TPOT ms | 41.34 | 40.10 | -3.0% |

Decode: +3-4% tok/s (−3-4% TPOT) at c=64, c=256 and in the 32k-context point, −1.7% TPOT at c=1 (host-bound). Prefill: a consistent −2.5-2.8% TTFT on all four points

### Accuracy (per build, same session)

Each rung of the ablation was also evaluated on its own: **gsm8k** (1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, lm_eval `local-completions`)

| build | gsm8k flexible-extract % | gsm8k strict-match % |
|---|---|---|
| main | 93.33 ± 0.69 | 93.10 ± 0.70 | 
| +#55736 | 93.03 ± 0.70 | 92.95 ± 0.71 |

## Duplicate-work check

`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "fused_recurrent_kda stride"`, `"MoERunner gate router_logits Glm5Next"`, `"GLM-5.3-Flash prefill"`: no open PR covers these (the open GLM-5.3-Flash PRs #54951 / #55222 / #55385 / #55543 touch the indexer prefill sharding, SM90 sparse-MLA dtypes and the SM90 FA/FlashMLA wiring).

## Tests

- `pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py` (new; fp32 PyTorch reference for plain and spec-decode shapes, strided-vs-contiguous bit-identity, unaddressable layouts rejected): 6 passed.
- bmm into a transposed `out`: max diff 0.0 vs `bmm().transpose()`, profiler shows a single `nvjet` kernel.
- `pre-commit run ruff-check / ruff-format` on the changed files: passed.
- e2e: serving smoke (chat sanity); prompt-logprob A/B on real 4k/12k/30k/60k prompts vs main is within ~1-2.5x the main-vs-main run-to-run noise floor with identical next tokens; **gsm8k 1319 questions (5-shot, greedy): main 93.03% ± 0.70, full series 92.65% ± 0.72** (5 questions, < 1σ; measured on the three PRs together).
