title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Dense/masked-MHA sparse prefill for the NoPE (256, 0, 256) layout + skip the NoPE K concat
body:
## Purpose

One of three independent GLM-5.3-Flash perf PRs 

On main, GLM-5.3-Flash's MLA layout (qk_nope 256, qk_rope 0, v 256) is unknown to the FlashAttention prefill backend and to the masked-MHA allow-list, so `MLACommonImpl` logs `No MLA prefill backend supports this model` and **every prefill token goes through the per-token top-k MQA kernel**. Profiling shows that kernel is KV-gather bound at the HBM roofline: 5.9 ms/layer per 16k-token chunk, and still 1.6 ms/layer for 8x2048 where dense MHA needs ~0.2 ms.

Three commits:
1. **Register the (256, 0, 256) dims with `FlashAttnPrefillBackend`** (7 lines). Same lines as in the SM90 wiring PR vllm-project/vllm#55385; kept separate so it can be dropped once that lands. This alone gives the dense-MHA prefill path for sequences ≤ index_topk (2048).
2. **Masked-MHA allow-list**: `_is_masked_mha_available` only knew (128, 512, 128, 64, 128) and (64, 512, 192, 64, 256); GLM-5.3-Flash is (64, 512, 256, 0, 256). The kernels are identical for qk_head_dim 256 / v 256, so sequences between 2k and the existing FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE thresholds (36k at TP4, 64k at TP8) now use FA4 masked MHA instead of the per-token top-k MQA kernel.
3. **NoPE K concat**: `_concat_k_nope_k_pe` returns `k_nope` directly when there is no RoPE part instead of allocating and copying a same-sized tensor (134 MB/layer per 16k chunk).

## Test Plan

- Unit / kernel tests listed under "Tests" below.
- Serving benchmark, all builds back-to-back in one session on 4x GB300 (SM100), TP4, prefix caching disabled:
  ```bash
  vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash -tp 4 --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE \
    --max-model-len 69632 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching
  vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model glm53-flash --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 0 \
    --ignore-eos --seed 0 --random-input-len <in> --random-output-len <out> --max-concurrency <c> \
    --num-prompts <n> --num-warmups <c> --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
  ```
 0 prefix-cache hit 
- Accuracy per build: `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs temperature=0` (1319 questions)

## Test Result

### Performance of this PR alone

Measured on top of #55736 + #55737 (main + #55736 + #55737) vs the same + this PR, 4x GB300, TP4, `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE --max-model-len 69632 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, **prefix caching disabled** (hit rate 0.0% checked in the server log), `vllm bench serve` random dataset with warmups, back-to-back in the same session. Decode tok/s is the steady-state window value; TPOT is the per-request median.

| point | metric | +#55736 +#55737 | +#55736 +#55737 +#55738 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prefill 8x2048 | mean TTFT ms | 395 | 361 | -8.5% |
| prefill 2x8192 | mean TTFT ms | 330 | 315 | -4.6% |
| prefill 8x32768 | mean TTFT ms | 4693 | 4347 | -7.4% |
| prefill 2x65536 | mean TTFT ms | 2450 | 2365 | -3.5% |
| 32k/256 c=16 | decode tok/s | 316 | 322 | +1.9% |
| 32k/256 c=16 | mean TTFT ms | 3642 | 3482 | -4.4% |
| 32k/256 c=16 | median TPOT ms | 37.50 | 36.97 | -1.4% |
| 1k/512 c=1 | decode tok/s | 147 | 147 | -0.2% |
| 1k/512 c=1 | median TPOT ms | 6.47 | 6.49 | +0.3% |
| 1k/512 c=64 | decode tok/s | 3132 | 3133 | +0.0% |
| 1k/512 c=64 | median TPOT ms | 19.24 | 19.09 | -0.8% |
| 1k/512 c=256 | decode tok/s | 7717 | 7755 | +0.5% |
| 1k/512 c=256 | median TPOT ms | 31.30 | 31.29 | -0.0% |

Prefill up to the masked-MHA threshold (≤ 36k at TP4): −8.5% TTFT for 8x2048 (dense MHA), −7.4% for 8x32k (masked MHA), −4.4% TTFT in the 32k-context serving point. 2x8192 shows −4.6%, but that 16-request point has a ~4% run-to-run noise floor (last column of the ablation below), so treat it as indicative only. 64k prompts are above the threshold and stay on the sparse kernel; the −3.5% there (0.0% noise floor) is the K-concat removal alone. Decode is unchanged (±0.8%).


### Accuracy (per build, same session)

Each rung of the ablation was also evaluated on its own: **gsm8k** (1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, lm_eval `local-completions`), **prompt-logprob agreement** on real 4k/12k/30k/60k prompts (mean |Δ logprob| per token vs the main build; the "main again" row is the run-to-run noise floor of this FP8 model), and a **needle-in-a-haystack** retrieval set (12 codes per length at 6k/16k/30k tokens, greedy, `reasoning_effort=low`), which exercises the 2k-36k prefill range where #55738 switches kernels.

| build | gsm8k flexible-extract % | gsm8k strict-match % |
|---|---|---|
| main | 93.33 ± 0.69 | 93.10 ± 0.70 |
| +#55736 +#55737 +#55738 | 93.10 ± 0.70 | 93.10 ± 0.70 |


### Caveat: runtime JIT

The first request in each new sequence-length bucket JIT-compiles the FA4 CuTeDSL `mask_mod` variant (`BlackwellFusedMultiHeadAttentionForward`) plus the Triton `_scatter_topk_single_req_kernel` (~7 s each; `jit_monitor` warns). `FA4MLAPrefillKernel.get_warmup_keys` does not cover mask_mod, so this is a pre-existing gap for every masked-MHA model; a warmup for the masked variants should be a follow-up before relying on this in production.

## Duplicate-work check

`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "NoPE masked MHA 256"` / `"GLM-5.3-Flash prefill"`: #55385 covers the FA dims (commit 1 here is the same 7 lines); #54951 / #55222 / #55543 touch the indexer prefill sharding, the indexer workspace and SM90 fp8 KV. None adds the masked-MHA layout or the K-concat skip.
- vllm-project/vllm#53969 / #55277 add NoPE support to the SM120 FlashInfer sparse backend only (`flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm120.py`); no overlap with the masked-MHA allow-list or the K-concat skip.

## Tests

- New unit tests (all pass on GB300, 14 cases):
  - `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_sparse_backend_prefill_correctness[glm53_flash_nope_hd256_v256-*]`: dense MHA, masked MHA and masked MHA with chunked context for the NoPE `(64, 256, 0, 256)` layout against the per-token SDPA reference.
  - `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_is_masked_mha_available_model_dims`: allow-list accepts the DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5 and NoPE GLM-5.3-Flash geometries and rejects quantized KV, FA3, `(256, 64, 256)` and a different head count.
  - `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_selector.py::TestBackendValidation::test_flash_attn_accepts_glm53_flash_nope_dimensions`: `FlashAttnPrefillBackend.validate_configuration` accepts `(256, 0, 256)` and still rejects `(256, 64, 256)`.
  - `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py::test_concat_k_nope_k_pe_matches_torch_cat[rope|nope]`: `_concat_k_nope_k_pe` equals `torch.cat` of `k_nope` and the broadcast `k_pe`; with no RoPE part it returns `k_nope` itself (same `data_ptr`).
- `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py`, `tests/kernels/test_glm5next_kda_recurrent_strided.py` unaffected; prompt-logprob A/B on real 4k/12k/30k/60k prompts vs main: mean|Δ| 0.06-0.12 vs a main-vs-main noise floor of 0.04-0.11 (≈2.5x at 4k where dense/masked MHA replaces the sparse kernel), identical next tokens; **gsm8k 1319 questions (5-shot, greedy): main 93.03% ± 0.70, full series 92.65% ± 0.72** (measured on the three PRs together).
- `pre-commit run ruff-check / ruff-format`: passed.
- AI assistance: developed with Claude Fable 5.1 and reviewed by the submitter; profiling notes and raw benchmark logs available on request.

## Notes for review

title: [Fix] Guard out-of-bounds gather in DeepSeek-V4 cache_utils Triton ke…
body:
#closes 55692
ready-run-all-tests
Root Cause
In vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/cache_utils.py, _compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens_kernel performs a block-table lookup to map token top-k indices to global KV cache slots:

python


block_table_ptr + req_idx * block_table_stride + block_indices
Previously, the kernel only checked local_idx >= 0. It failed to validate:

Row index bounds: req_idx (request index) could be out of range (req_idx < 0 or req_idx >= num_reqs), e.g., during CUDA-graph padding or unmasked request slots.
Column index bounds: block_indices could exceed block_table_stride.
This allowed unmasked loads from invalid memory addresses (causing cudaErrorIllegalAddress) or corrupted slot lookups, and incorrectly incremented active sequence counts in topk_lens.

Key Fixes Made
Row Boundary Parameter (
cache_utils.py
):
compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens now extracts num_reqs = block_table.shape[0] (with an optional parameter override) and passes num_reqs into _compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens_kernel.
Comprehensive Gather Masking:
Defined valid_mask in Triton to enforce both row and column boundaries:
python


valid_mask = (
    (local_idx >= 0)
    & (req_idx >= 0)
    & (req_idx < num_reqs)
    & (block_indices < block_table_stride)
)
Safe Memory Load & Index Clamping:
Clamped request and block indices (safe_req_idx, safe_block_indices) prior to pointer calculation so address arithmetic remains in-bounds.
Guarded tl.load with mask=mask & valid_mask, other=-1.
Set slot_ids = tl.where(valid_mask, slot_ids, -1) so invalid entries resolve to -1.
Updated length calculation count += tl.sum((valid_mask & mask).to(tl.int32), axis=0) to exclude invalid entries from topk_lens.
Regression Test Suite (
test_deepseek_v4_cache_utils.py
):
Added unit tests comparing kernel outputs against a PyTorch reference implementation across normal lookups, out-of-bounds req_idx (req_idx >= block_table.shape[0], req_idx < 0), out-of-bounds block_indices, and padding token masks.

title: [Bug]: sparse-MLA (DSA) models unservable on SM120 in v0.28.0 — two faults in the MHA prefill path
body:
Serving any DeepSeek-style sparse-MLA (DSA) model on consumer Blackwell (sm_120) with stock vLLM 0.28.0 hits **two independent faults in the MHA prefill path**. Fix the first and you immediately hit the second. Together they make GLM-5.3 / GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek-V4 unservable on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / RTX 5090 at realistic prompt lengths.

Reporting them together because they are sequential failures in the same code path and would likely be fixed by one PR.

## Why it matters

Either fault alone makes any DeepSeek-style sparse-MLA (DSA) model — GLM-5.3,
GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V4 — fail with `EngineDeadError` on consumer Blackwell (sm_120:
RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, RTX 5090) as soon as a prompt is long enough to select the
MHA prefill path.

⚠️ **Short prompts pass.** A one-line smoke test succeeds and the server looks
healthy; the failure only appears under a realistic prompt length. That is why this
is easy to miss in bring-up.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| vLLM | 0.28.0 (stock `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0`) |
| torch | 2.13.0+cu130 |
| flashinfer-python | 0.6.16.post3 |
| nvidia-cutlass-dsl | 4.6.2 |
| GPU | 8× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120) |
| driver | 580.126.09 |
| model | `LibertAIDAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4` (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) |
| backends | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` + `FLASH_ATTN` MLA prefill |

## Fault 1 — `FlashInferMLASparseSM120Impl` has no `masked_mha_available`

`model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py:812` reads the attribute with no
guard (the `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` on that line is a hint that it is not on
the base class):

```python
use_masked_mha = (
    self.prefill_backend is not None
    and self.impl.masked_mha_available          # <-- line 812, AttributeError
    and self.impl.dcp_world_size <= 1
    ...
    and self.impl.masked_mha_workspace_fits(prefill)
)
```

`v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm120.py` sets
`self.supports_quant_query_input = False` in `__init__` but never defines
`masked_mha_available`.

Observed:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error ''FlashInferMLASparseSM120Impl' object has
no attribute 'masked_mha_available''
  -> vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError
```

**Suggested fix.** Define it on the impl (or default it on the base class).
`_is_masked_mha_available()` in `sparse_mla_attention.py` already returns `False`
for anything outside `is_device_capability_family(100)`, so `False` is the
semantically correct value here:

```python
self.supports_quant_query_input = False
self.masked_mha_available = False
```

## Fault 2 — dense-MHA prefill calls `forward_mha()`, unimplemented on sm_120

With fault 1 patched, a longer prompt then selects the dense-MHA prefill path
(`use_dense_mha`) and calls `self.impl.forward_mha(...)`, which falls through to the
base implementation in `v1/attention/backend.py`:

```python
    ) -> None:
        """MHA-style prefill forward pass."""
        raise NotImplementedError
```

`FlashInferMLASparseSM120Impl` implements **only** `forward_mqa` — it has no
`forward_mha`. Observed:

```
File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py", line ...
    self.impl.forward_mha(  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
File ".../vllm/v1/attention/backend.py", line 1106, in forward_mha
    raise NotImplementedError
NotImplementedError
  -> RuntimeError: Worker failed with error ''
  -> vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError
```

**Workaround (supported, no patch):**

```
--attention-config '{"sparse_mla_force_mqa": true}'
```

which forces the sparse MQA path — the only one sm_120 implements.

**Suggested fix.** Either implement `forward_mha` for the sm_120 sparse impl, or
gate `use_dense_mha` / `use_masked_mha` on the impl actually providing an MHA path
(e.g. an `mha_available` predicate) so the backend selector cannot pick a path the
impl does not implement.

## Performance note (not a bug, but the reason we care)

Forcing MQA is not free. A torch-profiler trace on this box (c=16 × 1024-token
prefill, rank 0) attributes **36.4% of all GPU kernel time** to
`sparse_mla_prefill_kernel<(ModelType)2, (ComputeMode)0, 8, 2048, 64>`.

With `index_topk=2048`, every prompt **shorter than 2048 tokens** gets no sparsity
benefit at all — the context is smaller than the top-k — yet still pays a
sparse-gather kernel where a dense FlashAttention prefill would do. So on sm_120 the
missing `forward_mha` is not only a crash, it also removes the fast path for exactly
the prompt lengths where it would help most.

title: glm5_next (GLM-5.3-Flash): fp8_ds_mla cache path asserts pe_dim==64 but the model has qk_rope_head_dim=0 (NoPE MLA) — engine init fails on SM120
body:
### Commit / version
vLLM wheel built from 98ed0856f31fa3aaf5e27464e2b4ef5a8ee6b2f5 (PR #53906, Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration + FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120), wheel `vllm-0.28.1rc1.dev359+g98ed0856f-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_28_x86_64`.

### Hardware
2× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, capability 12.0), tensor_parallel_size=2.

### Model
`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4), config (verified from `config.json`):
- `qk_rope_head_dim = 0` (NoPE MLA — rope lives ONLY in the sparse indexer, `index_head_dim=128`, `index_n_heads=32`, `index_kpool=4`, `index_topk=2048`)
- `kv_lora_rank = 512`, `qk_nope_head_dim = 256`, `q_lora_rank = 1536`
- `full_attn_layers = [3,7,...,43]` (11 DSA layers), the rest KDA linear attention

### What happens
Engine init gets all the way through weight load (70.73 GiB/GPU, TP2), selects `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` with `kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla` (the only backend the selector offers on capability 12 for this model), allocates the KV pool, compiles the TileLang kernels — then dies at the first cache update:

```
RuntimeError: concat_and_cache_mla, /workspace/csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu:928,
pe_dim must be 64 for fp8_ds_mla
```

Stack (worker): `Glm5NextMLAAttention.forward` → `attn_layer.impl.do_kv_cache_update` → `ops.concat_and_cache_mla(...)` → `torch.ops._C_cache_ops.concat_and_cache_mla` — inside the `fused_rope_unified_mla_kv_cache_update` compilation fusion (`vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion.py`).

### Root cause
`vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/attention.py` carries the comment

```python
self.rope_dim = config.qk_rope_head_dim  # 64
```

but GLM-5.3-Flash's actual `qk_rope_head_dim` is **0**. The fp8_ds_mla `concat_and_cache_mla` kernel (cache_kernels.cu:928) hard-asserts `pe_dim == 64` — the DeepSeek-V3.2 DSA geometry. With `pe_dim=0` the assertion fires and every engine-init attempt dies, ~30 min into weight loading each time.

Note the failure is *silent* at the urun layer: the OOM-adjacent cgroup pressure and this assert both kill the worker without surfacing to the launcher, which is why it took 10+ boot attempts to isolate.

### Config used
`tensor_parallel_size=2, enable_expert_parallel=true, kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla, gpu_memory_utilization=0.95, speculative_config={method: mtp, num_speculative_tokens: 2}, max_model_len=1048576, cpu_offload_gb=22 (UVA, experts-only via cpu_offload_params), no --quantization flag (auto-detect compressed-tensors nvfp4)`.

### What we'd need
Support for `qk_rope_head_dim=0` in the fp8_ds_mla cache-update path for glm5_next (pe_dim=0: skip the pe concat), or an alternative SM120-capable cache layout for glm5_next sparse-MLA. With bf16/auto KV the selector's only other option (TRITON_MLA) was rejected for this config, so there is currently no working attention backend for glm5_next on SM120 in this build.

Full context and boot receipts: https://github.com/urun-sh/urun-infra/issues/2208 (related infra incident) — happy to provide the complete 3000-line boot log.

title: fix(mla): support NoPE head sizes by zeroing RoPE tail in SM120 backend
body:
NoPE architectures with `qk_rope_head_dim=0` and `head_size=512` failed under `fp8_ds_mla` cache lines because the underlying kernel expects a 64-dim RoPE tail to preserve the packed 656-byte cache ABI. Zero-padding `k_pe` to 64 elements during `do_kv_cache_update` satisfies the hardware memory layout without requiring kernel modifications or cross-architecture fallbacks. This enables native SM120 sparse MLA execution for models without positional embeddings while leaving standard 576-dim paths intact.

Fixes #55773.

title: [Attention] Require explicit DCP support from attention implementations
body:
- Default `AttentionImplBase.supports_dcp` to `False` so implementations must explicitly opt into DCP.
- Enable eleven existing DCP implementation classes, preserving thirteen registered backends, including FlashAttention, FlashInfer, and the supported MLA variants.
- Reject unsupported ROCm, standard Triton, FlexAttention, and TurboQuant DCP configurations during selection, before loading model weights.
- Preserve the existing sparse AITER MLA and B12X exclusions and ordinary execution with DCP disabled.
- Extend ROCm selector tests to cover dense and sparse MLA, automatic and explicit selection, and valid DiffKV/TurboQuant configurations with DCP on and off.
- Add regression coverage for supported backend eligibility and the custom-backend default, and use CUTLASS MLA's supported block size 128 in its selector tests.

This follows [the review on #54404](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54404#discussion_r3949253134), which raised concern that the new selection check could reject supported backends such as Triton MLA. The `True` default originated in [#40996](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40996); #54404 preserved it and explicitly disabled DCP for sparse AITER MLA. Local testing confirmed that Triton MLA remained usable, but several unsupported implementations also inherited `True` and failed the worker's missing-LSE check after loading weights. Explicit opt-ins move those failures into backend selection and prevent new implementations from advertising DCP implicitly.

| Explicit `True` declaration | Backends covered |
| --- | --- |
| `FlashAttentionImpl` | `FLASH_ATTN`, `FLASH_ATTN_DIFFKV` |
| `FlashInferImpl` | `FLASHINFER` |
| `TritonMLAImpl` | `TRITON_MLA` |
| `AiterMLAImpl` | `ROCM_AITER_MLA`, `ROCM_AITER_TRITON_MLA` |
| `CutlassMLAImpl` | `CUTLASS_MLA` |
| `FlashMLAImpl` | `FLASHMLA` |
| `FlashInferMLAImpl` | `FLASHINFER_MLA` |
| `TokenspeedMLAImpl` | `TOKENSPEED_MLA` |
| `FlashAttnMLAImpl` | `FLASH_ATTN_MLA` |
| `FlashMLASparseImpl` | `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` |
| `FlashInferMLASparseImpl` | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` |

Prepared with AI assistance (OpenAI Codex).

title: [BugFix] Group GLM-5 hybrid KV cache specs (indexer/state roles) correctly
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

GLM-5.3 hybrids mix 34 KDA (mamba-style) layers with 11 sparse-MLA layers whose caches carry **three roles**: the main MLA latent (`tokens_per_state=1`), the kpool indexer K pool, and the compressor state (`tokens_per_state>1`). Upstream grouping mishandled this mix in three ways:

1. `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` lacked `get_page_sizes()` / `get_num_layer_tuples()` accessors that the hybrid-layout path needs; add them.
2. The hybrid-grouping guard treated every non-MLA spec as ineligible, dropping the indexer/state specs out of the GLM layout; extend it to accept `KpoolTailSpec` / `SlidingWindowMLASpec` alongside `MambaSpec`.
3. The pad-consistency assert assumed no pads survive pre-grouping, which does not hold when smaller indexer pages are padded up to the MLA page size; relax it to "at most one distinct pad".

Also routes the GLM-5 tensor-layout path so the mixed groups resolve to the shared hybrid layout.

Companion of vllm-project/vllm-ascend#16005 (the kpool sparse-attention backend these caches serve).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes — GLM-5 hybrid models group their KV caches correctly instead of falling back to a generic layout that over-allocates (observed: 23 GB vs the correct 441 MB per rank).

### How was this patch tested?

End-to-end on Atlas 910B3 with a 48-layer GLM-5.3 hybrid + official W8A8 weights: cache groups resolve to the GLM layout, the model serves with the kpool backend (GSM8K-level gate 12/12), and FULL graph capture works.

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Add merged MoE front
body:
## Summary

Integrates the Kimi-K3 merged MoE front from ROCm/aiter#5321.

Kimi-K3's MoE front applies three projections to the same `x[M, 7168]`:
shared gate/up `7168 -> 1536`, router logits `7168 -> 896`, and routed latent
`7168 -> 3584`. For the measured token counts this PR replaces them with one
BF16 GEMM into an FP32 `7168 -> 6016` accumulator followed by AITER's generic
SiTU/split epilogue. Routed experts remain on the existing modular AITER MXFP4
backend.

Unsupported configurations and token counts fall back to the native front.
There is no feature environment variable.

## Safety gate

The merged path is enabled only when all assumptions used by the optimized
implementation hold:

- gfx950;
- exact Kimi-K3 BF16 CUDA weight shapes and compatible devices;
- DP, EP, and PCP are all 1;
- sequence parallelism is disabled;
- the routed latent tail is shardable and has not already been reduced;
- modular routed experts are in use;
- activation is `SituAndMul(beta=4, linear_beta=25)`.

The runtime token gate contains 57 measured shapes:

```text
1..16, 18, 20, 24, 25, 30, 32, 35, 36, 40, 42, 45, 48,
50, 55, 60, 64, 65, 70, 75, 80, 85, 90, 95, 96, 100, 112, 128, 192,
```

The 29 additions cover complete DSpark verification batches for the C4
(k=5, up to 8 active requests) and C10 (k=4, up to 20) recipes, plus nine
prefill candidates. Build-specific hipBLASLt 1.4.1 / `8d1ae90e` selections
are in [ROCm/aiter#5956](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5956), which updates
`aiter/configs/model_configs/kimik3_bf16_tuned_gemm.csv` for the normal default
configuration merge.
M=8192 was also tuned and validated but stays on the native path because
its full merged front was 7.39% slower. Other unlisted token counts also
use the native front. The prefill candidates are not a runtime hit histogram.

## Resource lifecycle

hipBLASLt is initialized only when a selected tuned row actually dispatches to
hipBLASLt. Initialization is process-cached, and all Kimi-K3 MoE layers in one
worker share a single front workspace (213 MiB at max M=6144). Weight processing therefore does not
allocate one hipBLASLt workspace per layer or unnecessarily reduce the KV pool.

The native fallback calls the internal implementation directly so a fallback
from the custom-op boundary does not advance the MoE layer index twice.

### 🐛 Describe the bug **Summary.** The `fs` and `obj` secondary tiers of the native KV offloading connector namespace persisted blocks under `/_`, where the digest is a SHA-256 over `FileMapper.fields` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/file_mapper.py:54-76`). Those fields cover the model, dtype, `tokens_per_hash`, `blocks_per_file`, TP/PP/PCP/DCP and the runner/canonical flags — but not `kv_cache_layout`. On the direct (non-canonical) path a persisted page is a verbatim copy of the GPU block in the worker's resolved layout, written to disk unchanged and read back with only a size check. LBNHC and LBHNC are the same bytes in a different order, so two runs sharing a `root_dir` under different layouts map the same token prefix to the same file: the size check passes, the lookup hits, and attention is handed the bytes in the wrong order. There is no error and no cache-related log line; the output is garbage. Two runs resolve different layouts when `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT` differs between them, or when an attention backend cannot satisfy the connector's requested LBHNC layout and overrides it — FlexAttention, HPC and TurboQuant are LBNHC-only. The documented multi-instance "shared PVC" pattern (`tiering/fs/manager.py:99-104`) puts both into one namespace. **Minimal reproduction (no GPU).** The two configurations below differ only in `kv_cache_layout`: ```python from unittest.mock import MagicMock from vllm.v1.kv_offload.base import OffloadingSpec from vllm.v1.kv_offload.config import ( OffloadingCacheConfig, OffloadingConfig, OffloadingModelConfig, OffloadingParallelConfig, ) from vllm.v1.kv_offload.file_mapper import FileMapper def mapper(kv_cache_layout: str) -> FileMapper: spec = MagicMock(spec=OffloadingSpec) spec.config = OffloadingConfig( groups=(), worker_kv_bytes_per_block=0, enable_kv_cache_events=False, extra_config={}, engine_id="engine", model=OffloadingModelConfig(name="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", dtype="bfloat16"), cache=OffloadingCacheConfig(tokens_per_hash=16, blocks_per_chunk=1), parallel=OffloadingParallelConfig( rank=0, world_size=1, tp_size=1, pp_size=1, pcp_size=1, dcp_size=1, data_parallel_index=0, data_parallel_size=1, data_parallel_rank_local=None, is_parallelism_agnostic=False, ), kv_cache_layout=kv_cache_layout, ) return FileMapper.from_offloading_spec( root_dir="/tmp/cache", offloading_spec=spec, blocks_per_file=1 ) nhd, hnd = mapper("LBNHC"), mapper("LBHNC") print(nhd.base_path) print(hnd.base_path) assert nhd.base_path == hnd.base_path # passes on main: one namespace ``` On `main` @ `6f7df92a8e` both layouts produce the same namespace. **End-to-end reproduction.** Two `vllm serve` instances of `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` (bf16, TP=1, `--enforce-eager`, `TieringOffloadingSpec` with one `fs` tier) sharing one `root_dir`, differing only in `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT`. One greedy completion (`seed=0`, 48 tokens), token ids compared. | run | layout | root | result | |---|---|---|---| | `A_cold` | LBNHC | shared | populates the tier; baseline | | `A_control` | LBNHC | shared | fresh process, same layout — matches `A_cold` | | **`B_shared`** | LBHNC | shared | fresh process, other layout — **48 tokens of garbage** | | `B_isolated` | LBHNC | private | control: the layout alone is fine — matches `A_cold` | Observed `B_shared` text: ```text ınaष linebackeres:hover_temperatureuality** heavilycl,exportsốcすぐすぐäsäh˝ashikut重重ashlştırl ``` `B_shared` reuses the existing block files — the `.bin` count in the shared root does not change, every lookup hits — and its log contains no error and nothing about the cache. The same LBHNC configuration against a private `root_dir` reproduces the baseline. The same script reproduces this on GB10 (sm_121, aarch64) with `nvidia/Cosmos-Reason2-2B`. The failure is silent and persistent: the digest matches, the size matches, the lookup hits, the model runs, and the polluted namespace survives restarts — the run that wrote it may be long gone. The canonical path is not affected, because `canonical_format` (`v1-nhd` / `v1-hnd`) already identifies the layout family. The `p2p` tier derives its peer-compatibility fingerprint from the same `FileMapper.fields`, so it has the same missing dimension. The same class of bug on the neighbouring model-runner axis was fixed in #49440. **Expected behaviour.** Runs whose persisted bytes are not interchangeable must not share a namespace, as is already the case for every other field of `FileMapper.fields`. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Model] Mamba2: Row-gated decode with full CUDA graphs in batch-invariant mode
body:
> **Conflict synchronization — October 15, 2026:** Head `11ee7f412189399894c10a61360fa8cc469b3cc4`, tree `f4a7030dc35fb242fa68c234861c52f5840d02c9`, incorporates main `c5f8adc0` and the updated stack dependencies through merge commits. The Mamba checkpoint length fix from main is retained. Existing PR history is preserved. The maintainer's Mamba2 RFC/hold remains in effect; this update does not request re-review.
>
> Codex performed the synchronization and checks. Historical GB200/model results and first-person human statements below remain attributed to their original revisions. Fresh human review and personal test execution of this synchronization are not attested.

### October 15 validation

**Runtime evidence from the synchronized downstream #56244 tree** `f179d2de751374dd390ffa0f9325cb8a7810d75f`: 30 passed, 17 failed and 3 two-GPU cases skipped across exact-replay, emit, attention and mixer selections. This does not establish a green runtime suite for this branch.

The `False-0-64` emit failure was reproduced on the untouched original `fc697366` at the same position 180 (chunk 2, offset 52). The emit implementation, test and six supporting kernel/helper files are byte-identical between that original, pre-sync `cda097cb` and the synchronized downstream tree. Only this one failure has a before/after negative control; the other 16 failures are not declared pre-existing. Two downstream model determinism attempts failed during EngineCore initialization because this source-only checkout lacks the build-generated `vllm.third_party.flashmla.flash_mla_interface`; they did not reach numerical assertions.

All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks passed on 22 files, including mypy targeting the oldest supported Python version. Each run exited 0 with no source modifications or blocked hook environments. The newly triggered upstream pre-commit run remains blocked by contributor eligibility; these local results are independent of upstream CI. PR-scope whitespace, Python syntax and Ruff checks passed.

Focused pytest selections:

```text
tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_exact_replay.py
tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_ssd_emit.py
tests/v1/attention/test_mamba2_batch_invariant.py
tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_mixer2.py -k "batch_invariant or fallback"
tests/v1/determinism/test_mamba2_batch_invariance.py
```

Execution used `uv run --no-project ~/vllm-run/.venv/bin/python <audit>/run-native-overlay-tests.py --candidate <checkout> --report <report> -- <pytest selection>`, with `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1`, offline model cache and a strict native-only import finder propagated to subprocesses. Candidate Python source was verified with zero installed-source fallback. WSL2/Python 3.12.3, RTX 4060 Laptop (SM89, 8 GiB), Torch 2.13.0+cu132 and Triton 3.7.1 were used. Reused native extensions come from installed baseline `cb6458c5`; current main requires Torch 2.14.0. This is partial local regression evidence, not a current-main native build, final model-output validation, multi-GPU validation or an upstream CI success.

## Purpose

Stacked on #57539 and #55627 (the exact-replay step and its wiring) and on #55895 (the pinned SSD tiles): this PR adds row-gated decode on top of those dependencies. Tracked in #55524.

#55627 makes Mamba2 prefill, chunked prefill and decode bitwise identical in `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` mode, but its decode step re-runs the chunked-scan kernels over the whole partial chunk and runs outside CUDA graphs. That costs about 10x decode throughput on a pure Mamba2 model and 12x on a hybrid. This PR keeps the semantics and the state layout of #55627 and replaces the decode step.

- Row-gated kernels compute only the new token's output row from the buffered inputs and the fp32 boundary state, and write the token's x, dt and B into the buffers. They reproduce the reduction order of the pinned prefill kernels (same head tile for the dt cumsum, same K blocks for the C·B row, same M/N/K tiles for the scan's dot products; smaller M tiles change the bits), so every row is bitwise that of a single-shot prefill. They grew out of the emit kernels of an earlier batch-invariant Mamba prototype, whose author is credited as co-author on that commit.
- A fold kernel runs over every row and returns early unless the row's token completes a chunk; for those rows it repeats the pinned chunk_state kernel over the buffered chunk and folds the result into the boundary state with an explicit `tl.fma`, the same instruction the state-passing kernel now uses, so the two round identically by construction.
- The decode metadata shrinks to one int32 tensor with each row's position inside its partial chunk, computed on the device and kept in a persistent buffer per KV cache group. CUDA graph padding rows get position 0 and never fold. Every step has shapes that depend only on the batch size, so decode-only batches run in full CUDA graphs as in default mode.
- Prefill keeps the replayed scan of #55627.

The kernels take their tiles from the pinned configurations of #55895; with autotuning the prefill side is not guaranteed to use them.

Not a duplicate: #54993 targets decode == recompute through a multi-token SSU replay; this PR targets decode == single-shot prefill through the chunked-scan arithmetic.

## Trade-offs

Each decode row still pays for a full 64-row M tile of the chunk-scan MMA to reproduce the prefill kernel's rounding, and the cumsum and C·B kernels are small launches, so the gap to the single-token update grows with the number of concurrent sequences. Throughput on GB200 (`vllm bench throughput`, 256-token prompts, 512 output tokens, FlashAttention 2 pinned on both sides, two repetitions, requests/s; measured on earlier revisions of the CUDA-graph commit, f198a7ec4 for the 128-request rows and 0b7c7ad3b for the rest; the later commits change kernel launch parameters and the split's imports but not the arithmetic, and were not re-benchmarked):

| model | prompts | default mode | #55627 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| mamba2-130m decode | 128 | 72.6, 72.2 | 7.4 | 30.8, 39.3 |
| mamba2-130m decode | 512 | 130.7, 131.6 | | 41.4, 47.5 |
| granite-4.0-h-350m decode | 128 | 38.1, 38.4 | 3.2 | 27.6, 25.0 |
| granite-4.0-h-350m decode | 512 | 63.2, 62.7 | | 31.3, 34.1 |
| mamba2-130m prefill (2048-token prompts) | 256 | 156.8 | same as this PR | 155.6 |
| granite-4.0-h-350m prefill | 256 | 143.5 | same as this PR | 95.5 |

Prefill is unchanged by this PR; the granite prefill row shows the cost of the mode on a hybrid, whose attention and MLP layers also run the batch-invariant kernels.

## Test Plan

```bash
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_ssd_emit.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_exact_replay.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_ssd_batch_invariance.py
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mamba2_batch_invariant.py
pytest tests/v1/determinism/test_mamba2_batch_invariance.py
```

The second determinism test covers a one-token prompt joining a batch that is already decoding, the shape the runner dispatches to a full CUDA graph while the Mamba builder keeps that request a prefill row.

Engine-level oracle, same harness as #55627: mamba2-130m with 8 concurrent requests at chunk-unaligned lengths, with and without `max_num_batched_tokens=100`, CUDA graphs and eager, plus TP2; granite-4.0-h-350m with `num_gpu_blocks_override=33` so one request is preempted, CUDA graphs and eager; Nemotron-H-8B-Base-8K at TP1 and TP2 with CUDA graphs.

## Test Result

GB200, Triton 3.7.1.

- 25 kernel-level cases pass (emit tests at chunk sizes 64, 128 and 256): emit at every position of a 3-chunk sequence equals the single-shot rows, the fold equals the single-shot chunk states and leaves rows that are not at a chunk end untouched, a 4-sequence prefill plus decode schedule with a padding row, plus the #57539 and pinned-config suites. 9 metadata and config cases pass, and both determinism tests pass with the default CUDA graph mode.
- Oracle: 0 mismatching logprobs in every configuration listed above (1190 generated tokens per mamba2-130m configuration, 5750 for granite and for Nemotron-H), all on the final commit.
- pre-commit passes on the changed files.

## AI assistance

AI tools assisted with the implementation, tests and documentation. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731: deterministic wrong token on deep-context exact retrieval at 1-in-4 prompt lengths (reasoning off) — vLLM 0.28.0 + SGLang, reproduced on two hosted providers (DeepInfra, Baidu); one provider (OpenInference) is correct
body:
## Summary
With reasoning disabled, an exact-string needle placed ~28k tokens into a ~57k-token prompt is returned with its last digit wrong (`PROVOCATIVE-8417` → `PROVOCATIVE-8411`) whenever the prompt length ≡ 3 (mod 4) tokens. It is deterministic (temperature 0, same wrong token every time), independent of the surrounding text (fully repetitive filler and a mixed filler both fail), and independent of the top-k backend. With reasoning enabled the same prompts are 16/16 correct. Needles early in the context, or with padding *after* the needle, are always correct.

The same checkpoint served by another provider (OpenRouter → OpenInference, fp8, reasoning_tokens=0) returns the correct code at the same prompt lengths; served by DeepInfra (fp8) and by Baidu (fp8) it returns the same wrong `8411` at every failing length. Four independent stacks agree on the wrong token; one provider does not — so this is not a property of the weights and not specific to our GPU.

## Environment (reporter)
- GPU: 4× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120), driver 580.173.02, CUDA 13.0
- vLLM 0.28.0 (`vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0`), torch 2.13.0+cu130, flashinfer 0.6.16.post3 (+cubin, +jit-cache cu130), vendored DeepGEMM, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.2
- Checkpoint: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` @ `7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062` (official; `quantization_config.scale_fmt=ue8m0`)
- Launch (from the official recipe's rtx_pro_6000_8x pill, TP=4):
  `--trust-remote-code --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 --attention_config.use_fp4_indexer_cache False --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --reasoning-config '{"reasoning_parser":"deepseek_v4","reasoning_start_str":"","reasoning_end_str":""}' --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"thinking": false}'`
- Startup log lines of note: `Selected DeepGemmFp8BlockScaledMMKernel for Fp8LinearMethod`, `Using FP8 indexer cache for Lightning Indexer`, `DeepGEMM E8M0 enabled`, `Using DeepSeek's fp8_ds_mla KV cache format`, `[AutoTuner]: Tuning sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4`
- Also reproduced (identical lengths, identical wrong token) on SGLang v0.5.18 and `nightly-dev-20260901-07c8f729` (`--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, dsv4 attention backend), with `--dsa-topk-backend sgl-kernel` and `torch`.

## Minimal reproduction
```python
import json, urllib.request
URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions"; M = "deepseek-v4-flash-0731"
fox = ("The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. " * 20 + "\n") * 285   # ~57k tokens
code = "PROVOCATIVE-8417"; Q = "\n\nWhat is the secret access code? Answer with just the code."
for n in range(16):  # 16 consecutive prompt lengths; every 4th fails
    q = "pad " * n + fox[:len(fox)//2] + f"\nThe secret access code is {code}.\n" + fox[len(fox)//2:] + Q
    b = {"model": M, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": q}], "max_tokens": 64, "temperature": 0,
         "chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking": False}}
    d = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(URL, data=json.dumps(b).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})))
    c = d["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]; print(d["usage"]["prompt_tokens"], "OK" if code in c else f"WRONG {c!r}")
```
Observed (vLLM 0.28.0, thinking off):
```
57316 OK 57317 OK 57318 OK 57319 WRONG 'PROVOCATIVE-8411' 57320 OK 57321 OK 57322 OK 57323 WRONG 'PROVOCATIVE-8411'
57324 OK 57325 OK 57326 OK 57327 WRONG 'PROVOCATIVE-8411' 57328 OK 57329 OK 57330 OK 57331 WRONG 'PROVOCATIVE-8411'
```
Same 16 lengths with `"thinking": True`: 16/16 OK. Mixed (non-repetitive) filler, thinking off: 4/16 wrong at 56730/56734/56738/56742 (same period). Padding appended *after* the needle instead of before it: 16/16 OK. Needle at ~4k tokens instead of ~28k: 16/16 OK.

## Cross-provider control (same checkpoint via OpenRouter, `reasoning: {enabled: false}`, reasoning_tokens=0, identical prompt_tokens)
| prompt_tokens | reporter vLLM 0.28.0 (sm_120) | reporter SGLang (sm_120) | OpenInference (fp8) | DeepInfra (fp8) | Baidu (fp8) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 57319 (bad) | 8411 | 8411 | refusal (unrelated) | **8411** | **8411** |
| 57323 (bad) | 8411 | 8411 | **8417** ✓ | **8411** | **8411** |
| 57327 (bad) | 8411 | 8411 | **8417** ✓ | **8411** | **8411** |
| 57331 (bad) | 8411 | 8411 | **8417** ✓ | **8411** | **8411** |
| 57318 / 57322 (good) | 8417 ✓ | 8417 ✓ | 8417 ✓ | 8417 ✓ | 8417 ✓ |

Four independent serving stacks (reporter's ×2, DeepInfra, Baidu) agree on the identical wrong token at the identical lengths; one provider (OpenInference) does not. Whether OpenInference deviates from the reference attention path (e.g. dense fallback) or has a fix is unknown to us. DeepSeek's first-party endpoint: not obtainable through our OpenRouter key policy.

## Expected
Exact retrieval should not depend on prompt length mod 4. The failing set is the DSA sparse-attention path with the needle deep in context; the mod-4 period and the single-token corruption suggest an indexer/logits or paged sparse-attention alignment issue rather than a model behavior.

_Repro script and provider-control scripts available on request; the minimal repro above is self-contained._

title: [ROCm] Removed branch logic that bypassed aiter sparse mla kernel due to old restrictions
body:
## Purpose

Fixes issue #55615. On gfx950, the ROCm AITER sparse-MLA decode path used to fall back to vLLM's native top-k kernel for small-batch (<= 256 rows), long-context (> 64 KiB compressed) shapes. That fallback existed only because early AITER (v0.1.19)
decode was "one-block only". Modern AITER handles these shapes correctly and is faster. This PR removes that decode fallback (and its two dead constants) so eligible gfx950 decode shapes use the AITER top-k kernel directly. No correctness change
(same top-k set); ~18-23% faster decode top-k at 64K-128K context.

## Testing

**Environment**
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` — vLLM `0.28.1rc1.dev516+g9ea8f3ffc`
- GPU: AMD MI350X (gfx950)
- AITER enabled (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`)

### 1. Unit tests
`tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py::test_aiter_c4a_topk_kernel_selection` — **4 passed**.
The two previously-ineligible decode cases now correctly select the AITER decode
kernel instead of returning `None`:
- `num_rows=1, max_valid_seq_len=65537`
- `num_rows=256, max_valid_seq_len=125000`

### 2. Dispatch (before vs after)
Same selector inputs, guard vs no-guard:
| num_rows | compressed seq len | old | my fix|
|---------:|-------------------:|-------------------|---------|
| 40       | 65536              | AITER             | AITER   |
| 40       | 131072             | `native`  | AITER   |
| 256      | 125000             | `native`  | AITER   |

(Boundary is correct: guard was strict `>`, so 65536 was already AITER.)

### 3. Correctness
AITER decode top-k vs `torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode` vs `torch.topk` reference at > 64K context: **100% top-k index-set agreement** across all rows and contexts tested.

### 4. Microbenchmark (AITER vs vLLM native, k=2048, fp32)
Median over 3x30 iters, rows in {16, 32, 40, 64}:
| compressed context | delta |
|--------------------:|-----------------|
| 65536               | **+23.1%**      |
| 131072              | **+18.4%**      |

Matches the issue's reported ~ -24% / -20%.

### 5. End-to-end smoke test
Served `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` (real sparse-MLA / indexer model, `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`, fp8) with my fix, TP=4, `--max-model-len 131072`.
- `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`; **FULL decode CUDA graphs captured at max_model_len=131072** — i.e. exactly the small-batch/long-context path the old guard diverted to native now runs the AITER decode kernel, and captured cleanly.
- Greedy (temp 0) generations coherent:
  - "The capital of France is" -> " Paris" (then "...Germany is Berlin...Italy is Rome")
  - "2 + 2 =" -> " 4"
  - "Water is made of hydrogen and" -> " oxygen"
  - "The opposite of hot is" -> " cold"

title: [Feature][Spec Decode] Add Uno shared-model drafting with a draft-only LoRA adapter (Model Runner V2)
body:
**TL;DR.** Speculative decoding with no separate draft model: the target model drafts its own candidates through a small LoRA adapter, and vLLM's native rejection sampler verifies them. Measured against plain vLLM on the same card, same client and same serving shape: **2.1 to 2.4x single-stream on a GB10 and 1.7 to 1.9x on an RTX 3090** with this implementation, and **2.6x on an H100** with our earlier Model Runner V1 build of the same design, which this implementation beats in every cell measured side by side. It stays ahead under load (1.1 to 1.6x at four and sixteen streams on the GB10; 2.2x at eight streams and 1.7x at 32 on the H100). Output is lossless: greedy tokens match plain wherever plain reproduces itself, sampled-distribution tests pass, GSM8K is within one answer of plain. Uno stays out of vLLM's core files: outside its own modules the PR adds a two-line hook call in the V2 model runner, a five-line request check, and configuration. Tested on NVIDIA Ampere, Hopper (FlashAttention 2 and 3) and Blackwell, single GPU and tensor parallel, and on an AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (ROCm, TRITON_ATTN). The reference SGLang implementation lands within 3% of the H100 build at every concurrency.

## Purpose

Adds native Uno self-drafting through `speculative_config.method="uno"` for Model Runner V2. One target model
produces `K` draft candidates per request from one base-weight seed row and `K-1` noise rows routed through the Uno
adapter; verification uses the native MRV2 rejection sampler. This follows the MRV2 direction agreed in
[RFC #55267](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55267). The earlier revision of this PR targeted Model Runner V1; this revision replaces it. Current head: reworked on 2026-10-11 so Uno stays out of vLLM's core files, on main at `ff440c7805`, then extended to AMD ROCm in Uno's own files; see the revision history below.

The change includes:

- A native MRV2 speculator that shares the target model, attention layers and KV cache with the drafter and applies the
  adapter only to noise rows, through the LoRA manager's public adapter-mapping call.
- Fused draft-input preparation in one kernel; the prompt length and the request count are runtime values, so it compiles once.
- Native request state, Gumbel sampling, verification, async scheduling and draft CUDA graphs; K lookahead KV slots
  with correct ownership at full acceptance, block boundaries, preemption and prefix-cache reuse. Near a request's length
  or context limit, the scheduler's existing per-request spec-token cap and lookahead cap apply; Uno adds no scheduler code.
- Startup and request validation (fail-closed for KV transfer, KV-sharing fast prefill, which would wrap the shared target and draft layers incorrectly and hand verification wrong prompt logits, pipeline/data/context parallelism, unsupported attention layouts, request-specific LoRA; tensor parallelism is supported and the draft uses the target's degree), a Qwen3-8B recipe ([the Uno docs page](https://github.com/brntech/vllm/blob/uno-core-upstream/docs/features/speculative_decoding/uno.md)), CPU regression tests and end-to-end model tests.

**Changes outside Uno's own files** (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/uno*.py`, its tests and docs):

| File | Lines | What |
|---|---:|---|
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` | +2 | a generic `speculator.set_lora_manager(...)` call after the speculator loads |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py` | +9 | that hook, a no-op on `BaseSpeculator` |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/__init__.py` | +4 | the factory branch |
| `vllm/config/speculative.py` | +47 | the method, its fields and their validation |
| `vllm/config/vllm.py` | +10 / −2 | K lookahead slots, the async-scheduling allowlists, the V1 refusal |
| `vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py` | +5 | refuses a request-specific LoRA adapter with Uno |
| `.buildkite/test_areas/spec_decode.yaml` | +30 | the Uno jobs |
| `tests/v1/core/` | +269 | scheduler and prefix-caching cases for Uno's lookahead slots |

`scheduler.py`, `async_scheduler.py`, `sched/output.py` and `warmup.py` are unchanged. AMD support adds no line outside Uno's own files.

**Platforms.** Uno runs on NVIDIA GPUs with the `FLASH_ATTN` or `TRITON_ATTN` attention backend, and on AMD ROCm GPUs with `--attention-config '{"backend":"TRITON_ATTN"}'`. It restricts the attention backend, not the card: it admits exactly the backends its tests run, and any other attention backend (FlashInfer included), or on ROCm an unset backend, is refused when the config is validated, before weights load. A backend must also pass the capability checks Uno already had (native draft decode metadata updates; graph support for draft graphs), and `load_model` re-checks the backend each layer built. On ROCm, Uno has been tested on the Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201); `TRITON_ATTN` on NVIDIA on one RTX 3090 (sm_86).

Initial scope is NVIDIA GPUs (single GPU and tensor parallel) and AMD ROCm GPUs (tested single-GPU on the Radeon AI PRO R9700), text-only decoder models with one homogeneous full-attention KV group, the attention backends above, Model Runner V2 with async scheduling. A draft decode graph is captured only when some `cudagraph_capture_sizes` entry is at most `max_num_seqs * K`. The documented adapter is the original [`s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B`](https://huggingface.co/s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B) for `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`.

Uno is introduced in [Unlocking Lossless Speedups in LLMs via Discrete Diffusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04010); the method and adapter are credited to its authors. Development was assisted by AI tools, disclosed in the commit
trailers. A ready-to-run container of this revision is published at [github.com/brntech/vllm-uno](https://github.com/brntech/vllm-uno) (release v0.2.0, image `ghcr.io/brntech/vllm-uno:0.2.0`).

## Test Plan

Base: `ff440c7805` (main, 2026-10-10).

CPU (container, Python 3.12, no GPU):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_config.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_prepare_mrv2.py \
       tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_lora_mrv2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_mrv2.py \
       tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_preemption.py -q
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
       tests/v1/engine/test_preprocess_error_handling.py -k uno -q
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only upstream/main HEAD)
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --all-files
```

GPU. Tested on NVIDIA Ampere, Hopper and Blackwell, single GPU and tensor parallel. The recorded Python-source overlay reproduces every GPU run on the base's per-commit CI image. Earlier revisions were run on a GB10 (Blackwell sm_121, ARM64), an H100 PCIe and an H100 NVL (FlashAttention 2 and 3), and at tensor-parallel 2 on two RTX 5090s (Blackwell sm_120); the current head was run on an RTX 3090 (Ampere sm_86) and an AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, ROCm 7.2):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_prepare_mrv2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_lora_mrv2.py -x -v
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_gumbel_sample.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py \
  -k 'logits_cache or drafting_uses_a_separate_noise_stream or greedy_temperature_zero or gumbel_drafted_rejection_sample_is_unbiased or greedy_rejection_sample or chunked_requests_match_full_batch or placeholder_draft_token_rejected' \
  -v
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py -v -s
# The greedy matrix on TRITON_ATTN on NVIDIA:
VLLM_UNO_TEST_ATTENTION_BACKEND=TRITON_ATTN pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py::test_uno_greedy_matches_base_model -v -s
# On ROCm the e2e module runs on TRITON_ATTN by default:
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_*.py tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py -v -s
```

## Test Result

### Throughput over plain vLLM

Every ratio is Uno divided by plain vLLM measured on the same card with the same client, model, precision and serving shape, in output tokens per second. GB10 and RTX 3090 figures are medians of three measured repeats after one warm-up; the H100 study reports mean per-prompt throughput at one stream and means of three warm batches at eight and 32 streams.

| Card | Workload | 1 stream | 4 / 8 streams | 16 / 32 streams |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| H100, earlier optimized MRV1 build (Qwen3-8B bf16, controlled, prefix caching off) | math | **2.58x** | 2.20x (8) | 1.74x (32) |
| GB10, this line at `49ffe316bb` (Qwen3-8B bf16, production shape) | short chat | **2.36x** | 1.31x (4) | 1.14x (16) |
| GB10 | long prompts | **2.21x** | 1.44x (4) | 1.15x (16) |
| GB10 | mixed | **2.06x** | 1.58x (4) | 1.12x (16) |
| RTX 3090, head `5da19391` (Qwen3-8B bf16, production shape) | short chat | **1.65x** | 1.18x (4) | 0.74x (16) |
| RTX 3090 | long prompts | **1.71x** | 1.13x (4) | 0.77x (16) |
| RTX 3090 | mixed | **1.85x** | 1.46x (4) | 0.72x (16) |

The H100 row is our earlier optimized Model Runner V1 implementation of the same design, measured in
[the study that IFM cites](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22652610) (single-prompt operating points on the same card: math 375 tokens/s, code 306, prose 212). The GB10 rows are this MRV2 line at `49ffe316bb` and the RTX 3090 rows head `5da19391`, both under one identical production shape (K=8, async scheduling, ctx 4096, `max_num_seqs` 16, 2048 batched tokens, 2 GiB KV, prefix caching, 128 output tokens). On the same GB10, with the optimized MRV1 release measured as a third arm, MRV2 exceeded it in all nine cells, by 1.03 to 1.31x. Uno is ahead wherever the card has compute headroom to verify drafts in: at four streams on every card, at sixteen on the GB10, at 32 on the H100. The reference SGLang implementation, measured on the same H100 against the same plain server, lands at 2.60x / 2.24x / 1.79x, within 3% of the H100 build at every concurrency.

### First-token latency

At head `5da19391`, same card, same client, median of three repeats: single-stream steady first token Uno 28.0 / 28.2 / 30.5 ms against plain 26.8 / 26.8 / 29.1 ms (short / mixed / long). The draft-input kernel takes the prompt length and the request count as runtime values, so it never recompiles for a new length or batch size. Since the rework there is no startup warmup of the draft sampler, so the first request compiles its sampler kernels.

### Lossless output

**Greedy exact-token matrix.** Seven K=1/K=8 cases (eager, CUDA graphs, prefix caching, dual-stream LoRA) compare Uno's greedy tokens with the plain engine's, each with a same-arm plain-vs-plain control. A first divergence is excused only where the plain engine's own top two raw logits are one bfloat16 step apart at that position, at most one prompt per batch, and every excused position is printed. Each case prints an instrument receipt (card, compute capability, graph mode, attention version, control coordinates, tie positions). At the current head the matrix also asserts that the attention implementation built is the requested backend's. RTX 3090, `TRITON_ATTN`: 7/7, every batch exact in tokens and text, no tie excused. RTX 3090, `FLASH_ATTN`: 7/7, exact except one excused tie in each of two cases (raw-logit gaps 0 and one bfloat16 step, at positions earlier rounds also met). R9700, `TRITON_ATTN`: 7/7, exact, no tie excused. Earlier heads: 7/7 on the GB10 and on the H100 under both FlashAttention 3 and 2.

**Context limit.** A nightly test serves four concurrent requests to `max_model_len` at K=8 and audits every draft KV slot against the limit and the request's block-table row; all four finish at exactly `max_model_len` with tokens and text equal to the plain engine's, and no draft row writes a slot at or past the limit.

**Sampled output.** Sampled-distribution permutation tests (256 samples for each of three prefixes, 16 tokens) pass for both Uno arms and for the independent plain-repeat control; raw greedy matches are 7/8 for both Uno arms against plain and 7/8 for plain against itself on a same-server repeat. GSM8K-128 (five-shot, temperature zero): plain 119/128, Uno MRV2 118/128, optimized MRV1 117/128.

### Request features under speculative decoding

Structured output (valid JSON from a `json_schema` request), logprobs, repetition and presence penalties and `ignore_eos` are all served with Uno drafting active. Min-p and logit bias are refused at admission by vLLM's general spec-decode guard, the same one EAGLE-3 hits. A request-specific LoRA adapter is refused before it is queued; a request can never select Uno's own adapter, including through a prebuilt `EngineCoreRequest` (a nightly test checks both, with exact outputs and the engine serving on).

### Continuous batching under KV pressure

The survivor test pins a 69-block KV pool, admits a seed request, two long peers and an abort peer, and asserts that a long peer is preempted while still generating and that its tokens after resumption equal its solo run. The pool is sized to force the crossing even when one long peer stalls at its admission footprint. It passed on the GB10, the H100 NVL (FlashAttention 3 and 2) and, at the current head, the RTX 3090 and the R9700. The test records the preemption at the scheduler's own event, resolves requests by the scheduler's internal ids, and writes its receipt to a file, so a non-firing run fails with a trace instead of skipping.

### Test counts

At the current head: CPU Uno modules 187 passed; pre-commit and mypy 3.12 clean (model runner V2 and factory 37, scheduler and prefix caching 391 at the previous head; this revision changes none of their files). The GPU rows below ran one local revision earlier; the only code change since removes an AMD chip check, so the unit suite now has one admission case fewer.

| Platform | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `FLASH_ATTN` | Uno unit tests | 202 passed |
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `FLASH_ATTN` | nightly group: context limit + KV-slot audit, survivor, prebuilt LoRA | 3/3 |
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `FLASH_ATTN` | 7-case greedy matrix | 7/7 (two excused bf16 ties) |
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `TRITON_ATTN` | 7-case greedy matrix | 7/7, no excused ties |
| Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), `TRITON_ATTN` | Uno unit tests | 202 passed |
| Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), `TRITON_ATTN` | e2e module: matrix, context limit, survivor, prebuilt LoRA | 10/10, no excused ties |

No package dependencies are added. The Uno Buildkite job triggers on the spec-decode paths only and runs the greedy matrix; the context-limit, survivor and prebuilt-request tests run in a nightly job.

## Not in this patch

Three optimisations are left out to keep changes to vLLM's core files minimal. Each would first need a small generic hook, and can follow as a separate PR if wanted:

- **Early length-tail policy:** stop drafting on a step that may be a request's last, saving `K` lookahead KV rows near its length or context limit. Needs a per-request "next draft width" that a speculator can set.
- **Startup draft warmup:** compile the draft sampler's kernels at startup instead of on the first request. Needs a speculator warmup hook beside the existing dummy-propose warmup.
- **Cached LoRA metadata:** reuse precomputed adapter mappings for the draft rows instead of rebuilding them every step. Needs a public way to reuse a LoRA mapping.

Together they are worth about 2% at 16 concurrent requests on an RTX 3090 (Qwen3-8B, K=8, 16 greedy chats × 256 tokens, 3 repeats: 710.7 vs 726.2 tokens/s); single-stream is unchanged within noise (103.6 vs 104.4).

## Revision history

**2026-10-11, AMD ROCm.** Uno runs on AMD ROCm GPUs with `TRITON_ATTN` (tested on the Radeon AI PRO R9700, gfx1201), and on NVIDIA with `TRITON_ATTN` as well as `FLASH_ATTN`. It admits exactly the attention backends its tests run: any other backend, FlashInfer included, and an unset backend on ROCm, are refused when the config is validated, before weights load. Only Uno's own files change; the core footprint is unchanged. The greedy matrix asserts the attention implementation it built, and the survivor test no longer holds its in-process engine across the runner exit (only ROCm's teardown memory wait caught that reference).

**2026-10-11, rework.** Uno now stays out of vLLM's core files. `scheduler.py`, `async_scheduler.py`, `sched/output.py` and `warmup.py` are back to main; the V2 model runner change is a two-line call to a generic `set_lora_manager` speculator hook (a no-op on `BaseSpeculator`), and Uno's serving checks moved next to the method. Dropped: the early length-tail policy (the scheduler's existing per-request cap and lookahead cap keep the context limit correct, checked by a new nightly test that audits every draft KV slot), the startup draft warmup (the draft-input kernel takes the request count as a runtime value instead), and the cached LoRA-metadata restore (draft rows use the LoRA manager's public mapping call). A request-specific LoRA adapter is refused in the input processor, and no request can select Uno's own adapter. The greedy matrix counts ties in bfloat16 steps of the raw logits. The Uno CI job triggers on spec-decode paths only; the longer end-to-end tests run nightly.

**2026-10-10, merge of main `ff440c7805`.** Conflict resolved in the V2 model runner: #60754 moved the drafter hidden-state helper to `spec_decode.utils.get_drafter_hidden_states` and renamed `dp_sync` to `dp_sync_state`; Uno's proposal path and `propose()` follow both. API adaptations: #60736 (request-slot index mappings are int64; Uno's draft sample mapping follows, and the fused input preparation refuses a non-int64 one) and #57169 (packed KV layout: `BlockTables.kernel_block_sizes` is gone, so Uno's slot preparation reads `block_sizes`, without which the engine failed at warmup; the draft graph replay maps the kernel block table first). Method and scope are unchanged.

**2026-10-06, merge of main `385d86a6cf`.** Conflicts resolved in the V2 model runner (#40704) and in the imports of `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`. Method and scope are unchanged.

**2026-10-05, merge of main `74c5cbcd7b`.** Conflicts resolved in `vllm/config/vllm.py` (Uno's lookahead rule beside #59105's fill-in DSpark rule) and the V2 model runner (#57053, dynamic K: Uno requires a fixed `num_speculative_tokens` and `UnoSpeculator.propose` accepts the new argument). Method and scope are unchanged.

**2026-10-04, merge of main `84bcbc6264`.** Conflicts resolved in `spec_decode.yaml` (#57237's split), `tests/v1/core/utils.py`, `vllm/config/vllm.py` (`dflash` and `uno` on the async allowlists), the scheduler and the V2 model runner; adapted to #56497, #56807 and test-side changes from #55939, #58459, #58784 and #59359.

**2026-09-17, cleanup pass (on a fresh merge of main `91a4c40b45`).** The per-step timing tracer, the launch-key debug module and the JIT-monitor hooks were removed entirely, with their switches and scheduler-output fields.

**2026-09-16.** Merged with main at `af1c0149`; a pre-commit fix; DCO sign-off on the two commits.

**2026-09-14.** Model Runner V2 revision replaces the V1 revision; rebased onto main at `b87339888d`.

title: [Perf] Add fused DFlash2 grouped convolution
body:
## Summary

- Fuse DFlash2's grouped dynamic convolution in one Triton custom op, keeping the existing Torch CPU fallback. The kernel stays in `qwen3_dflash2.py`.
- Use row-aligned tiles: 1024 elements for at least 128 rows with hidden width divisible by 1024, otherwise 512. Four warps; no autotuner.
- Cover non-power-of-two dimensions, strided coefficient views, multiple tap counts, and both tile paths in FP32/BF16.
- Add real-checkpoint GSM8K accuracy and acceptance-length coverage to the existing H200 35 GB DFlash nightly job. Keep this case excluded from its AMD mirror; the Speculators/MTP job is unchanged.

The implementation docstring credits LightSeek TokenSpeed PR https://github.com/lightseekorg/tokenspeed/pull/1399.

## End-to-end validation

One NVIDIA B300, TP=1, V2 model runner, compilation and CUDA graphs enabled. Target: `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`; unchanged BF16 draft: `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`. Full GSM8K: 1,319 questions, 5-shot chat, thinking disabled, temperature 0, max output 256 tokens, max model length 4,096, max batch 32, seven speculative tokens.

| Implementation | GSM8K accuracy | Mean acceptance length |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original Torch convolution, NVFP4 target, run 1 | 92.0% | 6.14 |
| Original Torch convolution, NVFP4 target, repeat | 91.2% | 6.13 |
| Fused kernel before final tuning, NVFP4 target, run 1 | 91.1% | 6.13 |
| Fused kernel before final tuning, NVFP4 target, repeat | 92.2% | 6.14 |
| Final row-aligned kernel, NVFP4 target | **92.2%** | **6.14** |

All passed. Acceptance length is `1 + accepted_tokens / draft_steps`. Accuracy varies across runs; this is not an exact-output-equivalence claim. The compiled draft graph was inspected to confirm it invokes the convolution custom op. CI checks accuracy >= 90% and AL >= `6.14 * 0.95` (5.833).

The NVFP4 target reduces reported target-plus-draft model-load memory from 54.0 GiB to 22.85 GiB; this is not total serving/KV-cache memory. The case runs in the existing H200 35 GB DFlash nightly job, with its 90-minute timeout unchanged, and remains excluded from the AMD mirror. H200 has a Marlin weight-only fallback for the NVFP4 target. Local validation was on B300; H200 execution and memory fit remain unverified.

Earlier BF16-target validation also passed: original Torch convolution 92.2% / AL 6.19; initial fused kernel 92.0% / AL 6.19 in two runs. CI now uses the smaller NVFP4 checkpoint instead.

## Kernel performance

### Initial fusion versus Torch (before the final row-aligned tuning)

Actual checkpoint shape: hidden size 5,120, BF16, block size 8, group size 16, two taps, strided coefficients. B300, FlashInfer CUPTI timing, CUDA graphs, cold L2, four alternating-order trials; median latency. Baseline is the existing expression under `torch.compile`. Correctness checked before timing.

| Batch | Torch / Triton latency (us) | Torch / Triton effective GB/s | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1.889 / 1.920 | 103 / 101 | 0.98x |
| 2 | 2.064 / 2.016 | 179 / 183 | 1.02x |
| 4 | 2.176 / 2.112 | 329 / 339 | 1.03x |
| 8 | 2.496 / 2.320 | 566 / 609 | 1.08x |
| 16 | 3.296 / 2.720 | 851 / 1,032 | 1.21x |
| 32 | 4.576 / 3.599 | 1,222 / 1,554 | 1.27x |

Effective bandwidth counts each input once and the output once: `2 * (2*rows*5120 + rows*2*320 + 2*5120)` bytes, `rows = batch*8`. These are kernel-only gains, not end-to-end speedups; batch 1 is approximately neutral.

### Final row-aligned tuning versus the posted fused kernel

Integrated confirmation on all 11 surveyed hidden-width/block-size pairs, at batches 1/32/256, BF16, group 16, two taps, strided coefficients. B300, CUPTI, CUDA graphs, cold L2, four alternating-order trials of 100 ms. Compared with posted commit `fd19503785`: batch 1 is effectively unchanged; batch 32 is 1.006–1.172x faster; batch 256 is 1.078–1.328x faster.

Representative batch-256 results (posted fused kernel → final tuned kernel):

| Hidden / block | Tile | Useful GB/s | Latency (us) | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2560 / 8 | 512 | 2649 → 2856 | 8.384 → 7.776 | 1.078x |
| 5120 / 8 | 1024 | 3038 → 3921 | 14.624 → 11.328 | 1.291x |
| 6656 / 16 | 512 | 3300 → 3610 | 35.057 → 32.049 | 1.094x |

Useful bytes = `2 * (2*rows*hidden + (2*rows-batch)*(hidden/16) + 2*hidden)`, excluding unused second-tap coefficients at block starts. This is an ideal useful-bandwidth estimate, not measured HBM traffic. These remain kernel-only speedups. Block-7/anchor/MoE entries in the shape sweep are kernel coverage, not full-model compatibility claims.

## Tests

All GPU workloads used `chg run -g=1 --`; no `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` overrides. Commands below assume the checkout's Python environment is activated (including its `bin` directory on PATH):

```bash
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py -q
chg run -g=1 -- env VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py -k dflash2
pre-commit run --files .buildkite/test_areas/spec_decode.yaml tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash2.py
```

- Focused suite: **16 passed**, including the aligned 1024-tile path and non-aligned 512-tile fallback.
- Integrated scratch boundary sweep: **570/570 bitwise comparisons passed** against the posted kernel. Covers all 11 model shape pairs, FP32/FP16/BF16, empty/one-row inputs, strided inputs/coefficients, ragged rows/widths, 1/2/3 taps, log-scaled values, and 127/128/129-row boundaries.
- Full NVFP4 model test: **1 passed** for each of the five runs above, including the final tuned implementation (**226.52 s**, including startup). First NVFP4 runs took about 5.5 minutes due to compilation/autotuning; warm-cache runs took 3.5–3.7 minutes. The smaller checkpoint is not a claim of faster CI.
- Changed-file pre-commit: **passed**, including mypy, SPDX, forbidden-import and CUDA API checks. CI YAML parsing/selection checks passed.
- Local environment: PyTorch 2.13.0, Triton 3.7.1, Transformers 5.15.0, FlashInfer 0.6.17. Initial startup failed on both branches due to a missing generated FlashMLA Python module in the worktrees; linking the existing installed artifact fixed the environment without code changes. The first NVFP4 attempt on both branches also stopped before evaluation because `ninja` was missing from PATH; using the already-installed venv `bin` directory resolved it without dependency/code changes.

## Duplicate work

Rechecked open vLLM PRs for `dflash2 conv`, `fused grouped conv`, and DFlash2 GSM8K/acceptance coverage. No other open PR implements this kernel/dispatch or this CI case. The companion TP-reduction and packed-top-k PRs remain separate.

AI assistance was used to analyze the upstream implementation, implement the change, and write/run the tests and benchmarks. Human submitter review is required before merge.

title: [KV Connector] Generalize declarative connector stats (TypedKVConnectorStats)
body:
## Summary

Generalizes the offloading connector's declarative stats into `kv_connector/v1/metrics.py` so any connector can report metrics without a per-connector `KVConnectorStats` / `KVConnectorPromMetrics` subclass:

- `MetricMetadata` / `CounterMetadata` / `GaugeMetadata` / `HistogramMetadata` (moved from `vllm/v1/kv_offload/base.py`; the `Offloading*Metadata` names remain as aliases).
- `TypedKVConnectorStats`: the self-describing `{types, data}` payload with `increase_counter` / `set_gauge` / `observe_histogram`, and type-driven `aggregate` / `reduce` / `is_empty`. `OffloadingConnectorStats` is now an alias of it.
- `TypedKVConnectorPromMetrics`: registers one Prometheus metric per definition and records payloads by metric type. `OffloadPromMetrics` subclasses it and only keeps the deprecated `transfer_type`-labelled CPU offload metrics.

Because every connector using this shares one concrete stats type keyed by metric name, metrics from different families compose by recording into the same instance (or aggregating), and `MultiConnector` continues to work unchanged. Nixl / Mooncake / HF3FS keep their bespoke stats classes; the base interface does not change.

The next PR in this stack (HiSparse cache metrics) is the first non-offloading user.

Not duplicating an open PR: searched open PRs for "KVConnectorStats", "typed"/"declarative" connector metrics, and "connector metrics definitions"; #50878 (external metrics providers for stat logger plugins) and #41790 (SimpleCPU offload metrics) are unrelated.

## Tests

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_typed_metrics.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ tests/v1/kv_offload/ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py -q
```
- `test_typed_metrics.py` + `offloading_connector/` + `kv_offload/`: 913 passed, 16 failed. All 16 failures are `test_scheduler.py::test_swa_offload_window_covers_unaligned_hit`, which fails identically on the base commit (`f3d4fa2394`, `SimpleNamespace` fixture has no `.config`) and is untouched here.
- `test_multi_connector.py`: 22 passed, 1 failed (`test_multi_example_connector_consistency`, fails identically on the base commit).
- `test_offloading_connector.py` (e2e): could not run in my environment (`ModuleNotFoundError: flash_attn` during CUDA-graph profiling).
- `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual` on the changed files: passed.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the implementation and for the review of the original HiSparse metrics diff that motivated this change.

title: [HiSparse] Expose cache metrics via typed KV connector stats
body:
## Summary

Reworks #53782 on top of the typed connector stats from #55969 so HiSparse cache metrics flow through the existing `KVConnectorStats` pipeline with no HiSparse-specific code in the model runner, output aggregator, scheduler, or Prometheus logger:

- The swap-in kernel accumulates hot-buffer hits and misses into a per-index-group `uint64[2]` device counter (unchanged from #53782).
- `HiSparseConnectorWorker.get_kv_connector_stats()` snapshots the counters every 2,000 worker steps via a pinned host copy ordered after in-flight swaps, and reports the completed delta as a `TypedKVConnectorStats` with three counters: `vllm:hisparse_cache_hits`, `vllm:hisparse_cache_misses`, `vllm:hisparse_host_to_device_bytes`.
- `HiSparseConnector` declares its metrics in `hisparse/metrics.py` and implements `get_kv_connector_stats` / `build_kv_connector_stats` / `build_prom_metrics` with the generic classes, so no stats subclass is needed and the stats compose with other metric families (e.g. inside `MultiConnector`).

Compared to #53782 this removes `KVConnectorBase_V1.finish_step`, `ModelRunnerOutput.hisparse_stats`, `SchedulerStats.hisparse_stats`, `HiSparseStats`, the aggregator branch, and the hard-coded counters in `PrometheusStatLogger`; it also picks up the `no_forward` and `MultiConnector` paths for free since they already call `get_kv_connector_stats`. The stats assertion in `test_hisparse_swap_in_preserves_rows_across_eviction` is fixed to use the real `swap_in` signature.

Known follow-ups (carried over from #53782, not addressed here): dummy runs (profiling, eager warmup, DP idle steps) still increment the device counters; hits/misses are summed across TP ranks; the 2,000-step sampling interval hides short runs.

Stacked on #55969; intended to replace #53782 (which #55398 currently stacks on) once reviewed.

## Tests

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_typed_metrics.py -q
```
42 passed.

```
chg run -g 1 -- pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "hisparse_swap_in_preserves_rows_across_eviction or hisparse_multi_step" -q
```
2 passed. Also `-k hisparse` over the whole file: 30 passed (H100, extensions rebuilt from this branch's csrc). `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual` on the HiSparse files: passed.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the implementation; the original metrics collection is from #53782.
