title: [Perf] Trim redundant per-step Python work on the GDN decode and V2 spec-decode paths
body:
## Purpose

Eleven small, semantics-preserving rewrites on lines that run once to forty-eight times per engine step, in the GDN/causal-conv1d decode path and in the V2 runner's speculative-decoding path. No configuration is touched, no new state or invariant is introduced; every hunk is a local rewrite whose output is the same object, value, dtype and shape as before.

Why it matters: with piecewise cudagraphs the CPU sits on the critical path of every step. On the deployment this was written against (Qwen3.8-27B hybrid, 48 GDN + 16 full-attention layers, MTP k=3, FlashInfer, RTX 4090) an nsys profile put the GPU idle for 4.16 ms of a 24.73 ms step across ~1445 launches -- the GPU is waiting on Python. These are the Python lines that were doing redundant work on that path, each measured.

### What changes, and how often it runs

**`vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/` -- once per GDN layer per step (48x on this model), both runners**

| hunk | before | after | per call |
|---|---|---|---|
| `qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py`, 4 sites | `self.conv1d.weight` read 3x to build one view (each read = two `nn.Module.__getattr__` hops) | bound once | 0.92 µs |
| `causal_conv1d.py` dtype-in | `x = x.to(conv_state.dtype)` dispatched unconditionally | guarded on dtype inequality | 0.31 µs |
| `causal_conv1d.py` dtype-out, 2 sites | `return out.to(original_x_dtype)` | same guard | 0.31 µs |
| `causal_conv1d.py` next_power_of_2, 2 sites | `triton.next_power_of_2` (8-step twiddle) | `vllm.utils.math_utils.next_power_of_2` (one shift), already used by 18 modules | 0.19 µs |

`Tensor.to(same_dtype)` returns `self`, so the guards yield the identical object and only skip the ATen dispatch; under the default `mamba_cache_dtype="auto"` the conv state has the model dtype and both conversions were no-ops. The two `next_power_of_2` implementations agree for every n ≥ 1; `state_len` here is `width-1` (or `width-1 + seqlen-1` on the spec path) with `width ≥ 2`.

**`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/` -- once or twice per step, V2 runner**

| hunk | what goes away | per step |
|---|---|---|
| `model_runner.py` cumsum | a separate `.sum()` pass; the total is the cumsum's last element | ~0.7 µs |
| `rejection_sampler.py` zero rebase | `- lo` when `lo == 0` (the single-chunk case, i.e. the common one): one `aten::sub` dispatch, one allocation, one `cudaLaunchKernel`, on the gap between target forward and first draft | ~2 µs + 1 launch |
| `speculator.py` double slice | `buf[:n][:n]` -- `build_attn_metadata` re-applies the same bound as its first statement | 0.7 µs × 2 |
| `attn_utils.py` empty groups | building and discarding a 27-field `CommonAttentionMetadata` plus tensor selects for every KV-cache group the drafter owns no layer in (3 of 4 on this model) | 6.8 → 1.9 µs × 2 builds |

The rejection-sampler change swaps a fresh tensor for a view of the input-batch buffer when `lo == 0`. Every consumer of `chunk_cu_num_logits` only reads it (the verify kernels `tl.load`; the one escaping use is cloned), so the aliasing is not observable; the guard tests the value rather than trusting the invariant, so it stays correct if a chunk ever starts at a non-zero offset.

Total on a V2 deployment of this shape, from the per-call numbers: roughly 100 µs per step, ≈0.4 % of a 25 ms step. This is offered as cleanup with a measured benefit, not as a headline win. Happy to split it by area (`mamba/` vs `v1/worker/gpu/`) if that is preferred.

### Verified and deliberately left out

Two further hunks were verified to the same standard and dropped from this PR: a dirty flag to skip `num_blocks.copy_to_uva()` on steps with no block appends, and caching `slot_mappings.shape[1]`/`stride(0)`. Both add state for ≤4 µs per step; the risk/benefit did not clear the bar.

## Test Plan

**Component-level differential test (GPU).** The real functions were run under the stock tree and under this branch with fixed seeded inputs and the produced bytes hashed: `causal_conv1d_update` across bfloat16/float16/float32 decode and across 24 `(kernel_width, query_len)` combinations on the spec-decode varlen path (the range over which `NP2_STATELEN` actually varies); `causal_conv1d_fn` (the chunked-prefill path, which carries two of the patched lines) across 3 widths × 3 sequence layouts; the `nn.Module` attribute-identity property the weight hoist relies on, checked against `ColumnParallelLinear`'s MRO for a `weight` property or pre-hook; `next_power_of_2` vs `triton.next_power_of_2` for n in 1..19999; the cumsum identity over 1080 random batch shapes including `num_reqs == 0`; slice-minus-zero and double-slice view identity on device. The harness fails hard if any case raises, so a case that raises identically in both trees cannot pass as a false match.

**CPU equivalence checks.** 29 property checks pinning exactly what each rewrite depends on (`.to(same)` is `self` incl. non-contiguous and 0-dim; `x[a:b] - 0` is value/dtype-identical to `x[a:b]`; empty-group loop contributes nothing across five layouts; etc.).

**Premise re-check against current `main`.** The hunks were authored against v0.28.0; `main` has since changed five of the six files (`attn_utils.py` by 463 lines, `model_runner.py` by 493). Every anchor still matches verbatim, and each hunk's premise was re-established statement by statement against the code as it is now (e.g. all three `get_extra_common_attn_kwargs` implementations return a fresh dict; `CommonAttentionMetadata` has no `__post_init__`; every `seq_lens` consumer sees the callee's slice, never the full buffer).

**Lint.** `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on all six files.

**Upstream tests, on the branch itself.** Every test file that imports one of the six touched modules (16 files), run against this branch using the documented Python-only build -- `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 pip install -e .` in a fresh venv, which pairs the branch's Python with the compiled extensions published for its base commit `5af4cc33e` -- on an RTX 4090.

**End-to-end.** Greedy (temperature 0, fixed seed) completions on four prompts are byte-identical to a control build of the same compile provenance.

## Test Result

- Component-level: **bit-identical** to stock in every case, 11 cases, 0 raised.
- CPU equivalence: 29/29 pass.
- ruff: clean.
- Upstream tests on the branch (`VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1` over `5af4cc33e`, RTX 4090): **275 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed.**

| file | result |
|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py` | 164 passed |
| `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py` | 19 passed |
| `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py` | 17 passed |
| `tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py` | 16 passed |
| `tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_fused_mtp.py` | 16 passed |
| `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py` | 10 passed |
| `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py` | 7 passed |
| `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py` | 7 passed |
| `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py` | 5 passed |
| `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle_draft_attn_metadata.py` | 4 passed |
| `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_extract_hidden_states_speculator.py` | 4 passed |
| `tests/v1/worker/test_kv_cache_allocation_scope.py` | 3 passed |
| `tests/v1/streaming_input/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_streaming.py` | 2 passed |
| `tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_prefill_flashinfer.py` | 1 passed |
| `tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_split.py` | skipped -- CuteDSL prefill backend, requires SM10x |
| `tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py` | skipped -- CPU-only |

**Timing, stated honestly.** On the author's deployment the engine selects the **V1** model runner, so of the eleven hunks only the five under `model_executor/layers/mamba/` execute there; the V2-runner hunks are exercised by the component tests above and by CI, not by this timing run. A 6-round paired study (stock / compile-matched sham / this branch, arm order rotated through a Latin square, seed shared within a round, rounds as the independent unit) measured this branch against the sham at

```
ITL median:  +0.016 %   CI95 [−0.063, +0.095]   p = 0.63   MDE(80 %) = 0.107 %
```

i.e. neutral within a resolution of ~0.1 %. Two methodological notes that may be useful to others measuring small changes here: (1) any edit to files under `model_executor/` invalidates the `torch.compile` AOT artifact and the build is recompiled on every launch, so the control arm must touch the same files or it does not control that axis -- on this rig that asymmetry alone measured +0.117 % (p = 0.034); (2) with `benchmark_combo_kernel=True` two builds with different source hashes can select different combo kernels, which is why the byte-identical output check is done against a same-provenance control rather than against stock.

title: [Model Loader] Bound fastsafetensors peak memory with the 0.4 fit planner
body:
## Purpose

`--load-format fastsafetensors` stages a whole shard per rank in device memory
before distributing it, so peak load memory tracks the checkpoint's shard layout
rather than the memory actually available. Where a shard is large relative to
free memory, the load runs out of memory on a model that otherwise fits.

fastsafetensors 0.4 provides a fit planner for exactly this: whole-file loads
while headroom is ample, per-file chunk budgets declining as the device fills.
Its budget is caller-supplied by design (`parallel_loader.py`, 0.4.0):

> **The caller picks the number — it knows what else lives on the device and,
> under broadcast loading, must pass the same value on every rank (e.g.
> all-reduce(MIN) of each rank's free memory)** so the plan stays identical
> across ranks.

This PR computes that budget from free device memory, agrees it across ranks
with all-reduce MIN, and passes it — with `use_chunk_budget_as_allocation_size`
for how chunks are sized, `accumulate_resident` for whether the consumer's
memory grows during the load, and `BudgetInfeasibleError` handled for a plan
that cannot be satisfied. It raises the dependency floor from
`fastsafetensors >= 0.3.3` to `>= 0.4`, which is where the planner lands.

## meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B

Public checkpoint, 55.5 GiB in 2 shards: largest shard 46.52 GiB, largest tensor
2.505 GiB. Single 96 GB card, weight-load time from vLLM's own log line:

| loader | weight load |
| --- | ---: |
| default (`auto`) | 52.74 s |
| `fastsafetensors`, main + 0.4.0 | **OOM** — `Tried to allocate 46.52 GiB`, 38.31 GiB free |
| `fastsafetensors`, this PR | **10.16 s** |

The planner needs twice the largest tensor, 5.01 GiB. Reported independently by
the fastsafetensors maintainer on a single 80 GB A100/H100
(foundation-model-stack/fastsafetensors#71).

## What this changes

- **Device memory budget**, derived from free device memory and reduced with
  all-reduce MIN so every rank plans identically. Shards larger than the budget
  load in sub-shard chunks, each capped at `2 x` the largest tensor the load
  keeps: a chunk must hold that tensor, the second copy lets the producer read
  ahead, and beyond it the cap stops binding (measured: `T` +7.4% load time,
  `2T` +2.4%, `4T` identical to uncapped). The budget carries the reason when
  it is absent -- asked for, residency not modellable, free memory unreadable,
  or no memory to reserve from -- so an unplanned load can be explained.
  Planned loads select buffered reads up front, since the 0.4 GDS copier cannot
  chunk; `VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_DEVICE_MEMORY_BUDGET=0` selects GDS instead.
- **`accumulate_resident=False`.** Every quant method reachable from this loader
  creates its parameters at model-init time, so the load only copies into memory
  already allocated — measured on the default path, free device memory is
  unchanged across `load_weights()`. Online quantization is the exception: it
  materializes a smaller quantized parameter than the bytes it reads, which the
  plan would over-charge, so those loads are left unplanned unless a budget is
  set explicitly.
- **The budget all-reduce is unconditional**, with `0` meaning unbounded. A rank
  returning early — no reading, too little free memory, an unplannable consumer —
  would leave the others blocked in the reduce while it went on to the loader's
  broadcast sequence.
- **An infeasible plan raises**, naming the shortfall, rather than falling back
  to whole-shard staging — which needs a buffer at least as large as the tensor
  the plan could not place, so it is more likely to run out of memory, not less.
- **`VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_ALL_LOCAL`** (opt-in, off by default). Every rank reads
  the whole checkpoint from storage instead of one rank reading and
  broadcasting. Enable it when ranks read from storage they do not share: on
  2x GB10 over RoCE, each node reading its own NVMe copy loads
  Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 in 16.6 s against 21.8 s broadcasting (n=2 per arm,
  non-overlapping). On a single node whose ranks share one NVMe it is a loss
  (43.2 s against 29.6 s), because the extra reads land on the contended device
  and the broadcast being avoided is cheap.
- **`VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_DEVICE_MEMORY_BUDGET`** overrides the derived budget;
  `0` removes the bound and stages whole shards. An escape hatch for a plan you
  believe is wrong, not a remedy for insufficient memory — and not the only
  route to an unbounded load, since one also runs unbounded when no budget can
  be derived.

Docs: `LoadConfig.load_format` now lists `"fastsafetensors"`, and the extension
page gains `VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_QUEUE_SIZE`, the TP>1 GDS behavior, when
`ALL_LOCAL` pays, the online-quant exemption, and the `2 x largest tensor`
planning floor that decides whether a checkpoint is loadable by this format.

## Found deploying it at TP4 + DCP2 on 4x GB10 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 475 GiB)

- **Budget agreed on gloo, not CUDA over `WORLD`.** vLLM computes on the
  TP/DCP/EP subgroups, so `WORLD` often has no NCCL communicator at load time
  and the 8-byte budget `all_reduce` created one. NCCL's proxy connect pins
  ~9.19 MiB of host memory per connection for the communicator's lifetime,
  invisible to `torch.cuda.host_memory_stats()`. Reducing on
  `get_world_group().cpu_group` issues no NCCL collective during the load, as
  `--load-format auto` issues none. Host `Shmem` after load:

  | | Shmem after load | MemAvailable after release | boot |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
  | `--load-format auto` | 8.21 GiB (+0.00) | 31.08 GiB | healthy |
  | fastsafetensors, CUDA reduce | 12.06 GiB (**+3.85**) | 27.60 GiB | dies in FlashInfer autotune |
  | fastsafetensors, gloo reduce | 8.35 GiB (**+0.13**) | 30.12 GiB | healthy |

  Wasteful on a discrete GPU; on unified memory it comes out of the pool that
  KV cache and graph capture need.
- **EP filter honoured.** `default_loader` did not pass `local_expert_ids` to
  `fastsafetensors_weights_iterator`, so under expert parallelism this format
  read every expert while `auto` skips the ones the rank does not own (experts
  are ~85-90% of weight bytes). Now both formats select the same tensors. A
  `tensor_filter` is incompatible with broadcast, so a filtered load reads
  all-local. Verified on Qwen3-Coder-Next-FP8 (512 experts) at TP2 +
  `--enable-expert-parallel --enable-ep-weight-filter`: `loading 256/512
  experts` on both ranks, and generations byte-identical to `auto`.
- **Chunk cap sized from kept tensors.** `_safetensors_largest_tensor` takes the
  loader's predicate, so a tensor that is never read cannot set the cap. With
  DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's on-disk Engram tables it was 183 GiB instead of
  2.47 GiB, and the cap bounded nothing.

With all three the model boots and serves (count-to-100 exact, 30/30
structured-output gate, 7/7 vision + tool calling, KV pool unchanged), loading
in 54-63 s per rank against 133-177 s for `auto` on the same local shards.

## Validation

Three tests added to `tests/model_executor/model_loader/fastsafetensors_loader/`:

- `test_fastsafetensors_sub_shard_chunking` — a 384 MiB budget forces GPT-2's
  522 MiB shard to load as four chunks, which must still match
  `safetensors_weights_iterator` bitwise.
- `test_fastsafetensors_budget_infeasible` — a 1 MiB budget must raise
  `BudgetInfeasibleError` naming the shortfall, covering the no-fallback policy.
- `test_fastsafetensors_accumulate_resident_skips_derived_budget` — the same
  budget that raises above must load when the consumer's residency cannot be
  modelled, covering the online-quant exemption.

All run single-rank. At TP=2 on a checkpoint that already fits
(DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 3.4 GiB shards) load time is unchanged: 29.26 / 29.62 /
29.68 s against 28.62 / 30.00 s for stock.

Rebased on `19b0efce3`. On GB10 at `47232f3c7` (torch 2.14.0) with fastsafetensors
0.4.0, the `fastsafetensors_loader/` suite goes from 3 passed (base) to 6 passed. Upstream
#60152 now filters the shard list before this iterator; the planner sees
the filtered list, identically on every rank.

Lockfiles (`requirements/test/{cpu,cuda,rocm}.txt`) regenerated against
fastsafetensors 0.4.0 — one line per file, no other dependency changes.

## Model evaluation

This changes how weight bytes reach the device, not what they are; the chunking
path asserts bitwise equality against the reference safetensors iterator.

Generation across loaders at TP=2 with expert parallelism on DeepSeek-V4-Flash
was correct and coherent in every configuration. Token-level identity is not
asserted — that configuration is not reproducible run-to-run even at
`temperature=0` with a fixed seed.

## Duplicate check

Nothing open addresses this. The adjacent PRs are complementary:

- **#51554** adds a `fastsafetensors_sharded` load format in
  `sharded_state_loader.py` for pre-sharded checkpoints; this PR changes the
  default `fastsafetensors` path in `weight_utils.py`. The two touch
  `docs/models/extensions/fastsafetensor.md` in common — happy to rebase around
  whichever lands first.
- **#54416** (merged) fixes a PP draft-model deadlock by falling back to the
  standard loader; different failure, different code path.
- **#57973** (safetensors prefetch, successor to #52462) and **#53901** (ROCm PP)
  are unrelated axes.

## Upstream coordination

The fastsafetensors changes this depends on are merged and released in 0.4.0
(foundation-model-stack #81, #90, #91, #108). `BudgetInfeasibleError` is
exported from the package root, so vLLM catches it without importing a private
module. Design discussion: foundation-model-stack/fastsafetensors#71.

## AI assistance disclosure

Claude Code was used to survey the integration points, draft the loader change,
docs and tests, and run pre-commit; and to run and analyse the measurements
reported above. The submitter authored the original loader integration (#40183),
produced the benchmark results on their own hardware, has reviewed every changed
line, and will maintain the contribution and respond to review feedback.

title: [ROCm][AITER] Skip AITER norm kernels when flattening to 2D would copy
body:
## Purpose

The AITER norm kernels take 2-D inputs only, so the wrappers in
`vllm/kernels/aiter_ops.py` flatten the leading dims with `Tensor.reshape`:

```python
if x.dim() > 2:
    x_original_shape = x.shape
    x = x.reshape(-1, x_original_shape[-1])
```

`reshape` silently degrades to `.contiguous()` when the flattened shape is not
expressible with the input's strides, injecting a whole-tensor device copy. The
support predicates (`rms_no_var_16bit_only`, `rms_add_no_var_16bit_only`) check
only dtype and `variance_size`, so AITER is still selected in that case — and
the copy costs more than the kernel saves.

Per-head QK norm hits this on every layer: `q`/`k` are last-dim slices of the
fused QKV projection viewed as `(num_tokens, num_heads, head_dim)`, whose
leading dims cannot be merged without a copy. Qwen3-8B at 4096 tokens:

```
q_by_head  shape=(4096, 32, 128)  stride=(6144, 128, 1)  is_contiguous=False
q_by_head.reshape(-1, 128) shares storage: False   # full 4096x4096 bf16 copy
```

This adds `flatten_to_2d_is_free(x)` and requires it in both predicates. When it
returns `False`, `IrOp.dispatch` falls through to the next provider — on ROCm
`native`, i.e. Inductor codegen, which consumes arbitrary strides directly and
fuses the norm into its neighbours. Numerically equivalent; only the copy is
gone. The predicate runs once per graph node during `VllmIRLoweringPass`, not
per forward, so it costs nothing at steady state.

**Scope.** Only a rank > 2 input that is a slice of a larger buffer can be
affected; a contiguous rank-3 tensor flattens for free and still dispatches to
AITER. The dividing line is the norm class, not the model family: the 9 in-tree
files whose QK norms are `GemmaRMSNorm` (gemma, gemma2, gemma3, gemma3_mm,
qwen3_5, qwen3_next, rnj1, step3p5, step3p5_mtp) pass an fp32 weight and already
fail the pre-existing `weight.dtype == x.dtype` check, one condition *before* the
new guard, so their dispatch cannot change in either direction. The ~27 files
that build `RMSNorm(head_dim)` for per-head QK norm (qwen3, qwen3_moe, gemma4,
glm4_moe, exaone4, plamo3, lfm2, lfm2_moe, apertus, afmoe, …) are candidates for
the win.

## Test Plan

New `tests/kernels/ir/test_aiter_norm_dispatch.py` asserts the predicate agrees
with whether `reshape` preserves the storage pointer, over flattenable and
non-flattenable layouts.

End-to-end, on 1x MI355X (gfx950) and 1x MI325X (gfx942), TP=1:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=1

vllm bench throughput --model <model> \
  --input-len 1024 --output-len 128 --num-prompts 1000 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code
```

Three interleaved base/patched pairs per model with the order alternated per
repeat, so drift and thermal ramp are shared rather than charged to one variant;
deltas are pairwise and the reported figure is the median. Each arm gets its own
`VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` **and** `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` — `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE`
alone does not stop Inductor's FX graph cache, and a shared cache lets the
patched arm reuse graphs the base arm compiled, erasing the difference being
measured. The change is Python-only, so both arms share the same compiled `.so`.

Kernel level: the per-head QK-norm geometries the dispatch probe actually
observed, x {1024, 2048, 4096, 8192} tokens x {q, k}, bf16, compiled through
`VllmIRLoweringPass` with priority `["aiter", "native"]`. Per-call GPU time from
replaying a captured graph over 4 rotating input buffers (so the copy is not
absorbed by Infinity Cache), refill timed separately and subtracted.

Dispatch probe: instrumented the predicate to log every distinct
`(shape, stride, dtype, verdict)` reaching it, per model, with a cold Inductor
cache so the lowering pass reruns.

## Test Result

New tests pass (8/8). Numerics match `native` within `atol=rtol=2e-2` across
bf16/fp16 and contiguous / per-head-strided shapes.

### End-to-end throughput

| Model | dispatch | MI355X (gfx950) | MI325X (gfx942) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B (`qwen3_moe`) | 2/3 rejected | **+5.17 %** | **+6.87 %** |
| lfm2-1.2b (`lfm2`) | 2/3 rejected | **+3.19 %** | **+3.28 %** |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it (`gemma4`) | 4/6 rejected | **+2.37 %** | **+2.34 %** |
| Gryphe-Gemma-4-31B-StyleTune (`gemma4`) | 4/6 rejected | **+2.48 %** | — |
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B (`qwen3_5`) | 0/4 reach the guard | no-op control | — |

Every pair is positive on both architectures, including the reversed-order
pairs. Within-variant spread is 0.06–1.03 % except lfm2-1.2b (2.2 %), whose run
is short enough that scheduler ramp dominates. Qwen3-30B-A3B is the cleanest
signal: +5.17 % against a 0.10–0.21 % spread on gfx950. KV cache size matched to
within 0.01 % between arms on every model.

Qwen3.5-122B-A10B is the control: `Qwen3NextAttention` does apply per-head QK
norm on a fused-QKV slice, so it looks like the exact target pattern, but all 28
predicate calls are rejected on weight dtype and **0** reach the flatten guard.
Same for Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 at TP=2 and TP=4 (26/26 and 44/44).

### Kernel level

Sum of best-of-3 x 200 iters over all cases:

| Input layout | `aiter` | `native` | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| gfx950 — per-head slice of fused QKV | 1601.4 us | 814.0 us | **1.97x** |
| gfx950 — contiguous per-head (control) | 1007.5 us | 689.3 us | |
| gfx942 — per-head slice of fused QKV | 2635.7 us | 671.9 us | **3.9x** |
| gfx942 — contiguous per-head (control) | 2061.3 us | 650.8 us | |

Splitting the saving by holding the provider at `aiter` and only making the input
contiguous: the hidden copy this PR removes is **75 %** of the win on gfx950 and
**29 %** on gfx942, the remainder being AITER's norm kernel trailing Inductor
codegen at `head_dim`-wide rows, independent of any copy. `native` is close to
layout-insensitive — the strided slice costs it +18 % on gfx950 and +3.2 % on
gfx942, where `aiter` pays +59 % and +28 % — confirming the patch's load-bearing
assumption that Inductor consumes arbitrary strides without materialising a copy.

On the patched tree all slice cases select `native` (814.0 us, matching the
forced-`native` control) and all contiguous cases still select `aiter`,
confirming the guard moves only the layout it targets.

### Dispatch coverage

| Model | implementation | layouts | rejected |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-8B / Qwen3-14B-FP8 / Qwen3-30B-A3B | `qwen3`, `qwen3_moe` | 3 | **2** |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it / Gryphe-Gemma-4-31B | `gemma4` | 6 | **4** |
| lfm2-1.2b | `lfm2` | 3 | **2** |
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 | `qwen3_5` | 0 | 0 |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | `deepseek_v4`, MLA | 53 | 0 |
| MiniMax-M2.7 | MoE, norms already 2-D | 4 | 0 |
| Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 | no QK norm | 1 | 0 |

Qwen3-8B rejects exactly the two QK-norm layouts `(s, 32, 128)` and `(s, 8, 128)`,
both `stride=(6144, 128, 1)` — `6144` being the fused QKV row stride. Matching
counts on Qwen3-14B-FP8 show quantization is orthogonal. gemma-4 is a broader
case: 4 of 6 layouts rejected across two distinct QKV geometries, while one of
its accepted layouts is a *contiguous* rank-3 vision-tower activation
(`[1, 2048, 1152]`, stride `[2359296, 1152, 1]`), showing the guard rejects
strided slices specifically rather than rank-3 inputs generally.

Unaffected by structure, measured rather than assumed: DeepSeek-V4-Flash and
MiniMax-M2.7 reach the guard with zero rejections, every input 2-D contiguous.
GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) and Kimi-Linear-48B resolve to MLA
implementations (`deepseek_v32`, `kimi_k3`) whose norms are sized only by
`hidden_size` / `q_lora_rank` / `kv_lora_rank`, so no per-head layout can reach
the guard; Falcon-H1 and Granite-4.0-H likewise define `hidden_size` norms only.

Full per-architecture numbers, harness details and the predicate-level
instrumentation are in the comments below.

---

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom); reviewed and measured by hand.

title: [ModelOpt] Unify MoE methods onto QuantSpec + ModelOptMoEMethod
body:
## Purpose

Unify ModelOpt MoE the same way #49381 unified linear methods.

One factory (`build_moe_method`) and one method class (`ModelOptMoEMethod`).
`resolve()` still builds the QuantSpec. MoE looks up a weight-key scheme in
`MOE_SCHEME_FOR` (not linear `SCHEME_FOR`).

Folds `ModelOptFp8MoEMethod`, `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE`, and
`ModelOptMxFp8FusedMoE` into `ModelOptMoEMethod`. Config classes stay split.
Deepseek V4 NVFP4 experts go through the same factory.

Mixed block-FP8 MoE (`FP8_PB_WO` / `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES`) continues to use
`Fp8MoEMethod`.

The rebase onto current `main` also preserves routing-sink forwarding and the
pre-processed NVFP4 MoE path in the unified method.

Related: #55339

## Test Plan

Unit:

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py -k "not checkpoint_setup"
```

Parity, same method as #49381 (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `--enforce-eager`,
old vs new weight/kernel hash and prefill logit delta) on every ModelOpt MoE
format this PR serves:

| Format | Checkpoint class | Weight/kernel hash | Logit delta | GSM8K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FP8 per-tensor MoE | ModelOpt FP8 MoE | pending | pending | pending |
| NVFP4 W4A4 MoE | ModelOpt NVFP4 | pending | pending | pending |
| W4A16 NVFP4 MoE | ModelOpt W4A16_NVFP4 | pending | pending | pending |
| MXFP8 MoE | ModelOpt MXFP8 | pending | pending | pending |

Also:

- mixed-precision checkpoint (linear + MoE, including block-FP8 MoE experts)
- Deepseek V4 NVFP4 experts (`moe_quant_algo=NVFP4`)

GSM8K settings match #49381: 1319 Q, 5-shot, T=0, 512 tok.

## Test Result

On macOS, `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py -k "not checkpoint_setup" -q` passed: 45 passed, 3 skipped, 3 deselected. Ruff 0.14.0 check and format checks passed on the changed Python files.

Parity hashes, logit deltas, and GSM8K for the four MoE formats remain pending.
Results will be filled into the table above.

## (Optional) Documentation

No new model. Existing design docs now point at `ModelOptMoEMethod`.

## Not duplicating existing work

This is the MoE half of the ModelOpt QuantKey rewrite. #49381 already landed
the linear side and left MoE on the old per-format classes. This PR replaces
those classes. Mixed block-FP8 MoE from #55513 stays on `Fp8MoEMethod`.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Cursor and OpenAI Codex) was used to draft and edit the change.
I will review every line of the rebased diff and run the model evaluations
before requesting merge.

title: [Test][MLA] Cover padded spec-decode context lengths in the DSA indexer
body:
## Purpose

**What.** Minimal regression coverage for the padded spec-decode context-length invariant fixed in #51538: for MTP (`next_n = 2`) with three live requests and one CUDA-graph padding request (`seq_len = 0`), the DSA indexer's per-token context lengths for the padded request must be `[0, 0]`, not `[-1, 0]`. One parametrised test (58 lines) in the existing `tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_native_next_n.py`, built on the real `DeepseekV32IndexerMetadataBuilder`, covering both the native `(B, next_n)` path and the flattened uniform-decode kernel path. No production change.

**Why.** A downstream fork that predates #51538 reproduced the old defect while serving with FlashInfer sparse MLA on SM12x, where it presented as a FlashInfer decode hang (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5015). The investigation showed the FlashInfer launch was queued on the same stream behind vLLM's already-wedged `persistent_topk`, which had read the unclamped `-1` as `uint32` (#51593). The producer clamps landed in #51538 without a direct test; this pins them so the invariant cannot silently regress again.

## Duplicate check

- #51538 (merged) already contains the production fix (producer clamps in `indexer.py` and the `persistent_topk` length guard). This PR does **not** duplicate that fix; it adds the regression coverage that was missing from the merged change.
- Searched `gh pr list --state open` for `persistent_topk`, `indexer padded`, `51593 in:body`, `51538 in:body`, `flashinfer 5015`. The only overlap is the *kernel-side* invariant: open #55122 (`[Kernel] Make persistent_topk deterministic`) adds `test_persistent_topk_degenerate_lengths` (row length `0` / `-1` → all `-1`). I therefore deliberately did **not** add a kernel-side negative-length test here; this PR covers only the producer side, which no open PR tests. #43970 touches `indexer.py` for block-table alignment and does not cover the clamp.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_native_next_n.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k persistent_topk
pre-commit run --files tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_native_next_n.py
```

## Test Result

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, cc 12.0), driver 580.173.02, torch 2.13.0+cu132, vLLM main `fc6b6e1feb` with the precompiled `_C` (`VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e .`).

| command | result |
|---|---|
| `pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_native_next_n.py` | **11 passed** (9 existing + 2 new, 16.9 s) |
| negative control: same file with the two #51538 producer clamps temporarily removed from `indexer.py` | **2 failed**, both new cases: `At index 6 diff: -1 != 0` (then restored) |
| `pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py` | 45 passed, 1 failed — `test_indexer_builder_deepseek_v4_compressed_slot_mapping_uses_num_states` fails in this environment on the gated `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B` config download (HTTP 401, no HF token on the box); unrelated to this change |
| `pytest -q tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k persistent_topk` | 54 passed, 136 deselected |
| `pytest -q tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py` (full) | 120 passed, 19 skipped, 51 failed — all 51 are `cooperative_topk` parametrisations (0 `persistent_topk`), a backend vLLM excludes on the SM120 family; identical on unmodified main, unrelated to this change |
| `pre-commit run --files tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_native_next_n.py` | all hooks passed (ruff check/format, typos, mypy 3.10, SPDX, …) |

## Model eval

Not applicable: test-only change, no serving or model-output path is modified.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate the issue, write the test and run the validation on the hardware above. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the test results before submission.

title: [HiSparse] Describe KV cache placement with block pools
body:
Suggestion PR against #53781 (base: `feat/hisparse-mla-decode-main`). Merge it into that branch or cherry-pick; close it if you disagree.

## What

HiSparse currently encodes "this memory lives on the host" three separate ways:

- `KVCacheTensor.host_resident`
- `KVCacheGroupRole.HISPARSE_SOURCE`, paired with a nullable `block_pool_id`
- `KVCacheConfig.hisparse_host_num_blocks`

Every consumer reconciles them independently, and `KVCacheConfig.__post_init__` exists mostly to check that the three agree with each other.

This replaces all three with placement on the block pool:

```python
class KVCachePlacement(str, Enum):
    DEVICE = "device"
    HOST = "host"

@dataclass
class KVCacheBlockPoolSpec:
    num_blocks: int
    placement: KVCachePlacement = KVCachePlacement.DEVICE
```

`KVCacheConfig.block_pools` carries them, so `block_pool_id` becomes a plain `int` on groups, tensors, blocks and copies, and `host_block_pool_id` / `host_group_ids` / `host_layer_names` answer placement questions directly.

Net effect on this PR's diff vs `main`: **183 insertions, 204 deletions** (-21).

## What it collapses

- `__post_init__` goes from 35 lines of cross-field validation to 6.
- Every `block_pool_id is None` / `pool_id is not None` guard and assert disappears (kv_cache_manager, worker/utils, attn_utils, hisparse_coordinator, nixl, mooncake).
- NIXL stops deriving the host block count from `cache.shape[0] // physical_blocks_per_logical_kv_block` — it reads `block_pools[pool_id].num_blocks` like every other group.
- Mooncake and NIXL both ask `layer_name in kv_cache_config.host_layer_names` instead of threading a `tensor_configs` map through to reach `host_resident`. Both local maps are now dead and removed.
- `get_unique_kv_cache_group_id` is gone; the host group is identified by placement.
- `hisparse_coordinator.owns_block` becomes `block.pool_id == self.host_block_pool_id` instead of a bounds-and-identity check against the host pool's block list.

## Deliberate scope boundaries

- **`KVCacheGroupRole` is kept**, with `HISPARSE_INDEXER` only. That is a *functional* role, orthogonal to placement, and it selects offloading groups in `offloading/config.py`. Expressing it as "device groups with `enable_kv_transfer`" would also pick up regular (non-MLA) groups when a model has them, which I could not verify, so I left the selection untouched.
- The host pool is still built by `HiSparseCoordinator.create_host_block_pool` and `coordinator.block_pools` remains device-only. It now reads its size from `block_pools[host_id]` rather than a dedicated field. Folding the host pool into the runtime pool list is a larger behavioral change (watermarks, admission tuples) and is not part of this PR.

## Behavior changes to review

1. `KVCacheManager.take_new_block_ids` now explicitly skips host groups. Previously host groups fell out of the device bookkeeping implicitly, because their `block_pool_id` was `None`.
2. Host `KVCacheBlockCopy.block_pool_id` is now the host pool id rather than `None`. `HiSparseConnector.build_connector_meta` filters on that id; `test_hisparse_host_cow_copy_is_drained_without_a_gpu_pool` was updated to match.

## Not duplicating existing work

Checked `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "hisparse"` and `--search "53781 in:body"`. The open HiSparse PRs (#53782, #55398, #55970, #53592, #52760, #53263) are feature work in other areas. This targets only the placement encoding introduced by #53781, which is untouched by them. It is also deliberately *not* the KV-cache-planning refactor you already landed in 8645447 and c2e4512 — this sits on top of those.

## Testing

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
       tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py \
       tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py
```

**1281 passed, 17 deselected.**

The 17 deselected are pre-existing failures on `feat/hisparse-mla-decode-main`, verified by stashing this change and re-running on the unmodified branch:

- `test_swa_offload_window_covers_unaligned_hit` (16 params) — fails on the base branch.
- `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma[google/gemma-3-1b-it-512]` — NIXL/UCX cannot register memory on my box (`ulimit -l` capped at 8192 kB), environmental.

`pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual` and `ruff check` / `ruff format` pass on all 21 changed files.

**Not run:** `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`. This is a pure refactor with no intended change to model output, so no eval numbers are included, but the DeepSeek-V3.2 e2e path has not been exercised — worth a run before merging, particularly for the NIXL host block-count change.

## AI assistance

This change was written with AI assistance (Claude). I have reviewed it, but flagging clearly since it is a mechanical refactor across 21 files touching KV cache placement — the two behavior changes listed above deserve a careful look.

### 🐛 Describe the bug Summary When using DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with vLLM 0.25.1、vLLM 0.26.0 in an agentic tool‑calling loop, the first malformed tool‑call response (containing both visible text and DSML tags) causes vLLM to return an OpenAI‑incompatible assistant message with non‑empty content and tool_calls simultaneously. After this first occurrence, every subsequent tool‑calling turn in the same session suffers the same corruption until the server is restarted. Steps to Reproduce Start vLLM 0.25.1、vLLM 0.26.0 with the following command: bash docker run -d \ --gpus all \ --shm-size=128g \ -p 8000:8000 \ -v /aipublic/model:/aipublic/model \ --name vllm-deepseekv4 \ --restart unless-stopped \ -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \ -e SPEC_CONFIG='{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}' \ --entrypoint "" \ vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1 \ bash -c '\ vllm serve DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --port 8000 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 \ --served-model-name DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --speculative_config "$SPEC_CONFIG" \ --trust-remote-code \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --max-num-seqs 16 \ --block-size 256 \ --enable-log-requests \ --enable-prompt-tokens-details' Send a chat completion request that triggers a tool call, where the model produces a mixed output like: text I'll gather the data for 工商银行... <｜DSML｜tool_calls> {"name": "some_tool", "arguments": {...}} Observe the returned assistant message in the response: json { "role": "assistant", "content": "I'll gather the data for 工商银行...", "tool_calls": [...] } Continue the conversation with more tool‑calling turns. Every subsequent turn will now return the same malformed structure, even if the model output correctly starts with <｜DSML｜tool_calls>. Restart the vLLM server to restore normal behavior for a fresh session. Expected Behavior Per OpenAI API specification, an assistant message containing tool_calls must have an empty content string ("content": ""). After a valid tool call is parsed and executed, subsequent turns should work correctly without corrupting the parser state. Actual Behavior The assistant message includes both a non‑empty content and a valid tool_calls array. Critical: The parser state becomes poisoned after the first malformed response. All future tool‑calling turns in the same session reproduce the same violation. This suggests the internal parser (DeepSeekV4ToolParser) or the post‑processing logic (_postprocess_messages) does not reset per request and retains an error state. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix] Flag every KV cache group holding a separately prefixed drafter's layers as a draft group
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #52047, complementary to #55390.

On **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next** (`Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`: GDN + QSA + MTP, packed grouping path) no KV cache group is ever identified as the drafter's, so the coordinator falls back to flagging every group, the four Mamba groups included, as a draft group. Effects on a live server:

- `kv_cache_utils.py:1893` warning on every start.
- Zero cross-request prefix-cache hits: a replay of 8 prompts with shared prefixes (34K/41K/45K chained, 140K then 250K sharing the 140K) queried 816,343 tokens and hit 0.

Why the existing rules miss it:

1. Rule 1 (`non_causal_multi_token_decode`) is DSpark-only.
2. Rule 2 (last registered layer) is gated on `model_type == "deepseek_v4"`. #55390 generalizes the gate to `method == "mtp"` but, as its docstring notes, flags only the group holding the very last layer. The Qwen4Exp MTP block registers **three** caches under `mtp.` (QSA attention KV, compressed-key `MLAAttentionSpec`, ring `CircularBufferSpec`) that land in **two** packed groups, so the group holding the drafter's attention KV can still be left unflagged.

## Fix

Rule 3 in `_annotate_eagle_groups`: when no group was flagged, and the last registered layer's top-level module prefix differs from the first layer's (a separately built drafter registered after the target), flag every group holding a layer under that prefix. Drafters that reuse the target's prefix (EAGLE heads under `model.`) are not detected and keep the conservative all-groups fallback, as before.

`_warn_if_unannotated_eagle_mamba` now keys on `use_eagle_block_drop()`, which is what `KVCacheManager` actually receives; with `disable_eagle_block_drop` no group is a draft group and the warning was spurious.

If #55390 lands first this rebases on top of it cleanly (rule 3 only runs when rules 1 and 2 flagged nothing).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py -q
```

New: `test_annotate_eagle_groups_flags_separately_prefixed_drafter_layers` (draft layer under `mtp.` flags its group and leaves the Mamba group alone; same-prefix layout flags nothing; no block drop configured leaves everything untouched).

## Test Result

`106 passed` on `main` (d2906091b), CPU.

Live, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 on one RTX PRO 6000, MTP 3, 262,144 context, 240 blocks of 1,600 tokens (3x12 GDN, 1 PLE, 13 QSA rings, 13 QSA main+compressed):

| | draft groups | 1893 warning | replay hits |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | none flagged (all 6 treated as draft) | yes | 0 of 816,343 queried tokens |
| after | groups 4 and 5 (the two holding `mtp.` layers) | no | 41K after 34K: 33,600 cached, 0.88 s (was 4.0 s); 250K after 140K: 139,200 cached, 11.5 s (was 25.6 s) |

Footprint unchanged (140K prompt = 113 of 240 blocks before and after). Note that the first request extending a prefix still misses with the trailing-block drop on, because the align-mode Mamba checkpoint sits on the last full block while the attention hit is offered one block lower; that is #52244's write-side fix, and the numbers above were taken with `disable_eagle_block_drop` as a stand-in.

---

title: [Bug][ROCm][DSv4] JIT warmup compiles launch_pdl=True Triton kernels and fails with invalid griddepcontrol on AMD
body:
### Describe the bug

After #50176 (`[4/N][warmup][DSv4] Migrate common attention kernels`, merged 2026-09-08), serving DeepSeek V4 on ROCm dies during **JIT kernel warmup**, before the API server comes up.

Triton emits NVIDIA PDL PTX into an AMD hsaco:

```
error: invalid instruction
        griddepcontrol.wait; // dummy s6
        ^
error: invalid instruction
        griddepcontrol.launch_dependents; // dummy s6
        ^
ld.lld: error: target emulation unknown: -m or at least one .o file required
RuntimeError: LLD failed to link hsaco source /tmp/... into object file ...
```

EngineCore then fails with `Worker failed with error 'LLD failed to link hsaco...'`. The subsequent TCPStore / ProcessGroupNCCL `Broken pipe` logs are fallout from the worker crash, not the root cause.

This did not happen on builds from before #50176. Runtime dispatch already disables PDL on ROCm via `current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl()` (the base platform returns `False`). Only the **new warmup compile-key enumeration** eagerly compiles the `launch_pdl=True` variant.

Parent tracking PR #49627 already notes: *"The migration has been validated on NVIDIA platforms only."*

### Environment

- vLLM: `0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b.rocm723` (`385dce36bcee42309924a5ece951a96db3dce7f2`)
- Introduced by: `6ddbab03de` / #50176
- Model: DeepSeek V4 (`DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`), V1 runner on ROCm
- Hardware: 8x gfx950 (MI350-class), TP=8
- ROCm 7.2.3, torch 2.12.0+hip, triton 3.7.1, Python 3.12
- Linker: `/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/ld.lld` (AMD LLD 22.0.0) - toolchain is correct, not a CUDA-lld mixup

### Reproduction

Serve DeepSeek V4 on a current `main` (post-#50176) ROCm build, e.g. TP=8. Startup reaches:

```
JIT kernel warmup (141 compile keys):  31%|/ | 4/13 ... Fuse
ERROR [...] kernel_warmup.py JIT kernel warmup failed
```

Workaround that confirms this is warmup-only: `--kernel-config.enable-jit-warmup=false` (runtime never compiles `launch_pdl=True` on ROCm). Reverting #50176 also restores startup without a native rebuild, since the commit is Python-only.

### Root cause

The warmup spaces hardcode both PDL variants, with no platform filter:

```python
# vllm/models/common/ops/fused_qk_rmsnorm.py
return self._trace_dispatch(self.dispatch)(
    ...
    launch_pdl=(False, True),
)
```

```python
# vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py
return self._trace_dispatch(self.dispatch)(
    ...
    launch_pdl=(False, True),
)
```

Those kernels then emit NVIDIA-only inline PTX when `launch_pdl` is true:

```python
if launch_pdl:
    tl.extra.cuda.gdc_launch_dependents()
    tl.extra.cuda.gdc_wait()
```

`tl.extra.cuda.gdc_*` expands to `griddepcontrol.*` (see Triton's `third_party/nvidia/language/cuda/gdc.py`). The AMD assembler rejects it, so `ld.lld` has no object to link.

The same tree already special-cases ROCm at **runtime** in `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/compressor.py`:

```python
pdl_kwargs = (
    {}
    if current_platform.is_rocm() or current_platform.is_xpu()
    else {"launch_pdl": False}
)
```

The warmup enumeration missed that filter.

### Suggested fix

Do not enumerate `launch_pdl=True` unless `current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl()` is true, e.g.:

```python
launch_pdl=(False, True) if current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl() else (False,)
```

It would also be worth auditing the other kernels that landed in the same warmup series (`tl.extra.cuda.gdc_*` / `launch_pdl=(False, True)`), including shared `common/` ops that run on ROCm. The `_when` predicate from #49315 is probably the right place, so NVIDIA still warms both keys.

### Related

- Introduced by: #50176
- Parent: #49627 / tracking #49349
- Related but different: #42876 (TileLang MHC `PDL is not supported` in TVM, not this Triton hsaco path)

title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Fix heterogeneous PP transfer completion
body:
## Purpose

Fix Mooncake transfers when prefill and decode use different pipeline-parallel sizes and decode has multiple stages, such as P-PP4 to D-PP2.

The existing receiver contacts every producer PP stage when the PP sizes differ. Producer-side layer matching rejects peers that own different layers, while completion accounting only counts consumer TP ranks. Allowing those pulls without correcting the count would release producer KV before all consumer PP stages finish.

Carry the consumer PP size in transfer metadata, match only shared layers for mismatched PP layouts, and count every consumer PP pull, including peers with no shared layers. Keep the existing all-peer routing instead of assuming that PP rank ratios imply aligned layer boundaries. Missing occurrences within a shared layer still fail validation.

Add one regression test for P-PP4/D-PP2: the producer sends its layer to one consumer, retains KV, then accepts the other consumer's no-op pull and reports completion without waiting for expiration.

## Related work

Checked open PRs for Mooncake PP fanout and heterogeneous PP. #45112 explicitly leaves decode-side PP out of scope; #46004 addresses shared-KV metadata. Neither implements this layer-matching and completion-accounting fix. Scheduler recovery, DSpark, cache-group remapping, and routing optimizations are outside this change.

## Test Plan

- **Hardware/image:** NVIDIA H20 GPUs, vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0.
- **DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813:** 4 nodes × 8 GPUs; two-node Prefill **TP4/PP4** → two-node Decode **TP8/PP2**, Mooncake RDMA, eager execution, FP8 MLA KV cache, no speculative decoding.
- **Qwen3.5-2B:** one node, 6 GPUs; Prefill **TP1/PP4** → Decode **TP1/PP2**.
- **Falcon-H1-0.5B-Instruct:** one node, 6 GPUs; Prefill **TP1/PP4** → Decode **TP1/PP2**.

## Test Result

- **DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813:** before the fix, PD requests timed out with producer/consumer layer-alignment errors. After the fix, PD requests completed successfully with KV transfer and resource cleanup. Validated with 200 GSM8K samples (97.5% accuracy).
- **Qwen3.5-2B:** also verified successful PD requests, KV transfer and cleanup, and outputs matching the direct Decode reference (tested with the fixes from #51718).
- **Falcon-H1-0.5B-Instruct:** also verified that baseline PD requests timed out, while fixed requests completed with KV transfer and cleanup, and outputs matching the direct Decode reference (tested with the fixes from #51718).

title: [ROCm][Perf] Integrate AITER KDA prefill for Kimi-K3
body:
## Purpose

Add an explicit AITER Kimi-K3 prefill backend on ROCm:

- use AITER's fused BF16 QKV causal Conv1D kernel;
- expose AITER FlashKDA through `--kda-prefill-backend flashkda`;
- preserve the existing Triton implementation as the fallback and explicit
  `--kda-prefill-backend triton` path;
- stage the AITER Conv weight while loading the checkpoint; and
- warm the AITER kernels with a bounded representative profile when FlashKDA
  is selected.

The default policy remains native-fused-first. On ROCm, `auto` selects the
native fused backend whenever it is supported, otherwise FlashKDA when AITER is
enabled, and otherwise Triton. The existing Kimi-K3 GSM8K configuration remains
on `auto`; this PR does not make FlashKDA the default on gfx950.

### Relation to existing PRs

This does not duplicate #54038. That PR adds the vLLM-native gfx950 HIP
implementation of the KDA prologue and recurrence, which remains the default
and is faster on gfx950. This PR adds AITER FlashKDA as an explicit alternative
and as the `auto` fallback when the native fused backend is unavailable. It
adds no KDA C++ kernel to vLLM.

#54055 changes the generic KDA operator's packed-QKV API for an external
backend; it does not provide the ROCm AITER Conv/FlashKDA execution path added
here.

This PR uses the AITER API already present in the version pinned by vLLM. It
does not require or change the global AITER version pin.

## Test Plan

On an 8x MI355X system:

```bash
pytest -q \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_prefill.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_chunk.py
```

Run the complete 1319-question GSM8K evaluation with the existing
`Kimi-K3-pruned75-DSpark-AITER-TP4.yaml` configuration using its default `auto`
KDA selection.

Run serving benchmarks with Kimi-K3, TP8, 100 prompts, concurrency 32, OSL 1,
and ISL 4096 and 16384. Compare `fused`, `flashkda`, and `triton` on the same
node. FlashKDA measurements use the explicit
`--kda-prefill-backend flashkda` option.

Run pre-commit on every changed file, including the manual Python 3.12 mypy
hook.

## Test Result

- Kimi-K3 tests: **95 passed, 27 skipped**. The skipped cases require CUDA or
  native fused-decode kernels unavailable in the ROCm test container.
- AITER upstream selected FlashKDA tests: **8 passed**.
- GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot greedy:
  - strict match: **97.04%**
  - flexible extract: **96.97%**
- Same-node prefill measurements are reported below.

Each result is the arithmetic mean of three runs. Since these are
prefill-focused OSL=1 tests, input throughput is calculated for each run as
`total token throughput - output token throughput`. All runs completed 100
requests with zero failures.

| Backend | Input length | Input throughput (tok/s) | Median TTFT (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Triton | 4K | 15,088.06 | 8,672.46 |
| FlashKDA, AITER v0.1.21.post2 | 4K | 15,459.96 | 8,464.19 |
| FlashKDA, AITER #5436 experimental build | 4K | 15,670.53 | 8,351.33 |
| Native fused | 4K | 15,845.68 | 8,258.32 |
| Triton | 16K | 14,680.45 | 35,688.11 |
| FlashKDA, AITER v0.1.21.post2 | 16K | 15,022.81 | 34,871.61 |
| FlashKDA, AITER #5436 experimental build | 16K | 15,218.27 | 34,425.96 |
| Native fused | 16K | 15,390.05 | 34,043.83 |

On gfx950, native fused remains the fastest backend and therefore remains the
default. Compared with native fused, the AITER version currently pinned by
vLLM has 2.43% lower input throughput at 4K and 2.39% lower input throughput at
16K. This PR therefore does not claim an end-to-end performance improvement
over current main on gfx950.

The experimental AITER build containing ROCm/aiter#5436 improves FlashKDA over
the currently pinned AITER by 1.36% at 4K and 1.30% at 16K, but remains about
1.1% behind native fused. These #5436 numbers are forward-looking validation;
this PR does not update vLLM's global AITER pin.

- All pre-commit hooks for the changed files passed.
- Manual Python 3.12 mypy hook passed.

## AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex was used to assist with code investigation, implementation,
review, and test orchestration. The human contributor selected the target
implementation, directed the integration and review decisions, and is
responsible for the submitted changes.

---

<details>
<summary>Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist</summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR is described, including related open PRs.
- [x] The test plan includes the commands and workloads used.
- [x] Test, model-evaluation, and performance results are included.
- [x] User-facing CLI help is updated, while the existing AMD evaluation
  configuration retains its default backend selection.

</details>

title: [Bug][ROCm/gfx942] GLM-5.3-Flash Memory access fault is three paths, not #54296 / 32-page: mixed-length MTP decode, prefill _kpool_tail_seed_kernel, equal-length short MTP
body:
## Status of this write-up

Cross-links: #55280, #54359, #54296, #53906.

**#54296 (V2 `in_range` slot-mapping guard) is not this family.** Crash C, D, and E all died on images that already had that guard (Crash B already did too; see the #55280 correction). Do not close this as a duplicate of #54296.

The ROCm indexer-alignment gap in #55280 (hybrid `block_size=1152` → virtual 32-page split) is still real on `main` and still worth fixing. It is **not** a sufficient explanation of the three aborts below. All three ran with `block_size=1280`, native `page_size=64`.

---

## Environment (all three)

- 8× MI325X, gfx942, ROCm 7.2.3
- TP=4 on GPUs 0–3 (`HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3`), host network, port 8000
- Checkpoint: `orcarouter/GLM-5.3-Flash-Uncensored-FP8` snapshot `3cec42d6ed14ec197e328c09650c17fd3660c26a`
- Serving tree: #53906-era GLM-5.3-Flash ROCm image + later local patches (MTP Triton gate, V2 slot-mapping guard, kpool64 align)
- MTP `{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}`
- Prefix caching on, chunked prefill on, `max_model_len=1000000`, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`
- Boot (after kpool64 align): attention `block_size=1280`, kpool `page_size=64`, contiguous indexer KV
- Not OOM (`OOMKilled=false`). EngineDead → APIServer shutdown → docker `ExitCode=0`
- GPU coredump handler missing (`execvp failed: No such file or directory`)

---

## Crash C — mixed-length MTP decode (2026-09-04)

**Assertion bound:** scheduler dump is measured. Kernel name is **inferred**, not `HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING`. Local overlay (`split_per_req` on skewed / capturing B>1) replayed the shape with zero faults; that does not prove the inferred kernel on the dying tag.

### Symptom (measured)

Image already 1280 / page_size=64 and already #54296 V2 `in_range`. Started 2026-09-04T03:44:09Z, died 2026-09-04T06:10:46Z (~2.5 h).

- 06:10:43Z: 1 running req, gen 92.3 tok/s, KV 1.3%, prefix-cache 93.6%. That long request had already emitted 3419 tokens.
- 06:10:43Z: two new `POST /v1/chat/completions` (short MTP joins).
- 06:10:46Z:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-5 (Agent handle: 0x4d7f1420) on address 0x70ff1de00000. Reason: Unknown.
Worker proc VllmWorker-3 died unexpectedly (exit code: -6)
```

Dying dump:

```
Dumping scheduler output for model execution: SchedulerOutput(scheduled_new_reqs=[], scheduled_cached_reqs=CachedRequestData(req_ids=['chatcmpl-a0eafa3af4652789-86ed705d', 'chatcmpl-8721914b0e77862d-92b00472', 'chatcmpl-aea9a6c10e02bcc2-a5d89ac5'],resumed_req_ids=set(),new_token_ids_lens=[],all_token_ids_lens={},new_block_ids=[None, None, None],num_computed_tokens=[129934, 20, 20],num_output_tokens=[3419, 1, 1]), num_scheduled_tokens={chatcmpl-a0eafa3af4652789-86ed705d: 3, chatcmpl-aea9a6c10e02bcc2-a5d89ac5: 3, chatcmpl-8721914b0e77862d-92b00472: 3}, total_num_scheduled_tokens=9, scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={chatcmpl-aea9a6c10e02bcc2-a5d89ac5: [-1, -1], chatcmpl-8721914b0e77862d-92b00472: [-1, -1], chatcmpl-a0eafa3af4652789-86ed705d: [-1, -1]}, scheduled_encoder_inputs={}, num_common_prefix_blocks=[0, 0, 0, 0, 0], finished_req_ids=[], free_encoder_mm_hashes=[], scheduled_encoder_input_stats=null, preempted_req_ids=[], has_structured_output_requests=false, pending_structured_output_tokens=false, num_invalid_spec_tokens=null, kv_connector_metadata=null, ec_connector_metadata=null, ec_manager_metadata=null, new_block_ids_to_zero=null, kv_cache_block_copies=null, partial_tail_offloads=null, num_spec_tokens_to_schedule=2)
Dumping scheduler stats: SchedulerStats(num_running_reqs=3, num_waiting_reqs=0, num_skipped_waiting_reqs=0, step_counter=0, current_wave=0, kv_cache_usage=0.015652377058754774, ...)
```

32-page alignment is **not** sufficient: this abort is already on native 64-page. `new_block_ids` are all `None`, so this step is not a slot-mapping OOB of the #54296 kind.

### Inferred path (not HIP-captured)

Serving aiter 0.1.19. vLLM calls `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` **without** `VarCtxSchedule`, so gfx942 uses `_gluon_deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle`. MTP nst=2 flattens to `next_n=1`, `B=num_decode_tokens`. Mixed long+short rows then share one SplitKV.

We did **not** re-run `HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING` on the dying Crash C tag (kernel name remains inferred).

Solo ~130k MTP (uniform long context, 3419 output tokens) had been stable on the same kernel. The abort is the first step after two short MTP reqs joined.

### Local overlay (scope: decode only)

When `max(ctx) > max(4*min(ctx), min(ctx)+256)`, launch gluon **per request**. Host `.item()` is skipped while the stream is capturing (`hipErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported` measured 2026-09-07 on the kpool custom-op path, which is **not** `eager_break_during_capture`). During capture, B>1 is always split.

Replay on that overlay (2026-09-07): prompt=130486, completion=64, two short MTP joins after first decode token; gate log `mixed-length decode B=15 next_n=1 ctx_min=4 ctx_max=32622; per-request gluon`; `32622 == 130486/4` (kpool compression); zero `Memory access fault`.

That overlay does **not** cover prefill tail seed (Crash D) and does **not** split equal-length B>1 (Crash E).

---

## Crash D — chunked prefill `_kpool_tail_seed_kernel` (2026-09-07)

**Assertion bound:** kernel name is **measured** with `HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` on the dying Crash C tag. Crash C's mixed-length decode gate did not cover this path.

### Symptom (measured)

Image already had the Crash C decode overlay. Started 2026-09-07T01:46:27Z, died 2026-09-07T08:18:08Z (~6.5 h).

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-5 (Agent handle: 0x314215f0) on address 0x7f58cab40000. Reason: Unknown.
Worker proc VllmWorker-3 died unexpectedly (exit code: None)
```

Dying dump is **1-req chunked prefill**, not Crash C's 3-way MTP decode:

```
Dumping scheduler output for model execution: SchedulerOutput(scheduled_new_reqs=[], scheduled_cached_reqs=CachedRequestData(req_ids=['resp_8c870b1ea788fa7a_0-a846c839'],resumed_req_ids=set(),new_token_ids_lens=[],all_token_ids_lens={},new_block_ids=[([3537], [], [3545, 3536], [3542, 3535], [3539, 3578])],num_computed_tokens=[211200],num_output_tokens=[0]), num_scheduled_tokens={resp_8c870b1ea788fa7a_0-a846c839: 2338}, total_num_scheduled_tokens=2338, scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={}, scheduled_encoder_inputs={}, num_common_prefix_blocks=[167, 0, 0, 0, 0], finished_req_ids=[], free_encoder_mm_hashes=[], scheduled_encoder_input_stats=null, preempted_req_ids=[], has_structured_output_requests=false, pending_structured_output_tokens=false, num_invalid_spec_tokens=null, kv_connector_metadata=null, ec_connector_metadata=null, ec_manager_metadata=null, new_block_ids_to_zero=[3537], kv_cache_block_copies=null, partial_tail_offloads=null, num_spec_tokens_to_schedule=2)
Dumping scheduler stats: SchedulerStats(num_running_reqs=3, num_waiting_reqs=0, num_skipped_waiting_reqs=0, step_counter=0, current_wave=0, kv_cache_usage=0.02394859813084116, ...)
```

- computed **211200**, scheduled **2338**, output **0**
- `scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={}` (no MTP this step)
- `2338 % 4 == 2`: last chunk is not kpool-aligned; prefill **must** seed the tail ring
- prefix-cache ~94.6% just before; KV 2.39%
- `num_running_reqs=3` in stats (dump lists only the one scheduled)

### Measured kernel

Short-lived `docker run` of the **dying Crash C tag**, GPU 0 only, `HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` + `AMD_LOG_LEVEL=3`. Probe: `kpool_seed_tail_cache`, `n_tail=2`, `bad_block=500000` (3537 vs 2478 stayed inside the HIP heap; an extreme id left it).

```
hipModuleGetFunction(..., _kpool_tail_seed_kernel)
ShaderName : _kpool_tail_seed_kernel
Memory Fault Error
Memory access fault by GPU node-2
```

Prefill `_kpool_tail_seed_kernel` did `blk = tslot // KPOOL` and `tl.store` with **no** `blk < tail.shape[0]` check. Decode stash already had `NUM_TAIL_BLOCKS` from Crash C. After prefix-cache churn, `own_block` can be main-KV magnitude while the tail tensor is a 1-block/req ring (`n_tail=8561` on the later crashD boot; 96 during dummy capture).

### Local overlay (scope: prefill seed)

Gate `_kpool_tail_seed_kernel`: `if blk >= NUM_TAIL_BLOCKS: return`, address via `tail.stride(0)/stride(1)`. Same probe on that image logs `[gfx942 kpool-prefill-seed] … NUM_TAIL_BLOCKS gated` and does not fault.

Replay: prompt=223903 (>211200+2338), completion=3, two shorts joined during prefill; zero `Memory access fault` on that container until Crash E.

---

## Crash E — crashD image still died; equal-length short MTP (2026-09-09)

**Assertion bound:** image, timestamps, fault banner, and scheduler dump are measured. Kernel name is **unchecked** (`HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING` empty on the serving container). Do **not** treat E1 as measured.

### Symptom (measured)

Image: `local/vllm-openai-rocm:glm53-flash-gfx942-v9-tritonspec-v2guard-kpool64-crashD` digest `sha256:247f3e1796d2318a0904322d6898ed03c95e5f51e6cc1bea5bb8ed6b90cbc2fe`.

Boot banners present: `n_tail=8561 kpool=4 (NUM_TAIL_BLOCKS gated)`; `CUDA-graph capture B>1: recording per-request gluon so replay stays mixed-length-safe`. Mixed-length gluon **did** fire once on this container (2026-09-07T08:43:38Z, `B=15 next_n=1 ctx_min=4 ctx_max=55976`) and **survived**. This container's only `Memory access fault` is Crash E.

Started 2026-09-07T08:32:20Z, died 2026-09-09T06:55:18Z (46.38 h). Last `GET /health` 200 at 06:55:04.921Z.

```
2026-09-09T06:55:08.617980407Z Memory access fault by GPU node-5 (Agent handle: 0x2a1702b0) on address 0x74da674c0000. Reason: Unknown.
2026-09-09T06:55:08.854978234Z GPU coredump: execvp failed: No such file or directory
2026-09-09T06:55:09.039093390Z Worker proc VllmWorker-3 died unexpectedly (exit code: None), shutting down executor.
```

Not a human `docker stop`: health 200 14s before the fault; EngineDead then Exit 0. Not image rollback (same crashD digest as 2026-09-07).

### Dying dump (verbatim)

```
2026-09-09T06:55:18.049867148Z (EngineCore pid=980) ERROR 09-09 06:55:18 [dump_input.py:79] Dumping scheduler output for model execution: SchedulerOutput(scheduled_new_reqs=[], scheduled_cached_reqs=CachedRequestData(req_ids=['chatcmpl-b2e63bc3aa201484-ae78933d', 'chatcmpl-bf031db55f3e9f36-b6b13065'],resumed_req_ids=set(),new_token_ids_lens=[],all_token_ids_lens={},new_block_ids=[None, None],num_computed_tokens=[20, 20],num_output_tokens=[1, 1]), num_scheduled_tokens={chatcmpl-bf031db55f3e9f36-b6b13065: 3, chatcmpl-b2e63bc3aa201484-ae78933d: 3}, total_num_scheduled_tokens=6, scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={chatcmpl-b2e63bc3aa201484-ae78933d: [-1, -1], chatcmpl-bf031db55f3e9f36-b6b13065: [-1, -1]}, scheduled_encoder_inputs={}, num_common_prefix_blocks=[0, 0, 0, 0, 0], finished_req_ids=[], free_encoder_mm_hashes=[], scheduled_encoder_input_stats=null, preempted_req_ids=[], has_structured_output_requests=false, pending_structured_output_tokens=false, num_invalid_spec_tokens=null, kv_connector_metadata=null, ec_connector_metadata=null, ec_manager_metadata=null, new_block_ids_to_zero=null, kv_cache_block_copies=null, partial_tail_offloads=null, num_spec_tokens_to_schedule=2)
2026-09-09T06:55:18.050067428Z (EngineCore pid=980) ERROR 09-09 06:55:18 [dump_input.py:81] Dumping scheduler stats: SchedulerStats(num_running_reqs=2, num_waiting_reqs=0, num_skipped_waiting_reqs=0, step_counter=0, current_wave=0, kv_cache_usage=0.0025700934579439005, iteration_details=None, prefix_cache_stats=PrefixCacheStats(reset=False, requests=0, queries=0, hits=0, preempted_requests=0, preempted_queries=0, preempted_hits=0), connector_prefix_cache_stats=None, kv_cache_eviction_events=[], spec_decoding_stats=None, kv_connector_stats=None, waiting_lora_adapters={}, running_lora_adapters={}, cudagraph_stats=None, perf_stats=None)
```

This step is **not** Crash D (not chunked prefill, no high `new_block_ids`, MTP spec present). It is **not** Crash C (no long row; computed is `[20, 20]`, equal length). Crash C's local gate only splits when capturing or `ctx_max > max(ctx_min*4, ctx_min+256)`. Equal-length B=2 takes the fused path. No mixed-length gluon warning near death.

Seven seconds before the fault there was a prefill `aiter` shape `M:1626` (`1626 % 4 == 2`, same kpool alignment as Crash D's `2338 % 4 == 2`), then `M:1945`, then several HTTP 200s, then the fault. HIP launches are async when `HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING` is off, so the dump may be the next queued step rather than the kernel that faulted.

### Hypotheses (not measured)

1. **E1, inferred:** two short MTP first-token steps (`spec=[-1,-1]`) on fused gluon paged-MQA, B=2 equal ctx. Crash C's `split_per_req` does not cover this.
2. **E2, inferred:** the faulting kernel was the 06:55:01 `M:1626` prefill tail seed, reported late; dump is the following 2-short decode. If true, Crash D's `NUM_TAIL_BLOCKS` gate still has a hole.

Cheapest next measurement (not run): crashD image + `HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` + `AMD_LOG_LEVEL=3`, replay **only** two concurrent short MTP requests (prompt ≈ 20, nst=2, no long request). ShaderName gluon paged-MQA → E1. No fault → replay a `len % 4 == 2` prefill → E2. Do not enable `HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING` on a production :8000.

---

## What this is not

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| #54296 V2 `in_range` | **Not this family.** C/D/E already had it. Crash E dump `new_block_ids=[None, None]`. |
| #55280 32-page split | **Not sufficient.** C/D/E already `page_size=64` / `block_size=1280`. The ROCm `_get_indexer_block_alignment` gap remains a separate bug. |
| #54359 indexer overwrite | Different symptom (silent wrong retrieval on gfx950). Related kpool stack, not these GPU faults. |
| #53906 missing ROCm path | #53906 merged 2026-09-03. These aborts are on a serving image that already runs GLM-5.3-Flash + MTP on gfx942. |
| OOM / human stop / image rollback | Measured false for C/D/E. |

---

## Suggested upstream (by path)

- **Crash D (measured):** every tail-ring writer (prefill seed **and** decode stash) must refuse `block >= tail_kv_cache.shape[0]`. Prefer a local 0..n_tail-1 id, not a main-KV physical id, for the 1-block/req tail tensor. On `main` the prefill seed was still ungated last time we read it (`kpool_compress.py` `_kpool_tail_seed_kernel`).
- **Crash C (inferred):** gfx942 preshuffle paged-MQA should not use a uniform SplitKV on mixed `ctx`. vLLM `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits`: pass `VarCtxSchedule` if aiter exposes it; do not hand `[B, next_n]` context_lens to a kernel that indexes `[B]`. Capture-safe split is required (kpool custom op is not `eager_break_during_capture`).
- **Crash E (unchecked):** do not patch from E1. Capture ShaderName first.

Happy to turn the Crash D tail-seed bound into a small PR if that is useful. Crash C/E need a kernel name on E before claiming a decode-side patch.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Avoid unsupported PDL warmup for fused QKV RMSNorm
body:
## Purpose

Fix DeepSeek-V4 startup on ROCm when generic JIT kernel warmup is enabled.

`FusedQKVRMSNormKernel` runtime dispatch selects `launch_pdl` with `current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl()`, but its warmup keys currently enumerate both `False` and `True`. On ROCm, compiling the unreachable `True` specialization lowers the CUDA GDC operations to `griddepcontrol.wait` and `griddepcontrol.launch_dependents`, which the AMDGPU linker rejects.

This mismatch was introduced by [#50176](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50176), which migrated the kernel to the shared warmup contract and added the unconditional `(False, True)` warmup space. The pre-migration runtime path already used the platform capability predicate and did not compile an unreachable PDL specialization on ROCm.

This PR makes warmup use the same platform capability decision as runtime dispatch:

- CUDA SM90 and newer return `True`, so warmup retains the PDL specialization used at runtime and stops compiling the unreachable non-PDL specialization.
- CUDA architectures older than SM90 return `False`, so warmup retains the non-PDL specialization used at runtime and does not attempt unsupported PDL compilation.
- ROCm, XPU, TPU, CPU, and other platforms that inherit the default capability return `False`, so warmup retains the only specialization runtime can request.

The active platform and device are fixed within each worker process; runtime does not dynamically fall back between the two values. The change therefore removes only unreachable startup compilation. It does not alter the Triton kernel, runtime dispatch, or inference behavior on any architecture.

AI assistance was used for this PR.

## Test Plan

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q tests/kernels/core/test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm.py
python3 -m pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_jit_warmup.py
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/common/ops/fused_qk_rmsnorm.py
```

Run an unpatched-versus-patched compile-only reproducer for `FusedQKVRMSNormKernel` on ROCm, then start stock `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` on four MI355X GPUs with TP=4, no speculative decoding, eager mode, and JIT warmup enabled.

## Test Result

- Unpatched ROCm: the platform reported no PDL support, but warmup generated both values. The first `launch_pdl=True` compile failed with the expected `griddepcontrol` linker error; a `launch_pdl=False` compile passed.
- Patched ROCm: warmup generated four keys, all with `launch_pdl=False`, and all four compiled.
- Fused Q/KV RMSNorm tests: `13 passed`.
- Shared JIT warmup tests: `38 passed`.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks: passed.
- Stock DeepSeek-V4 TP4: generic JIT warmup finished on all ranks, the server reached readiness, and one 128-input/64-output request completed successfully with zero failures.

title: [ROCm][MLA] Enable AITER mask0 decode for DSpark
body:
## Purpose

Enable `ROCM_AITER_MLA` for Kimi-K3 DSpark's non-causal multi-token
decode path on gfx950.

DSpark generates a query block in parallel. Every query in that block must
attend to the same committed KV prefix, rather than to a causal triangular
suffix within the draft block. Older AITER builds expose only causal MLA
decode, so vLLM currently selects `TRITON_MLA` for the draft model even when
the target model uses `ROCM_AITER_MLA`.

AITER v0.1.21.post1 includes the `causal` decode argument and gfx950 mask0
persistent kernels from ROCm/aiter#4565. This PR wires that capability into
the ROCm MLA backend while preserving all existing causal target paths.

## Changes

- Detect the AITER `causal` API at runtime and advertise non-causal support
  only on gfx950. Older AITER installations fail closed during backend
  selection.
- Pass the current batch's causality to AITER metadata generation and native
  `mla_decode_fwd`.
- Route non-causal DSpark decode around the causal-only Gluon verify and
  segmented DCP verify paths.
- Keep causal target verification unchanged:
  - non-DCP small-head BF16 verification may use Gluon;
  - DCP multi-token verification uses segmented MLA;
  - ordinary target decode uses native AITER MLA.
- Return per-row LSE from non-causal DCP decode so the existing cross-rank
  reducer can merge partial attention results.
- Materialize the speculative KDA state-index slice as contiguous before the
  fused kernel consumes it. This is a separate prerequisite commit for
  full/piecewise graph execution.

The AITER implementation changes only
`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py`. It does not modify common
MLA interfaces or CUDA/non-ROCm attention backends.

For Kimi-K3 DSpark K=4 with FP8 draft KV, the observed kernels are:

| Topology | Draft shape | AITER kernel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TP8 | padded H16, Q4 | `mla_a8w8_qh16_qseqlen4_gqaratio16_msk0_v3_ps` |
| TP8/DCP8 | gathered H64, Q4 | `mla_a8w8_qh32_qseqlen4_gqaratio32_msk0_lse_ps` |

The DCP shape is internally folded from H64/Q4 to the H32/Q4 kernel
configuration. The `_lse` variant supplies the statistics required for DCP
merge. Non-causal decode does not need causal round-robin position remapping.

## Test Plan

```bash
ruff check \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py

ruff format --check \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py

python3 -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py
```

Hardware validation used MI355X and:

```text
vllm/vllm-openai-rocm@sha256:67d4317ba8aa9e60171c4eaa74eda3d1e877011c809aa186687b524ab4472aaa
AITER v0.1.21.post1
Kimi-K3 TP8 and TP8/DCP8
DSpark K=4
FP8 target and draft KV caches
```

## Test Result

### Unit and static tests

- `ruff check`: passed
- `ruff format --check`: passed
- Python compile check: passed
- `test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py`: **55 passed**
- The capability tests verify that old AITER APIs fail closed and the new
  `causal` API enables the backend.
- Routing tests cover causal warmup, non-causal metadata, DCP LSE, and the
  native mask0 call.

### Kernel correctness

Standalone gfx950 numerical comparison for FP8 Q/KV, H64, Q4, QK dimension
576, value dimension 512, `causal=False`, and `return_lse=True`:

| Metric | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Output maximum absolute error | 0.010949 |
| Output mean absolute error | 0.001723 |
| LSE maximum absolute error | 0.000005 |

The run loaded
`mla_a8w8_qh32_qseqlen4_gqaratio32_msk0_lse_ps`.

### End-to-end correctness

Real-weight Kimi-K3 TP8/DCP8 with DSpark K4, FP8 target/draft KV, greedy
sampling, and real block rejection:

| Evaluation | Accuracy | Invalid responses | Output tokens | Duration |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K 5-shot, N=50, concurrency=64 | **50/50** | **0/50** | 5,339 | 28.18 s |

A dummy-weight `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` graph capture/replay also completed a
routed request while loading the FP8 mask0+LSE kernel on all eight ranks.

### Performance

Isolated draft-MLA kernel timing on one MI355X:

| Batch | Rank-local context | Triton | AITER | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 1,024 | 54.44 us | 55.58 us | 0.98x |
| 8 | 1,024 | 69.11 us | 54.71 us | 1.26x |
| 8 | 8,192 | 553.36 us | 58.86 us | 9.40x |
| 16 | 8,192 | 1,095.28 us | 76.24 us | 14.37x |

Real-weight fixed-random serving used 65,536 input tokens, 512 output tokens,
greedy sampling, `ignore_eos`, two warmup requests, full graphs, and synthetic
acceptance length 3.36 for K4:

| Topology | Variant | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT | Errors |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TP8, concurrency 1 | no spec | 36.72 | 4.338 s | 18.79 ms | 0 |
| TP8, concurrency 1 | Triton K4 | 64.14 | 4.248 s | 7.31 ms | 0 |
| TP8, concurrency 1 | AITER K4 | 65.65 | 4.251 s | 6.94 ms | 0 |
| TP8/DCP8, concurrency 40 | no spec | 99.39 | 102.853 s | 169.92 ms | 0 |
| TP8/DCP8, concurrency 40 | Triton K4 | 107.75 | 99.501 s | 145.03 ms | 0 |
| TP8/DCP8, concurrency 40 | AITER K4 | 108.78 | 98.776 s | 143.69 ms | 0 |

AITER versus Triton improves output throughput by 2.35% at TP8/concurrency 1
and 0.96% at TP8/DCP8/concurrency 40. The larger isolated-kernel gain shows
that draft MLA is accelerated, while the end-to-end result remains bounded by
the draft MoE, target verification, collectives, and prefill work.
