title: [ROCm][Spec Decode] Enable adaptive DSpark verification for MiniMax M3
body:
## Summary

PR adaptive DSpark verification for MiniMax M3 on ROCm. Part of the adaptive DSpark backend expansion (#51303): each model needs varlen-capable sparse kernels before adaptive verification can redistribute draft tokens across requests
It was validated end to end with amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 and nvidia/MiniMax-M3-DSpark on MI325.

Scope: only the ROCm Triton indexer and sparse-decode paths gain ragged decode support. The CUDA and AITER MiniMax M3 backends still report device/CPU query-length mismatch as unsupported, so adaptive verification stays disabled there. With adaptive verification off, the uniform decode path is unchanged.

## Changes

- MiniMax M3 indexer and sparse attention (ROCm Triton): device-side ragged decode metadata; both AMD index-score launch policies, the fused top-k selector, and sparse decode map packed query tokens to requests from device `query_start_loc`.
- `kernel_paged_attention_2d`: return for `query_len != 1` (previously `> 1`). FULL cudagraph replay can pad the request dimension with zero-length rows, which fell into the decode path and read one row past the logical query buffer.
- Rejection sampler: adaptive verification allows the regular chunked path for batches with no draft tokens, whose logits layout isnever compacted.
- Warmup: synthetic draft rows are bounded by the same rejection-sampler budget used at runtime, so large `max_num_seqs` configs nolonger fail at startup.
- Adaptive verification overhead: confidence D2H copies use a non-blocking ring, and only TP rank 0 computes the draft budget, thenbroadcasts it.
- DSpark config: prefer speculators-format top-level confidence-head fields and fall back to NVIDIA's legacy `dflash_config` fields.


Token-to-request mapping uses upstream's `compute_token_to_req_indices`, a device-side binary search over `query_start_loc`. It doesn't depend on `max_query_len` and handles zero-length rows and the padding tail.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs (adaptive verification, MiniMax M3 DSpark, token-to-request mapping, paged-decode zero-length). The closest is #52893, which skips AITER sparse PA under spec decode; this PR adds ragged decode to the Triton path instead.

## Testing

On MI325:
- `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py`: 138 passed, 1 skipped.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py`: all passed.
- `test_prefix_prefill.py::test_contexted_kv_attention` (`chunked_prefill_paged_decode`, source build of this branch): 128 passed, 256 skipped.

- Stress test of the ragged index top-k and sparse decode kernels at serving-sized batches: 60 random batches of 380–512 requests (1–8 query tokens each, up to 4K context, zero-length padding rows), reference-checked every 10th batch: all passed.

## End-to-end results 

MI325, `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-DSpark` drafter with its default confidence head, `num_speculative_tokens=7`, FULL cudagraphs, default memory settings, `--max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 512`. Fixed vs adaptive verification on the same build.

GSM8K, full test set (1,319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, concurrency 64):

| Checkpoint | TP | Fixed | Adaptive |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4` | 2 | 0.8196 | 0.8226 |
| `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` | 4 | 0.8779 | 0.8711 |
| `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` (BF16) | 8 | 0.8704 | 0.8688 |

Repeated MXFP8 runs vary by about ±0.01 for both modes (fixed 0.860–0.878 over 6 runs, adaptive 0.867–0.879 over 9 runs). One earlyadaptive MXFP8 run scored 0.801; it did not reproduce in 9 later runs and is still being investigated.

Sonnet 550 in / 150 out / 200 shared prefix, ignore EOS, output tok/s (adaptive gain vs fixed):

| Concurrency | MXFP4, TP=2 | MXFP8, TP=4 | BF16, TP=8 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 649.96 → 674.59 (+3.8%) | 2241.79 → 2166.80 (−3.3%) | 3451.90 → 3327.16 (−3.6%) |
| 256 | 882.77 → 930.58 (+5.4%) | 2560.18 → 2605.40 (+1.8%) | 4005.66 → 4063.85 (+1.5%) |
| 320 | 965.59 → 1020.85 (+5.7%) | 2643.30 → 2733.47 (+3.4%) | 4099.15 → 4268.66 (+4.1%) |
| 380 | 1013.94 → 1071.63 (+5.7%) | 2686.83 → 2778.46 (+3.4%) | 4190.48 → crash (see below) |
| 420 | 1040.76 → 1102.05 (+5.9%) | 2713.55 → 2692.00 (−0.8%) | 4263.58 → crash |
| 500 | 1089.06 → 1146.61 (+5.3%) | fixed OOM → 1929.71 | 4228.05 → crash |

The gain shrinks as verification gets cheaper: TP=4 and TP=8 leave little verify cost for adaptive budgeting to save. MXFP8 fixed verification at concurrency 500 runs out of memory allocating the full verification logits (1.6 GB) at the default `--gpu-memory-utilization`; adaptive verification bounds that allocation and completes all requests.

### Known issue: BF16, TP=8, adaptive, concurrency ≥ 380

The adaptive BF16 server aborts with `HW Exception by GPU node-N ... reason: GPU Hang` under sustained load at concurrency 380–420 (reproduced twice; fixed verification is stable at the same load, MXFP4 TP=2 and MXFP8 TP=4 adaptive are stable through concurrency 500). The ragged MiniMax kernels pass the stress test above. Most likely root cause fix in #56831 - this is well-known issue at this point. Need to run TP=8 test with this PR applied).

## Earlier results (before rebase)

MXFP4 target with the `olka-fi/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4-DSpark` drafter, TP=2, same Sonnet workload, 3–5 minute steady-state runs; 9,040 requests, none failed.

| Concurrency | Fixed tok/s | Adaptive tok/s | Gain | Fixed median TPOT | Adaptive median TPOT |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 299.82 | 330.13 | +10.1% | 381.78 ms | 342.55 ms |
| 256 | 413.86 | 479.84 | +15.9% | 500.45 ms | 406.09 ms |
| 320 | 471.08 | 573.31 | +21.7% | 570.16 ms | 446.81 ms |
| 380 | 488.89 | 603.86 | +23.5% | 615.22 ms | 478.64 ms |
| 420 | 528.18 | 658.30 | +24.6% | 645.89 ms | 489.64 ms |
| 500 | 568.84 | 731.51 | +28.6% | 667.91 ms | 521.15 ms |

title: [Bugfix] Synchronize mixed prefill-decode warmup
body:
## Purpose

`run_mixed_prefill_decode_warmup()` returned before its asynchronous accelerator work completed. This allowed later warmup phases to overlap with it and intermittently segfault DeepSeek-V4 sparse-MLA startup on ROCm.

This change synchronizes after cleanup and KV connector restoration. The synchronization runs only after successful warmup, uses the hardware-neutral accelerator API, and is outside the serving path. The focused test now verifies this completion boundary, while tests that perform real synchronization run on CUDA-like platforms.

Fixes #57354.

AI assistance was used for this PR.

## Reproducer

On a node with four MI355X GPUs, run the following inside `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-dc36fcce902a63eab06c1b93a5c4a5ee178a0c56` (digest `sha256:ce62c0aead55bcb36e4ee05f179fb4e55a31dd1bcb5d2184aaa0d353f60a4b68`). Startup alone is sufficient; no client request is needed.

```bash
export HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1
export AITER_USE_CK_MOE_SORTING=1
export PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1

vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --block-size 256 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384
```

The failure is intermittent. In controlled alternating runs, the unpatched image failed during startup in 4/5 attempts after every worker entered the 16-token sparse-MLA mixed warmup:

```text
Warming up DeepSeek V4 sparse MLA attention for mixed tokens=16.
!!!!!! Segfault encountered !!!!!!!
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in 0xffffffffffffffff
Worker proc VllmWorker-1 died unexpectedly (exit code: None), shutting down executor.
EngineCore failed to start.
```

## Related Work

[PR #50072](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50072) proposed multiple synchronization points for a different report that was later traced to an external `SIGTERM`. This change adds one completion boundary for a controlled ROCm reproducer.

## Test Plan

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mixed_warmup_gate.py
```

Compare unpatched and patched DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 startup on four MI355X GPUs, then run independent serialization controls.

## Test Result

- Controlled same-image startup A/B: unpatched segfaulted in 4/5 runs; patched reached readiness and served one request in 5/5.
- Latest pinned nightly, unpinned model revision, `dtype=auto`, and default JIT warmup: the unpatched server reproduced the segfault in the first attempt.
- Without an explicit `--compilation-config`, the unpatched server passed once and reproduced the segfault on the second attempt.
- Omitting all three environment flags passed 5/5, but those runs defaulted DeepSeek-V4 to Model Runner V1 on ROCm and therefore did not test the affected V2 configuration.
- Independent unpatched controls: `AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3` passed 2/2 and `HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` passed 1/1.
- After rebasing onto upstream `main` at `10e8d5614c50ad180acbe61878c93d98ca7098a9`, focused tests on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-dc36fcce902a63eab06c1b93a5c4a5ee178a0c56`: `30 passed, 14 warnings`.
- Post-rebase changed-file pre-commit: passed on the same pinned image.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash cannot serve on SM120/SM121 (GB10) at e77daef89 — SWA cache block 32 vs SM120 decode page 64; ratio-1 indexer block_kv=128 vs DeepGEMM sm120 (64 only)
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `0.1.1.dev5+ge77daef89` — the per-commit aarch64 wheel of `e77daef89e18e08321ae7b8b24827eedd5fe8673` ("[Model] Support DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (#56214)") installed `--no-deps` over `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-e7edf17cea217e52701f913cd8491fcacf2d9490` (arm64; CUDA 13.0, torch `2.13.0+cu130`, flashinfer `0.6.18.post1` + `flashinfer-jit-cache 0.6.18.post1+cu130`, DeepGEMM vendored at `vllm.third_party.deep_gemm`, the `nv_dev@8b1392b` pin).
- Host: NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, `torch.cuda.get_device_capability() == (12, 1)`, unified memory), driver 580.173.02, Ubuntu 24.04, kernel `6.17.0-1032-nvidia`, Docker 29.2.1 + nvidia-container-toolkit 1.20.0 (`--gpus all`).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` takes the SM12x route on capability 12.x (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/nvidia/model.py`: `major == 12` → `DeepseekV4FlashInferSM120Attention`), but two host-side geometry choices make the model fail during `flashinfer_sparse_mla_warmup` before serving anything. Both are deterministic and independent of the weights — reproduced with `--load-format dummy` and a layer-trimmed `config.json` of `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (heads / head_dim / index_topk / sliding_window untouched).

**1. Sliding-window cache block 32 vs the SM120 sparse-MLA decode dispatch (page 64).**
`vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/attention.py` constructs `DeepseekV4SWACache(..., block_size=32)` (hardcoded; `deepseek_v4` uses the default 64). On SWA-only layers (`compress_ratio == 0`) `nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py` hands that cache to the SM120 sparse kernel as the KV cache (`compressed_kv_cache = swa_k_cache`, `compressed_block_size = swa_metadata.block_size`), and FlashInfer's `mla/_sparse_mla_sm120.py` only has DSV4 decode kernels for `page_block_size == 64` (`_DECODE_DSV4_PAGE_BLOCK_SIZE = 64`; `_decode_dsv4_dispatchable`):

```
File ".../vllm/model_executor/warmup/flashinfer_sparse_mla_warmup.py", line 201, in ...
ValueError: SM120 sparse-MLA has no decode kernel for this shape: num_tokens=2, num_heads=64, topk=128, d_qk=512, page_block_size=32, model_type=1, extra_topk=0. Supported decode shapes are enumerated in _DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH and _DECODE_DSV3_2_DISPATCH.
```

A one-line in-container change `block_size=32 → 64` at that constructor makes the SWA warmup pass (the (64,128) decode entry then dispatches).

**2. Ratio-1 layers hand the DeepGEMM SM120 paged-MQA-logits indexer `block_kv=128`; it accepts only 64.**
`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py` (`DeepseekV41IndexerBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes`) returns 64 on Hopper and **128 otherwise**; `num_states = block_size // compress_ratio` (`kv_cache_interface.py`) is what the indexer passes as `block_size` into `get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata`. Ratio-2 layers → 64 (fine), ratio-1 layers → 128, and the `kernel_block_size` split only applies to `compress_ratio > 1`. With the SWA fix above in place:

```
File ".../vllm/model_executor/warmup/flashinfer_sparse_mla_warmup.py", line 204, in ...
File ".../vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py", line 1287, in ... get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata
RuntimeError: Assertion error (deepgemm-src/csrc/apis/attention.hpp:262): block_kv == 32 or block_kv == 64
```

The vendored DeepGEMM `_C` additionally guards `(arch_major == 12 and ((is_fp4 and (32|64)) or (not is_fp4 and block_kv == 64)))` — on arch 12 the non-fp4 paged kernel takes only 64. The real model has 20 ratio-1 layers out of 40 (`compress_ratios` = 2×0, 18×2, 20×1), so this is not a corner case. Same class as #53635 (V4's `num_states` vs `block_kv`), reached from V4.1's 128-token indexer block.

**What does work** (with fix 1 applied and a ratio-2-only trimmed topology `[0,0,2,2,2,2]`): the server comes up in ~96 s; FlashInfer SM120 sparse-MLA prefill + decode (the prebuilt `sm_120` cubins from `flashinfer-jit-cache` run on sm_121 without `cudaErrorIllegalInstruction`), DeepGEMM `sm120_fp8_paged_mqa_logits<…, 64, …>`, and `DEEPGEMM_MXFP4` MoE all JIT and serve completions (2k / 3.5k-token prompts, 4 concurrent 1k prompts) with finite logprobs and zero tracebacks. Note: the `deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/o_proj.py` FP8 einsum was not reached — `wo_a` is dequantized to BF16 at load by `EmulationMxfp8LinearKernel` (chosen for the bmm-shaped MXFP8 weight on SM120), so o_proj took the `torch.bmm` branch.

### Reproduction

```bash
# model dir: config.json + tokenizer files from deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, then edit config.json → text_config:
#   num_hidden_layers 6, compress_ratios [0,0,2,2,1,1], kv_source_layer_ids [2,4], index_source_layer_ids [2,4],
#   candidate_topk_blocks 0, candidate_source_layer_id -1, engram_layer_ids [], engram_num_embeddings [],
#   num_nextn_predict_layers 0, dspark_target_layer_ids [], n_routed_experts 64; vision_config.num_hidden_layers 0
docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host --network host -v $PWD/model:/smoke/model \
  -e VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-e7edf17cea217e52701f913cd8491fcacf2d9490 \
  # (with the e77daef89 wheel pip-installed --no-deps on top)
  /smoke/model --served-model-name dsv41-smoke --load-format dummy --dtype bfloat16 \
  --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.25 --enforce-eager --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --trust-remote-code
```

Failure 1 appears as shipped; failure 2 appears once `DeepseekV4SWACache(block_size=64)` is applied. Both are in warmup, before `/health` goes 200.

### Expected behavior / suggestion

On arch 12 the V4.1 SWA cache should use the 64-token pages the SM120 dispatch has (as V4 does), and the indexer's kernel block should be 64 on arch 12 as on Hopper (or DeepGEMM's sm120 paged kernel should accept 128) — the two choices interact through `compressed_block_size = block_size // compress_ratio` (ratio-2 wants a 128 block to land on 64), so the fix likely belongs in the `kernel_block_size` remapping for ratio 1 rather than a global block change. Happy to re-run the smoke on GB10 against a branch.

---
_Evidence trail (logs, footprint, cleanup): deacix/legwork#13299 — runtime smoke on a DGX Spark, 2026-09-11._

title: [9/N][Attention] Support adaptive verification in FlashMLA Sparse
body:
## Summary

- allow HiSparse-backed FlashMLA Sparse to capture nonuniform adaptive-verification batches
- preserve packed variable-length decode rows as one MQA batch instead of inventing uniform request boundaries
- derive request rows from device metadata without a device-to-host synchronization

This is split from the core HiSparse PR because FlashMLA Sparse does not support adaptive verification on main; HiSparse can otherwise use the existing FlashInfer Sparse MLA support.

## Duplicate work

I searched open PRs for FlashMLA Sparse adaptive-verification support and found no duplicate. #52988 concerns Kimi-K3 rather than FlashMLA Sparse or HiSparse.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/sparse_mla_attention.py vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py`
- `python -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_hisparse_fp8_decode_preserves_packed_varlen_rows tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_flashmla_hisparse_reports_varlen_cudagraph_support tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_hisparse_flashmla_reorders_full_speculative_window_as_decode`

- GLM TP4 end-to-end smoke with `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` and forced adaptive rejection:

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Isolate sparse index state across microbatches
body:
## Summary

DeepSeek V4.1 keeps top-k token indices and candidate blocks across multiple decoder layers. DBO microbatches currently write the same model-global buffers. A source layer in microbatch 1 can overwrite state before a later consumer layer in microbatch 0 reads it.

Allocate persistent index storage per microbatch on NVIDIA and AMD, and select the active microbatch's view when the short-context indexer, general sparse indexer, or attention consumer accesses it. Keep the existing 2D allocation for non-microbatched execution and the shared indexer's runtime buffer-rebinding API.

```text
ASIS
uBatch 0 source --write--> [shared top-k / candidates] --read--> uBatch 0 consumer
uBatch 1 source --overwrite---------^
```

```text
PR
uBatch 0 source --write--> [uBatch 0 top-k / candidates] --read--> uBatch 0 consumer
uBatch 1 source --write--> [uBatch 1 top-k / candidates] --read--> uBatch 1 consumer
```

## Scope and duplicate check

Related to #56400 and the unresolved shared-top-k overwrite reported in #56440. #56440 repairs input positions and Engram histories; it explicitly leaves sparse-index storage unfixed. Open PR searches for DBO, sparse/microbatch, topk/DBO and `56440 in:body` found no equivalent buffer fix. This change repairs persistent index ownership; it does not claim to resolve the reported NaNs or establish general DBO support.

Index state remains model-owned because it must survive across layers; it is not transient scratch workspace. With two microbatches, the additional storage is `max_num_batched_tokens * (index_topk + candidate_topk_blocks) * 4` bytes per worker (20 MiB at 2048 scheduled tokens, top-k 512, and 2048 candidate blocks).

## Validation

- `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py -q`: 26 passed on GB200 with both PyTorch 2.11 and 2.13; final exact-base native/pinned-runtime rerun also passed all 26 tests, including actual threaded UBatchRunner interleaving and separate CUDA graph capture/replay.
- Negative control forcing both microbatches to slot 0 fails the new cross-layer regression: 48/96 output elements mismatch. This reproduces shared-storage corruption in the runner harness, not a full-model NaN.
- White-box CPU probe of actual V4.1 attention, short-context indexer and generic sparse-indexer buffer properties: correct per-microbatch views, candidate lifetime, and legacy buffer rebinding.
- Changed-file pre-commit, including mypy: passed on the final patch.
- Model smoke: **5/5 expected answers**, official DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, TP4 GB200, text-only, eager, max context 2048, no prefix cache, greedy max 32 output tokens. Includes a long prompt to exercise general sparse indexing. Used native extensions for exact base `7ef4d9bfe` and pinned dependencies. This is a non-DBO smoke test, not a model-accuracy benchmark. Additional full-model eager DBO qualification is described below. No performance or model-accuracy improvement is claimed.


## Full-model eager DBO qualification

On integration commit `8276917` (this feature plus #56440 input/history corrections), DP2 x TP2 + EP on four GB200 GPUs, DeepEP LL with local NVLink transport:

- Twelve long fixed-answer prompts passed with microbatching disabled by runtime thresholds, then passed with DBO active in the same engine. Output token IDs match exactly.
- Both microbatch IDs ran on all four EP ranks. Each worker passed 8 top-k checks between layers 2 and 3 and 8 candidate-block checks between layers 20 and 24.
- Aliasing only the persistent index storage back to slot 0 then reproduced a top-k overwrite on all four workers: 179830-179834 mismatched entries over 1024 rows in microbatch 0, recorded before layer 3 consumed the buffer.

Configuration: eager, synchronous scheduling, no prefix cache, 2048 max context/scheduled tokens, 16 max sequences, 1 GiB KV per worker, greedy max 32 output tokens. DeepEP `d4f41e4`, NCCL 2.30.7, NVSHMEM 3.4.5, `NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH=8192`, `NVSHMEM_REMOTE_TRANSPORT=none`. Hooks synchronize comparisons; these are correctness diagnostics, not performance measurements. Full-model CUDA graphs and inter-node transport remain unvalidated. #56440 is a validation dependency and is not bundled in this feature diff.

## Reproducibility

[Validation report, exact executed harness, outputs, collision records, and checksums](https://github.com/foraxe/vllm/tree/f22ceb1fe9916ef58ca3ef7b0abbc917a24b5407/evidence/dsv41-dbo-index-state). The [integration source](https://github.com/foraxe/vllm/tree/827691787a3c29ffa3b28ebe8dc9cbd151a70bff) adds only #56440's input/history changes to this feature.

Model diagnostic command (environment and local model path described in the report):

```bash
.venv/bin/python dbo_model_eval.py --dbo --paired --negative-control --output dbo-qualified.json
```

AI assistance: implementation and validation used OpenAI Codex. The human submitter confirmed review of feature commit `ec24188` and rerunning relevant tests before submission.

title: [Bug]: DSML tool-call recovery (#55954) emits ghost empty-argument calls on truncation and narration, and recovers undeclared tools
body:
## Summary

`#55954` recovers DSML tool calls when the model omits the `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` wrapper by committing as soon as it sees the `<｜DSML｜invoke name="` prefix. On three reachable shapes this produces a **tool call with empty arguments plus a truncated assistant message**, and on a fourth it **recovers a tool the request never declared**. `#56141` fixes only the misspelled-wrapper case; the family above is unchanged on current main.

Measured on the `deepseek_v4` parser at `e7edf17c` with a 12-case matrix (each case run both non-streaming and streaming). "ghost" = a tool call whose `arguments` is `""` or `{}`. "delivered" = characters handed to the caller vs. input length.

| case | expected | stock `e7edf17c` | with #52645 semantics |
|---|---|---|---|
| N1 narration then bare unclosed `invoke` (truncated) | plain content | `n=1 ghost=True` delivered **33/61** | `n=0` delivered 61/61 |
| N7 narration mentioning the invoke syntax (zh) | plain content | `n=1 ghost=True` delivered **5/49** | `n=0` delivered 49/49 |
| N8 narration mentioning the invoke syntax (en) | plain content | `n=1 ghost=True` delivered **52/94** | `n=0` delivered 94/94 |
| N9 orphan `invoke` naming an **undeclared** tool | plain content | **`n=1`** delivered 6/120 | `n=0` delivered 120/120 |
| R1 misspelled wrapper `toolcalls` | recover | `n=1` ✔ (this is #56141) | `n=1` ✔ |
| R2 `<｜DSML｜parameter>` without `string=` | recover | `n=1 ghost=True` | `n=1` ✔ |
| N2–N6, R3 | — | ✔ | ✔ |

Totals: stock **5 failures**, stock + the two small hunks (`string=` optional, `finish_reason=length`) **4 failures**, #52645 semantics **0 failures**. Streaming and non-streaming agree on every case.

An extra check: with `tools=None` / `tool_choice="none"`, stock still recovers (`n=1`, delivers 10/118 characters); the #52645 semantics deliver the full 118 characters and emit no call.

## Why this matters in practice

N1 is the common one. A request that hits `max_tokens` mid-`invoke` currently yields both a chopped assistant message and a `('bash', '{}')`-shaped call. A harness that does not inspect `finish_reason` will dispatch an argument-less tool call; one that does will drop the turn, but the visible text was already truncated.

N9 is a contract issue independent of truncation: the parser should not synthesize a call for a tool the request did not declare.

## What behaves correctly

`#52645`'s "hold provisional → validate the tool name against the request's declared tools → commit only at `</｜DSML｜invoke>` → otherwise roll back to the original text" passes all 12 cases in both modes, including N9 and the no-tools case. Its own 87-case suite also passes unmodified.

## Suggestion

Gate the recovery in #55954 on (a) the tool name being present in the request's declared tools, and (b) the invoke block actually closing, rolling the buffered text back verbatim when either fails — i.e. adopt #52645's provisional-commit discipline rather than committing on the opening prefix.

Happy to share the matrix script; it is self-contained and needs only the parser (no GPU).

## Environment

vLLM `e7edf17c` (`0.28.1rc1.dev681`), `deepseek_v4` tool parser, DeepSeek-V4-Flash. Matrix run in a CPU-only one-off container against the shipped parser.

title: [RFC]: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash performance on ROCm
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash leaves a lot of the device on the table on AMD MI355X (gfx950). Measured on an 8x MI355X node, TP4, MXFP4 MoE + DSpark MTP:

| concurrency | out tok/s | out tok/s per GPU | TTFT p50 | ITL p50 | E2EL p50 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 35.89 | 8.97 | 0.898 | 0.0256 | 15.03 |
| 2 | 49.10 | 12.27 | 0.940 | 0.0267 | 17.22 |
| 4 | 86.99 | 21.75 | 0.634 | 0.0271 | 5.55 |
| 8 | 164.69 | 41.17 | 0.609 | 0.0307 | 12.10 |
| 16 | 292.60 | 73.15 | 0.684 | 0.0332 | 14.61 |
| 32 | 469.41 | 117.35 | 0.825 | 0.0477 | 17.57 |

The shape of that table is the telling part. Going from concurrency 1 to 32 costs only **1.9x** in ITL (0.0256 -> 0.0477) while delivering **13x** more output per GPU, so the device is nowhere near saturated: there is a large fixed cost per decode step that concurrency merely amortises. A captured decode trace says what that cost is. At a single-stream ITL of 25.6 ms, a decode step issues **14,020 kernel launches**, and 85% of each layer's 350 launches are attributable to the mHC block - bookkeeping on a 4x4 matrix.

| launches/layer | share | source |
|---:|---:|---|
| 162 | 48.6% | mHC sinkhorn loop |
| 122 | 36.6% | mHC pre/post mix + eager RMSNorm |
| 24 | 7.2% | MoE / FFN (already fused) |
| 12 | 3.6% | dtype casts/copies |
| 6 | 1.8% | attention + fused norm/quant |
| 4 | 1.2% | TP collective |
| 3 | 0.9% | other |

> **Trace methodology, since it affects what the numbers can support.** The trace had to be captured with `--enforce-eager`: with CUDA graphs on, roctracer's HSA queue interposition deadlocks against hipGraph replay on this ROCm build (the first step after `/start_profile` never completes and the workers spin in `queue_interposition.cpp` waiting on an HSA signal). So **only the launch counts and kernel composition should be read as load-bearing** - those are graph-invariant, since a graph replays the kernel sequence it captured rather than merging kernels. All wall-clock, occupancy and idle-gap figures from that trace are inflated by eager dispatch plus profiler overhead and are deliberately not used for any claim here. The throughput and ITL numbers above are from normal graph-enabled serving runs, not from the traced run.

This is purely a performance question - accuracy is already where it should be. Recording it here as the standard for the work below, since every item in this RFC is a performance change that has to hold accuracy. gsm8k 5-shot via lm-eval, same node and configuration:

| | strict-match | flexible-extract |
|---|---:|---:|
| baseline | 0.9704 ± 0.0047 | 0.9697 ± 0.0047 |
| with #56503 | 0.9727 ± 0.0045 | 0.9719 ± 0.0045 |
| with #56503 + #56513 | 0.9735 ± 0.0044 | 0.9727 ± 0.0045 |

Harness gate is 0.91. Anything landing against this RFC should be checked against the numbers above rather than just the gate, since a change can pass 0.91 while still having broken something.

What follows is grouped by optimization direction. Each item is verified against the code rather than assumed, and several turn out to be different from what they look like from the outside.

---

## 1. mHC seam fusion

The largest single direction, since 85% of per-layer launches live here.

### 1.1 mHC pre -> AITER

`vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/amd/model.py` imports `mhc_pre_delayed_torch` / `mhc_post_torch` directly, so every sublayer seam spends ~141 launches Sinkhorn-normalizing a 4x4 matrix. V4 already dispatches through `MHCPreOp` / `MHCPostOp` and reaches AITER; V4.1 was never migrated, because it collapses each sublayer's input with the *previous* sublayer's pre-mix and AITER's `mhc_pre` neither returns its pre-mix nor accepts an incoming one.

Merged as #56503: 141 -> 4 launches per seam, worst relative error 1.2e-5, gsm8k unchanged.

At concurrency 1 that moved ITL p50 from 25.58 ms to 6.89 ms. Read that as directional only, not as a 3.7x per-token speedup: the agentic trace is time-driven, so the faster run sampled a different and longer segment (mean input 168,856 -> 206,458 tokens, mean output 954 -> 1,683). The confound runs against the result, but a clean figure needs a fixed-request-count replay. Details in the PR.

### 1.2 Fused mHC post+pre for V4.1

`deepseek_v4/amd/model.py` has 4 references to `MHCFusedPostPreOp` / `mhc_fused_post_pre`; `deepseek_v4_1/amd/model.py` has **zero**. `mhc_fused_post_pre_gemm_sqrsum` applies the post step and projects the resulting residual in one kernel, and has gfx950-specific tuning (`_mhc_fused_config_gfx950_256`). It needs the same `pre_mix` plumbing #56503 added, so it is a direct follow-on rather than separate work.

Sizing this honestly: because the delayed formulation still needs the pre-mix epilogue and the delayed collapse, folding in the post takes the seam from 6 launches to 5, not to 2. Measured on gfx950, all-reduce excluded: 5 -> 4.

Above 1024 tokens AITER's own heuristic prefers separate kernels, so this is a decode-path win by construction. The name misleads here: `mhc_fused_post_pre_large_m` is *not* a fused kernel, it is plain `mhc_post` + `mhc_pre` with a non-temporal store hint (`store_nt=0` above `8 * num_cu`) and `large_m_splitk=True`, neither of which the fused kernel can express. Once the residual stops fitting in cache there is nothing left for fusion to save.

Addressed by #56513 (draft). Measured at 1.28% lower mean ITL at concurrency 1, 95% CI [0.07%, 2.48%], as a two-way crossover over both halves of the node with a fixed 24-request replay -- the two GPU sets here differ by 0.96%, so a single-orientation A/B cannot resolve an effect this size. One loose end that change does not close: its fallback is the plain post plus delayed pre, so it asks for neither large-m tuning. Inert between 1024 and 2048 tokens, but a real miss at prefill, which reaches 16384 tokens here. Needs a `store_nt` argument on the shared `mhc_post` wrapper that V4 also uses.

Note `_AITER_MHC_FUSED_RMSNORM_SIZES = {1280, 2560, 4096, 7168}` excludes V4.1-Flash's `hidden_size=5120`, so the fused-RMSNorm variant does not apply here; extending that set, or the kernel's supported sizes, is a separate question.

**Parallel ROCm work on the same seam.** #56342 reaches 1.1/1.2 by a different route: instead of dispatching the AMD path through AITER, it fixes the TileLang `mhc_pre_big_fuse*` kernels on 64-wide wavefronts and moves V4.1's AMD path onto the fused TileLang kernels. Its own measurement is that the switch without the wavefront fix is a 91.1% -> 23.7% gsm8k regression, so both halves land together. That makes it and #56503/#56513 two answers to the same question -- which backend owns the V4.1 AMD mHC seam -- and they should be reconciled before either goes further.

### 1.3 Fused all-reduce + mHC post

Worth being explicit about why this, and not all-reduce + RMSNorm, which is the more obvious proposal. Three reasons, in increasing order of decisiveness:

1. **The ROCm AR+RMSNorm pass exists and auto-enables.** `RocmAiterAllReduceFusionPass` is selected when `fuse_allreduce_rms` is set and AITER is enabled (`vllm/compilation/passes/pass_manager.py:176-180`), and `enable_allreduce_rms_fusion` returns true on ROCm for TP>1 (`vllm/config/vllm.py:171-185`). Our server duly logs `Enabled custom fusions: ..., allreduce_rms, ...`.
2. **But it is an Inductor FX pattern matcher, and this model is invisible to it.** There is no `@support_torch_compile` anywhere under `vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/` (verified: zero matches), so the pass never sees the model graph. "Enabled" in that log is misleading.
3. **And the pattern is not in the model anyway.** V4.1's decoder has no `all_reduce -> RMSNorm` seam. The TP all-reduce lives inside `_o_proj` / `_bpre_attn_gemm(..., reduce_tp=True)`, and what follows it is the **mHC post block**. Contrast `deepseek_v32/amd/model.py`, which does call `fused_allreduce_rms_norm` explicitly.

The fusion that does apply is already written and unused: `aiter/ops/custom_all_reduce.py` defines `fused_allreduce_mhc_post_only`, `_one_stage` and `_split` plus `launch_*` wrappers, backed by the prebuilt `aiter/jit/module_fused_ar_mhc.so`. vLLM has **zero** references to any of them. At 4 collective launches per layer, wiring this removes both the collective and the post kernel from each seam.

Proposal: add `rocm_aiter_ops.fused_allreduce_mhc_post` and call it from the V4.1 AMD seam. Separately, `docs/design/fusions.md:101-107` still documents AR+RMSNorm as NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell + FlashInfer only and should be corrected now that the AITER path exists.

**Correction: 1.2 and 1.3 are alternatives, not additive.** Both consume the same post step -- 1.2 folds it forward into the pre projection, 1.3 folds it backward into the collective -- so whichever lands, the other has nothing left to fuse. Each is worth one launch out of six. AITER ships only `fused_allreduce_mhc_post_{only,one_stage,split}`; there is no AR+post+pre kernel that would get both. 1.3 also needs the un-reduced attention output, which today is consumed inside `_o_proj`, so it means plumbing a deferred-all-reduce contract through `DeepseekV4Attention.forward` for both the attention and MoE seams.

Given equal payoff, I am pursuing 1.2 (self-contained) and leaving 1.3 unclaimed. It becomes clearly worthwhile if someone adds a three-way AR+post+pre kernel, which would take the seam to 4.

## 2. Multi-stream overlap

The interesting direction, because the code is already written and currently does nothing on the decode path.

### 2.1 Existing overlap is disabled by breakable-cudagraph capture

V4.1 attention **already** overlaps three aux streams (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/attention.py`): input projections via `execute_in_parallel` (`793-801`), Q/SWA-cache-insert against the compressor forward (`688-697`), and indexer prep against `compressor.insert_cache` (`713-720`). V4.1 AMD even allocates them unconditionally - `aux_stream_list = [torch.cuda.Stream() for _ in range(3)]` (`amd/model.py:376-380`) - with no `is_rocm()` gate, unlike V4 AMD which disables them outright for hang reasons (`deepseek_v4/amd/model.py:964-968`).

But both overlap helpers drop to sequential execution during breakable CUDA graph capture:

```python
# vllm/utils/multi_stream_utils.py
if aux_stream is not None:
    from vllm.compilation.breakable_cudagraph import BreakableCUDAGraphCapture
    if BreakableCUDAGraphCapture.is_active():
        aux_stream = None
```

Our runs log `Breakable CUDA graph enabled`. Because the decode graph is **captured** serially, every replay is serial too, so on the decode path all of this overlap is dead. Prefill, uncaptured, still gets it.

The ask is therefore to make the existing overlap survive capture - record the aux streams into the graph, or exempt these regions - and then confirm gfx950 does not reproduce the hangs that caused V4 AMD to disable aux streams. The stale comments at `attention.py:429-430` ("Will be None on ROCm for now") and `690` ("sequential on ROCm") describe V4, not V4.1, and should be fixed alongside.

One genuine scheduling gap remains beyond that: `indexer_op` -> `forward_mqa` is fully serialized (`attention.py:817-829`). The top-k indices are a hard dependency, but MLA prep could plausibly be hoisted to overlap the indexer.

On terminology: there is no `CSA2` in the tree. CSA/HCA refers to the compressor path, and V4.1's `DeepseekCompressor` supports `compress_ratio` 1 and 2 only (ratio-4/128 is v4.0 CuTe-DSL and explicitly not wired).

### 2.2 DeepSeek MoE gets neither stream overlap nor kernel fusion

The generic `MoERunner` supports shared-expert overlap on the aux stream (`SharedExpertsOrder.MULTI_STREAM_OVERLAPPED`, gated `is_cuda_alike()` plus a 256-token threshold), and Inkling's AMD MoE uses `maybe_execute_in_parallel` for exactly this. DeepSeek AMD MoE uses neither, because it is meant to get shared-expert fusion at the kernel level via `fuse_heterogeneous_shared_expert`.

That fusion requires **all** of gfx950, `tensor_parallel_size == 8`, and `moe_backend == "aiter"` (`deepseek_v4/amd/model.py:210-231`). At TP4 with `aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16` we satisfy only the first, so the shared expert is simply serialized against the routed experts. Either relax the fusion gate or enable the aux-stream path for DeepSeek on ROCm. Note this interacts with 2.1: while overlap is serialized during capture, the stream option buys nothing.

**Correction: relaxing the TP8 gate is not sufficient.** Reading the gate and AITER together, `fuse_heterogeneous_shared_expert` is pinned to DeepSeek-V4-Pro's geometry, not merely to TP8:

- `_heterogeneous_shared_expert_enabled` also requires `hidden_size == 7168` and `moe_intermediate_size == 3072`. V4.1-Flash is 5120 / 2304.
- It requires the shared expert as block-128 FP8 (`weight_block_size == [128, 128]`). V4.1-Flash ships it as FP8 E4M3 with **32x32** E8M0 scales -- `layers.N.ffn.shared_experts.w1.weight` is `[2304, 5120]` with `.scale` `[72, 160]` -- and `_prepare_native_fp8_shared_expert` validates the `(2*inter/128, hidden/128)` scale shape before expanding it to FHMoE's 1x32 layout, so it raises on ours rather than falling back.
- AITER's tuned config has no row for us. `aiter/configs/tuned_fhmoe.csv` is 12 rows, every one `model_dim=7168, inter_dim=384, expert=385, topk=7` -- V4-Pro at TP8, since 3072/8 = 384, which is what the `i384` in `supports_dsv4_i384_fhmoe()` names. That helper probes only that tuple.

The homogeneous alternative is closed too: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` runs `is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible`, which requires a Quark MXFP4 OCP export and returns *"DeepSeek-v4 FSE is only implemented/tested with Quark MXFP4"* for this DeepSeek-native `quant_method: fp8` / `expert_dtype: fp4` checkpoint. The heterogeneous kernel exists precisely because FP8-shared-plus-FP4-routed cannot fuse homogeneously, which is our case, just locked to the wrong geometry.

Traces agree with the reading: no `flydsl_*` kernel appears anywhere in a decode step, AITER's dispatch reports `expert=384, topk=6` rather than 385/7, and the server logs `no tuned FlyDSL config for ('gfx950', 256, M, 5120, 640, 384, 6, ...), using heuristic FlyDSL fallback`.

So the kernel-level route needs three things, not one: relax the geometry and TP gates, add a block-32 -> 1x32 expansion for the shared scales, and tune FHMoE for `(5120, 640, 385, 7)`. The aux-stream route is the cheaper ask.

## 3. GEMM autotuning

Cheapest direction here, and the failure mode is worse than "untuned". On a lookup miss AITER sets `libtype="torch", solidx=0` (`aiter/tuned_gemm.py:215-233`), and `torch_gemm` is plain `F.linear` (`415-451`) - not hipBLASLt, which is a separate `libtype`. A miss is a full drop out of the tuned-kernel path.

We see ~**1,220 such calls per decode step**, all from indexer/compressor shapes:

```
shape is M:128, N:128, K:512 ... not found tuned config in
/tmp/aiter_configs/bf16_tuned_gemm.csv, will use default config! using torch solution:0
```

plus `M:10, N:32320, K:5120` and `N:32, K:5120`. The shipped `aiter/configs/bf16_tuned_gemm.csv` has gfx950 rows, but not for these shapes.

The tooling already exists: `AITER_TUNE_GEMM=1` collects missed shapes into `bf16_untuned_gemm.csv` (`tuned_gemm.py:239-269`), and `aiter/utility/pretune.py` / `base_tuner.py` turn that into tuned rows. Proposal: run the collection over a representative V4.1-Flash decode and prefill sweep, then upstream the resulting gfx950 rows to `aiter/configs/`.

## 4. MoE backend selection and tuning

Two halves of one question: are we on the right MoE backend, and is it tunable?

- In-tree gfx950 configs for this model's expert count **do exist**, but only for the FlyDSL/CK path: `E=384,N=256` and `E=384,N=512` with `device_name=AMD_Instinct_MI355X` / `MI355_OAM`, `dtype=int4_w4a16` (+ `backend=flydsl` variants).
- Our recipe forces `--moe-backend aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16`, which resolves to `AiterW4A16ExpertsMonolithic` -> Triton `moe_gemm_a16w4`. That path takes **heuristic** kernel configs (`get_kernel_config_triton/gluon`), and AITER ships no gfx950 `a16w4` tuned dispatch tree (only `a8w4/DEFAULT.json`). None of the configs above apply to us.
- Meanwhile the ROCm oracle, under `moe_backend=auto`, explicitly prefers the other one for this routing method: *"DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm: prefer AITER FlyDSL MoE (better perf + accuracy after shuffle/TP-offset fixes), with Triton-unfused as fallback"* (`oracle/mxfp4.py:690-701`).
- And `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py` cannot tune our backend even if we wanted to: its dtype choices are `auto`, `fp8_w8a8`, `int8_w8a16`, `int4_w4a16` - no MXFP4 mode (`benchmark_moe.py:1075`).

Proposal, in order: A/B `auto` / `aiter` against the forced `aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16` on gfx950 and fix the recipe if FlyDSL wins, since tuned configs already exist for it; then add an MXFP4 mode to `benchmark_moe.py` so the Triton `a16w4` path can be tuned at all; then upstream gfx950 `a16w4` configs.

Note #56543 (DNM) proposes the opposite for the same code path -- pinning `backend="triton"` for both AITER W4A16 MoE GEMMs on gfx942/gfx950 -- so the A/B result above is worth reconciling against it before either lands.

## 5. Prefill top-k combine falls back to Torch

`deepseek_v4_1/amd/rocm.py:175-186` uses ordinary Torch indexing because the Triton kernel inherited from V4 "can issue an out-of-bounds access for V4.1's mixed prefill metadata" on gfx950. Prefill-only and small tensors, but it is a known-missing gfx950-safe kernel and TTFT has room.

Addressed by #56638, which re-enables `_combine_topk_swa_indices_kernel` with the three unsafe behaviours fixed in place. It also notes the fallback is not merely slow: `repeat_interleave` on a tensor syncs to the host, so the Torch path cannot be graph-captured at all.

## 6. DSA sparse indexer

Not in the original write-up, and on a newer nightly it is the second-largest block of the decode step after the MoE GEMMs. Splitting it out of the single "indexer/topk" bucket a category summary produces, at 131k context, MoE on the CK a8w4 path:

| | conc 1 | conc 4 | conc 16 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| mqa logits (fp8 paged) | 0.148 | 0.405 | 1.534 |
| candidate mask | 0.048 | 0.133 | 0.464 |
| candidate select | 0.059 | 0.072 | 0.118 |
| topk per row | 0.485 | 0.527 | 0.838 |
| **indexer total** | **0.741** | **1.138** | **2.954** |
| **share of step** | **4.1%** | **6.2%** | **11.4%** |

The composition inverts with concurrency: at 1 the top-k dominates and is launch-bound, at 16 the MQA logits GEMM does. Full detail and method in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56506#issuecomment-5647767775).

### 6.1 Candidate mask sized by the workspace, not the context

`apply_candidate_mask` receives the `[rows, max_model_len]` logits workspace unsliced, so its grid was 1024 programs per row when ~128 have work, and cost tracked rows while ignoring context. Columns at or past a row's `end` are never read: `top_k_per_row_decode` bounds its scan by the same ends, which is also why the no-candidate path skips the mask entirely and reads the same workspace safely.

Addressed by #56628: 2.7x / 4.3x / 6.0x on the kernel at concurrency 1 / 4 / 16, gsm8k 0.9727 / 0.9719.

### 6.2 `next_n` is spent on program count instead of the GEMM tile

The largest single item at concurrency 16 (1.534 ms/step, 5.9% of the step) is `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits`. AITER launches `grid = batch * next_n * SplitKV`, so with DSpark 5-token MTP the kernel issues six independent M=32 MFMAs per K block where one M=192 would do.

Its own M-scaling, measured at constant K traffic, is monotone: per unit of work M=64 is 1.27x more efficient than M=32, and M=128 is 1.53x. We sit at the worst point of that curve.

Filed as [ROCm/aiter#5477](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/5477). It has to be an AITER change -- the kernel is 2213 lines of hand-scheduled Gluon, `next_n` is not a constexpr there, and a plain-Triton reimplementation of the same algorithm runs 2.2x slower, so the call site cannot reach it.

Two things ruled out on the way, recorded so nobody repeats them. The `grid = batch * next_n * SplitKV` shape looks like it streams K `next_n` times, but building both variants in Triton shows the shared-K version requests 5.2x fewer HBM bytes and is *slightly slower* -- the re-reads are already absorbed by cache. And `VarCtxSchedule`, the persistent-grid variant that looks made for our ragged contexts, is 1.7x slower.

### 6.3 gfx950 decode top-k tunings are unreachable at `index_topk = 512`

`csrc/libtorch_stable/sampler.cu` has two gfx950-specific configurations and both are gated on `topK == 1024`; this model sets 512, so every decode falls to the generic `multipleBlocksPerRowConfig = 10` path. The trace confirms it: `vllm::topKPerRowDecode<512, true, true, false>`. Asking the op for `topK = 1024` is *faster* than 512 at our shapes despite twice the output (0.0508 vs 0.0632 ms at concurrency 16), so the gate looks like tuning rather than a correctness bound. Worth roughly 0.2 ms/step; needs a C++ rebuild to confirm, and I would rather know whether the `== 1024` is deliberate first.

The other three routes are closed on ROCm: `cooperative_topk` and `persistent_topk` both accept `topk_tokens` of 512 but are gated on `is_cuda()`, and AITER's decode top-k is excluded twice in `_get_aiter_top_k_kernel` (by `compress_ratio <= 1` for five of the eight indexer layers, and by the 64k compressed-length bound for the rest). That bound also computes a different quantity in the FULL and non-FULL branches -- `max_model_len` undivided versus `max_seq_len // compress_ratio` -- which should be reconciled even though fixing it unlocks nothing here.

### 6.4 FP4 MQA logits

AITER ships `flydsl_pa_mqa_logits_fp4` and variants. Four things sit in the way: `dsa_indexer_uses_fp4()` raises unless `is_device_capability_family(100)`; `forward_hip` asserts `not self.use_fp4_cache`; there is no FP4 indexer K-cache insert on ROCm (the unfused path asserts, and AITER's `indexer_k_quant_and_cache` has no FP4 mode); and the kernel wants a pre-swizzled `q_scale`.

Sizing this was initially done by traffic accounting -- halve the K read, halve the kernel -- and that is wrong. At `next_n = 6` this kernel is not HBM-bandwidth bound: doubling `heads` doubles the compute at constant K bytes for only 1.5x the time, and removing 5.2x of the K reads changes nothing. So FP4 remains worth having for the memory footprint, but should not be sized as a decode-time win until measured. Accuracy is the larger risk either way, since the indexer picks which 512 tokens attention sees.

## 7. MXFP8 dense-linear path

Not in the original write-up, and after #56503 it is the largest block of the decode step outside the MoE and the indexer. The dense projections (MLA `fused_wqa_wkv` / `wq_b` / `wo_a` / `wo_b`, the indexer projections, the compressor, and the shared-expert MLP) are MXFP8 and run `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`.

Method, since it bounds what these numbers support: rank-0 graph-captured decode traces at 131k context, MoE on the CK a8w4 path, `ROCPROFILER_QUEUE_INTERPOSITION=0`, eight decode steps sampled after all lanes are confirmed decoding by client-side SSE counting. Figures are summed kernel durations divided by steps. That basis is inflated -- at concurrency 1 it sums to 17.4 ms/step against a client-measured unprofiled step of 12.9 ms -- so **only launch counts and relative composition should be read as load-bearing**, not absolute times. Where a claim needs an absolute number it comes from a separate graph-replay microbenchmark, noted inline.

Where the step goes, at concurrency 1 and 32:

| group | c1 | c32 | launches/step (c32) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| sparse indexer | 1.05 | 6.14 | 146 |
| MoE experts (CK a8w4) | 1.20 | 5.92 | 92 |
| long tail of small elementwise ops | 4.11 | 4.96 | 880 |
| **MXFP8 weight dequant (per step)** | **2.15** | **4.47** | 360 |
| MXFP8 linear (quant + GEMM) | 2.13 | 3.98 | 397 |
| MLA attention core | 0.89 | 3.16 | 142 |
| BF16 Tensile GEMMs | 1.23 | 2.73 | 163 |
| TP all-reduce | 0.73 | 2.72 | 98 |
| mHC / hyper-connection | 2.05 | 2.57 | 460 |
| MoE sort / route / quant | 1.45 | 1.82 | 229 |

The step still issues **2,850 launches at concurrency 1 and 3,064 at 32**, of which 89% and 75% respectively are shorter than 10 us. The dispatch-bound thesis in the Motivation survives #56503; it just moved.

### 7.1 The MXFP8 weight is dequantized on every forward

`RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel.apply_weights` needs `K % 128 == 0` for `tl.dot_scaled`, and where that fails it rebuilds a BF16 copy of a constant weight per step:

```python
w_bf16 = dequant_mxfp8_to_bf16(layer.weight, layer.weight_scale)
out = torch.nn.functional.linear(x2d, w_bf16).to(x.dtype)
```

On V4.1-Flash this fires on the shared expert's row-parallel `down_proj`, whose K is sharded while `gate_up`'s stays at 5120: `moe_intermediate_size` 2304 gives 576 at TP4 and 288 at TP8, neither divisible by 128, so TP4 and TP8 pay it on every layer while TP1 and TP2 never see it.

`dequant_mxfp8_to_bf16` is six pointwise kernels with an FP32 intermediate, so it is far off what the bytes justify -- about 97 us per layer in these traces. The `exp2_kernel_vectorized4` launch count is an unambiguous fingerprint for it: 43.4 per step at concurrency 1 and 45.9 at 32, one per layer, flat in concurrency because the work is weight-sized. Summed over the signature kernels it is 2.09 -> 4.33 ms/step, a steady 11-12% of kernel time at every concurrency measured.

Addressed by #56560, which converts once in `process_weights_after_loading` and dispatches on the weight's element size, as `EmulationMxfp8LinearKernel` already does. Reported at 4.6% / 2.3% lower median TPOT at concurrency 1 / 8 with `exp2_kernel_vectorized4` going to exactly zero, and 0.11 GiB more weight memory per rank. Its only failing check is the `pre-run-check` label gate, not a test.

### 7.2 The activation quant is a separate launch per GEMM

`_mxfp8_dot_scaled_linear` calls `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` and then the GEMM, so the pair `_kernel.kd` -> `_mxfp8_linear_kernel.kd` is the most frequent back-to-back chain in the step: 187.2 occurrences at concurrency 1 and 198.2 at 32, and adjacency is 100% -- every quant launch is immediately followed by its GEMM. The quant kernel is dispatch-floor rather than work: it moves 92 KB at M=6 (11 ns of traffic at 8 TB/s) and its marginal cost measures 4.4 us, matching the 4.15 us the trace attributes to it. AITER's `per_1x32_mx_quant_hip` measures 2.05 us against the Triton kernel's 2.04 us on the same shape, so swapping implementations is not the lever.

**The obvious fix does not work.** Folding the quant into the GEMM prologue -- recomputing the per-32 E8M0 scale in registers inside the K-loop and feeding `tl.dot_scaled` directly -- is numerically correct and **0.28-0.89x**, i.e. up to 3.5x slower. It is not the redundant work across N-tiles, which is the intuitive explanation: sweeping N from 16 to 1280 (grid_n 1 to 80) holds the ratio flat at 0.41-0.45x, so it is just as slow when the activation is quantized exactly once. The in-register quant adds 26 us on top of a 12 us GEMM to save a 4.4 us launch, against roughly 0.3 us of actual arithmetic, and a ~100-config tile sweep got no further than 0.71x. That gap is how Triton lowers the reshape-and-reduce on gfx950, not something tuning reaches. Recorded so nobody repeats it.

**The producer side works.** Asking the trace what *produces* these activations: `aiter::add_rmsnorm_quant_kernel` immediately precedes the quant 78.6 times per step at concurrency 1 and 83.1 at 32. That kernel already normalizes and quantizes, so folding the MX quant into it costs no redundant work. AITER supports this today in principle -- `rmsnorm2d_fwd_with_add_dynamicquant` routes a 1-byte E8M0 scale plus a `group_size` to the HIP `add_rmsnorm_quant`, which is exactly the format `tl.dot_scaled` consumes.

It was blocked by one arithmetic detail. The kernel picks `thread_data_size` from the hidden size and then asserts `group_size % thread_data_size == 0`; hidden 5120 lands in the `n <= 6144` band at `thread_data_size = 24`, and 32 does not divide 24, so it aborts. Confirmed across the ladder: 1024, 2048, 4096 and 6272-8192 all accept group 32, and only 5120 and 6144 -- the two `tds=24` sizes -- are rejected. This is a latent AITER bug rather than a missing feature, since the existing `per_1x32` MXFP4 test path hits it too; it survived because the test's default `-n` sweep skips that band entirely.

Fixed by [ROCm/aiter#5480](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5480), which mirrors the group-aware config selection the `n <= 8192` branch already uses into the `n <= 6144` band, reusing instantiations that branch already relies on. It is strictly additive: `group_size == 0` and multiples of 24 keep today's config. With it, hidden 5120 emits MXFP8 matching a reference MX quantizer on 99.7% of block scales, within one E4M3 ULP dequantized, residual bit-exact, and AITER's own MXFP4 test passes at 5120 and 6144 where it previously aborted.

Worth **1.49x at M=8 rising to 1.77x at M=256** on the norm-plus-quant pair (2.2 us and 4.1 us saved per occurrence, graph-replay latency with the replay floor amortized over 64 copies per graph). At step level that is ~175 us at concurrency 1 and ~343 us at 32, so about **1% of kernel time** -- less than the quant kernel's full 4.5%/2.2% share, because the fused norm is itself ~0.9 us more expensive than the plain one and only ~80 of the ~190 quant calls have this producer. It also removes ~80 of the 2,850-3,064 launches per step.

Still open: the vLLM side needs an op returning the norm's `(fp8, E8M0 scale)` pair and a `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` entry point that accepts a pre-quantized activation instead of quantizing internally. And the remaining ~107 quant calls per step have different producers -- `elementwise_kernel_manual_unroll` (45/step) and another Triton kernel (43/step) -- each needing its own fusion.

### 7.3 The GEMM itself is already at its ceiling

Recording this so nobody re-tunes it. At decode shapes the kernel reaches 13-24% of the 8 TB/s weight-read roof, and its time is flat in N -- at M=6, K=5120 a 6.6 MB weight and a 13.1 MB weight both take 5.4 us -- so cost tracks K-loop iterations, not work. A ~100-config sweep over `BLOCK_N`, `BLOCK_K`, warps and stages found the shipped `_select_cfg` choice already optimal, best alternative 1.07x. Naive split-K is 2-8x worse: the FP32 output atomics dominate.

The alternatives, graph-replay microbenchmarked at N=1280, K=5120 (us per call, quant included where applicable):

| M (capture size) | Triton MXFP8 | BF16 hipBLASLt | AITER block-128 FP8 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | 7.7 | 6.7 | 17.2 |
| 128 | 13.7 | **10.1** | 15.8 |
| 256 | 19.0 | **12.7** | 15.9 |

So BF16 wins 1.2-1.5x at the capture sizes DSpark reaches at concurrency 16 and 32 and is a wash at 1, at the cost of doubling these weights. AITER's block-128 CK GEMM is flat in M and loses at every decode size, which also means requantizing the checkpoint to block-128 to reach the `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle` path in `_bpre_attn_gemm` would not help decode. Two routes are simply closed on gfx950: AITER's native `gemm_a8w8_mxfp8` / `gemm_a8w4_mxfp8` are gfx1250 asm and hard-fail, and `torch._scaled_mm` rejects the MX scaling config on torch `2.12.0+git6bbd260`.

MI355X x8 (gfx950, 256 CU, 288 GiB), ROCm 7.x, vLLM `0.28.1rc1.dev398+g79a7108d9`, torch `2.12.0+git6bbd260`, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (40 layers, hidden 5120, 384 routed experts / 6 per token, MXFP4 MoE + MXFP8 dense, DSpark 5-token MTP), TP4, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` cudagraph mode.

- [x] I have made sure that the title and body are clear and self-contained, and that I have searched for related issues and RFCs.

title: [Model] Fix DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash SM120/GB10 geometry mismatch for SWA …
body:
Fixes #56461.

## Summary

On SM120 and SM121 architectures (such as GB10), DeepGEMM kernels enforce a strict hardware invariant: the number of kernel states (`num_states`) must equal 64. 

For DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, this created a geometry mismatch because the SWA cache layer block size was hardcoded to 32, and the indexer backend attempted unsupported virtual block splitting between ratio-1 and ratio-2 layers. This PR aligns the block size geometry across SWA and indexer backends on SM120/SM121 to satisfy the DeepGEMM requirement without altering the behavior on older architectures.

## Hardware and Kernel Context

- DeepGEMM SM120 kernel constraint: `num_states == 64`.
- For ratio-1 layers (`tokens_per_state == 1`): requires `kernel_block_size == 64` to yield 64 states.
- For ratio-2 layers (`tokens_per_state == 2`): requires `kernel_block_size == 128` to yield 64 states (`128 // 2 == 64`).
- SWA sliding-window cache: aligned to block size 64 on SM120/121 so paged attention allocations match the indexer's kernel state geometry.

## Changes

- SWA block size resolution (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/attention.py`):
  Checks platform capability family and selects block size 64 for SM120 and SM121, falling back to 32 when the platform is unavailable or on other architectures. Uses `kv_cache_spec.get_num_kernel_states` to guard against zero compression ratios.

- Indexer backend (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`):
  Exposes `[64, 128]` on SM120/SM121 instead of forcing `[128, 64]`, allowing both ratio-1 and ratio-2 layers to take their required spec size directly without virtual block splitting. Added explicit layout guards naming packed and strided layouts.

- Backend capability declarations:
  Updated `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/sparse_mla.py` and `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py` to declare block size 64 support on SM120/SM121.

- Regression tests (`tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v41_block_size.py`):
  Added comprehensive tests covering block size selection across SM90, SM120, and SM121, verifying ratio-1, ratio-2, and common-size resolution paths.

## Validation

- ruff check: All checks passed with 0 errors.
- ruff format: Compliant with the 88-character limit across all touched files.
- pytest: Verified test suite passes cleanly.

title: [Perf][Kimi-K3] Make GEMM-AR SM margin configurable
body:
## Purpose

Kimi-K3 fused GEMM-AR can be faster in isolation but slower during TP8 + PP2 serving. Add `VLLM_KIMI_K3_GEMM_AR_SM_MARGIN` to reduce its persistent CTA budget so concurrent kernels have room to run. The default is 0; setting it to 8 on B200 caps the grid at 140 CTAs instead of 148. Existing 2-CTA cluster rounding is preserved, invalid margins are rejected before workspace allocation, and GEMM-RS is unchanged. This limits the grid; it does not reserve specific physical SMs.

Related to #55261, but independent of its Lamport backend and crossover work. Searches found no open PR providing this SM-margin control. This PR does not change the crossover or claim that PP contention is the only source of latency. The environment-variable documentation includes the new setting through its existing `envs.py` inclusion.

## Test Plan

```bash
pre-commit run --files vllm/envs.py \
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/cute_dsl/gemm_rs_ar.py \
  tests/kernels/test_kimi_k3_gemm_rs_ar.py

# Pending on the PR checkout; requires two SM100 GPUs.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_kimi_k3_gemm_rs_ar.py -v
```

The existing distributed numerical test is extended to margins 0, 7, and 8, invalid margins, alternating shapes, output lifetime, CUDA Graph replay, and unaffected RS behavior. N is increased to 1024 so the largest shape actually reaches the CTA cap.

### Deploy

Run on both nodes, setting `NODE_RANK=0` on the API node and `NODE_RANK=1` on the worker. Set `MODEL`, `DRAFT_MODEL`, and `HEAD_IP` to the local model paths and head address. Compare AR off, AR on with margin 0, and AR on with margin 8.

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=bond0 NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=bond0
export VLLM_KIMI_K3_GEMM_AR=1 VLLM_KIMI_K3_GEMM_AR_SM_MARGIN=8
export VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1
NODE_ARGS=(--host 0.0.0.0 --port 8008)
if [[ "$NODE_RANK" == 1 ]]; then NODE_ARGS=(--headless); fi

vllm serve "$MODEL" --trust-remote-code --seed 0 --served-model-name k3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --nnodes 2 \
  --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --master-addr "$HEAD_IP" --master-port 29521 \
  --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"FLASHINFER","use_prefill_query_quantization":true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 16000 --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
  --mamba-backend triton --mamba-cache-mode align --enable-prefix-caching \
  --additional-config '{"kda_decode_backend":"triton"}' \
  --speculative-config "{\"method\":\"dspark\",\"model\":\"$DRAFT_MODEL\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":8,\"enable_adaptive_verification\":false,\"rejection_sample_method\":\"synthetic\",\"synthetic_acceptance_length\":4}" \
  "${NODE_ARGS[@]}"
```

### Benchmark

Warm up with 96 requests and 128 output tokens, then run the following twice. Reset the prefix cache before each run. Loading and warmup are excluded from the reported throughput.

```bash
curl --fail -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8008/reset_prefix_cache
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8008 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions --model k3 --tokenizer "$MODEL" --trust-remote-code \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --random-prefix-len 0 --num-prompts 960 \
  --max-concurrency 96 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 42 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,95,99 \
  --save-result
```

## Test Result

Two nodes, 8 × B200 each; TP8, PP2, DCP1; full Kimi-K3 with DSpark 8, synthetic acceptance length 4, snapshot state recovery. Each row summarizes two 960-request runs at concurrency 96 with fixed 8192-token input and 1024-token output. Every request succeeded and produced the requested token count. These are controlled performance measurements, not a quality or real-acceptance evaluation.

| Configuration | Output tokens/s, run 1 / run 2 | Mean output tokens/s | vs. AR off | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| AR off | 2266.8 / 2282.5 | 2274.7 | baseline | 6573.2 | 35.00 |
| AR on, margin 0 | 1776.1 / 1783.6 | 1779.8 | -21.8% | 9339.5 | 44.04 |
| AR on, margin 8 | 2320.3 / 2337.5 | 2328.9 | +2.4% | 6488.4 | 34.11 |

Margin 8 recovers the large regression versus margin 0 (+30.8%), but the incremental gain over disabling fusion is only +2.4%. The two AR-on configurations had identical KV cache capacity; AR off had about 0.32% more. A later two-run AR-off recheck measured 2268.6 / 2283.6 output tokens/s (mean 2276.1, +0.06% versus the initial baseline), supporting the stability of this small gain.

Isolated BF16 GEMM-AR sweeps on both nodes covered M=128 through 16000, K=1536/4224, N=7168, margins 0/8, with numerical checks against GEMM + all-reduce. Most shapes changed little; the large dense shape (M=16000, K=4224) regressed by about 4–5% with margin 8. This is why the setting remains opt-in rather than selecting a hardware-wide default.

Provenance: serving measurements used source `30aa0ade39ab6625674865f578fae19a49cf3e43`, Torch 2.13.0+cu130 and FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, with an experimental wrapper applying the same CTA cap. The underlying GEMM-RS/AR file matches this PR's base. All arms shared a DSpark draft-loader configuration fix and an isolated current-source grouped-FP8-cache operator to bridge the older image's native ABI. Measured startup used fastsafetensors for the main model and auto for the draft; the reproduction command above uses the default loader, which changes startup rather than the timed inference path. Focused GPU checks loaded this PR's exact kernel and environment-variable implementation into the established runtime on all 16 GPUs. The PR test's numerical, output-lifetime and CUDA Graph checks passed for RS and AR at margins 0/7/8; invalid margins -1/147/148 were rejected. These checks reused the test function bodies directly; the full pytest command on the complete PR checkout remains pending.

A controlled TP8+PP2 overlap probe delayed one PP sender by 5 ms. At M=16000, K=1536, N=7168, the original kernel at margin 0 increased from 585.8 us without PP traffic to 4712.1 us with the delayed PP operation; margin 8 measured 585.8 us in both cases (50-sample median of maximum TP-rank CUDA-event latency). This supports a concurrent-resource contention explanation, without identifying the exact limiting per-SM resource.

Local pre-commit checks passed, including Ruff, spelling, mypy, and repository checks. AI assistance was used for implementation, analysis, and test execution. Human review is pending; no human-run validation is claimed.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Keep inline system messages in place for encoder-based tokenizers (Anthropic API)
body:
## Purpose

Fix prefix caching for Anthropic Messages API clients that send `role: system` messages inside
`messages` (Claude Code appends `<total_tokens>N tokens left</total_tokens>` after every tool
result) when the model uses an encoder-based tokenizer with no jinja chat template
(`--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4`, `deepseek_v41`).

`_detect_merge_inline_system()` returns `True` whenever `chat_template` is falsy, so every inline
system message is merged into the leading system block. Each turn then changes the prompt right
after the system+tools region and the whole conversation is re-prefilled on every call.
Observed with Claude Code against DeepSeek-V4-Flash: `cache_read_input_tokens` pinned at
8192/12288 for 101 calls while the context grew to 84K tokens (4.97M prompt tokens sent, 4.30M
re-prefilled, 0.52M actually changed).

Fixes #<issue>.

## Changes

- `TokenizerLike.supports_inline_system_messages` (default `False`): the tokenizer's encoder
  renders `role: system` at any position and still emits the generation prompt after a trailing one.
- DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 wrappers set it to `True` (their `encode_messages` already appends the
  assistant header after a mid-conversation or trailing system message).
- `AnthropicServingMessages._detect_merge_inline_system(chat_template, tokenizer)`: with no
  template, merge unless the tokenizer explicitly declares support. Jinja-template detection is
  unchanged. Every other tokenizer keeps today's behavior.

## Test plan

- `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py::TestDetectMergeInlineSystem`:
  4 new cases (no flag → merge, flag → no merge, non-bool truthy attribute → merge, DeepSeek V4
  wrapper declares support). File passes (66 tests).
- pre-commit clean (ruff, mypy, typos, SPDX).
- Live: Claude Code 2.1.268 → vLLM `/v1/messages` → DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP=2 on 2x DGX Spark.
  `cache_read_input_tokens` per consecutive tool turn: stock 15104/15104/15104/15104, patched
  15104/15360/15616/15872; each request is an exact token-level extension of the previous one and
  every prompt still ends with `<|Assistant|><think>` (verified by rendering captured requests).

Note: an older vLLM build (0.25.2.dev, July) lacks the encoder change that appends the assistant
header after a trailing system message; on that build a downstream workaround also emits inline
system text as a user message. `main` already has the encoder change, so this PR only touches the
adapter/tokenizer contract.

title: [Bug][ROCm]: Intermittent worker segfault in libhsa-runtime64 — ROCPROFILER_QUEUE_INTERPOSITION=0 forces an unfixed ROCr heap overflow
body:
## Summary

`docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base:426` sets `ENV ROCPROFILER_QUEUE_INTERPOSITION=0`. That
disables rocprofiler-sdk's inline dispatch tracing and forces the legacy
`hsa_amd_queue_intercept_create` path — which in ROCm 7.2.x contains an
unfixed heap overflow. The result is an intermittent host-side SIGSEGV during
engine startup on any workload with a high kernel dispatch rate.

Setting `ROCPROFILER_QUEUE_INTERPOSITION=1` on the same image removes the crash,
keeps async execution, and keeps `torch.profiler` GPU capture working.

## The ROCr bug

`intercept_queue.cpp` hardcodes the staging buffer to 256 entries while the AQL
ring holds up to `ROC_AQL_QUEUE_SIZE` (default **16384**):

```cpp
staging_buffer_.resize(256);                        // line 131
...
for (uint64_t j = 0; j < packet_count; ++j)         // line ~410, no bound check
  staging_buffer_[j] = ring[(next_packet_ + j) & mask];
```

`packet_count` is bounded only by `amd_queue_.hsa_queue.size`, so a batch of more
than 256 pending packets that wraps the ring writes 64-byte AQL packets past the
allocation — up to ~1 MB of heap corruption. The write is in bounds only if
`queue_size <= 256`, and queue size must be a power of two, so **no setting of
`ROC_AQL_QUEUE_SIZE` above 256 is safe**; AMD notes in #4066 that 256 hangs RCCL
initialisation.

Fixed upstream in **ROCm/rocm-systems#4066** (merged to `develop` 2026-03-17,
one line). Not present in the 7.2 release branch, and **not in either ROCr commit
vLLM pins**:

| ref | `staging_buffer_.resize(...)` |
|---|---|
| `mawong-amd@b539bf7` (in the image we ran) | `256` — buggy |
| `mawong-amd@c7e40e16` (current `main` pin) | `256` — buggy |
| `rocm-7.2.1` … **`rocm-7.2.4`** | `256` — buggy |
| `therock-7.13`, `7.14`, `10.0`, `develop` | `hsa_queue.size` — fixed |

ROCm 7.2.4's release notes list no ROCR-Runtime changes, and
`release/rocm-rel-7.2` has no cherry-pick, so waiting for a 7.2.x patch will not help.

## Why the env var matters

`InterceptQueue` is constructed at exactly one site, `hsa_amd_queue_intercept_create`
("For use by tools only"). rocprofiler-sdk chooses between that and an inline
path; 1.3.2 has the inline implementation. With `ROCPROFILER_QUEUE_INTERPOSITION=0`
the legacy interception is used, so the buggy code runs **even when no profiler is
attached** — kineto registers tracing contexts at process init, and the decision is
made once at startup.

## Measurements (4x MI355X / gfx950, TP4, ROCm 7.2.3, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash)

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-2a02f6efe319c885e3ccbcecde402e0028f9ec1e`.
Trigger: one extra Triton kernel in the sparse-prefill path. Baseline ~50% of
startups segfault.

| setting | startup | profiler | throughput |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ROCPROFILER_QUEUE_INTERPOSITION=0` (current default) | **~50% segfault** | works | intact |
| **`ROCPROFILER_QUEUE_INTERPOSITION=1`** | **3/3 clean** | **works** (start in 0s, 5 traces, 38k launches) | intact |
| `HSA_TOOLS_DISABLE_REGISTER=1` | 4/4 clean | **silently produces 0 GPU events** | intact |
| `AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3` | clean | works | **serialised** |

Backtrace, caught with `rocgdb` by breaking on `raise` (tvm_ffi's SIGSEGV handler
re-raises with `SIG_DFL`, so frames below the trampoline are the real fault):

```
#0  raise()
#1  libtvm_ffi.so                <- handler, re-raising
#2  <signal handler called>
#3  libhsa-runtime64.so.1        <- fault
#4  libhsa-runtime64.so.1
#5  libc start_thread
#6  libc clone
```

All 4 workers faulted inside `libhsa-runtime64` / `libamdhip64`, on runtime-owned
threads. It is a host-side SIGSEGV, not a GPU memory fault (those report
`Memory access fault by GPU node-N` and die on SIGABRT).

## Why `=0` was set, and why it may no longer be needed

#55099 set it to avoid the profiler hang in #54087 / #54171: "*While most of them
were resolved by said PR, a few remain in some profiling workloads.*"

The hang needed ROCm/rocm-systems#7796, #7924 and #8093 (via #8212). This image
carries all of them (`ROCPROFILER_SDK_COMMIT: 2b22ab01…` plus the two patched in at
`Dockerfile.rocm_base:398-405`). With `=1` on this image we could not reproduce the
hang: `/start_profile` returned in 0s, `/stop_profile` in 7s, 5 traces written,
zero `Async signal handler still waiting` markers.

So the guard now costs more than it saves: it trades an intermittent profiler hang
(fixed in this build) for a heap corruption that is **not** fixed and will not be
on 7.2.x.

## Suggested fix

Set `ROCPROFILER_QUEUE_INTERPOSITION=1` in `Dockerfile.rocm_base` for builds that
include the interposition fixes, since the Dockerfile knows its own patch level.
Optionally also bump `ROCM_RUNTIME_COMMIT` past #4066 (and #7874, a second
out-of-bounds in `InterceptQueue::Submit()`, also absent from 7.2.x).

## What we cannot verify

#55099 kept `=0` because "a few [hangs] remain in some profiling workloads". **We do
not know which workloads those are.** We tested one — DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with a
`/start_profile` capture — and could not reproduce a hang on this image. If the
residual cases are also covered by the fixes now in the image, `=1` strictly
dominates `=0`: it avoids a heap corruption that will not be fixed on 7.2.x, at no
cost to profiling or throughput. That call needs someone who knows the remaining
hang cases; this report is meant to supply the missing half of the tradeoff.

Other caveats:

- Counter and PC-sampling contexts still fall back to the legacy path, so
  `rocprofv3` counter runs would continue to hit the ROCr bug regardless.
- 3/3 clean startups against a ~50% baseline is ~12% by chance, not conclusive on
  its own; the source-level confirmation and the mechanism are the stronger evidence.

---

title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Zero mamba state blocks on (re)allocation to stop stale-state poisoning on hybrid models
body:
# [Bugfix] Zero mamba state blocks on (re)allocation to stop stale-state poisoning on hybrid models

**Status: draft pending CI + unit tests. Validated in production on an 8×B300 node serving `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (hybrid MLA + KDA/mamba, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, prefix caching, dspark spec-decode).**

## Problem

Mamba/KDA state blocks are handed out by `BlockPool.get_new_blocks` **without zeroing**, and the attention-only zeroing queue never covers them:

- `KVCacheConfig.needs_kv_cache_zeroing` is set to `True` for mamba models (`kv_cache_interface.py`, "Required for Mamba layers, whose state is read before it is fully written (#35219)"),
- but `SingleTypeKVCacheManager.__init__` only sets `_record_new_block_ids` for `AttentionSpec` (`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`), so mamba block IDs are never recorded for the zeroing queue,
- and `KVBlockZeroer` (`vllm/v1/worker/utils.py`) skips non-`AttentionSpec` layers and non-`Tensor` `kv_cache` values — KDA layers bind a **tuple** of state tensors (`conv_state, recurrent_state, *recoverssm_records = self.kv_cache`, `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/kda.py`), so both guards exclude them.

Any read of a mamba state slot that was not written by the current tenant therefore inherits **arbitrary bytes from a previous tenant**. We observed this in production as cross-request poisoning: after an aborted prefill, a retry resumed from a state block previously freed mid-write and emitted unbounded multilingual garbage until engine restart.

## Fix

1. `_record_new_block_ids`: record allocations for `MambaSpec` managers (in addition to attention).
2. `MambaManager.allocate_new_blocks` (align cache mode): record the IDs returned by its direct `block_pool.get_new_blocks()` call, which bypasses the base-class recording path.
3. `KVBlockZeroer.__init__`: accept `MambaSpec` groups and unpack tuple/list `kv_cache` bindings, emitting one segment per state tensor. The existing per-block segment math applies unchanged (state tensors are `[num_blocks, ...]` block-strided carves of the shared page).

Per-step ordering is already `zero → block copies → forward`, so a slot read before its legitimate write returns zeros (i.e. a *fresh* recurrent state) instead of a previous tenant's bytes — degrading quality gracefully instead of corrupting the session.

## Cost

~0.6–1.0 MiB zeroed per mamba state block per layer group (K3: 69 KDA layers / 14 groups ⇒ a few MiB per block ID in practice), only at allocation time; mamba blocks are allocated at prefill-chunk boundaries. Measured overhead in production: none observable (throughput and TTFT unchanged within noise).

## Validation

- Reproducer (`storm4.py`, attached below): N workers sharing a 40k-token prefix; each cycle aborts mid-prefill (~1.2 s in) and immediately retries. Unpatched nightly: 1–2 in 36 retries poisoned with garbage (verified by full-text inspection). Patched: 0/72.
- `idlegap.py`: cache-hit-after-idle regression test, passes.
- `verify.py` functional suite (text/reasoning/vision/prefix-cache) passes; `stress_multiturn.py` (3×6-round growing sessions) passes; throughput unchanged (243–246 tok/s single-conn decode).

## Related

- #51039 (KDA one-token misclassification — different path, separate PR #51483)
- #53912, #43650, #48375 — surrounding hybrid/mamba prefix-cache issues

*AI-assisted (Claude Code / Kimi Code agent) root-cause and patch authoring, with human operator running all production experiments.*

(POC repro script and full production logs available; happy to attach.)
