title: [RFC][KV Offload]: Align sliding-window restore coverage with MTP-retained history
body:
### Motivation

Native KV offload can report a sliding-window prefix hit and then try to load an older chunk that was never included in that hit. I reproduced both `Chunk ... not found in cache` and `Chunk ... is not ready for reading` through the real Python offload scheduler, CPU manager, and GPU block allocator classes, without concurrent eviction or any GPU kernel execution.

The trigger is `SlidingWindowSpec.extra_retained_tokens > 0`. `get_kv_cache_configs()` sets this to `num_speculative_tokens - 1` for multi-module MTP. That field extends the history retained by the block manager, but offload lookup and the producer's reachable-store mask still use the attention window without that extension.

This RFC asks whether the offload contract should cover the entire retained interval. My proposed first fix is to make lookup and store coverage match the existing allocation contract. The alternative—allocating only the attention-required interval on an external hit—needs a separate proof that later MTP replay and caching cannot read or publish the omitted history.

Source inspected and exercised: upstream main at [`fa1b3b1922ccb2d7a597925765c4bec7f358d748`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/fa1b3b1922ccb2d7a597925765c4bec7f358d748).

### Reproduced failure

A small hybrid layout is sufficient:

- Full-attention group: 64 tokens per block.
- Sliding-window group: 16 tokens per block, attention window 32, extra retained history 3.
- One block per offload chunk, 16 tokens per hash, 65-token prompt, zero local cache hits.
- CPU cache contains the full-attention prefix and SWA chunks 2 and 3. SWA chunk 1 is independently missing, pending, or ready.

At the 64-token hit boundary, attention needs history starting at token `64 - 32 + 1 = 33`, within SWA chunk 2. The actual allocator retains history starting at `64 - 32 + 1 - 3 = 30`, within chunk 1.

| Extra history | Chunk 1 | Reported hit | Allocated SWA offsets | Load result |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| 0 | missing / pending / ready | 64 | 2, 3 | succeeds |
| 3 | missing | 64 | 1, 2, 3 | `not found in cache` assertion |
| 3 | pending | 64 | 1, 2, 3 | `not ready for reading` assertion |
| 3 | ready | 64 | 1, 2, 3 | succeeds |

The missing chunk does not require an eviction race. For this hybrid layout, the real `_reachable_store_block_mask()` returns `[False, False, True, True]` at the 64-token boundary even with extra history enabled: the producer's filter itself omits chunk 1.

This is a bookkeeping reproduction, not a full model-serving reproduction. The prompt hashes and config objects are synthetic; `OffloadingConnectorScheduler`, `CPUOffloadingManager`, `BlockPool`, `FullAttentionManager`, and `SlidingWindowManager` are the actual implementations. No scheduler or allocator function is mocked. The target SWA descriptor is populated directly to isolate the retention contract; the probe does not instantiate an MTP drafter.

### Code path

1. [`get_kv_cache_configs()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa1b3b1922ccb2d7a597925765c4bec7f358d748/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py) tags sliding-window specs for multi-module MTP.
2. [`SlidingWindowManager.get_num_skipped_tokens()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa1b3b1922ccb2d7a597925765c4bec7f358d748/vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py) subtracts `extra_retained_tokens`. Initial local-block adoption pads fewer null slots; external allocation therefore allocates the older retained block too.
3. [`get_sliding_window_size_in_chunks()` / `load_window_size_in_chunks()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa1b3b1922ccb2d7a597925765c4bec7f358d748/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py) omit that extension. Lookup reports 64 matched tokens without checking chunk 1.
4. `update_state_after_alloc()` starts from the first fresh non-null block, including chunk 1. [`CPUOffloadingManager.prepare_load()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa1b3b1922ccb2d7a597925765c4bec7f358d748/vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/manager.py) then correctly rejects the unavailable chunk.
5. `SlidingWindowManager.reachable_block_mask()`, used by offload store filtering, also derives coverage from `sliding_window` alone.

### Proposed change

Keep the current allocator and MTP retention semantics. Make native offload coverage include every chunk that those semantics cause an external restore to read:

1. Derive offload lookup coverage from the retained interval, including partial-chunk alignment. Apply the same interval to the in-flight-load conflict check and relevant recency touches.
2. Extend the producer's offload store mask to supply that interval. Changing the lookup window alone would turn affected restores into misses because the producer can still omit the required chunk.
3. Keep the current outcomes: a missing required chunk shortens/rejects the hit; a pending required chunk defers lookup; a complete hit can be allocated and loaded. Preserve the existing `prepare_load` assertions.
4. Keep the actual model attention window, wire format, cache keys, and transfer ownership unchanged. No new user option is needed for an internal correctness contract.

The invariant is: **every chunk consumed by an admitted restore must be covered by the confirmed lookup, and every required chunk must be reachable through the corresponding producer store policy.**

A diagnostic baseline expands only the offload coverage descriptor from window 32 to 35 while preserving the real allocator's original `window=32, extra=3` spec. With this expansion, the mask becomes `[False, True, True, True]`; a missing chunk produces zero hits, a pending chunk defers, and a ready chunk restores 64 tokens successfully. All six `extra=0` controls are unchanged across the two modes. The script below checks all 12 combinations.

This descriptor substitution is an experiment, not the proposed production implementation. Production code should express offload coverage explicitly rather than changing a model's attention window. Wider coverage also has a cost: this example stores/loads three SWA chunks instead of two. It needs measurement, not an assumption that extra history is free.

### Validation before a PR

- Protect the confirmed missing/pending/ready behavior and zero-extra controls in the existing offload scheduler suite.
- Exercise a producer-to-consumer replay using actual store selection, CPU completion, lookup, and allocation; check that demanded keys were offered for storage.
- Cover chunk factors greater than one, unaligned hybrid hit boundaries, EAGLE tail handling, and in-flight loads with the same coverage invariant.
- Validate real multi-module MTP outputs and acceptance, plus cache bytes/hit rate and end-to-end latency on a prefix-reusing workload. These model/performance results have not been run and are not claimed here.

### Related work and duplicate check

Searched open PRs and issues for `extra_retained_tokens`, offload + retained history, multi-module + offload, and offload window/load coverage on 2026-09-13.

- #55818 addresses sliding-window allocation scaling and preserves extra retention; it does not align offload lookup/store coverage.
- #52287 addresses store windows moved by EAGLE's volatile-tail pop. This reproduction has no EAGLE pop.
- #56486 addresses a pending flag left behind by an invalid suffix. This reproduction has a complete reported hit and a later load failure.
- #54914 reports a similar load assertion under DSpark. I have not reproduced that deployment or established this mechanism as its cause; this RFC does not claim to resolve it.

### Feedback period

One week. The main decision is whether native offload should restore the entire retained interval, as proposed here, or whether initial external-hit allocation should distinguish retention-only history from the history required to resume. The latter must also preserve MTP replay and cache-publication correctness.

### Reproducer and environment

The 12-case diagnostic was executed with Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, the pinned Python source above, and existing precompiled extensions in WSL Ubuntu 24.04. No GPU kernels or model inference were executed. This is not validation on the repository's current PyTorch 2.13 dependency matrix.

Save the following as `retained_window_probe.py` in an installed checkout and run `.venv/bin/python retained_window_probe.py`. It writes a JSON result beside the script and checks the expected outcomes, including the two assertions in the unmodified path.

<details>
<summary>Executable 12-case diagnostic</summary>

```python
"""Exercise real offload lookup/allocation with MTP's retained SWA history."""

import json
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

import torch

from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.offloading.scheduler import (
    OffloadingConnectorScheduler,
)
from vllm.v1.core.block_pool import BlockPool
from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_manager import KVCacheBlocks
from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import BlockHash
from vllm.v1.core.single_type_kv_cache_manager import (
    FullAttentionManager,
    SlidingWindowManager,
)
from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (
    FullAttentionSpec,
    KVCacheConfig,
    KVCacheGroupSpec,
    SlidingWindowSpec,
)
from vllm.v1.kv_offload.base import OffloadingKVEventsConfig
from vllm.v1.kv_offload.cpu.manager import CPUOffloadingManager


def probe(extra: int, older_state: str, expanded_coverage: bool = False):
    kv_spec = SlidingWindowSpec(
        block_size=16,
        num_kv_heads=1,
        head_size=1,
        dtype=torch.float32,
        sliding_window=32,
        extra_retained_tokens=extra,
    )
    full_spec = FullAttentionSpec(
        block_size=64,
        num_kv_heads=1,
        head_size=1,
        dtype=torch.float32,
    )
    groups = [KVCacheGroupSpec(["full"], full_spec), KVCacheGroupSpec(["swa"], kv_spec)]
    manager = CPUOffloadingManager(num_chunks=8)
    spec = SimpleNamespace(
        config=SimpleNamespace(
            groups=tuple(
                SimpleNamespace(group_id=i, tokens_per_block=g.kv_cache_spec.block_size)
                for i, g in enumerate(groups)
            )
        ),
        tokens_per_block=(64, 16),
        tokens_per_hash=16,
        blocks_per_chunk=1,
        offload_prompt_only=True,
        kv_events_config=OffloadingKVEventsConfig(
            enable_kv_cache_events=False, self_describing_kv_events=False
        ),
        get_manager=lambda: manager,
    )
    config = SimpleNamespace(
        speculative_config=None,
        cache_config=SimpleNamespace(
            enable_prefix_caching=True, prefix_cache_retention_interval=None
        ),
        parallel_config=SimpleNamespace(world_size=1, decode_context_parallel_size=1),
    )
    sched = OffloadingConnectorScheduler(
        spec,
        config,
        KVCacheConfig(num_blocks=32, kv_cache_tensors=[], kv_cache_groups=groups),
    )
    if expanded_coverage:
        # Diagnostic only: expand the offload coverage descriptor, preserving the
        # real GPU allocator's spec. This is not a production model patch.
        coverage_spec = replace(
            kv_spec, sliding_window=32 + extra, extra_retained_tokens=0
        )
        group = sched.config.kv_group_configs[1]._replace(
            sliding_window_size_in_chunks=(32 + extra + 15) // 16,
            kv_cache_spec=coverage_spec,
        )
        sched.config = sched.config._replace(
            kv_group_configs=(sched.config.kv_group_configs[0], group)
        )
    req = MagicMock()
    req.request_id = "replay"
    req.kv_transfer_params = None
    req.num_tokens = req.num_prompt_tokens = 65
    req.block_hashes = [BlockHash(f"block{i}".encode()) for i in range(4)]
    req.skip_reading_prefix_cache = False
    sched.on_new_request(req)
    state = sched._req_status[req.request_id]
    state.update_offload_keys()
    full_keys, keys = (g.offload_keys for g in state.group_states)
    ready = full_keys[:1] + keys[1 if older_state == "ready" else 2 :]
    store = manager.prepare_store(ready, state.req_context)
    assert store is not None
    manager.complete_store(store.keys_to_store, state.req_context)
    if older_state == "pending":
        assert manager.prepare_store([keys[1]], state.req_context) is not None
    external, async_load = sched.get_num_new_matched_tokens(req, 0)
    pool = BlockPool(32, enable_caching=True, hash_block_size=16)
    managers = [
        cls(
            kv_cache_spec=g.kv_cache_spec,
            block_pool=pool,
            enable_caching=True,
            kv_cache_group_id=i,
            scheduler_block_size=64,
        )
        for i, (cls, g) in enumerate(
            zip((FullAttentionManager, SlidingWindowManager), groups)
        )
    ]
    store_mask = sched._reachable_store_block_mask(
        sched.config.kv_group_configs[1], 0, 4, 4, ()
    )
    record = dict(
        extra_retained_tokens=extra,
        older_state=older_state,
        expanded_coverage=expanded_coverage,
        hit_tokens=external,
        async_load=async_load,
        swa_store_mask=store_mask,
    )
    if external:
        for m in managers:
            m.add_local_computed_blocks(req.request_id, [], 0, external)
        for m in managers:
            m.allocate_external_computed_blocks(req.request_id, 0, external)
        blocks = managers[1].req_to_blocks[req.request_id]
        record["allocated_offsets"] = [i for i, b in enumerate(blocks) if not b.is_null]
        try:
            sched.update_state_after_alloc(
                req,
                KVCacheBlocks(tuple(m.req_to_blocks[req.request_id] for m in managers)),
                external,
            )
        except AssertionError as exc:
            record["error"] = str(exc)
        else:
            record["load_jobs"] = len(sched._jobs)
            for job in sched._jobs.values():
                manager.complete_load(job.keys, state.req_context)
    return record


if __name__ == "__main__":
    records = [
        probe(extra, older, expand)
        for expand in (False, True)
        for extra in (0, 3)
        for older in ("missing", "pending", "ready")
    ]
    for r in records:
        if r["extra_retained_tokens"] == 0 or r["older_state"] == "ready":
            assert r["hit_tokens"] == 64 and r["load_jobs"] == 1, r
        elif r["expanded_coverage"]:
            assert r["hit_tokens"] == (0 if r["older_state"] == "missing" else None), r
            assert "error" not in r, r
        else:
            assert r["hit_tokens"] == 64 and "error" in r, r
    output = json.dumps(records, indent=2)
    Path(__file__).with_suffix(".json").write_text(output + "\n")
    print(output)
    print("All 12 diagnostic cases matched their expected outcomes.")
```

</details>

### AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with issue/PR searches, source inspection, the reproducer, execution, and this RFC. This is a design discussion with a verified bookkeeping failure, not a reviewed production patch or a claim of completed model validation.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash cannot start on SM120 — sm_120 missing from kernel-block-size branches, and prefill SWA width ignores --language-model-only
body:
### Your current environment

- **GPU**: 4× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (compute capability **12.0**, sm_120), 96 GB each, no NVLink
- **Image**: `vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv41-flash-0909` (`sha256:00d577a6a63281e15336029d5bcee4e9a2cf182214a4f20ba6111b1c8e79893d`)
- **vLLM**: `0.1.dev20904+g179dd0fa9` · **flashinfer-python**: `0.6.18` · **torch**: `2.13.0+cu130`
- **Model**: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, TP4, `--language-model-only`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`
- Also reproduced on `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (`0.29.1rc1.dev9+g2671fedfc`) — identical behaviour.

The recipe lists `h200 / gb200 / gb300 / mi350x` as verified, so sm_120 is understood to be
unsupported. This report is about *why*, since two of the three causes look like plain bugs
rather than missing kernels, and one of them is not sm_120-specific.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash cannot start on sm_120. There are three distinct causes; the first two
look like straightforward fixes, the third is a FlashInfer kernel-coverage gap that currently
makes the configuration unsatisfiable.

---

#### 1. Prefill SWA index width ignores `--language-model-only`

`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_swa.py` (~L449):

```python
self.max_image_tokens = (
    getattr(hf_config, "vision_max_n_token", 0)
    if getattr(hf_config, "vision_n_layers", 0) > 0
    else 0
)
self.prefill_index_width = self.window_size + self.max_image_tokens
```

The test asks whether the **model** is vision-capable, not whether **this deployment** enabled
images. With `--language-model-only`, vLLM logs

```
Disabled mm_prefix attention mode because multimodal inputs are configuration-disabled.
```

and `DeepseekV4Attention.max_image_tokens` correctly resolves to `0`, but this builder keeps
`1024`. The two then disagree: the attention module believes index rows are 128 wide while the
builder allocates `128 + 1024 = 1152`.

On sm_100 this is only wasted columns. On sm_120 it is fatal — `_DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH`
enumerates `top_k ∈ {128, 192, 256, 512, 1024}`:

```
ValueError: SM120 sparse-MLA has no decode kernel for this shape:
  num_tokens=2, num_heads=16, topk=1152, d_qk=512, page_block_size=32, model_type=1
```

Keying off `ModelConfig._supports_multimodal_for_mm_prefix()` (the same signal that emits the
log line above) fixes it and takes `topk` to 128.

---

#### 2. sm_120 missing from the kernel-block-size capability branches

Three sites select the kernel block size, and all treat sm_120 as sm_100:

| file | line | current |
|---|---|---|
| `vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/sparse_mla.py` | 90 | `[64 if is_device_capability_family(90) else 128]` |
| `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py` | 263 | `[64 if is_device_capability_family(90) else 128]` |
| `vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py` | 113 | `return [128]` |

But FlashInfer's sm_120 kernel is compiled for **64**
(`flashinfer/mla/_sparse_mla_sm120.py`: `_DECODE_DSV4_PAGE_BLOCK_SIZE = 64`), and DeepGEMM's
paged MQA logits accepts `num_states = kernel_block_size // tokens_per_state` only in
`{32, 64}` (`deepgemm/csrc/apis/attention.hpp:262`).

V4.1 has both ratio-1 and ratio-2 indexer layers, so claiming 128 leaves **no** working
setting:

- default → ratio-1 layers give `128 // 1 = 128` → `RuntimeError: Assertion error ... block_kv == 32 or block_kv == 64`
- `--block-size 64` → `ValueError: No common block size for 64.` (`64 % 128 != 0`), *because these backends claim 128*

Adding `is_device_capability_family(120)` to the 64 branch in all three resolves both
(`64 // 1 = 64`, `64 // 2 = 32`). `DeepseekV4Attention` also hardcodes `block_size=32` for the
SWA cache (`models/deepseek_v4_1/attention.py` ~L456), which needs to be 64 on sm_120 for the
same reason.

---

#### 3. Terminal blocker: no DSV4 prefill template for `extra_page_block_size == 32`

With 1 and 2 fixed, startup reaches:

```
Unsupported sparse-MLA prefill configuration: model=DSV4 num_heads=16 topk=128
  page_block_size=64 topk_extra=512 extra_page_block_size=32
```

`flashinfer/data/csrc/sparse_mla_sm120_prefill.cu` compiles DSV4 dual-cache prefill for
`extra_page_block_size` **64 or 2 only**:

```c
if (topk != 128) return false;
if (extra_page_block_size == 64)      DISPATCH_BY_NH_PBSX(64);
else if (extra_page_block_size == 2)  DISPATCH_BY_NH_PBSX(2);
return false;
```

`extra_page_block_size == cache_block_size // compress_ratio`, and V4.1 mixes ratio-1 and
ratio-2 layers, so the two constraints are mutually exclusive:

| cache block | indexer ratio-1 | indexer ratio-2 | extra page (ratio-2) | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **64** | 64 ✅ | 32 ✅ | **32 ❌** | no compiled prefill template |
| **128** | **128 ❌** | 64 ✅ | 64 ✅ | DeepGEMM `block_kv` assert |

Both ends were reached empirically. No global block size satisfies both, so on sm_120 this
needs either a FlashInfer build carrying `extra_page_block_size == 32` DSV4 prefill templates,
or vLLM routing V4.1's ratio-2 layers away from the dual-cache prefill path.

### 🔧 Suggested fixes

1. `sparse_swa.py`: gate `max_image_tokens` on `_supports_multimodal_for_mm_prefix()` — this is
   worth fixing regardless of sm_120, since the width is currently wrong in any text-only
   deployment of a vision model.
2. Add `is_device_capability_family(120)` to the 64 branch in the three sites above, and make
   the SWA cache `block_size` arch-aware.
3. Track the missing FlashInfer template as an upstream dependency.

Happy to open a PR for 1 and 2 if that's useful — I have both changes running locally and they
take startup from the first error to the point where only 3 remains.

title: [Bugfix] DeepSeek V4/V4.1: honor enable_thinking over legacy thinking and treat null flags as unset
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 resolved thinking mode with `bool(thinking or enable_thinking)` and treated a present-but-null key as specified. That caused two inconsistent public-API cases:

- Canonical `enable_thinking: false` lost to legacy `thinking: true`.
- `thinking: null` or `enable_thinking: null` disabled thinking instead of acting as unspecified.

Both keys can coexist because `chat_template_kwargs` is a free-form public dictionary that accepts the canonical name and its legacy alias. A concrete conflicting request is:

```json
{"chat_template_kwargs":{"thinking":true,"enable_thinking":false}}
```

This PR applies one rule throughout both families:

1. A non-null `enable_thinking` is canonical.
2. A null `enable_thinking` falls through to legacy `thinking`.
3. Absent or all-null flags default to thinking enabled.
4. `reasoning_effort: "none"` disables thinking afterward, as before.

The normal default request path does not inject conflicting keys.

## Changes

- `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py`, `vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py`, and `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v41.py` use the same precedence and null rules.
- The V4 tokenizer/parser matrices cover conflicting and null combinations, plus a render-and-parse round trip for streaming and non-streaming disabled-thinking responses.
- The V4.1 tokenizer/parser matrices mirror those combinations.

`DeepSeekV41Parser` inherits `DeepSeekV4Parser.__init__`, so the parser fix is shared. `DeepseekV4Renderer` delegates to the registered tokenizer and has no independent flag resolution. The duplicated four-line resolution at the tokenizer and parser boundaries is intentional; mirrored tests guard against drift. Encoding, model, kernel, and runtime files are unchanged.

## Related work and duplication check

Open PR and issue searches covered `enable_thinking`, `DeepSeek thinking`, alias precedence, and the model-specific tokenizer paths.

- #53389 adds aliases to other parsers and retains OR semantics; it does not fix this conflict.
- #54198 documents DeepSeek V4 effort normalization; this preserves that mapping.
- #57882 edits the independent V4.1 tokenizer for generation-prompt and continuation behavior. It does not touch these thinking-resolution lines. The changes are independent; whichever lands second may need to rebase the small adjacent hunk.
- #43728 describes cross-component thinking-name inconsistencies; this PR fixes the concrete V4/V4.1 precedence and null cases.

## Validation

Run on top of upstream `main` at `5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c` with Python 3.12:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/parser/engine \
  tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py
# 135 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/tokenizers_ \
  tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py
# 38 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/tokenizers_ \
  tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py -k 'thinking or reasoning_effort'
# 28 passed, 24 deselected
```

`py_compile`, `git diff --check`, Ruff check, and Ruff format check pass on the changed files. A combined run of both tokenizer files produced 89 passes and one unrelated environment failure: an image-sentinel test imports optional `llguidance`, which is not installed locally. This PR does not claim that combined suite is green; upstream CI must cover it.

No model-generation evaluation was run on this rebased upstream branch. The motivating deployment exercised equivalent thinking controls, but that packaged runtime is supporting evidence rather than a substitute for this branch's tests.

## CI and review status

The PR remains draft. Upstream CI has not run on this head, and the repository-required human line-by-line review and human-run tests are not claimed. The earlier CI pre-run failure was an authorization gate for first-time contributors, not a reported code or test failure.

## AI assistance

Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, rebase, and validation. Grok 4.7 authored the V4.1 extension at its highest available CLI effort (`xhigh`; the installed CLI does not support `max`). Claude Fable 5.1 reviewed both rounds at `max`. These reviews do not replace the repository-required human review.

title: [Spec Decode] Draft within the requests' top-k / top-p support

The Gemma 4 assistant already drafts inside the target's top-20 most of the time, so the gain is within noise; the cost stays at 0.5% of ITL.
## Details Two Triton kernels compute one threshold per row on each draft step. The Gumbel kernel drops logits below it. Nothing runs on the host, so CUDA graphs keep working. Tradeoffs: - About 0.02 ms per draft step with top-k, 0.002 ms without. - Only rows with 1 ≤ top-k ≤ 1024 are masked. - 413 non-test lines, 276 in the new `draft_support.py`.
How it works 1. The model runner hands the drafter the sampler's per-request top-k / top-p once. The drafter copies the current values into its own fixed-address tensors on every step, as it does with the temperature. 2. On each draft step two Triton kernels compute one threshold per row: the maximum of each vocabulary block (at most 4096 blocks), then the k-th largest block maximum by bisection and the top-p cut above it. 3. The Gumbel sampling kernel drops logits below the threshold, for sampling and for the cached draft logits, so rejection sampling stays exact. Nothing is decided on the host, so it works inside the drafter's CUDA graphs. Rows without top-k and padding rows return at once. The threshold never drops a token of the draft's own top-k / top-p set. It is exact for vocabularies up to 4096 tokens; above that it can keep a few extra tokens. Logits at -inf (EAGLE3 heads with a reduced draft vocabulary) are skipped. DSpark samples outside `sample_draft` and applies the same threshold there. A draft watermarker gets the masked logits; the acceptance estimator gets them unmasked. The sampler's `apply_top_k_top_p_triton` is not reused. On random logits at batch 32 (248k vocabulary, RTX 4090, inside a CUDA graph) it takes 0.22 ms per call, fp32 copy included, and it would run once per draft step, three times per proposal. title: [Core] Preempt hybrid requests whose sync KV load failed
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #50388, which stopped EngineCore from crashing on a KV load failure with a hybrid KV cache by recomputing the affected request in full. For a request in the `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` state that works: its blocks are freed once the transfer finishes and it is re-admitted. For a **running** request (a synchronous load under `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`) the recompute is done in place, rewinding `num_computed_tokens` to 0 while the request keeps its blocks and stays in `running`. That is not a valid restart:

- With overlapping batches (async scheduling, pipeline parallelism) the next step was scheduled before the failure was reported, so its `allocate_slots` already ran `remove_skipped_blocks` on the loaded prefix: the sliding-window and Mamba groups now point at the shared null block for the positions they no longer needed. The recompute from 0 writes those positions' KV into the null block and the attention right after them reads it back.
- The in-flight step's output for that request was computed on the failed load, but nothing marks it stale, so it is delivered as a real token.
- Any per-request worker state derived at admission stays as it was. The DeepSeek-V4.1 SWA bounded replay in #56227 has such state (the replay boundary), which is what surfaced this.

This PR preempts such requests instead of rewinding them in place. `_preempt_request` already does everything a from-scratch restart needs: it frees the blocks, moves the request to the head of the waiting queue, reports it in `preempted_req_ids` so the worker drops its state, and with `drop_stale_output=True` drops the in-flight output. Before preempting, the request's blocks are evicted from the prefix cache; a sync load is cached at allocation, so the retry would otherwise hit the garbage. Single-group models keep the block-precise in-place rewind, and the async path is unchanged.

Retry semantics: the re-admitted request goes through normal admission, so the connector is asked for a match again (as it is today for the request-level `_handle_failed_recving` path). A connector that keeps offering a load it cannot deliver would retry each admission.

Not a duplicate: #56135, #50742, #45497, #48216 and #54733 address the crash that #50388 fixed or work out a precise per-group truncation point; #53298 keeps the in-place rewind and repairs Model Runner V2 state around it for single-group models. None of them changes how a running hybrid request is restarted after #50388.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py
```

The new `test_hybrid_sync_load_failure_preempts_request` covers a running hybrid request whose sync load fails: it is preempted with no output appended, its blocks are released and no longer cached, and the next `schedule()` re-admits it from scratch with `preempted_req_ids` set.

## Test Result

207 passed. Pre-commit (ruff, mypy) clean. Not run end to end against a KV connector that injects load failures; the unit test exercises the scheduler path only.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode][PCP] Scope CP impl checks to the target model's layers
body:
## Purpose

`check_attention_cp_compatibility()` iterates every `AttentionLayerBase` in `static_forward_context`. That context is shared with the draft model, and a DFlash/DSpark draft collapses PCP and DCP (its `ParallelConfig` is `pcp=1, dcp=1`), so its KV is never CP-sharded — yet its full-attention layers were being held to the **target's** interleave:

```
AssertionError: MTP with cp_kv_cache_interleave_size > 1 is not supported in FlashAttentionImpl.
```

Reached with DSpark7 at PCP8+DCP8+EP8 behind NIXL P/D (interleave auto-adjusted to 64), on GLM-5.3 / H200, once the draft `ParallelConfig` was made valid by #56723.

## Fix

The caller (`gpu/model_runner.py`) already passes `target_attn_layer_names`, and the PCP backend check in the same loop already scopes itself to them (`check_pcp`). The two `impl` assertions — MTP at interleave > 1, and LSE-for-DCP — did not. This scopes them the same way: layers outside the target set are skipped, exactly as they already were for the backend check. Behaviour for target layers is unchanged; `target_layer_names=None` (the `gpu_model_runner.py` caller) still checks everything.

## Relationship to other PRs

- #56723 makes the DSpark draft config valid under PCP+DCP (this assertion is the next thing that fires).
- #56722 declares the flag on `FlashMLASparseImpl` for the *target's* sparse-MLA layers, which do need it at interleave 64. This PR is about not applying that requirement to the draft's non-sharded layers.

## Test Plan

- Unit test (no GPU) exercising the function with a fake forward context containing a target layer whose impl declares the flag and a draft layer whose impl does not: passes when `target_layer_names` excludes the draft layer, and still fails when `target_layer_names=None`. Being added.
- End-to-end: DSpark7 at PCP8+DCP8+EP8 → TP8+EP8 over NIXL, gsm8k + Prometheus-counter acceptance; queued, result to be posted here.

title: [Feature][DSv4.1] Add eager MRV2 decode context parallelism
body:
## Summary

DeepSeek V4.1 currently rejects DCP for its compressed indexer and sliding-window cache layout. Add an initial MRV2 eager FlashMLA path that shards the shared main/index caches by logical record while retaining replicated sliding-window and compressor state.

```text
ASIS
TP replicas: full C1/C2 source caches + SWA/state
DCP > 1 -> unsupported cache/indexer layout
```

```text
PR
C1/C2 records -> unique DCP owner, shared across consuming layers
SWA/state    -> replicated; SWA counted once in attention
global TopK  -> owner partials -> merged heads -> sink once
```

Per-group placement has backward-compatible defaults. Compression precedes record ownership; main and index caches agree on the mapping. Candidate source 20 exchanges global block scores separately from its unmasked token TopK, and later indexers filter in global record coordinates. Attention compacts owner-local decode indices and merges unsunk output/LSE with explicit empty-partition handling before applying the sink once.

The initial scope is NVIDIA FlashMLA, MRV2 eager, DCP2/4, interleave 1, FP8 indexer caches, text-only input, no prefix caching, PCP1/PP1, no DBO or speculative decoding. Unsupported combinations fail at startup. Deployment instructions are included.

This is an explicit-communication correctness baseline; no serving-speedup or measured-capacity claim is made. It is separate from V4.0 DCP PR #44573, whose ratio-4/128 compressor does not match V4.1's ratio-1/2 shared-source topology. Refreshed V4.1 DCP searches found no equivalent open implementation. Existing peer-memory optimizations are follow-ups, not dependencies.

## Validation

- TP4 GB200, MRV2 eager, native binaries matching upstream eed1f3d and source-pinned CuTeDSL 4.7.1. Automatic cache sizing at utilization 0.55, maxbatch 8192, maxseq 4, maxlen 32768.
- Four fixed-answer stress requests pass in DCP1/2/4, including 23,023/23,024-token retrieval. Pinned five-shot 32-question GSM8K: 31/32 control, 31/32 DCP2, 32/32 DCP4; no truncations or newly incorrect answers. This is bounded no-regression evidence, not bitwise parity or an accuracy-improvement claim.
- Profiles native attention, exchange and merge scratch, mixed-layout metadata, and small-batch lazy workspaces before selecting the automatic KV budget. DCP2/4 stay 151/148 MiB below their profiled budgets on this stress workload. The unchanged upstream DCP1 path underprofiles by 448 MiB. Higher concurrency and serving performance remain unqualified.
- Post-merge attention and runner-profiling tests: 24 passed. Final focused suite: 187 passed; one existing V4 case requires gated Llama metadata (HTTP 401). The same assertions pass with an accessible OPT config fixture; both results are retained. Applicable Ruff, format, mypy and commit hooks passed.
- Earlier fixed 512 MiB-budget smoke, 23K retrieval, 32-question evaluation and kernel/placement checks are retained with their distinct runtime and workload.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py tests/model_executor/layers/test_dsv41_dcp_attention.py tests/distributed/test_dsv41_dcp_candidate_blocks.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py -k "not test_indexer_builder_deepseek_v4_compressed_slot_mapping_uses_num_states"
# From the workspace with the recorded runtime overlay and GPU lease:
vllm-dcp/.venv/bin/python artifacts/dcp/runtime_qualification.py --dcp 2 --output artifacts/dcp/runtime-471/final-dcp2-auto.json
```

AI assistance was used for implementation, testing and investigation. The submitting human confirmed review of every changed line and a relevant test rerun.

[Validation report, raw results, drivers and checksums](https://github.com/foraxe/vllm/tree/2ee0d437f3008f929a66e4d13564ddc90d158470/evidence/dsv41-dcp-eager). Feature candidate 936c40f; base eed1f3d.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Test 1280-token GLM sparse-MLA int32 slot overflow
body:
## Purpose

Keep GLM-5.3-Flash sparse-MLA prefill from overflowing signed int32 when the KV row stride is 512 and the serving page is 1280 tokens.

#53906 already promotes `slot` via `_sparse_kv_row_offset` and tests the native hybrid 640-token page (overflow at block 6554). On gfx942 we align hybrid 1152 up to `index_kpool*64=256`, so serving `block_size` is **1280**. Then:

```
INT32_MAX / (1280 * 512) = 3276.8
```

A production dump on MI325X TP4 first assigned MLA `new_block_ids` 3278–3280 on the dying chunked-prefill step (`computed=46080`, `scheduled=3840`). Without the int64 promote, `_sparse_attn_prefill_ragged_kernel` does `slot * kv_stride_n` in int32 and Memory-access-faults.

## Changes

Parametrize `test_sparse_prefill_kv_row_offset_does_not_overflow_int32` with both layouts:

- 640-token pages, first overflowing block 6554 (existing)
- 1280-token pages, first overflowing block 3277 (serving)

No kernel change. Main already has `_sparse_kv_row_offset`.

## Test

`tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_glm5next_sparse.py` (ROCm).

## Related

- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56037 (occupancy comment; do not close — mixed-length decode / equal-length short MTP still open)
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56059 is kpool tail-seed, not this path

title: [Bugfix] Make DSA prefill top-k deterministic on equal scores
body:
## Draft status — known integration issue (19 September 2026)

**Do not merge the current diff yet.** Our follow-up audit found that the helper returns absolute column indices, while the native prefill operator and its consumers expect indices relative to each row's `ks`. For a nonzero row start, that mismatch can select the wrong KV entries. The original CPU expectations also used the wrong coordinate convention.

A local correction now returns relative indices and preserves `-1` padding. A regression covering nonzero row starts fails against the published helper; the corrected local suite passes all 11 CPU tests and applicable changed-file checks. **That correction has not been pushed to this PR.** GPU/model results from our separately patched deployment do not qualify this published revision.

This PR remains draft pending the correction, appropriate integration/model validation, and the submitting human's line-by-line review and testing required by `AGENTS.md`. No human review or human-run tests are claimed. The historical validation below describes the original revision and must not be read as resolving this newly identified contract error.

---

## Purpose

The same long prompt should not change which compressed-context tokens sparse attention uses, or the generated answer, just because several indexer scores were exactly equal. Today the DeepSeek prefill path calls `ops.top_k_per_row_prefill`. On equal finite logits that kernel can emit different index sets for the same row when the row batch changes, so later attention sees a different KV subset.

This PR replaces that prefill call with a stable value-desc / index-asc selector: columns in `[ks, ke)` only, equal scores keep the smaller column index, unused slots stay `-1`.

## Changed behavior

- File: `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py` (code owner @zyongye).
- Prefill only. Decode still uses `indexer_topk.py` (`persistent_topk` / `cooperative_topk` / `top_k_per_row_decode` / …).
- No new CUDA kernel. The selector is `torch.argsort(..., descending=True, stable=True)` plus a validity mask, matching a production wrap that overwrote the CUDA result.

## Related work (not duplicates)

Checked open PRs/issues for `top_k_per_row_prefill`, `prefill topk tie`, and #53691.

- #55122 makes **`persistent_topk`** deterministic. Different registered operator; its `topk.cu` / `persistent_topk.cuh` change does not cover this prefill path.
- #55314 repairs radix threshold-bin overflow and **permits an arbitrary subset after full-key equality**, so it does not guarantee this exact-tie membership.
- #55363 changes prefill kernel thread count; correctness is still `torch.topk` set match, not index-stable ties.
- #50201 hardens NaN / under-filled output. #49897 is the SM12x NaN crash fallback.
- #53691 (closed; follow-up #54394) includes an offline harness where **injected ties** make `top_k_per_row_prefill` selection sets differ under row batching. Their live H100 sample found no boundary ties. This PR does not implement TP sharding.
- #56708 is unrelated DeepSeek-V4 `enable_thinking` precedence. Not stacked with this change.

## Validation

CPU, macOS arm64, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.0, no CUDA. Source checkout with `PYTHONPATH`, not a native vLLM GPU build (`vllm._version` warning):

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/kernels \
  tests/kernels/test_sparse_prefill_topk.py
# 10 passed in 0.75s
```

Cases: equal finite scores keep the smaller index; `[ks, ke)` clipping; empty range; k wider than the valid range; valid `-inf` vs invalid columns; two-row ties; 244 vs 640 boundary tie; 1-row vs batched-row identity under ties; 20-repeat identity; CPU inverted-bounds error.

Changed-file pre-commit (`--hook-stage manual`, three paths): ruff check/format, typos, mypy 3.10–3.13, SPDX, root lazy imports, forbidden imports, torch.cuda API, config validation, boolean-with. `compileall` and `git diff --check` passed.

**Not run on this branch:** CUDA `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py`, current-main GPU serving, or model evals. Existing kernel tests still allow set-equality under ties for the CUDA op; that op is no longer used on this DeepSeek prefill path.

Supporting deployment evidence (different tree, NVIDIA vLLM 0.27.1 overlay, wrap image `b15aa6ff`): the same selector contract was 24/24 byte-stable across 10 runs / two serving starts and 48/48 long retrieval including 120k. That is **not** a general fidelity claim and is **not** a current-main GPU result.

## Limits

- GLM kpool and ROCm aiter prefill still call `top_k_per_row_prefill`.
- `torch.argsort` over the logit row is a correctness-first replacement; this PR does not claim a prefill latency win.
- No invented GPU algorithm.

## AI assistance and review status

Grok 4.6 assisted with duplicate-work comparison against current `origin/main` (`52dd0d7562adb3c2d556ce6fe7ca7c3226e1976b`), implementation, CPU tests, and this description. title: [Perf][Distributed] Make MNNVL Lamport RS/AG message-size caps configurable
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 enables sequence parallelism when a MegaMoE backend is selected (EP, TP>1, PP1). Every decoder layer then gathers the mHC hidden states before attention and reduce-scatters the attention output through `CustomAllreduce`'s MNNVL multicast Lamport kernels; messages larger than 16 MiB (reduce-scatter) or 2-8 MiB (all-gather) fall back to the NCCL collective. At `max_num_batched_tokens 65536`, full-chunk messages are about 640 MiB (RS) / 80 MiB (AG) per layer, so most prefill SP collectives take the fallback.

On 8xB200 TP8 the existing Lamport kernels are faster than the production NCCL fallback across the whole relevant range (below), so this PR exposes both caps as `VLLM_MNNVL_REDUCE_SCATTER_MAX_SIZE_BYTES_MB` and `VLLM_MNNVL_ALL_GATHER_MAX_SIZE_BYTES_MB`. Defaults are preserved; raising a cap only grows the multi-stage symmetric staging buffer (6x the cap, plus AG x world_size). Recommended recipe for this deployment: RS=96, AG=40 MiB (staging 96 MiB -> 1.88 GiB per rank). Giant-chunk RS (>320 MiB) is intentionally left to NCCL: the kernel advantage there is <= 2% end-to-end unmeasurable, and a 640 MiB cap would cost a 4 GiB stage per rank.

Why this is not duplicating existing work: #55072 adds a *new* low-SM multimem reduce-scatter backend with a dispatcher policy for the <=16/64 MiB bands; this PR does not introduce any new kernel or backend policy, it only sizes the existing Lamport path (the two are complementary and can be recombined later). #49194 changes NCCL symmetric-memory RS staging, not the custom Lamport path. No other open PR makes these caps configurable.

## Test Plan

Deployment (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 8xB200, TP8/EP, FlashInfer sparse MLA, FP8 KV, SP via MegaMoE backend):

```bash
vllm serve /gpfs/mszn/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code --served-model-name dsv4 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp --enable-expert-parallel \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 65536 \
  --max-num-seqs 96 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune
# PR arm adds: VLLM_MNNVL_REDUCE_SCATTER_MAX_SIZE_BYTES_MB=96 VLLM_MNNVL_ALL_GATHER_MAX_SIZE_BYTES_MB=40
```

Benchmarks on the same server/session, seed 42, `--ignore-eos`:

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --endpoint /v1/completions --model dsv4 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --random-prefix-len 0 --num-prompts 100 \
  --max-concurrency 16 --request-rate inf
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --endpoint /v1/completions --model dsv4 \
  --dataset-name prefix_repetition --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 32768 \
  --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 2048 --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 96 \
  --prefix-repetition-output-len 1024 --num-prompts 960 --max-concurrency 96 \
  --request-rate inf --temperature 0
```

Kernel-level sweep: 8-GPU offline harness timing `CustomAllreduce.custom_{reduce_scatter,all_gather}` vs the NCCL fallback at hidden 5120 BF16 (max-rank median CUDA-event time), included in the PR records.

## Test Result

Kernel sweep (median of 30 reps, max rank; both paths' outputs agree within BF16 reduction-order noise, rel RMSE ~4e-3, AG max_abs_err 0):

| msg MiB | RS Lamport us | RS NCCL us | gain |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 10 | 50.2 | 99.6 | +98.4% |
| 80 | 151.9 | 203.5 | +34.0% |
| 160 | 271.4 | 308.3 | +13.6% |
| 320 | 507.3 | 543.9 | +7.2% |
| 640 | 978.1 | 994.3 | +1.7% |

| AG MiB | Lamport us | NCCL us | gain |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 5 | 89.8 | 167.1 | +86% |
| 20 | 263.2 | 299.0 | +14% |
| 40 | 497.0 | 539.0 | +8.5% |
| 80 | 963.7 | 1012.4 | +5.1% |

Serving A/B, same main revision (`b7e0cdac5d`), baseline = stock 16/2-8 MiB caps, PR = RS 96 / AG 40 MiB caps via the new envs; 0 failed requests in all runs.

random 8192/1024, concurrency 16:

| arm | out tok/s | TTFT p50 ms | TTFT p99 ms | TPOT p50 ms | E2EL p50 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline | 1251.6 | 1229.2 | 4908.2 | 9.60 | 10965.9 |
| PR | 1375.5 | 1160.6 | 1611.9 | 9.52 | 10872.1 |
| delta | +9.9% | -5.6% | -67.2% | -0.8% | -0.9% |

prefix_repetition 32768/2048/1024, concurrency 96:

| arm | out tok/s | TTFT p50 ms | TTFT mean ms | TPOT p50 ms | E2EL p50 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline | 3793.7 | 3896.1 | 5311.8 | 18.74 | 22301.0 |
| PR | 4064.7 | 2553.8 | 4753.6 | 18.04 | 21347.4 |
| delta | +7.1% | -34.4% | -10.5% | -3.8% | -4.3% |

(A replication of the same PR configuration with hardcoded caps instead of the envs gave out 4065.8 tok/s / TTFT p50 2194.8 / TTFT mean 4279.3 / TPOT p50 18.72 / E2EL p50 21385.4. Attribution runs: with only the RS 96 MiB raise, TTFT p50 3340.1 / mean 4700.1; adding the AG 40 MiB raise contributes the rest. A 672 MiB RS variant was also measured and adds nothing over RS 96.)

title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Skinny GEMM dispatch for tiny-M decode projections
body:
## Purpose

At tiny M (1–4 rows) the dense projections on DeepSeek-V4.1's decode path are dispatch-mismatched: MXFP8 CuTeDSL and BF16 cuBLAS kernels sized for bulk traffic run weight-bound rounds. This PR adds a shape-keyed skinny dispatch table (SM100/B200 only, TP8 shapes) that swaps in the measured winners exactly where they win — a Triton SIMT GEMM for the three MXFP8 projections, CuTe skinny for the BF16 indexer/lm_head projections, and ll_bf16 dotprod for the FP32 compressor scores, 20 (shape, M) cells in total.

Semantics are preserved exactly: MXFP8 candidates keep the per-32-element E8M0 activation scale and FP8 rounding (`round_mx` in the SIMT kernel reproduces the baseline MXFP8 quantization), and FP32 compressor outputs stay FP32. Everything falls back to the original kernels off-table, off-device, non-BF16 input, with LoRA attached, with a bias, or under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`. The dispatch runs at model init for the three unquantized BF16 modules (K3/GLM-5.2 quant-method replacement precedent) and at the model-layer call sites for the fused/wo_a/compressor paths, so module forward and any wrappers are untouched off the table.

## Test Plan

Deployment (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 8xB200, TP8/EP, MegaMoE+SP, FlashInfer sparse MLA, FP8 KV, C1/C4/C16 client suites, `vllm bench serve`, seed 42, ignore-EOS, tokenizer trusted):

```bash
vllm serve /gpfs/mszn/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code --served-model-name dsv4 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp --enable-expert-parallel \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 65536 \
  --max-num-seqs 96 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune

for C in 1 4; do vllm bench serve --backend vllm --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model dsv4 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 \
  --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 0 --random-prefix-len 0 \
  --num-prompts 100 --max-concurrency $C --request-rate inf --ignore-eos \
  --seed 42; done
vllm bench serve ... --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts 100 --max-concurrency 16  # identical flags otherwise
```

Unit/kernel tests:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py tests/kernels/test_dsv41_mxfp8_skinny_gemm.py -q
```

## Test Result

- pytest on 8xB200 (SM100): `204 passed, 267 skipped` (the skips are the existing SM90/SM103-gated K3/GLM cases; all DSV4.1 cases and every shared case for this arch pass). Coverage includes the 20-cell table vs `selected.json` configs, install gating (SM100/dtype/LoRA/shape/bias/M-miss fallbacks byte-equal to the original calls), SIMT-vs-reference rel-RMSE across 5 activation scales (1e-5..100), the wo_a chain vs the real DeepGEMM `fp8_einsum` baseline, and compressor ll_bf16 vs `torch.mm(out_dtype=fp32)`.
- pre-commit: `ruff check`, `ruff format`, mypy-3.10, check-torch-cuda-call all pass on the touched files.
- Serving A/B (same main revision `b7e0cdac5d`, baseline = original kernels, PR = skinny dispatch; 0 failed requests in all runs):

random 1024/256, C1:

| metric | baseline | PR | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| out tok/s | 117.5 | 120.3 | +2.3% |
| TPOT p50 (ms) | 8.001 | 7.801 | -2.5% |
| E2EL p50 (ms) | 2176.3 | 2127.1 | -2.3% |

random 1024/256, C4:

| metric | baseline | PR | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| out tok/s | 439.9 | 442.0 | +0.5% |
| TPOT p50 (ms) | 8.523 | 8.473 | -0.6% |

random 8192/1024, C16:

| metric | baseline | PR | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| out tok/s | 1375.6 | 1385.5 | +0.7% |
| TPOT p50 (ms) | 9.428 | 9.385 | -0.5% |

Prefix-cache suite (prefix_repetition 32768/2048/1024, C96) is unchanged within the run-to-run spread (out 4064.7 -> 4051.4 tok/s, -0.3%; TPOT 18.04 -> 18.48 ms); the dispatch only covers M<=4 cells, which C96 decode does not satisfy per step.

C1 was measured twice on fresh servers: round 1 out 120.3 tok/s (+2.3%) / TPOT 7.801 ms; round 2 out 119.9 tok/s (+2.0%) / TPOT 7.802 ms against the same baseline. The direction and size hold across server starts.

- Quality: 150-question GSM8K smoke (5-shot, flexible-extract, temperature 0, identical harness to #56568's eval): **98.0% / strict-match 83.3%** on the PR configuration (model family trend on this main revision is 96-98.7%, so no quality regression is visible). Numerics identical-by-construction is asserted by the scale-preserving specializations and covered by the two pytest suites above. A V1-runner startup plus GSM8K smoke on the same tree also passes (piecewise graph capture succeeds on all ranks).

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Kimi Code CLI): the measured winning dispatch table comes from a prior experimental campaign by this team (documented in-tree in `benchmarks/kernels/experimental/dsv41_skinny/`), and I integrated, verified and measured it; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

title: [Feat][Model] DeepSeek-V4.1 decoder-side SWA bounded replay
body:
## Purpose

Stacked on #56227 (base branch `feat/dsv41-swa-bounded-replay`; the diff shows only this PR's three commits). DeepSeek-V4.1's layers past the last KV-source layer (21-39 on V4.1-Flash) own nothing but sliding-window KV: every later layer attends the compressed KV of the source layers, and only the last 128 tokens' window KV is read after prefill. This is DeepSeek's decoder-side SWA bounded replay: in prefill those layers run on each request's last 128 tokens only, cold prefills included, while layers 0-20 still run on every token. It is a deliberate approximation, not an equivalent reduction of work: the kept rows' window attention in layers 21-39 is bounded at the trailing window (the SWA kernels read no window KV below it), so the last token's hidden state is not bit-identical to a full prefill; the long-range context reaches it through the compressed KV. The accuracy runs below (gsm8k on TP4 and DP4, two passes each) and DSpark's unchanged acceptance length are what this rests on.

- `DeepseekV4Model` (`nvidia/model.py`): when the layers after the last KV source are all sliding-window and the configuration allows it, the forward is split into `_run_layers` up to the cut, `DecoderReplayLayers` for the rest, and the final mHC collapse. Otherwise the forward is unchanged and a warning names the reason.
- `DeepseekV41ModelState.prepare_attn` (`nvidia/model_state.py`): after the step's own metadata it builds the replay layers' batch from the same inputs: the replay rows (one Triton kernel fills the rows, the row-subset `InputBuffers`, its slot mappings and its replay start), attention metadata through metadata builders of its own (the runner's hold the batch's metadata past the forward) and, under piecewise graphs, the size of the replay layers' graph. Everything lives in persistent buffers because that graph reads them by address. The result is set on `DecoderReplayLayers.replay_batch`; it is None when nothing trims in an eager forward and under FULL graphs (uniform decode).
- `DecoderReplayLayers` (`decoder_replay_layers.py`): gathers the seven layer inputs by the rows, runs the layers under a copy of the forward context with the replay batch's attention metadata, slot mappings, padding mask, batch descriptor and DP metadata, and scatters the outputs back to full-batch rows. Under breakable piecewise graphs the replay is an eager break of the model graph: the layers run in a graph of their own (`ReplayCudaGraphs`, keyed by the replay batch's padded size) captured inside the model graph's capture of the same size. Only prefills trim, so a capture's dummy batch keeps all its rows and every capture size gets a replay graph of that size; at runtime the replay batch pads to the smallest capture size that fits, which therefore always exists.
- Data parallelism: the replay layers' MoE collectives need every rank's token count, so the model state has the ranks agree in `prepare_attn` with one CPU all-reduce carrying whether each rank trims and its replay token count. Any rank trimming makes every rank replay on those counts; under graphs all ranks run the one replay graph size that fits the largest count.
- DSpark (`dspark/speculator.py`): the drafter derives its context KV from the target's aux hidden states, which under decoder replay exist only for the last window of each request; `_context_rows` bounds the context KV writes to the drafter's own window.
- Shared changes, none behavioral for other models: `AttentionGroup.make_metadata_builder` (a builder outside the group's own list), `prepare_inputs_to_capture` hands the model state the capture's real cudagraph mode (the default state treats PIECEWISE like NONE), and an eager break of a breakable capture may capture graphs of its own.

The decoder side stays off, with a warning, when the pipeline stage does not hold every layer after the last KV source, under sequence-parallel MoE, prefill context parallelism or microbatching, with an Engram layer after the cut, or with a drafter whose window is wider than the target's. DeepSeek-V4.1 turns sequence-parallel MoE on for EP with TP > 1 under DP, so under DP the decoder side runs with TP = 1 today.

No other open PR implements the decoder side of SWA replay; #56227 is the encoder side this builds on.

## Usage

Nothing to configure: with #56227 and this PR, DeepSeek-V4.1 on model runner V2 replays on both sides by default, including under `--data-parallel-size > 1` with TP = 1. `--no-swa-bounded-replay` turns both sides off.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_decoder_replay_layers.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_context_rows.py
```

Accuracy: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` served on a GB200 node with `vllm serve` (default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` with breakable piecewise graphs), gsm8k (5-shot) run twice against the same server, pass 2 re-sending every prompt so each request is a full-prompt prefix hit, concurrency 512: TP4 (`--max-num-seqs 1024`) and DP4 x TP1 x EP4 (`--max-num-seqs 256` per rank). Baseline arms are `--no-swa-bounded-replay` on the same tree.

## Test Result

Unit tests cover the replay rows and sub-batch fields (including prompt-logprobs requests, which keep every row, and the adaptive-verification query bound), the graph-size and DP agreement rules, an idle DP rank's dummy batch, gather/scatter with the indexer buffers, the replay graph against the eager path on a batch it never saw, nested breakable captures and the DSpark context rows; pre-commit and mypy are clean.

gsm8k, n=1319, 0 request errors in every pass, decoder replay engaged on every rank:

| arm | pass 1 (cold) | pass 2 (prefix hits) |
|---|---|---|
| TP4, replay on (encoder + decoder) | 0.9249 | 0.9249 |
| TP4, `--no-swa-bounded-replay` | 0.9295 | 0.9295 |
| DP4 x TP1 x EP4, replay on (encoder + decoder) | 0.9287 | 0.9333 |
| DP4 x TP1 x EP4, `--no-swa-bounded-replay` | 0.9295 | 0.9196 |

All arms are within run-to-run noise of each other (one standard error at n=1319 is 0.0075). DSpark with adaptive verification on TP4 kept its acceptance length on an earlier revision of this branch (3.28 vs 3.29).

title: [Model][Engram] Disk-backed Engram n-gram tables for DeepSeek-V4.1
body:
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's Engram n-gram tables come to about 189 GiB. Tensor
parallelism splits them across ranks rather than replicating them, so that
figure holds whatever the parallel layout, and on most hosts it is what decides
whether the model fits. The lookup is a pure gather of one row per head per
layer per token, so the resident working set is tiny next to the tables.

This adds `EngramConfig.disk_offload_dir`, which memory-maps each shard from a
file instead of holding it in anonymous pinned host memory. It builds on the
Engram prefetch and DP sharding merged in #56512, reusing its
`_allocate_weights` and `_storage` hooks.

## Enabling it

    vllm serve ... --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"disk_offload_dir":"/raid/engram"}'

or `VLLM_ENGRAM_DISK_OFFLOAD_DIR=/raid/engram`, which supplies the default. The
option requires `cpu_offload`, is rejected alongside `dp_shared_memory` because
the two are alternative placements for the same table, and requires a cudagraph
mode that still executes the forward in Python on live steps (`PIECEWISE`).
Unset, nothing changes: the UVA and shared-memory paths remain the default.

For the directory given above, each shard is written as
`/raid/engram/engram_v<vocab_start>_<vocab_end>_r<shard>.weight.bin`, with a
matching `.scale.bin` and a `.done.json` recording the shard geometry. The
vocab slice is part of the name because a rank hosts one shard per Engram
layer, and keying on the rank alone makes the layers collide on one file. The
first boot streams the checkpoint through a read-write mapping, so a host with
less free RAM than the tables can still load them. Later boots map the finished
file and skip the checkpoint read. A half-written file, or one left by a
different TP or EDP layout, is rebuilt rather than gathered from.

The directory must be node-local storage. The gather is random 4 KiB reads
scattered across the tables with no locality, which is the access pattern a
network filesystem serves worst, and the per-step host round trip is already
the binding cost at low concurrency. Pointing several servers at one shared
export would read the same shards over the network on every step, and the
build path has no cross-node locking, so concurrent first boots against one
directory would interleave. Shared storage is usable as a staging origin,
copied to a local directory before serving, but not as the serving path.

A mapped file cannot be read through UVA, which needs page-locked memory, and
pinning the mapping would return the table to RAM. Rows are therefore gathered
on the host, deduplicated there, and dequantized on the device by
`_engram_dequant_rows_kernel`, which mirrors the existing kernel's index and
ue8m0 math. The gather is host work and is skipped during capture, since
capture mode is global and rejects it from any thread.

## Composability

Independent of the KV offload backends. The Engram mapping is clean page cache
while a KV connector's pool is pinned, so the kernel evicts Engram pages under
pressure instead of failing the KV allocation. Verified on B200 TP4 with
`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` holding 186.26 GB per rank, 745 GB across the node,
alongside disk-backed Engram: free memory 784 GB, page cache falling from 1671
GB to 1188 GB as the pinned pool took its share. This is the case the feature
exists for, since the freed DRAM is what makes a KV tier affordable.

Shard naming keys on the index from `_get_shard_info`, which is the TP rank
under tensor parallelism and the EDP head rank under Engram DP sharding, so
both layouts name shards correctly and a layout change invalidates the sidecar.

## Results

B200 TP4, CUDA graphs, no eager.

Fixed 8k1k at concurrency 16, three runs per arm:

| | pinned + UVA | disk |
|---|---:|---:|
| throughput, 3 runs | 13,632 +/- 806 tok/s | 14,168 +/- 104 tok/s |
| host memory in use | 352 GB | 95 GB |


The row gather overlapped against the decoder layers, measured against an
otherwise identical inline build run back to back:

| 8k1k, conc 16 | inline | overlapped |
|---|---:|---:|
| throughput | 14,163 tok/s | 14,330 tok/s |
| mean TTFT | 984.79 ms | 696.70 ms |
| P99 TTFT | 6,508.53 ms | 4,145.65 ms |
| median TTFT | 190.34 ms | 212.27 ms |
| median TPOT | 8.71 ms | 8.42 ms |

Agentic traces across the concurrency sweep, disk against the published
baseline for the same recipe:

| conc | baseline tok/s | disk tok/s | disk / baseline | baseline P90 TTFT | disk P90 TTFT |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 19,338 | 12,272 | 63% | 958 ms | 1,205 ms |
| 2 | 25,059 | 14,587 | 58% | 558 ms | 695 ms |
| 4 | 34,897 | 24,453 | 70% | 533 ms | 548 ms |
| 8 | 61,151 | 47,598 | 78% | 477 ms | 497 ms |
| 16 | 112,212 | 101,218 | 90% | 551 ms | 598 ms |
| 32 | 226,006 | 207,582 | 92% | 784 ms | 685 ms |
| 64 | 348,969 | 330,709 | 95% | 1,325 ms | 1,092 ms |
| 96 | 222,396 | 301,346 | 135% | 18,217 ms | 4,992 ms |
| 128 | 76,717 | 112,567 | 147% | 290,749 ms | 193,493 ms |

The two arms cross between concurrency 64 and 96. The baseline loses 36 percent
of its concurrency-64 throughput by 96 while the disk arm loses 9 percent, and
by 128 the baseline has fallen to 22 percent of its own peak against 34 percent
for disk. Freed host memory is what widens the margin there, so the disk path
is strongest exactly where the pinned tables squeeze the rest of the system.

Median TPOT carries a near-constant offset of about 2.6 ms per token that does
not scale with batch size, so it dominates where steps are short and vanishes
where they are not. The offset is the per-step host round trip rather than
device I/O: random 4 KiB reads on the array measure 70 microseconds, and the
pages are cached in the steady state. Overlap does not change the throughput
column, since short steps have little decoder compute to hide a gather behind,
but it does move the tail at the concurrencies where prefill volume is largest.

Low-concurrency serving is therefore the weak case today. Collapsing the round
trip to one per step rather than one per Engram layer was tried and measured
slower, so the remaining follow-up is computing the hashes on the host, which
would let the gather start before the forward rather than waiting on the hash
kernel.

title: feat(DSv4): wait for per-layer KV loads before attention
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek V4 owns its attention call and registers directly into static_forward_context, so it never reaches @maybe_transfer_kv_layer and never gets the connector wait that decorator provides. With a layer-wise KV connector the asynchronous loads are then unordered against the compute that reads them, and the model reads KV that has not landed.

Add maybe_wait_for_kv_layer() alongside maybe_transfer_kv_layer, carrying the same guards, and call it from DeepseekV4Attention._prepare_and_attn before the KV insert, the indexer and the compressor touch this layer's caches.

title: [MoE][Humming] Share permute scratch workspace across MoE layers
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #56759

Humming currently keeps a layer-local `MoEPermuteScratch` for each MoE layer.
For large MoE models, this makes persistent scratch memory scale with the number
of MoE layers, even though these layers execute sequentially.

This PR moves `MoEPermuteScratch` ownership to `WorkspaceManager` and reuses
compatible scratch buffers across MoE layers.

The shared scratch remains isolated per active `(ubatch, lane)` workspace
context, and the existing DP-aware scratch sizing semantics are preserved.

## Test Plan

- Verified the model can start with TP=4 using the default
  `max_num_batched_tokens`; before this change it required reducing
  `--max-num-batched-tokens` to 2048.
- Verified with DP=8 + EP=8 that exactly one Humming permute scratch is created
  per worker instead of one per MoE layer.
- Ran the repository pre-commit hooks locally.

## Test Result

Local pre-commit checks passed:

- ruff check
- ruff format
- typos
- mypy
- SPDX/header checks
- forbidden import checks
- other enabled repository hooks

Memory validation with DP=8 + EP=8 showed that scratch allocation no longer
scales with the number of MoE layers.

A Marlin comparison showed:

```text
                         Marlin        Humming (shared scratch)
Model loading            88.62 GiB     88.62 GiB
CUDA graph capture        4.60 GiB      4.62 GiB
Available KV cache       20.92 GiB     18.61 GiB
```

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark speculative decoding — illegal memory access in SM120 sparse-MLA prefill on long prompts
body:
# [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark speculative decoding — illegal memory access in SM120 sparse-MLA prefill on long prompts

> Cross-ref: #55757 (same box family, same reporter — sequential sm_120 sparse-MLA investigation; that one covers the non-spec MHA prefill faults, this one is DSpark-specific).

## Environment

- **Model**: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (476 GiB), vision enabled
- **Hardware**: 4× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, 96 GiB each), PCIe-only (no NVLink)
- **vLLM**: nightly `69db1c26` + PR #56214 overlay (`e77daef89`), flashinfer-python 0.6.18
- **Patches for SM120 serving**: topk 1152/640 instantiations in `sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4.cu` + the Python `_DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH` mirror, prefill dispatch arms for the same shapes (dual-cache `DISPATCH_BY_NH_PBSX_TK`), SWA cache block 32→64, divergent block sizes (ratio-1: 64, ratio-2: 128). Without DSpark this configuration serves cleanly: 60 tok/s c=1, 12K prefill in 2.1 s, stable in production.

## Repro

Serve with:

```json
{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}
```

Then send any prompt ≳4K tokens (12K reproduces reliably). Short prompts work; long prompts hard-crash the engine with an illegal memory access.

## Findings (instrumented)

1. `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` localizes the fault to `flashinfer` `sparse_mla_sm120_prefill.cu`, `launch_prefill_mg_dual` (`cudaLaunchKernelExC`, ~line 212/268), instantiation `<DSV4, FP8, nh=16, TOPK=1152, pbs=64, pbs_x=64>`, on the chunked-prefill chunks (`ntok=4092` with k=5).
2. **The same instantiation with the same shape tuple runs clean without DSpark** (12K prefill → 456× `(topk=1152, pbs=64, topk_x=512)`, zero errors), so it is input *content*, not kernel shape coverage.
3. Host-side launch-time probes of all kernel inputs found per-token lengths and index values plausible — but in some runs **garbage extra-topk lengths** (`max_elen=2139095040` on a 512-wide row → kernel K-loop reads OOB) in ~9/81 calls. In other runs the crash reproduces with clean lens at launch time, so the garbage lens are a symptom, not necessarily the trigger.
4. `compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens` (`deepseek_v4_1/common/ops/cache_utils.py`) fully initializes every lens row, so garbage lens imply never-written or overwritten memory — consistent with a cross-stream/capture-time aliasing issue specific to the DSpark path.
5. PR #56598 (padded draft rows → generic MoE router, fixes #56389) does **not** fix this crash — tested on top of our tree. This is a different kernel (sparse-MLA prefill, not the dsv4_topk Triton router).

## Suspects

Cross-stream memory aliasing under DSpark (freshly-allocated lens tensors consumed by asynchronously-queued prefill kernels), or the DSpark SWA index widening (`get_dspark_swa_index_width(128,5)=192`) interacting with prefill metadata that assumes window 128.

Happy to provide probe outputs, shape histograms, and exact repro commands.

The same failure also reproduces with per-commit wheels from `https://wheels.vllm.ai/` (see the regression bracket below). ### Describe the bug Starting a plain `vllm serve` of GLM-5.3-Flash crashes deterministically during startup memory profiling, inside piecewise cudagraph capture, with `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument`. No cudagraph, compilation, or attention-backend flag is passed; vLLM logs `INFO [vllm.py:762] Auto-enabling VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1. Set VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 to opt out.` and then dies, so this is a default-configuration crash. It fails on multiple TP ranks (observed on `Worker_TP0` and `Worker_TP2`) and reproduced on every attempt across five separate runs on two different hosts. ### Steps to reproduce On a 4-GPU aarch64 (GB200 NVL) node using the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image: ``` vllm serve --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --served-model-name glm-5.3-flash-321b-a18b --tensor-parallel-size 4 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 2200 --port 28100 --load-format runai_streamer --trust-remote-code ``` No other flags or environment overrides are needed. ### Expected behavior Startup memory profiling completes, KV cache is sized, and the server reaches `Application startup complete.` (this is exactly what the immediately preceding commit does; see the regression bracket below). ### Actual behavior The server aborts during `determine_available_memory` with `CUDA error: invalid argument`. Condensed frame chain (all frames are inside the installed vLLM wheel or torch): ``` vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:582 in determine_available_memory vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:981 in profile_cudagraph_memory vllm/v1/cudagraph_utils.py:834 in capture_model (profile_only=True) vllm/v1/cudagraph_utils.py:401 in forward_fn (CUDAGraphMode.PIECEWISE) vllm/v1/cudagraph_utils.py:499 in run_pw_graph vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py:341 in __call__ vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py:390 in _capture ... model forward (GLM multimodal / remote-code attention) ... vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py:244 vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla_attention.py:864 in torch.ops.vllm.unified_mla_attention_with_output vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py:117 in wrapper (@eager_break_during_capture) vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py:206 in add_eager vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla_attention.py:1483 / :1110 in forward_mqa vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse.py:473 vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_mla_attention.py:734 vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/index_group.py:95 -> :133 self.side_stream.wait_event(self.logical_topk_ready) torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument ``` ### Suspected root cause 1. During PIECEWISE capture, `vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py:244` calls `record_logical_topk_ready()` **inline and undecorated**, so `logical_topk_ready.record(current_stream())` is recorded as a node *inside* the captured graph segment. 2. `unified_mla_attention_with_output` is wrapped by `@eager_break_during_capture`. Under `CUDAGraphMode.PIECEWISE` the wrapper does **not** early-return (it early-returns only for the `FULL` path, cf. #56312), so it proceeds into `add_eager`, whose first action is `_end_segment()` -> `capture_end()`, clearing the capturing state. 3. The eager body then runs `index_group._convert_once`, which at `index_group.py:133` calls `side_stream.wait_event(self.logical_topk_ready)`. The event was only ever recorded into a graph that is no longer capturing and has not been replayed, so waiting on it from a non-capturing stream yields `cudaErrorInvalidValue`. Notably the sibling branch at the same site (`has_indexer is False`) uses `side_stream.wait_stream(compute_stream)` and needs no event, which is why only the HiSparse indexer path is affected. ### Regression bracket Bisected with per-commit wheels, holding image, model, launcher, flags, and every other dependency fixed and varying only the vLLM wheel: - **Last known good:** `120ec4ebd2803c3cc63729e18fcfd42b5ba47447` - `https://wheels.vllm.ai/120ec4ebd2803c3cc63729e18fcfd42b5ba47447/vllm-0.1.1.dev48+g120ec4ebd-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl` reaches `Available KV cache memory: 81.74 GiB` and `Application startup complete.` - **First bad:** `d43bb2f37f87a63d3a9a299c97050443cf6a2520` (#53781) - `https://wheels.vllm.ai/d43bb2f37f87a63d3a9a299c97050443cf6a2520/vllm-0.1.1.dev49+gd43bb2f37-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl` fails at `index_group.py:133` as above. This is the only commit in that file's history, and the failing statement is still present on `main`. ### Possible fix directions - Record `logical_topk_ready` outside the captured segment (or mark the record site so it is not captured), so the event is valid for the eager consumer. - Have `index_group._convert_once` synchronize with `wait_stream(compute_stream)` on the eager-break path instead of waiting on a captured event, mirroring the existing `has_indexer is False` branch. - Make `eager_break_during_capture` / `add_eager` re-record or invalidate cross-stream events it strands when it ends a segment. One guard we tested does **not** work and is worth flagging: checking `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()` inside `_convert_once` is always false there, because `capture_end()` has already run by the time the eager body executes (verified experimentally; the patched build crashed identically with the failing line shifted by exactly the number of inserted lines). ### Before submitting a new issue Searched the tracker for `logical_topk_ready`, `side_stream`, `index_group`, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH`, `eager_break_during_capture`/`add_eager`, and GLM-5.3-Flash + `cudaErrorInvalidValue`; also reviewed #56312, #42304, #53030, #46372 and #54361. No existing issue, open PR, or landed commit covers this interaction, and the failing statement is unchanged on `main`. --- _This issue was drafted with assistance from the `opus` AI model._
