title: [ROCm][Perf] Tiny-dot kernel for the Qwen MoE shared-expert gate
body:
## Summary

A Qwen MoE block gates its shared expert with `sigmoid(shared_expert_gate(x))`, where `shared_expert_gate` is a `ReplicatedLinear(hidden_size, 1)`. During decode with a single token that is a 1x1xK GEMM, and hipBLASLt answers it with a 64x96x32 macro tile plus a SplitK post-pass in order to produce one scalar. Qwen3.5-35B-A3B has 40 such layers, so this fires 40 times per decode step.

This series replaces that shape with a dot product, then folds the surrounding work into the same kernel. On gfx1151 it is worth **3.2% of decode throughput** end to end, with prefill and TTFT unchanged. Everything is gated on `on_gfx1151()`, the only architecture measured here.

## What this touches

The dispatcher change fires for any unquantized bf16/fp16 `Linear(K, 1)` on a single token, which in this tree means the `shared_expert_gate` in `qwen2_moe`, `qwen3_moe`, `qwen3_next`, `qwen3_5` and `interns2_mobius`. The only other 1-wide projection, `qwen3_dspark`'s `proj`, is fp32 and therefore excluded.

The call-site change is narrower: it lives in `Qwen2MoeMLP`, so it reaches Qwen2-MoE, Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5-MoE and InternS2 Mobius. `qwen3_moe` has its own `Qwen3MoeMLP` whose `forward` is line-for-line identical; I left it alone because I have not measured it, but folding the two would be the obvious follow-up.

Checkpoints without a shared expert are untouched, as is any deployment running with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS`, where `expert_gate` is `None`.

## Commits

| commit | what it does |
|---|---|
| `Replace the 1x1xK BLAS call with a fused dot on gfx1151` | Routes the m == n == 1 shape to `(x*w).sum(dtype=x.dtype)` instead of BLAS. |
| `Serve the tiny scalar projection from a Triton kernel` | Replaces the two-launch eager chain with a single-workgroup fp32-accumulated kernel, for `bias=None` and K within the register budget. `_tiny_dot` holds that choice so callers do not repeat it. Adds the correctness test and the A/B benchmark. |
| `Fold the shared_expert_gate sigmoid into the tiny-dot kernel` | `APPLY_SIGMOID` constexpr collapses mul + sum + sigmoid into one launch at the `Qwen2MoeMLP` call site, and the scalar output is allocated in the input dtype so the store does the rounding rather than a separate copy. Extends the benchmark with `--sigmoid`. |

## End-to-end results

Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-W4A16 on gfx1151 (Strix Halo), concurrency 1, 100-token prompts, 128 output tokens, 10 prompts, `max_num_seqs=1`. Three runs per arm, medians below.

| metric | `upstream/main` | this branch | change |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| prefill | 612 tok/s | 627 tok/s | unchanged |
| TTFT | 163 ms | 159 ms | unchanged |
| **decode** | **43.3 tok/s** | **44.7 tok/s** | **+3.2%** |
| **TPOT** | **23.11 ms** | **22.39 ms** | **−3.1%** |
| end-to-end latency | 3098 ms | 3003 ms | −3.1% |

## Kernel microbenchmark

`benchmarks/kernels/bench_tiny_dot.py`, times in µs. Each cell is the median of five separate process invocations, because the BLAS arm is not repeatable enough for a single reading (see below).

| K | dtype | BLAS | eager fused | Triton | Triton vs BLAS |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | bf16 | 12.60 | 9.16 | **5.24** | 2.40x |
| 1024 | fp16 | 9.98 | 9.08 | **4.88** | 2.05x |
| 2048 | bf16 | 16.12 | 8.36 | **5.22** | 3.09x |
| 2048 | fp16 | 11.28 | 8.26 | **4.88** | 2.31x |
| 4096 | bf16 | 22.94 | 8.64 | **5.20** | 4.41x |
| 4096 | fp16 | 13.88 | 8.56 | **4.92** | 2.82x |

The Triton kernel is flat in K at roughly 5 µs, being one launch over a single workgroup, while BLAS grows with K. Qwen3.5-35B-A3B uses K=2048.

With `--sigmoid`, which is how the gate is actually used, at K=2048 bf16:

| | dot only | with sigmoid |
|---|---:|---:|
| BLAS | 16.12 µs | 18.92 µs |
| eager fused | 8.36 µs | 10.88 µs |
| Triton | 5.22 µs | 5.26 µs |

Folding it into the kernel is what makes the sigmoid free; the other two arms pay another launch for it, so the Triton margin over the eager chain widens from 1.60x to 2.07x.

## Accuracy

GSM8K, 5-shot, temperature 0, 400 questions per arm, no invalid responses on either side.

| arm | accuracy |
|---|---:|
| `upstream/main` | 0.9225 (369/400) |
| this branch | 0.9125 (365/400) |

## Testing

```
pytest tests/kernels/test_tiny_dot_triton.py          24 passed
pre-commit run --files <the four changed files>       clean (ruff, ruff-format, mypy, SPDX)
```

The new test compares the kernel against the eager reference across K = 32 / 1024 / 2048 / 4096 / 65536 / 131072, both dtypes, with and without the folded sigmoid. The two largest K exercise the multi-warp launches.

## Software stack

Measured on ROCm 10.1.0a20260822 (`torch.version.hip` 7.16), PyTorch 2.13.0, Triton 3.8.0. This is newer than what `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` pins for the shipped image (ROCm 7.2.3, PyTorch 2.12, Triton 3.7). On older stack, improvement is even bigger.

## Not a duplicate

No duplicated PRs identified.

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Claude). Every line was reviewed by the submitter, and the measurements above were run and checked by hand.



---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

title: DSpark checkpoints exported in fill-in (DFlash 1+N) layout silently serve with <1% acceptance: the optional layout flag is absent from their configs, and the default anchor-first sampler is wrong for them
body:
Serving a DeepSpec-trained DSpark drafter on vLLM 0.27.1 produced a ~0.9% acceptance rate with no error or warning anywhere. The checkpoint was healthy; the failure was a layout mismatch that vLLM resolves silently in the wrong direction.

**What we observed.** The drafter was trained in the DFlash-style fill-in layout (`1 + N` query positions, anchor acts as the bonus token, every non-anchor position is a mask slot to fill). vLLM's `DSparkSpeculator` defaults to `sample_from_anchor=True` (the native DSpark layout: anchor is the first *predicted* token), and our draft configs carried no `sample_from_anchor` key the loader could use to detect the difference — so an anchor-position output was consumed as a predicted token and every subsequent position conditioned on the wrong context.

The absence of the key is worth explaining, because the field does exist upstream: `sample_from_anchor` was added to speculators' DFlash/DSpark configs only recently ([speculators #760](https://github.com/vllm-project/speculators/pull/760), 2026-07-13, defaulting to `True` for DSpark and `False` for DFlash, and serialized with the rest of the config; wired into vLLM's DSpark loader by [#48639](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48639), 2026-07-20). It remains an *optional* field, and export paths that predate it or bypass the speculators config dump still emit configs without it — both of our checkpoints, exported by a training pipeline built on a speculators fork (0.7.0.dev176), do. A consumer then has no choice but to fall back to the family default.

Because nothing raises, this presents only as "a terrible drafter": aggregate acceptance under 1%, per-position acceptance collapsing after position 0, and a trained-in-vain loss curve. We initially attributed exactly this symptom to an exposure-bias training bug and discarded two checkpoint families before measuring.

**One-line fix, measured.** Adding `"sample_from_anchor": false` to the draft config copy (no weight or system-package change; stock vLLM 0.27.1, all shims via PYTHONPATH) flips acceptance in place — same weights, same engine, same data, only the layout flag differs:

| checkpoint | default layout | `sample_from_anchor: false` | pairing granularity |
|---|---|---|---|
| an older 5-epoch teacher-forced draft — **main evidence** | **0.85%** | **47.4%** agg / 7.11 tokens per round | full 100-sample runs on **both** sides |
| draft B (full run) — corroborating | 0.089% | **43.3%** | smoke probes (~10K drafted tokens) on both sides |

A third data point on a separate checkpoint (draft B, 300-step arm) with the fixed layout reached **40.3%** aggregate / 6.04 tokens per round (full 100-sample run; no default-layout counterpart was run for this checkpoint).

> Measurement note for reviewers: each row pairs the same checkpoint weights under the two layout flags at the same eval granularity. The main row is a fully controlled A/B — full-length 100-sample runs on both sides; the default-layout side (0.85% over 258,929 rounds) reproduces the historical ~0.9% collapse, and the fixed side's per-position acceptance runs .880 (pos0) → .159 (pos14). The corroborating row is smoke-probe granularity on both sides. Raw metrics snapshots available on request.

With the layout fixed, the same drafters reach the expected band (TPOT 0.58/0.51 ms vs autoregressive 2.07 ms; lossless 97/100 vs greedy AR on both arms, divergent indices identical across arms — batch-shape numeric drift, not draft error).

**Root cause, two halves:**

1. **Exporter half (speculators):** the layout discriminator is new and optional. `sample_from_anchor` exists in speculators main since #760 (2026-07-13, default `True` for DSpark / `False` for DFlash, serialized with the config) and vLLM reads it since #48639 (2026-07-20) — but nothing requires it. Export paths that predate the field or bypass the speculators config dump (as our training pipeline, built on a speculators fork, did for both checkpoints) silently emit configs without the key, and the consumer is left guessing by family default.
2. **Consumer half (vLLM):** `DSparkSpeculator` reads a top-level `sample_from_anchor` attribute and silently defaults to anchor-first when it is absent. Contrast the DFlash path, which *does* fail fast when `sample_from_anchor=True` appears in its config (`dflash/speculator.py` raise) — and which #56088 blocker 3 requests flipping to support anchor-trained DFlash. The DSpark direction of the same axis — a fill-in checkpoint meeting an anchor-first default — has no guard at all. Worse, the two paths do not even agree on where the flag lives: DFlash reads it from the nested `dflash_config` dict (`dflash_config.get("sample_from_anchor", False)`), DSpark from a top-level attribute of the draft hf_config (`getattr(..., "sample_from_anchor", True)`). The same axis has two spellings with two opposite defaults across adjacent speculators families — exactly the kind of inconsistency that turns a config omission into a silent mismatch instead of an error.

**Proposal:**

- vLLM: when a DSpark draft's config lacks `sample_from_anchor`, either auto-detect the layout from `block_size`/query-geometry evidence, or at minimum warn loudly and document which default applies to which checkpoint family.
- speculators: make `sample_from_anchor` mandatory in Markov-conditioned draft configs and harden the export path so a config cannot ship without it (a missing layout flag should fail at export time, not surface as a ~1% acceptance rate at serve time).

Happy to send a PR for either option once a direction is chosen (a warn-loudly reference implementation is ready).

**Reproduction sketch** (stock vLLM 0.27.1, single A800-80GB, no system-package edits): serve a multimodal-OCR target with `--speculative-config num_speculative_tokens=15` pointing at a DeepSpec DSpark drafter whose config is the training-time one; measure `/metrics` spec-decode counters over 100 temp=0 samples; flip `"sample_from_anchor": false` in the draft config copy and re-measure. Full launch commands and shim inventory can be shared if useful.

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash DSpark mean acceptance length only 2.82 on GSM8K (k=5, 2×8 H20)
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM: `0.28.1rc1.dev673+gc9d909e80.cu129` (`c9d909e802`, `[Model] Add DSparkV41DraftModel example model entry`)
- Python: 3.11.15
- PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu129
- flashinfer: 0.6.18.post1
- OS: Linux 5.4 (x86_64)
- GPU: 2 nodes × 8× NVIDIA H20 (SM90), driver 535.161.08
- Parallelism: DP=2, per-node TP=8 + EP (TEP), `--language-model-only`
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (in-checkpoint DSpark: `dspark_block_size=5`, 3 stages, target layers 37–39)
- Spec config (matches the V4.1 recipe EVAL_ONLY / AMD block-verify command):

```json
{
  "method": "dspark",
  "num_speculative_tokens": 5,
  "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic",
  "rejection_sample_method": "block",
  "enable_adaptive_verification": false
}
```

`enable_adaptive_verification` is left **false** because adaptive DSpark is currently broken on SM90 ([#54011](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54011)).

Other relevant serve flags: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --compilation-config '{"mode": 0, "cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY", "custom_ops":["all"]}' --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41`.



### 🐛 Describe the bug

On **real GSM8K** (not `random` tokens), DSpark on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash accepts far fewer tokens per step than the published k=5 golden and than prior V4-Flash DSpark numbers on the same GPU family.

This is **not** a correctness failure: the same server scores **93.4% flexible / 93.4% strict** on GSM8K greedy completions (`lm_eval` `local-completions`, 5-shot). Outputs are coherent; the draft is just rejected early.

### Measurement (isolated Prometheus delta)

Idle check: 2 s of `/metrics` with **0** new drafts, then the full GSM8K test set, then a second snapshot. Counters from both DP engines are summed. Formula is the vLLM convention (includes bonus token):

`mean_acceptance_length = 1 + Δaccepted / Δdrafts`

| | |
|---|---|
| Workload | `openai/gsm8k` main **test**, 1319/1319 OK |
| Protocol | `/v1/completions`, 5-shot `Question: …\nAnswer:`, stop=`Question:` |
| Sampling | `temperature=0`, `do_sample=false`, `max_tokens=4096` |
| Concurrency | 32 |
| k | 5 (always fully drafted: 220185 draft tokens / 44037 drafts = 5.000) |
| Theoretical max AL | 6.0 |

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| **Mean acceptance length** | **2.817** |
| Draft acceptance rate | 36.3% (80010 / 220185) |
| Drafts / accepted / drafted | 44037 / 80010 / 220185 |
| Mean completion tokens | 95.0 |
| Per-position accept (unconditional) | **0.724, 0.516, 0.301, 0.180, 0.096** |
| Conditional continuation | 0.71, 0.58, 0.60, 0.53 |

Position 0 is OK; **positions 3–4 are almost unused** (pos4 = 9.6%). This is a tail-decay problem, not the “pos0-only then collapse to 0” pattern in [#51009](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51009) (that issue was largely `random` tokens and was closed).

Server log during the same window matches the delta, e.g.:

```
SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 2.83, ...
Per-position acceptance rate: 0.728, 0.522, 0.315, 0.177, 0.093,
Avg Draft acceptance rate: 36.7%
```

Mixed production traffic on the same process was even lower (~2.45–2.69). GSM8K only lifts that by ~0.15, which is surprising for a low-entropy math set.

### Why this looks too low

| Reference | Model | k | Workload | Hardware | Mean AL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V4.1 recipe (InferenceX / AgentX) | V4.1-Flash | **5** | AgentX traces | recipe golden | **3.51** |
| [PR #53972](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53972) | V4-Flash-0731 | **7** | GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 | **2×H20** TP2+EP | **4.386** |
| [PR #46995](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46995) Hopper field report | V4-Flash-DSpark | **5** | mixed real traffic | 2×H100 | **3.86** (pos **0.82 / 0.67 / 0.55 / 0.45 / 0.37**) |
| [#54011](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54011) `adaptive=false` | V4-Flash-0731 | 7 | speed_bench | 8×H20 | 2.7 |
| **This run** | **V4.1-Flash** | **5** | **GSM8K 5-shot greedy** | **2×8 H20** | **2.82** (pos **0.72 / 0.52 / 0.30 / 0.18 / 0.10**) |

GSM8K is usually *easier* for spec decode than AgentX/chat. Hitting **2.82 vs golden 3.51** (~20% lower), and a **pos4 of 9.6% vs 37%** on the Hopper k=5 field report, looks like SM90 / V4.1 DSpark is leaving a lot of the 5-token block on the table.

### Reproduce

Serve (recipe-style DSpark, adaptive off):

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
```

Then GSM8K 5-shot completions (`temperature=0`) against `/v1/completions`, and take `/metrics` before/after:

```
vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total
vllm:spec_decode_num_draft_tokens_total
vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total
vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_per_pos_total
```

`lm_eval run --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=4096` is sufficient if you snapshot Prometheus around it. Do **not** use `--dataset-name random` ([#51009](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51009)).

### Questions for maintainers

1. Is **~2.8 AL / pos4≈10%** on GSM8K greedy the expected DSpark quality for V4.1-Flash on Hopper/H20 with k=5, or should we be closer to the **3.51** golden (and to V4-Flash-0731’s **4.39** on the same exam)?
2. Any known SM90 draft-attention / Markov / `map_draft_to_target` gaps vs GB200 that would specifically hurt **later** draft positions?
3. For greedy eval, should `draft_sample_method` be `greedy` rather than `probabilistic`? We followed the V4.1 recipe (`probabilistic` + `block`). Happy to rerun that ablation if useful.
4. We have not yet measured chat-template + thinking-mode GSM8K (V4.1 thinking defaults ON). If that is the intended high-AL path, we can add it.

Happy to run any extra A/B (greedy draft, thinking on, single-node TP8, larger `--max-num-batched-tokens`, `per_request_spec_decode_metrics`).


### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Performance] Reuse max query length in model runner gather
body:
## Purpose

`GPUModelRunner.execute` already computes `max_query_len` from `scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens`. `gather_batch_req_state` immediately traverses the same values again.

This change threads the already-computed value into `gather_batch_req_state` through an optional `max_query_len` argument, avoiding the duplicate host-side `max(values())` traversal on the common execute path. The `None` fallback is preserved for callers that do not precompute the value, including the existing encoder/default path. Adaptive-verification behavior is unchanged: the scheduled-token maximum is still the value used by the gather logic before the later `num_tokens` rewrite.

The patch is intentionally limited to the model-runner handoff and focused regression coverage; it does not change scheduler policy, token accounting, or attention semantics.

Duplicate-work check: a current GitHub PR search in `vllm-project/vllm` for both `gather_batch_req_state` and `max_query_len` returned no other PR; exact same-head PR checks were also empty before this Draft was created. This is a scoped duplicate check for this specific mechanism, not a broad novelty claim.

AI assistance was used for implementation/review support. The commit includes `Co-authored-by: OpenAI Codex` and `Signed-off-by: Ruiqiu Zheng <191817791+Ruiqiu-Zheng@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Test Plan

Focused coverage in `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py` checks:

- the supplied-max path does not traverse `dict.values()` again, including dummy batches;
- the fallback path still performs one traversal and matches the supplied path for a heterogeneous mixed batch;
- the supplied scheduled maximum remains semantically correct when adaptive verification later rewrites batch `num_tokens`.

Repository-prescribed native command for this existing test file:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py -v
```

Patch-integrity command actually run on the publication tree:

```bash
git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD
```

## Test Result

- `git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD`: **PASS** on publication HEAD `dc6c2787db99414bf529a98f013ae8f6b568730b`.
- Native focused pytest on this publication tree: **NOT RUN**. Earlier attempts were blocked before the test bodies by the available repository environment, and the current branch-preparation environment has no prescribed `.venv`/`uv`; no dependencies were installed or downloaded to work around that.
- Ruff / publication-tree `py_compile`: **NOT EVALUATED** for the same missing prescribed environment; this Draft does not report them as passing.
- Source-equivalent CPU component harness: 2,620/2,620 correctness cases passed with 0 mismatches, including 626 adaptive-verification reuse checks.
- Component-only timing at batch size 128: median 5.900 us -> 3.360 us; paired median saving 2.585 us (43.81%), with the candidate faster in 4,998/5,000 samples. This is a host-component microbenchmark only, not an end-to-end throughput, TTFT, TPOT, GPU/NPU, or production claim.

No documentation change is required for this internal model-runner optimization.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Route untuned fp8 block-scale GEMMs to AITER Triton at large M
body:
## Purpose

aiter picks the CK instance for `gemm_a8w8_blockscale` from a table keyed on
`(gfx, cu_num, M, N, K)`. When a shape is absent it does not search or fall back
heuristically — `gemm_op_a8w8.py` runs one default instance, no `kernelName` and no
`splitK`, at *every* M, and that instance cannot fill the MFMA pipeline at prefill-sized M.

This is not a corner case. On gfx950/`cu_num=256` the shipped table has no row for any of
Qwen3-14B-FP8's four linear shapes — `(7168,5120)` qkv, `(5120,5120)` o, `(34816,5120)`
gate_up, `(5120,17408)` down — so every block-scale GEMM in that model takes the degraded
path, and aiter says so on every startup:

```
[aiter] shape is M:600, N:34816, K:5120, not found tuned config in
        .../a8w8_blockscale_tuned_gemm.csv, will use default config!
```

Measured, that default instance flatlines at **418 TFLOP/s** for every M ≥ 512, while
aiter's Triton block-scale kernel — which buckets its config by M — reaches
**870–1040 TFLOP/s**. Triton loses at decode-sized M, so the choice has to be made per call.
`_rocm_aiter_gemm_a8w8_blockscale_impl` now delegates to the Triton kernel when `M >= 384`
and `(N, K)` has no tuned CK config.

The branch lives inside the custom op rather than in the caller because the caller is traced
once by Dynamo and a branch there would freeze at the shape seen during tracing, while a
custom op is opaque and re-evaluates per call. `is_blockscale_tuned()` is the
non-preshuffled sibling of the existing `is_blockscale_bpreshuffle_tuned()`, reusing
`_load_gemm_tuned_configs` and its `(gfx, cu_num)` filter so the check is per card, not per
arch; the loader is `@functools.cache`d and `M < 384` short-circuits ahead of it, so decode
never pays for the lookup.

384 rather than 256: aiter's generic Triton config has a bad `BLOCK_SIZE_M=256` bucket
covering M ∈ (128, 256] where Triton is 1.3–4.8× *slower* than CK, and returns to
`BLOCK_SIZE_M=64` above it. Measuring the two impls head-to-head the crossover lands in
(256, 320] on all four shapes, so 384 is that cliff plus margin.

Only shapes absent from aiter's tuned table change behaviour. aiter ships per-model tuned
CSVs (`ds_v3`, `qwen3_235b`, `qwen3_next_80b_a3b`, `qwen3_vl_*`, `dsv4`, …) and this is inert
for models those cover — `Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8` is very nearly inert for exactly
that reason and is used as the low-water-mark control below. It is also inert on RDNA4/gfx1250, where
`use_triton` is already true so the caller never enters the CK impl, and unreachable off
ROCm, where `register_ops_once()` never registers the op.

One thing I could not settle, stated up front:

- **gfx942 is untested and not equivalent.** `is_fp8_fnuz()` is true on gfx94x and
  `is_triton_gemm_w8a8_tuned()` whitelists only gfx950/RDNA4, so nothing routes block-scale
  to Triton there today; this predicate checks neither, so on MI300/MI325 it would newly
  send `e4m3fnuz` through the Triton kernel. I have no gfx94x card — glad to add
  `not current_platform.is_fp8_fnuz()` if you would rather keep it scoped to gfx950.

## Test Plan

MI355X gfx950, 256 CU, TP=1, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR=1`.

Micro — authored, over `rocm_aiter_ops.gemm_a8w8_blockscale` (the op this changes) across
M ∈ {64…16384} × the four Qwen3-14B-FP8 shapes; 200-iteration warmup because Triton
JIT-compiles on first use, median of 5 × 100 timed iterations, 3 interleaved A/B pairs with
the arm order alternated. Nothing under `benchmarks/kernels/` covers this:
`benchmark_block_fp8_gemm.py` asserts `current_platform.is_cuda()` and
`benchmark_w8a8_block_fp8.py` is a Triton config tuner, not an A/B of the aiter op.

E2e and accuracy:

```
vllm bench throughput --model Qwen3-14B-FP8 --input-len 2048 --output-len 128 \
  --num-prompts 600 --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1

lm_eval --model vllm --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto \
  --model_args pretrained=Qwen3-14B-FP8,max_model_len=4096,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,tensor_parallel_size=1
```

Throughput pairs alternate arm order; a leading pair is discarded to absorb model load,
`torch.compile` and Triton autotune for both arms.

## Test Result

### Performance

Micro, median over the 28 routed points (M ≥ 384): **+54.2 %**, range +33.5…+59.9 %, no
point regressing.

| shape (N x K) | M=384 | M=512 | M=2048 | M=8192 | M=16384 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7168 x 5120 | +52.5 % | +55.3 % | +54.2 % | +59.9 % | +56.4 % |
| 5120 x 5120 | +33.5 % | +46.1 % | +36.2 % | +59.6 % | +59.6 % |
| 34816 x 5120 | +53.8 % | +54.4 % | +54.1 % | +56.3 % | +56.6 % |
| 5120 x 17408 | +43.5 % | +52.7 % | +39.4 % | +58.1 % | +58.1 % |

The 12 points below the threshold are an in-run control — both arms execute identical CK
code there — and measure **−0.1 % median, every point within ±0.7 %**.

E2e, Qwen3-14B-FP8, ISL 2048 / OSL 128, 600 prompts:

| pair | order | before | after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | after→before | 13284 tok/s | 23108 tok/s | +74.0 % |
| 2 | before→after | 13146 tok/s | 24005 tok/s | +82.6 % |
| 3 | after→before | 13118 tok/s | 22811 tok/s | +73.9 % |
| **median pairwise** | | | | **+74.0 %** |

The arms' ranges are disjoint and both allocated the same KV cache (0.015 % apart) at the
same 350× max concurrency. A leading pair is discarded as warmup; the patched arm keeps
gaining across pairs (22.0 → 23.1 → 24.0k) as the Triton cache warms while the baseline
holds to 1.3 %, so the pairwise median is the conservative reading. For scale, 13.1k tok/s
is 349 TFLOP/s of linear-layer work against a measured baseline GEMM rate of 418 TFLOP/s,
i.e. these four GEMMs are ~83 % of baseline step time, which is what lets an e2e number
land this close to the kernel number.

Across four models spanning dense, MoE+MLA and MoE-DSA, with the affected share taken from
the shapes actually observed at the op rather than derived from `config.json` (which is
wrong for MLA — it predicted `(33792,4096)` for DSV4-Flash where the truth is
`(32768,1024)`):

| model | architecture | affected | e2e | before-spread | after-spread |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Qwen3-14B-FP8` | dense | 100 % of linear FLOPs | **+74.0 %** | 1.3 % | 5.2 % |
| `GLM-5.3` | `glm_moe_dsa`, TP=4 | 6 untuned `(N,K)` | **+14.0 %** | 0.2 % | 0.1 % |
| `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` | `deepseek_v4`, MoE+MLA | 80 % of linear FLOPs | **+4.5 %** | 0.5 % | 0.5 % |
| `Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8` | `qwen3_next` | 3 untuned `(N,K)`, ~55x fewer routed calls | −0.5…+1.4 % | 2.6 % | 1.9 % |

All three affected models have disjoint before/after ranges. The last row is the useful
control: it is the least affected model here by a wide margin, so it bounds what a flat
result looks like. **Correction to an earlier version of this description**, which called it
a 0 % / *provable* no-op: instrumenting the shapes aiter reports as untuned during a run, it
has three `(N, K)` with no tuned row — `(1024, 2048)`, `(2048, 512)`, `(2048, 4096)` — all
reached above the threshold, so it is routed 9 times in a full GSM8K run against
Qwen3-14B-FP8's 492. It measures flat because its affected surface is tiny, not because it
cannot reach the path. Its baseline was re-run five times alone on one card to pin the noise
floor — 37365/37496/37745/37751/38339 tok/s, **2.6 % spread** — which is the figure to
judge the rows above against.

Against a 2.6 % noise floor that is 28×, 5.4× and 1.7× respectively; DSV4-Flash is the
weakest of the three and rests on its own 0.5 % arm spreads and disjoint ranges rather than
on margin.

The point of the table is less any single number than the ordering: the gain tracks how much
of the model's linear work the predicate can reach — 100 % → +74 %, six shapes → +14 %,
80 % of a share that is itself small next to MoE expert GEMMs → +4.5 %, three rarely-hit
shapes → flat.
That is also the answer to "will this help my model": it depends entirely on whether aiter
has tuned your shapes, and on how much of your step time is dense linear work.

`cudagraph_capture_sizes` reaches 512 and includes sizes at and above the threshold, so under
the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` mode the Triton kernel is captured rather than only run
eagerly on the piecewise prefill path. FULL capture completes with no errors; the numbers
above are from that configuration.

### Accuracy

gsm8k, 5-shot, full 1319 samples. The two kernels agree to max abs 1.9e-6 / mean relative
2e-7 on bf16 output, which is still enough to flip a near-tied argmax, so greedy
continuations do diverge on some prompts and a text diff is not the right test.

Before:
|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr|
|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.8484|±  |0.0099|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.8863|±  |0.0087|

After:
|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr|
|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.8423|±  |0.0100|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.8870|±  |0.0087|

---

Happy to file the one-line collect_env fallback separately. Build note: both the good and bad builds carry a one-line local overlay in `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` (adds `"qwen4_exp"` to the deepseek_v4 eagle-group fallback tuple in `_is_deepseek_v4_eagle`, needed until upstream lands the model in the KV-group path). Identical overlay in good and bad builds; unrelated to streams/decode. ### 🐛 Describe the bug The `eed1f3d0 → dc36fcce` range reintroduces an intermittent decode-throughput collapse on **context-load decode rows at depth 32768, concurrency 1** (and inter-sweep jumpiness on `pp2048 (c1)`), on a stack that PLE-CPU-offloads via UVA — i.e. exactly the path #56512 rewires. Benchmark: llama-benchy 0.4.0, identical command per build: `--pp 2048 --tg 128 --depth 0 8192 32768 131072 --concurrency 1 4 --runs 3 --latency-mode generation --enable-prefix-caching` | row (`t/s` mean ± sd) | eed1f3d0 (5 sweeps) | dc36fcce sweep #1 | dc36fcce sweep #2 | |---|---|---|---| | `ctx_tg @ d32768 (c1)` | 127–148, sd ≤ 8.7 | **82.50 ± 46.37** | **95.16 ± 61.63** | | `pp2048 (c1)` | stable | 17203 ± 209 | 12913 ± 53 | | `tg128 (c1)` | 139–169 | 151.63 ± 14.11 | 143.92 ± 8.84 | | `tg128 (c4)` | 354–406 | 408.72 ± 22.92 | 382.54 ± 18.20 | | `ctx_pp @ d131072 (c1)` | ~10003–10400 | 10406.56 ± 1.13 | 10379.13 ± 6.26 | *(good-build column: the V0/V3/V4/V4b/V5 sweeps on eed1f3d0 with this exact config; V1-eager and V2-no-spec sweeps excluded as different configs.)* ### Reproduction Boot the bad build (same command works for the good build by swapping the tag; requires the model checkpoint and a host with ≥60 GiB free RAM for the pinned PLE table): ```sh docker run --gpus all --ipc=host --shm-size=8g \ -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \ vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-dc36fcce902a63eab06c1b93a5c4a5ee178a0c56 \ vllm serve dicksondickson/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4-reshard-mtp-fix \ --quantization modelopt \ --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}' \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.96 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --max-num-seqs 12 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --long-prefill-token-threshold 4096 \ --max-model-len 262144 \ --kv-cache-dtype auto \ --trust-remote-code \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' ``` (Our production launch additionally sets `--enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml --chat-template `; omitted above as irrelevant to decode performance.) Then run, per build, and compare the `ctx_tg @ d32768 (c1)` row between two independent full invocations: ```sh llama-benchy --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 \ --model dicksondickson/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4-reshard-mtp-fix \ --served-model-name qwen-3-8-flash-next \ --pp 2048 --tg 128 --depth 0 8192 32768 131072 --concurrency 1 4 \ --runs 3 --latency-mode generation --enable-prefix-caching ``` Expected: `ctx_tg @ d32768 (c1)` ≈ 127–148 t/s with sd < 10 across runs (as on eed1f3d0). Actual on dc36fcce: one normal run (~145 t/s) plus one-to-two collapsed runs (~40–65 t/s) in every full sweep, mean sd 46–62. The identical command against the good build never collapsed in 5 sweeps. ### Isolation evidence (same bad build, same engine boot) - **Isolated 7-run repro of the sick cell** (`--depth 32768 --concurrency 1 --runs 7`): `ctx_tg @ d32768 = 150.08 ± 7.73` — clean. - **Replay of the sweep prefix** (d8192 c1+c4 then d32768 c1): `146.46 ± 15.60` — clean. - Only the **full sweep sequence** (all four depths, c1+c4, ~14 min sustained) reproduces, in 2/2 attempts. ### Ruled out - **KV pressure / preemption:** zero preemption-related engine log lines during either bad sweep window, and the KV pool (269,228 tokens) is byte-identical to the good build's boot report. - **Engine-visible graph fallback:** no capture/fallback/degrade log lines during either sweep. - **Host interference:** a monitoring-stack (Prometheus+Grafana) container start landed mid-sweep #1, but sweep #2 ran with no other containers active and reproduced identically. No Xid / throttling / OOM entries in `dmesg`/journal. - **#56654 (MRV2 Triton JIT warmup revert):** exonerated by construction — it byte-exactly reverts #56323, whose merge (2026-09-13T00:24) postdates the good base, so migration+revert cancel within the range. ### Prime suspects in the range 1. **#56512 — the prefetch side-stream** (`_prefetch_stream`, `record_stream`/`wait_stream` on per-step lookup tensors). The affected rows are exactly context-load decode (first decode steps after a 32k prefix load = the heaviest prefetch bursts). If the event/stream pattern interacts badly with CUDA-graph replay (e.g. captured graph vs live-event ordering under sustained mixed load), degradation would be silent — which matches: no log lines, no preemptions, only a subset of steps falling back or serializing. 2. **#56682 (dummy-init / CPU engram fill changes)** — alters what gets warmed at startup; possible lazy first-capture/compile during serving. (Less likely: a single one-time event would poison 1 run, not 2 of 3, and isolated short runs would likely also catch it.) ### Asks - Could #56512's maintainers check the prefetch event pattern against CUDA-graph replay and against `cudagraph_capture_sizes`/`FULL` decode-graph modes? Specifically: `record_stream` on inputs captured into a replayed graph, and `wait_stream`/event ordering when the current stream is a replayed graph's stream. - If there's a debug switch (e.g. env to disable prefetch while keeping `cpu_offload`), pointing it out would let me bisect on-host between "#56512 fault" vs "range collateral" within a single boot — happy to run any experiment and post results. - For calibration: the async prefetch measured **no** throughput win on this box (deep-context decode at 131k/c4: 8.45/6.49 t/s vs 6.91 on the good build — within noise), so if this is a known-risky interaction, it currently costs stability without visible benefit on a TP=1 UVA-offload setup. ## Additional context Two full result tables, the isolated-repro table, the prefix-replay table, and engine logs for both bad sweeps are available; I can attach them or provide the exact llama-benchy invocation and per-cell raw JSON (`llama-benchy --save-result`) on request. Host is a single-GPU community box (244 GiB RAM) running this as a daily driver, currently pinned to `nightly-eed1f3d0` and avoiding all nightlies containing #56512 until this resolves. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix] Bill hidden-state extraction at its own KV cache group width
body:
## Purpose

Fix KV-cache admission for `extract_hidden_states` on hybrid Mamba/MLA models. The 1-layer hidden-state group was charged at the width of the widest peer group (e.g. 24 MLA layers), so a ~5.4 GiB extraction cache was billed as ~130 GiB and startup failed.

Fixes #56774.

This is not a duplicate of #53074: that PR isolates hidden-state specs from DeepSeek-V4 MLA/SWA packing. This bug is on the uniform-page-size grouping path used by hybrid Mamba/MLA.

## Details

Hidden-state layers are filtered out of target grouping and appended as a singleton with the common page. The shared pool still sizes every block to `max(group width)`, and admission is `bytes_per_block * total_blocks`. The extraction group needs many blocks (small tokens/block), so it pays for unused MLA slots on every block.

Changing only the admission formula would still allocate overlay blocks at that wide width. When a hidden-state group is appended, split every group to one layer so the pool width is one page and extraction is billed at its own width. This only runs with `extract_hidden_states`; models without a hidden-state cache keep the original grouping. The block-outermost packed path is unchanged.

Merged latest `main` (2026-10-19). `get_kv_cache_groups` now lives in `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_planning.py` (#61183), so the split and its regression test moved there (`tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py`), adapted to the new `_pool_bytes_per_block(vllm_config, groups)` / `_max_memory_usage_bytes_from_groups(builder, ...)` signatures. `#50894`'s `_ensure_min_page_size` (TP page scaling for hidden-state extraction) is kept.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py -k hidden_state -v
ruff check / ruff format --check (v0.14.0) on the two changed files
```

## Test Result

After merging current `main` (CPU-only box):

- `test_hidden_state_extraction_group_billed_at_own_width` passed; with the split call disabled it fails (hidden-state group stays merged with the wide groups)
- `test_hidden_state_group_preserves_hybrid_prefix_cache_granularity` passed
- `test_hidden_states_with_tp_scales_page_size` passed (`#50894` TP page scaling still holds after the split)
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on both files
- Across `test_kv_cache_planning.py`, `test_kv_cache_utils.py`, `test_contiguous_kv_packing.py` and `test_kv_cache_config_builder.py`, the set of failures on this CPU-only machine (device-type inference without a GPU) is identical with and without this change, apart from the new regression test

No model eval: this is KV admission/grouping math only; generated tokens are unchanged.

AI assistance was used to investigate the grouping/admission path and implement this change. Every changed line has been reviewed by the human submitter. The targeted behavior is covered by a CPU unit test of the bytes-per-block and admission math.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Synchronize adaptive DSpark decisions across TP ranks
body:
## Purpose

Adaptive DSpark derives its verification budget from rank-local confidence state. Small differences across TP ranks can therefore produce different total budgets or per-request boundaries, causing divergent execution layouts and possible collective hangs.

This change makes rank 0 authoritative for both values:

- broadcast the selected draft budget;
- broadcast partial-allocation capacities before building request boundaries.

The adaptive policy remains enabled and unchanged. Related to #54011. I found no open PR implementing this TP-consensus fix.

## Test Plan

- Unit coverage for TP1/2/4/8 with deliberately different rank-local confidences.
- Real NCCL TP2 and TP4 tests on H100s with Qwen3-4B and the official `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7` draft.
- Natural adaptive rank tracing, GSM8K correctness, and concurrency-128 serving stress.

## Test Result

- `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py -q`: 33 passed in the CUDA validation environment.
- `pre-commit run --files ...`: passed all applicable hooks.
- Injected rank drift: original code produced 20 consensus mismatches at both TP2 and TP4; patched code produced 0. Each run covered 120 compiled allocation cases and CUDA-graph boundary replays.
- Natural adaptive execution remained active: TP2 had 568 partial-budget steps; TP4 had 559. Budget and request-boundary traces matched exactly across all ranks.
- Patched TP2 and TP4 each completed 2,304/2,304 requests at observed concurrency 128 with no request failures or hangs.
- GSM8K completed all 1,319 samples with no invalid or empty responses. TP2: 86.20% original vs 86.43% patched; TP4: 85.75% vs 85.44% (net -4 answers, treated as finite-sample variation rather than equivalence proof).

The original issue's TP8/H20/DeepSeek-V4 environment was not available for end-to-end validation.

@LucasWilkinson @benchislett @zihanlin-ai @DingYinfan — would appreciate your review, especially of the TP-consensus boundary. Thanks!

AI assistance was used for test orchestration and review; I reviewed the changes and validation results.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Fuse DeepSeek V4 MXFP4 indexer K production and cache insertion (gfx950)
body:
## Scope Adds opt-in AITER FlyDSL paged MXFP4 indexing for DeepSeek V4 on ROCm gfx950. **The key distinction from #60834 is the fused K-production path:** this PR fuses **pooling, RMSNorm, RoPE, MXFP4 quantization, and cache insertion into a single kernel**, writing directly to the paged MXFP4 indexer cache. In contrast, #60834 first writes pooled K to a BF16 scratch buffer, then calls `k_norm_rope_mxfp4_cache`. This fused path avoids that intermediate BF16 buffer and the extra kernel launch. Select with: ```bash --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}' ``` FP8 remains the default. If the installed AITER does not expose the required stride-capable FP4 scorer APIs, vLLM warns and falls back to FP8. Supported ROCm configuration: - gfx950 - C4 compression - 64 query heads, head dimension 128 - 64-token compressed cache pages - DCP=PCP=1 This PR changes only the sparse indexer's Q/K cache precision and scorer path. It does not change model/MoE weights or the main attention KV cache. ## Implementation - The fused ROCm K producer writes packed E2M1 values and UE8M0 scales directly in the AITER preshuffled page layout. - The fused Q producer emits packed Q plus AITER's scale swizzle. - The cache adapter creates zero-copy value/scale views over vLLM's shared allocation. - Prefill and decode dispatch directly to AITER's paged FP4 scorers. - Folded index weights are rounded to BF16 for the AITER scorer contract. - Speculative rows are flattened before C4 length conversion. - Unsupported architectures, shapes and context-parallel configurations fail explicitly. The shared-pool page-stride and 64-bit address support is provided by ROCm/aiter#5518. ## Platform isolation The AITER path is selected only under `current_platform.is_rocm()`. - NVIDIA retains the existing DeepGEMM/CuTeDSL implementation. - CUDA FP4 packing and scale layout are unchanged. - FP8 remains the default on every platform. - ROCm-only packing uses a separate `_fp32x2_to_fp4x2_rocm` path. ## Tests Added focused host contract tests: - `tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_fp4_dispatch.py` - default/auto/explicit FP8 remains unchanged - gfx950 and DCP/PCP gates - missing-AITER fallback - NVIDIA SM100-family gate without probing AITER - `tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_dispatch.py` - existing FP8 dispatch and output dtype - ROCm FP4 packed-Q/scale shapes - unsupported ROCm shape rejection - existing NVIDIA Triton/CuTeDSL routing and scale views ```bash python -m pytest -q \ tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_fp4_dispatch.py \ tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_dispatch.py ``` Result: **35 passed**. These are host dispatch/layout tests; they are not NVIDIA GPU numerical validation. AITER scorer validation is in ROCm/aiter#5518 and covers: - exact FP4-dequant reference agreement (`cos=1.000000`) - direct FP4-vs-FP8 and both paths vs BF16 - random nonuniform Q/K and scales - shuffled physical pages and padded block-table strides - nonzero storage offsets - 2 GiB, 4 GiB and 4.608 GB physical offsets - ragged, tail, nonzero and empty windows - prefill and decode graph replay - deliberate page-map and scale-permutation sensitivity checks ## Decode schedule reuse The final commit preallocates a graph-stable FP4 CTA schedule buffer in the indexer metadata builder. The builder refreshes the schedule once per decode step; all sparse-indexer layers consume the same `cta_info` and `total_ctas`. The 512-CTA floor is unchanged. This does not change cache format, scorer math, top-k, BF16 weight handling, or NVIDIA paths. Validation: - focused host dispatch/schedule tests: **36 passed**; - AITER strided decode eager + graph replay: **PASS**; - historical isolated AgentX ablation: FP4 40.397M -> FP4+schedule 40.793M tokens/$, **+0.98% relative to FP4** and +3.66% vs the 39.354M baseline. The historical schedule result is one full3600 run and is superseded by the 2026-09-23 AgentX A/B below, which was measured with every commit of this PR present in both arms. ## Results All numbers in this section were re-measured on **2026-09-23** with the current PR head. They supersede the earlier serving tables, which are kept at the bottom for history. Common setup for every arm below: - Single node, 8 x MI355X (gfx950), ROCm nightly image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-0bfc7a15d095fe83ecc82b50561a93c177fece2d` - `DeepSeek-V4-Pro` snapshot `b5968e9190ef611bbf34a7229255be88a0e937c1`, FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache - vLLM overlay at `db7aa888e3`, AITER overlay carrying [ROCm/aiter#5603](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5603) + [ROCm/aiter#5518](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5518) - **Both arms** mount the AITER [ROCm/aiter#5603](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5603) FP8 split-k `fp8_mqa_logits` overlay, so the baseline is FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603 and the reported delta is attributable to FP4 indexing alone, not to ROCm/aiter#5603. - The MXFP4 arm additionally mounts this PR's five vLLM indexer files and AITER's three FlyDSL `pa_mqa_logits_fp4*` kernels, and sets `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}'`. Everything else - image, weights, serve flags, client, seed - is byte-identical. ### AgentX agentic-coding replay, TP1/DP8, concurrency 128 The primary end-to-end result. DP attention, MTP speculative decoding (3 tokens, synthetic acceptance 2.49), prefix caching enabled, full + piecewise CUDA graphs, 3,600 s measured window per arm after a 1,422-request warmup. Workload is the 393-entry `semianalysisai/cc-traces-weka-062126` shared-prefix coding trace. One run per arm. | Metric | FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603 | MXFP4 (this PR) | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Total throughput, tok/s | 137,450 | 150,709 | **+9.65%** | | Input throughput, tok/s | 136,277 | 149,423 | **+9.65%** | | Output throughput, tok/s | 1,174 | 1,286 | **+9.59%** | | Per-GPU throughput, tok/s | 17,181 | 18,839 | **+9.65%** | | Requests profiled | 5,506 | 5,948 | **+8.03%** | | Errors | 0 | 0 | - | | Measured duration, s | 3628.3 | 3629.6 | +0.04% | | Latency | FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603 | MXFP4 (this PR) | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | TTFT mean | 5,493.05 ms | 4,562.79 ms | **-16.94%** | | TTFT p50 | 2,896.13 ms | 2,614.69 ms | **-9.72%** | | TTFT p90 | 10,802.88 ms | 8,984.89 ms | **-16.83%** | | TTFT p95 | 15,963.95 ms | 14,005.84 ms | **-12.27%** | | E2E mean | 111.09 s | 95.03 s | **-14.46%** | | E2E p50 | 58.16 s | 49.57 s | **-14.77%** | | E2E p90 | 242.64 s | 209.55 s | **-13.64%** | | E2E p95 | 375.87 s | 315.21 s | **-16.14%** | | ITL/TPOT mean | 142.59 ms | 119.03 ms | **-16.52%** | | ITL/TPOT p50 | 125.44 ms | 108.11 ms | **-13.82%** | | ITL/TPOT p90 | 221.58 ms | 179.90 ms | **-18.81%** | | ITL/TPOT p95 | 289.97 ms | 218.43 ms | **-24.67%** | | Interactivity p50, tok/s | 7.97 | 9.25 | **+16.02%** | | Interactivity p95, tok/s | 3.45 | 4.58 | **+32.76%** | | Cache / KV | FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603 | MXFP4 (this PR) | |---|---:|---:| | Trace theoretical prefix-cache hit | 95.38% | 95.51% | | Server prefix-cache hit | 89.77% | 90.29% | | GPU KV-cache usage | 64.12% | 50.47% | | ISL p50 / p90, tokens | 56,846 / 197,988 | 59,382 / 202,331 | | OSL p50 / p90, tokens | 392 / 1,639 | 393 / 1,652 | Three points worth calling out: 1. The gain is larger at the tail than at the median: p95 ITL improves 24.7% and p95 interactivity 32.8%, versus 13.8%/16.0% at p50. Long-context agentic requests are exactly where the indexer dominates. 2. GPU KV-cache usage drops from 64.12% to 50.47%. Storing indexer K/scales in MXFP4 frees KV pool, which is what lets the MXFP4 arm admit 8.03% more requests in the same wall-clock window. 3. Prefix-cache hit rate is effectively identical (89.77% vs 90.29%, against a 95.38%/95.51% trace-theoretical ceiling), so the throughput delta is not a cache-luck artifact. ### Kernel-level attribution Torch profiler capture of 4 engine iterations per arm, rank 0, same serve shape for both (TP8/DP1, `max_model_len` 10,240, `max_num_seqs` 64, prefix caching off, no MTP), same seeded synthetic client (ISL 8,000 / OSL 2,000, concurrency 64). Captured steps are mixed chunked-prefill + decode (2 context requests of ~8,135 tokens plus 54-59 generation requests per step) and are composition-matched across arms. | Indexer kernel group | FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603, us | MXFP4 (this PR), us | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | mqa_logits scorer | 10,873.4 | 8,661.4 | **-20.34%** | | top-k selection | 12,169.6 | 9,019.5 | **-25.89%** | | KV compress + quant insert | 1,951.5 | 1,979.1 | **+1.41%** | | indexer quant-cache gather | 681.3 | 0.0 | removed | | FP4 prefill planning (new) | 0.0 | 290.6 | new | | | | | | | **Indexer path total** | **25,675.8** | **19,950.5** | **-22.30%** | | Shared (non-indexer) kernels | 1,220,442.9 | 1,216,620.0 | -0.31% | | All GPU kernels | 1,246,118.7 | 1,236,570.4 | -0.77% | Per engine step the indexer path costs 6,418.9 us on FP8 and 4,987.6 us on MXFP4, i.e. -1,431.3 us saved per step (-22.3%). The indexer is 2.1% of rank-0 GPU kernel time on FP8 and 1.6% on MXFP4. The saving splits roughly evenly between the two things this PR changes: the paged FP4 scorer replaces the gluon FP8 scorer plus its preshuffle (-20.34%), and the vLLM per-row top-k replaces AITER's radix top-k plus the prefill localisation pass (-25.89%). The FP8 path's separate `_cp_gather_indexer_quant_cache` kernel disappears entirely, and the new FP4 prefill-planning kernels run once per step for 290.6 us total, which is noise against the 5.7 ms saved. Note the scope difference: at this short-context shape the indexer is only 2.1% of GPU kernel time, so a 22.3% indexer saving is just -0.77% of total kernel time. That is consistent with, not contradictory to, the +9.65% AgentX result, where mean ISL is ~57K instead of 8K and the freed KV pool also raises the admitted batch. The trace establishes the mechanism; the AgentX table establishes the magnitude. ### Fixed 8,192-token input / 1,024-token output, TP8 Two A/Bs are reported here because they answer different questions, and the difference is entirely in **what the FP8 arm contains**. Serve configuration is identical in both: TP8/DP1, `max_model_len` 10240, `max_num_seqs` 64, `max_num_batched_tokens` 8192, `gpu_memory_utilization` 0.86, prefix caching disabled, no MTP. Client is identical too: fixed ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, `--random-range-ratio 0`, `num_prompts = 4 x concurrency`, `--request-rate inf`, `--ignore-eos --seed 42`, warmup excluded from the timed interval. #### (a) Whole-PR A/B: stock vLLM vs this PR The FP8 arm is the **unmodified vLLM from the nightly image** with only the AITER [ROCm/aiter#5603](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5603) `fp8_mqa_logits` overlay applied. It carries no part of this PR. This measures what merging the PR is worth, and uses the same baseline definition as the AgentX A/B above. | C | Metric | FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603 (stock vLLM) | MXFP4 (this PR) | Change | |---:|---|---:|---:|---:| | 16 | Output tok/s | 728.81 | 770.98 | **+5.79%** | | 16 | Total tok/s | 6,559.28 | 6,938.84 | **+5.79%** | | 16 | Mean TTFT ms | 1,781.45 | 1,683.61 | **-5.49%** | | 16 | Mean TPOT ms | 20.20 | 19.10 | **-5.47%** | | 16 | Median TPOT ms | 20.44 | 19.32 | **-5.48%** | | 64 | Output tok/s | 1,444.57 | 1,544.26 | **+6.90%** | | 64 | Total tok/s | 13,001.16 | 13,898.37 | **+6.90%** | | 64 | Mean TTFT ms | 4,155.55 | 3,931.95 | **-5.38%** | | 64 | Mean TPOT ms | 40.14 | 37.51 | **-6.55%** | | 64 | Median TPOT ms | 41.90 | 39.30 | **-6.22%** | All requests completed with zero failures in both arms (64/64 at C16, 256/256 at C64). One run per cell. #### (b) Dtype-only A/B: same PR code, `fp8` vs `mxfp4` Measured earlier on the Sep-10 nightly image. Here **both** arms run a vLLM tree that already contains this PR; the FP8 arm is the PR ported to that nightly and launched with `indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`. It therefore isolates the cache-dtype and scorer switch while holding the surrounding PR code fixed, and is the stricter of the two comparisons. | C | Metric | FP8 (PR code, fp8 dtype) | MXFP4 (PR code, mxfp4 dtype) | Change | |---:|---|---:|---:|---:| | 16 | Output tok/s | 694.81 | 700.04 | **+0.75%** | | 16 | Total tok/s | 6,253.32 | 6,300.33 | **+0.75%** | | 16 | Mean TTFT ms | 1,917.70 | 1,891.14 | **-1.39%** | | 16 | Mean TPOT ms | 21.15 | 21.00 | **-0.69%** | | 64 | Output tok/s | 1,371.40 | 1,406.04 | **+2.53%** | | 64 | Total tok/s | 12,342.63 | 12,654.40 | **+2.53%** | | 64 | Mean TTFT ms | 4,126.00 | 4,015.88 | **-2.67%** | | 64 | Mean TPOT ms | 42.53 | 41.49 | **-2.44%** | #### Why the two differ The gap between +0.75%/+2.53% and +5.79%/+6.90% is a baseline-composition difference, not a change in the PR's effect: - In (b) the FP8 arm already carries this PR's indexer restructuring (schedule reuse, prefill planning, the reworked `fused_indexer_q`), so those gains are present on both sides and cancel. Only the dtype/scorer switch is left. - In (a) the FP8 arm has none of it, so the measured delta includes the whole change set. - The two runs also used different nightly images, which moved both arms: the FP8 arm alone went from 694.81 to 728.81 tok/s at C16 between them. Absolute values are therefore not comparable across the two tables, only the within-run deltas are. Both comparisons agree on direction and on the trend with concurrency. ### Accuracy GSM8K, 1,319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, `max_tokens=2048`. Three independent runs per arm on the same servers as above. | Arm | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 | Mean | Output tokens (mean) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603 | 0.9454 | 0.9462 | 0.9492 | **0.9469** | 120,259 | | MXFP4 (this PR) | 0.9447 | 0.9492 | 0.9492 | **0.9477** | 120,160 | Mean accuracy difference is **+0.0008** in favour of MXFP4, well inside the 0.9447-0.9492 spread seen across repeats of either arm. Both arms produce the same number of output tokens to within 0.1%. FP4 indexing remains accuracy-neutral on GSM8K. ## AITER indexer micro-benchmark MI355X/gfx950, H=64, D=128, page=64. Three independent seeds per shape; 10 warmups and 50 timed iterations per repetition; medians shown. FP8 total is the existing two-stage paged gather + FP8 logits path. FP4 is the direct-paged scorer. | Shape | B | Query rows/request | Context | FP4 us | FP8 total us | FP8 / FP4 | FP4 vs BF16 cos | FP8 vs BF16 cos | FP4 vs FP8 cos | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Small | 1 | 32 | 2,048 | 4.86 | 20.65 | **4.24x** | 0.987927 | 0.999334 | 0.986520 | | Medium | 4 | 64 | 2,048 | 8.65 | 23.08 | **2.67x** | 0.987752 | 0.999327 | 0.986317 | | Long | 4 | 64 | 8,192 | 21.91 | 63.15 | **2.88x** | 0.987072 | 0.999290 | 0.985555 | | Very long | 8 | 16 | 32,768 | 38.82 | 201.39 | **5.19x** | 0.987316 | 0.999299 | 0.985813 | These are AITER indexer micro-benchmarks, not vLLM server latency. See ROCm/aiter#5518 for commands and full correctness coverage. ## Validation gaps - The AgentX A/B is one run per arm. The two arms ran back to back on an otherwise idle host with identical flags and seed, and completed 5,506 and 5,948 requests with zero errors, but run-to-run variance is not characterised. - GSM8K was repeated three times per arm; the fixed 8K/1K serving cells were run once per arm. - The kernel trace is a mixed prefill+decode step at 8K context, not a pure decode step at AgentX context length. - Router load across the 8 DP ranks was uneven in both arms (prompt tokens ranged 66.1M-118.3M per engine under `consistent_hash`). This inflates tail latency symmetrically and is unrelated to this PR. - NVIDIA GPU numerical tests were not run on this ROCm host. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used at the author's request. Human review remains required before marking ready. Signed-off-by: LiuYinfeng01
Superseded earlier measurements (pre-2026-09-23, kept for history) ## vLLM serving benchmark: fair old-checkpoint A/B Re-measured on the exact old `DeepSeek-V4-Pro` snapshot `b5968e9190ef611bbf34a7229255be88a0e937c1`, single-node 8 x MI355X, TP8/DP1, fixed 8,192-token input and 1,024-token output, request-rate `inf`, and concurrency 1/4/16/64. Prefix caching is disabled. Each measured concurrency is preceded by a full unmeasured request wave using a different random seed, so prompt reuse and first-shape JIT compilation are outside the timed interval. Both arms use the Sep-10 nightly stack and differ only in `indexer_kv_dtype=fp8|mxfp4`. Another user's SGLang service occupied about 46% of each GPU during this run, so both arms used `gpu-memory-utilization=0.50`. This changes absolute throughput versus an idle host but is symmetric across the A/B arms. All requests completed with zero failures, and the MXFP4 log confirms `Using MXFP4 indexer cache for Lightning Indexer`. | Concurrency | FP8 output tok/s | MXFP4 output tok/s | Throughput change | FP8 TPOT | MXFP4 TPOT | TPOT change | FP8 TTFT | MXFP4 TTFT | TTFT change | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 70.06 | 68.98 | -1.54% | 13.91 ms | 14.14 ms | +1.60% | 383.64 ms | 383.68 ms | +0.01% | | 4 | 240.71 | 237.26 | -1.43% | 15.62 ms | 15.86 ms | +1.53% | 1027.18 ms | 1030.44 ms | +0.32% | | 16 | 701.37 | 694.48 | -0.98% | 20.86 ms | 21.09 ms | +1.09% | 1991.73 ms | 1989.60 ms | **-0.11%** | | 64 | 1408.45 | 1420.83 | **+0.88%** | 41.26 ms | 40.87 ms | **-0.96%** | 4173.31 ms | 4170.87 ms | **-0.06%** | On the old checkpoint's TP8 service path, MXFP4 remains approximately neutral: low concurrency regresses throughput/TPOT by about 1%-1.6%, while C64 crosses over to **+0.88% output throughput** and **-0.96% mean TPOT**. TTFT is flat. This matches the isolated scorer's local-batch crossover and supersedes the previous prefix-cache-enabled TP8 8K/1K table. ### Accuracy Same nightly stack and servers, GSM8K 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, seed 42, concurrency 64, `max_tokens=2048`. | Arm | Accuracy | Invalid responses | Output tokens | |---|---:|---:|---:| | FP8 baseline | 0.9484 | 0.000 | 119,898 | | This PR (MXFP4) | 0.9484 | 0.000 | 119,575 | FP4 indexing is accuracy-neutral on GSM8K: identical accuracy, no invalid responses in either arm. The same nightly stack was also measured with **TP1/DP8** attention (one engine per GPU), prefix caching enabled, no MTP, identical flags across arms. One warmup wave and four measured waves per concurrency. All requests completed; zero failures. Fixed 8,192-token input / 1,024-token output: | Concurrency | FP8 output tok/s | FP4 output tok/s | Change | FP8 TTFT ms | FP4 TTFT ms | Change | FP8 TPOT ms | FP4 TPOT ms | Change | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 40.99 | 41.14 | **0.37% ↑** | 1272.34 | 1274.07 | 0.14% ↑ | 23.18 | 23.09 | **0.40% ↓** | | 4 | 128.07 | 143.83 | **12.30% ↑** | 2173.05 | 2104.56 | **3.15% ↓** | 29.13 | 25.78 | **11.52% ↓** | | 16 | 412.47 | 483.54 | **17.23% ↑** | 3919.93 | 4134.51 | 5.47% ↑ | 34.98 | 29.07 | **16.91% ↓** | | 64 | 1274.52 | 1277.74 | **0.25% ↑** | 7356.77 | 7735.81 | 5.15% ↑ | 43.04 | 42.55 | **1.14% ↓** | Under DP8 the same 8k1k workload becomes a gain: C4 and C16 improve output throughput by 12.30% and 17.23% with 11.52%/16.91% lower TPOT, while C1 and C64 are flat. Per-GPU decode batch, not service concurrency, drives this: DP8 gives each rank its own batch and KV pool. Fixed 131,072-token input / 1,024-token output, same TP1/DP8 stack: | Concurrency | FP8 output tok/s | FP4 output tok/s | Change | FP8 TTFT ms | FP4 TTFT ms | Change | FP8 TPOT ms | FP4 TPOT ms | Change | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 21.04 | 20.94 | 0.44% ↓ | 24967.88 | 24517.07 | **1.81% ↓** | 23.18 | 23.83 | 2.82% ↑ | | 4 | 70.16 | 73.75 | **5.11% ↑** | 19716.25 | 19515.48 | **1.02% ↓** | 37.72 | 35.15 | **6.79% ↓** | | 16 | 129.69 | 121.04 | 6.67% ↓ | 50244.40 | 47654.64 | **5.15% ↓** | 74.25 | 85.57 | 15.25% ↑ | | 64 | 190.99 | 179.52 | 6.01% ↓ | 81471.37 | 81494.17 | 0.03% ↑ | 255.31 | 276.60 | 8.34% ↑ | At 128K the picture is mixed and does not reproduce the earlier archived-overlay long-context result: FP4 improves TTFT at every concurrency except C64 (where it is flat) and improves C4 throughput/TPOT, but regresses decode throughput and TPOT at C16/C64. At this context length each request occupies a large share of the per-rank KV pool, so admitted batches stay small and scheduling/queueing dominates; the isolated scorer advantage at large local batch is not reached. Each cell is one run per arm. ### Decode scheduling analysis There is no serving-concurrency or C64 branch in this PR. Cache and table strides come from the tensors. The only fixed scheduling choice is the same decode floor used by ATOM: `parallel_unit_num=max(512, rows)` with `block_k=256`. At 128K maximum context, isolated scorer results with 512 CTA are: B1 0.87x, B2 1.02x, B4 1.49x, B8 1.73x, B16 1.81x and B64 2.37x (FP8 latency divided by FP4 latency). This explains the serving crossover: TP1/DP8 service concurrency 64 is roughly local batch 8, while C1/C4 leaves most ranks at local batch 0-1. A 128/256/512 CTA sweep found 256 CTA can recover B1/128K to parity, but B4+ prefers 512 and short-context low-batch optima differ. Auto-grid is slower at larger batches. No context/batch heuristic is included: selecting from GPU lengths must not introduce a host synchronization, and the measured table does not justify a stable rule across context, batch, MTP and graph buckets. ## Historical end-to-end result Prior single-node 8x MI355X AgentX full3600 ablation; only the archived FP4 indexer overlay/env arm differed. This was one run per arm. | Arm | Total tok/s | tokens/$ | P90 interactivity | Output tok/s | Completed | Errors | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | FP8 baseline | 131180.83056 | 39354249.168 | 14.02075 | 1019.04494 | 4052 | 0 | | FP4 indexer | 134658.15928 | 40397447.784 | 14.07660 | 1080.84186 | 4158 | 0 | Historical throughput/TCO: **+2.65%**. Input throughput: **+2.62%**; output throughput: **+6.06%**; mean TTFT: **-3.69%**; mean TPOT: **-2.71%**; completed requests: **+2.62%**. The FP4 arm also had a 17.66% larger reported KV pool (61.3M vs 52.1M tokens), while both arms saw about 92.3% measured prefix-cache hit rate. AgentX prompts were much longer than fixed 8k1k (mean 116.6K, p90 251K tokens) and came from a 393-entry shared-prefix coding trace. Those conditions can benefit from smaller indexer storage and long-context prefill; fixed random 8k1k has no prefix reuse. Output TPS is additionally affected by different realized output lengths (943 vs 913 mean tokens). With one run per arm (`single_run_warning=true`), the +2.65% remains suggestive, not a stable reproduction. ## Validation gaps - All four serving matrices (TP8 8k1k, DP8 8k1k, DP8 128k1k) were run once per arm; repeat runs are needed for variance, especially the DP8 128k cells. - The DP8 128k result disagrees with an earlier archived-overlay 128k run that showed C16/C64 gains; only the nightly-stack numbers above are reported as current-PR evidence. - NVIDIA GPU numerical tests were not run on this ROCm host. - Historical AgentX, fixed-length serving and AITER micro-benchmarks measure different scopes and are reported separately. ## AITER [ROCm/aiter#5603](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5603) and FP4 prefill-planning follow-up Runtime: old `DeepSeek-V4-Pro` snapshot `b5968e9190ef611bbf34a7229255be88a0e937c1`, 8x MI355X TP8, ROCm 10 Sep-10 nightly `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm@sha256:72e90adf360ccffb231a098a15eadfb808719c029c6cd43f6386095064552b7e` (vLLM `2a02f6efe3`), AITER [ROCm/aiter#5603](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5603) split-k plus ROCm/aiter#5518 stride/rebase APIs. The additional prefill-planning commit plans direct-paged FP4 chunks by `rows * max(request context)` rather than the gathered-FP8 `rows * sum(request contexts)` workspace. It also computes ragged windows and the FP4 CTA schedule once in metadata instead of once per indexer layer. ### Kernel profile On one 16-request mixed-context prefill (56,064 prompt tokens): | Metric per TP rank | Existing FP4 | New planner | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | FP4 scorer launches | 60 | 30 | **-50.0%** | | FP4 scorer device time, max rank | 2.383 ms | 1.910 ms | **-19.9%** | | Window + row-plan + CTA-info launches | 180 | 6 | **-96.7%** | | Window + row-plan + CTA-info time, max rank | 2.230 ms | 0.083 ms | **-96.3%** | | Combined scorer + planning time | 4.613 ms | 1.993 ms | **-56.8%** | A first HTTP experiment incorrectly sent 16 separate requests with prefix caching enabled. Its apparent 18.30% wall-time improvement was a scheduler/cache artifact and is excluded. The corrected experiment sends one completion request containing all 16 token-ID prompts, disables prefix caching, and performs a shape-identical warmup. Median wall times were 2317.98 ms for FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603, 2320.69 ms for existing FP4, and 2326.11 ms for the new planner: all within 0.35%, i.e. no measurable end-to-end difference in this sample. The traces explain why kernel and wall-time results differ. The scheduler still split the logical request into 8-9 `execute_context` steps with different token buckets between arms. FP4 reduces indexer work, but the saved few milliseconds are diluted by roughly 2.3 seconds of model/MoE/attention execution. Therefore the kernel result is valid, while the earlier 18.30% wall-time attribution was not. ### Fixed 8K/1K service increment Two runs per FP4 arm; medians shown. FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603 was measured once as the current baseline. All requests completed with zero failures. | C | Metric | FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603 | Existing FP4 | New FP4 | New vs existing FP4 | New vs FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603 | |---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 16 | Output tok/s | 689.14 | 674.83 | 681.62 | **+1.01%** | -1.21% | | 16 | Mean TTFT ms | 2040.03 | 2273.73 | 2226.27 | **-2.09%** | +9.00% | | 16 | Mean TPOT ms | 21.22 | 21.48 | 21.29 | **-0.89%** | +0.50% | | 64 | Output tok/s | 1527.11 | 1550.19 | 1552.95 | **+0.18%** | **+1.78%** | | 64 | Mean TTFT ms | 3960.79 | 4070.55 | 3988.94 | **-2.00%** | +0.71% | | 64 | Mean TPOT ms | 37.93 | 37.20 | 37.21 | +0.02% | **-1.91%** | The new planner therefore improves the mixed-context prefill path materially and adds a small, repeatable C16 fixed-load gain. C64 throughput is effectively flat versus existing FP4; the FP4 stack remains about 1.8% faster than FP8 + ROCm/aiter#5603 at C64. The fixed 8K prefill shapes selected `num_kv_splits=1`; therefore these service rows use the ROCm/aiter#5603 source but do not exercise split-K. AITER [ROCm/aiter#5603](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5603) is not uniformly faster on this Triton build: exact source-only tests found one tested prefill shape improved while five were flat or slower. FP8 old/split logits, masks and top-k indices were bitwise identical; all 152 ROCm/aiter#5603 tests passed. ### Three-arm accuracy GSM8K, all 1,319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, seed 42, concurrency 64: | Arm | Correct | Accuracy | Invalid | |---|---:|---:|---:| | FP8 + AITER [ROCm/aiter#5603](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5603) | 1254 / 1319 | 0.950720 | 0 | | Existing FP4 (`bd2f8acf`) | 1254 / 1319 | 0.950720 | 0 | | New FP4 prefill planner | 1254 / 1319 | 0.950720 | 0 | The prefill-planning change is accuracy-neutral on the full evaluation.

title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4.1 on sm_120 (RTX PRO 2000 Blackwell): no FlashInfer SM120 sparse-MLA kernel for (num_heads=64, topk=1152); FlashMLA sparse is SM90a/SM100f only
body:
### Your current environment
vLLM 0.29.1rc1.dev9+g2671fedfc (`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-2671fedf…`, torch 2.13.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1), NVIDIA RTX PRO 2000 Blackwell 16 GB (compute capability 12.0, sm_120), driver 595.84, x86_64.

### 🐛 Describe the bug
`DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` cannot start on an sm_120 GPU: the FlashInfer SM120 sparse-MLA path has no kernel for the V4.1 decode shape, and the FlashMLA alternative is SM90a/SM100f only.

Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (EXL3 routed experts via the `vllm-exl3` plugin, non-routed weights delegated to `deepseek_v4_fp8`, experts/Engram in pinned host memory via UVA). The model loads, profiling runs, KV cache is allocated (0.99 GiB / 110,964 tokens), JIT warmup finishes, then the FlashInfer warmup fails:

```
INFO [flashinfer_sparse_mla_warmup.py:267] Warming up DeepSeek V4 sparse MLA attention for mixed tokens=16.
...
  File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py", line 895, in _forward_prefill
    flashinfer_trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4(
  File ".../flashinfer/mla/_sparse_mla_sm120.py", line 394, in _paged_attention
ValueError: SM120 sparse-MLA has no decode kernel for this shape: num_tokens=16, num_heads=64, topk=1152, d_qk=512, page_block_size=32, model_type=1, extra_topk=0. Supported decode shapes are enumerated in _DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH and _DECODE_DSV3_2_DISPATCH.
```

FlashInfer's DSV4 SM120 table only instantiates topk ∈ {128, 192, 256, 512, 1024} (`_DECODE_DSV4_TOPKS` on FlashInfer main as well); V4.1 asks for 1152.

With `--attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` (same model, same host) the load also completes and then fails:

```
RuntimeError: sparse_attn_prefill_interface, .../flashmla-src/csrc/api/sparse_fwd.h:116, Sparse Attention Forward Kernel is only supported on SM90a and SM100f architectures.
```

Additionally, with `--max-num-batched-tokens 512` (instead of 1024) the engine core segfaults deterministically (2/2) right after `Using BLHNC KV cache layout.` at profiling start (Python frames only: `PyObject_Vectorcall` ← `_PyEval_EvalFrameDefault`); with 1024 the profiling forward completes. I could not capture the native frame (no gdb in the image); happy to run a debug build if useful.

Launch (TP1, eager, no speculative decoding, text-only):
```
vllm serve <model> --quantization exl3 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --language-model-only \
  --offload-backend uva --cpu-offload-gb 300 --cpu-offload-params w13_trellis w13_suh w13_svh w2_trellis w2_suh w2_svh \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 --enforce-eager --hf-overrides '{"quantization_config":{...non_routed_quantization: deepseek_v4_fp8 [32,32] ue8m0...}}'
```

Expected: either an sm_120 sparse-MLA kernel covering the V4.1 topk (1152) or a clear, early capability error before the ~10-minute load (the shape is known from the config at startup).

Side observation: under the `deepseek_v4_fp8` delegate, `attn.wo_a` stays bf16 (2.5 GiB for 40 layers) while `wq_b`/`wo_b`/shared experts are fp8; on a 16 GB card that matters.

Reported by YUKI (Lna-Lab / @Tono_Ken3); full logs available.

title: [Bugfix] Apply the mHC input RMSNorm in forward_native
body:
## Purpose

`MHCPreOp` and `MHCFusedPostPreOp` accept `norm_weight` / `norm_eps` and their callers expect a normalized `layer_input`. On `main` the unfused paths disagree about who applies that norm:

| path | applies the norm? |
|---|---|
| `forward_cuda` | yes, inside the fused kernel |
| `forward_hip` with AITER or TileLang | yes, inside the fused kernel |
| `forward_hip` fallback | yes, `_apply_mhc_norm` on top of `forward_native`'s output |
| `forward_native` | **no** — takes both parameters and ignores them |

`CustomOp.forward_oot` falls back to `forward_native`, so every out-of-tree backend loses the normalization. The failure is silent: nothing raises, no NaN appears, the numbers are just wrong.

I hit this running GLM-5.3-Flash on Intel Gaudi 2. All 45 mHC layers lost their input norm; generation degraded to unrelated tokens with a near-uniform logit distribution (top-1 probability 0.99%, top-10 nearly equiprobable), while every per-layer NaN/Inf check stayed clean. @shiweijiezero hit the same thing independently on the MetaX backend.

## Change

`forward_native` of both ops now applies `_apply_mhc_norm` to the mix it returns. The HIP fallback branches, which used to apply it on top of `forward_native`, now return `forward_native`'s result directly — otherwise they would normalize twice. That is the shape `MHCPreDelayedOp.forward_hip` already has. The AITER and TileLang branches are unchanged. (HIP fallback fix suggested by @shiweijiezero.)

Not in scope: `forward_cpu` does not go through `forward_native`; it calls `mhc_pre_cpu`, which also accepts `norm_weight` / `norm_eps` without applying them. Its only in-tree caller today, the DeepSeek-V4 CPU model, passes no norm weight, and I cannot build the CPU kernel to test a change there.

## Test Plan

Two tests in `tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py`, each parametrized over both unfused paths — `forward_native`, and `forward_hip` with AITER and TileLang disabled — for 8 cases in total:

- `test_mhc_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once`
- `test_mhc_fused_post_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once`

Each compares `layer_input` against the `norm_weight=None` mix normalized once by hand, and asserts the two differ *before* comparing, so the test cannot pass vacuously. On the HIP fallback they also check that with `norm_weight=None` every output matches `forward_native` exactly (suggested by @shiweijiezero). Every other mHC test is gated on `HAS_TILELANG_MHC` or AITER, which is why neither unfused path had coverage.

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py -k unfused_applies_norm_once
```

## Test Result

The same 8 tests against three versions of `mhc.py`:

```
main (forward_native skips the norm)
FAILED test_mhc_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once[4-4096-1-native]
FAILED test_mhc_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once[4-4096-8-native]
FAILED test_mhc_fused_post_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once[4-4096-1-native]
FAILED test_mhc_fused_post_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once[4-4096-8-native]
4 failed, 4 passed

first revision of this PR (native norm added, HIP fallback still re-normalizing)
FAILED test_mhc_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once[4-4096-1-hip_fallback]
FAILED test_mhc_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once[4-4096-8-hip_fallback]
FAILED test_mhc_fused_post_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once[4-4096-1-hip_fallback]
FAILED test_mhc_fused_post_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once[4-4096-8-hip_fallback]
4 failed, 4 passed

this PR
8 passed
```

The whole file on this branch, rebased onto `main` @ `2798f668`: `192 passed, 136 skipped` (the skips need TileLang or AITER).

The magnitude of the difference, measured on CPU with GLM-5.3-Flash's shapes (hidden 4096, hc_mult 4, 20 sinkhorn iterations):

```
raw mix    (what forward_native returns) std=0.020015
normalized (what callers expect)         std=1.006403
max abs diff = 3.897   ->  50x in standard deviation
```

End-to-end on Gaudi 2 with GLM-5.3-Flash, greedy decoding, prompt `中国的首都是` ("The capital of China is"):

| | output |
|---|---|
| before | `(e цErrorIdError(e ?以前?aid?Souomeaisaubaub` |
| after | `北京，北京是中国的政治、文化中心，也是中国的` |

Single-token top-1 probability went from 0.99% (`'Å'`) to 43.1% (`'北京'`). That run used the first revision, whose `forward_native` is unchanged since; the review change touches only the HIP fallback, which Gaudi never executes.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on both changed files.

---

*AI disclosure: this change was developed with assistance from Claude (Claude Code). I reviewed every changed line, reproduced the bug and validated the fix end-to-end on real hardware, and ran the tests myself.*
