title: [ROCm][MLA] Add an AITER ASM round-robin decode route for DCP multi-token verify
body:
## Purpose

Adds an opt-in AITER ASM route for decode context parallelism (DCP) combined with speculative decoding on ROCm gfx950.

With DCP, each rank holds a round-robin shard of the KV cache (token `t` on rank `t % dcp_world_size`). A causal verify step of `qlen > 1` cannot run on the ordinary decode kernel, because that kernel applies causality on local indices, which is wrong over a round-robin shard. Today these steps are served by the segmented route (#51705), which expands each verify group into one single-query row per token and runs the Triton decode kernel.

This PR adds the AITER round-robin (`cprr`) ASM decode as an alternative. It keeps the verify group as one row of `qlen` queries and rebuilds each token's global position in-kernel from `g_kv_indptr`, `cp_rank` and `cp_world_size`, so the causal window is applied inside the kernel.

`VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY` selects the route (validated by `env_with_choices`):

- `segmented` (default): existing behavior.
- `asm`: opt-in AITER round-robin ASM decode.

### Per-batch routing

The metadata builder selects exactly one route per decode batch and stores it in the decode metadata:

| route | when |
|---|---|
| PLAIN | `qlen == 1`, or a non-causal block |
| CPRR | causal, `qlen >= 3`, `asm` selected, gfx950, DCP with interleave size 1, speculative decoding |
| SEGMENTED | every other causal `qlen > 1` batch, including `qlen == 2` |

There is no `cprr` kernel below `qlen == 3`, so a `qlen == 2` batch (configured `num_speculative_tokens=1`, or a larger configuration clamped at runtime) uses segmented MLA under `asm` as well. The plain kernel never serves a causal `qlen > 1` batch.

The `cprr` kernels exist only at the native DCP-gathered head counts (16, 32, 64, 128). Other counts are padded up (96 → 128). The output is sliced back as a view; a post-kernel copy would race the symmetric-memory all-to-all combine.

### Non-causal DCP drafts

`supports_non_causal_multi_token_dcp = True` lets a non-causal draft (for example a DSpark draft with `dflash_config.causal = false`) run under DCP. Such a batch takes the PLAIN route: each rank attends its whole local shard without a mask, and the per-row LSE merge across ranks is exact, because non-causal attention needs no cross-shard causal window. This does not depend on `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY` and was validated end to end on the default `segmented` route (below).

### KV split cap (CPRR only)

When CPRR is selected, `max_split_per_batch` is capped at the device CU count. At low batch size, splitting the KV axis is the main source of parallelism; without a cap, AITER's reduction scratch can reach about 9.35 GiB. Scratch sizing, metadata generation, and the kernel launch all use the same cap, so the buffers they share cannot disagree. The default segmented route is unchanged.

## End-to-end validation

Same build, model, and hardware for every row. Only `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY`, `num_speculative_tokens`, and (last row) the draft's causality change.

- 8× MI355X (gfx950), TP8, DCP8, fp8 KV cache
- `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (MXFP4) + `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` draft, probabilistic drafting, block rejection sampling
- Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-dee37d89115db4c94a820a79a78a7828e141c910` (AITER 0.1.21.post1) with this PR's `vllm/envs.py` and `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py` applied

Serve command:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY={asm|segmented} \
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
  --dcp-comm-backend a2a --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors --moe-backend auto \
  --language-model-only --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' \
  --enable-prefix-caching --prefix-cache-retention-interval 12288 \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","max_cudagraph_capture_size":128,"custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated","+situ_and_mul"]}' \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":N,"attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_MLA","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}'
```

### Accuracy: GSM8K

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=16,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,trust_remote_code=True \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5
```

5-shot, all 1319 questions. Standard error is about ±0.005.

| route | `num_speculative_tokens` | strict-match | flexible-extract | acceptance rate | acceptance length |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| asm | 7 | 0.9666 | 0.9659 | 0.418 | 3.92 |
| segmented | 7 | 0.9606 | 0.9606 | 0.418 | 3.93 |
| asm (qlen 2 → segmented fallback) | 1 | 0.9613 | 0.9613 | 0.937 | 1.94 |
| segmented | 1 | 0.9606 | 0.9598 | 0.937 | 1.94 |
| segmented, **non-causal draft** | 7 | 0.9606 | 0.9606 | 0.446 | 4.12 |

All routes are within one standard error, and acceptance is unchanged by the route, as expected: only the target's attention kernel differs.

### Performance: `vllm bench serve`, ISL 100K, OSL 256

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code \
  --dataset-name custom --dataset-path longctx_code_100k.jsonl \
  --custom-output-len 256 --skip-chat-template --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency C --num-prompts max(8, 2*C) --num-warmups 1 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
```

The dataset is 16 distinct prompts of 99.9K–100K tokens of real source code (vLLM's own Python sources), so the draft sees natural text. Random-token prompts give near-zero acceptance and are not meaningful for this comparison. Acceptance comes from the server's `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters, differenced around each run.

`num_speculative_tokens=7` (target verify at qlen 8):

| C | route | output tok/s | mean TPOT ms | p99 TPOT ms | acceptance rate | acceptance length |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | segmented | 21.7 | 22.10 | 27.74 | 0.215 | 2.50 |
| 1 | asm | **28.6** | **10.92** | 14.38 | 0.208 | 2.46 |
| 2 | segmented | 51.1 | 36.05 | 50.16 | 0.186 | 2.30 |
| 2 | asm | **120.2** | **14.56** | 17.03 | 0.169 | 2.18 |
| 4 | segmented | 66.5 | 53.13 | 64.58 | 0.182 | 2.28 |
| 4 | asm | **200.8** | **15.59** | 25.25 | 0.229 | 2.60 |
| 8 | segmented | 36.8 | 179.18 | 312.60 | 0.180 | 2.26 |
| 8 | asm | **57.9** | **110.10** | 223.37 | 0.183 | 2.28 |

Mean TPOT improves 2.0× at batch 1, 2.5× at C=2, 3.4× at C=4 and 1.6× at C=8. At C=1 the output throughput gain is smaller than the TPOT gain because each 256-token request also pays a ~6 s 100K-token prefill. At C=8 both routes' TPOT includes decode steps that share the batch with other requests' 100K-token chunked prefills.

`num_speculative_tokens=1` (every verify step at qlen 2, so `asm` falls back to segmented):

| C | route | output tok/s | mean TPOT ms | acceptance rate |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | asm | 24.4 | 17.00 | 0.650 |
| 1 | segmented | 24.6 | 16.69 | 0.675 |
| 4 | asm | 104.7 | 33.56 | 0.598 |
| 4 | segmented | 106.5 | 32.70 | 0.613 |

The two settings match within noise, as they should when both serve qlen 2 on the segmented kernel.

### Routes actually taken

Counted from the per-batch route in the decode metadata (local instrumentation, not part of this PR):

- `asm`, N=7: target (96 heads) and draft (64 heads) verify batches all on CPRR; PLAIN only for qlen 1 warmup.
- `asm`, N=1: about 6,600 target verify batches at qlen 2 on SEGMENTED, plus a qlen 3 batch on CPRR in the same server, so the mixed CPRR/segmented path runs end to end under `asm`.
- `segmented`, N=7: all verify batches on SEGMENTED.
- `segmented`, non-causal draft: draft batches (qlen 7, non-causal) on PLAIN, target on SEGMENTED.

### ROCm 7.2 nightly

Re-validated on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098` (ROCm 7.2, AITER 0.1.22.post1, which ships the `cprr` kernels) with this PR applied. Same hardware, model, serve command and datasets as above.

| route | `num_speculative_tokens` | GSM8K strict-match | GSM8K flexible-extract | acceptance length (GSM8K) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| asm | 7 | 0.9613 | 0.9613 | 4.34 |
| segmented | 7 | 0.9651 | 0.9651 | 4.37 |
| asm (qlen 2 → segmented fallback) | 1 | 0.9636 | 0.9636 | 1.95 |

| C | route | output tok/s | mean TPOT ms | p99 TPOT ms |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | segmented | 21.2 | 23.23 | 32.44 |
| 1 | asm | **29.3** | **10.26** | 12.32 |
| 4 | segmented | 66.8 | 53.95 | 66.00 |
| 4 | asm | **204.4** | **15.31** | 21.16 |

Accuracy is within one standard error across routes, and mean TPOT improves 2.3× at batch 1 and 3.5× at C=4, consistent with the ROCm 10 results. Under `asm`, all N=7 verify batches took CPRR; at N=1, about 6,000 qlen-2 batches took the segmented fallback.

Note: on this image, Kimi-K3 with a DSpark draft and CUDA graphs fails during startup on either route, independent of this PR. The draft caches its KV-cache pointers during CUDA graph memory profiling, which runs against a throwaway KV cache that is freed before the real one is allocated. These runs include the fix from #58814, which refreshes those pointers when the KV cache is re-bound.

## Test Plan

```bash
# routing and selection (CPU)
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py

# real metadata builder + real ASM kernel (gfx950 + AITER)
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr_numerics.py

# pre-existing AITER MLA split suite
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py

pre-commit run --files vllm/envs.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr_numerics.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py
```

## Test Result

On MI355X (gfx950), images `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098` (ROCm 10) and `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098` (ROCm 7.2), each with this PR applied, with identical results:

| file | result |
|---|---|
| `test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py` | 22 passed |
| `test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py` | 65 passed |
| `test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr_numerics.py` | 4 passed |

`pre-commit` passes on all changed files.

The numerics tests drive the real `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder.build()` and ASM kernel for each of 8 simulated DCP shards at 128 gathered heads (native) and 96 (padded to 128), check each shard against an exact torch reference, check that the LSE merge reproduces full-context attention, and include a positive control: telling the kernel the wrong `cp_rank` must break the result.

**AITER requirement.** Needs an AITER build that ships the round-robin MLA decode kernels (ROCm/aiter#4521).

title: [ROCm][Bugfix][Spec Decode][DCP] Align ranks before DFlash speculator graph capture
body:
## Purpose

**Fixes a boot blocker for decode context parallelism (DCP) combined with speculative decoding: the DFlash/DSpark speculator faults during CUDA graph capture.**

When the DFlash/DSpark draft is **DCP-sharded**, the graph captured by `DFlashSpeculator.capture()` contains a context-parallel collective. Graph capture is only safe when every rank enters it aligned: a rank still finishing earlier work can have its collective recorded into a peer's graph, which faults. Nothing currently quiesces or aligns the ranks before `capture()` runs.

Symptom: every rank dies in `Capturing model for DSpark speculator...` with
`Memory access fault by GPU node-N ... Reason: Unknown`, at a **fresh fault address each time**, with a clean teardown.

**It is a race, not an out-of-bounds access.** The decisive evidence is that booting the same configuration with `AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3 HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` **succeeds**: a configuration that only fails when kernels overlap is a race by construction. The logs show ranks entering `capture()` staggered by ~1 s.

### Why this has not been reported before

The precondition is a **sharded** draft. The replicated draft of #51705 ran at `dcp=1`, so its captured graph contained no collective and there was nothing to race. That changed with **#55472** (merged 2026-09-08), which rebuilds the draft's `ParallelConfig` from the target's and therefore preserves `decode_context_parallel_size`, so a `--decode-context-parallel-size N` run with a DSpark draft now gets a draft at `dcp=N`. The window in which this is reachable upstream is about a week old.

**Reproduction:** multi-rank, `decode_context_parallel_size > 1`, DSpark draft, CUDA graphs enabled. It is a startup race, so it is timing-dependent rather than deterministic; serializing kernel launches masks it.

This adds that alignment, and only where it is needed:

```python
if (
    current_platform.is_rocm()
    and self.vllm_config.parallel_config.decode_context_parallel_size > 1
):
    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
    get_tp_group().barrier()
```

Three things worth calling out:

- **Gated on DCP.** With `decode_context_parallel_size == 1` the draft is not sharded, the captured graph holds no collective, and a barrier would additionally require an initialised process group on the single-GPU path. The gate reads the *draft's* config (`self.vllm_config` is the draft-adjusted one), so it tracks whatever the draft actually runs.
- **`GroupCoordinator.barrier()`, not `torch.distributed.barrier()`.** This is a correctness point, not style. The latter is an NCCL barrier, which (per its own docstring in `parallel_state.py`) "is internally a broadcast operation with secretly created GPU tensors. It is easy to mess up the current device." Doing that immediately before graph capture is exactly the wrong thing; `GroupCoordinator.barrier()` uses the CPU group instead. A test pins the choice so a later simplification cannot quietly undo it.
- **Boot-time only**, once per speculator. No steady-state cost.

### Scope: ROCm only

Gated on `current_platform.is_rocm()`. The fault was measured on gfx950 and the
fix is untested on CUDA, so other platforms keep their current behaviour rather
than take an unverified change to graph capture. DCP is not backend-specific, so
the same staggered-entry fault may exist there; we have no way to exercise it.
Widening it is one condition if a maintainer can test it.

### Scope and placement

One-shot alignment is sufficient: the **target's** `CudaGraphManager.capture`
already loops many sizes with DCP collectives in the graph and no barrier at all,
and that works. What fails is the draft, where ranks arrive from target capture
up to ~1s apart. The barrier sits between the target's `graph_capture()` exiting
and the draft's entering, so it runs outside any capture-stream context.

**Why the TP group.** `__init__` forces the draft to `prefill_context_parallel_size=1`,
and at `pcp == 1` config validation requires `tp % dcp == 0`
(`config/parallel.py:562`), so the draft's DCP group is a subset of its TP group.
The captured draft graph carries the draft's TP all-reduces as well as the DCP
collective, so at `dcp < tp` a DCP barrier would align only some participants:
`tp=8/dcp=2` gives `[[0,1],[2,3],[4,5],[6,7]]` against a graph spanning all 8
ranks. At `dcp == tp` they coincide, which is why the measurement below does not
discriminate between the two. TP is the full set either way, at the same cost.

**No PP deadlock.** The speculator is built only on the last PP rank
(`model_runner.py:279`), and every DCP and TP group lies within a single PP
stage, so either all members reach the barrier or none do.

**It runs twice per boot**, not once: `profile_cudagraph_memory()` bootstraps a
throwaway KV cache and runs `capture_model()` for the memory estimate, which
reaches `speculator.capture()` too. Symmetric across ranks and harmless, and
profiling is where ranks are most staggered.

### Reproduction on unmodified main

The passing 8x MI355X run used a local port that shards the draft. Upstream
reachability is argued from #55472 (which copies the target's `ParallelConfig`
into the draft, making a sharded draft reachable on stock main) rather than
demonstrated on a vanilla boot. Stated plainly so a reviewer can weigh it.

### Relationship to #56723

#56723 touches the same file: it adds `draft_parallel_config()` and rewires `__init__`. The two are **independent and compose**: it does not touch `capture()`, and it refines the draft's effective DCP, which is exactly the value this gate reads. Note the skip-under-PCP behaviour is **not** on this branch today: `__init__` currently forces `prefill_context_parallel_size=1` but leaves `decode_context_parallel_size` alone, so with PCP on the gate still fires. **If** #56723 lands, it collapses the draft's DCP to 1 and this barrier then correctly no-ops under PCP; that PR is unmerged, so this is conditional on it. With PCP off it returns the config unchanged and the barrier applies either way.

There is no logic overlap; whichever lands second needs a one-line rebase of the import block.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_capture_dcp_barrier.py

# no regression in the neighbouring speculator tests
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py \
       tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py
```

**These are unit tests, not a regression test, and that is a deliberate limitation.** The bug is a multi-rank boot-time race; reproducing it needs several ranks and a real capture, which no unit test can do. They instead pin the three properties that prevent it:

1. under DCP, the device is quiesced and the ranks aligned, and both happen **before** capture begins (asserted on call order, not just call count);
2. with DCP off, neither happens, so the single-GPU path pays nothing and needs no process group;
3. the barrier goes through the DCP `GroupCoordinator` and **not** `torch.distributed.barrier()`.

The speculator is constructed with `object.__new__` and only the attributes `capture()` dereferences, so no draft model is loaded and the tests run anywhere.

## Test Result

```
tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_capture_dcp_barrier.py  3 passed
tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py
tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py           16 passed
```

Removing the two barrier lines turns the ordering test red:

```
with the barrier removed:  1 failed, 2 passed
with the barrier present:  3 passed
```

Measured on 8x MI355X (gfx950, ROCm 7.2.3), Kimi-K3 + DSpark, world size 8 with
TP=8 and DCP=8. Both attention groups are sharded: target `num_heads=12 dcp=8
decode_num_heads=96`, draft `num_heads=8 dcp=8 decode_num_heads=64`.

Every boot died at speculator capture. With the barrier the server reaches
`Application startup complete` in 280 s with no serialization penalty, and a
full concurrency sweep then ran 9/9 `rc=0`.

The stack carries a local port that makes the DSpark draft DCP-sharded, so
upstream reachability rests on the #55472 argument above rather than on a boot
from an unmodified tree.

### Does the barrier group matter in practice?

At DCP == TP both groups are the same 8 ranks, so the run above cannot tell a TP
barrier from a DCP one. Tried to settle it at `dcp < tp`, where a DCP barrier
aligns only some of the ranks the captured graph spans:

| config | barrier | result |
|---|---|---|
| TP=8, DCP=2 | DCP group | not testable: fp8 asm MLA has no kernel for the draft's `gqa=16, qseqlen=2`, so the boot dies in `get_heuristic_kernel_mla` well before speculator capture |
| TP=8, DCP=4 | DCP group | boots clean |
| TP=8, DCP=4 | TP group | boots clean |

So a DCP-only barrier did **not** fault at `dcp < tp` on this stack, and the
change to TP is not measured-necessary. It is kept because it is a strict
superset of the DCP group for the draft at the same cost, and because the
participant set is the property that has to hold rather than the one
configuration we can boot. One clean boot each is weaker evidence than the
DCP == TP failure, which reproduced on every boot.

title: [KV Offload] CPU offload capacity is divided by the number of KV cache groups on hybrid models: every `OffloadKey` (block_hash, group_idx) allocates a full multi-group chunk row
body:
## Environment

- vLLM nightly `dc36fcce` (`0.29.1rc1.dev47+gdc36fcce9`), image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-dc36fcce`
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (hybrid MLA + sliding-window-MLA, `sliding_window=128`), 9 KV cache groups (`kv cache group sizes [32, 32, 32, 32, 32, 32, 32, 64, 8]`, `kv lcm block sizes 64`; the 8-token `CircularBufferSpec` group is not prefix-cacheable), TP=8 on one 8-GPU node (80 GB each), `--kv-offloading-size 500 --kv-offloading-backend native --enable-cumem-allocator --prefix-cache-retention-interval 4096 --max-model-len 1048576 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}'`. Same result with and without `--speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", ...}'` (with it there is one more 32-token draft group).
- To get the connector to initialise at all we bind-mount a one-line change in `offloading/config.py::get_offloading_group_ids` returning `kv_cache_config.prefix_cacheable_group_ids` instead of every group (same idea as #54743; without it `tokens_per_block=8 not divisible by tokens_per_hash=32` aborts startup). 8 groups are therefore selected.

## Summary

With 500 GiB of host cache the connector stores KV continuously (280 GB written in one night) but never loads anything back: `vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total` stays at 0 and `kv_offload_size_sum{transfer_type="CPU_to_GPU"}` stays at 0 after a 139k-token prompt is evicted from the GPU cache (by ~9M tokens of unrelated cold prefill) and re-sent.

The reason is capacity accounting, not lookup logic: the CPU chunk row is sized for **all selected groups × all workers**, but a store allocates **one row per `OffloadKey`**, and an `OffloadKey` is `(block_hash, group_idx)`. Each row therefore holds one group's page and leaves the other 7/8 of the row unused. Effective capacity is `kv_offloading_size / num_selected_groups`, which on this model is smaller than the GPU KV pool, so the host tier is always evicted before the GPU tier (same LRU order) and can never serve a hit.

## Where it happens

- `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/config.py::build_offloading_config`: `worker_kv_bytes_per_block = sum(_group_kv_bytes_per_block(group) for _, group in selected_groups)` (or `total_gpu_kv_bytes // num_blocks` when all groups are selected) — bytes of one block index across **all** selected groups.
- `vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/spec.py::CPUOffloadingSpec.__init__`: `kv_bytes_per_chunk = worker_kv_bytes_per_block * world_size * blocks_per_chunk`; `num_chunks = cpu_bytes_to_use // aligned_kv_bytes_per_chunk`.
- `vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/shared_offload_region.py`: one row per chunk, `row_stride = kv_bytes_per_chunk`; each worker cell "holds all canonical tensors for that worker and chunk concatenated" (`create_next_worker_view`).
- `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py`: `RequestOffloadState.update_offload_keys` builds `make_offload_key(block_hash, group_config.group_idx)` per group; `_build_store_jobs` collects keys across groups into one list and calls `manager.prepare_store(new_offload_keys)`.
- `vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/manager.py::CPUOffloadingManager.prepare_store`: `_allocate_chunks(keys_to_store)` — one chunk (row) per key.
- `vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py::_fill_direct_ops`: a job copies only `layer_refs_per_group[g_idx]` for its group into the row.

## Numbers from the run (metrics closed exactly)

- `vllm:kv_offload_cpu_cache_usage_perc` sampled at two moments: `0.0025015974875260017` and `0.0033173357986757846`. Both are integers over **73,553** (184 and 244 pending chunks), so `num_chunks = 73,553`.
- `500 GiB / 73,553 = 7,299,072 B` per row = exactly 1,782 × 4 KiB pages = 8 workers × 8 groups × 114,048 B (all selected groups have equal 114,048-byte pages here).
- Bytes actually written per allocated chunk: `kv_offload_store_bytes_total / kv_offload_cpu_allocation_size_sum = 1.62e11 / 180,892 ≈ 896 KB` = 8 workers × **one** 114 KB page.
- Chunk consumption: the full-attention group stores one key per 64 tokens; the 7 sliding-window groups store 4 tail chunks per 4096-token segment each (`sliding_window=128`, block 32, retention 4096) plus the replay-boundary tail. ≈ 0.0225 rows per prompt token → **≈ 3.3M tokens** of effective host capacity, versus a GPU pool of 4.1M tokens (with the draft model) / 8.2M tokens (without).
- Consequence observed three times: store a 139k-token prompt → push ≥ GPU-pool worth of cold prompts → re-send: `cached_tokens=0`, external hits 0, CPU→GPU bytes 0. The only external hits seen all night (27k tokens) were short-range reuse within the effective capacity.

## Expected

`--kv-offloading-size 500` on this model should hold on the order of 500 GiB / (bytes per token) ≈ 25–30M tokens, i.e. several times the GPU pool.

## Suggested fix

Size and allocate chunks per group (or per group page size) instead of per key-with-full-row: e.g. one chunk pool per selected group with `kv_bytes_per_chunk = group_bytes_per_block * world_size * blocks_per_chunk`, and route `prepare_store/lookup/prepare_load` by `get_offload_group_idx(key)`. Alternatively, when several groups store the same `block_hash` in the same step, pack them into one row and key the row by `block_hash` only (this does not cover sliding-window groups, which store sparse tails, so per-group pools look cleaner).

Happy to test a patch on this deployment.

title: [Bug/Perf] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, 8xTP): extremely low decode throughput with --enforce-eager; CUDA graphs unusable — please prioritize SM120 graph capture fix
body:
## Environment

- **GPU**: 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition (96 GB each), compute capability **12.0 (SM120)**
- **Driver**: 590.48.01
- **vLLM**: official image `vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv41-flash-0909` (V4.1-Flash day-0 image, 2026-09-09)
- **Model**: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (FP8 checkpoint), served with the community SM120 patch set (patched `indexer.py`, `sparse_attn_indexer.py`, `cache_utils.py`, `attention.py` under `vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/`, plus `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`)
- **Launch flags**:

```
--tensor-parallel-size 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 128 \
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --max-num-seqs 16 --max-model-len 524288 \
--enforce-eager --language-model-only
```

## What works

- Model loads cleanly (48/48 shards, ~48 GiB/GPU), KV cache 28+ GiB/GPU, serving works, outputs are correct.
- TileLang kernels (`mhc_post_tilelang`, `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang`, …) compile and run.

## Observed problem: decode throughput is ~2–4 tok/s TOTAL (3 concurrent requests)

Engine-side metrics during a 3-concurrent-request benchmark (300 completion tokens each):

```
Engine 000: Avg generation throughput: 2.3–4.0 tokens/s, Running: 3 reqs
```

i.e. roughly **~1 tok/s per request** on 8x 96 GB Blackwell GPUs — orders of magnitude below what this hardware class delivers on other backends (for reference, DS-V4-Flash on the same 8x RTX PRO 6000 reaches ~2452 tok/s aggregate in published recipes).

### Why: `--enforce-eager` is mandatory on SM120 for this model

CUDA graph capture is not usable on SM120 for V4.1-Flash (known limitations carried over from the V4-Flash SM12x bring-up: graph capture failures / instability with the MLA-sparse + MoE path). Without CUDA graphs, every decode step pays full Python/dispatch overhead on a 552B-parameter model, which produces the ~1 tok/s/request result above.

### Additional data point: DSpark speculative decoding is net-negative on SM120

With `--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}'` (note: `num_speculative_tokens` must be divisible by `n_predict=5`; `7` fails validation at startup):

```
SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 1.67–2.40,
Avg Draft acceptance rate: 13.3%–28.0%
```

~72–87% of drafted tokens are rejected, so speculation only adds overhead on top of eager mode. We removed DSpark.

Two deployment footguns hit along the way (maybe worth a docs/UX note, not the main topic):
1. `/dev/shm` 64 MiB default is too small once DSpark is enabled → `RuntimeError: Insufficient space in /dev/shm: 160 MiB required`; fixed with `--shm-size=8g --ipc=host`.
2. DSpark `num_speculative_tokens=7` → pydantic validation error (`must be divisible by n_predict=5`).

## Ask

**Please prioritize making CUDA graph capture work on SM120 (compute capability 12.0) for the DeepSeek V4/V4.1 architecture.** Eager-mode decode on SM120 is effectively unusable for interactive serving of this model. With the FlashMLASparse MTP work landing on main (e.g. `4be3dcf0`), SM120 users would benefit greatly from graph-capture support in the same path.

Happy to run any test builds / capture logs on this 8x SM120 machine if useful.

title: [KV Offload] Offload namespace records a different cache_dtype depending on the executor, so a TP1 MLA engine never shares blocks with mp engines
body:
The secondary-tier namespace identity is built from `cache_config.cache_dtype` on the scheduler side ([offloading/config.py#L239-L240](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/663d7f679eda78a8d48613dfede8a4b4bcff2b74/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/config.py#L239-L240)). For sparse MLA models the worker rewrites that field in place ([mla_attention.py#L510](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/663d7f679eda78a8d48613dfede8a4b4bcff2b74/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py#L510), `fp8` -> `fp8_ds_mla`). Whether the scheduler sees the rewrite depends on the executor: with `world_size == 1` the default is `uni`, the worker runs in the EngineCore process, and the namespace records `fp8_ds_mla`; with `mp` the rewrite stays in the worker process and the namespace records `fp8`. The trigger is the executor, not TP: two TP1 engines split the same way if only one passes `--distributed-executor-backend mp`, and a TP1 engine that gains that flag on restart moves to a new namespace and can no longer see the blocks it wrote before.

Observed on `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `canonical_layout: true`, fs secondary tier on a shared directory), `nightly-385dce36`:

- TP1 engine, default executor: `config.json` with `dtype: fp8_ds_mla`, namespace `..._7e96a44f05b8`.
- TP2 engine (`mp`): `config.json` with `dtype: fp8`, namespace `..._0f58f9645522`.
- Same model, same block size, same hash seed, same canonical format; zero hits in either direction because the two engines never look in the same directory. The P2P tier hashes the same fields into its session fingerprint (`FileMapper.from_offloading_spec` -> `config_fields`), so by source a TP1 `uni` peer and an `mp` peer would also reject each other with `config fingerprint mismatch`; in this run the P2P handshake failed earlier on the #56772 length check, so that rejection was not observed directly.
- Restarting the TP1 engine with `--distributed-executor-backend mp` puts both in `..._0f58f9645522` and cross-engine hits appear (24128 / 24147 tokens).

Expected: the namespace identity should not depend on which process mutates `cache_dtype`. Either the scheduler-side offloading config should read the normalized dtype the same way the workers do, or the identity should be derived from the effective KV cache spec dtype rather than from `cache_config.cache_dtype`.

Related: #56772 (row sizes; this split was noted there as a separate reproduction obstacle).

cc @Etelis @jongukc @Change72 @rshavitt

title: Port PR #55738 (GLM-5.3-Flash NoPE MLA prefill) to older vLLM trees + SM120 note
body:
## Context

vLLM PR #55738 (merged 2026-09-14) adds GLM-5.3-Flash's NoPE MLA layout
(`qk_nope_head_dim=256, qk_rope_head_dim=0, v_head_dim=256`) to the
FlashAttention MLA prefill allow-list and the masked-MHA availability check,
plus a short-circuit for the no-op `k_pe` concat.

We applied the equivalent changes to an **older vLLM tree**
(`glm53-sm120nope` image, vLLM `0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187`, built 2026-08-27)
running GLM-5.3-Flash on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120). This document is the exact
patch content we applied, as a portable reference for others on older trees.
It also documents an important caveat we measured: **if your deployment still
shows `No MLA prefill backend supports this model`, you are leaving large
prefill throughput on the table — this patch is the fix.**

## Files touched (3)

### 1. `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py`

In `_concat_k_nope_k_pe`, right after the docstring:

```python
        if k_pe.shape[-1] == 0:
            # NoPE MLA: nothing to append, so no copy either.
            return k_nope
```

Rationale: GLM-5.3-Flash has `qk_rope_head_dim=0`, so `k_pe` is
zero-width; the concat allocates a full tensor and copies for nothing
on every layer, every step.

### 2. `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/sparse_mla_attention.py`

`_is_masked_mha_available` — allow the GLM NoPE dims through the
availability gate. On the older tree the check is an inequality chain
(upstream #55738 refactored it into a tuple set); the equivalent
rewrite is:

```python
    # PR #55738: allow GLM-5.3-Flash NoPE layout (256, 0, 256) to use masked MHA
    valid = (
        (num_heads_total == 128 and kv_lora_rank == 512
         and qk_nope_head_dim == 128 and qk_rope_head_dim == 64 and v_head_dim == 128)
        or (num_heads_total == 128 and kv_lora_rank == 512
            and qk_nope_head_dim == 256 and qk_rope_head_dim == 0 and v_head_dim == 256)
    )
    if not valid:
        return False
```

### 3. `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/flash_attn.py`

In `supports_mla_dimensions`, append to the allow-list:

```python
            # GLM5Next NoPE layout: qk_head_dim 256 + 0 and v_head_dim 256 run
            # the same kernels as the (192, 64, 256) DeepSeek-V3.2 layout.
            MLADimensions(
                qk_nope_head_dim=256,
                qk_rope_head_dim=0,
                v_head_dim=256,
            ),
```

## Measurement caveat (honest negative-ish result on our node)

We benchmarked before/after on our 8x RTX PRO 6000 node
(GLM-5.3-Flash, TP=8, CUDA graphs FULL):

- decode (500 tok): 5.0 s → 5.0 s (~100 tok/s, unchanged)
- prefill TTFT, ~3.6K-token prompt (cold): 8.72 s → 9.24 s (noise, unchanged)
- prefill TTFT, ~25K-token prompt (cold, unique random prefix): 1.74 s
  (~9K tok/s prefill) — the older `glm53-sm120nope` image we run was
  **already carrying an equivalent NoPE prefill path** (it was built from a
  community DGX-Spark recipe that predates #55738), so the patch adds no
  incremental gain on that particular image.

The patch is still worth publishing because:

1. **Stock vLLM images on SM120/GLM-5.3-Flash** log
   `No MLA prefill backend supports this model` and push every prefill
   token through the per-token top-k MQA kernel (KV-gather bound).
   If you see that line in your logs, this patch is your fix until you
   upgrade past #55738.
2. The zero-copy short-circuit (patch 1) is strictly beneficial on any
   NoPE MLA model.

## Verification on our node

- All three files compile (`py_compile` OK)
- Service restarts cleanly, CUDA graphs capture FULL (51/51)
- Log line changes from the slow path to
  `Using FLASH_ATTN MLA prefill backend`
- Zero errors / tracebacks over 16+ min of serving
- Original files backed up before patching (`/tmp/vllm_bak_*`)

## Environment

- vLLM: `0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187` (older tree, pre-#55738)
- GPU: 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (SM120)
- Model: GLM-5.3-Flash (NoPE MLA: 256/0/256), FP8, TP=8
- Related upstream PR: #55738 (merged 2026-09-14)

title: [CI] Split (H200 MIG 35GB / MI300) Multimodal Models (Extended Generation 1) into Audio, Vision and Omni jobs
body:
## What

Group the Extended Generation 1 tests into `audio/`, `vision/` and `omni/` folders under `generation/`, and run each folder as its own named job instead of a three-replica `case` block. Every job keeps the original `-m 'not core_model'` selection and trigger paths.

## Old

```text
generation/
└── test_*.py                 # flat audio, vision and omni tests

one job, key multi-modal-models-extended-generation-1:
pytest generation -m 'not core_model' --ignore test_common.py; pytest test_mapping.py
```

## New

```text
generation/
├── audio/     # audioflamingo3, gemma_ragged_audio, granite_speech, moss_audio, transformers_audio, whisper
├── vision/    # keye, maverick, moondream3, nemotron_parse, phi4mm, phi4siglip, pixtral, vit_cudagraph
├── omni/      # ultravox, voxtral, voxtral_realtime
└── test_*.py  # core-only files owned by Standard jobs, plus test_moondream3_moe.py
```

| Job | Key | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Extended Generation 1: Audio` | `multi-modal-models-extended-generation-1-audio` | `pytest generation/audio -m 'not core_model'` |
| `Extended Generation 1: Vision` | `multi-modal-models-extended-generation-1-vision` | main's `pytest generation -m 'not core_model' --ignore test_common.py`, now also ignoring the three folders; then spawn-mode `pytest generation/vision -m 'not core_model'` from the repo root |
| `Extended Generation 1: Omni + Mapping` | `multi-modal-models-extended-generation-1-omni` | `pytest generation/omni -m 'not core_model'`; `pytest test_mapping.py` |

The old key is referenced nowhere else. Each job shares the original `source_file_dependencies` through one anchor and has its own MI300 `mirror.amd` block.

## Notes

- **Root discovery is kept.** The Vision job's first command is main's `generation/` discovery command, with an `--ignore` added for each folder that now has its own job. A new non-core file added at the `generation/` root therefore still runs. Today that command picks up only `test_moondream3_moe.py`, a `cpu_test` that initializes a gloo group and so keeps its own process.
- Fixed `test_audioflamingo3.py`'s fixture path after the move: it now resolves to `tests/models/fixtures` again instead of silently skipping 2 tests.
- The vision folder keeps spawn mode from the repo root: `test_moondream3` holds a module-scoped in-process LLM, and an EngineCore forked after it hangs on startup. The legacy `test-amd.yaml` Extended Generation 1 copies still run the whole `generation/` tree in one command, so they need no change.
- `test_vit_cudagraph_image[deepseek_v41]` fails on `main`'s nightly (build 91173) and in this layout the same way, a GPU↔CPU sync assertion. It is a trunk failure, not caused by this PR. Stack: independent of #57065 (conflict only in Standard 4 paths); #57067 contains both. AI assistance was used.

## Expected runtime and overhead

Labelled predictions. Per-job times come from build 91132, whose Extended Generation 1 replicas ran exactly these three folders, compared with `main`'s nightly build 91173 (one job, 43.9m wall).

| Job | pytest | running wall | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Audio | ~16–19m | ~17–20m | ~1m | checkout + image pull |
| Vision | ~14m | ~15m | ~1–2m | checkout + image pull, two pytest starts |
| Omni + Mapping | ~8.5m | ~9.5m | ~1m | checkout + image pull, two pytest starts |

About 42–45 worker-minutes replace 43.9, so the change is roughly cost-neutral, well inside the 20-minute aggregate budget. The slowest job drops from 43.9m to Audio's ~16–19m. The upper end comes from the sum of the audio files' times in 91173's single process. That job sits above the 15-minute headroom target, so if the validation build confirms it, I'll give Granite Speech its own job in a follow-up.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Derive the namespace cache dtype from the KV cache specs
body:
Closes #56894

## What

The native offloading secondary-tier namespace identity is built from `cache_config.cache_dtype` on the scheduler side. Sparse MLA workers normalize that field in place (`fp8` -> `fp8_ds_mla`) inside `MLAAttention` construction, which runs in the worker process. With the default `uni` executor the worker shares the EngineCore process so the scheduler sees the rewrite; with `mp` it never leaves the worker. The same model then writes to two different namespaces depending on the executor, cross-engine hits drop to zero, and a TP1 engine that later gains `--distributed-executor-backend mp` can no longer see the blocks it wrote before restart.

## How

The KV cache specs travel from the workers at registration, so `MLAAttentionSpec.cache_dtype_str` carries the normalized dtype string under both executors. `build_offloading_config` now derives the model identity dtype from the specs when they agree on one, and keeps the config knob when they do not or carry no string (non-MLA specs leave `cache_dtype_str` at its `None` default, so nothing changes for everyone else).

## Validation

- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py`: 53 passed, including two new cases — a spec carrying `fp8_ds_mla` with the knob at `fp8` yields identity `fp8_ds_mla`, and a spec without a dtype string keeps the knob.
- Red-green checked: with the config change reverted, the first test fails (identity falls back to the knob) and the second still passes.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_canonical_mapping.py`: 27 passed.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py`: full file pass (exact counts in the CI run).
- Not run: a live two-engine fp8_ds_mla share over a real fs tier (no GPU on this box); the mechanism is covered by the unit cases above.

AI assistance: this PR was prepared with an AI assistant (Kimi). I reviewed the change and ran the listed tests.

title: [Perf][Engram] Fuse head reordering with MXFP8 quantization
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram shards embedding heads across TP ranks, but its replicated
`wkv` projection consumes token-major inputs. On the non-SP path, gathering along
`dim=1` reorders the rank-major collective output through a BF16 clone before
MXFP8 quantization. At 8192 tokens and width 6144, that intermediate is 96 MiB.

Gather once along `dim=0`, then fuse head reordering and padded-head removal into
MXFP8 quantization. The Triton kernel reads the gathered rank-major rows directly
and produces token-major FP8 values and F8_128x4 scales. `wkv` consumes the
`QuantizedActivation` directly, skipping its separate activation quantization.
There is still exactly one TP all-gather; the quantization helper performs no
communication.

The SP path already gathered along `dim=0` and used `_engram_select_rows` to
copy this rank's token window into a `T/tp`-sized BF16 buffer before
quantization. The same kernel takes `token_start` and `out_tokens`, so the SP
shard is quantized straight out of the gathered buffer as well; rows past the
last token quantize as zeros, exactly as the select kernel produced them.
Embedding lookup is unchanged under SP: every rank still looks up all `T`
tokens for its head shard, and only the projection and gate run on the shard.

Eligibility lives in the module-level `can_quantize_engram_gather`: TP>1 and a
`wkv` whose advertised input key is `kMxfp8Dynamic` on a FlashInfer CuTe-DSL or
CUTLASS MXFP8 kernel, because `QuantKey` does not encode the F8_128x4 scale
layout. The check goes through `get_input_quant_key`, so
consumers that require unquantized inputs fall back. Other configurations retain
their existing path. The kernel is launched with the PDL launch attribute as well
as the in-kernel `gdc_wait`/`gdc_launch_dependents`, matching the other Triton
kernels in the tree.

### Duplicate-work check

On 2026-09-15, searched open `vllm-project/vllm` PRs for `Engram`,
`MXFP8 gather`, and `Engram quantize`. No PR implementing this non-SP
reorder-plus-quantization fusion was found. Related
[#56435](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56435) changes SP redistribution
to all-to-all; [#56926](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56926) serializes
lookup streams, and [#56436](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56436)
controls lookup overlap. These address different operations. #56435 changes the
SP data layout, so whichever lands second must re-derive the SP window indexing
here. No issue number was provided for this change.

## Test Plan

Run from the repository with its CUDA-enabled `.venv` and FlashInfer CuTe-DSL
available. Both `.venv/bin` (for `ninja`) and the CUDA toolkit must be on `PATH`,
otherwise FlashInfer detection fails and the CUTLASS cases error instead of
skipping:

```bash
export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:/usr/local/cuda/bin:$PATH"
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py -q --disable-warnings --maxfail=1
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py -q \
  -k 'gather_quant or quantized_gather' --disable-warnings --maxfail=1
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/ops/engram_quant.py \
  tests/kernels/test_engram.py
git diff --check
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_engram_gather_quant.py
```

## Test Result

- Full Engram suite: **157 passed**, including a real two-GPU all-gather comparison.
- Focused tests: **73 passed, 84 deselected**.
- Bitwise equality of FP8 values and the complete scale buffer, including scale
  padding, across TP2/4/8 layouts, padded heads, zero tokens, decode and prefill
  shapes, the full token range plus first and last SP windows (including the
  zero-filled tail of the last shard), and CUDA Graph replay. Numerical tests cover every finite BF16 value
  in constant and mixed groups, signed zero, and very small/large inputs.
- Both real FlashInfer MXFP8 linear backends preserve bitwise-identical `wkv`
  outputs for non-SP and for SP ranks 1 and 3 of TP4, in eager execution, `torch.compile` with the eager backend, full CUDA
  Graph replay, and `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture` with the CPU-offload prefetch
  wait as a real eager break (one break, replay against refreshed rows). Tests
  reject accidental requantization of the fused input and check that
  `requires_unquantized_input` disables the fusion.
- Pre-commit and `git diff --check`: **passed**.

### Checkpoint projection validation

An additional local harness loaded actual `wkv` weights and scales from layers
1 and 14 of `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, revision
`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`. Both projections have weight shape
`[25600, 6144]`. With synthetic BF16 embedding rows and TP4 layouts, baseline and
fused CuTe-DSL projection outputs were bitwise identical at 1, 17, 128, and 8192
tokens: **8/8 comparisons passed**. This harness is not included in the PR.
Full-model generation, accuracy evaluation, and serving benchmarks were not run;
the fused path is bitwise identical to the existing quantization, so model output
is unchanged.

### Performance

Reproduced with `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_engram_gather_quant.py`.

One NVIDIA GB200; PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132; FlashInfer 0.6.18; Triton 3.7.1; BF16
input, head dimension 256. Measurements use CUPTI, CUDA Graph replay, cold L2,
and the median sum of kernel times, with compilation and warmup excluded. The
benchmark starts from a simulated rank-major collective output and excludes
all-gather, embedding lookup, and GEMM. These are local operation timings, not
end-to-end speedups.

| TP | Heads | Tokens | Reorder + quantize (us) | Fused (us) | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4 | 24 | 1 | 2.272 | 2.240 | 1.01x |
| 4 | 24 | 16 | 6.240 | 2.368 | 2.64x |
| 4 | 24 | 128 | 7.040 | 2.672 | 2.64x |
| 4 | 24 | 1024 | 23.072 | 5.600 | 4.12x |
| 4 | 24 | 8192 | 144.127 | 26.368 | 5.47x |
| 4 | 23 (padded) | 8192 | 247.136 | 26.368 | 9.37x |

For the 8192-by-6144 case, the net saving is **117.8 us (81.7%)** per Engram
layer per forward. The table was measured with the final kernel, including the
`token_start` / `out_tokens` window arguments; they are `do_not_specialize`
runtime scalars, and calling with eleven different (num_tokens, token_start,
out_tokens) combinations produced a single compiled variant. The kernel processes 128 MXFP8 groups per program with 4
warps, which measured about 2x faster than 32 groups at 1024 and 8192 tokens
and equal at decode sizes. At 8192 tokens it streams at about 5.6 TB/s, faster
than a plain PyTorch BF16-to-FP8 cast of the same bytes (29.8 us). At 1 to 16
tokens it is within 0.5 us of that cast and about 1 us above an empty launch,
so decode-size timings are launch-bound.

SP window, TP4, 24 heads, rank 1, same setup. Baseline is
`_engram_select_rows` plus FlashInfer quantization of the `T/tp` window:

| Tokens | Window | Select + quantize (us) | Fused (us) | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16 | 4 | 3.904 | 2.272 | 1.72x |
| 128 | 32 | 4.224 | 2.528 | 1.67x |
| 1024 | 256 | 7.776 | 3.328 | 2.34x |
| 8192 | 2048 | 29.120 | 9.056 | 3.22x |

Per Engram layer per forward this saves roughly 117 us (non-SP) or 20 us (SP)
at 8192 prefill tokens and 0 to 4 us at decode batch sizes, so end-to-end
throughput impact is small.

AI assistance was used for implementation, validation, and this PR description
(OpenAI Codex), and for review, kernel tile tuning, PDL launch wiring, and the
breakable-capture test. Human review of every changed line and
independent execution of relevant tests are required before submission.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Only inherit expert parallelism for a MoE drafter
body:
# [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Only inherit expert parallelism for a MoE drafter

## Summary

Since #55914, a MoE target served with a **dense** drafter and
`--enable-expert-parallel` fails to start on every rank:

```
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for SpeculativeConfig
  Value error, Number of experts in the model must be greater than 0 when expert
  parallelism is enabled.
```

`create_draft_parallel_config` copies the target's `enable_expert_parallel` onto the
draft's `ParallelConfig`. `SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__` then runs

```python
draft_model_config.verify_with_parallel_config(draft_parallel_config)
```

which reaches `ModelConfig._verify_with_expert_parallelism` and raises, because the
drafter has no experts. This happens during engine-config construction, before any
weight is loaded, so the engine never comes up.

## Why the flag is copied at all

#55914 added the copy to fix DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE, whose **drafter is itself MoE** and
raises `NotImplementedError: DeepSeek V4 MegaMoE currently requires expert parallel`
without it. That case is legitimate — the fix here keeps it working.

The problem is only that the copy is unconditional, so it also lands on drafters that
have nothing to shard. Expert parallelism is a property of a model with experts; a
dense MTP head or draft model has none.

## Fix

Inherit the flag only when the drafter actually has experts:

```python
draft_is_moe = draft_model_config is None or draft_model_config.is_moe
enable_expert_parallel=(
    target_parallel_config.enable_expert_parallel and draft_is_moe
),
```

`create_draft_parallel_config` gains an optional `draft_model_config` parameter
defaulting to `None`, which preserves the previous behaviour for any caller that does
not pass it. There is one call site in-tree (`SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__`), which
already has `self.draft_model_config` in scope.

## Blast radius

- **Affected:** any MoE target with a dense drafter under `--enable-expert-parallel` —
  dense MTP heads and draft models across families. Deterministic; the engine never
  starts.
- **Not affected:** MoE drafters (the MegaMoE case #55914 addressed) keep inheriting
  the flag; anything without `--enable-expert-parallel` is unchanged.
- **Regression window:** #55914 only, so this is not present in v0.29.0 or earlier
  releases.

## Test plan

Added `tests/config/test_draft_parallel_config_expert_parallel.py` — hermetic, no GPU,
no network, no checkpoints. It pins both directions: a dense drafter never inherits the
flag, a MoE drafter still does (guarding #55914 against a naive "just drop the copy"
fix), EP is never invented when the target has it off, and the `None` case keeps the
previous behaviour.

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/config/test_draft_parallel_config_expert_parallel.py -q
5 passed, 16 warnings in 2.17s
```

Full `pre-commit` (ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy, SPDX, forbidden-imports,
config validation) passed on both changed files.

Verified against real checkpoints that engine-config construction now succeeds where it
previously raised, using `RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-Dynamic` (128 experts) with
the dense `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-assistant` drafter at
`--tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel`: `draft_parallel_config
.enable_expert_parallel` is now `False` and `create_engine_config()` returns instead of
raising.

Verified end-to-end on a current nightly (`0.29.1rc1.dev128+gcd10ed6f9`), which carries
this regression. With this patch the engine gets past config construction — the stage
that previously aborted — and the API server comes up at `--tensor-parallel-size 2
--enable-expert-parallel` with a dense MTP drafter and serves correctly:

```
Worker_TP0_EP0 / Worker_TP1_EP1
Model loading took 14.14 GiB memory per rank

spec_decode_num_drafts_total            40
spec_decode_num_draft_tokens_total     160
spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total   87
accepted per position            31 / 27 / 17 / 12
```

That is a mean acceptance length of 1 + 87/40 = **3.18 tokens per target forward** (54%
of draft tokens accepted) over four greedy chat completions — a small, indicative sample
rather than a benchmark. Answers were correct (e.g. `17 * 23` → `391`).

Nightly also carries the separate Gemma-4 defect fixed in #56936, which aborts later at
draft load, so both patches were applied for that run. This PR is the one that gets past
engine-config construction; neither alone is sufficient on a current tree.

That the configuration this unblocks is a valid and useful one is separately
demonstrated end-to-end on a **v0.29.0** image, which predates this regression and so
does not need this patch. There the same pair — MoE target
(`RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-Dynamic`, 128 experts) with the dense
`google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-assistant` drafter, `--enable-expert-parallel`, MTP
speculative decoding — loads and generates correctly:

```
user: Explain expert parallelism in one sentence.
  Expert parallelism is a distributed training strategy where different "experts"
  within a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model are partitioned across different computing
  devices, ...

user: What is 17 * 23? Answer with the number only.
  391
```

(That run needed #56936 for the Gemma-4-specific defect, and used
`--tensor-parallel-size 1` because only one GPU was free. It does not exercise the code
this PR changes — on v0.29.0 there is nothing here to fix — it only shows that a dense
drafter under an expert-parallel MoE target is a configuration worth keeping servable.)

## Model evaluation

Not applicable: this changes only which parallel configuration the drafter is validated
and sharded with. It alters no numerics for the MoE-drafter path, and the dense-drafter
path it unblocks could not run at all before.

## Related

A MoE Gemma-4 target with its MTP drafter additionally hits a second, independent defect
in `Gemma4Speculator._create_draft_vllm_config`, which fails later at model-load time.
That is fixed separately; this PR stands alone and is required for every affected
family.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude). The tests and linters quoted
above were run on this change, and the submitter has reviewed it before opening.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Don't swap the Gemma4 MTP draft into the target's VllmConfig
body:
# [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Don't swap the Gemma4 MTP draft into the target's VllmConfig

## Summary

With `--enable-expert-parallel` on a MoE Gemma-4 target and MTP speculative decoding
via the `gemma-4-*-assistant` draft, engine start fails on every TP rank with:

```
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for VllmConfig
  Value error, Number of experts in the model must be greater than 0 when expert
  parallelism is enabled.
```

`Gemma4Speculator._create_draft_vllm_config` built the draft's config with
`replace(self.vllm_config, model_config=draft_model_config)`. `replace()`
(`vllm/config/utils.py:119-127`) reconstructs the pydantic dataclass, re-running
`VllmConfig.__post_init__` (`vllm/config/vllm.py:1274`) →
`verify_with_parallel_config` (`vllm/config/model.py:1420`) →
`_verify_with_expert_parallelism` (`vllm/config/model.py:1373`) with the **draft** as
`model_config` and the **target's** `parallel_config`. The draft
(`Gemma4AssistantForCausalLM`, rewritten to `gemma4_mtp`) has no experts, so the check
fails. The validator is correct; it is being asked a question with no valid answer,
because the two halves of the config come from two different models.

## Why the `model_config=` swap was redundant

- `get_model()` already receives the draft `model_config` as an explicit argument
  (`gemma4/speculator.py:42`), and it takes precedence —
  `vllm_config.model_config` is only the fallback when that argument is `None`
  (`model_loader/__init__.py:138-139`).
- `Gemma4MultiTokenPredictor` reads its config from
  `speculative_config.draft_model_config` (`models/gemma4_mtp.py:342`, `:466`, `:516`)
  and never reads `vllm_config.model_config`. Its quantization likewise comes from
  `get_draft_quant_config()`, which reads `speculative_config.draft_model_config`
  (`models/utils.py:964`).

This matters because `initialize_model` constructs new-style model classes as
`model_class(vllm_config=vllm_config)` — the explicit `model_config` argument only
selects the class. Removing the swap is safe precisely because the Gemma-4 MTP model
sources its config from `speculative_config`.

## Consistency with every sibling path

No other speculator builds a `VllmConfig` whose `model_config` is the draft:

| Path | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `eagle/utils.py::load_eagle_model` | `replace()`s `kernel_config`/`cache_config`/`attention_config`; passes draft `model_config` separately (`:111`) |
| `dflash/utils.py` | same pattern (`:45`) |
| `dspark/utils.py` | same pattern (`:85`) |
| `v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py::_create_draft_vllm_config` | overrides `kernel_config`/`attention_config`/`cache_config` only (`:1274-1310`) |

Notably `vllm/v1/spec_decode/gemma4.py:150` — the same Gemma-4 override in the other
proposer tree, with a byte-identical docstring — already does exactly what this patch
does: it calls `super()._create_draft_vllm_config()` and only carries the attention
backend through. This change brings the Model-Runner-V2 speculator in line with it.

The fix keeps only the `attention_config.backend` carry-through, which is what the
method's docstring says it exists for.

## Why not reset `enable_expert_parallel` on the draft's `parallel_config` instead

`SpeculativeConfig.create_draft_parallel_config` deliberately propagates the flag
(`enable_expert_parallel=target_parallel_config.enable_expert_parallel`,
`vllm/config/speculative.py:1749`), so forcing it off for the drafter would contradict
an intentional convention. It would also only patch EP: the TP-divisibility and
PP-support checks in `verify_with_parallel_config` would still be evaluated against the
draft, so the same class of failure would recur with the next target-level validator.
Not constructing the mismatched config at all fixes the category.

## Regression introduced in

`ceb0111a90` ("[Model Runner V2][Spec Decode] Add Gemma4 MTP support", #43241), which
added `_create_draft_vllm_config` with the full-config `replace()`. Reproduces on
v0.28.0 and v0.29.0; the combination worked on older builds predating this method.

## Not a duplicate

Checked open PRs and issues before opening this:

- **#44086** (`fix(spec_decode): ensure draft model uses correct parallel/model config
  in all proposers`) — touches the other tree (`vllm/v1/spec_decode/`) and moves in the
  **opposite** direction: it *adds* a `model_config` override to the shared base
  `_create_draft_vllm_config`. If merged as-is it would propagate this same category
  error to every proposer in that tree. Flagging it here for reviewer awareness — the
  two changes conflict in intent and should be reconciled.
- **#55593** — `gpu_model_runner.py` only; no overlap.
- **#43254**, **#49120**, **#47629**, **#46329** — unrelated areas.

No open PR touches `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/gemma4/speculator.py`.

## Test plan

Added `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_gemma4_draft_config.py` — config-only, no GPU and no
checkpoints, following the existing `test_draft_moe_backend_override.py` /
`test_draft_attention_backend_override.py` pattern so it runs in CI rather than
skipping. It asserts the returned config keeps the **target's** `model_config`, that
the attention-backend carry-through still works, and that the target config is not
mutated.

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_gemma4_draft_config.py \
    tests/v1/spec_decode/test_draft_attention_backend_override.py \
    tests/v1/spec_decode/test_draft_moe_backend_override.py -q
10 passed, 18 warnings in 12.93s
```

Confirmed the new test actually catches the bug: loading the pre-fix (HEAD) version of
the module and running the same assertion returns `model_config == 'draft-model-config'`
and fails, while the patched version returns `'target-model-config'` and passes.

Full `pre-commit` suite (ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy, SPDX, forbidden-imports,
config validation) passed on both changed files.

## Model evaluation

No accuracy evaluation is applicable: this change does not alter numerics or the
constructed draft model. The draft's architecture, weights and quantization all derive
from `speculative_config.draft_model_config`, which is untouched. `quant_config` is
also unchanged in practice — `VllmConfig.__post_init__` only recomputes it when it is
`None` (`vllm/config/vllm.py:1361`), and `replace()` carries the target's
already-computed value through in both the old and new code. The change is purely which
`ModelConfig` object rides along in the draft's `VllmConfig`, and nothing in the
Gemma-4 MTP path reads it.

What the change does affect is startup: a configuration that previously aborted now
gets past the point it aborted at.

A/B verified on a **v0.29.0** image against the real checkpoints
(`RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-Dynamic`, 128 experts, with the dense
`google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-assistant` drafter, `--enable-expert-parallel`). v0.29.0 is
a released version where this defect is the only blocker, so the fix can be isolated.

**Before** (stock image) — fails at exactly the frames above:

```
speculator.py", line 38, in load_draft_model
    draft_vllm_config = self._create_draft_vllm_config()
speculator.py", line 59, in _create_draft_vllm_config
config/utils.py", line 127, in replace
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for VllmConfig
  Number of experts in the model must be greater than 0 when expert parallelism is enabled.
```

**After** (same image, this patch applied in place) — the drafter loads, its MTP layers
are wired into the target's KV cache, and generation completes:

```
Loading weights took 7.54 seconds        (target)
Loading weights took 0.24 seconds        (draft — previously unreachable)
Gemma4 MTP: draft layer 0 (sliding_attention) -> language_model.model.layers.28.self_attn.attn
Gemma4 MTP: draft layer 3 (full_attention)    -> language_model.model.layers.29.self_attn.attn
Model loading took 26.61 GiB memory
```

(That v0.29.0 run used `--tensor-parallel-size 1`, as only one GPU was free at the
time; the defect is in config validation and is TP-independent.)

Additionally verified at **TP=2 with expert parallelism**, the shape of the original
report, on a nightly image (`0.29.1rc1.dev128+gcd10ed6f9`) carrying this patch plus
#56930 — the separate expert-parallel defect that aborts earlier, since merged upstream
as `c58ff535f4` but not yet in a published nightly. The API server comes up and serves:

```
Worker_TP0_EP0 / Worker_TP1_EP1
Gemma4 MTP: draft layer 0..3 -> language_model.model.layers.28/29.self_attn.attn
Application startup complete
```

Speculative decoding is doing real work, not merely failing to crash. From `/metrics`
after greedy chat completions with `num_speculative_tokens=4`:

```
spec_decode_num_drafts_total                  52
spec_decode_num_draft_tokens_total           208
spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total        132
spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_per_pos      44 / 36 / 28 / 24
```

A mean acceptance length of 1 + 132/52 = **3.54 tokens per target forward**, 63% of
draft tokens accepted, with the monotonic decay across positions you would expect.
Draft tokens are exactly 4x drafts, and the per-position counts sum to the accepted
total, so the drafter is proposing and being verified as intended.

Two independent runs — one with `enforce_eager`, one on the normal `torch.compile`
serving path — landed on the same 3.54, so this is not a small-sample artefact. It is
still a handful of short prompts rather than a benchmark.

Output is correct. With the chat template applied, the patched engine — MoE target,
dense MTP drafter, expert parallelism on — generates coherently:

```
user: Explain expert parallelism in one sentence.
  Expert parallelism is a distributed training strategy where different "experts"
  within a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model are partitioned across different computing
  devices, ensuring that each device only processes a specific subset of the model's
  specialized parameters.

user: What is 17 * 23? Answer with the number only.
  391
```

(For anyone reproducing: passing these prompts raw to `llm.generate()`, without the
chat template, yields degenerate text on this instruct checkpoint. That is unrelated
to this change — a control on the **stock, unpatched** image with speculative decoding
**disabled entirely** produces the same degenerate text, byte-identical on one of the
two prompts.)

Note that reaching engine start also requires the fix from #56930, a separate and
independent defect that rejects a dense drafter under `--enable-expert-parallel` during
engine-config construction, before this code path runs. That one is **already merged**
(`c58ff535f4`), so current `main` needs only this PR; the runs above used an older
nightly image with `c58ff535f4` applied on top.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude). The tests and linters quoted
above were run on this change, and the submitter has reviewed it before opening.

title: [ROCm][DSv4] Enable confidence-based adaptive scheduler for DSpark
body: ## Inherits [#52362](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52362) This work inherits and rebases the ROCm DSpark adaptive-verification implementation from #52362. It is not an independent implementation of the feature. This branch should only be submitted after explicit coordination with the author of #52362, or after that pull request is closed. If submitted as a replacement, it supersedes #52362 and preserves its original design and attribution. ## Summary Enable confidence-scheduled DSpark adaptive verification for DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm. The change: - constructs and loads the AMD DSpark confidence head; - preserves fail-closed behavior when confidence-head checkpoint weights are absent; - enables Adaptive Verification CUDA-graph support in the ROCm sparse MLA and sparse SWA metadata builders; - enables the ROCm flattened device query-length path required by uneven adaptive verification budgets; - replaces an optimization-removable assertion in `compute_confidence()` with an explicit `RuntimeError`; - adds focused AMD confidence-head and ROCm adaptive-indexer regression tests. ## Source Revision - PR branch: `larryli2-amd:enable_adaptive-dspark-rocm` - PR head: `945abd627010c926cbf288f4b374e8b63d7443bf` - Base used when preparing the branch: `bbbd0a02c9d1bec965ee818af29a1319baefa69c` - Changed files: 3 runtime files and 2 focused test files - Total diff: 413 insertions, 6 deletions ## Focused Validation ```text tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_dspark_rocm.py tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_rocm_adaptive.py ``` Result: `10 passed`. The tests cover confidence-head mapping/loading/fail-closed behavior, the explicit missing-head error, ROCm adaptive CUDA-graph support, flattened query-length selection, the single-request uniform path, and stable buffer replay under changed allocations. Changed-file lint and formatting checks also passed. ## Serving Smoke Validation A live `adaptive_k7` ROCm serving smoke test completed successfully: - `/health` returned HTTP 200; - `Application startup complete` was observed; - a single request completed with 48 generated tokens; - no `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT`, worker death, queue hang, or traceback was observed; - the DSpark draft model loaded 97 parameters; - the ROCm indexer logged `use_flattening=True`; - breakable CUDA graphs were enabled. Observed speculative-decoding counters during the smoke request: ```text num_drafts_total: 18 num_draft_tokens_total: 126 # 18 × K=7 num_accepted_tokens: 29 ``` This demonstrates that the DSpark speculative path executed. It is not a throughput, latency, quality, or adaptive-vs-fixed performance measurement. ## Reproduction Environment ### Hardware - 8 × AMD Instinct MI350X - Tensor parallel size: 8 - Data parallel size: 1 ### Model - Model: [`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark) - Local validation path: `/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark` - Architecture: `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` - Quantization: FP4 expert weights with FP8 mixed precision - Checkpoint size: 166,878,536,440 bytes across 48 safetensor shards - `config.json` SHA256: `6c8f3d2d3b48707541b88f32f22ef3f0f8a6b57d8523281e2b8d3cdb0ae9a023` - `model.safetensors.index.json` SHA256: `98efab455cf08dfbbbaaba6f570e1bf10bf927d2b4c3c453a59c2f6f0e3be92b` ### Container Provenance The performance validation used a locally derived, pinned image: ```text Image tag: dspark-av-sep11:52362-ad170197-aiter804648bc Image ID: sha256:49067946ae13f4047605ce9edca3d9705903b602f43f8c1fcd0ecdb8927511d5 Base digest: sha256:72e90adf360ccffb231a098a15eadfb808719c029c6cd43f6386095064552b7e vLLM base: 2a02f6efe Original patch: ad170197f40a3e48eddbb92bd195a2e5db684267 AITer: 0.1.21.post2.dev2+g804648bcb AITer commit: 804648bcbf87646ddef4b7add10da9c3b322567c AITer wheel: SHA256 30360d15819a9c8e3ec8e4ae665683abf4c5358d5be1f49a9aa2f7962c0032db PyTorch: 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0 ``` The exact image tag is a locally derived artifact rather than a public registry image. A byte-identical reproduction requires access to that image or reconstruction from the pinned base digest and the exact AITer wheel above. ## Serving Configuration ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 export VLLM_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT_LEN=8192 export AITER_USE_CK_MOE_SORTING=0 export AITER_USE_FLYDSL_MOE_SORTING=0 export VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MOE_DISPATCH_POLICY=0 vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark \ --served-model-name dsv4flash \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --data-parallel-size 1 \ --async-scheduling \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --max-model-len 32768 \ --max-num-seqs 256 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --moe-backend aiter \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","max_cudagraph_capture_size":2048}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"enable_adaptive_verification":true}' ``` ## Throughput Methodology The benchmark used a frozen 880-request SPEED-Bench Throughput-1K request set: ```text Temperature: 1.0 Top-p: 1.0 Maximum output length: 2048 Concurrency order: 256, 128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4 ``` Each cell used an independent cold server boot. A result is valid only when client and server generated-token counts match, no preemptions occur, and no GPU fault is observed. ## Resutls The results are expected: Compared with the non-adaptive scheduler, DSpark with the confidence-based adaptive scheduler delivers comparable performance at low concurrency and significant speedup at high concurrency.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Shard DSA prefill indexer rows across TP ranks
body:
## Overview

Shard ROCm DSA prefill indexer query rows across tensor-parallel ranks, then reconstruct Top-K indices with one AllReduce(MAX). Mirrored early/late stripes distribute causal work without a stripe-size setting.

> Review head `213f069be994b20059356b7b85024c5e7f66b776` on upstream main `0f112d180033f3757cf283723f5593a40b02ed82` (AITER pin `v0.1.24.post1`). Existing review history is retained through a merge update. The historical GPU/model reports below were measured on their stated commits, **not this updated head**. GPU/model revalidation remains pending.

## Claims

- Use the cached `rocm_aiter_ops.is_cp_indexer_enabled()` predicate on the execution path. `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CP_INDEXER` remains opt-in, default off; the stripe-size env var is removed.
- Split each chunk into early/late halves and assign mirrored stripes, with round-robin remainders. A batch that needs a collective assigns **every** prefill row to exactly one rank, including short tail chunks. A batch with no chunk reaching TP-size stays replicated and issues no collective.
- Enlarge the chunk budget only for the uncompressed FP8 path that can shard. Compressed/candidate, FP4, and PCP/DCP paths retain their original bounds. CPU and paged MXFP4 chunker overrides accept the new argument without increasing their budget.
- Add real multi-GPU correctness tests plus CPU partition/budget tests. The TP2 cases are wired into the AMD distributed CI job; TP8 cases require eight GPUs.

## Validation

### This review update

- Local CPU contract harness: **101 passed**. It executes the exact extracted partition/chunker definitions and the committed CPU tests, checks the Top-K comparator, and exercises the actual operator body with CPU substitutes for scoring, Top-K, and the collective. This is **not** a full vLLM import, GPU-kernel, RCCL, or serving test.
- The same control-flow reproduction against the previous mirrored implementation fails four mixed-chunk cases (TP2/TP8, a large chunk plus tiny head/tail chunks). The updated implementation passes: tied rank-local sets cannot be merged into duplicate keys because each reduced row has one writer.
- GPU suite: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_rocm_aiter_indexer_m_split.py -v`. Includes TP2/TP8, ragged halves, mixed short/large chunks, narrow causal windows, unique valid Top-K keys, ownership, and skipping the collective for fully replicated batches. **Not run here: no ROCm GPU in this environment.**
- Previously reported operator run: 14 passed on 8x MI355X for the earlier interleaved implementation (2026-09-18); this does not validate the new mirrored/updated head.
- **Passed** `pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only 0f112d180033f3757cf283723f5593a40b02ed82 HEAD)`, including Ruff, Python 3.10 mypy, and Buildkite test tethering. Python syntax compilation and `git diff --check` also passed.
- Model/GPU tests, a matched A/B against #46103, and quantitative compute/memory-bandwidth roofline analysis remain pending on this head. No kernel-efficiency or merge-readiness claim is made.

### Reported GPU/model evidence

The October 2 report compares baseline `36229e1337` with mirrored implementation `78506b4278`, before this latest-main adaptation and the mixed-tail/budget fixes. On GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP8, 8x MI355X, it reports +4.02–9.47% output throughput at ISL 50k; the full sweep and commands are retained below. These are supplied measurements, not newly executed results.

Accuracy is **not established as non-regressing**: the same report has GPQA-Diamond 0.631 → 0.596 and RULER 131072 0.992 → 0.978. GPQA truncation changes with the score, but that does not by itself rule out an effect of the implementation. Repeated, matched evaluation is still needed before automatic enablement.
