# CP indexer benchmark, rebased onto the new main: baseline vs feature

**Model:** `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`, TP8 on 8x gfx950 (MI355X), ROCm image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.30.0`

| config | commit | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | `36229e1337` | new upstream main, **no** CP indexer feature |
| feature | `78506b4278` | baseline + the 3 rebased CP-indexer commits (`30a07bd19d`, `d4be269917`, `4a58beda81`) + `78506b4278` (MXFP4 and CPU chunker overrides accept `m_split_world_size`) |

The four feature commits are **Python-only** (no `csrc`, no CMake), so both configurations run byte-identical kernels and the difference between them is purely the feature.

---

## Results

### ISL 50k / OSL 1k

| conc | tok/s base → cp | Δ | mean TTFT ms | Δ | mean TPOT ms | Δ |
| ---: | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| 4  | 190.66 → 198.32 | **+4.02%** | 5813 → 5229   | −10.05% | 15.31 → 15.07   | −1.57% |
| 8  | 265.70 → 281.11 | **+5.80%** | 7130 → 6664   | −6.54%  | 23.15 → 21.96   | −5.17% |
| 16 | 332.23 → 357.34 | **+7.56%** | 8602 → 7888   | −8.29%  | 39.76 → 37.07   | −6.77% |
| 32 | 374.01 → 406.86 | **+8.78%** | 10343 → 9258  | −10.50% | 75.46 → 69.60   | −7.76% |
| 64 | 389.37 → 426.27 | **+9.47%** | 19517 → 17653 | −9.55%  | 144.41 → 131.99 | −8.60% |

Throughput and TPOT gains grow with concurrency, and TTFT improves by 6.5–10.5% at every point.

### ISL 8k / OSL 1k

| conc | tok/s base → cp | Δ | mean TTFT ms | Δ | mean TPOT ms | Δ |
| ---: | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| 4   | 288.29 → 286.51   | **−0.62%** | 939 → 948   | +0.97% | 12.97 → 13.05   | +0.60% |
| 8   | 524.54 → 523.21   | **−0.25%** | 1508 → 1522 | +0.89% | 13.79 → 13.81   | +0.19% |
| 16  | 853.04 → 851.67   | **−0.16%** | 2242 → 2153 | −3.98% | 16.58 → 16.69   | +0.71% |
| 32  | 1207.11 → 1208.05 | **+0.08%** | 2617 → 2589 | −1.07% | 23.96 → 23.97   | +0.03% |
| 64  | 1622.53 → 1628.43 | **+0.36%** | 3150 → 3121 | −0.92% | 36.37 → 36.26   | −0.31% |
| 128 | 2033.40 → 2038.62 | **+0.26%** | 4167 → 4174 | +0.17% | 58.87 → 58.70   | −0.29% |
| 256 | 2380.92 → 2389.34 | **+0.35%** | 6243 → 6212 | −0.49% | 101.37 → 101.02 | −0.35% |

Throughput and TPOT stay within ±0.71% at every point, about the size of run-to-run noise: neutral. That's expected, because the CP indexer parallelises sparse-MLA **indexer prefill**, whose cost scales with context length, so at 8k there is little to split up. This single-run sweep does not establish an overhead bound for other shapes or hardware.

---

## Correctness

**gsm8k** (1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, thinking off):

| filter | baseline | CP indexer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exact_match, strict-match` | 96.44% (1272/1319) | 97.50% (1286/1319) |
| `exact_match, flexible-extract` | 96.66% (1275/1319) | 97.50% (1286/1319) |

**GPQA-Diamond** (198 questions, thinking on, 100k token cap):

| config | score | truncated_rate | stop_rate | error_rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 0.631 | 0.328 | 0.672 | 0.0 |
| CP indexer | 0.596 | 0.364 | 0.636 | 0.0 |

The 0.035 gap is 7 questions out of 198, and it follows the truncation rate: 65 baseline answers ran past the token cap against 72 for the CP indexer, and a truncated answer always scores zero. Of the answers that finished, both get about 94% right.

**RULER / NIAH** (`niah_single_2`, 500 documents per length, thinking on):

| sequence length | baseline | CP indexer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 65536 | 0.992 | 0.992 |
| 131072 | 0.992 | 0.978 |

### Eval commands

```bash
MODEL=amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4
URL=http://127.0.0.1:8586

# gsm8k
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template \
  --tasks gsm8k.yaml --log_samples --output_path zresult \
  --model_args "model=$MODEL,base_url=$URL/v1/chat/completions,trust_remote_code=True,eos_string=</s>,max_retries=1,num_concurrent=64,timeout=1800,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=262144" \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":16384,"temperature":0,"top_p":1,"chat_template_kwargs":{"thinking":false}}'

# GPQA-Diamond
sgl-eval run gpqa --base-url "$URL/v1" --model "$MODEL" \
  --num-threads 32 --n-repeats 1 --max-tokens 100000 \
  --chat-template-kwarg enable_thinking=true \
  --chat-template-kwarg "think_end_token=</think>" \
  --out-dir ./gpqa

# RULER / NIAH
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args "{\"model\":\"$MODEL\",\"base_url\":\"$URL/v1/chat/completions\",\"tokenizer\":\"$MODEL\",\"trust_remote_code\":true,\"num_concurrent\":16,\"timeout\":36000,\"max_retries\":1,\"tokenized_requests\":false,\"max_length\":262144}" \
  --tasks niah_single_2 --metadata '{"max_seq_lengths":[65536,131072]}' \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":8192,"temperature":0,"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":true,"think_end_token":"</think>"}}' \
  --apply_chat_template --batch_size auto --seed 1234 --log_samples
```

## Serving the model

Environment common to both configurations:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1
```

**Before** (baseline `36229e1337`): the feature does not exist at this commit, so nothing extra is set:

```bash
unset VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CP_INDEXER
```

**After** (feature `78506b4278`). The flag defaults to off, so it must be set:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CP_INDEXER=1
```

The serve command is identical for both:

```bash
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --linear-backend aiter --moe-backend aiter \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --port 8586
```

---

## Client side

Run this once for each concurrency value. The number of requests scales with it: `C * 10` requests, plus `C * 2` warmup requests that are not measured.

```bash
MODEL=amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4
C=32          # concurrency
ISL=51200     # 8192 for the ISL 8k sweep

vllm bench serve --trust-remote-code --backend openai \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8586 --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model "$MODEL" --tokenizer "$MODEL" \
  --max-concurrency $C \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len $ISL --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts $((C * 10)) --num-warmups $((C * 2)) \
  --request-rate inf --ignore-eos \
  --save-result --result-dir ./results --result-filename result.json \
  --percentile-metrics "ttft,tpot,e2el,itl" --metric-percentiles "0,75,90,99,100"
```

Sweeps run:

- ISL 8192: conc 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256
- ISL 51200: conc 4, 8, 16, 32, 64

- ISL 51200 — conc 4, 8, 16, 32, 64

---

## Notes

1. **`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` must be unset.** With it set the server does not start — weight loading fails with `KeyError: 'layers.10.mlp.shared_experts.down_proj.weight'`. This is not caused by the CP indexer: it breaks the same way on upstream main. Both configurations therefore run with fusion off.
2. **Each number comes from a single run.** Running the same configuration twice gives results that differ by about 0.5%, just from run-to-run variation. The ISL 50k gains (3.6–8.7%) are far larger than that, so they are real. The ISL 8k differences are smaller than 0.5–1%, so they cannot be told apart from noise — that is why ISL 8k is called neutral rather than a small win.
3. Prefix caching disabled throughout, `--ignore-eos` so every request emits exactly 1024 tokens.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Original interleaved-stripe evaluation and submission-time validation (historical)</summary>

The stripe-size settings and rebase validation in this archived section describe the original implementation. That setting is removed from the current implementation; these are historical results only.

## Test Plan

Hardware: 8x MI355X (gfx950, 288 GB each), ROCm 7.2.3. Model: `GLM-5.2-MXFP4` (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, `index_topk=2048`), TP=8.

Three configurations, each a fresh server boot:

- **before** = `main` @ `8c34a3723`. The env var does not exist on that branch.
- **after (stripe 512)** = this branch, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CP_INDEXER=1`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CP_INDEXER_STRIPE_SIZE=512`.
- **after (stripe 1024)** = same, with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CP_INDEXER_STRIPE_SIZE=1024`.

We benchmarked two `_STRIPE_SIZE` values, `512` and `1024`, because different stripe sizes can yield different performance results.

We ran the baseline on `main` rather than on this branch with the flag set to `0`, so the baseline cannot accidentally include any of this code.

All three use the same `vllm serve` command:

```bash
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --trust-remote-code --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --linear-backend aiter --moe-backend aiter \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --port 8586
```

Env vars for all runs: `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0`.

We turned prefix caching **off** with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. So every request does a full prefill. We checked this two ways: the engine log shows `enable_prefix_caching=False`, and every result has `total_input_tokens == num_prompts * ISL`.

Benchmark command for each point:

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8586 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions --model amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 \
  --tokenizer amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --trust-remote-code \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len $ISL --random-output-len 1024 \
  --max-concurrency $CONC --num-prompts $((CONC*10)) --num-warmups $((CONC*2)) \
  --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --save-result \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,e2el,itl --metric-percentiles 0,75,90,99,100
```

Test points: ISL/OSL 8192/1024 and 51200/1024, each at concurrency 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, plus 128 and 256 for 8192. 12 points per configuration, 36 runs in total.

Three correctness evals were run against the served model (the server config above is unchanged; these are all HTTP clients).

**gsm8k** — full 1319-question test set via lm-eval, 5-shot, greedy, thinking off:

```bash
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args '{"model":"amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4","base_url":"http://localhost:8586/v1/chat/completions","trust_remote_code":true,"eos_string":"</s>","max_retries":1,"num_concurrent":64,"timeout":1800,"tokenized_requests":false,"max_length":262144}' \
  --tasks gsm8k --include_path ./gsm8k --apply_chat_template \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":16384,"temperature":0,"top_p":1,"chat_template_kwargs":{"thinking":false}}'
```

**GPQA-Diamond** — 198 questions via sglang's `run_eval` (NeMo-Skills mcq prompt + `eval_mcq` grader), thinking on:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gpqa \
  --model amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8586 --num-threads 32 --max-tokens 100000 \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": true, "think_end_token": "</think>"}'
```

**RULER / NIAH** — `niah_single_2` at 64k and 128k via lm-eval, thinking on:

```bash
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args '{"model":"amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4","base_url":"http://localhost:8586/v1/chat/completions","tokenizer":"amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4","trust_remote_code":true,"num_concurrent":16,"timeout":36000,"max_retries":1,"tokenized_requests":false,"max_length":262144}' \
  --tasks niah_single_2 \
  --metadata '{"max_seq_lengths":[65536,131072]}' \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":8192,"temperature":0,"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":true,"think_end_token":"</think>"}}' \
  --apply_chat_template --batch_size auto --seed 1234 --log_samples --output_path ./niah
```

RULER needs `tokenizer=` because it sizes its own prompts to exact token counts. `timeout` is aiohttp's **total** per-request budget including time queued behind `num_concurrent`, so it must exceed the whole run's wall time, not just one request.

## Test Result

### Correctness

All three evals were run on **both** configurations.

Truncation moved by a similar amount in the same direction: 68 baseline responses against 75 indexer responses were cut off at the token cap and scored zero, a 7-question difference. At a ~35% truncation rate this eval is partly measuring whether the reasoning fits in the budget, so treat the table as a like-for-like comparison at a fixed budget rather than an absolute GPQA score.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse][NIXL] Recompute unaligned host-import tails locally
body:
# [Bugfix][HiSparse][NIXL] Leave unaligned host-import tails for local prefill

## Problem

NIXL pull advertises the whole prompt as externally computed. The host-only
HiSparse resident manager requires imported prefixes to end on a cache-block
boundary. A 32,019-token prompt with block size 64 therefore raises:

```text
ValueError: A host-only HiSparse import must end on a cache-block boundary.
```

This escapes scheduler admission and kills the decoder engine. It was observed
on unmodified main `a08dffe21534916f218dcc93012dbaa01f942691`, on 1P TP8 + 1D
TP8, two 8xB200 nodes, using `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` with HiSparse on D. The
new regression also fails on this patch's base, main
`9d14fd3095eb169044e2da0a2a98dd1f2c77ce22`.

## Change

- For host-only HiSparse pull imports, advertise only complete pages, aligned
  across resident and transferable cache groups.
- Omit the unimported tail from local destinations and remote source lists.
  The remote cap is applied after logical-to-kernel block expansion, before
  prefix-cache suffix matching. Rounding the count alone would shift reads
  toward the remote tail and copy the wrong blocks.
- Let normal local prefill compute the remaining tokens. No truncation of the
  user's prompt and no changes to CUDA-graph or memory-utilization settings.
- Keep notify-only receives valid when no complete block can be imported.

For 32,019 tokens / block size 64, import tokens `[0, 32000)` and compute
`[32000, 32019)` on D. Normal non-HiSparse imports retain their existing behavior.
This targets the P-to-D pull path, not bidirectional D-to-P or push admission.

## Validation

New/targeted regression selection:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  -k 'hisparse_import or nixl_hisparse' -q
```

- The original NIXL regression selection on base: **18 failed / 4 passed**.
- Final patched targeted selection, including allocation/resume and DCP
  source-page clipping regressions: **32 passed**.

Broader suite, in a CUDA-visible B200 `ve` environment:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_kv_connector.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  -k 'not test_fewer_blocks_with_hma' -q
```

**468 passed / 1 deselected** on final commit
`1e574140e08a053f5c99fe17b1b3757aca6e40f8` (129.04 seconds). The excluded
Gemma test was attempted in the earlier broad run and failed with HTTP 401
fetching gated `google/gemma-3-1b-it`, also seen in the main control.
Pre-commit passed on all six changed files, including the configured mypy hook.

## Model evaluation and limitations

A B200 smoke using 32,019-token prompts completed **4/4 requests with HTTP
200**, without the admission exception or engine exit. Decoder logs showed
**64 successful NIXL transfers**, **99.9% external prefix-cache hits**, and
7.6 prompt tokens/s over the reporting interval (the four 19-token tails).
The source files on D matched this commit byte-for-byte; both roles used the
pinned main `ve` environment, with this patch applied only to D.

However, **0/4 copy-word accuracy cases passed**: the prefiller reference
returned the requested words, while D's output was garbled. The earlier
aligned plain-main test also failed all four cases. This establishes the
admission fix and real transfer activity, **not end-to-end P/D correctness**.
This patch does not claim to fix that separate correctness issue. No
performance improvement is claimed.
A follow-up with 63-token prompts (no complete block to import) also completed
4/4 requests, and both servers remained healthy. Its copy-word accuracy was
again 0/4; the no-import fallback is not evidence that output correctness is
fixed.
DCP/heterogeneous-topology model evaluation has not been run for this patch.

This does **not** claim to fix #56699's `cudaErrorLaunchFailure` or the
FULL-graph host-mirror problem addressed by #56158.

## Duplicate work and AI assistance

Checked issue #56699 and its comments, open PRs mentioning that issue, and
open PRs matching HiSparse, unaligned, alignment, partial import, and import.
No open PR specifically addressing this admission failure was found.

- #56158 fixes FULL-graph host-mirror state, not import alignment.
- #55398 adds capacity-aware GPU landing. This patch keeps main's host-only
  placement; the two small empty-receive cleanup changes overlap with that PR
  and are reused here because sub-block prompts take the notify-only path.
- #56109 changes resident-page eviction and host-pool management.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for implementation, tests, and this
description. The submitting user confirmed review of the patch and explicitly
requested this upstream draft. GPU tests above were run by the agent; this
description does not assert that the human personally reran those commands.

title: [Bugfix][Kimi K3] Split DSpark draft out of the target MLA KV group
body:
## What

The K3-native DSpark draft marks its MLA layers `non_causal_multi_token_decode=True`. `MLAAttentionSpec.merge` ORs that flag, so when the draft's spec merges with the target's identically-shaped MLA spec, the causal target group inherits it too. That raises the group's TritonMLA reorder threshold and misroutes the target's short prefills and causal verification blocks into a decode path that expects one query row per request — producing corrupted output and illegal memory accesses during CUDA graph capture on Kimi-K3 DSpark.

Tag the draft's spec with `model_version="kimi_k3_dspark"` so the KV-cache group splitter keeps it apart from the target (`merge` requires a uniform `model_version`).

## Not a duplicate

- Distilled from #53577 (split requested in review). #55390 annotates MTP draft KV groups on the hybrid grouping path — different mechanism (positional annotation vs. model-version split) and not K3-DSpark-specific.

## Tests

- New `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_dspark_kv_group.py` (3 tests): the draft spec carries the model version, the target spec does not, and `MLAAttentionSpec.merge` refuses to combine them.
- `python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_dspark_kv_group.py -q` → 3 passed.

## Model evaluation

Verified end-to-end as part of #53577: Kimi-K3 DSpark native-draft TP8 and PP2×TP4 serving previously produced corrupted output / capture IMA without this split and are clean with it.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Size CPU cache slots for one KV group
body:
Fixes #56871.

An offload key identifies one KV cache group, but CPU slots can reserve the combined footprint of all groups. For eight equally sized, disjoint groups, a budget that should hold 16 group keys holds only two.

This change carries each selected group's byte size into the offloading config and sizes the shared slot pool for the largest group. Worker views start at the beginning of each slot for each group, preserving GPU strides, aliases, unpadded payload sizes, and partial chunks. Packed GPU layouts use group-specific transfer regions instead of copying the whole multi-group block. The layout applies to CPU offloading and the CPU primary tier of tiered offloading.

Slots remain fixed-size for secondary-tier transfers. Unequal groups can still leave unused space inside a slot. A storage-format identifier including row size separates compact rows from previously persisted rows; existing files remain on disk but are not reused. Single-group and external backends retain their existing layout by default.

## Duplicate-work check

The issue is claimed at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56871#issuecomment-5674698213. Issue discussion and open/closed PR searches were rechecked on 2026-09-15. Related work covers group eligibility (#54743), node-local sizing (#53474), capacity metrics (#53902, #56867), and worker interfaces (#56076); it does not implement this per-group slot layout.

## Validation

Base: `cd10ed6f9f6b37a8ace9cf380007e66fe12ec0c3`, after the v0.29.0 release. Linux, Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, RTX 3090.

- Capacity reproducer: all four cases fail on the unmodified base and pass with the fix. Eight equal groups hold 16 keys instead of two; unequal groups and `blocks_per_chunk=1,3` are covered.
- Configuration, factory, and shared-region suites: **142 passed**.
- CPU manager/policies, tier factories, tiered offloading, real filesystem I/O, mocked object storage, file identity, and connector scheduler suites: **422 passed**.
- GPU worker, canonical layout, and connector registration suites: **67 passed, 1 skipped** (ROCm-only test). Includes packed and aliased GPU pages, unequal groups, an empty group in a transfer, sparse chunk tails, and slot reuse across groups.
- Qwen3.5-0.8B, four cache groups, four prompts: cold generation followed by successful GPU prefix-cache reset and CPU reload. Both base and candidate load **32,907,264 bytes**. Generated token IDs and their logprobs match exactly between base and candidate; cold/reloaded token IDs also match in each run. Each reloaded prompt reports 1,088 cached tokens. Cold/reloaded logprob differences also occur identically on the base.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks pass, including mypy for Python 3.10; the manual Python 3.12 mypy hook also passes.

The GPU tests used reused native extensions with the checked-out Python sources. DeepSeek-V4.1 TP=8 production validation and throughput measurement remain outside this evidence.

The model comparison used the same standalone `model_roundtrip.py` harness from each checkout, invoked with `PYTHONPATH="$PWD" RUN_NAME=baseline` or `RUN_NAME=candidate`, using `.venv/bin/python /ch_data/wzp/oss-ai-infra/vllm-offload-groups-20260915-evidence/model_roundtrip.py`. The harness and JSON results are included in the review materials.

### Commands

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py \
```

title: [DSpark] Support PP prefill with KV transfer (disaggregated serving)
body:
## What

DSpark pipeline-parallel support, end to end: **aggregated (in-flight-batching) serving with PP targets** and **prefill on a pipeline-parallel producer with KV transfer** (PD-disaggregated serving).

This PR is self-contained: it re-applies #56956 (reverted in #58484 for further streamlining) and builds the PD producer path on top. Happy to iterate on the streamlining with you, @njhill.

Aggregated IFB PP (re-applied #56956):

- `PPHandler` broadcasts the last rank's sampled tokens (and draft tokens, for spec decode) to earlier stages on a side stream; earlier stages apply them `pp_size` steps later in a deferred post-update.
- The deferred post-update Triton kernel is pre-compiled during warmup with the exact serving specialization (int32 `idx_mapping`, 16-byte-aligned `num_sampled`/`num_rejected` via a padded combined buffer) — a mid-serving compile there would deadlock on the in-flight broadcast NCCL kernel.
- DSv4 router: pad the top-k buffer so non-last stages can drop EAGLE read-ahead rows.

PD prefill-only producer (this PR on top):

- `SpeculativeConfig.target_kv_transfer_config` + `is_dspark_prefill_only()`; NIXL is rejected for this mode (it cannot describe packed per-layer KV regions; Mooncake works).
- The scheduler narrows `use_eagle` (and eagle block-drop) for the prefill-only producer so it never does the EAGLE-style read-ahead.
- `DFlashSpeculator.materialize_context_kv()`: precompute and store draft context KV without drafting. `propose()` delegates to it when `is_dspark_prefill_only()` and returns `None`, so the model runner keeps its single call site unchanged and only skips the draft-side subsystems on the producer (rejection sampler, drafter graph capture, EPLB registration, draft-token handler) via one `dspark_prefill_only` flag. The preparation half is shared with `propose()` via `_prepare_draft_inputs()`; on the aggregated path the context-K/V store stays graph-aware as introduced by #57632 (merged here), while the producer stores eagerly (it captures no draft graph).
- The DSv4 draft in this mode builds only the attention submodule needed for prefill (`context_kv_only`) — avoiding transient MoE expert allocation — and loads just the context-KV weights (the merged `context_wkv_proj` plus per-layer `kv_norm`).

Kimi-K3 DSpark additionally relies on the TritonMLA causal multi-token fix from #51065 (merged; included in this branch's base; verified on SM120).

Split from #53577 (reviewer request).

## Tests

- `tests/config/test_dspark_prefill_only.py` (13 tests: mode detection, connector guard, last-stage drafter helper).
- `tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py` — broadcast/padding + the warmup-serving specialization match (`_post_update_kernel`).
- `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py` — input-prep kernel behavior incl. `context_only`.
- `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_profile.py` — context-K/V staging buffer stays at the draft hidden size under HC-residual targets (regression test for the fix below).
- `pytest tests/config/test_dspark_prefill_only.py tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py tests/v1/spec_decode/ -q` and `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py` → all green on this tree; pre-commit green.

## Model evaluation

Validated end-to-end on the pre-split stack (#53577 lineage): DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 DSpark PD disaggregation with PP on both sides — prefill PP2×TP2 (prefill-only DSpark producer) + decode PP2×TP2 with DSpark, Mooncake KV transfer (TCP transport): GSM8K strict-match **0.9447** (1319 samples, stderr 0.0063). This is exactly the P-PP + D-PP DSpark combination previously reported to produce garbled output.

This rebuild rebases that stack onto current main (including the #57632 context-K/V graph-capture refactor and the #58484 revert of #56956, which this PR re-applies); the rebase keeps the aggregated-path behavior and changes no model numerics.

Re-validated on this exact tree (SM120, same both-PP PD configuration, Mooncake TCP): GSM8K strict-match **0.9462** (1319 samples, threshold 0.8) — consistent with the pre-split stack's 0.9447. The re-validation caught one integration bug from the #57632 merge: the graph-captured context-K/V staging buffer was sized by the hc-widened `hidden_size` (that widening exists for MTP-style drafters whose forward eats the target's pre-hc_head residual), while DFlash only ever stores `combine_hidden_states` output there — fixed in `103ffe9e9e` by sizing it from the draft's own hidden size, with a regression test.

After the review-driven streamlining (model_runner.py diff down from 197 to 66 changed lines: the producer branch moved behind `propose()`, and `warmup_pp_decode_update` moved to warmup.py), re-validated again on HEAD `b2952d32d0` (SM120):

- Aggregated IFB PP2×TP2: GSM8K strict-match **0.9545** (1319 samples).
- Both-PP PD, Mooncake TCP: GSM8K strict-match **0.9431** (1319 samples). (Run on a host whose GPU P2P is disabled at the NCCL level for an unrelated IOMMU issue — transport-level only, no effect on the correctness paths under test.)

Infrastructure flakes observed during validation are unrelated to this PR: the known Mooncake bootstrap 5s HTTP timeout (#58543) on cold-start/high-load attempts, and a harness abort-mode teardown racing its GPU-memory cleanup check on one passing run.

title: [Feature] Add Responses Session Store for cross-request incremental token reuse
body:
## Purpose Multi-turn and agentic conversations against the Responses API resend the whole conversation on every request, so vLLM re-renders and re-tokenizes the full history even though only the latest turn is new. This PR adds a server-side Responses Session Store that keeps a session's tokenized history, so a follow-up request can reuse it and send only its new input. The store is disabled by default and opt-in per service: ```bash vllm serve /path/to/model \ --responses-store-config '{"enabled":true}' \ --responses-store-disk-path ./response-store-data/responses.sqlite3 \ --responses-store-key-file ./response-store-data/key ``` Two new `ResponsesRequest` fields, both defaulting to `false` and requiring the `x-session-id` header, drive the feature: `use_store` persists the token IDs added by a request, and `use_incremental_token` reuses the stored history for the next one. Existing behavior is unchanged when the store is disabled. **Feature documentation:** [vllm/docs/features/response_store/README.md](https://github.com/jwkkkkkkdada/vllm/tree/response-store-pr/docs/features/response_store) (covers requirements, the full `--responses-store-config` reference, usage examples, request-time errors, and encryption/restart semantics). ### Changes - `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/store/` — new package: memory and SQLite tiers with a tiered coordinator, TTL/LRU cleanup and eviction policy, framed AES-GCM encryption with key providers and automatic key rotation, metrics, and the service that owns the background tasks. - `responses/protocol.py`, `responses/serving.py`, `responses/api_router.py` — request fields, incremental prompt merge and single `save()` per completed request (streaming, non-streaming, background, tool follow-ups), `x-session-id` response header and 503 error mapping. - `tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py` — incremental chat-template encoding without a duplicate BOS. - Launchers (`app.py`, `cli_args.py`, `utils/server_utils.py`, `cli/serve.py`) — CLI arguments, lifespan start/close, and rejection of key-file mode with multiple API server processes. - `requirements/common.txt` — adds `cryptography`. - `docs/features/response_store/README.md` — feature documentation. ### Design notes - **Memory first, disk as a recovery tier.** Disk `save()` only enqueues; a single background writer batches concurrent writes into one SQLite transaction, so request completion never waits on disk I/O. - **Incremental disk writes.** Token IDs are stored as independently encrypted AES-GCM frames, so appending a turn never decrypts existing history. - **Only complete versions are readable.** Version bookkeeping makes reads fall back to a full rerender while the newest delta is pending or after a failed flush, instead of reusing stale history. - **Conditional eviction.** A memory copy is evicted only after a same-version readable disk copy is validated; guards and delete tombstones prevent in-flight batches from resurrecting deleted sessions. - **Keys.** Ephemeral by default; a key file persists key metadata and drives an atomic 90-day database-wide rotation with interrupted-rotation recovery. Session rows are always cleared at startup, including across restarts. ## Test Plan ```bash uv run --no-sync .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_cli_args.py \ tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_responses_store_lifespan.py \ tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_store_config.py \ tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_store_recovery.py \ tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py ``` ## Test Result Using DeepSeek-V4-Flash as an example, we ran performance benchmarks on 4 NPUs with the AISBench tool. The output len is fixed at 500. The comparison of results before and after vLLM framework optimization is shown below: The comparison result of output token throughput: The comparison result of TTFT

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Reuse physical top-k selection across decode layers
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 FlashMLA Decode maps the same index source's logical top-k to physical KV slots separately in the source layer and each Reuse follower. This opt-in change publishes exact physical indices and lengths once per eligible index-source group, then lets followers read them from one graph-stable buffer. The compressed-cache metadata is fresh for each forward and records the source layer and SWA metadata identity, so a new source, request ordering, block table, or validity path recomputes the selection. Ordinary single-token Decode without microbatching, PCP, or DCP is eligible; mixed Prefill, speculative query layouts, other attention backends, and unsupported capacities use the original path. Enable it with `--attention-config '{"dsv41_reuse_physical_selection":true}'`.

This does not duplicate #41105, which fuses one DeepSeek-V4 top-k with page-table translation, or #56254, which scores only candidate blocks in the DeepSeek-V4.1 indexer. This change reuses an already selected source's exact global physical indices and lengths across its V4.1 Reuse followers; it does not change logical top-k, SWA metadata, cache records, or floating-point model computation.

title: [KV Connector] Save decode-phase Mamba states and fingerprint MooncakeStoreConnector keys
body:
## Purpose

Hybrid Mamba/GDN models could not reuse KV cache from a shared Mooncake store past the prompt end.

Decode-phase Mamba boundary states were never stored: the scheduler dropped every boundary-state hand-off past `prefill_end_tokens` and skipped the `kv_consumer` role, so only the full-attention groups wrote decode blocks. A store lookup intersects all cache groups, so external hits stopped exactly at the prompt end even though the attention groups held the decode blocks.

This change claims every retained boundary once `save_decode_cache` is on, since all groups store each block as it fills, lets a decode-saving consumer claim finish-time partial tails too, and warns at startup when `--prefix-cache-retention-interval 0` leaves no Mamba boundary to save. It covers the hybrid half of the Decode-Phase KV Cache Put roadmap item (#45036).

Store keys also did not encode the settings that decide a block's bytes (KV cache dtype, model dtype, quantization, Mamba cache dtypes, block sizes, stored cache-group specs, parallel layout), so two instances of one model directory with different settings could read each other's blocks. They are now folded into a 12-hex-digit digest carried by every key as `@cfg:<digest>`; namespaces that already pin store TP and PP contribute only PCP and DCP. Existing store contents become unreachable after upgrading, which the usage guide states.

The closest open work touches the same files but not these behaviours: #54307 and #53078 (heterogeneous TP sharing for hybrid KV cache), #56615 (EAGLE/DSpark-drop-induced Mamba misses).

Fixes #56972.

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_layout.py
```

End-to-end on 8xH20, Mooncake in standalone-store mode over TCP, `--mamba-cache-mode
align`, `--prefix-cache-retention-interval` set to the resolved scheduler block size.
Producer: 1200 prompt tokens plus 1300 generated, which fills four blocks. Consumer: a
fresh instance whose first request is the continuation prompt, so it either loads those
blocks from the store or recomputes them.

| Setup (Qwen3.5-2B GDN hybrid and a 4000-token continuation unless noted) | block | external hit | TTFT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pre-change sources | 544 | 1088 (prompt end) | 0.202 s |
| this PR, same model and prompt | 544 | **2176** | **0.186 s** |
| no cache anywhere, same model and prompt | 544 | 0 | 0.236 s (0.231 s on the pre-change build) |
| this PR, `save_decode_cache=false` | 544 | 1088 | |
| this PR, random-weight Qwen3-Next hybrid, 2500-token continuation | 544 | **2176** | |
| this PR, Qwen3.5-4B GDN hybrid | 528 | **2112** | 0.316 s (cold 0.411 s) |
| this PR, TP=2 / CUDA graph / ngram spec decode | 544 / 544 / 576 | 2176 / 2176 / 2304 | |
| this PR, 8 concurrent requests | 544 | 2176 each (17408 total) | |

## Test Result

- 272 passed in the unit suites; 11 of the new assertions fail against the pre-change
  sources, so they pin the behaviour rather than the implementation.
- On the same model and prompt, this PR moves the external hit from 1088 to 2176 tokens,
  i.e. every block-aligned block of the continuation, and TTFT from 0.202 s to 0.186 s. The
  no-cache baseline is about 0.23 s on both builds, so the delta comes from the hit
  coverage and not from anything else in the change. Without `save_decode_cache` the hit
  stays at 1088.
- The 4B model shows the same shape at a larger block: 2112 of 4000 tokens, TTFT 0.316 s
  against 0.411 s with no cache.
- Divided out, recomputing a token costs about 59 us (2B) and 103 us (4B) against about
  36 us and 58 us to load one: the load is transfer-bound and the recompute is
  compute-bound, so the win grows with model size and link speed (measured over TCP, not
  RDMA).
- Greedy 32-token continuations are token-for-token identical to a cold recompute, and a
  consumer configured with a different `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` or `--dtype` logs a
  different digest and reads nothing from the producer.

## AI assistance

Developed with AI assistance and reviewed line by line by the submitter.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Reuse prefill main-KV gathers across decoder groups
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 decoder CSA2 groups currently dequantize and gather the same compressed main-KV prefix into a BF16 prefill workspace once per layer, although the four layers share one KV source. This change adds an opt-in, model-owned BF16 buffer with a strict 0–512 MiB budget: the first eligible layer gathers main-KV, its three followers reuse that exact region while each refreshes its own SWA region, and the next group or forward repopulates the buffer. The initial gate covers one-request FlashMLA prefill without DBO, PCP, DCP, or sequence parallelism; unsupported shapes and over-budget gathers use the existing path. It preserves the packed cache format, logical selections, and BF16 attention input. 

This does not duplicate #42504, which adds a single sparse-gather primitive without cross-layer reuse, or #56752, which trims decoder rows and changes the cold-prefill output contract; #54592 targets a quantized DeepSeek-V4 prefill kernel rather than exact DeepSeek-V4.1 BF16 group reuse.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Keep FP8 Engram rows packed through TP exchange
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram's CPU/UVA lookup currently expands checkpoint FP8 values and UE8M0 scales into BF16 before the TP head all-gather. This opt-in change stages each selected head as FP8 value bytes followed by its original scale bytes, exchanges one `uint8` payload, then reconstructs the existing BF16 tensor once before `wkv`. At head dimension 256 and 32-value scale blocks, the TP payload is 264 instead of 512 bytes per head row; this is a byte-count reduction, not a measured serving speedup. The original BF16 lookup and exchange remain the fallback for small batches and unsupported configurations.

Enable it with `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"packed_fp8_exchange":true,"packed_fp8_exchange_min_tokens":256}'`. The initial path requires effective Engram-DP size 1, TP>1, non-SP execution, no microbatching/PCP/DCP, and a head dimension divisible by the scale block size. The token threshold is a conservative policy knob pending target-hardware crossover measurements. Persistent packed staging keeps the asynchronous UVA lookup's addresses stable; all TP ranks select the same representation from the batch shape, and the post-exchange dequantization uses the same FP8-to-FP32, UE8M0 exponent and BF16 rounding sequence as the current lookup. `wkv` and the public Engram output contract are unchanged.

This does not duplicate #56929, which begins with a BF16 collective result and fuses head reordering with WKV activation quantization, or #56435, which changes SP redistribution to all-to-all. #56512 supplies the existing CPU/UVA prefetch that this path reuses. If those PRs land, the non-SP transport boundary and end-to-end crossover must be remeasured on the rebased head.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix][DCP] Validate the retention interval against the right block size
body:
## Purpose

**On ROCm under decode context parallelism, a legal `prefix_cache_retention_interval` is rejected, and the user is forced to checkpoint 8x more coarsely than the cache can use.**

### Background

Sliding-window and Mamba (linear-attention) groups cannot prefix-cache densely, so vLLM keeps periodic *checkpoints*, and a prefix-cache hit can only resume from one. `prefix_cache_retention_interval` sets how far apart those checkpoints sit.

A checkpoint is only useful where a hit can actually land, so the interval has to be a multiple of the hit granularity. That is what the validator is for.

### The two block sizes

vLLM has two, and they are computed as opposites (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`):

| | definition | property |
|---|---|---|
| `scheduler_block_size` | `math.lcm(*group_block_sizes)` | the **coarsest** common boundary — a block boundary in *every* group at once |
| `hash_block_size` | `math.gcd(*hashing_sizes)` | the **finest** common step — a valid boundary in every group, but not in all of them simultaneously |

Which one a hit is reported at depends on whether fine-grained partial hash hits are enabled. vLLM already encodes this, in `_cache_hit_alignment_tokens`:

```python
return (
    self.hash_block_size
    if self.enable_partial_hash_hits
    else self.scheduler_block_size
)
```

The validator, however, checks `retention_interval % scheduler_block_size` unconditionally.

### Why DCP exposes it

Without DCP the two values are typically equal and nothing is visibly wrong. DCP scales the full-attention group's block by `dcp_world_size`, which **raises the LCM and leaves the GCD alone**.

On a model with a 1536-token linear-attention block at DCP=8, the scaled full-attention block is 12288:

```
scheduler_block_size = lcm(1536, 12288) = 12288
hash_block_size      = gcd(1536, 12288) =  1536
```

So hits land every **1536** tokens, while the validator demands a multiple of **12288**. A user asking to checkpoint exactly where hits land is refused, and has to go 8x coarser — quantising every hit to a span the cache never reports, which costs prefix-cache hit rate.

### How it got this way

The validator was correct when written. `_validate_prefix_cache_retention_interval` arrived in **#43447** (2026-06-04), when `scheduler_block_size` was the only hit granularity there was.

**#46384** (2026-07-12) then added partial prefix-cache hits for hybrid models, introducing a *second*, finer granularity along with `enable_partial_hash_hits` and `_cache_hit_alignment_tokens` to express which one applies. The validator was not updated to ask.

So this is not a wrong check; it is a check left behind by a later change, and it only becomes visible when something pulls the two granularities apart. DCP is that something.

### The fix

`_cache_hit_alignment_tokens` is already the right answer, but it cannot simply be substituted into the base validator: it depends on `enable_partial_hash_hits`, which only the concrete coordinator resolves, after the base constructor has run.

So the check is split:

- the **base validator** keeps the checks that do not need alignment (non-negative; the "no sliding-window or Mamba group" rejection);
- a new **`_validate_retention_alignment`** runs once the coordinator has settled the granularity.

`HybridKVCacheCoordinator` passes the alignment it just computed. `UnitaryKVCacheCoordinator` never enables partial hash hits, so it passes `scheduler_block_size`.

The unitary path deliberately does **not** call `_cache_hit_alignment_tokens`: that property is defined on `HybridKVCacheCoordinator`, so reaching for it there raises `AttributeError` during construction — a boot failure for every single-group model. An earlier revision of this change did exactly that, so a test now pins which class owns the property.

### Relationship to #52527

**#52527** ("[Metrics] Report shared-prefix tokens lost to a missing sparse-retention checkpoint") is open and touches the same function, so whichever lands second will need a small rebase around `_validate_prefix_cache_retention_interval`.

The two are complementary rather than competing: #52527 *measures* prefix tokens lost to a missing retention checkpoint, and this PR removes one cause of those misses — a validator that forces checkpoints 8x sparser than the cache can use. Landing both gives you the metric and one fewer reason for it to fire.

Two other open PRs touch this file in unrelated regions: **#53479** (Mamba align) in the constructors, and **#50457** (all-sliding DFlash drafter) in `allocate_new_blocks`. Neither overlaps the lines changed here.

### Scope

**Scoped to ROCm**, which is the only platform where this has been tested. DCP is not backend-specific — `flashmla`, `flashmla_sparse`, `flashinfer_mla_sparse` and `flashattn_mla` all carry DCP support — so other platforms may well have the same latent mismatch. We have no way to exercise them, so we are not changing their behaviour on an untested claim.

**Off ROCm the original `scheduler_block_size` check is kept, not deferred.** This is the subtle part of gating: the alignment check now runs in a new place, so simply gating that new call would leave other platforms with *no* alignment validation at all — weaker than the status quo, not safer. Instead the base validator keeps its original check verbatim for them, and only ROCm takes the deferred, granularity-aware path. There is a test asserting the original rejection still fires off ROCm.

Within ROCm, the change only alters which value the interval is compared against; it does not change what a valid interval *does*.

If maintainers would like this widened once someone can test it on CUDA, the gate is a single condition in each of the two validators.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_retention_interval_alignment.py

# regression check on the neighbouring coordinator/utils suite
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
```

The new tests are CPU-only and call the validators directly. They pin:

1. an interval equal to the hit alignment is accepted — the DCP case that used to be rejected;
2. an interval that cannot land on a hit boundary is still rejected;
3. `None` (dense) and `0` (latest boundary only) skip the check, since neither describes a spacing;
4. a multiple of the alignment is accepted;
5. **the regression itself** — 1536 accepted against `hash_block_size`, rejected against the DCP-scaled `scheduler_block_size`, which is the before/after in one test;
6. the base validator still rejects a negative interval;
7. the base validator no longer checks alignment, so the DCP case can reach the deferred check at all;
8. `_cache_hit_alignment_tokens` belongs to the hybrid coordinator and not the unitary one — the `AttributeError` guard described above;
9. **off ROCm, the original `scheduler_block_size` rejection still fires**, a scheduler-aligned interval is still accepted, and the deferred check is inert — i.e. behaviour there is byte-for-byte what it is today.

## Test Result

```
tests/v1/core/test_retention_interval_alignment.py   12 passed
```

The platform is patched rather than detected, so both branches are exercised on any runner.

**The tests have power, they are not merely green.** Two independent mutations each turn the expected tests red:

```
drop the off-ROCm fallback:     1 failed, 11 passed   (other platforms lose validation)
drop the ROCm alignment check:  2 failed, 10 passed   (the fix itself)
both present:                  12 passed
```
The first mutation is the one worth noting: it catches the failure mode that gating naively would have introduced.

No new failures in `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`.

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes in full, including `ruff`, `mypy` 3.10-3.13, `typos` and `check-spdx-header`.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Implement get_top_tokens() on the generic MTP drafter
body:
## Purpose

`speculative_config.use_local_argmax_reduction` is unusable with the generic MTP
drafter: enabling it does not fall back to a slower path, it fails engine startup.

```
ValueError: use_local_argmax_reduction is enabled but draft model DeepSeekMTP
does not implement get_top_tokens().
```

The reduction itself already lives in core as `LogitsProcessor.get_top_tokens()` — each
TP rank argmaxes its own vocab shard and only `(value, index)` pairs are gathered. Both
opt-in sites probe the draft model for the method and raise without it:

- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py` (V2 model runner)
- `vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py`

`vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_mtp.py` has `compute_logits` but no
`get_top_tokens`, so every checkpoint that resolves to it raises. On current `main` that
is the `deepseek_v3` family — DeepSeek-V3 and R1 — on every platform:

| checkpoint `model_type` | architecture | resolved draft class | platform |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek_v3` | `DeepSeekMTPModel` | `deepseek_mtp.DeepSeekMTP` | all |
| `deepseek_v32`, `glm_moe_dsa` | `DeepseekV32MTPModel` | `deepseek_mtp.DeepSeekMTP` | XPU, CPU only |

`DeepSeekMTPModel` maps to `deepseek_mtp` in `registry.py` with no platform dispatch, so a
DeepSeek-V3 / R1 MTP drafter is this class on CUDA and ROCm alike. `deepseek_v32` and
`glm_moe_dsa` are dispatched in `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/__init__.py`: CUDA uses
`nvidia/mtp.py`, which already implements the method, and since #51915 ROCm uses
`amd/mtp.py`. So for the DSA family only XPU and CPU still fall back here. `amd/mtp.py`'s
own `DeepseekV32MTP` has the same gap, but it is a different file with its own pre-head
path and is out of scope for this PR.

This PR adds the two forwarding methods, mirroring the `compute_logits` pair already in
the file. The capability has been rolled out per model since the flag landed in #34049,
and `deepseek_v3` was never covered on any platform.

### Which checkpoints this actually reaches

Resolving real `config.json`s through `hf_config_override` and the registry on
`main@94f4170df3` (ROCm), then asking the speculator's own question
(`hasattr(cls, "get_top_tokens")`). Of the current flagship checkpoints that ship MTP
layers at all:

| verdict | checkpoints |
|---|---|
| **reached by this PR** | DeepSeek-R1-0528 (fp8 and MXFP4) |
| already had the method | GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next` → `Glm5NextMTP`) |
| still blocked, different class | DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3 (ROCm: `amd/mtp.py`); DeepSeek-V4-Flash / -Pro, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MiniMax-M3 |

What it does not reach matters as much. On ROCm the DSA family now has its own drafter
class, as do the DeepSeek-V4 line and MiniMax-M3; on CUDA the DSA family already works
through `nvidia/mtp.py`. Kimi-K3, Qwen3.5-397B, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Qwen3-Next-80B ship
no MTP layers in the checkpoints checked.

### Scope

Resolving every entry of `_SPECULATIVE_DECODING_MODELS` on `main@94f4170df3` and asking
`hasattr`, 27 of the 62 speculative architectures satisfy the guard and 34 do not, so this
flag is broadly unavailable rather than uniquely broken here. 24 of the 27 get it from
`LocalArgmaxMixin` (the EAGLE, DFlash and DSpark families, plus Qwen3.5 MTP); only
`Gemma4MTP`, `InklingMTP` and `Glm5NextMTP` write the method themselves (plus
`DeepseekV32MTP` in the CUDA-only `nvidia/mtp.py`).

This PR fixes one of the 34 rather than sweeping them, because the correct call differs
per family and getting it wrong is silent:

- `deepseek_mtp.py`'s draft layer returns `(pre-final-norm, post-final-norm)` and the
  proposer consumes the first element, so `compute_logits` — and therefore
  `get_top_tokens` — must apply `shared_head` (the final RMSNorm).
- `deepseek_v32/nvidia/mtp.py`'s layer returns the post-norm hidden in both tuple
  positions, so its `get_top_tokens` correctly applies the LM head only.

Reusing the second form in the first file does not raise; it just returns a different
draft token. The added test is built to fail in that case (see Test Result). Extending
this to the remaining families needs the same per-family check, which is better done in
separate PRs by people who can run those models.

A second commit amends the flag's own docstring. It currently says only "reduces
communication from O(vocab_size) to O(2 * tp_size)", which reads as unconditional; the
measurements below show it is a break-even-dependent trade, and low-concurrency serving
at high TP is the case where the current wording would mislead someone into enabling it.

`LocalArgmaxMixin` in `models/interfaces.py` is the right tool where it fits, and
`Qwen3_5MTP` shows it fits some MTP models: it owns a flat `self.lm_head` and its
`compute_logits` is just `self.logits_processor(self.lm_head, hidden_states)`. This class
is not like that. It has no `self.lm_head` at all — the head is
`self.layers[str(mtp_start + spec_step_idx)].shared_head.head`, chosen per draft step,
and the hidden state has to pass through `shared_head`'s norm first. The mixin reads
`self.lm_head` and applies no norm, so it cannot serve this class.

### What this cannot affect

`use_local_argmax_reduction` defaults to `False`, and every call site of
`get_top_tokens` is behind it — no site probes for the method to auto-enable anything.
With the flag off, this PR adds two unreachable methods and changes nothing.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_local_argmax.py
pytest tests/v1/sample/test_head_dtype.py   # existing coverage of get_top_tokens
```

New `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_local_argmax.py` builds a real `SharedHead`
(RMSNorm + `ParallelLMHead`) and `LogitsProcessor` on a single vocab shard and asserts
`get_top_tokens()` picks the same token as `compute_logits().argmax(-1)`, including with
a padded vocab. The norm's weight is given a non-uniform gain on purpose: the argmax is
invariant to the norm's per-row rescale, so a default all-ones weight would let a
skipped `shared_head` pass unnoticed.

End to end, on a `deepseek_v3` checkpoint (DeepSeek-R1-0528, official fp8 weights) at TP=4,
with a fresh server per run:

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528 -tp 4 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1,
                         "use_local_argmax_reduction":true}'
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --num-prompts 288 \
  --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos --seed 1234 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
```

The base arm is upstream `main` with the flag off; with it on, `main` raises at engine
init.

## Test Result

Hardware for every number below: MI355X (gfx950), ROCm. Correctness and micro numbers
are at real model shapes in bf16 at TP=2 and TP=4; GSM8K and end to end are
DeepSeek-R1-0528 (official fp8 weights) at TP=4 against `main@94f4170df3`.

### Correctness

`tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_local_argmax.py`: 3 passed. Mutating the patch to drop
`shared_head` from `get_top_tokens` turns 2 of the 3 into failures, so the equivalence
assertion is load-bearing rather than decorative.

`tests/v1/sample/test_head_dtype.py`: identical results with and without this PR
(7 passed, 1 pre-existing failure in the `core_model` e2e test, which downloads
`facebook/opt-125m`).

Token-for-token equivalence over a sweep at real model shapes, **TP=2**, batch sizes 1 to
1024: **agreement 1.0000 in all 20 cases**. Cross-rank tie-breaking is the part a
single-shard test cannot reach, and it agrees too. The same sweep run against a variant
that skips `shared_head` agrees on as little as **0 %** of tokens.

Before this PR, the `vllm serve` / `vllm bench` invocation above raises the `ValueError`
at engine init. After it, both workers log

```
Using local argmax reduction for draft token generation
(communication: O(2*tp_size) vs O(vocab_size)).
```

and generation completes.

### Accuracy (GSM8K)

A vocab-parallel argmax is a reduction-order change, so "the unit tests pass" does not
cover it. On DeepSeek-R1-0528, all 1319 items, 5-shot greedy: **no measurable accuracy
change on GSM8K, within the base-repeat noise floor.** Patched scores 0.9568 against
0.9530 / 0.9560 for two runs of `main` — a base-vs-base drift of 0.0030, which the
patched-vs-second-base difference (+0.0008) sits well inside. Per-sample agreement is
inside the same control range. Full table in the comment below.

### Micro benchmark

The two providers on a real vLLM process group with a real `SharedHead` and
`LogitsProcessor`, driven through the patched predictor so the only difference between
arms is the collective:

- baseline — `compute_logits(h).argmax(-1)`, what the drafter does today
- patched — `get_top_tokens(h)`

Five interleaved pairs per point, arm order alternated per pair, 300 iterations after
100 warmup, no other tenant on the box. The `delta` column is what actually matters:
both arms pay the same per-call launch overhead (~200 µs in this harness, which times
the sampling step in isolation), so the *percentage* exaggerates the cost at small batch
and the absolute difference does not.

**TP=2**, GLM-5.2 shapes (`hidden_size` 6144, `vocab_size` 154880) / DeepSeek-V3 shapes
(7168, 129280):

| batch | GLM base | GLM patch | GLM delta | DSV3 base | DSV3 patch | DSV3 delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1    |  204.2 µs | 228.4 µs |    +24 µs |  222.4 µs | 219.2 µs |     -3 µs |
| 8    |  252.4 µs | 270.7 µs |    +18 µs |  251.7 µs | 271.1 µs |    +19 µs |
| 16   |  287.4 µs | 269.1 µs |    -18 µs |  273.0 µs | 273.4 µs |     +0 µs |
| 32   |  354.1 µs | 271.7 µs |    -82 µs |  317.0 µs | 270.4 µs |    -47 µs |
| 64   |  473.8 µs | 287.0 µs |   -187 µs |  398.8 µs | 271.7 µs |   -127 µs |
| 128  |  713.5 µs | 318.1 µs |   -395 µs |  598.6 µs | 299.1 µs |   -300 µs |
| 256  | 1202.4 µs | 364.8 µs |   -838 µs |  922.6 µs | 298.7 µs |   -624 µs |
| 512  | 2166.8 µs | 535.2 µs |  -1632 µs | 1778.0 µs | 494.3 µs |  -1284 µs |
| 1024 | 4124.6 µs | 848.3 µs |  -3276 µs | 3289.3 µs | 811.0 µs |  -2478 µs |

Within-arm spread over the five pairs is ≤ 1 % for 34 of the 40 arms and ≤ 4.7 %
everywhere, and the per-pair deltas are tight (e.g. GLM bs=128: +55.2, +55.4, +55.4,
+55.3, +55.4 %).

**TP=4**, same shapes, same protocol:

| batch | GLM base | GLM patch | GLM delta | DSV3 base | DSV3 patch | DSV3 delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1    |  218.5 µs | 308.2 µs |    +90 µs |  224.5 µs | 314.0 µs |    +90 µs |
| 32   |  286.3 µs | 382.3 µs |    +96 µs |  294.7 µs | 395.2 µs |   +100 µs |
| 64   |  317.6 µs | 384.5 µs |    +67 µs |  295.2 µs | 393.3 µs |    +98 µs |
| 128  |  443.9 µs | 392.2 µs |    -52 µs |  379.6 µs | 385.2 µs |     +6 µs |
| 256  |  710.0 µs | 387.6 µs |   -322 µs |  573.1 µs | 391.7 µs |   -181 µs |
| 512  | 1322.0 µs | 385.9 µs |   -936 µs | 1003.5 µs | 386.8 µs |   -617 µs |
| 1024 | 2583.3 µs | 579.0 µs |  -2004 µs | 1854.6 µs | 488.9 µs |  -1366 µs |

So the trade is a **fixed per-step overhead — one extra small collective, ~20 µs at TP=2
and ~95 µs at TP=4 — against a gather that grows with `batch × vocab_size`.** The patched
arm is nearly batch-independent (382–392 µs across bs=1..512 at TP=4); the baseline is
not. Break-even draft batch is **≈ 16–32 at TP=2 and ≈ 128–256 at TP=4**, and it moves
right as `tp` grows because the reduction's own collective is latency-bound while the
gather it replaces is bandwidth-bound.

Being explicit about the cost: **below break-even this is a regression**, up to -41 % of
the sampling step at TP=4 bs=1 (which is +90 µs in absolute terms). A batch-size median
is a bad summary here since it just reflects which batch sizes one tabulates; the
crossover and the absolute delta are the honest statement. The flag is opt-in, so the
decision can be made per deployment, and the numbers above are what it should be made on.

Token agreement was asserted at every point before timing: **1.0000 in all 40 cases
across TP=2 and TP=4.** Cross-rank tie-breaking is what a single-shard test cannot
reach, and it agrees at both rank counts.

Communication per draft step, derived from `logits_processor.py` rather than measured:
the default path materializes a `[batch, vocab_size]` logits tensor on every rank, the
reduction gathers `[batch, 2 * tp_size]` fp32 instead.

| model | `vocab_size` | tp | batch | default | reduction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V3 | 129280 | 2 | 512 | 126.2 MiB | 8.0 KiB |
| GLM-5.2 | 154880 | 2 | 512 | 151.2 MiB | 8.0 KiB |
| GLM-5.2 | 154880 | 8 | 1024 | 302.5 MiB | 64.0 KiB |

### End to end

DeepSeek-R1-0528 at TP=4, the invocation in the Test Plan, median of three runs per arm
after one warm-up:

| metric | `main` | this PR, flag on | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total tok/s | 5764.9 | 5812.4 | +0.8 % |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 29.49 | 29.49 | 0.0 % |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 332.0 | 328.7 | −1.0 % |

**Flat, which is what the micro numbers predict for this point.** Concurrency 64 puts the
draft batch at 64, below the TP=4 break-even, where the reduction costs ~+70–100 µs per
step — about 0.3 % of a 29.5 ms TPOT, under the ~5 % within-arm spread of throughput.
So at this operating point the flag costs nothing measurable. The gain needs a draft batch
above break-even, i.e. higher concurrency at TP=4, or TP=2. Per-run numbers, including
mean TPOT and TTFT, are in the comment below.

---

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom); reviewed and measured by hand.

title: [Rust Frontend] Normalize native renderer reasoning controls
body:
## Purpose

Normalize reasoning behavior across the native Rust renderers for DeepSeek V3.2/V4/V4.1, Harmony, Inkling, and Kimi K3.

### Behavior changes

1. **Apply deployment defaults.** Native renderers now consume reasoning controls from `default_chat_template_kwargs`, with request controls taking precedence over deployment controls and model defaults. An enabled request without a concrete effort can inherit deployment effort. Each source validates its selected input types before fallback.
2. **Unify control precedence.** `thinking` takes precedence over `enable_thinking`, and the top-level request effort takes precedence over kwargs effort. Explicit disabling discards effort; explicit enabling with `reasoning_effort="none"` inherits an enabled default effort. A standalone `"none"` disables reasoning.
3. **Align model input handling.** DeepSeek V3.2 recognizes standard effort as a thinking control; V4 and Harmony consume kwargs effort; V4.1 and Inkling follow the shared toggle/effort rules. K3 consumes standard `reasoning_effort` and ignores input `thinking_effort`. Model adapters retain their supported effort grades and ranges.
4. **Expose the resolved state downstream.** `effective_template_kwargs` now reflects the same mode and model-mapped effort used to build the prompt, including defaults. Both thinking aliases are synchronized; disabled reasoning exports `reasoning_effort="none"`. K3 also exports derived `thinking_effort` when enabled and removes it when disabled.
5. **Validate controls as request errors.** Selected thinking controls must be booleans, and active effort inputs must be strings or numbers; null effort means omitted. Invalid controls and unsupported model effort map to HTTP 400 `invalid_request_error`, including cases previously classified as template errors.

HF template input handling is preserved.

Related work: #52739 covers Python effort remapping, #56708 covers Python DeepSeek flag precedence, and #54198 covers Python behavior documentation. This PR implements shared source resolution and prompt/kwargs consistency for Rust native renderers.

AI assistance: Codex assisted with implementation and validation.

## Test Plan

```bash
cd rust
cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server
cargo clippy -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo check --workspace --all-targets
cargo fmt --all --check
```

Run pre-commit on changed files. Use a short, private `TMPDIR` for tests that create Unix sockets and serial-test locks.

## Test Result

785/785 chat/server tests passed, including all 19 real-model tokenizer/renderer/parser roundtrips. Coverage includes control precedence, request/deployment fallback, model effort validation, HTTP input boundaries, HF raw inputs, and prompt/kwargs consistency. Clippy, workspace check, formatting, and pre-commit passed.

Validation is CPU-only; GPU generation and accuracy evaluation were omitted for this change.

title: [Feature][Spec Decode] Support MiniCPM5-2B-DSpark
body:
### Motivation

OpenBMB recently released `openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B-DSpark`, an official DSpark draft model paired with `openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B`.

The draft model is relatively small:

* 5 draft layers
* ~324M parameters
* 7 draft tokens per forward
* target hidden-state layers: `[1, 10, 20, 30, 39]`

OpenBMB currently documents DSpark deployment with SGLang, while MiniCPM5 DSpark does not appear to have an explicitly validated path in vLLM.

Since vLLM already has generic DSpark infrastructure, it would be useful to bring up and validate this model pair as a lightweight single-GPU DSpark configuration.

### Proposed scope

* Bring up `openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B` with `openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B-DSpark`
* Verify draft checkpoint loading and target hidden-state extraction
* Validate DSpark proposal / verification correctness
* Compare output correctness against non-speculative decoding
* Measure acceptance length and decode throughput
* Add a lightweight regression test if suitable
* Add a documented launch configuration / example

A likely configuration is:

```bash
vllm serve openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B \
  --speculative-config '{
    "method": "dspark",
    "model": "openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B-DSpark",
    "num_speculative_tokens": 7
  }'
```

### Related

There are existing generic DSpark issues such as #50851. I intend to keep this issue focused on MiniCPM5 model-family bring-up and validation, and reuse/fix the generic DSpark path rather than introduce model-specific machinery unnecessarily.

I'd like to work on this.

### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug **Environment** - vLLM 0.27.1 (pip wheel), torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.126.09, Linux 5.15. - One RTX 4090 (sm_89). Attention: `TRITON_MLA` (the only MLA backend on sm_89) with the `FLASH_ATTN` MLA prefill backend; `TRITON Fp8 MoE`; `CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`. - Server: `vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --trust-remote-code --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 4096` (default execution mode: torch.compile + CUDA graphs; prefix caching on). The KV pool size and `--num-gpu-blocks-override` make no difference (checked both ways). As soon as **three or more** sequences are decoded in the same batch, **every request in the batch returns NaN log-probs** (HTTP 400 "Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan" when `logprobs` is requested; without `logprobs` the text is garbage, e.g. `"should should should ..."`). The engine logs nothing: no warning, no error, just NaN in the logits. | concurrent greedy requests (prompt 10-115 words, decode 16-640 tokens) | default (compile + CUDA graphs) | `--enforce-eager` | |---|---|---| | 1, or 2 (joining during the first's prefill or its decode) | fine | fine | | 3 (three repeats), 4, 5, 8, 16, 24, 32 | NaN on every request (in some 4-request rounds one survives) | fine, 3 and 5 alike | Preemption is not involved (the preemption counter stays at 0 up to 8 concurrent requests). Isolating the execution mode: | server | K=2 | K=3 | K=5 | |---|---|---|---| | default (torch.compile + CUDA graphs) | fine | NaN x3 | NaN x5 | | same, default KV pool size | fine | NaN x3 | NaN x5 | | torch.compile on, `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}'` | fine | **fine** | **fine** | | `--enforce-eager` | fine | fine | fine | | default mode, `--max-num-seqs 2` | fine | fine (never three in a batch) | fine | So the NaN comes from **CUDA-graph replay of a decode batch of three or more sequences** on the `TRITON_MLA` + online-FP8 path; inductor alone is fine and the block pool is irrelevant. `--enforce-eager` or `cudagraph_mode: NONE` fixes it; `--max-num-seqs 2` sidesteps it. Online FP8 is the documented way to fit this model on a 24 GB card (the bf16 checkpoint is 32 GB), and the default configuration produces garbage for every request the moment the server has three in flight. ### Reproducer Standalone (only `httpx`), against a default server on one 4090: 1, 2, then 3 concurrent 16-token greedy requests with `logprobs`. Expected: three HTTP 200 rounds. Observed: 200, 200, then three HTTP 400 (`... not JSON compliant: nan`); with `--enforce-eager`, three 200s. vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --trust-remote-code --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 4096 --port 8000 python3 repro_dsv2lite_fp8_nan.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 # --k 3 (default), try --k 5 ```python # Standalone reproducer (no dependency on this repo): DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat with online FP8 on an # RTX 4090 (sm89, TRITON_MLA) returns NaN log-probs / garbage text as soon as three requests are # decoded in the same batch; two are fine; --enforce-eager or --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}' is fine # (torch.compile without CUDA graphs), so the fault is in CUDA-graph replay of a >=3-sequence decode batch. # # vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --trust-remote-code --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 4096 --port 8000 # python3 repro_dsv2lite_fp8_nan.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 [--k 3] import argparse, math, random, threading import httpx def prompt(seed, n_words=80): rng = random.Random(seed) return " ".join(f"w{rng.randrange(10000)}" for _ in range(n_words)) def one(base, model, seed, n, out): r = httpx.post(base + "/v1/completions", json={"model": model, "prompt": prompt(seed), "max_tokens": n, "temperature": 0.0, "logprobs": 1}, timeout=600) if r.status_code != 200: out[seed] = f"HTTP {r.status_code}: {r.text[:90]}" return ch = r.json()["choices"][0] lps = ch["logprobs"]["token_logprobs"] nan = sum(1 for x in lps if x is None or (isinstance(x, float) and math.isnan(x))) out[seed] = f"HTTP 200, nan_logprobs={nan}/{len(lps)}, text={ch['text'][:32]!r}" ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--base-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:8000") ap.add_argument("--model", default="deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat") ap.add_argument("--k", type=int, default=3) ap.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=16) a = ap.parse_args() for K in (1, 2, a.k): out, ths = {}, [] for s in range(K): th = threading.Thread(target=one, args=(a.base_url, a.model, 100 * K + s, a.max_tokens, out)) th.start(); ths.append(th) for th in ths: th.join() print(f"{K} concurrent request(s):") for s in sorted(out): print(f" {out[s]}") ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
