Notes: `collect_env.py` ran inside a one-GPU scheduler reservation (hence `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=5`); the reproduction below uses two of the eight B300s. vLLM is the upstream `main` commit `5be911ee871604895c5a950ac1a5675c71896fd2` (2026-09-15), installed with the matching precompiled wheel, unmodified tree. Model `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-FP8`. ### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary Adding the two HiSparse flags to an otherwise plain `vllm serve` of GLM-5.2 makes every completion come back as token noise, including for a six-word prompt. The first generated token matches the non-HiSparse control exactly and every token after it is wrong; on the same HiSparse server, a chain of eight `max_tokens: 1` requests reproduces the control's output exactly, so prefill is fine and decode is not. Nothing is logged: no error, no NaN, no preemption, and the boot lines report HiSparse as active. An earlier sweep of the same configuration at TP4, on the FlashInfer sparse-MLA backend, measured GSM8K 5-shot strict-match 0.0000 with HiSparse against 0.9409 without it. ## Related issues - #56889 reports the same symptom (GSM8K ~94% to 0% strict-match with `HiSparseConnector` on GLM-5.2) on a two-node DEP8 deployment with FP8 KV and P2P offloading; a commenter sees it at TP8. This issue narrows it down: a single node, TP2, BF16 KV, no offloading connector, default settings, deterministic, and confined to decode passes. Likely the same root cause; filed separately so the minimal reproduction and the exclusion list have their own tracking. - #56699 (`cudaErrorLaunchFailure` in the host-mirror path under P/D imports) and #56785 (indexer crash during piecewise capture, fixed by #56825, which is in this checkout) are different failures. ## Reproduction Model `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-FP8` (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, DSA sparse MLA, `index_topk` 2048), BF16 KV cache, 2x B300 275 GB, TP2; also reproduced at TP4 and TP8. Attention backend `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` and Model Runner V2 in both arms, auto-selected. The checkpoint is 417 GiB, so TP2 is the smallest that fits on 275 GB cards; `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` would fit one card but HiSparse refuses DeepSeek V4 (`vllm/v1/hisparse/layout.py`), and every other DSA checkpoint is several hundred GiB, so we have no reproduction for an 80 or 141 GB part. ``` # broken vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192 \ --attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{}}' \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":32}}' # control: the same command without those two flags vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192 # one request, identical against both curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-FP8","prompt":"What is the capital of France?","max_tokens":32,"temperature":0}' ``` `choices[0].text` as returned, `finish_reason` `length`, 32 completion tokens in both cases: ``` observed " (, \"' .'CC\"1adad.ss))) of,,)..-1..) of-" expected " (Paris)\n\nI am an AI language model, so I don't have personal desires or wants. However, if you are referring to the integrated system of Brain" ``` Both start with the same first token, `" ("`; the second is `","` with HiSparse and `"Paris"` without. `"2 + 2 ="` behaves the same way, returning `" .,# Had,, of to S58"` against `" 5\nThe phrase \"two plus two equals five\"..."`. Repeating a request within one server returns byte-identical noise, and two separate boots of the same command return the same text, so the corruption is deterministic. We ran the two arms on different ports so both could be up at once; nothing else differs from the commands above. ### Prefill-only requests are correct on the broken server This is the one thing we found that does not reproduce. Against the broken server above, drive the same continuation one token at a time, so every token is produced by a prefill pass: ```bash M=RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-FP8; T='What is the capital of France?'; G= for i in $(seq 8); do P=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "$(jq -cn --arg m "$M" --arg p "$T" '{model:$m,prompt:$p,max_tokens:1,temperature:0}')" \ | jq -j '.choices[0].text'; echo X); P=${P%X} T=$T$P; G=$G$P done printf '%s' "$G" | jq -Rsa . ``` The `jq -j` and the `echo X` sentinel matter: the third token of this continuation is `")\n\n"`, and command substitution would otherwise strip those newlines and feed a different prompt into the next step. The loop prints `" (Paris)\n\nI am an AI language"`, exactly what the control returns for one `max_tokens: 8` request, while one `max_tokens: 8` request on the HiSparse server returns `" (, \"' .'C"`. We also ran the chain with a fresh `cache_salt` per request, to rule out prefix-cache hits (prefix caching is on by default here), and got the same result. Same server, same weights, same boot: right while every token comes out of a prefill pass, wrong as soon as tokens come out of a decode pass. We found no HiSparse configuration that decodes correctly; the knobs below are the ones we varied. ## What was tried On the upstream `main` checkout above, at TP2, all through `vllm serve` plus `curl`: - `--enforce-eager`, so no CUDA graph is captured at all: still noise, byte-identical to the run above. - `hisparse_config.device_buffer_size` 2048 (the minimum for this model, one `index_topk`, no LRU slack) and 32768 (the maximum the config accepts, 8x the default 4096): still noise on both, byte-identical to the default 4096. - `--no-enable-prefix-caching`: still noise, byte-identical. - MTP speculative decoding, where `device_buffer_size` then resolves to 6144: still noise, different noise. This one arm ran through the offline `LLM()` API, not `vllm serve`. From an earlier sweep on a local branch at base `b443c1cc4`, whose HiSparse and FlashInfer code paths were unmodified upstream, at TP4 and TP8 with `host_pool_gib` 256 and a 14-prompt harness: - GSM8K 5-shot strict-match 0.0000 against 0.9409 for the control, 1319/1319 questions, all needle prompts missed, and the same first-token-right pattern. - `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`, no full decode graphs: still noise, byte-identical on 10 of 14 prompts. - `hisparse_config.eager_host_mirror=false`: still noise, byte-identical on 10 of 14. - Prefix caching on in one run and off in the rest: noise either way. - `--distributed-executor-backend ray`, private per-rank host pools instead of the shared mmap: still noise. - `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` instead of the auto-selected `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`: still noise, so both sparse-MLA backends are affected. Not tested: `MultiConnector` with `NixlConnector`, because UCX needs a locked-memory limit above this account's 8 MB cap. ## Where the evidence points The split falls exactly on the prefill/decode boundary, and it is deterministic rather than a race: eager mode, piecewise graphs, non-eager host mirroring, private per-rank host pools and prefix caching on or off all produce byte-identical wrong output. Hot-buffer capacity does not change it either: at `device_buffer_size=2048` every decode step must evict a row, at 32768 it almost never does, and the output is the same to the byte, which argues against an eviction or LRU-pressure race and for a fixed error in how decode addresses the buffer. That points at the hot-buffer decode lane in `vllm/v1/hisparse/runtime.py`, where `_prepare_for_batch` sets `decode_batch` and `_resolve_residency` (`hisparse_resolve_residency`), `_swap_rows` (`hisparse_gather_compact`) and `mirror_write_target` all branch on it. We have not isolated which of those is wrong. #56158, missing host mirror writes under FULL cudagraph replay, does not cover this: `--enforce-eager` captures no graphs and still reproduces. The boot warning recommends `NixlConnector` or `MooncakeStoreConnector` instead, but `hisparse/layout.py` raises unless the host pool comes from a `HiSparseConnector`, so the configuration above is the only shape available for a single-node run, and it is the shape the e2e test uses. ## Why the e2e test does not catch this `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py` runs with `load_format="dummy"` and a shrunk config, and its only output assertion is `assert actual == expected`, comparing generations before and after a spill. A consistently wrong decode path passes that test, because both sides are wrong in the same way, and random weights give no reference for what the output should have been.
HiSparse boot lines from the broken server ``` WARNING [vllm.py:1657] HiSparse host-resident KV is configured with connector HiSparseConnector. NixlConnector (GPU-staged host imports) and MooncakeStoreConnector (shared-store offload) are the validated paths; other connectors are treated as debug/fallback paths. INFO [cuda.py:536] Using FLASHMLA_SPARSE attention backend out of potential backends: ['FLASHMLA_SPARSE', 'FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE']. INFO [runtime.py:1276] Enabled experimental HiSparse HMA hot cache: top_k=2048, device_buffer_size=4096 (4096 LRU rows), max_num_seqs=1024. INFO [layout.py:340] HiSparse HMA: 32.0 GiB host source (5974 blocks), 34.3 GiB shared GPU indexer/resident/hot pool (124898 blocks). INFO [factory.py:62] Creating v1 connector with name: HiSparseConnector and engine_id: 5e430938-373a-4ce7-969b-ce4e6e402d18 INFO: Application startup complete. ``` No traceback, CUDA error, NaN or assertion appears anywhere in either server log.
### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [DONT merge][Exp][DSV4.1] Fuse MXFP8 wo_b GEMM with sequence-parallel reduce-scatter
body:
## Purpose

Fuse DeepSeek-V4.1's MXFP8 `wo_b` GEMM and sequence-parallel reduce-scatter into one SM100 CuTe DSL kernel. Opt in with `VLLM_DSV41_GEMM_RS=1` on TP4 within one NVLink multicast domain; batches below 1,024 tokens retain the existing GEMM + RS path. The kernel preserves MXFP8 operands and block-32 scales, reduces BF16 partials with FP32 accumulation, and shares one workspace across layers. Activation quantization remains a separate kernel. The head now runs that mainloop as a (256,128) 2-SM MMA with a (2,1) TMA-multicast cluster and PDL enabled.

Duplicate-work check: #56611 is closed and concerned shifted mHC overlap; #54151 implements Kimi-K3 AG-GEMM; #56751 optimizes tiny-M DSV4.1 projections. This change targets the large-M MXFP8 output projection and its RS, using Kimi's symmetric allocation/reduction helpers without invoking its BF16 GEMM. No matching open MXFP8 GEMM-RS PR was found.

## Test Plan

### Deploy

Executed independently on node17 and node30, four B200 GPUs per server, with TP4 + EP4 + MegaMoE + SP. Start fresh servers for `VLLM_DSV41_GEMM_RS=0` and `1`, then swap baseline/candidate across nodes. Both arms use source/native build `78eaaad2c7a7f8c7864d9c9c72772e3f9f2669d0` (including merged Mega-mHC), PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, and CUTLASS DSL 4.7.1. The dependency image is `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-dc36fcce902a63eab06c1b93a5c4a5ee178a0c56`; `/opt/dsv41-native` overlays native libraries and DeepGEMM from the exact source-commit wheel. Other FlashInfer versions have not been validated; this kernel currently imports private FlashInfer helpers.

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=/opt/dsv41-native:/gpfs/mszn/workspace/vllm
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export VLLM_DSV41_GEMM_RS=1  # 0 for baseline
uv run --no-project /opt/dsv41-gemm-rs/.venv/bin/python \
  -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve \
  /gpfs/mszn/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --served-model-name dsv41 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18517 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --max-model-len 9216 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 1024 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --no-enable-prefix-caching --seed 2026
```

### Benchmark

The commands below retain the measured flags; result paths are shortened. Startup/autotuning and eight warmup requests per case are excluded from timing.

```bash
for concurrency in 16 64 964; do
  requests=$((concurrency * 2))
  if (( requests < 128 )); then requests=128; fi
  uv run --no-project /opt/dsv41-gemm-rs/.venv/bin/python \
    -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench serve \
    --backend vllm --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18517 --model dsv41 \
    --tokenizer /gpfs/mszn/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
    --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
    --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 2026 \
    --max-concurrency "$concurrency" --request-rate inf \
    --num-prompts "$requests" --num-warmups 8 \
    --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 \
    --save-result --save-detailed --result-dir results \
    --result-filename "gemm-rs-${VLLM_DSV41_GEMM_RS}-c${concurrency}.json"
done
```

Correctness and kernel benchmark (same Python/runtime environment):

```bash
uv run --no-project /opt/dsv41-gemm-rs/.venv/bin/python \
  -m pytest tests/kernels/test_dsv41_gemm_rs.py -q
uv run --no-project /opt/dsv41-gemm-rs/.venv/bin/python \
  -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node 4 \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_gemm_rs.py \
  --tokens 128 256 512 1024 2048 4096 8192 \
  --workspaces 10 --samples 40 --output results/kernel.json
```

## Test Result

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 4×B200, TP4/EP4/MegaMoE/SP, random fixed-length 8192-input/1024-output tokens. Re-measured on a single node (b200-1-30) with sequential arms: baseline is `VLLM_DSV41_GEMM_RS=0` on the same build; fused is this branch head (PDL + (256,128)/(2,1) cluster). 128/128/1,928 requests at concurrency 16/64/964; the c964 fused arm was repeated three times and its median run is shown (runs ranged 6,665.5–7,053.8 tok/s). Mean latencies are request-weighted.

| Concurrency | Output tok/s: baseline → fused | Change | Mean TTFT (s): baseline → fused | Mean TPOT (ms): baseline → fused |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16 | 1468.5 → 1481.3 | +0.9% | 0.84 → 0.82 | 10.08 → 10.00 |
| 64 | 3251.0 → 3340.1 | +2.7% | 2.62 → 2.53 | 17.00 → 16.56 |
| 964 | 6496.0 → 6973.3 | +7.3% | 36.61 → 33.85 | 108.50 → 101.08 |

All measured requests succeeded with exact 8192/1024 token lengths and zero KV preemptions. A/B runs of this head against the previous (128,128)/(1,1) kernel config land within the ±3% run-to-run drift end-to-end; the earlier two-node c64 anomaly (-7.0%/+10.9%) did not reproduce under single-node sequencing. Routed experts use MegaMoE; main's shared-expert shape guard disables shared-expert fusion for this checkpoint in both arms.

The TP4 correctness test passed, covering independent dequantized FP32 references, nonuniform scales, odd-M padding, workspace reuse, changed-input CUDA graph replay, and output lifetime. The kernel benchmark passed, including the model dispatch's small-M fallback. With the PDL + (256,128)/(2,1) config on node30, quantization + GEMM + RS latency changed from 47.50/100.93/140.98/227.78 µs at M=1024/2048/4096/8192 to 46.27/61.44/94.21/159.74 µs (2.6%/39.1%/33.2%/29.9% reductions; CUDA-graph medians over 10 rotating workspaces, quantization included). The previous (128,128)/(1,1) config read 61.46/95.02/161.79 µs at M=2048/4096/8192 on the same benchmark, i.e. this update adds −0.0%/−0.9%/−1.3%. Smaller shapes still regress in the native kernel and use the existing path below M=1024; the TP4 correctness suite (odd M, graph replay with changed inputs, workspace reuse) passed on the new config.

Model validation is limited to serving and generation smoke tests. Baseline and fused generated text differed; the long-prompt baseline also varied across runs. No task-level accuracy acceptance has been established. The feature remains off by default, and formal accuracy evaluation is pending.

All applicable staged-file pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, formatting, typos, mypy, SPDX, and device API checks. Submission cleanup only changes annotations, local naming, license attribution, and test/benchmark device APIs; the fusion algorithm and serving configuration are unchanged from the measured runs.

AI assistance: Codex implemented the change and ran validation; Kimi Code found and fixed the clustered-grid co-residency deadlock, applied the PDL + (256,128)/(2,1) tuning, and re-ran the kernel tests plus the node30 measurements shown above. This draft is submitted for the human author's line-by-line review and independent test verification; those reviews are not claimed complete.

title: [Model][Engram] Add Mooncake-backed DeepSeek V4.1 tables
body:
## Purpose

This PR adds an optional Mooncake Store placement for DeepSeek V4.1 Engram
tables on top of #56757.

When `VLLM_ENGRAM_MOONCAKE_CONFIG` points to a published layout manifest:

- all DP replicas address the same globally stored TP shards, matching the
  existing `dp_shared_memory` placement semantics without Engram-DP sharding or
  per-step DP gather collectives;
- each model rank keeps no local copy of the external Engram table weights;
- each rank fetches only the hash heads owned by its TP shard;
- all local Engram layers share one backend and one snapshot-backed ranged-read
  request;
- reusable CUDA buffers are registered with Mooncake and packed rows are read
  into them with GPUDirect RDMA, avoiding pinned-host row staging and full-row
  H2D copies;
- hash IDs for compatible layers are copied to host together, and the
  background lookup overlaps model execution;
- only the small dead-row mask is copied to CUDA before packed rows are
  dequantized there;
- A10-class GPUs are supported by decoding E4M3FN bytes without requiring
  native FP8 compute support;
- the device's GPUDirect RDMA write-ordering capability is queried, and remote
  writes are flushed only when required by the hardware.

The PR also includes a publisher that packs the checkpoint's Engram weight and
scale tensors, publishes TP-only physical shards, verifies boundary rows,
writes the layout manifest, and keeps the owning Store segment alive.

Mooncake connection settings continue to use the standard `MOONCAKE_*`
environment variables. Real safetensors loading requires
`safetensors_load_strategy='lazy'` so external Engram tensors are not
materialized in worker memory.

## Dependencies

This PR is stacked directly on
[vLLM #56757](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56757), which introduces
the DeepSeek V4.1 Engram model, configuration, CPU-offload placement, and
model-level prefetch hooks used by this integration.

The required Mooncake stack, in validation order, is:

1. [Mooncake #4083](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4083): provides
   the Store-owned `EngramStore` API and lifetime model, including
   `EngramStore(configs, store_client=store, local_dir=...)`, populate, and
   ranged lookup.
2. [Mooncake #4095](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4095): adds the
   reusable ranged-read snapshot shared by Engram, resharding, and future
   ranged-read users.
3. [Mooncake #4117](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4117): is
   stacked on #4095 and adds the optimized RDMA scatter path,
   `lookup_many_into`, and `lookup_many_into_registered` for direct CUDA
   destinations.

The backend checks for `lookup_many_into_registered` at runtime and fails with
an explicit version error when the required Mooncake stack is unavailable.

This remains a draft while the dependency PRs are under review and a full-weight
DeepSeek V4.1 serving run is being prepared.

The current DCO failure is inherited from the cross-repository #56757 commit
present in this stacked branch. The commits authored by this PR are signed; the
inherited status can be removed by rebasing after #56757 lands.

## Test Plan

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/path/to/mooncake:. python -m pytest -q \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_engram_mooncake.py \
  tests/test_config.py -k mooncake

python -m pytest -q tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py

ruff check \
  examples/basic/offline_inference/deepseek_v41_mooncake.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_engram_mooncake.py \
  tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py \
  tests/test_config.py vllm/config/engram.py \
  vllm/distributed/parallel_state.py vllm/envs.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/nvidia/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/nvidia/engram_mooncake.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/nvidia/model.py
```

The cross-machine benchmark uses the same synthetic Engram access shape as
Mooncake #4083: token count 8, two Engram layers, 24 heads per layer, 264-byte
packed rows, 384 ranges, and 101,376 bytes per request. It runs on two A10x8 +
ERDMA machines. Each result below is the median of three independent runs, each
with 50 warmups and 2,000 measured iterations. Local and cross-machine runs use
the normal automatic RDMA path with registered CUDA destinations; no
benchmark-only `MC_STORE_MEMCPY` override is applied.

## Test Result

- Mooncake/config targeted tests: **23 passed**.
- Engram parallel semantics tests: **24 passed, 2 platform skips**.
- Ruff, Python compilation, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Global Store placement uses TP-only physical shards, skips Engram-DP group
  creation, and performs no DP hash or row gather.
- Cross-machine correctness passed for two layers, dead rows, two reusable
  slots, registered CUDA destinations, and A10 Triton dequantization.
- A10 reports GPUDirect RDMA write ordering `NONE` and host flush support. The
  required `cudaDeviceFlushGPUDirectRDMAWrites` costs about 1.35 us per request.
- The benchmark deployment lacks the complete vLLM test-only dependency and
  extension set, so GitHub CI remains required for the full unit suite.

### Performance

| Path | Token-8 p50 | Token-8 p95 | Cross/local gap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Local registered CUDA | 791.61 us | 832.23 us | - |
| Cross-machine registered CUDA | 890.30 us | 939.31 us | 98.69 us |

Cross-machine phase medians are:

| Stage | p50 |
|---|---:|
| Prefetch enqueue and combined ID D2H submission | 95.91 us |
| Background lookup wait | 625.22 us |
| Dead-mask copy and two GPU dequant submissions | 163.17 us |

The Store/Transfer Engine portion was measured on the exact combined
#4083/#4095/#4117 source tree: 411.57 us p50 / 431.32 us p95 cross-machine,
versus 385.08 us p50 / 410.55 us p95 local. The raw p50 transfer gap is 26.49
us. At the backend level, most of the remaining 98.69 us gap is visible in the
background lookup wait rather than GPU dequantization.

The benchmark is a component-level read-path integration test with #4083-style
synthetic tables; it is not a full-model TTFT result.

---

- [x] The purpose of the PR is described.
- [x] The test plan is provided.
- [x] Before/after and local/cross-machine results are provided.
- [x] Required dependency PRs are listed.

</details>

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Preserve per-layer offsets in KV cache bindings
body:
FIX https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57019

## Purpose

Fix cross-layer KV overwrites when HiSparse packs multiple layers into one allocation. Both resident and hot bindings used the tensor's base offset for every layer, allowing later layers to overwrite earlier layers' cached rows. Compute `tensor.offset + layer_index * tensor.layer_stride` once per layer and use it in both bindings.

Addresses #57019; the faulty bindings were introduced by #53781.

Add a nightly HiSparse GSM8K job using the existing accuracy harness and real `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` weights. It runs on four B200s with TP4, BF16 KV, eager execution, and a 32 GiB host pool. All 1,319 questions are evaluated with 5 shots and an explicit 90% minimum accuracy. The job is optional in regular CI, following the existing nightly-job convention. No new unit test or standalone evaluation harness is added.

Duplicate-work check: read #57019 and its comments, searched open PRs for `57019 in:body`, `HiSparse`, and `HiSparse offset`. No open PR addressing these missing layer offsets was found. The host-mirror replay work in #56158 addresses a separate failure path.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, validation, and this description. The human submitter is responsible for line-by-line review and independent test validation.

## Test Plan

Run the new nightly test:

```bash
chg run -g 4 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest -s -v \
  tests/evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py \
  --config-list-file=configs/models-hisparse.txt
```

Existing GPU suites run against the binding fix:

```bash
chg run -g 1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k hisparse -q

chg run -g 1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py -q
```

## Test Result

- New nightly configuration, run locally on four B300s: **94.39% (1,245/1,319)**, **zero invalid answers**, evaluation time **594.9 seconds**. The 90% accuracy assertion passed. B200 execution remains for CI.
- Local pytest teardown failed in the existing `RemoteOpenAIServer._get_gpu_memory_used` check: it reads physical NVML indices `0..3` instead of mapping `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,2,5,6`, so growth in another user's GPU allocations exceeded its baseline. All our server/worker processes exited and GPUs 0, 2, 5, and 6 returned to 0 MiB; the full pytest command is therefore **not** reported as passing.
- Set `request_timeout_seconds: 1800` because the evaluator's total timeout includes waiting for a connection. An initial run with the default 600 seconds timed out approximately 60 queued requests; the final configuration completed all requests without API errors or timeouts.
- Negative control for the nightly server configuration: restored only the original `bind_hisparse_kv_caches` from `0136df94b0` in all four workers, keeping TP4, BF16 KV, concurrency 32, and automatic GPU cache sizing. The first **64 GSM8K questions scored 0/64 (0%)**, with no request errors or timeouts (72.9 seconds). This was a sampled negative control, not a full 1,319-question unpatched run. Its GPU pool was 138.1 GiB and reported about 8.4% usage, demonstrating that low cache capacity is unnecessary to expose the missing layer offsets. This does not establish memory-pressure spill coverage. The local validation helper scoped NVML cleanup checks to the reserved GPUs; production code and the GSM8K scorer were unchanged.
- HiSparse attention tests on B300: **30 passed**.
- Spill/prefix-restore tests on B300: **2 passed**, covering standalone/offload variants and FULL CUDA graph replay.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Buildkite step-key validation.

Earlier sampled evaluation, separate from the new nightly configuration: `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` revision `53e0691e21895a3863a606dfd12910c69eba94ab`, TP2 on B300, automatically selected FP8 KV, eager mode. Used the existing GSM8K scorer with the first 64 questions, 5 shots, 256 output tokens, temperature 0, seed 42, concurrency 16; server limits were model length 8192, 32 sequences, and 4096 batched tokens. The fixed arm enabled default HiSparse settings with a 32 GiB host pool.

| Sampled GSM8K arm | Correct | Accuracy | Invalid answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HiSparse disabled | 61/64 | 95.3125% | 0 |
| Fixed HiSparse | 59/64 | 92.1875% | 0 |

**Accuracy parity remains unverified.** The sampled fixed-arm continuations were readable but differed from the control. This uses a different checkpoint and KV dtype from the issue's RedHatAI/BF16 reproduction.

## Curl reproduction: unpatched versus fixed HiSparse

Both responses below were captured with HiSparse enabled, the same NVIDIA checkpoint/revision, TP2 on B300, FP8 KV selected by the checkpoint, eager mode, and the same request. The before run restored only `bind_hisparse_kv_caches` from `0136df94b0` in the workers; the after run used the fix. These are not the HiSparse-disabled control responses.

Equivalent server command for either version:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \
  --revision 53e0691e21895a3863a606dfd12910c69eba94ab \
  --served-model-name glm52 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --enforce-eager --seed 0 \
  --attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":32}}'
```

Request (the after response was captured earlier using the equivalent HTTP JSON request):

```bash
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"glm52","prompt":"What is the capital of France?","max_tokens":32,"temperature":0,"seed":0}' \
  | jq '{text: .choices[0].text, finish_reason: .choices[0].finish_reason, completion_tokens: .usage.completion_tokens}'
```

Before, unpatched HiSparse:

```json
{
  "text": " ( is is'] .istsististig, \"..\" of of of23-2-; of----!.",
  "finish_reason": "length",
  "completion_tokens": 32
}
```

After, fixed HiSparse:

```json
{
  "text": " (Oh, I know this one!)\nWhile searching our database we found 1 possible solution for the: What is the capital of France? (Oh, I",
  "finish_reason": "length",
  "completion_tokens": 32
}
```

The token noise is replaced by a readable continuation. This short completion example does not establish answer correctness or parity with HiSparse disabled; see the GSM8K results above.

title: [Bug]: V2 model runner keeps stale ModelState.max_model_len after auto-fit -> AssertionError in DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA (C128A) during CUDA graph capture
body:
### Your current environment

```text
vLLM build:  0.1.dev20759+gb40673cd0 (built from local-inference-lab/vllm @ dev/jovian-judgement, 2026-09-13)
             The relevant code paths are identical on vllm-project/vllm main as of 2026-09-15 (see "Upstream check").
PyTorch:     2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Python 3.12.3
Hardware:    2x NVIDIA GB10 (compute capability 12.1), driver 580.173.02, Linux 6.17 aarch64
Model:       DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, tensor parallel 2, DSpark speculative decoding (k=5)
Flags:       --max-model-len auto (full context 1048576), --kv-cache-dtype fp8, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Summary**

When `max_model_len` is auto-fitted down because the KV cache cannot hold the full context, the V2 GPU model runner keeps using the *original* length in its `ModelState`, while attention metadata builders created afterwards size their buffers from the *reduced* `model_config.max_model_len`. For DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA this makes `_build_c128a_metadata` fail its assertion during CUDA-graph capture, and the engine dies at startup.

It is not deterministic: it only triggers when free memory at startup is slightly too small for the full context. The same configuration started fine on a second attempt (KV cache 12.3 GiB → no reduction).

**Log**

```text
max_model_len: reduced from 1048576 to 980224 to fit in available GPU memory (9.81 GiB KV cache)
...
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", in compile_or_warm_up_model
    cuda_graph_memory_bytes = self.model_runner.capture_model()
  ...
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/default.py", in prepare_attn
    attn_metadata = build_attn_metadata(
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py", in build_attn_metadata
    metadata = attn_metadata_builder.build_for_cudagraph_capture(
  File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v4/sparse_mla.py", in _build_c128a_metadata
    assert active_topk_width >= cm.max_seq_len // self.compress_ratio
AssertionError
```

**Root cause**

1. `ModelState.__init__` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/interface.py`) caches `self.max_model_len = self.model_config.max_model_len` when the model is loaded (`load_model` → `init_model_state`). No method updates it later.
2. After KV sizing, `Worker.update_max_model_len` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py`) writes the reduced value into `model_config.max_model_len` and calls `model_runner.update_max_model_len`.
3. `GPUModelRunner.update_max_model_len` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`) only updates `self.max_model_len` and `self.req_states.max_model_len` — **`self.model_state` keeps the original length**.
4. The attention metadata builders are created afterwards. `DeepseekV4SparseMLAMetadataBuilder.__init__` sizes the C128A buffers from the **reduced** `model_config.max_model_len`: `c128a_max_compressed = align_up(cdiv(980224, 128), 128) = 7680`.
5. During CUDA-graph capture, `prepare_attn` in `model_states/default.py` uses `max_seq_len = self.max_model_len` (`for_capture` branch) → the **stale** 1048576 → `max_seq_len // 128 = 8192`.
6. `_build_c128a_metadata` clamps `active_topk_width` to `c128a_max_compressed` (7680) and then asserts it is `>= 8192` → `AssertionError`.

**Upstream check**

On `vllm-project/vllm` `main` (2026-09-15): `ModelState.__init__` sets `self.max_model_len` from `model_config` and never updates it; `prepare_attn` uses it for capture; `GPUModelRunner.update_max_model_len` does not touch `model_state`; `sparse_mla.py` computes `c128a_max_compressed` from `model_config.max_model_len` and has the same assertion. We have not reproduced it on a `main` build ourselves.

**Reproduction**

Any DeepSeek-V4 sparse-MLA configuration with `max_model_len` on auto (or `-1`) where the available KV cache is smaller than the full model context, e.g. lower `--gpu-memory-utilization` until the startup log shows `max_model_len: reduced from …`.

**Workaround**

Set an explicit `--max-model-len` that fits the KV cache (we use 900000). Then no auto-fit happens and both values agree.

**Suggested fix**

Propagate the update to the model state, e.g. in `GPUModelRunner.update_max_model_len`: `self.model_state.max_model_len = max_model_len` (plus any other cached copies) — or let `ModelState` read `self.model_config.max_model_len` instead of caching it.

**Related**

#46794 describes the same pattern in the V1 `GPUModelRunner` (`InputBatch` built with the original `max_model_len` before the auto-fit, stale block table → `RuntimeError` during decode). This one is the V2 runner's `ModelState`; a general fix could make every component that snapshots `max_model_len` pick up the auto-fitted value.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I searched existing issues and PRs (related but different: #46794, #53600).

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Handle MoE padding sentinel in AITER fused experts
body:
VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING (enabled by default) lets the topk kernels mark cudagraph padding rows by writing -1 into topk_ids, so downstream MoE kernels can skip work for them. The AITER fused-expert path never handled that sentinel and passed topk_ids straight into aiter.fused_moe, where moe_sorting indexes the expert weights with the raw id. A value of -1 reads outside the weight buffer and trips a GPU memory access fault:

  Memory access fault by GPU node-9 on address 0x7f255b5b2000.
  Reason: Unknown.

This reproduces on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (MXFP4 experts, TP=4, MI355X): the profiling run builds a fully synthetic batch whose rows are all marked as padding, so every routing index is -1 and all ranks fault before the server can start. It is not limited to startup -- trailing cudagraph padding rows are marked the same way on real batches.

Neutralize the sentinel where the other AITER dtype fixups happen: route padding rows to expert 0 with zero weight, contributing nothing to the output. The rewrite is branchless so it remains cudagraph-capturable.

title: [Config] Infer HiSparse attention config from HiSparseConnector
body:
## What

HiSparse needed to be turned on twice: `HiSparseConnector` in `--kv-transfer-config` *and* `--attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{}}'`. The empty `{}` carries no information — configuring the connector already implies HiSparse, and `hisparse_config` without the connector is rejected at startup anyway (`hisparse/layout.py:78`).

`VllmConfig.__post_init__` now defaults `attention_config.hisparse_config = HiSparseConfig()` when `kv_transfer_config.has_connector("HiSparseConnector")` (direct or MultiConnector child), placed before the existing HiSparse validation block so CUDA/PP/DCP/DSA/HMA errors still fire. Explicit `--attention-config` is now only for tuning (`device_buffer_size`, `eager_host_mirror`).

## How HiSparse is run now

Decode side of a NIXL P/D setup, before:

```bash
--attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{}}' \
--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer",
  "kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[
    {"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer"},
    {"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
     "kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":128}}]}}'
```

after: identical, minus the `--attention-config` line.

title: [ROCm][Quant] Support mixed mxfp4 + fp8 checkpoints
body:
## Purpose

Kimi-K3 ships MXFP4 routed experts and bf16 dense projections. Serving a
checkpoint that mixes the two — MXFP4 experts plus fp8 dense projections —
does not work on ROCm today, for two independent reasons. This PR fixes both.

Both changes are **inert for a stock checkpoint**: neither alters behaviour
unless a checkpoint declares more than one config group, or its index
contradicts the file being read.

## The two fixes

**1. `mxfp4.py` — delegate non-mxfp4 Linears to compressed-tensors.**

`Mxfp4Config.get_quant_method` returns `UnquantizedLinearMethod()` for *every*
`LinearBase`, so a checkpoint carrying a second, fp8 `config_groups` entry has
that group silently ignored and the layers built unquantized. It surfaces much
later as `KeyError: '...weight_scale'` at load.

Only the `LinearBase` branch is patched. The MoE deliberately stays on
`Mxfp4MoEMethod`: routing the routed experts through compressed-tensors hits
`prepare_moe_fp4_layer_for_marlin`, and Marlin is CUDA-only
(`AttributeError: '_OpNamespace' '_C' object has no attribute
'gptq_marlin_repack'`).

**2. `weight_utils.py` — honour the safetensors index at tensor granularity.**

vLLM resolves a sharded checkpoint in two stages that disagree about what the
index means. `filter_duplicate_safetensors_files` narrows the *file* list to
those the index references, but `safetensors_weights_iterator` then does
`for name in f.keys()` and yields *every* tensor in each of those files.

For an ordinary checkpoint the distinction never surfaces, because every tensor
in a referenced shard is also in the weight map. It surfaces immediately for
any checkpoint that repoints some tensors at replacement shards while leaving
the originals in place: both versions are yielded under the same name and
**filename sort order decides which one wins**. This is a latent correctness
bug independent of quantization.

## What this enables

A mixed MXFP4 + fp8 checkpoint becomes loadable and servable on ROCm. For
Kimi-K3 that means the 276 `shared_experts` projections (92 layers x
gate/up/down, 12.16G parameters) can be carried as fp8 instead of bf16:

| `shared_experts` weights | on disk | per GPU at TP8 |
|---|---:|---:|
| bf16 (stock checkpoint) | 22.64 GiB | 2.83 GiB |
| fp8 + per-channel scales (this PR) | 11.33 GiB | 1.42 GiB |
| **freed** | **11.32 GiB** | **1.41 GiB** |

Scales cost 0.007 GiB in total, so the saving is essentially the full halving.
On a TP8 deployment that is ~1.41 GiB per GPU returned to the KV cache.

Accuracy is unchanged: **GSM8k 0.9659** over all 1319 questions, 5-shot, both
strict-match and flexible-extract, with real joint verification (not the
synthetic acceptance used for throughput runs) - identical to the bf16
baseline.

## On performance

This is a capability change, and no end-to-end speedup is claimed for it.

The numbers in the tables below were measured on an **earlier nightly build**
and are kept only for completeness. They should not be read as a result for
this PR on current main: the fp8 shared-expert path there dispatches a
different GEMM and adds a separate per-token activation-quant launch per
Linear, and neither is tuned for these shapes. A fair end-to-end comparison on
the new build requires that kernel tuning first, which is out of scope here.

<details>
<summary>End-to-end measurements from the earlier build (retained for reference)</summary>

MI355X, TP8, conc=1, DSpark MTP depth 6, 1200 s, interactivity p90:

| | p90 | vs control | GSM8k (full 1319) |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| stock bf16 | 110.28 | - | 0.9659 |
| fp8 `shared_experts` | 111.99 | +1.55% | 0.9659 |

The noise floor of a 1200 s conc=1 arm is roughly 1%, so this was never a
tight measurement even on that build.

Three other targets were built, gated and measured on the same build. None
improved on `shared_experts` alone, which is why the scope here is narrow:

| target | Linears | p90 | GSM8k |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `shared_experts` | 184 | 111.99 (+1.55%) | 0.9659 |
| `o_proj` | 93 | 111.74 (+1.32%) | 0.9651 |
| `shared_experts` + `o_proj` | 277 | 112.00 (+1.56%) | 0.9659 |
| MLA projections | 96 | 109.96 (-0.29%) | 0.9689 |

The accuracy column is the durable part of that table: MXFP4 on these same
dense projections cost 0.9 GSM8k points (0.9568), which is why fp8 rather than
MXFP4 is the right precision for them.

</details>

## Reproducing this

The code changes make a mixed checkpoint *servable*; they do not produce one.
`examples/features/kimi_k3_fp8_dense/` adds the tooling:

```bash
cd examples/features/kimi_k3_fp8_dense

# build (~12 GB, CPU only, one command; originals are symlinked, not copied)
python build_overlay.py --src /path/to/Kimi-K3 --dst /path/to/Kimi-K3-fp8se \
                        --target shared_experts

# verify it will actually be served as fp8
python verify_overlay.py --overlay /path/to/Kimi-K3-fp8se --target shared_experts

# serve
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve /path/to/Kimi-K3-fp8se \
    --load-format safetensors --tensor-parallel-size 8 ...
```

The README documents the full conc=1 agentic recipe: the exact serve flags,
the speculative and compilation configs, and how to confirm from the server
log that the layers were really delegated.

Two flags are load-bearing and easy to get wrong:

* **`--load-format safetensors` is required.** `fastsafetensors` uses a
  separate `ParallelLoader` path with no equivalent index hook, so it will
  silently serve the stale bf16 weights and measure the control.
* **`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`** routes the fp8 linear to aiter; without it the
  scheme resolves elsewhere and the numbers above do not apply.

`verify_overlay.py` exists because the failure mode is silent:
`should_ignore_layer` is consulted **before** `config_groups`, so a layer still
matched by an `ignore` regex is served as bf16 even with byte-perfect fp8
tensors on disk. The server logs a clean load, accuracy is unchanged because it
is the original model, and the speedup just fails to appear — it looks like a
null result, not a bug.

## Relationship to online quantization

vLLM can already quantize these layers online from a stock checkpoint
(`--quantization-config`, #51392), with no overlay, and that path is much
easier to adopt.

The two solve different problems: #51392 composes an online method onto layers
the checkpoint leaves *unquantized*, whereas this PR lets vLLM *read* fp8
weights that are already on disk alongside MXFP4 experts. Only the latter
covers a pre-quantized checkpoint published as mixed-precision, and only the
latter avoids paying the quantization cost at every load.

They also differ in scheme: the online shorthands are static-activation, while
a checkpoint built this way carries w8a8 with dynamic per-token activations.

## Not a duplicate

Checked against open work in this area before and during this PR:

* **#51392 (merged)** composes an *online* quantization method onto layers the
  checkpoint leaves unquantized. It cannot read fp8 weights that are already on
  disk — `get_quant_method` asserts `issubclass(quant_method_cls,
  OnlineLinearBase)`. This PR is the pre-quantized case.
* **#53154 / #54068 / #54066 (draft, rebklee)** fuse MXFP4 *activation* quant
  into the Kimi-K3 attention epilogues. That is a fusion of a different
  precision choice, and is inert until `o_proj` is made MXFP4. This PR does not
  touch those paths; it also reports an accuracy measurement relevant to
  them: MXFP4 on these dense projections costs 0.9 GSM8k points.
* **#53847 (draft)** requants FP8 shared experts *to* MXFP4 for DeepSeek-V4,
  the opposite direction on a different model.
* **#55367, #54556** are other quantization bugfixes with no overlap.

No open PR addresses `Mxfp4Config` ignoring `config_groups` for Linear layers,
or the safetensors index/file disagreement.

## AI assistance

**AI assistance was used** for this PR (Claude). The accuracy gate, the memory
figures, and the rejected alternatives were produced by running the workloads
described above on real hardware or read directly off the checkpoint; every
claim in this description corresponds to a run or a measurement, not an
estimate. The submitter has reviewed each changed line.

Two notes in the spirit of the policy: no end-to-end speedup is claimed, and
the end-to-end numbers that exist are explicitly scoped to the earlier build
they were measured on rather than presented as a current result. The
alternatives that were tried and failed are reported rather than omitted.

## Test plan

- [x] GSM8k full 1319, 5-shot, real joint verification: 0.9659 both filters,
      unchanged from the bf16 baseline
- [x] 1200 s conc=1 agentic A/B against a shared control on the same image
      (earlier build; see the performance note above)
- [x] Weight footprint read off the built overlay: 276 fp8 weights + 276 F32
      scales, 11.33 GiB against 22.64 GiB for the same tensors in bf16
- [x] Stock single-group checkpoint unaffected (both changes inert)
- [x] Overlay round-trip verified: 276 fp8 weights, 276 scales, no bf16
      reachable, sampled tensors dequantize to within 0.0265 relative RMS

Commands run:

```bash
# overlay build + integrity check
python examples/features/kimi_k3_fp8_dense/build_overlay.py \
    --src <Kimi-K3> --dst <Kimi-K3-fp8se> --target shared_experts
python examples/features/kimi_k3_fp8_dense/build_overlay.py \
    --src <Kimi-K3> --dst <Kimi-K3-fp8se> --target shared_experts \
    --check-unreferenced
# -> ok: 276 fp8 weights, 276 scales, no bf16 left reachable,
#    3 sampled tensors dequantize correctly (relRMS 0.02646-0.02648)

# scheme resolution
python examples/features/kimi_k3_fp8_dense/verify_overlay.py \
    --overlay <Kimi-K3-fp8se> --target shared_experts
# -> OK: 276 layers -> group_fp8_shared_experts (w8a8-dynamic, channel)

# accuracy: GSM8k full 1319, 5-shot, rejection_sample_method=block
# -> 0.9659 strict-match, 0.9659 flexible-extract (baseline 0.9659)

# perf: agentic workload, conc=1, TP8, DSpark MTP depth 6, 1200s
# -> interactivity p90 111.99 vs 110.28 baseline (+1.55%)
```

Line length checked at 88 for both added scripts.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse][NIXL] Import full blocks without tail prefill on D
body:
## Purpose

HiSparse currently rejects host imports whose computed-token count is not block aligned. This draft explores an alternative to #56946: receive the full final block and restore its contents into one writable GPU page, so a successful NIXL full-prompt import resumes with a single-token forward instead of prefilling the unaligned tail on D.

The idea is that we want to avoid having to run prefill on D, however short they might be (<block_size here), with north star being deploying D with decode-only CG (aligned with rest of cases).

### NIXL analogy: transfer capacity is not sequence length

NIXL already transfers physical blocks containing partially filled prompt tails. Moving the unused bytes does not make them computed tokens. HiSparse can use the same distinction:

| For a 32,019-token prompt, block size 128 | This approach |
| --- | --- |
| Real imported tokens | 32,019 |
| Host blocks received | 251 |
| Physical capacity | 32,128 token slots |
| Unused tail capacity ("holes") | 109 token slots |
| Prompt work on D after a full import | The usual last-token replay for logits |

The holes are unused rows within the request's final host block. They do not change token positions or sequence length, and generation fills them at their normal offsets. P does not compute dummy padding tokens. No sub-block allocator or NIXL wire-protocol change is required.

### Implementation and tradeoff

- Reserve one writable resident page for the final imported block, including aligned prompts whose last token is replayed.
- After a successful external receive, enqueue a full-page host-to-device restore on every TP rank. Copies run on the compute stream before the forward/CUDA-graph replay.
- Retain both endpoints until every participating worker completes its copy. Avoid publishing an uninitialized resident copy to prefix-cache users, and keep an incomplete host page unsealed.
- Register a completed, valid restored GPU page for later prefix hits only after all workers finish. Pending restores remain hidden, and incomplete pages and aborted requests are excluded. This incorporates [NickLucche/vllm#12](https://github.com/NickLucche/vllm/pull/12).
- Continue using the existing row-mirror and page-sealing paths for newly generated KV.

Compared with #56946, this transfers the final block and pays for one page of H2D copying per layer/rank rather than recomputing up to `block_size - 1` prompt tokens. It also reserves a resident tail page for aligned imports. The unused host rows are ordinary tail capacity, not extra logical tokens or permanent gaps between prompt and output. No performance improvement has been measured.

The intended benefit is to keep successful full-prompt P/D handoffs on single-token execution, compatible with decode-only graph capture. This is not a guarantee that D can never prefill: cache misses, failed transfers, preemption, or partial external hits can still require recomputation.

### Related work

Checked #56699 and its comments, open PRs mentioning it, and open PRs matching HiSparse import, landing, tail, partial, full block, and tail restore.

- #56946 addresses the same admission failure by rounding the imported prefix down and prefilling the remainder locally. This draft is the explicitly requested alternative that retains all real prompt KV and changes tail residency instead.
- The notify-only read and empty-region shape fixes are reused verbatim from #56946 (originally #55398). They prevent empty local destinations from entering region expansion when P and D have different cache-group layouts. They are independent of tail policy; empty receives notify P, and report `finished_recving` only when `awaiting_kvs=True`.
- #55398 chooses direct GPU landing for imported history when capacity permits. This draft preserves host landing and restores only the final page.
- #56109 concerns broader pool/residency management. This draft uses the current pool model.

Related to the deployment discussion in #56699; this does not claim to fix that issue's CUDA launch failure or establish end-to-end P/D correctness.

## Test Plan

Exercise aligned, unaligned, and sub-block imports; last-token resumption; partial-page publication; multi-worker completion and abort lifetime; and tail-copy contents on both host-writer and non-writer ranks.

Before marking ready, run real NIXL P/D on NVIDIA GPUs with decode-only graphs, check generated-token/logprob parity against the prefiller reference, and exercise page-boundary crossing, eviction/preemption, and concurrent traffic. Heterogeneous TP/DCP coverage remains pending.

## Test Result

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py \
  -k 'hisparse or connector_completes_partial_prefix' -q
```

**99 passed, 2 skipped, 117 deselected** on macOS. The two skipped cases require CUDA. Commit-time pre-commit hooks passed, including the configured mypy hook.

Rerun after integrating #12 and rebasing onto `upstream/main` at `fc8132a5e5`: **99 passed, 2 skipped, 117 deselected**. The existing import test now checks that one worker completion does not publish the GPU copy and that full completion publishes aligned tails. Pre-commit hooks passed across all PR files. GPU/model validation of the combined change remains pending.

Additional existing empty-receive checks after restoring those two NIXL hunks:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  -k empty_recv_is_reported_only_when_awaited -q
```

**4 passed, 130 deselected** on macOS. The separate completion-time positional group-pairing workaround reported by the GPU investigation is not included in this draft.

After rebasing onto `upstream/main` (`c6fa1f05d1`, including #57027), fixed the H200 CI failure in `test_hisparse_spill_and_prefix_restore[offload]`: the sync checker reports the tail copy as potentially synchronous because PyTorch does not recognize the host pool's external `cudaHostRegister` registration. A narrow `gpu_sync_allowed()` scope covers that copy; the transfer and stream ordering are unchanged. The existing CUDA tail-restore test now allocates the host pool through the production registration path and enables strict sync checking.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k hisparse -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  -k empty_recv_is_reported_only_when_awaited -q
```

Post-rebase results on macOS: **88 passed, 2 CUDA cases skipped** and **4 passed**, respectively. Pre-commit hooks passed across all PR files. The CUDA regression and failing GPU e2e test still require the new CI run.

**Model evaluation / GPU serving: not run.** This is a draft for design review, published at the submitter's explicit request without waiting for GPU testing. No accuracy, graph-replay, throughput, or latency claim is made.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for implementation, tests, and this description. Human line-by-line review and human-run GPU validation remain pending before this draft is ready for merge.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] DeepSeek V4: drop orphan DSML structural closers in content
body:
## Purpose

Reported on a DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash deployment: responses intermittently end with a stray closing tag (for example `</｜DSML｜parameter>`) appended to the completed answer. It reproduces only under long-context / degenerate generation, which is exactly when the model emits orphan DSML fragments.

Root cause is in the engine's no-transition fallback:

- `StreamingParserEngine._on_terminal` calls `_emit_for_state(value, ...)` whenever `(state, terminal)` has no transition. In `CONTENT`/`REASONING` that echoes the raw terminal text as a `TEXT_CHUNK` / `REASONING_CHUNK`.
- `deepseek_v4_config` defines transitions only for the `TOOL_*` states, so an orphan structural closer that arrives in a plain content state is emitted verbatim into the client-visible content.

## Fix

- Add a declarative `absorb_terminals` set to `ParserEngineConfig`.
- In `_on_terminal`, drop a declared terminal that reaches a plain content state (`CONTENT`/`REASONING`) with no transition.
- Guard the drop with `not self.skip_tool_parsing`, and declare `PARAM_CLOSE`, `INVOKE_END`, `TOOL_END` in `deepseek_v4_config`.

The `skip_tool_parsing` guard is essential. In the delegating architecture the reasoning pass runs with `skip_tool_parsing=True` and must pass tool markup through verbatim so the downstream tool adapter can parse it. Absorbing there starves the tool parser.

### Why not state-machine transitions

The obvious alternative — adding `(CONTENT, "PARAM_CLOSE")`-style transitions - is unsafe here. Those transitions also fire in the reasoning pass, which then drops the closers from the reasoning-stripped content handed to the tool adapter. On the real engine that reproduces as `test_registered_adapters_parse_complete_output` losing every parameter after the first (`{"city": ...}` instead of `{"city": ..., "count": ...}`) and `TestDelegatingParserLargeDelta` failing. The engine-level rule with the skip-pass guard keeps the reasoning pass untouched.

Only the tool-owning pass absorbs; reasoning-channel orphans keep their existing behaviour.

## Tests

- `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py::TestOrphanStructuralCloserAbsorption` - non-streaming and streaming, all three closers, plus a normal-tool-call regression.
- `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py::test_orphan_structural_closer_is_absorbed` - spaced V4.1 dialect, thinking on and off.

## Verification

Ran both test modules against a real DeepSeek-V4.1 serving engine (vLLM dev build, `--tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41`):

- every new test passes;
- the delegating reasoning + tool-adapter tests still parse all parameters and remain byte-for-byte unchanged;
- the only remaining failure in the module is a pre-existing engine-version drift unrelated to this change.

## Related

#51914, #52645 and #49117 cover missing or malformed DSML *start* wrappers / orphan-invoke recovery. This change is complementary and addresses the orphan *closer* leak into content, which those do not.

title: [CI] Split (B200) V1 Attention into Sparse MLA, MLA, DCP, Dense/SSM, and ROCm jobs
body:
## What

Replace the opaque two-replica `(B200) V1 Attention` hash shard with named jobs for Sparse MLA, MLA Correctness, Dense and SSM, and a shared job for the three short units (DCP, MLA Backends, ROCm). Each job runs whole semantic directories; only MLA Correctness uses pytest sharding within its own directory.

## Old

```text
(B200) V1 Attention Shard %N [v1-attention-b200]
└── pytest v1/attention --num-shards=2
```

## New

| Buildkite job | key | whole coverage unit | replicas |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `(B200) V1 Attention / Sparse MLA` | `v1-attention-b200-sparse-mla` | `sparse_mla/` | 1 |
| `(B200) V1 Attention / MLA Correctness Shard %N` | `v1-attention-b200-mla-correctness` | `mla/correctness/` | 3 |
| `(B200) V1 Attention / Dense and SSM` | `v1-attention-b200-dense-ssm` | `dense/` + `ssm/` | 1 |
| `(B200) V1 Attention / DCP, MLA Backends and ROCm` | `v1-attention-b200-dcp-mla-backends-rocm` | `dcp/` + `mla/backends/` + `rocm/` | 1 |

## Notes

- The three short units share one worker, each as its own `pytest` invocation, so process isolation is unchanged and a failure still names the unit it came from. Separately they measured about three minutes of pytest between them, which does not justify three checkouts and three container startups.
- `test_mla_backends.py` is split three ways: its correctness tests go to `mla/correctness/test_mla_backend_correctness.py`, a verbatim move of `main`'s two tests. The shared bodies go to the non-collected `tests/v1/attention/_mla_backends.py`, which keeps `main`'s `_prefill_backend_dimension_params` and `_run_backend_correctness`. The remaining tests go to `mla/backends/`. Collected cases match `main` apart from the path, and a new prefill backend is covered without a new file.
- Every top-level `tests/v1/attention` test file moves into a unit. The shared job also runs any test file added later at the `v1/attention` or `v1/attention/mla` root. `tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py` imports the GDN builder test from `ssm/`.
- The H100 job and its MI300 mirror keep their existing whole-area sharding (#57238 follows up on those). Earlier validation comments describe superseded layouts. AI assistance was used.

## Expected runtime and overhead

Measured in build [90322](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90322) on the same job boundaries. The MLA Correctness file is now one file instead of per-backend wrappers, so its hash split changes. Remapping 90322's per-case times to the new node IDs gives an even split (3.6 / 4.1 / 4.4 min of per-case time per shard). A build on this head will confirm it.

| job | pytest | running wall | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Sparse MLA | 14m05s | 14m31s | 0m26s | checkout and container startup |
| MLA Correctness 1 / 2 / 3 | 14m31s / 14m58s / 13m13s | 14m56s / 15m18s / 13m33s | ~0m20s each | same |
| Dense and SSM | 9m13s | 9m33s | 0m20s | same |
| DCP, MLA Backends and ROCm | 3m17s | 3m43s | 0m26s | same |

- Worker time 90m23s → 71m34s against same-coverage baseline build 90324, which is **about 19 fewer worker-minutes**. The slowest worker is ~15m wall, against 46m51s of pytest for the slowest old replica.
- Timeouts are sized to about twice each job's wall time.

title: [Bug][ROCm][Attention][KV Connector] DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.x DSA sparse-MLA decode is garbage under CUDA graphs in PD-disaggregation (remote-prefilled KV)
body:
## Summary
In PD-disaggregated serving on ROCm/MI300X (MoRIIO KV connector, WideEP DP8/EP8), the **decode** engine emits degenerate repeated-token garbage (`locklocklock…` / `!!!`) for **remote-prefilled** requests whenever decode runs under **any CUDA-graph capture** (`FULL`, `PIECEWISE`, or `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`). With `DECODE_CUDAGRAPH_MODE=NONE` (eager) the identical stack decodes **coherently**. Colocated (non-disagg) serving and vLLM v0.27.1 are unaffected.

## Environment
- vLLM **0.28.0** (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.28.0`), AITER 0.1.19, ROCm 7.2.3
- 2× **MI300X (gfx942)**, RoCEv2; KV connector = **MoRIIOConnector** (WRITE mode), `block_size=1`, fp8 KV
- Models: **GLM-5.3-FP8** and **GLM-5.1-FP8** (both `GlmMoeDsa`, DeepSeek-V3.2-style **DSA sparse-MLA**)
- Topology: 1P1D **WideEP DP8/EP8**; MTP on or off (does not matter)

## How to reproduce
1. Launch 1P1D PD-disagg (MoRIIO WRITE) — e.g. the AMD harness `.buildkite/amd-disagg/run-slurm-disagg-test.sh` with `WIDE_EP_MODE=1 MORIIO_READ_MODE=0` — using `DECODE_CUDAGRAPH_MODE=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`.
2. Send any request → decode returns `locklocklock…` (garbage).
3. Set `DECODE_CUDAGRAPH_MODE=NONE` (eager) → decode is coherent. (`FULL` and `PIECEWISE` are each garbage too.)

## Expected behavior
Decode under CUDA graphs produces the same coherent output as eager decode (and as colocated single-node / vLLM v0.27.1).

## Isolation — what did NOT fix it vs what WORKED
We walked the full transfer→decode path with per-step, on-device instrumentation applied identically to both engines.

**Did NOT fix it (still garbage), i.e. ruled out as the cause:**
- **KV-cache content / transfer** — the transfer is complete and **bit-exact** (producer == consumer bytes for every layer, including the sparse-indexer k_cache). Explicitly transferring the indexer k_cache changed nothing.
- **MoRI library version** — swapping v1.1.0 ↔ commit `42e895472b08` (the version used by the working v0.27.1 recipe) made no difference.
- **MoRI-EP `combine()` fix** (#56073 / ROCm/mori#475) — inert here (our EP8 runs the single-node **IntraNode** combine, not the InterNodeV1 path that fix targets).
- **Decode metadata** — byte-identical local-vs-remote for the same prompt (`num_computed_tokens`, positions, seq_len, block_table, indexer top-k, and post-remap global KV slots all match). Nothing to correct.
- **KV dtype** — reproduces with **fp8 and bf16** (so not an fp8-scale/dequant issue).
- **Transfer mode** — reproduces in **both READ and WRITE** MoRIIO modes.
- **MTP** — reproduces with speculative decode **on and off**.
- **Widening the eager CUDA-graph region** — restoring a broad `eager_break_during_capture` over the whole sparse decode (breakable/PIECEWISE) **still produced garbage**.

**WORKED (coherent), i.e. the differentiators:**
- **`DECODE_CUDAGRAPH_MODE=NONE` (eager decode)** — coherent, 3/3 prompts, MTP on and off.
- **Colocated single-node DP8/EP8** on the *same* v0.28 build/kernels/model (no remote KV) — coherent.
- **vLLM v0.27.1 + WideEP overlay** — the *same* PD-disagg path decodes coherently.

→ Coherent vs garbage turns on exactly **two conditions being simultaneously true: (1) the DSA sparse-MLA decode is captured in a CUDA graph, AND (2) it is consuming remotely-populated KV.** Removing *either* — run decode eager, or serve the same request colocated (locally-populated KV) — restores coherence. Reproduces on ≥2 DSA models (GLM-5.3-FP8, GLM-5.1-FP8). The corruption therefore lives in the **CUDA-graph capture/replay × remotely-populated-KV buffer lifecycle** of the DSA sparse-MLA decode (replayed steps appear to read stale sparse-index / remote-KV state), and it is **not** in transfer, metadata, scales, dtype, mode, MTP, or the eager-region width.

## Possibly related — and why
- **#51425 "[Perf] Narrow DeepSeek V3.2 eager CUDA graph region"** — the most direct link. It moved most of the DSA attention (query prep, norm/RoPE, GEMMs) *out* of the eager break and *into* the captured graph, leaving only `_sparse_indexer_and_attn` eager. This is the v0.28 change that first placed per-step DSA sparse-decode state under CUDA-graph capture, and GLM-5.x (DeepSeek-V3.2 architecture) rides exactly this path.
- **#51430 / #51768 / #52401 (DeepSeek-V4 analog)** — strong precedent that this class silently corrupts. #51430 applied the same narrowing to V4; #51768 then documented that **V4 + Model-Runner-V1 + PIECEWISE/FULL_AND_PIECEWISE = silent output corruption** and rejected that combo, noting **eager/NONE** as the mitigation (exactly our workaround); #52401 fixed it by choosing the eager region **per model runner**. So the fix pattern exists — but it was applied to **V4 only**, not to **V3.2 / GLM-5.x**, and not to the **PD-disagg remote-KV** case.
- **#56726 "[ROCm][Bugfix] Ignore descales for unquantized AITER caches"** — same *failure shape*: an AITER decode kernel consuming a **stale/unused scale (descale) tensor** corrupts output, and it surfaces under **CUDA-graph recapture**. Our MLA decode kernel is invoked as `mla_decode_fwd(q_scale=_q_scale, kv_scale=_k_scale)` — the direct analog; if those descales are captured stale, it matches our capture-only, dtype-independent signature. (#56726 patches the FA backend for *unquantized* caches, so it is not a drop-in fix for our MLA-sparse/fp8 path, but the mechanism is the same.)

**Why the existing fixes don't cover us:** widening the eager region (the #52401-style broad eager break over the sparse decode) **did not** restore coherence in our repro — so the corrupting operation is in a segment that stays captured even under the broad eager region. The residual defect is the **CUDA-graph × remotely-populated-KV buffer lifecycle**, which is deeper than eager-region width alone and specific to the PD-disagg (remote-prefill) decode path that none of the above PRs exercised.

## Workaround
`DECODE_CUDAGRAPH_MODE=NONE` (eager decode) — coherent, but ~5–8× slower decode throughput.

<sub>Investigation/repro assisted by AI tools; results reviewed and validated on-cluster.</sub>

title: [CI] Split the mixed (H200 MIG 35GB) Multimodal Standard 4 / Extended Generation 1 test files into core and extended wrappers
body:
## What

Split the four mixed multimodal files into core and extended wrappers over shared non-collected helpers. Keep Whisper and ViT wrappers flat under `standard/`; the correlated Moss/Voxtral audio pair shares a folder.

## Old

```text
generation/
├── audio/{test_whisper,test_moss_audio}.py
├── omni/test_voxtral.py
└── vision/test_vit_cudagraph.py
# each mixes core and extended cases
```

## New

```text
models/multimodal/
├── generation/{audio,omni,vision}/ # extended wrappers
└── standard/
    ├── _whisper.py  _vit_cudagraph.py  _voxtral.py  _moss_audio.py
    ├── test_whisper.py
    ├── test_vit_cudagraph.py
    ├── test_gemma_ragged_audio.py
    └── audio/{test_voxtral,test_moss_audio}.py
```

## Notes

- Shared bodies and parameter partitions are preserved. Flat singleton imports, and the CPU, Arm, distributed, Intel and legacy pipeline paths, are updated.
- After the core halves move out, nothing under `generation/audio` or `generation/vision` carries a `core_model` mark, so those two `-m 'not core_model'` filters are dropped as dead. The `omni` filter stays because `omni/test_ultravox.py` is still a mixed file.
- Includes #57065's moves and #56901's layout. Rebased onto current `main`, with `main`'s newer ViT configs (DeepSeek-V4.1, video metadata) carried into the shared helper. #57067 then splits Standard 4 into three named jobs; review this PR from "Split the four mixed…" onward (eight commits; the moondream, spawn and keep-flat ones are #56901's).
- Validation: wrapper move-equivalence, a static check that the ViT configs match `main`, Python/YAML parse, and Ruff all pass. The stack is validated once at #57067. AI assistance was used.

## Expected runtime and overhead

Routing only: the same cases run in the same jobs, and the dropped filters excluded nothing, so neither runtime nor worker-minutes change.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse][PD] Align region-mapped pulls across logical block sizes
body:
## Purpose

Fix a NIXL pull that can silently load the wrong prompt pages when P and D allocate KV differently. The motivating setup has **plain NIXL on P and NIXL + HiSparse on D**, with **`--block-size 128` on both servers**.

The same command-line block size does not guarantee the same allocation. A logical block is the unit the scheduler allocates; a physical page is the unit used by the attention kernel and transfer. With a kernel that requires 64-token pages, plain P can keep 128-token logical blocks and split each into two physical pages. HiSparse's setup on D resolves its MLA scheduler blocks to the native 64-token size directly. That produces this geometry in the affected path:

| | Command-line block size | Scheduler's logical block | Physical/kernel page |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| P: plain NIXL, HiSparse disabled | 128 | 128 | 64 |
| D: NIXL + HiSparse | 128 | 64 | 64 |

For a **160-token prompt**, P must allocate two logical blocks: capacity for 256 tokens, or **four physical pages**. D needs only **three physical pages**. Let `A` and `B` each hold 64 tokens, and `C` hold the remaining 32:

```text
P advertises:       [ A | B | C | unused ]
D has space for:    [   |   |   ]

Current selection:  [ B | C | unused ]  <- last three producer pages
Correct selection:  [ A | B | C ]
```

Logical-to-physical expansion already happens. The mistake comes afterward: the region-based suffix matcher assumes that any extra pages on P represent a prefix D has already cached. Here the extra page is unused capacity at the end, so that assumption shifts the whole transfer. If D has actually cached `A`, the remaining transfer should select `B, C`; the old logic selects `C, unused`.

**The fix selects pages by token position.** Pass the producer's existing `remote_num_tokens` through to the worker, combine it with each destination group's cached-prefix offset, and select the corresponding physical pages. Whole-page transfers remain: `C` is transferred with its unused rows, but the entirely unused fourth page does not shift the selection. This adds no prefill on D.

**HiSparse also exposes a separate assumption at transfer completion.** P can keep main KV and indexer KV in one merged cache group. D separates host KV and GPU indexer KV into different groups, so NIXL uses *regions* to match the corresponding memory buffers. The old `get_transfer_results()` still pairs groups by position. Looking up P's group 1 for D's group 1 can fail because P has only group 0, or pair the wrong blocks when the index exists.

Completion now uses the region read plan. The worker records `region_blocks_to_zero`: whole destination pages that were allocated but excluded from the read. For example, in the reverse allocation geometry, D may reserve four pages while P supplies three:

```text
D after the read:   [ A | B | C | untouched ]
D after completion:[ A | B | C | zeroed    ]
```

For two example regions with destination IDs `[10, 11, 12, 13]` and `[20, 21, 22, 23]`, receiving three pages into each produces a cleanup plan of `[[13], [23]]`. Completion clears page 13 only in its region and page 23 only in its region, then skips the old positional group processing.

This plan is local to one request on the receiving worker. `None` means use the existing completion path; empty per-region lists mean a region-mapped read with nothing to zero. In the original P-four-pages/D-three-pages example, D receives all its pages, so there is **no zeroing**. The plan does not include cached prefix pages or unused rows within the transferred partial page. It is discarded with the request's receive metadata; failed reads skip this cleanup.

Scope: pure MLA region pulls with equal physical page sizes, DCP=1, and one cache-group owner per region. Heterogeneous logical geometry without the required metadata or with shared-group regions is rejected. Existing homogeneous fallback behavior remains.

**Dependency:** the empty-receive fixes belong to #57049 (also present in #56946, originally from #55398). They are excluded from this PR, which will be rebased after that prerequisite lands. #57049's HiSparse tail-import policy remains separate from this transfer-alignment fix.

Duplicate checks included related issue #57019, its comments, and open PR searches for that issue, NIXL logical/physical geometry, and region padding. #57027 fixes layer binding offsets. #55374 introduces broader piecewise token-window loading in the ordinary group-based pull/push paths; its current diff does not wire that through the region-based path introduced by #53780. This PR addresses that region path without adding the piecewise-loading API.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, and validation. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing the changed lines and validating the patched GPU deployment. GPU accuracy validation remains pending.


## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py -m cpu_test -q

uv run --no-project pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/metadata.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/pull_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py
```

GPU follow-up: apply this fix alongside #57049 and #57027, restore block size 128, and repeat the same 100-question GSM8K sample with the same model, prompt/scoring settings, and concurrency 10. A full matched evaluation remains pending.

## Test Result

- CPU suite: **91 passed, 1 deselected**. Includes real receive-path page expansion and descriptor selection with transport mocked, producer/consumer padding, unequal per-region cache hits, and completion zeroing across strided layer views.
- Negative control: restoring main's mapping methods in memory makes the 160-token regression fail on the source descriptors: `[21, 22, 23, 121, 122, 123]` versus `[20, 21, 22, 120, 121, 122]`.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Tile DSV4 inverse RoPE for sparse prefill
body:
## Purpose

Optimize the inverse GPT-J RoPE step in the ROCm DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA
prefill path on gfx950.

The production `T >= 256, H=64, D=512, rope_dim=64` BF16 shape uses an
8-row tiled kernel with `num_warps=4`. Other shapes and dtypes continue to use
the existing row-wise kernel. This complements the existing AITER OPUS routing
without changing the OPUS kernel, DP/TP process groups, or communication.

## Test Plan

- Validate inverse-RoPE dispatch at 255/256/257 tokens against the independent
  PyTorch reference.
- Validate CUDA graph capture and replay.
- Run single-GPU microbenchmarks on MI355X.
- Run matched nightly baseline/candidate TP8 E2E benchmarks with random
  8K-token input, 1K-token output, and concurrency 64/128.

## Test Result

Completed on one MI355X GPU:

- Python compilation and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Inverse-RoPE 255/256 dispatch boundary: pass.
- CUDA graph replay: pass.
- NoPE lanes: bit-exact.
- RoPE lanes: pass reference tolerance.
- Fallback shapes, dtypes, and architecture guard: pass.

Inverse-RoPE latency:

| 256 | 13.16 us | 5.57 us | 2.36x |
| 1024 | 45.82 us | 20.66 us | 2.22x |
| 8192 | 568.74 us | 184.85 us | 3.08x |

Matched TP8 E2E on eight MI355X GPUs:

- Nightly baseline includes the existing AITER OPUS sparse-prefill routing.
- Candidate uses the same nightly image plus this PR's source patch.
- TP8, DP1, exact 8192-token input and 1024-token output.
- Concurrency 64 uses 640 prompts; concurrency 128 uses 1280 prompts.
- Every run completed all requests with zero failures.
- The workload selected AITER OPUS, so the measured local-compute change is
  the inverse-RoPE optimization in this PR.

| Metric | c64 baseline | c64 candidate | Delta | c128 baseline | c128 candidate | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Request throughput (req/s) | 1.00312 | 1.00201 | -0.111% | 1.23075 | 1.23087 | +0.009% |
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 9244.78 | 9234.52 | -0.111% | 11342.59 | 11343.65 | +0.009% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 3472.84 | 3474.07 | +0.035% | 5139.87 | 5141.06 | +0.023% |
| P99 TTFT (ms) | 29754.04 | 29747.73 | -0.021% | 58680.66 | 58694.92 | +0.024% |

The observed E2E differences are within approximately +/-0.15%, so this run
does not show a measurable TP8 throughput improvement. The microbenchmark
benefit is diluted by the full 8K/1K model workload.
