title: [ROCm][Perf] FP8 o-projection for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash MLA on AMD MI355X
body:
## FP8 o-projection for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash MLA on AMD MI355X

Ports the FP8 output-projection chain (`wo_a`) from the CUDA path to ROCm
on MI355X (gfx950). CUDA already runs `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`; ROCm was
dequantizing the FP8 E4M3 `wo_a` weight to BF16 and running `torch.einsum`
on every forward pass of all 40 layers.

### What changes

**`vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/amd/rocm.py`**

- `rocm_prepare_inv_rope_woa_fp8` / `prepare_wo_a_fp8`: new load-time hook
  that rearranges the checkpoint's 32×32 E8M0 block scales to the 128×128
  layout expected by `batched_gemm_a8w8_mxscale`, storing the result and a
  pre-computed FP32 cos/sin cache on the layer.
- `DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention.forward`: FP8 fast path using
  `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` (Triton) → `batched_gemm_a8w8_mxscale`
  (AITER CK), with fallback to the existing BF16 path when
  `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()` and the cache is cold.

**Why load-time, not lazy:**
Decode at this serving configuration dispatches `CUDAGraphMode.FULL`. A cold
cos/sin cache at CUDA-graph capture time permanently bakes the BF16 fallback
into every replay for the lifetime of the process. The preparation therefore
runs in `process_weights_after_loading`; V4.1 reaches this hook twice (once
pre-quant-finalize), so the prime uses a sticky-retry/recompute guard.

### Correctness

Scale rearrangement (32×32 → 128×128 E8M0) measures **164.7 dB** against the
exact fp32 dequant — the same tensor. End-to-end SNR **31.4–31.6 dB** equals
the producer-alone SNR at every M (1, 6, 192, 4096), confirming that all
precision loss is FP8 activation quantization — identical to what CUDA's
`deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` performs, not introduced by the scale rearrangement.
Output is bitwise-identical to the BF16 path within FP8 tolerance at every
measured shape.

### Component-level speedup (MI355X gfx950, graph-captured, weakest-of-5)

| Batch M | Serving context | `wo_a` kernel: BF16 → FP8 |
|--------:|----------------|--------------------------|
| 1 | decode / TPOT | **1.51×** |
| 6 | DSpark verify block | **1.17×** |
| 192 | C32 operating point (25.73 µs → 18.85 µs) | **1.53×** |
| 4096 | prefill / TTFT | **1.38×** |

Speedup fades toward large M as expected for a weight-bandwidth-bound kernel.

### End-to-end benchmark (MI355X, TP=4, C=32, agentic-coding scenario)

| Metric | Before | After | Δ |
|--------|-------:|------:|--:|
| Output throughput | 231.76 tok/s/chip | 244.33 tok/s/chip | **+5.42%** |
| p90 interactivity | 33.77 tok/s/user | 36.97 tok/s/user | **+9.48%** |
| p90 TPOT | 29.6 ms | 27.1 ms | **−8.5%** |

~5.8σ above the measured cross-run coefficient of variation (0.94%).

Note: developed with AI assistance (Claude). All changes reviewed and validated end-to-end by the submitter.

title: [ROCm][MLA][DCP] Enable ROCM_AITER_MLA non-causal DSpark draft under DCP
body:
## Purpose

Let `ROCM_AITER_MLA` serve Kimi-K3 DSpark's **non-causal** multi-token draft block while the MLA KV cache is **DCP-sharded**, so the draft no longer has to fall back to `TRITON_MLA` when the target runs on AITER.

DSpark emits a query block in parallel: every query token attends the same committed KV prefix rather than a causal triangular suffix within the block. The AITER backend already serves this on the single-rank decode path (`supports_non_causal_multi_token_decode`) and already returns per-row LSE on the DCP decode path for the cross-shard merge. Two things kept it off under DCP.

## Changes (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py`)

- **Advertise the capability.** Set `supports_non_causal_multi_token_dcp = True` on `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder`. The eligibility gate `AttentionBackend.supports_non_causal_dcp()` reads this; leaving it `False` made backend selection reject the draft.
- **Keep non-causal blocks off the causal-only segmented DCP verify.** `use_segmented_dcp_verify` now also requires `causal`. The segmented path applies its causal bound in-kernel and cannot express the untruncated range; a non-causal block routed there comes back silently causally masked.
- **Thread causality into the DCP native decode.** The `dcp_world_size > 1` path calls aiter's native `mla_decode_fwd` (to keep the LSE the wrapper drops) but was not passing `causal`, so the persistent kernel masked causally regardless. Pass `attn_metadata.causal` so the `mask0` kernel is selected.

Causal target verification is unchanged (ordinary decode, Gluon small-head verify, and segmented DCP verify all still take the causal path).

## Relationship to prior PRs

- Revives the `ROCM_AITER_MLA` half of the **closed #56051**. The merged **#55966** kept only the non-DCP non-causal decode and left `supports_non_causal_multi_token_dcp` `False`.
- Parallel to **#54546**, which advertises the same capability for `TRITON_MLA`.
- Complements **#51705** (merged) which handles causal multi-token target verification under DCP.

## Requirements

Requires an AITER build exposing `aiter.mla.mla_decode_fwd(..., causal=)` with the gfx950 `mask0` persistent decode kernels (ROCm/aiter#4565, AITER ≥ v0.1.21.post1). Older wheels fail closed at backend selection via `supports_non_causal()`.

## Status / validation

**Draft.** Boots on 8×MI355X TP8/DCP8 (A2A DCP, FP8 KV, 1M ctx, DSpark draft on `ROCM_AITER_MLA`). Full GSM8K / accuracy A/B vs `TRITON_MLA` still pending and must be completed by a human submitter before this leaves draft.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to author this change.

title: [Kimi-K3][Perf] Overlap shared-output all-reduce with routed experts
body:
## Purpose

Overlap Kimi-K3's shared-expert output all-reduce with monolithic routed-expert
execution when the existing latent-tail fusion does not cover the current token
shape:

```text
shared-expert MLP
  -> low-SM shared-output TP all-reduce (aux stream)
     || routed-expert monolithic W1/W2 BMM (main stream)
  -> join -> routed-latent all-reduce + RMSNorm
  -> replicated latent up-projection -> add pre-reduced shared output
```

The optimization is disabled by default behind
`VLLM_KIMI_K3_SHARED_OUTPUT_AR_OVERLAP`. This lets disaggregated decode workers
opt in without changing prefill workers. When disabled, or when the device,
collective, dtype, parallel layout, or tensor shape is unsupported, the runner
keeps its existing schedule. Shapes already handled by K3 latent-tail fusion
also keep that path.

The reusable `LowSMAllReduce` implementation is a bounded BF16 NVLS collective
for NVIDIA SM100/SM103. It derives TP size, payload capacity, doorbell storage,
and result-slot count at runtime; rank-validates the contract; uses one
single-flight slot per ubatch; and falls back collectively if symmetric-memory
or NVLS resources are unavailable. The CUDA kernel uses four CTAs so routed
expert work can retain most SMs while the reduction is in flight.

### Duplicate-work check

No open upstream PR implements this NVIDIA K3 schedule:

- #53556 removes the shared reduction for DeepGEMM MegaMoE tail fusion, a
  different dependency/configuration path.
- #56510 makes the existing fused GEMM/all-reduce SM margin configurable.
- #55072 adds a low-SM MNNVL reduce-scatter rather than an all-reduce.
- #51437 and #56167 target ROCm backends.

## Benchmark Result

Historical end-to-end measurements of the same schedule/kernel design on two
four-GPU GB300 nodes, TP8+DCP8, DSpark 7, concurrency 64, and shared output
`[448, 7168]` were:

| Metric | Baseline | Overlap | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Target TP critical path | 85.581 ms | 82.064 ms | **-4.11%** |
| Median batch duration | 17.539 s | 16.804 s | **-4.19%** |
| Median throughput | 3.649 req/s | 3.809 req/s | **+4.38%** |

All 7,360 sampled shared-output reductions overlapped routed W1. These are
supporting historical measurements, not a performance claim for every runtime
TP size or shape, and this upstream adaptation was not rebenchmarked end to
end.

The prior final native reducer also passed cross-node TP8 H7168/M448 eager
comparison and 47,104 captured collectives with zero sampled error. A
deterministic 128-prompt Kimi-K3 A/B completed with 128/128 HTTP 200 responses
and zero errors in each arm. Output token IDs/text were exact for 117/128
prompts; direct isolation characterized the difference as normal BF16
reduction-order rounding (maximum absolute difference 0.125 at M24), while
M401/M412/M448/M512/M896 were bitwise equal to NCCL.

title: [Bug] GLM-5.3 hybrid (nvfp4, GB10/sm121, TP2): concurrent batching corrupts non-ASCII generation — fragment-token state poisoning + silent DecodeStream FFFD flush
body:
# [Bug] GLM-5.3 hybrid (nvfp4, GB10/sm121, TP2): concurrent batching corrupts non-ASCII generation — fragment-token state poisoning, plus silent DecodeStream FFFD flush

## Environment
- vLLM: v0.29.1rc1.dev145+gbb5507741 (stock checkout)
- Model: GLM-5.3-Flash nvfp4 checkpoint (182GB, BF16 lm_head/embeddings)
- Hardware: 2× NVIDIA GB10 (sm121) TP2 over rail; bf16 KV cache
- transformers 5.16.1, nccl 2.29.7
- Attention backend: FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120 — the only backend accepted
  for this configuration (FLASHMLA_SPARSE and FLASHINFER_MLA are rejected by
  supports_combination), so the sparse path could not be A/B'd
- Speculative decoding: off (`speculative_config=None`)

## Reproducer
4 concurrent `/v1/chat/completions` requests, emoji-dense prompts
("write a huge wall of emojis (~350) mixed with short words"), temperature 0,
`chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}`, max_tokens ~2000.
Sequential requests: mostly clean. Concurrent: U+FFFD appears reliably
(8–80 per ~500-char wall before mitigation). Concurrency is the amplifier;
non-ASCII output density is the sensitivity knob. ASCII-only generation is
unaffected.

## Primary finding: corruption is in the sampled token ids (state poisoning class)
1. **Near-miss CJK glyphs** (valid but wrong characters) — cannot be produced
   by any downstream string surgery.
2. **Fragment-token rate explodes under load**: ~1 empty-render token per
   wall sequential vs 6+ concurrent (measured via logprobs, which mirror the
   sampled ids).
3. **Margin capture at corrupt slots** (logprobs + top_logprobs=3): corrupt
   slots show token pairs — a moderately-confident byte-fragment pick
   (−1 to −2) followed immediately by an ultra-confident fragment
   (−0.0x) — and the **entire top-3 at those slots is byte-fragment
   tokens**: the intended merged emoji token is pushed out of contention.
   This is a distribution scramble (state-level), not a near-tie flip, not
   NaN (`VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS=1` produced zero hits), not the sampler.
4. **Autoregressive cascade**: once a fragment lands, follow-up fragments go
   ultra-confident (one wall snowballed to 80 FFFD in 492 chars).
5. **Mojibake is model output**: byte-alphabet token strings (e.g. `ðŁ§¿`,
   the raw UTF-8 bytes of an emoji as Latin-1-class characters) get emitted
   when corrupted history is replayed — the model imitates them.

## Exhausted flag matrix (all configurations corrupt)
- KV cache dtype: fp8_ds_mla AND bf16
- Prefix caching: on and off
- CUDA graphs: on and off (`--enforce-eager`)
- Both text endpoints, streaming and non-streaming
- Offline byte-exact replays through the HF tokenizer, the Rust DecodeStream,
  and the full FastIncrementalDetokenizer pipeline are clean — all text
  handling exonerated; the ids themselves are wrong
- TP1 infeasible for isolation (182GB > 121GB per-node pool)

## Secondary bugs (amplifiers, each independently reportable)
1. **Silent FFFD flush on tag interrupt** — `vllm/v1/engine/detokenizer.py`
   `_protected_step` (~lines 224–248): when a single-token tag
   (`</think>` = 154842, `<tool_call>` = 154843) interrupts a pending
   partial UTF-8 sequence, the pending bytes are flushed as U+FFFD with **no
   logging on this path**. A one-line warning would have saved us an evening.
2. **Silent tool-call swallowing**: FFFD-contaminated tool names fail
   `validate_tool_names` and the whole call is dropped with no surface error.
3. **`_flush_arg_converter` drops argument tails** on prefix-invariant
   violations instead of re-syncing.
4. **Corruption self-propagates through history**: mojibake in context gets
   imitated, so agentic loops compound the damage.

## Working mitigation (8/8 concurrent walls, zero FFFD)
- System-prompt steering toward ASCII output
- `logit_bias` blocking the 1,024 token ids that are invalid UTF-8 alone
  (of 1,095; note: >1024 ids raises `ValueError: Too many logit bias tokens`
  — cap worth revisiting for this use case) — by construction this leaves
  all legitimate multi-byte tokens unblocked
- Client-side scoped strip (FFFD + emoji ranges U+1F000–1FAFF, U+2600–27BF,
  FE0F, 200D) on every rendered message before history append

## Asks
1. Investigate batch-shape-dependent numerics/state in the GLM hybrid path
   (DSA/indexer, sparse MLA on sm120-named kernels running on sm121, MoE
   grouped GEMMs) under concurrent batching.
2. Log the DecodeStream tag-interrupt FFFD flush.
3. Harden tool-name validation and `_flush_arg_converter` to re-sync rather
   than silently drop.
4. Consider raising or documenting the logit_bias 1024-id cap.

Happy to provide the full margin-capture JSON, repro scripts, and the
offline replay harness on request.

title: [Bugfix] Validate activation schemes for Marlin and Triton WNA16 MoE
body:
## Problem and change

Marlin and Triton WNA16 MoE capability checks currently accept arbitrary activation keys whenever the weight key matches. An NVFP4 W4A4 request can consequently select a Marlin path that does not implement NVFP4 activation quantization.

Require the activation contract actually used by these integrations (`activation_key=None`). Apply the check in `MarlinExpertsBase`, covering standard and batched Marlin, and in `TritonWNA16Experts`. Preserve FP8's existing Marlin fallback by explicitly resolving its effective activation key in the FP8 oracle, matching the quantization config it constructs. INT WNA16 and MXFP4 selectors already supply the corresponding effective key.

**This does not mean Marlin cannot quantize activations.** Marlin supports internal INT8/FP8 activation quantization selected separately through `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE`; those existing integrations still use `activation_key=None` and pass unquantized inputs into the experts wrapper. The environment-controlled A8 mode, its weight preparation, and the internal quantizer are unchanged. Nonempty activation keys must not be accepted merely because some other activation quantization mode exists. The stale constructor comment saying activation quantization is unimplemented is replaced with this distinction.

Declared NVFP4 W4A16 remains eligible; explicit/automatic NVFP4 activation-quantized requests cannot substitute Marlin. Per-token keys and CuTe-DSL support remain in the later split PRs.

## Relationship to existing work and attribution

This is the first prerequisite extracted from #50030 following the [requested three-way split](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50030#issuecomment-5690078085). The Marlin guard is taken from S1ro1's change, with S1ro1 retained as the first commit author. This extends that fix to Triton WNA16, protects FP8 fallback compatibility, and adds regression coverage. This PR owns all Marlin activation-contract changes. The per-token-specific Marlin guard is removed from #57176 in favor of this generic check, so merge order is #57091 → #57176 → #50030. No per-token key needs to be introduced here: any nonempty activation key is rejected by the existing generic rule.

Searches for open Marlin/activation, weight-only activation, and #50030-related PRs found no separate PR for this capability fix. Related but distinct work: #56535 fixes B12x's W4A16 execution handoff; #55675 concerns compressed-tensors MXFP4 linear activation-declaration reporting. Dense Marlin linear kernels have separate, intentional weight-only fallback interfaces and are not changed here. The OCP MX emulation capability predicate is intentionally unconditional because its oracle selects it directly.

## Validation

- Dependency validation after moving all Marlin changes to #57091: applied #57091's five-file diff to this revision, then ran `PYTHONPATH=/var/tmp/pr57176-humming-deps .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py -k 'nvfp4_per_token_backend_contract or nvfp4_per_token_rejects or weight_only_experts or preserves_marlin or does_not_substitute or internal_a8' -q --tb=short`: **30 passed, 71 deselected**. The prerequisite patch was removed after validation; it is not duplicated in #57176. These are configuration tests, not GPU numerical/model evaluation.

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py -k 'weight_only_experts or preserves_marlin or does_not_substitute or internal_a8' -q --tb=short`: 26 passed. Covers every advertised weight key for standard/batched Marlin and Triton WNA16, quantized-activation rejection, and explicit/automatic FP8 and NVFP4 selection. Four additional cases verify that both standard/batched Marlin remain eligible and preserve internal INT8/FP8 mode in the constructed experts object. FP8 hardware eligibility is simulated in these configuration-only tests; they do not validate A8 GEMM numerics.
- Running the original 22 regression tests against unmodified production files at `031f5810c1` reproduces 11 failures; the remaining 11 compatibility cases pass.
- Full `tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py` before the four A8 configuration cases were added: 43 passed, 1 skipped, 2 failed. Both failures also reproduce on unmodified production files: installed Humming lacks `humming.transform`, and the reused local native extension has the older `gptq_marlin_repack` argument schema.
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py -k dispatches_to_marlin_when_w4a16 -q --tb=short`: collection blocked by missing `vllm.third_party.flashmla.flash_mla_interface` in this worktree; no ModelOpt result claimed.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks on the five changed files passed, including Ruff and mypy; `git diff --check` passed.
- Tests used the existing Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130 environment on GB200, with existing native extensions linked into the isolated worktree. No kernel implementation or arithmetic changed. Model accuracy/serving evaluations have not been run; the native-extension mismatch prevents treating this environment as validated for current-source Marlin execution. This is a draft pending compatible GPU validation and human line-by-line review.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped audit related paths, implement the extension of the original fix, and run validation.

title: [Rust Frontend] Add MiniCPM5 tool parser support
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57096/files) against `main`.

## Summary

Implement the `minicpm5` tool-parser parity item for the Rust frontend from #44280. This updates the existing PR rather than opening a duplicate.

Add native MiniCPM5 XML-style function-call parsing and register it with Rust chat serving. Support non-streaming and streaming output, arbitrary decoded chunk boundaries, multiple calls, schema-aware parameter conversion/validation, wrapped parameters, aliases, and invalid/truncated-input fallback. Streaming emits each call ID/name once and reconstructs valid JSON arguments.

Add four real-model OpenAI E2E cases to the existing tool-use suite: single/multiple calls × synchronous/streaming responses. Reuse its model configuration and fixtures, and add a MiniCPM5 command to the existing Rust frontend tool-use CI job.

## Test Plan

Rebased onto vLLM main `ab35354c21cc3c36439e79e18070f85cfafc3af2`, addressing the merge-conflict report. Feature commit: `2f97de24b32844019fee456ccc757b313c19e9a3`; E2E commit / tested head: `48ec263c5558b91e485106cb9c7dd08e4fbe9520`.

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat --lib
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat \
  --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo build --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --release -p vllm-cmd --bin vllm-rs

VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 pytest -v -s tests/tool_use/test_tool_calls.py \
  --models minicpm5 --extended -k test_minicpm5_auto_tool_calls
```

## Test Result

| Test | Tested revision / scope | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MiniCPM5 parser unit tests | Rebased head; XML parsing, chunk boundaries, schema handling, fallback | 5 passed (included below) |
| Parser regression | Rebased head, `cargo test -p vllm-parser --lib` | 462 passed |
| Chat unit regression | Rebased head, `cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib` | 333 passed, including MiniCPM5 registry test |
| Chat integration | Rebased head, `tests/chat.rs` | 17 passed |
| Cross-model HF roundtrip | Rebased head, `tests/roundtrip.rs` | 1 passed; 18 failed fetching HF model files due to connection timeouts; not counted as passed |
| Rust formatting / Clippy | Rebased head; parser/chat all targets, `-D warnings` | Passed |
| Python lint / format / diff hygiene | Rebased head; repository-configured Ruff, `git diff --check` | Passed |
| Release Rust frontend build | Rebased head, `vllm-cmd --bin vllm-rs` | Built successfully |
| Real GPU E2E before rebase | Four new pytest cases; original feature binary | 4 passed, 2 deselected, 85.36 s |
| Real GPU E2E after rebase: single call, non-streaming | Rebuilt Rust frontend + real MiniCPM5-2B / DSpark | Passed |
| Real GPU E2E after rebase: single call, streaming | Same; reconstruct JSON arguments, ID/name emitted once | Passed |
| Real GPU E2E after rebase: two calls, non-streaming | Same; unique IDs and expected city set | Passed |
| Real GPU E2E after rebase: two calls, streaming | Same; indexed deltas and `finish_reason=tool_calls` | Passed |
| Four-case post-rebase E2E aggregate | Exact committed pytest file, SHA256 `9d704048f2db8f4db8b1f923e10a3e8b99bac8654b11cf4b254a2008eecba9c8` | 4 passed, 2 deselected, 14.39 s |
| H200 / ROCm CI and broad model quality / performance | Not run locally | Pending CI / outside targeted validation |

Real GPU serving uses one NVIDIA L20, vLLM 0.29.0, BF16 MiniCPM5-2B and MiniCPM5-2B-DSpark, eager mode and seven speculative tokens. The Rust frontend is rebuilt from the rebased source; the Python engine is the installed vLLM 0.29.0 runtime, not a full Python-main engine validation. Binary SHA256: `6f8a55e37930f2c0e86e7bae207c1d0130f2ba47bbbdc0ad07b2ced45b36ae45`.

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 .venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve \
  /path/to/MiniCPM5-2B --served-model-name MiniCPM5-2B \
  --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 2048 --enforce-eager \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"/path/to/MiniCPM5-2B-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7}' \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser minicpm5
```

The earlier real-model smoke passed a non-streaming weather call, streaming tool-call deltas with reconstructable JSON arguments, and two weather calls in one completion, all with `finish_reason=tool_calls`. DSpark itself is not modified by this PR. These are targeted tool-serving regressions, not broad model-quality or performance evaluations.

The local four-case run uses the committed pytest file against an independently started real service, with a live-server client fixture (`AsyncOpenAI` at localhost), not a mock engine. CI uses the existing tool-use server fixtures and the new `--models minicpm5 --extended` command. JUnit and server logs are retained. Draft pending review.

title: [Kimi K3 Bug] Fix kimi k3 reasoning parser
body:
## Purpose

This bug from a real user case, minimal reproduce command:

```bash

vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --load-format fastsafetensors \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000 \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-speculator.dspark","method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":8,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"standard"}'   --use-replayssm   --max-num-seqs 48
```

## Test

Use this script

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reproduce Kimi-K3 truncated-reasoning classification through vLLM."""

import json
from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen


URL = "http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions"
MODEL = "moonshotai/Kimi-K3"

payload = {
    "model": MODEL,
    "messages": [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": (
                "Solve this carefully: find the exact number of distinct ways to "
                "color the vertices of a dodecahedron with four colors, modulo all "
                "rotational symmetries. Return only the required JSON after reasoning."
            ),
        }
    ],
    "temperature": 0,
    # Deliberately stop K3 before it can finish its reasoning.
    "max_tokens": 16,
    "stream": False,
    "response_format": {
        "type": "json_schema",
        "json_schema": {
            "name": "answer",
            "strict": True,
            "schema": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {"answer": {"type": "string"}},
                "required": ["answer"],
                "additionalProperties": False,
            },
        },
    },
    "chat_template_kwargs": {
        "thinking": True,
        "enable_thinking": True,
    },
}

request = Request(
    URL,
    data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
    headers={
        "Authorization": "Bearer EMPTY",
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    method="POST",
)

try:
    with urlopen(request, timeout=120) as response:
        result = json.load(response)
except HTTPError as error:
    print(f"HTTP {error.code}: {error.read().decode('utf-8', errors='replace')}")
    raise SystemExit(1) from error
except URLError as error:
    print(f"Cannot connect to {URL}: {error.reason}")
    raise SystemExit(1) from error

choice = result["choices"][0]
message = choice["message"]
content = message.get("content")
reasoning = message.get("reasoning") or message.get("reasoning_content")

print(f"finish_reason: {choice.get('finish_reason')}")
print(f"content: {content!r}")
print(f"reasoning: {reasoning!r}")

if choice.get("finish_reason") == "length" and content and not reasoning:
    print("\nBUG reproduced: truncated reasoning was incorrectly returned as content.")
elif choice.get("finish_reason") == "length" and reasoning and not content:
    print("\nFIX verified: truncated text is reasoning; content is empty.")
else:
    print("\nThe model did not take the expected truncation path; rerun the request.")

```
Before:

```bash
python repro_kimi_k3_truncated_reasoning.py 
finish_reason: length
content: 'We need solve. Need return only JSON after reasoning. Need compute exact number of'
reasoning: None

BUG reproduced: truncated reasoning was incorrectly returned as content.
```

Now

```bash
python repro_kimi_k3_truncated_reasoning.py
finish_reason: length
content: None
reasoning: 'We need solve. Need return only JSON after reasoning. Need compute exact number of'

FIX verified: truncated text is reasoning; content is empty.
```

title: [Perf][MRV2] Share token-to-request mappings across KV cache groups
body:
## Purpose

`build_attn_metadata()` creates one `CommonAttentionMetadata` per KV cache group, and each group lazily launches its own token-to-request mapping kernel — even though every group in the same call sees identical query boundaries and token padding. A DeepSeek V4.1 spec-decode trace shows 6 mapping launches in target prep and 3 in draft prep per step, all computing the same mapping.

## Change

Share one mapping across KV cache groups within a single `build_attn_metadata()` call (+3 lines in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py`):

- A per-call local cache is threaded through each group's `CommonAttentionMetadata` (`_token_to_req_indices_cache`).
- The first group that needs the mapping builds it into its existing persistent buffer; later groups reuse that tensor instead of launching the kernel again.
- The cache lives only for the duration of one call, so target/draft prep stay isolated and each step recomputes from fresh inputs — no cross-step state, safe under CUDA-graph replay.

Builds on merged #56562 (Triton mapping kernel) by removing repeat launches across groups. Dup checks: searched open PRs for `token_to_req_indices`, `"metadata" "KV" "share"`, `56562 in:body` — none. Related but distinct: #56996, #41834.

## Test Plan

GB200, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py
git diff --check
```

## Test Result

- 30 passed, 1 failed — the failure (`test_indexer_builder_deepseek_v4_compressed_slot_mapping_uses_num_states`) needs access to the gated HF repo `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B` (401 in this environment); unrelated to this change.
- Mapping launches: target **6 → 1**, draft **3 → 1**; total kernel launches 30 → 25 and 12 → 10

### Metadata-builder benchmark

The benchmark calls the real SWA, MLA, indexer, and compressor builders through `build_attn_metadata()`, approximating the trace's launch pattern: target prep uses six KV groups with six query tokens per request, draft prep three noncausal SWA groups with five; context 8,192, SWA window 128, block size 128, persistent token capacity 16,384.

Measured quantity is **host wall time per `build_attn_metadata()` call** (builder Python + kernel submission; input prep and compilation excluded). 100 warmup calls, then 12 rounds × 200 calls alternating baseline/candidate; medians of per-round averages, no profiler, GC disabled during timing, GPU clocks not locked.

| Batch | Builder suite | Before (µs) | After (µs) | Saved (µs) | Reduction |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | Target | 1261.14 | 1120.84 | 140.30 | 11.12% |
| 1 | Draft | 484.71 | 425.06 | 59.66 | 12.31% |
| 16 | Target | 1237.62 | 1100.57 | 137.05 | 11.07% |
| 16 | Draft | 469.18 | 415.60 | 53.57 | 11.42% |
| 128 | Target | 1242.93 | 1102.52 | 140.41 | 11.30% |
| 128 | Draft | 482.71 | 426.00 | 56.72 | 11.75% |

At batch 1 the target+draft host medians sum to **1.746 → 1.546 ms**, i.e. **0.20 ms saved per step** of metadata building. GPU-side span (CUPTI, CUDA-graph replay, cold L2, median of 4×100 replays): target 66.7 → 58.0 µs, draft 27.7 → 24.1 µs.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex implemented the change and ran the reported checks under the submitter's direction; human review of every changed line and human-run validation remain required.
