title: [Kernel][PCP] Publish direct-final KV into ExtensibleKVCache storage
body:
## Summary

Publish replicated PCP KV updates directly into ExtensibleKVCache-owned storage. The existing fused Norm/RoPE/cache writer writes each rank's updates into every PCP peer's final cache, then a system-scope publication barrier makes the local replica ready for the unchanged Indexer and sparse MLA consumers.

```text
ASIS
Norm/RoPE -> rank-local KV tensors -> PCP AllGather
         -> native cache insertion -> local replicated KV -> attention

PR
ExtensibleKVCache owns VA + physical pages
         -> export/import handles -> stable PCP peer mappings
Norm/RoPE + cache writer -> final peer KV stores -> publication barrier
         -> local replicated KV -> attention
```

KV backing remains owned by ExtensibleKVCache; this change does not allocate a second KV cache through PyTorch SymmetricMemory. Peer address reservations and pointer tables remain stable while the owner commits additional physical chunks. Peer mappings are released before owner physical pages are released. Rank-local slot mappings retain the same base address for CUDA Graph capture and replay.

**Draft; depends on #56492.** This branch includes the tested allocator snapshot `6a4ef9654ce2b31d3205a87712e167fdf207b366`, integrated with main at `24bfbd5d4d`. #56492 remains open and has advanced since that snapshot; this draft will need synchronization before landing. The full diff against main therefore includes the prerequisite. Review this feature alone in [commit c33c40aafd](https://github.com/foraxe/vllm/commit/c33c40aafdd309094daea3287bf4abbd1b3702d1) (13 files).

This is not a second SymmetricMemory implementation of #52863: it replaces SymmetricMemory-owned KV backing with ExtensibleKVCache-owned VA/physical storage, adds incremental peer mappings for cache growth, and validates decode-only full-graph replay using #53867's infrastructure. Unlike the earlier VMM prototype in #49517, the direct-publication domain does not own the KV allocation. #52863 remains unchanged; this draft proposes the integration path for the new allocator, not two independently selectable KV allocators.

## Initial supported scope

- Explicit opt-in: `VLLM_USE_PCP_DIRECT_KV=1` with ExtensibleKVCache enabled.
- The tested #56492 allocator snapshot requires a common block stride. GLM-5.2 validation uses the existing `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLNHC` layout; its default layer-outermost layout has different MLA/Indexer strides and is rejected by the prerequisite.
- Initial graph scope is `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` (or eager execution). The main-branch sparse-PCP graph guard remains for other graph modes and for the ordinary collective path.
- Single-host CUDA, replicated PCP greater than one, DCP1, identical peer cache layouts. Peer handles are transferred using POSIX FD passing, not integer handle values in an object collective.
- Existing DeepSeekV3.2-family direct writers: BF16, FP8 and `fp8_ds_mla` MLA cache; FP8 Indexer cache. NVFP4 model weights are distinct from the unsupported NVFP4 KV-cache format.
- No PP, microbatch overlap, speculative decoding, PD transfer, HiSparse or sleep-mode support in this first version.
- An unsupported requested configuration or mismatched peer layout/growth fails explicitly; it does not silently use the collective KV-update path.

This does not owner-shard historical KV, increase KV capacity through sharding, change paged attention consumption, or remove hidden-state/output collectives.

## Test Plan

Focused commands below use the qualified Torch 2.13/cu130 environment as `.venv`; run from the repository root with `PYTHONPATH="$PWD"`:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_pcp_vmm_direct.py --confcutdir=tests/distributed -xq --tb=short
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py tests/v1/worker/test_pcp_direct_final_config.py --confcutdir=tests/v1/worker -xq --tb=short
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/utils_/test_extensible_tensor.py tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py --confcutdir=tests/utils_ -xq --tb=short
```

The engine smoke checks full-graph replay counters, advancing publication epochs, stable owner/peer-table addresses, and generated-token parity against the same-engine collective eager oracle. Detailed settings and results follow. These are recorded results for `c33c40aafd`, not a rerun against newer main or the newer #56492 head.

## Test Results

Local four-GB200 component tests passed PCP4 and TP2PCP2. The actual fused peer writer matched the native local writer for BF16, FP8 and `fp8_ds_mla`, including CUDA Graph replay across growth and physical-page recommit, invalid slots, and stable owner/peer/pointer-table addresses. This is component correctness evidence, not engine validation.

The combined PCP-manager/configuration suite passed 87 tests, including rejected unsupported configurations, persistent rank-local slot mapping addresses, and the restricted sparse-PCP graph enablement.

The existing ExtensibleTensor/ExtensibleKVCache regression suites passed all 16 tests. Together with the two four-GPU component cases, this is 105 focused tests passed. The component rerun also verifies coordinated rejection of mismatched peer layouts and growth plans. Ruff and `git diff --check` passed.

Full GLM-5.2-NVFP4 engine validation passed on four GB200 with Torch 2.13/cu130 and MRV2. Settings: TP1/PCP4/EP4/DCP1; FP8 KV; BLNHC; FlashInfer sparse MLA with FLASH_ATTN prefill; FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE; FULL_DECODE_ONLY with capture sizes 1/2/4; compilation mode NONE; prefix caching disabled; 64 KV blocks; maximum model length 128; maximum batched tokens 64; maximum sequences 4. This is a bounded correctness smoke, not a long-context benchmark.

The smoke generated four greedy tokens from a 64-token prompt at batch sizes 1, 2, 4, and 1. Instrumentation confirmed actual full-graph replay and stable owner/peer-pointer-table addresses. Generated tokens matched a same-engine native collective eager oracle. The oracle switch is test-only; the production opt-in never silently falls back. Engine startup captured graphs before final physical KV growth and rebinding. No serving-speedup claim is made.

## Attribution

Developed with AI assistance. Human review is required before merging.

Co-authored with [@taoyuanyuan](https://github.com/taoyuanyuan)

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Derive SWA token validity inside the index kernels
body:
## Purpose

`DeepseekSparseSWAMetadataBuilder.build` runs once per KV-cache group, per step.
Before the SWA index kernel it issued three eager ops whose only consumer is
that kernel:

1. `slot_mapping >= 0` — an elementwise compare producing a temporary bool tensor.
2. `is_valid_token.copy_(...)` — a copy of that temporary into the persistent buffer.
3. `decode_swa_lens[num_decode_tokens:] = 0` — a fill of the lens tail.

On DeepSeek-V4.1 with 3 KV-cache groups that is 12 launches per step where 3
would do, and on a bs=1 speculative-decode step the host is the critical path:
a torch-profiler trace of that path shows the builder loop occupying ~2.7 ms of
wall time per round while producing ~51 us of GPU work.

## Performance

Microbenchmark of the build path, 3 KV-cache groups, GB200, `window=128`,
`block_size=64`, `context=4096`, median of 3 runs. CPU is host submit time with
no sync; GPU is CUPTI with a CUDA graph (without one the per-iteration span is
dominated by the launch gaps this PR removes and merely restates the CPU
column).

| batch size | launches/step | CPU submit (us) | GPU (us) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 12 → 3 | 326.7 → 133.9 (2.44x) | 19.3 → 6.7 (2.88x) |
| 32 | 12 → 3 | 319.1 → 124.9 (2.55x) | 21.6 → 8.6 (2.51x) |
| 128 | 12 → 3 | 312.4 → 121.5 (2.57x) | 21.9 → 8.4 (2.61x) |
| 256 | 12 → 3 | 284.5 → 126.2 (2.25x) | 18.7 → 8.8 (2.13x) |

The saving is flat in batch size because what is removed is per-group launch
and dispatch overhead, not per-token work. That is exactly the regime that
hurts: at bs=1 the decode step is host-bound.

## Tests

New `test_decode_validity_and_lens_are_derived_per_group[1/32/128/256]`: three
groups that invalidate different slots, driven through a full batch, a shrunk
batch and a grown batch, with `seq_lens` and the invalid positions changed at
every step so stale contents of the persistent buffers would be detected. It
asserts validity, lens and the gathered index rows against the reference.
`run_swa_kernel` now passes an uninitialised validity buffer and asserts the
kernel fills it, so the existing kernel tests cover the new path too.

```
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py
```


## Not a duplicate

This supersedes the earlier revision of this same PR rather than opening a new
one. #54790 (CUDA) and #52628 (ROCm) opt sparse-MLA backends into the fused
*multi-step draft* framework, which removes rebuilds *between* autoregressive
draft steps; the launches removed here are *within* one step, one per KV-cache
group, and neither PR touches these kernels. #39936 batches
`MultiGroupBlockTable` commit and slot-mapping work, a different call site.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the trace analysis, the consumer audit
and drafting this change.

title: Qualify GLM native LoRA replacement and sparse MLA on v0.28
body:
Native LoRA replacement with max_loras=1 needs independent BF16 receiver buffers and a retained prior generation until fleet activation succeeds. This change stages rank-local factors, atomically activates the new adapter, and preserves rollback/retry and unload behavior while bounding retained generations.

The same release composition carries the GLM sparse-MLA LoRA and R3 route-capture corrections needed for trainer/inference numerics. It is based on the exact v0.28.0 release (2cf0a6915ce544dc493a0990f2ea38d81601128a); #53240 is merged on main but absent from this release base, so its route-capture correction is explicitly backported here. No C++/Rust/native-extension sources change.

Public diagnostics expose receiver-owned active and retained tensor buffers so qualification can verify dtype, storage identity, generation, memory bounds and unload without private manager access. The exact qualification commit is e555066a7bcdf04baad07c7242eceecb4c3f85b8, paired with Bridge 66143846e7e21152706e97078a9b96d0285fa243.

Validation: affected CPU LoRA tests passed; final local-manager suite passed 57 tests with 1 skip, including independent BF16 storage and retained-generation retirement. Source review accepted the composition. Live Qwen/GLM/Tau qualification remains pending; this draft makes no GPU correctness or performance admission claim.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Support FP8 KV cache for NoPE sparse MLA
body:
## Summary

- route rope-free sparse MLA to the ROCm Triton implementation for every KV-cache dtype
- dequantize FP8 KV rows in the Triton ragged-prefill kernel using the layer KV scale while keeping Q in model dtype
- use 64-bit query-row offsets so wide, long-context prefills cannot overflow 32-bit pointer arithmetic
- preserve custom MLA geometry and FP8 cache dtype in the attention benchmark harness

## Problem

AITER precompiled sparse MLA kernels assume the DeepSeek cache-row geometry: 512 latent elements plus 64 RoPE elements. GLM-5.3-Flash is rope-free and stores a 512-element row. FP8 NoPE requests currently reach the AITER path, whose 576-element assumption can read past the cache row and cause a ROCm GPU memory fault.

The existing Triton ragged path already handles the NoPE geometry. This change makes its routing geometry-based instead of BF16-only, adds scaled FP8 KV dequantization, and avoids FP8-quantizing Q for that path.

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR found addresses ROCm NoPE FP8 sparse-attention KV rows. #39168 overlaps the ROCm ops file but changes the separate FP8 indexer-cache MQA path; the open GLM-5.3 NoPE FP8 PRs target NVIDIA backends. The previously bundled SharedTopkIndicesBuffer no-op was dropped because #57252 already landed ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl.record_logical_topk_ready().

## Validation

Rebased onto main@63d9ad0a. Head: ae5cad3d.

Hardware validation used a full ROCm wheel from the previous head (73860da5) on the GLM-5.3-specific ROCm base image. The rebase kept the same kernel/backend/benchmark hunks and only resolved a header-constant conflict with the new upstream FP8_DTYPE plus dropped the now-redundant top-k no-op.

- pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_glm5next_sparse.py: **23 passed** on the pre-rebase validated image
- FP8 sparse MLA attention sweep: **24/24 shapes passed**
- TP=4 GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 serving matrix: **20/20 points passed, 1,360/1,360 requests succeeded**
- post-rebase: ruff check and ruff format --check pass on all 5 changed files; git diff --check clean; files py_compile clean

The serving matrix used `--max-num-batched-tokens 131072 --no-enable-chunked-prefill` so each long prompt exercises the full-query FP8 MLA path. During diagnosis, default partial chunking on current main showed a separate GPU fault only after all instrumented sparse indexer and attention calls had synchronized and returned; it reproduced across both generic-nightly and GLM-specific runtime bases and is outside this FP8 MLA kernel change.

## GSM8K

Same recipe as other GLM-5.3-Flash PRs (#57590, #56960, #56176, #55738, #54925): EleutherAI `lm_eval` against `/v1/completions`, 5-shot, greedy. Not chat completions.

```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve .../GLM-5.3-Flash \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
    --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE --max-num-seqs 64

lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=glm53,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:9610/v1/completions,tokenizer=.../GLM-5.3-Flash,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 --gen_kwargs temperature=0 --seed 12345
```

`gen_kwargs`: `until=['Question:', '</s>', '<|im_end|>']`, `do_sample=False`, `temperature=0` (lm_eval gsm8k.yaml defaults). Full 1,319 questions. No GPU faults.

| Filter | n-shot | Metric | Value | Stderr |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| flexible-extract | 5 | exact_match | **0.9158** | ± 0.0076 |
| strict-match | 5 | exact_match | **0.9158** | ± 0.0076 |

That matches the published GLM-5.3-Flash `lm_eval` completions band: #54925 0.9158 / 0.9143 (model card 0.9128), #56176 0.9121 BF16 / 0.9219 MXFP4, #57546 0.9174 / 0.9166, #56960 0.9249 / 0.9234, #55738 93.03% ± 0.70.

## Serving performance (BF16 KV vs FP8 KV)

`vllm bench serve` random dataset, same recipe as ROCm GLM-5.3-Flash PRs #57590 / #57979 (and NVIDIA #55736): `--backend vllm --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8000 --random-output-len 1000 --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos --seed 5678 --num-prompts $((8*CONC)) --num-warmups $CONC`. Each point was run 3 times; the table shows the median of the 3 runs' median TPOT, output tok/s and median TTFT.

Head 291fe72f80, with this PR's Python tree overlaid on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-81198e97` (main including #58584). Both arms use this build, so FP8 and BF16 decode both go through the split-K kernel. Baseline is **BF16 KV** (main cannot boot FP8 NoPE). TP=4 on MI355X, `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching`. 24/24 runs, 2,736/2,736 requests succeeded.

| ISL/OSL | conc | BF16 TPOT ms | FP8 TPOT ms | TPOT Δ | BF16 tok/s | FP8 tok/s | tok/s Δ | BF16 TTFT ms | FP8 TTFT ms | TTFT Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8000/1000 | 1 | 8.75 | 8.76 | +0.2% | 111.0 | 110.9 | -0.1% | 262 | 261 | -0.5% |
| 8000/1000 | 8 | 11.36 | 11.33 | -0.3% | 639.2 | 640.4 | +0.2% | 1159 | 1160 | +0.1% |
| 8000/1000 | 16 | 15.78 | 15.74 | -0.2% | 919.8 | 918.9 | -0.1% | 1632 | 1831 | +12.2% |
| 8000/1000 | 32 | 20.41 | 20.35 | -0.3% | 1444.7 | 1446.8 | +0.1% | 1849 | 1860 | +0.6% |

FP8 TPOT and throughput are within 0.3% of BF16 at every concurrency. The c=16 TTFT delta comes from queueing, not from the kernel: the 16 concurrent 8k prompts fill the 16k-token prefill budget about two at a time, so the median request lands on one of two prefill waves. Both arms hit both values across identical repeats (BF16 1628 / 1821 / 1628 ms, FP8 1599 / 1831 / 1831 ms).

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, test, rebase, and prepare this change.

title: [Model] Add Xing4_0 support
body:
## Summary

This PR adds native vLLM support for the upcoming **Xing4_0** MoE causal model.

Xing4_0 reuses the DeepSeek-V2/V3 backbone (MLA attention, MoE block, optional DSA indexer) and replaces the standard residual connection with **Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC)**: the residual stream is expanded into `num_residual_streams` parallel streams mixed by input-dependent, doubly-stochastic matrices produced via Sinkhorn-Knopp projection. The mHC math matches the shared ops in `vllm.model_executor.layers.mhc`, so no private kernels are introduced.
Additionally, this PR enables optional FlagOS/FlagGems acceleration for Xing4_0: it enables the hot-path kernels (MoE, attention, softmax, topk, etc.) and brings measurable end-to-end inference speedups — up to 19.87% TTFT and 26.32% TPOT reduction on high-concurrency long-prompt workloads (H100 benchmark), opt-in and disabled by default.

## Changes

1. `vllm/model_executor/models/xing4_0.py`: full model implementation (`Xing4_0ForCausalLM`), including forward pass, mHC adapter, and tensor-parallel `load_weights()`.
2. Register `Xing4_0ForCausalLM` in `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py` and related `__init__.py`.
3. Reasoning parser (`vllm/reasoning/xing4_0_reasoning_parser.py`) for reasoning-capable variants.
4. Tool parser (`vllm/tool_parsers/xing4_0_tool_parser.py`) for auto tool calling.
5. Register `xing4_0` in `vllm/config/speculative.py`, `vllm/transformers_utils/model_arch_config_convertor.py`, and `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py`.

## Optional FlagGems acceleration (opt-in)

An optional acceleration path is gated behind the env var `USE_FLAGOS=1` (disabled by default). When set, it enables a curated subset of FlagGems kernels via `flag_gems.only_enable(include=[...])`.

> **Scope note:** The acceleration is only enabled from the Xing4_0 model path — the flag_gems.only_enable(...) call lives exclusively inside xing4_0.py and is gated behind the env var, so no other model load path triggers it. The whitelist is intentionally narrow (...), and with the env var unset the behavior is fully unchanged. 
 For completeness: only_enable substitutes operators at the PyTorch dispatch level, so once enabled the kernels apply to any op in the same process that matches the whitelist — we therefore consider this an acceleration prototype and welcome feedback on a more scoped kernel backend.

```bash
pip install flagtree==0.6.1 flag-gems==5.3.4 -i https://resource.flagos.net/repository/flagos-pypi-nvidia/simple            # see version constraints in the PR discussion
USE_FLAGOS=1 vllm serve ${model_path} \
    --chat-template ${model_path}/chat_template.jinja \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name $mode_name \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dtype bfloat16 \
    --nnodes 1 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --max-model-len 262144 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --reasoning-parser xing4_0 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser xing4_0 \
    --uvicorn-log-level info \
    --enable-log-requests \
    --disable-custom-all-reduce
```

All Xing4_0 hot-path tests below run with FlagGems **disabled**.

## Benchmark method (H100 × 1)

- Framework: this branch vs. vanilla vLLM baseline (same branch, env var unset).
- Metric: **TTFT** (time to first token) and **TPOT** (time per output token).
- Workload: cold cache for each (input tokens + output tokens) pair.
- Each run: 5 repetitions, report the **median**; standard deviation in parentheses when ≥ 1%.
- No kernel warmup excluded; results reflect end-to-end served latency.

| input+output | concurrency | vanilla TTFT (ms) | flaggems TTFT (ms) | TTFT Δ | vanilla TPOT (ms) | flaggems TPOT (ms) | TPOT Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50K+500 | 1 | 3965 | 3971 | ~0% | 10 | 10 | ~0% |
| 50K+500 | 10 | 23827 | 23050 | 3.26% | 60 | 62 | ~0% |
| 10K+500 | 1 | 486 | 483 | 0.62% | 8 | 8 | ~0% |
| 10K+500 | 10 | 1439 | 1153 | 19.87% | 38 | 28 | 26.32% |
| 1K+500 | 1 | 98 | 98 | ~0% | 8 | 7 | 12.50% |
| 1K+500 | 10 | 185 | 189 | ~0% | 17 | 17 | ~0% |

**Reading:** gains concentrate in the high-concurrency long-prompt case (10K+500, concurrency=10): ~19.87% TTFT / ~26.32% TPOT. Low-concurrency and short-prompt cases are neutral. The benefit is workload-specific, not universal.

## Test plan (internal non-public checkpoint)

1. Single-GPU: init, weight loading, text generation.
2. Tensor-parallel size=2: weight loading and inference.
3. Generation outputs and logits aligned with the Hugging Face transformers reference implementation (layer-wise comparison, reported in the accompanying notes).
4. FlagGems dual-path: default path (env unset) and accelerated path (env set) both produce consistent outputs/logits.

## Usage
```bash
vllm serve ${model_path} \
    --chat-template ${model_path}/chat_template.jinja \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name $mode_name \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dtype bfloat16 \
    --nnodes 1 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --max-model-len 262144 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --reasoning-parser xing4_0 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser xing4_0 \
    --uvicorn-log-level info \
    --enable-log-requests \
    --disable-custom-all-reduce
```

## Known limitations / open items for review

- **mHC checkpoint biases** (`bias_pre` / `bias_post` / `bias_res`) and the `h_res` clamp: currently merged/omitted to match the shared `MHCPreOp` signature. **Please review whether the folded formula is equivalent to the official checkpoint** — this is the main correctness item I need confirmed.
- `_xing4_0_transpose_contiguous` custom op exists to keep `comb_mix` C-contiguous for the TileLang `mhc_post` kernel that torch.compile cannot prove. Happy to simplify if reviewers prefer.
- Pipeline parallelism is not supported in mHC mode (n_streams > 1); tensor parallelism is.

## Checklist

- [x] Model registers and loads (single + TP=2)
- [x] Logit alignment vs HF reference (documented)
- [x] Test entry in `tests/models/registry.py` (pending weights release)
- [x] Docs entry in `docs/models/supported_models.md` (pending weights release)
- [ ] CI green

title: [Feature]: SM8x (Ampere A100/A800) support for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash landed with #56214 / #56228, and the tracking issue #56400
lists it as verified on **H200, GB200, GB300, MI350X**. There is no Ampere
(sm_80) path, and — unlike sm_120, which has field reports in #56700, #56837 and
#56892 — nobody appears to be working on one: searching issues and PRs for
`V4.1` combined with `ampere` / `A100` / `sm80` / `A800` returns only #50576,
which is the **V4** (not 4.1) Ampere tracking issue I opened in July.

This issue tracks getting `DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` running on 8×A100/A800
(sm_80), and offers to do the work. I previously ported DeepSeek-V4-Flash and
V4-Flash-0731 (DSpark) to this same box and reported the result in #50576.

A800 is still the most widely deployed 80 GB datacenter GPU in China, and
V4.1-Flash's 510 GB of weights fit on a single 8×80 GB node, so there is real
demand for this.

### Environment

```
8× NVIDIA A800 80GB PCIe (sm_80), driver 580.159.04, CUDA 13.0
vLLM main @ 9ca6dbba71
Model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
  (bf16 + fp8 weight_block_size [32,32] scale_fmt=ue8m0, expert_dtype=fp4)
```

### What I measured first: DeepSeek's own reference kernels on sm_80

Before proposing anything I ran the reference TileLang kernels shipped in the
checkpoint (`inference/kernel.py`) directly on an A800. That file sets
`TL_DISABLE_WARP_SPECIALIZED` and `TL_DISABLE_TMA_LOWER`, so much of it is
already free of Hopper-only machinery, and the results split cleanly:

| reference kernel | sm_80 | detail |
|---|---|---|
| `sparse_attn` (BF16 gather + online softmax + attn sink) | **works** | compiles and matches a torch reference, max rel err 2.9e-3 (bf16-level) at h=64, d=512, topk=512 |
| `act_quant` (bf16 → fp8 e4m3 + fp32 scales) | **works** | conversion only, no MMA |
| `fp4_act_quant` (bf16 → fp4 + e8m0 scales) | **works** | conversion only, no MMA |
| `fp8_gemm` | **fails** | TileLang lowers `T.gemm` on fp8 operands to CUTLASS `SM89_16x8x32_F32E4M3E4M3F32_TN`; device assert `CUTE_ARCH_MMA_F32_SM89_ENABLED` |
| `fp4_gemm` | **fails** | same wall |

The useful conclusion: the *sparse-MLA attention math itself is portable to
Ampere* — what is not portable is narrow-precision **MMA**, because sm_80 has no
FP8/FP4 tensor-core instruction. That is a much smaller problem than it looks,
since vLLM already routes narrow-precision GEMM on older arches through Marlin
and dequant-to-BF16 paths.

Notably `act_quant` working is significant on its own: Triton on sm_80 cannot
represent `fp8e4nv` at all, which is what blocks the fp8 KV-cache write kernels
today (#48374). TileLang *can* do the conversion on sm_80, so the fp8 KV cache
has a viable route that does not need hand-rolled bit manipulation.

### Why it does not run today — the blocker chain

**1. No sparse-MLA attention backend admits sm_80.**

- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/sparse_mla.py:125` — `supports_compute_capability`
  returns `capability.major in [9, 10]`
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py:133` —
  `capability.major in [10, 12]`

`_select_dsv4_attn_cls` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py:148,152`)
falls through to `DeepseekV4FlashMLAAttention` for every non-sm_12 CUDA device,
and FlashMLA's sparse kernels are SM90a/SM100f only.

**2. The plain SWA path is also FlashMLA-bound.**
`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_swa.py:34` imports `FlashMLASchedMeta,
get_mla_metadata` from `vllm.v1.attention.ops.flashmla` for the tile-scheduler
plan. Every V4.1 layer has a sliding window (`sliding_window: 128`), so this is
not an optional path.

**3. The indexer requires DeepGEMM, which has no sm_80 support.**
`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py` gates its fast paths on
`has_deep_gemm()`, and the V4.1 `DeepseekV41SparseIndexerBackend`
(`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_indexer.py:117-124`) hard-requires an
SM100-class GPU plus DeepGEMM ≥ 2.8. `dsa_indexer_uses_fp4` (`indexer.py:67`)
restricts the mxfp4 indexer cache to sm_10x.

**4. FP8 KV cache is mandatory and the Triton write path cannot express it on
sm_80.** Same wall as V4 (#50576 / #48374): `common/ops/cache_utils.py`,
`common/ops/fused_compress_quant_cache.py` and `common/ops/indexer_k_store.py`
all go through Triton fp8 conversions that sm_80's Triton backend rejects. As
noted above, TileLang gives a way out here.

**5. New in 4.1 — MXFP8 dense linears.** V4 used fp8 blocks of `[128,128]`; the
V4.1 checkpoint uses `weight_block_size: [32,32]` with `scale_fmt: ue8m0`, which
`DeepseekV4FP8Config.get_quant_method` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/quant_config.py`)
routes to `ModelOptLinearMethod` with `kMxfp8Static` / `kMxfp8Dynamic`.
`EmulationMxfp8LinearKernel` is arch-agnostic and dequantizes to BF16 at load,
so a working (if suboptimal) fallback exists — but it has to actually be
reached, and `MarlinMxfp8LinearKernel`, which sits ahead of it in
`_POSSIBLE_MXFP8_KERNELS[CUDA]`, needs an sm_80 verdict.

**6. New in 4.1 — Engram.** Two n-gram tables of 384 M rows × 256 (E4M3 with
E8M0 scales), **203 GB** of the checkpoint. The hashing kernels in
`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py` are plain-integer Triton and look
arch-neutral; the embedding gather is FP8 and inherits (4).

**7. New in 4.1 — vision tower + DeepSelect candidate pre-filter.** The ViT in
`nvidia/vl_model.py` has no arch-specific ops and should port directly; the
candidate-block pre-filter (`candidate_topk_blocks: 2048`,
`candidate_block_size: 8`) rides on the indexer and inherits its gate.

**8. Already fine.** Mega-mHC is gated to sm_100 with a TileLang fallback
(`nvidia/ops/mega_mhc.py:22-31`) — the path our V4 Ampere port already
exercises. MXFP4 experts have `MARLIN` / `EMULATION` backends on CUDA.

### Memory budget on 8×80 GB (measured from the checkpoint)

| component | size | per rank (TP8 + EP) |
|---|---|---|
| MoE experts (fp4) | 296 GB | 37 GB |
| Engram tables | 203 GB | 25.4 GB sharded |
| backbone / embed / head / vision / mtp | ~11 GB | ~1.5 GB |
| **total** | **510 GB** | **≈64 GB** |

That leaves roughly 15 GB/rank for KV cache, activations and graphs — tight but
workable, and the engram tables have host-offload work already in flight
(#56757 disk-backed, #57023 Mooncake, #56357 mmap/prefetch) on a box with 692 GB
of RAM.

### Proposed plan

Mirroring the `nvidia/` and `amd/` split already in `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/`:

1. An Ampere sparse-MLA + SWA attention path that does not go through FlashMLA's
   tile scheduler, built on the reference `sparse_attn` shape that already runs.
2. TileLang-based fp8 E4M3 conversion for the KV cache, indexer K store and the
   engram gather, replacing the Triton fp8 path that sm_80 rejects.
3. A DeepGEMM-free indexer path.
4. Narrow-precision GEMM routed to Marlin / BF16-dequant rather than the
   reference fp8/fp4 GEMMs, which need sm_89+ MMA.
5. Engram sharding/offload sized for 80 GB ranks.

I have the box, the model and the prior V4 port to work from, and I am happy to
carry this as a PR series.

Two questions for maintainers before I go further:

- Is there any in-flight Ampere work on V4.1 I have missed?
- Would you prefer an `ampere/` subpackage under `models/deepseek_v41/`, or
  platform-generic kernels plus a thin model shim (the shape #56120 / #47629
  took for V4)?

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Model] Add ZEDA-GLM-4.7-Flash-Dynamic (Glm4MoeLitePlusPlus) support
body:
## Purpose
Adds support for **ZEDA-GLM-4.7-Flash-Dynamic** (`Glm4MoeLitePlusPlusForCausalLM`), a dynamic MoE variant of GLM-4.7-Flash that introduces **Zero-Compute Experts (ZCE)**: the router gate emits logits for all experts (n_routed_experts + sum(zce_nums) = 64 + 32 = 96), but zero-compute expert slots are not executed as FFNs — they are remapped to expert 0 with weight 0 at the fused-MoE kernel level, avoiding a per-expert Python loop and keeping the whole path graph-compilable.

The vLLM side only makes vLLM **recognize** the model and **recreate the 96-dim gate**; the actual "skip" of zero-compute experts is handled by the companion vllm-ascend patch.

- The model uses sigmoid + `e_score_correction_bias` + group topk routing, so the gate **must** output 96 logits for topk selection to "see" the zero-compute slots. Keeping the inherited 64-dim gate makes ZCE routing silently inactive.
- The model uses DeepSeek-style **MLA**, so it must be added to the `is_deepseek_mla()` whitelist, otherwise it falls back to plain MHA and errors with `rotary 102 != 64`.
- Config is registered in `_CONFIG_REGISTRY` so the checkpoint loads **without `trust_remote_code`** (no need for a forked transformers).

New files:
- `vllm/model_executor/models/glm4_moe_lite_plus_plus.py` — thin override of `Glm4MoeLite`:
  - `Glm4MoeLitePlusPlusDecoderLayer`: after the parent builds the standard MoE layer, recreates `mlp.gate` as a `total_num_experts`-dim `nn.Linear`, creates a matching `e_score_correction_bias` Parameter, and sets `routed_experts.zero_expert_num` / `zero_expert_type` for the downstream fused-MoE kernel. Dense layers (non-MoE) are left untouched via an `isinstance` guard.
  - `Glm4MoeLitePlusPlusModel`: re-implements `__init__` only to swap in the `++` decoder layer; decorated with `@support_torch_compile` so it is capturable by `torch.compile` + cudagraph (`FULL_DECODE_ONLY`), unlike the eager fallback.
  - `Glm4MoeLitePlusPlusForCausalLM`: wires up the `++` model and replicates MoE/MLA weight-loading setup (`packed_modules_mapping`, `fuse_qkv_a_proj`, `set_moe_parameters()`).
- `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/glm4_moe_lite_plus_plus.py` — `Glm4MoeLitePlusPlusConfig(PretrainedConfig)` exposing `zce_nums` / `zce_types` / `use_zce_mask` and `total_num_experts`/`total_zce` properties.

Modified files (registration plumbing):
- `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py` — map `Glm4MoeLitePlusPlusForCausalLM` → `glm4_moe_lite_plus_plus` module.
- `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py` — `model_type` `glm4_moe_lite_plus_plus` → `Glm4MoeLitePlusPlusConfig` in `_CONFIG_REGISTRY`.
- `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/__init__.py` — lazy module path in `_CLASS_TO_MODULE` + `__all__`.
- `vllm/transformers_utils/model_arch_config_convertor.py` — add `glm4_moe_lite_plus_plus` to the `is_deepseek_mla()` whitelist (MLA attention path).

The override reuses the parent's weight loading / forward / MLA attention; no eager dispatch and no new trainable parameters (the bias is already part of the checkpoint's expert-parameter set). Design follows vllm-ascend PR #14905 (Qwen3 MoE++).
## Test Plan
- [x] `python -c "from vllm.model_executor.models.glm4_moe_lite_plus_plus import Glm4MoeLitePlusPlusForCausalLM; print('model OK')"`
- [x] `python -c "from vllm.model_executor.models.registry import ModelRegistry; print('registered:', 'Glm4MoeLitePlusPlusForCausalLM' in ModelRegistry.get_supported_archs())"`
- [x] Config loads without weights / without `trust_remote_code`:
  ```python
  from vllm.transformers_utils.config import get_config
  c = get_config('/path/to/ZEDA-GLM-4.7-Flash-Dynamic', trust_remote_code=False)
  print(type(c).__name__, c.model_type, 'total_num_experts=', c.total_num_experts)
  # expect: Glm4MoeLitePlusPlusConfig glm4_moe_lite_plus_plus total_num_experts= 96
  ```
- [x] Eager + graph (FULL_DECODE_ONLY) inference on Ascend with the companion vllm-ascend patch; numerical parity checked against a transformers 4.57 fork golden trace.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4.1 produces NaN with CUDA graphs on SM120/121 — dummy capture batches poison the null KV block
body:
## Your current environment

```
vLLM            main @ b443c1c (built from source)
FlashInfer      0.6.18.post1
PyTorch         2.13 + CUDA 13.0
GPU             8x NVIDIA GB10 (sm_121), 121.6 GiB unified memory each
OS              Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64
Model           DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8 + EP8
Backend         FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41
KV cache        fp8_ds_mla, indexer MXFP4, block size 64 (SWA cache 32)
```

## Describe the bug

With CUDA graphs enabled, `DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` returns empty or garbled completions.
`--enforce-eager` is correct. All graph modes fail identically: `FULL`, `PIECEWISE`, and
`FULL_DECODE_ONLY`.

Eager, correct:

```
prompt: "The capital of France is"   ->  " Paris."
```

PIECEWISE, same build and weights:

```
prompt: "The capital of France is"   ->  ""
```

## Root cause

**Every attention output row is NaN from the first decoder layer onward, while its inputs are
finite.** A replay-time probe on the breakable-CUDA-graph segments shows layer 0 receiving
finite `hidden_states`, `q` and `kv`, then writing NaN into the real-token rows of its output
buffer.

The NaN comes from the KV cache, specifically block 0.

`sparse_mla_sm120/decode_dsv4_kernel.cuh` deliberately gathers slot 0 for invalid indices and
relies on softmax masking to discard it. The scale load is guarded:

```cpp
// line 272
if (idx_raw >= 0) {
  ...
  scale_word = __ldg(...);
}
```

but the NoPE/RoPE data load is not — it clamps instead:

```cpp
// line 299
const int idx = (idx_raw >= 0) ? idx_raw : 0;
const int block_idx_g = idx / section_pbs;
```

The intent is documented at line 431:

> Invalid = position past section_len OR slot id = -1 (indexer-padded; IO already gathered
> slot 0 into smem with idx clamped — masking to -inf kills it in softmax).

Masking sets the logit to `-1e30`, so softmax yields `p ≈ 0`. But the PV accumulation still
computes `p * v`, and in IEEE arithmetic `0 * NaN = NaN`. In MLA the NoPE tensor serves as both
K and V, so non-finite data in slot 0 propagates into `acc_nope` regardless of the mask.

**The kernel therefore has an undocumented precondition: block 0 must hold finite data.**

Measured contents of block 0, same build, immediately before the first real request:

| Mode | slot 0 NoPE | slot 0 RoPE | scales |
|---|---|---|---|
| eager | 0.0 | 0.0 | all zero |
| PIECEWISE | **NaN** | **~3.2e35** | all zero |

CUDA graph capture is what pollutes it. Dummy capture batches carry an all-zero block table,
so writes land in block 0 while the graph is being recorded.

## Reproduction of the causal step

Rather than argue from correlation, I copied the cache and re-ran the same kernel with the same
inputs, changing only block 0:

| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| E: block 0 as-is | output rows 0-4 NaN |
| F: block 0 zeroed | output finite and correct |

Cloning every input tensor (`q`, `sparse_indices`, `swa_topk_lens`, `sinks`, `out`,
`workspace_buffer`) and re-running reproduced the NaN, which rules out the inputs.

Also ruled out, each tested individually: stream mismatch (`torch.cuda.synchronize()` and
`tvm_ffi.use_torch_stream()` both made no difference), the autotuner's `chunks_per_block`
tactic (tested -1, 1, 2, 3, 8), page-block-size handling, and widening the eager region
(`VLLM_V41_WIDE_EAGER=1`).

## Workaround

Zeroing block 0 before each kernel call fixes it completely. Block 0 is vLLM's reserved
`null_block` (`vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py`, popped at init and never handed to a request), so
this is safe:

```python
for key in ("swa_kv_cache", "compressed_kv_cache"):
    cache = kw.get(key)
    if cache is not None:
        cache[0].zero_()
```

Cost is about 18 KB of writes per layer. Single-stream throughput went from 17.2 tok/s
(`--enforce-eager`) to 32.6 tok/s with graphs enabled, and all outputs are correct.

## Open question for maintainers

I verified that block 0 holds non-finite data after capture and that zeroing it fixes the
output, but I did not trace which write produces it. `get_dummy_slot_mappings` fills with
`PAD_SLOT_ID`, and the fused SWA insert kernel does skip `slot_id < 0`, so the polluting write
is somewhere else — possibly an indexer or compressor cache insert that does not guard negative
slots. A maintainer who knows those paths could pin it down quickly.

## Suggested fix

Three options, in what I think is decreasing order of merit:

1. **Zero the null block once after graph capture completes.** Real requests never touch block 0,
   so this holds for the life of the process and costs nothing per step.
2. **Guard the data load in FlashInfer**, matching what the scale load at line 272 already does.
   Correct at the source, but adds a branch to the hot path.
3. **Prevent dummy batches from writing to block 0** during capture. Cleanest conceptually,
   but requires finding the unguarded write first.

I am happy to open a PR for whichever direction you prefer.

## Related

Not a duplicate of any of these, but they share territory and may help whoever picks this up:

- **#55636** — DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA indexing a nonexistent block-table row during CUDA-graph
  warmup, also on DGX Spark / GB10. Same hardware and model family, and also a
  warmup-metadata problem, but it surfaces as an illegal address or a wrong KV slot in the
  Triton top-k mapper rather than NaN out of the FlashInfer decode kernel. Possibly worth
  checking whether both trace back to the same warmup path.
- **#57094** (fixes #57017) — NaN from CUDA-graph padding in Triton MLA decode. Same family,
  different mechanism: there `seq_len=0` makes stage 2 compute `0/0`; here a clamped index
  reads poisoned data and the PV accumulation computes `0 * NaN`. Both are padding slots
  interacting badly with MLA decode, which suggests the pattern is worth a general look.
- **#57028** — SM120 FlashInfer serving blockers for DSv4.1 (page geometry, multi-stream
  capture fallback). Adjacent to this code path but does not address the null-block NaN;
  I confirmed the NaN reproduces independently of page-geometry handling.

## Additional context

This surfaced while bringing DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash up on 8x DGX Spark. Full write-up, the probe
patches used to localize it, and the benchmark harness are at
https://github.com/sumsliu/dgx-spark-deepseek-v41 — see `docs/findings.md`.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Zero the null KV block after CUDA graph capture
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57156.

CUDA graph capture runs dummy batches whose block table is all zeros, so capture can leave
uninitialized values in block 0 of the KV cache. Attention kernels that deliberately gather
block 0 for masked or padded entries rely on the softmax mask to discard the result. That only
holds while the gathered data is finite: a non-finite value survives masking as `0 * NaN == NaN`
in the value accumulation and poisons every real token in the batch.

Block 0 is the reserved null block (`BlockPool.null_block`, popped at init and never handed to a
request), so restoring it to zeros once after capture holds for the lifetime of the process.

## Root cause

Observed on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with the FlashInfer SM120 sparse-MLA backend. In
`sparse_mla_sm120/decode_dsv4_kernel.cuh`, the scale load guards on the index:

```cpp
// line 272
if (idx_raw >= 0) { scale_word = __ldg(...); }
```

while the NoPE/RoPE data load clamps instead:

```cpp
// line 299
const int idx = (idx_raw >= 0) ? idx_raw : 0;
```

The intent is documented at line 431: *"IO already gathered slot 0 into smem with idx clamped —
masking to -inf kills it in softmax"*. Masking sets the logit to `-1e30` so softmax yields
`p ≈ 0`, but the PV accumulation still computes `p * v`, and in MLA the NoPE tensor is both K
and V. So non-finite data in slot 0 reaches `acc_nope` regardless of the mask.

Measured contents of block 0 immediately before the first real request, same build:

| Mode | slot 0 NoPE | slot 0 RoPE |
|---|---|---|
| eager | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| PIECEWISE | NaN | ~3.2e35 |

Eager never captures, so block 0 stays zeroed and the bug does not appear.

This is not specific to one backend: any kernel that gathers a sentinel block and relies on
masking has the same precondition. #57094 fixes a sibling case in Triton MLA decode where CUDA
graph padding produces `0/0`.

## Test Plan

Verified on 8x DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), TP8 + EP8, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, with the per-call
workaround disabled so this change is the only thing preventing the NaN:

- single stream, 1024-token generation, three prompts
- concurrency 1 / 16 / 64, 1024-token input, 128-token output

## Test Result

All completions correct, no NaN anywhere in the outputs or logs.

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `"The capital of France is"` | `""` | `" Paris."` |
| Single stream | NaN | 69 / 40 / 81 tok/s |
| Concurrency 64 | NaN | 244 tok/s |

Speeds match the per-call workaround, confirming the once-after-capture placement is sufficient
and cheaper. Single-stream throughput with CUDA graphs enabled is 32.6 tok/s against 17.2 tok/s
under `--enforce-eager`.

## Notes

I verified that block 0 holds non-finite data after capture and that zeroing it there fixes the
output, but I did not trace which specific write produces it — `get_dummy_slot_mappings` fills
with `PAD_SLOT_ID` and the fused SWA insert kernel does skip `slot_id < 0`, so the polluting
write is elsewhere. Restoring the invariant after capture is correct regardless, but if a
maintainer would rather fix the write itself I am happy to rework this.


---

## AI assistance disclosure

Per [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/AGENTS.md), this section covers
the required disclosures for AI-assisted contributions.

**AI assistance was used.** The investigation, root-cause analysis and patch were produced with
Claude Code. The submitter reviewed every changed line and reproduced the failure and the fix on
the hardware described below.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched before opening:

```bash
gh api "search/issues?q=repo:vllm-project/vllm+DeepSeekV41+NaN"
gh api "search/issues?q=repo:vllm-project/vllm+null_block+NaN"
gh api "search/issues?q=repo:vllm-project/vllm+flashinfer+sparse+mla+NaN"
```

The closest existing work is #57094, which fixes CUDA-graph padding NaN in **Triton MLA** decode
where stage 2 computes `0/0` for `seq_len=0`. That is a different backend and a different
mechanism; this PR addresses a clamped index reading a poisoned null block, where the value
accumulation computes `0 * NaN`. #55636 is a sibling warmup-metadata bug on the same hardware but
surfaces as an illegal address rather than NaN. #57028 touches the same SM120 path but covers page
geometry, not the null block; the NaN reproduces independently of it.

**Test commands and results.** On 8x DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), TP8 + EP8, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,
CUDA graphs enabled, with no other workaround in place so this change is the only thing preventing
the NaN:

```bash
# correctness
curl -s "$API/v1/completions" -d '{"model":"deepseek-v4.1-flash","prompt":"The capital of France is","max_tokens":4,"temperature":0}'
# before: ""        after: " Paris."

# single stream, 1024-token generation, three prompts
python3 bench.py single --rounds 3

# concurrency sweep, 1024-token input, 128-token output
python3 bench.py batch --concurrency 1,16,64 --in-len 1024 --out-len 128 --seed-offset 42
```

**Model evaluation.** This change affects serving output, so results are included rather than
waiting to be asked:

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `"The capital of France is"` | `""` | `" Paris."` |
| Single stream (3 prompts) | NaN | 69 / 40 / 81 tok/s |
| Concurrency 1 / 16 / 64 | NaN | 65 / 164 / 244 tok/s |
| NaN occurrences in output or logs | every token | 0 |

Long-context retrieval was verified with the earlier per-call variant of this fix (zeroing block 0
before every kernel call), not with this once-after-capture version: a passcode buried at the 60%
mark is retrieved correctly at 131K, 262K, 524K and 1,040,139 input tokens, each with a unique
random prefix so the prefix cache is not hit. The two variants restore the same invariant, but I
have not re-run long context against this exact change.

Style: `pre-commit run --all-files` clean; all added lines are within the 88-character limit.

title: [GLM-5.3-Flash] Rework kpool compress and dual-stream indexer scheduling
body:
## Purpose

Supplements vLLM's `Glm5Next` sparse-MLA kpool indexer with the kpool optimizations

What changes in vLLM:

- `vllm/models/glm5next/{nvidia,amd}/ops/kpool_compress.py`: `_kpool_softmax_rotate_write_cache_kernel` switches from a two-pass to an **online softmax** (each pool's gate scores are read once instead of twice) and takes a (row stride, slot stride, row offset) triple so one kernel serves both the pooled `[n_pools, kpool, D]` layout (`row_offset = 0`) and the **flat token layout** (`row_offset = kpool - 1`: row `i` pools tokens `i - kpool + 1 .. i`, SGLang's "assemble" kernel shape). Rows whose slot is negative, or too early in the batch to own a full pool, return before any load — replacing the `write_mask` mechanism. The prefill and decode kernels share one `_hadamard_quantize_fp8` helper; the decode/verify kernel also uses the online softmax (matching SGLang's verify-side kernel).
- `vllm/models/glm5next/{nvidia,amd}/sparse_indexer.py`: the prefill insert becomes a single launch of the new `kpool_compress_tokens_and_write_cache` on the prefill slice (was: `arange`/`clamp`/`>=`/`&`/index tensors + `k[idx]`/`gate_score[idx]` gathers + int64 conversion = 12 launches per indexer layer per prefill step). On **eager pure-prefill batches** the compress + tail-seed writes now run on the global aux stream, overlapping the current stream's topk-buffer fill and gather/logits preparation, joined before the first KV gather (SGLang's `_can_overlap_prefill`). The overlap is gated off under CUDA graph capture and breakable CUDA graphs.
- `vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py`: new `is_in_breakable_cuda_graph()` (true during breakable capture or replay) so cross-stream code can stay single-streamed under breakable graphs — the vLLM counterpart of SGLang's guard with the same rationale (the BCG eager break must finish its indexer work on one stream).
- `vllm/models/glm5next/common/attention.py` (`Indexer.forward`): the head gate is `torch.mm(hidden, w.t(), out_dtype=torch.float32)` on the bf16 operands on CUDA (fp32 accumulation and output, no `hidden.float()` copy, no cached fp32 weight; the fp32-upcast fallback is kept for other platforms). Under CUDA graph capture the K path (wk GEMM, k_norm, compress-gate GEMM) runs on the aux stream while the current stream projects, Hadamard-rotates and quantizes Q and computes the head gate — the two streams join before the indexer op (SGLang's "rebalance dual-stream indexer preparation"). Eager batches stay sequential (the fork/join would cost host time there).

## Duplicate-work check

`kpool`, `GLM-5.3-Flash indexer` and `glm5next` (2026-09-15) shows no PR touching the compress kernels, the prefill insert path, the head-gate GEMM or the indexer's stream scheduling. Related but different open PRs: #55358 moved `sparse_attn_indexer_kpool.py` into the model folder (a refactor this PR is rebased on top of), #54951 shards long-context indexer prefill rows across TP, #56607 / #56059 are ROCm fixes to the Q quant and the tail-seed kernel, #55270 fixes the paged-MQA varlen launch mode.

## Perf Changes

Kernel-level microbenchmarks (H100, GLM-5.3-Flash shapes: kpool 4, head_dim 128, 32 indexer heads, page 64):

- Prefill compress-write path per indexer layer: 12 launches -> 1. Wall time 154-216 us -> 32-36 us at n = 256 / 2048 / 8192 tokens (-79% .. -84%); summed GPU kernel time 29.0 -> 4.4 us at n = 2048 and 67.9 -> 6.7 us at n = 8192. 
- Online softmax was validated across 44 numerical and boundary cases (pool sizes 4/16). The maximum FP32 difference from the previous two-pass algorithm was 4.77e-7, and the new flat, pooled-prefill, and decode writers produced byte-identical caches. Bitwise equivalence with the previous algorithm is not guaranteed near BF16 rounding boundaries: constructed midpoint cases showed 0.22–0.32% relative L2 differences after dequantization, while both algorithms had approximately 3.16% total quantization error against the ideal reference, with no material additional error observed in these cases.
- `Indexer.forward` GEMM/quant sequence, CUDA-graph replay time: T = 48 tokens 39.7 -> 34.3 us (head gate) -> 22.7 us (head gate + dual stream), -43%; T = 288 (48 sequences x MTP 6) 50.8 -> 30.8 us, -39%; T = 1024: 94.4 -> 54.3 us, -42%; T = 4096 (head gate only; the stream overlap is off above 1024 tokens): 255.4 -> 172.7 us, -32%. Head-gate weights differ by at most 1.3e-9 (fp32 summation order).
- Decode tail-update kernel: unchanged time (launch-bound, ~36.5 us at B = 48, next_n 1 and 6) and byte-identical output.

End-to-end (`vllm bench serve`, GLM-5.3-Flash, `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --max-num-seqs 48 --max-model-len 131072 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'`, breakable CUDA graphs; client `--dataset-name random --ignore-eos --seed 0`; main = 206e45d470, same machine, back-to-back runs):

**8xH100:**

| Config/conc 1 | Metric | main | this PR | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8192 in / 16 out, 32 prompts | mean TTFT | 440.2 ms | 426.3 ms | -3.2% |
| | median TTFT | 432.5 ms | 422.4 ms | -2.3% |
| | p99 TTFT | 513.5 ms | 502.8 ms | -2.1% |
| | mean E2EL | 683.4 ms | 665.5 ms | -2.6% |
| | output throughput | 23.4 tok/s | 24.0 tok/s | +2.7% |
| 2048 in / 256 out, 96 prompts | mean TTFT | 390.8 ms | 384.4 ms | -1.6% |
| | mean ITL | 18.13 ms | 18.05 ms | -0.4% |
| | mean TPOT | 11.55 ms | 11.65 ms | +0.9% |
| | output throughput | 76.8 tok/s | 76.3 tok/s | -0.6% |

**8xB200:**

| Config | Metric | main | this PR | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8192 in / 16 out, 32 prompts, conc 1 | mean TTFT | 173.3 ms | 169.7 ms | -2.1% |
|  | median TTFT | 173.7 ms | 169.6 ms | -2.3% |
|  | p99 TTFT | 181.1 ms | 176.6 ms | -2.5% |
|  | mean E2EL | 241.3 ms | 236.3 ms | -2.1% |
|  | output throughput | 66.3 tok/s | 67.7 tok/s | +2.1% |
| 2048 in / 256 out, 96 prompts, conc 1 | mean TTFT | 129.1 ms | 124.8 ms | -3.4% |
|  | mean ITL | 8.77 ms | 8.63 ms | -1.5% |
|  | mean TPOT | 1.98 ms | 1.94 ms | -1.8% |
|  | output throughput | 403.7 tok/s | 412.5 tok/s | +2.2% |

The prefill-side changes land where they work: TTFT drops 2-3% on prefill-heavy traffic (11 indexer layers x 11 fewer launches, ~60 us less GPU time and one overlapped write phase per layer per prefill chunk). Decode-heavy traffic is neutral within run-to-run noise (the decode-side kernel is launch-bound and unchanged).

Higher-concurrency runs (same servers and flags as the table above):

**8xH100:**
| Config | Metric | main | this PR | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8192 in / 16 out, 128 prompts, conc 16 | mean TTFT | 1321.5 ms | 1359.7 ms | +2.9% |
| | median TTFT | 1210.8 ms | 1220.6 ms | +0.8% |
| | mean E2EL | 4583.6 ms | 4364.1 ms | -4.8% |
| | output throughput | 55.3 tok/s | 58.1 tok/s | +5.1% |
| 2048 in / 256 out, 256 prompts, conc 32 | mean TTFT | 805.6 ms | 801.7 ms | -0.5% |
| | p99 TTFT | 2855.6 ms | 2823.6 ms | -1.1% |
| | mean ITL | 96.98 ms | 99.25 ms | +2.3% |
| | output throughput | 629.8 tok/s | 621.2 tok/s | -1.4% |

**8xB200:**
| Config | Metric | main | this PR | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8192 in / 16 out, 128 prompts, conc 16 | mean TTFT | 1365.0 ms | 1329.1 ms | -2.6% |
|  | median TTFT | 1407.5 ms | 1262.1 ms | -10.3% |
|  | mean E2EL | 2558.9 ms | 2498.7 ms | -2.4% |
|  | output throughput | 98.5 tok/s | 100.7 tok/s | +2.3% |
| 2048 in / 256 out, 256 prompts, conc 32 | mean TTFT | 339.9 ms | 334.7 ms | -1.5% |
|  | p99 TTFT | 1318.4 ms | 1285.8 ms | -2.5% |
|  | mean ITL | 56.86 ms | 57.48 ms | +1.1% |
|  | output throughput | 2163.5 tok/s | 2136.6 tok/s | -1.2% |

At concurrency the prefill-heavy config gains 5.1% output throughput and 4.8% mean E2EL while individual TTFTs (queueing-dominated, chunked into mixed batches) stay within a few percent; the decode-heavy config is neutral within run-to-run noise.

## Tests

- `tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py`: 3 new tests — the flat-token writer equals the pooled writer on explicitly gathered rows across a request boundary that is not pool-aligned inside the batch (kpool 4 and 16), a slot on a row too early to own a full pool is skipped, and a batch shorter than one pool writes nothing. The existing exact-equality tests against the two-pass fp32 CPU reference (incl. 20 fuzz seeds) and the decode-vs-prefill writer equality keep passing with the online-softmax kernels. Whole file: 31 passed, 2 skipped (ROCm-only). `tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py`: pass (50 passed / 2 skipped combined).
- Live server (breakable CUDA graphs: prefill PIECEWISE/FULL + decode FULL graphs captured cleanly with the dual-stream fork/join inside, MTP speculator): greedy sanity (`17 * 23` -> `391` with a correct reasoning trace, identical to main) and the bench runs above.
- GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 300 --max-concurrency 1`, 5-shot, greedy, MTP k=5, same servers): this PR 0.920, main 0.923 on the paired run; across all runs on this machine both sides span 0.920-0.923 (greedy outputs are not bitwise reproducible across runs on this fp8 MoE + EP deployment even on unmodified main), so this is parity, not an accuracy claim. The only numerics that changed are bounded: 9 of 278,784 cache bytes on an 8192-token prefill (fp8 rounding from the online softmax) and <= 1.3e-9 fp32 summation order in the head gate.
- Pre-commit hooks (ruff, ruff-format, mypy, typos, ...) pass on all changed files.

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Size the profile-run chunked-prefill workspace from the active backend's builder
body:
## Purpose

`MLAAttention.chunked_prefill_workspace_size` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py`) unconditionally called `MLACommonMetadataBuilder.determine_chunked_prefill_workspace_size()` — the **dense** MLA sizing, `min(max(8 * max_model_len, 4 * max_num_seqs * block_size), 64K)` rounded up to the block size — regardless of which backend the layer actually runs on.

That value is used only during the profile run (`forward_impl`, `attn_metadata is None` branch) to allocate a worst-case
`torch.empty((workspace_size, num_heads, qk_nope_head_dim + v_head_dim))` that simulates the `kv_b_proj` up-projection performed by `_compute_prefill_context`.

Sparse MLA backends (DeepSeek-V3.2-style DSA: `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE`, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` / `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`) build their metadata with `SparseMLACommonMetadataBuilder` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/sparse_mla_attention.py`), which overrides `determine_chunked_prefill_workspace_size` to cap the workspace at `max_num_seqs * index_topk` rows. Their `_project_kv` can therefore never see more context rows than that cap, yet the profile run reserved the dense worst case — and the KV cache was then sized against that inflated activation peak.

The fix asks the active backend for its own builder: `self.attn_backend.get_builder_cls()`, then `getattr(builder_cls, "determine_chunked_prefill_workspace_size", MLACommonMetadataBuilder.determine_chunked_prefill_workspace_size)`.

Builders defining the classmethod today (`grep -rn determine_chunked_prefill_workspace_size vllm/`):

- `MLACommonMetadataBuilder` (dense MLA: `TRITON_MLA`, `FLASHMLA`, `FLASH_ATTN_MLA`, `CUTLASS_MLA`, `FLASHINFER_MLA`, ROCm/CPU MLA, …) — **unchanged**, same function as before.
- `SparseMLACommonMetadataBuilder` (the sparse backends above) — now actually used by the profile run.
- `XPUMLASparseMetadataBuilder` does not define it, so it keeps the dense sizing via the fallback (no behaviour change).

The change is hardware-agnostic: it is pure Python config arithmetic in the layer, with no kernel or device-specific code.

> Note: this PR was written with AI assistance (Claude Code); the change and all measurements below were reviewed and run by the submitter.

## Test Plan

- New unit tests in `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py` (no GPU required):
  - `test_profile_workspace_follows_sparse_backend_cap` — a stub backend whose `get_builder_cls()` returns a `SparseMLACommonMetadataBuilder` subclass must make the property return the sparse cap.
  - `test_profile_workspace_keeps_dense_sizing` — `MLACommonMetadataBuilder` and a builder class without the classmethod both keep the dense sizing.
  - Run: `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py`
- End-to-end memory measurement on a real sparse-MLA (DSA) serve, comparing profile-run peak activation, available KV cache and GPU KV cache size before/after, plus an accuracy/behaviour check (GSM8K, MTP acceptance rate).
- `pre-commit` (ruff-format, ruff-check, SPDX, forbidden-imports, torch.cuda, boolean-context-manager hooks) on the changed files.

## Test Result

title: [Bugfix][Model] Enable pipeline parallelism for GLM-5.3-Flash (materialize deferred mHC state; load MTP drafter embedding)
body:
## Purpose

Two independent bugs kept GLM-5.3-Flash from running usefully under pipeline parallelism. Both fixes are hardware-agnostic (pure Python model/loader code, no kernels touched).

### 1. Pipeline parallelism was gated off (`vllm/models/glm5next/common/model.py`)

`Glm5NextModel` shipped without `make_empty_intermediate_tensors`, so `supports_pp()` was `False` for `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` and `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1` was rejected. The in-tree comments spelled out why: *"PP is gated off for GLM-5.3-Flash (no make_empty_intermediate_tensors)"*.

The obstacle is mHC (manifold-constrained hyper-connections). Each token carries `config.mhc_num_residual_streams` (4) residual streams, and every decoder layer **defers** its `hc_post` mix into the *next* layer's fused post+pre kernel, returning `(x, residual, post, comb)` (`Glm5NextDecoderLayer.forward`). At a stage boundary there is no next layer to fuse with, so the deferred `post`/`comb` had nowhere to go and were simply dropped.

This PR resolves the deferred state at the boundary rather than propagating it:

* `Glm5NextModel.__init__` now installs `make_empty_intermediate_tensors`. For mHC it is the new `_make_empty_mhc_intermediate_tensors`: a single `"hidden_states"` key of shape `(batch, mhc_num_residual_streams, hidden_size)` — the residual streams themselves, token dim leading so the runner's per-batch slicing works. For non-mHC configs it is the standard `make_empty_intermediate_tensors_factory(["hidden_states", "residual"], hidden_size)`.
* `Glm5NextModel.forward` materializes the pending `hc_post` on the **sending** rank, through the last active layer's `hc_post()`, before constructing the `IntermediateTensors`. Only the residual streams cross the boundary. Under sequence parallelism the streams are flattened, all-gathered and reshaped (collectives expect 2-D), mirroring what the last rank already does before its final norm.
* On the **receiving** rank `residual`/`post`/`comb` start as `None`, so its first layer takes the standalone `hc_pre` path — which is exactly the layer-0 path minus `hc_expand` (`layer_idx != 0` there, so no re-expansion).
* `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` alias `make_empty_intermediate_tensors` so `supports_pp()` is satisfied. `Glm4vForConditionalGeneration.forward`, which the multimodal class inherits, already passes `intermediate_tensors` through to `language_model.model` and returns them unchanged on non-last ranks.

**Why this is equivalent:** `MHCFusedPostPreOp` is defined as `hc_post` followed by `hc_pre` on the updated streams. Splitting the two halves across a stage boundary computes the same two operations with the same parameters; only the kernel fusion is lost, for one layer per stage.

### 2. MTP drafter ran with an uninitialised embedding under PP (`vllm/models/glm5next/common/mtp.py`)

With PP enabled, MTP accepted **exactly zero** draft tokens. Outputs remained correct (verification is untouched), so MTP was pure overhead. Three things lined up:

* The checkpoint has no `layers.45.embed_tokens`; the MTP input embedding is the target's `model.embed_tokens.weight`.
* `Glm5NextMTP.load_weights` dropped that weight — the name arrives with the `model.language_model.` prefix already stripped, and `get_spec_layer_idx_from_weight_name` returns `None` for it.
* `maybe_share_target_embed` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/eagle/utils.py`) early-returns when `pp_world_size > 1` and the drafter does not declare `has_own_embed_tokens`; and on the last PP stage the target's `embed_tokens` is a `PPMissingLayer` anyway, so there is nothing to alias.

`Glm5NextMTP.__init__` now sets `self.has_own_embed_tokens = not get_pp_group().is_first_rank`, and `load_weights` loads `model.embed_tokens.weight` into the drafter's own `VocabParallelEmbedding` when that flag is set. With PP=1 the flag is `False`, the weight is skipped as before, and the target's embedding is aliased — no second copy, no behaviour change.

## Test Plan

* New CPU-only unit test `tests/models/glm5next/test_pp_intermediate_tensors.py` (no GPU, no process group, no weights): `make_empty_intermediate_tensors` keys/shapes/dtypes for mHC and non-mHC, and the `Glm5NextModel.forward` PP branch wiring on first/middle/last ranks with a patched `get_pp_group` and stand-in layers — including that exactly the last active layer's `hc_post` is called at a send, and that `supports_pp()` holds for both model classes.

  ```bash
  pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_pp_intermediate_tensors.py -q
  ```

* Standalone kernel-level comparison of `MHCPreOp` / `MHCPostOp` / `MHCFusedPostPreOp`: fused path vs. the split (post-then-pre) path used at a stage boundary.

* End-to-end serving on 4x NVIDIA CMP 170HX (GA100, sm_80, 64 GB) with `--pipeline-parallel-size 4`, checkpoint `canada-quant/GLM-5.3-Flash-W4A16-MTP`, vLLM `a31ec3a68`:
    * greedy free-form generation, coherence check;
    * GSM8K, first 50 test problems, greedy, chat template, with and without MTP;
    * `SpecDecoding` metrics with `num_speculative_tokens` 1 and 2, eager and CUDA-graph;
    * single-stream 256-token latency with and without MTP.

## Test Result

Unit test: `9 passed`. `ruff format` and `ruff check` clean on the three changed files, along with the `check-spdx-header`, `check-forbidden-imports`, `check-torch-cuda-call`, `check-root-lazy-imports` and `check-boolean-context-manager` pre-commit hooks.

Kernel-level fused-vs-split comparison: **bit-identical** residual streams for token counts > 32 (where the fused op already runs unfused internally); for <= 32 tokens, where the TileLang fused kernel keeps fp32 state, <= 1 bf16 ulp on `x` (max absolute difference 3.1e-2 at |x| ~ 4.7) and ~1e-3 on the mixes.

End-to-end at PP=4:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| PP=4 serving | refused (`supports_pp()` False) | works end to end, coherent greedy output |
| GSM8K (50 problems, greedy, chat) | n/a | **0.98** with MTP and without |
| SpecDecoding, N=1 and N=2, eager and CUDA-graph | `Accepted: 0 tokens, Drafted: 604+` | mean acceptance length **2.45–2.81** |
| per-position acceptance | 0 | **0.85 / 0.60** free-form, **0.95 / 0.86** GSM8K |
| single-stream 256-token generation | ~5.7 s (no MTP) | ~3.3 s (MTP) |

GSM8K accuracy is identical with and without MTP, as expected since speculative verification is unchanged.

**Hardware note:** the end-to-end numbers were measured on sm_80 (CMP 170HX) with an out-of-tree sparse-attention backend for that architecture. **That backend is not part of this PR** and neither fix depends on it — both changes are plain Python in the model definition and the MTP weight loader, with no architecture-specific code, so they apply to any accelerator that can run GLM-5.3-Flash. The PP=4 end-to-end evidence is what the author had hardware for; reviewers with Hopper/Blackwell nodes may want to confirm the same acceptance rates there.

**AI assistance disclosure:** this change was developed with AI assistance (Claude). The submitter reviewed every changed line, ran the tests, and validated the behaviour end to end on the hardware above. The commits carry `Co-authored-by:` trailers.

title: [Prototype][MRV2] Stage DeepSeek decode tokens for imbalanced DBO graph replay
body:
## Purpose

Related issue: #57177; RFC: #50738. Built on MRV2 FULL-graph DBO support in #51700.

During imbalanced DP decode, a rank can leave the last physical microbatch empty even though a FULL CUDA Graph was captured. The original prototype stages real tokens into the captured regions and restores logical request order before sampling. It also keeps returned routed-expert records in the correct microbatch and slot order.

This update extends that path to a synchronized active microbatch count and adjusts NIXL EP dispatch capacity and communication handoff. It remains a prototype for design review.

## Duplicate-work check

Open-PR searches for `57177 in:body` and `DBO staging` were refreshed on 2026-09-28. This updates the existing #57184; the former search found only this PR, and the latter found no other PR for the same MRV2 NIXL staging path. Open #57020 handles the empty-tail boundary by falling back to eager; this PR stages eligible real tokens to retain FULL replay. The overlapping predicate still needs reconciliation before merge.

## Changes

- Keep conditional staging, post-forward input restoration, and routed-expert record ordering. Capability gates cover FLASH_ATTN_MLA and a constrained unquantized BF16 FLASH_ATTN path with FULL/AOT metadata; they still exclude unsupported parallel layouts and auxiliary inputs.
- Let `--ubatch-size` specify a fixed count. With MRV2, NIXL EP, DP>1, `--enable-dbo`, and no fixed count, select an active count from 2 up to the configured resource limit (default 8) using synchronized DP load and captured graph layouts. Capture the corresponding variants and use the selected count for slices, threads, workspace, and shared-expert state.
- Keep DeepEP at two microbatches; reject larger counts for backends with only two handle slots.
- Use synchronized padded execution metadata, with NIXL receive-extent alignment, for runtime dispatch capacity. Keep the static scheduler budget as a reservation limit. Match batched expert output views to the runtime shape.
- Hand NIXL DBO dispatch/combine between communication and compute streams and preserve receive data ownership when more than two microbatches overlap.

More capture variants and receive snapshots can increase startup work and memory use. These changes do not establish a throughput gain.

## Validation

On the pushed head `fb317c5ec5`:

```text
.venv/bin/pre-commit run
  passed, including Ruff, mypy, configuration validation, and sign-off hooks
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py
  159 passed, 30 skipped
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/moe/test_nixl_ep.py -k 'not microbatches_capture_and_replay'
  29 passed, 5 deselected
git diff --check
  passed
```

The three-ubatch NIXL test now distinguishes slice rows `[42,42,44]` from the aligned dispatch capacities `[44,44,44]`. The machine used for this update cannot communicate with the NVIDIA driver, so real NIXL CUDA Graph capture/replay and a new full-model run were not performed. Earlier exploratory H200 runs of the current WIP timed out in the two-ubatch capture/replay test; the cause remains unresolved. GPU correctness and ABI compatibility still need validation before merge.

## Model evaluation

No model evaluation was run on the pushed head because this machine has no usable GPU. The previous two-microbatch PR revision completed 5,124 DeepSeek-V2-Lite DP2/DP4 serving requests with the recorded sampling and routed-expert checks; those results do not validate this update's dynamic counts, NIXL stream changes, or runtime capacity. Historical H200 measurements on an earlier local source snapshot verified OFF capacity 128 and ON capacities 64+64, while DBO ON remained slower than OFF in the measured B workload. Those measurements are not a performance claim for this pushed head.

## AI assistance and human review

OpenAI Codex assisted with the rebase, test-contract correction, static checks, and PR preparation. The submitting user explicitly requested this push. Human line-by-line review and independent execution of the relevant tests have not been confirmed; the repository's human-review requirements remain applicable before merge.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] AMD-Quark mixed-precision DeepSeek-V4.1 support with Quark OCP MXFP8
body:
## Purpose

Fix `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-MXFP4` loading issue. It is a **mixed-precision** AMD-Quark export — MXFP4 experts, but 226 per-layer attention specs in MXFP8:

| | scheme |
|---|---|
| `global_quant_config` | `fp4` / `per_group` / `group_size=32` / `e8m0` |
| `layer_quant_config` (226 entries) | `fp8_e4m3` / `per_block` / `block_size=[32,32]` / `float8_e8m0fnu` |

Exsiting DeepSeek **V4**'s require `128x128` block geometry, or the DeepSeek-native scale naming. 
 
This PR fix the blockers and support MXFP8 by routing through the normal Quark matcher chain via QuarkOCP_MX, like MXFP4 and MXFP6. Changes (8 files, +300/−241):

    - ocp_mx_utils.py — Add mxfp8_e4m3 to quant key maps; add ocp_mx_weight_dtype_and_rows() normalizer accepting both config dialects (canonical per-group and V4.1 per-block)
    - quark.py — Rewrite _is_w_ocp_mx_a_x around the normalizer; delete the MXFP8 short-circuit; thread scale_block_rows through init_scheme
    - quark_ocp_mx.py — Extend QuarkOCP_MX with unpacked MXFP8 path: 3-way packed_factor, create_weights with repeat_interleave scale loader, init_mxfp8_linear_kernel() branch, terminal else: raise
    - quark_w8a8_mxfp8.py — Deleted
    - config_utils.py — Fix KeyError for per-block configs missing group_size
    - quark_moe.py — Explicit MXFP8 rejection message; else: raise in get_packed_dim
    - test_quark.py — Shape A + Shape B dispatch tests; MoE rejection test; updated existing test to assert QuarkOCP_MX
 

### End-to-end

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-MXFP4` (48 shards, 475 GB) on 4x MI355X at TP=4: all
shards load in 74.5 s, MXFP8 attention resolves to `QuarkW8A8Mxfp8`, and the
model is coherent.

Accuracy was measured rather than eyeballed — `lm_eval` gsm8k, full 1319
problems, 5-shot, greedy

Filter | 5-shot accuracy |
-- | --
flexible-extract | 91.58% ± 0.76
strict-match | 91.66% ± 0.76

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][GLM-5.3-Flash] Apply deferred tilelang.jit already on attribute access
body:
## Purpose

Required to run GLM-5.3-Flash on MI350, otherwise errors during warmup with:

```bash
File "vllm/model_executor/warmup/jit_warmup.py", line 969, in compile_many
  self.compile(compile_key)
File "vllm/model_executor/warmup/jit_warmup_tilelang_helper.py", line 141, in launch
  return compile_tilelang(jit_impl, *args, **call_kwargs)
File "vllm/model_executor/warmup/jit_warmup_tilelang_helper.py", line 104, in compile_tilelang
  compiled = jit_impl.compile(*args, **kwargs)
AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'compile'
```

### Why

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51159 added lazy import of tilelang and made the `tilelang_jit` decorator return a **regular function on ROCm** instead of a `tilelang.jit.JITImpl`. On ROCm, this function would create and return the JITImpl when **called**. That's fine as long as you just _call_ the kernel the first time you need it, which is how warmup was previously done.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50178 refactored the warmup logic of tilelang mHC kernels. Previously the warmup was done by literally calling/running the mHC layers. After that PR, warmup now runs `.compile(...)` on the kernel to compile it, and later caches the compiled kernel manually. That's ok on CUDA where the kernel is a JITImpl, but not on ROCm where it's a regular function.

Hence the assumption that the tilelang kernel will be _called_ the first time it's used is no longer true. It's no longer launched during warmup, just `.compiled()`. This PR ensures that the first time we touch the (lazily created) kernel we convert it into a JITImpl to be compiled.

## Test Plan

<details> <summary> Running the official recipes: </summary>

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE 
```
```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
```
