title: [Model][DSv4.1] Add shared host Engram lookup for SP token owners
body:
## Purpose

Add an opt-in CPU storage mode for DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram that lets each
sequence-parallel rank read all hash heads for its own tokens. Today each rank
reads its head shard for all tokens, then all-gathers embeddings and selects its
local token slice. Sharing the full host table makes that exchange unnecessary.

### Summary

```text
ASIS
TP-owned head shards -> lookup all tokens/local heads
  -> TP all-gather -> select local tokens -> WKV and gate
```

```text
PR
one host table mapped by TP ranks -> lookup local tokens/all heads
  -> final BF16 rows -> WKV and gate
```

Enable with `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"sp_shared_memory":true}'`.
The flag defaults off. The initial path requires same-host TP>1, DP1/PP1,
MRV2, active SP, and single-threaded checkpoint loading. The tested DP1 setup
uses EP and DeepGEMM mega-MoE on GB200.
CP, microbatching/DBO, speculative decoding, sleep mode and DP storage modes are
rejected. Checkpoint parameters retain their TP shard shapes and each loader
writes a disjoint range of the common table. The existing registered shared-host
allocation and lifetime machinery are reused. Padded SP rows are written as
zeros. WKV and gating are unchanged.

The two full host tables occupy about 188.83 GiB once, rather than once per
process. This does not reduce table memory relative to an ordinary TP-sharded
replica. At an 8192-token ceiling, each rank retains 24 MiB of staging per layer:
`[8192,6,256]` becomes `[2048,24,256]`. Registration and NUMA costs remain relevant;
this is an explicit placement option, not a general serving-speedup claim.

Duplicate check: #56435 retains partitioned table visibility and uses all-to-all;
#56989 keeps embeddings packed through exchange; #56929 fuses reorder and input
quantization; #56926 changes prefetch scheduling. This change removes the Engram
exchange through shared visibility and token ownership. It does not implement
those other paths.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py \
  tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/config/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py \
  tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py \
  docs/design/engram_sp_shared_memory.md
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/config/engram.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py
```

## Test Result

- 120 Engram kernel/distributed tests passed on the final rebased code.
- Changed-file pre-commit and Python 3.12 mypy passed.
- TP2/4 exact row parity, disjoint shard loading, padding/empty rank slices,
  graph replay, mapping failure rollback and registered-storage lifetime covered.
- Both model modes pass ten fixed-answer canaries and context retrieval checks.
- Pinned five-shot GSM8K, 32 questions: fixed repeated evaluation gives control
  31/32 then 32/32; direct 32/32 then 31/32, with no truncated outputs. The same
  break-even question varies. This is bounded accuracy evidence, not bitwise or
  broad model-quality equivalence. An earlier 1024-token direct run capped that
  answer; it is retained in the evidence, not counted as an untruncated pass.

TP4/EP4, DP1, GB200, MRV2, normal graphs, APC off, 4 GiB KV/rank, 64 outputs:

| Input tokens | Batch | Control tok/s | Direct tok/s | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 512 | 1 | 103.35 | 104.14 | +0.76% |
| 8192 | 1 | 95.68 | 101.33 | +5.90% |
| 512 | 16 | 1466.10 | 1477.10 | +0.75% |
| 512 | 64 | 2908.84 | 2978.69 | +2.40% |
| 8192 | 16 | 347.11 | 348.49 | +0.40% |
| 8192 | 64 | 423.98 | 431.71 | +1.82% |
| 512 / 2048 / 8192 mixed | 24 | 726.68 | 709.73 | -2.33% |

One warmup and three timed repeats per case. Prompts and scheduler signatures
match within each pair; no preemptions. B1 uses max_num_seqs=4 and the earlier
synthetic prompts; wider batches use max_num_seqs=64 and varied document prompts.
Mixed means eight requests each at 512/2048/8192 tokens. These are single-load
observations, not a general speedup guarantee; the mixed-length regression is
retained. Registration and NUMA costs remain, and existing shutdown warnings
are not addressed by this change.

[Validation scripts, raw results, and provenance](https://github.com/foraxe/vllm/tree/32ce421f9a8a11b02b7a95aee86b275696845df7/evidence/engram-sp-direct).

AI assistance was used for implementation, testing, and documentation.

title: [Bugfix][PP] Isolate FlashInfer autotune groups and caches by pipeline stage
body:
## Purpose

Keep synchronized FlashInfer autotuning within a pipeline stage's tensor-parallel group, and isolate each group's persistent cache. Different pipeline stages can execute different operations and tuning rounds; using the world group couples incompatible collective sequences and permits incompatible stage caches to be reused.

- With PP enabled, use the TP CPU group for tactic timing and initial cache broadcast/load synchronization.
- Choose one cache writer per tuning group and add the group's global ranks to its cache filename.
- Keep the existing world-group behavior and cache filename for PP1, and preserve final world synchronization and exception cleanup.
- Extend the existing warmup suite for heterogeneous stages, TP1/TP4, cold/warm/asymmetric cache hits, PP1 compatibility, and exception propagation/group reset.

## Scope and duplicate check

This generic warmup repair is independent of the MiniMax-M3 auxiliary-state transport in #57197 and of the six existing SM120 attention/indexer/router/proposer PRs. None of their changed files contains this repair. No ROCm platform or AMD-specific source is changed.

Related work was inspected rather than duplicated:

- #48714 introduces distributed autotuning/cache synchronization; this corrects its pipeline-stage grouping, not the original feature.
- #52292 provides an opt-out from distributed synchronization for #52291. This draft instead retains synchronization within each TP group and isolates stage caches. It does not claim to solve every multi-node transport issue from that report.
- #55671 migrates to managed autotune caches and still selects the world CPU group. This draft stays on the current cache API and does not duplicate that migration.

## Validation already obtained

The same PP grouping/cache repair was present in the retained composed GPU validation build on eight RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs: MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 target TP4/PP2, EAGLE3 draft TP4/PP1, K3, concurrency 12.

- Full 1,319-question GSM8K: 1,278 strict matches (96.8916%) and 1,277 flexible matches (96.8158%), all raw records captured, no empty or invalid rows.
- Approximately 3,600 seconds of measured serving plus drain: 1,119 sent, 1,117 completed, 1,116 successful, one profiling error and two grace cancellations. Two invalid warmup rows remain separately recorded. Existing serving validators passed; this was not an error-free run.

These are shared composed-build results, not another GPU run, isolated causality/speedup proof, a distributed FlashInfer serialization unit test, or execution of this exact new PR head. Newer upstream HiSparse warmup behavior is preserved here; test fixtures were adapted to its existing attention configuration and `skip_attn` keyword.

Publication checks:

```text
ruff check tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py
ruff format --check tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py
git diff --check
```

All passed; both changed files compile. **The exact public-source imported suite now passes all 10 cases**: 10 collected, 10 executed, no failed/error/skipped reports, pytest exit 0 in 12.51 seconds. Normal production-module imports were checked against the selected public source. The independent allocation requested zero GPUs and recorded CUDA as uninitialized; compatible dependencies and 17 pinned native binaries were reused, not rebuilt for this head. Source remained unchanged and the allocation was released. This qualifies the imported CPU suite, not a new distributed/GPU build.

The earlier local collection failure on missing Torch remains a zero-test attempt, not baseline RED. No same-suite before-fix run was performed in this successful attempt. The focused command is:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py -q
```

The new tests exercise the imported production function and atomic cache writer with mocked groups/tuner and temporary cache files. They do not replace real distributed/GPU validation.

## Current-public-source targeted GPU validation

Real eight-SM120 MiniMax-M3 runs now cover the planned TP4/PP2 cold and same-cache warm arms, plus the TP8/PP1 compatibility control:

- Cold created distinct stage caches with 70/40 new configurations. All eight warm workers loaded the corresponding caches; both leaders saved zero new configurations, preserving the cache hashes and ordered GPU mapping.
- The separate PP1 control retained the unsuffixed cache filename and tuned 70 new configurations. Its supported profiler configuration disables stack tracing while preserving shape recording, CPU/CUDA profiling and graph execution.
- Each completed arm produced two HTTP 200 responses with 128 generated reasoning tokens each, and successful profiler start/stop acknowledgments. All eight retained profiles per arm contain actual FlashInfer GPU kernels and 254 CUDA graph launches per rank. The final PP1 request/profile session completed in 40.836 seconds; cold/warm were not rerun.
- Current public source and reused native-library identities were checked. This is exact-public-source runtime evidence, not a new native-library rebuild, startup per-tactic RPC trace, full-answer accuracy benchmark or comparative performance result.

The existing lifecycle thresholds passed, but shutdown limitations remain explicit. The final PP1 run reported five remaining process-group members after SIGKILL, force-kill/resource-tracker warnings and 5.33 GB GPU memory against its 7.48 GB threshold. The model step exited 0 and the owned allocation was released; no independently pristine-process or zero-memory cleanup is claimed. Original raw qualification flags and prior failed attempts remain unchanged.

title: [MiniMax-M3] Bound decode indexer chunks by available work
body:
## Purpose

Bound MiniMax-M3 decode indexer partitions by the work available, instead of creating avoidable score producers and partial top-k results for short contexts.

- Cap score chunks by the existing CPU-visible page bound, retaining at least one chunk.
- Bound partial top-k chunks by available blocks relative to twice the padded selection width.
- Extend the existing decode numerical test to both 1,025 and 8,193 tokens, including padded requests and speculative-query layouts.

The bounds use existing shape-derived inputs; this adds no device-to-host synchronization and does not change score arithmetic or kernel bodies.

## Dependency and duplicate checks

This is the narrow work-cap follow-up to #49229, whose launch-budget retuning remains owned by Kyle. **Neither launch-budget constant is changed here**: this main-based draft retains `TARGET_GRID=512` and `TOPK_TARGET_GRID=64`. Review/landing should be coordinated with that PR; its larger-budget change is not copied into this diff.

Fresh open-PR and file-diff checks found no duplicate of these two caps and this decode-test extension. #56149 owns the fused decode top-k merge, #56150 owns prefill splitting, and #56151 owns FP8 admission/scoring. They share files but their changes are not included or overwritten here. #53448 and #47665 address different indexer/backend behavior; #56932 changes sparse attention rather than this indexer wrapper.

This is not a combined-stack replacement or a claim that these caps are necessary for a benchmark winner or minimum stack.

## Test plan

- On a supported GPU, run the existing numerical suite:
  ```bash
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py -k test_decode_index_topk_correctness -q
  ```
- Review composition with the related PRs without changing their owned constants, kernels, or admission policy.
- Maintainer review, submitting-human line review and independent manual execution remain pending before merge. The bounded standalone model/path validation below is independently checked and ready for technical review.

## Test results and limits

**Current repaired draft: 12 selected, 12 executed, 12 passed; zero failures, errors or skips.** The existing decode numerical selection ran with normal repository imports and fixtures on one independently allocated RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU. It retains both 1,025/8,193-token lengths, both padding choices, and all three actual/maximum decode-query layouts. The strict unordered index-set assertion is unchanged. Pytest exited 0; all setup/call/teardown reports and per-case XML agree. Applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, typos, mypy and source checks.

**Preserved RED and diagnosis:** the first current-draft run actually executed 12 cases: **11 passed and one failed** for the 8,193-token/two-padded-request/one-actual-query/maximum-width-four case. That original unseeded run did not retain its RNG state or tensors, so its exact random sample is not claimed replayed. A bounded diagnostic of that same parameter tuple retained a deterministic failing input at seed 149. On those identical tensors, the unchanged parent production module and this PR returned bitwise-identical valid scores and selected indices. Both use 64 score chunks and four top-k chunks for this shape; neither new cap changes that case.

The seeded discrepancy comes from FP32 fixture inputs: the kernel's TF32-truncated dot and the full-FP32 oracle reverse a close ranking. For the cutoff candidates, oracle scores favor block 19 over 62 (8.749260 versus 8.748881), while both production versions favor 62 over 19 (8.744544 versus 8.744464). These numbers describe the retained seed-149 reproduction, not the uncaptured original sample.

**Minimal test repair:** fix seed 149 and convert the same generated query/cache tensors to production BF16 before both kernel and reference consume them. Production exposes no FP32 indexer-cache mode. No assertion, tolerance, parameter coverage, cap, launch budget or kernel body was changed by this repair. The same selected pytest case records **RED: one failure → GREEN: one pass**, followed by the **full 12-case PASS** above. The existing independent owner accepted the exact bounded test delta; that is peer code review, not submitting-human approval.

Both independent allocations requested one GPU, one CPU and 8 GiB RAM under a 15-minute limit; the scheduler allocated two CPU threads. They terminated and released their allocations after 2m01s and 9m52s respectively, with isolated-runtime cleanup recorded. The intentional RED step remains recorded as failed; it is not relabeled a passing run.

**Native-carrier/composition limits:** the complete selected public Python source and exact test bytes were verified with normal imports, using a separately pinned compatible dependency environment and 17 pinned native files. This was not a native wheel rebuilt from the final draft. The environment reports Python 3.12.13, Torch 2.13.0+cu130 and driver 595.58.03 on SM120. The runs emitted 15 warnings each, from absent generated version metadata and Torch JIT deprecations; no warning is counted as an error or skip. The new result qualifies this seeded BF16 numerical selection only—not arbitrary FP32/FP8 inputs, universal seed stability, AMD-native behavior, composed-stack interactions, graph/stream coverage, model accuracy, serving, isolated performance or minimum-stack necessity.

**Retained earlier standalone evidence:** the earlier CPU, SM120 numerical, graph/tie and concurrency checks used a standalone configuration with retuned launch budgets. They remain historical evidence, not additional validation of this draft, which retains `TARGET_GRID=512` and `TOPK_TARGET_GRID=64`.

The numerical runs above did not perform model or serving validation; the subsequent standalone model/path result below is separate. The broader full-accuracy/performance/minimum-stack work remains open. AI assistance was used for diagnosis, test repair, execution and reporting; the submitting human's line review and independent manual execution remain pending.

## Standalone real-model/path validation — September 17, 2026 UTC

**PASS: one bounded real MiniMax-M3 request using this PR's Python source on eight RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs.** The configuration was TP8/PP1, EAGLE3 K5, BF16 indexer, FP8 main KV, S16, CUDA graphs, and a 4,096-token model bound, without a fused-stack or FP8-indexer overlay.

title: [Perf][DSA] Use DeepSelect for eligible sparse-indexer prefill chunks
body:
## Purpose

Extend the existing opt-in `deep_select` sparse-indexer backend to supported prefill chunks. Today the option accelerates decode, while prefill still calls `top_k_per_row_prefill`. For eligible chunks, reuse DeepSelect with the causal per-row end bounds and the existing preallocated output buffer.

The fast path requires a single request in the indexer chunk, SM100-family hardware, no PCP or DCP, and supported input/output alignment. A single request's gathered KV starts at column zero, so DeepSelect's `end` argument represents the original causal interval. Multi-request chunks, context parallelism, and unsupported layouts retain the existing kernel. A multi-request batch can still benefit when the chunk planner places each request in its own chunk.

Enable with `--kernel-config '{"sparse_indexer_topk_backend":"deep_select"}'`. Defaults and decode dispatch are unchanged. No new kernels or dependency changes.

## Duplicate-work check

Follow-up to merged #56464, which integrated DeepSelect for decode. Checked #56217 and its comments, open PRs referring to that issue, and DeepSelect/prefill-top-k searches.

- #55363 changes the existing prefill kernel's thread count; this selects DeepSelect through the existing explicit backend option.
- #56749 introduces stable tie-breaking with a different selector; this does not promise index-stable ties.
- #56258 changes context-parallel prefill sharding/publication; this fast path excludes context parallelism.
- #57109 adds a decode GVR backend; this extends prefill only.

None implements this DeepSelect prefill path.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k deep_select_topk -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/config/kernel.py vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files vllm/config/kernel.py vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py --hook-stage manual
```

Extend the existing preallocated-output test to cover bounded selection and CUDA graph replay after updating row ends. Includes empty/short rows, lengths around top-k, full-length rows, strided output, untouched padding, and `-1` tails. Compare selected scores against PyTorch.

## Test Result

Standalone commit `3e850c278d`, based on `42919b49c5`: **26 GPU tests passed** on GB200 (250 deselected). Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy 3.10, and explicit mypy 3.12 passed. The three changed files exactly match the previously validated patch.

Earlier validation of the same patch included three full-model parity probes: 4K prefill/~100K KV, eight 1K prefills/~100K KV, and a mixed-chunk case exercising both DeepSelect and the nonzero-start fallback. All observed output errors were zero.

### Performance evidence and limitations

**The earlier approximately 6.3x top-k speedup is a dummy-model benchmark result, not a demonstrated real-weight serving speedup.** Those profiles used `v41_benchmark_dummy` weights and generated KV history. The 4K-query/~100K-KV profile measured 7.52 ms versus 1.19 ms summed over ten prefill top-k launches per forward; both arms had matching launch counts and row counts. It was not a 6.3x full-model speedup. The previously quoted exploratory 8.0%/10.8% full-forward gains also predate the benchmark metadata-reset correction and should not be treated as validated production gains.

#### Captured real-model logits

We repeated kernel timing on logits captured from actual `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` weights (revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`), TP4/EP4, MegaMoE, FlashInfer FP8 KV and the MXFP4 NEW sparse indexer. Prompts contained repository documentation, with actual context lengths of 8,192, 51,200 and 102,400 tokens. We captured the first eligible matrix at each column width; these samples do not cover every layer or prompt distribution.

| Logits columns | Query rows in captured chunk | Existing prefill top-k | DeepSelect | Native / DeepSelect |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4,096 | 8,192 | 110.4 us | 193.6 us | 0.57x |
| 8,192 | 8,192 | 135.6 us | 227.8 us | 0.60x |
| 25,600 | 2,048 | 111.5 us | 151.8 us | 0.73x |
| 51,200 | 2,048 | 176.7 us | 195.4 us | 0.90x |
| 102,400 | 1,310 | 233.7 us | 180.9 us | 1.29x |

Here “native” means vLLM's existing CUDA `top_k_per_row_prefill`, not PyTorch or FlashInfer. Both selectors used identical captured FP32 logits, causal bounds, top-k 512 and preallocated outputs. Measurements used a GB200 on `gb200-rack1-04`, CUPTI CUDA-graph timing with cold L2, 25 warmup calls and four alternating timing rounds. Selected-score equality, valid/unique indices and short-row tails passed for every case before timing. Matched normal-random controls produced similar trends.

**The original dummy-input result overstated the benefit for these sampled real-model workloads.** DeepSelect regressed on the captured 4K–50K-column matrices and improved the 100K-column matrix by about 1.29x, not 6–7x. These are isolated selector timings, not end-to-end serving gains. In particular, 100K actual context also includes compressed 50K-column selections where DeepSelect was slower.

#### Synthetic controls

Fresh single-GB200 kernel measurements show that both shape and score distribution matter. With normal-random FP32 logits, top-k 512, 4K query rows, causal row bounds, uncompressed KV, preallocated outputs, CUPTI CUDA-graph timing and cold L2:

| KV / logits columns | Existing prefill top-k | DeepSelect | Native / DeepSelect |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8,192 | 80.9 us | 135.0 us | 0.60x |
| 51,200 | 321.4 us | 352.4 us | 0.91x |
| 102,400 | 688.3 us | 499.9 us | 1.38x |

A controlled distribution ablation at the **same** 8K-query/8K-KV shape demonstrates why random logits cannot stand in for every indexer workload:

| FP32 score distribution | Existing prefill top-k | DeepSelect | Native / DeepSelect |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Normal random | 122.4 us | 225.1 us | 0.54x |
| Same random values + 100 | 1168.0 us | 241.8 us | 4.83x |
| Same random values * 1e-8 | 1153.6 us | 224.3 us | 5.14x |

All cases passed selected-score correctness checks. The native selector initially bins scores through FP16 conversion; concentrated values increase histogram contention and can require further selection work. DeepSelect is much less affected in this ablation. This demonstrates input-dependent performance, but does **not** by itself establish the cause of the exact 6.3x historical model-profile result.

For the tested DSV4.1 checkpoint, 102,400 actual context tokens produce 51,200-entry KV in layers 2–19 and 102,400-entry KV in layers 20–39. With the NEW sparse indexer, dense prefill top-k runs at index sources 2/8/14 over the compressed context and source 20 over the uncompressed context; later indexers use selected candidate blocks. A single nominal KV-length threshold does not describe all of these selections.

**No universal 6–7x speedup or real-weight end-to-end gain is claimed by this PR.** The captured real-model measurements argue against using DeepSelect unconditionally for prefill. Any automatic dispatch should depend on the actual logits width and be validated with corrected model-level measurements; the random-logit sweep alone is insufficient to establish a production cutoff.

Real-weight evaluation previously completed with this patch in the combined optimized model configuration: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, TP4/EP4, native MegaMoE/shared fusion, FlashInfer sparse attention. Full GSM8K, lm-eval 0.4.12, five-shot multi-turn chat, thinking disabled, greedy generation, 1024 output tokens, seed 123:

| Configuration | Correct / 1319 | Accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Auto-MoE/FlashMLA FP8-indexer baseline, three runs | 1270–1274 | 96.2851–96.5883% |
| Combined optimized configuration, FP8 indexer | 1269 | 96.2092% |
| Combined optimized configuration, MXFP4 sparse indexer | 1266 | 95.9818% |

These combined evaluations include separate attention and MoE changes; they do not isolate DeepSelect's quality effect. Selection tests check score correctness, not identical membership among tied scores.

## AI assistance

Codex assisted with implementation, validation, and this description. Woosuk Kwon requested upstreaming this change after reviewing its scope and reported results.

title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Segment FlashInfer FP8 prefill queries for faster attention tiles
body:
## Purpose

Bound FP8 prefill query segments to 1024 tokens in the DeepSeek-V4.1 FlashInfer sparse-MLA backend. The existing TRTLLM-GEN launcher selects a faster query tile for these shapes. An 8192-query request is presented as eight segments in one attention call, using the same query/KV/output storage and sparse indices.

Preserve absolute positions by giving each segment sequence length `original_seq_len - original_query_len + segment_end`. Query starts and segment sequence lengths use persistent buffers; the sequence-length values are refreshed from device metadata on each build. Decode dispatch and BF16 query grouping remain unchanged. This works with the existing FlashInfer API and requires no FlashInfer source patch.

This is a vLLM-side workaround for FlashInfer's tile-selection heuristic. The 1024-token cap should be reassessed when that heuristic changes; a future FlashInfer dispatch fix could remove this metadata adaptation.

## Duplicate-work check

Checked #56217/comments, open PRs referencing that issue, and FlashInfer/prefill/segmentation/sparse-MLA searches. No open PR implements this query segmentation. Related SM120 backend fixes, SM90 prefill additions, and indexer chunk-planning changes target different paths. This is independent of #57204 and #57206.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py -k segments_preserve_positions_and_replay_updates -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py --hook-stage manual
```

The tests cover FP8 segmentation and unchanged BF16 grouping, mixed decode/prefill batches, padded query offsets, preserved positions, persistent buffer addresses, and CUDA graph replay after sequence lengths change.

## Test Result

Standalone commit `9890a68a89`, based on `6ca2b23e22`: **12 tests passed** on GB200 (10 deselected). Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy 3.10, and explicit mypy 3.12 passed. The newer upstream output-projection fix is preserved.

Earlier four-GB200 matched profiles showed Q16 attention tiles replacing Q8 for 8K prefill, reducing total attention kernel time from **35.53 to 20.74 ms**. Exploratory isolated full-forward latency reductions were 10.55% for 8K prefill/~8K KV, 8.50% for 4K prefill/~100K KV, and 9.84% for an 8K prefill plus 31 decode requests/~100K KV. Full-model parity probes observed zero output error.

Those isolated timing probes predate a benchmark metadata-reset correction affecting two SWA mapping calls in both arms; they are not fresh standalone-branch end-to-end measurements. The later corrected full matrix validated the combined configuration, rather than isolating this patch's contribution.

Real-weight evaluation previously completed with this segmentation in the combined optimized configuration: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, TP4/EP4, native MegaMoE/shared fusion, FlashInfer sparse attention. Full GSM8K, lm-eval 0.4.12, five-shot multi-turn chat, thinking disabled, greedy generation, 1024 output tokens, seed 123:

| Configuration | Correct / 1319 | Accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Auto-MoE/FlashMLA FP8-indexer baseline, three runs | 1270–1274 | 96.2851–96.5883% |
| Combined optimized configuration, FP8 indexer | 1269 | 96.2092% |
| Combined optimized configuration, MXFP4 sparse indexer | 1266 | 95.9818% |

These combined evaluations include separate MoE and indexer changes and do not isolate segmentation's quality effect. The 1M model limit was used; these GSM8K evaluations do not test 1M-token prompts.

## AI assistance

Codex assisted with implementation, validation, and this description. Woosuk Kwon requested this PR after reviewing the segmentation approach, measured gains, and maintenance tradeoff.

title: [Build] Bump DeepGEMM pin to a6bbb80
body:
## Purpose

Bump the `vllm-project/DeepGEMM` fork pin from `ad1f172` to `a6bbb800` (current head of the fork's `dev` branch), picking up three fixes:

- **[DeepGEMM#9](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/9)** — corrects the ported SM120 GEMM and MQA execution paths, and moves the SM120 regression tests into dedicated `tests/test_sm120_*.py` files so the fork's copies of upstream-owned test files stay byte-identical to `dev` (removes a recurring sync-conflict surface on upstream's per-release test rewrites).
- **[DeepGEMM#11](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/11)** — drops the Mega-Gate finite-score device trap. The selected-expert-ID clamp is retained; non-finite scores now propagate instead of aborting on device.
- **[DeepGEMM#13](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/13)** — raises `kNumTimeoutCycles` from 60s to 300s. That is the device-side spin-wait budget shared by *every* wait in `comm/barrier.cuh`: the NVLink cross-rank barrier, the intra-device grid sync, and the mega-MoE combine peer wait. At 60s it could fire on long-running multi-rank workloads that were still making progress, turning a slow peer into a device assert.

Both pin sites are updated: `cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake` and `tools/install_deepgemm.sh`, which each carry a comment requiring them to be kept in sync.

## Not a duplicate

Checked open PRs against `vllm-project/vllm`:

```
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "deepgemm"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "bump DeepGEMM"
gh search prs --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open "install_deepgemm"
```

No open PR bumps the DeepGEMM pin. #56266 (`[DSv4.1] Integrate Mega-Gate from DeepGEMM`, draft) is the only open PR touching `deepgemm.cmake`, and it refactors the `FetchContent_Populate` block — it does not change `_DEEPGEMM_UPSTREAM_TAG`. No conflict beyond a trivial textual one if both land.

## Test Plan

The pin's risk is twofold: that the ref is fetchable as declared, and that DeepGEMM's `_C` still compiles against it. The changed `csrc/apis/{attention,einsum,gemm,sm120_dispatch}.hpp` are compiled into `_C` on every arch, so a `_C` build exercises them even on non-SM120 hardware.

1. Confirm the new ref is the `dev` head and fetches with the two submodules `deepgemm.cmake` declares (`third-party/cutlass`, `third-party/deep_jit`).
2. Build `_C` at the new pin using `tools/build_deepgemm_C.py` — the same script `deepgemm.cmake` drives.
3. `pre-commit run` on the changed files.

## Test Result

```console
$ git ls-remote https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM.git dev
a6bbb8000161c0dc3a85a0300a905f76898a7913        refs/heads/dev

$ git submodule status
 f3fde58372d33e9a5650ba7b80fc48b3b49d40c8 third-party/cutlass (f3fde58)
 e5bdee2bc4ca519eba00cfc5f0c6e950e6a96a16 third-party/deep_jit (e5bdee2)

$ CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-13.1 .venv/bin/python tools/build_deepgemm_C.py <src> <out> .venv/bin/python
# succeeded; only pre-existing -Wattributes visibility warnings from deep_jit/utils/gil.hpp
$ ls <out>
_C.cpython-312-aarch64-linux-gnu.so
```

`pre-commit run` on the two changed files: all applicable hooks pass (`shellcheck`, `typos`, dockerfile-graph, spaces-in-filenames, config-validation); the rest are skipped as no-files-to-check.

Environment: GB300 (SM103), CUDA 13.1, aarch64, Python 3.12.

## Evaluation

No model evaluation is included. This PR changes only a dependency pin and no vLLM code path. Of the three picked-up commits, none alters numerics on the hardware available here:

- #9 is SM120-only (this host is SM103), and its non-SM120 portion is a test-file reorganization inside DeepGEMM.
- #11 removes a device-side abort on non-finite Mega-Gate scores; it changes failure behavior, not values on well-formed inputs.
- #13 only lengthens a hang-detection timeout.

Evaluating the SM120 correctness fixes in #9 would need SM120 hardware, which I do not have. If a reviewer wants an eval on SM120 or a Mega-MoE accuracy run before merge, please say so and I will arrange it.

## Note on AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change. I have reviewed every changed line, ran the commands above myself, and can defend the change end-to-end.

title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Prefer MegaMoE for supported local expert parallelism
body:
## Purpose

For DeepSeek V4.1, resolve `--moe-backend auto` to `deep_gemm_mega_moe` for supported local expert-parallel deployments. Previously `auto` went through generic FusedMoE selection and never reached the model's MegaMoE path. In particular, TP4/DP1 with expert parallelism did not enable the model's sequence parallelism; the new selection enables it without requiring an explicit backend flag.

Resolve the choice during model configuration, before construction selects sequence-parallel and shared-expert paths. Preserve explicit backend choices. Restrict automatic selection to SM100-family CUDA devices with DeepGEMM enabled/available, MXFP4 experts, supported routing and dimensions, and a fully NVLink-connected local EP group. Leave other configurations on the existing selection path, including PP/CP, remote DP, Ray, speculative decoding and microbatching.

This changes backend selection only; it does not modify kernels or attention/indexer defaults. This should land after #57204 to avoid making the existing padding/duplicate-storage overhead the default. That padding change is not included in this diff.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open issues and PRs for DeepSeek/MegaMoE/default and auto-MoE selection, including PRs referencing #57204. No open PR implements this model-specific default selection. #40833 integrates generic MegaMoE support, #54049 integrates a FlashInfer MegaMoE implementation, and #57204 changes native MegaMoE padding; those are separate changes.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -k deepseek_v41_auto_moe -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/config.py tests/test_config.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files vllm/model_executor/models/config.py tests/test_config.py --hook-stage manual
```

<details>
<summary>Real-checkpoint evaluation commands</summary>

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --revision dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277 \
  --served-model-name dsv41-gsm8k --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8003 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend auto \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --no-enable-prefix-caching --language-model-only \
  --generation-config vllm --seed 123 \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"thinking":false}' \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'
```

After the server is ready:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m lm_eval run --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=dsv41-gsm8k,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8003/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,timeout=600,max_retries=2,max_gen_toks=1024,max_length=16384,seed=123 \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=1024 temperature=0.0 do_sample=False "chat_template_kwargs={'thinking': False}" \
  --seed 123,123,123,123 --log_samples --output_path gsm8k-results
```

Repeat on parent commit `1085b64425` with `--moe-backend auto` for the original selection path. For this comparison, the parent model-configuration file was restored while all other runtime source files were identical. The PR configuration file was restored after evaluation.

</details>

## Test Result

25 configuration cases passed on GB200. Applicable pre-commit hooks and mypy 3.12 passed. Coverage includes eligible selection, explicit overrides, hardware/dependency/topology guards and unsupported model/parallel configurations.

Real checkpoint: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, four GB200 GPUs, TP4/DP1/EP4, `max_model_len=1048576`, FULL decode graphs, lm-eval 0.4.12. Full GSM8K, five-shot multi-turn chat, thinking disabled, greedy generation, 1024 output tokens, seed 123.

| Selection | Correct / 1319 (flexible extraction) | Accuracy | Strict-match accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Parent `auto` → FlashInfer TRT-LLM MXFP4/MXFP8 | 1272 | 96.4367% | 79.8332% |
| Proposed `auto` → DeepGEMM MegaMoE | 1269 | 96.2092% | 78.3927% |

All 1319 document, prompt and target hashes match. Eight baseline errors became correct and eleven baseline-correct answers became errors: a net difference of three questions in this single paired run. This does not establish statistical equivalence across workloads.

Both runs retain upstream attention/indexer defaults: the server selected `FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41` with the NVFP4 attention cache format and the FP8 indexer. No separate attention, indexer or padding patches were included. The 1M model limit does not mean GSM8K tested 1M-token prompts. Startup and graph capture succeeded for both arms.

Validated source commit `cac37db059`, parent `1085b64425`, with precompiled CUDA/runtime assets from that exact parent commit. The initial checkout reused older runtime assets and failed before serving; the results above come from the matched runtime after those setup failures were resolved.

Memory tradeoff: these TP4/EP4 runs reported 81.46 GiB/GPU allocated during model loading for MegaMoE versus 71.03 GiB/GPU for the former default. This is the model-loading allocation reported by vLLM, not total serving peak memory; automatic MegaMoE selection can leave less room for KV cache. Source accounting attributes about 7.03 GiB/GPU to routed FP4 weight padding (2304 → 2560), 1.32 GiB/GPU to retained original shared weights alongside padded fused copies, and 0.99 GiB/GPU to shared-weight replication versus TP4 sharding, before scale/layout differences. #57204 removes the first two causes; the full 10.43 GiB gap should not be interpreted as intrinsic MegaMoE overhead. These component estimates are calculated from checkpoint dimensions, not a runtime tensor census.

## AI assistance

Codex assisted with implementation, validation, and this description. Woosuk Kwon requested the default change after reviewing the TEP backend-selection and sequence-parallel behavior.

title: [Bug][ROCm/gfx950] GLM-5.3-Flash 16K-chunk prefill: GPU memory-access fault when indexer triton kernels JIT during lazy CUDA-graph capture — clean under --enforce-eager
body:
## GPU memory-access fault on gfx950 (MI350X) when triton kernels JIT during lazy CUDA-graph capture of a 16K-token chunked prefill (GLM-5.3-Flash, KDA/sparse-indexer path)

### Environment

- vLLM: `v0.28.1rc1.dev681+ge7edf17ce` (V1 engine), aiter @ `2693202`, triton 3.7.0
- Hardware: 8× AMD MI350X (gfx950), TP8 + expert-parallel
- Model: GLM-5.3-Flash fp8 (MLA + KDA sparse attention indexer → uses aiter `batched_gemm_a16wfp4`, `_gluon_fp8_mqa_logits`, `_cp_gather_indexer_quant_cache_gfx950_kernel`)
- Config: `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-model-len 524288 --enable-expert-parallel --distributed-executor-backend mp`, default `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`

### Symptom

The **first** 16K-token chunk prefill crashes the engine with `Memory access fault` on all 8 ranks (e.g. `Memory access fault by GPU node-4 (Agent handle: 0x59ba0110) on address 0x7f733a000000. Reason: Unknown.`). Decode-only traffic and prefill chunks ≤8192 tokens are stable. Production impact: crash-looping pods on the first long-prompt request.

### Isolation: it's the graph capture, not the kernels

Differential with an identical request repro across cudagraph modes:

| Cudagraph mode | First 16K prefill |
|---|---|
| FULL | fault ×8 ranks |
| PIECEWISE | fault ×8 |
| FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | fault ×8 |
| **`--enforce-eager`** | **clean (0 faults, full repro suite)** |

At the moment of the fault, every kernel in the indexer chain is JIT-compiling *during inference* (boot warmup only exercised decode shapes; the 16K-prefill shapes are first seen at request time, when the 16384 cudagraph bucket is lazily captured):

```
WARNING [jit_monitor.py:141] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: BuildPrefillChunkMetadataKernel.kernel ...
WARNING [jit_monitor.py:141] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: _cp_gather_indexer_quant_cache_gfx950_kernel ...
WARNING [jit_monitor.py:141] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: _gluon_fp8_mqa_logits_kernel ...
WARNING [jit_monitor.py:141] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: _expand_pools_and_append_tail_kernel ...
WARNING [jit_monitor.py:141] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: _batched_gemm_a16wfp4_kernel ...
Memory access fault by GPU node-4 ...
```

### What we ruled out (in-server A/B, one full boot + repro per leg)

- Skipping `_gluon_fp8_mqa_logits` (correct-shape −inf logits substituted) → fault persists
- Skipping `_cp_gather_indexer_quant_cache_gfx950` (zero-fill) → fault persists
- Skipping `batched_gemm_a16wfp4` → **fault gone** (kernel execution required)
- Cloning **all** bmm tensor args (x, w, w_scales, y) to fresh contiguous memory in-server → fault persists (addresses innocent)
- `AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3` on/off → no effect
- Standalone replay with the **exact tensors dumped from the faulting call** (real strides/scales layout), M-sweep 4096→16000, workspace-pool carving with offset sweeps, two-stream interleave, plain `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` capture, and fresh-variant-JIT-inside-plain-capture → **all clean**

So: the kernel is individually correct and capture-safe in isolation, eager execution is correct, but vLLM's lazy capture of the 16384 bucket (with fresh triton JIT in the same window) faults on gfx950. We could not reproduce it outside vLLM's capture machinery.

### Current workaround

`--enforce-eager` (fully stable at 16384) — at a significant decode-throughput cost. Chunk 8192 also avoids the fault but sacrifices prefill chunk size.

### Possible directions

1. Cover the 16K-prefill shapes in boot warmup *before* the lazy capture (so JIT and first launches happen eagerly, then capture) — if the fault is specifically first-launch-during-capture, this may be sufficient and cheap.
2. Investigate whether triton-on-ROCm first-launch/module-load inside a lazily-captured graph is a known-unsafe pattern (cc ROCm/aiter#5512 — same fault, tracked there with the full bisect matrix and tensor dumps).

Happy to provide the in-pod pytest harness (~6s per leg), tensor dumps, and boot logs.

title: [RFC][ROCm]: Decode Context Parallelism (DCP) for DeepSeek-V4 hybrid SWA + compressed KV cache
body:
### Motivation.

## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 is MLA-based (1 latent KV head), so under TP, every rank stores a full replica of the KV cache. This means TP8 spends ~8x the KV memory than technically required, leading to reduced HBM headroom. DCP removes this replication by sharding the KV cache along the sequence dimension. On agentic workloads with huge sequence lengths (comprising mostly of prefill work) and heavy cache pressure, aggregate KV capacity is the dominant lever for being able to fit many requests in the cache and achieve high throughput. DP-attention also solves this problem, but can suffer from very high latency, especially when a single GPU is computing a large uncached prefill.






### Proposed Change.

## Scope / Hardware

Primary target is **ROCm on MI355X (gfx950)**. All development and validation runs on an 8xMI355X node. The ROCm/AITER leg is the focus of this work. Most of the work is vendor-neutral in nature (scheduler geometry, ownership/layout math, compressor Triton kernels, merge collectives, etc.), but we focus on MI355X for validation and performance optimization. The NVIDIA/FlashMLA attention leg is transplanted from #44573 directly, however we have no NVIDIA hardware to validate it.


## Current State

#44573 (DCP) and #43809 (PCP) by @baonudesifeizhai implemented DSV4 CP for the NVIDIA/FlashMLA path in May/June, however both are inactive since June and predate the mainline DCP framework consolidation. The merged K3 DCP stack from #51705 (decode-LSE) and #53598 (per-group cache geometry) provides the framework upon which this line of PRs is being built. However, no DSV4 model-specific support in vllm/models/deepseek_v4/ currently has the necessary DCP wiring. Additionally, mainline's DCP support currently does not support deduplication for DSV4's SWA/compressed groups.


## Proposal

We are implementing DSV4 DCP as a new PR series on top of the current main and with ongoing efforts to support DCP on other models such as Kimi-K3. Current draft PRs are here (WIP draft: <TODO>), and focuses on transplanting the validated #44573 mechanisms to the currently merged framework. The overall structure of the ongoing contribution is detailed below:

1) Interleaved position ownership with logical block tables, so prefix caching works on sharded DSV4 groups. Needs design alignment with the #53598 geometry (see below).
2) Compressor under DCP: per-rank partial softmax-pool stats -> 1 all-gather/all-reduce merge -> owner-masked cache insert.
3) Sink-free local attention returns LSE, cross-rank merge via mainline collectives such as dcp_a2a_lse_reduce / cp_lse_ag_out_rs, attn sink applied only once after merge has completed.
4) ROCm leg: LSE return + deferred sink for DSV4 sparse split-K/ragged Triton kernels, Triton topk twin for CuteDSL-only indexer merge, DCP wiring for DeepSeekV4ROCMAiterMLAAttention.forward_mqa. Validation on 8xMI355X (gfx950).
5) interleave=1 only initially, to adhere to the sparse-indexer gate. Future work could involve allowing other interleaving degrees if there is potential performance benefit.


## Asks

1) **Cache Geometry**: we are extending dcp_world_size_for_kv_cache_spec to respect the supports_context_parallel flag. Is the current design compatible with the AMD roadmap for hybrid cache DCP? cc @tjtanaa @YukioZzz @okorzh-amd 
2) **AITER**: the gfx950 OPUS sparse prefill (pa_sparse_prefill_opus) returns output only without LSE. For the initial implementation, DCP>1 prefill falls back to the triton ragged path, which can be detrimental for performance. Otherwise, we may run into the issue of double counting attn sink for DCP>1. We can prototype and contribute this, once the initial implementation is finished and validated.
3) @baonudesifeizhai we are building on your #44573/#43809 work with co-authored credit on transplanted commits. Happy to collaborate if you're still interested.

### Feedback Period.

We are requesting a feedback period of ~1-2 weeks, as implementation is already underway. 

### CC List.

cc @tjtanaa @YukioZzz @okorzh-amd 


### Any Other Things.

_No response_

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.






## Design update (v2): 2026-09-22
After looking at the relative cache sizes, we decided to drop the #44573 shard-every-cache design. DSV4's SWA cache and compressor state rings are constant-size per request, and is not worth the tradeoff of sharding those in our opinion. v2 only shards the two MLAttentionSpec groups (compressed KV + indexer K), which is already sharded in the mainline and ongoing PRs. This makes the same design decision as the ongoing work in #56738.

Status update:
scheduler geometry (hybrid coordinator whitelist) -> DONE (#57382 
CP-aware compressed/indexer slot mappings -> DONE (#57239)
per-group worker block-table geometry -> DONE (#57239)
indexer top-k merge -> IN PROGRESS
attention wiring -> TODO
ROCm kernel LSE changes -> TODO

## Related work

- #44573 / #43809 : the original DSV4 DCP/PCP implementations (mechanism reference, design superseded per above)
- #51705 / #53598 : the merged K3 DCP foundation this builds on
- #56738 : DSV4.1 DCP on Model Runner V2 (NVIDIA FlashMLA, no prefix caching) -> complementary scope, same cache-placement design
- #57832 / #57840 / #57909 : MiniMax-M3 context-parallel indexers on ROCm
- #57858 / #57859 : candidate-only DSA indexer scorers on gfx950 -> composes with DCP shard-restricted scoring
- #56834 : ROCm mxfp4 indexer cache (DCP=1 gated; layout coordination needed if combined with DCP later)

title: [CI] Split (H100) V1 Attention into Sparse MLA, MLA Backends/Correctness, Dense/SSM, and DCP/ROCm jobs
body:
## What

Replace the two opaque `(H100) V1 Attention` whole-area shards with named jobs for Sparse MLA, MLA Backends, MLA Correctness, Dense and SSM, and DCP with ROCm Compatibility. Only the two large directories use pytest sharding; the remaining jobs run whole coverage units once.

## Old

```text
(H100) V1 Attention Shard %N [v1-attention-h100-mi300]
└── pytest v1/attention --num-shards=2
```

## New

| Buildkite job | key | whole coverage unit | replicas |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `(H100) V1 Attention / Sparse MLA Shard %N` | `v1-attention-h100-mi300` | `sparse_mla/` | 2 |
| `(H100) V1 Attention / MLA Backends` | `v1-attention-h100-mla-backends` | `mla/backends/` | 1 |
| `(H100) V1 Attention / MLA Correctness Shard %N` | `v1-attention-h100-mla-correctness` | `mla/correctness/` | 2 |
| `(H100) V1 Attention / Dense and SSM` | `v1-attention-h100-dense-ssm` | `dense/` + `ssm/` | 1 |
| `(H100) V1 Attention / DCP and ROCm Compatibility` | `v1-attention-h100-dcp-rocm` | `dcp/` + `rocm/` | 1 |

## Notes

- This PR is stacked on #57063; its CI changes touch `.buildkite/test_areas/attention.yaml` and `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml`.
- The existing key stays on Sparse MLA so the generated `amd-v1-attention-h100-mi300` mirror key remains stable.
- Mirror all five H100 groups on MI300 (seven workers including shards) and all six B200 groups on MI355 (eight workers). Matching smaller native AMD jobs replace both whole-area jobs, preserving each test once per hardware lane. AMD groups retain the existing source dependencies and use an 85-minute timeout, preserving the prior 40-minute allowance over the NVIDIA parent.
- The AMD follow-up changes no test bodies, parameters, assertions, skip marks, or NVIDIA job settings. Only AMD MLA Correctness jobs explicitly enable `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`; otherwise all 580 existing AITER correctness cases skip in the local environment. AI assistance was used.

## Expected runtime and overhead

| semantic job | replicas | prediction | main overhead cause |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Sparse MLA | 2 | under the per-replica target | checkout and container startup |
| MLA Backends | 1 | under the per-replica target | checkout and container startup |
| MLA Correctness | 2 | under the per-replica target | checkout and container startup |
| Dense and SSM | 1 | under the per-replica target | checkout and container startup |
| DCP and ROCm Compatibility | 1 | under the per-replica target | checkout and container startup |

This changes the H100 lane from two workers to seven. Existing per-file evidence supports this as the smallest named-job layout that keeps every job under the runtime target and predicts aggregate extra worker time within the 20-minute budget. Fresh scoped validation will measure the final job boundaries.

## AMD validation

This follow-up reorganizes the existing coverage from #42793, #49916, and #53351 within this PR. It replaces the broad AMD jobs rather than adding a second copy of their tests.

- Actual `pytest --collect-only -q` runs with each AMD job's paths, AITER setting, and shard flags verify all **4,514 cases exactly once per hardware lane**. Structural checks confirm all 11 mirrors match their native jobs and preserve NVIDIA definitions.
- `.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files .buildkite/test_areas/attention.yaml .buildkite/test-amd.yaml` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Targeted MI355 runtime validation: **1,219 passed, 35 skipped, five setup failures**. The five failures require the gated `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B` configuration; Hugging Face returned HTTP 401 before assertions, and that configuration was not cached locally.

Portable checks used `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q <scope> --timeout=120`, with each of these scopes under `tests/v1/attention/`: `mla/backends/`, `dcp/`, `rocm/`, `ssm/`, `sparse_mla/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py`, and `dense/test_chunked_local_attention.py`. Another 12 original MLA correctness cases ran with `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, covering DeepSeek/GLM dimensions, BF16/FP8 caches, scaled Q/K, decode/prefill/speculative batches, and all four chunked-context cases.

Runtime validation was targeted and used MI355; full-suite runtime, MI300 execution, and rendered AMD pipeline validation remain pending. Existing CUDA-only sparse/FlashInfer coverage gaps are unchanged. OpenAI Codex assisted with the AMD implementation and validation.

The current branch still contains the older six-group B200 layout from #57063. After rebasing onto that PR's latest combined layout, combine the corresponding MI355 short groups and repeat the coverage audit.

title: [Model][ROCm][DCP] DeepSeek-V4 decode context parallelism
body:
## Purpose

Model-layer DCP support for DeepSeek-V4 (hybrid SWA + compressed KV), per RFC #57228. Builds on the merged Kimi-K3 DCP framework from #51705 + #53598 and transplants the validated mechanisms from the inactive #44573 w/ co-author credit to @baonudesifeizhai. Adds onto current main, with ROCm/AITER leg being validated on 8xMI355X.

**Draft / WIP**: opened early for visibility and design alignment, not yet ready for review. Currently only contains the foundations for the functionality.

- [x] ContextParallelLayout + Triton ownership helpers (interleaved token/slot ownership, logical block table addressing)
- [x] DSV4 DCP merge ops: sink-after-merge via the consolidated v1/attention/ops/dcp.py collectives, compressor softmax reduce
- [x] Compressor partial-stats kernel (per-rank online-softmax pooling)
- [x] Compressor finalize kernels (owner-masked insert: compressed KV + indexer K caches)
- [x] Scheduler geometry: supports_context_parallel spec flag + logical_block_size composed with dcp_world_size_for_kv_cache_spec
- [x] Metadata localization (SWA / indexer / compressed slot mapping)
- [x] Attention wiring (gather-Q, sink-free local attend + LSE, merge) w/ C4A decode top-k localization fix
- [x] ROCm kernels: LSE + deferred sink in the sparse decode/prefill Triton kernels, Triton stable-topk twin for the indexer merge
- [x] Tests + parity (tp8 vs tp8×dcp{2,4,8}, passkey + GSM8K) + AgentX benchmark on 8x MI355X


## Not duplicating

#44573 is the direct ancestor of this PR (inactive since June, NVIDIA-only, before DCP framework consolidation). This PR series is it susccessors on the current main, validated and meant for ROCm. No other open PR or issue implements DSV4 DCP (checked 2026-09-16).

title: [ROCm] Add HiSparse Support on ROCm
body:
## Purpose

Enables HiSparse (#53781) on AMD ROCm/CDNA3+, tested on gfx950 (MI355X).

HiSparse keeps the bulk of the sparse-MLA KV cache in pinned host memory and
pulls only the indexer-selected rows back just in time, so long-context agentic
sessions stop getting preempted. #53781 landed it CUDA-only.

This PR enables for ROCm.

It also fixes **one bug in shared, platform-neutral code** that affects CUDA
equally — see *Platform-neutral fixes* below. That fix is the reason GLM-5.3
produces coherent output rather than garbage, and it is not ROCm-specific.

## Changes

### 1. HIP kernel port (`csrc/`)

The four fused HiSparse cache ops now build and run on ROCm. The port is
mechanical — vectorized copy widths, `__nv_bfloat16` → `hip_bfloat16`, and
warp-primitive shims added to `csrc/cuda_compat.h`. No algorithmic change; CUDA
codegen is unaffected.

### 2. ROCm backend wiring (`rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`)

The substantive work. Every CUDA HiSparse backend consumes a **dense**
`[tokens, topk]` index tensor plus `valid_counts`; AITER's tuned decode kernel
consumes a **ragged** flat list plus an indptr. Bridging that is the core of
this change:

- `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` accepts an `index_group_builder` and registers with
  it, which is what makes `mla_attention.py:575` pick up `hisparse_cache` and
  drive KV mirroring.
- Decode: `convert_decode_logical_to_physical_topk` → dense physical top-k →
  compacted to ragged → attention runs against `physical_kv_cache` (the hot
  buffer) instead of the paged KV cache.
- Prefill: mirrors the CUDA guard, staging host rows via `stage_prefill_rows`
  when the context is not fully resident. This is not optional — once a context
  has been offloaded, `all_context_pages_resident` is False and
  `index_group.py:232` asserts outright.
- AITER's persistent work-stealing metadata is disabled under HiSparse: its
  buffers are sized in `build()`, but HiSparse rewrites the indptr at forward
  time from resolver counts. Correctness first; noted as a perf follow-up.

One new Triton kernel, `compact_topk_to_ragged_triton`. The existing
`fetch_id_to_ragged_triton` was not reusable: a mid-row `-1` must *drop out*
rather than displace a valid entry.

**ROCm does not import the CUDA sparse module.** Following the precedent at
`xpu_mla_sparse.py:85-106`, this backend declares
`ROCMAiterMLASparsePrefillMetadata` locally.

### 3. Config gate (`vllm/config/vllm.py`)

Opens HiSparse for ROCm, with `fp8_ds_mla` (the 656-byte packed row) rejected
by name rather than failing deep in a kernel. Packed-layout support on ROCm is
a separate project. Every other platform keeps the existing rejection.

## Platform-neutral fixes

These are in shared code and (I think) would affect CUDA too. 

**`vllm/v1/hisparse/binding.py` — per-layer KV offset dropped.** Both bind
sites used `byte_offset=tensor_config.offset`, omitting the
`l * layer_stride` term the addressing contract requires
(`kv_cache_interface.py:1370`). `HiSparseHotSpec` and `HiSparseResidentSpec`
both return `has_layer_views = False`, so `allocate_kv_cache` hands every layer
in a group the whole raw slab and the per-layer term must be applied at bind
time. Without it **every layer in a hot group aliases the same KV region**. 
This is invisible to the existing e2e suite, which shrinks the model to 8
layers — that yields one-layer hot groups, where `l` is always 0 and the missing
term is exactly zero. Added `tests/v1/hisparse/test_layer_byte_offset.py` to 
remedy this. 

**`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/index_group.py` — event record does not
survive nested `torch.compile`.** `self.logical_topk_ready.record(...)` is
traceable, so Dynamo lowers it to a `torch.ops.streams.record_event` node whose
event lives in a process-global side table. `reset_user_object_tracking()`
clears that table on compile entry. vLLM nests compiles
(`CustomOp.maybe_compile` wraps `forward_native`), so an inner compile firing
during an outer graph's execution wipes the entry that graph's node depends on.
Replaced with an opaque custom op keyed by an integer group handle, so the
event never becomes a graph input.  Believe CUDA has not hit this only because 
its call path reaches `set_logical_topk_ready` from outside the compiled region.

**`vllm/distributed/.../hisparse/worker.py` — mirror guard for unbracketed
runs.** Warmup and profiling runs execute the model with the connector
disabled, so `start_step`/`finish_forward` never bracket them and
`_per_layer_mirrored` is never cleared between passes. The second warmup pass
then trips `RuntimeError: HiSparse layer 0 mirrored twice.` Added a
`_step_in_flight` flag so mirroring is skipped outside a real step. The
double-mirror check is unchanged inside a step.


## Test Plan

Hardware: MI355X (gfx950), ROCm, AITER.

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_hisparse_kernels.py           # kernel oracles
pytest tests/v1/hisparse/test_layer_byte_offset.py                # binding regression
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_index_group.py
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_ragged.py
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_sparse_import_boundary.py
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py
pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py
```

## Test Result

| Suite | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_hisparse_kernels.py` (oracles) | 16 passed, 76 skipped | **92 passed, 0 skipped** |
| upstream `-k hisparse` | 15 passed, 15 skipped | **28 passed, 2 skipped** |
| ROCm backend unit tests (5 files) | n/a | **71 passed** |
| `test_layer_byte_offset.py` | 3 failed, 2 passed | **5 passed** |
| `test_hisparse.py` (e2e) | skipped (CUDA-gated) | **2 passed** |


## Model Evaluation

GLM-5.3, TP4, full 78-layer model, greedy (`temperature=0`), Model Runner V2 in
both arms. MRV2 must be forced in the baseline too — HiSparse enables it
implicitly, and comparing against an MRV1 baseline reintroduces a confound.

| Prompt | HiSparse ON vs OFF |
|---|---|
| "The capital of France is" | identical ~27 tokens, then divergent filler; both correct |
| "Write one sentence explaining why the sky is blue." | identical throughout |
| "List the first five prime numbers:" | both `2, 3, 5, 7, 11` |

Divergence in trailing filler is expected: the hot-buffer decode path reorders
reductions. Bit-exactness is enforced at the kernel level by the oracle suite
above.

Before the `binding.py` fix, the same configuration produced a correct first
token followed by garbage:
`' Paris of  str of of\n\n1 - when B -11" E picture ...'`

Throughput benchmarking against a pure-CPU-offload baseline (mirroring the
GLM-5.3 hybrid-offloading blog post) is in progress and will be posted as a
follow-up comment.

## Limitations

- **`fp8_ds_mla` is not supported on ROCm** and is rejected with a clear error.
  bf16 and standard fp8 rows work — the HiSparse runtime is dtype-generic
  (`row_width` is a constructor parameter).
- **AITER's persistent work-stealing decode path is disabled under HiSparse.**
  Correctness first; a perf follow-up.
- **MTP under HiSparse on ROCm is untested.**
- **Cross-rank IPC events are unproven.** `Event(interprocess=True)` +
  `ipc_handle()` verified single-process on gfx950; TP>1 exercised end-to-end
  at TP4 without issue, but not isolated as its own test.
- Verified on gfx950 only. Other CDNA targets are untested.

---

*AI assistance was used in preparing this change.* All changes reviewed.

title: [LoRA] Add DeepSeek V4.1 text and vision adapter support
body:
## Purpose Resolve #57166 Enable LoRA for the DeepSeek V4.1 multimodal model, including its language model, vision tower, and connector. The multimodal wrapper currently lacks LoRA registration, while the grouped attention output projection and compressor projection call GEMMs directly and bypass adapter application. - Register the supported packed projections and multimodal module mapping, excluding the MTP draft head from adaptation. - Apply the grouped output projection's LoRA contribution for both BF16 and FP8 base weights, including gathering LoRA-A for fully sharded adapters. Add the compressor's adapter contribution while preserving the base GEMM's FP32 output. - Scope tower and connector adapter metadata to each image using its original batch index, including when images are distributed across TP ranks. Restore batch metadata after encoding, including on exceptions. Count only the patch rows processed by each module, excluding image-span delimiters. - Avoid retaining temporary single-slice adapter tensors in the Triton pointer caches. Add regression coverage in the existing LoRA test files. ## Test Plan - Write and run newly added test cases - End to end test with verl LoRA RL using Megatron backend https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/pull/6199 ## Test Result - Test cases pass ---

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoE] Fix AITER MoE routing fallback to eager torch.topk for scoring_func=softmax
body:
## Purpose

MoE token routing in `fused_topk_bias()` falls back to the slow, unfused eager `torch.topk` path whenever AITER MoE fusion is enabled (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1`) and `scoring_func != "sigmoid"`.

**Root cause:** the routing dispatch only had a fused fast path for `scoring_func == "sigmoid"` (via `rocm_aiter_ops.biased_grouped_topk`) and `"sqrtsoftplus"` (via `dsv4_topk`). Any other case -- notably `"softmax"`, used by classic/DeepSeek-V3-style MoE routing -- falls through every dispatch branch to a fully eager PyTorch implementation (`softmax()` + `torch.topk()` + `.gather()`), even though vLLM already ships a fused `vllm_topk_softmax` kernel for this exact case (already used on the non-AITER path).


**Fix:** add an explicit dispatch branch for `scoring_func == "softmax"` that routes to the existing fused `vllm_topk_softmax` kernel before falling through to the eager path. This is a routing-logic fix only,  no new kernel code, just correcting which existing, already-tested kernel gets called.

**Known follow-up (out of scope here):** `scoring_func == "sigmoid"` with `topk < num_expert_group` still falls through to the eager path both before and after this fix; left untouched to keep this PR minimal.

## Test Plan

Added `test_fused_topk_bias_softmax_dispatches_to_fused_kernel_under_aiter` in `tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py`, which mocks `rocm_aiter_ops.is_fused_moe_enabled() == True` and asserts `vllm_topk_softmax` is called (not eager `torch.topk`) for
`scoring_func="softmax"`.

## Test Result

Full test suite on real MI350 (gfx950) hardware: **721 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, including the new regression test above.

Direct microbenchmark (`num_tokens=4096, hidden_size=8192, num_experts=128, topk=8`, bf16, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1`):

| Path | Latency |
|---|---|
| eager `torch.topk` (before fix) | 0.0546 ms/call |
| fused `vllm_topk_softmax` (after fix) | 0.0130 ms/call |

**4.19x speedup** on the routing call itself.

---

title: [Bug][ROCm] Nightly af1c01499: GLM-5.3-Flash cannot boot — ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl missing record_logical_topk_ready + jit-warmup tilelang crash
body:
## Nightly `af1c01499` (2026-09-16): two boot regressions for GLM-5.3-Flash on ROCm — model cannot start

Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-af1c01499b289be555c475669ba50a88e96d846e` (`vllm 0.29.1rc1.dev187+gaf1c01499`), 8×MI350X, TP8, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, serving `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`.

### Regression 1: `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` missing `record_logical_topk_ready`

```
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py", line 235, in forward
    self.mla_attn.impl.record_logical_topk_ready()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
AttributeError: 'ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl' object has no attribute 'record_logical_topk_ready'
```

`mla.py:235` calls the new `record_logical_topk_ready()` API (defined on the base sparse impl in `sparse_mla_attention.py:717`), but `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py:756`) doesn't implement or inherit it. Engine dies at first forward.

Workaround: add a no-op `record_logical_topk_ready` to `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl`.

### Regression 2: JIT kernel warmup crash — `'function' object has no attribute 'compile'`

```
File "vllm/model_executor/warmup/jit_warmup_tilelang_helper.py", line 141, in launch
    compiled = jit_impl.compile(*args, **kwargs)
AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'compile'
```

The new `--kernel-config` jit-warmup subsystem (on by default, `enable_jit_warmup: bool = True`) crashes in the tilelang helper on this path. All 8 workers die at `JIT kernel warmup starting`.

Workaround: `--kernel-config '{"enable_jit_warmup": false}'`.

With both workarounds the model boots and serves (and for us it also carried the `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` fix for the 16K-chunk fault in #57227). Both regressions block any GLM-5.3-Flash ROCm serving on the nightly.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Add record_logical_topk_ready to ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl (GLM-5.3-Flash boot crash)
body:
## Why this is not duplicating #56604

#56604 (open since 2026-09-12) fixes the same crash class by adding a **default no-op `record_logical_topk_ready` on the `MLAAttentionImpl` base class** in `vllm/v1/attention/backend.py`, so every backend silently inherits it.

This PR instead adds the method **on `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` itself**, mirroring the existing `SparseMLACommonImpl` contract (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/sparse_mla_attention.py:717`): impls that participate in sparse-MLA index groups implement the hook with real semantics; impls that don't declare an explicit no-op at their own site.

Trade-off: the base-class default in #56604 is broader (also covers any other backend that skips `SparseMLACommonImpl`) but weakens the interface — a new sparse backend that *should* implement index-group notification would silently no-op instead of failing loudly. This PR keeps that failure loud and fixes the one backend that currently crashes (ROCm AITER sparse MLA, GLM-5.3-Flash on MI350X). Either fix resolves the boot regression in #57248; happy to withdraw this in favor of #56604 if maintainers prefer the base-class default.

## Description

`MLAAttention.forward` calls `impl.record_logical_topk_ready()` on every sparse layer (`vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py:235`). `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` inherits `SharedTopkIndicesBuffer` directly (not `SparseMLACommonImpl`) and never gained the method, so serving GLM-5.3-Flash on ROCm (gfx950, `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`) crashes at the first forward with `AttributeError: 'ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl' object has no attribute 'record_logical_topk_ready'`.

This impl shares the top-k indices buffer via `SharedTopkIndicesBuffer` but does not participate in `SparseMLAIndexGroup` host-side prefetching, so the correct implementation is a no-op.

Fixes the first boot regression in #57248.

## Test commands run and results

- Reproduced on the cluster before the fix: nightly `af1c01499` on 8×MI350X TP8, engine dies at first forward with the AttributeError above.
- With the equivalent no-op method patched in-pod (same 5-line change), the model boots and serves; combined with `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` it passes the full chunked-prefill repro suite with zero faults (details in #57227).
- `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(...)"` — syntax OK; AST check confirms the method is now on the class.
- No GPU/ROCm environment is available in CI for the full path, so no new automated test is added here; #56604 already adds an interface-level test (`tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_topk_ready_hook.py`) that covers this method's presence on backends.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Hermes Agent). The change was reviewed and validated end-to-end on the affected hardware by the submitter: the same no-op patch was applied in-pod on the MI350X cluster and confirmed to resolve the crash.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Resolve stripped special-token terminals without holding the stream
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57232

With an engine-based tool parser, no reasoning parser and a request without tools, the renderer never calls `adjust_request()`, so `skip_special_tokens` stays `True` and the detokenizer strips the reasoning markers from `delta_text`. `TokenIDScanner` then defers the marker terminal and waits for text that never arrives: every later delta is held, and at `finish()` the deferred terminals are flushed after the held text with text decoded from their ids, which the `skip_reasoning_parsing` bypass from #47562 emits as content. On the wire the stream returns nothing until the last delta, and that delta ends with the stripped markers.

This is not gemma4-specific. The same shape on `qwen3_coder`, `deepseek_v4`, `qwen3_xml` and `minimax_m2` (`<think>`/`</think>` ids, no reasoning parser, `skip_special_tokens=True`) returns `plananswer<think></think>` on main.

Fix: the scanner receives the terminal ids the tokenizer strips (`all_special_ids`) and the request's `skip_special_tokens`. A deferred terminal that can never receive text is resolved text-less at the next delta, or at finish, in token order. Hold-back deferral for text that may still arrive is unchanged. This changes `engine/` rather than `gemma4.py` because the behavior is wrong for every engine parser.

Three test fixtures streamed special-token text under a request that still said `skip_special_tokens=True`. Serving never produces that shape, since `adjust_request()` clears the flag before such text reaches a parser, so those fixtures now clear it (`replay_harness.py`, `test_gemma4_streaming_reasoning.py`, `tests/parser/test_streaming.py`).

### Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

#57247 fixes the gemma4 half inside `Gemma4Parser._preprocess_feed` and also covers #57231. I tested its head (`0c51215a7`): the gemma4 rows are fixed there, but the four other engine parsers above still return `plananswer<think></think>`, because the deferral lives in the scanner. This PR is the engine-level half, does not touch `gemma4.py`, and does not claim #57231. Duplicate checks (`gh pr list --search "57232 in:body"` and area keyword searches) were run before pushing; #57247 is the only related open PR.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine -q
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files <8 changed files>
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <8 changed files>
# reporter's probe from the issue (gist sha256 57b5a5cf...), google/gemma-4-E2B-it tokenizer, no weights
PYTHONPATH=$PWD .venv/bin/python probe_gemma4_unpaired.py
```

## Test Result

- `tests/parser/engine`: 4321 passed, 0 failed on this branch (7 tests added). The three new behavioral tests fail on main; the scanner tests error on main because the new constructor argument does not exist there.
- Reporter's probe, real Gemma 4 tokenizer, 25 rows:

| Row | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 15 (no tools, closer, per-token) | `work it out: 17*23the answer is 391<channel\|>` | `work it out: 17*23the answer is 391` |
| 19 (no tools, thinking, per-token) | `thought\nwork it out: 17*23the answer is 391<\|channel><channel\|>` | `thought\nwork it out: 17*23the answer is 391` |
| 1–13, 24, 25 (requests with tools) | baseline | identical to main at the delta level |

  Text now arrives per delta instead of in one delta at finish. Row 21 (bypass forced off, markers stripped) now splits reasoning/content correctly instead of holding all 21 deltas. Row 22 still starts with the synthetic `<|channel>` from `_preprocess_feed`; that is #57231 and is left to #57247.
- Lint: ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy 3.10 and mypy 3.12 pass.
- Environment: macOS, M4 Pro, Python 3.12, no CUDA, pure-Python parser path. On this machine `tests/reasoning`, `tests/tool_parsers` and `tests/parser/test_streaming.py` segfault under pytest on unmodified main as well, so CI needs to cover them; the `test_streaming.py` fixture edit was made on reasoning alone.

AI assistance was used (Claude Code) for the investigation, the code, the tests and the measurements. I directed the work, reviewed every changed line, and ran the commands above on my machine.
