title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Project sequence shards before all-gather
body:
## Purpose

With DeepSeek-V4.1 sequence parallelism, every TP rank currently gathers the full hidden states and repeats the same attention input projections. This change computes the replicated Q-latent/KV, compressor-score, and indexer-weight projections on each rank's token shard, then gathers their outputs. It removes redundant projection work and reduces communicated bytes while preserving the residual/mHC ordering and downstream TP-sharded projections.

Enabled by default when sequence parallelism is active; no environment flag is needed. The existing path remains below 256 scheduled tokens and with ubatching, LoRA, speculation, or batch invariance. Dispatch uses the captured token count, not actual KV length. No new communication kernel or FlashInfer source changes are introduced.

Duplicate checks found no open PR for this DSV4.1 projection reorder. #57021 fuses the output GEMM with reduce-scatter; this PR neither includes nor depends on it. #54151 pipelines Kimi-K3 all-gather/GEMM; this change instead moves replicated DSV4.1 input projections before the gather. Searches included `57021 in:body`, `54151 in:body`, `DeepSeek projection gather`, `projection-before-AG`, and replicated DeepSeek projections; both related PR discussions were read.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_projected_all_gather.py -q -rs
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/attention.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_projected_all_gather.py
```

The focused CPU test exercises the production attention forward with simulated collectives: disabled/small-batch fallback, the 256-token boundary, padded sequence shards, all optional compressor/indexer combinations, and BF16/FP32 output dtypes. It does not substitute for distributed numerical validation.

The final default-on evaluation uses the server below. Its baseline is the archived run on original PR commit `238c80dd0e` with projected gather disabled; that baseline uses the same checkpoint, native runtime and serving/evaluation settings. The earlier flag no longer exists on the current head:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=0 \
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve \
  deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --revision dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277 \
  --served-model-name dsv41-gsm8k --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8003 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --kernel-config '{"sparse_indexer_topk_backend":"deep_select"}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --no-enable-prefix-caching --language-model-only \
  --generation-config vllm --seed 123 --enable-logging-iteration-details \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"thinking":false}' \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'

.venv/bin/python -m lm_eval run --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args 'model=dsv41-gsm8k,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8003/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,timeout=600,max_retries=2,max_gen_toks=1024,max_length=16384,seed=123' \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=1024 temperature=0.0 do_sample=False "chat_template_kwargs={'thinking': False}" \
  --seed 123,123,123,123 --log_samples --output_path ./gsm8k-default
```

## Validation

- **24 tests passed** on final default-on/256-token commit `2c32c5300a`; all applicable pre-commit hooks passed.
- Fresh full GSM8K on final default-on/256-token commit `2c32c5300a`: **1267/1319 (96.058%)**, versus archived AG-off baseline **1265/1319 (95.906%)** on `238c80dd0e`. Eleven answers improved and nine regressed; this is not an accuracy-gain claim. Strict match: 1038 versus 1036. Documents, prompts, targets and arguments match; zero empty responses. Scheduler logs confirm 962 candidate iterations at or above 256 tokens and 1477 below, reaching 8192 tokens, so both the new path and fallback are exercised.
- Earlier standalone AG-only full GSM8K on `238c80dd0e` with the original 2048-token cutoff: **1265/1319 (95.906%) baseline; 1267/1319 (96.058%) candidate** (flexible extraction). Nine improved and seven regressed; not an accuracy-gain claim. Documents, prompts, targets and arguments matched; no empty responses. Both arms exercised large batches up to 8192 tokens. This is prior validation, not the result for the new cutoff.
- Native runtime: published wheel `929aa2a7ed`; native build inputs (`csrc`, `cmake`, `setup.py`, DeepGEMM installer) match PR base `62f9482583`.

## Token cutoff and performance

Full-forward measurements on four GB200 GPUs, TP4/DP1/EP4, native MegaMoE, FlashInfer FP8 attention, MXFP4 indexer and DeepSelect. Single-sequence prefill with 100K target KV and a fixed 1M model limit. Both arms use the standalone PR implementation with GEMM-RS/AR and other experimental optimizations absent; a benchmark-only override selects the path at each token count. The production code has no opt-in flag.

| Scheduled tokens | Baseline ms | Project before AG ms | Latency reduction |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 128 | 16.7895 | 16.7962 | -0.04% |
| 256 | 19.4081 | 19.2921 | 0.60% |
| 512 | 22.6549 | 22.3702 | 1.26% |
| 1,024 | 29.0403 | 28.2825 | 2.61% |
| 2,048 | 44.8942 | 42.6755 | 4.94% |
| 4,096 | 72.4893 | 69.2494 | 4.47% |
| 8,192 | 128.4496 | 123.5147 | 3.84% |
| 16,384 | 246.3443 | 235.2476 | 4.50% |

The 128-token case is tied within noise. The first measured benefit is at 256, followed by larger gains at 512 and above, so the cutoff is **256 tokens**. This is an empirical cutoff for TP4/EP4 on GB200, not a universal crossover claim for every GPU/parallelism setting.

Each point uses ten samples of repeated FULL graph replays. The refined 256/512 cases use 90 seconds warmup and 500 replays/sample; 4K uses 45 seconds and 100; 8K/16K use 45 seconds and 50. All refined pairs have matching expert routing and common GEMM tactics, CV below 0.91%, and zero eager/graph/replay error. The initial 128/1K/2K pairs also match routing/tactics with CV below 1.73%; all samples, including outliers, are retained. Model source was `9babf6cb1d`, harness `1bf76c661d`, refined probe `94924dc928` (initial probe `bf97644880`).

All 40 eligible layers are checked against gather-before-project. The audit uses atol 2e-4/rtol 5e-3, also permitting adjacent BF16 values, plus relative RMS <=0.005 for every output; FP32 retains the strict bounds. One 4K BF16 element failed the original bound. An FP64 dot-product check on saved input/weight tensors showed the candidate was correctly rounded and the baseline was the adjacent BF16 value near a rounding midpoint. The original failed result is retained; this is not hidden by dropping a sample.

## Memory

**No additional projection weights:** the affected replicated projections occupy **398.4375 MiB/GPU in both arms** (unique parameter/buffer storage measured). They were already replicated before this change (`disable_tp=True`/`ReplicatedLinear`). Additional memory comes from changed activation and communication buffer lifetimes/allocation, not weight replication.

Fresh-process measurements select each arm before model initialization and inspect all four ranks after every timed batch. The table reports live tensors outside the measured graph plus its entire private allocator pool, including graph-resident reusable buffers. It excludes transient setup peaks and ordinary allocator cache; these full-forward graph measurements are not a universal eager/piecewise serving-memory surcharge.

| Tokens | Change in graph/tensor memory per GPU |
| ---: | ---: |
| 256 | +2.00 MiB |
| 512 | -17.25 MiB |
| 4,096 | +276.70 MiB |
| 8,192 | -24.00 MiB |
| 16,384 | -48.00 MiB |

The real GSM8K serving configuration also reports unchanged model-loading memory (**72.14 GiB/GPU**) and identical graph-capture memory records (**1.14 GiB** and **0.49 GiB** per rank for the two capture phases). Available KV-cache memory is effectively unchanged: 90.22 GiB baseline and 90.23 GiB candidate. These decode captures top out at 128 tokens, below the cutoff; this observation does not replace the large-prefill graph measurements above.

At 4K, the graph pool grows by 276 MiB and other live tensors by 0.704 MiB. The non-monotonic result across shapes reflects graph allocation/buffer lifetimes; it should not be extrapolated as a fixed per-token cost.

AI assistance: Codex prepared the implementation and ran these checks at the human author's direction. The human submitter confirmed reviewing every changed line and running relevant tests for original commit `238c80dd0e` before submission. The default-on and measured-cutoff revisions were subsequently requested by the human author; this draft does not claim a second human review of those new lines.

title: [Frontend] Upgrade XGrammar to 0.2.7 and Rust structural tags to 0.3.0
body:
## Purpose

Pin the shared Python frontend/engine dependency to `xgrammar==0.2.7` and regenerate the CPU, CUDA, ROCm, and XPU test lockfiles. The CPU lockfile also updates `apache-tvm-ffi` to satisfy XGrammar's minimum version.

Use the upstream `deepseek_v4_1` structural-tag builder through the standard builtin route, removing the local wrapper and older-version fallback. This makes V4.1 parameter-schema enforcement consistently available. The CLI parser name remains `deepseek_v41`; serving continues to pass `reasoning=False` because the engine owns the reasoning boundary. Existing tests cover required/named/strict-auto choices, invalid parameters, and non-strict parallel calls.

Upgrade Rust `xgrammar-structural-tag` to 0.3.0, which tracks XGrammar 0.2.7. Adapt the local Kimi K3 builder to `ReasoningMode`, preserving its enabled/disabled behavior and handling the new auto mode. Refresh Kimi K3 and HY serialization snapshots for the updated structural-tag format; token and character budgets remain unset.

Replace Rust's local DeepSeek V4.1 builder with `Model::DeepSeekV41.builder()`, enabling parameter-schema enforcement through `deepseek_v4_1_xml`. Kimi K3 keeps its handwritten typed-argument grammar, including type/value correlation and marker-safe enum handling, alongside its existing channel framing and raw-JSON argument branch.

Related to #54497's dependency-upgrade proposal. Its `max_whitespace_cnt` configuration plumbing is separate work. A search of open XGrammar upgrade PRs, 0.2.7 references, and #54497 references found no overlapping implementation. #56408 already added conditional use of the upstream V4.1 builder; this change makes that dependency available consistently and removes the compatibility path.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py

.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  requirements/common.txt \
  requirements/test/cpu.txt requirements/test/cuda.txt \
  requirements/test/rocm.txt requirements/test/xpu.txt \
  vllm/tool_parsers/structural_tag_registry.py \
  vllm/tool_parsers/deepseekv41_engine_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py

.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  rust/src/parser/src/tool/deepseek_dsml/deepseek_v41.rs \
  rust/src/parser/src/tool/deepseek_dsml/deepseek_v41/tests.rs \
  rust/src/parser/src/unified/kimi_k3/structural_tag.rs

cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all --check
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml \
  --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml \
  -p vllm-parser --all-features --locked
```

## Test Result

- Final builder-routing and DeepSeek V4.1 parser suites: **109 passed** with XGrammar 0.2.7.
- Final Rust parser suite: **457 passed, 0 skipped**. Workspace Clippy with all targets/features and warnings denied passed during the upgrade; final formatting checks passed.
- A temporary local Rust exporter and Python XGrammar 0.2.7 matcher harness verified **40 DeepSeek V4.1 cases**, covering auto/required/named choices, strict opt-out, `any_order`, missing/duplicate/invalid parameters, enums, nested references, and integer/null unions. This supplemental harness is outside the repository.
- Additional validation during the upgrade passed for structured-output request validation, stop-token masking, regex compilation timeouts, structured-output manager behavior, and Cohere structural tags. The manager suite retained one existing Guidance xfail.
- Pre-commit passed, including requirement-lock regeneration, Ruff, and type checking; `git diff --check` passed.
- Validation used Python 3.12 on Linux aarch64 with existing precompiled vLLM extensions, Torch 2.11.0, and Transformers 5.11.0. CPU grammar/parser tests were run; GPU model generation and accuracy evaluations remain pending.

AI assistance: Codex implemented the changes, ran local validation, and prepared the PR for review.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Compact large decoder prefills with a dependency-preserving halo
body:
## Summary

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash processes the full prompt through layers 21-39 even though
those layers reuse the encoder's global KV and have only a 128-token causal
sliding window. This opt-in retains enough earlier rows to preserve their causal
dependencies, redistributes sequence-parallel states once, and reuses the compact
attention metadata across the suffix.

```text
ASIS
encoder 0..20: full prompt + global KV
        |
decoder 21..39: full prompt at every layer
        |
final sampled rows
```

```text
PR
encoder 0..20: full prompt + unchanged global KV
        |
select each request's dependency halo (2414 -> aligned 2560 rows)
        |
one SP state exchange + private compact metadata
        |
decoder 21..39: reuse the fixed compact layout
        |
restore retained rows to the sampling layout
```

The retained halo is `window + (decoder_depth - 1) * (window - 1)`, rounded up to
256 rows. It preserves the final query output's dependencies and every layer's
trailing cache inputs across chunked prefill and decode. Different GEMM/MoE
shapes can still change floating-point rounding; this is not a bitwise-output
claim.

Batches below 16384 scheduled tokens, decode/captured batches, requests for
prompt logprobs, and batches with no trimmable queries use the full path.
Unsupported topology/feature combinations are rejected. The initial scope is
text MRV2, DP1/PP1, uniform-window Mega attention, no CP/DBO/speculation/APC/LoRA.
See the added design document for the full scope and launch example.

This differs from #56752: that PR keeps a 128-token replay window, changes the
cold-prefill attention contract, and excludes sequence parallelism. This change
keeps the full multilayer dependency halo and validates TP4/EP4 SP. #56986 caches
BF16 main-KV gathers across decoder groups; it does not remove decoder query rows.
#57021 targets output-GEMM/reduce-scatter fusion and is independent.

## Performance

Base `5efbf0886a7110ae0801b9540e3072e89a23eb36`, candidate `dec8e010e05e00dd920aa941e740f8e99176be3b`.

| Prompt | Batch | Full prefill tok/s | Fixed tail tok/s | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8192 | 1 | 107.05 | 106.58 | -0.44% |
| 8192 | 16 | 518.31 | 662.40 | +27.80% |
| 8192 | 64 | 645.93 | 875.96 | +35.61% |
| Mixed 512/2048/8192 | 24 | 1026.10 | 1197.35 | +16.69% |
| 512 | 16 | 1596.31 | 1594.10 | -0.14% |

Matched full/fixed-tail modes in the same loaded model: GB200 TP4/EP4, MRV2,
normal decode graphs, 32768 scheduled-token budget, max 64 requests, APC off,
4 GiB KV per rank, varied document prompts, 64 forced output tokens, two warmups
and three measured repetitions per arm. B64 repeats in ABBA order. Prompt hashes
and scheduler signatures match in every pair; there were no preemptions.

Both arms use Torch 2.13.0+cu130 and the coherent DeepGEMM 2.8.0 package
from native wheel `3bb7826` (DeepGEMM pin `ad1f172`), held fixed between modes.
The tested source base's default DeepGEMM pin is `a6bbb80`; the exact dependency
and native-source compatibility checks are recorded in the evidence.

The larger scheduling budget is material. At an 8192-token budget the original
shrinking-tail implementation lost 6-28% throughput. Reusing a fixed halo removed
most of that overhead, but small batches remained launch-bound, motivating the
minimum-token gate. No HTTP-serving or general hardware speedup claim is made.

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_tail.py -q`: 12 passed.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks and Python 3.12 mypy.
- Exact heterogeneous SP transport checks at TP2/TP4, including empty sender ranks.
- Arithmetic canaries, 8192/8193-token retrieval and decode continuation,
  simultaneous long-prompt retrieval, and prompt-logprob fallback.
- Pinned five-shot GSM8K subset, plus paired eight-question evaluation with
  8192-token prompts to exercise the compacted path. Current-main short subset: 31/32; long-context paired subset: control 8/8 and candidate 8/8, no truncation, with the compacted route confirmed active.

Evidence, source/runtime provenance, exact prompts/scheduler signatures, and
rerun commands: [pinned evidence](https://github.com/foraxe/vllm/tree/e98f65b4f4039e6c4ebcd804d80295f1124972b7/evidence/dsv41-fixed-decoder-tail).

AI assistance was used for implementation and validation. The submitting human
confirmed review of the final changes and a relevant test rerun before submission.

title: [ROCm] Add head-fused HIP sparse MLA decode kernel for gfx950
body:
## Purpose

Add head-fused HIP sparse MLA decode kernel for MI355X (gfx950). The kernel groups MQA heads (HG=2) so each token's KV latent is loaded once and reused across heads, cutting KV read traffic ~2x vs the per-head Triton path. Targets DSpark spec-decode batch range B=33-72 (C=8 → B=48 for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash).

Gated behind `VLLM_ROCM_USE_HIP_SPARSE_MLA=1` env var — opt-in, zero impact when disabled. Falls through to existing Triton ragged decode outside the dispatch range.

## Test Plan

1. Build kernel: `hipcc -x hip --offload-arch=gfx950 -O3 -std=c++17 -fPIC -shared csrc/rocm/mla/sparse_mla_decode_m5.hip -o libsmla_m5.so`
2. Set env vars: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_HIP_SPARSE_MLA=1 VLLM_ROCM_HIP_SPARSE_MLA_M5_SO=<path>/libsmla_m5.so`
3. Microbench: rocprofv3 kernel trace at B=48/64, verify device time < Triton baseline
4. E2E: 3600s agentx bench on MI355X TP=4 C=8 with MTP spec-decode (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash)
5. Fallback: unset env var, verify Triton path fires unchanged

## Test Result

**Microbench (rocprofv3, MI355X gfx950):**

| Batch | M5 (µs) | Triton (µs) | Speedup |
|-------|---------|-------------|---------|
| B=48  | 9.9     | 12.4        | 1.25x   |
| B=64  | 10.1    | 13.9        | 1.38x   |

SNR vs Triton reference: 51.77 dB at B=48.

**E2E (agentx, 3600s, C=8, TP=4, MTP spec-decode, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MI355X):**

| Metric | Baseline | With M5 | Delta |
|--------|----------|---------|-------|
| P90 Interactivity (tok/s/user) | 139.5 | 146.6 | **+5.1%** |
| P90 TTFT (s) | 1.067 | 0.970 | **−9.1%** |
| Output tok/s/chip | 93.0 | 93.7 | +0.8% |

title: [Bugfix] Isolate supplemental FlashInfer BF16 autotuning
body:
## Purpose

The supplemental 32-token FlashInfer BF16 warmup currently applies its bounded `tuning_buckets` to every operation in the dummy run. An MXFP8 drafter GEMM with M=40 can consequently inherit the BF16 bucket cap and reuse a low-M tactic that does not support its input.

Run this supplemental pass after the full-model autotune context exits. Only `flashinfer_bf16_mm` enables tuning and installs the BF16 buckets; other operations execute using their normal cache lookup or fallback. Preserve the existing token-count helper's default behavior while excluding the supplemental BF16 pass from the full-op loop. Deferred-MoE tuning retains its own pass even when its token limit is also 32. Skip-op controls, HiSparse skip-attention, distributed tuning and cache persistence remain in effect.

This isolates the BF16 supplemental pass; it does not change the bucket policy of full-model/deferred-MoE passes or provide a general cached-tactic validity fix. Related: #50572, #55377 and https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5269.

Duplicate-work checks found no equivalent isolation fix. #54524 changes default BF16 backend selection, while #55671 migrates autotune cache persistence; neither isolates the supplemental BF16 tuning context.

## Test Plan

```bash
pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/utils/flashinfer.py \
  vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py
```

Existing repository pytest targets (not added or modified by this PR; the full pytest run was not completed):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py \
  tests/kernels/test_flashinfer_bf16_gemm.py -q
```

## Test Result

- The two modified files passed Ruff, formatting and mypy for Python 3.10–3.13 in a clean tracked-files snapshot. `git diff --check` passed. Repository-wide pre-commit also reports pre-existing EC connector docstring/formatting issues; those unrelated files are intentionally unchanged by this PR.

**Single-GPU validation on PR head `16964585e3`:** NVIDIA B200, torch 2.13.0+cu130, CuTe DSL 4.7.0, FlashInfer source at `d3ad3b1387078a61f846df91e07bbdad8fb70df6`. Standalone probes execute the changed vLLM source functions with real FlashInfer autotuning and CUDA kernels, bypassing unrelated vLLM package imports. These are local validation scripts, not committed tests in this PR. The results below are from those probes, not from the repository pytest command above.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| BF16 supplemental tuning | Exactly `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32]`; M=32 numerical comparison passed. The existing vLLM BF16 eligibility predicate accepts M=32 and rejects M=33/8192 for this CuTeDSL path. |
| MXFP8 full warmup | Completed all 21 buckets through M=8192. At `(M,N,K)=(8192,1792,5120)`, the selected tactic produced finite output with cosine similarity **0.99930** against the PyTorch reference. |
| MXFP8 inside the BF16-only pass | M=8192 remained mapped to bucket **8192**, reused the same winning tactic with autotuning disabled, and retained cosine similarity **0.99930**. It did not inherit the BF16 cap of 32. |

Separate checks passed for existing token-count behavior, skip-op propagation and exception-state restoration. The earlier M=40 scope check also confirmed that MXFP8 maps to bucket 64 during the BF16-only pass.

Full pytest collection was blocked by missing `tblib` in the available environment. The probes are not a full vLLM pytest run. End-to-end serving/model evaluation has not been run.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix DeepSeek V4.1 graph capture on gfx942
body:
## Motivation

On 4× MI325X (gfx942), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash consistently segfaults during the second FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graph-capture pass on the latest vllm nightly image -> `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-af1c01499b289be555c475669ba50a88e96d846e`

FULL_DECODE_ONLY and --enforce-eager start successfully. AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3 also makes FULL_AND_PIECEWISE reliable, indicating an asynchronous stream race.

## Suggested Fix

Disable the DeepSeek-V4.1 auxiliary attention streams on gfx942:


```
aux_stream_list = (
    None if on_gfx942() else [torch.cuda.Stream() for _ in range(3)]
)
```

Other ROCm architectures and CUDA retain the existing multi-stream path.

## Explanation

The V4.1 target model creates three auxiliary streams, while its ROCm MTP path already executes this work serially. On gfx942, asynchronous work from these streams can overlap PIECEWISE graph capture and cause a native worker segfault.

With auxiliary streams disabled only on gfx942, the real TP4 checkpoint completed all PIECEWISE and FULL graph captures, reached readiness, and handled concurrent prefill and decode requests. Neither --enforce-eager nor global kernel serialization was required.

After the fix the server completed FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graph capture, reached readiness, and successfully handled both standalone prompts and concurrent prefill/decode requests with coherent outputs.

## Reproduction / Validation Command

Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-af1c01499b289be555c475669ba50a88e96d846e`


Environment Vars:

```
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
```

Serving command:

```
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --port 8100 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-model-len 262144 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --mm-processor-cache-type shm \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}'
```

title: [AMD][Bugfix] Make the nested-RoPE patch reach automatic validation
body:
## Summary

Two spec-decode checkpoints fail to load at the same line, for two unrelated reasons:

```
AttributeError: 'float' object has no attribute 'get'    # poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-NVFP4
AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'      # deepseek-ai/dspark_gemma4_12b_block7
  transformers/modeling_rope_utils.py:850, in validate_rope
```

`validate_rope` treats a `rope_parameters` mapping as nested whenever the config declares `layer_types` and any top-level key appears in it, then iterates **all** of the mapping's values, guarding only against `None`. Any non-dict entry next to the per-layer dicts therefore raises, and the reported type is just whichever stray the iterator reaches first.

**Two producers, and only one is a malformed config.**

- `deepseek-ai/dspark_gemma4_12b_block7` ships the strays itself: its `config.json` stores `"rope_type": "default"` and `"rope_theta": null` beside the `full_attention` / `sliding_attention` dicts. `Gemma4TextConfig` overrides `convert_rope_params_to_dict` with a bare `return kwargs` — one of six config classes in transformers 5.17 that do (`DiffusionGemmaTextConfig`, `Gemma4TextConfig`, `Gemma4UnifiedTextConfig`, `LagunaConfig`, `MellumConfig`, `MiMoV2FlashConfig`) — so neither it nor `standardize_rope_params` ever runs to normalize them.
- `poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-NVFP4`'s checkpoint is clean: its `rope_parameters` holds only the two per-layer dicts. The stray is injected at load time. The repo ships remote code (`auto_map` → `configuration_laguna.LagunaConfig`, under `trust_remote_code=True`) which inherits the base `convert_rope_params_to_dict`, and that does a flat `rope_parameters.setdefault("rope_theta", ...)` without checking for the nested shape; `standardize_rope_params` Case 2 then only walks `set(layer_types)`, so it never removes it again.

**The existing workaround does not run on the path that needs it.** `huggingface_hub`'s `@strict` decorator snapshots every `validate_*` method into `__class_validators__` at class creation, and automatic post-`__init__` validation dispatches off that snapshot rather than off the class attribute. Assigning `PretrainedConfig.validate_rope` therefore only affects explicit `config.validate_rope()` calls — which is why `laguna` fails today *even though its `model_type` is already in the allowlist*. That list is not unique to `PreTrainedConfig` either: transformers decorates individual config classes with `@strict` and each owns a separate snapshot.

## Changes

- Add `_install_hf_config_validator`, which sets the class attribute and then walks the loaded `PretrainedConfig` subclass tree, rewriting each `__class_validators__` snapshot that still holds the superseded function. Matching is by **identity**, so a genuine per-model override such as `DeepseekV4Config.validate_rope` is left in place. Classes imported later snapshot the patched function themselves.
- Route **both** rope patches through it. Routing the `sarvam_mla` shim is load-bearing rather than tidiness: if it keeps the plain assignment, a later nested-rope patch supersedes a function that is in no snapshot and the rewrite silently has no effect.
- Add `gemma4_text` to `_PATCH_HF_NESTED_ROPE_VALIDATION`. Per review, the patch stays gated on `model_type` rather than installing for every model, so malformed checkpoint configs are not silently accommodated. The subclass walk is what makes the gate sufficient: it repairs an already-frozen snapshot, so it no longer matters whether the patch installs during the target's parse or the draft's.

Four hunks in one file. The warning, the removal predicate, the wrapper signature and the existing docstrings are unchanged.

**No tests are added.** The two reproducers are GPU e2e suites; I did not add unit coverage for `_install_hf_config_validator` (the snapshot rewrite and the identity-match carve-out). Happy to add it in `tests/test_config.py` next to the regression #57189 introduced, if reviewers want it.

## Testing

Run on MI355X in `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-af1c01499b289be555c475669ba50a88e96d846e`, with this branch's Python source overlaid on the image's compiled extensions. Caveat: that image is 125 commits behind this branch's base and predates the transformers 5.17.0 bump (#56108), so the kernels are older than the Python. The image ships `transformers==5.17.0` / `huggingface_hub==1.31.0`, the transformers minor that introduced the crash. Each test ran in its own pytest session, matching how CI shards them.

```bash
python3 -m pytest -v -s -rA tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dspark/test_dspark.py -k gemma4-deepspec --no-header
python3 -m pytest -v -s -rA tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py -k laguna-nvfp4-mrv2 --no-header
python3 -m pytest tests/test_config.py -q --no-header
```

| | `main` (fef55fd26d) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `test_dspark_...[gemma4-deepspec]` | **FAILED** — `'str' object has no attribute 'get'` | **PASSED** — accuracy 0.930, acceptance rate 0.567, acceptance length 4.971 (floors 0.874 / 0.551 / 4.750) |
| `test_dflash_correctness[laguna-nvfp4-mrv2]` | **FAILED** — `'float' object has no attribute 'get'` | GSM8K eval runs end to end; **fails the acceptance assertion**, `3.051 < 3.195`, accuracy 0.895 |
| `tests/test_config.py` | 2 failed, 371 passed, 6 skipped | 2 failed, 371 passed, 6 skipped |

The `test_config.py` failures are identical on both sides and pre-existing — `test_rope_customization` and `test_eagle_draft_model_config` need gated HF repos and the container has no token. Also checked: a non-allowlisted model with a flat `rope_parameters` is left untouched, and the `sarvam_mla` legacy `validate_rope(ignore_keys=...)` path still works.

**The bug is not ROCm-specific.** Reproduced on an **NVIDIA GB300** (`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-0bfc7a15d0...`, same transformers 5.17.0, native NVFP4 via `FlashInferCuteDslNvFp4LinearKernel` + `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` MoE): the same `Dropping ['rope_theta'] from rope_parameters` fires and both Laguna configs resolve, so unpatched CUDA fails the same way AMD does.

**On the laguna result, stated plainly: this change does not turn that test green.** It turns a config-parse crash into an assertion failure — the GSM8K eval now runs end to end, which it never did before, and the test then fails the acceptance-length threshold. That shortfall is not caused by this change, and it is not AMD-specific:

| hardware | NVFP4 path | acceptance_len | accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|
| MI355X | emulation | 3.051 | 0.895 |
| GB300 | native | **3.0495** | 0.890 |
| enforced floor | | **3.195** (`3.55 × 0.9`) | 0.700 |

Two vendors, native versus emulated quantization, agreeing to three significant figures, ~14% under the reference. In-run metrics oscillate 2.97 / 3.09 / 3.04, so ~3.05 is steady state rather than a tail artifact. The `3.55` figure is annotated in the sibling references as coming from Table 1 of the DFlash paper rather than a measured run, and this parametrization has never completed in CI — it has crashed at config parse since it was added in #50330 — so nothing has ever checked it. I have not found a prior run of it on any hardware to compare against. Worth fixing platform-agnostically in a separate PR rather than with a per-platform carve-out; if anyone has an H200 nightly result for it, that would settle it.

Note these two suites are `optional: true` nightlies (`:nvidia: (H200 MIG 35GB) Spec Decode AL DFlash/DSpark Nightly`, with `:amd: (MI300)` mirrors) whose `source_file_dependencies` do not include `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py` — so this PR does not trigger either job, and no CI number is coming without a manual run.

`ruff check` and `ruff format` pass at the pinned v0.14.0. The diff touches configuration parsing only, but the patch deletes keys from `rope_parameters` before validation for the two gated model types, so it is not output-neutral by construction. Evals run: the two acceptance-rate tests above. Not run: the other four parametrizations in these shards.

Related to #57188, which the merged #57189 already fixed and closed — that layer-type gate is on `main` and this change leaves it byte-identical. title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Fail fast on SM120 when FlashInfer lacks runtime page sizes
body:
## Purpose

Narrows this PR after review feedback (thanks @lucifer1004). Related to #56461 and #59203.

flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5197 makes FlashInfer's SM120 sparse-MLA page sizes a runtime argument, so DeepSeek-V4.1 on SM120 no longer needs vLLM to switch to 64-token pages. #59846 serves V4.1 on SM120 with the existing 128-token kernel blocks and 32-token SWA pages. The geometry change this PR originally proposed is dropped.

What remains is a startup guard. #5197 is in FlashInfer 0.7.1rc1/rc2 but not in the pinned 0.7.0.post1, whose SM120 decode kernels are instantiated only for 64-token pages. On such a build, V4.1 on SM120 currently fails with an error that does not name the cause. This PR checks for runtime page sizes when `DeepseekV4FlashInferSM120Attention` is constructed and raises:

```
FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 on SM120 requires FlashInfer >= 0.7.1 (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5197). ...
```

The probe uses FlashInfer's public `supported_sparse_mla_sm120_configs()` and reads `page_block_size_is_runtime` on the `dsv4` entry. That field exists only in builds that contain #5197, so the probe needs no version parse and works with dev builds. It sits next to the existing `has_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_config` probe and runs only on the SM120 path. SM90 and SM100 behavior is unchanged.

Once vLLM pins FlashInfer >= 0.7.1, the guard always passes on supported installs and only catches stale environments.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py -q
```

The new tests stub FlashInfer, so they run without an SM120 GPU. They cover: no config API, no `dsv4` entry, the 0.7.0.post1 config shape (no runtime flag), the runtime flag off, the runtime flag on, and the decode API missing.

## Test Result

- `ruff check` / `ruff format` pass.
- The probe logic was checked against the `SparseMLASm120DecodeConfig` shapes from FlashInfer v0.7.0.post1 (returns `False`) and v0.7.1rc2 (returns `True`).

---

AI assistance (Claude) was used for implementation, tests, and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [CPU] Add Qwen3.8-Flash-Next CPU backend
body:
## Purpose

This PR adds a native x86 CPU backend for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`Qwen4ExpForCausalLM` and `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`) using Model Runner V2.

The CPU backend:

- implements the Qwen4Exp model, model state, HyperConnection, QSA, PLE, and N-gram embedding paths under the CPU-owned model package;
- uses Triton-CPU kernels for QSA scoring, index expansion, side-cache compression and storage, sparse attention, PLE N-gram hashing, PLE gating, PLE short convolution, and HyperConnection operations, while shared QSA metadata, top-k selection, and main KV-cache updates use PyTorch CPU tensor operations;
- supports block-FP8 checkpoints with BF16 activations and BF16 QSA KV cache;
- pads serialized block-FP8 MoE experts when needed so valid tensor-parallel partitions remain block-aligned;
- supports tensor parallelism, compiled and eager execution, and prefix caching, with TP1 and TP2 validated; and
- extends the dedicated CPU Buildkite shard with focused CPU configuration,
  HyperConnection, PLE, and QSA tests.

### Implementation provenance

This backend is a CPU port of the existing Qwen4Exp implementation rather than an independent model implementation. The model, QSA/indexer, PLE, HyperConnection, model-state, and N-gram embedding structure was copied and adapted from the existing NVIDIA and AMD backends. The CPU Triton kernels also reuse and adapt the corresponding kernel math: HyperConnection and sparse QSA attention draw from both vendor implementations; QSA scoring, expansion, cache-store, and compression kernels are adapted primarily from the AMD implementation; and PLE gating, N-gram hashing, and short-convolution kernels are adapted primarily from the NVIDIA implementation.

The CPU copies replace backend-specific launch and runtime behavior with Triton-CPU thread configuration, CPU cache layouts and buffer shapes, CPU-resident PLE weights, and PyTorch CPU tensor operations for metadata and top-k selection. They intentionally omit CUDA/ROCm-only behavior such as PDL, UVA, asynchronous prefetch, and GPU-specific top-k paths. The duplicated host-side orchestration and kernel math are marked with scoped follow-up comments where common extraction may become practical.

The CPU model path is kept separate from the AMD and NVIDIA implementations. The shared QSA metadata entry point retains the Triton path for CUDA/ROCm tensors and selects the PyTorch implementation for CPU tensors.

Current CPU support is intentionally limited to:

- x86-64 with an active Triton-CPU backend;
- Model Runner V2;
- text-only execution with `--language-model-only`;
- pipeline parallel size 1; and
- BF16 activations and BF16 QSA KV cache.

Speculative decoding, LoRA, multimodal/MRoPE execution, dual-batch overlap, microbatching, and pipeline parallelism are not supported by this initial CPU backend and fail with explicit errors.

The unquantized/BF16 path is covered at the configuration and PLE embedding unit level, but this PR does not claim end-to-end validation of a BF16 checkpoint.

This work does not duplicate an existing PR. #53896 added the original Qwen3.8-Flash-Next accelerator support for NVIDIA and AMD. #53899 and #54431 concern CPU offload for accelerator execution rather than a native CPU model backend. The optimization tracker #55922 also lists CPU offload as a separate TODO; it does not track native CPU execution.

## Test Plan

### Conditional Buildkite coverage

The existing `qwen4-exp-unit-tests-cpu` shard runs the mapped CPU
configuration, HyperConnection, PLE, and QSA test files. HyperConnection and
the Triton-backed PLE/QSA cases skip when the CI image does not provide an
active Triton-CPU backend. Consequently, a green shard without Triton-CPU is
configuration coverage, not evidence that the CPU kernels executed.

### Active-Triton local and static validation

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config_cpu.py \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_hc_ops_cpu.py \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple_cpu.py \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_cpu.py
```

The shared configuration and registry cases affected by the CPU dispatch were
also run directly.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/test_config.py::test_breakable_cudagraph_platform_default \
  'tests/models/test_registry.py::test_registry_imports[Qwen4ExpForCausalLM]' \
  'tests/models/test_registry.py::test_registry_imports[Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration]' \
  'tests/models/test_registry.py::test_registry_imports[Qwen4ExpMTP]'
```

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
```

### Real-checkpoint serving

During branch validation, the following configuration was exercised with TP1 and TP2, both with and without `--enforce-eager`:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1

vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
  --revision 236dfdf285828023ca3bcd3f37366c58a3469b13 \
  --tensor-parallel-size {1|2} \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --language-model-only
```

Eager-mode validation used the same command with `--enforce-eager`.

### Model evaluation

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=20 \
.venv/bin/lm_eval run \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --model vllm \
  --model_args '{"pretrained":"Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8","revision":"236dfdf285828023ca3bcd3f37366c58a3469b13","tensor_parallel_size":2,"max_num_seqs":128,"enable_prefix_caching":false,"enable_thinking":false,"language_model_only":true,"max_model_len":4096,"limit_mm_per_prompt":{"image":0,"video":0}}' \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --fewshot_as_multiturn true \
  --batch_size 128 \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=512 temperature=0.0
```

## Test Result

### Active-Triton local and static validation

- Mapped Qwen4Exp tests: `54 passed, 29 skipped`.
- The Triton-CPU runtime probe was active, and no test in the CPU
  configuration, HyperConnection, PLE, or QSA files skipped. The 29 skips were
  accelerator-only cases in the shared PLE test file.
- Shared configuration and registry sanity: `15 passed, 1 skipped`; the skip
  is the expected unsupported Qwen4Exp MTP import on CPU.
- Ruff, formatting, typos, mypy, SPDX, import-boundary, and configuration pre-commit checks: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

### Real-checkpoint serving

During branch validation, every configuration loaded all 131 checkpoint shards, selected the CPU GDN and CPU FP8 MoE implementations, reached application startup, and completed two seeded greedy requests:

| Tensor parallelism | Execution mode | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TP1 | Compiled | Passed |
| TP1 | Eager | Passed |
| TP2 | Compiled | Passed |
| TP2 | Eager | Passed |

Outputs were deterministic within each configuration. This does not claim byte-identical output between compiled and eager TP2 execution.

A repeated-prompt TP1 serving test also completed 4/4 requests and recorded a 1,664-token prefix-cache hit.

### Model evaluation

| Task | Samples | Strict exact match | Flexible exact match |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K, five-shot | 1,319/1,319 | 0.956785 | 0.957544 |

## AI Assistance

AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used to develop and review this change.

title: [Bug]: TieringOffloadingSpec leaks /dev/shm mmap files on non-graceful shutdown (barrier-unlink fix from #52596 not applied)
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Description PR #52596 fixed `SharedOffloadRegion` so the backing `/dev/shm/vllm_offload_{engine_id}.mmap` file is unlinked immediately after all workers have mapped it (via a `barrier` callback), so the kernel reclaims the memory on process exit regardless of how the process exits (including `SIGKILL` or a non-graceful container restart). However, this fix was only wired up in `vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/spec.py` (`CPUOffloadingSpec.create_worker`), which passes `barrier=_all_workers_barrier`. The `TieringOffloadingSpec` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/spec.py`) creates **two** `SharedOffloadRegion` instances — the scheduler-side region (`get_manager`) and the worker-side region (`create_worker`) — **neither passes a `barrier`**. As a result, these regions still rely solely on the old `cleanup()`-on-graceful-shutdown path, and the `.mmap` file is leaked in `/dev/shm` whenever the engine process is killed non-gracefully (e.g. `SIGKILL`, OOM-kill, or a container restart that doesn't fully drain the graceful-shutdown signal chain). ### Impact In a Kubernetes deployment using `medium: Memory` `emptyDir` for `/dev/shm` (shared at the Pod level, not the container level), restarting just the model container (without recreating the Pod) leaves the old engine's offload region file behind. The next engine startup generates a new `engine_id`/mmap file and needs the *full* configured offload size again, so `/dev/shm` free space is effectively halved (or exhausted) after every non-graceful restart, causing: RuntimeError: Insufficient space in /dev/shm: 131072 MiB required, 32768 MiB free. ### Reproduction - `--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"spec_name":"TieringOffloadingSpec","cpu_bytes_to_use":137438953472,"offload_prompt_only":false}}'` - Send `SIGKILL` (or `kill -9`) to the EngineCore process (or otherwise bypass the graceful shutdown path). - Observe `/dev/shm/vllm_offload_.mmap` still present after the process exits. ``` ls -lh total 128G -rw------- 1 root root 128G Sep 17 05:00 vllm_offload_a2d4948b-0aab-4fec-8e44-8de823cd614d.mmap ``` - Restart the engine; it fails or has drastically reduced `/dev/shm` headroom due to the leaked file. ### Suggested fix Wire up a `barrier` callback (similar to `_all_workers_barrier` in `cpu/spec.py`) for both `SharedOffloadRegion` instantiations in `tiering/spec.py` (`get_manager`'s `scheduler_mmap` and `create_worker`'s `worker_mmap`), so the eager-unlink-after-barrier behavior from #52596 applies uniformly to `TieringOffloadingSpec` as well. ### Environment - vLLM version: v0.29.0 (also reproduced against latest `main` @ `0bfc7a15d0`) - Deployment: Kubernetes, `/dev/shm` backed by Pod-level `emptyDir(medium: Memory) ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Offload] Avoid /dev/shm mmap file leak in TieringOffloadingSpec on non-graceful shutdown (#57303)
body:
## Purpose
Fixes #57303.

In #52596, a distributed barrier-unlink mechanism was introduced for `CPUOffloadingSpec` so that the shared backing mmap file `/dev/shm/vllm_offload_{engine_id}.mmap` is unlinked after all workers map it, ensuring the kernel reclaims the shared memory on non-graceful exits (e.g. `SIGKILL`, crash, container restart) with zero memory leaks.

However, `TieringOffloadingSpec` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/spec.py`) was not wired to use this barrier, leaving files leaked in `/dev/shm` on pod restart.

Unlike `CPUOffloadingSpec` (where only worker processes map the shared region), `TieringOffloadingSpec` maps the shared region in both:
1. Worker processes (`create_worker`)
2. The scheduler process (`get_manager`, creating the primary CPU tier)

If workers were to unlink the file upon their barrier, the mmap file would be deleted before the scheduler initializes in `EngineCore.__init__`. When `get_manager()` runs next, `os.open(..., O_CREAT | O_EXCL ...)` would succeed and create a brand-new, disconnected 131 GB file (split-brain memory and double `/dev/shm` allocation). Moreover, the scheduler process does not initialize PyTorch distributed (`_WORLD is None`), so calling `_all_workers_barrier()` in `get_manager()` would crash with an `AssertionError`.

### Solution: Coordinated Deferred Unlink
1. **`SharedOffloadRegion` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/shared_offload_region.py`)**:
   - Added `defer_unlink: bool = False` to `__init__`.
   - Added explicit, idempotent `unlink(self) -> None` method.
   - When `barrier` is provided and `self._creator`: if `not defer_unlink`, calls `self.unlink()`. If `defer_unlink=True`, unlinking is deferred.
   - In `cleanup()`, catches `FileNotFoundError: pass` prior to generic `Exception` handling so graceful shutdown does not log spurious warnings when an mmap file was already eagerly unlinked.
2. **`TieringOffloadingSpec` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/spec.py`)**:
   - In `create_worker()`: passes `barrier=_all_workers_barrier, defer_unlink=True`. Workers synchronize across ranks without prematurely deleting the file.
   - In `get_manager()`: once `scheduler_mmap` is instantiated and mapped, calls `scheduler_mmap.unlink()`. At this point, both all workers and the scheduler hold valid open mappings, and the file name is removed from `/dev/shm`.
3. POSIX semantics ensure that open descriptors and memory mappings stay active and intact until all engine processes exit, while guaranteeing immediate kernel reclamation on hard kills/restarts.

## Test Plan
Added unit tests covering:
1. `tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py`:
   - `test_tiering_spec_create_worker_uses_single_slot_for_replicated_layout` & `test_tiering_spec_create_worker_folds_device_index_for_sharded_layout`: assert `barrier is _all_workers_barrier` and `defer_unlink is True`.
   - `test_tiering_spec_get_manager_unlinks_scheduler_mmap`: verifies scheduler mmap `unlink()` is invoked in `get_manager()`.
2. `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py`:
   - `test_defer_unlink_preserves_file_after_barrier`: verifies file is kept after barrier when `defer_unlink=True` until `unlink()` is called.
   - `test_unlink_method_idempotency_and_suppression`: verifies idempotency and `FileNotFoundError` suppression.
   - `test_cleanup_suppresses_file_not_found_without_warning`: verifies cleanup after eager unlink raises no warnings.
   - `test_real_fs_defer_unlink_and_manual_unlink`: verifies real `/dev/shm` filesystem behavior.

Commands:
```bash
pytest --noconftest tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py
pytest --noconftest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py -k "test_defer_unlink or test_unlink_method or test_cleanup_suppresses or test_real_fs"
ruff check vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/shared_offload_region.py vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/spec.py tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py
```

## Test Result
All tests pass and ruff formatting / lint checks pass:
- `tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py`: 42 passed
- `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py`: 3 passed, 1 skipped (skipped on non-Linux mac lacking `/dev/shm`)
- `ruff check`: All checks passed!

## Attribution & Non-Duplication
- **Duplicate Check**: Verified that no open PR addresses #57303.
- **Assistance Notice**: Implemented with AI pair-programming assistance (DeepMind Antigravity) and verified/tested by the author.

title: [Feature][KV Offload] Support joint GPU/CPU prefix cache lookup
body:
## Purpose

### Background

We deploy DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision Exp with vLLM Ascend v0.27 in our internal network, with Simple CPU Offload enabled. During operation, we observed a cache miss rate exceeding 10%. Investigation showed that some reusable cache entries were not being retrieved due to the unimplemented TODO in `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py`: the existing API only matches a CPU suffix following the GPU prefix, rather than searching for a complete valid prefix across both pools.

After implementing joint lookup, we ported the change to the v0.27 branch in our fork and redeployed it in the same environment. The deployment has been running for five days, with normal operation and successful retrieval of cache entries previously affected by this limitation.

This PR targets upstream main. The deployment observations above come from the v0.27 backport in our fork.

### Changes

Support valid prefixes composed of interleaved GPU and CPU cache blocks, replacing the limitation of matching a GPU prefix followed by a CPU suffix.

For example, given a `GPU → CPU → GPU` cache layout, reuse both GPU blocks directly and allocate and load a target block only for the middle CPU block. When both pools contain a required block, prefer the GPU copy.

The implementation:

- Provides a read-only joint lookup view for existing attention-specific matching algorithms, preserving hybrid-attention convergence and memoizing queries within each request.
- Records hit sources by group and block position, distinguishing GPU hits, CPU blocks requiring loads, and attention padding.
- Pins source blocks before allocation and allocates targets only for CPU hits. Targets are registered in the cache after loading completes, without re-registering interleaved GPU hits.
- Attributes GPU/CPU cache statistics and cache events to their actual sources.
- Preserves full-block CPU loads, copy-on-write for partial GPU hits, and existing watermark and speculative-decoding reservation rules. If capacity is insufficient, allocation of the entire match is deferred.

### Relationship to related work

This PR implements joint lookup for interleaved GPU/CPU prefixes in `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`. The related #52773 / #52774 address boundary backfill in `OffloadingConnector`, so the connector and implementation scope differ.

## Test Plan

Cover the following behaviors:

- All-GPU, all-CPU, multiple interleavings, duplicate hits across pools, missing intermediate blocks, and different sources across groups.
- GPU block identity reuse, exact CPU transfer positions, and no publication of target cache entries before loading completes.
- SWA/Mamba, different block sizes, DCP/EAGLE matching boundaries, final-token recomputation, and copy-on-write for partial blocks.
- Insufficient capacity, speculative-decoding reservations, and reference cleanup after retries, cancellation, and reset.
- Bypassing separate GPU/CPU scans on the joint path, with no repeated probes for the same hash/group.
- GPU/CPU statistics and interleaved cache events.

Regression command after the latest code cleanup:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py \
  -q
```

Run pre-commit on modified files, along with Python 3.10/3.12 type checks.

Local real-model validation uses OPT-125m, Qwen3-0.6B, and Qwen3.5-0.8B. GPU cache capacity is constrained and cache residency layouts are controlled to trigger actual CPU loads. Validation compares cold-cache and warm-cache outputs under deterministic generation settings and checks transfer positions and reference cleanup.

## Test Result

After the September 20 rebase, 575 distinct relevant tests passed (574 in the broad run and one rerun after restoring the Ray test dependency), along with pre-commit and Python 3.10/3.12 type checks. This includes regressions for discarding short joint hits under bounded prefix replay and replaying longer hits after CPU loading. Earlier, 22 real-model combinations passed, completing 9,146 exact cold/warm output comparisons and exercising actual CPU loads, copy-on-write, and preemption; that model matrix has not been rerun after this rebase. Some OPT/MTP combinations showed cold/warm differences that also reproduced on the legacy lookup path and are excluded from the passing results.

## AI assistance

GPT-6 Astra assisted with the implementation, tests, and this description. The code has undergone human review.

title: [V1][Perf] Cap detokenizer prompt-prime window for long prompts
body:
## Purpose

- `FastIncrementalDetokenizer` primes the `tokenizers` `DecodeStream` with the entire prompt (`DecodeStream(ids=request.prompt_token_ids)`). Priming is O(prompt_len) and runs lazily on the first output token's decode step, so for very long prompts it dominates first-token detokenization latency. Incremental decoding of output tokens only needs a short trailing window of prompt context, so this PR caps the primed ids to the last MAX_PROMPT_PRIME_TOKENS (128).

- The value of MAX_PROMPT_PRIME_TOKENS, 128, is a large-enough magic number for any BPE-merge / multi-byte span.
- On DeepSeek-V4-Flash (vocab ~129k), a 998k-token prompt: the first decode step drops from ~386 ms to ~0.1 ms.

## Test Plan

title: [Rust Frontend] Build full-output grammars from initialized reasoning parsers
body:
## Purpose

Strict tool grammars currently start after the engine detects the end of reasoning. This change builds the reasoning phase from the initialized Rust parser and composes it with the visible-output grammar, allowing XGrammar to constrain the generated stream from token zero.

Step 2, following the merged #55269. That PR introduces the parser-owned grammar interfaces and request lifecycle; this follow-up activates `FromTokenZero` coverage for supported delimited reasoning parsers. The open-PR search found no separate implementation of this layer.

- Build the reasoning continuation from the final prompt state, including model-specific closing separators and any separator suffix remaining after prompt prefill.
- Enable the wrapper for DeepSeek R1/V3, Qwen3, GLM45, Step3/Step3.5, Nemotron V3, and HY3/HY4 through their existing parser implementations and aliases.
- Project the MiniMax M2 builder to its visible-output grammar before composing the reasoning wrapper, with an explicit check of the expected builder prefix.
- Preserve the existing tool-grammar activation policy. Supported requests use `reasoning_ended = Some(true)` through Step 1's lowering; the grammar requires the reasoning close before entering visible output.

K3, Gemma4, Inkling, and Harmony remain follow-up work.

## Test Plan

The builder-parity invariant is:

```text
reasoning-wrapped visible tool tag = builder output with the matching reasoning mode
```

`assert_builder_parity` checks 54 cases: nine reasoning/tool parser pairs × `ReasoningMode::{Enabled, Auto}` × required/named/strict-auto tool choices. Enabled initializes inside a prefilled reasoning block; Auto initializes without a reasoning boundary. Every case asserts `FromTokenZero` coverage. The comparison flattens nested sequences and ignores `AnyText.excludes`, including inside `Optional`, while retaining token and character budgets. It checks normalized grammar structure.

## Test Result

- After restacking onto main with #55269 merged: **1513 parser/chat/text/server/LLM/engine-client tests passed, 1 skipped**, including production renderer/parser roundtrips; XGrammar structural tags 0.3.0.
- Auto parity was confirmed failing before extending normalization into `Optional`, then all **54 cases passed** with the recursive normalization.
- Strict Clippy, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Earlier local XGrammar 0.2.7 validation: 18 HY3/HY4 grammar configurations passed 72 token-mask/acceptance/stop replays with a controlled vocabulary; 9 HY3 configurations passed 36 replays with its cached model tokenizer.
### Prior GPU end-to-end regression checks

Paired GB200 runs on September 17–18 compared Step 1 [`ef67e07c`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ef67e07c686c0e758815701d239a28e48da1e169) with Step 2 [`b38299c9`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/b38299c9fa958ac1471a77455969868457153d4b), using the same checkpoint, requests, and serving settings within each pair. The following model/parser configurations had **zero candidate-only task failures in the evaluated samples**. Success requires the expected answer and tool/direct-text behavior, with completion within the output budget. Counts show Step 1 → Step 2; existing failures remain included.

| Model family / tested checkpoint | Reasoning parser | Tool / unified parser | Paired GPU e2e result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3: Qwen3-4B | `qwen3` | `qwen3_xml` | Native tasks 33/33 → 33/33; GSM8K 14/16 → 15/16; explicit starting states 21/21 → 21/21 |

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] Read the NVFP4 compressed KV cache in the gfx950 sparse decode
body:
DeepSeek-V4.1 stores its compressed KV as NVFP4 (288 B/token: 512 e2m1 values packed two per byte, then 32 e4m3 scales of 16 dims each) next to an fp8 sliding-window cache. Only FlashMLA's SM100 sparse decode could read that record, so `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla` was rejected everywhere else and ROCm kept the 584 B V4 record for both caches.

Add an NVFP4 row loader to the gfx950 sparse decode tile, selected per cache from the record width the KV-cache spec publishes, and let a layer whose kernel can read the record opt in instead of gating on SM100 alone. The sliding-window record and the fp8 path are unchanged.

The loader decodes a nibble pair with gfx950's v_cvt_scalef32_pk_f32_fp4. That instruction's scale operand is E8M0, so this record's e4m3 scale is applied separately, and its destination is a register pair, so the result is taken as one 64-bit value whose halves are the even and odd dim of the byte.

Measured on MI355X (gfx950) at the shape this model decodes at on 4 ranks -- 16 local heads, index_topk 512, sliding window 128 -- captured in a HIP graph with prebuilt ragged indices: within 1% of the 584 B record from 1 to 64 decode tokens, for a compressed cache half the size. Correctness against a torch softmax over the same dequantized rows: cosine 0.999998, relative error 2.0e-03.

This change was written with AI assistance (Claude Code).

title: [Feature]: [CPU][GLM5Next] Add native sparse MLA / KeyPool indexer support for GLM-5.3-Flash
body:
## Motivation

GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` / `glm5next`) is now supported in vLLM, but its native sparse MLA / KeyPool attention path is not implemented for the CPU backend.

This is different from #54018 / #54029.

Those address the older `glm_moe_dsa` path and provide a way to disable sparse attention and fall back to dense MLA on CPU.

For GLM-5.3-Flash, I would like to request **native CPU execution of its sparse MLA + KeyPool/KeyPoolIndexer path**, preserving the model's sparse-attention behavior rather than converting it to dense MLA.

## Current state on `main`

The generic CPU attention selector still rejects sparse attention:

```python
if attn_selector_config.use_sparse:
    raise NotImplementedError("Sparse Attention is not supported on CPU.")
```

At the same time, CPU support has recently progressed significantly: DeepSeek-V4 now has its own x86/AMX CPU sparse-MLA/indexer implementation, including CPU kernels for the sparse attention/indexing pipeline.

`vllm/platforms/cpu.py` explicitly documents the DeepSeek-V4 CPU kernels under:

```text
csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/
├── flash_mla
├── store_cache
├── compressor
├── paged_mqa_logits
└── topk
```

and configures DeepSeek-V4 separately with its required block size.

This makes GLM5Next support seem like a useful next target rather than requiring CPU sparse attention infrastructure to be created entirely from scratch.

## GLM5Next-specific gap

GLM-5.3 uses a different sparse-indexing scheme from DeepSeek-V4.

The current GLM5Next sparse-indexer dispatcher is effectively:

```python
if current_platform.is_rocm():
    from .amd.sparse_indexer import SparseAttnIndexerKpool
else:
    from .nvidia.sparse_indexer import SparseAttnIndexerKpool
```

There is no CPU branch.

Therefore a CPU build falls into the NVIDIA implementation rather than a CPU implementation.

GLM5Next's attention implementation also currently imports:

```python
from vllm.models.glm5next.nvidia.ops.kpool_compress import fwht128_quant_fp8
```

and constructs the model-specific:

```text
SparseAttnIndexerKpool
Glm5NextIndexerCache
Glm5NextTailCache
KeyPool/KPool compression
top-k sparse selection
```

The GLM5Next indexer has additional semantics that are not identical to the DeepSeek-V4 Lightning Indexer:

* NoPE MLA
* KeyPool/KPool compression
* per-token KeyPool gate score
* FP8 indexer K cache
* tail cache for the current/incomplete pool
* top-k pool/token selection
* KeyPool state that must remain synchronized with the MLA KV cache

So simply routing GLM5Next through the existing generic CPU MLA backend would not be sufficient.

## Requested feature

Add a native CPU implementation of the GLM5Next sparse MLA / KeyPool pipeline.

A possible architecture could be:

```text
GLM5Next hidden states
        │
        ├── indexer Q/K projections
        │
        ├── KeyPool compression
        │
        ├── KeyPool / tail-cache update
        │
        ├── indexer score computation
        │
        ├── top-k sparse selection
        │
        ▼
selected MLA KV entries
        │
        ▼
CPU / AMX MLA
```

It may be possible to reuse parts of the recently added DeepSeek-V4 CPU sparse-MLA implementation, especially:

* paged/cache addressing
* top-k
* MQA score computation
* sparse metadata
* AMX MLA kernels
* chunked-prefill / prefix-cache integration

while implementing the GLM5Next-specific KeyPool compression and cache semantics separately.

## Possible implementation direction

I am not proposing a specific internal API, but one possible approach would be:

1. Add an explicit CPU branch in `vllm/models/glm5next/sparse_indexer.py`.

```python
if current_platform.is_rocm():
    ...
elif current_platform.is_cpu():
    from .cpu.sparse_indexer import SparseAttnIndexerKpool
else:
    ...
```

2. Implement a CPU/reference version of the GLM5Next KPool indexer first.

3. Add optimized x86 paths where useful for:

   * FWHT + quantization
   * KPool compression
   * paged MQA logits
   * top-k selection
   * MLA decode

4. Reuse the existing AMX MLA backend where the GLM5Next NoPE geometry permits it.

5. Support both:

   * chunked prefill
   * decode

6. Preserve:

   * prefix caching
   * hybrid KV-cache grouping
   * `k_cache`
   * `tail_cache`

A correctness-first implementation would already be valuable even if the initial indexer is slower than the NVIDIA/AMD paths. AMX/AVX-512 optimization could follow.

## Why dense fallback is not sufficient

Falling back to dense MLA is useful for compatibility and CI, as discussed in #54018/#54029, but it removes the primary computational benefit of GLM-5.3's sparse attention at long context lengths.

For CPU inference in particular, avoiding unnecessary KV-memory traffic is important, so native sparse execution is much more valuable than making the model merely boot with dense attention.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

* GLM-5.3-Flash can construct its MLA/indexer layers on `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`.
* CPU does not import/use NVIDIA-only KPool operators.
* Positive `index_topk` remains enabled.
* Sparse KeyPool selection is actually performed rather than silently using dense MLA.
* Prefill works.
* Decode works.
* Chunked prefill works.
* Prefix caching works.
* KeyPool `k_cache` and `tail_cache` remain synchronized correctly.
* Results match a GPU reference within expected BF16/FP8 tolerance.
* x86 AMX is used where supported/appropriate.

## Relationship to existing CPU work

This request is **not** a generic "please add sparse attention to CPU" issue.

There is already model-specific DeepSeek-V4 CPU sparse-attention/indexer support on current `main`.

The request is to extend CPU sparse-attention support to **GLM5Next's KeyPool architecture**, ideally reusing/commonizing the new DeepSeek-V4 CPU infrastructure where practical.

It is also separate from #54018/#54029, which concern `glm_moe_dsa` and dense fallback.

Would it make sense to build the GLM5Next CPU KeyPool implementation on top of the recently added DeepSeek-V4 CPU sparse-MLA/indexer infrastructure, or should GLM5Next initially have a separate CPU backend because its KeyPool semantics differ?


### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

title: [Feature]: [CPU][GLM5Next][KDA] Add CPU KDA backend for GLM-5.3-Flash
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Motivation

GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) is a hybrid model containing both:

* sparse MLA layers
* KDA (Kimi Delta Attention / gated delta-rule) linear-attention layers

Even if GLM5Next's sparse MLA / KeyPool path is made CPU-compatible, the model still cannot execute end-to-end on CPU without a KDA backend.

I would like to request native CPU support for GLM5Next KDA.

## Current state

The GLM5Next KDA implementation currently lives under the accelerator-specific path:

```text
vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/kda.py
```

and uses GPU-oriented Flash Linear Attention / Triton operators such as:

```text
chunk_kda_with_fused_gate
fused_recurrent_kda
```

There does not appear to be a corresponding:

```text
vllm/models/glm5next/cpu/kda.py
```

or other CPU KDA execution path for GLM5Next on current `main`.

This makes KDA an independent CPU blocker from sparse MLA / KeyPool support.

GLM-5.3-Flash has a large number of KDA layers, so this cannot reasonably be worked around by supporting only the sparse-MLA portion of the model.

## Related CPU infrastructure already exists

The CPU backend already has substantial support for related linear-attention/state-space workloads.

In particular, current CPU platform code contains an accelerated GDN path using:

```text
AMX tiles
or
AVX-512 BF16 / VDPBF16PS
```

and vLLM already has CPU machinery for stateful hybrid models, including:

* recurrent state caches
* convolution state
* chunked prefill
* decode
* hybrid KV/state-cache management

KDA is not identical to GDN, but they are closely related enough that it may be possible to reuse much of this infrastructure.

## KDA-specific work

As I understand it, GLM5Next KDA needs CPU equivalents for the KDA-specific operations around the existing gated-delta/state machinery, including:

```text
Q/K/V short convolution
        │
        ▼
KDA gate computation
        │
        ▼
chunked gated-delta prefill
        │
        ▼
final recurrent state
        │
        ▼
single-token recurrent decode
        │
        ▼
gated/RMSNorm output
```

The important parts include:

* q/k/v convolution and convolution-state update
* KDA gate calculation
* per-channel decay/gating behavior
* `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` equivalent for prefill
* `fused_recurrent_kda` equivalent for decode
* initial-state gathering
* final-state writeback
* mixed decode/prefill handling
* state-cache addressing
* chunk boundaries
* prefix-cache/state restore correctness

## Requested feature

Add a CPU KDA backend for GLM5Next.

A correctness-first implementation would be useful even before full AMX optimization.

One possible structure could be:

```text
vllm/models/glm5next/
├── common/
├── nvidia/
├── amd/
└── cpu/
    └── kda.py
```

with explicit platform dispatch rather than allowing CPU to reach the NVIDIA implementation.

## Possible implementation phases

### Phase 1: reference CPU implementation

Provide a functional PyTorch/C++ CPU implementation for:

* short convolution
* chunked KDA prefill
* recurrent KDA decode
* KDA gate/output
* state gather/scatter

The initial goal would be correctness and end-to-end execution.

### Phase 2: reuse existing CPU GDN kernels

Where the mathematical operations overlap with the existing CPU GDN backend, share or extend those implementations rather than creating duplicate infrastructure.

### Phase 3: x86 optimization

Optimize the expensive GEMM/state operations with:

* AMX BF16
* AVX-512 BF16
* oneDNN / existing vLLM CPU kernels where appropriate

For Sapphire Rapids, AMX acceleration would be particularly useful.

## Important correctness cases

KDA is stateful, so I think CPU tests should cover more than a single one-shot prompt.

Suggested tests:

### Prefill equivalence

Compare:

```text
one-shot prefill
```

against:

```text
chunk 1
→ save state
→ chunk 2
→ save state
→ ...
```

The final output/state should match within expected numerical tolerance.

### Prefill → decode

Verify that the state produced by chunked prefill can be consumed by recurrent decode without divergence.

### Mixed batches

Verify batches containing both:

* ongoing decode requests
* new prefill requests

because these exercise different sequence/state layouts.

### Prefix caching

Verify that restoring KDA state after a prefix-cache hit produces the same continuation as recomputing the prefix.

### Request slot reuse

Verify that state belonging to a completed request cannot leak into a newly allocated request slot.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

* GLM5Next KDA layers construct successfully on CPU.
* No CUDA/Triton/NVIDIA KDA operator is imported or invoked by the CPU path.
* Chunked prefill works.
* Recurrent decode works.
* Prefill-produced state is valid for decode.
* Multiple sequences in the same packed batch remain independent.
* Mixed prefill/decode batches work.
* Prefix caching/state restoration works.
* Output is numerically comparable to an existing NVIDIA/ROCm reference implementation.
* An optimized AMX/AVX-512 path can be selected on capable x86 systems.

## Scope

This issue is specifically for **KDA CPU execution**.

GLM-5.3-Flash also requires CPU support for its NoPE sparse MLA / KeyPool indexer path; I am tracking that separately because the two features are independent.

Conceptually:

```text
GLM-5.3-Flash
        │
        ├── KDA layers
        │       └── CPU backend needed  ← this issue
        │
        └── sparse MLA / KeyPool layers
                └── CPU backend needed  ← separate issue
```

Fixing either one alone is not sufficient for end-to-end GLM-5.3 CPU inference.

Would maintainers prefer implementing KDA by extending/reusing the existing CPU GDN backend, or keeping a separate GLM5Next/KDA CPU implementation first and sharing kernels later?


### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
