title: [Bugfix][torch.compile] Honor an explicit RoPE+KV-cache fusion request
body:
## Purpose

Setting `fuse_rope_kvcache=True` silently turns it back off.

`set_splitting_ops_for_v1` splits `vllm::unified_kv_cache_update` out of the compiled
graph so Inductor can reuse the piecewise graphs (#33267). `RopeKVCacheFusionPass`
rewrites that op, so it can only match while the op is still in the graph. Rather than
say so, the code overwrites the user's flag with `False` and suggests `splitting_ops=[]`
or `use_inductor_graph_partition=True` — the first gives up piecewise structure
entirely (#20059), the second is a much larger change than "please fuse RoPE with the
KV cache write".

The suggestion is also stale. The graph reuse being protected only breaks while
`layer_name` is baked into the graph as a string constant; on torch >= 2.11 it is
hoisted as an opaque graph input (`_USE_LAYERNAME`) and Inductor reuses the graph
whether or not the op is split out. On a Llama-3.1-8B cold start with a fresh Inductor
cache, keeping the op in the graph costs **+0.08 s per compile range** with hoisting on
and **12.8x** with it off (1.26 s -> 16.02 s), so the trade is real in one regime and
free in the other.

This PR keeps the op a requested fusion rewrites inside the compiled graph, gated on
`_USE_LAYERNAME` so the pre-2.11 cliff is never paid silently; the warning there now
states the actual reason. Piecewise splitting on the attention ops is untouched.

Two related defects in the same path:

- `_set_compile_ranges()` ran *before* `set_splitting_ops_for_v1()`, so a fusion that
  was then dropped still left its `rope_kvcache_fusion_max_token_num` endpoint behind.
  On `main`, requesting the fusion yields `compile_ranges_endpoints=[256, 256, 16384]`
  with both flags off — two extra graph specialisations compiled for a fusion that
  cannot run. It now runs after.
- `enable_qk_norm_rope_kvcache` lacked the `splitting_ops_contain_kv_cache_update()`
  guard `enable_rope_kvcache_fusion` has, so it resolved `True` only to be overwritten.
  Net behaviour is unchanged; the contradictory log pair and the duplicate endpoint go
  away.

`fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla` is handled the same way, so only the op a fusion actually
rewrites is kept. This overlaps #49142, which makes the MLA-only version of this change
and additionally enables that fusion by default on CUDA; I have no NVIDIA hardware to
evaluate the default change, so that part is left to it. #50758 / #40187 remove the
layer-name string outright and would make this block unnecessary; until one lands, an
explicit flag should not be inverted.

## Scope

`PassConfig.__post_init__` forces `fuse_rope_kvcache` and `fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache`
off when `not current_platform.is_rocm()`, so for those two this is a no-op on CUDA and
CPU. `fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla` is gated on `is_cuda_alike()` and is therefore reachable
on CUDA: its default there is unchanged, since `enable_rope_kvcache_mla_fusion` resolves
to `False` while `splitting_ops is None` with graph partition off, but a CUDA user who
sets it explicitly now gets the fusion instead of a silently dropped flag. The
`_set_compile_ranges()` reorder cannot change CUDA behaviour — the only compile-range
inputs `set_splitting_ops_for_v1` touches are the two ROCm-only flags. See the comment
below for the per-scenario breakdown and the interaction with #49142.

Reaching the non-MLA pass also needs an `Attention` layer whose backend implements
`fused_rope_kvcache_supported()`, and RoPE applied directly to the qkv split. Probed on
gfx950 with all three flags forced on:

| Model | `Attention` / `MLAAttention` | Patterns replaced |
|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | 32 / 0 | 1 |
| Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct | 32 / 0 | 1 |
| gpt-oss-120b | 36 / 0 | 1 |
| Qwen3-14B / Qwen3.5-397B / Qwen3-Next-80B / gemma-4-26B | 8–30 / 0 | **0** — QK-norm sits between the qkv split and RoPE |
| MiMo-V2.5-Pro | 8 / 0 | **0** — `TritonAttentionDiffKVImpl` does not advertise the fusion |
| DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, GLM-5.2/5.3, Kimi-K3, Kimi-Linear | 0 / N | **0** — MLA-only, so `get_layers_from_vllm_config(config, Attention)` sees nothing |
| MiniMax-M3 | non-MLA + QK-norm | **0** — already calls one fused `qknorm_rope_kv_insert`, no `rotary_embedding` node to match |

So the flag matters for Llama/Mistral/Mixtral-class models and gpt-oss; current MLA
flagships are structurally unaffected either way.

## Test Plan

- `tests/compile/test_config.py -k splitting_ops`, on ROCm.
- Kernel-level A/B of the fused `triton_rope_and_cache` against the unfused
  `rotary_embedding` + KV-cache write it replaces, on both cache layouts a supported
  backend allocates, timed inside a CUDA graph.

## Test Result

`tests/compile/test_config.py -k splitting_ops`: 8 passed. The new cases are
parametrised over all three flags and fail against three builds differently — 6 fail on
`main`, and the three `needs_hoisted_layer_names` cases fail on a variant of this patch
with the `_USE_LAYERNAME` guard removed, which otherwise passes the whole suite on
torch 2.12.

**Fusion now runs.** On `main`, `RopeKVCacheFusionPass` is never constructed; with this
patch, on Llama-3.1-8B:

```
Enabled custom fusions: norm_quant, act_quant, mla_dual_rms_norm, rope_kvcache
rope_kvcache_fusion.py:459] Replaced 1 patterns
pass_manager.py:119] Skipping RopeKVCacheFusionPass with compile range (257, 16384)
```

One pattern covers all 32 layers because `_USE_LAYERNAME` wildcards `layer_name`; the
skip at `(257, 16384)` is the intended `rope_kvcache_fusion_max_token_num` guard.

**Kernel level.** MI355X (gfx950), torch 2.12, bf16, Llama-3.1-8B TP=1 shapes, 32
invocations per CUDA graph. Four pairs with the arm order alternated, first pair
discarded; the table medians the other three and gives each arm's own spread. Both arms
are asserted to land the same K/V in the cache (`max|Δ| ≤ 0.031`, bf16 rounding) before
either is timed.

`ROCM_ATTN` (the backend a dense bf16 model gets by default here):

| tokens | unfused (µs) | fused (µs) | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.89 ± 0.04 | 2.59 ± 0.02 | +55.98 % |
| 8 | 6.21 ± 0.02 | 2.67 ± 0.02 | +57.08 % |
| 16 | 6.31 ± 0.02 | 2.96 ± 0.05 | +53.07 % |
| 32 | 6.43 ± 0.11 | 3.34 ± 0.03 | +48.06 % |
| 64 | 6.65 ± 0.10 | 4.37 ± 0.04 | +34.76 % |
| 128 | 7.28 ± 0.01 | 6.12 ± 0.05 | +15.90 % |
| 192 | 7.93 ± 0.02 | 7.69 ± 0.14 | +3.24 % |
| 256 | 8.65 ± 0.51 | 8.70 ± 0.10 | −0.52 % |

`ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` / `ROCM_AITER_FA` (flash layout) gives +48.10 % at 1 token,
+38.56 % at 64, +21.33 % at 128 and −6.57 % at 256.

Median over the decode shapes the fusion applies to (1–64 tokens): **+51.0 %** on
`ROCM_ATTN`, **+48.1 %** on the flash layout. The crossover near 192–256 tokens
independently reproduces the existing `rope_kvcache_fusion_max_token_num = 256` default.

**Accuracy.** GSM8K, 5-shot, greedy, all 1319 items, `max_gen_toks=256`,
`enable_prefix_caching=False`, seed 1234, against a base-vs-base repeat as the noise
floor:

| Model | patch Δ | base-repeat Δ | stderr |
|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B | +0.0008 | +0.0008 | 0.0089 |
| Mixtral-8x7B | −0.0045 | +0.0000 | 0.0093 |
| gpt-oss-120b | +0.0167 | +0.0243 | 0.0087 |
| Qwen3-14B (0 patterns) | −0.0008 | +0.0000 | 0.0061 |

Every delta is within half a standard error, and on gpt-oss the base repeat drifts
further than the patch does. No measurable accuracy change on GSM8K, within the
base-repeat noise floor — which is not a claim of bit-exactness: swapping two kernels
for one changes reduction order, and per-sample text agreement is 98.6 % on
Llama-3.1-8B and 55.5 % on Mixtral-8x7B against 99.3 % and 99.6 % for the base repeat.
Qwen3-14B, where the pass matches nothing, still shows 95.1 % against 100.0 %: keeping
the op in the graph changes the compiled graph even when no pattern matches.

End-to-end serving numbers to follow in a comment.

---

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom); reviewed and measured by hand.

title: [Perf][Attention] FlashInfer: skip the seq_lens copy with speculative decoding
body:
## Overview

With speculative decoding, the FlashInfer builder copies `seq_lens` from the GPU on every step.
The copy waits for all queued GPU work, so the CPU cannot prepare the next step.

This PR plans fa2 (Ampere, Ada) from CPU bounds instead, so the copy is gone.

It extends #57214, which removed the same copy without speculative decoding.
@WoosukKwon suggested planning from a close upper bound in #29134.
No open PR removes this copy with speculative decoding.

## Claims

- Output tokens/s +1% to +23% with MTP and EAGLE3 on RTX 3080, 4090 and 4050.
- Acceptance length and gsm8k accuracy do not change.
- Without speculative decoding, only the pinned-buffer handling changes.

## Validation

Output tokens/s, this PR vs sham (main with comment-only edits in the same files), 12 rounds, 95% CI:

| GPU | Model, drafter | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTX 4090 | Qwen3.5-0.8B, MTP 3 | +5.4% [+4.5, +6.4] | +4.9% [+3.4, +6.4] | +18.0% [+17.1, +19.0] |
| RTX 4090 | Llama-3.1-8B, EAGLE3 3 | +7.2% [+7.2, +7.3] | +5.8% [+4.7, +6.8] | +3.6% [+2.9, +4.2] |
| RTX 4090 | Qwen3-8B, EAGLE3 3 | +7.5% [+6.3, +8.7] | +5.7% [+5.0, +6.3] | +3.5% [+2.9, +4.2] |
| RTX 4090 | Qwen3.8-27B 2.8-bit, MTP 3 ¹ | +6.5% [+4.7, +8.3] | +2.8% [+1.9, +3.7] | +1.9% [+1.2, +2.5] |
| RTX 3080 | Qwen3.5-0.8B, MTP 3 | +10.1% [+8.8, +11.4] | +15.1% [+13.5, +16.8] | +14.2% [+13.5, +15.0] |
| RTX 3080 | Qwen3-1.7B, EAGLE3 3 | +22.6% [+22.4, +22.8] | +14.2% [+13.3, +15.2] | +5.9% [+5.4, +6.5] |
| RTX 4050 Laptop | Qwen3.5-0.8B, MTP 3 | +4.8% [+4.8, +4.9] | +1.4% [+0.1, +2.7] | +1.2% [+0.4, +2.0] |

¹ `Intel/Qwen3.8-27B-bpw2.8-AutoRound`; its config misses the 4-bit MTP entry, which I added.
Median ITL is lower in every cell.
ShareGPT prompts give the same gain (Speed details).

- 7354 tests on RTX 3080, failures re-run on RTX 4090: no test fails on this PR that passes on main.
- Greedy outputs at c=1 match main: 16 of 16 prompts, two models.
- `VLLM_DEBUG_SEQ_LENS_BOUNDS=1` under load: no assertion. A lower bound raised by 1 trips it.
- `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` with MTP and EAGLE3 under load: no sync reported, on main and on this PR.
- Not run on Hopper or Blackwell.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_plan_from_bounds.py tests/v1/worker/test_seq_len_bounds.py
pytest tests/v1/attention tests/v1/worker tests/v1/spec_decode tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer*.py
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main

vllm serve <model> --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 32 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --language-model-only \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'   # or eagle3 with its head
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 \
  --max-concurrency <c> --num-prompts <n> --ignore-eos --seed <round>
```

gsm8k uses the prompts and scoring of `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`: 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, 256 tokens.

</details>

## Details

The runner passes a CPU lower bound next to the existing upper bound.
fa2 plans from the upper bound and reads the exact lengths from the GPU.
Where the two bounds fall on different pages, that build keeps the copy.

Tradeoffs:
- Up to 8 extra pinned buffers (64 MB) per builder.
- Outputs are not bit-identical to main: a row can get one more planned page, so split-KV sums in another order (Accuracy).
- 360 non-test lines, most in `flashinfer.py`.

<details>
<summary>How it works</summary>

- The two bounds differ only by drafts that may still be rejected.
- fa2 plans from the upper bound. The builder then writes the exact lengths to the GPU, and fa2 reads those.
- A verification row whose bounds fall on different pages keeps the copy for that build.
- Kernels other than fa2 skip the copy only when both bounds are equal.
- `plan()` uploads from a pinned buffer. While an upload is pending, the wrapper takes a fresh buffer. A builder adds at most 8 buffers (64 MB); then `plan()` waits. This also covers the path from #57214.
- The copy stays with context parallelism, sinks, adaptive verification, pipeline parallelism and the V1 runner.
- A wrapper created with `backend="auto"` picks its kernels on its first `plan()`. That first build keeps the copy.
- It relies on three fa2 details: `plan()` stages through `_pin_memory_int_workspace_buffer`, the kernel reads `_paged_kv_last_page_len_buf` on the device, and a non-positive last-page length is an empty page. Without these fields the copy stays. `test_fa2_plan_from_upper_bound_matches_exact_plan` fails if FlashInfer changes them.
- `VLLM_DEBUG_SEQ_LENS_BOUNDS=1` asserts `lower <= seq_lens <= upper` on the device in every build that uses the bounds. Off by default.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Answers to #29134</summary>

@yavarb reported three problems with planning drafts from the upper bound:
- Illegal memory access under load: the next `plan()` overwrote its pinned buffer during an upload. Here the wrapper takes a fresh buffer instead.
- Aliasing: the bounds here are new tensors. Nothing writes to the runner's pinned buffers.
- Lower acceptance length: there the kernel attended over the upper-bound window. Here fa2 reads the exact lengths. Acceptance length does not change.

</details>

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used.

title: [CI] Raise GSM8K startup max wait to 2400s for flaky 30B+ MoE eval configs
body:
## Summary

Deflakes the GSM8K eval configs whose failures cluster at the server-startup timeout. The harness already supports a per-config `startup_max_wait_seconds` key (`tests/evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py`, default `DEFAULT_STARTUP_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS = 1200`); this PR only raises it to 2400s on the flagged large-MoE configs. No harness code changes.

## Flaky tests addressed (Buildkite Test Engine, 28-day window)

| Test | Reliability | Failed/Passed | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_gsm8k_correctness[GLM-5.2-NVFP4-TP2-PCP2-EP]` | 0.338 | 96/145 | [link](https://buildkite.com/organizations/vllm/analytics/suites/ci-1/tests/d91a4034-dc55-8f30-b93e-f4adfce7ba94) |

| `test_gsm8k_correctness[Qwen3-30B-A3B-NvFp4-CT-fi-cutedsl-deepep-ll]` | 0.867 | 16/104 | duration_max 1226.7s ≈ 1200s cap; [link](https://buildkite.com/organizations/vllm/analytics/suites/ci-1/tests/64fd146b-d789-8124-9e26-9e1950e0a246) |
| `test_gsm8k_correctness[Qwen3-30B-A3B-Fp8-AutoFp8-deepgemm-deepep-ll]` | 0.875 | 15/105 | same harness/pattern (startup timeout + threshold jitter) |
| `test_gsm8k_correctness[Qwen3-30B-A3B-NvFp4-ModelOpt-fi-cutedsl-deepep-ll]` | 0.875 | 15/105 | same harness/pattern (startup timeout + threshold jitter) |

## Root cause

These configs serve 30B+ MoE models (DP2 + expert parallelism, `deepep_low_latency` all2all, DeepGEMM/CuTeDSL kernels). On contended GPU runners, model download + JIT kernel compilation + MoE weight loading push server startup past the 1200s default cap — measured `duration_max` of 1217–1228s sits right at the timeout, and the Fp8/NvFp4 deepep-ll siblings fail in lockstep (identical 16/104), indicating per-build infra slowness rather than a model bug.

## What changed

Set `startup_max_wait_seconds: 2400` (2 lines each) in:

- `tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-TP2-PCP2-EP.yaml`
- `tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/moe-refactor-dp-ep/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Fp8-CT-Block-deepgemm-deepep-ll.yaml`
- `tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/moe-refactor-dp-ep/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NvFp4-CT-fi-cutedsl-deepep-ll.yaml`
- `tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/moe-refactor-dp-ep/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Fp8-AutoFp8-deepgemm-deepep-ll.yaml`
- `tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/moe-refactor-dp-ep/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NvFp4-ModelOpt-fi-cutedsl-deepep-ll.yaml`

The key also feeds `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S`, so the engine-side ready window stays consistent with the client-side wait. Same approach as recent timeout raises in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57334 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57335.

Not touched: `Qwen3-30B-A3B-MXFP4A16-humming-act-fp8-block` (rel 0.469, 17/32) — its config was intentionally removed in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54099.

## Masking-risk assessment

Low. This only widens the server-startup budget; the accuracy assertion (`measured >= threshold - tolerance`) is unchanged, so no regression in model quality can be masked. The only cost is that a genuinely hung server takes up to 2400s (instead of 1200s) to fail on these five configs. No accuracy thresholds were re-baselined — that needs run data (mean − 2σ over recent passing runs) and is left as follow-up, along with pre-staging model weights on runners and splitting startup-timeout from accuracy failures in Test Engine analytics (related: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34333).

## Testing

No GPU on the authoring machine; these are YAML-only changes. Verified: all five configs parse with `yaml.safe_load` and expose `startup_max_wait_seconds == 2400`; pre-commit hooks pass on the commit. The harness already reads this key (covered by existing configs such as `DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4.yaml`).

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for "gsm8k startup timeout" / "startup_max_wait_seconds" — no open PR covers these configs.

title: [RFC]: Asymmetric P/D Deployment for DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash
body:
## Summary. DeepSeek-V4.1's bounded-replay structure creates an opportunity to make Prefill/Decode disaggregation substantially more asymmetric. Today, a Prefill worker still loads the full 40-layer model even though, after layer 20, only the final 128 prompt tokens need to be processed. This keeps almost half of the model weights resident on P for a small decoder-layer workload whose MoE utilization is likely poor. This RFC proposes moving that final 128-token window entirely to the Decode worker: - For a prompt of length `N`, P computes only `[0, N-128)` and transfers the resulting prefix KV state. - D computes `[N-128, N)` as its first full-model step and samples the first output token. - The request then continues through normal speculative decode with `q_len = 1 + num_spec_tokens`. This asymmetry has two main benefits. - First, P would load only the causal encoder plus the minimal layer-20 KV/Indexer projection path, potentially removing close to half of its transformer-layer weights; a key target is fitting a production Prefill replica on one B300 GPU. - Second, moving the decoder-layer work to D increases the computational intensity of that work by executing it as part of D's much larger token batches, improving utilization relative to processing the 128-token replay on P. The execution model on D also becomes simpler than layer-local decoder replay. D never needs separate encoder and decoder token batches: ```text first D step: all L0-L39 process the same 128 prompt tokens later D steps: all L0-L39 process the same 1 + num_spec_tokens tokens ``` The trade-off is that each newly admitted request contributes 128 bounded-prefill tokens to a D step, which can temporarily increase the Decode token count and affect ITL (TPOT). This incremental cost is expected to be modest for DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash: its light KV cache permits large Decode batches, and DSpark also makes each Decode batch process many tokens. Against that baseline, adding 128 tokens when a new request is admitted is a relatively small increase. This RFC is a design proposal for discussion. I do not currently plan to implement it, and there is no prototype or benchmark result yet. Implementation ownership is open. ## Proposed Change. ### Model placement and token ownership ```mermaid flowchart LR I[Prompt: N tokens] I -->|Prefix: N-W tokens| P I -->|Final window: W tokens| D subgraph P[Prefill worker: partial model] PE[Causal encoder L0-L19] PK[Minimal L20 Main-KV / Indexer
projection path] PE --> PK end subgraph D[Decode worker: full model] BR[First step: bounded prefill
L0-L39, q_len = W] FT[Sample first output token] ND[Later steps: speculative decode
L0-L39, q_len = 1 + num_spec_tokens] BR --> FT --> ND end P -->|Prefix Main / Indexer KV| D ``` For prompts no longer than `W`, P performs no model forward and D processes the complete prompt. Conceptually, P would retain: - embeddings and complete layers L0-L19; - the minimal layer-20 projections needed to produce its canonical C1 Main KV and Indexer K; and - the state required by the KV connector handoff. P would not retain the complete layer-20 attention/MoE path, layers 21–39, final normalization, or the LM head. ### Request flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant P as Prefill worker participant D as Decode worker P->>P: Run prompt prefix [0, N-W) P->>P: Produce prefix Main/Indexer KV P->>D: Send prefix KV D->>D: First step: run final W prompt tokens D->>D: Sample first output token D->>D: Later steps: normal speculative decode ``` Moving first-token generation to Decode is intentional. To minimize changes to the P-node scheduler, the P-node can compute the entire prompt (N tokens) instead of (N−W) tokens, since W is generally much smaller than N and the resulting redundant computation is negligible. ### Uniform Decode execution Decode has two full-model step shapes: ```text new request, first step: q_len = W active layers = L0-L39 later speculative decode steps: q_len = 1 + num_spec_tokens active layers = L0-L39 ``` The first step is a bounded prefill using the transferred prefix state. After sampling, the request joins normal speculative decoding. This avoids changing the token set after layer 20. The attention history differs by cache group, but the query rows do not: - prefix-cacheable Main/Indexer groups read the transferred prefix state; - SWA groups are rebuilt locally over the replay window, following the mechanism in #56227; and - every layer executes the same `W` query rows in the first D step. If bounded-prefill requests and ongoing decode requests are scheduled together, their request-level `q_len` values differ. This step is a non-uniform batch and may fallback to piecewise cudagraph. ## Why This May Help. ### Smaller Prefill replicas Prefill node no longer needs the complete decoder stack or LM head. This is expected to remove close to **`half of the weights`** from each Prefill node. The exact saving depends on embeddings, KV pools, connector buffers, CUDA graphs, and allocator headroom. For DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash, savings map straight to GPUs: tiny KV cache + offloading make Prefill HBM weight-bound, so halving transformer weights nearly halves the Prefill GPU count. A key target is fitting one production Prefill replica on a single B300 GPU. ### Avoid a low-density late-decoder tail on P The bounded replay contains at most 128 tokens per new request. Running it on P produces a small decoder-layer token workload and low arithmetic intensity because Prefill batchsize is usually small. In this proposal, D executes the final window as an ordinary full-model bounded-prefill step. It can batch multiple newly admitted requests and coordinate them with the larger Decode workload to get a **`higher arithmetic intensity`**. ### Simpler, unified model execution The split is by workers and token ranges, not by layer ranges within a forward: - P runs the entire model (encoder + layer-20 KV/Indexer projection path) on the prompt, using the same workload throughout each step—no workload reset between encoder and decoder layers. - D runs the entire model (encoder + decoder) on the bounded final window or normal decode workload. This makes the execution architecture **`simpler and more uniform`**, while naturally accommodating Chunked Prefill, Prefix Caching, and Context Parallelism. ### Cost and Trade-offs. The main cost is a larger first step on D: ```text new request, first step: q_len <= 128 later steps: q_len = 1 + num_spec_tokens ``` Potential costs include: - D must support both bounded-prefill and speculative-decode shapes. - Admission bursts may increase ITL/TPOT for running requests. - Mixing both request types in one scheduler iteration may require piecewise CUDA graphs or eager fallback. This is likely **`acceptable`** for DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash because its compressed KV cache permits a **`large Decode batch`**, and steps admitting new requests are usually a small fraction of all Decode steps. This requires measurement. ## Relationship to Existing vLLM Work. This proposal builds on, but is different from, two open vLLM PRs. ### #56227: encoder-side SWA bounded replay [#56227](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56227) already provides much of the required runtime behavior: - after a local or KV-connector prefix hit ending at `H`, the scheduler rewinds the final window; - the worker recomputes `[H-W, H)` locally; - Main/Indexer KV remains cached or transferred, while SWA is rebuilt locally; and - `Request.replay_start` and attention metadata floor the replay window. This PR is nearly orthogonal to the current RFC and provides sound logic for the P node's execution. ### #56752: decoder-side SWA bounded replay [#56752](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56752) compacts the batch after layer 20 so layers 21–39 process only each request's trailing window. That design still performs one forward in which different layer ranges process different token sets: ```text L0-L20: full prompt rows L21-L39: trailing W rows ``` This RFC proposes a different deployment boundary: ```text P: [0, N-W), L0-L19 and L20's KV/Indexer projection path D: [N-W, N), through all L0-L39 ``` Within a Decode step, every layer processes the same rows. There is no layer-20 compaction boundary, internal gather/scatter, or replay-layer sub-batch. ### Feedback Period. ### CC List. _No response_ ### Any Other Things. _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Model] Use upstream GLM-5.3 and Qwen4-Exp configs and processor
body:
## Purpose

Transformers ships `glm5_next` as of **v5.16.1** and `qwen4_exp` as of **v5.16.0**, so the vendored copies can go. Raises the `transformers` floor in `requirements/common.txt` from `>= 5.10.4` to `>= 5.16.1` — CI already pins `transformers==5.16.1` exactly in `requirements/test/{cuda,rocm,xpu}.in`, so this only makes the declared minimum match what is already tested.

Removed:

- `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/glm5_next.py` (420 lines)
- `vllm/transformers_utils/processors/glm5next.py` (953 lines)
- `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/qwen4_exp.py`
- `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/config.py`

Net **-1961 lines**.

### Not a straight deletion

The upstream classes are not drop-in replacements, so the model code moves to their spellings:

| vLLM read | upstream ships |
|---|---|
| `mla_nope` | `mla_use_nope` |
| `num_experts_per_token` | `num_experts_per_tok` |
| `moe_renormalize` | `norm_topk_prob` |
| `mhc_num_residual_streams` | `hc_mult` |
| `mhc_sinkhorn_iterations` | `hc_sinkhorn_iters` |

`is_moe` / `is_kda_layer` / `is_linear_attn` now derive from `layer_types`, and text-level reads go through `hf_text_config` now that the top-level config no longer mirrors its `text_config` via `__getattribute__`.

I verified the rename table by loading the real `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` `config.json` through upstream's `Glm5NextConfig` and diffing the resolved attribute surface against every attribute the model tree reads.

### Behaviour deliberately preserved

Three things in the vendored code were intentional divergences, not schema, and are kept with their explanations:

1. **Vision `rms_norm_eps` stays 1e-6.** The checkpoint ships 1e-5 and upstream honours it; the vendored config force-overrode it because 1e-5 "produces repetitive/degraded image descriptions". Now a named constant at its single call site.
2. **The frame sampler moves to `Glm5NextVideoBackend._sample_frame_indices`**, its only consumer, rather than being replaced by upstream's `sample_frames`. See the open question below — this one is worth a second look.
3. **The `NotImplementedError` guards** for config options this implementation lacks move into `_validate_supported_config`, called from `Glm5NextModel.__init__`.

Three GLM-5.3 values have no source in either the checkpoint or the upstream config, so they become named constants rather than silently-missing attributes: `mhc_tau` (0.05), `mhc_post_mult_value` (2.0), `logit_scale` (1.0).

### Hybrid layer accounting

Both vendored configs supplied a `layers_block_type` property that mapped their sparse-attention layer type onto `"attention"`. Without it, `ModelConfig.get_num_layers_by_block_type` falls through to its `layer_types` branch, which only recognised `"full_attention"` — so both models would have counted **zero** attention layers. It now counts `deepseek_sparse_attention` and `qwen_sparse_attention` too, which is what both properties did.

`_get_full_attention_layer_indices` in the turboquant config has the same blind spot, but it already checks `layer_types` first and so is unchanged by this PR. Flagging it as a separate pre-existing issue rather than widening scope here.

### Open question: the frame sampler

This PR keeps vLLM's own frame sampler, but I am not confident that is the right call and would like a view on it.

The sampler's docstring justifies diverging from the reference implementation by noting that the linspace variant "cost 4 points on video grounding evals". That comment describes only the **short-clip** branch (`total_frames < extract_t`), which requires `fps < 2`; I could not construct a case where that branch differs from upstream at all.

The branch that does differ is the common one, for an unrelated reason: vLLM walks at `1/(temporal_patch_size * target_fps)` (0.25s), collecting ~2x the candidates, then re-spreads them with `linspace`. Upstream walks at `1/target_fps` (0.5s) and keeps its picks. Over a sweep of realistic sources, **38/53 cases differ** — same frame counts, different indices:

| case | vLLM | upstream |
|---|---|---|
| 30s @30fps | `0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 76, 91, 106` | `0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90, 105` |
| 3 frames @2fps | `0, 1, 2, 2` | `0, 1` |

vLLM's spacing drifts off the target fps and short sources pick up a duplicated tail frame from the odd-parity pad. There is also no consistency argument for keeping our own: `create_hf_metadata` sets `do_sample_frames = len(valid_frame_indices) == source.total_frames_num`, so whenever the backend sub-samples the processor is told not to re-sample, and the backend's choice is authoritative either way.

So switching to upstream's `sample_frames` would delete the last vendored piece and looks more correct on the merits — but it changes frame selection for nearly every video, so it needs a video eval that I could not run. Keeping ours (what this PR does) preserves exactly what ships today at no eval cost. Happy to switch if a reviewer with a GPU wants to take the eval.

### Dropped code left over from Qwen3-Next — please sanity-check

`Qwen4ExpDecoderLayer` selected between a MoE block and a dense `Qwen3NextMLP`:

```python
mlp_only_layers = getattr(config, "mlp_only_layers", [])
num_experts = getattr(config, "num_experts", 0) or 0
absolute_layer_id = self.layer_idx + 1
is_moe_layer = self.layer_idx not in mlp_only_layers and (
    num_experts > 0 and absolute_layer_id % config.decoder_sparse_step == 0
)
```

This is a verbatim lift of `qwen3_next.py:479-485`, which arrived with the original support PR (#53896) — Qwen4Exp derives from Qwen3-Next and still subclasses `Qwen3NextAttention` and `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock`. `decoder_sparse_step` and `mlp_only_layers` are Qwen3-Next concepts; upstream's `Qwen4ExpTextConfig` declares neither, and neither appears anywhere in `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` or `...-FP8`. They only resolved because the vendored config subclassed `Qwen3NextConfig` and inherited them, which is why nothing ever flagged the branch as dead.

Evaluating the original expression against both checkpoints with the old vendored config gives `is_moe_layer` **True for 48/48 layers**, no dense layers: with `mlp_only_layers=[]`, `num_experts=512` and `decoder_sparse_step=1` it reduces to `True` for any layer index. So this PR builds the MoE block unconditionally and drops the branch, its guards and the `Qwen3NextMLP` import (`-38/+6`).

Worth a second opinion, since it is a deletion rather than a rename: a hypothetical future checkpoint setting `mlp_only_layers` or `decoder_sparse_step` would previously have been honoured and now would not. Upstream's `qwen4_exp` has no dense path at all (neither key appears in the model, and `validate_architecture` requires `num_experts > 0`), so such a checkpoint would not load in transformers either — which is why I think dropping it is right. Happy to restore it as `getattr(config, "decoder_sparse_step", 1)` with only the dead `else` removed if a reviewer would rather keep the guard.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_config.py \
       tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py \
       tests/transformers_utils/test_config.py \
       tests/multimodal/test_video.py \
       tests/test_config.py
pre-commit run --all-files
```

Also ran a differential check of the vendored vs upstream `smart_resize` across an 8232-point grid of sizes, frame counts and token budgets, since upstream denominates its bounds in vision tokens where the vendored one took raw pixels.

## Test Result

Every suite was run on this branch **and** on the base commit in a second worktree, because this machine has pre-existing video-codec failures.

| suite | base | branch |
|---|---|---|
| the four files above | 24 failed, 433 passed, 18 skipped | 24 failed, **430** passed, 18 skipped |
| `tests/multimodal/test_video.py` | 14 failed, 70 passed, 6 skipped | 14 failed, 70 passed, 6 skipped |

**Identical failure sets.** The −3 passed is exactly accounted for: 7 removed cases that tested the vendored config's own behaviour, 4 added for the relocated layer-type accounting. The 24 pre-existing failures are macOS video-codec and unrelated `test_vllm_config_defaults` / `test_ir_op_priority_ctx` cases, all failing identically at the base commit.

`smart_resize` differential: **8232/8232 agree, 0 mismatches.**

`pre-commit run` passes on all changed files, including `mypy`.

Both public checkpoints were loaded through the upstream config classes to check the ported attribute surface directly, rather than inferring it:

- `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next`: **37/39** attributes the model tree reads resolve; the two that do not are `decoder_sparse_step` and `intermediate_size`, both discussed above.
- `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`: every renamed field resolves to the expected value, and the three with no source anywhere are the named constants above.

Layer accounting on the real `layer_types`, which both vendored `layers_block_type` properties used to supply:

| checkpoint | layer_types | attention | linear_attention |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next | 36 `linear_attention`, 12 `qwen_sparse_attention` | 12 | 36 |
| GLM-5.3-Flash | 34 `linear_attention`, 11 `deepseek_sparse_attention` | 11 | 34 |

Both sum to the full layer count. Without the `get_num_layers_by_block_type` change, both would report **0** attention layers.

### Not covered

- **No GPU here, so no model eval was run.** The change is intended to be behaviour-preserving and the value-level equivalences above were verified statically against the real checkpoint config, but a multimodal smoke test on GLM-5.3-Flash would be worth having before merge — the vision `rms_norm_eps` path in particular fails silently rather than loudly if it regresses.

## Notes

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change.

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Fix SM120 sparse-MLA prefill IMA with DSpark speculative decoding (#56771)
body:
When running DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on SM120 with DSpark speculative decoding, long-prompt prefill chunks triggered an Illegal Memory Access (IMA) in FlashInfer's sparse-MLA backend. This PR fixes the underlying memory aliasing, stride mismatch, and out-of-bounds loads.

## Root Cause

1. Workspace memory aliasing under CUDA graphs:
With DSpark speculative decoding, decode verification is captured inside CUDA graphs while prefill chunks run eagerly. Both paths were sharing a single 128MB workspace buffer from `_flashinfer_dsv4_workspace_by_device`. Eager prefill chunks overwrote scratchpad memory that the active decode graph expected to remain valid, corrupting memory during graph execution.

2. Index tensor geometry mismatch:
FlashInfer's sparse MLA decode kernel expects a 3D coordinate layout `(num_tokens, 1, topk)`. The decode path already reshapes its indices to 3D, but `_forward_prefill` passed a 2D tensor `(num_prefill_tokens, topk)`. FlashInfer accessed this buffer using 3D stride assumptions, which caused pointer calculations to index out of bounds on longer prompts.

3. Unbounded block table loads and uninitialized memory:
In `_compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens_kernel`, loads from `block_table_ptr` lacked upper-bound checks against `block_table_stride`. Large local indices read past the request row in the block table. In addition, outputs in `compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens` were allocated using `torch.empty`, leaving uninitialized garbage when reusing memory from CUDA caching pools.

## Changes

- Workspace isolation: Separated prefill workspace allocation using `is_prefill=True` in `_get_flashinfer_dsv4_workspace` so eager prefill runs in its own memory buffer without interfering with decode graphs.
- 3D index layout: Reshaped `extra_sparse_indices` to 3D `(num_prefill_tokens, 1, -1)` in `_forward_prefill`, matching the decode path.
- Triton kernel hardening:
  - Initialized `global_topk_indices` with `-1` and `topk_lens` with `0`.
  - Added bounds checking: `valid_block = is_valid_token & (req_idx >= 0) & is_valid & (block_indices >= 0) & (block_indices < block_table_stride)` with `safe_req_idx = tl.maximum(req_idx, 0)` and `mask=mask & valid_block, other=-1`.
  - Added early exit `if num_tokens == 0:` to protect against empty grid launches.
  - Kept the original 12-parameter kernel signature intact to avoid recompilation churn.
- Regression tests: Added tests in `tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py` covering workspace isolation, 3D index geometry, and empty token batch handling.

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Fix DCP pulls across MLA cache regions
body:
When prefill and decode use different cache-group layouts, as with a HiSparse decoder, NIXL matches their KV blocks by memory region. That receive path currently assumes a single source rank and fails when a DCP prefiller supplies multiple ranks.

Create a read for each source rank using the existing region mapping. For each region, reuse `_apply_dcp_prefix_caching` to select the pages owned by that rank and skip the decoder's cached prefix. Bound the reads by the sequence length and zero any remaining allocation padding. The ordinary DCP path stays unchanged. Requires unshared MLA regions with matching logical/kernel page sizes.

Independent of #55398's GPU-landing feature; #57077 covers DCP1 only.

### Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py -m cpu_test -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/pull_worker.py vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py
```

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Guard record_transfer against None telemetry
body:
## Title
[Bugfix][NIXL] Guard `record_transfer` against `None` telemetry

## Body

### Problem
Some NIXL backends do not enable transfer telemetry capture by default (UCX without `NIXL_TELEMETRY_ENABLE=1`, OBJ in some configs). In these cases `get_xfer_telemetry()` returns `None` instead of an `nixlXferTelemetry` struct. The current code at `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py` calls `self.xfer_stats.record_transfer(res)` unconditionally, so with `res is None` it raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'xferDuration'`. The surrounding `try/except Exception` block catches the `AttributeError` and marks the request as a transfer failure (`transfer_exception`), invalidates the blocks, and downstream workers report the request as failed. With Dynamo P/D disaggregation, the frontend returns HTTP 500 to the client. This bug is independent of any specific NIXL backend; it triggers whenever a backend reports `xfer_state == "DONE"` but cannot populate telemetry.

### Reproduction
Deploy DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D disaggregation on NVIDIA H200 hardware with the NIXL UCX backend. `NixlBaseConnectorWorker` calls `get_xfer_telemetry()` per DONE handle. The UCX plugin returns `None` (no telemetry buffer allocated by default). `record_transfer(None)` raises `AttributeError`, the request is marked failed, and Dynamo returns HTTP 500. Stack trace excerpt from production deploy (2026-09-17):

```
ERROR vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.nixl.base_worker:_pop_done_transfers:3031
Marking blocks as invalid
transfer_exception
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'xferDuration'
```

The error is logged at WARN/ERROR level on every KV transfer completion, so log noise alone makes this impossible to ignore in production.

### Fix
Guard `record_transfer()` so we only record telemetry when the backend actually returned data:

```python
res = self.nixl_wrapper.get_xfer_telemetry(handle)
if res is not None:
    self.xfer_stats.record_transfer(res)
self.nixl_wrapper.release_xfer_handle(handle)
```

This is a minimal, behavior-preserving change for backends that DO return telemetry. For backends that don't, the metric just isn't recorded for that transfer, which is preferable to marking the transfer as failed.

### Related
- #55576 (open) addresses a sibling case (OBJ tier explicitly enabling telemetry). My fix is complementary: even with telemetry fully enabled, defensive None-guarding prevents future backends from triggering the same crash.
- #35876 (open) reworks throughput computation (different metric path).

### Test plan
- Run existing unit tests under `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/`.
- Add a regression test that mocks `get_xfer_telemetry` to return `None` and verifies the transfer is released cleanly without raising.

### Before/After diff

```diff
                 try:
                     xfer_state = self.nixl_wrapper.check_xfer_state(handle)
                     if xfer_state == "DONE":
+                        # Some NIXL backends (e.g. UCX without NIXL_TELEMETRY_ENABLE, OBJ in some configs) return None from get_xfer_telemetry() when telemetry capture is not enabled. Without this guard, record_transfer(None) crashes and the surrounding except marks the transfer as failed.
                         res = self.nixl_wrapper.get_xfer_telemetry(handle)
-                        self.xfer_stats.record_transfer(res)
+                        if res is not None:
+                            self.xfer_stats.record_transfer(res)
                         self.nixl_wrapper.release_xfer_handle(handle)
```

title: [Bugfix] Fail closed in is_uva_available() when the UVA alias is not live
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57224. Related: #57562, #57680.

`is_uva_available()` only checks that pinned memory is available. That is necessary but not sufficient: the callers depend on the device view being a live alias of the host tensor, and nothing verifies that.

Under NVIDIA Confidential Computing, a `pin_memory=True` allocation stays page-locked but `is_pinned()` reports False. `get_accelerator_view_from_cpu_tensor` is gated on `is_pinned()`, so it takes the non-pinned branch and returns a detached one-time copy instead of a live view. Writes made after the view is created never reach the device. The V2 model runner fills its UVA buffers after creating them, so per-request sampling parameters arrive on the GPU as zeros and generation degenerates. Requests still return 200.

Because the predicate stays `True`, none of the existing fallbacks can engage. `NonUvaBuffer` from #56908 is only selected when it is `False`, `StagedWriteTensor` keeps the large tensors in UVA, and the weight offloader and the Engram models skip their guards.

This probes the contract at runtime: create the view, write to the host tensor afterwards, and confirm the device sees it. The probe needs an initialized accelerator, so callers that run before the worker sets its device get an optimistic answer that is not cached, and the worker-side call decides. It fails closed, since the fallback paths are correct and only slower. `@cache` moves from the predicate to the probe, so the answer is still resolved once per process.

Duplicate-work checks found no open PR that changes `is_uva_available()` itself. #50671 removes the `is_pinned()` gate in `cuda_view.cu` so the mapping is attempted where the hardware supports it; this is the other half, making the predicate honest so vLLM degrades safely where it does not. #54655 and #47579 consume the predicate rather than changing it. #52226 adds `is_confidential_compute()` for decode performance and is MRV1 only.

Hardware measurements are in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50671#issuecomment-5712253233

## Test Plan

Cherry-picked onto `main` and built on an H100 NVL with Confidential Computing enabled (driver 595.84, CUDA 13, torch 2.13.0), single GPU, `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`.

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/core/test_uva.py -v
```

Serving before and after, where "before" reverts only the predicate:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct --port 8100 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.30
# prompt: "Write one sentence about the sea.", max_tokens=40
# 3 seeds each at temperature 0.0 and 1.5
```

Control on a non-CC A100-SXM4-40GB (driver 580.82.07, torch 2.11.0+cu128), calling the CUDA runtime directly with no vLLM in the loop, to confirm the probe still passes on ordinary hardware.

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `typos` at the pinned pre-commit versions.

## Test Result

### Predicate

On the CC box `is_uva_available()` now returns `False` and logs the mismatch:

```
UVA reports available but the device view is not a live alias of host memory:
wrote [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8], device read [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0].
Falling back to explicit copies. This is expected under GPU Confidential Computing.
```

Unpatched it returned `True`. A driver-level probe confirms zero-copy itself is live on this hardware and only the torch pinned view is detached, so the failure is the alias contract rather than the GPU.

### Serving, before the fix

Predicate reverted, UVA path active:

```
=== temperature=0.0 ===
httphttphttphttphttphttphttphttphttphttphttphttphttphttphttphttp
://://://://://://://://://://://://://://://://://://://://://://
!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
```

Degenerate at every temperature, 200 throughout.

### Serving, after the fix

```
=== temperature=0.0 ===
The vast expanse of the ocean is a breathtaking sight to behold, with its endless blue
waters and diverse marine life.
(identical across all 3 seeds)

=== temperature=1.5 ===
The sea is a vast expanse of saltwater that covers much of Earth's surface, with waves
and tides creating beautiful scenery.
The vast expanse of blue and green waters stretches endlessly, teeming with marine life
in this awe-inspiring natural wonder.
The sea is a vast body of salty water that surrounds the Earth's continents and plays an
important role in shaping the planet's climate and environment.
(3 distinct outputs)
```

Greedy is deterministic again and temperature is respected.

### Control on non-CC hardware

Same sequence, one variable changed:

```
                              A100 (no CC)      H100 NVL (CC on)
Tensor.is_pinned()            True              False
cudaHostGetDevicePointer      0 (no error)      0 (no error)
host wrote                    [1..8]            [1..8]
device read                   [1..8]            [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
coherence                     LIVE              DETACHED
```

The probe passes on ordinary hardware, so the predicate still returns `True` there and UVA stays enabled. Only the CC case flips.

### Unit tests

`test_uva_unavailable_when_view_is_detached` and `test_uva_unavailable_when_probe_raises` pass. `test_uva_available_when_alias_is_live` skips on the CC box, which is correct for that hardware.

The first run on CC also surfaced a problem in the file's existing guards. `@skipif(not is_uva_available())` is evaluated at collection time, before the accelerator is initialized, so it saw the optimistic `True` and the CC-dependent tests ran instead of skipping. The guard now resolves after initializing the device, and the two tests that patch the view no longer carry it since they do not need working UVA.

`benchmarks/benchmark_pin_memory.py` called `cache_clear()` on the predicate, so both call sites now point at the probe.

Lint, format and typos are clean.

## Notes

No throughput measurement for the explicit-copy path. It only engages where UVA is already broken, and the alternative there is incorrect output.

Not exercised: the weight offloader, `model_loader/utils.py`, the Engram models, and TP. They gate on the same predicate and should now fail with a clear error rather than corrupt silently.

The CC build used a 0.29.0 precompiled wheel over `main` sources because no per-commit cu130 wheel exists, so unrelated compiled-path failures in that run are ABI noise. The predicate result is corroborated independently by the driver-level probe.

Independently validated on an Azure H100 NVL with AMD SEV-SNP: greedy output matches V1 on 8/8 prompts, the #57562 repro completes 12/12, and decode throughput is on par with V1 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57224#issuecomment-5910454602).

AI assistance was used in preparing this change. I have reviewed every changed line and ran the tests listed above.

title: [ROCm][Spec Decode] Compact probabilistic Kimi-K3 synthetic verifier suffix
body:
## Summary
- extend Kimi-K3 synthetic verifier suffix compaction to probabilistic DSpark drafts
- for K=3 / synthetic acceptance length 3, execute 3 target rows instead of 4
- retain the first zero-rate draft as the rejection/recovery row; only the unreachable bonus row is omitted
- preserve full draft logits and residual sampling for probabilistic rejection

This is a separate follow-up to #57048. It is stacked on that PR until #57048 merges; the follow-up-specific change is the second commit.

## Correctness
For K=3 / AL=3, the minimum-variance unconditional schedule is `[1, 1, 0]`. Two draft positions are always accepted and the third is always the rejection/recovery position, making the fourth target bonus row unreachable.

The implementation remains opt-in through `VLLM_KIMI_K3_SYNTHETIC_VERIFY_COMPACTION=1` and continues to reject adaptive verification.

## Validation
- 20 focused CPU tests pass, including the already-compacted K=3 warmup layout
- probabilistic compact/full GPU outputs match exactly at temperatures 0.7 and 1.0
- MI355X TP8, K=3 / AL=3, probabilistic DSpark drafts, matched 1200-second AgentX A/B results:
  - conc=4: p90 interactivity +1.03%; throughput -0.99%
  - conc=8: p90 interactivity +4.61%; throughput +1.37%
  - conc=10: p90 interactivity +4.56%; throughput +1.65%
  - conc=14: p90 interactivity +6.05%; throughput +1.82%

These matched 1200-second A/B results are the performance evidence for this PR; no 3600-second uplift claim is made without a matched full-run control.

title: [Perf][Attention] Run non-causal DFlash draft rows on the Triton 3D kernel
body:
## Purpose

A DFlash/DSpark drafter sends `1 + k` non-causal query rows per request. On `TRITON_ATTN`,
`unified_attention` only takes the segmented 3D launch for single-token rows, so draft
rows always run the 2D launch. Its cost grows with context: at batch 8 and 131k tokens,
one draft attention call takes 6.1 ms.

**`triton_unified_attention.py`**
- Non-causal multi-token rows may take the 3D launch when the softmax scratch holds every
  query token. Batches with a sliding window, sinks, an image-prefix mask, a quantized KV
  cache or too little scratch keep the 2D launch.
- Causal rows keep their current routing.

**`triton_attn.py`**
- Only builders for a non-causal speculator (`attention_config.use_non_causal` with a
  speculative config) size the scratch per draft token:
  `min(seq_threshold_3D, max_num_seqs) * (1 + k)` rows, and 128 segments on ROCm.
  All other builders keep their current scratch.
- The scratch head size comes from the group's KV cache spec. The draft builder is given
  the target's model config, so for Kimi-K3 it used the MLA head size (576, padded to
  1024) instead of the drafter's 64.

`reduce_segments` is unchanged, so single-token decode compiles and runs exactly as before.

### Why this is not a duplicate

- **#56148** (open) adds a 3D route for *causal* speculative verify and explicitly keeps
  non-causal rows on 2D. Both PRs change the scratch sizing in `TritonAttentionMetadataBuilder`
  and the `max_seqlen_q > 1` condition, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.
  #56148 sizes the scratch for every builder with a speculative config; this PR only
  for non-causal draft builders.
- **#44652** (open, stale since June, merge conflicts) relaxed the condition to
  `max_seqlen_q <= 16` for all rows but kept the per-sequence scratch, so a multi-token
  batch can write past it. Its non-causal support has since landed separately.

## Test Plan

Unit A/B on 8x AMD MI325X, ROCm nightly `af1c01499b`, same tests in both arms: upstream
`main`'s two files vs this branch's.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_triton_attn_metadata_builder.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention_diffkv.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py::test_non_causal_backend_correctness \
  tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py::test_causal_backend_correctness
```

New and changed tests:
- `test_triton_unified_attn_multi_query_3d`: non-causal q_len 3/4 rows at contexts 7, 1536
  and 8192 plus a cudagraph padding request take the 3D launch and match the reference;
  causal rows and a too-small scratch stay on 2D and also match.
- `test_3d_scratch_holds_draft_tokens_only_for_non_causal_drafts`: only a non-causal draft
  builder gets per-token rows; the scratch head size follows the KV spec.
- `NON_CAUSAL_BACKENDS_TO_TEST` now includes `TRITON_ATTN`; its small batches take the new
  3D launch.

Speed: CUDA-graph replay of `unified_attention`, one GPU per arm, then swapped.

End to end: Kimi-K3 TP8 + DSpark (`num_speculative_tokens` 3), 8x MI325X, c=8, same-prompt
decode differential with the first probe discarded, drafter on `ROCM_AITER_FA` vs
`TRITON_ATTN` with this change, one boot each on the same node.

## Test Result

**Unit tests:** no test goes from pass to fail.
- The new kernel test passes 12/12; upstream fails its 4 non-causal 3D cases.
- The builder test passes 4/4; upstream fails all 4.
- `test_triton_unified_attention.py` and `test_triton_unified_attention_diffkv.py`
  otherwise pass identically in both arms.
- Backend correctness: all 93 pass (3 non-causal, including `TRITON_ATTN`, and 90 causal).
  Our environment cannot download the gated Meta-Llama-3-8B config, so these ran with
  `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, which has the same attention geometry (32 query heads, 8 KV heads,
  head size 128).
- CUDA was not tested; the change is platform-independent except the ROCm segment count.

**Kernel speed** (µs per call, median, both GPU orders):

| case | upstream | this PR |
|---|--:|--:|
| decode q_len 1, B=8, 1k (3D) | 19.4 / 19.7 | 19.5 / 19.1 |
| decode q_len 1, B=8, 8k (3D) | 75.3 / 73.0 | 73.5 / 73.6 |
| decode q_len 1, B=32, 8k (2D) | 469.0 / 469.6 | 469.5 / 468.4 |
| causal verify q_len 4, B=8, 8k (2D) | 324.5 / 324.8 | 322.9 / 324.0 |
| causal prefill 2048 (2D) | 350.3 / 346.4 | 348.6 / 347.7 |
| draft q_len 4, B=8, 8k, 16 / 128 segments | 317.4 | 36.0 / 30.9 |
| draft q_len 4, B=8, 131k, 16 / 128 segments | 6069.7 | 509.0 / 272.4 |
| draft q_len 4, B=1, 8k, 128 segments | 244.2 | 14.7 |
| draft q_len 4, B=16, 8k, 128 segments | 316.6 | 47.8 |

Existing paths use Llama-3-8B shapes (32/8 heads, head 128); draft rows use the Kimi-K3
drafter's per-rank shape at TP8 (8/2 heads, head 64).

**End to end at 150k** (step = 8 x acceptance / tok/s):

| drafter attention | tok/s | acceptance | step ms |
|---|---|---|--:|
| `ROCM_AITER_FA` | 429.9, 456.1, 433.2 | 2.99, 2.99, 3.04 | 54.7 |
| `TRITON_ATTN`, this PR | 499.8, 508.0, 501.4 | 3.03, 3.01, 3.04 | 48.1 |

Both arms ran the same Kimi-K3 stack apart from the drafter backend. That run used an
earlier revision with extra padding guards in `reduce_segments`; draft-row kernel time is
the same without them (272.4 µs in both). GSM8K (first 200, greedy) with this drafter path
on an earlier revision of the same stack: 97.0%, acceptance 3.66.

**With DCP:** Kimi-K3 TP8 + DCP8 on the moonmath DCP PR with this change: needle 3/3, GSM8K
97.0%, 8k 45.7 ms/step and 131k 51.1 ms/step, against 50.8 and 71.2 ms/step with the
drafter on `ROCM_AITER_FA` (same image, one boot each).

**Pre-commit:** ruff-check / ruff-format 0.14.0 and typos pass; mypy not run locally.

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Add moonmath kernels for gfx942 MXFP4 SiTU MoE and MLA decode, with decode context parallelism
body:
Stacked on **#56723**: the first commit is its net diff at `903e47e4fd`, unchanged. This PR is
the four commits after it (17 files, +862/-33). E2E results also use **#56434** (ROCm drafter
hidden-state fix) and, for the `TRITON_ATTN` drafter, **#57409**.

## Purpose

Kimi-K3 on AMD MI325X (gfx942) has no kernel for its MXFP4 SiTU MoE, no bf16-query / fp8-KV MLA
decode for its 12 heads per rank, and no MLA decode that works under decode context parallelism
(DCP). This PR adds them from the optional
[`moonmath_amd`](https://github.com/moonmath-ai/amd-kernels) package; without it nothing changes.

- **MoE** (`moonmath_mxfp4_moe.py`): `MoonmathW4A16SituExperts` subclasses the AITER W4A16
  experts and claims only SiTU. The routing weight is applied in an fp32 top-k reduce.
  `AITER_TRITON_MXFP4_BF16` aligns SiTU to 128, since the generic 256 round-up adds 33% MoE memory.
- **MLA** (`moonmath_mla.py`, `ROCM_MOONMATH_MLA`): subclasses the AITER MLA backend and replaces
  only decode and verify; batches outside the kernel's domain go to AITER.
- **DCP**: each rank's decode walks its shard using the global lengths and returns the LSE. To boot
  K3 with #56723 on ROCm:
  - `resolve_kv_cache_layout` keeps a layer-outer layout (padding the draft pages) when no
    backend has a block-outer one, instead of failing.
  - `AiterMLABackend` declares layer-contiguous layouts: its decode `.view()`s each layer's cache,
    which crashed under `BLNHC` with a `TRITON_ATTN` drafter.
- **AITER_FA**: accepts K3's unsplittable 1536-token drafter block, which failed at boot.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- No open PR adds these kernels. Other routes: #50813 and #53954 (quantized activations), #51274
  (int4), #50817 (AITER tile configs).
- #56723 needs a target backend that returns an LSE; this adds one for gfx942. #57085 and #56861
  cover `ROCM_AITER_MLA` with an MLA drafter; #52188 is NVIDIA.

## Test Plan

Unit tests on MI325X with ROCm nightly `0bfc7a15d0`, as shipped vs with this branch: the test files
this PR and #56723 touch, plus the AITER MLA / AITER_FA tests.

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_moonmath_mla.py tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_fa.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sink.py tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_cp_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_dspark_utils.py
```

E2E: Kimi-K3, TP8 + DCP8, c=8, same-prompt decode differential (first probe discarded).

```bash
vllm serve kimi-k3 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-model-len 163840 --moe-backend aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"kimi-k3-dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3,
                         "attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}'   # or TRITON_ATTN
```

## Test Result

**Unit:** no test goes from pass to fail, and all 99 new or DCP-specific tests pass. The 4 failures
are identical in both arms (a model not cached offline).

**E2E** (backends `ROCM_MOONMATH_MLA` and `MoonmathW4A16SituExperts`; step = 8 x acceptance / tok/s):

| | drafter `ROCM_AITER_FA` | drafter `TRITON_ATTN` (#57409) |
|---|---|---|
| Needle, 3 in ~120k | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| GSM8K, first 200, greedy | 97.0%, acceptance 3.66 | 97.0%, acceptance 3.65 |
| 8k decode | 470, 459, 465 tok/s (50.8 ms/step) | 504, 516, 539 tok/s (45.7 ms/step) |
| 131k decode | 322, 320, 334 tok/s (71.2 ms/step) | 429, 431, 491 tok/s (51.1 ms/step) |

GPU KV cache at DCP8: 5.08M tokens.

title: WIP: fix(decode bench): remember zero-token prefix fills
body:
DecodeBenchConnector currently records a request as filled only when the
  synthetic prefill contains at least one external token. A one-token prompt has
  a zero-token synthetic prefill, so a later preemption causes the connector to
  treat generated output as a new prompt and offer it as externally computed KV.

  With HiSparse, that false import can reach the host-only path at an arbitrary
  token offset and terminate the engine with:

  ValueError: A host-only HiSparse import must end on a cache-block boundary.

  This change records the completed one-shot lookup after allocation, even when
  the external token count is zero. This prevents generated history from being
  refilled after preemption while preserving retries after failed allocation.

  The reproduction used a two-node GLM-5.2-FP8 EP16 decode deployment with
  DecodeBenchConnector composed with HiSparseConnector, one input token, 10,624

title: [Core][Kernel] Share persistent workspaces for Marlin and Humming
body:
## Purpose

Co-authored by: ErinYin <liang.yin@daocloud.io>

Humming grouped MoE currently retains permutation scratch in every layer, so its persistent memory grows with the number of layers. Marlin lock buffers are also owned by individual layers or kernels, tying their lifetime to weight preparation and reload.

This PR gives both resources a shared owner in `WorkspaceManager`:

- Add `get_persistent_resource(key, factory)` for objects with stable storage and `get_persistent(...)` for fixed-shape tensors. Resources are cached separately for each `(ubatch, lane)` and must exist before workspace locking.
- Share compatible Humming `MoEPermuteScratch` objects across sequential layers. Compatibility includes capacity, routing dimensions, device, hidden size, and dtype.
- Acquire Marlin locks at execution time, with separate buffers for concurrent CUDA streams as well as ubatches and lanes. Zero-initialize once; successful Marlin calls restore their counters to zero.
- Resolve dense Marlin workspace lookup inside a runtime custom op so `torch.compile` does not trace execution-context selection.
- Preserve standalone allocation when no workspace manager exists and support explicit Marlin workspaces.

### Relationship to existing work

This combines the direction of #50626 and #56764 with a general resource API. #50626 is the earlier tensor-only Marlin implementation; #56764 adds a Humming-specific cache and accessor to `WorkspaceManager`. Here, the manager handles resource lifetime and execution-slot isolation, while each backend defines its own resource and compatibility key. The intent is to consolidate both changes around that shared API.

Addresses the memory issue in #56759 and relates to the runtime-storage ownership discussion in #48312. Searches for those issues and for `marlin workspace`, `workspace persistent`, and `humming scratch` found the related PRs above; the distinction is the combined, backend-independent resource API.

#55105 remains complementary: its dispatch-capacity and runtime-dtype fixes can feed into the shared scratch accessor, while its activation-buffer fixes stay in Humming. Those fixes are not included here.

## Test Plan

Tests cover resource reuse and locking, standalone fallback, isolation across execution slots and CUDA streams, weight-preparation behavior, and compiled Marlin execution. Permutation tests compare outputs with and without persistent scratch; CUDA graph tests change inputs, routing, and graph sizes to detect stale metadata or aliasing.

Latest targeted runs on NVIDIA B300:

```bash
# 488 passed
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py \
  -k 'permute or humming or workspace or persistent' --timeout=180 -q

# 20 passed
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py::test_moe_permute_scratch_isolated_across_execution_slots \
  tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py \
  tests/quantization/test_humming_ignore.py --timeout=180 -q

# 1 passed; run with FlashInfer 0.6.17 pinned via PYTHONPATH
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py::test_moe_permute_scratch_reused_across_graph_sizes \
  --timeout=180 -q

# 112 passed, 13 skipped
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_tile_padding.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py \
  -k 'marlin or workspace' --timeout=180 -q

# 1 passed
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_gemm.py -k persistent_locks -q

.venv/bin/pre-commit run
git diff --check
```

All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, formatting, mypy, and repository checks.

Before publication, the commit was rebased onto `f3aa88d230`. The only conflict was an obsolete Marlin workspace docstring; the implementation was preserved. Hooks passed again, followed by **60 passed** in this focused run (FlashInfer 0.6.17 pinned via `PYTHONPATH`):

```bash
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_gemm.py \
  -k 'persistent or humming or scratch or marlin_prepare_layer or marlin_post_load or marlin_workspace' \
  --timeout=180 -q
```

## Test Result

### Humming memory

Before the rebase, compared clean base `35dc273072ff133743bc5fcfa306bf030fa8730b` with this change using the same compiled extensions and dependency versions. Model: `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`, revision `a1ff8c8967426709e5528307c14c52c17616b008` (40 MoE layers, hidden size 2048, 256 experts, top-k 8).

Configuration: one B300, TP=1/DP=1, BF16, Humming for linear and MoE, **`VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE=grouped`**. Worker probes confirmed all 40 layers used `HummingGroupedExperts`. Fixed 8 GiB KV cache, max model length 8192, max sequences 32, async scheduling disabled, seed 0, V2 runner, compilation and CUDA graphs enabled with capture sizes `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32]`. PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, FlashInfer 0.6.17.

Live PyTorch GPU allocation immediately after initialization, in GiB (2^30 bytes):

| Max batched tokens | Before | After | Saved |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2048 | 33.412 | 30.953 | **2.459** |
| 8192 | 41.352 | 31.516 | **9.836** |

The number of scratch objects falls from 40 to 1. At 8192 tokens, their storage falls from 10330.684 MiB to 258.267 MiB: **97.5% less scratch memory**. Each distinct configuration or concurrently active execution slot still needs separate storage. Fixing the KV-cache budget keeps vLLM from consuming the saving as a larger KV cache.

The 8192-token pair ran sequentially on the same reserved GPU, with fresh processes. The 2048-token baseline and repeated full baseline used another B300 of the same model. These measurements do not establish a latency improvement.

### Model evaluation

Full GSM8K with the grouped Humming configuration above, 1319 questions, five shots, greedy sampling, and a 256-output-token limit, using the repository's GSM8K prompt/scoring helpers:

| Run | Correct | Accuracy | Invalid |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before | 1208/1319 | 91.58% | 1 |
| After | 1203/1319 | 91.21% | 1 |
| Before, repeated control | 1201/1319 | 91.05% | 1 |

The candidate falls within the observed baseline accuracy range. This does **not** establish bitwise equivalence or rule out a causal accuracy effect: 690/1319 token sequences match between before/after, while only 669/1319 match between the two unmodified baseline runs. Repeated greedy requests also vary on both versions, including after prefix-cache resets; the cause remains unresolved.

Marlin additionally passed the repository GSM8K serving evaluation on 128 questions with five shots: **119/128 (92.97%), zero invalid answers**, using the same model with both backends set to Marlin, max sequences 16, max batched tokens 2048, and graph sizes `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16]`.

### Remaining validation

No H200 or end-to-end distributed DeepEP v2/HT/LL, DBO, or DSpark serving run was performed. Expert-map and execution-slot tests cover local behavior and do not substitute for those runs. The model evaluation uses BF16/SILU and does not cover the FP8/SITU cases discussed in #55105.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, testing, and drafting this PR.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Unlink shared mmap by inode after all ranks map
body:
Fixes a /dev/shm region leak in TieringOffloadingSpec, and a stale-generation unlink that could delete a live engine's file.

## Purpose

`/dev/shm/vllm_offload_{engine_id}.mmap` is unlinked once every process has mapped it, so a hard kill can't leak the region. Two gaps:

1. **`TieringOffloadingSpec` never dropped the name.** It maps the region in the workers *and* the scheduler, and the scheduler maps last, so nothing was positioned to unlink. The file survived every restart.
2. **Unlink targeted the path, not the file.** A stale generation shutting down late could delete the file belonging to the engine that replaced it.

Fix: `SharedOffloadRegion.unlink()` records `(st_dev, st_ino)` at map time and removes the pathname only if it still names that inode. All four unlink sites route through it. `get_manager()` calls `scheduler_mmap.unlink()` once the scheduler-side mapping exists — EngineCore builds it only after the synchronous worker `initialize_from_config` RPCs return, so every TP worker has already mapped.

Single-generation behavior is unchanged; the guard only turns a wrong unlink into a no-op.


```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py \
                          tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py -v
```

Two existing tests extended, both of which fail on `main`:

- `test_joiner_flag_not_set` — a joiner (the scheduler mapping) can drop the pathname; all mappings stay valid and coherent.
- `test_backing_file_unlinked_after_barrier` — a stale generation's `unlink()` returns `False` and leaves the replacement's inode at the path.

## Test Result

```
92 passed, 14 warnings in 41.03s
```

No model evaluation: startup/teardown lifecycle only, no effect on the offload data path or generated output.

title: [Scheduler] Balance async PP decode batches
body:
## Purpose

Balance established decode batches automatically when Model Runner V2 uses asynchronous pipeline parallelism.

Async PP makes a request eligible again after `pipeline_parallel_size` scheduler steps. Prompt-completion timing can therefore create persistent, uneven cadence groups such as Q7/Q13/Q2/Q10. This change limits established decode requests selected in each step to:

```text
ceil(max_num_seqs / pipeline_parallel_size)
```

The limit applies to both `RUNNING` requests and established decode requests resumed from `WAITING`. Prefill, chunked prefill, and chunks that complete a prompt in the current step remain uncapped because mixed batches require token-aware rather than sequence-count balancing. If priority preemption removes a selected decode, its cohort slot is restored.

The policy is active only for MRV2 `AsyncScheduler` with pipeline parallelism greater than one. PP1, synchronous scheduling, and MRV1 retain the existing effective limit of `max_num_seqs`.

This advances Workstream A of #50853.

### Why this is not a duplicate

#50410 is the only overlapping open PR. It caps the total number of scheduled requests, including prefill. On a matched Kimi-K3 + DSpark Mooncake replay, that global cap reduced output throughput by 8.21% versus natural scheduling. The decode-only policy here improved output throughput by 22.95% versus natural scheduling and by 33.95% versus #50410.

The distinction is implemented and tested explicitly: all 32 prompt-completing requests are scheduled together before decode is divided into two disjoint Q16 cohorts under PP2.

## Test Plan

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py
```

## Test Result

- Async scheduler tests: `20 passed`
- File-scoped pre-commit suite: passed, including Ruff, formatting, and mypy

Matched Kimi-K3 + DSpark serving results on B200:

| Workload | Topology | Natural cohorts | Balanced cohorts | Output tok/s change |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| Fixed 64k/400, C64 | TP8/PP2 | Q19/Q13 | Q16/Q16 | +4.74% |
| Fixed 64k/400, C64 | TP8/PP4 | Q7/Q13/Q2/Q10 | Q8/Q8/Q8/Q8 | +12.62% |
| Mooncake trace, C64 | TP8/PP4 | natural | decode cap 8 | +22.95% |

The submitting human reviewed every changed line and the test results. AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used to implement the reviewed change, run validation, and prepare this PR description.

title: [Kernel][Model][MiniMax-M3] Add per-rank context-parallel sparse indexer scoring Triton kernel
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

Add a Triton module that computes MiniMax-M3 sparse indexer context scores independently per context-parallel (CP) rank, opt-in and decoupled from the global DCP configuration.

The new `indexer_context_scores` helper (backed by the `_context_score` Triton kernel) assigns logical KV blocks round-robin across ranks (`block = local * world + rank`) so each rank only scores the shard of context it owns. It returns a `[heads, tokens, ceil(blocks/world)]` float32 score tensor. Inputs are strictly validated:

- Queries must be BF16 `[tokens, heads, 128]` with a contiguous D dimension.
- Index cache must be contiguous `[pages, 128, 128]` in BF16, FP8 `e4m3fn`, or FP8 `e4m3fnuz`.
- Block table and sequence lengths must be int32; the block table must cover the requested context.
- All inputs must live on the same GPU.

This is **PR 1 of a 3-PR series**:

- **PR 1 (this PR, kernel):** per-rank context-parallel sparse indexer scoring.
- **PR 2 (feature):** [#57438](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57438) — Add top-k candidate exchange for context parallelism.
- **PR 3 (test):** [#57439](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57439) — Add correctness tests for context indexer.

This PR adds a new, opt-in code path only; it does not modify existing kernels or dispatch. Because the module is new, there is no pre-PR baseline for this specific path — the path did not exist before this PR.

## Test Plan

title: [Kernel][Model][Hardware][AMD] Add MiniMax-M3 sparse indexer top-k candidate exchange for context parallelism
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

This PR adds a ROCm/Triton module implementing **top-k candidate exchange** across context-parallel ranks for the MiniMax-M3 sparse indexer.

After each rank scores its own KV shard (via `indexer_context_parallel`, added in the sibling feature PR), ranks currently would need to exchange the full score matrix to select global winners. This module instead exchanges only each rank's **top-k candidates**, reducing the cross-rank payload from O(blocks) to O(topk) — critical for long-context AgentX-style workloads.

The module exposes two stages:

- `local_candidate_keys` / `_local_topk`: reduces a per-rank `[heads, tokens, local_blocks]` FP32 score tensor to `[heads, tokens, topk]` packed int64 `(score, block)` keys. Forced init (sink) and local (sliding-window) blocks are pinned so they always survive the local reduction.
- `merge_candidate_keys` / `_merge_topk`: gathers `[world, tokens, topk]` (or `[tokens, world*topk]`) candidate keys, selects the global top-k, and emits the sparse block table / context lengths.

**Correctness note:** rank R keeps `topk` candidates (not `topk/P`). A global winner on rank R cannot be missing from R's local top-k, since it would have beaten `topk` blocks already in the global set. Forced blocks are pinned in *both* stages so a forced block that lost its rank's local top-k still arrives at merge.

This is part of a series:
- PR 1 (feature): [#57437](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57437) — Add per-rank context-parallel sparse indexer scoring Triton kernel
- **This PR (#57438):** top-k candidate exchange across ranks
- PR 3 (test): [#57439](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57439) — Add correctness tests for context indexer

## Test Plan

All benchmarks target AMD Instinct MI300X (ROCm) with the Triton backend.

1. Kernel correctness + microbenchmark:
   ```
   python benchmark_sparse_indexer_candidate_exchange.py
   ```
   Verifies that candidate-exchange top-k indices match a full-matrix reference across ranks, and reports per-kernel latency.

2. Accuracy (gsm8k) on MI300X:
