title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] Add gfx950 FP4 compressed-KV paged attention
body:
## Purpose

Extend the DeepSeek V4.1 compressed-KV cache introduced by #56935 to ROCm gfx950 and add a gfx950-native MXFP4 option.

- Keep the sliding-window cache in the existing FP8 DS-MLA record.
- Store only compressed KV as either 288-byte NVFP4 (256-byte E2M1 payload + 32 E4M3 scales) or 272-byte MXFP4 (256-byte E2M1 payload + 16 E8M0 scales).
- Add gfx950 writers and gather fallbacks for both formats.
- Read FP4 pages directly in sparse decode, including split-K and graph replay.
- Reuse the direct paged decode kernel for sparse prefill, bounded to 4096 query rows per launch to cap split-K scratch.
- Reject FP4 DS-MLA cache formats on ROCm architectures other than gfx950.

The indexer cache remains FP8. The ROCm AITER MoE padding-sentinel fix in #57036 is intentionally not included in this branch. Performance runs applied #57036 and the same ROCm100 MXFP8 LDS-stage compatibility overlay to every cache-format arm, so the only arm difference was `--kv-cache-dtype`.

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

Benchmark setup: 8x MI355X, TP8+EP8, AITER MoE, fixed seed 42, temperature 0, `ignore-eos`, random 8K/1K and 128K/1K requests.

## Test Result

### Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| ROCm sparse-attention suite on gfx950 | 79 passed |
| Applicable pre-commit hooks | Passed |
| TP8 startup: FP8 / NVFP4 / MXFP4 | All ready |
| PR commits/authors | 1 / Liuyinfeng01 only |

### Kernel decode sweep

Values are latency speedup versus FP8 at `heads=8`; negative values are regressions. Each cell used 20 warmups, 100 graph replays per sample, and 5 alternating-order samples.

| Format | Context | B1 | B4 | B16 | B64 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| NVFP4 | 8K | -17.13% | -16.93% | -24.92% | -37.82% |
| NVFP4 | 128K | -15.32% | -16.54% | -24.29% | -41.46% |
| MXFP4 | 8K | -19.17% | -19.65% | -26.92% | +31.87% |
| MXFP4 | 128K | -19.59% | -20.24% | -27.33% | +39.37% |

### End-to-end serving

Output-token throughput below is the median of the two complete, independent restarts shared by all three arms. `num-prompts=concurrency`. A third restart completed for NVFP4/MXFP4, but the FP8 third restart was stopped and is excluded to keep the comparison paired.

| Workload | C | FP8 tok/s | NVFP4 tok/s | NVFP4 delta | MXFP4 tok/s | MXFP4 delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8K/1K | 1 | 109.93 | 105.47 | -4.06% | 106.07 | -3.51% |
| 8K/1K | 4 | 366.23 | 355.07 | -3.05% | 366.75 | +0.14% |
| 8K/1K | 16 | 1086.52 | 844.06 | -22.32% | 909.58 | -16.29% |
| 8K/1K | 64 | 2016.10 | 1895.65 | -5.97% | 2367.18 | +17.41% |
| 128K/1K | 1 | 64.39 | 65.35 | +1.49% | 72.56 | +12.69% |

| 128K/1K | 64 | 147.51 | 165.65 | +12.30% | 223.69 | +51.65% |

### GSM8K-1319

Five-shot, greedy, max tokens 256, concurrency 64. FP8 was stopped before its full run, so these are completed-arm results rather than a valid accuracy A/B.

| Arm | Questions | Accuracy | Invalid | Output tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

title: [CPU] Add KDA backend for GLM5Next
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a correctness-first CPU execution path for GLM-5.3-Flash / GLM5Next KDA for #57346.

The path is deliberately feature-local:

```text
GLM5Next common KDA layer
  -> CPU platform dispatch
  -> CPU state helpers and causal convolution
  -> CPU KDA recurrence/chunk contract
  -> optional _C_AVX512 recurrent operator
```

It does not implement #57345 (CPU sparse MLA / KeyPool), Kimi K3 support, a generic GDN refactor, or a new GLM CPU model hierarchy. The two GLM5Next CPU PRs are intentionally separate so that KDA and sparse MLA can be reviewed and tested independently.

## Self-review / Implementation notes

### Scope and design

The initial source audit showed that CPU support required more than changing the two KDA imports. The common layer also reaches causal-convolution and state gather/scatter boundaries that have GPU-oriented implementations. I therefore kept the change at the GLM5Next KDA execution boundary and preserved the existing common projection, metadata, and routing code.

I did not add `glm5next/cpu/model.py` or a new backend registry. The hardware-specific difference is limited to KDA execution, so a model-level fork would add review and maintenance cost without solving a concrete blocker.

The related CPU GDN implementation was used as a reference for stateful CPU integration, but it was not treated as a drop-in KDA implementation. KDA differs in safe-gate semantics, beta handling, V-major state layout, and speculative state routing.

### KDA semantics preserved

The CPU backend keeps the existing GLM KDA contract:

* q/k normalization and query scaling;
* bounded safe gate using per-head `A_log` and per-head/key-dimension `g_bias`;
* V-major recurrent state `[slots, heads, V, K]`;
* separate chunk-prefill and recurrent-decode state semantics;
* chunk beta timing versus recurrent sigmoid-beta handling;
* 1-D ordinary decode slots and 2-D speculative accepted-token slots;
* NULL-slot skipping and in-place state writeback.

`chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` currently evaluates each packed sequence as a token-wise recurrence. This is mathematically equivalent to the chunk state transition; chunk-level parallelization is an optimization and remains outside this correctness-first change.

### Reuse and native boundary

Ordinary CPU convolution continues to use the existing CPU causal-convolution implementation. GLM5Next speculative decoding has an additional accepted-token rolling-window contract, so only that feature-specific wrapper is implemented here; generic causal-convolution APIs are unchanged.

The Python backend is the explicit fallback and semantic contract. When the supported dense-state conditions are met and `torch.ops._C.glm5next_kda_recurrent` is registered, the recurrent path can use the native AVX-512 operator. Unsupported configurations do not silently route to Triton or NVIDIA KDA.

### Validation

The independent reference implementation remains in the test module and shares no backend helper code. The focused suite covers:

* recurrent output and final-state parity;
* FP32 and BF16 native parity;
* packed prefill and sequence isolation;
* shuffled state slots and NULL slots;
* prefill-to-decode state handoff;
* speculative recurrent routing and accepted-token offsets;
* CPU causal-convolution rebinding and speculative rolling state;
* production-shaped `Glm5NextLinearAttention` prefill, decode, and speculative paths.

With the real `_C_AVX512` extension loaded on the CPU server, the previously validated result is:

```text
27 passed, 14 warnings
```

The native parity checks recorded approximately `2.98e-7` FP32 output error, `5.96e-8` FP32 final-state error, `1.35e-3` BF16 output error, and `1.19e-7` BF16 final-state error. Targeted Ruff, Ruff format, Typos, SPDX, lazy-import, forbidden-import, torch.cuda, and C++ clang-format hooks pass on the final files; manual Python 3.12 mypy also passes.

The final detached verification worktree without the prebuilt CPU extension ran 23 tests, with two failures at the unregistered causal-convolution operator/native spy boundary. Those failures are environment/build limitations of that worktree, not a replacement for the extension-backed result above.

### Deliberate non-goals and remaining boundary

This PR makes no performance claim. AMX, additional precision-specific vector kernels, chunk-level parallelization, NUMA/batch benchmarks, and FP16/FP8 kernel work are follow-ups. Full GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoint generation still depends on #57345 and a real checkpoint validation run.

Please review in particular the CPU boundary in `common/kda.py`, state-slot semantics, the native operator guard/fallback, and whether any existing common helper should be reused without broadening this PR.

## Duplicate-work check

The issue and open-PR searches found no separate open implementation of #57346 or a GLM5Next CPU KDA backend. #57687 is the separate sparse MLA / KeyPool effort.

This is an AI-assisted contribution. The human submitter will review every changed line and defend the design and validation results.

Refs #57346

title: [RFC]: Stateless Responses API in the Rust frontend
body:
## Motivation.

Add native Responses API support to the Rust frontend so clients can use its serving pipeline without a Python API-server fallback. The API must preserve structured conversation input and produce consistent Responses objects whether the client requests buffered JSON or streaming events.

> [!NOTE]
> This RFC follows up on the **non-stateful Responses API** item under "Additional APIs" in the [June 2026 Rust Frontend Feature Parity roadmap (#44280)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44280). The item was marked 🧭 for a design discussion before implementation, covering the intended API/architecture, engine co-design if needed, and testing plan.

This proposal defines a useful first subset, its ownership boundaries and its validation plan. It reuses existing inference infrastructure rather than porting every Python Responses feature or adding an agent runtime.

## Proposed Change.

### 1. Design principles

1. **Self-contained requests, no server-owned conversation state.** Clients supply the complete relevant history. The frontend retains no response objects or conversation history for later requests and introduces no future storage scaffolding.
2. **Shared execution, API-specific ownership.** Reuse rendering, media processing, tokenization, parsing and engine access. Responses owns input conversion, its public items and events, and its output lifecycle.
3. **Explicit acceptance and compatibility choices.** Reject unsupported options that change behavior. Document deliberate compatibility exceptions and their costs.
4. **Validation proportional to distinct risk.** Check protocol invariants with deterministic CPU tests and integration with shared Python/Rust real-engine tests. Python is a comparator, not an oracle.

### 2. Scope

#### Architectural non-goals

The frontend will not own response/conversation storage, response-ID continuation or durable background execution. This is a lasting responsibility boundary. Transient request buffers and existing engine KV/prefix caches are unaffected. Full-history multi-turn requests remain supported, with roles, ordering and function-call associations preserved.

Responses will not introduce a second inference pipeline or forward generation through the Chat Completions HTTP endpoint or Python frontend. It uses the existing Rust serving and engine-client boundary. No engine wire-protocol, scheduler, kernel or tokenizer implementation change is proposed.

#### Initial delivery

Support foreground `POST /v1/responses`, buffered and streaming, with text, supported complete-history items, reasoning, client-executed function calls/results, supported generation controls, JSON structured output, existing image processing, usage, request context and disconnect cancellation. Reporting generation parameters resolved by shared Rust preparation is part of this contract.

The initial delivery excludes server-side tool execution/MCP/agent loops; Harmony-specific execution and serialized-history extensions; encrypted reasoning; a separate Responses render endpoint; audio/video or managed files; new model processors; output logprobs; `allowed_tools`; and automatic history truncation. These exclusions bound the first implementation without committing to later support. A request-local tool loop could be stateless: excluding orchestration is a separate responsibility decision, not a consequence of the storage rule.

Model qualification is separate from API scope. Reusing an existing processor does not qualify every model using it. The validation plan below defines the proposed coverage; this RFC does not claim completed implementation or validation.

### 3. API contract and compatibility choices

| Surface | Initial contract |
| --- | --- |
| Input | String or ordered supported items: role-bearing messages, assistant text/reasoning, function calls and function-call outputs. Preserve `call_id` relationships. |
| Instructions and continuation | Reuse shared instruction placement. Continue a final partial assistant text message; reject partial reasoning because the current renderer cannot continue that channel faithfully. |
| Output | Typed message, reasoning and function-call items, stable IDs/indices, usage and terminal status. Streaming changes delivery, not intended generation semantics. |
| Functions | Reuse schemas, parser selection and `auto` / `none` / `required` / named choices. Return calls to the client; never execute them. |
| Generation and JSON | Map supported sampling controls, `reasoning.effort`, `include_reasoning` and `text.format` to existing validation and engine constraints. |
| Generation metadata | Return `temperature`, `top_p` and `max_output_tokens` resolved by shared Rust preparation for engine submission, including inherited defaults and the context-based output cap. |
| Images | Existing URL/data-URL processing, access policies and limits; no new processors or file-ID service. |
| Storage | Accept omitted `store`, false and true; always return `store=false` and retain nothing. |
| Stored references | Structured 404 for `previous_response_id` and stored-ID retrieval/cancellation; reject input `item_reference`. These handlers have no backing lifecycle subsystem. |
| Unsupported behavior | Reject `background=true`, `truncation="auto"`, legacy `previous_input_messages` and other unsupported behavior-changing fields before dispatch. |

**Storage normalization is an intentional compatibility exception.** It matches [Python with response storage disabled](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/75dc5882699be65eaee144cb7d0b06c1f86d3cec/vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py#L330) and avoids rejecting otherwise usable generation requests. Its cost is that an explicit request to retain a response is not fulfilled. Return `store=false` and document that retrieval/ID continuation are unavailable. Rejecting explicit true is a reasonable stricter alternative, but is not recommended for this subset. The protocol does not require this normalization.

**Generation metadata reports the prepared configuration.** Return the values resolved by shared Rust request preparation for engine submission, rather than null for omitted fields. `max_output_tokens` reports the prepared budget, including the context-based cap, not the number of tokens actually generated. These values are not an acknowledgement of engine-side normalization or a guarantee of identical Python response echoes. For example, Rust preparation preserves `temperature=0, top_p=0.4`, while [Python sampling normalization](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/75dc5882699be65eaee144cb7d0b06c1f86d3cec/vllm/sampling_params.py#L533) sets `top_p=1.0` for greedy sampling. [Python Responses](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/75dc5882699be65eaee144cb7d0b06c1f86d3cec/vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/protocol.py#L782) likewise reports resolved parameters, but at its own preparation boundary. Reusing the Rust result avoids a second resolver and an engine-protocol change; exact cross-frontend echo parity is not the contract.

**Reasoning compatibility depends on delivery mode.** Preserve raw reasoning rather than relabeling it as a summary. Buffered items follow [Python's existing SDK-backed shape](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/75dc5882699be65eaee144cb7d0b06c1f86d3cec/vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/utils.py#L63): `ResponseReasoningItem` with an empty `summary` and raw `reasoning_text` in `content`, not a new private field. Streaming also follows vLLM's [locally defined reasoning-part events](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/75dc5882699be65eaee144cb7d0b06c1f86d3cec/vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/protocol.py#L806). Typed clients without these event variants may not consume that stream correctly; ordinary text interoperability does not establish raw-reasoning streaming compatibility or exhaustive Open Responses conformance.

**Final SSE framing deliberately differs from the pinned Python baseline.** Rust sends the final `[DONE]` marker required by [Open Responses](https://www.openresponses.org/specification#http-responses); the [Python SSE formatter](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/75dc5882699be65eaee144cb7d0b06c1f86d3cec/vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/api_router.py#L34) emits typed events without this marker. Clients that require the marker therefore cannot treat the two frontends as wire-identical. Changing Python framing is outside this proposal.

### 4. Architecture and ownership

![Responses architecture: peer API adapters above shared serving, expanded input and output ownership, and reuse of cancellation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/86086260-b408-422c-b2ed-f6e4545594a9)

*Figure 1. Logical responsibility boundaries, not separate services. Chat Completions and Responses are peer adapters; teal identifies Responses-specific logic and output. The dashed resolved-settings arrow is the proposed internal metadata handoff. The engine protocol stays unchanged, and cancellation reuses existing stream ownership and Abort.*

The shared layer already exposes structured text/reasoning blocks, tool events, usage and finish information through `ChatRequest` / `ChatEvent`. Responses can preserve those distinctions directly, without reconstructing them from aggregated public Chat JSON or serialized SSE.

| Handoff | Information and owner |
| --- | --- |
| Responses conversion → shared serving | `ChatRequest`: ordered supported history, call associations and mapped generation options. Responses validates its contract; shared serving retains model/template/parser selection and request preparation. |
| Responses conversion → output assembly | Request-local context and Responses-only options, including output visibility and API metadata. They need not be represented in engine input. Reuse existing resolved request identity. |
| Shared serving → output assembly | `ChatEvent`: structured content, tool events, usage and finish information, plus the three Rust-prepared generation values through a narrow request-scoped handoff. |
| Output assembly → HTTP delivery | One accumulated Responses result drives buffered JSON and streamed item/event projections, including the terminal response object. Transport code does not independently decide item identity or completion status. |

**One assembler owns the public output.** Apply reasoning visibility before allocating public indices; assign item identities once; accumulate content and usage; and map finish/error information to terminal state. Buffered and streaming paths share this logic, reducing duplicated invariants without introducing a general event framework.

**Input fidelity includes the renderer.** In a continuation such as user message → assistant function call → client function result, retain the role and `call_id` structure rather than flattening the history into text. HF and DeepSeek renderers serialize assistant channels in a particular order. Coalesce adjacent items only when that serialization preserves their order; otherwise retain separate assistant messages. An ordered internal vector alone does not prevent text-before-reasoning from being reordered or partial-text continuation from truncating a preceding call. Respect model templates that intentionally omit historical reasoning.

**The shared-layer addition is narrowly scoped.** Capture the three values after successful text request preparation and return them with the `ChatEventStream` handle, not as an in-band generation event. The assembler can read them when `chat()` resolves, before constructing its first Responses object. Preparation or stream-creation failure returns an HTTP error without a partially initialized Responses object; after streaming begins, a failure response retains the same prepared values. This carries existing preparation results without resolving defaults twice or adding metadata to the engine wire protocol.

Keep wire types, validation/conversion and assembly in focused server-route modules. Reuse existing model/LoRA resolution, request context and engine-client ownership. Preserve the existing request-ID precedence from the resolved request context, including `X-Request-ID` over the body `request_id`.

| Alternative | Tradeoff and decision |
| --- | --- |
| Internal structured-event adapter | Preferred: the required execution boundary already exists, and Responses retains its own context and output lifecycle. |
| In-process public Chat adapter | Viable, but aggregation/serialization can obscure event information or Responses-only context that must then be carried separately. It offers no demonstrated advantage here. |
| HTTP forwarding to Chat or Python | Adds transport, error and cancellation boundaries and prevents a self-contained Rust frontend. |
| Separate inference/rendering pipeline | Duplicates existing responsibilities without a demonstrated missing capability. |

### 5. Lifecycle and wire contract

- Keep response/item/call IDs stable within a request, with consistent output/content indices and monotonically increasing event sequence numbers. Reuse completed items in the final response object.
- Normal stop produces `completed`; token exhaustion produces `incomplete` with `max_output_tokens`. Engine errors, aborts and premature EOF must not become successful completion.
- Before buffered delivery or stream headers, return an appropriate HTTP error. After streaming starts, expose failure as `response.failed` with error information. This subset does not add a separate preceding error event.
- The request/response owns the underlying chat stream in both delivery modes. A disconnect drops that stream and reaches existing engine Abort and cleanup; no detached foreground generation or new cancellation subsystem is introduced.
- After the semantic terminal event on a normally concluded SSE exchange, emit `data: [DONE]`, following [Open Responses HTTP framing](https://www.openresponses.org/specification#http-responses). `[DONE]` ends the stream; it does not override the response's success, incomplete or failure status. A broken connection cannot be promised a terminal marker.

Test both raw framing and supported SDK consumption: EOF-tolerant clients do not prove that a required marker was sent, while raw protocol assertions do not establish client interoperability. Compare reconstructed content and lifecycle invariants, not identical chunk sizes or UUIDs across separate requests.

### 6. Validation plan

Run a shared OpenAI SDK pytest subset against `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0/1`, with Python storage disabled and matched engine/model/tokenizer/template/parser settings. Keep Python-only capability tests separate. Treat documented compatibility differences, such as generation-metadata reporting boundaries, explicitly; do not normalize away protocol defects to make the comparison pass. Assert the final `[DONE]` marker in Rust-only raw-HTTP coverage, outside the shared SDK subset; both arms retain common content, identity and lifecycle assertions.

| Layer | Purpose and bounded coverage |
| --- | --- |
| CPU conversion/rendering | Parameters, roles/call linkage, instruction placement and actual rendered ordering. Use negative controls for concrete rendering regressions. |
| CPU parameter reporting | Explicit values, omitted/default values and context-capped output budgets. Assert that reported values match shared Rust preparation. In existing failure cases, check HTTP errors before stream creation and unchanged metadata after streaming starts; do not duplicate the resolver or require engine-normalized echoes. |
| CPU output/HTTP/SDK | Controlled text/reasoning/tool events; identities, indices and terminal states; request context; media rejection; stream failure; disconnect-to-Abort; and Rust-only raw SSE framing, including `[DONE]`. |
| Real-engine shared subset | Qwen3-1.7B for ordinary text/reasoning/functions/JSON; existing Qwen3-8B cases for regression continuity; Qwen2.5-VL-3B for image conversion and Responses-versus-Chat input-token agreement. |
| Existing CI | Reuse Entrypoints jobs and add relevant Rust source dependencies, without a new test framework or GPU-type matrix. |

Model selection follows distinct serving paths. DeepSeek-V4.1 validation is limited to CPU renderer/parser fixtures, not full GPU serving qualification. One sufficiently sized supported GPU exercises the adapter. Additional GPU types/counts or models must expose a distinct integration risk. Parameter reporting and exact lifecycle edge cases belong in CPU tests.

When a real-engine assertion fails, compare Python using matched effective generation settings, then isolate conversion/rendering, parser output and model behavior. Both frontends failing does not by itself establish model incapability. Use controlled events for exact protocol assertions and real engines for integration, rather than requiring a probabilistic model to manufacture every lifecycle condition.

### 7. Initial delivery and feedback requested

Deliver the complete proposed subset through the existing Rust frontend selection, including the metadata handoff and final SSE framing. Do not change the default frontend or remove Python capabilities. Python remains an operational fallback; no state-mode flag, render service or new deployment component is needed. The implementation must demonstrate the validation plan before being presented as ready to ship.

Feedback is requested on three decisions:

1. Does the shared boundary carry sufficient information while keeping Responses input/output ownership clear, including the narrow prepared-settings handoff?
2. Is the initial subset useful and its acceptance/rejection policy reasonable, particularly storage normalization and raw reasoning compatibility?
3. Does the focused validation plan demonstrate input fidelity, consistent output lifecycle and cleanup without unnecessary tests or model/hardware expansion?

## Feedback Period.

At least one week from posting.

## CC List.

@BugenZhao @njhill — Rust frontend code owners.

@franciscojavierarceo — Agentic API maintainer; feedback on Responses semantics and stateless API boundaries.

@gcanlin — Author of #53380.

## Any Other Things.

### Related work and discussion

[#53380](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53380), by @gcanlin, provides an initial implementation using the shared Rust serving pipeline. This RFC complements that work by making the proposed API contract, responsibility boundaries, compatibility choices and validation criteria explicit, and seeks community feedback on those decisions.

The design is consistent with the following scoped discussions and accepted work. These are precedents for specific choices, not approval of this proposal.

| Reference and status | Relevance |
| --- | --- |
| [Ben Browning on core Responses responsibilities](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/24603#issuecomment-5059872281), July 23, after the original RFC closed; [Francisco Javier Arceo's review of #53380](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53380#pullrequestreview-5202547054), September 14, COMMENTED | Complete-history requests and stateless core serving align with keeping state/orchestration outside this frontend. Ben is a vLLM tool-use/reasoning committer; Ben and Francisco are Agentic API maintainers. Python's optional state/tools remain separate capabilities. |
| [#50289 renderer interface review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50289#discussion_r3719644178) and [follow-up clarification](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50289#discussion_r3727661591); merged August 6 | Explicit consumers, information boundaries and compatibility rationale are useful design precedents. Here the boundary is internal structured chat events, not a public rendering service. |
| [Ben's approving review of rendering-parity tests #50334](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50334#pullrequestreview-4822128073); merged July 31 | Shared tests expose Chat/Responses drift, supporting targeted parity checks for the proposed subset. |
| [Python rendering refactor #50195](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50195) and [DarkLight1337's scope comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50195#issuecomment-5479689463); merged September 7 | Rendering reuse can be separated from Responses orchestration/output. This proposal makes that separation inside the frontend without a new scale-out service. |

Roles are recorded in [vLLM governance](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2bdbbc80804b2199cbf39b75e78cf7269d0383a4/docs/governance/committers.md) and [Agentic API CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/vllm-project/agentic-api/blob/588d8bd7de783472cc7e1577a35b158d7a12d69b/.github/CODEOWNERS). The earlier [Rust roadmap #44280](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44280) requested non-stateful Responses and design discussion; it closed with that item unchecked, so it establishes prior intent rather than completed support.

[SMG's Chat-SSE conversion](https://github.com/smg-project/smg/blob/4a58ce9323cc34ad36157882e584fb9f1d16f2f8/model_gateway/src/routers/grpc/regular/responses/streaming.rs#L182-L209), [Dynamo's unified request](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/8c5a73723109058f96c15fff3fc912231d65ad6e/lib/llm/src/protocols/unified.rs#L4-L32) and [SGLang's shared Chat preprocessing](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/2cb51f5d22635f3ea9f2a062abeda486ba015c35/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py#L667-L716) illustrate viable alternatives. Existing vLLM structured events make direct projection appropriate here; this is a repository-specific choice rather than a universal layering rule.

title: [RFC][NIXL] Add graceful peer retirement example for UCX v1.22.x memory release
body:
## Summary

Replace the earlier CPU-only sketch with the **GPU-tested, version-pinned
graceful peer-retirement example**, its source patches, CPU tests and measured
memory-reclamation evidence. This is an RFC ready for implementation/design
review, not a production-ready autoscaler or a change to default serving.

Scope: **a normally drained Prefill exits; healthy Decode instances release
its old CUDA IPC references without restarting**. The tested stack is vLLM
0.26.0, NIXL 1.4.1 and a pinned UCX v1.22.x build. Abrupt P death, OOM,
segfaults, incomplete-transfer cancellation and forced unmapping are excluded.

## Code in This PR

The old `examples/disaggregated/peer_retirement_cpu/` is removed. Its replacement,
`examples/disaggregated/peer_retirement_graceful/`, includes:

- Worker-thread prepare/commit, exact-generation fencing, busy-state checks,
  and reuse of `_cleanup_remote_engine()` / `remove_remote_agent()`.
- Authenticated, opt-in lab middleware with full-D admission fencing,
  collective-RPC validation of all TP ranks, and fail-closed handling of
  partial cleanup or an unknown result.
- SHA-256-guarded v0.26.0 patches for old-generation reads/handshakes/heartbeats,
  TTL safety and notification-only metadata cleanup.
- CPU tests using actual pinned v0.26.0 methods with a fake NIXL boundary;
  an explicit fixture preparation step makes subsequent tests offline.
- A minimal Docker layer, an isolated exercise guide and sanitized GPU results.
  The Dockerfile requires an existing matching native stack; it does not
  build or upgrade UCX.

The three core Python files have identical ASTs to the isolated GPU-tested
lab implementation; packaging changes are license headers, formatting and
test fixture paths. The host-specific controller and private operational
files are not included. This is not a one-command portable GPU reproducer.

The integration is deliberately an opt-in version-pinned example, **not an
upstream-main `/drop_peer` serving implementation**. It demonstrates the
tested lifecycle for review before merging it into an agreed production API.

## Problem and Lifecycle

For N-P/M-D serving on one multi-GPU host, a P process can exit while surviving
D workers retain imported memory resources. Its former GPU capacity can remain
occupied and prevent a replacement from loading. Stopping the entire D pool
has reclaimed that memory, but interrupts unrelated work and defeats
independent P scaling.

```text
Stop new router admissions to the exact old P generation
  -> finish admitted requests and KV handoff
  -> quiesce the D being cleaned and fence the old generation on every TP rank
  -> release destination descriptor lists, then remove the remote NIXL agent
  -> verify acknowledgements from every relevant D/rank
  -> normally stop P and measure its GPU memory
  -> verify surviving D identities and fresh transfers from another P
```

In the tested protocol, the D being cleaned has zero active HTTP responses,
and background traffic is routed to the other D. Its whole admission path is
frozen across prepare/commit. A partial failure or timeout retains that freeze
for diagnosis; potentially partial native cleanup is not blindly retried.
Python-visible connector queues are checked, not every native worker queue.

## GPU Results: UCX v1.22.x

One isolated eight-GPU **H20** host, 2P2D with TP=2 each, DeepSeek-V4-Flash
(non-0731), vLLM 0.26.0, NIXL 1.4.1. UCX was the **v1.22.x branch at
`5288e74cd40be622e109489de7bb80d821341bd5`**, not a claimed formal-release
validation. Settings: `UCX_TLS=tcp,cuda_ipc,cuda_copy`,
`UCX_CUDA_IPC_CACHE=n`, NIXL UCX `num_threads=8`.

| Check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Control: normally stop P without explicit D cleanup | 42,912 MiB retained on each former P GPU for about 120 seconds |
| Explicit D cleanup, then normally stop P | Both former P GPUs at 0 MiB for all 60 samples over 119.502 seconds |
| Surviving D instances | Container identities and TP worker PIDs unchanged |
| Fresh 64K transfer from the other P to each D | Each pair added 578,062,080 NIXL bytes; zero failed-transfer increment |
| Drain / cleanup / memory observation | 163/163 logical P-D requests succeeded |
| Replacement P | New generation started on the same GPU pair |
| Background traffic during replacement | 107/107 succeeded; maximum completion gap 2.179 seconds |
| Final four P-D pair checks | Short and 64K requests: 8/8 succeeded |

With eight baseline requests, 286 logical P-D requests passed the experiment's
checks. Final transfer and notification failure counters on both D instances
were zero. Final full teardown occurred only after acceptance and is not used
as evidence that P-only retirement reclaimed memory.

Control and candidate used the same native NIXL/UCX binaries. The candidate also
contains fences, TTL guards and metadata cleanup, so this is not a one-line
comparison. Runtime library paths and cache settings were checked.

## Native Release Boundary

At the tested UCX commit, rkey release can reach
`uct_cuda_ipc_unmap_memhandle()`. Mapping references are decremented, and a
zero-reference region is destroyed when the remote mapping cache is disabled.
`UCX_CUDA_IPC_CACHE=n` does not release outstanding higher-level references
still held by D. The control case demonstrates why that setting alone is
insufficient here.

No direct `uct_cuda_ipc_destroy_cache_by_iface_address()` or forced unmap is
introduced. Individual native unmap/CUDA close calls were not traced. Therefore
`cleanup_returned` intentionally does **not** report verified native release;
the evidence is measured VRAM recovery with surviving D processes and
successful unrelated transfers. See `VALIDATION.md` for sources and limits.

## Relationship to Existing Work

- #50047 (inspected at `8d742243fa9a3032fcc014ff5c3e17aa871a2bff`) cleans a
  replaced pull peer after successful new-engine handshake at the same address.
  This explicit normal scale-down path does not require a replacement P, which
  may not exist or may be unable to load until retained memory is released.
  Cleanup mechanisms should be shared, not duplicated in production.
- #56341 handles P-side cleanup after D death: the opposite direction.
- #55471 handles locally missing NIXL metadata while P remains alive.
- Existing in-flight protections such as #54689 remain essential.

This updates the existing RFC rather than opening another overlapping PR.

## Test Commands and Results

Run from the repository root with an isolated Python 3.12 environment:

```bash
EXAMPLE=examples/disaggregated/peer_retirement_graceful
.venv/bin/python "$EXAMPLE/prepare_sources.py" --source-dir '<stock-v0.26.0-nixl-source-directory>'
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -c /dev/null -p no:cacheprovider \
  --confcutdir="$EXAMPLE" "$EXAMPLE/test_retirement.py" -q
# 39 passed (2026-09-21).

.venv/bin/python -m ruff check "$EXAMPLE"
.venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check "$EXAMPLE"
git diff --cached --check
# Passed; Python compileall and SPDX-header checks also passed.
```

The two fixtures match the public v0.26.0 sources by SHA-256. Tests are
method-level with mocked native resources, not full-import vLLM/native tests.
The historical separate lab runtime/controller suite passed 51 tests; that
number is not claimed for this new public directory.

The full pre-commit run was attempted with the repository configuration and
installed hooks, but dependency initialization did not finish within a
150-second bound (last progress: fetching the public `crate-ci/typos` hook).
It is **not** reported as passed. The checks listed above ran independently.
Commit hooks were bypassed for this packaging commit after that infrastructure
timeout; full CI/hook validation remains pending.

No new GPU run was performed during packaging; the GPU results above belong to the same core
Python logic tested on September 20. The portable Docker wrapper was not
rebuilt locally on this Mac. Model-output checks are limited to the stated
functional lifecycle exercise, not broad accuracy or throughput evaluation.

## Remaining Work and AI Assistance

Unverified: crashed/OOM P, native cancellation or stuck cleanup, multiple API
processes, bidirectional/push mode, native destructor tracing, this exact
candidate on B300, other UCX builds, long-duration stability and production SLA.
The D-wide freeze means this is not general lossless autoscaling under arbitrary
traffic. These restrictions are enforced/documented rather than hidden behind
a claim of completed production recovery.

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, testing, investigation and reporting.
The human submitter requested replacing the old prototype, publishing this
tested implementation and marking the existing RFC ready for review. This
disclosure is not a claim that a new current-main serving API has been reviewed
or certified. No private addresses, credentials, production manifests or
customer request content are included.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Add AITER paged MXFP4 sparse indexing on gfx950
body:
## Purpose

Add opt-in AITER paged MXFP4 sparse indexing for DeepSeek V4/V4.1 on ROCm gfx950.

Select with:

```bash
--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}'
```

FP8 remains the default. This PR changes only the sparse indexer's Q/K cache precision and scorer path. It does **not** change the main attention KV cache and does not overlap the NVFP4 compressed main-KV implementation in #57463.

The AITER scorer implementation, shared-pool page strides, and 64-bit physical-page rebasing are provided by ROCm/aiter#5518. This vLLM PR contains only the integration:

- packed MXFP4 indexer K-cache production on ROCm;
- packed Q production and scale layout;
- zero-copy cache views and AITER prefill/decode dispatch;
- graph-stable decode schedule reuse across indexer layers;
- gfx950/geometry/dependency gates and FP8 fallback;
- focused dispatch and layout contract tests.

This clean branch supersedes #56834. It deliberately excludes the main-attention compressed-KV work from #57489, which overlaps #57463.

## Performance and accuracy

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 8x MI355X, TP8+EP8, 8K input / 1K output,
`--block-size 128`, prefix caching disabled. Each measured concurrency is preceded
by an unmeasured full request batch with a different random seed so runtime JIT
compilation is outside the timed interval. One measured run per arm (`n=1`):

| Concurrency | FP8 tok/s | MXFP4 tok/s | Throughput change | FP8 TPOT | MXFP4 TPOT |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 112.25 | 112.10 | -0.13% | 8.69 ms | 8.71 ms |
| 4 | 405.66 | 405.19 | -0.11% | 9.20 ms | 9.21 ms |
| 16 | 1240.42 | 1244.42 | +0.32% | 10.88 ms | 10.87 ms |
| 64 | 2561.00 | 2563.72 | +0.11% | 17.81 ms | 17.87 ms |

All performance requests completed with zero failures. The MXFP4 indexer is
throughput-neutral at model level for this V4.1 configuration; its isolated
scorer is faster, but the indexer is a small fraction of total model time.
Earlier negative results were invalid: the timed request compiled uncached
MXFP4 helper kernels and the FP8 run reused prompt prefixes.

Isolated V4.1 scorer shapes on MI355X:

| Path | FP8 gather+score | MXFP4 page 128 | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Decode B64/H32/D128/8K | 9.33 us | 6.30 us | 1.48x |
| Prefill 8192 queries/H32/8K | 610.05 us | 309.00 us | 1.97x |

Both MXFP4 kernels match the exact FP4-dequant reference at cosine 1.000000.

GSM8K-1319, 5-shot greedy, temperature 0, one run per arm:

| Arm | Accuracy | Invalid | Output tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FP8 indexer | 90.9780% | 0% | 912.77 |
| MXFP4 indexer | 90.6748% | 0.0758% | 910.73 |

The accuracy delta is -0.30 percentage points, within single-run noise. The one
invalid MXFP4 response is retained in the reported denominator.

## Test plan

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_fp4_dispatch.py \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_dispatch.py

pre-commit run --files \
  docs/design/attention_backends.md \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_dispatch.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_fp4_dispatch.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/fused_compress_quant_cache.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/fused_indexer_q.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py
```

Result: **39 passed**; applicable pre-commit hooks passed. End-to-end MXFP4 completed all four service loads and GSM8K-1319.

AITER #5518 separately covers exact FP4-dequant agreement, eager and graph replay, shuffled pages, nonzero offsets, 2/4/4.608 GB address boundaries, and page-map/scale sensitivity.

## Dependency and non-duplication

- Depends on ROCm/aiter#5518 for the FP4 MQA kernels.
- Does not include AITER kernel source.
- Does not implement main-attention compressed KV; #57463 owns that scope.
- Supersedes the older integration draft #56834.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used at the author's request. Human review remains required before marking ready.

title: [Bug][Perf][DSpark] #54674 stacked context WKV regresses TTFT ~3.3% on 2-node DGX Spark (GB10, TP=2), with no decode gain
body:
## Summary

[#54674](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54674) ("[Perf][DSpark] Stack DeepSeek V4 context WKV projections", merged 2026-09-17) is a **TTFT regression of ~3.2-3.3%** on 2-node DGX Spark (GB10 / SM121, TP=2) serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 NVFP4. It also costs ~1.5% of the KV pool. We measured no compensating decode or acceptance-rate gain.

Since the PR targets the context/prefill path, a TTFT regression is the opposite of its intended effect, so we are reporting it rather than just dropping the patch locally.

## Why the usual A/B is not enough here, and what we did instead

Throughput metrics on this platform have a large boot-to-boot spread, so a single A-vs-B comparison cannot resolve a few percent. We ran **A-B-A** (three full engine restarts) and used the two A runs to calibrate the noise floor:

| metric | A1 (without #54674) | B (with #54674) | A2 (without #54674) | A1↔A2 spread |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| greedy 32K decode tok/s | 65.62 | 64.57 | 60.92 | **7.2%** |
| temp0.6 8K decode tok/s (mean of 3) | 61.54 | 65.70 | 65.23 | **6.0%** |
| temp0.6 acceptance rate | 0.6539 | 0.7016 | 0.6961 | **6.5%** |
| **TTFT 8K (s)** | **2.502** | **2.589** | **2.512** | **0.4%** |
| **TTFT 32K (s)** | **10.191** | **10.551** | **10.221** | **0.3%** |

Decode throughput and DSpark acceptance rate swing 6-7% between two boots of the *same* build, so every apparent "gain" for B in those rows is inside the noise band. TTFT, by contrast, is stable to 0.3-0.4% across the two A runs — and B is consistently **+3.2%** (8K) and **+3.3%** (32K) relative to the A mean, which is roughly an order of magnitude outside that spread.

A 128K-prefill probe agrees in direction: 62.6 s with the patch vs 61.9 / 62.1 s without.

Secondary cost: GPU KV cache pool drops from **1,655,061** to **1,630,430** tokens (-1.5%), and reported max concurrency at 1M context from 1.58x to 1.55x.

## Hypothesis

With `--max-num-seqs 6` on a 2-node TP=2 GB10 pair, the stacked WKV projection does not have enough concurrent context work to amortize its extra setup, so the stacking overhead lands directly on TTFT. Configurations with larger batch or more GPUs may still benefit — we are not claiming the PR is wrong in general, only that it is a net loss in this shape.

## Reproduction

Serve command (2 nodes, one GB10 each, RoCE):

```
vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-NVFP4 \
  --revision f1caa71142bd0be02f728c79f75042ac1e461579 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --nnodes 2 --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --trust-remote-code --max-num-seqs 6 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --block-size 256 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --quantization deepseek_v4_fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.825 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","disable_eagle_block_drop":true}' \
  --no-async-scheduling --enable-flashinfer-autotune
```

Measure TTFT at 8K and 32K prompt with 384 output tokens, greedy. **Restart the engine between arms and run A-B-A**; a single A/B will not separate a 3% TTFT effect from the decode noise if you look at throughput, and will look like a *win* if you look at `temp0.6` decode or acceptance rate.

## Environment

- 2x DGX Spark (GB10, SM121, 48 SMs, driver 580.173.02), TP=2 over RoCE, unified 128 GB/node
- vLLM nightly `2671fedf` + the merged `#54674` diff applied as a source overlay (byte-identical to the merged version apart from the `diff --git`/`index` headers)
- flashinfer 0.6.18.post1 with the #4802 SM120 sparse-MLA sources overlaid (+#5048, +#5097)
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 NVFP4, `fp8_ds_mla` KV, DSpark k=5
- Benchmarks run on an idle cluster with periodic synthetic load disabled

Happy to re-run with different `--max-num-seqs` or on a larger batch shape if that would help locate the crossover.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Read the V4.1 MXFP8 KV record on gfx950
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 stores its sliding-window KV as MXFP8 — all 512 dims as fp8 e4m3 with the RoPE tail included, one UE8M0 scale per 32 dims. The reference implementation says so outright: `_window_kv` RoPEs the vector and calls `act_quant(kv, fp8_block_size=32, scale_fmt="ue8m0", ...)`, documented as "the K stays fp8, quantized over the whole post-RoPE vector, RoPE tail included".

vLLM's 528 B V4.1 record matches that exactly, but `_use_v41_mxfp8_kv_record` returns true only on SM100, because FlashMLA decodes it only there. Every other arch keeps the 584 B V4 record: 448 fp8 NoPE dims, 64 **bf16** RoPE dims, UE8M0 per 64. So ROCm stores 56 B/token more than the model was built for, on the cache that dominates its page budget, and decodes the same weights into different numbers than SM100 does.

Nothing about the 528 B record is NVIDIA-specific: its writer is portable Triton that already sanitizes NaNs for gfx950, and the prefill gather dispatches on the record width with no platform gate. Only the decode tile was missing.

## Approach

The gfx950 tile now takes the per-token width the KV-cache spec publishes instead of a boolean, separately for the sliding-window cache and the compressed one. The two fp8 records differ only in three constants and in what the last chunk holds, so they share one branch:

```python
DATA:   tl.constexpr = 512 if RECORD == 528 else 576
SCALES: tl.constexpr =  16 if RECORD == 528 else   8
QUANT:  tl.constexpr =  32 if RECORD == 528 else  64
```

V4.1 quantized the RoPE dims, so its last chunk is another exact chunk; V4 kept them in bf16 and still splices its tail. `_load_fp8_ds_mla_gfx950_nope_exact_chunk` gains the scale granularity as a constexpr, the only change it needs to serve both. Net 51 insertions against 48 deletions.

The other decode kernels address the V4 record by a fixed stride and split its bf16 tail before the dot, so they keep asserting the V4 width. This turns on for every gfx950 run with no flag, the way the SM100 gate follows its own arch — say so if you would rather it stayed opt-in.

## Test plan

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_sparse_mla_v41_records.py

vllm serve DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --max-model-len 65536 --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --moe-backend aiter --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 16
```

The test drives `rocm_sparse_attn_decode` against a torch softmax over the same dequantized rows, parametrized over the four record pairs the model allocates, so the two V4 arms are the regression case. Because it packs with a reference written against the Triton writer, the numbers below also come from a cross-check where the three production implementations meet: written by `rope_quant_insert`, read back by `dequantize_and_gather_k_cache_triton`, read again by the decode tile. None of the three was written against the others.

## Test result

MI355X (gfx950), 16 passed; the cross-check agrees to cosine 0.9999983 for both records.

**Capacity**, TP=4 and 65,536 context, identical 121.51 GiB of KV memory and nine cache groups in both arms:

| record | GPU KV cache | max concurrency |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| V4 584 B | 8,885,130 tokens | 135.58x |
| V4.1 MXFP8 528 B | 9,714,620 tokens | **148.23x** |

Stacked on the NVFP4 compressed record the pair reaches 11,020,825 tokens and 168.16x, +24.0%.

**Kernel paths**, every path a token takes:

| path | V4 584 B | V4.1 528 B | |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| write, `rope_quant_insert` | 0.0092 ms | 0.0087 ms | V4.1 4–6% faster |
| prefill gather | 0.1339 ms | 0.0418 ms | **V4.1 3.2x faster** |
| decode, in a HIP graph | 0.0287 ms | 0.0290 ms | V4 1–3% faster |

Decode is at the shape this model runs on 4 ranks (16 local heads, `index_topk` 512, sliding window 128) with prebuilt ragged indices. It is the only path V4.1 loses on: it carries 16 UE8M0 scales per token where V4 carries 7, and this kernel is bound by its dependent loads, so those loads outweigh the 56 bytes they save.

**Serving**, GSM8K 1319 questions, 5-shot, concurrency 16, both arms back to back on one node:

| record | output throughput | accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| V4 584 B | 474.3 tok/s | 0.9098 |
| V4.1 MXFP8 528 B | **480.8 tok/s** | 0.9060 |

**Accuracy.** Two GSM8K comparisons give −0.38 pt and −1.06 pt; at 1319 questions the standard error is 0.83 pt, so neither is worth quoting as the number. What is deterministic is the record's own error against the unquantized row — 0.02652 on the NoPE dims for both records, and **0.00166 against 0.02653** on the RoPE dims. Only the bf16 RoPE dims were carrying extra precision, and the reference implementation does not ask for it.

## Known follow-up

- Stacked on #57463, which introduced the record selector this generalizes. That PR alone measures below `fp8_ds_mla`; the two together reach +24.0%.
- Serving DeepSeek-V4.1 on ROCm additionally needs #57036.
- The finer scale block buys nothing measurable: per-32 and per-64 give the same 0.02652 NoPE error, because e4m3's relative precision is scale-invariant. The record is worth taking for the capacity and for matching the reference, not for its granularity.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used in preparing this change.

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

title: [Security] Skip target-only sampling observations in the acceptance estimator
body:
## Summary

When adaptive verification uses the online acceptance estimator, draft sampling copies only temperature and seed. Request-specific transforms such as `allowed_token_ids`, penalties, and `bad_words` are applied on the target but not on the draft, so accept/reject labels from those requests were pooled into worker-wide estimator coefficients used to size verification for later unrelated requests. This change drops those observations from estimator updates. Requests without those transforms still train the estimator as before.

## Changes

- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py`: add `target_only_sampling_transforms()` for the draft-ignored sampling fields.
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py`: drop masked rows before `OnlineAcceptanceEstimator.step`.
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`: pass the mask from the sampler into `observe_verification`.

## Codepath coverage

- All OpenAI-compatible and SageMaker/gRPC inference entry points reach this sink through `GPUModelRunner` → `DraftModelSpeculator.observe_verification`. The skip is applied at that sink.
- DSpark with a confidence head does not construct the estimator (`acceptance_estimator is None`), so it is unchanged.
- Offline `LLM.generate` uses the same worker path.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open/merged PRs for "acceptance estimator", "adaptive verification", "observe_verification", and "draft sampling parameters".
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56724 applies draft-side top-k/top-p for acceptance rate; it does not isolate estimator updates and does not cover `allowed_token_ids`.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57107 disables Triton specialization on estimator kernels; not this control.

## Tests

- `test_target_only_sampling_transforms_match_draft_ignored_fields` / `test_target_only_sampling_transforms_are_per_request`: mask is true for `allowed_token_ids` and other draft-ignored fields, false for temperature-only.
- `test_observe_verification_drops_target_only_sampling_requests`: skipped rows do not accumulate into the estimator.
- `test_select_estimator_observations_*`: row filter keeps, drops-all, and passthrough cases.

Commands:

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_estimator_observation_filter.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_estimator.py -v
```

Result: 4 passed on CPU (observation filter). The two CUDA suites were skipped on this host (`torch.cuda.is_available()` is false); they are intended for GPU CI.

`.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files` on the changed files passed.

## AI assistance

This PR was developed with AI assistance.

title: [Perf][GLM] Fuse the kpool tail slot mapping into one Triton kernel
body:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash sparse-MLA models keep a one-block-per-request circular tail cache (kpool). Every decode step — twice per step with MTP, once for the target model and once for the drafter — `KpoolTailMetadataBuilder.build()` maps each token to its request's tail ring with a chain of small torch ops (`arange` + `searchsorted` + `clamp` + `index_select` + `remainder` + `copy_`): 12 kernel launches and ~250 us of CPU enqueue time per build.

This PR replaces the chain with a single Triton kernel driven directly by `query_start_loc`, including the CUDA-graph padding rows. The CPU-tensor path keeps the torch implementation, and the emitted values are bit-identical to it.

With #57317 the generic `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` no longer runs for `KpoolTailSpec`, so `compute_kpool_tail_slot_mapping` is now the only slot-mapping path for the tail group — this fusion covers all of it. It composes with #57477 (the seed-kernel stride fix): this PR only produces the logical slot ids (`block * kpool + pos % kpool`) that consumers decompose with `// kpool` / `% kpool`; physical addressing of the padded tail view is untouched, and the kernel reads the block table through its real `stride(0)`.

Not a duplicate: #56562 covers the sparse-indexer decode expansion and the token→request mapping (an earlier revision of this PR had similar pieces and was rescoped); #57161 reworks the kpool *compress* kernel and #57458 the NoPE query packing — neither touches the tail slot mapping.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_native_next_n.py
```

E2E setup: 4x GB300 (SM103), TP4, `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (FP8, `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE), `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE --max-model-len 69632 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`, V2 model runner; `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos`, two runs per build, base = `42a33039eb`.

## Test Result

- `test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py`: 17 passed — 4 new CUDA cases check the Triton path against the torch reference, including tokens past the last request boundary, CUDA-graph padding rows, and a non-contiguous (strided-view) block table.
- `test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py` + `test_indexer_native_next_n.py`: 16 passed.
- Bit-exact vs the torch formulation → no output-affecting change, so no separate model eval was run.

Micro (`compute_kpool_tail_slot_mapping`, kpool=4, GB300; CPU = enqueue time without sync, GPU = profiler device time):

| shape | torch CPU | this PR CPU | torch GPU | this PR GPU | launches |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| decode bs=1 (2 tok, MTP k=1) | 157 us | 38 us | 18.2 us | 1.5 us | 12 -> 1 |
| decode bs=16 (32 tok) | 266 us | 35 us | — | — | 12 -> 1 |
| decode bs=64 (128 tok) | 259 us | 34 us | — | — | 12 -> 1 |
| decode bs=256 (512 tok) | 254 us | 33 us | 22.1 us | 2.0 us | 12 -> 1 |
| prefill 1x8192 | 251 us | 33 us | 22.9 us | 12.2 us | 12 -> 1 |
| prefill 2x8192 | 243 us | 32 us | — | — | 12 -> 1 |

E2E (8k in / 1k out, output tok/s, two runs per build):

| point | main | +this PR | Δ (avg) | main run-to-run noise |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 | 220.1 / 215.3 | 229.0 / 228.7 | +5.1% | ±2.2% |
| c=16 | 1359.8 / 1433.0 | 1461.9 / 1397.8 | +2.4% | ±5.4% |
| c=64 | 2229.8 / 2266.4 | 2148.2 / 2285.4 | -1.4% | ±1.6% |
| c=256 | 4176.0 / 4158.9 | 4183.4 / 4188.9 | +0.4% | ±0.4% |

Median TPOT deltas are within noise at every point (-0.6% to +2.7%). The c=1 throughput ordering was consistent across both pairs of runs (and c=1 mean TPOT was 4.19 ms on both PR runs vs 4.37/4.47 ms on main), but with n=2 per build this sits at the edge of the noise floor. The durable claim is the removed per-step CPU work (~0.44 ms/step with MTP: two builds x ~220 us) and 11 fewer launches per build, which async scheduling largely overlaps on this hardware.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the profiling, the implementation and the benchmark harness; every changed line was reviewed and the tests/benchmarks above were run by the submitter.

title: [BugFix][XPU] Skip Qwen4Exp registry import test on XPU
body:
Qwen4Exp (Qwen4ExpForCausalLM, Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration, Qwen4ExpMTP) is only supported on CUDA and ROCm; its module raises NotImplementedError on XPU. ModelRegistry ._try_load_model_cls swallows that exception and returns None, so test_registry_imports failed the 'assert model_cls is not None' check on non-CUDA/ROCm runners instead of skipping.

Add a skip guard for Qwen4Exp following the existing precedent for DSparkDraftModel, Dots3Note, HYV4, and DeepseekV4 vision.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Fix GLM-5.3 kpool indexer block sizes
body:
## Purpose

  Fixes #54359: GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer overwrites its own KV cache.

  On ROCm, GLM-5.3-Flash compresses one indexer state from every
  index_kpool tokens. However, the generic ROCm indexer backend currently
  advertises the following kernel block-size support in token units:

  [1, MultipleOf(16)]

  This allows the complete KV manager block to be selected directly as the
  kernel block size.

  For index_kpool=4 and a 640-token manager block, this selects 640 tokens,
  which represents 160 compressed states. The paged-MQA kernels operate on
  pages of 32 or 64 states, so the block table is not split at the granularity
  used by the kernel.

  As described in
  #54359, this can cause
  multiple logical indexer pages to address the same physical cache slots,
  silently corrupting the indexer cache and degrading long-context retrieval.

  ## Changes

  - Add a cached kpool-aware indexer backend.
  - Scale paged-MQA state page sizes by index_kpool when advertising
    supported kernel block sizes.

  - Use the kpool-aware backend only for Glm5NextIndexerCache on ROCm.
  - Keep the non-ROCm path unchanged.
  - Keep the generic DeepSeek indexer backend unchanged.
  - Add regression coverage for both the 32-state and 64-state page cases.

  For index_kpool=4, the kpool-aware backend advertises:

  32 states × 4 tokens/state = 128 tokens
  64 states × 4 tokens/state = 256 tokens

  This causes the existing hybrid block-table implementation to split the
  manager block into correctly sized virtual kernel pages.

  ## Scope

  This change only affects the attention-backend metadata selected by the
  GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer on ROCm.

  It does not change:

  - KV cache allocation size;
  - model weights or model computation;
  - CUDA backend selection;
  - generic DeepSeek indexer behavior;
  - GPU kernels;
  - deployment or serving parameters.

  ## Validation

  Validation environment:

  - 8× AMD Instinct MI300X
  - gfx942:sramecc+:xnack-
  - ROCm 7.2
  - Tensor parallel size: 8
  - Model: GLM-5.3-Flash
  - index_kpool=4
  - Actual KV manager block size: 640 tokens
  - Prefix caching enabled

  The three changed files were copied to the MI300X validation container and
  syntax-checked:

  python3 -m py_compile \
    vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py \
    vllm/models/glm5next/common/attention.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py

  Result:

  PY_COMPILE=PASS

  The current-main block-size declarations and the proposed kpool-aware
  declarations were then passed through select_common_block_size in the
  MI300X container.

  Results:
| Manager block | Before | Before states | After | After states | Virtual pages per manager block |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 640 | 640 | 160 | 128 | 32 | 5 |
| 1280 | 1280 | 320 | 256 | 64 | 5 |
             

  GEOMETRY_ASSERTIONS=PASS

  For the production configuration, the important result is:

  manager block:  640 tokens
  index_kpool: 4 tokens/state
  old kernel block:640 tokens = 160 states
  fixed kernel block:28 tokens =  32 states
  virtual split: 640 / 128 = 5 pages

  The added regression test covers both mappings:

  pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py \
    -k test_select_common_block_size_scales_kpool_pages_to_tokens

  The validation container uses an older backported vLLM runtime
  (v0.1.dev1+gfdd64a3db) and therefore cannot directly execute the complete
  current-main test module. Equivalent block-size selection assertions were
  executed successfully in the MI300X container. The repository regression
  test is intended to run in the current-main CI environment.

  ## Model correctness evidence

  The original reproducer and before/after results are documented in
  #54359:

  - distinct cache slots written: 864/4096 before and 4096/4096 after;
  - needle recall: 0/6 before and 8/8 after;
  - fixed-build coverage from approximately 6.7K to 1M prompt tokens.

  Detailed needle-in-a-haystack results are available in
  this issue comment.

  An independent MI325X/gfx942 confirmation is available in
  this issue comment.

  That independent result reports:

  - inconsistent top-k index sets before correcting the block-table granularity;
  - consistent top-k index sets across runs and TP ranks after correction;
  - needle recall improving from 1/3 to 3/3.

  This PR implements the kpool-aware backend selection described by that
  root-cause analysis.

  ## Duplicate check

  As of 2026-09-18,
  #54359 remains open,
  and no dedicated PR implementing kpool-scaled backend block-size selection
  was found.

  The original model-support PR,
  #53906, does not contain
  this fix.

title: [CI][Test] GLM-5.3-Flash layer-pruned checkpoint tests (e2e, KV offload, NIXL PD)
body:
## Purpose

Give the GLM-5.3-Flash serving stack (hybrid KDA + DeepSeek-sparse-MLA with the kpool indexer / tail
scratch group, fp8 MoE, mHC, MTP, PD disaggregation, KV offload) CI coverage that does not need a
4-GPU node holding the 328 GB checkpoint.

The asset is a **layer-pruned real checkpoint**, `JaredforReal/GLM-5.3-Flash-4L`: original layers 0-3
(one 3x KDA + 1x DSA-MLA period, dense MLP on 0-2, MoE on 3) plus the MTP layer, with **every width
unchanged** (288 routed experts, 64 KDA heads, MLA/indexer dims, vision tower). Only whole layers were
removed, so kernel selection and the KV cache layout match the 300B model: the same
`{MLA+indexer}`, `{kpool tail}` and Mamba groups aliasing the MLA slot, and the same auto block size
(4352 / 2176 / 1152 tokens at TP1 / TP2 / TP4). 18.5 GiB, loads in ~8 s. Derivation and the exact config
edits are documented in the model card.

New tests (SM90/SM100 only: the DeepGEMM paged-MQA indexer and FlashMLA/FlashInfer sparse MLA do not run on L4):

| test | GPUs | guards |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/models/glm5next/test_pruned_e2e.py` | 1 | KV groups = {MLA + indexer}, {kpool tail}, 3 Mamba groups aliasing the MLA tensor; greedy reproducibility across a block boundary with a prompt longer than `index_topk`; MTP drafter loads and agrees with target-only greedy. A strict xfail documents the `fused_recurrent_kda` gridDim.z overflow at 64 heads x 1024 seqs (#56973, fixed by #56974; the marker must be dropped once that lands).; **prefill checkpoint pages**: a prompt crossing a block boundary leaves, in every Mamba group, a cached checkpoint page equal to a cold prefill ending at that boundary (relative error <= 0.03 observed, >= 1 when a group's checkpoint goes to another group's page, the #59536 regression that the greedy repeat test does not notice) |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py::test_update_block_table_matches_fresh_build` | 1 | `update_block_table()` for a sibling Mamba group equals a fresh `build()` on that group's block table in every metadata field (recursively over nested dataclasses), so a per-group field added later cannot stay pointed at the source group; fails before #59536 on `checkpoint.state_indices` |
| `tests/v1/kv_offload/test_glm5next_pruned_e2e.py` | 1 | SimpleCPUOffloadConnector / OffloadingConnector round trip through `reset_prefix_cache`, asserting CPU hits and identical tokens. Fails on main today because the kpool tail group (block 4, not prefix-cacheable) is not skipped (`resolve_block_hashes` assert / `tokens_per_block=4 not divisible by tokens_per_hash`); SimpleCPUOffload passes with #56810. |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_glm5next_pd_test.sh` + `test_hybrid_pd_consistency.py` | 2 | NixlConnector 1P1D with `VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS`; reuses `test_mamba_prefix_cache.py` (its ~9000-token prompt spans two 4352-token blocks) and checks P-only vs P->D top-1 logprobs within a tolerance. Hybrid PD recomputes the last prompt token on D (`_prefill_backoff`), so exact text equality as in `test_edge_cases.py` is not the right assertion for this model. |

Buildkite: single-GPU jobs on `h200_35gb` (models_language.yaml, lm_eval.yaml), the PD job on 2x `h100`
(disaggregated.yaml); MIG slices cannot do cross-device NIXL and the existing PD sweeps run on L4. The
Pruned E2E step also depends on `vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py`, `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/`,
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/` and `vllm/v1/core/`: #58762 (cross-group metadata reuse) changed only those paths and
would not have triggered a step keyed on `vllm/models/glm5next/` alone.

Known interactions: #55219 (draft) replaces `KpoolTailSpec` with a `CircularBufferSpec` tail, which
would change the spec names asserted in `test_kv_cache_layout`.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Searched open PRs/issues for "GLM-5.3-Flash CI", "glm5next test", "pruned checkpoint", "GLM-5.3-Flash nixl"
(2026-09-18): no PR adds a reduced GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoint or e2e/PD/offload tests for it. Related but
different: #56974 (KDA grid.z fix; the kernel still launches `grid.z = num_seqs * heads`, but the TP1
startup at `max_num_seqs=1024` no longer reaches it on current main, so `test_default_max_num_seqs_tp1` is a
plain test now), #56810 (SimpleCPUOffload tail-group skip, the offload test's expected fix), #55219 (tail spec
rework), #59536 (the checkpoint-page regression the new test guards; merged 2026-10-01).

## Test Plan

```bash
# 1 GPU (SM90+)
pytest -v -s tests/models/glm5next/test_pruned_e2e.py
pytest -v -s tests/v1/kv_offload/test_glm5next_pruned_e2e.py
pytest -v -s tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py -k update_block_table
# 2 GPUs
bash tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_glm5next_pd_test.sh
```

`GLM5_PRUNED_MODEL` / `MODEL` override the checkpoint path for local runs.

## Test Result

GB300 x4, main 18553c5c9f, `enforce_eager`:

| run | result |
|---|---|
| `test_pruned_e2e.py` (TP1) | 3 passed + 1 xfailed (strict) on main 18553c5c9f; **5 passed** on main b538d807ff (2026-10-01, includes #59536). Checkpoint-page relative errors per layer (conv / recurrent): 4e-4 / 2e-3, 1e-2 / 9e-3, 2e-2 / 2e-2; with #59536's two files reverted the same test fails with 2.4 / 4.3, 1 / 1, 1 / 1 |
| `test_gdn_metadata_builder.py -k update_block_table` | 4 passed on main b538d807ff; the new equivalence test fails on the pre-#59536 tree at `checkpoint.state_indices` |
| `test_glm5next_pruned_e2e.py` on main | 2 failed as designed (tail-group asserts above) |
| same, SimpleCPUOffloadConnector on the #56810 branch | passed (CPU prefix-cache hits > 0 after `reset_prefix_cache`, cold == warm tokens) |
| `run_glm5next_pd_test.sh` (1P1D, `--max-num-seqs 256`) | 2 passed: D-side prefix hits cut NIXL transfer 26.8 MB -> 22.2 MB, outputs equal; P-only vs P->D first-4 max logprob delta 0.20 / 0.07 / 0.61 (short / mid / 6.5k-token) with P-only vs D-only 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.06 |

Notes from the local runs: all tests are text-only (`limit_mm_per_prompt={"image":0,"video":0}`) because
cold encoder profiling of the 24-block vision tower took ~25 min of cuDNN/CUTLASS JIT; the fp8 MoE was
forced to `deep_gemm` on this SM100 node because the FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE module was re-JIT-compiled on
every engine start (not relevant on the H100/H200 CI targets).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the analysis, the checkpoint builder and the test drafts; all
runs above were executed by the author.

title: [Build] Fix DeepGEMM CUDA 12.9 release builds
body:
## Purpose

Restore the six CUDA 12.9 release targets that fail in [release-v2 #6858](https://buildkite.com/vllm/release-v2/builds/6858): x86_64 and aarch64 wheels, plus both architectures' default and Ubuntu 24.04 images.

All six fail while compiling DeepGEMM's host extension because `layout/mega_mhc.cuh` uses `__nv_fp8_e4m3` without including `<cuda_fp8.h>`. CUDA 13's transitive includes mask the missing declaration; CUDA 12.9 does not. The subsequent `y_fp8` errors are consequences of that missing type.

Update both synchronized DeepGEMM pins from `a6bbb800` to the merged upstream commit [e1f418c2](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/commit/e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f) from [DeepGEMM#12](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/12). The dependency delta is exactly five include lines in two headers; it preserves all current SM90/SM120 and Mega MoE changes.

## Duplicate-work check

The header fix is merged in DeepGEMM#12; this PR consumes that work in vLLM and does not propose another upstream implementation. The merged commit has vLLM's current pin as its sole parent. title: [fix] Mistral-Large-3 accuracy regression on `main`
body:
## Purpose

It appears some changes to the config parsing for Mistral Large 3 degraded accuracy. These changes try to remediate.

### Root cause

Mistral-Large-3 ships a Mistral-format `params.json` with

```json
"yarn": {"factor": 36, "beta": 32, "alpha": 1, "original_max_position_embeddings": 8192, "apply_scale": false},
"llama_4_scaling": {"beta": 0.1, "original_max_position_embeddings": 8192}
```

i.e. YaRN frequency interpolation **without** YaRN's magnitude correction (mscale), plus
llama4-style position-dependent attention scaling. vLLM serves it as
`MistralLarge3ForCausalLM`, a subclass of `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM`, so the DeepSeek
attention code runs on a config synthesized by the Mistral adapter
(`vllm/transformers_utils/configs/mistral.py`).

Commit `c191787a68`, "[Bugfix] Align vLLM YaRN with Transformers and stop re-scaling
max_model_len" (#56446, merged 2026-09-11).

Mistral-Large-3 is the only model that both goes through the Mistral remap and asks for
YaRN without magnitude scaling, which is why nothing else moved. Verified by loading the
checkpoint's config through `get_config(..., config_format="mistral")`: on `main` the
resulting `rope_parameters` has `attention_factor: 1.0` and no `apply_yarn_scaling`.

## Test Plan

Start server with `vllm serve` and evaluate on GSM8K.

Identical for both arms (TP1 / DP4 / EP4, default MoE backend, which resolves to
FlashInfer TRTLLM for this checkpoint):

```bash
vllm serve \
    /models/Mistral-Large-3-675B-Instruct-2512-NVFP4 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
    --moe-backend auto --tokenizer-mode mistral --language-model-only \
    --max-model-len 5120 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --seed 42 --port 8000
```

Testing is done using the gsm8k eval, launched with the helper script: `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` from the vLLM checkout against the running server, five
times back to back per arm (only `--save-results` changes between passes, we ran multiple times to reduce variance):

```bash
python /workspace/vllm/tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py \
    --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
    --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 \
    --temperature 0 --seed 42 --max-concurrency 128 \
    --save-results gsm8k-rep<N>.json
```

## Test Result

(accuracy, %)

| arm | pass 1 | pass 2 | pass 3 | pass 4 | pass 5 | mean | sd |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main-no-fix` (`4c6c1a40b3`) | 87.41 | 87.72 | 87.49 | 87.87 | 89.76 | 88.05 | 0.97 |
| `fix` (`265b1c54e3`) | 92.49 | 92.72 | 92.95 | 92.80 | 92.19 | 92.63 | 0.30 |

Difference: **+4.58 points** for the fix (about 60 more correct answers per pass of 1,319).
Welch t = 10.1 on 5 vs 5 passes; the per-pass binomial noise floor at this accuracy is
0.81 points. Invalid-answer rate was 0.00% in every pass except one fix pass at 0.08%
(one question). The fixed arm matches the 92.2 / 92.8% measured on 2026-09-10, before
#56446 was merged.

title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash (glm5_next, qk_rope_head_dim=0 / NoPE MLA) crashes — concat_and_cache_mla requires pe_dim==64
body:
### Summary

vLLM cannot serve `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (or its NVFP4/FP8 quants, e.g. `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`). The model's MLA is **NoPE** (`qk_rope_head_dim = 0`), but `glm5_next`'s only attention backend, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`, uses the `fp8_ds_mla` / `nvfp4_ds_mla` KV-cache format, whose `concat_and_cache_mla` kernel hardcodes DeepSeek geometry (`pe_dim == 64`, `kv_lora_rank == 512`). It loads, wires up TP, and profiles the KV cache successfully, then dies in MLA warmup:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'concat_and_cache_mla, csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu:939, pe_dim must be 64 for fp8_ds_mla'
```

### Why it's not just the assertion

`concat_and_cache_ds_mla_kernel` launches `block(96)` = 64 threads for the 512-wide NoPE part + threads 64–95 copying exactly 64 RoPE elements into a fixed 656-byte entry. For `pe_dim=0` there is no RoPE section, so relaxing the `STD_TORCH_CHECK(pe_dim == 64, ...)` would make the RoPE threads read nonexistent `k_pe` and write a bogus rope region → silent corruption. Supporting NoPE MLA needs a dedicated kernel variant + entry layout + format routing. The same `pe_dim == 64` requirement exists in the `nvfp4_ds_mla` path, and both are still present on `main` (`csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu`).

### Repro

```
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --distributed-executor-backend ray \
  --trust-remote-code --enforce-eager
```

(also fails single-node). Removing `quantization_config.kv_cache_scheme` from the checkpoint config does **not** help — the sparse-MLA backend selects `fp8_ds_mla` regardless.

Relevant model config:

- `qk_rope_head_dim = 0`  ← NoPE
- `qk_nope_head_dim = 256`
- `kv_lora_rank = 512`
- `v_head_dim = 256`
- hybrid full-attention + KDA linear-attention layers
- DeepSeek sparse attention (`DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER`)

### Environment

- vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev347+gdee37d891` (`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-aarch64`)
- CUDA 13.0
- 2× NVIDIA GB10 (Grace-Blackwell, SM120), aarch64
- TP=2 across two nodes over RoCE/RDMA (Ray executor)

The model loads (~89 GiB/node), wires up tensor-parallel over the interconnect, and profiles a ~460K-token KV cache before hitting the assertion during MLA warmup — so everything except this KV-cache kernel path works.
