Quantization (including GPTQ) and Model Executor (including tensorizer) remain off DPX. Their main-CI AMD mirrors run on `mi300_1`; legacy coverage retains `mi300_1` plus the existing full-card `mi355_1` Quantization jobs. These suites retain their normal assertions and failure reporting.

General LM Eval Small Models, MoE Kernels, Quantization Kernels, and Core Operation Kernels run on MI300 in both pipelines. The legacy labels and hardware selectors match that queue. Their commands, shard counts, timeouts, and failure policies are preserved. Dedicated DPX jobs cover native quantization, FP4/INT4 MoE, and the small gfx950 evaluation model list.

The resulting main pipeline contains 77 DPX groups / 106 shards; the legacy pipeline contains 74 DPX groups / 110 shards. All 225 legacy groups are retained, including the incoming full-card DSv4-Flash disaggregated and TurboQuant t3nc jobs.

The supporting Python, shell, and model-list changes are in [#58244](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58244). This split avoids duplicating those changes across the two PRs. **Merge #58244 first**: the YAML references its new `tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/models-gfx950-small.txt` and relies on its supporting fixes.

The MI355 DPX Fullgraph job temporarily sets `TORCHINDUCTOR_PRECOMPILATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=0` to avoid the concurrent Triton LLVM codegen/LLD race seen in [Buildkite #90998](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90998#01a0d46e-00d5-4a44-b7eb-1f683ecc6d4b). The failure is `GCNRegPressure.cpp:524: Assertion 'MRI && "call reset first"' failed`. This disables background precompilation while keeping compilation and autotuning enabled; cold compilation may take longer. Remove the workaround once the ROCm Triton pin includes [triton-lang/triton#11567](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/11567).

All five passed generated step-key, queue, and GPU-resource checks, including single-partition DPX requests without an extra GPU claim.
- Semantic comparison after the merge confirmed all 223 pre-merge legacy groups remain, with only the incoming Helion dependency path correction; both new jobs exactly match main. The merged pipeline has 225 legacy groups. DPX routing, MI300 exclusions, Torchrun timeouts of 55 minutes, and Hybrid SSM timeouts of 80 minutes are preserved.
- Local workaround smoke test: `TORCHINDUCTOR_PRECOMPILATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=0 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s 'tests/compile/fullgraph/test_full_graph.py::test_custom_compile_config[compilation_config1-RedHatAI/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-FP8-dynamic-model_kwargs1]'` passed in 137.79 seconds with fresh Triton/Inductor/vLLM caches. This ran on local vLLM `310f15d354`, stock Triton `3.7.1+gitf0b55c07`, and a full-card MI355. Logs confirmed 16 background-precompile bypasses, 16 autotuning passes, and four generated outputs.

title: [ROCm] Enable Hisparse on ROCm : Sparse MLA Hot-Buffering
body:
# [ROCm] HiSparse: host-resident sparse-MLA hot-buffering on gfx950

## Purpose

Enables HiSparse (#53781) on AMD ROCm, verified on gfx950 (MI350X, CDNA4).
HiSparse keeps the bulk of the sparse-MLA KV cache in pinned host memory and
pulls back only the indexer-selected rows just in time, so long-context agentic
sessions stop getting preempted. #53781 landed it CUDA-only.

## Changes

**Route HiSparse attention through the int64-safe Triton kernel.** HiSparse
points attention at a view over the *whole multi-layer KV slab*, so emitted row
indices scale with total block count: max row index is 33 off HiSparse and 7.5M
on. AITER's decode kernel computes `row_index * row_width` in int32, so on
GLM-5.3 (`row_width=576`) it wraps above row 3,728,270 and returns approximately
zero — no NaN, no assert. Force Triton kernel for HiSparse for time being. 

**ROCm backend wiring.** CUDA HiSparse backends consume a dense `[tokens, topk]`
tensor; AITER's decode kernel consumes a ragged list plus indptr. Bridging that
is most of the diff: `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` registers with an
`index_group_builder` (which is what makes `mla_attention.py` pick up
`hisparse_cache`), decode converts dense physical top-k to ragged and attends
against the hot buffer, and prefill stages host rows via `stage_prefill_rows`
when the context is not fully resident. One new Triton kernel,
`compact_topk_to_ragged_triton` — `fetch_id_to_ragged_triton` was not reusable
because a mid-row `-1` must drop out rather than displace a valid entry.
AITER's persistent work-stealing metadata is disabled under HiSparse (its
buffers are sized in `build()`, but HiSparse rewrites the indptr at forward
time); noted as a perf follow-up.

**HIP kernel port (`csrc/`).** The four fused HiSparse cache ops build and run
on ROCm. Mechanical: vectorized copy widths, `__nv_bfloat16` → `hip_bfloat16`,
warp-primitive shims in `csrc/cuda_compat.h`. CUDA codegen unaffected.

**Config gate.** Opens HiSparse for ROCm; `fp8_ds_mla` (656-byte packed row) is
rejected by name rather than failing deep in a kernel.

**Keep batched KV copies off the HIP blit path.** HIP routes copies at or below
`GPU_FORCE_BLIT_COPY_SIZE` through a blit kernel that faults once enough are
outstanding, and HiSparse's host mirror submits ~160k descriptors per step.
Defaulting it to 2 (KB) sends them to SDMA instead. A 2x2 crossover isolates
the engine rather than the dtype: forcing fp8 onto SDMA passes 20/20, forcing
bf16 onto blit fails 0/20.

The constant has to sit below the *smallest* KV page in play, not just
HiSparse's. At 4 it lifts HiSparse's 9216 B page off blit but leaves
`OffloadingConnector`'s 2112 B rope page on it, and that path still dies; at 2
both clear. This also fixes CPU offload above concurrency 1 on ROCm, which
previously crashed outright - see the throughput table.

**Pass `indexer_slot_mapping` in the amd module.** `common/kernels.py`
substitutes `slot_mapping` when `indexer_slot_mapping` is `None`, and the amd
path never passed it, so the fused norm+rope kernel wrote the indexer's keys at
the MLA slots. Invisible without HiSparse, where the indexer and MLA groups
share one slot mapping.

## Platform-neutral fixes

These are in shared code and affect CUDA too.

- **`index_group.py` — event record does not survive nested `torch.compile`.**
  `record(...)` is traceable, so Dynamo lowers it to a node whose event lives in
  a process-global side table that `reset_user_object_tracking()` clears on
  compile entry. vLLM nests compiles, so an inner compile wipes the entry an
  outer graph depends on. Replaced with an opaque custom op keyed by an integer
  handle. CUDA appears to escape this only because its call path reaches
  `set_logical_topk_ready` from outside the compiled region.
- **`hisparse/worker.py` — mirror guard for unbracketed runs.** Warmup runs the
  model with the connector disabled, so `_per_layer_mirrored` is never cleared
  and the second pass trips `HiSparse layer 0 mirrored twice`. Added a
  `_step_in_flight` flag; the double-mirror check is unchanged inside a step.
- **`worker_base.py` — layout query runs outside the config scope.**
  `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` calls `get_current_attn_backends(...)` with
  no config set, but a backend's supported set can depend on it. Wrapped in
  `set_current_vllm_config`.
- **`hisparse/runtime.py` — `cudaGetLastError` is absent on ROCm**, so the
  unregister-failure handler raised `AttributeError` and masked the real error.
  Guarded with `getattr`; the clear is best-effort cleanup.

## Required AITER fix (out of tree)

**This branch does not run on stock AITER.** With HiSparse enabled, gfx950 takes
a `Memory access fault` in AITER's 1-stage fp8-blockscale MoE
`fmoe_fp8_blockscale_g1u1`. Not a HiSparse bug, but HiSparse is what makes it
fire. [ROCm/aiter#5764](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5764) backs the tail
with real memory at the `per_1x128` launch site, returning a view with the
original shape so no observable value changes. **Every number below was produced
with that patch applied.**

## Tests and Result

8× MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, AITER 0.1.21.

| Suite | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_hisparse_kernels.py` | 16 passed, 76 skipped | **41 passed** |
| `test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py` | 4 passed | **4 passed** |
| `test_sparse_mla_backends.py` | 84 passed, 688 skipped | **101 passed, 687 skipped** |
| `-k hisparse` across `tests/{kernels,v1}/attention` | 15 passed, 15 skipped | **75 passed, 16 skipped** |
| `test_fused_deepseek_v32_norm_rope.py` | 130 passed, 8 skipped | **130 passed, 8 skipped** |
| `test_amd_fused_call_parity.py` (new) | — | **1 passed** |
| `test_hisparse.py` (e2e) | skipped (CUDA-gated) | **2 passed** |

`test_amd_fused_call_parity.py` compares the `fused_norm_rope` kwargs at the
CUDA and ROCm call sites. A silent `None` default cannot be caught by reading
one call site, and that omission class produced both amd-module bugs fixed here.

## Accuracy

GSM8K, 200 questions, 5-shot, greedy (`temperature=0`), seed 42. GLM-5.3, TP4,
78 layers, gfx950, 32k context, cudagraphs on, 128 GiB pinned host pool.
Model Runner V2 forced in **both** arms.

| Arm | KV dtype | Accuracy | invalid | Latency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HiSparse **off** | bf16 | 0.915 | 0.00 | 18.1 s |
| HiSparse **on** | bf16 | **0.940** | 0.00 | 34.4 s |
| HiSparse **on** | fp8 | **0.920** | 0.00 | 36.7 s |

**Accuracy while the host path is live.** GSM8K runs below HiSparse's offload
watermark, so it does not exercise the feature. A needle probe (TP8,
`--max-model-len 80000`, 256 GiB host pool, bf16) loads the pool with holder
requests until KV usage sits just under the watermark, then measures with short
probes alongside: **60/60**, 12/12 at every depth (10/30/50/70/90%), **245.4 GiB
host→device during the probe window**, 0 preemptions. A 25-probe run at lighter
load agrees (25/25), as does a below-watermark control.

## Throughput

The GLM-5.3 hybrid-offloading blog workload: OpenHands-style agentic
conversations, 13 turns, first turn ~74k tokens, output pinned to 220. **TP4 on
4x MI350X** (the blog ran TP8 on H200), `--max-model-len 131072`, bf16 KV,
sequential arms, fresh server per point. All three arms run to completion.

tok/s/GPU:

| arm | conc 1 | conc 8 | conc 16 | conc 24 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| no offloading | **3505** | **10466** | 2334 | 2339 |
| CPU offload 512 GiB | 3117 | 7100 | 2218 | 1473 |
| **HiSparse 512 GiB** | 1409 | 2503 | **4270** | **4358** |

TTFT median:

| arm | conc 1 | conc 8 | conc 16 | conc 24 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| no offloading | 0.3 s | 0.9 s | 68.3 s | 132.0 s |
| CPU offload 512 GiB | 0.3 s | 1.1 s | 71.9 s | 210.5 s |
| **HiSparse 512 GiB** | 0.6 s | 1.5 s | **1.6 s** | **1.4 s** |

## Limitations

- **AITER's tuned ASM sparse decode is unusable under HiSparse** until its row
  offset is widened to 64 bits
- **`fp8_ds_mla` is not supported on ROCm**
- **Gated on [ROCm/aiter#5764](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5764).**
- **Imported IPC events cap at 32 record/wait cycles on ROCm** 
- **`MultiConnector` combining HiSparse with `OffloadingConnector` crashes** on
  ROCm; each works alone.

---

*AI assistance was used in preparing this change.* All changes reviewed by the
submitter.

title: [Bugfix] Plain MTP must not trigger the all-groups eagle-group fallback (it zeroes all prefix-cache insertions)
body:
## Purpose

On hybrid GDN/mamba models with plain built-in MTP (`method="mtp"`), enabling prefix caching alongside spec decode silently zeroes **all** prefix-cache hits: `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` stays at exactly 0 even for byte-identical repeated prompts. Root cause and repro context: #54360 (this PR fixes the mechanism described there).

Chain: no group is identified as the draft's (plain MTP shares the target KV, so there is no draft group by construction) → `KVCacheCoordinator`'s conservative fallback flags **all** groups as eagle → `get_replay_boundaries()` takes the eagle branch and, with `scheduler_block_size` at 3200 and a 4,137-token prompt, both `resend` and `extension` floor to 3200, returning boundaries of `{0}` → `cache_blocks()` inserts nothing → the radix tree is empty and every query misses.

Plain MTP proposes from target hidden states and **has no separate draft KV group**, so "no group identified" is the expected state, not an annotation failure; flagging every group is wrong for it. Methods that do ship a real draft KV (eagle/eagle3/draft_model/dflash/dspark) keep the fallback unchanged.

## Does this introduce a breaking change?

No. Non-MTP methods are unaffected (same `use_eagle` value as before). For plain MTP it restores correct insertion; the trailing-block pollution guard (`use_eagle_block_drop`) remains fully active — this is not the same as the user-side workaround of setting `disable_eagle_block_drop: true`, which additionally disables that guard.

## Testing

DGX Spark GB10 (SM121), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 (125B-A6B hybrid GDN+QSA), MTP k=3, align mode, `--enable-prefix-caching`, piecewise cudagraphs, 262K ctx:

| config | prefix_cache_hits_total | repeat 4,137-token prompt TTFT | MTP acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|
| nightly, no workaround | **0** | 3.6 s every time | 44.5% (piecewise bench) |
| nightly + `disable_eagle_block_drop` (workaround) | 6,400/12,778 = 50.1% | 3.6 → 1.6 s | 44.5% |
| **this PR (no workaround, guard retained)** | **6,400/12,778 = 50.1%** | **3.6 → 1.6 s** | unchanged |

Multiturn conversations stable across all three configs; no regressions in an 8-category decode benchmark (38.9 tok/s median with our disk-backed PLE table, matching the workaround config).

## AI disclosure

Assisted-by: AI agent (ZCode). The submitter analyzed, patched, and measured everything on hardware and reviewed every changed line.

title: [Example][Model] Add V2-interface NGramPerReqLogitsProcessor for DeepSeek-OCR
body:
## Summary

Add `NGramPerReqLogitsProcessorV2` — a Model Runner V2 custom logits processor providing the no-repeat-ngram constraint used by DeepSeek-OCR / Unlimited-OCR.

Context: as noted in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46564#issuecomment-4824395098, Unlimited-OCR needs `NGramPerReqLogitsProcessor` for good long-document OCR, but that class implements the V1 `AdapterLogitsProcessor` interface, which the V2 runner's loader rejects. This PR re-implements it as a standalone **custom logits processor** in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/ngram_per_req.py`, against the V2 `LogitsProcessor` interface, configured per request via `SamplingParams.extra_args` (`ngram_size`, `window_size`, `whitelist_token_ids`) — no `SamplingParams` or protocol changes, since this is not a built-in.

**Stacked on #56497** (Model Runner V2 custom logits processor support, including the `seq_lens_upper_bound_np` `LogitsContext` plumbing). Only the top commit is new:

- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/ngram_per_req.py`: `NGramPerReqLogitsProcessorV2` + the batched core `_ban_repeated_ngrams` + shared `_validate_ngram_params`.
- `vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_ocr.py`: the V1 `NGramPerReqLogitsProcessor` stays for the V1 runner and now shares parameter validation from the new module.
- DeepSeek-OCR examples switched to the V2 class.
- `tests/v1/sample/test_ngram_per_req.py`: new unit tests.

Implementation notes:

- The batched core is sync-free vectorized PyTorch: candidate ngrams are gathered right-aligned from `req_states.all_token_ids`, prefix-matched with broadcast comparisons, and banned via `scatter_reduce_(amax)` on a float32 mask (plain `scatter_` races when a token is banned at one position and merely gathered at another; CUDA scatter_gather has no bool kernel). Requests are grouped by `ngram_size` on the host from `ctx.seq_lens_upper_bound_np` / `idx_mapping_np`.
- Two V1 quirks are preserved for parity: only output tokens are scanned (prompt excluded), and `ngram_size == 1` is a no-op (the V1 slice `output_ids[-(n-1):]` degenerates to the whole sequence, which never matches).
- Speculative decoding is rejected in `__init__`, matching the V1 runner's rejection of custom logits processors under spec decode.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- #46564 (Unlimited-OCR) explicitly needs this processor on V2 but does not implement it.
- #57540 adds a *native built-in* GPU no-repeat-ngram masking (`no_repeat_ngram_size` only). This PR is the per-request custom-logits-processor route the model family uses today, and additionally supports `window_size` and `whitelist_token_ids`, which OCR grounding requires (special tokens such as `<|det|>` must stay exempt from banning).

## Test plan / results

- `tests/v1/sample/test_ngram_per_req.py` (new): 14 passed, local CPU and on GB200 — randomized equivalence against the V1 `NoRepeatNGramLogitsProcessor` (n in {1,2,3}, window, whitelist on/off), prompt-exclusion, and `validate_params` coverage. A separate 500-trial fuzz comparison against the V1 processor showed 0 mismatches.
- GPU sampler regression suites on GB200: `tests/v1/worker/test_logits_processor_loader.py`, `test_gpu_batch_shard.py`, `test_gpu_logits_processors.py` all pass.

title: [Bugfix] Scope the nested-RoPE validator patch to the allowlisted model types
body:
Closes #57623

## Purpose

#57289 made the nested-RoPE validator patch reach transformers' automatic validation and, per review, kept it "surgical" by installing it only for the model types in `_PATCH_HF_NESTED_ROPE_VALIDATION` (`laguna`, `gemma4_text`). The installed wrapper, though, replaces `PretrainedConfig.validate_rope` for the rest of the process and drops shared `rope_parameters` entries for any config it validates. So once a `laguna` or `gemma4_text` config has been parsed, a later config of any other model type with the same malformed shape is accepted with a warning instead of failing validation. This PR makes the wrapper check the model type as well, so only the allowlisted types get the accommodation.

Reproduction on `main` (config loading only, no GPU): a `gemma3_text` config with a shared `rope_theta` beside its per-layer dicts raises `AttributeError: 'float' object has no attribute 'get'` when built; after `get_config("poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-NVFP4", trust_remote_code=True)` in the same process, the identical config builds with `Dropping ['rope_theta'] from rope_parameters` logged. Same through `vllm.config.ModelConfig`. Issue linked above has the snippet.

This is the nested-map sibling of #57188 (the same wrapper mutating later flat `rope_parameters`), which #57189 fixed with the layer-type gate.

## Changes

- `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py`: in `_patch_hf_transformers_nested_rope_validation`'s wrapper, an early return to the original `validate_rope` when `getattr(self, "model_type", None)` is not in `_PATCH_HF_NESTED_ROPE_VALIDATION`. Five added lines, nothing removed. The install gate, the allowlist, the `__class_validators__` walk and the `sarvam_mla` shim are unchanged.
- `tests/test_config.py`: the #57189 test's nested namespace gets `model_type="laguna"` (the contract it now depends on); new `test_nested_rope_validation_patch_is_scoped_to_allowlisted_model_types`, same `monkeypatch` style, asserts a nested mapping on `model_type="llama"` keeps its shared key and reaches the original validator once. Fails on `main`, passes here.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -k nested_rope_validation
# as the Engine Core shard runs it, from tests/
.venv/bin/python -m pytest test_config.py
pre-commit run --files vllm/transformers_utils/config.py tests/test_config.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files vllm/transformers_utils/config.py tests/test_config.py --hook-stage manual
```

Config-level checks with the real checkpoints (public `config.json`, no weights): the two reproducers from #57289 (`deepseek-ai/dspark_gemma4_12b_block7`, `poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-NVFP4`) with the allowlist intact; the `gemma3_text` snippet above before and after a laguna parse; and the other two checkpoints the CI e2e suites use (`RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-NVFP4`, `poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-DFlash-NVFP4`) with the patch bypassed.

## Test Result

Fedora 44, Python 3.12, torch 2.13.0+cpu, transformers 5.17.0, huggingface_hub 1.31.0, no GPU.

| | `main` (50d812b66) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `-k nested_rope_validation` | new test fails: `Right contains 1 more item: {'rope_theta': 10000.0}` | 2 passed |
| `tests/test_config.py` | 13 failed, 360 passed, 7 skipped | 13 failed, 360 passed, 7 skipped, the same 13 |
| pre-commit, mypy-3.12 | | all hooks passed |

The 13 failures are this host's, not the change's: gated `meta-llama` repos with no token here (`test_rope_customization`, `test_is_encoder_decoder[Llama-3.2-1B]`, the `test_vllm_config_defaults` cases that load `Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct`), `pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla: expected True, got False` (a CUDA default asserted on CPU), and two async-scheduling defaults on CPU. Identical list on unmodified `main`.

Behaviour, config loading only:

| | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `gemma3_text` with a shared `rope_theta`, before the laguna parse | `AttributeError: 'float' object has no attribute 'get'` | same |
| the same config after the laguna parse | built, keys dropped, second `Dropping` warning | `AttributeError`, identical to before the parse |
| through `vllm.config.ModelConfig` | built, keys dropped | `AttributeError` |
| `dspark_gemma4_12b_block7`, `Laguna-XS-2.1-NVFP4` (allowlist intact) | load, keys dropped, one warning each | identical |
| `RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-NVFP4` (`gemma4_unified`), `Laguna-XS-2.1-DFlash-NVFP4` (`laguna`), patch bypassed | load clean, no shared entries | identical (not affected by the patch) |

The last row is the blast radius on the two nightly e2e suites #57289 was written for: every config that needs the drop (`laguna` target, `gemma4_text` draft) is allowlisted, so the scoped wrapper drops exactly what the merged wrapper dropped for them.

Also run: the check inverted on purpose makes the #57189 test fail (the laguna namespace keeps its stray) and the early return deleted makes the new test fail; both reverts byte-identical (sha256). Install order of the two rope patches, repeated installs, classes imported or `@strict`-decorated after the install, a class without its own snapshot, and the legacy `validate_rope(ignore_keys=...)` call behave exactly as on `main` (probe outputs identical line for line). The 13 rope-related tests in two seeded shuffled orders and after a SIGKILL mid-run: same single gated-repo failure each time. A fresh clone with a fresh venv following `docs/getting_started/installation/cpu.md` reproduces the two tests passing and the behaviour table.

Model evaluation: not applicable. The change only decides whether a malformed config is repaired or rejected at load time; every config that loaded before still loads with the same values, and no model was run.

## Not in this PR

- Whether the patch should exist at all. The review on #57289 already said the real fix is the checkpoint (`poolside/Laguna-XS.2` discussion 12, still open); this PR only makes the existing patch do what its gate says.
- `gemma4_unified_text` is not on the allowlist and does not need to be: `RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-NVFP4` carries no shared entries.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for `validate_rope`, `nested rope`, `rope_parameters validation`, `_install_hf_config_validator`, `_PATCH_HF_NESTED_ROPE_VALIDATION`, `__class_validators__`, and open and closed issues for `validate_rope`, `nested rope_parameters`, `rope_parameters layer_types AttributeError`. #51268 changes RoPE hashing in `rotary_embedding/__init__.py`; #56742 is Qwen4Exp's own config parsing. #57188 (closed) is the flat-map variant of this leakage, fixed by #57189. Nothing covers the nested case for non-allowlisted model types.

## AI assistance

Claude Code assisted me with this. I chose the target, set the workflow and the evidence bar (reproduce on a real host before touching code, a test that fails first, every claim in this description backed by a run), directed each step and reviewed the code, the tests and the evidence before anything was posted. The tracing, the fix and tests, the runs listed above and the first draft of this description were done with it under that direction.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Auto-enable fp32 weights for the gfx950 router GEMM in GateLinear
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55351. The gfx950 low-M FP32 router GEMM added in #54845 never runs: `GateLinear` call sites (deepseek_v2, glm5next, deepseek_v4 nvidia/amd/cpu/xpu) pass the router dtype as `out_dtype` only, so the gate weight stays in the model dtype (bf16) and `allow_fp32_router_gemm` — which requires `self.weight.dtype == torch.float32` — is never true. The kernel is unreachable for the exact shapes it was instantiated for, e.g. DeepSeek-family `(6144, 256)`.

## Approach

Rather than updating every call site to pass `force_fp32_compute` (only nemotron_h does today), self-enable inside `GateLinear`: when `is_gfx950 and (input_size, output_size) in ROCM_FP32_ROUTER_GEMM_SUPPORTED_SHAPES and not bias`, set `force_fp32_compute = True` so the existing logic stores fp32 weights. One-site fix; the eligibility flags then light up through the normal path.

## What does NOT change

- CUDA paths (Hopper/Blackwell specialized kernels, bf16×bf16→fp32 epilogue): `is_gfx950` is false, guard inert.
- Unsupported shapes on gfx950 (e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash's `(4096, 288)`): `is_rocm_fp32_shape` false, clean fallback.
- Biased gates: guard excludes bias (kernel/torch.mm path has no bias term).

## Verification

No GPU locally, so verified by simulation of the exact decision tree in `GateLinear.__init__`:

| Case | weights | fp32 kernel |
|---|---|---|
| gfx950, (6144, 256), no bias (issue repro) | fp32 | **enabled** (was: unreachable) |
| gfx950, (4096, 288) (GLM-5.3-Flash) | bf16 | unchanged fallback |
| CUDA H100, (6144, 256) | bf16 | unchanged |
| gfx950, biased gate | bf16 | unchanged |

`tests/kernels/test_gate_linear_rocm_dispatch.py` covers these flags with mocked platforms but requires a CUDA-built torch to instantiate `nn.Linear`; happy to run it on a gfx950 box if CI doesn't pick it up.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Stack DSpark context KV projections
body:
## Purpose

On DeepSeek-V4.1, the DSpark drafter's `precompute_and_store_context_kv` projects the same context hidden states once per draft layer through each layer's fused `wq_a|wkv` projection and discards the Q half every time — 3 activation quantizations + 3 Q+KV GEMMs per step, with ~70% of the GEMM output columns (the Q half) dead. This eager path sits on the bs=1 spec-decode host critical path: a torch-profiler trace shows ~352 µs of host time per `vllm::mm_mxfp8` wrapper call for ~8.5 µs of GPU work.

## Change

Stack the draft layers' KV projections into one existing `MergedColumnParallelLinear` (+32/−6 in `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/dspark.py`):

- Each checkpoint `mtp.*.attn.wkv.{weight,scale}` now additionally loads into the corresponding shard of `model.context_wkv_proj`; the per-layer `fused_wqa_wkv` still receives its own copy because the draft layers' attention forward continues to use it.
- The step does one activation quantization + one KV-only GEMM over the stacked weight, then per-layer norm / RoPE / cache insert are unchanged.
- No new kernel and no private ABI: it reuses the existing FlashInfer cute-dsl MXFP8 backend and the merged-linear loader.

Trade-off: the stacked replica adds ~7.73 MiB per TP rank (K=5120, 3×512 KV rows, native MXFP8). Configs whose checkpoint scale layout is not 128-row-concatenable, or checkpoints with more draft layers than shards, fail loudly at load time in the merged-linear weight loader, not silently.

Not a duplicate: #54674 (merged) did the same restructuring for V4 (`deepseek_v4`); this PR is the V4.1/MXFP8 port, which #55654 explicitly does not cover (V4-only, and it changes insert/norm rather than the projection). Dup checks on 2026-09-18: `context_wkv_proj` (0 open PRs), `KV-only`, `dspark context`, `deepseek v4.1 projection` — nothing else covers the V4.1 context projection. Independent of #57122 and of the input-prep fusion work.

## Test Plan

GB200, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/dspark.py tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/dspark.py
```

## Test Result

- `tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py`: **28 passed**. Test diff is kept small (+20/−6): the existing scale test additionally asserts that `mtp.*.attn.wkv.scale` lands in both `context_wkv_proj` (shard = draft layer) and `fused_wqa_wkv`, and the existing stacked-projection test is parametrized over V4 and V4.1.
- pre-commit including mypy: passed; `git diff --check` clean.
- Bit-exactness: eager and CUDA-graph-replay outputs of the stacked projection match the original three-projection reference exactly (`max_abs=0`) for M = 1/6/32/512/8192, using native V4.1 MXFP8 with the real 32×32 checkpoint-scale expansion, the real merged-linear loader, and post-load processing; ModelOpt per-row scales checked on the same shapes.

Microbenchmark (same GB200, no profiler, medians; projection only — no norm/insert/serving E2E), before → after:

| M (tokens) | CPU submit (µs) | GPU, CUPTI + graph, cold L2 (µs) |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | 600 → 209 | 25.0 → 9.1 |
| 6 | 608 → 208 | 25.1 → 9.2 |
| 32 | 612 → 207 | 26.9 → 9.9 |
| 512 | 594 → 200 | 43.4 → 15.4 |
| 8192 | 599 → 203 | 247.1 → 81.1 |

Not yet run: full-model quality/acceptance eval and serving E2E; happy to add those numbers if reviewers want them before merge.

title: [Perf][MRV2] Fuse per-request input preparation into one Triton kernel
body:
## Purpose

`prepare_inputs()` launches three per-request Triton kernels over the same `idx_mapping` / `query_start_loc`, each with its own Python argument preparation:

- `_prepare_pos_seq_lens_kernel` — positions and `seq_lens`
- `_combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens_kernel` — last sampled and draft ids into `input_ids`, plus `logits_indices`
- `_expand_idx_mapping_kernel` — the per-logit request mapping, when drafts are scheduled

They are not independent: `combine` re-loads from global memory the `seq_lens` that `prepare_pos` has just written, and `expand` walks the same `cu_num_logits` that `combine` walks. On a bs=1 DeepSeek-V4.1 spec-decode step the host is the critical path — a torch-profiler trace of that path shows input prep running ~2.5 ms of wall time per round for ~15 µs of GPU work — so the per-launch cost matters more than the arithmetic.

## Change

Fold the three into one `_prepare_decode_inputs_kernel` with one program per request (+85/−128 in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/input_batch.py` and `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`, net −43 lines):

- One program computes `seq_len` once and keeps it in a register instead of storing it and having the next kernel reload it, then writes positions, `seq_lens`, the sampled/draft ids, `logits_indices` and — under a `constexpr` flag — the expanded mapping.
- The last program still pads unused `seq_lens` to 0 for full CUDA graphs, exactly as `_prepare_pos_seq_lens_kernel` did.
- `prepare_decode_inputs()` returns `(logits_indices, expanded_idx_mapping, expanded_local_pos)`, the last two `None` when no drafts are scheduled, so `prepare_inputs` drops its separate `expand_idx_mapping` branch.
- Same allocations as before (`logits_indices` plus the two expanded tensors); only launches and Python dispatch are removed. Per-request semantics, grid shape and buffer addresses are unchanged, so CUDA-graph replay is unaffected.

Dup checks: searched open PRs for `prepare_inputs fuse`, `combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens`, `expand_idx_mapping`, `prepare_pos_seq_lens`, `MRV2 input preparation`, `input_batch triton kernel fuse` — none touch these kernels. Related but distinct: #42131 (decode fast path in the *v1* scheduler and `gpu_model_runner.py`), #57102 (metadata mapping shared across KV groups, a different call site).

## Test Plan

GB200, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch_v2.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/input_batch.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch_v2.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual \
  --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/input_batch.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py
git diff --check
```

## Test Result

- 24 passed and 105 passed; pre-commit, `mypy-3.12` and `git diff --check` clean.
- New `test_prepare_decode_inputs_matches_per_request_reference[bonus-only | bonus-plus-drafts | drafts-only]` checks positions, `seq_lens`, `input_ids`, `logits_indices` and the expanded mapping against a per-request reference. The batch includes a request still in prefill, whose ids must survive untouched, and a request with more query rows than logit rows, which exercises the `end - num_logits` placement.
- Kernel launches per step: **3 → 1** with drafts, 2 → 1 without.

### Input-prep benchmark

The benchmark calls the real functions through the same entry points `prepare_inputs` uses, with the DSpark decode shape: `num_speculative_tokens=5`, so six query rows and six logit rows per request, context 4,096. Baseline and candidate run from the same script against two checkouts.

Measured quantity is **host wall time per call** (Python plus kernel submission, no synchronisation inside the loop; allocation of the persistent inputs and Triton compilation excluded): 20 warmup calls, then 200 timed calls per round, 3 rounds, medians below. GPU time is CUPTI with CUDA-graph replay and cold L2 — without the graph the per-iteration CUPTI span is dominated by the launch gaps this PR removes and merely restates the host column. GPU clocks not locked.

| Batch | Host before (µs) | Host after (µs) | Reduction | GPU before (µs) | GPU after (µs) | Reduction |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 72.5 | 40.2 | 44.6% | 6.3 | 3.9 | 38.1% |
| 32 | 63.5 | 36.5 | 42.5% | 6.7 | 3.6 | 46.3% |
| 128 | 61.8 | 36.3 | 41.3% | 6.7 | 4.1 | 38.8% |
| 256 | 62.1 | 36.5 | 41.2% | 6.8 | 4.1 | 39.7% |

The saving is flat in batch size because what is removed is per-launch submission cost, not per-token work — which is the regime that hurts, since bs=1 decode is where the host is the critical path. In absolute terms this is ~30 µs of a ~20 ms bs=1 round, so the main value of the change is the 43 fewer lines and one kernel instead of three; the latency is a bonus.

title: [Perf][MRV2] Upload cu_num_logits and query_start_loc in one H2D copy
body:
## Purpose

`prepare_inputs()` builds two per-request prefix sums every step, `cu_num_logits` and `query_start_loc`, and moves each to the device on its own: a fresh `np.empty`, a fresh pinned staging tensor, a CPU copy and a `cudaMemcpyAsync` for each, plus a `torch.arange` kernel for `cu_num_logits` on the common no-draft path. They are the same shape (`[num_reqs + 1]`, int32), computed a few lines apart, and consumed together. On a bs=1 spec-decode step, where the host is the critical path, that is two device round-trips for what is one small table.

## Change

Keep both prefix sums in one persistent `[2, max_num_reqs + 1]` int32 buffer with a matching NumPy staging array, upload it once, and hand out views (+11/−9 in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/input_batch.py` and `model_runner.py`):

- `InputBuffers.batch_cumsums` holds the two rows; `InputBuffers.query_start_loc` is now an alias of row 1, so its address — which FULL graphs capture — and every existing reference to it (`make_dummy`, `pcp_manager.py`, `model_runner.py:646`) are unchanged.
- The two cumsums are written straight into the staging rows; one `async_tensor_h2d(out=)` replaces the two uploads and the `torch.arange`.
- Pinned staging still goes through `async_tensor_h2d`, so the caching host allocator keeps managing its lifetime; no persistent pinned buffer is introduced and nothing changes for #54269's `prepare_inputs_event` protocol.
- Adaptive verification still replaces both values via `reallocate_drafts` afterwards; that path is unchanged.

### Supersedes #35561 on these two buffers

#35561 targets the same two uploads through a `CpuGpuBuffer` with a persistent pinned mirror per buffer and an `arange_gpu` slice for the no-draft case. It has had no update since 2026-02-28, its body is a single line, GitHub reports it as not mergeable, and it patches `prepare_inputs` at line ~643 of a file where the function now starts at ~1287. The two approaches differ:

| | #35561 | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| mechanism | persistent pinned CPU mirror per buffer | one device buffer, one upload, views |
| memcpy per step | 2 | 1 |
| pinned allocations per step | 0 | 1 (via `async_tensor_h2d`, allocator-managed) |
| no-draft `cu_num_logits` | persistent `arange_gpu` slice | same single upload |
| new abstractions | `CpuGpuBuffer` in `buffer_utils.py` | none |
| diff | new class + several runner sites | +11/−9 |

The two are complementary rather than exclusive — a persistent pinned `[2, N]` mirror on top of this layout would remove the remaining allocation — but that reintroduces the reused-pinned-buffer race #54269 is fixing, so this PR deliberately stops at one upload. If #35561 is revived, this reduces to a rebase onto its buffer type.

Dup checks: searched open PRs for `query_start_loc h2d`, `cu_num_logits`, `async_tensor_h2d prepare_inputs`, `prepare_inputs pinned staging`, `InputBuffers query_start_loc`, `MRV2 host overhead h2d`. Besides #35561: #54269 (event guard for pinned reuse under async scheduling; touches `__init__`/`execute_model`, disjoint lines), #57628 (fuses the per-request kernels a few lines below; disjoint hunks, whichever merges second rebases trivially).

## Test Plan

GB200, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch_v2.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/input_batch.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/input_batch.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py
git diff --check
```

## Test Result

- 126 passed. `test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py` and `test_gpu_pcp_manager.py` drive the real `prepare_inputs`, so the `query_start_loc` alias is exercised end to end, not only by inspection; pre-commit, `mypy-3.12` and `git diff --check` clean.
- No new test: the change adds no behaviour, it removes a copy. Equality of both outputs against the previous code is asserted inside the benchmark before timing.
- Device ops per step for these two buffers: **2 → 1** (draft path: two memcpys → one; no-draft path: memcpy + `arange` kernel → one memcpy).

### Prefix-sum upload benchmark

Both arms mirror the diff hunks line for line and call the production `async_tensor_h2d`; the untouched `idx_mapping` upload, allocation of the persistent buffers and compilation are outside the timed region. `max_num_reqs=256`, 6 query tokens per request. Host is submit-only wall time per step, 20 warmup then 200 timed calls, median of 3 runs; GPU is summed device-op time per step from `torch.profiler` (memcpy + kernels, no launch gaps).

| path | BS | host before (µs) | host after (µs) | saved | GPU before → after (µs) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| with drafts (spec-decode verify step) | 1 | 111.7 | 68.9 | 42.8 (38%) | 1.73 → 0.86 |
| | 32 | 111.1 | 70.3 | 40.8 (37%) | 1.61 → 1.00 |
| | 128 | 132.9 | 77.8 | 55.1 (41%) | 1.61 → 1.01 |
| | 256 | 116.0 | 67.8 | 48.2 (42%) | 1.63 → 1.00 |
| no drafts (plain decode) | 1 | 72.5 | 52.2 | 20.3 (28%) | 2.00 → 0.85 |
| | 32 | 92.3 | 69.6 | 22.7 (25%) | 2.06 → 1.01 |
| | 128 | 90.7 | 67.6 | 23.1 (25%) | 1.97 → 0.85 |
| | 256 | 91.5 | 65.3 | 26.2 (29%) | 2.12 → 1.01 |

The saving is flat in batch size because what is removed is a fixed number of host calls, not bytes. In absolute terms this is ~40 µs of a ~20 ms bs=1 DSpark round; the point is that it is a net two-line change that deletes a copy and a kernel launch, not a latency headline. Not measured: end-to-end TPOT.

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3][Perf] Fuse MLA decode KV-cache write and Q-prep via AITER
body:
## Purpose

On ROCm, Kimi-K3 MLA decode runs the per-layer query preparation and the KV-cache
write as separate launches:

1. `vllm::concat_and_cache_mla_kernel` — the fp8 KV-cache write
2. `triton_poi_fused__to_copy_cat_clamp_mul_reciprocal_view_0` — the
   `[ql_nope | q_pe]` concat and that query's static fp8 quant

This collapses both into a single AITER `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla`
launch: **288 → 144 kernel launches and 1351.8 → 682.8 µs (1.98×) per rank over
6 decode steps**, i.e. **9.39 → 4.74 µs per MLA layer per decode step** on
MI355X at TP=8.

Kimi-K3 MLA is NoPE (`mla_use_nope`), while that kernel always applies RoPE and
takes the cos/sin caches as required arguments. It is fed an **identity rotation**
(`cos = 1, sin = 0`) so the rotation degenerates to a no-op — the same approach
ROCm/ATOM uses to route K3 through this kernel.

The identity cache is a **single row**. AITER's per-head and `_opt` decode kernels
clamp `pos` into `[0, cos_cache.size(0))` before indexing, so real positions pass
straight through; a full-length constant cache would otherwise cost ~268 MB at
K3's `max_position_embeddings` of 1 048 576 to express a provable no-op. AITER's
*general* decode kernel does **not** clamp, so the layer refuses
the head counts that would select it (`kv_lora_rank * num_heads < 2048`, i.e.
≤3 heads/rank, reachable at TP=32).

## Scope, and why this is small

This is a **kernel-count / device-time optimization on the MLA decode path**. The
two replaced kernels are a sub-1% slice of a decode step, on 24 MLA layers in a
model that is roughly 1:3 MLA:KDA. End-to-end serving throughput improvement is below 1%

## Relationship to #47757 and #57452

**This supersedes #57452**, which I opened for the same optimization and will
close in favor of this one. That PR stacked on #47757: it carried #47757's six
commits so CI could run, and extended its hook in the shared
`MLAAttention.forward_impl`, also touching
`vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py`. Two problems with that shape:

- it could not merge until #47757 did, and it is still under review
- it modified shared MLA code, so every MLA model and backend was in the blast
  radius of a Kimi-K3-only optimization

This PR drops both. It touches **no shared code at all** — only
`vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/` — mirroring the vendor-local q/kv RMSNorm fusion that
the same wrapper already owns (#52494, merged). Consequences:

- no dependency on #47757, so CI runs standalone and this can merge in any order
- zero blast radius: no other model, backend or platform can be affected
- it is a **single file** — the AITER call lives directly in the K3 wrapper

#47757 remains complementary: it fuses the **sparse** MLA path (deepseek_v32)
through the shared hook, while this fuses the **dense** Kimi-K3 path inside the
vendor wrapper. Different call sites, no conflict in either merge order.

**Updated after review** (thanks @Rohan138) — the fused call is no longer a
registered custom op, the `torch.compiler.is_compiling()` guard is gone, and the
branch now lives directly in `forward()` instead of a helper returning `None`.
That folded the separate ops module away, so this is now one file. All numbers
below were re-measured on the refactored code.

On `is_compiling()`: the baseline's `triton_poi_fused…` kernel comes from
`mla_decode_concat_quant_fp8` compiling its own `forward_native` (class docstring
at `mla_attention.py:1541`), not from the model being compiled — Kimi-K3 is not
`@support_torch_compile`. The guard was dead code.

### Why not a duplicate

- **#47757** — same kernel, sparse MLA on deepseek_v32; this is the dense K3 path
  and the NoPE handling is new.
- **#55230** — same kernel family, DeepSeek-R1, edits shared `layers/mla.py`.
- **#45798 / #38313 / #41099 / #41101** — the same fusion as a torch.compile
  graph-rewrite pass. Kimi-K3 is not `@support_torch_compile`, so those never fire.
- **#53166** — K3 ROCm MLA, but chunked-context *gather*, a different op.
- **#52494** (merged) — the sibling q/kv RMSNorm fusion in this same wrapper.

## Implementation

One file, `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/mla.py`, on the existing K3 wrapper:

- **`_fused_qk_prep_supported()`** resolves everything fixed at load time —
  platform, KV-cache dtype, shapes, DCP/PCP/HiSparse, head padding, and which
  `W_UK` variant is live. Evaluated once in `__init__`.
- **`_fused_decode()`** mirrors `MLAAttention.forward_impl`'s `W_UK` dispatch
  *including its precedence* (fp4 before fp8; both flags can be set at once) so
  `ql_nope` is bit-identical to what the unfused path feeds its concat+quant,
  then issues the fused call and continues through `impl.forward_mqa` and
  `_v_up_proj`.

With the static gating hoisted into `__init__`, the only per-batch condition left
in `forward()` is that the batch is **decode-only**. Everything else takes the
stock `MLAAttention` path, unchanged:

- any batch that is not purely decode (the fused call covers only the MQA slice,
  so a mixed batch's prefill rows would never reach the KV cache)
- **DCP** (the kernel skips `slot < 0` rows, which would then be garbage after the
  query all-gather), **PCP** and **HiSparse** (both rewrite the KV inputs/slots
  before the standalone write, which this path bypasses)
- the fp8-bmm and AMX `W_UK` variants, and any `q_pad_num_heads` head padding
- profile/dummy runs, an unallocated KV cache, or a missing slot mapping
- non-ROCm, non-fp8 KV cache, or head counts that would select AITER's
  non-clamping general decode kernel

## Test Plan

All numbers below are from the **stock upstream nightly**
`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-0bfc7a15d095fe83ecc82b50561a93c177fece2d`
(2026-09-16), 8× MI355X, Kimi-K3 fp4, TP=8, with **no benchmark harness and no
vendor patches** — plain `vllm serve` + `vllm bench serve`:

### Server (identical for both arms)

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1

vllm serve $MODEL \
  --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --load-format fastsafetensors \
  --language-model-only \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8010
```

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` is the only environment variable set.

### Perf

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --tokenizer $MODEL --trust-remote-code \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8010 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 8192 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts $CONC --max-concurrency $CONC \
  --seed 42 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```

### Kernel census

Add `--profiler-config` to the same serve command, then bracket a decode phase:

```bash
# appended to the serve command above
--profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch","torch_profiler_dir":"/out/traces",
                    "torch_profiler_use_gzip":true,"ignore_frontend":true,
                    "delay_iterations":0,"max_iterations":6}'

# with a bench in flight and past prefill:
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8010/start_profile
sleep 15
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8010/stop_profile
```

### Accuracy

```bash
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template \
  --tasks gsm8k --output_path out --log_samples \
  --model_args model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8010/v1/chat/completions,\
api_key=EMPTY,eos_string='</s>',num_concurrent=32,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=32768 \
  --gen_kwargs max_tokens=4096,temperature=0,top_p=1
```

## Results

### 1. Decode kernel census — two kernels become one

Rank-0 torch profile, 6 engine steps, 24 MLA layers, `144 = 24 × 6`:

| kernel | baseline | fused |
|---|---:|---:|
| `vllm::concat_and_cache_mla_kernel` | 144 (668.0 µs) | **0** |
| `triton_poi_fused__to_copy_cat_clamp_mul_reciprocal_view_0` | 144 (683.8 µs) | **0** |
| `aiter::fuse_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla_kernel` | 0 | **144** (682.8 µs) |

**288 → 144 launches, 1351.8 → 682.8 µs = 1.98×.**
Per MLA layer per decode step: **9.39 → 4.74 µs**.

Dispatch lands on AITER's `_opt` decode kernel rather than `per_head` —
`per_head` requires `kv_cache.size(1) == 1` and vLLM derives 1536 here. The `_opt`
gate is `kv_lora_rank × num_heads ≥ 2048`; at TP=8 that is 512 × 12 = 6144.
`_opt` is also the position-clamping kernel the single-row identity cache needs.

### 2. GSM8K — no accuracy regression

Full 1319 questions, 5-shot, `temperature=0, top_p=1`, `max_tokens=4096`,
chat template applied:

| arm | strict-match | flexible-extract | stderr |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| fused | **0.9545** | 0.9553 | 0.0057 |

### 3. E2E serving — unchanged within noise

ISL 1024 / OSL 8192 C=1|8|32 one repeat showed TPOT p50 (ms), ITL p50 (ms), ITL p90 (ms), out tok/s for Conc 1 and 8 are flat to within 0.2%. Conc 32 moves ~0.7% in the baseline's favor, having moved ~1% the other way before the refactor — same essential code, opposite sign, so nothing is claimed in either direction.

This is the expected outcome. The fusion removes a sub-1% slice of a decode
step's device time; for scale, `cross_device_reduce_2stage` alone is ~46% of
rank-0 decode device time in the same trace.

title: [CI Failure]: MI250 Multimodal Processor - test_common.py::test_processing_correctness[DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash]
body:
### Name of failing test

MI250 Multimodal Processor shards 3 and 5:

```text
tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py::test_processing_correctness[1.0-32-0.3-deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash]
tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py::test_processing_correctness[1.0-32-0.5-deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash]
tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py::test_processing_correctness[1.0-32-1.0-deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash]
```

### Basic information

- [ ] Flaky test
- [x] Can reproduce locally
- [ ] Caused by external libraries

### Describe the failure

DeepSeek V4.1 fails to import when Triton is unavailable. The MI250 processor jobs now use the native CPU path, which hits this error before the tests can process any input.

This also fails on main. [Build #89918](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89918) tests `62af3df7347cf890b4b925a18ab6a2afd00c70b9`; [shard 3](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89918#01a0b695-859c-4086-b72b-c3f89e0dc9bc) and [shard 5](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89918#01a0b692-cdc3-4f50-b1f9-f97ecb7d3513) both fail. I also hit it in #57487.

The import reaches `sparse_mqa_logits.py`, which calls `tl.constexpr` at module scope. Without Triton, vLLM uses a placeholder where `constexpr` is `None`:

```text
File "vllm/models/deepseek_v41/attention.py", line 27, in <module>
  from vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_mqa_indexer import SparseMQAIndexer
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_mqa_indexer.py", line 20, in <module>
  from vllm.model_executor.kernels.attention.dsa.sparse_mqa_logits import (
File "vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/sparse_mqa_logits.py", line 73, in <module>
  _INT32_BIG = tl.constexpr(2**31 - 1)
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not callable
```

I reproduced the same error on main at `038cb14bd7874030e98bb6edc4b6f4efe649fff7`, in a Linux arm64 CPU container without Triton:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=/tmp/deepseek-processor-before \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py \
  -k 'DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash' -v --tb=short
```

All three cases fail. The container uses Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu and Transformers 5.16.1, with vLLM v0.29.0 CPU native libraries and the main branch's Python source. No model weights are needed for this test.

### History

The same import error was [reported in #56254](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56254#issuecomment-5644796189). After #56162 changed the MI250 jobs to the native path, shards 3 and 5 failed in main builds [#89914](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89914), [#89918](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89918) and [#89941](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89941). I checked the traceback in #89918 against the local failure.

I proposed a fix in #57654. It makes the Triton placeholder's `constexpr` return its input and updates the existing fallback tests.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Reuse decode topk global indices across consumer layers
body:
## Purpose

On DeepSeek-V4.1, every compressed attention layer maps its index source's local top-k indices to global KV-cache slots on its own (`compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens`), although the indices and the block table are shared by every layer below the same index source. DSv4.1-Flash has 38 compressed layers reading 8 index sources, so one decode step launches the kernel 38 times for 8 distinct results — inside the target CUDA graph, ~2.2 µs of GPU time each (launch-bound, a few GB/s at decode shapes). A torch-profiler trace of bs=1 DSpark decode on 4×GB200 (TP4) shows 38× `_compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens_kernel` per step, 84 µs of GPU timeline.

## Change

Build the mapping once per (index source, compress ratio) and let the layers below read through (+53/−45 in `vllm/`, no kernel change):

- `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadata` gains `decode_global_topk_cache`, cleared alongside the existing per-step FlashInfer cache in `update_draft_decode_metadata`.
- `DeepseekV4Attention._decode_global_topk` fills that cache; the FlashMLA, mega-attention and FlashInfer SM120 decode paths call it instead of the kernel.
- The SM100 FlashInfer mixed sparse indices, already cached for SWA-only layers, now cache compressed layers under `c{ratio}a:{index source}` — the same shape the DSv4 backend uses (`swa_only` / `c128a`).
- Output-neutral by construction: consumers receive the very tensors the first layer of the step built.

Not a duplicate: #57434 does this for the ROCm backend only (`deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py`, ragged form) and leaves the NVIDIA paths untouched; #49678 is the same idea for GLM-5.2 in `v1/attention/backends/mla`; #41105 (draft) fuses the mapping into the DSv4 top-k kernel and keeps the per-layer recompute. Dup checks on 2026-09-19: `topk metadata across layers`, `reuse global topk indices`, `compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens`, `57434 in:body`. Orthogonal to #55744 / #55692 (kernel bounds fixes in `deepseek_v4/`).

## Test Plan

GB200, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_swa.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/attention.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashmla.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flash_mla_mega_attn.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <same files>
```

## Test Result

- `test_flashmla_sparse.py` + `test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py`: **44 passed, 8 skipped**.
- pre-commit including mypy: passed.

Microbenchmark (same GB200, FlashInfer CUPTI, CUDA graph, cold L2, `index_topk=512`, block_size 64, medians; kernel only): one launch, and a step's 38 launches (before) vs 8 (after):

| Tokens | 1 launch (µs) | Per step, 38× → 8× (µs) |
|-------:|--------------:|--------------------------:|
| 1 | 2.18 | 68.0 → 15.6 |
| 6 (bs=1 DSpark) | 2.14 | 69.4 → 14.1 |
| 96 | 2.50 | 73.2 → 15.3 |
| 1536 | 3.87 | 116.4 → 25.1 |
| 8192 (prefill-sized) | 12.26 | 323.7 → 71.3 |

title: [Bug]: NIXL P/D disagg silently corrupts output when hybrid-attention layers share a storage base with different block lengths (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash)
body:
### Summary

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash served via NIXL PD disaggregation (2P×TP8 + 2D×TP8, 2×H200 nodes, RDMA) produces garbled output (nonsensical characters, or empty content/reasoning fields) with no errors or crashes — silent data corruption. The same image serves a single-full-attention model (GLM-5.3) correctly in the same topology. Mooncake, CUDA graphs, and MultiConnector were ruled out.

### Root cause

In `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py`, region registration deduplicates transfer regions by `base_addr` alone, and the collapsed branch only refreshes `block_len/stride/num_blocks` when `is_mla_region` is true.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's `layers.2.attn.compressor.state_cache` (`CircularBufferSpec`, needs block_len=32768) shares its storage base address with `layers.0.attn.swa_cache` (MLA, block_len=19008). It folds into region 0 without updating block_len, so its compressor state is transferred with only 19008 bytes per block and offsets computed from the swa view — truncated and misaligned. `layers.2.attn.indexer.k_cache` hits a second instance of the same base-address conflict.

Diagnostic signature: the affected region simultaneously shows `rgid=-1` (shared), `scratch=True`, and `is_mla=True` — three mutually contradictory attributes. After the fix, `num_regions` grows 12 → 14.

### Fix

Deduplicate by `(base_addr, block_len)`: regions with distinct transfer geometry stay separate; identical-geometry aliases still fold as before. A PR follows.

### Verification

- Cluster (2×8 H200, P/D disagg): before the fix — all-garbled short completions, 200-token generations fully corrupted, Chinese chat returns empty content/reasoning; after the fix — normal English/Chinese output, 0% garble rate over 200-token generations, clean output across 6 concurrent streams.
- Unit tests: new regression test fails on HEAD and passes with the fix; the existing NIXL unit test failure set is byte-identical before/after (no regressions).

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Dedup transfer regions by (base_addr, block_len)
body:
Fixes #57661

- **Root cause**: NIXL region registration deduped transfer regions by `base_addr` alone, and the collapsed branch only refreshed block geometry for MLA regions. In hybrid-attention models, a layer with a different block length aliasing another layer's base address (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash compressor `state_cache` / indexer `k_cache` overlaid on `swa_cache`) was silently folded and inherited the first region's block length. PD transfers of its state were truncated and misaligned, producing garbled output with no errors.
- **Fix**: dedup key is now `(base_addr, block_len)`. Identical-geometry aliases still fold (`test_overlaid_transfer_groups_share_region_geometry` continues to pass, confirming the lossless path is unchanged).
- **Behavior change (maintainer sanity-check welcome)**: `test_ring_scratch_without_mamba_registers_and_addresses_its_own_regions` now expects `_scratch_region_indices == [2]` instead of `[1]`. That fixture (introduced in #56214) overlays rings on a paged region whose block_len differs from the rings' page size — the old expectation had recorded the benign form of this very bug (the ring inheriting the paged region's geometry). If overlay folding was intentional design, this one assertion is trivially revertible.
- **Tests**: added `test_shared_base_regions_with_distinct_block_lens_stay_separate` (two geometries at one base address — 256B MLA swa page vs 128B compressor ring page — must register as two regions with their own block lens and descriptor geometry). Verified in a container: target test fails on HEAD / passes with the fix; `test_nixl_connector_hma/push_connector/tp_mapping` failure sets are identical before/after. `ruff check` + `ruff format` pass.

**Why this is not a duplicate**: searched open issues/PRs (nixl region dedup, deepseek pd disagg, base_addr, garbled output); #52627 is Mooncake-specific and #54926 is un-transferred draft KV — different root causes.

**Model evals**: 2×8 H200 cluster, NIXL P/D disagg — before: fully garbled output; after: clean English/Chinese generations, 0% garble rate, 6 concurrent streams clean (details in #57661).

**AI assistance disclosure**: root-cause analysis and this fix were produced with ZCode (local agent); cluster diagnosis, the initial mitigation patch, and remote test runs were done with Chaterm (remote agent). The submitter has reviewed every changed line and performed the end-to-end cluster verification above.

title: [Bugfix][DSA] Avoid runtime JIT for offset candidate end buffers
body:
## Purpose

Mixed prefill batches can pass an offset view of the candidate expansion's `end` buffer after warmup used an aligned pointer. Triton specializes on that alignment and JIT-compiles another kernel during serving.

Disable alignment specialization for `end_ptr`: each program stores one scalar, so alignment does not enable vectorized stores. Extend the existing reference tests to cover both aligned and offset output buffers, including strided outputs and untouched padding. Candidate selection, ordering and bounds are unchanged.

Extracted from #57643 at the author's request; the fix and tests are removed from that PR. This targets `main` independently of the all-reduce/mHC changes. Open-PR searches for `end_ptr`, sparse candidate alignment and sparse-indexer warmup found no other PR addressing this specialization; #57206 changes prefill selector dispatch instead.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py -k candidate -q -rs
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/sparse_mqa_logits.py tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py
```

Standalone GB200 GPU test results: **16 passed, 17 deselected** on commit `325d7bf6ad`. Applicable pre-commit hooks passed.

Earlier real-weight validation used this exact patch together with the separate mHC and FlashInfer warmup fixes: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, TP4, no speculative decoding, FlashInfer FP8 attention and MXFP4 sparse indexer. All 23 requests (3–8192 prompt tokens, mixed batches up to eight requests, 736 generated tokens) completed with `--jit-monitor-mode error` and zero runtime JIT events. This is combined warmup coverage, not an isolated end-to-end performance claim. No additional GSM8K evaluation: kernel arithmetic is unchanged and reference tests check exact candidate outputs.

AI assistance was used for implementation, validation and this description.

title: [Perf][Attention][PCP] Reuse MLA context across PCP virtual rows
body:
## Purpose

PCP represents chunks of the same request as separate virtual rows. During MLA prefill with an existing KV cache, adjacent PCP rows from the same request can independently materialize overlapping historical context.

This PR reuses the shared cached context across eligible PCP virtual rows. For an adjacent two-row same-request layout, the shared historical context is materialized once, while the second row only processes the additional cached tail it needs.

The optimization preserves the original query slices and attention semantics. Unsupported layouts fall back to the existing chunked-context path.

The current optimization is limited to:

* dense causal MLA;
* DCP=1;
* no sliding-window attention;
* at most two adjacent PCP rows for the same request.

The change is complementary to existing MLA context optimizations: it specifically removes duplicated same-layer historical-context preparation introduced by PCP virtual rows.

### Relation to existing work

This PR does not duplicate the closest existing MLA context optimizations:

* #50613 changes how MLA context chunks are scheduled into the workspace to reduce the number of chunks. It does not deduplicate overlapping historical context represented by multiple PCP virtual rows of the same request.
* #53166 fuses the cost of an individual MLA context gather/projection path on ROCm/AITER. This PR instead reduces how many times the same historical context is materialized, and targets the common dense MLA path used by PCP.
* #56986 reuses the same main-KV gather across multiple DeepSeek-V4.1 decoder layers and explicitly excludes PCP. This PR operates within one layer, reusing context across adjacent PCP virtual rows of the same request.

The optimization here is therefore PCP-specific, same-layer reuse across virtual rows, rather than workspace scheduling, per-gather kernel fusion, or cross-layer reuse.

AI assistance was used during implementation and review. All changes and test results were reviewed by the submitter.

## Test Plan

Unit test:

```bash
pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_pcp_context_reuse_mla.py
```

The tests cover:

* shared-context reuse plus an additional cached tail;
* non-page-aligned cached-context gaps;
* mixed decode/prefill batches;
* singleton requests around a PCP pair;
* fallback when DCP > 1.

Performance was evaluated using:

| Setting                   | Value                      |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| Model                     | GLM-4.7-Flash-8E           |
| GPU                       | 2× NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 |
| Weight quantization       | FP8                        |
| KV cache dtype            | FP8                        |
| TP / PP / DP              | 1 / 1 / 1                  |
| PCP / DCP                 | 2 / 1                      |
| `max_num_batched_tokens`  | 16384                      |
| `max_num_seqs`            | 1                          |
| Chunked prefill           | enabled                    |
| Prefix caching            | disabled                   |
| Execution                 | eager                      |
| MLA prefill backend       | FLASH_ATTN                 |
| MLA decode backend        | TRITON_MLA                 |
| Output length             | 1                          |
| Concurrency               | 1                          |
| Requests per input length | 3                          |

Input lengths ranged from 16K to 192K.

The detailed Nsight Systems profiling below was collected on the v0.29.0-based benchmark branch. #54013 was applied identically to both the baseline and optimized configurations because this RTX 5090 + FP8 environment otherwise hits the MLA decode shared-memory issue addressed by that PR. #54013 is independent of this optimization and is not part of this PR.

## Test Result

### Unit test

```text
pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_pcp_context_reuse_mla.py

5 passed in 16.26s
```

### End-to-end performance

At 192K input length, average end-to-end latency over 3 runs decreased from:

```text
58.21 s -> 54.75 s
```

a **5.9% reduction**.

The benefit increases with context length, consistent with eliminating duplicated processing of shared historical context.

### 192K profiler attribution

| GPU work                              | Baseline PCP | Context reuse |     Change |
| ------------------------------------- | -----------: | ------------: | ---------: |
| `gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache_page` |     651.5 ms |      325.7 ms | **-50.0%** |
| `direct_copy` kernel family           |     17.561 s |       9.123 s | **-48.0%** |
| CUTLASS GEMM candidates               |     21.083 s |      12.750 s | **-39.5%** |
| Dynamic FP8 quantization              |      1.266 s |       0.830 s | **-34.4%** |
| FlashAttention variants, combined     |    281.029 s |     277.817 s |  **-1.1%** |
| `concat_and_cache_mla`                |     118.6 ms |      119.3 ms |        ~0% |
| `merge_attn_states`                   |     909.9 ms |      961.4 ms |      +5.7% |
| PCP AllGather + ReduceScatter         |     13.499 s |      13.489 s |        ~0% |

The near-50% reductions in KV gather/dequant and direct-copy work are consistent with eliminating duplicated materialization of shared historical context for the second PCP virtual row.

In contrast, aggregate FlashAttention time, MLA cache concatenation, attention-state merging, and PCP collective time remain approximately unchanged. The measured benefit is therefore concentrated in cached-context preparation rather than the underlying attention computation or communication.

Profiler values are summed CUDA kernel durations. PCP values sum kernel time across both GPUs, so these totals should not be interpreted as wall-clock latency.

The CUTLASS kernels and FlashAttention variants cannot be uniquely mapped to individual MLA operations from this trace because corresponding business-level NVTX ranges are not present. They are therefore reported as kernel families/candidates rather than attributed to a specific projection or attention sub-path.

<details>
<summary>Detailed 16K–192K profiler results</summary>

The value order in the following tables is **baseline PCP / context reuse / single GPU** unless otherwise noted. PCP values sum CUDA kernel durations across two GPUs, while the single-GPU values contain one GPU only. They are included for profiling context and should not be interpreted as direct wall-clock comparisons.

### Overall GPU kernel breakdown

GPU kernel total and Flash totals are in seconds; CUTLASS candidates are in milliseconds.

| Input length |        GPU kernel total (s) |             Flash total (s) |       CUTLASS candidates (ms) |
| -----------: | --------------------------: | --------------------------: | ----------------------------: |
|          16K |       4.197 / 4.088 / 3.040 |       1.899 / 1.910 / 1.879 |         466.0 / 422.2 / 360.0 |
|          32K |    12.657 / 12.214 / 10.019 |       7.514 / 7.587 / 7.523 |       1,159.7 / 958.5 / 783.1 |
|          64K |    42.778 / 40.852 / 35.713 |    30.302 / 30.408 / 30.160 |   3,246.4 / 2,377.0 / 1,812.2 |
|          96K |    91.068 / 86.515 / 77.429 |    69.213 / 68.945 / 68.241 |   6,288.4 / 4,281.6 / 3,089.2 |
|         128K | 157.580 / 149.108 / 134.969 | 123.945 / 123.190 / 121.619 |  10,284.7 / 6,654.9 / 4,593.3 |

### FlashAttention kernel variants

The two variants are distinguished by a boolean parameter in the kernel template signature. The available trace does not establish that either variant uniquely corresponds to historical-context attention or current/suffix attention.

| Input length |              Flash variant A (ms) |          Flash variant B (ms) |
| -----------: | --------------------------------: | ----------------------------: |

|         192K | 274,735.6 / 265,782.6 / 250,839.4 | 6,293.5 / 12,034.2 / 23,241.8 |

At 192K, variant A decreases by 3.3% while variant B increases substantially, but their combined time changes only from 281.029s to 277.817s (-1.1%). The trace therefore supports a change in FlashAttention kernel-shape/variant distribution, while aggregate FlashAttention work remains nearly unchanged.

### Historical-context preparation and cache kernels

All values are milliseconds.

| Input length |         `direct_copy` family | `concat_and_cache_mla` | gather + maybe-dequant |       Dynamic FP8 quant |
| -----------: | ---------------------------: | ---------------------: | ---------------------: | ----------------------: |
|          16K |         153.8 / 103.8 / 77.7 |        9.8 / 9.9 / 6.0 |          2.2 / 1.7 / 0 |      38.0 / 36.3 / 45.8 |
|          32K |        546.9 / 328.8 / 214.3 |     19.7 / 19.8 / 12.1 |        9.0 / 6.1 / 1.5 |      85.6 / 77.9 / 94.2 |
|          64K |    2,045.0 / 1,137.9 / 667.4 |     39.4 / 39.6 / 24.4 |      55.4 / 25.4 / 9.2 |   220.5 / 175.8 / 198.4 |
|          96K |  4,496.7 / 2,419.1 / 1,357.7 |     59.2 / 59.5 / 36.7 |    144.5 / 66.5 / 27.7 |   406.9 / 304.8 / 318.3 |

`gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache_page` includes FP8 dequantization as part of that kernel. The dynamic FP8 quantization column is a separate quantization path and is therefore reported separately rather than included in the gather/dequant number.

The strongest scaling signal appears in the historical-context preparation path: at 192K, gather/dequant decreases by 50.0% and the `direct_copy` family decreases by 48.0%, while `concat_and_cache_mla` remains essentially unchanged.

### Attention-state merge and related elementwise work

All values are milliseconds.

| Input length |       Elementwise candidates |   `merge_attn_states` |             KV gather |
| -----------: | ---------------------------: | --------------------: | --------------------: |
|          16K |          142.7 / 93.7 / 58.7 |     36.7 / 40.8 / 0.0 |       2.2 / 1.7 / 0.0 |

|          64K |    1,999.9 / 1,097.1 / 591.3 | 183.6 / 176.6 / 121.8 |     55.4 / 25.4 / 9.2 |

Single-GPU runs do not contain the PCP AllGather/ReduceScatter path, so these columns contain only **baseline PCP / context reuse**.

| Input length |    AllGather (ms) | ReduceScatter (ms) |
| -----------: | ----------------: | -----------------: |

```text
13.499 s -> 13.489 s
```

This provides a negative control for the optimization: the measured end-to-end improvement is not explained by reduced PCP communication.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Add SM90 native-head sparse attention backend
body:
## Overview

Rework this as an opt-in SM90 backend with centralized selection and separate Triton prefill/decode, as requested in review. DeepSeek V4.1 TP8/TP4 keeps its 8/16 local query heads instead of padding to 64.

## Claims

- Select with `--attention-backend TRITON_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41`; default backend selection is unchanged.
- Eligible verification-query pairs share sparse KV reads. Other decode shapes use the direct Triton decoder.
- H20×8/TP8 output throughput improves 5.4–8.7% in the measured workloads, with lower p95 TTFT and end-to-end latency.

## Validation

Same image and flags, changing only the attention backend. Source and native libraries built from `0c16eee3`; DSpark adaptive/5, Humming 0.1.16/BF16, batch 8192, max 64 sequences, `fp8_ds_mla` and fixed KV budget 22,191,197,696 bytes/GPU.

EvalScope 1.11.1 with a reasoning-field timing fix: 200 streaming requests per point, identical frozen prompts, isolated prefixes, 1024 output tokens with EOS ignored. All requests succeeded; no timed compilation, cache hits or preemptions observed in the included samples.

| Input / concurrency | Output tok/s, FlashMLA → Triton | Change | p95 TTFT | p95 E2E |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8K / 64 | 1372.8 → 1446.3 | +5.4% | −7.5% | −8.1% |
| 32K / 8 | 399.4 → 434.2 | +8.7% | −8.1% | −10.0% |
| 32K / 32 | 487.4 → 526.9 | +8.1% | −8.7% | −10.8% |
| 32K / 32, repeat | 485.2 → 526.8 | +8.6% | −8.8% | −6.8% |

32K ran Triton→FlashMLA; 8K uses a warmed FlashMLA→Triton rerun because the first candidate sample compiled an auxiliary kernel. Median TTFT was more variable: +1.5% and −29.0% in the two 32K/C32 runs.

84 tests passed (52 CPU, 32 GPU), with zero failures or skips. Coverage includes independent FP32 references, packed/strided KV, large offsets, warmup and mutable CUDA Graph replay. Prefix-growth, named-tool and reasoning-stream checks passed on both backends. Changed-file pre-commit and mypy passed; H100 CI coverage is wired, upstream CI pending.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_fewhead_prefill_gate.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_fewhead_sparse_prefill.py \
  tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py::test_v41_compressor_metadata_maps_tokens_to_their_ring -q
```

Full GSM8K, 16-shot greedy chat, max 1024 tokens: **1281/1319 → 1284/1319**, zero request errors. Three answers changed from correct to wrong and six from wrong to correct; length stops were 1→2. This does not establish output equivalence.

## Details

The direct decoder and packed-KV loader come from [#59418](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59418) by luoyuctl (`eddfa5ed50c1`), with three page-size parameters specialized as `tl.constexpr`. They are isolated in the first commit. This PR adds independent backend integration, native-head prefill and query pairing; it does not add #59418's automatic FlashMLA dispatch. Shared-decoder landing order still needs coordination. Query-union prior art: #55372. Unlike #54592, prefill keeps BF16 queries. Reported gains measure the whole backend, including the shared decoder and DSpark interactions.

Requires SM90, BF16 queries, 512D heads/64D RoPE and packed `fp8_ds_mla` KV. Prefill stays outside FULL CUDA Graphs. The context limit is 1M; measured performance inputs are 8K/32K. TP4 full-model, actual 1M inputs and comprehensive multimodal evaluation are not qualified.

Driver-memory maxima sampled every 60 seconds changed by −2.04 to +1.40 GiB/GPU; the 32K cases used about 1.4 GiB/GPU more. These are sampled values, not exact peaks or a memory-saving claim.
