title: [Refactor][Model Loader] Share post-load module iteration order
body:
## Purpose

Cold-start weight processing and layerwise weight reload each hand-wrote the same
post-load visiting order:

- `model_loader/utils.py::process_weights_after_loading` — one pass over every
  module dispatching `quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(module)`, a
  second pass over the deferred attention-like layers, then the model-level hook.
- `model_loader/reload/layerwise.py::finalize_layerwise_processing` — the same
  two passes, no model-level hook.

Two copies of one policy, maintained independently. That is not hypothetical: the
cold-start copy grew a third pass for `HpcModule` that the reload copy never had,
which is the bug #56706 fixed by deleting the pass. This defines the order once,
in a new `model_loader/post_load.py::iter_post_load_modules()` yielding
`(name, module, PostLoadPhase)`, and has both callers consume it. Each caller
keeps its own per-phase policy; only the traversal is shared.

It also removes the reason the two hooks had different signatures. The loader
threaded `model_config.dtype` into the attention-layer hook so the layer could
tell its backend impl the activation dtype — a value the layer already stores as
`self.dtype`, set from the same source. The argument becomes optional and both
loops call a uniform zero-argument hook, which resolves the `TODO(lucas)` in
`utils.py`. `finalize_layerwise_processing`'s `model_config` argument is then
unused and kept only so existing callers keep working.

`PostLoadPhase.MODEL` yields the model unconditionally and each consumer owns its
dispatch policy — cold start applies a `hasattr` test, reload skips the phase
outright — so the iterator commits to an order rather than to one hook name. It also makes reload's skipping of the model-level hook a branch you can
read instead of a line that is missing.

## Where the order lives

Cold start and reload genuinely depend on each other, so neither module can host
the shared order:

- `model_loader/utils.py` calls `record_metadata_for_reloading` from
  `initialize_model`, which imports the `reload` package, so
  `reload/layerwise.py` importing back from `utils.py` closes a cycle.
- Flattening `reload/__init__.py` does not open a path either:
  `reload/torchao_decorator.py` imports `layerwise` directly, so
  `utils.py → torchao_decorator → layerwise → utils.py` closes the same cycle.
- Moving `record_metadata_for_reloading` out to `initialize_model`'s five callers
  would trade the cycle for a step that silently does not run when a caller
  forgets it.

A module inside `reload/` would import cleanly and is the cheaper mechanical
answer, but then cold start would take its traversal order from the reload
feature's internal helpers. So the dedicated module is an ownership choice, not a
necessity the cycle imposes. The cycle itself is worth fixing — `get_layerwise_info` and
`record_metadata_for_reloading` belong in `reload/types.py` and `reload/meta.py`
rather than in `layerwise.py`, `torchao_decorator.py`'s `layerwise` import is only
needed inside a function, and `reload/__init__.py` could re-export lazily the way
`vllm/__init__.py` and `vllm/platforms/__init__.py` already do. That is a separate
change to the reload package's import structure, with its own risk, and it does
not belong in a PR about traversal order. Once it lands, this module folds into
`utils.py` and the import in `layerwise.py` is the only line that moves.

## Deliberate behavior differences

This is a refactor, but not an unconditionally identical one. Four differences,
none of them exercised by an in-tree flow. All four were found by an adversarial
review pass and are listed here rather than left for a reviewer.

**1. The hook receives the layer's dtype, not the caller's.** If a caller handed
finalize or cold start a `ModelConfig` whose dtype differed from the dtype its
layers were built under, the effective dtype would change. Normal loading cannot
separate them: every loader constructs under
`set_default_torch_dtype(model_config.dtype)` and later hands the same config to
post-load; `GPUModelRunner.reload_weights` pairs `self.get_model()` with
`self.model_config`; the IPC, NCCL and sharded-RDT engines each finalize their
own model/config pair. The three in-tree `set_default_torch_dtype` overrides
(`deepseek_vl2`, `whisper`, `minicpmv`) construct timm models, an `nn.Embedding`
and `nn.MultiheadAttention` — none of them an `AttentionLayerBase`, so the
deferred pass never reaches them.

Platform coverage: an AST sweep of every `process_weights_after_loading` in the
tree resolves five layer-level hooks (`Attention`, `MLAAttention`,
`MMEncoderAttention`, Kimi `MultiHeadLatentAttention`, and
`DeepseekV4CPUAttention`), all now with an optional argument. Everything under
`cpu/`, `xpu/`, `amd/` and `rocm/` is either quant-method or kernel level, taking
`layer`, which this does not touch, or model level and already zero-argument.
`DeepseekV4CPUAttention` is the one platform layer that needed the signature
change; XPU has no layer-level hook at all.

One route can separate them, and I would rather name it than claim it away:
`GPUModelRunner.update_config` accepts a `model_config` dtype override and
replaces the config without rebuilding the model, so a later reload hands
finalize a dtype the layers were not built under. Nothing in-tree calls it that
way. On that route the layer's own dtype is the correct one, since it is what the
weights were actually created under, so the change is an improvement there rather
than a regression. The hook keeps its `act_dtype` parameter for callers that mean
to override it, which several tests do; finalize's `model_config` no longer does.

**2. The deferred attention pass is a live rescan, not a captured list.** Cold
start already rescanned `named_modules()` for its second pass; reload collected
`(layer, info)` pairs during its first pass. Keeping both policies would have been
possible; sharing one traversal and picking the rescan is a choice. The rescan
*discovers* a deferred layer that a sibling's hook installed during the first pass;
whether that layer is then finalized is a separate question, because reload still
skips it unless `info.can_load()` holds, so merely attaching a fresh layer is not
enough — its loading state has to be initialized too. No in-tree hook installs or
removes one.

**3. On reload, a deferred attention layer that cannot load is reset in the
second pass rather than the first.** Nothing between the passes reads that
per-layer state.

**4. A model that is itself a deferred attention layer is offered in all three
phases.** Before, the attention pass passed a dtype and the model pass passed
nothing, so a concrete `Attention` root raised `TypeError` on that second call;
the optional argument now lets it through and the hook runs twice. The double
dispatch itself predates this change. No in-tree model's root is an attention
layer.

## Not a duplicate

- #46828 (`[Core] Add post-load weight processing registry`) touches the same
  function from the other direction: it adds a registry so out-of-tree code can
  append post-load callbacks, where this consolidates the two existing in-tree
  traversals. It has been `CONFLICTING` with no activity since 2026-06-30. If it
  is revived, it applies on top of one traversal instead of two.
- #56706 (merged) deleted the third cold-start-only pass. This removes the
  duplication that let that pass exist in one copy and not the other.
- No open PR mentions `iter_post_load_modules`, `finalize_layerwise_processing`
  or the `TODO(lucas)`.

## Tests

Environment: aarch64, 4x GB200, editable install. Commands and results:

```
# reload suite, unit subset
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py \
    tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_tying.py -q \
    -p no:randomly -k "not test_reload_weights and not test_kv_scale_reload \
    and not test_online_quantize_reload"
48 passed, 21 deselected
# (test_reload.py alone selects 44 of these; the other 4 are the weight-tying file)

# suites that call the layer-level hook with an explicit dtype, i.e. the
# callers the optional argument must keep working
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/core/test_vit_fp8_scaling.py \
    tests/compile/passes/test_mla_attn_quant_fusion.py -q -p no:randomly
13 passed, 1 skipped

# lint
$ pre-commit run --files <changed files>            # all hooks pass
$ pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual   # pass
```

Not run to completion in this environment, with the reason:

- `test_reload_weights`, `test_kv_scale_reload`, `test_online_quantize_reload`
  need real checkpoints and fail here with a
  `torch.ops._C.vocab_parallel_embedding` Dynamo error. Verified environmental:
  a worktree on unmodified `origin/main` produces the identical failure, same
  count, same error (`2 failed` on both, 28 occurrences of the error on both).
- `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` skips at module level on sm100, on
  this branch and on unmodified `origin/main` alike.

New tests:

- `test_post_load_iteration_order` — the order itself, including the root's
  position, the deferred layers appearing in both passes, and the model being
  offered in `MODEL` whether or not it carries the hook.
- `test_cold_start_post_load_dispatch_order` / `test_reload_post_load_dispatch_order`
  — what each caller actually invokes, in order. On cold start: every quant method,
  then every attention hook, then the model-level hook exactly once and last. On
  reload the deferred layers are deliberately interleaved instead —
  `quant(a), attention(a), quant(b), attention(b)` — and the model-level hook never
  runs. Both arms pass no dtype argument.
- `test_cold_start_tolerates_model_without_post_load_hook` — pins cold start's
  `hasattr` guard, since `MODEL` is offered whether or not the model has a hook.
- `test_attention_hook_defaults_to_construction_dtype` — builds a real
  `Attention` through `__init__` under a float16 default dtype and asserts the
  impl sees float16 for the zero-argument call and bfloat16 when overridden.
  Built through the constructor on purpose: a stub with `dtype` assigned by hand
  would still pass if the constructor stopped recording it. Deleting
  `self.dtype = dtype` from `Attention.__init__` makes this test fail.

Known test gap, stated rather than hidden: `MLAAttention.dtype` and Kimi
`MultiHeadLatentAttention.dtype` are not unit-pinned, because constructing either
layer needs a `kv_b_proj` and a backend. A missing assignment raises
`AttributeError` on the first cold start of any model using them, so it cannot
ship silently, but it would not be caught by a CPU-only unit test. Happy to add
one if a reviewer wants it pinned directly.

## Model evaluation

Ran an A/B on real models instead. Accuracy is the wrong instrument here — GSM8K's
0.08 tolerance would not notice the absorbed MLA weights flipping bf16 -> fp32 — so
each arm records the observable the change actually produces and the two are diffed:
the ordered sequence of every `process_weights_after_loading` call (module and
quant-method, with the dtype argument and the *effective* dtype), the
dtype/shape/stride and two float64 checksums of every absorbed
`W_UV`/`W_UK_T`/`W_K`/`W_V`, and the model-level hook's call count — per rank, and
per model pass.

Both arms are the **same** stock image,
`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-a8d1aa9c99b8698a2a78b611b7a10c30e6b3995b` (arm64 digest
`sha256:de1e3637...`), on two exclusively-claimed 4x GB200 nodes. The image's build
commit is 4 commits behind this PR's base and **all 7 files this PR touches are
byte-identical between those two commits**, so the 8 changed files were copied into
one container with a per-file gate requiring the worktree `HEAD` blob sha256 to equal
the container's installed file sha256. All 8 gates passed, and the resulting files
are byte-identical to this PR's HEAD. No rebase, and the same image otherwise.

**17 configurations, 26 independently compared units (rank x model pass):**

| | result |
|---|---|
| post-load call order identical | **17/17** |
| absorbed MLA weights identical (dtype/shape/stride + 2 float64 checksums) | **17/17**, covering **111 MLA layers** |
| model-level hook call count identical | **17/17**, and `== 1` on every rank wherever a model defines one |
| `effective_dtype` identical on every single call | yes |

Coverage: dense FP8, online `--quantization fp8` (which also routes cold start
through `finalize_layerwise_processing`), DeepSeek-V2-Lite at TP1/TP2/EP2 (27
absorbed MLA layers each), DeepSeek-V4-Flash at TP1/TP4/TP2+PP2 (model-level hook,
verified once per rank on a partial module tree under PP), its MTP draft, Kimi-K3
(the `MultiHeadLatentAttention` this PR edits, plus 27 `MMEncoderAttention` and a
nested root hook), Qwen3-VL, bert pooling (`EncoderOnlyAttention`), a separately
loaded speculative draft model (a second, independent post-load pass),
`--cpu-offload-gb 2` (the only setting where `device_loading_context` does work),
NVFP4/compressed-tensors, and GPTQ. The GPTQ cell is the sharpest single check: an
fp16 model, where the fallback resolves to `torch.float16`, so a fallback that
resolved to anything fixed would have failed there.

Bit-exact output A/B through a real server, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-FP8`, 200 GSM8K
questions, temperature 0 / seed 42, compared record-by-record:
`same_records=true`, `same_count=true`, `different_indices=[]`.

Reload suite inside the container, which also covers the reload path this PR
changes. Baseline code with the image commit's `test_reload.py`: **1 failed, 44
passed**. Patched code with this PR's `test_reload.py`: **1 failed, 46 passed** — the
same single failure, `test_kv_scale_reload`, which fails on the *untouched* baseline
with `assert 6575.090356905132 < 10` and so is pre-existing here.
`test_reload_weights` — which drives `collective_rpc("reload_weights")` ->
`finalize_layerwise_reload` on a real DeepSeek-V3 MLA checkpoint — and
`test_online_quantize_reload` **pass on both arms**. (Two environmental fixes were
needed first: `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn`, or EngineCore inherits pytest's
CUDA context and dies with `cudaErrorInitializationError`; and caching the
`*-debug-{add,multiply}*` checkpoints, or `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` fails those tests before
they reload anything.)

Running the *old* test file against the patched code adds 4 failures, all
`test_attention_{first_load_processes_weights,reload_defers_post_load}` on the
`_Reloadable{Attention,MMEncoder}Layer` doubles — that is those doubles following the
hook's new signature, which this PR's diff already does.

**One negative result, reported rather than argued away.** Three DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cells produced different greedy tokens, always at token 20 of 24 on one prompt while
the other prompt matched, with bit-identical absorbed weights. A control on a single
node settles it:

| comparison | tokens identical? |
|---|---|
| baseline code vs **itself**, same node, two runs | **no** |
| baseline code vs **patched** code, same node | **yes** |

The baseline cannot reproduce itself while the patched build reproduces the baseline
exactly, so that channel is run-to-run non-deterministic for this MoE model and
cannot gate anything. It passed on the other 12 cells and on the 200-question server A/B.

**Not covered, explicitly.** CPU AMX MLA (`amx_mla.py:287`) is the only attention
backend impl that consumes `act_dtype` and cannot run on this aarch64 host; its
fallback resolves to the same value the old call site passed, which is an argument,
not evidence. ROCm is the most sensitive platform and is not covered here —
`deepseek_v4/amd/model.py`'s model-level hook calls the **non-idempotent**
`prepare_attn_preshuffle()`, so "fires exactly once" only becomes silent corruption
there, and `mla_attention.py` feeds the absorbed weights into mxfp4/fp8
re-quantization, which amplifies a dtype error; the same scripts run unchanged on
MI3xx and I will post those results. Also uncovered: XPU; `CrossAttention` /
`WhisperEncoderAttention`, because whisper-small fails engine init at this commit
identically on both arms; `load_format="ipc_cache"`, the third caller of the changed
function; and difference 4, which has no in-tree instance and so rests on unit tests.

Ruled out by inspection rather than skipped: Mamba / linear-attention / indexer /
conv-state layers never enter the ATTENTION phase (`AttentionLayerBase` declares no
hook — verified by runtime probe), the tensorizer loader never calls the changed
function, and EPLB and sleep/wake do not re-run post-load.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted. The change was reviewed line by line by me, and audited over five
rounds by a second model tasked with falsifying the zero-behavior-change claim
(round 1 requested changes; rounds 2-5 approved, with a noted disagreement).
The four differences above, the constructor-dtype test and the `update_config`
route all came out of that audit, as did the four wording corrections in this
description — the cold-start-only scope of the ordering claim, the `can_load`
qualification on the rescan, "dispatch policy" rather than "`hasattr` test", and
the test command that actually produces the 51-test result. The standing
disagreement is that preserving both traversal policies would also have been
possible, which is difference 2 above. Tests were run and their results are reported verbatim.

title: [Bugfix] Rebuild DeepSeek-V4.1 DSpark draft KV after Mooncake load
body:
## Status: obsolete

Closing this PR because the merged upstream bounded-SWA replay implementation in #56227 already covers the DeepSeek-V4.1 + DSpark + external-KV-cache path. No additional Mooncake-specific DSpark handling is required.

## Verification

- DSV4.1 DSpark registers only each draft layer's `swa_cache_layer` as draft KV.
- With bounded replay enabled (the default on model runner V2), `SlidingWindowMLASpec.prefix_cacheable` is `False` for both target SWA and DSpark SWA.
- `MooncakeStoreWorker` already constructs its store/lookup/load groups from `KVCacheConfig.prefix_cacheable_groups`, so both SWA groups are excluded before Mooncake group convergence.
- #56227 records `replay_start = H - 128`, replays the suffix after local, synchronous connector, and asynchronous connector hits, pads writes to prefix-cacheable target groups, and rebuilds target/DSpark SWA state.
- #56227 merged on 2026-09-18 with its core, attention, KV-connector, and speculative-decode CI coverage passing.
- Our two-round 1,000-sample OCRBench evaluation exercised the same valid runtime path: round 2 loaded 8,878,464 target-KV tokens with zero request/KV-load failures; 128-token replay acceptance changed by only -0.013 percentage points from cold, with no material accuracy regression.

The remaining change in this PR was only a Mooncake-specific fail-fast validation for disabling bounded replay. It did not alter the normal runtime path and is not sufficient justification for a separate model-specific PR.

## Why this PR was opened

The initial analysis incorrectly treated the DSpark draft group as an independently prefix-cacheable EAGLE group. Inspecting `get_draft_kv_cache_layer_names()`, `SlidingWindowMLASpec.prefix_cacheable`, and `KVCacheConfig.prefix_cacheable_groups` together shows that assumption was wrong: the DSpark cache is bounded SWA and is already excluded by the generic cache-spec policy.

Thanks to the reviewers; no action is needed on this PR.

title: [Draft][CPU][GLM5Next] Add sparse MLA / KeyPool backend
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a correctness-first CPU sparse MLA / KeyPool execution path for GLM5Next for #57345.

The implementation keeps the common GLM5Next model graph and adds only the GLM-local CPU indexer, KeyPool lifecycle, metadata, and sparse MLA adapters required for execution. It is independent of the CPU KDA work in #57496.

## Self-review / Implementation notes

### Why a GLM-specific path

The existing dense CPU MLA backend does not match the GLM5Next sparse contract. The DeepSeek CPU implementations were useful structural references, but GLM5Next has distinct KeyPool compression, gate-score pooling, pool-level top-k, pool-to-token expansion, incomplete-pool tails, index-cache representation, and request-local pool boundaries.

For that reason this PR does not copy a complete DeepSeek attention object graph and does not introduce a generic sparse framework. The feature-local flow is:

```text
GLM5Next common attention
  -> CPU indexer metadata
  -> KeyPool compression/tail/cache lifecycle
  -> selected-row sparse MLA
  -> existing latent/value/output projections
```

I intentionally did not add `glm5next/cpu/model.py`. The existing model hierarchy remains usable; only sparse indexer/MLA execution and the minimum platform/backend injection differ on CPU.

### KeyPool lifecycle

For complete pools, the CPU path preserves the intended sequence of pooling, BF16 round-trip, Hadamard transform, FP8 quantization, and index-cache write. For incomplete pools it preserves raw K/gate tail state. Decode reads the request-local tail before adding the new token, then performs pool completion, cache write, top-k selection, and token expansion in that order.

The metadata builder carries pool-granular lengths, block tables, slot mappings, request expansion, and physical-page addressing rather than reconstructing those values heuristically inside the backend.

### Runtime cases validated

The focused suite exercises the production metadata builder, paged caches, KeyPool, and sparse MLA together. It covers:

* one-shot and multi-step pool completion;
* mixed prefill/decode and request reorder;
* request-local pool boundaries even when flattened positions look contiguous;
* dirty physical slot reuse;
* block-aligned prefix restore without tail state;
* non-aligned restore with circular tail state;
* relocation of index, latent, and tail caches;
* independent FP8 bytes/scales and pool top-k checks;
* selected-row sparse MLA versus an independent dense calculation;
* real `Glm5NextMLAAttention.forward` through the CPU path.

The final clean branch passes:

```text
24 passed, 15 warnings in 11.73s
```

The extra warning is the expected detached-worktree absence of generated `vllm._version`; the remaining warnings are existing torch.jit deprecations. Targeted Ruff, Ruff format, Typos, SPDX, lazy-import, forbidden-import, torch.cuda, and manual Python 3.12 mypy hooks pass on the final files. `git diff --check` passes.

### Bugs found and fixed by lifecycle tests

The tests exposed several semantic issues that were fixed in the implementation:

* selected history could consume `index_topk` and truncate the incomplete tail;
* the CPU metadata builder lacked pool-granular slot/length information;
* CPU indexer scores omitted the NVIDIA-compatible per-head ReLU;
* CPU platform handling unnecessarily disabled chunked prefill and prefix caching for this GLM sparse path.

These checks are included because a finite end-to-end tensor would not reliably expose cache ownership or intermediate representation errors.

### Deliberate non-goals and remaining boundary

This is a transparent PyTorch correctness baseline. It does not include native C++/AVX-512 kernels, performance claims, padded speculative decode, a generic sparse-attention refactor, KDA changes, or a full GLM-5.3-Flash generation run with a production checkpoint. Those are separate follow-ups.

Please review the local backend injection point, KeyPool metadata/state representation, request-local slot ownership, prefix/tail restoration, and the narrow CPU block-size/platform handling.

## Duplicate-work check and relationship to #57496

The issue and open-PR searches found no separate open implementation of #57345 or a GLM5Next sparse MLA / KeyPool backend. #57496 is the separate CPU KDA PR. Together they cover the two accelerator-specific attention halves of GLM-5.3-Flash, while remaining independently reviewable.

This is an AI-assisted contribution. The human submitter will review every changed line and defend the design and validation results.

Refs #57345

title: [Kernel][Model][ROCm] Add MiniMax-M3 context-parallel Triton indexer (Triton CP, bf16 index cache)
body:
## Purpose

Add `MiniMaxM3IndexerTritonCPImpl`, a context-parallel Triton indexer subclass for ROCm, in `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/indexer_context_parallel.py`.

With tensor parallelism enabled, the MiniMax-M3 sparse-attention indexer currently scores the full set of KV blocks on every rank. This PR distributes indexer decode scoring across TP ranks: each rank scores its own round-robin shard of KV blocks via the Triton kernel `indexer_context_scores`, then the partial score matrices are combined with an `all_reduce(op=MAX)` across the TP group to reconstruct the full score matrix. The standard top-k selector (`minimax_m3_index_decode`) then runs on the allreduced result, preserving identical selection semantics to the non-CP path.

Behavior details:
- Decode: each rank scores `1/world_size` of the block shards; allreduce (MAX) reconstructs full scores; standard top-k runs on the result.
- Prefill: unchanged — delegates to the base `MiniMaxM3IndexerTritonImpl.forward`.
- Activation: gated by `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP=1` with `TP>1` on ROCm, dispatched through `select_indexer_impl_cls` in `common/indexer.py`.

This is PR 1 of a series; a follow-up (PR 2) replaces the O(blocks) allreduce with an O(topk) candidate-exchange scheme (noted in the module docstring).


## Design context

This PR applies the same round-robin block-sharding + score-allreduce pattern established in the DCP RFC ([#57228](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57228)) and the active DCP PR ([#57239](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57239)) to the MiniMax-M3 sparse lightning indexer. It is not a new framework primitive — it is a subclass of the existing `MiniMaxM3IndexerTritonImpl` that applies CP within the model's own indexer decode path. The approach (shard blocks round-robin across TP ranks, MAX-allreduce scores, run standard top-k) is identical in structure to the DCP indexer pattern in the Triton decode path.

## Test Plan

1. gsm8k accuracy parity between the baseline bf16 indexer (`VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP` unset) and the new context-parallel indexer (`VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP=1`):

```bash
bash benchmark_minimax_m3_cp_indexer_gsm8k_parity.sh
```

2. Long-context serving throughput sweep for MiniMax-M3 at TP=8 on ROCm (MI300X/MI355X), comparing baseline vs. context-parallel indexer:

```bash
bash benchmark_minimax_m3_cp_indexer_tp8_rocm.sh
```

3. Repo lint and type checks:

```bash
pre-commit run --all-files
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual
```

## Test Result

### gsm8k correctness (parity)

| Metric | Baseline (CP off) | Context-parallel (CP on) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| exact_match (strict) | TBD — to be filled after benchmarking | TBD — to be filled after benchmarking |
| exact_match (flexible) | TBD — to be filled after benchmarking | TBD — to be filled after benchmarking |

### Throughput (TP=8, ROCm MI300X/MI355X)

| --- | --- | --- |
| output_throughput (out_tok/s) | TBD — to be filled after benchmarking | TBD — to be filled after benchmarking |

Note: this feature is gated behind `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP=1`; with the flag unset the code path is unchanged from `main`, so the baseline column reflects the existing non-CP indexer.

title: [ROCm][MLA][DCP] Add native CPRR and two-stage speculative verify
body:
## Summary

Add opt-in AITER paths for causal multi-token MLA verification with round-robin decode context parallelism:

1. A native CPRR path that passes global KV indptr, CP rank, and CP world size to AITER's persistent MLA decode kernel.
2. A two-stage experimental path that splits the shared committed prefix from the causal draft window, with `mask0` and flattened Gluon stage-A variants for controlled A/B measurement.
3. Graph-stable metadata buffers and a DSpark-aware persistent metadata bound.
4. Explicit non-causal multi-token DCP capability detection for the DSpark draft attention group.

The existing segmented verification path remains the default. Native CPRR is enabled with `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_NATIVE_DCP_VERIFY=1`; the two-stage experiment is off by default and selected with `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_DCP_AB_VERIFY=mask0|gluon`.

## Why

The segmented DCP verification path expands a K-token verify block into K single-query rows. Those rows repeatedly read almost the same committed KV prefix. AITER's native CPRR kernel keeps the query block together and applies the causal boundary using global positions, allowing the prefix read to be amortized across the block.

The optional two-stage implementation explores the same issue without requiring the prefix stage to understand the causal boundary inside the draft window:

- stage A attends the common committed prefix without a causal mask;
- stage B attends the dense causal draft window on rank 0;
- output and natural-log LSE are merged before the existing cross-rank DCP reduction.

The two-stage modes are retained as experimental A/B controls; native CPRR is the best-performing route in the measurements below.

## Implementation notes

- Native CPRR is enabled only when DCP is active, interleave is one, and the installed AITER entry point exposes `g_kv_indptr`, `cp_world_size`, `cp_rank`, and `causal`.
- Full-graph runs use persistent storage for the global KV indptr so replay does not capture a transient tensor address.
- Native target verification is bounded to the DSpark verify width and larger short-extend shapes retain the existing segmented path.
- The DCP path calls AITER directly because vLLM needs the returned LSE for the cross-rank merge.
- Non-causal draft attention is admitted only when the installed backend exposes the required causal selector.
- Unsupported configurations fail closed or retain the existing segmented route.

## Validation

### Current rebased head

Validated on `vultr-mi355x-5`, MI355X, against current `main`:

```text
80 passed, 1 deselected, 14 warnings
ruff check: pass
ruff format --check: pass
```

The deselected case is a historical non-persistent native-kernel test that aborts inside the installed AITER binary instead of returning a test failure. The production CPRR path uses persistent metadata.

### Kimi-Linear correctness isolation

On the original implementation base, Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct, TP2/DCP2, FP8 KV, ngram K4:

| Path | Graph mode | GSM8K | Request errors |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| segmented | NONE | 44/50 | 0 |
| native CPRR | NONE | 44/50 | 0 |
| native CPRR | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | 45/50 | 0 |

The segmented and native eager runs missed the same six examples.

### Kimi-K3 correctness and kernel proof

On the original implementation base, real Kimi-K3 and DSpark weights, TP8/DCP8, FP8 target/draft KV, DSpark K4, AITER MLA, block rejection, and full graphs:

```text
GSM8K N50/c64: 49/50, 0 request errors
CPRR target kernel loads: 8
mask0 draft kernel loads: 8
segmented qh96 kernel loads: 0
server errors / tracebacks / HSA faults: 0
```

The only GSM8K miss was the known idx13 baseline miss.

### Native CPRR performance

Single-node fixed 8K-context/128-output probe:

| Concurrency | segmented full graph | native CPRR full graph | Change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 15.23 tok/s | 19.15 tok/s | +25.7% |
| 8 | 136.95 tok/s | 265.38 tok/s | +93.8% |
| 32 | 216.81 tok/s | 374.38 tok/s | +72.7% |

These fixed-probe runs used the same request shape, but the archived segmented run used dummy weights and a PD route while the native run used real weights on one colocated node. They are directional rather than a perfectly isolated A/B.

With the final metadata bound, real-weight full graph, explicit 40 GiB KV, and synthetic acceptance length 3.36, a c40 long-prefix run completed 200/200 requests:

```text
duration:                  176.72 s
output throughput:         579.45 tok/s
total token throughput: 75,908.26 tok/s
TTFT mean / median / p99:  8.92 / 6.01 / 32.98 s
TPOT mean / median / p99: 51.38 / 53.71 / 62.77 ms
acceptance length:           3.37
```

### AgentX c48 full-stack validation

The final one-hour Kimi-K3 integration run included the native CPRR and DSpark metadata-bound implementation from this PR. The optional two-stage path was disabled.

```text
P/D: TP8/DCP8, FP8 target and draft KV
MoRIIO: RDMA READ
DSpark: K4, synthetic acceptance length 3.36
AITER: native CPRR target verify
P cache: SimpleCPU fine-grained
concurrency: 48
profile wall time: 3625.31 seconds
```

Result:

```text
successful/total profiling requests: 3867/3869
input throughput: 149,024.39 tok/s
output throughput: 1,045.05 tok/s
total throughput: 150,069.45 tok/s
P combined cache hit: 93.57%
```

The optimization progression showed native CPRR increasing output throughput from about 756 to 1,045 tok/s. Separately, changing the prefill graph policy from piecewise to eager increased usable KV cache from 16.84 to 45.14 GiB and raised c48 input throughput from about 112,315 to 148,781 tok/s. Replacing coarse LMCache reuse with fine-grained SimpleCPU caching increased combined cache-hit coverage.

The client completed successfully. Two requests failed out of 3,869 (0.052%); failed requests were excluded from the token numerator while their execution time remained substantially represented in the wall-time denominator. The result is an end-to-end full-stack measurement rather than a kernel-only CPRR benchmark.

## Historical validation scope

The real-model results above were collected on the earlier K3 integration base at native CPRR commit `aba9c5514` plus metadata-bound commit `698883d91`. Those commits are the historical versions of this PR's first two commits. The current branch rebases and extends that implementation onto current `main`; current-head validation so far is the focused MI355X suite above. The full historical commands, logs, kernel-symbol checks, and benchmark artifacts are retained in the development record.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for implementation review, test construction, experiment orchestration, and documentation. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing and defending every changed line.

title: [Kernel][Model][ROCm] Add MiniMax-M3 context-parallel AITER fp8 indexer (PR B — fp8 index cache path)
body:
## Purpose

This PR adds `MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterCPImpl`, a context-parallel (CP) variant of the AITER fp8 MFMA block-scoring indexer for MiniMax-M3 on ROCm.

Today the AITER fp8 indexer (`MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterImpl`) scores the full set of KV blocks on every TP rank during decode. This PR distributes that work: each TP rank scores only its round-robin shard of KV blocks (`block = local * world_size + rank`) via the AITER `pa_sparse_block_score_decode` kernel, and the partial score matrices are reconstructed with an `all_reduce(MAX)` across the TP group before the standard top-k selection runs. Semantics of top-k selection are identical to the non-CP path.

Scope and relation to other work:

- This is the production path on MI350X with an **fp8** index cache.
- PR A (#57702) covers the **bf16** index cache via a Triton CP path; this PR is the complementary fp8 path and does not duplicate it.
- The new impl is selected only when `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP=1` and `TP>1` on ROCm, dispatched via `select_aiter_indexer_impl_cls` in `amd/indexer_aiter.py`. When the flag is unset behavior is unchanged.
- Prefill is unchanged and delegates to the base AITER impl.

Note: the `_score_shard` and `_select_topk` helpers in this diff currently `raise NotImplementedError` and are placeholders; the CP dispatch/allreduce scaffolding is in place but the shard-scoring and top-k bodies are not yet implemented in this diff.


## Design context

This PR applies the same round-robin block-sharding + score-allreduce pattern established in the DCP RFC ([#57228](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57228)) and active DCP PR ([#57239](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57239)) to the MiniMax-M3 AITER fp8 indexer path. It is not a new framework primitive — it is a subclass of the existing `MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterImpl` applying CP within the model's own indexer decode path. PR A ([#57702](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57702)) covers the bf16/Triton path with the same approach; this PR covers the fp8/AITER path (the production path on MI350X).

## Test Plan

Accuracy (correctness of the CP fp8 indexer vs the TP-only fp8 baseline):

```bash
bash benchmark_minimax_m3_cp_indexer_gsm8k.sh
```

This runs GSM8K 5-shot `exact_match` on MI350X/MI300X for (1) the TP-only fp8 baseline and (2) TP + decode-CP fp8, and prints a summary table.

Throughput (TP-only non-CP baseline vs TP + decode-context-parallel):

```bash
bash benchmark_minimax_m3_cp_indexer_throughput.sh
```

This prints a SUMMARY table on both MI350X and MI300X: output token throughput (out_tok/s), total token throughput, and request throughput.

Lint / type checks:

```bash
pre-commit run --all-files
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual
```

## Test Result

GSM8K 5-shot exact_match (MI350X / MI300X, fp8 index cache):

| Config | exact_match |
| --- | --- |
| TP-only fp8 baseline | TBD — to be filled after benchmarking |
| TP + decode-CP fp8 | TBD — to be filled after benchmarking |

Throughput (out_tok/s, total tok/s, req/s):

| Hardware | Config | out_tok/s | total tok/s | req/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MI350X | TP-only (non-CP baseline) | TBD | TBD | TBD |
| MI350X | TP + decode-CP | TBD | TBD | TBD |
| MI300X | TP-only (non-CP baseline) | TBD | TBD | TBD |
| MI300X | TP + decode-CP | TBD | TBD | TBD |

Before/after note: the CP fp8 path is new and did not exist before this PR, so there is no prior CP fp8 number to compare against; the baseline column is the existing TP-only fp8 path. Numbers are TBD pending execution of the benchmark scripts above on MI350X/MI300X hardware.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Opt-in split-KV decode for the mega attention backend
body:
> **Draft — blocked on https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashMLA/pull/25.**
> This is a no-op until that lands and `cmake/external_projects/flashmla.cmake` pins a FlashMLA commit containing it. The code is capability-gated, so it is safe in the tree meanwhile: with an older FlashMLA the decode path is unchanged and a warning is logged.

## Purpose

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57448

`fused_norm_rope_attn_rope_cast_decode` (the FlashMLA mega attention kernel behind `FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41`) schedules one cluster per query token and has no split-KV, so a small decode batch leaves most of the GPU idle. Measured on one B200, h_q=64, topk 128+512, CUDA graphs: the kernel costs the same **26.6 us at s_q = 1, 6 and 96**.

FlashMLA#25 adds an opt-in fp32 partial-output mode to that kernel. This PR is the vLLM side: `_forward_decode_mega` hands it per-split partial buffers and merges them with a Triton combine that applies the attention sink once and runs the FP8 epilogue (per-32 ue8m0 scales, permuted wv-group layout).

## Behaviour

Off by default. Two env vars:

* `VLLM_DSV41_MEGA_SPLITKV` — max splits, `0`/`1` disables (default `0`)
* `VLLM_DSV41_MEGA_SPLITKV_MAX_TOKENS` — only split at or below this decode-token count (default `8`)

`_splitkv_supported()` inspects the op schema; if the linked FlashMLA predates the new arguments the feature disables itself with a one-time warning.

**The token cap is load-bearing.** The partials cost `num_splits * s_q * h_q * d_v * 4` bytes *per layer per step* — 1.05 MB/layer at one decode token with 8 splits, but 16.8 MB/layer at 16 tokens. Splitting at 16 saturated HBM and regressed that lane by ~35% end to end, even though a single-layer microbenchmark still showed a win there. The default of 8 keeps C16 exactly at baseline.

## Test plan

Kernel-level correctness is covered by the test added in FlashMLA#25 (oracle = the same kernel at `num_splits=1` through the fp32-partial path; 20 cases pass).

For this PR, split vs unsplit through vLLM's own op and this combine, TP4 geometry (16 live heads), `s_q` in {6, 16}, splits in {2, 4, 8}, `attn_sink` in {absent, zeros, trained-like}:

```
lh=16 sink=none  s_q=  6 | ns=2: fp8 95.0% sf 99.5% | ns=4: fp8 94.4% sf 99.7% | ns=8: fp8 94.3% sf 99.7%
lh=16 sink=real  s_q= 16 | ns=2: fp8 95.1% sf 99.7% | ns=4: fp8 94.3% sf 99.5% | ns=8: fp8 94.0% sf 99.4%
```

FP8 codes agree with the fused path ~94-95%, scale exponents ~99.5%+, and the sink cases match the no-sink case — the residual is fp32 re-association showing through as 1-ulp differences, not a logic error (with non-cancelling KV values the codes are 99.6% bit-identical, and the LSE is exact to 9.5e-07 at every split count).

End to end — DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, **TP4 + EP + MegaMoE + SP**, `FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41`, nvfp4_ds_mla KV, `vllm bench serve` random 4096/256 `--ignore-eos`, 3 seeds per lane, cold server per configuration, 1x8 B200 node:

| lane | metric | off | on | delta |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| C1 | out tok/s | 120.12 / 121.67 / 121.72 | 130.69 / 132.55 / 132.55 | **+8.9%** |
| C1 | TPOT ms | 7.77 / 7.78 / 7.78 | 7.11 / 7.10 / 7.10 | **-8.7%** |
| C16 | out tok/s | 1301.84 / 1304.29 / 1299.16 | 1299.77 / 1290.00 / 1290.72 | -0.6% (noise) |

A C64 lane was run and **discarded**: it is bimodal on this setup (1399.59 vs 2556.37 tok/s on the same server, same configuration, seeds 44/45), so it cannot resolve a change of this size. Split-KV is disabled at 64 decode tokens by construction anyway.

`ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on both files.

> **Revision note.** The numbers above were measured on the first revision of this branch. The current revision is a refactor only (five module-level helpers and a duplicated 20-argument kernel call collapsed into one cached config function plus one method); it is lint- and compile-clean and the split-count arithmetic was checked to be identical to the measured revision over 12,960 parameter combinations, but it has not been re-run on GPU yet. A re-run will land before this leaves draft.

## Model evaluation — outstanding

The change alters output: ~6% of FP8 codes move by 1 ulp. A GSM8K run on the split path is **not yet done** and should land before this leaves draft.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open vLLM PRs for split-KV / mega-attention decode work on DSv4.1 (`in:title Perf`, `MegaAttn`, `FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN`, `split-KV`) — nothing overlapping. #57673 targets SM90 *prefill* few-head dispatch and explicitly leaves decode on the padded FP8 path; #56966 reuses physical top-k selection and does not touch the attention kernel's scheduling.

## Follow-ups

* Bump the FlashMLA pin once FlashMLA#25 merges (required for this to do anything).
* Replace the Triton combine with a CUDA one under FlashMLA's `smxx/decode/combine` using PDL — the current one is launch-bound and does not overlap the main kernel's tail, so it gives back part of the win (main kernel alone is 1.86x at s_q=1 vs 1.44x with this combine).
* `h_q == 128` (CLUSTER_SIZE == 2) is unsupported upstream, so TP2/TP1 geometries do not split yet.
* A selection heuristic beyond the env var, once the combine cost is known.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The submitter has reviewed every changed line.

title: [Bug] Kimi-K3 TP8xPP2 + DSpark spec-on: mid-decode target-forward NaN detonates MLA decode under concurrency (fp8 latent-cache bytes carry the corruption)
body:
# vLLM issue draft — Kimi-K3 NaN detonation under concurrency (NVIDIA B200)

File to vllm-project/vllm; remove nothing in body below; click create.
Keys the public can't see in the body below: internal paths, image refs, node names,
deployment names, the request-id prefixes. Everything else is real.

---

**Title:** [Bug] Kimi-K3 TP8×PP2 + DSpark spec-on: mid-decode target-forward NaN (fp8 latent-cache bytes) under concurrent load — NaN pool bytes detonate MLA decode despite the masked-score structure; P·V leaks them (0×NaN=NaN)

## Summary

Kimi-K3 (TP8×PP2, fp8 latent KV cache + Mamba/KDA hybrid layers 0–2, MLA layers 3+, DSpark spec decoding with block rejection) intermittently emits an **utter NaN target logit** on a subset of verify steps under *any* concurrent load. The failing step's target logits are all-NaN (`argmax` = index 0 / degenerate token id), the request's subsequent steps stay poisoned (the drafter's proposal scores turn NaN for good), and — without the containment guard we built (`KIMI_SPEC_NAN_ABORT`) — requests would live-lock to the max-token cap. The cloud's public tests keep presenting us with mid-generation NaN rows of q rows in the engine's pooled latent KV cache — a condition the decode kernel can't safely read: the causal mask replaces their QK scores with `-1e6`, but the P·V MMA multiplies the (now-zero) probabilities by the *bytes* of the poisoned columns — emblematic `0 × NaN = NaN` propagation.

Environment:

- Hardware: 2× B200 (GB100), PP=2 × TP=8 (16 ranks over a TCPStore pair).
- vLLM: forked from main ~Sep 2026 (per commit hash in images below).
- Serving config: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, DSpark spec-configuration `{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"rejection_sample_method":"block"}`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, TRTLLM_RAGGED prefill backend + TOKENSPEED_MLA decode backend, Model Runner V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`), `--all2all-backend deepep_v2`.
- Reproduced on 3 different detached engine runs, fresh nodes, cold GPU memory pools, and roughly 3-30 min of concurrent scene traffic (1–3 concurrent long sequences of 2–10k generated tokens at ~100 req tokens/call stepping to 65k max).

## What NaN looks like (trace-level proof)

Per-module finiteness watchers (both TP ranks of both PP stages) show the NaN first appears at `layers.N.self_attn` (both N=3 and N=11 and N=47 observed across runs) with ALL inputs finite (hidden, quantized fp8 query, block_table, seq_lens) and the output all-NaN for one or two rows of the 16 tokens in the verify batch. The target top1 logits on the verification path are `[0.0 ×8]` for that step, and from there on every later step of the same request. The co-landing of `layers.11+` first-sites with `layers.N` halving (57344 of 114688 finite = exactly half of the row-parallel GEMM's output columns) proves the origin is the re-all-reduce pooling of a rank-local NaN.

## Where the bytes are coming from (pool forensics)

The pooled fp8 latent cache tensors of the blade dying request contain scattered `0x7F`/`0xFF` bytes (e4m3 NaN encodings) at the **head rows of the most recently allocated pages** (a few bytes each on rows 0..~5 of the pages that the request's block table just crossed over a 64-row page boundary into at gate commit time). Their presence explains every downstream evidence except the obvious path of "**the KV insertion wrote quantized NaN latents**: the KV projection chain (up-projection output) at those positions was NaN at insert time".

We consider these write paths with the artifacts of each; everything is instrumented and counted in our trace stream (a `nan_write` probe verifies the written bytes were dirty at insert time):
- The decodes' pages are rewritten each step — yet the head-row positions are *only written once* per page (at the request's crossover into that page). The only writes to those positions before the detonation are the discrete `fused_mla_decode_q_concat_kv_cache_insert` calls on decode steps.
- For those bytes to be NaN, the quantized source vectors had to be NaN at insert time. The packed KDA prefill chunk kernel (`chunk_kda_with_fused_gate`) **is proven to return NaN for decode rows in mixed prefill+decode batches** (upstream #50649 fixed the ROCm copy of that; our nvidia copy lacks it — see below).
- With those rows' "first beams," each subsequent decode step of the affected request then reads them → half-NaN on the o_proj of whichever MLA layer sits downstream (shapes vary with gate widths).

## Reproduce at kernel level (with our poison-injection harness)

A dedicated script (in-pod, runs alongside the live engine) drives `tokenspeed_mla_decode` with handcrafted pools:

| Case | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Clean pool, q_len=8, causal | passes, matches the PyTorch SDPA reference |
| q_len=8 + NaN bytes ONLY in rows [seq, vd*64) of last valid page | **NaN output** |
| q_len=1 + same | finite (single-token decode tiles don't read the tail) |
| Past-valid columns via extra table entries + NaN bytes solely there + is_var_split_kv path | **NaN output** |
| Workspace bytes dirtied (0x7F fill) + otherwise clean input | passes (workspace is correctly sanitized) |

Harness details are shareable (a `kubectl cp`'able runner that patches the standalone `mla_decode_fp8` module's executive entry with integrity-window hooks and runs alongside production, using the actual pooled engine). The reproduce material is done in ~70 lines.

## What we ruled out (all measured on live deployments)

- MRV2 vs MRV2, fp8 vs bf16 KV: the bf16-KV control detonates too (worse, actually — see the table at the end); first-order precision is not the seat of the bug.
- Depth scaling of the drafter (halved `num_speculative_tokens` didn't change the failure).
- Prefix caching-disabled didn't close it.
- The drafter is Inferact/DSpark `Kimi-K3-DSpark`(ours, and separately the RedHatAI speculator): both reproduce the same picture.
- Kernel nondeterminism on the same sequences replayed on clean servers detonates at the same position twice (gs_04337@seed ratifies: same absolute position 4608 both times) — content+seed determines the onset position when the trigger fires.

## Live mitigations we landed (details shared for the community)

Every layer below survived its own detonation clock and dropped the onset depth by a constant factor. None of them is the fix; all of them are load-bearing observability tide:

- `KIMI_SPEC_NAN_ABORT` (on by default on our images): per-request abort the moment a verify step sees a full-NaN logits row; corrupt tokens never reach the client; the engine doesn't restart; the prefix cache gets the request's block ids evicted and quarantined on free.
- NaN-site module watchers with per-rank attribution and per-step deduplication ([ns0->ns8]).
- Block-table pinning: make table entries past each request's valid depth point to that request's own tail-zeroed last valid page, so any overrun reads in-domain.
- Per-group direct zero of newly allocated KV pool blocks (the stock `KVBlockZeroer`'s spec check skipped the MLA uniform-spec group).
- Stream-ordered H2D for the staged block-table writes (UVA round-off reuse is ambiguous with async scheduling depth of pp+1).
- The drafter-dummy-write protection from the upstream fix #56734 ported to the DFlash/DSpark speculator paths.

## Related upstream tracking we drew from

- #50649 (AMD Kimi-K3 fix: Fused KDA NaN on mixed batches — the chunk kernel NaNs decode rows of mixed batches; and a racy `num_stages=4` autotune on gfx950) — **we believe the NVIDIA copy of the same KDA logic needs the same split**; we've ported it from `amd/kda.py` to our nvidia/kda.py family and are verifying on the pools now.
- #51039 (packed KDA prefill leaks across sequences; permanent per-request staleness; author almersawi)
- #52792 (mixed spec/non-spec batches OOB/KDA state fault — the contiguous state_indices story)
- #56734 (the dummy-batch stale slot writes that latch onto a conversation in prefix cache)

We can produce the standings team-forward shape work or run full arms of our reproduction scripts on demand.

## Ask

Does the nvidia `kimi_k3` KDA `mixed_batch` handler need the #50649 `split_non_spec` fix for decode slices? We have everything save the approved instrumentation. If yes: we have the ported fix and its gate evidence ready to upstream.

---


END OF ISSUE BODY

This is draft-safe for the public vLLM tracker: no secret or internal identifier. Post via:
gh issue create --repo vllm-project/vllm --title "[Bug] Kimi-K3 TP8×PP2 + DSpark spec-on: mid-decode target-forward NaN (fp8 latent-cache bytes) under concurrent load" --body-file <this file>

title: [Bug]: /tokenize returns 400 "cannot pickle ValidatorIterator" for assistant `content: null` + `tool_calls` (DeepSeek-V4.1), while chat completions accepts the same messages
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM: `0.29.1rc1.dev47+gdc36fcce9` (nightly build, official Docker image), OpenAI-compatible server
- Python 3.12, pydantic 2.13.x (inside the image)
- Model / tokenizer: DeepSeek-V4.1 (`tokenizers/deepseek_v41.py`, rendered through `DeepseekV4Renderer`)

Full `collect_env.py` output omitted on purpose: the failure happens in request validation / chat-template preprocessing of `/tokenize`, before anything touches the engine, so it is independent of hardware. I also checked the current `main` branch and the relevant code is unchanged (details below).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`POST /tokenize` (chat form) returns **400** for a perfectly ordinary OpenAI-style tool round trip — an assistant message with `"content": null` plus `tool_calls` — while `POST /v1/chat/completions` accepts the *identical* messages and runs fine. `content: null` + `tool_calls` is what the OpenAI SDK and most agent frameworks emit for tool-call turns, so in practice `/tokenize` is unusable for agentic conversations with this tokenizer.

**Minimal reproduction**

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8000/tokenize -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Shanghai tomorrow?"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": null,
     "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "type": "function",
                     "function": {"name": "lookup_weather", "arguments": "{\"city\": \"Shanghai\"}"}}]},
    {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": "{\"temp_c\": 24, \"condition\": \"cloudy\"}"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Do I need an umbrella?"}
  ],
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "lookup_weather",
             "description": "Look up the weather for a city.",
             "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}}}]
}'
```

Actual:

```json
{"error": {"message": "cannot pickle 'pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidatorIterator' object", "type": "BadRequestError", "param": null, "code": 400}}
```

Expected: `200` with a token count, the same prompt that `/v1/chat/completions` renders for these messages.

Observations from the same server; only the assistant message changes:

| assistant message | `/tokenize` |
|---|---|
| `"content": null` + `tool_calls` | **400** (error above) |
| `"content": ""` + `tool_calls` | 200, `count=372` |
| `content` key omitted + `tool_calls` | 200, `count=372` |
| `"content": null`, no `tool_calls` | 200 |

With an equivalent synthetic conversation (different text) I also sent each variant to `/v1/chat/completions` with `max_tokens=1`: the `content: null` variant is accepted there (200), and `usage.prompt_tokens` was identical for all three variants and equal to the `/tokenize` count of the two variants that work. In a larger matrix (tool result as string / content-part array, parallel tool calls, conversation ending on the tool message, no `tools` in the request, assistant text + `tool_calls`), `/tokenize` and `prompt_tokens` matched exactly in every case that got past validation. So rendering is consistent between the two endpoints; only the `null` case is rejected by `/tokenize`.

**Root cause (from reading the code)**

1. `ChatCompletionMessageParam` is a union of the OpenAI SDK TypedDicts and `CustomChatCompletionMessageParam`. The custom type declares `content: str | list[...]` (no `None`) and `tool_calls: list[...] | None`; the OpenAI assistant type allows `content: None` and declares `tool_calls: Iterable[...]`. When `content` is a string or absent, the custom member matches and `tool_calls` validates to a plain `list`. With `content: null` the custom member fails, the OpenAI member wins, and pydantic validates the `Iterable` field lazily into a one-shot `ValidatorIterator`.
2. `ChatCompletionRequest` already compensates for this: `_materialize_tool_calls_after` (added in #34844) converts those `ValidatorIterator` wrappers back to lists. **`TokenizeChatRequest` has no equivalent validator.**
3. `tokenizers/deepseek_v41.py::_normalize_messages` does `copy.deepcopy(messages)` on the *original* request messages (the renderer passes `messages=messages` in addition to the parsed `conversation`). A `ValidatorIterator` cannot be deep-copied, hence the `TypeError`, surfaced as a 400.

Both endpoints share the same renderer and tokenizer wrapper; the only difference is the missing materialization step on the tokenize request model. On current `main`, `vllm/entrypoints/serve/tokenize/protocol.py` still has only the `check_generation_prompt` validator and `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v41.py` still deep-copies the original messages.

**Possible fixes**

- Apply the same `tool_calls` materialization to `TokenizeChatRequest` (e.g. a shared mixin / helper with `ChatCompletionRequest`), or
- make `_normalize_messages` robust by materializing iterator-valued fields before the `deepcopy` (this would also cover other `Iterable`-typed fields such as content-part arrays if they ever end up on the OpenAI member of the union).

Reproducing the validation step locally with pydantic 2.13 and TypedDicts shaped like the two union members suggests `"content": null` with an **empty** `"tool_calls": []` hits the same path (an empty list is still wrapped in a `ValidatorIterator`); I have not confirmed that one against a running server.

**Workaround** for anyone hitting this: send `"content": ""` (or omit the key) instead of `null` on assistant tool-call messages when calling `/tokenize`; the rendered prompt and token count are identical.

I searched existing issues/PRs (`ValidatorIterator`, `tokenize cannot pickle`, `TokenizeChatRequest tool_calls`) and only found the chat-completions-side fixes (#34844, and #9951 for the Mistral tokenizer), nothing for `/tokenize`.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Searched existing issues and PRs for this problem (queries listed above); no existing report found.

title: [Model Loader] Run model-level post-load finalization from the loader hook
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

**`load_weights` must not assume all weights arrive in one call.** RL weight updates call it once per bucket: verl sends 512 MB buckets tensor by tensor, and the NCCL engine calls it once per tensor (inside `disable_mtp_completeness_check()`). A weight and its scale, or the two halves of a merged tensor, can therefore land in different calls. Any post-load work inside `load_weights` then runs on partial weights, once per bucket. Context: RFC #54477, tracker #50079.

The PR has three parts:
1. **One finish step for every load.** `finalize_model_weights(model)` runs once after a full load and once at the end of every reload. It raises if a multi-tensor weight is still missing a part, then calls the model's `process_weights_after_loading()`. There are no per-model opt-ins. This mirrors SGLang, which post-processes once at `end_weight_update`.
2. **Cross-call pairing.** One shared helper, `stash_weight_part`, replaces every call-local pairing buffer.
3. **Post-load work moves out of `load_weights` into the hook.** That includes the blocks that used to rebuild derived state on every call.

Coverage: an AST script enumerated every `def load_weights` in `vllm/` (447), and each was checked in source. That covers multimodal wrappers, MTP/EAGLE/DSpark/DFlash drafters, adapters, `AutoWeightsLoader`, layer-level loaders, model loaders and the `vllm/models/*` platform variants. Every model-level `process_weights_after_loading()` was also checked for whether it is safe to re-run on new weights.

## Claims

**Finish step.** `finalize_model_weights` is called from two places, and nowhere else:
- `model_loader/utils.py::process_weights_after_loading`: cold load (dummy loads too), after per-layer quant processing.
- `finalize_layerwise_reload`: used by `reload_weights` and by `finish_weight_update` in the NCCL, IPC, M2N and sharded-RDT engines.

No `load_weights` calls the model hook anymore. The DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 VL wrappers drop `finalizes_weights_during_load` / `_weights_finalized` and the language-model-first regrouping, and `stream_language_model_first` is deleted.

**Cross-call pairing.** `stash_weight_part(module, key, part, tensor, parts)` parks a part on the module, keyed by module prefix. The parked part is cloned, because transfer buckets reuse their buffers. The helper returns all parts once the set is complete and drops the entry. Leftover parts raise at the finish step and are never dropped silently. It replaces:
- **FP8 indexer `wk` weight+scale dequant:** DeepSeek-V2, `deepseek_mtp`, DeepSeek-V3.2 nvidia/amd (model and MTP), HY-V4 amd/nvidia model and nvidia MTP, dots3. Before, a pair split across calls was dropped; dots3 raised at the end of the call.
- **GLM5-next:** indexer `wk` and the BF16-kept MLA projections, model and MTP.
- **MiMo-V2 and MiMo-V2 MTP:** fused FP8 qkv. These already kept their own dict on `self`, but nothing checked it for leftovers.
- **Molmo/Molmo2 split embedding:** a call without both halves raised `KeyError`.
- **Llama4 DP-vision q/k/v concat:** a split triple failed in `torch.cat`.
- **Jina-v3 LoRA merge:** a split triple raised `KeyError`.

**Moved from `load_weights` to `process_weights_after_loading`:**
- **DFlash-family fused context-KV buffers:** Qwen3 DFlash, plus Qwen3 DSpark, Gemma4 DSpark and LiLiCorr through the inherited hook, and Laguna. The hook reads weights after quant processing. So the fused raw-weight path is used only when the projections are unquantized and not repacked by CPU (`_reads_raw_weights`). Otherwise each projection runs through its quant method, as Qwen3 DFlash already did for quantized drafts.
- **BERT MLM:** the tied-decoder copy, decided by `config.tie_word_embeddings`.
- **DeepSeek-V4 NVIDIA and V4.1 NVIDIA/AMD:** the mHC broadcast.
- **LiLiCorr:** the inference buffers. A `dummy` load now builds them.
- **OpenPangu:** the `post_weight_load` sweep. `StaticSinkAttention.update_sink_kv` now clears `sink_populated`, so a re-run rewrites the cached sink KV.
- **Gemma4 MTP:** the lm-head cache invalidation and the suppress-token index.
- **DeepSeek-V4 XPU:** `finalize_mega_moe_weights` for target, MTP and DSpark. The lazy call in MegaMoE `forward()` is gone.
- **MiniCPM-V/O:** the resampler device move. A `dummy` load used to crash.
- **DeepSeek-V4.1 NVIDIA:** the Engram page-cache drop and THP collapse.

**Decisions on one call's loaded set run only for a complete load.** They are gated on `is_mtp_completeness_check_enabled()`, which the weight-transfer engines turn off. They used to fire on every bucket:
- `AutoWeightsLoader._check_skipped_aliases`.
- DSpark `confidence_head` drops: gemma4, qwen3, DeepSeek-V4/V4.1.
- Checkpoint checks: Qwen3 DSpark, Eagle3 `mask_hidden`, AliceAI and LiLiCorr coverage.
- The Phi-3-V embedding alias.
- The NemotronVL seq-cls head init.
- The MTP layer checks that were still ungated: Bailing V3, DeepSeek-V3.2 AMD, GLM5-next, Kimi-K3.

**Raw (non-vLLM-serialized) tensorizer** checkpoints load through `BaseModelLoader.load_model`. Before, a private helper skipped per-layer quant processing. This is the same change and test as #55318.

## Validation

GB200, image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-1b2a666391f2a24228a1436b64d547c34cc6b6ce`. A is the image as-is; B is the image plus this commit, overlaid behind per-file SHA-256 gates.

The probe cold-loads the model and snapshots every parameter, buffer and tensor attribute. It then reloads the same checkpoint twice: once with a single `load_weights` call, and once bucketed, with one call per tensor under `disable_mtp_completeness_check`. It runs two finish modes:
- **plain:** `load_weights` followed by `process_weights_after_loading(model, ...)`, as verl does.
- **layerwise:** `initialize_layerwise_reload`, then the loads, then `finalize_layerwise_reload`, as `reload_weights` and the engines do.

Every tensor is compared bit-exactly with the cold snapshot, and greedy outputs are compared before and after.

| model (real weights) | cold output A vs B | bucketed reload, plain: A / B | bucketed reload, layerwise: A / B |
|---|---|---|---|
| bert-base-uncased (`BertForMaskedLM`) | identical | equal / equal | equal / equal |
| Phi-3-vision-128k-instruct | identical | raises (alias guard) / equal | crashes (meta-tensor copy) / equal |
| Qwen3-1.7B + AngelSlim Eagle3 drafter | identical | equal / equal | equal / equal |
| MiniCPM-V-4.7-1B + DSpark drafter | identical | `confidence_head` deleted / equal | crashes (fused-KV build on meta tensors mid-reload) / equal |
| MiniCPM-V-2_6 | identical | equal / equal | equal / equal |
| openPangu-Embedded-1B | identical | equal / equal | equal / equal |
| Qwen3-0.6B-FP8 | identical | fails on both arms (loading into already-processed FP8 params: no `load_row_parallel_weight`) | equal / equal |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash 4-layer slice, EP + MegaMoE | identical | n/a (reload of this model fails upstream) | n/a |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp 4-layer slice | identical | n/a | n/a |

A single-call full reload of Phi-3-Vision trips the alias guard on both arms. That is pre-existing.

**Tests (B):**
- 58 passed in the PR test set: the new `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_parts.py`, `test_lilicorr.py`, `test_deepseek_v4_vl.py`, `test_openpangu_post_load.py`, the mHC hook test, the tensorizer test and `test_expert_substitution.py`. A cannot collect the new file.
- `test_quark.py -k glm5next`: 4 passed.
- `test_dflash2.py` (including the quantized-projection fallback): 21 passed.
- `test_gemma.py -k dspark`: 4 passed.
- `tests/model_executor/model_loader/` (not `slow_test`): B has 24 failures/errors, a strict subset of A's 27. The failures on both arms are offline HF hub and optional dependencies. The tensorizer test and both MoNe cases pass only on B.
- `pre-commit` passes.

`test_weight_parts.py` covers a weight and its scale split across two calls, in both orders, with the bucket buffer overwritten after the first call. It also checks that a leftover part raises once at finish, that the reload finish runs the model hook exactly once, and that the Molmo/Molmo2 embedding halves can split across calls.

**Not validated at runtime:** XPU and ROCm (no hardware); the large pairing models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM5-next, HY-V4, dots3, MiMo-V2, Llama4, Molmo, Jina-v3), whose conversions are covered by the unit test of the shared helper; Laguna/Gemma4 DSpark drafts.

## Details

Verdicts over the 447 `load_weights`:

| verdict | count | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| per-weight | 364 | dispatch, remap or transform of the incoming tensor, routing, delegation |
| loader | 6 | model-loader entry points |
| moved | 21 | post-load work now in the hook |
| paired | 14 + 4 gated MTPs | parts paired across calls via `stash_weight_part` |
| gated | 18 + 10 upstream | checks/decisions on this call's loaded set, complete loads only |
| exception | 14 | per-name choices that build no derived state (Roberta prefix sniff, Whisper zero `k_proj` bias, ColPali lazy head), Inkling EP padding, error paths |

Re-running each model-level hook on new weights (finish of a reload):
- **Same result as a cold start:** BERT, DFlash family, Laguna, LiLiCorr, Gemma4 MTP, MiniCPM-V/O, OpenPangu (with the `sink_populated` fix), expert substitution, DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 mHC, V4.1 Engram THP (idempotent OS hints), Beam warmup, Kimi-K3 DSpark-MLA metadata, the VL wrappers (they delegate).
- **Not re-runnable, left as follow-ups:**
  - **dots3 vision MoE.** It FP8-packs the experts, then deletes the bf16 experts. A reload of vision weights fails loudly because there is no target param. Making it re-runnable means keeping the bf16 experts resident.
  - **DeepSeek-V4 AMD MegaMoE.** The shuffle is guarded by `_runtimes`, and the fused shared-expert module is dropped. DeepSeek-V4 reload already fails earlier upstream, on both arms.
  - **XPU:** out of scope.
- **Unchanged paths that do not run the hook:** kernel-format reload (`is_checkpoint_format=False`), sparse-NCCL patches and vLLM-serialized tensorizer. None of these calls `load_weights`.
- **verl:** its FP8/QAT finish paths process layers themselves and do not call the model hook. Its default path calls `process_weights_after_loading(model, ...)` and gets the finish step.

Overlap: the tensorizer change and its test are the same as draft #55318 (nicole-lihui, co-author). Whichever lands first, the other drops it.

**AI assistance.** Done with Claude Code. Codex, Kimi and Claude audited the diff and the coverage over three more rounds. Confirmed findings were applied: a quantized Gemma4-DSpark/Laguna draft read post-quant weights raw (fixed by the shared predicate and the per-projection fallback), and a comment nit. The last round confirmed nothing; its one claim, that the V4.1 AMD hook lost the mHC call, is false.

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Guard record_transfer against None telemetry
body:
> Supersedes #57403, which was closed because its head picked up merge commits from an updated `main` (354 files, diff unreadable). This PR carries the same single-commit fix (patch-id `c182a17c19c1538a7e4fe2fb84217732e7ae2371`), rebased onto current `main`. cc @NickLucche

### Problem
Some NIXL backends do not capture transfer telemetry by default (UCX without `NIXL_TELEMETRY_ENABLE=1`, and OBJ in some configs). For these, `get_xfer_telemetry()` returns `None` instead of a `nixlXferTelemetry` struct.

`NixlBaseConnectorWorker._pop_done_transfers()` in `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py` passes that result straight to `self.xfer_stats.record_transfer(res)`. When `res is None`, the call raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'xferDuration'`. The surrounding `try/except Exception` catches it and treats it as a transfer failure (`transfer_exception`): the blocks are invalidated and downstream workers report the request as failed. With Dynamo P/D disaggregation, the frontend then returns HTTP 500 to the client.

The bug does not depend on any one backend. It triggers whenever a backend reports `xfer_state == "DONE"` but cannot fill in telemetry.

### Reproduction
Deploy DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with P/D disaggregation on NVIDIA H200 using the NIXL UCX backend. `NixlBaseConnectorWorker` calls `get_xfer_telemetry()` for each DONE handle, and the UCX plugin returns `None` because it allocates no telemetry buffer by default. `record_transfer(None)` then raises `AttributeError`, the request is marked failed, and Dynamo returns HTTP 500. Stack trace excerpt from a production deploy (2026-09-17):

```
ERROR vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.nixl.base_worker:_pop_done_transfers:3031
Marking blocks as invalid
transfer_exception
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'xferDuration'
```

This error is logged on every KV transfer completion, so the log noise alone makes it a production problem.

### Fix
Make `NixlKVConnectorStats.record_transfer()` (`nixl/stats.py`) accept `None` and skip recording when the backend returned no telemetry:

```python
def record_transfer(self, res: "nixlXferTelemetry | None"):
    # Keep metrics units consistent with rest of the code: time us->s
    if res is None:
        return
    ...
```

The guard sits inside `record_transfer()` rather than at the call site, so every caller is covered, including future ones. Nothing changes for backends that do return telemetry. For backends that don't, that transfer simply isn't recorded in the metrics. That's better than marking a successful transfer as failed.

### Related
- #55576 (open) handles a sibling case: the OBJ tier explicitly enabling telemetry. This fix complements it. Even with telemetry fully enabled, the `None` guard stops future backends from hitting the same crash.
- #35876 (open) reworks throughput computation, which is a different metric path.

### Test plan
- [ ] Run the existing unit tests under `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/`.
- [ ] Add a regression test that mocks `get_xfer_telemetry` to return `None` and checks that the transfer is released cleanly without raising.

### Diff

```diff
-    def record_transfer(self, res: "nixlXferTelemetry"):
+    def record_transfer(self, res: "nixlXferTelemetry | None"):
         # Keep metrics units consistent with rest of the code: time us->s
+        if res is None:
+            return
         self.data["transfer_duration"].append(res.xferDuration / 1e6)
         self.data["post_duration"].append(res.postDuration / 1e6)
         self.data["bytes_transferred"].append(res.totalBytes)
```
