title: [RFC] Load attention sinks through the current weight_loader
body:
﻿## Summary

Design doc for a correctness bug in online weight update: checkpoint-backed
attention sink parameters are loaded with a bare `copy_` in several model
`load_weights()` implementations, which bypasses `param.weight_loader` — the
only entry point the layerwise reload path can observe.

```python
param.data.copy_(narrow_weight)
params_dict[name][:n].copy_(narrow_weight)
```

Cold load works. Live update does not: during RL / online weight update /
layerwise reload the parameter is on `meta`, so the write lands on a temporary
tensor and `_place_kernel_tensors` restores the saved kernel tensor unchanged.
The reload reports success while the attention kernel keeps using the old sink.

Design doc: `docs/design/attention_sink_weight_update.md`

## Confirmed scope

20 direct-copy sites across 19 files:

| Model family | Files |
| --- | --- |
| DeepSeek V4 target | `deepseek_v4/{cpu,xpu,amd,nvidia}/model.py` |
| DeepSeek V4 MTP | `deepseek_v4/{xpu,amd,nvidia}/mtp.py` |
| DeepSeek V4 DSpark | `deepseek_v4/{xpu,amd,nvidia}/dspark.py` |
| DeepSeek V4.1 target | `deepseek_v41/{amd,nvidia}/model.py` |
| DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark | `deepseek_v41/{amd,nvidia}/dspark.py` |
| HY-V4 target / MTP | `hy_v4/nvidia/{model,mtp}.py` |
| MiMo-V2 target | `model_executor/models/mimo_v2.py` |
| GPT-OSS | `model_executor/models/gpt_oss.py` (3 quant paths) |

Deliberately not changed: Granite / GraniteMoE (TP slicing already lives in a
`sharded_weight_loader`), Qwen3-DFlash and Laguna (they slice `loaded_weight`
in preprocessing and still yield through `AutoWeightsLoader`), MiMo-V2 MTP
(already calls `param.weight_loader`).

## Proposed contract

> Every checkpoint-backed, online-updatable parameter must be loaded through the
> parameter's **current** `weight_loader`. Model `load_weights()` must not write
> to such a parameter with a bare `copy_`.

DeepSeek pads its runtime sink to the platform head count with an `-inf` tail,
so the checkpoint slice cannot be handed to the loader directly (shape mismatch,
and the padding semantics would be lost). A single shared helper rebuilds the
padded representation and routes it through the current loader:

```python
load_padded_attn_sink(param, loaded_weight, head_start, head_end)
```

HY-V4, MiMo-V2 and GPT-OSS keep their existing TP slicing in `load_weights` and
then call the current loader; slicing must have exactly one owner so no shard is
taken twice.

## Implementation plan

Each step is a separate PR, stacked on this RFC.

| Task | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Shared DeepSeek padded sink helper + unit test |
| 2 | DeepSeek V4 target: `cpu`, `xpu`, `amd`, `nvidia` `model.py` |
| 3 | DeepSeek V4 MTP: `xpu`, `amd`, `nvidia` `mtp.py` |
| 4 | DeepSeek V4 DSpark: `xpu`, `amd`, `nvidia` `dspark.py` |
| 5 | DeepSeek V4.1 target and DSpark |
| 6 | HY-V4 target and MTP |
| 7 | MiMo-V2 target, aligned with MTP |
| 8 | GPT-OSS all three quantization load paths |
| 9 | Audit: no checkpoint-backed sink load bypasses `weight_loader` |

Linked PRs are added to this description as they open.

## Testing plan

Tests drive the real layerwise reload lifecycle rather than asserting that a
mock loader was called, because the defect is precisely a load the framework
never sees: `record_metadata_for_reloading` -> `initialize_layerwise_reload` ->
`load_weights` -> `finalize_layerwise_reload`, asserting the new value reached
the kernel tensor storage, that `data_ptr` is unchanged, and (DeepSeek) that the
padding tail is still `-inf`. Includes `tp_rank != 0` so a double slice cannot
hide behind rank 0. An end-to-end oracle (cold-load B vs cold-load A + live
update to B, compare forward outputs) is planned for one model.

## Status

- Code changes for tasks 1-9 are implemented and pass `ruff check` / `ruff
  format` against the repository config.
- GPU validation is pending. The target H20 cluster has CUDA 13.0 and the
  precompiled vLLM wheel index publishes only up to cu129, so validation
  requires a from-source build that is in progress. Results will be posted here.
- One deliberately out-of-scope observation: `gpt_oss._load_weights_other` also
  writes some quantized weights with `param.copy_(weight)` a few lines above the
  sink branch. Those are not sinks and are not touched by this RFC.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, and test authoring.
The submitter reviews every changed line and is responsible for the validation
results.

## Validation

Environment: H20 (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0, vLLM built from source at commit
`4817c287e8`, the head of the stacked series).

```text
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
    tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_attn_sink_reload.py \
    tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_attention_sink_load_audit.py \
    tests/models/deepseek_v4/test_attn_sink_loader.py -q
43 passed
```

The failure mode is measured, not inferred. Driving a padded sink through the
real `initialize_layerwise_reload` / `finalize_layerwise_reload` cycle:

```text
OLD     got=[0.0, 0.0, 4235.352, 0.0]  want=[-0.0, -1.0, -2.0, -3.0]
        tail_is_neginf=False  buffered=['proj']  data_ptr_stable=True
helper  got=[-0.0, -1.0, -2.0, -3.0]   want=[-0.0, -1.0, -2.0, -3.0]
        tail_is_neginf=True   buffered=[]       data_ptr_stable=True
```

So the pre-fix path does not merely keep the old value: the restored kernel
tensor holds unwritten storage, and the `-inf` padding tail is not
re-established. `data_ptr` is stable in both cases, so pointer identity alone
does not detect the bug.

`ruff check` / `ruff format` against the repository config: clean.

Still outstanding: the end-to-end forward-pass oracle on a real checkpoint,
which needs model weights and the matching attention backend. The CPU and XPU
backends cannot be exercised on this cluster; those variants share the helper
and are covered structurally by the audit.

title: [Bugfix][RL] Load DeepSeek V4 MTP attention sinks through weight_loader
body:
﻿## Stacked on #57797

This PR contains the shared helper from #57797 plus the changes below. Review
only the last commit; the earlier commits are #57797 and will disappear from the
diff once it merges.
Same direct copy in the three V4 MTP draft models (`xpu`, `amd`, `nvidia`).
Without this, a live update of the drafter leaves its attention sink stale.
## Context

RFC: #57795 (`docs/design/attention_sink_weight_update.md`)

Layerwise reload can only replay loads that pass through `param.weight_loader`.
A model `load_weights()` that writes a sink with a bare `copy_` is invisible to
`online_process_loader`, so a live weight update leaves the kernel tensor that
the attention backend reads at its old value.

## Validation

- `ruff check` / `ruff format` against the repository config: clean.
- `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_attention_sink_load_audit.py` passes,
  and catches the pre-fix revisions of all eight affected files with line
  numbers.
- H20 GPU run is pending; a from-source CUDA build is in progress and results
  will be posted on the RFC.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used. The submitter reviews every changed line.

Environment: H20 (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0, vLLM built from source at commit
`4817c287e8`, the head of this stacked series).

$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
    tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_attn_sink_reload.py \
    tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_attention_sink_load_audit.py \
    tests/models/deepseek_v4/test_attn_sink_loader.py -q

The model change in this PR is the same load path exercised by
`test_attn_sink_reload.py`, which drives the real
`record_metadata_for_reloading` -> `initialize_layerwise_reload` ->
`load_weights` -> `finalize_layerwise_reload` lifecycle. Measured on the same

title: [Core][KVConnector] Keep the offloaded KV tier across pause/sleep
body:
## Summary

`pause`/`sleep` exist to hand GPU memory back. An external KV connector tier
(CPU/SSD offload) is the one cache that *survives* that handover, and the
pause/sleep cascade evicts it. For an RL rollout that time-shares the GPU
(`sleep(1)` → train → `wake_up()`), that tier is what makes resumption cheap:
without it the resume re-prefills every in-flight sample.

Whether the tier is still valid depends on the caller replacing the weights,
which the engine cannot know at pause time. Block hashes do not cover the
weights, so the default stays "evict" and this adds an opt-out:

```python
llm.sleep(level=1, clear_connector_cache=False)   # same weights on wake-up
```

Threaded through `pause_scheduler`/`sleep` to `_reset_caches(reset_connector=)`,
the Python and Rust clients, and `/pause` and `/sleep`. Default `True`
everywhere, so nothing changes unless a caller opts out. The Rust client sends
the argument only when opting out, so a new frontend still drives an older
engine.

## Measured

2x GB200, slurm job 30001, on the nightly image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`
(`0.29.1rc1.dev422`), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, this branch's files bind-mounted
over the image one by one (mounting the whole package would hide the compiled
`_C` that ships in it).

Server, on the head node's 4 GPUs:

```bash
VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve $MODEL --served-model-name dsv41 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 65536 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --port 8712 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{"block_size":128,"cpu_bytes_to_use":34359738368}}'
```

Client, from the second node: 16 concurrent completions of ~19.5k tokens each
(311,744 tokens queried in total), then `/sleep?level=1` with and without
`&clear_connector_cache=false`, then `/wake_up`, then the same 16 prompts
again. Full script in the details block below.

| replay after wake-up | default | `clear_connector_cache=false` |
|---|---|---|
| external prefix-cache hits | **0** / 311,744 | **311,296** / 311,744 |
| `kv_offload_load_bytes_total` | 0 | **1.31 GB** |
| `kv_offload_store_bytes_total` | 1.31 GB (all recomputed) | 0 |
| p50 latency | 4.421 s | 0.490 s |

The counters are the evidence: with the tier cleared the replay stores the same
1.31 GB all over again, with it kept it reads exactly that 1.31 GB back. The
latency column is indicative only — the two arms run in sequence against one
server and share prompts, so the second arm starts warmer.

Two things about this run that a reviewer should know:

- The patch set mounted into the image also carried #57813, so the connector
  config above additionally had `"pin_in_flight_chunks": true`, which is that
  PR's key and not part of this one. It cannot have moved these numbers: the
  run stores 1.22 GiB into a 32 GiB tier, so nothing is ever evicted and
  pinning has nothing to do. Reproducing this PR alone means dropping that key,
  as the command above does.
- The client's prompt generator counts words, not tokens, so `--prompt-tokens
  4096` produces ~19.5k tokens per request. The absolute latencies depend on
  that; the hit/miss counters do not.

<details>
<summary>Client script</summary>

```python
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
"""Does the offloaded KV tier survive a sleep, and does a resume reuse it?

Sequence per arm:
  1. warm N distinct long prefixes (they land in the CPU tier),
  2. sleep(level=1) -- with or without clear_connector_cache,
  3. wake_up,
  4. replay the same prefixes and read the external-cache hit counters.

With the tier kept, step 4 hits the offloaded blocks; with it cleared, step 4
re-prefills from scratch. The difference is the point of PR #57810.
"""

import argparse
import json
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

import requests


def metrics(base: str) -> dict[str, float]:
    out: dict[str, float] = {}
    for line in requests.get(f"{base}/metrics", timeout=30).text.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("#") or " " not in line:
            continue
        name, _, value = line.rpartition(" ")
        if "prefix_cache" in name or "offload" in name or "connector" in name:
            try:
                out[name] = out.get(name, 0.0) + float(value)
            except ValueError:
                pass
    return out


def prompt(idx: int, tokens: int) -> str:
    # Distinct prefixes, long enough to fill several offload chunks.
    return f"session-{idx}: " + " ".join(f"w{idx}_{i}" for i in range(tokens))


def fire(base: str, idx: int, tokens: int, max_tokens: int = 8) -> float:
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    r = requests.post(
        f"{base}/v1/completions",
        json={
            "model": "dsv41",
            "prompt": prompt(idx, tokens),
            "max_tokens": max_tokens,
            "temperature": 0.0,
        },
        timeout=600,
    )
    r.raise_for_status()
    return time.perf_counter() - t0


def run_arm(base: str, keep_tier: bool, n: int, tokens: int) -> dict:
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=n) as pool:
        warm = list(pool.map(lambda i: fire(base, i, tokens), range(n)))
    before = metrics(base)

    params = {"level": 1, "mode": "abort"}
    if keep_tier:
        params["clear_connector_cache"] = "false"
    requests.post(f"{base}/sleep", params=params, timeout=600).raise_for_status()
    requests.post(f"{base}/wake_up", timeout=600).raise_for_status()

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=n) as pool:
        replay = list(pool.map(lambda i: fire(base, i, tokens), range(n)))
    after = metrics(base)

    delta = {k: after.get(k, 0.0) - before.get(k, 0.0) for k in set(before) | set(after)}
    return {
        "keep_tier": keep_tier,
        "warm_p50_s": sorted(warm)[len(warm) // 2],
        "replay_p50_s": sorted(replay)[len(replay) // 2],
        "metric_delta": {k: v for k, v in sorted(delta.items()) if v},
    }


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
    ap.add_argument("--requests", type=int, default=16)
    ap.add_argument("--prompt-tokens", type=int, default=4096)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    base = f"http://{args.host}:{args.port}"
    result = {
        "cleared": run_arm(base, False, args.requests, args.prompt_tokens),
        "kept": run_arm(base, True, args.requests, args.prompt_tokens),
    }
    result["verdict"] = (
        "tier reused on resume"
        if result["kept"]["replay_p50_s"] < result["cleared"]["replay_p50_s"]
        else "no measurable difference"
    )
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    with open(args.out, "w") as f:
        json.dump(result, f, indent=2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

## Not a duplicate

`_reset_caches` / the connector eviction on pause is untouched by any open PR.
#57296 is KV *event* payloads, #56754 is request draining, #49789 is
graph/runtime state across weight reloads.

## Test plan

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q                          # 177 passed
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector -q          # 467 passed
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py -q -k "pause or sleep_forwards"  # 10 passed
cargo test -p vllm-server -- pause_route sleep_route                # 5 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed>                                   # passed
```

The rest of `test_engine_core.py` starts a real engine and does not run on my
box (another process holds the GPU: "Free memory on device cuda:0 (92.93/139.8
GiB) ... less than desired GPU memory utilization"). CI covers it.

`test_pause_clear_connector_cache_opt_out` covers both values through
`EngineCore.pause_scheduler`; `test_pause_forwards_connector_flag` covers the
immediate and deferred `EngineCoreProc` paths and that an omitted argument
clears; `sleep_route_sends_connector_opt_out_only_when_requested` pins the Rust
wire format.

No model-quality impact: sampling, weights and attention are untouched.

## Review rounds

Adversarial automated review, several rounds.

**Round 1** rejected the original design (removing the eviction outright):
block hashes exclude the weight version and weight updates do not reset
connectors, so that eviction is what prevents stale KV — hence the opt-out. It
then found a P1 in the Rust client, which sent three positional arguments
unconditionally and broke `/pause` and `/sleep` against an older engine.

**A later round found a P1 that this revision fixes, and it is the reason the
connector file is in this diff.** Keeping the tier crashed the very case the
feature exists for:

```
sleep(level=1, mode="keep", clear_connector_cache=False) -> wake_up()
AssertionError at offloading/scheduler.py:1792
```

`_reset_caches` preempts the running requests, and `preempted_req_ids` is only
consumed by the *next* `schedule()`. Nothing is scheduled while the engine
sleeps, so that set survives the sleep and lands on the step that resumes the
request — and with the tier kept, that step already carries the request's
resume **load**. The preemption flush asserted that a preempted request can
only hold stores, which is true when preemption and resumption are separate
steps, and false here.

The flush now takes the store jobs and leaves the load alone: a load reads no
freed block, so it is not what the flush is there to settle. Default clearing
never reached this, because with the tier gone there is no load to find —
which is also why the completed-request measurement above could not have
caught it. `test_preempted_request_resumed_in_the_same_step` covers both
scheduling modes and fails on the previous revision.

### The opt-out is now refused where it is not safe

The flag reaches whatever connector is configured, and the same-step resume is
a state every connector that tracks per-request transfers has to expect. Only
`OffloadingConnector` does, after the fix above. `MooncakeStoreConnector` also
implements `reset_cache`, also consumes `preempted_req_ids`, and pops
`load_specs[req_id]` and `_unfinished_requests[req_id]` for them
(`mooncake/store/scheduler.py:226-231`) — the entries its new-request loop
then asserts on four lines later.

Rather than change a second connector I cannot exercise here, the opt-out is
fail-closed: connectors declare `supports_retained_cache_on_pause` (default
`False`, `True` on `OffloadingConnector`, the conjunction of its children on
`MultiConnector`), and a pause that asks to keep a cache the connector cannot
keep is refused before anything is paused:

```
MooncakeStoreConnector cannot keep its cache across a pause: the resume lands
in the step that reports the pause's preemptions, which this connector does
not expect. Drop clear_connector_cache=False.
```

Making Mooncake handle it is a separate, testable change; until then its users
get an error at the call instead of a crash at the wake-up.

Two related notes:

- This is the same interaction as #52360 (preemption vs in-flight transfers).
  This PR does not change the flush for stores, which is what protects against
  it. It does extend how long a bad entry would survive if a connector ever
  produced one, which is an argument for the default being "evict".
- Follow-up worth filing separately: nothing on the weight-update path
  force-evicts the tier. `finish_weight_update` doing so would remove the
  footgun at no false-positive cost.

The same round also asked for, and this revision adds, the `/pause` opt-out
wire test, a `sleep(level>=1)` threading test, the one-line note on why the
Python client may always send the argument (client and engine ship together,
so they cannot disagree), and the parameter's documentation on
`EngineCoreProc.pause_scheduler`, which is the docstring MP clients read.

A further round, told about all of the above, checked for any path where the
flag defaults to `False` by accident, the reverse gRPC skew (old frontend, new
engine), whether the typed bool query parameter changes the accepted request
format (`False`/`false`/`1`/`0`), and whether the deferred
`engine_idle_callback` closure can run with a flag a later pause changed. No
defects.

## AI assistance

Developed with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed every changed line, ran the
tests above, and I am the accountable submitter.

title: [KV Offload] Let unfinished requests keep the chunks they will resume from
body:
## Summary

An offloaded chunk becomes evictable the moment its store completes, so the
prefix an *unfinished* request will resume from competes with everything else on
recency alone.

That is fine for serving, where a request either runs to completion or is
preempted and recomputed. It is not fine for a colocated RL rollout: generation
is paused for a weight update, the frozen requests touch nothing, they become
the LRU victims, and on resume they pay a full re-prefill even though their
blocks were already sitting in the CPU tier.

This adds `pin_in_flight_chunks` (default **off**) to the CPU offloading
manager. When enabled it refcounts the chunks observed by unfinished requests
and prefers evicting everything else; the refcount is released at request
finalization.

```
"kv_connector_extra_config": {"pin_in_flight_chunks": true}
```

## It cannot wedge the cache

Pinning is a preference, not a guarantee. If eviction cannot be satisfied
without touching pinned chunks, the manager retries with the original protected
set, so a cache holding nothing but in-flight chunks still admits new stores.
That fallback is covered by a test.

## Relationship to #50422

#50422 (`Session Aware Eviction Policy`) adds a new `CachePolicy` that groups a
session's blocks and evicts session-worst-first, tail-first, so a shared prefix
outlives its suffix. It orders eviction *within* the cache; it does not
distinguish a request that is still running from one that finished.

This PR is orthogonal and policy-agnostic: it is a lifetime signal in the
manager (`in flight` vs `finished`) that applies to `lru`, `arc`, a custom
policy, and to SAE if it lands. The two compose — SAE would still choose which
chunk dies first among the unpinned ones.

## Not a duplicate

Also checked: #50014 (protects unread *promotions* from speculative promotion
thrash — a different lifetime, inside the tiering path), #54327 (bounded
capacity for the filesystem tier), #38984 (SLRU policy). None of them expresses
"this request has not finished yet".

## Test plan

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu -q
# 161 passed, 1 skipped
# (test_swap_blocks_batch.py::test_swap_blocks_batch_default_stream fails on this
#  box with cuMemcpyBatchAsync error 1 — a CUDA kernel test, unrelated to this
#  change, on a node whose GPUs are fully allocated to another job)
```

Two new tests:

- `test_unfinished_request_chunks_survive_eviction` — an unfinished request's
  chunk survives while a finished request's chunk is evicted instead.
- `test_pinning_falls_back_when_every_chunk_is_in_flight` — a fully pinned cache
  still admits a new store.

Lint:

```
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/manager.py vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/spec.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md
# all passed
```

No model-quality impact: eviction ordering only; no change to what is computed.

## AI assistance

Developed with AI assistance (Claude). The motivation comes from the
DeepSeek-V4.1 tech report §5.2.3, which requires exactly this lifetime rule for
async RL — in-flight rollout states are retained and released per sample as each
one completes. I reviewed every changed line, ran the tests above, and I am the
accountable submitter.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


## Review rounds

A later adversarial round, told about the fixes already made (distinct-key scan
budget, ARC's carried `virtual_t1_size`, the capability flag replacing
signature sniffing, the two-argument call for out-of-tree policies, and the
keyword-only constructor argument) and asked for new defects, found two gaps in
what the pin actually covers.

**Fixed: a chunk still being stored was pinned only by its writer.**
`prepare_store` sorted an offered key into "not resident" or "resident and
ready". A chunk another request is *mid-store* on is neither, so it was never
recorded, and the pin counted only the writer. Two rollouts sharing a prefix —
the case this PR exists for — therefore lost the chunk the moment the writer
finished, while the reader was still unfinished. Reproduced in review and now
covered by `test_a_chunk_still_being_stored_is_pinned_by_its_second_reader`
on both policies.

The fix keeps the pin separate from cache-access accounting: pending chunks are
pinned through a new `_pin()` helper and tracked in `state.pinned_keys`, so
they do not enter `key_groups` or the reuse counters and nothing about policy
adaptation changes.

**Known limitation: a mixed GPU/CPU prefix hit does not pin the GPU-hit part.**
When part of the prefix is already in the GPU cache, the scheduler loads only
the suffix but advances `next_stored_chunk_idx` past the whole prefix
(`offloading/scheduler.py:1134`, `:1180`), so the manager never observes the
GPU-hit chunks and their CPU copies stay ordinary eviction candidates. If the
request is later preempted and those GPU blocks are lost, CPU prefix lookup
stops at the first missing chunk (`:700`), which costs the pinned suffix too.
Closing this means changing what the scheduler reports to the manager, which is
a different component's contract; this PR keeps the manager-side change and I
would rather do that separately than widen this one.

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/ -q
177 passed, 1 skipped
```

(`test_swap_blocks_batch_default_stream` fails identically on an unmodified
tree in my environment and is unrelated.)

When calling the `/tokenize` endpoint with chat conversations containing assistant messages with `content: None` and `tool_calls` (standard in multi-turn tool-calling formats like DeepSeek V4.1 or OpenAI schemas), Pydantic v2 wraps the `tool_calls` iterable in a `ValidatorIterator` during union type validation of `ChatCompletionMessageParam`.

title: [Bugfix][Determinism] Refuse batch-invariant mode on the sparse indexer
body:
## Summary

`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` looks like it works on DSA / sparse-indexer models. It
does not: the indexer's top-k has no batch-invariant backend, so which keys a
row attends to can change with the rest of the batch.

Every path is batch-dependent:

| backend | what makes it batch-dependent |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` | switches kernels at `AUTO_COOPERATIVE_MAX_ROWS` (64) rows — `indexer_topk.py:_resolve_auto` |
| `per_row` | picks among three algorithms from the **padded column count**, i.e. the batch's longest sequence (`sampler.cu`, `kSortingAlgorithmThreshold` / `kSplitWorkThreshold`); on gfx950 it also splits a row across blocks by row count |
| `persistent` | sizes its cooperative launch from occupancy and the batch's max sequence length, and falls back to `per_row` when the launch does not fit (`topk.cu`) |
| `cooperative` | only applicable under the 64-row cap, so it is by definition batch-conditional |

None of this changes the logits. It changes tie-breaking and therefore the
selection — and a different sparse selection is a different forward pass, not a
rounding difference.

The failure mode is silent: output drifts with concurrency instead of raising,
which is exactly what #53257 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash non-deterministic at
temperature=0, rate scales with concurrency) and #54521 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
greedy decoding non-deterministic from `persistent_topk`) describe.

This PR refuses at construction, naming the batch-dependent inputs, instead of
serving results the flag promises are batch-invariant.

## Why this matters beyond a debug flag

The GLM-5 tech report attributes an RL training collapse to exactly this class
of mismatch: a non-deterministic sparse selection "caused drastic performance
degradation during RL after only a few steps, accompanied by a sharp drop in
entropy." Rollout/training mismatch in sparse selection is not cosmetic, and a
flag that claims to eliminate it while not doing so is worse than no flag.

## Not a duplicate

- #55122 (`[Kernel] Make persistent_topk deterministic`) makes **one kernel**
  deterministic for a fixed launch. Complementary and necessary — but batch
  invariance also requires the *dispatch* not to change with the batch, which is
  what this PR is about. With #55122 merged, a row still takes a different
  kernel at 64 rows and a different algorithm when another request lengthens the
  padded width.
- #55958 (`Refuse batch-invariant mode on unsupported platforms`) applies the
  same philosophy at the platform level; this is the sparse-indexer case.
- #57129, #57109, #56084, #56258 add or gate indexer top-k backends; none of
  them is about batch invariance.

## Alternative considered

Pinning `auto` to a single backend under the flag. Rejected: it would still not
be batch-invariant, because `per_row`'s algorithm choice follows the padded
column count, so the guarantee would still be false — just harder to notice.
Making one backend genuinely invariant (fixed algorithm, batch-independent
padding) is kernel work and belongs in a separate change.

## Test plan

```
pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_indexer_topk_batch_invariance.py -q
# 5 passed
```

CPU-only; no GPU needed. Covers all four backend spellings refusing under the
flag, and unchanged construction without it.

```
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/indexer_topk.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_indexer_topk_batch_invariance.py
# passed
```

No model-quality impact: the only behavior change is an explicit failure in a
configuration that was already producing results the flag says it does not
produce.

## AI assistance

Developed with AI assistance (Claude). The batch-dependence claims above were
each traced to the specific dispatch code, not inferred. I reviewed every
changed line, ran the tests above, and I am the accountable submitter.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)



## Review rounds

A later adversarial round, told about the fixes already made and asked for new
defects, found two that the current revision addresses. Both are about the
reference backend's selection, not about pinning it:

- **P1 — `topk` does not pin tie order.** `torch.topk` documents that the
  order of equal values "is not guaranteed to be stable and may vary across
  different invocations", and the CUDA implementation dispatches differently by
  row count. A filtered row is nothing *but* ties, so selecting with `topk`
  left the very property this PR is pinning the backend for undefined.
- **P2 — a short row could lose one of its own tokens.** With the row shorter
  than the budget, an in-row `-inf` column tied with the padding and could lose
  to it. Both kernels emit `0..seq_len-1` in that case
  (`cooperative_topk.cuh:495`, `persistent_topk.cuh:934`), so the reference was
  dropping a token the kernels return, and `sparse_utils.py` treats the
  resulting `-1` as absent — a different attended set, not just a different
  order.

Both come from the same root: expressing the selection through float sentinels.
The revision drops that and orders by **(in row, score, column index)**
directly — a stable sort by score, then a stable sort that lifts the row's own
columns above the padding they tie with. Nothing rewrites a score any more, so
the previous revision's floor-clamp special case is gone too, and a genuine
score sitting at `finfo.min` keeps its rank (`test_a_filtered_column_never_outranks_a_real_score`).

Three tests cover the new contract: `test_padding_columns_never_fill_the_tail_of_a_short_row`
(replacing an assertion that encoded the P2 bug), `test_a_filtered_column_beats_padding_in_a_short_row`,
and `test_tied_scores_resolve_the_same_way_in_every_batch`.

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_indexer_topk_batch_invariance.py -q
17 passed
```

title: [Bugfix][DeepSeek V4] Name the config field a checkpoint is missing
body:
## Summary

`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/**` reads six fields straight off the config object
while building layers, with no default anywhere in the stack:

```python
self.n_groups = config.o_groups                       # attention.py:212
self.topk_tokens = config.index_topk                  # attention.py:928
self.hc_mult = config.hc_mult                         # amd/model.py:724 (+20 more)
self.swiglu_limit = config.swiglu_limit               # amd/model.py:535
is_hash_moe = ... < config.num_hash_layers            # amd/model.py:553
```

A checkpoint whose `config.json` omits one of them fails deep inside layer
construction with:

```
AttributeError: 'DeepseekV4Config' object has no attribute 'o_groups'
```

which names the attribute but not the file it belongs in. This PR raises from
the config classes instead, naming `config.json` and the full required set.

## Why not defaults

Because a default would be a guess at the model's shape. `index_topk` sets the
sparse selection size, `compress_ratios` the per-layer cache type, `o_groups`
the o-proj grouping — a wrong value builds a model that does not match the
weights and fails later, or worse, silently produces bad output. An explicit
error is the correct behaviour for a checkpoint that does not say.

## Cost

The hook is `__getattr__`, which Python only calls when normal lookup fails, so
a complete checkpoint pays nothing and behaves exactly as before. Unrelated
missing attributes keep raising a plain `AttributeError(name)`, so `copy`,
`to_dict` and the transformers machinery are unaffected — covered by a test.

title: [Bugfix][DeepSeek V4.1] Keep the vision tower across a config round-trip
body:
## Summary

`DeepseekV41Config` flattens the nested `vision_config` onto itself, but
`to_dict()` emits only the flat names — there is no `vision_config` in the dict.
Rebuilding a config from its own dict therefore arrives with the flat fields
already set by `PretrainedConfig.__init__` and nothing nested, and the vision
block overwrote them from an empty dict:

```python
c = DeepseekV41Config(vision_config={"num_hidden_layers": 3, "hidden_size": 2048})
r = DeepseekV41Config.from_dict(c.to_dict())

(c.vision_n_layers, c.vision_dim)   # (3, 2048)
(r.vision_n_layers, r.vision_dim)   # (0, 1024)   <- text-only defaults
```

`vision_n_layers == 0` is how the rest of the stack asks "is this text-only",
so anything that serializes a config and rebuilds it silently turned a
multimodal checkpoint into a text model.

## Fix

Take each vision field from the nested block when it is there; otherwise keep
what is already on the config, and only then fall back to the default. Nested
input still wins, and a genuinely text-only config still gets the defaults.

## Not a duplicate

`gh pr list --search "DeepseekV41Config vision"` is empty; no open PR or issue
touches the V4.1 config flattening.

## Test plan

```
pytest tests/transformers_utils/test_deepseek_v41_config_roundtrip.py -q
# 6 passed
```

CPU-only. Covers the round-trip across six vision fields, nested input still
taking precedence, and the text-only defaults being unchanged.

```
pre-commit run --files vllm/transformers_utils/configs/deepseek_v41.py \
  tests/transformers_utils/test_deepseek_v41_config_roundtrip.py
# passed
```

No model-quality impact for configs that are built once from a checkpoint; for
configs that get serialized, this restores the vision tower that was being
dropped.

## AI assistance

Developed with AI assistance (Claude). This one surfaced during an adversarial
review of a different config change, which flagged the round-trip as a
pre-existing bug; I reproduced it on `origin/main` before writing the fix. I
reviewed every changed line, ran the tests above, and I am the accountable
submitter.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


## Review rounds

A later adversarial round, told about the fix above and asked for new defects,
checked round-trip fidelity through `to_dict`/`to_diff_dict`/JSON, coverage of
the published checkpoint's `config.json`, flat-vs-nested precedence on
disagreement, whether each default matches what the model assumes when the
field is absent, the interaction with #57818's missing-field error, and shared
mutable defaults. It executed the round-trips: all 10 vision fields survive
dict, diff-dict and JSON, explicit values win over nested ones, and no default
is shared across instances. No new defects.

title: [Bugfix][DeepSeek V4] Say why every MXFP4 MoE backend was rejected
body:
## Summary

Trying to start DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` on a GB200,
every worker died with exactly this and nothing else:

```
NotImplementedError: No MXFP4 MoE backend supports the deployment configuration.
```

The generic MXFP4 selector in the same file raises with the diagnosis attached:

```python
raise NotImplementedError(
    "No MXFP4 MoE backend supports the deployment configuration. "
    f"weight_key=kMxfp4Static, activation_key={activation_key}. "
    f"Candidate backends were: {[b.value for b in AVAILABLE_BACKENDS]}. "
    f"Unsupported reasons: {unsupported_log}. "
)
```

`select_deepseek_v4_mxfp4_moe_backend` collects the same per-backend reasons,
logs them at `debug_once`, and then throws them away. So on the models most
likely to land in an unusual configuration, the failure says the least.

In my case the reason was the batch-invariance gate in
`modular_kernel.is_supported_config` (`envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT and not
cls._supports_batch_invariance()`), which I could only find by reading the
source. With this PR the error says it.

## Change

Collect the rejection reasons in the DeepSeek-V4 path and include them in the
error, with the wording the generic path already uses.

## Not a duplicate

`gh pr list --search "mxfp4 backend selection error"` returns backend *additions*
and unrelated fixes (#55232, #54032, #55275, #54109); none of them touches the
error path.

## Test plan

```

pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_b12x.py -q -k deepseek           # 3 passed
```

  tests/kernels/moe/test_dsv4_mxfp4_backend_error.py

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Say what to do about mixed KV block sizes
body:
## Summary

Issue #48919: DeepSeek-V4-Pro with DSpark speculative decoding and
`--block-size 256` crashes every worker during connector init with

```
AssertionError: If 'block_size' is specified in kv_connector_extra_config,
there must be at least one KV cache group, and all groups must have the
same block size.
```

`--block-size 128` happens to work, which tells an operator nothing about why.

`block_size` in `kv_connector_extra_config` sizes one offload chunk **in
tokens**, so it is converted once, against a single block size. A model whose
offloaded groups have different block sizes makes that conversion ambiguous —
and speculative decoding's draft group is the usual reason a second block size
shows up.

This PR raises with the sizes, the groups they belong to, and the parameter that
does not have the ambiguity:

```
'block_size'=64 in kv_connector_extra_config sizes one offload chunk in tokens,
which needs every offloaded KV cache group to share a block size. This model's
offloaded groups have [16, 32] tokens per block (group ids [0, 1]). Set
'blocks_per_chunk' instead to size the chunk in blocks.
```

The neighbouring not-a-multiple error already points at `blocks_per_chunk`; this
makes the two consistent.

## What this does not do

It does not make mixed block sizes work with a token-sized chunk, and it does
not exclude draft groups from offloading the way the issue suggests — they *are*
offloaded (`offloading/scheduler.py` gives them their own `is_eagle_block_drop`
and partial-tail handling), so excluding them from the block-size check while
still chunking them would be wrong. `blocks_per_chunk` is the supported way to
express this today, and now the error says so.

## Not a duplicate

`gh pr list --search "48919 in:body"` is empty, as is a search for the assert
text. #50653 (referenced from #50821) is about PP-inconsistent `num_cpu_blocks`,
a different failure.

## Test plan

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py -q
# 60 passed
```

CPU-only. Two new tests: a config with 16- and 32-token groups plus a
token-sized `block_size` raises an error naming `[16, 32]` and
`blocks_per_chunk`; and the same config with `blocks_per_chunk` set builds
successfully — so the message points somewhere that actually works.

```
pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/config.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py
# passed
```

No behaviour change: the same configurations are accepted and rejected, and no
model-quality impact.

## AI assistance

Developed with AI assistance (Claude). I read the offloading scheduler's draft-
group handling before deciding not to implement the issue's suggested fix, and
say so above. I reviewed every changed line, ran the tests, and I am the
accountable submitter.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


## Review rounds

An adversarial automated review was run over this diff against `origin/main`:
the span arithmetic per group type, the DCP scaling claim, whether the remedy
selection can recommend one that does not work, the `assert` -> `ValueError`
control-flow change, and the message for a plain single-group setup. It found
no defects.

One behaviour change worth stating explicitly: under `python -O` the old
`assert` was stripped, so a mixed-block-size configuration silently picked an
arbitrary member of the set. It now raises. That enforces an invariant the code
already relied on rather than adding a new restriction.

title: [Bug]: minimax_m2 / glm47_moe / deepseek_v4 arg converters drop the last parameter when the model omits the closing tag (same class as #57699)
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM main (probed 2026-09-20; minimax_m2.py @ 24bfbd5d, deepseek_v4.py @ 39e33db7)
- Parser-only bug: reproduction needs no GPU, no model, no server.

### Describe the bug

#57699 describes a bug class for qwen3: when the model closes the tool call **without closing the last parameter tag**, the trailing value is dropped by the final (partial=False) conversion. #57707 fixes qwen3 only - but the same structure exists in three other converters, none of which are covered by that PR:

**1. minimax_m2 - vllm/parser/minimax_m2.py `_minimax_m2_arg_converter`**

`_PARAM_RE` only ends a value at the closing parameter tag or at the next parameter open tag. The trailing `_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE` extraction runs only under `if partial:`, so the final conversion drops the last parameter. With `stream_arg_deltas=True`, the streamed partial conversions have already emitted the value, and the flush at tool-call end produces a shorter JSON - the same client-visible divergence as #57699.

Model output:

```
<minimax:tool_call><invoke name="get_weather">
<parameter name="city">Seattle</parameter>
<parameter name="unit">celsius
</invoke></minimax:tool_call>
```

non-streaming: `arguments == {"city": "Seattle"}` - `unit` is silently lost.

**2. glm47_moe - vllm/parser/glm47_moe.py `_glm47_arg_converter`**

`_ARG_RE` requires the value close tag; the `_PARTIAL_ARG_RE` extraction is under `if partial:`. `stream_arg_deltas=True` is set. Same divergence: a tool call that omits the last closing arg_value tag yields non-streaming `arguments` without the trailing parameter.

**3. deepseek_v4 (inherited by v32/v41) - vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py `_dsml_arg_converter`**

Same `if partial:` structure. Additionally, the partial branch swallows JSON failures with `contextlib.suppress` and **drops the value entirely**, while the complete branch falls back to the literal text. So a trailing `string="false"` parameter whose partial value is not yet valid JSON is discarded even mid-stream.

### Reproduction (CPU only)

```python
from vllm.parser.minimax_m2 import _minimax_m2_arg_converter

raw = '<parameter name="city">Seattle</parameter>\n<parameter name="unit">celsius\n'
print(_minimax_m2_arg_converter(raw, partial=True))   # {"city": "Seattle", "unit": "celsius\n"}
print(_minimax_m2_arg_converter(raw, partial=False))  # {"city": "Seattle"}  <- unit dropped
```

Equivalent direct calls to `_glm47_arg_converter` (glm47_moe) and `_dsml_arg_converter` (deepseek_v4) show the same drop.

### Expected behavior

Mirror the qwen3 fix (#57707): the trailing-partial extraction should also run in the final conversion, so a properly closed tool call keeps its last parameter value. For deepseek_v4, the partial branch should also fall back to the literal text like the complete branch does.

I can send PRs (one per parser, following the fix shape of #57707) with regression tests mirroring TestUnclosedLastParameter in tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3.py.

title: [ROCm][Model][MiniMax-M3] Context-parallel sparse lightning indexer (Triton, opt-in)
body:
## Purpose

Adds **context-parallel decode scoring** for MiniMax-M3's sparse lightning indexer on ROCm (TP>1, bf16 index cache, opt-in via `--attention-config '{"minimax_m3_indexer_cp": true}'`).

### Problem

MiniMax-M3 selects a sparse set of KV blocks per query token with a lightweight indexer that scores every block in the request's context. Index heads shard like KV heads (`sparse_num_index_heads == num_key_value_heads == 4`), and the index-K cache is a single shared head replicated on every rank. So with TP>1 every rank streams the whole index cache — the same `seq_len/128` blocks — once per decode step, just to score its own head(s). That read is duplicated `world_size` times and at long context and large decode batches it is a large term in the step.

### Solution

Shard the **blocks** instead of duplicating the read. Because each rank owns different index heads, every rank has to score every head on its shard:

1. All-gather the index queries — `heads * 128` bf16 per token (1 KB at M3's 4 heads).
2. Each rank scores **all global heads** on its `1/world_size` round-robin block shard (`block = local * world + rank`).
3. For each head, take the local top-k of the **full** `k` over the shard, pack each candidate into one int64 `(score, global block id)` key, and all-gather the keys — `P * heads * k * 8` bytes per token, independent of context length.
4. Merge per global head, keeping only the heads this rank owns.

Index-cache traffic per rank drops to `1/P`; scoring compute per rank is unchanged (`heads` heads over `1/P` of the blocks). The merge is exact: for a given head, a block in that head's global top-k is necessarily in its own shard's top-k for the same head. Forced init/sink and sliding-window blocks are pinned on both the shard and the merge.

**Default: OFF** (`AttentionConfig.minimax_m3_indexer_cp = False`); nothing enables it automatically. Turning it on is a startup error unless the index cache is bf16 (`indexer_kv_dtype` "auto" or "bf16") — the score kernel reads the cache without a scale; the fp8 path is #57909 — and when the fused decode path (#59653) is also enabled, since that kernel computes indexer top-k itself. It is also a startup error on non-ROCm platforms or with `tensor_parallel_size == 1`.

**When to enable:** long-context workloads. CP adds a fixed per-layer cost (two small all-gathers, scoring every index head, the merge), so it slows decode on short contexts and speeds it up on long ones. On MI350X at TP=4 (`vllm bench serve`, OSL 1024), mean TPOT changes by +15% / +7% at 4k ISL (concurrency 8 / 32), breaks even around 64k / 32k, and improves by 9% / 16–27% at 128k. TTFT is unaffected. Agentic traces (AgentX, ISL ~74k) fall on the winning side.

### CUDA graph capture

Two properties are required for CP to work under `cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY`.

**CP must be what gets captured.** vLLM v2 records FULL decode graphs with `cudagraph_runtime_mode=NONE` (see `ModelCudaGraphManager.capture`), so a `CUDAGraphMode.FULL` guard never fires. Guarding on `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()` would record the **non-CP** indexer into the decode graph that is then replayed. The only guard is `torch.compiler.is_compiling()`, because Dynamo tracing cannot capture the collectives. Persistent buffers (in `IndexerCPDecode`) keep the decode path allocation-free so CP is what gets captured.

**Kernel shapes must be capture-stable.** Capture goes through `_dummy_run`, which sets `seq_lens = max_query_len`. Shapes derived from the batch's `max_seq_len` would specialize a one-block context into every decode graph. All kernel shapes come from `max_model_len`, and block counts and strides are runtime arguments rather than `tl.constexpr`. `test_indexer_context_scores_independent_of_shape_bound` asserts scores are identical whether the grid is sized for the batch or for a bound 8x larger.

`--enforce-eager` is not required.

### MiniMax-M3 sparse attention pipeline

| Stage | Backend | Index cache dtype | When selected |
|---|---|---|---|
| Indexer | **Triton** (this PR) | `bf16` | `indexer_kv_dtype=bf16`; no AITER dependency |
| Indexer | AITER (#57909) | `fp8_e4m3` | `indexer_kv_dtype=fp8` |
| Attention | **AITER_SPARSE_PA** | — | `SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1` + `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` |
| Attention | Triton | — | Fallback when AITER unavailable |

## Changes

| File | Type |
|---|---|
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/indexer_context_parallel.py` | New — `IndexerCPDecode` (Q all-gather, per-head score/exchange/merge) and `MiniMaxM3IndexerTritonCPImpl` |
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/ops/indexer_context_parallel.py` | New — Triton `_context_score` shard kernel (bf16 cache only) |
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/ops/indexer_cp_exchange.py` | New — packed-key local top-k, all-gather (AITER IPC, RCCL fallback), per-head merge |
| `vllm/config/attention.py` | Modified — `minimax_m3_indexer_cp: bool = False`; rejects non-bf16 index caches and fused decode at startup |
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/common/indexer.py` | Modified — CP dispatch in `select_indexer_impl_cls` (ROCm, TP>1) |
| `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_indexer_cp.py` | New — shard scores, capture-shape invariance, per-head top-k merge (1 and 4 heads), head ownership |
| `tests/distributed/test_minimax_m3_indexer_cp_tp.py` | New — multi-GPU CP vs non-CP top-k per global head |
| `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` | Runs the multi-GPU test in the AMD 4-GPU distributed job |

With `minimax_m3_indexer_cp` unset (the default) no existing code path changes.

## Test Plan

### Hardware and image
8x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950). `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-92044241a02f05de51420d654daf669de20b4691` with this PR's files applied on top of that exact commit.

### Correctness
```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_indexer_cp.py -v
pytest tests/distributed/test_minimax_m3_indexer_cp_tp.py -v
```
The distributed test runs the production CP decode across real TP ranks and compares each rank's top-k with the non-CP decode kernel (`minimax_m3_index_decode`) on the full context, **per global index head**, using M3's config (4 heads, top-16, init 0, local 1) on 32k–82k token contexts. It is parametrized over TP 2/4/8 (TP=8 covers head replication), `query_len` 1/4 (spec-decode verify), and RCCL vs AITER IPC all-gather. It also asserts the four heads select different blocks on ≥90% of rows, so a merge that mixed heads would fail.

Contexts are deliberately long: at top-16 x 128-token blocks plus a forced local block, any prompt under ~2k tokens selects every block, so short-context evals cannot detect a wrong selection.

### Server (MXFP4 weights, Triton bf16 indexer)
Baseline is the same command without `"minimax_m3_indexer_cp":true`.
```
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1
export VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_CAST_BF16_TO_FP16=0
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION_MIN_SIZE_KB=256

vllm serve /model/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 \
  --served-model-name amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --port 8779 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --trust-remote-code \
  --block-size 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 65536 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --language-model-only --enable-prefix-caching \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN --moe-backend aiter \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"bf16","minimax_m3_indexer_cp":true}' \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"thinking_mode":"enabled"}' --stream-interval 20 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
```

### AgentX benchmark
```
aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp \
  --url http://localhost:8779 --endpoint-type chat \
  --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126_256k \
  --concurrency 32 --benchmark-duration 900 \
  --streaming --use-server-token-count \
  --trajectory-start-min-ratio 0.0 --trajectory-start-max-ratio 0.0 \
  --model amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --tokenizer /model/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 \
  --tokenizer-trust-remote-code --apply-chat-template
```
aiperf 0.12.0, 900 s per point after a 90 s warmup.

## Test Result

### Correctness
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_indexer_cp.py`: 16 passed (including config validation).
- Server started with only `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"bf16","minimax_m3_indexer_cp":true}'` selects the CP indexer; the same flag with `"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"` exits at startup with the bf16 error.
- `tests/distributed/test_minimax_m3_indexer_cp_tp.py`: 12 passed (TP 2/4/8 x `query_len` 1/4 x RCCL/AITER).

### AgentX sweep (MXFP4, TP=4, no speculative decoding)

Same node, same image, same PR code in both arms; only the CP switch differs. (These runs used the earlier environment-variable switch; it has since moved to `attention_config.minimax_m3_indexer_cp` with no change to the CP code path.) CP ran first, baseline second, then CP conc=15 was repeated on a fresh server. Every point has 0 failed requests.

| Concurrency | Baseline (tok/s/GPU) | CP (tok/s/GPU) | Throughput | Requests | ITL baseline → CP (ms) | ISL baseline | ISL CP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15 | 12,652 | 12,997 | +2.7% | +1.6% | 16.2 → 14.7 (−9.5%) | 73,900 | 74,737 |
| 15 (repeat) | 12,652 | 13,320 | +5.3% | +3.3% | 16.2 → 13.8 (−14.9%) | 73,900 | 75,319 |
| 20 | 15,245 | 15,957 | +4.7% | +3.9% | 19.3 → 16.9 (−12.2%) | 75,343 | 75,935 |
| 24 | 15,385 | 17,115 | **+11.2%** | +7.7% | 22.7 → 19.7 (−12.9%) | 74,606 | 76,245 |
| 32 | 20,125 | 23,175 | **+15.2%** | +14.4% | 37.6 → 28.6 (−23.9%) | 73,741 | 74,232 |

The gain grows with decode batch size, as expected when the term being divided by `P` is per-sequence index-cache traffic. At concurrency 15 the throughput delta is about the size of run-to-run variation (baseline conc=15 measured 12,936 and 12,652 in two passes); ITL improves at every point. ISL is within 3% across arms with CP's the higher, so the delta is not a shorter-trajectory artifact.

One earlier pass on the same node was discarded: its baseline engine (CP off) exited partway through conc=32 (42% failed requests), and its CP conc=15 point ran at half speed with no errors. Neither reproduced in the pass above, which also logs both servers in full.

**Withdrawn:** the previous version of this PR scored only each rank's own index head on its shard and merged across ranks, which mixes different heads' candidates at TP=4. The AgentX, EAGLE3 and GSM8K results previously reported here were measured on that code and are removed. EAGLE3 has not been re-measured. GSM8K is not repeated because it cannot distinguish a correct selection from a wrong one at its context lengths (see Test Plan); the per-head equivalence test replaces it.

**Hardware note:** these are MI355X numbers; absolute tok/s/GPU is not comparable to the MI350X figures in earlier revisions. Every comparison is baseline vs CP on the same node.

## AI assistance

This PR was developed with AI assistance, including the per-head CP design, the CUDA-graph capture analysis, the multi-GPU equivalence test, and running the benchmarks above on our hardware, and was prepared with assistance from [PR Pundit](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/pr-pundit). I have reviewed every changed line and the results.

This does not duplicate #57909, which implements indexer CP for the **AITER fp8** path (`indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`). This PR covers the **Triton bf16** path. The two select different `MiniMaxM3Indexer` implementations and do not overlap in code.

## Related
- #57909 — CP indexer for the AITER fp8 path.
- #59653 — fused sparse-layer decode; CP is refused when it is enabled.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Materialize tool calls in tokenize requests
body:
## Summary

Fixes `/tokenize` request validation for assistant messages containing
`content: null` and `tool_calls`.

`TokenizeChatRequest` could leave `tool_calls` as a Pydantic
`ValidatorIterator` after validation. Downstream tokenizers such as DeepSeek V4
deep-copy the message list, which fails because `ValidatorIterator` is not
pickleable.

This change materializes non-list `tool_calls` after validation, matching the
existing behavior in `ChatCompletionRequest`.

## Testing

Added regression coverage for an assistant message with `content=None` and
`tool_calls`.

Verified that:

- `tool_calls` is materialized as a `list`
- `deepcopy(request.messages)` succeeds
- existing tool-call serialization tests pass
- tokenize serving tests pass
- pre-commit checks pass

## AI assistance

ChatGPT was used to help investigate the issue, compare the existing
`ChatCompletionRequest` behavior, and assist with drafting the regression test
and validator change. I reviewed the changed lines and validated the behavior
locally.

Fixes #57730

title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Keep trailing parameters in minimax_m2, glm47 and deepseek_v4 conversions
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57827. Fixes #57826 (same report, filed twice).

Same bug class as #57699 / #57707 (qwen3): when the model closes a tool call without closing the last parameter tag, the trailing value must survive the final (non-partial) conversion too. #57707 covered qwen3 only; this PR covers the three other converters the report names, on current `main`'s `vllm/tool_parsers/` layout:

- `minimax_m2_tool_parser._parse_single_invoke`: after the complete-tag loop, pick up one unclosed trailing `<parameter>` with the same newline trimming and `_convert_param_value_with_types` conversion.
- `glm4_moe_tool_parser.extract_tool_calls` (the shared parent of `glm47_moe`): after the `func_arg_regex` pairs, pick up one unclosed trailing `<arg_value>` with the same `_is_string_type`/`_deserialize` path. glm4 and glm47 both benefit.
- `deepseekv32_tool_parser._parse_invoke_params`: pick up one unclosed trailing `<｜DSML｜parameter>`.

Each parser gets regression tests for the unclosed tail plus a fully-closed control proving no double-counting.

## Not a duplicate

- #57707 (mine, open) is qwen3-only; the issue explicitly calls out that minimax_m2 / glm47_moe / deepseek_v4 are not covered by it. `gh pr list --search "57827"` and `--search "tool parser trailing parameter"` show no open PR for the other three converters.
- No changes to the streaming flush behavior; non-streaming extraction only.

## Test plan

Parser-only, no GPU or model needed. On `origin/main` the three repro shapes each drop the trailing parameter (`{'city': 'Seattle'}`); with the fix each returns `{'city': 'Seattle', 'unit': 'celsius'}`.

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tool_use/test_minimax_m2_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_glm4_moe_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py -q
# 31 passed
```

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on the touched files (the pre-commit hook bootstrap could not download `typos` offline, so hooks were run directly; no unrelated lines reformatted).

No model eval: the change is parser-level error handling on malformed tail tags and does not alter behavior for well-formed outputs (the fully-closed control tests assert byte-level parity).

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Kimi Code); the human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [ROCm][Model][MiniMax-M3] Context-parallel AITER sparse indexer (fp8, opt-in)
body:
## Purpose

Adds **context-parallel decode scoring** for the AITER fp8 indexer on ROCm (gfx950, fp8 index cache, TP>1, opt-in via `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP=1`).

Same distributed algorithm as #57832 (Triton bf16 path), adapted for the AITER kernel interface:
- Each rank scores its 1/world_size shard of KV blocks via `pa_sparse_block_score_decode` with a shard block table
- Scores scattered into global-shape `[heads, tokens, max_block]` tensor pre-filled with `-inf`
- MAX allreduce reconstructs all positions from their owning rank
- `pa_sparse_block_topk` runs on the complete allreduced scores

**Default: OFF** (`VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP=False`). Same env var as #57832. AITER path selected when fp8 index cache + gfx950 + TP>1. The per-step allreduce adds latency that only pays off at moderate-to-high concurrency and mid-range context (10k–90k ISL).

### MiniMax-M3 sparse attention pipeline

| Stage | Backend | Index cache dtype | When selected |
|---|---|---|---|
| Indexer | Triton (#57832) | `bf16` | `indexer_kv_dtype=bf16` — default |
| Indexer | **AITER** (this PR) | `fp8_e4m3` | `indexer_kv_dtype=fp8` — requires AITER sparse PA |
| Attention | **AITER_SPARSE_PA** | — | `SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1` + `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` |

This PR targets the **AITER fp8 indexer** path. The fp8 MFMA scoring kernel is faster per block than the Triton bf16 path, so CP provides the same absolute latency reduction but against a faster baseline.

## Changes

| File | Type |
|---|---|
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/indexer_aiter_cp.py` | New — `MiniMaxM3IndexerAiterCPImpl` |
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/indexer_aiter.py` | Modified — CP dispatch in `select_aiter_indexer_impl_cls` |
| `vllm/envs.py` | Modified — `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP` (shared with #57832) |

## Test Plan

### Hardware
8× AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950), 256 GB HBM3 per GPU, ROCm 6.4 / rocm100

### Image
`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-e9757321527ca1ecd514c07c1418dd2c53da3d19` (vLLM v0.3.1.dev311)

### Server (MXFP4 model weights, AITER fp8 indexer)
```
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1
export VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_CAST_BF16_TO_FP16=0
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION_MIN_SIZE_KB=256
export VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP=1           # set to 0 for baseline

vllm serve /model/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 \
  --served-model-name amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 \
  --port 8766 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --block-size 128 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
  --language-model-only \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --moe-backend aiter \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' \
  --max-model-len 130000
```

### Benchmark command
```
vllm bench serve \
  --model amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --tokenizer /model/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 \
  --base-url http://localhost:8766 \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 20000 --random-output-len 512 \
  --max-concurrency 8 --num-prompts 24
```

## Test Result

### MXFP4 Throughput ISL Sweep (vLLM 0.3.1)

**Indexer:** AITER fp8 (`indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`) | **Attention:** AITER_SPARSE_PA (`kv_cache_dtype=fp8`)

| ISL | Baseline (tok/s) | CP Indexer (tok/s) | Delta | TTFT (ms) | p99 TTFT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **20k** | 364.2 | **473.3** | **+29.9%** | 6,130 → 3,281 | 18,095 → **6,612** |
| 64k | 327.5 | 327.1 | −0.1% | 5,052 → 5,025 | 8,196 → 8,161 |
| 100k | 261.9 | 262.7 | +0.3% | 8,494 → 8,430 | 18,794 → 18,623 |

At 20k: **+30% throughput**, **−46% mean TTFT**, **−63% p99 TTFT**.
At 64k+: neutral — AITER sparse attention dominates; indexer is not the bottleneck.

### Comparison: AITER fp8 vs Triton bf16 indexer (both with CP)

| ISL | Triton bf16 CP (#57832) | AITER fp8 CP (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| 20k | 466.0 tok/s | **473.3 tok/s** (+2%) |
| 64k | 303.7 tok/s | **327.1 tok/s** (+8%) |
| 100k | 237.4 tok/s | **262.7 tok/s** (+11%) |

The AITER fp8 path is consistently faster due to the fp8 MFMA scoring kernel; the CP delta is similar for both paths.

### Benchmark C — AgentX Pareto Sweep (MXFP4+EAGLE3, TP=4, vLLM 0.3.1)

**Indexer:** AITER fp8 (`indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`) | **Attention:** AITER_SPARSE_PA
**Server:** `max-num-seqs=64`, `enable-chunked-prefill`, `enable-prefix-caching`, EAGLE3 MTP spec decode (`synthetic_acceptance_length=2.78`)
**Benchmark:** aiperf `inferencex-agentx-mvp`, Weka trace `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126_256k`, 900s per point
**Methodology:** Single server per run (baseline then CP back-to-back), 60s warmup — eliminates ISL trace variance.

| Concurrency | Baseline (tok/s/GPU) | CP (tok/s/GPU) | Delta | vs ATOM (MI355X) | ISL baseline | ISL CP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15 | 14,732 | 14,767 | +0.2% | 0.66x | 79,387 | 79,464 |
| 20 | 19,505 | 19,579 | +0.4% | 0.57x | 81,224 | 81,343 |
| 24 | 19,686 | 19,713 | +0.1% | 0.48x | 80,464 | 80,486 |
| 32 | 27,708 | 27,992 | +1.0% | 0.61x | 75,857 | 75,812 |

CP is neutral (0–1%) at all concurrency points with EAGLE3 spec decode. With speculative decoding, decode is fast enough that the indexer is not the bottleneck. The AITER fp8 indexer already scores blocks in ~1/8 the time of a single-rank Triton bf16 scorer; CP further reduces this to ~1/64 — but at these concurrencies and ISLs the attention kernel dominates.

**Hardware note:** Our MI350X vs ATOM/MI355X gap is hardware, not config. CP adds zero overhead in both cases.

**Reference (MI355X TP=4, from [PR #57909](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57909)):**
| Concurrency | ATOM | vLLM+CP (#57909) | Uplift |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 | 22,276 | 22,022 | 0.99x |
| 20 | 34,277 | 33,682 | 0.98x |
| 24 | 41,155 | 40,556 | 0.99x |
| 32 | 46,211 | 45,973 | 0.99x |

### Correctness

Mathematical equivalence: MAX of non-overlapping partial scores = MAX of full scores. Same algorithm as #57832 (validated with GSM8K 5-shot: 93.5% on both CP=0 and CP=1 with the Triton path).

## Related
- #57832 — Triton bf16 CP indexer (same algorithm, bf16 index cache path)
- #57909 — Upstream CP indexer (Fangzhou/Ai): at conc=20, 98% of ATOM throughput (33,681 vs 34,277 tok/s/GPU)

title: [Bugfix][DSV4.1] Warm DeepGEMM mHC projection specializations
body:
## Purpose

DSV4.1 can compile a DeepGEMM mHC prenorm projection during intermediate prefill because decode and maximum-prefill startup runs miss a reachable split count. Register the projection's input widths and reachable split counts with JIT warmup, then execute one dummy row per specialization. Token count is dynamic in this kernel, so large prefill buffers are unnecessary.

Extracted unchanged from #57643, where the implementation, registration, and tests have been removed. This fix is independent of all-reduce fusion and of the FlashInfer cached-tactic warmup in #57842. Open-PR checks found #51802 and #49707 addressing DeepSeek V4 TileLang warmup; neither implements this DSV4.1 DeepGEMM projection warmup.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_jit_warmup.py -q -rs
```

- 30 tests passed; pre-commit passed.
- Fresh-cache GB200 check compiled six specializations (widths 5120/20480, splits 1/4/16), then exercised 26 runtime shapes from 1 to 8192 tokens with subsequent compiler invocations forbidden. No runtime compilation occurred; projection and squared-sum results matched their references exactly.
- GPU validation used retained allocation 29900 on gb200-rack1-04 with `srun --overlap`.
- No model arithmetic changes or new model accuracy evaluation. The earlier combined real-model evaluation remains documented in #57643; it is not an isolated evaluation of this startup-only fix.

AI assistance was used for extraction and validation.

title: [ROCm] Calibrate gfx950 decode Top-K routing by rows × compressed-context
body:
## Purpose

Fix a miscalibrated kernel routing gate in `_get_aiter_top_k_kernel()` (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`) that causes the AITER `top_k_per_row_decode` kernel to be bypassed in favor of native on gfx950, even when AITER is measurably faster.

Two bugs in the existing gate:

**Bug 1 — FULL-graph replay always forces native.** The call site passes `max_model_len` (1 048 576) instead of the live compressed sequence length under `CUDAGraphMode.FULL`. The condition `max_valid_seq_len > _GFX950_C4A_AITER_MAX_COMPRESSED_SEQ_LEN` evaluates to `1 048 576 > 65 536 = True` for every FULL-graph decode step, unconditionally routing to native.

**Bug 2 — The 64 K threshold is wrong even with the correct live length.** Measured on gfx950 (MI350X): AITER is 1.08–2.08× faster than native at C32 (192 verification rows) for live compressed contexts up to 262 144 tokens. The 64 K cutoff forces native for any context above 64 K, including the typical long-context operating point (50 K–300 K tokens).

This PR replaces the one-dimensional `max_valid_seq_len > 64K` gate with a two-dimensional `(rows, live_compressed_ctx)` policy calibrated on gfx950. Native is preserved conservatively for `CUDAGraphMode.FULL` (where live context is unavailable at replay time).

## Test Plan

**Policy correctness (no GPU required):**
```bash
python3 tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_topk_routing.py
```

**Full suite on gfx950/gfx942:**
```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_topk_routing.py -v
```

Tests cover:
- 20-shape calibration grid correctness (all `rows ∈ {48, 96, 192, 384}` × `live_ctx ∈ {32 K, 65 K, 131 K, 262 K, 524 K}`)
- `CUDAGraphMode.FULL` always returns native (`live_ctx=None`)
- C32 AgentX operating point (192 rows, ctx ≤ 262 K) always routes AITER
- Full 524 K context always routes native at all row counts
- Bitwise index-set match between AITER and native kernels across 5 shapes (GPU tests, `requires_rocm_cdna3_or_newer`)

## Test Result

### Kernel-level calibration — gfx950 MI350X, `nightly-eed1f3d0c6`

Method: graph-captured weakest-of-5, 200-iteration GPU clock warmup, `logits_width = 524 288`, `Top-K = 512`. Bitwise index-set correctness verified before timing accepted.

**Context sweep at C32 (192 rows):**

| live_ctx | native (µs) | AITER (µs) | winner | speedup |
|---------:|------------:|-----------:|:------:|--------:|
|    8 192 |       39.94 |      19.20 | AITER  |  2.08×  |
|   32 768 |       90.29 |      24.21 | AITER  |  3.73×  |
|   65 536 |       93.42 |      36.61 | AITER  |  2.55×  |
|  131 072 |      107.40 |      69.39 | AITER  |  1.55×  |
|  262 144 |      129.96 |     120.27 | AITER  |  1.08×  |
|  524 288 |      181.48 |     223.88 | native |    —    |

**Full 20-shape policy validation:**
```
policy=20/20 c32_grid_speedup=1.3931x
kernel_comparisons_trustworthy=20/20, policy_correct=20/20
```

### End-to-end — MI350X 4-chip TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash FP4

Workload: AgentX agentic-coding trace replay, concurrency 32, DSpark depth 5, `DURATION=600 s`. Run-to-run noise: ±0.79% throughput, ±1.7% p90 interactivity.

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Delta |
|:-------|--------:|--------:|------:|
| Output throughput (tok/s/chip) | 237.96 | 236.70 | −0.53% *(within noise)* |
| p90 interactivity (tok/s/user) | 34.46 | 36.78 | **+6.75%** |
| p50 interactivity (tok/s/user) | ~71 | 74.06 | +4.3% |
| p90 TPOT (s) | ~0.029 | 0.02719 | −6.2% |

Throughput −0.53% is within the ±0.79% noise band. p90 interactivity +6.75% is well outside the ±1.7% band. The gain is concentrated in the slow tail (requests with moderate context hitting native unnecessarily); full-context requests are unchanged.

**Why throughput is not positive:** `CUDAGraphMode.FULL` steps (majority at high concurrency) conservatively retain native — live context is absent from the graph replay key. The p90 gain comes from `PIECEWISE` steps. Extending the policy to FULL graphs by bucketing `live_compressed_ctx` into the capture key is a follow-on.

---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results

title: [Perf] Use custom all-gather for full-vocabulary logits
body:
## Purpose

Use the existing custom all-gather for full-vocabulary logits when the device
communicator supports the input. This preserves vocabulary order and padding
removal, with the existing collective as fallback. It reuses the communicator's
workspace and does not change model weights or sampling policy.

DSpark already replicates its Markov embedding and projection. This optimization
instead targets the base LM head's once-per-block vocabulary gather, and also
applies to target logits produced through the common LogitsProcessor.

This PR is independent of #57643 and does not change mHC. It does not duplicate
#54332 / RFC #54333: those avoid full-vocabulary communication through reduced
sampling, whereas this retains the complete logits required by the DSpark Markov
head and other full-logit consumers. #57770 changes greedy reduction after logits
are available; #57627 changes context projection. Open-PR and related-issue checks
were run on 2026-09-21.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py -q -rs
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/logits_processor.py tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py
```

33 tests passed; pre-commit passed. Coverage includes vocabulary ordering,
padding removal, multidimensional logits, unavailable/unsupported custom
collectives, and preservation of the replicated Markov path.

GB200 TP4, BF16, local vocabulary shard 32,320, full vocabulary 129,280.
Collective plus layout conversion, warmed CUDA graphs, alternating arm order,
per-sample maximum across ranks, median microseconds:

| Logit rows | NCCL | Custom |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 15.29 | 5.53 |
| 5 | 20.64 | 10.93 |
| 6 | 21.46 | 11.21 |
| 16 | 32.28 | 17.53 |
| 40 | 66.72 | 31.70 |
| 48 | 69.89 | 36.01 |
| 64 | 76.03 | 45.35 |

All cases passed eager and changed-input graph-replay comparisons against NCCL.
These are collective measurements, not end-to-end speedup claims. Performance
has been measured on GB200 TP4; other configurations retain the custom
communicator's existing eligibility checks and fallback.

Real-weight DSV4.1-Flash, TP4, fixed DSpark draft length 5, FlashInfer FP8 cache,
MXFP4 sparse-logits indexer: GSM8K 5-shot, greedy, thinking disabled,
128-example smoke test: **125/128 (97.66%) flexible extraction**. This matches the
previous smoke baseline; it is not a full-dataset score. During this evaluation,
a validation worker compared every eligible custom gather with NCCL, including
inside captured draft graphs: **3,828 additional comparisons per rank, all equal**.
The validation worker is not part of the production patch or performance timing.

Complete captured draft backbone + LM head + five sequential Markov greedy
sampling steps, TP4, KV8704, fixed five-token draft, synthetic weights/cache,
identical prepared inputs and pinned 210-entry tactics:

| Request batch | NCCL µs | Custom µs | Reduction |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 636.82 | 624.81 | 1.9% |
| 8 | 897.44 | 836.73 | 6.8% |

Five samples of 20 graph replays after three seconds of warmup; each sample
uses the slowest rank. Eager/graph and changed-input replay checks passed.
Cross-arm input IDs and sampled tokens match exactly on every rank. This scope
excludes target verification, eager context preparation, and serving overhead.
No whole-request speedup is claimed. No extra persistent workspace or replicated
weights are introduced; the existing custom communicator is reused.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and validation.
Human review and test attestation: the submitter confirmed reviewing every changed line of commit 1082d2ddad and running the relevant tests.

title: [ROCm][Perf] MXFP8 K-loop mask and activation sharing for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on gfx950
body:
## Purpose

Two fixes to `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on AMD gfx950 (MI355X).

**1. K-loop mask (`EVEN_K` constexpr)**
The Triton `tl.dot_scaled` K-loop was unmasked, so `apply_weights` guarded with `K % 128 == 0` and dequantized the full weight to BF16 on every forward pass for shapes where `K % 32 == 0` but `K % 128 != 0`. Adding `EVEN_K: tl.constexpr` to predicate the tail mask relaxes the guard from `% 128` to `% 32`. On DSv4.1-Flash at TP=4, `shared_experts.down_proj` (K=576) now runs natively: 37.2 µs → 7.1 µs at M=192 (gfx950, graph-captured, weakest-of-5).

**2. Activation sharing via `input_quant_key()`**
Without this, the base class returned `None` from `input_quant_key()`, leaving `layer.input_quant_key` unset. On DSv4.1-Flash, `wq_b` and `indexer.wq_b` both consume the same normalized q-lora tensor; neither could accept a pre-quantized input, so the same tensor was MXFP8-quantized twice per layer per step. Adding `input_quant_key() -> kMxfp8Dynamic` lets a fused RMSNorm+quant producer hand both GEMMs a single pre-quantized activation and skip the second quantization entirely.

Also splits `_mxfp8_dot_scaled_linear` into:
- `_mxfp8_dot_scaled_gemm(x_q, x_scale, w, w_scale, out_dtype)` — GEMM-only, accepts pre-quantized fp8 + E8M0 scales
- `_mxfp8_dot_scaled_linear(x, w, w_scale)` — quantizes then calls `_mxfp8_dot_scaled_gemm`

This is not a duplicate of any open PR. AI assistance was used; every changed line has been reviewed and verified.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Dispatch proof: verify K=576 now routes to native kernel (not BF16 fallback)
python eval/eval_mxfp8_dense_gemm.py --shapes all --sweep-m 1,6,192,4096 \
    --warmup 200 --iters 100 --reps 3

# Activation-sharing parity: bitwise-identical output at M=6..16384
python eval/eval_a1_rocm_prequant_consumer.py
python eval/eval_a1_rocm_query_quant_producer.py

# E2e benchmark (MI355X, TP=4, C=32, agentic-coding, 600 s):
python bench.py --scenario agentx --conc 32 --duration 600
```

## Test Results

**Component (gfx950, graph-captured, weakest-of-5):**

| M | Shape context | BF16 fallback | FP8 native | Speedup |
|--:|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | decode/TPOT | — | — | **1.51×** |
| 6 | DSpark verify | — | — | **1.17×** |
| 192 | C32 operating point | 25.73 µs | 18.85 µs | **1.37×** |
| 4096 | prefill/TTFT | — | — | **1.38×** |

Scale rearrangement (32×32 → 128×128 E8M0): 164.7 dB vs exact fp32 dequant — the same tensor. End-to-end SNR 31.4–31.6 dB equals producer-alone SNR at every M, confirming all precision loss is FP8 activation quantization (same as CUDA's `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`).

**End-to-end (MI355X, TP=4, C=32, agentic-coding, 600 s — this change in isolation):**

| Metric | Before | After | Δ |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Output throughput | 231.76 tok/s/chip | 244.33 tok/s/chip | **+5.42%** |
| p90 interactivity | 33.77 tok/s/user | 36.97 tok/s/user | **+9.49%** |
| p90 TPOT | 29.6 ms | 27.1 ms | **−8.7%** |
