title: [ROCm][Perf] Candidate-only MQA scorer for DSA sparse indexer prefill on gfx950
body:
## Purpose

Adds a candidate-only MQA logits kernel for the DSA sparse indexer **prefill** path on AMD gfx950 (MI355X).

Consumer attention layers in DSv4.1-Flash DSA hold a candidate set of at most `n_cand × block_size` columns (16 384 here) before scoring. The current code scores the full KV buffer width (up to 1 048 576 columns), masks it, then takes the top-k — three passes proportional to `row_span`. The new `candidate_mqa_logits` Triton kernel scores only the candidate columns directly: one pass, O(capacity)/row, flat regardless of context length.

**Gate:** `candidate_scoring_admits()` uses a row-weighted `mean_row_context` (new field on `DeepseekV32IndexerPrefillChunkMetadata`, computed host-side in `build_prefill_chunk_metadata`, no device sync). Gate threshold: `span/capacity ≥ 2.0×`. Below the measured crossover (~1.0–1.5×) the dense path stays, avoiding a 0.6× regression on chunks of many short requests whose rows are already covered by their candidate set.

Added to `candidate_blocks.py`: `candidate_scoring_admits`, `candidate_mqa_logits`, `compact_topk_bounds`, `remap_compact_indices`, and the backing Triton kernel `_candidate_mqa_logits_kernel`.

This is not a duplicate of any open PR. `candidate_mqa_logits` returns 0 results across all PR searches. PR #57459 ("DSA candidate-block kernels walk each row's live context") is a different optimization that strides the existing dense mask kernel rather than replacing it with a candidate-gather approach. AI assistance was used; every changed line has been reviewed and verified.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Correctness: bitwise match against torch reference at 143.8 dB SNR
python eval/eval_b1_candidate_scoring.py

# Gate crossover verification (confirms 0.6x below crossover, >1x above)
python eval/eval_b1_candidate_gather_equiv.py

# E2e benchmark (MI355X, TP=4, C=32, agentic-coding, 600 s):
python bench.py --scenario agentx --conc 32 --duration 600
```

## Test Results

**Component (gfx950, n_cand=2048, block_size=8, capacity=16 384):**

| span/capacity | Dense (µs) | Candidate-only (µs) | Speedup |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| ≤1.0× | — | — | 0.60–0.68× (gate blocks, dense stays) |
| 4.5× (p50 C32) | 817 | 258 | **3.17×** |
| 9.8× (p90 C32) | — | — | **4.26×** |

**End-to-end (MI355X, TP=4, C=32, agentic-coding, 600 s — this change in isolation):**

| Metric | Before | After | Δ |

| Output throughput | 248.03 tok/s/chip | 261.60 tok/s/chip | **+5.47%** |
| p90 interactivity | 38.87 tok/s/user | 42.98 tok/s/user | **+10.56%** |

title: [ROCm][Perf] Candidate-only paged MQA scorer for DSA sparse indexer decode on gfx950
body:
## Purpose

Adds a paged SHUFFLE-layout candidate-only Triton scorer for the DSA sparse indexer **decode** path on AMD gfx950 (MI355X), along with the prefill scorer from the sibling PR.

Decode consumer layers (4 of them at positions 24/28/32/36) score candidates from a paged KV cache in SHUFFLE layout. The current code runs dense score → mask → full-width top-k. The new `paged_candidate_mqa_logits` Triton kernel reads only the live candidate pages per row, computes logits directly over the candidate set, and feeds a compact top-k + remap step (`remap_decode_compact_indices`). A device-side `live_slots` length gate and `_decode_candidate_scoring_admits` guard the fast path. A varctx schedule integration (`_varctx_schedule`) passes schedule metadata to the paged logits kernel for cache-line-aligned access on variable-context batches.

Also eliminates the 25 MB/layer hot-path allocation (full-width logits buffer) on the 4 affected consumer decode layers.

This also includes the prefill `candidate_mqa_logits` scorer (see sibling PR) since the decode and prefill paths share `candidate_blocks.py`.

This is not a duplicate of any open PR. No open PR implements `paged_candidate_mqa_logits` or decode-path candidate-only scoring. AI assistance was used; every changed line has been reviewed and verified.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Fuse indptr prefix sum into DSA decode pack kernel for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
body:
## Purpose

Fuses the ragged indptr prefix sum into `_pack_global_topk_ragged_kernel` for the DSA decode index build on AMD gfx950 (MI355X), eliminating dispatch overhead that CUDA never incurs.

`compute_global_topk_ragged_indices_and_indptr` runs 38× per decode step (once per sparse attention layer). On ROCm, the previous code called `_build_indptr_from_lengths` which launched `torch.zeros` + `torch.cumsum` (a rocprim lookback scan) to prefix-sum 193 int32s. Measured cost: ~305 µs/step of pure kernel dispatch. CUDA never pays this: `build_flashinfer_mixed_sparse_indices` in `common/ops/cache_utils.py` emits its indptr inside the pack kernel's registers in a single launch.

This change ports that approach to ROCm: each token program derives its own indptr offset via a masked `tl.sum` over `NTOK_PAD` lanes in-register and stores its own entry before the early-return. `topk_indptr` is now `torch.empty` (no pre-zeroing needed since every entry is written by the kernel). The `else: topk_indptr.zero_()` branch covers the degenerate empty case. `_build_indptr_from_lengths` is removed.

Result: 4 → 2 graph nodes per call, 152 → 76 kernel launches/step (−50%), 1.69× on the cluster, bitwise-identical output.

This is not a duplicate of any open PR. PR #56638 ("Re-enable the fused combine_topk_swa_indices on gfx950") addresses a different function on the prefill path. AI assistance was used; every changed line has been reviewed and verified.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Correctness + launch count verification (bitwise match at 6 shapes,
# including 768-row max batch, ragged rows, invalid rows)
python eval/eval_e2a_fused_ragged_index_build.py

# Profile to confirm graph node count: 4.0 -> 2.0 per call
python eval/eval_kernel_attribution.py

# E2e benchmark (MI355X, TP=4, C=32, agentic-coding, 600 s):
python bench.py --scenario agentx --conc 32 --duration 600
```

## Test Results

**Component (gfx950, measured on live import path via profiler):**

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|--:|--:|
| Graph nodes / call | 4.0 | **2.0** |
| Kernel launches / decode step | 152 | **76** (−50%) |
| Cluster speedup | 1.00× | **1.69×** |
| Per-step saving | — | **126.6 µs** |

Scaling: flat across 1→768-row sweep, confirming dispatch-bound mechanism. Output bitwise-identical at all 6 measured shapes.

**End-to-end (MI355X, TP=4, C=32, agentic-coding, 600 s — this change in isolation):**

| Metric | Before | After | Δ |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Output throughput | 325.28 tok/s/chip | 324.91 tok/s/chip | −0.1% (within noise) |
| p90 interactivity | 64.76 tok/s/user | 65.97 tok/s/user | **+1.9%** |
| p90 TPOT | 15.4 ms | 15.2 ms | **−1.8%** |

Note: the throughput delta is within the measured noise band. The primary value of this change is the 50% launch reduction, which reduces CUDA-graph replay overhead and creates headroom for future kernel additions within the decode step budget.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Reject hash routing for unsupported monolithic backends
body:
- Add a per-layer `has_hash_routing` field to `FusedMoEConfig`, defaulting to false.
- Populate it from the hash table supplied to `FusedMoEFactory`.
- Reject hash-routed layers in the common capability check for all current monolithic backends, whose interface does not carry token IDs or hash tables.
- Preserve modular hash routing and ordinary non-hash monolithic selection.
- Add six factory-to-oracle cases covering monolithic AITER, native modular AITER, and modular Triton with and without hash routing.

This issue was uncovered during local MI300 reproduction of the [CI 90039 speculative-decoding group](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90039/list?sid=01a0bd6c-73d2-48d6-82a3-1e021270e178&tab=output). The A16 DeepSeek V4 capability added in [#46516](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46516) already lacked a hash-input path, and [#50622](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50622) later made that backend available on gfx942. Modular execution selects experts using token IDs and the hash table, but current monolithic execution bypasses that router and drops the required inputs. Recording the layer requirement before backend selection prevents an otherwise eligible monolithic backend from silently using a different routing algorithm. 

Related work: [#45711](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45711) extends the monolithic interface and implements hash routing for a new AITER MXFP8 backend. This standalone change contains none of that implementation and intentionally rejects every monolithic backend under the current interface. If that extension lands, this blanket check must be revisited to admit explicitly implemented hash capability while continuing to reject unsupported backends. [#50844](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50844) bounds token IDs in a hash-routing kernel; it addresses input validation rather than backend eligibility.

Investigation, implementation, validation, and this description were AI-assisted.

title: [Feature][KVConnector][DSv4.1] Encoder-only prefill with Mooncake P/D
body:
## Purpose

Implement encoder-only Prefill for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D serving with the direct `MooncakeConnector`, following the asymmetric P/D design in RFC #57383 and the full-prompt cache-hit replay design in RFC #57738.

P executes through the L20 pre-mix boundary and produces the transferable Main KV and Indexer K. D receives those regions, replays the bounded tail through the full target, and samples the first token.

## Implementation

This PR is intentionally split into two commits:

1. `13d89a71d0` - feature implementation and streamlined tests
   - Adds `KVTransferConfig.dsv41_encoder_only_prefill` for dedicated Mooncake producer and consumer roles.
   - Adds the V4.1 execution boundary, explicit transfer profile, cache-only zero-token P completion, GPU completion event, request validation, and proxy `cache_only` handoff.
   - P runs L0-L19 plus the L20 pre-mix and canonical Main-KV/Indexer-K writes, then skips L20 attention/FFN, L21-L39, final norm, LM head, sampling, and DSpark.
   - D keeps bounded-replay state and DSpark state local. The validated D path supports DSpark K5 adaptive verification and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` CUDA graphs.

2. `8d5b2b21c9` - Mooncake release-only pull fix
   - Bounded replay can discard a short remote hit while Mooncake still needs to release the producer blocks.
   - An empty pull has no local blocks and the consumer never enters `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`. This commit releases the producer blocks without reporting a receive completion to the scheduler.

The current boundary is direct `MooncakeConnector`, NVIDIA, model runner V2, PP=1, no PCP or microbatching, SWA bounded replay with a 128-token window, the 40-layer V4.1-Flash topology, text-only requests, and no prompt logprobs. P requires `--no-async-scheduling` and must not configure a speculator.

## Validation

### Latest-main rebase (2026-09-29)

Rebased onto `05d89636fc`. On macOS with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, the focused model-boundary, cache-only, scheduler, config, and Mooncake tests passed (18 passed):

```bash

  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_encoder_only_prefill.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_cache_only_prefill.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_dsv41_cache_only_prefill_finishes_without_sampling \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_dsv41_encoder_only_profile_transfers_global_groups_only \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_dsv41_encoder_only_profile_rejects_missing_or_mixed_global_state \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py::test_cache_only_runner_waits_for_kv_writes_before_output \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_config.py::test_dsv41_encoder_only_handoff_requires_bounded_replay \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_config.py::test_dsv41_encoder_only_handoff_separates_producer_compile_hash \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_config.py::test_dsv41_encoder_only_handoff_rejects_unsupported_config \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py::test_encoder_only_cache_ready_triggers_mooncake_transfer \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py::test_encoder_only_mooncake_rejects_extra_consumer_cache_regions
```

`uvx ruff check` and `uvx ruff format --check` passed on all 21 changed Python files; `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed. The upstream CUDA replay-batch suite could not be collected on this CPU-only machine because it allocates CUDA tensors at import time. The H20 serving and GSM8K measurements below were taken on the earlier nightly and have not been rerun on this rebased head.

### Environment

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-a9eafde59cbd55182dc2265cc398b7186f0a0eaa`
- Hardware: two nodes, each with 8 NVIDIA H20 96 GB GPUs; one node for P and one for D
- Mooncake: 0.3.13.post1 over RDMA
- Baseline: the fixed nightly plus the release-only fix (tested with commit `50dcc87d1c`)
- Candidate: the same nightly with both PR commits

The baseline used conventional Mooncake P/D. Because D used DSpark K5, baseline P also used static DSpark K5 (`enable_adaptive_verification=false`) to keep the registered cache groups aligned. Candidate P did not load DSpark; candidate D used DSpark K5 adaptive verification. Decode used TP1 + DP8 + EP8 and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`. DeepEP was disabled: neither arm set `--all2all-backend`, and both selected the default `AgRsAll2AllManager` at runtime.

title: [Bug]: fp8 FlashMLA sparse decode crashes at engine init with --enforce-eager on SM90 (dummy-run aten::new_empty dispatch failure, size-dependent)
body:
### Your current environment

```
vLLM       : dev tree at e378275a8 (≈ main mid-Sep 2026) + index-kpool fix,
             rebuilt from source (vllm 0.1.dev427+gb90f0e8fb.cu131)
GPU        : 8 × NVIDIA H100 80GB (SM90), TP=8
Model      : zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash (Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration,
             NoPE MLA: kv_lora_rank=512, qk_rope_head_dim=0)
Backend    : FLASHMLA_SPARSE (head_size 512, fp8_ds_mla kv cache)
```

###  Describe the bug

Booting with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` (fp8_ds_mla envelope on the FlashMLA
sparse backend, per the NoPE-512 envelope mechanism in PR #55543) plus
`--enforce-eager` crashes during the engine's init dummy run:

```
vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py:1245, in _fp8_flash_mla_kernel
    out, lse = flash_mla_with_kvcache(...)
vllm/third_party/flashmla/flash_mla_interface.py:175, in flash_mla_with_kvcache
    out, lse, new_tile_scheduler_metadata, new_num_splits = flash_mla_cuda.sparse_decode_fwd(...)
RuntimeError: torch_call_dispatcher("aten::new_empty", "", stack.data(),
    (((0ULL + 2) << 56) | ((0ULL + 13) << 48) | ((0ULL + 0) << 40) | ((0ULL + 0) << 0)))
API call failed at torch/csrc/stable/ops.h, line 939
```

Call chain: `kernel_warmup()` → `flashinfer_autotune()` →
`_run_flashinfer_autotune_dummy_runs()` → the fp8 sparse decode kernel.

**Trigger isolation (three arms):**

1. Engine init with `--enforce-eager` at `max_num_batched_tokens=16384` →
   crashes as above.
2. The same engine init at `max_num_batched_tokens=8192` → boots and
   serves fine.
3. Direct eager kernel calls with REAL shapes (same interface, same dtypes,
   outside the dummy-run context) → do NOT crash.

So the trigger is size-dependent and lives in the dummy-run path (a
degenerate batch shape the warmup runs at 16K but not 8K, or a
dummy-run-specific metadata state), not in the fp8 sparse kernel itself.

**What works (control):**
- Same serve with CUDA graphs ON (no `--enforce-eager`): boots, serves,
  passes GSM8K at 0.995 accuracy on this exact envelope path.
- bf16 kv cache (same backend, no fp8_ds_mla): boots fine with
  `--enforce-eager`.

**Minimal repro shape** (from our repro script; happy to attach):

```python
# arm (C) — the crash:
LLM(model="/data/models/glm53flash", kv_cache_dtype="fp8",
    enforce_eager=True, max_num_batched_tokens=16384,
    tensor_parallel_size=8)
# arm (A) — OK: same with max_num_batched_tokens=8192
# arm (B) — OK: direct flash_mla_cuda.sparse_decode_fwd eager calls
#     at real shapes (q=[T,H,576] bf16, 656B fp8_ds_mla cache, topk=128)
```

**Impact:** any SM90 user running `--enforce-eager` with fp8_ds_mla on the
sparse-MLA path hits this at startup. The production graph path is
unaffected.

### Notes

- Our tree carries PR #55543's NoPE-512 envelope port plus small fixes; the
  crash reproduces on the fp8 sparse decode path regardless of the envelope
  shim (it fires inside `sparse_decode_fwd` before any model-specific
  padding is read).
- Suspected classes: degenerate dummy-run shape at ≥16K tokens, or a
  stable-ABI/eager-dispatch edge in `sparse_decode_fwd` (the error is a
  stable-ABI `aten::new_empty` dispatch failure, not a CUDA IMA).
- Happy to run further isolation (specific dummy shapes, other
  max_num_batched_tokens values, nvfp4_ds_mla) on request.

*(AI-assisted reproduction and isolation; every number/log line above was
verified by a human reviewer. Full traceback available on request.)*

title: [ROCm][DSv4][DSV4.1][Perf] Fill decode wave counts and fuse the reduce at one split
body:
## Summary

Two related fixes to the ROCm DSv4 sparse MLA decode split-K path on gfx950.

**1. Fill wave counts with fewer split iterations.** The split heuristic sized
splits to hit a workgroup target, which could leave a wave partly idle while
each workgroup still walked more `BLOCK_K` iterations than necessary. Among all
split counts that land in the *same* wave count, pick the one with the fewest
per-workgroup iterations; never trade an extra wave for fewer iterations.

**2. Fuse the reduce into the partial kernel when there is one split.** At one
split the split-K machinery is pure overhead: the partial kernel writes fp32
running state (`part_m`, `part_l`, `part_acc`) that the reduce immediately reads
back, divides, and stores as bf16 — a full round trip through memory plus a
second launch to finish work the partial kernel already had in registers.
Normalize in the partial epilogue and store bf16 straight to `out`, skipping both
the staging buffers and the reduce launch. Attention sinks fold into the same
epilogue. Shapes taking more than one split are untouched.

Single-split is not a corner case: it is what the heuristic picks once rows fill
the device, i.e. the high-concurrency and long-spec-decode points that set decode
throughput.

## Results

MI355X (gfx950), decode partial+reduce under CUDA-graph replay, 192 shapes:
2 profiles (DSv4.1-Flash topk=512, V4-Pro topk=1024) x {16, 32} heads/rank x
concurrency 1-128 x spec-decode length 1-6.

Both arms of each comparison are timed **back-to-back inside one process**,
alternating order and taking medians. Re-measuring identical code in a fresh
session on this machine drifts by several percent, which is the same order as
the effects being measured, so whole-sweep CSV-vs-CSV comparison is not reliable
here.

| change | scope | geomean | best | worst | regressions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| split heuristic | 46 shapes it changes | **1.139x** | 1.362x | 1.047x | 0 |
| split heuristic | all 192 shapes | **1.032x** | — | — | 0 |
| single-split fusion | 22 single-split shapes | **1.064x** | 1.094x | 1.031x | 0 |

Fusion by config, both at 32 heads/rank:

| config | range |
|---|---|
| DSv4.1-Flash TP=2, conc 64-128, q_len 2-6 | 1.065x - 1.094x |
| V4-Pro TP=4, conc 64-128, q_len 2-6 | 1.041x - 1.056x |

## Where the kernel now sits against its roofline

Measured machine limits: 3.4 TB/s for random 576 B gathers (the KV access
pattern), 4.63 TB/s streaming, 232 TFLOP/s at the decode's own MFMA tile shape,
and a graph-replay launch floor of 10.8 us (one kernel) / 12.5 us (two).

Taking `launch + max(memory, compute)` as the floor, with memory counting the KV
gather alone, for 32 heads/rank:

- **Rows <= ~48**: 89-117% of floor — at the ceiling, launch- and gather-bound.
- **Rows 96-192**: 74-89% of floor.
- **Rows 384-768**: 55-60% of floor, and here `actual ~= gather + dot + launch`
  almost exactly (Flash at 768 rows: 111 + 139 + 11 = 261 us modelled vs 255 us
  measured; Pro at 768 rows: 173 + 250 + 11 = 434 vs 438). The kernel gets
  essentially **no overlap** between the KV gather and the MFMA work at large
  rows.

That serialization is the remaining headroom, and it is not reachable from the
launcher: `num_stages` 1/2/3, `num_warps` 4/8, and `waves_per_eu` 0/1/2 are all
flat to within 1% at 128/384/768 rows, because the accumulators (4 x [16,128]
fp32) plus the staged Q tile leave no register budget for the compiler to
prefetch a KV tile. Closing it needs a kernel restructure, not tuning, so it is
left out of this PR.

### At the TP=4 serving config

The figures above are 32 heads/rank. The end-to-end section below serves
DSv4.1-Flash at TP=4, which is 16 heads/rank — half the MFMA work per row
against the same KV traffic — so those shapes are reported separately here.

The floor is `launch + max(gather + stream, compute)` over the bytes the kernel
is *obliged* to move at that shape:

- gather: `rows x 640 x 576 B` of fp8_ds_mla KV at 3.4 TB/s. MLA shares one
  latent entry across all heads, so this does not scale with head count.
- stream at 4.63 TB/s: Q in, `out` back, and — only when there is more than one
  split — the fp32 `part_m`/`part_l`/`part_acc` buffers, which the partial
  kernel writes and the reduce reads straight back,
  `rows x splits x heads x (576 x 4 + 8) B` each way.
- compute: `rows x heads x 640 x 2 x (576 + 512)` FLOP at 232 TFLOP/s.

Counting the split staging matters: at 192 rows and 4 splits it is 13.8 us of
required traffic against 20.8 us of KV gather. A KV-only floor omits it and
makes the kernel look considerably worse than it is.

Graph-replay time for the decode call, q_len 6:

Each arm is scored against its own floor, since the split count it picks sets
how much staging traffic it is obliged to move.

Each arm is scored against its own floor, since the split count it picks sets
how much staging traffic it is obliged to move. "before" is `upstream/main`.

| conc | rows | before splits | before us | before floor | before % | PR splits | PR us | PR floor | PR % |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 6 | 32 | 24.9 | 16.3 | 65% | 16 | **22.7** | 14.7 | 65% |
| 2 | 12 | 32 | 27.5 | 20.0 | 73% | 22 | **25.3** | 18.1 | 71% |
| 4 | 24 | 8 | 25.4 | 18.4 | 72% | 8 | 25.4 | 18.4 | 72% |
| 8 | 48 | 4 | 29.9 | 21.2 | 71% | 4 | 30.0 | 21.2 | 71% |
| 16 | 96 | 6 | 44.3 | 32.9 | 74% | 8 | **41.0** | 35.9 | **88%** |
| 32 | 192 | 3 | 69.1 | 44.1 | 64% | 4 | **52.2** | 47.1 | **90%** |
| 64 | 384 | 2 | 83.3 | 69.5 | 83% | 2 | 83.7 | 69.5 | 83% |
| 128 | 768 | 1 | 151.0 | 112.5 | 74% | 1 | **137.6** | 100.2 | 73% |

The heuristic changes its choice at 6, 12, 96 and 192 rows and leaves 24, 48,
384 and 768 alone, and the timings track that exactly: every shape it touches
gains (1.08x to 1.32x) and every shape it does not is flat to within 0.5%.

Across 96-384 rows the kernel runs at 83-90% of what the model allows, so there
is little left on the table in the range that sets decode throughput. The two
soft spots are at opposite ends. At 48 rows and below it sits at 65-72%, but
there the floor is mostly the 12.5 us two-kernel replay launch and the kernel
moves under 20% of the gather bound — the device is idle, so that gap is fixed
overhead rather than inefficiency. At 768 rows it falls to 73%, a 37 us
absolute gap, and that is where the gather/MFMA serialization described above is
least well hidden.

At 192 rows this PR is the difference between 64% and 90% of floor, and it gets
there while moving *more* staging traffic than base (4 splits against 3): the
win is iteration count, not bytes.

Percent-of-floor is only comparable within an arm. At 768 rows the fusion drops
the floor from 112.5 us to 100.2 us by removing the staging round trip
altogether, so this PR reads as a lower percentage (73% against base's 74%)
while being 13.4 us faster in absolute terms. Across arms, compare microseconds.

## End-to-end serving

Full server A/B on MI355X: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP=4, `--moe-backend aiter`,
DSpark MTP with 5 draft tokens, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`,
`--max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024`, Rust frontend, torch profiler off.
Steady-state decode step time is read from `vllm:iteration_tokens_total_count`
and `vllm:generation_tokens_total` on `/metrics`.

The two arms are this branch and **its own merge parent**
(`382970ee6c`), so they differ by this PR alone. Both are served concurrently on
disjoint 4-GPU halves of one node and sampled at the same wall-clock instant, so
host and PCIe drift is common-mode and cancels in the ratio. Six paired reps per
point, then the arms are **swapped across the two GPU halves** and the six reps
repeated, so a systematic difference between the halves cannot produce the
result. Speedup is the median of the paired per-rep ratios.

| conc | rows | base ms/step | PR ms/step | base tok/s | PR tok/s | speedup | 95% CI | n |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| 1 | 6 | 10.26 | 10.21 | 342.8 | 344.4 | 1.0049x | 1.0045-1.0057 | 10 |
| 4 | 24 | 11.66 | 11.66 | 1204.0 | 1203.2 | 0.9991x | 0.9981-1.0010 | 11 |
| 16 | 96 | 16.12 | 15.99 | 3482.0 | 3511.6 | 1.0075x | 1.0060-1.0114 | 12 |
| 32 | 192 | 20.56 | 19.88 | 5464.3 | **5651.5** | **1.0344x** | 1.0269-1.0363 | 12 |
| 64 | 384 | 29.97 | 29.95 | 7498.4 | 7501.1 | 1.0010x | 0.9992-1.0026 | 12 |

Geomean across all points is 1.0094x. The gain concentrates at concurrency 32,
which is 192 decode rows once DSpark's 1+5 verify shape is applied — the range
the split heuristic targets. Concurrency 4 (24 rows) and 64 (384 rows) are flat
because the heuristic picks the same split count there as before; neither is a
regression, and both straddle 1.0x. The c32 result reproduces across the GPU-half
swap: 1.0337x on one assignment and 1.0347x on the other.

The serving result and the kernel table agree. Feeding each measured kernel
speedup through Amdahl with sparse MLA attention's share of the decode step
(6.7% at c1 rising to 12.6% at c32) predicts +0.58 / +0.00 / +0.75 / +3.18% at
c1 / c4 / c16 / c32, against +0.49 / -0.09 / +0.75 / +3.44% measured — within
0.26 points at every point.

Note on methodology, in case this harness is reused: the sampling window must be
short enough that every stream is still generating when it closes. If the streams
hit their token limit mid-window the engine idles for the remainder, the step
counter stops advancing, and `ms_per_step` collapses to `window / steps_at_limit`
— an identical number at every concurrency, which looks like a perfectly flat
step time rather than a broken measurement.

## Tests

The existing suite passes unmodified against this change, on MI355X (gfx950):

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py -q
72 passed in 79.70s
```

`test_sparse_attn_decode_split_k_kernel` already parametrizes `num_splits=1`
across the sink and extra-segment combinations, so the fused epilogue this PR
adds is checked against the torch reference on the path it changes.

## Accuracy

The split change reorders float accumulation across splits; the fusion performs
the same arithmetic without the fp32 round trip, so results differ only in where
the final bf16 rounding lands. Measured max deviation vs. the staged path is
1.2e-4 (one bf16 ulp) across both profiles, 16 and 32 heads/rank, with and
without attention sinks.

GSM8K on the served model, full 1319 questions, TP=4, DSpark MTP with block
rejection (not the synthetic-acceptance perf setting, whose generations are not
meaningful):

| arm | strict-match | flexible-extract |
|---|---|---|
| base | 0.9765 +/- 0.0042 | 0.9757 +/- 0.0042 |
| this branch | 0.9765 +/- 0.0042 | 0.9757 +/- 0.0042 |

Identical to four decimal places on both extractors.

## Note

AI assistance was used for this change.

title: [Bugfix] Honor generation controls in the DeepSeek V4.1 tokenizer
body:
# [Bugfix] Honor generation controls in the DeepSeek V4.1 tokenizer

## Purpose

The independent `deepseek_v41` tokenizer currently ignores
`add_generation_prompt` and `continue_final_message`. This produces identical
prompts with the generation prompt enabled or disabled, and leaves EOS at the
end of an assistant prefix even when continuation was requested.

This change forwards the controls to the V4.1 encoder and:

- suppresses only the final generation cue, preserving historical separators;
- opens a fresh assistant turn after a completed assistant message;
- supports system-only generation;
- removes only the final assistant EOS for continuation;
- keeps a partial reasoning-only assistant message inside its thinking block;
- rejects continuation without a final assistant message.

Continuation takes precedence over the generation prompt. This also handles
`ChatCompletionRequest(continue_final_message=True)` where the default
`add_generation_prompt=True` remains in the renderer kwargs. The request schema
already rejects callers that explicitly set both fields to true.

The reference fixture files are unchanged. Both fixtures end in a completed
assistant message, so the test now checks their exact reference encoding with
`add_generation_prompt=False`, and separately checks the new generation cue.

### Related Work And Scope

Related: #46256 and #46257. The existing open PR #46257, by @fank, fixes the
older `deepseek_v4` encoder; it does not modify the independent `deepseek_v41`
wrapper or encoder. This proposal is limited to V4.1 and follows the generation
control semantics discussed there. It does not claim to resolve the V4/V3.2
parts of #46256, and should not auto-close that issue.

Open-PR searches and the issue discussion were checked on 2026-09-21. This
follow-up changes only the independent V4.1 implementation, not the files in
#46257; its scope is also explained in the
[issue discussion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46256#issuecomment-5756372341).

No NIXL, scheduling, DSpark, Triton, or CUDA code changes. This is not a claimed
fix for H20 worker deadlocks or production garbage output.

## Test Plan

In a development environment installed according to the repository AGENTS.md:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v41.py vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v41_encoding.py tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py
```

Coverage includes thinking on/off, final user/developer/system/assistant roles,
system-only prompts, preservation of historical EOS, partial reasoning,
request-to-renderer kwargs, caller-message immutability, and existing reference
tool/image/effort fixtures.

## Test Result

Base main: `8ec00ec2bc2d294b742f7814041d3a3043e0a90e`.

Tests executed in an isolated Linux container on an H20 host. Only the two
tokenizer modules from this main checkout were overlaid in the test process;
other dependencies came from nightly `0.29.1rc1.dev422+gd05da62e9`. This is not a
claim of full-checkout integration testing.

- New suite against unpatched main tokenizer modules: **18 failed, 30 passed**.
- Same suite against the patched modules: **48 passed**.
- Real downloaded DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash tokenizer: both thinking modes passed
  generation/continuation string-to-ID consistency checks; ordinary user-ended
  prompts retained identical token IDs before and after the patch.
- Ruff 0.14.0, using this checkout's pyproject.toml: check and format check passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `pre-commit run --files` for the three changed files: passed (inapplicable
  hooks skipped), including mypy and the repository-specific checks.

The container regression runner loads the two checked-out tokenizer modules
process-locally and then invokes the existing test file with pytest. The
executed command was:

```bash
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
  /tmp/dsv41-audit-venv/bin/python /work/tokenizer-pr-final/run_tests.py \
  --source /work/tokenizer-pr-final --tests /work/tokenizer-pr-final
```

### Model Smoke Evaluation

An isolated H20 TP8 server loaded the real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model using the
unmodified nightly above. Baseline and patched tokenizers rendered the same
five synthetic conversations to token IDs; those IDs were sent serially to
`/v1/completions`. No live tokenizer modules were replaced.

Generation settings: `temperature=0`, `seed=2026`, `max_tokens=128`,
`stream=false`, `skip_special_tokens=false`. All 10 requests returned HTTP 200;
all five patched cases contained the expected answer fragment.

| Case | Baseline output | Patched output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Normal user math question | `323` | `323` (prompt IDs unchanged) |
| Continue assistant `The result is ` | Raw BOS marker, then `# 17 * 19 = 323.` | `323.` |
| Fresh turn after completed assistant | Raw BOS marker and unrelated `#sustainable agriculture#`, then the answer | `The capital of France is Paris.` |
| System-only `Reply exactly OK.` | Empty text | `OK` |
| Continue partial reasoning `17 * 19 = 17 * (20 - 1) = ` | Generated `# Invalid Request` text after a raw BOS marker | `340 - 17 = 323.</think>323` |

The baseline "Invalid Request" was generated model text, not an HTTP error.
This is a narrow prompt-control smoke evaluation, not a broad accuracy
benchmark or full patched `/v1/chat/completions` integration test. No
throughput or production-output correctness claim is made from these samples.

## AI Assistance And Human Accountability

OpenAI Codex assisted with source review, implementation, test construction,
and test execution. The human submitter reviewed the changes and personally
reran the relevant tests successfully before submission, and is responsible
for the contribution. AI-executed validation is reported separately above.

title: [Bug]: Async EPLB silently stops making progress — rearrangement step counter runs away negative forever, no warning/error (EP16 cross-node, use_async=True, communicator=nixl)
body:
### TL;DR With async EPLB enabled (`use_async=True`, `communicator=nixl`) on an **EP16 deployment spanning two 8-GPU nodes**, the async transfer worker stops being consumed and **no further expert rearrangement ever happens**. The engine stays fully healthy — `/health` is 200, `/v1/models` is 200, real completions return correct results — while EPLB is silently dead: - the periodic stat line counts **downward forever**: `steps until the next rearrangement: -1000 → -1400 → -2000` and never resets - the async EPLB worker is blocked in `CpuGpuEvent.wait()` **with `pending_result` already published**, so it has finished its GPU transfer and is waiting for the main thread to consume it - there is **no warning, no error, no timeout, no exception, no metric** anywhere Because `step()` deliberately bails out (early `return`) while an async rearrangement is in flight, the counter is never reset and `rearrange()` is never called again. The stall is also **not free**. For as long as it persists, every forward pass still issues a cross-node, cross-DP gloo `all_reduce` in `_all_ranks_result_ready()` that can only ever return `False` (captured live on the main thread — see below), and per-step expert-load recording stays permanently enabled. To monitoring, this deployment is indistinguishable from a healthy one. ### Your current environment
Environment - vLLM version: `0.1.dev20904+g179dd0fa9` - Deployed image: vendor tag `deepseek-v41-dspark-eplb-pr56387-800b319ba8-backport`. The machinery involved here (`CpuGpuEvent`, `AsyncEplbLayerResult`, one EPLB layer transfer per forward pass, the `consumed_event` handshake) matches the upstream implementation introduced by #39431 — this is not vendor-invented code. Line numbers below are from that image and may be off by a few lines relative to `main`. - PyTorch: `2.13.0+cu130` - CUDA (driver-reported): 13.2, NVIDIA driver `595.58.03` - Hardware: 2 nodes × 8× NVIDIA H20 (SM90), cross-node over eRDMA/RoCE - NIXL: 1.3.2 (`nixl_cu13`), communicator `NixlEplbCommunicator` - Model: `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (40 MoE layers, 384 routed experts; DSpark drafter, 128 experts) - Parallelism: `tensor_parallel_size=8`, `data_parallel_size=2`, `enable_expert_parallel=True` → **EP16 across two nodes** (world size 16; `EP rank 0..15`, `EPLB rank 0..15`; node A = DP0/EP0-7, node B = DP1/EP8-15). The EP group therefore spans **both DP ranks and both nodes** — this matters below. - `moe_backend=deep_gemm`, `load_format=fp8_overlay`, `kv_cache_dtype=fp8`, `block_size=64`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.93`, `max_model_len=1048576` - Speculation: `method=dspark`, `num_speculative_tokens=5`, `enable_adaptive_verification=True` ```python EPLBConfig(window_size=1000, step_interval=1000, num_redundant_experts=64, log_balancedness=True, log_balancedness_interval=100, use_async=True, policy='default', communicator='nixl') ``` EPLB is enabled for the target model only; the DSpark drafter is correctly excluded (see [note on scope](#note-on-scope-dspark-draft-eplb-is-not-involved)).
### 🐛 Describe the bug The rearrangement step counter goes monotonically negative and never resets: ```text INFO 09-21 06:29:42 [eplb_state.py:601] EPLB step: 2300 ... steps until the next rearrangement: -1300 INFO 09-21 06:29:47 [eplb_state.py:601] EPLB step: 2400 ... steps until the next rearrangement: -1400 INFO 09-21 06:36:23 [eplb_state.py:601] EPLB step: 2500 ... steps until the next rearrangement: -1500 INFO 09-21 06:36:47 [eplb_state.py:601] EPLB step: 3000 ... steps until the next rearrangement: -2000 ``` `step_interval=1000`, so the counter should reset at 1000 and trigger a rearrange. It passed 1000, then 2000, then 3000, and kept counting. The `-1000` at step 2000 shows the first stall started at step 1000. At the same time, on **both pods** and on multiple EP ranks, the async worker is parked here: ```text Thread 966 (idle): "Thread-2 (thread_target)" wait (threading.py:355) wait (threading.py:655) wait (vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_utils.py:44) # self._recorded.wait() transfer_run_periodically (vllm/distributed/eplb/async_worker.py:160) Locals: ep_rank: 0 model_state: layer_idx: 27 num_layers: 40 transfer_metadata: consumed_event: thread_target (vllm/distributed/eplb/async_worker.py:37) ``` `consumed_event.wait()` is only reached **after** `model_state.pending_result = AsyncEplbLayerResult(...)` was published (`async_worker.py:150-160`), and `transfer_metadata` being live confirms the layer-27 transfer already completed. So the worker is not stuck on GPU work or on the NIXL transfer — it is waiting for the main thread to consume a result that is already visible. Reproduced identically on: - node A (`172.27.228.137`), `Worker_DP0_TP0_EP0` pid 222 → `eplb_utils.py:44`, `layer_idx: 27` - node B (`172.27.228.139`), `Worker_DP1_TP0_EP8` pid 178 → `eplb_utils.py:44` #### The stall is not idleness, and it is not free When the server is idle the worker freezes completely; when traffic arrives it makes almost no progress either. Under a sustained load burst (32 concurrent requests, `max_tokens=512`, ~500 forward passes, `avg_tokens` rising to 720 / `max_tokens` 1556) the counter only moved from `-1400` to `-2000` and the worker stayed parked at `eplb_utils.py:44`. Every request completed successfully throughout. While that load was running, `py-spy` caught the **main thread** inside the very collective that would have to return `True` to unblock the worker: ```text Thread 222 (idle): "MainThread" all_reduce (torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py:3252) wrapper (torch/distributed/c10d_logger.py:83) _all_ranks_result_ready (vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_state.py:996) step (vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_state.py:641) step (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/eplb_utils.py:126) wrapper (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/eplb_utils.py:32) execute_dummy_batch (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:1279) ``` So the stalled cycle keeps charging a cross-node, cross-DP gloo `all_reduce` to every step, and it can only ever return `False` while the state machine is wedged. #### DP ranks drift out of lockstep at the same time ```text WARNING 09-21 06:49:46 [coordinator.py:406] Received stats for out-of-order step (19, 0) from engine 0 (expected > (19, 1)) WARNING 09-21 06:55:09 [coordinator.py:406] Received stats for out-of-order step (24, 0) from engine 0 (expected > (24, 1)) WARNING 09-21 06:55:09 [coordinator.py:406] Received stats for out-of-order step (24, 0) from engine 0 (expected > (24, 1)) ``` This is directly relevant: as noted above, the EP cpu group in this deployment spans **both DP ranks**, so `_all_ranks_result_ready()`'s `all_reduce` is a collective whose membership is exactly the set of engines that the DP coordinator reports as out of order. Whether the drift is a cause or a consequence of the EPLB stall, it puts that collective squarely in the danger zone. ### Evidence that this is a silent failure While EPLB is in this state: ```text GET /health -> 200 (0.2 ms) GET /v1/models -> 200 (0.2 ms) POST /v1/completions -> 200, correct output, 0.199 s ``` No `warning`, `error`, `exception`, or timeout is emitted anywhere. The `_drain`/shutdown path emits `Draining async EPLB worker for model ...` and it never appears, so nothing is attempting to recover the in-flight cycle. One further observation we could not explain: the `EPLB step` line itself **stopped appearing entirely** after `06:36:47` — 0 occurrences in a 15-minute window during which the `coordinator.py:406` warnings above show engine 0 was still executing and reporting steps. If the counter genuinely stopped advancing, the last externally visible trace of this failure is gone too; if it is still advancing, the logging gate (`expert_rearrangement_step % log_balancedness_interval == 0`) is not behaving the way the code suggests. Maintainer input on this would be welcome. ### Code-level analysis The only path that clears `pending_result` and therefore unblocks the worker is `step()` → `_all_ranks_result_ready()` → `_move_to_workspace()`: ```python if self.is_async: for eplb_model_state in self.model_states.values(): # rebalanced must remain consistent amongst all ranks otherwise the # all_reduce in _all_ranks_result_ready will hang if eplb_model_state.rebalanced and self._all_ranks_result_ready( eplb_model_state ): _move_to_workspace(model_state=eplb_model_state, ep_rank=ep_group.rank()) if self.expert_rearrangement_step >= self.expert_rearrangement_step_interval: if self.is_async and any( eplb_model_state.rebalanced for eplb_model_state in self.model_states.values() ): # Still performing asynchronous rearrangement; update # should_record (step > step_interval, so always True) and # bail out before the step counter is reset. self._update_layer_should_record(log_stats=log_stats) return self.expert_rearrangement_step = 0 self.rearrange() ``` Several hazards are visible here, and the observed state is consistent with at least one of them firing: 1. **`_all_ranks_result_ready()` is an unconditional "all ranks must have a pending result" barrier with no timeout.** It is an AND over the whole EP cpu group (`int(flag.item()) == cpu_group.size()`). A single lagging rank — one that has already consumed layer N and is still inside `transfer_layer()` / `cuda_stream.synchronize()` / the coordinated-stop `all_reduce` for layer N+1, where `pending_result` is momentarily `None` — makes *every* rank's check return `False`, so *nobody* consumes, so the lagging rank never catches up. This is a livelock-shaped failure rather than a crash. 2. **The collective call itself is gated on `rebalanced`, which two threads mutate concurrently.** `_move_to_workspace()` clears it on the last layer (main thread) and the async worker clears it on the coordinated-stop path (`async_worker.py:126`). If the value diverges across ranks, the *number* of `all_reduce` calls per step diverges too, which turns a conditional collective into a call-count mismatch. The comment in the source already flags this as a hang risk. 3. **No timeout anywhere on the critical path.** `CpuGpuEvent.wait()` is `self._recorded.wait()` — a bare `threading.Event.wait()` with no timeout (`eplb_utils.py:44`), and the `all_reduce` in `_all_ranks_result_ready()` has no timeout either. A stalled cycle is therefore indistinguishable from a healthy one. 4. **The bail-out path is silent and unbounded.** The early `return` at `expert_rearrangement_step >= step_interval` never resets the counter and logs nothing, so once a cycle stalls the counter grows without bound, `_should_record_current_step()` is unconditionally true (extra per-step work), and `rearrange()` is skipped forever. 5. **Group asymmetry worth double-checking.** `_all_ranks_result_ready()` uses `get_ep_group().cpu_group`, while the rest of the async EPLB machinery uses `get_eplb_group()` (`async_worker.py:84-85`). `parallel_state.py:2209-2213` says the EPLB group is created as a *separate* process group specifically "to isolate EPLB communications ... with torch.distributed in execution". Using the EP group for one half of the handshake and the EPLB group for the other may be intentional, but it is worth confirming, since it means the two sides of the producer/consumer handshake are not even on the same communicator. It also couples the handshake to DP/EP membership — see the DP drift above. ### Note on scope: DSpark draft EPLB is not involved The DSpark drafter is correctly excluded from EPLB in this deployment (thanks to #56387), so this is purely a target-model EPLB issue: ```text WARNING 09-21 04:12:37 [utils.py:39] EPLB is disabled for the DSpark draft model. EPLB remains enabled for the target model. INFO 09-21 04:12:42 [eplb_utils.py:101] EPLB is enabled for MoE part of model /mnt/models. INFO 09-21 04:12:47 [eplb_communicator.py:96] Initialized EPLB communicator: NixlEplbCommunicator. ``` There is exactly one EPLB model state (the target), so the `for eplb_model_state in self.model_states.values()` loop performs a single collective per step. ### Suggested directions 1. Put a timeout and a diagnostic on `CpuGpuEvent.wait()` and on the `all_reduce` in `_all_ranks_result_ready()`, so a stalled cycle fails loudly (and reports which rank(s) did not publish a result) instead of hanging silently. 2. Log a warning when the `>= step_interval` bail-out is hit repeatedly, and/or surface the in-flight state (`rebalanced`, `pending_result.layer_idx`, per-rank presence) as a metric. Today the runaway negative counter is the *only* externally visible trace — and it stopped being emitted at all in our run. 3. Reconsider gating the `_all_ranks_result_ready()` collective on `rebalanced`. Making the collective unconditional — or at least ensuring all ranks agree on its membership — would remove the call-count mismatch class entirely. 4. Consider making progress independent of forward passes, or bounding how long a cycle may stay in flight before it is drained/aborted. 5. Confirm whether the EP-group/EPLB-group split in the handshake is deliberate, given that it makes the handshake's collective membership sensitive to DP rank lockstep. ### Duplicate-work check Searched issues and PRs for `EPLB async hang`, `EPLB rebalance hang rebalanced async`, `eplb async rearrange stuck`, `EPLB deadlock consumed_event`, `NixlEplbCommunicator`, and `EPLB communicator`. Closest hits, none of which cover this failure: - #51567 — `[Bug]: EPLB fails to transport E8M0 expert state` (startup-time failure with a clear error; different) - #27774 — `[RFC]: Fault-Tolerant Expert Parallelism` (proposes hang detection for *rank failures*; unrelated to this state-machine stall) - #39431 — `[EPLB] Add a shutdown mechanism for the Async EPLB worker` (open; a graceful-stop mechanism, not a stall fix) I can provide longer `py-spy` dumps, full worker logs, the exact image tag, or additional instrumentation data on request.

title: [Perf][Attention] Avoid redundant sparse attention metadata operations
body:
## Purpose

Sparse attention metadata preparation launches unnecessary GPU work on every decode step. Write SWA token validity directly into its persistent buffer, and compute compressed prefill sequence lengths only when the batch contains prefills.

For the tested DSV4.1 TP4 configuration, this eliminates four validity copies and one unused division per decode step. No new kernels, flags, or dispatch thresholds are introduced.

## Validation

Real-weight DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4x GB200, TP4, no speculative decoding, FlashInfer sparse attention, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE CUDA graphs, concurrency 1, exact 8192-input/1024-output tokens; eight requests per arm in the same loaded server:

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Mean TPOT | 4.467 ms | 4.457 ms |
| Median ITL | 4.383 ms | 4.365 ms |
| Median request TPOT | 4.414 ms | 4.422 ms |

This is a small reduction in typical token interval; mean TPOT is effectively flat. No material end-to-end speedup or tail-latency improvement is claimed. Serving measurements and evaluation were collected before rebasing this unchanged two-file patch onto current main, with the independent breakable-graph warmup fix present in both arms.

GSM8K five-shot greedy smoke: 126/128 (98.4375%) flexible extraction, matching the prior smoke score; strict extraction 107/128. This is a smoke evaluation, not a full accuracy result. Independent serving outputs were not bitwise identical (3/8 exact text matches).

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch_v2.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py -q -rs

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_swa.py
```

Tests: 101 passed, 8 expected skips for unsupported attention backend/cache combinations. The same test results and pre-commit pass were confirmed after rebasing onto current main.

## Duplicate check and AI assistance

Open-PR searches for validity, compressed sequence lengths, and metadata preparation found no equivalent change. #57756 concerns ROCm-specific metadata fusion; #57458 concerns GLM sparse MLA preparation. Neither modifies these operations. Constant-offset reuse overlapping #35561 was excluded.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped implement and validate this change.

Evaluation command (against the candidate server):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m lm_eval run --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args 'model=dsv41-gsm8k,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8003/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=2,timeout=600,max_retries=2,max_gen_toks=1024,max_length=16384,seed=123' \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=1024 temperature=0.0 do_sample=False "chat_template_kwargs={'thinking': False}" \
  --seed 123,123,123,123 --log_samples --output_path gsm8k --limit 128
```

title: [Spec Decode] Support Kimi-K3 MLA drafts in DFlash2
body:
## Purpose

Add support for `lightseekorg/kimi-k3-dflash2`, an MLA-based DFlash2 draft model for `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`.

The checkpoint advertises `DFlash2DraftModel` with `model_type: qwen3`, but uses MLA rather than the existing Qwen3 GQA backbone. This change recognizes `dflash_config.attention_mode: mla` and loads the corresponding draft implementation.

The implementation includes:
- MLA draft layers with DFlash2 grouped convolutions, candidate selection, and context KV precomputation.
- Non-causal sliding-window attention through Triton MLA, preserving visibility of subsequent tokens within the draft block.
- FlashInfer MLA as the default full-attention backend, with Triton MLA available as an alternative.
- KV cache metadata and configuration fixes for mixed target/draft attention, including preserving automatic block-size selection.
- CUDA graph support for uniform non-causal Triton MLA draft batches and independent target/draft graph compatibility checks.
- Usage documentation.

This is a draft PR. End-to-end serving has been brought up successfully; performance evaluation and unit-test coverage are still in progress.

## Duplicate-work checks

Public GitHub searches for open Kimi/DFlash PRs and Lightseek-related issues/PRs did not identify an equivalent Kimi-K3 MLA DFlash2 implementation.

Related work covers different scopes:
- #55960: DFlash2 grouped-convolution optimization.
- #56434: Kimi-K3 auxiliary hidden-state handling on ROCm.
- #48392: DFlash/DSpark support under decode context parallelism.

This PR adds the MLA DFlash2 draft backbone and its attention/cache integration. No specific issue is linked. Duplicate-work checks will be refreshed before marking the PR ready for review.

## Validation

- End-to-end serving: successfully exercised by the author on the source implementation.
- Performance evaluation: in progress; results will be added before requesting review.
- Unit tests: not included or run in this draft; coverage will be added in a follow-up update.
- Local checks on the migrated changes:
  - `git diff --check`: passed.
  - Python AST parsing of all 14 changed implementation files: passed.
  - Runtime, kernel, dependency, and build-definition files compared against the source implementation: identical.

The migrated branch has not yet been independently validated end to end. Reproducible serving commands, hardware/software configuration, and results will be added before marking this PR ready.

## Remaining work

- [ ] Add and run focused regression tests for model loading, MLA configuration, sliding-window attention, KV cache handling, and CUDA graphs.
- [ ] Validate existing GQA DFlash2 behavior.
- [ ] Document reproducible end-to-end commands and environment.
- [ ] Report output-correctness/model evaluation results.
- [ ] Report draft acceptance, latency, and throughput against a non-speculative baseline.
- [ ] Run the required lint/type checks.
- [ ] Complete human review of every changed line and rerun relevant tests.

## Current limitations

- Prefill and decode context parallelism are not supported.
- The grouped MLA context-cache write path requires BF16; FP16 fallback or explicit validation remains to be addressed.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to port the implementation, inspect compatibility, and prepare this description. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing every changed line, running the relevant tests and evaluations, and understanding and defending the change before requesting review.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Speed up small Engram lookups
body:
## Overview

Use two-row tiles for small Engram lookups, retaining the persistent 16-row path for larger batches. Complements #59327's sorted host lookups.

## Claims

Historical GB300 results: 1/2/4-user lookup kernels improved 6.1%/19.4%/28.1%. Six balanced serving pairs measured +0.11% throughput (95% CI −1.55% to +1.80%): no demonstrated serving gain.

Refreshed onto main `b0b23a48d4`. GB300, NGC 26.08: 64 isolated production-lookup cases passed, including host/HBM, sorting, padding and graph replay; both benchmark capture variants passed. Fixed the benchmark's stale kernel arguments. Ruff and Linux-targeted mypy passed. The Mac pre-commit type check hits main’s existing Linux-only `mmap.MADV_HUGEPAGE` constant. These checks do not replace the full integration suite or repeat the historical performance measurements.

The kernel math is unchanged. Small batches spread across more SMs; larger batches keep the existing launch policy. AI-assisted update; draft retained for review.

title: [Bug]: deepep_low_latency buffer sizing ignores EPLB redundant experts — 32 GiB limit hit, documented 2048 threshold is stale
body:
### Summary

With EPLB enabled and redundant experts configured, `moe.num_experts` is inflated (384 routed + 64 redundant = 448 in our case), and that inflated count is what reaches DeepEP's buffer sizing. DeepEP's low-latency path requires `num_rdma_bytes / 16 < INT_MAX`, i.e. a buffer below 32 GiB. The redundancy therefore silently consumes the buffer budget, and a configuration that looks fine against the documented 2048 threshold fails.

### Setup

- `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, hidden 5120, 384 routed experts, EP16
- `--enable-eplb --eplb-config '{"window_size":1000,"step_interval":1000,"num_redundant_experts":64,...}'`
- ⇒ engine logs `[EP Rank 0/16] Local/global: 28/448`
- The inflated `moe.num_experts` is what the all2all buffer construction path consumes (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/all2all_utils.py`)

### Buffer size vs `num_max_tokens_per_rank`

hidden=5120, num_ranks=16, num_experts=448:

| `num_max_tokens_per_rank` | `num_rdma_bytes` | under 32 GiB? |
|---:|---:|---|
| 2048 | 35.55 GiB | no |
| 1856 | 32.21 GiB | no |
| **1840** | **31.94 GiB** | **yes** |
| 1536 | 26.66 GiB | yes |

So the real ceiling is **≤ 1840**, not the 2048 the guidance implies. The 2048 figure appears to be computed against 384 experts and does not account for EPLB redundancy.

### Disclosure on methodology

We could not validate this end-to-end on our own hardware: our NICs are Alibaba eRDMA, and NVSHMEM's IBGDA transport is mlx5-only, so the low-latency path is unreachable for us (reported separately on the DeepEP repo). The numbers above come from the buffer sizing formula, not from a completed run. Flagging that explicitly so the claim is not overstated.

### Questions

1. Should buffer sizing use the **non-redundant** expert count, given that EPLB redundancy is a placement detail rather than a change to the routed expert space?
2. If it must use the inflated count, could we get a config-time validation that fails fast with a message naming `num_redundant_experts` as the amplifier? Right now the failure surfaces far downstream and the error does not point at the cause.
3. If the 2048 threshold is quoted elsewhere, it likely needs the same correction.

---

*Written with AI assistance from operator-collected measurements on the deployment above; the human submitter reviewed the content.*

title: [RFC]: Stable runtime tensor lifecycle for sleep and live weight reload
body:
### Motivation.

Some models and kernel helpers store weight-derived tensors as ordinary Python attributes. These allocations are invisible to module buffer traversal, sleep-mode level-2 restoration, and generic graph-storage management. Merely registering a buffer does not solve reload correctness: PWAL can produce a correct temporary value, after which layerwise reload restores the old graph-captured allocation with stale contents. Helpers can also retain aliases to temporary storage.

This RFC establishes common **module ownership, stable in-place updates, and a reload completion lifecycle**, building on #53509 and [aoshen02/vllm#56](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/56).

### Proposed Change.

## State ownership and semantics

Every tensor storage that must survive sleep, reload, or CUDA Graph replay belongs to an `nn.Module`. Non-module helpers retain aliases, metadata, and Python control state.

| State | Owner | Update policy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Checkpoint Parameter | Module | checkpoint loader |
| Processed/runtime Parameter | Module | PWAL or supported selective transform |
| Static runtime buffer | Module | preserve |
| Weight-derived buffer | Module | commit or recompute in place |
| Helper attribute | alias to module storage | rebind |
| Runtime/protocol state | Module | protocol-specific reset |

Do not classify every non-persistent buffer as derived. Do not convert existing processed Parameters to buffers solely for this RFC.

## Derived-buffer contract

`register_derived_buffer(module, name)` declares a non-persistent `None` placeholder and records the name in a module-local semantic registry (`_vllm_derived_buffers`).

`set_derived_buffer(module, name, value)` requires a declared derived buffer, returns the installed tensor, and follows:

- First materialization: `None → Tensor`, before graph capture for graph-visible state.
- Subsequent updates: `existing.copy_(value)`; preserve the allocation.
- Shape, dtype, or device mismatch: raise; a full reload/graph recapture is required.

Metadata capture and meta restoration must retain `None` placeholders. The derived schema is independent of freshness: restore declared derived entries as `None`, even if metadata was captured after materialization, and retain declarations introduced by a later class swap or PWAL. A first value produced during reload becomes stable storage if the snapshot had no materialized allocation. Non-persistent buffers remain outside `state_dict()`.

## Two distinct derived-state update mechanisms

### 1. PWAL-produced representations with discarded sources

Some packed representations cannot be recomputed after PWAL because the original loader-side weight has been released. Explicitly marked derived buffers therefore participate in layerwise copy-back:

```text
load W2 into temporary layer → PWAL produces D2
→ validate stable A against D2 → A.copy_(D2)
→ restore A on the owning module
```

For module-level transforms that consume/release checkpoint sources, opt affected source modules into `_vllm_defer_weights_reload`. Their newly loaded weights remain staged until a parent/owner `process_weights_for_reload()` transform consumes them; the core restores stable runtime storage only after those transforms complete. This phase owns any child PWAL it requires. Native MegaMoE/shared experts, vision MoE, and ROCm preshuffle use this boundary. Every reload must regenerate representations from the current staged sources; cached runtime state does not establish freshness.

Preparation/eligibility hooks run before any meta placement: quant-method `prepare_for_reload(layer)` and module `prepare_for_reload()` can invalidate processing guards or reject unsupported reload safely.

This happens before final placement. Unmarked non-persistent buffers that were not checkpoint-loaded retain the existing preservation policy. A secondary cache with no temporary value must be refreshed by its completion hook; source-dropping representations require a produced value.

### 2. Secondary state recomputable from final weights

FP32 mirrors, inverse scales, merged convolution weights, and other surviving-source caches use explicit refresh methods:

```text
restore final stable W2 and buffer storage
→ post_weights_reload()
→ stable_buffer.copy_(derive(W2))
```

Cold processing and reload share the derivation logic. An already materialized lazy cache still needs refresh: `buffer is not None` says nothing about freshness.

## Generic helper alias API

Provide generic `bind_runtime_buffer(owner, consumer, consumer_attr, owner_buffer_name)` and `rebind_runtime_buffers(owner, consumer)`. Record attribute-to-buffer mappings and validate ownership; the generic implementation has no hard-coded `_moe_` namespace.

Binding does not decide whether contents are derived, static, or protocol state. Derived contents use the derived-buffer setter; static contents are preserved; protocol state uses its own reset lifecycle. Model/backend callers choose buffer names.

## Common completion hook

`post_weights_reload()` begins only after the current update's primary/runtime weights and graph-visible storage are in their final stable locations. It may refresh secondary state, rebind aliases, invalidate caches, and validate runtime invariants. It must not depend on meta layers, `kernel_tensors`, or temporary PWAL storage.

The dispatcher runs **quant method first, module second**, exactly once per successfully completed layer reload. Hooks are idempotent. Ordinary processing, no-loaded-weight restoration, and deferred attention must obey the same boundary. Completion is dispatched after all primary storage is restored, children before parents, so parent caches can read their child weights. Attention's completion hook follows its final PWAL/scale handling.

```text
layerwise: load → PWAL → commit processed derived values
           → restore stable storage → post_weights_reload()
```

## Compatibility with selective reload (#54477)

The proposed integration is:

```text
restore_weights_before_loading()
→ weight_loader()
→ refresh_derived_state()
→ post_weights_reload()
```

The selective finish phase produces final primary representations and may already refresh supported secondary state. The common completion hook then performs any remaining refresh/alias recovery; sharing derivation routines must avoid double application of destructive transforms. This RFC supplies storage/lifecycle primitives; it does not enable selective reload for unsupported backends or replace #54477's eligibility and failure contracts. A future common selective dispatcher should invoke completion rather than requiring each model to call it manually.

## Sleep/wake and protocol boundary

Keep `post_weights_reload()` and `post_weights_wake_up()` separate. Humming locks are protocol state: rebind after reload, rebind/reset after wake. Resetting Humming's `processed` flag is only legacy layerwise compatibility, not a selective-reload requirement. MiniMax Lamport flags, sentinels, layouts, and pointer arrays use protocol-specific wake recovery.

## Implementation split and merge order

All implementation branches start directly from upstream main. Each PR contains only its own changes; none includes another unmerged PR's commits. API dependencies are expressed as merge order rather than stacked branches. After a prerequisite merges, rebase the affected independent branch onto main before integration CI.

| Recommended order | Slice | PR | Changed files | Merge prerequisite |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Core ownership, derived schema, helper aliases, staging, preflight, stable copy-back and ordered completion | #53509 | 14 | main |
| 2 | GLM5-next FP32 mirror and merged convolution | #58991 | 3 | #53509 |
| 3 | Kimi MLA inverse scales | #58992 | 2 | #53509 |
| 4 | Native DeepSeek/Kimi MegaMoE routed/shared packed buffers | #59003 | 4 | #53509 |
| 5 | DeepSeek V4/V4.1 hyperconnection broadcast | #58995 | 4 | #53509 |
| 6 | ROCm projection preshuffle and scales | #58999 | 4 | #53509 |
| 7 | CPU packed projection and FP32 norm cache | #58996 | 3 | #53509 |
| 8 | FlashInfer NVFP4 epilogue alpha ownership | #59002 | 2 | #53509; recommended after #59003 |
| 9 | dots3 vision fused experts and retained loader topology | #59001 | 2 | #53509 |
| 10 | Gemma4 MTP TP gathered head and static suppression indices | #59000 | 2 | #53509 |
| 11 | Humming module-owned locks and wake/reload protocol recovery | #53510 | 3 | #53509 |
| 12 | MiniMax Lamport wake protocol recovery | #53511 | 3 | #53510 wake dispatcher |

Orders 2–10 are primarily an orderly review/merge sequence: these migrations are sibling branches, and unrelated model slices can merge in another order once #53509 is present. Shared edits in model files should be reconciled during the post-merge rebase, without adding prerequisite commits to PR diffs.

All model/backend modifications in aoshen02/vllm#56 are assigned above. The port adds freshness and staged-transform handling instead of reproducing registration-only changes. Source-dropping conversions require complete checkpoint source groups; this work does not enable selective reload. XPU MegaMoE retains its existing unsupported runtime guard.

FlashInfer scope is deliberately limited to the explicit alpha tensors. External packed weights and opaque backend state still need their own ownership protocol, so initialized FlashInfer MegaMoE reload is explicitly rejected instead of silently retaining old backend weights. Suppression indices are static buffers, not derived state.

The end-to-end CUDA Graph oracle remains a separate validation follow-up, proposed in the issue discussion with ownership not yet confirmed. No empty validation PR has been created, and no graph/backend runtime pass is claimed.

Related alternative work: #49789 uses ReloadArena tensor/object slots and identity checks on a release branch; #55595 owns selective FP8 MoE reload; #57733 improves cold post-load traversal. These migrations use module buffers and a shared reload lifecycle rather than introducing another arena, selective engine, or cold traversal redesign.

## Validation requirements

Core regressions cover stable pointers and changed values, source-dropping PWAL copy-back, helper identity, lazy cache refresh, repeated A → B → A updates, placeholder round trips, ordered/exactly-once completion, and shape/dtype/device rejection. Model-specific PRs add focused regression coverage. Local validation uses Ruff lint/format, Python compilation, diff whitespace checks, test-tether checks, and sign-off auditing. Windows pytest collection is blocked by missing uvloop; runtime/backend/graph checks remain pending. No remote H20 validation was requested or run.

The end-to-end CUDA Graph oracle compares cold B with cold A followed by live B, checking output correctness, graph-visible pointers, derived values, and aliases. Sleep/wake protocol validation stays in its separate PRs.

### Feedback Period.

Please allow at least one week for RFC feedback before implementation is merged.

_No response_

### Any Other Things.

title: [Bugfix] Honor tokenizer revision in DeepSeek V4.1 Engram
body:
# [Bugfix] Honor tokenizer_revision when building DeepSeek V4.1 Engram hashes

## Purpose

`NgramHashState` independently loads a tokenizer to build its compressed token
map. It currently passes `model_config.revision`, while the serving tokenizer
uses `model_config.tokenizer_revision`. Explicitly selecting a tokenizer
revision can therefore load a different vocabulary for Engram, or fail if the
model revision does not exist in the tokenizer repository.

Use `tokenizer_revision` consistently. The existing ModelConfig fallback already
handles configurations that do not specify an independent tokenizer revision.
No hashing math, kernels, checkpoint weights, or serving parameters are changed.

The regression covers differing revisions, a tokenizer-only revision, and the
same-revision control. Two vocabularies have the same compressed vocabulary size
but different mappings; the test checks the actual constructed mapping rather
than only asserting a mocked call.

## Duplicate Work

On 2026-09-21, searches for open PRs matching `Engram tokenizer` and issues
matching `"Engram" "revision"` found no fix for this selection mismatch. Other
Engram kernel/performance/parallelism PRs address different behavior.

## Test Result

Base: `3c84ad13ed3f9fcd816bf1d15acb83c28cfa02f9`.

- Focused regression on unchanged main: 2 failures, 1 passing same-revision control.
- Local fixed source, real CPU torch/tokenizers/transformers: 3 passed.
- Both modified files pass applicable pre-commit hooks.
- H20 installed-code suite: 74 passed, 38 deselected (28 regression cases plus
  46 existing CUDA/Triton cases, including graph replay). One unregistered
  `distributed` marker warning comes from the isolated test configuration.
- Restarted the real Flash TP8 H20 service with only these two source hunks
  installed: 10/10 identical HTTP smoke cases pass before and after the change,
  plus 5/5 additional unbiased image/color/counting checks after restart.
  Runtime: vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev422+gd05da62e9`, torch `2.13.0+cu130`,
  real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash weights, TP8+EP and DSpark (5 draft tokens,
  adaptive verification disabled). The original versions of the two target
  modules are byte-for-byte identical to the main base noted above.

The local CPU harness AST-loads source definitions and replaces unused vLLM
types. It is not a full vLLM integration run. The GPU validation separately uses
the real installed vLLM runtime.

## Test Plan

Focused upstream regression command:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py -k uses_tokenizer_revision -q
```

The H20 harness invoked pytest on the real installed modules with these arguments
(the second file was staged from the separate vision-profiling fix):

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --tb=short --confcutdir=tests \
  -o addopts= -p no:cacheprovider \
  -k 'uses_tokenizer_revision or profile_image or default_profile or hash_cache_replay or lookback_window_reproduces or lookup_matches_torch or fused_engram_post_wkv' \
  tests/kernels/test_engram.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_deepseek_v41.py
```

Both fixes were installed for the real-service integration run; only Engram's
revision selection and its regression belong to this PR. All requests were
serial, capped at 128 output tokens. The smoke checks are not a comprehensive
model accuracy benchmark, and no performance improvement is claimed.

## Scope and Accountability

The change was developed with AI assistance (OpenAI Codex). The submitting human
has reviewed the changes and confirmed personally rerunning the relevant tests
for these new fixes successfully. Automated test results above were also
collected by the assistant; the submitter's confirmation is separate.

A local-checkpoint service smoke test does not demonstrate independent remote
revision selection: a local tokenizer directory ignores Hub revision lookup.
The targeted revision regression provides that selection coverage. No claim is
made that this bug explains any prior production deadlock or corrupted output.

title: fix(flashmla): bypass aten::new_empty int32 overflow during massive dummy runs
body:
Fixes #57878.

**Root Cause**: 
During the engine initialization dummy run with `--enforce-eager` on SM90, a massive dummy shape (e.g., 16384 tokens) causes the FlashMLA C++ backend's internal shape math to overflow PyTorch's 32-bit `aten::new_empty` integer limit, triggering an immediate crash.

**Fix**:
Truncate the query tensor to a safe element boundary before calling the C++ kernel during the dummy run. After the kernel executes, we pad the output tensor back to its full massive size (e.g., 2.14GB) using Python's `new_zeros` (which safely uses 64-bit sizes). This correctly reserves the memory for the profiler without crashing the C++ dispatcher.

title: [Spec Decode] Support Kimi-K3 MLA drafts in DFlash2
body:
## Purpose

Add support for `lightseekorg/kimi-k3-dflash2`, an MLA-based DFlash2 draft model for `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`.

The checkpoint advertises `DFlash2DraftModel` with `model_type: qwen3`, but requires an MLA backbone. This change recognizes `dflash_config.attention_mode: mla` and loads the corresponding implementation.

Supersedes #57892, which I closed while correcting the branch base. This draft is based on `main` and contains one adaptation commit, without the unrelated release-branch commits.

## Changes

- Add the Kimi-K3 MLA draft backbone, reusing DFlash2 grouped convolutions and candidate selection.
- Implement latent context KV precomputation and checkpoint weight loading.
- Support non-causal sliding-window attention through Triton MLA, retaining visibility of later tokens in the draft block.
- Default full-attention layers to FlashInfer MLA, with Triton MLA available as an alternative.
- Preserve non-causal metadata when merging sliding-window MLA cache specifications and preserve automatic block-size selection when overriding the draft cache dtype.
- Evaluate target CUDA graph support independently of draft attention layers using the existing main-branch interfaces.
- Document configuration and usage.

## Duplicate-work checks

This replaces the closed #57892 rather than introducing a parallel implementation.

The initial public GitHub searches for Kimi/DFlash and Lightseek-related work did not identify an equivalent Kimi-K3 MLA DFlash2 adaptation. Related work covers different scopes:

- #55960: DFlash2 grouped-convolution optimization, now present in the main baseline and reused here.
- #56434: Kimi-K3 auxiliary hidden-state handling on ROCm.
- #48392: DFlash/DSpark support under decode context parallelism.

Duplicate-work checks will be refreshed before requesting review.

## Validation and current status

**This PR is a draft.**

End-to-end serving was successfully exercised on the original v0.28.0-based implementation. The main-based revision has not yet been validated end to end. Performance evaluation is in progress; no performance improvement is claimed yet.

Checks completed on this revision:

- `PRE_COMMIT_HOME=/tmp/vllm-office-pre-commit .venv/bin/pre-commit run` — passed, including Ruff, formatting, mypy for Python 3.10, and Markdown checks.
- `git diff --cached --check` — passed.
- Python AST parsing of all 12 changed Python files — passed.

Unit tests have intentionally not been included or run in this draft and will be added in a follow-up update.

Before marking this PR ready for review:

- [ ] Add and run focused regression tests for model loading, configuration, attention, KV cache handling, and CUDA graphs.
- [ ] Validate existing GQA DFlash2 behavior.
- [ ] Validate end-to-end serving on this main-based revision.
- [ ] Provide reproducible commands, checkpoint revisions, and hardware/software details.
- [ ] Report output-correctness/model evaluation results.
- [ ] Report acceptance length, latency, and throughput against a non-speculative baseline.
- [ ] Complete human review of every changed line and reproduce the relevant checks.

## Current limitations

- Prefill and decode context parallelism are not supported.
- The grouped MLA context-cache write path requires BF16 inputs; FP16 fallback or explicit validation remains to be addressed.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to port the implementation, resolve conflicts with main, inspect compatibility, run static checks, and prepare this description. The human submitter remains responsible for reviewing every changed line, running the relevant tests and evaluations, and understanding and defending the implementation.

title: [ROCm][PERF] Enable MiniMax-M3 Indexer CP
body:
## Purpose

Adds **indexer-only context parallelism** for the MiniMax-M3 lightning indexer on ROCm (gfx950), opt-in behind `--attention-config '{"indexer_cp": true}'`. Under tensor parallelism each rank owns one index head and scores *every*
128-token block, so at long context every rank re-reads the whole index cache on every decode step and that cost grows linearly with the context. This PR inverts the split: every rank projects **all** index heads and scores **1/P of the
blocks**, then one small exchange gives each rank every shard's candidates for the heads it owns. That turns the index-cache reads into `1/P`, which is the only term here that scales with context.

This PR depends on Aiter PR: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6359
