title: [ROCm][Quantization][MOE] Enable fused shared experts for MXFP8 checkpoints
body:
## Purpose
`is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible` only recognises `DeepseekV4FP8Config`, `QuarkConfig` and `Fp8Config`, and refuses everything else, so [MiniMax-M3-MXFP8](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8) (a `ModelOptMxFp8Config` checkpoint) hits the fallthrough and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` is a no-op that only logs a warning. Shared-expert fusion was enabled for this exact model by #46545 (Jun 26) and worked until #51695 (Aug 18) introduced this refuse-by-default quantization gate, which silently turned it back off; CI missed it because `test_models_fse_init` covers `minimax_m3` but installs a `QuarkConfig`. 

This adds the missing `ModelOptMxFp8Config` branch: MXFP8 carries a single whole-model quant algo plus `exclude_modules` and no per-layer config, so consistent exclusion of routed and shared experts is exactly what guarantees the shared expert has the same weight format as the routed slot it is appended into. Partially excluded packed shards are already rejected by `is_layer_skipped`, and MXFP8 is always 1x32 block-scaled with a leading expert dimension on its scales.
## Test Plan
Serving A/B on MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, TP4 on MI355X, identical stack with and without the fix, to
show the now-reachable fused path is a win on throughput and neutral on quality: 8K/1K
throughput at concurrency 1/16/64, and gsm8k on the full 1319-doc test split, 5-shot.

## Test Result
`tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py`, run on MI355X in
`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`:

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| unmodified `main` | 84 passed |
| new cases, unpatched `vllm` | 5 failed, all `shared-expert FSE quantization compatibility is not implemented for ModelOptMxFp8Config` |
| patched | 89 passed |

### Serving A/B

`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8`, TP4 on MI355X, in `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`
(image id `d65c1f85e583`, `vllm 0.3.1.dev190+g3df4ae153`). Both arms run the same image and
the same command below; the only difference is whether this patch is applied before the
server starts. Env for both arms:

```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1
VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1
VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
```

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port $PORT \
    --language-model-only \
    --tensor-parallel-size=4 \
    --max-model-len=131072 \
    --block-size=128 \
    --kv-cache-dtype=fp8 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization=0.85 \
    --max-num-seqs=64 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens=32768 \
    '--attention-config={"backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA","indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' \
    --moe-backend=aiter \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    '--compilation-config={"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","max_cudagraph_capture_size":512}'
```

Note that `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` is set in *both* arms; without the
patch it is simply ignored, which is the bug. The logs confirm the arms really differ:
unpatched emits 228 `not implemented for ModelOptMxFp8Config` refusals (57 MoE layers x 4
ranks) and builds the aiter MoE with `128, 4` experts, patched emits none and builds
`129, 5`, the extra slot being the fused shared expert.

#### Throughput

`vllm bench serve`, random 8192-in / 1024-out, `--ignore-eos --temperature=0 --seed=42`,
10/80/320 prompts at concurrency 1/16/64:

| conc | tok/s no FSE | tok/s FSE | delta | TPOT no FSE | TPOT FSE | delta | TTFT no FSE | TTFT FSE | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 121.7 | 154.4 | **+26.9%** | 8.00 ms | 6.26 ms | **-21.8%** | 234.1 ms | 233.6 ms | -0.2% |
| 16 | 988.2 | 1101.7 | **+11.5%** | 14.27 ms | 12.63 ms | **-11.5%** | 1878.5 ms | 1815.4 ms | -3.4% |
| 64 | 1841.9 | 2077.9 | **+12.8%** | 31.85 ms | 28.18 ms | **-11.5%** | 2921.1 ms | 2812.8 ms | -3.7% |

#### Accuracy

`lm_eval==0.4.12`, gsm8k full test split (1319 docs, no `--limit`), 5-shot, greedy, task
defaults otherwise. Server as above except `--max-model-len=4096`:

```bash
python3 -m lm_eval \
    --model local-completions \
    --tasks gsm8k \
    --num_fewshot 5 \
    --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=1024 \
    --log_samples \
    --output_path <out> \
    --model_args "base_url=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/v1/completions,\
model=MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8,tokenized_requests=False,num_concurrent=32,max_length=4096"
```

| filter | no FSE | FSE |
|---|---|---|
| strict-match | 0.8992 +/- 0.0083 | 0.8923 +/- 0.0085
| flexible-extract | 0.8992 +/- 0.0083 | 0.8931 +/- 0.0085

title: [Spec Decode] Enable GLM-5.2 DSpark under pipeline parallelism
body:
## Summary

Enable GLM-5.2 (`DeepseekV32ForCausalLM`) to support DSpark speculative
decoding under pipeline parallelism by extending the community #50514
`relay_aux_hidden_states` mechanism to the DeepSeek-V3.2 backbone.

## Motivation

#50514 introduced `supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp` and the
`relay_aux_hidden_states` / `pack_local_aux_hidden_states` /
`collect_remote_aux_hidden_states` family to carry DSpark/EAGLE-3 aux
hidden states across PP stages. This covers DeepSeek-V4, Kimi-K3, Llama,
and Qwen2.

GLM-5.2 reuses the DeepSeek-V3.2 (`deepseek_v32`) backbone but does not
set `supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp`, so DSpark under PP cannot relay
aux hidden states across stages — `collect_remote_aux_hidden_states`
returns `[]` and the draft never sees upstream aux. This PR fills that
gap.

## Modifications

All changes are in `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/nvidia/model.py` (+16, -5):

1. **Inherit `EagleModelMixin`**: `DeepseekV32Model` now inherits
   `EagleModelMixin` and sets `supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp = True`,
   enabling the #50514 relay path for GLM-5.2.

2. **Fix `set_aux_hidden_state_layers` bypass**: The parent
   `DeepseekV2ForCausalLM.set_aux_hidden_state_layers` directly assigns
   `self.model.aux_hidden_state_layers = layers`, bypassing
   `EagleModelMixin._set_aux_hidden_state_layers` and leaving
   `_aux_slot_base_cached` at 0. This breaks
   `collect_remote_aux_hidden_states`. Override to call
   `self.model._set_aux_hidden_state_layers(layers)`.

3. **Switch to capture-after**: Change `if idx in aux` to
   `if idx + 1 in aux` (and move the capture after the layer call). This
   aligns with the `bisect_right` base-offset used by `pack_local` /
   `collect_remote`. Without this, an aux layer at a PP stage boundary
   (e.g. aux 39 at stage start 39) is mis-assigned and the relay index
   collides.

4. **Integrate relay in forward**: Add `collect_remote_aux_hidden_states`
   at the top, `pack_local_aux_hidden_states` in the non-last-rank
   return, and merge `remote_aux + aux_hidden_states` on the last rank.

## Verification

Aux layer assignment with `aux = [2, 20, 39, 58, 75]`, `pp = 4`,
`partitions = [19, 20, 20, 19]`:

| Stage | start | base | local aux | pack indices |
|-------|-------|------|-----------|--------------|
| 0 | 0 | 0 | [2] | [0] |
| 1 | 19 | 1 | [20, 39] | [1, 2] |
| 2 | 39 | 3 | [58] | [3] |
| 3 | 59 | 4 | [75] | [4] |

Last rank collects `aux_states_0..3` and adds local `aux_states_4`,
yielding `[2, 20, 39, 58, 75]` — matching the draft config's
`aux_hidden_state_layer_ids`.

## Test

```bash
# Existing EAGLE-3 PP test (confirms relay framework not broken)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/eagle/test_eagle3_pp.py -v
```

## CI Label Request

I'm a first-time contributor (0 merged PRs), so the pre-commit workflow
can't trigger without a label. Could a maintainer add `verified` so I can
confirm my DCO sign-off and lint/format pass? This PR only touches
`deepseek_v32/nvidia/model.py` (+16/-5), so `verified` should be
sufficient at this stage. Thanks!

title: [ROCm][DO NOT MERGE] RDNA3 (gfx1100) full inference stack — tracking branch for splitting into landable PRs
body:
## What this is

**Draft, do not merge.** This is my long-running `perf/rdna3_full_stack` branch: the
complete inference stack I run on 4× RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100, RDNA3, PCIe P2P — no XGMI). It
stays open as a single tracking PR so ROCm maintainers can see the whole picture and tell
me **which pieces are worth landing and in what order**. Each piece goes out as a small,
self-contained PR against a fresh `main`; nothing here is proposed for merge as-is.

The branch last merged `main` at `df417f780a` (2026-10-07). Measured against that
merge-base, the branch adds ~28k lines in 160 files; part of the commit list is merge
drift of work of mine that already landed (#41394, #44075, #40835, #39931, #55522,
#60388).

## Status as of 2026-10-08

| piece | PR | state |
|---|---|---|
| qwen4_exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) AMD path in fp16 | #60650 | open, ready for review |
| qwen4_exp fused HyperConnection for gfx1100 decode (+5.8% decode) | #60657 | draft, stacked on #60650 |
| qwen4_exp 4-bit NF4 n-gram embedding table (AMD) | #60670 | draft, waits for #56273 (NVFP4 table, same interface) |
| Octave KV (`ROCM_OCTAVE`), native 3-bit KV cache | #59774 | draft |
| RDNA3 W4A16 MoE: N-first compressed-tensors layout | #60388 | **merged** |
| RDNA3 W4A16 MoE: cold-expert CPU offload | #49321 | draft, experimental |
| Native HIP MXFP4 (dense + MoE) for RDNA3 | #46676 | open (separate branch, not in this one) |

## Hardware and models under test

| | |
|---|---|
| GPUs | 4× RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100), TP4, PCIe P2P (no XGMI) |
| ROCm / torch | ROCm 7.2.3, torch 2.11 |
| Models | Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 27B dense W4A16 (hybrid GDN + full attention); Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (qwen4_exp) pruned to 256 experts, GPTQ W4A16 asymmetric; gpt-oss-20b MXFP4 |
| Serving | fp16, CUDA graphs on, MTP speculative decoding (k=3), INT8 per-token-head or Octave KV cache |

This is a configuration nothing in vLLM CI covers: RDNA3 + wave32 + no MFMA + no XGMI +
hybrid Mamba/attention + quantized KV cache.

## What is in the branch

Grouped by what I think a landable PR would look like. Marked **generic** where the
change is platform-independent.

1. **HIP INT8/INT4 per-token-head attention kernels for gfx1100** — paged prefill
   (`csrc/attention/paged_prefill_attn_rdna3_v2*.cu`, INT8 with WMMA QK), split-KV decode
   (`pth_decode_int{4,8}_rdna3.cu`), a GQA-grouped decode, an INT8 decode on WMMA with
   independent waves, and a GQA-packed WMMA prefix attention for head size 256. A previous
   attempt was #41455 (closed). Related, different target: #43835 (CDNA). Largest block
   without a PR; I would split it into decode and prefill.
2. **Octave KV** — #59774. Pending for that PR: a per-layer exact window (the qwen4_exp
   MTP draft layer needs exact keys up to ~1000 positions back; with the default 64 it
   accepts ~15% fewer tokens per step) and `--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers` support in the
   AMD QSA, both in this branch.
3. **qwen4_exp on AMD** — fp16 (#60650), fused HyperConnection (#60657), a 4-bit NF4
   n-gram embedding table (#60670, draft until #56273 lands: that PR adds NVFP4 through the
   same interface and rejects it on AMD), and the Octave main KV cache for the QSA (part of
   #59774). Related: #59442 (HyperConnection on CDNA through AITER), #55040 (FP8 n-gram
   table).
4. **RDNA3 W4A16 GEMM beyond #41394** — decode kernels for the 5..128-row GEMMs of
   speculative-decode verification (WMMA), a `v_dot2` kernel for fp16 at 1..10 rows, a
   128×128 WMMA prefill tile, an exact fp16 dequant and a deterministic split-K. No PR yet.
5. **RDNA3 W4A16 MoE** — asymmetric (zero-point) checkpoints, the next PR now that #60388
   is merged; cold-expert offload (#49321); an optional shared expert-LoRA.
6. **Triton prefill launch tuning for wave32** — BLOCK_M / num_warps by sequence length.
   Overlaps #52684 and #56232 (both open, by others).
7. **Hybrid KV page-size unification by LCM** (`70d00a2a23`) — **generic**. Needed when
   a Mamba/GDN state page and a quantized attention page disagree on block size.
8. **gfx11 custom all-reduce over PCIe P2P** — custom all-reduce and QuickReduce enabled
   on gfx11, plus my own all-reduce kernel (low-latency protocols, fused with the
   following RMSNorm). On a Z790 chipset host peer reads returned zeros while writes
   worked; on a PCIe switch host all P2P works. **Overlaps #57767** (open, by another
   author); if that lands, this block should be reconciled with it or dropped.
9. **Model Runner V2** — a prefill lane that runs long prefills concurrently with decode,
   sampling from gathered top-k logits under TP, and a restricted vocabulary for the MTP
   draft head (+6.3% tok/s, no acceptance loss). The prefill lane touches core
   scheduling and would need a design discussion first.
10. **ROCm correctness fixes** — blocking H2D for GDN chunk metadata and conv1d program
    indices, stale CUDA-graph `mid_o` pointer on the int8 decode path, unbounded split-K
    `mid_o` allocation, per-token-head KV metadata not refreshed on the spec-decode
    verify step, GDN readout buffer dtype, GDN reads/writes in place in spec decode.
    Several are **generic** or Mamba-generic, and are the ones I would send first.
11. **Unconditional zero-temperature guard in the sampler** (`0aa0085946`) —
    **generic**. The guard only ran when the batch already contained a greedy request,
    so a single `temperature=0` probe could poison a batch.
12. **Qwen3 tool parser: terminate a parameter at the surrounding structure**
    (`053a5b773d`) — **generic**. Overlaps #50955 (open, by another author).

## Measured results

Kernel microbenchmark, ctx=8000 ql=512, 2× RX 7900 XTX TP2, Qwen3.6-27B W4A16:

| Kernel | Time | vs Triton baseline |
|---|---|---|
| Triton INT8 per-token-head | ~25 ms | — |
| HIP INT8 | **3.03 ms** | **8.3×** |
| HIP INT4 | **3.05 ms** | **8.2×** |
| Triton FP16, default M16w4 | 11.2 ms | — |
| Triton FP16, tuned M64w4 | **3.0 ms** | **3.7×** |

End-to-end TTFT, same setup (attention is ~20% of runtime here, GEMM dominates, so an
8× kernel win yields ~10% e2e and grows with context):

| Prompt | Baseline FP16 | INT8 full stack | INT4 full stack |
|---|---|---|---|
| ~2K | 2.81 s | 2.74 s (−2.5%) | 2.78 s (−1%) |
| ~8K | 11.15 s | 10.99 s (−1.4%) | 11.25 s (+1%) |
| ~16K | 23.74 s | 22.52 s (−5.1%) | 22.96 s (−3.3%) |
| ~24K | 38.44 s | **34.84 s (−9.4%)** | **35.49 s (−7.7%)** |

KV cache capacity at a fixed 33.3 GB budget — the metric that actually decides what the
card can serve:

| KV dtype | Max context | Concurrent @8K | Concurrent @32K |
|---|---|---|---|
| FP16 | 136K | 17 | 4 |
| INT8 | 273K | **34** | **8** |
| INT4 | **545K** | **68** | **17** |

Qwen3.8-27B W4A16 G32, TP4, INT8 per-token-head KV, MTP k=3: sustained **113–119 tok/s
decode** at both short and 167K context, mean speculative acceptance 3.13/4 on real code
traffic.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next pruned to 256 experts, GPTQ W4A16, TP4, 512K context, MTP k=3:

| | value |
|---|---|
| KV cache, fp16 → `octave_k3v3` | 398K → **1.98M tokens** |
| decode, one user | 105–114 tok/s (peaks ~149) |
| fused HyperConnection, fp16 KV, no MTP | 72.5 → **76.6 tok/s (+5.8%)** |
| MTP layer exact window 64 → 1020 | tokens per step +11–27% on code, JSON, tables and refactors, +3% on prose; 4.00/4 on a counting task |
| GSM8K (chat, no thinking, 200 q) | 96.0% |

Quality: INT8 per-token-head is cosine 1.000000 against the FP16 reference (symmetric,
no precision loss); INT4 is 0.999995.

## Why this is not mergeable as it stands

- 94 commits behind `main` today; every piece is rebased onto a fresh `main` when it
  goes out on its own.
- **No CI covers gfx1100.** The kernels are guarded to gfx1100 and compile out elsewhere
  (there are compile-guard tests for exactly that), but nobody in CI executes them. This
  is the main thing I want maintainers' opinion on.
- Blocks 6, 8 and 12 may be superseded by other people's open PRs listed above.

## What I am asking for

1. Are gfx1100 HIP attention kernels wanted in-tree at all, given no CI runs them? If
   yes, in what shape — alongside the CDNA ones of #43835, or separate?
2. Should the generic fixes (items 7, 10, 11) go out as small standalone PRs? I think yes.
3. For items 6, 8 and 12, tell me to stand down if the existing PRs cover it — I would
   rather review theirs than compete.
4. Is the Model Runner V2 prefill lane (item 9) something you would want as an RFC?

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs for `RDNA3`, `gfx1100`, `qwen4_exp`, `Octave`, `HyperConnection`, `ple_embedding_dtype` and my
own authorship. Overlaps found and disclosed inline above: #57767, #52684, #56232, #43835,
#50955, #59442, #55040, #56273, and my own #49321, #46676, #59774, #60650, #60657, #60670. Already-landed
work of mine that this branch merely carries forward: #41394, #44075, #40835, #39931,
#55522, #60388. No open PR covers the branch as a whole, which is why this is a tracking
PR and not a merge request.

## Testing

On gfx1100, against this branch (2026-10-08):

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py        # 51 passed
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rdna3_mid_o_buffer_bound.py       # 9 passed
pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_readout_buffer_dtype.py      # 7 passed
pytest tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py             # 85 passed
pytest tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3.py                         # 73 passed
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna3_w4a16.py            # 32 passed
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna3_moe_w4a16.py        # 147 passed
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_octave.py               # 117 passed
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_amd.py                    # 21 passed
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_pre_indexer_amd.py        # 16 passed, 8 skipped
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_hc_ops_amd.py                 # 11 passed
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py                        # 80 passed
```

title: [Perf][HiSparse] Avoid repeated prefix scans and residency updates
body:
## Purpose

HiSparse's scheduler overhead grew with both context length and the number of resident groups:

- `plan_prefix_materialization` rescanned every computed page on each call, including the durable prefix it always skips.
- `plan_prefix_materialization` and `update_residency` ran from `HiSparseResidentManager.cache_blocks`, which the generic per-group loop calls once per resident group. With 20 resident groups this repeated the same coordinator-wide work 20 times per request per step.

At 2,048 concurrent agentic requests this used most of a scheduler core and delayed workers before their DP collective.

## Changes

- **Scan cursor:** the write-back scan starts at `max(ready_prefix_pages, importing_pages)`. Every page below `ready_prefix_pages` is already durable, so nothing it skipped is lost.
- **Once per step:** the per-step residency work (`plan_prefix_materialization` + `update_residency`) moves to `HiSparseConnectorScheduler.build_connector_meta` through `HiSparseCoordinator.advance_scheduled`, which runs once per scheduled request. The `cache_blocks` override in `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` is removed, so this PR only shrinks core.
- **Adoption publishes a block-table update:** adopting GPU copies on a host-prefix hit (#59282) now happens after the step's block IDs are captured, so `_adopt_copies` adds the request to `block_table_updates`. Without this the worker keeps reading the page from host while the coordinator pins its copy.
- **Reprefillable tokens stay out of write-backs:** like `KVCacheCoordinator.cache_blocks`, `advance_scheduled` excludes the last `num_reprefillable_tokens` (re-prefilled by multi-module MTP), so a page is not written back and marked durable before its rows are final. The auxiliary managers no longer force `enable_caching`, whose only purpose was the removed hook.

Behavior differences, both on the pressure path only:

- A request that just received its hot buffer releases its durable pages, and the low-pool watermark check runs, one step later than before. Pages written back at completion are still released in `update_connector_output`, before scheduling.
- Adoption runs after the whole scheduling pass, so a later request's allocation in the same pass can evict a copy first. The eviction watcher keeps this safe; the page is read from host instead.

## Performance

B300, one EP8 prefill node and one EP8 decode node, 2,048-concurrent Scale-SWE agentic rollouts, GLM-5.3 NVFP4, HiSparse 300 GiB/decode GPU (measured by @S1ro1 on a `7f47d2b`-based build; instrumented live-system measurements, not a fixed-batch benchmark). "Full fix" here deduplicated per-group work with a first-manager check; this revision gets the same deduplication by running it once from the connector.

| Phase | Output tokens/s/decode GPU | Mean ITL | Planner + residency CPU/step |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Original | 1,527 | 158.7 ms | 110.64 ms |
| Cursor only | 2,429 | 93.9 ms | 33.68 ms |
| Full fix | 2,711 | 79.1 ms | 2.68 ms |
| Original restored | 1,300 | 187.2 ms | 133.77 ms |
| Full fix restored | 2,782 | 81.7 ms | 2.85 ms |

CPU microbenchmark, 20 resident groups, 512 durable pages: 512.01 → 24.83 → 6.63 µs per request cache update (original / cursor / full fix).

This revision, same setup (20 resident groups, 512 durable pages, one request's per-step residency work, CPU platform): **327.9 µs on main → 1.3 µs** (main runs `cache_blocks` once per resident group; this PR runs `advance_scheduled` once).

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open HiSparse scheduler, prefix-scan and bookkeeping PRs; none overlap. @LucasWilkinson's alternative #58965 is closed in favor of this one.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_stats.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py
pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py  # H100 and B200
```

- Write-back tests run with one and three resident groups (incomplete and out-of-order writes, per-step budgets).
- Cache-manager tests drive the per-step work through `advance_scheduled`, as the connector does.
- New `test_hisparse_does_not_write_back_reprefillable_tokens` fails without the cap.
- New `test_scheduled_prefix_hit_publishes_adopted_copies` runs `build_connector_meta` on a host-prefix hit and checks that the adopted copies reach the step's block table. It fails without the `_adopt_copies` change.

## Test Result

948 passed, 4 skipped (CPU platform, also including `tests/v1/test_kv_cache_spec_registry.py` and `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector`). The 3 `test_bind_kv_cache*` failures in `tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py` also fail on unmodified main in this environment. Pre-commit passes. No model-output change is expected (scheduling bookkeeping only).

GPU e2e (`tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`) at `22e3bc84e5`: 4 passed on H100 and 4 passed on B200 (`test_hisparse_spill_and_prefix_restore[standalone]`, `[offload]`, `test_hisparse_host_exhaustion_defers_requests`, `test_hisparse_terminal_prefix_reuse`).

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex, then Claude Code) was used for investigation, implementation, tests and this description.

title: [Bug]: --kv-cache-memory suggestion double-counts CUDAGraph memory (regression of #37426, reintroduced by #49208)
body:
### Your current environment
<details>
<summary>Environment details</summary>

```
==============================
        System Info
==============================
OS                           : Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64)
GCC version                  : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0

==============================

Python platform              : Linux-7.0.0-1011-gcp-x86_64-with-glibc2.39

==============================
Is CUDA available            : True

GPU models and configuration :
GPU 0-7: NVIDIA B200 (x8)
Nvidia driver version        : 580.173.02

==============================

==============================
[pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.18
[pip3] torch==2.13.0+cu130
[pip3] transformers==5.17.0
[pip3] triton==3.7.1

==============================
         vLLM Info
==============================
vLLM Version                 : 0.1.dev20904+g179dd0fa9 (git sha: 179dd0fa9)  # custom build of vLLM main
  CUDA Archs: 7.5 8.0 8.6 8.9 9.0 10.0 11.0 12.0; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled

==============================
     Environment Variables
==============================
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1
TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1
TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_root
```
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The `--kv-cache-memory` value that vLLM prints at startup double-counts CUDA-graph memory whenever `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=1` (the default). For models with a large CUDA-graph pool the suggested value comes out **negative**, so it cannot be used and, since #47374, it also silently defeats `VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1`.

#### Background: what the `--kv-cache-memory` recommendation is

`--kv-cache-memory` (config `kv_cache_memory_bytes`) lets the operator hard-code the KV cache size in bytes. When set, vLLM skips the memory-profiling measurement and the CUDA-graph memory estimation pass, and reserves exactly that amount instead of deriving it from `--gpu-memory-utilization` (a short `profile_run()` for compilation still happens). The value is only meaningful if it reproduces the current allocation: too optimistic and the engine OOMs at graph capture, too conservative and batch concurrency (hence throughput) is capped. It is valid only on the same GPU with the same initial free memory.

Because the profiled value is deterministic for a fixed (model, config, hardware, library) combination, `gpu_worker.py` recomputes the exact `--kv-cache-memory` that reproduces the current allocation on every boot and logs it at INFO (promoted from DEBUG in #47374, "Surface the --kv-cache-memory suggestion at INFO and document fast-startup knobs"). The message offers two numbers:

```
Replace gpu_memory_utilization config with `--kv-cache-memory=<X>` (<X> GiB) to fit into
requested memory, or `--kv-cache-memory=<Y>` (<Y> GiB) to fully utilize gpu memory.
```

`X` fills up to the `--gpu-memory-utilization` target; `Y` uses all free device memory. Both are meant to be copied back verbatim, and `X` is also what the opt-in `VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1` feature (same PR, #47374) persists under `$VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/startup_plan/` to skip profiling on subsequent boots. That feature's guard rejects non-positive recorded values, so a negative `X` makes the whole fast-startup mechanism inert for exactly the models that would benefit most.

#### Impact

- The copy-paste `--kv-cache-memory` suggestion is unusable (negative) on large-graph models.
- `VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1` records the negative value and its guard rejects it, so fast startup is a silent no-op.
- No OOM: the double count only affects the reported recommendation, not the live allocation (`Current kv cache memory in use` is still correct).

### Reproduction

Serve any model whose CUDA-graph pool is large relative to the device — e.g. a DeepSeek-class MoE with dspark/MTP speculative decoding (`num_speculative_tokens=5`, 85 + 81 capture sizes) — and read the startup memory-profiler line. Here `--gpu-memory-utilization` was left at its 0.92 default, TP=8:

```
Free memory on device (175.81/178.35 GiB) on startup. Desired GPU memory utilization is
(0.92, 164.08 GiB). Actual usage is 58.44 GiB for consumed memory (weights + non-torch),
62.33 GiB for peak activation, and 63.99 GiB for CUDAGraph memory. Replace
gpu_memory_utilization config with `--kv-cache-memory=-22362854379` (-20.83 GiB) to fit
into requested memory, or `--kv-cache-memory=-9766683136` (-9.1 GiB) to fully utilize gpu
memory. Current kv cache memory in use is 43.31 GiB.
```

The engine runs fine with 43.31 GiB of KV cache, yet both suggested values are negative. The same run also logs:

```
CUDA graph pool memory: 63.99 GiB (actual), 57.45 GiB (estimated), difference: 6.55 GiB (10.2%).
```

### Root cause

The allocation path counts CUDA-graph memory once; the suggestion path counts it twice.

Allocation path — `determine_available_memory` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py`):

```python
self.peak_activation_memory = (
    profile_result.transient_peak_headroom + cudagraph_memory_estimate_applied
)
...
self.available_kv_cache_memory_bytes = (
    self.requested_memory
    - profile_result.non_kv_cache_memory          # = total_consumed + transient_peak_headroom
    - cudagraph_memory_estimate_applied
)
```

Suggestion path — `compile_or_warm_up_model` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py`):

```python
non_kv_cache_memory = (
    self.total_consumed
    + self.peak_activation_memory          # already contains cudagraph_memory_estimate_applied
    + cuda_graph_memory_bytes              # actual captured pool, added again
)
```

With the numbers above:

| Term | Value |
|---|---|
| `total_consumed` (weights + non-torch) | 58.44 GiB |
| `transient_peak_headroom` | 4.88 GiB |
| `cudagraph_memory_estimate_applied` | 57.45 GiB |
| `cuda_graph_memory_bytes` (actual) | 63.99 GiB |
| `self.peak_activation_memory` (= transient + estimate) | 62.33 GiB |

```
non_kv (current) = 58.44 + 62.33 + 63.99  = 184.76 GiB   # estimate counted twice
fit              = 164.08 − 184.76 − 0.15 = −20.83 GiB

non_kv (correct) = 58.44 +  4.88 + 63.99  = 127.31 GiB
fit              = 164.08 − 127.31 − 0.15 = +36.62 GiB
full             = 175.81 − 127.31 − 0.15 = +48.35 GiB
```

For small graph pools (a few GiB) the error keeps the suggestion positive but still under-reports the achievable KV cache; for large pools it goes negative.

### Regression history

- Introduced by #30515; fixed by **#37426** ("fix CUDAGraph memory being counted twice", merged 2026-03-20), which removed `+ cudagraph_memory_estimate_applied` from `peak_activation_memory`.
- Reintroduced by **#49208** "[copy of #45208] CuMem slept-L1 fragmentation accounting" (commit `58b2012aa2`, merged 2026-07-20), which rewrote the accounting (`torch_peak_increase`/`non_torch_increase` → `total_consumed`/`transient_peak_headroom`) and restored the estimate term.
- Still present on `main` as of this report.

### Suggested fix

Restore #37426: use the transient headroom (not `peak_activation_memory`) when computing `non_kv_cache_memory`, so CUDA-graph memory is counted once:

```diff
             non_kv_cache_memory = (
                 self.total_consumed
-                + self.peak_activation_memory
+                + profile_result.transient_peak_headroom
                 + cuda_graph_memory_bytes
             )
```

or equivalently keep `self.peak_activation_memory = profile_result.transient_peak_headroom` as it was before #49208. This also makes the #47374 startup-plan feature effective for large-graph models.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Perf][HiSparse] Allow full graphs for P/D prompt-token replay
body:
A successful HiSparse P/D full-prompt import still replays the final prompt token to produce logits. Model Runner V2 marks that token as logical prefill, which currently disqualifies an otherwise single-token decode batch from FULL CUDA graphs. A new P/D arrival can consequently send the whole batch through the fallback graph path.

This patch records successful full-prompt imports in scheduler/request state and carries the imported length to MRV2. Graph dispatch treats the last-token replay as decode-shaped when HiSparse is enabled, the query length is one, and PCP is absent. Logical prefill state is retained for input preparation and HiSparse loading. Genuine prefills, partial imports, failed transfers, preempted requests, and speculative/multi-token replay retain their existing classification. The marker is reset on preemption and each receive completion.

Based on main `82daf9f5`. Main now has a separate sliding-window bounded-replay path; that path is explicitly excluded when recording this marker. No connector transport, model math, scheduler-overhead optimization, Rust frontend fix, or configuration change is included.

### Serving evidence and limits

The equivalent patch has run on B300 with GLM-5.3 NVFP4 (`RadixArk/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`, revision `11af4cba759e6559eda70358a5778bd1bddddd78`), 1 EP8 prefill node and 1 EP8 decode node, FP8 KV, HiSparse, index cache, NIXL, Mooncake, DeepEP LL decode, and FULL_AND_PIECEWISE breakable graphs. EPLB and speculative decoding were disabled.

An early live Scale-SWE comparison recorded:

| Observation | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Output tokens/s/decode GPU | 1,402 | 1,487 |
| Mean request TPOT | 130.9 ms | 124.4 ms |
| FULL graph steps/s | 4.58 | 7.86 |
| PIECEWISE graph steps/s | 2.93 | None reported in sampled window |
| Active decode requests | 1,491 | 1,517 |
| Mean completed prompt length | 10,363 | 9,524 |

These are unmatched live windows across a restart (three minutes before, two minutes after), with changing histories and tool activity. They demonstrate the observed dispatch change, not a controlled throughput improvement or a guarantee that D never prefills.

The current deployment also produced Nsight captures under C2048 agentic load: all eight decode ranks recorded 10 CUDA graph launches and 10 GPU graph activity events, with 218–235 active requests per rank before capture. That deployment additionally includes the separate scheduler speedup and Rust frontend fix; its total throughput is not attributed to this patch.

GPU evidence uses a local `7f47d2b`-based wheel with unchanged native binaries. **This exact current-main revision has not had GPU or token/logprob-parity validation.** Correctness testing beyond the focused checks below remains pending; this draft is for design review, not a claim of established model accuracy.

### Validation

**177 passed**, 16 deprecation warnings. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy. The test wrapper asserts that imports resolve to this PR checkout and selects `CpuPlatform` before calling `pytest.main`; these are CPU scheduler/classification checks using the existing dependency environment.

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" VLLM_PLUGINS='' \
  uv run --project /home/matej/prime-rl-pd-validation --no-sync python \
  /home/matej/prime-rl/outputs/glm53-pd-system/20260921/replay-graph-pr/run_tests.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/v1 tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py -q
uv run --project /home/matej/prime-rl-pd-validation --no-sync pre-commit run \
  --files vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  vllm/v1/request.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/states.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py
```

The graph-classification regression exercises full versus partial/unmarked imports, incomplete replay positions, multi-token queries, HiSparse disabled, PCP, mixed replay/decode batches, and preservation of logical prefill state. The existing full-block import regression also checks that receive completion records the imported length.

### Related work and assistance

Searched open HiSparse replay/graph PRs, exact `full_prompt_kv_import_len` mentions, and references to #57049. No existing PR implementing this eligibility marker was found. This follows merged #57049, which imports complete blocks and restores the final page; it does not itself change MRV2's graph eligibility. #56158 addresses missing host-mirror preparation during FULL replay, a separate correctness change. #57930 removes repeated CPU prefix/residency bookkeeping and is not included here. No issue is being claimed or closed.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for implementation, investigation, tests, and this description. Tests reported here were run by the agent. The user explicitly requested this draft for collaborator review; human line-by-line review and independent GPU validation remain pending.

title: [ROCm] Dspark MLA module
body:
## Purpose

On ROCm, Kimi-K3 DSpark currently instantiates `nvidia.dspark_mla` / NVIDIA `MultiHeadLatentAttention` (bf16 `torch.bmm` absorb and the HIPified fused decode concat).
The Kimi-K3 target and MTP already dispatch through `vllm.models.kimi_k3`. This PR does the same for the drafter.
- Add `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/dspark_mla.py`.
- Register `K3DSparkModel` as `("vllm.models.kimi_k3", "K3DSparkForCausalLM")`
  so ROCm imports `amd.dspark_mla` instead of hard-coding the NVIDIA module `nvidia.dspark_mla`.
  CUDA dispatch is unchanged.

### Details
- Draft MLA is `KimiK3MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper` + generic `MLAAttention`
  (RoPE + `non_causal_multi_token_decode=True`). Do not use `KimiMLAAttention`
  (NoPE-only). `K3DSparkConfig` rejects `mla_use_output_gate`.
- **Decode:** absorb BMM and KV-cache write go through `MLAAttention`
  (`concat_and_cache_mla`). Absorb can use AITER FP8/FP4 BMM when those
  flags are on; otherwise `torch.bmm`. Wrapper RoPE is unchanged.
- **Context KV:** grouped `concat_and_cache_mla_grouped` into
  `layer.self_attn.mla_attn` caches. Allowlist `auto`/`bfloat16`/`fp8*`
  (with stacked `_k_scale` when quantized); same block-layout fallback
  as NVIDIA.
- Synced with NVIDIA DSpark on main: `attention_factor`-based YaRN vs
  llama scaling; fused context metadata in `process_weights_after_loading`;
  Markov head; grouped insert + scales.
- Draft **attention kernel** stays `TRITON_MLA` (This PR is orthogonal to AITER MLA / #53001).
- Speculative KV names are `*.self_attn.attn` (`mla_attn.layer_name`), not the wrapper.
- Tests: collect `tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py` in Basic Models / AMD CI.
  `test_k3_dspark_decoder_uses_mla_wrapper` is ROCm-only (no `cpu_test`;
  `is_rocm()` is false on CPU jobs).

### Out of scope
- AITER `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla` (decode RoPE + cache after absorb) left as a follow-up.
- Refactoring to avoid the near-copy of NVIDIA `dspark_mla.py` (~641 lines) This is the house style for `kimi_k3/{amd,nvidia}/`, not a new pattern. Drift is real: context-KV grouping, Markov head, weight mapper, and RoPE-type mapping must stay aligned. This PR already had to catch up some drift (`apply_yarn_scaling` vs `attention_factor == 1.0`).

## Test plan
- [ ] `pytest tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py -k k3_dspark or dspark_mla` on ROCm:
      mapping tests + `test_k3_dspark_decoder_uses_mla_wrapper`.
- [ ] Profiler (decode, flags on): AITER FP8/FP4 BMM instead of `aten::mm`;
      `_C_cache_ops.concat_and_cache_mla` instead of
      `vllm::kimi_k3_fused_ops::fusedKimiK3MLADecodeQConcatKVCacheKernel`
      (and no `hipPointerGetAttribute` from that HIPified concat).
      Do **not** expect AITER fused QK-RoPE+cache in this PR.
- [ ] Perf: `vllm bench serve` / spec-bench over output length × max concurrency,
      `speculative-config: '{"method": "dspark", "model": "Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark",
      "num_speculative_tokens": 5, "attention_backend": "TRITON_MLA",
      "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic", "rejection_sample_method": "block"}'`

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [X] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [X] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

title: [Model] Backport DeepSeek-V4.1 dependencies to v0.29
body:
## Why

[vllm-ascend#16925](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/16925) added DeepSeek-V4.1 support against vLLM commit `84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c`. The `v0.29.0` release tag predates the required frontend and shared Engram APIs, so the merged Ascend integration cannot be validated on that tag without a focused vLLM compatibility patch.

This PR is a validation carrier for testing DeepSeek-V4.1 with vLLM `v0.29.0` / `releases/v0.29.0`.

## What this backports

- DeepSeek-V4.1 Python frontend support: config, tokenizer/encoding, parser, renderer registration, multimodal preprocessing, and focused tests.
- Generic Engram configuration: config/CLI/environment plumbing and focused tests.
- Platform-independent Engram helpers consumed by vllm-ascend: token-map construction, hash multipliers, and bucket layout.

## Deliberately out of scope

- Rust frontend changes (the v0.29 default uses the Python frontend).
- CUDA/Qwen Engram model, UVA, communicator, embedding, and kernel implementations.
- CUDA/AMD DeepSeek-V4.1 model implementations; the Ascend model implementation remains in vllm-ascend.

## Upstream provenance

- `b47b01cf3383d50a5fae8569cadcbd0736076234` — DeepSeek-V4.1 Python frontend.
- `3116c5d06bfe76501b3dd6b5434bfc7f3274f5e7` — generic Engram configuration.
- `9b959b86577c082c0b2bf9e2c22263255a36ad83` — shared Engram helpers.

The original authors and co-authors are preserved in the backport commits.

## Validation completed

- `git diff --check`
- Ruff check and format verification with repository-pinned Ruff `0.14.0`
- typos `1.43.5`
- Python syntax compilation for all 30 changed Python files
- repository SPDX, lazy-import, forbidden-import, torch-CUDA, config, and boolean-context-manager checks
- mypy Python 3.10 pre-commit hook
- cross-repository import-closure scan against the merged vllm-ascend #16925 change: 156 new vLLM import references checked, with no missing modules or symbols

## Runtime validation still required

The local Windows workspace cannot run the Torch/NPU-dependent tests. Before treating this as release-ready, please run:

- the targeted vLLM test files added or changed by this PR;
- vllm-ascend model import / CPU UT coverage against this branch;
- DeepSeek-V4.1 dummy-weight smoke;
- DeepSeek-V4.1 real-weight Ascend smoke.

title: [Bug]: AMD mirror declarations disagree with test-amd.yaml steps - declared MI355/MI250 groups carry the MI300 agent pool and gfx942 lanes
body:
#### Before submitting, I searched the existing and past issues for `mirror`, `parity group`, `test-amd`, `MI355`, `agent_pool`, `reallocation` — nothing reports this.

**SECURITY WARNING:** no tokens, keys, passwords, private endpoints or personal data are included below.

### Your current environment

Not applicable: this report is about the CI definition files under `.buildkite/`, no runtime environment is involved. (`python vllm/collect_env.py` fails on this host with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'regex'`.)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`.buildkite/test_areas/*.yaml` declares, for many nvidia/CPU steps, an AMD twin in a `mirror:` → `amd:` block (`label`, `device`, `commands`, `env`). The twin that actually reaches the AMD pipeline is the step in `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` (its header: "will be feed into Jinja template in `test-template-amd.j2` … to generate the final pipeline yaml file"). The two files disagree for 43 of the 141 declared mirrors, silently — nothing validates the mirror → step mapping.

**28 groups: same test name, different tier / lane / agent pool.** The mirror declares `device: mi355_N` (or `mi250_N`); the AMD step carries `mirror_hardwares: [amdexperimental, amdproduction, amdgfx942nightly, amdmi300]` and `agent_pool: mi300_N`. `mirror_hardwares` is documented in `test-amd.yaml`'s README as the selector for which AMD pipelines include the step, and `agent_pool` picks the pool — so these groups run on MI300 (gfx942) while every declaration around them says MI355 (gfx950).

Two raw examples:

```
.buildkite/test_areas/pytorch.yaml:195-198
      label: ":amd: (MI355) PyTorch Fullgraph"
      device: mi355_1
      timeout_in_minutes: 90

.buildkite/test-amd.yaml:736-740
- label: ":amd: (MI300) PyTorch Fullgraph" # TBD
  timeout_in_minutes: 90
  mirror_hardwares: [amdexperimental, amdproduction, amdgfx942nightly, amdmi300]
  dind: false
  agent_pool: mi300_1
```

```
.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:133-135   label: ":amd: (MI355) Distributed Compile + RPC", device: mi355_2
.buildkite/test-amd.yaml:827-831                - label: ":amd: (MI300) Distributed Compile + RPC" # TBD
                                                mirror_hardwares: [..., amdgfx942nightly, amdmi300]
                                                agent_pool: mi300_2
```

Same shape for (mirror tier → amd tier): Entrypoints Unit and Entrypoints Integration (Responses API) MI355→MI300, vLLM IR MI355→MI300, Mamba Kernels MI250→MI300, MCR Eval Small Models MI355→MI300, Extrtact Hidden States Integration and Async Engine Inputs Utils Worker and Acceptance Length (Large Models) and Basic Models (Initialization) MI355→MI300, Language Models (MTEB) MI250→MI300, Multimodal Processor Shard %N MI250/MI355→MI300, Multimodal Models (Extended Generation 2) Shard %N MI355→MI300, Plugin Integration MI250→MI300, GGUF Plugin MI355→MI300, ray_compat Ray Dependency Compatibility Check MI355→MI300, Rust Frontend OpenAI Coverage / Core Correctness / Tool Use MI355→MI300, Samplers MI250→MI300, DeepSeek V2-Lite Prefetch Offload Accuracy MI355→MI300.

**9 declared mirrors have no same-named AMD step at all:**

- `:amd: (MI355) LM Eval Spec Decode` (`test_areas/lm_eval.yaml`, `device: mi355_4`)
- `:amd: (MI355) Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 Accuracy Eval` (`test_areas/lm_eval.yaml`) — `test-amd.yaml:3851` carries the same step as `:amd: (MI355) Qwen3-8-Flash-Next-FP8 Accuracy Eval`, i.e. misspelt against the model's own spelling (`tests/evals/qwen4_exp/configs/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8-rocm.yaml`, `test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:615,633`)
- `:amd: (MI355) Rust Frontend Serve/Admin Coverage` (`test_areas/rust_frontend.yaml`)
- `:amd: (MI355) Entrypoints Integration (Pooling)` (`test_areas/entrypoints.yaml`) — only `… (Pooling) Shard %N` exists (`test-amd.yaml:3742`)
- `:amd: (MI300) Qwen4 Exp` (`test_areas/models_basic.yaml:148`), `:amd: (MI300) Multimodal Models (PPL)` (`test_areas/models_multimodal.yaml:195`), `:amd: (MI300) Spec Decode {DeepSeek MTP Parallel Load, AL DFlash Nightly, AL DSpark Nightly}` (`test_areas/spec_decode.yaml`)

**6 further mirrors declare `:amd: (MI250) X` while the AMD file carries `:computer: (CPU) X`** with `amdgfx90anightly`/`amdmi250` lanes and `agent_pool: mi250_1` (Rust Frontend Cargo, Rust Frontend Cargo Style + Clippy, Docker Build Metadata, Basic Models Other, Multimodal Processor Shard %N) — same name, different lane label.

### Reproduction

From the repo root, `python3 repro.py` (pure stdlib, no deps):

```python
import os
import re

ROOT = "."


def clean(text):
    t = text.strip()
    if t[:1] in ('"', "'"):
        end = t.find(t[0], 1)
        return t[1:end] if end != -1 else t
    return t.split(" #")[0].rstrip()


def name_of(label):
    return label.split(")", 1)[1].strip() if ")" in label else label


steps = {}
cur = None
for line in open(os.path.join(ROOT, ".buildkite/test-amd.yaml")).read().split("\n"):
    if line.startswith("- label:"):
        cur = clean(line.split("- label:", 1)[1])
        steps[cur] = ""
    elif cur and line.startswith("  agent_pool:"):
        steps[cur] += " pool=" + line.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
    elif cur and line.startswith("  mirror_hardwares:"):
        steps[cur] += " lanes=" + line.split(":", 1)[1].strip()

d = os.path.join(ROOT, ".buildkite/test_areas")
mirrors = []
for f in sorted(os.listdir(d)):
    if not f.endswith(".yaml"):
        continue
    for line in open(os.path.join(d, f)).read().split("\n"):
        if re.match(r"\s+label: [\"']:amd: ", line):
            mirrors.append((f, clean(line.split("label:", 1)[1])))

by = {}
for s in steps:
    by.setdefault(name_of(s), []).append(s)

tier = cpu = absent = 0
for src, lab in mirrors:
    if lab in steps:
        continue
    same = by.get(name_of(lab), [])
    if not same:
        absent += 1
        print("ABSENT ", src, lab)
        continue
    for s in same:
        if s.startswith(":computer:"):
            cpu += 1
        else:
            tier += 1
        print("DRIFT  ", src, lab, "\n         amd:", s + steps[s])
print(f"\nmirrors declared={len(mirrors)}  tier_drift={tier}  cpu_lane={cpu}  absent={absent}")
```

Output ends with `mirrors declared=141  tier_drift=28  cpu_lane=6  absent=9`.

### Expected vs actual

Expected: every `mirror.amd.label` in `.buildkite/test_areas/*.yaml` has a step in `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` under that label, with `mirror_hardwares`/`agent_pool` matching the declared `device`. The mechanism does land elsewhere — `test_areas/pytorch.yaml:92-94` declares `:amd: (MI355) PyTorch Compilation H100 Cases` and `test-amd.yaml:3415-3419` carries exactly that label with `[…, amdgfx950nightly, amdmi355]` and `agent_pool: mi355_1`.

Actual: 43 of 141 declared mirrors disagree, so the AMD coverage the mirrors declare is not the coverage the AMD pipeline runs, and the difference is silent.

### History

`git log -S'":amd: (MI355) PyTorch Fullgraph"' -- .buildkite/` → `d406f09eb8` (#55252 Stage F gating); `.buildkite/test_areas/pytorch.yaml` was touched later by `f1c2f6ada8` (#57080, "MI355 test reallocation"); the AMD step's `(MI300)` label comes from `4f66bc3e0d` (#52976, "Standardize AMD test job labels by device"). For this and the other 27 groups the MI355 placement declared in the mirror never reached the AMD file.

### Need a call

Which side is intent: the mirrors (move the steps to MI355/MI250 including lanes and pool) or `test-amd.yaml` (the declarations are stale). I can prepare either diff; what I could not read from this repo is the MI355/MI250 agent capacity plan.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Raise a DFlash or DSpark draft's max_position_embeddings to the target's max_model_len
body:
## Purpose

A DFlash draft checkpoint ships `max_position_embeddings` equal to its target's native context. When the target is served with a longer context (`--hf-overrides`, YaRN), the draft's rotary `cos_sin_cache` is still sized from the draft's own value while the drafter is handed the target's absolute positions for its context KV, so the first request longer than the draft's value reads past the end of that cache and takes the engine down with a CUDA illegal memory access. The access is asynchronous, so the traceback usually lands in the target model's next GEMM rather than in the drafter.

Reported in #57941 (target extended to 393216 with `--hf-overrides`, draft `z-lab/Muse-Glimmer-30B-DFlash2` at 131072; a 150k-token request kills the engine) and independently in a comment on #55279 (target at 1M through YaRN, draft `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` at 262144; the first request over 512k kills it).

This is a V2 model runner failure, which is the default runner since 0.29.0. The V1 runner keys `effective_drafter_max_model_len` on the draft's own `max_model_len` (the smaller of the draft config's value and the target's) and `_input_fits_in_drafter` stops drafting for a batch that exceeds it, so on V1 the same request just runs without speculation. The V2 speculator has no such gate: it works from the target's `max_model_len` and drafts at every length the target accepts.

`SpeculativeConfig._maybe_override_draft_max_position_embeddings` already handles this for EAGLE drafts (#49343, for #48894) by raising the draft's `max_position_embeddings` to the target's `max_model_len` so the cache is sized for every position the drafter can see, but it only runs for `eagle` and `eagle3`. DFlash drafts share the target's positional space in the same way (`qwen3_dflash.py`, `qwen3_dflash2.py` and `laguna_dflash.py` all size their rope from the draft config's `max_position_embeddings`), and the issue's workaround, editing that value in a local copy of the draft's config, is exactly what the override does.

DSpark drafts are built the same way: `Qwen3DSparkModel` and `Gemma4DSparkModel` subclass the DFlash model and size their rope from the same value, and a speculators-format DSpark config is flattened from `transformer_layer_config`. A comment below reports the same crash past 262,144 tokens with `RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-speculator.dspark`, fixed by raising that value by hand.

## Changes

`vllm/config/speculative.py`: apply the existing override to `dflash` and `dspark` as well, and say so in the comment, the docstring and the log line. No new code path; DFlash and DSpark drafts now get the same treatment as an EAGLE draft.

`tests/config/test_speculative_draft_max_position_embeddings.py`: a CPU-only case, run for a DFlash draft (`z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` on `Qwen/Qwen3-4B`) and a DSpark draft (`deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_8b_block7` on `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`), both at 40960, with the target served at 65536 through `hf_overrides`; the draft's `max_position_embeddings` must come out as 65536 with the override logged. The existing `draft_model` case still checks that an independent draft keeps its own limit.

Two things this does not change:

- `draft_model_config.max_model_len` is computed before the override and stays at the draft's original value, so the V1 runner keeps skipping speculation past it while V2 now drafts there. That is how EAGLE behaves today; making the two runners agree means refreshing that value after the override, which touches EAGLE on V1 too and is better done separately.
- V2 has no drafter-capacity gate at all, so an independent `draft_model` drafter with a shorter context than the target hits the same illegal access on V2, and for it the answer is to skip rather than resize. That is a separate change.

The cache grows with the target's context: about 6 MB for 40960 to 65536 here, about 270 MB for the 262144 to 1M case in #55279. A draft whose own config uses YaRN sizes its cache from `original_max_position_embeddings` and is not affected by this value; neither shipped DFlash draft does.

## Test Plan

- `tests/config/test_speculative_draft_max_position_embeddings.py` on main 6ad2e06c4, on the previous head of this PR (DFlash only) and on this PR; the new cases must fail where the method is not covered.
- Real server, vLLM v0.29.0 wheel with only this change overlaid, RTX 6000 Ada, `--enforce-eager`: `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` with `--max-model-len 65536 --hf-overrides '{"max_position_embeddings": 65536}'` and `--speculative-config '{"method": "dflash", "model": "z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16", "num_speculative_tokens": 8}'`. Send a 30k-token completion (inside the draft's 40960), then a 50k-token one, then a short one, checking `/health`, the server process and the spec-decode counters in `/metrics` after each. Run on the V2 runner (default) and on V1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`).

## Test Result

Config test: main 6 passed, 2 failed (both new cases; the draft's `max_position_embeddings` stays 40960). Previous head: 7 passed, the DSpark case fails the same way. This PR: 8 passed.

Config-level check with the speculators-format `RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-speculator.dspark` on `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` served at 524288: the draft's `max_position_embeddings` stays 262144 on the previous head and becomes 524288 with this PR.

`pre-commit` hooks ruff-check, ruff-format, typos, mypy-3.10 and mypy-3.12 pass on the two files.

Server, DFlash (run before the DSpark change):

| | v0.29.0 | v0.29.0 + this change |
|---|---|---|
| V2, 30k-token request | 200 | 200 |
| V2, 50k-token request | 500 `EngineCore encountered an issue`; log: `illegal memory access`, fatal `CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED` in the target's `linear.py` forward; `/health` 503, server process exits | 200, 49,946 prompt tokens, drafter running (600 draft tokens, 52 accepted over 128 output tokens), `/health` 200 |
| V2, short request afterwards | connection refused | 200 |
| V1, 50k-token request | 200; the V1 gate stops the drafter past 40960 (1016 zeroed draft slots, 0 accepted) | 200; same, still gated (see above) |
| V1 and V2, 30k-token request | 200, 656 draft tokens, 47 accepted | 200, identical text and counts |
| startup log | | `Overriding draft model max_position_embeddings from 40960 to the target model's max_model_len (65536)` |

title: [AuxOutput] Add Mooncake backend with keys-only R3 output
body:
## Summary Add a Mooncake backend on top of the AuxOutput implementation merged in #45635. This PR targets `main` and does not include the legacy commit stack. It promotes the validated implementation reviewed in aoshen02/vllm#7 upstream. Duplicate check: no open upstream PR implements this keys-only R3 storage backend. #57966/#57025 concern prefix omission/KV-offload compatibility, not publishing complete R3 to Mooncake for external retrieval. The fork PR is the earlier review copy, not a separate upstream proposal. ```text GPU worker R3 -> existing background writer -> Mooncake full blocks EngineCore -> clip accepted boundaries -> Mooncake boundary/tail objects TITO HTTP -> ordered aux_output_keys only trainer -> get(keys), concatenate -> complete R3 ``` - Reuse native Mooncake batch I/O, existing configuration/setup and background writer. SHM remains the default. - Return keys on the terminal TITO response, including stored partial tails; no inline R3 with Mooncake. Publication completes before exposing final keys. Requests with string stops publish incremental keys internally so API-side termination can deliver complete R3; HTTP still exposes keys only at completion. - Share full-block keys across instances and DP ranks using block hash and reset generation. P/D must use the same generation, model/R3 profile, hash configuration/seed, block size and Mooncake store. - No new RPC, ACK protocol, publisher thread, TTL registry or retry state. Retention is deployment-owned; missing/evicted objects fail explicitly. - EngineCore owns a separate client for boundaries finalized after Scheduler stop/length handling. Scheduler shutdown closes it; closing the Worker client in another process cannot release it. This does not delete remote objects. ## Validation Local tests: **128 distinct tests passed** across these suites/tests: ```bash python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py -q HF_HUB_CACHE= HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_aux_output_keys_preserve_existing_output_wire_positions tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_terminal_aux_output_keys_survive_ipc_and_output_processing -q python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py::test_mooncake_decode_crosses_blocks_and_clips_terminal_output tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_request_output_collector -q ``` Commands used `/home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python`. A combined run initially had one missing offline default-model snapshot; rerunning that config test in the normal cache environment passed. Changed-file pre-commit, including mypy, passes. On this `main`-based branch, reruns passed **92 store/config tests + 34 TITO/IPC tests**, and all changed-file hooks. The new worktree initially lacked local FlashAttention extension links; collection passed after reusing the same installed extensions as the earlier worktree, without source changes. The additional command passed 3 tests (one store rerun and two collector cases). Tests cover the renamed `aux_output_keys` field through IPC, aggregation, streaming/non-streaming HTTP, absence of the old HTTP field, and client close. An attempted full OutputProcessor suite had 10 passes and 33 fixture errors in offline mode; an online retry confirmed HTTP 401 for the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` fixture. That full suite is **not** claimed passing. Slurm GB200 validation: two independent DP4/TP1/EP vLLM instances on two nodes, one shared Mooncake master, RDMA, async scheduling and prefix caching. Consumers run on the opposite node and fetch complete R3 using only returned keys. - 256K context, concurrency32 per instance: cold raw-data equality, hot prefix equality and fresh-client reads after requests finish pass (job30127). - MTP rejection and real stop clipping:32outputs match same-execution raw request/token-position data; fresh reads pass (job30130). - Forced preemption:88preemptions per instance,256requests total, all raw-position and fresh-reader checks pass, including local replay (job30144). Earlier runs with zero preemptions were rejected, not counted as coverage. - Matched SHM/Mooncake end-to-end throughput includes full cross-host retrieval and validation, two rounds,256K/concurrency32 per instance (jobs30115/30131): | Backend | Combined workload-span throughput | | --- | ---: | | SHM |115,758tokens/s | | Mooncake |115,038tokens/s | Difference **-0.62%**, including instance start skew. Averaging summed individual instance rates gives **-0.34%**. No material regression observed in these runs; two rounds are not a confidence interval or a precise intrinsic overhead estimate. Actual weights were **DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base**, despite a0731served alias. GPU tests used a pinned-image Python port of the change, not a full target-revision rebuild. Correctness hooks were disabled for throughput measurements. RDMA results do not establish TCP stress reliability; high-key-count TCP reads previously encountered native transport resource exhaustion. The raw oracle checks accepted same-position provenance, not a specific replay version. These GPU runs precede the API-field rename; the rename was validated locally, not with another GPU throughput run. AI assistance was used for implementation and validation; five independent Claude audit rounds of the preceding implementation concluded APPROVE; this follow-up naming/lifecycle review was self-audited. Human line-by-line review and acceptance of the test evidence remain required before merge. ## Multi-turn scaling follow-up (2026-09-21) GB200, actual DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base weights, DP4/TP1/EP per deployment, 256K initial context, 32 concurrent conversations per deployment, four turns (16 generated tokens + 1024 appended input tokens per turn). Prefix caching, chunked prefill and async scheduling enabled. Full R3 is fetched and validated on another node every turn; timing includes retrieval, decoding and validation. Median request-turns/s over three repetitions: | Engine replicas / concurrent conversations | SHM | Mooncake, 4 readers/deployment | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 4 / 32 | 0.623869 | 0.750283 | +20.3% | | 16 / 128 | 2.410555 | 2.954281 | +22.6% | The single-reader control did **not** outperform SHM (0.618058 / 2.361755). Independent native reader clients reduce client-side serialization; this is not an unconditional backend speedup. Each additional reader costs 128 MiB of local transfer buffer. At four deployments, configured Mooncake capacity is 256 GiB versus 128 GiB SHM, so this is not an equal-memory-cost comparison. Backend order was Mooncake then SHM, not randomized; three repeats do not establish statistical significance. Synthetic fixed-token conversations measure serving performance, not model quality. Jobs 30153/30154 completed successfully. Across the 18 phases (including the single-reader control), all 5,760 request-turns passed shape/dtype, output-token and within-conversation cached-prefix R3 equality checks. No preemptions occurred in this performance run; preemption/raw-oracle coverage is reported separately above. This does not assert cross-run, cross-backend bitwise R3 equality. Reproduction configuration: pinned image `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:95569a195dfe088c22983b08509e8e7156c26b356726147db4072600cba416ed`, image revision `2671fedfc7ae604761990603fc736c0c4f21de57`, with the archived source patch; Mooncake 0.3.12.post1, RDMA, shared master, reader `global_segment_size=0`, 128 MiB local buffers and 8 GiB per writer/publisher. Use 1 and 4 deployments, 32 HTTP threads/deployment, and 1/4 native reader clients as separate cases. Reset prefix cache before each repetition and exclude warmup; aggregate throughput by the whole workload time span. The Slurm recipe and raw logs are currently cluster-local, not a portable public benchmark. These frozen-image runs precede the latest mechanical cleanup; they are not a fresh GPU measurement of the final PR head. Latest cleanup removes repeated per-output block-size metadata, uses the Scheduler's authoritative hash granularity and shares output construction between backends. Changed-file pre-commit (including mypy) passes. Latest focused rerun: **107 passed, 173 deselected**: ```bash /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k 'mooncake or aux or routed_experts or store' -q --tb=short ``` ## Profiling follow-up (2026-09-22) Same frozen runtime and 256K/four-turn workload as above, one DP4 deployment, 32 concurrent conversations, cross-host RDMA retrieval with four native readers. Each backend has two unprofiled controls and one profiled run (Slurm 29958.60). Mean control throughput: **SHM 0.596435 vs Mooncake 0.743928 request-turns/s (+24.7%)**. Mean workload duration: 214.65s vs 172.07s; about 95% of the time saved is in the three warm/prefix-reuse turns. This compares complete delivery paths, not intrinsic RDMA versus shared-memory read speed. Mean per-request Mooncake costs over 192 warm requests in the two controls: | Stage | Wall time | | --- | ---: | | Native batch get, including lookup/transfer/wait | 526 ms | | Copy buffers to bytes and release handles | 36.5 ms | | Final bytes concatenation | 10.2 ms | | Whole get_concatenated, including the above | 578 ms | | Separate per-client lock wait | 1486 ms | SHM materializes R3, encodes NumPy/Base64 and sends it through HTTP; Mooncake returns keys and fetches raw bytes separately. Mean warm-request HTTP completion is 17.88s vs 4.26s; post-HTTP retrieval/decoding/checking is 1.84s vs 2.45s. Mooncake therefore adds post-HTTP work but saves substantially more on HTTP delivery. For 128 profiled requests, the client HTTP read chain consumes 97.49 vs 6.28 CPU seconds, JSON decoding 8.23 vs 0.77; SHM also spends 14.04 CPU seconds on Base64 decoding. HTTP body volume is 11.61 GB vs 0.89 GB, with Mooncake still fetching another 8.71 GB of raw R3. The dominant observed saving is avoiding the large Python HTTP/JSON/Base64 path, not eliminating data transfer or concatenation. Mooncake publication/flush waiting is higher; not every stage is faster. Profile timings are inclusive CPU totals, not additive request latency. Profiling reduces throughput by 11.8% (SHM) and 3.3% (Mooncake); the table and throughput comparison use unprofiled controls. Native API time is not pure RDMA wire time, and exported function profiles do not fully account for native CPU. The SHM after-control used a restarted, re-warmed server after a profiler-export failure. These two controls are not a confidence interval. All six phases passed 768 request checks and 576 cached-prefix R3 equality checks, with identical prefix-hit counts and zero preemptions. This retains the fixed-token/model-weight, memory-capacity and frozen-image limitations above; it does not establish model quality or cross-backend bitwise equality. Raw profiles, controls and recipes are archived cluster-locally. ## Independent Aux configuration (2026-09-22) AuxOutput now requires `VLLM_AUX_OUTPUT_MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`; KV retains `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`. There is no implicit fallback. Both variables may explicitly point to the same file. The existing config class and native setup are reused; no new RPC, thread or abstraction is introduced. Worker, EngineCore publisher and external helper readers use the same Aux factory. Ray propagates the variable, not the file; the path must be readable on each relevant node. KV-specific `enable_offload` does not restrict Aux initialization, including when both variables explicitly select the same file. The initial configuration-isolation commit touched five files (+90/-9). The follow-up below removes the standalone document and corrects its erroneous offload restriction; those initial counts do not describe the final PR. Validation: **159 distinct local tests passed** and changed-file pre-commit (including configured mypy) passed: ```bash /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py tests/test_ray_env.py tests/test_ray_env_utils.py -q --tb=short /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py -k config -q --tb=short ``` A new GB200 run (Slurm step 29958.61) passed **32 request-turns and 16 cached-prefix R3 equality checks** across two independent DP4 deployments and opposite-node RDMA readers. Both containers inherited a KV config path pointing to a nonexistent file; valid writer/reader configs were supplied only through the new Aux variable. Workload: 32K initial prompt, eight conversations per deployment, two growing turns, 16 output tokens, async scheduling and chunked prefill. Keys-only responses, full R3 shape/dtype, token counts and cached-prefix equality passed; each instance recorded 260096 prefix-hit tokens and zero preemptions. This freshly tests the config patch on the pinned-image Python port described above, not a rebuild of the current full PR head. It is not a throughput A/B, model-quality evaluation, concurrent KV-connector traffic test or full Ray-cluster test. KV compatibility and Ray environment propagation are covered locally. ## Audit fixes (2026-09-22) - Remove the Aux rejection of KV `enable_offload=true`; shared configuration remains valid. The field controls KV-specific load policy, not Aux storage. - Fix API-side string stops: publish accepted incremental keys internally for requests with string stops and accumulate them in OutputProcessor. Ordinary requests retain terminal publication; external HTTP still returns keys only at completion. This avoids finishing at the API before EngineCore sends keys. - Correct the Mooncake Worker test to exercise keys-only output, not only a swapped storage backend. Add a network-independent tokenizer regression that checks two-step R3 byte equality when the API stops and aborts EngineCore. - Remove `docs/features/aux_output_mooncake.md` and its code reference. Final local validation: **148 tests passed** (112 store/config/related Scheduler cases, 173 deselected; 36 TITO/IPC/collector cases). Changed-file pre-commit, including configured mypy, and `git diff --check` passed. ```bash /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k 'mooncake or aux or routed_experts or store' -q --tb=short HF_HUB_CACHE= HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_aux_output_keys_preserve_existing_output_wire_positions tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_terminal_aux_output_keys_survive_ipc_and_output_processing tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_request_output_collector -q --tb=short ``` String-stop requests incur more small-object writes; that performance cost has not been measured. The GPU runs above predate these audit fixes and are not claimed as validation of the new string-stop path. No new GPU run was performed. ## Backend layout follow-up ```text aux_output_connector/ store.py Shared BlockObject, error and background writer shm.py ShmBlockObjectStore mooncake.py MooncakeBlockObjectStore and output publisher ``` Move the existing SHM implementation into its own module and update imports, type references and test patches. No new interface, RPC or thread. The split also removes a redundant `slot is None` guard in SHM `put`; it is not a class-name-only AST change. Two older Worker test fixtures now explicitly select the SHM backend. Validation: **107 store/config tests + 18 capture tests passed**; changed-file pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed. One additional capture test fails while importing the installed Humming dependency (`humming.dtypes.float4e0m3` missing). Running that test's original HEAD source reproduces the same failure; it is not counted as passing. No new GPU benchmark was run for this mechanical split. ```bash /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py -q --tb=short /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py -q --tb=short ``` ## Mooncake PD + R3 handoff (2026-09-22) Enable `MooncakeConnector` with the Mooncake Aux backend. P runs the full prompt with `max_tokens=1` and no R3 prompt cropping; D receives the same prompt and the normal KV-transfer parameters plus: ```json "aux_output_prefix": {"block_size": 4, "keys": ["

", "

"]} ``` The block size is the R3/hash granularity (4 in this test), not the KV page size. D reuses shared full-block keys directly. Scheduler sends only the key for an unaligned first-forward boundary; Worker restores that block's missing prefix and joins newly computed R3. Aligned starts require no restore read. No full-prefix import or republication is needed. P objects remain immutable; the caller must keep source objects available. The configuration-level KV connector/PD blacklist has now been removed for both Aux backends. This is not a claim that every connector/backend implements remote R3 handoff; this PR's tested handoff is Mooncake PD + Mooncake Aux. Identical keys retain the first published value. After a cache miss and recomputation, returned R3 may therefore differ from the latest execution. This is an explicit accepted limitation; no overwrite or version mapping is introduced. Fresh tail keys can also wrap slices of older full objects. Validation: - 117 store/config tests passed; changed-file pre-commit, including mypy, passed. - Slurm 30373, two GB200 nodes, independent DP4/EP4 instances, real RDMA KV transfer and a shared Mooncake Store: all five cases passed. - Prompts 1025/1027/1028/1029/4099; D started at 1024/1026/1027/1028/4098. Covered 2–5 prefill chunks, streaming/nonstreaming, immutable P keys, complete external readback and later local reuse without the manifest. - First handoffs matched raw GPU rows exactly. Repeated keys retained their bytes; repackaged tails were checked against current or previously validated same-position rows, consistent with the first-writer contract. - Actual weights: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base. Same pinned image/Python adapter as above; modified Aux modules match the candidate source. This is not a full target-revision rebuild, throughput benchmark, or model-quality evaluation. - The initial retry oracle incorrectly assumed every new tail key represented new computation. Its failure logs were retained; the corrected checker and successful explicit retry are archived with the job. Slurm was cancelled after that retry passed, releasing both nodes. ```bash HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py -q --disable-warnings ``` AI assistance was used for this follow-up. Human review and acceptance of the semantic tradeoff and test evidence remain required before merge. ## Shared-key PD simplification (2026-09-23) Remove instance/DP namespaces and full-prefix restoration: production net **-28 lines**, touching only the two Aux connector modules and existing tests. No Scheduler/ModelRunner changes, new RPC or background-thread removal. Same P/D generation is an explicit deployment requirement. - **113 store/config tests passed**, changed-file pre-commit (including mypy) and `git diff --check` passed. Command is the store/config command above. - Independent Claude Opus 5.5 and Kimi K3 multi-round audits concluded APPROVE. - New Slurm **30589**, GB200 17/18, native RDMA: five PD cases passed with prompts 1025/1027/1028/1029/4099, 2–5 prefill chunks, streaming/nonstreaming, shared full-key equality, immutable P objects and later local cache reuse. D first-forward positions were 1024/1026/1027/1028/4098, confirming KV loading. - First checker failed on a later reuse: it only allowed the immediately prior response's R3, excluding an older valid first-writer row at the same position. The corrected checker allows previously validated same-position rows for new repackaged tails, while checking old-key immutability. Independent Kimi review approved the correction; the explicit rerun passed all five cases. Original failure logs remain: the batch retains exit 1 from the first checker; the rerun checker exited 0. No production patch was needed for this failure. - Actual weights: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base; existing pinned-image adapter, with changed modules byte-identical to this candidate. Not a full PR-image rebuild, throughput A/B or model-quality evaluation. Resources have been released. AI assistance was used. Human review remains required before merge. ## Main merge and PD policy (2026-09-23) Merged main (`88aa0d287d`) without force-push. Removed the entire AuxOutput KV connector blacklist, rather than keeping backend/connector exceptions. Other compatibility checks (model runner, PP/DCP/PCP, etc.) are unchanged. Configuration/store tests: **231 passed**; merge-file pre-commit passed. This permits configuration; it does not supply SHM with cross-host object access. Matched PD vs PD+R3 throughput completed successfully (Slurm **30597**, GB200 17/18, 20m13s). Same nodes, order PD -> PD+R3 -> PD, two measured rounds per phase; 64 requests/round, concurrency32, 32768 input +128 output tokens. Both P/D use DP4/EP4, async scheduling and real Mooncake RDMA KV transfer. | Mode | HTTP output tokens/s | Including full R3 retrieval | | --- | ---: | ---: | | PD, pooled before/after | 232.506 | 232.506 | | PD+R3 | 230.966 | 230.590 | | Change | -0.66% | -0.82% | Startup/warmup excluded. Each of the six measured rounds recorded2097152 external-KV hit tokens and zero P/D preemptions. All384 measured requests passed token checks;128 R3 requests passed full key-readback size checks, fetching1.086GB total. Raw-position correctness is covered by the prior E2E, not by this throughput checker. Four reader clients fetch R3 after HTTP; thread slots remain occupied through retrieval, so HTTP throughput is not an isolated model-execution metric. Before/after baseline drift was0.12%. Actual weights remain DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base, using the established frozen-image adapter, not a full latest-main rebuild. No raw GPU trace hooks, no MTP; synthetic cold prompts at one workload point. Few repeats are not a confidence interval. Resources released; user allocation14/15 untouched.
