title: [Bugfix] Pin num_splits for the FA4 hd256 kernel in sparse MLA
body:
## Purpose

`SparseMLAAttention._run_masked_mha` calls `flash_attn_varlen_func` with `fa_version=4` but never pins `num_splits`. On Blackwell (SM100/SM110) with `head_size == head_size_v == 256`, FA4 dispatches its dedicated hd256 kernel, which asserts `not is_split_kv`. Once the batch is large enough for the split-KV heuristic to fire, that assertion trips and takes down the engine core.

This affects `glm_moe_dsa` models (GLM-5.2 / GLM-5.3 family), whose `v_head_dim` is 256.

## Symptom

```
assert not is_split_kv, "SM100 forward with head_dim=256 does not support SplitKV"
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed / engine core proc died
```

Reproduced on 4x B200 (TP=4), `max_model_len 32768`, GLM-5.2 NVFP4: serving is stable at low load and the engine dies once concurrency reaches roughly 32. Below that threshold the heuristic does not split, which is why this does not show up in small smoke tests.

## Root cause

The dense FA path already knows this kernel cannot split — `uses_fa4_hd256_kernel` exists in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/fa_utils.py` and is consulted in `flash_attn.py`. The sparse MLA call site is the one place that builds FA4 kwargs for the same kernel without the corresponding guard.

## Fix

Pin `num_splits = 1` when the hd256 kernel is in play, reusing the existing helper rather than hardcoding the head size:

```python
if uses_fa4_hd256_kernel(q.shape[-1], v.shape[-1]):
    kwargs["num_splits"] = 1
```

The helper already checks the device capability (major in `(10, 11)`), so this is a no-op on every other platform and on every other head size. No behaviour change outside the configuration that currently crashes.

## Test

Verified on `v0.29.0` with the equivalent guard applied to the same call site: the engine survives a concurrency sweep of 8 / 32 / 64 / 128 / 256 with zero failed requests, where the unpatched build dies at 32. The change in this PR is rebased onto `main` and switched to the existing helper; I do not have a Blackwell box running `main` to re-run the sweep there, so a second pair of eyes on Blackwell would be welcome.

I could not find an existing issue or PR covering this path — happy to rework if one exists.

CUTLASS 4.8.0 dev

CuTe DSL

  • New features

    • Initial Rubin support to accelerate dense GEMMs. The following features are available:

      • CuTe DSL
        • Rubin new FP8 and FP4 Tensor Core support
        • B collector reuse
        • Extended TMEM size from 512 COL to 576 COL
        • Larger shared memory allocations (328KB)
        • Enhanced mixed precision throughput (FP8/FP4)
      • Primitives
        • Rubin new FP8 and FP4 Tensor Core support
        • Extended TMEM size from 512 COL to 576 COL

      NOTE: Executing Rubin kernels (SM107) requires the R615 driver which will be released with CUDA Toolkit 13.4 GA. R610 from CUDA Toolkit 13.4 Developer Preview is not sufficient.

    • CuTe DSL extensions has several new features:

      • CTA-V maps are now inferred automatically for cute_ext TMA load, store, multicast, and reduce-store operations. Explicit CTA-V maps remain supported as overrides.
      • Added asynchronous atomic TMA reduce-store and sparse MMA operations.
      • Added reusable cute_ext GEMM mainloop and TMA epilogue helpers.
      • Added opt-in TMEM accumulator-buffer planning, including overlapping ping-pong storage for capacity-constrained kernels.
      • Improved device-side TMA descriptor updates and grouped GEMM performance through SMEM-staged updates, workspace reuse, and reduced prologue and synchronization overhead.

    • This release includes an opt-in preview of the CuTe DSL extensions (cute_ext) compiler pipeline for ordinary Cute DSL kernels. This pipeline lets user mix cute_ext APIs directly into @cute.jit and @cute.kernel code and is required for kernels that mix the two API surfaces. You may test this feature with the following: CUTE_DSL_USE_EXTENSION_COMPILER=1 python your_program.py The pipeline is expected to preserve program behavior, but generated PTX/SASS may differ. The pipeline is planned to become the default in a future release.

    • Added examples for better control over Primitives' compiler warnings/errors introduced in 4.7.0. See the CuTeDSL/experimental/compiler_diagnostic/ directory.

    • IKET Profiler Tool

      • Rubin kernels (sm107) can now be profiled.
      • It is now possible to only dump timing data for a specific cluster to reduce profiling overhead. Previously all clusters were profiled.
      • Task Scheduling can instrument the schedule with IKET ranges when constructing TaskManager objects (iket_enable_profiling=True). Task execution will generate an IKET range and individual pipeline stages in a schedule may generate separate ranges (iket_profiling_stages).

    • A number of new examples were added in this release:

      • Rubin (CuTe):
        • Dense GEMM for legacy data type with B collector reuse as applicable
        • Grouped GEMM with B collector reuse
        • Dense blockscaled GEMM with FP4/FP6/FP8 mixed precision and UE5M3 / block-32 scale-factor support
        • Grouped blockscaled GEMM with B collector reuse as applicable
        • Blockwise GEMM
      • Rubin (CuTe extension):
        • FP4 blockscaled GEMM
        • Grouped GEMM with B collector reuse
      • Blackwell (CuTe extension):
        • Dense GEMMs
          • Back-to-back GEMM
          • Blockscaled GEMM
          • Persistent GEMM with alpha/beta scaling
          • CLC scheduler/dynamic persistent GEMM
          • GLU GEMM
          • Mixed input GEMM

title: [Refactor][Core] Use torch's device-agnostic streams and events in the V2 model runner
body:
## Purpose

The V2 model runner (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/`) creates its copy streams and events as `torch.cuda.Stream` / `torch.cuda.Event`, switches streams with `torch.cuda.stream(...)`, and reads the current stream with `torch.cuda.current_stream()` in `async_utils`, `pp_utils`, `structured_outputs`, `spec_decode/utils`, `spec_decode/adaptive_verification` and the runner's `main_stream`. None of that code is CUDA-specific: it needs a stream, an event and the current stream of whatever accelerator torch is running on.

This PR switches those sites to torch's device-agnostic API: `torch.Stream(device=...)`, `torch.Event(device=..., blocking=True)`, `torch.accelerator.current_stream()`, and the existing lightweight `stream()` context manager in `async_utils`, which now uses `torch.accelerator.set_stream()`. On CUDA these resolve to the same objects, so in-tree behaviour is unchanged. `cudagraph_utils` and `ubatch_utils` keep `torch.cuda`, since graph capture and the cuBLAS handle are CUDA features.

Why: every non-CUDA runner today gets past these lines by aliasing `torch.cuda` process-wide. The in-tree XPU runner rebinds `torch.cuda.Stream`, `Event`, `graph` and `CUDAGraph` around `super().__init__()` (`vllm/v1/worker/xpu_model_runner.py`), the in-tree CPU runner installs `_StreamPlaceholder` / `_EventPlaceholder` (`vllm/v1/worker/cpu/shm.py`), and vllm-ascend assigns twelve `torch.cuda.*` attributes to `torch.npu.*` with an empty `finally` (`vllm_ascend/worker/v2/utils.py`). The checklist to route these through the platform in #9268 has been open since 2024. Using the generic API removes the need for any routing: torch dispatches to the current accelerator.

The CPU V2 runner (`vllm/v1/worker/cpu/model_runner.py`, a `GPUModelRunner` subclass) has no accelerator. On CPU-only torch, `torch.accelerator.current_stream()` / `set_stream()` raise, and a CPU `torch.Stream` cannot `wait_stream`. `cpu/shm.py` already maps `torch.Event` and `torch.cuda.*` to its placeholders, so this PR adds `torch.Stream`, `torch.accelerator.current_stream` and `torch.accelerator.set_stream` to that list.

Two small semantic notes for review:

- `copy_event.record()` inside a `with torch.cuda.stream(s):` block becomes `copy_event.record(s)`, which records on the same stream explicitly.
- `torch.Event(device=..., blocking=True)` is the generic spelling of `torch.cuda.Event(blocking=True)`. The step timing events in `async_utils` (`StepTimingEvents`) become `torch.Event(enable_timing=True)`.

## Test Plan

- `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files (ruff, mypy, typos).
- The change is a rename of API surface on CUDA; the objects and their behaviour are the same. CI on this PR exercises the async output path, structured outputs, pipeline parallelism and speculative decoding.
- CPU: on CPU-only torch 2.14.1, I checked that the new calls fail without the `shm.py` patches (`current_stream`: `Accelerator expected`; `set_stream`: `Cannot access accelerator device when none is available`; `Stream.wait_stream`: `cpu backend doesn't support events`). I then ran the PR's stream/event sequence (`current_stream`, `torch.Stream`, `torch.Event(device=, blocking=True)`, `stream()`, `wait_stream`, `record(s)`, `synchronize`) with the `shm.py` patch block applied, and it completed.
- Downstream, the same change was run on a non-CUDA accelerator that implements `torch.Stream` / `torch.Event` and has no `torch.cuda`: async output, structured outputs, prompt logprobs, pooling, DP=2 and EAGLE/EAGLE3 speculative decoding end to end.

## Test Result

```
pre-commit run --files <6 files>   ruff-check, ruff-format, mypy-3.10, typos: Passed
ruff check / format --check cpu/shm.py: Passed
git diff main..HEAD                7 files changed, 49 insertions(+), 42 deletions(-)
```

Merged with main at 814301b268; no conflicts, and main added no new `torch.cuda` stream/event sites under `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/` outside `cudagraph_utils` / `ubatch_utils`.

Downstream (v0.26.0 port of this change, non-CUDA accelerator): V2 e2e 6 passed, EAGLE + EAGLE3 2 passed.

Not run locally: the CUDA test suite and a CPU-backend vLLM end-to-end run (the development host has no GPU, and no CPU build of vLLM). A reviewer with a GPU should confirm that `torch.Event(device=..., blocking=True)` and `torch.accelerator.set_stream` behave as `torch.cuda.Event(blocking=True)` and `torch.cuda.set_stream` on the async output path; CI should cover this. No CPU CI job sets `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER`, so the CPU MRV2 path is not exercised by CI.

title: [Bug]: KVCR secondary-tier configuration fails to start after the backpressure factory change
body:
## Environment

- vLLM Python source: `c723a831a81cb4ff89ea6d61b2d15109306ed1bc` on `main`, tested on 2026-09-22.
- Editable source with precompiled native artifacts; installed distribution metadata: `0.1.dev648+g1fee69838.precompiled`.
- Linux x86-64, Python 3.12.14, NVIDIA RTX 3090.
- PyTorch `2.13.0+cu132`, Transformers `5.16.1`.
- KVCR `0.1.0`, source revision `317e62f301300c101bf9c911e020fb89b35f1583`.
- `nixl` / `nixl-cu13` `1.3.2`.
- Model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, local weights, FP16.

## Description

A normal `OffloadingConnector` configuration with `TieringOffloadingSpec` and a `kvcr` secondary tier fails during engine initialization:

```text
TypeError: KVCRSecondaryTierManager.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'backpressure_detector'
```

No backpressure option is configured. The factory now passes `backpressure_detector=None` unconditionally, but the KVCR adapter does not accept this keyword. The server exits before becoming healthy or serving any request.

KVCR's [official developer guide](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/kvcr/blob/317e62f301300c101bf9c911e020fb89b35f1583/docs/dev-guide.md) documents this secondary-tier configuration. The integration is experimental, but it is an in-tree registered adapter. The failure affects the normal factory construction path for KVCR; ordinary primary-only CPU offloading still starts and generates successfully in the same environment.

## Reproduction

Install the optional KVCR/NIXL dependencies in the vLLM environment, then run the following with a local Qwen3-0.6B model directory. This is the generation-only configuration used for the GPU reproduction; it needs neither a submitted request nor a remote transfer to fail.

```bash
MODEL=/path/to/Qwen3-0.6B
KV_CONFIG='{
  "kv_connector": "OffloadingConnector",
  "kv_role": "kv_both",
  "kv_connector_extra_config": {
    "spec_name": "TieringOffloadingSpec",
    "cpu_bytes_to_use": 134217728,
    "self_describing_kv_events": true,
    "secondary_tiers": [{
      "type": "kvcr",
      "router_capabilities": ["router_hint"],
      "control_host": "127.0.0.1",
      "control_ports": [17779],
      "control_advertise_host": "127.0.0.1",
      "operation_timeout_ms": 5000,
      "abandon_timeout_ms": 10000,
      "enable_telemetry": true
    }]
  }
}'

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 \
  .venv/bin/vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --served-model-name audit-qwen --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18556 \
  --dtype half --enforce-eager --max-model-len 1024 \
  --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 128 --block-size 16 \
  --kv-cache-memory-bytes 268435456 --enable-prefix-caching \
  --kv-transfer-config "$KV_CONFIG"
```

Expected: the engine initializes the KVCR adapter and becomes ready to serve.

Observed: the engine exits with status 1. The relevant end of the traceback is:

```text
File "vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py", line 573, in __init__
    self.manager: OffloadingManager = spec.get_manager()
File "vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/spec.py", line 374, in get_manager
    tier = SecondaryTierFactory.create_secondary_tier(
File "vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/factory.py", line 91, in create_secondary_tier
    return tier_cls(
TypeError: KVCRSecondaryTierManager.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'backpressure_detector'
```

Changing only `secondary_tiers` to `[]` allows the reference server to start. Three identical deterministic completion requests returned HTTP 200 and token IDs `[7407, 304, 279, 3283, 315, 12095, 13, 362]`. This control separates the KVCR construction failure from model loading and the primary CPU offload setup.

## Regression and related work

The KVCR adapter was added by [#53624](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53624). [#50045](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50045), commit `23e26e058839fb2a3e77c78fbf2184f563593227`, subsequently added the unconditional factory keyword and updated other secondary tiers, but omitted the KVCR constructor. Its current call to `SecondaryTierManager.__init__` also does not forward a detector.

Existing KVCR tests construct the adapter directly and therefore miss the production factory path. Routing their existing helper through the factory reproduces the same constructor error in all 21 cases. A local fix accepting the optional parameter and forwarding it to the base class passes all 229 tests across six related suites. The identical GPU configuration then starts and serves all three requests, with token IDs and corresponding per-token logprobs matching the primary-only reference.

Issue/PR searches and the related discussions were checked again immediately before submission on 2026-09-22. The KVCR constructor, factory, base class, and KVCR tests remain unchanged at upstream `496c6472cb70d5eb8681dadae238d160f5086454`. [#57500](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57500) handles cleanup after a native KVCR startup failure; its patch does not change the constructor signature and does not address this failure, which occurs before entering the constructor.

OpenAI Codex assisted with the investigation, reproduction, implementation, and execution of the validation reported above.

title: [CI] Emit a kernel symbol map from the csrc build (opt-in, for test selection)
body:
## Purpose

Part of the CI test-selection work in vllm-project/ci-infra (#555, #610, #611). The nightly CI runs now record which GPU kernels every step launches. To turn that into a decision ("this PR changed `csrc/foo.cu`, which steps launched a kernel from it?") CI also needs to know **which source file produced each kernel symbol**. That has to come from the real build, because the mangled names depend on template instantiations, the arch list and what CMake actually compiled.

This PR adds `tools/ci/kernel_symbol_map.py`, run inside the `csrc-build` Dockerfile stage right after the compile layers. Per compiled object it records the source file, the CMake target, the headers `ninja -t deps` says it read, and the kernel entry symbols `cuobjdump -symbols` finds in the fatbin. Output is one gzipped JSON, ~3.4 MB. A scratch stage `kernel-symbol-map` exposes the file and `image_build.sh` bakes that target with a local output and uploads it as a build artifact.

**Off by default.** Everything is gated on the build arg / env `VLLM_KERNEL_SYMBOL_MAP=1`, which only the nightly and daily full-run schedules will set. A normal build gains one `COPY` and one `RUN` that prints "Skipping", both after the compile layers so their cache is untouched. The script never fails the build; an empty map with a `reason` is the failure signal downstream.

Also regenerates `docs/assets/contributing/dockerfile-stages-dependency.png` for the new stage (pre-commit hook).

## Test Plan

Ran the image build on a fork branch with the arg set, image-build step only, three times while iterating (Buildkite `vllm/ci` builds 90006, 90008, 90011), then joined the resulting map with kernel recordings from real CI steps.

## Test Result

- Map produced in 62 s inside the (cached) `csrc-build` layer: 567 objects, 543 device objects, 10,447 kernel entry symbols, 0 `cuobjdump` errors, every object attributed to its CMake target (`_vllm_fa3_C` 194, `_C_stable_libtorch` 113, `_deepselect_C` 79, `_vllm_fa2_C` 79, `_flashmla_C` 56, ...). 89 of the 98 `.cu` files under `csrc/` appear (the rest are ROCm-only or not in the CUDA 13 arch list); 111 of 163 headers appear as dependencies.
- Probe in the build log: `fusedQKNormRopeKernel -> csrc/libtorch_stable/fused_qknorm_rope_kernel.cu`.
- Joined with the first nightly's recordings (187 CUDA steps): a change to `fused_qknorm_rope_kernel.cu` (the file behind #55755, which selects 225 of 226 steps today) selects 6 steps and drops 176; `topk.cu` selects the 12 DeepSeek/Qwen4/B200 attention steps; `cuda_compat.h` selects 169, as a header included everywhere should.
- With the arg unset (every other build): the `RUN` prints "Skipping kernel symbol map" and nothing else changes.

title: [CI Failure]: (MI355) Core Operation Kernels Shard 1: kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py::test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope
body:
### Name of failing test

```
kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py::test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[True-0-False]
kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py::test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[True-0-True]
kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py::test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[True-64-False]
```

### Basic information

- [ ] Flaky test — **no**, fails deterministically on every attempt, including in-build retries
- [ ] Can reproduce locally — no MI355 hardware available to me; reproduced only in CI
- [ ] Caused by external libraries — no, the failure is in vLLM code

### 🧪 Describe the failing test

`(MI355) Core Operation Kernels Shard 1` fails on ROCm only. The same test file passes on `(H200 MIG 35GB) Core Operation Kernels Shard *`, and MI355 shards 2 and 3 are green — only shard 1 receives `kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py`.

```
FAILED kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py::test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[True-0-False] - IndexError: tuple index out of range
FAILED kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py::test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[True-0-True]  - IndexError: tuple index out of range
FAILED kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py::test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[True-64-False] - IndexError: tuple index out of range
3 failed, 1164 passed, 168 skipped, 24 warnings in 1072.49s (0:17:52)
```

Traceback (from the nightly `main` build, Buildkite #90376):

```
kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py:177:
/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/custom_op.py:134: in forward
    return self._forward_method(*args, **kwargs)
/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py:1561: in forward
    decode_q, _ = quant_fn(self, decode_q_flat, scale, scale_ub)
/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:159: in forward_hip
    return self.forward_cuda(x, scale, scale_ub)

self = _DecodeConcatQuantFP8()
decode_ql_nope = tensor([[  24.8750,  276.0000, ...]], device='cuda:0', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
decode_q_pe = tensor(0.3000, device='cuda:0'), scale = None, scale_ub = None

    def forward(
        self,
        decode_ql_nope: torch.Tensor,
        decode_q_pe: torch.Tensor,
        scale: torch.Tensor,
        scale_ub: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
>       if decode_q_pe.shape[-1] == 0 and decode_ql_nope.is_contiguous():
E       IndexError: tuple index out of range

/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py:1556: IndexError
```

#### Root cause: the HIP fallback re-enters the subclass override

`_DecodeConcatQuantFP8` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py:1540-1568`) builds all three of its forward methods from one factory, so every method has the 4-argument signature `(decode_ql_nope, decode_q_pe, scale, scale_ub)`:

```python
forward_native = _make_forward(QuantFP8.forward_native)
forward_cuda = _make_forward(QuantFP8.forward_cuda)
forward_hip = _make_forward(QuantFP8.forward_hip)
```

`QuantFP8.forward_hip` ends with a fallback to the CUDA implementation (`vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:159`):

```python
# Fallback to CUDA implementation
return self.forward_cuda(x, scale, scale_ub)
```

On `_DecodeConcatQuantFP8`, `self.forward_cuda` is the *wrapped* 4-argument method, not `QuantFP8.forward_cuda`. So the 3-argument fallback call re-enters the wrapper with arguments shifted by one: `decode_q_pe` binds to the per-tensor `scale` (a 0-dim tensor, `tensor(0.3000)`), and `decode_q_pe.shape[-1]` raises `IndexError`.

CUDA never re-dispatches, which is why only the ROCm lane fails. On MI355 the AITER early-return branches in `forward_hip` are not taken for this configuration, so the fallback path is reached.

A minimal fix is to call the base implementation unbound, so the fallback cannot re-enter a subclass override with a different signature:

```python
return QuantFP8.forward_cuda(self, x, scale, scale_ub)
```

I have not opened a PR for this — I have no MI355 hardware to verify a fix, and I would rather leave it to the ROCm/attention owners than push an unverified change through CI.

### 📝 History of failing test

First red MI355 shard 1 today was Buildkite #90366 at 05:26Z. The guard line that raises (`if decode_q_pe.shape[-1] == 0 and decode_ql_nope.is_contiguous():`) was introduced by **#57458 "[Perf][Attention] Reduce GLM sparse MLA preparation overhead"** (merge commit `a369a7bec`, merged 2026-09-22T00:24:26Z), which is ~5 h before the first observed failure.

Note the underlying re-dispatch is older than #57458 — before it, the wrapper's first statement was `torch.cat((decode_ql_nope, decode_q_pe), dim=-1)`, which would also fail on a 0-dim tensor. #57458 changed the symptom to `IndexError`, and the failure is what surfaced the latent dispatch bug.

Every finished `(MI355) Core Operation Kernels Shard 1` run I checked on 2026-09-22 is red, across unrelated PRs and on `main`:

| Build | Trigger | Shard 1 | Shards 2 / 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#90366](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90366) | PR #58069 | fail, 2 attempts | pass |
| [#90376](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90376) | **`Full CI run - nightly` (`main`, no PR)** | fail, 2 attempts | pass |
| [#90377](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90377) | PR #49953 | fail, 2 attempts | pass |
| [#90380](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90380) | PR #56252 | fail, 3 attempts | pass |
| [#90388](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90388) | PR #55721 | fail, 2 attempts | pass |
| [#90390](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90390) | PR #57945 | fail, 2 attempts | pass |

The nightly `main` build #90376 has no PR attached and reproduces the failure with an identical log (same three parametrisations, same `mla_attention.py:1556`, `3 failed, 1164 passed`), so this is not caused by any of the PRs above.

Retrying does not help — several of the builds above show 2-3 attempts on the same job, all failed. The step has no `soft_fail`, so it blocks the `buildkite/ci/pr` rollup for every PR whose diff matches the step's `source_file_dependencies` (which include `vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/` and `tests/kernels/core`).

### CC List.

@GirasoleY @ZJY0516 (#57458), @LucasWilkinson @MatthewBonanni (`/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention` owners), @tjtanaa @dllehr-amd (ROCm)

title: [Bugfix][V1] Read ModelState max_model_len from model config
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57034.

When auto-fit reduces `max_model_len` after model loading, V2's `ModelState` retains the original length while attention metadata builders use the reduced limit. CUDA graph capture can then request more context than those builders support. For example, fitting 1,048,576 tokens down to 980,224 leaves DeepSeek-V4 C128A capture requesting 8,192 compressed entries from a buffer with capacity 7,680.

Make `ModelState.max_model_len` a read-only property backed by `model_config.max_model_len`. All model-state capture paths follow the worker's resolved limit without maintaining another cached copy or extending the runner's update list. Update the existing Mamba test fixture to supply its limit through the config.

Allocation capacities remain distinct from the serving limit: for example, `RopeState` uses its saved length as a physical buffer stride and must retain that value unless its storage is rebuilt.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py::test_prepare_attn_forwards_positions -q
```

Result: 9 passed.

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/interface.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py
```

Result: all applicable hooks passed.

A temporary CPU reproduction using the real `DefaultModelState.prepare_attn` and `DeepseekV4SparseMLAMetadataBuilder` reproduced the original C128A assertion. With this change, capture uses 980,224 tokens and requires 7,658 compressed entries, within the builder's 7,680-entry capacity. The final GPU kernel was stubbed; full DeepSeek model startup and inference were not run.

## Contribution notes

The duplicate audit found #46794 and #46884, which address V1 InputBatch/block-table sizing. This PR addresses V2 ModelState capture; the update stays on the existing PR for #57034.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, and validate this update.

title: [Bug]: vLLM does not ignore temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty for DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode, unlike the official DeepSeek API
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Summary According to the official DeepSeek API documentation, the DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode does not support the temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty parameters. For backward compatibility, passing these parameters does not raise an error, but they have no effect. However, vLLM does not behave consistently with the DeepSeek API. When serving DeepSeek V4 series models in thinking mode, these parameters are still applied to sampling instead of being ignored. Expected behavior For DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode, vLLM should accept temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty without raising an error, but silently ignore them — matching the official DeepSeek API behavior. Actual behavior These parameters are still honored by the sampler, which can lead to different (and unexpected) outputs compared to the official API. Impact Users migrating from the official DeepSeek API to vLLM may get inconsistent results. Clients that rely on the documented "accepted but ignored" behavior may unintentionally change model output. Reproducibility across the official API and vLLM is broken for these models. Steps to reproduce Serve a DeepSeek V4 series model in thinking mode with vLLM. Send a request with different values of temperature (or presence_penalty / frequency_penalty). Observe that the output changes, whereas the official DeepSeek API would produce identical sampling behavior regardless of these values. Suggested fix Detect DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode and skip applying temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty in the sampling path, while still accepting them in the request schema for compatibility. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: v0.30 dependencies raise the effective compiler floor above GCC 11.3
body:
## Summary

vLLM v0.30.0's declared source-build floor remains GCC/G++ >= 11.3, but multiple pinned dependencies now require C++20 `<format>` / `std::format`. With libstdc++, that raises the effective GCC floor to GCC 13.

This is broader than the first observed DeepSelect failure: the DeepGEMM revision pinned by v0.30.0 independently uses `<format>` in host code that is included unconditionally when building its Python extension.

## Declared vLLM contract

vLLM both enforces GCC >= 11.3 and recommends installing GCC 11 on Ubuntu 22.04:

- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/CMakeLists.txt#L23-L29
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.cuda.inc.md#L140-L149

## DeepSelect: first observed failure

vLLM pins DeepSelect commit `d96d33afe1fab0d6066da49cdc91e64c2bee65ea`:

- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/cmake/external_projects/deepselect.cmake#L19-L22

That revision includes `<format>` and uses `std::format` once to construct a stride-validation error message:

- https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepSelect/blob/d96d33afe1fab0d6066da49cdc91e64c2bee65ea/csrc/api.cpp#L15-L19
- https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepSelect/blob/d96d33afe1fab0d6066da49cdc91e64c2bee65ea/csrc/api.cpp#L89-L97

With GCC 11.4 and `-std=c++20`, compilation stops at:

```text
csrc/api.cpp:17:10: fatal error: format: No such file or directory
   17 | #include <format>
      |          ^~~~~~~~
```

Root-upstream tracking and the proposed portable replacement are available here:

- https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSelect/issues/21
- https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSelect/pull/22

## DeepGEMM: independent compiler-floor drift

vLLM v0.30.0 pins `vllm-project/DeepGEMM` commit `e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f`:

- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake#L30-L36

That exact pinned tree also requires `<format>`:

- `csrc/apis/attention.hpp` includes `<format>`, includes the SM100 sparse-MQA implementation, and uses `std::format`:
  - https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/blob/e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f/csrc/apis/attention.hpp#L1-L15
  - https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/blob/e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f/csrc/apis/attention.hpp#L64-L67
- `csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm100_sparse_mqa_logits.hpp` includes `<format>` and uses `std::format` repeatedly to construct JIT source:
  - https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/blob/e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f/csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm100_sparse_mqa_logits.hpp#L1-L9
  - https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/blob/e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f/csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm100_sparse_mqa_logits.hpp#L82-L109
- `csrc/python_api.cpp` includes `apis/attention.hpp` unconditionally, so runtime architecture gating does not prevent the host compiler from parsing this code:
  - https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/blob/e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f/csrc/python_api.cpp#L1-L15

DeepGEMM's own current requirements explicitly call for "Compilers and standard libraries with C++20 `<format>` support":

- https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/blob/e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f/README.md#L24-L33

This source path did not produce the observed CI failure only because Ninja stopped after the earlier DeepSelect error. The pinned source and unconditional include chain show that fixing DeepSelect alone is insufficient for a GCC 11 build.

## What changed from v0.29.0

The known-good v0.29.0 build used GCC 11.4. Its DeepGEMM integration pinned the older `deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM` revision `8b1392b978f5a03c828dd1711090d7fb50958b8a`, before the linked sparse-MQA `<format>` code was present. DeepSelect was introduced in v0.30.0 as a new extension.

- v0.29.0 DeepGEMM pin: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake#L30-L34
- Known-good GCC 11.4 build: https://github.com/neuralmagic/nm-cicd/actions/runs/34346952915
- Failing v0.30.0 build: https://github.com/neuralmagic/nm-cicd/actions/runs/35729206971

## Compatibility decision needed

vLLM should make the declared and effective build contracts agree. The main options are:

1. Preserve GCC 11.3 compatibility by replacing or conditionally excluding incompatible `<format>` usage in all pinned host dependencies, then validate the minimum compiler in CI.
2. Intentionally raise the source-build requirement to a compiler and standard library with C++20 `<format>` support (GCC 13 for libstdc++), update the CMake guard and installation documentation, and validate that new floor in CI.

The DeepSelect PR above is still a useful portability fix, but it addresses only the first failure and does not resolve DeepGEMM's independent requirement.

title: [Perf][MRV2] Keep padded prompt-tail verification on FULL CUDA graphs
body:
## Purpose

Keep scheduler-padded prompt tails on MRV2 FULL CUDA graphs. Preserve raw prefill metadata during input preparation, then share the decode classification with drafters. PCP/adaptive verification remain excluded.

The scheduler requires computed context before padding, keeping uncached one-token prompts on the normal prefill path.

Related work checked: #54102 fixes residual padding, #55126 enables idle-worker tail padding, and #54810 changes DP scheduling. This PR fixes the remaining graph-dispatch fallback.

## Validation

Pre-commit passed; **47 runner/drafter + 8 scheduler tests passed**.

<details>
<summary>Unit-test commands</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --import-mode=importlib --confcutdir=tests/v1 \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd_cug.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --import-mode=importlib --confcutdir=tests/v1 \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k spec_decode_padding
```

</details>

## Performance test

**Hy4-preview, ModelOpt MXFP8 weights, real P/D:** 16 GB300 GPUs, P and D each TP1/DP8/EP8, MRV2/MTP3, FP8 KV (`fp8_ds_mla`), FLASHMLA_SPARSE, NIXL. P eager; D FULL_DECODE_ONLY. The checkpoint config specifies `quant_algo: MXFP8`, and both server logs confirm `quantization=modelopt_mxfp8`.

Both arms share processes/captures; baseline restores the old scheduler/dispatch behavior. Current PR Python source (`d84c01b`) overlays nightly `0.29.1rc1.dev452+g3df4ae153` compiled extensions, not a clean rebuild. Both arms use the same independent Sparse-MLA capture prerequisite outside this PR.

Fixed 512 input / 256 output tokens, 512 requests/run, concurrency 32, three repeats per arm/load (AB/BA/AB). **6144/6144 succeeded**. Values below are medians of the three run-level metrics.

| Offered QPS | p99 TPOT, before → after | Reduction | Actual req/s, before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4 | 84.16 → 21.75 ms | 74.2% | 2.024 → 3.876 |
| 8 | 78.37 → 23.41 ms | 70.1% | 2.076 → 5.139 |

Baseline saturates below the offered load. Sampled D ranks 0/4 showed padded-tail dispatch changing from NONE to FULL.

<details>
<summary>vLLM serve startup commands (P and D)</summary>

Each role uses two nodes with four GPUs per node. On each node, run the shared setup below, set `NODE_INDEX=0` or `1` within that role, then run the corresponding P or D command. The server environment must contain the PR source and shared Sparse-MLA capture prerequisite described above.

Shared setup:

```bash
MODEL_PATH="/path/to/Hy4-preview-MXFP8"
SERVER_PYTHON="/path/to/server-venv/bin/python"
HF_CACHE_PATH="/path/to/huggingface-cache"
P_MASTER="prefill-node-0"
D_MASTER="decode-node-0"
NODE_INDEX=0  # 0 on the first node of this role; 1 on the second
NET_IFACE="bond0.231"  # Network interface used in the experiment

export HF_HOME="$HF_CACHE_PATH" HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0
export VLLM_USE_RUST_BENCH=0 VLLM_ENABLE_HPC_OPS=1
export VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600
export NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1
export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME="$NET_IFACE" GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME="$NET_IFACE"
export UCX_NET_DEVICES=all UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE=n UCX_MEMTYPE_REG_WHOLE=n
export UCX_TLS=cuda_copy,cuda_ipc,tcp UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_MNNVL=y
export VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST="$(hostname)"

common_args=(
  --served-model-name hy4-preview --host 0.0.0.0
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 8
  --data-parallel-size-local 4
  --data-parallel-start-rank "$((NODE_INDEX * 4))"
  --data-parallel-hybrid-lb
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend deepep_v2
  --max-model-len 65536 --kv-cache-dtype fp8
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --disable-uvicorn-access-log
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
)
```

Prefill — run on both P nodes:

```bash
export VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5587
export FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MOE_OVERLAP_RESERVED_SMS=0
"$SERVER_PYTHON" -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve "$MODEL_PATH" \
  "${common_args[@]}" \
  --port 18800 --data-parallel-address "$P_MASTER" \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port 18801 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail","kv_connector_extra_config":{"kv_lease_duration":120}}'
```

Decode — run on both D nodes:

```bash
export VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5588
export FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MOE_OVERLAP_RESERVED_SMS=14
"$SERVER_PYTHON" -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve "$MODEL_PATH" \
  "${common_args[@]}" \
  --port 18802 --data-parallel-address "$D_MASTER" \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port 18803 \
  --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[4,8,12,16]}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail","kv_connector_extra_config":{"kv_lease_duration":120}}'
```

P also uses MTP3 to satisfy the NIXL compatibility check. The measured run additionally loaded `--worker-extension-cls experiment_probe.ProbeWorkerExtension` for dispatch counters, with the experiment-only mode-switch/probe installed separately; the commands above show the serving configuration without that instrumentation.

On the benchmark client, route requests to both P and both D API endpoints:

```bash
ROUTER_BIN="/path/to/router-venv/bin/vllm-router"
P0="prefill-node-0"; P1="prefill-node-1"
D0="decode-node-0"; D1="decode-node-1"
"$ROUTER_BIN" --vllm-pd-disaggregation \
  --policy round_robin --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18880 \
  --prometheus-port 18881 --worker-startup-timeout-secs 3600 \
  --request-timeout-secs 1800 --disable-retries \
  --prefill "http://$P0:18800" --prefill "http://$P1:18800" \
  --decode "http://$D0:18802" --decode "http://$D1:18802"
```

</details>

Full `vllm bench serve` command for candidate round 1 at 4 QPS (paths parameterized):

```bash
MODEL_PATH="/path/to/Hy4-preview-MXFP8"
CLIENT_PYTHON="/path/to/client-venv/bin/python"
HF_CACHE_PATH="/path/to/huggingface-cache"
RESULT_DIR="/path/to/benchmark-results"

VLLM_USE_RUST_BENCH=0 \
HF_HOME="$HF_CACHE_PATH" \
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
"$CLIENT_PYTHON" -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench serve \
  --backend vllm \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18880 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --served-model-name hy4-preview \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 512 \
  --random-output-len 256 \
  --random-range-ratio 0.0 \
  --num-prompts 512 \
  --request-rate 4 \
  --max-concurrency 32 \
  --seed 123 \
  --ignore-eos \
  --extra-body '{"temperature":0,"seed":123}' \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \
  --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 \
  --save-result \
  --save-detailed \
  --result-dir "$RESULT_DIR" \
  --result-filename bench-r1-qps4-candidate.json
```

For 8 QPS, change `--request-rate` to `8`; result filenames identify each round/load/arm. The harness switches baseline/candidate server behavior between drained phases; the filename itself does not select the arm.

## accuracy test

Same Hy4-preview MXFP8 P/D setup, with the PR enabled. Full GSM8K test split, upstream evaluator, 5-shot, greedy/seed 42, max 512 tokens, concurrency 32.

Post-change GSM8K scores:

- **Hy4-preview MXFP8 + MTP3:** original **90.75% (1197/1319)**; repeat evaluations **91.13% (1202/1319)** and **90.83% (1198/1319)**.
- **Qwen 27B BF16 + MTP3** (`qwen38-27b-hf`, hybrid GDN, TP1 P/D on two GB300 GPUs, BF16 KV): **94.47% (1246/1319)** and **94.54% (1247/1319)**. Same evaluation settings and PR Python/nightly overlay.

Called upstream `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` through a wrapper saving per-question outputs:

```python
evaluate_gsm8k(
    num_questions=1319, num_shots=5, max_tokens=512, model="hy4-preview",
    host="http://127.0.0.1", port=18880, temperature=0.0, seed=42,
    max_concurrency=32, request_timeout_seconds=1800,
)
```

ABBA repetitions with baseline controls showed no consistent score decrease; same-mode repetitions also changed answers. On 16 predetermined prompts per model, all four serial baseline/candidate runs produced identical tokens and complete returned top-5 logprob objects. Both models' dispatch counters confirmed padded-tail NONE → FULL.

A Qwen early-EOS case reproduced in both modes under mixed batching: EOS and newline were near-tied, and small logprob changes changed the greedy choice. All 32 serial repeats of that case were identical and normal. Hy4 also exposed stop-string/last-number parsing artifacts in the upstream evaluator. These checks do not establish concurrent output equivalence. Earlier K3/long-context numerical differences and other backend/drafter coverage remain unresolved.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, tests, experiments and this description. Human review and outstanding validation remain required before merge.

title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Add AITER topk backend for decodes
body:
## Purpose GLM-5.3-Flash indexer dispatches to `torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode` during decode. This leads to two calls to HIP kernel `topKPerRowDecode512DeviceLengthAware` which is quite slow for this model. We instead allow dispatching to an AITER kernel through the SparseIndexerTopk abstraction. Enable with `--sparse-indexer-topk-backend aiter`. Benchmarking suggest to use this AITER kernel whenever ctx>=64k. Models like DSv4 keep their old path, because DSv4 uses a different tuning (see `dsv4_indexer_prefers_native_top_k`) **Perf: -1-5% ITL on 64k+ ISL.** ## Test Plan ### 1. GSM8k vs main on gfx950 for GLM-5.3-Flash and DSv4-Flash ### 2. GLM-5.3-Flash perf diff on vllm bench serve sweep (MI350) ``` VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --max-num-seqs 512 \ --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE --sparse-indexer-topk-backend aiter ``` ### 3. Microbenchmarks Check where the aiter kernel is beneficial: ```bash HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ python3 benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_top_k_per_row_decode.py \ --rows 4 16 32 64 \ --lens 2048 8192 16384 65536 128000 256000 \ --capacity 262144 \ --graph ``` ### 4. Non-regression of DSv4-Flash vs main, bench serve sweep
```bash vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --trust-remote-code \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --block-size 256 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --max-num-seqs 512 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --compilation-config '{"mode": 3, "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' ```
## Test Result ### 1. title: [Perf][Attention] Avoid CPU-GPU sync in DCP sequence lengths
body:
## Purpose

Passing an integer `dcp_rank` to `get_dcp_local_seq_lens` creates a CUDA scalar tensor, introducing a synchronous host-to-device copy during DCP attention metadata construction. Keep the rank as a Python scalar so PyTorch uses it directly in the existing tensor arithmetic.

Related work: #54790 includes the same scalar fix alongside fused draft metadata updates for sparse MLA. This PR intentionally extracts the shared helper fix into a separate, minimal change so it can be reviewed and landed independently of that larger feature. The implementation overlap is acknowledged.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex was used to implement and validate this change and prepare the PR.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_cp_utils.py \
  -k 'get_dcp_local_seq_lens or skip_gate' -q
```

<details>
<summary>Standalone CUDA synchronization check</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import torch
from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import get_dcp_local_seq_lens

seq_lens = torch.arange(33, dtype=torch.int32, device='cuda')
expected = torch.tensor(
    [sum((pos // 2) % 4 == 2 for pos in range(length)) for length in range(33)],
    dtype=torch.int32,
)
previous_mode = torch.cuda.get_sync_debug_mode()
try:
    torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode('error')
    actual = get_dcp_local_seq_lens(seq_lens, 4, 2, 2)
finally:
    torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode(previous_mode)
torch.testing.assert_close(actual.cpu(), expected)
print('PASS: no synchronizing CUDA operation; values match the reference.')
print('GPU:', torch.cuda.get_device_name())
print('PyTorch:', torch.__version__)
PY
```

</details>



</details>

## Test Result

- Existing focused tests: **18 passed**.
- CUDA synchronization check on NVIDIA GB300 with PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`: before the fix, `RuntimeError: called a synchronizing CUDA operation`; after the fix, no synchronization error and exact agreement with the reference.
- All configured commit hooks passed, including Ruff, formatting, mypy, and sign-off checks.
- Sequential and concurrent smoke requests: **12/12 passed**, including short arithmetic and retrieval from 2,528- and 5,024-token prompts, covering chunked prefill.
- GSM8K, first 64 samples, 5-shot completions, temperature 0, concurrency 8, max output 1,024 tokens: **59/64 (92.19%)** for both strict and flexible exact match; **0 request errors**. This is a serving/accuracy smoke evaluation; no pre-change model baseline was run.

- [x] Test results provided.
- [x] Documentation impact considered; no user-facing documentation change is needed.

title: [Bugfix][Offload] UVA offload: allocate exact-size pinned host memory instead of Tensor.pin_memory()
body:
## Purpose

Fixes the first half of #58178. Fixes #56410 (same bug, reported earlier by @raj-parihar).

Related: #56413 (@Vaishnavi220506) drops the same `pin_memory()` call in `wrap_modules`; this PR overlaps that hunk and additionally covers the re-offload in `device_loading_context`, adds the opt-in, and carries the GB300 measurements below.

`UVAOffloader.wrap_modules` pins each offloaded parameter with `Tensor.pin_memory()`, which goes through PyTorch's CachingHostAllocator and rounds every allocation up to the next power of two. For MoE expert tensors that is a 33–45% host-memory tax the log never shows: a 4.5 GiB `w13_weight` occupies 8 GiB of host memory, and `--cpu-offload-gb 305` consumed ~504 GiB on a 494 GiB Grace host and was OOM-killed mid-load, while the log reported "Total CPU offloaded parameters: 305 GiB".

`get_cuda_view_from_cpu_tensor()` (`csrc/libtorch_stable/cuda_view.cu`) already handles an *unpinned* input by allocating exact-size mapped pinned memory with `cudaHostAlloc` and copying into it — the view is pinned either way. This PR hands the unpinned CPU tensor straight to it on the UVA path, and does the same in `device_loading_context`'s re-offload after `process_weights_after_loading`. The non-UVA fallback path (`VLLM_WEIGHT_OFFLOADING_DISABLE_UVA`) keeps `Tensor.pin_memory()` as before, since there the tensor is what the GPU copies from.

**Opt-in to the old pinning.** Exact-size is the default because it is the only behavior that honors `--cpu-offload-gb`. `VLLM_WEIGHT_OFFLOADING_UVA_CACHING_PIN=1` restores `Tensor.pin_memory()` on the UVA path for users who have the host headroom. On the DSV4.1-Flash / GB300 A/B below it gives back about 2.5% decode, at the cost of power-of-two host rounding. `VLLM_WEIGHT_OFFLOADING_DISABLE_PIN_MEMORY` is now documented as not affecting the default UVA path, since the default already takes the exact-size branch it used to select. It still governs the non-UVA fallback and the opt-in.

Not changed here: the re-offload after `process_weights_after_loading` still makes a second host copy of the repacked tensor; that's the second half of #58178 and a separate change.

## Test Plan

In-process `LLM(...)` on a DGX Station GB300 (494 GiB Grace host), `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL` truncated to 16 layers (`hf_overrides={"num_hidden_layers": 16}`, needs #58184), `--offload-backend uva --cpu-offload-gb 40 --cpu-offload-params routed_experts.w13_weight routed_experts.w2_weight`, `--moe-backend marlin`. Read `/proc/meminfo` before construction and after load; report `(MemTotal − MemAvailable)` delta. Page cache dropped between runs.

Parity: forward hooks dumping the last-token residual after every decoder layer for a fixed prompt, stock vs this PR.

## Test Result

| configuration | host memory used by the load |
|---|---|
| `main`, default env (`Tensor.pin_memory()`) | **90.3 GiB** |
| `main`, `VLLM_WEIGHT_OFFLOADING_DISABLE_PIN_MEMORY=1` (takes the `cudaHostAlloc` branch today) | 57.8 GiB |
| this PR, default env | **58.4 GiB** |

40 GiB of experts offloaded in every row; the 32 GiB difference is the power-of-two rounding.

Output parity: per-layer residuals bit-identical to `main` (max abs diff `0.0` over all 16 layers); first-token top-5 unchanged. Full 70-layer model with 320 GiB offloaded loads on the same box with 126 GiB host free and serves correctly (that boot used the env-var route; this PR makes it the default behavior).

**Decode cost** ([full data](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58185#issuecomment-5833189800)). DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 1× GB300, off60 routed experts, nightly `dee37d89`. Nine sequential boots, page cache dropped before each, same saved autotune set:

| | host shmem | C1 tok/s | C16 tok/s | load |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| stock (3 boots) | 380.2 GiB | 91.0 | 420.4 | 192–194 s |
| this PR, default (4 boots) | **325.4 GiB** | 88.8 (−2.5%) | 409.8 (−2.5%) | 201–204 s |
| this PR + `VLLM_WEIGHT_OFFLOADING_UVA_CACHING_PIN=1` | 380.2 GiB | 91.5 | 425.1 | 192 s |

The default costs ~2.5–2.8% decode at every concurrency 1–16. The opt-in returns to stock memory and speed. Greedy parity (18 prompts): 8 of 9 boots were byte-identical to stock, and one PR boot differed on one tool-call prompt (still a valid call; two other boots of the same code were identical). The mechanism for the decode gap is not known yet; both paths end up pinned and mapped. Tested on one Grace-Blackwell box only.

`ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on all changed files. New test: `test_cpu_offload_uva_caching_pin` (output equality with the opt-in on).

title: [Core] Pick hybrid KV cache group size by worst-case padding bytes; add --min-kv-cache-group-layers
body:
## Purpose

`_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size` splits each KV cache bucket into groups of `group_size` layers and pads the last group of each bucket. The current heuristic uses the smallest bucket as `group_size` (or the largest, if it is within 1.5x). A single-layer bucket, typically a speculative drafter layer whose spec cannot merge with the target's, drives this to `group_size = 1`, which means one KV cache group per layer, each rebuilding attention metadata every step. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash ends up with 46 groups.

This PR replaces the min / 1.5x-max heuristic:

- **Search** group sizes from `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` (capped at the largest bucket) up to the largest bucket.
- **Pick** the group size that wastes the fewest worst-case bytes per request on padding layers. Each padding layer costs its spec's `max_memory_usage_bytes` at `max_model_len`, so full attention padding scales with context length, while sliding window / mamba padding stays bounded. Ties prefer fewer groups.
- **New option `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` (default 3)** trades metadata overhead (more groups) against KV capacity (more padding).
- **Equal page sizes share a group** (from tomasruizt/vllm#16, by @tomasruizt): attention layers with different head shapes but the same block size, token-slot semantics and page bytes (e.g. Qwen3.5-4B's 4×256 target and 8×128 DFlash drafter) share one KV cache group; each keeps its own spec.
- **TP-invariant planning with a KV connector:** P/D peers may run different TP sizes, which change per-rank page bytes. When `kv_transfer_config` is set, padding is costed in the pages each layer needs per request at its own page size *before* page-size unification (TP changes page bytes, not page counts), and layers are not shared by equal page size (which also depends on TP). Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash then plans 10 groups at TP 1/2/4/8 (vs 17/17/5/10 without a connector).

This subsumes the 1.5x rule (gpt-oss + eagle still pads sw 12 → 13 instead of full 13 → 24).

Grouping at `max_model_len=256k`, default `--min-kv-cache-group-layers 3`:

| Layer buckets (target + *drafter*) | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash `[30 mamba, 10 full, *5 sw, 1 full*]` | gs=1, 46 groups | gs=3, 17 groups; 2 target full + 2 drafter full + 1 drafter sw padding layers |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B + Eagle3 `[30 mamba, 10 full, *1 full*]` ¹ | gs=1, 41 groups | gs=5, 9 groups; 4 drafter full padding layers |
| MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash `[9 full, 39 sw, *5 sw*]` | gs=5, 11 groups; 1 full + 1 sw padding | gs=3, 18 groups; 1 drafter sw padding |
| Kimi-K3 + DSpark `[69 KDA, 24 MLA, *5 sw*]` | gs=5, 20 groups; 1 MLA + 1 KDA padding | gs=3, 33 groups; 1 drafter sw padding |
| Gemma3-27B `[52 sw, 10 full]` | gs=10, 7 groups; 8 sw padding | gs=5, 13 groups; 3 sw padding |
| gpt-oss-20b + eagle `[12 sw, 13 full]` | gs=13, 2 groups | unchanged |
| Gemma3-1B/4B/12B, Llama4-Scout, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | — | unchanged |

¹ Computed assuming the drafter's KV bytes per token equal the target's; not measured.

Behavior change: group sizes can now go below the smallest bucket, trading more groups for less (bounded) padding, e.g. Gemma3-27B 7 → 13 groups, MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash 18 groups. Whether to keep a floor at the smallest bucket is open (it gives 7 / 7 / 17 groups for Gemma3-27B / MiMo / Kimi-K3, at the cost of more bounded padding).

### Comparison with #58175

#58175 targets MiMo. On DFlash / Eagle3 it keeps main's per-layer grouping (gcd of `[10, 1]` = 1). On MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash this PR now picks the same group size (gs=3, 18 groups, no full attention padding, 1 drafter sw padding layer).

Relation to other PRs:
- #51742 ignores single-layer buckets when taking the min (gs=5 for DFlash) without bounding the resulting full attention padding.
- #49472 minimizes `padding + num_groups` in layer counts, without distinguishing full attention from bounded-memory padding (e.g. pads 3 full attention layers on Gemma3-27B).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hidden_states_connector.py -q
```

## Test Result

**4 tests currently fail** after allowing group sizes below the smallest bucket (`test_hybrid_group_size_selection[10-52-0-3-10]`, `[9-39-5-3-9]`, `test_get_kv_cache_config_one_worker`, `test_hybrid_draft_full_attention_shapes[8-5-9]`); their expectations will be updated once the floor question above is settled. `test_kv_transfer_group_planning_is_tp_invariant` and `test_equal_page_size_sharing_disabled_with_kv_connector` cover the KV connector behavior. `test_hybrid_group_size_selection` covers the drafter (floor 2 and 3), gpt-oss + eagle, Gemma3-27B and MiMo layouts. One sub-case of `test_get_kv_cache_config_one_worker` changed expectation: at its `max_model_len=16`, a sliding window layer's worst case (2 blocks) exceeds full attention's (1 block), so padding full attention is now cheaper.

### Benchmarks

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 + z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash, 1× B300, BF16 mamba states, GSM8K, single runs, acceptance length 5.1–5.2 in all runs.

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --max-num-seqs 32 --no-enable-prefix-caching --block-size 128 \
  --mamba-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 --min-kv-cache-group-layers $M \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash","method":"dflash","num_speculative_tokens":7}'
vllm bench serve --model Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --dataset-name hf --dataset-path openai/gsm8k --hf-split test \
  --num-prompts max(32, 8*C) --max-concurrency C --num-warmups 2*C
```

(`--block-size 128` is needed on main too: the DFlash drafter's FLASH_ATTN backend only supports 128-token kernel blocks on B300, but the hybrid block size is aligned only to the target backend, giving 592 → `No common block size for 592`. Separate issue.)

Left: this PR. Right: this PR + #52297 (GDN metadata, orthogonal). `--min-kv-cache-group-layers 1` reproduces main's grouping (46 groups).

![min-kv-cache-group-layers sweep](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LucasWilkinson/vllm/af4013a3827d250b266c6e48b1fc124880523780/pareto_min_layers.png)

Grouping and padding cost per request vs. context length. Target full attention is 2 KiB/token/layer (2 KV heads × 256); drafter layers are 4 KiB/token/layer (8 KV heads × 128). For reference, the unpadded full attention KV is 24 KiB/token (10 target + 1 drafter layer).

| `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` | gs | groups | KV cache capacity | padding layers | full-context padding | 8k | 32k | 128k | 256k |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (= main) | 1 | 46 | 7.42M tokens | none | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 2 | 2 | 24 | 6.42M tokens | 1 drafter full, 1 drafter sw | 4 KiB/token (+17%) | 48 MiB | 144 MiB | 528 MiB | 1.02 GiB |
| 3 (default) | 3 | 17 | 5.19M tokens | 2 target full, 2 drafter full, 1 drafter sw | 12 KiB/token (+50%) | 112 MiB | 400 MiB | 1.52 GiB | 3.02 GiB |
| 4 | 5 | 10 | 4.80M tokens | 4 drafter full | 16 KiB/token (+67%) | 128 MiB | 512 MiB | 2 GiB | 4 GiB |

The sliding window padding layer adds a bounded ~16 MiB (4096-token window × 4 KiB), included above. The measured KV cache capacity drops (−13.5% / −30% / −35%) track the full-context overhead.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Replace torch.topk in DSA candidate block selection
body: ## Summary `select_candidate_blocks` picks the top-k blocks per row with `torch.topk`, which runs a multi-pass radix select (`computeBlockDigitCounts`, `computeBlockwiseWithinKCounts`, `gatherTopK`). That does two things this caller does not need: - **It orders the results.** The only consumer is `_candidate_flags_kernel`, which does `flags[block] = 1`. Nothing downstream reads the ranking or the scores — only the *set* of selected block ids matters. - **It scans the whole padded workspace.** The logits workspace is padded to `max_model_len`, so `nblocks` is `max_model_len / block_size` no matter how short the context is. Past a row's end every block scores `-inf` and can never win a slot, but `torch.topk` has no way to express a per-row extent, so it reads all of it. This PR replaces that select on ROCm with a Triton kernel: - Each score and its index are packed into one order-preserving `int64` key, so `tl.topk` returns both at once and the separate `_store_candidates_kernel` pass disappears. The float bits are sign-transformed so IEEE order becomes unsigned order, and the index rides inverted in the low bits so ties resolve to the smaller index, matching `torch.topk`. - Each row is bounded by its own `end`, which is the part `torch.topk` cannot do. At 4K context in a 256K workspace this skips ~98% of the columns. - Decode rows are `batch * next_n`, only 1–640, which is too few to fill the GPU one program per row. Rows are split across programs and merged, with the split size computed **on device** from each row's live extent — a host-side bound would need a sync, and sizing from the padded width instead measured 6.3x → 2.0x at low concurrency. **The CUDA path is unchanged**; the new kernel is behind `current_platform.is_rocm()`. ## Not a duplicate Checked open PRs touching this area: - **#57858** is the only other open PR touching `candidate_blocks.py`, but it optimizes **prefill consumer-layer scoring** (`candidate_mqa_logits`, scoring only candidate columns). The producer-side block select this PR rewrites is untouched there. The two are complementary. Note #57858 also flips `_store_candidates_kernel`'s NaN handling (`!=` → `>`); the ROCm path here bypasses that kernel entirely, so the behaviors do not collide. - **#48726** (LiteTopk) is the indexer's *token* top-k, a different kernel and stage. - **#50470**, **#46172**, **#56944** touch `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` only (AITER dispatch, indexer optimization, prefill row sharding), not block candidate selection. No open PR optimizes `select_candidate_blocks`. ## Correctness The new path must select the same block *set* as the existing path. Verified against the unchanged path across 27 configurations — contexts 512 to 262144, rows 1 to 640, ragged per-row ends, non-zero `row_ks` starts, `row_repeat` decode grouping, `topk_blocks > nblocks`, and NaN scores: ``` 27 cases, 0 mismatches ``` Two cases this caught during development, both now handled: - `torch.topk` ranks NaN *highest*, and `_block_scores_kernel` can emit NaN during warmup, so keys force NaN above `+inf`. - When `nblocks < topk_blocks` the internal `K_PAD` shrinks below the output width, leaving tail columns unwritten; they are now `-1` filled. ## Tests ``` $ pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_candidate_mask.py -q 9 passed, 14 warnings in 4.23s $ pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py exit=0 (no failures) ``` ## Kernel performance (MI355X) Full `select_candidate_blocks`, CUDA-graph timed, swept over the decode shape space: concurrency 1–128 x spec-decode depth 1–5, `max_model_len=262144`, `block_size=8`, `k=64`. All 120 points are faster. | context | median | range | | --- | --- | --- | | 4096 | 4.16x | 3.97–5.08x | | 16384 | 3.99x | 3.27–4.70x | | 65536 | 2.94x | 1.64–3.15x | Representative points (microseconds): | context | conc | next_n | rows | before | after | speedup | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 4096 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 47.55 | 11.20 | 4.24x | | 4096 | 32 | 1 | 32 | 58.00 | 13.96 | 4.16x | | 4096 | 128 | 5 | 640 | 293.54 | 67.86 | 4.33x | | 16384 | 32 | 1 | 32 | 59.19 | 14.31 | 4.14x | | 16384 | 128 | 5 | 640 | 299.65 | 91.67 | 3.27x | | 65536 | 32 | 1 | 32 | 60.31 | 19.30 | 3.13x | | 65536 | 128 | 5 | 640 | 330.51 | 185.83 | 1.78x | These shapes are TP-independent: the DSA indexer is replicated across ranks (`index_n_heads` is not divided by `tp_size`, unlike the main attention heads), so TP2 and TP4 run identical selections and one sweep covers both. ## Notes The kernel is still well above the bandwidth roofline (~45x at the largest shapes, more at small ones where it is latency-bound on two launches), so there is headroom left. `TILE=512` is a compromise: 1024 would take 65536-context from 2.36x to 2.79x but drop 4096-context from 23.8x to 14.4x. A context-aware tile choice could get both. Benchmarks used uniform context per batch; heavily ragged batches are bounded by their longest row. ## End-to-end serving Measured on MI355X TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, dspark MTP (5 speculative tokens, acceptance pinned at 3.51 so acceptance variance cannot contribute). Both arms are the **same build** differing only by an env toggle on the selection path, run concurrently on separate 4-GPU sets, after a warmup pass over every shape so Triton JIT and graph capture are paid before measurement. snapshot of trace: Before: After: **There is no measurable end-to-end difference, and none should be expected.** Output throughput, ISL 4096 / OSL 128: | concurrency | baseline tok/s | this PR tok/s | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 259.4 | 257.1 | | 8 | 1287.7 | 1282.4 | | 32 | 1068.9 | 1070.3 | | 128 | 1253.8 | 1254.8 | Repeating a single configuration three times shows run-to-run spread of 1112–1191 tok/s on baseline and 1142–1166 on this branch, with the sign of the difference flipping between repeats. The noise floor is several percent, while the expected effect is about 0.2%: the selection saves roughly 45 us per step against a 14.6 ms inter-token latency. The kernel win is real but it is a sub-1% slice of step time, so it cannot show up above noise in serving throughput. Median ITL, the most stable metric here, is unchanged (14.59-14.64 ms baseline vs 14.61-14.73 ms this branch). This PR should therefore be read as removing a hotspot that is prominent in kernel traces and cutting its cost 2-5x, not as an end-to-end throughput win. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used for this change.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Gate MXFP8 linear LDS budget on gfx950, not the Triton version string
body:
### Purpose

`_BK256_STAGES` drops from 3 to 2 on gfx950 because `TRITON_HIP_USE_ASYNC_COPY`
adds an LDS buffer that leaves no room for `num_stages=3` at `BLOCK_K=256`. The
condition guarding that reduction tests the Triton **version string**:

```python
_BK256_STAGES = 3
if triton.__version__.startswith("3.8") and current_platform.is_rocm():
    from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx950
    if on_gfx950():
        _BK256_STAGES = 2
```

AMD ships ROCm Triton builds that carry the async-copy default on gfx950 while
still reporting **3.7.0**. The `"3.8"` test misses them, `num_stages` stays at
3, and the kernel cannot be launched. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
(`hidden_size` 5120) the fused `wq_a`/`wkv` GEMM aborts during startup:

```
File "vllm/models/deepseek_v41/attention.py", line 843, in _fused_wqa_wkv_gemm
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py", line 2575, in apply
File "vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/rocm_native.py", line 94, in _mxfp8_dot_scaled_linear
triton.runtime.errors.OutOfResources: out of resource: shared memory,
Required: 204272, Hardware limit: 163840. Reducing block sizes or
`num_stages` may help.
```

All four TP ranks fail and `EngineCore` never initialises, so this is a hard
startup failure rather than a performance regression.

### Fix

The version string is the wrong signal. What determines whether the extra LDS
buffer is resident is the **architecture** â€” and whether async copy is enabled â€”
not which Triton release is installed. Gate on `on_gfx950()`, and additionally
honour an explicit `TRITON_HIP_USE_ASYNC_COPY=0`, under which the buffer is
absent and `num_stages=3` fits again:

```diff
-_BK256_STAGES = 3
-if triton.__version__.startswith("3.8") and current_platform.is_rocm():
+_BK256_STAGES = 3
+if current_platform.is_rocm():
     from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx950
 
-    if on_gfx950():
+    if on_gfx950() and os.environ.get("TRITON_HIP_USE_ASYNC_COPY", "1") != "0":
         _BK256_STAGES = 2
```

The existing `TODO(rasmith)(Rohan138)` referencing #50605 is preserved.

### Scope

Only widens when the reduction applies: on gfx950 with async copy at its
default it now fires on Triton 3.7 as well as 3.8. Non-gfx950 ROCm and CUDA are
unaffected, and users who explicitly disable async copy keep `num_stages=3`,
which is the faster configuration when the buffer is absent.

A reviewer may reasonably prefer querying Triton's own knob
(`triton.knobs.amd.use_async_copy`) rather than reading the environment
variable. I used the env var because the knob reads `None` when unset â€” the
default is resolved inside the backend, so `None` does not tell you which way it
will go â€” whereas the env var is exactly the user-facing opt-out. Happy to
switch if there is a supported API for the resolved value.

### Test Plan

Hardware: 4x AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.4, torch
2.10.0+rocm7.2.4, **Triton 3.7.0**, TP=4.
Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (fp8, `weight_block_size` [32, 32],
`hidden_size` 5120, 510 GB / 48 shards).

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```

Three arms: unpatched; patched at the async-copy default; patched with
`TRITON_HIP_USE_ASYNC_COPY=0`.

### Test Result

| Arm | Startup | c1 | c8 | c16 | c32 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| unpatched | **OutOfResources, engine dead** | â€” | â€” | â€” | â€” |
| patched, async copy default (`num_stages=2`) | OK | 100.3 | 672.2 | 1102.9 | 2281.9 |
| patched, `TRITON_HIP_USE_ASYNC_COPY=0` (`num_stages=3`) | OK | 106.3 | 683.2 | 1230.4 | 2297.9 |

tok/s aggregate, 256 output tokens/request, median of 3, unique prompts. The
two patched arms are equal within run-to-run noise (these are short runs
varying 10â€“20%), so the default is left at the vendor setting rather than
disabling async copy globally for every other kernel.

Correctness after the fix: `17*23` â†’ 391, `2^10` â†’ 1024, capital of Japan â†’
Tokyo. Zero `Memory access fault` occurrences across the concurrency sweep.

No new tests are included: this is a module-level constant selected from
platform state at import time, so exercising it needs either a gfx950 device or
a fairly invasive import-time monkeypatch of `current_platform` and
`on_gfx950`. Happy to add one if maintainers prefer a particular pattern.

title: [Bug][CPU][Spec Decode]: PR #56323 left 6 CPU Triton fallbacks patching module globals that are no longer read — spec decode broken on arm64
body:
### Summary

`CPUModelRunner._postprocess_triton()` installs C++ fallbacks for Triton kernels
when Triton is unavailable. Six of those patches rebind a **module-level global**
that nothing reads at call time any more, so the fallbacks are never installed.

This is the production path on `linux/arm64` and macOS: `docker/Dockerfile.cpu:139`
builds `triton-cpu` only for `TARGETARCH=amd64`, so `HAS_TRITON` is `False` there.
The x86 CPU lane has Triton, so CI never exercises these fallbacks.

### Root cause: a regression in #56323

Commit `aed894c19` (#56323, "[6/N][warmup][DSv4] Migrate sampling, and DFlash JIT
kernels") moved these kernels behind `@triton_kernel_dispatcher_with_warmup`.
The dispatcher captures the kernel into the **instance** at import time
(`jit_warmup_triton_helper.py:656`) and launches `self.kernel` (`:270`).

Before that commit the kernels were launched by module-global lookup, so the
monkey-patch worked. At parent `e19a3e172`, `rejection_sampler.py:597` read:

```python
expand_kernel[(batch_size,)](...)      # name resolved at call time
```

Today `expand_batch_to_tokens` calls the dispatcher instead
(`rejection_sampler.py:612`), and rebinding `rejection_sampler.expand_kernel`
has no effect.

#56323 updated 3 of the patches to the new `.kernel` form (+3/-4 in
`cpu_model_runner.py`) and left the rest in the old style.

### The 6 dead patches (`vllm/v1/worker/cpu_model_runner.py`)

| line | patched name | dispatcher that actually holds the kernel |
|---|---|---|
| 94  | `spec_decode_utils.copy_and_expand_dflash_inputs_kernel` | `_copy_and_expand_dflash_inputs` (utils.py:782) |
| 105 | `spec_decode_utils.eagle_step_slot_mapping_metadata_kernel` | `_eagle_step_slot_mapping_metadata` (utils.py:120) |
| 108 | `rejection_sampler.rejection_greedy_sample_kernel` | dispatcher at rejection_sampler.py:808 |
| 111 | `rejection_sampler.rejection_random_sample_kernel` | dispatcher at rejection_sampler.py:931 |
| 114 | `rejection_sampler.expand_kernel` | `_expand` (rejection_sampler.py:991) |
| 115 | `rejection_sampler.sample_recovered_tokens_kernel` | dispatcher at rejection_sampler.py:1112 |

Lines 97-104 additionally `setattr` the kernel onto the `vllm.v1.spec_decode.dflash`
module, but `dflash.py` imports the dispatcher `_copy_and_expand_dflash_inputs`
(`:16`) and calls it (`:149`); it never reads that name.

Correctly patched (for contrast): `block_table._COMPUTE_SLOT_MAPPING_KERNEL.kernel`,
`_eagle_prepare_inputs_padded.kernel`, `_eagle_prepare_next_token_padded.kernel`,
`_copy_and_expand_eagle_inputs.kernel`.

### Expected failure mode (derived from source, not yet executed)

Without Triton, `triton.jit` returns the function unchanged
(`vllm/triton_utils/importing.py:104-121`), so `self.kernel` stays a plain
function and `launch()` does `kernel[grid](**kwargs)`, which should raise:

```
TypeError: 'function' object is not subscriptable
```

This is the signature reported in #55480 for `mamba_utils.batch_memcpy`, which
reaches the same placeholder through a different route.

**I want to be explicit that I have not yet executed this.** The report above is
from reading the source and `git` history; my arm64 build is not finished. The
part I am confident in is the binding analysis, which is verifiable statically:
the dispatchers hold `self.kernel`, and nothing reads those module globals at
call time. If maintainers with a working arm64 CPU build can confirm the runtime
behaviour, that would settle it faster than my build will. I will post the
traceback here once mine completes.

### Relationship to other issues

- #55480 fixes `batch_memcpy` only, at its call site. Different kernel.
- #55005 / #55006 fix a dtype copy-back **inside** `_expand_kernel_impl`. That is
  orthogonal and currently unreachable on arm64, since the shim is never installed.

### Suggested fix

Retarget the six patches to the dispatcher objects' `.kernel`, matching the four
that are already correct, and drop the dead `dflash_module` block (which is the
only user of `import sys` in that file).

A more durable alternative, if maintainers prefer: have the dispatcher resolve
its kernel dynamically, so this class of breakage cannot recur silently.

### Verification script

Once built, this needs no model, server or GPU:

```python
import vllm.utils.cpu_triton_utils as cpu_tl
import vllm.v1.sample.rejection_sampler as rs
from vllm.v1.worker.cpu_model_runner import CPUModelRunner

CPUModelRunner._postprocess_triton(None)   # reads no instance state
print(rs._expand.kernel is cpu_tl.expand_kernel)          # expected False today
print(rs._rejection_greedy_sample.kernel is cpu_tl.rejection_greedy_sample_kernel)
```

### Environment
- Analysis against `bc162b3f9` (main, 2026-09-22)
- Target platform: `linux/arm64`, where `HAS_TRITON` is `False`
- Runtime reproduction pending (build in progress)

---

AI assistance was used to investigate and write up this report. The binding
analysis and the `git` archaeology were checked against the source at the
commits cited above.

title: [Bugfix][DSA] Bound DeepSelect sentinel columns in the sparse top-k remap
body:
## Problem and fix

DSV4.1 startup can hit a CUDA illegal memory access in `_sparse_topk_remap_kernel`. Dummy runs feed NaN indexer logits by design (`deep_select_topk` disables its NaN trap for this reason). For a row with NaN inside its valid prefix and `end > topk`, DeepSelect writes an internal sentinel (`0x3f3f3f3f`) to slot 0 of the output row and returns without writing the other slots, which keep whatever the `col_indices` scratch held (the previous call's columns, always in `[0, width)` or `-1`). The remap only rejected negative columns, so slot 0 indexed `sparse_indices[row, 0x3f3f3f3f // SBK]`, about 500 MiB past the row. Whether that faults depends on what happens to be mapped there: it crashes on some layouts (observed on TP4) and silently writes garbage positions on others.

Treat columns outside `[0, width)` as invalid, like `-1`. For a NaN row this makes slot 0 `-1`; the other slots remap stale in-bounds columns, which is harmless for the dummy runs that produce NaN logits. Finite logits are unaffected, since DeepSelect only returns columns below `end <= width`.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
```
