title: [Feature][MoE] Collect expert distributions with or without EPLB
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add opt-in logical expert-routing statistics with or without Expert Parallel Load Balancing (EPLB), without changing routing or enabling expert rearrangement.

Rebased on October 5, 2026 onto public main `54d93af9fb89d0bb8392bdb72db42bb6a17cb4ca`; head `46c8d680bd6ae15c58e209c93ceb2c72912dcecc`. This PR remains **draft** for design/code review and the remaining GPU validation.

## Claims

- One collection configuration and logical-expert JSONL schema work with EPLB on or off.
- Support interval histograms and bounded, sampled per-layer/per-target-iteration traces.
- Count rank-local source-token ownership without additional observability collectives or per-expert Prometheus labels.
- Disabled collection creates no tracker or device/export buffers. Enabled collection has instrumentation/export costs; no overhead or speedup result is claimed.

## Validation

- October 5: `pre-commit run --from-ref 54d93af9fb89d0bb8392bdb72db42bb6a17cb4ca --to-ref HEAD` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Focused CPU-only suite after rebase: **110 passed, 92 skipped**:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_expert_load_stats.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py \
  tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py::test_expert_load_stats_cli \
  tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_eplb.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py -q
```

The local invocation used a temporary plugin applying `skip_global_cleanup` and a CPU device-type override for CLI default construction. These environment workarounds are not committed. Accelerator tests were skipped, not passed.

Coverage includes common options with EPLB on/off, routed-expert-capture coexistence, PP layer selection, non-owning replicas, ownership rules, trace limits/backpressure, warmup resets, and writer errors. Earlier isolated negative controls failed the PP-selection, ownership-allocation, export-error, compact-log, and warmup-reset regressions when their fixes were removed.

Added CUDA tests cover exact histograms (3, 32, 64, 96, and 256 experts), graph replay, asynchronous export, and preservation of EPLB mapping/sampling. They are wired into existing worker CI but have not been run. A synthetic kernel benchmark is provided without measured results.

**Before promotion/merge:** run CUDA correctness and graph tests, distributed ownership checks, output-equivalence/model evaluation, end-to-end overhead measurements, and serving-time synchronization checks with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. No GPU/serving or performance result is claimed. GPU CI on a draft requires a maintainer or configured trusted contributor. On the October 5 head, [hosted pre-run-check](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/37345076368/job/111881502632) and [Read the Docs](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/34949716/) stopped at the contributor-verification prerequisite, before linting or building documentation.

## Details

Use the same collection configuration in either mode:

```sh
# Observe without balancing.
vllm serve MODEL --data-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --expert-load-stats-config '{"enabled":true,"log_interval":1000,"output_dir":"./expert-load"}'

# Collect the same statistics while balancing.
vllm serve MODEL --data-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --enable-eplb \
  --expert-load-stats-config '{"enabled":true,"log_interval":1000,"output_dir":"./expert-load"}'
```

Dotted CLI options and Python configuration are also supported. Existing EPLB policy, recording windows, and balancedness logging retain their meaning. Logical routing skew is distinct from physical EP-rank balance.

Instrument non-monolithic `BaseRouter` target routing: use a histogram kernel without EPLB and fuse logical counting into the existing mapping traversal with EPLB, preserving its physical counters. Explicit Triton histogram masks exclude invalid/padded/unowned lanes; sentinel binning is not safe on Triton 3.7.1.

Persistent counter buffers support graph replay. Two bounded export slots move D2H copying and writing off the inference thread; slow exports drop trace samples, not summary counts. Writer waits are confined to the reporter thread and shutdown. Filesystem failures disable JSONL writes and log once without stopping serving; console summaries and export-error counts continue. CUDA errors are not suppressed.

Iteration IDs are local target-forward counters, not synchronized DP steps. Target verification tokens count even if rejected later. Draft forwards, warmup, dummy work, padding, and shared experts are excluded. Full per-expert vectors require JSONL; console output is a compact interval overview. Global layer IDs are validated per PP stage; unselected stages and non-owning TP replicas allocate no tracker.

Initial support is CUDA/non-monolithic routing. Custom/monolithic routers, LoRA, DBO/ubatching, CP, elastic EP, encoder disaggregation, KV-sharing fast prefill, and adaptive verification fail closed; see the feature guide for full scope.

The shared collector keeps lifecycle/export logic outside the model runners. MRV2 brackets real target forwards explicitly; MRV1 retains compatibility for existing deployments using the same CLI. This larger feature still warrants maintainer design review, especially its ownership and export lifecycle. Current main's EPLB startup, dummy-weight handling, compilation tests, and CPU routed-expert tests are preserved; feature semantics are unchanged by the rebase.

Open-PR searches were refreshed on October 5. #43715 / #30696 concern physical EPLB metrics/Prometheus; #41141 concerns offline placement, #56716 EPLB warmup, and #57100 synthetic routing distributions for benchmarks. None provides this EPLB-independent logical-expert collection interface.

Checklist review: no new rebase-related code issue. Shared infrastructure, explicit unsupported-path checks, documentation, and tests are retained. GPU correctness, disabled/enabled overhead, distributed ownership, and end-to-end validation remain open; the rebase does not establish those results.

title: [Bug] NIXL lease reaper strands expired KV blocks behind a heartbeated head entry
body:
### Your current environment

`v0.27.1`. Found by source inspection; the repro below is standalone stdlib and
needs no vLLM install. I have not yet quantified the runtime impact on a live
deployment — filing this because the control flow looks unambiguous and the
reclaim path it affects is shared by both NIXL connector modes.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The NIXL lease reaper in `NixlConnectorWorker` relies on `_reqs_to_send` being ordered by expiry, but `_handle_heartbeat` breaks that invariant. A request that keeps receiving heartbeats can sit at the head of the dict and block every entry behind it from ever being reaped, even long after those entries' leases expire.

**The invariant.** The reaper exits at the first non-expired entry:

```python
# vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py (~L2147)
while self._reqs_to_send:
    req_id, expires = next(iter(self._reqs_to_send.items()))
    # Sorted dict, oldest requests are put first so we can exit early.
    if now < expires:
        break
    ...
    del self._reqs_to_send[req_id]
```

That is correct only while expiry order matches insertion order.

**What breaks it.** Heartbeats update the value in place:

```python
# same file (~L2198)
if req_id in self._reqs_to_send:
    old = self._reqs_to_send[req_id]
    self._reqs_to_send[req_id] = max(old, new_expiry)
```

Updating an existing key in a Python `dict` does not change its insertion position, so a renewed request keeps its original (early) slot while its expiry moves arbitrarily far into the future. Requests are inserted once (`pull_worker.py` asserts `req_id not in self._reqs_to_send` before inserting), so the position is never revisited.

**Consequence.** This is the common case under load: the oldest pending-send request is the one most likely to still be queued on D, and therefore the one being heartbeated, while newer requests behind it are not.

### Minimal reproduction

```python
LEASE_DURATION = 30.0     # kv_lease_duration default
LEASE_EXTENSION = 20.0    # kv_lease_duration * 2 // 3

def reap(reqs_to_send, now):                      # verbatim control flow
    done = []
    while reqs_to_send:
        req_id, expires = next(iter(reqs_to_send.items()))
        if now < expires:
            break
        del reqs_to_send[req_id]
        done.append(req_id)
    return done

def handle_heartbeat(reqs_to_send, req_id, now):  # verbatim
    if req_id in reqs_to_send:
        reqs_to_send[req_id] = max(reqs_to_send[req_id], now + LEASE_EXTENSION)

reqs = {"A": 0.0 + LEASE_DURATION,   # 30.0, enters first, stays queued on D
        "B": 2.0 + LEASE_DURATION,   # 32.0, never renewed
        "C": 4.0 + LEASE_DURATION}   # 34.0, never renewed
for t in (20.0, 40.0, 60.0, 80.0):
    handle_heartbeat(reqs, "A", t)   # A -> 100.0, still at the head

for now in (35.0, 50.0, 90.0):
    print(now, reap(dict(reqs), now))
```

Output:

```
35.0 []
50.0 []
90.0 []
```

`B` and `C` expired at `t=32.0` and `t=34.0`. At `t=90.0` neither has been released. They stay stranded for as long as `A` keeps receiving heartbeats, which by design can be indefinite ("each heartbeat extends the lease ... keeping blocks alive indefinitely while D is healthy" — `docs/design/nixl_kv_cache_lease.md`).

### Impact

Blocks that should have been reclaimed within `kv_lease_duration` (default 30s) of their reader disconnecting are held indefinitely on P, reducing available KV cache. This is the exact failure mode lease renewal was introduced to avoid (#41383): the design doc motivates the short initial lease by noting that under the old fixed 480s timeout "P would hold onto potentially several GBs of 'dead' blocks for up to 8 minutes". The head-of-line case restores that behaviour without a bound.

It also makes `vllm:nixl_num_kv_expired_reqs` under-report, since stranded entries are never passed to `record_kv_expired_req()`.

### Note on one fix that does *not* work

Re-inserting on heartbeat (delete + insert to move the entry to the tail) does not restore the invariant, because `max(old, now + extension)` can still be smaller than a later-inserted entry's initial expiry:

```
Y inserted t=0   -> expiry 30
X inserted t=25  -> expiry 55
Y renewed at t=26 -> max(30, 46) = 46, moved to tail
order: X(55), Y(46)   # at now=50, X blocks the already-expired Y
```

### Candidate fixes

1. **Scan all entries** instead of exiting early. Simplest and obviously correct; `O(n)` per step in the number of pending sends rather than amortized `O(1)`.
2. **Expiry-ordered heap with lazy deletion.** Push `(expiry, req_id)` on insert and on each renewal; pop while `top.expiry <= now` and skip entries whose expiry no longer matches the dict. `O(log n)`, more code.
3. **Keep the dict, maintain a separate ordered index** keyed by expiry.

Happy to send a PR for whichever shape maintainers prefer.

One thing to check alongside the fix: the reaper calls `self._reqs_to_process.remove(req_id)` (`base_worker.py` ~L2160) while other paths use `.discard()` (`pull_worker.py` ~L90). Any fix that reaps entries the current code never reaches will exercise that line for request IDs it previously never saw, so `remove()` vs `discard()` there may need a second look.

### Related but distinct

- #53095 (`NixlPushConnector heartbeat fails to renew KV leases`) is the opposite
  direction: leases expiring while the consumer still wants the blocks. This
  report is about a renewed entry preventing *other* entries from expiring. Both
  touch `_handle_heartbeat` / `_reqs_to_send` in `base_worker.py`, which is shared
  by the push and pull paths, so a fix here may be worth checking against that
  report.
- #46283 concerns decode-side *recv* blocks leaking on abort, and notes in passing
  that the `_reqs_to_send` reaper covers only the send side. That observation is
  consistent with this report but the defect is a different one.
- #53128 (closed) is the `TieringOffloadingSpec` p2p `_UNBOUND_STORE_TIMEOUT_S`
  path, a separate mechanism.

### Before submitting a new issue...

title: [Feature] [KV Offload] Support sharing SimpleCPUOffload prefix caches across local DP replicas
body:
# Motivation

`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` (#37160) keeps a private CPU prefix cache per
DP replica. Unlike the native `OffloadingConnector`, the Simple connector is
agnostic to KV organization and adapts to day-0 models without per-model
integration, which makes it a natural fit for throughput-oriented DP-heavy
deployments (e.g. 8×H100 with DP8/TP1/EP). In such deployments each
replica's CPU KV pool is small, and identical prefixes are recomputed
whenever a request is routed to a different local replica, even though a
completed CPU copy exists on the same host. Sharing the local CPU pool would
let these deployments draw on a larger combined KV pool instead of many
small private ones.

Measured on a diagnostic DP4/TP1/EP topology (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, two hosts,
two logical workers sharing each physical GB10 GPU — timings are diagnostic,
not production throughput numbers). Routing a repeated ~6K-token prefix to a
peer replica costs **14.41 s TTFT (full recompute)**; with shared offload it
costs **5.22 s (91.7% of prompt tokens restored via external KV transfer)** —
a 63.8% reduction.

# Proposed approach

Opt-in `cpu_offload_shared=true` in `kv_connector_extra_config`:
- Reuse `SharedOffloadRegion` (#50094), `BlockPool` hash/LRU, `ChunkStatus`, connector handshake; no new copy backend or allocator
- Fixed per-writer slot partitions; shared publication index + `flock` on the metadata region fd; reader references protect slots during peer DMA
- Node-local only; eager offloading; any TP×DP combination (each TP coordinate shares its own KV shard pool); startup fails closed on incompatible hash/model/layout
- PP/DCP/PCP beyond 1 is not supported yet; extending to those is desirable follow-up work, not required for the initial version

# Context

- Duplicate check against open PRs: #53474, #53073, #47324, #57418, #43483,
  #57422, #54743, #52921 — none publishes prefix hashes across DP schedulers.
- No code dependency on #53474 or #53073: peer discovery uses the existing
  `in_the_same_node_as` and region APIs. #53474 is actively reshaping the native connector's region geometry, so this feature deliberately avoids
  coupling to it; overlapping files (worker.py, docs) should need only routine rebases.

# [Feature] [KV Offload] Support sharing SimpleCPUOffload prefix caches across local DP replicas

## Summary

Implement #58240. `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` currently keeps an independent CPU prefix cache
in each DP replica. When a request is routed to another local replica, that replica recomputes
a prefix even though a completed CPU copy is available. This change adds an opt-in
`cpu_offload_shared=true` mode that lets local DP replicas reuse completed CPU prefixes.

This builds on [#37160](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37160), which
introduced `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` and its private per-replica CPU cache.
This PR extends that connector with opt-in cross-DP publication and lookup; it
does not change the native offloader's per-replica semantics.

## Configuration

Add `cpu_offload_shared`, a JSON boolean in `kv_connector_extra_config`,
defaulting to `false`. Set it to `true` to share completed CPU prefixes with
compatible DP replicas in the same IPC namespace and distributed DP group.
Leaving it unset retains the existing private CPU pools.

The CPU capacity remains a per-worker budget: `cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank`
reserves each worker's write partition. Corresponding local DP peers can read
published entries from one another's partitions, while writes remain owned by
the worker that allocates the slot. For example, two local DP peers configured
with 8 GiB each expose a 16 GiB node-local region for published slots and
metadata; this is shared visibility, not a dynamically rebalanced write pool.

Pass the following to `--kv-transfer-config`:

```json
{
  "kv_connector": "SimpleCPUOffloadConnector",
  "kv_role": "kv_both",
  "kv_connector_extra_config": {
    "cpu_offload_shared": true,
    "cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank": 8589934592,
    "lazy_offload": false
  }
}
```

Shared mode requires the CPU backend, eager offloading (`lazy_offload=false`),
prefix caching, compatible model/KV layouts and reproducible prefix hashes.
It supports fixed MoE DP groups and TP, with `PP=DCP=PCP=1` and no LoRA or
elastic EP. Each TP coordinate shares its own KV shard with corresponding
local DP peers. Cross-node transfer requires a network-capable connector or tier.

## Implementation

Use the existing `SharedOffloadRegion` type, as established for native
`CPUOffloadingSpec` storage by
[#50094](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50094), and the DMA/`BlockPool`
interfaces for storage and transfers; the cross-DP publication index, locking
and reader reference semantics are new code in this PR. Each writer owns a
fixed partition, and the shared pool does not dynamically move free write slots
between workers. Lookup and pinning use `flock` on the metadata region's descriptor;
prefixes are published after all worker stores complete, and reader references
prevent slot reuse until peer loads finish. The workers use the existing DMA
backend for transfers.

The rebased base also includes the upstream prefix-cacheable-group handling from
[#56810](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56810). This PR consumes that
group eligibility behavior and adds cross-DP publication; it does not duplicate
the upstream hybrid-model bug fix.

| Production file | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/simple_cpu_offload_connector.py` | Parse and validate `cpu_offload_shared`; connect worker and scheduler handshakes. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/shared_offload.py` (new) | Discover local DP peers, verify cache identity/layout, and allocate shared KV views per TP coordinate. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/shared_block_pool.py` (new) | Add shared hash publication, slot versions, locking and peer read references to `BlockPool`. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/metadata.py` | Define the worker-to-scheduler shared-pool handshake. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py` | Attach the shared pool and synchronize scheduler lookup, allocation and completion handling. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/worker.py` | Allocate/pin shared CPU views, expose the handshake and release mappings on shutdown. |

Tests and documentation changed:

- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py`
- `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py`
- `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py`
- `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`

## Why this is not a duplicate

The following open PRs address adjacent behavior, but none adds cross-DP CPU
prefix publication and peer loading for `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`:

- [#53073](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53073) targets shared mmap
  startup ownership and cleanup. This PR targets completed-prefix visibility
  and safe peer reads after asynchronous DMA. It follows the mmap lifetime
  rules but adds a different metadata publication and reader-lifetime protocol.
- [#53474](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53474) targets node-local
  sizing and worker placement for native `OffloadingConnector`. This PR targets
  node-local prefix reuse for `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, including one pool
  per TP coordinate. The connectors, allocation path and target behavior differ;
  this PR has no code dependency on #53474.
- [#47324](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47324) targets a GPU
  load/compute stream race inside one worker. This PR targets host-side slot
  ownership when another worker reads a completed prefix. It does not implement
  the open PR's load-path stream-ordering fix; the two changes are complementary,
  and this PR adds separate cross-worker reader references.
- [#57418](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57418) targets concurrent
  requests waiting for the same in-flight load inside one engine. This PR
  targets completed CPU prefixes shared by different DP engines; it does not
  change connector-side coalescing of simultaneous loads.
- [#43483](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43483) targets routing a
  request to the DP rank that already owns a GPU prefix. This PR targets actual
  CPU KV publication and peer loading when routing selects another replica;
  routing-only ownership hints cannot provide that transfer.
- [#57422](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57422) targets inode-safe
  unlinking of existing shared mmap files. This PR uses the existing mmap
  lifetime model but adds cross-DP prefix metadata and reader references.
- [#54743](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54743) targets which KV
  groups receive offload configuration. This PR keeps the existing group
  eligibility rules and adds sharing only for groups already handled by
  `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`.
- [#52921](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52921) targets aligning
  scheduler and worker pool sizes across PP/speculative workers. This PR keeps
  the existing per-worker capacity calculation and adds node-local sharing
  after those capacities agree.

## Validation

Validation was run on `b9b640c09dd7ace867f84077902567c5625cad06`, based on
upstream `3e2a7e74a556623ddee3a327299d7bf04055501e`.
The current branch commit `c7756cf854aad81a6adb5d4c749886c96fb5b3d4` rebases
that version onto upstream `dd30786fef8b15bd83205833c7b3348b0ba0ebc7`;
conflict resolutions and a type-checking adjustment are limited to tests,
leaving this PR's implementation patch unchanged.

On the rebased source, the focused scheduler, KV-event and connector suite passed
**135 tests** on the DGX Spark CUDA environment:

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_metrics.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py -q
```

The suite includes shared scheduler publication, reader pinning, delayed
publication, metadata mismatch rejection, non-prefix-cacheable groups and the
TP configuration acceptance test. Ruff and the applicable pre-commit checks pass.

The model validation used two DGX Spark hosts, each with one NVIDIA GB10
(SM121), CUDA 13.2, driver 580.173.02, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132 and
FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1. Because only two physical GPUs were available, the
model tests used a diagnostic topology with two logical workers per GPU. This
is functional evidence, not independent-GPU performance evidence; PyTorch
requires NCCL processes to have exclusive GPU access.

All TTFT and GSM8K results below use the TP2×DP2 topology described above.

For the TP2×DP2 diagnostic, the four logical workers were mapped as follows:

| Logical launch rank | DP | TP | Host | HTTP port |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| 0 | 0 | 0 | DGX Spark 1 | DP0 endpoint |
| 1 | 0 | 1 | DGX Spark 2 | Headless |
| 2 | 1 | 0 | DGX Spark 1 | DP1 endpoint |
| 3 | 1 | 1 | DGX Spark 2 | Headless |

The TP shard probe restored distinct TP0 and TP1 byte patterns through their
corresponding local DP groups and passed the all-shard publication barrier.
The full model run used DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, DSpark K5 probabilistic
sampling, CUDA graphs, Rust frontend, RoCE and 2 GiB CPU/GPU KV capacity per
worker.

### Experiment setup

Use the same source commit and model weights for both modes. The launch below
shows the TP2×DP2 settings used for the TP shard and recovery probe. Run one
process for each logical launch rank in the table above: ranks 0 and 2 on the
first host, and ranks 1 and 3 on the second. Here `--nnodes 4` counts four logical
launches across two physical hosts; the DP size is 2.

Set `MODEL` to the
[DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731)
weights, then set `NODE_RANK`, `DP_RANK`, `DP_PORT` and the coordinator ports and
address for the deployment. Use distinct HTTP ports for DP0 and DP1, one shared
DP RPC port, and one shared TP master port. Logical ranks 1 and 3 are headless.
The host-specific network environment is intentionally omitted.

```bash
KV_CONFIG='{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_offload_shared":true,"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":2147483648,"lazy_offload":false}}'

PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:False \
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve "$MODEL" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port "$DP_PORT" \
  --data-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-rank "$DP_RANK" \
  --data-parallel-external-lb \
  --data-parallel-address "$HEAD_IP" --data-parallel-rpc-port "$DP_RPC_PORT" \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --enable-ep-weight-filter \
  --nnodes 4 --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --master-addr "$HEAD_IP" --master-port "$TP_MASTER_PORT" \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --trust-remote-code --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.47 --kv-cache-memory-bytes 2147483648 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 64 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' \
  --enable-prefix-caching --prefix-caching-hash-algo sha256 \
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details --per-request-spec-decode-metrics detailed \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' \
  --kv-transfer-config "$KV_CONFIG"
```

Add `--headless` for logical ranks 1 and 3. For the private control, change only
`cpu_offload_shared` to `false`. Keep `expandable_segments:False` in both
connector runs because the upstream KV-connector guard rejects
`expandable_segments:True`.

External DP routing gives one configured endpoint port to DP0 and another to DP1
on the coordinator host; the TP followers are headless. Send case `i` to DP rank
`i % 2` for the cold phase and to `1 - (i % 2)` for the peer phase, preserving
the prompt and `cache_salt`. The port selects the replica; it is not part of the
prefix hash.
Between phases, wait for requests and stores to finish, then POST to
`/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true` on both endpoints for a cold run, or
`/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=false` to clear only GPU caches before peer
replay. Check that both resets succeed before issuing requests. Confirm reuse
with the external CPU-prefix counters.

### Offload correctness and latency

The GPU DMA tests and TP2 shard probe restored distinct TP0/TP1 byte patterns
after peer loads and withheld publication until all TP workers completed their
stores.

#### Performance improvement test

The rebased-source one-shot test used 24 unique approximately 6K-token prefixes,
one in-flight request per endpoint and streaming `max_tokens=1` requests. Each
prefix was populated on its owner, GPU caches were reset, and the prefix was
requested exactly once from its local DP peer.

| Mode | Peer TTFT p50 | Peer TTFT p95 | External transfer | Local compute |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Private | 9.17 s | 12.22 s | 0 / 140,652 | 140,652 |
| Shared | 4.91 s | 9.29 s | 129,024 / 140,652 | 11,628 |

Shared peer TTFT was 46.4% lower in this rebased-source diagnostic run. All 24
peer requests had zero errors, empty outputs, replacement characters,
invalid controls or cold/peer output mismatches. This is a diagnostic result;
the topology with two logical workers per GB10 is not a production throughput
setup.

### Accuracy validation

The rebased-source GSM8K evaluation used three fresh cold/peer pairs with the
same 200 five-shot questions, `temperature=0`, `seed=0`, concurrency 32 and a
512-token output limit:

| Configuration | Round 1 | Round 2 | Round 3 | Mean | Min–max | DSpark acceptance |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Private cold | 189 | 189 | 189 | 94.50% | 94.50–94.50% | 64.10% |
| Private peer | 191 | 189 | 190 | 95.00% | 94.50–95.50% | 64.20% |
| Shared cold | 188 | 189 | 189 | 94.33% | 94.00–94.50% | 63.94% |
| Shared peer | 190 | 190 | 189 | 94.83% | 94.50–95.00% | 64.60% |

All 2,400 requests completed without request errors, empty output, replacement
characters or invalid control characters. These repeated evaluations show normal
serving-workload variation and are not a statistical equivalence claim. The
TP2×DP2 recovery probe separately passed 8/8 cold and 8/8 peer requests in both
modes with token-exact output; private peer CPU hits were 0 and shared peer CPU
hits were 45,056 tokens. The independent TP-shard/publication probe also passed.

## AI assistance

The implementation and analysis were assisted with AI and reviewed by human.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix][Spec Decode] Add compact_topk_indices to the ROCm DSA MTP drafter
body:
## Purpose

On ROCm, MTP speculative decoding crashes for every GLM-5.2 / GLM-5.3 checkpoint on
current `main`, out of the box:

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 -tp 4 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

```
File "vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py", line 613, in propose
    self.model.model.compact_topk_indices(token_indices_to_sample)
AttributeError: 'DeepseekV32MultiTokenPredictor' object has no attribute
'compact_topk_indices'
```

The engine starts, and the first draft step fails on every TP worker.

### Cause

GLM-5.x checkpoints set `index_share_for_mtp_iteration: true`. With that set, the legacy
proposer checks the drafter for `set_skip_topk` and then calls both methods:

```python
if self._share_mtp_indices and hasattr(self.model.model, "set_skip_topk"):
    self.model.model.set_skip_topk(True)
    self.model.model.compact_topk_indices(token_indices_to_sample)
```

On ROCm, `deepseek_v32` and `glm_moe_dsa` are dispatched to
`vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd/` (#51915). That module's `DeepseekV32MultiTokenPredictor`
implements `set_skip_topk` but not `compact_topk_indices`, which #47238 added only to the
generic drafter in `deepseek_mtp.py`. It is the only drafter on `main` with one method and
not the other. The generic, NVIDIA DSA, GLM-5-Next, HY-V4 and both Qwen4-Exp drafters
have both.

### Change

- `amd/mtp.py`: add `compact_topk_indices` to `DeepseekV32MultiTokenPredictor`. It
  follows the amd drafter's own layout: `topk_indices_buffer` lives on `self_attn`
  itself, where `set_skip_topk` already looks for `skip_topk`, not under
  `self_attn.mla_attn`. Copying the generic method body would find no buffer. It would
  silently leave the buffer uncompacted, and steps 1+ would reuse the wrong rows instead
  of crashing.
- `llm_base_proposer.py`: decide index sharing once, after the draft model is loaded, and
  require both methods. This is what the V2 MTP speculator already does
  (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/mtp/speculator.py`). A future drafter with only
  `set_skip_topk` then falls back to not sharing instead of crashing.

Every other drafter on `main` has both methods, so their behaviour does not change. Until
this lands, `"index_share_for_mtp_iteration": false` in `--speculative-config` avoids the
crash on `main`.

### Affected checkpoints

Each checkpoint's real `config.json` was resolved through the draft-model registry on both
`main` and this branch. Each one then ran on ROCm with its architecture truncated and
dummy weights.

| checkpoint | `model_type` | drafter on ROCm | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.3 (fp8), GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8, GLM-5.2-FP8, GLM-5.2-MXFP4 | `glm_moe_dsa` | `deepseek_v32/amd/mtp.py` | `AttributeError` on the first draft step | runs, index sharing on |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 | `deepseek_v32` | `deepseek_v32/amd/mtp.py` | runs, no sharing (config does not ask) | same |
| GLM-5.3-Flash | `glm5_next` | V2 model runner's MTP speculator | runs | same — never reaches this proposer |

GLM-5.3-BF16 has the same config as GLM-5.3 and was not run separately. The other
first-tier checkpoints (DeepSeek-V4 line, Kimi, MiniMax, Qwen, gpt-oss, gemma-4, Llama)
have no DSA indexer or no MTP drafter, and they resolve identically on both trees.

Two open PRs touch the same file, and both are in different hunks: #55081 edits the
`DeepseekV32MTP` wrapper, and #53953 edits `DeepseekV32MultiTokenPredictorLayer`. Neither
adds this method.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/models/deepseek_v32/test_amd_mtp.py   # ROCm only; skipped elsewhere
```

The new tests build the amd predictor with real `topk_indices_buffer` tensors. They check
that `compact_topk_indices` gathers the requested rows to the front, leaves the rest
alone, covers every MTP layer, and compacts identically to the generic drafter given the
same buffer and slots.

End to end: GLM-5.3 (official fp8 weights), TP=4, `num_speculative_tokens=3`. The baseline
is `main` with `"index_share_for_mtp_iteration": false`, because that is the only way it
runs on `main`. It is compared against this PR with the checkpoint's own setting, using
GSM8K (`lm_eval`, 5-shot, all 1319 items) and `vllm bench serve` with a fresh server per
run.

## Test Result

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm, against `main@94f4170df3`.

### The crash is fixed

GLM-5.3 (official fp8 weights), TP=4: on `main`, the first draft step fails on all four TP
workers with the `AttributeError` above. The same happens for the other three
`glm_moe_dsa` checkpoints in the table. With this PR every one of them runs, with
`compact_topk_indices` and `set_skip_topk(True)` called on every draft step.

Each unit test was run against three trees, to show that the assertions discriminate
rather than merely pass:

| tree | result |
|---|---|
| `main` | 4 failed — the method does not exist |
| the generic drafter's body copied in (`self_attn.mla_attn` path) | 3 failed, 1 passed — the method exists but compacts nothing |
| this PR | 4 passed |

These were run from a directory outside the repository, with the imported module's
`__file__` checked for each tree.

### No accuracy or performance regression

GLM-5.3 (official fp8), TP=4, `num_speculative_tokens=3`, this PR against the `main`
workaround:

| | `main`, sharing off | this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| GSM8K strict-match | 0.9181 (repeat: 0.9196) | 0.9174 | within the base-repeat drift |
| Total tok/s | 2673.1 | 2676.5 | +0.1 % |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 63.79 | 64.04 | +0.4 % |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 369.6 | 370.5 | +0.2 % |

All three bench metrics are inside their own within-arm spread. On the drafter alone,
`propose()` time does not move beyond the spread between two identical baseline runs at
`num_speculative_tokens` 1, 2 and 3, for context up to 97k and batch up to 83. So index
sharing costs nothing measurable, and it gives no speedup either. Full tables and per-sample
GSM8K agreement are in the comment below.

---

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom); reviewed and measured by hand.

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Prevent SM90 sparse MLA planner work-list overflow
body:
## Overview

Prevent large SM90 sparse MLA steps from overflowing FlashInfer's planner work list by planning and running independent row chunks. Rebased on main with #58684 and #55222.

## Claims

- Bound query tiles by head count, leaving headroom for split-KV work.
- Apply each chunk's global row offset to the async KV-length clamp.
- Share one 128 MiB float workspace and write chunks into one output tensor.

## Validation

H20, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, base `6fa67afed999`:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py -v --tb=short
```

**33 passed, no skips.** Real-wrapper tests cover 16,600 rows, nonuniform contexts, FP8/NoPE, BF16/RoPE, and CUDA Graph replay with refreshed lengths and indices. Outputs match exact-planned references (`atol=rtol=1e-2`). Omitting the row offset makes both numerical cases fail. Planner-capacity tests also cover 64/65/128/384 heads and partial plans.

GLM-5.3-Flash FP8, H20 x8, TP8, FP8 KV, async scheduling, forced MQA, eager execution, and `max_num_batched_tokens=32768`: a 28,201-token prompt completed with finite logprobs; all eight ranks exercised four chunks. This smoke test used the preceding revision; the head-aware cap preserves its TP8 path. The final revision passed the complete suite above. This is not a task-accuracy or throughput benchmark.

Pre-commit passed. The existing H100 V1 Attention CI job collects this suite.

## Details

`MLAPlan` still has an unchecked 16,384-work allocation in FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1; the 65,536 limit is for another planner. The upstream fix is [flashinfer#5170](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5170), still absent from the pinned release.

Rows are independent (`causal=False`). The cap is `8192 // ceil(num_heads / 64)`, using the smallest query tile; GLM TP8 retains 8192-row chunks. Each chunk keeps its own integer plan and index buffers, so additional chunks still cost memory.

This fixes planner overflow, separate from the merged async/dtype fixes and #58892's backend-selection change. The optional strict GPU-sync diagnostic still reports FlashInfer's unpinned H2D staging on both unpatched main and this candidate; normal serving validation used the default setting.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4 chat template puts `tools` into a synthetic leading system message instead of on the existing system message (diverges from the reference encoder)
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Collected with `python -m vllm.collect_env` in the serving conda environment on a CPU dev box (the template rendering reported below does not involve a GPU; the same environment serves on 4x B300 with TP=4). OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 CMake version : version 3.31.6 Libc version : glibc-2.39 PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 Python version : 3.12.14 (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-5.10.25-nvidia-gpu-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 Is CUDA available : False (CPU dev box; serving nodes: 4x NVIDIA B300, driver from the same image) [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.18 [pip3] nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.29.7 [pip3] torch==2.13.0 [pip3] torchaudio==2.11.0 [pip3] torchvision==0.28.0 [pip3] transformers==5.12.1 [pip3] triton==3.7.1 [pip3] tokenspeed-triton==3.8.10.post20260906 vLLM Version : 0.28.0 vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled The same code path (vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py, apply_chat_template) is present in 0.24.1 builds we also run. ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary With `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4`, `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py` renders the request `tools` by inserting a **new** system message at index 0 that carries only `tools`, even when the conversation already starts with a `system` message. The DeepSeek reference encoder (`encoding/encoding_dsv4.py` shipped in the model repo, and its `test_encoding_dsv4.py`) attaches `tools` to the existing system message instead. As a result every tool-calling request served by vLLM renders as ``` [effort prefix] ## Tools ...tool schema block... ...to invoke tool calls. <｜User｜>... ``` whereas the reference renders ``` [effort prefix] ## Tools ...tool schema block... <｜User｜>... ``` Same tokens, different order: the tools block moves in front of the system prompt, and the system prompt ends up glued to the last line of the tools block with a single `\n` and immediately followed by `<｜User｜>`. The rendering is otherwise identical (same length, same tokens), so this is easy to miss. ## Environment - vLLM 0.28.0 (`vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py`, `apply_chat_template`); the same code is present in 0.24.x. - Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` (`--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice`). - Reference: `encoding/encoding_dsv4.py` and `encoding/test_encoding_dsv4.py` from the model repository. ## Reproduction ```python import copy, importlib.util from vllm.tokenizers.deepseek_v4 import DeepseekV4Tokenizer MODEL = "/path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash" # local checkout with encoding/encoding_dsv4.py spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("enc", f"{MODEL}/encoding/encoding_dsv4.py") enc = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(enc) tool = {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "bash", "description": "Execute a bash command", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"command": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["command"]}}} messages = [{"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."}, {"role": "user", "content": "List /tmp."}] tok = DeepseekV4Tokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL) served = tok.apply_chat_template(copy.deepcopy(messages), tools=[tool], enable_thinking=True, reasoning_effort="high", tokenize=False) ref_messages = copy.deepcopy(messages); ref_messages[0]["tools"] = [tool] # how the reference tests attach tools reference = enc.encode_messages(ref_messages, thinking_mode="thinking", reasoning_effort="high") print(len(served), len(reference)) # 1681 1681 print(served.find("## Tools"), served.find("You are a helpful assistant.")) # 499 1615 -> tools first print(reference.find("You are a helpful assistant."), reference.find("## Tools")) # 497 527 -> system first print(served == reference) # False ``` Served text around the system prompt: ``` ...defined tool name and parameter schemas to invoke tool calls.\nYou are a helpful assistant.<｜User｜>List /tmp. ``` Reference text around the system prompt: ``` ...no assumption is left unchecked.\n\nYou are a helpful assistant.\n\n## Tools\n\nYou have access to a set of tools... ``` ## Where it comes from `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py` (0.28.0, lines 37-41; identical in 0.24): ```python conversation = kwargs.get("conversation", messages) messages = conversation.copy() if tools is not None and len(tools) > 0: messages.insert(0, {"role": "system"}) messages[0]["tools"] = tools ``` The encoder renders a system message as `content + "\n\n" + render_tools(tools)` and puts no separator between two consecutive system messages, so the synthetic tools-only message becomes `"" + "\n\n## Tools ..."` followed directly by the caller's system text. The reference encoder's README states: "Tools are defined on the `system` or `developer` message via the `tools` field (OpenAI-compatible format)", and `test_encoding_dsv4.py` does `messages[0]["tools"] = td["tools"]` on the existing system message; its golden output `tests/test_output_1.txt` starts with `<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>You are a helpful assistant.\n\n## Tools`. ## Why it matters - Fine-tuning pipelines that pack data with the reference encoder put the tools block after the system prompt. Serving the same model through vLLM shows it the tools block before the system prompt on 100% of tool requests, a systematic train/serve prefix mismatch that no length or token-count check catches. - The caller's system prompt loses its blank-line separation on both sides (`...invoke tool calls.\nSYSTEM<｜User｜>`), which is not a layout the reference ever produces. - Anyone comparing vLLM prompts against the reference encoder (or against another serving stack) gets a mismatch that looks like a template bug elsewhere. ## Proposed fix In `apply_chat_template`, attach `tools` to the first message when it is a `system` (or `developer`) message without its own `tools`, and only insert a synthetic system message when the conversation has no leading system/developer message: ```python if tools: if messages and messages[0].get("role") in ("system", "developer") and not messages[0].get("tools"): messages[0] = {**messages[0], "tools": tools} else: messages.insert(0, {"role": "system", "tools": tools}) ``` Both the bundled `deepseek_v4_encoding.py` and the reference encoder already support `tools` on system/developer messages, so no encoder change is needed. If backward compatibility with the current layout is a concern, a `chat_template_kwargs` switch would let users pick, but the reference layout should be the default. ## Related (separate, smaller) - The DeepSeek-V4 tool parser keeps the trailing `\n\n` of visible text before a `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` block in `message.content`, and the encoder appends its own `\n\n` when re-rendering that history turn, so text-then-call turns round-trip with four newlines instead of two. - Tool messages whose `content` is a list of text parts are joined with `\n` by `chat_utils` (content_format="string") but with `\n\n` by the reference encoder. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep every multimodal feature in the partial-block KV event
body:
> **Rescoped after review.** This PR originally also changed `request_block_hasher` in `kv_cache_utils.py`. @sawsa307 pointed out that #51694 already covers that; I dropped that hunk and its tests, and this PR is now only the `block_pool.py` bug, using the same bisect helper #51694 uses.

## Purpose

`BlockPool.cache_partial_block` emits the `BlockStored` event that external KV cache consumers key on, and builds its `extra_keys` starting at the **last** multimodal feature:

```python
block_end = num_tokens
curr_mm_idx = -1 if block_start > 0 else 0
extra_keys, _ = generate_block_hash_extra_keys(
    request, block_start, block_end, curr_mm_idx
)
```

The event window is the last hash block of the partial block:

```python
# _get_partial_block_parent_hash_and_start
num_hash_blocks = num_tokens // self.hash_block_size
block_start = (num_hash_blocks - 1) * self.hash_block_size
```

and that window can reach into more than one feature — the tail of one plus the whole of a shorter next one. Starting at the last feature drops the others, so the event is published under a key that does not distinguish the dropped feature, and a consumer can hand one request the KV computed for another.

Reproduced through the real path, `hash_block_size=4`, `block_size=8`, `num_tokens=12`, features at `(offset=6, length=3)` and `(offset=10, length=2)`, so the event window is tokens `[8, 12)`:

```
emitted extra_keys : [(('B', 2),)]            # 'A' is missing
correct            : [(('A', -2), ('B', 2))]
```

## Changes

One site in `block_pool.py`: scan from the first feature that overlaps the window instead of from the last one, using `get_mm_features_in_window` — the same bisect over the sorted features that #51694 uses for the block hasher, so the two sites stay consistent.

## Test

`tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_partial_block_stored_event_keeps_every_mm_feature` builds a `BlockPool` with `enable_kv_cache_events=True`, calls `cache_partial_block` on a request whose partial block spans two features, and asserts the emitted event's extra keys.

On current `main`:

```
E   AssertionError: assert [(('B', 2),)] == [(('A', -2), ('B', 2))]
FAILED tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_partial_block_stored_event_keeps_every_mm_feature
```

With this PR:

```
$ pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
121 passed
```

`main` gives 120 passed on the same host; the 5 failures present in both runs are platform-gated cases unrelated to this change (`test_mla_with_incompatible_swa_uses_one_full_allocation_group`, `test_unidentifiable_draft_with_mamba_warns`, `test_non_mtp_eagle_hybrid_still_warns[eagle|eagle3|dspark]`) — this is a CPU-only machine. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both changed files.

## How this was found

By asserting an invariant that was not covered — a block's cache key must not depend on when it was computed, and changing one multimodal input must change every key that covers it — and fuzzing it. The same fuzz is what surfaced the hasher-side problem that #51694 fixes.

---

*AI assistance disclosure, per [contributing/README.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/contributing/README.md#ai-assisted-contributions): prepared with Claude Code. Every changed line was reviewed, the failure was reproduced through the real `cache_partial_block` path on current `main`, and the test was run with and without the fix. Commit carries `Co-authored-by: Claude`.*

title: [Feature][KVConnector][DSv4.1] Encoder-only prefill with NIXL P/D
body:
## Purpose

Implement encoder-only Prefill for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D serving with the direct `NixlConnector` pull path. This follows the full-prompt, cache-hit-replay design in RFC #57738 and builds on the asymmetric P/D direction in RFC #57383: P runs L0-L19 for the whole prompt and produces L20 Main KV/Indexer K, while D reconstructs the adopted replay tail through the full target and samples the first token.

This PR makes the NIXL handoff concrete without depending on the Mooncake implementation in #57872. Both connector paths share the same execution boundary, but their request and transfer protocols differ. P still loads the full target weights in this first change; weight omission is separate work.

I'll validate this PR on real GPU soon and check whether it is better to forward NIXL version before Mooncake.

## Implementation

- Add opt-in `KVTransferConfig.dsv41_encoder_only_prefill` for dedicated `NixlConnector` producer and consumer roles. Restrict this PR to the existing pull connector.
- On P, run L0-L19 normally, execute the L20 pre-mix and canonical compressor/Main-KV/Indexer-K writes, and skip L20 attention/FFN, L21-L39, final norm, LM head, sampling, and draft work.
- Finish a cache-only P request after its full prompt is consumed without generating a token. Each P worker synchronizes its cache writes before completion. The NIXL proxy marks the P request `cache_only=true`, then forwards the remote block/engine metadata returned in P's zero-token response to D for a normal NIXL pull.
- Select transferable groups from V4.1's Main-KV and Indexer-K owner layers. Missing, duplicate, or mixed global/local groups fail closed. Target SWA, compressor continuation, and draft groups stay D-local; D uses the existing bounded-replay path.
- For same-layout, non-DCP pulls, align producer blocks to the range D actually adopts after bounded replay. Use D's per-group local prefix counts to distinguish cached prefix blocks from a discarded partial P tail block; reject mismatched block geometry.
- Limit the initial configuration to NVIDIA, MRV2, PP=1, no PCP or microbatching, a 128-token bounded-replay window and the 40-layer/L20 source topology, text-only requests, and no prompt logprobs. P requires `--no-async-scheduling`; neither role enables speculative decoding in this first path. NIXL's compatibility hash includes drafter settings, so an asymmetric P-without-drafter/D-with-DSpark pair needs separate support.

Enable the option on both server roles:

```json
{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","dsv41_encoder_only_prefill":true}
{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","dsv41_encoder_only_prefill":true}
```

Use the NIXL toy proxy with the dedicated P and D instances. Conventional NIXL requests ignore the proxy's `cache_only` marker when the option is off.

## Validation

## Relationship to other work

RFC #57738 analyzes NIXL pull as its initial path. #57872 implements the same V4.1 execution boundary for direct Mooncake P/D and has separate H20 measurements; it does not validate NIXL. This PR does not bring Mooncake's generic empty-pull completion change into NIXL. NIXL already tracks whether D awaits KV for a real transfer. #56227 provides the bounded-replay foundation used on D.

Open PRs were checked by RFC number and by NIXL/encoder-only/V4.1 keywords. No other open PR implements this boundary on the direct NIXL pull path. The model-side execution code currently overlaps #57872; I am happy to rebase or stack the shared part if maintainers choose a common base, while keeping connector-specific handoff and tests reviewable.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, validation, and drafting. The human submitter will review every changed line, run target-GPU P/D and model evaluation, and defend the change before marking this PR Ready.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## 🐛 Describe the bug Multi-node TP=8 (2 nodes × 4 H200) serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash hangs indefinitely during engine startup, inside `ncclCommInitRank` graph/connection phase — before weight loading begins. The hang is deterministic and reproducible across 8+ restarts with different NCCL env configurations. Launch commands (per official multiprocessing multi-node docs) Head node: ```bash vllm serve /.cache/deepseek-v41-flash \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --enable-chunked-prefill \ --nnodes 2 --node-rank 0 \ --master-addr \ --trust-remote-code --disable-custom-all-reduce ``` Worker node: same + `--headless --node-rank 1`. Observed behavior (NCCL_DEBUG=TRACE) Both nodes bootstrap fine (TCP bootstrap OK, `commId` shared, 2 nodes detected). Then, with IB enabled: Even local_ranks (0, 2 / 4, 6) complete `Init COMPLETE`, log their `Trees`, and establish cross-node GDRDMA channels: `Channel 00/0 : 0[0] -> 4[0] [send] via NET/IB/4/GDRDMA`, `Channel 01/0 : 2[2] -> 6[2] [send] via NET/IB/5/GDRDMA` Odd local_ranks (1, 3 / 5, 7) stop after `comm 0x... rank N nRanks 8 nNodes 2 localRanks 4 localRank N MNNVL 0` + one `Trees` line — no Channel lines, no Init COMPLETE, indefinitely The APIServer loops forever on: `Waiting for 1 local, 0 remote core engine proc(s) to start.` Weight loading (`Loading safetensors`) never starts All worker threads sleep (futex / socket / ib_uverbs_event_read) — no spinning, no watchdog timeout, no error With `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` (Socket transport): the same hang, but now all 8 ranks block at the `MNNVL 0` boundary with zero Channel lines. The even/odd localRank asymmetry (the most distinctive part) On both nodes, exactly cudaDev 0 and cudaDev 2 (even local_ranks) complete init and own the cross-node GDRDMA channel pairs (0↔4 on one rail, 2↔6 on another). Odd local_ranks never establish their cross-node connections (1↔5, 3↔7). The pattern is stable across restarts and independent of: Variable tested Result `NCCL_IB_QPS_PER_CONNECTION=8` vs default ❌ no change `NCCL_CROSS_NIC=0` vs `1` ❌ no change `NCCL_NCHANNELS_PER_NET_PEER=4` vs `8` vs unset ❌ no change (worse: all ranks block) `NCCL_MAX/MIN_NCHANNELS=16/8` vs unset ❌ no change `NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL=SYS` + `NCCL_NET_GDR_READ=1` vs unset ❌ no change `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` (Socket transport) ❌ all 8 ranks block (earlier) `--disable-custom-all-reduce` ❌ no change Worker `--headless` (was missing initially — fixed) ❌ no change to the even/odd pattern env propagation ✅ verified — every NCCL_* var logged as "set by environment" on both nodes Ruled out TCP connectivity: bootstrap + `distributed_init_method=tcp://...:29501` reachable from both nodes (tested live) `/dev/shm`, UID, permissions: identical on both nodes GPU-NIC topology: NV6 intra-node, NICs PIX-adjacent to their NUMA-local GPUs, GDR works (GDRDMA channels DO form for even ranks) Env propagation: NCCL TRACE confirms every var read on both nodes Same model + same topology works on SGLang (NCCL 2.28.3) with identical k8s/network setup — 4 rails, GDRDMA, TP8/EP8 Hypothesis The rank-pair channel assignment during `ncclCommInitRank` graph-connect deadlocks when ranks need to establish cross-node QP connections in an order that requires the odd-rank pair's initiator to be a rank that is itself still initializing. ## Additional context Related: #53894 (DeepSeek-V4-Pro 2-node hang — `--disable-custom-all-reduce` fixed their case, not ours), #46097 (MiniMax multi-node collective deadlock — "ranks not in the same collective instance" hypothesis), #57423 (FlashInfer autotune rank-0-only cache — ours hangs earlier, at comm init) ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix] Attach DeepSeek-V4 request tools to existing system/developer messages
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58280.

DeepSeek-V4 still put request-level `tools` on a synthetic leading system message whenever the conversation started with a **developer** prompt. That renders `## Tools` *before* the instructions, so serving diverges from the reference encoder (`{content}\n\n## Tools`) and from how the same data is packed at train time.

`#51856` already attaches tools to an existing **system** message. This extends that to **developer** as well: attach to the first `system`/`developer` message, and only insert a synthetic system message when neither is present.

Not a duplicate of `#52255` (stale, needs-rebase; would redo the already-landed system case). Smaller nits in the issue (tool-parser newlines, tool-message join) are left alone.

AI assistance was used to implement and test this change. A human reviewed the diff.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py -v
```

## Test Result

`tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py`: **45 passed**.

That includes the existing system-message / golden fixture cases plus the new checks:

- `test_deepseek_v4_request_tools_follow_system_prompt_golden_layout` (`You are a helpful assistant.\n\n## Tools`)
- `test_deepseek_v4_attaches_request_tools_to_existing_developer_message`

No model-eval change: this only reorders the tools block onto an existing developer/system message.

title: [Bugfix] DeepSeek-V4 parser: drop the content/tool separator so parsed turns re-render byte-identically
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4's chat template renders an assistant turn that carries visible text and a tool call as `{content}\n\n<｜DSML｜tool_calls>...` (`deepseek_v4_encoding.py`, `tc_content += '\n\n' + tool_calls_template...`), and the reference parser shipped with the model treats that `\n\n` as part of the tool-call opener (`tool_calls_start_token = "\n\n<｜DSML｜tool_calls"` in the model repo's `encoding_dsv4.py`), so the parsed `content` never contains it.

vLLM's `DeepSeekV4Parser` runs with `strip_content_whitespace_with_tools=False` and cuts content at `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>`, so the client receives `"Let me check.\n\n"` as `message.content`. When the client echoes that turn back as history (every agent loop does), the encoder appends its own `\n\n`, and the turn re-renders as `Let me check.\n\n\n\n<｜DSML｜tool_calls>`: four newlines where the model generated two. Every text-then-tool-call turn in a multi-turn agent conversation therefore drifts from the bytes the model produced.

This PR adds an opt-in `content_tool_separator` to `ParserEngineConfig` and sets it to `"\n\n"` for DeepSeek-V4 (V4.1 inherits the config):

- Non-streaming: exactly one trailing separator is removed from `content` when a tool call follows. Nothing else changes (`"text\n"` stays `"text\n"`, `"text\n\n\n"` becomes `"text\n"`, content without a tool call keeps its trailing whitespace).
- Streaming: a trailing (partial) separator is withheld until the engine knows whether a tool block follows; it is dropped when one does and released unchanged when more text arrives or the turn ends without a tool call (`finish_streaming`).

`strip_content_whitespace_with_tools=True` parsers are unaffected (the separator strip runs before their `.strip()`); parsers that do not set the option are unaffected.

Related: #58280 (this PR addresses the first item under "Related" in that issue; the issue's main point, tools placement, is already handled on `main` by the `Match the Rust renderer` change in `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py`).

## Test Plan

New tests in `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py::TestContentToolSeparator`:

- non-streaming `extract_tool_calls` / `parse`: exactly one `\n\n` dropped; `\n` and no-separator inputs untouched; no tool call keeps trailing newlines
- streaming: separator in one chunk, split across chunks (`"\n"`,`"\n"`), attached to the opener chunk, and whole turn in one chunk; separator released when text continues or at `finish_streaming`
- round trip: render a history turn with the bundled encoder, take the assistant segment as the model output, parse it, echo the parsed message back, and assert the re-rendered prompt is byte-identical

```
pytest tests/parser -q --ignore=tests/parser/cohere
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv3_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv31_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py tests/reasoning/test_deepseekv3_reasoning_parser.py -q
```

## Test Result

Run on a CPU box against this branch with the nightly wheel's compiled extensions:

```
tests/parser -q --ignore=tests/parser/cohere        4333 passed (includes the 12 new TestContentToolSeparator cases)
tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py    12 passed
```

`tests/parser/cohere` and `tests/parser/mistral` need tokenizers/deps the box cannot fetch, so they were not run locally; CI covers them.

Before this change the new `test_non_streaming_drops_exactly_one_separator[Let me check.\n\n-Let me check.]`, the streaming cases and the round-trip test fail (content is `"Let me check.\n\n"` and the re-rendered prompt has four newlines); after it they pass and the existing tests are unchanged.

title: [Bugfix] DeepSeek-V4 renderer: join tool-result text parts with a blank line like the encoder
body:
## Purpose

Clients such as Claude Code / Cursor send tool results as OpenAI content parts (`[{"type": "text", "text": "..."}, ...]`). `chat_utils._parse_chat_message_content` flattens those parts with a single `"\n"` before the chat template runs, because most templates only accept string content for `tool` messages. The DeepSeek-V4 encoder, however, joins text parts of a tool result with a blank line (`"\n\n".join(text_parts)` in `deepseek_v4_encoding.render_message`), so through vLLM the `<tool_result>` block differs from what the reference encoder renders for the same request.

This PR pre-joins list-of-text `tool` results with `"\n\n"` in `DeepseekV4Renderer` (sync and async paths) before `parse_chat_messages`, so the encoder receives the string it would have produced itself. String content is untouched, and tool results that contain non-text parts (e.g. `tool_reference`) keep the structured list exactly as before.

Related: #58280 (this PR addresses the second item under "Related" in that issue; the issue's main point, tools placement, is already handled on `main` by the `Match the Rust renderer` change in `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py`).

## Test Plan

New `tests/renderers/test_deepseek_v4.py`:

- `_join_tool_text_parts`: text parts join with a blank line, string content untouched, non-text parts left structured, input not mutated
- `render_messages` / `render_messages_async` with a stub tokenizer: the conversation handed to `apply_chat_template` carries `"line 1\n\nline 2"`

```
pytest tests/renderers/test_deepseek_v4.py tests/renderers/test_kimi_k3.py -q
```

## Test Result

Run on a CPU box against this branch:

```
tests/renderers/test_deepseek_v4.py tests/renderers/test_kimi_k3.py    28 passed
```

title: [Perf][SM120][MLA] Use compact FP8 KV rows for NoPE models
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to merged #55277: use compact 528-byte `fp8_ds_mla` rows for native NoPE on the FlashInfer SM120 backend. Rebased onto upstream main `e6674262f1`. Only tests conflicted: #55528 made the MLA KV-spec test's fake layer carry `attn_backend`, and the HiSparse test helper gained `max_union_rows`; both were resolved by keeping both sides. The two commits are now `aab1e922fa` and `e879b2ef44` (head), and the branch merges cleanly into current main.

The row contains 512 FP8 latent bytes and four FP32 group scales. There is no RoPE payload. A single backend-owned row-size method supplies both the KV spec and early HiSparse registration. On SM120, compact selection depends solely on `kv_lora_rank=512` and `qk_rope_head_dim=0`, independent of model name, connector, or offloading configuration. Other backend layouts are unchanged; real RoPE64 `fp8_ds_mla` retains 656-byte rows. No new dtype or CLI option is added.

The writer accepts NoPE 528/656, preserves legacy zero-tail behavior for 656, and rejects RoPE64 with 528. It distinguishes logical row width from physical stride. The fixed 576-dimensional gather rejects compact input. HiSparse uses actual row widths for byte movement and rejects incompatible shared-staging layouts.

No connector changes, layout negotiation, or old-cache migration are added. Local prefix caching remains supported. External connectors were not tested end to end.

Duplicate-work check: #53969/#55778/#55543 use padded compatibility layouts; #55219/#57169 address broader paging/stride plumbing, not this compact writer/spec change. The community B12X GLM_NEXT path already uses the same 528-byte encoding; that is a useful precedent, not the FlashInfer backend wiring implemented here. Reference: local-inference-lab/vllm `cff8aebfeb73de96c97b4c5a0550c5a49f27451c`, `b12x_mla_sparse.py`. FlashInfer compact-row support was merged in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5075.

## Test Plan

Validation used 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell for official NVIDIA GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4, TP4, BF16, no speculation, text-only, context 65536, max sequences 32, batched tokens 4096, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs. FlashInfer source: `dc04f50c9aa3eabcdaa5feb0934edb3d85e9529a`.

Commands below are shown without local environment wrappers, not as verbatim execution transcripts. Paths are relative to the vLLM checkout unless noted. The following checks were rerun after the rebase onto main:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py \
  -k concat_and_cache_ds_mla -q -rs
python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_cp_gather_fp8.py -q
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py::test_mla_kv_cache_spec_uses_layer_cache_dtype \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_hisparse_index_group_preserves_row_width \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_hisparse_shared_staging_requires_uniform_row_width \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_hisparse_swap_in_preserves_rows_across_eviction \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_hisparse_gather_prefill_cache_prefers_resident_rows
prek run --from-ref c843f0cab78b413f2b0a5c2282cb71e3a3937b11 --to-ref bea90f7efee
```

Earlier validation from the FlashInfer checkout, not rerun after the rebase:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/attention/test_sparse_mla_sm120.py \
  -k glm53_nope_compact_rows -q
```

Model validation preceded gate removal and was not rerun after the rebase. It used GSM8K and random-8k1k workloads with `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` explicitly selected. As in #55277, successful runs used the disclosed distributed-autotune workaround:

```text
VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_SKIP_OPS=fp4_gemm,trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1,trtllm::fused_moe::gemm2
```

This PR does not fix that separate autotune issue or the noncanonical-layout calibration restriction. FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, pinned in upstream vLLM, is not the dependency used for this validation.

## Test Result

### Revalidation after the rebase onto `e6674262f1` (head `e879b2ef44`)

Run on 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell with FlashInfer built from main (includes flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5075) and vLLM's CUDA extension rebuilt from a tree containing this branch:

- CUDA writer (`test_cache.py -k concat_and_cache_ds_mla`): **9 passed, 3 skipped**. Fixed-layout gather (`test_cp_gather_fp8.py`): **18 passed**. KV-spec tests (`test_mla_backends.py -k kv_cache_spec`): **10 passed**.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py`: **119 passed**, 7 failed. All 7 fail identically on `e6674262f1` without this PR: `test_sparse_backend_prefill_correctness[*-auto-masked_mha*]` for deepseek_hd192_v128, glm5_hd256_v256 and glm53_flash_nope_hd256_v256, and `test_hisparse_speculative_rows_resolve_host_misses_consistently[long_mtp]`.

| | Without this PR (656-byte rows) | With this PR (528-byte rows) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Engine-reported KV tokens | 3,234,669 | 3,972,729 (**+22.8%**) |
| GSM8K (chat, flexible-extract) | 0.973 | 0.972 |

Both evaluations ran on the same integration tree with unrelated changes for other models; one run each.

### Earlier results (before this rebase)

At head `bea90f7efee`:

- Selected spec and HiSparse width/guard/data-path tests: **31 passed, no skips**. Includes uint8 528/656 host miss, hit, eviction/reload, and prefill byte gather. No claim of a complete model-level HiSparse deployment or external-connector end-to-end test.
- CUDA writer: **9 passed, 3 existing unsupported-geometry/input-size skips**. Includes compact/padded rows, row/page gaps, invalid slots, and legacy payload parity.
- Fixed-layout gather regression: **18 passed**.
- All applicable `prek` hooks passed across **all 10 changed files**, including Ruff, formatting, and mypy.

Earlier validation, not rerun after the rebase:

- FlashInfer compact/padded/sliced cache attention parity and CUDA graph replay: 3 passed (before gate removal).
- Broader `test_mla_backends.py` attempt stopped after 53 passes at an SM100 CUTLASS-only operator unavailable in this SM90/SM120 build. The complete cross-architecture suite was not qualified.
- GSM8K strict match, #55277 parent → compact: **1223/1319 (92.72%) → 1228/1319 (93.10%)**, concurrency 32, max output 2048. The compact evaluation gate passed; +5 samples is not evidence of a meaningful accuracy gain. Its recipe initially failed the immediate cleanup check; a subsequent managed stop verified all allocated devices freed.
- Random 8K/1K: **both runs completed 252/252 requests with zero failures**, with 4 × concurrency requests per level. Matrix server cleanup verified.

### KV-cache capacity

Compared with #55277 on the same hardware and serving configuration:

| Metric | #55277 | Compact |
|---|---:|---:|
| Encoded bytes per KV row | 656 | 528 (**−19.51%**) |
| Engine-reported KV token capacity | 4,301,231 | 5,282,546 (**+22.81%**) |
| Available KV-cache memory | 40.57 GiB | 40.57 GiB |

The benefit is more KV capacity within the same memory budget, not a throughput claim or a 19.51% reduction in total GPU allocation. Capacity is engine-reported, not saturation-tested; the validation runs used dirty source trees with differing build metadata.

title: [Bugfix][Engram] Reject offloaded tables larger than host memory
body:
## Purpose

With `cpu_offload=True` (the default), each rank pins its shard of the Engram tables in host memory (`torch.empty(..., device="cpu", pin_memory=True)`). Nothing checks that the node can hold them before allocating. The per-rank view is also misleading: all TP ranks of an engine pin their shards inside the same container, so the node needs the **whole** table.

On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`engram_num_embeddings=[384006168, 384016682]`, `head_dim=256`) the tables come to 188.8 GiB. At TP8 each rank asks for only 23.6 GiB, which looks fine against, say, a 55 GiB pod limit. Once all eight ranks allocate, the container is OOM-killed during worker init with no hint about the cause or the fix.

This adds `EngramConfig.verify_host_memory()`, next to the existing `verify_*` methods, and calls it from `DeepseekV4Model` right after the `/dev/shm` sharing decision (a fallback from `/dev/shm` is exactly what puts the tables on the per-rank pinned path). The check:

- computes what **this node** pins: a full table per local DP replica, or the local share when `embedding_across_dp` shards one table over DP;
- raises only when that exceeds a hard limit (the cgroup limit, or physical RAM when that is lower or there is no cgroup). Pinned memory cannot be reclaimed or swapped, so such a request can never succeed. The error gives the size and suggests `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload": false}'`;
- otherwise hands off to the existing `check_cgroup_memory_available`, which only warns, because current usage may be reclaimable.

It skips GPU-resident tables and `dp_shared_memory`, since `can_share_engram_tables` already checks `/dev/shm` for the latter. It also moves the table-size formula into `engram_table_bytes()` so the `/dev/shm` check and this one share it.

It assumes an engine's TP ranks share one node, which is how Engram is deployed today.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/config/test_engram_host_memory.py
ruff check / ruff format --check on the changed files
```

The tests fake cgroup and physical limits. They cover: the whole table is rejected even though one TP8 shard fits; physical RAM is used without a cgroup; the tighter of the two limits applies; a table that fits goes to the soft check; each local DP replica pins a full table; `embedding_across_dp` pins only the local share; nothing is checked for GPU-resident or `/dev/shm`-backed tables.

## Test Result

- `8 passed` on `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0` with the changed config module overlaid.
- As a control, a mutant that checks only one rank's shard (the per-rank view) fails 5 of 8.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`: clean.
- Context: we hit this on 8× RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120) serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP8 under a 55 GiB pod limit, and currently run with `cpu_offload: false`.

AI assistance was used to write this patch and its tests. The tests above were run as described.

title: [Rust Frontend] Accept custom chat roles for HF templates
body:
## Purpose

The Python Chat Completions API accepts roles outside the OpenAI set and passes them through to chat templates (`CustomChatCompletionMessageParam`, since #4758). The Rust frontend's HTTP `ChatMessage` is a closed enum tagged by `role`, so the same request fails with HTTP 400 before rendering.

Some public templates depend on this. The `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` chat template maps a leading `root` message to its high-priority system prompt, replacing the default model identity text, while `system` / `developer` go to the lower-priority developer prompt. Under the Rust frontend, callers that override the identity with `root` are rejected.

Changes:

- **HTTP DTO:** add `ChatMessage::Custom { role, content }`. The serde derive now uses `remote = "Self"` and covers only the standard roles; hand-written `Serialize` / `Deserialize` impls dispatch on the role tag. Standard roles go through the derived impl unchanged, and any other string role becomes `Custom`. A `#[serde(untagged)]` fallback variant was rejected: serde falls back to it whenever the tagged variant fails, so a malformed standard message (e.g. a `tool` message without `tool_call_id`) would be silently accepted as a custom role, and field errors would be replaced by the generic untagged-enum error.
- **`vllm-chat`:** add `ChatMessage::Custom`, `ChatRole::Custom(String)`, and `ChatMessage::custom()`. The HF renderer passes the role string to templates unchanged (`TemplateMessage` now borrows its role). Media in custom-role content is collected like other content-bearing roles.
- **Native renderers** (DeepSeek V3.2 / V4 / V4.1, Harmony, Inkling, Kimi K3) reject custom roles with a new `Error::UnsupportedChatRole`, classified as a request validation error (HTTP 400) rather than an internal template error.
- `name` on custom-role messages is dropped, consistent with how the Rust frontend treats `name` on the other roles (Python forwards it to the template).

Duplicate check: searched open PRs for custom / `root` chat roles in the Rust frontend; none found.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change and description.

## Test Plan

```bash
cd rust
cargo nextest run -p vllm-server -p vllm-chat
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all --check
```

New tests:

- `prepare_chat_request_accepts_custom_role_messages`: a `root` message in the request JSON lowers to `ChatMessage::custom("root", ..)`.
- `chat_http_message_keeps_standard_role_errors`: a `tool` message without `tool_call_id` still fails with `missing field \`tool_call_id\``.
- `chat_template_passes_custom_roles_unchanged`: the HF template sees `root` / `system` / `user` roles as sent.
- `custom_roles_are_rejected_as_request_errors`: the DeepSeek V4 renderer rejects a custom role with a request validation error.

Manual parity check against the public `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` template (revision `f0e1c1e04d`, metadata files only): start `vllm-rs render` on the snapshot, send `[root, system, user]` with `chat_template_kwargs={"thinking_mode": "disabled"}` to `/v1/chat/completions/render`, and compare the token IDs with `transformers` `apply_chat_template(..., add_generation_prompt=True)` followed by `encode(..., add_special_tokens=False)`.

## Test Result

- `cargo nextest run -p vllm-server -p vllm-chat`: 801 passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- Parity check: Rust and `transformers` 5.17.0 produce identical token IDs (126 tokens). The `root` content replaces the default identity in the system prompt, and the `system` message renders in the developer prompt.
- Error behavior on the render server: `{"role":"tool","content":"x"}` returns 400 `messages[0]: missing field \`tool_call_id\``; `{"role":"root"}` returns 400 `messages[0]: missing field \`content\``.

No model evaluation: the change affects prompt rendering only for requests that were previously rejected; standard-role deserialization and rendering are unchanged.
