title: [Bugfix][Attention] Resolve kernel block sizes per attention group
body:
## Purpose

`prepare_kernel_block_sizes` picks the kernel block size of each KV cache group from `backend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()`. That is a class-level query, and `FlashAttentionBackend` answers it from the model-wide `ModelConfig` head size: on SM100/SM110 with head size 256 it advertises only the FA4 hd256 page, `[128]`. An attention group whose layers do not share the model-wide shapes, in practice a spec-decode drafter (DFlash, EAGLE-3, DSpark, MTP) with a different head size, therefore gets the target's constraint instead of its own.

This hard-fails whenever the KV manager block is not a multiple of 128 and the target itself does not need it to be. e.g. for hybrid Mamba/GDN target with head size 256: its block is aligned to the Mamba page, its full-attention layers run on FlashInfer, which accepts that block, and a FlashAttention drafter with a smaller head size is then held to a 128-token page that does not divide it. 

Example: Qwen3.8-27B (GDN hybrid, head size 256, block aligned to 832) + `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (head size 128) on GB200:

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7}'
...
ValueError: No common block size for 832.
```

`--block-size 896` works around it. #58207 notes the same failure for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash on B300 (`No common block size for 592`).

## Fix

resolve kernel block sizes per attention group, from that group's KV cache spec.

- `AttentionBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes_for_spec(kv_cache_spec)`, defaulting to the model-wide answer, so other backends are unaffected.
- `FlashAttentionBackend` resolves the hd256 page from the spec's `head_size`, which is what its metadata builder already does when it decides `fa4_hd256` for a group. The model-wide `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()` / `get_preferred_block_size()` are unchanged.
- `select_common_block_size` takes optional per-backend specs; `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` passes each attention group's spec. Other callers (NIXL/Mooncake connectors, HiSparse) are unchanged.

Only groups whose head size differs from the model-wide one change. A smaller-head drafter behind a head-size-256 target is no longer held to the 128-token page (the failing case above). Conversely, a head-size-256 group behind a smaller-head target now advertises the 128-token page like a head-size-256 target does, instead of silently running FA2 when the block is not a multiple of 128.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py -k fa4_hd256_block_size_advertisement
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -k select_common_block_size
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -k "kernel_block_size or hisparse_block_size or preserve_global"
```

E2E on 1x GB200 (SM100): Qwen3.8-27B (bf16) + `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, `num_speculative_tokens=7`, no `--block-size`, before and after.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 6 + 6 + 9 passed (new: `test_fa4_hd256_block_size_advertisement_per_spec`, `test_select_common_block_size_resolves_sizes_per_spec`).

E2E, after (this branch, no `--block-size`): server starts with the same 832-token manager block (`Setting attention block size to 832 tokens ...`), both CUDA-graph captures complete, GPU KV cache 603,130 tokens (575,953 with the `--block-size 896` workaround). Closed-loop bench, ISL 1 / OSL 1024, concurrency 1, 8 requests, acceptance length pinned to 3: TPOT 4.52 ms, 218 output tok/s, similar to the performance with the workaround.

---

Code written with AI assistance (Claude); reviewed, tested and validated end to end by the author.

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Add Humming to the W4A8 (INT4xFP8) MoE oracle
body:
## Purpose

Fix compressed-tensors INT4/FP8 MoE checkpoints being routed to the CPU-only INT8 method on Blackwell. Add Humming to the W4A8 oracle, check quantization types during dispatch, and retain CUTLASS on SM90. Both backends use the same runtime weight names; Humming reuses the existing layer-based helpers.

Duplicate checks found no existing PR for this dispatch fix: #53848 handles a separate static-FP8 checkpoint format, #53880 covers MXFP4/block-FP8, and #58326 covers INT4/INT8.

## Test Plan

End-to-end evaluation of the full `gpustack/GLM-5.3-W4A8` checkpoint on 4× NVIDIA B300 with TP=4, expert parallelism, and automatic Humming selection:

```bash
chg run -g=4 -- vllm serve gpustack/GLM-5.3-W4A8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser glm47

.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000
```

## Test Result

GSM8K, 1,319 questions, 5-shot:

```text
Accuracy:                 0.911
Invalid responses:        0.000
Total latency:            119.744 s
Questions per second:     11.015
Total output tokens:      126251
Output tokens per second: 1054.342
```

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Keep prefill batches off varlen FULL decode graphs
body:
With adaptive verification, MRV2 captures variable-length FULL decode graphs that match on max_query_len alone (uniform_token_count unset). A batch containing prefilling requests of <= K+1 tokens (a fresh short prompt, a small prompt chunk, or a padded one-token prompt tail) was therefore dispatched to a FULL decode graph.

For Kimi-K3's KDA layers, the only recurrent-state backend that allows adaptive verification, the metadata builder takes its prefill path for such rows and skips the persistent-buffer staging the captured decode graph relies on. The prompt's recurrent state is never written and the batch's decode rows read stale state indices (the #50532 mechanism).

Offer no max_query_len bound when the batch has a prefill, so varlen FULL graphs are not eligible. DP ranks already treat a missing bound as None across all ranks.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve DeepSeek's unclosed final tool parameter
body:
## Purpose

Addresses the DeepSeek V4, V3.2, and V4.1 part of #57827. When a tool call ends without closing its final DSML parameter tag, final conversion drops that parameter. An unfinished `string="false"` value can also be dropped when it is not yet valid JSON.

This change preserves the trailing parameter in final conversion. During streaming, it defers invalid partial JSON until its type is stable, so later chunks cannot invalidate arguments already sent to the client.

Adds regression tests for streaming and non-streaming calls with string, numeric, and invalid JSON values.

Together, this PR, #58349 (MiniMax M2), and #58418 (GLM-4.7 MoE) cover all three parser cases reported in #57827. The issue should be closed once all three PRs have merged. This PR is distinct from #57707, which fixes Qwen3, and #53739, which changes the shared streaming engine.

AI assistance was used to develop this change.

## Test Plan

Run the DeepSeek parser suites:

`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/parser/engine tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v32.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py -q`

Run the repository's pre-commit hooks on the four changed files.

## Test Result

- 148 DeepSeek parser tests passed. The run emitted 14 Torch JIT deprecation warnings.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed when run directly on the staged files.
- No model inference evaluation was run. This is deterministic post-generation parsing, covered by CPU-only parser tests.

title: [Qwen4Exp] Checkpoint-mapped PLE storage for unified-memory GPUs (DGX Spark)
body:
## Purpose

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next cannot be served on a unified-memory GPU such as **DGX Spark (GB10, 128 GB shared by CPU
and GPU)** with either of the storage options #54371 introduced for its 47.7 GiB FP8 PLE table:

- **device-resident:** the table does not fit next to the ~72 GiB of weights;
- **pinned host (`cpu_offload`, the default):** a 47.7 GiB anonymous host copy of the table, in the same physical
  pool as the weights and the KV cache. It cannot be cheaply dropped and re-created under memory pressure. On a
  128 GB Spark, the pinned table plus weights plus KV has hard-reset the machine.

This PR adds a third, opt-in option, `--engram-config '{"checkpoint_mapped": true}'`, which **reads the table
in place from the checkpoint's safetensors files**. On GPUs that access pageable host memory through the host
page tables (`CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_PAGEABLE_MEMORY_ACCESS_USES_HOST_PAGE_TABLES`), the lookup kernel reads a
read-only mapping of the files. There is no table-sized device or pinned allocation, no resident duplicate of
the table, and no CPU-gather/H2D staging path; the kernel still copies the selected rows into its output
buffer. The table's pages are clean, file-backed page-cache pages that the kernel can drop and re-read, shared
by every process that maps the same files.

**Design:**

- **New backend.** `Qwen4ExpPLEPageableHostEmbedding`, a third backend in the #54371 hierarchy. It reuses the
  pinned backend's buffer, ETP reduction and finalize path; only the storage and the gather differ.
- **Gather.** A Triton kernel gathers rows byte-wise through a per-shard base-address table, because the
  safetensors data offsets are not aligned. It writes zeros for rows outside the rank's ETP range; the
  existing ETP all-reduce combines ranks.
- **Current stream.** The lookup runs on the current stream, not the pinned backend's side stream. With the
  inherited side-stream lookup, greedy outputs on GB10 were not reproducible within one server start
  (identical prompts, cold vs warm: 2/8 equal, |Δlogprob| up to 1.41). The observed cause on GB10: the side
  stream reads the ids tensor from the CUDA-graph memory pool after the graph has released it, and later
  segments overwrite it at replay. Reading a persistent copy instead made it reproducible (8/8); #57785's capture-time sync did not
  (1/8). On the current stream: 8/8, |Δlogprob| 0, and identical across fresh starts. That race (#58441) is
  now fixed on main by #58489's persistent ids buffer, which this backend also uses. The lookup stays on the
  current stream, which also keeps FULL CUDA-graph capture free of a second stream: this backend does not
  join the pinned side stream (a GPU test captures `start_prefetch` + forward in one FULL graph). A side-stream
  lookup on top of #58489 was not measured.
- **Host-side page prefetch.** GPU faults on non-resident file pages are serviced one page at a time. A cold
  30k-token prefill (≈480k rows) took **88 s** with GPU faults alone, and **1.6 s** when 64 CPU threads fault
  the step's rows in first. The prefetch is driven from `Qwen4ExpModelState.prepare_inputs`, from a CPU hash
  of the same inputs, and only when `checkpoint_mapped` is set. It is only a hint: the lookup is correct
  whether or not it has finished.
- **File resolution.** Files come from the default loader's preparation, so `--download-dir`, subfolders and
  the `model.safetensors.index.json` filter apply exactly as for loading. Every shard that owns rows must exist
  once, with its exact shape and dtype; nothing is truncated.
- **Formats.** FP8 and unquantized (BF16) tables. `--load-format dummy` maps private anonymous zero pages.
- **Reload.** On a reload every incoming PLE shard is compared **in full** with the newly mapped files.
  `reload_weights(weights_path=...)` streams those files, so it matches and remaps the new checkpoint (during
  reload processing, or at the latest on the next lookup). PLE weights delivered from memory (weight sync)
  differ from the files and are rejected. A rejected load stays rejected rather than falling back to the
  previous mapping, and binding commits its state only after the mapping succeeded. The cost is one extra
  pass over the table, on reloads only.
- **Guards.** Rejected with `dp_shared_memory` (mapped pages are already shared), with `embedding_across_dp`
  (the host prefetch only sees this DP rank's requests), for architectures without this backend (DeepSeek
  V4.1), and off CUDA (the ROCm Qwen4Exp path from #57497 has no mapped backend and would otherwise allocate the
  pinned table silently). A warning is logged on non-integrated GPUs that report the attribute, such as Grace Hopper or Grace
  Blackwell: **validated on DGX Spark only.**

## Test Plan

**Unit tests** (`tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple_pageable.py`, wired into the existing `models_basic` Qwen4Exp
job):

- CPU tests, 22:
  - discovery across files, short last shard, other layers ignored;
  - refusals: missing, short-coverage, extra, short-interior and duplicate shards, dtype mismatch;
  - index-filtered discovery;
  - file resolution through the real default loader, not a stub;
  - CPU views address the checkpoint rows;
  - the zero mapping commits no memory when read (RSS);
  - config rejections (DeepSeek V4.1, off CUDA, `dp_shared_memory`, `embedding_across_dp`);
  - reload A→B remaps to B; an in-memory reload is rejected, including one with a single changed row that
    no sample would hit; a rejected load stays rejected and a later reload from disk recovers.
- GPU tests, 6, skipped without pageable access (the prefetcher test without CUDA):
  - bit-exact FP8/BF16 gather with an ETP range over a 0xFF-poisoned allocation;
  - CUDA-graph replay switching valid ids to invalid ids yields zeros, not stale bytes;
  - one FULL CUDA graph capturing `start_prefetch` + forward, replayed with new ids;
  - the zero mapping;
  - short-then-long steps through the host prefetcher's pinned staging.
- Each regression test fails on the behaviour it replaced (checked by mutating the fixed line back).

**End-to-end on DGX Spark** (GB10, sm_121, TP=1, driver 580.178, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13, this branch's code on
the `1ea7c63f4` nightly wheel). Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with an NVFP4 body, the FP8 PLE table (47.68 GiB,
320,001,536 × 160 B in 128 shards / 10 files), MTP n=3. `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` 31 GiB unless noted.
These were measured before the rebase onto current main (below); the rebased head is covered by the unit tests.

## Test Result

**Unit tests:**
Head rebased onto main `378504a54`, which includes #57497, #58489, #56926 and #58086.
- `models_basic` Qwen4Exp job set (`test_config.py`, `test_ple.py`, `test_ple_pageable.py`): 53 passed,
  42 skipped (GPU-only) on CPU.
- `test_ple_pageable.py` on GB10: 28/28 (22 CPU + 6 GPU).
- `tests/test_config.py -k engram`: 39 passed.
- pre-commit clean on the changed files.

**Memory.** There is no working baseline on unmodified main (see Purpose), so the reference is the previous
offload implementation (#53899's worker, never merged) serving the same checkpoint:

| | #53899 worker (reference) | `checkpoint_mapped` |
|---|---|---|
| swap used, steady state | 50–53 GiB | 5–6 GiB |
| table-sized pinned allocation | none (anonymous table, 47.7 GiB) | none (4 small pinned staging slots) |
| extra processes | 1 (offload worker) | 0 |

**Speed**, two fresh starts per arm:

| | reference | `checkpoint_mapped` |
|---|---|---|
| TTFT, 3 prompts of 24–29k tokens, sum | 32.99 / 33.47 s | 31.77 / 31.97 s |
| TTFT, 3 prompts of 7–8k tokens, sum | 9.27 / 9.37 s | 9.01 / 9.02 s |
| decode, c=16, tok/s | 197.6 / 201.1 | 199.1 / 198.7 |

**Correctness:**
- Rows handed to the model equal the checkpoint bytes: in-server check on 6 steps per start, including
  4,096-token prefill chunks.
- Every recorded serving step of a mixed prefill/decode workload: 2,500 steps, 11.36 M rows, recorded with
  stream-ordered async copies and no sync before the consumer. The ids equal a CPU hash of the recorded inputs,
  and the rows the model consumed equal the checkpoint bytes, **including all 255 mixed prefill+decode steps**.
  The only id mismatches were 8 CUDA-graph capture-time calls, where the ids buffer is not yet computed; those
  are not serving steps.
- Greedy outputs are identical across fresh starts and cold vs warm (8/8, Δlogprob 0).
- A BF16-table copy of the checkpoint (rows = the FP8 path's `fp8 * scale` in BF16, mapped as 320 B rows)
  generates **bit-identical** output to the FP8 table: 8/8 sequential prompts and 8/8 determinism probes.

**Auto KV sizing** (no `--kv-cache-memory-bytes`): KV sized itself to about 33 GiB. 20 min of c=8 diverse
traffic (2k–60k-token prompts): 248 requests, 0 errors, MemAvailable ≥ 2.0 GiB, swap ≤ 6.8 GiB, memory PSI
`full avg10` ≤ 6.8 % (p90 3.3 %). The speed numbers above use an explicit 31 GiB KV cap, so both arms are
compared at equal KV.

**Not covered:**
- TP>1 on hardware (single-GPU box; the ETP range is unit-tested).
- Grace Hopper / Grace Blackwell.
- NVFP4 tables (main has no NVFP4 PLE method).
- Model Runner V1: the lookup is correct there, but the host prefetch hooks into the MRV2 model state, so cold
  prefill is slow.
- Kernel-format weight reload (a full table cannot be copied into the mapping; this fails loudly).

## Comparison with other PLE-table storage implementations

What each implementation documents, plus what we measured ourselves on GB10. Other PRs' numbers are not repeated
here, and nothing was measured for #54129.

| | where the table lives | who gathers rows | copies per step | extra process / privileges | target hardware | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #54371 device | GPU memory | GPU kernel | — | — | any CUDA-alike | merged; on GB10 does not fit next to the weights |
| #54371 pinned host (default) | pinned host memory (full table) | GPU kernel via UVA, on a side stream | — | — | UVA-capable | merged; on GB10 the 47.7 GiB pinned table plus weights plus KV exceeds the unified pool |
| #53899 offload worker | anonymous host memory in a CPU worker process | CPU | rows over IPC to the GPU | 1 process, `CAP_SYS_PTRACE` | any | closed unmerged; **was our GB10 production path: 50–53 GiB swap** |
| #54070 disk dir | file mapping of a table written at first boot to `VLLM_PLE_DISK_OFFLOAD_DIR` | CPU (the #53899 worker) | as #53899 | as #53899 | any | open, but built on the closed #53899 |
| #54129 mmap | read-only mapping of the checkpoint safetensors (page cache) | CPU worker threads at input preparation | staged H2D copy into stable GPU buffers | — | any GPU (MRV2) | open |
| #57497 ROCm | pinned host memory | GPU via UVA | — | — | AMD | merged |
| **this PR** | read-only mapping of the checkpoint safetensors (page cache) | **GPU kernel reading the mapping directly**; CPU threads only fault pages in | none beyond the kernel writing the selected rows | — | GPUs that read pageable memory through host page tables (validated: DGX Spark) | — |

**Relation to #54129.** Both keep the table file-backed and reclaimable in the page cache, and share the
discovery and validation concerns; this PR borrows #54129's approach to resolving and validating checkpoint
files.
- **#54129** is the portable path: a CPU gather plus a host-to-device copy, which works on discrete GPUs.
- **This PR** is the unified-memory variant: where the GPU can dereference pageable memory, the gather reads the
  mapping directly, with no host-side gather or staging copy.

The two could share discovery code, or `checkpoint_mapped` could become the unified-memory mode of one
file-backed backend. We are happy to rebase onto #54129 if it lands first. SGLang has an NVMe-backed path for
the same table (sgl-project/sglang#36567).

## Open design questions

1. **File resolution.** It reuses `DefaultModelLoader._prepare_weights`, a private method, to get exactly the
   files the loader read (download dir, index filter). Should the loader expose the resolved file list instead?
   Its return value already changed once under this PR (#58086); a test now calls the real loader.
2. **Host page prefetch.** A 64-thread CPU prefetcher lives in `Qwen4ExpModelState`. It is only a hint; the
   lookup is correct without it, but cold prefill is about 50× slower. Is the model state the right home, or
   should it hang off a runner hook?
3. **Selection.** Opt-in today. Should it be auto-selected on integrated GPUs that report pageable host-page-table
   access, where the pinned default does not fit?
4. **Relation to #54129.** One file-backed backend with two gather modes, or two backends?

## Related

- **#54371:** the storage hierarchy this extends.
- **#54129 (mmap PLE table, open):** also file-backed, via a CPU gather plus H2D copy. This PR is the
  unified-memory variant: the GPU reads the mapping directly, so there is no host gather and no staging copy.
  The validation approach borrows from it.
- **#58441 (issue), #58489 (merged):** the graph-pool reuse of the side-stream ids, reported from this work
  and fixed on main by #58489.
- **#57785 (open):** eager-break side-stream work left unjoined at capture. Tested with the inherited
  side-stream lookup on GB10: it did not remove the non-reproducibility above (1/8).
- **#57497 (merged):** ROCm pinned-table offload; `checkpoint_mapped` is rejected there.
- **#58310 (open), #56926 (merged):** host-memory guards, and serialization and huge pages for host-offloaded
  tables. They are orthogonal.

title: [Spec Decode][Qwen3.8] Enable fused draft metadata updates for the QSA side cache
body:
## Purpose

With MTP `num_speculative_tokens > 1`, the Model Runner V2 autoregressive speculator reuses one
attention-metadata build across draft steps only if every attention group's builder sets
`supports_draft_decode_metadata_update`. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's QSA side-cache builder
(`QSAMetadataBuilder`, backend `QWEN4_EXP_EXP_QSA_STATE`) does not, so the speculator logs

```
Fused multi-step draft decode is not supported by attention backend(s) QWEN4_EXP_EXP_QSA_STATE;
falling back to rebuilding attention metadata between draft steps.
```

and rebuilds metadata on every draft step for the whole model.

This PR opts the QSA builder in. `update_draft_decode_metadata` re-launches the builder's own
`_build_qsa_metadata_kernel` in place on the metadata's persistent tensors, following the
pattern of `DeepseekSparseSWA`'s update, so draft-step metadata (`token_to_req`,
`logical_positions`, `visible_blocks`, `slot_mapping`, and the compressed cache's
`k_work_metadata`) is computed by exactly the code path `build()` uses.

## Changes

- `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/qsa_cache.py`
  - Factor the kernel launch out of `build_qsa_metadata_triton` into
    `_launch_qsa_metadata_kernel`, shared by `build()` and the new update. No behavior change
    for `build()`.
  - `QSAForwardMetadata` gains `common_slot_mapping` (the compressed layout reads it to keep
    padded tokens inert) and `num_mapped_tokens` (previously read from `query_start_loc_cpu`,
    which is not capture-safe inside the draft loop).
  - `QSAMetadataBuilder.supports_draft_decode_metadata_update = HAS_TRITON` and
    `update_draft_decode_metadata`. The PyTorch fallback builder keeps the rebuild path.
- `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py`
  - `test_qsa_draft_decode_metadata_update_matches_rebuild`: for the plain, compressed and
    circular layouts, an in-place update after advancing `seq_lens` by one equals a fresh
    `build()` at `seq_lens + 1`. The sequence lengths cross a compression boundary, so
    `visible_blocks` must change; the test also asserts the update changed state.

`max_seq_len` is intentionally not refreshed: in this model it is only consumed by the prefill
selection path, and the fused draft loop is decode-only.

## Not a duplicate

- #55292 adds `supports_multi_step_drafting = True` to the same builder. That is a different
  capability (the V1 proposer's multi-step validity check, ROCm-gated) and does not add
  in-place draft metadata updates. The two changes touch adjacent lines of the same class and
  should rebase trivially onto each other.
- #54790 does the equivalent for sparse MLA backends under DCP — different backend.
- No open PR sets `supports_draft_decode_metadata_update` for `QSAMetadataBuilder`.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py -v \
    -k "draft_decode_metadata_update or triton_metadata_matches_pytorch or side_metadata_marks or compressed_metadata_keeps or circular_buffer_metadata_keeps or fused_metadata_matches"
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/qsa_cache.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py
```

## Test Result

- pre-commit (ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy-3.10, SPDX, forbidden imports,
  check-test-tethering): **passed**.
- pytest on NVIDIA GB10 (SM121), CUDA + Triton, vLLM 0.30.0 image with this change applied:

  ```
  pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py -k "draft_decode_metadata_update or \
      triton_metadata_matches_pytorch or side_metadata_marks or compressed_metadata_keeps or \
      circular_buffer_metadata_keeps or fused_metadata_matches"
  19 passed
  ```

  The new test for all three layouts, plus the neighboring metadata tests that exercise
  `build()` through the refactored launch helper.
- Mutation check of the new test (not part of the PR): an update that refreshes everything
  except `visible_blocks`, and a no-op update, both fail the new test in all three layouts
  (6/6 caught).

## Performance

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (NVFP4 checkpoint), 2× DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), TP=2, MTP
`num_speculative_tokens=4`, bf16 KV, vLLM 0.30.0 with this change, `max_num_seqs=64`.
Same image for both arms; the fused path was toggled at runtime by forcing
`supports_draft_decode_metadata_update` off. Averages of steady-state samples; runs per cell
in parentheses.

| concurrency | decode steps/s, stock | decode steps/s, this PR | Δ | output tok/s, stock → this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (8) | 21.93 | 22.20 | +1.2 % | 90.0 → 92.8 |
| 2 (6) | 17.7 | 18.2 | +2.8 % | 147.8 → 152.3 |
| 4 (4) | 13.4 | 13.7 | +2.2 % | 223.8 → 226.8 |
| 8 (4) | 9.73 | 9.93 | +2.1 % | 324.8 → 330.5 |
| 12 (4) | 7.75 | 7.93 | +2.3 % | 388.3 → 396.3 |
| 16 (3) | — | — | — | 439 → 440 |
| 32 (3) | — | — | — | 546 → 539 (−1.3 %) |
| 64 (3) | — | — | — | 701 → 693 (−1.1 %) |

At 2–12 concurrent requests the step-rate ranges of the two arms do not overlap. The gain
tracks the per-draft-step metadata rebuild the fused path removes: it matters when decode
steps are short and fades as they lengthen; above ~16 requests the in-place refresh on the
draft path costs slightly more than the host-side rebuild it replaces.

## Accuracy

Speculative decoding is exact; the fused path only changes when draft-step metadata is
computed. Mean acceptance length is unchanged at every concurrency (e.g. 4.13–4.26 vs
4.08–4.31 at c=2, 4.15–4.21 vs 4.16–4.21 at c=16–64), and per-position acceptance at c=64 is
0.90 / 0.83 / 0.77 / 0.68.

GSM8K (`gsm8k_cot_zeroshot`, the same 400 seeded questions in every run, thinking on,
temperature 0.6 / top-p 0.95 / top-k 20, max 32k tokens, 32 concurrent requests), two
runs per arm to measure run-to-run noise:

| run | accuracy | truncated |
|---|---|---|
| this PR #1 | 97.75 % | 0 |
| this PR #2 | 98.00 % | 0 |
| stock #1 | 97.75 % | 0 |
| stock #2 | 97.25 % | 0 |

Per question, the two runs of the same arm disagree on 8 (this PR) and 7 (stock) of the 400;
the four cross-arm pairs disagree on 8, 5, 2 and 7. Cross-arm disagreement is no larger than
within-arm disagreement, i.e. no measurable change in outputs.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The AI agent also ran the tests,
benchmarks and evaluations reported above, on the submitter's hardware and at the submitter's
direction. The submitter has reviewed every changed line and can answer for the change.

title: [GLM5.3 Perf] Optimize glm 5.3 metadata op, 1.6~4.8x kernel level performance improvement
body:
## Purpose

- Reuse `arrange`
- persistent GPU buffer + Triton kernel for `_build_req_id_per_token`

## Test

Acc covered by current unit test

Perf can be seen in this ai generated script

```py

import statistics
import time

import numpy as np
import torch

from vllm.utils.torch_utils import np_to_pinned_tensor
from vllm.v1.attention.backend import CommonAttentionMetadata

TOKENS = [2**i for i in range(16)]  # 1 ... 32768
MAX_REQS = 128
WARMUP = 20
ITERS = 500
ROUNDS = 5


def bench(old, new):
    for _ in range(WARMUP):
        old()
        new()
    samples = [[], []]
    for r in range(ROUNDS):
        for i in (0, 1) if r % 2 == 0 else (1, 0):
            fn = (old, new)[i]
            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
            start = time.perf_counter()
            for _ in range(ITERS):
                fn()
            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
            samples[i].append((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1e6 / ITERS)
    return [statistics.median(s) for s in samples]


def main():
    buffer = torch.empty(max(TOKENS), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    offsets = torch.arange(max(TOKENS) + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    print(torch.cuda.get_device_name())
    print(f"Buffer: {max(TOKENS)} tokens; requests: min(tokens, {MAX_REQS})")
    print("Eager amortized wall time in us/call; initialization excluded.")
    print(
        " tokens  reqs | mapping old      new  speedup | arange old    slice  speedup"
    )

    for n in TOKENS:
        num_reqs = min(n, MAX_REQS)
        lengths = np.full(num_reqs, n // num_reqs, dtype=np.int32)
        lengths[: n % num_reqs] += 1
        starts = torch.from_numpy(np.r_[np.int32(0), lengths.cumsum(dtype=np.int32)])
        common = CommonAttentionMetadata(
            query_start_loc=starts.cuda(),
            query_start_loc_cpu=starts,
            seq_lens=torch.tensor(lengths, device="cuda"),
            num_reqs=num_reqs,
            num_actual_tokens=n,
            max_query_len=int(lengths.max()),
            max_seq_len=int(lengths.max()),
            block_table_tensor=torch.empty(
                num_reqs, 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
            ),
            slot_mapping=torch.empty(n, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64),
        )

        def old_mapping(common=common, n=n):
            starts_cpu = np.asarray(common.query_start_loc_cpu, dtype=np.int32)
            lens = np.diff(starts_cpu)
            req_ids = np.repeat(np.arange(len(lens), dtype=np.int32), lens)
            buffer.fill_(0)
            buffer[: len(req_ids)].copy_(
                np_to_pinned_tensor(req_ids), non_blocking=True
            )
            return buffer[:n]

        def new_mapping(common=common):
            # A new scheduler step must rebuild the mapping, not hit the cache.
            common._token_to_req_indices_cache = None
            return common.token_to_req_indices(buffer)

        def old_offsets(n=n):
            return torch.arange(n + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")

        def new_offsets(n=n):
            return offsets[: n + 1]

        expected = old_mapping().clone()
        torch.testing.assert_close(new_mapping(), expected)
        torch.testing.assert_close(new_offsets(), old_offsets())
        m_old, m_new = bench(old_mapping, new_mapping)
        a_old, a_new = bench(old_offsets, new_offsets)
        print(
            f"{n:7d} {num_reqs:5d} | {m_old:11.2f} {m_new:8.2f} {m_old / m_new:7.2f}x"
            f" | {a_old:10.2f} {a_new:8.2f} {a_old / a_new:7.2f}x",
            flush=True,
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

And we can get

```bash
NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC
Buffer: 32768 tokens; requests: min(tokens, 128)
Eager amortized wall time in us/call; initialization excluded.
```

title: [Bugfix] Ignore DeepSeek V4 thinking sampling overrides
body:
## Purpose
Fixes #58155 
DeepSeek V4 thinking mode accepts `temperature`, `presence_penalty`,
and `frequency_penalty` for API compatibility but should ignore them.

This change ignores those request overrides only when:

- The resolved architecture is DeepSeek V4.
- Thinking mode is enabled.

Other models and DeepSeek V4 non-thinking requests retain their existing
sampling behavior.

No existing open PR was found for #58155 or this sampling behavior.

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \
  -k deepseek_v4_thinking_sampling_overrides -q

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py
  
  ```
  
## Test Result
All pre-commit checks passed, including Ruff and mypy.
96 isolated conversion-boundary cases passed.
Full pytest collection could not run locally because the macOS arm64
environment has no compatible precompiled vLLM runtime.
Model evaluation was not run because DeepSeek V4 cannot be served on
this development machine. Linux CI is requested for the repository test.

title: [WIP][Sampling] Add adaptive verification support to batch-sharded sampling
body:
### Benchmarks: adaptive verification with and without batch-sharded sampling

**Setup.** 4x GB200, TP4 + expert parallel, vLLM `main` @ 13058faa49 + this PR.
`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark`, `--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","enable_adaptive_verification":true}'`,
`--max-num-seqs 256 --max-model-len 32768 --block-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --moe-backend deep_gemm --enable-expert-parallel --no-enable-prefix-caching --kernel-config.enable_flashinfer_autotune=False`,
`--compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size": 2048}'` (so 256 requests x 8 tokens stay under CUDA graphs; the default 1024 falls back to eager above 128 requests).
Both arms have adaptive verification enabled; the sharded arm adds `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling`.

**Client.** `vllm-bench` (Rust), SPEED-Bench `throughput_2k` (all categories), 2048 output tokens, temperature 1.0, no top-p/top-k, `--num-warmups <conc>`, prompts = 8x concurrency (min 32, max 1024).

**Method.** 4 server boots in ABBA order (shard, base, base, shard), 2 full concurrency sweeps per boot, so n=4 per cell; a throwaway warmup run at conc 256 after each boot absorbs first-request JIT. Each boot was checked for the "Batch-sharded sampling enabled" log line count (4 for shard, 0 for base). Delta = shard vs base; negative ITL/TPOT/TTFT is better, positive tok/s is better.

title: [Feature]: [ROCm][Hy4] Add calibrated FP8 KV-cache support for sparse MLA
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

While doing validation on https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58056 I noticed that `tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8` provides FP8 weights but no calibrated FP8 KV-cache scales:

```json
"kv_cache_quant_algo": null
```

When `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` is enabled, vLLM defaults the Q/K scales to `1.0`.
This causes a large accuracy regression with `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`.

Matched 20-example GSM8K results:

| KV-cache dtype | Accuracy | Truncated |
|---|---:|---:|
| BF16 (`auto`) | 95% | 5% |
| FP8 | 50% | 40% |

From a bit of digging, I think there are two options here:

1. **Static calibrated scales** (less work up front, but not necessary robust across workloads)
   - Calibrate and export per-layer Q and compressed-KV scales.
   - Load them following the Kimi K3 or DeepSeek V3.2 pattern.

2. **Dynamic block scales** (more impl work upfront, but scales to new workloads)
   - Add ROCm support for an embedded-scale format similar to `fp8_ds_mla`.
   - Compute per-token or per-block UE8M0 scales when writing the cache,
     following DeepSeek V4.

cc: @akii96 

### Alternatives

Use `--kv-cache-dtype auto` so Hy4 keeps a BF16 KV cache.

vLLM could also reject or require explicit opt-in for uncalibrated FP8 KV when
the checkpoint declares `kv_cache_quant_algo: null`.

### Additional context

- Hardware: 8× AMD Instinct MI350X (`gfx950`)
- Parallelism: TP8
- Backend: `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`
- Model revision: `4215ec29de873a998e849cee902654490c7ff4d1`
- vLLM commit: `79468c20ef23227d4e051f807e10fd54fb24e24f`
- Related: #54594, #58056


### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Resolve kernel block-size constraints per layer head size
body:
## Purpose

`FlashAttentionBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()` decides its FA4 hd256 page constraint (`[128]` on SM100/SM110) from the model-wide `ModelConfig` head size. Layers with a different head size, in practice a spec-decode drafter (DFlash, EAGLE-3, DSpark, MTP) with smaller heads than its target, therefore get the target's constraint instead of their own at every place block sizes are chosen:

1. backend selection under a user `--block-size` (`validate_configuration`);
2. the default block size (`Platform.update_block_size_for_backend`, which since #49845 consults every backend found in the loaded layers, including the drafter's);
3. each KV cache group's kernel block size (`prepare_kernel_block_sizes` / `select_common_block_size`);
4. a sliding-window layer's own block size (`_largest_kernel_block_within`).

Example: Qwen3.8-27B (GDN hybrid, head size 256, full attention on FlashInfer) + `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (head size 128, FlashAttention) on GB200. The Mamba alignment gives an 832-token block, which the drafter's 128-token page constraint does not divide.

- Before #49845, KV-cache init failed: `ValueError: No common block size for 832.` (#58425).
- On `main` today with the default block size, Phase 1 honors the drafter's constraint and picks 896 instead of 832: Mamba page padding 9.5% instead of 1.7% and a 4.5% smaller KV cache.
- On `main` today with `--block-size 64`, FlashAttention is precluded for the drafter, which falls back to FlashInfer and, lacking CUDA-graph support for the DFlash2 draft, runs it eagerly: 1.7x slower decode.

#58207 notes the same failure for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash on B300.

## Fix

Resolve a backend's block-size constraints from the head size of the layers it serves. `head_size` is FlashAttention's only per-layer input to the decision, and it is available at all four sites.

- `AttentionBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes_for_head_size(head_size)` and `supports_block_size_for_head_size(head_size, block_size)`, defaulting to the model-wide methods (`None` means model-wide). Other backends are unchanged, including CPU_MLA's exact-size `supports_block_size` override. The block-size test shared by `supports_block_size` moves into `supports_kernel_block_size`.
- `FlashAttentionBackend` overrides both, resolving the hd256 page from the given head size.
- `validate_configuration` checks the block size for the layer's head size.
- `Platform._find_non_ssm_backend_head_sizes` collects distinct `(backend, head size)` pairs from the layers; `_preferred_block_size_for_backends` takes the head sizes as an optional parallel argument. `_find_non_ssm_backends`, its CPU/XPU callers and the later alignment phases are unchanged.
- `select_common_block_size` takes optional per-backend head sizes; `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` passes each attention group's. Other callers are unchanged.
- `_largest_kernel_block_within` takes the layer's head size.

Only layers whose head size differs from the model-wide one change. A smaller-head drafter behind a head-size-256 target is no longer held to the 128-token page. Conversely, a head-size-256 drafter behind a smaller-head target now makes the default block size 128 model-wide, as a head-size-256 target does, instead of silently running FA2 when the block size is not a multiple of 128.

Supersedes #58425, which only covered site 3.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py -k fa4_hd256_block_size_advertisement
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -k "select_common_block_size or preferred_block_size"
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -k "kernel_block_size or hisparse_block_size or preserve_global"
```

E2E on one GB200: Qwen3.8-27B (bf16) + `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (`num_speculative_tokens=7`), default block size and `--block-size 64`, on `main` and with this PR; single-request decode benchmark with the acceptance length pinned to 3.

## Test Result

Unit tests pass (new: `test_fa4_hd256_block_size_advertisement_per_head_size`, `test_preferred_block_size_resolves_constraints_per_head_size`, `test_select_common_block_size_resolves_sizes_per_head_size`).

| | `main` (8b660ce96b) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| default block size | block 896, Mamba padding 9.54%, KV cache 578k tokens, TPOT 4.53 ms | block 832, padding 1.71%, KV cache 605k tokens, TPOT 4.53 ms |
| `--block-size 64` | drafter precluded from FlashAttention, eager FlashInfer draft, TPOT 7.88 ms | drafter on FlashAttention with CUDA graphs, TPOT 4.51 ms |

---

Code written with AI assistance (Claude); reviewed, tested and validated end to end by the author.

title: [Bugfix] Don't sync-police or retry FlashInfer all-reduce workspace creation in eager mode
body:
## Purpose

Fix a nightly regression from #58197 ("[Core] Disable JIT warmup in eager mode").

With `--enforce-eager` the V2 `warmup_kernels` dummy forward is now skipped. The standalone FlashInfer all-reduce (`FlashInferAllReduce`, enabled by default through `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=1`) creates its workspace lazily. The profile run uses large tensors that are above the FlashInfer size cap (e.g. 0.5 MB at TP8 or 2 MB at TP4 on H200), so it never touches the workspace. As a result, the workspace is first created inside the first real `execute_model`, which runs after `enable_gpu_sync_check()`. In CI (`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`), `flashinfer_comm.create_allreduce_fusion_workspace(...)` then raises `RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected` part-way through a collective. The failure is caught and returns `None`, and `get_fi_ar_workspace` does not remember it. The mnnvl attempt fails, the trtllm fallback fails, and the collective creation keeps getting retried. Each retry leaks partially created buffers, which leads to CUDA OOM, then a deadlock, then `TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out` and `EngineDeadError`.

Evidence (nightly build 90589):
- H200 LM Eval DeepSeek V3.2 TP8 (`--enforce-eager`): https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90589#01a0ccda-d861-443c-bcb5-9c8b22260601. At 11:45:56 it logs `Failed to initialize FlashInfer All Reduce workspace: GPU<->CPU sync detected`, followed by repeated `Failed to initialize FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=trtllm`. OOM follows by 11:46:18 and the RPC timeout at 11:50:53.
- B200 HiSparse (GLM-5.2-NVFP4 TP4), job `01a0cd35-9fed-4cff-a2be-b8c4ea5fb773` in the same build, fails the same way.
- Passing build 90513 (before #58197) logs `Initialized FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=mnnvl` during warmup.
- This is likely also behind the H100 Fault Tolerance E2E failure (`rank 0 did not report UNHEALTHY within 45s`) that #58318 is bisecting. That link is not verified.

## Fix

In `vllm/distributed/device_communicators/flashinfer_all_reduce.py`:
1. Wrap the one-time `create_allreduce_fusion_workspace` call in `gpu_sync_allowed()`. This covers both the regular and the quant workspace paths, since both go through `_create_workspace`. Setup syncs are expected here and are not a per-step cost.
2. Remember a failed creation (`_fi_ar_workspace_failed` / `_fi_ar_quant_workspace_failed`) so a collective creation is never retried on every all-reduce call. `destroy_fi_ar_workspace()` resets both flags.

I also considered creating the workspace eagerly before `enable_gpu_sync_check()` when warmup is skipped. That approach would have to guess the hidden size and dtype in the worker. It would also leave the retry-storm failure mode in place for any other lazy-creation failure. The change above is smaller and local to the module that owns the workspace.

## Not a duplicate

- `gh pr list --state open --search "flashinfer all reduce workspace"`, `"58197"`, `"gpu_sync_allowed"`, `"flashinfer allreduce eager"` and `"enforce-eager warmup"` returned no PR that fixes this.
- #58318 is a DNM CI-bisect probe that reverts #58197. It is not a fix.

## Test Plan / Results

GPU checks ran on an idle 8×H200 host (GPUs 0-3), using the nightly image `public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:de6674b0023b...` (the same image as build 90589). For "after", the patched file was mounted over the installed one. At that commit the file is identical to current `main`.

Repro: `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, `LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", tensor_parallel_size=4, enforce_eager=True)`, 3× `generate` of 4 prompts. TP4 puts the FlashInfer cap at 2 MB, so the profile run skips it, which matches the CI case.
- **Before:** `Failed to initialize FlashInfer All Reduce workspace: GPU<->CPU sync detected` (mnnvl, then trtllm), then `Failed to initialize FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=trtllm`. Generation still finished because this small model falls back to other all-reduce backends, so the full OOM/deadlock cascade seen with DeepSeek V3.2 TP8 did not reproduce here.
- **After:** `Initialized FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=mnnvl` during the first step. No sync errors, and output is correct (`' Paris. ...'`).

Unit tests, run in the same image with the patched files mounted:
```
pytest distributed/test_comm_ops.py -k "flashinfer or checkpoints"
14 passed, 17 deselected
```
The new `test_flashinfer_workspace_failure_is_not_retried` checks that a failing creation runs once (mnnvl plus the trtllm fallback) across repeated calls and runs again after `destroy_fi_ar_workspace()`.

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes.

Not verified: the full DeepSeek V3.2 TP8 and GLM-5.2 HiSparse CI jobs themselves, and the H100 Fault Tolerance E2E job.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). @khluu will review every changed line and is responsible for the change.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Preserve partial external hits under bounded replay
body:
## Purpose

When a KV connector reports a non-block-aligned prefix hit for DeepSeek-V4.1 bounded replay, the scheduler rounds it down to a whole block before applying the replay window. With a 64-token block, a 128-token replay window, and an 8,439-token remote hit, this reduces the adopted hit to 8,384 tokens, moves the replay start from 8,311 to 8,256, and can make the Decode block range disagree with the Prefill block range.

The rounding introduced in #56227 protects the SWA block containing the first replay token. This PR instead ensures generated bounded-replay SWA cache specs retain that boundary block, then preserves the exact connector hit only when every replay-enabled group has this guarantee. Direct or legacy configs without the guarantee keep the existing rounding fallback. The attention window is unchanged.

## Relationship to other work

This fixes a mainline scheduler/cache-config interaction from #56227 and does not depend on #58132. It is distinct from #57613's sparse local prefix-cache retention, #56709's native-offloading coverage for already configured `extra_retained_tokens`, and #58289's NIXL-specific source-block alignment. This PR does not claim to fix every connector's legacy block-mapping behavior.

## Test Plan & Test Result

### Environment and scope

- Model and hardware: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 8 × H20 Prefill and 8 × H20 Decode; the router ran with Decode.
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-e9757321527ca1ecd514c07c1418dd2c53da3d19`; the candidate additionally applied this PR at `88367fbc319683a8a1f6ad6b795af7326cd17f6e`.

Serving tests used Mooncake. I reviewed the corresponding NIXL hit and block-pairing code, but did not run NIXL transport or NIXL serving tests for this PR; I can add that validation if reviewers need it.

The unmodified nightly encountered an unrelated Mooncake release-only-pull issue before the target test: `MooncakeConnectorWorker.process_pulling_result` could report receive completion for a pull with no local destination blocks, although Decode had not entered `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`, triggering a scheduler request-ID assertion. We applied the same temporary guard to both arms so testing could proceed: report receive completion only when `pull_tasks_count == 0 and any(local_block_ids)`. This guard is not part of this PR; the only A/B code difference was the PR.

### Single-request end-to-end check

The same 8,439-token ID sequence was sent to both arms with Decode's local prefix cache reset, a fixed seed, and exactly 1,500 generated tokens.

| Metric | Baseline | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| External KV hit | 8,384 | 8,439 |
| Replay start / prompt rows (derived from the hit) | 8,256 / 183 | 8,311 / 128 |
| DSpark mean acceptance length | 2.1398 | 2.3675 |
| Generation time | 7,809.51 ms | 6,610.95 ms |

### Aligned and non-aligned boundary benchmark

These are the essential serving arguments; cluster-specific network settings were identical across arms.

```bash
# Prefill
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT=8998 vllm serve /data00/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001 --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash --trust-remote-code --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len auto --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --enable-cumem-allocator --block-size 64 --swa-bounded-replay --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --mm-encoder-tp-mode data --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail","kv_buffer_device":"cuda","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma","enforce_handshake_compat":false}}' --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}' --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}'
# Decode
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT=8999 vllm serve /data00/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8002 --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash --trust-remote-code --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len auto --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --enable-cumem-allocator --block-size 64 --swa-bounded-replay --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --mm-encoder-tp-mode data --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail","kv_buffer_device":"cuda","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma","enforce_handshake_compat":false}}' --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":true}' --enable-expert-parallel --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' --enable-per-request-metrics --per-request-spec-decode-metrics summary
```

We ran `vllm bench serve` with `prefix_repetition`, 80 measured requests per input length, 16 concurrent requests, fixed 512-token outputs, temperature 0, seed 1104, and separate warmup and P/D cache resets for each tier. The representative measured command below uses a 936-token prefix and a 64-token suffix for the 1,000-token tier; the other tiers used prefix lengths 960, 986, 1,023, and 1,024.

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --base-url http://192.168.1.220:30000 --model /data00/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash --tokenizer /data00/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --trust-remote-code --dataset-name prefix_repetition --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 5 --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 936 --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 64 --prefix-repetition-output-len 512 --num-prompts 80 --num-warmups 0 --max-concurrency 16 --request-rate inf --seed 1104 --temperature 0 --ignore-eos --disable-shuffle
```

`Aligned` means the actual tokenized input length is divisible by the 64-token KV block size; 1,024 and 1,088 were the intended aligned controls.

| Requested input tokens | Output tok/s, baseline → PR | DSpark mean acceptance, baseline → PR | Mean TPOT, baseline → PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,000 | 1,297.9 → 1,645.7 (+26.8%) | 3.169 → 4.552 | 10.213 → 7.369 ms |
| 1,024 (aligned) | 1,815.2 → 1,798.8 (−0.9%) | 5.133 → 5.132 | 6.655 → 6.928 ms |
| 1,050 | 1,462.4 → 1,678.1 (+14.8%) | 3.750 → 4.810 | 9.025 → 7.340 ms |
| 1,087 | 1,292.6 → 1,718.6 (+33.0%) | 3.002 → 4.721 | 10.569 → 7.215 ms |
| 1,088 (aligned) | 1,754.8 → 1,730.9 (−1.4%) | 5.026 → 4.728 | 7.188 → 7.458 ms |

All 400 measured requests per arm completed with exactly 512 output tokens. The baseline's lost external-hit tokens matched the sum of actual input lengths modulo 64, while the candidate lost none; one nominally aligned 1,088-token request tokenized to 1,089. Mean TTFT in the non-aligned group rose 14.4% under this saturated workload, so the demonstrated performance gain is in Decode TPOT and output throughput.

### Accuracy: full GSM8K A/B

EvalScope ran the complete 1,319-sample GSM8K test split at 0-shot with `temperature=0.2`, `top_p=0.95`, `seed=42`, and `reasoning_effort=high`. Baseline scored **1,269/1,319 (96.209%)**; this PR scored **1,268/1,319 (96.133%)**, a difference of −0.076 percentage points. Both arms completed every request, with no statistically distinguishable accuracy regression in this run. Their generated output-token totals differed, so this evaluation is not used for a throughput claim.

title: [Bugfix] Keep closing </think> delimiter in MiniMax M2 append-think mode
body:
## Summary

The MiniMax M2 tool parser dropped the closing `</think>` delimiter from `content`
when it appeared in the CONTENT state — i.e. when combined with the
`minimax_m2_append_think` reasoning parser, which intentionally keeps the
reasoning delimiters in `content`. The opening `<think>` survived but the
closing `</think>` was silently consumed, breaking the output contract clients
rely on to distinguish thinking from the answer / tool invocation.

## Problem

Reported in #58486. With

```
--enable-auto-tool-choice
--tool-call-parser minimax_m2
--reasoning-parser minimax_m2_append_think
```

a fixed model output like

```
I should add them.</think><minimax:tool_call><invoke name="add">...</invoke></minimax:tool_call>
```

produced `content = "<think>I should add them."` — the closing `</think>` was
missing. The tool call itself was extracted correctly; only the delimiter was
lost. This affects both streaming and non-streaming responses with
`tool_choice="auto"`.

## Root cause

`MiniMaxM2AppendThinkReasoningParser` returns `(None, "<think>" + model_output)`,
so reasoning is *not* stripped and everything — including both `</think>`
delimiters — is supposed to live in `content`. The tool parser engine then
processes this text already in the CONTENT state. In the declarative config
(`vllm/parser/minimax_m2.py`), the transition

```python
(ParserState.CONTENT, "THINK_END"): Transition(ParserState.CONTENT, ()),
```

emits no events when it matches `</think>`. That is correct for the *normal*
reasoning path (where `</think>` is the `REASONING -> CONTENT` boundary, handled
by the `REASONING/THINK_END` transition that emits `REASONING_END`), but in
append-think mode the closing delimiter is data, not a boundary — so it was
silently dropped. The `<think>` opening tag has no `CONTENT/THINK_START`
transition and therefore falls through as ordinary content, which is why only
the closing delimiter was lost.

This transition was introduced by the engine migration in #45701.

## Solution

Emit `EventType.TEXT_CHUNK` on the `(CONTENT, "THINK_END")` transition so the
matched `</think>` literal is appended to content instead of being consumed
silently. The `REASONING/THINK_END` transition still owns the normal
reasoning/end-of-reasoning boundary, so standard `minimax_m2` reasoning
extraction is unchanged.

## Testing

New regression test in `tests/parser/engine/test_minimax_m2.py`:

- `TestThinkEndInContent::test_closing_think_end_in_content_is_preserved` —
  feeds `<think>thoughts</think>answer</think>` immediately followed by a tool
  call and asserts `content == "answer</think>"` while the tool call is still
  parsed correctly.

Existing MiniMax M2 parser and reasoning-parser tests are unchanged in
expectation.

## Compatibility

- No API or config changes.
- Standard reasoning mode (`minimax_m2`, not append-think) is unaffected: the
  end-of-reasoning `</think>` still goes through `REASONING/THINK_END`. A
  literal `</think>` that genuinely appears inside answer text is now preserved
  verbatim, which is the correct literal behavior.

## Related

Fixes #58486.

## Readiness gate

Run at head `7ee4043` on a CPU-only box (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`).

**A gap in the shipped test, found by the edge-case review.** The description says the
dropped `</think>` affects *both* streaming and non-streaming responses, but the test
added with the fix only drives `extract_tool_calls`. The streaming counterpart is now
covered by `test_streaming_closing_think_end_in_content_is_preserved`, which uses the
repo's own `simulate_tool_streaming` helper: `<think>` opens reasoning, the first
`</think>` closes it, and the second one sits in content, where it is data rather than a
boundary. Both cases fail against the previous config — `(CONTENT, "THINK_END")`
emitting no events — and pass with it, so the streaming half of the claim is measured
rather than assumed. The file is 16 passed.

**The follow-up commit contains no product change**: it adds one test, so a review of
`e769f90` still applies as-is.

**Patch coverage could not be measured on this box.** `pytest --cov` fails here (torch
under coverage's import instrumentation), and `coverage run` on this target dumps core;
the same tooling fails across this PR series for the same class of reason. The
behavioural evidence is stronger than a percentage in this case: the changed line is a
single value in the `minimax_m2_config()` transition table, every test builds the engine
from that config, and the two cases above fail without the change and pass with it —
which can only happen if the changed line is active.

**Cross-config / cross-provider.** Seven parser configs define a
`(CONTENT, "THINK_END")` transition — `kimi_k2`, `qwen3`, `mistral`, `glm47_moe`,
`deepseek_v4`, `gemma4` and this one — and the other six keep `()`, i.e. they still
consume a `</think>` seen in the content state. That is deliberate and correct for them:
none of them has an append-think mode, so a `</think>` in content there is a stray
delimiter rather than data. `grep append_think` finds only `vllm/parser/minimax_m2.py`
plus the reasoning-parser registry, so the change is confined to the config that needs
it. The shared engine is untouched — `TEXT_CHUNK` is an existing event type that other
transitions already emit — and the normal `minimax_m2` reasoning path still has its
boundary owned by the `(REASONING, "THINK_END")` transition; the changed transition only
matches a `</think>` reached while already in `CONTENT`, which is the append-think case.
The file's pre-existing reasoning and streaming cases still pass.

title: [ROCm][Perf] MXFP8 GEMM on native 32x32 block scales for gfx950
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek V4/V4.1 checkpoints store MXFP8 weight scales in 32x32 blocks. The
ModelOpt loader expands them to one scale row per weight row, and on gfx950
`RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` then runs one generic `tl.dot_scaled`
kernel on those per-row scales. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash these linears
(`fused_wqa_wkv`, `wq_b`, the indexer `wq_b`, `wo_b`, and the shared-expert
`gate_up` and `down`) make up 11.7% of GPU kernel time per decode step at
TP2 conc32.

This PR keeps the checkpoint's 32x32 scale blocks and adds a GEMM that reads
them directly, tuned per shape for the V4.1-Flash projections. It is 1.49x
faster than the current kernel at the median, and 1.07x faster than the
native group32 GEMM in ROCm/aiter#5750 (latest head). End to end, over a
1-hour InferenceX agentx run (TP2, conc 32, DSpark x5), TPOT is 4.8% lower.

## What changes

- **`rocm_block32_gemm.py` (new):** a `tl.dot_scaled` GEMM for an MXFP8
  activation times an e4m3 weight with `[N/32, K/32]` E8M0 block scales.
  - A tiled kernel for larger M.
  - A packed kernel for small M. It fills the MFMA's rows with K panels
    instead of tokens and keeps only the matching-panel (block-diagonal)
    products, so a handful of tokens still streams the weight at full width.
  - Either kernel can split K. Normally the last program of each output tile
    sums the partials in split order within the same launch, so the result
    is deterministic and needs no second launch. A tile's splits run on one
    XCD, so they meet in its L2. The arrival counters are kept per stream.
    If a stream's first split-K launch happens inside a graph capture, it
    has no counters yet and uses a second reduce launch instead.
  - N and K are `constexpr` and M is runtime (`do_not_specialize`), so
    serving does not recompile per batch size.
  - The tile, split-K, MFMA shape and occupancy come from a table tuned on
    MI355X for the ten V4.1-Flash projections at TP2/TP4. Untuned shapes
    use a generic default.
  - It is registered as a custom op, because the config choice branches on
    M and the linear runs under `torch.compile`.
- **`RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`:**
  - `process_weights_after_loading` recovers the `[N/32, K/32]` blocks when
    every 32 rows share their scales, which is exactly what the loader
    produces from a 32x32 checkpoint.
  - `apply_weights` dispatches on the scale shape, so pre-processed
    (IPC-cached) weights work either way.
  - The block-scaled path also runs `K % 32 == 0` natively. DeepSeek-V4.1's
    shared-expert `down` at TP4 (K=576) was dequantized to BF16 at load
    before.
  - Checkpoints with per-row (1x32) scales keep the existing kernel
    unchanged.
- **Grouped MXFP8 `wo_a` GEMM (#58456):** `wo_a` goes through the same
  linear kernel, so its scales are now compact too. The kernel derives the
  scale row block from the scale shape and reads either layout.

## Kernel performance (MI355X, gfx950)

The numbers go through the vLLM entry point (custom op plus table lookup).
Weights are cold (rotated past the 256 MB MALL), timing uses HIP graphs,
and every arm gets identical MXFP8 inputs. All three kernels ran in one
session.

**Current kernel -> this PR**, in µs:

| shape (N x K) | M=2 | M=16 | M=48 | M=96 | M=160 | M=192 | M=384 | M=768 | M=2048 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fused wq_a\|wkv (1792x5120) | 7.2 -> 4.9 (1.47x) | 7.3 -> 5.6 (1.31x) | 9.0 -> 6.7 (1.35x) | 17.8 -> 7.8 (2.27x) | 17.8 -> 9.8 (1.82x) | 18.1 -> 10.0 (1.81x) | 27.2 -> 14.6 (1.87x) | 27.2 -> 22.7 (1.20x) | 33.1 -> 31.3 (1.06x) |
| wq_b TP2 (16384x1280) | 7.0 -> 5.4 (1.29x) | 7.2 -> 5.7 (1.27x) | 13.6 -> 7.1 (1.91x) | 12.1 -> 8.6 (1.41x) | 17.3 -> 10.9 (1.59x) | 17.5 -> 11.1 (1.58x) | 25.0 -> 16.2 (1.54x) | 47.7 -> 27.3 (1.75x) | 84.3 -> 60.0 (1.41x) |
| wq_b TP4 (8192x1280) | 5.9 -> 3.9 (1.49x) | 6.0 -> 4.2 (1.41x) | 7.9 -> 5.3 (1.50x) | 8.1 -> 6.5 (1.25x) | 10.4 -> 7.5 (1.40x) | 10.6 -> 7.6 (1.39x) | 16.2 -> 10.2 (1.58x) | 24.8 -> 15.6 (1.59x) | 43.4 -> 31.2 (1.39x) |

| shared down TP4 (5120x576) | 4.7 -> 2.8 (1.64x) | 4.6 -> 2.7 (1.68x) | 5.3 -> 3.4 (1.57x) | 5.8 -> 3.7 (1.58x) | 8.0 -> 4.3 (1.86x) | 8.7 -> 4.3 (1.99x) | 9.9 -> 5.7 (1.72x) | 9.8 -> 7.9 (1.25x) | 14.8 -> 15.1 (0.98x) |

**This PR vs ROCm/aiter#5750** at its latest head (`0dbc6c98e4`, with its
fused split-K and tuned DSv4.1 configs, and compact 32x32 scales). Values
are aiter time ÷ this PR time, so above 1 means this PR is faster:

| shape (N x K) | M=2 | M=16 | M=48 | M=96 | M=160 | M=192 | M=384 | M=768 | M=2048 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| wo_b TP2 (5120x4096) | 1.04 | 1.01 | 1.06 | 1.04 | 1.02 | 0.98 | 1.06 | 1.05 | 1.07 |
| wo_b TP4 (5120x2048) | 1.00 | 1.09 | 1.09 | 1.17 | 1.16 | 1.17 | 1.10 | 1.10 | 1.14 |
| shared gate_up TP2 (2304x5120) | 1.04 | 1.06 | 1.22 | 1.09 | 1.25 | 1.25 | 1.01 | 1.02 | 1.00 |
| shared gate_up TP4 (1152x5120) | 1.00 | 1.05 | 1.13 | 1.27 | 1.19 | 1.18 | 1.13 | 1.01 | 1.03 |
| shared down TP2 (5120x1152) | 1.04 | 1.00 | 1.12 | 1.27 | 1.02 | 1.02 | 1.11 | 1.05 | 1.16 |

| over the 90 points | median | min | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| vs the current vLLM kernel | 1.49x | 0.98x | 2.37x |
| vs aiter#5750 | 1.07x | 0.95x | 1.27x |

- **vs the current kernel:** the one point below 1x is shared-expert `down`
  TP4 at M=2048 (14.8 vs 15.1 µs), where the current path is BF16
  hipBLASLt.
- **vs aiter:** three points are below 1x, the lowest being shared-expert
  `down` TP4 at M=2 (2.7 vs 2.8 µs).
- **Off-grid check:** 110 more points at M in {3, 12, 20, 40, 72, 110, 175,
  230, 300, 600, 1200} give the same 1.07x median against aiter. The
  lowest are 0.94x, at shared-expert `down` TP4 M=3 and `wo_b` TP2 M=1200.
- **Error:** the max relative error vs an fp32 reference is 1.67e-3 at
  every point, the same as the current kernel.

## End to end

This reproduces the InferenceX `dsv41flash_fp4_mi355x_vllm_mtp` agentic job
([run 35696055681](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/35696055681),
TP2 conc32). It uses the same server flags (DSpark x5, synthetic acceptance
3.51, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, cudagraph capture size 1024) and the
same aiperf client: `inferencex-agentx-mvp`, `cc-traces-weka-062126`, 10
warmup requests per lane, then a 3600 s window. The two servers ran side by
side on one node. The baseline is `main` `26f49e336a`, which includes
#58456.

| server (GPUs) | output tok/s | ITL avg / p50 / p90 (ms) | TTFT p50 (ms) | tok/s/user p50 | server TPOT avg (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` (4-5) | 984.7 | 14.24 / 11.09 / 23.03 | 938 | 90.1 | 13.57 |
| this PR (6-7) | 995.2 | 13.57 / 10.77 / 22.34 | 911 | 92.9 | 12.93 |
| **change** | **+1.1%** | **-4.7% / -2.9% / -3.0%** | **-2.8%** | **+3.1%** | **-4.8%** |

The acceptance rate is identical on both servers, so the gain comes from
faster steps: the per-step verify time drops from 47.1 ms to 45.7 ms.

- **Consistency:** an earlier run, before the rebase onto #58456, used two
  swapped server pairs. Both PR servers beat both `main` servers (TPOT
  -4.2%), so placement does not explain the gain.
- **Measured commit:** this run is at `3b46e2d306`, before the in-launch
  split-K and retune. That change only makes the kernels faster. Most of its
  gain is at small M, but at this run's decode batch (M=192) it speeds up
  `fused_wqa_wkv` by 12% and shared `gate_up` by 2-3%. So this number is
  conservative.

## Accuracy (GSM8K)

TP4, DSpark x5, the InferenceX `gsm8k.yaml` (5-shot, chat completions,
concurrency 128, `max_tokens=12288`, greedy), with the server flags of the
InferenceX `dsv41flash_fp4_mi355x_vllm_mtp` job.

| | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| baseline ([InferenceX run](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/35696055681/job/106807089723)) | 0.9727 +/- 0.0045 | 0.9735 +/- 0.0044 |
| this PR (`c3c00323dd`) | 0.9727 +/- 0.0045 | 0.9735 +/- 0.0044 |

The scores match the baseline exactly.

## Not a duplicate

- **#57857** (open) edits the same kernel for the same model. It masks the K
  tail of the existing per-row kernel so K=576 runs natively, and it adds
  `input_quant_key()` so `wq_b` and the indexer `wq_b` can share one
  pre-quantized activation. This PR instead keeps the checkpoint's 32x32
  scales and replaces the GEMM for them. It covers K=576 as well, at 4.3 µs
  vs the current 8.7 µs at M=192. The activation sharing is orthogonal and
  composes with this. Both touch `rocm_native.py`, so whichever lands second
  rebases.
- **ROCm/aiter#5750** (open) proposes the same idea as an AITER GEMM. This PR
  keeps the kernel in vLLM, so it does not depend on an AITER release, and
  it measures on par or faster at the V4.1 shapes (table above).
- **#48427 and #57760** re-quantize MXFP8 checkpoints to FP8 PTPC. That is a
  different trade-off: it changes the weights.

## Test Plan / Results

```
$ pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py -q    # MI355X
83 passed
$ pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py -q   # MI355X
95 passed
```

New tests:

- `test_rocm_mxfp8_linear_block32_matches_dequant_reference`: 7 V4.1 shapes
  at TP2/TP4, including K=576, and token counts covering the packed, tiled
  and split-K configs. The block scales must stay compact and the output
  must match an fp32 reference.
- `test_rocm_mxfp8_linear_keeps_per_row_scales`: per-row scales are not
  compacted.
- `test_rocm_mxfp8_block32_split_k_in_launch`: the in-launch split-K, tiled
  and packed, with K and M tails. It must match the reference and be
  bitwise repeatable.
- `test_rocm_mxfp8_block32_split_k_first_use_in_capture`: a first split-K
  launch inside a graph capture must fall back and stay correct.
- `test_rocm_mxfp8_wo_a_bmm` runs with both compact 32x32 and per-row
  `wo_a` scales.

The existing tests pass unchanged. `pre-commit run` (including mypy) is
clean.

title: [ROCm][CI] skip the ROCm MRV1 default where MRV1 cannot serve the config
body:
## Purpose

**Split out of #50519**, where the problem showed up. That PR adds a DSpark
FP8 config for DeepSeek-V4-Flash to the MI355 spec-decode evals, and the group
fails on it. The config comes along here because nothing already on `main`
asks for this combination, so without it there is nothing to exercise the fix.

**What it exposed.** On ROCm a few architectures default to the V1 model
runner because V2 is slower for them there. That default was applied before
anything asked whether V1 can serve the config, and DSpark exists only in V2,
so the two collided at startup:

> ValidationError: 1 validation error for VllmConfig
> Value error, Model Runner V1 does not support: dspark speculative decoding

The code path is entirely on `main`, and a plain `vllm serve` reproduces it
without either PR. #50519 does not introduce it; it is only the first config
to ask for the combination.

**The fix consults the predicate that already exists.**
`_get_v1_model_runner_unsupported_features` is what the later validation
raises on, so the default now asks it first. Reusing it rather than
special-casing DSpark keeps prefill context parallelism, DFlash2 drafts and
the rest under one rule.

The default is skipped, not inverted. The Triton and V2 feature checks still
run, so a config neither runner can serve lands on V1 and reports the same
error as before, and configs V1 does accept keep the V1 path unchanged. On
other platforms the block does not execute at all.

## Test Plan

`tests/test_config.py`, and the new eval on MI355X (gfx950, TP4) as the
spec-decode group runs it.

## Test Result

Both pass.

title: [Perf][DSA] Shard the decode indexer rows across TP ranks
body:
## Purpose

On CUDA, every tensor-parallel rank runs the sparse-attention (DSA) indexer on every decode row: paged MQA logits, DeepSeek-V4.1 candidate selection or mask, and top-k. Every rank ends up with the same indices. At long context this is a large part of the decode step.

This PR adds an opt-in, `VLLM_DSA_DECODE_INDEXER_ROW_SHARD=1`, that splits the decode rows across TP ranks:

- **Row assignment:** rank `r` scores the rows of requests `r, r + tp, r + 2·tp, …`. All of a request's rows stay on one rank, because the varlen `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` reads a request's KV once for all of its rows.
- **Metadata builder:** gathers each rank's rows, block-table rows and context lengths into persistent buffers and builds that rank's DeepGEMM schedule. The plan depends only on the padded row count, so CUDA graphs replay with the same buffers.
- **Indexer op:** scores the local rows, keeps DeepSeek-V4.1 candidate blocks rank-local, all-gathers the int32 top-k indices across TP ranks, and restores request order in `topk_indices_buffer`.
- **When it applies:** uniform decode batches with at least `VLLM_DSA_DECODE_INDEXER_ROW_SHARD_MIN_REQS` requests (default 8), on the varlen paged-logits path, without DCP/PCP or the sparse-logits indexer.

## Test Plan

**Serve.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4× B200. The only difference between main and this PR is `VLLM_DSA_DECODE_INDEXER_ROW_SHARD`: `0` behaves exactly like main, `1` is this PR.

```bash
VLLM_DSA_DECODE_INDEXER_ROW_SHARD=1 \
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1 \
VLLM_DISABLE_DSV4_MEGAMOE_SHARED_EXPERT_FUSION=0 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --served-model-name dsv41 --port 8008 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 512
```

**Benchmark.** AIPerf with the InferenceX AgentX traces: long-context, multi-turn agentic sessions with a mean input of ~135K tokens. 64 concurrent sessions, 1,200 s (the concurrency-128 runs use `--concurrency 128`):

```bash
aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp --url http://127.0.0.1:8008 \
  --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --endpoint-type chat --streaming --model dsv41 \
  --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-trust-remote-code \
  --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126 --num-dataset-entries 393 \
  --concurrency 64 --benchmark-duration 1200 --random-seed 42 \
  --trajectory-start-min-ratio 0.25 --trajectory-start-max-ratio 0.75 \
  --warmup-requests-per-lane 10 --trace-idle-gap-cap-seconds 300 --warmup-grace-period 1800 \
  --failed-request-threshold 0.10 --use-server-token-count --no-gpu-telemetry
```

Main and this PR ran at the same time on one 8× B200 node: one server on GPUs 0–3, the other on GPUs 4–7.

**Long-context benchmark (`vllm bench serve`).** 64 distinct 126,000-token random prefixes are sent once with 1 output token to fill the prefix cache. Each measured prompt is one of those prefixes (round-robin, so every wave of 64 requests reads 64 different KV histories) plus a fresh 2,000-token random suffix: 128,000 input tokens with 98.4% prefix reuse, 1,024 output tokens, concurrency 64. Both files use the `custom` dataset format, one `{"prompt": ..., "output_tokens": ...}` per line. Main and this PR again ran side by side on one node.

```bash
# 1. Warm the 64 prefixes
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model dsv41 --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8008 --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --dataset-name custom --dataset-path warm.jsonl --custom-output-len 1 --skip-chat-template --disable-shuffle \
  --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 16 --ignore-eos --seed 0 --temperature 0

# 2. Measure: prefix + fresh 2,000-token suffix
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model dsv41 --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8008 --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --dataset-name custom --dataset-path measure.jsonl --custom-output-len 1024 --skip-chat-template --disable-shuffle \
  --num-prompts 512 --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos --seed 0 --temperature 0 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
```

**Unit test.**

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_decode_row_shard.py
```

## Test Results

AgentX, concurrency 64, 1,200 s. Two runs with main and this PR on swapped GPU groups:

| metric | main (run 1) | this PR (run 1) | main (run 2) | this PR (run 2) | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 2,411.6 | 2,508.8 | 2,408.7 | 2,501.1 | **+3.9%** |
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 321,158 | 337,083 | 322,167 | 335,165 | **+4.5%** |
| Request throughput (req/s) | 2.38 | 2.46 | 2.38 | 2.45 | +3.2% |
| TTFT avg / p50 (ms) | 398 / 197 | 368 / 199 | 337 / 198 | 364 / 195 | −0.4% / −0.4% |
| ITL avg / p50 / p90 (ms) | 11.85 / 10.94 / 16.87 | 10.62 / 9.47 / 15.56 | 11.78 / 10.96 / 17.26 | 10.53 / 9.50 / 15.51 | **−10.5% / −13.4% / −9.0%** |
| Output tok/s per user (avg) | 101.6 | 111.7 | 102.3 | 112.3 | +9.9% |

Run 1: main on GPUs 0–3, this PR on GPUs 4–7. Run 2: swapped. Change = mean of the two runs.

AgentX, concurrency 128, 1,200 s. Same two-run layout:

| metric | main (run 1) | this PR (run 1) | main (run 2) | this PR (run 2) | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 3,359.7 | 3,422.4 | 3,354.7 | 3,394.2 | +1.5% |
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 354,405 | 352,926 | 344,214 | 351,535 | +0.9% |
| Request throughput (req/s) | 3.86 | 3.87 | 3.79 | 3.84 | +0.8% |
| TTFT avg / p50 (ms) | 542 / 316 | 545 / 313 | 552 / 334 | 541 / 322 | −0.8% / −2.3% |
| ITL avg / p50 / p90 (ms) | 34.84 / 37.72 / 47.80 | 34.63 / 38.08 / 47.98 | 36.22 / 39.49 / 51.09 | 34.93 / 38.44 / 48.04 | −2.1% / −0.9% / −2.8% |
| Output tok/s per user (avg) | 39.3 | 40.0 | 37.9 | 39.4 | +2.8% |

At concurrency 128 the gain is small: each step carries far more prefill work (ITL ~35 ms vs ~11 ms at concurrency 64), so the decode indexer is a smaller share of the step.

Long-context prefix reuse (`vllm bench serve`), 128,000 input / 1,024 output tokens, concurrency 64, 512 prompts. Same two-run layout:

| metric | main (run 1) | this PR (run 1) | main (run 2) | this PR (run 2) | change (run 1 / run 2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 5,279.8 | 5,701.9 | 7,461.8 | 7,813.3 | +8.0% / **+4.7%** |
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 665,256 | 718,443 | 940,192 | 984,476 | +8.0% / **+4.7%** |
| Request throughput (req/s) | 5.16 | 5.57 | 7.29 | 7.63 | +8.0% / +4.7% |
| TTFT mean (ms) | 2,693 | 2,919 | 1,491 | 1,450 | +8.4% / −2.8% |
| TTFT p50 (ms) | 1,181 | 1,409 | 1,286 | 1,321 | +19.3% / +2.8% |
| TPOT mean (ms) | 9.18 | 8.08 | 6.83 | 6.35 | −11.9% / −7.0% |
| ITL p50 (ms) | 24.41 | 20.97 | 24.42 | 21.09 | **−14.1% / −13.7%** |
| Speculative acceptance length | 5.72 | 5.76 | 5.76 | 5.70 | |

Run 1: main on GPUs 0–3, this PR on GPUs 4–7. Run 2: swapped. The prefix-cache hit rate was 98.4% on every server. Run 1 was the first run in a new container, and both arms were about 30% slower than in run 2 (most likely first-use kernel compilation), so run 2 is the steadier comparison. ITL p50, about one decode step, drops 14% in both runs. Throughput gains less because about half of each request's time is spent in steps that also carry prefill, which this PR does not change.

GSM8K accuracy (main vs this PR): to be added.
