title: [RFC]: KV cache grouping for hybrid models with speculative drafters
body:
**Status:** Draft · **PRs:** #58207 (group size), #58380 (prefer `BLHNC`, stacked on #58207)

## TL;DR

Speculative drafters on hybrid models add a small KV cache bucket of their own, which breaks vLLM's KV cache grouping heuristic in two ways:

- **Too many groups (Qwen3.5 / 3.6 + DFlash):** a one-layer drafter bucket forces **one group per layer**: Qwen3.5-27B goes from 4 to 70 groups (#49730), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B from 4 to 46. Each group rebuilds attention metadata every step, so DFlash loses much of its speedup; forcing fewer groups today costs KV cache capacity.
- **Full attention padding (MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash):** the 5-layer drafter bucket sets the group size, which doesn't divide the target's 9 full attention layers, so a full attention padding layer is allocated for the whole context (#58175). Kimi-K3 + DSpark has the same problem: its 5-layer drafter bucket pads the 24 MLA (full attention) layers, with 20 groups.

Checked and unaffected (identical grouping with and without these PRs): GLM-5.3-Flash + DFlash2, MiniMax-M3 + DSpark, DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSpark.

A two-part proposal fixes both:

| part | problem | fix | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash | MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1 · #58207** | small drafter buckets force per-layer KV groups, or full attn padding | pick the group size by worst-case padding **bytes**; `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` (default 3) | 46 → **17** groups, **+54%** tok/s @c=1, **+36%** @c=32 | 11 → **7** groups, no full attn padding, KV capacity 5.76M → 5.96M |
| **2 · #58380** | `LBHNC` forces padding when drafter bytes/token ≠ target's | prefer `BLHNC` when the backends can run it and it avoids full attn padding or needs fewer groups | **5** groups, no padding, 7.53M tokens (> main's 7.42M); Triton only today | stays `LBHNC` at 7 groups (`BLHNC` would need 12 and has no full attn padding to remove) |

The parts are complementary: part 2 picks the path; part 1 is the fallback path (§5).

---

## 1. Background

**Motivation.** Enabling DFlash on Qwen3.5-27B raises the number of KV cache groups from 4 to **70**. Without a drafter, its 64 layers (48 GDN + 16 full attention) form 4 groups of 16; with DFlash, every layer gets its own group (64 target + 6 drafter). The drafter adds a one-layer full attention bucket, and the grouping heuristic falls back to one group per layer (#49730). Every group rebuilds its attention metadata each step, and GDN (linear attention) metadata builders are expensive, so this becomes per-step host overhead and DFlash runs well below its expected speedup; the effect is larger on Qwen3.5-4B. Forcing a larger group size recovers the throughput but, with today's grouping, costs KV cache capacity.

A drafter can also cost KV cache capacity rather than speed. MiMo-V2.5 + its DFlash drafter has buckets `[9 full, 39 SW, 5 drafter SW]`: the drafter bucket is the smallest, so the group size becomes 5, and the 9 full attention layers get a padding layer that grows with context (#58175 reports ~10% more KV capacity once it's removed). Kimi-K3 + its DSpark drafter behaves the same way (Case 3).

Related reports:

| report | model | groups | effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| #49730 | Qwen3.5-27B / 4B + DFlash (H100) | 4 without DFlash → 70 with (one per layer) | DFlash ITL much slower than expected; forcing gs=16 recovers ~10% tok/s on 27B but shrinks KV capacity 216k → 141k tokens |
| #51742 | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash (H200) | 46 | `build_attn_metadata` ~31 ms/step vs ~6 ms at 10 groups; output tok/s ~2× at c=1 with fewer groups |
| #52297 | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash | — | one GDN `build()` takes ~900 µs and is repeated per group |
| #58175 | MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash | 11 | 1 full attn padding layer; removing it gives +10.57% KV capacity (their setup); +8.4% in ours (5.76M → 6.25M) |
| this RFC | Kimi-K3 + DSpark (`RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-speculator.dspark`, TP4) | 20 | 1 MLA (full attn) padding layer; #58207: 17 groups, no MLA padding, +0.37% KV capacity |
| #42505, #46462 | Qwen3.5 / 3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash | — | DFlash slower than expected / than baseline at higher concurrency; not root-caused, likely related |

This RFC's own measurement (§4.1): Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash on B300 goes from 460 → 733 tok/s at c=1 when the 46 groups drop to 17.

### 1.0 Terms

| term | meaning |
|---|---|
| bucket | all layers whose KV cache specs merge (same attention type and shape) |
| group / `group_size` (gs) | a KV cache group shares one block table; buckets are split into groups of `group_size` layers |
| page | one layer's slice of a block; its size is that layer's bytes/token × block size |
| padding | layer slots in a group with no layer behind them; allocated but never written |
| manager vs kernel block | the KV manager allocates *manager* blocks; attention kernels may need them split into smaller *kernel* blocks |
| `LBHNC` | layer-outermost `KVCacheLayout` (today's default): every page is resized to one size, each group gets `group_size` pages per block |
| `BLHNC` | block-outermost `KVCacheLayout`: a block is one contiguous run of per-layer pages, so pages of different sizes share a block. `LBNHC`/`BLNHC` group the same way as `LBHNC`/`BLHNC` |

### 1.1 Buckets, groups, padding

```
Legend:  F/f = target/DRAFTER full attn   S/s = target/DRAFTER sliding window   M = mamba/GDN
         ▓ = full attn padding (grows with context, up to max_model_len)
         ░ = SW / mamba padding or idle page (bounded by window / state)

drafter full-attn group, group_size = 5 (one physical block):
│ f │ ▓ │ ▓ │ ▓ │ ▓ │   4 of 5 pages never written

every group's block has the same byte size (block IDs are shared across groups)
```

| cost | grows with | note |
|---|---|---|
| per-step metadata | # groups | one block table + builder call per group; GDN builders are expensive |
| KV capacity | padded slots × bytes/request | full attn slot: up to `max_model_len` tokens; SW / mamba slot: bounded |

### 1.2 Bad cases

```python
group_size = min(bucket sizes)                       # main
if max(bucket sizes) < 1.5 * min(bucket sizes):
    group_size = max(bucket sizes)
```

The heuristic sizes groups from bucket **counts** only. A drafter adds a small bucket of its own, which breaks it in the ways below. Each group is drawn as `[ ]` with one letter per layer slot.

#### Case 1: Qwen3.5 / 3.6 + DFlash: a one-layer drafter bucket forces one group per layer

Qwen3.5-27B + DFlash (4 → 70 groups), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash (4 → 46), Qwen3.5-35B-A3B + Eagle3 (4 → 41). Per-step metadata overhead grows with the layer count.

```
Qwen3.6 alone:     buckets [30 M, 10 F]              gs = 10  →  4 groups
Qwen3.6 + DFlash:  buckets [30 M, 10 F, 5 s, 1 f]    gs = min(30, 10, 5, 1) = 1

bucket                   layers   groups on main (one layer each)
target mamba/GDN    M      30     [M][M][M][M][M][M][M][M][M][M] … [M]   30
target full attn    F      10     [F][F][F][F][F][F][F][F][F][F]         10
drafter SW          s       5     [s][s][s][s][s]                         5
drafter full attn   f       1     [f]   ← smallest bucket sets gs = 1     1
                                                                        ────
                                        metadata builds per step:        46
```

With #58207: Qwen3.6 + DFlash 17 groups, Qwen3.5 + Eagle3 9 groups.

#### Case 2: MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash: the drafter's bucket doesn't divide the target's

MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash. The 5-layer drafter bucket is the smallest, so it sets gs=5, and the 9 full attention layers get a padding slot that grows with context.

Why full attention padding is the one that matters: a padding slot costs whatever a real layer of that type would hold for each request.

| padding slot | holds per request | MiMo-V2.5, per slot |
|---|---|---|
| full attention | every token of the context | 2.5 KiB/token × 256k tokens ≈ **640 MiB** (≈ 2.5 GiB at 1M) |
| sliding window | only the window (128 tokens), plus tokens in flight | 5 KiB/token × 128 ≈ **0.6 MiB** (≈ 41 MiB worst case with 8k in-flight tokens) |

So one full attention padding slot wastes as much as hundreds of sliding-window slots, and it keeps growing with context length.

```
main    gs = 5 → 11 groups
  F  [FFFFF][FFFF▓]              ← full attn padding
  S  [SSSSS] ×7 + [SSSS░]
  s  [sssss]

#58207  gs = 9 → 7 groups
  F  [FFFFFFFFF]                 ← no full attn padding
  S  [SSSSSSSS░] ×4 + [SSSSSSS░░]
  s  [sssss░░░░]
```

#### Case 3: Kimi-K3 + DSpark: same as Case 2, with MLA

Kimi-K3 has 69 KDA (linear attention) and 24 MLA (full attention) layers; the DSpark drafter (`RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-speculator.dspark`) adds 5 sliding-window layers. The drafter bucket sets gs=5, which doesn't divide 24, so an MLA padding slot is allocated for the whole context.

```
L = KDA (linear attention)

main    gs = 5 → 20 groups
  L  [LLLLL] ×13 + [LLLL░]
  F  [FFFFF] ×4 + [FFFF▓]        ← MLA (full attn) padding
  s  [sssss]

#58207  gs = 6 → 17 groups
  L  [LLLLLL] ×9 + [LLLLL░] ×3
  F  [FFFFFF] ×4                 ← no MLA padding
  s  [sssss░]
```

Served (Kimi-K3-pruned75, same 93 layers, TP4): KV capacity 4.76M → 4.78M tokens at 131k context. #58380 keeps `LBNHC` here.

---

## 2. Part 1 · #58207: group size by worst-case padding bytes

Replace the [min / 1.5×-max heuristic](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/b3a87b2d04e6439e2a1aef0cbf9ca65328076c86/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L1547-L1558) with a search over group sizes that minimizes **worst-case padding bytes** per request, bounded below so groups can't explode:

```python
lo = max(smallest bucket, min(min_kv_cache_group_layers, largest bucket))
group_size = argmin over gs in [lo, largest bucket] of
    (Σ padding_slots(bucket, gs) × spec.max_memory_usage_bytes(vllm_config), num_groups(gs))
```

Padding is costed in bytes, so full attention padding (which grows with `max_model_len`) is avoided in favor of bounded sliding-window / mamba padding. The lower bound keeps groups from exploding: never below the smallest bucket, and never below `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` (default 3), so a one-layer drafter bucket can't force one group per layer.

```
Qwen3.6 + DFlash, gs = 3 → 17 groups (each bucket padded independently)
  M  [MMM] ×10    F  [FFF][FFF][FF▓][FF▓]    s  [sss][ss░]    f  [f▓▓]
```

## 3. Part 2 · #58380: prefer `BLHNC`

In `BLHNC` a block is one contiguous run of per-layer pages, so pages of different sizes share a block instead of being padded to one size. The widest non-state bucket sets the block; mamba / SW groups split to fit it. #58380 prefers these layouts when specs have mixed page sizes **and** every backend runs each attention block unsplit, since packed blocks can't be split into smaller kernel blocks:

| backend (B300) | kernel block sizes | can use `BLHNC` |
|---|---|---|
| Triton | any multiple of 16 | yes |
| FlashInfer | 16 / 32 / 64 | no |
| FlashAttention hd256 (FA4) | 128 | no |

**`BLHNC` cost check:** `BLHNC` is not always better (MiMo below: 7 → 12 groups), so #58380 also computes both groupings from the specs and picks `BLHNC` only if the `LBHNC` grouping would pad full attention, or `BLHNC` needs fewer groups.

Each row below is a separate group; rows align because every block is the same size:

```
Qwen3.6 + DFlash: 5 groups, 12-page blocks
full-attn ×1   │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │   f   │   10 target + drafter (2 pages): no padding
mamba ×3       │ M │ M │ M │ M │ M │ M │ M │ M │ M │ M │ ░ │ ░ │   10 GDN states each, 2 idle pages
drafter sw ×1  │   s   │   s   │   s   │   s   │   s   │ ░ │ ░ │   5 layers × 2 pages, 2 idle pages

MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash under `BLHNC` (not picked by the cost check): 12 groups, 9-page blocks
full-attn ×1   │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │   9 full pages: no padding
SWA ×10        │   S   │   S   │   S   │   S   │ ░ │   4 layers × 2 pages, 1 idle page (one group has 3)
drafter SW ×1  │  d d d d d  (1.6 pages each)  │ ░ │   5 layers × 64 KiB = 8 pages, 1 idle page
```

## 4. Results by model and layout

### 4.1 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash (1× B300)

| plan | groups | padding / request @256k | KV capacity | tok/s c=1 / c=32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 46 | 0 | 7.42M | 460 / 4654 |
| #58207 | 17 | 3.05 GiB (full attn) | 5.19M | 733 / 6495 |
| **#58380** (Triton, `BLHNC`) | **5** | **58 MiB** | **7.53M** | **746 / 7463** |

### 4.2 MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash (TP2)

| plan | groups | padding / request @256k | KV capacity |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 11 | 726 MiB (incl. 1 full attn layer) | 5.76M |
| #58175 | 18 | **90 MiB** | **6.25M** |
| #58207 | **7** | 469 MiB | 5.96M |
| `BLHNC` (#58380 doesn't pick it) | 12 | 266 MiB | 6.10M |

Padding is worst case (8192 in-flight tokens). Full attn padding grows with context, so `BLHNC` wins outright for Qwen3.6; MiMo has none, so it's a trade between groups and bounded bytes.

### 4.3 Qwen3.6 + DFlash: `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` sweep

![min-kv-cache-group-layers sweep](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LucasWilkinson/vllm/af4013a3827d250b266c6e48b1fc124880523780/pareto_min_layers.png)

| `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` | gs | groups | KV capacity | padding/req @256k | c=1 | c=32 | with #52297 ² c=1 / c=32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (= main) | 1 | 46 | 7.42M | 0 | 460 | 4654 | 653 / 5735 |
| 2 | 2 | 24 | 6.42M | 1.02 GiB (+17%) | 684 | 5711 | 716 / 6247 |
| **3 (default)** | 3 | 17 | 5.19M | 3.02 GiB (+50%) | 710 | 6339 | 727 / 7100 |
| 4 | 5 | 10 | 4.80M | 4 GiB (+67%) | 726 | 6676 | 758 / 6865 |

² #52297 (open PR) computes GDN attention metadata once per step instead of per group, making extra groups cheaper.

### 4.4 Qwen3.6 + DFlash: `BLHNC` vs `LBHNC`

![BLHNC vs LBHNC](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LucasWilkinson/vllm/f52d0d4bb0b941fff5dbc5834f62d865db084188/pareto_packed.png)

## 5. How the two parts fit together

**Defaults after both PRs merge** (default backends, no `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT`). Padding is per request at 256k context (worst case, 8192 in-flight tokens):

| model (B300 backend) | main today | after #58207 + #58380 |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6 + DFlash (FlashInfer/FA) | `LBHNC`, 46 groups, no padding | `LBHNC`, **17** groups, 3.05 GiB padding (full attn) |
| Qwen3.6 + DFlash (`--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN`) | `LBHNC`, 46 groups, no padding | **`BLHNC`, 5** groups, 58 MiB padding |
| MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash (FA) | `LBHNC`, 11 groups, 726 MiB padding (640 MiB full attn) | `LBHNC`, **7** groups, 469 MiB padding (no full attn) |
| Kimi-K3 + DSpark (TP4) | `LBHNC`, 20 groups, 1 MLA padding layer | `LBHNC`, **17** groups, no MLA padding |
| MiMo-V2.6 + MTP (FA) | `LBHNC`, 6 groups, 203 MiB padding (SW) | unchanged |
| Qwen3.5 + Eagle3 (FlashInfer/FA) | `LBHNC`, 41 groups, no padding | `LBHNC`, 9 groups, 4 drafter full attn padding slots |
| GLM-5.3-Flash + DFlash2, MiniMax-M3 + DSpark, DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSpark | unchanged | unchanged |
| single page size (Gemma3, gpt-oss, Llama4, Qwen3.5, …) | unchanged | unchanged |

**Recommendation:** land #58207 first (helps every layout/backend), then #58380. `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT` / connector preferences still win.

---

## 6. Alternatives considered

Other open PRs that change this heuristic, and what each gives for Qwen3.6 + DFlash:

| PR | approach | Qwen3.6 + DFlash | shortcoming |
|---|---|---|---|
| #51742 | ignore one-layer buckets when taking the min | gs=5, 10 groups | pads the drafter's full attn layer with 4 slots that grow with context |
| #58175 | shrink gs to a divisor of the full attn bucket sizes (targets MiMo) | gs=1, 46 groups | doesn't help drafters |
| #49472 | minimize padding + number of groups, counted in layers | gs=5, 10 groups | a padded full attn layer counts the same as a sliding-window one, so it pads full attn |

Other approaches:

- **Bigger `block_size` for the lone drafter group** (same bytes, fewer layers): prefix-cache hits align to the LCM of group block sizes, so hits get ~5× coarser for every group.
- **Only forbid one layer per group (`group_size ≥ 2`) and minimize padding:** still 24 groups for Qwen3.6 + DFlash, and over-splits models with cheap padding (Gemma3-27B 7 → 31 groups).
- **Absolute cap on the number of groups:** the right cap depends on the backend (GDN vs FlashAttention metadata cost).
- **Drafter-aware sizing** (size groups from target buckets, pad the drafter): worst case when the drafter has a full attention layer, and drafter layers can only be identified heuristically at grouping time.
- **Separate KV pool for drafter layers:** removes the constraint entirely, but is a much larger allocator change.
- **#58345 (rescale sliding-window blocks for `BLHNC`):** on main (since #53007) sliding-window layers already use the full attention block size when the backend allows it (group block sizes 262144 ×3, 592, 592); when it doesn't, rescaling would need kernel-block splitting, which `BLHNC` can't do.

---

## 7. Open questions

1. **Default `--min-kv-cache-group-layers`:** 3 (17 groups, −30% KV capacity on Qwen3.6 + DFlash) or 4 (10 groups, +2–5% tok/s, −35%)? Should it depend on whether the model has GDN layers?
2. **`BLHNC` with FlashInfer / FlashAttention:** re-page inside the kernels (as #55219 / #57169 do for sparse MLA), or stop inflating the block size for block-outermost layouts (but then few GDN states fit per block)?
3. **FlashAttention drafter block size:** the 128-only FA4 hd256 kernel block is derived from the *target's* head size and applied to a hd128 drafter, causing `No common block size for 592` on main unless `--block-size 128` is set. Fixed separately by #58630.
4. **Validation:** #58380 switches mixed-page-size models to `BLHNC` when the cost check passes on capable backends; needs accuracy and throughput validation beyond DFlash and MiMo.

---

## 8. Methodology

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --max-num-seqs 32 --no-enable-prefix-caching --block-size 128 \
  --mamba-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 [--min-kv-cache-group-layers N] \
  [--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN] \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash","method":"dflash","num_speculative_tokens":7}'
vllm bench serve --model Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --dataset-name hf --dataset-path openai/gsm8k --hf-split test \
  --num-prompts max(32, 8*C) --max-concurrency C --num-warmups 2*C
```

| item | value |
|---|---|
| hardware | 1× B300 per run (MiMo: TP2, `max_model_len` 1M) |
| runs | single; noise ~2–3% (repeated gs=5) |
| interactivity | 1000 / p99 TPOT |
| acceptance length | 5.1–5.2 in all Qwen runs |
| `--block-size 128` | needed on all variants, including main: FlashAttention's 128-only FA4 hd256 kernel block is derived from the target's head size and also applied to the hd128 drafter, which otherwise fails with `No common block size for 592` |


---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to run the experiments and draft this RFC; I have reviewed its contents.

title: [Bug]: When using the V4 parser in vLLM to parse outputs from DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, the leading extra space in V4.1 DSML tags breaks state machine matching and parameter regex, filters arg deltas, and prevents streaming return of tool call arguments.
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug vLLM does not ship a dedicated parser for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and reuses the existing V4 parser to process model outputs generated by V4.1 Flash. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash introduces an extra leading space inside DSML tags compared to the V4 specification. This difference triggers multiple failures in the legacy V4 parser: 1. The state machine for DSML tag matching fails to recognize tags due to the unexpected leading space. 2. The hardcoded regular expressions used in `_dsml_arg_converter` cannot match the parameter content, as the regex patterns do not account for the leading space. 3. The argument delta filtering logic with `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")` buffers all delta content that does not contain the `>` character and suppresses incremental streaming delivery. As a combined result, tool call arguments cannot be streamed back to the caller. The proposed fix is to implement a new V4.1-specific parser inheriting from the V4 parser class: adjust tag definitions and regular expressions to accommodate the leading space, disable the arg delta filtering logic, and register the parser under an independent name. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [KVConnector][NIXL] Move remote region alignment into nixl utils
body:
## Purpose

**Stacked on #50499; land after it.** Both target `main`, so GitHub also lists #50499's commits. The change here is the last commit: [`488e5f7d6a...bab44092cf`](https://github.com/zixi-qi/vllm/compare/488e5f7d6af2819db8abf1fb74de06ed621b1cd6...bab44092cfd90b3f3cdd4bf8b462cca64dee3a72) (4 files, +143/−125).

Follows up on a [review note on #50499](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50499#discussion_r4098037609): `_align_remote_regions_by_layer` only transforms the remote `NixlAgentMetadata`, so it does not need to live on the worker.

- Move it to `nixl/utils.py` as `align_remote_regions_by_layer(meta, layer_names, local_region_indices, local_block_lens)`. It read exactly those three pieces of worker state, which are now passed explicitly.
- Add `select_remote_regions(meta, indices)`, which reindexes every per-region metadata list in one pass. Layer routing and the existing PP layer-window slice in `add_remote_agent` both use it, replacing two hand-written copies of the same seven-field reindexing.
- The packed-layout loop iterates `zip(..., strict=True)` instead of indexing three sequences by position.

No wire-format, registration, or transfer change; the validation checks and their messages are unchanged. One tightening: the PP layer-window slice now fails with "Remote region metadata lengths disagree" when a peer's per-region list length differs from its address list, where it previously truncated silently. Real peers always send equal lengths, since `register_kv_caches` asserts it.

Not a duplicate: no open PR moves or rewrites this function. Draft #56187 also builds on #50499 and changes this function under its earlier name; whichever lands second rebases onto the other.

## Test plan

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3 VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5700 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl*.py
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3 VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5700 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_output_aggregator.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_tp_mapping.py
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only 488e5f7d6a HEAD)
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files $(git diff --name-only 488e5f7d6a HEAD)
```

Existing alignment tests now call the utility through a small `_align` helper; one new test covers the tightened length check, including that a rejected peer's metadata is left unmodified.

## Test results

Head `bab44092cf` on `488e5f7d6a` (#50499 with `main` merged), four GB200s: 568 NIXL tests passed (2 ROCm-only skips) and 42 supporting tests passed; changed-file pre-commit and mypy 3.12 passed.

No model evaluation: the change moves code without changing registration or transfers. The E2E evidence for the packed MLA path (Gemma-4 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GSM8K) is in #50499.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude) was used for implementation, tests, and validation. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and is responsible for the change end to end.

title: [RFC]: Hardening /v1/messages (Anthropic API) for Claude Code across model families
body:
### Motivation

Claude Code can run against vLLM through the Anthropic Messages endpoint (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` → `/v1/messages`). Claude Code's agentic loop is a demanding client of that endpoint:

- It sends every request with ~25 tools, many with large nested JSON schemas.
- It uses interleaved thinking with parallel tool calls.
- It sends inline `role: "system"` messages that change every turn.
- It sends side queries (title generation, the auto-mode permission classifier) with `stop_sequences` and small `max_tokens` budgets.
- It recovers from context overflow based on the error it gets back.

This issue audits the current converter (`vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/`) and the HF chat templates of the major open model families against real Claude Code traffic. We found:

- several gaps that affect every model family;
- a set of model-specific breakages, some of which return **400 on Claude Code's default requests**.

Many of the small fixes already have open PRs, often more than one per problem. This issue gathers them so they can be deduplicated and prioritized, and it proposes the pieces that have no owner yet.

**How we checked**

- We captured `/v1/messages` traffic from Claude Code 2.1.281 through a logging proxy (~50 requests covering main-loop turns, title generation and the auto-mode classifier).
- We replayed synthetic Claude Code-shaped conversations through `AnthropicServingMessages.to_chat_completion_request` → `chat_utils` post-processing.
- We rendered the result with the current HF templates, and with `mistral_common` / the DeepSeek Python encoders / Harmony where applicable.

Items marked *(unverified)* were not reproduced at runtime.

**Observed request shape (from captures)**

| Field | Values seen |
|---|---|
| `system` | List of text blocks with `cache_control`. The first is the `x-anthropic-billing-header` line. |
| `messages` | Contains inline `role: "system"` messages at non-leading positions (e.g. a `<total_tokens>` update each turn). |
| `thinking` | `{"type":"adaptive"}`, `{"type":"adaptive","display":"omitted"}`, `{"type":"enabled"}`, `{"type":"disabled"}`, or absent |
| `output_config` | `{"effort":"high"}`; title generation adds `format: json_schema` |
| `context_management` | `{"edits":[{"type":"clear_thinking_20251015","keep":"all"}]}` |
| `max_tokens` | `32000` (main loop), `2112` (classifier, `stop_sequences: ["</block>"]`), `64` (stage-1 classifier, `stop_sequences: ["</severity>"]`) |
| `tool_result` | `is_error` is set on most results. Content is a string or a list of text/image blocks. User turns often carry extra text blocks (system reminders) after the tool results. |

---

### Part 1: Converter / API gaps (all models)

| # | Gap | Location | Impact | Existing work |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Inline system messages are always hoisted into the leading system prompt.** `_detect_merge_inline_system` is called with the CLI `--chat-template` value, which is `None` by default, so it returns `True` for every deployment that uses the model's own template. Claude Code sends a changing inline system message every turn, so the leading system text changes every request. | `serving.py:142,152,248-257` | **Prefix cache misses on the whole conversation, every turn.** Also changes semantics: mid-conversation instructions become part of the global system prompt. | #53393, #48874, #41114, #46710; PRs #53501, #56520, #52978, #47681 (competing approaches) |
| 2 | **The `thinking` request field is silently dropped.** `AnthropicMessagesRequest` has no `thinking` field and pydantic ignores extras. `output_config.effort` → `reasoning_effort` then forces `enable_thinking=True` (`chat_completion/protocol.py:585`). Anthropic's default when `thinking` is absent is *off*, but we use the template default, which is usually *on*. | `protocol.py:121` | Side queries (title generation, classifier) reason and spend their `max_tokens` budget before answering. `display: "omitted"` is ignored. | PRs #58613, #53058 |
| 3 | **Stop strings are matched against reasoning text.** `check_stop_strings` runs over the full detokenized output. | `v1/engine/detokenizer.py:130` | The classifier's `</block>` / `</severity>` can match inside `<think>` and end the request with no verdict. | #51669 (related) |
| 4 | **Context-overflow errors are not in Anthropic's format.** vLLM returns "This model's maximum context length is …". Claude Code decides whether to auto-compact or retry with a smaller `max_tokens` based on Anthropic's context-limit error messages *(exact strings unverified)*. Claude Code always sends `max_tokens=32000`, so a 128k-context deployment rejects prompts once they pass ~99k tokens. | `renderers/params.py:357,499` | Long sessions fail hard instead of compacting. | none found |
| 5 | **Unknown content-block types reject the whole request (422).** `AnthropicContentBlock.type` is a closed `Literal`. `document` (PDFs from the Read tool), `search_result`, `tool_addition` / `tool_removal` and server-tool blocks all fail. Once one is in the history, every later request in the session fails. | `protocol.py:41` | Session becomes unrecoverable. | #57324, #46790; PRs #45653, #57693, #46797, #47747, #47877 |
| 6 | **Images in a `tool_result` become a separate `user` message** inserted between tool messages. | `serving.py:445-455` | Gemma 4 silently drops later tool results. Mistral returns 400 (`Unexpected role 'tool' after role 'user'`). DeepSeek-V3.2 raises. MiniMax-M3 and Gemma 4 could render the image inside the tool message natively. | none found |
| 7 | **`tool_reference` produces an extra tool message, and the first one is empty.** | `serving.py:457-465` | 400 on Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 (`Unexpected item type in content`) and DeepSeek-V3.2 (`No tool calls but found tool output`). Python repr rendered on MiniMax. | #52489; PRs #52498, #52610 |
| 8 | **User text after `tool_result`s in the same turn becomes a separate trailing `user` message.** Templates that keep reasoning only after the last user message then drop the current tool loop's reasoning. | `serving.py:306` | Interleaved thinking lost mid-loop on GLM-4.7/5/5.1/5.2, Qwen3.5/3.6, MiniMax-M2.x and DeepSeek-V3.2. | none found |
| 9 | **`is_error` on `tool_result` is dropped.** | `serving.py:408-445` | The model cannot tell failed tool calls from successful ones. | none found |
| 10 | **System blocks are joined with `""`.** | `serving.py:257` | Prompt text runs together, e.g. `…for Claude.You are…`. | none found |
| 11 | **Malformed tool-call arguments crash non-streaming** (`json.loads` → 500). | `serving.py` (`messages_full_converter`) | Hard failure on a single bad generation. | PRs #57244, #52519 |
| 12 | **Error envelopes and types don't match Anthropic's.** FastAPI 422s are not wrapped in Anthropic's error format. Stream errors use `internal_error` instead of `api_error` / `overloaded_error`. Mid-stream upstream errors are replaced with "Invalid data format received". | `api_router.py`, `serving.py` | Client retry/backoff logic doesn't fire correctly. | PRs #58023, #46162 |
| 13 | **`x-api-key` is not accepted** by `--api-key` auth. | `serve/middleware/authenticate.py` | Requires `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` instead of `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. | PRs #51675, #51588 |
| 14 | **No `ping` or early `message_start` during long prefills** (100k+ token prompts). | `serving.py` (`message_stream_converter`) | Idle-timeout risk through proxies and load balancers *(unverified)*. | none found |
| 15 | **Tool-call id collisions/format.** vLLM-generated ids are reused across turns for some parsers (e.g. Kimi `functions.X:0`). | | See Kimi below. | PR #35667 |

---

### Part 2: Model / template-specific findings

The common thread: every family uses **different names and values** for thinking and effort. Examples: `enable_thinking`, `thinking`, `thinking_mode`, `low_effort`, `thinking_budget`, and effort sets such as `{low,high}`, `{none,high}` or `{xhigh,medium,low}`. Passing `output_config.effort` straight through as `reasoning_effort` therefore gives inconsistent behavior, and 400s on several families.

| Family | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Qwen3.8** (27B, Flash-Next, 2.4T) | The template raises `Unexpected reasoning effort high. Supported types are xhigh (default), medium, and low.` Claude Code sends `high` by default, so **every default Claude Code request returns 400**. 2.4T also raises `Disabling thinking is not supported.` | confirmed |
| **Qwen3.5 / 3.6** | Keep reasoning only after the last user message (item 8). 3.6 supports `preserve_thinking`, which vLLM never sets. The system-first guard is hidden only by item 1. | confirmed |
| **Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Coder** | Historical arguments rendered with `\| string` produce Python `True`. Qwen3-Coder renders nested `anyOf` lossily. | confirmed (template-side) |
| **GLM-5.2 / 5.3** | Effort is mapped as `'high' if effort == 'high' else 'max'` (5.2), or only `{low,high}` is recognized (5.3), so `low`/`medium` become **Max**. 5.3 cannot disable thinking: the generation prompt is always `<think>`. `glm47_moe` parser switches to content-only when `enable_thinking=False`, so a naive disabled-thinking mapping would leak reasoning into `content`. | confirmed |
| **MiniMax-M3** | The template's `thinking_mode` (`enabled`/`disabled`/`adaptive`) maps 1:1 to Anthropic `thinking.type`, but vLLM never sets it. The template has no branch for non-leading system messages, so they are silently dropped once item 1 is fixed. | confirmed |
| **MiniMax-M2.x** | Reasoning is dropped before the last user message (item 8). | confirmed |
| **DeepSeek-V3.1** | The stock HF template does `'<｜tool▁sep｜>' + arguments`, but `chat_utils` has already turned arguments into a dict, so rendering raises `TypeError` on any history containing a tool call. It also never renders `tools`. Workaround: `examples/tool_chat_template_deepseekv31.jinja`. | confirmed |
| **DeepSeek-V3.2** (encoder) | `drop_thinking = messages[-1]["role"] == "user"` drops the current loop's reasoning (item 8). The strict tool-ordering check breaks on items 6 and 7. A non-merged inline system message has no role token and lands inside `<think>`. | confirmed |
| **DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1** | V4 is fine. V4.1 raises on `effort: "medium"` (accepts low/high/xhigh/max). | confirmed |
| **Kimi K2-Thinking / K2.5 / K2.6** | The template renders only the tool-call **id**, never the tool name (`<\|tool_call_begin\|>{{ id }}`). Any id not generated by Kimi on vLLM (`toolu_…`, `chatcmpl-tool-…`, after `/model` or a resumed session) loses the tool name. Thinking uses `thinking`, not `enable_thinking`. | confirmed |
| **Kimi K3** | Only low/high/max effort are accepted, so `medium` / `xhigh` return 400. Tool-result matching is robust to foreign ids. | confirmed |
| **gpt-oss (Harmony)** | `max` / `xhigh` effort raise. Reasoning cannot be disabled. Images are dropped. Each inline system message becomes a new developer message. JSON Schema → TypeScript is lossy: `anyOf`+enum, `allOf`, `$ref` and `const` become `any`, and `additionalProperties` maps become `{}` (affects Claude Code's `AskUserQuestion` / `Workflow` tools). | confirmed |
| **Mistral / Devstral** | `validate_request_params` allows only `{none, high}` effort, so Claude Code's other values return 400. Devstral-Small-2 and Devstral-2 raise `think tokens are not available for this tokenizer` whenever the history contains a thinking block. `truncate_tool_call_ids` works but logs a WARNING per historical tool call on every request. | confirmed |
| **Gemma 4** | Later tool results are lost when a user message is inserted (item 6). The template renders `anyOf` as an empty type, renders enums only for strings, and renders map-typed objects as fake properties (hits `AskUserQuestion`). | confirmed |
| **Nemotron v3** | The template reads `low_effort`, which vLLM never sets, so effort has no effect. Thinking cannot be disabled via the Anthropic API. | confirmed |
| **Seed-OSS** | Thinking is controlled only by `thinking_budget` (default unlimited). The default tool rendering is Python signatures that drop nested types and enums; `use_json_tooldef` fixes this but is off by default. Historical arguments use Python repr. | confirmed |

---

### Proposed Change

Suggested priority order:

1. **Per-model thinking/effort mapping layer.** Map Anthropic `thinking.type` (+ `budget_tokens`) and `output_config.effort` onto each model's native switch (`enable_thinking`, `thinking`, `thinking_mode`, `low_effort`, `thinking_budget`) and clamp to the levels that model accepts. Treat absent `thinking` as disabled only where the model can actually disable it. This extends #58613 and #52738, and removes most of the 400s above.
2. **Inline system handling that preserves the prefix.** Keep inline system messages in place, or fold them into the adjacent user turn when the template requires system-first (as proposed in #53393). Never hoist them into the leading system block. Detect the template requirement against the *resolved* tokenizer template, not the CLI flag.
3. **Converter structure fixes.**
   - Keep tool-result images inside the `tool` message.
   - Emit one merged user message per Anthropic user turn, so the trailing text doesn't cut off reasoning.
   - Mark `is_error` (e.g. an `Error:` prefix).
   - Join system blocks with `\n\n`.
   - Emit a single `tool_reference` message.
4. **Error compatibility.**
   - Translate context-overflow errors to Anthropic's messages so Claude Code can auto-compact or reduce `max_tokens`.
   - Degrade unknown content blocks to text instead of failing with 422.
   - Use Anthropic error types and envelopes throughout.
5. **Model-specific fixes.**
   - Rewrite Kimi tool-call ids to `functions.{name}:{idx}`.
   - Drop historical reasoning for Mistral tokenizers without `[THINK]`.
   - Add a schema-normalization pass (flatten `anyOf`/`$ref`) for Harmony, Gemma 4 and Seed-OSS.
   - Evaluate stop strings against content only, not reasoning.
6. **Regression coverage.** Add a small Claude Code-shaped fixture (captured request shapes, no user content) to `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/`, rendered through the converter for each supported template family.

### Feedback Period

~2 weeks.

### CC List

_No response_

### Any Other Things

AI assistance was used for this investigation (Claude Code): it analyzed the captured traffic, read the converter code and rendered templates across model families. File/line references are against `main` at e33de821c0.

title: [ROCm][CI] Mirror split kernel groups on MI355 and fix exposed tests
body:
- Add MI355 mirrors and matching native AMD jobs for mHC, FLA Ops, and Miscellaneous Kernels.
- Preserve the existing exclusions and supported AMD coverage across 32 test files; NVIDIA commands are unchanged.
- Fix two DeepSeek-V4.1 CSA2 assertions to compare the query in its required `[tokens, heads, head_dim]` shape.
- Read logical k-pool K and scale bytes through the platform cache layout in the writer-parity and rejected-draft tests.

[#50519](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50519) established AMD coverage for the miscellaneous-kernel group, and [#58609](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58609) split the NVIDIA workload into three named jobs. Both prerequisites have merged. This PR replaces the old AMD catch-all with those groups and avoids duplicate execution.

The new MI355 Miscellaneous Kernels mirror exposed three existing test failures in [Buildkite build 91691](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91691/list?jid=01a0ea7b-3ae4-4234-823b-60187d02526a&tab=output); the same three failed in both attempts while 1,130 other tests passed. Two CSA2 tests compared the returned `[19, 1, 512]` query with a flat `[19, 512]` fixture, although the three-dimensional shape is required by attention. The k-pool test read contiguous bytes even though ROCm preshuffles K; its pool-1 slice contained none of that pool's K bytes. Reading the correct offsets showed 122 of 128 pool-1 K bytes differed from the reference, confirming the one-pool ring check. The production kernels are unchanged.

OpenAI Codex assisted with the implementation and local validation.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Fix index_kpool handling in FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA
body:
## 1. Root cause

The FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA builder incorrectly used the main MLA cache's
`tokens_per_state` as the sparse indexer's `index_kpool`. These values describe
different layouts: GLM-5.3-Flash stores one main MLA cache state per token
(`tokens_per_state=1`), while its sparse indexer pools every four tokens
(`index_kpool=4`).

For example, with `index_topk=2048` and a context length of 2051, the indexer
produces 2048 selected token slots plus three tokens from the incomplete trailing
pool. The correct valid length is:

```text
2048 + 2051 % 4 = 2051
```

The old code instead calculated:

```text
2048 + 2051 % 1 = 2048
```

The three trailing slots were generated correctly but excluded from the length
passed to FlashInfer, so the kernel did not attend to them. Once the context
exceeds 2048, this can omit one to three recent tokens on three out of every four
decoding steps.

GSM8K did not expose the issue because every evaluated request stayed below 2048
tokens. In GPQA, it repeatedly trigges the incorrect length calculation.

## 2. Fix

Read `index_kpool` from the model configuration. Models without an `index_kpool`
value fall back to `1`, representing no pooling:

```python
index_kpool = getattr(hf_config, "index_kpool", None)
self._index_kpool = 1 if index_kpool is None else int(index_kpool)
```

## 3. Test results

All evaluations used GLM-5.3-Flash native FP8 weights, BF16 KV cache, TP8, no
speculative decoding, on H200.

| Status | Backend | GSM8K | GPQA Diamond |
|:---|:---|---:|---:|
| Before | FlashInfer SM90 | 1238/1319 (0.9386) | 108/198 (0.5455) |
| Before | FlashAttention Sparse | 1238/1319 (0.9386) | 148/198 (0.7475) |
| Before | FlashMLA Sparse | 1234/1319 (0.9356) | 143/198 (0.7222) |
| After | FlashInfer SM90 | 1237/1319 (0.9378) | 151/198 (0.7626) |

title: [Bug]: Rust frontend: top_logprobs repeats the sampled token; prompt + max_tokens over max_model_len silently accepted
body:
### Your current environment

- `vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv41-flash-0909` (vLLM `0.1.dev20904+g179dd0fa9`, `vllm-rs` of the same build), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8 on 8× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120).
- Flags: `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --max-model-len 131072`.
- `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`. The same engine with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0` is the control.
- Each check ran twice on each frontend; every result reproduced.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The Rust frontend differs silently from the Python frontend in two places. Both return HTTP 200, so clients cannot tell.

**1. `top_logprobs` repeats the sampled token.** `logprobs: true, top_logprobs: 3`, greedy:

```
Rust:   top_logprobs = [Red -0.000267, Red -0.000267, Here -8.75]
Python: top_logprobs = [Red -0.000272, Here -9.125, Three -9.50]
```

The sampled token's entry seems to be prepended to the engine's top-k list without de-duplication. The list therefore holds k-1 distinct alternatives, and the sampled token is counted twice.

**2. Requests over the context budget are accepted.** Two requests against `max_model_len 131072`:
- a 123,454-token prompt with `max_tokens: 8192`;
- a short prompt with `max_tokens: 200000`.

Rust returns 200 and silently clamps the output budget. Python returns 400 `This model's maximum context length is 131072 tokens. However, you requested 8192 output tokens and your prompt contains at least …`. With Rust, clients get a shorter completion than requested and no error. A prompt that alone exceeds the limit (134k tokens) is rejected with 400 on both frontends.

Also noted, documented rather than a bug: `n > 1` → 400 `Only n=1 is supported.` on Rust; Python returns n choices.

### Expected

Match the Python frontend: de-duplicate `top_logprobs` (or not prepend the sampled token when it is already in the top-k), and reject `prompt_tokens + max_tokens > max_model_len` with the same 400.

title: [Bugfix][DeepGEMM] Restore SM12x alignment behavior for grouped GEMMs
body:
## Fixes

Fixes #58624

## Problem

On SM12x (GB200, GB10, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell), DeepGEMM's `get_theoretical_mk_alignment_for_contiguous_layout` returns alignment 128 regardless of per-expert M. DeepGEMM 2.6.1 returned alignment 64 when each expert gets at most 64 rows, which is significantly faster for decode-shaped batch sizes.

This causes ~15% decode throughput regression since #56876 moved to DeepGEMM `e1f418c`.

## Solution

Add an SM12x-specific override in `get_theoretical_mk_alignment_for_contiguous_layout` that computes per_group_m and returns alignment 64 when per_group_m <= 64, matching the pre-#56876 behavior.

The fix is placed after the degenerate case guards (`num_groups <= 0`) as suggested by @hclsys in the issue discussion.

## Validation

- Issue author @lucamotz measured ~15% decode throughput improvement on GB10 (SM121) with the fix
- Contributor @bluemelov1 independently confirmed on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120)
- Bit-identical outputs confirmed with and without the fix (correctness suite: needle, greedy repeats, shared-prefix divergence, DSpark acceptance)

## Testing

Hardware validation was performed by issue reporters on GB10 (SM121) and RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120).

AI assistance was used for code changes, validated against the issue reporter's provided diff and reviewer feedback.

## Related

- DeepGEMM-side fix: vllm-project/DeepGEMM#18

title: [CI][ROCm] Mirror split V1 attention groups on MI355
body:
- Add `mi355_1` mirrors and matching native AMD jobs for all four V1 attention groups: Sparse MLA, MLA Correctness, Dense/SSM, and DCP/MLA Backends/ROCm; retain three-way MLA correctness sharding.
- Exercise native ROCm and AITER dense attention, normal no-sink AITER sparse MLA, DSv4/DSv4.1 DSpark window graph replay, and the supported FlashAttention MLA prefill fallback.
- Fix the native ROCm sliding-window boundary exposed by these tests, and make the KV-connector selector test independent of the ambient AITER MHA setting.

[#57063](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57063) splits the B200 V1 attention suite, while [#50519](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50519) adds its earlier whole-suite AMD mirror and references the old MLA test path. It is a draft targeting `main` and must wait for **both #50519 and #57063** to merge, then be rebased to retain just this follow-up.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip the seq_lens D2H sync in the AITER sparse MLA metadata key
body:
## Purpose

This is the ROCm counterpart of #58684, which has the background.

On every build of `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` with persistent metadata (the default for DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.x sparse MLA), `seq_lens[:num_reqs].cpu()` runs, decode steps included. That is a blocking D2H copy, and under async scheduling it stalls the CPU until the GPU catches up. The copy only feeds the cache key that decides whether to re-run `get_mla_metadata_v1`, which was added in #42982. The metadata itself is already built on device from `paged_kv_indptr`.

The key only looks at seq_lens and context lens clamped to `index_topk`, so exact values usually aren't needed. This PR builds the key from `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` whenever that gives the same key:
- **No spec decode:** the upper bound is exact, so it's always used.
- **Spec decode:** the bound can overshoot by up to `num_speculative_tokens`. It's used once every request's `context_ub - num_speculative_tokens >= index_topk`. Past that point both lens clamp to `index_topk`, so the key is identical to the exact one. That's the steady state for long-context decode, the same regime #42982 targeted.
- **Otherwise:** it falls back to the current D2H copy.

Unlike #58684, no device fixup is needed, since AITER already plans on device.

Not changed here:
- The `synchronize()` after a metadata recompute (#47404) is untouched. The fast path never recomputes, since the key stays the same.
- Batches with any short-context request under spec decode still sync.

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs for this backend. #58354 edits the same `build()` (it drops dead ops) but doesn't touch this sync. Whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py`. The new `test_persistent_metadata_key_from_upper_bound` checks three cases: no spec decode, spec decode with saturated contexts, and spec decode with short contexts. In each it checks whether the D2H copy runs, and that the key equals the one built from exact seq_lens.
- **Needs validation on ROCm hardware.** I don't have MI300/MI355 access. The test module is ROCm-only, so I ran it on CPU with the platform guards removed and `np_to_pinned_tensor` / `triton.next_power_of_2` stubbed. It would be great if someone with ROCm hardware could run the test file, GSM8K, and an async + MTP serving bench (e.g. GLM-5.x or DeepSeek-V3.2) against main.

## Test Result

On CPU with the guards stripped: 7 passed. With the upper-bound path disabled, the two "no sync" cases fail, as expected.

No hardware numbers yet (see above).

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change. I reviewed every changed line.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Zero reused FlashInfer MLA KV blocks
body:
## Why

FlashInfer MLA kernels can consume values from the unwritten suffix of a KV-cache block. When a recycled block still contains non-finite data from its previous owner, masking is insufficient (`0 * NaN` remains NaN), which can corrupt attention outputs.

vLLM already has a scheduler-to-worker path for zeroing newly allocated KV blocks, but uniform-precision attention models do not currently enable it. This change adds a generic attention-backend capability and opts in only FlashInfer MLA dense/sparse today.

## Summary

- Add a generic `AttentionBackend.requires_kv_cache_zeroing` capability and publish it on the base `AttentionSpec`.
- Preserve the capability across attention-spec merges, uniform-type scheduler projection, and composite backends.
- Enable it for FlashInfer MLA dense and all registered FlashInfer MLA sparse variants, including DeepSeek V4/V4.1 compressed and sliding-window caches.
- Leave FlashMLA dense/sparse and all other attention backends unchanged.

## Reviewer guide

- `vllm/v1/attention/backend.py` and `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py` contain the core logic: the generic backend opt-in, base attention-spec metadata, merge propagation, and zeroing decision.
- `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` preserves the capability when a `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` group is collapsed for the scheduler.
- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/composite.py` ORs the requirement from either child backend.
- The FlashInfer backend files only opt the relevant dense/sparse backend classes into the generic capability.
- The tests cover backend scoping and propagation through base/MLA, sliding-window, uniform-type, and composite paths.
- No kernel or block-zeroer implementation changes are needed; this uses the existing newly-allocated-block zeroing pipeline.

## Duplicate check

This is not a duplicate of the closest related work:

- #51749 generalized the existing worker zeroer to all `AttentionSpec` subclasses, but did not enable zeroing for uniform-precision MLA configurations.
- Closed, unmerged #37530 enabled zeroing for every MLA backend; this change is deliberately restricted to FlashInfer MLA dense/sparse.
- #52187 optimizes zeroing by cache group.
- #57158 restores the reserved null block after CUDA graph capture.
- #55085 zeroes unwritten tails after partial Mooncake loads.

Searches performed:

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "FlashInfer MLA KV cache zeroing"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "KV cache corruption FlashInfer"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "flashinfer mla zero OR stale OR reused"
```

## Test plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py -k attention_kv_cache_zeroing
# 16 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_mm_prefix.py -k composite_backend_preserves_kv_cache_zeroing_requirement
# 1 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -k only_flashinfer_mla_backends_require_kv_cache_zeroing
# 1 skipped locally because FlashInfer is not installed

# Directly imported and exercised customize_spec for all seven sparse FlashInfer MLA backend classes.
# verified sparse customize_spec paths

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files <changed files>
# all applicable hooks passed, including Ruff and mypy
```

## Model evaluation

Not run in this CPU-only development environment because FlashInfer and a CUDA accelerator are unavailable. GPU reproduction of the incident and an output-correctness check are required before this draft is marked ready for review.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to investigate the relevant backend/cache-spec paths, implement the change, and draft this description. The submitter must review every changed line and validate the fix on the affected GPU configuration before merge.

title: [ROCm][CI] Cover the AITER MQA logits dispatch on gfx950
body:
## Purpose

**Split out of #50519** and carried over unchanged in intent. Test only.

`rocm_fp8_mqa_logits` picks between three paths: flydsl on gfx942, the AITER `fp8_mqa_logits` kernel when that module resolves, and a pure-torch fallback. Nothing covered the AITER path. Since the fallback returns the same values, a silent drop to it would still look like a pass, so a value-only test would not have caught it.

## What changed

One fixture and one test, 59 lines added, nothing existing modified.

**The dispatch is pinned down.** The test runs only on gfx950, enables AITER through a fixture that refreshes the cached env flags and restores them afterwards, and asserts both that AITER is enabled and that its module resolves. It then wraps `module.fp8_mqa_logits` in a counting proxy and requires exactly one call, so the torch fallback cannot satisfy the test.

**Ragged masking is checked in both directions** with `torch.equal(torch.isneginf(actual), ~valid)`, over intervals that include a single element, a full row, and two empty ones, one of them at the end of the key range. This catches a masked position that is not `-inf` as well as a valid position that wrongly is.

**Both documented scale layouts** are parametrized, `[N]` and `[N, 1]`, matching what the docstring of `rocm_fp8_mqa_logits` allows. Values are compared against a float reference built from the already-quantized inputs, so the comparison carries no quantization error.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py
```

## Test Result

On gfx950, the two new cases pass, and the file as a whole is `97 passed`, which confirms the fixture leaves no state behind for the existing cases.

`(MI355) Attention Kernels Shard %N` already runs the whole `kernels/attention` directory and does not ignore this file, so the new cases are picked up there. On MI300 they skip, as intended.


---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Stop the host pool feeding device KV cache residency metrics
body:
> **NOTE:** This PR was reduced to a one-line change: the HiSparse host pool no longer gets the device pool's metrics collector (`metrics_collector=None` in `HiSparseSourceManager.bind_host_pool`), so host blocks stop feeding the device `vllm:kv_block_*_seconds` histograms. That removes the block-ID collision described below at its source, instead of keying samples by pool. Host-tier residency metrics are proposed separately in #59485 (on top of #58949). The description below is the original.

## Purpose

With HiSparse and `--kv-cache-metrics`, the host and GPU pools share a metrics
collector, but each pool numbers its blocks independently. The collector keys
samples by `block_id` alone.

This results in incorrect metrics recording in KV cache block activities
when using HiSparse.

A false lifetime, idle-time, and reuse-gap histogram will affect users
relying on it to investigate cache turnover and reuse.

For example, allocate GPU block 1 at t=1 s and host block 1 at t=2 s. The host
allocation currently emits a false one-second GPU eviction sample, even though
the GPU block remains allocated. With this fix, **both histories remain active
and no eviction sample is emitted**.

This MR key samples by `(block.pool, block.block_id)` in allocation, access
and eviction callbacks. Allowing the KV cache block activities to be correctly
accounted.


The callbacks only update telemetry; allocation and eviction decisions are
unaffected. Ordinary hybrid/SWA groups sharing one pool retain their existing
behavior.


## Test Coverage

`test_hisparse_host_pool_preserves_device_lifecycle`
(`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py:59`) verifies the
production-wiring example. The test fails with metrics enabled without the fix.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex was used for implementation and validation.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DFlash speculator fails at startup (fp8_ds_mla draft KV dtype; 16384 vs 4096 hidden states)
body:
### Your current environment

vLLM `main` @ 73a78e6f1f, 2× B300 (SM100), TP2 + expert parallel. Reproduced with `--load-format dummy` (the failures are at startup, before any weights matter).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`DeepSeek-V4-Flash` + the `RedHatAI/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-speculator.dflash` DFlash drafter fails at startup on current `main`, in one of two ways depending on the drafter's KV cache dtype.

**1. fp8 target KV cache (default draft KV dtype): no attention backend for the drafter**

```bash
vllm serve RedHatAI/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 131072 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --block-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --load-format dummy --enforce-eager \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"RedHatAI/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-speculator.dflash","num_speculative_tokens":7}'
```

The drafter's sliding-window layers inherit the target's `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache dtype, which no non-MLA backend supports:

```
ValueError: No valid attention backend found for cuda with AttentionSelectorConfig(head_size=256, dtype=torch.bfloat16, kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla, block_size=256, use_mla=False, ..., has_sliding_window=True, ...). Reasons: {FLASHINFER: [kv_cache_dtype not supported], FLASH_ATTN: [kv_cache_dtype not supported, FP8 KV cache requires FA3 on SM90, FA4 with head_size=512 on SM90, or FA4 on SM100], TRITON_ATTN: [kv_cache_dtype not supported], FLEX_ATTENTION: [kv_cache_dtype not supported], TURBOQUANT: [kv_cache_dtype not supported, sliding window not supported]}.
```

(Forcing `"attention_backend": "FLASH_ATTN"` in the speculative config fails the same way: `kv_cache_dtype not supported`.)

**2. bf16 draft KV cache: hidden-state width mismatch in `propose`**

Same command, with `"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN","kv_cache_dtype":"auto"` added to the speculative config. The backend check passes, and the profile run then fails:

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 947, in profile_run
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 887, in _dummy_run
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py", line 376, in propose
    self.hidden_states[:num_target_tokens].copy_(hidden_states[:num_target_tokens])
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (16384) must match the size of tensor b (4096) at non-singleton dimension 1
```

`aux_hidden_states` is empty here, so `propose` falls back to the target's final hidden states. For DeepSeek-V4 those are 16384 wide (4 hyper-connection streams × 4096), while the drafter's buffer is 4096 wide. It looks like DeepSeek-V4 doesn't expose aux hidden states for DFlash, similar to what #55682 adds for GLM-5.3-Flash.

**Expected:** DeepSeek-V4-Flash + its DFlash speculator starts. Suggested fixes: pick a draft KV cache dtype the draft's backend supports instead of inheriting `fp8_ds_mla`, and capture the aux hidden states DFlash expects from DeepSeek-V4.

For reference, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark` (bundled DSpark drafter) starts fine on the same setup.

Found while testing KV cache grouping for #58638. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to reproduce and write this up; I reviewed it.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: MFU/MBU silently drops attention and FFN for GPTQ, AWQ, gpt-oss, DeepSeek-V4 FP8 and online-quantized models
body:
### Your current environment

`main` at `38cc054fc2` (25/09). Reproduced without a GPU (macOS, vLLM imported from source, `UnspecifiedPlatform`) with real `ModelConfig`s and the real quantization-config resolution (`VllmConfig._get_quantization_config`); `vllm/v1/metrics/perf.py` only needs the configs, no weights or GPU.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`AttentionQuantizationConfigParser` and `FfnQuantizationConfigParser` look up `quant_config.get_name()` in `_QUANT_WEIGHT_BYTE_SIZE` and raise `InvalidComponent` for any name that is not in the table. `ModelMetrics.__init__` catches that and skips the whole component at `logger.debug` level, so `--enable-mfu-metrics` reports **unembedding only**, with no warning.

The table was last expanded in #37231 (03/2026); later edits (#43841, #39612, #43529) only removed entries. Since then several quantization configs were added or renamed and return names that are not in the table:

| Model / flag | `ModelConfig.quantization` | `get_name()` | Components billed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, `openai/gpt-oss-120b` | `gpt_oss_mxfp4` | `gpt_oss_mxfp4` | `unembed` only |
| `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro` | `deepseek_v4_fp8` | `deepseek_v4_fp8` | `unembed` only |
| any GPTQ checkpoint (`Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-GPTQ-Int4`), no flag or `--quantization gptq` / `gptq_marlin` | `auto_gptq` | `auto_gptq` | `unembed` only |
| any AWQ checkpoint (`Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-AWQ`), no flag or `--quantization awq_marlin` | `auto_awq` (`awq` on CPU) | `auto_awq` | `unembed` only |
| bf16 checkpoint (`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`) with `--quantization fp8`, `fp8_per_tensor`, `fp8_per_block` or `fp8_per_channel` | as given | `online` | `unembed` only |
| control: `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8` | `fp8` | `fp8` | `attn`, `ffn`, `unembed` |

- `gpt_oss_mxfp4` came in #39604, `auto_gptq` in #38288, `auto_awq` in #42727 and `deepseek_v4_fp8` with the DeepSeek-V4 support. `gptq`, `gptq_marlin`, `awq` and `awq_marlin` now all map to `AutoGPTQConfig` / `AutoAWQConfig`, whose `get_name()` is `auto_gptq` / `auto_awq`, so the four matching entries in the table can no longer be hit.
- Every online shorthand resolves to `OnlineQuantizationConfig` (#38138), whose name is `online`; `--quantization fp8` on an unquantized checkpoint is the deprecated alias of `fp8_per_tensor`.
- `humming` and `modelopt_mixed` are also missing from the table (not measured here).

Magnitude for one decode step (batch 1, context 1024, `per_gpu=True`), current table vs. the same table with the missing name added:

| Model | `main` | with the name added | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b (`gpt_oss_mxfp4: 0.5`) | 1.16 GFLOP / 1.16 GB | 7.44 GFLOP / 2.70 GB | ×6.4 FLOPs, ×2.3 bytes |
| gpt-oss-120b (`gpt_oss_mxfp4: 0.5`) | 1.16 GFLOP / 1.16 GB | 10.58 GFLOP / 3.47 GB | ×9.1 FLOPs, ×3.0 bytes |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (`deepseek_v4_fp8: 1`) | 1.06 GFLOP / 1.06 GB | 16.21 GFLOP / 8.64 GB | ×15 FLOPs, ×8 bytes |
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro (`deepseek_v4_fp8: 1`) | 1.85 GFLOP / 1.85 GB | 58.27 GFLOP / 30.08 GB | ×31 FLOPs, ×16 bytes |

For DeepSeek-V4 the second column still has no attention: `MLAAttentionMetrics` fails separately with `Missing required attr kv_lora_rank in config` for the `deepseek_v4` / `deepseek_v41` configs (`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, which resolves to `fp8`, is billed `ffn` + `unembed` for the same reason). That looks like a separate gap; noting it so the numbers above are not read as complete.

Repro (no GPU needed):

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace
from vllm.config import LoadConfig, ModelConfig, VllmConfig
from vllm.v1.metrics.perf import ModelMetrics

mc = ModelConfig(model="openai/gpt-oss-20b")
qc = VllmConfig._get_quantization_config(mc, LoadConfig())
cfg = SimpleNamespace(
    model_config=mc, quant_config=qc,
    cache_config=SimpleNamespace(cache_dtype="auto"),
    parallel_config=SimpleNamespace(data_parallel_size=1, tensor_parallel_size=1,
                                    pipeline_parallel_size=1, enable_expert_parallel=False),
)
print(qc.get_name(), [m.component_type() for m in ModelMetrics(cfg).metrics])
# gpt_oss_mxfp4 ['unembed']
```

Possible fix: add the missing names (`gpt_oss_mxfp4`, `deepseek_v4_fp8`, `auto_gptq`, `auto_awq`, `online`, `humming`, `modelopt_mixed`; for `online` the byte size could come from the resolved `QuantizationConfigArgs`), and for an unknown method fall back to the model dtype with a `logger.warning_once` instead of dropping the component, so a future rename degrades the estimate rather than removing most of it. `test_quantization_config_parser_unknown_method` currently asserts the drop and would need to change.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the scripts and this report; I ran the checks and reviewed the results.

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Support BF16 KDA recurrent state
body:
## Overview

Honor `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16` in the ROCm Kimi-K3 KDA path, including paged prefill states and checkpoints.

## Claims

- Plan recurrent caches using the requested dtype.
- Read and write BF16 paged states directly in HIP prefill, retaining FP32 accumulation and scan workspaces.
- Select BF16-compatible backends under `auto`, preserving the existing FP32 backend priority.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=SD .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_{chunk,decode}.py -q
# 133 passed
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0 VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=SD .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_{checkpoint,adaptive_verification}.py -q
# 28 passed
```

Coverage includes BF16/FP32 state writes, checkpoint resume, graph replay, padded rows, backend selection, and Gluon FP32 kernels. The two BF16 selection cases fail against the pre-guard code. Metadata tests use AITER=0 because their borrowed Qwen configuration otherwise selects the unrelated GDN FlyDSL backend.

Real Kimi-K3 weights, TP8/DCP8, FP8 KV, BF16 SSM, AITER enabled, default KDA `auto`, eager execution; full GSM8K, 5-shot, concurrency 64, `max_tokens=512`:

| Decode | Correct | Accuracy | Error / abort |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Ordinary | 1266 / 1319 | 95.98% | 0 / 0 |
| DSpark K4, standard rejection | 1258 / 1319 | 95.38% | 0 / 0 |

Both modes completed all requests and produced the same single whitespace-only answer. DSpark accepted 71.50% of proposed tokens. Observed pure and mixed batches used HIP BF16 prefill and Triton BF16 decode/verify while AITER remained available.

Validation used the complete candidate source and rebuilt HIP extension with `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-e68efc685ab1e6f1eda004ced7157e3ca411da2f`. A previous same-runtime wrapper/native prefill comparison had identical output and state tensors for three operator cases. These results establish correctness, not an end-to-end speedup.

## Details

The model and layer previously dropped the requested recurrent-state dtype. The HIP prefill kernel also assumed FP32 persistent states. This update propagates the dtype and adds native BF16 state I/O, including checkpoint stores. FP32-only Gluon and HIP decode paths are excluded when the recurrent cache is BF16; AITER BF16 support can be enabled separately once available. This extends the existing PR rather than introducing an overlapping change.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Uses the existing state dtype and backend selection interfaces.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** GPU regressions, a pre-fix reproducer, and full model evaluations are described above.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Changes stay within KDA and its existing tests; relevant lint and type checks passed.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Scope, validation, and backend support boundaries are documented.

</details>

**BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>**

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Gather nvfp4_ds_mla chunked-context KV with the NVFP4 kernel
body:
## Status (2026-10-15)

Reworked after @zyongye's review (thanks — every point was right) and @LucasWilkinson's stu-cao/vllm#2, which proposed the same `seq_starts` change; rebased onto `main` `19b0efce30`. Lucas's kernel-level test (random cache bytes, non-block-aligned starts, bit-exact against the same slots gathered without starts) is included as his commit in `tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py`. Where this differs from #2: the BF16 workspace hunk is dropped (zyongye's point 1, it was unreachable) and DCP is rejected at startup instead of being left to fail in the generic gather (point 4).

- **`seq_starts` on the NVFP4 gather kernel** instead of a block-table shim. `cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache` gains an optional `seq_starts` like its fp8 twin (`token_offset = out_token - workspace_starts[req] + seq_starts[req]`), and the dense dispatch passes `chunk.starts` exactly as the `fp8_ds_mla` branch does. `shift_block_table_to_starts`, its alignment precondition, the clamp, the per-chunk gather and its CPU test are gone. Other callers are unchanged (the argument defaults to `None`).
- **Dropped the `MLACommonMetadataBuilder` workspace hunk and the `fp8_query` test arm.** `nvfp4_ds_mla` is only accepted by `FlashMLASparseBackend`, whose builder (`SparseMLACommonMetadataBuilder`) allocates its own BF16 workspace and hard-codes a BF16 prefill query, so neither was reachable.
- **DCP is rejected at startup** (`VllmConfig.validate_nvfp4_kv_cache_with_mla`) instead of in the per-layer forward on the first request with context; covered by `tests/test_config.py::test_nvfp4_ds_mla_rejects_decode_context_parallelism`.
- The raw `kv_c_and_k_pe_cache` pass is intentional: the `nvfp4_ds_mla` cache is allocated as `torch.uint8`. The three other gather dispatch sites that still send `nvfp4_ds_mla` to the generic gather (`mla_attention.py` DCP path, `kimi_k3/nvidia/mla.py`, `sparse_mla_attention.py`) are unreachable today and left for a follow-up.

Verification on the rebased head (`dc6aa4ae53`, B300 SM103, from-source build): **17 passed, 0 failed** — `test_mla_prefill_context_nvfp4.py` (1, the `seq_starts` path on real NVFP4 rows), `test_mla_context_chunks.py` (14), `test_config.py::test_nvfp4_ds_mla_rejects_decode_context_parallelism` (2); registered schema `cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache(..., int batch_size, Tensor? seq_starts=None)`; torch 2.14.0+cu130, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.3a`. `tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k nvfp4`: 27 passed including `test_cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache_with_seq_starts`.

## Purpose

`--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla` crashes in the MLA chunked-context prefill:

```
mla_attention.py  _compute_prefill_context
_custom_ops.py    gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache
RuntimeError: get_fp8_kv_cache_data_type, csrc/attention/dtype_fp8.cuh:34,
              Unsupported fp8 kv cache data type: nvfp4_ds_mla
```

`MLACommonBaseImpl._compute_prefill_context` gathers each chunk's cached context KV into a BF16 workspace. It has a branch for `fp8_ds_mla`; every other dtype goes to `gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache`, which only knows the fp8 variants. The NVFP4 upconvert kernel added with the `nvfp4_ds_mla` format, `cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache`, is never called here.

Sparse MLA reaches this path through its dense-MHA prefill: a prefill whose total length is `<= index_topk` and that has cached context. In practice:

- **speculative-decoding warm-up**: the dummy batch takes this path, so an engine with `nvfp4_ds_mla` KV and a DFlash draft never finishes starting;
- **chunked prefill splitting a short prompt**: the continuation step has context;
- **prefix-cache hits** on short prompts.

Longer prefills use the sparse FlashMLA kernels, which already handle `nvfp4_ds_mla`.

**Fix:**

- Route `nvfp4_ds_mla` to `cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache`.
- Give that kernel an optional `seq_starts` (csrc + bindings + `_custom_ops`), mirroring `cp_gather_and_upconvert_fp8_kv_cache`: a continuation chunk reads from its context start instead of the request's first token. Without it, every chunk after the first would silently re-read the request's first tokens.
- Reject `nvfp4_ds_mla` with decode context parallelism at config validation; that combination is not validated.

Other dtypes are unaffected. I found no existing issue or PR for this.

## Test Plan

New tests:

- `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_context_nvfp4.py` (SM100). Writes random KV into an `nvfp4_ds_mla` cache with `concat_and_cache_mla`, then runs `_compute_prefill_context` on it. The reference is the same method on a BF16 cache holding the dequantized values, through the generic gather. Every chunk must see bit-identical Q/K/V; the batch includes a chunk that continues one request and starts another.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py::test_cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache_with_seq_starts` (SM100): the kernel's `seq_starts` with non-block-aligned starts, bit-exact against a full gather.
- `tests/test_config.py::test_nvfp4_ds_mla_rejects_decode_context_parallelism` (CPU).

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_context_nvfp4.py tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py tests/test_config.py -k "nvfp4 or context_chunks"
```

End-to-end on 1 × GB200 node (4 GPUs), run with the first revision of this change (block-table shift; same gather semantics):

- **Model:** GLM-5.3 (NVFP4 weights) + DFlash2 draft (fp8 KV, k=4).
- **Engine:** aggregated TP4, `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla`, `--block-size 1024`, `--max-model-len 1048576`, prefix caching on.
- **Arms:** the same build with and without this change, plus an fp8-KV reference at `--max-model-len 262144`, since fp8 cannot fit one 1M-token request on TP4.
- **Checks:** startup; 6 distinct verifiable prompts, sequential then 12-way concurrent × 3 rounds; 12 concurrent ~1.7K-token prompts with `--max-num-seqs 8` and an 8192-token budget so some are necessarily split and their continuation runs this path, compared with the same prompts served unsplit; draft acceptance over 3 × 400 tokens on a short and a ~10K-token prompt.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix DeepSeek V4 DFlash input and cache formats
body:
## Purpose

Addresses #58733: DeepSeek-V4-Flash with the RedHatAI DFlash checkpoint fails during draft attention setup or profiling, and its published FC weight shape does not match the existing hidden-state path.

- Fall back to model-dtype draft KV storage when the target uses `fp8_ds_mla`, preserving explicit draft overrides. Share the resolution between model loading and attention metadata configuration, including the legacy runner.
- Keep the DFlash context buffer at the projected draft width (4096), rather than the raw HC residual width (16384).
- Infer the FC input width from `hc_mult` when `target_hidden_size` is absent, and export full stream-major auxiliary states from the NVIDIA DeepSeek V4 target when requested by the draft. Preserve mean-pooled states for other drafters and size PP receive buffers to the exported width.

For this checkpoint, five 16384-wide auxiliary states feed an `[4096, 81920]` FC weight and produce 4096-wide context features. The training-side HC handling is documented in https://github.com/vllm-project/speculators/pull/524.

The patch changes six existing source files, with no new files or test changes. It is scoped to the NVIDIA target implementation reported in the issue.

Duplicate check: no open PR references #58733. Related #48381 addresses DSpark KV storage and DCP; it does not fix this DFlash buffer/FC/auxiliary-state path.

## Validation

- Ruff 0.14.0 lint and formatting checks: passed on the changed files.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Earlier investigation reproduced the original copy mismatch with nonempty auxiliary states and inspected the public checkpoint's safetensors header. Those checks establish the original failures, not end-to-end validation of this patch.
- No runtime tests were run on this final reduced patch, at the requester's instruction. No B300/TP2/EP serving test or model-quality/acceptance evaluation has been completed; the available local GPU has 4 GB VRAM.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for investigation, implementation. I have personally reviewed all changes and found no issues.
