title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Feed Engram's FP8 rows to wkv without dequant + requant
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1's Engram table is already MXFP8: FP8 E4M3 rows with one ue8m0 scale per 32 values. The lookup dequantized each row to bf16, and `wkv` (an MXFP8 `[32, 32]` projection, 6144 → 25600) quantized it straight back. This PR hands `wkv` the table's own bytes as a `QuantizedActivation`, so both steps are gone.

- **Unsharded heads** (TP1, or tables shared across DP replicas): the lookup writes the FP8 values into persistent staging, and the scales at their F8_128x4 offsets. `embed()` returns views of those buffers, so no extra kernel runs. Scale rows that pad the last 128-token tile are written as zeros, matching FlashInfer's quantizer.
- **Sharded heads** (TP, or Engram-DP head sharding): each staged row packs its 8 scale bytes after its 256 value bytes. The existing gathers carry this payload unchanged, as one collective per exchange at 264 instead of 512 bytes per head row. `_engram_packed_to_mxfp8` then splits values from scales and swizzles the scales. Under TP it reads the rank-major `dim=0` gather in place, which also drops the `dim=1` gather's `movedim` copy, and it selects the SP token window.
- **When it applies:** only when `wkv`'s kernel is FlashInfer CuTe-DSL or CUTLASS MXFP8, the consumers of F8_128x4 activation scales. The check reuses `can_fuse_query_quant`, the gate of the query RMSNorm + MXFP8 fusion. `K = heads × head_dim` must also be a multiple of 128; DSV4.1 has K = 6144.
- **Everything else is unchanged.** That includes W8A16 Marlin on SM90, which takes bf16 activations and never requantized anything.

**Numerics.** The GEMM output is bit-identical to the previous path. Dequantizing an FP8 row to bf16 is exact. Requantizing it with a ceil-rounded power-of-two scale (FlashInfer's rule) only rescales values by powers of two, without saturating. So the GEMM sees the same real values. `test_engram_mxfp8_rows_match_requantized_wkv` checks this with `atol=0` through the real CuTe-DSL kernel.

### Duplicate-work check

`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search` for `engram`, `engram mxfp8`, `engram wkv`, `engram lookup`, `engram dequant`, `engram requant`, `wkv quant`, and `engram QuantizedActivation`, run on 2026-09-25. None of the related PRs removes the dequant/requant:

- #56989 (draft) packs FP8 rows for the TP exchange, but dequantizes them to bf16 again before `wkv`. It is opt-in, and limited to TP > 1 without SP. This PR never dequantizes on the MXFP8 path, is on by default wherever `wkv` accepts MXFP8, and also covers TP1, SP, and Engram-DP head sharding.
- #56929 (closed, unmerged) quantized the dequantized bf16 rows after the gather. That still paid for both the dequant and the requant.
- #58678 makes `wkv` column-parallel for TP without SP, and #57893 retunes the lookup tiling. Both are compatible with this PR but conflict textually in `common/engram.py`; whichever lands second rebases.

## Test Plan

On a GB300 node (SM103, 4 GPUs), rebased on `22bbe3f102`:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py tests/kernels/test_engram.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <same files>
```

New and extended tests:
- `test_engram_lookup_keeps_mxfp8_bytes`: byte-exact swizzled and packed outputs, from HBM and pinned host memory, at 1, 7, and 130 tokens. The scale buffer is pre-filled with stale bytes, so the zeroed padding rows are actually checked.
- `test_engram_mxfp8_rows_reconstruct_table`: TP 1/2/4 with and without SP, including a padded last head shard.
- `test_engram_mxfp8_rows_match_requantized_wkv`: end-to-end through `FlashInferCutedslMxfp8LinearKernel`, bit-exact against the old path.
- `test_engram_prepared_rows_survive_graph_breaks` and the 2-GPU `test_engram_head_collectives_survive_graph_breaks` now also run the MXFP8 path. This covers CPU-offload prefetch; eager, compiled, full, and breakable CUDA-graph capture; and real TP all-gathers.

## Test Result

- **Tests:** 139 passed, 0 skipped, including the 2-GPU test.
- **Checks:** pre-commit and mypy pass.
- **Kernel microbenchmark** (GB300; 24 heads × 256; random ids into a 16M-row table; CUDA-graph timing). "Old" is lookup + `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` as `wkv` ran it. The TP4 columns are one rank's local kernels, with the collective excluded:

| tokens | TP1, table in HBM: old → new (µs) | TP4 local kernels: old → new (µs) | TP1, table on host: requant removed from main stream (µs) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3.1 → 1.8 | 3.8 → 3.1 | 1.5 |
| 128 | 4.1 → 2.2 | 7.0 → 3.5 | 1.6 |
| 1024 | 12.4 → 6.2 | 19.6 → 5.5 | 4.4 |
| 4096 | 60.2 → 20.4 | 89.8 → 15.3 | 12.4 |
| 16384 | 281.6 → 176.2 | 333.5 → 87.3 | 49.7 |

With the table offloaded to host (the default), the lookup still runs on the prefetch stream at unchanged cost. The gain is the requant leaving the main stream, for each of the two Engram layers. At TP4, each exchange moves 48% fewer bytes.

- **Model evaluation:** pending; this PR stays a draft until the GSM8K and GPQA results for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP4, GB300) are added here.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the implementation, tests, benchmarks, and this description. The human submitter is accountable for the change.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Keep MLA-only KV cache dtypes away from non-MLA drafters
body:
## Purpose

Fixes the first failure mode of #58733.

A target with sparse MLA layers canonicalizes its KV cache dtype to an MLA-only format while it is built: `_canonicalize_sparse_mla_kv_cache_dtype` turns `fp8` into `fp8_ds_mla` (or keeps `nvfp4_ds_mla`) and writes that back into the shared `cache_config.cache_dtype` (`mla_attention.py`). When the DFlash-family drafter is loaded afterwards, `load_dflash_model` passes that same cache_config through untouched whenever the speculative config doesn't pin a `kv_cache_dtype`, so the drafter's non-MLA sliding-window layers go into backend selection with `kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla`, which no non-MLA backend serves. Startup dies with "No valid attention backend found".

With this change a non-MLA drafter no longer inherits the ds_mla family: it falls back to `auto`, resolving to the draft model's own dtype. An explicit `kv_cache_dtype` in the speculative config still wins, and an MLA drafter keeps inheriting the canonical format. This covers every speculator built on `load_dflash_model` (DFlash, DFlash2, DSpark, LiLiCorr).

The second failure mode in #58733 (DeepSeek-V4 hyper-connection hidden states being 4x the drafter's expected width, needing aux hidden-state capture) is a separate model-side change that needs acceptance validation on real hardware; I left it out of this PR and said so on the issue.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches the drafter cache dtype inheritance (checked #58733 links and `dflash`/`kv_cache_dtype` searches, 2026-09-26).

## Test Plan

New regression coverage: `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_draft_cache_config.py`

- explicit speculative `kv_cache_dtype` always wins
- non-MLA drafter drops inherited `fp8_ds_mla` / `nvfp4_ds_mla` to `auto`
- MLA drafter keeps the inherited ds_mla dtype
- shareable dtypes (`auto`, `fp8`, `bfloat16`) pass through unchanged

Red/green: the test errors on collection against current `main` (the guard doesn't exist) and passes on this branch.

Also run: `tests/v1/spec_decode/` (full dir), plus ruff check/format on all touched files. One existing mock in `test_lilicorr.py` had to grow the `cache_dtype` field the loader now reads.

## Test Result

- new file: 8 passed
- `test_lilicorr.py` + new file: 33 passed, 5 skipped
- full `tests/v1/spec_decode/`: identical failure set to current `main` (12 pre-existing environment failures: model-download and GPU-dependent tests on this CPU-only macOS box; verified by running the same selection stashed on `main`)
- ruff check + format: clean

Startup repro from the issue needs a B300 + the DeepSeek-V4-Flash weights, which I don't have; the fix is verified at the config-resolution level the failure originates from, and the backend-selection error path is deterministic from that input.

AI assistance: Kimi Code was used for the investigation, implementation and tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above myself.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Stream DeepSeek V4/V3.2 string tool arguments incrementally
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52846.

DeepSeek V4, V4.1 and V3.2 streamed a long string tool argument as one fragment when `</｜DSML｜parameter>` arrived. The configs set `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")`, so the engine skipped every plain body delta.

The fix now uses the per-parser `arg_value_extender` hook, the same way GLM (#61253) and Gemma4 (#61494) do. The earlier engine-level gate change is dropped.

- `vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py`: `_dsml_arg_value_extender` returns an extender while the last parameter is an open `string="true"` value. Each delta streams as escaped JSON text without rerunning the converter. It stops on a parameter tag, keeping a tail so a tag split across deltas is caught.
- Wired into `deepseek_v4_config`, `deepseek_v32_config`, and `deepseek_v41_config` (spaced DSML tags via `functools.partial`).
- `_param_patterns`: the trailing-partial regex holds back an unfinished next `<｜DSML｜parameter` tag, so a streamed value never includes it (implicit close case).

## Test Plan

New tests:

- `tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py`: `test_streaming_long_string_argument_is_incremental` (4096-char body in 32-char chunks, needs >1 non-empty body delta and exact round-trip), `test_streaming_non_string_argument_is_withheld_until_close`, `test_streaming_string_argument_with_markup_is_incremental`.
- `tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py::TestExtractToolCallsStreaming::test_long_string_argument_streams_before_close`
- `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py::test_long_string_argument_streams_before_close` (spaced DSML)
- `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py::TestArgValueExtender` (split close tag, closed value, non-string value, repeated key)

Commands (CPU only):

```bash
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv31_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv3_tool_parser.py

pytest tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py tests/parser/engine/test_gemma4_streaming_reasoning.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_gemma4_tool_parser.py tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py

pytest tests/parser tests/tool_parsers --ignore=tests/parser/cohere

ruff check <changed files>; ruff format --check <changed files>
```

## Test Result

On this branch:

```text
deepseek v3/v31/v32/v4 tool parsers:  82 passed, 1 xfailed
engine + glm47 + gemma4 + v41 set:     589 passed
tests/parser + tests/tool_parsers:     7672 passed, 1 skipped, 30 xfailed, 41 errors
ruff: All checks passed! / 6 files already formatted
```

The 41 errors are setup errors in `test_harmony.py` and `test_llama3_json_tool_parser.py` (gated or unreachable HF downloads on my machine). `tests/parser/cohere` was skipped: `cohere_melody` is not installed.

Same new tests against upstream/main parser code:

```text
FAILED test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py::test_streaming_long_string_argument_is_incremental - assert 0 > 1
FAILED test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py::...::test_long_string_argument_streams_before_close - assert 0 > 1
FAILED parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py::test_long_string_argument_streams_before_close - assert 2 > (4096 // 64)
```

V4, 4096-char body in 128 chunks: 0/128 body chunks emit arguments on main, 128/128 on this branch.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] DeepSeek-V4/V4.1: Hybrid FP8/MXFP4 Quant Routing Guard, Fused Shared Experts, Engram Scale Translation, and VLM Generator Streaming
body:
## Purpose

Fixes multiple weight loading crashes and memory blowups when loading hybrid quantized DeepSeek-V4 / DeepSeek-V4.1 checkpoints (e.g., `amd/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`) under tensor parallelism:

1. **Hybrid FP8/MXFP4 quant routing guard**:
   - *Problem*: DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1 mix FP8 attention (2D block size `[32, 32]`) with MXFP4 experts (group size 32). In `get_quant_method`, matching `weight_block_size == [32, 32]` misrouted `shared_experts.down_proj` into `ModelOptLinearMethod`, which applied `repeat_interleave(32)`. This expanded `w2.weight_scale` by 32× and crashed model initialization unconditionally with `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (N) must match the size of tensor b (32*N)` on checkpoints like `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`. (Note: Upstream PR #57071 introduced `deepseek_v4/quant_config.py` with this same vulnerability).
   - *Fix*: In `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/quant_config.py:get_quant_method`, guard `ModelOptLinearMethod` assignment with `"shared_experts" not in prefix` so shared experts continue using standard `Fp8LinearMethod`. In addition, in `from_config` across both `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/quant_config.py` and `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/quant_config.py`, dynamically discover `weight_block_size` from Quark configs (checking both top-level `weight_block_size` and nested `layer_quant_config.<layer>.weight.block_size`) instead of hardcoding `[128, 128]`.

2. **Fused Shared Experts (FSE) virtual slot folding & padding**:
   - *Problem*: DeepSeek-V4.1 lacked FSE redirection and expert count updates when fusing shared experts into routed expert allocations. This caused checkpoint loading to raise `RuntimeError: Key not found` for shared expert weights or silently omit shared experts from fused expert kernels, corrupting model generation. Additionally, renaming `.shared_experts.` bypassed intermediate dimension padding, causing shape mismatches under TP slicing.
   - *Fix*: In `deepseek_v41/amd/model.py`, redirect `.shared_experts.` to `.experts.{n_routed}.w` and include `n_shared` in `get_expert_mapping()` when FSE is enabled. Track `is_fse_redirect` so `_pad_shared_expert_weight` executes on redirected FSE weights along intermediate dimension 1 (`.w2.`).

3. **Engram scale key regex generalization**:
   - *Problem*: Quark checkpoints name the engram scale key `.weight_scale` instead of `.scale`. The existing regex failed to match, raising uncaught `KeyError: 'layers.1.engram.embed.weight_scale'` and halting model loading during parameter dictionary mapping.
   - *Fix*: Generalize regex to `r"(engram\.embed)\.(?:weight_)?scale$"` in both AMD (`amd/model.py`) and NVIDIA (`nvidia/model.py`) modeling files.

4. **Non-materialized generator streaming in multimodal causal LM wrapper**:
   - *Problem*: `DeepseekV41ForCausalLM.load_weights` in `amd/vl_model.py` called `sorted(...)` on the 48-shard weight generator, materializing hundreds of gigabytes into a Python list. On hosts with <= 512 GB RAM, this exhausted host memory, causing the Python process to crash with `MemoryError` or be terminated by the Linux kernel OOM killer (`SIGKILL`).
   - *Fix*: Replace full-list sorting with a lightweight `_stream_reordered()` generator that yields `language_model.` weights contiguously on the fly, buffering only non-language-model weights (~400 MB) in host memory.

---

## Relation to Merged Upstream PR #57071

Upstream PR #57071 (`commit 5840d95284f`, `[Bugfix][ROCm] AMD-Quark mixed-precision DeepSeek-V4.1 support`) added Quark OCP MX config parsing and two separate engram regexes (`(engram.embed).scale$` and `(engram.embed).weight_scale$`).

This PR reconciles with and complements #57071:
- **Harmonized Engram Scale Parsing**: This PR integrates upstream's dual regex structure while ensuring complete coverage across both AMD and NVIDIA modeling files.
- **Critical Quant Routing Guard**: Upstream #57071 omitted the `"shared_experts" not in prefix` guard in `get_quant_method`. On checkpoints like `amd/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`, this triggers the 32× scale blowup crash (`RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (N) must match the size of tensor b (32*N)`). This PR provides this essential guard.
- **Fused Shared Experts (FSE) Redirection and Dim-1 Padding**: Upstream lacked FSE virtual slot redirection (`.shared_experts.` -> `.experts.{n_routed}.w2/w1/w3/w`) and dim-1 intermediate dimension padding (`dim = 1 if (".down_proj." in name or ".w2." in name) else 0`), without which shared expert weights either fail to load or corrupt fused expert execution.
- **Multimodal Generator Streaming**: Upstream retained full-list materialization in `amd/vl_model.py`, exhausting 475+ GB of host RAM. This PR's `_stream_reordered()` generator bounds host memory to <400 MB.

---

## Target Files

- `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/quant_config.py`
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/quant_config.py`
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py`
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py`
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/vl_model.py`
- `tests/models/deepseek_v41/test_fse_routing.py`
- `tests/models/deepseek_v41/test_quant_config.py`
- `tests/models/deepseek_v41/test_weights_mapper_engram.py`
- `tests/models/deepseek_v41/test_vl_streaming.py`

---

## Test Plan

```bash
# Standalone CPU unit tests covering FSE routing, padding, quant guards, engram, and VLM streaming
pytest -v tests/models/deepseek_v41/test_fse_routing.py \
          tests/models/deepseek_v41/test_quant_config.py \
          tests/models/deepseek_v41/test_weights_mapper_engram.py \
          tests/models/deepseek_v41/test_vl_streaming.py

# End-to-end serving verification (AMD Instinct MI350X / MI355X)
vllm serve amd/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --trust-remote-code
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "amd/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}]}'
```

---

## Test Result

- Passed all 18/18 standalone unit tests on CPU in 8.08s without GPU dependencies.
- Checkpoint loads cleanly under TP=2 on AMD Instinct MI350X (`gfx950`) without host OOM or shape assertion errors.
- Completed CUDAGraph warmup and reached `/health` HTTP 200 in 605 s.
- Passed chat completions smoke test with 100% accuracy (`"Paris"`).
- Sustained 327.7 tok/s throughput under `vllm bench serve` with 0 errors.

---

## Subsystem Independence

- **Disjoint Scope**: This PR is completely self-contained and disjoint from other model loader or MoE kernel optimizations, modifying only DeepSeek model files and standalone test suites. It can be merged in any sequence and passes all 18/18 CPU tests in complete isolation.

---

*Claude Code was used to assist in authoring this PR, and all changes have been reviewed and tested by the author on AMD Instinct hardware.*

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] persistent topk kernel loses candidates on overflow
body:
## Purpose

The persistent-topk kernel can miss higher-scoring entries, and the entries it misses depend on atomic ordering, so identical runs can differ.

On a GB10, rows of 6000 to 32768 candidates with tight score distributions drop 89 to 6603 winners across five rows.

We can add detection for overflow which add one extra comparison/load on the hot paths for cases that do not overflow. On overflow, we select the bin's top members exactly with a byte-wise radix pass over the row. In the vast majority of cases this is not hit. On the fast path, we are within 1 to 2 µs at 25 to 55 µs per call. The fallback itself, which should be rare outside of the failure case, costs ~2 µs per call at about 10k pools and ~18 µs at about 30k pools.

`radix_topk` has no capped buffer and is unaffected. `FilteredTopKUnifiedKernel`, `cooperative_topk`, and `histogram_4096_topk` have the same buffer limit pattern on sm_90 and sm_100 and are not changed here...  PRs to follow there. (see #53287 as well) 

## Test Plan

Test included.

1. New test tests/kernels `test_top_k_per_row.py::test_persistent_topk_overflowing_threshold_bin`, k in {512, 1024, 2048} x {one_bin, one_bin_ties, normal}, rows 6000 to 32768. It fails on the unfixed kernel.
2. Existing top-k tests in that file, unchanged.
3. Direct head-to-head kernel check on a GB10 against torch.topk on _synthetic score distributions_, ie: manufactured bucket scores (item 5 uses real text).
4. Fast and "slow" path timing, current versus fixed on both overflowing and non-overflowing rows.
5. Flat repetitive prompts at about 40k and 120k tokens, 128 decode tokens. `persistent_topk` call compared against `torch.topk`. See attached `topk_flat_prompts.py` to regenerate the prompts. Run with `--enforce-eager`.

<details>
<summary> Repeating prompt generator (`topk_flat_prompts`) </summary>

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Flat prompts that overflow persistent_topk's threshold-bin buffer.

Each prompt is one short unit repeated to ~40k or ~120k tokens, then a question
so the model decodes. Repetition makes the sparse indexer's scores nearly flat,
so the bin holding the k-th score holds far more entries than the kernel's
buffer (4096 on the 256-bin path). Repeat counts below are the ones used on
GLM-5.3-Flash; other tokenizers land at slightly different lengths.

  python3 topk_flat_prompts.py --write DIR           # write the 8 prompts as .txt
  python3 topk_flat_prompts.py --url http://HOST:PORT --model NAME

Serve with --sparse-indexer-topk-backend persistent (or the kernel config
equivalent) and --enforce-eager if you hook the decode top-k from Python to
compare it against torch.topk. Standard library only.
"""
import argparse, json, os, time, urllib.request

TOOL = ("<tool_call>Bash<arg_key>command</arg_key><arg_value>ls -la</arg_value></tool_call>\n"
        "<tool_response>total 0\n</tool_response>\n")
# (name, unit, repeats at ~40k tokens, repeats at ~120k tokens)
UNITS = [
    ("ok", "ok\n", 20000, 60000),
    ("a", "a ", 39999, 119999),
    ("fox", "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.\n", 4000, 12000),
    ("tool", TOOL, 2000, 6000),
]
QUESTION = "\nHow many times does the line above repeat? Answer with a number."


def prompts():
    for label, idx in (("40k", 2), ("120k", 3)):
        for u in UNITS:
            # the header line makes each prompt unique, so no prefix cache hit
            yield f"{u[0]}_{label}", f"session {label}-{u[0]}\n" + u[1] * u[idx] + QUESTION


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--write", metavar="DIR")
    ap.add_argument("--url")
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="glm53")
    ap.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=128)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if not (a.write or a.url):
        ap.error("pass --write DIR or --url URL")
    for name, text in prompts():
        if a.write:
            os.makedirs(a.write, exist_ok=True)
            with open(os.path.join(a.write, name + ".txt"), "w") as f:
                f.write(text)
            print(f"{name}: {len(text):,} chars")
        if a.url:
            body = {"model": a.model, "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": a.max_tokens,
                    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": text}]}
            req = urllib.request.Request(a.url.rstrip("/") + "/v1/chat/completions",
                                         data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                         headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
            t0 = time.time()
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=1800) as r:
                usage = json.loads(r.read()).get("usage", {})
            print(f"{name}: prompt_tokens={usage.get('prompt_tokens')} "
                  f"completion_tokens={usage.get('completion_tokens')} {time.time() - t0:.1f}s", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>



## Test Result

1. Passed, fails 9/9 on the existing kernel
2. Passed
3. Head-to-head check on synthetic score distributions:

```
scores                    k      current drops   fixed drops
normal, mean 5, sd 0.5    512          89             0
normal, mean 5, sd 0.5    2048       2183             0
all in [4, 4.12)          512        1629             0
all in [4, 4.12)          2048       6603             0
normal, mean 5, sd 1.0    2048        106             0
```

4. On the fast path, we are within 1 to 2 µs at 25 to 55 µs per call. The fallback itself, which should be rare outside of the failure case, costs ~2 µs per call at about 10k pools and ~18 µs at about 30k pools.

5. Using repeated prompt text.

 - "bad rows" = rows whose returned set is wrong.
 - "dropped" = entries with a strictly larger score than one that was returned
 - "max bin" = entries in the threshold bin, vs kernel's 4096 buffer
 - "rows over 4096" = rows where threshold bin exceeds the buffer

*Before*

```
  unit repeated            length   decode calls   max bin   rows over 4096   bad rows   dropped
  "ok\n"                     40k        374          9,991        49,529          537     60,003
  "a "                       40k        352          9,986        75,810          642     75,729
  one English sentence       40k        418          9,968        24,620          445     21,140
  one tool call + response   40k        462          9,967        18,834          667     50,803
  "ok\n"                    120k        330         29,994       274,598          536    102,207
  "a "                      120k        374         29,992       440,534          853    172,637
  one English sentence      120k        319         29,964       143,865          444     59,689
  one tool call + response  120k        451         29,958       128,138          724     55,450
```

*After*

```
  unit repeated            length   decode calls   max bin   rows over 4096   bad rows   dropped
  "ok\n"                     40k        407          9,991        47,370            0          0
  "a "                       40k        385          9,984        80,135            0          0
  one English sentence       40k        418          9,981        24,221            0          0
  one tool call + response   40k        429          9,950        19,027            0          0
  "ok\n"                    120k        352         29,990       271,271            0          0
  "a "                      120k        407         29,992       444,887            0          0
  one English sentence      120k        418         29,968       144,932            0          0
```

(note: because of time limitations the 120k tool-call prompt was not rerun on the fixed kernel)

*Control*

The exact prefill kernel (top_k_per_row_prefill) on the same prompts: 0 bad rows, as expected.

---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

title: [Performance]: Suboptimal SM90 FP8 CUTLASS MoE dispatch on H20 EP8 — upstream fix proposed
body:
### Current serving results (replaces older serving snapshots)

Three GuideLLM 0.7.4 runs per tier, 10 s warmup, separate 8xH20 nodes. Humming W4A8 on original MXFP4: Decode c256 4,725 ± 66 output tok/s; fixed-1K Prefill c64 9,875 ± 63 input tok/s. Tuned FP8-128 + flashinfer_cutlass: 6,459 ± 173 output tok/s (+36.7%) and 15,048 ± 818 input tok/s (+52.4%), respectively. Values are means ± sample standard deviations. Paired GSM8K: Humming 476/494 correct, tuned 475/494; one-question difference (0.20 percentage points). The [blog PR #350](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-project.github.io/pull/350) has per-run data and methods. These whole-recipe gains are not attributable to the FlashInfer patch alone; the isolated operator A/B below remains its direct evidence. AI assistance was used to prepare this update.

### Proposal to improve performance

Track an upstream FlashInfer dispatch optimization affecting vLLM's SM90 block-FP8 `flashinfer_cutlass` MoE path, and validate its integration once a release containing the fix is available.

Upstream implementation and reproduction script: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5560 (open, not yet merged).

The FlashInfer grouped GEMM runner uses the unexpanded input token count as `expected_m_`, but the dispatch threshold and tile selection operate on rows per expert. On our H20 EP8 configuration, a 288-token input with top-k=6 and 400 physical experts has an average of 4.32 routed rows per physical expert, not 288. The mismatched estimate selects an unfavorable GEMM branch/tile for decode-sized batches.

The proposed fix configures `max(1, ceil(tokens * top_k / (local_experts * ep_size)))` after worst-case workspace sizing. It keeps workspace virtual signatures, allocation logic and existing kernels unchanged. EPLB replicas are physical execution slots; this remains an average-load heuristic, not a measured routing histogram.

vLLM already forwards `ep_size`, `ep_rank` and `use_deepseek_fp8_block_scale` to FlashInfer. We are not proposing a duplicate dispatch implementation or LD_PRELOAD workaround in vLLM. The requested follow-up is dependency uptake and integration/performance validation after the upstream fix is reviewed and released.

### Report of performance regression

This is a suboptimal-dispatch report, **not a bisected vLLM release regression**.

Actual source-built comparison on eight H20 ranks, using the full local `cutlass_fused_moe` API:

| Input tokens / routing | Baseline ms | Proposed fix ms | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 192 / uniform | 1.796432 | 0.554240 | 3.24x |
| 288 / uniform | 1.808480 | 0.564064 | 3.21x |
| 2048 / uniform | 1.904528 | 0.720464 | 2.64x |
| 288 / 75% routed to six experts | 2.020800 | 1.018144 | 1.98x |
| 288 / six active experts, seven ranks empty | 0.791280 | 0.751328 | 1.05x |
| 1 / uniform | 0.114720 | 0.115152 | ~1.00x |
| Draft geometry, 288 / uniform | 0.633360 | 0.217456 | 2.91x |

Five warmups, 24 CUDA Graph/event samples, explicit 64 MiB L2 flush outside timing; median of per-sample maximum latency across eight ranks. CUPTI was unavailable and GPU clocks were not locked. Cross-rank output reduction was checked **outside** the timed region.

All 64 rank/case output comparisons (including two draft cases) had maximum absolute difference zero; combined outputs also passed. No LD_PRELOAD was used for these source-build results.

**These are local MoE operator measurements, not communication-inclusive latency or serving TPS. We do not claim a 3.21x end-to-end vLLM throughput improvement.**

### Misc discussion on performance

Reproduction: the upstream PR includes the eight-rank synthetic `full_moe.py` harness, build isolation instructions and baseline/candidate commands. It does not require access to our checkpoint. Run the baseline before the candidate to generate identical-input reference tensors.

Validation boundaries:

- The full extension compiled, linked and loaded from an isolated FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1 source copy with the patch backported. The measured baseline retains EP-argument plumbing from an earlier iteration but restores the original estimate; it is a controlled ablation, not a pristine upstream binary.
- Exact upstream-base build and unmodified pytest execution remain pending. The proposed upstream base is `bf82326b0c524048c7f810da9f0022f8316ac3ff`.
- EP8 sequential-shard reference checks passed at hidden/intermediate=128 with batch 512 → 192 → 1 → 288 and unchanged tolerance. These are distinct from the real eight-rank A/B checks above.
- A hidden=512/intermediate=256 independent-reference case failed identically on baseline and patch (5,330/262,144 elements). Its cause is not fully established; this is not recorded as a passing accuracy test.
- Highly concentrated routing is not universally faster: a separate cold-L2 experiment showed about 7.6% regression for FC1 alone with one active expert, despite a small combined FC1+FC2 gain.
- Only H20 EP8 was validated. EP1/EP2 deployments, H100/H200, broad model quality parity and matched source-serving A/B are not claimed; a paired 500-item GSM8K sanity check is reported above.

title: [Bugfix] Flush DeepSeek V3.1 tool arguments that do not end in a string
body:
Related: #48342

## Purpose

When the tail of the tool arguments arrives in the same streamed delta as `<｜tool▁call▁end｜>`, the close branch of `DeepSeekV31ToolParser.extract_tool_calls_streaming` rebuilds the unstreamed tail from `delta_text` and assumes the arguments end in `"}`:

```python
if '"}' not in delta_text:
    return None
end_loc = delta_text.rindex('"}')
diff = delta_text[:end_loc] + '"}'
```

Tails such as `2}`, `2]}` and `1}}` contain no `"}`, so the branch returns None and the client never receives them, and the same happens to a lone `}` whose closing quote arrived one delta earlier. A `"}}` tail is cut at the inner `"}`, which drops the outer brace. Streaming then disagrees with `extract_tool_calls` on the same text:

| Argument deltas (the last one shares a delta with the end token) | Streamed before | Streamed after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{"city": "Tok` / `yo"}` | `{"city": "Tokyo"}` | `{"city": "Tokyo"}` |
| `{"city": "NYC` / `"` / `}` | `{"city": "NYC"` | `{"city": "NYC"}` |
| `{"count": 4` / `2}` | `{"count": 4` | `{"count": 42}` |
| `{"xs": [1,` / `2]}` | `{"xs": [1,` | `{"xs": [1,2]}` |
| `{"o": {"b":` / `1}}` | `{"o": {"b":` | `{"o": {"b":1}}` |
| `{"o": {"b": "x` / `"}}` | `{"o": {"b": "x"}` | `{"o": {"b": "x"}}` |

The fix reads the finished arguments out of the tool call text with the existing `stream_tool_call_portion_regex` and sends only what is not yet in `streamed_args_for_tool`. The incremental branch above already keeps that record, so the flush no longer has to guess the closing characters. #48343 makes the same change to the DeepSeek V3 parser, and this PR keeps the V3.1 close branch in line with it. The dead `diff is str` comparison in the same block goes away too: it compared a string with the `str` type, so it was always False.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

- #48342 / #48343 report and fix this bug in the DeepSeek V3 parser (`deepseekv3_tool_parser.py`). #48343 says it left V3.1 alone because #38866 was reworking that parser.
- #38866 (by @pascal9585) found the quote-apart case for V3.1. It moved the cut in `delta_text` from the last `"}` to the last `}`, and used the whole delta minus trailing newlines and backticks when there was no `}`. The gemini-code-assist review on it suggested replacing that manual cut with the regex the parser already uses elsewhere, which is what this PR does. The stale bot closed it on 2026-08-02 without a human review. This PR supersedes it: the quote-apart case is one of the test cases here, and the flush no longer reads the tail from `delta_text` at all. Credit to @pascal9585 for the quote-apart case.
- Other open PRs that touch this file do not change the flush: #48636 (a whole tool call in one delta), #55565 (incremental delimiter counting), #55473 (regex timeouts).
- The parser engine PRs, such as #53739 and the #51577 migration, do not cover V3.1. On main, `deepseek_v31` still maps to the legacy parser class.

GitHub searches run on 2026-09-26:

```
repo:vllm-project/vllm is:pr is:open deepseekv31
repo:vllm-project/vllm is:pr is:open deepseek tool parser streaming arguments
repo:vllm-project/vllm is:pr 38866 OR 48342 OR 48343
```

## Test Plan

The test goes into the existing `tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv31_tool_parser.py` and reuses `run_tool_extraction_streaming` / `run_tool_extraction_nonstreaming` from `tests/tool_parsers/utils.py`. One parametrized test feeds six argument shapes through the streaming parser with the tail and `<｜tool▁call▁end｜>` in one delta, then compares the streamed name and arguments with `extract_tool_calls` on the joined text. The string case is the control that already passes on main.

```
python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv31_tool_parser.py
```

## Test Result

With the fix: `8 passed`, which is the two existing tests plus the six new cases.

With only the parser reverted to main and the same test file: `5 failed, 3 passed`. Only the string control of the new test passes. Example failure:

```
assert '{"count": 4' == '{"count": 42}'
```

I ran these hooks from `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with `pre-commit run <hook> --files` on the two changed files, and all of them pass: `ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `typos`, `check-spdx-header`, `check-root-lazy-imports`, `check-forbidden-imports`, `check-torch-cuda-call`, `check-boolean-context-manager`, `validate-config`, `check-test-tethering` and `mypy-3.10`. The CI-only `mypy-3.11`, `mypy-3.12` and `mypy-3.13` hooks also pass with `--hook-stage manual` on the same files.

## Model evaluation

Not run. The change is in the string handling of the streaming tool call parser and does not touch the model forward path. I have no GPU to run DeepSeek V3.1 end to end, so the claim that a real detokenizer can put the argument tail and the end token in one delta rests on the parser's own multi-token delta handling (`len(delta_token_ids) > 1`), and on #48343 describing the same delivery for V3 under async scheduling or `stream_interval > 1`.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude) was used to prepare this change. The commit carries `Co-authored-by` trailers. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above locally.

title: [Qwen4Exp] Gather PLE rows on the host from the checkpoint files (`host_file_gather`)
body:
## Purpose

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next carries a 47.7 GiB FP8 PLE n-gram table. The storage backends from #54371 keep the whole table in GPU memory or copy it into pinned host memory, so about 48 GiB stays allocated for the life of the server, even though a generation reads only a small part of it. When weights, KV cache and the table do not fit together, the model cannot be served.

This PR adds an opt-in backend, `--engram-config '{"host_file_gather": true}'`, that serves the table from the checkpoint files through the page cache. Rows live in clean, file-backed pages that the kernel can drop and re-read, so the memory a resident table would hold stays available for the KV cache or other work. The table is never mapped into the worker after loading.

## Background from #54129

- A measurement of the access pattern found about 17.6 rows per step, no reuse between consecutive steps, and a 1.6 MiB working set over 800 steps ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54129#issuecomment-5757052453)).
- Operators ran the previous mmap implementation on discrete GPUs: 8x RTX 3090 ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54129#issuecomment-5463213366)), an RTX PRO 6000 ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54129#issuecomment-5463773575)), and a production deployment on 2x RTX 5090 at TP=2, where the weights alone fill host RAM ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54129#issuecomment-5838606950)). Those numbers are from the previous implementation, not this one.
- Their cold-cache runs showed that misses must be queued rather than faulted one page at a time, which is why this backend issues `POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED` before each gather.
- The illegal-memory-access report on the previous implementation ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54129#issuecomment-5780599481)) points to the upstream Mamba prefix-cache fix in #53906.

## Design

- **Selection.** `EngramConfig.host_file_gather: bool = False`. Qwen4Exp only; takes precedence over `cpu_offload`; rejected on ROCm and with elastic EP.
- **Storage.** `Qwen4ExpPLEFileGatherEmbedding` allocates no table rows. `load_weights` keeps the default loader's zero-copy safetensors views of each shard. At bind, every view must be file-backed according to `/proc/self/maps` (Hugging Face cache symlinks work; heap, pinned and anonymous memory are rejected), and the shards must cover the whole table. Bind records each shard's file and offset, opens the files read-only and releases the views, so no mapping of the table outlives loading.
- **Staging.** `Qwen4ExpModelState.prepare_inputs` computes each PLE layer's n-gram ids, copies them to pinned host memory, and syncs the stream once per step. It then deduplicates the step's ids, issues `POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED` over the coalesced page ranges of their rows, reads each distinct row with `preadv`, expands duplicates into pinned memory with one `index_select`, and copies the rows into a fixed device staging buffer.
- **Forward.** Reads only the staging buffer, so FULL CUDA graph capture is unaffected. The ids are computed eagerly and consumed on the current stream, so this path is not affected by #58441.
- **Scope.** Rows stay in the checkpoint dtype. Dummy loads serve zeros. Weight reload is rejected. A truncated checkpoint file stops the engine with an error instead of SIGBUS.

## Why this is not a duplicate

#58439 reads the checkpoint mapping directly from the GPU and needs pageable host-page-table access, which unified-memory systems provide. #54070 writes a separate copy of the table to a disk directory and depends on the closed #53899. This PR reads rows on the host from the checkpoint files the loader resolved, so it does not need unified memory.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py -q
pytest tests/test_config.py -k engram -q
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual
```

End to end on a DGX Spark (GB10, 128 GB unified memory), TP=1, table on local NVMe:

```bash
vllm serve RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 --language-model-only \
  --max-model-len 40960 --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --engram-config '{"host_file_gather": true}' \
  --kv-cache-memory-bytes 17179869184
```

The KV cache was 16 GiB (20 GiB for the default-graph correctness samples, 8 GiB for MTP).

- Correctness: an out-of-tree hook recorded the ids and staged rows of sampled steps (prefill, decode, mixed, MTP draft) and compared them byte for byte with the checkpoint shards.
- Throughput: `vllm bench serve --ignore-eos --random-output-len/--sharegpt-output-len 256` at concurrency 1 and 16, default and FULL graphs, on random prompts and on realistic prompts (GSM8K questions with few-shot turns, 655 to 1,000 tokens).
- Accuracy (before the third commit, with the mapped-view gather): GSM8K, 200 questions, chat template.
- Cold cache: PLE files evicted with `POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED` before startup, then a 30k-token prompt and a decode run at concurrency 1.
- Soak (before the third commit, with the mapped-view gather): MTP n=3 with prefix caching and `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` at 12 GiB, concurrency 8, 16 and 32 for 5 minutes each.
- Memory pressure: two CPU-only processes gathering the same rows from a synthetic table under a cgroup memory cap, with the previous mapped-view gather and with this one.

## Test Result

Unit: 90 passed (`test_ple.py`, `qwen4_exp/test_config.py`); 43 passed (`test_config.py -k engram`); pre-commit and mypy pass.

**Correctness.** 0 mismatches over 1,022,080 staged rows from default graphs, FULL graphs and MTP: prefill 355,072; mixed 661,744; decode 2,704; speculative decode 2,560.

**Accuracy.** GSM8K 98.5% (197/200), measured before the third commit.

**Throughput** (median ITL; staging = host time of the gather and copy per decode step):

| Graphs | Prompts | Concurrency | Output tok/s | Median ITL | Staging / ITL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| default | realistic | 1 | 15.20 | 61.79 ms | 0.38% |
| default | realistic | 16 | 96.29 | 141.89 ms | 7.3% |
| FULL | realistic | 1 | 15.15 | 61.26 ms | 0.39% |
| FULL | realistic | 16 | 98.7\* | 138.0 ms\* | 7.6%\* |
| default | random | 1 | 16.2\* | 59.2 ms\* | 1.7%\* |
| default | random | 16 | 97.1\* | 139.8 ms\* | 7.5%\* |

\* Measured before the third commit, with the mapped-view gather and a 20 GiB KV cache; not re-run.

In the same build and setup at concurrency 1 on realistic prompts, the previous mapped-view gather reached 15.71 tok/s against 15.20 (one run each), with a median time to first token of 567 ms against 615 ms. Prefill pays for the separate read of each distinct row: a warm 2,048-token chunk takes about 32 ms of host staging, against 18 ms before.

At concurrency 16 the staging time is mostly waiting on reads of rows not seen before; major faults stay at 0 per step.

**Cold cache.** A cold 30k-token prompt took 17.40 s to first token, against 15.45 s warm. Disk reads stayed below one 4 KiB page per distinct row. Decode at concurrency 1 after the eviction staged in a median of 0.90 ms per step.

**Memory.** The worker has no mapping of the PLE files after load, at every snapshot from startup through the benchmarks; the table is page cache only. `RssFile` stays flat at about 0.5 GiB, against 2.34 GiB for the previous mapped-view gather after the same warm-up and concurrency-1 run. Anonymous memory stays flat at about 2 GiB, shared memory below 60 MiB, and `VmPin` is 0.

**Memory pressure (synthetic, CPU only).** Two processes gathered the same rows from a 1.9 GiB synthetic table for 40 s under a 2,330 MiB cgroup memory cap (kernel 6.17, MGLRU). With the mapped-view gather they completed 930 and 926 steps, touches of their heap took 64 and 60 ms at p99, and 1.33 GiB of the table was mapped. With this gather they completed 9,648 and 9,647 steps, heap touches took 0.28 ms at p99, and 1.3 MiB was mapped. Both modes still swapped part of each process's heap under this deliberately tight cap.

**Tester result (TP=2, discrete GPUs).** A tester ran this head on 2x RTX 5090 at TP=2, with MoE experts offloaded to host memory out of tree, under a 90 GB cgroup memory cap. Decode on real documents matched their previous mmap build, with a sub-second time to first token; the cold first request ran slowly while the table paged in ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58815#issuecomment-5865802209)). That was a 15-minute session at up to 2 concurrent requests.

**Soak.** 817 of 817 requests completed across the ramp, plus 177 of 177 on long shared prefixes, with no errors (before the third commit).

## Not covered

- No throughput or memory comparison against the pinned or device backend. On the test machine, the weights (about 70 GiB) plus a resident 47.7 GiB table do not fit in 128 GB with any KV cache, so neither backend can serve this model there.
- Not validated by the author on a discrete GPU or at TP>1; the only such result is the tester's short run above. The author reproduced TP>1 memory-pressure behaviour only on the CPU, with two processes and a synthetic table under a cgroup memory cap.
- Staging is synchronous. At 16 concurrent requests it is 7.3% of ITL; overlapping the host gather with GPU work is possible follow-up work.
- Under memory pressure, evicted pages are read back from NVMe.
- The checkpoint files must stay unchanged while serving: an in-place overwrite serves the new bytes and truncation stops the engine with an error naming the file and offset. Deleting or renaming them is safe.
- Not supported: PP>1, Model Runner V1, ROCm, elastic EP, weight reload.

## Related

- #54371: the storage backends this extends.
- #58441: not affected (see Design).
- #56177: an expert pool measured on top of PLE mmap to fit this model on discrete GPUs.
- Supersedes #54129.

## AI assistance

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and measurements above.

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR.
- [x] The test plan.
- [x] The test results.
- [x] Documentation update: `docs/features/engram.md`.
- [ ] (Optional) Release notes update.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Share the FlashMLA decode plan across KV cache groups
body:
## Purpose

`DeepseekSparseSWAMetadataBuilder.build()` creates one empty `FlashMLASchedMeta` per DeepSeek-V4 layer type. The first `flash_mla_with_kvcache` call of each type runs FlashMLA's tile-scheduler planner, and the later layers of that type reuse the plan (the comment calls it "shared across all ~60 layers of that type within a decode step").

However, the builder runs once per KV cache group. With the packed KV cache layout, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's sliding-window caches are spread over 8 groups, and each group builds its own holders. So the planner runs once per (group, layer type). A torch-profiler trace of one TP8 decode step shows 18 planner launches in the target model (before layers 0-9 and 20-27) and 3 in the DSpark drafter (one per draft layer), where 4 are enough.

`get_mla_metadata_kernel` is a single 32-thread block with a serial loop over the SM partitions, and every launch sits in front of its layer's attention. On H20 it takes 16.6 µs per launch at 1 request and about 41 µs at 64 requests.

A plan depends on the batch shape and on the values of the decode `topk_length` / `extra_topk_length`. FlashMLA's interface allows reuse only while those values stay the same, but it asserts only shapes and config. Across the KV cache groups of one metadata build pass the values do match:
- The SWA lengths come from the same query and sequence lengths, window, valid-token mask and `replay_start`. Each group builds the mask from its own slot mapping, but every sliding-window group writes each scheduled token, so the masks agree; `replay_start` is one tensor passed to every builder.
- The top-k lengths count the valid entries each index layer writes. Every decode top-k path fills the entries past a row end derived from `seq_lens` and `next_n` alone with -1 (for example `rowEnd` in `csrc/libtorch_stable/sampler.cu`), under the same valid-token mask. So each index layer of a compress ratio yields `min(rowEnd, topk)`.

That second point is also why a group's same-type layers can already share one plan today, though they take their top-k from different index layers.

This PR lets the groups share the holders:
- MRV2's `build_attn_metadata` passes one dict to every group's `CommonAttentionMetadata`, next to the existing `_token_to_req_indices_cache`.
- The sliding-window builder takes its plan holders from that dict, keyed by its block size, causality and index width.

What stays as before:
- Callers that do not pass the dict (the V1 runner, the draft metadata refresh of the autoregressive speculator) keep one plan per group.
- DBO micro-batches and the DSpark drafter build in separate passes, so they never share a plan.
- SM100 does not take this path: it defaults to FlashMLA mega attention, which does not use these plan holders.

Planner launches per decode step drop from 21 to 4.

**Duplicate check.** `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search` for `tile_sched`, `FlashMLASchedMeta`, `get_mla_metadata`, `tile scheduler` and `planner flashmla` shows no PR that shares the plan across KV cache groups.

Related: #58762 (RFC #58638) reuses Mamba/GDN metadata across KV cache groups in the same `build_attn_metadata` loop. This PR does the same for DeepSeek-V4's FlashMLA plans, which are built per group however many groups there are.

## Test Plan

**Setup**
- Hardware: 8× H20 (SM90, 96 GB, NVLink).
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, HF revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`.
- vLLM: "main" is the nightly wheel `0.30.1rc1.dev85+g8b84e1506` as installed; "this PR" is the same wheel with this diff applied as a Python overlay. The three changed files are identical between that nightly and current `main`.

**Server.** TP8 + EP8. DSpark uses synthetic acceptance with a configured mean acceptance length of 3.51, the same distribution in both arms, so acceptance does not depend on the model's outputs:

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --revision dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --max-model-len 262144 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.51,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch","torch_profiler_dir":"<dir>","torch_profiler_activities":["CUDA"],"torch_profiler_with_stack":false,"ignore_frontend":true,"max_iterations":20}'
```

**Load.** One `vllm bench serve` call per point, with these values:

| Point | ISL | OSL | C | N |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8K prompt TTFT | 8192 | 1 | 1 | 5 |
| 1K in / 1K out, C1 | 1024 | 1024 | 1 | 6 |
| 1K in / 1K out, C64 | 1024 | 1024 | 64 | 192 |


```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len <ISL> --random-output-len <OSL> --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency <C> --num-prompts <N> --num-warmups <C> --seed 1
```

**Arms.** Five fresh servers, run in the order B1, A1, A2, B2, B3:
- main (A1, A2);
- a prototype that shared the plans at forward time (B1, B2);
- this PR's metadata-level sharing (B3).

B3, the profile and this PR's GSM8K runs used the diff before `non_causal` joined the cache key. In every measured path the target groups are causal and the drafter builds in its own pass, so that key element changes nothing there. Every arm passes the same `--profiler-config`, which stays idle while the benchmarks run.

**Profile.** 20 decode steps under the torch profiler (`/start_profile`), 1K in / 1K out, at C1 and C64.

**Accuracy.** Full GSM8K (1,319 questions) through `/v1/chat/completions`: 5-shot multi-turn chat, thinking off (`chat_template_kwargs: {"thinking": false}`), temperature 0, seed 123, `max_tokens` 1024, 32 concurrent requests; 

## Test Result

**Serving.** The last column compares B3 with the mean of the main arms. Higher output throughput and lower ITL and TTFT are better.

| Point | Metric | main A1 | main A2 | this PR B3 | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1K in / 1K out, C1 | output tok/s | 317.3 | 318.9 | 326.0 | **+2.5%** |
| 1K in / 1K out, C1 | median ITL (ms) | 10.42 | 10.36 | 10.12 | **−2.6%** |
| 1K in / 1K out, C64 | output tok/s | 1937.6 | 1942.7 | 1949.2 | +0.5% |
| 1K in / 1K out, C64 | median ITL (ms) | 84.15 | 83.84 | 83.51 | −0.6% |
| 8K prompt, C1 | TTFT (ms) | 1216.5 | 1220.0 | 1216.6 | −0.1% |

B3 is a single run. The main arms differ by 0.5% at C1 and 0.3% at C64, so the C64 change is small. The gain is largest at low concurrency, where the planner is a larger share of a short step. Prefill does not plan decode tiles, so TTFT is unchanged. The forward-time prototype, which also launches the planner 4 times per step, measured 325.2 and 329.2 tok/s at C1 and 1957.9 and 1952.6 tok/s at C64.

**Profile** (rank 0, 20 decode steps, B3's code):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Planner launches per step (target + drafter) | 21 | 4 |
| Planner time per step, C1 | 348 µs | 66 µs |
| Planner time per step, C64 | 868 µs | 161 µs |

**Accuracy.** Two full GSM8K runs per side, each on a fresh server:

| GSM8K, 5-shot chat, greedy (1,319 questions) | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Run 1 | 96.97% (1279) | 96.44% (1272) |
| Run 2 | 96.51% (1273) | 96.74% (1276) |
| Mean | 96.74% | 96.59% |
| DSpark acceptance length (runs 1 / 2) | 3.863 / 3.851 | 3.865 / 3.851 |

main's own two runs differ by 6 questions, more than the 2-question gap between the means. Greedy decoding at concurrency 32 varies with how requests are batched, so this rules out a large accuracy change but cannot show identical outputs.

**What covers the new path.** The unit tests below construct `CommonAttentionMetadata` directly, so `_cross_group_cache` stays `None` and they never take the sharing branch. They only show nothing else changed. The new path is covered on H20 by:
- the profile: 4 planner launches per step, so the groups do share;
- the serving runs;
- GSM8K with real DSpark verification.

The serving numbers use synthetic acceptance to measure speed and say nothing about accuracy.

**Tests.** `tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py` and `tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py` give 38 passed and 31 skipped on one H20, with and without this diff. The pinned `ruff` (0.14.0) and `typos` checks pass on the changed files.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py
```

AI assistance: Claude Code helped profile and run the benchmarks. I reviewed every changed line and checked the results above.

title: [Perf][Model Loader] Fast MoE Tri-Modal Ingestion Engine: Cold NVMe Streaming and Layer-Bounded 3D Bulk DMA
body:
## Purpose > **Git Stacking:** Branches from and stacks strictly on **PR #58767** (PR 1) and **PR #58791** (PR 4). Zero git dependency on PR #58770, #58782, or #58794. All 51 standalone unit tests execute and pass in complete isolation. Addresses checkpoint loading bottlenecks on Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models under tensor parallelism on high-bandwidth PCIe Gen5/Gen6 systems: 1. **Cold start disk queue serialization**: - *Problem*: On cold starts, 4–8 TP workers concurrently read shards from disk, causing parallel I/O contention in Linux NVMe queues (<400 MB/s per rank) and taking >35 minutes on large checkpoints. - *Fix (Mode 3/3+1 Streaming Pipeline)*: Rank 0 sequentially streams shards at physical NVMe wire speed (2.14–2.95 GiB/s) using `preadv` + `posix_fadvise(POSIX_FADV_SEQUENTIAL)` into a `/dev/shm` IPC pool registered via `hipHostRegister`/`cudaHostRegister`. A native C++ OpenMP Batch Slice Packer packs slices into contiguous 3D layer staging buffers in <650 ms, while layer-monotonic preorder buffering prevents loader split stalls. 2. **Warm start mmap_lock contention & micro-DMA serialization**: - *Problem*: Multi-rank mmap on warm restarts triggers kernel `mmap_lock` contention, while thousands of uncoalesced 2D slice copies cap transfer rates at 3–4 GiB/s despite 50+ GiB/s PCIe bandwidth. Consequently, warm model reloads spend 8–15+ minutes in CPU-bound micro-DMAs and kernel lock contention instead of completing in under 90 seconds. - *Fix (Mode 1 & Mode 2)*: - **Mode 1 (<= 300 GB / TP <= 2)**: Consolidates 2D slices and fuses 3D SwiGLU projections in a bounded <= 3.8 GiB pinned host pool, dispatching contiguous bulk Host-to-Device DMA at 52+ GiB/s. - **Mode 2 (> 300 GB & TP >= 4)**: Shard-driven direct-to-VRAM with pipelined prefetching and bounded 2-handle sliding window. 3. **Multi-factor structural routing & cache thrashing elimination**: - *Problem*: Calling `posix_fadvise(POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED)` in multi-rank environments purges shared OS page cache pages that peer TP ranks are actively trying to read. This eviction thrashing drops effective throughput from 52+ GiB/s RAM bandwidth down to <400 MB/s disk I/O, causing random worker desynchronization and initialization stalls. - *Fix*: Automatically inspect physical Linux page-cache warmth via `mincore`. Checkpoints with < 80% resident pages automatically route to Mode 3+1; warm checkpoints route to Mode 1 or Mode 2 based on memory budget. Obsolete `posix_fadvise(POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED)` cache eviction hooks are completely eliminated, preventing multi-rank Linux page-cache thrashing across TP peer ranks on shared nodes. --- ## Relation to Merged Upstream PRs #58720 and #57071 PR 6 rebased cleanly onto PR 4 following upstream merges: - **Stacking on Harmonized 3D DMA Pipeline (#58720 / PR 4)**: PR 6 leverages PR 4's contiguous 3D DMA bulk loading interface (`can_bulk_load`), extending it to full-pipeline cold NVMe streaming (Mode 3) and direct-to-VRAM streaming (Mode 2). Where upstream #58720 accelerated 2D string mapping, PR 6 eliminates the physical I/O and DMA bottlenecks across both disk and PCIe. - **Support for Quark MXFP4 & FSE Architectures (#57071 / PR 3)**: Mode 2's direct streaming integrates Fused Shared Experts (FSE) routing, ensuring that Quark-quantized models such as DeepSeek-V4.1 and GLM-5.3-Flash load with full numerical parity and zero shape-padding overhead. - **Upstream Environment Variable Harmonization**: Reconciled `vllm/envs.py` with newly merged upstream flags (`VLLM_MOONCAKE_CONNECTOR_TIMEOUT`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2`) without conflicts, cleanly exposing `VLLM_FAST_MOE_BYPASS`, `VLLM_FAST_MOE_MODE`, `VLLM_FAST_MOE_CROSSOVER_GB`, and `VLLM_MOE_FORCE_O_DIRECT`. --- ## Target Files - `vllm/model_executor/model_loader/moe_fast_loader.py` - `vllm/model_executor/model_loader/direct_block_reader.py` - `vllm/model_executor/model_loader/shared_pinned_pool.py` - `vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py` - `vllm/envs.py` - `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_direct_block_reader.py` - `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_fast_bypass_loader.py` --- ## Test Plan ```bash # Run standalone unit test suites covering bitwise parity, EP, and direct block I/O pytest -v tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_direct_block_reader.py \ tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_fast_bypass_loader.py ``` --- ## Test Result Empirically verified on AMD Instinct MI350X & MI355X (`gfx950`, ROCm 10.0 nightly) across production model architectures: | Model Checkpoint | Quantization Format | TP | Checkpoint Size | Cold: Stock | Cold: Fast MoE | Cold Speedup | Warm: Stock | Warm: Fast MoE | Warm Speedup | |---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next** | Quark MXFP4 | TP4 | 169.7 GiB (131 shards) | 490.71 s | **86.23 s** | **5.69×** (-6m 44s) | 319.88 s | **25.25 s** | **12.67×** (-4m 54s) | | **GLM-5.3-Flash** | Quark MXFP4 | TP4 | 172.4 GiB (62 shards) | 431.43 s | **88.29 s** | **4.89×** (-5m 43s) | 421.63 s | **87.18 s** | **4.84×** (-5m 34s) | | **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** | Hybrid MXFP4/FP8 | TP2 | 474.6 GiB (48 shards) | 2,366.20 s | **222.13 s** | **10.65×** (-35.73 min) | 2,307.80 s | **246.94 s** | **9.35×** (-34.35 min) | | **MiniMax-M3** | Quark MXFP4 | TP4 | 226.0 GiB (59 shards) | 1,023.61 s | **141.51 s** | **7.23×** (-14.70 min) | 960.39 s | **124.49 s** | **7.71×** (-13.93 min) | | **Kimi-K3** | Native FP4 / BF16 | TP8 | 1,453.7 GiB (96 shards) | 1,409.60 s | **329.60 s** | **4.28×** (-18.00 min) | 107.51 s | **87.96 s** | **1.22×** (-19.55 s) | - Passed all 30/30 standalone unit tests in 0.98s (and 51/51 including stacked PR 4 tests) without GPU dependencies. - Bitwise weight parity verified across all loaded parameters (`torch.equal` against stock loader). - End-to-end task accuracy verified within standard generation variance: MMMU on GLM-5.3-Flash (68.34% vs 68.79% stock) and GPQA Diamond on Kimi-K3 (94.44% vs 90.91% stock). - Passed OpenAI `/v1/chat/completions` smoke tests across all evaluated models. --- ## Environment Variables & Configuration PR 6 introduces four environment variables in `vllm/envs.py` for operator control and testing: | Variable | Default | Description | |:---|:---:|:---| | `VLLM_FAST_MOE_BYPASS` | `0` (disabled) | Master opt-in switch. When disabled, vLLM defaults unconditionally to the stock checkpoint loader. | | `VLLM_FAST_MOE_MODE` | `auto` | Pipeline selection:
• **`auto`**: Dynamic selection via page-cache warmth (`mincore`) and model size.
• **`direct_io`**: Forces Mode 3 (cold sequential NVMe streaming + `/dev/shm` IPC broadcast).
• **`direct_vram`**: Forces Mode 2 (warm direct-to-VRAM streaming with prefetch window).
• **`host_staging`**: Forces Mode 1 (warm 3D host staging in bounded $\le 3.8$ GiB pinned RAM). | | `VLLM_FAST_MOE_CROSSOVER_GB` | `300.0` | Scale threshold (GiB) between Mode 1 and Mode 2. Models $\le 300$ GiB stage in pinned host RAM to saturate PCIe (52+ GiB/s); models $> 300$ GiB stream direct to VRAM to bound host memory. | | `VLLM_MOE_FORCE_O_DIRECT` | `0` (disabled) | Forces Linux `O_DIRECT` block I/O (bypassing the page cache) on memory-constrained hosts. Automatically falls back to buffered sequential I/O if unsupported. | --- ## Git Dependency Isolation vs. Multi-Model Runtime Serving To assist upstream maintainers during review, the distinction between **code-level git stacking** and **orthogonal runtime model fixes** is delineated below: 1. **Code-Level Git Dependency Boundary (PR 6 Isolation)**: - PR 6 stacks **strictly on PR 1** ([vllm#58767](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58767)) and **PR 4** ([vllm#58791](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58791)). - PR 6 has **zero code-level git dependency** on PR 2 ([vllm#58770](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58770)), PR 3 ([vllm#58782](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58782)), or PR 5 ([vllm#58794](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58794)). All 51/51 standalone unit tests pass in complete isolation on PR 1 + PR 4. 2. **Multi-Model Benchmark Validation Matrix (Runtime Environment)**: - The Fast MoE loader engine itself is completely model-agnostic and validated on standard Generic MoE architectures using only PR 1 + PR 4 + PR 6. - For empirical evaluation on non-standard architectures (Kimi-K3 and DeepSeek-V4.1), orthogonal model-specific bugfix PRs were included in the serving environment to bypass unrelated modeling issues: | Model Architecture | Quantization Format | Git Stack (PR 1 + PR 4 + PR 6) | PR 2 ([#58770](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58770)) (Model Fix) | PR 3 ([#58782](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58782)) (Model Fix) | PR 5 ([#58794](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58794)) (Model Fix) | Serving Validation Status & Architectural Scope | |:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---| | **Generic MoE** (`GLM-5.3-Flash`, `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next`, `MiniMax-M3`) | Quark MXFP4 / FP8 | **Self-Contained** | - | - | - | **Core Loader Target**: 100% self-contained on PR 6's git stack. Validates cold NVMe streaming, 3D DMA staging, and TP synchronization. | | **Kimi-K3** (`moonshotai/Kimi-K3`) | Native FP4 / BF16 | **Self-Contained** | - | - | Validated With | Validated with PR 5 to disambiguate `.weight_scale` from `.weight` in custom Kimi linear layers (orthogonal to loader engine). | | **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** (`amd/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`) | Hybrid MXFP4/FP8 | **Self-Contained** | Validated With | Validated With | - | Validated with PR 2 (nested `[32, 32]` block discovery) and PR 3 (hybrid scale guard/engram mapping) to bypass DeepSeek modeling bugs. | --- *Claude Code was used to assist in authoring this PR, and all changes have been reviewed and tested by the author on AMD Instinct hardware.* 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Kernel][SM100] Add fused CuTeDSL BF16 gated GEMM for Kimi K3
body:
## Purpose

Add an SM100 CuTe DSL BF16 packed gate/up GEMM with a register-only SiLU or SiTU epilogue for the unquantized, non-sequence-parallel Kimi K3 MLP path.

For packed weights `[2I, K]` and activations `[T, K]`, the kernel computes:

```text
gate = X @ W_gate.T
up   = X @ W_up.T
```

followed by either:

```text
SiLU: output = gate * sigmoid(gate) * up
```

or:

```text
SiTU: output = beta * tanh(gate / beta) * sigmoid(gate)
              * up_branch
```

where `up_branch` is `up` when `linear_beta=None`, otherwise
`linear_beta * tanh(up / linear_beta)`.

Both projections accumulate in FP32 TMEM. The activation is selected through a compile-time `cutlass.const_expr` branch, and the result is written directly as BF16 without materializing the packed gate/up activation in global memory.

## Implementation

- Added `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/cute_dsl/cutedsl_bf16_gated_gemm.py`.
- Added one-CTA and two-CTA Blackwell MMA configurations.
- Loads activation, gate-weight, and up-weight tiles through a pipelined TMA mainloop.
- Reuses each activation tile for both projections.
- Keeps gate and up accumulators in separate TMEM regions.
- Applies SiLU or SiTU in registers.
- Includes the activation mode and epilogue parameters in the compiled-kernel cache key.
- Preserves the existing 26 tactic configurations.
- Added Kimi K3 dispatch and fallback checks.
- Added correctness tests for both activation modes.
- Added a CUDA-graph benchmark under `benchmarks/kernels/`.

## Correctness tests

Hardware:

```text
NVIDIA B200
Compute capability: 10.0
```
The tests cover:

- SiLU and SiTU;
- FP32 PyTorch references;
- BF16 output conversion;
- representative one-CTA and two-CTA tactics;
- ragged token/tile shapes;
- separate activation formulas for both modes.

Tolerance:

```text
rtol=2e-2
atol=0.25
```

Static validation:

```text
git diff --check: passed
ruff check: passed
ruff format --check: passed
```

## CUDA-graph benchmark
Results below are CUDA-graph replay medians on NVIDIA B200. Each row was checked against the separate BF16 output before timing.

| Activation | Tokens | I | K | Tactic | Fused (us) | Separate BF16 (us) | Speedup |

title: [Qwen4Exp] Checkpoint-mapped PLE: read a decode step's cold pages with readahead
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #58439 (stacked on it; the diff to review is the last commit, [3f2142c](https://github.com/jschmied/vllm/commit/3f2142c11117), +94/−1 in 3 files).

With `checkpoint_mapped`, a freshly started server holds almost none of the PLE table in the page cache: loading
the weights streams them through it and evicts the table (0.03 of 47.7 GiB resident at ready on DGX Spark). A
decode step's rows are known only once the previous step has sampled, so the host prefetch has no lead: the GPU
lookup reaches the step's ~57 missing pages at the same time. Today the prefetch touches them serially in one
thread (the `< 4096 rows` path), and the GPU faults them itself, one at a time (~150 µs each).

The misses are not limited to that cold window. Under concurrent agent traffic on new text, steps keep touching rows that are not resident: an independent port of this fill path on v0.30 took eight coding-agent sessions from 62.5 to 93.1 tok/s in aggregate and cold 50K prefill from 1,144 to 1,896 tok/s (@antoniocuegervas, one GB10; [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58835#issuecomment-5862458756)).

This PR fills decode-sized row sets with `MADV_WILLNEED` for every page, which queues readahead and returns at once
so the SSD serves the pages in parallel, followed by `MADV_POPULATE_READ` per page (both through ctypes, which
releases the GIL). The GPU's faults then wait on reads already in flight instead of issuing them one by one. There
is no new option and no wait on the lookup. Larger row sets keep the thread-pool touch; before Linux 5.14 (no
`MADV_POPULATE_READ`) the table falls back to the plain touch.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests (`tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple_pageable.py`), on the branch base (main `378504a54` wheel + #58439):
  30 passed; the two new tests (`test_fill_populates_the_rows`,
  `test_touch_falls_back_when_populate_is_unsupported`) fail on the #58439 head.
- Page fill on an idle box (57 cold pages, page cache dropped, 25 reps).
- Serving A/B on DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, TP=1), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, MTP n=3, KV 4 GiB,
  `checkpoint_mapped`: per fresh start, 6 different 300-token requests (cold pass), then the same 6 again (warm
  pass); 2 starts per arm, alternating; output hashes compared per request.
  Our locally converted checkpoints do not load on current main (`MergedColumnParallelLinear.load_weights` falls
  back to the module for keys it does not know), so the serving A/B ran on our serving stack (nightly
  `1ea7c63f4` + #58439) with this PR's fill path applied to the same `MappedTable.touch`.

## Test Result

Page fill, idle box (median of 25):

| fill | ms |
|---|---|
| serial touch (current) | 4.6–4.7 |
| `MADV_WILLNEED` all pages, then `MADV_POPULATE_READ` per page (this PR) | **0.36** |

Serving (ms per decode step):

| | base, start 1 / 2 | this PR, start 1 / 2 |
|---|---|---|
| cold pass (6 requests) | 59.15 / 59.41 | **56.80 / 56.50** (−2.35 / −2.91) |
| warm pass | 54.73 / 54.71 | 54.95 / 54.75 (+0.22 / +0.04) |

- Faster on 12/12 paired cold requests (−1.37 … −3.78 ms/step); major faults per step during the cold pass
  29–33 → 0.1. Output hashes identical to base in all 48 requests.
- Not measured: TP > 1; discrete GPUs (the backend targets unified memory); tables on slower storage than NVMe.

## Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist
- [x] The purpose of the PR.
- [x] The test plan.
- [x] The test results, before and after.
- [x] Documentation update (`docs/features/engram.md`, one paragraph).

AI assistance: developed with Claude (Anthropic); the submitter reviewed every line.

title: [Bug]: Intermittent Xid 31 MMU fault in pynccl all_reduce during CUDA graph
body:
### Your current environment

vLLM 0.29.0 (image vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0 + ray 2.56.1, pip package b12x 1.3.0)
torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, transformers 5.16.1
GPU: 6x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), driver 595.91.07
Host: Ubuntu, kernel 7.0.0-31-generic, Docker
Cluster: two nodes (4 + 2 GPUs), Ray 2.56.1, 100 GbE direct link
Model: nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4, PP=3 / TP=2, VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=31,29,18

Launch command:

  vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --distributed-executor-backend ray \
    --pipeline-parallel-size 3 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
    --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"b12x","linear_backend":"flashinfer_b12x",
                      "enable_cutedsl_warmup":true,"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true}' \
    --attention-config '{"sparse_mla_force_mqa":true}' \
    --disable-custom-all-reduce --no-async-scheduling \
    --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.98

Note: --disable-custom-all-reduce is required on SM120, so every reduction goes
through the pynccl path.

(collect_env.py output can be provided on request - the engine runs inside a
container on a two-node Ray cluster, so the script does not capture the full
picture.)


### 🐛 Describe the bug

Roughly every third engine start dies during CUDA graph capture. The crash is a
driver-level Xid 31 MMU fault; on the Python side it surfaces as an NCCL error
inside the tensor-parallel all_reduce that is being captured. It is intermittent:
the identical command succeeds on the next attempt, and once the engine is up it
serves for days without a single Xid.

Kernel log:

    NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:41:00): 31, pid=147307, name=ray::vllm_Worke,
    channel 0x00000002, intr 00000000. MMU Fault: ENGINE GRAPHICS GPC0
    GPCCLIENT_T1_0 faulted @ 0x284_e8006000.
    Fault is of type FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ

Engine log - the crash happens at "Capturing CUDA graphs (FULL): 71%|5/7",
in Worker_PP1_TP0:

    reduced = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(hidden_states)
      -> get_tp_group().all_reduce(input_)
      -> torch.ops.vllm.all_reduce(input_, group_name=...)
      -> group._all_reduce_out_place(tensor)
      -> self.device_communicator.all_reduce(input_)
      -> out = pynccl_comm.all_reduce(input_)
      -> self.nccl.ncclAllReduce(...)
      -> RuntimeError: NCCL error: unhandled cuda error
    During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
      torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered

## Controlled comparison

Same hardware, same command, only --enforce-eager added. All other models shut
down, GPUs verified free between runs:

    with graph capture   first-attempt failures ~30 % (6 of 22)   startup ~3:00 min
    --enforce-eager      first-attempt failures 0 of 8            startup ~1:45 min

22 first attempts recorded over five days; 6 died this way. Two further failures
were an unrelated out-of-memory condition and are excluded. In a deliberate
reproduction run today the failure appeared on the 4th consecutive start.

Seven Xid occurrences so far, on all four GPUs of the head node (PCI 01:00,
21:00, 41:00, 61:00), so this is not a defective card. The faulting addresses
repeat across incidents (0x284_e8006000 four times, 0x24f_78006000 twice).

## What we ruled out

- GPU memory pressure: same behaviour at --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 and 0.98.
  At crash time the cards sit at 95.8 GiB of 97.9 GiB, 350 W power cap, 33 C.
- Defective hardware: all four GPUs of the head node produced the fault.
- #50189: that is a *write* fault under concurrent load with the flashinfer_b12x
  MoE backend. We use the native b12x MoE backend, our fault is a *read* at
  startup, and the engine never faults while serving.
- #40742: requires PDL (we set neither TRTLLM_ENABLE_PDL nor
  TORCHINDUCTOR_ENABLE_PDL) and raises "operation not permitted when stream is
  capturing", not a driver Xid.
- #30044: GH200, no Xid, deterministic rather than intermittent.

## Guess at the mechanism

Capturing an ncclAllReduce inside a CUDA graph appears to hit a race. The
faulting addresses repeat across incidents, which looks more like a deterministic
allocation being touched at the wrong moment than random corruption. We cannot
verify this from the outside.

## Workaround

Our autostart script retries up to five times, waiting for all GPUs to be
released between attempts; attempt 1 or 2 normally succeeds. --enforce-eager
avoids the fault entirely at the cost of throughput.

Full engine log, dmesg excerpt and nvidia-smi output of a failing run are saved
and can be attached on request.



### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
