title: [Perf][MRV2] Share GDN, Mamba and Kimi-K3 KDA batch metadata across KV cache groups
body:
## Overview

Move MRV2 cross-group metadata reuse into GDN, Mamba and Kimi-K3 KDA builders, extending merged #58762 to KDA and speculative Mamba.
Explicitly avoiding the MRV1 code reuse from the interim solution in #58762 

## Claims

- Share batch metadata while preserving group-local state, checkpoints and CUDA graph buffers. Every group, the first included, derives those in one per-group function; cross-group tests compare every metadata field with an independent build.
- Extend Mamba aligned-index precompute from plain GDN and nvidia KDA to Mamba1, Mamba2, ShortConv, PLE short-conv and ROCm KDA, and remove redundant slices. No MRV1 features restored.
- PLE short-conv, for non-speculative batches, and ROCm KDA now also share metadata; neither is GPU-tested.
- Move Mamba2's per-group checkpoint regather from #57329 into `_update_state_indices`, so the V1 `update_block_table` path and the MRV2 cross-group path both use it.
- Works with MRV1 fully removed: MRV2 no longer calls `update_block_table` or reads `supports_update_block_table`. With `gpu_model_runner.py` and that API deleted, the 13 Mamba test modules still pass on `eb206ad240` (CPU).

## Validation

Two GB10 nodes, CUDA 13, full Python sources with compatible precompiled binaries. Measured `8abc56f46c` against main `710ac56e69`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/attention/test_{gdn,mamba,replayssm}_metadata_builder.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py::test_pcp_draft_metadata_keeps_graph_padding_in_decode
```

- Focused: **204 passed, no failures/skips**. Wider: **1194 passed / 5 failed / 188 skipped**, versus main **1189 / 4 / 188**.
- Four failures reproduce on main (CUPTI/Proton). Final `b2f2182ce8` fixes the remaining string-device constructor failure; the GPU reproducer passes with MRV2 on/off. No full-suite or benchmark rerun after that one-line fix.
- **103 metadata scenarios match; 279 CUDA captures and 837 changing-input replays per revision pass.** All eight serving synchronization checks pass.
- Serial greedy tokens/logprobs match on all four models. Mixed-batch variation also occurs on main. Kimi uses dummy weights; no quality claim.

Output-interval change with paired 95% intervals: five independent main/PR pairs, four for TP2. CUDA API counts use separate 200-step profiles.

| Model | c1 | c16 | CUDA APIs/step, main→PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Granite-4.0-H-micro, align | −0.45% [−0.58, −0.31] | −0.47% [−0.59, −0.36] | 130.98→68.98 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 + DFlash | −0.12% [−0.56, +0.33] | −0.24% [−0.95, +0.48] | 122.05→122.05 |
| Reduced Kimi-K3, align/RecoverSSM | −0.53% [−1.37, +0.33] | −0.30% [−1.10, +0.50] | 103.08→99.08 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP2/MTP | −0.06% [−1.40, +1.30] | −0.41% [−1.06, +0.24] | 144.97→144.95 / 143.94→143.94 |

Intervals measure engine output timing, not GPU execution time. ROCm, SM100 and single-host multi-GPU cases remain untested. The GPU results above predate the rebase and the per-group function; on CPU, the metadata of 630 two-group scenarios (values and buffer aliasing) is unchanged from the previous revision `01607f5869`. `eb206ad240` on main `02e55d2af3`, Mac CPU: 13 Mamba test modules **260 passed / 86 skipped** versus main **240 / 86**, no failures; pre-commit and mypy pass. No regression means it maintains the performance improvement from #58762 

## Details

Cache lifetime is one metadata build, including capture; keys include cache spec and builder class. #58818 targets FlashMLA and shares cache plumbing; whichever lands second must deduplicate it.

body:
## Purpose

Large HiSparse host pools (384–480 GiB) are pinned twice on 4 KiB pages: by `cudaHostRegister` and by NIXL/RDMA registration. In the shared TP pool, every rank also registers the whole pool. At 450 GiB that's about 118M pages per pass, and we've seen it wedge K8s nodes during startup.

This PR adds an opt-in `host_pool_dir` key on `HiSparseConnector`. When it's set, the host pool is a file-backed mmap in that directory, typically a hugetlbfs mount. With 1 GiB pages, 450 GiB becomes 450 pages, so pinning and MR translation tables become trivial.

```json
{"kv_connector": "HiSparseConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both",
 "kv_connector_extra_config": {"host_pool_gib": 384, "host_pool_dir": "/dev/hugepages-1Gi"}}
```

On K8s: `emptyDir: {medium: HugePages-1Gi}` plus `resources.limits.hugepages-1Gi: <pool size>`. The node must reserve 1 GiB huge pages.

Changes:
- `SharedOffloadRegion` gets a `shm_dir` argument, defaulting to `/dev/shm`, so existing behavior doesn't change. The mapping is rounded to the filesystem page size (`statvfs().f_bsize`); callers still see exactly `total_size_bytes`. On hugetlbfs the tmpfs free-space check is skipped, because hugetlbfs `statfs` reports 0 free without a `size=` limit. `mmap` reserves the huge pages instead, and an `ENOMEM` is turned into a clear error.
- HiSparse shared pool (TP>1, mp): passes `shm_dir` through. Each rank's prefault shard is rounded to the huge page size, so ranks don't fault the same huge page. It skips the psutil RAM check, because reserved huge pages don't count toward `MemAvailable`.
- HiSparse private pool: when `host_pool_dir` is set, allocates an unlinked, pre-faulted file mapping in that directory instead of `torch.empty`.

**Not a duplicate:** #45693 (draft, needs rebase) adds hugetlbfs support to the OffloadingConnector `TieringOffloadingSpec`. This PR targets the HiSparse host pool, which that PR doesn't touch. The two overlap only in `SharedOffloadRegion`, and the change there is kept minimal so they can be reconciled.

**Status: mockup / draft.** Not yet validated on a real hugetlbfs mount (see test plan).

## Test Plan / Results

- `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`: 230 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py -k "hisparse or host_pool"`: 14 passed.
- New unit tests:
  - Region mapping is rounded to a 2 MiB page size while exposing only the logical size, and the free-space check is skipped.
  - The private file-backed pool leaves no file behind and is registered at its exact size.
  - Shared-pool kwargs are covered with and without `host_pool_dir`.
- GPU check (H200): an 8 GiB file-backed private pool registered with `cudaHostRegister` in 3.6 s, and a D2H copy ran at 54 GB/s with correct data. This used tmpfs-backed files, because the dev box has no reserved huge pages and no root.
- TODO: repeat the check on a hugetlbfs mount with 1 GiB pages at 384+ GiB with NIXL enabled.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change; it will be reviewed end-to-end before being marked ready.

title: qwen4_exp: reinterpret FP8 PLE as int8 for SM86 lookup
body:
## Purpose

Fix FP8 E4M3 PLE lookup for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next when using the pinned-host PLE embedding path.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next supports FP8 E4M3 PLE embeddings, which can be stored in CPU pinned memory and accessed from the GPU through the existing pinned-host PLE lookup path. The lookup kernel only needs to copy the FP8 values from the PLE table into the output tensor.

In the current vLLM implementation, passing the FP8 tensor directly to the Triton lookup kernel fails on architectures where Triton does not support the native FP8 pointer type (`fp8e4nv`):

```text
ValueError("type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture.
The supported fp8 dtypes are ('fp8e4b15', 'fp8e5')")
```

Since the kernel only copies the underlying bytes, the FP8 tensor can be reinterpreted as `int8` for the lookup without changing the stored values.

This change:

* Reinterprets FP8 E4M3 PLE storage as `int8` when invoking the pinned-host lookup kernel.
* Reinterprets the output tensor as `int8` for the corresponding byte-wise store.
* Leaves the existing path unchanged for non-FP8 PLE embeddings.

## Test Plan

Tested [Jon-Nielsen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-AWQ-INT4-FP8PLE](https://huggingface.co/Jon-Nielsen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-AWQ-INT4-FP8PLE) on 4× NVIDIA RTX 3090 (SM86).

The model `config.json` was updated for the test with: `"ple_embedding_dtype": "float8_e4m3fn"` which causes vLLM to select `Qwen4ExpPLEFp8EmbeddingMethod` for the FP8 PLE table and enables the checkpoint to use the built-in PLE CPU-offload path on SM86.

The test run used TP4/EP4 with the built-in PLE CPU-offload path.

```bash
vllm serve Jon-Nielsen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-AWQ-INT4-FP8PLE \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}' \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.96 \
  --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --max-model-len auto
```

Validation:

* TP4 / EP4 model initialization succeeded on 4× RTX 3090 (SM86).
* FP8 PLE embedding initialized with `Qwen4ExpPLEFp8EmbeddingMethod`.
* PLE weights loaded on CPU pinned memory.
* The pinned-host lookup executed using the `int8` view of the FP8 storage.
* vLLM server reached `Application startup complete`.
* Sent an inference request after startup.
* Received a valid response.

## Test Result

* Model initialization succeeds on 4× RTX 3090.
* The pinned-host lookup executes using an `int8` view of the FP8 storage.
* Inference succeeds and returns a valid response.

The `int8` reinterpretation is byte-preserving: FP8 E4M3 and `int8` both occupy one byte per element, and the lookup kernel only gathers/stores those bytes.

## References

* [todiadiyatmo/rtx-3090-vllm-recipe-qwen-flash-next](https://github.com/todiadiyatmo/rtx-3090-vllm-recipe-qwen-flash-next): Contains an equivalent local Ampere FP8 PLE lookup workaround, using the PLE data as raw bytes because the upstream pinned-host kernel rejects FP8 on SM86.
* [jon-nielsen/qwen38-flash-next-3090-kit](https://github.com/jon-nielsen/qwen38-flash-next-3090-kit): Independently contains a pinned-PLE byte-move implementation for its SM86 serving stack.

title: [Question][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer: does the 640-token block table reach 32-pool pages on gfx942/gfx950 too?
body:
We found this on hardware vLLM doesn't support (gfx1030, Radeon Pro V620), running GLM-5.3-Flash without aiter. The code path involved is shared with gfx942/gfx950, and we have no MI300/MI355 to check it on. Could someone with one confirm or rule it out?

**What we see.** `Glm5NextIndexerCache` stores pooled keys in pages of 32 pools (storage block 128 tokens at `index_kpool=4`). The hybrid KDA page rule makes the attention block 640. On ROCm the sparse-MLA and indexer backends accept `MultipleOf(16)` (`get_supported_kernel_block_sizes`), so `select_common_block_size` keeps kernel block 640. The indexer metadata builder only converts the table when the storage block is a multiple of the kernel block (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`, prefill and decode branches; unchanged on main):

```python
if (
    kernel_block_size is not None
    and self.kv_cache_spec.block_size != kernel_block_size
    and self.kv_cache_spec.block_size % kernel_block_size == 0
):
    factor = self.kv_cache_spec.block_size // kernel_block_size
    indexer_block_table = (block_table[:, ::factor] // factor).contiguous()
```

128 % 640 ≠ 0, so the 640-token table goes to `get_compressed_slot_mapping` (the kpool writer) and to `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache_triton` as if each entry named one 32-pool page. With per-chunk block allocation:
- pools written before their block exists land in padding;
- positions past the allocated blocks alias block 0;
- positions past the 52-column table (at `max_model_len` 32768) are masked by the gather.

On NVIDIA the kernel block is 64, so the `// factor` branch applies. As far as we can tell nothing here is aiter-specific: the kpool path uses `forward_cuda` on ROCm whether aiter is on or off.

**Reproducer.** One GPU, stock vLLM only, no model: [`repro_rocm_kpool_table.py`](https://github.com/Omnicef/vllm/blob/glm53-v030/tests/local/repro_rocm_kpool_table.py). It writes a 9,432-token prompt in the served prefill chunks with the real ROCm kpool writer and slot mapping, gathers it back with the real gather, and compares against the writer's own output. The two arms are the table as the builder produces it and a page-granular table (block `b` → pages `5b … 5b+4`). On gfx1030, identical over two runs:

```
table as the builder produces it  : ooo000000000000xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmm  (3/74 pages correct)
page-granular table               : oooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooo  (74/74 pages correct)
```

(`o` correct, `0` all-zero, `x` wrong keys, `m` masked.) Above `index_topk`, where the indexer actually selects, this breaks long-context retrieval: a two-fact needle at ~9k tokens failed for us until the table was expanded. If it reproduces on MI300, the fix we use expands each kernel-block id into its storage pages when the kernel block is a multiple of the storage block (about 20 lines in the builder, happy to send).

**Secondary note (tile order).** With aiter off (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` unset), the decode logits fall back to `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch`. It reads each page token-major, while two ROCm writers store values in 16×16 tiles when `block_size > 1`: `indexer_k_quant_and_cache_triton` and the GLM-5.3 kpool writer. DeepSeek-V4's C4A compressor (`compress_norm_rope_store_triton`) writes token-major, so its pages are unaffected. See the correction on #51555 for numbers. aiter's reader passes `Preshuffle=block_size > 1` and isn't affected.

title: [Kimi-K3][ROCm] AttnRes: runtime strides, packed D loads, and per-phase launch tuning
body:
## Purpose

Speed up the AMD AttnRes kernel in `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/attn_res.py`, which runs 187 times per Kimi-K3 decode step (93 layers, `attn_res_block_size` 12, two calls per layer plus the final one).

**Addressing (first commit).** 

- Apply the Triton kernel optmization.
    - remove nonnecessary tl.constexpr to reduce number of kernels
    - provide compiler hints to improve vectorization
    - pipeline loop
    - add heuristics based on the tuned configs 
    - use exp2 fast intrinsics.

**Auxiliary prefix store (third commit).** The five DSpark target layers each launched a bf16 add of `prefix + mlp_output` (about 4.1 us, 0.02 ms/step) and then the next AttnRes added that same pair. AttnRes already rounds that sum to bf16 for the in-place prefix update. This commit stores that packed value into the auxiliary buffer from the same store, and `KimiLinearModel` passes the buffer in instead of adding. The snapshot stride is a runtime pitch, like the other row strides. A non-final pipeline-parallel rank whose last layer is an auxiliary layer still uses one `torch.add` into that buffer, because no following AttnRes runs on that rank.

## Test Plan

- First commit: bit-compare against the previous kernel on MI355X (gfx950), Triton 3.8:
  - decode, hidden 7168, with delta and output norm
  - padded rows (prefix/delta/block pitches not divisible by 16)
  - prefill, 320 tokens
  - `num_blocks == 0` with a block write and output norm
- First commit: confirm the generated AMDGCN still uses `buffer_load_dwordx4` / `buffer_store_dwordx4` on those launches.
- Second commit: the same ISA check on every new launch config (decode single-tile `BLOCK_L` of 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16 with 8 warps; prefill `BLOCK_L = 1`, 4 warps, 2 stages), including a padded-row launch.
- Second commit: sweep `BLOCK_L` x `num_warps` x loop stages per block count (0-8) at decode (8 tokens) and prefill (512 tokens), graph-replayed on MI355X with no profiler.
- Both commits: `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_attn_res.py` from the full checkout.
- Timing of the final kernel over the K3 decode call mix, and prefill at 320 tokens.
- Third commit: `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_attn_res.py` checks the auxiliary snapshot equals the bf16 prefix update, including padded rows and the no-delta path.
- Fifth commit: `test_amd_attn_res.py` adds 255 and 256 tokens, where the launch changes from the decode tile to the prefill tile. The FP8 test also passes the auxiliary snapshot, because the DSpark target path uses both in one launch. `test_eagle3.py` checks that `KimiDecoderLayer` gives its snapshot to the pre-attention AttnRes.

## Test Result

**Correctness.** The first commit matched the previous kernel bit-for-bit on the four shapes above, including the in-place prefix update and the optional block write, and its compiled AMDGCN still contains `buffer_load_dwordx4` and `buffer_store_dwordx4` (8–20 loads and 4–8 stores, depending on the constexpr variant).

The second commit keeps that packing. On MI355X, every launch config above compiles to `buffer_load_dwordx4` and `buffer_store_dwordx4`:

| launch | loads x4 | stores x4 |
|---|---:|---:|
| decode, 0 blocks, write + output norm, `BLOCK_L=1`, 8 warps | 4 | 4 |
| decode, 1 block, delta + output norm, `BLOCK_L=2`, 8 warps | 12 | 4 |
| decode, 2 blocks, delta + output norm, `BLOCK_L=4`, 8 warps | 15 | 4 |
| decode, 4 blocks, delta + output norm, `BLOCK_L=8`, 8 warps | 19 | 4 |
| decode, 8 blocks, delta + output norm, `BLOCK_L=16`, 8 warps | 27 | 4 |
| decode, 5 blocks, padded rows, write, `BLOCK_L=8`, 8 warps | 6 | 2 |
| prefill, 4 blocks, delta, `BLOCK_L=1`, 4 warps, 2 stages | 24 | 8 |
| prefill, 8 blocks, delta + output norm, `BLOCK_L=1`, 4 warps, 2 stages | 28 | 8 |

Aligned rows use only those packed accesses (no `dwordx2`, scalar `dword`, or 16-bit load/store). The padded-row launch still has a 16-bit fallback where the pitch is not divisible by 16 (103 loads, 32 stores), the same path as the first commit. No scratch traffic and no VGPR spills on any of these launches.

The second commit is no longer bit-identical to the previous kernel: the single-tile reduction order, the pipelined loop and `exp2` move outputs by at most one bf16 ulp. The in-place prefix update and the block write are unchanged. `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_attn_res.py` from the full checkout at `985e9792` (`PYTHONPATH` on `xguo/attn-res-triton-hints`, not a copied kernel file): 9 passed on MI355X in 9.55s.

**Performance.** MI355X, hidden 7168, graph-replayed, no profiler. Decode is weighted by the K3 call mix (187 calls per step):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| decode, 8 tokens | 6.65 us/call, 1.24 ms/step | **5.59 us/call, 1.05 ms/step** |
| prefill, 320 tokens, 4 blocks | 13.6 us | **11.9 us** |
| prefill, 320 tokens, 8 blocks | 20.6 us | **17.2 us** |

Per block count at decode, the single-tile config was the fastest at every block count from 1 to 8. The largest win is 8 blocks (9.52 -> 7.46 us), where the previous `BLOCK_L = 4` needed three loop trips. Pipelining helps configs that actually loop (e.g. 1-source tiles at 8 blocks, 13.5 -> 11.0 us), but at decode it did not beat the single tile. At prefill, 2 stages were consistently faster (7–11%) and 3 stages were often slower.

**Third to fifth commits.** MI355X (gfx950), rebased on `main`, latest ROCm nightly:

```bash
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_attn_res.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_eagle3.py
```

30 passed. The full `tests/models/kimi_k3` folder: 319 passed, 83 skipped. `test_latent_moe_tail.py` did not collect, because the image has no `ray` module. When the decoder layer does not pass the snapshot, the new wiring test fails.

AI assistance: Cursor was used for code editing, benchmark analysis, test execution, and drafting this PR description.

title: [Bug]:  GLM-5.3-MXFP4 DP8 without EP crashes during FlashInfer autotune with CUDA illegal memory access
body:
### Your current environment


Hardware: 8× NVIDIA GB300  
vLLM commit: `4be061c5afab`  
PyTorch: `2.13.0+cu130`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Description

GLM-5.3-MXFP4 fails to start with TP1/DP8 and expert parallelism disabled. The crash occurs during the 32K-token FlashInfer autotune dummy run in sparse MLA logical-to-physical top-k index conversion.

This reproduces on a clean vLLM `main` build and is unrelated to our CUTLASS MXFP4 EP changes.

### Reproduction

Hardware: 8× NVIDIA B300  
vLLM commit: `4be061c5afab`  
PyTorch: `2.13.0+cu130`

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \
VLLM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_EXPERT_FP4_MOE=262144 \
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-MXFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser glm47 \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --data-parallel-size-local 8 \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
  --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --block-size 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
Do not pass --enable-expert-parallel.
Error
All eight DP workers fail after:
Running FlashInfer autotune with 32768 tokens
The relevant stack is:
flashinfer_mla_sparse.py::forward_mqa
sparse_mla_attention.py::_convert_logical_to_physical_topk
index_group.py::_convert_once
sparse_utils.py::triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index

RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered
Additional information
Without VLLM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_EXPERT_FP4_MOE=262144, startup fails earlier because DP8 all-gather produces m_numtopk=2097152, exceeding the default MXFP4 capacity.
PR #56825 is already present in this commit. That PR fixes a piecewise CUDA graph event error, while this failure occurs in the workspace-overflow conversion path during FlashInfer autotune.
```

title: [Perf][Model Loader] Fault in mmap'd weight pages before host-to-device copies on integrated GPUs
body:
## Purpose

Addresses #58726.

On integrated GPUs (DGX Spark / GB10), the shared weight loaders copy each checkpoint tensor to the GPU with `param.copy_(loaded_weight)` straight from the safetensors mmap view. For a contiguous, same-dtype source, PyTorch passes that pageable pointer directly to the driver copy, so the page faults happen inside the copy. On GB10 that is several times slower than faulting the same pages on the CPU first: 1.7–3.0 ms vs 0.08–0.64 ms per 800 KiB tensor in #58726. `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` has at least 140k such tensors, and its main weight load takes 452 s from NFS and 475 s from local NVMe.

This adds `copy_weight_(dst, src)` to `vllm/model_executor/utils.py`. On an integrated GPU it touches one byte per page of `src`, then runs `dst.copy_(src)`. It is used at the 26 copy sites of the shared loaders: `linear.py` (8), `parameter.py` (6), `routed_experts.py` (8), `vocab_parallel_embedding.py` (2) and `default_weight_loader` (2).

- **Gate:** `current_platform.is_integrated_gpu()` for a CUDA destination, cached per device. On a discrete Ada Lovelace GPU the same micro-benchmark shows the plain copy is fastest in every cache state, and the touch adds 0.022–0.028 ms per tensor, so it stays off there. When off, the extra checks cost ~0.46 µs per call (0.91 vs 0.45 µs for a 16-byte CPU copy), about 0.14 s per 300k tensors.
- **Only contiguous, same-dtype CPU sources are touched.** Non-contiguous or dtype-converting copies already go through a CPU temporary in PyTorch (`copy_requires_temporaries` in `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Copy.cu`), which faults the pages on the CPU.
- **Why at the copy site rather than in `safetensors_weights_iterator`** (discussed with @gitbisector in #58726):
  - Under TP each rank touches only the slice it copies. A prefault in the iterator read whole tensors: ~287 GiB per rank on DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4, and a slower load at the default `read_ahead_kb=128`.
  - The touch runs right before the copy, so a consumer that buffers the weight stream can't have the pages evicted in between.
  - Tensors a model serves from the mapping (#58439) are never copied, so they are never touched, and no size cap is needed.
- **Not covered:** model-specific loaders that call `.copy_()` or `.to(device)` themselves keep today's behaviour until they call the helper. Its docstring says to. @stecasta routed one such out-of-tree expert loader through it: ~55 GiB of copies moved onto the touch path, and its weight loading took about 70% less time.
- **Measured only on GB10** (TP=1 below, TP=4 by @gitbisector). Other integrated devices, such as Jetson Orin / Thor, will take the touch path but are untested. I haven't checked what GH200 reports as `is_integrated`; if it reports 0, nothing changes there.

## Test Plan

- New tests in `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py`:
  - `test_copy_weight_prefault_copies_exact_bytes`: with the gate forced on, the helper accepts 0-d, empty, bf16, fp8 and dim-1-narrowed sources and copies them byte for byte. CI has no integrated GPU, so this is the only coverage of that path.
  - `test_copy_weight_prefault_maps_the_mmap_view`: after the call, every page of a safetensors view is mapped (`/proc/self/smaps` Rss of the file mapping). With the touch disabled it fails: 64 KiB mapped vs 4 MiB.
- Existing CPU-runnable loader tests, before and after the change.
- `pre-commit` on the changed files, including `mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual`.
- Boot A/B on a DGX Spark.

```bash
# CPU only, repo on PYTHONPATH inside vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 (torch 2.13.0+cu130), no GPU
docker run --rm -v $PWD:/w:ro -e PYTHONPATH=/w -w /w --entrypoint bash vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 -c \
  "uv pip install --system -q tblib pytest && python3 -m pytest -q \
   tests/model_executor/test_utils.py \
   tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py tests/kernels/moe/test_fp8_tp_loading.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_tying.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_gpt_oss_weight_loading.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py"

pre-commit run --files <changed files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <changed files>
```

## Test Result

- `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py`: 18 passed (12 existing, 6 new).
- Loader tests: 216 passed, 5 skipped. 38 tests fail with and without the change, the same set on both, all because the container has no GPU:
  - 18 error at setup with `Failed to infer device type`.
  - 18 `test_reload` cases fail because `current_platform.device_count` is `None`.
  - 2 `test_fp8_tp_default_keeps_refined_layout[*-triton]` cases can't confirm the Triton kernel, so the layer pads its TP shard instead of refining the block shape.
- `pre-commit` and `mypy-3.12` passed.

### Boot A/B, DGX Spark (GB10), TP=1

Nine full server boots of `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, interleaved, with the client page cache for the checkpoint dropped before each one.

- **Build:** the image is vLLM v0.30.0 plus out-of-tree patches, not `main`. The helper is copied from this branch and applied to v0.30.0's copies of the same files (25 sites; v0.30.0's `_load_w2` has no chunk loop). It predates a cleanup that renamed the gate function and dropped a redundant `numel() > 0` check, which doesn't change behaviour here. A counting wrapper, not part of this PR, logged the gate and how many copies were touched.
- **Out-of-tree patches on in every arm:** the expert-name index (= #58720, merged), an MTP name prefilter, and the PLE table served from the mapping (never copied).
- **Storage:** NFS with the client's `read_ahead_kb` at 16384, or local NVMe at the default 128.

| loader | storage | main load (s) | MTP load (s) | start → `/health` (s) | swapped out, start → KV profile (GiB) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| stock | NFS | 451.8 | 36.1 | 584 | 4.4 |
| this PR (3 boots) | NFS | 25.9 / 27.0 / 28.0 | 0.8 | 124–129 | 3.6–4.3 |
| stock | NVMe | 475.2 | 31.7 | 609 | 4.2 |
| this PR (2 boots) | NVMe | 46.4 / 54.5 | 2.6–2.9 | 149–153 | 3.2–4.0 |
| *out-of-tree, for reference: `pread` tensors ≤ 64 MiB in the iterator, clone / chunked copy above that* | NFS / NVMe | 21.0 / 88.5 | 1.2 / 1.3 | 113 / 179 | 0 / 0 |

- The gate logged `cuda:0 = True` in every boot with this PR. By the counter's last line (140,000 calls), 139,965 copies (63.4 GiB) had been touched. The other 35 were copies PyTorch stages through a CPU temporary anyway.
- Greedy outputs (5 prompts × 400 tokens, temperature 0) and first-token logprobs are identical in all nine boots, and decode speed is unchanged. No accuracy eval was run here: the touch only reads the source, so the loaded weights are byte-identical (unit test above). @stecasta's GSM8K run is below.
- Swap: loading from mmap views pushes 3.2–4.4 GiB of other memory to swap on this 128 GB machine, and stock loading does it as much as this PR. The pread variant doesn't map the files and doesn't swap. vLLM counts the swapped-out memory as free when it sizes the KV cache. I haven't looked into why the kernel swaps here.

### TP=1, warm cache (from @hclsys, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#issuecomment-5919067348))

`Qwen3-1.7B` on one GB10, `load_format=safetensors`, `enforce_eager`, page cache warm, fresh process per run, this branch vs its merge-base `77871126f9`.

| | `Loading weights took` | `LLM()` init |
|---|---:|---:|
| merge-base (3 runs) | 20.2–23.7 s | 44.4–54.8 s |
| this PR (2 runs) | 0.50 / 0.69 s | 26.3 / 29.4 s |

The third base run came after the PR runs, so the difference isn't cache order. With the cache warm the time isn't disk reads but the faults taken through a fresh mapping during the copy. On a discrete RTX PRO 6000 the touch makes no difference, ~0.1 ms per tensor either way (@gitbisector, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58726#issuecomment-5918595410)).

### TP=1, cold cache (from @stecasta, [review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#pullrequestreview-5496877797))

`nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` with a DFlash2 drafter on one GB10, v0.31.0 plus internal patches with this PR applied as a Python overlay. Checkpoint on local disk (`read_ahead_kb=128`), page cache dropped before every boot, two boots per arm.

| | `Loading weights took`, main model | `Model loading took` | start → `/health` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| stock | 96.5 / 96.7 s | 122 / 122 s | 595 / 591 s |
| this PR | 9.5 / 9.8 s | 16 / 16 s | 486 / 486 s |

GSM8K-256 with this PR: 244/256, in line with stock. Minimum `MemAvailable` (~38.5 GiB) and peak swap (0.5 GiB) during load were the same in both arms.

### TP=4 (from @gitbisector, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#issuecomment-5852543296))

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` on four GB10s, this PR ported to a v0.28.1-based build (25 of the 26 sites), load-only boots, page cache dropped before each, arms interleaved. Times are `Model loading took` on the slowest rank.

| `read_ahead_kb` | boots | stock | this PR | read per rank vs stock |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 3 + 3 | 192–195 s | 156–161 s (−18%) | +0–8 GiB |
| 128 | 3 + 3 | 205–207 s | 149–151 s (−27%) | +0–8 GiB |
| 1024, consumer that sorts the stream | 1 + 1 | 248 s | 225 s | +2–10 GiB |

At 128 the iterator-level prefault made this load slower (202 → 241 s) because every rank read whole tensors (~287 GiB); at the copy site each rank reads about what stock reads. Most of the gain is the slowest rank catching up: in stock, the ranks holding slices 0 and 2 lag by 25–60 s on small same-dtype slices (expert scales, FP8 attention rows). The routed experts there are `I8` loaded into `uint8` params, a converting copy that PyTorch already stages on the CPU, so the helper touches 5.6 of 72.3 GiB per rank.

## Duplicate-work check

- No open PR references #58726; searches for "prefault", "integrated gpu weight loading" and "mmap page fault copy" found none that change these copy sites.
- #49991 (ROCm, clones in the iterator behind an env flag, for a KFD copy-on-write issue) and #50794 (Ascend, clones before the H2D copy to avoid a DMA hang) handle the same copies on other platforms, for different causes.
- #57973 (safetensors prefetch loader) and #55985 (fastsafetensors fit planner) are alternative load paths.
- #58857 / #58782 remove the `sorted()` buffering in the DeepSeek-V4 VL wrappers; complementary to this.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted (Claude Opus 5.5): implementation, tests, the boot A/B scripts, and a draft of this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and boots above on my own machines.

title: [ROCm][Perf][WIP] Extend a4w4 MoE default to DeepSeek V4 (untested)
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #58819 (DeepSeek V4.1 a4w4 default). DeepSeek V4 shares the
same MoE shape and AITER `GateMode.SEPARATED` dispatch path as V4.1, so this
extends `_use_mxfp4_w4a4_moe_activation`'s auto-detection to
`deepseek_v4`/`deepseek_v4_text` as well.

**Status: DeepSeek V4 is untested end-to-end.** Only AITER's own
kernel-level cosine-similarity check (`op_tests/test_moe_2stage.py`) has run
against this shape — no GSM8K accuracy check or AgentX perf sweep on a real
DeepSeek V4 checkpoint yet, unlike V4.1 (see #58819's Test Plan). Opening as
**draft** to track this and get that validation done before merge; do not
merge until then.

## Test Plan & Result

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py -v
pre-commit run --files vllm/envs.py vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/config.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py
```
36 passed, 1 pre-existing failure (`test_aiter_fused_moe_fake_tensor_support`,
missing AITER JIT module, unrelated, reproduces on unmodified `main`).
pre-commit: clean.

**Still needed before merge:** GSM8K (or equivalent) accuracy run and an
AgentX/perf sweep on a real DeepSeek V4 checkpoint, matching what #58819 did
for V4.1.

## Duplicate-work check

Same heuristic/gate-mode path as #58819; no other open PR touches it for
DeepSeek V4.

## AI-assistance disclosure

Drafted with Cursor (Claude Sonnet 5): extending the model-type detection
and this PR description. I (the submitting human) reviewed the diff; the
GSM8K/AgentX validation above is still outstanding and will be run before
this leaves draft.

title: [Bug][ROCm]: GPU memory fault in AITER MLA FP8 prefill under async scheduling (race on persistent PS metadata)
body:
**Fix:** #58887 plans FP8 prefill metadata into two pinned host buffers and copies the active buffer on the current stream, tracked by a CUDA event, so the update is ordered after in-flight prefill kernels. AITER follow-up: [ROCm/aiter#5879](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/5879). ## Environment | | | | --- | --- | | Image | `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098` | | vLLM | `0.30.1rc1.dev143+g29468dde8` | | ROCm / HIP | ROCm 10 (HIP 7.15), torch `2.12.0+rocm10.0.0`, triton `3.8.0` | | AITER | `amd-aiter 0.1.22.post1` | | GPU | 8x MI355X (gfx950) | | Model | `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`, TP8 (12 attention heads per rank, padded to 16 for AITER) | The same nightly on ROCm 7.2 (`nightly-29468dde…`, ROCm 7.2.3, triton 3.7.1) has the same race. Its Python and AITER ASM kernels are byte-identical to the ROCm 10 image. Default ROCm 7.2 serving often hides the fault; the standalone reproduction below faults on both runtimes. See [Why ROCm 7.2 serving often stays up](#why-rocm-72-serving-often-stays-up). Common server settings for the runs below: TP8, FP8 KV cache, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, `max_num_seqs=256`, `max_model_len=131072`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, async scheduling, `max_cudagraph_capture_size=512`. `$HF_HOME` is the local Hugging Face cache. Dummy weights are enough for the crash. ## Bug With `ROCM_AITER_MLA`, an FP8 KV cache, and async scheduling, serving hits a GPU memory fault under load. The FP8 MLA prefill path (`mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd` and `mla_reduce_v1`, one launch per layer) reads scheduling metadata from one set of persistent device buffers. Every batch that contains a new prefill rewrites those buffers from the host, and that write is not ordered on the current stream. Step N+1's plan can land while step N's prefill kernels are still queued, so step N runs with step N+1's work and reduce maps. When the stale indices stay in bounds, the prefill output is silently wrong and the process stays up. The measured accuracy runs did not show that drop; see [Accuracy](#accuracy). Decode is unaffected. Its plan comes from `get_mla_metadata_v1`, a device-side kernel on the current stream ([L1221](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py#L1221)). ## Reproduction ### Kimi-K3 ```bash docker run --rm --entrypoint '' --network host --ipc host \ --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --shm-size 128G \ -v $HF_HOME/hub:/root/.cache/huggingface/hub \ -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \ -e VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2=1 \ -e VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \ vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098 \ vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --load-format dummy --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --trust-remote-code --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \ --max-model-len 131072 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 256 --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --max-cudagraph-capture-size 512 \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' --async-scheduling ``` ```bash python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm --dataset-name random \ --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --port 8000 --request-rate inf \ --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0.8 \ --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 1024 --warmup-requests 32 --seed 4 ``` On a given machine the fault is deterministic for a given request stream. Whether a stream triggers it varies, so try a few. 128 prompts is usually too little exposure. Each fault shows up in under 10 minutes, including server startup. | Stream (8k/1k) | Fault at request | With the fix | | --- | --- | --- | | concurrency 32, 1024 prompts, seed 4 | 111 (x3; also with `--enforce-eager`) | 1024/1024 | | concurrency 32, 2048 prompts | 79 | 2048/2048 | | concurrency 64, 1024 prompts | 61 | 1024/1024 | | concurrency 32, 1024 prompts, seed 5 | 117 | 1024/1024 | ### DeepSeek-V3 Same image and the same shared flags, with `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3` (TP8, 128 heads, 16 per rank, so no head padding). Drop the Kimi-K3 parser, tool-call, and multimodal options: ```bash docker run --rm --entrypoint '' --network host --ipc host \ --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --shm-size 128G \ -v $HF_HOME/hub:/root/.cache/huggingface/hub \ -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \ vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098 \ vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --trust-remote-code \ --max-model-len 131072 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --max-num-seqs 256 --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-cudagraph-capture-size 512 \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' --async-scheduling ``` Same `sglang.bench_serving` command, with `--model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3`. `--load-format dummy` is enough for the crash. | Workload | Unpatched | With the fix | | --- | --- | --- | | 8k/1k, concurrency 32, 1024 prompts, seed 4 | fault at request 111 | 1024/1024 | | `lm_eval` gsm8k 5-shot, `num_concurrent=64` | GPU memory fault (x2), after ~80 s | completes; scores in [Accuracy](#accuracy) | The engine dump matches the Kimi-K3 crash batch: one new prefill (8175 tokens in the benchmark, ~1k tokens on gsm8k) plus the running requests. gsm8k's short prompts trigger it too. The race is in the shared FP8 MLA prefill path. Output throughput was not recorded separately for DeepSeek-V3. ### Standalone (one gfx950 GPU, no server) Same AITER calls vLLM makes. Faults on ROCm 7.2 and ROCm 10: 1. Plan batch A (one 8175-token prefill, no partial tiles) into persistent device buffers with `aiter.get_ps_metadata_v1`. 2. On a non-blocking `torch.cuda.Stream()` (the stream vLLM uses), queue a GPU delay (`torch.cuda._sleep`), then A's `mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd` and `mla_reduce_v1`. 3. Immediately plan batch B (three prefills: 6992, 6896, 2495 tokens) into the same buffers from the host, as step N+1's metadata build does under async scheduling. 4. Synchronize and compare A's output with a reference run. | Mode | ROCm 7.2 | ROCm 10 | | --- | --- | --- | | vLLM's current pattern | GPU memory fault on the first iteration | GPU memory fault on the first iteration | | `stream.synchronize()` before planning B | output matches reference | output matches reference | | plan B into pinned host memory, `copy_(non_blocking=True)` on the stream | output matches reference | output matches reference | The fault has the serving signature: `Memory access fault ... on address 0x1d000` / `0x64000`, `Write access to a read-only page` (or `Unknown`). Script: `aiter_ps_metadata_race.py` ([gist](https://gist.github.com/amd-mghanimi/970e190ceea417467594980b96f3604b)). Run it inside either vLLM ROCm image with `python3 aiter_ps_metadata_race.py`. Add `--streams 12` for the per-stream table in the ROCm 7.2 section.
aiter_ps_metadata_race.py ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Standalone reproducer: AITER MLA FP8 prefill plan rewritten while in use (vLLM async scheduling). Mirrors vLLM's ROCM_AITER_MLA FP8 prefill (rocm_aiter_mla.py @ 29468dde, _build_fp8_prefill_ps_metadata + _mla_fp8_prefill_attn) on one gfx950 GPU: 1. Plan batch A (one 8175-token prefill) into persistent device buffers with aiter.get_ps_metadata_v1, as vLLM does. 2. On a non-blocking stream (as vLLM uses), queue a GPU delay standing in for step N's earlier layers, then A's mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd + mla_reduce_v1. 3. Immediately plan batch B (three prefills) into the same buffers from the host, as step N+1's metadata build does under async scheduling. 4. Synchronize and compare A's output with a reference. Default run, one stream, three modes (each in its own process, since a GPU fault kills it): race vLLM's current pattern: device outputs, stream-less hipMemcpy inside AITER. synced stream.synchronize() before planning B. fixed plan into pinned host staging, copy_(non_blocking=True) on the stream (the vLLM fix). python3 aiter_ps_metadata_race.py Expected on ROCm 7.2 and ROCm 10 alike: race faults, synced and fixed match the reference. Why ROCm 7.2 serving can still look fine: python3 aiter_ps_metadata_race.py --streams 12 runs the race on each of 12 non-blocking streams. It first probes which streams a stream-less 1 KiB hipMemcpy waits behind, i.e. which share the null stream's in-order hardware queue. AITER's first plan copy is that small, so it runs as a copy kernel on the null stream's queue. Only prefill streams on a shared queue are protected. Queue assignment differs between ROCm versions and runtime settings (try DEBUG_HIP_DYNAMIC_QUEUES=1 or GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=16 on ROCm 7.2). """ import argparse import ctypes import json import os import subprocess import sys import time TILE_Q = 256 # _FP8_PREFILL_TILE_Q NHEAD = 16 # 12 heads/rank (Kimi-K3 TP8) replicate-padded to 16 for the ASM prefill QK_DIM, V_DIM = 192, 128 # mla_pfl_qh192_vh128_* MAX_REQS, MAX_TOKENS = 256, 16384 BATCH_A = [8175] # the crash batch's prefill BATCH_B = [6992, 6896, 2495] # a following multi-prefill batch PLAN_KW = dict(qhead_granularity=1, qlen_granularity=TILE_Q, kvlen_granularity=128, block_size=1, is_causal=True) def alloc_plan_buffers(torch, device, pin=False): from aiter import get_ps_metadata_info_v1 info = get_ps_metadata_info_v1(batch_size=MAX_REQS, num_head_k=NHEAD, max_qlen=MAX_TOKENS, qlen_granularity=TILE_Q) bufs = [] for size, dtype in info: shape = size if isinstance(size, tuple) else (size,) bufs.append(torch.empty(*shape, dtype=dtype, device=device, pin_memory=pin and device == "cpu")) return bufs # work_meta, work_indptr, work_info, reduce_indptr, reduce_final, reduce_partial def plan(torch, bufs, seq_lens): from aiter import get_ps_metadata_v1 lens = torch.tensor(seq_lens, dtype=torch.int32) qo = torch.zeros(len(seq_lens) + 1, dtype=torch.int32) qo[1:] = lens.cumsum(0) get_ps_metadata_v1(qo, qo.clone(), lens, 1, NHEAD, *bufs, **PLAN_KW) class PrefillA: def __init__(self, torch): self.torch = torch torch.manual_seed(0) total = sum(BATCH_A) fp8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn self.q = (torch.randn(total, NHEAD, QK_DIM, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(fp8) self.k = (torch.randn(total, NHEAD, QK_DIM, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(fp8) self.v = (torch.randn(total, NHEAD, V_DIM, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(fp8) self.qo = torch.tensor([0, total], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") self.kv_indices = torch.arange(total, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") self.total = total self.one = torch.ones((), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda") # vLLM carves per-call scratch from a pre-reserved workspace. self.workspace = torch.empty(64 << 20, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda") def launch(self, dev_bufs, num_partial_tiles): from aiter import mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd, mla_reduce_v1 torch = self.torch shapes = [((num_partial_tiles * TILE_Q, NHEAD, V_DIM), torch.float32), ((num_partial_tiles * TILE_Q, NHEAD), torch.float32), ((self.total, NHEAD), torch.float32)] scratch, off = [], 0 for s, d in shapes: n = torch.Size(s).numel() * torch.empty((), dtype=d).element_size() scratch.append(self.workspace[off:off + n].view(d).view(s)) off += (n + 255) // 256 * 256 logits, lse, final_lse = scratch _, work_indptr, work_info, reduce_indptr, reduce_final, reduce_partial = dev_bufs out = torch.empty(self.total, NHEAD, V_DIM, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd(self.q, self.k, self.v, self.qo, self.qo, self.kv_indices, work_indptr, work_info, max(BATCH_A), QK_DIM ** -0.5, True, logits, lse, out, self.one, self.one, self.one) mla_reduce_v1(logits, lse, reduce_indptr, reduce_final, reduce_partial, TILE_Q, 0, out, final_lse) return out def child(mode, num_streams, index, iters, delay_ms, probe): import numpy as np import torch print(f"HIPVER {torch.version.hip}", flush=True) torch.zeros(1, device="cuda") # the null stream exists first, as in frameworks # Load AITER and allocate before creating streams, as vLLM does (model load, then streams). dev_bufs = alloc_plan_buffers(torch, "cuda") staging = [alloc_plan_buffers(torch, "cpu", pin=True) for _ in range(2)] a = PrefillA(torch) plan(torch, dev_bufs, BATCH_A) torch.cuda.synchronize() streams = [torch.cuda.Stream() for _ in range(num_streams)] # HIP binds a stream to a hardware queue at its first launch; launch on every stream once, # in order, so the stream-to-queue mapping does not depend on the tested index. for s in streams: with torch.cuda.stream(s): torch.cuda._sleep(1000) torch.cuda.synchronize() stream = streams[index] with torch.cuda.stream(stream): torch.cuda._sleep(1_000_000) t0, t1 = torch.cuda.Event(True), torch.cuda.Event(True) t0.record() torch.cuda._sleep(50_000_000) t1.record() t1.synchronize() cycles = int(50_000_000 * delay_ms / t0.elapsed_time(t1)) if probe: hip = ctypes.CDLL("libamdhip64.so") hip.hipMemcpy.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_size_t, ctypes.c_int] dst = torch.empty(1024, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda") src = np.zeros(1024, dtype=np.uint8) hip.hipMemcpy(dst.data_ptr(), src.ctypes.data, 1024, 1) torch.cuda.synchronize() shared = [] for j, s in enumerate(streams): with torch.cuda.stream(s): torch.cuda._sleep(cycles) t = time.perf_counter() hip.hipMemcpy(dst.data_ptr(), src.ctypes.data, 1024, 1) if (time.perf_counter() - t) * 1000.0 > 0.5 * delay_ms: shared.append(j) torch.cuda.synchronize() print("PROBE " + json.dumps(shared), flush=True) with torch.cuda.stream(stream): plan(torch, dev_bufs, BATCH_A) ref = a.launch(dev_bufs, int(dev_bufs[3][-1].item())) torch.cuda.synchronize() mismatches, walls = 0, [] for it in range(iters): with torch.cuda.stream(stream): if mode == "fixed": host = staging[it % 2] plan(torch, host, BATCH_A) for d, h in zip(dev_bufs[1:], host[1:]): d.copy_(h, non_blocking=True) tiles = int(host[3][-1]) else: plan(torch, dev_bufs, BATCH_A) tiles = int(dev_bufs[3][-1].item()) torch.cuda._sleep(cycles) # step N's earlier layers still running out = a.launch(dev_bufs, tiles) # step N's prefill reads the plan if mode == "synced": stream.synchronize() t = time.perf_counter() if mode == "fixed": # step N+1's plan, stream-ordered host = staging[(it + 1) % 2] plan(torch, host, BATCH_B) for d, h in zip(dev_bufs[1:], host[1:]): d.copy_(h, non_blocking=True) else: # step N+1's plan, stream-less hipMemcpy into the shared buffers plan(torch, dev_bufs, BATCH_B) walls.append((time.perf_counter() - t) * 1000.0) torch.cuda.synchronize() mismatches += int((out.float() - ref.float()).abs().max().item() > 0) print("RESULT " + json.dumps({"mismatches": mismatches, "plan_b_ms": round(sum(walls) / len(walls), 1)}), flush=True) def run_child(args, mode, num_streams, index, probe): cmd = [sys.executable, os.path.abspath(__file__), "--child", mode, "--streams", str(num_streams), "--index", str(index), "--iters", str(args.iters), "--delay-ms", str(args.delay_ms)] + (["--probe"] if probe else []) out = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True) text = out.stdout + out.stderr info = {"hip": next((l[7:] for l in out.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("HIPVER ")), "?"), "probe": next((json.loads(l[6:]) for l in out.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("PROBE ")), None)} res = next((json.loads(l[7:]) for l in out.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("RESULT ")), None) if res is not None: info["verdict"] = "WRONG OUTPUT" if res["mismatches"] else "ok" info["detail"] = f"output matches reference; plan B call {res['plan_b_ms']} ms" \ if not res["mismatches"] else f"{res['mismatches']}/{args.iters} iterations differ" elif "Memory access fault" in text or "illegal memory access" in text or out.returncode < 0: info["verdict"] = "GPU FAULT" fault = next((l.strip() for l in text.splitlines() if "Memory access fault" in l), "") info["detail"] = fault or "illegal memory access" else: info["verdict"] = "error" info["detail"] = (text.strip().splitlines() or [f"rc={out.returncode}"])[-1][:100] return info def main(): p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter) p.add_argument("--streams", type=int, default=1, help="create this many non-blocking streams; >1 runs the race on each") p.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=5) p.add_argument("--delay-ms", type=float, default=50.0) p.add_argument("--child", choices=["race", "synced", "fixed"], help=argparse.SUPPRESS) p.add_argument("--index", type=int, default=0, help=argparse.SUPPRESS) p.add_argument("--probe", action="store_true", help=argparse.SUPPRESS) args = p.parse_args() if args.child: child(args.child, args.streams, args.index, args.iters, args.delay_ms, args.probe) return env = " ".join(f"{k}={os.environ[k]}" for k in ("GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES", "DEBUG_HIP_DYNAMIC_QUEUES", "AMD_SERIALIZE_COPY") if k in os.environ) or "runtime defaults" if args.streams == 1: rows = [(m, run_child(args, m, 1, 0, False)) for m in ("race", "synced", "fixed")] print(f"HIP {rows[0][1]['hip']}, {env}, {args.delay_ms:.0f} ms delay, {args.iters} iterations") print(f"{'mode':<7} | {'result':<12} | detail") print("-" * 72) for m, r in rows: print(f"{m:<7} | {r['verdict']:<12} | {r['detail']}") return rows = [(i, run_child(args, "race", args.streams, i, True)) for i in range(args.streams)] hip_ver = rows[0][1]["hip"] print(f"HIP {hip_ver}, {env}, race mode, {args.streams} streams, " f"{args.delay_ms:.0f} ms delay, {args.iters} iterations") print(f"{'prefill stream':>14} | {'shares null-stream queue':>24} | {'result':<12} | detail") print("-" * 96) for i, r in rows: shares = "?" if r["probe"] is None else ("yes" if i in r["probe"] else "no") print(f"{i:>14} | {shares:>24} | {r['verdict']:<12} | {r['detail']}") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
## Error On most ranks at once, with the address in `0x6c000`–`0x6f000`: ```text Warning: Queue error - HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT Memory access fault by GPU node-4 (Agent handle: ...) on address 0x6c000. Reason: Write access to a read-only page. terminate called after throwing an instance of 'c10::AcceleratorError' what(): CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered ``` On ROCm 7.2, once the queue assignment is changed so the race is visible, the same batch dies with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`. The batch vLLM dumps always has the same shape: one new, unchunked ~8.1k-token prefill plus 29–30 decodes (for example `num_scheduled_tokens` sum 8204 = 8175 + 29 × 1). That step is larger than `max_cudagraph_capture_size`, so it runs outside CUDA graphs. ## What removes the fault Each row changes one thing on the Kimi-K3 reproduction (concurrency 32, seed 4, 1024 prompts) unless noted. | Change | Result | | --- | --- | | none | fault at request 111 | | `--enforce-eager` | fault at request 111 | | FP8 ASM prefill disabled (`_fp8_mla_prefill_supported()` forced to `False`) | 1024/1024 | | `--no-async-scheduling` | 1024/1024 | | `torch.cuda.synchronize()` immediately before `get_ps_metadata_v1` | 1024/1024 (x2) | | real LSE buffer passed to the decode kernel (`final_lse` non-null) | fault at request 78 | | instrumentation that synchronizes after every MLA call | 1024/1024 | | ROCm 7.2 image, default runtime settings | no fault end to end (the standalone reproduction does fault) | | `AMD_SERIALIZE_COPY=1` | 1024/1024 (this stream faulted at request 78 without it) | | `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=1` | 1024/1024 (same stream) | | this fix | 1024/1024 on every stream above | `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING` makes no difference with an FP8 KV cache. `use_gluon_decode()` returns `False` for any quantized KV cache before the setting is read, so `asm` and `auto` run the same kernels. CUDA graphs are not involved (`--enforce-eager` still faults). Decode is not involved (a real LSE buffer still faults). The fault goes away when the FP8 prefill path is off, when async scheduling is off, or when the metadata rewrite is ordered on the stream. ## Root cause 1. One persistent set of FP8 prefill PS metadata buffers is allocated per builder ([`_init_fp8_prefill_ps_buffers`, L785–L804](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py#L785-L804)). 2. Every batch with an unchunked prefill rewrites them via `aiter.get_ps_metadata_v1` ([`_build_fp8_prefill_ps_metadata`, L901–L918](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py#L901-L918), called from [`build()`, L1315–L1320](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py#L1315-L1320)). Each step's metadata only references the shared buffers ([L937–L941](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py#L937-L941)). 3. `get_ps_metadata_v1` plans on the host and copies the result into the caller's device tensors with blocking `hipMemcpy` and no stream ([aiter `v1_2_host.cuh` L395–L418](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/v0.1.22.post1/csrc/kernels/mla/metadata/v1_2_host.cuh#L395-L418)). 4. The consumers, `mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd` and `mla_reduce_v1`, are launched asynchronously once per layer ([L1799–L1832](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py#L1799-L1832)). 5. The builder's `.item()` sync on `reduce_indptr[-1]` comes after the rewrite, so it cannot prevent it ([L930–L931](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py#L930-L931)). `get_ps_metadata_v1` accepts pinned host output tensors and produces byte-identical plans to device outputs (five batch shapes, including the crash batch). `work_info` alone is ~8.9 MB at `batch=256, max_qlen=16384`. ## Why ROCm 7.2 serving often stays up ROCm 7.2 has the same race. In default serving, its plan copy happens to wait behind GPU work that is already queued. **Same rules on both versions.** - vLLM runs these kernels on a non-blocking stream it creates, on both runtimes. - A stream-less `hipMemcpy` waits only for the null stream and for blocking streams. The code path is the same in the two HIP runtime builds in these images (`ROCm/rocm-systems` `af70edc9` for 7.2 and `25e14349` for ROCm 10, per vLLM's `Dockerfile.rocm_base` / `Dockerfile.rock_base`). - In a two-stream test, `get_ps_metadata_v1` returns on both versions while a kernel on a vLLM-style stream is still running, and the new bytes are already visible. - The standalone reproduction faults on both. **The overlap window opens about as often.** With a non-synchronizing counter, about 7–11% of prefill plan updates start while the previous step's prefill is still queued, on both images. **The copy duration during that overlap differs.** `get_ps_metadata_v1` timed in the server, with no added synchronization: | When the previous prefill is still queued | ROCm 10 | ROCm 7.2 | | --- | --- | --- | | Mean plan-update time | ~0.8 ms | ~105–133 ms | | Updates that returned only after that prefill finished | almost none | about two thirds | | Mean plan-update time with no overlap | ~0.9 ms | ~14.5 ms | On ROCm 7.2 the copy usually sits behind in-flight work, including the prefill still reading the plan. On ROCm 10 it lands immediately. **Why a blocking copy can wait for unrelated work.** - The first of AITER's five copies, `work_indptr` (1,028 bytes), is below HIP's 16 KiB blit threshold (`GPU_FORCE_BLIT_COPY_SIZE`). The runtime runs it as a small copy kernel on the null stream's hardware queue. The other four copies use the SDMA engines. - Hardware queues are in order. A process with more streams than hardware queues (default 4 per GPU) shares them. - If the null stream's queue holds in-flight work, that copy waits for it. Because every `hipMemcpy` blocks, the whole plan update waits too. HIP binds a stream to a hardware queue at first use, so which stream shares the null stream's queue depends on launch order. `DEBUG_HIP_DYNAMIC_QUEUES=0` does not protect ROCm 10 in vLLM: the static mapping still faults at request 117, because the collision lands on other streams. Changing ROCm 7.2's queue assignment makes the unpatched server crash, on the same request numbers as ROCm 10, with the usual crash batch. Two machines, including the stock image: | ROCm 7.2 server env | Stream | Unpatched | With the fix | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | defaults | 8k/1k streams above | 1024/1024, 2048/2048 | 1024/1024 (concurrency 32) | | `DEBUG_HIP_DYNAMIC_QUEUES=1` | 1024 prompts, `--seed 5` | crash at request 117 (x3); plan update now ~0.8 ms | 1024/1024 | | `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=16` | 1024 prompts, `--seed 4` | crash at request 111 (x2) | 1024/1024 | A single-GPU run of the standalone script launches the prefill on each of 12 non-blocking streams. On ROCm 7.2 defaults, only streams that share the null stream's hardware queue are protected. With either setting above, or on ROCm 10, every stream faults. `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=1` on unpatched ROCm 10 also hides the fault, by putting every stream on one in-order queue. That serializes streams vLLM otherwise runs together, and it is slower than the fix at the default queue count. Dummy Kimi-K3, TP8, 8k/1k, concurrency 32, 1024 prompts, seed 4: | | Requests | Output tok/s | Median ITL | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Unpatched, `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=1` | 1024/1024 | 1043.87 | 19.24 ms | | This fix, default queues | 1024/1024 | 1082.6 | 18.14 ms | `AMD_SERIALIZE_COPY=1` hides it the same way: copies wait for already-queued work. The copy has no ordering guarantee on any ROCm version. ## Fix vLLM-only, in #58887: - Plan into two pinned host staging slots. - Copy the active slot to the device buffers with `copy_(non_blocking=True)` on the current stream. - Reuse a slot only after its previous copy completes (CUDA event). - Read `num_partial_tiles` from the host plan, which removes a GPU sync per prefill step. An AITER-side planner that is ordered on a stream, or a device-side planner like decode, would make device outputs safe for every caller: [ROCm/aiter#5879](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/5879). This is separate from #58814 (DSpark startup fault). That fault still reproduces with this change applied, and #58814 alone fixes it. ## Measurements ### Performance Kimi-K3, dummy weights, same 8k/1k benchmark. No change: | 8k/1k | Output tok/s (before / after) | Median ITL (before / after) | | --- | --- | --- | | concurrency 4 | 236.05 / 236.05 | 15.49 / 15.50 ms | | concurrency 32 | 1083.0 / 1082.6 | 18.14 / 18.14 ms | DeepSeek-V3 output throughput was not recorded separately. The 8k/1k stream above goes from a fault at request 111 to 1024/1024. ### Accuracy Kimi-K3, `niah_single_2`, single runs: | | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | 4k, concurrency 4 / 32 / 64 | 0.974 / 0.954 / 0.970 | 0.974 / 0.978 / 0.984 | | 64k, concurrency 32 | 0.922 | 0.928 | | 128k, concurrency 32 | 0.888 | 0.888 | DeepSeek-V3, same server, then: ```bash lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --seed 1234 \ --model_args '{"model":"deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3","tokenizer":"deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3", "base_url":"http://localhost:8000/v1/completions","num_concurrent":64, "tokenized_requests":false,"max_retries":3,"timeout":3600}' ``` | Server | gsm8k 5-shot, flexible-extract | | --- | --- | | before, `--async-scheduling` | GPU memory fault (x2), after ~80 s; one new ~1k-token prefill with 64 running | | after, `--async-scheduling` | 0.657, 0.673, 0.666 (3 runs) | | after, `--no-async-scheduling` | 0.680 | | before, `--no-async-scheduling` | 0.739, 0.691 (2 runs) | | before, `--kv-cache-dtype auto` (FP8 prefill path off), `--async-scheduling` | 0.671 | With `--no-async-scheduling`, before and after build identical plans. The two unpatched runs (0.739 and 0.691) are a run-to-run spread of about ±3 points, larger than lm_eval's per-run ±0.013. Every before/after difference sits inside that spread. The fixed runs match the arm where this path is inactive (bf16 KV). Absolute scores are low for DeepSeek-V3 in every arm, including bf16 KV, so they are only for comparison between arms. ### Unit tests MI350X (gfx950). `tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_prefill.py` passes 9/9. It runs production `_build_fp8_prefill_ps_metadata` and the real kernels against an SDPA reference. The rest of the AITER MLA tests (`tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_*.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_*.py`) pass, 634 cases. Before and after match, and none are skipped. ## How this was narrowed down - Reproduced on a fixed request stream at the same request count, including eager mode. - FP8 KV routes decode to the padded ASM persistent kernel `mla_a8w8_qh16_qseqlen1_gqaratio16_ps`, whatever the ASM padding setting. - ROCm 7.2 and ROCm 10 images: identical vLLM/AITER Python and identical ASM `.co` files. Kernel-argument layouts match their declared sizes. Compiled AITER modules and the HIP runtime differ. - Toggled one component at a time (table above). The fault remains until the FP8 prefill path is removed, async scheduling is removed, or the metadata rewrite is ordered. - Confirmed the host planner writes full output buffers with stream-less `hipMemcpy`, and that pinned host outputs match device plans byte for byte. - Confirmed vLLM's stream is non-blocking on both images, and that a stream-less `hipMemcpy` does not wait for queued kernels on it. The standalone reproduction then faults on ROCm 7.2 as well. This report and the experiments behind it were produced with help from a Cursor agent. ## Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix] Keep FlashAttention sparse ahead of FlashInfer SM90 for NoPE-512 MLA
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #56564. For SM90 NoPE-512, the automatic sparse MLA priority puts `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` ahead of `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE`. The issue reporter measured lower throughput with that default on H100 and confirmed that explicitly selecting FlashAttention avoids the regression. These are the reporter's measurements, not a benchmark performed by this PR's author.

## Changes

- Remove the head-size-512 priority exception. Keep FlashInfer SM90 available after FlashAttention and FlashMLA as a fallback.
- Shorten the source comment.
- Replace the existing priority-only test with automatic-selector coverage for head sizes 512 and 576: prefer FlashAttention when available, and select FlashInfer when the other sparse backends fail their availability probes.
- Merge current main (`9367d8b96`) and preserve its new `fp8_ds_mla` compatibility test unchanged.

## Validation

- Ruff check and format: passed for the affected files.
- An isolated execution of the actual selector functions with mocked backend availability passed all four preferred/fallback combinations. Restoring the FI-first choice makes the NoPE-512 preferred assertion fail.
- Full CUDA pytest could not collect locally because `vllm._C_stable_libtorch` is unavailable. The isolated check is not a substitute for the full suite or GPU validation.
- No new throughput measurements are claimed.

title: [Feature]: [RFC] Dynamic Latent-Trajectory Consensus Governor for Reasoning Models (DeepSeek-R1 / QwQ) to Free KV-Cache 4.5x Faster
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
Research paper :
[SubNeutralize__The_Geometry_of_Reasoning_and_the_Elimination_of_the_Overthinking_Trap (4) (1).pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32702285/SubNeutralize__The_Geometry_of_Reasoning_and_the_Elimination_of_the_Overthinking_Trap.4.1.pdf)
## 1. Problem & Systems Motivation

Autoregressive reasoning models (e.g., `DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B`, `QwQ-32B`) present a massive throughput bottleneck in vLLM:
* In up to 40% of coding and reasoning tasks, models derive the correct solution within early generation (80–120 tokens).
* Instead of emitting the final answer, the model enters repetitive post-deduction monologue loops ("Wait, let me double check... what if null? Actually, step 1 was right..."), consuming 1,500+ tokens.
* **The vLLM Impact:** This unnecessarily occupies PagedAttention KV-cache slots for 2+ minutes per sequence, starving the scheduler, inflating queues, and degrading global serving throughput.

---

## 2. Proposed Mechanism: Latent Trajectory Consensus

Rather than applying arbitrary token limits or heuristic string parsing, we propose an early-exit mechanism (**SubNeutralize**) computed directly from latent trajectory dynamics at the model's cognitive bottleneck layer (layer 14 on 1.5B/7B, layer 32 on 32B).

During token decoding, we track cosine velocity and momentum in Python:

```python
# 1. Directional velocity between current and previous hidden states
velocity = 1.0 - cosine_similarity(h_current, h_prev)

# 2. Update exponential moving average (alpha = 0.10)
ema_velocity = (0.10 * velocity) + (0.90 * ema_velocity_prev)

# 3. Scale-free momentum ratio
momentum_ratio = velocity / ema_velocity

# 4. Consensus check (after minimum 60 tokens, with 2-token debounce)
if token_step >= 60 and (momentum_ratio < 0.82 or velocity < 0.135):
    # Trajectory has stabilized into consensus equilibrium.
    # Transition immediately into answer/code emission.
    trigger_early_stop()
```

---

## 3. Empirical Benchmarks on NVIDIA A100-SXM4 (DeepSeek-R1-32B)

Tested under an identical **1,500-token ceiling** for both Vanilla and Governed runs on enterprise backend coding tasks (Rate limiters, SQL sanitizers, JWT claims validators, TTL LRU caches):

| Metric | Vanilla vLLM Baseline | Governed (SubNeutralize) | Improvement |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **Total Tokens Consumed** | 5,698 tokens | **1,261 tokens** | **77.9% Compute Saved** |
| **Total Inference Latency** | 596.1 s | **132.3 s** | **4.51x Speedup** |
| **Average Query Latency** | 149.0 s | **33.1 s** | **-115.9 s per sequence** |
| **Verified Unit Test Pass Rate** | 4/4 (100%) | **4/4 (100%)** | **Zero Accuracy Loss** |
| **KV-Cache Eviction Speed** | ~150 s / req | **~33 s / req** | **Cache freed 4.5x faster** |

---

## 4. Kernel Overhead & Computational Budget

* The consensus check operates on a single-layer 1D hidden vector (d = 3584 or 5120).
* On an NVIDIA A100, computing cosine similarity and EMA takes **less than 15 microseconds per decode step**.
* Compared to the forward pass latency of a 32B model (~25–35 ms per token), compute overhead is **less than 0.05%** (negligible).

---

## 5. Potential vLLM Integration Points

We would love to discuss the cleanest architectural pattern for vLLM:
* **Option A (Worker forward hook):** Hook intermediate hidden states in the decoder layer prior to the lm_head logit projection.
* **Option B (Custom StoppingCriteria):** Register an opt-in reasoning governor via `SamplingParams(early_consensus_stopping=True)` or a worker plugin.

---

## 6. Resources & Reference Implementation

* **Apache-2.0 Reference Implementation:** https://github.com/Arnab758/subneutralize
* **PyPI Package:** `pip install subneutralize` (v0.1.2)
* **Research Paper (Zenodo DOI):** https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22941619

Would the maintainers be open to an RFC/PR exploring this integration for reasoning models?


### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on SM120 (RTX PRO 6000): Xid 31 illegal memory access during long prefill — deterministic with CUDA graphs enabled, flaky in eager mode (v0.30.0 + FlashInfer 0.7.0)
body:
### Describe the bug

Running DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (sparse MLA + Engram compressed KV cache) on 4× RTX PRO 6000 (SM120, sm_120) with vLLM v0.30.0, the serving container dies with **Xid 31 (MMU Fault, FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ)** on all 4 GPUs simultaneously during **long prefill (>35K tokens)**.

The failure boundary is now well-characterized across 70+ controlled experiments:

| Config | Short sequences | Long prefill (35K+) |
|---|---|---|
| eager / compile-only (CUDAGraphMode=NONE) | ✅ pass | 2 crashes / 6 passes (~25%, flaky) |
| CUDA graphs = FULL / FULL_DECODE_ONLY / PIECEWISE | ✅ pass | **0/3 — crash on the FIRST 35K prefill, 100% reproducible** |

The same request sequence succeeds and fails across identical runs in eager mode, ruling out any single-request trigger (speculative decoding, prefix caching, and guided decoding were each explicitly isolated and excluded).

### To Reproduce

1. Hardware: 4× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), driver 580.x, CUDA 13.0
2. Image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 + FlashInfer 0.7.0 (also reproduced on stock 0.6.18.post1)
3. Serve DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP=4, `--attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' --block-size 64`
4. Send a single 35K-token prefill request → container exits with Xid 31 on all workers within ~15s (graph modes), or intermittent (eager)

### Xid signature (dmesg)

```
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:16:00): 31, name=VLLM::Worker, MMU Fault: ENGINE GRAPHICS GPC*, faulted @ 0x7f..., Fault is of type FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ
```
All 4 GPUs fault at the same instant (different GPCs per card) — software-side invalid GPU virtual address, not hardware.

### Environment details

- vLLM v0.30.0 (also affected: stock image with no patches)
- FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1 → upgraded to 0.7.0 (incl. #4802 SM120 sparse MLA refactor, #5048 SM120 prefill hang fix, sm120f jit-cache) — **not fixed by 0.7.0**
- CUDA 13.0, driver 580.x
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (43 layers, compress_ratios [0,0,2×18,1×20,0,0,0])

### Startup patches required on SM120 (context)

To even boot this model+GPU combo on v0.30.0, 9 patches were needed (happy to share): SWA window 32→64, flashinfer_sparse block-size declaration [128]→[64,128], indexer cache spec ×2, compressed-layer page-spec ×2, topk indices alignment, etc. The Xid 31 crash occurs **after** a fully healthy startup (READY, warmup OK).

### Performance context (why this matters)

When it does run, the stack is fast: 128K prefill = 7,893 tok/s (vs SGLang TP4 baseline 4,217). Decode requires CUDA graphs for usable throughput (8.2 → 64.0 tok/s with FULL_DECODE_ONLY) — but graphs are exactly what makes long-prefill crash deterministic. This blocks production use entirely.

### Related

- flashinfer #4973 — same Xid signature (SM120 + RTX PRO 6000 + sparse_mla_sm120_prefill.cu illegal access, short OK / long prefill crash); reporter's workaround (B12X backend) does NOT apply to V4.1-Flash (model code hard-selects sparse path)
- flashinfer #4802 (in 0.7.0) — SM120 sparse MLA refactor; did not fix our shape
- vLLM #55775 — same signature family (Xid 31, MTP decode); our config has speculative decoding disabled, but the "state-dependent illegal address" pattern matches

We can provide: full crash matrix (config × sequence × outcome), 4-layer verification logs (eager/graph mode actual effect), dmesg captures, and a 100%-reproducible graph-mode sequence.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Emit buffered post-reasoning text when no tool parser is configured
body: ## Purpose With an engine-based reasoning parser and no tool parser, streaming can drop the text right after the end of reasoning. For example, with `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --reasoning-parser qwen3 --stream-interval 2` and the greedy prompt "Reply with only this exact HTML and nothing else: `hello`", the answer is `"\n\nhello"` without streaming but `"hello"` when streamed. It happens when one delta carries several tokens around ``. When reasoning ends inside a delta, `DelegatingParser.parse_delta` gets the text the engine held back from `finish_streaming()` and adds it only to `current_text`, which is the tool parser's input. With no tool parser, nothing emits it. #47606 added this flush for the reasoning-to-tool case. This PR emits the text as content when there is no tool parser. The fix is in `abstract_parser.py` because every engine-based reasoning parser is affected (14 of 15, see below). Not a duplicate: I searched open and merged PRs for stream interval, multi-token deltas, `finish_streaming` and `abstract_parser.py`. #51669 edits the same block, but for non-engine parsers and a different bug. #55210, #53924 and #39044 change the non-engine `BaseThinkingReasoningParser`. None of them fixes this case. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/parser/test_streaming.py -k no_tool_batched_holdback pytest tests/parser tests/reasoning tests/tool_parsers tests/v1/structured_output ``` - Every engine-based reasoning parser, no tool parser: stream `plan it\n\nbold a < b done` (with the parser's own markers) in 60 random chunkings of 1-4 tokens and compare the content with `parse()`. - End to end on GPU: compare streamed and non-streamed content of greedy chat and Responses requests. ## Test Result - New test (3 cases): fails on main, passes with this PR. - Suites: 6877 passed (main: 6874; the difference is the new tests). Both have the same 15 setup errors, from a gated Llama tokenizer. - Chunkings whose streamed content differs from `parse()`: | parser | main | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | deepseek_v4, deepseek_v41, glm45, glm47, kimi_k2, ling3, mimo, minimax_m2, mistral, nemotron_v3, qwen3, seed_oss | 17/60 | 0/60 | | gemma4 | 33/60 | 0/60 | | granite_thinking_parser | 8/60 | 0/60 | | inkling | 0/60 | 0/60 | ling3, nemotron_v3 and inkling used the Qwen3 tokenizer; the others used their own model's tokenizer. - End to end, 1x L4, 8 greedy prompts, requests whose streamed content differs (chat / Responses): | model, `--stream-interval` | main | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | Qwen3-0.6B, 1 | 0/8 / 0/8 | 0/8 / 0/8 | | Qwen3-0.6B, 2 | 3/8 / 3/8 | 0/8 / 0/8 | | Qwen3-0.6B, 4 | 3/8 / 3/8 | 0/8 / 0/8 | | Qwen3-1.7B, 2 | 3/8 / 3/8 | 0/8 / 0/8 | Each non-streamed request was sent twice; all pairs matched, so the differences are not nondeterminism. AI assistance: I used an AI assistant (Claude) for parts of the analysis, the patch and the tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above myself.
