title: XPU: get_attn_backend_cls never calls validate_configuration - all attention backend capability gates are dead on XPU
body:
## Summary

`XPUPlatform.get_attn_backend_cls` never calls `validate_configuration()` on the
resolved attention backend, while the CUDA and ROCm platforms both do.

```python
# vllm/platforms/cuda.py   -> 2 occurrences
# vllm/platforms/rocm.py   -> 2 occurrences
# vllm/platforms/xpu.py    -> 0 occurrences
```

Because the validation is skipped, every capability gate the attention backend
defines is **dead code on XPU**. An unsupported configuration is not rejected —
it is accepted and run, and the failure mode depends on what the gate would have
caught.

## Why this is the structural issue

The validation function in `vllm/attention/backends/registry.py` (roughly lines
274-350) is where backends declare and enforce their constraints: head size,
KV-cache dtype, block size, `mm_prefix` support, attention sinks, batch
invariance, and PCP/DCP constraints. On XPU, none of it runs.

This is why several other XPU attention bugs present as *silent* wrongness
instead of a clean error. It is the difference between "unsupported head size
256 raises a clear error" and "the kernel runs anyway and produces garbage".

## Concrete example

`FlashAttentionBackend` reports capability flags that contradict the XPU
platform's own documented limitations:

- `supports_batch_invariance() -> True`
- `supports_non_causal() -> True`

while `vllm/platforms/xpu.py:165-178` and `:184-197` state that FlashAttention
on XPU is **not** batch-invariant and **cannot** service the `mm_prefix`
bidirectional mask. Both branches honour an explicit request and return anyway.
With `validate_configuration` wired up, those requests would be rejected up
front instead of silently mis-executed.

## Suggested fix

Mirror what CUDA and ROCm do in `get_attn_backend_cls`: after resolving the
backend class, call its `validate_configuration` and let a mismatch raise.

```python
# in XPUPlatform.get_attn_backend_cls, after resolving the backend class
backend_cls.validate_configuration(...)
```

Worth pairing with: make the unsupported cases fail loudly. A user asking for
batch-invariant attention on XPU should get a clear error, not a config that
silently is not batch-invariant.

## Environment

- GPU: Intel Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage G31, `0xe223`), 32 GB
- Driver / compute-runtime 26.18.38308.4, UR 1.15.38308+4, IGC 2.34.4
- Fedora 43, kernel 7.1.8, `xe` driver
- vLLM 0.30.0+XPU, torch 2.13.0+xpu, vllm-xpu-kernels 0.1.14.1

## Verification

Confirmed by reading the installed vLLM source: occurrence counts of
`validate_configuration` per platform file, and the
`FlashAttentionBackend.supports_batch_invariance` / `supports_non_causal`
implementations versus the warnings in `platforms/xpu.py`. No GPU execution was
needed — this is a control-flow gap, verifiable statically.

Related: the DeepSeek-V4.1, `minimax_m3`, `inkling`, `dots3_note` and `kimi_k3`
model packages also branch only on `is_rocm()` and silently fall through to
NVIDIA paths on XPU. That is a related family of missing-platform-check issues
and may be worth tracking together.

title: [Bugfix][Metrics] Retain components for resolved quantization configs
body:
## Overview

Fixes #58742. Resolved quantization names missing from the estimator lookup silently drop attention and FFN work from MFU/MBU estimates.

## Claims

- Resolve weight size from GPTQ/AWQ bit widths, online quantization specifications, and mixed linear/expert precision.
- Retain components with a deduplicated warning and model-dtype estimate when an unsupported method or checkpoint layer selection cannot be represented by one width.
- Preserve existing supported methods and unquantized controls.

## Validation

Rebased onto current main `276fbcf`, resolving the upstream move of `Self` into `typing`. Implementation and test bodies are unchanged from the previously tested branch.

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/metrics tests/v1/metrics/test_perf_metrics.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/metrics/perf.py tests/v1/metrics/test_perf_metrics.py
```

**100 metrics tests passed.** All applicable pre-commit checks passed, including the repository's minimum-version mypy check.

Executed 16 real checkpoint/flag combinations six times against the rebased stack: **96 online runs passed**, each evaluating prefill and decode. A separate 16-case run used the unpatched current-main estimator with identical checkpoint revisions, configuration hashes, and resolved layer lists. All repeats were identical; unaffected controls and the previously approved estimates were unchanged.

| Checkpoint | Upstream decode GFLOPs | Patched decode GFLOPs |
|---|---:|---:|
| GPT-OSS-20B | 1.158 | 7.436 |
| Qwen2.5 GPTQ/AWQ | 0.272 | 1.076 |
| Qwen3 bf16 control | 1.427 | 1.427 |

Validation used Python 3.12 and CPU Torch with actual `ModelConfig`, `VllmConfig._get_quantization_config`, and estimator execution. No weights were loaded or GPU inference run; model outputs, kernels, and serving behavior are unchanged.

## Details

Both attention and FFN parsers share weight-size resolution. GPT-OSS retains bf16 linear layers and FP4 expert accounting; DeepSeek-V4's FFN accounting is restored while its separate unsupported attention architecture remains outside this fix.

The fallback can overestimate weight traffic and does not provide per-layer accounting. Automatically discovered layer lists in the tested Qwen GPTQ/AWQ checkpoints trigger the documented 2-byte fallback rather than assuming every projection is 4-bit.

No overlapping fix was found in issue-number or area searches. Related #58745, #58836, and #54228 address speculative-token accounting, hybrid attention, and expert activation counts respectively.

- [x] Design Fit: confines changes to the analytic estimator and shares resolution between its parsers.
- [x] Testing and Validation: regression coverage and real configuration execution passed; upstream CI remains maintainer-authorized.
- [x] Code Quality and Style: current pre-commit and type checks passed.
- [x] Pull Request Contents: issue, reproducer commands, results, and limitations are included.

</details>

title: [ROCm] rocm_unquantized_gemm crashes on CPU tensors (dispatch ignores tensor device)
body:
## Report of bug

`tests/models/language/generation/test_gemma.py::test_gemma4_dspark_loads_confidence_head` (added in #57263) fails on ROCm CI:

```
NotImplementedError: Could not run 'vllm::rocm_unquantized_gemm' with arguments
from the 'CPU' backend. This could be because the operator doesn't exist for
this backend, or was omitted during the selective/custom build process...
'vllm::rocm_unquantized_gemm' is only available for these backends: [CUDA, ...]
```

### Root cause

`dispatch_unquantized_gemm()` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py` picks `rocm_unquantized_gemm` for **any** ROCm build based solely on `current_platform.is_rocm()`, regardless of the input tensor's actual device:

```python
def dispatch_unquantized_gemm(linear_backend: str = "auto"):
    if current_platform.is_rocm():
        return rocm_unquantized_gemm
    elif current_platform.is_cpu():
        return cpu_unquantized_gemm
    elif not current_platform.is_cuda():
        return default_unquantized_gemm
    ...
```

`rocm_unquantized_gemm`'s custom op is only registered for the CUDA/HIP dispatch key, so any CPU tensor crashes. The test builds `Gemma4DSparkForCausalLM` and calls `compute_confidence(hidden, markov)` with plain CPU tensors (no `.cuda()`), which routes through `DSparkConfidenceHead.proj` (a `ReplicatedLinear`) — on a ROCm build this always hits `rocm_unquantized_gemm`. The CUDA and CPU branches already fall back gracefully (`default_unquantized_gemm`/`cpu_unquantized_gemm` both ultimately call `torch.nn.functional.linear`), the ROCm branch didn't.

Never caught before because this specific ROCm CI job (`amd-mi355-dpx-language-models-extended-generation`, `optional: true`) didn't run on #57263 itself.

### Fix

vllm-project/vllm#58867 (a different PR: AITER version bump) surfaced this while running full ROCm CI; fix proposed in #58923: guard `rocm_unquantized_gemm` with `if not x.is_cuda: return default_unquantized_gemm(...)`, mirroring the existing CUDA/CPU fallback behavior.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fall back to default GEMM for CPU tensors on ROCm builds
body:
## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Searched for existing fixes before starting: `gh pr list --search "rocm_unquantized_gemm"`, `--search "test_gemma.py"`, `--search "gemma4_dspark"`, and the ~20 open/merged DSpark/confidence-head PRs in this area — none touch `dispatch_unquantized_gemm`/`rocm_unquantized_gemm` or this device-dispatch bug. Filed as vllm-project/vllm#58922 for tracking.

## What broke

`tests/models/language/generation/test_gemma.py::test_gemma4_dspark_loads_confidence_head` (added in #57263, merged 2026-09-26) fails on ROCm CI:

```
NotImplementedError: Could not run 'vllm::rocm_unquantized_gemm' with arguments
from the 'CPU' backend. ... 'vllm::rocm_unquantized_gemm' is only available for
these backends: [CUDA, ...]
```

`dispatch_unquantized_gemm()` picks `rocm_unquantized_gemm` for any ROCm build purely from `current_platform.is_rocm()`, ignoring the tensor's actual device. The custom op is only registered for the CUDA/HIP dispatch key, so a CPU tensor (as this test uses, exercising `DSparkConfidenceHead.proj`, a `ReplicatedLinear`, without moving it to a GPU) hard-crashes. The CUDA and CPU branches of the same dispatcher already fall back to plain `torch.nn.functional.linear` for this kind of case; the ROCm branch didn't.

This surfaced while running full ROCm CI on an unrelated PR (#58867, AITER version bump) — `amd-mi355-dpx-language-models-extended-generation` is `optional: true` and never ran on #57263 itself, so it was never caught.

## Fix

Add the same device fallback the CUDA/CPU branches already have:

```python
def rocm_unquantized_gemm(layer, x, weight, bias=None):
    if not x.is_cuda:
        return default_unquantized_gemm(layer, x, weight, bias)
    return torch.ops.vllm.rocm_unquantized_gemm(x, weight, bias)
```

No change to real GPU-tensor behavior/perf; only changes the previously-crashing CPU-tensor case.

## Test commands run and results

Could not run pytest locally (this sandbox has no torch/GPU install); relying on ROCm CI (`amd-mi355-dpx-language-models-extended-generation`) to validate `test_gemma4_dspark_loads_confidence_head` now passes, and the rest of the ROCm suite to confirm no regression from the added device check.

## AI assistance disclosure

This fix was investigated and written with AI assistance (Cursor agent) while triaging CI failures on #58867; I reviewed the change and root-cause analysis before opening this PR.

title: [HiSparse] Log steady-state max concurrency and expose host-tier utilization gauges
body:
## Purpose

HiSparse's host KV pool is invisible at runtime, and the startup `Maximum concurrency` line understates a warm server's capacity: it charges every request its full admission footprint, while running requests that read from host pin only their active tail pages. This PR adds:

- **Startup log**: steady-state maximum concurrency, `1 + (num_blocks - admission) / steady` (all but one request at its active tail, plus one being admitted), capped by the host pool. Logged from the scheduler-side connector, so it uses the KV cache config after the cross-rank minimum.
- **Gauges**, sampled by the scheduler each engine step (constant-time read of the host block pool, no device sync):
  - `vllm:hisparse_host_cache_usage_perc`: host pool usage, mirroring `vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc`. Evictable cached blocks count as free.
  - `vllm:hisparse_pending_page_transfers`: write-backs and restores not yet completed.
- **CLI**: `HiSparse host KV cache usage %` in the `KV Transfer metrics` line.
- **Docs**: a HiSparse section in `docs/usage/metrics.md` (metric names are now literals so the generator picks them up) and the two bounds in `docs/design/hisparse.md`.

Supersedes #58805.

## Test Plan

Unit tests (macOS, CPU):

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_stats.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py \
  -k "hisparse or host_usage or stats"
```

E2E on H100: shrunk DeepSeek-V3.2 (4 layers, dummy weights), FP8 KV, block size 64, `/metrics` scraped every 0.2 s.

- **A**: TP2, `MultiConnector[HiSparseConnector (host_pool_gib 4), OffloadingConnector (cpu_bytes_to_use 4e9)]`, `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 1000000000`; `vllm bench serve` random 8000 in / 512 out, 64 prompts, concurrency 32.
- **B**: TP1, `HiSparseConnector` (host_pool_gib 4), `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 250000000 --max-model-len 16384`; random 15000 in / 1300 out, 40 prompts, concurrency 40 (saturates the GPU pool).

## Test Result

Unit: 45 passed at HEAD (with `test_multi_connector.py`) (`test_draft_layer_rows_mirrored_after_drafter` needs CUDA, not run on macOS).

E2E at `f792b5bd11` (later commits switch the ratio to the equivalent `BlockPool.get_usage()` and trim comments/docs). All requests succeeded, no errors.

A:

```
GPU KV cache size: 1,016,234 tokens, Maximum concurrency for 163,840 tokens per request: 6.20x
HiSparse steady-state maximum concurrency for 163,840 tokens per request: 8.07x (running requests reading from host).

vllm:hisparse_host_cache_usage_perc        0.0 -> 0.161 (32 running) -> 0.0
vllm:hisparse_pending_page_transfers       up to 256 during prefill, 1-2 during decode, 0 idle

KV Transfer metrics: HiSparseConnector={..., 'HiSparse host KV cache usage %': 15.8}, OffloadingConnector={...}
```

One series per gauge; peak usage matches 32 requests x ~129 pages / 25574 host blocks, so nothing is counted twice across ranks or connectors.

B: logged 3.88x generic and 9.50x steady state; observed up to 10 running requests, sustained, while reading from host. Like the generic line, the steady-state value is an estimate, not a hard limit: requests prefilling together do not all hold their full window at once.

Logging and metrics only; no change to attention, caching or scheduling.

title: [Bug]: QSA indexer uses cooperative_topk on sm_110 (Jetson AGX Thor) and fails with "cluster misconfiguration"
body:
### Your current environment

- NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor (T5000), compute capability 11.0 (sm_110), 122.9 GiB unified memory, driver r595 (CUDA 13.2 driver)
- `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0` (`sha256:8a69ffad015f138d7170c4ddc429e230a3bc1c1719f67e14324749df200a4b90`), torch 2.13.0+cu130
- Model: `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (qwen4_exp, QSA attention), TP 1, MTP speculative decoding

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On sm_110 the QSA indexer picks `cooperative_topk`, which fails to launch during engine start-up (CUDA graph capture / first decode):

```
RuntimeError: launch_cooperative_cluster, /workspace/csrc/libtorch_stable/cooperative_topk.cu:48,
cooperative_topk launch failed: a kernel launch error has occurred due to cluster misconfiguration
```

The dispatch in `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ops/qsa_indexer.py` (unchanged on `main` as of b9e2903b89):

```python
use_cooperative_topk = (
    logits.shape[0] <= 64
    and logits.stride(0) % 4 == 0
    and current_platform.has_device_capability(90)
    and not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(120)
)
```

sm_12x (e.g. DGX Spark's GB10) is already excluded and falls back to `persistent_topk`; sm_110 is not, so it takes the cooperative path whose cluster configuration it does not support.

Excluding family 110 as well makes it work on the Thor:

```python
    and not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(120)
    and not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(110)
```

With that change the model starts and serves correctly (e.g. 17*23 → 391, correct code, about 44 tokens/s with MTP 3). The same `cooperative_topk` gating may be worth checking in `model_executor/layers/indexer_topk.py` (`kernel_config.sparse_indexer_topk_backend="auto"`) for sm_110 as well.

Note: to fit this checkpoint in 122 GiB we ran it with a third-party single-device setup that keeps the PLE table in a file; the failing kernel and the dispatch above are unmodified vLLM code.

Reported by Raytone AI Lab.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Recover host backing for active GPU-only pages
body:
## Description

When the HiSparse host pool fills, an active request can retain GPU-only pages
with null host entries when no host page is available. Later allocations extend
the host table, so freeing host capacity does not give those old pages backing
and their GPU blocks stay pinned.

Retry one old page per connector step after scheduler allocations. The recovered
page gets a host destination and a copy to host. Its GPU blocks become reclaimable
only after every worker completes the transfer.

In the 64-token regression case, releasing one donor host block lets the active
request backfill logical page 1. Completion makes **one GPU block per resident
group reclaimable**; partial acknowledgement makes none.

## Test coverage

`test_hisparse_host_exhaustion_keeps_gpu_pages_readable`
(`tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py:855`) fails on the baseline because the
old host entry remains null.

| Reviewer question | Test |
|---|---|
| Can retries duplicate work or monopolize capacity? | `test_hisparse_host_recovery_rotates_requests_with_limited_capacity` (`tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py:939`) |
| Can a late completion validate a reused request ID? | `test_hisparse_host_recovery_retains_cancelled_transfer_endpoints` (`tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py:981`) |
| Does eager mirroring copy the recovered page? | `test_host_recovery_copies_pages_even_with_eager_mirroring` (`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py:59`) |

AI assistance from Codex was used for the implementation, tests, and this
description.

## Validation

The CPU run completed with **205 passed**:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py -q --tb=short
```

The H100 model-path regression completed with **2 passed** (eager host mirroring
on and off):

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py -k host_capacity_recovery -v -s -x --tb=short
```

Each H100 case copied 3 recovered pages, reclaimed 24 GPU blocks across 8
resident groups, and preserved all 16 generated tokens with zero preemptions.
Host rows matched resident rows. The run used reduced DeepSeek-V3.2 with dummy
FP8 weights, so trained-model accuracy was not evaluated. Serving throughput
was not measured.

## Existing PRs

Open PR searches for HiSparse host capacity recovery, exhaustion, and backfill
found no implementation of recovery for old null host entries. #56109 addresses
resident cache policy and does not backfill these entries.

title: [Perf][HiSparse] Avoid repeated prefix scans; drive residency from the connector
body:
Alternative to #57930, following the review thread at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57930#discussion_r4068549511. It keeps @S1ro1's prefix-scan cursor fix and folds in the restructure from S1ro1/vllm#9. That restructure removes the `resident_managers[0]` identity check that @NickLucche flagged: per-step residency work now runs in HiSparse-specific code, not in `HiSparseResidentManager.cache_blocks`.

### Changes

1. **Prefix-scan cursor** (from #57930, authored by @S1ro1, unchanged): `plan_prefix_materialization` now starts scanning at `max(ready_prefix_pages, importing_pages)`, so it no longer rescans pages it already knows are durable.
2. **Residency driven from the connector** (from S1ro1/vllm#9):
   - Removes the `HiSparseResidentManager.cache_blocks` override. Previously every resident group ran the shared `plan_prefix_materialization` and `update_residency` calls; #57930 limited this to one run per step with the identity check.
   - Adds `HiSparseCoordinator.advance_scheduled`. `HiSparseConnectorScheduler.build_connector_meta` already runs once per step and iterates every scheduled request. It now calls `advance_scheduled` just before `build_offload_command`, using the same finalized-token cap that `allocate_slots` used (`min(computed + scheduled, request.num_tokens)`). Spills planned in a step therefore still ship in that step.

### Behavior difference

`update_residency` has two side effects that used to run during scheduling and now run after it:
- releasing pinned-clean pages when a request acquires its hot region
- the low-pool watermark check that requests a hot region

For the rest of that scheduling pass, both now take effect one step later. Pages that become clean after a spill are unaffected, because they are released in `update_connector_output`, before scheduling. The net effect is a one-step delay at the transition, not a lost release.

Moving the calls into `HiSparseSourceManager.cache_blocks` was also tried, and it does not work. `allocate_slots` calls the coordinator's `cache_blocks` unconditionally, but the per-group loop skips managers with `enable_caching=False`. So with prefix caching off, the host manager never runs.

### Performance

See #57930 for @S1ro1's end-to-end B300 P/D measurements of the cursor + single-invocation fix. In their CPU microbenchmark (20 resident groups, 512 durable pages), request cache-update bookkeeping dropped from 512.01 to 6.63 µs/request. This PR keeps the single-invocation property: residency work runs once per scheduled request per step, regardless of how many resident groups there are. The end-to-end run has **not** been repeated on this revision.

### Tests

The HiSparse tests in `test_prefix_caching.py` expected residency work to happen inside `allocate_slots`. They now go through a small `_allocate_scheduled` helper that calls `allocate_slots` and then `advance_scheduled` with the same cap. The test diff is mostly this mechanical change.

Rebased on main `4a190dc5`:

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q
163 passed

pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_stats.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/test_config.py -k "hisparse or HiSparse" -q
23 passed
```

`pre-commit run --files` passes on all four changed files.

Not yet run: GPU end-to-end or accuracy validation on this revision.

AI assistance was used for this change.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On pinned vLLM commit `153242a314153637999eb6ebe8dd830e63433bb6`
(`0.30.1rc0+precompiled`), Qwen3-4B greedy serving can produce a different
*first* token when V2 speculative decoding is enabled. In the selected
row-46 replay, ordinary autoregressive serving emits token ID 334; serving
with a seven-token DFlash2 or DSpark drafter emits 95456. The client sends
requests sequentially (concurrency 1). The divergence occurs during the
initial target prefill, before a draft token or rejection decision exists.

Configuration: Qwen3-4B target, matching custom Qwen3-4B drafters, BF16,
flash-attn, tensor parallel size 1, prefix caching enabled, max model length
4096, max batched tokens 32768, max sequences 32, greedy sampling,
`ignore_eos`, 128 output tokens. Both services receive the same preceding
46 requests in the same order before the selected row-46 request. Exact
launch commands and checkpoint hashes were saved in the run provenance.

The selected prompt is:

> **Blueprint for Serverless Computing with AWS Lambda and API Gateway for Blockchain Administration on AWS**
>
> ---
>
> ## **1. Introduction**
>
> This blueprint outlines a comprehensive, secure, and scalable architecture
> for managing a blockchain system using **AWS Lambda** and **API Gateway**,
> leveraging the robust infrastructure of **Amazon Web Services (AWS)**.
> The system is designed to support the administration of a blockchain
> network, ensuring **seamless node communication**, **data integrity**,
> **security**, and **high throughput**. The architecture is built with a
> **stratified analytical methodology**, considering the interplay of
> components and their potential impacts on system performance and security.
>
> ---

This prompt alone is **not** a standalone reproducer: the previous requests
establish the saved serving state, and the two drafter checkpoints are custom.
I can provide the exact ordered requests, checkpoint access, launch commands
and provenance if suitable for a public reproduction.

What we isolated:

- The original AR and DFlash2 AOT artifacts use the same source for three
  fused RMSNorm variants, but select different reduction-block settings.
- A control that only changes the selected prefill dispatch/padding keeps
  the original token IDs and returned scores.
- A prefill-only intervention that aligns those RMSNorm launch settings to
  AR makes all 36 layers' prompt K/V, the selected hidden state and all raw
  prefill logits bitwise equal to AR. DFlash2 then emits all 128 original AR
  token IDs in three fresh-server repetitions, beginning with 334.
- The corresponding DSpark intervention also needs its Q/K RMSNorm+RoPE
  launch configuration aligned to obtain bitwise-equal prefill state. It
  restores the first token to 334, although its later output still diverges.
- Probe-off / probe-on / probe-off runs agree on token IDs, returned scores
  and finish reasons within each condition. The arithmetic intervention is
  deliberately output-changing; the passive capture controls preserve the
  original output.

This establishes a case-specific numerical cause in prefill compilation /
autotuning. It does not establish a production fix, full-heldout agreement,
or a performance result. The installed vLLM runner and rejection sampler
were not edited for these experiments. The pinned checkout had a pre-existing
dirty change in speculative configuration/scheduling; that patch is retained
in provenance.

A separate decode case prevents misdiagnosing this as a rejection-sampler
failure. At a reached row-5 replacement slot, independent AR token A and
submitted draft D are both 334, while the speculative target chooses V=3786
and emits E=3786. The recorded target logits differ, and the rejection
decision is consistent with those logits. Thus `D=A, E!=D` alone does not
imply a verifier bug. Likewise, later output divergence alone does not
establish KV corruption.

Could maintainers advise whether cross-mode consistency of these autotuned
RMSNorm launch configurations is expected, and where a regression test for
this initial-prefill behavior should live?

title: [Bugfix][Model] Avoid rank-local compilation of GLM indexer key norm
body:
## Purpose

Related to #58636. This patch replaces the separately compiled GLM5Next indexer key-normalization leaf with the existing `LayerNorm` module. It preserves fp32 normalization, the same weight/bias/epsilon, and the activation-dtype cast-back, without changing checkpoint names or private/global Inductor configuration. Pointwise compiled leaves remain unchanged.

The goal is to remove rank-local reduction autotuning from a replicated key path, where differing reduction orders can change near-tie sparse selections. This is a conservative correctness candidate. Reporter-provided eager-mode rank-agreement results are now available for the production file at the current head, as detailed below. Full-head CUDA tests, model accuracy, and serving benchmarks remain outstanding.

### Why this is not duplicate work

The issue is unassigned and its complete discussion contains no implementation claim. Fresh searches for #58636 and the norm leaf found no matching PR. Nearby row-sharding work (#54394, #54951, #58536) does not change this leaf and retains replicated fallback paths. #57815 concerns downstream batch-invariant top-k behavior; #54851 changes captured KV-cache writes in `deepseek_v32/attention.py`, not this GLM5Next norm.

## Test Plan

```sh
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/glm5next/test_sparse_indexer_topk_dispatch.py \
  tests/test_config.py \
  -k 'kpool or test_breakable_cudagraph_platform_default' -q -rs
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/models/glm5next/common/attention.py \
  tests/models/glm5next/test_sparse_indexer_topk_dispatch.py \
  tests/test_config.py
git diff --check
```

## Test Result

On Apple Silicon with CPU PyTorch 2.13.0, rerun on October 11, 2026 at `fcbbd5b7`: **21 passed, 18 skipped, 421 deselected**. The 18 skips are four CUDA dispatch, eight ROCm dispatch, and six CUDA/graph validation cases. This assistant-run CPU check does not satisfy the submitting-human or GPU requirements. Applicable pre-commit hooks and whitespace checks passed during the prior branch update.

The new regression reaches normalization through a real tiny `Indexer.forward`, real projection layers and single-rank Gloo. A hook stops immediately after normalization, before unavailable GPU-only quantization/indexer operations. It checks strided keys, fp32/fp16/bf16 inputs and nontrivial fp32 parameters against explicit fp32 `F.layer_norm`.

Before the change, the CPU regression fails at the compiled norm under `torch.compiler.set_stance("fail_on_recompile")`; after the change, all six CPU normalization cases pass. This proves removal of that compilation path and the CPU numeric contract, **not** reproduction or resolution of the reported GPU numerical divergence. Four existing CUDA dispatch cases and six new CUDA/graph-replay cases are skipped locally.

## External validation update (October 11, 2026)

[The reporter's October 5 report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58979#issuecomment-5998912306) includes [raw logs and exact configuration](https://gist.github.com/Bizuayeu/0caa413f62be892150d83d4376990a3e). The baseline was `138810056093301f4881050fcf2b1786939da387`; the candidate used the same image with `attention.py` from `fcbbd5b7b5f56f50910216d76f9e45f3c019fba0`. This was reporter-run testing of the production change, not a local run of the full PR test suite.

Across eight fresh baseline launches, replicated keys differed in four launches and candidate sets differed in one. Across four candidate launches, keys and candidate sets agreed at every traced call. Both arms had within-launch greedy-completion variation from other paths, so those completion hashes do not demonstrate model-output equivalence. Reported token rates were explicitly not a serving benchmark.

The requested `lm_eval` accuracy evaluation and `vllm bench serve` comparison with raw output logs remain pending, as do the new CUDA/graph-replay tests. The available local machine is an Apple M4 with CPU PyTorch (`torch.cuda.is_available() == False`, zero CUDA devices), not suitable hardware for these runs. No GPU or model result is inferred from CPU checks. The separate October 6 older-pin/alternative-implementation report is not validation of this PR head.

## Required follow-up before ready for review / merge

- [ ] Run the CUDA norm and graph-replay cases.
- [x] Reporter supplied matched two-GB10 TP2 fresh-launch rank traces and completion hashes for main plus the current production file. The completion hashes did not isolate this change's effect; see limitations below.
- [ ] Run GLM model evaluation and prefill/decode performance measurements. Native normalization can add launches/memory traffic relative to the fused leaf; no performance non-regression is claimed.
- [ ] Complete submitting-human test/model validation under the contribution policy.

Default non-ROCm GLM5Next architectures use breakable CUDA graphs with `CompilationMode.NONE`; the config regression covers these defaults. Explicit opt-out/full-model compilation configurations are not claimed as validated.

## AI assistance

Prepared and independently code-reviewed with OpenAI Codex. The submitter confirmed reviewing the code and explicitly requested this draft. The local CPU tests and lint above were run by the assistant; the submitter has not personally rerun the tests. Human test/model validation and GPU verification remain outstanding and are not asserted complete.

title: [Performance]: DeepSeek-V3.2 under DCP: FP8 sparse attention processes other ranks' masked top-k slots on Hopper
body:
### Proposal to improve performance

With decode context parallelism (DCP), each rank holds 1/dcp of every request's KV cache. For DeepSeek-V3.2, `FlashMLASparseImpl._forward_fp8_kv_mixed_batch` filters the indexer's 2048-wide top-k row per rank with `triton_filter_and_convert_dcp_index(..., compact_valid_to_front=False)`: slots owned by other ranks become `-1`, and the FP8 FlashMLA kernel runs on the full 2048-wide row. The kernel's work follows the row width, not the number of valid slots, so about (dcp-1)/dcp of the slots each rank processes are masked (~75% at DCP4). Under DCP this path also runs the prefill rows.

On Hopper this cannot be fixed in vLLM alone: the SM90 V3.2 sparse decode kernel asserts `topk_length == nullptr` and takes `topk` from `indices.size(-1)`. Slicing the compacted row to a fixed width is fast, but it drops tokens whenever a rank owns more slots than the width, so it is not exact.

Proposal:

1. FlashMLA: let the SM90 V3.2 sparse decode kernel honor `topk_length`, as SM100 already does. The same kernel change is open upstream as deepseek-ai/FlashMLA#216.
2. FlashMLA: the lengths differ per layer, so every layer needs its own schedule plan, and FlashMLA's single-threaded planner (16-24 us per call on H20) eats much of the gain at small batch. Make the planner faster while producing identical plans.
3. vLLM: compact each rank's slots with the in-kernel compaction the trtllm-gen path already uses, pass their count as `topk_length` with one batch entry per token, and bump FlashMLA.

On 8x H20 (TP8 + DCP4 + EP, V3.2, `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache, vLLM main), steps 1 and 3 cut the prefill time of fresh prompts by 24-28% and the decode step time by 3.9-8.3% at 16-32 concurrent requests, with the attended token set unchanged. At 8 requests the decode time is unchanged (-1.9% to +0.8%); with step 2 as well, the decode step time drops by 2.6-10.8% at every point measured. GSM8K accuracy is unchanged.

Does this direction look right? The three changes are ready and tested; I will open the PRs and reference this issue from them.

cc @LucasWilkinson @drakosha

### Report of performance regression

_No response_

### Misc discussion on performance

Related: #46514 (DCP on the `fp8_ds_mla` mixed-batch path, which introduced the masked call), #46076 (DCP for `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, which uses the compacted prefix).

title: [Perf][DCP] DeepSeek-V3.2: skip other ranks' top-k slots in FP8 sparse attention on Hopper
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58980. Under DCP, each rank owns about 2048/dcp slots of the indexer's 2048-wide top-k row. `_forward_fp8_kv_mixed_batch` kept the other ranks' slots as `-1` and ran FlashMLA on the full width, so ~(dcp-1)/dcp of every rank's sparse attention went to masked slots, for decode rows and, under DCP, prefill rows alike.

This PR:

- Compacts the rank's slots into a prefix with the existing in-kernel compaction (`compact_valid_to_front`, already used by the trtllm-gen path) and passes their count as `topk_length`.
- Calls FlashMLA with one batch entry per token, since `topk_length` is per batch entry (the layout the DeepSeek-V4 decode path uses). Each call gets a fresh `FlashMLASchedMeta` because the lengths, and so the plan, differ per layer. Tokens are split across calls so that FlashMLA's fp32 split-KV accumulators stay within 256 MiB per call (2048 tokens at 64 heads).
- Neutralizes empty rows by `topk_length == 0` instead of an all-`-1` scan.
- Passes HY V4's attention sink to the new call as well, since its `_fp8_flash_mla_kernel` override is no longer on the DCP path.
- Moves the query head padding into a helper shared by both FP8 wrappers.
- Needs SM90 V3.2 `topk_length` support in FlashMLA (vllm-project/FlashMLA#27). The `GIT_TAG` bump and the two new kernel files in `cmake/external_projects/flashmla.cmake` follow once it merges. That PR now sits on vllm-project/FlashMLA#30, so they go on top of #61371, which moves the pin to that sync. The faster planner in vllm-project/FlashMLA#28 is optional on top.

The attended token set is exactly the same as before; only the kernel's accumulation order changes.

This does not duplicate an open PR: the masked call comes from #46514, written when the SM90 V3.2 kernel did not accept `topk_length`, and no open PR replaces the masking. This stays a draft until vllm-project/FlashMLA#27 merges and #61371 lands; the `GIT_TAG` bump will then point at the merge commit.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py -k "flashmla or FlashMLA or dcp or fp8 or hyv4"`
  - `test_fp8_mixed_batch_dcp_neutralizes_empty_rows` is updated to the new filter return value.
  - New `test_fp8_dcp_topk_length_matches_masked_rows` (GPU) runs `_forward_fp8_kv_mixed_batch` and checks it against the masked call for DCP 2 and 4, KV interleave 1 and 16, and both 64-token blocks and GLM-5.3's 128-token blocks at a 192-row stride (#57169). It covers rows with fewer than top-k candidates, rows the rank owns nothing of, and batches split across several calls.
  - New `test_hyv4_fp8_per_token_kernel_passes_sink` checks that HY V4's sink reaches the new call.
- Accuracy:
  - GSM8K with `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` (1319 questions, 5-shot), without and with MTP (`num_speculative_tokens=3`).
  - Passkey retrieval at 16K-120K tokens.
  - Teacher-forced log-likelihood of 8 natural documents of ~32K tokens.
- Performance, on prompts of random tokens:
  - Decode step time over a 6 s window in which every request is decoding, at 32K and 128K context with 8, 16 and 32 concurrent requests.
  - Prefill wall time of fresh prompts (no prefix-cache hits) with one output token, for 8 x 32K and 2 x 128K prompts.

Setup: 8x H20, vLLM main (a9eafde59, before the rebase onto current main), FlashMLA 0eee43b with the two FlashMLA PRs as they were before vllm-project/FlashMLA#30, DeepSeek-V3.2, `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 64`, CUDA graphs on.

## Test Result

Unit: 358 passed, 0 failed on H20, on main 818f70c29 with FlashMLA 5dceadb + vllm-project/FlashMLA#27 and vllm-project/FlashMLA#28. The compiled vLLM ops come from the a9eafde59 cu129 nightly: later nightlies are CUDA 13 only and this host's driver is 12.9, and this PR changes only Python.

`pre-commit run --files` on the three changed files: all hooks pass.

The performance and accuracy numbers below predate the rebase (2026-09-28); I'll re-run them on the final pin.

Decode step time (ms):

| context x concurrency | before | after | change | change with both FlashMLA PRs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32K x 8 | 22.80 | 22.36 | -1.9% | -3.4% |
| 32K x 16 | 28.93 | 26.96 | -6.8% | -9.5% |
| 32K x 32 | 41.18 | 37.78 | -8.3% | -10.8% |
| 128K x 8 | 23.30 | 23.48 | +0.8% | -2.6% |
| 128K x 16 | 30.85 | 29.65 | -3.9% | -7.7% |

"after" uses vllm-project/FlashMLA#27 only; the last column adds vllm-project/FlashMLA#28. All columns come from one session. With the first alone, planning every layer (FlashMLA's planner takes ~16 us per call, and V3.2 has 61 layers) takes back what the kernel saves at 8 concurrent requests; the second cuts the planner to ~4 us. Since vllm-project/FlashMLA#30 the stock planner takes ~9 us at that size.

Prefill wall time of fresh prompts (s, mean of two runs):

| prompts | before | after | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 x 32K | 90.85 | 65.44 | -28.0% |
| 2 x 128K | 104.58 | 79.30 | -24.2% |

"after" is with the 256 MiB accumulator bound. Planning up to 8192 tokens per call measured 65.17 and 79.10 s; in a 16K-token batch the bound makes the attention call 1.4-1.8% slower on H20.

Accuracy:

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K (5-shot, 1319) | 0.951 | 0.955 |
| GSM8K with MTP (3 tokens) | 0.955 | 0.957 |
| passkey 16K / 32K / 64K / 120K (10 each) | 10 / 10 / 10 / 10 | 9 / 10 / 10 / 10 |
| mean NLL over 8 x 32K-token documents | 0.60493 | 0.60485 |

The mean MTP acceptance length is 3.11 before and 3.12 after. 38 of the 40 passkey completions are byte-identical before and after. The one miss answers "The pass key is" with "the piece of information you were supposed to find and memorize." instead of the digits. title: [Rust Frontend] Relax schema-aware tool argument conversion
body:
## Purpose

Make the shared schema-aware tool-argument conversion (`tool/parameters.rs`, used by the XML-style tool parsers: Qwen3-Coder, GLM-4.5/4.7, MiniMax M2/M3, DeepSeek DSML, and Hy) more forgiving of how models spell typed values, and stricter about composite types:

- Non-string types ignore surrounding whitespace, so `" 7 "` becomes `7` for an `integer` parameter. `string` parameters keep their text verbatim.
- Integers and numbers accept single underscores between digits (`1_000`), as Python numeric literals do.
- `"nullable": true` (the OpenAPI spelling of an optional parameter, also produced by Transformers' `get_json_schema`) adds `null` to the accepted types.
- `object` / `array` parameters only accept JSON that decodes to that type. Previously `"5"` for an `object` parameter became the number `5`, and `"[1]"` became an array; such values now stay strings, and unions such as `["object", "array"]` still pick the matching member.

This is the bottom of a stack; the `hf` response-template parser above it (#59005) reuses this conversion, so all Rust tool parsers share one set of argument-typing rules instead of each following a different reference implementation.

No open PR covers this conversion.

## Test Plan

```sh
cd rust
cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast --exclude vllm-tool-parser-py
cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat --test roundtrip --no-fail-fast
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

New unit tests in `tool::parameters` cover whitespace handling (including that `string` values are untouched), digit separators and invalid underscore placement, `nullable`, and type-matched composite decoding.

## Test Result

- All 1887 workspace tests pass, including the existing tool-parser suites unchanged; clippy and fmt are clean. `vllm-tool-parser-py` was excluded because it cannot load `libpython3.14.so` on this host, unrelated to this change.
- All 20 chat roundtrip tests with real tokenizers and chat templates pass.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Preserve host prefix publication after request completion
body:
With HiSparse, a request can reach EOS or its output limit in the same step that reports completed host writes. The scheduler handles the final token and cleans up the request before processing the transfer acknowledgements from that same output. Any prefix publication still waiting for those acknowledgements is discarded, leaving valid host KV unavailable for reuse.

This PR preserves the publication information and host-page references until acknowledgement, then publishes the valid pages for reuse.

## Validation

- Four manager cases passed, covering terminal/nonterminal cleanup, partial acknowledgements, request-ID reuse, and allocation pressure.
- One H100 case passed with eager mirroring enabled and delayed acknowledgement: the repeated prompt reused 256 tokens and produced the same output token.
- Model testing used reduced DeepSeek-V3.2 with dummy FP8 weights.
- Formatting and type checks passed.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k 'cleanup_publishes_only_finalized_terminal_pages or terminal_prefix_waits_for_all_workers_and_preserves_identity' -v -s -x --tb=short
# 4 passed

VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py -k terminal_prefix_reuse -v -s -x --tb=short
```

title: [RFC]: Software-dequant fp8 KV cache for MLA on Ampere (sm80/sm86) — consolidate the existing pieces, a 1M-ctx field case, and a validation offer
body:
**Software-dequant fp8 KV cache for MLA on Ampere (sm80/sm86): the pieces exist, here is a consolidated path, a concrete field case, and a standing validation offer**

Three threads on this have stalled independently. This issue asks for a maintainer decision on a merge path and volunteers a production validation site.

**Problem**
MLA models (DeepSeek V4.x, Kimi-K3, GLM-5.3) on Ampere are bf16-KV-only today:

- `TritonMLAImpl` raises for any `--kv-cache-dtype fp8*` below SM89 ("native FP8 (fp8e4nv) requires SM89+") — even though the `fp8_ds_mla` layout is *storage-only*: queries stay bf16 and pages are dequantized on load, so no native fp8 arithmetic is required;
- `TRITON_MLA_SPARSE` lists only auto/fp16/bf16 (`triton_mla_sparse.py`);
- the fp8-capable sparse kernels (FlashMLA-sparse, FlashInfer-MLA-sparse) are sm90+ only.

Cost: **1152 B/token/layer instead of 656 B** (the fp8_ds_mla layout) — 1.76× KV capacity left on the table for every Ampere MLA deployment.

**The pieces already exist (all open, none merged)**
- #47629 — TRITON_MLA_SPARSE for sm80 (stated prerequisite in #48374's discussion)
- #48374 — sparse-path fp8 KV RFC; author verified end-to-end on sm_86, including an engine-level boot on a GLM MoE-DSA model (teacher-forced cosine 0.999996 vs bf16, 1.76× pool) and describes the implementation as working
- #52202 — dense TritonMLA decode RFC (~220-line software-dequant kernel sketch, storage-only fp8_ds_mla)
- #55173 — portable Triton fp8e4nv conversions (SM75 bitcode), A100-validated
- #55184 / #55177 — DSV4 pre-sm90 software-fp8 sparse-MLA omnibus, A100-validated (currently conflicted/unreviewed)

**Field case (why this matters beyond 24 GB cards)**
We run GLM-5.3-Flash (hybrid KDA + sparse-MLA indexer, AWQ W4A16) in production on 4× A800 (sm80) at max-model-len 1M — stock vLLM cannot serve this model on sm80 (no sparse-MLA backend), so a fork is required (wtdcode/vllm-backport v0.13.1). Baseline, verified this week on the bf16 path: 930K-context needle recall 5/5, decode 70 tok/s at 930K context, KV/token 11.6 KiB.

- KV budget 24.7 GiB/card → 2.25M tokens → max **2** concurrent full-length 1M requests (2.15×);
- with fp8 KV the same budget yields **~3.7×**, and 4× full-length becomes reachable within the existing headroom.

Ampere A800 remains the most widely deployed 80 GB datacenter GPU in China (per #57144); "more concurrent full-length contexts" is a measurable, recurring demand there.

**Proposed path (please advise or pick)**
1. Land #55173 (portable conversions) as the shared foundation.
2. Once #47629 lands, accept the sparse-path fp8 KV as a PR based on #48374's verified work.
3. For dense TritonMLA, evaluate #52202's sketch. Everything gated behind explicit `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`/`fp8_ds_mla`; bf16 stays default; warmup/autotune must key on the cache dtype (the dtype-blind autotune behavior is documented in #48374).

**Standing offer**
We can validate candidate branches on our A800 sm80 fleet with a production-shape harness: teacher-forced parity vs bf16, needle-recall at 930K–1M contexts, throughput/concurrency sweeps, and a cross-session state-pollution canary (this hybrid model class is sensitive to cache interactions; our canary keeps the comparison isolated from speculation). We will report numbers publicly either way.

**Questions**
1) Is software-dequant fp8 KV for Ampere acceptable in principle?
2) Preferred sequencing among the pieces above?
3) For the dense TritonMLA decode kernel, is the #52202 sketch the shape you would accept?

title: [RFC]: Meta-device operator capture: see which operators a model runs on this platform, without weights or device memory
body:
**Authors:** @sachinkademane, @imrkbhandari25 ### Motivation. Platform bring-up, kernel planning and performance modelling all start with the same questions: - Which operators does model X execute on platform Y, in what order, with which shapes and dtypes? - Which attention, MoE and quantization backends did vLLM pick for it? - Which kernels are missing on this platform, before downloading the weights or having enough devices to hold them? - When a model or backend changes, which operators change? Today the only way to answer them is to serve the model on real hardware under the torch profiler. That means downloading the checkpoint and holding it in accelerator memory. For current frontier models (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, Ring-2.5-1T) that is a full node per question. Tracing with `FakeTensorMode`/`make_fx` on a booted engine hides vLLM's custom-op bodies behind their fake implementations, so the actual kernels are not visible either. This RFC proposes **meta-device operator capture**. The model is built on `torch.device("meta")` from its HF config alone, and one forward pass is recorded. The **real `current_platform` makes every selection**: attention backend, KV-cache layout and dtype, block sizes, MoE and quantization kernels, IR op priority. Only the device is fake. There are no weights, no model-sized device memory and no kernel execution. Capture runs on a host of the target platform. Its vLLM build (the compiled custom ops and their schemas) and a visible device drive platform detection and backend selection, so XPU operators are captured on an XPU host and CUDA operators on a CUDA host. One small device suffices for any model size: the results below, up to DeepSeek-V4-Pro and Ring-2.5-1T, come from a single Arc Pro B60. Use cases: - kernel coverage planning for a new platform ("which ops have no kernel here") - inputs for performance models and simulators (Chakra execution traces) - CI regression checks on operator sequences when backends change - debugging backend selection ### Proposed Change. A new opt-in package `vllm.profiler.op_capture`, plus three small hooks in core. Nothing changes in the serving path unless `load_format="meta"` or `capture_model_ops` is used. ```python from vllm.profiler.op_capture import BatchSpec, capture_model_ops, format_report capture = capture_model_ops("deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro", device="meta", batch=BatchSpec(num_reqs=2, num_tokens=16)) print(format_report(capture)) ``` ```bash python examples/features/profiling/capture_model_ops.py \ --model zai-org/GLM-5.3 --batch 2,16 --batch 4,4,512 --output-dir out/ ``` #### How it works ```mermaid flowchart TD A["HF config.json only
(no weights)"] --> B["EngineArgs -> VllmConfig
on the REAL current_platform"] B --> C["ForwardHarness.setup()
process groups, workspace, IR op priority,
XPU torch.cuda aliases"] C --> D["get_model(load_format='meta')
MetaModelLoader: build under torch.device('meta'),
quant process_weights_after_loading, skip weight load"] D --> E["KV cache
get_kv_cache_spec -> get_kv_cache_configs
(min_kv_cache_memory_bytes) -> meta tensors in the
platform's layout, bound to the attention layers"] E --> F["Attention metadata builders
one per KV-cache group, real backend classes,
CommonAttentionMetadata from BatchSpec"] F --> G["set_forward_context(attn_metadata, ...)"] G --> H["model.forward (+ embed_multimodal) under OpRecorder"] H --> I{"dispatched op?"} I -- "vllm glue op in
DIRECT_REGISTERED_OPS" --> J["run its Python body
(inner ops recorded at depth+1)"] I -- "leaf kernel
_C / _xpu_C / _rocm_C ..." --> K["record; meta kernel from schema
or OVERRIDES table"] I -- "Triton launch
kernel[grid](meta args)" --> L["record as triton::name, skip launch"] I -- "aten op" --> M["record; native meta kernel"] J --> H H --> N["compute_logits / pooler"] N --> O["OpCapture
ops, module tree, SelectionMetadata, platform gaps"] O --> P["format_report / write_capture_files
(report.txt, ops.txt, ops.sequence.txt, capture.json)"] O --> Q["Chakra ET (optional)"] Q --> R["compare_devices: meta vs real device
in separate processes -> MATCH / MISMATCH"] ``` Step by step: 1. **Config.** `EngineArgs` → `VllmConfig`, exactly as for serving, on the host's real platform. All `EngineArgs` are accepted, e.g. `--hf-overrides '{"quantization_config": null}'` to capture without quantization. `--trust-remote-code` is opt-in, never automatic. 2. **Model on meta.** `load_format="meta"` (`MetaModelLoader`, about 50 lines) builds the model under `torch.device("meta")` and runs the quantization methods' `process_weights_after_loading`, so the repacked weight layouts are the real ones. It reads no weights. 3. **Runner setup, replayed.** `ForwardHarness` reproduces what the worker and model runner do before a forward: - process groups (gloo; for TP>1, one process per rank via `capture_ranks`) - workspace - KV-cache spec, grouping and allocation, sized by the new public `min_kv_cache_memory_bytes` - one attention-metadata builder per group - the forward context Encoder-only, pooling, Mamba/hybrid and multimodal (`BatchSpec.num_mm_items`, the same dummy inputs `profile_run` uses) are covered. 4. **Recording.** `OpRecorder` is a `TorchDispatchMode` that records each op's name, shapes, dtypes, outputs and owning module: - **Glue ops.** vLLM ops registered through `direct_register_custom_op` (now tracked in `DIRECT_REGISTERED_OPS`) have their Python body run rather than their fake. So the attention custom op shows the backend kernels it calls. - **Leaf ops.** Compiled-extension ops get meta kernels derived from their schema (mutating/aliasing) or from a small `OVERRIDES` table. Otherwise `UnsupportedMetaOpError` names the op. - **Triton.** Launches with meta arguments are recorded as `triton::` and not launched. 5. **`keep_going`.** A glue op whose body cannot run on meta (e.g. a `.item()`) is finished with its fake and flagged `body_error`. A forward that still fails returns the partial capture plus a `CaptureFailure` (module and source line). 6. **Report.** The report contains: - selection metadata (platform, backends, KV layout and dtype, block sizes, sliding windows, MoE experts) - **platform gaps**: ops with no kernel for this platform's dispatch key, placeholders, tensors materialized on the device by explicit `device=` - a collapsed module tree and a summary - per-batch differences - files and an optional Chakra ET 7. **Oracle.** `compare_devices(model, "cuda" | "xpu" | ...)` captures the same batch on meta and on the real device, in separate processes, and diffs the normalized execution traces. The same CI job that runs it also catches harness drift. #### Validation (Intel Arc Pro B60, torch 2.14.0+xpu) `compare_devices`, meta vs XPU, gives an exact match for: - Qwen2.5-0.5B - bge-small and bge-reranker (encoder-only / pooling) - Qwen3-Embedding - mamba-130m (prefill and decode) - granite-4.0-h-tiny (hybrid) - Qwen2.5-VL-3B: text batch 1350/1350 ops; image batch 2952/2952 ops Full-size frontier configs on meta only, 2 requests × 16 tokens, `keep_going`: | Model | Ops | Distinct | Notes | | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | | deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro | 11,577 | 64 | XPU sparse MLA + indexer + compressor | | deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 | 8,146 | 64 | | | zai-org/GLM-5.3 | 11,921 | 57 | XPU MLA sparse; needs the small XPU `record_logical_topk_ready` fix (in #59019) | | Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B | 6,202 | 49 | GDN + FlashAttention | | inclusionAI/Ring-2.5-1T | 7,230 | 51 | `vllm::linear_attention` body_error (`.item()`), reported as a gap | | XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL | 4,698 | 40 | fp8, diff-KV Triton attention | | XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL | 3,224 | 40 | | | Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-Next | 3,243 | 49 | | | openai/gpt-oss-120b | 2,751 | 42 | MXFP4; TP=2 also captured (73 all_reduce per rank) | | nvidia/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 | — | — | real gap: modelopt NVFP4 unsupported on XPU | | moonshotai/Kimi-K3 | — | — | real gaps: unconditional `cutlass` import in the model, then XPU MXFP4 MoE lacks the SiTU activation; without quantization, KDA needs a CUDA-only kernel (XPU support: #49598) | The last two rows show the intended use: the capture points to what is missing on this platform, with the source line. The 13 open-weights models on [artificialanalysis.ai](https://artificialanalysis.ai/), same batch: | Result on XPU | Models | | --- | --- | | Full capture | GLM-5.3 (11,921 ops), K2-Horizon-375B-A23B (6,503), Muse-Glimmer-30B (5,482), Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B (5,006), MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL (4,698), Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B (3,801; needs the `requantize_with_max_scale` meta fix in #59019), gpt-oss-120b (2,751), Qwen3.8-27B (2,019) | | Partial, stops at a named gap | MiniMax-M3 (its `nvidia/` path calls FlashInfer), Inkling (imports `vllm.vllm_flash_attn`) | | Fails to build | GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5next` raises on XPU), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (attention requires CUDA), Kimi-K3 (see above) | The five that do not capture fully have only `amd/` and `nvidia/` implementations in `vllm/models/`. #### Design question for maintainers: harness vs. runner hook `ForwardHarness` (in `capture.py`) duplicates a slice of the model runner's setup: - KV-cache allocation - metadata-builder construction - `CommonAttentionMetadata` - the forward context It does not boot an engine, because the runners assume a real device throughout: CUDA graphs, pinned buffers, `.item()` syncs, the sampler. - **Cost:** it can drift from the runner. - **Mitigation:** `compare_devices` runs in CI, with jobs added for Intel, L4 and MI300, and fails on drift. - **Alternative:** a meta/dry-run hook in the V2 runner (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/`) would remove the duplication but touch hot code. Which do maintainers prefer? The PR implements the harness. It can move onto a runner hook later without changing the public API. #### Scope and limits - Only the eager path is captured. Inductor fusions and CUDA-graph replay are not; see #45069 for graph-level tracing. - Code that branches on `tensor.device` sees `meta`; there are a handful of sites. Kernels that bypass the dispatcher are recorded where they are launched (Triton) but not inside (FlashInfer, DeepGEMM, CuTe DSL, aiter wrappers). Both are documented in `docs/design/meta_op_capture.md`. - Only TP is supported. PP, DP and CP are refused, and so are encoder-decoder models (Whisper). - A capture is only valid for the platform it ran on. It needs that platform's vLLM build and a visible device, but not one large enough for the model. - Validated on XPU only so far. The code is platform-neutral, but it has not yet been run on CUDA or ROCm. Help from CUDA/ROCm owners to run `compare_devices` would be appreciated. #### Plan Implementation: #59019. - **One PR** with the feature, in logical commits: loader/registry → capture/recorder → gaps → model families → batches/`keep_going` → TP → multimodal. TP and multimodal can be split out if reviewers prefer. - Small fixes the capture found: - in #59019, as separate commits: XPU `record_logical_topk_ready`, `gather_initial_states` accepting meta tensors, and `requantize_with_max_scale` skipping its value check on meta weights - Kimi-K3's unconditional cutlass import and KDA on XPU: left to #49598, which adds an XPU Kimi-K3 implementation - Ring's `.item()`: a separate PR, since it changes the serving path ### CC List. @22quinn (model loader) @heheda12345 (KV cache) @jikunshang @xuechendi (XPU) - **AI assistance.** Claude Code was used to write the prototype and this RFC. The author reviews every line and is accountable for the design.

title: [Feature][Profiler] Meta-device operator capture
body:
## Purpose

Implements RFC #59018 (full design, flow diagram and results there).

`capture_model_ops(model, device="meta")` returns the operators a model would
execute on the **current platform**: order, shapes, dtypes and owning module.
It needs no weights, allocates no accelerator memory and runs no kernels. The
real `current_platform` still chooses the attention, KV-cache, MoE and
quantization backends; only the device is fake.

Changes, in logical commits:

- **Core hooks (small):**
  - `load_format="meta"`: `vllm/model_executor/model_loader/meta_loader.py`
    and its registration
  - the `DIRECT_REGISTERED_OPS` registry in `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py`
  - public `min_kv_cache_memory_bytes` in `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`,
    with a test
  - `_torch_cuda_wrapper` → `torch_cuda_wrapper` in the XPU runner, so the
    capture can reuse it
- **`vllm/profiler/op_capture/`:**
  - `capture` (`ForwardHarness`, `BatchSpec`)
  - `recorder` (`OpRecorder` TorchDispatchMode; runs glue-op bodies)
  - `meta_ops` (schema-derived meta kernels, `OVERRIDES`, Triton launch
    recording)
  - `report` (selection metadata, platform gaps, module tree, files)
  - `trace` (Chakra ET, `compare_devices`)
  - `parallel` (TP ranks)
- **Coverage:**
  - decoder, MLA/sparse MLA, fp8 KV cache, encoder-only/pooling, Mamba/hybrid,
    multimodal encoder inputs, TP>1
  - `keep_going` partial captures
  - several batches per run
- **Supporting files:**
  - tests: `tests/profiler/test_op_capture.py`
  - docs: `docs/design/meta_op_capture.md`
  - example CLI: `examples/features/profiling/capture_model_ops.py`
  - CI: `op-capture` (L4) and its MI300 mirror in
    `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`, and `op-capture-intel` in
    `.buildkite/intel_jobs/misc_intel.yaml`
- **Three small fixes the capture found:**
  - `XPUMLASparseImpl.record_logical_topk_ready`: a no-op, mirroring ROCm.
    `MLAAttention.forward` calls it on every sparse layer, so without it GLM-5
    fails on XPU with `AttributeError` on its first forward.
  - `gather_initial_states` also accepts meta tensors, so the KDA and Kimi GDN
    prefill paths can be captured. Real-device calls are unchanged.
  - `requantize_with_max_scale` skips its value check on meta weights, so
    static per-tensor FP8 checkpoints such as Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B load
    with `load_format="meta"`. Real-device loading is unchanged.

Apart from the XPU `record_logical_topk_ready` fix, serving behavior does not
change: everything else is opt-in or only taken on meta tensors.

## Not a duplicate

I searched open issues and PRs for "meta device operator capture", "op capture
meta", "load_format meta" and "operator list profiler". Nothing overlaps.
#45069 (CUDA-graph capture tracing) is complementary. The RFC for this work is
#59018.

The fixes have no open PR: searches for `record_logical_topk_ready`,
`xpu_mla_sparse`, `gather_initial_states` and `requantize_with_max_scale`
found none. #56604 was closed as
superseded by #57252, which added the hook for ROCm only; its closing note says
the XPU case is not covered. Kimi-K3's other XPU gaps (the unconditional
cutlass import in `kimi_k3/nvidia/`, KDA on XPU) are left to #49598, which adds
an XPU Kimi-K3 implementation.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/profiler/test_op_capture.py tests/v1/worker/test_xpu_model_runner.py \
    tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py -q
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD)
python examples/features/profiling/capture_model_ops.py \
    --model <model> --max-model-len 2048 --batch 2,16 --keep-going --output-dir out/
```

Parity is checked with `compare_devices(model, "xpu")`, which captures on meta
and on the device in separate processes and diffs the normalized Chakra
execution traces.

## Test Result

- **Tests and lint.** Intel Arc Pro B60 (torch 2.14.0+xpu), rebased on
  `0074fae5dc`:
  - pytest: **186 passed**
  - pre-commit on the changed files passed, including mypy and
    check-test-tethering
- **Parity, meta vs XPU: exact match** for:
  - Qwen2.5-0.5B
  - bge-small
  - bge-reranker
  - Qwen3-Embedding
  - mamba-130m (prefill and decode)
  - granite-4.0-h-tiny
  - Qwen2.5-VL-3B: text 1350/1350 ops; image batch 2952/2952 ops
- **Full-size configs, meta only.** Eleven frontier models, 2 × 16 tokens. Nine
  capture fully:
  - DeepSeek-V4-Pro: 11,577 ops
  - GLM-5.3: 11,921 (needs the XPU `record_logical_topk_ready` fix above)
  - DeepSeek-V4-Flash: 8,146
  - Ring-2.5-1T: 7,230, one `.item()` body_error
  - Qwen3.8: 6,202
  - MiMo-Pro: 4,698
  - MiMo-Flash: 3,224
  - Qwen3-Coder-Next: 3,243
  - gpt-oss-120b: 2,751, also run at TP=2

  Two stop at real XPU platform gaps, which the report names: GLM-5.3-NVFP4 and
  Kimi-K3. See the RFC table. Without quantization, Kimi-K3's KDA layers need
  the aligned Mamba state indices that Model Runner V2 computes with a
  CUDA-only kernel. The capture computes them on CUDA/ROCm and refuses
  elsewhere, naming the kernel. Past that point a CUDA capture would reach
  `gather_initial_states`, which now accepts meta. That is not run yet; on XPU
  a unit test covers it, since the capture stops earlier.
- **The open-weights models on artificialanalysis.ai**, 13 of them, same
  batch. Eight capture fully: GLM-5.3, K2-Horizon-375B, Muse-Glimmer-30B,
  Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B, MiMo-V2.6-Pro, Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B (3,801 ops,
  needs the `requantize_with_max_scale` fix above), gpt-oss-120b and
  Qwen3.8-27B. The other five have no XPU implementation yet: MiniMax-M3 and
  Inkling capture partially and the report names where they stop (FlashInfer,
  `vllm_flash_attn`); GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Kimi-K3 fail to
  build.
- **Report metadata, corrected against the eleven models.** The selection
  metadata describes one representative attention layer, and hybrid models broke
  both of its counts:
  - Head counts came off whichever `AttentionLayerBase` came first, which on a
    hybrid model is a Mamba mixer or an indexer's KV cache. GLM-5.3, Qwen3.8,
    Qwen3-Coder-Next and both DeepSeek-V4 models reported `0 query, 0 kv, head
    size 0`, and Ring-2.5-1T reported `64 query, 0 kv, head size 0`. They now
    report what their configs give: GLM-5.3 and Ring `64 query, 1 kv, head size
    576` (MLA, `kv_lora_rank` 512 + `qk_rope_head_dim` 64), Qwen3.8 `64/4/256`
    without picking up its Gated DeltaNet's 16/128. A model whose attention
    class reports no counts now reads `unknown`, not a fabricated zero.
  - The attention layer count included layers that own a KV cache but run no
    attention, so DeepSeek-V4-Pro reported 243 layers over its 61 decoder layers
    and GLM-5.3 reported 99 over 78. That count was also the denominator of the
    summary's per-layer column, so an operator issued once per decoder layer read
    `0.25` and `0.79` instead of `1.00`. Per-layer counts now divide by decoder
    layers, and the total names the kinds it is made of:
    `99 (78 MLAAttention, 21 DeepseekV32IndexerCache)`.

  Both are metadata only: `ops.txt` is byte-identical across all nine captures
  before and after, and the three non-hybrid models' reports are unchanged too.
- **Not run on CUDA or ROCm yet.** The CI jobs above would be the first run;
  help from CUDA/ROCm owners is welcome.
- **Model evals:** not applicable. The op capture does not affect serving,
  output or accuracy: nothing runs unless `load_format="meta"` or the op-capture
  API is used. The `record_logical_topk_ready` fix is a no-op method that
  replaces an `AttributeError`. I could not serve GLM-5.3 on one B60 to show
  that end to end.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change. The submitter reviews
every changed line, runs the tests above and is accountable for the design.

title: Hidden-state extraction for GLM-5.3-Flash
body:
## Update, October 12, 2026

**Hidden-state extraction works on main** (`258b97ff6b`), following the merges of #56983 (auxiliary-state capture) and #57169 (generic packed KV layout).

Validated the full `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` FP8 checkpoint (`eb9eb208eb0d988989d07a6a12d0fdeb5f52574a`) on 4 B300 GPUs, TP4, MRV2, through Speculators' launcher and HTTP client. All 40 requests passed, including 20 byte-exact comparisons between saved states and references from the same execution. Captured layers: 5/22/43/45. Cases covered mixed lengths, chunk boundaries, repeated requests and identical prompts.

### Observed KV capacity

Both values below come from actual full-model server logs on unmodified main, with extraction off and on. Extraction retains **19.8% of pure-inference KV capacity** in this configuration.

| Server-log measurement | Pure inference | Hidden-state extraction |
|---|---:|---:|
| KV token capacity | 5,196,003 | 1,027,855 |
| Available KV memory per GPU | 149.48 GiB | 150.38 GiB |

Both runs used `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`, `--max-model-len 4096`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 512`, `--max-num-seqs 4`, `--no-enable-prefix-caching`, text-only input, and BLHNC. Pure inference also passed a generation request. The small KV memory-budget difference reflects graph and activation reservations. Pure inference captured CUDA graphs, while extraction selected graph mode `NONE`.

Relevant server-log excerpts:

```text
Pure inference:
Available KV cache memory: 149.48 GiB
GPU KV cache size: 5,196,003 tokens

Hidden-state extraction:
Available KV cache memory: 150.38 GiB
GPU KV cache size: 1,027,855 tokens
```

To observe this, start the model with the settings above, first without speculative decoding or a KV connector, then with `method: extract_hidden_states`, auxiliary layers `[5, 22, 43, 45]`, and `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector`. Read the `Available KV cache memory` and `GPU KV cache size` startup lines in each server log. These are reported cache capacities, not measured throughput or concurrent-request limits at other context lengths.

### Remaining limitations

The packed path keeps 1,152 tokens per hidden-state block. Four BF16 captured layers of width 4,096 need 32 KiB per token, making the hidden-state page 36 MiB. This increases the shared block stride from 13.4 MiB to 36.1 MiB. Extraction also reserves additional state blocks. The smaller cache limits work in flight, but did not prevent successful extraction.

Scope: text prompt states with `max_tokens=1`, prefix caching disabled. Generated-token extraction, dynamic layer switching, 128K-context capacity and performance were not validated.

Draft #59037 is closed because extraction no longer needs it. Its remaining cache-sizing and graph-selection improvements are deferred to prioritize enabling extraction for other models.

Related memory-accounting work: #56822, #53074 and #50894.

Validation and analysis used AI assistance.


---

The original issue is preserved below as a reference for the prerequisite and validation workflow. Its status statements describe the situation before this update.

## TLDR

| PR | Status | Why |
|---|---|---|
| [#56983](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56983) | ✅ merged | Aux hidden-state capture in `glm5next` |
| [#57169](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57169) | ✅ merged  | Replace GLM-5.3-Flash's custom kv-layout with the generic packed one |
| [#59037](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59037) | WIP - Builds on #57169, and #56983 | `HiddenStateCacheSpec` + connector under `BLHNC` |

## Motivation

We want to use `method: extract_hidden_states` on `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, for example to generate training data for EAGLE3/DFlash/DSpark drafters with speculators. On main (`25b0add7b8`) this doesn't work. Several PRs cover parts of it, mostly aimed at DFlash2 serving. This issue lists what has to be solved and which PRs and issues address each part.

## What is missing on main

1. `glm5next` does not implement `SupportsEagle3` / `EagleModelMixin`, so there is no aux hidden-state capture. Startup fails with `Model does not support EAGLE3 interface`.
2. From reading the code on main, the KV cache groups can't be built once a `HiddenStateCacheSpec` layer is present:
   - `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` requires `type(spec) is MLAAttentionSpec`. `HiddenStateCacheSpec` is a subclass of `MLAAttentionSpec`, so the check fails and the function returns `None`.
   - The generic fallback then fails on page-size unification for `indexer.k_cache`, because MLA pages can't be padded.
   - The full-allocation fallback explicitly rejects `HiddenStateCacheSpec`.

## What needs to be solved

### 1. Aux hidden-state capture in `glm5next`

- `glm5next` must implement `SupportsEagle3` and capture the mHC-complete layer output (`hc_post` + `hc_contract`, not `hidden + residual`). [#56983](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56983) does this (reviewer: @ivanium). [#58834](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58834) fixes the sequence-parallel layout of the non-mHC layers in the same file, which the aux capture relies on.
- **Recommendation:** land [#56983](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56983).
- Related: [#55682](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55682) (same capture, with unit tests; largely redundant), [#55423](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55423) and [#55620](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55620) (earlier attempts), [#54451](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54451) (issue).

### 2. Generic kv-layout for GLM-5.3-Flash

At startup, GLM-5.3-Flash's custom grouping (`_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next`) doesn't support `HiddenStateCacheSpec`: it only knows GLM-5.3-Flash's own cache types (MLA, indexer, kpool tail, KDA state) and has no place for an extra layer in its kv-layout. vLLM then falls back to the generic grouping, which can't unify GLM-5.3-Flash's MLA and indexer page sizes, and startup fails with `NotImplementedError` on `indexer.k_cache`.

- **Generic packed kv-layout (recommended):** [#55219](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55219) / [#57169](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57169) remove the custom kv-layout and route GLM-5.3-Flash through the generic packed (`BLHNC`) kv-layout, which supports mixed page sizes. They are not aimed at hidden-state extraction. Land [#57169](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57169).
- **Extend the custom kv-layout:** the [`shanjiaz/vllm` fork](https://github.com/shanjiaz/vllm/tree/glm5-next-aux-hidden-state-concurrency-fix) appends the hidden-state group and places its storage after the native pages. It works under concurrent load, but the custom GLM-5.3-Flash kv-layout code is being replaced by [#57169](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57169).

### 3. `HiddenStateCacheSpec` and the extractor/connector under `BLHNC`

The generic packed path already adds hidden-state layers as their own KV cache group, so it may work as is on top of [#57169](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57169), but this hasn't been tested with GLM-5.3-Flash. To check:

- **Block size:** the hidden-state group keeps GLM-5.3-Flash's block size (1152 tokens on GB200 TP4), so its page would be ~66 MB (~57 KB per token). The packed kv-layout sizes every block by the largest group's page, so the native blocks (~13 MB) would grow to ~66 MB and be ~80% padding, cutting the target's KV capacity ~5×. This is a memory cost, not a correctness issue; if confirmed, a smaller hidden-state block size (e.g. 128–256 tokens) would fix it in a small follow-up PR.
- **Connector:** `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector` asks for `LBNHC`. The resolver falls back to `BLHNC` with a warning, but reading and writing hidden states under `BLHNC` is untested.
- **Tests:** a regression test that no hidden-state page overlaps a native page, and an end-to-end test with concurrent, mixed-length requests that checks each request's hidden states are finite, have the expected shape, and agree with a serial reference.

Related: [#56822](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56822) (hidden-state memory accounting on hybrid models), [#53074](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53074) (DeepSeek-V4), [#50894](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50894) (TP page size).

Keep an eye on:
- [#53558](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53558): pluggable `KVCacheConfigBuilder` that lets models and platforms override KV cache planning; it also touches the hidden-state connector tests.
- [#58636](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58636) / [#58979](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58979): the GLM-5.x sparse indexer's key norm is autotuned per TP rank, so outputs can differ between launches. This affects comparisons against a serial reference in the end-to-end test.

## Adjacent (not required for extraction)

- [#58454](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58454): kpool corruption with speculative decoding (k ≥ 2).
- [#55800](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55800): sliding-window DFlash drafter admission scales with the full sequence length.
- [#58638](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58638): RFC on KV grouping for hybrid models with drafters.
- [#56417](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56417) / [#56442](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56442): `extract_hidden_states` uses the first column's feedback for multi-token outputs (only relevant with `max_tokens > 1`).

### Speculators-related

- **Stale captures with prefix caching:** the speculators `dynamic_hidden_states` plugin (`AuxLayerWorkerExtension`) lets you change the captured layer set at runtime through `POST /aux_hidden_state_layers`. The hidden-state cache blocks are prefix-cached like any other KV block, so after a layer switch a prefix-cache hit returns hidden states from the old layer set. Upstream vLLM fixes the layer set at startup, so this can't happen there. Workaround: `--no-enable-prefix-caching`.
- **torch.compile / CUDA graphs:** the plugin's compiled path for dynamic aux-layer selection doesn't cover GLM-5.3-Flash yet, so it has only been validated with `--enforce-eager`.
