title: [Bug][ROCm] v0.30.0: GLM-5.3-Flash cannot boot on gfx942 — ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl missing record_logical_topk_ready (#57252 not in the release)
body:
### Your current environment

```
vLLM Version                 : 0.30.0
Image                        : vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.30.0 (official, digest sha256:2e7da1ad1c66…, no custom layers)
PyTorch version              : 2.12.0+git6bbd260
ROCm Version (image)         : 7.2.3 (/opt/rocm-7.2.3, bundled); host user space: ROCm 7.2.4
GPU                          : 8x AMD Instinct MI308X (gfx942), TP=4
Orchestrator                 : GPUStack v2.2.3 (docker backend)
Model                        : ZhipuAI/GLM-5.3-Flash — Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration,
                               native FP8 (weight_block_size [128,128]), 62 shards / 305.79 GiB
<!-- run `vllm collect-env` in the serving container and paste the full output here -->
```

Serve command (production):

```
vllm serve /models/GLM-5.3-Flash --served-model-name glm-5.3-flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_jit_warmup": false}'
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug


Every startup on v0.30.0 dies in `profile_run` (~2 min into init) on all TP workers, and the server never becomes healthy:

```
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 572, in determine_available_memory
  self.model_runner.profile_run()
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 955, in profile_run
...
File ".../vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/attention.py", line 590, in forward
File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py", line 235, in forward
  self.mla_attn.impl.record_logical_topk_ready()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
AttributeError: 'ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl' object has no attribute 'record_logical_topk_ready'

RuntimeError: Worker failed with error ''ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl' object has no
attribute 'record_logical_topk_ready'', ... Engine core initialization failed.
```

Root cause: `MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper.forward` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py:235`) calls
`impl.record_logical_topk_ready()` on **every** sparse MLA layer. On ROCm the only sparse MLA backend is
`ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`, whose impl `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` extends `MLAAttentionImpl` +
`SharedTopkIndicesBuffer`. In the `v0.30.0` tag neither base provides the method — the only definition lives on
`SparseMLACommonImpl` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/sparse_mla_attention.py:717`), which the ROCm impl
does not extend. The method was added on `main` by #57252 (merged 2026-09-17; present in tag `v0.30.1rc0`,
verified against `main`'s `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`), but it did not make it into `v0.30.0`.

This is the same regression as #58575 (GLM-5.3 `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` on MI325X) and regression 1 of #57248.
This report adds an independent reproduction for `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` (GLM-5.3-Flash) on MI308X
(gfx942) at TP=4, plus long-context findings below. Since the call site runs on every sparse MLA layer and ROCm
has no alternative sparse backend, no flag combination avoids it on ROCm.

Additional gfx942 data point: in the `v0.30.0` tag, `fwht128_quant_fp8`
(`vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/kpool_compress.py`) still hardcodes `torch.float8_e4m3fn` and the 448 clamp
(verified by exact-source match against #56607's diff anchors), so the >16K-token chunked-prefill indexer path on
gfx942 is expected to hit the flydsl compile failure documented in #56607. We validated long context **with**
#56607 applied (see below); we did not run the >16K case on stock v0.30.0.


### Workaround (validated on 8x MI308X, TP=4)

1. Add the no-op from #57252 to `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl`
   (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`) — equivalent to the base-class default proposed in #56604:

   ```python
   def record_logical_topk_ready(self) -> None:
       pass
   ```

2. Keep `--kernel-config '{"enable_jit_warmup": false}'` — the jit-warmup subsystem otherwise crashes on this
   path (`'function' object has no attribute 'compile'`, #57248 regression 2 / #57192).

With (1) alone the engine boots and serves short requests. With (1) + (2) + the still-open gfx942 GLM patches
(#56607, #56469, #56381, #56584), a 28,842-token chunked-prefill needle-in-a-haystack request completes with
exact recall (prefix cache hit 27,648 tokens), and the server has been running in production since.

### Request

- Backport #57252 into a `v0.30.x` patch release (same ask as #58575), or add a known-issues note for
  GLM-5.3 / sparse-MLA models on ROCm to the v0.30.0 release notes.
- Before pointing AMD ROCm users at `vllm-openai-rocm:latest` (= v0.30.0 today) for GLM-5.3-Flash, note that
  boot needs #57252 and gfx942 long context additionally needs the open PRs #56607 (and, for production
  correctness on MI308X, #56469/#56381/#56584 from the 0.29-based stacks).

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

*Search results: #58575 (same root cause, different model arch / GPU), #57248, #57252, #56604, #56607. This
report does not duplicate their content; it adds the MI308X/gfx942 + Glm5Next TP4 reproduction and the
long-context status on v0.30.0.*

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Never allocate GPU pages without host backing
body:
## Description

When the HiSparse host pool fills, `HiSparseSourceManager.allocate_new_blocks` gives new pages a null host entry. Those pages are never written back, so they never become clean and their GPU blocks can never be reclaimed: they stay pinned for the life of the request. Freeing host capacity does not fix it, because later allocations extend the host table and the freed blocks go to new tail pages, never to the old null ones. Host prefix publication for the request also stalls at the first null page.

The result is GPU KV pressure and preemptions that HiSparse is meant to prevent, plus lost host prefix-cache coverage, persisting after host capacity has recovered.

Fix: never allocate a page without host backing (alternative to #58963, which backfills null pages after the fact):

- `HiSparseSourceManager.get_num_blocks_to_allocate` requires host blocks for every page being allocated, not just external-load destinations, and reuses the existing admission sentinel when they don't fit. The scheduler then waits or preempts exactly as it does for GPU exhaustion.
- The best-effort `allocate_new_blocks` override (null padding) is deleted.
- `has_pending_reclamation` also reports host blocks that an in-flight write-back will return (freed request, spill not yet acked), so the scheduler waits a step instead of over-preempting.
- Startup rejects a host pool that cannot hold one `max_model_len` request (plus the null block and a copy-on-write tail), which would otherwise livelock.

## Effect on KV-cache memory over time

**Before.** While the host pool is full, every page a running request seals gets a null host entry and keeps its GPU block for the rest of the request. The pinned set only grows: host blocks freed later go to new tail pages, never to the old null ones. A request that decodes through a host-full window therefore holds GPU KV proportional to the tokens produced during that window, as if HiSparse were off for those pages, and releases it only when it finishes or is preempted. Across the batch, GPU free blocks drift down while the host stays full, and the scheduler preempts (and later recomputes) requests that HiSparse should have kept running. Prefix publication for those requests also stops at the first null page, so the host prefix cache never covers the rest of their context.

**After.** Every GPU-resident page has a host page, so its GPU footprint is transient: a sealed page is dirty until its write-back completes (about one step), stays pinned while within the two-page active tail, and is unpinned once the request can read from host (it has a hot region). Unpinned pages stay readable but count as free, so the GPU pool reclaims them under pressure. Per-request GPU usage is bounded by the hot region, the active tail and in-flight write-backs, independent of context length, for as long as the request runs.

The host pool becomes the hard capacity limit instead: running requests together hold one host block per computed page, and when it is full, new allocations wait or preempt even if GPU blocks are free. Since HiSparse only pays off when the host pool is much larger than the GPU pool, this replaces the gradual, hard-to-see GPU buildup above with a rare, explicit admission limit.

## Related

- #58963 fixes the same bug by backfilling host blocks for null pages after capacity frees up (one page per step). This PR prevents the null pages instead, which removes rather than adds state; only one of the two should land.
- #57457 also edits `HiSparseSourceManager.get_num_blocks_to_allocate` (counts GPU copies pinned by a host-prefix hit). The changes compose: its copy-pin count replaces this PR's final `return 0`.
- #58949's steady-state concurrency estimate assumes resident pages spill to host; this PR makes that hold under host pressure, and its host-pool gauges become the direct signal for the new admission limit.

## Test Plan

Repro on main (unit-level): with a 3-block host pool, the request's pages 1-3 get null host entries; after the donor frees its block, the capacity goes to new tail page 4, and pages 1-3 stay pinned (`ref_cnt=1`) indefinitely while page 5 is null again.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py -q
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py -v
```

## Test Result

- CPU: 341 passed; other HiSparse-tagged suites (scheduler, NIXL HMA, stats, config): 22 passed.
- e2e (B300, reduced DeepSeek-V3.2, dummy weights): 3 passed. The new `test_hisparse_host_exhaustion_defers_requests` fails on main (a scheduled request has a null host page).

Accuracy with trained weights and serving throughput under host pressure were not measured.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the implementation, tests, and this description.

title: [RFC]: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash performance on MI325X (gfx942)
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI325X (gfx942), TP4, `aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16`, DSpark-5, 262144→1024, prefix cache off, 16k chunk. Decode is in good shape. The open work is prefill.

Rank-0 `execute_context_1(16384)_generation_0` on nightly `g0961bbae2`, except the replay row:

| Stack | 16k step |
|---|---:|
| AITER indexer auto | 590.928 ms |
| Gated `mfma_r4_w4` ([#58366](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58366)) | 555.650 ms |
| That path + HIP QuickReduce INT4 | 494.994 ms |
| Same path, FlyDSL QuickReduce INT4 | 486.898 ms |
| FlyDSL QuickReduce + decoder replay | 473.4 ms |

The replay row is the median of sixteen `execute_context_1(16380)_generation_0` steps (range **408.4–557.3 ms**), not the `g0961bbae2` capture.

Serving GeoMean TTFT on the HIP QuickReduce row, concurrency 2/4/6/8, 20 prompts, is **34.71 s**. Decoder replay on that HIP path brings the same sweep to **18.96 s** (§7). FlyDSL QuickReduce is the selected collective (§6.2); it does not yet have its own MC2–8 GeoMean.

[vLLM #56506](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56506) is the gfx950 roadmap. [vLLM #52911](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52911) is the V4/Pro umbrella. This issue is the gfx942 follow-on. Ceilings below are trace search bounds, not promised uplift.

---

## 1. Indexer prefill

gfx942 prefill was on AITER's auto FlyDSL variant. [#58366](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58366) selects `mfma_r4_w4` when there is no PCP plan and no DCP shard. Other layouts stay on auto.

Measured 16k step **590.928 → 555.650 ms**. MC2 TTFT **29.716 → 27.901 s**. Dumped engine-window logits were bit-exact. That gate is the indexer in the 34.71 s result.

Later tests use merged [aiter#4963](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4963) plus occupancy splits [aiter#5921](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5921). A profile of that path launched 1256 `r4_w4` and 242 `r4_w2`.

## 2. Sparse MLA prefill

`_sparse_attn_prefill_ragged_kernel` is **4.455 s / 1320 calls** in the QuickReduce profile, **139.2 ms** of the 16k step. This is the largest remaining prefill attention slice.

It is not the gfx950 OPUS path ([#54855](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54855), merged). [aiter#6002](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6002) is the candidate kernel. It still needs numerical parity, an isolated A/B, a 16k trace, and a same-session serving A/B.

## 3. Dense GEMM

Flash dense weights are MXFP8 32×32 UE8M0. On gfx942 they still run as dequantized BF16 / mixed hipBLASLt `Cijk_*`. That slice is **21.0 ms / 38 calls**.

### 3.1 Library retune

Offline TunableOp on the 22 prefill shapes did not move the step. The largest 16k GEMM, `5120×16384×15360`, stayed on the default at **2.85 ms**. Closed at **0 ms**. Do not retune this path again.

### 3.2 Native MXFP8

AITER's MXFP8 GEMM family is gfx1250-only. A gfx942 32-group UE8M0 kernel is new work. The **21 ms** slice is the search ceiling, not a forecast.

## 4. mHC

Flash collapses each sublayer with the previous sublayer's pre-mix. Pro's immediate fusion does not apply.

### 4.1 Delayed pre, merged

[#56503](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56503) routes the delayed pre through AITER. [#56513](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56513) folds post into that pre at or below 1024 tokens, and falls back to separate kernels above that. Both are merged.

### 4.2 Large M

Above 1024 tokens the seam is still separate kernels. Isolated 16k cost is **1.033 ms/seam** versus **0.821–0.822 ms** for the immediate/fused seam. Eighty seams is about **17 ms/step**. Keeping the carried pre-mix may recover only part of that, or none.

[#52737](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52737) is merged and is the Pro immediate fusion. It is not a legal swap here.

### 4.3 Collapse + RMSNorm

Fusing only `hc_collapse` with the following RMSNorm, and leaving the HIP post and delayed-pre kernels alone, was **−0.55 ms** on the 495 ms stack (off/on/off **494.939 / 494.371 / 494.900 ms**). The fused op in that run was **256 µs**, against collapse **~199 µs** plus RMSNorm **~53 µs**. Not the 4.2 item.

[#5824](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5824) is merged. It replaces the whole seam with Triton split-K for gfx950. On gfx942 at M=16384 it was slower: **1.159 → 1.315 ms/seam**. Leave it for gfx950.

## 5. MoE prefill tile

The engine pads the TP4 intermediate **576 → 768**. gfx942 has no MXFP4 matrix instruction, so this stays MXFP4 weights with BF16 activations.

The tests below use Bn=128, Bk=128, 4 warps. [aiter#5667](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5667) is the JSON dispatch for that padded shape. Isolated W1+W2 at M=16384: stock Triton **24.86 ms**, Bn128/Bk128/w4 **6.85 ms**, #5667 **6.16 ms**. No engine A/B yet.

## 6. Collectives

### 6.1 HIP QuickReduce INT4

`VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4` selects the HIP path when FlyDSL is not wired in. With #58366, the 16k step is **494.994 ms**. This is the path in the 34.71 s result.

20 prompts, 262144→1024. Median TTFT / median TPOT / output tok/s / interactivity (1000/TPOT):

| MC | TTFT | TPOT | tok/s | ix |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 24.82 s | 11.06 ms | 56.45 | 90.38 |
| 4 | 41.17 s | 26.73 ms | 59.68 | 37.41 |
| 6 | 35.43 s | 60.60 ms | 60.57 | 16.50 |
| 8 | 40.10 s | 87.84 ms | 61.18 | 11.38 |
| GeoMean | **34.71 s** | **35.42 ms** | **59.44** | **28.23** |

### 6.2 FlyDSL QuickReduce

The kernel is merged [aiter#4970](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4970) (`QuickAllReduceInt4`). vLLM does not call it yet.

Use [#59478](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59478). With `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4` it builds the FlyDSL communicator in place of HIP, and falls back to HIP if FlyDSL cannot start. Until that PR is in the tree, wire the same kernel with a local hook on `VLLM_ROCM_FLYDSL_QR_INT4=1`. Leave the hook unset and INT4 stays on HIP `QUICK_REDUCE`. The measurements below used the hook. The log lists `FLYDSL_QUICK_REDUCE` first.

Matched 16k step **494.574 → 486.898 ms** (**−7.7 ms**). Same-session serving, 20 prompts, 262144→1024, DSpark-5, no replay, acceptance identical at **70.65% / 4.53**:

| Point | HIP median TTFT | FlyDSL median TTFT | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| MC2 | 24.868 s | 24.660 s | −208 ms |
| MC4 | 37.631 s | 37.096 s | −534 ms |

MC4 mean is flat (−34 ms). An earlier MC2 gap of about 1.5 s did not repeat against the HIP control at **24.868 s**. No MC6/MC8 on this pair, and no MC2–8 GeoMean.

## 7. Decoder SWA bounded replay

[#59039](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59039) constructs decoder replay on the AMD model and exposes it on `amd/vl_model.py`, which ROCm loads even with `--language-model-only`. It needs [#59136](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59136). Layers 21–39 run on the replay batch and are scattered back before the final mHC post, collapse, and norm. On with the V2 runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`). `--no-swa-bounded-replay` turns it off. Prefix-cache SWA replay stays off on ROCm.

gfx950 smoke is in the #59039 body: warm 16k TTFT **522 → 356 ms**, GSM8K strict-match **0.9143** off / **0.9166** on.

gfx942, HIP QuickReduce, decoder replay, DSpark-5, 20 prompts, 262144→1024. Median TTFT / median TPOT / output tok/s / interactivity, except the GeoMean row. Compare with the 34.71 s table in §6.1:

| MC | TTFT | TPOT | tok/s | ix |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 13.66 s | 7.52 ms | 95.45 | 132.98 |
| 4 | 22.51 s | 16.04 ms | 104.85 | 62.34 |
| 6 | 19.35 s | 34.60 ms | 107.39 | 28.90 |
| 8 | 21.71 s | 49.27 ms | 109.58 | 20.30 |
| GeoMean | **18.96 s** | **21.29 ms** | **104.17** | **46.96** |

60-shot GSM8K on that serve is **0.9219**.

FlyDSL QuickReduce plus decoder replay has MC2 and MC6 only, 20/20 succeeded. MC4 and MC8 were not run:

| MC | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | Mean TPOT | tok/s |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 12.54 s | 12.41 s | 7.08 ms | 103.4 |
| 6 | 20.66 s | 17.32 s | 28.74 ms | 117.7 |

Spec-off rank-0 trace, HIP INT4, 2 × 262144→1024, 16k chunks, nightly `gdc36fcce9` (not the `g0961bbae2` stack in the motivation table):

| | off | on |
|---|---:|---:|
| `execute_context_1(16384)` CUDA total | 21.699 s | 14.378 s |
| CUDA time avg | 678.097 ms | 224.656 ms |
| calls | 32 | 64 |

The off arm is the 678 ms annotation, not the 495 ms DSpark step above. The call count doubled, so 225 ms is not a substitute for either number. At the same launch count, MoE CUDA fell **9.81 → 6.33 s** and sparse prefill **4.43 → 2.31 s**. `hipPointerGetAttribute` inside the region also fell **8.73 → 4.59 s**; that is not replay work. The per-kernel slices in §§2–4 were taken from the **494.994 ms** step and have not been recomputed on the replay stacks.

## 8. Closed on this sheet

[#56628](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56628) strides the DSA decode candidate mask over the live context. Merged. No prefill credit here.

[#56638](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56638) re-enables the fused top-k + SWA combine. Open. Already inside the 590.9 ms baseline above.

---

## Tracking

- [x] gfx942 indexer prefill `mfma_r4_w4` ([#58366](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58366)) — 590.928 → 555.650 ms. Later tests use [aiter#4963](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4963) plus [aiter#5921](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5921)
- [ ] gfx942 sparse MLA prefill — 139.2 ms/step; candidate [aiter#6002](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6002)
- [x] hipBLASLt retune of the BF16 dense path — 0 ms
- [ ] gfx942-native MXFP8 32-group UE8M0 GEMM — 21 ms slice is the ceiling
- [x] Delayed mHC pre ([#56503](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56503))
- [x] Post folded into delayed pre for M ≤ 1024 ([#56513](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56513))
- [ ] Large-M delayed mHC seam — up to ~17 ms/step
- [x] Collapse + RMSNorm only — −0.55 ms, not 4.2
- [x] [#5824](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5824) — gfx950 whole-seam fusion; slower on gfx942 at 16k
- [ ] MXFP4 MoE prefill tile ([aiter#5667](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5667)) — no engine A/B yet; tests use Bn=128, Bk=128, 4 warps
- [x] HIP QuickReduce INT4 — 34.71 s GeoMean, 494.994 ms step, with #58366
- [x] FlyDSL QuickReduce INT4 measured — 494.574 → 486.898 ms; MC2 −208 ms, MC4 median −534 ms. Kernel [aiter#4970](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4970)
- [ ] Wire FlyDSL QuickReduce in vLLM ([#59478](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59478)). Until then, a local hook on `VLLM_ROCM_FLYDSL_QR_INT4=1`
- [x] Decoder replay on HIP QuickReduce ([#59039](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59039), [#59136](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59136)) — MC2–8 GeoMean TTFT 34.71 s → 18.96 s
- [ ] FlyDSL QuickReduce plus decoder replay — 16k step median 473.4 ms; serving is MC2 and MC6 only
- [x] DSA candidate mask ([#56628](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56628)) — no prefill credit
- [ ] Fused top-k + SWA combine ([#56638](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56638)) — open; already inside the 590.9 ms baseline

### Environment

MI325X (gfx942), TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MXFP4 MoE (`aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16`), MXFP8 dense weights, DSpark 5-token MTP, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, prefix cache off. The 494.994 ms table is vLLM nightly `0.3.1.dev251+g0961bbae2`.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug][ROCm] v0.30.0: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash cannot boot on gfx942 — Engram pinned-host CPU offload lost on the AMD path (+47 GiB/rank GPU), OOM in profile_run
body:
### Your current environment

```
vLLM Version                 : 0.30.0
Image                        : vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.30.0 (official, digest sha256:2e7da1ad1c66…, no custom layers)
PyTorch version              : 2.12.0+git6bbd260
ROCm Version (image)         : 7.2.3 (/opt/rocm-7.2.3, bundled); host user space: ROCm 7.2.4
GPU                          : 8x AMD Instinct MI308X (gfx942, 191.98 GiB each), TP=4 (DeepSeek on GPUs 0-3)
Orchestrator                 : GPUStack v2.2.3 (docker backend)
Model                        : deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash — DeepseekV41ForCausalLM,
                               FP8 (ue8m0) attention + MXFP4 experts, 48 shards / 475.25 GiB,
                               engram_num_embeddings=[384006168, 384016682], head_dim=256
Working image (baseline)     : vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-eed1f3d0c6043bd494424a22443ee198dd56f657
                               (vLLM 0.1.1.dev50+geed1f3d0c, 0.29.x nightly, ~2026-09-12)
<!-- run `vllm collect-env` in the serving container and paste the full output here -->
```

Serve command (production):

```
vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --tokenizer-mode=deepseek_v41 --tensor-parallel-size=4 --gpu-memory-utilization=0.94 \
  --moe-backend=aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16 --tool-call-parser=deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser=deepseek_v41 --mm-encoder-tp-mode=data \
  --max-model-len 819200 --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_MXFP8_EMULATION_DEQUANT_AT_LOAD=1
VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Every startup on v0.30.0 dies in `profile_run` (~2.5 min into init) on all TP workers, and the server never becomes healthy:

```
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 572, in determine_available_memory
  self.model_runner.profile_run()
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 955, in profile_run
...
File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/vl_model.py", line 309, in forward
File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py", line 1077, in forward
File ".../vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py", line 1045, in rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer
  workspace_manager.get_simultaneous(((decode_rows, max_model_len), torch.float32))
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/workspace.py", line 207, in _ensure_workspace_size
  self._current_workspaces[workspace_id] = torch.empty(...)
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 50.00 GiB.
GPU 0 has a total capacity of 191.98 GiB of which 37.10 GiB is free.
Of the allocated memory 150.30 GiB is allocated by PyTorch ...
```

(The same model + same args start fine on the 0.29.x nightly image above the same GPUs.)

### Root cause (code-level, both images inspected)

Two facts combine:

1. **0.30.0 lost the Engram pinned-host CPU offload on the AMD/common path.**
   On the 0.29 nightly, `vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/common/engram.py:914` wired
   `cpu_offload=engram_config.cpu_offload if engram_config else True` into the
   `ParallelEngramEmbedding`, so the two DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Engram tables
   (94.4 GiB each; 23.60 GiB per rank at TP4) lived in pinned host memory and were
   read via UVA — each rank's log shows
   `Engram table offloaded to pinned host memory: 9600xxxx rows x 256, 23.60 GiB per rank`,
   and `Model loading took 100.09 GiB` per rank.

   In v0.30.0 the tree was renamed `deepseek_v4_1` → `deepseek_v41`. The NVIDIA path
   still reads the config (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py:358-365`,
   `get_current_vllm_config().engram_config`), but the AMD model instantiates the
   common `Engram` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py:64`), whose
   `ParallelEngramEmbedding._allocate_weights()` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py:695`)
   now allocates unconditionally on the current (CUDA) device — the `cpu_offload`
   wiring is gone from this path entirely. `EngramConfig.cpu_offload` still defaults
   to `envs.VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` = `True` in 0.30.0, and
   `VllmConfig._resolve_and_verify_engram_config()` even auto-creates the config for
   models with Engram layers — the AMD path just never consults it.

   Result: `Model loading took 147.3 GiB` per rank (+47.2 GiB = exactly 2 x 23.60 GiB),
   no offload log lines.

2. **The profile-time sparse-indexer workspace reservation is unchanged and large.**
   `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` (profiling early-exit branch) reserves a decode-logits
   workspace of `(decode_rows, max_model_len)` fp32. `_max_decode_logits_rows()` would
   bound it to `max_num_seqs * (1 + num_speculative_tokens)` = 192 rows (592 MiB), but
   that bound requires `get_current_vllm_config()`, which is not set during `profile_run`
   in either version — so both images fall back to `num_batched_tokens` = 16384 rows:
   16384 x 819200 x 4 B = **50.00 GiB**.

   On the nightly this 50 GiB reservation succeeds (weights 100.09 GiB → ~80 GiB free)
   and the engine starts (`Available KV cache memory: 11.29 GiB`). On 0.30.0 with
   GPU-resident Engram tables only 37.10 GiB is free → the allocation OOMs and the
   engine core dies.

### Fix

Restore the nightly default on the common/AMD path — one small patch to
`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py::_allocate_weights()`:

```python
cpu_offload = True
try:
    engram_config = get_current_vllm_config().engram_config
    if engram_config is not None:
        cpu_offload = engram_config.cpu_offload
except Exception:
    pass
kwargs = {"device": "cpu", "pin_memory": True} if cpu_offload else {}
```

(also guarding with `is_uva_available()` like the NVIDIA path, and re-adding the
`Engram table offloaded to pinned host memory` log line).

With only this change, v0.30.0 boots identically to the 0.29 nightly on the same rig:

| | 0.29 nightly | v0.30.0 + engram patch |
|---|---|---|
| Engram offload log | 23.60 GiB per rank x8 | 23.60 GiB per rank x8 |
| Model loading | 100.09 GiB/rank | 100.09 GiB/rank |
| Available KV cache | 11.29 GiB (4,031,384 tokens, 4.92x concurrency) | 11.33 GiB (4,045,600 tokens, 4.94x) |
| init engine | 286.43 s | 280.38 s |
| Short request (17*23) | — | `391` correct |
| 30,060-token needle (chunked prefill) | — | exact recall |

### Suggested upstream fix

Make `ParallelEngramEmbedding._allocate_weights()` in
`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py` honor
`vllm_config.engram_config.cpu_offload` (with the `EngramConfig` default, i.e.
`envs.VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` / `True`), matching the NVIDIA variant
(`deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py`) and the pre-refactor behavior
(`deepseek_v4_1/common/engram.py:914`). Otherwise every ROCm deployment of
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 on 192 GB GPUs cannot boot on 0.30.0.

Side note: the profile-time fallback in `_max_decode_logits_rows()` means the 50 GiB
decode-logits workspace is reserved and locked even on healthy boots, which is why
TP4 MI308X ends up with only ~11 GiB of KV cache at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.94`.
The config-based tight bound (192 rows) would presumably be used if
`get_current_vllm_config()` were reachable during profiling — worth a look, though it
is orthogonal to this regression.

Related: #58310 (documents that `cpu_offload=True` is the intended default for these
tables; sizes match our measurements), #58808 (notes `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` churn),
#58782 (unrelated ROCm DSv4.1 Quark-checkpoint fixes).

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [CI] Allowlist-shrink batch 2: wire 9 tests/models/ files into Buildkite, fix 2 stale bugs found
body:
## Summary
- Follow-up to #54867 / #58055 (test-tethering check): shrinks the allowlist by 9 more entries, all of `tests/models/`.
  - Wires 5 CPU-safe files into `models_basic.yaml`'s `basic-models-test-other-cpu` job (`Basic Models Other`): `test_language_model_cache_is_weak.py`, `deepseek_v32/test_sequence_parallel.py`, `test_deepseek_v4_fi_moe_ep.py`, `test_dspark_mla.py`, `transformers/test_layer_registry.py`. None need a GPU (each is `cpu_test`-marked, says so in its own docstring, or has no device/compiled-op use). The job's timeout goes 20 -> 30 minutes for the added files.
  - Wires 3 ROCm-specific files (`test_deepseek_v4_dspark_rocm.py`, `test_deepseek_v4_rocm_wo_a.py`, `test_deepseek_v4_rocm_compressor_gemm_fusion.py`) into the `Basic Models (Other)` AMD MI355 mirror only; they are ROCm-named and not run in the NVIDIA job.
  - Splits `transformers/test_layer_registry.py`: its four unit tests (pure `layers._resolve` logic) stay in that file and run in the CPU job; the one test that serves a model through `vllm_runner` moves to a new `transformers/test_layer_registry_e2e.py`, wired into the `Basic Models (Other)` job (H200, + its AMD MI355 mirror). The two files' docstrings point at each other.
  - Wires `test_deepseek_v41_replay_start.py` into the same `Basic Models (Other)` job and its AMD MI355 mirror. It hardcodes `device="cuda"`, which is the HIP device on ROCm builds (`torch.cuda.is_available()` is true there), and uses only mocks and small tensors, so it runs on both vendors. It passes on a ROCm gfx1201 box. The mirror also now runs upstream's two sibling `deepseek_v41` replay tests (`test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py`, `test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py`), which were NVIDIA-job-only but pass on ROCm too.
- Since these files hadn't run in CI, running them surfaced pre-existing bugs (not introduced by this PR), now fixed:
  - `test_dspark_mla.py::test_dspark_markov_head_is_replicated` constructed a `ParallelLMHead` directly and called `.bias()` without calling `process_weights_after_loading()` (the step real model loading always performs before a layer's `quant_method.apply()` is usable). On any real platform this crashes: `NotImplementedError` on ROCm (no GPU tensor), `AttributeError` on a CPU build (`layer.cpu_linear` never set). Traced through `dispatch_unquantized_gemm()`'s `is_rocm()`/`is_cpu()` branches and reproduced both failures; the fix calls `process_weights_after_loading()` after constructing the head, matching real model loading.
  - `transformers/test_layer_registry.py`'s two caplog tests relied on plain `caplog`, which only sees vLLM's records before any `LLM()` has been constructed in the session: `vllm/logger.py` sets `propagate=False` on the `"vllm"` logger on the first `LLM()`, after which records never reach the root logger. In the target job `test_backend.py` constructs several `LLM()`s first, so this failed for real. They now use the shared `caplog_vllm` fixture from `tests/conftest.py` (which re-enables propagation for the test) instead of plain `caplog`. The per-file `caplog_vllm` copy previously added in `tests/test_zen_cpu_platform_detection.py` (#58055) is removed in favor of the shared one.
- `vllm/triton_utils/importing.py`: reuse `vllm_version_matches_substr("cpu")`, the shared helper `cuda_platform_plugin()`/`rocm_platform_plugin()` already use, instead of an inline `"cpu" in version("vllm")`. Behavior-preserving; included here rather than as a standalone 2-line PR.

## Test plan
- `python tools/pre_commit/check_test_tethering.py --all`: exit 0, all 9 entries tethered, no new gaps.
- All 5 CPU-job test files run with every GPU hidden (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`/`HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES`/`ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES` empty): 57 passed, 0 skipped. Also imported the `amd/`/`nvidia/` model modules they touch with vLLM's no-triton placeholder forced on: clean. (Local env is a ROCm build, so this approximates but is not the real CPU image; the CPU job is the real check.)
- `test_layer_registry.py` (4 unit tests), `test_layer_registry_e2e.py` (1 test) and the three `deepseek_v41` replay files (12 tests) pass on ROCm (gfx1201), i.e. 13 passed for the e2e + replay files.
- `pre-commit` hooks (ruff, ruff-format, typos, check-test-tethering, mypy, spdx, signoff) green on each commit.

AI assistance was used (Claude Code) to investigate the allowlisted tests, trace the bugs to their root cause, and wire the CI jobs. All changes reviewed and tested locally per AGENTS.md before opening.

title: [Bug]: Triton attention: spec-decode verify batches (q_len>1) forced onto the 2D kernel — 7-20x per-call attention slowdown at long context
body:
### Describe the bug

In `vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py` (and the DiffKV variant `triton_unified_attention_diffkv.py`), the 3D/2D launch decision includes `max_seqlen_q > 1` in the 2D-forcing condition:

```python
use_3d = not (
    ...
    or max_seqlen_q > 1
    or num_seqs > seq_threshold_3D
    ...
)
```

Every speculative-decode verify batch (q_len = k+1 > 1) therefore runs the **2D varlen kernel**. For a single-stream verify batch the 2D grid is `(total_num_q_blocks, num_kv_heads)` — e.g. **(1, 4) = 4 CTAs on a 70-SM GPU**, each CTA sequentially walking the entire KV history.

### Kernel-level measurements

MiMo-V2.6-Flash global-attention shape (64 Q heads / 4 KV heads / QK 192 / V 128, block 128, one sequence, CUDA events, 30 iters, CMP 170HX / sm80):

| q_len | stock kernel (ms/call) | 3D spec-verify path (ms/call) | speedup | KV len |
|------:|-----------------------:|------------------------------:|--------:|-------:|
| 1 | 0.27 | 0.28 | 1.0x (no regression) | 67K |
| 2 | **5.08** | **0.26** | **19.6x** | 67K |
| 3 | 3.99 | 0.58 | 6.8x | 67K |
| 4 | 3.98 | 0.56 | 7.1x | 67K |
| 2 | 1.15 | 0.16 | 7.4x | 19K |
| 3 | 1.14 | 0.18 | 6.4x | 19K |
| 4 | 1.14 | 0.18 | 6.4x | 19K |

Notes:
- q=1 is bit-identical between versions — pure decode is unaffected.
- Stock q=2 is *slower* than stock q=4 (5.08 vs 3.98 ms) — an artifact of the 2D tile path that further underlines the pathology.
- With the 3D path, a verify call costs ~2x a decode call (the q query positions share one KV read) — close to the theoretical optimum, versus 15-19x on stock.

### Serving-level effect

4x CMP 170HX (sm80, PP=4), MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL official fp8 checkpoint, MTP k=2, steady-state decode (unique-content prompts, thinking off, warmup dropped):

- 67K context: **16.5 tok/s** (stock) vs **33.7 tok/s** (3D verify) — 2x
- Without speculative decoding the same rig decodes 67K context at 56.1 tok/s, i.e. **the kernel bug turns speculative decoding into a net loss at long context on Triton-backend hardware.**
- The cliff starts around 5K context (42.5 tok/s with spec vs ~63 without).

### Fix

Allow small `q_len` batches onto the 3D split-KV path with `BLOCK_M = q_len x GQA group` so the segment axis supplies the parallelism. A complete, tested, MIT-licensed implementation exists in the MiaAI-Lab DGX-Spark recipe (drop-in on the sm80 backport fork, env-gated via `VLLM_DIFFKV_SPEC_3D_MAX_Q` / `_BLOCK_M` / `_NUM_WARPS` / `_TILE`):

https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash-DGX-Sparks/blob/main/recipe/patches/triton_unified_attention_diffkv.py

Happy to port this to mainline as a PR if the approach sounds acceptable.

### Impact scope

Any user on the Triton attention backend — the default/preferred path for pre-Hopper GPUs and for DiffKV-head models — running speculative decoding with non-trivial context lengths pays this per verify step. We found no prior report of it; the win is largest exactly where the Triton path is the only option.

Environment: vLLM v0.13-lineage backport fork for sm80 (the affected code is present on current main per `triton_unified_attention.py` around the `use_3d` decision), 4x CMP 170HX, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.

title: [RFC]: Release all releasable GPU memory in sleep mode (tracking)
body:
> **Update (tracking).** This issue started as a report about WorkspaceManager memory (original report below, by @penguin-wwy). Investigation showed that the workspace is one of several allocations that sleep mode leaves on the GPU. This issue now tracks all of them.

### Summary

Colocated RL setups call `/sleep` to hand GPU memory back to the trainer. With only `weights` and `kv_cache` under sleep-mode management, a sleeping DeepSeek-V4 engine still holds **14–21 GiB per GPU**. We attributed that memory to its owners on 4× GB300. The PRs below make the releasable parts releasable. With all of them applied, what remains is 5.6–6.2 GiB per GPU on DeepSeek-V4 (3.9–4.7 GiB with the existing `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend` plus #59360). Most of it is driver-side state: CUDA graph executables and the CUDA context.

### Current main (2026-10-04, `bdd31c31d`, with #59156/#59158/#59160 merged)

Memory per GPU while asleep (level 1), MiB, saving vs the first column in parentheses. Every run is bit-exact against the awake run (28 greedy + 28 seeded top-k/top-p probes, 3 cycles). "Open PRs" = #59228 + #59909 + #59360 + #59939 + #59625 + #59934 applied together.

| Model / setup | Main, sleep mode | Main + `--sleep-mode-offload-cudagraph` | Open PRs + `--sleep-mode-offload-cudagraph --enable-nccl-comm-suspend` | ... + #59537 + #59540 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4 + EP4, MTP | 10869 | 8633 (−2236) | **6451 (−4418, 41%)** | **6097 (−4772, 44%)** |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DP4 + EP4, DeepGEMM MoE, fp8 KV, mbt 8192 | 9953 | 8507 (−1446) | **7355 (−2598, 26%)** | **7323 (−2630, 26%)** |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DP8 + EP8 over 2 nodes (this issue's setup) | 9941 | 8495 (−1446) | **7343 (−2598, 26%)** | **7327 (−2614, 26%)** |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8 over 2 nodes, MTP off | 13653 | 6123 (−7530) | **4481 (−9172, 67%)** | **4247 (−9406, 69%)** |
| GLM-5.2-FP8, TP8 over 2 nodes, MTP | 20945 | 11655 (−9290) | **9991 (−10954, 52%)** | **9787 (−11158, 53%)** |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-FP8, TP4 + EP4 | 7617 | 7341 (−276) | **5051 (−2566, 34%)** | **4961 (−2656, 35%)** |

- #59909 frees the same graph memory as the merged backup mode, without the CPU copy (7.4 GiB/GPU less pinned host memory on V4.1).
- #59537 moves graph-capture memory to the KV cache (+0.62 GiB/GPU on V4-Flash TP4, +4.57 GiB/GPU on GLM-5.2).
- Qwen3-235B level 2 + `reload_weights`: bit-exact, same asleep memory as level 1.
- Wake takes 0.2-1.4 s longer with `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend`.
- These numbers are higher than the 09-30 tables below. On V4-Flash TP4 the 2.3 GiB gap breaks down as: +1.3 GiB of CUDA graph executable memory from this cluster's driver (the 09-30 code measures the same on this node; the 09-30 tables are from a different GB300 cluster), +0.5 GiB of MTP runner buffers that the merged #59158 no longer tags (a follow-up puts the model runner back in the `runtime` pool), and +0.5 GiB of FlashInfer TRT-LLM allreduce workspace since #56891, which #59360 releases. Host RSS stays at the asleep level after wake because PyTorch caches the pinned backup buffers.

### What stays on the GPU, and which PR releases it

| Resident while asleep | PR | How | Contents after wake |
|---|---|---|---|
| WorkspaceManager scratch (MoE / attention workspaces, scales with DP × `max_num_batched_tokens`) | #59156 | allocated in a `workspace` cuMem pool | discarded (scratch) |
| State built with the KV cache (block tables, sparse-MLA and indexer metadata) and buffers owned by the model runner (e.g. MTP speculator hidden states) | #59158 (includes the former #59162) | runner construction and KV-init state allocated in a `runtime` cuMem pool | backed up to CPU |
| CUDA graph memory pool (Model Runner V2) | #59160 | graph pools cuMem-backed under a `cudagraph` tag, remapped at the same addresses, no recapture | backed up to CPU |
| FlashInfer MNNVL allreduce workspace | #59360 | with `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend`, detached on suspend and restored at the same address on resume | restored (Lamport flags reset) |
| Documentation of the above and of what cannot be released | #59165 | docs | — |
| Worker refactor: GPU and XPU share workspace and runner init, so the PRs above touch one place | #59200 | refactor | — |
| Freeing a cuMem allocation while asleep double-unmaps (pre-existing; more frequent once graph pools are cuMem-backed) | #59228 | skip unmap for already-released handles | — |

### Savings per PR (memory per GPU while asleep, level 1)

All runs use the same nightly image with and without the PR on 4× GB300 per node. The last two columns were measured on 09-30 at #59156 `21c7a0be4c`, #59158 `0354f3d8a9`, #59160 `57d4f411ee`, #59228 `49b5f1ae43` and #59360 `0de03c0dfc`. The per-PR columns were measured at the previous heads; the latest #59156 change frees the same memory while asleep. With all PRs, the KV cache is the same size as unpatched (e.g. 202.44 GiB on V4-Flash TP4, 192.2 GiB on V4.1). Each cell shows memory while asleep and, in parentheses, the saving against unpatched. Every column except the last runs without `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend`, like its baseline.

| Model / setup | Unpatched | #59156 workspace | #59158 runtime ¹ | #59156 + #59160 graph pool ² | All PRs | All PRs + `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend` + #59360 ³ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4 + EP4, MTP | 15178 | 13857 (−1321) | 9975 (−5203) | 11515 (−3663) | **6313 (−8865, 58%)** | **4649 (−10529, 69%)** |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DP4 + EP4, DeepGEMM MoE, fp8 KV, mbt 8192 | 14528 | 12129 (−2399) | 10227 (−4301) | 10225 (−4303) | **5925 (−8603, 59%)** | **4773 (−9755, 67%)** |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DP8 + EP8 over 2 nodes, DeepGEMM MoE, fp8 KV, mbt 8192 (this issue's setup) | 16790 | 12135 (−4655) | 12489 (−4301) | 10229 (−6561) | **5929 (−10861, 65%)** | **4777 (−12013, 72%)** |
| DeepSeek-V4.1, TP8 over 2 nodes, MTP off | 21037 | 15753 (−5284) | 18583 (−2454) | 8143 (−12894) | **5693 (−15344, 73%)** | **4029 (−17008, 81%)** |
| GLM-5.3, TP8 over 2 nodes, MTP | 9449 | 9449 (0) ⁴ | 8655 (−794) | 8199 (−1250) | **7405 (−2044, 22%)** | **5741 (−3708, 39%)** |

Values are MiB. "All PRs" is #59156 + #59158 + #59160 + #59228. One or two GPUs per run carry an extra 126–128 MiB of driver memory, awake and asleep alike; the table shows the value common to the other GPUs.

1. #59158 now includes the former #59162 (runner buffers such as the MTP speculator hidden states: 512 MiB on V4-Flash, 192 MiB on GLM-5.3, nothing with MTP off). On Model Runner V1 it also moves the block tables rebuilt after CUDA-graph profiling into the `runtime` pool (V4-Flash TP4 on V1: 9187 → 7507 MiB).
2. #59160 is stacked on #59156, so this column includes #59156. It backs the graph pool up to CPU: the `cudagraph` tag is 2.29 GiB/GPU on V4-Flash, 7.43 GiB on V4.1 and 1.22 GiB on GLM-5.3. The first level-1 sleep takes up to ~1.7 s longer; wake time is unchanged.
3. `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend` releases the NCCL buffers; #59360 also releases the FlashInfer MNNVL allreduce workspace (~510 MiB/GPU on the TP configurations; DP does not use it). Each wake takes 0.3–1.0 s longer.
4. GLM-5.3's workspace is small. #59156 still reduces its level-1 host backup by 0.38 GiB per GPU.

**Accuracy.** GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0) is unchanged by every PR across awake, level-1 full wake and level-1 selective wake on all three models:

| | V4-Flash | V4.1 | GLM-5.3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unpatched → all PRs | 0.950–0.951 → 0.947–0.949 | 0.892–0.902 → 0.898–0.906 | 0.911–0.918 → 0.911–0.916 |

Per-PR tables are in each PR. On V4-Flash TP4, outputs after wake are bit-identical to before sleep: 553/553 requests across batch sizes 1–256.

**Known upstream issue, not caused by these PRs:** `reload_weights` after a level-2 sleep produces garbage for DeepSeek-V4 models with tensor parallelism > 1 on unpatched vLLM too. `layerwise.py` fails to load the V4 attention, rotary and n-gram modules. With pure DP (DP4 / DP8, TP1 per engine) level 2 + reload works; for example, GSM8K on DP8 is 0.965.

### Validation beyond memory

All of these are on 4× GB300 per node, with the same nightly image with and without the PRs. Every issue found also occurs on unpatched vLLM.

- **Bit-exactness:**
  - DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4: 553 deterministic requests (batch sizes 1–256) are identical to the awake run after every level-1 full wake and selective wake (weights-first and kv_cache-first).
  - Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B NVFP4, Qwen3-VL-8B (images), Kimi-Linear-48B (MLA + KDA) and Qwen3-235B-A22B FP8: also identical after level 2 + `reload_weights`.
- **Lifecycle:**
  - V4-Flash TP4, 300 consecutive cycles (alternating full and selective wake), all PRs with and without `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend` + #59360: every cycle bit-exact (34,140/34,140 requests), memory after wake equal to before sleep on every GPU (0 MiB), and a device-memory slope of 0.000 MiB/cycle.
  - Host RSS: about +5 MB/cycle of warm-up over the first ~50 cycles in every launch, patched or not. After that, slopes over 300 cycles are −1.8 to +3.6 MB/cycle patched (4 launches) and −0.5 to +0.6 unpatched (3 launches). The sign changes between launches of the same configuration, and one unpatched launch also rises steadily. All of the growth is process heap; the shared-memory backup is byte-for-byte constant.
  - Host RAM cost: the level-1 backup now also covers the `runtime`, `workspace` and `cudagraph` pools, about 8.1 GiB more host memory per GPU on V4-Flash TP4 (33 GiB per 4-GPU node). It is constant from the first sleep on, but host RAM has to be sized for it.
  - V4-Flash DP4, 100 cycles with level 2 + `reload_weights` every 10th: the first reload adds 2548 MiB/GPU outside the cuMem pools, identically on unpatched vLLM; flat afterwards.
  - Sleep before the first request.
  - Requests sent while asleep, or after a weights-only wake, are queued and complete after the full wake.
  - A double sleep or double wake is a no-op.
  - Level 1 followed by level 2 without a wake is ignored.
  - 256 concurrent requests right after wake: no errors, no NaN.
- **Configurations:**
  - Model Runner V1; `--enforce-eager`; chunked prefill; `--max-num-seqs 8`; MTP on and off.
  - PP2 × TP2, TP2 × DP2, DP4, DP8 over 2 nodes.
  - A KV connector (the `runtime` pool is skipped, as intended).
  - Custom allreduce forced (Qwen3-8B TP4) with #59160.
- **RL-style soak:** 100 iterations each on Qwen3-235B-A22B FP8 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash, all PRs applied.
  - Each iteration runs a rollout of 64–256 concurrent requests, then a level-1 sleep. On about a third to a half of the iterations, another process fills ~270 GiB/GPU of the freed VRAM during the sleep.
  - Wakes alternate full and selective; every 25th iteration on Qwen3-235B is level 2 + `reload_weights`.
  - Probes stay bit-exact, with no drift in GPU memory, host RSS or latency. 16,345/16,345 requests succeeded.
- **Serving performance while awake:** unchanged (V4-Flash TP4, `vllm bench serve`, concurrency 1–256).
  - Throughput and TTFT/TPOT match unpatched within noise, on a fresh server and after sleep/wake.
  - Throughput varies by up to ~45% between launches of the same code, because the FlashInfer MoE autotuner picks different tactics on each launch. Comparisons need several launches per arm.
- **Sleep/wake latency:**
  - Wake is unchanged (V4-Flash TP4 and V4.1 ~0.95 s, GLM-5.3 ~1.45 s).
  - The first level-1 sleep can take up to ~1.7 s longer on V4.1, because #59160 backs up the 7.4 GiB/GPU graph pool; later sleeps take ~1.2–1.4 s.
  - `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend` with #59360 adds 0.3–1.0 s per wake.
- **Review:** three rounds of adversarial review (two external code-review models plus a manual pass) across all PRs. Confirmed findings were fixed: the #59156 pool-lifetime rework, the #59158 V1 block-table placement, the #59360 restore-retry flag, and the #59228 test.
- **AMD (ROCm):** see the MI355X results below.

### What remains after all PRs

Memory per GPU while asleep (level 1), attributed with a driver-API hook plus torch allocator history. The unexplained remainder is ≤ 17 MiB in every configuration. Local memory is 480 MiB everywhere: NCCL kernels raise the per-thread stack to 1616 B, × 152 SMs × 2048 threads. TP8 adds a 384 MiB NVLS buffer on its first NCCL all-reduce, which is why V4.1 and GLM show 1644 MiB of NCCL.

| Item (MiB) | V4-Flash TP4 | V4-Flash DP4 | V4-Flash DP8 (2 nodes) | V4.1 TP8 (2 nodes) | GLM-5.3 TP8 (2 nodes) | Releasable? |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **Total asleep** | **6311** | **5923** | **5927** | **5693** | **7406** | |
| CUDA graph executables + capture-charged driver memory | 2536 | 2668 | 2668 | 1762 | 3102 | No ¹ |
| NCCL cuMem buffers | 1260 | 1260 | 1260 | 1644 | 1644 | Yes, `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend` ² |
| FlashInfer MNNVL allreduce workspace | 512 | — | — | 512 | 512 | Yes, #59360 with `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend` |
| torch SymmetricMemory | 132 | — | — | 164 | 164 | Needs suspend/resume support in torch SymmetricMemory |
| CUDA context + local memory + kernel modules | 1166 | 1162 | 1162 | 1160 | 1162 | No |
| cuBLAS, custom allreduce | ~96 | ~68 | ~68 | ~92 | ~88 | Partly, #59537 ³ |
| torch tensors outside any tag (router gate, sampler, GEMM outputs, …) | 281 | 281 | 281 | 202 | 206 | Partly, #59540 and #59537 ³ |
| FlashInfer sparse-MLA workspace (lazily allocated, untagged) | — | — | — | — | 394 | Yes, #59535 |
| Allocator fragmentation | 321 | ~480 | 483 | 151 | 122 | Mostly, once the untagged tensors above move to a tag |

1. **Graph executables:**
   - Destroying all graphs while asleep returns 0 MiB: the driver keeps graph-exec memory. Releasing it needs recapture on wake or a CUDA checkpoint (#56373).
   - The size scales with graph count. Breakable PIECEWISE capture creates about one graph per layer per batch size: GLM-5.3 (78 layers) has 6557 PIECEWISE graphs, against about 3.7–3.8k on V4 (40–43 layers).
2. **NCCL buffers:** with the existing flag plus #59360, all PRs reach:
   - **4029** MiB on V4.1 (−81% vs unpatched);
   - **4649** MiB on V4-Flash TP4 (−69%);
   - **4773** MiB on DP4 (−67%);
   - **4777** MiB on DP8 (−72%);
   - **5741** MiB on GLM-5.3 (−39%).

   Each wake takes 0.3–1.0 s longer. GSM8K was checked unchanged with the flag before #59360; with #59360, outputs after wake are bit-identical on V4-Flash TP4 (553/553).
3. **Untagged tensors:** most of them are scratch that belongs in `WorkspaceManager`, so they are released by #59156 once moved. Several "GEMM output" items are PyTorch's 32 MiB cuBLAS workspace, one per stream, kept for the process lifetime.
   - #59535 moves the FlashInfer MLA decode workspaces into `WorkspaceManager`: −394 MiB/GPU asleep on GLM-5.3, bit-exact after wake.
   - #59540 takes the top-k/top-p sampler scratch from `WorkspaceManager`: about −75 MiB/GPU on V4-Flash.
   - #59537 reuses one stream for every `graph_capture()` call instead of creating one per call: about −64 MiB/GPU on V4-Flash, bit-exact over 22 cycles.
   - Priming the remaining cuBLAS workspaces inside the `workspace` pool was prototyped. Discard and remap stay bit-exact, but destroying the profiling graphs frees the capture stream's workspace, so the real capture allocates a new untagged one. Not proposed yet.

### AMD MI355X (ROCm)

vLLM ROCm nightly image (`e975732152`, torch 2.12, RCCL 2.30.4) with each PR's diff applied, level-1 sleep. Memory per GPU while asleep, MiB (saving vs unpatched):

| Model / setup | Unpatched | #59156 | #59156 + #59158 | #59156 + #59160 (ROCm patch ¹) | All three | Graph memory ² |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP1 | 5677 | −930 | −1034 | −1094 | −1198 | 948 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 | 7946 | −770 | −880 | −908 | −999 | 1044 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite DP2 | 9430 | −1536 | −1628 | −1647 | — | 1543 |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 | 12018 | −888 | −1031 | −1030 (V2 runner forced) | — | 1743 |

- **#59156 and #59158** work on ROCm unchanged. Outputs are bit-identical after full and selective wake (TP2, DP2 within its pre-sleep variation, V4-Flash). Nested pools behave as on CUDA: the innermost pool wins.
- **#59160 is CUDA-only as posted.** Enabling it on ROCm also needs a C++ change: a blocking `hipMemset` in `cumem_allocator.cpp` breaks graph capture, and making it `hipMemsetAsync` on a non-blocking stream fixes it. Custom allreduce needs the same unregistered capture path as on CUDA. With that change it stays bit-exact over 10 cycles plus a level-2 reload, but frees only 72–244 MiB, because most graph memory is held by the HIP runtime outside torch pools. Unlike CUDA, ROCm returns that memory when graphs are destroyed, so destroying graphs on sleep and recapturing on wake would recover ~1–1.5 GiB/GPU at 9–50 s per wake. Both are possible follow-ups.
- **#59360 is a no-op on ROCm** (verified): FlashInfer allreduce is unavailable, so no workspace exists. Memory, bit-exactness and wake latency match unpatched.
- **`--enable-nccl-comm-suspend` frees ~0 MiB on ROCm by default:** RCCL does not allocate its buffers with cuMem. With `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1`, suspend frees 505 MiB but cuMem itself adds 389 MiB, a net saving of 116 MiB.
- **Wake latency:** 0.37–0.9 s; the #59160 ROCm patch adds 0.2–0.3 s.
- **50-cycle leak test** (DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP1 / TP2 / DP2, V4-Flash TP4; unpatched, #59156, #59156 + #59158): device-memory slope 0.00 MiB/cycle and every cycle bit-exact (sequential 8-prompt check, 50/50) in every arm. Host RSS does not grow over level-1 cycles; it steps up only at level-2 `reload_weights` cycles, unpatched too. After wake, in-process memory (`hipMemGetInfo`, torch, every cuMem tag) equals the value before sleep; `rocm-smi` steps once at the first wake and then stays flat, unpatched too. #59156 + #59158 + #59523 on V4-Flash TP4 (V2 runner): 30/30 cycles bit-exact, flat at 10779 MiB.
- **GSM8K before sleep and after wake** (1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0): every post-wake score stays within the server's own two awake rounds, give or take one standard error.

  | V4-Flash TP4 | Awake R1 / R2 | Full wake | Selective wake | +10 cycles |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Unpatched | 0.949 / 0.945 | 0.948 | 0.944 | 0.945 |
  | #59156 + #59158 | 0.947 / 0.948 | 0.949 | 0.948 | 0.947 |
  | V2 runner, unpatched | 0.947 / 0.949 | 0.951 | 0.948 | 0.948 |
  | V2 runner, all three + #59523 | 0.943 / 0.945 | 0.948 | 0.948 | 0.945 |

  DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 gives the same picture at 0.34–0.36, with about 250 of 1319 answers changing between two awake rounds even without sleep.
- **Exact logprob comparison is not reproducible on this ROCm image**, even awake against awake on unpatched vLLM (about 25% of requests identical on DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2, about 90% on V4-Flash), so bit-exactness on ROCm rests on the sequential check above.
- **Open on #59523:** one DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 startup with its cached-stream build hung in the kernel during KV-cache allocation (2 clean startups plus the unit test otherwise). The cause is not established; the earlier per-stream-per-call variant had no hang and is the one used for the GSM8K run.

1. #59523, stacked on #59160.
2. Asleep memory with CUDA graphs minus `--enforce-eager`, unpatched.

### Notes and related work
- **#59160 compatibility:**
  - Custom allreduce IPC-registers graph buffers, which fails on cuMem memory. #59160 makes it copy into its pre-registered buffer while capturing, which is the same approach as sgl-project/sglang#7873.
  - NCCL graph registration pins cuMem pages and goes stale after remap (see fzyzcjy/torch_memory_saver#88), so `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=0` is required in this mode. Serving cost is within ±5% noise.
- **Related work:**
  - #47700 captures graphs into the `weights` pool.
  - #56373 checkpoints the whole CUDA process on one GPU, which also frees graph executables.

### Tracking

Merged: #59200, #59156, #59158, #59160. Remaining memory PRs are independent unless noted.

- [x] #59200 Share workspace and model runner init between GPU and XPU workers (merged)
- [x] #59156 Release WorkspaceManager scratch on sleep (merged)
- [x] #59158 Offload runtime state on sleep (merged)
- [x] #59160 Offload V2 CUDA graph pools in sleep mode, opt-in `sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph` (merged)
- [ ] #59228 Don't unmap cuMem allocations freed while asleep
- [ ] #59909 Release the CUDA graph pool on sleep instead of backing it up (follow-up to #59160: no CPU copy; refuses if a tensor is live in the pool)
- [ ] #59523 ROCm support for the graph pool mode (`hipMemsetAsync` in the cuMem allocator)
- [ ] #59360 Release the FlashInfer MNNVL allreduce workspace with `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend`
- [ ] #59939 Release DeepEP all2all buffers with `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend` when CUDA graphs are off (~1 GiB/GPU high-throughput, ~4.4-6 GiB/GPU low-latency on V4-Flash)
- [ ] #59535 Move FlashInfer MLA decode workspaces into `WorkspaceManager`
- [ ] #59537 Reuse one stream for every `graph_capture()` call
- [ ] #59540 Take the top-k/top-p sampler scratch from `WorkspaceManager`
- [ ] #59847 Register KV caches with the connector outside the runtime pool (fixes a #59158 regression with LMCache)
- [ ] #59165 Docs: what stays on the GPU in sleep mode

KV connectors (P/D) across sleep: sleep remaps the KV cache to new physical pages at the same addresses, so a connector that registered it with a NIC or another process keeps stale registrations.

- [ ] #59625 Connector API (`supports_sleep_mode`, `release_kv_caches`/`restore_kv_caches`), startup refusal for connectors that cannot follow the remap (NIXL, MoRIIO, non-RDMA Mooncake, MooncakeStore), and MooncakeConnector support over RDMA. Self-contained; supersedes #59624.
- [ ] #59934 MooncakeStoreConnector support (stacked on #59625)
- [ ] #59635 NIXL pull connector support (stacked on #59625; re-registers and peers re-handshake on a registration epoch, no lease)
- [ ] #59993 `pause(mode="wait")` drains requests whose async KV load is in flight (pre-existing 500 with any async-load connector)
- [ ] #59994 Offload model runner construction buffers (e.g. MTP hidden states, 512 MiB/GPU on V4-Flash); follow-up to #59158
- [x] ~~#59162~~ folded into #59158

---

<details>
<summary>Original report (by @penguin-wwy)</summary>

### Summary
In colocated RL training setups, when the training process is running, a sleep request can be used to free the GPU memory held by the vLLM process. However, I found that the memory allocated by WorkspaceManager is not covered by sleep mode.

### Root cause analysis
In `EngineCore._initialize_kv_caches`, `determine_available_memory` is called first to compute the available memory before allocating the KV cache blocks. Following the call stack, this triggers a dummy run that goes through the full inference path:

```
gpu_worker.py: determine_available_memory
                     ↓
gpu_model_runner.py: _dummy_run
                     ↓
            attention / moe
                     ↓
current_workspace_manager().get_simultaneous(...)
                     ↓
self._ensure_workspace_size(total_bytes)
                     ↓
self._current_workspaces[workspace_id] = torch.empty(
    (required_bytes,), dtype=torch.uint8, device=self._device
)
```
This path triggers the workspace manager's allocation logic, but the allocation is not covered by either `self._maybe_get_memory_pool_context(tag="weights")` or `self._maybe_get_memory_pool_context(tag="kv_cache")`. As a result, sleep mode cannot release this chunk of memory.

### Reproduction / observed impact
For example, with the following launch command:
```
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4
```
The leftover MoE workspace size is proportional to dp_size × max_num_batched_tokens, which amounts to roughly 6.1 GiB in this configuration.

### Question / proposal
Could this workspace memory also be brought under the management of sleep mode, so that it can be released together with weights and KV cache when the engine sleeps?

</details>

title: [KV Cache] Add layer-sharded MLA cache with NCCL broadcast (KVPP)
body:
## Summary

Add opt-in `--enable-kvpp` for replicated MLA KV caches on NVIDIA GPUs. Each layer bundle has one persistent owner within a **PCP × TP** replica group; other ranks materialize it in two reusable scratch slots. NCCL broadcast prefetches the next bundle before the current attention, with CUDA events protecting cache writes and buffer reuse.

The intended workload is multi-prefix serving where limited KV memory causes cache eviction. Layer ownership increases cache capacity while preserving ordinary attention tensor views.

## Integration and usage

- Reuse the existing logical block, prefix-cache, scheduler, and KV config construction flows. Account for owner storage and scratch in capacity calculation, then apply physical placement after the common block count is finalized.
- Share one storage plan between allocation, broadcast, and owner-only `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` registration.
- Manage the KVPP communicator in `parallel_state`, scoped to each DP replica and PP stage. Reuse PCP's existing KV gathering with DCP=1.

Requires Model Runner V2 and PCP × TP ≥ 2. Use `--enforce-eager`, or:

```text
--enable-kvpp -cc.mode=3 -cc.cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE -cc.use_inductor_graph_partition=false
```

Keep the default attention/KV-update splitting ops. FULL graphs and GPU MRV1 are unsupported. PCP MoE also requires `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0`. See [design and compatibility limits](https://github.com/pisceskkk/vllm/blob/codex/kvpp-attn-prefetch-bcast/docs/design/kv_cache_layer_sharding.md) for other combinations.

## Accuracy and correctness

**DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, 4×H100, TP2 × PCP2, MRV2, compiled PIECEWISE:**

| Check | Replicated baseline | KVPP |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K accuracy, 200 questions / 5-shot | 64.0% | 63.0% |
| Invalid answers | 0 | 0 |
| Mixed short/long and repeated-prefix smoke | Reference | 8/8 token-for-token matches |

Both GSM8K results pass the existing 0.65 ± 0.08 threshold (max output 256, concurrency 8). Evaluation used `08cccd2edf` with the eager-only guard removed. Commit **`74a2ceb3a9`** passed a fresh four-GPU startup/capture, the same eight-request comparison, and all **9 configuration tests**. Observers confirmed graph replay with KVPP prefetch executing outside capture.

Earlier distributed tests cover owner/scratch lifetimes, communicator isolation, PP-stage ownership, and teardown/reinitialization. The `DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat-KVPP.yaml` e2e guard uses PIECEWISE. Ruff check/format and `git diff --check` passed.

## Best observed TP + KVPP prefix-pooling result

**DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, 4×RTX 5090, TP4, MRV2 eager, attention-before broadcast.** Both placements use a 512 MiB KV budget per rank. Four prefix families each have 4,096 shared tokens plus a 1,024-token unique suffix; 256 requests per round, concurrency 4, one output token. Two measured rounds exclude warmup.

| Metric | Replicated baseline | KVPP |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Logical KV capacity (tokens) | 17,248 | 51,776 |
| Prefix-cache hit rate, rounds 1 / 2 | 37.8% / 38.3% | 80.0% / 80.0% |
| Input tokens/s, rounds 1 / 2 | 67,988 / 68,586 | 124,651 / 124,638 |
| Mean input tokens/s | 68,287 | **124,645 (+82.5%)** |

This is GPU-resident prefix pooling without CPU offload. Throughput counts cached input tokens; the gain combines greater cache residency and broadcast scheduling. Both sides disabled FlashInfer autotune and used `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1`; configured max model length was 8,192 for baseline and 16,384 for KVPP, with identical 5,120-token requests.

These measurements describe the earlier eager implementation and this one-token-output workload. Current-revision throughput and long-output decode gains remain unmeasured. Gains are device/workload dependent: attention-before broadcast regressed in the H100 cropped-DSv3.2 CPU-offload pool experiment.

<details>
<summary>Validation commands and performance provenance</summary>

Rebased onto upstream/main at `94d14629247955c69d40bdf2a9d7e3bd45954452`. Patch equivalence (`git range-diff`), syntax parsing, Ruff check/format across 32 changed Python files, and `git diff --check` passed. GPU results above refer to the recorded pre-rebase revisions.

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_kvpp_runtime.py -k placement_requires_replay_time_cache_hooks -v
.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port <server-port> --num-questions 200 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 --max-concurrency 8
```

The accuracy services used prefix caching, `FLASH_ATTN_MLA`, max model length 4096, max batch tokens 512, max sequences 8, and 512 MiB KV per rank. The full distributed suite and helper tests were not rerun on `74a2ceb3a9`.

The performance snapshot was based on `11852548518b13c9a00a4e73dadd19d44e221e2b`, with production-source manifest SHA256 `ab72d58fece5b774caa8459427b8d1e5545635cdce0e3fc2b5aab981b89442d1`.

</details>

## Related work

Implements the motivation in #58329, with attribution to Z.ai LayerSplit and [vllm-ascend KVPP PR #16094](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/16094) by @recky-c. The Ascend implementation informed layer-bundle broadcast and the multi-prefix pooling experiments. Related PR #58428 provides a planning/placement prototype; this draft adds the CUDA runtime, lifetime ordering, and framework integration. PR #49741 explores CUDA VMM peer mappings for sparse attention.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for implementation, testing, and PR preparation.

title: [EPLB] Gate expert balancing during weight reload
body:
## Summary
- Add an EPLB reload gate around direct `collective_rpc("reload_weights")` worker calls.
- Gate NCCL/IPC weight-transfer reload lifecycle with exception-safe start/update/finish handling.
- Add EPLB state synchronization and DeepSeek V4.1 dynamic expert mapping support.
- Add focused EPLB and worker reload lifecycle tests plus day0 trace evidence scripts.

## Why this is not a duplicate
This change is scoped to generic reload + EPLB coordination and direct collective-RPC reload gating. It does not add the traced FP8 policy work covered by the existing draft reload PR #57561.

## Tests
- `git diff --check`
- Python `compileall` on all changed Python files
- Focused pytest was attempted but could not start because the shared environment lacks `tblib`; installing it was blocked by uv interpreter permissions.
- Pre-commit was attempted; the environment could not launch uv/pre-commit due interpreter permission errors. The changed script lint issues reported by the first hook run were fixed.

## AI assistance
AI assistance was used. The human submitter must review every changed line and verify the behavior end-to-end before merging.
