title: [Bug]: Kimi-K3 MXFP4: flashinfer_trtllm selects unsupported BF16/SiTU MoE backend
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment captured from the failing job logs</summary>

```text
- Base image: vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-7f1a5398e9610d96c473931a26c0e12bbe0d0423 (vLLM 0.30.1rc1.dev48+g7f1a5398e)
- vLLM builds tested: the image as shipped (7f1a5398e), plus per-commit wheels from https://wheels.vllm.ai/<sha>/cu130 installed on that image with --no-deps:
  - 0.26.1rc1.dev135+gaeeb36b1f
  - 0.30.1rc1.dev52+g44bf011f4
- Also observed on a container built from vLLM 0.29.1rc1.dev513+g0961bbae2 with FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1 (TP=16, DP=1 case below)
- FlashInfer: flashinfer-python / flashinfer-cubin / flashinfer-jit-cache (+cu130), versions 0.6.18.post1 and 0.7.0 (0.6.15.post1 also tried, see below)
- torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, NVIDIA driver 580.178.04, apache-tvm-ffi 0.1.11, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1, Python 3.12
- Hardware: 4 x GB200 NVL nodes (aarch64), 4 GPUs each (16 GPUs)
- Model: moonshotai/Kimi-K3 (revision f831ab66814297da540d832a5235f8e904f29d06); vLLM reports quantization=mxfp4, dtype=bfloat16
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug


Kimi-K3 (MXFP4 MoE weights, SITU activation) served with `--moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm` fails during engine start-up (`profile_run`). vLLM logs `Using 'FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16' Mxfp4 MoE backend.`, and then every worker fails inside FlashInfer:

```
RuntimeError: Error in function 'TrtllmGenBatchedGemmRunner' at .../flashinfer/data/csrc/trtllm_batched_gemm_runner.cu:239: No kernel found for the given options: mDtypeA: MxE2m1, mDtypeB: Bfloat16, mDtypeC: Bfloat16, mUseDeepSeekFp8: 0, mActType: 2, mEltwiseActType: 0, mTransposeMmaOutput: 1, mRouteAct: 1, mFusedAct: 1, mIsStaticBatch: 0, mTileSize: 32, mBiasType: 0, mFusedBiasShuffleMode: 0, mBiasDtype: Bfloat16, mUsePerTokenScaling: 0, mPerTokenSfDtype: Void, mUsePerChannelScaling: 0
```

`mActType: 2` is `ActType::SiTuGlu` (`include/flashinfer/trtllm/batched_gemm/KernelRunner.h`: `SwiGlu = 0, GeGlu = 1, SiTuGlu = 2, None = 3`). The API server never becomes ready.

Both TRTLLM MXFP4 expert implementations are affected:

- **Data parallel > 1 / expert parallel** uses `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular` → `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`.
- **Tensor parallel only (TP=16, DP=1)** uses `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsMonolithic` → `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe`.

**Reproduction 1: DP=4 / EP, modular path.** A Ray cluster spans 4 GB200 nodes; the command runs on the head node:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ENABLE_K3_LATENT_MOE_TAIL_FUSION=1
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --language-model-only \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 4 --data-parallel-size-local 1 --data-parallel-backend ray \
  --distributed-executor-backend ray --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --max-model-len 3840 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --load-format safetensors
```

Traceback (abridged; vLLM 44bf011f4 + FlashInfer 0.7.0; identical on every rank):

```
vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:612 determine_available_memory
 -> vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:949 profile_run -> :836 _dummy_run -> :1992 execute_model
 -> vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py (2110, 1626, 1338, 1096, 841)
 -> vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/latent_moe_runner.py:314 forward
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py:734 / 165 / 921 / 633
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts.py:1248 forward_modular
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py:866 apply
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:1708 / 1481 / 1321
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/trtllm_mxfp4_moe.py:436 apply -> :361 _invoke_kernel
 -> flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py:6673 trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe -> :3633 trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe_op -> :3559 run_selected_tactic
RuntimeError: ... No kernel found ... mDtypeA: MxE2m1, mDtypeB: Bfloat16 ... mActType: 2 ... mTileSize: 32 ...
```

**Reproduction 2: TP=16, DP=1, monolithic path.** Same 4-node GB200 Ray cluster, vLLM 0961bbae2 + FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1. The relevant flags are:

```bash
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --language-model-only \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --distributed-executor-backend ray \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":2}'
```

vLLM logs `Using 'FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16' Mxfp4 MoE backend.` and `Using TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsMonolithic`, then fails with the same error. Traceback (abridged):

```
-> vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/latent_moe_runner.py:311 forward -> :356 _fused_forward
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py:165 / 917 / 619
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts.py:1282 forward_monolithic
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py:889 apply_monolithic
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:1678 apply_monolithic -> :1550 apply
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/trtllm_mxfp4_moe.py:243 apply
 -> flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py:6217 trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe -> :3885 trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe_op -> :3813 run_selected_tactic
RuntimeError: Error in function 'TrtllmGenBatchedGemmRunner' at .../trtllm_batched_gemm_runner.cu:242: No kernel found ... mDtypeA: MxE2m1, mDtypeB: Bfloat16, mDtypeC: Bfloat16 ... mActType: 2 ...
```

**Expected.** vLLM either selects a backend variant that has SITU kernels (MXFP4 × MXFP8), or rejects the configuration with a clear error at backend-selection time.

**Actual.** A runtime kernel-lookup failure occurs in `profile_run`.

**Results (reproduction 1).** Base image, hardware, model and flags are the same in every row; only the vLLM wheel and the FlashInfer version change.

| vLLM | FlashInfer | Selected MoE backend | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| aeeb36b1f (#50000, Kimi-K3 support) | 0.6.15.post1 | none | `ValueError: Mxfp4 MoE backend 'FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8' does not support the deployment configuration since kernel does not support MoEActivation.SITU activation.` (this FlashInfer has no `ActivationType.Situ`) |
| aeeb36b1f | 0.6.18.post1 | FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16 | `No kernel found` (above) |
| 7f1a5398e (nightly image as shipped) | 0.6.18.post1 | (same error signature) | `No kernel found` |
| 44bf011f4 | 0.7.0 | FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16 | `No kernel found` |

This configuration has not worked on any public vLLM and FlashInfer combination we tried. On an earlier nightly (0961bbae2, FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1) with the DP=4 parallelism but `--moe-backend` left on auto, vLLM selected `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8` and got past MoE profiling. That run later failed because the requested 1M context exceeded the available KV-cache memory, so it is evidence that the MXFP8 SiTU path gets past profiling, not an end-to-end serving pass.

### Root cause and source recheck (2026-09-28)

The latest GPU reproduction above is **vLLM `44bf011f4` with FlashInfer `0.7.0`**. The September 28 update is a source and issue/PR review; the newer revisions below were not rerun on GPUs.

The relevant capability mismatch remains in vLLM `cd63bf9996d3fdbe24a3228f970b84310600612f`:

- [`TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsBase`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/cd63bf9996d3fdbe24a3228f970b84310600612f/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/trtllm_mxfp4_moe.py#L129-L147) accepts both `(kMxfp4Static, None)` and `(kMxfp4Static, kMxfp8Dynamic)`. For `MoEActivation.SITU`, `_supports_activation()` independently returns `has_flashinfer_situ_activation()`. This tests the presence of the FlashInfer activation enum rather than support for the specific weight/activation-format pair, so the BF16 variant also claims SiTU support.
- [The MXFP4 backend mapping](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/cd63bf9996d3fdbe24a3228f970b84310600612f/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py#L307-L311) still tries `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16` before `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8` for `--moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm`.
- Both `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsMonolithic` (`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe`) and `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular` (`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`) inherit the same capability checks. The tested TP16/DP1 and DP4/EP configurations therefore pass `ActivationType.Situ` with BF16 hidden states into FlashInfer.

FlashInfer's current source corroborates the unsupported combination:

- [FlashInfer #4180](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4180), merged July 29, added TRTLLM-Gen SiTU for **MXFP4 × MXFP8** and **NVFP4 × NVFP4**.
- At FlashInfer `85bfa5e4b599a9c616f073e2c06d3b9a1cdadee4`, the [TRT-LLM FP4 activation matrix](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/85bfa5e4b599a9c616f073e2c06d3b9a1cdadee4/docs/design_docs/flashinfer_moe_api.md#L823-L825) lists **only SwiGLU for MXFP4 × BF16**, while MXFP4 × MXFP8 includes SiTU.
- The [runner capability declaration](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/85bfa5e4b599a9c616f073e2c06d3b9a1cdadee4/flashinfer/fused_moe/runners.py#L5253-L5265) expresses that same restriction per quantization pair. vLLM's direct calls above do not use this unified-runner capability validation.

This supports retaining the report as a vLLM backend-selection/capability-validation bug. The observed `mTileSize: 32` is part of the failure signature; the evidence does not establish that merely choosing another tile makes BF16/SiTU supported.

### Suggested fix

1. **vLLM:** validate the activation type and quantization pair together for both TRTLLM MXFP4 expert implementations. Reject SiTU with `activation_key=None` while that combination is unsupported, allowing selection to continue to `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8` when supported on the target device, or fail early with a clear configuration error.
2. **FlashInfer:** alternatively or additionally, add TRTLLM-Gen MXFP4 × BF16 SiTuGlu kernels. vLLM could also consume a capability check covering the quantization pair, activation and target device instead of relying only on the enum's presence.

A possible user-side workaround on the tested GB200 platform is `--moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm_afp8`, which maps only to `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`. **This explicit flag was not tested in either exact reproduction configuration**, and the auto-selection result above is not an end-to-end validation.

The smallest model-level configuration tested here used 16 GB200 GPUs; the repro was not reduced further. A direct `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` or `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe` call with MXFP4 weights, BF16 hidden states and `ActivationType.Situ` is a candidate single-Blackwell-GPU reproducer, but has not been run.

### Related upstream work, checked 2026-09-28

A renewed search of vLLM and FlashInfer issues and PRs found no matching report or fix for this exact TRTLLM MXFP4 × BF16/SiTU kernel-lookup failure. Related activity includes:

| Reference | Status as of 2026-09-28 | Relation to this report |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [vLLM #58635](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58635) | Merged September 25 | Adds deferred finalization to modular TRTLLM-Gen experts. The SiTU/quantization capability mismatch remains in current source. |
| [FlashInfer #5430](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5430) | Merged September 27 | Adds a separate CuTe DSL W4A8 MXFP4/SiTU routed-MoE backend for SM100/SM103. It does not add the missing TRTLLM MXFP4 × BF16 support. |
| [FlashInfer #5639](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5639) | Open; created September 28 | Performance follow-up to #5430 for the same CuTe DSL W4A8 backend. |
| [FlashInfer #5518](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5518) | Open | Another CuTe DSL W4A8 MXFP4/SiTU implementation for B300, not the failing TRTLLM BF16 path. |
| [vLLM #58827](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58827) | Closed without merge | Targets unquantized BF16 Kimi-K3 dense/shared MLP projections, not the MXFP4 routed experts. |

Other references considered in the original investigation:

- [vLLM #50001](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50001): Kimi-K3 tracking.
- [vLLM #54723](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54723): FP8 DP/EP hang.
- [vLLM #52240](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52240): MXFP4 W13 layout.
- [vLLM #56770](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56770): compressed-tensors W4A16.
- [vLLM #52308](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52308): NVFP4 ReLU².
- [FlashInfer #5053](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5053): NVFP4 SiTU output scale factors.
- [FlashInfer #5337](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5337): MXFP8/MXFP4 SiTU routed-MoE performance.
- [FlashInfer #5296](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5296): blockwise FP8 SiTU.
- [FlashInfer #5462](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5462): SM107 CuTe DSL activation support.
- [FlashInfer #5183](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5183) and [#5455](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5455): NVFP4 SiTU paths.

title: [Bug]: FlashInfer MLA with DCP>1 crashes in kernel warmup on ragged spec/non-spec decode batch (`causal_seqlens_kv_global must have shape (9,), got (2,)`)
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Summarized from the collect_env output captured in the reproducing container: - Image: vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-7f1a5398e9610d96c473931a26c0e12bbe0d0423 (public image, unmodified) - vLLM: 0.30.1rc1.dev48+g7f1a5398e (commit 7f1a5398e9610d96c473931a26c0e12bbe0d0423) - flashinfer-python: 0.6.18.post1 - torch: 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1, nvidia-nccl-cu13 2.30.7 - CUDA runtime 13.0, NVIDIA driver 580.173.10 - Python 3.12.3, aarch64 (Linux 6.17) - GPUs: NVIDIA GB300 (SM103), 4 GPUs per node, 2 nodes (TP=8, DCP=8), Ray distributed executor The failing code paths (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py mixed spec/non-spec decode step, FlashInferMLAImpl.forward_mqa DCP branch) are unchanged on main at 09fe178dba08e6de4448ade1e37d14ae1dab3acf (2026-09-24). ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug With FlashInfer MLA plus decode context parallelism (DCP > 1) and DSpark speculative decoding, the engine dies during `warmup_kernels` (V2 model runner): ``` ValueError: causal_seqlens_kv_global must have shape (9,), got (2,) ``` **Expected behavior:** The engine finishes `warmup_kernels` and serves requests with FlashInfer MLA + DCP=8 + DSpark spec decode. The mixed spec/non-spec decode batch that warmup builds (and that real steps can produce when some requests get no draft tokens) is either handled by the DCP decode path or split into shapes the backend supports. **Actual behavior:** Every DCP rank (TP0_DCP0 … TP7_DCP7) raises `ValueError: causal_seqlens_kv_global must have shape (9,), got (2,)` in the warmup mixed spec/non-spec decode step. EngineCore fails to start with `RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'causal_seqlens_kv_global must have shape (9,), got (2,)'`, and the server never becomes ready. Model load (~194 GiB per rank), KV-cache allocation and CUDA graph capture all complete first. **Reproduction** (plain `vllm serve`, no KV connector or disaggregation), 2 nodes × 4 GB300, Ray cluster across both nodes: ```bash export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 export VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A=1 export VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_Q_GATHER=1 export VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_KV_GATHER=1 export VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=1 export VLLM_KIMI_K3_SHARD_SP_SHARED_EXPERT=0 export VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=0 export VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS export NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1 vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --revision f831ab66814297da540d832a5235f8e904f29d06 \ --trust-remote-code --language-model-only \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 1 \ --distributed-executor-backend ray \ --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1 --dcp-comm-backend a2a \ --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA \ --attention-config.mla_prefill_backend TRTLLM_RAGGED \ --attention-config.use_prefill_query_quantization true \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --enable-prefix-caching \ --max-model-len 3840 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 512 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --load-format fastsafetensors \ --speculative-config.model Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark \ --speculative-config.attention_backend FLASHINFER_MLA \ --speculative-config.method dspark \ --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 7 \ --speculative-config.rejection_sample_method block ``` Control: on the same image and hardware, the base TP=8 Kimi-K3 config without DCP and without DSpark starts and serves normally. We first hit the same traceback on vLLM 0.29.1rc1.dev573+ge97573215 (commit e9757321527ca1ecd514c07c1418dd2c53da3d19) serving the same engine config through ai-dynamo (`dynamo.vllm`) in prefill/decode disaggregation, where both the prefill and decode engines failed. It also fails with 3 speculative tokens. The standalone reproduction above rules out Dynamo and the KV connector. Log excerpt (one DCP rank; every rank fails the same way; `torch` wrapper frames trimmed): ``` WARNING [flashinfer_mla.py:362] FlashInferMLAImpl got a query of uneven length. This usually indicates an issue in batch reordering or incorrect setup in dummy_run. ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1053] WorkerProc hit an exception. Traceback (most recent call last): File ".../vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 1045, in _execute_worker_rpc output = func(*args, **kwargs) File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 859, in compile_or_warm_up_model warmup_kernels( File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py", line 235, in warmup_kernels _warmup_kernels(model_runner, worker_execute_model, worker_sample_tokens) File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py", line 446, in _warmup_kernels _run_decode_step(step_indices, step_spec_flags) File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py", line 415, in _run_decode_step worker_execute_model(decode_output) File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 1259, in execute_model output = self.model_runner.execute_model( File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 1992, in execute_model model_output = self.model(**model_inputs) ... File ".../vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/mla.py", line 619, in forward attn_out, gate = self._forward_q_lora(positions, hidden_states) File ".../vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/mla.py", line 534, in _apply_q_lora_attention self._attention(positions, q, kv_c_normed, k_pe.unsqueeze(1), attn_out) File ".../vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/mla.py", line 711, in _attention latent_out, lse = self.impl.forward_mqa( # type: ignore[attr-defined] File ".../vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla.py", line 432, in forward_mqa kernel_out = trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla( File ".../flashinfer/mla/_core.py", line 3816, in trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla backend = _validate_mla_dcp_args( File ".../flashinfer/mla/_core.py", line 2817, in _validate_mla_dcp_args raise ValueError( ValueError: causal_seqlens_kv_global must have shape (9,), got (2,) ``` **Analysis (source at 7f1a5398, unchanged on main 09fe178d):** 1. `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py` (line 433) adds a mixed spec/non-spec decode step when `num_reqs >= 2`: ```python decode_steps.append(([0, 1], [use_spec_decode, False])) ``` With 7 speculative tokens, this step is a causal decode batch of 8 + 1 = 9 tokens over 2 requests. 2. #52988 moved `FlashInferMLAMetadataBuilder` to `query_len_support=VARLEN` and `ALWAYS` cudagraph support, so this ragged batch now reaches `FlashInferMLAImpl.forward_mqa`. The causal ragged path (`cum_seq_lens_q`) is taken only when `dcp_world_size == 1` ("DCP keeps the uniform reshape below: it needs LSE, which the kernels do not return on the ragged path (flashinfer #3238)"). 3. With DCP > 1 the batch therefore falls into the "query of uneven length" branch. That branch does `q = q.unsqueeze(1)` (9 single-token rows) but leaves `row_req = None`. `block_table`, `seq_lens` and `decode.dcp_tot_seq_lens` stay per-request (2 rows), and FlashInfer's DCP validation rejects the mismatch. Even if the shapes matched, flattening a causal query block into independent single-token rows would need a per-row causal KV length. The non-causal branch's `_flattened_decode_metadata` builds only the row → request mapping. Warmup exercises this batch shape because, under spec decoding, real steps can contain requests with no draft tokens. So gating the warmup step alone (as suggested in #53391 for another backend) would likely move the failure from startup to serving. **Possible directions:** - For causal decode with DCP > 1, flatten ragged blocks into per-token rows with `row_req` and per-row causal KV lengths (local and `dcp_tot_seq_lens`), in the same way as `_flattened_decode_metadata`. - Or keep ragged decode batches away from this backend when `dcp_world_size > 1` (split into uniform sub-batches or reclassify, as before #52988) until FlashInfer returns LSE on the ragged path (flashinfer #3238). **Bracket:** We have no known-good revision for this configuration. Earlier attempts stopped at an unrelated DCP interleave-size configuration error (fixed by `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1`) before reaching this path. Both tested nightlies (e9757321, 7f1a5398) include #52988 and fail the same way. **Related:** #53391 (same warmup mixed spec/non-spec step, DSV4 FlashInfer sparse path), #52988 (VARLEN switch for FlashInfer MLA), #56723 (DCP target with non-DCP DSpark). ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions. (Searched issues and PRs for the error text and for FlashInfer MLA DCP ragged/uneven decode as of 2026-09-24. Related but distinct: #53391. The chatbot was not used.) ## Patch verification No unpublished patch was prepared or tested. --- _This issue was drafted with assistance from the `opus` AI model._

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][NIXL] Read a GQA draft's head slice from a PCP x DCP prefill
body:
Stacked on #58471 (the first four commits are that PR; review only the last commit, a85e65683a).

## Purpose

A TP1 PCP×DCP prefiller exposes its PCP ranks as NIXL transfer ranks and shards the MLA target by token. Since #56723 a non-MLA draft (e.g. DSpark) runs there without DCP, so every prefill rank holds all draft heads for all tokens at the same block IDs. #58471 raises `NotImplementedError` for this pairing (DCP > 1), so a PCP8×DCP8 prefiller cannot feed a TP8 decoder with a DSpark draft.

- Map the draft by the prefill's real TP (transfer TP // PCP). Each decode rank reads its head slice from prefill rank `tp_rank % transfer_tp`; handshake sizes are checked against the real TP.
- Pull draft blocks only from that rank, paired as a non-DCP read would pair them, in both the per-group and region-mapped (#57389) paths. MLA regions keep their DCP slices, and done-notification counts are unchanged.
- Accept any layout with contiguous heads per page on both sides. The DCP prefill needs a block-outer layout (`VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC`).
- Register head-sharded draft layers as their own NIXL regions. Block-outer groups alias at byte 0, so the first draft layer was merged into the first MLA layer's region, then transferred as MLA-sized bytes and made the region shared (which region-mapped DCP pulls reject).

Unsupported combinations still raise `NotImplementedError`: prefill real TP > 1 with DCP, decode DCP, decode TP below the prefill transfer TP.

## Test Plan

- New unit tests in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/{test_nixl_connector,test_nixl_connector_hma,test_nixl_desc_geometry}.py` (mapping/offset/size checks for PCP8×DCP8 → TP8, layout acceptance, rejection cases, per-group and region-mapped pulls with the draft from one rank, the aliased-region fix).
- GPU: GLM-5.3 + `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-speculator.dspark` (DSpark7, fixed verification), PCP8×DCP8×EP8 prefill → TP8×EP8 decode with HiSparse + native offload, 2× 8×H200, NIXL, `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC` on both roles.

## Test Result

- Unit: NIXL connector unit suite passes except 3 pre-existing failures that need a real engine (`test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller` ×2, `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma[gemma]`).
- gsm8k (5-shot, 200 samples, through the P/D router): **0.930**; 100% of prompt tokens served as external KV hits; 0 failed NIXL transfers.
- Draft-KV integrity: on a copy task inside the draft's 2048-token sliding window, DSpark acceptance through P/D matches decoder-local prefill on the same prompts (8K: 0.86 vs 0.87, 32K: 0.84 vs 0.86, 100K: 0.87 vs 0.89). A scrambled draft transfer shows up as a large gap here (previously ~0.3-0.45 vs ~0.57 local).

title: [Bug]: VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 breaks DeepEncoder models (DeepSeek-OCR family): mean_batch_invariant returns float32, LayerNorm2d then feeds fp32 into a bf16 conv2d
body:
### Your current environment

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:unlimited-ocr` (arm64 digest `sha256:2935d4d261b7972060c358d86b8811bc04ee484526a0fc265ad9fad92bde2e0e`), vLLM `v0.23.1rc1.dev541+g7aaf016a1`
- GPU: NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark class), single GPU
- Model: `baidu/Unlimited-OCR` @ `07dea832e22aefee32ad281d4b80551282e1c168` (bf16), served per the official recipe

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` the engine fails during memory profiling, after the weights load:

```
RuntimeError: Input type (torch.cuda.FloatTensor) and weight type (CUDABFloat16Type) should be the same
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/conv.py", line 134, in _forward_conv
    x = F.conv2d(
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above.
```

The same command **without** `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` starts and serves normally (and three greedy reads of the same page are byte-identical with `--max-num-seqs 1`).

**Root cause.** Batch-invariant mode registers `aten::mean.dim` -> `mean_batch_invariant`, which casts its input to float32 and returns float32 regardless of the input dtype:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a160c6fe5910957a0feac50074ec6fc183c2a92/vllm/model_executor/determinism/batch_invariant.py#L899-L920

`aten::mean` returns the input dtype when `dtype` is not given, so this override changes the dtype seen by model code. DeepEncoder's `LayerNorm2d` computes `u = x.mean(1, keepdim=True)`; `x - u` then promotes the activations to float32, and the following `conv2d` (bf16 weights) raises:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a160c6fe5910957a0feac50074ec6fc183c2a92/vllm/model_executor/models/deepencoder.py#L221-L226

Any model whose code calls `Tensor.mean` on bf16/fp16 activations and feeds the result into a dtype-strict op (conv, or a matmul outside the overridden set) is exposed; DeepSeek-OCR / DeepSeek-OCR-2 / Unlimited-OCR share this `LayerNorm2d`.

**Suggested fix.** Keep the float32 accumulation for determinism, but return the input dtype unless a dtype was requested (matching `aten::mean` semantics), e.g. at the end of `mean_batch_invariant`:

```python
    return result if dtype is not None else result.to(input.dtype)
```

### Reproduce

```bash
docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc host -e VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 vllm/vllm-openai:unlimited-ocr \
  baidu/Unlimited-OCR --trust-remote-code \
  --logits_processors vllm.model_executor.models.unlimited_ocr:NGramPerReqLogitsProcessor \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --mm-processor-cache-gb 0
```

The function and the `LayerNorm2d` above are unchanged on `main` as of 7a160c6fe5.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Searched existing issues for `mean_batch_invariant` / batch invariant + conv2d dtype; found none.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Use the group's own DCP factor for the SWA store mask
body:
## Purpose

The offloading scheduler passes the global `decode_context_parallel_size` to `SlidingWindowManager.reachable_block_mask` for every KV-cache group, and that mask scales the spec's block size by the factor it is given. A DCP-replicated sliding-window group (`dcp_sharded=False`, e.g. a non-DCP DSpark drafter next to a DCP target since #56723) therefore had its block span inflated by the DCP size. Under the default semantic-only retention (`prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`) the retained window tail ending at the replay boundary was stored at block index `aligned // (block_size * dcp)` instead of `aligned // block_size`, so the stored SWA chunks never formed a full window at any boundary a later request looks up. Every request then missed in the drafter group, and hence overall.

Pass the group's effective DCP factor, matching how the GPU-side `SingleTypeKVCacheManager` and the offload `tokens_per_block` resolution already treat `dcp_sharded`.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `test_dcp_replicated_swa_tail_store_then_lookup` in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py`, run with the draft group replicated and DCP-sharded: checks which blocks are stored, then that a longer request sharing the prompt hits up to the DCP-aligned boundary. The replicated case fails without this change.
- GPU: GLM-5.3 + `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-speculator.dspark` (window 2048) on a PCP8×DCP8×EP8 H200 prefiller with `OffloadingConnector` (TieringOffloadingSpec, 512 GiB), behind NIXL P/D. Restore probe: send a ~95K-token prompt, evict it from the GPU prefix cache with ~4.1M tokens of other prompts, resend.

## Test Result

- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/`: 461 passed, 2 skipped.
- Restore probe: before, the CPU tier served ~0% of queried tokens under an Agent X workload (23K of 44.6M). After, **94,720 of 94,931 tokens** came back as external hits on the resend (6.0 GB loaded, 0 GPU prefix hits).
- gsm8k (5-shot, 200) through P/D with the fix: 0.950.

title: [Bug]: Fill-in DSpark underallocates KV lookahead and can overwrite target KV (synthetic CUDA repro)
body:
### Bug

For DSpark checkpoints with `sample_from_anchor=false`, the drafter uses **N+1 query positions** (bonus token + N draft tokens), but `VllmConfig.num_lookahead_tokens` reserves only **N**.

With 137 prompt tokens, 7 draft tokens and 16-token KV blocks, the scheduler allocates 144 slots (positions 0–143), while the drafter also writes position 144. That lookup can read a stale block ID from the unused table tail and overwrite another request's target KV cache. This was observed during generation, causing repetitive malformed output.

### Reproduction

The regression is covered by [`test_dspark_lookahead_covers_query_window`](https://github.com/notimesea/vllm/blob/58eff92e78422231d670a0725b87508d351bdad8/tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_lookahead.py#L36) in #59105. It checks that the full draft query window fits the reserved blocks; no model weights or prompts are needed.

Run in a vLLM test environment:

```sh
python -m pytest --noconftest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_lookahead.py -k dspark_lookahead_covers_query_window -q
```

- Test-only commit `58eff92e7`: **1 failed**.
- Fix commit `a26af2d9d`: **1 passed**.

The test covers both anchor modes and the default, N=1/7, block sizes 16/32, and prompt lengths spanning two blocks. It checks allocation bounds; the actual KV overwrite was confirmed separately by GPU instrumentation.

Standalone [synthetic CUDA reproducer](https://gist.github.com/notimesea/7de52434b9ef659e1ae6a6aab4d201b7) exercises the actual draft slot-preparation kernel without model weights or user prompts. It fails before the fix and passes after it; instructions and expected output are included in the gist.

### Environment and validation

Observed on vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev284+gbeef814e1`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, Python 3.11.14, one H200, `google/gemma-4-31B-it` + `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-speculator.dspark`. BF16, FlashAttention 4, V2 runner, eager, synchronous scheduling, prefix caching off, no LoRA.

Before the fix, the workload reproducibly failed on batch 9. After the fix, three cold starts × 20 batches × 16 requests completed without the observed corruption. The originally failing batch had no invalid draft writes or target-KV mutations.

### Proposed fixes

- #59105: minimal two-file fix and regression test; reserve N+1 slots for fill-in DSpark while preserving anchor-sampling and DFlash behavior.
- #48909: a broader four-file alternative for the same mismatch, also introducing a shared query-width property and updating the older runner's max-length guard.

AI assistance: Codex.

title: PP on docker: gloo control plane resolves to bridge IP (535ms per send) and presents as a long-context decode collapse — suggest defaulting GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo for same-netns ranks
body:
## Summary

On a single-container PP deployment, the `cpu:gloo` control plane (`isend_object` for per-step scheduler / speculative-decode feedback) resolves the container hostname to the **docker bridge IP** (172.17.0.2) instead of loopback. Every control send then costs **~535 ms** (measured via torch-profiler `user_annotation gloo:send`). The payload grows with context (block tables / indices), so the tax presents as a **long-context decode collapse** that looks like a compute problem but isn't.

One-line fix:

```bash
-e GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
```

Originally filed against the sm_80 backport fork as wtdcode/vllm-backport#111; the `cpu:gloo` group for PP coordination is created the same way in upstream `parallel_state.py`, so the failure mode applies to any single-container / docker-bridge PP deployment.

## Environment

- 4× NVIDIA CMP 170HX (GA100, sm_80, 64 GiB, PCIe Gen2 x4, no P2P), single docker container, default bridge networking
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (764B, EXL3 2/3 bpw mixed), PP4 (10,10,11,9), DSpark `num_speculative_tokens=5`, `kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, 1M context, RustFrontend, prefix caching on
- backport image v0.13.0-lineage with exllamav3 1.5.3

## Symptom

Single-stream decode collapsed with context while **all silicon sat idle**:

| ctx | decode tok/s (before fix) |
|---|---|
| 60K | 57.0 |
| 128K | 46.7 |
| 524K | 35.8 |

During deep-context decode, per-rank GPU busy was **8–19 %** and every process (EngineCore, RustFrontend, API server, all 4 workers) sat at **0–3 % CPU** — the pipeline was waiting on the control plane, not computing.

## Root cause

Worker traces show the wait carrier directly:

```
user_annotation gloo:send   avg 535 ms/call, ~4.7 calls/s during decode
```

Same ~535 ms at 60K and 524K windows (constant per-send floor), but the number of bytes per send grows with context, which is what produces the context-dependent collapse. Gloo's default transport picks the interface from the container hostname → docker bridge, even though all ranks share a network namespace where loopback is the correct path.

## Fix and results

`-e GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo` on the container (for multi-host deployments, set it to the real internal NIC instead — do not use `lo` across hosts).

Single-stream decode, warm, identical prompts:

| ctx | before | after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32K | 57.0 | 60.7 | +6 % |
| 128K | 46.7 | 58.3 | +25 % |
| 300K | ~40 | 56.7 | +40 % |
| 524K | 35.8 | **54.7** | **+53 %** |

Slope across 32K→524K: **-37 % → -10 %**. Cold prefill (fully distinct fillers, see caveat) also improved ~+55 % (524K TTFT 129 s ≈ 4,060 tok/s) since chunk control messages share the same group.

No regressions: quality suite 7/7 + vision 2/2 unchanged; concurrency C8 200.6 / C16 199.4 / C24 252.1 decode tok/s (mixed scenarios, warm round).

## Suggestions

1. Consider defaulting `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo` when all PP ranks live in one network namespace, or warning at startup when the gloo interface resolves to a docker-bridge subnet — the failure mode is silent and looks like a model/kernel problem.
2. Benchmarking caveat we hit while verifying (may save others time): prefix caching in this stack matches blocks **by content**, so a changing head-nonce does not prevent hits — honest cold-prefill benchmarks need fully distinct filler text per point.

Happy to provide the trace-analysis tooling (per-rank kernel pickles, gloo annotation comparison) if useful.

title: [Attention] Support FlashInfer re-paging for packed BLHNC KV caches
body:
## Purpose

Enable FlashInfer dense GQA to use packed BLHNC KV caches with BF16/FP16 storage.

Manager blocks remain intact while FlashInfer reads smaller kernel pages through remapped indices and shared-storage views. This enables the existing packed grouping for configurations such as Qwen3.6 + DFlash, reducing KV groups from 46 to 5. The change also aligns ordinary sliding-window manager blocks with the primary attention block size.

Addresses question 2 in #58638. This complements #58380's layout selection and the sparse MLA work in #55219/#57169; it adds the dense FlashInfer read path without depending on #57169.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py \
  -k 'packed_flashinfer or sliding_window_keeps_manager_size or packed_allocation_retains_manager_blocks or clear_layer_kv_caches_releases_flashinfer_read_views'
```

Serving setup:
- 1× B300, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.0.
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 + z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash.
- MRv2, TP=1, FlashInfer, BF16 activation/KV/Mamba states, 7 speculative tokens.
- Max model length 262144, max sequences 32, max batched tokens 8192, block size 128, GPU memory utilization 0.8.
- Chunked prefill enabled; prefix caching disabled for throughput tests.
- `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`.

Both layouts use this branch. Each layout was tested on two fresh servers in alternating order. The workloads below used 8/8/32 warmup requests and 256/64/256 measured requests. Performance uses synthetic acceptance length 4; accuracy uses real speculative verification.

## Test Result

**8 focused regression cases passed**, covering graph replay, packed/dense read equivalence, manager-sized allocation, cache cleanup and SWA block sizing. Ruff and format checks passed.

Runtime checks confirmed that target and draft attention use the new path: **640-token manager blocks, 128-token kernel pages, shared storage**.

**Serving results**, averaged over two independent runs per layout:

| Workload | Metric | LBHNC | BLHNC | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192 input / 1 output, c1 | req/s | 6.419 | 7.015 | **+9.3%** |
| 1024 input / 1024 output, c1 | output tok/s | 286.56 | 427.01 | **+49.0%** |
| 1024 input / 1024 output, c32 | output tok/s | 5115.53 | 7221.04 | **+41.2%** |
| 8192 input / 1 output, c1 | p99 TTFT, ms | 160.59 | 148.02 | **−7.8%** |
| 1024 input / 1024 output, c1 | p99 TPOT, ms | 3.478 | 2.328 | **−33.1%** |
| 1024 input / 1024 output, c32 | p99 TPOT, ms | 6.038 | 4.274 | **−29.2%** |

The two c32 runs measured **7258.52** and **7183.57 tok/s**, improving over their paired LBHNC runs by **42.0%** and **40.3%**.

KV groups dropped **46→5**. Reported KV capacity increased **6,640,889→6,789,922 tokens (+2.2%)**, with comparable peak PyTorch allocated memory: **214.281→214.263 GiB**.

**NSYS**, 32 steady decode steps:

| Per-step measurement | LBHNC | BLHNC |
|---|---:|---:|
| Target metadata scope | 8.948 ms | 1.632 ms |
| Scheduler scope | 3.575 ms | 0.789 ms |
| GPU activity gaps | 16.542 ms | 7.521 ms |

The trace shows that enabling packed grouping reduces repeated metadata construction and scheduling work, allowing the GPU to spend less time waiting between operations.

**Correctness:**
- GSM8K, 250 questions, 5-shot chat, thinking disabled: **244/250 (97.6%)** for both layouts, with identical response texts.
- Real mean acceptance length: **5.297733** for both layouts.
- Fixed-prompt cold-cache and block-reuse checks: exact logits and greedy-token matches. Prefix-hit checks also produced identical greedy tokens.
- Two-GPU DCP kernel validation: **12 cases passed**, including BF16/FP16, empty local shards, partial pages and graph replay. Maximum output/LSE errors were **0.00862 / 1.91e-6**.

E2E/profiling measurements used `fb780b9b0`; the final guard simplification passed six routing-equivalence checks.



---

- [x] Test plan and commands.
- [x] Test results, before/after measurements and model evaluation.
- [x] Documentation changes considered; no new model or CLI option.

title: [Bugfix] Package the SM90 DeepGEMM mHC register lifetime fix
body:
## Purpose

Package the SM90 mHC prenorm GEMM register-lifetime fix from [deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#448](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/448), authored by jason (leevan). In a multi-stage K loop, the next iteration can overwrite register A operands before the previous asynchronous WGMMA has finished. Repeated calls with identical inputs can therefore produce different outputs. The upstream fix waits immediately after committing the WGMMA batch.

This integrates that existing fix into vLLM's packaged JIT header until the pinned DeepGEMM dependency contains it; it is not a new kernel implementation. DeepGEMM #448 is currently open. Remove the temporary integration once the dependency pin includes the fix.

This correctness change was split out of [vLLM #58986](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58986), which now contains only the H20 block-FP8 MoE tuning. This branch starts from main `07f1ba2ec66776650a490630ddfa9e3c92713c33` and does not depend on that performance PR. The corresponding v0.30 backport remains [mengziheng/vllm#3](https://github.com/mengziheng/vllm/pull/3). There is no throughput improvement claim for this correctness repair.

## Changes

- Generate a patched header during CMake configuration and install it without modifying a supplied `DEEPGEMM_SRC_DIR`. Exclude the original header from the directory install to prevent a same-timestamp overwrite.
- Use the same helper in the standalone DeepGEMM installer. Recognized patched input is idempotent; unrecognized source fails without overwriting the destination.
- Extend the existing mHC suite with six SM90 regressions: 256/512/1024 tokens, different split-K counts, default and side streams, independent FP32 references and exact repeatability. Skip when DeepGEMM is unavailable.

## Validation

The following GPU results were recorded on H20/v0.30 before this PR split. The main test path is `tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py`; the v0.30 suite used `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k 'sm90_mhc_prenorm_preserves_register_operands or test_mhc_fused_post_pre' -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k sm90_mhc_prenorm_preserves_register_operands -v
```

- The pinned original header fails the new regression; the fixed header passes all six cases. The final test including its DeepGEMM availability guard returned **6 passed, 212 deselected**.
- The broader selection returned **17 passed, 9 skipped, 1 failed**. The existing H=7168/M=128 BF16 reference case fails with both original and repaired headers. No tolerance was loosened; this is not a full-suite pass.
- A fresh-process audit of the complete mHC operation covers 12 shape/seed groups with five repeats each. Repaired results are exactly repeatable; the original produces inconsistent results at 256/512 tokens. This does not establish whole-model token determinism.
- An installation fixture using the actual CMake integration verified installed bytes equal the upstream fix, repeated configure/install preserves it, and supplied source content remains unchanged. Standalone idempotence and rejection of unknown input without destination overwrite also passed. A full wheel build was not performed.

Fresh local checks for this split:

```bash
pre-commit run --from-ref 07f1ba2ec66776650a490630ddfa9e3c92713c33 --to-ref HEAD
git diff --check 07f1ba2ec66776650a490630ddfa9e3c92713c33 HEAD
```

All applicable pre-commit checks pass. The three integration/helper files are byte-identical to the previously tested implementation, and the new regression's AST is identical. A local helper check again passed original-to-fixed conversion, idempotence, source preservation and unknown-input rejection. The generated header SHA256 is `b90beeaed11e279d3451ad3d438b8a64a41fd003c4b7f4d5e0a8fb79a20ad80b`. GPU tests were not rerun on this latest-main branch; these checks establish split equivalence, not a full main-wheel or full-model validation.

### Model evaluation

Historical validation uses the same GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoint on 4×H20, TP4, FP8 weights/BF16 activations and MTP3, with v0.30 native extensions and the patched JIT header. The corrected control without the MoE tuning and the corrected candidate with the tuning each score **121/128** on a GSM8K first-128, five-shot raw-completion diagnostic (greedy, concurrency 8, output cap 768). Each has 128 successful requests and no truncation. Only 39/128 output texts match exactly; each arm uniquely answers three questions correctly. This subset is not an accuracy-improvement claim or proof of full-model equivalence.

The corrected control completed **1,152/1,152** measured serving requests successfully; all three recorded control/candidate blocks completed **3,456/3,456** in total. The corrected candidate also passed six context-retrieval checks at 511/2047/2048/2049/4097/8193 tokens. Full serving settings, paired measurements and limitations remain in [#58986](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58986). Those performance differences belong to the MoE tuning, with this fix present in both arms.

B200, production traffic, long soak tests and full-model serving on latest main were not validated.

## Related work

The open-PR duplicate search was refreshed before splitting. [#50645](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50645) and [#53055](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53055) address missing-DeepGEMM fallbacks, [#52165](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52165) changes detection, [#48619](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48619) ports the SM100 kernel to CuTeDSL, and [#41834](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41834)/[#42856](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42856) concern SM12x support. [#55184](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55184) repairs sparse MLA on SM8x; [#54955](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54955) is an opt-in batch-invariant execution preview using explicit mHC operations. Neither addresses packaging this register-lifetime fix in the default SM90 path. No duplicate integration was found. The same code has been removed from #58986 so the two community PRs do not duplicate it. No second DeepGEMM fix PR is proposed.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Gather the compressed KV once per KV-source group in prefill
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 keeps compressed KV caches only on its kv-source layers: 2, 8, 14 and 20 on V4.1-Flash. The other 34 compressed layers read their source's cache and never write it.

Before this PR, the mega-attention prefill path (`_forward_prefill_mega`) still dequantized and gathered the whole compressed history into its bf16 workspace in **every** compressed layer:

- Each step made 38 gathers but read only 4 distinct caches.
- On a 16K-token mixed step at 128K context (8 prefills), the gather took ~330 µs per ratio-2 layer and ~655 µs per ratio-1 layer. That is ~19 ms of a 316 ms step, 6% of GPU time.

This PR gathers each source group's compressed history once:

- **Where the gathered data lives:** the gathered chunk sits at the tail of the shared workspace. The scratch of the layers in between is taken from the head, so it does not reach the tail.
- **Consumers:**
  - A consumer checks two things: the span is still intact, and it still holds the same source, step metadata object and chunk.
  - If both hold, the consumer skips the compressed gather and rewrites only its own SWA columns.
- **Source layers** always gather, because they have just inserted this step's rows.
- **`WorkspaceManager.get_retained(key, shape, dtype)`** is new:
  - It returns a view of the last bytes of the scratch workspace, plus a flag saying whether that span is untouched since the previous same-key, same-size call.
  - Any `get_simultaneous` request that reaches into the span clears the flag, as does a reallocation.
  - So the layer gathers again instead of reading stale data, and no memory is added.
- **Sparse indexer:** it now asks for its batch's K gather rows (`max_local_total_seq_lens` over its chunks) instead of the profiled bound `total_seq_lens`.
  - Before, every index layer claimed the whole workspace, which broke the span at L24/28/32/36.
  - The workspace itself is still sized by the profiled bound, so nothing else changes.

## Test Plan

**Serve.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4× B200, TP4 + EP + MegaMoE, DSpark:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1 \
VLLM_DISABLE_DSV4_MEGAMOE_SHARED_EXPERT_FUSION=0 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --served-model-name dsv41 --port 8008 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 512
```

The A/B toggle and the in-server check below come from a test-only copy of the attention file; they are not part of this PR.

- **In-server exactness check.** Every skipped gather was redone into a scratch tensor and compared with the reused columns bitwise, on real 128K-context traffic.

- **Long-context benchmark (`vllm bench serve`).**
  - Warm-up: 64 distinct 126,000-token random prefixes, each sent once with 1 output token to fill the prefix cache.
  - Each measured prompt is one of those prefixes plus a fresh 2,000-token suffix, round-robin over the prefixes.
  - Load: 128,000 input tokens, 1,024 output tokens, concurrency 64, 512 prompts.
  - Arms: the base arm runs the same code with reuse disabled (it gathers in every layer). The two arms ran side by side on one 8× B200 node, one on GPUs 0–3 and the other on GPUs 4–7.

  ```bash
  vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model dsv41 --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
    --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8008 --endpoint /v1/completions \
    --dataset-name custom --dataset-path measure.jsonl --custom-output-len 1024 --skip-chat-template --disable-shuffle \
    --num-prompts 512 --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos --seed 0 --temperature 0 \
    --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
  ```

- **Accuracy.** GSM8K through lm-eval 0.4.12: 5-shot, chat template, thinking off, greedy. Both arms were run.

- **Unit tests.**

  ```bash
  pytest tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py
  ```

## Test Results

**Exactness:**
- 15,400 skipped gathers matched a fresh gather bit for bit, with 0 mismatches.
- Before the indexer change, about 12% of consumer layers still regathered because an index layer had claimed the span (L24/28/32/36). That case always gathers again, so no stale read occurs; the indexer change removes it.

**Memory:** available KV cache memory is 66.3 GiB with this PR, identical to main (38,439,247 tokens). An earlier version with a dedicated buffer cost 4 GiB, because the shared workspace is already sized by the indexer's profiled K gather (5.28 GB).

**Throughput and latency, 128K prefix reuse, concurrency 64:**

These runs predate the indexer change, so the 4 extra gathers per step were still there. The numbers are a lower bound.

| arm | output tok/s | total tok/s | mean TTFT (ms) | p99 TTFT (ms) | p50 ITL (ms) | p99 ITL (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| base | 7,675.1 | 967,059 | 1,150.3 | 3,806.7 | 24.43 | 328.5 |
| this PR | 7,765.7 (+1.2%) | 978,484 (+1.2%) | 956.0 (−16.9%) | 3,695.8 (−2.9%) | 24.44 | 315.2 (−4.1%) |

- A second round with the GPUs swapped is excluded, because its base arm hit a stall.
  - Base arm: 77.4 s duration, p99 TTFT 9.2 s, mean TPOT 7.89 ms. The other three arms were at ~67.5 s, ≤3.8 s and 6.7–7.0 ms.
  - In one 10 s engine-stats window the base arm ran a full batch (64 running, 0 waiting) at 4.3K prompt and 4.3K generation tok/s, against ~11–19K and ~7–10K elsewhere.
  - The cause was not profiled.
- An earlier version with the same reuse logic measured +1.5% and +1.8% output tok/s over two swapped rounds.
- Decode ITL (p50) is unchanged, as expected: the change only touches prefill.

**Scaling:**
- The saved time scales with the compressed history length per prefill request. The rest of a mixed step scales with its new tokens.
- So the gain grows with longer contexts and shorter appends. The 128K context / 2K append above is a middle case.

**Accuracy (GSM8K, 5-shot, 1,319 questions):** identical on both arms.

| arm | exact_match (strict) | exact_match (flexible) |
|---|---:|---:|
| base | 0.7930 ± 0.0112 | 0.9621 ± 0.0053 |
| this PR | 0.7930 ± 0.0112 | 0.9621 ± 0.0053 |

**Unit tests:** `tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py` passes, 17 tests, 6 of them new for `get_retained`.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] Bound the prefill SWA window at the replay start
body:
## Purpose

Under SWA bounded replay, `gather_lens` is shortened so each request's gathered SWA buffer starts at its replay start. The ROCm prefill combiner (`amd/rocm.py`) still emits a full `min(pos + 1, window)` window, so the first replayed rows index below that buffer. This adds the bound the FlashMLA combine already has:

```python
swa_len = min(pos + 1, window, pos + 1 - gather_start)
```

in both the Torch path and `_combine_topk_swa_indices_kernel`. Without replay, `gather_start <= max(pos - window + 1, 0)`, so nothing changes.

Prefix-cache replay is still off on ROCm (#57906), and this does not lift that guard. Decoder-side replay (#58132 by @ivanium, #59039 by @frida-andersson) reaches this combiner without it, with `replay_start = seq_len - window`. #56638 (@JohnQinAMD) needs the same line in its fused kernel; whichever PR lands first, the other should carry it.

Not a duplicate: no open PR bounds this window. #56638 keeps it unbounded, and #58539 changes only the chunk plan.

No model evaluation: replay is off on ROCm on main, so no served output changes.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py -k rocm
```

The new ROCm-only test checks the combiner against the existing `combine_case` reference on a first replay chunk and a later chunk, for SWA-only and C4A.

## Test Result

- MI308X (gfx942), on main `94d14629`: the new test fails 4/4 before the change and passes 4/4 after; no other test in the file changes result. With #56638 (`38e16b51`) applied on main `53d2e16a`, it and `tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py` also pass.
- CPU (`TRITON_INTERPRET=1`), on main `1fde8ff7`: the same 4 FAIL → 4 PASS, also with #56638 applied. On 300 random batches, 242 fail before and 0 after; no batch without replay fails either way.
- Not run: gfx950.

AI assistance was used: Claude and Codex. Reviewed and tested by the submitter.

title: [Feature] Transfer bounded replay checkpoints from Prefill
body:
## Summary [Currently for Test-only]

Move DeepSeek-V4.1 bounded-replay state production to the Prefill instance for
Mooncake P/D deployments. Prefill now explicitly recomputes the final
`[H-128, H)` token range before publishing the checkpoint. After that
checkpoint is certified, Decode recomputes only the final prompt token instead
of replaying the last 128 tokens.

The feature is opt-in on both instances:

```json
{"kv_connector_extra_config":{"prefill_side_swa_replay":true}}
```

## Design

- Run ordinary Prefill without sampling, then atomically rewind the request by
  128 tokens and execute a second forward over the existing block table.
- Preserve cacheable Main/Indexer state while rebuilding target SWA,
  compressor continuation, and DSpark context state with the native replay
  masks.
- Run sampling and the normal DSpark proposal only after the replay forward.
- Record a producer CUDA event after target and drafter work, and wait for it
  before publishing checkpoint readiness.
- Certify protocol version, model/cache layout, transfer ID, logical boundary,
  prompt-token digest, local/remote block coverage, and every P/D worker.
- Keep the GDN `N-1` handoff contract so Decode recomputes the real final
  prompt token.

## Safety

The optimization is limited to direct Mooncake, model runner V2,
DeepSeek-V4.1, PP=PCP=DCP=1, text-only requests without LoRA or prompt
logprobs. Replay batches are isolated, cannot be split by the scheduler token
budget, and are cleared on preemption.

Missing, stale, incomplete, mismatched, or disagreeing requested checkpoints
are never consumed. Runtime certification failures follow
`kv_load_failure_policy`.

## Tests

Latest true-replay refactor:

- Prefix replay, Mooncake HMA, and output aggregation: 39 passed.
- GPU model runner V2 and scheduler output: 13 passed.
- Extended connector run: 65 passed, 1 skipped, and 1 unrelated failure
  because the environment could not access gated
  `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`.
- Python compilation and ruff format/lint: passed.
- Runtime smoke: 11-token and 4096-token requests passed.
- Runtime evidence confirmed a second Prefill forward over `[3968, 4096)` and
  certified checkpoint consumption on Decode.
- Formal performance workloads: current PR 768/768 and comparison C 768/768
  requests completed.
- Mooncake external cache hits were effectively 100%; no transfer failure,
  traceback, engine failure, or pod restart occurred.

Mypy could not start in the available local environment because
`pydantic.mypy` was unavailable.

## Compared Configurations

- **Current PR (D):** conventional full-target Prefill plus explicit Prefill
  128-token replay; Decode consumes the transferred replay checkpoint.
- **Comparison C:** the same baseline plus encoder-only Prefill, with the
  existing 128-token replay retained on Decode.

Both used nightly `a9eafde59c`, the same Mooncake release-only prerequisite,
Prefill TP8, and Decode TP1+DP8+EP8 with adaptive DSpark K5 and
`FULL_DECODE_ONLY`.

## Full Serving Commands

The commands below reproduce the validation topology. The runtime image was
built from
`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-a9eafde59cbd55182dc2265cc398b7186f0a0eaa`.

Common environment:

```bash
export NCCL_DEBUG=WARN
export NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1
export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
export VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1
export VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=600
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600
export VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip
export VLLM_ENABLE_CUDA_COMPATIBILITY=1
export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0
export UCX_NET_DEVICES=mlx5_1:1,mlx5_2:1
export NO_PROXY='*'
export no_proxy='*'
unset HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY http_proxy https_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy
ulimit -l unlimited
ulimit -s 67108864
```

### Current PR (D)

Prefill on `192.168.1.186`, TP8, full target plus static DSpark K5:

```bash

export VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT=8998

  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \

```

### Baseline Plus Encoder-only Prefill (C)

Prefill on `192.168.1.186`, TP8, encoder-only:

```bash

export VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT=8998

KV_TRANSFER_CONFIG='{

## Interpretation

Moving replay state production to Prefill improves isolated Decode efficiency.
Across 8K/16K/32K, Output TPS increases 3.02%, Mean TPOT decreases 8.72%,
P99 TPOT decreases 35.65%, acceptance increases 1.28 percentage points, and
verify steps decrease 1.04%.

That Decode gain does not recover the Prefill cost relative to encoder-only
Prefill. Across the same lengths, Prefill Mean TTFT increases 146.26%. In the
fixed-seed random E2E workload, Mean TPOT decreases 18.46%, but Output TPS
decreases 49.66% and Mean TTFT increases 125.69%.

The implementation is functionally viable, but it is not a positive
end-to-end replacement for encoder-only Prefill plus Decode-side replay in
this topology. Keep the PR draft/test-only.

## Duplicate Work

I searched open issues and PRs for Mooncake, bounded replay, Prefill-side SWA
state, and DeepSeek-V4.1 replay transfer. No open PR implements this design.
Related work differs:

- #58132 keeps bounded replay on Decode.
- #57872 and #58289 remove the full target from Prefill instead of transferring
  a restartable full-target checkpoint.
- #58504 addresses exact partial-hit retention, not replay-state ownership.

## AI Assistance

AI assistance was used for codebase analysis, implementation drafting, focused
test generation, and read-only diff review. The submitter reviewed the changes
and ran the checks listed above.

title: [Rust Frontend] Replay roundtrip output grammars through XGrammar
body:
## Purpose

Rust-built output grammars are currently checked only as structural-tag JSON. Nothing compiles them with the real XGrammar or verifies that the matcher accepts a real generation from token zero, which is the meaning of `reasoning_ended = Some(true)` since #57340.

Step 2.5 of the parser-owned output grammar rollout, following the merged #55269 and #57340. Stacked on #59148, which switches Rust MiMo to the MiMo structural-tag builder in `xgrammar-structural-tag` 0.4.1; only the last five commits belong to this PR. It adds test coverage only; production behavior is unchanged. The open-PR search found no other XGrammar replay harness for the Rust frontend.

- The chat roundtrip builds the output grammar from the same initialized processor that parses the completion. It runs with `--tool-strict-level parameter` so every builder-backed parser emits a grammar; the strict level affects grammar inputs only, not parsing.
- `tool_call_mix` runs once per tool-choice variant for every model:
  - `auto`, with content before the tool calls;
  - `required`, with tool calls only, the only shape builder grammars admit under `required`;
  - named `get_weather`, with a single call and no content.
- Each model's grammars are snapshotted into one `rust/src/chat/tests/grammar_replay/<model>.json` via `expect_file!`. The file records the model, model vocab size, and lowered stop set once. Each variant case records the `BuiltOutputGrammar`, the completion text, and the generation token IDs ending with a stop token. A stale file for a parser that no longer builds a grammar fails the roundtrip.
- `grammar_replay.py` is a PEP 723 uv script pinned to the `xgrammar` version in `requirements/common.txt`, with CPU torch. It builds `TokenizerInfo` and compiles each case the same way as `backend_xgrammar.py`. For `from_token_zero` cases it replays every token, checking both the bitmask and `accept_token`, and requires the stop token to terminate the matcher with `override_stop_tokens`. `final_output_only` cases are compiled only. It also requires the HF tokenizer to encode the completion to the recorded IDs, so tokenizer drift fails loudly.
- `grammar_replay.rs` wraps the script as a nextest test, so the existing Rust Frontend Cargo CI step runs it. That step already installs uv.
- `BuiltOutputGrammar` and `GrammarCoverage` derive `Serialize`. serde_json's `raw_value` is enabled for chat dev-dependencies only, to keep token ID arrays on one line.

Kimi K3 renders request-scoped control messages, such as the `tool_choice=required` instruction, after the whole history, as the official `encoding_k3.py` does. The generation prompt is then `A + C + G` while the closed history is `A + G + B + C`, so the prompt is no longer a prefix of the full render. The roundtrip now locates the completion `B` as the unique split of `C` and `G`. It falls back to the prefix cut when `C` is empty, which is the case for every other template. K3's grammar remains `final_output_only` here; it becomes a token-zero replay case with its native builder in Step 3.

The replay found the MiMo V2.6 grammar mismatch that #59148 fixes. MiMo renders compact `<tool_call><function=...>` calls, but on main the Rust MiMo parser reuses the Qwen3-Coder builder, whose tags are newline-delimited. Under `required` the replay rejected the call. Under `auto` the trigger never fired, so the grammar left the calls unconstrained. With #59148, MiMo runs all three variants, and its `auto` trigger and tags are compact. #58019 is the Python counterpart.

## Test Plan

```bash
cd rust
cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat --test roundtrip --test grammar_replay
UPDATE_EXPECT=1 cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat --test roundtrip  # regenerate cases
cargo nextest run -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
```

Negative controls: I copied the cases, mutated them, and ran the script on the copies.

## Test Result

- 12 models, 36 cases, `xgrammar-structural-tag` 0.4.1 output replayed with XGrammar 0.2.7, the version pinned in `requirements/common.txt`. XGrammar 0.2.7 ignores the new `excludes` field. The runner pin moves together with `requirements/common.txt`.
  - `auto`, `required`, and named, replayed from token zero and terminated: Qwen3, Qwen3.5, MiMo V2.6, MiniMax M2.5, DeepSeek V3.2/V4/V4.1, GLM-4.7/5.2, Hy3, and Kimi K2.5.
  - Kimi K3: `auto`, `required`, and named, `final_output_only`, compiled.
- All five negative controls fail at the expected token:
  - K3 relabeled `from_token_zero`: rejects `think` after `<|close|>`.
  - Qwen3 without the reasoning wrapper: rejects `<think>` at token 0.
  - DeepSeek V4 with a stop set lacking its terminator: does not terminate.
  - Unclosed final tool call: rejects `<|im_end|>`.
  - Completion text drift: reports a tokenizer mismatch.
- The named grammar replayed against the two-call `required` generation rejects the second call right after the first closes, for Qwen3, DeepSeek V4, and GLM-4.7.
- A modified case and a stale case each fail the roundtrip.
- `vllm-parser` + `vllm-chat`: 860 tests passed, including a unit test for the completion split. Workspace Clippy, `cargo sort`, and pre-commit passed.
- The replay takes about 28 s with warm uv and HF caches, dominated by loading 12 tokenizers. A cold uv environment added about 50 s locally.
- `trust_remote_code=True` is needed only for the Kimi K3 tokenizer. It is kept for all cases because production deployments of these models load their tokenizers with it.

AI assistance: implementation and validation assisted by Claude Code.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Constrain tool-call markers by token ID in engine st…
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58315. Related to #58105.

Under `tool_choice="required"` (and named tool choice) vLLM constrains generation
with an xgrammar structural tag built from xgrammar's builtin model templates.
Those templates spell the tool-call markers as **strings**
(`TriggeredTagsFormat(triggers=["<tool_call>"])`, `TagFormat(begin="<tool_call>get_weather", end="</tool_call>")`),
so the grammar admits any tokenization of that text, including `<` `tool_call` `>`
assembled from ordinary sub-tokens.

The streaming parser engine, once it has seen token IDs, recognises the markers listed
in `token_id_terminals` only by their dedicated token ID
(`StreamingParserEngine._process_lex_tokens`, `strict` branch) and treats the assembled
spelling as content. The two sides therefore disagree on what a tool call is:

| encoding of `<tool_call>get_current_time</tool_call>` (GLM-5) | grammar | parser |
|---|---|---|
| dedicated ids `[154843, ..., 154844]` | accept | 1 tool call |
| ordinary ids `[27, 14163, 13420, 29, ..., 522, 14163, 13420, 29]` | **accept** | **0 tool calls, text in `content`** |

A `required` request can thus return no tool call at all. For Qwen3 the parser recovers
the call through `<function=`, but leaks the literal `<tool_call>` into `content`.

## Change

`ParserEngineToolAdapter.get_structural_tag` now passes the builtin tag through
`bind_marker_tokens()` (new `vllm/tool_parsers/structural_tag_markers.py`), which
rewrites it so that every marker the engine resolves by token ID is matched by
xgrammar as that single token:

- `TriggeredTagsFormat` whose triggers all start with a marker →
  `TokenTriggeredTagsFormat(trigger_tokens=[marker])`
- `TagFormat` begin/end that start/end with a marker → `TokenFormat`, with the remaining
  literal text (`get_weather`, `\n<function=get_weather>\n`, ...) folded into the tag
  content as `ConstStringFormat`, so the accepted text is byte-identical
- `ConstStringFormat` containing a marker → sequence of literals and tokens
- `excludes` → `exclude_tokens`, keeping only entries that are single tokens

Markers that are not a single token in the vocabulary are left as strings, which is
exactly how the engine treats them (it only puts vocabulary hits in
`_resolved_token_ids`). So the invariant is: **the grammar constrains by token ID exactly
the terminals the parser recognises by token ID.**

`ParserEngine.token_id_markers` exposes that set. This touches `vllm/parser/engine/`
because the behaviour is wrong for every engine parser that declares
`token_id_terminals` (GLM-4.7/5, Qwen3, DeepSeek V3.2/V4, MiniMax, Kimi K2, ...),
not for one model.

Semantics that change for the free-text spans in `auto` mode: string `excludes`
(e.g. forbidding the text `</think>` in any tokenization) become token-level
`exclude_tokens`, because `TokenTriggeredTagsFormat` has no string excludes. That
matches the parser: with token IDs it reads the split spelling as content, and on the
text-only path (`extract_tool_calls`) a stray `</tool_call>` / `<arg_key>` in content is
also just content (verified on the GLM engine). The auto-mode test pins this down: a stray
dedicated `</tool_call>` token is still rejected where the builtin excludes it, the split
spelling is admitted and parsed as plain content. `required` remains as strict as before:
text before the first call is still rejected (verified against the builtin on GLM-5 and
Qwen3.6).

Note that today the two parser paths already disagree on the split spelling: the
text-only path parses `<tool_call>get_weather</tool_call>` spelled from ordinary tokens
as a tool call, the token-ID streaming path does not. Constraining the grammar removes
the ambiguity at the source instead of teaching one path the other's answer.

## Not a duplicate

- #58847 fixes the same issue on the parser side: a GLM-only config field that lets the
  streaming engine accept the text spelling of `<tool_call>` / `</tool_call>` under
  `tool_choice="required"` after `</think>`. That leaves the grammar unchanged, so named
  tool choice and every other engine parser with `token_id_terminals` (Qwen3, DeepSeek
  V3.2/V4, MiniMax, Kimi K2) keep the mismatch, and it reintroduces text matching for
  exactly the terminals the engine keys by ID. This PR changes no parser logic and covers
  all engine parsers and all three tool-choice modes. The two are alternatives, not
  complements; I am happy to consolidate whichever direction maintainers prefer.
- mlc-ai/xgrammar#935 switches the `glm_4_7` builtin to `TokenFormat` unconditionally and
  hand-builds the sequence/star structure instead of `TriggeredTagsFormat`. Even if it
  lands, vLLM pins xgrammar and other templates stay string-matched, so the vLLM-side
  binding is still needed; it is also a no-op on a template that already uses tokens.
- #58219 (docs) documents the contract for *user-supplied* grammars and does not change
  runtime behaviour. This PR fixes vLLM's own `required`/named grammar. Both can land.
- #50986, #57553, #56661 change how the Qwen3 parser validates/accepts markers in text;
  none touch the structural tag. No file overlap.
- No open PR references #58315. On #58105 the commenters explicitly deferred a code fix
  to a maintainer decision; this is that fix on the grammar side, where the reporter
  measured that only token elements reject the split encodings.
- Upstream I am proposing the same binding as an opt-in get_model_structural_tag(..., token_markers=True) in xgrammar (default output unchanged, per-builder marker_tokens; mlc-ai/xgrammar#940). Once an xgrammar release ships it, this rewrite can be replaced by passing that flag.

## Test plan

```bash
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_markers.py -q
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py tests/parser/engine \
       tests/tool_parsers/test_qwen3coder_tool_parser.py \
       tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py \
       tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/tool_parsers/structural_tag_markers.py \
    vllm/parser/engine/adapters.py vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine.py \
    tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_markers.py
```

- New file: 14 passed (`tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_markers.py`). Unit tests cover the rewrite on synthetic tags (trigger longer
  than the marker, nested `TagsWithSeparatorFormat`, literal splitting, non-marker
  triggers such as Llama's JSON prefix left alone, missing-vocab no-op, idempotence).
  End-to-end tests load the real `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` and `zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash`
  tokenizers, build the tag through `Qwen3EngineToolParser` / `Glm47MoeModelToolParser`,
  compile it with xgrammar and assert: dedicated-token encoding accepted and parsed as
  exactly one clean tool call; split encoding rejected; `auto` still accepts free text
  around a call.
- Existing suites: 4994 passed (teardown errors on my CPU-only box are the usual
  `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()` noise, unrelated).
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy` (tools/pre_commit/mypy.py, 3.12) clean.

## Model evaluation

No model run is included. The change only affects which token sequences the
`required`/named-tool grammar admits; it removes encodings the parser could never turn
into a tool call and leaves the dedicated-token encoding (the one models are trained on)
unchanged. A CPU reproduction with the real tokenizers is in the new test file.
I can run GLM-4.7-Flash with `tool_choice="required"` before/after if reviewers want
frequency numbers.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude) was used to survey the related issues, review the fix, and help
with the English wording. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above locally.

title: [ROCm][Perf][Attention] Reduce temporary allocations in sparse-indexer prefill
body: Reuse the freshly produced [H, M, N] score buffer for scaling, ReLU and head weighting in fp8_mqa_logits_torch, then mask the reduced logits in place, instead of allocating separate full-size FP32 temporaries. Inputs, FP32 operation order and the head reduction are unchanged. Targets the unpaged Torch prefill fallback.On RX 7900 XTX this cuts function wall time by 6.4–6.5% and incremental peak allocated memory by ~48% for prefill shapes (256, 576) and (256, 768). Outputs are byte-identical to baseline.
