title: [Feature] Release WorkspaceManager scratch on sleep
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59055.

Includes the allocator change that was briefly split out as #59577 (now closed): the first two commits keep every cuMem memory pool alive when a tag is re-entered; the last two are the workspace change.

Rebased on main after #59200 (shared GPU/XPU worker init). The `xpu_worker.py` hunk is gone because XPU now shares the init path.

`WorkspaceManager` allocates its scratch buffer with a plain `torch.empty`, outside the sleep-mode memory pool, so `/sleep` never releases it.
- At TP4 it is about 1.3 GiB per GPU.
- With DP and DeepGEMM/Marlin MoE (the default allgather/reduce-scatter all2all), it grows with `dp_size × max_num_batched_tokens`. DP8 reaches 4.5 GiB per GPU.

The scratch holds nothing between forward passes. This PR allocates it in the sleep-mode pool under a new `workspace` tag:
- `/sleep` discards it; nothing is copied.
- `/wake_up` remaps it at the same virtual address, so captured CUDA graphs stay valid.
- Persistent workspace resources are unchanged.

Changes:
- `WorkspaceManager` takes an optional `alloc_context` factory, defaulting to `nullcontext`.
  - The shared `Worker._init_workspace_and_model_runner()` (#59200) passes `_maybe_get_memory_pool_context("workspace")` once, which is also a no-op when the sleep-mode allocator is off. XPU uses the same init path, so it gets the tag without an `xpu_worker.py` change.
  - CPU does not support sleep mode and is unchanged.
- Selective wake may defer only the user-facing `weights` and `kv_cache` tags (`DEFERRABLE_TAGS` in `vllm/device_allocator/__init__.py`); the CUDA and XPU allocators restore every other tag, `workspace` included, on any wake. Without it, the common RL sequence (`wake_up(["weights"])`, update weights, `wake_up(["kv_cache"])`) would leave the scratch unmapped while captured graphs still point at it. Behaviour change: allocations under tags other than `weights`/`kv_cache`, including the default tag, are now restored by any wake.
- A workspace resize enters `workspace` again while blocks of the earlier buffer can still be live, so the allocator must handle a re-entered tag. On main, every `use_memory_pool(tag)` entry creates a new `MemPool`, and entering a tag again overwrites `allocator_and_pools[tag]`, the only reference to the previous pool. Main never re-enters a tag (`weights` once, `kv_cache` once), so nothing triggers this today; this PR (`workspace`) and #59158 (`runtime`) do.
  - A tensor still alive in a dropped pool is later freed with `cudaFree` instead of `my_free` (pytorch/pytorch#146431). The new `test_reentered_tag` reproduces this on main.
  - `allocator_and_pools` now holds a list of `(pool, allocator)` entries per tag, on CUDA and XPU, and `release_pools` flattens it. Every pool stays alive until `release_pools`.
  - Each entry still gets a new pool, as on main: the exit sweep unmaps free segments behind the caching allocator, so reusing a pool could hand out an unmapped block.
  - When a tag is entered again, the free segments of its older pools are unmapped first, so an outgrown buffer is returned before the next allocation. This is the exit sweep, factored out as `_trim`. PyTorch has no per-pool `empty_cache` for a live pool (pytorch/pytorch#145168, closed, unchanged by design).
  - XPU gets only the list (it has no exit sweep), so there an outgrown buffer stays mapped until shutdown.
  - Two older open PRs read `allocator_and_pools["weights"][0]` (#23875, #49151) and would need `[-1][0]` after this change.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `test_selective_wake_restores_internal_tags[workspace|default]`: `wake_up(["weights"])` restores a `workspace` or default-tag allocation while `kv_cache` stays asleep; `wake_up(["kv_cache"])` then restores it.
- New unit test `test_workspace_scratch_discarded_on_sleep`:
  - captures a CUDA graph on the scratch;
  - sleeps, and checks the scratch is discarded without a CPU copy;
  - wakes with `kv_cache` only, and checks the graph still replays;
  - holds a view of the pre-resize buffer across sleep/wake; once it is released, the next resize unmaps it, and a later wake does not remap it.
- New unit test `test_reentered_tag[x-freed|x-alive]`: enters a tag and allocates X, enters it again and allocates Y, frees X before or after the second entry, enters a third time and checks that only Y is still mapped; then writes Y, sleeps, wakes, reads Y back and calls `release_pools()`. With only `cumem.py` reverted to main, `[x-alive]` fails 5 of 5 runs (`assert 134217728 == 67108864`: X is never freed through `my_free`), and without that assert `wake_up()` raises `CUDA Error: invalid argument` on X's stale handle.
- Regression tests:
  - `tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py`: `test_basic_cumem`, `test_discard_tags`, `test_cumem_with_cudagraph`, `test_sleep_with_only_weights_asleep` (all 4), `test_level2_discards_ordinary_tensor_with_weights_tag`.
  - `tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py`.
- End-to-end on 4× GB300 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, MTP and CUDA graphs:
  - Patched vs unpatched in each configuration, same image and node.
  - Memory after `/sleep`; three rounds: level 1, level 1, level 2.
  - Prompt logprobs compared before sleep and after each wake.

## Test Result

Memory per GPU after `/sleep`. Unpatched vs patched, same image and node.

| Setup | Unpatched | Patched | Saved | WorkspaceManager (unpatched) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP4 + EP4, auto MoE (FlashInfer TRTLLM) | 15178 MiB | 13856 MiB | 1322 MiB | 1322 MiB |
| TP4 + EP4, DeepGEMM MoE | 14570 MiB | 13248 MiB | 1322 MiB | 1322 MiB |
| TP4 + EP4, Marlin MoE | 14731 MiB | 13195 MiB | 1536 MiB | 1536 MiB |
| DP4 + EP4, DeepGEMM MoE, fp8 KV, mbt 8192 | 14528 MiB | 12128 MiB | **2400 MiB** | 2400 MiB |
| DP8 + EP8 over 2 nodes, DeepGEMM MoE, fp8 KV, mbt 8192 (the #59055 setup) | 16790 MiB | 12134 MiB | **4656 MiB** | 4656 MiB |

- **Memory breakdown:** in every setup the saving equals the workspace size. A memory breakdown taken while asleep accounts for all but 4–10 MiB per GPU, and no workspace memory remains.
- **Correctness:** prompt logprobs after the level-1 wakes.
  - TP4 auto and TP4 DeepGEMM: bit-identical to before sleep.
  - TP4 Marlin and DP4: differences stay within the run-to-run variation these configurations already show while awake, patched and unpatched alike.
  - After a level-2 sleep, output is garbage in both patched and unpatched runs, as expected: weights are discarded and not reloaded.
- **Timing:** sleep 8–12 s, wake 0.6–1.0 s, the same as unpatched.
- **KV cache:** unchanged. TP4 auto 202.44 GiB / 13,044,408 tokens, the same as unpatched. (Revision 0a8463b137 kept outgrown scratch buffers mapped in their pools and gave 202.24 GiB / 13,031,717 tokens.)
- **Tests:** all unit tests above pass; pre-commit passes.
- **Re-run after the pool-lifetime change (0a8463b137), same image and nodes:** asleep TP4 auto 13857 MiB, DP4 12129 MiB, DP8 12135 MiB per GPU; with #59158, TP4 9165–9293 MiB. Gated bit-exactness harness on TP4 (553 requests per round, batch sizes 1–256), alone and with #59158: every request bit-identical (tokens, logprobs, prompt logprobs) after each of two full wakes and two selective wakes.
- **Re-run after releasing outgrown buffers (21c7a0be4c), same image, another GB300 rack:** TP4 auto asleep 13859 MiB per GPU, the same as 0a8463b137 on these nodes (13859; 13857 on the earlier rack), with KV 202.44 GiB / 13,044,408 tokens instead of 202.24 GiB / 13,031,717. Every request of the gated harness bit-identical in all 10 compared rounds, including two full and two selective wakes; 4 more sleep/wake cycles exact. At sleep, the three `workspace` entries hold no free mapped memory. Unit tests: `test_cumem.py` 14, `test_sleep_mode_backend.py` 9, `test_workspace.py` 11 passed.

**Large model accuracy (GLM-5.3, TP8 over 2 GB300 nodes, `mp` backend, MTP on).** GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0. Each cell is accuracy, and every run had 0 invalid answers.

| State | Unpatched | Patched |
|---|---:|---:|
| Awake | 0.914 | 0.912 |
| Level-1 sleep, full wake | 0.914 | 0.916 |
| Level-1 sleep, selective wake (weights, then kv_cache) | 0.918 | 0.912 |
| Level-2 sleep, `reload_weights` | 0.911 | 0.911 |

- The spread across states is 0.7 points or less, which matches the run-to-run variation at concurrency 64 with MTP.
- The level-1 backup is 0.38 GiB smaller per GPU, because the workspace is discarded instead of copied.
- No errors on either node.

**Large model accuracy (DeepSeek-V4.1, TP8 over 2 GB300 nodes, `mp` backend).** GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0. Each cell is accuracy / invalid rate.

| State | Unpatched | Patched |
|---|---:|---:|
| Awake | 0.892 / 0.002 | 0.896 / 0.001 |
| Level-1 sleep, full wake | 0.899 / 0.002 | 0.898 / 0.000 |
| Level-1 sleep, selective wake | 0.902 / 0.003 | 0.905 / 0.002 |
| Memory while asleep, per GPU | 21035 MiB | 15753 MiB (**−5282 MiB**) |

- `reload_weights` after a level-2 sleep produces garbage for this model with or without this PR: 172 "Failed to load weights" warnings from `layerwise.py` for `DeepseekV4MegaAttnAttention`, `DeepseekV4ScalingRotaryEmbedding` and `NgramHashState`. It is a separate, existing layerwise-reload gap, so level-2 accuracy is not compared here.

**Other model families (with #59158, TP4, 4× GB300).** In every phase, every request matches the first awake run exactly, text and all logprobs. The phases are level-1 full wake, level-1 selective wake, and level 2 + `reload_weights`. Level 2 + reload being exact confirms the workspace and runtime state come back.

| Model | Asleep MiB/GPU, unpatched → patched |
|---|---:|
| Qwen3-8B | 4019 → 3605 |
| Llama-3.1-8B NVFP4 | 3949 → 3535 |
| Qwen3-VL-8B (text + image) | 4045 → 3629 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B (MLA + KDA) | 4809–4937 → 4733 |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B FP8, EP | 7363–7491 → 6829 |

- **GSM8K, Qwen3-8B** (awake / full wake / selective / level 2 + reload): 0.888 / 0.886 / 0.887 / 0.885.

**Lifecycle edge cases (with #59158, DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4):** all pass, bit-exact after each.
- 300 consecutive sleep/wake cycles with all sleep-mode PRs (alternating full and selective wake): every cycle bit-exact (34,140/34,140 requests), memory after wake equal to before sleep on every GPU, device-memory slope 0.000 MiB/cycle. Host RSS grows by about +5 MB/cycle over the first ~50 cycles of every launch, unpatched too; later slopes change sign between launches of the same configuration in both arms (patched −1.8 to +3.6, unpatched −0.5 to +0.6 MB/cycle) and the shared-memory backup stays byte-for-byte constant.
- Sleep right after startup.
- A request sent while asleep, or after a weights-only wake: it is queued and completes after the full wake.
- Double sleep and double wake: no-ops.
- Level 1 followed by level 2 without a wake: ignored.
- 256 concurrent mixed-length requests right after wake: no errors, no NaN.

**Review:** three rounds of adversarial review (Codex, Kimi K3). The final round found no blocker or major issue.

---
This PR contains AI-assisted code (Claude Code); commits carry a `Co-authored-by` trailer.

### AMD MI355X (ROCm)

Works on ROCm unchanged (vLLM ROCm nightly `e975732152`, diff applied). Memory per GPU while asleep (level 1):

| Setup | Unpatched | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP1 | 5677 | 4747 (−930) |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 | 7946 | 7176 (−770) |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite DP2 | 9430 | 7894 (−1536) |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 | 12018 | 11130 (−888) |

Outputs are bit-identical after full and selective wake. `_trim` is safe on ROCm too: the Python-level unmap keeps the virtual address reserved, as on CUDA.

AMD 50-cycle leak test (DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP1 / TP2 / DP2, DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4): device-memory slope 0.00 MiB/cycle, 50/50 cycles bit-exact, no host-RSS growth over level-1 cycles, in-process memory after wake equal to before sleep. title: [Feature] Offload model runner buffers on sleep
body:
## Purpose

**Depends on #59158** (the `runtime` sleep tag). This branch contains that commit; only the last commit belongs to this PR.

The GPU model runner allocates persistent buffers when it is constructed in `Worker.init_device`. Examples are input buffers and the MTP speculator's `hidden_states` (512 MiB on DeepSeek-V4-Flash with `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`). This happens before weights load and outside every sleep-mode pool, so `/sleep` keeps them.

These buffers can't simply be allocated later, because memory profiling already uses them. Instead, this PR constructs the model runner inside the `runtime` pool. #59158 offloads that pool on sleep and restores it at the same addresses on wake.

The cumem "one instance per process" guard in `_maybe_get_memory_pool_context(tag="weights")` used to assert that the allocator was completely empty. It now checks only weights-tagged memory, via a new optional `tag` argument to `get_current_usage` on the CUDA and XPU allocators. Runtime buffers allocated before the weights therefore don't trip it, and a second engine instance in the same process is still caught.

## Test Plan

- End-to-end on 4× GB300 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash (TP4 + EP4, MTP, CUDA graphs), on top of #59158:
  - memory after `/sleep`;
  - prompt logprobs before sleep and after each wake (level 1 twice, then level 2).
- Existing sleep-mode tests (`tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/`, `tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py`).

## Test Result

TP4 + EP4, auto MoE, on top of #59158. Memory per GPU after `/sleep`:

| | #59158 only | #59158 + this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Residual | 10487 MiB | **9975 MiB (−512 MiB)** |
| MTP speculator buffers | 512 MiB | 0 |
| `runtime` tag (offloaded) | 4704 MiB | 5218 MiB |

- **Startup:** clean; the weights-pool guard does not trip.
- **KV cache:** unchanged (13.04 M tokens both ways).
- **Correctness:** prompt logprobs are bit-identical to before sleep after both level-1 wakes. The level-2 round completes without errors; its output is garbage only because weights are discarded.
- **Timing:** sleep 12.1–12.3 s (#59158 only: 9.4–11.3 s). Wake 0.95–0.99 s.
- **Scope:** router-gate output and sampler buffers (about 170 MiB) are allocated after runner construction, so this PR does not cover them.

**Large model accuracy (DeepSeek-V4.1, TP8 over 2 GB300 nodes, `mp` backend, MTP off).** GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0.

| State | Unpatched | #59158 only | #59158 + this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Awake | 0.892 | 0.906 | 0.902 |
| Level-1 sleep, full wake | 0.899 | 0.905 | 0.897 |
| Level-1 sleep, selective wake | 0.902 | 0.896 | 0.898 |
| Memory while asleep, per GPU | 21035 MiB | 18583 MiB | 18583 MiB |

**GLM-5.3 (TP8 over 2 nodes, MTP on):**
- **Memory while asleep, per GPU:** 8847 MiB with #59158 only and **8655 MiB with this PR (−192 MiB)**, which is the MTP hidden-states buffer at hidden size 6144.
- **GSM8K:** awake 0.921, full wake 0.912, selective wake 0.909, level 2 + `reload_weights` 0.917, against unpatched 0.914 / 0.914 / 0.918 / 0.911.
- **Errors:** none.

- **No extra saving here, as expected.** With MTP off there is no speculator buffer to move, so memory while asleep is the same as with #59158 alone. The saving shown above comes from the MTP buffers.
- **Level-2 `reload_weights`** fails on unpatched vLLM for this model too (existing `layerwise.py` gap), so it is not compared.
- **Errors:** none.

---

title: [Doc] Sleep mode: what stays on the GPU
body:
## Purpose

Adds a "What stays on the GPU" section to the sleep mode docs. It covers:
- the sleep-mode tags and what sleep does with each;
- what cannot be released without restarting the process, and how to reduce it;
- the `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` default.

The table describes behavior after the related PRs land: #59156 (`workspace`), #59158 and #59162 (`runtime`), #59160 (graph pool and `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER`). Keep this PR in draft until they are merged.

## Test Plan

Docs only. Numbers come from DeepSeek-V4-Flash runs on 4x GB300.

## Test Result

Docs only. Below are the results with all four PRs applied together (#59156, #59158, #59160, #59162) on GB300. Every run is the same image with and without the PRs. GSM8K is 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0.

**Memory per GPU while asleep (level 1):**

| Model | Setup | Unpatched | All PRs | Saved |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | TP4 + EP, MTP, 1 node | 14029 MiB | 5161 MiB | **8868 MiB (63%)** |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | DP4 + EP4, auto MoE, fp8 KV | 14193 MiB | 4975 MiB | **9218 MiB (65%)** |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | DP4 + EP4, DeepGEMM MoE, fp8 KV | 14528 MiB | 4897 MiB | **9631 MiB (66%)** |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 | TP8, 2 nodes (`mp`) | 21035 MiB | 5819 MiB | **15216 MiB (72%)** |
| GLM-5.3 | TP8, 2 nodes (`mp`), MTP | 9449 MiB | 7405 MiB | **2044 MiB (22%)** |

**GSM8K accuracy (unpatched → all PRs):**

| State | V4-Flash | V4.1 | GLM-5.3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Awake | 0.948 → 0.946 | 0.892 → 0.904 | 0.914 → 0.917 |
| Level-1 sleep, full wake | 0.943 → 0.954 | 0.899 → 0.898 | 0.914 → 0.910 |
| Level-1 sleep, selective wake | 0.948 → 0.949 | 0.902 → 0.905 | 0.918 → 0.912 |
| Level-2 sleep, `reload_weights` | 0.017 → 0.021 * | 0.000 → 0.000 * | 0.911 → 0.919 |

\* `reload_weights` after a level-2 sleep is already broken for DeepSeek-V4 models on unpatched vLLM. `layerwise.py` logs "Failed to load weights" for the V4 attention, rotary and n-gram modules. This is unrelated to these PRs.

- **What remains (V4-Flash DP4, about 5.0 GiB per GPU):** mostly driver-side state that no allocator tag can release. CUDA graph executables take 1944 MiB and other memory charged during capture takes 1142 MiB; the rest is the CUDA context (390 MiB), local memory (480 MiB), kernel modules (about 300 MiB), NCCL buffers (108 MiB) and cuBLAS (68 MiB). Releasing the graph executables would mean destroying and recapturing the graphs on wake.
- **Serving performance while awake is unchanged** (DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4, `vllm bench serve`, random 1024/256 at concurrency 1–256 and 4096/512 at concurrency 32).
  - Throughput and TTFT/TPOT match unpatched within noise, both on a fresh server and after a sleep/wake cycle.
  - Throughput differs by up to ~45% between launches of the same code, because the FlashInfer MoE autotuner picks different tactics on each launch. Matched comparisons need 2–3 launches per arm.
  - On GB300 the allreduce is FlashInfer MNNVL, so #59160's custom-allreduce copy path is not exercised.
- **RL-style soak, 100 iterations per model:**
  - Qwen3-235B-A22B FP8 TP4+EP and DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4.
  - Each iteration runs a rollout of 64–256 concurrent requests, then a level-1 sleep; on about a third to a half of the iterations, another process fills ~270 GiB/GPU of the freed VRAM during the sleep. Wakes alternate full and selective, and every 25th iteration is level 2 + `reload_weights` (Qwen).
  - Probes match iteration 0 bit-exactly. GPU memory, host RSS and latency show no drift. Qwen3 also has a one-time +14 MiB after the first level-2 reload. 16,345/16,345 requests succeeded.
- Sleep and wake latencies are unchanged, and there were no errors.
- Unit tests pass for all PRs combined (`test_cumem.py`, `test_sleep_mode_backend.py`, `test_workspace.py`: 37/37).

title: [EPLB] Add the MoE Load Balancer policy: pluggable expert placement and replica routing
body:
## Purpose

Add an optional expert-parallel load-balancing backend to EPLB: `--eplb-config '{"policy": "mlb", ...}'` delegates expert **placement** (the EPLB rearrangement) and, optionally, **per-token replica routing** to the [MoE Load Balancer](https://github.com/xutizhou/moe_load_balancer) (`moe_load_balancer`), a framework-neutral library of load-balancing policies (DeepSeek EPLB hierarchical/global, LPLB, Waterfill for the shared expert, and UltraEP's online placement/quota refresh). vLLM keeps the mechanism, the library keeps the policies.

What the PR adds, all inactive unless `policy: "mlb"` is selected (the package is imported lazily; vLLM starts and runs unchanged without it):

- `vllm/distributed/eplb/policy/mlb.py`: the `mlb` EPLB policy (L1 placement) behind the existing `AbstractEplbPolicy` interface.
- `vllm/distributed/eplb/mlb_runtime.py`: the routing runtime (L2). A policy can answer per token with replica shares or with resolved physical ids; both go through the existing fused EPLB map-and-record Triton kernel in `router/base_router.py`, so load recording, the record gate and the padding mask are untouched. UltraEP's online refresh re-solves placement and per-replica quotas every N representative batches and moves the affected expert weights with a pairwise send/recv mover over the EPLB communicator (a symmetric-memory mover is available for single-host / multi-node-NVLink deployments).
- `--eplb-config` keys `l2_algorithm`, `init_placement_path`, `save_placement_path`: routing expression, and fit-once / serve-with-held-placement (the equivalent of SGLang's `--init-expert-location`).
- `VLLM_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS` / `shared_expert_fusion.py`: dispatch the shared expert through the EP all-to-all as one slot per rank instead of a replicated MLP, so a policy (Waterfill) can place it on the least-loaded rank. Off unless requested by the env var or by a policy that needs it.
- A DP-synced `uniform_decode_across_dp` flag on the forward context (one more row in the existing DP coordination all-reduce): a policy that issues a collective inside the forward must reach the same verdict on every rank, and the per-rank `uniform_decode` is exactly the wrong signal when a rank runs a dummy decode while its peers prefill. The dummy-run path replays the policy's per-step collective for the same reason (upstream already replays `eplb_step` there).
- `rank_imbalance` (per-layer peak-rank / mean-rank load) next to the existing `balancedness` in the EPLB log, since the latter reduces over layers rather than ranks.
- Two DeepEP knobs that came out of running EP16 across nodes: `VLLM_DEEPEP_RDMA_BUFFER_SIZE_MB` (size the RDMA buffer separately; DeepEP caps the NVL buffer when RDMA bytes are non-zero) and `VLLM_DEEPEP_HT_USE_MNNVL` (+ `VLLM_DEEPEP_V2_*_GBS`) for multi-node NVLink fabrics. Separable if preferred.
- Docs: a "MoE Load Balancer policy" section in `docs/serving/expert_parallel_deployment.md`.

Intrusiveness: the touched core paths (`fused_moe/layer.py`, `router/base_router.py`, `eplb_state.py`, `gpu_model_runner.py`, `dp_utils.py`, `forward_context.py`, `deepseek_v2.py` weight loading) are additive and guarded; with the default policy the fused router kernel compiles the same variant as before (the new constexpr flags are false), the DP all-reduce carries one extra int per rank, and the model runner's replay is skipped when no MLB routing is active.

Tuning knobs are read through `vllm.envs` (`VLLM_MLB_L1_ALGORITHM`, `VLLM_MLB_L2_ALGORITHM`, `MLB_ULTRAEP_*`); we intend to fold the `MLB_ULTRAEP_*` ones into `--eplb-config` fields in a follow-up and would welcome guidance on the preferred shape.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests (skip cleanly without `moe_load_balancer`): `tests/distributed/test_eplb_mlb_policy.py`, `tests/distributed/test_eplb_mlb_routing.py`, `tests/distributed/test_eplb_replica_shares_kernel.py` (fused router kernel with replica shares / resolved ids, no MLB needed), `tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py` (extended), plus the existing `test_eplb_algo.py`, `test_eplb_utils.py`; wired into the EPLB Algorithm CI step.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: ruff, ruff-format, typos, SPDX, torch.cuda-call check, markdownlint, test tethering, mypy pass.
- End-to-end, DeepSeek-V3 FP8, DeepEP high-throughput, DeepGEMM, eager, 1000 x 1024-token prompts per round at concurrency 256, `max_tokens=1`: (a) 8 x Hopper, TP1 x DP8, EP8, red16; (b) 2 x 8 Hopper, TP1 x DP16, EP16, red16/red32, placement recorded on one dataset and served on another (gsm8k -> mmlu -> gpqa -> gsm8k rotation).
- Greedy-decode consistency probe (48 prompts x 32 tokens, `temperature=0`) against plain vLLM, with a placement-only (held static placement) reference for the numeric floor.

## Test Result

**Static checks.** `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: every hook passes (ruff, ruff-format, typos, SPDX, torch.cuda-call check, markdownlint, Buildkite test tethering, mypy 3.10).

**Unit tests** (8 x Hopper, `moe_load_balancer` installed): `tests/distributed/test_eplb_mlb_policy.py test_eplb_mlb_routing.py test_eplb_replica_shares_kernel.py tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py test_eplb_algo.py test_eplb_utils.py` -> 581 passed, 1 skipped.

**Single node, DeepSeek-V3 FP8, TP1 x DP8, EP8, 16 redundant experts, gsm8k prompts, placement fitted on gsm8k and held** (this branch):

| Arm | tok/s | rank imbalance |
|---|---|---|
| plain vLLM (`--enable-eplb` off), three launches | 19.44k / 19.47k / 19.51k | - |
| Static EPLB on the fitted placement (earlier report, same protocol) | 20.51k | 1.213 |
| `policy: mlb`, UltraEP L1+L2, refresh every 8 batches, direct mover, synchronous apply | 22.13k | 1.051 |

Greedy-decode consistency (48 prompts x 32 tokens, `temperature=0`, identical texts): plain vLLM vs plain vLLM (two launches) 48/48; plain vs Static EPLB on the held placement 21/48; plain vs UltraEP 20/48; Static vs UltraEP 25/48. Any change of expert placement moves the agreement to about 20/48 (FP8 grouped-GEMM accumulation order); UltraEP sits at that floor and every divergence inspected is a plausible alternative continuation at a near-tie token.

**Two nodes, DeepSeek-V3 FP8, TP1 x DP16, EP16, DeepEP high-throughput, placement recorded on one prompt set and served on another (gsm8k -> mmlu -> gpqa -> gsm8k), 84 arms** (this branch's code minus the final polish):

| red | serving set | Static EPLB, stale placement | Static EPLB, own placement | best UltraEP arm from the stale placement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | mmlu | 34.87k / 1.370 | 38.81k / 1.093 | UltraEP+Waterfill i=8: 38.04k (98.0% of own) |
| 16 | gpqa | 33.96k / 1.452 | 39.18k / 1.107 | UltraEP+Waterfill i=1: 37.71k (96.3%) |
| 16 | gsm8k | 31.93k / 1.616 | 39.15k / 1.112 | UltraEP+Waterfill i=1: 38.00k (97.1%) |
| 32 | mmlu | 34.79k / 1.391 | 39.11k / 1.088 | UltraEP+Waterfill i=8: 38.92k (99.5%) |
| 32 | gpqa | 34.46k / 1.406 | 38.59k / 1.099 | UltraEP+Waterfill i=8: 38.59k (100.0%) |
| 32 | gsm8k | 32.24k / 1.626 | 38.62k / 1.105 | UltraEP+Waterfill i=8: 39.09k (101.2%) |

A stale placement costs Static EPLB 10-18%; from the same stale placement UltraEP recovers to 96-101% of the no-drift reference. Arms whose code path this PR does not change (plain vLLM, identity layout, Static, Uniform) reproduce an earlier run of the same protocol within +-3%. `MLB_ULTRAEP_MOVER=auto` across the two hosts takes the collective fall-back to the direct mover on every rank and completes its first refresh without hanging.

## Notes

- `use_async` must be `false` with `policy: "mlb"`; the config validation says so.
- The MLB package is not added to vLLM's requirements; it is an optional dependency installed by the operator (documented).

title: [Feature]: Allow hardware plugins to opt into Engram configuration
body:
Current proposal: remove both CUDA-alike gates directly, as implemented in #59171. The `supports_engram()` interface described below was the initial proposal and is no longer part of the PR. Model/layer and parallel validation remain in place.

### Feature, motivation and pitch

Expose `Platform.supports_engram()` so hardware plugins can opt into the native Engram configuration without replacing its validation.

On main at `30f5c01d4e`, both `EngramConfig.verify_model_config()` and `VllmConfig._resolve_and_verify_engram_config()` require `current_platform.is_cuda_alike()`. A non-CUDA/ROCm plugin implementing Engram therefore cannot use an explicit native `EngramConfig`; omitting the config also skips automatic defaults. Model validation runs before the plugin's `check_and_update_config()` hook.

This affects the Ascend integration in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/17427. It already reuses upstream Engram config, resolver and node-local DP groups, but needs a temporary model-validation patch and platform-side default creation solely to get past these device gates.

Proposed behavior:
- Add `Platform.supports_engram()`, returning `self.is_cuda_alike()` by default to preserve current CUDA/ROCm support and rejection on other built-in platforms.
- Use this capability in both explicit model validation and automatic default resolution.
- Let plugins with an Engram implementation override the capability; retain the supported-model, non-empty-layer and parallel-config checks.

### Alternatives

Removing both device gates would also unblock plugins, but would enable Engram config on every platform regardless of implementation support. A capability allows explicit opt-in. Keeping downstream monkey patches duplicates upstream validation and requires extra maintenance.

### Additional context

The Ascend PR targets vLLM `ced6857a`, where these gates use `is_cuda()`; current upstream main uses `is_cuda_alike()` and has the same plugin limitation. This request concerns configuration extensibility, not adding Ascend kernels or changing CUDA/ROCm execution.

Searched existing issues and open PRs for `supports_engram`, `engram platform`, `engram CUDA`, and `engram Ascend`; no matching capability change was found. This report was prepared with AI assistance.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Fix mamba prefill checkpoint block reservation and prompt-end eviction in align mode
body:
## Purpose
Enabling Mamba prefill checkpoint in the `align` mamba cache mode allows for the elimination of a second forward pass in prefill when the chunked context lengths are not multiples of the block size. In enabling prefill checkpointing for Kimi-K3 on ROCm (#58344), two issues were found where the scheduler and kv cache manager disagree on the block boundaries, causing wasted allocation and dropped cache that hurt prefix cache hits. This PR extracts the fixes to the core parts that are hardware independent out from the ROCm checkpoint enablement and addresses the following:

### 1. Surplus block reservation
The scheduler determines checkpoint positions from the prefill_end token
```
vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py's _mamba_block_aligned_split
prefill_end = max(request.num_prompt_tokens, request.num_tokens - 1)
...
checkpoint_position = get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position(
    prefill_end, self.hash_block_size, drop_eagle_block=self.use_eagle_block_drop,
)
...
use_internal_checkpoint = (...
    and is_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_valid(..., checkpoint_position=checkpoint_position, ...)
)
```
whereas the `MambaManager` uses a prefill chunk's end token `num_tokens`.
```
vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py's MambaManager.get_num_blocks_to_allocate()
checkpoint_position = get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position(
    num_tokens, self.block_pool.hash_block_size, self.drop_eagle_checkpoint_block,
)
...
# member methods that call
is_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_valid(..., checkpoint_position=checkpoint_position, ...)
...
```
As the `num_tokens`-derived `checkpoint_position` is always below the end of the prefill chunk, the `query_start < checkpoint_position < query_end` condition in `is_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_valid` is always True for MambaManager, and it allocates an additional block even for chunks that are in the middle of the requests. This makes MambaManager allocate blocks for mid-request chunks that the scheduler never plans as the scheduler only plans for blocks at the prompt-end chunks. These mid-request blocks are immediately discarded as transients, but they still consume and evict physical blocks that have held real prefix. Measured with AgentX workload at concurrency 64, these surplus block reservation can drop cache hit rate from 89% -> 49%.

This PR addresses this by using the same `prefill_end` as the scheduler to evaluate `checkpoint_position` in `MambaManager`, so that `query_start < checkpoint_position < query_end` is True only for the prompt-end chunk and checkpoint blocks are only allocated there where they're only required. This is only changed under `retention_interval == 0` where the surplus checkpoint blocks are truly redundant.

### 2. Dropped prompt-end checkpoint states (Superseded, fixed by #59146)
MambaManager's `_cache_partial_tail_block` decides whether a checkpoint block is mid-request by
```
vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py's MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block
if (
    retention_interval == 0
    and **num_tokens < request.num_prompt_tokens**
    and checkpoint_position != request.shared_prefix_boundary
):
    self.block_pool._maybe_evict_cached_block(checkpoint_block)
    return None
```
where `num_tokens` is rounded down to block size by the HybridKVCacheCoordinator
```
def _align_cacheable(self, num_tokens: int) -> int:
    if self.enable_partial_hash_hits:
        return num_tokens
    return round_down(num_tokens, self.scheduler_block_size)

def cache_blocks(self, request, num_computed_tokens):
    cached_num_computed_tokens = self._align_cacheable(num_computed_tokens)
    ...
```

This makes last chunk of a non-multiple-of-block-size prompt rounded down to below the prompt length, and, under retention_interval=0, its hash is then removed on the same step the kernel writes it. The next conversation turn then cannot find the checkpoint states at the prompt-end boundary, and the reusable prefix becomes the last boundary or to zero, causing prefix to be recomputed.

This PR addresses this issue by adding `_is_reachable_checkpoint` where it decides if a checkpoint belongs to a prompt-end chunk using checkpoint position instead of the rounded-down count.

## Test Plan

New unit tests are added for core partial prefix cache hits:

- `test_intermediate_chunk_checkpoint_reserved_only_under_dense_retention`: prefills a prompt in two chunks and checks that the mid-prompt chunk reserves a checkpoint block only under dense retention while the prompt-end chunk reserves one either way. Fails on main under retention_interval=0.
- `test_prompt_end_checkpoint_survives_block_aligned_cache_count`: prefills a prompt whose length is not a multiple of the block size at the default match unit and checks that the prompt-end checkpoint stays in the prefix cache and that a replay of the same prompt resumes from it. Fails on main for the unaligned lengths.

## Test Result

The added unit tests pass where they fail on main branch.

The performance impact of the two issues were measured together with the ROCm Kimi-K3 mamba checkpoint enablement #58344 on MI355X. In the following benchmarks and evaluations, #58344 only adds the enablement of prefix checkpoint for Kimi-K3 on ROCm, and the pre- and post-fixes for KV cache manager and scheduler are the distinction between the main branch and this PR.

AgentX benchmark runs were performed to reflect agentic workloads with prefix caching, and different conditions were set so that the two issues could surface individually.

The issue 1 "Surplus block reservation"'s cost surfaces under memory pressure when physical blocks holding real prefix caches get evicted to make space for mid-request transient blocks that get discarded immediately. For this, the concurrency=64 AgentX benchmark setting was used.

title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Guard cross-node symmetric-memory rendezvous with fabric support
body:
## Purpose

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59185.

On two B200 nodes without a multi-node NVLink (MNNVL) fabric, a TP=4 group with two GPUs per node can hang during communicator initialization and fail at the 1,800-second Gloo timeout. `SymmMemCommunicator` currently enters symmetric-memory rendezvous without checking whether the topology supports cross-node memory handles. An error on some ranks can leave other ranks blocked, so catching `RuntimeError` alone does not provide a safe fallback.

This change checks locality before allocating symmetric memory. Single-node groups retain the existing path; cross-node groups enter rendezvous only if every rank reports fabric support. The fabric probe returns false when unavailable or unsuccessful. CustomAllreduce's existing group-wide MNNVL gate also requires fabric support, since local multicast capability alone is insufficient.

The branch is based on upstream `main` at `3e2a7e74a556623ddee3a327299d7bf04055501e`. The previously tested patch was adapted to retain main's `_all_ranks_true` helper. Regression tests extend the existing distributed suites to cover non-fabric groups, partial fabric support, supported groups, and avoiding allocation/rendezvous when disabled.

Duplicate-work check on September 29, 2026: issue #59185 had no comments or open PR referencing it. An open-PR search for `SymmMemCommunicator fabric` returned #41834, which concerns DeepSeek V4 support on SM12x and does not modify the three communicator files changed here. The merged #53253 added CustomAllreduce gating but did not guard the separate `SymmMemCommunicator` rendezvous.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change and description (OpenAI Codex), building on an internal recorded experiments.

## Test Plan

Re-run the two-node B200 reproduction from #59185 against the unmodified base and this branch using the same pinned software and workload configuration. Verify that TP=4 (two GPUs per node) starts and completes model evaluation, and retain the TP=2 control (one GPU per node). Also exercise single-node and MNNVL-connected configurations; the prior experiment did not cover those paths.

The change adds one same-node probe during SymmMemCommunicator construction and one CPU MIN all-reduce for cross-node groups. Check startup behavior on supported topologies as well as fallback on unsupported ones. An unavailable FlashInfer fabric probe conservatively disables cross-node symmetric-memory fast paths.

## Test Result

| Configuration | Unmodified vLLM | Combined candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8, TP=4, two nodes × two B200 GPUs | Startup fails; workload ends after ~1,921 s, including the 1,800-second Gloo timeout | Startup and GSM8K 10% subset evaluation complete in ~455 s; accuracy 0.4545 |
| Nemotron Super V3 120B-A12B FP8, TP=2, two nodes × one B200 GPU | Completes; GSM8K subset accuracy 0.9697 | Completes; accuracy 0.9394 |

Those experiments used vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev573+ge97573215` and the same upstream base digest, `sha256:f75fec992c293dd41042745f8aa71bfdf12b188b6a01e0baf075e4bca5d297e5`, with separate node allocations. They tested both communicator changes together, once per arm and configuration, and measured total workload time rather than startup latency. The evaluation subset had 132 questions and no pass threshold; the TP=2 score difference is four questions. These results support the candidate's startup fix but do not establish accuracy equivalence, isolate either change, or validate this rebase. Single-node, MNNVL, TP=8, and NVFP4 coverage remain outstanding.

---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.

No new model, API, or configuration option is introduced; no documentation update is proposed.

title: [Refactor] Share workspace and model runner init between GPU and XPU workers
body:
## Purpose

`XPUWorker.init_device` copied the tail of `Worker.init_device`: DBO ubatch count, `init_workspace_manager(...)`, model runner construction and usage stats. The copy had already drifted. It does not pass the workspace lane count, so XPU with the V2 runner and DSpark speculative decoding gets a single workspace lane and fails the first time the draft path uses lane 1.

This PR:
- Moves that tail into `Worker._init_workspace_and_model_runner()`.
- Adds a `Worker._make_model_runner()` hook. The GPU version keeps the existing V1 / V2 / MM-encoder selection.
- Has `XPUWorker` override only `_make_model_runner()` to return `XPUModelRunner` / `XPUModelRunnerV2`, and call the shared method.

Out-of-tree workers that copied the old `init_device` tail keep working unchanged. To pick up the shared path they can override `_make_model_runner()` alone, but they must not also keep their copied tail, or the workspace would be initialized twice.

No behavior change on CUDA or ROCm. On XPU the only change is the lane count fix. Net −10 lines.

This also means follow-up changes to workspace or runner setup land in one place. For example, the sleep-mode PRs #59156 and #59162 currently have to edit both workers.

## Test Plan

- `tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py` (covers `_num_workspace_lanes`)
- pre-commit (ruff, mypy)
- A GB300 run with an unchanged GPU init path

## Test Result

- pre-commit passes (ruff, mypy, typos).
- GPU smoke test on GB300 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4, sleep mode enabled:
  - Startup, KV cache size and CUDA graph memory are identical to unpatched.
  - GSM8K is 0.950 awake, 0.948 after a level-1 wake and 0.955 after a selective wake.
  - Memory while asleep is 15181 MiB, against 15178 MiB unpatched.
  - `test_workspace.py` passes 11/11.
- No XPU hardware was available; the XPU path is covered by review and CI.
- Adversarial review by Codex and Kimi K3 found no blocker. Kimi's open question on `use_dspark()` is answered by `SpeculativeConfig.use_dspark()`, which is defined for every config.

---
This PR contains AI-assisted code (Claude Code); the commit carries a `Co-authored-by` trailer.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash cannot run on SM120 (RTX PRO 6000): compressed-layer page_block_size=32 has no FlashInfer sparse-MLA decode kernel instantiation (only pbs=64)
body:
### Your current environment

- Hardware: 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, 96GB), single node TP8
- vLLM: 0.30.1rc1.dev327+g9af952c55 (nightly, pip)
- FlashInfer: 0.7.0 (flashinfer-python + flashinfer-cubin + flashinfer-jit-cache sm120f+cu130, all three packages installed)
- Model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (official 476GiB mixed MXFP4/MXFP8 checkpoint)
- Config: TP8, `--language-model-only`, `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'`, `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash fails to start on SM120 with:

```
ValueError: SM120 sparse-MLA has no decode kernel for this shape: num_tokens=8,
num_heads=8, topk=128, d_qk=512, page_block_size=32, model_type=dsv4, extra_topk=0.
```

### Root cause analysis

V4.1's two-tier sparse attention gives each layer a `compress_ratio` (this checkpoint: `[0,0,2,2,...,2,1,1,1,1,1]`). vLLM computes the compressed-layer KV page block size as `attn_metadata.block_size // compress_ratio`, so ratio-2 layers get pbs = 64//2 = **32**.

FlashInfer's SM120 dispatch planner (`flashinfer/mla/_sparse_mla_sm120_plan.py`) hard-codes `_PAGE_BLOCK_SIZE = 64` and instantiates the dsv4 decode kernels **only** at pbs=64 (the error message itself lists `page_block_size=32` as unsupported).

There is **no single global block size that works**:
- global block_size=64 → ratio-2 compressed layers compute pbs=32 → this crash
- global block_size=128 → vLLM reports "No common block size for 64 (FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41: [128]; ...)" because the SM120 kernel set has no pbs=128 dsv4 instantiation either (only 64)

So the two-tier architecture (mixed ratios 1 and 2) is fundamentally incompatible with the current SM120 kernel instantiation set, which only covers pbs=64.

### Steps we already walked through to get this far (all gates passed)

1. `indexer_kv_dtype="mxfp4"` → rejected on SM120 ("requires Blackwell datacenter GPUs sm_10x"); switched to `"fp8"`.
2. `indexer_sparse_logits=true` → requires MXFP4 indexer cache; removed the flag.
3. `flashinfer_jit_cache` shim wheel (4KB) had to be installed with `--no-deps` in addition to the `sm120f` provider wheel (the provider wheel alone lacks the Python module `flashinfer_jit_cache.__version__`).
4. torch/torchaudio CUDA mismatch from the nightly upgrade → uninstalled torchaudio.
5. Applied #53425 (SM12x block size 64 for DeepSeek-V4) — but it only covers the `deepseek_v4` (V4) family; the `deepseek_v41` family has its own two-tier block-size chain.

A debug stack trace (added at the raise site) confirms the failing path: `deepseek_v41/attention.py::forward` → `nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py::_forward_prefill` → `flashinfer_trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4` with `page_block_size=32` derived from the compressed cache tensor shape.

### What is needed (either/or)

1. **FlashInfer**: add SM120 dsv4 decode kernel instantiation at pbs=32 (or 32 and 128), OR
2. **vLLM**: allow per-layer/per-cache block sizes so compressed layers can keep pbs=64 independently of the global block size.

Until then DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is effectively unusable on SM120/SM121 hardware (the official recipe only verifies H100/H200/B200/GB200-class GPUs).

### Environment details available

Full `collect_env` available on request; reproduction environment is a dedicated 8x PRO 6000 node we can keep available for testing a fix.

Thanks!

title: [Hisparse] Support HiSparse for QSA
body:
## Purpose

Support HiSparse for single-engine Qwen3.8-Flash QSA, whose full K/V heads differ from sparse MLA geometry. QSA can read selected history after its GPU pages are reclaimed, using the existing resident/hot/host policy.

The indexer's selection budget, logical positions and valid counts are preserved. Indexer caches, raw-key rings and recurrent state stay on GPU; no additional attention approximation is introduced.

## Changes

- Add full-row QSA geometry, BLNHC layout, TP ownership and host accounting.
- Connect writes and selected reads to residency/refill, including nonresident prefill and independent BF16/FP8 main and indexer formats.
- Preserve MTP selection reuse with stable selected-K/V storage and a private padding request map for native FULL replay and async execution.
- Preserve writable ownership across partial prefix hits, recompute, cancellation and cleanup.

NIXL/P-D and DCP are outside this PR.

## Usage

Initial eager TP2 example with a compatible checkpoint:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve "$QSA_MODEL" \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"bf16","hisparse_config":{}}' \
  --enforce-eager --no-async-scheduling \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-chunked-prefill \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":8}}'
```

Keep the hybrid cache manager enabled. Host capacity is logical per DP replica; physical allocation depends on TP ownership/alignment. 

## Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py
```

Coverage includes TP ownership, BF16/FP8 main and indexer formats, refill after page reuse, MTP selection reuse, CUDA graph replay, prefix reuse and cleanup. Targeted regressions, lint and mypy passed. A three-request startup check with TP2, MTP3, FULL_DECODE_ONLY and async scheduling passed, followed by graceful shutdown. The final upstream increment received compatibility review only; the startup check and model tests were not rerun after it.

**GSM8K: 197/200 with HiSparse off and 197/200 on**, with no question-level gains or losses. This 200-question subset includes one HiSparse-on response that reached the 4096-token limit and remained scored incorrect. 

## Preliminary performance

### Finite-wave benchmark

![Output throughput versus per-user token speed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c353faa0-673b-4df4-8ddb-4edf317256a4)

Each plotted point is one complete off/on pair with N=C requests; * marks a paired retry. Per-user speed is `1000 / mean TPOT(ms)`. Three additional paired repeats at the concurrency with the highest observed throughput in either mode give the following medians [min, max]:

| Input/output tokens | C | Off output tok/s | On output tok/s | Change | Mean TPOT off/on (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 20,000/10,000 | 64 | 4846.42 [4813.67, 4882.21] | 3838.20 [3819.87, 3888.61] | −20.80% | 11.954 / 15.070 |
| 32,000/8,000 | 128 | 3233.18 [3218.93, 3246.51] | 3651.65 [3608.98, 3741.73] | +12.94% | 14.809 / 28.302 |
| 60,000/10,000 | 32 | 2585.73 [2564.60, 2589.29] | 2074.85 [2049.17, 2078.34] | −19.76% | 10.471 / 13.062 |

### AIPerf

AIPerf 0.13.0 maintains client concurrency for 600 seconds, then drains requests. Each point is one preliminary run with exactly 32,000 input and 8,000 output tokens per request. Off/on therefore complete different request totals. Aggregate throughput includes drain; mean tok/s/user averages per-request reciprocal ITL, unlike the finite-wave chart's reciprocal mean TPOT.

| C | Requests off/on | Output tok/s off/on | Change | Mean tok/s/user off/on |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32 | 224 / 192 | 2926.49 / 2407.26 | −17.74% | 96.06 / 79.18 |
| 64 | 298 / 256 | 3482.59 / 3142.21 | −9.77% | 65.30 / 53.05 |
| 128 | 362 / 303 | 3490.70 / 3413.72 | −2.21% | 65.51 / 35.56 |
| 256 | 490 / 429 | 3541.53 / 3354.45 | −5.28% | 64.81 / 31.42 |

All reported measurements completed with zero request errors and full input/output lengths. Finite waves show a workload-dependent throughput/latency tradeoff; **AIPerf did not show a throughput gain**. Neither establishes gains at the default GPU KV budget or a maximum supported concurrency.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark configuration</summary>

Both modes use TP2 on a GB300-provisioned machine (device-reported NVIDIA L20B, 284,208 MiB/GPU), NVFP4 weights, BF16 main/index KV, FP32 SSM and BF16 pinned-CPU PLE on both ranks. GPU KV is 32 GiB/rank; HiSparse hot capacity is 4096 rows and the indexer budget stays 2048. Requested and resolved `async-scheduling` are enabled, with FULL_DECODE_ONLY, MTP off, prefix caching off and chunked prefill on. Maximum context/batched tokens: 70,000/8192. Streaming completions use temperature 0, seed 42 and `ignore_eos`.

| Parameter | Finite wave | AIPerf |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Client | vLLM bench | AIPerf 0.13.0 |
| Logical host pool / max sequences | 128 GiB / 128 | 256 GiB / 256 |
| Graph capture sizes | Powers of two, 1–128 | Powers of two, 1–256 |
| Workload | Three profiles above; N=C | 32k/8k; C=32,64,128,256; 600 s issuance, up to 900 s drain |
| Warmup | Separate 1024-input/32-output requests | C full-profile requests, excluded from measurement |

The paired GPU byte budgets match, but startup hybrid-group capacity estimates differ: 2,349,200 tokens off versus 2,273,034 on. These are not measured admission ceilings. Python 3.12.3, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Torch compile mode 0; FA2 fallback warnings were observed. The short finite-wave warmup may include lazy compilation in measured timings. Validation used prebuilt native extensions and does not establish a clean build with all dependency constraints satisfied.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Latency, resource and transfer observations</summary>

AIPerf values below are off/on. Running includes prefill; client concurrency is not active decode concurrency. Gauge maxima are sampled within the profiling window, including drain and excluding warmup.

| C | Mean ITL (ms) | Mean TTFT (s) | GPU KV peak (%) | Running max | Waiting max |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32 | 10.425 / 12.653 | 3.978 / 4.986 | 59.153 / 56.230 | 32 / 32 | 27 / 26 |
| 64 | 15.633 / 19.186 | 12.443 / 8.313 | 100 / 89.976 | 64 / 64 | 54 / 57 |
| 128 | 15.717 / 31.001 | 129.610 / 23.027 | 100 / 90.107 | 64 / 128 | 114 / 117 |

Full-window D2H counts and GPU VRAM peaks are unavailable for both protocols; strict-window finite-wave KV peaks and running/waiting counts cannot be reconstructed. title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Enable AITER fused shared experts on gfx950
body:
## Purpose

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` is silently ignored for GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`): `Glm5NextMoE` builds `FusedMoE` with `n_shared_experts=None`, so each of the 42 MoE layers still runs the shared expert as a separate MLP (two FP8 block-scale GEMMs, a clamped SiLU and a quant) and adds it to the routed output.

This PR wires the flag up the way `DeepseekV2MoE` does:

- **MoE:** when `resolve_layer_fused_shared_expert()` allows it, `Glm5NextMoE` drops the separate MLP and passes `n_shared_experts` / `fuse_shared_experts` to `FusedMoE`, so the shared expert runs as one more expert inside the AITER fused MoE (`E=289, topk=9`). The routed weights keep `routed_scaling_factor` and the shared slot gets 1.0, so the output is the same `shared + routed` sum as before.
- **Loading:** in both the target and the MTP draft model, the checkpoint's `mlp.shared_experts.*` tensors (FP8 scales included) load into expert slot `n_routed_experts`. `is_model_fused_shared_expert_compatible()` keeps fusion all-or-nothing, and more than one shared expert raises.
- **Gate:** AITER has tuned configs for the fused shape only on gfx950 at TP4 and TP8 (ROCm/aiter#5735, shipped in AITER v0.1.23, already in vLLM's ROCm image since #58867). Like DeepSeek-V4's shared-expert gate, `_fused_shared_experts_tuned()` allows fusion only there, and only without data, prefill context or expert parallelism, which change the per-rank shape. Anywhere else the flag logs a one-time warning with the reason, and the shared experts stay a separate MLP.

Nothing changes unless the flag is set on gfx950 at TP4 or TP8: it defaults to off, and `resolve_layer_fused_shared_expert()` returns False on non-ROCm platforms. gfx942 will follow in a separate PR once its rows (ROCm/aiter#5953) ship; without them the fused MoE would run untuned kernels (4289 µs vs 3033 µs for one 16K-token MoE call on MI325X).

## Test Plan

gfx950 (MI350X), `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` FP8, on the stock ROCm nightly `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-0cbac6cd1305f710e12193596b27488397bcb205` (AITER v0.1.23) with no patches besides this PR. Flag-on and flag-off runs use the same image and differ only in the flag. Perf ran as three back-to-back sweeps on the same GPUs (flag on, off, on), with gsm8k after each.

```bash
# Flag off: VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0
# MTP runs add: --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 AITER_LOG_TUNED_CONFIG=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --max-model-len 262144 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code \
  --compilation-config '{"custom_ops": ["all"]}'

for c in 2 4 6 8 10 12 16; do
  vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 131072 \
    --random-output-len 1024 --num-prompts 20 --num-warmups 2 --max-concurrency $c
done

# lm_eval 0.4.13, all 1319 questions
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,timeout=3600,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=16384

pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py
```

Perf, gsm8k and MTP ran at [10a457c](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/10a457c764afe1274f4b93495d9833a3c73329d1), when the gate checked only the GPU (TP4 passes the full gate too). The gate runs and unit tests ran at [3c2d001](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/3c2d001f37069274f941d8fe4a95e2ff6c5c79e8), which has the same three files as the current head (18fa78d).

## Test Result

With the flag on, TPOT drops 6-9% at concurrency 2-4 and by up to 3% at 6-16, while gsm8k and MTP acceptance are unchanged.

**Perf (TP4).** "on" is the mean of the two flag-on sweeps, which agree within 1.4 points of throughput at every concurrency. TTFT is unchanged within noise: every run is within 3.5% of flag off. No request failed, and every request generated all 1024 output tokens.

| concurrency | output tok/s, off → on | TPOT (ms), off → on |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 101.8 → 106.5 (+4.6%) | 13.06 → 12.28 (-6.0%) |
| 4 | 133.2 → 142.3 (+6.8%) | 19.15 → 17.43 (-9.0%) |
| 6 | 149.8 → 152.0 (+1.5%) | 24.84 → 24.53 (-1.3%) |
| 8 | 160.8 → 165.8 (+3.1%) | 31.32 → 30.71 (-2.0%) |
| 10 | 178.2 → 179.1 (+0.5%) | 37.92 → 37.76 (-0.4%) |
| 12 | 180.3 → 182.3 (+1.1%) | 42.08 → 41.32 (-1.8%) |
| 16 | 180.8 → 185.7 (+2.7%) | 49.30 → 47.80 (-3.0%) |

<details>
<summary>Per-sweep numbers</summary>

| concurrency | tok/s off | tok/s on (run 1 / run 2) | TPOT off (ms) | TPOT on (run 1 / run 2) | mean TTFT off (s) | mean TTFT on (run 1 / run 2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 101.8 | 106.5 / 106.5 | 13.06 | 12.27 / 12.28 | 6.75 | 6.67 / 6.67 |
| 4 | 133.2 | 141.9 / 142.6 | 19.15 | 17.47 / 17.39 | 11.13 | 10.97 / 10.91 |
| 6 | 149.8 | 152.1 / 151.9 | 24.84 | 24.52 / 24.53 | 12.56 | 12.46 / 12.48 |
| 8 | 160.8 | 164.7 / 166.9 | 31.32 | 31.00 / 30.41 | 15.41 | 14.97 / 14.90 |
| 10 | 178.2 | 178.8 / 179.4 | 37.92 | 37.43 / 38.09 | 18.46 | 18.76 / 17.91 |
| 12 | 180.3 | 182.5 / 182.0 | 42.08 | 41.01 / 41.63 | 21.72 | 21.92 / 21.62 |
| 16 | 180.8 | 185.8 / 185.6 | 49.30 | 47.80 / 47.80 | 31.80 | 31.65 / 31.76 |

</details>

**Accuracy.** gsm8k strict-match / flexible-extract is 0.9757 / 0.9750 with the flag off, and 0.9712 / 0.9704 and 0.9735 / 0.9719 with it on. Each run's standard error is about ±0.0045, so accuracy is unchanged.

**Fused path.** `AITER_LOG_TUNED_CONFIG=1` shows every fused-MoE lookup is `(E=289, topk=9)` with the flag on and `(E=288, topk=8)` with it off. Flag-on lookups with 4, 8 and 1024-16384 tokens hit the gfx950 rows from ROCm/aiter#5735; the other decode sizes (1-2 and 16-512 tokens) have no tuned row in either arm and use AITER's defaults.

**MTP (k=5).** The draft model's MoE layer is fused too (every lookup in the flag-on run is `E=289, topk=9`), and acceptance from the engine's spec-decode counters over the gsm8k run is unchanged, within 0.006 at every position.

| | flag off | flag on |
|---|---|---|
| gsm8k strict-match / flexible-extract | 0.9727 / 0.9712 | 0.9742 / 0.9727 |
| draft acceptance rate | 63.66% | 63.56% |
| mean acceptance length (max 6) | 4.18 | 4.18 |

Without this PR's `mtp.py` change, MTP with fusion fails at load with `KeyError: model.layers.45.mtp_block.mlp.shared_experts.down_proj.weight`.

**Gate.** Only TP4 and TP8 fuse. At TP8, lookups with 8, 32, 128, 256, 512, 2048 and 16384 tokens hit the gfx950 TP8 rows.

| flag on | shared experts | fused-MoE lookups | gsm8k strict-match / flexible-extract |
|---|---|---|---|
| TP4 | fused | `E=289, topk=9` | 0.9704 / 0.9704 |
| TP8 | fused | `E=289, topk=9` | 0.9765 / 0.9757 |
| TP4 + `--enable-expert-parallel` | separate MLP; warns "expert parallelism is enabled" | `E=72, topk=8` (72 local experts per rank) | not run |
| TP4 + `--data-parallel-size 2` | separate MLP; warns "data_parallel_size is 2" | `E=288, topk=8` | not run |

On gfx942 (4x MI325X, at 10a457c, with MTP) the flag only logs the warning: every lookup stays `(E=288, topk=8)`, and gsm8k strict-match (0.9712 on, 0.9750 off) and draft acceptance (68.15% on, 67.96% off) are unchanged.

Unit tests: all 95 in `test_fused_shared_expert.py` pass, covering glm5_next in `test_models_fse_init`, the gate across GPU, TP, DP, PCP and EP, and the loader's shared-expert slot.

title: [Bugfix] Don't unmap cuMem allocations freed while asleep
body:
## Purpose

`my_free()` in `csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp` always calls `unmap_and_release()` on the handle returned by the Python free callback. For an allocation that is asleep, `sleep()` has already unmapped it and released the physical handle, so freeing a cuMem-pool tensor while asleep double-unmaps it. The driver error is left in the global `error_code`, so the next `create_and_map` (e.g. `wake_up()`) or cuMem allocation fails with that stale error. This happens on engine teardown while asleep, or when a pool tensor is freed during sleep. It becomes more frequent once CUDA graph pools are cuMem-backed (#59160).

Fix (CUDA path only; the ROCm path already skips an asleep allocation via an empty chunk list):
- `unmap_and_release()` sets `*p_memHandle = 0` after a successful release;
- `my_free()` skips `unmap_and_release()` for a zero handle and only frees the address reservation.

No Python change is needed: `_python_free_callback` already pops the entry, drops the CPU backup and returns the handle. The Python-only alternative, remapping physical memory before the free so the C++ unmap succeeds, can OOM when a colocated trainer holds the VRAM freed by sleep.

**Related:**
- Fixes item 2 of #36651: `my_free` on allocations already released by `sleep()`.
- #46203 fixed the same double unmap/release on the ROCm path by tracking asleep allocations. This is the CUDA counterpart.
- #46054 proposed the same zero-handle idea and was closed because the ROCm fix had landed; the CUDA path stayed unfixed.

## Test Plan

New `test_free_while_asleep` in `tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py` (discard and offload variants): sleep, free a pool tensor while asleep by releasing the pools with `release_pools()` (as engine shutdown does), then check that the pointer is untracked, the CPU backup is dropped, no memory is remapped, and `wake_up()` succeeds with the other tensors intact.

```
pytest tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py -k free_while_asleep
```

## Test Result

GB300, torch 2.13.0+cu130, extension rebuilt from this branch:
- **`test_cumem.py`:** 14/14 pass, including `test_free_while_asleep[discard]` and `[offload]`.
- **After the `release_pools()` test change:** the 7 non-LLM tests pass on this branch, and the 9 non-LLM tests pass with this PR applied on top of #59156, which stores a list of pools per tag. With the unpatched extension both new cases still fail with the same error. The test no longer depends on the layout of `allocator_and_pools`.
- **Unpatched extension:** both new cases fail at `wake_up()` with `CUDA Error: invalid argument at csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp:258`, from the stale `error_code` left by the double unmap.
- **End to end:** DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 with cuMem graph pools (#59160).
  - Setup: put the engine to sleep, fill all but 511 MiB of VRAM from another process, then shut the engine down (`--shutdown-timeout 60`).
  - Unpatched: 4× `CUDA Error: invalid argument`.
  - Remapping in Python before free: 4× `out of memory`.
  - With this fix: a clean teardown.

---

AI assistance was used to prepare this change; I reviewed the diff.

### Re-check on current main (`bdd31c31d`), GB300 (rebased; test-only conflict in `test_cumem.py` resolved by keeping both sides)

Re-checked on main bdd31c31d (rebased: the only conflict was the insertion point in
test_cumem.py next to the new #59156/#59158/#59160 tests; both kept), 4x GB300,
torch 2.13.0+cu130, extension rebuilt from this branch:
- test_cumem.py: 23/23 pass, 3 runs. With main's extension (shipped .so and a rebuild
  from main's csrc) both test_free_while_asleep cases fail at wake_up() with
  "CUDA Error: invalid argument at csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp:258".
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + MTP, --enable-sleep-mode, --shutdown-timeout 60: SIGTERM while
  asleep gives 4x "CUDA Error: invalid argument at cumem_allocator.cpp:258" (one per
  worker) on main in all 3 launches and 0 with this PR. Asleep memory (11321 MiB/GPU),
  wake time (1.26-1.34 s) and outputs (3 sleep/wake cycles, 28/28 greedy and 28/28
  seeded top-k/top-p identical to the awake reference) are unchanged.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Keep text after tool calls in non-streaming engine parsing
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59218.

`ParserEngine` defers text that follows a tool call to the next streaming delta, so a delta never mixes content and tool calls. `_single_pass_parse` never flushed it, so non-streaming responses lost text after and between tool calls (qwen3_coder, qwen3_xml, glm45, minimax_m2, ...), while streaming returned it.

This flushes it at the end of `_single_pass_parse` and removes the Inkling override that did the same thing for Inkling only.

In #59218 I also asked whether some models should drop that text instead (Rust minimax_m2 does). This PR keeps it, like streaming and Inkling already do. Parsers that drop it on purpose, like DeepSeek V4 (`test_trailing_content_dropped_consistently`), are not affected. Happy to change direction if you prefer.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/parser tests/tool_parsers --ignore=tests/parser/cohere
```

(`tests/parser/cohere` needs `cohere_melody`, not installed here.)

New `TestContentAroundToolCalls` in `tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3.py` checks that `parse()` keeps text after and between tool calls and matches streaming.

## Test Result

The 2 new tests fail on main and pass with this PR. The rest of the suite is unchanged: same failures before and after (gated tokenizers and similar, unrelated), 6715 passed. pre-commit clean.

Also checked against a real server (`vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`, output forced with `structured_outputs`): the repro from the issue now returns `'Done.'` in non-streaming, same as streaming.

Written with help from Claude Code; I reviewed it and ran the tests.

title: [Spec Decode] Allow MTP draft config transformation at the load boundary
body:
## Purpose

Replicated Ascend MTP uses PCP=1 for draft execution while retaining the physical EP worker topology. Passing that execution view through validated draft overrides can incorrectly reject TP1/PCP8 with EPLB, or DCP configurations that rely on PCP ranks.

Add an optional `config_transform` to `load_eagle_model`, applied after draft overrides and PP-safe loader configuration, immediately before model construction. Extract the MTP loading call into `_load_draft_model` so platforms can use this boundary without duplicating weight/top-k sharing. Default callers keep the existing behavior. The companion Ascend change (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/17771) supplies the execution-view conversion; this PR alone does not change Ascend configuration handling.

## Test Plan

With the companion Ascend patch, run `pytest -q tests/ut/worker/test_mtp_pcp_speculator_v2.py`. Its 25 new cases exercise five TP/PCP/DCP combinations and draft backend/cache/PP loader overrides using real validated configurations, stopping at the model-construction boundary.

Before marking ready: rerun that suite and functional serving on the final paired revisions; cover the default no-transform path as well.

## Test Result

- This clean upstream port: Python syntax, Ruff check/format check and `git diff --check` passed.
- Earlier paired development checkout with this fix: 84 targeted unit tests and 39 CPU logic checks passed. These are not results for this exact rebased HEAD.
- Earlier Ascend A3 eager run: TP1/PCP8, EP, MTP3, async EPLB, DeepSeek-V4-Flash W4A8; 11/11 requests completed, all three draft acceptance positions advanced, and 23 EPLB commits included 18 nonzero-transfer cycles. No runtime errors in the successful run.
- The latest upstream port has not been rerun end-to-end. Graph mode, full accuracy and performance equivalence remain unverified. Keep draft pending paired validation.

title: [Bug] DeepEP v2 IMA due to GDAKI context ABI mismatch when using the cu134-nightly image
body:
The GDAKI context changes from 72 to 88 bytes going from NCCL 2.30.4 to 2.30.7, and the 88 byte layout is incompatible with the Spectrum-X version SPCX 1.4.0.

* The cu134-nightly image has HPCX 2.50 and SPCX 1.4.0
* Upgrading to HPCX 2.51 and SPCX 1.5.0 would fix this

Looks like upgrading from:
`nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda-dl-base:26.08-cuda13.4-devel-ubuntu24.04`
To:
`nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda-dl-base:26.09-cuda13.4-devel-ubuntu24.04`
will resolve the issue as the latter has HPCX 2.51

## Summary

DeepEP v2 dispatch faults on the first multi-node call when NCCL 2.30.7 loads the Spectrum-X GIN plugin in the tested image. The same 16-rank, model-free dispatch/combine test passes with NCCL's internal `GIN_IB_GDAKI` backend, in both direct and hybrid modes. This affects both the merge-base and PR #57991; it is not a regression caused by that PR.

The plugin/device GDAKI context ABI is mismatched. The installed NCCL 2.30.7 headers make `ncclGinGdakiGPUContext` 88 bytes. Disassembly of the loaded Spectrum-X plugin shows that its typed `ncclCudaMemcpyAsync<ncclGinGdakiGPUContext>` copies `count * 72` bytes, and `ncclGinGdakiCreateContext` indexes the context array with stride `0x48` (72). The DeepEP CUDA JIT uses the installed 88-byte layout to index the same array. A CUDA core shows a null GDAKI queue pointer followed by an atomic access at address `0x4a0` (`doca_gpu_dev_verbs_reserve_wq_slots`).

This is a dependency ABI problem exposed by vLLM's `deepep_v2` backend. The proper fix is a compatible Spectrum-X plugin and NCCL backend-version handling. vLLM could also provide an explicit, early selection of the internal GDAKI backend or fail with a useful compatibility error before launching DeepEP kernels.

## Environment

- Four nodes, 4 × H200 each; 16 ranks total; InfiniBand.
- `docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:4a46ea7e4aff9d963566452e8b5545eaf8fb46f4782217af685f17a9b1f34818`.
- Torch `2.15.0.dev20260909+cu134`, NCCL `2.30.7`, DeepEP `2.0.0+local`, NVSHMEM `3.7.2`.
- Plugin: `/opt/hpcx/nccl_spectrum-x_plugin/lib/libnccl-net.so.0.0.0`, SPCX `1.4-0`, `ncclGinPlugin_v13`, ELF Build ID `eead9869e4d941db385491de7234dba96f68698c`.
- vLLM comparison: DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP=1, DP=16, EP=16, `--all2all-backend deepep_v2`, both PR #57991 and its merge base.

## Reproducer and observed result

Run 4 nodes × 4 GPU ranks under `torch.distributed.run` with DeepEP v2's `ElasticBuffer`. Each rank dispatches 32 BF16 tokens, hidden size 4096, top-k 6, to six experts on the next rank, then combines and checks exact equality with six times the input. Use `num_experts=256`, `num_max_tokens_per_rank=32`, `use_fp8_dispatch=False`, and try both `allow_hybrid_mode=False` and `True`. Initialize a NCCL process group and set `TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0`, `EP_NIC_NAME=ibp0`, `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`, `NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,NET`. Include the Spectrum-X plugin directory in `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.

| GIN selection | Direct mode | Hybrid mode |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default external `SPCX_GIN` | First dispatch: CUDA illegal memory access | First dispatch: CUDA illegal memory access |
| Internal `GIN_IB_GDAKI` via settings below | Exact dispatch/combine passes on all 16 ranks | Exact dispatch/combine passes on all 16 ranks |

The validated workaround uses these settings together on every rank before NCCL initialization:

```sh
export NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=none
export NCCL_GIN_PLUGIN=none
export NCCL_RMA_PLUGIN=none
export NCCL_GIN_TYPE=3
```

NCCL logs confirm `GIN_IB_GDAKI type 3` and GPU Direct RDMA. The four settings were tested as a set; individual necessity has not been established.

## ABI and core evidence

- [NCCL v2.30.4 GDAKI header](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/blob/v2.30.4-1/src/include/nccl_device/gin/gdaki/gin_gdaki_device_host_common.h): 72-byte context. [NCCL v2.30.7 GDAKI header](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/blob/v2.30.7-1/src/include/nccl_device/gin/gdaki/gin_gdaki_device_host_common.h): adds `last_issued_get` and `last_visible_get`, making it 88 bytes. Both define `NCCL_GIN_GDAKI_VERSION` as `200`.
- In the loaded plugin's `ncclCudaMemcpyAsync<ncclGinGdakiGPUContext>`, addresses `0x501e5` and `0x501f4` compute `count * 9 * 8` as the `cudaMemcpyAsync` byte count. `ncclGinGdakiCreateContext` uses `imul $0x48` to index contexts. Its device handle stores GDAKI type 3/backend version 200 (`0xc800000003`).
- CUDA core dumps in direct and hybrid modes report `Warp MMU Fault` at 64-bit atomic address `0x4a0` inside `deep_ep::elastic::{dispatch_impl,hybrid_dispatch_impl}`. Line information maps the operation to GDAKI/DOCA work-queue slot reservation, which requires a valid `gdqp`. The direct-kernel disassembly loads a null queue base.
- The system and Python-package NCCL libraries have identical SHA256 (`618968ee277041751512e619190132a9bdf351c3ce7129c73484f6ef441ad692`), ruling out a two-library mismatch.
- [NCCL's GIN developer guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/blob/master/plugins/gin/README.md#version-compatibility) says backend version should change with shared structure formats and plugins should check/adapt or fail gracefully. The unchanged value `200` prevents that check here.

This is distinct from #58365, whose illegal access is a vLLM `ep_gather` int32 output-offset overflow. This reproducer does not run a model or `ep_gather`.

## Requested behavior

1. Make a known compatible internal GDAKI selection available early for `deepep_v2`, before NCCL communicators initialize, without requiring operators to discover the four-variable workaround.
2. If practical, diagnose incompatible external GIN/plugin combinations before dispatch and emit an actionable error. NCCL's unchanged backend version means a generic vLLM-side layout check cannot be inferred from `backendVersion` alone.
3. Coordinate the underlying ABI/version correction with NCCL/Spectrum-X plugin maintainers. A plugin rebuilt for the 88-byte layout or a truly versioned compatibility layer is needed for the external path.

Source-backed root-cause analysis and full logs are retained locally; the proprietary plugin itself was not rebuilt, so a rebuilt-plugin validation is still outstanding.

title: [Attention][MLA] Support fp8_ds_mla KV cache for NoPE-512 models on SM90
body:
## Purpose

This supersedes #55543 by @Leoyzen, who is kept as co-author. It enables the `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache on SM90 for rope-free sparse-MLA models with head_size 512, such as GLM-5.3-Flash, through `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`.

On H100, plain `fp8` on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (with the fix from #55222) holds more tokens. FlashMLA is still clearly faster at long-context decode: up to +31% output throughput and −29% TPOT at 16k input (see the benchmarks below). The PR adds FlashMLA as an opt-in with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`. Default backend selection doesn't change.

The idea is the same as in #55543: keep the DeepSeek 656B row and leave the RoPE slot at zero. This version keeps all of the logic inside the backend.

**How it works**
- **Cache write:** nothing changes. `concat_and_cache_mla` already zero-fills the RoPE slot when `pe_dim == 0` .
- **Query:** `FlashMLASparseImpl` sets `q_head_size = kv_lora_rank + 64` for NoPE on `fp8_ds_mla`.
  - Its q workspaces are sized from `q_head_size`.
  - `forward_mqa` zero-pads the query to that width, so q_pe · 0 = 0.
  - This covers the tuple path, the mixed and prefill paths, and DCP, where the gathered query arrives unpadded.
- **Dense-MHA prefill:** the impl sets `supports_dense_mha_prefill = False` for this layout, because the dense prefill workspace is `kv_lora_rank` wide and cannot hold the 576-wide rows. The SM120 FlashInfer impl does the same.
  - #55543 left this path on, where the FA prefill backend would see a 320-wide head.
  - `AttentionImpl.supports_dense_mha_prefill` drops `ClassVar` so it can be set per instance.
- **Backend selection:**
  - `FLASHMLA_SPARSE.supports_combination` now accepts `fp8_ds_mla` for SM90 NoPE-512.

**Compared with #55543**
- Removed:
  - the global zero buffer
  - the string check on the backend name
  - the model and wrapper hooks in `mla_attention.py`, `sparse_mla_attention.py`, `mla.py` and the glm5next attention
  - the hard-coded insert index in `cuda.py`
- The test fixtures compute the fp8_ds_mla row size as `kv_lora_rank + 16 + 128`, since the RoPE slot is always present.

## Duplicate check

- #55543 is the original PR and is superseded by this one.
- #58892 changes the SM90 backend priority for bf16 NoPE; this PR is orthogonal to it.
- #55222 fixes plain `fp8` on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90`. It is a different cache format and backend, and the two PRs complement each other.
- #58305 and #53969 are SM120-only.

## Benchmarks (H100, GLM-5.3-Flash, TP8)

- **FI** is `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90`, with the #55222 plan-dtype fix applied.
- **FlashMLA** is `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla` on `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` (this PR).
- Both use the same code and differ only in that flag.
- MTP is off. The workload is `vllm bench serve` with random data and `--ignore-eos`.
- Prompts per run: 16 at C=1, 32 at C=8, 128 at C=32.

**Long context: 16k in / 256 out**

| C | out tok/s FI → FlashMLA | TPOT mean (ms) FI → FlashMLA | TTFT mean (ms) FI → FlashMLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 95 → 102 (+7%) | 6.11 → 5.94 | 1128 → 1001 |
| 8 | 257 → 337 (**+31%**) | 20.5 → 14.6 (**−29%**) | 2717 → 2340 |
| 32 | 347 → 414 (**+19%**) | 74.4 → 62.4 (−16%) | 4552 → 3782 |

**Short context: 1k in / 128 out**

| C | out tok/s FI → FlashMLA | TPOT mean (ms) FI → FlashMLA | TTFT mean (ms) FI → FlashMLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 144 → 146 | 6.05 → 5.92 | 123 → 122 |
| 8 | 685 → 706 (+3%) | 9.09 → 8.67 | 340 → 349 |
| 32 | 1241 → 973 (−22%) | 21.8 → 24.9 | 518 → 1039 |

**KV capacity:** 3.63M tokens with FI vs 2.83M with FlashMLA. The ratio is 1.28, which is the 512B vs 656B row size.

**Trade-off:**
- FlashMLA wins long-context decode.
- FI holds 28% more tokens and does better on short prompts at high concurrency. The C=32 short-prompt gap is most likely prefill; it is not profiled yet.
- The numbers above are single runs.

## Test Plan / Results (H100)

- `tests/v1/attention/test_flashmla_nope_sm90_backend_selection.py`: 34 passed.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k decode_correctness`: 168 passed, 1176 skipped. This includes the new `glm53_flash_nope` case on `fp8_ds_mla` and the DeepSeek regression cases.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k ds_mla`: 3 passed, 5 skipped. The skips are for other architectures or nvfp4.
- `pre-commit` passes, including mypy.
- **Accuracy:** GLM-5.3-Flash, TP8, MTP with 5 spec tokens, GSM8K 5-shot on all 1319 questions.

  | kv cache | backend | GSM8K |
  |---|---|---|
  | fp8_ds_mla (this PR) | FLASHMLA_SPARSE | 0.918 |
  | fp8 (+ #55222 fix) | FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90 | 0.913 |

**Not covered:** HiSparse, and DCP end to end. The DCP padding path is checked only by reading the code.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to rework the original PR, write the tests and run the benchmarks and evaluations. I reviewed every changed line and the results.
