title: [ROCm] Enable expert parallelism for AITER Triton W4A16 MoE
body:
### Summary
Enables expert parallelism for the monolithic AITER Triton W4A16 MoE (`AiterW4A16ExpertsMonolithic`). Previously `aiter_triton_kernel_w4a16_moe_forward` dropped `expert_map`, so under `--enable-expert-parallel` the kernel indexed the rank-local weight shard with global expert ids → memory-access fault; the backend was also rejected by `_supports_parallel_config`.

Changes (ROCm-only path):
- Thread `expert_map` to both `moe_gemm_a16w4` calls (kernel remaps the weight id and early-returns non-local experts).
- Build a per-gate validity mask from `routing_data.topk_ids` and pass it as `gate_valid` so the top-k combine skips non-local gates (no output zero-fill).
- Lift the `#57866` EP reject for W4A16 (naive EP: allow `use_ep`, still reject all2all / eplb / dp>1).

**Depends on** the AITER change [ROCm/aiter#5863](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5863) (`expert_map` support in `moe_gemm_a16w4` + `RoutingData.topk_ids`). Draft until that merges and the pinned AITER is bumped.

### Not a duplicate
No open PR enables EP for the AITER Triton W4A16 monolithic MoE (checked `aiter w4a16 expert parallel`, `aiter_mxfp4_w4a16`, `W4A16 expert parallel monolithic`).

### Test
gfx950 (MI355X), TP=8, `--enable-expert-parallel`, `--moe-backend aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16`, ISL/OSL 1024/1024. Pre-change: mem-access fault at init; post-change: boots clean.

`lm_eval` gsm8k (5-shot, limit 200, flexible-extract):
- gpt-oss-120b: 0.905
- DeepSeek-V4-Pro: 0.955

Output token throughput (tok/s) @ conc 1/8/32/64/128:
- gpt-oss-120b (16/128 local/global experts): 246 / 1359 / 3640 / 5554 / 8491
- DeepSeek-V4-Pro (48/384): 51 / 277 / 615 / 874 / 1219

### AI assistance
This change was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code) and reviewed by the submitter.

title: [KV Offload] Preserve packed layouts for layer-wise KV cache
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Let built-in CPU KV offloading retain the allocator's compatible packed layout
for layer-wise recipes. Fourth follow-up: #56155 -> #56156 -> #56116 -> this PR.
Related RFC: #57445.

## Claims

- Avoid forcing the default `LBHNC` connector layout for layer-wise recipes,
  allowing compatible packed attention/state-cache allocation.
- Reuse existing packed-row transfers for quantized payloads, scales, and
  recurrent-state bytes without conversion or new transfer kernels.
- Keep existing homogeneous and HiSparse layout behavior unchanged.

## Validation

- Scoped repository pre-commit checks pass, including mypy (Python 3.11), Ruff,
  formatting, test tethering, and Markdown checks:
  `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files <incremental changed files>`.
- CPU source isolation passes 26 prerequisite test-body cases, 36 resolver
  combinations, 17 platform/offload-layout cases, and eight ModelOpt factory
  cases. These are not full-vLLM pytest results.
- Earlier Nano TP4 serving tests exercised CPU offload/reload and recomputation
  with CUDA graphs and exact in-process output matching. This is historical
  evidence, not a fresh GPU result for this head or a cross-process determinism
  claim. Fresh GPU/offload-runtime validation remains pending.

## Details

The implementation adds five production lines. It preserves the fixed recipe
and topology and transfers the complete backing row, including unused space.
It does not introduce compact CPU slots or certify NIXL P/D, LMCache, secondary
tiers, or cross-topology cache transfer. Related #53544, #56953, #57216, and
#57824 do not duplicate this layout integration.

[Incremental diff](https://github.com/meenchen/vllm/compare/36ae3a4ff4666da693c8d7a8ca2b5de7310bddf2...7268f81226bc5e82c23a6e38b81272f8b5dea7e8):

This remains a draft pending submitting-author review and fresh runtime validation.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4 VL dummy image is not the worst case for multimodal profiling
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13.7 (trixie), x86_64, running under WSL2 Kernel: Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 glibc: 2.41 Python: 3.12.14 NumPy: 2.5.3 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cpu CUDA available: No vLLM package: Not installed; validation executed relevant code extracted from the vLLM v0.30.0 tag ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Summary `get_image_size_with_most_features` returns a square `756x756` image, but a square does *not* maximize the features within the token budget: real images produce up to **378 placeholder tokens vs. 346** and **3312 ViT patches vs. 2916** for the dummy. Memory profiling therefore runs on an input ~9% short on decoder multimodal tokens and ~14% short on ViT patches. Reproducing the Bug ```python from PIL import Image from vllm.models.deepseek_v4.common.mm_preprocess import ( DeepseekV4VLProcessingInfo, DeepseekV4VLProcessor, build_image_block_pad_free, ) from vllm.transformers_utils.configs.deepseek_v4 import DeepseekV4Config config = DeepseekV4Config(vision_n_layers=24) class Ctx: def get_hf_config(self, *args, **kwargs): return config info = DeepseekV4VLProcessingInfo(Ctx()) processor = DeepseekV4VLProcessor(config) def features(width, height): out = processor(images=[Image.new("RGB", (width, height))]) n_llm_h, n_llm_w = out["llm_grid"][0].tolist() types, _ = build_image_block_pad_free(n_llm_h, n_llm_w) return len(types), out["patches"].shape[0] dummy = info.get_image_size_with_most_features() print("dummy", dummy, features(dummy.width, dummy.height)) print("1932x336", features(1932, 336)) assert features(1932, 336) <= features(dummy.width, dummy.height) ``` ``` dummy ImageSize(width=756, height=756) (346, 2916) 1932x336 (378, 3312) AssertionError ``` Fix Search the LLM grids that fit the token budget instead of assuming a square. The loop runs once at startup and returns `1932x336` for the shipped config, matching the sweep maxima for both patches and tokens. ```diff --- a/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/mm_preprocess.py +++ b/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/mm_preprocess.py @@ def get_image_size_with_most_features(self) -> ImageSize: hf_config = self.get_hf_config() patch_size = hf_config.vision_patch_size downsample_ratio = hf_config.vision_downsample_ratio - # A square maximizes the ViT patch count (area) within the token - # budget; solve the budget-derived size directly to keep the dummy - # image small. - budget = hf_config.vision_max_n_token - (COMPRESS_PAD_TO - 1) - side = budget * patch_size * downsample_ratio - _, _, best_h, best_w, _ = solve_resize_ratio( - side, side, patch_size, downsample_ratio, budget - ) - return ImageSize(width=best_w, height=best_h) + max_wh_ratio = hf_config.vision_max_wh_ratio + # Every aligner row costs an extra IMAGE_NEW_LINE token, so height is + # more expensive than width and a square is *not* optimal: search the + # LLM grids that fit the budget for the one with the most ViT patches + # (ties broken by the longer sentinel block). + budget = hf_config.vision_max_n_token - (COMPRESS_PAD_TO - 1) + step = patch_size * downsample_ratio + best_grid = (1, 1) + best_key = (0, 0) + for n_llm_h in range(1, budget): + if ( + grid_tokens(n_llm_h * step, step, patch_size, downsample_ratio)[2] + > budget + ): + break + for n_llm_w in range(1, budget): + if max_wh_ratio is not None and n_llm_w > n_llm_h * max_wh_ratio: + break + num_tokens = grid_tokens( + n_llm_h * step, n_llm_w * step, patch_size, downsample_ratio + )[2] + if num_tokens > budget: + break + key = (n_llm_h * n_llm_w, num_tokens) + if key > best_key: + best_key, best_grid = key, (n_llm_h, n_llm_w) + n_llm_h, n_llm_w = best_grid + return ImageSize(width=n_llm_w * step, height=n_llm_h * step) ``` The `max_wh_ratio` guard keeps the returned size from being clamped back down by `load_image`; the selected grid also maximizes area, so it comfortably clears `vision_min_pixels` (649k pixels vs. the 147k minimum) and is not rescaled either. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Adopt GPU prefix copies after the hit's allocation
body:
## Purpose

Fix an engine crash (`Cannot get N free blocks from the pool`) on a HiSparse host-prefix hit under GPU memory pressure. This is an alternative to #57457.

A host-prefix hit re-pins free GPU copies of its pages so the prefix comes back GPU-resident. Admission counts those copies as free blocks, but adoption pinned them before the hit's own allocation (hot region and new pages), which could then run the pool dry.

#57457 fixes this by charging the pins at admission. That mixes host and GPU accounting in `HiSparseSourceManager.get_num_blocks_to_allocate`, and under pressure it defers a request that could run by reading its prefix from host, just to keep an optimization.

## Changes

- **Adopt after allocation.** `commit_computed_blocks` records the pages to adopt, and `update_residency` (in `cache_blocks`, after `allocate_new_blocks`) adopts the copies that survived. The allocation always gets what admission counted, so no admission accounting is needed. A copy the allocation reuses is dropped by its reuse watcher and never adopted.
- **Copies are evicted last.** `BlockPool.unpin_blocks` documents unpinned blocks as last-resort eviction candidates, but blocks freed afterwards were appended behind them, so an allocation evicted a prefix's copies before blocks nobody would reuse. `FreeKVCacheBlockQueue` now keeps a last-resort segment at its tail that later appends stay in front of, and `unpin_blocks` uses it.
- **Tail first.** HiSparse releases a prefix's pages tail first, matching `free_blocks`' convention, so pressure trims a prefix from its end.

Replaying #57457's scenario (a resumed 3-page host prefix hit, `free_blocks` left in the pool):

| `free_blocks` | main | #57457 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5–6 | rejected | rejected | rejected |
| 7 | crash | rejected | admitted, 0/3 copies |
| 8 | crash | rejected | admitted, 1/3 |
| 9 | crash | rejected | admitted, 2/3 |
| 10+ | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |

## Test Plan

- `test_hisparse_prefix_hit_under_pressure_adopts_surviving_copies[7, 9, 10]`: exact adopted pages, and no block shared between adopted copies and fresh allocations. `7` fails without the adoption timing, `9` without tail-first release, and `10` without the last-resort segment.
- `test_free_kv_cache_block_queue_last_resort_stays_behind`: later appends stay ahead of the segment after its first block is removed or popped.
- `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py` and `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`, with `CpuPlatform` selected:

```bash
python cpu_pytest.py --confcutdir=tests/v1/core tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
```

## Test Result

- New tests fail on main (3 of 4) and pass with this PR; each case was also checked against the partial fixes above.
- 297 passed. 8 errors are `fixture 'caplog_vllm' not found`, from running outside the top-level conftest, and are identical on main.

No GPU or model run: the change is scheduler-side block bookkeeping.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation, implementation, tests, and this description.

title: [Feature][KV Connector] Add UMBP standalone mode
body:
## Purpose

Adds `UMBPStoreConnector`, a KV connector that offloads full prefix-cached KV blocks to a UMBP host-DRAM pool (MORI) and restores them on a later prefix hit, after vLLM has evicted them from GPU memory (RFC #57187). Two deployments are supported:

- **Embedded**: each worker owns a private pool in its own process. No extra process to run.
- **Standalone**: one node-local `umbp_standalone_server`, started outside vLLM, owns the pool. Every engine, DP rank and worker on the node attaches to it, so engines share stored prefixes and the pool outlives an engine restart.

The branch is self-contained on `main` and includes the core and embedded mode also proposed in #58568, so the stack builds and tests on its own.

## Design

vLLM keeps scheduling, GPU block ownership and block hashes; a runtime owns the pool and the transfers.

- **Lookup**: the scheduler looks up the blocks after the local prefix hit and reports whole-block hits. Keys encode the model, KV layout, cache group, parallel rank (TP/DCP/PP) and draft model, so incompatible engines never share objects, and a hit requires every rank's object. The last block is dropped for EAGLE-style drafters, as core does.
- **Load**: loads target the blocks core allocated and run asynchronously by default, so the forward pass never waits on a transfer. A failed load reports its blocks and core recomputes them (`kv_load_failure_policy=recompute`).
- **Store**: newly completed blocks are stored after the forward pass. A store holds its GPU blocks until every rank has finished, and a preempted request's transfers finish or are cancelled before core can reuse its blocks.
- **Embedded runtime**: a MORI client per worker; scheduler lookups reach each rank over per-engine local sockets.
- **Standalone runtime**: workers register their GPU KV with the server over HIP IPC and the server copies between those allocations and its pool, so no KV bytes cross the socket. vLLM never starts or sizes the server: pool-sizing and auto-start options are rejected, as with Mooncake store and LMCache MP.
- **Hybrid models**: models with several KV cache groups (Mamba-style layers, sparse-attention indexers, draft-model groups) coordinate hits across groups with core's KV cache coordinator, store Mamba align states from core's boundary hand-offs, and always load asynchronously.
- **Observability**: `BlockStored`/`BlockRemoved` KV cache events and transfer counters through `KVConnectorStats` and Prometheus.

## Commit structure

The PR is split into seven commits, each self-contained with its own tests, meant to be reviewed in order:

1. Core connector and embedded mode, with docs, unit tests, GPU integration tests and an AMD CI step.
2. Bulk whole-block transfers, and skipping restored blocks that are still in the pool.
3. Transfer timeouts, cancelling queued transfers on preemption, and retrying puts while the pool evicts.
4. Optional asynchronous lookup off the scheduler thread.
5. Hybrid KV cache groups.
6. KV cache events and transfer metrics.
7. Standalone mode.

## Configuration

```json
{"kv_connector": "UMBPStoreConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_load_failure_policy": "recompute", "kv_connector_extra_config": {"mode": "embedded", "total_capacity_bytes": 10737418240}}
```

Standalone: start `umbp_standalone_server` on the node, then use `{"mode": "standalone", "endpoint": "/path/to/server.sock"}`. See `docs/features/umbp_embedded_dram.md` and `docs/features/umbp_standalone.md`.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests: `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_umbp_*.py` (core, embedded, async lookup, hybrid, events, standalone). Each commit passes its own suite and pre-commit.
- GPU integration tests: `tests/v1/kv_connector/umbp_integration/`, including a token-level end-to-end test that evicts a prompt from GPU memory, restores it from the pool and checks the generated tokens.
- Serving benchmarks against Mooncake Store (embedded and standalone) on GPT-OSS-20B and Llama-3.1-8B, one GPU per engine, 10 GiB pool: `vllm bench serve` with 256 requests of 8192 input / 1024 output tokens at 2 req/s, and 10 forced-restore trials of a 10,001-token prompt (cold run, GPU-only cache reset, replay that can only restore from the pool).
- Cross-engine restore through one standalone server: engine A computes a prompt, engine B restores it.
- Kimi-K3 with a DSpark drafter (TP=8, one node): restore of a long prompt with draft-acceptance comparison, plus a negative control that skips restoring the drafter's cache group.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 101 to 213 passed across the seven commits; GPU integration: all passed (14 at the top of the stack). Pre-commit clean.
- Every restore trial was verified by external-hit and native-load metrics (10,000 of 10,000 tokens restored, no GPU hit, no transfer errors), and restored output matched the cold output.

Restore latency of a 10,001-token prompt (median of 10 trials, ms):

| Model | Recompute | UMBP embedded | UMBP standalone | Mooncake embedded | Mooncake standalone |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Llama-3.1-8B | 144.7 | **45.8** | 53.6 | 67.4 | 51.7 |
| GPT-OSS-20B | 92.9 | **25.7** | 27.9 | 34.0 | 27.1 |

Embedded restore copies from the worker's own DRAM straight into GPU KV at about 45 GiB/s, which makes it the fastest restore path measured, 32% faster than Mooncake embedded on Llama-3.1-8B. Standalone restore is on par with Mooncake standalone.

Serving overhead (mean TTFT ms / TPOT ms, first measured run):

| Model | UMBP embedded | UMBP standalone | Mooncake embedded | Mooncake standalone |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPT-OSS-20B | 102.5 / 4.14 | 103.5 / 4.15 | 99.8 / 4.13 | 100.6 / 4.12 |
| Llama-3.1-8B | 179.1 / 11.70 | 184.0 / 11.83 | 178.9 / 11.65 | 178.3 / 11.71 |

TPOT is within 1% of Mooncake Store; storing runs off the forward pass without contending with it.

Cross-engine restore through one standalone server (median ms): GPT-OSS-20B 91.6 recompute on engine A versus 30.6 restore on engine B; Llama-3.1-8B 153.8 versus 70.0. When both engines serve the same prefix traffic, engine B serves 99.8% of the shared prefix tokens from the pool (GPT-OSS-20B).

Kimi-K3 with DSpark (42,932-token prompt, 4 trials per run, embedded and standalone):

| Metric | Cold | Restored |
|---|---:|---:|
| Tokens restored from the pool | 0 | 39,936 |
| TTFT | 5.4 to 6.1 s | 3.0 to 3.6 s |
| Draft acceptance (median over 10 runs) | 0.585 | 0.581 |

Skipping the restore of the drafter's cache group drops acceptance to 0, so the hybrid path restores every group the drafter reads.

Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct GSM8K through one standalone server (earlier revision of this branch, same hybrid design): cold 88.3 / 89.5, with pool hits 89.1 / 89.2, replay 89.5 / 88.7.

title: [ROCm][Perf] gfx950: use FlyDSL fp8 MQA logits kernel for the sparse indexer prefill
body:
## Purpose

Extends #49544 to gfx950: the sparse indexer's prefill MQA logits use the AITER FlyDSL kernel on gfx950 as well as gfx942 whenever AITER is enabled, instead of the Triton/Gluon kernel. 

Needs ROCm/aiter#4538, which is in AITER v0.1.23 (the version vLLM main pins).

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_flydsl_mqa_logits_dispatch.py`: gfx942 and gfx950 use FlyDSL when AITER is enabled; other archs use Triton/Gluon; AITER disabled uses the torch fallback. 4/4 pass on MI355X.
- End to end A/B on GLM-5.2-MXFP4: throughput sweep, GPQA Diamond and RULER niah_single_2.

## Test Result


GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4, MI355X. Same build for both runs; the only difference is the prefill MQA-logits kernel (Gluon before, FlyDSL with this change).

### Accuracy

| Eval | Gluon | FlyDSL |
|---|---|---|
| GPQA Diamond | 0.899 | 0.884 |
| RULER niah_single_2, 64k | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| RULER niah_single_2, 128k | 1.00 | 1.00 |

GPQA is a single run of 198 questions (stderr about 0.02).

### ISL 8192 / OSL 1024 and ISL 1024 / OSL 1024 (tput/GPU)

| Conc | 8k Gluon | 8k FlyDSL | Δ | 1k Gluon | 1k FlyDSL | Δ |

Geomean over all 18 points: 1560.4 → 1558.5 tok/s/GPU (−0.1%).

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Adopt GPU prefix copies after the hit's allocation
body:
## Purpose

Fix an engine crash (`Cannot get N free blocks from the pool`) on a HiSparse host-prefix hit under GPU memory pressure. This is an alternative to #57457.

Closes #59440.

"Adopting" a GPU copy means a host-prefix hit points its page at a still-valid GPU copy of that host page (a GPU-side prefix-cache hit) instead of reading the page back from host.

A host-prefix hit re-pins free GPU copies of its pages so the prefix comes back GPU-resident. Admission counts those copies as free blocks, but adoption pinned them before the hit's own allocation (hot region and new pages), which could then run the pool dry.

#57457 fixes this by charging the pins at admission. That mixes host and GPU accounting in `HiSparseSourceManager.get_num_blocks_to_allocate`, and under pressure it defers a request that could run by reading its prefix from host, just to keep an optimization.

## Changes

HiSparse-only (`vllm/v1/hisparse/coordinator.py`):

- **Adopt after allocation.** `commit_computed_blocks` records the pages to adopt, and `update_residency` (in `cache_blocks`, after `allocate_new_blocks`) adopts the copies that survived. The allocation always gets what admission counted, so no admission accounting is needed. A copy the allocation reuses is dropped by its reuse watcher and never adopted.
- **Tail first.** HiSparse releases a prefix's pages tail first, matching `free_blocks`' convention, so pressure trims a prefix from its end.

Replaying #57457's scenario (a resumed 3-page host prefix hit, `free_blocks` left in the pool):

| `free_blocks` | main | #57457 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5–6 | rejected | rejected | rejected |
| 7–8 | crash | rejected | admitted, 0/3 copies |
| 9 | crash | rejected | admitted, 1/3 |
| 10 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 2/3 |
| 11+ | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |

Near the boundary this keeps fewer copies than #57457, because blocks freed after the copies are queued behind them. #59283, stacked on this PR, is an optional core change that restores 3/3 at 10.

## Test Plan

- `test_hisparse_prefix_hit_under_pressure_adopts_surviving_copies[7, 10]`: exact adopted pages, and no block shared between adopted copies and fresh allocations. `7` fails without the adoption timing, and `10` without tail-first release.
- `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py` and `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`, with `CpuPlatform` selected:

```bash
python cpu_pytest.py --confcutdir=tests/v1/core tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
```

## Test Result

- Both new cases fail on main and pass with this PR.
- CPU (`CpuPlatform`): 295 passed. 8 errors are `fixture 'caplog_vllm' not found`, from running outside the top-level conftest, and are identical on main.
- H100, HiSparse unit tests across `tests/v1` (`-k hisparse`): 156 passed.
- H100, `test_prefix_caching.py` + `test_kv_cache_utils.py`: 301 passed. The 2 failures (`test_get_kv_cache_config_mamba_hybrid_sharing_pp_*`) need 4 visible GPUs and fail identically on main with 1.
- H100, `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: fails with this PR alone (see the dependency note); with #59235 merged in, 2 passed in each of 2 runs.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation, implementation, tests, and this description.

title: [Core][HiSparse] Keep unpinned blocks last in the free queue
body:
## Purpose

**Optional performance improvement, stacked on #59282.** #59282 fixes the crash on its own; this PR only affects how many HiSparse GPU prefix copies survive memory pressure, and so how many prefix pages are read from host instead.

`BlockPool.unpin_blocks` documents unpinned blocks as "last-resort eviction candidates", but it appends them to the free queue like any other block, so blocks freed afterwards are queued behind them. In #59282's scenario, a finished request's cached indexer block is freed after its MLA copies were unpinned, so the resumed request's allocation evicts a copy it was about to adopt while that indexer block survives.

## Changes

- `FreeKVCacheBlockQueue` keeps a last-resort segment at its tail: `append`/`append_n` insert in front of it, the new `append_last_resort_n` appends behind it, and `popleft`/`popleft_n`/`remove` advance its head when they take it.
- `BlockPool.unpin_blocks` uses `append_last_resort_n`, which makes its documented behavior true.

Only the HiSparse coordinator unpins blocks. Without unpinned blocks the segment is empty and the queue orders blocks exactly as before, at the cost of one pointer comparison per popped or removed block.

This does change HiSparse's eviction policy: unpinned blocks, meaning finished requests' copies and pages a running request released but still reads, now outlast every ordinary cached block rather than aging in LRU order. Evicting either kind forces reads from host.

Copies kept in #59282's scenario:

| `free_blocks` | #59282 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 7–8 | 0/3 | 0–1/3 |
| 9 | 1/3 | 2/3 |
| 10 | 2/3 | 3/3 |
| 11+ | 3/3 | 3/3 |

## Test Plan

- `test_hisparse_prefix_hit_under_pressure_adopts_surviving_copies[10]` now expects all three copies; it keeps two without the last-resort segment.
- `test_free_kv_cache_block_queue_last_resort_stays_behind`: later appends stay ahead of the segment after its first block is removed or popped.
- `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py` and `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`, with `CpuPlatform` selected.

## Test Result

- 296 passed. 8 errors are `fixture 'caplog_vllm' not found`, from running outside the top-level conftest, and are identical on main.
- Not yet measured: an end-to-end pressure benchmark showing fewer host reads. That should decide whether this is worth a core change.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation, implementation, tests, and this description.

title: [Perf][Kernel] Vectorized MLA KV-cache write for large launches
body:
## Purpose

`concat_and_cache_mla` writes one token's latent row (`kv_lora_rank` elements) and rope row (`pe_dim` elements) into the MLA KV cache. It runs for every MLA model on every layer, prefill and decode, from `MLACommonBaseImpl.do_kv_cache_update` inside the `unified_mla_kv_cache_update` op, so it is eager on every backend.

The kernel copies one element per thread with a 512-thread block per token: 576 scalar 2-byte loads and stores per token, 448 threads idle during the rope copy, and on the fp8 path a dereference of the scale pointer per element. At decode sizes that is at the launch floor and there is nothing to gain. At prefill sizes it is latency-bound: 16K tokens take 46 us to read and write 38 MB, 0.8 TB/s on a 3.35 TB/s part.

This PR adds vector variants of the kernel and of its grouped form (Kimi K3 MTP context insertion) and switches to them from 512 tokens for the plain cache and 1024 tokens for the fp8 cache: one 32-lane group per token, four tokens per block, 16-byte loads and stores through `vectorize_with_alignment` (the helper `reshape_and_cache_flash` uses), scale read once per thread. Rows that are not 16-byte aligned or not a multiple of the vector size fall back to scalar copies inside the helper, so `k_pe` passed as a slice of the latent projection is handled without a host-side check. Below the threshold the existing kernels run unchanged.

Why the threshold: I first measured the vector layout on its own (exploration runs on 0376f81530 with CUDA 12.9, under `exploration/` in the logs). It is 2.3x to 3.8x faster from 1K tokens but 0.63x to 0.9x at 1 to 128 tokens, where each lane's serialized vector round trips (and, for fp8, eight converts per vector) cost more than the extra threads save. Wider layouts (64 or 128 lanes per token) trade one regime for the other. Routing the small path through the vector helper at width 1 also measured 0.1 us slower than the original loop. The crossover sweep put parity at 256 tokens for the plain cache and 768 to 1024 for fp8. The thresholds are 512 and 1024. For the plain cache, the original 512-thread blocks fit 528 tokens in one wave on an H100 and pay a second wave past that (2.54 us at 512 tokens, 3.04 us at 640), while the vector kernel stays at 2.4 us. For fp8, rank 256 only reaches parity at 1024 tokens. Every measured shape is at or above main.

Cache bytes are identical on both paths: the `auto` path is a copy, and the fp8 path applies the same per-element `scaled_convert` with the same scale. Verified below.

**Where it matters.** Kernel time at prefill. End-to-end throughput on DeepSeek-V2-Lite is within noise (tables below); the profiles show the kernel's share of GPU time before and after.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR touches `concat_and_cache_mla_kernel` or the grouped kernel. The closest is #38646 (@ZJY0516, opt-in torch.compile pass that fuses rope into the MLA cache insert; stale and needs-rebase since 2026-09-02): it rewrites the graph to call the separate `concat_and_cache_mla_rope_fused` kernel that already exists on main, so it changes which op the compiled path calls and does not touch this kernel, which stays the default path for every MLA backend. #45573 is the manual-fusion port of the same pass, #57640, #55230, #45798 and #41099 are ROCm/AITER fusions in the AMD model files, #55654 is a DSpark context insert in its own kernel file, and #38354 is an SM100 fused decode draft. None of them change the code here.

## Test Plan

- Bitwise vs `main` (0af34418e9): sha256 of the cache bytes over bf16/fp16/fp32 inputs, `auto` and `fp8` caches, token counts 1 to 16384, (`kv_lora_rank`, `pe_dim`) in {(512, 64), (256, 64), (512, 0), (128, 32)}, three input layouts (contiguous, `k_pe` as a latent slice, odd-offset unaligned rows), a padded slot (-1), plus the grouped kernel over 3 layers.
- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py`. The MLA test now asserts `torch.equal` for both cache dtypes, and a new `test_concat_and_cache_mla_strided_input` asserts `torch.equal` between strided and contiguous inputs and against the reference. The strided test runs at 1, 42, 1000 and 4096 tokens, so both the original and the vector kernels are asserted exactly for both cache dtypes.
- Microbenchmark: H100 80GB, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, `do_bench_cudagraph` median; new `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_concat_and_cache_mla.py --strided` (k_pe as a latent slice, as the model passes it), plus a finer sweep around the thresholds, two interleaved rounds.
- E2e on deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (MLA, `kv_lora_rank` 512, `pe_dim` 64, 27 layers), bf16 cache and `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`:

```bash
lm_eval --model vllm --model_args pretrained=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat,trust_remote_code=True,max_model_len=4096,gpu_memory_utilization=0.9,seed=0 --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto --seed 0
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --trust-remote-code --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 --num-prompts 1000 --request-rate inf --seed 0
```

## Test Result

- Bitwise: **380 identical, 0 mismatched**.
- Tests: **698 passed** (`test_cache.py`), 46 of them the MLA cache tests.

**Microbenchmark**, bf16 input, `kv_lora_rank` 512, `pe_dim` 64, `k_pe` strided (us):

| tokens | auto main | auto PR | speedup | fp8 main | fp8 PR | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.50 | 1.50 | 1.00x | 1.57 | 1.56 | 1.00x |
| 32 | 1.79 | 1.79 | 1.00x | 1.87 | 1.86 | 1.00x |
| 128 | 1.91 | 1.91 | 1.00x | 1.98 | 1.98 | 1.00x |
| 512 | 2.37 | 2.18 | 1.09x | 2.52 | 2.52 | 1.00x |
| 1024 | 3.47 | 2.30 | 1.51x | 3.76 | 3.01 | 1.25x |
| 2048 | 5.53 | 2.66 | 2.08x | 5.94 | 3.33 | 1.78x |
| 4096 | 9.46 | 3.49 | 2.71x | 10.22 | 4.33 | 2.36x |
| 8192 | 17.58 | 5.28 | 3.33x | 18.79 | 7.20 | 2.61x |
| 16384 | 46.34 | 13.19 | 3.51x | 39.47 | 13.31 | 2.97x |
| 32768 | 108.25 | 34.39 | 3.15x | 108.68 | 32.35 | 3.36x |
| 65536 | 214.06 | 65.54 | 3.27x | 215.20 | 61.58 | 3.49x |

Below the threshold both builds run the same kernel; two interleaved rounds over that range (27 shapes across bf16/fp32, rank 256/512, auto/fp8) are 0.99x to 1.00x. Fine sweep in the 512 to 1024 window, plain cache, two interleaved rounds that agree to 0.01 us (round 1 shown):

| tokens | bf16 rank 512 | fp32 rank 512 | bf16 rank 256 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 384 | 1.00x | 1.00x | 1.00x |
| 512 | 1.07x | 1.08x | 1.01x |
| 640 | 1.29x | 1.29x | 1.07x |
| 768 | 1.38x | 1.34x | 1.11x |
| 896 | 1.42x | 1.35x | 1.14x |
| 1024 | 1.48x | 1.39x | 1.17x |

fp8 at its 1024 threshold is 1.22x (bf16 rank 512), 1.20x (fp32 rank 512) and 1.02x (bf16 rank 256). Over the check-script sweep (bf16 at rank 256/512, auto/fp8, contiguous and strided, plus fp32 at rank 512, 1 to 65536 tokens) the geomean is 1.45x; rank 256 reaches 2.6x and fp32 2.2x at the top end. At 64K tokens the bf16 `auto` path moves 151 MB in 65.5 us, 2.3 TB/s.

**E2e, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat**

|---|---:|---:|

| PR | 0.6641 ± 0.0130 | 0.6581 ± 0.0131 |

`vllm bench serve`, three interleaved rounds per build, bf16 cache:

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Request throughput (req/s) | 54.99 | 55.29 | +0.5% |
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 7039 | 7077 | +0.5% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 6823 | 6762 | -0.9% |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 75.33 | 75.12 | -0.3% |

Per-round req/s: main 55.08 / 54.55 / 55.35, PR 55.85 / 55.10 / 54.90. The PR build is ahead in two rounds and behind in the third; the gap is inside the round-to-round spread.

`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, five interleaved rounds:

title: [KV Cache] Map kernel blocks per attention group; GLM-5.3-Flash on the generic packed layout
body:
## Purpose

Alternative to #57169 (and its earlier version #55219). It keeps #57169's GLM-5.3-Flash move to the generic packed KV layout with a `CircularBufferSpec` tail. It replaces the builder-side re-paging of the kpool indexer with a generic, worker-side kernel-block mapping per attention group. As a result, `BlockTable` / `BlockTables` stop knowing about kernel blocks.

**Design**
- **Block tables and slot mappings** are always in KV cache manager blocks, in V1 and MRv2. `kernel_block_sizes` is removed from `BlockTable`, `MultiGroupBlockTable`, `BlockTables`, both input batches and both slot-mapping kernels. Slot values are unchanged: `b*bs + off == (b*bpk + off//kbs)*kbs + off%kbs`.
- **Mapping per attention group.** When a group's backend needs blocks smaller than the manager's (`AttentionGroup.kernel_block_size`), `AttentionGroup.build_metadata` / `build_metadata_for_cudagraph_capture` / `build_metadata_for_drafting` map its block table to kernel blocks. Kernel block `j` of block `b` is `b * kernel_block_stride + j`. The mapped table goes into a persistent per-ubatch buffer (`kernel_block_table`), so CUDA graphs see a stable address.
- **Ordinary splits.** In a dense (unpacked) layout the stride is blocks-per-kernel-block. KV views are allocated in kernel blocks as before.
- **Packed compressed caches.** Example: GLM-5.3-Flash's kpool indexer, which DeepGEMM paged MQA reads in 32/64-state pages. `AttentionGroup.map_kv_cache` re-strides the bound view over the packed blocks and takes the stride from the real tensor. It raises for token caches, which are written through manager-unit slot mappings.
- **Alignment.** A backend with only fixed kernel block sizes gets `block_stride_alignment = MultipleOf(max size)` (`customize_attention_spec`). `KVCacheSpec.get_block_stride_alignment()` resolves it in the engine against the *final* (possibly rescaled) block size, and returns 1 when the block runs whole.
- **Connectors** keep manager-block views. NIXL and Mooncake inline the removed `BlockTable.map_to_kernel_blocks`.

**Related:**
- #58630 resolves kernel block-size constraints per spec.
- #59112 re-pages packed BLHNC caches inside FlashInfer.

This PR instead makes kernel blocks a per-attention-group concern in the worker.

## Test Plan / Results

Run on B300 with `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`, one file at a time. Running several of these files in one process fails the same way on the base branch, from cross-file interference.

- **Unit tests, passing:**
  - `tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py`, including new tests for packed and split mapping, the token-cache error, and `MultipleOf` alignment resolution;
  - `test_gpu_block_table.py`, `test_gpu_input_batch.py`, `test_gpu_model_runner.py`, `test_kv_block_zeroer.py`, `test_gpu_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py`, `test_gpu_pcp_manager.py`;
  - `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer.py`, `test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py`;
  - `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py` (129);
  - `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py` (42), `test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py`;
  - `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py` (152 on its own);
  - `tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py`;
  - `tests/models/glm5next`.
- **Unit tests, known failure:** `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_length.py::test_eagle3_acceptance_length[FLASH_ATTN-...-gpt-oss-20b-eagle3]` fails on this branch (0.483) and on the reference branch (0.486) against a 0.4864 minimum, so it's pre-existing on this machine.
- **End-to-end greedy equivalence.** The reference is the same tree without the generic block-table change, which matches `main` for non-GLM models. FlashInfer autotuning was off and MoE was Triton, for determinism.

title: [glm] [pcp] [1/n] wire pcp for hybrid GLM sparse MLA
body:
## Purpose

Correct KV-cache handling for GLM-5.3's pooled sparse-MLA indexer (kpool) under prefill context parallelism (PCP). Pools span zig-zag PCP chunk boundaries, so kpool prefill writes gather every rank's prefill keys and gates, restore global sequence order, and pool the whole prefill into each rank's replicated cache. Decodes are replicated and ordered first on every rank, so their tail updates keep the local decode path.

Also:
- Tail slots are gathered from rank-local tokens and kept consistent across PCP ranks; NoPE latent cache gathers are handled.
- The current PCP manager is exposed to cache consumers, and the stale global batch is cleared for capture/dummy batches.
- With NCCL symmetric memory, dim-0 all-gathers return scratch reused per shape and dtype; both gathered slot mappings are cloned before being retained as metadata.
- Replicated MTP draft decodes carry an unexpanded slot mapping under PCP, so the indexer and the tail-slot builder gather only mappings that span the PCP group (as the generic sparse indexer already does).
- kpool prefill writes under PCP raise if the PCP manager is missing from the forward context, instead of being skipped silently; capture and dummy batches still skip them.

This PR does not enable PCP for the full GLM-5.3 hybrid model (the hybrid-PCP guard is unchanged). It is independent of the companion KCP PR #59304, which enables hybrid PCP for GLM-5.3 and should merge after this one.

**Not a duplicate:** searched open PRs for GLM/kpool/sparse-MLA PCP cache handling; the closest is #53173 (fused norm/rope with the PCP cache gather), a different change.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py \
       tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py \
       tests/test_pcp_dp.py \
       tests/models/glm5next --ignore=tests/models/glm5next/test_sequence_parallel.py
```
Run on GB300 (SM103) against this branch (rebased on `main` a96ee5935d). `test_sequence_parallel.py` is untouched here and needs the repo conftest, which our runtime could not load.

## Test Result

101 passed, 1 skipped (ROCm-only). New tests cover: the PCP tail-slot mapping owning gathered circular slots and keeping an unexpanded draft mapping local; the kpool prefill restore in global sequence order, including capture batches and a missing PCP manager (`tests/models/glm5next/test_sparse_indexer_pcp.py`); and the NoPE latent gather (`tests/test_pcp_dp.py`).

Model evaluation (GSM8K with PCP) requires #59304, since GLM-5.3 cannot run hybrid PCP without it; results will be added to both PRs before they leave draft.

---
AI assistance (Claude Code, Codex) was used to write and rebase this change. The tests above were run on this branch.

title: [Bug]: FlashMLA sparse decode allocates the split-KV workspace again on SM90 (regression of #53413)
body:
### Your current environment

H200 NVL, vLLM nightly `0bfc7a15d` (FlashMLA pin `0eee43b`), torch 2.13.0+cu130.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

#53413 (runtime OOM in `flash_mla_cuda.sparse_decode_fwd` on H200, fp8 mixed-batch path) was closed by #53755, which pulled in vllm-project/FlashMLA#19: the split-KV accumulators are only allocated when `num_sm_parts > 1`, and the no-split call returns before the combine.

The V4.1 sync, vllm-project/FlashMLA#20 (`c112cc1`), dropped that guard. `csrc/api/sparse_decode.cpp` now allocates `o_accum` and `lse_accum` under `if (enable_split_kv)`, with

```cpp
// Split-KV only pays off when a request has enough work. The sm90 kernel always splits.
bool enable_split_kv = arch.is_sm90a() || !(topk + extra_topk <= 640);
```

vLLM picked this up with the pin bump in #56893, so on Hopper the mixed-batch call again allocates a buffer that grows linearly with `--max-num-batched-tokens`.

Measured on one H200 NVL: a single `flash_mla_with_kvcache` call in the mixed-batch layout (`b=1`, `s_q=T`, `h_q=64`, top-k 2048, `fp8_ds_mla` cache), transient allocation during the call on top of inputs and outputs:

| T | workspace | out + lse |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 256.5 MiB | 64.2 MiB |
| 8192 | 2052 MiB | 514 MiB |
| 32768 | 8208 MiB | 2056 MiB |

That is exactly `(b + num_sm_parts) * s_q * h_q * d_v * 4` bytes with `num_sm_parts = 1`, the case #19 skipped. With the #53413 config (`--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`) every call again needs 8 GiB in one piece, which startup profiling does not see.

Our production image predates #56893, so we have not hit this in serving; we found it while reviewing #58985 and then measured it.

Restoring the `num_sm_parts > 1` guard for SM90 looks like the direct fix, unless the SM90 kernel now needs the accumulators even without a split. A vLLM-side chunking of the mixed batch (#49357) was closed in favour of that kernel fix.

cc @MatthewBonanni @zyongye

<details>
<summary>Measurement script</summary>

```python
import torch

from vllm.v1.attention.ops.flashmla import flash_mla_with_kvcache, get_mla_metadata

BLK, NB, TOPK, D, DV, H = 64, 4096, 2048, 576, 512, 64
cache = torch.zeros(NB, BLK, 1, 656, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")

for T in (1024, 8192, 32768):
    q = torch.randn(T, H, D, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    idx = torch.randint(0, NB * BLK, (1, T, TOPK), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
    seqlens = torch.full((1,), NB * BLK, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    block_table = torch.zeros((1, 1), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    before = torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    out, lse = flash_mla_with_kvcache(
        q=q.unsqueeze(0), k_cache=cache, block_table=block_table, head_dim_v=DV,
        cache_seqlens=seqlens, tile_scheduler_metadata=get_mla_metadata()[0],
        is_fp8_kvcache=True, indices=idx, softmax_scale=D**-0.5,
    )
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    results = out.numel() * out.element_size() + lse.numel() * lse.element_size()
    ws = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() - before - results
    print(f"T={T}: workspace {ws / 2**20:.1f} MiB")
```

</details>

title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3 NVFP4 with DCP and MTP does not start on Hopper on main (DSA MTP head, DCP a2a default)
body:
### Your current environment

4x H200 NVL, vLLM nightly `af7f9488c` (2026-09-28), `Inferact/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`, `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache, attention backend `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Our production command for GLM-5.3 boots on an image built from main of 2026-08-21 and fails on current main. There are two independent failures, hit in this order.

**1. The MTP draft fails to load: `NVFP4 weight_scale for layer 'parallel_lm_head' was never loaded (still NaN)`.**

This is #57532 again, on the other GLM path. #55442 fixed it by building the MTP `shared_head.head` as a deferred placeholder, but only in `Glm5NextMultiTokenPredictorLayer`. Since #52861, `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` drafts go through `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/nvidia/mtp.py`, and `DeepseekV32MultiTokenPredictorLayer` still builds `SharedHead(..., quant_config=quant_config)` without `defer_lm_head`. The NVFP4 head is created for a weight the checkpoint does not ship (`Inferact/GLM-5.3-NVFP4` has `lm_head.weight` and `model.layers.78.shared_head.norm.weight`, nothing under `shared_head.head`), and the NaN sentinel from #52501 fires. The placeholder would be replaced by the target `lm_head` right after loading anyway.

Checking `config.model_type == "glm_moe_dsa"` on the draft config does not work, because `SpeculativeConfig.hf_config_override` rewrites the draft's `model_type` to `deepseek_mtp`. Checking the target's `vllm_config.model_config.hf_config.model_type` does; with that change the model loads and serves with MTP 3.

The same draft-side check a few lines earlier in that constructor is therefore always false: `self._eh_plan = build_glm52_plan(...) if config.model_type == "glm_moe_dsa" else None` (#49791), so the GLM low-latency GEMM plan for the MTP `eh_proj` is never built.

**2. With the draft fixed, startup fails with `NotImplementedError: DCP for FlashMLA sparse is only validated with the default 'ag_rs' DCP comm backend; got 'a2a'`.**

#50382 made `a2a` with query replication the DCP default for `glm_moe_dsa`. On Hopper the sparse backend for this model is `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, which rejects anything but `ag_rs` (that guard is ours, from #46514, merged two days before #50382). With DCP on Hopper the model therefore defaults into a configuration its only backend refuses. Passing `--dcp-comm-backend ag_rs --no-dcp-q-replicate` gets past it.

A default that depends on the selected attention backend (keep `ag_rs` where `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` is used) would fix this without touching the Blackwell path; supporting the `a2a` combine in `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` would be the other way. If the backend-aware default is the preferred direction, we can send it.

### Reproduce

```bash
vllm serve Inferact/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --decode-context-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'
```

On 4x H200 the first failure stops model loading after about two minutes. With the draft head deferred, the second follows at backend initialization.

cc @lucamotz @LucasWilkinson @zhou9402

AI assistance was used for this investigation.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Keep GLM DSA's DCP defaults off a2a where FlashMLA sparse serves DCP
body:
## Purpose

Fixes the second failure in #59306, the DCP `a2a` default on Hopper. The MTP head failure from the same issue is fixed by #58209.

`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM.verify_and_update_config` defaults DCP to the `a2a` combine with query replication (#50382). FlashMLA sparse rejects anything but `ag_rs` under DCP; that guard is ours, from #46514, merged two days before #50382. On SM90 FlashMLA sparse is also the only sparse MLA backend that supports DCP (`FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` and `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` do not set `supports_dcp`, so the selector drops them), which is why the startup log lists a single candidate:

```
Using FLASHMLA_SPARSE attention backend out of potential backends: ['FLASHMLA_SPARSE']
NotImplementedError: DCP for FlashMLA sparse is only validated with the default 'ag_rs' DCP comm backend; got 'a2a'
```

GLM-5.x with DCP on Hopper therefore defaulted into a configuration its only backend refuses and needed `--dcp-comm-backend ag_rs --no-dcp-q-replicate` by hand.

The hook now leaves the stock defaults in place where FlashMLA sparse serves DCP: on SM90 (CUDA), and when the backend is forced to `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` on any platform. Unchanged:

- Blackwell keeps `a2a` + qrep.
- An explicit `--dcp-comm-backend` still wins. `set_dcp_defaults` only fills what the user left unset, so `--dcp-comm-backend a2a` on Hopper still reaches the guard and is refused as before.
- ROCm, gated by `is_cuda()`.

The other way to close this would be lifting the guard so FlashMLA sparse accepts the `a2a` combine. The DSA path already merges through `MLADCPManager.combine`, which implements `a2a`, so it may work as is, but it has not been validated on Hopper and this PR does not touch the guard.

### The `q_replicate=True` half of the default is inert on the CUDA DSA path

Since #52861 `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` on CUDA is `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/nvidia/model.py`. Its `DeepseekV32Attention` builds `q_b_proj` as a plain `ColumnParallelLinear`, never passes `dcp_q_replicate` to `MLAAttention`, and always all-gathers the query through `MLADCPManager.query_gather`. Only the generic `deepseek_v2.py` path (and `dots3_note`, `kimi_k3/amd`) reads `parallel_config.dcp_q_replicate`. So on main the flag neither replicates the projection (no +4.57 GiB/rank) nor skips the all-gather, on Hopper and Blackwell alike; the qrep measurement in #50382 predates #52861 by two days. This PR leaves that default alone. `dcp_q_replicate=True` still shows up in the config log. @LucasWilkinson, should qrep be wired into `DeepseekV32Attention`, or dropped from the GLM default?

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for `dcp_comm_backend`, `a2a DCP`, `set_dcp_defaults` and `59306 in:body`. #56906 adds an `a2a` default for Kimi-K3 on ROCm through the same hook, gated on the platform the same way, and does not touch GLM. #54472 is about direct A2A layouts. Nothing addresses the GLM default on Hopper.

## Test Plan

CPU-only unit tests next to the existing `set_dcp_defaults` tests, with `current_platform` patched so both branches run on any runner:

```
pytest tests/distributed/test_dcp_a2a.py -k TestDCPCommBackendConfig
```

The parametrized test pins three cases: SM100 keeps `a2a` + qrep, SM90 gets the stock `ag_rs` without qrep, `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` forced on SM100 gets the stock defaults. A second test pins that an explicit `--dcp-comm-backend a2a` is not overridden.

Both runs used the unpatched `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image (af7f9488c) in a CPU container: first with only the test file swapped in, then with the patched `config.py` mounted over the installed one.

## Test Result

Before, unpatched hook with the new tests:

```
FAILED tests/distributed/test_dcp_a2a.py::TestDCPCommBackendConfig::test_glm_moe_dsa_default_follows_backend[capability1-None-expected1]
FAILED tests/distributed/test_dcp_a2a.py::TestDCPCommBackendConfig::test_glm_moe_dsa_default_follows_backend[capability2-AttentionBackendEnum.FLASHMLA_SPARSE-expected2]
2 failed, 6 passed, 27 deselected in 2.46s
```

After, `TestDCPCommBackendConfig` plus the neighbouring CPU class `TestLSEWeightedCombine`:

```
18 passed, 17 deselected in 8.17s
```

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `typos` are clean on both files.

Hardware: 4x H200 NVL, `Inferact/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`, TP4 + DCP4 + EP, MTP 3, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, nightly af7f9488c with this change and #58209 applied, and no DCP flags on the command line. The engine config logs `dcp_comm_backend=ag_rs`, the model starts with `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` and serves normally. Without this change the same command stops at the `NotImplementedError` above. The change does not affect model output: it picks between configurations that already exist, and the one it picks was reachable through `--dcp-comm-backend ag_rs` before.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the investigation, the patch and the tests.

cc @LucasWilkinson

title: [ROCm][Perf] Pad N to 128 in AITER preshuffled PTPC FP8 GEMM to hit tuned FlyDSL kernels
body:
## Purpose

On ROCm, `AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel` (aiter `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle`, which dispatches to FlyDSL `flydsl_bpreshuflle_*` / CK kernels from aiter's tuned CSVs) is only selected when `(N, K)` has a tuned row. Some real shapes miss the table even though the next multiple of 128 is tuned. On Kimi-K3 at TP8, with online PTPC FP8 for the non-expert linears:

| Layer | N×K per rank | Tuned row in aiter `a8w8_bpreshuffle_tuned_gemm_kimik3.csv` |
|---|---|---|
| KDA `in_proj_qkvgfab` | 6288×7168 | 6400×7168 |
| MLA `fused_qkv_a_proj` | 2112×7168 | 2176×7168 |

This PR pads the weight's output dim up to a multiple of 128. The padded rows are zero and their scales are 1. Padding only happens when the unpadded N is untuned and the padded N is tuned. After the GEMM, the output is sliced back to N and bias is applied (aiter's bpreshuffle GEMM does not take a bias). 

Shapes that are already tuned, or can't be tuned even after padding, behave exactly as before.

**`AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A8W8_BPRESHUFFLE` must point at the kimik3 CSV.** If the env var is unset, aiter merges the default `configs/a8w8_bpreshuffle_tuned_gemm.csv` with every `configs/model_configs/*a8w8_bpreshuffle_tuned_gemm*.csv` into one table. Lookups are keyed on `(gfx, cu_num, M, N, K, q_dtype_w)` only, with no model name. On gfx950 / cu_num=256, both the default CSV (12 rows) and `dsv3_a8w8_bpreshuffle_tuned_gemm.csv` (17 rows) have **2112×7168**: DeepSeek-V3's `fused_qkv_a_proj` has the same shape. So with the default merge, 2112 counts as tuned and the padding is skipped. Kimi-K3 then runs those rows instead of the kimik3 2176 rows. From the tuner timings (dsv3 2112 vs kimik3 2176), that's ~11.2 µs vs ~6.3 µs at decode M=1–16. Only 6288 → 6400 gets padded.

At TP8 on MI355X, every FP8 bpreshuffle shape Kimi-K3 uses is in `a8w8_bpreshuffle_tuned_gemm_kimik3.csv`. No other CSV has them at cu_num=256, except the colliding 2112×7168:

| N×K | rows in kimik3 CSV (cu_num=256) |
|---|---|
| 1536×128, 7168×768, 2304×1536, 7168×4224, 1536×7168, 8448×7168, **2176×7168**, **6400×7168** | 62 each |
| 7168×1536 | 104 |

So the recipe restricts the bpreshuffle table to the kimik3 CSV only. That makes both 2112 → 2176 and 6288 → 6400 pad, and leaves every other shape's kernel unchanged.

Checked against aiter **v0.1.23** (the version `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` pins):
- The kimik3 bpreshuffle CSV is present, and `model_configs/` is merged automatically. Because of the merge, other models' rows (e.g. 2112×7168 from dsv3/default) shadow the padding decision unless `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A8W8_BPRESHUFFLE` is set (see above).
- For `libtype=flydsl`, `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle` dispatches to `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle_flydsl`.
- The weight shuffle layout `(16,16)` is unchanged.

## Recipe: Kimi-K3 MXFP4 on MI355X (TP8) with FlyDSL FP8 GEMMs

The checkpoint leaves attention, shared experts, the dense MLP and `lm_head` in bf16. Online PTPC FP8 quantizes those linears. `kv_b_proj` must stay bf16 because MLA dequantizes it to derive W_UK/W_UV. `*vision_tower*` and `*mm_projector*` are excluded too, matching ATOM's Kimi-K3 recipe. Without them the vision encoder and projector get quantized even with `--language-model-only`. With the exclusions, 489 linears are quantized instead of 599.

Note: with `--load-format fastsafetensors`, loading OOMed on MI355X; per-GPU VRAM grew steadily to 287 GiB. The default `safetensors` loader stays flat at ~190 GiB. Use the default loader with this overlay.

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1              # VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR defaults to 1
export VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2=1
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0
export SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1
# Use only the Kimi-K3 tuned bpreshuffle table so 2112 -> 2176 and 6288 -> 6400 both pad
# (the default merge contains DeepSeek-V3's 2112x7168 rows, which would skip the 2112 padding).
export AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A8W8_BPRESHUFFLE=$(python3 -c 'import aiter, os; print(os.path.dirname(aiter.__file__))')/configs/model_configs/a8w8_bpreshuffle_tuned_gemm_kimik3.csv
# export AITER_LOG_TUNED_CONFIG=1         # verification only: logs which tuned row/kernel each GEMM hits.
#                                         # Leave it off for benchmarking; in our runs it worsened E2E p95/p99 tails.

vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --language-model-only \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' \
  --quantization-config '{"linear":"fp8_per_channel","ignore":["*kv_b_proj","*vision_tower*","*mm_projector*"]}' \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len 262144 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

Expected kernels at M=72 (the M=128 tuned rows):

| N×K | Kernel |
|---|---|
| 6400×7168 (KDA in_proj, padded from 6288) | CK `a8w8_bpreshuffle_256x64x64x256_…` |
| 2176×7168 (MLA fused_qkv_a, padded from 2112) | `flydsl_bpreshuflle_32x32x1024_F8_F8_B16_0x1x4x2` |
| 576 / 1536 / 3584 / 8448 ×7168; 2304×1536; 7168×{1024,1536,4224} | `flydsl_bpreshuflle_*` |

## Test Plan

- [x] Serve with the recipe above on MI355X. Confirm with `AITER_LOG_TUNED_CONFIG=1`, or a torch profile, that the padded shapes resolve to the tuned 6400/2176 rows. This needs `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A8W8_BPRESHUFFLE` set; see Test Result.
- [x] Accuracy: GSM8K with lm_eval on online PTPC FP8 (this PR).
- [ ] Accuracy: GSM8K bf16 baseline for comparison.
- [x] Perf: 8k/1k `vllm bench serve` at concurrency 4/8/16: before, this PR without the env var, and this PR with the env var.
- [ ] Regression: existing ROCm FP8 PTPC tests (`tests/kernels/quantization`, `tests/quantization/test_online.py`).

## Test Result

MI355X ×8 (TP8), image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-36768d1bfd39094681cdbc8cb37d4b31c0729c89`, aiter v0.1.23. Kimi-K3 with DSpark draft (7 speculative tokens), `--max-num-seqs 2`, fp8 KV cache, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE cudagraphs. All runs use the recipe's `--quantization-config` (online FP8 PTPC) and the default `safetensors` loader; each runs in a fresh container.

- **Before**: the unpatched image. Untuned shapes (6288×7168 KDA `in_proj`) fall back to `RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`.
- **This PR, no env var**: the patch, `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A8W8_BPRESHUFFLE` unset (default merged table). 6288 → 6400 is padded; 2112×7168 stays on the default/dsv3 rows.
- **This PR + env var**: the patch, with the bpreshuffle table restricted so that 2112×7168 is untuned (the default merged table with only the 2112×7168 rows removed, which gives the same kernel selection as the kimik3 CSV alone; see below). Both 6288 → 6400 and 2112 → 2176 are padded.

With the patch, every FP8 PTPC linear selects `AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel`, and the `RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` fallback disappears.

### Tuned-row verification (`AITER_LOG_TUNED_CONFIG=1`)

Kimi-K3 TP8 on MI355X, agentic trace replay at concurrency 8:

| N×K (FP8 bpreshuffle) | Default merged table | 2112×7168 rows removed (≡ kimik3 CSV only) |
|---|---|---|
| 6288×7168 | untuned → padded to **6400**, all lookups tuned (kimik3 rows) | same |
| 2112×7168 | **tuned via default/dsv3 rows → not padded** | untuned → padded to **2176** |
| 2176×7168 | only the M=1 `can_implement` probe | all lookups tuned, FlyDSL |

With the kimik3 rows in effect, all 1,200 logged 2176/6400 hits used exactly the kimik3 CSV's kernel for that padded M, with 0 mismatches. For example, at M=72 (M=128 row): 2176 → `flydsl_bpreshuflle_32x32x1024_F8_F8_B16_0x1x4x2_default`, 6400 → CK `a8w8_bpreshuffle_256x64x64x256_…_intrawave_v3`. That run removed only the 2112×7168 rows from the merged table. As shown above, this gives the same kernel selection for every shape Kimi-K3 uses as setting `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A8W8_BPRESHUFFLE` to the kimik3 CSV.

### Perf

`vllm bench serve` with random prompts: 8192 input / 1024 output tokens, 1×concurrency warmups, 5×concurrency prompts, `--ignore-eos`. Draft acceptance is synthetic (`synthetic_acceptance_length=3.84`), fixed for all runs, so these numbers isolate the target-model speed. With `max-num-seqs 2`, runs decode with a batch of 2 and the extra requests queue, which is why TTFT grows with concurrency. TPOT/ITL are the cleanest signal for the GEMM change.

All three variants run with the same `--quantization-config '{"linear":"fp8_per_channel","ignore":["*kv_b_proj","*vision_tower*","*mm_projector*"]}'`, so in every column the non-expert linears (attention, shared experts, dense MLP, `lm_head`) run in online FP8 PTPC; only `kv_b_proj` (plus the excluded vision layers) stays bf16. **Before is not a bf16 baseline.** The only differences between the columns are the patch and `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A8W8_BPRESHUFFLE`:

| Variant | Patch | `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A8W8_BPRESHUFFLE` | FP8 PTPC kernels selected |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | no | unset | `AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel` + `RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` (torch fallback for untuned 6288×7168) |
| This PR, no env var | yes | unset | `AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel` only (6288 → 6400) |
| This PR + env var | yes | set (2112×7168 untuned) | `AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel` only (6288 → 6400, 2112 → 2176) |

Δ is relative to Before.

| Conc | Metric | Before | This PR, no env var | This PR + env var |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | Output tok/s | 289.48 | 292.97 (+1.2%) | 293.14 (+1.3%) |
| 4 | Mean TPOT (ms) | 6.33 | 6.26 (−1.1%) | 6.19 (−2.2%) |
| 4 | P99 TPOT (ms) | 6.76 | 6.79 (+0.4%) | 6.45 (−4.6%) |
| 4 | Mean ITL (ms) | 24.28 | 24.00 (−1.2%) | 23.75 (−2.2%) |
| 4 | Mean TTFT (ms) | 6,958 | 6,873 (−1.2%) | 6,936 (−0.3%) |
| 4 | Mean E2EL (ms) | 13,435 | 13,275 (−1.2%) | 13,271 (−1.2%) |
| 8 | Output tok/s | 302.35 | 305.36 (+1.0%) | 307.97 (+1.9%) |
| 8 | Mean TPOT (ms) | 6.22 | 6.16 (−1.0%) | 6.12 (−1.6%) |
| 8 | P99 TPOT (ms) | 6.41 | 6.41 (0.0%) | 6.37 (−0.6%) |
| 8 | Mean ITL (ms) | 23.84 | 23.62 (−0.9%) | 23.44 (−1.7%) |
| 8 | Mean TTFT (ms) | 18,656 | 18,453 (−1.1%) | 18,270 (−2.1%) |
| 8 | Mean E2EL (ms) | 25,018 | 24,757 (−1.0%) | 24,527 (−2.0%) |
| 16 | Output tok/s | 303.42 | 306.16 (+0.9%) | 306.67 (+1.1%) |
| 16 | Mean TPOT (ms) | 6.21 | 6.16 (−0.8%) | 6.14 (−1.1%) |
| 16 | P99 TPOT (ms) | 6.70 | 6.54 (−2.4%) | 6.55 (−2.2%) |
| 16 | Mean ITL (ms) | 23.79 | 23.60 (−0.8%) | 23.54 (−1.1%) |
| 16 | Mean TTFT (ms) | 42,813 | 42,377 (−1.0%) | 42,336 (−1.1%) |
| 16 | Mean E2EL (ms) | 49,165 | 48,677 (−1.0%) | 48,620 (−1.1%) |

- The patch alone gives ~1% (output throughput, TPOT, ITL, E2EL) by moving the 6288×7168 KDA `in_proj` off the torch fallback onto the tuned 6400×7168 kernel.
- Setting `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A8W8_BPRESHUFFLE` so 2112 also pads to the kimik3 2176 rows adds a further 0.3–1.1% mean TPOT, most visible at concurrency 4 (P99 TPOT −4.6%) and 8 (output +1.9%). At concurrency 16 the two patched variants are within noise.
- All requests succeeded in every run. Weight memory (~188.2 GiB/GPU) and KV cache (~60.1–60.3 GiB) are unchanged across the three variants; padding adds negligible memory.
- Single run per variant with 20–80 requests each, so differences below ~1% are near run-to-run noise; the direction is consistent across all three concurrencies.

### Accuracy

lm_eval gsm8k, 5-shot, full 1319 samples, via `local-completions` at concurrency 16 with `max_gen_toks=512`. This run uses real (`block`) rejection sampling instead of the synthetic one.

| Config | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| This PR (FP8 PTPC) | 0.9629 ± 0.0052 | 0.9629 ± 0.0052 |

A bf16 baseline gsm8k run is not included yet.

### DSpark draft is not affected

`--quantization-config` is stored only on the target `ModelConfig`. The draft `ModelConfig` is built without it (`vllm/config/speculative.py`). With an explicit `"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark"`, the draft does not inherit the target's `quantization` either. `K3DSparkModel` resolves its own config through `get_draft_quant_config()`, so the draft stays on its checkpoint's quantization. Avoid the `--quantization fp8_per_channel` shorthand, or a `"quantization"` key in `--speculative-config`, if the draft must stay bf16.

## Related PRs

No other open PR pads N for `AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel`. The closest analog is #55242 (NVIDIA: align Kimi-K3 nvfp4 `in_proj` by 128 so DeepGEMM is selected). Related and complementary:

- #54248 (merged): exposes `kFp8DynamicTokenSym` on AITER PTPC kernels. KDA `in_proj` and MLA `fused_qkv_a` now land on `AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel`, so they also advertise the key and can take fused `QuantizedActivation` inputs.
- #59069: fuses AttnRes output with per-token FP8 quant. Its description notes that "the current rowwise Torch FP8 KDA kernel does not expose the required input capability". That is the untuned N=6288 KDA `in_proj` fallback this PR removes, so #59069 can then fuse into KDA inputs too.
- #54254: fuses gated RMSNorm with per-token FP8 for the KDA `o_proj` (ATOM `_rmsnorm_gated_fp8_per_token_kernel`).
- #55043: fuses MLA sigmoid-mul with per-token FP8 for `o_proj` (ATOM `_fused_sigmoid_mul_fp8_per_token_quant_kernel`).
- #52968: AttnRes, sigmoid_mul and conv fusions ported from ATOM.
- #55001 (merged): `_ck_gemm_shape_is_tuned` now uses aiter's `get_GEMM_config_with_quant_type`, which this PR relies on.
- #56234: the same "select bpreshuffle when tuned" approach for FP8 blockscale.

#54254 and #55043 already use a `--quantization-config` PTPC overlay on Kimi-K3, the same approach as the recipe here.

title: Rocm/ci amd test areas parity
body:
AMD tests are defined in two places: the old test-amd.yaml pipeline and the AMD "mirror" copies in test_areas/*.yaml. The two have drifted apart. This PR makes both run the same tests with the same commands. Where they disagreed, it copies the newer version across.


**What the PR does:**

1. test_areas gains commands that only test-amd.yaml had:
- V1 Engine: config/test_mp_reducer.py
- Basic Models (Other): the vision test
- Distributed Models: the 2-GPU vision test on shard 2
- MoE Kernels: the AITER commands


2. test-amd.yaml gains a command that only test_areas had: LoRA TP gets test_batched_loras_tp.

3. New optional jobs in test-amd.yaml for groups it didn't have:
- DeepSeek MTP Parallel Load
- AL DFlash
- AL DSpark
- Multimodal PPL
- FP4/INT4 MoE Kernels
- Qwen4 Exp


**Brings test-amd.yaml and the test_areas/*.yaml AMD mirrors into parity:**

1. A test group present in both files now runs the union of its commands on both sides.
2. Groups that only exist in test_areas get an optional copy in test-amd.yaml.
3. No existing job is removed, split or moved.
4. Where both sides pinned a different version (torchao, the Mamba branch), the newer one is kept.
5. Groups that run on a different GPU in each file are left for a follow-up.

title: [Bug]: Sparse-indexer DCP top-k merge allocates (1 + 2 * dcp) * 8 * T * K bytes per step that the profile run never sees, OOM on the first long prefill
body:
## Your current environment

vLLM nightly `v0.30.1rc1.dev245+gaf7f9488c` (`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`), 4x H200, CUDA 13.
Model: `Inferact/GLM-5.3-NVFP4` (DSA sparse MLA, index_topk 2048), `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --decode-context-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --max-model-len 786432 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.945 --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'`, prefix caching on, chunked prefill on.

## Describe the bug

With DCP > 1 the sparse indexer merges each rank's local top-k into the global top-k in `_merge_dcp_topk_global` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py:83-133`). The merge is a plain-allocator transient of three tensors per call:

- `packed`, `(T, K, 2)` fp32, `sparse_attn_indexer.py:116-120`: `8 * T * K` bytes;
- the all-gather output, `(dcp * T, K, 2)` fp32, allocated by `DeviceCommunicatorBase.all_gather` (`vllm/distributed/device_communicators/base_device_communicator.py:257-259`): `8 * dcp * T * K` bytes;
- the copy `all_gather` makes to move the rank dimension inside: `reshape((dcp, T, K, 2)).movedim(0, 1).reshape((T, dcp * K, 2))` (`base_device_communicator.py:263-269`) cannot be a view, so it materializes another `8 * dcp * T * K` bytes while the un-moved output is still alive.

Peak per rank is `(1 + 2 * dcp) * 8 * T * K` bytes, on top of the `logits` tensor the caller still holds. `T` is the number of query rows in the indexer prefill chunk, up to `max_num_batched_tokens` (`sparse_attn_indexer.py:553-555` and `:630-638`); the decode call (`:780-787`) is bounded by the cudagraph batch and is small. With `T = 8192`, `K = 2048`, `dcp = 4` that is 128 MiB * 9 = 1.13 GiB per rank per step.

The profile run does not see any of it. The dummy run has no attention metadata, so the indexer takes the profiling branch (`sparse_attn_indexer.py:364-412`): it reserves the K-gather workspace and the radix top-k scratch through the workspace manager (`:369-381`) and allocates the `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` dummy (`:385-388`), then returns. The merge buffers are not in `profile_specs` and that branch never calls the merge, so the KV cache is sized as if the merge cost nothing. Whether the engine survives then depends on how much slack is left below `gpu_memory_utilization`; where that slack is under about 1.2 GiB the first long prefill fails:

```
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 512.00 MiB. GPU 3 has a total capacity of 139.79 GiB of which 498.00 MiB is free. ...
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py", line 630, in sparse_attn_indexer
    _merge_dcp_topk_global(
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py", line 130, in _merge_dcp_topk_global
    gathered = get_dcp_group().all_gather(packed, dim=1)
```

(512 MiB is `8 * dcp * T * K` for the numbers above; the first prefill was 8 requests of 32k tokens, scheduled as 8192-token chunks.)

In our case the headroom was smaller than usual on purpose: the image also dropped a workspace reservation the mixed-batch path never reads (PR linked below) and ran with `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0`, which together handed about 3 GiB per rank to the KV cache. With the cudagraph estimate at its default the same prefill passes, because the estimate over-reserves by about 1 GiB here (separate issue), which happens to cover the merge.

Line references are from main at `eec2a86b1e`; the nightly above has the same code.

## Reproduction

Any DSA model with DCP > 1 and a prefill batch that fills `max_num_batched_tokens`, on a host where the memory profiler leaves less than `(1 + 2 * dcp) * 8 * max_num_batched_tokens * index_topk` bytes of headroom. Raise `--gpu-memory-utilization` until the profiled budget leaves under 1 GiB free, then send eight 32k prompts at once.

## Proposed fix

Either of these makes the cost visible to the profiler and bounds it:

1. Reserve the merge buffers through the workspace manager: add `((T_max, K, 2), fp32)`, `((dcp * T_max, K, 2), fp32)` and `((T_max, dcp * K, 2), fp32)` to `profile_specs` when `dcp_world_size > 1` (`sparse_attn_indexer.py:369-381`) and take them from `get_simultaneous` in `_merge_dcp_topk_global` instead of `torch.empty` plus the communicator's out-of-place `all_gather` (`dist.all_gather_into_tensor` into the reserved buffer, then the transpose copy into the third one). The KV budget then shrinks by the true cost instead of the engine finding out on the first prefill.
2. Chunk the merge over rows. `pack_dcp_topk_candidates_cutedsl` takes `row_starts` per row and `stable_topk_from_gathered_candidates_cutedsl` is row-independent, so processing, say, 1024 rows per iteration caps the transient at `(1 + 2 * dcp) * 8 * 1024 * K` (144 MiB for dcp 4, K 2048) with no change to the result. Combined with (1) the reservation becomes small enough not to matter.

Related but different: #55132 is about the indexer reserving too much for the decode logits during profiling on ROCm; this report is about a buffer the profiling run does not reserve at all.

title: [Bug]: CUDA graph memory estimate (#53306) reports 2.16 GiB against 1.19 GiB actually captured on GLM-5.3 TP4/DCP4: the profiling pass measures things the real capture does not, and the FULL extrapolation uses the second-largest graph as the per-graph cost
body:
## Your current environment

vLLM nightly `v0.30.1rc1.dev245+gaf7f9488c` (`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`), 4x H200 NVL (139.79 GiB each), CUDA 13, model runner V2.
Model: `Inferact/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`, `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --decode-context-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --max-model-len 786432 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.945 --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'`, `cudagraph_mode FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, capture sizes `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, ..., 256]` (35 sizes), `compilation mode NONE`, `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS` at its default.

## Describe the bug

Startup log, per rank (identical on all four):

```
Capturing CUDA graphs (PIECEWISE): 35/35
Capturing CUDA graphs (FULL): 2/2
Capturing prefill CUDA graphs (FULL): 17/17
Capturing decode CUDA graphs (FULL): 7/7
Graph capturing finished in 23 secs, took 1.76 GiB            <- profile_cudagraph_memory pass
CUDA graph memory profiling is enabled ... --gpu-memory-utilization=0.9450 is equivalent to 0.9295 without CUDA graph memory profiling ...
Available KV cache memory: 13.32 GiB
...
Capturing CUDA graphs (PIECEWISE): 35/35
Capturing CUDA graphs (FULL): 17/17
Capturing prefill CUDA graphs (FULL): 17/17
Capturing decode CUDA graphs (FULL): 7/7
Graph capturing finished in 16 secs, took 1.19 GiB            <- real capture_model
CUDA graph pool memory: 1.19 GiB (actual), 2.16 GiB (estimated), difference: 0.97 GiB (82.5%).
```

The estimate takes 0.97 GiB per rank out of the KV cache budget that the capture does not use (2.16 GiB / 139.79 GiB is the 0.0155 utilization delta in the log). Reading `profile_cudagraph_memory` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py:870-983`) against these numbers splits the 0.97 GiB into two parts.

### 1. The profiling pass measures more than graph memory (0.57 GiB here)

`profile_cudagraph_memory` returns `measured - sum(mem_samples) + first_capture + (N - 1) * per_graph` (`cudagraph_utils.py:951-953`, `:975-983`), where `measured` is the return value of `capture_model(profile_only=True)`: the free-memory delta around the whole capture (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:1043-1044`, `:1081`, `:1090`), taken with `torch.accelerator.get_memory_info`, so it is everything the process allocated during that window, not the graph pool.

In the log the profiling pass reports 1.76 GiB with only 2 of the 17 FULL graphs captured, while the real pass reports 1.19 GiB with all 17. The profiling pass therefore charged at least 0.57 GiB that the real capture did not need, before any extrapolation. The two passes differ in what has already been allocated when they start: in `determine_available_memory` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:633-644`) the profiling capture runs right after `profile_run`, while the real capture runs in `compile_or_warm_up_model` after the warmup dummy runs, `kernel_warmup` and `warmup_kernels` (`gpu_worker.py:866-885`). Anything the model allocates on first use of the decode-shaped forward (persistent workspace growth for decode kernels, communicator buffers for the DCP all-gathers, the MTP draft's buffers, JIT and autotune scratch) lands inside the profiling delta and outside the real one. That is a hypothesis about which allocations make up the 0.57 GiB; the log does not say, because nothing in the profiling pass is logged apart from the total. It is the same class of problem as #50780 (a transient of the first FULL sample charged as graph memory), with a different set of allocations.

### 2. The FULL extrapolation uses the second-largest graph as the cost of every remaining graph (0.40 GiB here)

`_FULL_GRAPH_PROFILING_SAMPLES = 2` (`cudagraph_utils.py:864`) captures the two largest FULL descriptors (`_capture_descs` is sorted by `num_tokens` descending, `:367-369`, sliced at `:450`). `_extrapolate_full_graph_memory` (`:975-983`) then takes `mem_samples[1]`, the delta of the second-largest graph, as `per_graph` and adds it `N - 1` times. With N = 17 the estimate exceeds `measured` by 2.16 - 1.76 = 0.40 GiB, so `per_graph` came out at about 27 MiB. The per-graph delta is not constant: after the first graph has grown the pool, what a later graph adds is dominated by buffers whose size follows `num_tokens` (the outputs that outlive the capture, plus whatever the pool cannot reuse), so the second-largest graph (256 tokens here) is close to an upper bound for the fifteen smaller ones (1 to 200 tokens). Two samples give no information about the slope, and `_MIN_PER_GRAPH_BYTES` (`:866`) only bounds it from below.

I cannot separate how much of the 0.40 GiB is real from the log either: the real pass's 1.19 GiB is one number for 35 PIECEWISE, 17 FULL and 24 speculator graphs.

### What I would change

1. Log the components. `mem_samples`, `N`, `measured` and the extrapolated total at INFO in `profile_cudagraph_memory`, and have the "actual vs estimated" line in `compile_or_warm_up_model` (`gpu_worker.py:888-901`) say that the two numbers are measured in different states. Without this the 82.5% is not actionable for a user or for this report.
2. Measure the pool, not the free-memory delta. The profiling pass already captures into a private throwaway pool (`cudagraph_utils.py:901-904`). Summing the segments that belong to that pool (the allocator snapshot carries a `segment_pool_id` per segment) gives the graph memory itself and excludes the first-touch allocations of part 1. The same measurement on the real pool would make the "actual" number comparable.
3. Extrapolate with a size term or stop extrapolating. Either fit `per_graph(num_tokens)` from the largest, a middle and the smallest FULL descriptor, or capture all FULL descriptors in the profiling pass when their count is small (17 here; the real pass captured them in 4 s). #51590 goes the second way for a different reason (undercounting on ROCm) and would resolve part 2 as a side effect; it does not address part 1.

Related: #50780 (overcount from the first FULL sample's transient on hybrid GDN models), #44740 (negative estimate with MTP), #57936 (the `--kv-cache-memory` suggestion double-counts the estimate), #51590 (open PR: profile every descriptor instead of extrapolating).
