title: [RFC]: Weight Reload Refactor
body:
> **Revisions**
> - **Rev 3 (2026-10-19), current.** Design changes from rev 2:
>   - DIRECT modules run PWAL once at finish; only MODULEWISE modules run it as they complete.
>   - One `refresh()` tree walk replaces `register_refresh`, `refresh_model()` and `post_load_setup()`. MLA absorption moves into the attention layer's `refresh()`, so no PWAL reads another module.
>   - `reload_safe` flags on every post-load component (quant methods, kernels, attention layers and impls), checked once at `init_weight_transfer_engine`. `SupportsReload` becomes a marker.
>   - Coverage at finish (failing an update with a missing shard) is deferred. Completion stays.
> - Rev 2 (2026-10-17): direct loading by default with modulewise fallback, arrival units, opt-in core, one PR per family. Responses to the rev 1 review are [below](#user-content-responses-to-review).
> - Rev 1 (2026-09-30): layerwise with first-touch materialization, element counting, full integrity first. Full text is in the edit history.

## PR Tracker

```
PR 1 fixes + harness ─► PR 2 post-load contract ─► PR 3 core (opt-in) ─► family PRs (Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi, Nemotron) ─► flip default ─► delete layerwise
                                                              └──────► RDT / nccl_m2n (separate design) ─────────────────────────────────┘
```

- [ ] **PR 1: Reload fixes on main, refit harness** (#61287)
  - Fixes on today's path: gpt-oss Quark and fused-BF16 experts through the param loader; loader routing for colpali, colqwen3/3.5, nano_nemotron_vl, nemotron_parse, pixtral, voxtral; KV-scale dtype on reload; FlashInfer device bmm scales; online block-FP8 QuantFP8 op; DeepSeek-V3.2 indexer pairing state on `self`.
  - Refit-equals-fresh harness and tests.
- [ ] **PR 2: Post-load contract, no behavior change** (#60931)
  - The `refresh()` tree walk, `reload_safe` flags, the `SupportsReload` marker, the reload-safety check and `check_reload_support`.
  - MoE kernels built once, with weight-derived values refreshed in place: FP8, MXFP4, NVFP4, CT/Quark FP8, online FP8/INT8/MXFP8.
  - Cold start runs the same refresh walk and stays bitwise identical to main. Build-once applies only under the core; layerwise keeps main's rebuild.
- [ ] **PR 3: Reload core, opt-in** (`VLLM_RELOAD_CORE=1`)
  - DIRECT / MODULEWISE per module, arrival units and completion, post steps, slim integrity, the `collective_rpc` fix.
  - Benchmark: sync time and peak memory against layerwise.
- [ ] **PRs 4…N: one per supported family**: move weight-derived model-level work into `refresh()`, add `SupportsReload`, audit model-local loaders, add a refit case on the core.
  - [ ] Qwen
  - [ ] GLM
  - [ ] DeepSeek
  - [ ] Kimi
  - [ ] Nemotron
- [ ] **Flip the default** to the core. `VLLM_RELOAD_LEGACY=1` selects layerwise.
- [ ] **RDT / `nccl_m2n`** (separate design).
- [ ] **Delete layerwise**, one release after the flip and after the RDT / `nccl_m2n` track.

## TL;DR

RL frameworks update a running engine through `start_weight_update` → `update_weights` → `finish_weight_update`. The NCCL and IPC transports, and `reload_weights` from a path, all feed checkpoint-format tensors to the model's own `load_weights` under **layerwise reload**. Layerwise works for every quantization method, but:

- **Memory.** It buffers incoming tensors until a module is complete. Under NCCL broadcast that includes other ranks' TP rows and every expert the rank doesn't own.
- **Stale state under CUDA graphs.** PWAL rebuilds kernel objects, and values they derive (MoE alphas, `1/a1_scale`, FlashInfer KV scales) move while captured graphs keep reading the old addresses.
- **Silent failures.** Completion is inferred from element counts, writes other than `aten.copy_` are invisible, and a failed update can resume serving half-updated weights.

After an update, the engine must serve exactly what a fresh load of the same checkpoint would, with the cold-start CUDA graphs still in place and bounded extra memory. This RFC proposes a reload core built on four decisions:

1. **`load_weights` is the contract.** Every transport ends by passing checkpoint-named tensors to `model.load_weights`. Neither transports nor RL frameworks touch quant methods, kernels or module internals.
2. **Write in place when the live bytes can hold the checkpoint tensor (DIRECT).** Otherwise fall back to MODULEWISE: layerwise without GPU buffering or element counting. The choice is made per module, from metadata.
3. **PWAL is the only checkpoint → kernel transform, and kernels are built once.** After an update PWAL rewrites the same tensors in place, and `refresh()` hooks, found by walking the module tree, recompute derived state.
4. **DIRECT costs no extra memory for weights.** MODULEWISE scratch is only this rank's partition of a module, freed as soon as it completes.

The core lands opt-in and purely additive. Supported families convert one PR at a time, then the default flips and layerwise is deleted a release later.

**Scope.** We officially support and validate five families: Kimi, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM and Nemotron. Other models can opt in the same way; until they do, they get a warning, not a guarantee.

## Goals and non-goals

**Goals**

- A fresh-load-equivalent engine after every successful update, with CUDA graphs reused.
- One contract for every transport that feeds `load_weights`: IPC, NCCL (packed or not) and disk.
- Peak extra memory bounded by the per-rank scratch of the MODULEWISE modules open at once, and zero for DIRECT modules.
- Fail loudly before any write when an update can't be done correctly. A failed update never silently resumes serving.

**Non-goals**

- Rollback, and inverse transforms from kernel layout back to checkpoint layout.
- Partial (sparse or delta) writes into kernel layouts.
- Sharded RDT and `nccl_m2n`. They write into storage without calling `load_weights` on every update, so they get a separate design and stay on layerwise until then.
- Coverage: proving at finish that every module received its weights. Deferred (see [Loading](#user-content-3-loading-arrival-units-and-completion)).
- Improving layerwise. It stays the default until the flip and is then deleted.

## Proposed design

"Module" means any `nn.Module` that directly owns loadable tensors (a `QKVParallelLinear`, a `RoutedExperts`), not a decoder layer.

### 1. External API

The RL-facing calls are unchanged, on `LLM`, `AsyncLLM` and the HTTP router: `pause_generation` → `start_weight_update` → `update_weights` (any number of times) → `finish_weight_update` → `resume_generation`. A transport is correct if it delivers the same name/tensor pairs a checkpoint on disk would.

**Failure contract.**

- A failed start, update or finish raises on the caller. vLLM aborts the update, puts the original tensor objects back, and marks the engine dirty, because DIRECT modules may hold half-written bytes.
- While dirty, `resume_generation` refuses, so requests queue instead of reaching a corrupted model. The next successful full update clears the flag; a sparse update can't. With multiple ranks, every rank agrees before resuming.

**Kept internal.** Frameworks never see the DIRECT / MODULEWISE choice, when PWAL runs, quant-method hooks, `SupportsReload`, or the core's environment flags. `check_reload_support()` (`GET /check_reload_support`) returns the reload-safety report (§5), so frameworks can read it at startup.

### 2. Pre-processing: DIRECT and MODULEWISE

Every weight loader writes into a tensor shaped like the checkpoint, so each module needs such a target.

- **DIRECT (new).** If the live bytes can hold the checkpoint tensor, they are the target. The loader writes straight into live memory, and PWAL transforms it in place at finish. Nothing is allocated for the weights.
- **MODULEWISE (fallback).** On a module's first write, the core materializes checkpoint-layout scratch and the loader writes into it directly. When the module's expected units are in (§3), PWAL runs, the results are copied into the live tensors, and the scratch is freed. Only modules still receiving data hold scratch.

**Deciding whether scratch is needed.** Right after the model is constructed, `record_metadata_for_reloading` snapshots every param and persistent buffer as a meta tensor, keeping its class and `__dict__` (so `weight_loader`, `input_dim` and so on survive). That snapshot is the per-rank partition in checkpoint layout, from `create_weights`, before any PWAL. At `start_weight_update` the core compares it with the live tensor:

| Target | When | Extra memory |
|---|---|---|
| As-is | Live tensor matches the snapshot exactly and owns its storage | 0 |
| View | Different shape or stride, but the live bytes are large enough, aligned, and not shared | 0 |
| Scratch | Anything else: online quant (BF16 in, FP8 live), tensor subclasses, released params | The module's per-rank shard in checkpoint dtype |

A module is DIRECT when every tensor is as-is or a view; otherwise the whole module is MODULEWISE, so PWAL always sees one consistent layout. The decision follows from what PWAL actually did to the tensor, never from a quant method's claim. One exception keeps the big weights DIRECT: a small scale that PWAL shrinks gets a temporary **side buffer**. In per-tensor FP8 MoE the checkpoint `w13_weight_scale` is `[E, 2]` and PWAL reduces it to `[E]`; only that scale is buffered, and `w13_weight` / `w2_weight` are still written in place.

| Module | Path |
|---|---|
| Unquantized; block FP8; MXFP4 / NVFP4 weights; most MoE, shuffled or not | DIRECT, as-is |
| Per-tensor FP8 linear (`[K,N]` live vs `[N,K]` checkpoint) | DIRECT, view |
| Per-tensor FP8 / NVFP4 MoE | DIRECT, scales in side buffers |
| Online quantization (BF16 checkpoint, FP8 or MXFP8 live) | MODULEWISE |
| torchao subclasses, kernel-held opaque weights | MODULEWISE |

Two rules keep DIRECT safe: no forward runs between start and finish (start checks the engine is paused), and a DIRECT module's PWAL runs only at finish, after every module has landed. `VLLM_RELOAD_DIRECT=0` forces MODULEWISE everywhere. GPU incoming tensors are never buffered; CPU incoming tensors for a MODULEWISE module wait in host memory and are replayed into scratch once its units are in.

### 3. Loading: arrival units and completion

The core needs to know when a module is complete, for correctness (PWAL on a half-written module corrupts it) and for memory (MODULEWISE scratch can only be freed after landing). The trainer can't say: it sends checkpoint names in any order and batching, and doesn't know how vLLM fuses them (q, k, v into `qkv_proj`).

**Why not count elements.** Layerwise compares elements `copy_`'d with the module's size. Shared scale slots and duplicate shards over-count, so PWAL fires early on partial data. Padding under-counts, so scratch is held until finish. Writes other than `aten.copy_` are invisible.

**Count loader calls instead.** The core wraps every `weight_loader`; each call becomes a key `(module, tensor, shard, checkpoint name)`, with `shard` read from the loader's own arguments (`"*"`, `"q"`, `("w1", 7)`). A dry run of `load_weights` over metadata only gives each module its expected count per key. Each call decrements its key, and a module is complete when all counts reach zero.

- Counting writes, not names, matters: the shared MoE loader turns one fused `experts.gate_up_proj` name into 2E calls, and under EP each rank declines the experts it doesn't own, so the expected counts differ per rank and must be observed from the real loaders.
- Expected counts come from, in priority order: trainer metadata (sent at `init_weight_transfer_engine` when `send_weight_metadata` is on), the checkpoint's safetensors headers, or the keys observed during the cold load.
- Loaders usually need nothing. A loader that skips another rank's data calls `report_declined()`.
- An unexpected key warns and that module completes at finish (correct, costs memory). A key arriving more often than exact metadata declares raises. A call after its module completed raises.

**How each path uses it.** MODULEWISE: counts reaching zero trigger PWAL, landing and freeing scratch. DIRECT: only "touched" matters; at finish PWAL runs on every touched DIRECT module in tree order, and an untouched one is skipped (its bytes are already kernel layout).

**Coverage (deferred).** Finish doesn't yet check that every count reached zero. Callers are assumed to send the whole model; a module never sent keeps its old weights, and a DIRECT module sent only in part would get PWAL over mixed bytes. The counts are exactly what the coverage check will read once it lands.

### 4. Post-processing: PWAL and refresh

**When PWAL runs.** Each module has one PWAL, the one cold start calls: its quant method's, or the attention layer's own.

| Module | PWAL runs |
|---|---|
| MODULEWISE | As soon as the module completes, so its scratch is freed early |
| DIRECT | At finish, if touched |
| Declared `pwal_at_finish` | At finish, on every rank, in tree order |
| Declared `none` | Never: the loader already wrote kernel layout (as #60096 does for MegaMoE) |

The declaration is `reload_post_step` on the quant method. `none` is opt-in, listed by the reload-safety report, and needs a refit test. No PWAL needs `pwal_at_finish` today; it stays for future cross-module or EP-collective cases.

**Collectives.** Some PWALs run collectives: online FP8 amax over TP or the MoE group, static FP8 / NVFP4 MoE input scales over EP under EPLB, MLA with DCP. We assume every rank in a group receives data in the same order, which holds for NCCL broadcast, so ranks of a TP group complete a MODULEWISE module at the same point. EP is the exception (see [Known issues](#user-content-known-issues)).

**Build once.** Rebuilding kernel objects or derived tensors after cold start leaves captured graphs reading freed or stale storage. Kernels are built at cold start and reused on update (`FusedMoEMethodBase.reuses_kernel()`), derived tensors are registered buffers filled in place, and values computed from weights are recomputed by `refresh()`.

**Refresh: one hook, found by walking the tree.** After every PWAL and landing, one function walks the model children first, calling `quant_method.refresh(module)` and then `module.refresh()` wherever defined. It replaces `register_refresh` (the MoE runner's fused gate and KDA's merged conv just define `refresh()`), `refresh_model()` (the model class defines `refresh()`, reached last), and the derived half of attention PWAL (MLA `W_UK_T` / `W_UV` move into the attention layer's `refresh()`). A kernel's internal chain (quant config → prepare/finalize → experts) stays inside `quant_method.refresh`. Cold start and core finish call the same walk; layerwise is unchanged.

Rules for a refresh:

1. It reads only params and buffers, not another object's derived tensors.
2. It writes only derived tensors it declared, in place, allocated on the first call (at cold start, before graph capture).
3. It is idempotent.
4. It runs on every rank, unconditionally, never skipped because a module wasn't touched (MLA with DCP all-gathers inside absorption).

Setup that isn't derived from weights (compiling, memory placement) stays where it is; it only has to be harmless to rerun if an update reruns it.

### 5. Reload safety: `reload_safe` and `SupportsReload`

Each post-load protocol is a promise by a different author. Before the first update, the engine checks that every piece of this model, with this quantization and serving config, has made it.

**Each author stamps their own code.** `reload_safe` flags go on `QuantizeMethodBase` (default False; may be a property to veto a backend branch), on the kernel bases (MoE prepare/finalize and experts, the linear kernel bases), on `AttentionLayerBase`, and on `AttentionImplBase` (default True). A flag covers that author's code, including its `refresh()`, and nothing it delegates to. Runtime-chosen components (the kernel a method's oracle picked, the attention impls the selector picked) carry their own flags, so the check ANDs the objects actually in use. The model author vouches only for model code (module classes, `load_weights`, the model's `refresh()`) by implementing the marker `SupportsReload`; that code is trusted, not inspected, and refit tests prove the values.

**The check** runs once at `init_weight_transfer_engine`, after cold start: one pass over `named_modules()` checking the root for `SupportsReload`, each quant method AND the kernel it built, and each attention-like layer with a PWAL AND its impls. Each finding is SAFE, UNSAFE (names the module, component and reason) or UNVERIFIED (no marker).

**Enforcement**, refusing only what is known wrong:

- UNSAFE components are refused on the core under CUDA graphs and warned in eager mode.
- UNVERIFIED and the layerwise path only warn.
- `VLLM_RELOAD_ALLOW_UNSAFE=1` turns refusals into warnings (generalizes `VLLM_RELOAD_ALLOW_UNSAFE_MOE`).
- `start_weight_update` keeps its runtime checks for what can change after init: live tensor signatures and kernel objects replaced since the last update.

**Why a model's own PWAL is never called on reload.** Quant-method and attention PWALs have one job, converting their own tensors, so they can be rerun. A model's or submodule's own PWAL is arbitrary code that mixes weight-derived work, one-time setup and code that only works once. Reload can't tell these apart, so it calls none of them; the contract asks model authors to move weight-derived work into `refresh()`.

**Opting in.** PR 2 opts in everything known safe today (unquantized linear and embedding, the KV-cache method, the MoE backends in today's safe lists, `Attention`, `MLAAttention` and their default impls, the kernel bases they use). Anything new starts at False. To opt in a quant method, follow `Fp8MoEMethod`: always transform, build the kernel only if it doesn't exist, keep derived values in registered buffers that `refresh()` recomputes, set `reload_safe`, add a refit case.

### 6. Integrity (slim, in PR 3)

1. **Pause check.** The engine core refuses `start_weight_update` unless no step can run: `PAUSED_ALL`, or `PAUSED_NEW` with no requests left.
2. **Abort and dirty on failure.** Any exception aborts the session (original objects back, loaders unwrapped, scratch freed), sets the dirty bit and re-raises. A new start aborts a leftover session.
3. **No resume while dirty.** `EngineCore.resume_scheduler` (also called by `wake_up`) refuses while any worker is dirty. New requests queue rather than being rejected, which hung offline DP `generate()` on the prototype.
4. **Clearing.** The next successful non-sparse update clears the bit.
5. **`collective_rpc` after a one-rank failure.** `MultiprocExecutor.collective_rpc` now reads every expected reply before raising, so stale replies don't leak into the next call. Not gated by the flag.

Full integrity (auto-pause, serve guard, module sets on the API, structured reload report) is a follow-up.

### 7. What the opt-in flag gates

With `VLLM_RELOAD_CORE` unset, none of these run and layerwise behaves as on main:

| Place | Gated behavior |
|---|---|
| `start_reload` / `finish_reload` | Choose layerwise |
| Cold load | Key observation and the name-tracking wrapper |
| `init_weight_transfer_engine` | The dry run over trainer metadata |
| `reload_weights` | The safetensors header dry run |
| Engine core | The pause check and slim integrity |
| PR 2's reload-side behavior | Build-once, strict landing, refusal of UNSAFE components |

Sharded RDT and `nccl_m2n` call the layerwise entry points directly, so they stay on layerwise before and after the flip.

## Peak memory

Extra GPU memory of an update is at most: the transport's receive buffers (packed NCCL defaults to 2 × 1 GiB), DIRECT side buffers (scales only), the scratch of MODULEWISE modules open at once (each this rank's shard, about one module when the trainer sends in module order), and PWAL's own temporaries (the same as cold start).

Kimi K3 estimate (93 layers, 896 routed experts in 92 MoE layers, MXFP4 routed experts, everything else BF16), peak extra memory per GPU from the routed experts, on top of the transport buffers:

| Case | Path | EP = 8 | EP = 16 | EP = 64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MXFP4 checkpoint, MXFP4 serving | DIRECT, as-is | ≈ 0 | ≈ 0 | ≈ 0 |
| Online quantization (BF16 checkpoint) | MODULEWISE, one layer open | 6.9 GiB | 3.4 GiB | 0.86 GiB |
| Layerwise today, MXFP4 checkpoint | One layer materialized | 1.8 GiB | 0.92 GiB | 0.23 GiB |
| Layerwise today, online quantization | One layer of BF16 | 6.9 GiB | 3.4 GiB | 0.86 GiB |

This assumes layer-ordered sends; if the trainer interleaves layers, every partly sent MODULEWISE module holds its scratch (worst case all 92 layers, 317 GiB per GPU at EP = 16).

Measured on the prototype (single GB200, Qwen3-30B-A3B, peak over baseline):

| Model | Core | Forced MODULEWISE | Layerwise |
|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 | 0.64 GiB | 2.32 GiB | 2.62 GiB |
| FP8-block | 1.29 GiB | 1.75 GiB | 2.10 GiB |
| Online FP8 | 2.85 GiB | 2.85 GiB | 3.18 GiB |
| NVFP4 | 0.59 GiB | 1.48 GiB | 1.47 GiB |

Sync time hasn't been measured on the code this plan lands; PR 3 reports it for the core, forced MODULEWISE and layerwise, over packed NCCL from a sharded trainer.

## Known issues

- **Host-float scales baked into CUDA graphs.** The KV-cache method also keeps q/k/v scales as Python floats (`_k_scale_float`), which some decode paths pass as kernel arguments, so captured graphs bake them in and no in-place refresh changes them. The core refuses a change only for impls declaring `float_scales_in_decode` (FlashInfer). K3's CuTe DSL MLA decode reads them without declaring it, as do the native FlashInfer decode wrapper, DCP decode and attention + output-quant fusion. Fix options: detect any changed `_*_scale_float` and refuse under graphs, or make them 0-dim device tensors. RL checkpoints usually keep KV scales fixed.
- **A collective PWAL in a MODULEWISE module under EP.** Ranks decline different experts, so they can complete the same module at different points; a PWAL collective over the EP group could hang. It doesn't arise today: the EP collectives (input scales under EPLB) belong to static FP8 / NVFP4 MoE, which are DIRECT and run at finish. The fallback is `pwal_at_finish`, at the cost of holding that module's scratch.
- **MoE methods not declared `reload_safe`** are refused on the core under graphs: NVFP4 on B12x, MXFP8 on Triton, MXFP4 on FlashInfer CUTLASS, online MXFP4.
- **DeepSeek-V4 with FlashInfer MoE-EP experts** keeps weights in a FlashInfer object that graphs likely read; it needs an in-place refill API.
- **Level-2 sleep** frees all GPU memory and restores only registered buffers; off-registry constants come back as garbage until registered (#60009). `sleep(2)` followed by `wake_up()` also resumes before weights are reloaded.
- **EPLB.** `build_expert_params_mapping` uses the initial placement, so a reload after a rearrangement may write each expert into its startup slot. Not reproduced yet; needs a regression test and an update gate (#59063).
- **Validated only at small scale.** A full-size Kimi K3 / DeepSeek-V4 refit in graph mode (EP ≥ 2, DeepGEMM MegaMoE) is pending.

## Relation to RFC #54477 and #58382

[RFC #54477](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54477) (Selective Weight Reload) and its PR #58382 share this RFC's goals: stable `data_ptr()`s, `load_weights` as the only router, kernels built once, derived state refreshed in place, and explicit failure semantics. #58382's direct mode (loaders write live params; finish checks nothing moved) is this RFC's DIRECT-as-is case.

| | #54477 / #58382 | This RFC |
|---|---|---|
| Live layout ≠ checkpoint layout | Loader-side quantization, or explicit staging | View, side buffer or MODULEWISE scratch, chosen automatically |
| Transform on reload | Per-method refresh hooks | PWAL itself, the same code cold start runs |
| Derived state | `refresh_derived_state()` per method | `refresh()` found by the tree walk |
| Failure | Terminal | Dirty bit: paused until a successful full update |

We'd like one shared implementation of the refresh contract and the reload-safety check.

## Responses to review

| Comment | Response |
|---|---|
| **@aoshen02 1: staging should be the exception.** | Adopted in rev 2. DIRECT is the default; MODULEWISE only when live bytes can't hold the checkpoint tensor, chosen automatically from the snapshot. |
| **@aoshen02 2: completion from element counts is fragile.** | Adopted. `CopyCounter` is replaced by counting loader calls against expected counts observed from metadata. Coverage at finish is deferred in rev 3; the counts are what it will read. |
| **@aoshen02 3: reload runs a different PWAL branch; loader first; latency unmeasured.** | Reload runs the same PWAL as cold start. A module whose loader writes kernel layout declares `none` (#60096 does this for MegaMoE). PR 3 reports sync time and peak memory against layerwise. |
| **@ShuoleiWang 1: dirty clears on an empty finish.** | Dirty clears only on a successful non-sparse update on the core. |
| **@ShuoleiWang 2: required keys per name, not per shard; duplicate shards.** | Keys are per shard and per local expert. A key arriving more often than exact metadata declares raises. Missing-shard detection at finish comes with coverage (deferred). |
| **@ShuoleiWang 3: `refresh_derived_state` misses attention; sparse NCCL patches.** | The refresh walk runs on every module on every update, touched or not, attention included. Session-less sparse patches are unchanged and correct only where live layout equals checkpoint layout; sparse updates are refused while dirty. |

## Prototype and validation

**Rev 1** ([`hao-aaron/vllm:modulewise-reload-clean`](https://github.com/hao-aaron/vllm/tree/modulewise-reload-clean)) validated the modulewise mechanism on 4× GB200: about 25 configurations reloaded bitwise equal to a fresh load in graph mode with zero pointer changes, across dense, MLA, Mamba hybrid, FP8 / NVFP4 / MXFP4 MoE backends and online quantization, over NCCL, IPC and sharded RDT.

**Rev 2** ([`hao-aaron/vllm:reload-direct-modulewise`](https://github.com/hao-aaron/vllm/tree/reload-direct-modulewise)), built as a GPU-gated stack: reload unit and integration suites, refit-equals-fresh cases, online cold start, tiny real-format family checkpoints and all nine MoE backend matrix suites pass, also with MODULEWISE forced everywhere; weight-transfer (127) and sharded RDT (219) suites pass; an end-to-end weight-sync audit passes on Qwen3-0.6B and OLMoE. Shadow mode (keys recorded next to `CopyCounter`) found the counter completing `RoutedExperts` early in 16 of 16 layers on OLMoE static FP8, and 3 early and 3 never-complete modules on tiny K3; the keys were right in each case.

## PR plan

**Why this order.** Model-by-model alone multiplies per-model reload paths with no shared contract. Core-first with the default on day one would silently serve stale state for models that still finalize inside `load_weights` or keep derived state in plain attributes. So: a general core, opt-in; then one family at a time; then flip.

**Principles.**

- The core is purely additive until the flip; with the flag unset no core code runs.
- Structural PRs first, model conversions last; family PRs can land in any order before the flip.
- Every intermediate commit passes the reload unit, weight-transfer and sharded RDT suites and the refit cases enabled so far. Cases failing on main start as `xfail(strict=True)`.

| PR | Scope | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fixes on today's path, refit harness (#61287) | main |
| 2 | Post-load contract: refresh walk, `reload_safe`, `SupportsReload`, build-once MoE, reload-safety check. No behavior change | 1 |
| 3 | The core, opt-in: paths, arrival units, post steps, slim integrity, `collective_rpc` fix, benchmark | 2 |
| 4…N | One per supported family | 2, 3 |
| Flip | Core becomes the default; gated by the refit and weight-transfer suites with the core on | all above |
| Delete | Layerwise, `CopyCounter`, `weight_loader_numel` and the flag, one release after the flip and the RDT / m2n track | Flip |

**Supported families.**

| Family | Candidates | Known conversion work |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen | Qwen3 dense and MoE; Qwen3.5 / Next | None known for Qwen3 |
| GLM | GLM-4.x MoE; GLM-5-Next | KDA merged conv weight → `refresh()` |
| DeepSeek | V3 / V3.2 (MLA); V4 / V4.1 with MTP and DSpark | mHC broadcast → `refresh()`; remove finalize-in-`load_weights` |
| Kimi | K2; Kimi-Linear (KDA); K3 with DSpark | DSpark stacks → `refresh()`; KDA side copies |
| Nemotron | Nemotron-H / Nano (Mamba hybrid) | To be checked |

#60096 and #60064 load MegaMoE experts and DeepSeek-V4.1 mega attention straight into kernel layout, so those have no post-load step left.

**Follow-ups.** Coverage at finish, full integrity, per-expert completion for online MoE if the benchmark shows it matters, and kernel-format (runtime-layout) updates.

**De-risking.** Shadow mode (done on the prototype), a loader audit per family, fault injection (drop or duplicate a shard, reorder, stop mid-update), property tests over random batching (refit equals fresh over 1000+ seeds), forced MODULEWISE as a required CI stage, flag-off equivalence until the flip, and end-to-end weight-sync audits at each step of the sequence.

## Open questions

1. **#54477 / #58382 authors:** can we share one refresh contract and reload-safety check?
2. **Rollout:** is opt-in → per-family validation → flip → delete the right path, and is one release between flip and deletion enough?
3. **Integrity scope:** is slim integrity enough for PR 3?
4. **Send order:** should the trainer helpers enforce layer-ordered sends, or only document them? MODULEWISE peak memory depends on it.
5. **Drafters:** should EAGLE / MTP / DSpark drafters update with the main model or stay frozen? Until decided, they warn.
6. **Kimi K3 deployment shape:** which EP / TP do RL users run, so the estimate above can be checked against a measured run?
7. **FlashInfer owners:** is there an in-place refill path for the MoE-EP `_mega_layer`, and device-scale entry points for the native decode wrapper and DCP decode?

## Related PRs

| PR | Relation |
|---|---|
| #54477, #58382 | Selective Weight Reload RFC and its direct-reload PR |
| #60931 | PR 2: post-load contract |
| #61287 | PR 1: reload fixes, refit harness |
| #60009 | Registers every persistent device tensor as a parameter or buffer; PR 2 aligns its derived-tensor registration with it |
| #57733 | Model-level finalization moved into the model's PWAL. On the core that PWAL stays cold-start only, so family PRs move weight-derived parts into `refresh()` |
| #60096, #60064 | MegaMoE and DeepSeek-V4.1 mega attention loaded straight into kernel layout |
| #49459 | DIRECT reload for layout-identical tensors; generalized here |
| #55595, #50521, #53509, #49789 | Derived state across rebuilds; build-once removes the rebuild |
| #51520 | `nccl_m2n` backend; stays on layerwise |
| #59063 | EPLB update gate |

*Thanks to @new-TonyWang for an early review, and to @aoshen02 and @ShuoleiWang for the reviews that shaped rev 2.*

## CC

@aoshen524 @aoshen02 @new-TonyWang @RyanClark2k @kwen2501 @Ronald1995 @SumanthRH @ShuoleiWang

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Bump DeepGEMM pin for SM107 JIT compatibility
body:
## Overview

Bump both DeepGEMM pins to `550036ad`, which includes the SM107 runtime JIT workaround merged in [vllm-project/DeepGEMM#23](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/23). This addresses Rubin startup failures tracked in [deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#461](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/issues/461).

## Claims

- Use the merged workaround through both CMake vendoring and the standalone installer, with matching dependency pins.
- On physical SM107, DeepGEMM selects the compatible `100f` JIT target while preserving device capability reporting and other architectures' compiler targets.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Pre-commit on both changed files, shell syntax, and diff checks | Passed |
| Fresh CMake FetchContent check with CUDA compilation disabled | Fetched exactly `550036ad` and initialized the expected CUTLASS/DeepJIT submodules |
| C++17 host harness compiling the fetched JIT header with mocked CUDA calls | Only SM107 changed to `100f`; SM90, SM100, SM103, SM120, SM121 and a synthetic SM108 were preserved |

Commands run for the changed files:

```bash
git diff upstream/main --check
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake tools/install_deepgemm.sh
bash -n tools/install_deepgemm.sh
bash tools/install_deepgemm.sh --help
```

Prior Rubin startup and serving checks used a custom build with the same JIT override at an earlier dependency revision, as described in [DeepGEMM#23](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/23). The combined revision has **not** received a full CUDA build, GPU serving smoke test, or model accuracy evaluation in this update. Fresh GPU validation and CI are still needed; no performance improvement is claimed.

## Details

The pinned CUTLASS 4.2.1 headers lack native SM107 feature guards. DeepGEMM#23 temporarily selects the compatible SM100 family JIT target for physical SM107 devices. Its removal requires validated native SM107 support in DeepGEMM.

The bump from `e1f418c` also includes DeepGEMM #10/#14 (SM120) and #17/#19/#22 (NVFP4 Mega MoE). Their GPU paths need regression coverage. Related [vLLM#59385](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59385) proposes an earlier pin for SM120 page-32 support; this revision also includes the SM107 fix.

The original vLLM patch and its application logic have been reverted. Validate using a fresh dependency checkout: CMake can reuse an existing `_deps/deepgemm-src`, and an externally installed `deep_gemm` can override the vendored copy.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Exempt exactly the blocks an async KV load writes from zeroing
body:
## Overview

Prevent allocator zeroing from racing async KV loads, including sliding-window blocks below a local prefix hit and circular-buffer blocks at index 0. Keep zeroing enabled for groups the selected connector does not load.

## Claims

- Exempt newly allocated external blocks in exactly the groups declared by the connector; synchronous loads still zero before loading.
- Introduce `get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids(request)`, moved from #59197: prefix-cacheable groups by default, all transfer groups for NIXL/Mooncake P/D, and request-selected delegation for MultiConnector. #59197 consumes the same API for replay decisions.

## Validation

- Final unit run: 649 passed, 4 GPU/integration cases excluded by the command below. The two GPU setup cases were also exercised separately.
- Two GPU setup cases initially hit concurrent memory profiling failures; both passed when rerun sequentially on a separate GPU. The async failure fixture now declares its loaded group.
- Pre-commit and Python 3.12 mypy passed. Tests cover store/P/D group selection, async/sync zeroing, KpoolTail allocation, MultiConnector routing, replay and failure recovery.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_decode_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  -k "not test_multi_example_connector_consistency and not test_multi_connector_handle_preemptions_integration and not test_fewer_blocks_with_hma and not test_multi_connector_mixed_hma_disables_hybrid_kv_cache" -q --disable-warnings
pre-commit run --files <changed-files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <changed-python-files>
```

</details>

Earlier end-to-end results, collected before this API move: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D with NIXL, 1P1D TP4 + TP4, two-pass GSM8K 5-shot, concurrency 512. Pass 2 includes decode-side prefix hits. “Other wrong” excludes prompts with N % 32 == 31 (#59330); “t < 16” counts those with (N - 1) % 128 < 16. These model evaluations were not rerun for the API refactor.

| Build | Pass 1 | Pass 2 | Other wrong | t < 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.9174 / 0.9249 | 0.9219 / 0.9189 | 98 / 101 | 18 / 15 |
| #59330 + #59197 | 0.9234 | 0.9113 | 113 | 20 |
| #59330 + #59197 + this PR | 0.9242 | 0.9212 | 98 | 9 |

## Details

Token-range slicing cannot identify all transferred blocks for non-prefix-cacheable windows or circular buffers. Allocation already knows the new physical blocks; the connector now identifies which groups it restores. The scheduler passes those group IDs to allocation, replacing `_skip_zero_block_ids` and `get_zeroing_block_ids_in_range`. Store/offloading connectors retain zeroing for their excluded scratch/window groups.

Failed-load recovery is unchanged: multi-group loads free and retry; single-group partial failures re-record the unwritten suffix. Tests cover async/sync loads with and without the window, circular-buffer zeroing, and MultiConnector selection.

Not a duplicate: #59197 uses this shared contract to skip replay; #59164 concerns synchronous MoRIIO READ destinations; #55085 handles unwritten Mooncake Store tail pages; #52187 concerns worker-side per-group zeroing.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Accept needs_kv_cache_zeroing in SinkFullAttentionManager
body:
## Purpose

Since #44490 the KV cache coordinator passes `needs_kv_cache_zeroing` to every single-type manager, but `SinkFullAttentionManager` still spelled out its parent's old `__init__` signature. Any model using `SinkFullAttentionSpec` (openPangu with `StaticSinkAttention`) fails at KV cache manager init with `TypeError: SinkFullAttentionManager.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'needs_kv_cache_zeroing'`, whether or not zeroing is enabled.

This forwards `**kwargs` to the parent, matching the other manager subclasses (RSWA, SWA, chunked-local, Mamba, HiSparse), and adds a regression test that constructs the manager with `needs_kv_cache_zeroing=True` and checks its new blocks are recorded for zeroing.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this constructor (searched `SinkFullAttentionManager` and `needs_kv_cache_zeroing`; #47271 and #43374 modify nearby sink code but not this).

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/test_kv_cache_spec_registry.py
```

## Test Result

The new test fails on main with the `TypeError` above and passes with the fix; both files pass (81 passed). No model eval: the change only fixes a startup crash and does not affect outputs of models that already started.

title: [Core] Release the checkpoint page cache after weight loading
body:
Overview
  
  Release the model checkpoint from the OS page cache once weight loading completes, from the generic model loader. Reuses drop_checkpoint_cache() introduced in
  #56926, which until now was only reachable from one model.
  
  Claims
  
  - Returns the host memory consumed by reading the checkpoint as soon as loading finishes, instead of leaving it for the kernel to reclaim reactively under
    pressure.
  - Measured 545-707 GiB returned within 3-4 s of load completion on a 1.45 TiB checkpoint; per-NUMA-node free memory recovers from 10-64 GiB to 555-599 GiB.
  - Applies to every model and every load format - previously only deepseek_v41 released this memory, and only on its Engram THP path.
  - 12 lines of production code; the eviction mechanism itself is reused, not reimplemented.
    
  Validation 
  
  Measured on an 8-GPU tensor-parallel deployment spanning 2 nodes (~1.3 TiB host RAM per node), 1.45 TiB checkpoint in 96 safetensors shards,
  load_format=fastsafetensors. Host free memory sampled every 5 s per NUMA node.

  | run | free at end of load | free after eviction | released | vs idle baseline |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | A | 722.7 GiB | 1291.4 GiB | **+568.8 GiB** | -88.7 GiB |
  | B | 569.1 GiB | 1276.2 GiB | **+707.1 GiB** | -106.7 GiB |
  
Both land within 15 GiB of each other and within ~90-107 GiB of the node's idle baseline. The difference in released reflects how much cache survived to the end
  of loading, not a difference in effectiveness.
  
  Timeline from run A:
  
  17:16:21  "Loading weights took 113.63 seconds"
  17:16:19  total free   746.7 GiB     <- trough
  17:16:29  total free  1291.4 GiB     <- eviction complete, +545 GiB
  17:18:xx  a 640 GB host allocation proceeds into already-free memory
  
  The per-NUMA detail is the sharper signal: node 0 sits pinned at 10.6-10.7 GiB for the final minute of loading, then recovers to 555 GiB. Reproduced across four
  multi-node runs.
  
  Unit test added and passing alongside the existing drop_checkpoint_cache tests. ruff, typos, SPDX, lazy-import and mypy-3.12 hooks pass.
  
  Details
  
  Why a barrier. The eviction covers the whole checkpoint directory, and ranks reach this point seconds apart (~3 s measured across 8 ranks). Without
  synchronisation the first rank to finish would evict shards a slower peer has not read yet, forcing a re-read from what is usually a network filesystem. The
  existing deepseek_v41 call sites have no barrier; they are per-model and narrower in scope.
  
  Why it is unconditional. The page cache is dead the moment loading returns - the weights are on device. The trade-off is a re-read if the same checkpoint is
  loaded again on the same host shortly afterwards. Happy to gate it behind an env flag if maintainers prefer; that costs ~17 lines and an envs.py entry.
  
  deepseek_v41 now evicts twice - once generically, once on its Engram path. posix_fadvise is idempotent so the second is a no-op, and I have deliberately left
  that model's code untouched to keep the diff confined to the loader.
  
  Scope. BaseModelLoader.load_model is shared by all loaders (default, dummy, tensorizer, runai_streamer, sharded_state, modelexpress). Loaders without a local
  checkpoint - dummy in particular - are handled by the existing helper, which logs "No local checkpoint found ... skipping" and returns.
  
  Limitation. The new call site is not covered by the unit test, which exercises the helper directly; covering it would require constructing a full model load.

title: [Bugfix] Keep the GLM-5.3 kpool tail and Qwen4 QSA ring out of the null block
body:
## Purpose

Block id 0 is the null block. It is shared by every KV cache group and is assumed to stay zero. Since #35431, the runners mark rows that own no state with 0 in the block table, not `PAD_SLOT_ID`: dummy runs, CUDA graph capture and padding rows all carry 0. Two ring caches that address their pages through column 0 of the block table did not treat 0 as "no ring", so dummy runs wrote their rows into block 0:

- **GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail:** `_kpool_tail_slot_mapping_kernel` maps every token to `block_table[req][0] * kpool + pos % kpool`. Its torch fallback does the same.
- **Qwen4 QSA circular ring:** `circular_qsa_slot_mapping` and `_build_qsa_metadata_kernel` map tokens to `block_table[req, 0]` and kept every block `>= 0`. The compressed QSA path already keeps dummy slots inert (`test_qsa_compressed_metadata_keeps_dummy_slots_inert`); the ring path did not.

Every scheduled request owns its ring block, so a request on the null block has none. Its tokens now map to PAD, as the generic slot mapping does. The ring writers already skip PAD slots.

This is the same pattern as #58560, which fixes the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor ring.

## Changes

- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`: the kpool tail slot mapping (Triton and torch) emits PAD for requests on the null block.
- `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/qsa_cache.py`: the QSA circular ring slot mapping (torch and Triton) requires block `> 0`.
- Tests: the existing QSA circular metadata test, which runs the Triton builder, also checks a dummy batch (all-zero block table) and expects PAD. QSA tests that used block 0 as a real ring block now start real blocks at 1. This includes `_make_block_table` in the AMD pre-indexer test, which could randomly hand out block 0. For the kpool tail, the existing CPU padding test now ends with a padding request on the null block, and the existing Triton-vs-CPU test adds a mixed batch and an all-null dummy batch. Both check that the null-block request maps to PAD.

## Not a duplicate

- #58560 covers only the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor ring.
- #57158 zeroes block 0 after capture. That does not cover DP idle-rank dummy batches during serving.
- #57169 and #59297 move the kpool tail onto `CircularBufferSpec` / the packed layout but keep its slot kernel unchanged.
- #54296 masks out-of-range block indices in the generic slot mapping kernel, which neither ring uses.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_pre_indexer_amd.py tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

## Test Result

- Rebased on main `d6fe5dca68`. 102 passed, 16 skipped on GB200. The 16 skips are `test_qsa_pre_indexer_amd.py`, which requires ROCm.
- Control: with the QSA change reverted, the dummy-batch check fails: dummy tokens map to real slots in block 0.
- Control: with the kpool tail change reverted, the CPU padding test and the two null-block Triton cases fail.
- `pre-commit` passes.
- No model eval. Only tokens of requests on the null block change, and those are dummy or padding rows whose outputs are discarded. Real requests never own block 0 (`BlockPool` pops it as the null block at init), so their mappings and outputs are unchanged.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR. The submitter reviewed the changes and ran the tests above.

title: [Core] Move FlashInfer MLA decode workspaces into WorkspaceManager
body:
## Overview

Move the FlashInfer MLA decode workspaces (sparse trtllm-gen/cute-dsl, dense MLA, DSV4/DSV4.1 sparse) from module-global `torch.zeros` tensors into `WorkspaceManager` scratch. Part of #59055; with #59156 the memory is then released by `/sleep`.

## Claims

- The 394 MiB per GPU FlashInfer sparse-MLA workspace (GLM-5.3 / GLM-5.3-Flash) and the 128/256 MiB dense-MLA and DSV4 workspaces no longer stay resident while the engine sleeps once #59156 lands, and are no longer additive to the shared scratch while awake.
- No behavior change for the kernels: the buffers are requested at the same size, reserved before CUDA graph capture, and re-requested on every call (same pattern as `flashmla_sparse.py`, `prefill/trtllm_ragged.py`).
- The DCP sizing (`_required_workspace_bytes`) and `VLLM_FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BUFFER_SIZE` override are unchanged.

## Validation

- Read FlashInfer 0.7.0 (`mla/_core.py`, `data/csrc/trtllm_fmha_kernel_launcher.cu`, `cute_dsl/attention/{mla_decode.py,monolithic/mla_decode.py}`); 0.7.0.post1 (the pinned version) differs from 0.7.0 only in `aot.py`, `jit/gemm/core.py` and tests. On every decode path these backends use, the workspace holds only per-launch scratch (trtllm-gen: softmax-stats slab + split-KV scratch, semaphores live in the separate `multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer`; cute-dsl: split-KV `acc_o`/`acc_lse` partials consumed by the reduction kernel of the same call; SM120 sparse: `mid_out`/`mid_lse` partials), so no content survives between calls and no zero-init is needed. The prefill backends already hand trtllm-gen an uninitialized `WorkspaceManager` view.
- No other `WorkspaceManager` view is an input/output of these decode kernels on the paths read (inputs come from the persistent `topk_indices_buffer`, the index group, Triton converters, `_mtp_hidden_buffer`).
- Unit tests (H200, FlashInfer 0.6.12 venv): `tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_workspace.py`, `test_sparse_mla_backends.py`, `test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py`, `test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py`, `tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_decode.py`: 164 passed, 671 skipped (SM100-only), 18 failed; the 18 failures are identical on unmodified `main` in that environment (16 × `cp_gather_and_upconvert_fp8_kv_cache` signature mismatch of the local `_C` build in FlashMLA tests, 1 × FlashInfer 0.6.12 SM90 JIT build failure, 1 × `test_index_group_convert_during_piecewise_capture`).
- `pre-commit` (ruff, ruff format, mypy, etc.) passes on the commit.
- End-to-end, GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 with MTP, CUDA graphs and `--enable-sleep-mode` on 4× GB300, same image and node, on top of #59156 + #59158 + #59360 (so the `workspace` tag is released on sleep):
  - Memory per GPU after `/sleep` (nvidia-smi): 5945 MiB without this PR, 5551 MiB with it (-394 MiB, exactly the sparse-MLA workspace). Torch-allocated memory drops by 352 MiB while awake (263465 to 263113 MiB per worker) because the workspace now fits inside the existing 1520 MiB `workspace` slot; KV cache grows by 42 MiB.
  - Post-wake parity 0/0/0/0 MiB in both runs; 3 sleep/wake cycles (full, selective, full), 195/195 outputs identical to the pre-sleep reference in both runs; no `Workspace is locked` errors.
- Not validated: DCP, HiSparse, the dense `flashinfer_mla.py` path and the DSV4/DSV4.1 FlashInfer paths on a real model (V4-Flash in this image uses FlashMLA; forcing `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` rejects its packed KV layout).

## Details

- `flashinfer_mla_sparse.py`: `_get_workspace_buffer()` now requests `((bytes,), int8)` from the manager; a module-level int keeps the largest size requested so the DCP builder can still raise it in its `__init__`, before the first forward/capture. `FlashInferMLASparseImpl` and the SM120 impl reserve in `__init__` and re-request in `_run_mqa_kernel`; `_prepare_mqa_kernel` loses its `device` argument.
- `flashinfer_mla.py`: same, sized by `need_to_return_lse_for_decode` (known at construction).
- `deepseek_v4(1)/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py`: `_get_flashinfer_dsv4_workspace()` requests `((128 MiB,), uint8)`; the SM100 class reserves it in the dummy run (like the FlashMLA DSV4 path), the SM120 class already did via `_reserve_empty_forward_workspace`.
- Each `(ubatch, lane)` slot that runs these kernels grows to at least the workspace size; with DBO that is ×2, as for every other scratch user.
- Two tests that assigned `impl._workspace_buffer` directly now monkeypatch `_get_workspace_buffer`; the autotune test installs a `WorkspaceManager`.

title: [Core] Reuse one CUDA graph capture stream per device
body:
## Purpose

`graph_capture()` creates a new `torch.cuda.Stream` on every call. As a result, each capture pass (CUDA-graph memory profiling, model capture, speculator capture, encoder capture) runs on its own stream. PyTorch allocates a 32 MiB cuBLAS workspace for each stream at its first GEMM and keeps it until the process exits. Each extra capture stream therefore holds another 32 MiB, plus any other per-stream kernel state (for example DeepGEMM mHC barriers on DeepSeek-V4.1). This memory stays allocated while awake and is one of the untagged leftovers that survive `sleep()` (#59055).

This PR caches one capture stream per device. Every `graph_capture()` caller (`cudagraph_utils.py`, `encoder_runner.py`, `gpu_model_runner.py`) runs one after another on the worker thread, and the calls are never nested, so one stream per device is enough.

One thing for reviewers: PyTorch's `CUDAGraph::reset()` calls `clearCublasWorkspacesForStream()` on the graph's capture stream. With one shared stream, destroying any graph frees the workspace that every graph on that stream uses. Every current destruction path destroys all graphs together and does so before any recapture: profiling teardown happens before the real capture (and `freeze_gc_for_cudagraph_capture` runs `gc.collect()` first), elastic EP's `release_graphs()` clears the model and speculator graphs together, and shutdown destroys everything. On GB300 I checked after serving that the capture stream still held the same workspace (touching the handle allocated 0 bytes).

Why this is not a duplicate: no open PR changes the stream used by `graph_capture()`. #52553 deals with FlashInfer's GEMM workspace, not the per-stream cuBLAS workspace.

## Test Plan

- New CPU unit test `tests/distributed/test_utils.py::test_graph_capture_reuses_stream`.
- On 4x H200 in the CI image, with this branch's Python code on top: `tests/v1/cudagraph`, `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py`, `tests/distributed/test_pynccl.py`, `tests/distributed/test_pp_cudagraph.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py`, `tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py`, `tests/basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py`.
- On 4x GB300: DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + MTP with `--enable-sleep-mode`, on the nightly image with the sleep-mode stack (#59156, #59158, #59160, #59228) applied, with and without this change.
  - A 553-request round before sleep, compared token by token with the same round after wake.
  - 22 sleep/wake cycles, alternating full and selective wake. Each cycle runs a 64-request subset; every 10th cycle runs the full round.
  - Live 33,554,432-byte blocks outside any cuMem pool, counted from `torch.cuda.memory_snapshot()`.

## Test Result

- New unit test: 1 passed.
- `test_custom_all_reduce.py`: 50 passed, 1 skipped. `test_pynccl.py`: 15 passed. `test_pp_cudagraph.py`: 1 passed. `test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py`: 13 passed. `test_cumem.py`: 12 passed.
- `tests/v1/cudagraph`: 108 passed, 14 failed. All 14 failures are in `test_cudagraph_mode.py` and happen at model load, because the offline HF cache on the test machine has no weights for `Qwen/Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct`. I have not rerun these tests with the weights available.
- `test_sleep_mode.py`: 8 passed, 1 failed. The failing test is `test_deep_sleep_compressed_tensors_kv_scales`, whose model is not in the offline cache. Unmodified main fails it the same way.
- GB300, V4-Flash TP4 + MTP:
  - Before sleep vs. after wake: 553/553 identical, and memory changed by 0 MiB on all 4 GPUs.
  - 22/22 cycles bit-identical, with asleep and awake memory flat across cycles.
  - Untagged 32 MiB blocks per GPU: 5. An earlier snapshot of the same stack without this change had 6.
  - Asleep: 6249/6377/6377/6249 MiB per GPU, compared with 6313/6439 MiB for the stack without this change, a saving of 64 MiB per GPU. The run without the change is from an earlier launch on another node of the same type.

AI assistance was used for this PR (Claude Code). The submitter reviewed the change and ran the tests.

### Re-check on current main (`bdd31c31d`), GB300 (supersedes the earlier GB300 figure)

Re-checked on main bdd31c31d (applies cleanly), 4x GB300, DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + MTP,
--enable-sleep-mode, default V2 model runner, two launches each with and without this PR:
- Unit test: 1 passed, 3 runs (fails on main).
- CUDA graph capture memory: 5.56 GiB -> 4.94 GiB per GPU in every launch, so the KV
  cache grows from 201.51 to 202.13 GiB.
- Asleep: 10525 MiB/GPU in both launches with this PR vs 10869-11321 MiB/GPU on main
  (main's launches differ by a constant 452 MiB step unrelated to this PR), i.e. at
  least 344 MiB/GPU less.
- 3 sleep/wake cycles: 28/28 greedy and 28/28 seeded top-k/top-p outputs identical to
  the awake reference after every wake; wake 1.08-1.26 s (main 1.06-1.31 s).

title: [Core] Take the top-k/top-p Triton scratch from WorkspaceManager
body:
## Overview

Take the per-program float32 scratch of `apply_top_k_top_p_triton` from `WorkspaceManager`, reserved at its maximum size by the GPU model runners before capture and the workspace lock. Part of #59055; with #59156 the memory is then released by `/sleep`.

## Claims

- The sampler scratch (`min(num_sm, batch) × vocab × 4 B`; 77 MiB per GPU on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 92 MiB on GLM-5.3) no longer stays resident while the engine sleeps once #59156 lands, and no longer grows lazily under traffic after warm-up.
- Kernel behavior is unchanged: the same `(NUM_PROGRAMS, vocab)` float32 buffer is handed to `_topk_topp`.
- Callers without a reservation (CPU, tests, `diffusion_gemma`, the watermark sampler, batches larger than the reservation) keep the module-level cached buffer, so nothing can hit the workspace lock.

## Validation

- Unit tests (H200): `tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py`, `test_sampler.py`, `test_rejection_sampler.py`: 236 passed, 1 skipped, 7 failed; the 7 failures (`TestFlashInferDistributionMatch`, `No module named 'scipy'`) are identical on unmodified `main` in that environment.
- `pre-commit` (ruff, ruff format, mypy, etc.) passes on the commit.
- End-to-end, DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 with MTP, CUDA graphs and `--enable-sleep-mode` on 4× GB300, same image and node, on top of #59156 + #59158 + #59360:
  - Memory per GPU after `/sleep` (nvidia-smi): 6313/6439 MiB without this PR (an earlier 100-cycle run of the same stack on the same node, not a back-to-back A/B), 6023 MiB on all 4 GPUs with it. Only about 75 MiB of that is attributable to this change: torch-allocated memory outside the KV cache drops by 75 MiB (the lazily grown sampler buffer); the rest is caching-allocator reserved space (-162 MiB) and the +126 MiB the baseline shows on two GPUs from run to run.
  - Post-wake parity 0/0/0/0 MiB; 3 sleep/wake cycles (full, selective, full) with 195/195 outputs identical to the pre-sleep reference; no `Workspace is locked` errors.

## Details

- `reserve_topk_topp_workspace(vllm_config, device)` reserves `min(num_sm, max_num_seqs × (num_speculative_tokens + 1)) × vocab_size` float32 elements, the bound the kernel's own warm-up already uses (`_max_sampler_batch_size`), and records it per device. Both GPU model runners call it right after building their sampler, i.e. before kernel warm-up, capture and `lock_workspace()`.
- `apply_top_k_top_p_triton` requests `((NUM_PROGRAMS, vocab), float32)` from the manager when that fits the recorded reservation, else falls back to the existing cache. The reservation is a floor on the shared scratch slot, which the MoE workspaces already exceed on the models above.
- The sampler runs on the main thread in lane 0 after the forward; by the `WorkspaceManager` contract no view from the forward may be live across the next `get_simultaneous`, and none of the inputs (`logits`, `k`, `p`) is a workspace view.
- The split-row top-p cache (`_TRITON_SPLIT_CACHE`, ~1 MiB) is left alone.

title: [Kernel] EFC-style epilogues for the CuTe DSL Lamport TP all-reduce
body:
## Overview

Generalizes the consumer kernel of the CuTe DSL Lamport TP all-reduce (FlashInfer's `kernel_ll`, vendored for DSV4.1 in #58586) into one kernel whose epilogue is a Python function, modeled on CUTLASS's [Blackwell EFC example](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/tree/main/examples/python/CuTeDSL/cute/blackwell/efc). Draft for design feedback: no serving path calls it yet.

## Claims

- An all-reduce epilogue is now a short Python function, not a kernel template. `epilogues.py` has residual RMSNorm, Gemma RMSNorm, DSV4.1 mHC + RMSNorm, and RMSNorm or mHC followed by NVFP4, static FP8 or per-token-group FP8 (FP32 or UE8M0 scales).
- The generated kernels are bit-identical to the hand-written ones they generalize, and as fast:
  - residual RMSNorm and Gemma RMSNorm vs FlashInfer's `_LamportResidualRMSNormDeviceKernel`;
  - mHC + RMSNorm vs `_LamportMHCDeviceKernel` from #58586.
- Fused quant outputs are bit-identical to `scaled_fp4_quant`, `scaled_fp8_quant` and `per_token_group_quant_fp8`. Fusing saves 1.0–2.3 µs per boundary vs the all-reduce followed by the separate quant kernel, at M = 1–16 (TP4 GB300, hidden 5120).
- All epilogues share one Lamport mailbox, so each one works after both the plain publish and the MoE finalize publish.

## Validation

4× GB300 (one node), torch 2.13.0+cu130, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1, flashinfer 0.7.0, on main 87a4bf664f + this PR.

**Test**: `pytest -v -s tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py` → 52 passed (51 existing, including #58586's `test_all_reduce_mhc_matches_unfused_path`, plus the new test), 3m42s.

The new `test_all_reduce_efc_epilogues` needs 4× SM100 and skips elsewhere. For M in {1, 5, 16, 3}:
- The mHC epilogue matches `AllReduceMHC` (#58586) bit for bit.
- One epilogue stores the residual, the BF16 norm, NVFP4, static FP8 and group-128 FP8 (UE8M0) together:
  - the residual is bit-exact and the norm within 1 BF16 ULP of the epilogue's own torch reference;
  - each quantized output is bit-exact vs vLLM's quant op run on the kernel's BF16 row.
- The same epilogue is fed by the MoE finalize publish and compared against the plain publish of a torch finalize.
- CUDA graph replay picks up in-place input changes.

CI: this file runs in the optional 4× A100 Distributed job, where the SM100 tests skip (as #58586's does). No CI job has 4 Blackwell GPUs, so the runs above were done by hand.

<details>
<summary>Wider out-of-tree check (all bit-exact)</summary>

M ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 12, 16}, ±0 Lamport-sentinel collisions in the inputs:

- FlashInfer's `_LamportResidualRMSNormDeviceKernel` (`weight_bias` 0 and 1) compiled with the same tuning and run on the same mailbox, vs `residual_rmsnorm` and `residual_gemma_rmsnorm`. Both outputs match bit for bit; the norm is 0 ULP from the torch reference.
- `_LamportMHCDeviceKernel` on the same mailbox vs `mhc_rmsnorm`.
- vLLM's quant ops on the kernel's own BF16 row vs NVFP4, static FP8, and group-128 FP8 with FP32 and UE8M0 scales, after both RMSNorm and mHC.
- Torch reference: mHC within 1 ULP. NVFP4 differs from the reference in at most 22 bytes, because the reference divides exactly where the kernel (like vLLM's) uses `rcp.approx`.
- CPU-only compiles (`CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_100a`) for hidden 2048, 7168 and 16384 (clusters of 2, 7 and 8 CTAs; two trips per thread at 16384). Only hidden 5120 ran on GPUs.

</details>

**Kernel time**: µs per publish + consume. Each arm is captured in CUDA graphs of 8 and 40 calls; the per-call time is the slope between them, max over ranks, median of 50 replays. Hidden 5120, TP4. A second run on another node, before the rebase, agreed within ±0.1 µs.

| arm | M=1 | M=4 | M=8 | M=16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FlashInfer residual RMSNorm (hand-written) | 3.62 | 3.76 | 4.02 | 4.51 |
| EFC `residual_rmsnorm` | 3.63 | 3.78 | 3.98 | 4.46 |
| #58586 mHC + RMSNorm (hand-written) | 3.90 | 4.02 | 4.26 | 4.73 |
| EFC `mhc_rmsnorm` | 3.88 | 3.98 | 4.27 | 4.74 |
| EFC RMSNorm, then `scaled_fp4_quant` | 4.78 | 5.06 | 5.31 | 5.80 |
| EFC `residual_rmsnorm_nvfp4` | **3.70** | **3.84** | **4.06** | **4.55** |
| EFC RMSNorm, then `scaled_fp8_quant` | 5.21 | 5.47 | 5.71 | 6.21 |
| EFC `residual_rmsnorm_fp8` | **3.98** | **4.16** | **4.35** | **4.86** |
| EFC RMSNorm, then `per_token_group_quant_fp8` | 6.09 | 6.52 | 6.65 | 7.19 |
| EFC `residual_rmsnorm_fp8_group` | **4.12** | **4.27** | **4.53** | **5.03** |
| EFC mHC, then `scaled_fp4_quant` | 5.03 | 5.32 | 5.55 | 6.02 |
| EFC `mhc_rmsnorm_nvfp4` | **3.99** | **4.10** | **4.39** | **4.86** |

No end-to-end or accuracy numbers yet: nothing in serving calls this code, so no model output changes.

`pre-commit run` on the changed files and `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual`: pass.

## Details

**Writing an epilogue.** An epilogue is `fn(cfg, *params)`. Each parameter's annotation says how the kernel indexes that tensor:

| kind | tensor | interface |
|---|---|---|
| `Row` | [M, hidden]; reads BF16, writes BF16 / FP8 / packed E2M1 | `.load()`, `.store(v)` |
| `Streams` | [M, S, hidden] | `len(x)`, `x[s]` is a `Row` |
| `Weight` | [hidden] | `.load()` |
| `PerToken` | [M, *shape] FP32 | `x[i, ...]` is a per-token scalar |
| `DeviceScalar` / `Scalar` | one-element FP32 tensor / host float | `.load()` / the value |
| `GroupScale` subclasses (`NVFP4Scale`, `Group128Scale`) | one value per token and group; row-major or the NVFP4 128×4 layout | `.store(v)` |

`cfg` provides `accum()` (the FP32 cross-rank sum), `round(x, dtype)`, `row_sum`, `group_max`, `rsqrt`, `rcp_approx`, `where`, `maximum`/`minimum`/`clamp`, `abs` and `ue8m0_ceil`. For example:

```python
def mhc_rmsnorm_nvfp4(cfg, residual: Streams, post: PerToken, comb: PerToken, pre: PerToken,
                      weight: Weight, eps: Scalar, global_scale: DeviceScalar,
                      residual_out: Streams, q: Row, sf: NVFP4Scale):
    prenorm = mhc_post_pre(cfg, residual, post, comb, pre, residual_out)
    y = cfg.round(rms_norm(cfg, prenorm, weight, eps), torch.bfloat16)
    nvfp4_quant(cfg, y, global_scale, q, sf)
```

**Three phases.** As in EFC, the function runs three ways:
- an analysis pass with dummy values, which records which tensors and hc streams are read and written and counts the row reductions to size shared memory;
- device code generation, on each thread's 8-element fragments of the token row;
- a torch reference on [M, hidden] tensors.

**How this differs from the GEMM EFC.**
- One CTA cluster owns a whole token row, so an epilogue can reduce over the row (block plus DSMEM cluster sum, reusing FlashInfer's `_group_leader_block_sum`). It can also reduce over aligned groups of 16–256 elements with warp shuffles.
- Every load is hoisted ahead of the consumer's `griddepcontrol.wait`, as the hand-written kernels do. This is safe because the publish kernel waits on its own predecessor before it triggers the consumer.
- Rounding is explicit (`cfg.round`), so an epilogue states where the unfused path returns BF16. That is what lets the fused results match the unfused ops bit for bit.

**Duplicate check.**
- #59258 wires FlashInfer's fixed-pattern CuTe AR + RMSNorm into the compile pass, with static FP8 coming from flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5533. That PR adds graph-level dispatch; this one generates epilogues at the kernel level, covering patterns FlashInfer has no template for (mHC, NVFP4, per-group FP8, Gemma). They are complementary: that backend could dispatch to these epilogues.
- #51942 and #42597 use FlashInfer's fixed TRT-LLM fused all-reduce patterns.
- #58586 provides the protocol and the publish kernels reused here.

**Size.** About 1.9k lines (high complexity). The trade is that each new fusion costs about 10 lines of epilogue instead of a new consumer kernel; #58586's consumer alone is about 330 lines.

**Open before un-drafting.**
- The publish kernels and PTX primitives are imported from `vllm.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.ops.cute_dsl`, which pulls in the DSV4.1 model package. Move them here and have DSV4.1 import them; `AllReduceMHC` can then become `ar.bind(mhc_rmsnorm)`, deleting `_LamportMHCDeviceKernel`.
- Current scope: one rank lane, BF16 transport, hidden a multiple of 8, M up to the mailbox capacity (the low-latency regime), single-node NVLink multicast.
- Scale layouts are row-major or NVFP4 128×4; DeepGEMM's MN-major FP8 scale layout is not done.
- Static and group FP8 cost 0.35–0.6 µs more than plain RMSNorm. The cost is an IEEE division per element, needed to match vLLM's `x / scale` bit for bit; multiplying by a reciprocal would be cheaper but not bit-exact.
- No model wiring yet: the follow-up is to call these from #59258's backend or from the model files, then run evals.

title: Consolidate speculative decoding correctness and acceptance tests
body:
Speculative decoding tests repeat engine setup, GSM8K evaluation, acceptance-metric extraction, and threshold assertions across several suites. This makes fixes harder to apply consistently and makes it unclear which helper to extend for a new drafting method. We should share the common evaluation code while keeping each test's purpose and workload explicit.

## Current PRs:
* https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60239 by @adixg 
  * tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/eagle/utils.py
  * tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/_correctness.py
  * tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/speculators/test_speculators.py
  * common code to: tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/utils.py
* https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59602/ by @Dyslex7c
  * tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py
  * tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dspark/test_dspark.py
  * tests/v1/spec_decode/test_speculators_correctness.py
  * common code to: tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/utils.py

## Types of checks

- **Configuration and integration:** Checkpoint auto-detection, inferred target/draft models, method, speculative-token count, and basic generation.
- **Output correctness:** GSM8K accuracy and comparisons against non-speculative generation.
- **Acceptance regressions:** Overall acceptance rate/length and per-position acceptance against reference values.
- **Runtime behavior:** Async scheduling, unintended GPU–CPU synchronization, tensor/pipeline parallelism, and attention-backend compatibility.
- **Component correctness:** Rejection sampling, proposer/kernel behavior, dynamic SD, and adaptive verification.

These checks overlap in their setup and evaluation code, but they are not interchangeable.
For example, `test_speculators_model()` checks auto-detection and basic generation, whereas `assert_draft_model_correctness()` checks acceptance thresholds, optional GSM8K accuracy, and async scheduling.
Neither compares outputs against a non-speculative reference.

## Deduplication opportunities

### 1. Share accuracy and acceptance evaluation

[Draft-model tests](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/15ba199f0/tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_draft_model.py#L310), [XPress](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/15ba199f0/tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/xpress/test_xpress.py#L48), [DSpark](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/15ba199f0/tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dspark/test_dspark.py#L91), [DFlash](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/15ba199f0/tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py#L109), and [speculators correctness](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/15ba199f0/tests/v1/spec_decode/test_speculators_correctness.py#L186) repeat this workflow.

Extend shared configuration and evaluation helpers rather than copying the test body for each method.
Preserve the distinction between acceptance measured on separate prompts before GSM8K (draft model/XPress) and acceptance measured during GSM8K (DSpark/DFlash/speculators).
Sampling, batching, chat templates, and thresholds must remain explicit.

### 2. Consolidate acceptance-metric extraction

[Speculators correctness](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/15ba199f0/tests/v1/spec_decode/test_speculators_correctness.py#L92), [EAGLE3 acceptance](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/15ba199f0/tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_length.py#L180), and [shared SD utilities](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/15ba199f0/tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/utils.py#L189) contain overlapping calculations.

Use a common implementation for overall and per-position metrics, preserving denominators, zero-counter handling, and cumulative versus delta measurements.
Keep regression thresholds at the test/configuration level.

### 3. Share reference-comparison orchestration

[EAGLE](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/15ba199f0/tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/eagle/utils.py#L20), [MTP](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/15ba199f0/tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/test_mtp.py#L152), and [speculators integration](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/15ba199f0/tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/speculators/test_speculators.py#L28) already share `assert_request_outputs_match()`, but repeat reference/speculative generation and optional GSM8K evaluation.

Factor out the repeated orchestration while preserving method-specific setup and match thresholds.
Keep targeted regressions, such as MTP placeholder handling, separate.

### 4. Reuse the existing dataset acceptance helper

DFlash and Gemma4 MTP already use [`run_acceptance_length_eval()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/15ba199f0/tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/utils.py#L38).
Reuse it for future suites with the same sequential, per-prompt GSM8K/MT-Bench/HumanEval workload rather than introducing another evaluator.

~Start with metric extraction and accuracy/acceptance helpers in small changes.
Keep auto-detection assertions, runtime-specific checks, and component tests explicit rather than folding everything into one universal test.~

One example of reusing test code at high-level: https://github.com/tomasruizt/vllm/commit/b9a1ec2bdb12eceff6e840c2f1d69ed1e4425862

title: Diagnose NIXL PD handshake loopback (side-channel defaulting to localhost)
body:
## Problem

Setting up NIXL-based P/D disaggregation across nodes fails opaquely when the **producer** does not set `VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST` (its default is `localhost`):

- the producer advertises `localhost:<port>` as its handshake side-channel address,
- the consumer's `_nixl_handshake` connects to that address — **on the consumer's own host** — and reaches the consumer's own ZMQ listener,
- the only visible symptom is:

```
RuntimeError: Remote NIXL agent engine ID mismatch. Expected <producer engine id>, received <consumer's own engine id>
```

which reads like an engine-ID/plumbing bug and sends you digging in entirely the wrong place. (The request may even still succeed via the consumer's recompute fallback, so nothing else points at the handshake.)

## Change

One targeted branch at the mismatch site: when the received engine ID equals **our own** engine ID, the handshake provably looped back — raise a diagnostic that names the actual cause and fix:

```
Remote NIXL agent engine ID mismatch: the handshake reached this instance itself
(expected <producer>, received our own engine ID <self>). The remote instance most
likely advertised an unreachable NIXL side-channel address (the default
VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST is localhost). Set VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST on the
remote instance to an address reachable from here.
```

## Verification (two-node DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D, TP8 + TP8, NixlConnector)

1. **Repro** — producer started *without* `VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST`, request sent through `vllm-router`:
   - before this patch: `Remote NIXL agent engine ID mismatch. Expected f4c0…, received 1a2b…` (both are random per-instance UUIDs; no hint of the real cause);
   - after this patch: the new diagnostic fires in the same failing handshake, naming the environment variable.
2. **Healthy path** — producer restarted *with* `VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST=<its fabric IP>`: zero engine-ID mismatches, `NIXL compatibility check passed` on every consumer worker, KV transfer proceeds normally (`Transfer plan: local_tp=8, remote_tp=8`). No behavior change outside the loopback case.

This does not change any control flow — only the error message for a case that is currently undiagnosable from the log output alone.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Keep DeepSeek DSML tool arguments valid JSON
body:
## Overview

Keep DeepSeek DSML tool arguments valid JSON when model output contains `NaN`, `Infinity`, or overflowing exponents such as `1e999`. Preserve the original parameter text instead of producing non-JSON constants or losing it as `"Infinity"`.

## Claims

- Completed non-finite values, including values nested in arrays/objects, use the existing raw-string fallback; unfinished non-finite values wait for parameter completion.
- Wrapper unwrapping cannot reintroduce non-finite JSON by decoding the preserved string again.
- The shared DeepSeek V4/V3.2/V4.1 converter retains finite numbers, large integers, and quoted string values.

## Validation

The 38 new regression cases fail on unchanged source and pass with this patch. They exercise the production batch and streaming parsers at several chunk boundaries, strict JSON decoding, omitted/explicit string attributes, a `>` inside a JSON string before the non-finite value, wrapper handling, and an exponent that overflows as more digits arrive.

```bash
python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/parser/engine tests/parser/engine -q
```

Result: **5,376 passed**. Existing tokenizer fixtures were used on macOS arm64 CPU; no GPU or model-inference test was run. A source-checkout version warning was present. An additional comparison against the base implementation matched all 29 existing DSML corpus samples in batch and three streaming chunk sizes (116 comparisons).

## Details

Python's `json.loads` accepts non-finite constants and overflows large exponents to infinity; `json.dumps` then emits `Infinity`/`NaN` by default. Existing schema coercion does not necessarily inspect already-decoded nested containers. This reuses `_is_json_finite`, introduced for schema coercion in #43984, before retaining decoded DSML values and before unwrapping a decoded string wrapper. Literal fallback follows the converter's existing handling of values it cannot parse as JSON.

This is an AI-assisted draft, with source, tests, and validation prepared by agents for maintainer review.
