title: [Bugfix][KVConnector] Split MLA kernel rows larger than the NIXL block into dense pages
body:
## Overview

The NIXL connector registers MLA KV cache regions incorrectly when the model runner picks a larger kernel block for a KV cache group than the block size NIXL negotiates across all attention backends. This PR splits such rows into dense NIXL transfer pages. It reuses the path #53906 added for compressed MLA states.

## Claims

- Fixes `AssertionError: KV cache view cannot be partitioned into NIXL regions` at `register_kv_caches` when an MLA group's kernel row spans several NIXL pages.
- Fixes a silent case of the same mismatch. When the view happens to cover a block-major storage span, NIXL registers the whole backing storage as one region with the kernel-row stride. Transfers then address the wrong bytes without any error.
- Covers sliding-window MLA (`SlidingWindowMLASpec`) groups as well as full MLA.

## Validation

**Unit test.** New `test_register_mla_kernel_rows_larger_than_transfer_block` in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`. NIXL negotiates 64-token blocks (a second backend supports only 64) while the MLA group keeps a kernel block of 128 or 256.

| kernel block | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 128 | silently registers 1 region over the whole storage with stride = kernel row (wrong descriptors) | pass: 1 dense region per layer, 64-token pages |
| 256 | `AssertionError: KV cache view cannot be partitioned into NIXL regions` | pass |

**Regression suites** (B200): `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py` + `test_nixl_connector.py`: 379 passed (main: 377 passed; the difference is the 2 new cases).

**E2E smoke** (B200, 1P + 1D, NixlConnector):
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite` on `TRITON_MLA`, `--block-size 128`, with Eagle3 drafter `yschoi31/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Eagle3` on `FLASHINFER` (`use_trtllm_attention=false`). NIXL logs `logical block size (128) does not match physical kernel block size (64)`.
- GSM8K, 5-shot, 400 questions:

| setup | accuracy |
|---|---|
| standalone (no P/D) | 0.347 |
| P/D, `main` | 0.333 |
| P/D, this PR | 0.330 |

> [!NOTE]
> The e2e setup does **not** hit the bug. The target MLA layers and the drafter share one KV cache group, so the runner also picks 64 for the MLA group. I could not find an open-weights checkpoint on upstream that places MLA layers in a group without the smaller-block backend (e.g. MLA + sliding-window MLA layers with a drafter). The fix is therefore validated by the unit test, and the e2e run serves only as a no-regression smoke test.

## Details

**Root cause.**
- `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` selects a kernel block per KV cache group from that group's backends.
- `NixlBaseConnectorWorker._sync_block_size_with_kernel` selects one block size from *all* attention backends in the process. That includes a drafter on a backend with a smaller supported block set.
- When some group's kernel block (e.g. 128) is larger than NIXL's (64):
  - the cache view is `[num_blocks, 1, 128, C]`, so `stride(0)` is two NIXL pages;
  - NIXL's `num_blocks` is doubled, so `num_blocks * block_stride` exceeds the view.
- This either trips the partition assert or, when the storage-span check happens to match, registers whole storage rows.

**Fix.** Drop the `tokens_per_state > 1` requirement from `_uses_dense_virtual_transfer_pages` and accept `SlidingWindowMLASpec`. The geometry checks are unchanged:
- contiguous single-head-slot view;
- row is a whole multiple of the NIXL page;
- page count matches NIXL's `num_blocks`;
- view bytes equal `num_blocks * page`.

MLA rows are token-major and contiguous, so consecutive NIXL pages tile them exactly. Both peers derive the same pages, since `block_len`/`block_stride` are advertised in the handshake as before.

**Compatibility.**
- Unchanged: views whose row equals one NIXL page (the common case) and packed/strided views (not contiguous).
- DeepSeek-V4 `SlidingWindowMLASpec` caches only take the new path when their row spans several NIXL pages. That geometry was already broken before this change.

title: bench: add --metrics-url override for metrics scraping behind a router
body:
## Problem

`vllm bench serve` collects speculative-decoding (and diffusion) stats by scraping `{base_url}/metrics` before and after the run (`fetch_spec_decode_metrics` / `fetch_diffusion_metrics`). When the benchmark targets a **PD-disaggregated deployment through `vllm-router`**:

- `{router}/metrics` is not proxied to the backends (it answers `405 Method Not Allowed`),
- the actual `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters live on the **decode instance**,

so `fetch_spec_decode_metrics` returns `None` and every PD benchmark silently loses the acceptance section — no error, no hint.

## Change

Add an optional `--metrics-url` that overrides where server metrics are scraped from (defaults to the request base URL = previous behavior). For PD, point it at the decode instance.

## Verification (two-node DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D, vllm-router front-end, DSpark speculative decoding in both pools)

Without the flag (status quo):

```
Successful requests: 4        # ... but no Acceptance section at all
```

With `--metrics-url http://<decode-node>:8123`:

```
Successful requests:                     4
Acceptance rate (%):                     28.62
Acceptance length:                       2.43
  Position 0:                            60.24
  Position 1:                            35.86
  Position 2:                            21.89
  Position 3:                            14.67
  Position 4:                            10.41
```

Also confirmed directly: `curl {router}/metrics` → `405`; `curl {decode}/metrics` → 8 `vllm:spec_decode_*` series present.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Retain reasoning token counts across empty text deltas
body:
## Overview

Preserve reasoning-token usage when incremental detokenization produces empty text. For example, a byte-fallback tokenizer emits `中` from three token IDs, but streaming parsing currently reports one reasoning token while batch parsing reports three.

## Claims

- Retain ordinary token counts across empty deltas and stop-string buffering, assigning them after the surrounding control boundaries resolve.
- Preserve count-only prefixes and tails when deferred special-token boundaries resolve or flush.
- Keep byte tokens inside text-based control markers out of reasoning usage.

## Validation

The 59 added cases use a local Hugging Face ByteFallback tokenizer and the production vLLM incremental detokenizer, plus focused scanner checks. They cover DeepSeek V4, Qwen3, GLM4.7, a DeepSeek V4.1 text-tool boundary, several token batch sizes and stop-buffer holdbacks, incomplete UTF-8, and deferred THINK_END/DROP markers. **43 fail and 16 controls pass on the unchanged base; all 59 pass after the patch.**

```bash
python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/parser/engine tests/parser/engine -q
```

Result: **5,397 passed** on macOS arm64 CPU. Full pre-commit hooks, including mypy and test CI tethering, passed. An exact-base corpus comparison matched all 174 existing samples in batch and three streaming modes: **696 matching outputs and reasoning counts across 15 formats**.

The run used local tokenizer fixtures and excluded top-level GPU fixtures. A source-checkout version warning was present. No GPU, model inference, or live-server validation was performed.

## Details

The scanner previously discarded ordinary IDs when their incremental text was empty. Counting them immediately in the current state is insufficient: a detokenizer can buffer both text and a control boundary. The scanner now carries counts on the appropriate side of deferred markers, and the lexer holds count-only input until subsequent text or a flush determines whether it belongs to content or a text control marker. The engine propagates the resulting count-only events.

This targets lost empty-delta counts. Existing token/text alignment limitations with arbitrary text-only reasoning markers remain outside this change. Related #46159 handles replacement-character state transitions, whereas this change retains counts for empty text and deferred boundaries.

This is an AI-assisted draft, with source, tests, and validation prepared and independently reviewed by agents for maintainer review.

title: [Bugfix] Keep text after DeepSeek V3.1 tool calls
body:
## Overview

The DeepSeek V3.1 tool parser dropped any text that came after a tool-calls block on the non-streaming path. Streaming already returned that text. This is the same gap as #56263. #56265 covers the V3 parser only. This change is the V3.1 parser, which is a separate file and still registered as `deepseek_v31`.

## Claims

- `extract_tool_calls` returns the text before the tool-calls block plus the text after `tool_calls_end`.
- A missing end marker keeps the old behavior: prefix only.
- Tool names and arguments are unchanged.
- Streaming is not modified.

## Validation

The non-streaming cases were run here with a tiny in-memory tokenizer: prefix only, prefix plus suffix, and suffix only. All three returned the expected content and tool names. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` passed on the two files.

The existing unit tests download `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1` and were not run on this machine. Importing vLLM here fails before the tokenizer step.

```bash
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv31_tool_parser.py
```

## Details

`extract_tool_calls` used to slice at the start marker and ignore the rest. Streaming emits a content delta once the tool-call start and end counts match again, so the text after the block reaches the client only on the streaming path.

title: [ROCm][CI] Drop two no-GPU AMD mirrors from the CPU test areas
body:
## Overview

Removes the `(MI250) Basic Models Other` and `(MI250) Multimodal Processor Shard %N` AMD mirrors. Both set `no_gpu: true`, so they resolve to `CpuPlatform` and provide no ROCm coverage while occupying an MI250 agent.

## Claims

- With `no_gpu: true`, `amdsmi` reports no processor handle, `rocm_platform_plugin()` returns `None`, and vLLM falls back to `CpuPlatform`. Neither mirror runs a line of ROCm code.
- What is ROCm-relevant under them is already on a real card: `test_tensor_schema.py` in `(MI355 DPX) Multimodal Processor Shard %N`, and `model_executor/layers/test_activation.py` in `(MI300) Model Executor`.
- The other five paths have no ROCm branching, so a card tells us nothing a CPU agent does not.
- The NVIDIA/CPU parents are untouched: neither mirror overrode `commands:`.

## Validation

- `check_test_tethering.py --all` exits 0 with no output; no test file is left uncollected.
- Both YAML files parse, and the parents keep `commands`, `source_file_dependencies` and `parallelism` byte for byte against `main`.
- AMD mirrors go 206 → 204 and `no_gpu` 6 → 4; the 200 that claim a card are unchanged.
- Guard sweep over all six `Basic Models Other` paths and the whole `models/multimodal/processing` tree for `is_rocm()`, `version.hip`, `VLLM_ROCM`, `is_cuda_alike()`, `torch.cuda.is_available`, `ROCM_`, `gfx9`, `hipblas` and `AITER`: zero hits outside `test_tensor_schema.py`, which stays on a card.
- `models/multimodal/processing` was run on an MI300 under `RocmPlatform` and on a no-GPU arm under `CpuPlatform`. Results matched except three `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp` parametrisations that `_CPU_EXCLUDED_MODEL_IDS` drops on CPU, and those run on a card via `test_tensor_schema.py`.

## Details

The `(MI250)` and `(MI355 DPX)` processor-shard jobs were complementary, not duplicated: the `no_gpu` one ran the directory *except* `test_tensor_schema.py` and `(MI355 DPX)` runs *only* that file. Since the excluded file is where the ROCm behaviour lives, the `no_gpu` half contributed nothing.

For future audits, two things worth recording. `no_gpu: true` is not by itself a reason to remove a job — four AMD mirrors keep it deliberately because they cover the image rather than the hardware (`Docker Build Metadata`, both `Rust Frontend Cargo` jobs, `Torch Stable ABI Audit`), and none is affected here. And the label names the agent pool, not the mode: these two said `(MI250)` while running as CPU jobs, so enumerate by `no_gpu: true` rather than grepping for `(CPU)`.

title: [Core][KV Connector] Keep the connector's head order when its KV layout is unsupported
body:
## Overview

When the KV connector's requested layout is not supported by every backend, `resolve_kv_cache_layout` now falls back to the first candidate that keeps the requested head/token order, instead of the backends' first choice.

## Claims

- Mooncake (and NIXL) request `LBHNC` so heterogeneous-TP transfers can slice pages by KV head. On a hybrid model whose backends only accept block-outer layouts, the fallback now picks `BLHNC` (head-major) instead of `BLNHC`, so a page can still be cut by head.
- With that layout, prefill TP1 → decode TP2 over Mooncake works for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. With `BLNHC` the handshake fails.
- No throughput or latency cost on that model at equal TP (tables below).
- Connectors whose requested layout is supported, and runs with `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT` set, are unchanged.

## Validation

- New tests in `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`: `test_connector_layout_fallback_keeps_head_order` (an `LBHNC` request against `[BLNHC, BLHNC]` resolves to `BLHNC`, and against `[BLNHC]` still falls back to `BLNHC`), and `test_kv_cache_layout_is_head_major`. The first case fails without the change.
- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/distributed/test_kvlayout.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py`: 285 passed.
- pre-commit hooks pass on the changed files.
- End to end, on RTX PRO 6000 with Mooncake over RDMA, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (QSA attention + GDN, 2 KV heads), prefill TP1 → decode TP2. These runs set `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC`, the layout this change now selects, and used the connector with #53078 applied for the GDN state.
  - `BLNHC` (today's fallback): every pull fails the handshake, `local=39739392` (TP1 page registered as one opaque row) vs `remote=1605632`.
  - `BLHNC`: GSM8K (200 questions, 32 in flight) 0.970, 0 errors. A TP2 → TP2 pair scores 0.985 on the same set; the extra misses are coherent reasoning, not garbled output.
- Performance at equal TP2 (single instance, no connector, `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT` set, 8K in / 1K out random prompts, output tok/s):

  <details><summary>BLNHC vs BLHNC</summary>

  TP2, MTP3 speculative decoding:

  | C | BLNHC | BLHNC |
  |---:|---:|---:|
  | 1 | 236.1 | 235.6 (-0%) |
  | 4 | 653.9 | 643.8 (-2%) |
  | 16 | 1282.8 | 1293.8 (+1%) |
  | 32 | 1628.3 | 1640.9 (+1%) |
  | 64 | 1493.9 | 1491.0 (-0%) |

  TP2, no speculative decoding:

  | C | BLNHC | BLHNC |
  |---:|---:|---:|
  | 1 | 110.2 | 110.2 (+0%) |
  | 4 | 348.5 | 348.6 (+0%) |
  | 16 | 831.4 | 836.4 (+1%) |
  | 32 | 1176.1 | 1175.5 (-0%) |
  | 64 | 1214.0 | 1215.2 (+0%) |

  p50 TPOT is the same within noise at every concurrency.
  </details>

## Details

Mooncake and NIXL request `LBHNC` because a heterogeneous-TP transfer splits each page by KV head, which needs each head's tokens to be contiguous. QSA declares `(BLNHC, BLHNC)`, so `LBHNC` is not a candidate, and the fallback took `BLNHC`, where heads are interleaved per token. At TP2 a page holds one head, so it is still contiguous and equal-TP transfers work. At TP1 it holds two, cannot be sliced, and registers as one row the size of the whole block.

The fallback now picks the first candidate whose head/token order (`KVCacheLayout.is_head_major`, H outside N) matches the request, and otherwise the backends' first choice as before. The other layout requests follow the same rule: offloading and HiSparse ask for head-major layouts, and the example hidden-states connector asks for `LBNHC` to keep each token's data together, so an unsupported request now falls back to a token-major candidate.

Related: #53078 (Mooncake heterogeneous TP for hybrid GDN models) and #59592 (Mooncake block-size handshake), from the same TP1/TP2/TP4 testing. #58380 changes the layout order the worker reports for mixed page sizes and keeps connector requests taking precedence; it does not touch this fallback.

title: [Tests][Spec Decode] Deduplicate acceptance-metric and GSM8K evaluation helpers
body:
## Summary

Reworks this PR per review feedback toward higher-level reuse (single evaluation function) instead of small shared helpers, following the XPress consolidation pattern (`tomasruizt/vllm@b9a1ec2`).

three spec-decode test suites (DSpark, DFlash, speculators) each contained their own copy of the same check: run GSM8K, read the spec-decode counters, and compare accuracy and acceptance numbers against thresholds. Fixing or changing that sequence meant editing three files.

* Teaches the existing evaluate_llm_for_gsm8k() helper to accept GSM8K options (question count, temperature, chat template, and so on) and pass them through. When no options are given it behaves exactly as before, so the suites already using it (EAGLE, MTP, draft-model) are unaffected.
* Adds one small assert_spec_decode_metrics() helper that compares the acceptance rate and length against given thresholds. A threshold can be left out when a suite doesn't check it (DFlash and speculators don't check the rate).
* Rewrites the three suites to use these two helpers: run GSM8K, grab the metrics, assert. Each suite still sets up its own engine, picks its own GSM8K options, and keeps its own threshold numbers — only the repeated plumbing is shared. The speculators suite also keeps its own per-position acceptance checks, which the other two don't have.

Test-only change; no serving/output behavior change.

## Duplicate-work check

Not duplicating an existing PR:

* Searched open PRs for `spec decode test deduplicate` and `compute_spec_decode_stats` — no open PR covers this refactor.
* Aligns with the direction in `tomasruizt/vllm@b9a1ec2` rather than duplicating it (that commit lives on a fork; this repo has no `xpress/` suite to consolidate yet).

## Test commands and results

* `py_compile` on the touched file: **OK**.
* 88-char line-length check: **clean**.
* Module import check with GPU marks stubbed (this machine has no built vLLM/GPU, so plain `pytest --collect-only` fails environmentally at `@single_gpu_only` with `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not callable` from `UnspecifiedPlatform` — reproduces on the base file too): **IMPORT_OK**, and all new `ArgsTest` defaults verified behavior-preserving.
* Full GPU e2e suites were **not run** — require GPUs/models; needs `/ci run`.

## Model evaluation results

N/A — test-only refactor, no model, accuracy, or serving-path changes.

title: [Bug]: Structured output skips the `<tool_call>` that implicitly ends reasoning, so GLM-4.7/5.x `required`/named tool calls are lost
body:
> **AI disclosure:** this issue was investigated and drafted with an AI assistant (Claude). The reproducers were run on the hardware below, and every number in this issue comes from those runs. A human reviewed the issue before filing. ## Your current environment - vLLM main at `e5e38ba9b` (0.30.1rc1.dev505), editable install over the precompiled wheel for that commit. - 8x H100 80GB (SM90). All runs use TP4. - Model: `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`, `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45`. Default structured-output backend (xgrammar), default `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=1`.
vllm collect-env ``` ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.6 (Plow) (x86_64) GCC version : (GCC) 11.5.0 20240719 (Red Hat 11.5.0-5) Clang version : Could not collect CMake version : version 3.26.5 Libc version : glibc-2.34 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A XPU used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.9 (main, Mar 9 2026, 00:00:00) [GCC 11.5.0 20240719 (Red Hat 11.5.0-5)] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-5.14.0-570.98.1.el9_6.x86_64-x86_64-with-glibc2.34 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 CUDA_MODULE_LOADING set to : GPU 0: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 Nvidia driver version : 580.126.09 cuDNN version : Could not collect HIP runtime version : N/A MIOpen runtime version : N/A Is XNNPACK available : False ... (GPU 1-7: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3; CPU section omitted) ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1 [pip3] nccl-extensions==0.1.0 [pip3] nccl4py==0.6.0 [pip3] numpy==2.3.5 [pip3] nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.7.1 [pip3] nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.29.7 [pip3] pyzmq==27.2.0 [pip3] tokenspeed-triton==3.8.10.post20260920 [pip3] torch==2.13.0+cu130 [pip3] torch-c-dlpack-ext==0.1.5 [pip3] torchaudio==2.11.0+cu130 [pip3] torchcodec==0.16.0 [pip3] torchvision==0.28.0+cu130 [pip3] transformers==5.17.0 [pip3] triton==3.7.1 [conda] Could not collect ============================== vLLM Info ============================== ROCM Version : Could not collect vLLM Version : 0.30.1rc1.dev505+ge5e38ba9b (git sha: e5e38ba9b) vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled ```
## 🐛 Describe the bug **Expected:** with `tool_choice="required"` or a named tool, GLM returns the tool call, also when it goes straight from reasoning to `` without writing `` (the glm45/glm47 parsers accept that as the end of reasoning). **Actual:** the structured-output manager starts the tool grammar one token after that ``. The grammar never sees it, so it forces a second ``. The model writes `Write...`, the parser drops the call, and the response has `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` with no `tool_calls`. This happens in normal agent use. When a tool result quotes GLM's own tags, the prompt contains the real `` special token (id 154843), and the model sometimes copies it into its reasoning. On the prompt below, 7 of 40 seeds lost the call under `required` and 8 of 40 under a named tool. ### Reproduction Server: ```bash vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 32768 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 ``` (`--max-model-len 32768` only keeps startup short.) **1. Agent reads a file that mentions GLM's tags, then must call `Write`.** ```bash curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4", "temperature": 0.7, "seed": 8, "max_tokens": 1500, "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Read docs/parser.md and save a one-sentence summary of it to /tmp/summary.md."}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "Read", "arguments": "{\"file_path\": \"docs/parser.md\"}"}}]}, {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": "# Parser notes\n\nGLM-5.3 wraps every function call in ... tags; each argument is kv.\n"}], "tools": [ {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "Read", "description": "Read a file.", "parameters": {"type": "object", "required": ["file_path"], "properties": {"file_path": {"type": "string"}}}}}, {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "Write", "description": "Write a file.", "parameters": {"type": "object", "required": ["file_path", "content"], "properties": {"file_path": {"type": "string"}, "content": {"type": "string"}}}}}], "tool_choice": "required", "parallel_tool_calls": false}' | jq '.choices[0] | {finish_reason, tool_calls: .message.tool_calls, reasoning: .message.reasoning[-60:]}' ``` Expected: one `Write` call with `file_path` and `content`. Actual, in 4 of 4 runs: `"finish_reason": "tool_calls"`, `"tool_calls": null`. The reasoning stops mid-sentence at `...GLM-5.3 wraps every function call in`, which is where the model wrote ``. The raw output (from logprobs, `toolresult_repro.py`, seed 8) is: ``` ...GLM-5.3 wraps every function call in Readfile_pathdocs/parser.md<|obser... ``` Under `required` the doubled call is sometimes `Read` and sometimes `Write` (seed 17: `Writefile_path/tmp/summary.md...`). Either way the parser reads the name as `Read` or `Write`, drops it as unknown, and returns no call. Which seeds trigger varies between runs, so a loop over seeds is more reliable than one seed. Seed 8 with `required` triggered in every run we made. `toolresult_repro.py` (in the details below) loops over 40 seeds and counts a seed only if the first `` comes before any ``, the next output is a second `` (the special token or its text pieces), and the response has no complete `Write` call. Results on a fresh `e5e38ba9` server: | `tool_choice` | seeds lost to this bug (run 1) | (run 2) | |---|---|---| | `required` | 7 of 40 | 5 of 40 | | named `Write` | 8 of 40 | 4 of 40 | Under a named tool the response has no tool calls and `finish_reason` `"stop"` or `"length"`. Without `"parallel_tool_calls": false`, `required` keeps opening calls after the doubled tag: in 5 runs of the request above, 3 returned no call, one returned 15 calls (14 of them `Write({})`), and one looped until `finish_reason="length"`. **2. Deterministic variant with `logit_bias`.** `154842` is `` and `154843` is ``. The bias makes the model end its reasoning with ``. ```bash curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4", "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 400, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Paris?"}], "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "description": "Get the current weather for a city.", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}}}], "tool_choice": "required", "parallel_tool_calls": false, "logit_bias": {"154842": -100, "154843": 10}}' | jq '.choices[0] | {finish_reason, tool_calls: .message.tool_calls}' ``` Actual: `{"finish_reason": "tool_calls", "tool_calls": []}`. With `"tool_choice": "auto"` and no `parallel_tool_calls`, the same request returns `get_weather({"city": "Paris"})`. `parallel_tool_calls: false` only stops the +10 bias from opening extra calls. A small script that sends this request four ways gave the same result in 3 of 3 attempts:
live_repro.py output ``` [0] A auto (no grammar) tool_calls=[('get_weather', '{"city": "Paris"}')] finish_reason='tool_calls' | stream: ['get_weather'] 'tool_calls' raw output: ...'th the city "Paris".get_weathercityParis<|observation|>' [0] B required tool_calls=[] finish_reason='tool_calls' | stream: [] 'stop' raw output: ...'th the city "Paris".get_weathercityParis<|observation|>' [0] C named tool_calls=[] finish_reason='stop' | stream: [] 'stop' raw output: ...'th the city "Paris".get_weathercityParis<|observation|>' [0] D auto, parallel=off tool_calls=[] finish_reason='stop' | stream: [] 'stop' raw output: ...'th the city "Paris".get_weatherget_weathercityParis<|observation|>' ... 3/3 attempts: control A has the call, B, C and D lost it BUG PRESENT ``` A has no grammar. In B and C the grammar never saw the first ``, so it forced a second one. In D the `auto` grammar treated `get_weather` as free text and waited for its `` trigger. The same applies to `auto` with a `strict` tool, which we also saw lose the call (5 of 32 seeds on the tool-result prompt).
**3. CPU only.** A short script drives `StructuredOutputManager.accept_tokens` with the structural tag the server builds for `tool_choice="required"`: ``` model wrote: 'I need the weather.' grammar was fed: '' next tokens the grammar allows: ['<', ''] forced output: 'get_weathercityParis' parsed: tool_calls=None content=None BUG PRESENT: skipped by the grammar, required call lost ``` ### How often it happens On simple prompts GLM-5.3 almost always writes `` first: 0 of 128 `required` requests on a weather prompt at temperature 1 ended reasoning with ``. The trigger is a prompt that contains GLM's tool tags, for example a tool result or file that quotes them. There, 10 to 20% of seeds at temperature 0.7 lost the call. Separately, when this bug is fixed the request in (1) can still return `Write({})` on some seeds. That is a different bug: the reasoning ends with ``, then the `content` argument quotes `...` and the call is mangled. The seed counts above exclude it. ### Root cause Line numbers are on `e5e38ba9`. - `vllm/parser/glm47_moe.py:173-176` ends reasoning on `(REASONING, TOOL_START)`, emitting `REASONING_END` and `TOOL_CALL_START`. `ParserEngine._derive_reasoning_end_token_ids` (`vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine.py:615-635`) therefore puts both `` and `` into `reasoning_end_token_ids`. - `StructuredOutputManager._get_constraint_start` (`vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py:260-267`) returns `find_reasoning_end_offset(...) + 1`. The `+ 1` is right for ``, which is not part of the answer. It is wrong for ``, which is both the end of reasoning and the first token of the tool-call grammar. - `accept_tokens` (`vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py:444-466`) feeds `new_token_ids[constraint_start:]` to the grammar, so the `` is skipped. The frontend already treats this token as content. `ParserEngine.extract_content_ids` (`parser_engine.py:674-699`) returns `input_ids[i + 1:]` for `` but `input_ids[i:]` for the other reasoning-end ids. So the parser and the grammar gate disagree about where the answer starts. This came in with #55223 (merged 2026-09-08), which added `find_reasoning_end_offset` to `_get_constraint_start`. The refactor in #48200 kept the `+ 1`. A fix PR that links this issue follows. It lets the grammar consume a reasoning-end token that `extract_content_ids` keeps as content, while the bitmask still starts after that token, so speculative decoding does not force the end of reasoning early. With it, the seed loop in (1) finds 0 of 40 in both modes and the `logit_bias` request returns `get_weather({"city": "Paris"})`. ### Other parsers likely affected Only GLM was run live. For the other `ParserEngine` configs, we derived the reasoning-end token sets from the code. These also contain a tool-start token, which `_get_constraint_start` skips the same way: | Parser | Tool-start token in `reasoning_end_token_ids` | |---|---| | glm47_moe, qwen3, nemotron_v3, granite_thinking | `` | | seed_oss | `` | | gemma4 (thinking) | `<\|tool_call>` | | kimi_k2 | `<\|tool_calls_section_begin\|>` | | minimax_m2 | `` | | deepseek_v4 (thinking) | `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` | | mistral (special-token reasoning) | `[TOOL_CALLS]` | Whether a model actually ends reasoning this way, and whether its grammar starts with that token, varies per model. We did not check that live. ### Related No existing issue or PR covers this, as far as we found. Related but different: - #57714: kimi_k3, structured output never engages when the completion skips the think channel. Its fixes do not change the `+ 1`. - #44676: `thinking_token_budget` does not treat `` as an implicit reasoning end (Qwen3.5). Same implicit end, different component. - #58315: the GLM `required` grammar accepts split marker tokens that the streaming parser treats as content. - #39056: Qwen3.5 tool calls lost when the XML `` is emitted inside ``. - #44006 / #46149 (closed): the same reasoning/grammar boundary, under speculative decoding and for the structural-tag reasoning prefix.
toolresult_repro.py (standard library only; loops over 40 seeds) ```python #!/usr/bin/env python """Realistic live repro: a forced GLM tool call is lost after a tool result quotes GLM's own tag. An agent reads docs/parser.md (a Read call plus its tool result) and must save a summary with Write. The tool result mentions ..., and the chat template tokenizes that text into the real special token (154843). While thinking, GLM-5.3 sometimes copies that special token before any . The glm45/glm47 parsers treat it as the end of reasoning, but the structured-output manager starts the tool grammar one token later, so the grammar never sees it and forces a second . The parser then reads the name as "Write" and drops the call. Each seed is sent with tool_choice="required" and with tool_choice=Write (named). A response counts as this bug only with the bug's signature: - the first (id 154843) comes before any (id 154842), and - the next output text is a second "" (special token or the text pieces "<" "tool" "_call" ">"; the grammar allows both), and - the response lacks a single Write call with file_path and content. Other lost or empty calls are printed as "other loss (not this bug)". A known cause is a separate bug where a quoted inside the Write content argument mangles the arguments to {}. They do not affect the exit code. Server: vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 python toolresult_repro.py [--url http://localhost:8000] [--seeds 40] About 1 in 6 to 1 in 8 seeds hit the implicit end, and which seeds do varies between runs, so use at least 40 seeds. Exit codes: 1 = bug present, 0 = not reproduced (or fixed), 2 = error. Standard library only. """ import argparse import concurrent.futures as cf import json import sys import traceback import urllib.request THINK_END, TOOL_CALL = 154842, 154843 DOC = ("# Parser notes\n\nGLM-5.3 wraps every function call in ... tags; " "each argument is kv.\n") MESSAGES = [ {"role": "user", "content": "Read docs/parser.md and save a one-sentence summary of it to /tmp/summary.md."}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": { "name": "Read", "arguments": "{\"file_path\": \"docs/parser.md\"}"}}]}, {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": DOC}, ] def tool(name, args): return {"type": "function", "function": { "name": name, "description": f"{name} a file.", "parameters": {"type": "object", "required": args, "properties": {a: {"type": "string"} for a in args}}}} TOOLS = [tool("Read", ["file_path"]), tool("Write", ["file_path", "content"])] CHOICES = {"required": "required", "named": {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "Write"}}} def ask(url, model, choice, seed): body = {"model": model, "messages": MESSAGES, "tools": TOOLS, "tool_choice": CHOICES[choice], "temperature": 0.7, "seed": seed, "max_tokens": 1500, "logprobs": True, "return_token_ids": True} req = urllib.request.Request(url + "/v1/chat/completions", json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"}) c = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=900))["choices"][0] ids = c["token_ids"] toks = [t["token"] for t in c["logprobs"]["content"]] calls = [(t["function"]["name"], t["function"]["arguments"]) for t in c["message"].get("tool_calls") or []] implicit = TOOL_CALL in ids and (THINK_END not in ids or ids.index(TOOL_CALL) < ids.index(THINK_END)) first = ids.index(TOOL_CALL) if TOOL_CALL in ids else None doubled = first is not None and "".join(toks[first + 1:first + 5]).startswith("") good = (len(calls) == 1 and calls[0][0] == "Write" and {"file_path", "content"} <= set(json.loads(calls[0][1] or "{}"))) raw = "".join(toks) i = raw.find("") return dict(choice=choice, seed=seed, calls=calls, finish=c["finish_reason"], good=good, bug=implicit and doubled and not good, snippet=raw[max(0, i - 50):i + 110] if i >= 0 else raw[-120:]) def main(): ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--url", default="http://localhost:8000") ap.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, default=40) ap.add_argument("--choices", default="required,named") ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=8) args = ap.parse_args() url = args.url.rstrip("/") model = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(url + "/v1/models"))["data"][0]["id"] jobs = [(c, s) for c in args.choices.split(",") for s in range(args.seeds)] with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(args.workers) as ex: results = list(ex.map(lambda j: ask(url, model, *j), jobs)) bug, other = {c: [] for c in CHOICES}, {c: [] for c in CHOICES} for r in results: if r["good"]: continue kind = "BUG 1" if r["bug"] else "other loss (not this bug)" (bug if r["bug"] else other)[r["choice"]].append(r["seed"]) shown = r["calls"] if len(r["calls"]) <= 2 else f"{len(r['calls'])} calls" print(f"{r['choice']:8s} seed {r['seed']:2d} {kind}: tool_calls={shown} " f"finish_reason={r['finish']!r}") if r["bug"]: # other losses print one line only, to keep the log readable print(f" raw: ...{r['snippet']!r}...") print() for c in args.choices.split(","): print(f"{c}: bug 1 (doubled , call lost) in {len(bug[c])} of {args.seeds} seeds: {bug[c]}") print(f"{c}: other loss (not this bug) in {len(other[c])} of {args.seeds} seeds: {other[c]}") found = any(bug.values()) print("BUG PRESENT" if found else "not reproduced") return 1 if found else 0 if __name__ == "__main__": try: sys.exit(main()) except Exception: traceback.print_exc() print("ERROR: the repro could not run (exit 2)") sys.exit(2) ```

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek V4/V4.1 with --enable-eplb never loads the redundant expert slots
body:
> AI disclosure: this issue was investigated and drafted with an AI assistant (Claude). The reproducers were run on the hardware below, and every number in this issue comes from those runs. A human reviewed the issue before filing.

### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment summary</summary>

```text
vLLM:    0.1.dev22318+gcb6458c5c (precompiled wheel, upstream main at cb6458c5ce)
PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130
CUDA:    13.0
Python:  3.12
GPUs:    4x NVIDIA B300
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `--enable-eplb` and `num_redundant_experts=N > 0`, DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 never load weights into the redundant slots of each MoE layer. Below, "redundant slots" means the N physical expert slots with ids `n_routed_experts..n_routed_experts+N-1`. They keep whatever the allocation held. EPLB routes about half of the tokens for logical experts `0..N-1` to these slots. Nothing errors or warns.

The cause is that `DeepseekV4Model.get_expert_mapping` calls `fused_moe_make_expert_params_mapping(...)` without `num_redundant_experts`, so the argument defaults to 0:

- `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py:1809`
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py:1338`

The returned mapping only contains physical expert ids `0..n_routed_experts-1`. `load_weights` only passes the expert ids in this mapping to the weight loader (`for mapping in expert_mapping:` at `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py:1723` and `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py:1250`), so the redundant slots are never loaded.

Scope: every `--moe-backend` outside `MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS` (`vllm/config/kernel.py:160`) is affected, including the default `auto`. The MegaMoE branch (`deep_gemm_mega_moe` and the FlashInfer MoE-EP backends) uses `make_deepseek_v4_expert_params_mapping`, which is a separate path and not part of this report.

#### Why the redundant slots receive tokens

EPLB's initial placement maps physical slot `p` to logical expert `p % n_logical`, so redundant slot `n_logical + i` should hold logical expert `i`. For each token, the router picks one of a logical expert's slots by hashing the token index modulo its replica count. With one redundant slot per expert, about half of the tokens for logical experts `0..N-1` go to the unloaded slot.

This happens in `BaseRouter._select_experts`, which calls `_apply_eplb_mapping` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/base_router.py:300`, defined at `:203`), which calls `eplb_map_to_physical_and_record`.

Inferred, not measured: later rearrangement steps copy weights between physical slots, so an unloaded redundant slot could also be copied into other slots.

#### Trigger without a GPU

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace

from vllm.models.deepseek_v4.nvidia.model import DeepseekV4Model

n_routed, n_redundant = 4, 3
ffn = SimpleNamespace(use_mega_moe=False, n_redundant_experts=n_redundant)
fake = SimpleNamespace(
    config=SimpleNamespace(n_routed_experts=n_routed),
    layers=[SimpleNamespace(ffn=ffn)],
    start_layer=0,
    end_layer=1,
    named_parameters=lambda: iter(()),
)
ids = {expert_id for _, _, expert_id, _ in DeepseekV4Model.get_expert_mapping(fake)}
print(sorted(ids))
# main prints [0, 1, 2, 3]
# expected:   [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
```

The same happens with `vllm.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.model.DeepseekV4Model`. With `n_redundant = 0` the result is correct.

#### Reproducer on GPUs

Save as `minimal_repro.py` and run with `VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1 python minimal_repro.py` (needs 4 GPUs). It uses the same config as the run described under "Observed on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash".

```python
import torch

from vllm import LLM


def replica_slots(worker):
    from vllm.distributed import get_ep_group
    from vllm.model_executor.models.interfaces import get_mixture_of_experts_model

    model = get_mixture_of_experts_model(worker.model_runner.get_model())
    # expert_weights: per MoE layer, tensors of shape [num_local_experts, ...]
    nonzero = torch.stack(
        [
            torch.stack(
                [(w.view(torch.uint8).reshape(w.shape[0], -1) != 0).any(-1) for w in layer]
            ).any(0)
            for layer in model.expert_weights
        ]
    )  # [num_moe_layers, num_local_experts]
    return get_ep_group().rank_in_group, model.num_logical_experts, nonzero.tolist()


def main():
    llm = LLM(
        "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash",
        tensor_parallel_size=4,
        enable_expert_parallel=True,
        enable_eplb=True,
        eplb_config={"num_redundant_experts": 8},
        language_model_only=True,
        max_model_len=8192,
        kv_cache_dtype="fp8",
    )
    results = sorted(llm.collective_rpc(replica_slots), key=lambda r: r[0])
    nonzero = torch.cat([torch.tensor(r[2]) for r in results], dim=1)  # [layers, physical experts]
    n_logical = results[0][1]
    redundant = nonzero[:, n_logical:]
    print(f"redundant slots with all-zero weights: {(~redundant).sum()} / {redundant.numel()}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Output on main:

```text
redundant slots with all-zero weights: 320 / 320
```

The script counts all-zero slots because that is what an unloaded slot looked like here. The allocation is not initialized, so on memory that is not zeroed this count can be 0 even with the bug. In that case compare each redundant slot `n_logical + i` with slot `i`, as in the next section.

#### Observed on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

Setup: 384 routed experts, 40 MoE layers, 4x B300, TP=4 with `--enable-expert-parallel`, `--enable-eplb`, `eplb_config={"num_redundant_experts": 8}` (392 physical experts), default `--moe-backend auto` (selected the `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8` Mxfp4 MoE backend), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 8192`, language model only.

I computed a per-slot checksum over all EPLB-managed expert weights (`model.expert_weights`):

- All 320 redundant slots (8 per layer x 40 layers) differ from the slot holding the same logical expert.
- Every redundant slot was 100% zero bytes. Source slots have about 0.35% zero bytes.

Zero-filled memory is what I observed. It is not guaranteed, since the allocation is not initialized.

#### Quality impact

The impact is small and easy to miss. Only 8 of 384 experts per layer have a replica, and only the share of their tokens sent to the replica loses that expert's output. GSM8K does not detect it. Setup as above, 250 test questions, 5-shot, greedy; rows differ only in `num_redundant_experts` and the fix:

| Config | GSM8K | Replica slots that differ from their source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| N=0, main | 88.8% (222/250) | none (no replicas) |
| N=8, main | 88.8% (222/250) | 320 / 320 |
| N=8, with fix | 88.0% (220/250) | 0 / 320 |

Free-form greedy prompts showed it more clearly, though on a small sample. On main with N=8, two of four short prompts ("Write a Python function that returns the n-th Fibonacci number." and "Explain in two sentences why the sky is blue.") returned an empty completion. With N=0 and with the fix, all four returned normal answers.

#### Related

- #41920 / #41930: the same missing `num_redundant_experts` in DeepseekV2's `get_expert_mapping`. There `load_weights` builds its own mapping with the redundant slots, so only BitsAndBytes and LoRA are affected. In DeepSeek V4/V4.1, `load_weights` uses `get_expert_mapping` itself, so the weights are never loaded.
- #53022 changes the same function, but only for its static expert map path. It does not cover default runtime EPLB or V4.1.

#### Proposed fix

Pass the redundant expert count in both files. `first_layer` is already computed at the top of `get_expert_mapping`.

```diff
     num_experts=self.config.n_routed_experts,
+    num_redundant_experts=first_layer.ffn.n_redundant_experts,
 )
```

I will open a PR with this change and a unit test.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix][DeepSeek V4] Load redundant EPLB expert slots
body:
## Overview

Fixes #59609. With `--enable-eplb` and `num_redundant_experts > 0`, DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 never loaded the redundant expert slots. `get_expert_mapping` now passes `num_redundant_experts`, so `load_weights` fills those slots.

Scope: NVIDIA only. Only the NVIDIA V4 and V4.1 models allocate redundant expert slots; on ROCm, V4 builds its MoE layers without EPLB and V4.1 sets `n_redundant_experts = 0`.

## Claims

- On the FusedMoE path (every `--moe-backend` except `deep_gemm_mega_moe`, which already loads the replicas), redundant EPLB slots hold the weights of the logical expert they replicate. Before this change they kept uninitialized memory.
- No change when `num_redundant_experts=0`.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4x B300, TP=4, `--enable-expert-parallel --enable-eplb`, default `--moe-backend auto` (FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 8192`. "Replica slots that differ" compares a checksum of every redundant slot's EPLB-managed weights against the slot holding the same logical expert (8 slots x 40 MoE layers). GSM8K: 250 test questions, 5-shot, greedy.

| Config | Replica slots that differ | GSM8K |
| --- | --- | --- |
| N=0, main | no replicas | 88.8% (222/250) |
| N=8, main | 320 / 320 (all zero bytes) | 88.8% (222/250) |
| N=8, this PR | 0 / 320 | 88.0% (220/250) |

GSM8K is not sensitive to this bug: only 8 of 384 experts have a replica, and only the tokens routed to the replica lose that expert's output. Short greedy prompts show it more directly. On main with N=8, "Explain in two sentences why the sky is blue." ends at end-of-sequence as its first token (logprob -1.13 vs -1.63 for the runner-up). With this PR, " The" wins (-1.77) and end-of-sequence is second (-2.27).

The reproducer in #59609 prints `redundant slots with all-zero weights: 320 / 320` on main and `redundant slots with all-zero weights: 0 / 320` with this PR.

The new e2e test (below) fails on main and passes with this PR, run locally on 4x B300 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash:

| | Startup weight check | GSM8K (1319 q) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | `344 redundant expert slots differ from their source` (8 x 43 layers) | not reached |
| this PR | passes on all 4 ranks | 94.8% |

```
cd tests && PYTHONPATH=.. pytest -s -v evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py --config-list-file=configs/models-spec-decode.txt -k EPLB
```

## Details

`DeepseekV4Model.load_weights` loads routed experts only through the ids returned by `get_expert_mapping`. That mapping was built with the default `num_redundant_experts=0`, so physical ids `n_routed_experts..n_routed_experts+N-1` were never passed to the weight loader. EPLB's initial placement maps those slots to logical experts `0..N-1` and sends part of those experts' tokens to them.

DeepseekV2 has the same missing argument in `get_expert_mapping` (#41920, #41930). There, `load_weights` builds its own mapping with redundant slots, so only BitsAndBytes and LoRA are affected. In V4 and V4.1, `load_weights` uses `get_expert_mapping` directly, so the slots are never loaded.

Not changed:
- `deep_gemm_mega_moe` uses `make_deepseek_v4_expert_params_mapping`, which is a separate path.
- The ROCm V4.1 model sets `n_redundant_experts = 0`.
- The MTP loader (`deepseek_v4/nvidia/mtp.py`) builds its mapping without redundant slots too. The drafter is not registered with EPLB, so its router never selects those slots. This is inferred from the code, not tested.

Test: the GSM8K harness gets an optional `startup_rpc_checks` config key. It calls each listed worker-extension method through `/collective_rpc` after the server starts and before any request. The check runs before traffic because EPLB rearrangement can move expert weights. `tests/evals/gsm8k/eplb_checks.py` checksums every expert slot, gathers the checksums across the EP group, and compares each redundant slot with the first slot of the same logical expert. GSM8K alone does not catch this bug: on V4.1-Flash it scored 88.8% on main and 88.0% with the fix. The new `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-EPLB-TEP4.yaml` (TP4, EP, 8 redundant experts) runs in the nightly ":nvidia: (B200) LM Eval Spec Decode" job. The check takes a few seconds; the config adds one V4-Flash cold start plus about a minute of GSM8K to that job.

---

title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Feed the token that implicitly ends reasoning to the grammar
body:
## Overview

Structured output skipped a reasoning-end token that is also content, such as GLM's `<tool_call>` with no `</think>` before it. The grammar then forced a second `<tool_call>`, and `required`/named tool calls were lost. This PR feeds that token to the grammar, which matches what `extract_content_ids` already does. Fixes #59608.

## Claims

- For `ParserEngine`-based parsers, the grammar now consumes a reasoning-end token that `extract_content_ids` keeps as content, if the grammar accepts it. Close tags such as `</think>` are still skipped. `ReasoningParser` and legacy parsers do not change.
- On GLM-5.3-Flash, the doubled-`<tool_call>` signature went from 7/40 (`required`) and 8/40 (named) to 0/40. With MTP speculative decoding it went from 9/40 and 11/40 to 0/40.
- Under speculative decoding, a drafted `<tool_call>` cannot force the end of reasoning, and when it is the last draft the bonus row is masked from the grammar state after it.
- The same failure reproduces on Qwen3 (`qwen3` + `hermes`), and the fix removes it there too. Correct-call rates on the GLM tool-result prompt did not go up, because of a separate argument bug (see Limitations).

## Validation

### Unit tests

```
pytest tests/v1/structured_output tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py tests/parser \
  tests/reasoning tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_glm4_moe_tool_parser.py \
  --ignore=tests/parser/cohere
```

Result with 1 GPU visible: 6402 passed, 1 xfailed. `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` and the manual mypy-3.12 hook pass.

New tests are `test_inclusive_reasoning_end_token` and `test_end_token_committed_alone` in `tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py` (xgrammar and guidance), and `test_implicit_reasoning_end_of_parsers` (real `glm47_moe` config) in `tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py`. With grammar start forced to the constraint start, 8 of the 13 new cases fail: `inclusive`, `inclusive_first`, `inclusive_last` and `no_drafts`, on both backends.

CI runs these tests through `misc.yaml`. `tests/parser/cohere` is left out because it needs the optional `cohere_melody` package.

A CPU script that drives the scheduler flow (validate drafts, bitmask, accept, next bitmask) with `<tool_call>` as the last draft, the only draft, a mid-window draft and the recovered token gives a second `<tool_call>` in all 8 stock cases and none with the fix.

### Live runs

The live runs used the first version of this PR (5805e42cfa). The current commit only restructures that code, and the unit tests and the CPU check give the same results on both versions.

GLM-5.3-Flash (`RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`), TP4 on H100, xgrammar, the tool-result repro from the issue, 40 seeds at temperature 0.7:

```
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  [--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}']
```

| Doubled-`<tool_call>` signatures, 40 seeds | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `required` | 7 | **0** |
| named | 8 | **0** |
| `required`, MTP | 9 | **0** |
| named, MTP | 11 | **0** |

MTP draft acceptance was 59.1% before and 58.5% after.

Qwen3 (`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `--tool-call-parser hermes --reasoning-parser qwen3`), `logit_bias` -100 on `</think>` and +5 on `<tool_call>`, temperature 0, 3 repeats:

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --reasoning-parser qwen3
```

| Mode | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `required` | 0/3 calls, 3/3 signatures | **3/3 calls** |
| named | 0/3 calls, 3/3 signatures | **3/3 calls** |
| `auto` (control) | 3/3 calls | 3/3 calls |

No standard tool-calling eval (such as BFCL) was run.

## Details

**Root cause.** `_get_constraint_start` returned the index after the reasoning-end token. That is right for `</think>`, which is not content. A tool-call start that ends reasoning is content, so the grammar started one token after the content did. This came in with #55223, and #48200 kept it.

**Change.**

- `ParserEngine.find_reasoning_end_offset` becomes `find_reasoning_end`, which returns `ReasoningEnd(offset, implicit)`. `implicit` is True when the end token is not the close tag, the same rule `extract_content_ids` uses.
- `StructuredOutputManager._get_constraint_start` becomes `_get_constraint_bounds`, which returns `ConstraintBounds(grammar_start, constraint_start)`. For an implicit end that the grammar accepts, the grammar starts at the end token and masking starts one token later. Otherwise both equal the old value.
- `validate_tokens`, the spec-decode loop of `grammar_bitmask` and `accept_tokens` feed the grammar from `grammar_start`. Masked rows and early returns still use `constraint_start`, so a drafted `<tool_call>` cannot force the target to end reasoning.
- The "grammar accepts it" check keeps the old skip when the grammar cannot start with that token, such as a `json_schema` response format with tools present.

**Affected parsers.** Every in-tree `ParserEngine` config whose tool-call start ends reasoning now feeds that token to the grammar: glm47_moe (and ling3), qwen3 (and mimo), nemotron_v3, granite_thinking, seed_oss, gemma4, kimi_k2, minimax_m2, deepseek_v4, deepseek_v41, plamo3, and mistral with `reasoning_encoding="special_token"`. A token counts only if the tokenizer has a single id for it. On the real DeepSeek-V4 tokenizer the DSML opener is several tokens, so deepseek_v4 does not change in practice. For plamo3 the token is the end-of-turn tag, which is normally a stop token; I expect that to be harmless but did not test it.

**Tradeoffs.**

- No measurable cost. After reasoning ends, `_get_constraint_bounds` returns before any reasoner call. Only a step with an implicit end token runs one extra single-token `validate_tokens` on the CPU. There is no CPU/GPU sync.

**Limitations.**

- A separate bug, similar to #58315, remains. The GLM tool grammar allows the special `<tool_call>` token inside `<arg_value>`. When the model quotes tool-result text that contains it, arguments break (`Write({})`, missing arguments). Many responses this PR recovers now hit that bug. It will be reported separately.
- Legacy (non-`ParserEngine`) parsers such as `k2_horizon` keep the old behavior until they move to `ParserEngine`.
- Under spec decode, the target can still reject a draft and then sample an implicit end token that the grammar rejects. This predates the PR. @yzong-rh plans to file an issue for it.
- Also unchanged: a prompt that already ends with an implicit end token (`continue_final_message`) still starts the grammar after it, and multi-token text markers cannot be expressed as a token-id set.

**Related.** No open PR changes where the grammar starts after reasoning; #36138, #56403, #57718 and #57754 touch nearby paths.

This PR was investigated and drafted with an AI assistant (Claude). The tests and live runs listed here were run on real hardware, and a human reviewed the PR before submission.

title: [ROCm] Enable DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.3 sparse MLA on gfx11
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.3 don't run on gfx11. For sparse MLA, `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` is the only backend on offer, and its default path needs AITER's MLA kernels, which have no gfx11 build. On current main the server starts, but the first request fails in AITER's `get_mla_metadata_v1`:

```
RuntimeError: [module_mla_metadata] was built against a different pybind11 ABI
than module_aiter_core, so it cannot see the aiter_tensor_t registration ...
```

The Triton sparse path in the same file already handles the 512 + 64 RoPE layout, but `_use_rocm_sparse_triton()` only picks it when `head_size == kv_lora_rank`. This PR lets gfx11 take that path too.

Long-context decode on this path goes through the split-K BF16 kernel from #58584, which needs #61774 for the 576-wide layout. Without #61774, decode past 512 tokens fails with `arange's range must be a power of 2`.

Tests: one new routing test for the gfx11 case, and the existing routing tests now pin `on_gfx11` to `False` so they also pass on gfx11 hardware.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs and issues for `rocm_aiter_mla_decode_fwd`, GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V3.2 on gfx11, and sparse MLA fallback on ROCm. No duplicate.

- #61774 fixes the split-K reduction for non-power-of-two head dims. It is needed together with this PR for long-context decode.
- #52970 is about DeepSeek-V4 and AITER's Triton kernels. It does not touch `_use_rocm_sparse_triton`.

## Test Result

Tested on 4x Strix Halo / Radeon 8060S / gfx1151 with `TP=4`, ROCm nightly wheel, with #61774 applied.

```
vllm serve Tech2wild/GLM-5.3-Int4-Int8Mix \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --distributed-executor-backend ray \
    --max-model-len 32768 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \
    --enforce-eager
```

Before: the first request fails with the error above.

After:

```
"What is 17 times 23?"                      -> 17 × 23 = 391
needle in a ~1.7k-token prompt               -> correct
split-K decode (16 splits at 2048 tokens)    -> runs, matches single-pass
```

```
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_glm5next_sparse.py
  35 passed
```

title: [Bugfix][Structured Outputs] Keep tool-call openers that end reasoning inside the grammar constraint
body:
## Overview

Fixes #59608. When reasoning ends on a tool-call opener instead of `</think>` (GLM-4.7/5.x can jump straight from reasoning into `<tool_call>`), the structured-output gate started the grammar constraint one token past the opener. The grammar never saw the opener, so it forced the model to emit a second `<tool_call>`, the parser then dropped the malformed call, and `required`/named tool calls came back empty.

## Claims

- The reasoning-end fast path now distinguishes terminators that are pure reasoning syntax (`</think>`) from terminators that are the first content token (a tool-call opener), using the transition events already declared in each parser config.
- For content terminators the constraint starts at the marker and the marker is fed to the grammar, so the grammar state advances past the opener instead of re-forcing it. Pure terminators keep the existing `offset + 1` behavior.
- Configs affected on main: `glm47_moe` (the `glm45`/`glm47` reasoning parsers), `qwen3`, `gemma4`, `mistral`. Each has a `(REASONING, tool opener)` transition that emits both `REASONING_END` and `TOOL_CALL_START` on a single-token terminal.

## Validation

New unit coverage, all runnable on CPU:

- `tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py`: the GLM config derives `reasoning_end_token_ids == {</think>, <tool_call>}` and `reasoning_end_content_token_ids == {<tool_call>}`.
- `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py`: the multi-token DSML opener stays out of both sets (negative case).
- `tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py`: manager-level flows with real xgrammar/guidance/outlines grammars. Under a `z[0-9]+` regex with `z` as a content terminator, the marker row is constrained (`UCCC`, was `UUCC`), the grammar consumes the marker on accept, and afterwards a digit validates while a duplicate marker is rejected. A companion case locks the pure-marker path through the same fast-path branch (`UUCCC`, unchanged).

Commands and results:

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py -q
# 119 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py -q
# 49 passed, 1 xfailed (pre-existing guidance xfail)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py tests/v1/structured_output/ -q
# 179 passed, 1 xfailed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/ -q --ignore=tests/parser/cohere
# 5716 passed (cohere subdir needs the optional cohere_melody package, unrelated)
```

Red proof: with `vllm/` stashed, the new content-marker flow fails on all three backends (xgrammar/guidance/outlines) and the new derivation tests fail; the pure-marker guard passes both before and after.

I have no GPU on this machine, so I could not rerun the GLM-5.3 serving eval from the issue; the failing mechanism (constraint boundary skipping the opener) is reproduced and fixed at the manager flow level above.

## Details

Root cause: `_derive_reasoning_end_token_ids` collects every token that can end reasoning, and `_get_constraint_start` assumed any such terminator is pure reasoning syntax, placing the boundary after it (`offset + 1`). That assumption is wrong whenever the terminator doubles as the tool-call opener: the `glm_4_7` xgrammar structural tag wraps calls as `<tool_call>name<arg_key>...</tool_call>`, so the opener is the first grammar-constrained token. Skipping it left the grammar at its root expecting `<tool_call>`, which is exactly the duplicated opener the issue shows.

The parser engine now also exposes `reasoning_end_content_token_ids`: the subset of reasoning-end tokens whose transition out of `REASONING` also emits `TOOL_CALL_START`. The structured-output manager constrains from the marker for that subset and keeps `offset + 1` otherwise. This lives in the shared derivation (`engine/parser_engine.py`) rather than a model file because the misclassification is in the shared code, not in any one parser's config (per `vllm/parser/AGENTS.md`).

Duplicate check: #59608 has no linked PR and no comments. #36138 covers a different failure (draft tokens after the reasoning end not validated under speculative decoding) and predates the manager rewrite. #56403 constrains non-strict GLM tool calls via an EBNF grammar, a different path.

AI assistance was used (Kimi Code). I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests listed above.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Hold freed host blocks until the step's deferred writes land
body:
## Purpose

Since #59309, HiSparse copies a step's MTP draft-layer rows (and, in lazy mirror mode, its page spills) to host at the next step's start. By then the scheduler may already have freed a finished or preempted request's host blocks and handed one to a P/D import. NIXL writes are not ordered against the HiSparse copy stream, so the late copy could overwrite imported rows. GPU writes and host copy-on-write are already ordered by #59309.

This should be rare: it needs a nearly full host pool (freed blocks go to the tail of the free queue), an import allocated in the very next step that draws a finished request's last-step blocks, and the late copy landing after the NIXL write (most plausible with async scheduling, where the copy waits for the previous forward). When it does happen, it silently corrupts an unrelated request's KV, which is very hard to trace back, so the fix is worth its small cost.

## Changes

- The coordinator stamps each step's connector metadata with a step id.
- The coordinator's `free()` takes a freed request's host blocks and holds them, tagged with the latest scheduled step, instead of letting them return to the pool.
- The worker reports a step's deferred writes as done after flushing them, through the existing transfer enqueued/completed counts.
- Held blocks are released once their step (or a later one) is reported done, and count as pending work so an idle engine keeps stepping until then.

HiSparse-only (no core changes). Overhead: no stream or CPU synchronization; one event recorded on the copy stream per step, plus O(finished requests) scheduler bookkeeping. A freed request's host blocks return to the pool about one step later, and an engine that goes idle runs one extra empty step. The scheduler's generic `deferred_frees` fence covers the same hazard one step too early for HiSparse (and only for consumers with overlapping batches).

No other open PR addresses this. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; changes reviewed and tested by the submitter.

## Test Plan

- `test_hisparse_holds_freed_host_blocks_until_step_writes_land`: with the host pool exhausted, a request finishes and a P/D import is refused until that step's writes are reported done, then succeeds (fails without the hold).
- `test_draft_layer_rows_mirrored_after_drafter`: also checks the worker reports the step after flushing its deferred writes.
- H100 (on current main): `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py` 4 passed; HiSparse backend/connector/worker/prefix-caching/scheduler tests 160 passed (before the import-sequence test was added; CPU HiSparse tests 65 passed after).

title: [Bugfix] Make cooperative TopK exact on candidate overflow
body: ## Summary Cooperative TopK groups FP32 scores into coarse bins before selecting candidates. If too many scores land in the bin containing the TopK threshold, its bounded candidate buffer can drop scores that belong in the result. This PR detects that overflow before scattering candidates and uses exact FP32 selection for the affected row. The usual path remains in place when the threshold bin fits. # Context We need to differentiate three things here: * Synthetic vs. real score distributions. * Exact vs. approximate top-K in real NSA/DSA. * The impact of overflow. Even when overflow occurs (which *is a rare event*) the discarded candidates will have the same high bits as the retained ones. Retained and discarded candidates belong to the same current radix-threshold bin. Therefore, they share the radix prefix examined so far, meaning their values are very close. For this reasons, even if we can force the overflow with synthetic inputs, that doesn't mean non-exact topK translates into an negative accuracy impact for the reasons above. See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53287 for more context. ## Validation and performance I checked selected values against `torch.topk`, along with index range and uniqueness, across ordinary inputs and concentrated-score inputs, including the 2,048/2,049-candidate boundary. B300 CUDA-graph microbenchmarks show that ordinary-input latency is generally close to main. Recovery is not free: at 250K width, 64 rows, and k=2048, a controlled case measured ~40 µs with 2,048 candidates in the threshold bin, ~54 µs with 2,049, ~75 µs when the whole row was concentrated in [1.0, 1.01]. The last case is deliberately extreme and unrealistic; the 2,049 case shows the cost of merely entering recovery. The goal here is an exact TopK result when overflow occurs, not a claimed improvement in model accuracy. Whether the correction changes an evaluation score depends on how often a real workload reaches this condition and how sensitive it is to the selected positions. DeepSelect and Flashinfer topK are now integrated in vLLM and can be selected using `--sparse-indexer-topk-backend deep_select` and `--sparse-indexer-topk-backend flashinfer` respectively. TopK=512 TopK=1024 TopK=2048 Note the [1.0, 1.01] distribution is deliberately extreme and unrealistic, trying to represent worst-case scenario. ### E2E results (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, topk=512) DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash serving runs here show little change in mean TPOT or ITL. Together, these suggest limited practical impact for the workloads tested, but neither experiment measures overflow frequency or rules out an impact on other score distributions. We are including exact selection because the bounded candidate path can potentially drop better scores, while the normal-path overhead is small. title: [Spec Decode] Allow per-request synthetic acceptance length
body:
## Overview

Allow each request to select real or synthetic speculative acceptance without restarting the server. This supports benchmark sweeps on both GPU model runners.

## Claims

- A numeric `vllm_xargs.synthetic_acceptance_length` overrides the acceptance length. `null` selects real acceptance, and an omitted key inherits the server default.
- Chat, completion, and offline `SamplingParams(extra_args=...)` requests support the override when speculative decoding is enabled.
- Every request in a batch must select the same mode and numeric length. Mixed configurations assert, so drain outstanding requests before switching.

## Validation

AI assistance was used to implement, review, and test this draft. Searches for open PRs with `synthetic_acceptance_length` or per-request synthetic acceptance in their titles found no duplicate implementation.

The sampling-parameters suite passes 76 cases locally. Six request-batch cases pass locally, and 43 targeted cases pass on an H100 NVL.

```bash
.venv/bin/python3 -m pytest --noconftest tests/test_sampling_params.py -q
.venv/bin/python3 -m pytest --noconftest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch.py -q -k synthetic_acceptance
.venv/bin/python3 -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/test_sampling_params.py tests/v1/sample/test_rejection_sampler.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py \
  -q -k 'request_synthetic or synthetic_acceptance or synthetic_all or chunked_scores or replay_on_off or sampling_metadata_in_input_batch or swap_states_in_input_batch'
```

Serving checks use Qwen3-1.7B with a Qwen3-0.6B probabilistic draft, three speculative tokens, eager execution, and greedy and random requests. Both runners process a sweep within one server process. The legacy runner uses a synthetic server default, and the newer runner uses a standard server default.

The sweep tests lengths 1, 4, and 2.6, explicit real acceptance, and inheritance. Lengths 1 and 4 are exact. The measured fractional length stays within 0.2 of 2.6. Sequential real greedy outputs match before and after switching. Concurrent requests test acceptance lengths separately because greedy outputs can depend on batch size before any override.

The checks include nonstreaming completions, nonstreaming chat, streaming chat, 59 successful requests, and eight invalid requests rejected with HTTP 400. The newer runner runs with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Repository pre-commit hooks pass.

## Details

The patch reuses the existing acceptance schedule and rejection kernels. It carries one acceptance configuration per batch, caches small rate tensors, and uses the existing pinned asynchronous copy helper. It does not change the server default. Block verification does not support request overrides.

On the legacy runner, a synthetic server with probabilistic drafting previously used greedy drafts. It now honors the configured draft method so requests can select real acceptance correctly. These deployments now incur the probability-buffer memory and sampling cost that standard acceptance and the newer runner already incur. Block-default behavior stays unchanged.

The legacy runner registers both rejection modes for startup warmup. The newer runner retains its existing first-use compilation behavior. Warm up each acceptance mode before measuring performance. Synthetic acceptance changes generated tokens and serves performance experiments rather than accuracy evaluation. CUDA graph execution and other request protocols are outside the validation scope.

---

title: [HiSparse] Suggestion for #59450: keep spec expansion out of core KV cache sizing
body:
Suggestion PR into #59450 (`hisparse-admission-fit`). It shrinks the core diff against main without changing behavior.

## Changes

- **Expansion moves to the worker.** `resolve_hisparse_block_size` is renamed to `resolve_hisparse_specs`. It now also adds the derived resident/hot specs, and returns the specs instead of mutating them. `get_kv_cache_spec` calls it only when `hisparse_config is not None`. Workers report every cache they allocate, so `get_kv_cache_configs` needs no HiSparse step, and `expand_hisparse_kv_cache_specs` is inlined and removed.
- **`_max_memory_usage_bytes_from_groups` matches main again.** The `host_resident` filter moves to its one HiSparse call site, the "max seq len" check in `get_kv_cache_configs`.
- **Smaller HiSparse-local diffs.** In `get_hisparse_kv_cache_groups`, the `mla_specs` check is back where it is on main. In `create_hisparse_layout`, `min_host_blocks` is back to its one-line form. The `max_admission_blocks_per_request` docstring is one line.

The `host_resident` filter in `_pool_bytes_per_block` stays: the override conversion, the null-block reserve and the re-plan to the smallest rank all rely on it. The projection early return also stays.

Net diff vs main for #59450: 121 → 116 lines changed. `core/kv_cache_utils.py` goes from +18/−9 to +11/−10.

## Testing

- `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`: same results as #59450's head. Locally, 8 tests fail on both because of the environment. One is `test_hisparse_pool_must_fit_max_model_len[32768-657-True]`; see the notes.
- Not run: `tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py`. Its collection needs the flash-attn extensions, which the local env lacks. It needs CI.
- Not run: end-to-end HiSparse. Workers now report the derived specs to the engine core, so a TP=2 smoke run on this branch is still needed.

## Other review notes on #59450 (not addressed here)

1. **The new test depends on `async_scheduling`.** `test_hisparse_pool_must_fit_max_model_len[32768-657-True]` fails when `async_scheduling` resolves to True: `max_in_flight_tokens` becomes 4096, so a request needs 784 blocks instead of 656. Pin `async_scheduling = False`, or derive the expected values from `max_in_flight_tokens`.
2. **Auto-fit is off by one with `num_gpu_blocks_override`.** The HiSparse branch of `_estimate_max_model_len_from_groups` sizes against the full override and ignores the null block. Auto-fit then picks a length that needs exactly `override` blocks, which the "max seq len" check rejects. Probe at 32768 / 2048 batched tokens: an override of 656 or 657 makes auto-fit pick 24576 or 24640, and startup then fails.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR.

title: [Feature]: Support DFlash speculative decoding with dual_key_gumbel watermarking
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

`dual_key_gumbel` watermarking supports speculative decoding with `dspark`, `eagle`, `eagle3` and `mtp`, but not with DFlash. Watermarking is useful mainly for production serving, where speculative decoding is commonly enabled, so DFlash users currently have to choose between the two.

`VllmConfig._check_watermarking_unsupported` rejects DFlash twice: `dflash` is not in the method allowlist, and DFlash sets `parallel_drafting=True`, which is allowed only for `dspark`.

Removing the check is not enough. DFlash computes logits for all N draft positions in one forward pass, and `DraftModelSpeculator.sample_draft` passes the flattened `(request, step)` batch to the draft watermarker in a single call. The target verifies draft *k* with a context that includes drafts 0…k−1 (`GPUWatermarkSampler._get_contexts`). So a single call:
- gives each row the wrong context (rows are per request, not per request × step);
- never lets step *k* see the drafts of steps < *k*;
- can exceed the `max_num_reqs`-row draft-watermarker buffers;
- breaks the per-step context deduplication added in #56807, which assumes one call per step.

Proposal: keep DFlash's parallel forward pass, and sample the watermarked drafts one step at a time on the precomputed logits (the per-step pattern DSpark already uses). Candidate-head DFlash drafters (`DFlash2DraftModel`, `LiLiCorrDraftModel`) sample inside their own kernel and never reach the draft watermarker, so they should be rejected explicitly when draft watermarking is enabled.

### Alternatives

- Building all draft contexts up front from committed history and draft tokens. This is not possible, because the draft tokens of earlier steps are not known until they are sampled.
- Target-only watermarking (`allow_target_only_watermarking=true` with `gumbel`). This already works with DFlash, but accepted drafts are unwatermarked, which dilutes the signal by the share of accepted drafts (often more than half of the output).

### Additional context

Builds on #56122 (dual-key Gumbel for speculative decoding) and #56807 (context deduplication for speculative decoding). Implementation: #59554.
