title: [RFC]: Fast-Track Merging for Model Optimization PRs
body:
# [RFC]: Fast-Track Merging for Model Optimization PRs

### Motivation.

Frontier coding models have become extremely proficient at inference model optimization and efficient GPU kernel development. The frequency of new vLLM PRs is rapidly increasing, and is outpacing reviewer bandwidth.
Powered by fully autonomous optimization loops (e.g. "autoresearch"), optimization development can be scaled horizontally across a wide range of models, hardware architectures, and deployment scenarios.

The potential speedups are extremely large, but careful steps must be taken to ensure that vLLM's code quality, usability, and reliability is not sacrificed in the process -- this is why we have a comprehensive review process. Striking a balance between contribution barriers and performance upside is critical.

The fundamental goal of the fast-track is to merge PRs faster, with the same standard of quality. The way to achieve this is by systematically verifying aspects that ordinarily require manual reviewer verification (correctness, performance, no risk of breaking other workloads, etc.). By focusing on a subset of PRs whose changes are strictly contained to an isolated module (namely, the "model forward pass") we can tailor guardrails to decrease reviewer involvement while maintaining a high bar for stability.

### 1. Proposed Change.

I propose a relaxation of the review and merge requirements, limited to cases where changes are contained, comprehensively validated, and provably limited to explicitly validated deployment scenarios.

The remainder of the RFC details the following:
1. Process changes we can make to more efficiently merge "safe" optimization PRs
2. How we can systematically ensure that an eligible PR is "safe to merge"

#### 1.1: One-Touch Merge ("LGTM")

Reviewers often need to revisit PRs multiple times throughout review: one pass to leave comments, another pass to approve and enable CI, additional passes to rerun/retry CI, and possibly a final force-merge request must be made.

For contained model optimizations, much of this can be prevented:
- If no comments are required, a single reviewer action approves the PR and starts an automated procedure to merge: CI runs and executes an automated procedure of rebase and retry until the PR goes in (up to 3 times) or a fallback force-merge is automatically requested. 
- If only trivial edits or conflict resolution are requested, a reviewer may submit a "conditional approval" on the requested changes. After the changes are made the automated merge procedure begins. The "conditional approval" persists through rebase, conflict resolution, acceptance of reviewer-suggested edits, and changes localized to tests/, provided the changes preserve the approved behavior. An amount of trust is delegated to the contributor in the event of a conditional approval.

The CI runs should hopefully not be an obstacle in these cases as changes should be contained to localized files/directories which will mitigate the range of detected test cases.

In cases when a maintainer decides nontrivial changes are needed, the maintainer closes or demotes the PR and the contributor is responsible for updating and re-opening or re-requesting review.

#### 1.2: Primary-Maintainer Merge

One common issue that blocks merge is when the primary maintainer of a feature makes a small PR to update an aspect of that feature which they themselves have the most expertise with. In such cases it can be difficult to find a dedicated second reviewer who can confidently approve the changes.

To resolve this I propose we permit core committers to merge their own PRs, provided they follow the validation and isolation requirements of the fast-track specification below.

#### 1.3: Priority Review

I propose that eligible fast-track PRs be automatically labelled as such, and that maintainer review is prioritized towards fast-track PRs. This will involve slack integration, an automated tracking dashboard, and escalation when fast-track-eligible PRs are "stale" for more than N=7 days.

Because fast-track model optimizations are targeted towards a specific model (or small family of models), there should be a small set of assigned reviewers who can be held more directly responsible for triaging fast-track PRs. This burden will be opt-in, but should not be too heavy as triaging fast-track PRs should be very easy by design.

#### 1.4: PR Template

Similar to the [PR-Checklist](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57084) change which updated the PR template, there will be a dedicated template for fast-track PRs which formalizes the requirements and streamlines review. PR will follow the RFC within a few days.

### 2. Validations and Confidence

#### 2.1: Isolation of Code Changes

The primary risk of merging code tailored to optimize one use-case is impact to other deployments. Performance regressions, breaking other features, or correctness violations are all common side-effects of a seemingly harmless change.

The first pillar of raising confidence in safety is _isolation_: limiting code changes to a specific deployment scenario.

I propose the initial prototype require that fast-track changes be limited to "flat model" subdirectories (e.g. all diff is within a folder such as `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia`). 

#### 2.2: Bounded Impact on Deployments

Optionally, changes can be further gated programmatically (e.g. a kernel fusion only enabled at small input sizes). The more isolated a change is, the smaller the potential impact. By placing rigid bounds on the changes, we can limit the impact to a very small set of deployment scenarios which can be tested explicitly.

Naturally, limiting the scope in this way also reduces the net improvement per PR: other excluded scenarios might benefit from the changes as well. This may also increase code duplication and redundancy. However, it creates a clear path toward improving stability and scalability as we accelerate the pace of optimizations with coding agents.

[TensorRT-LLM has merged a design](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/19056) which isolates/replicates model code for each model, hardware, and parallelism triple (e.g. gpt-oss TP1 on SM103). This is a fairly extreme flavor of replication, but it highlights an architectural direction we can move towards for if the initial results from vLLM's flat-model design prove sufficiently maintainable.

#### 2.3: Explicit Validation of Affected Deployments

Once an isolated and bounded deployment is established for a contribution, what remains is to run sufficient validations against a representative set of configurations.

Since reviewers are still involved in the process, there is some flexibility in the extent of validation: some changes might warrant testing every parallelism configuration or testing on multiple hardwares, while others might be sufficient with only a single parallelism/HW configuration. If a contribution is not sufficiently validated, reviewers may request additional validation and approve conditionally (see 1.1) or they may demote the PR from the fast-track and/or close it as necessary. Submissions following the fast-track accept a higher evidence standard and a higher risk of reviewers closing low-quality PRs wholesale without discussion.

To codify expectations, I propose the following requirements:

- **E2E Correctness Evaluation:**
  - `GSM8k` and `GPQA-Diamond` be run for all proposed model optimizations
  - A long-context benchmark such as `MRCR v2 256K (8-needle)` and/or a long-generation benchmark such as `AIME25`/`AIME26` (pass@1 avg1) should be included when changes affect sensitive token-mixing operations such as FMHA or SSM.
  - A "hard" correctness benchmark such as `AIME25`/`AIME26` (pass@1 avg4+) or `HLE` or `TerminalBench (any)` should be included when changes include a "high correctness risk factor": low-level CUDA C++ or PTX/SASS or equivalent, or new communications kernels for which race conditions cannot be ruled out by formal verification.
  - All correctness evaluations should use at least "high" reasoning effort, where supported. All evaluations should compare against a known "good" baseline, either referencing official vendor reported numbers or those from a vLLM reference run. Running your own baseline on the vLLM main branch to compare against is acceptable. Measured scores should exceed or match the reference within one percentage point (absolute delta, after accounting for run-to-run variance).
  - Correctness validation runs should ensure that the deployment scenario is reproduced. For example, if adding a small-batch fusion, GSM8k should run at a correspondingly low batch size (to trigger the change and contribute coverage to the diff).
- **Kernel Correctness Evaluation:**
  - New kernels should be exhaustively validated for correctness on a broad range of inputs. This includes multiple possible input shapes as well as input distributions.
    - If bit-exactness is not maintained, it should be justified and validated with a strict tolerance.
    - If quantization or lossy optimizations are used, this is considered a "high correctness risk factor" and warrants additional E2E validation (see above).
  - For low-level CUDA kernels, include [compute-sanitizer](https://developer.nvidia.com/compute-sanitizer) tests such as `memcheck`, `racecheck`, and `synccheck` sanitization are required where applicable.
  - Note, committed tests should be a small subset of validation performed during development. These should exist strictly for regression checks, not for comprehensive reproduction. We do not want to run exhaustive correctness testing in CI every time we make a model change.
- **Performance Evaluation:**
  - PRs should include a "headline" speedup on a specified "target" workload. This is required but not sufficient for performance validation.
  - Performance change should also be swept across the range of bounded-affected-workloads: multiple concurrencies should be benchmarked almost always, as well as high/low sequence length when applicable. Any throughput or latency regression exceeding 1% for any measured configuration is unacceptable and disqualifies the PR from the fast-track.
    - For MoE models, ensure real prompts (such as speed-bench throughput_8k) are used so that expert balance is realistic. 

### Feedback Period.

Feedback period will continue for 12 days, ending on Oct 13. @benchislett will request maintainer review and open a candidate PR with a reference implementation of the proposed design. 

### CC List.

@njhill @LucasWilkinson @yewentao256 @WoosukKwon @mgoin @vllm-project/vllm-committers @xinli-sw 

### Discussion Areas

1. Do we want to further solidify the requirements from sec. 2.3 into a structured requirement matrix? Or do we want to leave it flexible for reviewers to decide on a per-PR basis if validation is sufficient?
2. How strict should we be about isolating code changes? Are minor one-liner integration patches in core files acceptable, or do we require rigid file-structure-based guarantees about isolation? Can we build static linting tooling (possibly AI powered) that can enforce or verify that changes are limited to the claimed workloads?
3. Is committer self-merge a good idea, or is it too permissive?
4. How much control are we comfortable delegating to automated verification systems, versus committer judgement? Should we be more/less aggressive in automating merge workflows?

title: [ROCm][DSV4.1][Perf] Single-launch DSA decode candidate mask
body:
## Overview

On ROCm, the DeepSeek V4.1 decode candidate mask goes from four kernels per consumer indexer layer to one. The flags kernel is folded into `_mask_candidates_strided_kernel` (added in [#56628](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56628)), and the int64 cast and `zeros_like` before it are dropped. No existing PR does this; [#57859](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57859) touches the same code, see Details.

## Claims

- The decode candidate mask is 1.06× to 2.50× faster on MI355X (not counting the two removed elementwise kernels, about 9.6 µs more per call).
- Mean TPOT -0.48% and throughput +0.44% end to end on MI355X, over 12 sweep points.
- Masking within `[0, end)` is unchanged, and GSM8K accuracy is unchanged within error.



## Validation



### Kernel

MI355X, CUDA graph (50 calls per replay, best of 5): width 262144, 2048 candidate blocks of 8, ends set to the live length. "Old" is `_candidate_flags_kernel` + `_mask_candidates_strided_kernel`. Every point matched the old output and the shared `apply_candidate_mask` exactly over `[0, end)`.

| ---- | --------- | ------ | ------ | ------- |
| 4    | 2048      | 5.71   | 3.11   | 1.84×   |
| 16   | 2048      | 6.03   | 3.20   | 1.88×   |
| 64   | 2048      | 8.04   | 3.54   | 2.27×   |
| 256  | 2048      | 17.11  | 6.84   | 2.50×   |
| 4    | 15000     | 6.22   | 3.51   | 1.77×   |
| 64   | 15000     | 8.82   | 4.48   | 1.97×   |
| 256  | 15000     | 20.06  | 9.64   | 2.08×   |
| 16   | 32000     | 6.90   | 3.92   | 1.76×   |
| 64   | 32000     | 10.02  | 6.48   | 1.55×   |
| 256  | 32000     | 25.94  | 16.98  | 1.53×   |
| 16   | 131072    | 9.98   | 7.10   | 1.41×   |
| 64   | 131072    | 20.27  | 18.01  | 1.13×   |
| 256  | 131072    | 53.21  | 50.28  | 1.06×   |




### End-to-end

vLLM on MI355X, TP4 + EP, FP8, fused against default. Mean TPOT in ms and output throughput in tok/s:


| input / output | concurrency | TPOT default | TPOT fused | Δ     | tok/s default | tok/s fused | Δ     |
| -------------- | ----------- | ------------ | ---------- | ----- | ------------- | ----------- | ----- |
| 8192 / 1024    | 4           | 8.05         | 7.99       | -0.7% | 470.57        | 472.20      | +0.3% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 8           | 9.81         | 9.73       | -0.9% | 772.13        | 778.70      | +0.9% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 16          | 11.85        | 11.74      | -0.9% | 1262.90       | 1273.77     | +0.9% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 32          | 16.16        | 16.07      | -0.6% | 1783.04       | 1793.30     | +0.6% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 64          | 23.07        | 22.84      | -1.0% | 2523.76       | 2545.75     | +0.9% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 128         | 35.20        | 35.15      | -0.1% | 3176.89       | 3182.50     | +0.2% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 256         | 57.90        | 57.72      | -0.3% | 3814.25       | 3827.03     | +0.3% |
| 60000 / 600    | 4           | 14.05        | 13.97      | -0.6% | 227.76        | 229.03      | +0.6% |
| 60000 / 600    | 16          | 40.27        | 40.02      | -0.6% | 335.86        | 337.69      | +0.5% |
| 60000 / 600    | 64          | 137.05       | 137.15     | +0.1% | 391.59        | 391.60      | +0.0% |
| 128000 / 1024  | 4           | 16.74        | 16.68      | -0.4% | 185.73        | 186.21      | +0.3% |
| 128000 / 1024  | 16          | 53.98        | 54.17      | +0.3% | 248.75        | 248.60      | -0.1% |


The mean is -0.48% TPOT and +0.44% throughput. No single point moves by more than 1%, but throughput improves at 11 of the 12 and TPOT at 10, and median TPOT gives the same answer at -0.53%.



### Accuracy

GSM8K, 5-shot, via `lm_eval`:


| filter           | default         | fused           | Δ       |
| ---------------- | --------------- | --------------- | ------- |
| flexible-extract | 0.9227 ± 0.0074 | 0.9363 ± 0.0067 | +0.0136 |
| strict-match     | 0.9219 ± 0.0074 | 0.9371 ± 0.0067 | +0.0152 |


The fused path scores higher on both filters, by 1.4σ and 1.5σ against a combined standard error of about 0.010, so the difference is not significant.



### Tests

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_candidate_mask.py \
       tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py
```

Both pass on MI355X. `test_matches_shared_kernel_model_shape` is new and runs 2048 candidates, crowded and spread, at 8 and 64 rows so both tile sizes run. `test_matches_shared_kernel_candidates_past_width` is new and covers the last-column clamp. `test_leaves_columns_past_end_untouched` now asserts that nothing at or past `end` is written. The mxfp4 indexer tests cover the other caller of `_apply_candidate_mask_strided`. CI runs these in the MI300 attention-kernels job.

At the call site, the old and new sequences give bitwise-identical logits and candidates for the mask and select paths, with `next_n` of 1 and 2 and with 1-D and 2-D `seq_lens`. A profiler run shows the old mask path launched three kernels per call and the new one launches one.

## Details

Each consumer layer (4 per decode step) masked its decode logits with four kernels:


| kernel                            | source                                                               | µs per call |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `direct_copy`                     | `visible.to(torch.int64)`                                            | 4.4         |
| `FillFunctor<long>`               | `torch.zeros_like(visible)`                                          | 5.2         |
| `_candidate_flags_kernel`         | clears all `nblocks + 1` flags per row, then scatters the candidates | 8.7         |
| `_mask_candidates_strided_kernel` | masks `[0, end)` from the flags                                      | 4.1         |


The flags kernel clears the whole row, however short the live context. The two elementwise kernels only build an all-zero starts tensor and an int64 copy of `seq_lens`, and the Triton kernels need neither.

`_mask_candidates_strided_kernel` now builds its own flags. Each row's tiles are handed out round-robin to its programs, and each program clears the flags of its own live tiles, scatters the candidates that land in them, and masks. Nothing past the live context is cleared. On AMD, `tl.debug_barrier()` only waits for LDS traffic, so a store wait goes before each barrier and the flags are read with `.cv`. The wait is `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)` on gfx9, `s_waitcnt_vscnt` on gfx11 and `s_wait_storecnt` on gfx12, since gfx10+ count stores separately. The tile is 2048 columns below 64 rows and 4096 from 64 rows up. It depends only on the row count, so the grid stays fixed under FULL CUDA graphs. Stores now stop at `end` instead of the next 1024-column boundary.

At the decode call site, the int64 cast, `zeros_like` and `repeat_interleave` are replaced by `None` starts, the int32 `seq_lens` and `row_repeat`, as on the CUDA path. This applies to both the mask and the select paths.

**Limitations.** The tile sizes were tuned on gfx950 only. gfx942 runs in CI but was not benchmarked. The gfx11 and gfx12 store waits were checked in the compiled ISA only, since no RDNA hardware was available.

## Existing PRs and interaction with #57859

I searched vllm-project/vllm PRs (open and closed) for the kernel names, "candidate flags / mask / fuse", `zeros_like` and `row_repeat` with ROCm. No PR fuses the flags and mask kernels or removes these two elementwise kernels. [#56628](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56628) (merged) added the strided decode mask that this PR builds on and kept the separate flags kernel. [#57859](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57859) (open) adds a candidate-only paged MQA scorer for gfx950 decode and edits the same code.

- **Its fast path skips the mask.** On gfx950, consumer layers with `compress_ratio == 1`, `next_n == 1`, no `requires_padding` and a page size that is a multiple of the candidate block size score only the candidate columns. Top-k then runs on the compact buffer, so no mask kernel runs. In that case, which probably covers the four V4.1 consumer layers in decode without speculative decoding, this PR's fused kernel doesn't run.
- **Its dense fallback still has what this PR changes.** The fallback keeps `repeat_interleave`, `.to(torch.int64)`, `zeros_like`, then select or mask. It is used by:
  - the candidate source layer, which always takes this path because the fast path requires `candidate_write` to be false, so removing the cast and zero-fill still saves two kernels per step there;
  - gfx942, `next_n > 1`, padded decode and `compress_ratio != 1`;
  - `rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py`, which calls the strided mask directly.
- **As posted, #57859 reverts code on** `main`**.** Its diff deletes `_mask_candidates_strided_kernel` and `_apply_candidate_mask_strided` (from #56628), so its fallback goes back to the shared full-width `_apply_candidate_mask`. It also deletes the C4A Triton paged-MQA decode path, the native top-512 gate in `_get_aiter_top_k_kernel` and `FP8_DTYPE`. `rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py` still imports `_apply_candidate_mask_strided`, so merging as-is would break that import. This is most likely a stale branch (last updated 2026-09-23) and needs a rebase.
- **Merge order.**
  - If this PR lands first, #57859's rebase should keep `_apply_candidate_mask_strided` in its fallback and adopt the `None` starts and `row_repeat` call. The conflict is in the same `if candidate_blocks is not None:` block.
  - If #57859 lands first, this change moves into its `else:` branch.

title: [Core][KVConnector] Don't wait on retained KV exports during cache-preserving keep pauses
body:
> [!NOTE]
> Moved from #58041 (originally by @S1ro1), which now carries only the HiSparse split-read fix. This PR is the general P/D part: it changes core pause semantics and needs a maintainer decision.

## Purpose

`pause(mode="keep", clear_cache=False)` on a NIXL producer can wait minutes during P/D weight updates even after model execution has stopped. Finished prefill requests whose KV the connector retains for a remote reader keep the engine active until the reader acknowledges or the lease expires. In a producer-first pause, a loaded decoder keeps renewing those leases for requests it hasn't read yet; @S1ro1 measured pauses over 60 s. The delayed-free gate already existed in v0.27; this is not a regression.

Related work: #51371 prioritizes KV work while unpaused; #57810 adds an opt-out from clearing the external offload tier during pause/sleep. Neither addresses pause completion with retained exports.

## Changes

- A keep pause that preserves the cache delivers newly finished request events, then leaves connector-retained blocks allocated across the pause instead of waiting for passive leases. Cleanup resumes after resume. Active push work and device synchronization still drain.
- Cache-clearing pauses keep the existing gate (`_reset_caches()` needs the blocks released), and `release_kv_cache_memory()` rejects retained KV.
- The engine sets the flag through a new optional `SchedulerInterface.set_preserve_paused_kv()` (no-op default), so `set_pause_state()` keeps its signature for out-of-tree schedulers. Any pause-state change clears it.

Open question: `POST /pause?mode=keep` defaults `clear_cache=true` (documented as ignored for keep), so the preserving path only engages when callers pass `clear_cache=false`.

## Test Plan

- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k "delayed_kv_connector_free_keeps_scheduler_active"`: retained KV keeps the scheduler active except during a preserving pause, and a pause-state change ends the preservation.
- `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py -k "kv_cache_release_rejects or pause_synchronizes"`: memory release rejects retained KV; the preserving pause synchronizes the device without resetting caches. (CUDA-gated module; run on CPU with the module skip removed.)

## Test Result

- Scheduler/connector lifecycle tests: 215 passed (CPU). Engine pause tests: 8 passed.
- Live validation by @S1ro1 (GLM-5.3 B300 RL, 2P+1D, DPEP8 per replica, NIXL + HiSparse + MooncakeStore, 2,048 concurrent rollouts): five trainer updates with natural pauses of 1.904 s, 2.647 s, 4.085 s, 3.860 s and 2.833 s; every weight update resumed; trainer mismatch KL 0.0218–0.0261. This used an equivalent Prime-RL runtime hook over the existing wheel together with a receive-side fix (now #58041), not a build of this branch. A receive-only patch still produced a 120 s loaded pause.

AI assistance was used (OpenAI Codex for the original change, Claude Code for the rework and this description).

title: [Bug]: cudagraph_mode=FULL crashes on prefill with FlashInfer sparse MLA on SM100
body:
### Your current environment

vLLM main @ `2a52715ef7`, 1× B200 (SM100), Model Runner V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `cudagraph_mode=FULL` and the FlashInfer sparse MLA backend on SM100 (`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`), the engine crashes as soon as a prefill chunk replays a FULL CUDA graph. `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, the default, works.

`FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMMetadataBuilder` declares `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS` (added in #52783), so `FULL` mode captures FULL graphs for mixed/prefill batches too. Neither MLA prefill backend can replay those:

| MLA prefill backend | Result |
|---|---|
| FlashAttention (default for DeepSeek-V3.2) | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` during FULL-graph replay |
| TRTLLM ragged (default for larger MLA dims, e.g. GLM-5.3) | `ValueError: TRTLLM ragged prefill contains mixed active and empty query rows: query_lens=[512, 0, 0, 0]`: the FULL graph pads the batch with empty requests |
| FlashInfer | not valid for these MLA dimensions |

In both failing cases, a 512-token prefill chunk is dispatched to a request-padded FULL graph. The variable-length verification FULL graphs that adaptive DSpark (#52783) needs may be what `ALWAYS` was meant for. If so, a lower support level plus the varlen-decode hook might cover that without capturing prefill.

**Repro** (DeepSeek-V3.2 shrunk to 4 layers, dummy weights; no HiSparse or KV connector). Pass `TRTLLM_RAGGED` or `FLASH_ATTN` as the argument to pick the prefill backend:

```python
# cudagraph_mode=FULL with FlashInfer sparse MLA (SM100) crashes when a
# prefill chunk replays a FULL graph. Usage: python repro.py [MLA_PREFILL_BACKEND]
import os
import sys

os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER", "1")

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

SHRINK = {"num_hidden_layers": 4, "hidden_size": 256, "intermediate_size": 512,
          "moe_intermediate_size": 128, "num_attention_heads": 8,
          "num_key_value_heads": 1, "n_routed_experts": 8, "num_experts_per_tok": 2,
          "n_shared_experts": 1, "first_k_dense_replace": 1, "index_topk": 128}


def shrink(config):
    config.update(SHRINK)
    if hasattr(config, "quantization_config"):
        delattr(config, "quantization_config")
    return config


def main() -> None:
    attention_config = {"backend": "FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE"}
    if len(sys.argv) > 1:
        attention_config["mla_prefill_backend"] = sys.argv[1]
    llm = LLM(
        "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2",
        load_format="dummy",
        hf_overrides=shrink,
        max_model_len=8192,
        max_num_seqs=4,
        max_num_batched_tokens=512,
        attention_config=attention_config,
        compilation_config={
            "cudagraph_mode": "FULL",
            "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512],
        },
    )
    prompts = [{"prompt_token_ids": list(range(1000, 3000))}]
    out = llm.generate(prompts, SamplingParams(max_tokens=16, ignore_eos=True))
    print("OK", len(out[0].outputs[0].token_ids))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

With `"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"` the same script prints `OK 16`.

This also blocks HiSparse users on `cudagraph_mode=FULL`. HiSparse has a separate hazard here: its prefill path branches on per-step page residency, which a FULL graph would freeze at capture. It is masked by this crash.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to reproduce and write up this issue.

title: [Bugfix][DeepSeek-V4.1] Keep the compressor ring out of the null KV block
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57156: identifies the write that poisons the null block. Thanks @sumsliu for the report and @hclsys for the scrub-ordering analysis there.

On SM12x with 64-token KV pages (tested on GB10), DeepSeek-V4.1 outputs one repeated token, because layer-0 attention returns NaN for real requests. FlashInfer's SM120 sparse-MLA kernels need those pages; `main` uses 32/128, so V4.1 doesn't run on SM12x yet without that support (see #57292).

Under block-outermost KV packing, block 0 (the null block) is shared by every group and must stay readable by all of them. The compressor ring's slot mapping comes from the block table, not from the per-token slot mapping that dummy runs fill with `PAD_SLOT_ID`. So dummy, warmup and capture runs, whose block tables are zeroed, write fp32 ring rows into block 0. FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1's SM120 sparse MLA clamps masked indices to 0 (`prefill_common.cuh:193`), so NaN bytes there get past the mask.

The existing block-0 scrub (`gpu/warmup.py:458`) runs only with JIT warmup and before CUDA graph capture, whose dummy runs write block 0 again. This PR masks block 0 out of the ring slot mapping instead. The ring's group has no per-token slot mapping (`CircularBufferSpec.uses_slot_mapping` is False), so the block id is the only signal, and real requests never hold block 0 (`block_pool.py:186`). It applies on every platform and changes nothing for real requests.

## Test Plan / Result

- New `test_v41_ring_slot_mapping_skips_null_block`: fails before the fix, passes after.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4× GB10 (`main` plus SM12x page support; TP4, DCP1 and DCP2, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE): before, repeated-token output; after, our count-to-100, structured-output and vision/tool gate passes.

cc @Juntian777 @zyongye (#59119 touched this kernel)

Drafted with Claude; reviewed and tested by me.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Kimi-K3: token-sharded residual stream for long prefills
body:
### Purpose

**Scope: ROCm only, Kimi-K3 only, opt-in.** All model changes are in
`vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/`, which is only loaded on ROCm, and the new path only
runs for Kimi-K3's attention-residual layers. It is off by default
(`VLLM_KIMI_K3_AMD_PREFILL_SP_MIN_TOKENS=0`). NVIDIA, other models and
CUDA-graph decode are unaffected.

With TP, every rank repeats the same per-token work (attention-residual mixing,
MoE router, latent down-projection, top-k) on all tokens. For eager steps with
at least `VLLM_KIMI_K3_AMD_PREFILL_SP_MIN_TOKENS` tokens (1024 recommended),
this PR shards the residual stream over tokens instead, padded to a multiple of
TP:

- Each block output all-reduce becomes a reduce-scatter plus an all-gather
before the next block, so communication volume is unchanged.
- Attention-residual mixing, the router and top-k run on the local shard only.
- The latent-MoE tail reduce-scatters its output over tokens instead of
all-reducing it.

It is off with PP, with DP > 1, during graph capture, and when aux hidden
states are requested (EAGLE drafters).

The NVIDIA Kimi-K3 path has something similar (`use_sequence_parallel` in
`nvidia/model.py`), but it only turns on with expert parallelism plus DP > 1
or DeepGEMM MegaMoE, for every step. This PR covers plain TP on ROCm, and only
for long prefill steps.

### Test Plan

- New `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_prefill_sp.py`: the MoE tail, regular and
token-sharded, matches the replicated result at TP4/TP8 for both the
`ColumnParallelLinear` and replicated up-projection layouts. The routing
all-gather and the gather of pre-quantized FP8 activations (data plus per-token
scale) are bit-exact, padded gather/scatter round-trips, and the enable
conditions are covered.
- With the existing Kimi-K3 AMD runner, KDA/MLA direct-return and sequence
parallel tests: 68 passed on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (vllm 77154ca61).
- End to end: 8x MI355X, Kimi-K3 MXFP4, TP8, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`
with and without `VLLM_KIMI_K3_AMD_PREFILL_SP_MIN_TOKENS=1024`,
`vllm bench serve`, random data, 1K output tokens. The agentic TP8 + DCP8
config (prefix caching, CPU KV offload, 24576 batched tokens) also serves
160/160 requests with and without the flag.

### Test Result

Δ vs stock nightly (same image, 2026-10-14); throughput is (input + output)
tok/s/GPU.

| Input | Conc. | Throughput | TTFT   |
| ----- | ----- | ---------- | ------ |
| 10K   | 32    | +4.4%      | -15.1% |
| 50K   | 32    | +8.5%      | -10.4% |
| 200K  | 8     | +7.4%      | -9.5%  |

An earlier 8-point sweep of the previous revision gave a geomean of +6.1%, with
1K prompts within run-to-run noise.

Accuracy matches stock (measured on the previous revision; the sharded path now
uses the same latent all-reduce as stock): GSM8K 5-shot 0.989 vs 0.982 (mean of
3 runs), passkey retrieval up to 190K 0.95-1.00 vs 0.95, and first-token top-1
agreement 20/20 on real-text prompts from 2K to 190K.

title: [Startup] Add VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE_ONLY to load the FlashInfer autotune cache and skip startup autotuning
body:
## Purpose

`flashinfer_autotune()` runs the FlashInfer autotuning pass on every engine start, even when a persisted cache for the same configuration exists: the cache is loaded, then the tuning dummy runs execute anyway. Deployments that restart the same configuration repeatedly have no way to say "use the cache I prepared and do not tune".

This PR adds an opt-in `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE_ONLY=1`:

- **Disabled by default.** With the variable unset, `flashinfer_autotune()` is unchanged.
- **When enabled**, each tuning group's leader reads its existing cache file (same path as today, including the per-PP-stage file), broadcasts it within the tuning group, and every rank loads it. After a successful load, the autotune dummy runs, ReplaySSM/Kimi tuning, the BF16 pass, `set_autotune_process_group`, the trailing barrier and the cache save are all skipped.
- **Fail-closed.** It does not fall back to autotuning or heuristics. If the file is missing, empty or unreadable, or if `AutoTuner.load_configs()` raises or returns `False` (FlashInfer's environment-metadata mismatch) on any rank, every rank raises the same `RuntimeError` naming the failing ranks.
- **Consistent decision across ranks.** Each rank's error (or `None`) is collected with one `all_gather_object` over the world CPU group, following the pattern in `engram.py`. Every rank therefore issues the same collectives (one tuning-group broadcast, one world gather) and reaches the same decision, including under PP > 1, where a missing stage-1 cache also stops stage 0. The cache is loaded from a per-rank temporary file, so nothing is written to the (possibly read-only) cache directory.
- **Scoped to `flashinfer_autotune()`.** DeepGEMM, JIT and attention warmups are untouched. The separate SM12x sparse-MLA decode autotune (`flashinfer_sparse_mla_decode_autotune_warmup`) is also unaffected. If `enable_flashinfer_autotune=False`, the variable has no effect and a warning is logged.
- Added to the `compile_factors()` ignore list next to `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE_DIR`, so toggling it does not invalidate the torch.compile cache. It does not enter `vllm_config.compute_hash()`, so the autotune cache path is the same with and without it.

### What a successful load does and does not mean

`load_configs()` returning `True` only means FlashInfer accepted the file. It does not mean every op this engine runs has an entry. Ops without an entry use FlashInfer's default tactic, and the log line says so. In particular, FlashInfer keys some MoE entries by `tp_rank`/`ep_rank` (`MoERunner.get_cache_key_extras`), so a cache saved by rank 0 alone (today's behaviour) has no MoE entries for other ranks; see #57423 / #57635. In cache-only mode those ranks do not deadlock, because nothing is tuned, but they run those MoE ops with the default tactic. Making the persisted cache cover all ranks is a separate problem (#57635, #55671) and is intentionally not part of this PR.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open and closed issues/PRs (titles and bodies) for "flashinfer autotune cache", "autotune cache only", `FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE`, `autotune_configs.json`, "skip flashinfer autotune", "flashinfer autotune load_configs", "reuse/offline/pretuned autotune" and related terms, plus flashinfer-ai/flashinfer. Related work and how this differs:

- #55671 (draft) migrates warmup to `autotune_v2` managed per-entry caches. It changes cache ownership and persistence and "does not claim … zero warm-start profiling". It has no opt-in skip and no fail-closed mode. The two touch the same function, so one will need a rebase onto the other. This PR is a small early-return and should be easy to carry.
- #57635 / #57579 (closed) / #54618 (closed) / #57423 (issue) fix the warm-cache deadlock by making per-rank cache hits consistent. That is cache content and consistency, not skipping the pass.
- #59435 skips the pass when the weight-cache daemon (`--load-format ipc_cache`) supplies a table, and falls back to tuning on a miss. That is daemon-only and fail-open. This PR covers file-based caches and is fail-closed.
- #52292 (opt out of synchronized tuning) and #48268 (`VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_SKIP_OPS`, merged) control *how* tuning runs, not whether it is skipped.

## Test Plan

CPU-only tests in `tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py`. They use a fake `AutoTuner` and fake process groups whose collectives rendezvous across one thread per rank, so a rank that skips or adds a collective shows up as a barrier timeout instead of a hang:

- success, TP=1 and TP=2: every rank loads the leader's bytes, no tuning runs, nothing is written to the cache directory;
- missing / empty / unreadable (directory) cache: all ranks fail with the same message naming rank 0, and no rank calls the loader;
- loader returns `False`, or raises, on the leader (rank 0) or on a non-leader (rank 3): all ranks fail with the same message naming that rank;
- PP=2 × TP=2: each stage loads its own `_tp_<ranks>` file through its TP-group broadcast; one world gather; a missing stage-1 cache fails stage-0 ranks too;
- variable set to `0`: the existing autotune path (synchronized tuning and rank-0 save) still runs.

Commands (macOS arm64, Python 3.12, torch 2.13.0 CPU, source tree on `PYTHONPATH`, no vLLM C extensions or FlashInfer installed):

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py -q
PYTHONPATH=. PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/test_envs.py -q
pre-commit run --files docs/configuration/optimization.md vllm/envs.py \
  vllm/model_executor/warmup/flashinfer_autotune_cache.py \
  vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <same files>
```

## Test Result

- `test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py`: **19 passed** (8 existing, 11 new). The cache-only subset was run 3 times with identical results.
- `tests/test_envs.py`: **57 passed**.
- pre-commit (ruff check/format, typos, markdownlint, mypy-3.10, test tethering, SPDX, forbidden imports, …): **passed**. `mypy-3.12` (manual stage): **passed**.
- Docs: `mkdocs build --strict -f mkdocs.yaml` (same strict mode as Read the Docs) **passed** locally. The new text renders in `configuration/optimization` and in the generated `configuration/env_vars` reference. The Read the Docs check on this PR was skipped because the first-contributor `pre-run-check` gate failed, not because of a docs error.
- Sanity checks on the tests themselves: with the implementation reverted, the new cache-only tests fail. Removing the world gather makes 8 tests fail; gathering over the PP-stage group instead of the world fails the PP test; ignoring `load_configs()`'s return value fails both rejection cases.

These are control-flow tests with fakes. **They are not GPU validation.**

### GPU validation status

**No GPU validation has been done on this upstream implementation.** I don't currently have access to a GPU machine.

The only GPU evidence is historical and comes from a different, locally patched build: a two-rank MiMo-V2.6-Flash deployment (TP=2, EP, FP8, `flashinfer_cutlass` MoE, DFlash speculative decoding) on vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev449` with FlashInfer `0.6.18.post1` on SM 9.0a. It ran with a local cache-only patch that this PR's design is based on, but not identical to. Both ranks logged `Loaded 84 configs` from the same cache file, the cache-only message, and `Config cache hit … source=config file` for the MoE GEMMs, and the engine served normally afterwards. That deployment also used a separately prepared cache containing entries for every rank, which this PR does not include. No startup-time measurements are claimed.

Checks I'd ask a GPU-equipped reviewer to run (Hopper or Blackwell, current pinned FlashInfer):

1. Single rank, cache hit: startup logs the cache-only message, no `Tuning …` lines, and serving works.
2. Single rank, missing cache and a cache from a different FlashInfer/GPU: startup fails with the cache-only `RuntimeError`, without autotuning.
3. TP=2 (+EP) MoE model, cache hit: all ranks load the cache and startup completes without a collective hang. Check which ranks report MoE cache hits (see the rank-keying note above).
4. TP=2, missing or invalid cache on one rank's node: all ranks fail with the same error and nothing deadlocks.
5. PP=2: per-stage caches load, and a missing stage cache fails the whole engine.
6. Variable unset: ordinary autotune and cache persistence are unchanged.
7. After cache-only startup, representative FlashInfer ops (MoE, GEMM, attention) execute, and no runtime JIT or tuning happens on first requests.

## Notes

- Env var versus `KernelConfig` field: I followed the neighbouring `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE_DIR` / `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_SKIP_OPS` env vars. Happy to switch to something like `--kernel-config.flashinfer_autotune=cache_only` if maintainers prefer.
- Known limitation: a rank that dies hard, for example from a segfault inside `load_configs`, can't take part in the gather, and the other ranks then wait for the process-group timeout. The engine's existing worker-death handling applies, as it does for any collective.

AI assistance was used to investigate, draft and test this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Expand indexer block tables when kernel blocks span several storage blocks
body:
## Overview

Fixes the sparse-attention indexer reading the wrong cache slots on GLM-5.3-Flash/ROCm once a sequence exceeds 2048 tokens (the dense-shortcut threshold). The indexer block table is in kernel-block units (1152 tokens), but the compressed indexer cache is paged in smaller storage blocks (128 tokens). The builder only converted the table when the kernel block was *smaller* than the storage block.

## Claims

- Fixes corrupted sparse top-k selection beyond 2048 tokens for GLM-5.3-Flash on ROCm (MI355X), in both prefill and decode.
- Restores GPQA-Diamond accuracy from 80.8–85.4% (with degenerate, non-terminating generations) to 89.9–91.4%. This matches the pre-regression baseline.
- No behavior change when the kernel block size equals the storage block size or divides it (the existing path). That covers NVIDIA, DeepSeek-V3.2 and every model that doesn't set `storage_block_size`.

## Validation

Unit tests (`tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py`):

- `test_to_storage_block_table`: CPU-only checks of the conversion helper. It covers no kernel block size, equal sizes, kernel smaller than storage (the existing collapse) and kernel larger than storage (the new expand).
- `test_indexer_builder_expands_kernel_blocks_to_storage_blocks`: builds the indexer metadata with a 1152-token kernel block over a 128-token / `tokens_per_state=4` storage spec. It checks every prefill compressed slot and every decode block-table entry against slots computed independently.

```
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py
# with fix:    33 passed
# without fix: 5 failed (the new tests), 28 passed
```

End to end, GLM-5.3-Flash on MI355X, TP=2:

Decode-vs-prefill consistency. For each sequence, I generate greedily, then re-score the same tokens with a single prefill. "Gap" is the mean |logprob(decode) − logprob(prefill)| over the first 64 generated tokens. "Flips" is the share of positions where the argmax differs.

| Build | Mean gap | Argmax flips |
|---|---|---|
| Older base (pre-regression) | 0.074 | 6.1% |
| Current main, unfixed | 0.53–0.69 | 23–25% |
| Current main + fix, bf16 | 0.075 | 5.3% |
| Current main + fix, MXFP4 MLA | 0.069 | 4.3% |

GPQA-Diamond (198 questions):

| Build | Accuracy |
|---|---|
| Current main, unfixed (8 runs, bf16 + MXFP4) | 80.81–85.35%, degenerate/runaway generations |
| Current main + fix, MXFP4, seeds 42/43/44 | 90.40 / 90.40 / 91.41% |
| Current main + fix, bf16, seed 42 | 89.90% |
| Older base, bf16 / MXFP4 | 88.89–91.41% / 90.40–91.92% |

With the fix, wall time per GPQA run also drops from ~3000–3700 s to ~2000–2400 s, because generations no longer run away to the max token limit.

## Details

**Root cause.** On ROCm, `Glm5NextIndexerCache.get_kv_cache_spec` sets `storage_block_size = page_size * kpool` = 128 tokens. A 1152-token hybrid-aligned block holds 288 kpool states, which isn't a multiple of 64, so it is stored as nine 32-state pages. The ROCm indexer backend accepts `MultipleOf(16)` kernel blocks, so `set_kernel_block_size(1152)` leaves the block table in 1152-token units. `DeepseekV32IndexerMetadataBuilder` only handled `storage % kernel == 0` (the `[:, ::f] // f` collapse). Otherwise it passed the 1152-unit table through as if it held 128-token ids. Slots were computed as `T[pos // 128] * 32 + (pos // 4) % 32`, so `pos // 128` indexed past the real table entries. Beyond the first few pages, states read zero padding and aliased onto null block 0, which every request shares. Below 2048 tokens the indexer takes a dense causal shortcut, so the bug only appears on long sequences.

Worked example, for a request whose block table is `[5, 7, 2]` (each physical block is 9 indexer pages):

```text
token 1400
  fixed: 1400 // 1152 = entry 1 -> block 7 -> page 7*9 + (1400-1152)//128 = 63 + 1 = 64
  old:   1400 // 128  = 10 -> table[10] is past the 3 entries -> padding 0 -> page 0 (null block)

early tokens (pos < 384)
  old:   table[pos // 128] = 5, 7 or 2, used directly as a page id -> pages 5/7/2, also inside null block 0
```

So every request read and wrote its compressed keys in the same few null-block pages.

**Fix.** Add `_to_storage_block_table`, which re-expresses the kernel-block table in storage blocks. It keeps the existing collapse when the kernel block divides the storage block. When the storage block divides the kernel block, it expands kernel block `k` into `k*f … k*f+f-1`. Both call sites (the compressed slot mapping / prefill table, and the decode paged-MQA block table) use it. If neither size divides the other, it returns `None` and the table passes through unchanged, as before.

**Scope.** Only specs with `storage_block_size` set and smaller than the kernel block take the new path. Today that is GLM-5.3 on ROCm. On NVIDIA the indexer kernel block is 64 tokens, so the existing collapse branch applies. DeepSeek V3.2 uses `compress_ratio = 1` without a storage split.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

title: [Bug][SM120] MTP speculative decoding acceptance rate drops to 0% on nightly with native FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120 backend (GLM-5.3-Flash)
body:
## Environment
- vLLM: `0.30.1rc1.dev539+g5b6b657e1` (nightly wheel, 2026-10-02 build, commit `5b6b657e1`)
- Hardware: 8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), PCIe, no NVLink
- Model: GLM-5.3-Flash (FP8 checkpoint, TP=8)
- flashinfer-python: 0.7.0
- Base image: vllm-openai v0.30.0 + nightly wheel force-reinstall (no-deps)

## Observed behavior
MTP speculative decoding drafts tokens but the acceptance rate is **exactly 0%** — every drafted token is rejected. Decode speed falls back to non-speculative baseline (~80 tok/s vs ~163-190 tok/s with working MTP).

SpecDecoding metrics from server log (eager mode, spec_tokens=3, 512-token essay generation):

```
Mean acceptance length: 1.00, Accepted throughput: 0.00 tokens/s,
Drafted throughput: 82.20 tokens/s, Accepted: 0 tokens, Drafted: 822 tokens,
Per-position acceptance rate: 0.000, 0.000, 0.000, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 0.0%
```

## Three-leg isolation (all on identical config: fp8, TP8, mem 0.94, block-size 2304, mtp, max-model-len 1M)

| Leg | Mode | spec_tokens | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CUDA graph (default) | 3 | 0% (76-83 tok/s) |
| 2 | --enforce-eager | 3 | 0% |
| 3 | --enforce-eager | 1 | 0% (100 drafted / 0 accepted) |

All three legs rule out graph-mode interaction and multi-step draft-forward as the cause.

## Key log lines

```
(Worker_TP0) speculator.py:116 Fused multi-step draft decode is not supported by attention backend(s) DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER, FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120, KPOOL_TAIL; falling back to rebuilding attention metadata between draft steps.
(APIServer) speculative.py:1136 method `glm5_next_mtp` is deprecated and replaced with mtp.
(APIServer) interface.py:1336 Unknown vLLM environment variable detected: VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND
```

The nightly auto-selects the native `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` backend (`VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND` env no longer recognized). The target model's forward is correct (generations are coherent), but the MTP drafter output is systematically rejected — suggesting the draft forward pass produces wrong logits under the native SM120 attention path.

## Working baseline (for contrast)
A community image based on v0.30.0 with a backported SM90 NoPE sparse-MLA path (forced `VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90`, flashinfer 0.6.18.dev20260819) on the **same hardware, same checkpoint, same spec config** achieves:
- Mean acceptance ~60.7%, acceptance length ~2.8
- decode 163-190 tok/s

So the regression is specific to the nightly native SM120 backend's interaction with MTP drafting (or the drafter's attention path), not the model or hardware.

## Reproduce

```
docker run --gpus all -v /path/GLM-5.3-Flash:/model:ro \
  -v vllm-0.30.1rc1.dev539...x86_64.whl:/tmp/nightly.whl:ro \
  --entrypoint bash vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 \
  -c 'pip install --no-deps --force-reinstall /tmp/nightly.whl && \
      vllm serve /model --served-model-name glm-5.3-flash --trust-remote-code \
      --tensor-parallel-size 8 --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 1048576 \
      --max-num-seqs 256 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.94 --block-size 2304 \
      --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --enable-auto-tool-choice \
      --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 \
      --speculative-config "{\"method\":\"mtp\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":3}"'
```

Then generate ~512 tokens and check `SpecDecoding metrics` lines: acceptance 0%.

Happy to provide full server logs or run additional diagnostics on request.

title: [Feature]: Integrate Cake kernels via FlashInfer: model-by-model tracker
body:
**End-to-end validation and issue reporting:** Our shape coverage and correctness have not yet been validated end to end in model serving. If you encounter (1) end-to-end accuracy degradation, (2) unsuitable API requirements, such as unnecessarily requiring contiguous inputs, or (3) faster kernel benchmarks but worse end-to-end performance because the shapes optimized by the kernel do not cover the actual model-serving workload, please open an issue and tag @yyihuang with the affected kernel, the missing or problematic shape(s), and relevant model/serving details or a reproducer. We will resolve reported issues within **6 hours**.

## Motivation

Track integration of Cake kernels already delivered through FlashInfer into vLLM, grouped by the models that requested them. The upstream inventory is [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4254](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4254); model requirements below come from its subissues and the linked implementation PRs.

The proposed integration is through FlashInfer's public/prepared APIs. Each task should connect the relevant model operator, weight/cache layout, and execution mode to an eligible kernel, then measure the complete serving path. Upstream kernel benchmarks are useful starting points, not claims of vLLM end-to-end speedup.

**Snapshot: 2026-10-03 (UTC; October 2 in US Pacific); FlashInfer main [46340689a5ab](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/46340689a5ab5665ab39f6281dac4d021d7ae94b).** “Merged” below means available in upstream FlashInfer, not necessarily in a released wheel or integrated here. Open follow-ups are explicitly marked and are not included in the merged coverage. Most listed kernels target SM100/SM103; exact architecture, SM-count, dtype, layout, and shape admission remain API-specific. Let the serving adapter retain its existing backend for configurations outside those contracts.

Notation: `T/M` = token rows, `B` = requests, `Q` = query tokens per request, `S` = KV length. MoE tuples are **(hidden size, expert intermediate size, number of experts, top-k)**; an intermediate size marked “local” is after TP sharding. Enumerated benchmark shapes are evidence points, not an assertion that every combination is supported.

vLLM already has FlashInfer hooks for several of these models. This tracker proposes selecting and qualifying the Cake implementations through those hooks and adding prepared adapters where needed.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Fuse main QK-norm/RoPE/gate and KV-cache write into the AMD QSA prepare launch
body:
## Overview

On ROCm, the Qwen4Exp QSA layer's main-attention QK-norm, RoPE, gate split and K/V cache write now run inside the fused QSA prepare launch, as #57097 did for NVIDIA.

## Claims

- MI355X TP2 `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`: +0.9% to +2.9% output throughput, faster in all 8 measured cells (4 points × 2 repeats).
- Accuracy neutral: GSM8K 0.9638 → 0.9605 over 6 pairs, a −0.33 point paired difference within run-to-run noise (paired t = −1.8, 5 df).
- Kernel numerics no worse than the unfused AMD chain against an fp64 reference; the gate is bit-identical.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (gfx950): 24 passed, 8 skipped.

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_amd.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py
```

- `test_qsa_prepare_amd.py` (renamed from `test_qsa_pre_indexer_amd.py`): in all 8 bf16 configurations, the indexer outputs match as before, and the main attention matches the AMD layer's unfused chain (split, Gemma RMSNorm, the layer's `rotary_emb`, `reshape_and_cache_flash`): Q and the paged K/V cache within bf16 tolerance, including MRoPE; the gate bit for bit, in the caller's buffer. The 8 FP8 cases skip: the AMD QSA caches are bf16-only.
- `test_qsa_amd.py`: the fused path passes the real tokens' `qkv`, `slot_mapping`, gate buffer, per-token cache view and norm weights; the unfused path never calls the kernel.
- Runs in the existing AMD `models_basic` step.

**Serving**, MI355X TP2, one-factor A/B against the same image without this change (#57947 in both arms), two repeats with the arms on rotated GPU pairs. `control → candidate`, mean of the repeats:

| ISL | OSL | Conc | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT (ms) | Per repeat, tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8,192 | 1,024 | 4 | 462.0 → 475.5 (+2.9%) | 7.39 → 7.12 (−3.7%) | +1.1% / +4.8% |
| 8,192 | 1,024 | 16 | 964.1 → 975.3 (+1.2%) | 13.70 → 13.51 (−1.4%) | +1.4% / +1.0% |
| 8,192 | 1,024 | 64 | 1457.2 → 1471.0 (+0.9%) | 35.44 → 35.17 (−0.8%) | +1.4% / +0.5% |
| 60,000 | 600 | 4 | 144.8 → 147.4 (+1.8%) | 14.23 → 13.96 (−1.9%) | +0.8% / +2.7% |

```bash
# plus the checkpoint card's ROCm environment and flags, identical in both arms
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 256 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code
vllm bench serve --model amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --max-concurrency 64 --num-prompts 128
```

**Accuracy**, GSM8K 5-shot on the checkpoint card's recipe (flexible-extract), 6 control/candidate pairs run side by side:

| pair | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | mean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| control | 0.9659 | 0.9674 | 0.9629 | 0.9621 | 0.9598 | 0.9644 | 0.9638 |
| candidate | 0.9560 | 0.9606 | 0.9636 | 0.9629 | 0.9553 | 0.9644 | 0.9605 |

One GSM8K run's standard error is about 0.005, so the per-pair differences (−1.0 to +0.1 points) sit within run-to-run noise.

<details>
<summary>Kernel numerics against fp64, 256 tokens at positions up to 200k, Flash-Next per-rank head counts</summary>

| | fused, max / mean abs error | unfused, max / mean abs error |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main Q, text RoPE | 0.0296 / 0.00130 | 0.0411 / 0.00139 |
| main K, text RoPE | 0.0259 / 0.00127 | 0.0432 / 0.00134 |
| main Q, MRoPE | 0.0302 / 0.00124 | 0.0302 / 0.00132 |
| main K, MRoPE | 0.0200 / 0.00123 | 0.0287 / 0.00132 |

</details>

## Details

- **Kernel.** `amd/ops/qsa_pre_indexer.py` becomes `amd/ops/qsa_prepare.py`, matching NVIDIA's naming, and takes #57097's main-attention programs unchanged. Its only other difference from NVIDIA's kernel is still #57947's two-masked-load state select.
- **Gate out of the op.** The AMD layer applies the output gate after its opaque QSA op, so the gate has to come out of it. A new `qwen4_exp_qsa_prepare_with_output` custom op takes the packed `qkv` and mutates `output` and `gate`; the wrapper's optional `main_gate_out` writes the gate straight into that buffer.
- **Padding rows.** `* sigmoid(gate)` stays in the compiled graph, where Inductor fuses it as before. NVIDIA's attention kernel gates real tokens only; AMD's graph gates every row, so the op zeroes the gate's cudagraph-padding rows, keeping them at the zero output `forward_qsa` writes. With no padding the fill launches nothing.
- **Eligibility.** On when the layer has an output gate, the indexer passes `supports_fused_pre_indexer`, and the main head dim is a power of two. The main RoPE reads the indexer's cos/sin table, which is the layer's own `rotary_emb`. Otherwise both prepares take the unfused chain, as on NVIDIA.
- **No CPU/GPU sync** on the hot path: eligibility is decided at init; the gate padding size is the static difference between the padded and real token counts.

- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

Non-streaming is fine. ### Steps to reproduce Deployed via Docker, vLLM 0.21.0: vllm serve /models/deepseek \ --served-model-name DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B \ --dtype bfloat16 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 8192 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --reasoning-parser deepseek_r1 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B","messages":[{"role":"user", "content":"请用三句话介绍一下你自己。"}],"temperature":0.6, "max_tokens":256,"stream":true}' ### Observed data: {...,"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning":"Ċ"},...}]} data: {...,"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning":"åĹ¯"},...}]} data: {...,"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning":"ï¼Į"},...}]} ### Expected first delta should be a newline, then "嗯", then "，" ### Additional information Byte-level analysis of the leaked glyphs: "Ċ" -> 0x0A -> "\n" "åĹ¯" -> E5 97 AF -> "嗯" "ï¼Į" -> EF BC 8C -> "，" i.e. the reasoning path looks like it returns convert_ids_to_tokens() output without the convert_tokens_to_string()/decode() step, and multi-byte characters also stay split across chunks at token boundaries. Control experiment: removing --reasoning-parser deepseek_r1 makes the same output arrive correctly (as regular content), and stream=false is also correct — so the issue is specific to the streaming reasoning path. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [ROCm][Attention] MXFP4 KV cache with native FP8 x FP4 sparse MLA attention for GLM-5.3-Flash
body:
## Overview

Adds an `mxfp4_mla` KV cache dtype for the ROCm AITER sparse MLA backend on rope-free (NoPE) latents such as GLM-5.3-Flash. It covers both the read/write path and low-precision attention arithmetic. Each 512-wide latent is stored as 256 bytes of E2M1 codes plus 16 inline E8M0 scales (one per 32 values): 272 bytes per token against 1024 for bf16, or 3.76× more tokens per GiB of KV cache. On gfx950, an opt-in native kernel computes attention directly on the packed cache with FP8 × FP4 scaled MFMA.

## Claims

- **KV capacity:** 3.76× more tokens per GiB than bf16 (272 vs 1024 bytes per token).
- **Throughput:** +6.1% to +8.5% output tokens/s over bf16 on upstream main, on MI355X at TP=4 from 16k to 130k context, using the native path.
- **Accuracy matches bf16:** GSM8K 97.42% vs 96.97%. GPQA-Diamond 90.40 / 90.40 / 91.41% over three seeds vs 89.90% for bf16 (see the note on the indexer fix below).
- **No change for other KV dtypes,** apart from two small decode-overhead trims that apply to every dtype. bf16 throughput on this branch tracks upstream main.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (MI355X / gfx950, with this branch's Python tree):

```
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mxfp4_mla*.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_sparse_host_decode_indptr.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_glm5next_sparse.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_triton_sparse_mla.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_decode_routing.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py
# 616 passed, 18 skipped (the skips are the CUDA-only layout tests)
```

The new tests cover:
- the format math, checked bit-for-bit against AITER's `per_1x32_f4_quant`;
- the store kernel, including slot offsets past 2^31 bytes;
- the Triton read path, checked against a dequantize-then-attend reference;
- the native HIP kernel and its Triton port, checked against a reference that mirrors their chunking and P rounding;
- the startup plumbing (hybrid block sizing, KV spec bytes) and the routing and return contract of the backend's forward.

Gating: the native, Triton-native and hardware-unpack tests skip off gfx950, and the other GPU tests skip off ROCm. Without a GPU the set gives 39 passed and 71 skipped, with no failures.

**Accuracy** (GLM-5.3-Flash on MI355X; GPQA uses temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 and a 163,840-token limit):

| Benchmark | bf16 | MXFP4 native, this PR |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K (1319 questions) | 96.97% (this PR's build) | 97.42% |
| GPQA-Diamond (198 questions), seed 42 | 89.90% (upstream main) | 90.40% |
| GPQA-Diamond, seed 43 | — | 90.40% |
| GPQA-Diamond, seed 44 | — | 91.41% |

Both GPQA columns were run with a fix applied for the sparse-indexer page-addressing bug on GLM-5.3-Flash/ROCm (issue #58858; open fix in #59412). Without it, upstream main degrades on long generations for bf16 and MXFP4 alike (80.8–85.4% across 8 runs), independently of this PR. For reference, an older base without that regression gave bf16 88.89–91.41% and MXFP4 90.40–91.92%.

**Serving** (TP=4 on MI355X, 128 output tokens, mean of 2 reps on separate boots, no other jobs on the GPUs; output tokens/s):

| Context / concurrency | bf16, main | bf16, this PR | MXFP4 native, this PR | vs main | Median ITL, main → MXFP4 (ms) | Median TTFT, main → MXFP4 (s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16k / 32 | 232.9 | 229.8 | 252.8 | +8.5% | 15.84 → 13.84 | 2.42 → 2.66 |
| 16k / 64 | 248.8 | 249.1 | 269.3 | +8.2% | 21.51 → 19.28 | 2.42 → 2.46 |
| 64k / 16 | 60.0 | 59.6 | 65.1 | +8.5% | 14.66 → 12.91 | 6.55 → 6.98 |
| 130k / 8 | 28.8 | 28.2 | 30.5 | +6.1% | 12.95 → 10.74 | 12.80 → 15.41 |

The serving and GSM8K numbers were measured with this commit on upstream `ed3f6d1`. I then rebased onto current main, which applied cleanly. None of the intervening commits touch the sparse MLA backend or ops, and I reran the unit tests above on the rebased tree.

## Details

**Format and write path.** The `mxfp4_mla` row is 256 bytes of packed E2M1 (low nibble holds the lower index) followed by 16 E8M0 scales. Scales use the round-up exponent, so no value clamps. `MLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec` reports the 272-byte row through `state_content_bytes`, and `Platform._align_hybrid_block_size` uses the same size so the mamba state still fits one attention page on hybrid models. `concat_and_cache_mla` can't express per-group scales (its `scale` is a single float), so a Triton store kernel behind `do_kv_cache_update` quantizes and writes the row.

**Read, portable path (default).** The ragged Triton sparse-attention kernel gains a `KV_IS_MXFP4` branch. It unpacks a gathered tile to bf16 once and feeds both existing `tl.dot` calls. On gfx950 with Triton 3.7, `tl.dot_scaled` lowers to a bf16 MFMA after upconverting anyway, so it would offer no arithmetic advantage over unpacking once. The decode-only kernels have no MXFP4 branch and refuse a packed cache rather than misread it.

**Read, native path (opt-in, gfx950).** This is a HIP kernel using `v_mfma_scale_f32_16x16x128_f8f6f4` for both QK and PV:
- Q is E4M3 with a per-head absmax scale.
- K and V are read directly as MXFP4.
- P is E4M3 with V's E8M0 group scales folded in.
- Work is split along the KV axis, and the partial results are merged with a log-sum-exp combine.

It's compiled with hipcc on first use and cached. A Triton port of the same arithmetic (`tl.dot_scaled` plus inline FP4 converts) can be selected for comparison: it matches HIP at decode sizes and is about 2× slower at prefill.

**Decode overhead (all dtypes).**
- Pure-decode steps build `paged_kv_indptr` on the host in pinned memory instead of launching three small kernels. This is disabled under speculative decoding, where the host sequence-length bound isn't exact.
- A contiguous NoPE query skips the `q_concat` copy.

**Limitations.**
- **Long-context TTFT:** median TTFT rises at 130k (12.8 s → 15.4 s), although P99 falls. Long-context MXFP4 prefill hasn't been profiled yet.
- **Where the gain comes from:** at 16k, a split-KV bf16 kernel matches the native kernel's per-step decode time. Don't read the throughput gain as 4-bit arithmetic alone; part of it is capacity and prefill.
- **Hardware:** the native path is gfx950 only. On other ROCm GPUs, `mxfp4_mla` uses the portable Triton path, which I haven't measured on gfx942.

**Open questions for reviewers.**
1. The native path is switched by `GLM53_MXFP4_NATIVE` / `GLM53_MXFP4_NATIVE_IMPL` (and `GLM53_NATIVE_CACHE` for the build cache), read with `os.getenv`. I'm happy to move these into `vllm/envs.py` as `VLLM_ROCM_*` variables, or into a config option.
2. The HIP kernel is built at runtime with hipcc rather than through CMake. Would you prefer it under `csrc/rocm`?
3. The two decode-overhead trims are independent of MXFP4. I can split them into a separate PR if that's easier to review.

title: [MRV2][Spec Decode] Context Aware Sparse LM Head
body:
## Overview **+13.8% decode at c=1 (+7.7% at c=4) from the sparse LM head alone**, with average AL unchanged (+0.1%), on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 + MTP (k=3) on one DGX Spark. It composes with quantization: +23.3% with NVFP4 rows, and +5.5 to 7.9% on top of a full NVFP4 draft head (#59973) across draft lengths k=3 to 8 (see below). Addresses #58578. **Why:** an MTP drafter reads the target's full lm_head for every draft token (248k x 2560 in BF16 on Flash-Next, about 7.4 ms per call on GB10), so on bandwidth-bound GPUs the head, not the drafter layer, dominates the draft step, while only a small, context-dependent part of the vocabulary is ever likely. **Why context-aware:** a fixed list alone misses whatever the current text needs beyond the common tokens: on SPEED-Bench a static 32k list loses 5.7% of average AL and 33% on multilingual, while adding the context-picked rows keeps average AL within 0.1% and cuts the multilingual loss to 4.7%. **How:** the drafter scores a fixed 32k-token list plus, per draft token, the 16k other rows that score best under a rank-256 SVD copy of the lm_head, computing exact logits only for those rows; the target still verifies with its full head, so only the acceptance length can change. Draft-vocabulary handling moves into model code: one shared `DraftVocab` helper returns target-vocabulary logits, and EAGLE3, DFlash and DSpark use it instead of their own `draft_id_to_target_id` scatter. Speculators no longer know about the draft vocabulary. Opt-in keys in `speculative_config`: `draft_token_map` (token ids, SGLang `.pt` or JSON), `draft_token_map_dynamic_rows` / `_rank` (context-picked rows, rank-256 basis built at load in 0.4 s), `draft_token_map_quantization` (`fp8` / `nvfp4` rows for an unquantized head). Quantized lm_heads are rejected here; support for them is in #60226. ## Results SPEED-Bench qualitative (11 categories, 409 requests, greedy, 256 tokens), Flash-Next, MTP k=3, FP8 KV, GB10, with this branch's fused kernel (3ed5c097f7, measured on the #60226 head, which stacks on this PR); each row against its own stock run on the same node: | draft rows (32k list + 16k dynamic) | AL avg | AL multilingual | decode c=1 | decode c=4 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | stock (full BF16 head), mean of the 3 runs | 2.667 | 2.827 | 39.6 tok/s | 26.4 tok/s | | BF16 | +0.1% | -4.7% | +13.8% | +7.7% | | FP8 | -1.1% | -8.1% | +20.6% | +11.0% | | NVFP4 | -0.8% | -6.6% | **+23.3%** | +13.6% | GSM8K (first 200, greedy): stock 98.5%, NVFP4 rows 98.0%. Disclaimers: - Low-concurrency feature: dynamic rows are gathered per token, so the gain shrinks with tokens per step (c=4 above). - Multilingual AL drops 5 to 8% (a static list alone loses 30% or more). - All comparisons are within one node; cross-node stock AL varies by about 0.5%.
More results: composition with quantization, other models, list source On top of a full NVFP4 draft head (#59973), same code as above, BF16 MTP-layer KV, each cell a same-node pair, decode c=1 (c=4): k=3 +5.8% (+3.7%), k=4 +7.5% (+3.7%), k=5 +5.5% (+1.4%), k=6 +6.8% (+2.7%), k=7 +6.1% (+0.5%), k=8 +7.9% (+6.7%), average AL within 1.5%. On checkpoints that ship an NVFP4 lm_head (#60226) the gain grows with draft length, because each draft token reads the head once: `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` +8.0% at k=3 to +13.7% at k=7, `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` +5.5% at k=3 to +12.2% at k=8. Earlier revision of this branch, same node per comparison: - Other BF16-head models, BF16 rows: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (`RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`) -0.4% AL, +35% decode; Qwen3.8-27B (`RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-BF16-LMHead`) -0.1% AL, +31%. - The list source barely matters with dynamic rows: model outputs, the lowest 32k ids, English Wikipedia, or no list land within 0.0% to -2.1% avg AL (static 32k alone: -5.7% to -9.6%).
Design details - `vllm/model_executor/layers/draft_vocab.py`: `DraftVocab.compute_logits` returns target-vocabulary logits that are `-inf` outside the draft vocabulary; `get_top_tokens` keeps local-argmax greedy drafting without full logits. The subset is either a checkpoint-pruned head with `draft_id_to_target_id` (EAGLE3, DFlash) or the `draft_token_map` rows of a full head. - MTP drafters share the target lm_head only inside `load_eagle_model`, so the listed rows are copied right after sharing; that is the one speculator-side hook. - Quantized rows run on the platform's weight-only kernels (`init_wfp8_a16_linear_kernel`, `init_nvfp4_linear_kernel`). vLLM's online quantization has no NVFP4 linear method yet, so `_Rows` sets the layer attributes a quantization scheme would. The scorer is FP8 when rows are quantized: an NVFP4 scorer ties at c=1 and loses 1.9 points at c=4. - The static list stays: dropping it (dynamic rows only, 16k to 49k) was 0.2% to 2.7% slower at the same precision.
This PR does not change verification, add `draft_token_map` to EAGLE3/DFlash/DSpark (they already prune in the checkpoint), or support lm_heads quantized in the checkpoint (rejected at load, #60226). Dynamic rows need TP=1.
Tests ```bash pytest -q tests/model_executor/layers/test_draft_vocab.py # pass on CPU and GB10 pytest -q tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_draft_vocab.py # passed on GB10 ``` New tests: pruned-head id mapping, listed rows, dynamic rows (full rank with every row picked equals full-vocab drafting), FP8/NVFP4 rows, TP shards, and `LocalArgmaxMixin` without a draft vocabulary. EAGLE3 is unchanged: `compute_logits` is bit-identical to the old scatter on `AngelSlim/Qwen3-8B_eagle3`, and greedy outputs match main on 64/64 prompts at batch 1 and 8.
**Not a duplicate.** #24343 and #29334 (FR-Spec, static lists only) were closed unmerged. #59973 quantizes the full draft head; this cuts the rows read, and the two compose. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the code, tests and benchmark harness; I reviewed every changed line and ran the measurements above.

title: [Bug][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash: recent-context pools not guaranteed in kpool top-k selection (always_select_tail covers only the incomplete pool)
body:
### TL;DR

On GLM-5.3-Flash (kpool sparse indexer, ROCm aiter path), per-layer top-k selection frequently drops the most recent context pools at long prompt lengths — even with a correct block table. The config sets `always_select_tail=True`, but the only tail the selection machinery guarantees is the ≤3-token *incomplete* pool; complete recent pools compete in the top-k like everything else and can rank below the `index_topk=2048` cutoff. Tail-of-context retrieval then fails non-deterministically. Forcing the last 128 pools (512 tokens, 25% of the budget) into every layer's selection fixed all our failing lengths up to the full 256K context.

### Setup

GLM-5.3-Flash-AWQ-W4A16, vLLM `0.31.0.dev0+git73859fec` (Sep-28 pin), TP=2 (ray across 2× AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Strix Halo, gfx1151), aiter sparse MLA, `index_topk` 2048, `index_kpool` 4, `max_model_len` 262144. Probe: needle ("Paris") in the final line, a single neutral decoy ("Berlin") in the first line, forced tool-call response, lengths 12K–255K prompt tokens.

### Measured evidence

- With the block-table granularity bug (#58858, fix in #59412) corrected on our tree (gather-site table expansion), tail retrieval still failed non-deterministically: ~12K ≈50/50, 54K ≈50/50, 75K FAIL, 105K FAIL (multiple runs each).
- Instrumenting the selection (per-layer, last query row of the failing chunk): the last token is always selected (the forced incomplete pool), but coverage of the last 48 positions varies per layer — e.g. **2, 6, 22, 30, 34, 42 of 48** across the 11–12 sparse layers. The answer flips only when enough layers see the needle, which explains the run-to-run flips.
- Forcing the most recent **128 pools (512 tokens = 25% of the 2048-token budget)** into every layer's selection at both the prefill and decode call sites fixed it end-to-end: 12K / 54K / 75K / 95K / 105K PASS (deterministic re-runs), and with the same setting 146K / 204K / 255K also PASS, plus an adversarial case (needle buried under a ×1000 repeated decoy). No measurable decode-throughput change; the trade-off is that the forced tail displaces ranked history within the fixed `index_topk` width.

### Suggested fix

Honor `always_select_tail` with a configurable recent-window guarantee: overwrite the lowest-ranked columns of each row's pool selection with the row's most recent visible pools (we used 128) inside the same `index_topk` budget. Our implementation is ~20 lines in `vllm/models/glm5next/amd/sparse_indexer.py` at the prefill + decode selection sites (`_force_recent_tail_pools`): <https://github.com/davidcanar/vllm-strix-halo> (`container/patches/vsh-idx-force-tail-sparse_indexer.py`).

### Relation to other work

- #58858 / #59412 (block-table granularity) is a distinct, deterministic mapping bug — both fixes are needed for long-context reliability.
- The paged kpool tail cache work on main (#57534, #56059) covers the in-progress (incomplete) pool at decode; as far as we can tell it does not guarantee recent *complete* pools in the selection. If this is being addressed elsewhere, feel free to close.

title: [Bug fix]: Fix streaming reasoning detokenization for DeepSeek R1 (by…
body:
Root Cause
DeepSeek R1 uses a byte-level BPE tokenizer. vLLM's incremental detokenizer emits text token-by-token  each token may decode to a single UTF-8 byte. The raw delta_text fed to extract_reasoning_streaming was being streamed directly to the client. For CJK or any non-ASCII content, this produces corrupted glyphs like "Ċ", "åĹ¯" (individual bytes, not assembled UTF-8).

Fix (deepseek_r1_reasoning_parser.py)
_decode_ids() — Re-decodes a list of token IDs via tokenizer.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=True), which assembles multi-byte UTF-8 sequences correctly across token boundaries.
_reasoning_token_ids() — Extracts only the token IDs inside the <think>…</think> span from the cumulative current_token_ids.
extract_reasoning_streaming() — On every streaming step, re-decodes the full reasoning span so far, then slices off only the fresh suffix (tracked via _prev_reasoning_decoded_len) to return as the delta. This is O(n) per step but correct the same approach used by other vLLM parsers for byte-level BPE models.
Content after </think> -Still uses delta_text directly (no corruption there since it's already in the regular content path).
