title: [Bugfix][Quark] Pass grouped-routing arguments to OCP MX monolithic kernels
body:
## Purpose

`QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod.apply_monolithic` does not forward `num_expert_group`, `topk_group`, `e_score_correction_bias` or `routed_scaling_factor` to the monolithic kernel, so the kernel falls back to their defaults.

Quark OCP MX picks its experts through `select_mxfp4_moe_backend`, the same path `Mxfp4MoEMethod` uses. `Mxfp4MoEMethod` has forwarded these four arguments since #50000; the Quark copy, added earlier in #38774, was never updated.

**Who is affected.** The bug needs three things at once:

1. A Quark **weight-only MXFP4 (`w_mxfp4`, W4A16)** checkpoint.
2. DeepSeek-V3/V4-style routing (grouped top-k and/or a correction bias with a scaling factor).
3. A **monolithic** MXFP4 kernel. On SM100, the BF16-activation priority list selects `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16` (`TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsMonolithic`, which supports `DeepSeekV3` routing) by default. On ROCm, `AiterW4A16ExpertsMonolithic` (`DeepSeekV3`/`DeepseekV4`) is used when requested explicitly.

In that setup the kernel routes with `n_group=0`, `topk_group=0` and no bias, and the scaling factor is `None` (TRT-LLM) or 1.0 (aiter).

The published Quark MXFP4 MoE checkpoints are W4A4: `amd/DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4`, `amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4`, `amd/Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4`, `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`, `amd/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MXFP4` and others. W4A4 resolves to the modular `AiterExperts` on ROCm and to emulation on CUDA, so routing happens in vLLM's router with every argument. As far as I can tell, no public checkpoint hits this today. This PR fixes a latent inconsistency before a W4A16 export does.

This PR forwards the four arguments exactly as `Mxfp4MoEMethod` does. Models without grouped routing pass `None` or the default values and are unaffected.

## Test Plan

- `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy).
- Code-path analysis above (`oracle/mxfp4.py` activation filtering and priority lists). There is no public W4A16 Quark checkpoint to run end to end.

## Test Result

`pre-commit` passes. Related: #59757 moves the monolithic kernel call into `FusedMoEMethodBase`, which also removes this inconsistency.

title: [Bug]: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen4Exp) fails to load on main after #57387: `ValueError: Invalid layer_type indexed_attention`
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev558+g0cbac6cd1` (`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-0cbac6cd1305f710e12193596b27488397bcb205`, main head `0cbac6cd`, 2026-10-02)
- transformers `5.18.0`, torch `2.13.0+cu130`
- NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120), TP=1
- Model: `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (resharded copy; `config.json` is the stock one: `model_type: qwen4_exp` / `qwen4_exp_text`, `layer_types` = `linear_attention` ×36 + `full_attention` ×12)
- Previous nightly `ac68c308` (2026-09-30) boots and serves the same checkpoint with the same command line.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Since #57387 ("[Model] Use upstream GLM-5.3 and Qwen4-Exp configs and processor", merged 2026-10-02 02:25Z) every Qwen3.8-Flash-Next boot dies in model construction, before weight loading:

```
(EngineCore pid=391) ERROR [core.py:1436] EngineCore failed to start.
  ...
  File ".../vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/model.py", in <lambda>
    return Qwen4ExpDecoderLayer(
  File ".../vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/model.py", line 231, in __init__
    raise ValueError(f"Invalid layer_type {layer_type}")
ValueError: Invalid layer_type indexed_attention
```

Deterministic: 3 crashes in 2 minutes under `restart: always`, same traceback every time.

**Root cause** — the two halves of #57387 disagree on the layer-type name:

1. vLLM now instantiates the upstream config class. `transformers/models/qwen4_exp/configuration_qwen4_exp.py` (5.18.0) normalizes the checkpoint's `full_attention` entries to `indexed_attention`:

```python
# configuration_qwen4_exp.py:181-185
# The real checkpoint contains "full_attention" entries for layers that are actually using an indexer
elif "full_attention" in self.layer_types:
    self.layer_types = [
        "indexed_attention" if layer == "full_attention" else layer for layer in self.layer_types
    ]
...
unsupported_layer_types = sorted(set(self.layer_types) - {"linear_attention", "indexed_attention"})
```

2. The model code still dispatches on the old vLLM-internal name `qwen_sparse_attention`, and nothing under `vllm/` knows `indexed_attention` (`grep -rn indexed_attention vllm/` → 0 hits in the installed package):

```python
# vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/model.py:205-231
if layer_type == "linear_attention":
    self.linear_attn = QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention(...)
elif layer_type == "qwen_sparse_attention":
    use_qsa = getattr(config, "indexer_n_heads", None) is not None
    ...
else:
    raise ValueError(f"Invalid layer_type {layer_type}")
```

Same literal in `nvidia/model.py:296,376`, `nvidia/mtp.py:213`, `amd/model.py:210,292,383`, `amd/mtp.py:223`.

So the model path is unreachable for every Qwen3.8-Flash-Next checkpoint on main; this is not a per-checkpoint config quirk (the stock `config.json` declares `full_attention`, which the upstream class rewrites).

**Suggested fix**: accept `indexed_attention` in the Qwen4Exp dispatchers (nvidia + amd `model.py`, both `mtp.py`), e.g. `elif layer_type in ("qwen_sparse_attention", "indexed_attention"):`, or normalize the upstream config's `layer_types` back to the internal name in one place when the config is loaded. A smoke test that constructs `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration` from the upstream config class would have caught this.

### Reproduction

```bash
docker run --rm --gpus all -v ~/models:/models vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-0cbac6cd1305f710e12193596b27488397bcb205 \
  /models/RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 --quantization modelopt --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' --trust-remote-code
```

(any Qwen3.8-Flash-Next checkpoint; the flags are irrelevant to the failure, which happens in `Qwen4ExpDecoderLayer.__init__`.)

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/) — no existing issue or PR mentions `indexed_attention` as of filing.

### 🐛 Describe the bug Output token throughput of DeepSeek-R1 (NVFP4) with data parallel attention and expert parallelism on 4x GB300 dropped by about 2% after [#48247](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48247) ("[Perf][ROCm] Add AITER custom AG/RS (DP only)", merge commit `ae48466cf3`). The PR targets ROCm, but it also changes shared code paths that CUDA uses. **Suspect change (hypothesis, not proven):** #48247 touches `cuda_communicator.py`, `parallel_state.py`, and `envs.py`. Two changes are visible in the diff: `graph_capture()` now also enters the DP group's graph capture, and uniform reduce-scatter sizes are normalized to `sizes=None`. The second change may route the CUDA reduce-scatter through the NCCL symmetric-memory path (the run below sets `VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=1`). That path could use a different reduction order. I did not profile this. I only know that the commit is the first slow one. **What the data shows** Benchmark: ISL 2000, OSL 1000, concurrency 2048, `avg_output_token_throughput`, DP4 + EP on 4x GB300. | Build | Throughput (tok/s) | |---|---| | Parent of #48247 (`0.28.1rc1.dev681+ge7edf17ce` baseline) | ~21,700 | | #48247 (`0.28.1rc1.dev683+gae48466cf`) | ~21,200 | | Before/after pair that differs only by #48247 | 21,681 vs 21,192 (-2.3%) | - A package-pin bisection over 95 commits narrowed the regression to #48247. - Pinning vLLM back to `0.28.1rc1.dev681` on the slow environment restores the throughput. The recipe and benchmark were unchanged. - The numbers above come from repeated nightly runs of the same recipe. I report them as measured. I did not rerun the pair for this issue. **Does it persist in a newer build?** A later nightly build, `0.30.1rc1.dev493+gac9126e58`, contains #48247 (it is ahead of `ae48466cf3` on `main`). It measures 20,774 tok/s at concurrency 2048. That run differs from the baseline in more than #48247, so the -4.2% against ~21,700 is not attributable to #48247 alone. I did not test the current `main` head (`8e58ac22aff6`, 72 commits after that build). I did not find a related fix in the titles of those 72 commits. **Reproduction** Server (public model, 4 GPUs): ```bash export VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=1 export NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1 export NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 export VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=1 vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-0528-NVFP4-v2 \ --served-model-name deepseek-r1-671b \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --dtype auto --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 \ --enable-expert-parallel --async-scheduling \ --max-num-seqs 1024 --max-model-len 10240 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --api-server-count 20 --stream-interval 20 \ --compilation_config.max_cudagraph_capture_size 2048 \ --compilation_config.cudagraph_mode FULL_DECODE_ONLY \ --compilation_config.pass_config.fuse_allreduce_rms true \ --compilation_config.pass_config.fuse_attn_quant true \ --compilation_config.custom_ops+=+quant_fp8,+rms_norm \ --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm ``` Client ([aiperf](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aiperf)): ```bash aiperf profile --url localhost:8000 --model deepseek-r1-671b \ --tokenizer nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-0528-NVFP4-v2 \ --endpoint-type completions --streaming --ui simple \ --extra-inputs min_tokens:1000 --extra-inputs max_tokens:1000 --extra-inputs ignore_eos:true \ --concurrency 2048 \ --synthetic-input-tokens-mean 2000 --synthetic-input-tokens-stddev 0 \ --output-tokens-mean 1000 --output-tokens-stddev 0 \ --request-count 10240 --warmup-request-count 1 ``` Compare `Output Token Throughput` between a build at `e7edf17ce` (or any commit before `ae48466cf3`) and a build at `ae48466cf3` or later. **Expected:** throughput at `ae48466cf3` matches its parent (~21.7k tok/s). **Actual:** throughput is ~2% lower (~21.2k tok/s). **What I did not verify** - I did not test with `VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=0`. **Related:** [#59189](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59189) reports a crash in the NCCL symmetric reduce-scatter on GB200 after the same PR. That is a different symptom, but it may share a cause. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions. title: [MOE][Quantization] Extend correctness test of `AITER_MXFP4_BF16` MOE backend and temporarily fix correctness issues with Swiglu + no bias code path
body:
## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

This PR adds correctness test for `AITER_MXFP4_BF16` MOE backend without bias in `tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py` and bypasses two uncovered AITER bugs until AITER fixes are merged, released, and the AITER version is bumped in vLLM, with workarounds.

These bugs were uncovered using `AITER_MXFP4_BF16` on a real internal model.

## Claims

This PR implements these two temporary fixes for numerical correctness:

- Use `GateMode.SEPARATED` in this case where `INTERLEAVED` is numerically wrong, fixing wrong outputs of `AITER_MXFP4_BF16` for bias-free SwiGLU (`SWIGLUOAI` / `SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE`).
- Fix `GateMode.SEPARATED` numerically wrong case for certain `model_dim` dimensions (non-multiple of 512) by extending `mxfp4_round_up_hidden_size_and_intermediate_size`, fixing wrong outputs on that path when the **hidden size is not a multiple of 512 (e.g. 256, 768)**

These two bugs arise with bias-free SwiGLU MXFP4 models (e.g. [amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4](https://huggingface.co/amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4)) served with `AITER_MXFP4_BF16` MOE backend and have fixes submitted to AITER:

- https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6022
- https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6086

`test_rocm_mxfp4_moe_oracle` is now parametrized over `has_bias`, hidden size, and intermediate size, and tests:

- the bias-free `AITER_MXFP4_BF16` path with strict thresholds (95% within `rtol=0.1`, 99.5% equal signs, was 70% within tolerance),
- an `EMULATION` reference case and an `AITER_MXFP4_BF16_SILU` case (SiLU on `AITER_MXFP4_BF16`, 90% within `rtol=0.5`, 98% equal signs), whose H=384 cases cover the hidden size alignment fix.

Other backends are skipped on bias-free weights and on the new shapes, and `AITER_MXFP4_BF16_SILU` with bias is skipped as AITER has no kernel for it (`TODO: ungate`).

**Note that on `main`, this test only covers weights with bias (GPT-OSS layout). The bias-free path was untested and fails for every shape (see below).**

## Validation

On MI350:

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py -k "(test_rocm_mxfp4_moe_oracle and (EMULATION or AITER_MXFP4_BF16)) or rounds_up or preserves_native"
```

65 passed, 12 skipped. `AITER_MXFP4_BF16` vs. the dequantized reference (equal signs / within `rtol=0.1`), bias-free weights:

| Shape (E-M-H-I) | `main` | This PR without padding | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8-16-256-256 | 76.88% / 0.9% | 72.02% / 7.3% | 99.88% / 98.6% (H padded to 512) |
| 8-16-512-256 | 76.28% / 0.4% | 99.90% / 97.9% | 99.90% / 97.8% |
| 8-16-768-256 | 75.14% / 0.3% | 73.53% / 7.3% | 99.85% / 97.7% (H padded to 1024) |
| 8-16-1024-256 | 74.54% / 0.2% | 99.83% / 97.7% | 99.82% / 97.7% |
| 128-16-6144-768 | 72.86% / 0.1% | 99.77% / 96.6% | 99.77% / 96.6% |

On `main`, all shapes dispatch to AITER's interleaved path (ROCm/aiter#6022). Without padding, the separated path still fails when the hidden size is not a multiple of 512 (ROCm/aiter#6086).

Regarding the `hidden_size` / situ padding bug:

`AITER_MXFP4_BF16_SILU` cases of `test_rocm_mxfp4_moe_oracle` (equal signs / within `rtol=0.5`), hidden size aligned to 128 (as on `main` for `Mxfp4MoEMethod`) vs. 256 (this PR):

| Shape (E-M-H-I) | H aligned to 128 | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8-16-256-256 | 98.83% / 95.0% | 98.83% / 95.2% |
| 8-16-384-256 | 63.95% / 21.6% | 98.39% / 94.1% (H padded to 512) |
| 8-16-384-768 | 58.19% / 0.0% | 98.52% / 94.1% (H padded to 512) |
| 8-16-6144-768 | 98.49% / 94.3% | 98.49% / 94.3% |

All other `AITER_MXFP4_BF16_SILU` shapes (H=512/768/1024) are unchanged at 98.4-98.7% equal signs. A wider sweep also showed NaN outputs for H=640 with the 128 alignment.

## Details

**ROCm/aiter#6022.** With interleaved gate/up, AITER runs CK-Tile stage 1 with `split_k=1`. No `(Swiglu, HasBias=false, split_k=1)` dispatcher specialization is built, so the default one runs SiLU. vLLM now selects `GateMode.SEPARATED` for bias-free SwiGLU-OAI in `rocm_aiter_moe.py` and shuffles the weights to match in `convert_weight_to_mxfp4_moe_kernel_format`.

**ROCm/aiter#6086.** The separated path forces CK-Tile split-K >= 2 for stage 1. The host derives the loop count from K rounded to the 256-wide K tile, while the kernel splits K at 32 granularity without masking, so results are correct only when `K % (split_k * 256) == 0`. AITER's `get_ksplit` only returns valid split counts but falls back to `split_k=2`, so the path is correct for hidden sizes that are multiples of 512. Two changes on the vLLM side:

- `mxfp4_round_up_hidden_size_and_intermediate_size` takes a new `has_bias` argument and pads the hidden size to a multiple of 512 for `AITER_MXFP4_BF16` + SwiGLU-OAI + `has_bias=False` only. The MoE runner already pads activations and slices outputs.
- `hidden_pad=0` is passed to AITER on this path. AITER uses it as `k_pad_zeros`, which skips the tail of the last K tile of every split-K partition, not only the last one, so passing the real `hidden_pad` drops real data (padding H=768 to 1024 with the real `hidden_pad` gives 68.20% sign agreement).

**Hidden size alignment for SiLU/SiTU.** #50582 and #51473 aligned both sizes to 128 for SiLU/SiTU on `AITER_MXFP4_BF16`, to keep Kimi-K3's and DeepSeek-V4's native intermediate sizes (e.g. 384 per partition at TP8). AITER's untuned FlyDSL fallback uses `tile_k=256` for stage 1, whose K is the hidden size, while stage 2 picks `tile_k=128` for intermediate sizes that are not 256-aligned. Hidden sizes that are odd multiples of 128 therefore read past K in stage 1. This was not visible before because only `Mxfp4MoEMethod` forwarded `activation`, and Kimi-K3/DeepSeek-V4 have H=7168.

title: [Performance]: Nemotron-3.5-Lightning NVFP4 decode ~16% slower on DGX Spark (GB10/SM121) since v0.29.0
body:
### Report of performance regression

Single-request decode of `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4` on DGX Spark (GB10, SM121) is **~16% slower from v0.29.0 onward** without speculative decoding, and ~8% slower with DSpark. v0.30.0 and current nightly do not recover it.

Same host, same command line, same weights, official images run back to back; only the image tag changes.

**Without speculative decoding** (decode tok/s, 1 request, 512 generated tokens, median of 5):

| image | greedy | temp 0.6 |
|---|---|---|
| v0.28.0 | **67.9** (67.7–68.0) | 67.1 |
| v0.29.0 | **57.2** (57.1–57.5) | 56.9 |

**With DSpark** (`num_speculative_tokens=3`), greedy, median of 5:

| image | decode tok/s | draft acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| v0.26.1rc1.dev994+gd626108b1 | 102.7 | 56% |
| v0.27.1 | 98.1 | 52% |
| v0.28.0 | **100.7** | 56% |
| v0.29.0 | **92.8** | 54% |
| v0.30.0 | 93.2 | 57% |
| v0.30.1rc1.dev558+g0cbac6cd1 (nightly) | 95.1 | 58% |

Draft acceptance is unchanged, so the drafter is not the cause; the per-step cost of the target went up.

**What I ruled out**

- **Model Runner V2**: v0.28.0 with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` gives 101.0 tok/s (DSpark, greedy), the same as default v0.28.0. (V1 cannot be tested on v0.29+: "Model Runner V1 does not support: dspark speculative decoding".)
- **Mamba SSU backend**: with `--mamba-backend=triton` instead of `flashinfer` the gap remains (DSpark, greedy: v0.28.0 102.7 → v0.29.0 95.2).
- **CUDA graphs**: both versions capture the same graphs (35 PIECEWISE, 17 FULL, 17 dspark FULL).
- **torch / CUDA / triton**: identical in both images (torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, triton 3.7.1).

What does differ between the two images: FlashInfer 0.6.16.post3 → 0.6.18 (#54313), fastsafetensors 0.3.3 → 0.4.0, and vLLM itself. Both versions select the same kernels in the log: `MARLIN` NvFp4 MoE backend, `MarlinNvFp4LinearKernel`, `FlashInferFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`, `FLASH_ATTN` for the target. Possibly related, not verified: #54048 (cuBLAS out_dtype router GEMM on all archs including GB10) and #54427 (weight-only NVFP4 routed through W4A16), both in v0.29.0. #58624 is a different SM12x decode regression (DeepGEMM MoE); this model uses Marlin for the MoE.

### Command (without speculative decoding)

```bash
docker run --gpus all --shm-size 8g -p 8803:8000 \
  -v $HF_CACHE:/root/.cache/huggingface vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0 \
  --model=nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4 \
  --served-model-name=Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B \
  --tensor-parallel-size=1 --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization=0.7 --max-model-len=262144 \
  --max-num-seqs=32 --max-num-batched-tokens=8192 \
  --kv-cache-dtype=bfloat16 --moe-backend=marlin \
  --mamba-backend=flashinfer --mamba-cache-mode=align \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --enable-prefix-caching \
  --load-format=fastsafetensors \
  --override-generation-config='{"temperature":0.6,"top_p":0.8,"top_k":20}' \
  --reasoning-parser=nemotron_v3 --tool-call-parser=qwen3_coder --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

For the DSpark numbers, add:
`--speculative-config='{"model":"nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`

### Measurement

Streaming `/v1/chat/completions`, `max_tokens=512`, a fresh UUID at the start of each prompt (no prefix-cache hits), one warmup request discarded. Decode rate = (completion_tokens − 1) / (time of last delta − time of first delta), counting both `content` and `reasoning` deltas. Draft acceptance from the `vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total` / `vllm:spec_decode_num_draft_tokens_total` deltas on `/metrics`.

### Environment

- NVIDIA DGX Spark, GB10 (SM121), 128 GB unified memory, driver 580.178.04
- Ubuntu 24.04.5, kernel 7.0.0-1019-nvidia, Docker 29.6.2
- `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0` (`sha256:61fc8a896b0a…`) vs `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0` (`sha256:c29147676055…`), linux/arm64

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Quantize the activation inside the MXFP8 block32 GEMM at small M
body:
## Overview

On ROCm, every MXFP8 linear with 32x32 block scales (all DeepSeek V4.1 attention and shared-expert linears) ran `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` and then the block32 GEMM from [#58510](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58510), which is two launches per linear. At decode sizes the GEMM now quantizes the bf16 activation in registers, bit-identically, so each linear is one launch. That removes about 210 graph nodes per DSv4.1 decode step at TP4. No existing PR does this; see Details for [#56674](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56674) and [#57857](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57857), which touch the same activations.

## Claims

- At 1–8 tokens, the DSv4.1 block32 linears are 1.14× to 1.61× faster per call on MI355X. Some shapes keep gaining up to 64 tokens. Above each shape's tuned limit (8 to 64 tokens), routing falls back to the old two-launch path and timing is unchanged.
- Activation quantization is bit-identical to `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize`. The only numeric change is accumulation order, where the small-M tile config differs from the existing table.



## Validation

### Kernel

MI355X, HIP graph of 64 calls per replay, best of 3, with enough weight copies to keep the 256 MB LLC cold. The comparison is `rocm_mxfp8_block32_linear` (new) against `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` + `rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm` (old), each with its tuned config. Values are speedup, new over old:


| linear (N, K)                   | M=1   | 2     | 4     | 8     | 16    | 32    | 64    | 128   | 512   | 4096  |
| ------------------------------- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| shared gate_up TP4 (1152, 5120) | 1.38× | 1.33× | 1.34× | 1.35× | 1.31× | 1.00× | 1.00× | 1.00× | 1.00× | 1.00× |
| wq_a|wkv (1792, 5120)           | 1.16× | 1.16× | 1.16× | 1.14× | 1.20× | 0.99× | 0.99× | 1.00× | 1.00× | 1.01× |
| indexer wq_b (4096, 1280)       | 1.50× | 1.47× | 1.48× | 1.37× | 1.24× | 1.09× | 1.00× | 1.00× | 1.00× | 1.00× |
| shared down TP4 (5120, 576)     | 1.61× | 1.60× | 1.61× | 1.58× | 1.38× | 1.32× | 1.14× | 1.00× | 1.00× | 1.00× |
| wo_b TP4 (5120, 2048)           | 1.46× | 1.46× | 1.45× | 1.27× | 1.00× | 1.00× | 1.00× | 1.00× | 1.00× | 1.00× |
| wq_b TP4 (8192, 1280)           | 1.41× | 1.41× | 1.41× | 1.34× | 1.19× | 1.00× | 1.00× | 1.00× | 0.99× | 1.00× |


In absolute terms that is, for example, 4.70 → 2.95 µs for shared down TP4 at M=1 and 7.73 → 5.59 µs for shared gate_up TP4. The TP2 shapes gain 1.09× to 1.46× up to their tuned limits. Shapes outside the table use one default config up to M=4. On six untuned shapes (the TP8 V4.1 linears and two arbitrary shapes) it was 1.03× to 1.63× faster.

### End-to-end

> TODO: E2E sweep for main vs this PR.



### Accuracy

> TODO: GSM8K (5-shot, `lm_eval`) for main vs this PR.



### Tests

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py           # 122 passed
pytest tests/kernels/test_minimax_m3_amd_ops.py -k "mxfp8 or linear"   # 28 passed
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py -k "wo_a or mxfp8"  # 25 passed
```

All pass on MI355X. Two tests in `test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py` are new:

- `test_rocm_mxfp8_block32_quant_x_matches_separate_quant` asserts the in-kernel path equals quantize-then-GEMM exactly, using the config each block32 shape routes to at 1, 3, 8, 19 and 64 tokens. The input includes all-zero and large-magnitude blocks and a row stride other than K.
- `test_rocm_mxfp8_block32_quant_x_split_k` does the same for packed and tiled split-K configs, in-launch and with a second reduce launch, on the K = 576 tail shape.

The existing `apply_weights` accuracy tests now go through `rocm_mxfp8_block32_linear`, so they cover both the fused and the fallback routes. CI runs this file in `:amd: (MI355 DPX) Native Quantization Kernels`, which triggers on `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/`.

## Details

**Motivation.** A DSv4.1 decode profile on MI355X (TP4, 2 requests) showed about 1,335 graph nodes per step and host-side graph submission as the bottleneck, at about 8 µs per node. The MXFP8 quantization (`_kernel`) and the block32 GEMM (`_block32_packed_kernel`) each ran 210 times per step at about 5 µs, a third of all nodes.

**Kernel.** `_block32_tiled_kernel` and `_block32_packed_kernel` take a `QUANT_X` constexpr. When it is set, they load the bf16 tile and quantize it per 32 columns with `_quant_mxfp8`, using the same fp32 operations as `_mxfp8_quant_triton_kernel`:

- the amax is clamped to the smallest normal fp32;
- the E8M0 scale is `ceil(log2(amax / 448)) + 127`, clamped to [0, 254];
- values are multiplied by the reciprocal power of two, then cast to e4m3.

This makes the result bit-identical. The packed kernel's K panels start on 32-column boundaries, so each row's groups are exactly the activation's MX blocks. The kernels also take an activation row stride, so a sliced input doesn't need a copy.

**Routing.** `rocm_mxfp8_block32_linear` is an opaque custom op, like the existing GEMM op, because the choice depends on the token count. It takes the fused path when `_TUNED_QUANT_X` (or `_DEFAULT_QUANT_X` for untuned shapes) has a tier for M. Otherwise it quantizes separately and uses the existing `_TUNED` table. The pre-quantized `rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm` op is unchanged for callers that already hold MXFP8 activations.

**Tuning.** I swept packed and tiled configs at 1–64 tokens for each DSv4.1 TP2/TP4 shape, under the same HIP-graph, cold-LLC timing as `_TUNED`. Each shape stops at the largest M where the fused config beat the separate path by at least 5%. A separate table is needed because the in-kernel quantization only pays off with different configs. With the existing `_TUNED` configs, it lost on most shapes and token counts, by 0.22× to 0.99×:

- **Large tiles:** `fused_wqa_wkv`'s 16×1024 packed tile ran at 0.72× even at 1–8 tokens.
- **Tiled configs at 24–32 tokens:** `indexer_wq_b` dropped to 0.33×.
- **48 tokens and up:** every shape lost, falling to about 0.5× at 1024 tokens and 0.22× for `wq_b` at 8192. Every N-tile program re-quantizes the same activation rows, so the kernel becomes bound on vector ALU work.

With small packed tiles (4–8 rows, K tiles of 128–256), the per-32 reduce is cheap. GPU kernel time drops as well as the launch count: for example, 6.38 → 4.46 µs for shared down TP4 at M=1 in profiler time.

**Relation to #56674's prologue result.** #56674 reports that it tried quantizing in the GEMM prologue and rejected it at 0.28–0.89×, with the reshape+reduce adding about 26 µs to a 12 µs GEMM. That attempt predates the block32 GEMM ([#58510](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58510)) and targeted `_mxfp8_dot_scaled_linear` with its existing tiles. The 0.22× to 0.99× above, from this kernel with the existing `_TUNED` configs, reproduces that result. The difference here is small-M configs tuned for in-kernel quantization, plus routing that only takes the fused path where it measured faster.

**Complexity.** +210 / −7 lines in `rocm_block32_gemm.py`, of which about 95 are the tuned table, and +3 / −4 in `rocm_native.py`. No core components are touched, and no CPU/GPU synchronization is added (the op reads only shapes and strides on the host).

**Limitations.**

- Tuned on gfx950 (MI355X) only, like `_TUNED`.
- DeepSeek-V4 (not V4.1) also uses this kernel through the default tier, but was not run end to end.
- Bit-exactness relies on both Triton kernels compiling the same fp32 math. The new tests check this on every CI run.



### Existing PRs and interaction

I searched vllm-project/vllm PRs (open and closed) for MXFP8 / block32 / dot_scaled together with quant fusion and ROCm. No PR fuses the activation quantization into the block32 GEMM.

- [#56674](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56674) (open, draft) fuses RMSNorm into the MXFP8 quantization by pattern-matching `rms_norm` followed by `torch.ops.vllm.mxfp8_quantize` in the compiled graph. It rejected prologue quantization for the pre-block32 kernel; see Details for why this result differs. This PR moves the quantization inside the opaque `rocm_mxfp8_block32_linear` op, so for block32 linears #56674's pattern would no longer match at any M, prefill included.
  - At decode both PRs remove one launch per linear. This PR also covers linears that don't follow an RMSNorm, and it stays bit-identical to `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize`. #56674's AITER quantizer rounds a few blocks per thousand to a scale one power of two apart.
  - At prefill, #56674 would remove a launch that this PR doesn't.
  - If both are wanted, a follow-up could let the block32 linear accept a pre-quantized input above the fused threshold. Reviewer input welcome.
- [#57857](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57857) (open, needs rebase) lets the ROCm MXFP8 linear take a pre-quantized activation, so `wq_b` and `indexer.wq_b` can share one quantization. This is complementary. At decode, each GEMM now quantizes in-kernel at almost no cost. Above the fused threshold, sharing would still save a launch.
- [#58510](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58510) (merged) added the block32 GEMM and `_TUNED` that this PR extends.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Retire in-flight output state on load-failure recompute
body:
## Overview

Fixes #45138. When KV-load-failure recompute truncates a request's `num_computed_tokens` at the first invalid block, the scheduler now also retires the request's in-flight output state: output placeholders are zeroed, drafted spec tokens are cleared, and outputs still in flight from the invalid KV are marked stale so they drain and drop as they return instead of landing as valid tokens.

## Claims

- `_update_requests_with_invalid_blocks` retires in-flight output state for every affected request, using the same `drop_stale_output` / `num_stale_output_tokens` idiom as `_handle_stopped_request`: in-flight outputs from invalid KV are dropped on return, placeholders restart at zero, and spec drafts are rebound to empty.
- Stale placeholders no longer leak into the scheduling arithmetic after recompute. That leak is what inflated `num_new_tokens` and stranded requests in the running queue in #45138.
- The reset is a no-op for requests with nothing in flight (sync scheduling, or async loads still waiting for remote KV), so non-failure paths are untouched.

## Validation

New regression test `test_sync_recompute_retires_inflight_output_state` builds the failure state directly: a running request with one outstanding placeholder share beyond the current step's, drafted spec tokens, and an invalid block reported mid-prompt. It asserts the truncated frontier, zeroed placeholders, exactly one stale share still outstanding with drop mode on (this step's share drains in lockstep inside `update_from_output`), and that the draft list is rebound rather than mutated.

Commands and results (CPU, macOS, worktree at 592c6f3fbc):

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py -q
# 4 passed (3 pre-existing + 1 new)

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/ -q \
  --ignore=tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  --ignore=tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py
# 1710 passed, 10 failed, 40 skipped
# All 10 failures reproduce identically on pristine upstream/main
# (verified via git stash on this branch): test_hf3fs_connector (4),
# test_hisparse_connector (2), test_multi_connector (1),
# test_nixl_connector_hma (1), test_offloading_connector (2).
# They are environment issues on this machine, unrelated to this change.

ruff check / ruff format --check on both touched files: clean
```

The two ignored modules fail collection on this machine for missing `ray`, unrelated to this change. End-to-end repro would need a GPU deployment with a KV connector reporting block-level load failures; not available here, so validation is at the scheduler unit level, matching how the neighboring invalid-block tests cover this code.

## Details

Root cause: the recompute path rewinds `num_computed_tokens` but left the request's output-side state untouched. Under async scheduling a request can have placeholders and in-flight sampled outputs at the moment the failure surfaces; those outputs were sampled from KV that is now known-invalid, and the leftover placeholders kept counting into `num_new_tokens` projections, which is the stranding mechanism reported in #45138.

Why not the existing PRs:

- #45146 fixes the placeholder half of this on an older tree and has been inactive since June. It does not touch in-flight outputs or spec drafts.
- #49252 covers the `num_computed_tokens` truncation for sync + async loads and has been stalled since August; its substance is largely absorbed by the current `_update_requests_with_invalid_blocks` rewrite, and it also leaves output-side state alone.
- This PR supersedes my own earlier #45430 (closed), redone against current main using the stale-output machinery that landed since (`num_in_flight_tokens` / `num_stale_output_tokens` / `drop_stale_output`), which keeps the fix to nine lines in the scheduler by reusing the drain loop in `update_from_output`.

AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR (Kimi Code). The change was validated as described above.

title: [Bug]: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next AutoRound/INC checkpoint fails because PLE rejects INCConfig even though PLE is unquantized
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM: `v0.30.0`
- Container: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0`
- Model: `Intel/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AutoRound`
- GPUs: `2x NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB`
- Compute capability: `SM80 / (8, 0)`
- Tensor parallel size: `2`
- Expert parallel: enabled
- Model dtype: `bfloat16`
- Quantization detected by vLLM: `inc`
- Max model length in the failing deployment: `262144`

The same checkpoint works with the dedicated Qwen3.8 preview image:

```text
vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next
vLLM: 0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198
```


### 🐛 Describe the bug

`Intel/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AutoRound` fails during model initialization on stock vLLM `v0.30.0`.

The checkpoint uses AutoRound / INC quantization for the model body, but the Qwen3.8 PLE embedding is intentionally left unquantized.

vLLM passes the model-level `INCConfig` to `Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod.from_quant_config()`. The PLE implementation does not recognize `INCConfig`, so initialization fails before weights are loaded:

```text
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py", line 695, in __init__
    embedding_quant_method = Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod.from_quant_config(

File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py", line 187, in from_quant_config
    raise NotImplementedError(

NotImplementedError: Qwen4Exp PLE embedding does not support quantization config INCConfig
```

This happens on both TP workers.

The rest of the AutoRound path appears to initialize correctly before the failure. In particular, the checkpoint is recognized as INC and the expected W4A16 MoE backend is selected:

```text
Using 'MARLIN' WNA16 MoE backend.
```

### Reproduction

A minimal reproduction should be possible with the public Intel checkpoint:

```bash
vllm serve Intel/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AutoRound \
    --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
    --enable-expert-parallel
```

My production configuration additionally uses long context, prefix caching, chunked prefill and MTP, but the exception occurs during model construction before those features are relevant.

### Expected behavior

The model should load successfully.

For an AutoRound/INC checkpoint where the PLE embedding itself is not quantized, the PLE layer should use the unquantized PLE embedding implementation rather than rejecting the model-level `INCConfig`.

Conceptually, this case seems equivalent to:

```python
if isinstance(quant_config, INCConfig):
    # PLE is excluded from AutoRound quantization in this checkpoint.
    return Qwen4ExpPLEUnquantizedEmbeddingMethod()
```

The exact implementation should probably verify the per-layer/checkpoint quantization metadata rather than assuming that every INC checkpoint necessarily has an unquantized PLE.

### Why this seems to be a PLE quantization-dispatch issue

The checkpoint is a mixed layout:

- the main model uses AutoRound W4A16 / `INCConfig`;
- PLE is not quantized by the AutoRound recipe;
- nevertheless, PLE method selection receives the model-level `INCConfig`;
- `Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod.from_quant_config()` interprets that config as if it described the PLE table itself and rejects it.

There are similar mixed-quantization PLE issues for Qwen4Exp where the body quantization config does not directly describe the PLE representation, e.g. #54765 and #56272.

### Workaround tested

As a diagnostic workaround, I patched `Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod.from_quant_config()` so that `INCConfig` selects the unquantized PLE method.

With that change, the model gets past the original exception and proceeds to initialize:

```text
Resolved Engram configuration:
EngramConfig(cpu_offload=True, embedding_across_dp=False, dp_shared_memory=False)

Using 'MARLIN' WNA16 MoE backend.
```

So the INC W4A16/MARLIN path itself is not the source of this particular exception.

I would prefer an upstream fix that determines the PLE representation correctly from the checkpoint/layer metadata rather than relying on this local workaround.

### Additional context

The older dedicated image `vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next` successfully serves this exact checkpoint on the same 2x A100 system.

That image uses the older separate PLE offload worker implementation, so this appears to be a compatibility regression/coverage gap in the newer Qwen4Exp PLE/Engram implementation rather than an unsupported AutoRound checkpoint in general.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Overlap the mHC gate projection with attention and FFN
body:
## Overview

On ROCm, each DeepSeek V4.1 mHC seam ran the whole fused AITER kernel pair on the default stream before the next sublayer could start. That pair is the post block, the gate projection, Sinkhorn, and the collapse with RMSNorm. This PR moves the gate projection onto a side stream inside FULL HIP graphs, so it overlaps with the following attention or FFN. The default stream now only runs the post block plus the RMSNorm'd collapse, in one new Triton kernel. This is the ROCm counterpart of the CUDA overlap in [#57603](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57603).

## Claims

- Output throughput is up 0.3% to 5.4% end to end on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, EP, FP8 KV, MI355X, at every concurrency from 1 to 128 at TP2, TP4 and TP8.
- The new residual and the gates (post, comb, next pre) are bit-identical to the fused AITER seam. The layer input is bit-identical up to 16 tokens and within one bf16 ulp above that.
- No change outside FULL-graph decode with at most 128 tokens. Prefill, piecewise graphs, eager mode, CUDA and DSpark draft layers keep the current path.



## Validation



### Kernel

MI355X, HIP-graph replay time per seam. "Fused" is `mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rms_norm_aiter` (main + reduce kernels). "Input kernel" is the new `mhc_post_collapse_rms_norm_triton`, the only part left on the default stream. "Gates" is the side-stream work.


| tokens | fused (µs) | input kernel (µs) | gates on side stream (µs) |
| ------ | ---------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- |
| 1      | 9.91       | 4.15              | 8.48                      |
| 4      | 10.24      | 4.26              | 9.01                      |
| 16     | 10.41      | 4.37              | 9.17                      |


The default-stream seam goes from about 10 µs to about 4.3 µs. That is roughly 0.5 ms per decode step across the 86 seams that take the overlap (43 layers × 2).

### End-to-end

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X, TP4, EP, FP8 KV, 12 sweep points. Mean TPOT in ms and output throughput in tok/s:


| input / output | concurrency | TPOT main | TPOT this PR | Δ     | tok/s main | tok/s this PR | Δ     |
| -------------- | ----------- | --------- | ------------ | ----- | ---------- | ------------- | ----- |
| 8192 / 1024    | 4           | 8.08      | 7.70         | -4.8% | 466.71     | 488.68        | +4.7% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 8           | 9.80      | 9.46         | -3.5% | 773.17     | 799.60        | +3.4% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 16          | 11.84     | 11.50        | -2.9% | 1262.50    | 1300.66       | +3.0% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 32          | 16.12     | 15.69        | -2.7% | 1786.03    | 1833.31       | +2.6% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 64          | 23.14     | 22.90        | -1.1% | 2516.82    | 2539.97       | +0.9% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 128         | 35.31     | 34.51        | -2.3% | 3161.18    | 3225.27       | +2.0% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 256         | 58.27     | 57.96        | -0.5% | 3795.31    | 3815.37       | +0.5% |
| 60000 / 600    | 4           | 13.80     | 13.47        | -2.4% | 227.83     | 233.61        | +2.5% |
| 60000 / 600    | 16          | 39.88     | 39.98        | +0.2% | 337.21     | 338.35        | +0.3% |
| 60000 / 600    | 64          | 138.79    | 136.17       | -1.9% | 388.60     | 394.46        | +1.5% |
| 128000 / 1024  | 4           | 16.85     | 16.53        | -1.9% | 185.12     | 187.66        | +1.4% |
| 128000 / 1024  | 16          | 54.22     | 53.73        | -0.9% | 247.55     | 250.08        | +1.0% |


The mean is -2.05% TPOT and +2.00% throughput. Throughput is higher at all 12 points and TPOT lower at 11; the exception is 60000 / 600 at concurrency 16, at +0.2%. Median TPOT gives -2.14%, also 11 of 12, so the whole distribution moves rather than a tail.

### Accuracy

GSM8K, 5-shot, `lm_eval` `local-completions`, full test split, `num_concurrent=32`:


| run     | flexible-extract | strict-match    |
| ------- | ---------------- | --------------- |
| default | 0.9227 ± 0.0074  | 0.9219 ± 0.0074 |
| this PR | 0.9234 ± 0.0073  | 0.9234 ± 0.0073 |


### Tests

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py -k rocm
```

All pass on MI355X. `test_deepseek_v41_rocm_mhc_overlap_matches_fused_seam` is new and runs at 1, 2, 7, 16, 64 and 128 tokens. After joining the side stream, it compares every output with `MHCPreDelayedOp.forward_hip` (the fused AITER seam):

- the residual and gates must match exactly;
- the layer input must match within one bf16 ulp, and it must already be usable before the join;
- the same checks are repeated across three HIP-graph replays with changing inputs.

CI runs it in `:amd: (MI355) mHC Kernels`.

## Details

**Why the split is exact.** In AITER's fused seam (`_mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rmsnorm_main_kernel`), the post-mix is rounded to bf16 once, and that rounded `R'` feeds the projection, the square sums and the collapse. This PR splits the seam in two:

- The new kernel recomputes `R'` with the same expression order, so it is bit-identical, then collapses it with the carried pre-mix and applies the RMSNorm.
- The side stream runs AITER's own fused kernel on `R'` without the post (`HAS_POST=False`). Its gates are therefore the same numbers.

Only the RMSNorm's row sum differs. The new kernel holds a token's row in registers and sums it in one pass, while AITER reduces it across split-K programs, so the order changes. That is exact at decode sizes, and within one ulp otherwise.

**Gating.** The overlap runs only inside FULL HIP-graph capture, not in piecewise graphs, with `0 < tokens <= MHC_OVERLAP_MAX_TOKENS` (128). Fork and join then become graph edges; `DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention` keeps its aux streams to captured graphs for the same reason. It also requires AITER's fused delayed seam (`HAS_AITER_MHC_FUSED_POST_PRE_DELAYED_RMS_NORM`), `hc_mult == 4`, and no ubatching. The 128-token limit is the largest tested point. The gain was still positive there but shrinking (above), and the overlap was not measured beyond it, although FULL graphs go up to 512 tokens.

**Seams.** The overlap applies to every FFN seam and to the attention seam of every layer after the first. Layer 0's broadcast seam and Engram seams already take a different path and keep it. The gate stream is joined after attention and at the end of each layer, which is where the gates are next read. The stream is separate from the attention aux streams, as on CUDA. `record_stream` keeps the side stream's inputs and the main stream's gate outputs alive across the fork. No host synchronization is added.

**Limitations.**

- **Tuning:** the token limit was tuned on MI355X TP2, TP4 and TP8.



### Existing PRs

I searched vllm-project/vllm PRs (open and closed) for mHC overlap, coefficient and side-stream work on ROCm. None moves the mHC seam off the default stream on ROCm.

- [#57603](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57603) (merged) is the CUDA version. It needs SM100 and DeepGEMM's `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`, and stops at 16 tokens. This PR follows its structure, gating and join points.
- [#56853](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56853) (merged) adds an attention-side aux stream for DeepSeek-V4 HCA layers. It keeps the mHC seam serial on the default stream, which is what this PR changes.
- [#58655](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58655) (merged) introduced the fused AITER delayed seam that this PR splits.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Pass no MoE padding to AITER on the a4w4 path
body:
AITER drops its tuned inline-sort MXMOE configs whenever hidden_pad or intermediate_pad is set, every call up to 512 tokens ran heuristic kernels. 

Details to be added

A4W4 MoE is still behind VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4=1, as it is already designed that way.

## Details

### Performance after changes
ISL=8K, OSL=1K, TP4, NP=10*C, no spec decoding

title: [Bug]: HiSparse cache-handle test passes a plain SparseMLAIndexGroup; follower path relies on an attribute only the leader writes
body:
### Your current environment

Found while working on #55485 (mypy for `tests/v1/worker`), where @hickeyma asked for an issue rather than a `cast` over it. Reproduced on `main` (`10f6ab01a`), CPU, torch 2.13.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py::test_hisparse_cache_handles_join_index_groups_during_construction` passes a plain `SparseMLAIndexGroup` to `vllm.v1.hisparse.runtime.create_hisparse_cache_handle`, whose parameter is typed `index_group: HiSparseMLAIndexGroup | None`. It only works because the leader call adds a missing attribute onto the plain group as a side effect.

- The test builds its groups with `SparseMLAIndexGroupBuilder(...).register_layer(is_leader)` and no `vllm_config`. `register_layer` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/index_group.py`, ~L362) only creates a `HiSparseMLAIndexGroup` when `vllm_config.attention_config.hisparse_config is not None`. Otherwise it returns a plain `SparseMLAIndexGroup`.
- In `create_hisparse_cache_handle` (`vllm/v1/hisparse/runtime.py`):
  - **Follower** calls read `index_group.hisparse_group` (~L1301). That field is declared only on `HiSparseMLAIndexGroup` (`hisparse_group: Any | None = None`).
  - **Leader** calls instead assign `index_group.hisparse_group = runtime.index_group` (~L1319). On the plain, non-slots dataclass, this silently creates a new instance attribute.

The test's follower lookups therefore succeed only because a leader ran first and wrote the field. The test never builds the `HiSparseMLAIndexGroup` that production uses (`HiSparseMLAIndexGroup.register_layer` passes `index_group=self`). If `SparseMLAIndexGroup` ever becomes `@dataclass(slots=True)`, the leader's write starts raising instead.

**Repro** (uses the test's own monkeypatches, runs on CPU):

```python
import torch
from types import SimpleNamespace
import vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.index_group as ig
import vllm.v1.hisparse.runtime as rt

rt._has_hisparse_ops = lambda: True
rt.ResolvedHiSparseConfig.from_vllm_config = classmethod(
    lambda cls, c, k: rt.ResolvedHiSparseConfig(top_k=4, device_buffer_size=8, max_union_rows=8))
rt._create_shared_topk_state = lambda *a: object()
ig._create_side_stream = lambda _: object()
ig._create_event = lambda: object()
config = SimpleNamespace(
    scheduler_config=SimpleNamespace(max_num_seqs=2, max_num_batched_tokens=2, async_scheduling=False),
    speculative_config=None, kv_transfer_config=None)

group, _ = ig.SparseMLAIndexGroupBuilder(torch.empty((2, 4), dtype=torch.int32)).register_layer(False)
rt.create_hisparse_cache_handle(config, 4, is_index_group_leader=False, row_width=8,
                                kv_dtype=torch.float32, index_group=group, device="cpu")
```

```
  File "vllm/v1/hisparse/runtime.py", line 1301, in create_hisparse_cache_handle
    else index_group.hisparse_group
AttributeError: 'SparseMLAIndexGroup' object has no attribute 'hisparse_group'
```

With `arg-type` enabled, mypy also flags the call: `Argument "index_group" to "create_hisparse_cache_handle" has incompatible type "SparseMLAIndexGroup"; expected "HiSparseMLAIndexGroup | None"`. `pyproject.toml` disables `arg-type` for `tests.*`, so this is invisible today.

**Possible fixes** (any one):
1. Have the test build real `HiSparseMLAIndexGroup`s, either by giving the builder a config with `attention_config.hisparse_config` set or by constructing them directly.
2. Narrow with `isinstance(index_group, HiSparseMLAIndexGroup)` in `create_hisparse_cache_handle` before touching `hisparse_group`.
3. Move `hisparse_group` onto `SparseMLAIndexGroup` if plain groups are meant to be accepted.

Happy to send a PR for whichever the HiSparse owners prefer.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix][Prefix caching] Fix inconsistent hybrid Mamba prefix cache boundaries and incomplete tail saves
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes various undesirable prefix cache miss issues for hybrid full-attention + Mamba models, including inconsistent prefix-cache boundaries and incomplete Mooncake tail saves.

Many changes in this PR are referenced from #56615 and #57180. Given prefix caching for hybrid mamba is quite involved, the PR aims to take a more thorough approach to address the problems.

## Problems addressed

Setup: FlashKDA prefill with DSpark/EAGLE, PMU/hash unit 128, GPU attention and Mamba block size 896, and scheduler LCM / Mooncake attention block size 7,168 tokens.

### 1. Incomplete external tail (Mooncake)

**Sequence:** 7,449-token prompt → GPU cache reset → resend the same prompt.

The replay on main recorded:

```text
Cached GPU Mamba state:          7,296
Cached GPU attention proof:      7,424
Cached Mooncake Mamba state:     7,296
Cached Mooncake attention tail:  7,296
GPU local hit before reset:      7,296
Mooncake hit after reset:            0
```

Normal Mooncake saves reach the LCM boundary at 7,168. Its separate partial-tail save registers full-attention KV under the Mamba replay boundary, 7,296. EAGLE requires attention proof through 7,424, so the external lookup returns a complete miss despite retaining the Mamba state.

### 2. Attention lookup capped below available EAGLE proof

**Sequence:** 7,040-token prompt → resend the same prompt, without GPU reset.

The replay on main recorded:

```text
Cached Mamba state:          6,784
Cached attention proof:     7,040
Current local hit:              0
Expected usable hit:         6,784
```

The Mamba checkpoint is derived from `P - 1` and EAGLE's drop; attention caches through `P`. Both are available, but lookup caps the attention proof scan at **7,039 tokens** (`max_cache_hit_length = P - 1`). The largest hash boundary within that limit is 6,912, so the cached attention entry at 7,040 is never inspected and the reusable prefix is missed.

### 3. Mamba checkpoint applies the resend limit twice with EAGLE

**Sequence:** 7,296-token prompt → resend the same prompt, without GPU reset.

Boundary calculation for the existing implementation (illustrative, not a measured replay):

```text
Cached Mamba state:        7,040
Cached attention proof:   7,296
Current hit upper bound:  7,040
Expected usable hit:      7,168
```

The Mamba checkpoint calculation rounds down from `P - 1`, then subtracts another 128 tokens for EAGLE, while attention caches through `P`. This limits the hit to 7,040 tokens, although the cached attention proof at 7,296 supports a 7,168-token hit after EAGLE's drop. Since both the `P - 1` limit and EAGLE's drop leave tokens to recompute on resend, this effectively applies the resend cap twice.

## Proposed design

1. **Use one resend-safe Mamba replay checkpoint.** For prompt length `P` and checkpoint unit `U`:

   ```text
   Without EAGLE: floor((P - 1) / U) × U
   With EAGLE:    max(floor(P / U) × U - U, 0)
   ```

   Without EAGLE, cap at `P - 1` so an exact resend can reuse the checkpoint while leaving at least one token to recompute. With EAGLE, the block drop already leaves tokens to recompute, so no additional `P - 1` cap is needed.

   Prompt extension could use a later checkpoint without the `P - 1` cap. However, current KDA prefill backends support only one intermediate checkpoint without extra prefill splits. We therefore use the resend-safe boundary as the common Mamba replay checkpoint for both resend and extension.

2. **Save the matching attention KV in Mooncake.**

   Save the full-attention KV needed to reuse the Mamba checkpoint, including the extra proof required by EAGLE. Keep the source blocks referenced until the asynchronous save completes.

3. **Allow lookup to inspect proof beyond the hit limit.**

   Bound the attention proof scan by the available hashes, not the final hit limit. For a 7,296-token prompt, confirming a 7,168-token hit requires inspecting the attention hash at 7,296—beyond the `prompt_len - 1` limit of 7,295. This is safe because we only inspect the proof; after EAGLE's drop, the returned hit is 7,168 and remains within the limit.

## E2E agentic benchmark results

Kimi K3, 1P1D DCP8 + DCP8, DSpark k4, PMU 128.

| Concurrency | Main TPS/GPU | PR TPS/GPU | Main prefix hit rate | PR prefix hit rate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64 | 13,762 | 13,963 | 95.763% | 96.009% |
| 80 | 15,163 | 15,253 | 94.817% | 95.080% |
| 96 | 15,973 | 16,669 | 94.413% | 95.031% |
| 112 | 13,976 | 15,668 | 92.432% | 94.165% |
| 128 | 11,371 | 15,754 | 90.466% | 94.041% |

## Implementation review order

Implementation files only, in suggested review order:

1. `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`  
   Unifies the resend-safe Mamba checkpoint calculation, avoiding the redundant `P - 1` cap when EAGLE already drops a cache unit.

2. `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`  
   Centralizes partial-hash-hit eligibility so checkpoint generation, local caching, and Mooncake use consistent alignment rules.

3. `vllm/config/cache.py`  
   Adds resolved hash and Mamba checkpoint block sizes as runtime fields, excluded from the configuration hash.

4. `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` and `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`  
   Populates those sizes before checkpoint metadata is built, including during CUDA-graph memory profiling, using the actual cache layout and DCP configuration.

5. `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/checkpoint.py`  
   Makes the checkpoint builder use the resolved checkpoint unit, matching the scheduler and cache lookup granularity.

6. `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`  
   Aligns prefill splitting with the shared resend-safe checkpoint calculation while preserving support for checkpoints materialized within a prefill chunk.

7. `vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py`  
   Allows the existing partial-entry registration path to register physical-block-aligned checkpoints too.

8. `vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`  
   Aligns attention and Mamba tail registration with the resend-safe boundary. Prevents transient intermediate states from being published as reusable checkpoints, while preserving retained checkpoints and shared junctions.

9. `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py`  
   Allows EAGLE attention lookup to inspect the required proof beyond the final hit limit, bounded by available hashes.

The following paths are under `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/`:

10. `data.py`  
    Adds completion and tail-publication metadata, separating the original prompt length from the expanded prefill horizon after preemption. Introduces a shared helper for identifying companion attention blocks.

11. `coordinator.py`  
    Applies the same EAGLE proof-lookup rules to external caching and identifies the exact attention blocks needed to accompany the Mamba tail.

12. `scheduler.py`  
    Emits tail-only saves when the prompt completes and keeps their source blocks referenced through asynchronous storage, including request cleanup.

13. `worker.py`  
    Saves the Mamba tail together with its matching attention proof, including EAGLE's margin and gaps beyond normal saves. Handles proof publication even when no new Mamba offload accompanies the completion step.

---

title: [BugFix][DiffusionGemma][CPU] Copy async output snapshots instead of aliasing reused buffers
body:
## Overview

Fixes #59828

## Claims

With async scheduling, the V2 model runner snapshots each step's sampled tokens and counts with `async_copy_to_np()`. It reads them after the next step starts. On GPU, `.to("cpu")` copies into new memory. On CPU it returns the same tensor, and the snapshot aliases the sampler's buffers. DiffusionGemma reuses those buffers on every step, and the next step overwrites the snapshot before it is read.

This is latent on `main`. CPU forces sync scheduling, which reads each output before the next step runs. I found it while testing DiffusionGemma structured reads on CPU with async scheduling enabled, after https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59107. Every read returned a phantom first token, overwritten tokens and one logprob row too few.

### Changes in this PR

- `async_copy_to_np()` passes `copy=True`. A CPU snapshot now owns its memory. GPU behavior does not change. The device-to-host copy already allocates.
- Add a regression test to `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py`, next to the other V2 model runner tests, instead of a new file. It snapshots a CPU tensor, overwrites the tensor and checks that the snapshot keeps its values.

I checked the other snapshots in `AsyncOutput`. Logprobs, sampling masks and prompt logprobs also alias on CPU. They are safe because their producers allocate new tensors on every step. I left them as is.

No open issue or PR covers this. I searched for `async_copy_to_np`, CPU async aliasing and overwritten sampled tokens. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58082 edits the code next to `async_copy_to_np()` but does not change it.

I used Claude Code to help with this PR. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests below.

## Validation

Hardware: 22 vCPU Intel Xeon Platinum 8481C, Ubuntu 22.04, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu. vLLM built from source for CPU at e006d761a5, with the real `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it` checkpoint in BF16. Unit tests also on macOS (Apple Silicon).

**Unit tests:**

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py
```

**End to end:**

1. Sync path, the default on CPU. Run greedy generation with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` and a DiffusionGemma structured read (32-token canvas on a 64-token server). Run on `main`, with this PR, and on `main` again for the noise floor. Compare tokens, logprobs and throughput.
2. Async path. Enable async scheduling on CPU with a local change to `CpuPlatform.check_and_update_config()`. Send the same DiffusionGemma read 10 times with a batch of 1 and 10 times with a batch of 4. Compare each read with sync.

## Test Result

Before (`main`, async on CPU), the read's tokens are overwritten. The issue has the details and the `collect_env.py` output.

```text
sync   tokens[:8] [45518, 45518, 107, 148436, 148436, 236787, 11262, 1]   logprob rows 32
async  tokens[:8] [45518, 1, 1, 1, 1, 148436, 236787, 11262]              logprob rows 31
```

After:

- Unit tests: 90 passed. The new test fails on `main` with `assert [1, 1, 1, 1] == [0, 0, 0, 0]`.
- Async: 50/50 reads match sync, up from 0/50. No snapshot changes before it is read, even with the reader delayed by 50 ms.
- Sync: [layer 3 results: tokens and logprobs before and after for both models, throughput against the noise floor]

## Details

On CPU, .to("cpu") returns the same tensor, and with async scheduling the next step overwrites the sampled-token snapshot before it is read. That corrupted every DiffusionGemma read I tested (linked in the issue).

This PR copies in `async_copy_to_np()`, the one place sampler outputs cross the async boundary. GPU behavior does not change. CPU pays one small copy per step. main is unaffected today because CPU forces sync scheduling. Logprob snapshots still alias but stay safe because their producers allocate new tensors.

---

## Summary

- Bump `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]` from 4.7.1 to 4.8.0 in `requirements/cuda.txt`.
- No other pin changes are needed: `quack-kernels==0.6.5` requires `>=4.7`, `flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1` requires `>=4.7.0a0`, and the FA4 source pin (`tml-fa4` @ `75765e76`) is already the latest commit in that repo.
- `requirements/rubin-prerelease.txt` is unchanged (still `4.8.0.dev0`); the Rubin cleanup stays with #59288.

## Why

`tokenspeed-mla>=0.2.12` declares `nvidia-cutlass-dsl>=4.8.0` (added with SM107 support), so newer TokenSpeed MLA releases cannot be installed against the current pin. #59462 currently carries this bump alongside its backend change. Landing it on its own keeps the CuTe DSL upgrade reviewable, bisectable and revertible separately from feature work, consistent with previous CUTLASS DSL bumps (#54927, #51566, #42991).

## Relation to other PRs

#59288 also changes this pin as part of the Rubin base-image migration. This PR isolates only the CUTLASS DSL bump so that dependents such as #59462 do not have to wait on the Rubin build changes. Whichever lands second only needs a trivial rebase of the same line.

## Tests

uv pip compile requirements/cuda.txt --python-version 3.12 \
  --python-platform {x86_64,aarch64}-manylinux_2_28 \

The full Buildkite run on #59288, which uses the same 4.8.0 pin, passed the B200 kernels, v1 attention, inkling (FA4), FLA ops, DeepSeek-V4 kernels, quantized MoE and Kimi-K3 jobs. Results for this PR will come from CI once it is labeled `ready`.

Not applicable. This is a dependency-only compatibility upgrade with no serving-logic change.

title: [Bugfix][DeepEP] Close GIN barrier data-visibility race in vendored DeepEP (per-context signals + NVLink fence)
body:
## Summary

DeepEP `d4f41e4e` (the commit we pin in `docker/Dockerfile` / `tools/ep_kernels/install_python_libraries.sh`) has a data-visibility race in `gin_barrier_wo_local_sync`, the completion barrier of low-latency dispatch/combine over NCCL GIN (GDAKI):

- The barrier publishes completion with a **single context-0 signal**, while dispatch/combine data rides **contexts 1..N as RDMA puts** and, for same-node peers, **NVLink TMA stores** to LSA symmetric memory.
- Signals and puts on different QPs are not ordered at the receiving NIC (confirmed by NVIDIA in nccl#2302; NCCL's own `ncclGinBarrier` with `ncclGinAllContexts` exists for exactly this failure mode), and GIN signals are not ordered with NVLink stores from other threads (fixed upstream in deepseek-ai/DeepEP#715, not in `d4f41e4e`).
- The receiver's copy epilogue (PDL-launched) can therefore read **stale raw-buffer rows from the previous dispatch**: phantom/missing expert routes, double-assigned slots, unwritten `recv_x` rows, occasionally OOB slots — the latter surfacing as the `combine_impl` illegal-memory-access crashes seen in DP=8 direct-mode nightlies.

Root-cause evidence (pristine DeepEP, host-side audit, zero kernel instrumentation): internal repro `repros/pr57991-waldorf-20260928/.../count-discrepancy-audit-20261002/REPORT.md`.

## The patch

`tools/ep_kernels/patches/deepep-gin-barrier-data-visibility.patch` — one file (`deep_ep/include/deep_ep/common/comm.cuh`), two changes mirroring shipped upstream fixes:

1. **Per-context signals**: after the existing flush + grid sync, signal every peer on every GIN context (`ginContextCount × kNumRanks` signals) and wait on the per-(context, signal id) slots. A signal posted on context `c` is SQ-FIFO-ordered behind all WQEs previously reserved on context `c`, covering the RDMA data puts. Mirrors NCCL's `ncclGinBarrierSession` with `ncclGinAllContexts` (`nccl_device/impl/gin_barrier__funcs.h`).
2. **`fence.acq_rel.sys` for world-team barriers** before the barrier signal, so same-node peers' NVLink TMA stores are visible before the GIN signal is published. Mirrors upstream DeepEP #715 (11d1cab), which postdates our pinned commit.

Applied in `install_python_libraries.sh` after the DeepEP clone, guarded to the pinned commit `d4f41e4e` (skips on any other ref) and idempotent (grep guard). `docker/Dockerfile` copies the new `tools/ep_kernels/patches` dir into the extensions-build stage.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

No vLLM PR touches the DeepEP barrier. Upstream DeepEP has neither an issue nor a PR for this (checked 2026-10-03); v2.5 (93eb6eb) has the #715 fence but still signals on context 0 only, so it closes only one of the two holes.

## Test commands and results

- Cluster validation of this exact patch (wheel built from pristine d4f41e4e + patch, NCCL 2.30.7, 3×H200 4+2+2 DP=8 direct mode, DeepSeek-V4-Flash `--enforce-eager`, host-side audit harness): **in progress** — will update with results.
  - Context: per-context signals alone (without the NVLink fence) did **not** pass validation — faulted with the same stale-row signature at a same-node (NVLink) sender pair within ~25 min, which is what motivated adding the fence. Pristine DeepEP faulted during warmup within ~3.5 min.
- `bash -n` + pre-commit (shellcheck) on the install script change; `patch --dry-run` verified against a fresh d4f41e4e checkout.

## Model evaluation results

None yet — behavior-neutral change intended (ordering only), but will run the audit + a serving smoke before marking ready.

## AI assistance

Prepared with AI assistance (patch authoring, validation harness, PR text); root-cause evidence produced by the cluster runs referenced above.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] SM120: decode DeepSeek-V4.1's own KV records with FlashInfer's DSv4.1 sparse MLA
body:
## Overview

On SM120/SM121, DeepSeek-V4.1 writes the V4 KV record and decodes it with FlashInfer's V4 sparse MLA kernels, and `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla` is rejected. FlashInfer's SM120 sparse MLA also decodes V4.1's own records (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5197). This PR writes the V4.1 record on SM120 and lets the KV cache option select the matching FlashInfer kernel. It is the base for further SM120 DSv4.1 work.

**Depends on FlashInfer ≥ 0.7.1:** the `fp8_dsv41` / `fp8_dsv41_fp4_ca` formats are in 0.7.1rc2 but not in the pinned 0.7.0.post1, so this needs the FlashInfer pin bump before it merges.

## Claims

- `fp8_ds_mla` on SM120 writes the 528 B V4.1 record (all 512 dims MXFP8) instead of the 584 B V4 record, and decodes it with FlashInfer's `fp8_dsv41` kernels: +8.7% KV tokens at TP4.
- `nvfp4_ds_mla` works on SM120 (previously rejected): MXFP8 sliding window plus an NVFP4 compressed cache, decoded with `fp8_dsv41_fp4_ca`: +31% KV tokens over `fp8_ds_mla`.
- GSM8K accuracy and fixed 8K/1K serving throughput are unchanged.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4 on 4× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), FlashInfer built from main with #5197, one run per configuration.

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype {fp8,nvfp4_ds_mla} --block-size 128 --max-model-len 65536 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

| KV cache | FlashInfer format | KV tokens | GSM8K (chat, flexible-extract) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fp8` before this PR (V4 record) | `fp8` | 214,991 | 0.951 |
| `fp8` → `fp8_ds_mla` (V4.1 record) | `fp8_dsv41` | 233,679 | 0.945 |
| `nvfp4_ds_mla` | `fp8_dsv41_fp4_ca` | 305,319 | 0.948 |

GSM8K: lm-eval `gsm8k` through the chat template, 1,319 problems, 32 in flight, `max_tokens` 16384. The three scores are within one-run noise (±8 problems).

Fixed 8K input / 1K output (random prompts, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, 8 requests per concurrency), output tok/s; each pair ran at the same time on the two GPU halves of one host:

| Concurrency | V4 record (before) | `fp8_ds_mla` | | `fp8_ds_mla` | `nvfp4_ds_mla` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 105.7 | 105.6 | | 106.9 | 104.7 |
| 2 | 180.8 | 178.5 | | 183.3 | 179.8 |
| 4 | 314.9 | 315.7 | | 313.4 | 314.3 |
| 8 | 502.4 | 504.6 | | 505.2 | 502.0 |
| 16 | 732.1 | 734.2 | | 734.3 | 732.9 |
| 32 | 857.2 | 856.4 | | 859.0 | 1003.1 |
| 64 | 1039.7 | 1041.2 | | 1042.2 | 1036.4 |

All within 2%, except `nvfp4_ds_mla` at 32 in flight (+17%, one run, not yet explained and not claimed). No preemptions in any case.

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py   # 12 passed
pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py    # 357 passed, 19 skipped (SM120)
```

The new unit tests run without a GPU. CI has no SM120 runner for the serving path; it was validated as above.

<details>
<summary>Validation environment</summary>

The serving runs used vLLM `e6674262f1` with this branch merged, alongside unrelated changes for other models. On the test host's kernel (which caps a single long-term pin below 2 GiB), the CPU-offloaded Engram tables also needed chunked pinning, a host-specific workaround outside this PR.
</details>

## Details

- **Record:** `_use_v41_mxfp8_kv_record()` now also returns true on the SM120 family, so the SWA and compressed caches, the indexer page alignment and DSpark all use the V4.1 record there, as on SM100. Its writers (the fused qnorm/RoPE/KV insert and the compressor insert) already handle it on every arch.
- **Kernel selection:** the SM120 layer passes `kv_cache_format` per call from the caches it reads: `fp8_dsv41_fp4_ca` when an `nvfp4_ds_mla` call includes the compressed cache, `fp8_dsv41` otherwise (FlashInfer has no `fp8_dsv41_fp4_ca` kernel without the compressed cache, which the uncompressed layers hit), and `fp8` for the V4 record.
- **Backend:** `DeepseekV4FlashInferMLASparseBackend` accepts `nvfp4_ds_mla` on SM120 only; the SM100 TRTLLM-gen kernels behind the same backend cannot read the NVFP4 compressed cache.
- **No version gate:** the KV cache option alone selects the kernel; older FlashInfer builds without the V4.1 formats are not supported on this path.
- **Related:** #57523 makes the same record switch for gfx950 (a small textual conflict either way). #57292, #56509 and #57028 change SM120 page geometry and are orthogonal. #59342 adds `nvfp4_ds_mla` to the V3.2 `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` backend on SM10x, a different backend and model.
- **Not a duplicate:** searched open and merged PRs for `fp8_dsv41`, `fp8_dsv41_fp4_ca`, `nvfp4_ds_mla SM120`, `DSv4.1 SM120`, `V4.1 KV record`, `mxfp8 kv record` and FlashInfer DSv4.1 sparse MLA; none switches SM120 to the V4.1 records or wires FlashInfer's V4.1 formats.

title: [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Pin the offloaded PLE table at its exact size
body:
## Overview

`pin_memory=True` rounds the offloaded PLE table up to a power of two. Register it at its exact size instead.

## Claims

- 47.7 GiB per-rank table: 65.2 → 47.8 GiB host memory (GB10).
- TP2 Qwen4Exp on 2× DGX Spark now boots at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.78` (OOM before).
- ROCm/XPU unchanged.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py` on GB10, rebased on d5e62627a: 113 passed → 115 passed (2 new), 2 skipped on both. The CI step now runs the whole file, so no CI config change. The packed NVFP4 tables from #56273 also go through this path; their tests pass.
- E2E: `Blackfrost-AI/CYBER-FROST-3.8-NVFP4`, TP2 across two GB10s, default `cpu_offload`. Before: OOM in memory profiling. After: serves, KV cache 491k tokens. Greedy outputs vs table-on-device are within run-to-run noise.

## Details

- Anonymous mmap + `cudaHostRegister`, unregistered by a finalizer after the last view. This is the DSv4.1 THP helper's pattern. A failed registration falls back to `pin_memory=True`.
- `pin_tensor` doesn't fit: it never unregisters and can't fall back.
- torch's `pinned_max_round_threshold_mb` is unsafe on 2.13.0 (pytorch/pytorch#192722). `pinned_max_cached_size_mb` disables caching of all large pinned blocks process-wide.
- Not a duplicate: #58185/#56413 fix UVA weight offload, not this table. DSv4.1's tables: #59849. #60909 adds a generic exact-size helper and leaves this table out on purpose; this can switch to it if that lands first.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Register CPU-offloaded Engram tables at their exact size
body:
## Overview

Same fix as #59848, for DSv4.1. Default `cpu_offload` Engram tables use `pin_memory=True`, which rounds each table up to a power of two. Register them at exact size through the existing THP helper, without huge pages. Draft: GB10 only. cc @Juntian777: could you run your #59327 lookup bench on GB200?

## Claims

- TP2 per-rank table: 66 → 47.2 GiB host memory.
- GB10 lookup kernel: ~1.8× faster unsorted, 7–21% faster with #59327's sort.

## Validation

GB10, Engram lookup kernel, TP4 per-rank table, 32K tokens:

| memory | host | unsorted | sorted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pin_memory` (before) | 33.1 GiB | 41.4 ms | 10.9 ms |
| exact `cudaHostAlloc` | 24.9 GiB | 41.4 ms | 10.9 ms |
| registered (this PR) | 24.3 GiB | 22.7 ms | 10.2 ms |

Exact size gives the memory saving; the registered memory type gives the speed. These are 4 KiB pages, not THP.

`pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py`: 116 passed. The new small-page case fails on main.

Still needed before un-drafting: GB200 and an E2E `cpu_offload` run.

## Details

- `_allocate_huge_page_storage(n)` → `_allocate_registered_storage(n, huge_pages)`, called once. The THP path and the sort are unchanged. A failed registration falls back to `pin_memory=True`.
- CUDA only; ROCm is unchanged.
- `use_thp` is opt-in and skips the sort, so default users still pay the rounding.
