title: [ROCm][MoE] Enable MoRI FP4 dispatch for DeepSeek V4.1 a4w4
body:
## Overview

Enable MoRI FP4 dispatch for DeepSeek V4.1 a4w4 (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4=1`) and trim MoRI's dispatch output to the valid token count. **Stacked on #59596**, which adds MoRI FP4 dispatch for MXFP4 W4A4 checkpoints. Only the last two commits are new here; this PR will be rebased once #59596 lands.

## Claims

* DeepSeek V4.1 a4w4 under `--all2all-backend mori_*` now dispatches packed FP4 with e8m0 block scales instead of BF16. Before this change, #59596's W4A4-only gate kept it on BF16 dispatch, because this mode runs on a W4A16 quant config with MXFP4 activations in AITER.
* The two copies of the "MoRI dispatches FP4" check (prepare/finalize selection and `AiterExperts.workspace_shapes`) are now a single `FusedMoEConfig.use_mori_fp4_dispatch()`.
* MoRI's dispatch outputs are sliced to `num_dispatchers * max(num_tokens_across_dp)` rows instead of the full `world_size * max_num_tokens` receive buffer, so AITER picks its MoE kernel config for the real M rather than the worst case.
* No accuracy change on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash DEP2: GSM8K is 0.974 with MoRI FP4 dispatch and trimming, against 0.977 on the default path.
* On MI355X DEP2 agentic-coding traces, output throughput per GPU is 1.8–11.0% higher than allgather/reducescatter at c32–c192. One MoE layer's dispatch+combine takes 1.33–1.49× less time than MoRI BF16 at 384–8,192 tokens/rank.

## Validation

### Unit test

`tests/kernels/moe/test_mori_moe.py` gets an `mxfp4_dsv4` scheme. It builds W4A16 weights in the SEPARATED gate/up layout, sets `use_mxfp4_w4a4_dsv4`, asserts FP4 dispatch is selected, and compares two-rank MoRI against AITER's non-EP path, including CUDA graph replay at m=32. Every case also asserts that the experts receive `2 * m` rows, the trimmed prefix, rather than MoRI's max-sized buffer.

```bash
FLYDSL_RUNTIME_CACHE_DIR=<writable dir> pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_mori_moe.py
```

On 2x MI355X, all 28 cases pass: 7 shapes each for bf16, fp8_token_channel, mxfp4 and mxfp4_dsv4. Without a writable `FLYDSL_RUNTIME_CACHE_DIR`, both MXFP4 schemes fail with a `PermissionError` on AITER's default FlyDSL cache dir in our image. That is unrelated to this change.

### E2E: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash DEP2 on MI355X

Setup: 1 node, 2 GPUs, `--tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend aiter --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 128 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, CUDA graphs on. Validated on a local stack of `main@0cbac6cd13` + #58014 + #59596 + this change.

**Accuracy.** InferenceX GSM8K eval: `lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template`, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, `max_tokens=16384`, `temperature=0`, `num_concurrent=64`, no speculative decoding.

| config | strict-match | flexible-extract |
|---|---|---|
| default path: a8w4 MoE, allgather_reducescatter | 0.9765 ± 0.0042 | 0.9757 ± 0.0042 |
| **a4w4 MoE, MoRI FP4 dispatch + trim (this PR)** | **0.9742 ± 0.0044** | **0.9735 ± 0.0044** |

The difference is within one standard error.

**Throughput.** InferenceX agentic-coding sweep (`semianalysisai/cc-traces-weka-062126`, aiperf through `vllm-router`, 1 h per point), a4w4 MoE on both sides (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4=1`), DSpark speculative decoding with 5 tokens and synthetic acceptance (3.51). The only difference between the two sides is `--all2all-backend`.

| conc | output tok/s/GPU, agrs → MoRI FP4 | Δ | p50 TPOT (ms) | p50 TTFT (s) | p50 interactivity (tok/s/user) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | 582 → 593 | +1.8% | 7.75 → 7.46 | 0.253 → 0.241 | 129.0 → 134.0 |
| 64 | 1015 → 1060 | +4.5% | 16.9 → 16.0 | 0.363 → 0.351 | 59.4 → 62.6 |
| 128 | 1237 → 1278 | +3.4% | 45.8 → 42.8 | 0.689 → 0.633 | 21.9 → 23.4 |
| 192 | 1091 → 1210 | +11.0% | 82.5 → 74.2 | 1.19 → 1.08 | 12.1 → 13.5 |

**Kernel.** EP2 dispatch+combine, hidden 5120, 384 experts, top-6, HIP-graph replay. FP4 times include the MXFP4 quantize before dispatch.

| tokens/rank | allgather + reducescatter | MoRI BF16 | MoRI FP4 dispatch |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 58 µs | 46 µs | 47 µs |
| 384 | 182 µs | 164 µs | 123 µs |
| 1152 | 474 µs | 449 µs | 316 µs |
| 8192 | 2.93 ms | 3.02 ms | 2.03 ms |

## Details

* The DSv4.1 a4w4 expert path already sets `q_dtype_a=fp4x2` and forwards `a1q_scale`, so #59596's pre-quantized FP4 handling in `rocm_aiter_fused_experts` applies unchanged. Only the gate needed widening.
* Trimming: the bound comes from `dp_metadata.num_tokens_across_dp_cpu`, so it is known on the host, needs no device sync, and is fixed for a given CUDA graph capture size. Each source rank sends a token at most once, so every valid received row is inside that prefix.
* The e2e gain is modest on EP2. With top-6 over 2 ranks, almost every token goes to both ranks, so dispatch volume is not reduced, and a single xGMI link between the two GPUs (~64 GB/s) carries all traffic. FP4 shrinks dispatch bytes about 3.6×, while combine stays BF16.
* I also tried MoRI's combine quantization on this model (EP2) without wiring it in. `fp8_direct_cast` was about 1.3× faster on combine but lowered accuracy (gsm8k 0.869 vs 0.897 on the repo's `gsm8k_eval.py`). The `fp8_blockwise` and `fp4_blockwise` modes were slower than BF16 combine at EP2. Combine is left BF16. #44323 covers combine dtype selection more broadly.
* Not a duplicate: #59596 only gates on `quant_config.use_mxfp4_w4a4`, and #44323 (MoRI dispatch/combine dtype refactor) has no DSv4.1 a4w4 handling. I'm happy to fold this into #59596 if the author prefers.

title: [Kernel][Quant] Fuse MLA v_up_proj output quantization (WIP, #43498)
body:
## Purpose

Part of the manual quant-fusion migration tracked in #43224 / Q3 roadmap
#48168 (SIG Quantization), specifically the MLA attention + quant fusion item
(#43498). **Draft, iterating in public per-commit.**

## What's in so far

**Commit 1** — standalone kernel (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/mla_v_up_proj_quant.py`):
`MLACommonImpl`'s decode (MQA) path has no mechanism to fuse output
quantization into the kernel: `forward_impl` calls `forward_mqa(...)` with no
`output_scale`, and only *after* `_v_up_proj` (the per-head batched
up-projection GEMM, `[N,B,L] @ [N,L,V]`) writes a plain bf16 result does a
separate generic tail quantize it. Added `v_up_proj_fp8_static_quant`,
dispatched on compute capability:
- **sm_90+ (Hopper/Blackwell)**: single Triton kernel, GEMM + FP8 quant in
  one launch.
- **Everything else (Ampere included)**: the same matmul immediately
  followed by vLLM's existing `_custom_ops.scaled_fp8_quant`, called from one
  explicit site instead of a compiler-matched pattern. Triton cannot emit
  `float8_e4m3fn` pre-Hopper (confirmed by actually running it on an A100:
  `type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture`), so Ampere uses this
  path, not a degraded fused one.

**Commit 2** — wired into the real call site
(`MLAAttention.forward_impl`): the MQA branch now calls this kernel directly
and returns early when static FP8 output quant is requested, the step is
decode-only (`num_mha_tokens == 0`), and the backend declares support.
Scoped to decode-only steps deliberately — the existing tail's `quant_idx`
bookkeeping only tracks one contiguous slice, so generalizing to mixed
prefill+decode steps needs more work (next increment). Decode-only is also
the common steady-state-serving case, and the exact scenario from the
GB10/disaggregated-PD issue that motivated this investigation.

## Why this is not duplicating existing work

- #43772 ("Port MLA attention + quantization fusion to manual fused kernel")
  is the only other PR against #43498. Stale (last commit 2026-07-23,
  unresolved merge conflicts, no reviewer activity), and fuses quantization
  into the *attention reduction* stage, before `_v_up_proj` runs — a fusion
  point that predates `_v_up_proj` existing in its current form on `main`.
  This PR targets the up-projection GEMM itself, where `o_proj`'s input
  actually gets produced today.
- #56935 (merged) ships a real fused MLA+quant kernel, but it's a bespoke
  `FlashMLAMegaAttnBackend` scoped to DeepSeek-V4.1 on SM100
  (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flash_mla_mega_attn.py`), not the generic
  `MLACommonImpl` path every other MLA model (DeepSeek V2, etc.) runs
  through.

## Status / what's NOT in this PR yet

- Mixed prefill+decode batches still can't use the fused path at all (falls
  back unchanged — zero behavior change there).
- Only FP8 static per-tensor quantization. Per-token-block FP8 and NVFP4
  (also in #43498's inventory) are follow-ups.
- The sm_90+ fused path is implemented but **unverified on real hardware** —
  no Hopper/Blackwell access here. Gated behind a compute-capability check so
  it's unreachable (not wrong) elsewhere until someone can test it.
- No model eval yet: nothing currently calls `forward_impl` with
  `output_scale` set outside this new branch and the pre-existing compiler
  pass, so this doesn't change default behavior for any model yet. Will add
  before claiming this is mergeable.

## Test plan

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_mla_v_up_proj_quant.py -v
```
7/7 passed on an A100 (portable path): the original matmul+quant-vs-fp32
cosine-similarity check, plus a new regression test
(`test_v_up_proj_fused_quant_writes_through_to_caller_buffer`) that
reproduces `forward_impl`'s exact view/slice arithmetic end-to-end to catch
aliasing mistakes without needing a full model instance.

```
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_quant_output.py -q
```
20 passed, 1 skipped — no regression from the `forward_impl` edit.

`tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` in progress, will report results
in a follow-up commit.

## AI assistance disclosure

Implemented with Claude Code. Per AGENTS.md: shapes, the quant-scale
convention, the sm_80 Triton failure, and the view/slice aliasing behavior
were all verified by reading the real call sites and actually running
against real MLA weight shapes on this hardware, not assumed — including
catching and fixing a wrong-tolerance assertion in my own test (comparing
FP8-quantized values with `assert_close`'s tight default instead of the
cosine-similarity check the existing test suite already uses for this exact
reason). I (the human submitter) am reviewing every line and will defend
this change end-to-end; opening as draft specifically to iterate in public
rather than present this as finished.

title: [DeepSeek-V4-P1] Reuse persistent SiLU FP8 quantization for batch invariance
body:
## Overview

Add DeepSeek-V4's fused, token-local SiLU x Mul FP8 quantizer to vLLM's existing stable `_C` extension. Its CUDA source lives under `csrc/quantization/fused_kernels/`, rather than a new extension or a model-specific source directory. Contiguous and masked expert inputs share this fused operator; this PR does not enable a model path by itself.

- Preserve token-local clamp, BF16 rounding, and FP8 conversion for FP32, rounded FP32, and packed UE8M0 scales. Hopper and Blackwell retain their respective arithmetic behavior.
- Support 64-bit group/output offsets, including tensors above `2**31` elements. The existing persistent masked quantizer also gains BI-compatible clamp and arithmetic options; its default behavior remains compatible.
- Default non-BI execution is unchanged.

## Test

- H20 on the current PR head: `tests/kernels/moe/test_silu_mul_fp8_quant_deep_gemm.py` **29 passed**; `tests/kernels/moe/test_silu_mul_per_token_group_quant_fp8_colmajor.py` **117 passed**.
- H20: the large-shape regression from the reference implementation passed **2/2** for `numel > 2**31`, with bitwise parity against chunked quantization. This diagnostic was run outside the PR diff.
- Reference fused kernel comparison: **42/42** H100 cases had byte-identical FP8 values and scales across masked/contiguous layouts, scale formats, clamp modes, and BF16-pattern inputs.
- SM100 behavior was not measured on B200.

### Acc

In a two-step H100 DP4/EP4 integration with the other DeepSeek-V4 changes and weight reload, `training/rollout_probs_diff_max` and `rollout_corr/log_ppl_abs_diff` were **0 at both steps** (3031 tokens per DP worker, `max_num_batched_tokens=1024`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.55`). This is a combined-path result, not an isolated model evaluation of P1.

title: [Kernel] Add opt-in SM90 Triton MXFP8 W8A8 linear backend
body:
## Purpose

Add an experimental, opt-in Triton MXFP8 W8A8 dense linear backend for SM90 with BF16 activations. On Hopper, automatic MXFP8 linear selection currently uses Marlin W8A16. This backend dynamically quantizes activations per K32 group and executes independent GEMV/GEMM paths for decode and prefill, without Marlin fallback or a second packed weight copy.

Select it with:

```bash
vllm serve <model> \
  --kernel-config '{"linear_backend_per_quant":{"mxfp8":"triton"}}'
```

The implementation retains contiguous E4M3 weights, decodes E8M0 weight scales to FP32, and uses shape-dependent tiling, fused activation quantization, and split-K reduction. M=1 uses a fused GEMV. The backend accepts two-dimensional weights with positive K divisible by 32; batched weights use the existing separate selection. This does not replace MoE or attention kernels. Automatic selection retains its existing preferred backends.

W8A8 is the quantization contract; not every internal path executes native FP8 tensor-core instructions. Activation quantization changes W8A16 numerics. Performance validation is on H20 only.

## Duplicate-work check

Open PR searches were run for `MXFP8 Hopper`, `MXFP8 Triton`, and `"mxfp8" "SM90"`. No matching independent SM90 MXFP8 W8A8 dense-linear backend was found in those results. No tracking issue was supplied, so issue-number-specific searches are not applicable.

Related work has different scope:

- #54592 adds SM90 Q8KV8 sparse MLA attention prefill, rather than dense linear GEMM.
- #45875 tunes existing ROCm/gfx950 MXFP8 linear and MoE tiles.
- #59782 fuses activation quantization into ROCm block32 GEMM at small M.
- #53709 converts MXFP4 expert weights to block FP8 for Hopper MoE prefill.
- #57977 preserves MXFP8 activations between DeepGEMM kernels.

## Validation

GPU validation ran through Slurm. The six submitted files match the SHA256 manifest of the validated candidate. Results below are from that candidate, not a fresh GPU rerun during PR preparation.

```bash
# Slurm job 4314: 54 passed, 477 deselected
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/kernels \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py -k triton_mxfp8 -q

# Slurm job 4319: 48 shape combinations, three timing repetitions
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_triton_mxfp8.py \
  --output triton-mxfp8.json

# Changed-file checks: passed during PR preparation
PRE_COMMIT_HOME=/tmp/leo-pre-commit-w8a8 .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_triton_mxfp8.py \
  docs/features/quantization/README.md \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py \
  vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py \
  vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/triton.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/triton_mxfp8.py
git diff --cached --check
```

Tests cover independent quantized-reference correctness, row/column tails, per-row scales, zero inputs, noncontiguous activations, bias, CUDA graphs, dynamic fullgraph compilation, explicit backend selection, and invalid shape/offset rejection. The benchmark includes activation quantization, uses CUPTI with CUDA graphs and cold L2, alternates backend order, and reports synchronized eager timing separately.

### Real-checkpoint serving and evaluation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 8 x H20-3e, TP8, BF16, fixed 16 GiB KV cache per GPU, max sequence length 16384, max sequences 32, max batched tokens 8192, prefix caching/speculation disabled, compile mode 0 with FULL_DECODE_ONLY graphs. Serving numbers are means across three runs. Decode requests use 128 input / 64 output tokens; prefill uses 8192 input / 32 output tokens.

| Workload | Metric | Marlin W8A16 | Triton W8A8 | Change |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Decode C1 | Mean TPOT | 6.943 ms | 6.465 ms | -6.88% |
| Decode C8 | Mean TPOT | 9.882 ms | 9.864 ms | -0.19% |
| Decode C16 | Mean TPOT | 12.330 ms | 12.417 ms | +0.71% |
| Decode C32 | Mean TPOT | 17.167 ms | 16.718 ms | -2.62% |
| Prefill C2 | Mean TTFT | 1585.996 ms | 1449.532 ms | -8.60% |

GSM8K 5-shot, all 1319 test questions: Marlin 1204/1319 (91.28%), Triton 1194/1319 (90.52%), a decrease of 0.758 percentage points. Paired wins/losses were 28/38; the observed difference does not establish quality equivalence. Evaluation responses were checked for empty, malformed, and zero-token results.

C16 decode TPOT regresses slightly, and individual kernel shapes can remain slower than Marlin. This PR makes no universal performance or accuracy-equivalence claim and keeps the backend experimental and opt-in.

## AI assistance and human accountability

AI assistance was used to implement the backend, tests, benchmark, documentation, and analyze validation results.

title: [Qwen4Exp] PLE pinned-host FP8 lookup will not compile on sm_86, so --engram-config cpu_offload is unusable on consumer Ampere
body:
# [Qwen4Exp] PLE pinned-host FP8 lookup will not compile on sm_86, so `--engram-config cpu_offload` is unusable on consumer Ampere

## Summary

On four RTX 3090 (sm_86), v0.30.0 gets all the way to the first forward pass of the PLE n-gram
lookup and then dies compiling the Triton kernel, because `fp8e4nv` is not a supported fp8 dtype on
this architecture. The model cannot run without host offload, and the host offload path is the one
that does not compile, so this is a hard stop rather than a performance question.

## What worked, so the scope is narrow

Stock `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0`, no patches of any kind, serving a Qwen3.8-Flash-Next checkpoint
whose main body is AutoRound W4 (`quantization_config.quant_method: auto-round`) and whose PLE table
is a separately quantized FP8 e4m3 sidecar. Everything up to the first model forward succeeded:

- `Resolved architecture: Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`, `model_type: qwen4_exp`, max model len
  262144 accepted
- `INCConfig.override_quantization_method` returned `inc` for the auto-round config, so the W4 body
  was claimed natively, no overlay
- the FP8 PLE method was selected from the checkpoint's own config, with no `Fp8Config` involved,
  because `Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod.from_quant_config` tests `embedding_dtype` before it looks at
  the quantization config. I set `"ple_embedding_dtype": "float8_e4m3fn"` in `text_config` and got:

```
INFO [ngram_embedding.py:720] Initialized PLE embedding language_model.model.layers.1.ple.ple_embedding.ngram_embedding:
  quantization_method=Qwen4ExpPLEFp8EmbeddingMethod, weight_dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn,
  weight_device=cpu, pinned=True
```

on all four ranks, which is the behaviour `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'` is supposed to
produce.

- the table itself loaded. I converted a per-row-scaled FP8 sidecar to the upstream layout
  (`...ngram_embedding.shard_N.weight` for N in 0..127 at F8_E4M3 [2500012, 160], plus one
  `weight_scale` at BF16 [1]) and the loader accepted it without complaint:

```
INFO [default_loader.py:430] Loading weights took 445.36 seconds
INFO [model_runner.py:428] Model loading took 18.56 GiB memory and 462.17 seconds   (all four ranks)
```

## The failure

First `profile_run`, so no user traffic and nothing exotic:

```
(Worker_TP1_EP1) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1055] WorkerProc hit an exception.
  File "vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py", line 470, in _lookup
    _lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel[(flat_ids.numel(),)](
  File "triton/runtime/jit.py", line 884, in _do_compile
  File "triton/compiler/compiler.py", line 307, in compile
  File "triton/compiler/compiler.py", line 80, in make_ir
triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError: at 1:0:
def _lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel(
ValueError("type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture. The supported fp8 dtypes are ('fp8e4b15', 'fp8e5')")
```

`fp8e4nv` is the e4m3fn spelling, and the kernel's own dtype annotation is what rejects it. The
engine then reports `RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed` and the container exits.

## Why this matters more than it looks

The PLE table is 51B parameters. At FP8 e4m3 it is 47.68 GiB, which does not fit across four 24 GB
cards alongside a W4 body of about 63 GiB, and at BF16 it is roughly 95 GiB, which fits nowhere on
this box. So host offload is not an optimisation for this hardware, it is the only way the model
runs at all, and `cpu_offload` with an FP8 table is exactly the combination that will not compile.

This is also, as far as I can tell, the reason a fork exists. The deployment I am replacing carries
its own PLE offload worker and its own E4M3 gather routine, and the note in its Dockerfile is that
the 64-wide BF16 profiles spill registers under decode and run about 22x slower, so FP8 mode selects
a 16-wide 4-warp profile that stays within 2 percent of BF16. Whoever wrote that hit this wall and
worked around it in software.

## Questions

1. Is sm_86 in scope for `--engram-config cpu_offload` at all, or is the pinned-host FP8 path
   deliberately Hopper/Blackwell-only? If it is out of scope, a config-time refusal would save a
   10-minute load before the first forward pass tells you.
2. Is there a supported way to keep the table in host RAM in a dtype that Triton will compile here?
   The obvious candidate is the unquantized pinned path, but that needs about 95 GiB of host RAM,
   which is why the fork quantized it to 47.68 GiB in the first place.
3. Would a non-Triton gather for the pinned lookup be acceptable upstream, or is the intent that
   consumer Ampere uses device-resident tables only?

## Environment

4x RTX 3090 (sm_86), TP4 with expert parallel, `--distributed-executor-backend mp`, no speculative
decoding, `--max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.965`,
`--kv-cache-memory-bytes 2147483648`, BF16 KV cache (upstream still refuses FP8 main KV for QSA on
this arch, `models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/qsa.py:110`), `--compilation-config '{"mode":0,
"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'`, `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`, vLLM 0.30.0 release image,
PyTorch 2.x as shipped in it, Triton as shipped in it.

Secondary observation, not diagnosed and offered only in case it is familiar: while the shards were
still loading, the allocator logged

```
[rank1] CUDACachingAllocator.cpp:508 expandable_segments: memory mapping failed with OOM on device 1
while trying to map 20971520 bytes (free: 8781824, total: 25295323136)
```

a handful of times per rank, and then the load completed normally at 18.56 GiB per rank. I do not
know what was holding the memory at that moment and I am not claiming it is the cause of the failure
above, which is unambiguous.

title: [DeepSeek-V4-P2] Extract deterministic sparse attention
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 sparse attention can change a request's result when candidate ordering, the sparse index list, workspace offsets, or the FlashMLA launch depend on neighboring requests. This PR makes the supported sparse-selection and attention path request-local in batch-invariant mode, without changing normal execution.

## Changes

- Add a stable-extension CUDA top-k selector that orders by score and then request-local source index. Use the same tie-break for supported prefill and batch-invariant decode instead of inheriting packed-batch offsets.
- Assemble C4/C128 sparse and sliding-window indices with stable ordering, padding, lengths, and graph-safe metadata. This matters because FlashMLA consumes the index list in order, not merely as a set.
- Launch batch-invariant prefill one request per chunk so the shared workspace dimensions and FlashMLA launch geometry are request-local. In supported decode, use model-capacity-based KV workspace offsets and stable C128 index widths rather than batch-local maxima.
- Add `VLLM_DS4_DECODE_KERNEL=sparse` to opt into the prefill-style sparse FlashMLA decode path. The default is `paged`; this choice is separate from `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`.
- Reject unsupported DCP/PCP batch-invariant sparse top-k and text-with-image aligned sparse attention, instead of silently changing the numeric contract.

## Data flow

![DeepSeek-V4 batch-invariant sparse attention architecture](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/inaniloquentee/d5a1e05c74fddb335aa38a58bf30fb4f/raw/a214f750b88f6ab043577f4e774cb3be059582b4/ds4-p2-sparse-attention-architecture.svg)

This depicts the batch-invariant sparse path, not the default paged decode path.

## Scope and dependencies

Builds on #59863 for the stable CUDA operator infrastructure; until that PR lands and this branch is rebased, this diff includes its kernel. The guarantee is limited to supported sparse selection, index assembly, and attention under the same request/input contract. It does not establish prefill/decode equivalence, full-model train/rollout alignment, or support for DCP/PCP and image tokens. MoE, mHC, reload, and split-K are outside this PR. Request-local prefill can trade batching efficiency for determinism.

## Validation

- Previously reported local H100 80GB run (Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130): **109 passed, 9 skipped** across targeted top-k, DeepGEMM, FlashMLA, kernel-contract, and environment suites. Native stable-ABI build and CUDA Graph replay checks also passed in that run.
- Tests cover score ties, packed-offset independence, C4/C128 index assembly, sparse FlashMLA behavior, and unsupported-path rejection. Applicable local pre-commit hooks passed.
- Upstream pre-commit CI was gated by the repository pre-run eligibility check; this is not a passing test result. Full-model alignment, Blackwell, multi-rank NCCL, and serving performance were not validated. No benchmark table is included because serving latency and throughput were not measured.

title: [Spec Decode][ROCm] Keep draft models at checkpoint precision under a4w4 and quantized quick reduce
body:
## Overview

Keep speculative-decoding draft models at their checkpoint precision when two ROCm opt-ins that lower precision are enabled: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4=1` (FP4 MoE activations) and `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION` (quantized TP all-reduce). The target model behaves as before.

## Claims

- Draft models load and run inside a new `draft_model_scope()`. The scope is applied once, in `initialize_model`, so it covers every proposer on both model runners (MRV1 and MRV2), including CUDA-graph capture and breakable CUDA graphs.
- `FusedMoEConfig` no longer enables a4w4 for draft MoE layers. DeepSeek V4.1's DSpark draft keeps the checkpoint's a8w4 (MXFP8 activations), and the target still runs a4w4.
- `QuickAllReduce.should_quick_allreduce` returns `False` inside a draft forward. Draft all-reduces fall back to the next all-reduce backend (AITER custom or custom all-reduce), which does no quantization. This also covers AITER's fused quick-reduce + RMSNorm path, which uses the same check.
- Without these opt-ins nothing changes: no other code reads the scope.

## Validation

Unit tests (`.venv` + this worktree on MI355X; GPU needed only for the AITER test):

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_mtp_validation.py \
  tests/distributed/test_rocm_quick_reduce.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py -k "a4w4 or draft or scopes or mtp"
# 17 passed
```

- `test_initialize_model_scopes_only_draft_models` checks that the scope is active while a draft is built and run. It also checks that the target, and an ngram config that aliases the target, never get the scope.
- `test_aiter_moe_a4w4_dsv4_skips_draft_model` checks that a4w4 is on outside the scope and off inside it.
- `test_quick_allreduce_rejects_draft_model_input` checks that an INT4 quick reduce of an eligible size is declined inside the scope.
- With either gate reverted, the matching test fails.

**End-to-end: pending.** Planned on MI355X: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with DSpark (k=5), TP4, a4w4 + INT4 quick reduce, using the InferenceX GSM8K harness (lm-eval chat completions, 5-shot). I'll compare real acceptance length and throughput with and without this PR. For reference, InferenceX evals of the same setup measured AL 3.94 with neither opt-in, 3.89 with INT4 quick reduce, and 3.90 with a4w4 + INT4 quick reduce ([InferenceX#3690](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3690)).

## Details

**Motivation.** A lower-precision draft never changes outputs, because rejection sampling corrects it. It only lowers acceptance, so evals don't catch it, and the cost shows up only as lost speculative speedup. Both opt-ins are global today. On ROCm the DSpark draft reuses `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer`, so a4w4 also turns the draft's MoE into FP4 activations, and the draft's attention/MoE all-reduces go through quick reduce's INT4 codec once batches pass the size threshold. Benchmark rules that require drafts to run as shipped (e.g. InferenceX's draft-precision check, which rejected [InferenceX#3697](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3697) for this) then rule out these knobs entirely, even though their target-side gain is legitimate.

**Design.**
- **Detection.** `initialize_model` identifies the draft with the existing idiom `model_config is speculative_config.draft_model_config`, also used by `_resolve_and_verify_engram_config`. It excludes the case where that object is the target's config (ngram/custom proposers).
- **Construction.** The scope covers draft construction. a4w4 is decided in `FusedMoEConfig.__post_init__`, and that config is built only at layer construction.
- **Forward.** The draft's `forward` is wrapped in the scope, because quick reduce is chosen at runtime, and at capture time under CUDA graphs. Proposers and graph wrappers (`CUDAGraphWrapper`, `BreakableCUDAGraphWrapper`) all call the draft module, so the wrapped `forward` always runs. The wrapper sits outside any compiled inner model, so the flag is set when the all-reduce op runs.
- **Placement.** The scope lives next to `set_current_vllm_config` in `vllm.config`, which both `vllm.distributed` and the MoE config already import.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- **Draft speed.** Draft all-reduces lose quick reduce's bandwidth savings. Draft reductions are small, about 50 KiB per running request per step for DeepSeek V4.1, so the effect should be minor, and end-to-end numbers will confirm it.
- **Compiled top-level drafts.** If a draft's top-level class is itself `@support_torch_compile`, its `forward` isn't wrapped, since Dynamo would trace the wrapper. Its construction is still scoped. Current drafts compile only their inner model, and ROCm DeepSeek V4/V4.1 drafts aren't compiled.
- **Scope of knobs.** Only these two opt-ins check the scope. Other knobs that lower precision can opt in later with `in_draft_model()`.

---

title: [Bug]: flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl passes enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce, which pinned FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 does not accept
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `main` @ 84bcbc6264
- `flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1` / `flashinfer-cubin==0.7.0.post1` (`requirements/cuda.txt`), `FLASHINFER_VERSION=0.7.0.post1` (`docker/versions.json`, `docker/Dockerfile`)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`FlashInferMoeEp.__init__` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/flashinfer_moe_ep.py`, added in #54049) builds the CuTeDSL megakernel config with a kwarg the pinned FlashInfer does not have:

```python
megakernel = api.Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig(
    ...
    enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce=False,
    ...
)
```

`Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig` is an alias of the dataclass `Sm100_Nvfp4_Nvfp4_Bf16_Cutedsl_MegaMoeConfig`. That dataclass names the field differently depending on the FlashInfer version:

| FlashInfer | field |
|---|---|
| v0.7.0, v0.7.0.post1 (pinned) | `in_kernel_fc2_reduce: bool = False` |
| v0.7.1rc1, v0.7.1rc2, main | `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce: bool = False` |

The rename came in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4604 and first shipped in v0.7.1rc1. No stable 0.7.1 has been released yet.

With the pinned FlashInfer, selecting `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` therefore fails at layer construction: the dataclass `__init__` raises `TypeError` for the unexpected keyword argument `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce`. The `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` backend is unaffected.

I checked every other kwarg the adapter passes to FlashInfer's MoE-EP types (`BootstrapConfig`, `FleetParams`, `MoEWeightPack`, `MegaConfig`, `DeepGemmMegaMoeConfig`, `Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig`). All of them exist in both v0.7.0.post1 and v0.7.1rc2, so this is the only mismatch.

**Why CI didn't catch it:** the only test that constructs the adapter, `tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py::test_init_warmup_forward_is_exact_on_grid_inputs`, requires SM100 and 2+ GPUs. The `kernels-moe-test` job runs on L4, so that test always skips. The CPU tests in `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_fi_moe_ep.py` don't construct the adapter.

**Proposed fix:** drop the kwarg. `False` is the field's default in every FlashInfer version from v0.7.0 through main, so behavior is unchanged with both the current pin and a future 0.7.1 bump. I'll also add a device-agnostic test that builds the adapter against the installed FlashInfer's real config types, faking only the megakernel layer. Any future kwarg drift would then fail on the L4 runners. I'll send a PR with a runtime repro and GB200 serving results.


_This issue was investigated with AI assistance (Claude Code). The version table was checked against the FlashInfer git tags listed above._

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Searched existing issues and PRs. Nothing matches `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce`, `in_kernel_fc2_reduce`, `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` or `Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig`.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Unblock scheduling after a failed async KV load
body:
## Overview

With `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`, a request whose async KV load fails with no usable prefix can sit in WAITING forever, even on an idle engine, and the requests queued behind it never run. Nothing errors. It takes a connector that offers the same async load again on the retry, e.g. MooncakeStoreConnector (async by default) or a MultiConnector whose offloading child holds the prefix after NIXL fails.

Related: #59096, #59099, #59102, #59325, #59329 (independent fixes in nearby KV load paths).

## Claims

- The failed request is admitted again once its load fits.
- Requests holding loaded blocks are no longer stuck behind it.
- No change when the failed load keeps a valid prefix.

## Validation

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py -q
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit tests/v1/core -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py
```

On main the two no-prefix cases fail (`assert <RequestStatus.WAITING: 1> == <RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS: 3>`) and the three-request case schedules neither loaded request (`assert 'id-7' in {}`); the valid-prefix control passes. With the fix all 18 tests in the file pass, and either half of the fix alone leaves a test red.

Suites, macOS arm64 (CPU), with the fix:

- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit`: 1905 passed, 12 failed, 42 skipped
- `tests/v1/core`: 919 passed, 1 failed, 4 errors

Without the scheduler change (new tests kept), `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit` gives 1902 passed and 15 failed: the same 12 plus the 3 new tests. `tests/v1/core` is unchanged. The other 12 and the core failures also fail on unmodified main here: NVIDIA-only paths (hf3fs, HiSparse, offloading tiering), Ray on the CPU platform, a gated model, and end-to-end tests that need more free RAM than this machine had.

CPU only: the tests drive the real Scheduler with a mocked connector, as the rest of this file does. No GPU run.

## Details

After the failure, `_update_waiting_for_remote_kv` frees the request's blocks ([scheduler.py:3097](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/84bcbc62644356270aaaa5e2d0237d03adc9bb3a/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L3097)) but leaves it in `_inflight_prefills` and `kv_holding_waiting`.

- Async admission reserves the remaining blocks of every in-flight prefill (#44560, [scheduler.py:1214](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/84bcbc62644356270aaaa5e2d0237d03adc9bb3a/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L1214-L1217)). Holding nothing, the request now reserves its whole sequence against its own retry, so the gate ([kv_cache_manager.py:575](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/84bcbc62644356270aaaa5e2d0237d03adc9bb3a/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py#L575-L579)) needs room for the load plus its full size. In the test: 10 usable blocks, a 6-block prompt, a 5-block hit, and 10 - 6 < 5 on every step.
- `kv_holding_waiting` is drained first so that a block holder never waits behind a request whose failed allocation stops the scan (#58947). The freed request is exactly that request.

The fix discards it from `_inflight_prefills` when its blocks are freed, as preemption does, and moves a request that no longer holds blocks (by `_holds_kv_blocks`, which the queues already route by) from `kv_holding_waiting` to the front of `waiting` before scheduling it. The reservation itself is unchanged.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes these lines on current main. #55297 makes MooncakeStore's next lookup a miss after an invalid-block failure; it is complementary and leaves the scheduler state, `failed_recving` and other connectors as they are. #57418 and #59343 use the reservation without touching this path; #53298, #54733 and #56733 handle sync or hybrid failures, and #59603 forwards failed loads to LMCache's scheduler side.

## AI assistance

I used an AI coding assistant (Claude) to audit this code path, write the fix and write the tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above myself. The commit carries a Co-authored-by trailer, as AGENTS.md asks.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Mooncake: transfer GLM-5.3-Flash's kpool indexer pages and tail like NIXL
body:
## Overview

GLM-5.3-Flash P/D over Mooncake fails: its kpool indexer stores several kernel blocks in one tensor row and keeps its kpool tail inside the same allocation, which #53906 taught NIXL but not Mooncake. This PR gives Mooncake the same handling, sharing NIXL's helpers.

## Claims

- GLM-5.3-Flash prefill/decode over Mooncake works: chat GSM8K 0.970 (0.974 with MTP), against 0.972 for a single server, with no failed transfers. Before this PR most transfers failed and requests errored.
- Other models keep their registration: the change only applies to a compressed cache whose rows hold several kernel blocks, the same predicate NIXL uses.

## Validation

GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4, TP4 prefill -> TP4 decode on one host (4+4 RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, two NUMA halves), Mooncake over RDMA, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 65536 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, one run each:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Mooncake transfers (prefill, per 5 s window) | ~4 succeeded, ~300 failed | ~200 succeeded, 0 failed |
| Descriptors per transfer | 837 | 65 |
| Chat GSM8K (1,319, flexible-extract, 32 in flight) | requests failed | 0.970 |
| Same, with `{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}` | — | 0.974 (94-95% draft acceptance) |

Before the fix, the prefill logged `Memory region not registered by any active device(s)` and `Failed to get segment descriptor ... 0x...6c00--0x...7000` (1 KiB, the kpool tail's half page).

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, same topology, as a regression check of another compressed-cache model: its caches do not match the predicate (the same 18 packed layer regions are registered), chat GSM8K 0.944 against 0.947 without this PR, no failed transfers.

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py   # 345 passed
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py  # 96 passed
```

<details>
<summary>Validation environment</summary>

The serving runs used vLLM `5f30fc7031` with this branch merged, alongside unrelated changes for other models (among them #53078, which reworks Mooncake's Mamba regions in the same function, and #58305). The unit tests above ran on this branch alone.
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** The kpool indexer is an `MLAAttentionSpec` with `tokens_per_state > 1` whose tensor row holds several kernel blocks, and the `KpoolTailSpec` cache is a view at the start of the same allocation. Mooncake registered the indexer per tensor row and the tail as a region of its own, then `_logical_to_kernel_block_ids` expanded both groups' block ids to kernel blocks (x36 here: 2304-token blocks over 64-token kernel blocks). Kernel block `j` was addressed as row `j` instead of page `j`, so the indexer and tail descriptors landed in the wrong bytes or past the registered memory.

**Change.**
- `register_kv_caches` registers a cache matching NIXL's `uses_dense_virtual_transfer_pages` page by page (stride and length = the kernel page), so kernel block `j` is page `j`.
- A `KpoolTailSpec` view inside such an allocation is not registered; its group is added to the indexer region's shared groups (`_SHARED_REGION_GROUP_ID`), so the tail group's blocks are read through the pages that hold them, as NIXL reads every attention group through each region. A tail that is not fully covered raises instead of transferring partially.
- `tensor_byte_span_end` and `uses_dense_virtual_transfer_pages` move from NIXL's `base_worker.py` to `kv_connector/utils.py` unchanged, so both connectors use one predicate.

**Related.** #57169 (and #55219 before it) and #59297 move GLM-5.3-Flash to the generic packed layout with a `CircularBufferSpec` tail and drop this layout from both connectors. This PR fixes Mooncake for the layout on main until one of them lands; if one does, this handling goes with it. No other open PR changes Mooncake's handling of this layout (searched `Mooncake kpool`, `Mooncake KpoolTail`, `Mooncake GLM-5.3-Flash`, `Mooncake compressed indexer`, `Mooncake tokens_per_state`, `mooncake register_kv_caches`).

title: [Bug]: flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl fails at model load because vLLM CUDA images don't ship nvshmem4py (No module named 'nvshmem')
body:
### Your current environment

- `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`, arm64 manifest `sha256:54fecd34465bfc9cdcd6e94f1537da94f87a1cfbc7c4a5b2536089dff473b134` (vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev616+g1a001d584`)
- `flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1`, `nvidia-nvshmem-cu13==3.4.5`, `torch==2.13.0+cu130`
- `nvshmem4py-cu13` is **not installed**: `import nvshmem.core` → `ModuleNotFoundError`
- 4× GB300 per node (Slurm + pyxis), and 4× GB200

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` can't run in vLLM's CUDA images or wheels, because the Python package it needs, `nvshmem4py` (`nvshmem.core`), isn't installed.

- **Where it's needed:** FlashInfer's CuTeDSL MoE-EP megakernel bootstraps NVSHMEM when the layer is built: `MoEEpMegaLayer.__init__` → `bootstrap_moe_ep_runtime` → `_init_nvshmem_after_dist` → `import nvshmem.core` (`flashinfer/moe_ep/core/runtime/bootstrap.py`). The kernel's comm shim also allocates its symmetric buffers through `nvshmem.core`.
- **Nobody declares it:** vLLM doesn't (`requirements/cuda.txt`, `docker/Dockerfile`), and neither does FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1. From 0.7.1rc1, FlashInfer lists `nvshmem4py-cu13` only in its `sm107` extra.
- **Nobody checks for it:** vLLM's support check for the backend doesn't look for the package. So an explicit `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` passes backend selection, loads the whole checkpoint, and only then fails on every rank in `process_weights_after_loading`:

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'nvshmem'
```

`flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` is unaffected: FlashInfer's DeepGEMM megakernel only needs `torch.distributed`.

**Repro.** On current `main` you first hit the `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce` `TypeError` (#59887; fix in review in #59900), so apply that fix to see this error:

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl
```

**Validation** (nightly image above + #59900, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `2cba9e42`):

| Setup | Result |
|---|---|
| GB200, DEP=4, no `nvshmem4py` | All 4 ranks fail with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'nvshmem'` about 135 s into startup, after the weights load |
| GB300, `tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py` CuTeDSL e2e, no `nvshmem4py` | Same `ModuleNotFoundError` |
| + `uv pip install nvshmem4py-cu13==0.4.0` (adds only it and `cython`) | e2e 8/8 pass. Serving works, with default CUDA graphs and correct answers. GSM8K (1319, 5-shot): 0.894 GB300 DEP=4, 0.905 GB200 DEP=4, 0.888 DEP=16 across 4 GB300 nodes |

**Proposed fix (PR to follow):**
1. Report a missing `nvshmem4py` as an unsupported reason for the CuTeDSL backend, so the oracle rejects it with an actionable message before any weights load.
2. Add `nvshmem4py-cu13` to `requirements/cuda.txt` for CUDA 13 on Linux with Python < 3.14 (there are no cp314 wheels). Skip it on CUDA 12 builds, because `nvshmem4py-cu12` caps `cuda-python` at 12.9.

cc @jdebache

_This issue was investigated and validated with AI assistance (Claude Code). Runs were on GB300/GB200 Slurm clusters using the nightly image above._

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Searched existing issues and PRs: no match for `nvshmem4py`, `nvshmem.core` or `No module named 'nvshmem'`.

title: [Bug]: flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm: 'ImportError: generic_type: type "Runtime" is already registered!' with vendored DeepGEMM
body:
### Your current environment

- `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`, arm64 manifest `sha256:54fecd34465bfc9cdcd6e94f1537da94f87a1cfbc7c4a5b2536089dff473b134` (vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev616+g1a001d584`)
- `flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1`, vendored DeepGEMM only (`vllm.third_party.deep_gemm`; no site-packages `deep_gemm`)
- 4× GB300 (Slurm + pyxis)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm`, any FlashInfer code path that does `from deep_gemm.utils import ...` crashes:

```
  File ".../vllm/third_party/deep_gemm/utils/layout.py", line 1, in <module>
    from .._C import (
ImportError: generic_type: type "Runtime" is already registered!
```

**Root cause.** `_expose_deep_gemm_to_flashinfer()` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/flashinfer_moe_ep.py`) only does `sys.modules.setdefault("deep_gemm", <vllm.third_party.deep_gemm>)`. The alias covers the top-level package and none of its submodules. So when FlashInfer imports `deep_gemm.utils`:
1. Python doesn't find `deep_gemm.utils` in `sys.modules` and re-executes the vendored `utils` package under the new name.
2. Its relative `from .._C import ...` then loads DeepGEMM's pybind11 extension a second time, as `deep_gemm._C`.
3. pybind11 refuses to register its types twice.

**Where FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 makes that import** (also in 0.7.1rc2/rc3):
- `fp8_fp4_bf16_deepgemm/weights.py` `_quantize_grouped_fp4`, when the weights it gets aren't pre-quantized;
- `fp8_fp4_bf16_deepgemm/staging.py`, the activation-staging fallback, used when `FLASHINFER_MEGA_FUSED_STAGE=0` or when the fused quant stage isn't supported for the input.

**Validation** (nightly image above, GB300):

| Path | Result |
|---|---|
| Minimal repro: `_expose_deep_gemm_to_flashinfer(); from deep_gemm.utils import per_token_cast_to_fp4` | `ImportError … "Runtime" is already registered!` |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py::test_init_warmup_forward_is_exact_on_grid_inputs[*-deep_gemm-*]` (bf16 weights) | 8/8 fail with the same `ImportError` |
| `vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` with `FLASHINFER_MEGA_FUSED_STAGE=0` | All 4 ranks crash with the same `ImportError` about 180 s into startup |
| Same serve command with default env | Works: MXFP4 weights arrive pre-quantized and the fused stage is used. GSM8K 0.901 |

**Proposed fix (PR to follow):** in `_expose_deep_gemm_to_flashinfer`, alias every already-loaded vendored submodule as well, so FlashInfer reuses the existing module objects instead of re-executing them. This is a no-op when DeepGEMM is installed in site-packages.

cc @jdebache

_This issue was investigated and validated with AI assistance (Claude Code). Runs were on GB300 Slurm nodes using the nightly image above._

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Searched existing issues and PRs: no match for `already registered`, `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` (other than #59887) or `deep_gemm` aliasing.

title: [Core] Release the CUDA graph pool on sleep instead of backing it up
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #59160. With `sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph=True`, sleep copied the CUDA graph pool to pinned host memory and copied it back on wake. The copy is unnecessary: after capture, no tensor is allocated in the pool. It only holds scratch (activations, kernel workspaces, indexer logits, MoE scratch) that every replay writes before it reads.

This PR:
- Releases the `cudagraph` tag on sleep without a CPU backup. Any wake still maps it back at the same addresses, so graphs replay without recapture.
- Refuses to release the pool if a tensor is still allocated in it (`Cannot release the CUDA graph pool: tensors are live`). The check runs before anything is unmapped, so a future buffer kept alive inside the pool fails loudly instead of waking up as garbage.
- Updates the config docstring and the sleep mode docs.

Effect: no pinned host memory for the pool, and less copying on sleep and wake. On DeepSeek-V4.1 (TP8, GB300) the pool is 7.43 GiB per GPU.

## Test Plan

- `test_cudagraph_pool_sleep` (levels 1 and 2), reworked:
  - sleep releases every `cudagraph` allocation with no backup;
  - sleep refuses, and unmaps nothing, while a tensor is alive in the pool;
  - any wake maps the pool back at the same addresses;
  - a replay is correct after wake.
- `test_sleep_cudagraph_pool` (FULL, PIECEWISE, breakable, TP2 with custom allreduce, off by default): outputs are exact after level 1 and level 2 sleeps.
- Liveness, measured before this change on the #59160 code: at the end of capture, the graph pool's allocated bytes, for
  - DeepSeek-V4.1 (TP8);
  - DeepSeek-V4-Flash with MTP;
  - 16 configs on H200: Qwen3 0.6B/4B/8B (FULL, PIECEWISE, breakable), V1 runner, TP2 with custom allreduce, draft model, DeepSeek MTP, MiMo MTP, DFlash, Qwen3-VL-2B encoder graphs, LoRA.
- Garbage fill, also measured before this change: after sleep and wake, fill the pool with 0xFF, then compare outputs with the awake run.

## Test Result

- CI image `5e56e9af2a` (main with #59160) plus this patch, run the CI way (`cd tests`, `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn`), on H200:
  - `test_cumem.py`: 21 passed.
  - `test_sleep_cudagraph_pool`: 5/5 passed in each of 3 runs.
  - `test_sleep_mode_backend.py`: 9 passed.
- Liveness: 0 allocated bytes in the graph pool after capture, and still 0 after generation, in every config above. Everything reserved is cached-free.
- Garbage fill: outputs token-exact in every config. Zero-filling the `weights` tag changes them, so the check can fail.
- Negative control: a 256 MiB tensor allocated during capture, kept alive, written once outside the graph and read by every replay, shows up as allocated in the pool. With this PR, sleep refuses it.

---
This PR contains AI-assisted code (Claude Code); commits carry a `Co-authored-by` trailer.

### Re-check on GB300 at scale (rebased onto main `bdd31c31de`, no conflicts)

- GB300 (arm64 nightly 18f8f9602 + this PR rebased on main bdd31c31de, the 3 PR files bind-mounted with sha256 gates), Model Runner V2, `--sleep-mode-offload-cudagraph`, 3 level-1 cycles then 1 level-2 cycle:

  | Model | Asleep MiB/GPU: flag off / #59160 / this PR | CPU backup GiB/GPU, L1 / L2: #59160 → this PR | Probes after each wake | GSM8K (1319, 5-shot) awake → after wake, this PR |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8 over 2 nodes | 14681 / 7071 / 7071 | 46.92 / 9.85 → 39.49 / 2.41 | 28/28 ×3 | 0.906 → 0.904 (2nd launch 0.904 → 0.906; flag off 0.898 → 0.900) |
  | DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4, MTP 1 | 10871 / 8635 / 8635 | 46.54 / 6.78 → 44.36 / 4.59 | 28/28 ×3 | 0.947 → 0.945 (flag off 0.945 → 0.948) |

  - Same asleep memory as #59160. The pool's CPU copy (7.43 GiB/GPU on V4.1, 2.18 GiB/GPU on V4-Flash with MTP) is gone at both levels: the backup equals the flag-off backup, and node MemAvailable drops ~30 GiB/node less at sleep on V4.1.
  - Wake is unchanged (0.8–1.1 s). Later sleeps are 1.1–1.2 s vs 1.25 s with #59160.
  - The "tensors are live" guard never fired.
  - Level-2 + `reload_weights` output is garbage in all arms, flag off included: the known DeepSeek-V4 TP>1 reload issue, not this PR.
- Unit tests on GB300 (aarch64, CUDA 13.0), rebased on main `bdd31c31d`, run the CI way, 3 runs each: `test_cumem.py` 21/21, `test_sleep_mode.py -k test_sleep_cudagraph_pool` 5/5 (including custom-ar-tp2 on 2 GPUs), `test_sleep_mode_backend.py` 9/9. The updated `test_cudagraph_pool_sleep` fails on main, as intended (main does not refuse while a tensor is live in the pool).

title: [Bugfix] Alias vendored DeepGEMM submodules for FlashInfer MoE-EP
body:
## Overview

Fixes #59904. With only vLLM's vendored DeepGEMM installed (the default in vLLM's images), `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` crashes with `ImportError: generic_type: type "Runtime" is already registered!` wherever FlashInfer does `from deep_gemm.utils import ...`. This PR makes vLLM's `deep_gemm` alias cover the vendored submodules too.

## Claims

- After `_expose_deep_gemm_to_flashinfer()`, `from deep_gemm.utils import ...` reuses the already-loaded vendored `utils` and `_C` modules, so DeepGEMM's pybind11 extension isn't initialized twice.
- The 8 `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` cases of `test_init_warmup_forward_is_exact_on_grid_inputs` pass; they failed 8/8 on the nightly. These pass bf16 weights, so FlashInfer quantizes them through `deep_gemm.utils`.
- Serving with FlashInfer's torch staging fallback (`FLASHINFER_MEGA_FUSED_STAGE=0`) no longer hits the `ImportError`.
  - With CUDA graphs off, it serves.
  - With CUDA graphs on, it still fails later, at graph capture. I haven't root-caused which op breaks capture; it's out of scope here.
- Default serving of pre-quantized MXFP4 checkpoints never reaches the dotted import, and it serves as before.
- New CPU-only test `test_deep_gemm_alias_reuses_vendored_submodules` in `tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py`, which the L4 MoE Kernels job runs. It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.

## Validation

All runs were on 4× GB300 (Slurm + pyxis) with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `2cba9e42`.
- **before:** `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` arm64 (`sha256:54fecd34…`, vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev616+g1a001d584`, which includes #54049, 8 commits behind this PR's base).
- **after:** `main` 84bcbc6264 + this PR's fix commit, built from `docker/Dockerfile` for linux/arm64.
  - Build: the arm64 CI base image, `torch_cuda_arch_list=10.0`, no sccache, `RUN_WHEEL_CHECK=false`, and local build parallelism.
  - Provenance: the commit was applied from a patch file, so the image reports `g436891372` (same `git patch-id` as 871a664).
  - Targets: `test` for pytest, `vllm-openai` for serving.
- Both images have `flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1` and only the vendored DeepGEMM.
- The unit-test row ran this branch's final test file, from the test-only follow-up `9e5898a`, against each image's installed adapter.

| Check | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| New unit test (`pytest kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py -k deep_gemm_alias`) | **fails** (run against the nightly's adapter) | **passes** |
| Minimal repro: `_expose_deep_gemm_to_flashinfer(); from deep_gemm.utils import per_token_cast_to_fp4` | `ImportError: generic_type: type "Runtime" is already registered!` | OK; `deep_gemm.utils` and `deep_gemm._C` are the already-loaded `vllm.third_party.deep_gemm.*` modules |
| `pytest kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py -k "test_init_warmup and deep_gemm"` (SM100 family, 2 and 4 GPUs, 4 geometries) | 8/8 fail (`ImportError`) | **8/8 pass** |
| Serving `vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` | serves; GSM8K 0.901 | serves (default CUDA graphs); answers correct; GSM8K 0.896 |
| Same + `FLASHINFER_MEGA_FUSED_STAGE=0` | all 4 ranks crash with the `ImportError` about 180 s into startup | reaches CUDA graph capture, then fails with `operation not permitted when stream is capturing` |
| Same + `FLASHINFER_MEGA_FUSED_STAGE=0 --compilation-config.cudagraph_mode=NONE` | — | serves (server env shows `FLASHINFER_MEGA_FUSED_STAGE=0`); answers correct; GSM8K 0.901 |

- **GSM8K:** `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-concurrency 128`, one run per row. 0.896 vs 0.901 is about 6 of 1319 questions, within the ~0.008 binomial standard error; this path never executes the changed import.
- **pytest flags:** all runs used `-v -rs --timeout=900`.
- **pre-commit:** `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes all hooks.

**Out of scope.** With `FLASHINFER_MEGA_FUSED_STAGE=0`, the DeepGEMM e2e test now gets past the import. It then fails with `RuntimeError: Inplace update to inference tensor outside InferenceMode is not allowed`. This is an interaction between vLLM's `FlashInferMoeEp.warmup` (`@torch.inference_mode()`) and the fallback's in-place copy, because the test calls forward outside inference mode afterwards. Serving runs forward under inference mode.

## Details

**Root cause.** `_expose_deep_gemm_to_flashinfer()` did `sys.modules.setdefault("deep_gemm", <vllm.third_party.deep_gemm>)`, which covers only the top-level package. When FlashInfer imports `deep_gemm.utils`:
1. Python doesn't find it in `sys.modules`, so it re-executes the vendored `utils` package as a new module named `deep_gemm.utils`.
2. That package's `layout.py` does `from .._C import ...`, which now resolves to `deep_gemm._C`. That's a cache miss, because the extension is registered as `vllm.third_party.deep_gemm._C`.
3. So the same `_C` shared object is initialized a second time, and pybind11 rejects re-registering `Runtime`.

**Where FlashInfer makes that import** (0.7.0.post1, also 0.7.1rc2):
- `fp8_fp4_bf16_deepgemm/weights.py` `_quantize_grouped_fp4`, when the weights aren't pre-quantized;
- `staging.py`'s torch fallback, used with `FLASHINFER_MEGA_FUSED_STAGE=0` or when the fused quant stage is unsupported for the input.

**Fix.** Alias every already-loaded `vllm.third_party.deep_gemm.*` module under the matching `deep_gemm.*` name. The vendored package imports `_C` at import time, so `deep_gemm._C` always resolves to the existing extension module, even if FlashInfer later imports some other submodule lazily. With a site-packages DeepGEMM the alias name equals the module name, so this is a no-op.

**Alternatives considered.**
- *A meta-path finder that redirects `deep_gemm.*`:* I rejected it. It adds a process-wide import hook and more code, and importlib would overwrite the existing module's `__spec__`.
- *A FlashInfer-side change:* FlashInfer could import only top-level `deep_gemm` attributes, which DeepGEMM re-exports. That would also avoid this, but vLLM pins 0.7.0.post1.

**Duplicate check.** `gh issue list` / `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm` searches for `already registered`, `deep_gemm`, `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` and `59904 in:body` found nothing relevant except #59904, which I filed for this bug, and #59900, where it was first noted as a follow-up.

title: [Bugfix] flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl: reject it without nvshmem4py and install nvshmem4py
body:
## Overview Fixes #59903. `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` loaded the whole checkpoint and then failed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'nvshmem'`, because `nvshmem4py` isn't installed. This PR rejects the backend at selection when `nvshmem.core` isn't usable, and installs `nvshmem4py` on Linux: `nvshmem4py-cu13` on CUDA 13 builds, `nvshmem4py-cu12` on CUDA 12 builds. The CuTeDSL path on FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 also needs #59900 (the #59887 fix), a separate PR that merges cleanly with this one; the test images below contain both. ## Claims - **Selection check:** without a usable `nvshmem4py` (`nvshmem.core`), an explicit `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` is rejected when the backend is selected, before any checkpoint shard loads, with a reason naming the package. `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` doesn't need NVSHMEM and isn't affected by the check. - **Dependency:** wheels and images depend on `nvshmem4py-cu13` (unpinned; Linux, Python < 3.14, since there are no cp314 wheels), so the resolver takes the newest release (0.4.0 as of 2026-10-10). CUDA 12 builds swap in `nvshmem4py-cu12` at the same three sites (`setup.py` and both Dockerfile blocks) that already rewrite `humming-kernels[cu13]`. - **CUDA 12.9 resolution:** `nvshmem4py-cu12` caps `cuda-python` at 12.9, so the `cuda-python` metapackage resolves to 12.9.0. `cuda-bindings` (12.9.9, within torch cu129's `>=12.9.4,<13`), torch and `nvidia-nvshmem-cu12` (3.4.5, torch's pin) are unchanged. - **Together with #59900:** in images built from this PR merged with #59900, the CuTeDSL backend needs no runtime install of `nvshmem4py`: kernel e2e tests and DEP serving pass on GB200 and GB300 (CUDA 13, including DEP=16 WideEP across 4 GB300 nodes) and 8× B200 (CUDA 12.9). The current-head serving runs also needed in-container workarounds for two unrelated `main` bugs (see Validation). ## Validation ### Retest at the current head (`1154f27`: `main` c41b2639e2 merged in, `nvshmem4py` unpinned) Images were built from `docker/Dockerfile` for `main` c41b2639e2 + this PR (`1154f27`) + #59900's 3 commits (#59900 is still needed for the CuTeDSL path on FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1), with `torch_cuda_arch_list=10.0`, no sccache and `RUN_WHEEL_CHECK=false`: - **aarch64, CUDA 13:** arm64 CI base image; targets `test` (pytest) and `vllm-openai` (serving). - **x86_64, CUDA 12.9:** built like the release pipeline's "x86_64 - CUDA 12.9" step (`CUDA_VERSION=12.9.1`, `pytorch/manylinux2_28-builder:cuda12.9-78e737ad…`, `INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=true`), target `vllm-openai`. All serving, here and in the earlier validation below, used DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `2cba9e42` and `vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --data-parallel-size --enable-expert-parallel --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --moe-backend ` with default CUDA graphs (DEP=16 adds `--data-parallel-size-local 4` and the head node's `--data-parallel-address`/`--data-parallel-rpc-port`). platform_system == "Linux" and python_version < "3.14"` | works | | aarch64 CUDA 13 `test` | `nvshmem4py-cu13` 0.4.0 | 13.0.3 / 13.0.3 (test lock) | same | works | | x86_64 CUDA 12.9 `vllm-openai` | `nvshmem4py-cu12` 0.4.0 | 12.9.0 / 12.9.9 | `nvshmem4py-cu12; `has_nvshmem4py()` is True | | `pytest kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py -k test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer` | 2/2 pass | | `pytest kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py -k "test_init_warmup and cutedsl"` (2 and 4 GPUs, 4 geometries) | **8/8 pass** | | `pytest kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py -k "test_init_warmup and deep_gemm"` | 8/8 pass | | DEP=4 serve, `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` | serves (`Using 'FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_CUTEDSL' Mxfp4 MoE backend`, FULL and PIECEWISE graphs captured); - **GSM8K:** `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-concurrency 128`, one run each (binomial standard error about 0.008 per run, about 0.012 for a difference). At the current head, with the decoder-replay patch, CuTeDSL scored 0.888 (GB200 DEP=4), 0.895 (GB300 DEP=4), 0.897 (GB300 DEP=16) and 0.893 (B200 DEP=8), in line with the earlier 0.885–0.898 (those builds predate #59532 and needed no patch). For reference, on the earlier `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` arm64 image (also before #59532; GB300 DEP=4), `deep_gemm_mega_moe` and `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` both scored 0.901. - **pytest:** run from `tests/` (as in CI) with `-v -rs --timeout=900`. - **Resolution check:** `uv pip compile` of `torch==2.13.0` + `nvshmem4py-cu12==0.4.0` for x86_64/Python 3.12 with the cu129 PyTorch index gives the CUDA 12.9 versions above. 0.4.0 is the newest `nvshmem4py-cu12`/`-cu13` release, so the unpinned requirement resolves the same way (confirmed in the images above). - **pre-commit:** `pre-commit run --files ` at `1154f27` passes all hooks. `pip-compile` leaves `requirements/test/cuda.txt` unchanged. **Not validated:** - an x86_64 CUDA 13 or aarch64 CUDA 12.9 image; - a host whose driver only supports CUDA 12 (simulated by removing CuTeDSL's `cu13` flavor); - CuTeDSL MegaMoE performance on CUDA 12; - a Python 3.14 install. ## Details **Root cause.** - **Where it's needed:** FlashInfer's CuTeDSL megakernel declares the runtime requirements `{TORCH_DIST, NVSHMEM}` (`cutedsl_runtime_requirements`). `MoEEpMegaLayer.__init__` → `bootstrap_moe_ep_runtime` → `_ensure_nvshmem` → `_init_nvshmem_after_dist` then does `import nvshmem.core`, and the kernel's comm shim also allocates its symmetric buffers through `nvshmem.core`. - **Nobody declares it:** FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 doesn't list `nvshmem4py`. 0.7.1 lists `nvshmem4py-cu13>=0.3.1` only in its `sm107` extra. - **Nobody checks for it:** vLLM's `flashinfer_moe_ep_unsupported_reasons` didn't check for the package, so the oracle accepted the backend and the failure surfaced only in `process_weights_after_loading`. **Fix.** 1. `has_nvshmem4py()` in `vllm/utils/import_utils.py`. A spec check keeps an absent package silent, and a trial import catches a broken native install. 2. A CuTeDSL-only unsupported reason in `flashinfer_moe_ep_unsupported_reasons`. The NVFP4/MXFP4 oracles turn it into a `ValueError` when the quant method is built. 3. The requirement in `requirements/cuda.txt`, which feeds both the wheel and the Docker image. The CUDA 12 paths rename it to `nvshmem4py-cu12`. **Tradeoffs.** - The requirement adds `nvshmem4py` (about 5 MB) plus `cython` to every Linux CUDA install on Python < 3.14, for an opt-in backend. If the build owners prefer a Docker-only install (like DeepEP) or an extra, it can be reduced to that, and the selection check stands on its own. - It is unpinned, so new `nvshmem4py` releases (and any change to their `cuda-python`/`cuda.core` bounds) flow in automatically; `has_nvshmem4py()` checks that `nvshmem.core` imports, not its version. A release whose `nvshmem.core` fails to import makes the backend fail selection with the reason above; a release with conflicting bounds resolves to an older `nvshmem4py`. An API break would only show up when CuTeDSL runs on SM100, which CI does not exercise (the CPU test stubs `has_nvshmem4py()`, and the kernel e2e tests are skipped without SM100). - `nvshmem4py` leaves `nvidia-nvshmem-cu1x` unpinned. torch 2.13 pins 3.4.5 for both CUDA majors, which is what was tested. - On CUDA 12 the `cuda-python<=12.9` cap is harmless with torch cu129. Without the documented cu129 index, PyPI's default (CUDA 13) `torch==2.13.0` with `nvshmem4py-cu12` still resolves, but to `cuda-python==12.6.2.post1` plus an extra `nvidia-nvshmem-cu12` 3.8.0. A cu129 vLLM wheel on CUDA 13 torch is already a mismatched environment. - FlashInfer documents `moe_ep` as CUDA 13 only, but its CuTeDSL MegaMoE path has no CUDA-version gate in 0.7.0.post1; the B200 runs above are the CUDA 12.9 evidence. - CuTeDSL loads the newest toolkit flavor the driver supports. `nvidia-cudnn-frontend` (via FlashInfer) already pulls `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]` into CUDA 12.9 images, so on R580+ drivers CuTeDSL runs its `cu13` flavor there. At the current head the B200 runs used the `cu13` flavor; in the earlier B200 validation, the kernel e2e tests (8/8) and DEP=8 serving (GSM8K 0.894) also passed with only the `cu12` flavor present. - The requirement can be dropped once FlashInfer declares the dependency for the backends vLLM uses. **CI.** - `requirements/cuda.txt`, `docker/Dockerfile` and `setup.py` trigger the full CI run. PR CI builds only CUDA 13 images; the CUDA 12 rename is exercised by the release CUDA 12.9 builds. - `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_fi_moe_ep.py`, including the new test, runs in `basic-models-test-other-cpu` (`.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml`). The kernel e2e tests need SM100 GPUs and are skipped in CI. **Duplicate check.** `gh issue list` / `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm` searches for `nvshmem4py`, `nvshmem.core`, `No module named 'nvshmem'` and `59903 in:body` found nothing relevant except #59903, which I filed for this bug, and #59900, where it was first noted as a follow-up. ---

title: [Feature][DCP] --dcp-gather: gather-based DCP for MLA attention without native DCP (+ DSv4)
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`--dcp-gather` runs decode context parallelism (DCP) for MLA models whose attention backends can't run DCP natively.
- The KV cache keeps native DCP's block-sharded layout, so capacity scales with the DCP size as usual.
- Before each layer's attention, every rank pulls the batch's pages from the other ranks into a scratch cache, and attention runs as if DCP were off. Attention backends are unmodified.
- The pull runs on a side stream through symmetric memory, overlapped with the previous layer's output projection and MoE.
- DeepSeek-V4, which has no native DCP, always uses it.

It is an alternative to layer-sharded KV (KVPP, #59059).

Related fixes, split out:
- #59951: native DCP group rank order when the group spans TP × PCP (needed for the native-DCP baseline below).
- #59961: DSv3.2 top-k across PP stages (needed for correct PP results).

## Results

All numbers are from 2026-10-06 on 4x B300, Inferact/GLM-5.3-NVFP4, 32 GiB/GPU KV budget.

- **KV capacity.** Gather-DCP holds 2.40M tokens at TP1×PCP4 and TP4. Native DCP holds 2.54M, KVPP 2.18M, and no DCP 637K.
- **Working set fits (TP1×PCP4, 24 prefixes).**
  - Gather-DCP runs at 146.0K tok/s, against 144.1K for native DCP and 142.7K for KVPP.
  - That is 2.85x no DCP (51.5K), whose 637K-token cache can't hold the 1.44M-token working set.
- **Working set near capacity (36 prefixes, 2.16M tokens).** Gather-DCP runs at 122.3K tok/s, against 127.6K for native DCP and 98.3K for KVPP.
- **Where native DCP is slow or missing.**
  - TP4: 62.2K tok/s, 1.57x native DCP (39.7K) and level with KVPP (62.2K).
  - PP2×TP2: 102.0K tok/s, 1.73x no DCP (59.0K) and level with KVPP (102.1K).
  - DeepSeek-V4 gets DCP with no attention-backend changes.
- **Overhead.** On a working set that even the replicated cache holds, gather-DCP is about 1% slower than no DCP. On an interleaved A/B it is about 2% faster than KVPP.
- **Accuracy.** GSM8K matches the baselines on GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4-Flash and DeepSeek-V2-Lite.

## Validation

GSM8K (5-shot) on 4x B300, MRV2. PP rows also include #59961.

Baselines were measured on the same day, on main or #59951, except DeepSeek-V4, which uses main without DCP.

| Model | Layout | `--dcp-gather` | Baseline |
|---|---|---:|---|
| GLM-5.3-NVFP4 | TP1×PCP4, DCP4 | 0.925, 0.920, 0.935, 0.900 (200 q each) | no DCP 0.925; native DCP 0.890, 0.920 (200 q) |
| GLM-5.3-NVFP4 | TP2×PCP2, DCP4 | 0.920 (500 q) | native DCP 0.905 (500 q) |
| GLM-5.3-NVFP4 | TP4, DCP4 | 0.915 (200 q) | native DCP 0.915 (200 q) |
| GLM-5.3-NVFP4 | PP2×TP2, DCP2 | 0.880 (200 q) | no DCP 0.875 (200 q) |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | TP4, DCP4 | 0.952 (500 q) | TP2, no DCP 0.952 (500 q) |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | TP2, DCP2 | 0.946 (500 q) | TP2, no DCP 0.952 (500 q) |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat | TP2, DCP2 | 0.640 (200 q) | no DCP 0.650 (200 q) |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat | TP2×PCP2, DCP4 | 0.630 (200 q) | TP2×PCP2, no DCP 0.630 (200 q) |

Prefill throughput on GLM-5.3-NVFP4 (4x B300, 32 GiB/GPU KV budget). Prefix-pooled prefill: 60K shared + 6K unique tokens per request, output length 1, concurrency 8.

**Interleaved A/B, TP1×PCP4.** One server per run, two runs per mode, total tok/s. Each server is warmed on 4 prefixes and runs GSM8K before the benchmarks. The 24-prefix working set is 1.44M tokens. The 6-prefix sets (seeds 5 and 7, 12 prompts per prefix) fit every cache, including the replicated one.

| Mode | 24 prefixes | 6 prefixes, seed 5 | 6 prefixes, seed 7 | KV cache (tokens) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| No DCP | 51,526 | 209,660 | 210,356 | 636,928 |
| KVPP (#59059) | 144,581 / 144,326 | 203,665 / 203,410 | 203,695 / 203,839 | 2,182,528 |
| `--dcp-gather` | **146,993 / 147,166** | **207,461 / 207,604** | **208,345 / 208,060** | 2,400,510 |

**Layouts.** One server per row, total tok/s for 6 prompts per prefix, run after GSM8K. TP1×PCP4 runs eager because PCP requires it. TP4 and PP2×TP2 use the default CUDA-graph mode; gather mode runs PIECEWISE. Native DCP uses `--dcp-comm-backend ag_rs`.

| Layout | Mode | 24 prefixes | 36 prefixes | KV cache (tokens) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TP1×PCP4 | No DCP | 51,526 | | 636,928 |
| TP1×PCP4 | Native DCP4 (#59951) | 144,131 | **127,610** | 2,540,936 |
| TP1×PCP4 | KVPP (#59059) | 142,717 | 98,273 | 2,182,528 |
| TP1×PCP4 | `--dcp-gather`, DCP4 | **146,035** | 122,330 | 2,400,510 |
| TP4 | Native DCP4 | 39,716 | | 2,540,936 |

| TP4 | `--dcp-gather`, DCP4 | 62,204 | | 2,400,510 |
| PP2×TP2 | No DCP | 58,961 | | 1,264,448 |

The TP1×PCP4 no-DCP row is from the A/B harness above.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_generic_kvp.py  # 1 passed
```

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0 vllm serve Inferact/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 1 -pcp 4 -dcp 4 --dcp-gather \
  --enable-expert-parallel -cc.cudagraph_mode=NONE --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --enable-prefix-caching \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-model-len 72000 --max-num-seqs 64 --kv-cache-memory-bytes 32G
# Other layouts: -tp 4 -dcp 4 --dcp-gather, or -pp 2 -tp 2 -dcp 2 --dcp-gather (no -pcp, default CUDA graphs)
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash -tp 4 -dcp 4 \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 64 --enable-prefix-caching
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 500 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256
vllm bench serve --port 8000 --model Inferact/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --dataset-name prefix_repetition \
  --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 60000 --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 6000 \
  --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 24 --prefix-repetition-output-len 1 --num-prompts 144 --max-concurrency 8 --seed 1
```
</details>

## How it works

- **KV layout.** The engine plans the KV cache exactly as for native DCP: a block spans `N` pages, and rank `r` stores page `r`. Scheduler, prefix caching and block IDs are unchanged; there are no engine or scheduler changes.
- **Worker.** Gather mode sets the worker's DCP size to 1 before distributed init, so attention runs unsharded. The KV cache is allocated from torch's symmetric-memory pool so that peers can read it directly. Every layer with the same cache shape shares one scratch cache with `N`x the blocks; kernel block `b*N + r` is page `r` of block `b`.
- **Per forward,** on one side stream, in layer order:
  1. Pull layer 0's pages of the batch's blocks from every rank.
  2. When layer `l` releases its cache (after its attention), copy this rank's pages of the blocks the forward wrote back to its own cache, then pull layer `l+1`.
  3. Layer `l` acquires its cache (waits for its pull) before its first KV access, then writes its new KV into the scratch cache as usual.
  4. One symmetric-memory barrier per forward orders peers' reads of the write-backs against block reuse.
- **Data movement.** New tokens need no communication: every rank computes all of them (the MLA latent is replicated under TP, and PCP gathers KV before the insert). Each rank pulls the other `(N−1)/N` of the old tokens, which is the minimum. Blocks shared by several requests are copied once.
- **Hooks.** Layers call `acquire`/`release` around their KV accesses in the generic MLA cache-update and attention ops, the sparse indexer, DSv3.2's attention and DSv4's attention. The model runner builds the runtime with the KV cache and calls it once per step.
- **Capacity.** One scratch cache per cache shape comes out of the KV budget. For GLM-5.3 at `N=4` that leaves 2.40M tokens, versus KVPP's 2.18M and native DCP's 2.54M.

**Size.** About 480 lines including the unit test; about 280 of them in the new `generic_kvp.py`. No engine, scheduler, `vllm/distributed` or attention-backend changes.

## Limitations

- **Single NVLink domain only** (symmetric memory).
- **MRV2 and MLA caches only.** FULL CUDA graphs are downgraded to PIECEWISE.
- **Rejected at startup:** spec decode, DBO/microbatching, elastic EP, in-process executors and sleep mode.
- **Not yet supported:** layerwise KV connectors, HiSparse, and DSv4 with PCP (main has no DSv4 PCP; see #59857).
- **Decode** pulls the full history every step. The target is prefill (e.g. P/D prefill nodes); use native DCP for decode where it is supported.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR implements generic gather-based DCP. #59059 (KVPP) is the layer-sharded alternative compared here. #57239, #44573 and #56738 add native DeepSeek-V4 DCP through backend or kernel changes.
