title: [Kernel] Add opt-in LiteTopK FP32 decode with producer histograms
body:
Thanks to @TKONIY for the collaboration on this work.

## Overview

Add opt-in producer-assisted LiteTopK for paged FP8/FP32 decode and verify,
ported from the SGLang decode work. Requires
[DeepGEMM #24](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/24).
This description includes the optimized companion producer measurements;
the vLLM FP32 integration needs no additional code change.

## Claims

- Supports the H32/D128, page64, top2048 SM100-family decode contract for n=1..4.
- Selects exact logical indices with lower-index tie breaking and persistent
  workspace; preserves prefill, explicit backend and unsupported-path fallbacks.
- The updated companion removes repeated varlen histogram flushes for n>1.

## Validation

B200 (148 SMs), Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12.3, PDL enabled.
Three isolated process blocks per version; nine shuffled CUDA-graph samples per
block. Captured GLM-5.2/DSpark operands use distinct KV replicas totaling at least
256 MiB. Timings include metadata generation/copy once per eight layers and are
reported per layer. They exclude the rest of the model and are not serving
latency. Across all 40 shapes, live logits, exact histograms and logical-index
selection agree between submitted and optimized versions in all 240 cases.
The full grid with ranges, the method and the validation record are below.


| dtype | B | n | context | submitted µs | optimized µs | old/new | default/new |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fp32 | 1 | 4 | 1048320 | 65.637 | 39.280 | 1.671x | 1.565x |
| fp32 | 4 | 4 | 1048320 | 222.181 | 116.323 | 1.910x | 1.511x |

The updated producer suite passed 8 FP32 native/varlen cases, including live
length and request-ID changes during graph replay. The combined route suite
passed 18 cases; the unchanged native selector passed its 30-case suite during
the original migration. Commands:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_litetopk_decode.py -v -s
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_litetopk_decode.py --widths 8192 65536 262144 1048576 --requests 1 4 --repeats 5
```

The repository benchmark is a hot per-layer check and excludes shared metadata.
The table above comes from the metadata-inclusive captured benchmark below. Some 8K shapes remain slower than default.

DeepGEMM was rebuilt from the companion changes. vLLM validation
used current Python source, the separately compiled selector, and unchanged
binaries from `f944491db`; this was not a full exact-base wheel build.
The complete draft-test module is unavailable because the generated FlashMLA
Python interface is missing; the two modified cases and actual metadata builder
were executed through narrow imports. Applicable lint/type checks and clean
patch-application/tree checks passed.

**Model evaluation:** not completed. The available model weights total
510,296,708,312 bytes, more than the single ~179 GiB B200 I had for this.
No output-quality, speculative-acceptance or end-to-end serving gain is claimed.
Full model evaluation remains required before merge.


<details>
<summary>Full FP32 results, method and validation record</summary>

Geometric means over the FP32 grid (B={1,4}, n={1,4}, context {8192, 65536, 262144, 1048320}):

| dtype | cells | submitted / optimized | default / submitted | default / optimized |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fp32 | 16 | 1.164x | 1.128x | 1.311x |

| dtype | B | n | context | submitted µs | optimized µs | old/new | default/new |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fp32 | 1 | 1 | 8192 | 9.926 [9.549, 10.124] | 9.847 [9.748, 10.227] | 1.008x | 0.942x |

title: [Kernel] Extend LiteTopK decode to BF16 V4.1 top512 and next_n 1-6
body:
Thanks to @TKONIY for the collaboration on this work.

Stacked on [vLLM #59921](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59921): the first commit belongs to that PR, so please review the other two.

## Overview

Extend [vLLM #59921](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59921) with
MXFP4/BF16 top512 decode for n=1..6, ported from
[SGLang #42351](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42351).
Requires [DeepGEMM #25](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/25),
stacked on [#24](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/24).

## Claims

- Supports page128 H32/D128 MXFP4 decode and exact top512 of BF16 producer scores.
- Builds the paired split384 schedule from final live lengths/IDs once per
  metadata group and reuses it across layers, including draft updates and graphs.
- Uses direct FP32 input weights for n=1..5 with the new producer capability;
  preserves the explicit BF16 cast for n=6 and for older DeepGEMM versions.
- Preserves BF16 candidate publication, mask-consumer and explicit-backend fallbacks.

## Validation

B200 (148 SMs), Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12.3, PDL enabled.
Three isolated process blocks per version; nine shuffled CUDA-graph samples per
block. Captured GLM-5.2/DSpark operands use distinct KV replicas totaling at least
256 MiB. Timings include metadata generation/copy once per eight layers and are
reported per layer. They exclude the rest of the model and are not serving
latency. Across all 40 shapes, live logits, exact histograms and logical-index
selection agree between submitted and optimized versions in all 240 cases.
The full grid with ranges, the method and the validation record are below.


| dtype | B | n | context | submitted µs | optimized µs | old/new | default/new |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| bf16 | 1 | 1 | 8192 | 12.213 | 8.833 | 1.383x | 1.021x |
| bf16 | 1 | 1 | 65536 | 14.444 | 11.580 | 1.247x | 1.339x |
| bf16 | 4 | 4 | 1048320 | 76.814 | 71.796 | 1.070x | 1.923x |
| bf16 | 4 | 6 | 1048320 | 96.479 | 92.879 | 1.039x | 1.849x |
| bf16 | 1 | 6 | 8192 | 15.418 | 13.471 | 1.145x | 0.775x |

The final stack passed 32 producer cases (24 BF16 dtype/PDL/n combinations),
18 actual sparse-indexer route cases, the actual compressed/ragged metadata
builder with changing graph inputs, and two draft metadata-update cases.
The unchanged selector passed 30 cases during the initial migration.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_litetopk_decode.py -v -s
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py -k capture_safe -v -s
```

The second command is the full-environment reproduction target; my run used
the narrow-import execution described below, not full-module pytest.
Short contexts still include regressions against default; results do not
justify enabling this backend by default.

DeepGEMM was rebuilt from the companion changes. vLLM validation
used current Python source, the separately compiled selector, and unchanged
binaries from `f944491db`; this was not a full exact-base wheel build.
The complete draft-test module is unavailable because the generated FlashMLA
Python interface is missing; the two modified cases and actual metadata builder
were executed through narrow imports. Applicable lint/type checks and clean
patch-application/tree checks passed.

**Model evaluation:** not completed. The available model weights total
510,296,708,312 bytes, more than the single ~179 GiB B200 I had for this.
No output-quality, speculative-acceptance or end-to-end serving gain is claimed.
Full model evaluation remains required before merge.

**n=6.** The first direct-FP32-weight n=6 variant regressed on long B=4 decode. The earlier implementation launched split384 metadata and a weight cast in every
layer. The builder now maintains stable schedule storage after flattening,
compression and final request IDs, with refreshes for draft steps. Standalone
calls without a shared schedule still build fresh metadata.

FP32 weights are rounded inside the producer with the same BF16 rule as an
explicit cast. A three-arm captured-data probe found a long-context regression
for the n=6 swizzled direct-weight kernel. n=6 therefore retains packed BF16
weights while benefiting from schedule reuse; this avoids a context-dependent
host read and preserves the score contract.

title: [DeepSeek-V4-P3] deterministic MoE DeepEP
body:
## Overview

Wire DeepSeek-V4's supported MoE/DeepEP low-latency path for batch-invariant execution. Stable expert selection, token-local quantization, rank-synchronous dispatch capacity, and graph-safe metadata are separate parts of the contract; unsupported kernels fail closed.

- Use the supported DeepGEMM expert backend and stable router GEMM. Align masked/contiguous SiLU x Mul FP8 scales, routed-expert clamp, and accumulation.
- Stage DeepEP LL dispatch at `VLLM_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` (default **128**). The rank-wide token maximum sets the stage count, so empty tail stages still join collectives. Shared experts run once for the full local batch.
- Avoid live GPU-to-host expert maxima during graph capture; choose the shared-expert auxiliary stream on MNNVL only when its preconditions hold.

## Architecture

![DeepSeek-V4 MoE and rank-synchronous DeepEP staging](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/inaniloquentee/d5a1e05c74fddb335aa38a58bf30fb4f/raw/7970e2de8109265c8b1c62eeb723f57e76cf7b1c/ds4-p3-deepep-moe-architecture.svg)

## Test

The stable `_C` extension rebuilt on an **unpublished** current-`main` merge candidate on H20. Targeted sparse-index, top-k, paged/contiguous logits, and MoE dispatch checks: **16 passed, 2 skipped**. The two skips require a DeepGEMM build with batch-invariant masked-grouped controls absent from the currently pinned package. These are not CI results on the current PR head. Multi-rank DeepEP staging and full-model evaluation remain unrun; this PR does not claim train/rollout equivalence.

### Perf

The shared-expert stream commit reported **17,036 -> 18,150 tok/s (+6.5%)** on DS4-Flash/GB200. It was not rerun for this PR, and the report lacks GPU count, workload, and variance. This is not an end-to-end gain for the whole MoE path.

title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Flash tool-call format failures associated with prefix-cache reuse; worst for short cached head + long uncached suffix; `cache_salt` reduces failures but is confounded with hit shape (v0.27.1, fp8 KV, MTP)
body:
## Summary

Intermittent tool-call formatting failures with DeepSeek-V4-Flash on vLLM v0.27.1 (fp8 KV cache, prefix caching, MTP speculative decoding), observed over ~3 weeks in an agentic workload.

What we measured, in decreasing order of confidence:

1. **Failures were concentrated on requests that reused prefix cache, and were replica-local.** Production first turns with `cache_read_input_tokens = 0` had 0 failures in two pre-mitigation samples (0 / 83 and 0 / 67), but cold requests were not failure-free everywhere: 2 / 83 in direct replays (both no-tool class, 0 strict) and 3 / 59 among post-mitigation cold first turns. The same request set on two replicas at the same time: 0 / 35 vs 17 / 19.
2. **Among cache-reading first turns, failure rate depended strongly on hit shape.** Same day, same tool set, thinking enabled, before mitigation, both replicas pooled: hit of only the ~3.6k-token shared tool-schema head followed by 40–70k uncached prompt tokens failed **41 / 65 (63%)**; hit of >30k tokens with a short uncached suffix failed **22 / 96 (23%)**. On the one replica with enough data: 23 / 34 vs 5 / 38.
3. **A dedicated `cache_salt` namespace reduced failures** (direct replay 0 / 37 vs 44 / 55; production first turns 35/138 → 3/203 after the change). But in our replay design the salted requests were all long hits over blocks the replay itself had written cold, and the unsalted ones were head-only hits over shared blocks. **The comparison therefore confounds three variables — hit shape, the computation path of the blocks being read (cold-computed vs. computed on top of a hit), and replica state — and does not isolate any of them.**

An earlier hypothesis of ours (cached head blocks drifting through repeated rewrites on top of partial hits) was tested against logs and **not supported**: first turns that read the shared head within 10 minutes of an observed cold recomputation of that prefix still failed 33 / 82. It is not excluded, because we have no per-block lineage instrumentation.

We do not know the mechanism. This report lists the observations, the checks, the confounds we could not remove, and the experiment we would run.

## Environment

- vLLM **v0.27.1**, torch 2.13.0, transformers 5.15.0
- Model: **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** (fp8 weights; fp4 experts via the MARLIN MXFP4 backend on SM90). Exact checkpoint revision not recorded.
- Two independent replicas, each **8 × H100 80GB, TP=8**, no KV sharing between replicas. Identical settings:
  - `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`
  - `--speculative-config '{"method":"deepseek_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`
  - `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"}'`
  - `--max-model-len 524288`, `--reasoning-parser deepseek_v4`, `--enable-auto-tool-choice` with a custom tool parser plugin (a fallback parser that also rescues some non-DSML tool syntax)
  - prefix caching enabled (default), chunked prefill 8,192, block size 256, `prefix_caching_hash_algo=sha256`, async scheduling enabled (default)
- Attention path: FlashMLA sparse fp8 kernels, indexer top-k 512. Engine startup lists five KV-cache groups (compressed KV C4A/C128A, SWA KV, compressor state, indexer KV).
- Sampling: the client omits `temperature`/`top_p`. We did not verify the effective values on the server (checkpoint `generation_config.json` or server overrides). No temperature-0 comparison was run.
- **Production path:** application → gateway → load balancer → vLLM native Anthropic `/v1/messages`, streaming, thinking enabled, 16–18 tools, first-turn prompts 40k–75k tokens. Requests with the same tool set share a ~3.6k-token prefix (tool schemas), so first-turn `cache_read_input_tokens` is typically exactly 3,584 (16-tool set) or 4,608 (18-tool set), or 0.
- **Replay path:** requests converted with vLLM's own Anthropic→chat conversion and sent directly to each replica's `/v1/chat/completions` (bypassing the load balancer), `return_token_ids` requested. Prompt **token counts** matched the original requests in 123 / 123 replays; token-ID-level equality of the rendered prompt was not checked. Format classification was made on the response content after `</think>` (DSML tags visible as text in the content). Whether the classification code used returned output token IDs or the content string is not recoverable from the logs we still hold.

## Failure definition

A thinking-enabled request with tools is counted as failed when any of:

- **dialect** — the text contains a non-DSML tool-call syntax (`<tool_call>`, `<function …>`, `<｜DSML｜tool name=…>`, …) and the response has no `tool_use` block;
- **rescued** — `stop_reason = tool_use` but no `tool_use` block (the fallback parser rescued a non-DSML call; the Anthropic stream converter then dropped the id-less tool call — see below). The underlying output was non-DSML;
- **no-tool** — `stop_reason = end_turn` with no `tool_use` block on a first turn (≤3 messages).

The no-tool class is workload-specific: in this agent the first turn is expected to act through tools, and inspected cases end with text announcing an action ("I'll check … first") without calling anything. We cannot rule out that some are legitimate text answers, so every table below also gives the **strict** count (dialect + rescued only). A cache-free canary request run periodically against the same replicas scored 0.6% under the full definition. Gateway-side labels and the independently computed labels used here agreed on 2,120 / 2,120 joined records.

## Observed behavior

Text is otherwise coherent (no garbage tokens, no unexpected CJK). In inspected failures the visible deviation starts at the first token after `</think>`; this identifies the visible symptom, not the first point where internal state differed.

Rates varied widely across windows: ~0.01% in quiet periods; hourly first-turn failure median 0.0% (47 h) before an incident vs 13.8% (43 h, max 52%) during it. Failures dropped to ~0 immediately after restarting an affected replica; on another occasion they declined within a day without a restart.

## Direct replays (same prompts, conditions varied)

31 first-turn prompts that had failed in production, thinking enabled, replayed directly against the replicas. Rows are separate comparisons; do not pool.

| Comparison | Condition | Fail / n |
|---|---|---:|
| 2×2, no salt | cold (`cache_read = 0`) | 1 / 23 (no-tool) |
| 2×2, no salt | cache hit (shared namespace; first rep hits the ~3.6k head, later reps hit the previous rep's full prompt) | **44 / 55** |
| 2×2, salted | cold | 1 / 60 (no-tool) |
| 2×2, salted | cache hit (own namespace, written cold by the first salted rep; median hit 46,592, max 74,752) | **0 / 37** |
| Interleaved, same 12-min window, same two replicas | no salt | 10 / 12 |
| Interleaved, same window | salted | 0 / 36 |
| Same inputs concurrently | replica A (healthy at the time) | 0 / 35 |
| Same inputs concurrently | replica B | 17 / 19 |
| Replica A, ~15 min later, during a burst of ~35 cold 60k-token replays | no salt | 22 / 27 |
| "Tail fresh": head cached, tail forced to recompute from token ~36.7k | no salt; the 7 requests whose hit actually covered the head | 7 / 7 |

Two details that do not fit a single-variable story:

- 16 same-replica, same-input pairs had one failure and one success. In one pair the hit lengths were 62,464 (fail) and 62,720 (ok) — a **long** unsalted hit failed. In the unsalted condition, those long hits read blocks written by the previous replay rep, which had itself been computed on top of a head hit; in the salted condition, long hits read blocks written cold.
- The salted and unsalted arms were never matched on hit shape: salted = long hit over cold-written blocks; unsalted = head-only hit over shared blocks (first rep) or long hit over hit-derived blocks (later reps).

## Production, by hit shape (gateway records)

Definitions: `cache_read_input_tokens` is taken from the usage the gateway recorded for each response (streaming usage merged by the gateway; we did not re-verify that code for this report). Records with the field missing were kept as null and excluded (35 of 10,636), not treated as 0. Uncached suffix = `input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens` (prompt tokens actually prefilled). Prompt total = sum of the three.

**Before mitigation, one day, 16-tool set, thinking enabled, first turns (≤3 messages), both replicas pooled** (replica identity known for about half the records):

| `cache_read` | Uncached suffix (min / median / max) | Prompt total (median) | Fail / n | Strict (dialect+rescued) | n_msg = 1 only |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 (cold) | 40.7k / 58.5k / 75.3k | 58.5k | **0 / 28** | 0 / 28 | 0 / 20 |
| = 3,584 (shared head only) | 43.2k / 54.2k / 73.5k | 57.8k | **41 / 65 (63%)** | 17 / 65 (26%) | 39 / 58 |
| 10k–30k | 26k / 28k / 36k | 57.8k | 5 / 6 | — | 5 / 5 |
| > 30k (long hit) | 78 / 504 / 34.4k | 60.6k | **22 / 96 (23%)** | 5 / 96 (5%) | 18 / 40 |

Per replica where known: head-only 23 / 34 vs long-hit 5 / 38 on the affected replica; 1 / 4 vs 1 / 2 on the other. Cold first turns across all tool sets that day: 0 / 67 (thinking enabled).

The two hit-shape buckets differ in more than hit length: head-only requests are almost all first messages (58 / 65), long-hit requests are mostly third messages (56 / 96, i.e. a correct DSML example may be in context). Restricting to n_msg = 1 narrows the gap (67% vs 45%) but does not remove it.

An unconditioned view of the same day (all tool sets, thinking on and off, before and after mitigation; 916 first turns) shows **no** gradient: ≤3,584 → 26 / 181 (14.4%), 3,585–4,608 → 9 / 18, >4,608 → 88 / 634 (13.9%), cold 0 / 83. The gradient appears only after conditioning on thinking-enabled, one tool set, and pre-mitigation. We report both.

**After mitigation (run-scoped salt), same day, 16-tool set, thinking enabled, first turns:** cold 3 / 59 (1 rescued, 2 no-tool; prompts 55k–75k, single-message), own-namespace hit = 3,584 → 0 / 40, own-namespace hit > 30k → 0 / 12. Later turns in their own namespace: 0 / 52. The incident was also fading during this period, so these are not matched controls.

## Test of the "head rewrite accumulation" hypothesis (log analysis)

Hypothesis: head blocks are repeatedly recomputed on top of partial hits during pool churn and drift; readers of a many-times-rewritten head fail. Predictions: (1) readers of a head recomputed cold shortly before should rarely fail; (2) failure should rise after partial head rewrites; (3) rise with rewrite count.

Method: gateway records joined to load-balancer logs that carry replica identity. LB log: 2,176 rows (21 without tools). Gateway records inside the LB time window: 2,145; 19 without tools excluded → 2,126; matched 1:1 on end time ±3 s plus exact input and output token counts → 2,120; 6 unmatched; 0 with more than one candidate; each LB row used once. The 99.7% is the match rate of those 2,126, not a statement about traffic capture. Replica identity is therefore available for 3.3 h; the rest of the day is analyzed without it. "Writers" of a prefix are requests of the same tool set with `cache_read` below the head length; a reader is a first turn with `cache_read ≥` head length. Lineage is inferred from timing on the same replica — **physical block identity was not verified**, and vLLM can hold duplicate blocks for one hash.

- (1) Readers whose most recent observed same-prefix writer on that replica was a **cold** request within the previous 10 min: **33 / 82 (40%)** failed in production, 30 / 35 in replay. Predicted ≈0.
- (2) Partial head rewrites (0 < `cache_read` < head) were rare: 7 in 8.7 h; in the replica-identified window 2, with no readers after them. Not testable with power.
- (3) Readers with ≥1 inferred rewrite: 0 / 4.
- Most direct sequence (replay, one replica): T+0 `cache_read = 0` (ok) → T+2m24s `cache_read = 3,584` (fail) → T+4m03s (fail); no intermediate writer in the logs we hold. T+4m22s cold (ok) → T+7m40s, T+7m57s (fail).
- Cold recomputation of the shared head was observed roughly every 3 min on both replicas (median 2.8–3.5 min). We did not instrument eviction; this shows repeated cache misses on the same prefix, not pool state.

We treat the accumulation hypothesis as not supported by this analysis and not excluded.

## Other production observations

- Low concurrency did not protect: 8.8% at concurrency 1–2 vs 0.1% at 25–48 (observational strata, different windows).
- Active KV usage ≤35%, `num_preemptions_total` 0, waiting ≤1, ECC errors 0 in the monitored window.
- Thinking disabled: 0 failures / 855 (separate observation).
- If the previous turn in a conversation had failed, the next turn failed 57.6%; otherwise 7.8% (dialect text left in history; causal effect not isolated).
- Side finding, separate from the cache question: when the fallback tool parser rescues a non-DSML call during streaming, it emits a `DeltaToolCall` without an `id`; the Anthropic stream converter in v0.27.1 only opens a `tool_use` block when `tool_call.id` is present, so the client receives `stop_reason = tool_use` with no tool block. These are the "rescued" cases above. We can file this separately if useful.

## What we checked (static reads of v0.27.1) and what remains open

- **Hashing:** sha256 chain over (parent hash, 256 token ids, extra keys). Prompt token counts matched in replay; no evidence of a collision; block contents not validated.
- **Block registration vs. execution:** blocks registered in `allocate_slots()` before the forward; with async scheduling the worker executes scheduled tokens before an abort is processed; no KV connector. Code reading only.
- **Hybrid cache-hit coordination:** `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit` converges hit lengths across groups with 256-token alignment. A final hit length of 0 is the coordinated result; it does not by itself say every group's blocks were absent. Runtime restoration of the five groups not independently validated.
- **Batch invariance:** under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, v0.27.1 force-disables prefix caching for the TRITON_MLA and FLASHINFER MLA backends ([`mla_attention.py#L466-L479`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6e448d0ea9bf3d88d898b65449ca6dc2aec170ac/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py#L466-L479)). This is a support limitation, not evidence of an error on FlashMLA sparse, which the check does not cover. We have not measured any cold-vs-hit numerical difference in our setup.
- **Request path:** replays bypassed the load balancer; the Anthropic→chat conversion (offline) and the chat endpoint's own template/parser remained in the path. Non-DSML syntax was visible in the response text itself.
- **Replica state:** the same hit shape failed 63% on one replica and 0 / 35 on the other at the same time. "Incident state" is a label for something we cannot observe, not an explanation.

**What the data cannot separate:** (a) hit shape — short cached head followed by a long uncached suffix; (b) the computation path of the blocks being read — computed cold vs. computed on top of a hit (own-namespace long hits over cold-written blocks: 0 / 37, 0 / 52; shared-namespace long hits over hit-derived blocks: 23%, plus the 62,464-token failure); (c) replica state. Each of the three is consistent with the salt effect.

## Working hypotheses — not verified

1. Numerical differences between cold prefill and cache-hit continuation (fp8 KV, sparse MLA, chunked prefill over a short cached prefix, MTP), possibly re-registered into the cache and re-read, amplified by some replica state. No KV drift, indexer selection or logprob divergence has been measured. We are not asserting which kernel path is involved.
2. A cache-state restoration or MTP lookahead/last-block interaction affecting one or more hybrid groups (`_annotate_eagle_groups_deepseek_v4` carries a FIXME in v0.27.1).
3. An integration issue in the parser/endpoint path (not eliminated; the rescued-call `id` issue above is a confirmed, separate integration defect).

This report concerns output correctness; the evidence does not establish cross-user data disclosure or adversarial cache poisoning.

## Questions

1. Are there known v0.27.x correctness issues for DeepSeek-V4-Flash prefix-cache reuse with fp8 KV, in particular when a short cached prefix is followed by a long chunked prefill (restoration of compressed KV, compressor state or indexer KV)?
2. Is #55390 "[Bugfix] Annotate MTP draft KV cache groups positionally on the hybrid grouping path" (merged 2026-09-22) relevant to this configuration (DeepSeek MTP, hybrid groups), and in which release? We are asking about relevance, not claiming it fixes this.
3. #51843 "[Bugfix] Disable fine-grained prefix-cache hits for incompatible hybrid KV layouts" (merged 2026-08-12) and #58368 "[Bugfix][Mamba] Restore prompt-tail prefix-cache hits with MTP" (merged 2026-09-24; described as addressing a Mamba/GDN regression from #55390) — does either change cache-hit behavior for this layout? Is there a recommended version?
4. Is there a supported way to record block lineage (cold vs. hit-path computed) or to verify restoration of each hybrid group at runtime?
5. How would you recommend a matched cold-vs-hit comparison for MLA + fp8 KV: (i) free-generation format failure rate, and separately (ii) logits at a fixed, identical continuation through the tool-format boundary, while keeping the cache-hit path engaged?

## Experiment we would run (no hardware access at present)

Goal: separate hit shape from block provenance under controlled cache state, on a replica in the affected state and on a quiet one.

For each trial, generate a **new** `cache_salt` so the namespace starts empty, then:

- **A — cold:** send the measurement prompt P directly.
- **B — short hit:** first send a request whose rendered prompt is exactly the first ~3.6k tokens of P (verify with `/tokenize` that it is a token prefix of P after the chat template), then send P.
- **C — long hit:** first send a request whose rendered prompt is P minus its final block(s) (same verification), then send P.

The measurement request is identical P in all arms (no appended assistant turns). Randomize arm order per prompt, use ≥10 independent prompts, and record per trial: actual `cache_read`, requested vs. realised hit length (MTP and per-group alignment may change it), raw output tokens, and the first-token logits after `</think>` under a fixed thinking continuation for the logits comparison. A new salt separates lookups; it does not reset physical buffers or process state, so also log replica-level counters per arm. Read: B ≫ A ≈ C supports hit-shape dependence under these conditions (not a kernel-level cause); B ≈ C > A points at the hit path generally; all ≈ 0 is a failed reproduction. 30 trials per arm is a starting point, not a power guarantee. We would not enable dev mode or reset caches on production replicas for this.

## Related reports (symptom-level, not confirmed duplicates)

- #53257 — DeepSeek-V4-Flash family non-determinism on v0.27.1 (B300, TP=1, NVFP4, DSpark; setup differs)
- #33123 — cache-hit vs. cold logprob divergence (ROCm/MI355X, Qwen3-0.6B)
- #47194, #53912, #43559 — prefix caching + speculative decoding on Qwen hybrid models
- #55766 — Qwen GDN: corrupted block re-cached after a hit; `cache_salt` as workaround
- #16016 — cache-salting RFC (the sharing boundary used here)

We can share field definitions, denominators and aggregation rules, and discuss a sanitized replay harness. Production prompts, token-ID sequences, raw thinking, tool arguments/results, credentials and live salt values are excluded.

title: [KV Connector] Support sleep mode with MooncakeStoreConnector
body:
## Purpose

Stacked on #59625; only the last commit is new.

MooncakeStoreConnector registers the GPU KV cache with the Mooncake store (`register_buffer`). Over RDMA, that registration pins the physical pages. Sleep mode unmaps the KV cache, and wake maps new pages at the same virtual addresses. The store keeps using the old pages, so puts and gets read and write memory the model no longer uses.

Evidence on main (GB300, Qwen3-8B, two instances sharing one store; instance A sleeps at level 1, instance B never sleeps):

- After the wake, every store hit on A gives wrong output: 0/8 for KV that B put, and 0/8 for A's own post-wake puts.
- A's puts after the wake store stale bytes. B reads them and also returns wrong output (0/8), even though B never slept.
- While asleep, A still holds 67.8 GB of GPU memory, because the KV cache stays pinned. After the wake it holds 150.8 GB (85.4 GB before the sleep).
- There are no errors and no log lines.

With #59625 alone, this combination is refused at startup ("MooncakeStoreConnector does not support sleep mode").

This PR implements the #59625 hooks for MooncakeStoreConnector:

- `release_kv_caches()` runs before the KV cache is unmapped. It waits until the put queue and the shared get queue have no queued or running tasks, then calls `unregister_buffer` on each device KV region. All store puts and gets run on those queues; lookups only query keys.
  - The wait is bounded by `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` (480 s by default), the same bound `MooncakeConnector` uses for its release in #59625. That is well above Mooncake's 60 s per-transfer timeout, so a slow queue does not fail the sleep. On timeout it raises `TimeoutError` and keeps the registration. The wait shares one helper with `close()`.
- `restore_kv_caches()` runs after the KV cache is mapped again. It registers the same addresses and lengths.
- Both calls are all or nothing and idempotent. If an (un)register call fails partway, the calls already made are undone and the error is raised. A failed sleep leaves the engine awake and fully registered; a failed wake leaves the regions released, so a retry starts clean.
- Host-resident (HiSparse) regions are host memory, which sleep does not touch, so they stay registered.
- `supports_sleep_mode()` reads the protocol from the Mooncake config file (`MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`). The workers use the same file to set up the store. It accepts `rdma` and `tcp` and refuses other configured protocols. The check runs only when sleep mode is enabled, and it does not import mooncake. If the config is missing, startup fails with the existing "MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH is not set" error.
  - Why RDMA and TCP: no peer holds a key to our KV cache. Puts and gets use our local lkey against peers' host-DRAM segments, so registering again locally is enough.
  - TCP registration only records the address range. Data moves with `cudaMemcpy` on the virtual address, and nothing is pinned.
  - Other configured protocols (e.g. nvlink) can export handles to peers, so they stay refused.
  - It also refuses when `MC_FORCE_MNNVL` or `MC_INTRANODE_NVLINK` is set. Mooncake then installs an nvlink transport even with `protocol: rdma`. Like Mooncake, it checks only that the variable is set, not its value.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests (CPU, fake store), one per invariant:
  - Release and restore round-trip exactly the device regions, with the same addresses and lengths (dense layout, and HiSparse with one host group plus one device group). Both calls are idempotent across two cycles.
  - Release waits for a queued or running put or get. A real thread finishes the task when a `threading.Event` is set. A timeout keeps the registration.
  - A failed unregister or register is rolled back, and a retry then succeeds.
  - The config gate: rdma/tcp accepted; nvlink, `MC_FORCE_MNNVL` (also `=0`) and `MC_INTRANODE_NVLINK` refused; missing config. Mooncake is blocked from import.
- Mutation check: each piece of the change was altered on its own (gate and each env var, region recording, host skip, idempotence, state, lengths, rollback, each drained queue, the bound, the deadline). 23 mutants, all killed, and every test kills at least one.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/{test_config,test_mooncake_store_*,test_mooncake_connector,test_multi_connector}.py tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py`. The store tests were also run 5 times. pre-commit was run on the changed files.
- Hardware (GB300, Mooncake 0.3.13.post1, RDMA, standalone `mooncake_master`, Qwen3-8B):
  - Two servers share one store: A sleeps and B never sleeps. GPU prefix caching is off, so every cached token comes from the store.
  - 8 random 2048-token prompts per phase, greedy decoding, 32 output tokens.
  - After every cycle: A gets KV that B put, B gets KV that A put after the wake, and A gets its own post-wake put back.
  - Cycles: 3× `/sleep?level=1` + `/wake_up`; 1× level-1 sleep then `/wake_up?tags=weights` and `/wake_up?tags=kv_cache`; 1× `/pause` + `/release_kv_cache_memory` + `/wake_up?tags=kv_cache`.
  - Control run: `/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true` at the same points. This performs the same store wipe as sleep, without unmapping anything.

## Test Result

- Unit tests (`test_config`, `test_mooncake_store_worker`, `test_mooncake_connector`, `test_multi_connector`, `test_sleep_mode_backend`): 407 passed, 2 failed. The 2 failures are in `test_multi_connector.py` and are unrelated to this change: one needs the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`, the other needs `ray`, which is not installed. They fail the same way on #59625 alone. All `test_mooncake_store_*` files: 332 passed in each of the 5 runs.
- Hardware, sleep run vs awake control: 224/224 outputs are token-for-token identical across all 28 phases. Every hit read 2032 tokens from the store.
  - Before this change, each post-wake hit phase was 0/8.
  - Each run also compares hits with the cold output of the same prompt. A few phases there show 7/8, and the control run shows exactly the same mismatches. These come from near-tie prompts where a store hit and a cold prefill differ, not from sleep.

| GPU memory on A | this PR | main (earlier run) |
|---|---|---|
| awake | 85.1 GB | 85.4 GB |
| asleep, level 1 (3 cycles) | 2.1 GB each time | 67.8 GB |
| after wake | 85.1 GB each time | 150.8 GB |
| selective wake: weights only | 19.4 GB | — |
| after `release_kv_cache_memory` | 19.7 GB | — |

- After the review changes (rollback, env check, shared drain), a shorter rerun on the final commit with 2 level-1 cycles gave 104/104 outputs identical to its control. Every hit read 2032 tokens from the store. A held 2.1 GB asleep and 85.1 GB awake in both cycles.
- Transfer errors: none in either run (non-zero error counters, glog `E` lines, `ERROR` lines, and tracebacks were all 0 on A and B).

Not covered:

- TCP on hardware. On this cluster, TCP puts and gets fail with `TRANSFER_FAIL` even without sleep, with both P2PHANDSHAKE and the HTTP metadata server. An earlier H200 run of main with TCP and sleep returned 8/8 with memory fully freed, but it was not repeated with this commit.
- The HiSparse path on hardware (unit-tested only).
- TP > 1 and multi-GPU runs.
- The in-process engine (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`). The drain inside `release_kv_caches` is what covers it there.

Known limitations:

- Mooncake builds with NVLink support (such as the cuda13 wheel) also install an nvlink transport when they find no RDMA NIC. That can't be detected at config time, so it is not refused.
- Pre-existing: sleep at level ≥ 1 and `release_kv_cache_memory` reset the connector before the release. On rank 0 that reset waits for the put queue with no bound, so a stuck put hangs there, not in the bounded release.
- Pre-existing: a load task that raises before the `try` in `KVCacheStoreRecvingThread._handle_request` never calls `task_done`. The drain then never sees an empty queue, and every later sleep fails with `TimeoutError`. We found no scheduler input that reaches it. A fix needs a load-error report too, so it is left for a follow-up.
- Pre-existing, not specific to this connector: `/sleep?mode=wait` (and `/pause?mode=wait`) while connector loads are in flight returns 500 "Failed to reset KV cache ...", and the scheduler stays paused until `/resume`. Under `PAUSED_NEW` the scheduler counts only running requests, so requests holding blocks for an async load look idle. Use `mode=abort`, or call `/resume` and retry.

Known separate issue, not fixed here: sleep at level ≥ 1 resets the connector, which runs `remove_all(force=True)` on the Mooncake master. One instance's sleep therefore deletes the KV of every instance that shares the master. It should be scoped by tenant.

### Additional Test Result: stress run

- Stress run (GB300, 1 node, Qwen3-8B, Mooncake RDMA, one shared store; the image plus per-file mounts of this stack, sha-checked):
  - Three servers: TP2 and TP1 sleep with staggered, overlapping windows, and a TP1 server never sleeps; `store_tp_size=2`, so TP2 and TP1 share keys. 20 cycles. After each wake: get of keys another server put while it was asleep, own put read back, and cross-server read-back of its post-wake puts.
    - 2080/2080 outputs are token-identical to an awake control run (`/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true` at the same points). Every hit read 2032/2048 tokens from the store.
  - TP2 plus a never-sleep server, 10 cycles: full sleep, selective wake (`weights`, then `kv_cache`), and `release_kv_cache_memory`. 400/400 identical to control.
  - Memory had no drift: TP2 at 3583 MiB/GPU asleep and 86467 woken, TP1 at 2077 / 85101, the same in every cycle. Host RSS of each server was unchanged from cycle 1 to cycle 20. 0 transfer errors.
  - 64 concurrent requests up to `/sleep?mode=wait`, with puts in flight: 64/64 complete, 0 timeouts, and requests not yet scheduled run after the wake. `mode=abort`: all aborted, and sleep takes 0.5 s.
  - HiSparse (GLM-5.2-FP8 TP4, HiSparse + MooncakeStore through MultiConnector): 78 host regions stay registered and the device region is released and registered again. 12 `release_kv_cache_memory` cycles: device memory returns to the same value every cycle, and store hits read 4160+ tokens. Exact-retrieval accuracy on store hits after a release equals an interleaved control on the same prompts (72/96 vs 72/96, with 140/144 per-request outcomes equal). Level-1 sleep was not run on this model: it would back up about 704 GB of weights to host RAM.

title: [Docs] Clarify Qwen4Exp PLE Engram configuration
body:
## Overview
Improves the Engram documentation for [#59897](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59897) with a concrete Qwen3.8-Flash-Next two-A100 configuration.

## Claims
Documents tensor parallel size 2 as the starting topology for two GPUs on one host.
 Replaces the unsupported VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD environment-variable guidance with the supported engram-config option.
Explains Qwen4Exp PLE ETP sharding and calls out the SM8x pinned-host FP8 lookup limitation.

## Validation
 git diff --check passed.
 The pre-commit typo hook passed.
 Markdown linting was started locally but did not finish in the available Windows environment.

## Details
The existing Engram page describes CPU offload and Qwen4Exp PLE behavior, but it does not connect those controls to the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next two-A100 use case. The new section gives an actionable command, clarifies that VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD is not read by vLLM, and distinguishes tensor parallelism from pipeline parallelism for a single host.The section explicitly states that A100 UVA support does not bypass the SM8x FP8 Triton lookup compatibility requirement, so operators do not interpret CPU offload as universally available until a release containing the lookup fix is installed.

title: [Core] Release DeepEP all2all buffers on sleep with comm suspend
body:
## Purpose

Part of RFC #59055 (release more GPU memory in sleep mode).

With `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend`, sleep mode now also releases the DeepEP all2all buffers of `deepep_high_throughput` and `deepep_low_latency`. Before this change those buffers (the NVL IPC buffer, plus the NVSHMEM heap for low-latency) stayed on the GPU while the engine was asleep.

How it works:

- `All2AllManagerBase` gets two no-op hooks, `suspend()` and `resume()`. `CudaCommunicator.suspend()` / `resume()`, which `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend` already calls on every group from `Worker.sleep()` / `wake_up()`, now call them.
- `DeepEPAll2AllManagerBase.suspend()` calls `Buffer.destroy()` on every cached buffer. vLLM already creates the buffers with `explicitly_destroy=True`.
- `resume()` re-runs `Buffer.__init__()` on the same Python object with its cached kwargs. The prepare/finalize objects keep a reference to that object, so they stay valid, and the handle cache still finds it.
- One flag, `_suspended`, records that the buffers are destroyed. While it is set, `destroy()` (shutdown) skips them, so shutting the engine down while asleep is clean.
- Both steps are collective over the EP group, like `ncclCommSuspend`: `destroy()` has GPU barriers and `__init__()` exchanges handles with `all_gather_object`. As with NCCL suspend, the engine must be idle.
- With `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend`, `NVSHMEM_DISABLE_NCCL=1` becomes the default (a value the user sets wins). NVSHMEM otherwise builds NCCL communicators for its default teams on every init, which DeepEP never uses; they cost ~1.6 GiB/GPU while awake, ~4 s per wake and most of the per-cycle growth below.

The buffers stay on the GPU, and a log line says why, in two cases:

1. **CUDA graphs on** (`cudagraph_mode != NONE`). Captured graphs hold the buffer addresses, and the NVL buffer and workspace get new addresses when they are re-created. In a standalone test, replaying a graph captured before a destroy/re-create matched for two cycles and then failed with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` on the third. The NVSHMEM buffer happened to come back at the same address, but the NVL buffer did not. Releasing the buffers with graphs on would need either graph recapture on wake or fixed-address allocation inside DeepEP; neither is in this PR. In practice this means `deepep_low_latency` with CUDA graphs (the default for that backend) keeps its buffers. `deepep_high_throughput` runs without CUDA graphs when DP > 1, so it is covered.
2. **`VLLM_DEEPEP_LOW_LATENCY_USE_MNNVL=1`**. In this mode DeepEP allocates the NVL buffer with fabric handles. Its `destroy()` does not drop all references to that allocation (`cuMemRetainAllocationHandle` in `get_mem_handle` is never released), so the memory is not freed. On GB300 each destroy/re-create cycle leaked one NVL buffer (+1036 MiB per GPU per cycle with the default 1 GiB buffer, +518 MiB with 512 MiB). The legacy `Buffer` that vLLM pins (d4f41e4) has this bug; DeepEP main no longer has the legacy `Buffer`.

The default behavior does not change. Without `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend`, nothing new runs.

Known limitations (not handled in this PR):

- `--enable-fault-tolerance` with DeepEP LL: re-init zeroes DeepEP's rank mask, but vLLM keeps its last-seen mask, so a rank masked before sleep could show up as a new fault after wake. A dead rank also makes the re-init hang.
- A weights-only wake (`wake_up(tags=["weights"])`) already re-creates the buffers (and runs NVSHMEM init for LL), as NCCL resume does today, so they come back before the KV cache.
- Two LL buffers with different shapes in one process would share the global NVSHMEM state, which the second `destroy()` finalizes twice. No current vLLM model creates two LL buffers; shutdown `destroy()` already has this issue.

Relation to #59360: #59360 uses the same `CudaCommunicator.suspend()` / `resume()` path for FlashInfer all-reduce workspaces. The two PRs do not conflict in behavior. Each adds an independent call, and neither uses NCCL (DeepEP syncs with its own GPU/NVSHMEM barriers and gloo), so the order relative to NCCL and to each other does not matter. They do conflict textually: both add lines to `CudaCommunicator.suspend()` / `resume()` and add tests next to each other in `tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py`. Whichever lands second keeps both calls.

## Test Plan

Unit tests (`tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py`):

- `test_cuda_communicator_suspend_recreates_deepep_buffers[ht-eager|ht-cudagraph|ll-eager|ll-cudagraph|ll-mnnvl]`: builds the real HT/LL manager (so the policy set in `__init__` is covered), then suspends twice and resumes twice through `CudaCommunicator`. The handle cache holds only weak references; the test keeps the buffers alive the way the prepare/finalize objects do. With CUDA graphs off, each buffer is destroyed once and re-initialized in place with its original kwargs. With CUDA graphs, or LL with MNNVL, it is left alone. MNNVL does not affect HT. NCCL suspend/resume are still called.
- `test_deepep_destroy[awake|asleep]`: shutdown `destroy()` destroys each buffer exactly once and clears the cache, both awake and while suspended.
- Mutation check (16 mutants): each makes at least one test fail. Policy: ignoring the resident reason, removing the CUDA graph check, removing the MNNVL check, applying the MNNVL check to HT. State: no double-suspend guard, not setting or not clearing the flag, no resume guard, re-creating a new object instead of re-init in place, re-init without the kwargs, destroying only some handles, `destroy()` ignoring the flag, never destroying, or not clearing the cache. Wiring: `CudaCommunicator` not calling the all2all suspend or resume.

Hardware (NVIDIA GB300, 4 GPUs per node, driver 580.105.08, CUDA 13.0):

- Same image for stock and patched. The changed files are bind-mounted one by one, with sha256 checks against the base commit and the patch.
- Server flags: `--enable-sleep-mode --enable-nccl-comm-suspend --enable-expert-parallel --data-parallel-size 4|8 --no-enable-prefix-caching`.
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash also uses `--trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192`, plus `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` (HT) or `256` (LL).
- A driver sends 16 greedy prompts (48 tokens), one at a time, with each prompt pinned to one DP rank by `X-data-parallel-rank`. It records the awake outputs, runs level-1 sleep/wake cycles (and one level-2 cycle in some cases), and compares the outputs after every wake with the awake outputs.
- GPU memory while asleep is read with nvidia-smi on every GPU of every node, 4 s after `/sleep` returns.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 9 passed (`-k "deepep or suspend or checkpoint"`, 5 runs). pre-commit passes on the changed files.

Shutdown while asleep: after the last cycle of each run, the driver puts the server to sleep and sends SIGTERM or SIGINT to the `vllm serve` process. Every server exits with code 0, and no log has a DeepEP traceback or a DeepEP "destroy() was not called" warning.

- With the default `--shutdown-timeout 0`, the process manager kills the engine processes right away, so the workers never run `destroy()`. To exercise that path, the Qwen3 HT and LL runs were repeated with `--shutdown-timeout 60`. The workers then go through `destroy_model_parallel()` while asleep and exit gracefully. As a control, the earlier version of this PR (without the skip in `destroy()`) raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'destroy'` on the same run.
- Unrelated noise, also seen when the PR changes nothing: some runs log one `EngineDeadError` traceback from an API server's output handler during shutdown, including V4-Flash LL with CUDA graphs, where the buffers stay resident. With `--shutdown-timeout 60`, each worker logs `CUDA Error: invalid argument at cumem_allocator.cpp:258` once at exit; stock logs the same 4 lines.

GPU memory used while asleep, per GPU (MiB). All GPUs in a run were within 4 MiB of each other.

| Model, setup | Backend | CUDA graphs | Stock | This PR | Freed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B, DP4 EP, 1 node | `deepep_high_throughput` | off (forced) | 2813 | 1749-1751 | 1062 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B, DP4 EP, 1 node | `deepep_low_latency` | off (`--enforce-eager`) | 6177 | 1769 (cycle 1) | 4408 |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DP4 EP, 1 node | `deepep_high_throughput` | off (`--enforce-eager`) | 2529 | 1469-1473 | 1058 |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DP4 EP, 1 node | `deepep_low_latency` | off (`--enforce-eager`) | 7473 | 1481 (cycle 1) | 5992 |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DP4 EP, 1 node | `deepep_low_latency` | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | not run | 9503 (kept, log line printed) | 0 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B, DP8 EP, 2 nodes | `deepep_low_latency`, MNNVL | off (`--enforce-eager`) | 6041 | 6041 (kept, log line printed) | 0 |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DP8 EP, 2 nodes | `deepep_low_latency`, MNNVL | off (`--enforce-eager`) | not run | 7337 (kept, log line printed; earlier revision, same resident path) | 0 |

Outputs: 16/16 identical to the awake outputs after every level-1 wake, in every run above (3 cycles, 15 for the drift runs).

Sleep and wake time (level 1):

- HT: same as stock, within 0.1 s.
- LL: wake is about 4-5 s slower than stock and sleep about 1-2 s slower (NVSHMEM finalize and init). Example, V4-Flash LL: wake 5.7-6.1 s vs 1.4 s stock.
- With the `NVSHMEM_DISABLE_NCCL=1` default (latest revision), Qwen3-30B-A3B LL eager, 15 level-1 cycles, outputs 16/16 every cycle:

  | Setup | Before the default | With the default |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 node: asleep cycle 1 -> 15, growth per cycle, wake | 1769 -> 1801 MiB, 2.29 MiB, 4.6-5.4 s | 1761 -> 1791 MiB, 2.14 MiB, 1.5-1.75 s |
  | 2 nodes (RDMA): asleep cycle 1 -> 15, growth per cycle, wake | 1773 -> 1889 MiB, 8.29 MiB, 5.0-5.6 s | 1761 -> 1791 MiB, 2.14 MiB, 1.0-1.3 s |

  The remaining ~2.1 MiB/GPU per cycle is NVSHMEM 3.4.5 leaking 4 CUDA streams and 2 events on every init/finalize (`init.cu`, `ibgda.cpp`; still present in v3.8.0), reproduced with a 40-line NVSHMEM-only program. It needs an NVSHMEM fix.

Repeated cycles:

- HT: flat. V4-Flash stays at 1469-1473 MiB over 3 cycles. In a standalone DeepEP test, used memory rises by 32 MiB over the first 3 destroy/re-create cycles and then stays flat through 30.
- LL: about +2 MiB per GPU per cycle, and it does not level off. Qwen3 over 15 cycles: 1769 -> 1801 MiB with this PR, flat 6177 MiB with stock. A standalone DeepEP test shows the same rate (+72 MiB over 30 cycles). The rate is the same with no NVL buffer and with `NVSHMEM_REMOTE_TRANSPORT=none`, so the leak comes from NVSHMEM finalize + init, not from DeepEP's NVL buffer or the IB transport. On one node, 1000 cycles cost about 2.3 GB, still far less than the ~4.4-6 GB per GPU that LL frees on each sleep. Across nodes the rate is higher (see the RDMA path below).

Level 2: Qwen3 HT and LL match 16/16 after level-2 sleep, `reload_weights` and wake. DeepSeek-V4-Flash does not match after level 2: HT gives 0/16 with this PR and also 0/16 on stock with the same flags. LL gives 3/16 with this PR and the same 3/16 (same prompts) on stock. This is a separate problem in V4-Flash weight reload, not in this change.

Cross-node:

- The two nodes are in one NVLink domain (same fabric cluster UUID and clique, IMEX running), and they have 4 GPUs each.
- DeepEP's legacy `Buffer` treats up to 8 ranks as NVLink peers (`LEGACY_NUM_MAX_NVL_PEERS = 8`). So DP8 over two 4-GPU nodes never takes the RDMA (NVSHMEM over RoCE) path; the run that works uses the NVLink fabric. These limits also hold on stock; this PR does not change buffer creation:
  - `deepep_high_throughput` fails at startup with `num_ranks > LEGACY_NUM_MAX_NVL_PEERS or low_latency_mode`, because vLLM asks for an RDMA buffer when the group spans nodes.
  - `deepep_low_latency` with the default IPC handles fails at startup (`cudaIpcOpenMemHandle` cannot open buffers on the other node).
  - `deepep_low_latency` with `VLLM_DEEPEP_LOW_LATENCY_USE_MNNVL=1` runs. With this PR the buffers stay resident (case 2 above). Outputs were 16/16 after each of 3 cycles, with no hang and no growth across cycles.
- Without the MNNVL check (an earlier version of this PR), the same Qwen3 run freed memory on the first sleep (2801 MiB asleep), then grew by 1036 MiB per cycle (2801 -> 3837 -> 4875 -> 5911). That is the DeepEP leak described above, and the reason for the check.
- RDMA path (LL only):
  - DeepEP's legacy `Buffer` accepts fewer than 8 ranks or a multiple of 8 (`buffer.hpp:114`); DP12 on 4-GPU nodes fails at startup on stock with that assert. HT internode needs blocks of 8 ranks that share plain IPC handles, and those blocks span two nodes here, so HT cannot use RDMA on this cluster.
  - LL uses RDMA across nodes with the NVL buffer off and MNNVL off (`VLLM_DEEPEP_BUFFER_SIZE_MB=0`, DP8 over 2 nodes): NVSHMEM lists only the local GPUs as P2P peers and reaches the other node through IBGDA on RoCE.
  - With `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend --enforce-eager`: Qwen3-30B-A3B goes from 5013 to 1773-1791 MiB per GPU asleep, DeepSeek-V4-Flash from 6307 to 1483-1501. Outputs are 16/16 after each of 3 level-1 wakes. Wake is about 4.3 s slower than stock. Nothing hangs, and SIGTERM while asleep exits cleanly on both nodes.
  - Asleep memory grows by about 8 MiB per GPU per cycle across nodes (2.4 on one node), in vLLM and in a 30-cycle standalone DeepEP test. It appears only with remote IBGDA peers, so it comes from NVSHMEM finalize and init. At that rate, about 400-600 cycles in one process use up what one sleep frees.

Note: the DeepEP in the current vLLM image is built for `sm_90a` / `sm_100a` only (`TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST='9.0a 10.0a'` for ep_kernels in the Dockerfile), so DeepEP kernels fail on GB300 (`sm_103`). For these tests, DeepEP d4f41e4 was rebuilt with `10.0a 10.3a`. That is a separate issue and is not changed here.

title: [Bugfix] Resolve eager_break_during_capture at call time, not import time
body:
## Overview

Fixes #59940. `@eager_break_during_capture` decided whether to wrap a function when the decorated module was
imported. With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the breakable-graph flag is turned on later, inside `VllmConfig` (#57586).
Any import of `attention.py` before that point leaves `unified_attention_with_output` unwrapped, and FA2 then produces
wrong tokens for short prefills. This PR makes the decorator always return its wrapper, so the setting is read at call
time. It's a 2-line removal plus CPU tests.

## Claims

- Breakable-graph eager breaks no longer depend on import order. In-process and default-fork engines with a cold
  model-info cache now get the wrapped attention op.
- With the flag off, behavior is unchanged: the wrapper calls the function directly when no breakable capture is
  active.
- Every current and future user of the decorator is covered (33 sites, plus those added by #46372 and #57881), with no
  new imports.

## Validation

Environment: `uv venv --python 3.12`, `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e .`, plus `requirements/lint.txt`, `pytest`
and `tblib`; Python 3.12.14, main 5f30fc703 plus this commit. Tests ran on CPU only.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py -v
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py tests/test_ray_env_utils.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py
```

| Test | Before (main 5f30fc703) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_decorator_breaks_when_enabled_after_decoration` | FAIL | pass |
| `test_attention_op_breaks_when_imported_before_enable` (subprocess, real op) | FAIL | pass |
| `test_decorator_passthrough_returns_fn_result[False/True]` | pass | pass |
| `test_decorated_op_traces_without_graph_break[False/True]` (`fullgraph=True`) | pass | pass |
| whole `test_breakable_cudagraph.py` | 2 failed, 11 passed, 13 skipped | 13 passed, 13 skipped (the skips need CUDA) |

`tests/test_config.py` and `tests/test_ray_env_utils.py`: 13 failed, 424 passed, 5 skipped, with and without this patch
(identical failing test IDs: they need gated HF models such as Llama-3.2 and Mixtral, plus the engram DP shared-memory
config tests, on my host). pre-commit: all hooks pass.

End to end on GPU (RTX PRO 6000, SM120, FA2, default V2 model runner, Qwen3-1.7B, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, fresh `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` per cold
run, main 5f30fc703), using the repro from the issue:

| Run | Output |
|---|---|
| unpatched, in-process, cold | `first_token=16448 first_logprob=-2.7350 hash=5f5950387de45eaa` (wrong) |
| unpatched, in-process, warm (same cache root) | `first_token=271 first_logprob=-3.8602 hash=19ba86ff8b6b181d` |
| patched, in-process, cold | `first_token=271 first_logprob=-3.8602 hash=19ba86ff8b6b181d` |
| patched, default multiprocess, cold | `first_token=271 first_logprob=-3.8602 hash=19ba86ff8b6b181d` |

BI=0 (`VLLM_COMPILE`) is not run-to-run deterministic on this shared host, so bitwise comparison isn't a valid check. On
main 5f30fc703, 14 prompt lengths (2 to 513), 2 runs per tree: both trees compile one graph with 0 graph breaks and 0
recompiles. Two unpatched runs agree on 10/14 hashes (all 14 token sequences equal, max |Δlogprob| 0.097). One patched
run is bitwise identical to one unpatched run (14/14); the other patched run differs from every other run (3 token
sequences, max |Δlogprob| 0.11). On 766b4ae54 a single pair was 14/14 identical. With the flag unset no breakable capture
exists, so the wrapper only calls the function.

`vllm bench latency --num-iters-warmup 3 --num-iters 10` (input 32, output 128, batch 8), avg latency per run, shared host
with other jobs on the GPUs:

| | Unpatched | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| BI=0 | 0.507 ± 0.061 s (n=3): .466 .477 .577 | 0.560 ± 0.151 s (n=3): .472 .474 .735 |
| BI=1 | fast runs: .488 .498; slow runs: .707 .642 .632 .608 .747 .663 | .495 .495 .503 .492 .536 .564 |

No run showed the patched tree slower than the unpatched one: patched BI=1 took 0.49-0.56 s in all 6 runs, unpatched
0.49-0.75 s. Both trees have identical worker state (flag set before attention is imported, `CompilationMode.NONE`).

Pass-through overhead, from a microbenchmark of 1e6 calls × 5 with no capture active: about 0.5 µs per call on a shared,
loaded x86_64 host with Python 3.12. That's an upper bound of about 14 µs per step for 28 attention layers. Before this
change, the cost only arose when the flag was on.

## Details

- **Root cause:** `vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py` had `if not is_breakable_cudagraph_enabled(): return fn`.
  On a cold model-info cache, `ModelConfig` construction imports `attention.py` via `registry._save_modelinfo_to_cache`
  → `weight_utils.atomic_writer` before `VllmConfig._maybe_enable_breakable_cudagraph` sets the env. Forked engine
  cores inherit the bare op. First reported by @Taimys in #58918 and in the #57311 thread.
- **Scope beyond batch invariance:** as @LioEinaudi pointed out in #59940, the other branch of
  `_maybe_enable_breakable_cudagraph` (`_uses_breakable_cudagraph_by_default`, #52861) sets the same env var after the
  same early import, for the `DEFAULT_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH_ARCHITECTURES` models on CUDA, with no
  `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` involved. The ordering hazard is the same and this change covers it. I only validated the
  `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` path above, and I did not run those models, so I can't say whether their outputs are
  affected.
- **Why this isn't a duplicate of #57311:** #57311 (open) removes that particular import chain, and @Taimys confirmed it
  fixes that trigger on L20. The decorator stays import-order dependent, though: with #57311 applied on main and a warm
  cache, a user script that imports `vllm.model_executor.model_loader` before building `LLM` still ends up with the
  unwrapped op (verified by inspecting the op, not by comparing outputs). #53293 fixed the same root cause for Ray only. This PR removes the
  dependence at its source and works alongside #57311.
- **Dynamo:** the wrapper's thread-local lookup traces without a graph break (`fullgraph=True` test), so no
  `is_compiling()` fast path is needed.
- **Not included:** a GPU end-to-end regression test. Maintainers: would you like one (for example a cold-cache
  `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` FA2 run in the BI test suite)?

title: [Bugfix][DCP] Sort DCP group ranks so rank_in_group matches collective order
body:
## Overview

Fix garbage output when a DCP group spans TP × PCP (e.g. TP2 × PCP2 × DCP4): sort each DCP group's ranks so `rank_in_group` agrees with the order collectives return shards in.

## Claims

- TP2 × PCP2 × DCP4 on GLM-5.3-NVFP4 goes from GSM8K 0.000 to 0.905.
- No change for DCP groups that were already ascending (DCP within TP, or DCP == PCP), which covers every previously validated configuration.

## Validation

GSM8K (5-shot) on 4x B300, MRV2, GLM-5.3-NVFP4, `-tp 2 -pcp 2 -dcp 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla -cc.cudagraph_mode=NONE`:

| | GSM8K |
|---|---:|
| main | 0.000 |
| this PR | 0.905 |

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_dcp_a2a.py -k test_dcp_group_ranks_match_collective_order  # 5 passed
```

## Details

**Root cause.** With PCP, `initialize_model_parallel` builds a DCP group that spans TP × PCP PCP-first (`all_ranks.transpose(-1, -2)`), giving member lists like `[0, 2, 1, 3]`.
- `torch.distributed.new_group` sorts its ranks, so all-gathers return shards in global-rank order.
- `GroupCoordinator.rank_in_group` is `ranks.index(rank)` on the unsorted list.
- The DCP LSE merge (`correct_attn_out`) uses `rank_in_group` to pick this rank's LSE from the gathered LSEs. So DCP ranks 1 and 2 rescaled their partial outputs with each other's LSE.

The new unit test checks that DCP groups are ascending for TP-only, PCP-only and TP × PCP layouts.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR touches DCP group rank order (searched "dcp rank order", "DCP group ranks").

title: [DeepSeek-V4-P5] Rewrite matmul_persistent with a split-K plan
body:
## Overview Increase parallelism for long-K, skinny-N `matmul_persistent` projections without changing a row's arithmetic when it is co-batched differently. Split only for `N <= 64` and `K >= 1024`. Chunk boundaries depend on `(K, N)` and the K tile size on dtype. title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Count pull completion notifications per transfer
body:
## Overview

**We add a generic way to count notifs to expect for a READ that doesn't use consumers as a "proxy", but allows each D to just tell P how many xfers it's started**. This is the case for HiSparse(see below), but also enables future protocols where D may want to send multiple reads (or similarly P writes for push mode, looking ahead).

For HiSparse in particular, mixed DRAM/device NIXL pulls currently notify the producer only after the decoder polls both READ handles complete. Attach native completion notifications to each READ and count them on the producer, so a paused decoder does not strand the producer's release acknowledgement.

Alternative approach to #58041: that PR keeps the paused decoder stepping; this changes pull completion accounting and removes its deferred notification queue.  

Duplicate-work searches found no open PR implementing this protocol change. Broader pause/resume and retained-export semantics remain separate from this change and #59670.

## Claims

- Every posted pull READ carries a completion notification. A split read declares its number of nonempty transfers before either can complete; the producer waits for all of them.
- The producer counts notifications per NIXL sender agent, allowing different readers of the same request to issue different numbers of transfers. Topology still determines how many readers must finish.
- Full cache hits, empty slices, and unused MLA replicas send explicit zero-transfer acknowledgements. Missing completions after partial submission or transfer failure leave the source retained until its existing lease expires.

## Details

The pull notification payload becomes `request_id:expected_readers:transfers_from_this_reader`. `get_new_notifs()` supplies the sender agent identity. The producer retires each reader only after its declared number of notifications arrives, then releases the request once every expected reader is finished. A zero-transfer reader sends one standalone acknowledgement.

Mixed reads prepare every nonempty handle with the full split count before submitting any handle. If only one sibling completes, its notification cannot release the producer's source blocks. Local receive polling, postprocessing, and failure retirement retain their existing responsibilities.

This replaces one manually sent notification per mixed read with one native notification per transfer and adds producer bookkeeping per reader. NIXL connector protocol version is bumped from 13 to 14: P and D must upgrade together. Push notification payloads are unchanged.

Queued reads, handshake progress during pause, lease validity, cache invalidation, and weight-update coordination are outside this PR's claim. In particular, native notifications do not establish full P/D pause/resume safety.

title: [Qwen4Exp] PLE disk offload
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds `--engram-config '{"disk_offload": true}'` for Qwen4Exp. The PLE n-gram table stays in the checkpoint files, and each step reads only its rows on the host. On DGX Spark (GB10), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 loads with 27.0 GiB less memory. Decode is within 3.5% of the resident table, and GSM8K is unchanged.

This carries forward @Trosfy's design from #58815 (their commits are kept, co-authored). It is rebased onto the NVFP4 PLE tables from #56273 and renamed `disk_offload` to pair with `cpu_offload`.

## Claims

- **Memory:** no table in GPU or pinned host memory, and no copy in an offload directory. Recently read rows sit in the OS page cache, which the kernel can reclaim. On unified-memory Spark, `cpu_offload` does not help, because pinned memory comes out of the same pool as the weights and the KV cache.
- **Formats:** BF16, FP8 and NVFP4. Rows are read in checkpoint format and decoded on the GPU with the existing PLE kernel.
- **CUDA graphs:** the forward reads fixed device buffers, so graphs replay unchanged.
- **Cost:** decode within 3.5% at c=1/4/8, and about 11% higher TTFT.

## Validation

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 (`local-inference-lab@6c01ac3`), one GB10, both arms in one job on the same node. MTP n=3, FP8 KV (6 GiB), prefix caching off.

| | Resident | `disk_offload` | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weights loaded | 99.09 GiB | 72.09 GiB | -27.0 GiB |
| Host `MemAvailable` after startup | 4.6 GiB | 32.0 GiB | +27.4 GiB |
| Decode tok/s/user, c=1 | 33.63 | 32.45 | -3.5% |
| Decode tok/s, c=4 | 72.57 | 73.33 | +1.0% |
| Decode tok/s, c=8 | 94.04 | 91.99 | -2.2% |
| MTP acceptance length, c=1 | 2.33 | 2.31 | flat |
| TTFT, 8K prompt (median of 15) | 2540 ms | 2820 ms | +11.0% |
| GSM8K | 247/256 | 246/256 | -1 |

- Decode: aiperf, SPEED-Bench coding prompts, 1024 output tokens, active decode time only. One run per arm, so noise is a few percent.
- TTFT: exact-length random token ids with `max_tokens=1`. With the page cache dropped, the first 8K request took 3018 ms.
- The image was `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-5555a2d8f7`, with every file touched by this PR and #56273 overlaid from this branch.
- CI: the H200 and CPU Qwen4 Exp lanes run the new tests. The Spark numbers were measured outside CI because there is no GB10 lane. On GB10 the new tests pass for all three formats.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 --language-model-only \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --kv-cache-memory-bytes 6G --gpu-memory-utilization 0.87 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
  --compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size": 32}' \
  --engram-config '{"disk_offload": true}'   # resident: '{"cpu_offload": false}'

pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py
pytest tests/test_config.py -k engram
```

</details>

## Details

- **Load:** the default loader hands over zero-copy safetensors mmap views. Their file and offset are found in `/proc/self/maps`, the files are opened read-only, and the views are released. Loading fails if the shards do not cover the table, if a dtype does not match, or if a view is not file-backed (for example `.bin` or `fastsafetensors`).
- **Per step:** `Qwen4ExpModelState.prepare_inputs` computes and deduplicates the n-gram ids, reads each row with `preadv` (after a `WILLNEED` read-ahead hint), and copies the rows to the staging buffers.
- **Parallelism:** every TP rank stages full rows, so no ETP reduction is needed. Elastic EP is rejected.
- **Alternatives:** #58439 reads the checkpoint mapping from the GPU through host page tables. #54070 writes a second copy of the table to disk. This PR reads rows on the host from the files the loader already opened.

This PR does not batch the per-row reads for long prefills (that is the TTFT cost) or support weight reload.

title: [Bugfix][DSv3.2] Carry the shared indexer top-k across pipeline stages
body:
## Overview

Fix a GSM8K accuracy loss on GLM-5.x / DeepSeek-V3.2-style models under pipeline parallelism. These models reuse the previous layer's indexer top-k, and when a PP stage starts on a reusing layer, that stage read a stale top-k. This PR sends the top-k along with the intermediate tensors.

## Claims

- GLM-5.3-NVFP4 PP2 × TP2 on main: GSM8K 0.879 → 0.908. Before the fix, stage 1's first three layers attend with the previous step's top-k.
- With gather-based DCP (#59916), where it was more visible: 0.820 → 0.908.
- Only stage boundaries that land on a top-k-reusing layer send anything extra (`(num_tokens, index_topk)` int32 per step). Other models and partitions are unchanged.

## Validation

GSM8K (5-shot, all 1319 q) on 4x B300, MRV2, GLM-5.3-NVFP4, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla -cc.cudagraph_mode=NONE`:

| config | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `-pp 2 -tp 2` | 0.879 | 0.908 |
| `-pp 2 -tp 2 -dcp 2` with gather DCP (#59916) | 0.820 | 0.908 |
| same, `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=38,40` (boundary aligned to a top-k group), no fix | 0.882 | - |

## Details

**Root cause.** GLM-5.3 sets `index_topk_freq=4` with offset 3, so groups of layers reuse the top-k computed by the group's first layer.
- The default PP2 split puts the stage boundary at layer 39, which is inside a group.
- Stage 1's first layers (39-41) therefore skip the indexer and read `topk_indices_buffer`. On that stage the buffer holds the top-k of the previous step's last indexer layer, for the previous batch.
- Aligning the partition (38/40) restored accuracy, which confirms the cause.

**Fix.** `reuses_previous_topk(config, layer_id)` is factored out of the attention init.
- The model adds `topk_indices` to its intermediate tensors when any stage starts on a reusing layer.
- The receiving stage copies it into its top-k buffer.

Only the NVIDIA `deepseek_v32` model path is patched. The AMD path has the same structure and could get the same fix in a follow-up.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR fixes top-k across PP stages (searched "pp topk_indices", "pipeline topk").

title: [ROCm][DCP] Default MLA DCP verify to the round-robin asm decode where it applies
body:
## Purpose

#56861 added the AITER round-robin asm decode (`cprr`) for causal multi-token verify under decode context
parallelism, but left `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY` defaulting to `segmented`, which expands every verify token
into its own paged-KV row. At realistic batch sizes `segmented` is much slower, so DCP + speculative decoding is not
worth enabling on MI355X with the default.

This PR adds `auto` as the new default: use `cprr` wherever `_asm_dcp_verify_configured` holds (gfx950, DCP with
interleave 1, speculative decoding) and the gathered head count is servable, otherwise `segmented`. Explicit `asm`
and `segmented` behave as before (`asm` still raises on an unservable shape; `auto` raises only if neither route can
serve the batch). The unservable-shape error now names the configured route and only suggests `segmented` when the
AITER build supports it. It also lower-cases the value before comparing: `env_with_choices(case_sensitive=False)` validates
case-insensitively but returns the raw string, so `ASM` silently meant `segmented`.

## Test Result

Kimi-K3 (MXFP4), 8x MI355X, TP8 / DCP8 (a2a), DSpark k=4.

Verify route microbenchmark (60k shared prefix + 4k unique, OSL 256, 48 prompts, conc 48, same node and image):

| verify route | output tok/s | median TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|
| `segmented` (current default) | 141.0 | 170.8 ms |
| `cprr` (this PR's default) | 212.6 | 101.0 ms |

At OSL 1024 `segmented` completed no request inside the benchmark window.

InferenceX agentic-coding trace, conc 48 (synthetic acceptance length 3.36, as in InferenceX CI):

| configuration | tot tok/s/GPU | interactivity p90 | TPOT p50 | e2e p50 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DCP8, no spec, 900 s | 12,317 | 19.1 | 38 ms | 13.1 s |
| DCP8 + DSpark k=4 on `cprr`, 900 s | 13,551 (+10.0%) | 21.6 | 20 ms | 7.0 s |
| DCP8 + DSpark k=4 on `cprr`, 3600 s, CI warmup | 14,903 | 19.3 | 28 ms | 9.0 s |
| InferenceX CI MI355X c48 (no spec), for reference | 12,090 | 14.7 | 49 ms | 18.1 s |

The 900 s rows are on the same node; the 3600 s row also includes other open K3 PRs in the test image
(#58861, #59070) and `--stream-interval 10`.

### Accuracy

gsm8k 5-shot, 1319 questions, `lm_eval --model local-completions` against the served model, `num_concurrent=64`;
Kimi-K3 MXFP4, 8x MI355X, TP8 / DCP8 (a2a), FP8 KV cache, async scheduling, FULL CUDA graphs. The test base is vLLM 36768d1b plus the open K3 PRs
#58861 and #59070 and merged #56960 #59175 #58344. Spec runs use DSpark k=4 with real (block) rejection, so acceptance length reflects actual draft quality.

| configuration | strict-match | flexible-extract | mean acceptance length |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| no speculative decoding (test base without #58887) | 0.9568 ± 0.0056 | — | — |
| DSpark k=4, `cprr` forced via env, without this PR (vLLM 36768d1b + #58887) | 0.9568 ± 0.0056 | 0.9568 | 3.78 |
| DSpark k=4, **with this PR** (and #59966; `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY` unset), test base + #58887 | **0.9583 ± 0.0055** | 0.9583 | 3.84 |

The no-spec run predates #58887 and scored normally; the spec runs need it. Bases older than #58887 (merged 2026-10-01) lose accuracy with DCP + spec at this concurrency
regardless of this PR (gsm8k 0.90-0.93; see #58886).

## Why this is not a duplicate

- #56861 (merged) introduced the `cprr` route as opt-in; this PR only changes the default on gfx950.
- #58555 (open) routes *gfx942* DCP verify to Triton split-KV; `cprr` is gfx950-only. Complementary; the two touch
  neighbouring lines of the metadata builder, so whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase.
- #59824 (open, DSpark adaptive verification on MI355X) does not change the verify route selection.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py`:
  101 passed (vLLM ROCm nightly ac9126e5 with this branch's Python sources on top). Builder-level tests run the
  real `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder.__init__` on CPU at TP8/DCP8 + spec decode and check the route each env value
  resolves to: `auto` (and unset/`AUTO`) takes cprr at 96 gathered heads padded to 128; `auto` falls back to
  segmented above 128 and raises naming `auto` when segmented is also unavailable; `asm`/`ASM` take cprr and
  refuse 256 heads; `segmented`/`SEGMENTED` never take cprr; `auto` off gfx950 stays segmented. Removing the
  `.lower()` makes two of them fail.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: pass (ruff, mypy, typos, SPDX, CI wiring).
- Serving + gsm8k + agentic benchmarks above.

## AI assistance

Developed with AI assistance (Claude). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and benchmarks
above.
