title: [ROCm][DCP] Pad the AITER MLA decode query without byte-wise strided copies
body:
## Purpose

With DCP on ROCm, the cprr AITER MLA decode pads the gathered query to a native head count (96 -> 128 for Kimi-K3 at DCP8). `AiterMLAHelper.get_mla_padded_q` did this with `repeat` (2x heads) followed by `[:, :m].contiguous()`. For an FP8 query both go through PyTorch's one-element-per-lane strided copy for a 1-byte dtype, which is slow on MI355X.

`get_mla_padded_q` now writes exactly `m` heads into the padded buffer, copying through an int64 view of the rows (`_copy_rows`). Results are bit-identical.

The change is ROCm-only. The shared DCP query gather in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/dcp.py` is unchanged; its relayout copy can be a follow-up.

## Test Result

MI355X, Kimi-K3 TP8 / DCP8, DSpark k=4, cprr verify, conc 48. Decode-step torch profile (batch 48 x 5 verify tokens), same node, image and capture window for both arms:

| | query gather + pad copies per decode step |
|---|---:|
| before | 1.88 ms (72 byte-wise copies) |
| this PR | 0.91 ms |

The remaining 0.91 ms is the gather relayout in `dcp.py` (0.59 ms, unchanged here) plus the int64 pad copies (0.33 ms).

### Accuracy

gsm8k 5-shot, 1319 questions, `lm_eval --model local-completions` against the served model, `num_concurrent=64`; Kimi-K3 MXFP4, 8x MI355X, TP8 / DCP8 (a2a), FP8 KV cache, async scheduling, FULL CUDA graphs, DSpark k=4 with real (block) rejection. Measured with the earlier revision of this PR, which contained this padding change plus a gather change; both are bit-exact.

| configuration | strict-match | flexible-extract | mean acceptance length |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| without this PR (vLLM 36768d1b + #58887) | 0.9568 ± 0.0056 | 0.9568 | 3.78 |
| with this PR | 0.9583 ± 0.0055 | 0.9583 | 3.84 |

## Why this is not a duplicate

No open PR changes `get_mla_padded_q`. #54494 (Kimi-K3 query replication) removes the DCP gather when `dcp_q_replicate` is on and does not touch the cprr padding.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_head_padding.py tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py` in the ROCm image: 37 passed, 5 skipped (cprr 96 -> 128 tile pad, bf16 and fp8).
- `pre-commit run --from-ref upstream/main --to-ref HEAD`: pass.

## AI assistance

Developed with AI assistance (Claude). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and benchmarks above. The padding-only scope follows @GirasoleY's rework (hyukjlee/vllm#1).

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Bound sparse indexer decode workspace at layer build time
body:
## Overview

ROCm-only alternative to #58014 for #55132. The ROCm sparse-MLA indexer works out its decode-row bound when the layer is built and passes it to the ROCm ops, instead of reading the vLLM config during the profiling run. `gpu_worker.py` is not changed.

## Claims

- The decode-logits workspace reserved during memory profiling is `max_num_seqs * (1 + num_speculative_tokens)` rows again, not `max_num_batched_tokens` rows. This covers the AITER FP8 indexer (`rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer`) and the MXFP4 indexer (`rocm_mxfp4_sparse_attn_indexer` / `rocm_mxfp4_sparse_mqa_indexer`).
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8x MI355X at 1M context gets about 32 GiB more KV cache per GPU.
- The CUDA path and shared worker / model-runner code are unchanged.

## Validation

End-to-end on 8x MI355X (gfx950) with dummy weights:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --load-format dummy -tp 8 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}'
```

| | Available KV cache memory (per GPU) | GPU KV cache size |
|---|---|---|
| main (`89439db727`) | 174.95 GiB | 90,340,997 tokens |
| this PR | 206.92 GiB | 106,889,551 tokens |

The 31.97 GiB difference matches the expected saving: (8192 − 96) rows × 1M columns × 4 B ≈ 31.6 GiB. With the fix, 16 concurrent completions (prompts of 301–4801 tokens, 32 output tokens each) all finished with no workspace errors. That confirms the smaller locked workspace still covers real decode steps.

Tests:

- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py -k profiling_bounds` passes (new test). It builds `RocmSparseAttnIndexer` while the config is set, then runs the profiling branch with no current config and checks that the reserved rows are `16 * (1 + 5)`.
- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py tests/models/glm5next/test_sparse_indexer_topk_dispatch.py tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_glm5next_sparse.py tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py`: 49 passed, 4 skipped, and 18 failed. The same 18 tests fail on main on this machine. The cause is the environment: AITER/FlyDSL can't write its JIT cache under a read-only `site-packages`. This PR changes nothing in those tests.
- `pre-commit run` passes.

This change only affects how much memory is reserved, not model outputs, so no accuracy eval was run.

## Details

Root cause: `Worker.determine_available_memory` calls `profile_run()` without `set_current_vllm_config`. `_max_decode_logits_rows()` called `get_current_vllm_config()`, which raised. The `except` branch then quietly returned `max_num_batched_tokens`. The workspace is locked after profiling, so the oversized reservation stayed for the life of the engine and counted as non-KV memory.

#58014 fixes this by setting the config context around `profile_run()` in `gpu_worker.py`. That is a change to the core worker for a problem that only shows up in ROCm code. This PR keeps the fix on the ROCm side instead:

- `max_decode_logits_rows()` (in `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`) reads the bound once, when the layer is constructed. The model is built inside `set_current_vllm_config`, so the config is available then. This follows how `SparseAttnIndexer` already handles its DCP scalars.
- The ROCm ops take a new `max_decode_rows: int = 0` argument, and the profiling branch reserves `min(num_tokens, max_decode_rows)` rows. A value of 0 (bound unknown) keeps the old conservative behavior.
- `SparseAttnIndexer` (the shared layer) gets one new attribute, and only its `forward_hip` reads it.

Not in this PR: the GLM5-Next kpool profiling path (`sparse_attn_indexer_kpool` in `models/glm5next/amd/sparse_indexer.py`) has the same root cause with the opposite effect. With no config it reserves 0 decode-logits rows, so it under-reserves. That can be fixed the same way in a follow-up.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4.1 DSpark adaptive verification + FULL_AND_PIECEWISE: illegal memory access under concurrent prefill (FlashInfer sparse DSV41 builders declare ALWAYS)
body:
### Your current environment

`vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0` (digest `sha256:a4a4c0437bf7…`), 2× B300 (SM103), TP2, Model Runner V2, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (rev `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With DSpark adaptive verification on and `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, the engine dies with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` once the scheduler runs mixed prefill+decode batches at high concurrency. The error surfaces at the event sync in `AdaptiveVerification.record_confidences` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/adaptive_verification.py:264`, called from `model_runner.sample_tokens`). Because the error is async, that frame is only where it is reported.

Serve command (relevant flags):

```
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 -tp 2 \
  --max-model-len 1040000 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --long-prefill-token-threshold 4096 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":"VLLM_COMPILE","cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":true}'
```

Load: closed-loop multi-turn chat, 96 concurrent streams, prompts 0.6K–118K tokens (~90% prefix-cache hits), outputs 8–5,000 tokens. The engine dies 30–60 s into the run, with ~90 requests running and the KV cache only ~3% used. We reproduced it 4 times in 4 tries across two nodes.

| Arm (same node, same load) | Result |
|---|---|
| adaptive verification **on**, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | IMA within 1 min at c96 (4/4) |
| adaptive verification **off**, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | stable: 30 min at c96 + 15 min at c128 |
| adaptive verification **on**, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` | stable: 15 min at c128 |

The fix only has to keep mixed/prefill batches out of FULL graphs while adaptive verification is on. That points at the same class as #59681 / #59751. In 0.31.0 the DSV4.1 FlashInfer sparse builders (`DeepseekV4FlashInferSparseMLAMetadataBuilder` and `DeepseekSparseSWAFlashInferMetadataBuilder` in `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py`, along with the compressor and FlashMLA builders) all declare `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS`. #59751 changes only the generic `FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMMetadataBuilder`, so it will not cover this path. The likely fix is the same move for these builders: `UNIFORM_BATCH` plus `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len` returning `max_decode_query_len(vllm_config)`.

Workaround: `enable_adaptive_verification: false`. Throughput was the same within noise (c128: 1,643 vs 1,608 out tok/s per GPU for on + `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`).

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Searched existing issues (#59681 and #59751 are related, but they cover the generic backend and `cudagraph_mode=FULL`).

title: [Model Runner V2] Optional post-capture warmup of every decode batch size, logits row count and graph size
body:
## Overview

Adds an opt-in startup pass to Model Runner V2, `--kernel-config '{"enable_batch_size_warmup": true}'` (default off). It runs right after CUDA graph capture. The pass runs one scheduler step for every decode batch size, every logits row count and every CUDA graph capture size. Each shape's first use then happens at startup, not on a live request.

## Claims

- After capture, each captured graph (target and drafter) gets replayed once. The pass reaches every uniform-decode batch size from 1 to `max_num_seqs` and one prefill at every capture size.
- The eager logits GEMM, the TP logits gather and the sampler/rejection sampler run at every row count a step can have: `q*a + c` rows with `a + c <= max_num_seqs`, where `q = num_speculative_tokens + 1`. That covers first-use cuBLAS heuristic selection, lazy CUDA module loading, Triton specializations and graph upload. Without this pass, each of these can stall the first request that reaches a new batch size.
- The plan depends only on the config, so every TP rank runs the same steps and collectives.
- With the flag unset, nothing changes.

## Validation

### Test plan

- CPU unit tests (new file `tests/v1/worker/test_batch_size_warmup.py`). They check the plan's coverage: every decode batch size, every reachable logits row count, and every capture size within the token/context limits. A stub worker replays the steps and checks the KV block reservations: lookahead included, block 0 never used, no block held by two live requests. The tests also check that every warmup request finishes, and that the pass skips when the KV cache is too small or under DP.
  ```
  pytest tests/v1/worker/test_batch_size_warmup.py
  ```
- `ruff check`, `ruff format` and `mypy` on the touched files.
- GPU check (not yet run on this branch). Start any V2 model with the flag and compare it with a run without the flag. Check the `Batch-size warmup ran N steps ... in X s` log line on every rank. Then check that `--jit-monitor-verbose` reports no compiles during a mixed-concurrency replay. For example:
  ```
  VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve <model> -tp 2 \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "eagle3", "model": "<draft>", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
    --kernel-config '{"enable_batch_size_warmup": true}'
  ```

### Test result

- Unit tests: 8 passed on CPU (macOS, torch 2.14.1). ruff and mypy are clean.
- GPU evidence comes from an earlier, larger, model-gated version of this mechanism, not from this branch. Setup: 8×B300, MiniMax-M3 NVFP4, TP2 engines with EAGLE3 (3 draft tokens) and CPU KV offload, an older nightly (`af7f9488c`) and our own benchmark harness. That version ran the same steps, but used dispatch introspection to skip graph sizes that were already hit. It also had an extra model-specific cuBLAS sweep, which is not part of this PR. We have not yet measured this PR on main.
  - **Without the warmup:** first use of a new batch size during serving JIT-compiled sampler kernels (`_topp_sb_*`, `_topk_topp_kernel`) mid-replay, and caused multi-second stalls. Separately, 5 of 94 TP2 engine runs hung. Each hang came on the first step of a new size (a new graph or eager lm-head row count), all within ~15 min of serving start. In one dump, one rank sat inside the first eager lm-head GEMM at a new M while its peer waited in the logits all-gather. We have not established the root cause of the hang. Pre-warming removes its precursor, but that does not prove it is fixed.
  - **With the warmup:** all 113 captured graphs replayed and 141 logits row counts ran (146 steps, about +5–12 s of startup at TP2, `max_num_seqs` 36, `num_speculative_tokens` 3). Serving logged no first-use JIT compile and no stall, and KV cache capacity was unchanged.
    - We then made the warmup the default for all our TP2 runs. Since then we have seen no further first-use hang. We did see one TP2 hang with a different signature: GPU-side, on a step that was not a first use. So this is not a fix for every TP hang.
    - Later runs without the warmup hung again on the first decode step at a new batch-size peak, inside the first-use cuBLAS lm-head GEMM.
    - GSM8K with the warmup in the stack matched the baseline.
    - We have no clean throughput A/B that isolates the warmup. It only changes startup, so we expect no steady-state effect.
- Startup cost of this branch's plan, as step counts from a CPU dry run (the time per step depends on the model):

  | max_num_seqs | num_speculative_tokens | Steps (with 26 capture sizes) |
  |---|---|---|
  | 36 | 3 | 167 |
  | 256 | 0 | 282 |
  | 256 | 7 | 2053 |

## Details

**Motivation.** The existing `warmup_kernels` runs before capture, at a handful of shapes, and targets the JIT registry and sampler features. It does not reach every batch size. Shape-dependent first-use work stays lazy until serving, as do the first replay of each captured graph and cuBLAS kernel selection for the eager lm-head GEMM at each M. Under TP, a first-use stall on one rank also holds its peers in the next collective. #48572 (open, V1 runner) fixes one instance of this: the spec-sized logits all-gather. This PR covers all row counts in V2.

**Design.**
- `plan_batch_size_warmup` (pure, unit-tested) builds the step list:
  1. Prefill a pool of `min(max_num_seqs, budget // (q+1))` requests.
  2. For `r = pool..1`, decode `r` requests. With spec decoding, also decode `r-1` of them next to `b = 1..q-1` new prefills.
  3. Run one prefill of each capture size.
- `warmup_batch_sizes` turns the steps into `SchedulerOutput`s and drives them through the worker's `execute_model`/`sample_tokens`, the same path as `warmup_kernels`.
  - KV blocks are reserved with the existing `_warmup_block_counter`, so lookahead is included. They start at 1 and are recycled after their request finishes.
  - The KV connector is disabled during the pass, and block 0 is re-zeroed afterwards, as in `warmup_kernels`.
  - Sampling uses the model's default generation-config parameters, the ones serving requests get by default. It does not use `for_sampler_warmup()`, whose `prompt_logprobs` would make capture-size prefills allocate full-vocab logits for every prompt token.
- A CPU dry run checks the block and context needs first. If they don't fit, the pass logs a warning and skips.
- The hook sits in `Worker.compile_or_warm_up_model`, after `capture_model` and before the seed reset.

**Why opt-in.** Startup time grows with `max_num_seqs × num_speculative_tokens`, and most deployments don't need it. It pays off for latency-sensitive or large TP deployments where a first-use stall is visible.

**Limitations.**
- Skipped for PP, DP, PCP, adaptive verification, pooling and encoder models. DP engines may size different KV caches and so plan different steps, which would desynchronize their DP collectives.
- The pass covers one decode query length, so dynamic speculative decoding is only partly covered. It does not cover eager steps above the largest capture size, where cuBLAS can pick new kernels at each M; `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=EAGER` is the M-independent backstop for module loading there. Prompt-logprobs shapes are also not covered.
- Some capture sizes may be warmed twice, because the plan does not ask the dispatcher which graph each step hits. That keeps the code small, at the cost of a few extra cheap steps.

title: [Model][MiniMax-M3] Split-KV indexer prefill scoring and sync-free prefill metadata
body:
## Overview

This PR makes two changes to the prefill side of the MiniMax-M3 MSA (SM100) indexer, `vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/indexer_msa.py`:

1. **Sync-free prefill metadata (always on).** The prefill score plan is now built from host lengths, and the page table from a gather index built on the host. This removes the two blocking device-to-host syncs in the metadata build.
2. **Split-KV prefill scoring (opt-in).** A new option, `attention_config.minimax_m3_indexer_prefill_kv_split`, splits the prefill index score's KV walk across CTAs when a long-context prefill would leave most SMs idle. The scores are bitwise identical to the unsplit plan.

## Claims

- **Bitwise identical scores.** Split and unsplit scores are equal by construction. This is checked with `torch.equal` in the new SM100 test.
- **No change to the default output path.** The split defaults to off. The sync-free metadata produces the same plan inputs and the same page table as before; only how they are computed changes.
- **Fewer GPU stalls on prefill steps.** The metadata build no longer calls `seq_lens.cpu()` or does a boolean-mask gather, so it does not wait for the GPU queue to drain.
- **Faster deep-context prefill scoring (split on).** Before this change, a short chunk at 200k context ran the index score on 11 of 148 CTAs. That score took 37% of the step in a B300 trace (see Validation). On an older nightly, end-to-end gains were +4.8% to +8.0% p90 tok/s/user and +1.6% to +3.0% tok/s/GPU (see Validation for caveats).

## Validation

**Unit tests (CPU).** `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_indexer_prefill_split.py` covers:
- the segment plan: partition, bottom-right causal offsets, no empty split, and the cases that stay unsplit;
- the page gather, compared against the boolean-mask gather;
- the host-length fallback.

I ran these helpers on CPU (11 passed). I also ran a stubbed-builder check over 2,000 random mixed batches: the page table and plan inputs match the previous code whenever the split is off.

**Kernel and impl tests (SM100).** I have not run these on this branch yet:
```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_indexer_prefill_split.py -k bitwise
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py -k test_msa_indexer_impl_matches_triton
```
- `test_split_prefill_score_bitwise` runs `_fmha_sm100` with the unsplit plan and with the split plan, for BF16 and FP8 index caches and 1, 2 and 4 index heads, at contexts up to 66k (2 to 29 splits). It asserts `torch.equal`.
- The impl-level MSA-vs-Triton parity test now also runs with the split on, and asserts that the split engaged.
- On a cold JIT cache, the split variant of the parity test first compiles the fmha_sm100 score variants, which takes a few minutes.

**Earlier GPU evidence.** These results come from the same mechanism as an out-of-tree patch on an older nightly (af7f9488c, MSA pin f355c37). They were not measured on this branch. The current main pins MSA be4a52a, so the kernel test above needs to pass on main before these numbers carry over. Setup: MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 on 8x B300, our own agentic-coding trace-replay harness.

- **In-engine bitwise check.** A debug mode re-ran the unsplit plan after every split score call and compared the two. Across 10 prefill steps (16k-token chunks, 16k to 66k context, 2 splits) × 57 layers, all 570 calls were bitwise identical with max |diff| = 0. A host-vs-device seq_lens check over the same run found 0 mismatches.
- **Trace (stock path, TP4, 2.7k-token prefill at about 211k context).** The indexer prefill score took 53.0 ms of a 144 ms step. Only 11 of 148 CTAs had work, and each walked 211k keys serially. The trace also showed a 4.8 ms host gap while the prefill metadata was built.
- **End-to-end, with both changes on.** Each config was run once for 3,600 s.

  | Deployment | Baseline | p90 tok/s/user | tok/s/GPU | TTFT p90 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | TP4, conc 40 | published reference config | +4.8% | +1.6% | +3.2% (1.795 → 1.853 s) |
  | 2× TP4, conc 64 | same deployment without this change | +8.0% | +3.0% | -1.7% |

  Caveats:
  - Our run-to-run noise floor is 2%.
  - The conc-40 baseline is a published point, not a same-harness run of stock code.
  - The conc-64 baseline had a 65 s mid-run JIT stall, and our router placed sessions less evenly in that run. Correcting for both gives about +5.6% to +7.7% p90 and +2.1% to +3.0% tok/s/GPU.
  - A short conc-10 screen was neutral (+1.7% / -0.7%, inside its 5% noise floor). Even there, the requests this targets (context of 32k or more, new prefill of 2k or less) had a paired median TTFT ratio of 0.92, about -25 ms.
- **Accuracy.** GSM8K was 0.971 with both changes on. GSM8K prompts are too short to engage the split (it needs at least 2k context), so the bitwise checks are the accuracy evidence for the split.

**Still to do before review (needs Blackwell):**
- The two SM100 tests above.
- A same-harness A/B on this branch with long prompts, for example `vllm bench serve` with random 64k-input prompts, short outputs and concurrency of 8 or more. Run it once with `--attention-config '{"minimax_m3_indexer_prefill_kv_split": true}'` and once without, and compare TTFT and throughput.

## Details

**Sync-free metadata.** `CommonAttentionMetadata.seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` is documented as exact on prefill rows; the Mamba builders already rely on this. The prefill builder uses it, with two guards:
- It falls back to the previous `seq_lens.cpu()` read if any prefill-side row has a query length within the decode threshold (such a row could be an async spec-decode row, where the bound is optimistic), if the bound is missing, or if it is inconsistent with the query lengths.
- The page table used a boolean-mask gather, which syncs on the result size. It is now a `(row, col)` index built with numpy, copied from pinned memory with `non_blocking=True`. An assert replaces the mask's silent clipping at the block-table width.

**Split-KV plan.** fmha_sm100 honors `num_kv_splits > 1` only on its 128-query tile, and its own adaptive split syncs on the plan cost. So when the unsplit plan would launch fewer CTAs than there are SMs, and the context is at least 2048 tokens, the builder does the following:
- **Segments.** Each prefill request is cut into segments of at most 128 queries. Segment `[s, e)` of a request with context `c` gets `kv_len = c + e` and offset `c + s`. Every query row therefore sees exactly the keys it sees in the unsplit plan.
- **Split count.** The count is chosen to fill about one wave of CTAs and is capped:
  - at 32;
  - at ≥4 256-key iterations per split, mirroring the fmha planner;
  - by a bound on workspace rows;
  - and so that no split is empty.
- **Exactness.** Only per-128-key-tile max scores are produced, and each tile belongs to exactly one split. There is no cross-split combine, so the result is exact.
- **Unsplit fallback.** Two shapes keep the unsplit plan:
  - more than one index head with segments of 32 queries or fewer, which would need pack-GQA split variants;
  - batches with padded tokens after the last request, where the per-split workspace would not match the score call's rows.

**Precompiling.** fmha_sm100 JIT-compiles each variant on first use, which takes about 1 min per variant. With the split on, warmup's long prefills take the split plan, so some unsplit variants were first compiled mid-serving: we saw a 65 s stall. When the option is on, the builder therefore compiles every OnlyScore variant either plan can select. It mirrors the library's dispatch, using its own `_compute_pack_factor`, and compiles 5 to 7 variants depending on the index-head count. If the compile fails, it logs a warning and disables the split.

**Why the split is opt-in.**
- It adds startup compile time on a cold cache.
- It allocates a cached fmha_sm100 split workspace outside vLLM's memory profiling: up to 2^18 rows × 128 × BF16 = 64 MB per device.
- Its benefit is measured only at TP4 (one index head per rank) on B300.

Default-on could be considered after the A/B on main.

**Scope.** The change touches only MiniMax-M3's NVIDIA indexer and its tests, plus one `AttentionConfig` field next to the existing `minimax_m3_msa_decode_backend`.

**Limitations.**
- The split helper reads fmha_sm100 private entry points (`_compute_pack_factor` and the JIT `get_fmha_variant`), so an MSA dispatch change could make the precompiled set stale. The cost would be a lazy JIT compile, not a wrong result.
- The NVFP4 index-K path is not exercised here.

---

title: [Model][MiniMax-M3] Context-parallel indexer decode scoring across TP ranks
body:
## Overview

Adds an opt-in, default-off decode path for the MiniMax-M3 MSA indexer on Blackwell (`VLLM_MINIMAX_M3_INDEXER_DECODE_CP=1`, TP 4 or 8). It shards the index-K blocks across TP ranks, so a rank no longer scores its head over the whole context. The ranks then merge an exact top-16. This is the NVIDIA (MSA/CuteDSL) counterpart of the ROCm proposals #57832, #57840 and #57909, and of the WIP #48649. All four are open and touch only the AMD indexer paths. This PR is independent of them and touches only the NVIDIA MiniMax-M3 files, plus `envs.py` and one CI line.

## Claims

- **Decode indexer cost per sparse layer (TP4, 8xB300, microbenchmark):** 88.3 → 45.5 µs at bs16 over 50k to 500k tokens of context, and 56.9 → 37.8 µs at bs16 with 170k tokens. This is 1.1 to 2.4 ms per decode step over the 57 sparse layers.
- **Serving, MiniMax-M3 NVFP4, TP4, concurrency 40, long-context agentic replay:** +7.7% p90 output tok/s/user and +0.9% tok/s/GPU against the same deployment without the flag (fast screen).
- **Same selection as the default path:**
  - the scores are bitwise identical;
  - the selected block ids are identical, except at exact fp32 ties that straddle the 16th place (see Details);
  - GSM8K is unchanged.
- **Off by default.** When the flag is off, the CuteDSL score kernel traces exactly as before (`cp_size == 1` resolves every `const_expr` branch to the old code).

## Validation

**Unit tests:** `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_indexer_decode_cp.py`, added to the Blackwell kernels CI step.
- `test_cp_topk_matches_full_topk` (any CUDA GPU, Triton): simulates 4 or 8 ranks on one GPU. Rank r's compact row is a strided slice of one full score tensor; columns the rank does not own are poisoned with `1e30`, so reading them would change the result. The all-gather is a stack. Every rank's merged top-16 must equal a full-context reference, bit for bit. The cases are:
  - random scores, heavy ties and clustered winners;
  - page counts 0, 1, 3, 15, 16, 17, 129, 2048, 2049, 5078, 8192 and 8197 (the last one is clamped);
  - with and without forced init/local blocks.
- `test_cp_topk_matches_sparse_topk_select` (SM100): the CP selection equals the default `fmha_sm100.sparse_topk_select` on tie-free scores.
- `test_cp_score_columns_match_full_score` (SM100): for bf16 and fp8, at query lengths 1 and 3/8, each rank's compact score columns are bitwise the default kernel's scores for the blocks it owns.

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_indexer_decode_cp.py
```

**Validation outside CI** (8xB300, MiniMax-M3 NVFP4). These runs used an earlier revision of this change on an older nightly (`af7f9488c`). They were **not re-measured on current main**.
- **Multi-GPU microbenchmark, 4 and 2 ranks, real custom all-gather (MNNVL Lamport kernel), 57-layer CUDA graphs, cold L2:**
  - 0 score-bit mismatches and 0 wrong selections in every case: ctx 4 to 1M, padded graph rows, bf16 and fp8 index cache;
  - ties appeared only in the heavy-ties case and were resolved as documented;
  - CUDA-graph replay was bitwise equal to eager.
- **Microbenchmark timing, TP4, µs per sparse layer (default → CP):**

  | decode batch / context | default | CP |
  |---|---|---|
  | bs16, 50k to 500k | 88.3 | 45.5 |
  | bs16, 170k | 56.9 | 37.8 |
  | bs16, 500k | 152.3 | 61.5 |
  | bs16, 50k (short context) | 22.9 | 27.3 (loss) |

  - **Two-level local top-k** (the revision in this PR), on the in-situ mix of one 0.65M-token request plus 7 requests of 56k to 162k tokens: 36.9 → 26.5 µs per layer compared with the earlier chunked local top-k. The selection is bit-identical.
- **Serving, TP4, concurrency 40, MTP speculative decoding** (fast screen, earlier revision with the chunked local top-k):
  - p90 tok/s/user 93.4 → 100.5 (+7.7%);
  - tok/s/GPU +0.9%;
  - TTFT p50/p90 0.45/1.33 s.

  A full-length run that also changed an unrelated KV-offload setting gave +12.1% / +4.1%. That number is confounded and is not claimed here.
- **Accuracy:** GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 docs) gave 0.9712 strict / 0.9704 flexible, identical to the run without the flag. The speculative-decoding acceptance length was unchanged (3.30).
- **TP2** was neutral in serving (+4.2% / +0.5%, inside noise), so this PR does not enable TP2.
- **Not validated end to end:** TP8. It passes the kernel tests, but it was not served.

The CPU-only checks ran the module and the test helpers with numpy ports of the Triton kernels and emulated rank threads. They cover TP4/TP8, query lengths 1 and 4, contexts up to 1M tokens and the gate conditions, and a mutation check confirmed the tests catch a wrong group decode. Lint: `ruff check`, `ruff format`, `typos` and `mypy` are clean on the changed files.

## Details

**Why it helps.** MiniMax-M3 has 4 index-query heads and one index-K head. The index-K projection is replicated across TP ranks, so in decode every rank reads the full index-K cache for its own head, every layer, every step. That read is the term that grows with context. Under CP, rank r scores all 4 heads but only blocks `j*TP + r`, which is 1/TP of the index-K reads. The added cost is two small all-gathers per layer:
- the index queries;
- `16*TP` int64 candidates per (token, head).

Neither depends on context length.

**Algorithm, per sparse layer, decode-only batches:**
1. **All-gather** the index queries. The score kernel reads the gathered buffer as a strided view through its TMA descriptor, with no permute copy; it falls back to `.contiguous()` if the strides don't meet the compiled signature.
2. **CuteDSL score kernel** with `cp_size`/`cp_rank`: it iterates only the owned blocks and writes compact columns.
3. **Two-level exact local top-16** over packed keys `1<<48 | ordered(score)<<16 | (0xFFFF - block)`. Forced init/local blocks get FLT_MAX, the same clamp and forced window as `sparse_topk_select`.
   - Stage 1 takes the max key of each of 128 groups and keeps the top-16 groups.
   - Stage 2 takes the top-16 over those groups' tiles.
   - This is exact because keys are unique: a top-16 key cannot sit in a group outranked by 16 other group maxima.
4. **All-gather** the candidates.
5. **Merge** the candidates of the rank's own heads into ascending block ids, padded with `-1`. This is the `sparse_topk_select` output contract, written into the shared `topk_indices_buffer`. The merge is exact because each rank keeps its full top-16, not 16/TP.

**Tie-break.** Exact fp32 ties at the 16th place are resolved differently from the default path:
- the CP path picks the lower block id, deterministically;
- the default `sparse_topk_select` order for such ties is not specified.

Every other selection is identical.

**Gating.** The fallback to the default path is automatic in each of these cases:
- **Batch-level (checked each step):** mixed prefill/decode batches; fewer than `VLLM_MINIMAX_M3_INDEXER_DECODE_CP_MIN_TOKENS` (default 32) decode tokens; more decode tokens than `max_num_seqs*(1+spec)`; or `heads x query_len > 32`, the score kernel's tile limit.
- **Configuration-level (checked once at startup, with a warning):** TP not 4 or 8; `decode_context_parallel_size > 1`; `topk_blocks != 16`.

The gate depends only on batch shape, so all TP ranks take the same branch. The path has no host sync, persistent buffers shared by all layers, and is CUDA-graph safe.

**Tradeoffs and limitations:**
- **Small batches or short contexts lose.** At bs16 with 50k context, CP costs 4.4 µs per layer more than the default, so the flag stays opt-in. The MIN_TOKENS default reflects TP4 measurements.
- **Scope:** NVIDIA MSA path only. The ROCm paths are covered by the PRs linked above. If maintainers prefer one knob for both, this could move to the `--attention-config` field proposed in #57909.
- **Complexity:** about 500 lines, almost all in a new self-contained module. Changes to existing code are small: 2 constexpr parameters in the score kernel, a 20-line branch in the MSA impl, and 2 environment variables.

title: [XPU][Spec Decode] RecoverSSM: route Qwen GDN through the Triton/FLA core on XPU
body:
Follow-up to #58863, as suggested there. **Stacked on #58863; only the last commit is new.** Independent of #59983 (PP > 1); either can merge first. The hardware numbers below come from one setup with both changes.

## Purpose

Only when RecoverSSM is active, this routes XPU through `forward_cuda` (the Triton/FLA core, where the RecoverSSM verify lives) instead of `forward_xpu`. Without RecoverSSM nothing changes on XPU, and nothing changes on other platforms.

Why: on XPU, `QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention` fixes `_forward_method` to `forward_xpu`, which calls the native XPU GDN kernel. That kernel still keeps per-draft states in speculative blocks, so with `--use-replayssm` it never reaches the RecoverSSM verify and fails in `_xpu_ops` with `spec_state_indices_tensor must be contiguous`. (The pointer-table overflow that also blocked XPU is already fixed in #58863.)

## Test Result

2× Intel Arc Pro B70, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next MXFP4, PP=2, MTP K=1:

| | native XPU GDN, no RecoverSSM | Triton/FLA GDN, no RecoverSSM | RecoverSSM |
|---|---|---|---|
| KV tokens per GiB | 15,474 | 15,360 | 22,784 (+47%) |
| single-stream decode | 32.0 ms/tok | 33.5 ms/tok | 33.3 ms/tok |

MTP acceptance stayed within the window-to-window variation (about 1.7–1.8 in all three). Greedy outputs are not deterministic run to run on this setup even without RecoverSSM, so we compared per-token logprobs over the common prefix against the Triton/FLA run (32 prompts, 1 and 13 concurrent): within the run-to-run noise.

- **Tested on hardware**: the same change on our own tree, which carries other local XPU patches that Flash-Next needs to start on XPU (e.g. for the Engram platform gate).
- **Not tested**: this exact branch on hardware, and the current #58863 head together with this change (our runs used a uint64 variant of the pointer-table fix instead of the bit-pattern version in #58863).
- `ruff check` / `ruff format` pass. No unit test yet: the dispatch is chosen in `__init__` on the XPU platform. Happy to add one with a mocked platform if that's wanted.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; every changed line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Keep DSV4.1 sparse prefill out of FULL cudagraphs
body:
## Overview

Fixes #59970. The five DSV4.1-specific sparse metadata builders declare `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS`, so with `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` prefill and mixed batches get FULL-graph captured even though their prefill metadata is not graph-safe, and the engine dies with an illegal memory access once adaptive verification runs mixed batches at concurrency. Downgrade them to `UNIFORM_BATCH` and report the speculation width as the varlen decode bound, mirroring the reviewed pattern from #59751.

## Claims

- Prefill and mixed batches leave FULL capture for all five builders named in #59970: `DeepseekV4FlashMLAMetadataBuilder`, `DeepseekV4FlashInferSparseMLAMetadataBuilder`, `DeepseekSparseSWAFlashInferMetadataBuilder`, `DeepseekSparseSWAFlashMLAMetadataBuilder`, `CompressorMetadataBuilder`. `FlashMLAMegaAttnBackend` inherits the same builder, so it is covered too.
- FULL varlen decode graphs are kept for uniform batches sized up to 1 + num_speculative_tokens, so DSpark adaptive verification keeps its decode graphs.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -q
```

82 passed on CPU. The 10 new parametrized cases pin, per backend and num_speculative_tokens in {0, 7}, that support resolves to `UNIFORM_BATCH`, that decode widths up to the speculation width stay graph-eligible, and that one token wider is rejected with the reported bound. Changed-file pre-commit (ruff-check, ruff-format) passed.

Not run: the B300 (SM103) end-to-end reproducer from the issue, no compatible hardware available here, and CI does not exercise these builders. The change only narrows what FULL graphs capture: prefill moves to the piecewise path that the issue's adaptive-verification-off and FULL_DECODE_ONLY arms already exercise for 30+ minutes under load, so no batch that was not captured before becomes captured.

## Details

Root cause, from the issue's arm table: adaptive verification on + FULL_AND_PIECEWISE hits the IMA 4/4 within a minute; verification off in the same mode is stable; verification on with FULL_DECODE_ONLY is stable. The failing ingredient is prefill inside FULL graphs. Each affected builder now also overrides `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len` to return `max_decode_query_len(vllm_config)` (1 + num_speculative_tokens on MRV2), the same width the V2 runner uses when it builds varlen decode replays.

Not a duplicate of #59751: that PR changes only the generic `FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMMetadataBuilder` for #59681, while the DSV4.1 model wires its own five builders, which the #59970 reporter calls out explicitly. Checked the issue thread and open PRs referencing #59970 before starting; nothing else covers them.

AI assistance: Kimi Code (Kimi K3) prepared the patch and tests; I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

title: [Bugfix] Offload model runner construction buffers on sleep
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #59158. Part of RFC #59055.

#59158 builds the KV-cache initialization state inside the `runtime` cuMem pool, so sleep backs it up to CPU and restores it on wake. Buffers that the model runner allocates in its constructor are still allocated outside every pool, so they stay on the GPU while asleep. On DeepSeek-V4-Flash with MTP, the drafter's `hidden_states` buffer (`spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py`) is 512 MiB/GPU.

The earlier revision of #59158 built the model runner inside the `runtime` pool too; that part was dropped before merge. This PR brings it back:

- `Worker` builds the model runner inside the `runtime` pool.
- The one-allocator-per-process check moves from the `weights` pool to that first pool entry.

## Test Plan

- New test `test_model_runner_buffers_survive_sleep` in `tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py` (levels 1 and 2): a buffer allocated while the runner is built lands in the `runtime` tag and keeps its contents across sleep and wake.
- `tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py`, with and without this change.
- GB300, DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP4 with MTP, level-1 sleep: memory while asleep, with and without `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend`, and outputs after wake compared with the awake run.

## Test Result

- The new test passes 3/3 with this change and fails 3/3 without it (`assert set() == {'runtime'}`).
- `test_cumem.py`: 16 passed with this change vs 14 on main; the 7 failures are the same on both sides (models not in the offline cache). `test_gpu_worker.py` + `test_sleep_mode_backend.py`: 29 passed on both.
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4, memory per GPU while asleep:

| | main (+ graph pool released) | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| sleep mode | 8633 MiB | 8121 MiB (−512) |
| + `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend` | 6451 MiB | 5939 MiB (−512) |

- The `runtime` tag grows from 4704 to 5218 MiB. Outputs after two wakes are identical to the awake run, and wake time is unchanged.
- Not yet covered: Model Runner V1 and GSM8K.

---

title: [Startup] Add an opt-in FlashInfer MoE search strategy
body:
## Overview

Expose FlashInfer's shorter ordinary-MoE search through `KernelConfig.flashinfer_moe_search_strategy`. This depends on [FlashInfer #6032](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6032); exhaustive search remains the default. The draft is for integration review and cannot merge until the API is available in the pinned dependency.

## Claims

- Pass the opt-in through the existing shared warmup, without changing the MoE backend, precision, graph settings or compilation-cache identity.
- Retain current main's per-stage tuning groups, cache persistence and exception cleanup.
- Leave the new FlashInfer keyword out of default calls, preserving their existing API contract.

```text
--kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true,"flashinfer_moe_search_strategy":"factorized"}'
```

## Validation

The preceding full-model experiment used the same opt-in on vLLM `ac68c3087`, with identical four-file overlays in both arms, on two B300s. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP2, 8k context, Engram CPU offload, local weights, normal graphs; one instrumented observation per condition:

| Empty preparation caches | Exhaustive | Factorized |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First correct response | 730.759 s | 523.674 s |
| FlashInfer tuning | 265.952 s | 58.452 s |

Four answer checks and 96 fixed-length serving requests passed per arm, with unchanged reported KV capacity. Prepared starts reused both workers' MoE caches without repeated MoE profiling. These bounded probes do not establish general accuracy or steady-state throughput. [Full result and limits](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6032).

The current-main transplant is separate from that performance measurement. On Linux, its isolated `tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py` suite passes 13 cases, including both runner signatures, PP-group/cache isolation, failure cleanup and unchanged compilation hash. The two candidate Python modules were overlaid on the pinned official runtime; this is not a full current-main image qualification. Both policies also pass a tiny CUDA warmup and fresh-process cache reuse with correct output and graph replay. Changed-file commit hooks pass, including mypy and Buildkite test tethering.

<details>
<summary>Unit command used in the pinned Linux image</summary>

The test file from this head was copied to an isolated directory to avoid the repository-wide serving fixtures. The process loaded the candidate config/warmup modules over the image’s existing dependencies and native binaries; loaded paths and source hashes were verified.

```sh
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 /tmp/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=/task/candidate/tests -p no:cacheprovider \
  /task/candidate/tests/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py -q
# 13 passed
```

</details>

## Details

Cached tactics are reused across strategies. Use a fresh tuning-cache directory to compare search policies or retune; changing this setting alone does not imply exhaustive search reruns.

This reduces uncached search. It does not duplicate [#59698](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59698), which skips warmup with a prepared cache, or [#57635](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57635), which changes per-rank persistence. Exact-option and factorized-search PR searches found no duplicate. [#55671](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55671) migrates to `autotune_v2`; that API remains exhaustive in the dependency PR and needs coordination before combining the changes.

The stock FlashInfer dependency does not yet support the opt-in. Keep this draft until the upstream API and dependency pin are available. AI assistance was used to prepare the implementation and checks.

title: [Bugfix] Free the pinned CPU weight backup on wake_up
body:
## Purpose

After the first level-1 sleep, every worker keeps a host copy of its weights in pinned memory for the rest of the engine's life, including while it is awake.

**Cause.**
- `CuMemAllocator.sleep()` backs each offloaded allocation up into `torch.empty(..., pin_memory=True)`. That memory comes from torch's caching host allocator.
- `wake_up()` copies the data back and drops the tensor. The caching host allocator keeps the freed pinned block resident for reuse, and it rounds every block up to a power of two.
- So host RSS never goes back down. On DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 (GB300), each worker goes from about 10 GB RSS before the first sleep to 55 GB awake: 48.5 GiB of cached pinned blocks for a 43.0 GiB backup. Per node, MemAvailable while awake drops from 881 GiB to 703 GiB.
- This matters for colocated RL, where the trainer runs on the same node and needs that host RAM while vLLM is awake.

**Fix.** The CPU backup becomes pinned memory that `cumem.py` owns explicitly, outside torch's caching host allocator. This is what `torch_memory_saver` (SGLang) does: its CPU backup is a raw `cudaMallocHost`, and by default it is freed right after the resume copy (retention is opt-in).
- `sleep()` allocates each backup with `cudaHostAlloc` at its exact size (`hipHostMalloc` on ROCm). The memory is exposed as a non-owning uint8 tensor, so `AllocationData` is unchanged.
- `wake_up()` frees each backup with `cudaFreeHost` (`hipHostFree`) as soon as it has been copied back. A partial wake (for example `kv_cache` only) keeps the backups of tags that are still asleep.
- The backup is also freed when its allocation is freed, and at allocator shutdown.
- `CudaRTLibrary` gets `cudaHostAlloc` / `cudaFreeHost` bindings with their HIP mappings. No private torch API is used.
- When pinned memory is unavailable (`PIN_MEMORY` is False), the backup stays a pageable `torch.empty`, as before.

**Cost.** The next sleep has to pin its backup again, so each sleep costs about what the first sleep on main costs. On V4-Flash TP4 this is about +1.7 s per sleep: 2.8 s instead of 1.1 s, measured on one node with an earlier variant that re-pins the same way. On the node in the table below, where pinning is slower, it is 3.65–4.10 s instead of 0.95 s. Wake gets 0.5–0.9 s slower because of `cudaFreeHost`. The first request after wake is unchanged.

V4-Flash TP4 EP, per worker, 3 cycles, on one GB300 node:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Worker RSS awake (after the first sleep) | 55.0–55.6 GB | 9.5–10.2 GB |
| Node MemAvailable awake | 703.5 GiB | 877.2–877.7 GiB |
| Worker RSS asleep | 55.0–55.6 GB | 53.4–54.1 GB (no power-of-two rounding) |
| Node MemAvailable asleep | 703.5 GiB | 709.0–709.5 GiB |
| Sleep | 4.06 s first, then 0.94–0.95 s | 3.65–4.10 s every time |
| Wake | 0.91–1.08 s | 1.58–1.82 s |
| First request after wake | 0.36 s | 0.36 s |

Alternatives I measured and did not pick:
- Keep `torch.empty(pin_memory=True)` and call `torch._C._host_emptyCache()` after wake. It releases as well as this PR, but it uses a private API, still rounds up while asleep (48.5 instead of 43.0 GiB per worker), and empties torch's whole pinned host cache, not only the backups.
- Backup in pageable `torch.empty` + `cudaHostRegister`: the torch CPU allocator does not return all of it to the OS. Workers kept 13–17 GB RSS awake, against 10 GB.

## Test Plan

- New test `test_wake_releases_pinned_cpu_backup` in `tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py`. It measures process RSS from `/proc/self/smaps_rollup` over two sleep/wake cycles with a 256 MiB `weights` allocation:
  - sleep must add at least the backup size;
  - a `kv_cache`-only wake must keep it;
  - the `weights` wake must give back at least half of it;
  - the weights must be bit-exact after every wake.
- The checks are per-cycle deltas, because an unrelated one-time RSS growth of about 100 MiB appears during the second sleep on both main and this PR.
- Mutation checks:
  - main;
  - this PR without `cudaFreeHost` on wake;
  - this PR with a wake that also frees the backups of tags that are still asleep.
- `test_cumem.py` (3 runs) and the sleep-mode suites: `sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py`, `model_executor/test_sleep_mode_tensor_ownership.py`, `entrypoints/serve/dev/test_sleep.py`. Each is compared with main.
- GB300 hardware: DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 EP, three sleep(level=1)/wake cycles, with 28 greedy probes compared against the awake reference after every wake. Each run ends with a SIGTERM while asleep, which exercises the shutdown free.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files.

## Test Result

- New test: 5/5 passed. It fails on main 3/3, fails 3/3 on each of the two mutants, and passes 3/3 on the `_host_emptyCache` variant.
- `test_cumem.py`: 22/22 passed, 3 runs (GB300, torch 2.13.0+cu130).
- Sleep-mode suites: 37 passed, 3 failed, 2 skipped, the same as main. The 3 failures are environment issues on both: a missing `kaldi_native_fbank`, a Voxtral config attribute, and a model that is not cached.
- V4-Flash TP4: probes 84/84 bit-exact. The numbers are in the table above. Clean SIGTERM shutdown while asleep: exit code 0, no Traceback, no shutdown error.
- `pre-commit`: all hooks pass (ruff check/format, mypy, typos, SPDX, test tethering, and the rest).

---

title: [Bug]: OffloadingConnector with LHBNC returns wrong output on CPU hits
body:
### Your current environment

vLLM 0.30.0 (ced6857), torch 2.13.0+cu129, NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe, driver 575.51.03. The code below is unchanged on main (0c16eee).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC` and the native CPU offload, a request whose prefix is loaded back from the CPU tier produces wrong output. There is no error or warning, and the blocks are counted as stored and as hits.

`register_kv_caches` builds a `(num_blocks, page)` view per layer with the layer's block stride, and treats any layer whose block stride differs from its page size as a packed layout:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0c16eee3f1ff777298cc894c3eeb85f3880c6d6a/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/worker.py#L104-L111

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0c16eee3f1ff777298cc894c3eeb85f3880c6d6a/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/worker.py#L133-L163

The comments assume a packed layout (DSv4) has block stride > page. LHBNC is the opposite case: the heads of one block sit a whole layer of blocks apart, so the block stride is `N*C` while the page is `H*N*C`. The packed branch then offloads `block_stride` bytes per block, which is head 0 of layer 0. (Before #51718 the packed case came from `is_kv_cache_tensor_packed`, not from this stride comparison.)

Repro (A100, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B: 48 layers, 8 KV heads, block 16):

```bash
VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B \
  --kv-offloading-size 30 --kv-offloading-backend native \
  --num-gpu-blocks-override 4500 --max-model-len 71936 --enforce-eager
```

1. Send a 7,060-token prompt at temperature 0. The prompt repeats a sentence about Gutenberg and ends with "Who combined movable metal type with a screw press, and around which year?".
2. Send a 71,900-token prompt so the first prompt is evicted from the GPU cache.
3. Send the first prompt again; its prefix is loaded from the CPU tier.

| | LBNHC | LHBNC |
|---|---|---|
| step 1 output | ` Johannes Gutenberg combined movable metal type with a screw press around 1440.` | same |
| step 3 output | same as step 1 | ` _140140101010101010101010101401` |
| GPU→CPU bytes for a 64K-token prompt (`vllm:kv_offload_total_bytes_total`) | 12.9 GB | 33.5 MB (1/384 = 1/(48 layers × 8 heads)) |

Expected: offload the whole page, or reject the layout at startup. `OffloadingConnector` prefers LBHNC, so only an explicit `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC` reaches this path.

Supporting LHBNC here is possible by offloading each (block, layer, head) slice separately, the way the offload handler used to split K/V-first caches (`kv_dim_before_num_blocks`), or more generally by letting connectors tell layout resolution which layouts they can handle. For now I propose failing at startup with a clear error, and I will open a PR for that. If the design discussion picks this up later, I am happy to help; feel free to ping me.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Reject LHBNC at startup
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #60004. With `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC`, `OffloadingConnector` offloads only head 0 of layer 0 per block, so CPU-tier hits return wrong output; reject that layout at registration instead.

### User case

1. A user sets `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC` and enables native CPU offload.
2. In `register_kv_caches`, a layer's block stride (`N*C`, 8 KiB) differs from its page (`H*N*C`, 64 KiB), so the layer takes the packed-layout branch meant for DSv4, where the stride exceeds the page.
3. That branch offloads `block_stride` bytes per block, which is head 0 of layer 0, and the block is still counted as stored and later as a hit.
4. A request whose prefix comes back from the CPU tier decodes from mostly unrestored KV. On DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B a 64K-token prompt stores 33.5 MB instead of 12.9 GB, and a question about Gutenberg is answered with ` _1401401010…` instead of ` Johannes Gutenberg … around 1440.`

The fix raises a `ValueError` in `register_kv_caches` when an attention layer's block stride is smaller than its page, naming the layer, both sizes and a layout to use instead.

Unchanged: LBHNC (the connector's preferred layout), LBNHC and the block-outermost layouts take the same paths as before. A one-head (MLA) cache under LHBNC has stride equal to page and is still accepted.

Not a duplicate: no open issue or PR covers this. The open PRs touching the offloading worker (#53544, #56076, #59265) change mapping placement, pointer resolution and quantized-layout preference, not this check. The stride comparison came in with #51718.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/
```

`test_register_kv_caches_covers_whole_page` builds the KV cache for every `KVCacheLayout` the way the engine does, marks one block in every layer, and checks that the offloaded regions hold all of its bytes. LHBNC must raise instead. The test fails on main.

## Test Result

```text
main:     1 failed, 484 passed  (test_register_kv_caches_covers_whole_page[KVCacheLayout.LHBNC]: DID NOT RAISE)
this PR:  485 passed
```

| DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B, A100 | LBNHC | LHBNC before | LHBNC after |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPU→CPU bytes, 64K-token prompt | 12.9 GB | 33.5 MB | — |
| output after a CPU-tier hit | correct | wrong | startup error |

<details>
<summary>Measurement details</summary>

- Unit tests: main (0c16eee) Python sources on a vLLM 0.30.0 precompiled build (torch 2.13.0+cu129), A100 80GB PCIe, driver 575.51.03. `register_kv_caches` is the same in 0.30.0 and main apart from the HiSparse condition.
- Engine runs: vLLM 0.30.0 with and without this patch, `--num-gpu-blocks-override 4500 --max-model-len 71936 --enforce-eager --kv-offloading-size 30 --kv-offloading-backend native`. Each check sends a 7,060-token prompt at temperature 0, then a 71,900-token prompt that evicts it from the GPU cache, then the first prompt again. Byte counts are deltas of `vllm:kv_offload_total_bytes_total`.
- With this patch, LBNHC still returns identical output for the first request, an immediate repeat and the CPU-tier hit; LHBNC stops at startup with `block stride 8192 B < page 65536 B`.
- This PR only stops the silent corruption. Supporting LHBNC would mean offloading one `N*C` slice per (block, layer, head) (8 KiB here, H times more descriptors, all below the 28 KiB DMA/Triton cutoff) plus per-head canonical mappings, or letting connectors declare the layouts they can handle during layout resolution. I left that to a design discussion (see the issue) and am happy to help with it.

</details>

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the investigation, code and tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and measurements on my own hardware.

title: [Bug]: TRITON_MLA is not batch invariant under chunked prefill with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (DeepSeek-V2-Lite, DeepSeek-V3.1)
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `main` at `f590eb2448a51028f6044c6f60104ce0ef3189e9`, torch 2.13.0+cu130
- NVIDIA GB300 (SM 10.3), driver 580.167.08, CUDA toolkit 13.1
- Models: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` (TP=1) and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1` (TP=4)
- Attention backend: `TRITON_MLA`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`

### 🐛 Describe the bug


With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the output of an MLA model changes when its prefill is split into chunks. Both DeepSeek models above fail the chunked-prefill test of the batch-invariance suite, while their needle tests and `bs1_vs_bsN` bitwise tests pass. Both are on the tested-models list in `docs/features/batch_invariance.md`.

**Repro**

```bash
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat \
  pytest -v -s "tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_ragged_chunked_prefill[TRITON_MLA]"
```

```text
AssertionError: Batch invariance violated under chunked prefill (max_num_batched_tokens=131):
prompt 1 (263 tokens): logprobs differ, max|delta|=8.945e-02; prompt 8 (248 tokens): tokens differ;
prompt 10 (97 tokens): tokens differ; ...
```

Three runs in fresh processes give the same failure and the same delta. `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1` fails the same test the same way.

**Isolation**

The difference does not need other requests in the batch. One prompt run alone, with only the token budget changed:

| `max_num_batched_tokens` | Prefill | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4096 | one chunk | reference |
| 131 | several chunks | selected-token logprobs differ from the first step (about 1e-3), sampled tokens differ from decode step 9 |

Other observations:

- With `max_num_batched_tokens=4096` the batched test input shows no mismatch. With 512 one prompt still mismatches.
- `enforce_eager=True` still fails, so CUDA graphs and `torch.compile` are not needed to trigger it.
- Prefix caching is off (the test disables it, and it is disabled for `TRITON_MLA` in batch-invariant mode).

Since chunk boundaries depend on the scheduler's token budget, and so on the other requests in the step, this makes the output depend on batch composition.

**Suspected area (not proven)**

The MLA prefill path for a chunk that has cached context (`_compute_prefill_context` in `mla_attention.py`): cached context is gathered and up-projected per context chunk, attended separately, and combined with `merge_attn_states`. A single-chunk prefill does not go through that merge, and merging LSE-rescaled partial results is not bitwise associative. I have not instrumented it at layer level. #46592 discusses canonical chunk boundaries for a related reason (prefix caching).

**CI coverage**

The Batch Invariance jobs run the full `test_batch_invariance.py` only with the default model. For `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` they run only the needle test with `-k TRITON_MLA`, so the chunked-prefill test (added in #55612) is not exercised for `TRITON_MLA`.

I only ran this on GB300, but nothing in this path looks Blackwell-specific. Happy to run more experiments on this hardware.



### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Model][Core] Register every persistent device tensor as a parameter or buffer
body:
## Overview

Sleep mode level 2 discards the weights memory pool. On wake, only `model.named_buffers()` are restored in place, and parameters come back through the weight update. A device tensor that is built at load and kept as a plain attribute is therefore garbage after sleep level 2 + wake.

This PR fixes each such tensor at its own site. Most fixes are `register_buffer(name, t, persistent=False)` with the same tensor object, so addresses do not change. It adds no walker, no exemption table and no CI scan. Context: #54477, #50079.

## Fixed (one site each)
- NVFP4 linear emulation: the layer holds the E2M1 lookup table as a buffer.
- Humming linear (MXFP4/6/8, NVFP4, mixed precision, FP8/INT8 scaled-mm, `HummingLinearMethod`): `locks` is a layer buffer.
- `Attention`: `_k_scale_cpu`/`_v_scale_cpu` are created on CPU explicitly. ALiBi slopes / fp32 sinks (impl-derived state) moved to #62634 (runtime cuMem pool, as in #62358).
- `_k_scale_cpu`/`_v_scale_cpu` are created on CPU. They were built under the target-device context, so on main they landed on the GPU.
- DSv4.1 mega attention: the `permute_on_load` permutations are built on CPU (the weight-loader closures keep them).
- DSv4.1 fused mHC all-reduce: `_stage_state` is a model buffer.
- Model constants are buffers: GraniteSpeech `attention_dists`, Phi-4-MM `pe`, Bailing/MiniMax `tp_slope`, Gemma4 MTP `_suppress_idx`, Gemma4-DSpark `_v_norm_weights` (constant ones), OpenPangu-VL `inv_freq`.

## Known limitations / follow-ups
- MoE kernel tensors (experts constants, activation gscales, MXFP4 permute cache): follow-up PR.
- Kimi-K3 latent-MoE tail fusion still raises under sleep mode; unchanged here.
- Kimi-K3 `SpecializedDecode` state is built at load in the weights pool. It is off by default and rejects sleep mode.
- Held by non-module objects: DCP workspaces, EPLB maps, MiniMax Lamport workspace, Qwen4Exp `ngram_context_offsets`.
- LoRA slots: handled by #62358 (LoRA state restore on level-2 wake).
- Same pattern, left out: ROCm/XPU-only sites, INC `ark_bias`, CT wNa8o8 static scales, FlashAttn-MLA-sparse `cu_seqlens_q_buffer`, Qwen4Exp deepstack embeds.
- Weight-derived copies (DFlash, Gemma4-DSpark k-norm stack, Kimi-K3 DSpark context-KV norm weights/scales, beam DFlash2, LiLiCorr, DSv4/DSv4.1 `hc_attn_fn_broadcast`) stay plain attributes. Layerwise reload skips copying non-persistent buffers it did not load, so registered copies would come back stale. Fix that in reload first.
- Staleness after weight updates, not sleep (#57733 territory): MoE fused router/shared gate, GLM5-next `_wp_fp32`/`_merged_conv_weight`, CPU attention sinks cast, and non-persistent derived buffers on layerwise reload.
- Risk, IPC weight cache + DSv4.1 fused mHC: an IPC client replaces `_mhc_ar_stage_state` with the daemon's tensor, so it no longer aliases the kernel state and sleep restores the wrong memory.

## Validation
- `pre-commit` (incl. mypy) passes.
- Sleep A/B on GB200, main vs this PR, same node and config, real weights, CUDA graphs on. Per run: greedy baseline on 8 prompts (tokens + logprobs), cold GSM8K, then 3 x (`sleep(level=2)` -> wake -> restore -> regenerate), GSM8K after the last wake. Restore (i) = `reload_weights()` from the checkpoint; (ii) = in-place restore via `sleep_preserve_parameter_names=["*"]`. Backends were checked from the loaded model.

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Register compressed-tensors block-FP8 weight scale as weight_scale_inv
body:
## Overview

`CompressedTensorsW8A16Fp8` registers its block-strategy weight scale as `weight_scale` in
`create_weights`, and only renames it to `weight_scale_inv` in
`process_weights_after_loading` — i.e. *after* loading. A checkpoint that stores that tensor
as `weight_scale_inv` therefore cannot load: `LinearBase.load_weights` finds no matching
attribute (`param = getattr(self, name, self)` in `layers/linear.py`), falls back to the
module itself, and the layer's `weight_loader` raises

    AttributeError: 'MergedColumnParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'data'

Register the block-strategy scale as `weight_scale_inv` from the start — the name the plain
FP8 path registers (`quantization/fp8.py:339`; MoE FP8 uses
`"weight_scale_inv" if self.block_quant else "weight_scale"`, `quantization/fp8.py:486`) and
the name this scheme renames it to anyway — and keep the post-loading rename behind a
presence check so parameters created by the old path still get renamed.

This scheme is not exotic: `CompressedTensorsConfig.get_scheme`
(`compressed_tensors.py:851-868`) falls back to it for block-FP8 weights wherever the FP8
W8A8 kernel is unsupported, so block-FP8 artifacts that carry dynamic activation quant still
land here on SM80-class devices.

Refs #43564 (its load-time strand; the issue was closed stale without a fix).

## Claims

- A compressed-tensors FP8 **block** checkpoint whose scale is stored as `weight_scale_inv`
  now loads instead of failing on the missing parameter name, and such a model serves:
  load + generation verified end-to-end (see Validation).
- A regression test pins the naming contract (red on unpatched `main`, green with the fix).
- No numerics change: only parameter naming at load time. After loading, the block strategy
  ends up with exactly the same single parameter (`weight_scale_inv`) holding the same data.
- TENSOR/CHANNEL strategies and every other compressed-tensors scheme are untouched.

## Validation

All runs below use vLLM at `f03026a548` + this patch, on an NVIDIA A100-PCIE-40GB (SM80),
`tensor_parallel_size=1`, `enforce_eager=True`, engine in-process.

1) Regression test (added by this PR), red/green:

    $ pytest tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py -k w8a16_fp8_block_scale -x -q
    # unpatched main:  1 failed
    #   AttributeError: 'MergedColumnParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'data'
    # with this patch: 1 passed        (1.78s, no model download, no GPU kernel work)

The failing frame is the same one a real deployment hits:
`layers/linear.py:987 load_weights` -> `param.weight_loader(...)` -> `layers/linear.py:767
param_data = param.data`.

2) End-to-end reproducer on a real engine. Scratch conversion of `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`: every
`*.weight` under `model.layers.*` is block-128x128 quantized to FP8 E4M3 with per-block
`weight_scale_inv` (the naming a real block-FP8 artifact uses), and `config.json` gets the
`quantization_config` of a real block-FP8 artifact (weights: 8-bit float, block [128,128];
inputs: dynamic group-128) — the configuration that routes to this scheme on SM80:

    $ python -c "from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams; \
      llm = LLM(model=<converted Qwen3-0.6B>, max_model_len=512, enforce_eager=True); \
      print(llm.generate(['The capital of France is'], SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=16))[0].outputs[0].text)"

    # unpatched main:
    ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight_scale_inv'
    in Qwen3Model. The available parameters belonging to layers.0.mlp.down_proj
    (RowParallelLinear) are: {'layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight_scale', 'layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight'}

    # with this patch:
    Loading weights took 0.18 seconds
    KV cache size: 99,360 tokens, Maximum concurrency for 512 tokens per request: 194.06x
    init engine (profile, create kv cache, warmup model) took 11.60 s
    OUTPUT>>> ' Paris. The capital of France is also the capital of the French Republic. The'

(The two failure surfaces — `AttributeError` and the loader's name check — are the same
missing parameter name seen along two loader paths.)

Model evaluation: **not applicable** — no weight, scale or activation value changes and no
kernel selection changes; the only difference is the parameter name during loading.

## Details

Root cause: vLLM is internally inconsistent about this tensor's name. The plain FP8 path
registers `weight_scale_inv` for block quant (`quantization/fp8.py:338-339`, commented
"intentional for deepseekv3"), and this compressed-tensors scheme *also* renames to
`weight_scale_inv` after loading — but it registers `weight_scale` *during* loading, so a
`weight_scale_inv` checkpoint has nothing to match.

Why this is not a duplicate (checks run 2026-10-05 against open PRs/issues):

- #43290 and #43723 fix the **opposite** direction (artifacts storing `weight_scale` where
  vLLM expects `weight_scale_inv`) and are model-file specific (DeepSeek-V4).
- #42657 only transposes `weight` in `process_weights_after_loading` (Marlin shape
  heuristic); upstream has since absorbed that with `.t()` + dim tags.
- #53107 / #53118 only make `LinearBase`'s missing-parameter error clearer — the load still
  fails.
- #52966 (merged) added the post-loading rename for Marlin; it does not touch `create_weights`.
- #43564 requested this direction and was closed stale without a fix; the load-time PR its
  comment thread points to (#43655) is closed and unrelated (DSV4 quant_config plumbing).
- Searches that produced this list: `gh issue view 43564 --comments`,
  `gh pr list --state open --search "43564 in:body"` (empty),
  `gh pr list --state open --search "compressed tensors fp8 weight_scale_inv"`,
  `gh pr list --state open --search "compressed_tensors_w8a16_fp8"`.

Compatibility (both readers handle either name, so post-loading behavior is unchanged):

- `quantization/utils/marlin_utils_fp8.py:197-201`:
  `if hasattr(layer, "weight_scale"): … elif hasattr(layer, "weight_scale_inv"): …` — both
  branches write the same permuted scales to whichever name exists.
- `quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py:53-65` `get_fp8_block_weight_scale()`: Quark → `weight_scale`,
  otherwise → `weight_scale_inv`.

The delete-then-rename block stays behind `if "weight_scale" in layer._parameters`, so any
parameter created by the old path is still renamed. Complexity: 1 file changed, 0 lines of
logic removed, well under the "low complexity" bar; the second file is the regression test.

AI assistance: **yes** — the patch, the test, and this description were produced with AI
assistance, per vLLM's agent instructions. The validation commands and their raw outputs are
included above so a reviewer can reproduce them.

---

title: [ROCm][Attention] Support multimodal Prefix-LM in ROCM_ATTN
body:
## Overview Add bidirectional image-token attention to ordinary `ROCM_ATTN` for multimodal Prefix-LM models such as Gemma3. Related to [#48172](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48172) and the ordinary-backend portion of [#59095](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59095). ## Claims - Support global, sliding-window and window-clamped image attention using shared Triton mask helpers. - Enable MRV2 `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` where image prompt extensions can safely replay the causal decode graph, including fixed multi-token speculative verification. Preserve MRV1 eager/`PIECEWISE` compatibility. - Protect context block-table boundaries and invisible cached NaNs; fix a pre-existing zero-token padding write in paged decode. ## Validation Gemma3-4B IT BF16 on Radeon 8060S (`gfx1151`), AITER disabled; PyTorch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0, Triton 3.8.0. The focused attention tests pass 43 cases, and image-prefill hidden states pass the existing HF comparison. Pre-commit, Python 3.12 mypy and diff checks pass. Model evaluation and attention regression use `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.
Upstream test commands ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 export VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/attention/test_mm_prefix.py \ tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py \ tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py \ -k 'rocm_prefix or prefix_lm or rocm_backend_sliding_window or qwen3_nonstandard_block_size or cached_kv_block_table_boundary' -q .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_mm_prefix_lm.py -k ROCM_ATTN -v ```
**Accuracy:** AI2D test subset of 512 distinct diagrams, shuffled with seed 20261005; identical order, one run per configuration, greedy generation, batch 8, at most 8 output tokens, no prefix cache. Invalid formats count as incorrect. | Runner / decoding / graph mode | ROCM_ATTN correct | TRITON_ATTN correct | | --- | ---: | ---: | | MRV2 ordinary / eager | 354/512 (69.14%) | 357/512 (69.73%) | | MRV2 ordinary / PIECEWISE | 351/512 (68.55%) | 352/512 (68.75%) | | MRV2 ordinary / FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | 353/512 (68.95%) | 352/512 (68.75%) | | MRV2 speculative (3 draft tokens) / PIECEWISE | 354/512 (69.14%) | 355/512 (69.34%) | | MRV2 speculative (3 draft tokens) / FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | 354/512 (69.14%) | 355/512 (69.34%) | | MRV1 ordinary / PIECEWISE | 354/512 (69.14%) | 353/512 (68.95%) | Full-mode backend comparisons match complete token sequences on 510/512 ordinary and 507/512 speculative samples. Actual full decode replay was verified at widths 1 and 4. Longer-output speculative smoke matches 8/8 sequences across ROCM full, ROCM piecewise and Triton full, with nonzero draft acceptance. Small output differences remain. Speculative decoding uses a fixed budget of 3 draft tokens per step, which the target model verifies. The text-only Gemma3-270M IT validation copy has 64 zero embedding rows appended to match target vocabulary 262208, preserving existing tokenizer IDs. Adaptive verification is disabled. **Performance:** End-to-end offline medians in milliseconds, five paired repeats per configuration. Prefill = T1; decode = `(T65−T1)/64` per sequence output token. Initialization/compilation/warmup excluded; image execution included. EOS ignored, detokenization and prefix cache disabled. title: [ROCm][Perf] Call aiter.paged_mqa_logits for the sparse indexer decode logits
body:
## Purpose

Review feedback on #59422: vLLM should ask AITER for paged MQA logits and let AITER pick the kernel, instead of carrying a Gluon/FlyDSL switch that changes every time one of the kernels improves. This calls AITER's `paged_mqa_logits` (`from aiter.paged_mqa_logits import paged_mqa_logits`, imported lazily like `aiter.fused_moe`) for the sparse indexer decode logits on gfx942/gfx950. AITER picks Gluon or FlyDSL, and their launch knobs, from its tuned table (ROCm/aiter#6140), the same model as its fused-MoE dispatch.

vLLM passes the same tensors it passes to the Gluon kernel today and no backend knobs (`ChunkK`, `WavePerEU`, `SplitKV`). When the installed AITER has no `aiter.paged_mqa_logits` module, the existing Gluon call runs unchanged, so this is a no-op until vLLM's AITER pin includes the op.

## Dependency

ROCm/aiter#6140 (`aiter/paged_mqa_logits.py`, its tuned table and tuner).

## Details

- The 2D `(B, next_n)` `seq_lens` table is passed through as-is: `aiter.paged_mqa_logits` takes `[B]` or `[B, next_n]` and reduces to one length per sequence itself, so this path does not need #59420.
- No change to the C4A / Triton / torch paths or to non-gfx942/gfx950 archs.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_paged_mqa_logits.py` (new): the AITER op gets the caller's tensors, the 2D `seq_lens` and only `Preshuffle` / `KVBlockSize`; the Gluon call runs when AITER lacks the op.
- MI355X, real tensors through `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` with the 2D `seq_lens` table, against the torch reference, with ROCm/aiter#6140 installed. Shapes picked to hit both backends in the tuned table.

## Test Result

- Unit test: 2/2 pass on MI355X.
- Real tensors (`AITER_LOG_TUNED_CONFIG=1` shows the pick):

| batch | next_n | context | AITER pick | calc_diff vs torch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 3 | 8192 | gluon ChunkK=128 WavePerEU=4 | 9.2e-11 |
| 256 | 3 | 8192 | flydsl | 8.5e-11 |
| 8 | 1 | 32768 | gluon ChunkK=256 WavePerEU=4 | 7.5e-11 |
| 64 | 8 | 8192 | flydsl | 8.5e-11 |

- Kernel level (from ROCm/aiter#6140, MI355X, GLM-5 indexer shape, batch 1..256, `next_n` 1..8): the tuned pick vs the Gluon `ChunkK=256, WavePerEU=2` this file passes today is -10.8% geomean at 8k context and -17.1% at 32k; FlyDSL is picked on 16 of 72 shapes, all at batch >= 32.
- End-to-end serving benchmark and accuracy: not run yet.
