title: [Bugfix][Core] Count only held blocks against the sliding window admission cap
body:
## Purpose

Fixes a scheduler deadlock with asynchronous KV loads (KV connectors) on models that have sliding-window or chunked-local KV cache groups.

`_request_remaining_blocks` (#44560) reserves, for every request whose KV is still loading, the blocks it will need to resume prefill, so that further loads are not admitted into that space. For recycling-aware groups the reservation is capped by `max_admission_blocks_per_request`, but the cap was compared with `len(req_to_blocks)`, and that list pads the positions outside the window with null blocks. For a request with a long computed prefix the length far exceeds the cap, the subtraction comes out negative, and the sliding-window reservation becomes zero, even though every prefill chunk still needs one slot per token in those groups. The non-fast path has the same problem through `num_skipped_blocks`.

With the reservation undercounted, loads keep being admitted until the free pool is smaller than one prefill chunk of the queue head. The head cannot allocate, `schedule()` breaks on it, and because nothing is running there is nothing to preempt: the engine sits at `Running: 0` forever.

**Observed in serving.** DeepSeek-V4-Flash (full-attention plus sliding-window KV groups with block sizes 4 and 8) served with pipeline parallelism, the CPU `OffloadingConnector` and DSpark speculative decoding, with contexts up to 1M tokens. While serving, the engine stopped at `Running: 0, Waiting: 20` and never recovered. The scheduler state, dumped from the live `EngineCore`:

- 16 requests had finished their async loads and were waiting to resume; the connector had no jobs in flight.
- The free pool held 502 blocks; the sum of the in-flight reservations was 168.
- The queue head (645,989 prompt tokens, 638,720 computed) needed 846 blocks for its next 2048-token chunk, 771 of them in the two sliding-window groups. Its reservation was 30.

**Fix.** In the capped branch, count the blocks from the first one still inside the window, capped, and subtract the real blocks the request already holds (the non-null suffix of its block table) and the real blocks among the effective prefix hits. Execution allocation is unchanged; only the reservation and the admission estimate move. The uncapped path keeps its previous arithmetic.

**Cost.** The capped branch no longer takes the running-request fast path, but `apply_admission_cap=True` is only used at admission time: by `_request_remaining_blocks` when a new async load is admitted, and by `allocate_slots(full_sequence_must_fit=True)`. Per-step allocation for running requests still uses the fast path. Inside the branch, the backward scan stops at the first null block, so it is bounded by the cap (the window plus in-flight tokens, in blocks).

### Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs and issues touching `max_admission_blocks_per_request`, `_request_remaining_blocks`, `get_num_blocks_to_allocate` and the sliding-window admission path (2026-10-05):

- #55818 caps execution allocation at the window and drops the in-flight term from the admission cap, which reverses the invariant covered by `tests/v1/core/test_swa_inflight_window_free.py` (out-of-window blocks must stay allocated until the step that reads them has been processed). This PR leaves allocation unchanged and only fixes the reservation.
- #42568 lets a queue head that cannot allocate be skipped instead of breaking. It would mask this deadlock in some shapes but does not fix the undercounted reservation.
- #50169 changes drafter grouping and pool sizing and explicitly leaves the runtime admission gate unchanged.
- #39734 is the origin of the admission cap; this PR keeps its semantics.

## Test Plan

New tests:

- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py::test_async_load_reserves_sliding_window_blocks_for_inflight`: full attention plus a sliding-window group (block 16, window 32), pool of 160 blocks, two 1280-token requests each async-loading 1024 tokens. Before the fix both loads are admitted and no tokens are ever scheduled after the loads complete; the test asserts that the scheduler makes progress.
- `tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py::test_admission_accounts_for_prefix_hits`: for SWA and chunked-local, with shared hits, evictable hits and plain allocation, the capped estimate must equal the blocks the allocator actually pulls.

Regression suites, run on a GPU node with and without the fix (`vllm/` reverted, tests kept):

```bash
pytest -q tests/v1/core \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector
```

End to end: the serving configuration above was restarted with the fix and the workload that triggered the deadlock was replayed for 30 minutes.

## Test Result

- Regression suites, with the fix: 1436 passed. Without the fix: 1431 passed, 5 failed. The 5 failures are exactly the new tests: the deadlock reproducer and the four capped cases of `test_admission_accounts_for_prefix_hits` (its two uncapped cases pass on both sides, as the uncapped path is unchanged).
- End to end: the 30-minute replay completed with 0 errors and 0 preemptions; without the fix the same workload deadlocked. The change only affects scheduling, so model output is unchanged.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, implement, test and draft this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Preserve exact P/D replay endpoints (stacked on #59197)
body:
## Overview

Preserve an exact direct P/D KV endpoint when every transfer-enabled replay group is loaded, while still replaying a missing Decode-only/local group. **Draft, stacked on and dependent on #59197.**

The branch contains exactly #59197's two prerequisite changes plus this follow-up, rebased onto main `710ac56e691d4713feca50a43e6c440f07d373fd`. **The two prerequisite commits will be removed after #59197 merges**, leaving only the endpoint fix for review and merge.

## Claims

- Keep `512 + 86 = 598` as the external-load endpoint instead of rounding the external hit to 64 and ending at 576. A missing local replay group still rebuilds from `598 - 128 = 470`.
- Avoid querying connector loaded-group state on a zero external hit.
- Retain the replay-start block at 32/64-token boundary-minus-one endpoints, with matching admission-memory accounting. The Mooncake regression preserves source pairing `8 -> 829`, `9 -> 499`.

## Validation

**Checks run on this new three-commit stack:** changed-file pre-commit passed across all nine changed Python files, including Ruff check/format, typos, mypy 3.10, SPDX/import/config checks, and Buildkite test tethering. Changed-file mypy 3.12, Python 3.12 compilation, AST parsing, and `git diff --check` also passed. Exact added/removed-line comparison passed for each of the three source-to-ported commits. The worktree is clean.

Commands run from the new worktree (zsh; compile-cache path abbreviated):

```sh
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv
uv pip install -r requirements/lint.txt
changed_files=("${(@f)$(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD)}")
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files "${changed_files[@]}"
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files "${changed_files[@]}"
PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX="/path/to/artifact-cache" .venv/bin/python -m compileall -q "${changed_files[@]}"
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

**Local pytest was intentionally not run.** The existing suites now include the exact endpoint/local replay, zero-hit, boundary-retention, and Mooncake source-pairing regressions. Their execution on this rebased stack remains pending:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py -v
```

**Prior GPU integration evidence, supplied by the submitter and checked against the existing validation report:** H20 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with Mooncake; TP8/PCP1 and TP4/PCP2 Prefill arms shared the fixed Decode overlay at source revision `24cc448760f1d7e412c32690a7f8229714861f09` (DP8/EP8, DSpark K5, Decode prefix caching and bounded replay enabled).

| Gate | TP8/PCP1 post-fix control | TP4/PCP2 integration candidate |
|---|---|---|
| EOS handoff | Passed | Passed |
| 8193-token cold/repeat Mooncake | Passed; identical 64 output token IDs | Passed; identical 64 output token IDs |
| Direct-client C16, three consecutive runs | 15/16 each; zero cross-associations, token caps, or infrastructure failures | 15/16 each; zero cross-associations, token caps, or infrastructure failures |
| GSM8K200 | 194/200; zero length finishes | 194/200; one PCP residual request reached the 65,536-token cap |
| P/D transfer metrics | Zero failed transfers, failed receives, or expired requests | Zero failed transfers, failed receives, or expired requests |

GSM8K used EvalScope 1.11.1, ModelScope GSM8K, four-shot prompts, limit 200, batch/concurrency 16, seed 42, temperature 0, top-p 1, reasoning effort high, and max tokens 65,536. The candidate's broader PCP correctness gate remains incomplete despite matching numerical accuracy. These GPU runs used integration overlays containing additional changes; GPU validation has not been rerun on the newly rebased upstream stack. No isolated performance improvement or general PCP support is claimed here.

## Details

The old replay decision required every replay group to appear in connector loaded-group IDs before preserving an unaligned external endpoint. A Decode-only group with `enable_kv_transfer=False` therefore forced a valid 86-token direct hit down to 64 tokens. Prefill ended at 598, while Decode allocated for 576, shifting Mooncake's tail-aligned source pairing.

Separate the conditions: loaded transfer-enabled replay groups determine whether to preserve the exact endpoint; all replay groups determine whether replay can be skipped. A missing local group keeps replay enabled without shrinking the peer endpoint. Bounded-replay sliding windows retain one additional token, and the admission bound includes that retention.

Stack mapping:

| Source | Ported commit | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `4b8d4c186699801a94157189a283c6c864fc81fd` | `6f1959930b76e9284eb4c1f8f213b8d693a83fc3` | #59197 loaded-window replay contract |
| `58f4a61f258aac28b227015ce5fd62ac3f9e3a7c` | `438cfbc0ee80367faa1777983060e38b0537c330` | #59197 bounded-replay N-1 handoff |

Review the follow-up separately at [4e8385161e](https://github.com/wangyicong52/vllm/commit/4e8385161e1fd5f0da43dc4894d34b7c70e4b303). One Mooncake test-context conflict was resolved by keeping only the exact pairing regression. title: [Bugfix] Register the aten::mm out_dtype overloads for batch invariance
body:
## Overview

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` and an fp32 lm_head (`--hf-overrides '{"head_dtype": "float32"}'`, which
`ModelConfig` documents as "required for RL training-inference consistency"), the head runs
`torch.mm(x, w, out_dtype=torch.float32)`. That call dispatches to `aten::mm.dtype`, a separate overload
from `aten::mm`, so on CUDA SM8x, where batch-invariant mode installs the Triton matmul overrides, it
stays on cuBLAS. Whether the result then depends on the batch size depends on the shape: on an A40,
Mistral-7B-v0.1 (vocab 32000) shows it and Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B (vocab 151936) do not. This PR registers
`aten::mm.dtype` and `aten::mm.dtype_out` next to `aten::mm`.

## Claims

- **Bug:** on `main`, Mistral-7B-v0.1 with an fp32 head gives different logprobs at batch size 1 and 32
  for 32 of 32 prompts on an A40. In an earlier run on an A40 (`main` 34051ad714, driver 595.91.07,
  2026-10-05), Qwen3-0.6B (bs 32) and Qwen3-1.7B (bs 64) with an fp32 head showed no difference; there,
  `torch.mm(out_dtype=fp32)` gave the same row 0 for every M tested at N = 151936, but not at N = 4096,
  8192 or 32000.
- **Root cause:** `aten::mm.dtype` and `aten::mm.dtype_out` are separate overloads of `aten::mm`, and
  `enable_batch_invariant_mode()` does not register them.
- **Fix:** one function, `mm_dtype_batch_invariant`, is registered for both overloads.
  `matmul_persistent()` takes an `out_dtype` and allocates its output in that type; the kernel already
  accumulates in fp32 and casts on store. The function keeps ATen's dtype checks for these overloads
  (for each case the same `RuntimeError` and message as `_mm_dtype_out_cuda`); shape errors still come
  from `matmul_persistent`, as with the existing `aten::mm` override.
- **Scope:** only the CUDA SM8x branch, and every `torch.mm(..., out_dtype=)` there, not just the
  lm_head. In-tree, that is also `GateLinear` tier 5 (the cuBLAS bf16→fp32 router GEMM), the non-SM90
  branch of the Inkling MoE router and the DeepSeek-V4 compressor/indexer scores. On the A40, `GateLinear`
  tier 5 was batch dependent on `main` at all four router shapes tested and is invariant with this PR.
  The lm_head runs eagerly (`compute_logits` is outside the compiled graph) and reaches `aten::mm.dtype`;
  `aten::mm.dtype_out` is what Inductor emits for the compiled callers. Hopper and Blackwell do not install
  the Triton overrides. XPU is unchanged: the fp32-head path is CUDA/ROCm only, and XPU's `aten::mm`
  override uses `matmul_descriptor_persistent`, which this PR does not touch. ROCm has no Triton matmul
  overrides on `main`; #52231 adds them and registers `aten::mm.out`, not `aten::mm.dtype`, so the same
  gap would reach ROCm when it lands.
- **Cost:** with the flag on, the fp32 head GEMM runs on the Triton persistent matmul instead of
  cuBLASLt. On the A40 that is 0.2–0.3 ms slower per call up to M=32 (Mistral-7B head shape), about the
  same at M=128 and 9% slower at M=512. It did not show in `vllm bench serve`.

## Validation

Commands, output excerpts and the full logs: [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60047#issuecomment-6012055668) and
[the dtype-check follow-up](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60047#issuecomment-6044314681). NVIDIA A40 (SM86), vLLM nightly wheel for
`main` `30ab428235` (`0.30.1rc1.dev708+g30ab42823`), torch 2.13.0+cu130.

- `pytest tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py::test_mm_out_dtype_batch_invariance`
  fails on `main` (8166 of 8192 values of row 0 differ between M=1 and M=32) and passes with this PR.
- `test_mm_out_dtype_keeps_aten_dtype_checks`: with the flag on, invalid `out_dtype` / `out` dtypes raise
  the same errors as ATen (passes on `main` and with this PR; failed on the PR's earlier head).
- End to end, `repro_60047.py`: 32 of 32 prompts differ between batch size 1 and 32 on `main`
  (max |Δ logprob| 5.531e-05), 0 of 32 with this PR. Greedy tokens did not change in either run.
- `vllm bench serve` with the fp32 head, two runs per side (main, this PR, this PR, main): 3.87 and
  3.86 req/s on `main`, 3.86 and 3.88 req/s with this PR.

The new tests run in CI's A100 Batch Invariance job (`-k mm_out_dtype`, one line added here); the B200
job, which runs the whole file, skips them because Blackwell installs no Triton overrides.

## Details

- **Related:** #52231 (open) adds batch invariance on ROCm, including the `.out` overloads of
  mm/addmm/bmm. #59985 (open) turns `GateLinear` tier 5 off under the flag; on SM8x it overlaps with this
  PR there, without conflicting. #59952 (draft) rewrites `matmul_persistent`, and #55249, #54503, #55466
  and #60034 also edit these files, so one of them will need a small rebase.
- **Not a duplicate:** on 2026-10-06 I searched all vLLM PRs for `"mm.dtype"`, `"mm.dtype_out"`,
  `out_dtype batch invariant`, `head_dtype batch invariant`, `fp32 lm_head batch invariant` and
  `logits fp32 batch invariance`; the only match is this PR.
- **Not changed:** `aten::bmm.dtype` and `aten::bmm.dtype_out` have the same gap, but no in-tree caller
  uses them.
- **Limitations:** the fix was verified end to end on one model (Mistral-7B-v0.1) on one GPU (A40). It
  was not run on A100 or XPU.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change and to run the measurements. I reviewed every changed line and the logs.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Preserve dummy tokens across PIECEWISE padding
body:
## Overview

Fix MRV2 `draft_model` adaptive profiling startup when PIECEWISE padding expands draft input beyond its compiled range. Initially discovered during Gemma3 Prefix-LM validation for [#60040](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60040), then independently reproduced on upstream with **Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B (target) + Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (draft)** on **TRITON_ATTN and ROCM_ATTN**, confirming a shared MRV2 dummy-path bug independent of #60040's Prefix-LM changes.

## Claims

- Preserve valid dummy query counts across PIECEWISE input padding, retaining room for draft correction tokens.
- Keep trailing tokens marked as padding and write context positions only for valid queries; preserve FULL dummy query reshaping.
- Cover padding/context behavior and PIECEWISE dispatch with two focused tests, including a FULL varlen control.

## Validation

Actual **`vllm serve`** runs and HTTP requests on a single gfx1151 Radeon 8060S, BF16, AITER disabled, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. All patched runs show nonzero draft acceptance and FULL/PIECEWISE execution in native metrics/logs. No worker monkeypatches or profiling skips.

### Qwen3: independent upstream validation

**Target: `Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B`; draft: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`.** 

| Backend | Before | After | GSM8K, 128 questions |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| **TRITON_ATTN** | Startup fails: `1032` outside `[1,1024]` | 16/16 smoke requests completed | **83/128 (64.84%)**, 0 invalid |
| ROCM_ATTN | Same startup assertion | 16/16 smoke requests completed | **82/128 (64.06%)**, 1 invalid |

Smoke requests include eight ordinary prompts and eight boundary prompts of 65–1800 tokens. GSM8K uses five shots, greedy, 256 output tokens, seed 0 and concurrency 8. Draft/accepted token counts: Triton **13,923/11,047** (smoke + GSM8K), ROCm **14,466/10,958** (smoke + GSM8K). Both backends completed all 128 evaluation requests successfully; the ROCm invalid answer could not be parsed as a numerical answer.

<details>
<summary>Qwen3 serve and GSM8K commands</summary>

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0
export VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error

.venv/bin/vllm serve ~/models/Qwen3-1.7B \
  --served-model-name adaptive-validation --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8017 \
  --dtype bfloat16 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --seed 0 \
  --max-model-len 2048 --max-num-seqs 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.3 --kv-cache-memory-bytes 2147483648 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --cudagraph-metrics \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8,12,16,32,512,1024]}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"draft_model","model":"/home/tang/models/Qwen3-0.6B","num_speculative_tokens":3,"enable_adaptive_verification":true}'
```

```bash
.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py \
  --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 8017 \
  --num-questions 128 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 \
  --temperature 0 --seed 0 --max-concurrency 8 \
  --save-results /tmp/gsm8k-adaptive-triton.json
```

For ROCm, replace `TRITON_ATTN` with `ROCM_ATTN` in the serve command and repeat both the smoke requests and GSM8K evaluation, changing `--save-results` to `/tmp/gsm8k-adaptive-rocm.json`.

</details>

### Gemma3: integration validation with #60040

The bug was initially discovered during Gemma3 validation for [#60040](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60040). The Qwen3 reproduction above confirms it also occurs independently of that PR's Prefix-LM changes.

**Target: `google/gemma-3-4b-it`; draft: `google/gemma-3-270m-it`.** The text-only draft uses a local validation copy, `gemma-3-270m-it-vocab262208`, with **64 zero embedding rows appended** to match the target vocabulary size of 262208; existing tokenizer IDs are preserved. Baseline: #60040 head `309e622d88`; after: that head plus this fix.

| Backend | Before | After | AI2D, 128 diagrams |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| **TRITON_ATTN** | Startup fails: `1032` outside `[1,1024]` | 8/8 smoke requests completed | **88/128 (68.75%)**, 0 invalid |
| ROCM_ATTN | Same startup assertion | 8/8 smoke requests completed | **87/128 (67.97%)**, 1 invalid |

Smoke covers single-image, two-image and text requests; all six color/shape/arithmetic checks pass on both backends. AI2D uses 128 unique diagrams shuffled with seed 20261005, greedy, 8 output tokens and batches of eight concurrent requests; invalid answer formats count as incorrect. Response text matches on **127/128** samples. Draft/accepted counts (smoke + AI2D): Triton **570/140**, ROCm **579/146**.

<details>
<summary>Gemma3 serve command</summary>

Run from a checkout containing #60040 plus this fix, retaining the environment variables in the Qwen3 commands:

```bash
.venv/bin/vllm serve ~/models/gemma-3-4b-it \
  --served-model-name adaptive-validation --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8017 \
  --dtype bfloat16 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --seed 0 \
  --max-model-len 2048 --max-num-seqs 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.3 --kv-cache-memory-bytes 2147483648 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":2}' --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --cudagraph-metrics \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8,12,16,32,512,1024]}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"draft_model","model":"/home/tang/models/gemma-3-270m-it-vocab262208","num_speculative_tokens":3,"enable_adaptive_verification":true}'
```

Repeat with `ROCM_ATTN`. AI2D requests use `/v1/chat/completions` with `image_url` content and instruct the model to return only the option letter.

</details>

These runs validate startup and serving; they do not establish general adaptive accuracy parity or performance improvements.

<details>
<summary>Regression and style commands</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -o addopts= \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch_v2.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py -q
# 50 passed, 3 skipped

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -o addopts= \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_dispatch.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch_v2.py::test_dummy_context_preserves_token_padding \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py::test_dummy_dispatch_preserves_piecewise_token_budget -q
# 150 passed, 5 skipped; 3 existing Ray-dependent cases failed before Ray was installed

uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python 'ray==2.56.1'
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -o addopts= \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py::test_parallel_config_manages_decode_sharding -q
# 3 passed
```

Restoring the original `execute_model` and `set_dummy_context` functions makes the two regression cases fail; the FULL control still passes. Existing worker CI covers these files on H200 and MI355. NVIDIA and multi-GPU execution were not tested locally.

</details>

## Details

`_dummy_run` reserves eight correction slots (1024 → 1016), but PIECEWISE dispatch pads to 1024 and dummy preparation counts that padding as valid queries. Draft expansion then produces 1032 tokens. Passing valid and padded counts separately through `InputBatch.make_dummy` restores the distinction already used for real requests.

This fixes the additional startup bug discovered while testing #60040; #60040's Prefix-LM changes are used only for Gemma3 integration validation and are not included in this patch. Qwen3 + Triton reproduces the problem without Prefix-LM.

Duplicate check (2026-10-05): no direct duplicate found. #54065/#54077 adjust profiling splits, #56182 separates profiling passes, #58984 handles DP request padding, and #55990 refactors standalone drafting

AI assistance was used for implementation, review, and validation.

---

title: [refactor][model] Kimi-K3 DSpark MLA common base class
body:
## Purpose

Currently, the Kimi-K3 DSpark draft model has only one NVIDIA implementation,
and the dispatch is hard-wired to it on every platform. A ROCm module that copies that file drifts.
This PR moves the draft model into `vllm/models/kimi_k3/common/dspark_mla.py` and leaves NVIDIA as a thin binding.
NVIDIA behavior stays the same: the same `MultiHeadLatentAttention`, the same layer name, and the same kernels.
The registry still loads `vllm.models.kimi_k3.nvidia.dspark_mla`:
removing the hard-wired dispatch is left for a follow-up PR (#60857).

## What changes

- The decoder, context-KV insert, weight mapper, Markov head, and confidence head live once, in `common/dspark_mla.py`. That file imports neither `amd/` nor `nvidia/`.
- NVIDIA supplies `build_self_attn` and `build_mlp`. `kv_cache_layer` defaults to the attention module, so context-KV insert and `get_draft_kv_cache_layer_names()` still use `self_attn`.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py` passes.
- Existing tests cover the registry class, the weight mapper, duplicated context-KV shards, the replicated Markov head, and the compile-free entry point. Construction monkeypatches target `vllm.models.kimi_k3.common.dspark_mla`.
- New tests check that the NVIDIA binding's attention class is `MultiHeadLatentAttention`, that `kv_cache_layer` returns the attention module, that a wrapper subclass's `mla_attn_cls` is constructed with a `prefix` ending in `.attn`, and that the default hooks return their inputs.
- The file is collected in Basic Models, including the CPU job. Main's newer DeepSeek and layer-registry entries in that job stay on the command line.

## Details

AMD and  NVIDIA attention and cache architecture for MLA differ: NVIDIA `MultiHeadLatentAttention` owns the KV cache, while the AMD stack is `KimiK3MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper` around a generic `MLAAttention` whose `layer_name` is `prefix + ".attn"`. Geometry, norms, and context RoPE   already sit on `self_attn` on both sides. This PR refactors so that the three reads that differ (cache, dtype and scale, layer name) go through `kv_cache_layer`.

- `common/` does not construct the NVIDIA attention class. A default there would import `nvidia.mla`, which is also the NVIDIA target K3 attention.
- `#58814` pointer refresh is in the shared path: `_has_uniform_block_layout` keys the cache on `data_ptr()` and drops `_context_cache_ptrs` when the allocation changes.
- `enable_confidence_head` builds `DSparkConfidenceHead`, keeps those checkpoint weights, and `compute_confidence` serves adaptive verification. The head stays `None` when the flag is off.
- `MLAAttention` stores positions as `_rope_positions` (assigned every forward, including `None`). The wrapper takes `mla_attn_cls`. Three hooks default to today's behavior: `_prepare_kv_cache_update`, `_prepare_mha_inputs`, and `_form_decode_q`. Custom-op schemas stay as they are.         Positions are module state the ops read.
- CUDA-graph replay sees new positions and slot mappings only while those tensors stay the persistent buffers the runner updates in place. Replacing either tensor freezes the captured pointer. Comments on both sites say so.

A planned fusion of QK-RoPE plus cache insert (fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla) requires an epilogue to replace query formation and the KV write.
The fusion cannot live only in the draft model: Absorb runs inside `MLAAttention.forward_impl`, and `unified_mla_kv_cache_update` cannot take `positions`.
This PR adds three defaulted hooks as an extension point for this decode epilogue, to avoid needing a second refactor immediately after this. The defaults do not read `_rope_positions`.

The Kimi-K3 DSpark MLA is under active development, causing a naive duplicate-and-modify approach to quickly drift, as shown by #57942:
- #58814 pointer refresh (`_kv_cache_ptrs_key`, drop `_context_cache_ptrs` when the cache is rebound).'
- Grouped FP8 context-KV insert (see commit [f589f93](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/f589f93347b951b0763b6d0991c3b2f298fc6159))
- Missing confidence head.

Refactoring reduces the drift, allowing both platforms to gain new features in a single change.

## Out of scope

- The AMD binding and the ROCm registry dispatch (#60857).
- AITER `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla` (#60864).

## Suggested review order

Review by commit. The aggregate diff looks like a rewrite of `nvidia/dspark_mla.py` because that path stays as the public binding, so Git does not record a rename.

title: [Attention][MLA] Add DCP support to Triton sparse MLA
body:
## Purpose

Add decode-context-parallel (DCP) correctness to the `TRITON_MLA_SPARSE` backend introduced by #47629.

Under DCP, each rank computes attention over only its KV-cache shard. The shared MLA path can combine those partial outputs only when the backend also returns each shard's softmax log-sum-exp (LSE). The Triton sparse backend currently returns `(output, None)`. It also converts the indexer's global top-k token positions with the non-DCP converter, which can map positions owned by another rank through the local block table and read unrelated cache rows.

## Dependency / stacked-PR note

This draft is intentionally stacked on #47629 because `TRITON_MLA_SPARSE` is not in `main` yet. The DCP change is the single top commit, `7994efeb68`. Once #47629 merges, GitHub will reduce this PR to that commit. Until then, the earlier commits in the diff belong to #47629 and should be reviewed there.

## Changes

- Opt `TritonMLASparseImpl` into the shared DCP output/LSE reduction.
- Expose natural-log LSE from the single-pass and split-KV Triton kernels. Both kernels already maintain the online-softmax maximum and denominator, so this surfaces existing state rather than recomputing attention.
- Make an empty rank-local sparse row return the merge identity: zero output and `LSE=-inf`.
- Filter global top-k positions by DCP ownership and convert surviving positions to rank-local KV-cache rows, respecting `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size`.
- Preserve the DCP-gathered runtime query-head count instead of slicing output/LSE back to the pre-gather local count.
- Warm the LSE-returning specialization before serving when DCP is enabled, preserving the backend's no-JIT-during-capture behavior.

## Not duplicate work

- #47629 adds the Triton backend but does not localize indices for DCP or return LSE.
- #46514 and its release backport #54541 solve the analogous problem for **FlashMLA sparse**, not Triton.
- #47779 targets the **FlashInfer SM120** sparse wrapper.
- #48196 optimizes the shared DCP merge after a backend has produced valid partial outputs and LSE; it does not make this backend produce them.

No open PR found by searches for `TRITON_MLA_SPARSE DCP` and `triton sparse MLA LSE` implements this backend-specific fix.

## Testing

Production B200 image:

- `pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_mla_sparse_kernel.py`
  - **57 passed**
  - Includes single/split LSE parity, dense `logsumexp` comparison, and empty-row merge identity.
- Focused new tests after a cold compile:
  - **4 passed**
- Full pre-commit suite on the four changed files:
  - **passed**, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX, forbidden-import, and CUDA-API checks.

Downstream integration validation used the generalized 320-wide Triton variant that exposed this bug: an exact-shape TP2/DCP2 sparse attention-layer test passed against dense SDPA. A full served-model evaluation has not been run for this draft.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex was used for investigation, implementation, testing, and drafting. This remains a draft pending human review of every changed line and confirmation that the submitter can defend the change end-to-end.

title: perf: persist FlashInfer multi-CTA-KV counter buffer in sparse MLA
body:
## Summary

FlashInfer's `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` (sparse MLA decode) builds a
fresh runner on every call, so the trtllm-gen multi-CTA-KV kernel's semaphore
counter region is re-allocated and re-zeroed each decode step. That shows up as a
`FillFunctor<uint8>` launch before every FMHA kernel — one per layer per step —
sitting on the serial attention critical path at small batch sizes and
contributing nothing but latency.

This PR ports the persistent-counter pattern already used by SGLang and by vLLM's
dense MLA path (`flashinfer_mla.py`) into the sparse path
(`FlashInferMLASparseImpl.forward_mqa`): vLLM now owns a persistent, lazily-grown,
zero-initialized uint8 counter buffer passed via `multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer`.
The kernel self-resets its semaphores at the end of each launch, so the buffer is
zeroed once and safely reused across CUDA-graph decode iterations.

Key details:
- Optional-API probe (`_FI_HAS_MULTI_CTAS_COUNTER_API`) preserves behavior on
  FlashInfer < 0.6.16.
- The buffer is handed over only when the Q head count is tileable per
  trtllm-gen's CTA tiling rules and the KV page size is 32/64.
- Sized at `__init__` for the scheduler worst-case batch and max head count
  (including DCP gather): allocated once during warmup, never after graph capture.
- `VLLM_DISABLE_PERSISTENT_MLA_COUNTER=1` restores the original per-step
  behavior for A/B comparison.

## Performance

GLM-5.2-NVFP4, 4x B200 (TP=4), BS=1, ISL=4, OSL=2048, fp8_e4m3 KV cache. Both
arms measured on the same binary/image and FlashInfer build; baseline = feature
disabled via the env toggle.

| Metric | Baseline | Patched | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 130.8 | 132.5 | **+1.35%** |
| Mean ITL (ms) | 7.591 | 7.490 | **-1.33%** |

Verified reproducible across two independent runs (+1.05% / +1.35% throughput).
Nsight Systems confirms the mechanism: the `FillFunctor<uint8>` launch fires
3,900x in the baseline trace (78 layers x 50 steps) and 0x in the patched trace;
decode step wall time drops by the corresponding ~124 us.

## Correctness

GSM8K (lm_eval, 200 samples, identical harness for both arms):
flexible-extract 0.930 -> 0.955, strict-match 0.930 -> 0.955. No quality loss.

## Tests

New `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_counter_buffer.py`: 26 CPU-runnable
tests covering head-tileability and counter-bytes formulas, buffer lifecycle
(allocate-zeroed / reuse / grow / device change), dispatch behavior with a fake
FlashInfer kernel (eligibility, fallback paths, env disable), nope-MLA
`sparse_mla_top_k_lens` coexistence, and startup logs. Local run: 24 passed,
2 skipped (intentional: FlashInfer/CUDA not installed). Pure Python change —
one source module + one test file, no recompilation needed.

AI-based Amalgamator was used to prepare this PR. Human reviewed changes.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] KV-only insert for the DSpark context KV
body:
## Overview

The DSpark context KV insert built a zero query of [tokens, local heads, 512] and ran the fused Q+KV insert on it, then dropped the query.
This PR enables the KV-only fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert (#56441), as the NVIDIA DSpark model already does.

## Claims
MI355X, 16,384 context tokens per call: no extra memory, 18-19 us per call instead of 163-602 us.

test_dspark_context_kv_matches_query_insert, CUDA-only so far, now also runs the ROCm function on ROCm (byte-exact against the query insert, all four cache records, with and without graph replay).

This leads to less memory usage (no dummy query tensor) and faster kv insert for dspark.

Deepseek-v4 ROCm DSpark has the same issue but this PR focuses on dsv41.


## Validation
16,384 context tokens per call (a full prefill chunk):

| cache format | local heads | old: transient | new: transient | old: µs per call | new: µs per call | max abs diff, old vs new |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fp8_ds_mla (584 B) | 16 (TP4) | 512 MiB | 0 | 166 | 19.1 | 1.9e-6 |

| per-tensor fp8 | 16 / 32 / 64 | 384 / 768 / 1,536 MiB | 0 | 182 / 324 / 599 | 17.4-17.8 | 0 |


DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4 on MI355X, DSpark 5+1, GSM8K (lm-eval, 5-shot, chat template, thinking at effort high

| | GSM8K strict | flexible | DSpark acceptance length |

title: [MoE] MXFP4 oracle: add CUTLASS W4A4 backend and BF16 activation fallback
body:
## Purpose

First step of #54959 for the packed MXFP4 MoE methods. This PR only touches the MXFP4 oracle; no quant method changes behaviour yet.

**Contract.** The `activation_key` passed to `select_mxfp4_moe_backend` is the activation precision the checkpoint declares (`None` = BF16). Backends that match it are preferred. If none supports the deployment, the oracle falls back to BF16-activation backends and logs a warning, so a W4A4 checkpoint runs as W4A16 on hardware without a W4A4 kernel. Activations are never quantized below what the checkpoint declares.

Previously a non-`None` key was an exact filter, so a W4A4 checkpoint raised on any deployment without a W4A4 kernel (including `--moe-backend marlin`). This matches the MXFP4 linear kernels, where weight-only kernels already accept MXFP4 activation keys as a fallback.

**CUTLASS W4A4 backend.** `CUTLASS_MXFP4_MXFP4` (vLLM's `CutlassExpertsMxfp4`) is added to the oracle: enum, kernel class, scale swizzle in `convert_weight_to_mxfp4_moe_kernel_format`, quant config and 128 round-up. Today that kernel is only reachable through device probes hand-rolled in `CompressedTensorsW4A4Mxfp4MoEMethod` and `INCMxfp4MoEMethod`.

**Behaviour change for existing callers.** Callers that pass no activation key (gpt-oss) and callers of `select_deepseek_v4_mxfp4_moe_backend` (DeepSeek-V4, Kimi-K3) select the same backend as main for every `--moe-backend` value I compared. Callers that already pass a key (online MXFP4, Quark W4A4 and static-FP8 W4A8) change only where main raises:

| Caller | `--moe-backend` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Online MXFP4 / Quark W4A4 | auto | raises | CUTLASS W4A4 |
| Online MXFP4 / Quark W4A4 | marlin, flashinfer_trtllm, triton_unfused, humming | raises | that backend, BF16 activations |
| Quark W4A8 static FP8 | auto | raises | TRTLLM BF16 |
| Quark W4A8 static FP8 | marlin, flashinfer_trtllm, triton_unfused, humming | raises | that backend, BF16 activations |
| gpt-oss with `quantization_config.moe.activation=mxfp8` | marlin, triton, triton_unfused, humming | raises | that backend, BF16 activations |

Measured on NVIDIA SM103 without `amd-quark`. I have not loaded a model through these newly reachable combinations, and could not measure ROCm. With `amd-quark` installed on CUDA SM100, W4A4 would select CUTLASS ahead of EMULATION.

**Relation to #59460.** The fallback is the default here; #59460 (`VLLM_STRICT_QUANT_SCHEME`) is the opt-in to refuse it. This PR passes BF16 fallback backends their own key, so whichever lands second should pass the checkpoint key through and let `executed_activation_key` report the downgrade, replacing the warning added here.

**Why this is split out.** #55232, #56306 and #56523 each move the CUTLASS swizzle into the oracle and each add a different selection path next to it (an `input_quant` flag, `select_w4a4_mxfp4_moe_backend`, a `candidates=` list). The mechanical part is the same in all three; the selection contract is what differs and what review has stalled on. This PR settles the contract in the existing `activation_key` argument, with no new entrypoint. A follow-up reduces the compressed-tensors and INC methods to weight creation plus oracle delegation.

Not a duplicate: those PRs change the quant methods; this one does not, and is intended as the base they (or the follow-up) build on.

**Follow-up motivation (measured on main, NVIDIA B300).** `CompressedTensorsW4A4Mxfp4MoEMethod` selects `CutlassExpertsMxfp4` with MXFP4 activations for every checkpoint and every `--moe-backend` except `b12x`, including weight-only (A16) checkpoints, and fails on shapes that are not 128-aligned (`shape '[960, 34]' is invalid for input of size 36864`).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py -k select_mxfp4
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py -k oracle_matches
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_b12x.py tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py \
  tests/quantization/test_gfx950_moe.py tests/quantization/test_online.py \
  tests/quantization/test_quark.py tests/quantization/test_auto_round.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_kernel_selection.py
pre-commit run; pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual
```

- `test_select_mxfp4_moe_backend_respects_checkpoint_activation` (CPU): exact match wins, BF16 fallback (auto and explicit backend), BF16 checkpoint never quantized.
- `test_cutlass_mxfp4_oracle_matches_direct_kernel` (SM100): the oracle-built kernel equals calling `run_cutlass_moe_mxfp4` with manually swizzled scales.

To check the API is sufficient, I also prototyped the follow-up (compressed-tensors method as a thin `Mxfp4MoEMethod` subclass that passes the checkpoint activation to this oracle) and compared it with main through a real `RoutedExperts` layer on a B300.

## Test Result

NVIDIA B300 (SM103): 2552 passed, 77 skipped, 5 failed across the suites above. The same 5 fail on unmodified main on this machine and are unrelated (Int8 unsupported on SM103, a DeepGEMM JIT panic, MXFP8 AutoRound). pre-commit and mypy pass.

Three of the four new selection cases fail on main and pass here.

Follow-up prototype vs main (layer harness, random MXFP4 weights, B300):

title: [Perf][HiSparse] Cache per-request residency instead of rescanning every page each step
body:
## Purpose

HiSparse decode is CPU-bound on main because of one scheduler-side scan. Every step, `HiSparseCoordinator.all_context_pages_resident` walks every page of every scheduled request in every resident group (one group per layer), only to decide whether prefill can skip host staging. That is O(requests × context pages × layers) Python per step, even for pure-decode batches.

The scan arrived in c4b9b7deac ("bypass host resolution for resident decode"), after the GLM-5.3 results in #53781 were measured, and shipped with 3/N. This PR caches the requests whose resident pages are all non-null. A request is scanned once. Pages become null only at admission or host import, before the first scan, or when the pool reuses an unpinned page (`_lose_page`), so those paths plus `free` drop the cache entry. The per-step check is O(requests).

HiSparse-only change (`vllm/v1/hisparse/coordinator.py`). Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this scan.

## Results

GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on B200, fp8 KV, block 64, random prompts, 1k output tokens. Each point is one run, main vs. this PR back to back on the same node and config. The gain tracks how much resident context the scan walks per step relative to GPU step time: it's largest when every page is GPU-resident and contexts are long. It disappears at low concurrency, and in the host-offload regime, where the old scan already exited at the first host page.

| TP | input | concurrency | peak KV | main tok/s | this PR tok/s | Δ | mean TPOT main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 16k | 64 | 61% | 764 | 1209 | **+58%** | 73.3 → 42.0 ms |
| 4 | 16k | 40 | 76% | 809 | 906 | **+12.0%** | 40.9 → 35.7 ms |
| 4 | 4k | 160 | 89% | 2470 | 2583 | +4.6% | 57.7 → 54.8 ms |
| 4 | 4k | 128 | 70% | 2777 | 2882 | +3.8% | 40.1 → 38.3 ms |
| 4 | 8k | 64 | 64% | 1510 | 1551 | +2.7% | 35.8 → 34.7 ms |
| 4 | 16k | 24 | 46% | 744 | 760 | +2.2% | 26.5 → 25.8 ms |

For reference, the TP8 16k c=64 config without HiSparse gives 1302 tok/s and 39.2 ms TPOT. Single-run differences under ~3% are within noise.

```bash
# TP8: host_pool_gib 128; TP4: -tp 4 and host_pool_gib 64 (the host pool lives in /dev/shm)
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 \
  --max-model-len <input+2048> --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":128}}'
vllm bench serve --model RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len <input> --random-output-len 1024 --num-prompts <2×concurrency> \
  --max-concurrency <concurrency> --ignore-eos --seed 42
```

Notes:
- The TP4 runs restarted the server per point and included the #60109 crash fix (#60117, cherry-picked) on both sides. Without it, reusing a server across points crashes.
- The TP8 row is a single fresh-server run of 128 prompts on main and on this PR; it has no prefix hits, so it doesn't trigger #60109.

## Test plan

- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k hisparse`: 58 passed (CPU).
- `pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_stats.py`: 17 passed (H100).
- Coverage: `test_hisparse_reports_when_context_is_fully_resident` and `test_hisparse_keeps_resident_pages_until_hot_buffer_is_allocated` already assert resident (which now populates the cache), make the pool reuse a page, then assert non-resident. Removing the `_lose_page` invalidation fails 3 of their cases, so no new test is needed.

AI-assisted (Claude).

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Pass output_size to repeat_interleave in the Torch combine_topk_swa_indices
body:
## Purpose

On gfx950 the ROCm V4.1 sparse prefill uses the Torch `combine_topk_swa_indices`, once per layer per prefill chunk. Its two `torch.repeat_interleave(x, query_lens)` calls pass no `output_size`, so each one syncs with the host twice, to size the output and to validate `repeats`. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash that is 160 host syncs per prefill step (40 layers), and the GPU drains at each one.

This PR passes `output_size=num_tokens` to both calls. The caller slices `topk_indices` and `query_start_loc` with the same chunk bounds, so `query_lens` sums to `num_tokens`. Outputs are bit-identical, and decode and the NVIDIA paths are unchanged.

## Test Plan

MI350X (gfx950), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP=4 with expert parallelism, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`. Measured on the ROCm image's vLLM `0.3.1.dev160+gd05da62e9`, whose `combine_topk_swa_indices` is byte-identical to main; every measured step runs a single prefill chunk, as it would on main. Main and this PR were swapped in place on one server and interleaved in rotated order with the same seeds.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash -tp 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
    --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 768 --no-enable-prefix-caching

B="--model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --ignore-eos"
vllm bench serve $B --random-output-len 1 --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 24          # TTFT
vllm bench serve $B --random-output-len 1 --random-range-ratio 0.25 --num-prompts 256   # prefill
vllm bench serve $B --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0.25 \
    --max-concurrency 64 --num-prompts 192                                              # serving

pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_triton_sparse_mla.py -v   # <paste result>
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py                              # 1319 questions, 5-shot
```

Against main on five metadata cases (non-zero `query_start_loc` base, 1-token query, zero-query slot, 16K-token request, SWA-only layer), the outputs are bit-identical, and the host syncs per call drop from 7 to 3 under `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("warn")`.

## Test Result

Mean of 3–5 reps per arm; main's and this PR's ranges are disjoint in every row.

| workload | metric | main | this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192 in, concurrency 1 | median TTFT (ms) | 340.7 | 321.1 | −5.7 % |
| 8192 ± 25 % in, rate inf | prompt tok/s | 31,440 | 32,443 | +3.2 % |
| 8K/1K ± 25 %, concurrency 64 | output tok/s | 1,717 | 1,763 | +2.7 % |
| | median TTFT (ms) | 608.7 | 572.2 | −6.0 % |
| | median TPOT (ms) | 33.34 | 32.47 | −2.6 % |
| | P99 ITL (ms) | 359.9 | 340.3 | −5.4 % |

That is about 20 ms saved per prefill step, roughly 120 µs per removed sync. GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy): main 0.9014, this PR 0.9083, standard error ±0.008.

---

AI assistance (Cursor) was used. Yida Wu reviewed every changed line and reproduced the results.

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Fused vocab-parallel argmax for LogitsProcessor.get_top_tokens()
body:
## Overview

On CUDA at TP > 1, compute `LogitsProcessor.get_top_tokens()` (the `use_local_argmax_reduction` path) with one Triton pass over the logits shard, a dim-0 all-gather of a `[B, 16]` fp32 candidate tensor and one small pick kernel, instead of the current sequence of small torch ops. Same result as `torch.argmax` over the full vocabulary. Split out of #59727 after review.

## Claims

- Same algorithm as today (reduce each shard locally, gather per-row candidates, pick), with fewer kernels: 2 kernels plus the collective instead of 9 plus the collective (see Details).
- Same selected token as `torch.argmax` over the concatenated logits for every input, including ties within and across shards, `inf` and NaN (first NaN wins, ties go to the lowest id).
- Microbenchmark, one TP4 shard of a 131072-entry vocabulary, bf16, CUDA graph, communication excluded: the reduction takes about 75 % less time at 1-8 rows and about 60 % less at 64 rows.
- No end-to-end claim: this change was not measured end to end on its own.

## Validation

On `ac9126e58` (nightly image with this branch's `vllm/` files overlaid), 1x / 4x B200:

- `pytest -v tests/model_executor/layers/test_vocab_parallel_argmax.py`: **27 passed**. Simulated TP 2 / 3 / 4 / 8 shards, bf16 / fp16 / fp32, 131072 and 32001 vocab, 1-64 rows, against `torch.argmax`: random values, integer ties, ties across shards, all `-inf`, `+inf` ties, NaN, `-0.0` / `+0.0` ties; column-major and strided-column shards; 50 CUDA graph replays.
- `pytest -v tests/distributed/test_vocab_parallel_argmax.py` (TP2 / TP4, Ray): **2 passed**. Real `ParallelLMHead` + `LogitsProcessor.get_top_tokens()` across ranks against the full-vocabulary greedy path (`argmax` of the gathered logits), with tie-heavy integer weights, 131072 and 32001 (padded) vocab, 1-8 rows, eagerly and from a captured CUDA graph.
- Microbenchmark (same shard as above, 20 calls captured per CUDA graph, communication replaced by a same-size copy in both paths):

Time per call relative to the existing reduction:

| rows (B) | existing torch reduction | this PR |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.00 | 0.25 |
| 2 | 1.00 | 0.23 |
| 4 | 1.00 | 0.24 |
| 8 | 1.00 | 0.25 |
| 64 | 1.00 | 0.41 |

The existing path in this benchmark also gets 54 / 54 simulated-shard cases (NaN, ties, signed zeros) equal to `torch.argmax`, so the change does not alter the selected token.

## Details

**What the existing path does per call** (after the head GEMM, soft-cap / scale and padding mask, which are unchanged):

- on each rank: `logits.max(dim=-1)` (1 reduction kernel), `+ vocab_start`, `.float()` on the values and on the indices, `torch.stack` (4 elementwise kernels): 8 bytes per row;
- `all_gather(dim=-1)`: NCCL gather along dim 0 plus the copy that moves the rank dimension next to the last dim;
- `argmax` over ranks, `gather`, `.to(int64)` (3 kernels).

That is 9 small kernels around the collective, each a separate launch.

**This PR:** `local_argmax_candidates` scans the shard once with 8 programs per row; each writes its best `(value, global id)` as fp32 (exact for bf16 / fp16 / fp32 values and ids below 2^24, the same assumption as today). The candidates (64 bytes per row and rank) are gathered along dim 0, so no rearranging copy is needed, and `pick_from_candidates` picks per row. The kernel takes row and column strides, so non-contiguous logits need no copy. TP = 1 and non-CUDA platforms keep the torch path.

**Exactness:** every comparison uses `torch.argmax`'s total order with an index tie-break (NaN first, then larger value, then lower id, `-0.0 == +0.0`). The maximum under such an order over a partition of the vocabulary equals the maximum of the per-part maxima, so the result does not depend on the shard or chunk boundaries.

**torch.compile:** this path is not compiled. For MTP drafters such as Nemotron-H, `@support_torch_compile` is applied to the inner model (`NemotronHMultiTokenPredictor`), so only its `forward` is traced. The speculator's `sample_draft()` calls `get_top_tokens()` after that forward, outside the compiled region, so Inductor never fuses these ops. With FULL CUDA graphs the eager kernels are captured into the drafter's graph and replayed one by one, once per draft position; with PIECEWISE they run eagerly. The kernel count is therefore what runs at decode.

**Race-free:** two kernels plus vLLM's normal TP all-gather, all on the caller's stream; each kernel writes a fresh output; no atomics, no persistent state, no cross-program communication.

**Related:** #59727 (Nemotron-H MTP `get_top_tokens()`, needed to use this path with that drafter), #56995 (generic MTP drafter hook), #57770 (split-vocabulary argmax on already-gathered logits for DSpark; different call site).

**Duplicate check:** `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "get_top_tokens"` -> #59727, #56995, #52072, #57770, #47584; `--search "vocab parallel argmax"` and `--search "local argmax reduction"` -> the same plus unrelated sampler / diffusion items. None changes the reduction inside `LogitsProcessor.get_top_tokens()`.

**AI assistance:** Claude Code was used to write this change and its tests, run the validation and draft this description. The human submitter reviews every changed line before this leaves draft.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Route gfx942 sparse MLA prefill to AITER pa_prefill_sparse
body:
## Summary

On gfx942, fp16/bf16 sparse MLA prefill with at least 512 query rows goes to AITER `pa_prefill_sparse`. Shorter calls stay on the in-tree kernel. The import and the `Using AITER pa_prefill_sparse for sparse MLA prefill on gfx942` log happen only when that kernel launches.

## What changed

- `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`: after the gfx950 OPUS attempt, call `pa_prefill_sparse` when the gfx942 gate passes. One KV pool. The caller output is passed as `out` when it matches `q`; a narrower output is copied from the kernel result.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py`: the dense Triton fallback test stubs the getter, so that case stays in-tree.

## Gating

gfx942, AITER enabled, `q` fp16 or bf16, `kv.dtype == q.dtype`, and `q.shape[0] >= 512` (`_GFX942_AITER_PA_PREFILL_SPARSE_MIN_QUERIES`).

`pa_prefill_sparse` does not split the KV. Under 512 rows the call stays on the in-tree ragged prefill, which also does not. DeepSeek-V4.1 decode uses `rocm_sparse_attn_decode` and does not enter this function. The 2-row and 16-row shapes stay off `pa_prefill_sparse`. On this branch that is the in-tree kernel, not Gluon split-K.

## Depends on

title: [Perf][HiSparse] Fuse per-layer slot invalidation and shorten the all-resident resolver path
body:
## Purpose

Cut HiSparse's per-layer decode overhead on the GPU and in launches:

- **One slot-invalidation launch per step.** Today it's one eager launch per leader layer after the forward graph (61 for DeepSeek-V3.2). The kernel now runs over (written tokens × index groups) using a cached device table of each group's `device_global_indices`. `HiSparseRuntime.invalidate_written_slots` is replaced by `HiSparseSlotInvalidator`.
- **Resolver masks CUDA-graph padding rows itself** from `num_valid_rows`. This removes the per-layer `copy_` + `masked_fill_` and the `request_ids`/`row_indices` buffers.
- **Cheaper all-resident resolver path.** Resident and invalid entries resolve before the host-row hash table is built, with an early exit when no host rows exist. Power-of-two block arithmetic uses shift/mask.

Stacked on #60083 (includes its commit); review only the top commit.

## Results (proxy only, not yet validated on a real server)

DeepSeek-V3.2 dummy weights, 61 layers / 8 experts, TP4, H100, batch 32, 16k context, nsys per decode step:

| kernel | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| invalidate | 495 µs (61 launches) | 5.8 µs (1) |
| resolve_residency | 421 µs | 372 µs |
| masked_fill_ + copy_ | 166 µs | 0 |

TPOT (`--out 384`, 3 reps each, back to back): 38.83 / 38.47 / 39.25 → 37.79 / 37.61 / 38.04 ms (~2.7%).

TODO: GLM-5.3-NVFP4 serve A/B on B200.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k hisparse tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`: 88 passed. New `test_hisparse_invalidation_covers_every_index_group`.
- [x] `pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: 4 passed (H100).
- [ ] GLM-5.3-NVFP4 serve A/B (B200)

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches these kernels. AI-assisted (Claude); I'll review every line before marking ready.

title: [Bugfix][Sampler] Stabilize standalone Triton top-p normalization
body:
## Overview

Fixes #60030 by stabilizing standalone Triton top-p normalization when hot logits exceed the reference estimated from the first tile. Preserve the existing reference on ordinary dense rows to avoid the retained-count regression found during review.

## Claims

- Prevents overflow and the resulting keep-all mask on the sparse regression inputs.
- Preserves the current search, outlier heuristic, top-k and split paths without another vocabulary pass or host/device synchronization.
- Retains probability-space boundary-tie handling and the existing monolithic NaN fallback, and adds the reported dense input to the existing sampler suite.

## Validation

Validated against main `074c83a09` on H100 with Torch 2.13.0+cu129, Triton 3.7.1 and FlashInfer 0.6.18, reusing existing native extensions.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_triton.py tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py
git diff --check
```

The full official sampler file passes 153 cases, with one existing ROCm-only skip. This includes the large int64 row-offset test and FlashInfer tests. All applicable project hooks pass.

The reviewer's 79 dense inputs at batch sizes 1 and 65 produce the same retained counts as main. For `(V=32768, seed=25, d=+2)`, the previous head keeps 8,505 tokens; this update and main keep 8,192, versus 8,193 in PyTorch/FP64. The new regression uses the existing comparison tolerance and fails on the previous head. Matching main is a non-regression result, not exact-CDF correctness; existing search errors remain.

Controlled real Qwen3.5-0.8B Model Runner V2 generation uses 65 simultaneous requests and actual sampler logits `(65, 248320)`. With backgrounds -200 and -100, two hot tokens and top-p 0.5, main retains the entire vocabulary and samples the two hot tokens 32/33 times. This update retains one hot token, no background, and selects it for all 65 requests. The moderate-background three-way tie control also retains one token. An additional run without the diagnostic mask observer passes with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` active. These are controlled serving regressions, not language-quality evaluations.

Five alternating FP32 top-p 0.95 timing rounds give update/main latency ratios of 0.99891, 1.01009, 1.00912 and 1.01180 for `(batch, vocabulary)` shapes `(1, 32000)`, `(65, 32000)`, `(65, 151936)` and `(384, 151936)`. CUDA event/graph timing includes the same input reset in both arms, excluding allocation and compilation. The GPU was shared with training, so these are performance controls, not isolated speedup or serving-throughput claims. Both arms meet the unchanged count tolerance.

No clean full-native rebuild, triton-cpu or ROCm validation is claimed. For serving, current main's required humming-kernels 0.1.17 was provided in an isolated directory and the pinned generated FlashMLA interface was restored; existing environment packages were not modified.

## Details

The old kernel uses `avg_logit + 10 * std_logit` from the first tile as a fixed exponential reference. Later hot logits can overflow it. This update raises the reference only when a larger logit is encountered and rescales the accumulated denominator. The true maximum remains separate for the existing mask guards and probability bounds.

The earlier version always changed the reference to the true maximum. That altered dense-row rounding and exposed the existing coarse-search termination error. Keeping the sampled reference when it is sufficient avoids that added regression. Boundary duplicates are still matched in probability space, and NaN still reaches the existing invalid-pivot guard.

This does not copy #59804's gate/search rewrite or require it to land first. Its broader search corrections remain separate; this update does not claim to fix the baseline's remaining dense or split-path inaccuracies.

title: [Bug][HiSparse] GLM-5.3 TP8 on B200: illegal memory access when admitting a new request wave
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `528772a4bf` (main, 2026-10-05), torch 2.13.0+cu130, flashinfer-python 0.7.0.post1
- 8× NVIDIA B200, driver 595.91.07
- Model `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`, TP8, FlashInfer sparse MLA, default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs, MRv2

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With HiSparse enabled, the server crashes when a new wave of requests is admitted after an earlier wave has finished on the same server. Every GPU-memory-related error surfaces inside HiSparse's residency resolution during piecewise-graph replay (or as a segfault in `cudaGraphLaunch`). It reproduced in 3 of 3 attempts on main, and also with #60083 applied. The same workload without `--kv-transfer-config` doesn't crash.

```bash
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 \
  --max-model-len 22528 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":128}}'

# passes: 4/4 requests
vllm bench serve --model RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 20480 \
  --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --seed 42 --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 4
# crashes immediately: 0/8 requests, engine dead
vllm bench serve --model RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 20480 \
  --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --seed 42 --max-concurrency 4 --num-prompts 8
```

GPU KV usage is ~1% when it crashes, so everything is GPU-resident and no host spills are needed.

Error (Worker_TP4; asynchronous, so the faulting kernel may be earlier):

```
gpu/model_runner.py:2025 run_pw_graph -> breakable_cudagraph replay
-> models/deepseek_v32/attention.py:594 _sparse_indexer_and_attn
-> v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse.py:526 forward_mqa
-> v1/attention/backends/mla/index_group.py:253 convert_logical_to_physical_topk
-> v1/hisparse/runtime.py:1081 swap_in -> :1019 _resolve_and_stage_group
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

Other occurrence:

```
!!!!!!! Segfault encountered !!!!!!!
  cuGraphLaunch <- cudaGraphLaunch <- at::cuda::CUDAGraph::replay()
```

Notes:
- A single run at `--max-concurrency 64 --num-prompts 128` with 16k inputs completed without crashing, so continuous admission inside one benchmark run doesn't seem sufficient by itself.
- Under `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` the c=4 phase was too slow to finish, so that run is inconclusive.
- Root-causing in progress; tracked in #60072.

cc @LucasWilkinson

title: [ROCm][Perf][Kimi-K3] Fold q_b_proj and W_UK into one GEMM for the MLA decode query
body:
## Purpose

On the ROCm/AITER decode path every Kimi-K3 MLA layer spends two launches on the query
projection (M = 56 rows at the InferenceX c14 point, 12 heads per rank at TP8):

| Kernel | What it does | Before (µs) | After (µs) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hgemm_bf16_t16x32x128x5` | `q_b_proj`: x[56,1536] → q[56,12,192] | 6.76 | – |
| `_batched_gemm_a16wfp4_kernel` | absorb-in BMM: q_nope × W_UK (fp4) → ql_nope[56,12,512] | 5.49 | – |
| `_gemm_a16_w16_kernel` (aiter Triton `gemm_a16w16`) | x[56,1536] × W_fold[1536,6912] → [ql_nope \| q_pe] | – | 9.20 |
| **per layer** |  | **12.25** | **9.20** |

`q_b_proj` and the `W_UK` are consecutive linear maps, so
`ql_nope[h] = x · (W_UK[h] · W_qb_nope[h])ᵀ`. This PR builds once at load, from the bf16
checkpoint weights,

    W_fold[h] = [ W_UK[h] · W_qb_nope[h] ; W_qb_pe[h] ]        # [512 + 64, 1536] per head


**Decode only:** the W_UK absorb exists only on the MQA decode path. Prefill uses the
un-absorbed form and keeps `q_b_proj`, so any step with prefill tokens takes the original path.

**Small M win:** the fold reads 21 MB instead of 7.5 MB and does 2.5x the FLOPs. The save shrinks as M grows and would turn negative at prefill sizes, which this path never sees. 

We do additional 1.9Gb for the extra weight fold for all 93 layers of Kimi k3.

We're actively testing the prefill shape such that it cannot be much worse than non w-fold so that we don't have to pay for extra 1.9Gb.

## Server command:

export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 PYTHONHASHSEED=42 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1

  --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --max-model-len 1048576 --enable-prefix-caching \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL","max_cudagraph_capture_size":112,"custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"],"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[2,3,...,112]}' \

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Carry adopted prefix pages in the new request's row
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #60109: HiSparse servers crash with an illegal memory access when a new request hits a prefix whose published host pages still have GPU copies.

The coordinator adopts those copies after the scheduler has already built the request's `NewRequestData`, so the adopted row went out as a `block_table_updates` entry. For a new request, model runner V2 then stages two full-row writes for the same row in one step (`add_requests`, then `update_requests`), and the staged-write kernel applies them in parallel with no ordering. A rank that kept the pre-adoption row saw null resident pages, while the scheduler reported every context page resident. The resident-prefill shortcut then sent the prefill rows through the decode residency resolver, whose host union overflowed `max_union_rows` and faulted.

The fix puts the adopted row in the new request's `block_ids`; `block_table_updates` stays for running requests. HiSparse-only (`hisparse/connector.py`).

Note: MRv2's staged block-table writer doesn't order overlapping writes to the same row. This PR stops HiSparse from producing them; changing that in core is a separate discussion.

## Reproduction on main

GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on B200, either TP8 or TP4 (`host_pool_gib` 128 or 64):

```bash
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 \
  --max-model-len 22528 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":64}}'
vllm bench serve --model RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 20480 \
  --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --seed 42 --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 4
vllm bench serve --model RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 20480 \
  --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --seed 42 --max-concurrency 4 --num-prompts 8
```

Because of the fixed seed, the second wave repeats the first wave's prompts, so its requests hit the published prefix and adopt the GPU copies on admission.

| | c=1 (4 prompts) | c=4 (8 prompts) |
|---|---|---|
| main `528772a4bf` (TP4 3/3 runs, TP8 4/4 runs) | 4/4 | 0/8: illegal memory access, engine dead |
| this PR (TP4, 3 servers × 3 c=4 waves) | 4/4 | 8/8 in every wave, no CUDA errors (9/9 waves) |

## Performance

No change expected: one dict pop per newly scheduled request per step, and one fewer row write on the GPU for adopted requests.

## Test plan

- [x] Repro above: fails on main (TP4 3/3, TP8 4/4), passes with this PR (9/9 c=4 waves over 3 TP4 servers), B200.
- [x] Unit test `test_scheduled_prefix_hit_publishes_adopted_copies` now asserts the adopted row arrives in the new request's `block_ids` with no `block_table_updates` entry for it. Fails without the fix (`block_table_updates` still holds the request's row), passes with it.
- [x] B200, 1 GPU:
  - `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py`: 8 passed
  - `pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: 4 passed
  - `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k hisparse`: 36 passed

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this path. AI-assisted (Claude).

title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 on B300: CUDA illegal access persists with MTP disabled; blocking/eager reports persistent_topk
body:
## Summary

We observed repeated CUDA illegal-memory-access failures serving GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 on a single 8×B300 node. Disabling multi-token prediction (MTP), switching the MoE backend to FlashInfer CUTLASS, and subsequently using TP4 with BF16 KV cache did not yield a stable configuration.

These are the same symptom class, not a proven common root cause. All attached experimental runs used Dynamo 1.5's vLLM worker wrapper and native frontend. We have not validated a bare-vLLM reproduction with these synthetic inputs and cannot exclude integration or environment effects.

Potentially related: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54317 . That report uses a different hardware/build configuration. Please advise whether this evidence belongs there or warrants a separate issue.

## Environment

- Single node: 8× NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC; compute capability 10.3; driver 580.178.04.
- Model: nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4; revision 09b04e5e74bca08ca8549fc736d4cdd8624bfde3.
- Worker image: docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:0674a3ea3c971706cea310bca71daadff68ea1717c758d2f54affa5def001b86.
- This digest matched the Linux/AMD64 child of vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash when checked on October 2; the digest, not the mutable tag, identifies our image.
- Live vLLM build: 0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b.
- Earlier same-image runtime snapshot: torch 2.13.0+cu130; flashinfer-python 0.6.18. These are not a fresh complete environment dump from the latest run.
- ai-dynamo==1.5.0 installed at worker startup; transitive dependencies were not fully pinned. A protobuf/CUTLASS-DSL dependency warning was present; its relevance is unknown.
- No LMCache or external/offloaded KV cache in these tests.

## Observed failures

1. Default FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE, 4×TP2 engines, expert parallelism, NVFP4 weights, FP8 KV and MTP3: illegal access reported while initializing a TMA descriptor via trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe. Complete pre-crash logs were lost; only a surviving excerpt is included.
2. CUTLASS MoE, otherwise the same settings: illegal access reported in KDA's chunk_kda_scaled_dot_kkt_fwd_kernel_intra_sub_inter. This occurred in concurrency-16 warmup for the second planned concurrency-32 run.
3. CUTLASS MoE with MTP disabled, FP8 KV and 4×TP2: four concurrency-32 repeats completed; the fifth failed. Detection was at copy_event.synchronize in output handling, not an identified originating kernel.
4. Same MTP-off setup plus CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 and --enforce-eager: three concurrency-32 repeats completed; the fourth failed. Both TP ranks reported torch.ops._C.persistent_topk, /workspace/csrc/libtorch_stable/topk.cu:227, in GLM's sparse-attention indexer. This is a vLLM custom C++ operator, not a FlashInfer MoE kernel. Blocking improves localization but does not itself prove where corruption originated.
5. Latest test: 2×TP4 engines, expert parallelism, CUTLASS MoE, NVFP4, BF16 KV, MTP disabled, ordinary nonblocking/graph execution. Startup and API smoke test succeeded, but the first concurrency-16 warmup failed. Both engines reported illegal access along build_prefill_chunk_metadata → _BUILD_PREFILL_CHUNK_METADATA_KERNEL → Triton load_binary. The exception occurred during Triton binary/handle initialization; this is not proof that the metadata kernel performed the illegal write. It is not a KDA or persistent_topk traceback.

A FlashInfer CUTEDSL alternative was also rejected at startup because of the unquantized MTP layer. That rejection was a compatibility failure, not a CUDA illegal-access reproduction.

Latest failure: 2026-10-05 18:21:33 UTC. Of 32 warmup requests, 17 returned HTTP 200 and 15 returned HTTP 503. No measured concurrency-32 requests or full repeats completed. We have no validated workaround and output correctness remains unverified.

## Workload and configuration

The attachments contain synthetic code-like prompts, not customer requests. Each prompt has approximately 125,011 chat-templated input tokens and requests 400 output tokens. There are two reusable prefix groups with approximately 107,499 prefix tokens; this gives an approximately 86% theoretical reuse ceiling, not a guaranteed measured hit rate.

Original benchmark: AIPerf 0.11 with a request-journaling proxy. Each repeat uses 32 warmup requests at concurrency 16, then 128 measured requests at concurrency 32; caches are not reset between repeats. Proxy-observed latency is not directly comparable with direct-client benchmarks.

Request payload: POST /v1/chat/completions, model=zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash, one user message containing the dataset text, stream=true, stream_options={"include_usage":true}, max_completion_tokens=400, ignore_eos=true, temperature=0.

Latest worker settings include TP4, EP enabled, modelopt_fp4, dtype=bfloat16, kv_cache_dtype=bfloat16, max_model_len=1048576, max_num_seqs=48, max_num_batched_tokens=65536, kv_cache_memory=123480309760, chunked prefill and prefix caching enabled, moe_backend=flashinfer_cutlass, no speculative-config and no enforce-eager. Full engine flags and environment are in deployment.sanitized.yaml.

The sanitized deployment is a review template, not a directly validated reproducer: namespace, storage and cluster placement must be supplied. The frozen datasets preserve the actual synthetic request text. We have not minimized the workload or independently validated an upstream standalone reproduction.

## Request to maintainers

Could the GLM/vLLM kernel owners investigate these failures and advise on a supported fix or workaround preserving NVFP4? In particular, please triage the persistent_topk traceback reproduced with MTP disabled, launch blocking and eager execution, and the newer TP4/BF16-KV traceback. If a smaller reproducer or Compute Sanitizer capture is required, please specify the exact configuration and evidence needed.

## Attachments

A sanitized evidence ZIP has been prepared for attachment through GitHub’s web interface (not uploaded by this connector). It includes sanitized traceback blocks for every retained failure site, the surviving default-MoE excerpt, a sanitized latest request journal and summary, environment details, a sanitized deployment template, and frozen synthetic warmup/measured datasets with checksums. It does not contain raw customer logs, customer prompts, internal cluster identifiers or credentials. No Xid-based hardware-fault conclusion is established by this package.
