title: [Bugfix][Attention] Make TRITON_MLA prefill batch invariant under chunked prefill
body:
## Overview Fixes #60007. With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the output of a prompt served by `TRITON_MLA` depends on how the scheduler splits its prefill into chunks. This PR computes prefill rows with the per-row decode kernel in batch-invariant mode, so a row's result no longer depends on the chunk it was scheduled in. ## Claims - `test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_ragged_chunked_prefill[TRITON_MLA]` fails on `main` and passes with this PR (DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat). The two `bs1_vs_bsN[...-TRITON_MLA]` tests, which also fail on `main` with this model, pass as well. - Nothing changes when `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is unset: `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` and `tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_mla_causal_verify_flatten.py` have the same set of failing tests on `main` and on this PR (the failures are FP8 KV-cache cases that this GPU does not support). - gsm8k accuracy in batch-invariant mode is unchanged within the reported standard error. - Cost: prefill is slower in batch-invariant mode, because the decode kernel works row by row. See the `vllm bench serve` runs below (6: prefill-heavy, 7: mixed). ## Validation All runs: 2x NVIDIA A10 (SM 8.6), tensor-parallel 2, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat`, `main` at `d09ff77637` versus the same commit with this PR applied. The blocks below are copied from the logs without editing. (`VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` is only there because this machine cannot JIT-compile the FlashInfer sampler.) ```text | NVIDIA-SMI 580.126.20 Driver Version: 580.126.20 CUDA Version: 13.0 | 0.30.1rc1.dev679+gd09ff7763 2.13.0+cu132 ``` **1. Reproduce** ```text $ CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,2 VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat VLLM_TP_SIZE=2 VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=2 VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.9 python -m pytest -p no:rerunfailures -p no:cacheprovider -v "tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_ragged_chunked_prefill[TRITON_MLA]" # main E AssertionError: Batch invariance violated under chunked prefill (max_num_batched_tokens=131): prompt 1 (263 tokens): logprobs differ, max|delta|=1.028e-01; prompt 8 (248 tokens): logprobs differ, max|delta|=3.877e-02; prompt 10 (97 tokens): logprobs differ, max|delta|=6.318e-02; prompt 13 (90 tokens): logprobs differ, max|delta|=1.340e-01 ================== 1 failed, 17 warnings in 83.73s (0:01:23) =================== # this PR ======================= 1 passed, 17 warnings in 37.36s ======================== ```
2. The other TRITON_MLA ids of tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py (same environment variables as above, one process per test; raw summary lines) ```text ## test_batch_invariance.py::test_v1_generation_is_deterministic_across_batch_sizes_with_needle[default-TRITON_MLA] # main ================== 1 passed, 17 warnings in 123.52s (0:02:03) ================== # this PR ================== 1 passed, 17 warnings in 94.81s (0:01:34) =================== ## test_batch_invariance.py::test_v1_generation_is_deterministic_across_batch_sizes_with_needle[vllm_c-TRITON_MLA] # main ================== 1 passed, 17 warnings in 117.80s (0:01:57) ================== # this PR ================== 1 passed, 17 warnings in 96.22s (0:01:36) =================== ## test_batch_invariance.py::test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_bs1_vs_bsN[16-16-TRITON_MLA] # main E Failed: Batch invariance violated in 2/32 prompts. See output above for details. ======================= 1 failed, 17 warnings in 50.56s ======================== # this PR ======================= 1 passed, 17 warnings in 49.32s ======================== ## test_batch_invariance.py::test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_bs1_vs_bsN[8-16-TRITON_MLA] # main E Failed: Batch invariance violated in 2/32 prompts. See output above for details. ======================= 1 failed, 17 warnings in 52.98s ======================== # this PR ======================= 1 passed, 17 warnings in 49.45s ======================== ## test_batch_invariance.py::test_simple_generation[TRITON_MLA] # main ======================= 1 passed, 17 warnings in 51.90s ======================== # this PR ======================= 1 passed, 17 warnings in 31.57s ======================== ## test_batch_invariance.py::test_logprobs_without_batch_invariance_should_fail[TRITON_MLA] # main ================== 1 passed, 17 warnings in 63.39s (0:01:03) =================== # this PR ======================= 1 passed, 17 warnings in 28.94s ======================== ```
**3. New unit test** (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is patched inside the test). Benchmark, prefill-heavy** (same server as above) ```text $ vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --dataset-name random --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9256 --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 1 --request-rate inf --num-prompts 64 --num-warmups 8 # main ============ Serving Benchmark Result ============ Successful requests: 64 Failed requests: 0 Benchmark duration (s): 23.86 Total input tokens: 262144 Total generated tokens: 64 Request throughput (req/s): 2.68 Output token throughput (tok/s): 2.68 Peak output token throughput (tok/s): 3.00 Peak concurrent requests: 64.00 Total token throughput (tok/s): 10988.81 ---------------Time to First Token---------------- Mean TTFT (ms): 12100.73 Median TTFT (ms): 12093.34 P99 TTFT (ms): 23697.55 -----Time per Output Token (excl. 1st token)------ Mean TPOT (ms): 0.00 Median TPOT (ms): 0.00 P99 TPOT (ms): 0.00 ---------------Inter-token Latency---------------- Mean ITL (ms): 0.00 Median ITL (ms): 0.00 P99 ITL (ms): 0.00 ================================================== # this PR ============ Serving Benchmark Result ============ Successful requests: 64 Failed requests: 0 Benchmark duration (s): 51.07 Total input tokens: 262144 Total generated tokens: 64 Request throughput (req/s): 1.25 Output token throughput (tok/s): 1.25 Peak output token throughput (tok/s): 2.00 Peak concurrent requests: 64.00 Total token throughput (tok/s): 5134.42 ---------------Time to First Token---------------- Mean TTFT (ms): 25498.33 Median TTFT (ms): 25437.67 P99 TTFT (ms): 50545.74 -----Time per Output Token (excl. 1st token)------ Mean TPOT (ms): 0.00 Median TPOT (ms): 0.00 P99 TPOT (ms): 0.00 ---------------Inter-token Latency---------------- Mean ITL (ms): 0.00 Median ITL (ms): 0.00 P99 ITL (ms): 0.00 ================================================== ```
7. Benchmark, mixed (1024 input tokens, 128 output tokens; raw output) ```text $ vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --dataset-name random --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9256 --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 --request-rate inf --num-prompts 128 --num-warmups 16 # main ============ Serving Benchmark Result ============ Successful requests: 128 Failed requests: 0 Benchmark duration (s): 23.17 Total input tokens: 131072 Total generated tokens: 16384 Request throughput (req/s): 5.53 Output token throughput (tok/s): 707.22 Peak output token throughput (tok/s): 2161.00 Peak concurrent requests: 128.00 Total token throughput (tok/s): 6364.94 ---------------Time to First Token---------------- Mean TTFT (ms): 8932.80 Median TTFT (ms): 8781.20 P99 TTFT (ms): 14807.81 -----Time per Output Token (excl. 1st token)------ Mean TPOT (ms): 95.68 Median TPOT (ms): 95.22 P99 TPOT (ms): 140.75 ---------------Inter-token Latency---------------- Mean ITL (ms): 95.68 Median ITL (ms): 61.30 P99 ITL (ms): 189.05 ================================================== # this PR ============ Serving Benchmark Result ============ Successful requests: 128 Failed requests: 0 Benchmark duration (s): 21.43 Total input tokens: 131072 Total generated tokens: 16384 Request throughput (req/s): 5.97 Output token throughput (tok/s): 764.37 Peak output token throughput (tok/s): 2134.00 Peak concurrent requests: 128.00 Total token throughput (tok/s): 6879.31 ---------------Time to First Token---------------- Mean TTFT (ms): 6303.87 Median TTFT (ms): 5018.15 P99 TTFT (ms): 12970.00 -----Time per Output Token (excl. 1st token)------ Mean TPOT (ms): 103.16 Median TPOT (ms): 111.69 P99 TPOT (ms): 136.04 ---------------Inter-token Latency---------------- Mean ITL (ms): 103.16 Median ITL (ms): 61.56 P99 ITL (ms): 247.60 ================================================== ```
## Details **Root cause.** For prefill, `forward_mha` attends to the new tokens of the step and to the cached context separately (`_compute_prefill_context`) and merges the two partial results. Where the split falls depends on the scheduler's chunking, so the rounding of a token's output depends on it too. This is the same mechanism that made #29125 disable prefix caching for `TRITON_MLA` in batch-invariant mode. **Change.** - `MLAAttention.forward_impl`: in batch-invariant mode, if the backend opts in (`supports_batch_invariant_mqa_prefill`), all rows of the step go to `forward_mqa`. The KV cache has already been updated for the step, so each row can be computed from the cache alone. This reuses the branch that sparse MLA already has for routing prefill rows to MQA. - `TritonMLAImpl`: a new `_forward_mqa_all_rows` gives every query row its own causal extent and calls the existing `decode_attention_fwd` (one program per row, `num_kv_splits = 1`). Rows are launched in groups of 256 to bound the scratch buffer; rows are independent, so the group size cannot change results. The existing decode path is unchanged. - The routing is used only for causal attention without PCP/DCP; otherwise the existing path is kept and a warning is logged once. `Dots3NoteTritonMLAImpl` (sliding window) opts out. **Trade-offs and limitations.** - Prefill in batch-invariant mode is slower (run 6 above). Decode is not affected, and nothing changes outside batch-invariant mode. - Routed prefill allocates per-row latent outputs (`rows x heads x kv_lora_rank`), like the sparse MQA-prefill path does. - Alternatives I considered: disabling chunked prefill for `TRITON_MLA` in batch-invariant mode (as was done for prefix caching), which costs no prefill speed but restricts scheduling; and canonical chunk boundaries in the prefill path, which is a larger change. I am happy to switch to either if that is preferred. - Validated on SM 8.6 with BF16 KV cache only. The FP8 KV-cache cases of the MLA backend tests cannot run on this GPU. ---

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Write a new request's block-table update once
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #60109 (HiSparse servers crash with an illegal memory access on prefix hits).

A `block_table_updates` row supersedes a request's normal block-table write, and `update_requests` already skips `new_block_ids` for running requests that have one. New requests lacked that guard. `add_requests` staged the `NewRequestData` row, `update_requests` staged the update, both for the same row in the same step, and `_apply_write_kernel` applies staged writes as unordered programs. Ranks could keep either row. With HiSparse prefix-copy adoption, ranks that kept the stale row read null resident pages, and the decode residency resolver overflowed.

Fix: `add_requests` skips the `NewRequestData` row when a table update exists, and `update_requests` writes the update as before.

## Why this instead of #60117

- **It fixes the race where it happens.** MRv2 accepts two unordered writes to one row; #60117 only stops today's single producer (HiSparse) from sending them.
- **It's smaller and symmetric.** Five lines extend the guard `update_requests` already has. #60117 instead has the HiSparse connector rewrite an already-built `NewRequestData`, which also changes what every other reader of that field sees.
- **It costs nothing for other users.** A dict lookup per new request, and one fewer GPU row write when an update exists.

Tradeoff: this touches `gpu/model_runner.py`, while #60117 is HiSparse-only.

## Test plan

GLM-5.3-NVFP4 repro from #60109 (TP4, c=1 then c=4 with repeated prompts), 4×B300, same box:

| | c=1 | c=4 waves |
|---|---|---|
| main `8bd7737a03` | 4/4 | 0/8, illegal memory access |
| this PR (`cba1d1ef72`) | 4/4 | 8/8 ×3, 0 CUDA errors |

Main also crashed in 7/7 runs on B200 (TP4 and TP8).

- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py`: 9 passed on head `2d774bf397`. The new `test_new_request_table_update_is_written_once` fails on main.
- `pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: 4 passed (B300, `cba1d1ef72`).

The head differs from `cba1d1ef72` only by moving the `table_updates` assignment. AI-assisted (Claude).

title: [KV Offload] SimpleCPUOffload: one host buffer per rank, opt-in HugeTLB pages
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

**Functionality**
- `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` allocates each rank's CPU KV caches as views into one host mapping of `cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank` bytes, pinned with a single `cudaHostRegister`.
- The new `cpu_hugepage_block_size` key (`"1GB"` or `"2MB"`) backs that mapping with explicit HugeTLB pages; without it, ordinary pages are used.
- The mapping prefers the GPU's NUMA node.
- A HugeTLB pool or container hugetlb limit that's too small fails at startup with an error naming the shortfall, never falling back to 4 KiB pages.
- The mapping is excluded from `fork()` (`MADV_DONTFORK`), so child processes can't make pinned pages copy-on-write.

```json
{"kv_connector": "SimpleCPUOffloadConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both",
 "kv_connector_extra_config": {"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank": 137438953472,
                               "cpu_hugepage_block_size": "1GB"}}
```

**Performance implications**
- In `vllm serve` (TP=2, 64 GiB per rank, ordinary pages), engine init takes 19.0 s vs 20.2 s before.
- With 1 GiB pages, pinning 128 GiB takes 0.19 s instead of 2.5 s on ordinary pages.
- GPU↔CPU copy bandwidth is unchanged at about 42 GB/s.

**Known limitations**
- On CUDA, a single registration of 512 GiB or more fails (#51081), so a per-rank buffer must stay below that; ROCm accepts 520 GiB.
- Each rank needs `ceil(cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank / page size)` HugeTLB pages, reserved on the host and, on Kubernetes, requested as `hugepages-<size>`.
- Up-front population needs Linux 5.14+ for HugeTLB pages; ordinary pages fall back to first touch on older kernels.

Related: #45693 (same key name for `OffloadingConnector`), #58852, #59430, #51081.

## Validation

MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, Linux 6.8, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-92044241a0` with this PR's three changed files overlaid; the image's copies were byte-identical to this PR's base.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_host_buffer.py tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py` | 32 passed |
| 8 ranks × 38 GiB (1 GiB pages), random store/load with byte-level checks, 120 s | 0 mismatches; every rank's pages on its GPU's NUMA node |
| More 1 GiB pages than the host has (330 on 320) | Fails at `mmap` with a clear error |
| 150 GiB soak, 10 min, 6,724 concurrent `fork()`s | 0 mismatches |
| `vllm serve` (TP=2, 32 GiB of 1 GiB pages per rank): `SIGKILL` a worker, `SIGKILL` the engine core, `SIGTERM`, then restart; plus `SIGKILL`/`SIGSEGV`/exception at buffer level, including mid-populate, mid-pin, and with forked children still alive | Requests served; the HugeTLB pool and GPU memory return to baseline within 5 s each time, and the restarted engine serves |

The 8-rank, soak and pool rows ran on the previous revision, which populated pages with 16 threads; this revision populates with one `madvise` call and was re-checked with the unit tests and the `vllm serve` crash/restart row.

Not yet done: an output-quality comparison with offload on and off, and a CUDA run. AMD CI already runs `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload`; the HugeTLB tests skip on hosts without a pool.

title: [Bugfix] Fix Qwen4Exp FP8 PLE pinned lookup kernel failing to compile below SM89
body:
## Overview

Fixes #59868. On GPUs below SM89 (the report uses 4 × RTX 3090), Qwen4Exp with an FP8 E4M3FN PLE table and `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}'` crashes in `profile_run`. The crash is a Triton `CompilationError` from `_lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel`. This PR makes that kernel copy rows as raw bytes, so the FP8 type never enters its signature.

## Claims

- `_lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel` now compiles and runs on sm_86 with an FP8 E4M3FN table, and it copies FP8 rows bit-exactly.
- On an A40, three existing FP8 pinned-lookup tests in `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py` failed before this change. They now pass.
- BF16 lookups are unchanged: same bits, same speed.
- The module still imports when Triton is not installed.

## Validation

Hardware: a machine with 4 × NVIDIA A40 (sm_86). The reproducer uses one GPU. Software: vLLM commit `92044241a` (`0.30.1rc1.dev648+g92044241a`), with and without this PR, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, Python 3.12.12.

**Reproducer.** The reported path needs a checkpoint with FP8 PLE weights and a global scale. The public `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` checkpoint has BF16 PLE weights and no scale. So the reproducer launches the kernel directly with a small FP8 tensor. Below is the core of the script that ran. The full script only adds prints and a `try`/`except`.

```python
import torch
from vllm.models.qwen4_exp.common.ngram_embedding import (
    _lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel,
)

N, D, BLOCK_D = 4, 16, 16
device = torch.device("cuda", 0)
weight = torch.zeros(N, D, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device=device)
ids = torch.tensor([0], dtype=torch.long, device=device)
output = torch.zeros(1, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)

_lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel[(ids.numel(),)](
    weight, ids, output, D, 0, N, BLOCK_D=BLOCK_D,
)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
```

Run it from outside the source tree: `python -P repro_59868.py`.

| | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 3 of 3 failed | `CompilationError`, exit code 1 | | After | 2 of 2 passed | launch completes, exit code 0 |

Two of the "before" runs used the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-92044241a02f05de51420d654daf669de20b4691` image, and one used a source install. The "after" runs used the final patch. Three more runs on earlier versions of the patch also passed. Before the fix, every run showed the same error as the report:

```
triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError: at 1:0:
def _lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel(
^
ValueError("type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture. The supported fp8 dtypes are ('fp8e4b15', 'fp8e5')")
```

The reproducer writes from an FP8 weight into a BF16 output. vLLM never does this, because `_lookup` requires `output.dtype == weight.dtype`. After the fix, that call copies the raw FP8 bytes. So the reproducer only shows that the launch compiles. The tests below check the values on the real path.

**Existing tests.**

```
python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py -q --noconftest -k "pinned or uva"
```

`--noconftest` was used only because `tblib` was not installed locally.

- Before: `3 failed, 13 passed, 59 deselected`. All three fail with the error above: `test_ple_pinned_embedding_loads_on_cpu_and_looks_up_through_uva[True]`, `test_amd_pinned_embedding_output_written_under_compile[fp8]` and `test_amd_pinned_embedding_output_written_under_cudagraph_capture[fp8]`. They go through `_lookup` and check exact values.
- After: `16 passed, 59 deselected`. The full `test_ple.py` together with `tests/test_triton_utils.py` gives `88 passed`.

**Other checks.** These used one-off scripts that are not part of this PR.

- NVIDIA serving flow with FP8 on the A40 (`start_prefetch` → `forward` → `dequantize`): bit-exact against `weight[ids]` for row widths 3 and 160. With an ETP size of 2, rows owned by the other rank come out as zero bytes, in FP8 and in BF16.
- Large BF16 lookup with 160-element rows, compared row by row with `weight[ids]`: 7,000,000 and 8,388,608 rows gave 0 wrong rows, with byte offsets up to 2,684,354,240. Without the int64 row index (see Details), 7,000,000 rows hit `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`.
- BF16 speed against the old kernel, reading a pinned host table through UVA: time ratio ×0.993 to ×1.03 for row widths 64 to 1024 and for 160 (the real model's width). Outputs were bit-identical.
- Import with Triton hidden (`sys.modules["triton"] = None`) passes. Without the placeholder change it fails with `AttributeError: module 'triton.language' has no attribute 'pointer_type'`.
- `pre-commit run --files` on both changed files passes.

**CI gap.** On NVIDIA, CI does not run the GPU tests in `test_ple.py`, and no CI runner is below SM89. So CI cannot catch this bug if it comes back. The runs above are the validation. The AMD MI355 job does run `test_ple.py`, so it covers the new byte copy on AMD.

## Details

**Root cause.** The kernel's pointer parameters had no annotations, so Triton took their types from the tensors. An FP8 E4M3FN table became a `*fp8e4nv` parameter. Triton 3.7.1 accepts `fp8e4nv` only on compute capability 8.9 and higher. It rejects the type while it lowers the signature, before it compiles the body. That is why the error points at `1:0`, the `def` line. On the A40, a kernel with an empty body and one `float8_e4m3fn` pointer fails the same way. With `float8_e5m2` it compiles.

**Fix.** The kernel does no math on the values. Its only caller, `Qwen4ExpPLEPinnedHostEmbedding._lookup`, requires the output dtype to match the weight dtype. FP8 scaling happens later, in PyTorch (`dequantize`). So the kernel is a pure row gather. Both pointers are now annotated `tl.pointer_type(tl.uint8)`. The caller passes `row_bytes = embedding_dim * weight.element_size()` and sets `BLOCK_D = next_power_of_2(row_bytes)`. This works for FP8 and for BF16. `_reduce_etp_embeddings` in the same file already moves FP8 rows as raw bytes. The fix has to be in the signature, because the signature is where the error happens. A `uint8` pointer cast inside the body would come too late. A `.view(torch.uint8)` at the call site would fix `_lookup`, but not a direct launch with an FP8 tensor like the reproducer.

The fix also needs two more changes:

- `row_id` is now int64. Offsets are now in bytes, so for BF16 `row_id * row_bytes` is twice the old element offset. An int32 product would overflow at half as many rows as before. With `embedding_across_dp`, it would overflow at DP × `max_num_batched_tokens` ≥ 419,431 instead of 838,861 (for example, DP8 × 65,536). `tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)` is the usual vLLM idiom.
- `TritonLanguagePlaceholder` gets `uint8` and `pointer_type`. Python evaluates parameter annotations at import time, so without these names the module fails to import when Triton is missing. This is the first `tl.pointer_type` annotation in `vllm/`. mypy rejects it, so both lines carry `# type: ignore[valid-type]`.

**Limitations.**

- No end-to-end `vllm serve` run with an FP8 PLE checkpoint (see Reproducer). Only sm_86 was tested, not sm_80.
- `_engram_lookup_kernel` in `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py` also takes an FP8 E4M3FN table with no annotation, so it may fail the same way below SM89. It was not run. It does math on the values, so this byte-copy fix does not carry over, and it is not part of this PR.
- No model evaluation was run. The lookups are bit-exact in the tests above.

## E2E results (patch)

`vllm serve` with `-tp 4 --enable-expert-parallel --max-model-len 32768 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}'`. The patch is applied on top of `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-92044241a02f05de51420d654daf669de20b4691`. GSM8K is 5-shot, chat mode, thinking disabled (stderr ≈ ±0.7).

| Model | GPU | PLE dtype | Result | GSM8K flexible / strict | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` | A100 (SM80) | FP8 E4M3, pinned host | starts and serves | 92.95 / 91.96 | 
| `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` | B200 (SM100) | FP8 E4M3, pinned host | bit-identical to unpatched | 92.49 / 91.51 |
| `Inferact/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` | B200 (SM100) | BF16, pinned host | bit-identical to unpatched | 93.40 / 92.34 |

"Bit-identical" means greedy decoding at batch size 1: 10/10 prompts and 640/640 tokens match the unpatched build, with exactly equal logprobs.

---

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Route gfx942 mHC seams through aiter mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed
body:
## Summary

On gfx942, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill runs the delayed mHC seam as separate AITER kernels. This routes the carried attention seam and every FFN seam through `torch.ops.vllm.mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_aiter`, which calls [aiter #6171](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6171) `mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed`, from 64 tokens. Shorter steps stay on the folded post GEMM. Layer 0 and Engram stay on the current AITER seam.

vLLM #59802 overlaps the mHC gate projection on gfx950 and does not change this prefill seam.

## What changed

- `vllm/model_executor/layers/mhc.py`: calls the torch op from 64 tokens when AITER's `mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_asm_supported` accepts the shape. No `gfx942_seam` flag.
- `vllm/_aiter_ops.py`, `vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/aiter.py`, `vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/__init__.py`: register `mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_aiter`.
- `vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py`: one launch at 64 tokens compiles `module_mhc_seam_asm`.
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py`: `MHCPreDelayedOp()`. Layer 0 passes `x`. Engram omits `sublayer_out`.
- `tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py`: 63 stays on the folded post GEMM, 64 calls the ASM seam once, and both match post then pre.

## Gating

Only the DeepSeek-V4.1 AMD decoder constructs `MHCPreDelayedOp`. No flag, no environment variable. A seam with `sublayer_out`, no `norm_weight`, and no layer-0 `x` calls the op from 64 tokens when the probe accepts the shape. The server logs `mhc_seam: aiter mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed from 64 tokens`. gfx950 stays on the RMSNorm route. A build without the symbol stays on the current AITER seam.

AITER's few-token kernel runs below 60 (`MHC_SEAM_SMALL_MAX_T`). The `b40` in the gates binary is not that cutoff, and 64 is not a measured crossover: on this machine the fused kernel was faster at 32, 60, 63, 64, 128, and 8192. The gate counts tokens in the forward. A decode-only step at concurrency 2 or 4 has 2 or 4 tokens and stays on the folded post GEMM. A step that carries a prefill chunk takes the kernel for the whole forward.

## Depends on

[aiter #6171](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6171), stacked on [aiter #6168](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6168). The kernels are not in this diff. Without the symbol, the server stays on the current AITER seam.

## Performance

Same machine, same AITER build, only this dispatch differs. 4× MI325X (gfx942), TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, language model only, speculative decoding off. vLLM `0.31.1rc1.dev1+gbb87d227d`. The on arm logged `mhc_seam: aiter mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed from 64 tokens` and loaded `mhc_seam_v3_b2_stnt`. `vllm bench serve`, 20 prompts, seed 7. Prefill chunks are 16384 tokens.

### Concurrency 2

| Shape | | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 262144→1024 | Off | 32.84 | 37310.48 | 24.48 | 25.14 |
| | On | 33.58 | 36063.46 | 24.35 | 26.51 |
| | Δ | +2.3% | −3.3% | −0.5% | +5.4% |

title: [ROCm][DSv4/4.1] Fuse inverse RoPE and MXFP8 quant into the aiter sparse MLA and sparse MLA gating changes
body:
## Overview

On ROCm with the aiter sparse MLA backend, DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 ran a separate `rocm_inverse_rope_rows_` pass (and, on V4.1, a separate MXFP8 quantization) after attention. The aiter kernel can now do both in its store, so this passes it the positions / cos-sin cache (and the MXFP8 output buffer) and drops the extra passes.

- DSv4.1: decode and prefill rotate in the store; with an MXFP8 `o_proj` input the store also quantizes into it.
- DSv4: decode and prefill rotate in the store when `wo_a` is BF16. The fp8 `wo_a` path is unchanged (`inverse_rope_group_quant` already rotates there).
- Rows not rotated by a kernel store still go through the standalone pass (none on the aiter path).
- Also, gluon sparse MLA path is disabled for num_heads > 64 + prefill. For those workloads, existing kv gather + OPUS is faster.

Requires the aiter change adding `inv_rope_positions`, `inv_rope_cos_sin_cache` and `out_mxfp8` to `sparse_mla_fwd`, merge after the aiter bump (already done, aiter v0.1.25 has the support for these changes).

Perf. and accuracy runs to be added.

## Details

title: [Attention] FA4 hd512 GQA on Blackwell for DiffusionGemma
body:
## Overview

Run DiffusionGemma's head-size-512 global attention layers on FA4 on Blackwell (SM100/SM110) instead of the Triton fallback. The vLLM side of vllm-project/flash-attention#204: this PR bumps the `vllm-flash-attn` pin to that PR's commit, so it must not merge before #204 does (the pin will be re-pointed at the merged commit).

## Claims

- On B300, the hd512 global-layer attention kernel takes 80 µs instead of Triton's 658 µs (k = 8256, page 128; 101 µs vs 662 µs with page 16).
- End to end, DiffusionGemma-26B-A4B on one B300 goes from ~947 to 1152–1206 block tok/s (+22–27%), with unchanged GSM8K accuracy within noise.
- FA4 is selected for d = dv = 512 on SM100/SM110 only, and falls back to FA2 for features the hd512 kernel lacks.

## Validation

End to end: DiffusionGemma-26B-A4B, BF16, TP1, one B300, concurrency 1. Workload and client from sgl-project/sglang#42099's reproduction gist (8k input, 1024 output positions, 96 requests). Default backend auto-selection puts the hd256 sliding layers on TRITON_ATTN (mm_prefix) and, with this PR, the hd512 global layers on FLASH_ATTN.

| | Block tok/s | Mean end-to-end | First block | GSM8K (128 questions) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Triton (main) | ~947 | 1.36 s | 0.55 s | 126/128 |
| FA4 hd512 (this PR) | **1152–1206** (3 runs) | 1.03–1.07 s | 0.39–0.42 s | 125/128 |

Denoising steps per canvas are unchanged (~20); the run-to-run spread tracks step count (20.2–20.9). The GSM8K difference is a single question flip: small numerical changes alter adaptive denoising trajectories.

Tests (B300, with the flash-attention sources from #204):

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_mixed_causal_attn.py      # 9 passed, 4 skipped (SM90-only FA4 cases)
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py -k "hd512 or hd256"   # 37 passed
```

- `test_flash_attn4_hd512_mixed_causal` (new, SM100): 16 query / 2 KV heads, d = 512, a batch mixing causal and bidirectional sequences (plus all-causal and all-bidirectional) through `split_dynamic_causal` and `flash_attn_varlen_func(seqused_q=...)`, against the existing reference.
- `test_fa4_hd512_fallback_matrix` (new): FA version selection for hd512, covering SM100 vs SM120, mismatched `head_size_v`, sinks, softcap, FP8 KV cache, DCP, R-SWA, and mm_prefix with and without `is_diffusion`.

CI gap: `tests/kernels/attention` runs on L4 in CI, so the selector cases run there but the SM100 kernel test skips (no B200 attention-kernel job); it was run locally on B300 as above. The flash-attention side has its own tests (130 passed on B300); see #204.

## Details

- **Pin bump** (`cmake/external_projects/vllm_flash_attn.cmake`): to #204's head. Besides #204, this picks up flash-attention #198 (SM90 SplitKV fix, which #59436 also bumps for), #195 and #200 (SM100 sparse MLA decode); those only add optional arguments and a new decode kernel.
- **Selection** (`fa_utils.py`): `uses_fa4_hd512_kernel` mirrors `uses_fa4_hd256_kernel` (d = dv = 512 on SM100/SM110). FA4 is kept for those shapes past the TMEM head-size gate, and `_fa4_hd512_fallback_reason` drops to FA2 for sinks, softcap, quantized KV cache, mm_prefix (except diffusion models, which use a per-sequence causal flag instead), R-SWA and DCP.
- **Per-sequence causal on SM100** (`flash_attn.py`): DiffusionGemma passes a per-sequence causal flag, and FA4's `dynamic_causal` is SM90-only. On other architectures the backend now issues two launches, one causal and one non-causal, each restricted to its own sequences with `seqused_q` (`split_dynamic_causal`, a module-level helper so the kernel test can drive the same split). The split is device-only (no host sync), and costs one extra launch per hd512 layer, already included in the e2e numbers. SM90 keeps the single `dynamic_causal` launch. A per-sequence causal flag combined with a sliding window still requires SM90 and raises otherwise (DiffusionGemma's windowed layers run on Triton).
- **Wrapper** (`flash_attn_interface.py`): passes `seqused_q` through to FA4.

Not a duplicate: open PRs touching this area are #45434 (SM90 FP8 KV cache for hd512) and #59436 (pin bump to the SM90 SplitKV fix, which this pin includes). None route hd512 to FA4 on Blackwell or split per-sequence causal for SM100.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change and its tests; I have reviewed it and ran the tests and benchmarks above.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Use AITER FlyDSL GEMM for DeepSeek V4.1's 32x32 MXFP8 linears on gfx950
body:
## Overview
On gfx950, DeepSeek V4.1's MXFP8 linears with 32x32 weight-scale blocks run on vLLM's Triton block-scaled GEMM (`rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm`). With AITER enabled, this PR runs them on AITER's FlyDSL MXFP8 GEMM instead. No other model or layer changes path.

## Claims
- **+3.7% total token throughput** at ISL 350k / OSL 350 / conc 32 and **+2.6%** at ISL 32k / OSL 32 / conc 32 
- Accuracy is unchanged: GSM8K 0.9735 vs 0.9727 (strict match, ±0.0045).

ISL 350k / OSL 350 / conc 32:
| metric | baseline | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| total tok/s | 44,011 | 45,641 | +3.70% |
| TTFT mean | 165.9 s | 159.9 s | −3.63% |
| TPOT mean | 210.9 ms | 203.4 ms | −3.55% |


ISL 32k / OSL 32 / conc 32:
| metric | baseline | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| total tok/s | 49,488 | 50,765 | +2.58% |
| TTFT mean | 14.14 s | 13.70 s | −3.09% |
| TPOT mean | 119.8 ms | 119.0 ms | −0.68% |

## Validation

**Unit Tests**
```shell
pytest -q tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py \
  "tests/kernels/test_minimax_m3_amd_ops.py::test_mxfp8_rocm_native_unaligned_k_dequantizes_at_load"
```

- `test_rocm_mxfp8_linear_flydsl_matches_block32_gemm` checks FlyDSL against the Triton block32 GEMM. It covers DeepSeek V4.1's seven 32x32 shapes (TP2/TP4) at M = 1, 7, 32, 33, 192 and 1024, with relative error < 1e-3.
- `test_rocm_mxfp8_linear_flydsl_leaves_other_layers_alone` checks that 1x32-scaled layers (every other MXFP8 model), K % 64 != 0 and batched layers keep their path and their weight bytes.

**E2E**

```shell

export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1

export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
vllm serve /data/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \

  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
``` 

bench command:
```shell

    --model="$MODEL_PATH" \
    --backend=vllm \
    --tokenizer="$MODEL_PATH" \
    --dataset-name=random \

```


lm-eval command:
```shell

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template \
    --tasks /app/scripts/infx/gsm8k.yaml \
    --output_path eval_infx_out --log_samples \
    --model_args "model=${MODEL_PATH},base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8000/v1/chat/completions,api_key=EMPTY,eos_string=</s>,max_retries=5,num_concurrent=16,timeout=1800,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=32768" \
``` 

## Details
- Only the GEMM call in `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`'s existing 32x32 branch is changed, other branches as is, and there is no new env var.
- FlyDSL runs when: AITER linear ops on, gfx950, BF16 model, 32x32 scale blocks, K % 64 == 0.
- The weights are preshuffled once at load.
- Batched gemm for attention output projection `wo_a` stays on the Triton BMM path (the perf gain in e2e wasn't worth the code footprint).

title: [Bug] DFlash2/DSpark + prefix caching corrupt output after a cache hit on Qwen3.8-27B (TP=1) on 0.30/0.31; 0.29 and MTP are fine
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM 0.31.0 (also reproduced on 0.30.0). vLLM 0.29.0 passes the same test.
- torch 2.13.0+cu130, flashinfer-python/cubin 0.7.0.post1 (0.6.18.post1 on 0.30.0), CUDA 13.3, driver 610.57.04
- 1× RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 48 GB (sm_120), Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 7.0.0-34
- Target: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` NVFP4 checkpoint, compressed-tensors mixed precision (NVFP4 on the MLP projections, FP8 W8A8 on attention / GDN projections / lm_head, `linear_attn.{in_proj_a,in_proj_b,norm}` and `mtp.*` unquantized via `ignore`)
- Drafter: `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (`DFlash2DraftModel`, sliding_window 2048), `num_speculative_tokens: 7`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Since 0.30.0, serving Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 with the DFlash2 drafter and prefix caching enabled produces garbage after a prefix-cache hit. The first requests of a conversation are fine. From the third request on, once the prompt resumes from cached blocks, the model emits a single repeated token (`duct`, over and over) with no coherent content, and the drafter accepts nothing (`SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 1.00, Accepted: 0 tokens`). The same five requests against 0.29.0 come back coherent every time. I have run the comparison twice on each version.

The test is a replay of a real agent conversation: five consecutive chat-completions requests from one session (31,776 / 45,606 / 52,737 / 65,364 / 67,502 prompt tokens, 25 tool schemas, seed 17), sent in order to a fresh engine so each request hits the previous one's prefix. The conversation itself is private, but I can build a synthetic equivalent if that helps.

Serve command (production flags):

```
vllm serve /models/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --max-model-len 250000 --kv-cache-memory-bytes 17379961324 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"/models/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7}' \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --override-generation-config '{"temperature":1.0,"top_p":0.95,"top_k":20,"min_p":0.0}' --scheduling-policy priority
```

env: `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=false`. Prefix caching on (default), `mamba_cache_mode` resolves to `align`.

### What I tried, to narrow it down

All on 0.31.0, same five requests, fresh engine each time:

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| nothing (command above) | fails at request 3 |
| PR #57128 applied (the `MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` / `drop_eagle_block` fix) | fails |
| `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` instead of FlashInfer | fails |
| `--linear-backend cutlass` (in-tree CUTLASS NVFP4 GEMM) | fails |
| `--linear-backend marlin` (weight-only W4A16, no activation quant) | fails |
| smaller KV pool / 180K window / util 0.94 (copied from my FP8 route) | fails |
| `"disable_eagle_block_drop": true` in the speculative config | worse: garbage from request 1, even cold |
| **no speculative config at all** | **passes 5/5** |
| **`{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}` (checkpoint's own MTP head)** | **passes 5/5** |
| **`{"method":"dspark","model":"RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-speculator.dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7}`** | **fails at request 3** |
| **FP8 target (`Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8`, `quant_method: fp8`) with the same DFlash2 config** | **passes 5/5, twice** |

A unique `cache_salt` per request on 0.30.0 also makes requests 3–5 pass, so the failure needs an actual cache hit.

So the NVFP4 GEMM kernels are not involved (three different kernels, including weight-only, all fail), the GDN prefill kernel is not involved, and the KV pool size is not involved. What it needs is: a hidden-state drafter (DFlash2 or DSpark; MTP is fine) + a prefix-cache hit + this compressed-tensors NVFP4 target, on 0.30 or later. The FP8 checkpoint with the identical drafter config is fine. Turning off the EAGLE trailing-block drop makes it strictly worse, which reads to me like the drafter is leaving bad Mamba/GDN state in the cached tail block and the drop normally hides it inside a request but not across requests.

The compressed-tensors checkpoint is the obvious difference from the FP8 one: it has an `ignore` list covering `linear_attn` sub-modules (the bf16 `in_proj_a` / `in_proj_b` / `norm`) alongside `config_groups` that target `linear_attn.{in_proj_qkv,in_proj_z,out_proj}` at FP8. If the drafter path resolves those layers differently from the plain `fp8` loader, that would be where I'd look first, but I haven't gone further than the table above.

Related: #53912 and #55766 describe neighbouring hybrid-GDN prefix-cache corruption with speculative decoding.

### What I can provide

Per-request replay output (prompt token counts, finish reasons, draft metrics), engine logs for every ablation above, and a synthetic reproducer on request.

title: [Docs][KV Connector] Explain effective HMA mismatches for NIXL peers
body:
## Overview

Document how asymmetric connector configurations can cause an effective HMA-state mismatch during the NIXL handshake. Addresses the documentation request in #60124; does not add field-level mismatch diagnostics.

## Claims

- Explain why omitting the HMA flag on both instances need not produce matching effective settings.
- Document supported remedies, HMA-required configurations, and the need to compare other compatibility fields.

## Validation

- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `pre-commit run --files docs/features/disagg_prefill.md docs/features/nixl_connector_compatibility.md` — passed.
- `API_AUTONAV_EXCLUDE='re:.*' VLLM_DOCS_BUILD=1 mkdocs build --site-dir <output>` — passed with existing API cross-reference warnings because API generation was excluded.
- Inspected generated HTML: both new anchor links resolve; the HMA note is inside the MultiConnector list item.
- Cross-checked the explanation against connector HMA support detection, config auto-disable behavior, the compatibility hash, and NIXL/HiSparse guards. Documentation-only: no model or GPU evaluation performed, and no end-to-end serving fix claimed.

## Details

MultiConnector requires every child to support HMA. Automatic configuration can therefore disable HMA only on one peer, while the other keeps it enabled. The handshake compares the effective state, not merely whether users supplied the same flags.

The workaround is intentionally conditional: HMA cannot be disabled for the documented SSM/Mamba or HiSparse configurations, and matching HMA alone does not guarantee compatibility. The transfer safety check remains unchanged.

Duplicate checks found no open PR for `60124 in:body` or the same HMA troubleshooting text. #59584 covers authentication/side-channel troubleshooting; #60113 changes heterogeneous KV-group transfer; #48882 changes subclass validation; #42620 implements LMCache HMA support. None supplies this explanation.

AI assistance was used for investigation, drafting, implementation, and automated review/validation. The human submitter reviewed the changes and authorized submission. The validation results above were obtained with AI assistance.

title: [Bug]: NIXL DCP config checks don't apply to NixlPullConnector
body:
### Your current environment

vLLM main `6ad2e06c4a`. Config validation only; reproduces on CPU.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`NixlConnector` is the backward-compatible alias of `NixlPullConnector`, but the NIXL checks in `vllm/config/vllm.py` match only the name `"NixlConnector"`. With `kv_connector="NixlPullConnector"` and `decode_context_parallel_size > 1`:

- the NIXL DCP check in `VllmConfig.__post_init__` doesn't run, so non-MLA models and DCP sizes other than the NIXL transfer parallel size are accepted;
- `adjust_dcp_kv_cache_interleave_size` leaves an unset `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size` at 1 instead of setting it to the block size, which NIXL P/D requires (`kv_transfer_state.py`). The NIXL worker doesn't check it.

```python
from vllm.engine.arg_utils import EngineArgs

for name in ("NixlConnector", "NixlPullConnector"):
    args = EngineArgs(
        model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct",  # GQA, not MLA
        tensor_parallel_size=4,
        decode_context_parallel_size=2,
        distributed_executor_backend="mp",
        kv_transfer_config={"kv_connector": name, "kv_role": "kv_both"},
    )
    try:
        args.create_engine_config()
        print(f"{name}: accepted")
    except Exception:
        print(f"{name}: rejected")
```

```
NixlConnector: rejected
NixlPullConnector: accepted
```

`NixlConnector` fails the assert "decode_context_parallel_size=2 must be 1 or equal to the NIXL transfer parallel size=4".

`validate_block_size` and the HiSparse connector warning also match only `"NixlConnector"`. The `validate_block_size` skip assumes the interleave size is pinned to the block size, which since #55531 holds only when `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size` is unset, so adding `NixlPullConnector` there would also stop checking an explicit interleave size for it.

`KVTransferConfig.has_connector` compares names literally, so a fix can go there or at each site. #60168 has a minimal per-site patch with test rows for the two bulleted sites.

title: [Bug]: [KV Offload][P2P] A NIXL error raised by `write_blocks` during a fetch is never reported to the requesting peer, so it waits the full round timeout
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `0.30.0+g87ecf7d`, plus open PRs #56836 and #57139 and some local P2P hardening patches (see the note below).
- torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, `nixl-cu13` 1.3.2 (UCX backend).
- 8× H100 80GB HBM3 per node, driver 580.126.20, RoCE.
- Model: GLM-5.3, disaggregated prefill/decode. Prefill is DP4 × PCP8, one DP rank per node, with `TieringOffloadingSpec`: a 512 GiB CPU primary tier plus a `p2p` secondary tier over UCX.

The code path below is unchanged on `main` (checked against `e11962fc1c`): our build's `session/server.py` is byte-identical to `main`, and `data/nixl.py`'s `write_blocks` is identical too.


### 🐛 Describe the bug


When the source side of a P2P fetch calls `NixlTransport.write_blocks` and NIXL raises (we saw `nixlRemoteDisconnectError` and `nixlNotFoundError`), the exception escapes to the session's message dispatcher, which only logs it. The requesting peer is never told the fetch failed. It waits for its round timeout (30 s here), aborts, and only then falls back to recomputing the prefix.

Call chain, from our traceback (line numbers from our build, same code on `main`):

```
session.py   _on_message            -> _dispatch_message
server.py    on_fetch               (line 390) -> self._submit_transfer(...)
server.py    _submit_transfer       (line 1072) -> self._transport.write_blocks(...)
nixl.py      write_blocks           (line 294) -> self._agent.transfer(handle)
nixl_cu13/_api.py transfer          (line 632) raises nixlRemoteDisconnectError / nixlNotFoundError
```

`_submit_transfer` already has a fail-fast path, but only for `write_blocks` *returning* `None` (no remote descriptor list for the peer). That path marks the round finishing and calls `_finalize_outbound(kv_request_id, round_key, success=False)` so that "the peer and the local store jobs don't wait for finish_request or for `_STORE_TIMEOUT_S` / `_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S`". A raised exception skips it. The dispatcher in `session.py` (`main` lines ~319-333) logs `error handling message 'fetch'`, increments `_dispatch_error_count` and continues. Nothing finalizes the round.

Observed on the source and requesting ranks for one pull (`kv_request_id` shortened):

```
05:16:26 source     P2PSession <requester>:7777: error handling message 'fetch' (count=1): NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT
                      File ".../p2p/session/server.py", line 390, in on_fetch
05:16:56 requester  P2PSession <source>:7777: paircheck-5d88… round=0 timed out, sending abort
05:16:56 source     P2PSession <requester>:7777: store job 6883 timed out
05:16:57 requester  load request paircheck-5d88… (job_id=6864) completed with failure after abort
```

Impact: each affected request took 37 s, against about 6 s to recompute the ~113K-token prefix locally and about 3.4 s for a successful pull. With any persistent transfer failure (see issue 2), every pull touching the bad peer pays the full timeout, and there is no request error to surface it.

It also looks like the handle from `make_prepped_xfer` is not released when `transfer` raises, though we did not confirm this.

### Expected behavior

A NIXL error while submitting a fetch's write should be handled like the existing `write_blocks -> None` case: finalize the round with `success=False`, so the requester falls back to recompute immediately rather than after its timeout.

### Suggested fix

One of:

- catch NIXL errors in `NixlTransport.write_blocks` around `make_prepped_xfer` / `transfer`, release the handle, log, and return `None`, which reuses the existing fail-fast path; or
- in `P2PSession._submit_transfer`, wrap the `write_blocks` call and send exceptions to the same branch as `transfer_id is None`.

A unit test could make the transport's `write_blocks` raise and assert that the round is finalized with `success=False` and the peer is notified, without waiting for `_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S`.

### Reproduction

Any condition that makes `agent.transfer` raise on the source while the control session stays up reproduces it. We hit it after issue 2: a peer whose NIXL path had gone stale. In that state, every directed pull to or from the peer showed the trace above, which we confirmed with requests carrying `kv_transfer_params.remote_kv_source = {kv_request_id, remote_host, remote_port}`.

Related: #56836 (bounds unanswered *lookup* waits; does not cover this *fetch* failure), #57139.


### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: [KV Offload][P2P] After a peer's EngineCore stalls ~45 s, P2P transfers to and from it fail permanently, although the control session reconnects
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `0.30.0+g87ecf7d`, plus open PRs #56836 and #57139 and some local P2P hardening patches (see the note below).
- torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, `nixl-cu13` 1.3.2 (UCX backend).
- 8× H100 80GB HBM3 per node, driver 580.126.20, RoCE.
- Model: GLM-5.3, disaggregated prefill/decode. Prefill is DP4 × PCP8, one DP rank per node, with `TieringOffloadingSpec`: a 512 GiB CPU primary tier plus a `p2p` secondary tier over UCX.


The P2P tier config on each prefill rank:

```json
{"type": "p2p", "host": "<pod ip>", "port": 7777, "backends": ["UCX"], "num_threads": 4,
 "connect_timeout_s": 30, "heartbeat_interval_s": 2, "heartbeat_timeout_s": 10}
```

Note: this build is vLLM `87ecf7d` plus #56836, #57139 (`data/nixl.py` byte-identical to #57139's head `590a8d97`) and four local patches: unacked handshakes expire to MISS; reconnects that reuse a peer's identity are accepted (`ROUTER_HANDOVER`); configurable heartbeat and connect timeouts (the last three fields above); and control sends that never block the scheduler. We have not yet reproduced this on plain `main`. The relevant path does exist there: `manager.py` (around line 774) calls `self._data.remove_remote_peer(pid)` when a peer goes down, and the session re-registers the peer on reconnect.

### 🐛 Describe the bug


One prefill rank's EngineCore, which also serves its P2P port, was paused with `SIGSTOP` for 45 s and then resumed with `SIGCONT`. This was under steady multi-turn load, 32 concurrent sessions with ~90K-token contexts. The DP group stalled and recovered as expected: 45 s is under DeepEP's timeout, and no request failed.

After the resume, the **control plane recovered but the data plane did not**:

- Peers marked the paused rank `down` and later logged `created connected session` for it; heartbeats and lookups work again.
- Every P2P data transfer **to or from** that rank fails, with all 3 peers, in both directions. Errors: `check_xfer_state failed … NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT`, then `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND`, and `error handling message 'fetch' … NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT / NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND` on the serving side.
- The first failures appeared 6 minutes after the resume, and transfers were still failing at our last check, 22 minutes after it. We saw no recovery in that time. Restarting the group (46 minutes after the resume) fixed it.
- Lookups keep succeeding: the source reports holding the prefix (219-221 of 219-221 chunk lookups hit), so the router and engine keep choosing pulls that cannot succeed. Each one then hits issue 1 (a 30 s wait, then recompute).
- Pulls between the other three ranks keep working throughout.

UCX (`UCX_LOG_LEVEL=diag`) logged exactly one error on the paused rank, at the moment of `SIGCONT`:

```
04:56:27 ucp_ep.c:1905 UCX ERROR ep 0x7fc41735c100 has already been closed
```

That suggests the peers closed their UCX endpoints to it during the freeze.

Directed pulls 20-22 minutes after the resume, each a ~113K-token prefix warmed on the source and requested on the target with the source named in `kv_transfer_params.remote_kv_source`:

| Source → target | Bytes pulled | Tokens via P2P | Request time |
|---|---|---|---|
| healthy → healthy | 6.16 GB | 112,640 | 3.5 s |
| healthy → healthy | 6.16 GB | 112,640 | 3.3 s |
| healthy → **paused rank** | 0 | 0 | 37.1 s (recomputed) |
| **paused rank** → healthy | 0 | 0 | 37.3 s (recomputed) |

For contrast, blocking the P2P port on a rank with an iptables DROP for 3 minutes is handled correctly. Peers mark it down within 17 s, handshake retries are bounded (`no ConnectAckMsg within 30.0s`), and transfers work again after the block is lifted. The difference with `SIGSTOP` is that the paused process keeps its own NIXL/UCX state across the freeze, while its peers tear theirs down.

### Expected behavior

After a peer reconnects, P2P transfers to and from it work again. If the data path cannot be re-established, the peer should be treated as unavailable, so lookups MISS immediately instead of matching and then failing every fetch.

### Questions for maintainers

- On reconnect, are both sides expected to `remove_remote_agent` / `add_remote_agent` and rebuild the prepped descriptor lists? The paused rank was frozen while its peers declared it down, so its own view of them may never have been reset.
- Could NIXL be reusing a stale UCX endpoint when the remote agent of the same name is re-added? That would fit `ep … has already been closed` followed by `REMOTE_DISCONNECT` and then `NOT_FOUND`. If so, this may need a NIXL change or a fresh agent name or generation per registration.

### Reproduction

1. Two or more prefill ranks with the `p2p` secondary tier, under load that produces pulls.
2. `kill -STOP` one rank's EngineCore for longer than the peers' heartbeat timeout (10 s here; we used 45 s), then `kill -CONT`.
3. Wait for sessions to reconnect, then send a pull between the paused rank and a healthy one, in either direction.

We can provide full prefill logs, the UCX diag log of the paused rank, and py-spy stacks of all engine processes taken at the first failure.

Related: #60204 (why each failed pull costs the full timeout), #57139 (peer registration), #56836.


### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Perf][Attention] Fuse DCP empty-row neutralization in sparse MLA decode into one Triton kernel
body:
## Purpose

Introduce `neutralize_dcp_empty_rows_`, a Triton kernel that fuses the eager `(topk_indices == -1).all(-1)` + two `masked_fill_` ops which zero `out` and set `lse` to `-inf` on rows where a DCP rank owns no top-k slots. Used in the DCP decode paths of `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` and `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`. Bit-identical to the previous ops.

## Test Plan

- Unit: new `tests/v1/attention/test_dcp_empty_row_masking.py`
## Test Result

Unit: `31 passed`.

Isolated, per call inside a CUDA graph (64 heads, head_dim 512, topk 2048):

| decode tokens | main (µs) | this PR (µs) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.34 | 2.29 |
| 16 | 12.82 | 2.38 |
| 64 | 15.85 | 2.41 |
| 256 | 25.44 | 3.52 |

E2E, 512 output tokens:

title: [Perf][MRV2] Avoid stream syncs in NonUvaBuffer host-to-device copies
body:
## Overview

Fixes #58849. `NonUvaBuffer`, the MRV2 buffer fallback when pinned memory is unavailable (WSL2 by default), copies its host buffer to the GPU with a blocking `copy_()`. This makes the copy `non_blocking`, as V1's `CpuGpuBuffer.copy_to_gpu` already does for pageable memory. The root cause and the two-line fix come from @joynerwk03 in the issue (co-author on the commit).

## Claims

- Removes the `cudaStreamSynchronize` after every `NonUvaBuffer.uva()` copy (~16 per decode step), so preparing step N+1 no longer waits for step N to finish.
- WSL2 with the default V2 runner: decode step time **-13.7% at batch 1 and -12.5% at batch 16** on an RTX 4050, the same as `VLLM_WSL2_ENABLE_PIN_MEMORY=1`. The reporter measured -12% on an RTX 3090.
- No change where pinned memory is available: those platforms use `UvaBuffer`.

## Validation

**Regression test** `tests/kernels/core/test_uva.py::test_non_uva_buffer_copies_without_stream_sync`: copies under `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")`, overwrites the host buffer right away, then checks the GPU values. On main it fails with `RuntimeError: called a synchronizing CUDA operation`; with this PR it passes.

**End to end**, main `888074b4` vs this PR: Qwen3-0.6B, default V2 runner, default compile and CUDA graphs, RTX 4050 Laptop 6 GB, WSL2 (Ubuntu 24.04, driver 581.86), torch 2.13.0+cu130. Arms alternated, 3 fresh engines per arm; each engine ran 2 warmup and 8 timed `LLM.generate` calls of 256 greedy tokens (`ignore_eos`).

| Decode step, median of 3 engines (range) | main | this PR | main + `VLLM_WSL2_ENABLE_PIN_MEMORY=1` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Batch 1 | 8.83 ms (8.68-8.91) | **7.61 ms** (7.43-7.67) | 7.64 ms (7.63-7.65) |
| Batch 16 | 10.98 ms (10.67-11.02) | **9.61 ms** (9.44-9.71) | 9.67 ms (9.66-9.84) |

**Outputs.** Comparing greedy outputs across restarts is confounded by #58899 (Inductor re-tunes reductions by timing), so I kept one engine alive (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`) and swapped `NonUvaBuffer.uva` between the blocking and `non_blocking` versions for four rounds of 16 prompts x 128 tokens: token ids and top-5 logprobs were bitwise identical in every round, in two separate engines (main `840c7c2`; `buffer_utils.py` is unchanged since).

## Details

Why the async copy is safe:
- **Stream ordering.** Every reader of a `NonUvaBuffer` GPU slot runs on the copy's stream, or on a side stream that calls `wait_stream` on it first (async output, spec decode and PP copy streams). This is from reading the code; ubatch/DBO, PP and DeepSeek-V4.1 paths were not exercised.
- **Reusing the host buffer.** The next step overwrites `cpu` right after the copy is issued. For pageable memory the driver stages the copy into pinned memory during the call, synchronizing with the stream when it has to ([CUDA API sync behavior](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/api-sync-behavior.html)); V1's `CpuGpuBuffer` relies on the same behavior. Measured on this driver: with a `non_blocking` pageable copy issued behind a ~7.5 ms GPU sleep and the source overwritten immediately, 0/200 results were corrupted from 4 B to 16 MiB (pinned control: 200/200). Copies up to 64 KiB were staged at call time and returned immediately; larger ones waited for the stream, keeping today's cost. `NonUvaBuffer` copies are far below 64 KiB.
- **`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK`.** Its copy checker flags every `non_blocking` copy from unpinned memory as possibly synchronous, so it flags `NonUvaBuffer` both before and after this change. I left the copy outside `gpu_sync_allowed()` so the checker keeps reporting it.

Not tested: native Linux without pinned memory, other drivers, TP/PP.

Duplicate check: no open or closed PR references #58849 or changes `NonUvaBuffer.uva()`. #59981 (Confidential Computing staged buffer) edits `buffer_utils.py` but leaves `NonUvaBuffer.uva()` unchanged; #57404 and #46690 touch other code.

AI assistance was used for implementation and validation. I reviewed every changed line and the results.

title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5] Fused sparse-layer decode via AITER MonoKernel
body:
## Overview

Opt-in decode path for GLM-5 (`glm_moe_dsa`) on ROCm gfx950. With `VLLM_ROCM_GLM_MONO_DECODE=1`, each decoder layer of a pure decode step (3 dense, 75 MoE) runs as one AITER MonoKernel launch per GPU. That launch includes the sparse indexer and both tensor-parallel all-reduces.

**Depends on ROCm/aiter#6173**, which adds the kernel (`aiter.ops.flydsl.glm5_mono`). The kernel comes from ROCm/FlyDSL#1204 and ROCm/ATOM#2435. The structure follows the MiniMax-M3 fused decode in #59653.

## Claims

- 8x MI355X, GLM-5.3 MXFP4, TP8, fp8 KV, serving benchmark:
  - TPOT -40.9% at concurrency 4 and -27.4% at 8 (8K input / 1K output).
  - TPOT -18.4% at concurrency 4 and -8.1% at 8 (60K input / 600 output).
- 4x MI355X, TP4: TPOT 1.41x faster at concurrency 1 (8K input / 256 output).
- Accuracy matches the regular path: NIAH 1.000 vs 1.000, GPQA Diamond 0.899 vs 0.879, GSM8K within run-to-run noise.
- The last two commits run the dense layers in the kernel and advance its epoch once per step: TPOT -6.1% / -2.9% at concurrency 1 / 4 on TP4 and -8.8% / -5.0% on TP8, on top of the above (8K).
- Default off. When it is on, steps the kernel does not cover (prefill, mixed, more than 8 tokens) keep the regular layers and their CUDA graphs.

## Validation

**Base used for these runs.** All measurements were taken on `ac68c308` plus #50535, #51309, #51314, #59280, #59420, #59421 and #59422. AITER was `5b2f7d1d` plus ROCm/aiter#6173 (and `7bfe279d` for the baseline). This branch is the same 4 files rebased onto current `main`:
- No conflicts.
- No upstream change under `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd/`.
- Every API the path uses is unchanged.
- The rebased branch has not been re-run on GPU yet; that will be done before marking ready.

**Serving, TP8.** `vllm bench serve`-style random dataset, `random-range-ratio` 0.8. 8192/1024 swept at concurrency 4 to 256, 60000/600 at 4 to 32. Baseline is the same stack with the flag off.

| ISL/OSL | Concurrency | TPOT off | TPOT on | Change | Output tok/s/GPU off | on | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8192/1024 | 4 | 13.10 ms | 7.74 ms | -40.9% | 36.67 | 61.02 | +66.4% |
| 8192/1024 | 8 | 15.05 ms | 10.92 ms | -27.4% | 62.31 | 85.72 | +37.6% |
| 8192/1024 | 16 (path off) | 17.89 ms | 17.84 ms | -0.3% | 105.16 | 106.11 | +0.9% |
| 60000/600 | 4 | 24.59 ms | 20.07 ms | -18.4% | 16.62 | 19.62 | +18.1% |
| 60000/600 | 8 | 36.41 ms | 33.46 ms | -8.1% | 23.13 | 24.88 | +7.6% |
| 60000/600 | 16 (path off) | 62.53 ms | 62.51 ms | 0.0% | 27.22 | 27.34 | +0.4% |

- Geomean over the full sweep: 8K TPOT -11.7% and output throughput +13.2%; 60K TPOT -7.0% and output throughput +6.4%. TTFT is unchanged (+0.0% / -0.4%).
- The two builds used different AITER commits. TTFT and every point at concurrency 16 and above, where the path is off, agree within 0.7%.

**Serving, TP4.** Same build for both runs, only the flag differs. 8K input / 256 output:

| Concurrency | TPOT on | TPOT off | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8.11 ms | 11.43 ms | 1.41x |
| 2 | 8.98 ms | 12.56 ms | 1.40x |
| 4 | 12.08 ms | 15.98 ms | 1.32x |
| 8 | 25.98 ms | 29.21 ms | 1.12x |
| 16 | 30.14 ms | 29.95 ms | path off |

This TP4 table was measured with the indexer still outside the kernel. With the in-kernel indexer, a single request's step time drops further at TP4: from 8.44 to 6.92 ms at 8K, and from 8.70 to 7.80 ms at 60K.

**Accuracy.**

| Eval | Flag off | Flag on |
|---|---|---|
| TP8, NIAH `niah_single_2` at 64K (lm_eval) | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| TP8, GPQA Diamond, thinking on, temperature 1, 198 questions | 0.879 | 0.899 |
| TP4, NIAH at 8K/32K/60K, 15 prompts, 4 concurrent | 15/15 | 15/15 |
| TP4, GSM8K 5-shot strict, 250 questions, 8 concurrent | 0.900 | 0.896 |
| TP8, GSM8K, same setup | 0.916 | 0.912 and 0.884 (two runs) |

GSM8K on 250 questions moves by about 3 points between runs. GPQA at temperature 1 moves by 0.5 points per question.

- No NaN in a probe at 1, 2, 4 and 8 concurrent requests, at TP4 or TP8.

**Dense layers in the kernel, one epoch advance per step (last two commits).**

| Check (4x MI355X, TP4, 8192/256) | PR head before | With these commits |
|---|---|---|
| Layers in the kernel | 75 (18 with the fused indexer) | 78 (3 dense, 21 with the fused indexer) |
| TPOT, concurrency 1 | 6.70 ms | 6.29 ms (-6.1%) |
| TPOT, concurrency 4 | 11.68 ms | 11.34 ms (-2.9%) |
| NaN probe, 1/2/4/8 concurrent up to 61K tokens | none | none |
| NIAH 8K/32K/60K, 15 prompts | 15/15 | 15/15 |
| GSM8K 5-shot strict, 250 questions | 0.896 | 0.904 |

Same image and GPUs for both columns, one run each.

TP8 (8x MI355X), same check: TPOT 5.67 to 5.17 ms (-8.8%) at concurrency 1 and 9.98 to 9.48 ms (-5.0%) at 4; no NaN, NIAH 15/15, GSM8K 0.880 (earlier TP8 runs of this path gave 0.884 to 0.912; 250 questions move by about 3 points).
- `pytest tests/models/test_glm_mono_decode_weights.py`: 4 passed. It checks that the W_UK/W_UV split keeps the checkpoint's FP8 blocks bit-exact. It is not wired into Buildkite: the path needs gfx950 and the GLM-5 checkpoint, and CI has neither.
- Not run yet: `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. The forward path has no `.item()`, `.cpu()` or `.tolist()` calls; eligibility is decided from host-side metadata.

<details>
<summary>Server command (TP8)</summary>

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_GLM_MONO_DECODE=1 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_SPARSE_INDEXER=1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-model-len 258048 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --async-scheduling --trust-remote-code \
  --compilation-config '{"pass_config": {"fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla": true}, "use_inductor_graph_partition": true}' \
  --hf-overrides '{"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": 4, "index_share_for_mtp_iteration": false}'
```

The baseline is the same command with `VLLM_ROCM_GLM_MONO_DECODE=0`.
</details>

## Details

**When the path runs.**
- Pure decode steps of 1, 2, 4 or 8 tokens, one token per request. A step of 1 is launched as 2 with a pad row.
- Startup checks, each failing with a reason: gfx950, TP 4 or 8, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`, no speculative decoding, `indexer_rope_interleave`, and indexer RoPE tables equal to the MLA ones.
- The decision depends only on the token count and the attention metadata, so every rank makes the same one.

**Residual stream.** The embedding feeds the first launch, and the kernel carries the full residual stream through all 78 layers; the final norm runs on it.

**Weights.**
- Experts are read in place: AITER-shuffled MXFP4, with the shared expert in the last slot.
- The dense layers' MLP (six times the expert width) is packed once as six expert-shaped MXFP4 slices; the kernel routes every row to all six with weight 1. This needs the row-major MXFP4 layout of the AITER Triton GEMM, the default.
- Block-FP8 attention projections are repacked once, about 4 GB per GPU.
- W_UK/W_UV are cut from `kv_b_proj`, keeping the checkpoint's FP8 blocks.
- The indexer's `wk_weights_proj` (bf16) and `wq_b` (block FP8) are bound as-is.

**Indexer.**
- On indexer layers the kernel reads and writes the layer's paged FP8 index cache through `block_table` and `req_id_per_token`.
- It writes the top-2048 global slots to `paged_kv_indices`, which the following shared-index layers reuse.
- Layer 2's fused indexer writes the slots that the following shared-index layers read, so nothing is converted outside the kernel.

**CUDA graphs.**
- Weights bind on the first eligible step, which runs eagerly before capture. Reaching the path inside a capture first raises.
- Pad rows added when a batch is padded to a captured size have slot < 0; the kernel writes no cache entry for them.
- Each kernel runtime advances its epoch once per step. Every layer has its own launch slot within the step, so the step counter is not bumped between layers.

**Numerics.** Greedy text diverges from the regular path after a few tokens. The kernel quantizes activations to MXFP8 for the MXFP4 experts, where the regular path quantizes them to MXFP4. That is why accuracy is checked with evals rather than token match.

**Size.** About 545 lines outside tests, almost all in the new `mono_decode.py`. The only change to an existing file is an 11-line hook in `DeepseekV32Model` plus one env var. No model runner, scheduler or attention backend changes.

**Limitations.**
- Only gfx950 and GLM-5 (`glm_moe_dsa`).
- Concurrency above 8 uses the regular path.
- Needs an AITER build that contains ROCm/aiter#6173.

---

title: [Attention] FlashMLA sparse: stage fp8 mixed-batch q/out in the workspace
body:
## Overview

The FlashMLA sparse `fp8_ds_mla` mixed-batch path now writes the head-padded query and the kernel output into the workspace buffers that `FlashMLASparseImpl` already reserves for `max_num_batched_tokens`, so it no longer allocates them on every call. This removes about 4.25 GiB of per-call allocation at 32K tokens per step. That allocation isn't counted by the startup memory profile, so it can cause runtime OOMs.

Related: #59305, #57878. Complements vllm-project/FlashMLA#29, which removes the kernel-internal fp32 split-KV `o_accum` buffer (the other 8 GiB at T=32K). This PR only covers the wrapper side.

## Claims

- On the fp8 mixed-batch path, the padded q (`T x 64 x 576` bf16) and the output (`T x 64 x 512` bf16) are written into the reserved workspace, and the output buffer is passed to the kernel via `out=`. At T=32768 this saves 4.25 GiB per call, measured. The workspace was already reserved, so KV cache capacity does not change.
- Outputs and LSE are bit-identical to the allocating path.
- GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 on 8xH100 (TP8, `max_num_batched_tokens=32768`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.85`) previously hit a runtime OOM in `flash_mla_with_kvcache` during warmup. With this change it serves the same workload without errors, and GSM8K accuracy matches.

## Validation

**Per-call peak allocation.** Single H100. GLM-5.3-Flash TP8 shapes: 8 heads/rank padded to 64, topk 2048, `s_q = T`. Measured through `FlashMLASparseImpl._fp8_flash_mla_kernel`:

| T | before (allocating path) | after (workspace path) | saved | outputs equal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 0.384 GiB | 0.251 GiB | 0.133 GiB | yes |
| 8192 | 3.068 GiB | 2.006 GiB | 1.063 GiB | yes |
| 16384 | 6.137 GiB | 4.012 GiB | 2.125 GiB | yes |
| 32768 | 12.273 GiB | 8.023 GiB | 4.250 GiB | yes |

The remaining ~8 GiB at T=32768 is the kernel's `o_accum`, which is addressed by vllm-project/FlashMLA#29.

**End-to-end, previously crashing config.** GLM-5.3-Flash FP8, 8xH100, `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-num-seqs 256 --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --max-model-len 131072`.
- Before this change: during the warmup with 8K input and concurrency 256, the server failed with `torch.OutOfMemoryError` (tried to allocate 8 GiB with 5.29 GiB free), and 255 of 256 requests failed.
- After this change: warmups at 8K/c256 and 64K/c64 completed with no errors, and there are no OOM lines in the server log. Peak `nvidia-smi` memory.used was 80923 / 81559 MiB. This is tight because `o_accum` is still allocated per call until FlashMLA#29 lands.

`vllm bench serve` results, random dataset, `--ignore-eos`. The comparison is against the existing MNBT=16384 config, which has a larger KV pool (2.66M vs 1.88M tokens), so this is a sanity check rather than an A/B:

| ISL/OSL, concurrency | completed | total tok/s, MNBT 32K + this PR | total tok/s, MNBT 16K baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8192/1024, c64 | 192/192 | 16717 | 16424 |
| 8192/1024, c256 | 768/768 | 20189 | 21522 (KV cache reached 100% at 32K) |
| 65536/1024, c16 | 48/48 | 23357 | 23141 |
| 65536/1024, c64 | 192/192 | 24263 | 25101 |

**Accuracy.** GSM8K, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, using `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` against the server:

| config | accuracy | invalid |
|---|---|---|
| main, MNBT 8192 | 0.919 | 0.000 |
| this PR, MNBT 32768 | 0.914 | 0.000 |

**Tests.**
- New test: `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k test_flashmla_fp8_mixed_batch_stages_in_workspace` (H100). 2 passed.
- Existing tests: `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "test_sparse_backend_decode_correctness and FlashMLA and fp8_ds_mla"` (H100). 84 passed, 84 skipped. These include the TP>1 cases that use the mixed-batch path, run with the workspace locked.

## Details

**Root cause.** For `fp8_ds_mla` with fewer than `MIN_HEADS_FOR_BF16_PREFILL` heads per rank (`fp8_use_mixed_batch`), every step makes a single `flash_mla_with_kvcache` call with `s_q = num_tokens`. The wrapper pads q to 64 heads with `new_zeros`, and the kernel allocates `out`, `lse` and `o_accum`, all O(T * 64). The profile run skips attention, so none of this is counted when the KV cache is sized. At large `max_num_batched_tokens`, a full step therefore OOMs after startup.

**Fix.** `__init__` already reserves `(max_tokens, padded_heads, 576)` and `(max_tokens, padded_heads, 512)` bf16 workspace slots for the BF16 prefill path, which is not used in mixed-batch mode. `_fp8_flash_mla_kernel(use_workspace=True)` takes flat views of those slots sized for the FP8 decode padding (the reserved head padding is at least as wide). It zeroes only the padding heads and passes `out=` to the kernel.
- Only the mixed-batch caller turns this on. Pure-decode, HiSparse and separate prefill/decode callers keep the allocating path, because their T is small.
- The returned output aliases the workspace. It is consumed by the `v_up` projection or the DCP merge before any other workspace user runs. The separate prefill/decode path already returns workspace-backed output the same way.
- The q input comes from workspace slot 0, the q-concat buffer, so it doesn't overlap the padded-q slot.
- No new CPU/GPU synchronization: the added checks are host-side shape asserts.
- `lse` is still allocated by the kernel (T x 64 x 4 B = 8 MiB at 32K).

**Limitations.** The kernel-internal `o_accum` (2 x T x 64 x 512 x 4 B = 8 GiB at T=32K on SM90) is still allocated per call and isn't counted by the profile run. That is fixed in vllm-project/FlashMLA#29. This PR removes the wrapper-side share.

title: [Spec Decode][GLM-5.3-Flash] Support adaptive verification
body:
## Motivation

Adaptive verification chooses on the GPU how many draft tokens to verify for each request. During full CUDA graph replay, the physical token buffer and captured control flow remain fixed, while the live request boundaries can change. GLM-5.3-Flash previously made two assumptions that were incompatible with this behavior:

- GDN captured the ordinary one-token decode path, even though replay could group those token rows into fewer requests with multiple verification tokens.
- The k-pool scatter path assumed every physical token row belonged to a live request, but a replayed graph can contain additional padding rows.

This PR updates both paths to handle GPU-selected request lengths and graph padding.

## Changes

- Allow the GDN backend to replay CUDA graphs whose per-request query lengths are chosen on the GPU.
- Capture GDN’s speculative path and the k-pool indexer at the maximum configured verification width.
- Update the k-pool scatter path to safely discard CUDA graph padding without synchronizing lengths back to the CPU.
- Add tests for variable verification lengths, graph padding, and sparse-indexer alignment.

## Testing

Added and ran focused tests covering:

- Mixed per-request GDN verification lengths
- CUDA graph padding in the k-pool scatter path
- Sparse-indexer sequence-length alignment
- Capture-time and replay-time request partition differences

## Throughput results

I benchmarked GLM-5.3-Flash with MTP on four B300 GPUs (TEP4). The sweep covered:

- Speculative depths `kmax = 1...5`
- 18 batch sizes from `B = 1` through `B = 256`
- Prefix lengths `S = 512, 8192, 32768`

The table reports decode throughput for adaptive verification relative to fixed verification at the same maximum depth. Each value is the unweighted mean over the `(B, S)` at that speculative depth.

| Maximum depth | Adaptive / fixed at same depth |
|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.965× |
| 2 | 0.958× |
| 3 | 0.965× |
| 4 | 1.065× |
| 5 | 1.127× |
