title: [ROCm][Perf][MLA][DCP] gfx942: run causal DCP verify on AITER single-token asm decode
body:
## Purpose

On gfx942, causal DCP verify (qlen > 1) currently runs on Triton segmented MLA
where it fits in LDS, and on the generic Triton split-KV decode otherwise
(#58555). This PR runs gfx942 verify on AITER's non-persistent single-token asm
decode whenever gfx942 ships a kernel for the DCP-gathered head count, which
covers Kimi-K3 (96) and DeepSeek-V3 (128). Each verify token becomes one qlen-1
row with its own causal KV window, the row view that #58555 already builds.

* New route `ASM_ROWS`, checked before TRITON and SEGMENTED on gfx942. It has
  its own config gate, `_asm_rows_dcp_verify_supported` (gfx942, DCP > 1,
  interleave 1). Head counts with no asm kernel keep the #58555 routing:
  segmented MLA where it fits in LDS, the generic Triton split-KV decode
  otherwise. No new env var.
* Query heads are padded to a count the gfx942 kernel can launch: bf16
  16/32/128, fp8 16/128. Counts with no kernel (above 128) never reach AITER,
  which would otherwise abort; they take the fallback above.
* KV splits per row: `min(cdiv(CUs, 2*rows), max_kv_len // 128, 64)`, floor 2.
  AITER's own choice stops at 16 splits, which is up to 1.89x slower at low
  batch. One split skips AITER's reducer, and the fp8 kernel then writes no LSE.
* The unpad helpers now take the same `target_heads` as `get_mla_padded_q`.
  Before, a repeat-interleaved pad (for example 64→128) was unpadded as a
  prefix slice. This also fixes CPRR's 8→16 case.

The segmented verify code itself is unchanged.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_verify_gfx942.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr_numerics.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_decode_routing.py
```

The DCP verify test runs the real builder and `forward_mqa` for 8 simulated
ranks and compares against a dense causal reference. It covers asm rows on the
Kimi-K3 768-token blocks, a shape segmented MLA fits, 64 heads padded to 128,
and DeepSeek-V3 MTP with fp8 KV and an fp8 query, each next to its Triton or
segmented baseline. The baselines disable asm rows by stubbing its head lookup,
the path taken when gfx942 has no kernel for the head count.
`test_asm_rows_heads_fall_back_without_a_kernel` checks which counts fall back.

## Test Result

MI325X (torch 2.12 / ROCm 7.15, amd-aiter 0.1.24.post1): 581 passed, 4 skipped
(gfx950-only).

**Kernel sweep** (810 verify shapes, 8-rank DCP: 16–128 heads, bf16/fp8, block
16/64/768, qlen 2–6, 1–32 requests, 1K–16K local tokens):

| asm rows vs         | shapes | geomean | min   | max   |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------- | ----- | ----- |
| current route (all) | 810    | 4.12x   | 1.01x | 19.0x |
| segmented MLA       | 513    | 4.35x   | —     | —     |
| Triton split-KV     | 297    | 3.74x   | 1.24x | —     |

The split rule is within 3.3% of the best split count on average (worst 1.26x).
Building the asm-rows metadata costs ~60 µs per step: 792/810 shapes recover it
within 4 MLA layers, and all of them within 30.

**Accuracy** (180 configs, 8-rank LSE combine): bf16 error is the same on all
routes. fp8 at 4K local tokens: max error 0.0090 (asm) vs 0.0116 (segmented)
and 0.0168 (Triton); mean error ~0.0006 vs ~0.0003. Empty local shards give
LSE −inf and combine correctly.

**E2E**: Kimi-K3 + DSpark (5 draft tokens), TP8/EP8/DCP8, MI325X. Same server,
restarted per arm. The Triton arm is the #58555 routing on `main`; the ASM arm
is this PR. These runs used an earlier revision with a temporary switch between
the two; the switch has since been removed with no change to either path.

Median TPOT is the primary metric. TPOT speedup is Triton / ASM. Throughput speedup is ASM / Triton. Values above 1 mean ASM is faster.

| Workload | Prompts | Conc | Triton median TPOT (ms) | ASM median TPOT (ms) | TPOT speedup | Triton output tok/s | ASM output tok/s | Throughput speedup | Triton median TTFT (ms) | ASM median TTFT (ms) | Triton p99 TPOT (ms) | ASM p99 TPOT (ms) | Acceptance | OK / fail |
| -------- | ------- | ---- | ----------------------- | -------------------- | ------------ | ------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ | ----------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------- | ---------- | --------- |
| 8k × 1   | 8       | 1    | 10.37                   | 10.02                | 1.04×        | 70.65               | 72.29            | 1.02×              | 1904                    | 1914                 | 10.60                | 10.22             | 3.611      | 8 / 0     |
| 8k × 8   | 32      | 8    | 37.70                   | 36.84                | 1.02×        | 168.92              | 171.31           | 1.01×              | 4698                    | 4737                 | 43.23                | 42.59             | 3.594      | 32 / 0    |
| 32k × 1  | 8       | 1    | 11.01                   | 10.25                | 1.07×        | 40.35               | 41.30            | 1.02×              | 7217                    | 7261                 | 11.11                | 10.31             | 3.588      | 8 / 0     |
| 32k × 8  | 32      | 8    | 109.33                  | 105.65               | 1.03×        | 62.10               | 63.85            | 1.03×              | 11912                   | 11827                | 118.45               | 115.13            | 3.589      | 32 / 0    |
| 128k × 1 | 8       | 1    | 13.12                   | 10.94                | 1.20×        | 24.09               | 25.39            | 1.05×              | 30558                   | 30569                | 13.25                | 11.22             | 3.602      | 8 / 0     |

ASM median TPOT is lower on every workload. The largest gap is 128k × 1 (13.12 ms Triton, 10.94 ms ASM, 1.20×). The other workloads are 1.02×–1.07×. Output throughput speedup is 1.01×–1.05×.

Acceptance length is identical on both arms for every workload (synthetically fixed at 3.6 with five DSpark draft tokens). Input and output token totals match, and every request completed.

**E2E accuracy**:

```
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 30 \
  --model_args "model=kimi-k3,tokenizer=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,trust_remote_code=True,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=8,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=135168"
```

title: [Test][Spec Decode] Share reference comparison across EAGLE, MTP and speculators tests
body:
## Purpose

Part of #59566 (item 3). `_run_eagle_correctness()`, `check_mtp_correctness()` and `test_speculators_model_integration()` repeated the same flow: start a speculative and a target engine, run the GSM8K check, and compare outputs. This PR moves that flow into `check_spec_decode_matches_reference()` in `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/utils.py`. Each test keeps its own setup, engine args and match threshold (60% / 80% / 66%).

Not a duplicate. #59602 also addresses #59566, but focuses on consolidating the GSM8K and acceptance-metric checks for DSpark, DFlash, and speculator correctness. This PR instead shares the reference-comparison flow across EAGLE, MTP, and the speculators integration test.

## Behavior changes

- The speculative engine runs first, then the target. For EAGLE/MTP this flips the previous order.
- MTP: the target run now does GSM8K before `chat()` (previously `chat()` first).
- Speculators: passes `target_model=None`; the helper reads the target vLLM resolves from the checkpoint and asserts it equals the new `expected_target_model` parameter. Config checks now run before GSM8K instead of after.
- All methods now assert async scheduling (previously not for speculators) and that a speculative config with `num_speculative_tokens > 0` exists (previously only for speculators).

## Test plan

- `pytest --collect-only -q tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode`: 68 tests collected; pre-commit passes.
- @tomasruizt ran them on B300: 8 passed, 10 skipped (eg. ROCm-only cases).
- On an A100, before/after: EAGLE (`test_eagle_correctness_light`), MTP (DeepSeek, Gemma4, MiMo, Qwen3.5) and speculators (Llama, Qwen3) tests all pass; match counts and GSM8K within normal run-to-run variance.

## AI assistance

Claude Code was used to help write the changes. I reviewed every change.

title: [ROCm][Perf][Kimi-K3] Run 12-head AITER MLA decode natively
body:
## Purpose

Run Kimi-K3's 12 TP-local MLA heads natively through AITER's gfx950 FP8
decode path instead of padding the query to 16 heads. Padding adds a per-layer
query copy and one-third more attention work.

This depends on the native H12 planner, decode dispatch, and reducer merged in
[ROCm/aiter#5695](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5695). vLLM probes the
complete path, calls the metadata sizing helper, and enables H12 only for
gfx950 FP8 KV configurations with `12 * query_length <= 128`. Unsupported or
partial AITER builds retain H16 padding.

No open vLLM PR implements this native-H12 capability check.

Two-node crossover, Kimi-K3 FP4 TP8, DSpark spec-7, fixed-ISL proxy:

| Node | Native H12 | Padded H16 | Gain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A | 178.25 | 176.42 | +1.0% |
| B | 178.94 | 176.77 | +1.2% |

Every ISL improved on both nodes; p90 per-token latency fell by 0.05–0.09 ms.

## Test Plan

Extend the existing ROCm AITER MLA head-padding suite with:

- native H12 eligibility for no speculation and spec lengths 1–10;
- fallback for BF16 KV, gfx942, unsupported AITER, and query length 11;
- deferred decision before vLLM configuration exists and stable reuse after
  backend setup;
- the existing real-kernel H12 numerical comparison and all padding cases.

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_head_padding.py
```

## Test Result

MI355X (gfx950), current ROCm vLLM nightly:

```text
44 passed, 14 warnings in 294.51s
```

All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff and mypy.

A 40-question GSM8K smoke completed with exact-match 1.0 for both native-H12
and padded-H16 configurations.

title: [ROCm][Perf][Kimi-K3] Overlap MoE routing and MLA gate projections
body:
## Purpose

Overlap two independent Kimi-K3 ROCm decode pairs on dedicated HIP streams:

1. MoE router GEMM/grouped top-k with the latent routed down-projection.
2. MLA attention frontend with the output-gate projection.

Both paths are opt-in and decode-gated to at most 128 tokens:

- `VLLM_KIMI_K3_AMD_MOE_ROUTER_DOWN_PROJ_STREAM=1`
- `VLLM_KIMI_K3_AMD_MLA_GATE_STREAM=1`

Prefill is unchanged. DCP/PCP, naive EP dispatch, routing capture, EPLB, and
monolithic routing configurations retain the sequential path.

The MoE side stream passes its precomputed expert selection through the
existing `router_logits` tensor slot as packed FP32 weights and bit-cast INT32
ids. A thin router wrapper accepts packed selections while preserving raw-logit
fallback. The runner still receives the original hidden states as
`shared_experts_input`, so generic shared-expert overlap remains unchanged.

No open vLLM PR implements these Kimi-K3 AMD stream overlaps.

Latest same-node/image/day full 60-minute scored comparison:

```text
overlap off: p90 interactivity 163.94 tok/s
overlap v4:  p90 interactivity 172.89 tok/s
gain: +8.95 tok/s
```

Earlier token-count sweeps showed improvements through 128 tokens and no gain
at 256, which defines the decode threshold.

## Test Plan

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_multistream_overlap.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_latent_moe_runner.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_mla_direct_return.py \
  tests/test_envs.py
```

Coverage includes:

- MoE and MLA parity between stream and sequential paths;
- the 128/129-token decode boundary;
- packed route round trips for INT32 and INT64 ids and raw-logit fallback;
- direct AITER grouped-top-k parity;
- original versus projected runner inputs;
- HIP graph capture/replay and input mutation;
- existing latent-MoE runner, direct-return MLA, and environment tests.

## Test Result

MI355X (gfx950), current ROCm vLLM nightly:

```text
89 passed, 15 warnings in 185.89s
```

All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff and mypy.

GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot, real DSpark acceptance:

```text
overlap off: 0.9158 +/- 0.008
overlap on:  0.9143 +/- 0.008
```

The difference is statistically indistinguishable (66 questions correct only
with overlap on, 68 only with overlap off; McNemar z = 0.17).

title: [Perf][V2] Add custom CPU DP metadata all-reduce
body:
# [Perf][V2] Add custom CPU DP metadata all-reduce

V2's small CPU metadata all-reduce can delay model dispatch as DP size grows. Add a recursive-doubling SUM using existing Gloo point-to-point operations: `log2(DP)` exchanges, with no GPU synchronization or new process groups.

Enable with `VLLM_DP_METADATA_TRANSPORT=gloo-tree` on every worker. The option is registered and validated in `vllm.envs`; Gloo all-reduce remains the default. The opt-in path requires power-of-two groups and serialized calls, and reserves P2P tags starting at 27100. Scratch storage follows the input shape without assuming a fixed metadata field count.

## Benchmark

**Model-serving A/B:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 16 GB300 GPUs (four nodes), TP1/DP16/EP16, client concurrency 512. Logical input/output lengths 8192/1024, DecodeBenchConnector to skip prefill, five DSpark draft tokens with synthetic acceptance 4.409. Both runs completed 5,120 measured requests with zero errors after 2,048 warmup requests. Recipes differed only in transport and job name; both used vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev312+g36768d1bf` and PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`.

| Metric | Original Gloo | Recursive doubling | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Output tokens/s/GPU | 2,974.6 | 3,682.9 | +23.8% |
| Tokens/s/user (1000 / mean TPOT) | 114.40 | 139.28 | +21.7% |
| Mean TPOT | 8.741 ms | 7.180 ms | −17.9% |
| Median TTFT | 1,061.17 ms | 564.53 ms | −46.8% |
| p99 request latency | 16,168.5 ms | 17,188.3 ms | +6.3% (worse) |
| Mean CPU metadata collective wall time | 9.164 ms | 3.507 ms | −61.7% |

One independently scheduled A/B pair, not a confidence interval. CPU timings include rank arrival skew; 6,202/6,136 samples match the local decode shape within the client measurement window, rather than complete synchronized cohorts. This measures decode-focused serving performance, not real-prefill throughput or answer accuracy. No Nsight capture was taken for this pair.

**CPU microbenchmarks:** DP16, `[6, 16]` int32 / 384 bytes, one Torch thread, no CPU binding or explicit Gloo interface override. Timing includes input preparation through the complete CPU result.

| Condition | Original Gloo median | Recursive-doubling median |
|---|---:|---:|
| Idle GPU | 4.741–5.385 ms (4 blocks) | 0.618–0.681 ms (3 blocks) |
| GPU-busy control | 6.440–6.793 ms (2 blocks) | 1.539 ms (1 block) |

Each block uses 20 warmups, then 200 idle or 60 busy iterations per rank. Ranges are block medians, not confidence intervals. The busy control launches a ~9.69 ms CUDA sleep; the tree operation returned while the GPU was still busy in every measured sample. Blocks share one allocation and rank samples are correlated. All **48,320 timed rank-samples** and **512 additional dense tree checks** passed.

## Validation

- The model-serving runs loaded the minimal source patch, with the helper verified byte-for-byte against this implementation. All **1,024 metadata parity checks per run** passed before measured requests.
- Distributed CPU harness: **11,520 exact checks** across DP2/4/8/16, both transports, sparse/dense inputs, six/seven fields, noncontiguous groups, uneven arrivals, and in-place reuse.
- Pre-commit checks passed for all three changed Python files. Environment registry checks covered defaults, supported values, invalid-value rejection, and cached access.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, validation, and this draft.

title: [Bugfix] Check batch-invariance support for every attention backend
body:
## Overview

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the attention selector refuses backends that do not declare `supports_batch_invariance()` ("VLLM batch_invariant mode is not supported for ..."). Models that select their own attention backend never go through the selector, so they start anyway and silently return batch-dependent output. This PR applies the same check to every attention layer when the attention groups are built.

## Claims

- `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` starts in batch-invariant mode on `main` and the determinism tests report violations (for example 32 of 32 prompts). With this PR the engine refuses to start with the existing error message.
- Models on the standard backends are unaffected: the determinism tests still pass for `Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507-FP8` (GB300), `Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B` and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` (A10). Every model on the tested list in `docs/features/batch_invariance.md` uses a standard backend.
- New unit test for the check.

## Validation

GB300 runs: 4x NVIDIA GB300 (SM 10.3), `main` at `182247257f` versus that commit plus this PR's source change. A10 runs: 2x NVIDIA A10 (SM 8.6), `main` at `d09ff77637` plus this PR's source change. One pytest process per test. The blocks are copied from the logs without editing.

**1. `main`: MiniMax-M3 runs in batch-invariant mode and is not batch invariant** (tensor-parallel 4)

```text
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 VLLM_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.9 python -m pytest -v "tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_v1_generation_is_deterministic_across_batch_sizes_with_needle[default-FLASH_ATTN]"
E               Failed: Nondeterministic outputs detected: 5 failed out of 5 trials (max_batch_size=128).
================== 1 failed, 32 warnings in 532.70s (0:08:52) ==================

VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 VLLM_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.9 python -m pytest -v "tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_bs1_vs_bsN[16-16-FLASH_ATTN]"
E           Failed: Batch invariance violated in 32/32 prompts. See output above for details.
================== 1 failed, 32 warnings in 116.67s (0:01:56) ==================
```

**2. This PR: the engine refuses to start for MiniMax-M3 in batch-invariant mode**

```text
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 VLLM_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.9 python -m pytest -v "tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_simple_generation[FLASH_ATTN]"
(Worker_TP2 pid=2792149) ERROR 10-06 05:23:45 [multiproc_executor.py:1058] RuntimeError: VLLM batch_invariant mode is not supported for MINIMAX_M3_SPARSE_INDEXER.
================== 1 failed, 32 warnings in 73.05s (0:01:13) ===================
```

**3. This PR: models on the standard backends still pass**

```text
# GB300, tensor-parallel 2: VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507-FP8 VLLM_TP_SIZE=2 VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=2 VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.9
tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_simple_generation[FLASH_ATTN] PASSED
================== 1 passed, 16 warnings in 131.31s (0:02:11) ==================
tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_v1_generation_is_deterministic_across_batch_sizes_with_needle[default-FLASH_ATTN] PASSED
================== 1 passed, 16 warnings in 197.04s (0:03:17) ==================
# A10: VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B
tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_v1_generation_is_deterministic_across_batch_sizes_with_needle[default-FLASH_ATTN] PASSED
================== 1 passed, 17 warnings in 113.06s (0:01:53) ==================
tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_simple_generation[TRITON_ATTN] PASSED
======================= 1 passed, 17 warnings in 53.84s ========================
tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_simple_generation[FLEX_ATTENTION] PASSED
======================= 1 passed, 17 warnings in 27.90s ========================
# A10, tensor-parallel 2: VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat
tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_simple_generation[TRITON_MLA] PASSED
======================= 1 passed, 17 warnings in 29.12s ========================
```

**4. New unit test** (without and with the source change)

```text
python -m pytest -v tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py::test_init_attn_backend_checks_custom_backend_batch_invariance
# main + only the new test
E       Failed: DID NOT RAISE RuntimeError
FAILED tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py::test_init_attn_backend_checks_custom_backend_batch_invariance[False]
=================== 1 failed, 1 passed, 14 warnings in 1.08s ===================
# this PR
======================== 2 passed, 14 warnings in 1.08s ========================
```

`lm_eval` and `vllm bench serve` comparisons are not included because the change is a start-up check only: no kernel or request path is touched, and for the affected model the "after" state is that the engine does not start.

## Details

**Root cause.** `supports_batch_invariance()` is enforced in `vllm/v1/attention/selector.py`. Attention layers that set their backend themselves (the model packages under `vllm/models/`, for example MiniMax-M3's sparse attention and indexer) are not created through the selector, and none of those backends declares support, so batch-invariant mode was accepted for them without any guarantee. I found this by running the determinism suite on MiniMax-M3: it fails on `main`, and still fails with #59985 applied, so it is not the router issue fixed there.

**Change.** `init_attn_backend` already visits the backend of every attention layer; it now raises the selector's error for a backend that does not declare support when `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is set. Backends that do support it only need to override `supports_batch_invariance()`.

**Trade-offs and limitations.**
- Models with self-selected backends (MiniMax-M3, DeepSeek-V4, Kimi-K3 and similar) now fail fast in batch-invariant mode instead of starting. None of them is on the tested list, and for the one I could test the mode did not hold.
- Only the Model Runner V2 path is changed; the equivalent loop in the V1 runner is left as is, given its deprecation.
- This does not make MiniMax-M3 batch invariant; it makes the lack of support explicit.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Align the a4w4 MXFP4 MoE intermediate to 256, unbreaking DeepSeek V4.1 at TP2
body:
## Purpose

On ROCm, `mxfp4_round_up_hidden_size_and_intermediate_size` relaxes
`AITER_MXFP4_BF16` SiTU/SiLU shards from the generic 256-alignment down to 128,
so Kimi-K3's A16W4 SiTU kernel keeps its native intermediate width instead of
inflating expert weights and starving the KV cache.

The `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4=1` opt-in rides the same backend and the
same SiLU activation, so it inherits that relaxation — but its MXMOE kernels
`e8m0_shuffle` the scales in groups of 8 columns and therefore stride
`8 * 32 = 256` elements of K per group. A shard that is 128- but not
256-aligned needs no padding, AITER keeps its inline-sort fast path, and that
path addresses the padded stride and reads past the intermediate scale buffer.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash shards `moe_intermediate_size 2304` to **1152** at TP2,
which is exactly that case. Every TP2 server dies during CUDA graph capture:

```
Warning: Queue error - HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT
Memory access fault by GPU node-4 (Agent handle: 0x31a3dcc0) on address 0x7f84c9d33000. Reason: Unknown.
[aiter] Error in moe_sorting: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

With `AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3` the fault lands immediately after AITER selects
the inline-sort pair at `inter_dim=1152`:

```
[aiter] [fused_moe] using 2stage (kernelName1='flydsl_mxmoe_g1_a4w4_16x128x256_f16in_hpf_nt_xcd4',
  kernelName2='flydsl_moe2_layout_afp4_wfp4_bf16_t16x128x128_atomic_nt_sbm16')
  for ('gfx950', 256, 16, 5120, 1152, 384, 6, <ActivationType.Silu: 0>, 'torch.bfloat16',
       'torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2', 'torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2', 'QuantType.per_1x32', True, False)
```

TP4 survives only by accident: `576` does need padding to `640`, the nonzero
`intermediate_pad` makes AITER reject the inline-sort path, and it logs
`[fused_moe] inline-sort config is unsupported (hidden/intermediate padding)`
34440 times per boot. The same build at TP2 logs that warning zero times.

This PR excludes the a4w4 opt-in from the 128-alignment relaxation, so the
shard the kernels actually require is allocated: 1152 → 1280 at TP2 and
576 → 768 at TP4. Kimi-K3 and the W4A16 path are untouched.

### Not a duplicate

[#55104](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55104) is the mirror image of
this change and documents the same kernel defect from the other direction: it
relaxes `AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4` from 256 to 128 for MiniMax-M3, and is explicitly
**blocked on ROCm/aiter#5232** because "aiter's CK-Tile 2-stage MXFP4 stage-2
kernel mis-indexes its E8M0 weight scales when `inter_dim % 256 != 0`: the host
pads the scale group dimension up to a multiple of 8 groups (8 x 32 = 256
elements) and the kernel's indexing does not account for it."

Both PRs agree that 256 is the contract until that aiter fix lands. They touch
different branches of the same function (`AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4` vs. the a4w4 arm of
`AITER_MXFP4_BF16`) and do not conflict in intent: #55104 cannot merge without
the aiter fix, and this PR restores the safe alignment that DeepSeek V4.1
silently lost. No other open PR or issue covers the TP2 fault
(`gh pr list --search "aiter mxfp4 intermediate 256 alignment memory fault"`,
`gh issue list --search "moe_sorting illegal memory access mxfp4"` — both empty).

## Test Plan

Hardware: 8x MI355X (gfx950, 256 CU), ROCm 10.0, torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0,
`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`.

**Unit**

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py -k "round or native_tp_shard" -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_fi_moe_ep.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py -q
```

`test_aiter_mxfp4_a4w4_rounds_intermediate_to_256` is added to the existing
MXFP4 size-rounding block in `test_ocp_mx_moe.py`. It pins both arms of the
branch at TP2 and TP4: with the opt-in set the DeepSeek shard must round to
256, and with it unset the K3-style 128 relaxation must still apply. No GPU
needed.

**End to end**, the full InferenceX MI355X recipe (1M context, DSpark
`num_speculative_tokens=5`, `--moe-backend aiter`, MXFP4 indexer KV,
`--max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024`, Engram CPU offload), run as a TP2/TP4 A/B
on one build:

```bash
TP=2 DEVICES=0,1 PORT=8321 bash dsv41_rocm_bench/repro_tp2.sh
TP=4 DEVICES=4,5,6,7 PORT=8324 bash dsv41_rocm_bench/repro_tp2.sh
```

**Accuracy**, GSM8K with the InferenceX eval invocation (`lm_eval` pinned at
`b315ef3b`, `local-chat-completions`, `--apply_chat_template`, all 1319
questions, 5-shot, `max_tokens=16384`, `temperature=0`, `top_p=1`,
`num_concurrent=64`).

## Test Result

**Unit.** 7 passed in the rounding block, 21 passed in
`test_deepseek_v4_fi_moe_ep.py`. `test_rocm_aiter_moe.py` is 67 passed / 3
failed; the three failures (`test_aiter_fused_moe_fake_tensor_support`,
`..._mi350_mxfp4_w4a16_accuracy`, `..._mi350_mxfp4_w4a16_determinism`) reproduce
identically with the patch stashed, so they are pre-existing on this container.

**Startup.** Before the fix, TP2 faults at CUDA graph 78/83 with
`HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT` on every attempt. After the fix, TP2 completes
all 83 captures and serves:

| config | graph capture | memory faults | `/health` |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| TP2, before | dies at 78/83 | 4 | never ready |
| TP2, after | 83/83 | 0 | 200 |
| TP4, after | 80/80 | 0 | 200 |

**Accuracy.** GSM8K, 1319 questions:

| config | flexible-extract | strict-match |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| TP2, before | n/a — server cannot start | n/a |
| TP2, after | **0.9629** ± 0.0052 | 0.9515 ± 0.0059 |
| TP4, after | **0.9697** ± 0.0047 | 0.9568 ± 0.0056 |

Both are above the 0.91 DeepSeek-V4 threshold this suite is gated on, and TP4
is unchanged within noise relative to its expected score, so moving TP4 from
640 to 768 is accuracy-neutral while TP2 goes from unusable to correct.

**Cost.** The TP2 intermediate grows 1152 → 1280 (+11.1 %) and TP4 576 → 768
(+33.3 %) in MXFP4 expert weights. There is no tuned AITER row at those widths
yet, so TP2 falls back to heuristic kernel selection; that is strictly better
than the current state, where the tuned 1152 row is the one that faults. A
follow-up tuning pass on the 256-aligned widths is worthwhile, and once
ROCm/aiter#5232 lands the relaxation can be revisited for this path too.

## Note on AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Opus 5 via Cursor) was used to root-cause the fault and
draft this change. I reviewed every changed line, ran all of the commands above
myself on the MI355X node, and can defend the change end to end.

title: [KV Connector] Support Kimi K3 DCP prefill + DEP decode disagg
body:
## Summary

Add NIXL push support for disagg serving with DCP prefill and DEP decode for hybrid MLA+Mamba models such as Kimi K3.

## Implementation

- **Map DCP cache pages to decode.** Each prefill rank sends its attention pages to the correct positions in the decode cache, skipping prefixes already cached on decode.
- **Match cache regions by name.** Match target attention, Mamba state, and DSpark draft KV regions when prefill and decode register them in different orders.
- **Reuse existing completion handling.** Wait for all contributing prefill ranks using the existing notification accounting. Clear unused destination pages beyond the transferred data.
- **Automatically resolve `cp-kv-cache-interleave-size` to the attention physical block size.** This keeps each page entirely on one prefill DCP rank, so it can be transferred directly to its position in the decode cache without splitting or repacking. The current implementation enforces this layout.

## Validation

Validated Kimi K3 with DCP8 prefill and DEP16 decode.

### GSM8K

| Setting / metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Questions | 1,319 |
| Shots | 5 |
| Maximum output tokens | 256 |
| Temperature | 0.0 |
| Accuracy | **94.2%** |
| Invalid responses | 0.1% |
| Total latency | 48.380 s |
| Questions per second | 27.263 |
| Total output tokens | 140,188 |

### AgentX performance

NVFP4 2P1D DCP8 + DEP16 with DSpark k4 and MegaMoE at concurrency 320:

| Metric | Result |
|---|---:|
| Throughput | **18,367 tokens/s/GPU** |
| Mean / p90 ITL | 23.46 / 27.77 ms |

This validates functional serving and retains the approximately 18K tokens/s/GPU performance observed with the earlier implementation.

Moves `tests/v1/ec_connector` from `SEPARATE_GROUPS` to `SILENT_GROUPS` in `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`, so it is checked at the stricter `follow_imports = "silent"` setting, and fixes the mypy errors that surfaces (49 errors in 9 files on current main). Claimed in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49569#issuecomment-6022784979.

## Claims

- `tests/v1/ec_connector`: 49 mypy errors → 0 under `follow_imports=silent`, on both Python 3.10 and 3.13.
- The directory now routes into the default (strict) pre-commit mypy group, so the fixes are enforced instead of being free to regress.
- No runtime behavior changes: fixes are runtime-true narrowing (`assert x is not None` / `isinstance`), real types for fakes, and two scoped `# type: ignore[method-assign]` for instance-level mock patching (the established pattern in ~28 other vllm tests).

## Validation

```bash
mypy --python-version 3.10 --follow-imports silent --warn-unused-ignores tests/v1/ec_connector
mypy --python-version 3.13 --follow-imports silent --warn-unused-ignores tests/v1/ec_connector
python tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.10 $(git ls-files 'tests/v1/ec_connector/*.py')
python tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.10 $(git ls-files '*.py' | grep -v third_party)

## Details

Fix categories:

- **Optional narrowing** (most of the 49): `CacheEntry | None`, `ECConnectorOutput | None`, `ModelRunnerOutput | None` attribute accesses guarded with `assert ... is not None`.
- **LSP-violating test fakes** (`test_ec_output_aggregator.py`): `FakeWorkerMeta.aggregate` / `FakeConnectorStats.aggregate` narrowed the parameter type relative to the supertype; widened the signatures to match the base class and `isinstance`-narrow inside, and `isinstance`-narrow at the use sites that read `.saves`.

- **Misc**: generator fixture return annotation (`-> Generator[...]`), a `MagicMock` narrowing for `.return_value` stubbing, and three `# type: ignore[method-assign]` on instance-level method patching in mock workers.

title: [Bugfix] DeepSeek-V4.1 VL: stream weights instead of sorting the iterator
body:
## Overview

`DeepseekV41ForCausalLM.load_weights` (the vision-language wrapper in `deepseek_v41/{nvidia,amd}/vl_model.py`) sorts the whole weight iterator before loading it, so it holds every checkpoint tensor at once. With `--load-format runai_streamer`, each rank then keeps the entire checkpoint in host memory, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (475 GiB) runs out of memory while loading. This PR streams the `language_model.` weights through and defers only the rest.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash now loads with `runai_streamer` from S3 at TP4 on H200. Before, host memory grew with every tensor until the load was OOM-killed at 74,056 of 96,085 tensors (1.47 TiB RSS, the job's 1500 GiB limit). After, memory plateaus at 0.68 TiB, peaks at 1.02 TiB, and loading finishes in 275 s.
- It also loads on GB300 at TP2 (aarch64), in 369 s with a 0.65 TiB peak.
- The same weights reach the same loaders. Only the order in which the language model receives them changes.

## Validation

**Setup.** One 8×H200 node, TP4 on four GPUs, 1500 GiB job memory limit. The checkpoint was read from an S3-compatible object store with:

```bash
RUNAI_STREAMER_MEMORY_LIMIT=0 RUNAI_STREAMER_CONCURRENCY=32 \
vllm serve s3://<bucket>/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --load-format runai_streamer --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data
```

`RUNAI_STREAMER_MEMORY_LIMIT=0` sizes runai's buffer to the largest tensor, a ~92 GiB Engram table; the 40 GB default rejects this checkpoint. **Before** is the `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0` image. **After** is the same image with only `nvidia/vl_model.py` replaced by this PR's version. `load_weights` is identical in v0.31.0 and `main`.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Tensors loaded | 74,056 / 96,085, then OOM-killed | 96,085 / 96,085 |
| Peak host RSS (`sstat` MaxRSS) | 1.47 TiB, at the 1500 GiB limit | 1.02 TiB |
| Model loading time | n/a | 275 s |

<details>
<summary>Host RSS against tensors loaded (15 s samples)</summary>

| Tensors loaded (before / after) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 764 / 298 | 0.43 TiB | 0.34 TiB |
| 5,554 / 3,796 | 0.75 TiB | 0.65 TiB |
| 32,864 / 32,222 | 1.09 TiB | 0.68 TiB |
| 59,495 / 57,436 | 1.40 TiB | 0.68 TiB |
| 64,624 / 62,918 | 1.47 TiB; OOM-killed by 74,056 | 0.68 TiB |
| 96,008 | | 0.69 TiB |
| 96,085, after both Engram tables | | 1.02 TiB peak, then 0.30 TiB serving |

</details>

After loading, the server passed our deployment checks. These cover a tool-call round trip, reasoning/content separation in streamed and non-streamed responses, prefix-cache reuse, a needle retrieved at 1,013,137 tokens, an over-length rejection, and an image prompt. A second launch, with the default `RUNAI_STREAMER_CONCURRENCY` and so a different tensor arrival order, also loaded all 96,085 tensors (in 711 s).

**GB300.** The arm64 build of the same patched image ran at TP2 on one GB300 node with an 850 GiB limit, using the Blackwell settings `--attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' --kv-cache-dtype fp8`. It loaded all 96,085 tensors in 369 s with a 0.65 TiB peak host RSS, and passed the same checks. The stock image was not run on GB300.

This PR adds no tests. The failure needs a streaming loader and the full checkpoint, and CI has neither. The AMD wrapper gets the same change but was not run, because no MI-series hardware was available.

## Details

**Root cause.** The wrapper maps HF names into its namespace and then sorts, so that the `language_model.` group reaches the child loader as one contiguous block. `AutoWeightsLoader` delegates once per contiguous prefix group, and the child's `load_weights` finalizes the fused MoE weights at its end, which must not run on a partially loaded model. To sort, `sorted()` must first consume the entire iterator. `runai_streamer` yields tensors that the consumer owns, so the sort holds the entire checkpoint on every rank. Without distributed streaming those are CPU tensors; with it, they are GPU tensors.

**Fix.** `language_model.` weights pass through as they arrive. The other weights (vision tower, aligner and image embeddings; 266 tensors in this checkpoint) are collected and follow, sorted as before. The language-model group is still contiguous, so the child's `load_weights` still runs once.

**Order.** The language model now receives weights in loader order instead of sorted order. Its loading does not depend on that order: each tensor goes to its own parameter through a weight loader, no state is kept between tensors, and finalization runs once, after the stream ends. Inside the child, the `model.` weights can now be split into two runs around `lm_head`, so `DeepseekV4Model.load_weights` may be called twice. That is safe, because it keeps no state between calls (unlike the FP8 indexer pairing that #59223 fixes for `deepseek_v32`).

**Not addressed.** Without distributed streaming, every rank still streams the whole checkpoint, and runai's buffer must hold the largest tensor.

title: [ROCm][Perf] gfx950: use aiter.mqa_logits for the sparse indexer prefill
body:
## Purpose

On gfx950, the sparse indexer prefill calls the Triton/Gluon `fp8_mqa_logits` directly, and moving it to another kernel takes a vLLM change each time (#59280 did this for FlyDSL). This calls `aiter.mqa_logits` (ROCm/aiter#6185) instead: AITER picks the backend and FlyDSL kernel variant per shape from its tuned table.

- gfx950 with AITER enabled: `aiter.mqa_logits`, when the installed AITER has it.
- Older AITER without `aiter.mqa_logits`: the existing Triton/Gluon path, unchanged.
- gfx942 keeps the FlyDSL path from #49544; other archs and AITER disabled are unchanged.

Needs ROCm/aiter#6185. Until the AITER that vLLM pins includes it, the import fails and gfx950 keeps the Triton/Gluon path, so this is safe to merge first.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mqa_logits_dispatch.py`: gfx942 uses FlyDSL; gfx950 uses `aiter.mqa_logits`, or Triton/Gluon when AITER lacks it; other archs use Triton/Gluon; AITER disabled uses the torch fallback.
- A real call of `rocm_fp8_mqa_logits` on gfx950 (seq_len 2048, seq_len_kv 16384, H=32, D=128), compared with `fp8_mqa_logits_torch`.

## Test Result

MI355X (gfx950), a vLLM 0.30.1rc1 dev build with this change applied to `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`, AITER from ROCm/aiter#6185, Triton 3.8.0, FlyDSL 0.3.4.1.

- Dispatch test: 5/5 pass.
- Real call: dispatched to `aiter.mqa_logits`, which used the tuned GLM-5 row (FlyDSL `mfma32x32x64_bkv128_r2_w4_lds3`). Same `-inf` mask as the torch fallback, `calc_diff` 1.4e-6.
- Kernel time on the 24 tuned GLM-5 prefill shapes (from ROCm/aiter#6185): -36.6% geomean against Triton/Gluon (-16.6% to -74.5%), -5.8% against the FlyDSL variant #59280 would pick (-15.4% to +3.3%).
- Not measured end to end yet.

title: [Perf][DSpark] Compute windowed draft context for trailing rows only
body:
## Purpose

A DFlash/DSpark drafter whose KV groups are all sliding-window only ever reads each request's last `window` context positions, but `DFlashSpeculator.propose` runs `combine_hidden_states` (DSpark's `main_proj`) and the per-layer context K/V precompute over every target row. On a 16K-token DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill step that is ~2.6 ms of GPU work, almost all of it for rows the drafter never reads. This PR projects and stores only each request's trailing rows.

- **Gate.** Trimming is on when every draft KV group is sliding-window with a window larger than `num_speculative_steps`, the dropped rows cannot be served later (prefix caching off, or no draft group is prefix-cacheable, as with DSv4.1's SWA bounded replay), no KV connector is configured, and the drafter has no context anchor (LiLiCorr reads `hidden_states` by target row). Other drafters are unchanged.
- **Threshold.** Only steps that drop at least 2048 context rows trim, since the row gathers cost a few fixed launches; decode steps only pay one integer compare.
- **Rows.** Each request keeps its last `window + num_query_per_req` rows (the query block can shift the window when clamped at `max_model_len`), counted back from the device `query_start_loc`, which adaptive verification may shorten for decodes. Aux hidden states are gathered before `combine_hidden_states`, and context positions and slots are compacted after `prepare_dflash_inputs`.

Not a duplicate: no open PR reduces the rows of the context precompute. #57627 (stacked context KV projection) and #55654 (V4 KV-only insert) make each row cheaper and are complementary; #43594 batches the KV writes; #59511 moves the combine into the draft CUDA graph and would gather the staged rows the same way.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_profile.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py -q

title: [ROCm][Attention] Add an mxfp4_mla KV cache for rope-free sparse MLA (read/write path)
body:
## Overview

Adds an `mxfp4_mla` KV cache dtype for the ROCm AITER sparse MLA backend on rope-free (NoPE) latents such as GLM-5.3-Flash. Each 512-wide latent is stored as 256 bytes of E2M1 codes plus 16 inline E8M0 scales (one per 32 values): 272 bytes per token against 1024 for bf16, or 3.76× more tokens per GiB of KV cache.

This is the first of the smaller PRs split out of #59739, as requested there. It contains only the cache format, the write path and a Triton read path. Everything is Triton or Python: no HIP or C++ sources, and no new environment variables.

## Claims

- **KV capacity:** 3.76× more tokens per GiB than bf16 (272 vs 1024 bytes per token).
- **Correctness:** attention over the packed cache is bit-identical to attention over the same dequantized values stored as bf16.
- **No change for other KV dtypes.** The only shared-kernel change is a branch on the cache pointer's element type, which Triton resolves at compile time, so the bf16 and FP8 specializations compile to the same code as before.
- **No speed claim.** The Triton read path unpacks to bf16 before both dots, so it doesn't make attention faster: at 16k tokens it takes about 1.13× as long as bf16 per layer. The gain is capacity. Faster arithmetic over this cache comes in a follow-up.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (MI355X / gfx950):

```
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mxfp4_mla*.py tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_glm5next_sparse.py
# 99 passed
```

The new tests cover:
- the format math, checked bit-for-bit against AITER's `per_1x32_f4_quant`;
- the store kernel, including padding slots and launches past 2^31 source elements;
- the Triton read path, checked against a dequantize-then-attend reference, with both the hardware and software unpack;
- the startup plumbing (KV spec bytes, hybrid block sizing, config validation);
- the routing that sends both prefill and decode through the ragged kernel.

**Accuracy** (GLM-5.3-Flash, TP=4 on MI355X, seed 42; bf16 and MXFP4 served from the same image):

| Benchmark | bf16 | `mxfp4_mla`, this PR |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy) | 97.19% (1282) | 96.89% (1278) |
| GPQA-Diamond (198 questions, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95), with #59412 | 90.91% (180) | 89.90% (178) |

Neither gap is significant. On GSM8K the two arms disagree on 12 of 1319 questions (4 right only with MXFP4, 8 right only with bf16; exact McNemar p = 0.39), and a repeat of the same bf16 configuration has differed by 0.76 points. On GPQA-Diamond they disagree on 16 of 198 (7 vs 9; p = 0.80), and both stay in the 88.9–91.9% range of earlier bf16 and MXFP4 runs without the indexer regression. For reference, the native FP8 × FP4 kernel over this same cache format scored 97.42% vs 96.97% for bf16 on GSM8K in #59739.

**Long-context accuracy needs the indexer fix in #59412.** On ROCm, main currently has a sparse-indexer page-addressing bug on GLM-5.3-Flash (#58858) that corrupts top-k selection beyond 2048 tokens, independently of the KV cache dtype. Without a fix, GPQA-Diamond fell to 80.8–85.4% for bf16 and MXFP4 alike across 8 runs on main `ed3f6d1`, with 13–18 of 198 generations running to the token limit. With #59412 applied, the runs above score 90.91% (bf16) and 89.90% (MXFP4), with 5 and 3 generations at the limit. GSM8K generations mostly stay below 2048 tokens and aren't affected. The GPQA row above is therefore measured with #59412 applied to both arms; this PR does not include or depend on it.

## Details

**Format and write path.** The `mxfp4_mla` row is 256 bytes of packed E2M1 (low nibble holds the lower index) followed by 16 E8M0 scales. Scales use the round-up exponent, so no value clamps. `MLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec` reports the 272-byte row through `state_content_bytes`, and `Platform._align_hybrid_block_size` uses the same size so the mamba state still fits one attention page on hybrid models. `concat_and_cache_mla` can't express per-group scales (its `scale` is a single float), so a Triton store kernel behind `do_kv_cache_update` quantizes and writes the row.

**Read path.** The ragged Triton sparse-attention kernel, which already serves both prefill and decode for rope-free models, gains a branch for a uint8 (packed MXFP4) cache, with no new kernel parameters. It unpacks each gathered tile to bf16 once and feeds both existing `tl.dot` calls:
- On gfx950 the unpack uses the hardware FP4 converter (`v_cvt_scalef32_pk_bf16_fp4`) via inline asm.
- On other GPUs it uses a software unpack. The two are tested bit-identical on gfx950, but I haven't run the software path on gfx942.

The decode-only kernels used by DeepSeek-V4 have no MXFP4 branch, so they refuse a packed cache rather than misread it.

## Follow-ups (stacked on this PR)

- A native FP8 × FP4 MFMA kernel for gfx950 that computes attention directly on the packed cache (opt-in).
- Split-K decode for the `mxfp4_mla` cache, building on #58584.

Separately, two decode-overhead trims that apply to every KV dtype (host-side `paged_kv_indptr` for pure-decode steps, and skipping the NoPE `q_concat` copy) will go up as their own PR against main.

title: [Bug]: Default -O2 leaves DeepSeek MLA RoPE and KV-cache fusion off
body:
### Your current environment

This is a config-default bug read from source on `vllm-project/vllm` main `d77cf8115601f2856aacbfdd82a436ee78a558e6` (2026-10-07). The same gating is on `b6d8e8afd985f5711eee68e343d2ce908d166488`.

`python collect_env.py` was not run. The pinned torch is 2.13.0. The machine used for the reading has torch 2.5.1, which cannot import current main (`torch._inductor.custom_graph_pass`, `torch.float8_e8m0fnu`). No GPU run was done.

### Describe the bug

At default `-O2`, DeepSeek-V2/V3 MLA never takes the existing RoPE + KV-cache fusion.

`MLARoPEKVCacheCatFusionPass` matches `k_pe.unsqueeze`, DeepSeek YaRN (or plain RoPE) on that slice, and `vllm::unified_mla_kv_cache_update`, then replaces them with `fused_rope_unified_mla_kv_cache_update` (`ops.concat_and_cache_mla_rope_fused`). The pass is added only when `pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla` is true (`vllm/compilation/passes/pass_manager.py`).

`-O2` sets that flag from `enable_rope_kvcache_mla_fusion`. The function is true only when `use_inductor_graph_partition` is on, or when `splitting_ops_contain_kv_cache_update()` is false. The default is partition off, `splitting_ops is None`, and `fuse_attn_quant` is false (`IS_QUANTIZED` is hard-coded false), so the predicate returns true early: both cache-update ops will be appended. The flag therefore stays false.

`set_splitting_ops_for_v1` then appends `vllm::unified_mla_kv_cache_update` because of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33267. Dynamo splits the graph on that op, so the fusion pattern is not in one compiled piece.

Forcing `-cc.pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla=True` without `use_inductor_graph_partition=True` does not warn. `fuse_rope_kvcache` and `fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache` are disabled in that situation. The MLA flag stays true, the pass is registered, and it matches nothing. The benchmark command on https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45573 is that shape: the flag is set, `use_inductor_graph_partition` is not.

On the pinned torch (2.13), `_USE_LAYERNAME` is true unless `VLLM_USE_LAYERNAME=0`. `LayerName` is a hoisted value-type opaque object, so torch.compile lifts the layer name as a graph input instead of a per-layer string constant. The #33267 reason for splitting this op out does not apply on a normal install. The non-MLA op `vllm::unified_kv_cache_update` should stay split, because the AITER RoPE+KV fusions are a different path.

What this is not:

- DeepSeek-V4 does not reach this pass. `DeepseekV4Attention` is not an `MLAAttention`, and the CUDA Q/K path is `fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_*_insert`, not `rotary_emb` plus `unified_mla_kv_cache_update`.
- This does not replace the manual-fusion rewrite in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43504 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45573.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50758 is the fallback for when `LayerName` is off. It is not this bug.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40392 added the pass. Its serve command sets both the flag and `use_inductor_graph_partition=True`, which is why that path works.

### Proposed fix

Keep the existing pass. At `-O2`, turn `fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla` on for CUDA/ROCm MLA models when `_USE_LAYERNAME` is set and `vllm::unified_mla_kv_cache_update` is not already a splitting op. In `set_splitting_ops_for_v1`, do not append that op in that case, so the pattern is in one Dynamo piece. Still append `vllm::unified_kv_cache_update`.

Leave the flag off when:

- the model is not MLA, or there is no model config (bare `VllmConfig()` splitting-ops snapshots stay as they are)
- the platform is not CUDA or ROCm
- `VLLM_USE_LAYERNAME=0` or torch is older than 2.11
- HiSparse is on and Inductor graph partition is off (`prepare_kv_cache_update` has to run every step; HiSparseConnector can turn HiSparse on after the `-O2` default is applied)

If the flag is true and the op is still a splitting op with partition off, warn and set the flag false, same as the other RoPE+KV fusions.

Do not turn `use_inductor_graph_partition` on by default. Do not change `splitting_ops_contain_kv_cache_update`, or the AITER `fuse_rope_kvcache` default flips on and is then forced off.

`-O0` and `-O1` keep the flag false.

I searched open issues for `fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla` and `unified_mla_kv_cache_update` and did not find a report of this default. I did not use the documentation chatbot.

- [x] Searched existing issues, including #33267, #43504, #45573, #50758, and #40392.

title: [Bugfix] Enable MLA RoPE+KV-cache fusion when layer names are hoisted
body:
## Overview

Fixes #60325.

Default `-O2` enables the existing MLA RoPE + KV-cache fusion for CUDA/ROCm MLA models when the attention layer name is a hoisted `LayerName`. The pass was off because `unified_mla_kv_cache_update` is still a Dynamo splitting op.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V2/V3-style MLA at default `-O2` leaves `vllm::unified_mla_kv_cache_update` in the compiled piece, so `MLARoPEKVCacheCatFusionPass` can match.
- Non-MLA models and a model-less `VllmConfig()` keep today's splitting ops.
- `VLLM_USE_LAYERNAME=0`, torch older than 2.11, and platforms other than CUDA/ROCm keep the flag off.
- An explicit `fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla=True` that still splits the op out is disabled, with a warning.
- HiSparse with Inductor graph partition off keeps the op eager, including when HiSparseConnector turns HiSparse on after the `-O2` default.
- `use_inductor_graph_partition` stays off by default. `splitting_ops_contain_kv_cache_update()` is unchanged, so the AITER RoPE+KV default does not flip on.

## Validation

Config decisions are covered in `tests/compile/test_config.py`:

- `test_mla_rope_kvcache_fusion_splitting`: MLA + LayerName, non-MLA, plain string names, non-CUDA, no model, explicit enable with and without LayerName.
- `test_mla_fusion_follows_inductor_graph_partition`: partition on still enables the flag with no model.
- `test_mla_fusion_disabled_when_user_splits_the_op`: a user `splitting_ops` list that still contains the MLA cache op.
- `test_mla_fusion_stays_split_for_hisparse`: HiSparse set before the default, and the late HiSparseConnector case.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` passed on the three files with ruff 0.14.10.

The new tests were not executed in this environment. Current main does not import on the local torch 2.5.1 (`torch._inductor.custom_graph_pass` and `torch.float8_e8m0fnu` are absent; main pins torch 2.13.0).

Not run, and they need a GPU:

- `tests/compile/passes/test_mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion.py`
- `tests/kernels/core/test_rotary_embedding_mla_cache_fused.py`
- a DeepSeek-V2/V3 compile under default piecewise CUDA graphs, to confirm the pass matches and the cache write replays

## Details

`-O2` applies `enable_rope_kvcache_mla_fusion` before `set_splitting_ops_for_v1`. With graph partition off and `splitting_ops is None`, `splitting_ops_contain_kv_cache_update()` returns true because #33267 will append both cache-update ops. The flag stays false, and the MLA op is then split out. The fusion pattern is RoPE and that op in one piece, so it cannot match.

On torch >= 2.11, `LayerName` is a hoisted graph input, so that string constant is gone. The new branch returns true only for an MLA model on CUDA or ROCm, and `set_splitting_ops_for_v1` then skips appending `vllm::unified_mla_kv_cache_update`. `vllm::unified_kv_cache_update` is still appended.

If the pattern matches, the piece contains `fused_rope_unified_mla_kv_cache_update`. If it does not, the unfused op is still inside the piecewise CUDA graph. `use_inductor_graph_partition=True` already does that: fusion runs on the full graph, then `maybe_use_cudagraph_partition_wrapper` wraps each partition. The op reads `slot_mapping` from `BlockTable.slot_mapping.gpu`, which is filled in place before replay. That replay was not checked on a GPU here.

HiSparse's `prepare_kv_cache_update` has to run from Python every step, so the op stays a splitting op when partition is off.

`use_mla` is also true for DeepSeek-V4. V4 attention is not `MLAAttention` and does not emit this op, so the pass registers nothing and the V4 kernels are unchanged. The compile hash can change because `splitting_ops` no longer names an op V4 does not run.

This does not replace the manual fusion in #45573, and it does not close #33267. #40392's serve path (flag plus Inductor graph partition) still works through the old branch.

title: [Spec Decode][MRV2] Suffix decoding speculator for Model Runner V2
body:
## Overview `method="suffix"` today needs Arctic Inference, runs on the CPU, forces Model Runner V1 and disables async scheduling. With this PR it runs on Model Runner V2 with a GPU speculator, with async scheduling and without Arctic; V1 keeps using Arctic. This is the "suffix" item in #47172. The speculator builds on `ngram_gpu` (#40704) and borrows from #52097 (thanks @zip95297). Related fix on main: #61509 (adaptive verification's startup profiling was counted as CUDA graph memory). ## Claims - `method="suffix"` runs on Model Runner V2: GPU-resident, no host sync on the propose path, async scheduling, no Arctic dependency. V1 is unchanged except for the default `num_speculative_tokens` (below). - Acceptance is on par with Arctic: 1.937 tokens per step vs Arctic's 1.923 (k=8) and 1.948 (k=24) on a 21K-request replay. - With adaptive verification, throughput matches or beats Arctic on V1 at every concurrency for Qwen2.5-7B (offline and online serving) and for Qwen2.5-1.5B from concurrency 64 up; at 1.5B concurrency 8 and 32 Arctic is ahead (below). Without adaptive verification, verifying every slot loses from concurrency 32 up, as with `ngram_gpu`. - GSM8K accuracy matches no speculation. - `num_speculative_tokens` now defaults to 8 for suffix decoding (was `suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth`, 24), because V2 verifies every slot. - Seeded sampled requests are reproducible regardless of the rest of the batch, also with adaptive verification. ## Validation **Tests** ```bash pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_suffix_speculator.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py # 46 passed pytest tests/test_config.py -k "speculative or suffix or heterogeneous or model_runner" # 50 passed pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_ngram_gpu.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py # 31 passed pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/ngram_suffix/test_ngram_suffix.py -k suffix # 3 passed ``` The e2e tests ran with the CI model's weights (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) on one L4: - The V2 GSM8K correctness test passes (76.3%). At the old default k=24 it ran out of memory: V2 profiles one logits row per request, while every step computes 1 + k. - The V2 cross-request test gives 0.74 → 4.47 accepted tokens per draft on the repeated pass. With Qwen2.5-1.5B it's 1.32 → 5.12, and 1.28 → 1.28 with the corpus off, which the test's `second > 2 * first` check rejects. - The Arctic acceptance test (V1) passes. **Runtime checks** - **No new host syncs:** `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` with and without adaptive verification, including seeded requests and ingestion. - **TP=2:** corpus, index, statistics and drafts are identical on both ranks after 312 requests, with and without adaptive verification, on the default ring and on a 2,048-token ring where bursts of up to 48 finished requests wrap over themselves. - **Seeded requests:** a seeded request alone vs in a 64-request batch gives identical output 4/4, with and without adaptive verification (before this change, 1/4 with it). **Acceptance.** Replay of 21,299 greedy Qwen2.5-1.5B requests with 5.1M output tokens (UltraChat, Alpaca, GSM8K, Spec-Bench, code edit, rewrite and templated JSON), in waves of 64, with a 1M-token corpus and k=8. Mean tokens per step. Arctic runs via `arctic_inference` and also sees responses still being generated. The kernel matches the replay on all 1,280 sampled drafts. | Drafter | All | Code edit | Rewrite | Templated JSON | |---|---|---|---|---| | Own history only | 1.651 | 5.50 | 4.74 | 1.65 | | **This PR** | **1.937** | 5.45 | 4.69 | 4.25 | | Exact corpus search + same vote (upper bound) | 1.956 | 5.45 | 4.69 | 4.28 | | Arctic (V1), k=8 | 1.923 | 5.12 | 4.07 | 3.89 | | Arctic (V1), k=24 | 1.948 | 5.89 | 4.37 | 4.11 | **Throughput.** Offline `LLM.generate` on this PR's final code. Output tokens/s relative to no speculation. - **Setup:** concurrency = `max_num_seqs`; prompts from a pinned pool with the replay's category mix (its GSM8K and Spec-Bench prompts also appear in the replay); greedy, `max_tokens=256`, k=8. - **Backends:** FlashAttention 2, except adaptive verification on `TRITON_ATTN`, which is compared against no speculation on `TRITON_ATTN`. - **Runs:** one per point; runs with another process on the GPU were discarded and rerun. | Model | Concurrency | `ngram_gpu` | Arctic (V1) | This PR | This PR + adaptive verification | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Qwen2.5-7B | 1 / 8 / 32 / 64 | 1.28 / 1.14 / 0.73 / 0.52x | 1.31 / 1.29 / 1.24 / 1.03x | 1.46 / 1.32 / 0.82 / 0.59x | **1.39 / 1.36 / 1.24 / 1.18x** | | Qwen2.5-1.5B | 1 / 8 / 32 / 64 / 128 / 256 | 1.45 / 1.25 / 0.84 / 0.55 / 0.50 / 0.44x | 1.41 / 1.43 / 1.17 / 1.00 / 0.91 / 0.82x | 1.66 / 1.47 / 0.97 / 0.64 / 0.56 / 0.52x | **1.56 / 1.29 / 1.15 / 1.05 / 0.99 / 0.91x** | - **Where Arctic wins:** 1.5B at concurrency 8 and 32, by 11% and 5% in absolute tok/s. Adaptive verification trims too much there (open question 2). - **Backend difference:** at 1.5B concurrency 128 / 256, `TRITON_ATTN` without speculation is 1.13 / 1.21x faster than FA2. Against the FA2 baseline the other columns use, adaptive verification is 1.12 / 1.10x. - **With #61509:** the 7B KV cache with adaptive verification grows from 21–46K to 50–70K tokens. 7B throughput becomes 1.38 / 1.32 / 1.30 / 1.15x, within run-to-run noise except at concurrency 32. **Online serving** (`vllm bench serve`, Qwen2.5-7B, prompts not in the 256-request warm-up, up to 256 output tokens, `--generation-config vllm`). Output throughput vs no speculation: | Config | Concurrency 1 / 8 / 32 / 64 | |---|---| | `ngram_gpu` | 1.26 / 1.11 / 0.73 / 0.53x | | Arctic (V1) | 1.42 / 1.37 / 1.24 / 1.10x | | This PR | 1.49 / 1.35 / 0.87 / 0.65x | | **This PR + adaptive verification** (vs no-spec on `TRITON_ATTN`) | **1.44 / 1.44 / 1.30 / 1.23x** | Median TTFT at concurrency 1 is 125 ms with this PR (with or without adaptive verification) and with `ngram_gpu`, vs 73 ms without speculation and 74 ms for Arctic on V1, which runs without async scheduling. That is about one decode step, so it's a V2 spec-decode cost rather than a suffix one.
GSM8K, workloads and correctness checks **GSM8K** (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, all 1,319 questions, 5-shot, `max_num_seqs=128`). Accuracy matches within noise (binomial SE about 1 point); at this load speculation doesn't speed it up: | Config | Greedy | Temperature 0.7 | Wall time (greedy) | |---|---|---|---| | No speculation (FA2) | 83.0% | 81.7% | 193 s | | No speculation (`TRITON_ATTN`) | 83.4% | 82.3% | 156 s | | Arctic (V1) | 83.4% | 83.2% | 252 s | | This PR | 82.8% | 83.6% | 387 s | | This PR + adaptive verification (`TRITON_ATTN`) | 82.9% | 81.6% | 157 s | **Workloads.** Offline, throughput vs no speculation (adaptive verification vs no-spec on `TRITON_ATTN`). Concurrency 32, except long context: | Workload | This PR | + adaptive verification | Arctic (V1) | |---|---|---|---| | VLM: Qwen2.5-VL-3B, 360 distinct camera frames, templated JSON reports and captions | 1.38x (3.18 tok/step) | 1.50x | 1.56x | | RL rollouts: Qwen2.5-1.5B, GSM8K, n=8, temperature 1 | 0.94x | 1.40x | 1.16x | | Multi-turn chat: Qwen2.5-7B, UltraChat history | 0.78x | 1.15x | 1.03x | | RAG + summarization: Qwen2.5-7B, Spec-Bench | 0.86x | 1.16x | 1.10x | | Long-context decode: 24K-token prompts, concurrency 3 | 1.38x | 0.29x; **1.46x with #61509** | 1.19x | At long context, adaptive verification's startup profiling cost the KV cache 1.9 GiB (43K instead of 80K tokens), so prefixes were evicted and re-prefilled. #61509 fixes that accounting on main. **Correctness** (this PR's final code; greedy outputs vs no speculation, 48 distinct prompts; fp32 Qwen2.5-0.5B on `TRITON_ATTN`, since FA2 has no fp32): | Check | This PR | + adaptive verification | `ngram_gpu` | |---|---|---|---| | Plain greedy | 45/48 | 45/48 | 46/48 | | Repetition/frequency/presence penalties | 43/48 | 44/48 | 43/48 | | Structured outputs (JSON schema, regex, choice), `max_tokens=2`, logprobs | identical | identical | regex 11/12, rest identical | | Stop strings with `min_tokens`; `ignore_eos` to 300 tokens | 48/48; 45/48 | 47/48; 45/48 | 47/48; 45/48 | | 24 distinct 800–1,800-word prompts with chunked prefill (`max_num_batched_tokens=512`); 8 prompts ending 40 tokens before `max_model_len` | 24/24, 8/8 | 24/24, 8/8 | 24/24, 8/8 | | Preemption (small KV cache, 144 requests, 355–509 preemptions) | 128/144 | 125/144 | 126/144 | - **Baseline noise:** two no-spec runs, async vs sync scheduling, differ on 1/48 plain prompts. - **Logprobs:** deltas on identical outputs are at most 5e-3, the same as `ngram_gpu`. - **Sampling** (Qwen2.5-1.5B bf16, temperature 1, top-p, top-k, n=16, each method with its own seed): total-variation distance of per-position token marginals vs a no-spec run is 0.153 / 0.079 / 0.131. A second no-spec run gives 0.161 / 0.059 / 0.128, `ngram_gpu` 0.148 / 0.056 / 0.131. Seeded requests reproduce 4/4. - **Aborts** (`vllm serve`, 48 streams aborted mid-generation): the server stays healthy. Greedy requests sent afterwards match those sent before 8/8 without adaptive verification. With it, 7/8 in fp32 (one flip at a 0.0004-nat near-tie) and 2/8 in bf16 7B: the number of verified slots changes the batch shapes.
## Details **How it works** - **Own history:** the longest suffix match within the request's prompt and output, up to `suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth`. Same kernel layout as `ngram_gpu`. - **Cross-request corpus:** finished responses go into a GPU token ring (`suffix_decoding_corpus_tokens`, default 1M). A hash index on each request's last 2 and last 4 tokens returns up to 16 candidate positions. Each is verified and extended to its full suffix match, so the index is only an entry point for suffix matching, and hash collisions or overwritten documents only cost a candidate. - **Frequency vote:** for each candidate match length, the candidates matching at least that long vote on the continuation, as in SuffixDecoding. The highest-scoring chain wins, ties going to the longer match; then the longer of the own-history and corpus matches wins. - **Adaptive verification** (`enable_adaptive_verification`): per-slot confidences, learned online by source, match length and position, let the runner trim slots that aren't worth verifying. - **Seeded requests** (explicit `seed`, temperature > 0) draft only from their own history, and adaptive verification verifies all of their slots. Under sampling, both the drafts and the number of verified slots change which tokens are drawn. Greedy requests keep the corpus. - **Ingestion:** one GPU program per (document, block). Each program replays the batch's placement to find its offset and skips positions that a later document of the same batch overwrites. Every position is written by exactly one program, so the result is exact and order-independent even when a burst is larger than the ring. A 256 × 4,096-token burst at the default 1M ring takes 0.58 ms. - **TP consistency without collectives:** finished ids are ingested in sorted order, index inserts use `atomic_max` over `(document << 32 | position)`, and the statistics are integer counters. - **Memory at the defaults:** 36 MB (4 MB corpus plus a 32 MB index). Suffix decoding also keeps the runner's token history on the GPU (`max_num_seqs × max_model_len × 4` bytes, e.g. 32 MiB at 256 × 32K).
How a corpus lookup works (diagram) ``` Request history: ... "report" "the" "camera" "at" "the" "north" "gate" └──── last 4 ────┘ └─ last 2 ┘ 1) LOOK UP hash(last 4), hash(last 2) -> buckets, 8 slots each (slot = newest occurrence in each of the last 8 documents) 2) EXTEND BACKWARDS each candidate against the request (up to 24 tokens): request: report the camera at the north gate corpus: log: the camera at the north gate -> match length 6 stale or colliding candidate -> length 0, dropped 3) VOTE + DRAFT candidates matching >= L tokens vote on the next k tokens; the chain with the highest summed probability wins 4) COMPARE with the longest match in the request's own history; the longer match wins, empty slots get the last token ``` Ingestion when a request finishes: `[last 3 prompt tokens | response]` is appended to the ring, and each position with at least 2 (4) tokens before it in the document is indexed under them: `table[hash][doc % 8] = max(existing, (doc, pos))`.
**Why a hash index** | Index | Propose cost (L4) | Notes | |---|---|---| | Suffix tree (Arctic, V1) | CPU, per request | Host sync, so no MRV2 or async scheduling | | Suffix array (#52097) | 1.3–4.5 ms as an eager library call (prototype measurement on a shared L4); #52097 reports 0.4–1.9 ms with its CUDA-graph path (L20, k=16) | Background rebuilds, epochs and a CPU collective for TP | | Brute-force GPU scan | 0.3–1.2 ms at batch 128 (prototype measurement) | Exact; cost grows with batch × corpus | | **Hash index + vote (this PR)** | **11–35 µs** GPU time for batch 1–256 (CUDA-graph microbenchmark), the same at 1M and 4M corpus tokens. As the engine runs it (eagerly): 89–95 µs per step at 4K context for batch 1–256, 231 µs at 128K context with 32 requests (`ngram_gpu`: 75–78 and 111 µs) | No rebuilds. The index alone is within 0.4% of an exact longest-match search; with the vote, about 1% below exact search + vote | One difference from Arctic: corpus matches need at least 2 tokens (so `suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth` must be at least 2 for the corpus), while own-history matches can be 1. Storing the last 3 prompt tokens with each response lets a response's first tokens be drafted from the corpus. **Taken from #52097 and @zip95297's MRV2 port** (`zip95297/vllm-dev`, branch `zip95297/suffix-gpu-mrv2`): GPU cross-request matching with no host sync; an `on_requests_finished` hook in `finish_requests` that ingests from `RequestState` and skips preempted requests (from the MRV2 port); sorting finished ids for TP consistency; the replay-based acceptance evaluation. **Changes outside the speculator** - `SpeculativeConfig`: suffix's default `num_speculative_tokens` is `min(8, suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth)` on both runners. On V1 it caps Arctic's dynamic draft length; set 24 for the previous V1 behavior. - `AdaptiveVerificationManager.pinned_requests`: optional drafter hook. Pinned requests keep all their scheduled drafts and the budget is chosen around them. Only suffix decoding sets it (seeded sampled requests); other drafters are unaffected. - `warmup.py`: drafters with a `reset_state` method reset after MRV2's kernel warmup, so the warmup requests don't stay in the corpus. - `model_runner.py`: `set_sampling_states`, `on_requests_finished` and (with adaptive verification) `add_request` hooks, each called only if the speculator defines it; dense `all_token_ids` for suffix. **Limitations** - The corpus is shared across requests regardless of `cache_salt` or LoRA adapter, like Arctic's global tree on V1 (documented; set `suffix_decoding_corpus_tokens: 0` to isolate). - Adaptive verification needs full CUDA graphs and an attention backend that replays variable-length decode batches. On L4 that is `TRITON_ATTN`: vLLM's FA2 backend declares uniform-batch support only. Until #61509 lands, its startup profiling also costs KV capacity, which matters at long context. - Under async scheduling a finished request can carry up to about 2k+1 tokens past the stop point into the corpus. ## Open questions 1. **Adaptive verification by default?** It is what makes suffix decoding pay off from concurrency 32 up. It isn't on by default here because it fails at startup on backends that can't replay variable-length decode graphs (FA2, the pre-Hopper default), so a default needs a fallback to off. Happy to add that here, or in a follow-up. 2. **Low-concurrency trimming.** Adaptive verification trims too much at low concurrency on small models: Qwen2.5-1.5B at concurrency 8 is 1.29x with it vs 1.47x verifying every slot (7B: 1.36x vs 1.32x). Tune it here (for example with a more optimistic prior) or later? 3. **Corpus default.** 4M tokens adds about 2–3% acceptance, but the index grows from 32 MB to 128 MB. 4. **Tokens past the stop point.** Pass the scheduler's final length down to ingestion? 5. **Arctic-only options** (`max_spec_factor`, `min_token_prob`) are ignored on V2 (documented). Warn as well? ## Follow-ups - Exclude filler slots from spec-decode metrics for GPU drafters (as #52097 does on V1 and its MRV2 branch does; see also #44056 and #50518). With adaptive verification, trimmed slots are still counted as drafted. - Index responses while they're still being generated. That may be why Arctic is ahead on the templated VLM workload. - CUDA-graph the propose path (@zip95297's bucketized draft graphs). - aarch64 benchmarks. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
**Not duplicating existing work:** the only other suffix decoding drafter PR is #52097 (`suffix_gpu` on V1), whose author is collaborating here; searches for "suffix decoding", "suffix_gpu" and "SuffixSpeculator" find no other MRV2 implementation. AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, prototype, write and test this change. cc @njhill @zip95297 @benchislett @TheEpicDolphin

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V3 tool parser returns no tool calls when the JSON arguments span several lines
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text vLLM 0.30.0 (the latest release) and 0.28.0, CPU, Python 3.12, Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Describe the bug `DeepSeekV3ToolParser`'s regexes match the body of the ```` ```json ```` block with `.` and without `re.DOTALL`, so arguments that the model pretty-prints over several lines are not matched. `extract_tool_calls` then returns `tools_called=True` with an empty `tool_calls` list, and the call is lost: ```python import json from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest from vllm.tool_parsers.deepseekv3_tool_parser import DeepSeekV3ToolParser class Tok: def get_vocab(self): return {"<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>": 0, "<｜tool▁calls▁end｜>": 1, "<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>": 2, "<｜tool▁call▁end｜>": 3, "<｜tool▁sep｜>": 4} args = json.dumps({"city": "Tokyo"}, indent=2) out = ("<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜><｜tool▁call▁begin｜>function<｜tool▁sep｜>get_weather\n" f"```json\n{args}\n```<｜tool▁call▁end｜><｜tool▁calls▁end｜>") print(DeepSeekV3ToolParser(Tok()).extract_tool_calls(out, ChatCompletionRequest(messages=[], model="m"))) # tools_called=True tool_calls=[] content=None (with json.dumps(..., indent=None): one call) ``` ### Expected One call `get_weather` with `{"city": "Tokyo"}`, whatever the whitespace inside the JSON block. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Enable the fused all-reduce + mHC boundary at TP2
body:
## Motivation

The fused CuTe DSL Lamport all-reduce + mHC post/collapse/RMSNorm (#57643, #58586) only runs at TP4. The Blackwell single-node recipes now default to TP2 (vllm-project/recipes#1002), so at TP2 every small-batch sublayer boundary still runs a separate all-reduce plus unfused mHC. The kernel is already parametrized by the TP world size, so this PR admits TP2 in `supports_mhc_all_reduce` (TP8 stays off) and extends the tests to TP2.

## Evaluation

Setup: 2 × GB200, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

**Correctness**
- GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 questions): main 0.901, this PR 0.901.

**Performance**: `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, ISL 1024 / OSL 512, no speculative decoding, mean of 3 seeds.

| Concurrency | TPOT p50 (ms) main → PR | Output tok/s main → PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.19 → 4.48 (−13.8%) | 184.6 → 213.0 (+15.4%) |
| 2 | 5.58 → 4.93 (−11.7%) | 347.7 → 390.7 (+12.4%) |
| 4 | 6.10 → 5.25 (−13.9%) | 607.2 → 701.5 (+15.5%) |
| 8 | 6.86 → 6.08 (−11.3%) | 1092.2 → 1212.9 (+11.1%) |
| 16 | 8.48 → 7.64 (−9.9%) | 1767.1 → 1919.2 (+8.6%) |
| 32 | 10.59 → 10.55 (−0.4%) | 2786.3 → 2658.8 (−4.6%, one outlier run) |
| 64 | 13.44 → 13.72 (+2.1%) | 4364.5 → 4346.2 (−0.4%) |

Swapping the two arms' GPUs (and NUMA nodes) gives the same picture: TPOT changes by −12.1%, −13.9%, −10.8% and +0.7% at C1, C4, C16 and C64. TTFT is unchanged.

With DSpark (recipe default, k=5):

| Concurrency | ITL p50 (ms) main → PR | Output tok/s main → PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 7.12 → 6.49 (−8.8%) | 616.7 → 680.6 (+10.4%) |
| 2 | 8.37 → 7.27 (−13.2%) | 986.9 → 1149.0 (+16.4%) |
| 4 | 9.63 → 8.33 (−13.6%) | 1423.3 → 1497.0 (+5.2%) |

At C≥8, DSpark steps exceed the 16-token fused limit, so the fused path is not taken.

## Notes

- TP2 + DSpark on main can hit the autotune `Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic` startup crash, which is unrelated to this PR. #58165 fixes it.
- AI assistance (Claude) was used. I reviewed all changes and ran the tests above.

title: [ROCm] [Feat] Enable HiSparse on ROCm
body:
## Overview

Enable HiSparse on ROCm/gfx950, extending #57602 with HIP host-memory registration, sparse MLA execution, and ROCm regression coverage.

## Claims

- Add BF16/FP8 sparse MLA support, shared TP host pools, and MTP/graph-path support on ROCm
- Reduce temporary residency-lookup allocations and batch clean-page release
- Fix host-memory ownership and shutdown cleanup handling
- Add regression coverage and wire relevant tests into ROCm Buildkite jobs

## Validation


The new metadata-event regression passes 3/3, versus 1 failed / 2 passed before the fix. Cumulative pre-commit checks passed:

```
