title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Parse DeepSeek-V3 tool calls with multi-line JSON args
body:
## Overview

`DeepSeekV3ToolParser` loses a tool call when the model pretty-prints the JSON
arguments over more than one line. Fixes #60342.

## Claims

- Non-streaming: `extract_tool_calls` returns the call, instead of
  `tools_called=True` with an empty `tool_calls` list.
- Streaming: the argument delta accumulates the whole object, instead of stopping
  at the first newline.
- Parallel tool calls stay separate calls, single-line or indented.

## Validation

Both regexes live in `__init__`, so I drove the reproducer from #60342 through the
patterns themselves against a `get_weather` block whose body is
`json.dumps({"city": "Tokyo", "unit": "celsius"}, indent=2)`:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tool_call_regex.findall` | `0` matches | `1` match, args `{"city": "Tokyo", "unit": "celsius"}` |
| `stream_tool_call_portion_regex` arguments group | `'{'` | `'{\n  "city": "Tokyo",\n  "unit": "celsius"\n}'` |

Single-line arguments are unchanged before and after. For the two-call output, the
non-streaming regex yields two matches with their own arguments both indented and
not, which is the case a plain `re.DOTALL` would break.

That case is now pinned by `test_pretty_printed_arguments` in
`tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv3_tool_parser.py`. It goes through the shared
`ToolParserTests` harness, so the existing `streaming` fixture runs it on both the
streaming and the non-streaming path:

```bash
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv3_tool_parser.py
```

## Details

Root cause: both regexes capture the fenced JSON body with `.` and neither is
compiled with `re.DOTALL`, so the argument group cannot cross a newline. The
non-streaming pattern then fails to match at all, and `extract_tool_calls` still
reports `tools_called=True` because it only checked for the start token. The
streaming pattern does match, but its argument group ends at the first line break,
so only `{` is ever streamed.

I scoped `[\s\S]` to the two argument groups rather than compiling the patterns
with `re.DOTALL`, because `type` and `function_name` are greedy `.*`: under
`DOTALL` they run past the end of one tool call, and a response containing two
calls collapses into one match with the first call's markup swallowed into the
name. Keeping those two groups line-bound is what preserves parallel calls, and
it is also true to the format — neither the type nor the function name ever
contains a newline.

The non-streaming argument group is lazy (`[\s\S]*?`) so it stops at its own
closing fence; the streaming one stays greedy, since it is matched against a
partial tool call and should carry as much of the argument text as has arrived.

Not a duplicate: searching open PRs for the issue number and for `deepseekv3`
/ tool-parser keywords turned up nothing touching this parser, and the issue has
no linked PR.

No model eval: the change is confined to string handling inside the tool parser
and does not touch generation, sampling or any model code path, so there is no
accuracy surface to measure. The behaviour is covered by the unit test above.

One thing I deliberately left out of scope: `deepseekv31_tool_parser.py` has the
same shape of defect in its own `tool_call_regex` and
`stream_tool_call_portion_regex` (lazy/greedy `.*` for the arguments, no
`DOTALL`), for its sep-token format rather than a fenced block. I kept this PR to
the parser the issue reports. Happy to fold V3.1 in here or send it separately,
whichever you prefer.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] DFlash2: map reduced-vocabulary candidates to target ids
body:
## Overview

DFlash2 drafters with a reduced draft vocabulary (`draft_vocab_size` smaller than `vocab_size`, with a `d2t` table) propose the wrong tokens. `compute_candidates` returns the top-k row numbers of the reduced head, and the speculator uses them as target token ids. It writes them into the draft tokens and looks up the selector codebooks with them.

Only rows where `d2t` is non-zero come out wrong. Pruned vocabularies usually keep the most frequent (lowest) ids, so `d2t` is the identity over a prefix and it's the rarer tokens past that prefix that break. You get lower acceptance rather than garbage drafts, and if the vocabulary happens to be a pure prefix of the id space you don't see it at all. That's how I missed it the first time I tested.

This hits any reduced-vocab DFlash2 drafter on any model or backend. The fix is in model code and nothing in it is ROCm specific.

## Claims

- Candidates from a reduced-vocab DFlash2 drafter go through `draft_id_to_target_id` before they reach the candidate selector, with the same `target = row + d2t[row]` mapping `compute_logits` already uses.
- Drafters with the full vocabulary (no `d2t`) are unchanged.
- No new host sync. The mapping is a gather on tensors that are already on the device.

## Validation

I added a test to `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py`, which already runs in the CPU and the GPU spec decode CI steps. It fails on main for the reduced-vocab case and passes with the fix:

```
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py
# CUDA (RTX A2000 Laptop, sm_86), torch 2.13.0+cu132:
#   main:        test_compute_candidates_returns_target_ids[True] FAILED (1 failed, 22 passed)
#   this branch: 23 passed
# CPU only: 13 passed, 10 skipped (the skipped ones need CUDA)
```

`pre-commit run` passes on the changed files.

I also ran an end-to-end acceptance A/B with stock checkpoints: target `RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4`, drafter `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, vLLM v0.31.1rc0 built for ROCm, one Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201). My only NVIDIA card is an 8 GB laptop GPU, so I couldn't repeat this part on CUDA. Settings were `num_speculative_tokens=4`, eager, prefix caching off, c=1, 8 prompts (6 code, 2 prose), greedy, 256 tokens each, thinking off. Acceptance comes from the engine's `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters.

For the pruned drafter I cut the z-lab drafter down to 32,768 rows (head rows copied from the target's `lm_head`, `d2t` = kept id minus row). I picked the vocabulary by token frequency over the CPython 3.12 stdlib source so anyone can rebuild it. Its `d2t` is the identity for rows 0 to 12,637 and non-zero for 20,130 of the 32,768 rows.

| drafter | code | mean acceptance length | draft acceptance | per position (0 / 1 / 2 / 3) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| full | main | 3.693 | 67.3 % | .880 / .738 / .596 / .479 |
| full | this PR | 3.672 | 66.8 % | .866 / .724 / .600 / .482 |
| pruned 32k | main | 2.916 | 47.9 % | .720 / .524 / .395 / .277 |
| pruned 32k | this PR | 3.449 | 61.2 % | .827 / .669 / .538 / .415 |

- With the fix the pruned drafter's mean acceptance length goes from 2.916 to 3.449 (+18.3 %). The gap that's left to the full drafter comes from the smaller vocabulary itself.
- With the full drafter, main and this branch give bit-identical output when I run them back to back in one session (558 drafts, 1,491 accepted, same text). The 3.693 vs 3.672 in the table is boot-to-boot variation on main, which lands on one of those two results each time the engine starts.
- The same drafter pruned to a pure prefix (ids 0 to 32,734 plus the 33 special/EOS ids, so only 33 rows with a non-zero `d2t`) shows no cost from the bug on main. So a quick test with that kind of vocabulary looks fine.

## Details

`DFlashQwen3ForCausalLM` already sizes `lm_head` to `draft_vocab_size`, loads `d2t` and maps through it in `compute_logits`. DFlash2's `compute_candidates` skips that step, but the selector codebooks, the proposal cache and the verifier all index the target vocabulary.

I went through the other drafters on main that allow a reduced vocab. Eagle3 (llama, qwen3, deepseek), DFlash and DSpark all map draft ids, and LiLiCorr refuses a reduced vocab, so DFlash2 looks like the only one missing it. This is MRV2 only, since that's the only place the DFlash2 speculator exists.

Related PRs I checked, none of them a duplicate:

- #59740 moves the `d2t` handling of Eagle3, DFlash and DSpark into a shared `DraftVocab` but leaves DFlash2's `compute_candidates` alone. It keeps `draft_id_to_target_id` on the model, so this applies on top of it as is. If it lands first I'm happy to switch this to `self.draft_vocab.map_draft_to_target(ids)`.
- #52883 also edits `compute_candidates` (unquantized heads in the selector) without touching the mapping, so whichever lands second just needs to keep these lines.
- #55961 packs the top-k all-gather and doesn't change the mapping.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write the code, run the tests and measurements, and draft this description. I reviewed the change and the results before posting.

title: [Perf][ROCm][Quantization] gfx942 MXFP8 linear for decode via AITER asm A16W8 GEMM
body:
## Overview

On gfx942 (MI300X, MI325X), MXFP8 linear layers are dequantized to BF16 at load time and run through hipBLASLt. This PR adds an opt-in kernel that uses AITER's MXFP8 GEMM for decode-sized batches instead, reading the FP8 weights directly.

Requires ROCm/aiter#6172.

## Claims

- Faster decode for MXFP8 models on gfx942. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP4, MI325X) the dense GEMMs take 0.4 to 0.6 ms less per decode step.
- No accuracy change on GSM8K.
- Off by default. Enable with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MXFP8_ASM_GEMM=1`.

## Validation

`pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_aiter_a16w8_mxfp8.py` passes on MI325X. It compares the new kernel with the existing emulation kernel and also checks kernel selection and CUDA graph replay.

End to end on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 4x MI325X, TP4:

| Concurrency | Dense GEMM time per decode step, without | with |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 2.91 ms | 2.32 ms |
| 4 | 3.00 ms | 2.55 ms |
| 6 | 3.41 ms | 3.00 ms |
| 8 | 3.46 ms | 3.03 ms |

GSM8K 5-shot: 0.9272 with the kernel, 0.9257 without.

These numbers were measured with an earlier revision of this branch that used the same kernels.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MXFP8_ASM_GEMM=1 \
  vllm serve <DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash> --tensor-parallel-size 4
```

## Details

- The kernel is only used on gfx942, with the flag set, and for weight shapes that AITER has tuned. Everything else keeps the current path.
- Prefill and other large batches still use hipBLASLt, so the layer keeps its BF16 weight next to the FP8 one. For DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 that is about 2 GB more memory per GPU.
- The choice between the two paths is made inside a custom op, so it works with `torch.compile` and CUDA graphs.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Separate manager and kernel block sizes in DFlash DCP slot mapping
body:
## Overview

Separates the KV-cache manager block size (`block_sizes[gid]`) from the attention kernel block size (`kernel_block_sizes[gid]`) in DFlash/DSpark Decode Context Parallelism (DCP) slot mapping so that DCP ownership and rank-local positions are computed in manager-block coordinates before indexing the expanded kernel block table.

Fixes #59184 (follows up on #51031 and #52188).

## Claims

- Fixes DFlash/DSpark context and query KV slot mapping when `cp_size > 1` and `block_sizes[gid] != kernel_block_sizes[gid]`.
- Eliminates duplicate block-table lookup and null-block masking boilerplate between context and query slot calculations in `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` by consolidating the two-phase lookup inside `cp_local_slot`.

## Validation

### Duplicate-Work Check

Verified no existing open PR addresses this issue:
- `gh issue view 59184 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments`
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "59184 in:body"` (0 results)
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "cp_local_slot"` (0 results)
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "prepare_dflash_inputs"` (only #58559, which adds a startup warmup loop and does not touch DCP block-size handling)

### Test Commands & Results

Validated locally using Triton's CPU interpreter (`TRITON_INTERPRET=1`) across all existing and new test cases in `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py` (GPU execution is exercised in Buildkite CI):

```bash
TRITON_INTERPRET=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py -v
```

| Configuration (`B=32, K=16, CP_SIZE=4, CP_INTERLEAVE=32`, block table `[10, 11, 12, 13]`) | Before Fix (RED) | After Fix (GREEN) | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target_positions=[63, 64, 65, 66]`, `cp_rank=2` | `ctx=[-1, -1]`, `q=[-1, -1, -1]` | `ctx=[-1, 160]`, `q=[161, 162, 163]` | `ctx=[-1, 160]`, `q=[161, 162, 163]` |
| `target_positions=[63, 64, 65, 66]`, `cp_rank=0` | `ctx=[-1, 176]`, `q=[177, 178, 179]` | `ctx=[-1, -1]`, `q=[-1, -1, -1]` | `ctx=[-1, -1]`, `q=[-1, -1, -1]` |
| `target_positions=[79, 80, 81, 82]`, `cp_rank=2` (crosses expanded sub-block `10 -> 11`) | `ctx=[-1, -1]`, `q=[-1, -1, -1]` | `ctx=[175, 176]`, `q=[177, 178, 179]` | `ctx=[175, 176]`, `q=[177, 178, 179]` |

All 8 parametrized test cases in `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py` pass.

## Details

### Root Cause

`BlockTables` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/block_table.py`) maintains two block sizes per KV-cache group `gid`:
1. `self.block_sizes[gid]` (physical/manager block size `B`), which defines DCP virtual-block ownership (`virtual_block_size = B * CP_SIZE`) and rank-local token position (`local_pos = virtual_block_idx * B + local_offset`).
2. `self.kernel_block_sizes[gid]` (attention kernel sub-block size `K`), into which each manager block is expanded (`bpk = B // K` kernel block IDs per manager block in `input_block_tables[gid]`).

When #51031 (`0ecc284790`) updated `BlockTables._compute_slot_mappings_kernel` to separate `kv_block_size` from `kernel_block_size`, `DFlashSpeculator.propose` and `cp_local_slot` (added in #52188, `d1e3eee6fb`) continued passing only `kernel_block_sizes[gid]` as `block_size` and indexing `input_block_tables` via `pos // (block_size * CP_SIZE)` prior to DCP localization. When `cp_size > 1` and `B != K`:
- Global positions were wrapped modulo `K * CP_SIZE` instead of `B * CP_SIZE`, assigning tokens to the wrong DCP rank.
- Because `local_offsets` spans `[0, B)` while `input_block_tables` entries have size `K`, the expanded block-table index `local_positions // kernel_block_size` must be computed *after* localizing global positions with `block_size`.

### Implementation

- **`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cp_utils.py` (`cp_local_slot`):** Computes `local_positions` and `is_local` using manager `block_size`, then indexes `block_table_row_ptr` using `local_positions // kernel_block_size` (masked by `is_local`), checks for the null block (`block_id != 0`), and computes `block_id * kernel_block_size + (local_positions % kernel_block_size)`.
- **`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py`:** Passes both `self.block_tables.block_sizes[gid]` and `self.block_tables.kernel_block_sizes[gid]` from `DFlashSpeculator.propose` into `prepare_dflash_inputs` and `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel`.
- **`tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py`:** Extends `_run_prepare` with `block_size` and `kernel_block_size` parameters and adds `test_prepare_dflash_inputs_dcp_with_smaller_kernel_blocks`.

### AI Assistance

AI assistance was used in root-cause analysis, drafting the fix, and running the `TRITON_INTERPRET=1` verification suite. Every changed line was reviewed by the human submitter.

title: [Spec Decode] Generic reduced-vocabulary get_top_tokens() for DraftModelSpeculator
body:
## Overview

Generic, opt-in `VLLM_SPEC_DRAFT_VOCAB` env var that attaches a reduced-vocabulary `get_top_tokens()` to any `DraftModelSpeculator`-based drafter whose model doesn't already have its own restriction mechanism — covers plain EAGLE and EXAONE 4.5's native MTP head, which #59740 (addressing #58578) doesn't reach. Posting on behalf of VENETA (I'm BRANTD-veta) — full writeup and the Korean draft-vocabulary files we built this against: https://github.com/veneta-ai/mtp-draft-vocab-ko.

## Claims

- +13.4% decode (15.83 → 17.95 tok/s median) on `yuhuili/EAGLE-LLaMA3.1-Instruct-8B` drafting for Llama 3.1 8B, acceptance unchanged, zero output difference between arms.
- +7.0% decode (5.57 → 5.96 tok/s median) on `LGAI-EXAONE/EXAONE-4.5-33B-FP8`'s native MTP head (`Exaone4_5_MTP`), acceptance unchanged, zero output difference between arms — a second confirmation on a different dispatch shape (native MTP head, not an auxiliary drafter).
- No new `speculative_config` keys, no changes to verification — a single env var read once at `load_model()` time, opt-in, no-op when unset.
- Generalizes across every speculator built on `DraftModelSpeculator` (EAGLE, MTP, dflash, dspark) by attaching at that shared layer instead of per-model-class, while still correctly leaving alone any model that overrides `LocalArgmaxMixin.get_top_tokens()` with its own mechanism (detected by identity comparison, not just `hasattr`).

## Validation

Measured on one DGX Spark (GB10), 10 Korean prompts, greedy decoding, k=3:

| drafter | vocab | decode tok/s (median) | accepted/draft | output diff |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| EAGLE-LLaMA3.1-Instruct-8B / Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | full (128,256) | 15.83 | 1.55 | — |
| same | reduced (65,536, Korean-biased) | **17.95 (+13.4%)** | 1.57 | 0 replacement/garbled chars |
| EXAONE-4.5-33B-FP8 (native MTP head, `Exaone4_5_MTP`) | full (153,600) | 5.57 | 1.07 | — |
| same | reduced (65,536, Korean-biased) | **5.96 (+7.0%)** | 1.07 | 0 replacement/garbled chars |

The EXAONE gain is smaller for two reasons, not just noise: this model keeps 42.7% of its vocabulary (65,536 of 153,600) against the EAGLE case's 51.1% of a much larger 128,256-token vocabulary in absolute rows cut, so there's proportionally less matmul being saved; and EXAONE 4.5 runs in reasoning mode by default (a long CoT before any answer token), with acceptance pinned at 1.07/3 in both arms regardless of vocab size — the target rejects most drafts either way, so the draft step is a smaller share of total decode time here than in the EAGLE case. Boot log for this one: `spec draft vocab: 65536 of 153600 tokens (42.7%) kept; get_top_tokens() attached to this Exaone4_5_MTP instance (lm_head 1500.0 -> 640.0 MiB per draft step)`.

A first attempt at this (not in this PR) masked `compute_logits()`'s already-full-vocabulary output after the fact instead of reducing the matmul — correct, but measured **zero speedup**, because the full matmul still ran before the mask was applied. That's the reason this PR attaches a real `get_top_tokens()` (a smaller matmul) rather than post-hoc masking logits — mentioning it since "we tried the obvious thing first and it didn't work, here's why" seemed worth keeping rather than silently landing only the working version.

Confirmed from the boot log that the mechanism is actually engaging, not a no-op: `lm_head` read shrank from 1002.0 MiB to 512.0 MiB per draft step (51.1%), matching the kept-vocabulary fraction almost exactly.

New unit tests (`tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_reduced_draft_vocab.py`, CPU-only, no GPU needed): no-op when the env var is unset; no-op when the model already overrides `get_top_tokens()` with its own mechanism (mirrors Gemma4's centroid head); no-op when `tp_size != 1` or the model has no plain top-level `lm_head`; correct id-remapping when ids are kept out of order and a non-kept row would otherwise win the argmax; and an explicit check that the reduced weight tensor never aliases the original `lm_head.weight` (the property that matters when an EAGLE drafter shares that exact weight object with its target via `load_eagle_model`).

I don't have a working current-`main` vLLM install on this machine to run these through the real CUDA path tonight (the model-class landscape has moved since the image we had locally), so I verified the committed function body by extracting it verbatim into a standalone harness against plain torch + a stub `LocalArgmaxMixin`/`logger` and running all six scenarios there — all pass. Would appreciate a CI run catching anything that harness couldn't.

## Details

**Motivation.** #58578 measured this general idea (+25–29%) and #59740 implements a considerably more sophisticated context-aware version of it (static list + per-token dynamic rows via a rank-256 SVD scorer, quantized rows, +15.2–22.6% on `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` + MTP k=3 — also on one DGX Spark, for what it's worth our own measurement of the *existing* MiaAI-Lab kit's mechanism on that exact model/hardware was +54%, a gap we can't explain and aren't asserting a cause for). That PR's changed-files list (`qwen3_5_mtp.py`, `qwen3_eagle3.py`, `qwen3_dflash.py`, `qwen3_dspark.py`, `llama_eagle3.py`, `deepseek_eagle3.py`, `gemma4_dspark.py`, `qwen4_exp/{nvidia,amd}/mtp.py`) doesn't touch plain `eagle/speculator.py`-dispatched models or `exaone4_5_mtp.py` — this PR is specifically the static-list-only piece for those classes, not a competing design for the ones #59740 already covers well.

**Why attach at `DraftModelSpeculator.load_model()` instead of per model file.** `MTPSpeculator`, `EagleSpeculator` and `AutoRegressiveSpeculator` all resolve to the same `_greedy_sample_draft`/`sample_draft` dispatch on the shared base class, and neither overrides it. A hook there, right after `self.model = self.load_draft_model(...)` and before `self._validate_local_argmax_reduction()` (which already requires `hasattr(self.model, "get_top_tokens")` whenever `use_local_argmax_reduction=True`), covers every method built on that class at once rather than needing one patch per model file.

**Why `LocalArgmaxMixin.get_top_tokens` identity comparison, not `hasattr`.** `hasattr(model, "get_top_tokens")` is true for almost every model already, via `LocalArgmaxMixin`'s own generic default — which is itself just a full-vocabulary matmul plus a TP-communication optimization, not a vocabulary restriction. A naive `hasattr` check would silently skip attaching to EAGLE/Llama models entirely (they already have *a* `get_top_tokens`, just not a reduced one), while still correctly skipping Gemma4's centroid-projection head, which overrides the mixin with something real. Identity-comparing the unbound function against `LocalArgmaxMixin.get_top_tokens` distinguishes "has the generic default" from "has its own mechanism" correctly in both directions.

**Safety.** `index_select` always allocates a new tensor, so the reduced weight is never a view onto the original `lm_head.weight` — this matters because `load_eagle_model` (in `eagle/utils.py`) commonly points a draft model's `lm_head` at the literal same object as the target's. `get_top_tokens()` is only ever called from this speculator's own `_greedy_sample_draft`/`sample_draft`, never from the target's own `compute_logits()`/rejection-sampler verification path, so there is no path by which this change can reach target verification regardless.

**Limitations, stated rather than glossed over.** Static list only — no context-aware dynamic rows, no quantization, no `tp_size > 1` support (explicit, logged no-op rather than silently wrong). `use_local_argmax_reduction` also requires `draft_sample_method != "probabilistic"` (pre-existing constraint, unrelated to this PR) so this only applies to greedy drafting. Models whose head is nested rather than a plain top-level `lm_head` (GLM-4 MoE's `shared_head.head`, DeepSeek's equivalent) aren't covered yet either — a straightforward extension, just not done here since I don't have a measurement for it.

---

- [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. — Code/comments: done. Docs: deliberately skipped; `docs/features/speculative_decoding/` doesn't mention this env var yet, and I didn't want to add docs that might conflict with #59740's own (more complete) upcoming config surface for the same area. title: [Model][Core] Share the Qwen4Exp PLE table between co-located replicas
body:
## Overview

Share the CPU-offloaded Qwen4Exp PLE (n-gram) table between co-located replicas, the way `EngramConfig.dp_shared_memory` already does for DeepSeek V4.1's Engram; plus a process-group-free variant (`shared_host_table_dir`) for replicas that cannot share a collective. Motivation: two single-card Qwen3.8-Flash-Next replicas on a 121 GiB node are OOM-killed at boot because each pins its own 47.7 GiB table.

## Claims

- `dp_shared_memory` now applies to `Qwen4ExpForCausalLM` / `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`: one table in `/dev/shm` per node-local Engram DP group instead of one per rank. Two DP replicas of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 boot on 101 GiB of host RAM where the unpatched pair needs about 136 GiB and dies.
- New `EngramConfig.shared_host_table_dir`: independent engine processes on one host share the table through a named file, no process group. Two single-card servers boot together in 150 s on 97 GiB; a restart maps the loaded table and is serving again in 99 s instead of reading 48 GiB.
- Lookups are unchanged (the pinned UVA path); answers are identical at temperature 0 and tool calling is unaffected.
- A request to share that cannot be honoured (no co-located group, `/dev/shm` too small) falls back to per-rank tables with a logged reason rather than an OOM-killed boot.

## Validation

Hardware: one node, two RTX PRO 6000 (96 GB each), 121 GiB host RAM, `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, `--kv-offloading-size 16`, `--max-num-seqs 16`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.94`, `/dev/shm` remounted at 104 GiB. Load: `vllm bench serve`, random 8K-in / 512-out prompts, `--request-rate inf`.

| configuration | boot | host RAM | load | output tok/s | TTFT p50 / p95 | errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| one card, unpatched (reference) | ~150 s | 85 GiB | 16 conc | 395 | 5.1 / 5.3 s | 0 |
| two single-card processes, unpatched | OOM-killed | ~136 GiB needed | — | — | — | — |
| `--data-parallel-size 2`, `dp_shared_memory` (this PR) | 195 s | 101 GiB | 32 conc | 718 | 5.2 / 9.9 s | 0 |
| two single-card processes, `shared_host_table_dir` (this PR) | both 150 s | 97 GiB | 16 conc each, at once | 406 + 411 = 817 | 4.9 / 9.4 s and 4.8 / 9.1 s | 0 |

Correctness: identical completions at temperature 0 across both servers; tool calling 20/20 structured calls per server through the `qwen3_xml` parser; restart of one file-shared server to a correct answer in 99 s. Memory split of the DP pair's cgroup: 79.8 GiB shared (one table and two 16 GiB KV offload tiers), 14 GiB anonymous.

Reproduce (file-shared):

```bash
# on each card, same model, same flags; the first to create the file loads it
vllm serve <model> --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true, "shared_host_table_dir": "/dev/shm"}' ...
# DP: add --data-parallel-size 2 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true, "dp_shared_memory": true}'

Tests (CPU, mocked groups in the style of the existing PLE tests): tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py::test_engram_group_creation_honors_model_and_options now expects the Qwen4Exp group, and none with embedding_across_dp or a resident table; tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py gains tests for the class selection and file-mode factory, the capacity fallback, both shared loaders' writer-only/fence contracts, the file naming and the ready-mark protocol; tests/test_config.py checks shared_host_table_dir requires cpu_offload. No multi-GPU CI test was added for the Qwen shared table (the DeepSeek one needs four GPUs); the hardware validation above stands in for it.

Details

Root cause. DPSharedEngramStorage and the node-local Engram DP group are DeepSeek-only: initialize_model_parallel builds the group only for DeepseekV41ForCausalLM, and Qwen4ExpPLEPinnedHostEmbedding allocates its whole table with pin_memory=True per rank without reading dp_shared_memory. The option is accepted and silently ignored for Qwen4Exp.

Design. The DeepSeek shape is kept: rank 0 creates a /dev/shm file, every rank maps it MAP_SHARED and cudaHostRegisters it, the lookup kernel is untouched, and the group fences on its CPU collectives (broadcast_object, all_gather_object, barrier) so the file is unlinked only after every rank has mapped it. The capacity check (can_share_ple_table) is the leader's decision, broadcast once per process and cached, because every PLE layer asks. The mapping code is one helper shared by both new classes. The group condition moves behind _engram_table_can_be_shared so DeepSeek's behaviour is unchanged and Qwen4Exp joins only when the table is offloaded and not already spread over the DP ranks by embedding_across_dp.

Why a second mode. Without --enable-expert-parallel, DP falls back to AllGather+ReduceScatter dispatch for every MoE layer, so DP replicas are not independent: on a board whose cards have no PCIe peer path (ours; ACS redirect, IOMMU faults) the per-layer collective hangs most boots. shared_host_table_dir gives those deployments the memory saving with no process group: O_EXCL decides the writer, the .ready mark is published ading and readers wait there, so a reader thatmapped early never reads an unfinished table. Theby design (a restart maps the loaded table); thename carries model, revision, layer prefix, shape so a changed checkpoint under the same name needsthe files removed — documented on the option.
Tradeoffs and limitations. About 400 non-test lines, of which the file-shared mode is roughly half; I am happy to split it into a follow-up PR if that eases review. docs/features/engram.md is updated for both. Readers in file mode trust the writer's .ready mark and a size check; there is no checksum. The ted whenever the table is offloaded, even ifsharing then falls back, which matches the DeepSeek path. No change to the model runner or scheduler; parallel_state.py gains one helper and a condition.

title: [Attention] FlashInfer SM120 route for the sparse indexer's paged MQA logits
body:
## Purpose

Add a FlashInfer-backed SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / RTX 5090, compute capability 12.x) route for the DeepSeek sparse-attention indexer's paged MQA-logits decode stage, selectable next to DeepGEMM, and let both backends run every speculative depth natively on SM12x.

Today the indexer's paged logits on SM120 go through DeepGEMM only (`fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits`; see #59725 and vllm-project/DeepGEMM#28). FlashInfer's experimental `sm120_paged_mqa_logits` (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6180, #6199 and the next_n 3/5/6 follow-up) ships the same stage with DeepGEMM's call shape — `get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata(context_lens, page_kv, num_sms)` and `fp8_paged_mqa_logits(q, kv_cache, weights, context_lens, block_table, schedule_meta, max_context_len, clean_logits=False)` — for 64- and 128-state pages, 32 and 64 indexer heads and `next_n` 1..6, with logits bitwise identical to DeepGEMM's SM120 kernel on every validated configuration and faster `next_n` 3 and 4 paths (one Q atom per request).

## Changes

- `--sparse-indexer-mqa-logits-backend {auto, deep_gemm, flashinfer_sm120}` (`KernelConfig.sparse_indexer_mqa_logits_backend`, mirrors the top-k backend knob). `auto` picks `flashinfer_sm120` on an SM12x device when the installed FlashInfer exports the route for the model's (heads, page size, next_n); otherwise DeepGEMM as before. Explicit `flashinfer_sm120` raises with the unmet constraints.
- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`: backend resolution at metadata-builder construction, `mqa_logits_backend` on the decode metadata, FlashInfer schedule metadata built with the same static-buffer pattern as DeepGEMM's (CUDA-graph safe).
- `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py`: the paged decode call dispatches on the metadata's backend; the FlashInfer branch passes the layer's fused `[blocks, page_kv, 1, 132]` cache view as uint8 (block-outermost layouts and padded pages hand over a strided view, which the kernel reads in place through its TMA block stride), the per-token weights and `max_context_len = max_model_len` so the top-k consumer sees the same logits width as with DeepGEMM.
- `vllm/utils/flashinfer.py`: lazy wrappers; the FlashInfer route is gated on an exported capability (`SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES`) and a readable catalog, and the set of natively supported depths is read from the catalog (`exported_next_n()`) instead of a constant, so a FlashInfer build that exports more depths is picked up without a vLLM change. Catalog read errors degrade to DeepGEMM with one warning instead of failing model load.
- DeepGEMM path on SM12x: with vllm-project/DeepGEMM#28 the family-120 kernel takes every `next_n` natively, so the decode metadata no longer pads `next_n` 3/5/6 to 4/8 there (uniform-batch CUDA-graph capture for `next_n >= 3` as on SM100); the padded path (other families) packs the per-token weights before the backend branch so DeepGEMM receives packed weights too.

## Test Plan

- `tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_mqa_logits_backend.py` (CPU): auto/explicit resolution per device family, FlashInfer availability and capability gating, catalog-driven depth set, heads/page/next_n coverage, block-outermost and padded layouts keep the FlashInfer route, unresolved page spec keeps DeepGEMM, catalog failure degrades to DeepGEMM.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_native_next_n.py` (CPU): the per-family native `next_n` set (SM12x native for 1..6 with DeepGEMM PR #28).
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_sm120_paged_mqa_logits.py` (SM12x + FlashInfer with the route): FlashInfer logits vs an fp32 torch reference on dequantized inputs for heads {32, 64} × page {64, 128} × next_n 1..6 × contiguous / strided per-layer cache views, FlashInfer vs DeepGEMM on identical FP8 inputs where both have the kernel, and the DeepGEMM SM120 kernel at every native `next_n` vs the torch reference.

## Test Result

Run on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (driver 595.84.01) inside the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image (vLLM 0.31.1rc1.dev23 at 43b4aaea3 with this change applied; DeepGEMM built from vllm-project/DeepGEMM#28), twice: with FlashInfer main at b5e50c20b (#6180 + #6199 merged) and with main plus the next_n 3/5/6 follow-up (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6219) on `PYTHONPATH`:

- `tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_mqa_logits_backend.py` + `tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_native_next_n.py`: **80 passed** (both FlashInfer states).
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_sm120_paged_mqa_logits.py`: **60 passed, 12 skipped** with #6219 (the skips are the 64-head × 128-page combinations, which FlashInfer does not ship); with FlashInfer main the next_n 3/5/6 FlashInfer cells skip as well (`auto` stays on DeepGEMM for them) and the DeepGEMM native-depth cases pass for every next_n 1..6.
- Serving (8× RTX PRO 6000, TP8, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, FP8 KV, random 1024/256 and 4096/256 at c = 1/4/16/64, with and without DSpark k=3): both backends return identical greedy answers on the QA and long-needle prompt sets (16/16 and 12/12 per arm, top-k active); throughput within noise without speculation, FlashInfer 1–13 % lower at DSpark k=3 on this single-run comparison (repeat in progress; the DeepGEMM arm there still ran the flattened path, which this PR also switches to native).

- Lint: `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --from-ref <base> --to-ref fa82f16e3` passes on the head commit (ruff check/format, typos, SPDX, forbidden-imports, torch.cuda-call, boolean-context-manager, test-tethering, validate-config, mypy 3.10–3.13), and `mypy --all-files` for 3.10–3.13 passes; no auto-fix diff. Run in the same `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image since the hosted pre-commit job is gated on a maintainer label.

Without a FlashInfer build that ships `sm120_paged_mqa_logits`, `auto` keeps selecting DeepGEMM and the GPU test skips. This PR requires flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6180 and #6199 (merged) for the base route and the next_n 3/5/6 FlashInfer follow-up PR for the full native depth set; the DeepGEMM native `next_n` 3/5/6 arm requires vllm-project/DeepGEMM#28 in the pinned DeepGEMM.

title: [Feature][Observability] Add production-ready Grafana dashboards
body:
## Overview

Adds five Grafana dashboards for vLLM's Prometheus metrics to `examples/observability/dashboards/grafana/`. **Service Status** is a large-print status board for the people who use a vLLM service. The other four are for the team that runs it: **Overview** (with latency SLOs), an **Instances** drill-down, **KV Cache**, and **Speculative Decoding**. The PR also updates the dashboard READMEs and adds a short *Grafana Dashboards* section to `docs/usage/metrics.md`.

The existing dashboards (`performance_statistics.json`, `query_statistics.json`, `prometheus_grafana/grafana.json`) and the Perses specs are unchanged. There are no Python code changes. No issue is linked; see *Duplicate-work check* under Details.

## Claims

- **Coverage:** the new dashboards chart 69 `vllm:*` metrics; the three existing Grafana examples chart 17 between them. The added coverage includes:
  - per-engine (data-parallel) views and SLO attainment
  - prefix caching by cache tier, KV block residency, KV connectors (NIXL) and KV offloading
  - speculative decoding, sleep mode, LoRA and MFU
  - the API server's HTTP and process metrics
- **Built for fleets:** every panel aggregates across instances and engines. Variables cover data source, job, model, instance and engine, plus ad hoc filters such as `namespace`. The dashboards link to each other and keep the time range and filters. Clicking a row in the per-model or per-instance table drills down to it.
- **Robust queries:**
  - ratios are guarded against division by zero
  - quantiles are computed from summed bucket rates
  - token-length panels use only the bucket boundaries that all selected servers share
  - the status board shows *Down*, and blanks its numbers instead of freezing them, as soon as a model's servers stop reporting
- **End-user view:** `vLLM / Service Status` shows one strip per model with Status (Online / Sleeping / Down), response time, output speed, success rate and requests per minute. The tiles are color-coded, readable from across a room, and work in kiosk mode.
- **Compatibility:** Grafana 10.4+ (tested on 10.4, 11.6 and 13.2) and Prometheus 2.26+ (including 3.x, Thanos and Mimir). Every queried metric name is defined on `main`.

## Validation

| Check | Setup | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Metric names | Every `vllm:*` series name the dashboards query (108, including `_bucket`/`_sum`/`_count`), checked against the metric definitions in `vllm/` on upstream `main` (8a26869) and in the nightly wheel | 108 / 108 defined |
| Real servers | Nightly CPU wheel `0.31.1rc1.dev1+gbb87d227d` on 4 vCPUs. `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` with n-gram speculative decoding, and `distilbert/distilgpt2` with `--kv-cache-metrics`. Prometheus 3.15.0, 5 s scrape. About 40 min of mixed traffic: streaming and non-streaming requests, shared prefixes, client aborts and invalid requests | 169 / 223 queries return data, 0 errors. The other 54 need features this setup doesn't run: LoRA, sleep mode, KV connectors / offloading, multimodal cache, and block reuse (none sampled) |
| Rendering, real servers | All five dashboards with every row expanded, in headless Chromium, on Grafana 13.2.3, 11.6.16 and 10.4.19 | 0 panel errors and 0 page errors on each version. *No data* appears only on the optional-feature panels listed above |
| Outage | Stopped and restarted the distilgpt2 server | Its status tile showed *Down* within one scrape and its other tiles went blank, with no stale values. It returned to *Online* after the restart, and the status timeline recorded the outage |
| Optional features | Simulated fleet: 3 servers, 2 models, data-parallel engines, and 1 unreachable target. vLLM's own `PrometheusStatLogger` and connector metric classes are driven with synthetic stats for sleep mode, weight updates, LoRA, spec decode, NIXL, `OffloadingConnector` and `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` | 221 / 223 queries return data (the 2 empty ones are the multimodal cache hit rate, which isn't simulated). On all three Grafana versions every panel renders with data, with 0 errors |
| Lint | `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` | typos and markdownlint pass |

**Screenshots.** These were taken on the real servers in Grafana 13.2.3, between 03:05 and 03:45 UTC. distilgpt2 was stopped at 03:13 and was back by 03:16. The servers run on CPU, so latencies are high, and the red 9 tok/s output-speed tile for Qwen is the expected result.

![vLLM / Service Status](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaby/vllm/172849090a95db18230e66a1bb4af0e4454c4b6a/pr-454/service-status.png)

| vLLM / Overview | vLLM / Instances |
| --- | --- |
| ![vLLM / Overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaby/vllm/172849090a95db18230e66a1bb4af0e4454c4b6a/pr-454/overview.png) | ![vLLM / Instances](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaby/vllm/172849090a95db18230e66a1bb4af0e4454c4b6a/pr-454/instances.png) |
| **vLLM / KV Cache** | **vLLM / Speculative Decoding** |
| ![vLLM / KV Cache](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaby/vllm/172849090a95db18230e66a1bb4af0e4454c4b6a/pr-454/kv-cache.png) | ![vLLM / Speculative Decoding](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaby/vllm/172849090a95db18230e66a1bb4af0e4454c4b6a/pr-454/speculative-decoding.png) |

The real-server run found two bugs, which are fixed in the last commit:
- The prompt/output length distribution added up to 177%, because request-token bucket boundaries scale with `--max-model-len` and the two models used different values.
- Grafana 13 threw an uncaught error for ad hoc filters on a templated data source. Defaulting the Data source variable to `default` fixes it.

![Prompt and output length distribution, before and after the fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaby/vllm/172849090a95db18230e66a1bb4af0e4454c4b6a/pr-454/length-distribution-fix.png)

**Model evaluation:** not applicable. The PR adds dashboard JSON and docs only; model outputs and serving are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction (real servers)</summary>

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12
uv pip install vllm \
  "triton @ https://github.com/triton-lang/triton-cpu/releases/download/v3.8.0/triton-3.8.0+cpu-cp312-abi3-manylinux_2_27_x86_64.manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl" \
  --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly/cpu --index-strategy first-index --torch-backend cpu

VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=2 VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=0-1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 8000 \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "ngram", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "prompt_lookup_max": 3, "prompt_lookup_min": 2}'
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=1 VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=2 vllm serve distilbert/distilgpt2 --port 8001 \
  --kv-cache-metrics --kv-cache-metrics-sample 1.0
```

- Prometheus scrapes both servers every 5 s.
- Grafana has a Prometheus data source and a file provider pointing at `examples/observability/dashboards/grafana`.
- Traffic comes from 6 async clients on `/v1/completions`: 70% streaming, a shared ~600-token prefix, repetitive text for n-gram drafts, 5% client aborts and 3% invalid requests.
- Every query was run through the Prometheus HTTP API with the variables set to *All*. A Playwright script rendered each dashboard with its rows expanded and checked every panel for errors.

</details>

## Details

**Motivation.** The existing examples have 13–16 panels each and chart 17 metrics between them, mostly request latency and throughput. They have no instance or engine dimension, no SLO view, and nothing aimed at the people who use the service.

**Design.**
- **Format and naming.** The dashboards are plain Grafana JSON (schemaVersion 39), so they work with UI import, the HTTP API or file provisioning. They are prefixed `vllm_`, tagged `vllm`, and have stable `vllm-*` uids so links between them work. The existing dashboards are kept so current imports keep working.
- **Optional features.** Rows for optional features are collapsed, and their titles name the flag they need (for example *requires --kv-cache-metrics*).
- **SLO tiles.** These count requests below a histogram bucket boundary, so the selectable targets are default boundaries; other targets need `--custom-histogram-buckets`, which the docs explain.
- **Status board.**
  - Tiles are instant queries that only return a value while the model is reporting.
  - *Output speed* is generated tokens per second divided by the average number of running requests. Unlike 1/TPOT, it counts every token of a speculative decoding step.
  - The color thresholds (1 / 3 s, 10 / 20 tok/s, 95 / 99 %) are defaults to tune.
- **Diff size.** Almost all of the diff is dashboard JSON (11,853 lines). The docs change is 120 added and 50 removed lines.

**Limitations.**
- No CI check covers the dashboards, so a renamed metric would not be caught automatically. The metric-name check above was run by hand.
- Real-server validation ran on CPU, not on a GPU deployment. GPU-only features (sleep mode, NIXL, offloading) are covered only by the simulator.
- Ray metrics (`RayPrometheusStatLogger`) use other names and are not covered. The Perses specs are not updated.
- HTTP and process metrics are not labelled by model, and process metrics are missing with `--api-server-count` > 1. The README documents both.
- Not charted: HiSparse, Mooncake store, HF3FS, KV-offload tiering, diffusion, realtime WebSocket and tool-parser metrics.

**Duplicate-work check.**
- A web search of vllm-project/vllm issues and PRs found no open PR that replaces or extends the example Grafana dashboards, only earlier merged updates such as vllm-project/vllm#9311.
- Upstream `main` (8a26869, 2026-10-07) has not changed `examples/observability/`, `docs/usage/metrics.md`, `docs/design/metrics.md` or `vllm/v1/metrics/` since this branch's base (5ab4e44).
- `gh` was not available in this environment, so the submitter should re-run the `gh issue` / `gh pr list` checks from `AGENTS.md` before opening the upstream PR.

**AI assistance.** This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code), which wrote the dashboards, docs and description and ran the validation above. Every commit credits Claude as co-author and carries the submitter's DCO sign-off. Before it goes upstream, the human submitter must still:
- review every changed line
- re-run the validation

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

title: [HiSparse] Read resident KV directly for FlashMLA BF16 prefills
body:
## Purpose

Part of #60420 (does not close it: host-backed prefills still stage).

With HiSparse, the FlashMLA sparse BF16 path stages every prefill: it copies the request's full history from host into a transient GPU buffer (`stage_prefill_rows`), even when all of its pages are GPU-resident, and joins decode and prefill outputs with `torch.cat` in mixed batches. Startup profiling doesn't cover either allocation (its dummy run is one chunk of short prefills), so a long accepted prompt can OOM a running server. The same failure was reproduced on the FlashInfer path; see #60417.

Fix: when every scheduled page is resident (`all_context_pages_resident`), convert all rows against resident pages and run one kernel. Host-backed prefills still stage; making that buffer accounted is tracked in #60072.

Independent of #60417. Both PRs carry the same 4-line `index_group.py` routing change (and its test case), so whichever lands second rebases trivially.

`test_hisparse_mixed_batch_bf16_row_split` keeps its KV in the host pool, so it now sets `all_context_pages_resident = False` to match that scenario. The default of `True` only went unnoticed before because this path never checked the flag.

## Test Plan

- [ ] `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "hisparse or flashmla"` (CUDA)
- [ ] HiSparse e2e with `--kv-cache-dtype auto` on FlashMLA sparse: long prompt + concurrent decodes, no OOM, peak memory vs main
- [ ] GSM8K HiSparse eval on this path

## Test Result

Pending.

title: [Bug]: HiSparse: long prefill batched with decodes can OOM a running server
body:
### Your current environment

vLLM main @ ad0f67a7ec (re-confirmed on 12b005eefa), 1×B200, FlashInfer sparse MLA, fp8 KV, Model Runner V2.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With HiSparse, a long prompt batched with running decodes can crash EngineCore with CUDA OOM, and the running requests die with it. This happens even when all of the prompt's KV is on GPU.

In a mixed decode/prefill batch, the prefill rows don't read the GPU-resident pages directly. Instead:
- the prefilling request's entire history is copied into a temporary GPU buffer on every layer (`stage_prefill_rows`), about 0.55 GiB at 1M tokens;
- decode and prefill run as two kernels joined by `torch.cat`, about 1 GiB at 16K batched tokens.

Neither allocation is needed when every page is GPU-resident, and startup profiling reserves neither. The cause is the `num_decode_tokens == 0 and all_context_pages_resident` condition: it was in the FlashInfer, FlashAttn and SM120 backends, and since #55866 it lives in the shared `SparseMLACommonImpl.forward_mqa`. FlashMLA sparse BF16 copies on every prefill.

**Not a risk: prompts that spill to host** (e.g. a 1M-token prefill misrouted to a HiSparse decoder). The history copy is required there and unreserved, but it is capped by `max_model_len` (one layer at a time). On GLM-5.3-NVFP4 TP4 with the prompt forced to spill (util 0.90, 24 decodes), main completes with the per-step peak only 0.88 GiB over the profiled peak, well within headroom. #60424 tried to reserve it and was closed.

### Repro

The model is cut to 4 layers so a 1M-token prompt fits on one B200's GPU.

```bash
vllm serve <GLM-5.3-NVFP4> --load-format dummy --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": 4}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 --scheduler-reserve-full-isl --attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":24}}'
```

Keep 2 requests decoding (512-token prompts), then send random-token prompts up to 1.04M with `max_tokens=1`.

| config | 1.04M prompt | per-step peak over base at ~1M |
|---|---|---|
| no HiSparse, with decodes | OK | 4.91 GiB |
| HiSparse, no decodes | OK | 4.91 GiB |
| HiSparse, with decodes | **EngineCore OOM at 934K context** | 6.30 GiB |

```
forward_mqa
    output = torch.cat((decode_out, prefill_out))
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1024.00 MiB ... 90.62 MiB is free ...
```

### Fix

- [ ] #60417: when all KV is on GPU, run decode and prefill rows in one kernel against the GPU pages (FlashInfer, FlashAttn, SM120, FlashMLA sparse BF16).

Related: #60429 removed a separate unaccounted buffer (per-layer prefill mirror staging). Tracking: #60072

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Size Humming scratch for PCP
body:
## Overview

Fix Humming grouped-MoE permutation scratch sizing when Prefill Context Parallelism (PCP) expands the token domain across PCP ranks.

`HummingExpertsBase._get_permute_scratch` currently sizes scratch for `max_num_tokens * dp_size`, but the non-DeepEP PCP path gathers MoE inputs across PCP ranks before Humming receives them. With PCP greater than one, the gathered `topk_ids` can therefore exceed the scratch capacity and fail during startup profiling.

This was discovered while validating DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash PCP in #59857 after #56997 made Humming the preferred SM90 MXFP4 backend. The failure is specific to the Humming and PCP combination: Humming with PCP1 and PCP with Marlin both start successfully.

## Related Work

#55105 also updates Humming scratch capacity, but for the DeepEP v2 and tensor-sequence-parallel path. This PR covers the distinct non-DeepEP PCP gather path, where the scratch calculation omitted the PCP expansion factor.

## Implementation

- Include `pcp_size` in Humming permutation scratch capacity.
- Extend the existing shared-scratch test to cover combined DP and PCP expansion for both ordinary top-k and expanded top-k=1 layouts.

## Validation

The fix was validated on one node with 8x NVIDIA H20 (SM90) GPUs using DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash while testing #59857.

| Topology | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| TP4/PCP2 | 8,192 gathered rows vs. 4,096 scratch rows; startup assertion | 8,192 scratch rows; Ready, zero restarts |
| TP2/PCP4 | 16,384 gathered rows would exceed the 4,096-row scratch | 16,384 scratch rows; Ready, zero restarts |

Post-fix validation completed all 18 PCP2/PCP4 Prefill benchmark points and both complete 1,319-record GSM8K runs with zero request errors or Pod restarts. The final no-instrumentation commit also passed image/source identity, startup, backend-selection, and smoke checks.

- changed-file pre-commit, including Ruff, formatting, Python 3.10 mypy, test tethering, and repository policy checks;
- manual Python 3.12 mypy;
- compileall, DCO, and `git diff --check`.

Additional model coverage for PCP with Humming may be added in a later update to this draft PR.

title: [HiSparse] Reserve and bound prefill staging memory
body:
**Closing: not worth the complexity.** Measured on a real model, the staging memory this PR reserves is not what limits HiSparse, and main does not crash in this scenario.

Investigated for scenario 2 of #60420: a long prompt whose KV spills to host, e.g. a 1M-token prefill misrouted to a HiSparse decoder.

**What it did:**
- Reserved HiSparse prefill staging in the shared workspace and split prefills into groups that fit.
- Bounded the `ensure_gpu_sources` temporaries by chunk size.
- Wrote mixed decode/prefill outputs in place.

**Result:** GLM-5.3-NVFP4 TP4, 4×B200, util 0.90, 24 decodes plus one 1.04M-token prompt. The prompt was forced to spill (`--num-gpu-blocks-override 160000`), and staging ran on every layer. The table shows the largest per-step peak above the profiled peak:

| main | + reserved staging | + bounded temporaries | + in-place outputs |
|---|---|---|---|
| +0.88 GiB | +0.88 | +0.66 | +0.67 |

All four completed; none OOMed.
- Staging copies one layer at a time (about 0.55 GiB at 1M tokens). The step peak is set elsewhere, so reserving staging does not lower it.
- Only the bounded temporaries help, and only by 0.22 GiB, against roughly 18 GiB of unused headroom at util 0.90.
- An earlier revision of this description claimed +1.53 → +0.57 GiB on the real model. Those runs never staged anything: the GPU KV pool held the whole prompt, so the claim was wrong.

The one reproducible crash (a 4-layer dummy model at util 0.97, OOM in the decode/prefill `torch.cat`) happens with all KV on GPU. #60417 fixes that.

Outputs were bit-identical to main (FlashInfer fp8, FlashMLA BF16, FA4) and unit tests passed on B200, but neither is a reason to land this. The DBO workspace issue found during review is filed separately.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Drop the unaccounted, write-only prefill mirror staging buffer
body:
## Purpose

`initialize_hisparse_runtime_buffers` allocates a per-layer prefill mirror staging buffer (`num_layers × max_num_batched_tokens × row_bytes`) after the KV cache is sized, so memory profiling never counts it. That's about 0.69 GiB per GPU for GLM-5.3 (78 layers).

Nothing reads it: `HiSparseConnectorWorker.start_step` sets `mirror_from_resident = True` every step, so the host mirror always copies from the resident cache, and only dummy batches ever wrote the buffer. This PR removes it, along with `mirror_write_target` and `mirror_from_resident`.

Related: #60420.

## Test Plan / Result

1×B200, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 cut to 8 layers with dummy weights, MNBT 16384, HiSparse with `host_pool_gib=24`. Measured persistent torch memory after init, excluding weights and KV:

| | allocated beyond weights + KV | KV budget |
|---|---|---|
| no HiSparse | 0.7031 GiB | 112.99 GiB |
| HiSparse, main | 0.7756 GiB | 112.96 GiB |
| HiSparse, this PR | 0.7052 GiB | 112.96 GiB |

- Greedy outputs are identical on main and this PR (4 prompts, 300–7000 tokens).
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -k "hisparse or profiling"`: 10 passed. The CUDA-only kv-update test now asserts only the resident write.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Size the permute scratch from its inputs
body:
## Overview

Stop predicting the MoE permute scratch capacity from `FusedMoEConfig`; size it from the inputs it actually receives, growing until the workspace manager is locked. This is intended as the root fix behind #55105 (DeepEP v2 + sequence parallelism) and #60423 (PCP), which each patch a different term of the same capacity formula for the `assert n_token <= self.max_num_tokens` failure in the Humming grouped path.

## Claims

- The Humming grouped experts no longer derive a row bound from `max_num_tokens * dp_size * experts_per_token`, so DP, sequence parallelism, PCP, and DeepEP v2's power-of-two receive buckets cannot make the scratch too small.
- The scratch no longer has a hidden-state buffer or dtype, which removes the `hidden_states.dtype == self.hidden_dtype` mismatch on the prequantized (block-FP8 activation) path.
- `CutlassExpertsFp8` and the CUTLASS W4A8 experts get the same behavior. They sized the scratch with `max_num_tokens` and no `dp_size` factor.
- One scratch is shared per `(num_experts, num_local_experts, device)` instead of one per `(capacity, topk, hidden size, dtype)`.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k "permute or humming or cutlass or block_fp8"` (1x B300) | 906 passed (with `tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py` and `-k "permute or humming or cutlass"`) |
| GSM8K, `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4`, `--moe-backend humming`, `VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE=grouped_contiguous`, 1x B300, eager (existing `configs/humming/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4-humming.yaml`) | 0.8817 on 1319 questions (threshold 0.86), 0 invalid |
| GSM8K, same model, DP=2 + EP, `allgather_reducescatter`, CUDA graphs, `--max-num-batched-tokens 3000` | 0.8969 on 1319 questions (threshold 0.86), 0 invalid |
| `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k "test_reload_weights and FP8_DYNAMIC"` (1x B300, `VLLM_CUTLASS` FP8 backend, in-place weight reload) | 1 passed, 1 skipped; failed in CI before the shared-scratch fix |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with PCP on 8x H20 (SM90), run by @wangyicong52 (results in #59857) | reported working; #60423 closed in favor of this PR |
| pre-commit on changed files, `mypy-3.12` | passed |

Not validated:

- The DeepEP v2 topology from #55105 is not reproduced here: DeepEP v2 is unavailable on the test machine (NCCL 2.29.7 < 2.30.4). @elvircrn, could you try this branch on your setup?
- The prequantized Humming grouped path (block-FP8 activations before dispatch) was not run with real kernels; in-tree coverage of `HummingGroupedExperts.apply` is mock-based. It is guarded by dtype and shape assertions.

## Details

**Root cause.** `workspace13`/`workspace2` are sized from the actual `M` and grow until `lock_workspace()`. `MoEPermuteScratch` was instead sized up front from config, which requires knowing how many rows every prepare/finalize backend can return in every topology. That bound is a property of the dispatcher, not of the experts, and it has been wrong for PCP, for DeepEP v2 with non-power-of-two capacities, and for CUTLASS with DP.

**Change.**

- `MoEPermuteScratch` holds only index metadata and gains `reserve(expanded_rows)`. It reallocates while the workspace manager is unlocked and raises `Scratch growth is not allowed after locking` afterwards, matching the shared workspace's contract.
- Permuted hidden states come from the caller's workspace. CUTLASS already passed a `workspace2` slice. Humming's prequantized path now writes into `quanted_gate_up_input`, which is allocated with the right shape and dtype and is otherwise unused when w13 quantization is skipped, so this costs no extra memory.
- The index buffers stay a persistent resource rather than moving into `get_simultaneous`: a second `get_simultaneous` call inside `apply()` would alias the live `workspace13`/`workspace2`, and `token_expert_indices` is an `arange` that would otherwise be refilled every call. They are small (seven int32 arrays over the expanded rows plus the sort workspace).

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**

- A runtime shape larger than anything seen during warmup still fails, with the same contract and at the same point as `workspace13`.
- `moe_permute(scratch=...)` without `permuted_hidden_states` now allocates that tensor per call. Both in-tree callers pass a buffer; `benchmark_moe_permute_unpermute.py`'s scratch numbers are not comparable to earlier ones.
- `get_persistent_resource`'s docstring is loosened from "must not resize" to "must not resize once the manager is locked".
- The CUTLASS experts use the same shared scratch as Humming. A scratch owned by the experts instance broke weight reload: the experts are rebuilt after the workspace is locked, so the new scratch was empty and could not grow (caught by `test_reload_weights` in CI build 93385).
- Anything that first reaches a scratch-using path after the lock, without that path having run during warmup, now fails where the old fixed-size scratch would have allocated lazily.

**Relation to open PRs.** Not a duplicate: #55105 and #60423 extend the capacity formula for one topology each and conflict with each other; this removes the formula. The DeepEP v2 handle-capacity change in #55105 (`next_power_of_2(ceil(max_num_tokens / sp_size))`) is independent and still useful. Searches for `MoEPermuteScratch` and `permute scratch workspace` found no other open PR.

AI assistance was used to analyze the capacity mismatch, implement the change, and run the validation above.

title: [Bug]: Sparse MLA indexer's expanded_block_table_buffer is allocated after KV sizing (1 GiB at 1M context)
body:
### Your current environment

vLLM main @ 9367d8b969, B200, Model Runner V2, DSA models (sparse MLA indexer).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The sparse MLA indexer's metadata builder allocates `expanded_block_table_buffer` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`):

```python
self.expanded_block_table_buffer = torch.zeros(
    (scheduler_config.max_num_batched_tokens, block_table_width), dtype=torch.int32, ...
)
```

Builders are constructed during KV cache initialization, after available memory has been profiled and the KV cache sized. So this buffer isn't accounted for and comes out of the activation headroom.

It grows with both `max_num_batched_tokens` and `max_model_len`. With the default 16384 batched tokens and `max_model_len=1048576` (block size 64), it's 16384 × 16384 × 4 B = **1 GiB** per GPU.

On 1×B200 (GLM-5.3-NVFP4 cut to 4 layers, `max_model_len=1048576`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.97`), persistent allocations ended up about 1.9 GiB above the planned budget, with or without HiSparse; this buffer is the largest identified piece. A long prefill then OOMed when a 2.25 GiB MoE workspace allocation couldn't fit. The same config without HiSparse failed the same way at 0.975.

Possible fixes: allocate it before memory profiling so it's counted, or size it to what the indexer actually needs. Decode token counts can in principle reach `max_num_batched_tokens`, so shrinking it needs care.

Related: #60429 (same class of bug in HiSparse, a buffer allocated after KV sizing).

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [CI][ROCm] Fix DSpark ROCm test stub after AITER MegaMoEV2
body:
## Overview

Fixes `:amd: (MI355) Basic Models (Other)` on main. It is non-optional and has been red since #59685 ([ROCm][DSv4] AITER MegaMoEV2) merged. Example: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93397#01a11807-77e4-4894-94e2-b18903ce011c

## Claims

- `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_dspark_rocm.py` passes again: 6/6, up from 4/6 on main.
- This is a test-only change; no model code changes.

## Validation

I ran the file in the CI image for main commit `08567505b0` (`vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:08567505b0…`) on one H200. The file has a module-level import that needs a visible GPU; the tests themselves are `cpu_test` stubs.

| | Result |
|---|---|
| main | `2 failed, 4 passed`: `AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'layers'`. This is the same error as the MI355 job. |
| this PR | `6 passed` |

Command: `pytest -q models/test_deepseek_v4_dspark_rocm.py`. I did not run it on MI355; the PR's MI355 job will confirm.

## Details

#59685 changed `DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM.load_weights` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/dspark.py:395`) to choose the routed-experts prefix from `self.model.layers[0].ffn.use_mega_moe`. The two `load_weights` tests build a `SimpleNamespace` stub for `model.model` that has only `confidence_head`, so the new attribute access fails. The stub now also has one layer with `use_mega_moe=False`, which matches the non-MegaMoE default. The tests monkeypatch `fused_moe_make_expert_params_mapping`, so the prefix value doesn't affect what they assert.

#59685's own CI didn't catch this because its changes didn't trigger the MI355 Basic Models (Other) job. #59050 added this test file to that job.

Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs for `dspark_rocm` / `test_deepseek_v4_dspark_rocm` and found none.

title: [Bugfix] Reserve sparse MLA indexer metadata before sizing the KV cache
body:
## Overview

Reserve the sparse MLA indexer's expanded block table before automatic KV-cache sizing (#60450). It is allocated after profiling and can otherwise push startup past the estimated budget.

## Claims

- Match runtime builder groups and table widths, including microbatches and independent draft contexts.
- Include the reservation in context auto-fit, preserve explicit KV capacity, and avoid charging it twice when replaying a startup plan.

## Validation

On `b05ede5`, 348 related tests and scoped pre-commit pass with PyTorch 2.14. A tiny standalone-draft run on an RTX 5070 Ti generated 32 tokens and accepted 24 draft tokens; the reserved and actual table allocations both measured 2,359,296 bytes.

<details>
<summary>Validation details</summary>

Linux/Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, torchvision 0.29.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2. DeepGEMM was rebuilt at the base's pinned `a7a9277`; other existing vLLM CUDA binaries were reused.

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_config_builder.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py -q
```

Two custom-placement regressions cover auto-fit and failure diagnostics. Ignoring the selected builder makes both fail: 36 tokens instead of 24. Six additional local checks cover HiSparse budget equivalence and four unchanged ready-response unit cases; the latter were extracted to avoid the test module's import-time gated tokenizer. The full engine-client suite was not run. After rebuilding DeepGEMM and restoring the installed CUTLASS import path, all 46 focused checks passed again.

The GPU fixture uses two random-weight layers, eager MRV2, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`, target/draft contexts of 65536/8192 and 512 batched tokens. This is capacity validation, not a trained-model quality or throughput result. CUDA graphs, multi-rank execution and the full B200/GLM report remain untested.

Earlier target-only A/B on `19c0bed` produced identical 32 tokens and logprobs. KV plus table allocation went from 2,052,710 bytes over budget to 65,434 bytes below it. That comparison was not repeated for this rebase.

</details>

## Details

The indexer reports its late allocation through a default-zero hook. The KV planner caches per-worker estimates during auto-fit and retains the selected `KVCacheConfigBuilder` for placement and diagnostics. Both model runners allocate this table; the hook adds no steady-state inference synchronization.

Related #46884, #46794 and #43970 address shape/alignment; this PR accounts for memory.

<details>
<summary>Earlier target-only reproducer</summary>

Use the same CUDA 13.0 environment on the baseline and patched checkout. Put these two files in the same directory, then run:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python reproduce_engine.py --label baseline --output baseline.json
# Apply this patch, then run in a fresh process:
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python reproduce_engine.py --label candidate --output candidate.json
```

The worker extension only reads allocation metadata through a named RPC; it does not alter inference or memory planning.

`metadata_probe_worker.py`:

```python
"""Read-only worker diagnostic, exposed through a named local test RPC."""
class MetadataProbeExtension:
    def inspect_metadata_budget(self):
        import torch
        runner = self.model_runner
        tables = []
        for groups in runner.attn_groups:
            for group in groups:
                for builder in group.metadata_builders:
                    table = getattr(builder, 'expanded_block_table_buffer', None)
                    if table is not None:
                        tables.append(dict(shape=list(table.shape),
                            storage_bytes=table.untyped_storage().nbytes(),
                            builder=type(builder).__name__, device=str(table.device)))
        return dict(tables=tables, num_gpu_blocks=self.cache_config.num_gpu_blocks,
            reserved_metadata_bytes=getattr(self, 'metadata_memory_bytes', 0),
            kv_allocation_bytes=max(t.size for t in runner.kv_cache_config.kv_cache_tensors
                if not t.host_resident),
            raw_available_kv_budget=self.available_kv_cache_memory_bytes,
            max_model_len=self.model_config.max_model_len,
            runner=type(runner).__module__, gpu=torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
            torch=str(torch.__version__), cuda=torch.version.cuda)
```

`reproduce_engine.py`:

```python
"""Full engine A/B with a small randomly initialized DeepSeek V3.2 model.

This is a systems regression fixture, not an accuracy evaluation of trained
DeepSeek/GLM weights. Production model, attention and indexer code are unchanged.
"""

faulthandler.enable()
faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(180, repeat=True)
import argparse
import json

import time

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--label', required=True)

    parser.add_argument('--backend', default='FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120')
    parser.add_argument('--kv-cache-dtype', default='fp8')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    out = Path(args.output)
    assert not out.exists(), 'Preserve previous result'
    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    model = root/'tiny_dsa'
    model.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    config = dict(
        model_type='deepseek_v3', architectures=['DeepseekV32ForCausalLM'],
        vocab_size=256, hidden_size=512, intermediate_size=1024,
        moe_intermediate_size=256, num_hidden_layers=2, num_attention_heads=32,
        num_key_value_heads=32, q_lora_rank=256, kv_lora_rank=512,
        qk_nope_head_dim=128, qk_rope_head_dim=64, v_head_dim=128,
        index_topk=2048, index_n_heads=64, index_head_dim=128,
        n_routed_experts=4, n_shared_experts=1, num_experts_per_tok=2,
        first_k_dense_replace=2, max_position_embeddings=65536,
        rope_theta=10000.0, rms_norm_eps=1e-6, hidden_act='silu',
        torch_dtype='bfloat16', tie_word_embeddings=False,

    )
    (model/'config.json').write_text(json.dumps(config,indent=2)+'\n')
    print('Creating full vLLM engine with local dummy-weight DSA fixture', flush=True)
    from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
    import vllm

    start = time.monotonic()
    llm = LLM(model=str(model), skip_tokenizer_init=True, load_format='dummy',
        dtype='bfloat16', enforce_eager=True, seed=7,
        max_model_len=65536, max_num_batched_tokens=512, max_num_seqs=4,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.35, enable_prefix_caching=False,
        kv_cache_dtype=args.kv_cache_dtype, block_size=64,
        attention_config={'backend':args.backend},
        worker_extension_cls='metadata_probe_worker.MetadataProbeExtension')
    initialized = time.monotonic()
    worker_info = llm.collective_rpc('inspect_metadata_budget')
    print(json.dumps(worker_info,indent=2), flush=True)
    prompts = [{'prompt_token_ids': [3+(i%253) for i in range(length)]}
        for length in (8, 256, 1024, 4096)]
    outputs = llm.generate(prompts, SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=8,
        ignore_eos=True, logprobs=5), use_tqdm=False)
    result = dict(label=args.label, source=vllm.__file__, version=vllm.__version__,
        init_seconds=initialized-start, generation_seconds=time.monotonic()-initialized,
        config=config, workers=worker_info, backend=args.backend,
        kv_cache_dtype=args.kv_cache_dtype,
        outputs=[dict(prompt_tokens=len(r.prompt_token_ids),
            token_ids=list(r.outputs[0].token_ids),
            logprobs=[{str(k):v.logprob for k,v in entry.items()}
                for entry in r.outputs[0].logprobs]) for r in outputs],
        scope='Real end-to-end engine and native GPU sparse attention, randomly initialized two-layer DSA fixture. This is not a trained-model quality benchmark or reproduction of the full B200 GLM deployment.')
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')
    print(f'Completed and wrote {out}', flush=True)

    main()

title: [Bug]: GLM-5.2-FP8 + prefix caching + FP8 KV cache returns empty content (gibberish reasoning) on repeated identical prompts
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py, reconstructed from startup ```text ============================== vLLM Version ============================== vLLM Version : 0.27.1 (V1 engine; system_fingerprint "vllm-0.27.1-tp8-...") ============================== Model / Serving ============================== Model : zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 (GlmMoeDsa, sparse-MLA / sparse_attn_indexer) served_model_name : zai-org--glm-5.2-fp8 dtype : torch.bfloat16 quantization : fp8 kv_cache_dtype : fp8_e4m3 tensor_parallel_size : 8 pipeline_parallel_size : 1 max_model_len : 524288 max_num_seqs : 32 gpu_memory_utilization : 0.8 enforce_eager : False cudagraph_mode : FULL_AND_PIECEWISE enable_prefix_caching : True enable_chunked_prefill : True speculative_config : None # no MTP / speculative decoding reasoning_parser : glm45 tool_call_parser : glm47 enable_auto_tool_choice : True moe_backend : aiter linear_backend : aiter custom_ops : ['+quant_fp8','+grouped_topk','+sparse_attn_indexer', ...] ============================== Hardware / Platform ============================== GPU : AMD Instinct MI300X x8 (ROCm / AITER backends) Engine image : hf-vllm-v0-27-1-amd (AMD build) ============================== Notable startup log lines ============================== [cache.py:296] Using fp8_e4m3 data type to store kv cache. ... it may cause accuracy drop without a proper scaling factor [mla_attention.py:522] Sparse MLA impl has no dense-MHA prefill path; using the top-k MQA path only. ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ## 🐛 Bug Sending the **same** ~43k-token request repeatedly: first N (fresh prefill) are correct, then once it hits the prefix cache a response comes back with `content: null`, an **incoherent multilingual `reasoning`** field, and `finish_reason: "stop"` — silent, no traceback. Prepending a unique prefix (forces fresh prefill) → **0/50 failures**. So the trigger is **prefix-cache reuse**, not length, parsing, weights, or MTP. ### Repro ```bash vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --max-model-len 524288 --max-num-seqs 32 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 --enable-prefix-caching \ --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 ``` ```python import json import urllib.request import uuid BASE = "http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions" MODEL = "zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8" SYS = ( "You are an interactive agent. Prefer dedicated file tools over shell. " "Before writing a file you MUST load the design skill. External scripts " "load only from approved CDNs. Never impersonate a real person or " "organization. " ) * 350 def body(system): return { "model": MODEL, "messages": [ {"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": "hi"}, ], "max_tokens": 4000, "temperature": 0, "stream": False, } def call(payload): req = urllib.request.Request( BASE, data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, ) return json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180).read()) def classify(message): content = (message.get("content") or "").strip() return "EMPTY" if content == "" else "ok" print("identical (cache hits):") for i in range(1, 300): out = call(body(SYS)) msg = out["choices"][0]["message"] label = classify(msg) print(i, label, out["usage"]["completion_tokens"]) if label != "ok": print(json.dumps(msg, ensure_ascii=False)[:600]) break print("unique prefix (fresh prefill):") for i in range(1, 51): out = call(body(uuid.uuid4().hex + SYS)) print(i, classify(out["choices"][0]["message"])) ``` ### Observed **Identical prompt (prefix-cache hits)** — fails on the 13th request: ```text identical (cache hits): [012] ok completion_tokens=85 [013] EMPTY completion_tokens=129 ``` The failing response: `content` is null and `reasoning` is gibberish, yet `finish_reason` is `"stop"`: ```json { "role": "assistant", "content": null, "reasoning": ", samoch3,1columnfk7help\">9 ... 、seb0 might8ひ7-" } ``` **Unique prefix (fresh prefill)** — all clean: ```text unique prefix (fresh prefill): [001] ok ... [050] ok # 50/50 clean ``` ## Expected A prefix-cache hit must not corrupt generation; repeated identical requests should return consistent, coherent output. ## Suspected area Prefix-cache reuse + `fp8_e4m3` KV cache + sparse-MLA top-k MQA prefill under CUDA graphs. Can A/B `--enforce-eager`, bf16 KV, or prefix caching off if useful. ## Potentially Related #59926 (v0.27.1, fp8 KV, prefix-cache reuse; cache_salt helps — closest), #50881 (FP8 KV garbage under CUDA graphs), #60174 (prefix-cache hit corrupts output). ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
