title: [Core] Add a generation readiness check `/health_generate`
body:
## Purpose

Adds a generation health check at `/health_generate`

The implementation is based on PR #59179, with improvements that cover more edge cases with DP > 1 and report why the server is not ready. I've added the author of #59179 as a committer on this PR. Please see #59179 for context on the initial design.

This does not duplicate other work: it continues #59179, and I'm not aware of another open PR adding a generation health check.

### Background

For long running inference deployments for online serving as well as RL use-cases, there can be a variety of inference engine failures or hangs. Broadly there are two sources of failures / hangs:

1. Infrastructure failures: GPU failures, network failures, etc. Some of these are recoverable (transient error that succeeds on retry) while some are not (GPU failure).
2. Software bugs: There are two styles of errors here:
a. Probabilistic, recoverable: Errors that happen due to low-probability events such as:
      1. An illegal memory access with vLLM that occurs once in millions of generations.
      2. A collective hang during weight syncing in DPEP setups.
      3. Generation [hang](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44185) with spec decoding + MoE + DP.
b. Irrecoverable bugs: Bugs that are deterministic failures in certain state.
      1. Misconfigurations, unsupported kernel on certain hardware, etc.

A generation health check helps users detect and recover from failures of class 1. and 2.a.

<details>
<summary> List of failures to handle</summary>

Here are a few relevant issues for vLLM server failures / hangs:

| Issue | Brief description | Failure mode |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| #44185 | DP + EP + MTP/speculative decoding can hang near `max_model_len` when DP ranks disagree about whether the drafter path should run. | EngineCore forward/collective hang; processes may stay alive while affected requests stop making progress. |
| #43547 | MoE + DP can drift collective sequence after zero-token scheduled steps skip DP coordination, eventually hanging a real MoE collective. | EngineCore forward collective hang, likely with worker processes alive but blocked in `reduce_scatter` or a related collective. |
| #36594 / #51481 | DPEP pause/wake coordination can leave DP ranks or the coordinator in the wrong running state around `pause_generation`, `sleep()`, `collective_rpc`, or online weight update. The older issue covers a late `START_DP_WAVE` re-arming a paused engine; the later PR fixes the coordinator assuming engines started merely because it forwarded a wake. | DP wave/coordinator control-plane hang: processes can stay alive, but drain times out, frontends may stop sending `FIRST_REQ`, or ranks can enter mismatched collectives during weight-sync/control RPCs. |
| #53130 | Running chunked-prefill work can consume the scheduler token budget every step, so waiting/deferred requests are not admitted or promoted. | Admission starvation / request-level timeout, not a full EngineCore hang; existing running requests may still progress. |
| #54173 | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next prefix-caching/GDN path can hit CUBLAS internal error or illegal memory access in fused Mamba/GDN kernels. | Kernel crash leading to EngineCore or worker failure after the async CUDA error surfaces. |
| #37035 | MTP/hybrid GDN illegal memory access under load, later tied to a drafter block-size/cache-pressure bug. | Kernel crash leading to EngineCore or worker failure; may require long-running/load-heavy traffic to trigger. |
| #60109 | HiSparse + GLM TP8 on B200 hits illegal memory access when a new request wave is admitted after a previous wave completes. | Wave-transition kernel crash leading to EngineCore or worker failure. |
| #59768 | SimpleCPUOffloadConnector can hit illegal memory access while async CPU-to-GPU prefix load is in flight. | Connector/load-side CUDA race causing EngineCore or worker failure, especially on prefix-cache/offload paths. |
| #45388 | KV-offloading plus prefix caching can deadlock the V1 scheduler under KV-cache pressure: the engine reaches `running=0`, `scheduled=0`, waiting requests remain stuck, and throughput stays at zero. | Scheduler/request-progress hang with EngineCore process alive. |

</details>

### What kind of health checks will detect such failures / hangs?

| Health check | Description | Failures caught |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Existing `/health` endpoint | API server and Engine process liveness. | #54173, #37035, #60109, #59768, once the CUDA/kernel failure surfaces as EngineCore or worker death. |
| `/health_generate` in SGLang | Gets the scheduler to admit a dummy request. If the scheduler is busy (running + waiting > 0), return early with a success response. If the scheduler is idle, execute a dummy forward pass (single token). | #44185, #43547, #36594 / #51481, #54173, #37035, #60109, #59768. However, issues like #45388 are not caught - this is because the scheduler can seem busy (running + waiting > 0) when it's not making any progress (running = 0, waiting > 0) for a long time. |
| Proposed `/health_generate` in vLLM (SGLang's check plus busy-stall detection) | Evaluated per engine rank. If a rank is busy, check how long it has been since it last processed tokens; past a timeout, the server is not ready. If a rank is idle, run a dummy forward pass on it and wait for it to finish on the device. If a rank is sleeping, report it. | #44185, #43547, #36594 / #51481, #54173, #37035, #60109, #59768 and #45388. |

One failure that is not caught by any of the methods above is #53130. I would argue that it is out of scope for the current effort, since the issue is a bit unclear on the exact root cause for the bug. A part of the issue also mentions that the hang occurs when the scheduler is already busy and is able to make progress on running prefill inputs, which means that the engine is alive and healthy.

Note that we haven't discussed any recoverable errors from infrastructure failures. Typical failures here lead to collective timeouts or EngineCore process death, which are of a similar nature to the failures above.

### Changes on top of #59179

**Readiness evaluation**

- **Per rank.** Each engine rank is checked separately:
  - a sleeping rank reports `sleeping`;
  - a busy rank is checked for stalls;
  - an idle rank gets the GPU probe.

  So a busy DP rank no longer hides an idle rank that is stuck in a control RPC.
- **Progress comes only from the engines.** The frontend no longer marks a rank busy when it sends a request. That mark could leave the server reporting `stalled` while idle, if the engine dropped the request before scheduling it.
- **Connector cleanup is not a stall.** Steps that only drain KV-transfer cleanup for finished requests (e.g. a P/D prefill node waiting on a remote pull) count as progress.
- **A dedicated broadcast.** EngineCore publishes readiness to every API server in its own message. Nothing is attached to request outputs any more.

**The idle GPU probe**

- **New `check_health_gpu` on the worker:**
  - It runs the dummy forward pass without adding dummy LoRA adapters or removing loaded ones.
  - It waits for the device to finish before replying, so a fault or hang in the probe's own forward pass fails that same call.
- **Every TP and PP worker must reply.** PP stages don't communicate during a dummy run, so a fault on an earlier stage would otherwise go unnoticed.
- **Out-of-tree platforms:** `WorkerBase.check_health_gpu` raises `NotImplementedError`, so platforms that don't implement it report `probe_failed`.
- **Shared result:**
  - Concurrent callers share one in-flight probe per rank.
  - A successful probe is cached for `VLLM_READY_IDLE_PROBE_CACHE_TTL_S`.

**DP > 1**

- Only count a DP dummy batch as progress when the rank has no local unfinished requests. A rank that holds requests but schedules nothing (e.g. #45388) keeps the wave alive with dummy batches, and was previously reported as making progress.
- Run the idle probe for DP > 1 instead of skipping it.
  - Dense DP ranks are independent engines and run the probe as with DP = 1.
  - MoE DP engines answer with a liveness-only ping, because a dummy batch outside the wave loop could deadlock against peer collectives. A busy loop stuck in a control RPC now makes the probe time out.

**Not-ready details**

- Every not-ready response is a 503 with a JSON body:
  ```json
  {"status": "not_ready", "reason": ..., "message": ..., <details>, "in_progress": [...]}
  ```
  - `reason` is one of `engine_dead`, `sleeping`, `stalled`, `probe_timeout` or `probe_failed`.
  - `engine_dead` returns only `status` and `reason`.
- `in_progress` lists the utility call each EngineCore is running, with its rank and elapsed time. EngineCore publishes the operation before running a utility and clears it afterwards, so every API server reports it, whichever one issued the call.

**Configuration**

| Env var | Default | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `VLLM_HEALTH_CHECK_GPU_TIMEOUT` | 20 s | How long a caller waits for the idle probe before reporting `probe_timeout`. |
| `VLLM_READY_STALL_TIMEOUT_S` | 60 s | A busy rank with no progress for this long reports `stalled`. `0` disables the check. |
| `VLLM_READY_IDLE_PROBE_CACHE_TTL_S` | 10 s | How long a successful idle probe is reused. `0` disables the cache. |

**Scope**

- **Rust frontend:**
  - The Rust client decodes the new readiness messages and ignores them, so normal Rust serving is unaffected.
  - The Rust `/health_generate` endpoint, and aggregating it in the DP supervisor, will come in a follow-up PR.
- **DP supervisor:** its `/ready` and `/readyz` are unchanged.
- **Render-only servers** (no engine) return 200.

**Why report additional not-ready details?**

Downstream applications, such as a load balancer or a health monitor daemon, decide whether to tear down a server based on the response. A 503 from `/health_generate` does not mean the server is broken; it means the server can't serve generation requests right now. For example, it returns 503 while waiting for a weight sync to complete.

### Comparison with the `/fault_tolerance/` APIs

The current fault tolerance APIs can detect failures/hangs during the forward pass in DPEP MoE deployments. This PR targets a broader set of failures/hangs, which is why it adds a separate `/health_generate` endpoint.

### Known limitations

- **Probe stuck for a long time, then recovers.** If the idle probe is stuck for longer than `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (300 s) and then completes, its late reply stays queued. The next executor RPC reads it, and the engine fails. The same applies to any timed-out `collective_rpc` utility call today.
- **`VLLM_HEALTH_CHECK_GPU_TIMEOUT <= 0`** makes every idle probe report `probe_timeout`.
- **Rust frontend:** `/health_generate` is not served yet (see Scope above).

## Test Plan

Apart from the unit tests added in #59179, I've added real E2E tests that cover failure modes from the list above. I think these E2E tests are important to guarantee failure recovery at the engine level.

New tests:

- **Unit tests** for:
  - per-rank evaluation, the DP probe and connector-cleanup progress;
  - shared and timed-out probes;
  - reason and `in_progress` reporting;
  - the engine-side operation broadcast.
- **Fault-injection E2E tests** in `tests/v1/engine/readiness`, using `--scheduler-cls` and `--worker-extension-cls`, split by GPU count:
  - `test_ready_single_gpu.py` (1 GPU): scheduler stall, a latent CUDA fault while idle (including a fault in the probe's own forward pass), and no false positives.
  - `test_ready_multi_gpu.py` (2 GPUs): MoE and dense DP = 2 variants, including a rank stuck in a mismatched DP collective, and a PP = 2 CUDA fault on the stage that doesn't return outputs.
  - These run in the V1 Engine and Distributed CI steps.
- **Rust:** a check that a Python-encoded readiness message decodes in the Rust client.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm_health.py -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/test_basic.py -v
pytest tests/v1/engine/readiness/test_ready_single_gpu.py -v   # 1 GPU
pytest tests/v1/engine/readiness/test_ready_multi_gpu.py -v    # 2 GPUs
cd rust && cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client
```

## Test Result

| Suite | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| `tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm_health.py` | 26/26 passed |
| `tests/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/test_basic.py` | 9/9 passed (`server_load` deselected, as in CI) |
| `tests/v1/engine/readiness/test_ready_single_gpu.py` | 4/4 passed |
| `tests/v1/engine/readiness/test_ready_multi_gpu.py` | 5/5 passed |
| `tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_dp_supervisor.py` | passed (unchanged from main) |
| Rust `vllm-engine-core-client` | 133/133 passed |

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR. I have reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [RFC]: Improving MooncakeConnector
body:
# [RFC]: Improving MooncakeConnector

MooncakeConnector is the built-in P/D disaggregation KV direct-transfer connector in vLLM. Its underlying Mooncake TransferEngine supports pluggable transports (RDMA/TCP/Ascend direct, etc.), making it **the primary path for P/D disaggregation on non-CUDA platforms**. Its engineering quality directly determines the usability of P/D disaggregation on those platforms. There are currently 20+ open issues in the vLLM repo pointing directly at MooncakeConnector, with crash/hang/leak and data-corruption reports making up the largest share.

## Motivation.

**Transfer and protocol**

1. **Single transfer mode**: push only — no pull path and no mode configuration; the decode side cannot pull on demand at its own scheduling pace.
2. **Redundant metadata**: the full KV region table of the decode node is rebuilt and re-sent with every request batch, and the prefill side re-aligns it every time — layout information that never changes during the engine lifetime sits on the per-request critical path.
3. **Fragile discovery**: the HTTP bootstrap server runs inside a prefill-side worker process and is affected by that process's GIL; the query side has a hard-coded timeout with no retry, the register side once blocked producer startup indefinitely, and under external DP LB all workers register as dp_rank 0.

    Refs: #58543 (query-side timeout), #55114 (registration blocking), #51531 (dp_rank)

4. **Questionable transfer correctness with no debugging means**: two independent reports reproduce `dst != src` after RDMA WRITE (concentrated on large descriptors), and the connector lacks a verified-transfer debug mode (per-descriptor verification / deferred confirmation) to tell whether the fault is in the connector or in the TransferEngine.

    Refs: #42395, #44238

**Robustness**

5. **Broken failure propagation**: failures in worker threads / the side channel / bootstrap are not propagated to the scheduler; requests hang with no terminal error visible to the client.

    Refs: #55870, #50425, #57530

6. **Preemption timing window**: request preemption (including the `reset_prefix_cache` path that preempts outside `schedule()`) races with in-flight KV transfers; the prefill side only has a 480s expire fallback, with no delay-free / state-retention protocol. The timing is more complex with PP > 1.
7. **Block-size semantics defect**: the `cache_config.block_size` collapsed across KV groups by `min()` is treated as the physical transfer block size, so hybrid models crash on the first P2P transfer; the hybrid Mamba/GDN path is bug-dense.

    Refs: #58362, #49537, #54392

**Feature coverage**

8. **Incomplete parallelism support**: neither DCP nor PCP is supported; there is no design for KVPP or for transfers where the draft model and the main model use different parallelism strategies; pipeline parallelism (PP) itself — running the prefill and decode stages of one request across PP ranks with in-flight KV handoff between stages — is not supported either, and interacts with the preemption window above. Hetero-TP (P/D sides with different TP degrees) is likewise not yet supported.

    Refs: #53205

9. **Incomplete HMA / new-model coverage**: the connector subclasses `SupportsHMA`, but end-to-end P2P disaggregation is not validated — and in places not implemented — for the wave of hybrid-memory-allocator models it is meant to serve (Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4 Pro, GLM-5.3, MiniMax M3, and newer variants such as GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, DeepSeek V4.1-Flash). These models stress exactly the paths where the connector is bug-dense today: heterogeneous KV groups with mixed block sizes (item 7), Mamba/GDN and sliding-window groups, per-group layouts, and multi-group `request_finished` semantics. There is no per-model conformance matrix telling users which of these models work over P2P PD today.

10. **Missing ecosystem integrations**: no layerwise (transfer cannot overlap with compute); no rd2h (remote KV landing directly in host memory); no integration with pooling/offload/hiSparse features at all.

**Quality infrastructure**

11. **Insufficient observability**: a stats container exists but there are no Prometheus metrics; `cached_tokens` is reported with wrong semantics.

    Refs: #47136

12. **Poor platform portability**: the registration interface's layout/alignment assumptions cannot parameterize platform differences (e.g., Ascend's 2MiB alignment and register-region count limits), which forced vllm-ascend to maintain a 4,290-line forked connector plus 5 variants, drifting on two fronts.

## Proposed Change.

**Phase 1 — Robustness and correctness**
- Land the failure spine: failures from worker threads / the side channel / bootstrap are uniformly propagated to the scheduler, which makes the fail-or-recompute decision and returns a terminal error to the client, eliminating hangs and stranded KV;
- Bootstrap reliability: configurable timeout and bounded retries on the query side, fix dp_rank registration, and review the closure status of the registration-retry PRs;

    - [x] #58919 (registration retry, landed on main)
    - [ ] #55763 (same-topic PR, still open)

- Fix block-size semantics (porting back the implementation validated on vllm-ascend); fix the hybrid Mamba/GDN path; converge the remaining bugs;

    - [ ] vllm-ascend#17414 (fix PR on the ascend side, open)

- Preemption protocol: first audit the P2P exposure under the "preemption outside `schedule()` + re-admission in the same step" window, then design a `handle_preemptions`-style hook / delay-free protocol; cover the PP > 1 + in-flight KV timing; and design mitigations that reduce prefill recompute on the decode side (prefill-side KV retention window with re-transfer / staging in-flight KV to host on P);
- Transfer correctness: a verified-transfer debug mode plus a reproduction suite to locate the root cause; if the root cause is confirmed in the TransferEngine, coordinate with kvcache-ai/Mooncake.

**Phase 2 — Pull mode and metadata rework**
- Add `MooncakePullConnector` (a separate registered name with compatibility-hash isolation, following the NIXL naming convention); **keep the existing push connector** (the prefill-side offload / layerwise scenarios depend on push);
- Move KV layout information from every request batch to a once-per-peer handshake with local caching; per-request payloads keep only lightweight fields;
- Evaluate de-HTTP-izing bootstrap (ZMQ side channel / unifying on `SupportsHMA`).

**Phase 3 — Parallelism and model coverage**
- Parallelism: drive the DCP PR to convergence (rebase + GPU-side validation); design drafts for PCP and for upstreaming KVPP; differentiated draft/main-model transfers; PP support (in-flight KV handoff across PP stages, coordinated with the preemption protocol in Phase 1 — lower priority than DCP/PCP but currently unsupported); hetero-TP (P/D sides with different TP degrees, including padded-page and NVFP4 constraint narrowings); and a systematic parallelism-combination test matrix;

    - [ ] #53205 (DCP PR, draft)

- HMA / new-model conformance (new): build a per-model conformance matrix over the representative HMA models listed in item 9 (K3 / DSV4 Pro / GLM-5.3 / MiniMax M3 / GLM-5.3-Flash / Qwen3.8-Flash-Next / DSV4.1-Flash), audit each model's KV-group shape against the connector's group/layout/block-size handling, fix the gaps that fall out (feeding back into the block-size and hybrid-group fixes in Phase 1), and land the matrix as a parameterized test + documented support table so "does model X work over Mooncake PD" has a definitive answer;
- Layout roadmap wrap-up: per-layer hidden size / HND-D-NHD / cross-layer KV.

**Phase 4 — Ecosystem integrations**
- Upstream layerwise (based on vllm-ascend's `MooncakeLayerwiseConnector`; there is no P2P-side layerwise PR in flight — the community layerwise PR/RFCs are all on the Store side); page-level descriptor coalescing (estimated ≤19×); metrics completion and semantics fixes; rd2h (remote KV landing directly in host memory, wired into `vllm/v1/kv_offload`); P→Store→D pool integration; hisparse host-pool awareness; and documentation/config consolidation.

    - [ ] #46898 (cached_tokens fix PR)

**Phase 5 — Platform unification and cross-connector patterns**
Platformize the registration interface: layout contract + per-layer address book + alignment recovery + region coalescing as pluggable hooks;


## Feedback Period.

**2 weeks**

## CC List.

@nwpu-zxr, @yaojiejia, @Sarimsaljook, @CAICAIIs, @ClockOfDestiny, @ivanium, @LCAIZJ, @dtcccc, @ApostaC, @orozery, @ZJY0516

## Any Other Things.

Relation to existing work
- [#36948](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/36948) (MooncakeConnector roadmap): this RFC provides an execution plan for each of its open items (layerwise, PCP/DCP, hybrid attention, error handling, physical block size, per-layer hidden size, HND-D-NHD, cross-layer KV)
- [#57530](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57530) (failure spine RFC): this RFC lands it as concrete Phase 1 tasks

The above are the problems identified so far. If you have questions, or see other problems we did not cover, please raise them — additions and discussion are very welcome.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

- vLLM v0.31.0 (official image, banner `version 0.31.0`) - 1x NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (SM103, 148 SMs), TP=1 - GLM-5.3-Flash, NVFP4 checkpoint (`nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`), `hidden_size=4096`, `hc_mult=4` ### 🐛 Describe the bug On GLM-5.3-Flash, every prefill step with 129-4736 tokens (148 SMs) JIT-compiles a new DeepGEMM `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` kernel the first time its split count is seen. Startup warmup never compiles these variants, so the engine stalls for 2.5-14 s per variant while serving. That is 20 variants and about 2 minutes of stalls in total on a fresh server. The JIT monitor does not watch DeepGEMM, so nothing is logged; it only shows up as TTFT/ITL spikes. This is the DeepGEMM counterpart of #57843, which warms the same projection for DeepSeek-V4.1 only. The TileLang side of the same mHC path is already warmed for GLM-5.3-Flash since #50178, and I confirmed it no longer compiles at runtime. **Why the variants are missed** - The mHC pre-norm GEMM uses a token-dependent split-K factor. [`_hc_prenorm_gemm_outputs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7436a7f119dedd0c4d5f4d745aa6c2305ee82252/vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang.py#L22-L57) gets it from [`compute_num_split`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7436a7f119dedd0c4d5f4d745aa6c2305ee82252/vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang_kernels.py#L45-L54) as `n_splits = max(1, min(n_sms // cdiv(num_tokens, 64), cdiv(K, 64) // 4))`, where K = `x.shape[1]` = `hc_mult * hidden_size`. GLM-5.3-Flash reaches it through [`mhc_pre_tilelang`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7436a7f119dedd0c4d5f4d745aa6c2305ee82252/vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang.py#L624) and [`mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7436a7f119dedd0c4d5f4d745aa6c2305ee82252/vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang.py#L953). - DeepGEMM's `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` takes the split count as the template parameter `kNumSplits`, so each distinct value is a separate compile. M is dynamic, so the token count itself does not cause a compile: the 10560-token request in the table below reused the kernel compiled for the 16384-token profile run. - With K = 16384 and 148 SMs this gives 22 distinct values over 1-16384 tokens. Startup only reaches two of them. Cudagraph capture (sizes 1-128 with `max_num_seqs=64`) gives 64. The profile run at `max_num_batched_tokens=16384` gives 1. Everything in 129-4736 tokens maps to the other 20 values. - GLM5Next calls [`register_warmup`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7436a7f119dedd0c4d5f4d745aa6c2305ee82252/vllm/models/glm5next/common/model.py#L459-L500) only for the TileLang mHC kernels. Nothing warms the DeepGEMM GEMM. DeepSeek-V4.1 bounds the split count to 1/4/16 with [`compute_mhc_pre_num_splits`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7436a7f119dedd0c4d5f4d745aa6c2305ee82252/vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/warmup.py#L18-L21), and #57843 warms those three. The GLM path uses the unbounded heuristic. - [`jit_monitor`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7436a7f119dedd0c4d5f4d745aa6c2305ee82252/vllm/utils/jit_monitor.py#L15-L20) covers CuTeDSL, Triton and TileLang but not DeepGEMM, so `--jit-monitor-mode error` would not catch this. The DeepSeek-V4 NVIDIA path calls the same two functions (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py`), so it is probably affected too. I did not test it. **Reproduction** Server (fresh container, so both JIT caches start empty): ```bash DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR=/var/tmp/jit/deep_gemm TILELANG_CACHE_DIR=/var/tmp/jit/tilelang \ vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --served-model-name zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 --trust-remote-code --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --block-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --max-model-len 32768 --load-format runai_streamer \ --no-enable-prefix-caching --jit-monitor-verbose --port 8000 ``` After the server is ready and idle, send one prompt per split bucket, one at a time, so each scheduler step holds exactly that many tokens. Each length is sent twice with fresh random token ids, and the script lists the DeepGEMM cubins created by each request:
client script ```python import glob, json, random, time, urllib.request URL = "http://localhost:8000/v1/completions" CACHE = "/var/tmp/jit/deep_gemm" # DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR of the server # One prompt length per n_splits bucket (148 SMs, K = hc_mult * hidden_size = 16384) LENGTHS = [64, 160, 224, 288, 352, 416, 480, 544, 608, 672, 736, 800, 864, 960, 1088, 1248, 1440, 1696, 2112, 2752, 3936, 10560] def cubins(): return set(glob.glob(f"{CACHE}/**/*.cubin", recursive=True)) rng = random.Random(0) for n in LENGTHS: for attempt in (1, 2): ids = [rng.randrange(1000, 30000) for _ in range(n)] body = json.dumps({"model": "zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash", "prompt": ids, "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0}) req = urllib.request.Request(URL, body.encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"}) before, start = cubins(), time.perf_counter() urllib.request.urlopen(req).read() new = sorted(p.split("/")[-2] for p in cubins() - before) print(n, attempt, f"{time.perf_counter() - start:.2f}s", new) ```
**Results** (v0.31.0, 1x B300) All 20 unwarmed buckets compiled exactly one `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` kernel on the first request and none on the second. The two buckets reached at startup compiled nothing. No TileLang kernel was compiled after startup (TileLang cache unchanged, no `TileLang JIT compilation during inference` in the verbose monitor log). | tokens in step | n_splits | warmed at startup | 1st request | 2nd request | new DeepGEMM kernels (1st request) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 64 | 64 | yes | 0.06 s | 0.03 s | - | | 160 | 49 | no | 3.58 s | 0.15 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 224 | 37 | no | 2.53 s | 0.13 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 288 | 29 | no | 11.86 s | 0.13 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 352 | 24 | no | 2.74 s | 0.13 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 416 | 21 | no | 5.86 s | 0.75 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 480 | 18 | no | 6.53 s | 0.74 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 544 | 16 | no | 3.52 s | 0.75 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 608 | 14 | no | 4.38 s | 0.76 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 672 | 13 | no | 13.57 s | 0.74 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 736 | 12 | no | 3.44 s | 0.77 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 800 | 11 | no | 5.93 s | 0.75 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 864 | 10 | no | 5.12 s | 0.13 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 960 | 9 | no | 11.61 s | 0.77 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 1088 | 8 | no | 13.23 s | 0.77 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 1248 | 7 | no | 5.85 s | 0.79 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 1440 | 6 | no | 5.96 s | 0.77 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 1696 | 5 | no | 3.57 s | 0.78 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 2112 | 4 | no | 23.01 s | 0.18 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`, `sm100_mqa_logits` | | 2752 | 3 | no | 2.87 s | 0.15 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 3936 | 2 | no | 2.61 s | 0.16 s | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` | | 10560 | 1 | yes | 0.38 s | 0.36 s | - | The 2112-token step also compiled DeepGEMM `sm100_mqa_logits`, another DeepGEMM entry point that is not warmed (see #49905). Under load the stalls show up as tail latency. I restarted the server (empty caches) and ran the same `vllm bench serve` twice back to back: random dataset, input 120-4680 tokens (`--random-input-len 2400 --random-range-ratio 0.95`), 32 output tokens, concurrency 4, 200 prompts, `--seed 0`, prefix caching off. | | cold (fresh server) | warm (same prompts again) | |---|---|---| | benchmark duration | 97.5 s | 41.3 s | | TTFT p99 / max | 6240 / 11615 ms | 511 / 2580 ms | | TPOT p99 | 492 ms | 39 ms | | E2E latency p99 | 20.3 s | 3.3 s | TPOT rises too, not just TTFT: a compile blocks the whole engine step, so every in-flight decode waits along with the request that triggered it. The cold run also hit a few Triton kpool kernels (`_kpool_tail_seed_kernel`, `_kpool_softmax_rotate_write_cache_kernel`, covered by draft #55348) and three CuTeDSL compiles reported as `wrapper`. The table above is the clean attribution; the benchmark only shows the user-facing impact. We first saw this on a pre-release vLLM build for GLM-5.3-Flash (2x B300, TP2): 10-56 s engine stalls during serving, with the GIL-holding stack inside `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` or the TileLang compile of `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang`. The TileLang part is gone on v0.31.0; the DeepGEMM part reproduces as shown. **Workaround:** keep `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` on a persistent volume so restarts reuse the compiled kernels, or send one prompt per split bucket (the lengths in the script above) before the server takes traffic. **Possible fixes** 1. Warm the DeepGEMM pre-norm GEMM for GLM5Next the way #57843 does for DeepSeek-V4.1. Register `(K, n_splits)` for every split count reachable up to `max_num_batched_tokens` and run one dummy row each, since M is dynamic. This moves the 20 missing compiles to startup. On B300 with a cold cache that is roughly 2 minutes of extra startup time (first minus second request time adds up to about 128 s in the table above), unless the variants can be compiled in parallel the way #56683 does for the TileLang ones. 2. Alternatively, or in addition, bound the split count in `_hc_prenorm_gemm_outputs` like `compute_mhc_pre_num_splits` (1/4/16), so only three variants exist. The TileLang big-fuse warmup keys would have to follow the same bucketing, and it needs a perf check against the per-shape heuristic. That check has to include decode: with the 1/4/16 mapping, steps of 128 tokens or fewer on B300 would go from 64 splits to 16. 3. Separately, it would help if `jit_monitor` covered DeepGEMM JIT, so `--jit-monitor-mode error` catches gaps like this one. Related: - #57843 (open PR): DeepGEMM mHC warmup for DeepSeek-V4.1 only - #50178 (merged PR): mHC TileLang warmup, which covers GLM-5.3-Flash - #49707, #51802 (open PRs): DeepSeek-V4 NVIDIA mHC TileLang warmup only - #49905: DeepGEMM entry points are not warmed - #49349: zero JIT compilation during runtime (tracking) - #48809, #51790: DeepSeek-V4 mHC kernels compiling at runtime I did not find an open issue or PR covering the GLM-5.3-Flash DeepGEMM path. AI assistance (Claude) was used to analyze logs and draft this report. I ran the experiment and checked the results. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`: `/v1/messages` hoists mid-conversation system messages without `--chat-template`, breaking prefix caching
body:
### Summary

**DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash supports mid-conversation system messages, but vLLM's `/v1/messages` frontend moves them into the leading system prompt when `--chat-template` is omitted. Every newly appended system reminder then changes the early prompt prefix and prevents reuse of the conversation that follows it.**

**Confirmed in a running deployment:** supplying the official V4.1 template with `--chat-template /app/model/chat_template.jinja` stopped mid-conversation system messages from disrupting prefix-cache reuse. The backend model remained DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.

The root cause is the native-renderer branch checking the missing CLI Jinja override (`None`) instead of the V4.1 encoder's actual capabilities. It consequently chooses `merge_inline_system=True`. This is a remaining case of #58727 after #58754, which fixed resolved-template detection for the HF-renderer path.

The symptom appeared after changing the Claude Code model identifier from `claude-opus-4-7` to `claude-opus-4-8`. The minimal reproduction below does not depend on Claude Code, LiteLLM, GPU inference, or private request data.

### Your current environment

- Observed vLLM version: `0.30.1rc1.dev219+ga9eafde59`
- Observed commit: `a9eafde59cbd55182dc2265cc398b7186f0a0eaa`
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`
- GPU: NVIDIA B300, tensor parallel size 8
- Tokenizer: `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41`
- Reasoning/tool parsers: `deepseek_v41`
- API: Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages`
- Initially no explicit `--chat-template`

Relevant serving arguments:

```bash
--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41
--reasoning-parser deepseek_v41
--tool-call-parser deepseek_v41
--enable-auto-tool-choice
--enable-prefix-caching
```

The same merge-detection branch is still present in main at `8352b2427f704652da1910f0d53f3fdcc2fa2b0d`, inspected on 2026-10-08. A live server on that newer commit has not been tested.

### Root cause

1. The renderer registry maps `deepseek_v41` to `DeepseekV4Renderer`. This is a shared renderer class; the active tokenizer and encoder are V4.1.
2. `AnthropicServingMessages._should_merge_inline_system()` treats this as a non-`HfRenderer` path and probes only `online_renderer.chat_template`.
3. With no CLI template override, that value is `None`, and `_detect_merge_inline_system(None)` returns `True`.
4. The constructor stores this result in `self._merge_inline_system`.
5. Actual message conversion collects the inline system text into the leading system message and omits the original inline message.

The frontend therefore mistakes the absence of a Jinja override for the absence of native inline-system support.

Source references at the affected commit:

- [Merge detection, conversion, and request path](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a9eafde59cbd55182dc2265cc398b7186f0a0eaa/vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py)
- [Renderer registration](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a9eafde59cbd55182dc2265cc398b7186f0a0eaa/vllm/renderers/registry.py)
- [V4.1 tokenizer wrapper](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a9eafde59cbd55182dc2265cc398b7186f0a0eaa/vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v41.py)
- [V4.1 encoding](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a9eafde59cbd55182dc2265cc398b7186f0a0eaa/vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v41_encoding.py)
- [Same detection branch on inspected main](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/8352b2427f704652da1910f0d53f3fdcc2fa2b0d/vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py)

### Minimal reproduction

Run this inside an environment with the affected vLLM installed. It needs the official V4.1 Jinja file but does not initialize a model, engine, or GPU worker.

If needed, obtain the official template first:

```bash
curl -fsSL \
  https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/resolve/main/chat_template.jinja \
  -o /tmp/deepseek_v41_chat_template.jinja
```

```python
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

import vllm
from vllm.entrypoints.anthropic.serving import AnthropicServingMessages as S
from vllm.renderers.deepseek_v4 import DeepseekV4Renderer

print("vLLM:", vllm.__version__)
template = Path("/tmp/deepseek_v41_chat_template.jinja").read_text()

# Only the renderer's type is needed by this branch of the probe.
# This is not an initialized renderer or a live server instance.
renderer = object.__new__(DeepseekV4Renderer)

for label, override in [("Default", None), ("Official", template)]:
    online = SimpleNamespace(renderer=renderer, chat_template=override)
    print(label, S._should_merge_inline_system(online))
```

Output of the affected detection logic:

```text
Default True
Official False
```

The default result is incorrect for the native V4.1 encoder.

In separate source-level validation, the affected commit's conversion methods and V4.1 tokenizer wrapper were executed on two synthetic tool-use requests. The second request kept all previous messages unchanged and appended an assistant tool call, a tool result, and a new system reminder. Token IDs were generated with the official V4.1 tokenizer:

| Conversion | First prompt tokens | Common prefix with second prompt |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Merge inline systems into the leading message | 6,711 | 51 |
| Preserve inline systems in place | 6,713 | 6,713 |

These are synthetic token-prefix measurements, not production cache-hit measurements. No GPU inference was involved in that comparison.

### Workaround confirmed in the deployment

Add the official model template and restart:

```bash
--chat-template /app/model/chat_template.jinja
```

Here the supplied file changes the Anthropic merge probe to `False`. The V4.1 tokenizer wrapper continues to call its dedicated Python `encode_messages()` implementation; it does not switch to Jinja rendering.

Source-level validation also confirmed that supplying the Jinja override does not change the V4.1 tokenizer wrapper's prompt output for the same messages. The operational confirmation is that new mid-conversation system messages no longer disrupt reuse of the existing prefix.

### Expected behavior / suggested fix direction

Detect inline-system support from the renderer's actual encoding capabilities. A native encoder that supports inline system messages should preserve them without requiring an otherwise unused CLI Jinja override.

Please keep the fallback for renderers/templates that genuinely require system-first ordering. This report is specifically about `deepseek_v41`; it does not establish support for every renderer that shares the `DeepseekV4Renderer` class.

A regression test should cover `deepseek_v41` with no explicit template and an append-only tool-use conversation, verifying that existing prompt tokens remain unchanged when a new inline system reminder is added.

### Related issues

- #58727, fixed by #58754: resolved-template detection for the HF-renderer path. This report covers the remaining dedicated V4.1 encoder path after that fix.
- #58647: Anthropic frontend hardening.

Existing issues were searched. AI assistance was used for source inspection, the synthetic comparison, and drafting. The deployment operator confirmed the before/after behavior of the workaround.

title: [Bugfix] PCP: replicate prefills too short for every rank, also without DCP
body:
# [Bugfix] PCP: replicate prefills too short for every rank, also without DCP

## Purpose

With PCP-only execution (`PCP > 1`, `DCP == 1`), a prefill step that is too short to
give every PCP rank its DualChunkSwap chunks is still split. With PCP=8, a 1-2 token
prefill step leaves 6-7 of the 8 ranks with no row of that prefill. That happens in
practice when a KV connector (for example LMCache) loads every prompt token except the
last one, so the step schedules a single-token prefill.

On v0.31.0 this hangs the engine. The workers log
`No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds`, then EngineCore dies
after the 300 s execute timeout (`TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out`).

## Root cause

`PCPManager.replicated_requests` replicates prefills that cannot fill all `2 * PCP`
chunks (`(2*PCP - 1) * ceil(q / 2*PCP) >= q`), but only when `dcp_world_size > 1`.
#56157 added the rule so that every rank holds the same number of rows per region, which
the PCP+DCP gathered KV layout depends on. PCP-only execution needs the same invariant:

- `_iter_rank_chunks` gives rank `r` chunks `r` and `2*PCP-1-r`, each of size
  `ceil(q / 2*PCP)`. For `q <= PCP - 1`, some ranks get no tokens of the prefill.
- On v0.31.0, `_gather_prefill_cache_inputs` returns early on a rank whose rows are all
  decodes (`num_decode_tokens == local_num_tokens`). That rank skips the PCP all-gather of
  the prefill KV, while the ranks that do hold prefill rows enter it. The collective never
  completes.

On current `main`, #52162 shards decodes across PCP ranks when `DCP == 1`. In that mode,
`_gather_prefill_cache_inputs` all-gathers unconditionally, which hides this particular
hang. The layout is still uneven, though, and the existing decode-sharding branch would
mishandle a replicated prefill: `_iter_rank_chunks` would give it one round-robin owner,
but `_build_batch_layout` only lets rank 0 write a replicated prefill's KV and provide its
hidden states. If the owner were not rank 0, the prefill's KV would not be written and
`hidden_restore_idx` would be left uninitialized for its tokens.

## Fix

- Apply the short-prefill replication rule for every DCP size: a split prefill must give
  every PCP rank both of its chunks, and anything shorter is replicated.
- When decode sharding is enabled, only decodes get a single round-robin owner. A
  replicated prefill runs on every rank, so rank 0 stays its canonical KV writer and
  hidden-state source, which is what `_build_batch_layout` already assumes.

Replicated prefills are short. With PCP=8 the longest is 225 tokens, so the redundant
compute is negligible. Long prefills are split exactly as before.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests in `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py`:
  - `test_pcp_only_short_prefill_gives_every_rank_work`: PCP=8, DCP=1, with and without
    decode sharding, query lengths 1, 2, 7, 15, 16, 17, 31. Each prefill is either
    replicated on every rank, or split with two non-empty chunks per rank that together
    cover the query exactly.
  - `test_pcp_only_long_prefill_is_still_split`: PCP=8, query lengths up to 187,648 keep
    the DualChunkSwap split.
  - `test_sharded_decode_replicates_short_prefill_on_every_rank`: in a mixed
    decode / short-prefill / decode batch with decode sharding, decodes are owned
    round-robin and the prefill is on every rank. Only rank 0's copy is written to the KV
    cache and used for the restored hidden states.
  - `test_dcp_replicates_prefills_too_short_to_split` is renamed to
    `test_replicates_prefills_too_short_to_split` and parametrized over
    `DCP=1` (with and without decode sharding) and `DCP=2`.
  - `test_num_tokens_for_dispatch_uses_largest_pcp_rank`: the `(PCP=4, [2, 9])` case
    expected the old split, in which ranks 0-2 received only one chunk of the 9-token
    prefill. That prefill is now replicated, so the largest rank-local batch is
    `9 + 2 = 11`. A `(PCP=4, [2, 16])` case keeps coverage of a split prefill alongside a
    sharded decode.
- End-to-end on 8x B300 with vLLM 0.31.0, a sparse-MLA model, PCP=8, DCP=1, and LMCache as
  the KV connector. This used the equivalent change for v0.31.0, which has no decode
  sharding, so removing the DCP gate was the whole change there.

## Test Result

Unit tests (macOS, CPU):

```
$ pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py -q
126 passed, 4 skipped, 15 warnings in 12.84s
```

The 4 skipped tests need GPU kernels. Without the fix, 24 of the new or updated cases fail.
With only the DCP gate removed and the decode-sharding branch unchanged, the short
prefill is missing from every rank but one, and the sharded-decode cases fail as well.

GPU, measured on 8x B300 with vLLM 0.31.0 (PCP=8, DCP=1):

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 187,648-token prompt, 187,647 tokens loaded from the KV connector (1-token prefill step) | hang: shm broadcast warnings, then EngineCore dies at the 300 s execute timeout | completes in 4.1 s |
| Needle-in-a-haystack answered from connector-loaded KV | n/a (hang) | 3/3 correct |
| 36-request concurrent burst | n/a | 0 hangs |
| Prefill throughput | 57.3-58.0k tok/s | 57.8k tok/s |

title: [CI] Make (H100) Distributed DP + EP optional
body:
## Overview

Mark `:nvidia: (H100) Distributed DP + EP` (`distributed-tests-8xh100`) as `optional` so it no longer blocks PR builds. Its AMD MI355 mirror is pinned to `optional: false` so it keeps running as before.

## Claims

- PR builds no longer wait on an 8×H100 node for this step.
- Coverage is unchanged for nightly builds and for the MI355 mirror. The H100 step can still be unblocked manually on any PR.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files .buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml` passes, including the step-key and test-tethering hooks.
- I checked the ci-infra pipeline generator (`buildkite/pipeline_generator/buildkite_step.py`):
  - Optional steps are skipped on PRs but still run when `nightly == "1"`.
  - AMD mirrors take `amd.get("optional", step.optional)`, so without the explicit `optional: false` the MI355 mirror would have become optional too.
  - The same override is already used in `.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`.

## Details

This is the only non-optional step in the `ci` pipeline that needs a whole 8-GPU node. Every other 8-GPU step (H200 LM evals, DSv4-Flash disagg, the AMD 8-GPU evals) is already optional. On `mithril-h100-pool`, smaller jobs keep the GPUs on each node split up, so this step can sit in `reserved` for hours. For example, in https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93472 it was the only unfinished job. It became runnable at 01:24 UTC and still had not started at 04:30 UTC.

Tradeoff: PRs touching `vllm/distributed/`, `vllm/config/parallel.py`, etc. no longer get NVIDIA DP+EP (torchrun tp=2/dp=4 with EP) coverage automatically. That coverage comes from the nightly build, from the MI355 mirror on each PR, or from unblocking the step manually.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this step (searched for `distributed-tests-8xh100` and "Distributed DP + EP optional").

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Autotune the sparse indexer's wq_b GEMM
body:
## Overview

Make FlashInfer autotune cover the DeepSeek-V4.1 sparse indexer's `wq_b` GEMM. In the autotune dummy run the indexer took its short-context path, which returns before `wq_b`, so that MXFP8 GEMM was never tuned. The autotune pass now tunes `wq_b` directly; the indexer forward is unchanged.

## Claims

- With `enable_flashinfer_autotune`, the indexer `wq_b` GEMM (K=1280, N=4096 on DSV4.1-Flash) is now tuned for every token bucket.
- Serving no longer hits untuned `mxfp8_gemm` shapes for it, so it no longer falls back to `CuteDSLMxfp8GemmRunner` and JIT-compiles mid-step.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MRV2, MegaMoE + MegaAttention, DSpark K=5, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` graphs to 8190, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, `--kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true,"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'`. Both runs tuned from an empty `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE_DIR` with the same 22 token buckets (1 to 16384), so the entry counts are comparable.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `mxfp8_gemm` entries in the saved autotune cache (per rank) | 110 | 132 |
| ... of which `(1280, 4096)` (indexer `wq_b`) | 0 | 22 |
| `No tuned config covers mxfp8_gemm` warnings in the server log | 35 | 0 |
| ... after the server was ready (during serving) | 3 | 0 |

- main: GB300, DEP2 (TP1 × DP2 + EP2), prefill-only AgentX replay at concurrency 256.
- this PR: GB200, DEP4 (DEP2 does not fit: 150.8 GiB of weights per GPU), `--max-num-seqs 256`, `vllm bench serve` with 256 random prompts (6.2K input tokens on average), all succeeded. Every rank saved the same counts.

The other GEMMs got the same entries in both runs (22 buckets each).

`wq_b` is tuned with a bf16 input, while the forward passes a pre-quantized `QuantizedActivation`. Both reach the same `mm_mxfp8` call with the same shapes, and the forward hit the tuned entries: there was no warning during CUDA graph capture (M from 6 to 8190) or serving.

To reproduce: start the server with FlashInfer autotune on and grep the log for `No tuned config covers mxfp8_gemm input_shapes=((..., 1280), (1280, 4096)`, or check the saved `autotune_configs_*.json` for `(1280, 4096)` entries.

`pre-commit` passes on the changed files. CI does not run this path: it needs SM100 and the DSV4.1 checkpoint. I did not add a unit test, because it needs an MXFP8 `wq_b` on SM100 with FlashInfer.

## Details

The autotune dummy run spreads `max_num_batched_tokens` over up to `max_num_seqs` requests, so each one has only tens of tokens. The indexer then takes its short-context path (`max_seq_len // compress_ratio <= index_topk`) and returns before `wq_b`. CUDA graph capture does run `wq_b` (it skips that path), but capture only reads the autotune cache.

On main, a step that hits an untuned M falls back to `CuteDSLMxfp8GemmRunner` and compiles a kernel for that shape inside `execute_model`. In one run, while another server on the same node was compiling, that step went past `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (300 s). The engine died with a `TimeoutError` in the shm broadcast dequeue, right after logging the `(16376, 1280) x (1280, 4096)` fallback.

`_run_flashinfer_autotune_dummy_runs` now calls `autotune_indexer_wq_b` inside the same `autotune(tuning_buckets=..., round_up=True)` context as the dummy run. It runs every indexer's `wq_b` at the max tuning M with a random bf16 input. FlashInfer keys each config on the op, runner, input shapes and runner extras (output dtype and PDL for `CuteDSLMxfp8GemmRunner`), and skips profiling on a cache hit. So indexers that share a key are tuned once, and any indexer with a different dtype, quantization or backend gets its own entries. On DSV4.1-Flash the 8 indexers share one key, and the autotune pass did not get slower.

Alternatives considered:

- Skip the short-context path in the indexer forward while FlashInfer is tuning (the first version of this PR). It works, but it makes the forward read FlashInfer's global tuner state on every step.
- Give the autotune dummy run a long context (`_dummy_run(context_len=...)`). This changes the autotune pass for every model, exists only in MRV2, and gives every dummy request about `max_model_len` of context, far more than the KV pool can hold.

No other open PR tunes this GEMM.

title: [PoC] Transfer hidden states for P/D
body:
Advantages:
- Avoids most of the N-1 truncation complexity and special case issues that introduces
    - For example related to prompt logprobs
- Avoids redundant computation of last prompt token on D
- Avoids need for MM encoding on D side (cases where we would back-off into image tokens)
    - Which could otherwise impact ITL
    - Can avoid loading mm encoder weights on D for more kv cache capacity
- Preserves target model uniform decode full cuda graphs in multi-module MTP case (which otherwise recompute k-1 prompt tokens)
- Consistency across model/attention types

This implementation stashes the final hidden states (including aux layers and extra positions for eagle3 / multi-module mtp) into kvcache token slots past the end of the prompt. This means:
- Usually zero additional memory or transfer overhead (uses existing block padding)
- Simpler code - we can piggy-back on much of the existing lifecycle logic without needing an additional custom buffer with it's own slot management and nixl registration
- Existing connectors with HMA support need minimal changes

This is tested and working with NIXL, including push/pull and hetero TP. Compatibility with the following will require some additional changes: CP, nixl host-buffer mode, HiSparse. Other P/D connectors also not yet tested.

Thanks to @Dao007forever and @ivanium for help with these ideas.

title: [KVConnector] Run NIXL receive post-process on the block's physical bytes
body:
## Purpose

The NIXL receive post-process helpers in `kv_connector/utils.py` — `kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive`, `kv_postprocess_blksize_on_receive`, `kv_postprocess_blksize_and_layout_on_receive` — assume the tensor they receive is in physical memory order: they `index_select` the received blocks and `reshape` the result as the bytes NIXL wrote. That was true when an NHD cache had shape `[B, N, H, D]`. Since the `KVCacheLayout` refactor (#42082) the connector registers the per-layer views from `create_kv_cache_views`, which are logical `[B, H, N, C]` views whose strides follow the layout. For an NHD (`LBNHC`) decoder, `index_select` therefore produces a copy in logical `(H, N, C)` order, and the helpers reinterpret that copy as physical `(N, H, C)` bytes. The two coincide only when `N == H`, which is why the existing coverage never caught it.

Checked against the current helpers with a block built the way `create_kv_cache_views` builds it (flat buffer + `as_strided` with the layout's strides), `N = 16, H = 4`:

| helper | local layout | current helper correct |
|---|---|---|
| layout (HND bytes → NHD block, `enable_permute_local_kv`) | LBNHC | no |
| blksize (block-size ratio > 1, same layout) | LBHNC | no |
| blksize | LBNHC | no |
| blksize + layout | LBNHC | no |

The blksize helper is wrong for HND as well: it permutes the logical copy and labels `N` as `n_kv_heads`. Separately, the partial-tail zeroing in `post_process_device_kv_on_receive` slices dim 1 of the logical view (heads) as if it were tokens.

This is hit in practice by GQA + linear-attention hybrids under heterogeneous TP (e.g. TP4 prefill, TP1×DP decode). Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B: its 2 KV heads replicate past TP2 while the GatedDeltaNet state keeps sharding, so the hybrid page alignment derives a 272-token attention block at TP4 vs 544 at TP1; FlashAttention takes the scheduler block as its kernel page, so the decoder sees `block_size_ratio = 2` and, being non-MLA, runs the blksize helper and the tail zeroing on every received block. MLA hybrids (Kimi-K3, GLM-5.3-Flash) are unaffected: FlashMLA's fixed 64-token page collapses the ratio to 1 and only the whole-block `index_fill_` runs.

No CI job runs an NHD decoder (`DECODER_KV_LAYOUT` is HND, BLHNC or empty), and the one unit test touching these helpers fed them a physical-order tensor.

### Fix

- The helpers take the `KVCacheLayout` and permute the block dims `(H, N, C)` of the logical view into physical order, keeping blocks on dim 0 (permuting by the full `layer_view_order` would put heads on dim 0 for LHBNC and make `index_select` pick heads by block id). The HND → NHD transposes assert a contiguous NHD block and run their `reshape`/`permute` on the bytes NIXL actually wrote; `index_copy_` writes back through the same physical view. The blksize helper regroups only when a block is one HND run (`layout.is_block_contiguous`: LBHNC, BLHNC); tokens-outer layouts and layouts that register one NIXL region per head (LHBNC) receive their sub-blocks in token order already, so they are left alone.
- `post_process_device_kv_on_receive` passes the layout and zeroes the untransferred token tail along dim 2 of the logical view (`cache[b, :, zero_from:]`), which is correct under every layout.

## Test Plan

New `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_postprocess.py` (CPU): builds a logical view over a flat buffer with the layout's strides, writes HND bytes / back-to-back sub-blocks into one block, runs each helper, and checks the logical view reads the true head/token values for `N != H`, with sentinels on neighbouring blocks; the blksize case is parametrized over LBHNC, BLHNC, LBNHC, BLNHC and LHBNC (per-head runs), plus checks that block ids never address heads on LHBNC and that the layout helpers refuse non-NHD targets and non-contiguous blocks. `test_post_process_zeroes_untransferred_tail` is updated to a logical-shaped cache.

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_postprocess.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py::test_post_process_zeroes_untransferred_tail
```

## Test Result

```
13 passed
```

All four helper cases in the new test fail against the previous helpers (same fixtures, old `utils.py`). Not covered here: an end-to-end NHD-decoder run in the disaggregated accuracy sweep, which would be the right regression test to add.

title: External speculators (DSpark Qwen3 draft, DFlash2) crash with kv_cache_dtype=nvfp4_ds_mla on GLM-5.3 NVFP4: draft-model code assumes split k/v
body:
Title: External speculators (DSpark Qwen3 draft, DFlash2) crash with kv_cache_dtype=nvfp4_ds_mla on GLM-5.3 NVFP4: draft-model code assumes split k/v

**Environment**: vLLM v0.31.0, GLM-5.3 NVFP4 (GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM), 8x B200, TP4/TP8 P/D (NixlConnector), --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla --block-size 64. With #58744 backported (nvfp4 chunked-context gather fix, without it warmup never finishes).

**Case 1, DSpark draft** (RedHatAI GLM-5.3-speculator.dspark, DSparkDraftModel):
```
vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py:2665 do_kv_cache_update
k_cache, v_cache = kv_cache.transpose(1,2).split(...)
ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)
```

**Case 2, DFlash2 draft** (modal-labs/GLM-5.3-NVFP4-DFlash, DFlash2DraftModel), reproduced with both the default backend selection AND --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE (verified in logs: "Using AttentionBackendEnum.FLASHMLA_SPARSE backend"):
```
vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash/cudagraph.py:118
vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py:169,:325
vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py:851 precompute_and_store_c
vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py:711 precompute_a...
vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py:2665 do_kv_cache_update
ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)
```
The DFlash2 precompute path hardcodes the flashinfer attention wrapper, which unpacks a split (k, v) layout; with nvfp4_ds_mla the target KV is a single fused tensor. The #58744 E2E report used an fp8 KV variant; nvfp4_ds_mla appears untested with both drafters.

**Ask**: speculator/draft-model code paths need nvfp4_ds_mla-fused-layout awareness, likely via the same upconvert kernel routing #58744 added, or #59342 (native nvfp4 sparse decode). Both drafters are unusable with NVFP4 KV on 0.31 stock + #58744.

title: [Bugfix][Anthropic] Preserve inline system messages for native encoders
body:
## Overview

Preserve mid-conversation `system` messages in `/v1/messages` for native
encoders (DeepSeek V4.1) instead of hoisting them into the leading system
prompt when `--chat-template` is omitted. Fixes #60537.

## Claims

- `deepseek_v41` deployments without `--chat-template` no longer merge
  inline system messages; prompt prefixes stay stable across turns.
- Fallback preserved: renderers without native support still merge
  (conservative default unchanged).

## Validation

- Issue repro on current code: `Default True` (wrong) / `Official False`;
  the `True` comes from probing the missing CLI override instead of the
  encoder's capabilities.
- New tests: `test_native_encoder_without_cli_template_preserves` and
  `test_no_marker_without_template_still_merges`.
- Commands run:
  - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py -q` → **107 passed**
  - `pre-commit run --files vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v41.py vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py` → all hooks passed (ruff, mypy, test-tethering, config-defaults).
- Duplicate checks: no open PR references #60537; complements merged
  #58754 (HF-renderer path) and is narrower than stalled draft #58772
  (full preserve/fold redesign).

## Details

Root cause: `DeepseekV4Renderer` extends `BaseRenderer`, not `HfRenderer`
(`vllm/renderers/deepseek_v4.py:24`), so `_should_merge_inline_system`
(`vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py:243`) probed only the CLI
`chat_template` (`None` when unset) and `_detect_merge_inline_system(None)`
returned `True`. The registry maps both `deepseek_v4` and `deepseek_v41`
to the shared renderer class, so renderer type alone cannot distinguish
them — the fix reads a `supports_inline_system_messages` capability flag
from the tokenizer (set by the V4.1 wrapper, whose Python
`encode_messages` renders mid-conversation systems in place per
`deepseek_v41_encoding.py:297`). Absent flag → current behavior.
`getattr(..., False) is True` keeps the check safe against mock
tokenizers in existing tests.

title: [Performance][NIXL] BLHNC MLA caches lost whole-row registration in #53781 and now need more NIXL descriptors than LBHNC
body:
## Your current environment
- GLM-5.3 (78 MLA + 21 indexer layers) with a DFlash2 draft (6 layers, GQA, 8 KV heads, fp8 KV, k=4).
- Prefill DEP8 (TP1 per rank). Decode TP4. Pull-mode `NixlConnector`, GPU-resident KV (no host buffer).
- vLLM main @ `4e0a414c44`, plus #58471 (GQA draft head slicing under an MLA target), the NVFP4
  prefill-context gather from #58744, and our NVFP4 KV decode path (`nvfp4_ds_mla` on
  `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, #59342).
- GB200 NVL72 (NIXL over NVLink), and B300 HGX (NIXL over RDMA).

## Describe the issue

### 1. Whole-row transfer is unreachable for page-contiguous BLHNC MLA caches
#53781 (HiSparse host-resident hot-buffering) put `not page_contiguous` in front of the
"packed MLA layouts transfer the complete storage row" branch of
`NixlConnectorWorker.register_kv_caches`:

```python
# before #53781
elif storage_is_block_major and (
    (packed_storage and is_mla_region)
    or (not hnc_contiguous and not self._is_csa_linear)
):
# after #53781
elif storage_is_block_major and (
    not page_contiguous
    and ((packed_storage and is_mla_region) or not self._is_csa_linear)
):
```

The gate is needed so a HiSparse decoder can land host-resident and device-only layers separately.
But `page_contiguous` is true for every GLM-5.3 layer, so a device-resident BLHNC cache registers one
region per layer. Every transfer then carries one descriptor per layer per block, and BLHNC
ends up costing more than LBHNC, the opposite of its purpose.

Registration on one GB200 decode rank, from the `prepared N descriptors into M strides` log line:

| layout | strides | descriptors |
|---|---:|---:|
| LBHNC, block 1024 | 62 | 2,488,080 |
| BLHNC, block 64, current main | 104 | 2,714,816 |
| BLHNC, block 64, whole row | 1 | 26,104 |

End to end, the whole-row run looked like this. GB200 runs: DEP8 prefill → 10× TP4 decode;
AgentX agentic traffic, 128 concurrent sessions, 1800 s per arm; 29,088 transfers.

| | LBHNC bs1024 | BLHNC bs64, whole row |
|---|---:|---:|
| NIXL xfer, mean | 85.23 ms | 22.30 ms |
| NIXL post, mean | 57.88 ms | 6.96 ms |
| TTFT p50 | 848 ms | 730 ms |

With fp8 KV on GB200 (DEP8 prefill → 1×TP8 decode, 32 sessions), current main's BLHNC took
2.0–3.6 s per transfer. Restoring the pre-#53781 gate brought that to 78 ms, against 146 ms for
LBHNC.

### 2. A naive re-enable misregisters a head-sharded draft
Under BLHNC, every KV cache group starts at byte 0 of the shared block row, so the first draft page
has the same base address as the first target page. Regions are deduplicated by base address.
So if the draft also takes the whole-row branch, it folds into the target's single replicated
region. Then #58471's per-rank head slice never runs, and each TP4 rank receives the TP1 prefill's
8-head draft pages unsliced. We shipped exactly that by narrowing the gate to
`(not page_contiguous or not self.use_host_buffer)`.

The same aliasing folds draft layer 0 into a target region even without whole-row: 104 strides
for 105 layers. That is #57661, fixed by #57662's `(base_addr, block_len)` key.

## Proposal (PR to follow, stacked on #58471 and #57662)
- Opt-in `kv_connector_extra_config.whole_row_regions` (default false).
- Replicated (MLA) layers of a block-major row register as one whole-row region.
- Head-sharded layers (a GQA draft under an MLA target) keep per-layer SPLIT regions, so each rank
  reads its own head slice.
- The flag is rejected with `kv_buffer_device=cpu` and with HiSparse host-resident groups, so
  #53781's case is untouched.
- With `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`, BLHNC packs the head-sharded draft pages inside the
  target's block row. Their size depends on TP, so a whole-row region would differ between a TP1
  prefill and a TP4 decode (2,721,312 vs 2,131,360 bytes; the handshake asserts). The flag must reject
  that layout at registration with a clear error.

Open question for maintainers: should this be opt-in, or automatic whenever no group is
host-resident?

## Not this issue: DFlash2 acceptance under BLHNC
BLHNC deployments with a DFlash2 draft also lose about 5.5 points of draft acceptance. That loss is
tracked in #60560. It comes from the hybrid KV cache manager turning the sliding-window draft into a
real SWA group, not from NIXL registration: the corrected registration proposed here (B300, 34.18%)
loses as much as the misregistration described above (GB200, 34.8%).

## Before submitting a new issue...
- [x] Searched open issues and PRs: #57661, #57662, #50717, #58471, #59586, #60368.
  - Related: #60560 (DFlash2 acceptance under BLHNC + HMA).

AI assistance (Claude) was used to analyze logs and draft this issue. A human reviewed and edited
every line.

title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Opt-in whole-row regions for replicated BLHNC layers
body:
> **Stacked on #58471 and #57662 (both open).** This branch carries their commits. Only the last three commits belong to this PR (+328/−19 across `base_worker.py`, `test_nixl_connector.py` and the connector docs):
> - `57978684fc`: opt-in whole-row regions;
> - `edb4a3c77b`: reject draft pages packed into the target row;
> - `9adc138cfc`: let the test fake take a mixed-spec group.
>
> Reviewing #57662 and #58471 first will shrink this diff to those three commits.

## Purpose

Fixes #60561.

Since #53781, a device-resident BLHNC MLA cache registers one NIXL region per layer, because `page_contiguous` is true for every layer. For GLM-5.3 that is 99 descriptors per block instead of one, so BLHNC transfers cost more than LBHNC's (104 vs 62 strides on a decode rank).

This PR adds `kv_connector_extra_config.whole_row_regions` (default `false`):
- **Replicated (MLA) layers** of a block-major row register as one whole-row region, as they did before #53781. The row length is the block stride, as on `main`.
- **Head-sharded layers** (a GQA draft under an MLA target) never take the whole-row branch. They keep per-layer SPLIT regions, so each TP rank reads its own head slice (#58471).
- **Non-MLA models** are unaffected; the flag only changes MLA regions.
- **Rejected configurations.** The flag errors out at registration for:
  - `kv_buffer_device=cpu`;
  - HiSparse host-resident groups, so #53781's case keeps its current behaviour;
  - a layout that packs head-sharded draft pages into the target's group and row. This is BLHNC with `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`. The row's size depends on TP there, so prefill and decode rows would differ, and without the check this only failed later as a handshake assert.

**Why #57662 is needed.** Under BLHNC every KV cache group starts at byte 0 of the shared row, so the first draft page aliases the first target page's base address. Without #57662's `(base_addr, block_len)` key, the draft region folds into a target region. The rebase keeps `main`'s rule that a packed PP producer never dedups aliased regions.

**Not a duplicate:**
- #57662 fixes only the dedup key.
- #59586 splits MLA kernel rows larger than the NIXL block into dense pages. That changes per-layer page geometry; it does not register one region per block row.
- #50717 preserves packed-MLA block geometry.
- #60368 simplifies #58471's head slicing.

None of them restores whole-row registration for page-contiguous caches in pull mode.

**Separate issue:** the DFlash2 acceptance drop seen on BLHNC deployments (#60560) does not come from NIXL registration. It comes from the hybrid KV cache manager's sliding-window draft group, and is fixed by #60767. This PR neither causes nor fixes it.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_tp_mapping.py
```

New tests:
- `test_blhnc_gqa_draft_reads_own_head_slice_from_tp1_prefill`, parametrized over `whole_row` in {False, True} and `tp_rank` in {0, 3}. A TP1 prefill and a TP4 decode each register a BLHNC MLA target plus a GQA draft. With whole-row on, the target row must be one region. Every draft layer must be its own region and read its own head slice.
- `test_whole_row_regions_rejects_host_buffer`.
- `test_whole_row_regions_rejects_draft_packed_into_target_row`.

End to end: GLM-5.3 (NVFP4) with a DFlash2 draft on 2× B300, DEP8 prefill to 2× TP4 decode over NIXL (RDMA), BLHNC block size 64, `whole_row_regions` on both roles, agentic multi-turn traffic (AgentX) at 32 concurrent sessions.

## Test Result

**Unit tests.** One B300 GPU, `test_nixl_connector.py`, `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py` and `test_tp_mapping.py`. Each tree was built with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1` on the kernels of nightly `51ef239768`.
- **`main` (`81d9c45e4b`):** 424 passed, 2 failed.
- **#58471 rebased:** 438 passed, 2 failed.
- **This PR's head:** 445 passed, 2 failed.
- **Same two failures everywhere.** `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[None]` and `[ray]` start a real engine that wants 50% of GPU memory, and only 17.6 of 268 GiB were free on the shared GPU. No failures are introduced by this PR.
- **New tests** (`-k "blhnc_gqa_draft or whole_row_regions"`): 6 of 6 pass.
- **Lint:** ruff and mypy pass on the changed files.

**End to end, with this PR's code.** These are from the B300 runs above. The NIXL connector's own metrics are summed over the profiling window of each run (~5,700 transfers each):

| BLHNC, block 64 | regions | descriptors / transfer | descriptors / MB | transfer time / GB |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `whole_row_regions` on (4 runs) | target row: 1; draft: per layer | 1,309 – 1,860 | **0.48 – 0.54** | 48 – 69 ms |
| per-layer regions | 1 per layer | 46,692 | **49.3** | 77 ms |

The per-layer row ran with `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`, which changes what is transferred (decode prefix hits rise and less KV is pulled), so its transfer time is indicative only. The descriptor reduction is the direct effect of this PR.

**Earlier variant, for context.** On GB200 (128 sessions), a predecessor of this change produced:
- **Registration:** 1 stride / 26,104 descriptors on a decode rank, vs 62 / 2,488,080 with LBHNC block 1024.
- **Transfer time:** mean NIXL transfer time 85.23 → 22.30 ms.
- **TTFT:** p50 848 → 730 ms.

That predecessor also folded the head-sharded draft into the whole-row region, which this PR deliberately avoids, so these are not this PR's numbers. The target's registration is the same; this PR adds the draft's per-layer regions on top.

**Not covered:** push mode (`main`'s packed-MLA push path is unchanged) and non-MLA models (the flag does nothing there).

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write the code, tests and this description, and to run and analyze the experiments. @stu-cao reviewed the change and is responsible for it.

title: [MRV2][Perf] Screened lm_head
body:
## Purpose

Opt-in `--screened-lm-head`: when sampling only reads the top-k logits (greedy, or temperature with top-k <= 32 and optional top-p, e.g. Qwen's default `temperature=1.0, top_k=20, top_p=0.95`), compute them from an FP8 screen of the lm_head plus exact logits for the few rows the screen cannot rule out. Same tokens for the same seed, about half the lm_head bytes. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on DGX Spark: +7.7% decode greedy, +6.2% at Qwen's default sampling (c=1, no speculative decoding).

- An FP8 copy of the lm_head scores every row, with a rigorous per-row error bound (FP8 error plus fp32 accumulation error of both GEMMs, computed in fp64 at load).
- A row more than one output ulp below the k-th best lower bound can neither enter nor tie the full head's top k. The rest (greedy: 15 rows per token on Flash-Next, top-20: about 1,200) get exact BF16 logits, the others `-inf`.
- Three Triton kernels, no host sync. Other batches (logprobs, penalties, logit bias, min-p, structured outputs, top-k > 32) use the full head. Unsupported setups (quantized or TP-sharded lm_head, LoRA, custom samplers, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, pre-SM89) raise at load.

**Scope:** the gain needs the lm_head to be a large share of the step (DGX Spark, Jetson Thor, RTX). On GB200/GB300 it is neutral to slightly negative, so it is opt-in.

## Results

Flash-Next NVFP4, SPEED-Bench (11 domains, 352 prompts, 256 tokens), same-node stock/screened pairs, both arm orders:

```
GPU     sampling          config         c=1             c=4             GSM8K stock / ours
GB10    greedy            plain decode   +8.0% / +7.4%   +5.9% / +5.8%   98.5 / 98.5
GB10    greedy            MTP k=3        +3.9% / +3.1%   +2.9% / +2.4%   98.0 / 98.5
GB10    T=1, k=20, p=.95  plain decode   +6.7% / +5.7%   +4.4% / +3.9%   98.0 / 97.0
GB10    T=1, k=20, p=.95  MTP k=3        +3.1% / +1.9%   +3.9% / +2.3%   97.5 / 98.5
GB200   greedy            plain decode   -0.4% / -2.0%   +0.4% / +0.8%   98.5 / 97.5
GB200   greedy            MTP k=3        +1.3% / -0.8%   +0.4% / -3.2%   98.0 / 98.0
GB300   greedy            plain decode   -1.6% / -1.5%   -1.2% / -3.0%   98.5 / 97.5
GB300   greedy            MTP k=3        -0.7% / +0.6%   -2.7% / +1.0%   98.5 / 98.5
```

lm_head alone on GB10 (248320 x 2560, CUDA graphs): full BF16 5.4 to 7.3 ms; screened -62% at 1 token, -46% (greedy) / -43% (top-20) at 16 to 28 tokens. On GB200 the screen reaches 3.6 TB/s against 7.1 TB/s for the BF16 GEMM.

Exactness (both heads on the same hidden states):
- Offline, 10,572 real Flash-Next rows at batch widths 1 to 64 plus 1,024 adversarial near-ties: 0 argmax mismatches; for top-20, 0 true top-20 rows screened out.
- Live, 1.36M greedy and 353k sampled rows: 0 true top-k rows screened out. 12 greedy argmax flips, all sub-ulp ties on a BF16 rounding midpoint where the screened value was the correctly rounded one.
- Kept logits differ from cuBLAS in 0.047% of entries, 99% of those by one BF16 ulp (summation order), as with any GEMM change.
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_screened_head.py`: 21 passed on GB10 and GB200.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code --quantization modelopt_mixed --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' --cpu-offload-gb 0 --linear-backend auto \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass --mamba-cache-mode none --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --block-size 16 --kv-cache-memory-bytes 7G --max-model-len 49152 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --language-model-only --gpu-memory-utilization 0.87 \
  --compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"fuse_act_quant":true},"max_cudagraph_capture_size":32}' \
  [--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"moe_backend":"marlin"}' \
   --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers 48] \
  --screened-lm-head   # omitted in the stock arm
# Requests: seed 1234, greedy or {"temperature": 1.0, "top_k": 20, "top_p": 0.95}.
pytest -v tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_screened_head.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker_weight_transfer.py
```

</details>

## Details

- Not the platform W8A16 kernels: the bound needs the screen's own arithmetic (fp32 accumulation of the stored FP8 values) fused with per-block maxima. A rank-256 SVD bound rules out almost nothing (flat spectrum); a fused select+exact kernel was 2% to 9% slower.
- Weight updates (`reload_weights`, weight transfer including draft updates) rebuild the FP8 copy; it lives in the weights memory pool for sleep mode.
- Memory: an FP8 copy of the lm_head (+0.64 GB on Flash-Next) plus `min(max_num_seqs * (k + 1), 64) x vocab x 8` bytes, allocated at load.
- Stock Flash-Next is not deterministic run to run on this stack (32/352 identical texts between two stock runs), hence exactness on shared hidden states rather than output texts.

Not a duplicate: #55494 packs the BF16 lm_head losslessly (0.77x bytes) for single-token decode and any sampling; this reads about 0.5x for greedy and top-k sampling and covers spec-decode verify widths.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write and test this change; I reviewed every line and ran the tests and benchmarks above.
