title: [Kernel][ROCm] qwen4_exp: fused HyperConnection combine+mix for gfx1100 decode
body:
## Overview

**Depends on #60650** (serve the AMD qwen4_exp path in fp16): this kernel is fp16-only, and without #60650 the model cannot run in fp16 on ROCm. This branch is stacked on it; the first two commits are #60650, only the last one is this PR. Draft until #60650 lands.

Fused HIP kernels for `GatedResidual.combine_and_mix` (qwen4_exp HyperConnection) on gfx1100 decode: the five-kernel chain becomes two kernels for 1-4 tokens. +5.8% decode tok/s for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on 4x RX 7900 XTX.

Related: #59442 targets the same boundary on CDNA (MI355X) through an AITER FlyDSL kernel, opt-in and waiting on ROCm/aiter#5913. AITER does not run on RDNA3, so the two do not overlap: this path is gated on gfx1x and on the kernel being built (`VLLM_ROCM_GFX1100`), and leaves the ROCm fallback untouched.

## Claims

- Decode, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, TP4 on 4x RX 7900 XTX, fp16 KV cache, no spec decode, one user: **72.5 -> 76.6 tok/s (+5.8%)**.
- HyperConnection time per decode step (96 calls, cold weights, CUDA graph): **2.85 -> 2.18 ms** at 1 token, 3.36 -> 2.87 ms at 4 tokens.
- Same output as the unfused chain within fp16 rounding; deterministic (fixed-order reduction, no split-K atomics).

## Validation

**Correctness**: `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_hc_ops_amd.py` (new, wired into the AMD Qwen4 Exp Buildkite job) compares `hc_combine_and_mix` against an fp32 reference with the module's fp16 roundings, for 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8 tokens (fused, fused-after-Triton-norm and unfused paths), shared and per-stream norm weights, and a strided injection (the first layer's injection is a `split()` view). Plus 20 repeated calls compared bit for bit.

```
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_hc_ops_amd.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_amd.py   # 32 passed (gfx1100)
```

**Serving on `main` + #60650 + this PR** (RX 7900 XTX, TP1, eager, in-process so the op calls can be counted): a 4-layer Flash-Next config with random weights (`--load-format dummy`, 64 experts), `--dtype float16`, 16 tokens per request at 1, 2 and 3 concurrent requests. All three dispatch branches run while serving:

```
qwen4_hc_combine_mix  1 token : 90 calls
qwen4_hc_combine_mix  2 tokens: 90 calls
qwen4_hc_mix_xn       3 tokens: 90 calls
```

**Microbenchmark** (RX 7900 XTX, 96 distinct layers so the 13 MB per call come from DRAM, one CUDA graph, median of 15 replays):

| tokens | unfused | fused | speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 2.852 ms | 2.181 ms | 1.31x |
| 2 | 3.109 ms | 2.399 ms | 1.30x |
| 3 | 3.192 ms | 2.731 ms | 1.17x |
| 4 | 3.358 ms | 2.869 ms | 1.17x |

**End to end**: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next pruned to 256 experts, GPTQ W4A16 (asymmetric, group 32), fp16, TP4 on 4x RX 7900 XTX, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, `--max-model-len 262144`, no spec decode. One request at a time, 512 output tokens, temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95; two server launches per arm in alternating order, five requests per launch:

| arm | launch 1 (medians) | launch 2 (medians) | tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| unfused | 71.9 72.6 72.4 72.7 72.5 | 71.5 72.5 72.5 72.7 72.6 | 72.5 |
| fused | 76.7 76.9 77.1 77.0 76.6 | 75.8 76.4 76.4 76.6 76.4 | 76.6 |

GSM8K (chat, no thinking, 200 questions, 4 concurrent, MTP k=3 on): 96.0% with the kernel, 95.0% without (same branch, within run-to-run noise at n=200).

The end-to-end numbers come from a branch that also carries other RDNA3 changes needed to serve this checkpoint (asymmetric W4A16 MoE, NF4 n-gram table), identical in both arms; the arms differ only in this kernel.

## Details

The unfused chain is combine+RMSNorm (Triton), the merged down+inject GEMM `[336, 10240]`, SiLU, the up GEMM `[10240, 320]` and the gate mix: five launches, 96 times per decode step, over 13 MB of weights that every TP rank holds in full (the HC weights are replicated). At decode sizes it is latency-bound.

- **Down kernel** (81 blocks): each block owns 4 rows of the down weight over the whole K, so the dot products need no split-K partials: the per-wave sums meet in a fixed-order LDS reduction, which keeps the op deterministic. The weights are requested first and the combine + RMSNorm overlaps with their arrival; the RMS of each stream is two waves exchanging sums through LDS. It writes the new residual, the normalized input, SiLU(lora) and the injection logits.
- **Up kernel** (80 blocks): the up GEMM and the gate mix in registers; lane reductions use DPP `row_xmask` and `v_permlanex16`.
- **Dispatch** inside the custom op (opaque to torch.compile, so the token count is a runtime value, not a trace-time one): 1-2 tokens take both kernels; 3-4 keep the Triton combine+norm and run the fused mix from its output (measured at 4 tokens: 2.82 ms against 2.91 ms for the full fusion; at 1 token the full fusion wins, 2.21 against 2.43 ms); 5+ keep the unfused chain, which is faster from 5 tokens on.
- Shapes are compile-time constants (hc_count 4, hidden 2560, lora rank 320, the only config using this path today); any other shape, dtype or non-contiguous weight falls back to the unfused chain.
- No spills (`.vgpr_spill_count` 0 for all template instances; 136-183 VGPRs).

**Tradeoffs and limitations**

- A persistent single-kernel variant (grid barrier between the halves) measured 78.4 tok/s, but it needs all 81 blocks co-resident, which occupancy predicts and nothing guarantees at launch; a cooperative launch guarantees it and captures in a graph on ROCm, but costs 21 us per launch against 4 us. Two kernels are kept.
- gfx1100 only (`VLLM_ROCM_GFX1100`); other ROCm targets and CUDA are unchanged.
- Prefill keeps the unfused path.

title: [Model] Apply Transformers checkpoint renamings during weight loading
body:
## Overview

Apply the weight renamings Transformers uses for each checkpoint (`transformers.conversion_mapping`) during weight loading, and update models so they no longer hand-map legacy checkpoint names. Supersedes #60131: GLM-5.3-Flash now uses the Transformers module names, so PEFT adapters trained with Transformers resolve without special-casing.

## Claims

- `get_checkpoint_renaming_mapper` builds the Transformers model on the meta device and takes the `WeightRenaming`s from `get_model_conversion_mapping`, so sub-model renamings are scoped exactly as in Transformers. `WeightConverter`s are skipped because vLLM fuses weights itself.
  - Renamings depend only on the `model_type`, even for custom code configs, because vLLM runs its own implementation either way.
  - vLLM's own config classes are converted to the native Transformers config class first. If the model still can't be built, the unscoped renamings of the `model_type` are used.
  - Regex quantization targets (`re:...`) are rewritten with the same renamings (`WeightsMapper.map_regex`), so e.g. Laguna NVFP4's `re:.*shared_expert\.(...)$` still matches the renamed `shared_experts`.
- The renamings are applied once, to the checkpoint weights, in `DefaultModelLoader` and `RunaiModelStreamerLoader`, so `hf_to_vllm_mapper` only has to map from current Transformers names.
  - LoRA, quantization configs and the `--mm-encoder-only` shard filter use the renamings followed by the model's mapper.
  - Drafts loaded from the target's checkpoint (MTP, DSpark) use the target's renamings.
  - The Transformers modeling backend no longer collects the renamings itself.
- Model updates. Every registered example checkpoint whose names Transformers renames was checked: ~80 architectures, ~70 of them native vLLM models.
  - **Renamed to the Transformers names:**
    - Mixtral, MiniMax-M2, MiniMax-M3, PhiMoE: `block_sparse_moe` -> `mlp`
    - Laguna: `shared_expert` -> `shared_experts`, gate bias
    - DeepSeek-V4: all backends + MTP/DSpark/VL
    - GLM-5.3-Flash: `forget_gate`, `attn_hc`/`ffn_hc`
    - MiMo-V2: `sinks`
    - CohereASR, DeepSeek-OCR-2, Step-VL encoder
    - GTE/Nomic-BERT, Inkling, HY-V3, HY-V4 (attention), Exaone-MoE
  - **Mapping from the new names:** VLM container prefixes (`model.language_model.` etc.) for the llava family, Granite-4-Vision, PaliGemma, Gemma3, Cohere2-Vision, LFM2-VL, Aria, ColPali, Qianfan-OCR, HyperCLOVAX, Kimi-K2.5, PaddleOCR-VL, Step-3.7, Qwen2-VL/2.5-VL, Qwen3.5 and the Qwen2-Audio family (AudioFlamingo3, GLM-ASR, Granite Speech). Also Granite MoE, Ernie-4.5, HRM, Gemma4-Unified, Cosmos3, Cosmos3-Edge, AXK1.
  - **Manual mappings removed:** legacy checkpoint names now covered, e.g. Qwen2-VL's `model.` -> `language_model.model.`, Bert's `LayerNorm.gamma/beta`, Aria's original-checkpoint entries, HY-V3 router names, Granite MoE suffixes, Cosmos3 flat-layout regexes, DeepSeek-V4 `head`/`embed`/`.ffn.gate.bias`.

## Validation

**Load check:** each affected model was built on the meta device with 2 decoder layers, and its real `load_weights` was fed meta tensors shaped like the real checkpoint (from the Hub safetensors headers). On the shared checker, the branch is never worse than `main` (88 architecture/checkpoint pairs):

| Result | Pairs |
|---|---|
| Same params loaded, same missing set as `main` | 54 |
| Same harness error on `main` and branch (FP8/NVFP4 kernels on CPU, per-layer config lists not truncated, tokenizer/processor needed, Mistral-format-only models) | 34 |

The models in the second row were re-checked with per-model checker variants that work around the harness limits. On those, the branch also loads the same params as `main` (DeepSeek-V4 + MTP/DSpark/VL, HY-V4, GLM-5.3-Flash, Kimi-K2.5, Laguna NVFP4, Step-3.7 + MTP, Inkling, Mistral-format models). A few models load more on the branch than on `main`:
- HyperCLOVAX: errors on `main`.
- Step-3.7 MTP: errors on `main`.
- Laguna and Exaone-MoE: `main` silently drops `e_score_correction_bias`.

On Laguna NVFP4 the renamed `shared_experts` linears get the same `CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4` scheme as on `main`.

**LoRA (GLM-5.3-Flash):** `...self_attn.forget_gate.f_b_proj.lora_A.weight` and the flat `...self_attn.f_b_proj...` both resolve to the existing `...self_attn.forget_gate.f_b_proj` module. On `main`, the `forget_gate` name matches no module (#60131).

**Tests (CPU):**
- `tests/models/test_utils.py`, `tests/models/multimodal/test_mapping.py`, `tests/models/multimodal/test_aria.py`, `tests/models/multimodal/test_cohere_asr.py`, `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_mm_encoder_only_weight_filter.py`, `tests/models/test_adapters.py`, `tests/models/inkling`, `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_weight_loading.py` and `tests/quantization/test_humming_ignore.py`: all pass.
- `test_pooling_prefix_probe_uses_hf_to_vllm_mapper` fails only when run after `tests/model_executor/test_paddleocr_vl_mrope.py`, the same as on `main` (test isolation).
- `tests/lora/test_utils.py` errors on missing `ray`, the same on `main`.
- `test_hf_model_weights_mapper` now runs for every native multimodal architecture. It was effectively disabled under Transformers v5, because it filtered on `_checkpoint_conversion_mapping`.

TODO before ready for review: GPU evals for a sample of the renamed models (Mixtral, Qwen2.5-VL, llava, DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3-Flash).

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_utils.py -k checkpoint_renaming
pytest tests/models/multimodal/test_mapping.py
```

## Details

- **Limitations:** the bitsandbytes, GGUF and tensorizer loaders do not apply the renamings.
- **Non-idempotent renamings:** a few Transformers renamings are not idempotent (AXK1, MiniMax-M3 `e_score_correction_bias`). Loading applies them once. Adapters or reloaded weights that already use the new names may be renamed twice.
- **Regex quant targets:** `map_regex` only applies renamings between plain names. It replaces whole segments, and may skip the shared leading segments only after a `.*`/`.+` wildcard. Regex renamings and complex quant patterns are left unchanged.
- **Follow-ups that still map back to existing vLLM names.** These modules are shared with models Transformers doesn't rename, or would need kernel rework:
  - CLIP/SigLIP `vision_model`
  - HY-V4 hyper-connections (`hpc_ihc.py`)
  - MiniMax-M3 indexer and DeepSeek-V4 indexer nesting
  - Qianfan-OCR's InternViT
  - Kimi vision tower and Kimi-Linear MoE/KDA (shared with Kimi-K3)
  - DeepSeek-OCR SAM encoder (shared with OCR v1)
  - Step-3.5 MoE names (shared with Step-3.5-Flash)
  - VLM language-model containers (`language_model.model` vs `model.language_model`)
- **f_a_proj LoRA:** LoRA on GLM-5.3-Flash `f_a_proj` (fused in `in_proj_qkvbfg_a`) is still unsupported, as on `main`.

title: [ROCm][Perf][Kimi-K3] Specialized decode for Kimi-K3 on MI355X
body:
## Purpose

An opt-in specialized decode for Kimi-K3 on MI355X (gfx950), TP8, following RFC #60904. It uses the same `specialized_decode` shape as #61867 (Kimi-K3, NVIDIA) and #60889 (GLM-5.2, ROCm), in layer mode. It is enabled with `additional_config={"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}` and has no other options.

A pure spec-verify decode step of at most 8 rows runs each MoE decoder layer as persistent FlyDSL MonoKernels. The TP all-reduces run in-kernel over peer memory:

- **Whole layers** (68 KDA layers): K1 (AttnRes, in_proj, f_b, spec conv, KDA recurrence, gated RMSNorm), then K2.
- **FFN layers** (24 MLA layers): vLLM's AttnRes and MLA up to o_proj's input, then K2.
- **K2**: o_proj + all-reduce + MLP AttnRes, then the latent MoE (router, top-16 MXFP4 experts, shared experts, latent all-reduce + RMSNorm, up_proj, final all-reduce).

The kernels read vLLM's loaded weights and KDA states in place. Every other step (prefill, mixed, wider and PIECEWISE steps) runs vLLM's layers. With `decode_backend=auto` (the default) nothing changes.

### Layout: no common code

```text
vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/specialized_decode/
    README.md        supported deployments, refusals, steps, fail-stop
    hooks.py         SpecializedDecodeMixin: the model-side hooks
    model_state.py   KimiK3ModelState: builds the executor after load, binds KV caches
    runtime/
        __init__.py  DecodeConfig, specialized_decode_config(), unsupported()
        decode.py    SpecializedDecode: plan() -> Step, Step.layer(i), prepare_kv(), after_step()
        guards.py    weight / KV cache refusals, fail-stop
        layers.py    layer kernels: vLLM tensors -> launches
        runner.py    per-rank launch state;  peer.py  peer memory, TP agreement
    mono/            kernel source (K1, K2, MoE stages, device primitives)
tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode/
```

The existing Kimi-K3 files only call into the folder (26 added lines):
- `linear.py`: `specialized_decode_config()` in `__init__` before any module allocates weights, `plan_specialized_decode()` in `forward`, `(step.layer(i) or layer)(...)` in the layer loop, and `after_specialized_decode_step()` in `compute_logits`.
- `model.py`: `get_model_state_cls`.
- `mla.py`: `skip_o_proj`, which returns o_proj's input for the MLA layers' K2.

Outside `vllm/models/kimi_k3/` the only change is one Buildkite step.

### Refusal and steps

- **Refusal.** An unsupported deployment fails at startup with one `ValueError` that lists every reason. Refusals run in three stages: the config in `__init__`, the loaded weights when the model state builds the executor, and the KV caches at every bind. Every TP rank agrees on each verdict. It is default-deny for PP/DP/EP/EPLB/PCP, DBO, LoRA, KV connectors, routed-expert capture, sleep mode, CPU offload, weight updates, adaptive or dynamic speculative decoding, ReplaySSM/RecoverSSM, the V1 runner, `STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE`, other model shapes, and other GPUs or partitioned GPUs.
- **Steps.** `plan()` runs once per step. It picks the kernels for pure spec-verify steps of whole uniform requests at a built width, i.e. multiples of `k+1` up to 8 rows.
- **CUDA graphs.** vLLM's capture sizes are not changed. Under FULL graphs the plan is baked in at capture. A replay with fewer requests than its graph pads whole requests (null state slot, one accepted token), and the kernels serve those like real ones.

### Fail-stop

Every in-kernel wait gives up after 10 s. The rank records it in its sticky health words, so a stalled peer fails every rank instead of hanging them. In `compute_logits` each rank queues a non-blocking copy of its `FAILED` word. Every 16 steps the TP ranks agree on what has landed over the TP CPU group, and then every rank raises at the same step. This keeps all ranks out of the next collective.

Detection takes up to about 16 steps. A zero-delay check through a core hook can follow in a separate PR.

## Not a duplicate

- #61867 is Kimi-K3 on NVIDIA (CuTeDSL, SM100); this is the ROCm/FlyDSL counterpart under `kimi_k3/amd/`.
- #60397, #60889, #61482 and #60731 target other models (DeepSeek-V4.x, GLM-5.2), with different attention, residual and MoE.
- #61311 proposes shared abstractions. This PR keeps its runtime per model, as #61867 and #60889 do, and can move onto shared helpers once those land.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/models/kimi_k3          # 8x MI355X; includes amd_specialized_decode/
pre-commit run --files <changed files>     # incl. mypy
```

- **CPU:** the switch (auto / unknown value), widths, layer pattern, every refusal (one at a time, then all at once), PIECEWISE warning, cache refusal, step eligibility, `plan()` routing (PIECEWISE, too wide, prefill, PP input, unbound or re-bound KV cache), weight-view refusals.
- **GPU:** K1 against vLLM's KDA op chain; K2 at TP8 against o_proj + all-reduce + AttnRes + KimiMoE, with 300 bit-identical graph replays; a stalled rank finishes every launch and fails the step; warm-up compiles without launching.
- **Engine:** an 8-layer dummy K3 at TP8 stalls rank 3 inside a served decode step. A request fails, every rank raises at the same step, and the server exits.

Kimi-K3, TP8, DCP8, DSpark MTP, fp8 KV, `--stream-interval 10`, MI355X, FULL CUDA graphs, Model Runner V2. "Off" means the same image, tree and flags with `decode_backend=auto`.

## Test Result

This revision ran on 8x MI355X with `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-1b2a6663`, which is 20 commits behind this branch's base with no `kimi_k3`, mamba, `gdn_attn` or model-state changes in between. This branch's `vllm/models/kimi_k3/` was mounted over the image.

- **pytest** `tests/models/kimi_k3`: **420 passed, 0 failed** (89 skipped). This covers the new suite and every existing Kimi-K3 test.
- **ISA:** all 17 production K1/K2 builds are byte-identical to the previous revision (df3693c), so the kernel results below carry over.
- **Startup refusal:** TP4 + V1 runner + no speculative decoding gives one `ValueError` with all three reasons. `decode_backend="fast"` is rejected.
- **8k/1k, c1, k=7, 3 seeds:** TPOT p50 5.44 → **4.31 ms (−20.8%)**, p90 5.48 → 4.35 ms, output 170.2 → 210.3 tok/s (+23.6%); the server logs `Kimi-K3 specialized decode: 92 layers, widths [8], 30 builds`.
- **GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 q:**
  - c1, k=7, on: 0.9651 ± 0.0051 (an earlier run of the same cell on this revision: 0.9538 ± 0.0058).
  - Padded replays (k=1, c3, vLLM's default capture sizes, so 3-request steps replay the 4-request graph): off 0.9621 vs on 0.9613 (±0.0053).

### Accuracy, previous revision (same kernels, ISA byte-identical)

The kernel path serves steps of at most 8 rows, so these configs fuse every decode step (conc x (k+1) <= 8):

| eval | config | off | on |
|---|---|---|---|
| GSM8K 5-shot | c4, k=1 | 0.9644 | 0.9629 / 0.9568 |
| GSM8K 5-shot | c2, k=3 | 0.9522 | 0.9568 |
| GSM8K 5-shot | c1, k=7 | 0.9598 | 0.9629 |
| GPQA-Diamond (198 q, CoT, 0-shot) | c4, k=1 | 0.9242 | 0.9394 |
| AIME24 + AIME25 (60 q), avg@4, T=1.0 | c4, k=1 | 0.7958 | 0.8083 |
| NIAH single_1 / single_2 / multikey_1 @ 8k | c4, k=1 | 1.00 / 1.00 / 1.00 | 1.00 / 1.00 / 1.00 |
| NIAH single_1 / multikey_2 / multikey_3 @ 32k / 128k / 256k | c1, k=7 | | 1.000 (all) |

Paired GSM8K (1319 q, c4/k1): 18 right only with the kernels on, 27 right only with them off, McNemar exact p = 0.23.

### Performance, previous revision

`vllm bench serve`, random, 1024 output tokens, ignore-eos, 2 seeds. TPOT p50 in ms:

| conc, k | widths | 8k off | 8k on | 64k off | 64k on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1, 7 | 8 | 5.47 | 4.35 (-20.5%) | 5.67 | 4.47 (-21.2%) |
| 2, 3 | 4, 8 | 21.58 | 16.79 (-22.2%)* | | |
| 4, 1 | 8 | 26.55 | 22.18 (-16.5%)* | | |
| 8, 1 | (16 rows: vLLM's path) | 32.60 | 32.58 | | |

\* Synthetic acceptance length 1.0, so TPOT is the decode step time at that width. c1/k7 uses the CI's synthetic acceptance length 3.84.

Per-layer time (graph-replayed, profiler): K1 36.7 us (vs about 54 us plus gaps for vLLM's ops), K2 104.8 us (vs about 178 us).

AI assistance (Claude) was used to develop this change.

title: [HiSparse] Bound prefill staging temporaries by chunk, not prompt length
body:
## Purpose

Part of #60420. When a HiSparse prefill stages history that has spilled to host, two temporaries grow with prompt length:

- `HiSparsePrefillStagingPlan.ensure_gpu_sources` built a `num_unique_blocks × max_blocks_per_req` int64 table (about 2.1 GiB at 1M tokens). It now indexes the entries it needs directly.
- The resident-row copy gathered a second staged-size tensor before copying. It now copies in 64K-row chunks.

Same results, smaller temporaries.

## Test Result

1×B200, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 cut to 4 layers with dummy weights, fp8 KV, 1.04M-token prompt with 2 requests decoding:
- Greedy token ids and logprobs are bit-identical to main (FlashInfer fp8), including spilled prompts up to 524K with decodes running.
- In this workload the peak isn't set by these temporaries, so it doesn't change on its own: #60424 + this PR measured the same as #60424 alone (+1.50 GiB over profile at 1.04M). These temporaries set the peak once the larger allocations are gone. An earlier version of #60424 that preallocated the attention output before staging ran out of memory in `ensure_gpu_sources` at about 640K tokens, and these two changes fixed that.
- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py` on B200: 412 passed, including the new `test_hisparse_gather_prefill_cache_prefers_resident_rows[3]`, which splits the copy into several chunks and fails if the chunk offset is wrong.

title: [HiSparse] Write mixed decode/prefill attention outputs in place
body:
## Purpose

Part of #60420. With HiSparse, a mixed batch runs its decode rows and prefill rows as two sparse-MLA kernels and joins them with `torch.cat`. That's a second output-sized allocation, about 1 GiB at 16K batched tokens, which memory profiling never sees. It's where the original #60420 repro ran out of memory.

FlashInfer, FlashAttn and FlashInfer SM120 now preallocate one output and pass each kernel its slice with `out=`. Decode-only batches are unchanged and keep the kernel's own output, which is the CUDA-graph path. FlashMLA BF16 isn't covered: writing into its output needs the padded-head workspace, which is a separate change.

## Test Result

1×B200, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 cut to 4 layers with dummy weights, fp8 KV (FlashInfer), 1.04M-token prompt with 2 requests decoding:
- Greedy token ids and logprobs are bit-identical to main, including spilled prompts up to 524K with decodes running.
- With #60424 and #60706, per-step peak over profile drops from +1.50 GiB to +0.50 GiB, both with the prompt spilled to host (util 0.90) and with all KV on GPU (util 0.97). On main the 0.97 case runs out of memory in this `torch.cat`.
- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py` on B200: 412 passed. `-k "hisparse or HiSparse or flashattn"` on H100: 65 passed.
- New test `test_flashinfer_hisparse_mixed_batch_writes_one_output` fails on main and passes here. The decode-only stub test now asserts that no `out` is passed.
- FlashInfer SM120: not validated (no SM120 GPU available).

Once #60424 lands, this needs a rebase: the staging branches loop over prefill groups, and the new test must mock `staged_prefills` instead of `stage_prefill_rows`.

title: [ROCm][Perf] W4A16: opt-in dense weight cache for RDNA hybrid prefill
body:
## Overview

Adds opt-in `KernelConfig.rdna_hybrid_w4a16_prefill_dequant` (`"enable"`/`"disable"`, case-insensitive, default `"disable"`). When it is `"enable"`, `RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel` caches a dense fp16/bf16 copy of each weight at load time and runs GEMMs with `M >= 256` on it, so prefill no longer dequantizes int4.

## Claims

- TTFT −22% to −26% on Qwen3-4B/8B w4a16 and −21% on Gemma-4-31B AWQ with MTP-3, on Strix
  Halo (gfx1151). TPOT is unchanged at concurrency 1.
- No accuracy change: GSM8K is within ±0.6 pp.
- Decode, small batches and spec-decode verify stay on the int4 path.
- Disabled by default, which leaves current behaviour unchanged.

## Validation

Usage: `--kernel-config '{"rdna_hybrid_w4a16_prefill_dequant": "enable"}'`. `vllm bench serve` with random 2048 in, concurrency 1, `disable` vs `enable` on the same build, interleaved (3 pairs per Qwen model, 2 for Gemma); values are the mean of per-run medians. Measured only on gfx1151; the kernel also runs on other gfx11/gfx12 parts, where the `M >= 256` threshold may need tuning.

| Model | TTFT disable → enable | TPOT disable → enable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RedHatAI Qwen3-8B w4a16, fp16 (asym) | 1328 → 1033 ms (**−22.2%**) | 27.7 → 27.7 ms |
| RedHatAI Qwen3-8B w4a16, bf16 (asym) | 1341 → 1023 ms (**−23.7%**) | 28.2 → 28.2 ms |
| RedHatAI Qwen3-4B w4a16, fp16 (sym) | 782 → 578 ms (**−26.1%**) | 16.4 → 16.5 ms |
| cyankiwi Gemma-4-31B AWQ, MTP-3, 128 out | 8.75 → 6.88 s (**−21.4%**) | 68.0 → 67.2 ms |

Disabled matches current main (554340f3d3) within 1% TTFT on all four models.

At concurrency 16 (Qwen3-8B fp16, 512 in / 256 out, 64 prompts, 2 pairs): TTFT 3069 → 2252 ms (−26.6%), TPOT 85.2 → 83.1 ms.

GSM8K (in-tree `tests/evals/gsm8k`, 5-shot, 500 questions, concurrency 16), Qwen3-8B: fp16 0.886 → 0.880, bf16 0.872 → 0.878.

`pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py`: All 293 passed on gfx1151.

## Details

- **Why opt-in:** the copy is 4x the int4 layer weight and is taken from the `gpu_memory_utilization` budget, so it comes out of KV cache. Qwen3-8B: +13.5 GiB weights, −13.5 GiB KV. Gemma-4-31B: weights 20.2 → 75.1 GiB, KV 71.6 → 16.6 GiB. The trade targets unified-memory parts like Strix Halo, where TTFT matters more than KV capacity. Enabling it caches every layer or none: if the copies do not fit while leaving 4 GiB of activation headroom plus KV cache for one `max_model_len` request, startup fails with an error naming the option. It is a mode string rather than a bool so further modes can be added without renaming it.
- **Why `M >= 256`:** below it the dense GEMM is still memory bound and reads 4x the bytes. Per-GEMM on gfx1151 it is up to 2.3x slower than int4 on Gemma-4-31B MLP shapes. At 256 and above it is no slower on any Qwen3-8B or Gemma-4-31B shape measured.

### Related Work
- no open PR caches a dense copy of W4A16 weights for this kernel.
- #55711 makes the int4 prefill dequant cheaper, and this PR skips it, so the two stack. On top of #55711 this PR still cut TTFT by 6.7% (Qwen3-8B fp16), 12.8% (Qwen3-4B fp16) and 23.0% (Qwen3-8B bf16, since #55711 is fp16 only)
- #52637 (int4 repack in `process_weights_after_loading`) and #55742 (profiler labels) touch the same file, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.
- #53709 applies the same idea (opt-in load-time dequant for prefill) to DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 experts on another GPU family. It's a different kernel with no shared code path.

title: [Misc] Consolidate csrc shared headers and prune dead code
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Tidy `csrc/`: merge one-macro/one-function headers, rename the misnamed `attention/` dtype directory, move stragglers next to the extension that builds them, delete unreferenced code, and flatten `csrc/libtorch_stable/` back into `csrc/` now that nearly every GPU kernel is stable-ABI. No functional change intended.

Not a duplicate: the only open PR touching this area is #38134 (WIP, removes the KV cache dtype enum), which has a different goal and predates the `libtorch_stable/` layout.

## Claims

- `csrc/` is now `core/` (shared by every extension), `cpu/` and `rocm/` (legacy-ABI code), and everything else is the stable-ABI CUDA/HIP tree. `libtorch_stable/` is gone; extension names (`_C_stable_libtorch`, `_moe_C_stable_libtorch`) are unchanged.
- Every quoted `#include` resolves to the same file before and after the flatten (scripted over all 250 sources).
- The built CUDA extensions register the same 160 op schemas as `main`.
- Every `csrc/` path in the CI `source_file_dependencies` filters exists again. 68 entries had been left naming paths that moved under `libtorch_stable/`.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| CUDA build of `_C_stable_libtorch`, `_moe_C_stable_libtorch`, `cumem_allocator`, `spinloop`, `fs_io_C` with `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="7.5 8.0 8.9 9.0 10.0 12.0"` (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13) | builds and links |
| Registered op schemas vs. a build of `main` (`torch._C._jit_get_all_schemas()` after loading each `.so`) | identical, 160 schemas |
| Unified Marlin generator vs. the two old scripts, all archs | byte-identical output, 27 files each |
| x86 CPU extension (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, GCC 13) | every TU compiles except `cpu/utils.cpp` (missing system `numa.h` on the build box, file untouched here); not linked |
| ROCm | **not compiled** (no HIP toolchain). Ran torch's `hipify` on the old and new trees and checked that every quoted include of every HIP translation unit resolves after renaming |
| `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD` | passes |

GPU kernel tests on an H200, run against the build of the first two commits (before the flatten):

| Tests | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/core/test_{layernorm,activation,pos_encoding,fused_quant_layernorm,fused_silu_mul_block_quant,fused_qk_norm_rope,opcheck}.py`, `tests/kernels/attention/test_{merge_attn_states,cache}.py`, `tests/kernels/test_{cache_kernels,concat_mla_q}.py` | 6215 passed, 590 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_{fp8_quant,fp8_quant_group,int8_quant,per_token_group_quant,cutlass_scaled_mm,machete_mm}.py` | all passed except `test_cutlass_subset` (see below) |
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_gemm.py` | 394 passed |
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_{cutlass_w4a8,quant_op_schema,awq,gptq}.py` | 136 passed, 8 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_{moe_align_block_size,moe_permute_unpermute,grouped_topk,fused_topk}.py` | 2266 passed |

After the last commit (generator dedupe, folded files, `div_ceil`), rebuilt and re-ran the tests covering what it touched:

| Tests | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_marlin_gemm.py` plus the Marlin cases of `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py` | 638 passed, 6 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_{per_token_group_quant,int8_quant,fp8_quant_group}.py`, `tests/kernels/mamba`, `tests/kernels/test_{cache_kernels,concat_mla_q}.py`, `tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py` | 2781 passed, 629 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_{cutlass_scaled_mm,machete_mm,cutlass_w4a8,block_fp8}.py` | 1375 passed, 108 skipped, 1 failed (`test_cutlass_subset`, see below) |

After the flatten commit, a fresh build directory builds and links for the same arch list with the same 160 op schemas, and:

| Tests | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_marlin_gemm.py`, `tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py` | 624 passed, 264 skipped |
| `test_merge_attn_states.py`, `test_layernorm.py`, `test_fused_quant_layernorm.py`, `test_machete_mm.py`, `test_cutlass_w4a8.py`, `tests/kernels/mamba` | 5450 passed, 39 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_{moe_align_block_size,grouped_topk,moe}.py` | 2079 passed, 127 skipped |

`test_cutlass_scaled_mm.py::test_cutlass_subset` fails identically on a build of `main` on the same machine, so it is not caused by this PR.

Caveats on the local build: the machine has GCC 11.5, so the GCC ≥ 13 gate was bypassed in a scratch build dir and the DeepGEMM / DeepSelect / FlashMLA external projects were not built. ROCm and non-x86 CPU rely on CI.

## Details

**Layout**

```
csrc/
  core/             registration.h  scalar_type.hpp  cuda_compat.h
                    utils.hpp       (math.hpp + batch_invariant.hpp)
                    vec_dtypes/     (was attention/)
  cpu/              + ops.h, dynamic_4bit_int_moe_cpu.cpp
  rocm/             + dispatch_utils.h, quickreduce/
  attention/ moe/ quantization/ cutlass_extensions/ mamba/ gdn/ kimi_k3/
  *.cu, *.cuh, ops.h, torch_bindings.cpp   (was libtorch_stable/)
  cumem_allocator.*, fs_io.cpp, spinloop.cpp, *_registration.cpp
```

- `csrc/attention/` only held `Vec`/`FloatVec` dtype helpers. ROCm paged attention is the one place they are used for attention; elsewhere they are half/bf16/FP8 conversions. Hence `core/vec_dtypes/`.
- The legacy `_C` extension is ROCm-only and contains just quickreduce, so its bindings, kernel and headers live in `rocm/quickreduce/`. The op namespace (`_C_custom_ar`) is unchanged.
- The top-level `ops.h` only declared CPU ops (plus quickreduce), so it moved to `cpu/`.

**Removed as unreferenced**

- Files: `core/exception.hpp`, `cache.h`, `torch_utils.h`, `attention_utils.cuh`, `mamba/static_switch.h`, `cutlass_extensions/common.cpp`, the int8 `per_token_group_quant.cu` wrapper and its header, the second Marlin `generate_kernels.py`.
- Symbols: `VLLM_IMPLIES`, `Qk_dot`, `VLLM_SHFL_SYNC`, `TORCH_LIBRARY_IMPL_EXPAND`, `DEVICE_INLINE`/`HOST_INLINE`, the legacy `AT_*` dispatch macros other than `VLLM_DISPATCH_FP8_TYPES`, `cuda_utils::ceil_div` (now `div_ceil`), `TrivialEpilogue`, `identity`, `equivalent_cutlass_type`, `enable_sm120_only`, `barrier_at_start_release`, and the non-stable-ABI branches in two CUTLASS headers.

**Things reviewers may want to look at**

- `TORCH_UTILS_CHECK` is replaced by `STD_TORCH_CHECK`. The stable build already resolved to it; in the legacy-ABI `_rocm_C` extension an unsupported KV cache dtype string now raises `std::runtime_error` instead of `c10::Error`.
- `div_ceil` is `constexpr` without `__device__` and is now called from device code in `cache_kernels.cu`, which is also built for HIP.
- The CUTLASS include dirs and `CUTLASS_ENABLE_DIRECT_CUDA_DRIVER_CALL` were dropped from the ROCm-only `_C` target, which no longer includes CUTLASS headers.
- The flatten renames about 190 files, so open PRs touching `csrc/libtorch_stable/` will need a rebase (git follows the renames for edits; newly added files need moving by hand).
- CI: the filter commits change which jobs trigger. Also, quickreduce and the CPU `ops.h` now sit under `csrc/rocm/` and `csrc/cpu/`, which `ci_config.yaml` excludes from its run-all pattern, so changes to them only trigger jobs listing those paths.

**Out of scope**

- Grouping the loose kernel files at the `csrc/` top level into subdirectories.
- `get_device_attribute` in `cuda_utils_kernels.cu` caches its first result in a function-local `static` regardless of arguments, so the SM-count and max-shared-memory queries can return each other's value. Found while reviewing; it needs its own fix.

title: [RFC]: Strcutured Outputs Not Respected When Reasoning Implicitly Ends
body:
### Motivation.

I want to start a discussion on how implicit reasoning end can break structured ouptuts + spec decode.

### Background

For structured outputs, we only apply constrained decoding after reasoning ends. This is to allow models to reason while constraining the user-visible content.

At each decode step, the scheduler roughly calls:
1. `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens` to validate the draft tokens need constraining and trim any grammar-invalid tokens
2. `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` to create bitmasks for the draft tokens that need constraining
3. `StructuredOutputManager.accpet_tokens` to advance grammar FSM over the constrained tokens

These three methods rely on a `StructuredOutputManager._get_constraint_start` helper to identify when reasoning ends. It returns `reasoning_end_index + 1`

### Implicit Reasoning Ends

Reasoning end is usually marked by a special token (e.g. `</think>` for GLM 5.3). However, reasoning can also end implicitly when the model starts emitting content or tool call without closing reasoning first (e.g. `<think> ... <tool_call>` instead of `<think> ... </think><tool_call>`). This presents challenges for strcutured output constraint start detection.

### Issues with Implicit Reasoning Ends

Currently, `StructuredOutputManager._get_constraint_start` assumes all reasoning end markers are explicit. For example, given `prefix <tool_call> suffix`,
1. `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens` doesn't validate the `<tool_call>`
2. `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` creates bitmasks for `suffix` only
3. `StructuredOutputManager.accpet_tokens` advances grammar FSM over accepted `suffix` + bonux token only.

This leads to two issues:
- I1: `<tool_call>` may not be grammar valid, yet it is unconditionally accepted
- I2: if a model is required to make a tool call, it will be forced to generate duplicate `<tool_call>` because the grammar isn't aware of the first one #59608

### Fix attempt: Adjust `_get_constraint_start` for implicit reasoning end markers. 

A simple fix seems to be to make `_get_constraint_start` return `reasoning_end_index` instead of `reasoning_end_index + 1` for implicit reasoning end markers. `_get_constraint_start` still returns `reasoning_end_index + 1` for explicit reasoning end markers.

Given `prefix <tool_call> suffix`,
1. `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens` now validates `<tool_call> suffix`
2. `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` creates bitmasks for `<tool_call> suffix`
3. `StructuredOutputManager.accept_tokens` advances grammar FSM over the accepted `<tool_call> suffix` and bonus token.

This seems to fix both issues:
- I1: `<tool_call>` is validated and rejected if grammar-invalid
- I2: grammar is aware of `<tool_call>`, not duplicate emission needed

However, the fix is subtly incorrect: spec decode changes the target model's output distribution:
- the drafter proposes `prefix <tool_call> suffix`
- structure outputs sees `<tool_call>` and determines that constraint should start
- but the target model could reject `<tool_call>`, it could choose to continue reasoning
- but structured ouputs forces a grammar-valid token to be sampled
Constraint start was determined by the drafter's output, before target model can accpet or reject it.

This was implemented in my intial attempt and in #59629

### Correct fix: Distinguish between `grammar_start` and `constraint_start`.

Make `_get_constraint_start` return a tuple of `grammar_start, constraint_start`. For explicit reasoning end markers, `grammar_start == constraint_start`. For implicit end markers, `grammar_start < constraint_start`.
1. `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens` validate from `grammar_start`
2. `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` is aware of tokens from `grammar_start` but only emit bitmasks from `constraint_start`
3. `StructuredOutputManager.accept_tokens` validate from `grammar_start`

Given `prefix <tool_call> suffix`,
1. `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens` validates `<tool_call> suffix`
2. `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` creatse bitmasks for `suffix` only
3. `StructuredOutputManager.accept_tokens` advances grammar FSM over the accepted `<tool_call> suffix` and bonus token.

This fixes both the issues without affecting the target model's output distribution.

This was implemented in #59627 and merged.

### Remaining Issues

The fix is currently limited to engine-based parsers. It also doesn't account for implicit multi-token reasoning end markers (e.g. deepseek_v4) or text-only reasoning end markers (e.g. inkling).

There's also one more fundamental issue that remains: we can still sample implicit reasoning ends even when they are not grammar-valid.

For example, suppose the grammar disallows tool calls, the drafts are `reasoning_prefix reasoning_suffix`.
1. `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens` doesn't validate anything since reasoning has not ended
2. `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` doesn't constrain anything
3. Target model rejects `reasoning_suffix`. Since there's no constraint, it can sample `<tool_call>`.
4. `StructuredOutputManager.accept_tokens` attempts to advance grammar FSM over `<tool_call>` and fails

This is unavoidable when a reasoning end marker can also be part of the grammar:
- We must not constrain any reasoning end marker because it forces the model to end reasoning, changing the output distribution
- We must constrain any token that's part of the grammar.
We can't satisfy both requirements with implicit reasoning ends

### Proposed Change.

As I see it, the only way to avoid this is disallow implicit reasoning markers. SGLang has a feature `--enable-strict-thinking` that "Blocks model-specific excluded tokens (e.g., tool call markers) during reasoning. Requires a grammar backend that supports token filtering." https://docs.sglang.io/docs/advanced_features/server_arguments

I see two ways to implement this:
1. Global implementation that reads a model's implicit reasoning end marker and disallow them during sampling
    - Con: Doesn't work for models with multi-token reasoning end markers. Additional logic to maintain.
2. Per-model structural tags (via the structural tags registry)
    - Con: Reliance on xgrammar, doesn't work with other backends

Questions for maintainers:
1. Do we want to add a `--enable-strict-thinking` feature to cover the reamining edge case?
2. If so, do we prefer a global implementation or per-model structural tags?
3. If not, do we have preferences on how to address remaining edge cases (multi-token / text only reasoning end, non engine-parsers)


### Feedback Period.

_No response_

### CC List.

_No response_

### Any Other Things.

_No response_

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Re-plan DSA indexer decode schedule for DBO's reduced DeepGEMM SM count
body:
## Overview

With `--enable-dbo` and an all2all backend that reserves communication SMs (e.g. DeepEP high-throughput), DSA models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x) crash in the sparse-attention indexer as soon as a microbatched step contains a decode-branch request:

```
RuntimeError: Assertion error (csrc/apis/attention.hpp:346): _schedule_meta_size == num_sms + 1 and _meta_info_size == 2
```

The indexer builder plans DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits schedule for the whole GPU, but DBO lowers DeepGEMM's SM count (`set_num_sms(total - VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS)`) while the microbatches run. This PR re-plans the schedule at the call site when the two counts differ. No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `schedule_meta_size`, `dbo indexer num_sms`, `paged_mqa_logits set_num_sms`: 0 results). Rechecked 2026-10-08 against open PRs: #56476 (DeepSeek-V4.1 per-microbatch index state) also edits `sparse_attn_indexer.py`, in different lines, and does not touch the schedule metadata.

## Claims

- Fixes the DSA indexer decode crash under DBO (Model Runner V1 and V2, CUDA + DeepGEMM).
- The re-planned schedule gives bit-identical indexer logits, so the fix does not change results: with it, GLM-5.3 accuracy under DBO matches DBO with SM partitioning disabled (`VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0`), where this code path never runs.
- Separately, GLM-5.3 accuracy with DBO on is well below DBO off (GSM8K ~0.6 vs 0.93) with or without this change. That is a separate, pre-existing DBO bug in GLM-5.x's shared top-k layers that this crash was hiding, fixed in #60734 (see Validation).
- No cost when the SM count is unchanged (one host-side `get_num_sms()` per indexer layer). Under DBO, one ~9 µs metadata kernel per microbatch per forward, reused by all indexer layers. No host syncs; CUDA-graph safe.
- XPU / ROCm paths unchanged.

## Validation

This branch is rebased onto main @ 240785b8; the rebase did not change the patch (same `git patch-id`). The unit and related tests below were re-run on the rebased commit (H200) with the same results. The GSM8K runs predate the rebase and used main @ 4a705c7b with and without this patch.

**Unit test (new)**, `tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_schedule_metadata.py`: plans a schedule for the full GPU, lowers DeepGEMM's SM count by 20 (what `create_sm_control_context` does), and checks that `get_schedule_metadata()` re-plans once, the kernel runs, and logits match the full-SM result on all valid columns; the original schedule comes back after the SM count is restored. Runs in the existing H100/B200 "V1 Attention" CI shards; skipped without DeepGEMM or below SM90.

| Build | GPU | Result |
|---|---|---|
| this branch (main @ 4a705c7b, precompiled from 2e06395f) | H200 | `next_n` 1, 2, 4: 3 passed |
| vLLM 0.29.0 + backport | H200 | `next_n` 1, 2: passed (`next_n=4` needs a newer DeepGEMM than 0.29 ships) |

Related existing tests on this branch (H200): `tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py` 5 passed, `test_indexer_native_next_n.py` 9 passed, `test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py` 7 passed, `test_indexer_dcp_localize.py` 114 passed, `test_sparse_mla_backends.py` 292 passed (1,188 skipped by hardware). `test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py`: 30 passed, 3 could not run locally (they load the gated `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B` config); they fail identically on main and do not touch the changed code.

**Kernel-level check** (H200, DeepGEMM `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits`, GLM-5.3 indexer shapes: 32 heads x 128, block 64, 13 requests with contexts 1 to 32k):

| SM count | Schedule planned for | Result |

| 132 | 132 | reference |
| 112 (inside vLLM's `SMControlContextManager`) | 132 | the production assertion |

Workload: random-token prompts of `64*k+1` tokens, then exact repeats (a full prefix-cache hit leaves a 1-token short extend at the head of the batch) mixed with fresh long prompts, pinned per DP rank. vLLM 0.29.0 with and without the backport of this patch (same two files):

| Run | DBO steps | Assertion | Requests |
|---|---|---|---|
| DBO off | 0 | 0 | 6 rounds, 0 errors |
| DBO on, without fix | 4 | yes, 6 s after the first DBO step | 29/32 failed in round 2, engine dead |
| DBO on, with fix | 28 | 0 | 6 rounds, 0 errors |
| DBO on, with fix, 30 rounds incl. decodes | 158 | 0 | 944 requests, 0 errors |

With the fix, DBO-on generations equal DBO-off: 944/944 identical sequences (7,440/7,440 tokens), first-token logprob difference at most 1.9e-6.

| vLLM | Config | GSM8K exact_match (flexible / strict) |
|---|---|---|
| this branch | DBO off | 0.927 / 0.928 |
| main (without fix) | DBO on | crash: the assertion on 8 workers, 4 engines dead, eval aborted |
| this branch | DBO on | 0.592 / 0.582 (all 1,319 answered) |
| main (without fix) | DBO on, `VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0` (fix path never runs) | 0.610 / 0.608 |
| this branch | DBO on, `VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0` | 0.623 / 0.606 |

The fix turns the crash into a completed eval. The drop from 0.93 to ~0.6 with DBO on is not caused by it: the `VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0` rows never re-plan (and never crash) and land in the same range. DBO with GLM-5.x has an accuracy bug of its own that this crash has been hiding: layers that reuse another layer's top-k read it from state shared across microbatches. #60734 fixes it; with both PRs, GLM-5.3 with DBO on scores 0.922 / 0.923 (DBO off: 0.927 / 0.928).

<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
# unit test
pytest -v tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_schedule_metadata.py

# GSM8K
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \

  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --enable-prefix-caching
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=256,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause** (main @ 240785b8):
- `create_sm_control_context` (`vllm/v1/worker/ubatch_utils.py:83-126`) uses `deep_gemm.set_num_sms` as the compute-SM setter whenever `has_deep_gemm() and comm_sms > 0`, so inside the microbatches DeepGEMM sees `total - VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS` SMs (132 - 20 = 112 on H100/H200). It keys on DeepGEMM being importable, not on `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM`. `comm_sms` is 0 only for DeepEP low-latency and NIXL-EP.
- The context wraps the microbatched forward in both runners (`gpu_ubatch_wrapper.py:426,453`; MRV2 `gpu/ubatch_utils.py:496`), after attention metadata has been built.
- The indexer builder plans the decode schedule for `num_compute_units` SMs (`v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py:967-968`, `:1688-1697`, MTP drafts `:1782-1789`), and `sparse_attn_indexer.py:729` / `glm5next/nvidia/sparse_indexer.py:582` pass it to `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits`, which asserts it against the current SM count.
- The decode branch takes every request with `query_len <= 1 + num_speculative_tokens`, including 1-token short extends of prefix-cached prompts, which the reorder puts first. A step is microbatched only when every DP rank votes for it.

**How it was found:** GLM-5.3 RL with P/D disaggregation; prefill DP32/EP32 with DeepEP high-throughput, DBO, `cudagraph_mode NONE`, prefix caching, vLLM 0.29.0 on H200. One prefill rank hit the assertion after ~28 h; the other 31 then timed out in DeepEP dispatch and failed with `torch.cat(): expected a non-empty list of Tensors`.

**Fix:** `DeepSeekV32IndexerDecodeMetadata` records the SM count and block size the schedule was planned with. `get_schedule_metadata()` returns the planned schedule when DeepGEMM's current SM count matches; otherwise it re-plans with the same inputs and caches the result per SM count. The planned count is stored rather than derived from the tensor shape because SM90 `next_n=4` plans `num_sms // 2 + 1` schedule rows. `update_draft_decode_metadata` rewrites `seq_lens` in place, so it clears the cache. In FULL-graph DBO capture the re-plan kernel is captured and reads the persistent `seq_lens`/`indices` buffers; eager warmups under the same context JIT-compile it before capture.

<details>
<summary>Alternatives considered</summary>

1. Plan for the reduced SM count in the builder: the builder would need to replicate `create_sm_control_context` (all2all `max_sms_used()`, `VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS`, the ROCm override) for both runners, and anything else that changes DeepGEMM's SM count would break it again.
2. Skip `set_num_sms` in SM control: removes DBO's compute/communication SM partitioning for every DeepGEMM GEMM.
3. Re-plan inside the `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` wrapper: no per-forward object to cache on, so every indexer layer would re-plan.
4. Build both schedules up front: an extra kernel every step even when DBO does not split.
</details>

**Not affected:** the sparse-MQA schedule of DeepSeek-V4.1 (planned inside the forward), FlashMLA scheduler metadata, and prefill `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits`.

**AI assistance:** Claude Code was used to trace the root cause, write the patch and test, run the validations above, and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line, can explain and defend the change, and checked the test results above.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Keep DSA shared-indexer top-k state per DBO microbatch
body:
## Overview

With `--enable-dbo`, GLM-5.x (DSA with shared top-k layers, `index_topk_freq > 1`) loses about a third of its GSM8K accuracy: 0.93 with DBO off, 0.61 with DBO on. The layers that reuse an earlier layer's sparse-attention top-k (57 of GLM-5.3's 78 layers) read it from buffers that have no microbatch dimension. DBO runs microbatch 1's index-producing layer between microbatch 0's producer and its consumers, so microbatch 0's consumers attend over microbatch 1's token selection. This PR gives every DBO microbatch after the first its own copy of that state. With it, DBO-on accuracy matches DBO off.

Companion to #60732 (DSA indexer crash under DBO, which hid this bug). The two fixes are independent; DBO with DeepEP high-throughput needs both. No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `dbo topk`, `index_topk_freq dbo`, `shared indexer microbatch`, `GLM-5 dbo accuracy`: 0 results). Related open PR: #56476 fixes the same class of bug for DeepSeek-V4.1 (its top-k and candidate buffers, via a new `dbo_select_buffer` helper). It does not cover the DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.x IndexCache path changed here; if it lands first, this PR can switch to its helper.

## Claims

- Fixes GLM-5.x accuracy under DBO on Model Runner V1 and V2: GSM8K 0.61 → 0.92 (DBO off: 0.92–0.93). Also with DBO microbatches replayed from FULL decode CUDA graphs (DeepEP low-latency): 0.44 → 0.85 (DBO off: 0.84–0.86).
- No change without DBO, and none for DSA models without shared top-k layers (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.1: every layer computes its own top-k, so no microbatch state is allocated). Measured: both score the same with DBO on as off, with and without this change, and report identical KV cache memory with and without it.
- Memory under DBO, per GPU and per extra microbatch: `(max_num_batched_tokens + G * (max_decode_rows + 1)) * index_topk * 4` bytes, where `G` is the number of index groups with followers (19 for GLM-5.3). GLM-5.3 at `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, `max_num_seqs=1024`: 216 MiB, measured as 0.22 GiB less KV cache memory.
- No host syncs, no extra kernels. The per-microbatch lookup is one dict read per access, the same one DBO already uses everywhere (`dbo_current_ubatch_id()`).
- HiSparse with DBO and shared top-k layers now raises at startup (it previously ran with the same corruption); supporting it needs per-microbatch HiSparse staging, out of scope here.

## Validation

**Unit test (new)**, `test_sparse_mla_index_group_keeps_topk_per_dbo_ubatch` in `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py`: one leader group without followers and one with a follower, built with `num_ubatches=2`. It checks that the leader-only group allocates nothing, that leader and follower impls resolve to the same per-microbatch buffer, and that after both microbatches' leaders write (in DBO order: leader 0, leader 1, then followers) each follower's logical and converted physical top-k equal its own leader's bit for bit. Runs in the existing "V1 Attention" CI shards.

| Build | Result |
|---|---|
| this branch | passed |
| base (without fix) | fails (the builder has no `num_ubatches`) |
| mutation: index group always returns microbatch 0's state | fails |
| mutation: impl not wired to the per-microbatch logical buffers | fails |

The two mutations each break one half of the fix and confirm the assertions catch it. Existing tests on this branch (H200): `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py` 293 passed (1,188 skipped by hardware), `tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py` + `test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py` 40 passed. `tests/v1/distributed/test_dbo.py` (DeepSeek-V2-Lite, DP2, DBO): 2 passed (`deepep_low_latency`, `deepep_high_throughput`). pre-commit's ruff check and format pass; mypy on the four changed source files reports no new errors (two fewer than base).

All tests and GPU runs in this description used main @ 4a705c7b. This branch is rebased onto main @ 240785b8, where the five files it changes differ only in HiSparse code it does not touch (`HiSparseMLAIndexGroup` routing, #60682; HiSparse tests, #60429 and #60682), and `ubatching.py` / `ubatch_utils.py` are unchanged. Re-run on the rebased commit (H200): the new test passes (and still fails on main without the fix), `test_sparse_mla_backends.py` 293 passed (1,188 skipped), `tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py` and `test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py` 40 passed, and `pytest -v -s tests/v1/distributed/test_dbo.py` 2 passed (`deepep_low_latency`, `deepep_high_throughput`). The GSM8K and long-prompt runs were not repeated on the new base.

**Model evaluation, GLM-5.3 FP8** (1 x 8 H200, DP4 x TP2, EP8, DeepEP high-throughput unless noted, `cudagraph_mode NONE`, fp8 KV, prefix caching, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`; `lm_eval` GSM8K 5-shot, 1,319 questions, `num_concurrent=256`; standard error ±0.007 at 0.92, ±0.013 at 0.61). Every DBO-on run microbatched 100+ steps per worker.

| vLLM | Runner | DBO | GSM8K flexible / strict |
|---|---|---|---|
| main + #60732 | V2 | off | 0.927 / 0.928 |
| main + #60732 | V1 | off | 0.924 / 0.924 |
| main + #60732 | V1 | on | 0.613 / 0.607 |
| main + #60732 | V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`) | on | 0.614 / 0.610 |
| main + #60732 + this PR | V1 | on | 0.922 / 0.923 |
| main + #60732 + this PR (repeat) | V1 | on | 0.923 / 0.921 |
| main + #60732 + this PR | V2 | on | 0.919 / 0.919 |
| main + this PR only, `VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0` | V1 | on | 0.923 / 0.923 |

Note that `--enable-dbo` alone falls back to Model Runner V1; the V2 rows set `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` (logs confirm "Using V2 Model Runner" and "Dual batch overlap is enabled").

**CUDA graphs** (DBO microbatches replayed from FULL decode graphs). This needs DeepEP low-latency (high-throughput cannot be captured) and pure decode steps on every DP rank, which `lm_eval`'s streaming load never produces at low-latency's 256-token step budget (0 microbatched steps in a full GSM8K run). Workload instead: the first 1,024 GSM8K test questions zero-shot, sent at once (256 per DP rank), 192 forced greedy tokens each, scored for the final answer. Same GLM-5.3 setup with `--all2all-backend deepep_low_latency`, `cudagraph_mode FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, Model Runner V1 in all runs. These runs also carry a one-line fix for a separate bug: the batched Triton FP8 MoE that low-latency mode uses (with DeepGEMM off) does not clamp `BLOCK_SIZE_K` to the 128-wide FP8 block (`fused_batched_moe.py:452`, unlike `fused_moe.py:844`), which gives GSM8K 0.02 even with DBO off; with the clamp, 0.93. That fix is its own PR (#60733).

With `--max-num-batched-tokens 512` (`NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH=4096`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.93`, so the prompts prefill in about 50 steps and most answer tokens are decoded in microbatched steps), each DBO-on worker replayed 180+ microbatched decode graphs and ran 50+ eager microbatched prefill steps:

| Run (1,024 questions, low-latency, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`) | Accuracy | vs DBO off #1: lost / gained (McNemar z) |
|---|---|---|
| DBO off #1 | 0.843 | |
| DBO off #2 | 0.857 | 11 / 26 (-2.5) |
| DBO on, main + #60732 | 0.440 | 442 / 30 (19.0) |
| DBO on, main + #60732 + this PR | 0.845 | 40 / 42 (-0.2) |
| DBO on, main + #60732 + this PR (repeat) | 0.850 | 31 / 38 (-0.8) |

At the default 256-token budget (fewer microbatched steps) the picture is the same: DBO off 0.849 / 0.848, without this PR 0.775 (z 6.4 vs off), with it 0.838 (z 1.4). Exact token sequences are not a usable signal in this mode: two DBO-off runs already differ at the first token for 100 of 1,024 prompts.

**Negative control, GLM-5.1 FP8** (DSA, `index_topk_freq=1`: no shared top-k layers), same setup (main + #60732): DBO off 0.946 / 0.948; DBO on without this PR 0.952 / 0.950; DBO on with this PR 0.947 / 0.950 (100+ microbatched steps per worker in both DBO runs). With and without this PR the DBO-on runs report the same model memory (100.48 GiB) and KV cache memory (15.16 GiB): nothing is allocated when every layer computes its own top-k. DSA plus DBO is fine when no layer reuses another's top-k.

**Second negative control, DeepSeek-V3.2** (61 layers, every one computes its own top-k), same setup. Note: in this configuration vLLM main crashes with an illegal memory access in the first microbatched profiling step for DeepSeek-V3.2 with DBO on, with or without either fix (also without #60732, where it shows up as a DeepEP timeout instead). It disappears with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, so it is a separate stream race, not investigated here. The DBO-on runs below therefore use `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, which keeps DBO's microbatch order: GLM-5.3 without this PR still shows this bug under it (0.607 / 0.596, vs 0.613 / 0.607 without blocking).

| DeepSeek-V3.2 | GSM8K flexible / strict | Long prompts vs DBO off: differ at token 0, median \|Δ logprob\| | KV cache memory |
|---|---|---|---|
| DBO off (second DBO-off run = noise floor) | 0.952 / 0.952 | 0, 0.0001 | 24.46 GiB |
| DBO on, without this PR | 0.954 / 0.952 | 0, 0.0000 | 23.22 GiB |
| DBO on, with this PR | 0.952 / 0.951 | 0, 0.0000 | 23.22 GiB |

**Isolating the cause** (GLM-5.3, main + #60732, DBO on):

| Experiment | GSM8K flexible | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| DBO only on decode steps | 0.601 | decode steps alone reproduce the full drop |
| DBO only on prefill steps (3 microbatched steps) | 0.901 | few prefill splits, small drop |
| prefix caching off | 0.619 | not prefix caching |
| `VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0` | 0.610 | not the DeepGEMM SM partition |
| prototype: per-microbatch converted (physical) top-k only, logical buffer still shared | 0.920 | short steps only read the converted copy |

**Long prompts, greedy** (GLM-5.3, same setup, Model Runner V1): 128 GSM8K-train prompts of 4.5k–7.7k tokens sent at once (prefill steps microbatch as 2 x 4096), 32 greedy tokens each with logprobs, compared against a DBO-off run. A second DBO-off run gives the noise floor (batching is not invariant, so long greedy continuations drift even without DBO).

| Run vs. DBO off | Identical 32-token outputs | Mean first differing token | Differ at token 0 | Median \|Δ logprob\| of token 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DBO off (second run) | 35 / 128 | 18.2 | 0 | 0.0001 |
| DBO on, main + #60732 | 0 / 128 | 3.0 | 7 | 0.0135 |
| DBO on, prototype with only the converted (physical) top-k per microbatch | 2 / 128 | 3.4 | 10 | 0.0081 |
| DBO on, main + #60732 + this PR | 24 / 128 | 17.1 | 0 | 0.0001 |

A step with more tokens than the conversion workspace (`max_decode_rows + 1`, 1,025 here) skips the cached conversion, and every follower converts from the logical buffer again. That is why the prototype fixes GSM8K but not long prefills, and why this PR keeps both the logical buffer and the converted state per microbatch.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
# unit test
pytest -v tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k dbo_ubatch

# GSM8K (add VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 for Model Runner V2)
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput --enable-dbo --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "NONE"}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --enable-prefix-caching
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=256,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause** (main @ 240785b8). GLM-5.x configs set `index_topk_freq=4`, `index_skip_topk_offset=3`: only 21 of 78 layers run the sparse indexer ("leaders": 0, 1, 2, 6, 10, …, 74); each of the other 57 reuses the top-k of the leader before it. That hand-off goes through state with no microbatch dimension:
- the model-wide logical buffer `DeepseekV32Model.topk_indices_buffer`, which the leader writes (`fused_norm_rope`, `sparse_attn_indexer`) and every follower's sparse MLA impl reads;
- per index group, `SparseMLAIndexGroup.physical_topk_indices` / `valid_topk_counts` (logical → physical conversion, done once by the leader and reused by its followers) and the `logical_topk_ready` / `physical_topk_ready` events.

DBO yields inside MoE dispatch/combine, so between microbatch 0's leader L and its follower L+1, microbatch 1 runs its own layer L and overwrites all of the above. Every follower of microbatch 0 except layer 3 (layers 0–2 are dense, so there is no yield between leader 2 and follower 3) then attends over microbatch 1's selected tokens, with block-table conversion done for microbatch 1's requests. Microbatch 1's followers read their own data and are unaffected. Leaders without followers (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.1, layers 0 and 1 here) are unaffected because they write and read within one layer.

**How it was found:** while validating #60732, GSM8K with DBO on came out at ~0.6 against 0.93 off, with or without that fix and with SM partitioning disabled. The table above narrowed it to decode-step microbatching independent of prefix caching and SM count; GLM-5.1 (same architecture, no shared top-k) was unaffected, which pointed at the shared top-k hand-off. A prototype that gave each microbatch its own converted top-k restored 0.920; the long-prompt test below shows it is not enough on its own.

**Fix:**
- `SparseMLAIndexGroupBuilder` takes `num_ubatches`. When a group gets its first follower, it allocates one `UbatchTopkState` (physical indices, valid counts, two events) per extra microbatch for that group, and, once per builder, one logical buffer per extra microbatch. Groups without followers allocate nothing.
- `SparseMLAIndexGroup._topk_state()` and `SharedTopkIndicesBuffer.topk_indices_buffer` return microbatch 0's existing state, or the extra microbatch's copy when `dbo_current_ubatch_id() > 0`.
- The leader's writers (`fused_norm_rope`, `sparse_attn_indexer` in `DeepseekV32Attention`) now take the buffer from `self.impl.topk_indices_buffer`, so writer and readers resolve the same per-microbatch buffer.
- `DeepseekV32Model` passes `num_ubatches=get_num_ubatches(parallel_config)`.

The extra buffers are allocated at model construction, before the KV-cache profile, so they come out of KV cache memory. In FULL-graph DBO capture, each microbatch thread resolves its own buffers at capture time.

<details>
<summary>Alternatives considered</summary>

1. Add a microbatch dimension to `topk_indices_buffer` itself: touches the MTP proposer's buffer sharing and every reader; the per-impl property was already the single resolution point.
2. Make followers recompute top-k under DBO: correct but runs the indexer on all 78 layers, which is what `index_topk_freq` exists to avoid.
3. Disable DBO for models with shared top-k layers: loses the overlap for exactly the models (GLM-5.x) that use DBO in production.
4. Allocate per-microbatch state in every index group: wastes memory for DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.1, which have no followers.
</details>

**MTP:** the draft's indexers are re-pointed to the target buffer through the module setter, which clears any microbatch buffers. The MTP layer is a leader-only group and the draft runs outside the microbatch threads, so it is unchanged.

**Not covered:** the ROCm DSA model (`vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd`) and the non-CUDA fallback in `deepseek_v2.py`/`glm4_moe_lite.py` still build their groups with one microbatch; they keep the old behavior if they run DBO with shared top-k layers. HiSparse raises instead (see Claims).

**AI assistance:** Claude Code was used to trace the root cause, write the patch and test, run the validations above, and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line, can explain and defend the change, and checked the test results above.

title: [Kernel][HYV4] CUDA fused iHC boundary op (post -> pre -> RMSNorm)
body:
## Purpose

**Depends on #58581** (cross-layer iHC fusion). Until it merges, this diff includes its commit; review only the last commit.

Adds a vLLM CUDA op, `torch.ops._C.hy_v4_ihc_boundary`, as an alternative to HPC's `fuse_ihc_post_pre` and `fuse_ihc_pre`. It follows the design of TRT-LLM's fused mHC kernel (`cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/mhcKernels`). On SM90+ builds `CudaIHCPostPre` is preferred over `HpcIHCPre` / `HpcIHCPostPre`, so the cross-layer schedule from #58581 no longer requires the external `hpc-ops` wheel.

The op runs two kernels per boundary:
- **Statistics kernel.** A CTA owns 16 tokens and one split of the 4 × hidden reduction. It applies the post step, stores the new residual, and computes the per-split sums of squares and the 8 gate projections. The projections run on tensor cores (`mma.sync` m16n8k16, N = 8 gates). The FP32 weight is split into three BF16 parts (hi + mid + lo), so the products equal FP32 products. Weight tiles are shared by the 16 tokens.
- **Finish kernel**, one CTA per token. It sums the splits in a fixed order, so results are deterministic. Then it computes the gates, the gated reduction and the RMSNorm.
- Both kernels launch with PDL.

## Numerics
Direct comparison with `hpc.fuse_ihc_post_pre` / `fuse_ihc_pre` on identical inputs (hidden 4096/6144, 1–8192 tokens, both forms):
- **Residual:** 100% bitwise equal. The post step is one FMA, so the new residual is the exact result rounded to BF16.
- **Hidden state:** 99.97–100% bitwise equal, relative L2 ≤ 3e-5 (FP32 summation order). By default the gated reduction enters the RMSNorm in FP32, like the HPC kernel; `round_before_norm=True` rounds it to BF16 first, like the unfused Triton path.
- **Gates:** max difference ≤ 1.1e-6.

## Test Plan
- `pytest tests/kernels/test_hy_v4_ihc_boundary.py`: compares the op with the unfused Triton pre + RMSNorm on the same residual, and the post step with an FP64 reference, across hidden sizes, split-count boundaries and offset views, in both rounding modes; checks determinism.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Preserve coordinator metadata and current eager-store placement
body:
## Overview

Keep SimpleCPU cache geometry and eager-store placement consistent with the device coordinator. Reconstructing only dataclass fields can lose plugin metadata; append-only request placement can retain stale page IDs after sliding-window recycling.

## Claims

- Keep the original configuration type and additional metadata while replacing CPU capacity and tensor descriptors.
- Leave the device configuration unchanged; retain the existing allocation calculation and shared-field behavior.
- Before selecting eager stores, use the existing connector block state to obtain the current request block table. Preserve the existing fallback when current placement is unavailable.

## Validation

Publication note: the vLLM branch now points to `1e37e847860f10e16404e1b163815a19b2eca28e` after a commit-message-only rewrite. The complete tested source tree is unchanged from `6b400f91586ece036ae6d5ecfa0b42f4a3b9c19f` (identical Git tree `554b4fc9ed241cb4a8e129394bf9915e26686c6c`); the measurements below were collected on that original commit.

```bash
# Executed in the vLLM checkout with the test virtual environment on PATH:
python /archive/run_vllm_cpu_tests.py -q \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py
```

96 passed on the NPU host using a CPU-only wrapper that applies the existing `skip_global_cleanup` marker to avoid unrelated accelerator allocator cleanup. Test bodies and assertions are unchanged; an offline OPT config is used for config construction, not model inference. The metadata regression fails with the original function (missing `kv_transfer_config`) and passes with this change. A separate real scheduler/Ascend coordinator probe passes 18 combinations; substituting the original function yields 6 failures (8704 matched tokens versus the expected 8192). That probe is CPU state validation, not DMA evidence. A second regression recycles an SWA page to another request with zero computed tokens: the original eager selector incorrectly stores both pages (`[1, 2]`); the fix stores only the current request page (`[1]`).

Existing SimpleCPU scheduler tests are included in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`. Local formatting checks passed. Hosted CI and human review are separate from these local results.

<details><summary>Real NPU serving, accuracy and paired performance</summary>

The paired NPU evaluation used real DSV4-Flash-0731 W8A8 weights on 8 x Ascend 910B4-1, TP8/EP, DSpark 7, MRV1, async scheduling and FULL_DECODE_ONLY. Both arms enabled prefix caching; CPU offload added a 448 GiB host pool (56 GiB/rank), with no disk tier. Max model length 69632, batch-token budget 8192, max sequences 16, memory utilization 0.9, indexer int8. Both arms explicitly use 4096 NPU cache blocks per rank to avoid capacity drift from startup memory profiling.

96 independent prefix families, 65536 input tokens/request, 58982 shared tokens within a family, 100 output tokens, greedy/seed 1234/ignore EOS. Each independent start has a cold round and two reuse rounds, clients 8/16; warmup is excluded. Each table row combines two equal-sized reuse rounds (192 requests).

| Independent start | Clients | PC TTFT | PC + CPU Offload TTFT | Reduction | PC NPU hit | Offload NPU / CPU hit |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 8 | 34.043 s | 7.565 s | 77.78% | 0.00% | 0.00% / 75.00% |
| 1 | 16 | 99.324 s | 21.839 s | 78.01% | 0.00% | 0.00% / 75.00% |
| 2 | 8 | 32.984 s | 7.526 s | 77.18% | 0.00% | 0.00% / 75.00% |
| 2 | 16 | 95.915 s | 20.996 s | 78.11% | 0.00% | 0.00% / 75.00% |
| 3 | 8 | 33.099 s | 7.244 s | 78.11% | 0.00% | 0.00% / 75.00% |
| 3 | 16 | 95.403 s | 21.061 s | 77.92% | 0.00% | 0.00% / 75.00% |

Hit-rate denominator: all input tokens in the two reuse rounds (192 x 65536), not only cache queries. All 3456 formal requests completed with 100 output tokens; observed preemptions across formal rounds: 0.

Cold rounds include initial cache population; positive change below means higher TTFT:

| Independent start | Clients | Cold PC TTFT | Cold offload TTFT | Offload change vs PC |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 8 | 37.010 s | 35.865 s | -3.09% |
| 1 | 16 | 101.174 s | 100.289 s | -0.87% |
| 2 | 8 | 36.071 s | 34.721 s | -3.74% |
| 2 | 16 | 97.414 s | 96.807 s | -0.62% |
| 3 | 8 | 34.762 s | 34.435 s | -0.94% |
| 3 | 16 | 97.461 s | 97.065 s | -0.41% |

These are paired results for enabling offload in the complete integration, not a speedup attributable to any single file. CPU reload and device-local hits are separately checked using prompt-token source counters. Three 64K marker requests per independent run verify content after device-only cache reset; task accuracy is evaluated separately:

- GSM8K standard: PC 1248/1319, offload 1249/1319; delta +0.0758 percentage points. Descriptive paired normal 95% interval: [-0.6371, +0.7887] points; correct-to-wrong / wrong-to-correct: 11 / 12.
  Invalid answers PC/offload: 0/0; output-limit finishes: 0/0. These rows remain in the score denominator, with no exclusion or retry.
- GSM8K long: PC 1246/1319, offload 1250/1319; delta +0.3033 percentage points. Descriptive paired normal 95% interval: [-0.3613, +0.9679] points; correct-to-wrong / wrong-to-correct: 8 / 12.
  Invalid answers PC/offload: 0/0; output-limit finishes: 1/1. These rows remain in the score denominator, with no exclusion or retry.

Both accuracy suites use the same eight-shot examples, last-number scorer, temperature 0, seed 1234 and output limit 512. The long-context suite prepends an 18K-token background and resets device cache before each batch of eight; CPU cache is preserved only in the Offload arm. CPU reload is confirmed per batch, while later requests within a batch can also hit NPU cache. This accuracy workload is distinct from the 64K rotating performance workload.

On the earlier vLLM `f48700f5` candidate, the initial 128-question long-context comparison failed the original 2-point limit: PC 125/128 versus offload 122/128 (-2.34375 points). That failure is retained. Predeclared diagnostic repeats yielded offload 122/128 and 125/128; serial device-cache-only repeats also changed answers before any CPU reload. A separate entirely-offload-disabled control showed changed correctness between hot repeats in 5 of 10 targeted case/repetition groups.

Before observing the expanded results, the long-context evaluation was increased to the entire fixed 1319-question test set, preserving prompts, scorer, sampling, serving configuration and the 2-point tolerance. Both arms ran once; the original failed 128 result was not replaced by a selected retry. Expanded-run first-128 subset: PC 122/128, offload 124/128. The full-set result above was rerun with the final live-block-table revision; earlier passing full-set scores were not reused. It is not a claim that the initial check passed.

On that earlier candidate, an instrumented diagnostic checked every transferred byte of real-model D2H/H2D pages on all 8 NPU ranks; all recorded comparisons matched. This is historical transfer-path evidence, not a byte audit of the final scheduler revision. Its synchronization is absent from the final full-set accuracy and performance runs. These byte checks do not prove every possible checkpoint lifecycle or rule out every asynchronous race. The original aborted Offload server text log was accidentally overwritten during diagnosis; raw accuracy responses/metrics and partial performance records remain preserved.

The predeclared observed accuracy-loss tolerances are 1 percentage point (standard) and 2 points (long context). Passing them is not a proof of lossless equivalence or statistical non-inferiority. GPU serving, disk I/O, other models beyond the Qwen regression, and long-duration CPU-pool churn are not established by this run.

Actual runtime: vLLM `6b400f91586ece036ae6d5ecfa0b42f4a3b9c19f` plus Ascend integration [`e32e105a08`](https://github.com/Liuchenbing-2026/vllm-ascend/commit/e32e105a086095244ab9891d81b38978b649e965), branch `task4-cpuoffload-main-integration-20261008`. The integration includes Offload `0a07a4d81059cb948e77b3f961ca4e9c74aaf7d9` and separate latest-main API/sampling/Engram compatibility changes; the minimal Offload branch alone is not the complete tested runtime. Base image: `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend@sha256:243bf20fad2f4f6de56aa1b041bcdfdbe5bb9d485f3190f40f1c5d0f418fc469`. Ascend native code was freshly built; the Offload changes are Python-only.

</details>

## Details

The pre-submission search and source comparison found no equivalent fix for these two SimpleCPU paths: current main still reconstructs CPU configuration with `dataclasses.replace` and selects eager stores from append-only request placement. Related work on transfer metrics, other connectors and physical-ID deduplication does not preserve this metadata or reject a single stale page belonging to another request.

`dataclasses.replace` copies declared dataclass fields and loses extra fields attached by hardware plugins. A shallow copy preserves those fields, after which this function replaces `num_blocks` and `kv_cache_tensors` with its existing derived values. This adds no transfer state machine, model predicate, environment variable, modelrunner behavior or new public option.

The eager-store selector now reads `KVConnectorBlockState.get_block_ids(req_id)` before choosing candidate pages. SWA recycling or copy-on-write can invalidate append-only placement; using the live table prevents saving a recycled page under the wrong request. This reuses the existing placement interface and changes neither the confirmation boundary nor CPU eviction policy. The metadata copy occurs during configuration derivation; the live-table lookup occurs in the existing scheduler store-selection path. Both fixes are needed by the tested hybrid configuration. The NPU integration also needs the companion Ascend implementation linked above; this change alone does not claim to enable NPU offload or provide the table's speedup.

---
