title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5] Fused decode with the MonoKernel in vLLM
body:
## Overview

Opt-in decode path for GLM-5 (`glm_moe_dsa`) on ROCm gfx950. With `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1` (the switch DeepSeek-V4.1 uses, #60397), each decoder layer of a pure decode step (3 dense, 75 MoE) runs as one FlyDSL MonoKernel launch per GPU. That launch includes the sparse indexer and both tensor-parallel all-reduces.

The kernel lives under `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd/ops/mono/`; the vLLM side is `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd/mono/`. The kernel comes from ROCm/FlyDSL#1204 and ROCm/ATOM#2435, with the paged indexer, the dense-layer mode and fixes from ROCm/aiter#6173. This PR replaces #60216.

Follows the MonoKernel standard proposed in #60904: one `forward_layer` call per layer, refusals that list every reason, bounded waits with fail-stop, checked weight views, the kernel under `ops/mono/` trimmed with an assembly-identity proof, and CPU plus MI355 CI.

## Claims

Same build for both arms, only the flag differs. MI355X, GLM-5.3 MXFP4, fp8 KV.

- TP8: TPOT -46% at concurrency 4 and -32% at 8 (8K input / 1K output); -26% and -18% (60K / 600).
- TP4: TPOT 1.83x faster at concurrency 1 (8K / 256).
- Accuracy: full GSM8K (1319 questions) within run-to-run noise (McNemar p = 0.79 at TP8, no consistent difference over 3+3 runs at TP4); NIAH 20/20 up to 128K at TP4 and TP8.
- Default off. Steps the kernel does not cover keep the regular layers and their CUDA graphs.

## How it plugs in

- **One routing call per layer.** `DeepseekV32Model.forward` calls `mono.forward_layer(...)` in its layer loop. On a kernel step, each layer is one launch and returns `(zeros, residual)`; the final norm reads the residual. Otherwise the call is the regular layer.
- **Built after weight loading.** `process_weights_after_loading` views or repacks the weights once. The per-width kernels are built on the first eager decode step, before CUDA graph capture; reaching the path first inside capture raises.
- **Refusals with every reason, in three places.**
  - At config time: gfx950 with 256 CUs, `glm_moe_dsa`, TP 4 or 8, fp8 KV, V2 model runner, FULL decode graphs. No PP, DP, EP, EPLB, DCP/PCP, speculative decoding, LoRA, KV transfer, routed-expert capture, prompt embeds, sleep mode or CPU offload.
  - After loading: fused shared experts, the MoE layout and the RoPE tables.
  - Per step: 1, 2, 4 or 8 tokens, one token per request, no PIECEWISE graph. Anything else takes the regular path.
- **Cache re-check.** The KV cache and block-table layout are re-validated whenever their address or size changes.

## Safety

- Every mailbox wait in the kernel is bounded (`POLL_LIMIT`). An expired wait sets its stage's error word and this rank's flag on rank 0, then finishes the launch instead of hanging.
- After each step, the host reads the error words without blocking the stream. On an expired wait, ranks other than 0 exit, and rank 0 raises after dumping tracebacks. `VLLM_MONO_UNSAFE_WARN=1` only logs.
- `VLLM_MONO_FAULT_INJECT="rank=R,step=N,us=D"` stalls one rank for tests; unset, no code is generated.
- `EngineCore` batch-queue fix: a failed forward is re-raised instead of returning `None`.

## Weights and numerics

- Weights are viewed where the kernel reads them as stored. Shapes, dtypes and contiguity are checked, with a clear error. The MXFP4 experts are checked as contiguous bytes in the TP-shard layout.
- Declared at startup: expert inputs are quantized to MXFP8 (vLLM: MXFP4), and TP all-reduces run in BF16 inside the launch.

## Validation

MI355X, GLM-5.3 MXFP4, a ROCm build of vLLM `43b4aaea` with this branch's `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd/` and `envs.py` on top. Both arms use the same build and differ only in the flag.

**Kernel code.** The kernel now keeps only the variant vLLM builds; dropping the unreachable branches leaves the compiled code unchanged. All 20 distinct kernels built by the op tests and the latency bench at TP4 and TP8 have byte-identical instruction streams before and after. Their outputs hash identically, and per-layer latency is unchanged.

**Tests.**
- CPU: `tests/models/deepseek_v32/amd_mono/test_glm_mono_routing.py` (refusals, step routing, cache re-check, fail-stop) and `test_glm_mono_weights.py`: 55 passed.
- GPU (4x MI355X): the MoE, dense and paged-indexer op tests pass at TP4 and TP8. `test_glm_mono_safety.py` checks 300 graph replays bit-identical at 2, 4 and 8 rows, and a fault run (rank 1 stalled 2 s) finishes with every rank reporting the expired stages and rank 0 seeing all four flags.
- Buildkite: the CPU tests join "Basic Models Other"; a new MI355 step runs the GPU tests.

**Cost of the bounded waits.** Per layer +0.2% to +1.3% depending on width and TP (for example 61.9 to 62.5 us at TP4, 2 rows). Against the previous revision (unbounded waits), two TP4 servers side by side, swapped across two rounds: TPOT 6.28 to 6.35 ms at concurrency 1 (+1.0%) and 8.72 to 8.80 ms at 4 (+0.9%) (8K / 256).

**Serving, TP8.** `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, fixed lengths, `--ignore-eos`.

| ISL/OSL | Concurrency | TPOT off | TPOT on | Change | Output tok/s off | on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8192/1024 | 1 | 11.67 ms | 5.26 ms | -54.9% | 83.7 | 181.0 |
| 8192/1024 | 2 | 12.22 ms | 5.60 ms | -54.2% | 153.9 | 314.4 |
| 8192/1024 | 4 | 12.69 ms | 6.83 ms | -46.2% | 292.3 | 515.4 |
| 8192/1024 | 8 | 14.28 ms | 9.64 ms | -32.5% | 514.9 | 710.3 |
| 60000/600 | 4 | 17.87 ms | 13.25 ms | -25.9% | 145.3 | 174.8 |
| 60000/600 | 8 | 30.89 ms | 25.33 ms | -18.0% | 185.9 | 198.1 |

**Serving, TP4.** Same setup, 256 output tokens. Median TPOT and inter-token latency (ITL):

| ISL | Concurrency | TPOT off | TPOT on | Speedup | ITL p99 off | on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1 | 12.81 ms | 6.46 ms | 1.98x | 13.01 ms | 6.55 ms |
| 1024 | 8 | 15.38 ms | 12.22 ms | 1.26x | 15.67 ms | 12.36 ms |
| 8192 | 1 | 11.58 ms | 6.31 ms | 1.83x | 11.70 ms | 6.43 ms |
| 8192 | 2 | 12.50 ms | 7.16 ms | 1.75x | 12.41 ms | 6.72 ms |
| 8192 | 4 | 15.29 ms | 8.82 ms | 1.73x | 14.08 ms | 8.56 ms |
| 8192 | 8 | 17.95 ms | 17.25 ms | 1.04x | 114.59 ms | 117.96 ms |
| 32768 | 1 | 11.83 ms | 6.75 ms | 1.75x | 12.01 ms | 7.48 ms |
| 32768 | 8 | 37.00 ms | 36.23 ms | 1.02x | 639.30 ms | 635.59 ms |

At concurrency 8 the TPOT includes the prefills that interleave with decode (p99 ITL); those steps take the regular path.

**Accuracy.**

| Eval | Flag off | Flag on |
|---|---|---|
| TP4, GSM8K 5-shot strict, 1319 questions, 8 concurrent, 3 runs | 0.897 / 0.884 / 0.900 | 0.889 / 0.901 / 0.904 |
| TP8, GSM8K, same setup, 1 run | 0.889 | 0.892 |
| TP4 and TP8, NIAH at 8K/32K/60K/128K, 20 prompts | 20/20 | 20/20 |

- McNemar (exact) over per-question results: on vs off p = 0.79 at TP8. At TP4 the nine on/off pairs give p from 0.03 to 1.0, and the one pair below 0.05 favours the flag on; off/off pairs give 0.08 to 0.80.
- Greedy agreement, 32 prompts, 64 tokens: the first 8 tokens match the regular path for 9-10 prompts, and every token is in its top 5 for 25-26 prompts. Two regular-path servers against each other give 6 and 29: this stack is not run-to-run deterministic, so this check only bounds the drift.

**Startup.** Cold start at TP8 is 1148 s with the flag vs 1027 s without (+2 min, FlyDSL builds the kernels for four widths; most of both is AITER JIT in a fresh container).

**Not covered.** Stage outputs are compared with the kernel's own references, not with vLLM's ops. The GPU tests need gfx950 and the GLM-5 checkpoint.

<details>
<summary>Server command (TP8)</summary>

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_SPARSE_INDEXER=1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-model-len 258048 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --async-scheduling --trust-remote-code \
  --compilation-config '{"pass_config": {"fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla": true}, "use_inductor_graph_partition": true}' \
  --hf-overrides '{"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": 4, "index_share_for_mtp_iteration": false}'
```

The baseline is the same command with `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=0`.
</details>

title: [ROCm][Perf][Qwen3.8] Mono decode layer for Qwen3.8 on MI355X
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->


## Overview

**Draft, stacked on #60683; #61325 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) is stacked on this PR.** Until #60683 merges, the compare view also shows #60683's two commits (`c8a3845fb0`, `5efc7825e2`, its earlier head rebased onto main at `2eb491e18b`); this PR is the commits after them: 4,715 added lines in 16 files ([this PR's commits only](https://github.com/mjkvaak-amd/vllm-project/compare/5efc7825e2...rocm/qwen38-mono-decode); Files changed shows 10.9k, #60683's 6.1k included).

This PR ports the Kimi-K3 mono decode (#60683, @hyukjlee) to Qwen3.8 (`Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`, `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`) at TP8 on MI355X (gfx950). It is opt-in behind the existing `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1`. On pure decode steps of up to 8 rows, and on MTP verify steps of up to 8 rows, each decoder layer runs as at most two persistent launches instead of the stock chain of GEMMs, norms, all-reduces and MoE kernels. It reuses #60683's mono framework (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/mono/common`): mailboxes, the peer buffer and the GEMV stage. The MoE, GDN and host code are written as a shared Qwen mono base (`vllm/models/qwen3_5/amd/mono/{moe,gdn}.py`, `mono_base.py`) parameterized by shape dataclasses, which #61325 reuses at Flash-Next's TP2 shapes.

Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs for "mono decode", "mono decode Qwen" and "Qwen3.8 mono". #60683 (Kimi-K3) and #60397 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) are the same technique for other models; neither covers GDN layers or softmax top-10 routing.

## Claims

Measured on `nightly-8cbd5d03`; TPOT, NIAH and the model-card GSM8K at `3346929b27`; GSM8K lm_eval and GPQA at `6a1c13b2fc`; MTP at this head. The two older revisions compute the same outputs bit for bit: the one path that changed (x quantized once by the norm CTAs at 6–8 rows) was asserted bitwise equal to the path kept. The move to the shared base leaves the kernels as they were: K2's ISA, and that of every K1 variant without the split `in_proj_ba`, is byte-identical to `3346929b27`'s.

- Mean TPOT −48.2% at concurrency 1, −32.6% at 4 and −22.0% at 8 (8k/1k); −52.0% at 60k/600 concurrency 1. `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4` TP8 on MI355X; see End to end.
- No loss past the 8-row cutoff: from concurrency 12 to 64, TPOT matches stock to within ±0.6% at 1k and 8k ISL. The gain at concurrency 8 shrinks from −24% at 1k to −6% at 128k ISL; see Where it stops helping.
- Launches per decode step 1684 → 1160 (8k/64, concurrency 4): no MoE launches and one all-reduce left; K1 + K2 are 161 of them.
- Accuracy unchanged: GSM8K with the model card's recipe 0.971 → 0.971 (all 1,319 questions, 8 threads). RULER NIAH (single 2), two paired runs: 0.888 → 0.896 and 0.856 → 0.864 at 64k, 0.760 → 0.796 and 0.766 → 0.794 at 128k, p ≥ 0.14. GPQA Diamond 0.924 → 0.934 at 8 client threads (unpaired; within noise).
- With MTP-3, verify steps on the kernels take mean TPOT from 3.48 to 3.03 ms at 8k/1k concurrency 1 (−13%), 4.19 → 3.88 ms at concurrency 2 (−7%) and 3.47 → 3.03 ms at 60k/600 concurrency 1 (−13%). GSM8K with every verify step on the kernels (2 threads) 0.969 → 0.973, mean acceptance length 3.77 in both; at 8 threads, where verify steps switch between the kernels and the stock path, 0.973 → 0.971 (3.73 / 3.72); see MTP.

## Validation

**Unit tests.**

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen3_5/test_amd_mono.py tests/models/qwen3_5/test_amd_mono_layout.py tests/models/qwen3_5/test_amd_mono_decode.py
```

55 passed on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-8cbd5d03006c33185f402249ff2b448efd594986` plus this branch, 8x MI355X: 13 in `test_amd_mono.py` and 42 host-only in the other two. `test_amd_mono_decode.py` (host only) covers the refusals, with every reason reported at once, including the MTP ones, and the per-step routing: decode steps and MTP verify steps of 1–8 rows take the kernels, prefills, wider steps and piecewise cudagraph steps do not.

- `test_amd_mono_layout.py` (4, host only): every fp4 byte and e8m0 scale of a routed expert, as aiter's `AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4` shuffles leave them after loading, is at the address K2 reads.
- `test_amd_mono.py::test_k1_matches_vllm_ops` (8, 1 GPU): K1 against AITER's conv update and fused gated delta rule, `GemmaRMSNorm` and `RMSNormGated`, at widths 1, 5 (4 real rows) and 8, and on the first layer, with `in_proj_qkvz` bf16 and online MXFP4. It checks the residual, conv state, SSM state and core output, that pad rows output zero, and that the null block is left untouched. Fed K1's own projections, the conv state matches exactly and the SSM state within 1e-6; end to end, the states are within 5e-4 and the core output's cosine is above 0.9999.
- `test_amd_mono.py::test_k2_tp8_matches_vllm_ops` (1, 8 GPUs): K2 against o_proj + all-reduce + `fused_add_rms_norm` + softmax top-10 renormalized routing + the MXFP4 experts + the sigmoid-gated shared expert, at widths 1, 3, 4, 8 and 8 again (both epoch parities); all ranks must agree. The MoE is checked against a torch emulation of the stock decode kernel's numerics (cosine > 0.9999), and against aiter's `fused_moe` itself (cosine > 0.9995, because that kernel's output varies from run to run; K2 measures 0.99994–0.99997). Over 40 repeated launches K2 is bitwise identical on all eight ranks. Four weight layouts are covered: bf16, the fused shared expert with the bf16 o_proj (with and without the attention output gate), and the fused shared expert with the MXFP4 out_proj.

Both kernels compile for widths 1–8 at gfx950 with no VGPR spills. K1 uses up to 139 KB of LDS and K2 up to 145 KB.

**Kernel evidence.** Torch-profiler trace at `f6e9c99ed2` (before the attention-front fusion and the faster kernels), 8k/64 at concurrency 4, per decode step (both arms the same image, only `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE` differs):

| Per decode step | Stock | Mono |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Launches | 1684 | 1160 |
| Kernel time | 14.94 ms | 14.08 ms |
| MoE launches | `fmoe` (≈32 µs each) + routing / sorting | 0 |
| Separate TP all-reduce launches | ≈22 µs each | 1 (the rest in-kernel) |
| K2 / K1 launches | — | 92 / 69 |
| Eager native ops (attention front) | 179 | 870 |
| TPOT in the trace run | 26.61 ms | 22.80 ms |

Per launch in that trace: K2 52 / 61 / 80 µs at 1 / 2 / 4 rows; K1 26 µs at 1 row and 33 µs at 4. K2 now measures 28.0 / 38.8 / 51.4 / 80.5 µs at 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 rows and K1 11.7 / 13.6 / 17.0 / 26.0 µs (graph replay, 8 ranks, weekly-best weight layouts). The 870 eager ops are the 23 full-attention layers' front (split, q/k `GemmaRMSNorm`, RoPE, input norm, gate), which this uncompiled forward ran as native ops at ~3.4 ms GPU time a step. `f3c2ec988b` replaces them with the fused Triton kernel the CUDA path uses plus two compiled elementwise helpers.

**End to end.** MI355X, `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4` TP8, `nightly-8cbd5d03` plus this branch; the arms differ only in `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE`. The stock arm ran on an image of the previous revision, which with `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=0` runs identical code. Both arms run the weekly-best stock flags this nightly has (fused shared expert, online-MXFP4 shared expert and GDN projections on the ASM FP4 GEMM, FlyDSL GDN prefill, 512 MB QuickReduce cap), with empty vLLM and AITER caches. The stock arm reproduces an earlier run on the same nightly to within 0.2 ms TPOT.

| ISL / OSL | Conc (prompts) | Output tok/s, before → after | Mean TTFT (ms, lower is better) | Mean TPOT (ms, lower is better) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8k / 1k | 1 (8) | 99.75 → 187.06 | 329.54 → 326.71 | 9.71 → 5.03 (−48.2%) |
| 8k / 1k | 2 (12) | 187.66 → 293.00 | 513.59 → 504.74 | 10.16 → 6.34 (−37.6%) |
| 8k / 1k | 4 (16) | 312.90 → 448.32 | 851.16 → 888.12 | 11.96 → 8.06 (−32.6%) |
| 8k / 1k | 8 (32) | 480.79 → 600.38 | 1147.47 → 1252.49 | 15.52 → 12.11 (−22.0%) |
| 60k / 600 | 1 (6) | 63.59 → 92.80 | 3054.29 → 3402.04 | 10.65 → 5.11 (−52.0%) |
| 60k / 600 | 4 (16) | 129.60 → 148.13 | 5412.98 → 5748.12 | 21.83 → 17.42 (−20.2%) |

Prefill runs the same stock code in both arms. Median TTFT is within 4% of stock in every cell except 60k/600 at concurrency 4, where it is 13% higher (5,116 → 5,788 ms). The previous revision measured the same there; I have not isolated why. The 60k concurrency-1 mean is one slow request (median 3,009 → 2,998 ms).

**Where it stops helping.** A wider sweep on the branch's previous revision, `6a1c13b2fc` (one run per cell, `sglang.bench_serving`, random dataset, OSL 1k). That revision's K2 is up to 5% faster at 6–8 rows; on the cells above it is within 1.3% TPOT of this one. The kernels cover decode steps of at most 8 rows. Past concurrency 8 most steps are wider and take the stock path, so the two arms run the same code and match to within run-to-run noise. Nothing regresses past the cutoff. Below it, the gain shrinks as context grows, because attention, which the kernels leave alone, takes a larger share of the step.

| ISL | Conc (prompts) | Output tok/s, stock → mono | Mean TPOT (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1k | 1 (8) | 101.7 → 196.6 | 9.71 → 4.96 (−48.9%) |
| 1k | 8 (32) | 553.8 → 725.3 | 14.05 → 10.63 (−24.3%) |
| 1k | 12 (36) | 641.3 → 640.7 | 18.13 → 18.24 (+0.6%) |
| 1k | 16 (48) | 846.0 → 849.5 | 18.37 → 18.29 (−0.4%) |

GSM8K lm_eval and NIAH are paired per question (same seed and prompts); in neither eval do the flips favour either arm. With the model card's chat recipe both arms score 0.971, against the card's 97.49; the lm_eval 5-shot completion prompts score lower (0.707–0.727) in both arms because they don't use the chat template. The NIAH rerun used the OOB benchmark config's settings (`niah_single_2` at 64k and 128k, 8 concurrent) on this revision's image and reproduces the first run within noise in both arms. Its generations differ between the arms on 96–98% of prompts, which is ordinary run-to-run churn for this model: the stock arm's own three GSM8K runs spread as widely. The stock GSM8K lm_eval arm ran on an earlier image of this branch with the same nightly and flags; with `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=0` the two images run identical code.

**MTP-3** (`--speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` as stock MTP needs here), stock vs mono in the same image, `nightly-8cbd5d03` plus this branch, same flags as End to end. A verify step has 4 rows a request, so concurrency 1 and 2 run on the kernels; concurrency 4 (16 rows) runs stock in both arms, which gives the noise floor.

| ISL / OSL | Conc (prompts) | Mean TPOT (ms), stock → mono |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8k / 1k | 1 (8) | 3.48 → 3.03 (−13%) |
| 8k / 1k | 2 (12) | 4.19 → 3.88 (−7%) |
| 8k / 1k | 4 (16), stock in both | 5.53 → 5.42 |
| 60k / 600 | 1 (6) | 3.47 → 3.03 (−13%) |

GSM8K with MTP-3, model card recipe at 2 threads, so every verify step runs on the kernels: 0.969 stock, 0.973 mono; mean acceptance length 3.77 in both. At 8 threads verify steps have 4–32 rows, so the run switches between the kernels and the stock path from step to step: 0.973 stock, 0.971 mono (3 questions of 1,319), mean acceptance length 3.73 / 3.72. In a torch-profiler trace (8k, concurrency 2) a verify step takes 14.6 ms of GPU time and 1,442 launches on the kernels. The GDN core's gated norm, run eagerly in the uncompiled mono forward, first cost ~12 kernels a layer (16.3 ms and 2,167 launches, TPOT −4% at concurrency 1 and +2% at 2). It now runs as one compiled launch, matching `RMSNormGated.forward_native` bitwise except one element in 2,048 off by one bf16 rounding step.

**Every eval keeps at most 8 requests in flight, so every decode step is within the kernels' 8-row cap.**

**Race stress.** #60397's AIME gap came from a per-width scratch race between consecutive steps of different widths. `test_amd_mono.py::test_mixed_width_graph_replay` (8 GPUs) captures K1 and K2 of two layers (the bf16 layouts, then the weekly-best ones) over six consecutive decode steps of widths 8, 1, 3, 8, 2, 5, with pad rows, in one HIP graph, as a FULL decode graph holds them. Replayed 300 times, every output and every conv / SSM state is bitwise equal to the eager run each time, and all eight ranks agree. The serving evals above also run at mixed widths: up to 8 requests in flight, finishing at different times.

**Reproduce:**

```bash
# the stock arm: the same command with VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=0
VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
AITER_USE_FLYDSL_MOE_SORTING=1 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 \
VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MAX_SIZE_BYTES_MB=512 \
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4 -tp 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 262144 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --gdn-prefill-backend aiter_flydsl --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --compilation-config '{"splitting_ops": [], "pass_config": {"fuse_rope_kvcache": true, "enable_qk_norm_rope_fusion": true, "fuse_allreduce_rms": true}}' \
  --quantization-config.targets '{"*shared_expert*": "mxfp4", "*linear_attn.in_proj_qkv": "mxfp4", "*linear_attn.in_proj_z": "mxfp4", "*linear_attn.out_proj": "mxfp4"}'

# End to end (one cell; the table's cells vary ISL / OSL, concurrency, prompts and seed)
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm --model amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 8 --warmup-requests 1 --seed 41

# GSM8K, model card recipe
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --host localhost --port 8000 \
  --model amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4 --num-threads 8 --num-examples 1319 --max-tokens 2048 \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'

# GSM8K lm_eval (run 3 times a side), NIAH
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 8 --seed 1234 --log_samples \
  --output_path gsm8k --model_args '{"model":"amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4","base_url":"http://localhost:8000/v1/completions","num_concurrent":8,"tokenized_requests":false,"max_retries":3,"timeout":1200}'
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks niah_single_2 --metadata '{"max_seq_lengths":[65536,131072]}' \
  --batch_size auto --seed 1234 --log_samples --output_path niah \
  --model_args '{"model":"amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4","tokenizer":"amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4","base_url":"http://localhost:8000/v1/completions","num_concurrent":8,"tokenized_requests":false}'
```

## Details

**Path.** The step is chosen as a whole in `Qwen3_5ForCausalLMBase.forward`, the uncompiled outer forward. Eligible steps are pure decode or MTP verify steps, 1–8 rows, no `inputs_embeds` or intermediate tensors, no Eagle3 aux layers, and not a piecewise cudagraph step (those graphs also serve short prefills, so they must be captured from the stock model). They run the mono forward; everything else runs the stock compiled model unchanged. The FULL decode graph captures the mono forward once per width, and vLLM's eager warmup at each capture size compiles the kernels before capture.

- **K1** (69 GDN layers): residual add + `input_layernorm` → `in_proj_qkvz` / `in_proj_ba` → causal conv1d update → gated delta rule → `RMSNormGated`, writing `out_proj`'s input. No cross-rank traffic.
- **K2** (all 92 layers): `out_proj` / `o_proj` + its TP all-reduce → residual add + `post_attention_layernorm` → softmax top-10 renormalized router → MXFP4 routed experts → sigmoid-gated shared expert → MoE all-reduce.
- **Full-attention layers** (23) run vLLM's `qkv_proj` and attention, with the input norm, q/k norm + RoPE and output gate as one fused Triton kernel plus two compiled elementwise helpers (`f3c2ec988b`), then K2.
- **MTP verify steps:** a request's rows are consecutive tokens of one sequence, and K1's recurrence keeps no per-draft-token state to roll back rejected drafts. So a GDN layer runs the input norm, vLLM's `in_proj_qkvz` / `in_proj_ba`, then vLLM's GDN core (`qwen_gdn_attention_core` on the step's spec-decode metadata) and the gated norm compiled into one launch, then K2. Full-attention layers and K2 run as on decode steps, so `out_proj` / `o_proj`, the all-reduces and the MoE stay on the kernels.

**Design decisions.**
- The dispatch is at the model level rather than per layer as in #60683. The Qwen3.8 serving config runs a FULL decode graph with no breakable cudagraph, so per-layer eager breaks are no-ops. Choosing the whole step keeps the compiled stock path byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **Numerics contract:** K1 reproduces AITER's decode kernels, including the conv's bf16 rounding of each product and softplus threshold 20. Pad rows (state index ≤ 0) write no state and output zero. Both residual add + norm stages follow vLLM's native `fused_add_rms_norm`, which `GemmaRMSNorm` uses: the residual is stored rounded to bf16, but the norm reads the unrounded fp32 sum.
- **Routed experts:** at 1–8 rows, stock runs AITER's one-stage `fmoe_bf16_pertokenMXfp4_g1u1_flat`. It takes bf16 input but runs both x and silu(g)·u through dynamic MXFP4 (1×32 blocks, scale `ceil_pow2(amax / 6)`). K2 does the same, and feeds the codes to the scaled fp4 MFMA.
- **Buffers:** each width has its own scratch for K1 and for K2. The peer buffer layout is width-independent, so consecutive steps of different widths never share a region; this guards against the #60397 race class. Mailbox tags carry a device epoch bumped once per step, so nothing is zeroed between steps.
- **Refusals, as in #60397:** an explicit `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1` that cannot run raises at init, listing every reason (CDNA4, TP8, no PP, no expert / data / context parallelism or EPLB, no LoRA, spec decode only as MTP with at most 7 draft tokens and AITER's Triton GDN kernels, no KV connector, at least 256 CUs so the grid is resident). A weight layout the kernels cannot read raises at the first decode step (`AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4` experts shuffled and all local, `in_proj_qkvz` and `out_proj` / `o_proj` bf16 or online MXFP4 on the ASM FP4 GEMM, the other dense weights bf16, `A_log` fp32). A model variant outside the kernels (other shapes, a replicated shared expert, layer scale, sequence parallelism) stays on the stock path, logged once. Launch arguments are checked with `ValueError`, not `assert`.
- **RFC #60904:** the layout follows #60397 as merged (`amd/mono_decode.py` + `amd/mono/`). The runtime still comes from #60683's `kimi_k3/amd/mono/common`: main's `deepseek_v41/amd/mono/common` lacks pieces K1 / K2 use (`ranks`, sync `shift`, the GEMV stage's API), and the RFC moves this code to a shared `common/mono/` once more models land. Bounded waits, error words and fail-stop are not in yet; they come with the shared library.

**Shared code.** `qwen3_5.py` gains 8 lines: the import, the constructor hook and the forward dispatch. With the env var unset, or off ROCm, `_mono` is `None` and nothing else changes; CUDA is unaffected.

Within `vllm/models/qwen3_5/amd/`, code a second Qwen model can use is split out of Qwen3.8's kernels, after #61482's `MonoSpec` / `Dims`:
- `mono/moe.py` on `MoeDims`: the fp4 GEMV, x quantization, `o_proj`, the route, the expert stages and the split-K row reduction;
- `mono/gdn.py` on `GdnDims`: the GDN tasks (conv, gates, recurrence, norm, `in_proj_ba` with the K split a parameter), with the model's b / a source and z gate as hooks;
- `mono_base.py` (`QwenMonoDecode`): the refusals, the step gate, the buffers, the weight checks' common part and the MTP verify steps. `mono_decode.py` keeps Qwen3.8's shape checks, weights and forward.

**Limitations and CI gaps.**
- **Scope:** TP8, gfx950, MXFP4 W4A4 routed experts only. gfx942 is not supported because the MXFP4 checkpoint does not run there and the kernels target gfx950 MFMA and LDS sizes. On gfx942 an explicit `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1` raises at init (the CDNA4 refusal).
- **MTP:** only verify steps of up to 8 rows run on the kernels: 2 requests at `num_speculative_tokens` 3. Larger batches verify on the stock path. The GDN core of a verify step is vLLM's. Other spec-decode methods are refused.
- **CI:** the numerics tests need gfx950 and 8 GPUs; the host-only tests run in the same step.
- **Size:** 3,515 lines under `vllm/models/qwen3_5/amd/`: 2,712 of kernels (`mono/layer.py`, `gdn.py`, `moe.py`), 633 of host code (`mono_base.py`, `mono_decode.py`) and 170 of layout and sources. Tests add 1,171 lines. Each kernel builds one fixed schedule per width and layout, with no tuning switches.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Apply paged MXFP4 sparse indexer dense path for DeepSeek-V4
body:
## Purpose

#58671 added a paged MXFP4 sparse indexer for DeepSeek-V4.1 on ROCm gfx950. The indexer K cache is stored as MXFP4 (68 B per token instead of 132 B for FP8) in the preshuffled page order that aiter's `pa_mqa_logits_mxfp4` reads. That kernel scores the cache in place, so prefill no longer gathers K first. The PR has two layers:

- the **dense** path, which scores the whole context. It is model-agnostic.
- the **candidate-pool** path, which only exists because of V4.1's two-level indexer.

This PR brings the dense path to DeepSeek-V4 (e.g. DeepSeek-V4-Pro: 30 indexer layers at compress ratio 4, 64 heads × 128, top-k 1024). Today V4 on ROCm can only use the FP8 indexer cache, because:

- `dsa_indexer_uses_fp4()` rejects every model except `deepseek_v41` on ROCm;
- `SparseAttnIndexer.forward_hip` asserts that the cache is not FP4;
- V4's own MXFP4 Q/K Triton kernels pack FP4 with CUDA PTX (`cvt.rn.satfinite.e2m1x2.f32`), so they cannot run on ROCm.

The feature is opt-in, as on V4.1:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro -tp 8 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "mxfp4"}'
```

The default path (FP8 indexer cache) is unchanged.

## Changes

### K write: ROCm pooling kernel + aiter's cache op

In V4 the indexer K is produced by the indexer's own `DeepseekCompressor`. One fused Triton kernel does pool → RMSNorm → RoPE → MXFP4 → cache store, and nothing before the norm ever reaches memory. On ROCm we split it into two launches:

1. A new Triton kernel, `_compress_pool_kernel`, does the softmax-gated overlap pooling. It is copied from V4's fused kernel, up to the norm. It writes one bf16 row per boundary token into a scratch buffer that all indexer layers share (`[max_num_batched_tokens, 128]`).
2. aiter's public `k_norm_rope_mxfp4_cache(..., shuffle=layout)` then applies norm → RoPE → MXFP4 and stores into the preshuffled pages. This is the same op V4.1 uses, through the same `rocm_mxfp4_indexer_k_store` wrapper.

This keeps the page layout and the quantization defined only in aiter, which is the principle #58671 follows (`rocm_paged_mxfp4_cache_layout` is the only place vLLM reads the layout).

The cost is one extra small launch per indexer layer, plus a bf16 round trip of the pooled row before the norm. That rounding error (~2⁻⁹) is two orders of magnitude below the MXFP4 quantization step. A fully fused ROCm kernel can follow if profiles show the extra launch matters.

### Q quant

The Q path uses aiter's `q_rope_mxfp4_quant`, through the existing `rocm_mxfp4_indexer_q_quant`. It produces fp32 weights with the softmax and head scales folded in, as the aiter MQA-logits kernel expects.

### Scoring and metadata

Both are reused unchanged:

- `RocmSparseAttnIndexer`, which calls `rocm_mxfp4_sparse_attn_indexer` with no candidate blocks;
- the model-agnostic `RocmMxfp4IndexerMetadataBuilder`.

A new `DeepseekV4RocmMxfp4IndexerBackend` subclasses `DeepseekV4IndexerBackend`, so V4's 256-token blocks and ROCm adaptive-verification support carry over. At compress ratio 4 that gives 64-entry pages, which is aiter's preferred page size.

### Keeping CUDA untouched

Shared V4 code only gains extract-method / ClassVar hooks. The code inside them is moved verbatim, and the ROCm subclasses override the hooks.

### Other changes

- `FusedKVCompressNormRopeInsertIndexerTritonKernel.get_warmup_keys()` returns no keys on ROCm with an MXFP4 indexer cache. The warmup is a process-wide singleton that every non-CUDA compressor registers, including V4's head-512 attention compressors, so without this guard the PTX MXFP4 variant was compiled at startup and failed (`error: unknown asm constraint 'f'`). ROCm never runs that kernel: it writes the cache with aiter's op.
- `dsa_indexer_uses_fp4()`: the ROCm branch now accepts `deepseek_v4` as well as `deepseek_v41`. The CDNA4 and aiter checks are unchanged, and the CUDA branch is untouched.
- `_aiter_indexer_cache_ops`, `rocm_mxfp4_indexer_k_store` and `rocm_mxfp4_indexer_q_quant` move from `models/deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py` to `v1/attention/ops/rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py`, so V4 and V4.1 share them. They are still importable from the old module.

## Test Plan

### Unit Test

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_dsv4_mxfp4_indexer.py
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py
pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_rocm_compressor_gemm_fusion.py \
    tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_rocm_wo_a.py \
    tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_dspark_rocm.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_rocm_adaptive.py \
    tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
    tests/kernels/test_deepseek_v4_cpu_kernels.py
```

### Benchmark

Benchmark with SA InferenceX `8k1k` and `agentic` workload with server launch commands below.

Fixed sequence length:

```bash
vllm serve /shared/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
    --port 8333 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --data-parallel-size 1 \
    --max-model-len 9472 \
    --max-num-seqs 512 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --async-scheduling \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --distributed-executor-backend mp \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --moe-backend aiter \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 2}' \
    --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
    --load-format fastsafetensors \
    --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "mxfp4"}'
```

Agentic replay:

```bash
vllm serve /shared/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8333 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --async-scheduling \
    --distributed-executor-backend mp \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --data-parallel-size 8 \
    --prefill-schedule-interval 8 \
    --long-prefill-token-threshold 16384 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.86 \
    --moe-backend aiter \
    --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --load-format fastsafetensors \
    --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "mxfp4"}'
```

### Accuracy Test

Accuracy test with `gsm8k` dataset using `lm_eval`:

```bash
lm_eval \
  --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=/shared/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8333/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=10,max_gen_toks=2048,timeout=60000 \
  --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --output_path . 2>&1 | tee -a eval.log
```

## Test Result

### Unit Test

- New tests: 4 passed. The ROCm compressor's pages match aiter's writer fed by torch pooling byte for byte (0 mismatched bytes). As a sanity check, feeding a shifted window mismatches 21.8% of bytes, so the test does detect wrong pooling.
- V4.1 MXFP4 indexer tests: 37 passed.
- V4 ROCm / compressor tests: 99 passed, 137 skipped (platform-gated).

### Benchmark

Fixed sequence length:

| Conc | Version | Output token throughput (tok/s) |  Change | Mean TTFT (ms) |   Change | Mean TPOT (ms) |  Change |
| ---: | :------ | ------------------------------: | ------: | -------------: | -------: | -------------: | ------: |
|    1 | Main (FP8 Indexer)    |                          145.99 |       — |         597.24 |        — |           6.24 |       — |
|    1 | This PR (MXFP4 Indexer) |                          156.34 | 7.09% ↑ |         413.91 | 30.70% ↓ |           5.96 | 4.49% ↓ |
|    4 | Main (FP8 Indexer)    |                          454.91 |       — |         504.07 |        — |           8.02 |       — |
|    4 | This PR (MXFP4 Indexer) |                          466.92 | 2.64% ↑ |         437.29 | 13.25% ↓ |           7.95 | 0.87% ↓ |
|   16 | Main (FP8 Indexer)    |                         1020.90 |       — |         744.88 |        — |          14.51 |       — |
|   16 | This PR (MXFP4 Indexer) |                         1030.30 | 0.92% ↑ |         681.89 |  8.46% ↓ |          14.46 | 0.34% ↓ |
|   64 | Main (FP8 Indexer)    |                         1629.53 |       — |        1637.36 |        — |          36.85 |       — |
|   64 | This PR (MXFP4 Indexer) |                         1656.28 | 1.64% ↑ |        1622.58 |  0.90% ↓ |          36.29 | 1.52% ↓ |

In summary, this PR delivers a clear overall improvement over Main: throughput increases across all concurrency levels, Mean TTFT decreases substantially—especially at low and medium concurrency—and Mean TPOT remains slightly better across the board. The results suggest that the optimization is beneficial for both latency-sensitive workloads and overall serving throughput, with the most pronounced gains appearing at lower concurrency.

Agentic replay:

| Indexer | Output Token Throughput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | KV Cache Capacity (tokens) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Main (FP8 Indexer) | 697.25 | 2,442.24 | 46.01 | 4,589,684 |
| This PR (MXFP4 Indexer) | 675.83 (3.07% ↓) | 2,321.05 (4.96% ↓) | 43.42 (5.62% ↓) | 5,010,749 (9.17% ↑) |

- **Latency improves: mean TPOT -5.62%, mean TTFT -4.96%.** TPOT is the most consistent signal: both MXFP4 runs (44.60 / 42.24 ms) had lower TPOT than both FP8 runs (46.98 / 45.03 ms). TTFT varied by up to 13% between runs of the same configuration, so treat its gain as indicative.
- **Output token throughput is within noise (-3.07%).** On this workload, aggregate throughput is driven mainly by the trace replay and by output lengths.
- **KV cache capacity: +9.17%.** The MXFP4 indexer cache takes 68 B per compressed token instead of 132 B, and the freed memory goes to the KV pool. Peak KV usage stayed below 40% in all runs, so this workload does not yet turn the extra KV capacity into throughput. Higher-concurrency or longer-context workloads should benefit more.

title: [Perf][Attention] Skip nonempty output rows during sparse MLA cleanup
body:
## Purpose

Rebased onto main `f7ba007b5e`. This is a performance change that preserves the
existing empty-row correctness contract, not a correctness fix. The submission
branch excludes the historical correctness-fix commit used by the benchmark runtime.

Avoid rewriting valid attention outputs when cleaning up empty sparse-attention
shards. On the tested GLM-5.2 c32 workload, this reduced TPOT by **5.98%** and
increased output throughput by **6.53%**, with lower TTFT and p99 ITL.

```text
ASIS
sparse attention -> scan Top-K indices for empty rows
                 -> masked_fill over the entire O tensor
                 -> masked_fill over LSE -> DCP combine
```

```text
PR
sparse attention -> read existing valid-token count per row
                 -> nonempty: leave O and LSE untouched
                 -> empty: write O=0 and LSE=-inf -> DCP combine
```

The index-remapping kernel already computes the required valid counts. A single
Triton launch uses one block per row and a device-side conditional, so changing
which rows are empty remains compatible with CUDA-graph replay. It replaces the
index scan and two masked fills without changing attention math, projection,
communication, or buffer ownership.

## Relationship to #48196 and #60627

This overlaps with the empty-row cleanup portion of #48196. That broader PR
also changes projection/merge ordering and can fold cleanup into A2A packing.
Its standalone cleanup kernel uses one block per row/head; this implementation
uses one block per row and loops over the output only when the row is empty.
We have **not** measured a head-to-head comparison against #48196 and do not
claim to outperform its standalone or fused implementation.

This PR isolates the cleanup change for review alongside #48196; it does not
replace the broader output-merge work. Overlap and landing order should be
coordinated with that PR's author.

This is separate from #60627, which accelerates the direct DCP Output/LSE
consumer. Both serving benchmark arms below already include #60627, so these
are incremental gains, not another measurement of that PR.

## Test Result

4x GB200 at 1800 MHz, GLM-5.2 NVFP4, TP4/DCP4/EP4, FP8 KV, FlashInfer sparse
MLA, 3072 input / 128 output tokens, c32. Prefix caching disabled, synchronous
scheduling, FULL_DECODE_ONLY/breakable CUDA graphs, compilation disabled.
Two fresh processes per arm, run in ABBA order; 128 counted requests per process
after identical correctness smoke and 32-request warmup. All 512 counted
requests succeeded.

| Metric | Baseline | PR | Improvement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TPOT | 81.548 ms | 76.672 ms | 5.98% |
| Output throughput | 340.204 tok/s | 362.425 tok/s | 6.53% |
| TTFT | 1589.456 ms | 1472.422 ms | 7.36% |
| p99 ITL | 314.744 ms | 287.427 ms | 8.68% |

Paired TPOT improvements were 5.49% and 6.47%. Process TPOT CV was 0.55% for
baseline and 0.031% for candidate. These are two-pair observations, not a
confidence interval or a claim about other workloads.

**Validation scope:** pinned runtime `71323cbf1a`, with #60627's final native
consumer in both arms and only this Python backend module substituted in the
candidate. This is not a full current-main build comparison. No split-KV
prototype or scheduler change is included.

## Why this helps

A short profile found that the BF16 output masked fill accounted for 7.92% of
summed GPU-kernel time in a mixed prefill/decode window. These batches contained
roughly 4096 tokens, exceeding the direct consumer's decode workspace. The
cleanup still traversed every output element even when no row needed changing.
The percentage describes that profile window, not all c32 serving wall time.

For 4096 rows, H=64, D=512, BF16 O and FP32 LSE, CUDA-graph operator timing
including the old mask construction and both fills:

| Empty rows | Baseline cleanup | New cleanup |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| None | 326.147 us | 2.914 us |
| One quarter | 288.615 us | 20.370 us |

These component results are separate from the serving measurements above.

## Test Plan

**Rebase validation (Oct 13):** 34 focused tests passed on GB200 using the rebased
Python/Triton sources, including four call-site cases for ordinary MLA and the
NoPE/HiSparse guard, with and without LSE. The existing NoPE guard is unchanged.
Tests reused the installed environment's native extensions and generated
FlashMLA binding; this is not a fresh current-main native build or model run.
All applicable pre-commit checks, including mypy and test-CI wiring, passed.

The optimized path still writes O=0 and LSE=-inf for empty rows, including NaN
payloads. Nonempty rows remain untouched; device-side branching handles changing
empty rows during graph replay. The valid-count tests establish equivalence to
the previous index-based empty mask.

Historical validation before the rebase:

- 30 focused repository tests passed: strided outputs, changing-input graph
  replay, FP16/BF16, NaN payloads, zero rows, and valid-count/empty-mask equivalence
  for DCP sizes 1/2/3/4/8. The latter simulates rank mappings on one GPU; it is
  not an eight-GPU distributed test.
- A separate 180-case numeric/graph sweep passed.
- On actual FlashInfer outputs at 1/32/4096 rows, cleanup matched the original
  index-based masks exactly, and attention left the valid-count tensor unchanged.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy, passed.
- GSM32 smoke scores were baseline 30/32 and 27/32, versus candidate 28/32 and
  28/32, with finite token logprobs throughout. This small variable smoke does
  not establish model accuracy equivalence; broader evaluation remains pending.

Focused tests, with the candidate backend loaded:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -q \
  -k 'flashinfer_empty_shards_preserve_valid_rows or dcp_valid_counts_match_empty_row_mask or flashinfer_cleanup_preserves_backend_empty_row_contract'
```

AI assistance was used for implementation, profiling, and validation.

title: [Performance][NIXL] Optimize nixl descriptors for block-outermost kv cache layout
body:
## Overview

Coalesce eligible, physically adjacent MLA KV-cache layer views into packed NIXL memory regions within each transfer group. This reduces repeated block-descriptor registration while preserving the transfer-group mappings.
The new partial-span coalescing applies to NIXL pull workers only. Push keeps its existing packed-row registration; this change does not add partial-span coalescing or mixed-layout fallback for push. Push can be supported with this optimization in follow-up PRs.

## Claims

The optimization requires a block-outermost KV-cache layout; the GLM-5.3 deployment used `BLHNC`. Coalescing also requires compatible region geometry and adjacency. Other layouts and ineligible regions use the standard registration path.

Validated with `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-MXFP4` on a GB200 NVL72, using one EP8 prefill replica and one EP8 decode replica. The deployment used the block-outermost `BLHNC` layout. The workload was Weka agentic multi-turn replay, with roughly 110–160K input tokens and 900–1,000 output tokens per request.

At concurrency 32, the NIXL numbers are:

- **NIXL post p95:** about 3.85 s before optimization, with spikes to 5 s; about 52 ms after.
- **NIXL transfer p95:** about 4.52 s before; about 81 ms after.
- **Pool-level registered descriptors:** 3,234,222 before versus 121,580 after, about 96% fewer, assuming comparable KV-pool sizes and configuration.

Latency figures are medians across the dashboards’ repeated p95 estimates during each run.

## Validation

Added unit coverage for NIXL descriptor geometry and push-connector layout metadata.

gsm8k validation
`RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-MXFP4`, P/D deployment prefill DEP8, decode DEP8, VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT: "BLHNC", dspark(`RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-speculator.dspark`)

```
|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr|
|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9598|±  |0.0054|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9598|±  |0.0054|

```



## Details

### Root problem
With GLM-5.3’s block-outermost KV layout, adjacent MLA layer views can occupy contiguous memory. NIXL’s registration loop still registers those views separately, repeating block descriptors across layers. This increases registered descriptor volume and contributes to NIXL post overhead.


### Design

Coalesce adjacent, geometry-compatible MLA views into a wider NIXL region within the same transfer group. Preserve the layer-to-region mapping and exclude packed-span regions from later address-based deduplication.

The optimization is guarded by backing-storage, device, cache-spec, stride, block-count, and adjacency checks. Ineligible regions continue through the normal registration path.

title: [ROCm] ROCm binding on common Kimi-K3 Dspark MLA module
body:
## Purpose

On ROCm, Kimi-K3 DSpark currently instantiates the NVIDIA draft module. This PR registers `K3DSparkModel` as `("vllm.models.kimi_k3", "K3DSparkForCausalLM")` and, on ROCm, imports `amd.dspark_mla`. CUDA still imports `nvidia.dspark_mla`.
Builds on top of #60054
Replaces #57942, which was the duplicate-and-modify approach (not touching NVIDIA).

## What changes

`amd/dspark_mla.py` is a binding over the common classes: a factory, `build_self_attn`, `build_mlp`, and `kv_cache_layer` returning `attn.mla_attn`.
Draft attention is `KimiK3MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper` around generic `MLAAttention`, with RoPE and `non_causal_multi_token_decode=True`.
`KimiMLAAttention` is not used: it is NoPE-only, and would add a second wrapper.
Context-KV insert, the weight mapper, the Markov head, and the confidence head stay in the common module, so the #58814 refresh and adaptive verification come along with the dispatch.

The factory duplicates the NVIDIA projection and YaRN setup.
The docstring records the settings that have to stay aligned.

HIP YaRN returns fp32. The query slice assignment casts Q back to bf16,
and rebinding `k_pe` used to leave it fp32. `concat_and_cache_mla` then stored those bits as the KV dtype.
After RoPE, the wrapper casts `k_pe` back with `k_pe.to(kv_c_normed.dtype)`.
On MI355 that cast removed the repetitive garbage in the target output.

Decode-only FP8 with a real embedding must not enter `_fused_decode`.
That path applies a one-row identity RoPE after the wrapper has already rotated.
The call site requires `rotary_emb is None`.
Target K3 still has `rotary_emb is None`, so its launch stays. DeepSeek does not use this wrapper.

## Trace

The baseline draft gap still launches `fusedKimiK3MLADecodeQConcatKVCacheKernel` five times per step, 21 µs total.
The trace for this PR does not use that kernel. Each draft layer instead runs native `DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding.forward_hip`, which calls `forward_native`, and then an ungrouped `concat_and_cache_mla`.
On the steady decode shape the eager gap grows from 3.41 ms to 3.85 ms (+0.44 ms, about 13%).

This PR is **slower** than the NVIDIA-module baseline on ROCm. The kernels that replaced the fused decode epilogue are the native YaRN elementwise chain plus the ungrouped cache insert.

## Potential follow-up

If the fusion in the follow-up (#60864) is not merged, then the following alternative should be considered:
`DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding.forward_hip` calls `forward_native`.
Pointing it at AITER Triton RoPE would remove the elementwise chain for this draft and for every other HIP model
that uses the same embedding.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py` on ROCm, including `test_k3_dspark_decoder_uses_mla_wrapper` (ROCm-only) and `test_hip_yarn_k_pe_is_cast_back_to_kv_dtype` (CPU; a fake fp32 RoPE, asserting the seen key is bf16).
- `test_amd_kv_cache_layer_returns_inner_mla_attn`: draft KV names end in `.attn`.
- `test_fused_decode_not_taken_when_rotary_emb_is_set`.

## Out of scope

- Integrating AITER `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla` (#60864).
- Changing `DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding.forward_hip`.

## 🐛 Describe the bug


### 🐛 Describe the bug


### Summary

Serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with DP=3 / TP=2 / EP and dspark speculative decoding, one worker process dies with `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure` during a decode step, taking the whole server down. It happened twice in a row on a freshly restarted server (after ~58 minutes and ~14 minutes of serving), on two **different GPUs** (local rank 1, then local rank 2), with a **byte-identical Python stack**. The common factor is a pure decode step with 5 speculative tokens scheduled per request and at least two requests in the batch over 100k tokens (up to 147k).

The identical stack on different GPUs makes a single bad device unlikely and points at a software path. Because CUDA faults are reported asynchronously, the frame where the error surfaces (`shared_experts.py:137`, recording a CUDA event for the shared-experts overlap stream) is probably not the kernel that faulted. Candidate upstream kernels on this step are the V4.1 sparse MLA indexer / sparse SWA attention at >100k tokens with fp8 KV, the dspark rejection/resample kernels, or the Engram pinned-memory gather.

A secondary bug is that once the engine is dead, the Anthropic `/v1/messages` adapter crashes with a pydantic `ValidationError` instead of returning a well-formed Anthropic error event, because `message_stream_converter` tries to parse the OpenAI layer's `{"error": ...}` chunk as a `ChatCompletionStreamResponse`.

The converter should detect an `"error"` key (or the OpenAI layer should raise instead of yielding) and translate it into the Anthropic error schema. This is minor compared to the crash but produces misleading "invalid response structure" reports from clients.

### Other observations that may or may not be related

- Several Triton kernels for speculative decoding were JIT-compiled during inference rather than at warmup, so those shapes were never captured or warmed up:
  `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel`, `_ring_slot_mapping_kernel`, `_compute_local_logits_stats_kernel`, `_rejection_kernel`, `_resample_kernel`, `_pad_replayed_slots_kernel` (`jit_monitor.py:140` warnings).
- Draft model warning at startup: `Draft model DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM does not support external multimodal embeddings ... using text-only draft inputs instead.`
- `Sharing Engram tables across DP replicas needs 188.8 GiB of /dev/shm (--shm-size or --ipc=host); sharding them across replicas instead.`
- The DP coordinator periodically logs `Received stats for out-of-order step (...)` warnings during normal operation.
- One request in crash 1 generated ~106k output tokens from a ~96-token prompt (`num_computed_tokens=106637`, `num_output_tokens=106541`), i.e. an extremely long decode. Whether this was a client with no `max_tokens` cap or a model degeneration loop is unknown, but it means the sparse attention path was exercised at >100k tokens in pure decode.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch with the command above (6 GPUs on one node, no NVSwitch).
2. Drive it with an agentic client (Claude Code via `/v1/messages`) that builds up conversations well past 100k tokens, with 3 to 5 concurrent streams.
3. After tens of minutes of decode at >100k tokens with dspark speculative decoding, one worker dies with `unspecified launch failure` and the server exits.

I have not yet isolated a minimal reproducer. Things I plan to try to bisect (happy to report back):

- `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` to find the actually faulting kernel.
- Disable speculative decoding.
- `--max-model-len 131072` and/or a client-side `max_tokens` cap, to test the long-context hypothesis.
- `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` and `--enforce-eager`.
- `--kv-cache-dtype auto`.
- Check `dmesg` for Xid errors at the crash timestamps.

### Expected behavior

- No CUDA fault during long-context decode with speculative decoding; or, failing that, the error should be attributable to a specific kernel.
- When the engine does die, `/v1/messages` should return a well-formed Anthropic error event rather than a pydantic `ValidationError` on the OpenAI error chunk.

title: [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Carry and checkpoint the PLE short-conv state in align mode
body:
## Purpose

Fix the PLE (per-layer n-gram embedding) short-conv state handling of `qwen4_exp` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) in `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, so that a request resumed from a prefix hit delivered by a KV connector (OffloadingConnector loads, PD) reads a valid conv state, and so that the blocks the prefix cache and the offloading tiers store for the PLE group are actually written.

Part of the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next tracking issue #55922 (KV offload section). Same component as #59642 (PD side of the PLE state). Possibly related symptoms: #55357 (episodic 0% MTP acceptance with prefix caching on), #53912.

## Root cause

In align mode the PLE metadata builder (`short_conv_attn.py`) takes `block_table[:, 0]` of the align-gathered block table, i.e. the block of the last *scheduled* token, and uses it both to read the initial conv state and to write the final one. The Mamba/GDN backends instead receive `block_idx_last_computed_token` and read the resumed state from the block of the last *computed* token inside their kernels; the PLE conv kernel has no align support at all.

Two consequences:

1. A request resumed at, say, 6400 computed tokens with 3714 new tokens has its loaded state in block 1 but the PLE reads block 3, which was just allocated and never written. When that memory contains NaN the NaN appears in the PLE output of layer 1 with clean inputs and poisons the whole model; when it contains finite garbage the state is silently wrong.
2. Blocks that end at a 3200-token boundary crossed by a prefill chunk are never written, so the prefix cache and the offloading tiers store uninitialized memory for the PLE group. Inspecting the stored blocks showed NaN in the PLE slot of every block of that group.

GPU-local flows (chunked prefill, local prefix hits) were not affected because the KV cache manager copies the state forward for them; connector loads do not go through that path.

## Changes

- `short_conv_attn.py`: in align mode compute per row the carry source (block holding the state after the computed tokens) and destination (block the kernels address). Decode and spec rows go into persistent builder buffers padded with `NULL_BLOCK_ID`, like `spec_state_indices_tensor`, so full CUDA graph replay reads valid indices. Prefill rows also carry the block-table rows, `seq_lens` and `num_computed_tokens` needed to write boundary checkpoints.
- `ple_layer.py`: copy the conv state from source to destination before each conv (decode, spec and prefill paths); after a prefill, write the exact state at every block boundary the chunk crossed into the block ending there, and zero the speculative scratch columns so stored blocks never carry garbage.

No behavior change when `mamba_cache_mode != "align"`: the new metadata fields stay `None` and the layer code paths are skipped.

## Test Plan

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 on DGX Spark (GB10, 119 GiB unified memory), `OffloadingConnector` with `TieringOffloadingSpec` (CPU tier + fs secondary tier), `mamba_cache_mode=align`, MTP k=3, prefix caching on, 8 GiB GPU KV cache. Load: 48 conversations of ~10.1k tokens (3200 shared system prompt + 6600 per-conversation context), 256 requests at concurrency 4, so most prefix hits come from the offloading tiers (6400-token external hits, ~49% of prompt tokens overall). A per-layer NaN probe was injected for the diagnostic runs.

## Test Result

Validated at TP=1 on two single-GPU hosts (GB10 and GB300). Not applicable to multi-node TP, for a reason unrelated to this fix (see below).

| run (GB10) | fix | external hits | NaN in model | MTP acceptance | stored PLE blocks |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP=2 baseline | no | 31% | yes, born in PLE layer 1 on resumed prefills | 2.2 -> 1.0 as hits start | NaN in PLE slot |
| TP=1 | no | 49% | none (uninitialized memory happened to be finite) | 2.13 | NaN in PLE slot |
| TP=1 | yes | 49% | none, 17,751 probe records | 2.19 | fully initialized, scratch zeroed |
| TP=1, tier on local NVMe | yes | 49% | none | 2.18 | fully initialized |
| GB300 Station, TP=1, CPU tier 32 GiB + NVMe tier | yes | 49% | none | 2.12 | fully initialized |
| GB300 Station, TP=1, CPU tier 4 GiB so hits are promoted from NVMe (1134 chunk hits from the fs tier) | yes | 49% | none | 2.08 | fully initialized |

The stored-block inspection is the direct evidence for the write side of the fix: before, the PLE slot of every stored block of that KV group contained uninitialized memory; after, it holds the boundary state with the three speculative columns zeroed. The TP=1-without-fix row shows why the bug can hide: the engine reads the wrong block either way, and only shows symptoms when that memory happens to hold NaN.

On a GB300 Station (256 GB HBM, 494 GB DRAM, local NVMe) the same load shows the expected gain with the fix in place: median TTFT 0.81 s for first occurrences vs 0.31 s for repeated conversations with hits served from the CPU tier, and 0.97 s vs 0.36 s when the CPU tier is shrunk to 4 GiB so that hits are promoted from the NVMe tier; MTP acceptance stays at 2.1 throughout. Before the fix the same hits made it collapse to 1.0.

Revalidated after rebasing on `main` (371745ebd6, after #58114 and #58997) with an image built from this branch, no file injection: GB300 Station, TP=1, MTP k=3, CPU tier 4 GiB + NVMe tier, 256 requests. No errors (the all-speculative decode path that the earlier rebase broke runs on every steady-state step), 1134 chunk hits served from the NVMe tier, 49% external prefix hits, MTP acceptance 2.12 on average (2.02-2.20 per window, flat from 0% to 49% hits), median TTFT 0.90 s first occurrence vs 0.40 s repeated. Note that on current `main` `--mamba-cache-mode` is deprecated and align mode follows `--enable-prefix-caching`, so this path is active by default whenever prefix caching is on.

TTFT on GB10 at TP=1 does not improve with offloading (10.5 s first occurrence vs 11.1 s repeat, both on NFS and on local NVMe) because the 99 GiB model leaves the node memory-starved (host<->GPU copies at 200 MB/s versus 56 GB/s on an idle node, prefill at ~750 tok/s); that is a platform limit of this model on a single GB10, not a property of the fix.

TP=2 on GB10 means multi-node TP (one GPU per node), and there the tiering manager runs in the scheduler process on rank 0's node and only sees that node's mmap region: only `_r0` files are ever written, rank 1 never creates the secondary tier, and on a load rank 1 copies a stale slot from its own `/dev/shm`. The result is wrong but finite KV on rank 1 (0 NaN in the layer probe, MTP acceptance collapses to 1.0 as soon as external hits start), with or without this fix and with or without #58413. That is the single-host assumption of #54415 (addressed by #46556); details posted there. A TP=2 validation of this fix needs a single host with two GPUs.

title: [ROCm] Fuse Kimi-K3 DSpark QK RoPE with the MLA cache write
body:
## Purpose

Apply AITER `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla` to the Kimi-K3 DSpark draft model.
The kernel fuses the QK RoPE, the absorbed query, and the KV cache write into one launch.
This PR fills the hooks introduced in #60054.

The shared op schemas stay unchanged. `unified_mla_kv_cache_update` is on the compile path of every MLA model and is a splitting op. Positions stay on `_rope_positions`.

## What changes

- The factory returns `KimiK3DSparkMLAWrapper`. After `super().__init__` it stores the embedding as `_epilogue_rotary_emb`.
- When fusion is on, the wrapper skips its own YaRN and passes `positions` into `MLAAttention.forward`. `positions is None` raises `RuntimeError`. There is no fallback that writes unrotated KV.
- Prefill context parallel is refused when fusion would otherwise be on. The gather changes the row count while positions stay local.
- Decode rows are dropped from the generic cache write; the fused kernel writes them. Prefill `k_pe` is cloned, rotated for the cache, and the caller's tensor stays unrotated so attention can rotate it again in `_prepare_mha_inputs`.
- `q_out` is FP8 when the KV cache is quantized and `supports_quant_query_input` is set (`ROCM_AITER_MLA`). Triton MLA clears that flag and keeps bf16. The absorbed query is made contiguous before the launch.
- The NoPE identity-RoPE path stays closed when `rotary_emb` is set, including inside `_fused_qk_prep_supported`.
- `MLACommonMetadata` is imported from `vllm.model_executor.layers.attention.mla_attention`.

## Validation

- CPU hook tests: fusion refuses PCP; fusion is off without an embedding or without the AITER probe; a decode-only update skips `do_kv_cache_update`; prefill `k_pe` is re-rotated for MHA and the caller's key stays unrotated until then; `q_out` matches the backend query dtype; fusion        requires positions.
- `test_fused_qk_rope_concat_requires_fp32_cos_sin` asserts the wrapper rejects a bf16 cos/sin table. The probe is false unless `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` and `aiter.fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla` imports. The AMD Basic Models job runs that test in its own pytest process with the flag
set, and filters it out of the broader command.
- E2E agentic run of Kimi-K3 with this drafter, compared with the NVIDIA draft module on the same prompts.
- Perf comparison against the NVIDIA drafter: `vllm bench serve` / spec-bench over output length × max concurrency, with

```json
{"method": "dspark", "model": "Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark", "num_speculative_tokens": 5, "attention_backend": "TRITON_MLA", "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic", "rejection_sample_method": "block"}
```

## Out of scope

- Changing `DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding.forward_hip` to AITER Triton RoPE. That would apply to every HIP user of the embedding. It can be a follow-up or alternative to this PR.

title: [KV Connector][ROCm] MoRIIO: hybrid READ for several attention groups and shared-group speculative methods
body:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) cannot run MoRIIO hybrid READ P/D on `main`. It has two transferable attention groups (MLA + indexer, and the kpool tail ring, a `CircularBufferSpec`), KDA groups, and MTP. `main` allows one attention group and DSpark only. With the packed `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` layout, `main` also classifies KDA groups as attention and silently skips recurrent-state transfer.

Changes (connector-only: `moriio_connector.py`, tests, one docs line):

- Hybrid READ payload is `[*attn_groups, *mamba_groups]`, byte-identical to `main` with one attention group.
- `_align_read_blocks` runs per attention group. Non-prefix-cacheable groups are read even on a full local hit.
- Each hybrid layer is routed to its own payload group. READ destinations of all attention groups are excluded from KV zeroing.
- A group is Mamba when every layer spec it covers is a `MambaSpec`.
- READ: the DSpark-only check is replaced by "the drafter shares the target's attention groups" (MTP, DSpark). Hybrid WRITE (#60544) is unchanged, including its DSpark check.
- `CircularBufferSpec` is accepted only for hybrid READ. Non-hybrid and hybrid WRITE still fail closed (`NotImplementedError` at init).
- Usage guide: drop the single-attention-group requirement.

Scope:

- Non-hybrid models do not reach the changed code (all scheduler changes are under `_has_mamba`).
- Single-attention-group hybrid READ is covered by byte-identity unit tests only.
- Drafters with a separate attention group are out of scope.

Requires #58585 (per-layer `block_len`), merged. The branch includes `main` with #60544 (hybrid WRITE).

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_*.py
```

Environment: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`, MI300X.

E2E: GLM-5.3-Flash-FP8, 1P/1D, MoRIIO READ, MTP 1, EP8 per leg, KV block 8, MI300X; `main` 19b0efce30 + this PR only.

## Test Result

### Unit

- After merging `main` 5be4266f5c: `test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py` 110 passed (104 on `main`); all `test_moriio_*.py` 299 passed, 0 failed (293 on `main`).
- Two `main` tests are intentionally replaced: the multiple-attention-group rejection and the READ case of the non-DSpark rejection.
- New tests: GLM-5.3-Flash grouping with MTP, payload pairing (partial/full hit), per-layer routing, single-group byte-identity, no-attention-group gate, `CircularBufferSpec` rejection (non-hybrid, hybrid WRITE), WRITE non-DSpark rejection. The non-hybrid gate test fails on the previous head.

### E2E without this PR

All 8 engine cores per leg fail at connector init; servers never come up:

```
moriio_connector.py, line 519, in __init__
MoRIIOError: MoRIIO hybrid READ requires exactly one transferable attention group, got 2; ...
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed.
```

Baseline below is therefore the prefill server queried directly (no KV transfer).

### E2E with this PR

Random data, 1024 output tokens, 16 requests at c=1, 32 at c=8, no failures. Cells: run 1 / run 2, different node pairs.

| ISL, concurrency | TTFT mean (ms) | TTFT P99 (ms) | TPOT mean (ms) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8K, c=1 | 1329 / 1262 | 2459 / 1943 | 9.8 / 10.0 | 90.3 / 88.9 |
| 8K, c=8 | 1720 / 1615 | 2962 / 2907 | 11.2 / 11.2 | 554 / 587 |
| 32K, c=1 | 3705 / 3626 | 3759 / 3685 | 10.4 / 10.1 | 71.5 / 73.4 |
| 32K, c=8 | 7052 / 6228 | 10915 / 10011 | 11.6 / 11.7 | 385 / 396 |
| 256K, c=1 | 31952 / 31517 | 32973 / 32512 | 8.8 / 9.3 | 25.0 / 24.9 |
| 512K, c=1 | 66391 / 65961 | 67178 / 67412 | 9.9 / 9.4 | 13.4 / 13.6 |

Run-to-run TTFT variation: 0.6–2.2% at c=1 (32K–512K), 6–12% at c=8.

| Check (run 1 / run 2) | P/D router | Prefill direct |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions, strict | 91.21 ± 0.78 / 91.89 ± 0.75 | 92.27 ± 0.74 / 92.57 ± 0.72 |
| NIAH found/10, seeds 0/1/2, 2K / 8K / 32K words | run 1: 10,10,10 / 10,10,9 / 1,10,10; run 2: 10,10,10 / 10,10,10 / 10,9,10 | all 10 (32K: one run) |
| 16-concurrent NIAH × 3 rounds | 48/48 / 48/48 | – |
| Single needle, 243K/486K/713K tokens × 3 depths | 7/9 / 9/9 | – |
| MTP acceptance during GSM8K | 93.4% / 93.3% | 95.1% / 95.1% |

- After merging `main` 5be4266f5c (2 runs): GSM8K 90.90 ± 0.79 / 91.96 ± 0.75; 16-concurrent NIAH 48/48 both; NIAH 2K 9,10,9 / 10,10,9, 8K 10,10,10 / 8,10,10, 32K 3,10,10 / 8,10,10.
- Without the packed-Mamba classification fix, NIAH was 0/10 at 2K words for 2 of 3 seeds.

Caveats:

- GSM8K router minus prefill-direct, paired by question: -1.06 (95% CI -2.37 to +0.25) and -0.68 (95% CI -1.78 to +0.42). Both include zero.
- NIAH misses are not transfer-related: on the merged tree, 2K words × 5 seeds × 3 passes, 4/15 prefill-direct and 3/15 router requests missed a needle, and same-path reruns flip between complete and incomplete (temperature 0).

- No `MoRIIOError` or tracebacks on either leg in any run.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Size the long-context prefill workspaces by what a chunk can use
body:
## Overview

At DeepSeek-V4.1's 1M `max_model_len` on SM90, the indexer K-gather and FlashMLA prefill-gather reservations share a 5.16 GiB workspace per GPU. That workspace is sized for chunks the indexer never forms and FlashMLA rarely forms. This PR sizes both reservations by what one prefill chunk can actually gather, which returns 3.70 GiB per GPU to the KV cache. #55222 fixed the GLM-5.3 counterpart by dividing by the pool ratio; that does not help here, because most DeepSeek-V4.1 index layers have compress ratio 1.

## Claims

- On 8×H20 at TP8 and 1M, available KV cache rises from 19.69 to 23.39 GiB per GPU (+18.8%).
- Indexer chunking is unchanged. FlashMLA splits a step only when several very long prefills share it, and the outputs are bitwise identical.
- Nothing changes below a `max_model_len` of about 84K. Only `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/` changes.

## Validation

**Tests.** The new cases and the existing splitter tests pass:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py -k dsv41_indexer_prefill_buffer
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k split_indexer_prefill_chunks
```

The new test runs the real splitter on the densest packing at 128K and 1M. No chunk exceeds the new reservation, and three of the four cases fill it exactly.

**Serving.** 8×H20, TP8, 1M, DSpark k=5.
- Adaptive verification is off, because main cannot start with it at 1M on H20.
- These runs predate the rebase. The reservation formulas are unchanged.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Available KV cache per GPU | 19.69 GiB | 23.39 GiB |
| KV cache tokens | 9.24M | 10.97M |
| GSM8K (5-shot chat, greedy) | 96.97% | 96.66% |

- **Pass-key prompts of 120K to 900K tokens:** both arms return identical outputs, and TTFT differs by under 0.04 s.
- **16 sessions × 128K with prefix hits:** each turn's first step carries 10 to 12 long prefills and runs FlashMLA in 2 chunks instead of 1. Turn TTFT is 2.82 s against 2.81 s on main. That is within the 6% spread between the two main servers.
- **GSM8K:** three runs of main on this nightly scored between 96.4% and 97.0%.

**Cost of the extra chunks.** One layer's `_forward_prefill` on H20, timed with FlashInfer CUPTI and a cold L2.
- With 16 × 131K contexts in one step, ratio-1 layers go from 1 chunk to 3: 5,721 → 5,829 µs (+1.9%).
- Ratio-2 layers go from 1 chunk to 2: +0.5%.
- Over all layers that is an estimated 2.6 ms per step. The outputs are bitwise equal.

<details>
<summary>Serve command (the memory and pass-key runs add `--no-enable-prefix-caching`)</summary>

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 8 --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
```
</details>

## Details

- **Indexer.**
  - `_split_indexer_prefill_chunks` packs requests only while `query_rows * keys <= max_logits_elems`. Each request brings at least one row and at most `max_len` keys, so a chunk has `keys**2 <= max_logits_elems * max_len`.
  - The indexer now reserves `max(max_len, isqrt(max_logits_elems * max_len))` rows, capped at the builder's budget. At 1M that is 11.9M rows instead of 41.9M.
  - A DeepSeek-V4.1 builder subclass with this budget would enforce the bound structurally. I kept the change in the model directory instead.
- **FlashMLA.** The prefill chunk area now holds as many full-length requests as fit in 2^20 bf16 rows (1 GiB), and at least one. That is one at 1M, three at 256K, and four (unchanged) below about 250K. Warmup and the runtime planner use the same value.
- **Scope.**
  - The FlashMLA part is SM90's default path.
  - On Blackwell only the indexer part applies. With the recipe's FlashInfer and MXFP4-indexer setup, that is an estimated 2.66 → 0.75 GiB.
  - ROCm is unaffected.
- **Duplicates.** No open PR changes these reservations for DeepSeek-V4.1.
