title: [Perf][Core][Mamba] Export prefill checkpoints at or before the initial-state column
body:
## Overview

With a fine-grained prefix match unit (e.g. `--prefix-match-unit 128` on GLM-5.3-Flash, KDA linear attention + sparse MLA), many partial-hit prefills pay one extra fixed-cost prefill step. The scheduler rejects the in-pass prefill checkpoint whenever its column is at or before the column holding the initial state, then splits the prefill at the checkpoint boundary. This PR lets a request's first chunk export that checkpoint in the same pass, so those prefills run as a single step. It also fixes a related cache-publishing bug in `MambaManager`. Follow-up to #56960; related to #59146, #59175, #59759 and #58021.

## Claims

- Partial-hit prefills whose checkpoint column is at or before the initial-state column (`checkpoint_col <= (start - 1) // block_size`) no longer split at the tail boundary. On GLM-5.3-Flash TP8 with pmu128, a hit of 2944/3300 tokens now prefills in one step. Median TTFT at c=1 goes from 58.8 ms to 41.4 ms. At c=16 it goes from 404 ms to 286 ms.
- No accuracy change: GSM8K and a multi-turn GSM8K that feeds the model's own answers back (every turn after the first is a prefix hit) match the unpatched image and the baseline. Prefix hit rates are unchanged.
- Fix: when a chunk resumed mid-block and ran past the block boundary, `MambaManager.cache_blocks` published that slot under its full-block hash, although the slot holds the initial (or checkpoint) state. A later request could then match it.

## Validation

GLM-5.3-Flash on 8xH100. Settings: TP8, `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, `fp8_ds_mla`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, prefix caching on, `--prefix-match-unit 128`. Geometry: mamba block 1152, hash block 128, checkpoint alignment 16. Both arms use the same image, with this PR overlaid on top; the PR is backported 1:1 to the image's vLLM version.

**Latency** (median TTFT; the two numbers are the profiled and unprofiled passes)

| workload | before | after | prefill steps (mixed) before -> after | continuation-only steps before -> after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| hit_c1 (3000-token prompt + 64 output, then +300 suffix; 2944 of 3300 cached) | 58.8 / 57.7 ms | 41.5 / 41.4 ms | 8 -> 5 | 3 -> 0 |
| hit_c16 (same, 16 concurrent) | 404 / 419 ms | 286 / 382 ms | 14 -> 11 | 1 -> 0 |
| sharegpt multi-turn, c16 (484 turns) | 298 / 291 ms | 275 / 285 ms | 237 -> 259 | 46 -> 50 |

- For reference, with the default unit (1152) hit_c1 caches only 2304 tokens and its TTFT is about 130 ms. A pmu128 run with the tail split disabled entirely got 40 ms; that run did not cache the checkpoint.
- sharegpt: prefix hits are identical before and after (190976 tokens, 57.8% hit rate).
  - Most sharegpt turns (382/484) have prompts of at most one mamba block (1152 tokens). For those, there is no earlier column to hold a checkpoint (`checkpoint_col < 0`), so they still split at the tail; this PR does not change that case.
  - The step-count and TTFT differences on this workload are within run-to-run variance. An earlier unpatched run had 266 mixed and 64 continuation-only steps.

**Accuracy** (GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy, max 256 tokens, concurrency 128; two passes on the same server, so pass 2 is mostly prefix hits)

| arm | GSM8K pass 1 | GSM8K pass 2 | multi-turn GSM8K (chains of 6) | multi-turn hit rate (turns > 0) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pmu128, before | 0.9189 | 0.9128 | 0.9234 | 80.2% |
| pmu128, after | 0.9151 | 0.9151 | 0.9272 | 80.1% |
| default unit, after | 0.9196 | 0.9212 | 0.9242 | 22.8% |

On the multi-turn run, 308 of the 1099 hit turns take the newly allowed path (219 with `checkpoint_col == initial_state_col` at a mid-block start, 89 with `checkpoint_col < initial_state_col`). Their accuracy is 0.915, vs 0.912 before. Server logs had no errors.

**Unit tests** (CPU)

- New tests in `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py`:
  - `test_partial_hit_prefill_exports_checkpoint_in_one_chunk`: five geometries. Each runs a partial-hit prefill through the scheduler split and the manager. It asserts a single chunk, then simulates the worker's state writes and checks that every cached Mamba block holds the state its hash claims.
  - `test_mamba_align_split_checkpoint_at_or_before_initial_state_needs_fresh_row`: a running request still splits.
  - All 7 cases fail on `main` and pass with this PR.
- `pytest tests/v1/core`: 1372 passed. Two `test_offloading_connector` failures also occur on `main` in this CPU-only environment. GPU-only tests were not run here.
- `pre-commit run` passes.

## Details

**Root cause.**
- In "align" mode with prefill-checkpoint blocks, the state at the prompt's last hash-block boundary `P` is written into column `cdiv(end, bs) - 2` of the request's Mamba block row in the same forward pass.
- `is_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_valid` required that column to be strictly after the initial-state column `(start - 1) // bs`. With a 128-token unit, a hit followed by a short tail often lands at or before it. For example, a hit of 2944 and a prompt of 3300 give checkpoint column 1 and initial-state column 2.
- The scheduler then fell back to stopping the chunk at `P`. The extra step costs about 20-35 ms for small chunks and about 120 ms for chunks above 512 tokens.

**Change.**
- `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`: `is_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_valid` accepts `checkpoint_col <= initial_state_col`, except for a block-aligned start where the two columns coincide (that column is the shared hit block). New helper `mamba_prefill_checkpoint_needs_fresh_row`.
- `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`: these geometries are allowed only for a request's first chunk (`num_computed_tokens == 0`), whose worker block-table row is sent whole. A running request's row is append-only and may still hold a stale id at that column, so it keeps splitting.
- `vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` (`MambaManager`):
  - For `checkpoint_col < initial_state_col`, reserve one extra block and put it in the skipped (null) slot.
  - For `==` with a mid-block start, the checkpoint overwrites the request's private copy-on-write block, which only fed the initial state.
  - `cache_blocks` skips past a slot whose content is not its full-block state. This is also the publishing bug fix listed under Claims.
- The worker side is unchanged. `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/checkpoint.py` already writes to whatever block id is in that column, for any backend (KDA, Mamba2, etc.).

**Related.** #59826 also changes how Mamba prefill checkpoint boundaries are computed (resend-safe boundary, EAGLE, Mooncake), but it does not touch the initial-state-column rule. The two PRs touch some of the same functions, so whichever merges second needs a rebase.

**Not addressed (separate issue).** With DCP8 on a KV-capacity-bound multi-session workload, pmu128 was much worse than the default unit, which is already partial at 1152 there. Prefix hit rate was 27% vs 66% and TTFT p50 4.5 s vs 0.67 s. A CPU replay of that session trace through the KV cache manager reproduces it from cache footprint and eviction, not from prefill splits: at 2415 blocks the hit rate is 0.22 with pmu128 vs 0.67 with the default. This PR moves it only slightly (0.22 -> 0.30), so it needs its own follow-up.

title: [ROCm] MonoKernel for GLM 5.2
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

An opt-in decode path for GLM-5.2 (`glm_moe_dsa`, MXFP4 experts) at TP8 on MI355X (gfx950). It runs each MoE decoder layer (3..77) as one persistent FlyDSL kernel, in "layer mode", inside the stock layer loop.

It uses the `SpecializedDecode` interface of #61867 (Kimi-K3, merged):
- the switch is `additional_config={"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}`;
- the model refuses unsupported deployments at startup;
- a `ModelState` builds and binds the executor;
- `plan()` runs once per step.

RFC: #60904.

**Related work, and why this isn't a duplicate.** Checked with `gh pr list --state open --search "GLM-5.2 monokernel"` / `"GLM 5.2 decode ROCm"` and against the RFC thread.

| PR | What it is | How it relates |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #61867 (merged) | Kimi-K3 SpecializedDecode, NVIDIA | Same interface and the same batch-size approach; this is the first AMD user of it, for a different model |
| #60397 (merged) | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash mono decode, MI355X | Different model and kernels |
| #61482, #60731, #60683, #61662 (open) | DSv4-Pro, DSv4.1 on gfx942, Kimi-K3, GLM-5.3-Flash on ROCm | Different models; nothing shared with GLM-5.2's DSA + MXFP4 MoE layer |
| #61311 (open) | Shared specialized-decode abstractions | This PR keeps its runtime per model, as #61867 does, and can move onto shared helpers if those land |

No other PR targets GLM-5.2 decode kernels.

## Claims

- **Speed:** decode TPOT falls by 2.30× at batch 1 and 1.51× at batch 8 on 8× MI355X, GLM-5.2-MXFP4, 3000-token prompts, FULL decode graphs.
- **Accuracy:** at parity with stock on GSM8K (5-shot, greedy, n=1319).
- **Weights:** served at the checkpoint's precision, read in place from vLLM's loaded modules. Nothing is re-quantized at load time.
  - BF16-attention checkpoints (`amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`) run BF16 attention, and vLLM's indexer refreshes the indexer layers. Validated on GPU.
  - Checkpoints that ship Quark per-channel FP8 attention (`amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`) run FP8 attention units with the checkpoint's per-row scales. With `max_model_len` ≤ 4096 they also run the indexer fused into the kernel. Validated on GPU (results below).
- **Supported configurations:** listed in `specialized_decode/README.md`, which grows as support is added.
- **Stock path unchanged:** without the switch, `specialized_decode_config()` returns `None`, and the model, model state and layer loop behave exactly as before.
- **Refusal at startup:** if you set the switch on a deployment it can't serve, startup fails with one `ValueError` that names every unsupported setting.

## Validation

**Performance.** TPOT in ms on current main, offline `LLM`, TP8, prompt 3000 tokens, FULL_DECODE_ONLY graphs. Each cell is the mean of 3 runs.

| Configuration | Batch 1 | Batch 8 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stock (`decode_backend=auto`) | 13.69 (13.68–13.69) | 17.47 (17.19–17.79) |
| Specialized decode | **5.94** (5.94–5.95) | **11.57** (11.52–11.66) |

**Model evaluation.** GSM8K, 5-shot (the first 5 train exemplars), greedy, `max_tokens=256`, all 1319 test questions, FULL graphs.

| Configuration | Strict | Flexible |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Specialized decode | 1247 (94.5% ± 0.6) | 1249 |
| Stock, same harness (earlier base) | 1218–1230 | |

> The table and GSM8K come from the previous revision of this PR configured as this revision's defaults (BF16 attention, `indexer_mode="indexer_only"`); the compiled kernels are byte-identical.

**This revision with vLLM's default capture sizes** (`max_num_seqs=32`, no `cudagraph_capture_sizes` set). Captured graphs up to 8 run the kernels; 16 and above capture vLLM's decode.

| Batch | 1 | 3 (pads to 4) | 8 | 16 (stock graph) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TPOT (ms) | 5.94 | 8.36 | 11.57 | 20.85 (stock alone: 20.77) |

GSM8K with batch sizes 10 and 12 also built and in use (limit raised to 12 for the run, `max_num_seqs=12`): 1236/1319 strict.

**FP8-attention checkpoint** (`amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`, fused indexer), against vLLM on the same checkpoint. TPOT in ms, same setup, mean of 3 runs.

| Batch | 1 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stock | 14.48 | 15.24 | 15.85 | 16.68 | 17.40 | 18.23 | 19.39 |
| Specialized decode | **4.89** | 5.98 | 7.34 | 8.74 | **10.27** | 14.83 | 17.24 |
| Speedup | 2.96× | 2.55× | 2.16× | 1.91× | 1.69× | 1.23× | 1.12× |

- **Batch 8:** the middle value is shown; the three runs were 10.27, 10.27 and 11.88.
- **Accuracy:** GSM8K strict is 1230/1319 for the specialized decode and 1226 for stock on the same checkpoint.
- **What vLLM loads:** vLLM selects `AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel` for the attention linears. The specialized decode reads those preshuffled FP8 weights and per-row scales without re-quantizing, and logs `FP8 per-channel attention (checkpoint precision); fused indexer on 18 indexer layers`.

**Batch-size sweep, BF16** (why `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` is 8). TPOT in ms, 3000-token prompts, FULL graphs, mean of 3 runs. Built up to 12 for the sweep; 16 and 24 run vLLM's graphs.

| Batch | 1 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 | 16 | 24 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stock | 13.71 | 14.71 | 15.52 | 16.59 | 17.38 | 18.44 | 19.51 | 20.77 | 24.80 |
| Specialized decode | 5.94 | 6.81 | 8.46 | 10.13 | 11.55 | 14.84 | 18.41 | 20.80 | 24.79 |
| Speedup | 2.31× | 2.16× | 1.83× | 1.64× | 1.50× | 1.24× | 1.06× | 1.00× | 1.00× |

- **Above 8 the kernel slows sharply.** Each extra request costs about 0.8 ms up to 8, then about 1.7 ms per request from 8 to 12, as the kernel moves to a second row group.
- **Throughput peaks at batch 8**, at 693 tok/s; batch 12 gives 652. The FP8 checkpoint falls off the same way above 8, so the limit is 8 for both.

**Other end-to-end checks**
- Eager and FULL-graph runs at batch 1 and 4 give coherent text.
- The executor reports the kernels ran on the decode steps.
- An unsupported deployment fails at startup on every rank with one message, e.g. `does not support: the V1 model runner (set VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1) (decode_backend=auto runs vLLM's decode)`.

**Reproduce**
```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve <GLM-5.2-MXFP4> -tp 8 \
  --additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
```

**Tests run**
```bash
pytest -v -s tests/models/deepseek_v32
#   69 passed, 2 skipped (the 2 FlyDSL kernel-build tests skip without a gfx950 toolchain;
#   both pass in a compile-only gfx950 container)
pre-commit run --files <changed files>   # all hooks pass, incl. mypy and test tethering
```

**CI coverage.** A new Buildkite step, `:amd: (MI355) GLM-5.2 Specialized Decode` (`mi355_1`), runs the tests above. End-to-end coverage isn't possible in CI because it needs the GLM-5.2 checkpoint on 8 GPUs. The end-to-end runs above were done locally on 8× MI355X.

## Details

**Shape.** Layer mode of the #61867 interface:
- `specialized_decode_config()` runs in `__init__`, before any weights are allocated.
- `DeepseekV32ModelState` builds the executor after the weights load, and calls `prepare_kv()` from `ModelState.initialize_kv_cache` at every KV bind.
- `forward()` calls `plan()` once per step. It returns a `Step` only for plain decode steps the kernels serve, and the layer loop then asks `step.layer(i)` for a kernel. Prefill and mixed batches run the stock layers unchanged.
- The kernel reads vLLM's loaded weights and its KV and index caches in place. There is no second weight copy or checkpoint re-read.

**Batch sizes.** This follows #61867's approach.
- Two constants in `specialized_decode/runtime/__init__.py` set the limit:
  - `BATCH_SIZES = (1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12)` is what the kernel can be built for;
  - `MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 8`, set from the sweep above.
- The kernels are built for the batch sizes up to 8: 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 8. A smaller batch pads up to the next of these (3 runs as 4).
- A step with at most 8 requests runs the kernels; a larger one runs vLLM's decode.
- Larger batches run vLLM's decode.
- Capture sizes and `max_num_seqs` aren't restricted. FULL graphs above 8 capture vLLM's decode. The startup log says `layers 3..77, batch sizes (1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8); larger batches run vLLM's decode`.

**Unsupported, refused at startup**
- model_type other than `glm_moe_dsa`; TP≠8; PP, DP, EP, DCP, PCP or DBO;
- speculative decoding, sleep mode, LoRA, KV-transfer connectors, routed-expert capture;
- AITER fused shared experts;
- dtype other than bf16; `kv_cache_dtype` other than auto/bf16;
- MRV1; `STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE`;
- not gfx950;
- malformed `specialized_decode` options; `step_sync` under FULL graphs.

**FP8-attention checkpoints**
- The path is chosen from the loaded weights, with no option to set:
  - all four attention matrices FP8 per-channel gives FP8 attention;
  - FP8 `wq_b` and `max_model_len` ≤ 4096 add the fused indexer.
- Partial or mixed FP8, and block, per-tensor or non-Quark FP8, are refused.
- vLLM's FP8 GEMM layouts, including AITER's (16,16) preshuffle, are undone by byte permutation only.
- The BF16 kernels compile to byte-identical code with this change. The FP8 + fused-indexer kernels build at every batch size with no VGPR spills.

**Checked later**
- When the executor is built: the MoE layout and backend, BF16 attention weights (a checkpoint with quantized attention is refused here), and the RoPE table.
- At each KV bind: the caches are bound and contiguous, use the MLA row layout, and are under 4 GiB.

**Core components and complexity**
- No core files are touched. Outside the new directories, the only changes are `amd/model.py` +60/−1, `amd/model_state.py` +21 (new) and one Buildkite step.
- New code: about 1.5k lines of runtime (`specialized_decode/runtime/`), 3.7k lines of vendored FlyDSL kernel (`specialized_decode/flydsl/`, JIT-compiled, no binaries, ruff-clean without excludes) and 1.5k lines of tests.

**MRV2 only.** The path is built on MRV2's `ModelState` hooks. With MRV1, startup is refused with the reason, since this architecture still defaults to MRV1 on ROCm.

**Tradeoffs and limitations**
- Only plain decode at batch sizes up to 8 is accelerated, which is the latency-serving case.
- **Host syncs:** `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` stops at `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py:726`, in vLLM's ROCm sparse-MLA metadata builder, and stock vLLM stops at the same line. With `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn` on the same workload (batch 1 and 8), stock logs 384 `synchronize` calls and the specialized decode 352, so the specialized decode adds none of its own.
- **Follow-ups:**
  - FP8-attention checkpoints (e.g. `amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`), including the fused indexer;
  - MTP, which is refused for now;
  - TP other than 8, and other GPUs.

**Interactions with open PRs**
- **#61941** turns AITER fused shared experts on by default for GLM-5.x MXFP4. This path refuses that setting, so once #61941 lands, users of this switch must turn the fusion off. Alternatively the kernel could learn that layout.
- **#61985** adds an MXFP4 indexer K cache, which needs a refusal or kernel support before it becomes the default.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used to write and refactor parts of this change, run the validation and draft this description.

title: [Bugfix] Dequantize DeepSeek-V4 wo_a for non-DeepGEMM linear backends
body:
## Overview

DeepSeek-V4 fails at engine init with `--linear-backend marlin` (#60587) or `triton`. `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` reads `wo_a.weight` directly and only understands the grouped `[g, r, d]` FP8 layout that the DeepGEMM linear kernels leave behind. Other backends lay the weight out for their own GEMM. This PR dequantizes such a `wo_a` to BF16 after loading so the existing BF16 bmm branch handles it.

Fixes #60587.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4-Flash starts and generates with `--linear-backend marlin` and `--linear-backend triton` (both crashed in `_o_proj` during profiling before).
- With real weights, GSM8K under `--linear-backend marlin` matches the default backend (table below).
- Default path (DeepGEMM / FlashInfer-DeepGEMM kernels) is unchanged: `wo_a` is already the 3D FP8 tensor, so the new hook returns early.

## Validation

New test in `tests/quantization/test_fp8.py`: builds a block-FP8 `wo_a` under `linear_backend` in {marlin, triton}, runs the kernel's `process_weights_after_loading`, then `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`, and compares with an FP32 reference.

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_fp8.py -k test_deepseek_v4_o_proj_with_non_deep_gemm_wo_a
```

1xH100: 2 passed. With the `maybe_dequant_wo_a` call removed from the test, both fail: marlin with `Expected size for first two dimensions of batch2 tensor to be: [2, 512] but got: [2, 128]` (same error as #60587), triton with DeepGEMM's `layout.hpp:46: t.dim() == N`.

E2E on 1xH100, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` with dummy weights, `hf_overrides={"n_routed_experts": 8}`, `enforce_eager=True`, 2 prompts x 16 tokens:

| `linear_backend` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| auto (FlashInfer-DeepGEMM) | ok | ok |
| deep_gemm | ok | ok |
| marlin | `RuntimeError: Expected size for first two dimensions of batch2 tensor to be: [8, 4096] but got: [8, 1024].` | ok |
| triton | DeepGEMM `layout.hpp:46: t.dim() == N` in `fp8_einsum` | ok |
| cutlass | `dispatch_scaled_mm ... scaled_mm_helper.hpp:17` | same, see below |
| torch | `Invalid scaling configuration.` | same, see below |

SM100 FlashInfer layer (RopeQuant recheck), 1xB200, same dummy setup reshaped to 128 local heads / 16 `wo_a` groups so RopeQuant applies, `kv_cache_dtype="fp8"`, `attention_backend="FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4"`:

| run | result |
|---|---|
| auto | RopeQuant on, ok |
| marlin, this PR | RopeQuant chosen in `__init__`, turned off after `wo_a` becomes BF16, ok |
| marlin, this PR minus the `_fuse_rope_quant` recheck line | `assert use_fp8` in `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` |

GSM8K, real weights, 2xH200, TP=2, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 --max-model-len 8192`, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5`:

| `linear_backend` | code | GSM8K | invalid |
|---|---|---|---|
| auto (FlashInfer-DeepGEMM, FP8 `wo_a`) | this PR (path unchanged) | 0.9492 | 0.0 |
| marlin | this PR (BF16 `wo_a`) | 0.9484 | 0.0 |

One run each, greedy; the gap is 1 question out of 1319. I did not rerun main with real weights; the main failure is the dummy-weight row above. Per-GPU model memory goes from 73.8 GiB to 74.52 GiB with the BF16 `wo_a`.

## Details

Root cause: `wo_a` is a `ColumnParallelLinear` marked `is_bmm`, but it is never called. `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` takes `wo_a.weight` (and its scale) and feeds them to `fp8_einsum`, or to a BF16 `bmm` when the weight is not FP8. Only `DeepGemmFp8BlockScaledMMKernel.process_weights_after_loading` (also used by the FlashInfer-DeepGEMM kernel) reshapes the weight to `[g, r, d]` with DeepGEMM scales. The kernel is picked in `create_weights`, before `is_bmm` is set, and `--linear-backend` applies to every FP8 linear, so `wo_a` can end up in Marlin's packed int32 layout or a plain 2D FP8 tensor.

The fix is local to the three CUDA attention layers that call `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` (FlashMLA, FlashInfer SM100, FlashInfer SM120). Their new `process_weights_after_loading` runs after every quant method's own processing (deferred attention layers), and calls `maybe_dequant_wo_a`, which uses `get_and_maybe_dequant_weights` (same helper MLA uses for `kv_b_proj`). For Marlin and the DeepGEMM-capable platforms it dequantizes through the kernel's own `apply`, so it does not depend on each backend's layout. ROCm/XPU/CPU subclasses are untouched since their `wo_a` paths differ. On the SM100 FlashInfer layer, RopeQuant was decided in `__init__` against the not-yet-loaded FP8 weight, so it is rechecked after the swap.

Tradeoffs: on non-DeepGEMM backends `wo_a` is held in BF16 (4096x8192 per layer, about 1.5 GB more for DeepSeek-V4-Flash at TP=1, split across TP ranks) and that projection runs as a BF16 bmm. The default backend keeps the FP8 path.

Limitations:
- `cutlass` and `torch` still fail before reaching `_o_proj`: their block-FP8 GEMMs reject the checkpoint's UE8M0 scales (#47988 covers CUTLASS/Triton E8M0 handling). Out of scope here.
- The reporter is on GB10 (SM121), which I don't have. I validated on H100/H200. The SM120 layer gets the same hook.

Not a duplicate:
- #56119 (open, last updated 09-24, merge conflicts, no review) dequantizes `is_bmm` weights inside `Fp8LinearMethod` only when Marlin is selected. This PR keeps shared FP8 code untouched and covers any backend that leaves `wo_a` outside the DeepGEMM layout: Triton is verified above; B12x (used by the GB10 recipe) also keeps a plain 2D FP8 weight and takes the same path, not run.
- #55172 adds a BF16 helper for SM8x. I applied its `o_proj.py` on H100 with `--linear-backend marlin` and it still fails (`marlin_gemm ... a.size(1) = 32768, size_k = 4096`), because it infers the group width from the packed Marlin weight.
- #41834 (SM12x enablement, open since May) makes Marlin refuse block-FP8 layers instead.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find the root cause, write the change and run the validation above.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Honor the largest shared block-size preference
body:
## Overview

When a model has more than one attention backend, `_preferred_block_size_for_backends` returns 16 whenever every backend accepts the default, and never calls `get_preferred_block_size`. Use the largest preferred size when every backend accepts it. Fixes #60871.

## Claims

- The largest preference replaces 16 only when every backend already accepts 16 and every backend accepts that larger size. A single backend is unchanged. If any backend rejects 16, the LCM search is unchanged.
- From declared sizes, not from end-to-end runs, that moves 16 to a larger preference for:
  - Llama-4, encoder-decoder models, and Inkling on XPU FlashAttention (16 to 64)
  - Llama-4 and cross-attention encoder-decoder on ROCm AITER unified (16 to 64)
  - a dense model with `ultraquant_4bit` and skip layers on ROCm (16 to 64)
  - Qwen4Exp with QSA on SM100, head size 256, and FA4 (16 to 128, before hybrid alignment)
- DeepSeek-V4.1 and Llama-4 with `--attention-backend B12X` stay on the current LCM result.

## Validation

`ruff` 0.14.0 format and check pass on the two changed files.

```bash
pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_preferred_block_size_satisfies_every_backend tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_preferred_block_size_keeps_default_when_largest_preference_is_rejected tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_preferred_block_size_searches_past_an_exact_size_backend tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_preferred_block_size_rejects_backends_with_no_common_size
```

Result on the previous revision: 8 passed in 0.42s. This update adds one LCM pin, `([[64], ([MultipleOf(32)], 256)], 64)`, so the same command now has nine cases. `ruff` 0.14.0 was run again on the two files. The new case was not executed in that earlier run.

## Details

`Platform._preferred_block_size_for_backends` (from #49845) calls `get_preferred_block_size` only for one backend. With two or more, `supports_block_size(16)` is true for `MultipleOf(16)` and for an exact 16, so the function returns 16. That skips preferences of 64 (`FLASH_ATTN` on XPU, `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`) and 128 (`HPUAttentionBackendV1`).

In-tree platforms do not crash on this. The HPU plugin does: the runner snapshots 128 before this selection overwrites the block size with 16, and prompt warmup then fails unflatten. vllm-gaudi works around it in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-gaudi/pull/1871. This change makes that workaround removable for the case where every backend accepts the larger preference.

The preference check sits inside the branch where every backend accepts the default. Putting it earlier also rewrites the LCM path: DeepSeek-V4.1 would take the SWA preference of 256 instead of 64 on SM90 and ROCm gfx942, or 128 on SM100 and SM120. Llama-4 with B12X on SM120 would move from 64 to 128. Those stay on the LCM result.

`ultraquant_attn.py` notes that decode geometry wants a block of 64, while Phase 1 currently selects 16 there. Phase 3 was not checked, so this is only an observation from the declared sizes.

#58630 changes how specs are queried. It does not apply this rule.

AI assistance was used to draft this change. The submitter reviewed the diff and ran the unit tests above.

title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] DeepGEMM FP8 MegaMoE with fused shared experts
body:
## Overview

Run GLM-5.3-Flash's MoE layers with DeepGEMM's FP8xFP8 MegaMoE (routed and shared experts in one kernel that also dispatches and combines across the EP group), using the official FP8 checkpoint. Enabled by `--kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'` with `--tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size N --enable-expert-parallel`.

Related: #55275 (BF16 / MXFP4 MegaMoE for GLM, open), #54049 (FlashInfer NVFP4 mega kernel).

## Claims

- On the AgentX replay at concurrency 96, DEP4 with MegaMoE gives 1.6x the output throughput of DEP4 on the generic MoE path.
- Against TP4 it is about level on throughput (+6%, one run each) and has about a fifth of the TTFT.
- It prefills 1.8x faster than DEP4 generic and 2.5x faster than TP4.
- No change for any other `moe_backend`.

## Validation

4x B200, nightly `8cbd5d03` with this change applied, MTP 5 with acceptance fixed by `synthetic_acceptance_length` 3.61. The three arms ran on the same node and in the same container, one run each; they differ only in parallel layout and `moe_backend`.

AgentX replay (InferenceX-pinned aiperf, `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126`), concurrency 96, 1 hour:

| metric | TP4 | DEP4, generic MoE | DEP4, MegaMoE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| output tok/s | 3,152 | 2,063 | **3,332** |
| input tok/s | 380,126 | 234,727 | **399,297** |
| total tok/s | 383,278 | 236,790 | **402,628** |
| requests completed (errors) | 11,372 (4) | 8,143 (1) | 11,986 (5) |
| TTFT avg / p50 / p99 | 3.93 / 2.19 / 23.8 s | 2.36 / 1.47 / 17.3 s | **0.81 / 0.49 / 5.99 s** |
| ITL avg | 18.3 ms | 45.6 ms | 19.5 ms |
| output tok/s per user | 64.0 | 26.2 | 64.1 |
| prefix cache hit | 93.9% | 92.4% | 94.0% |
| of which GPU / host reload | 6.2% / 87.7% | 50.9% / 41.5% | 71.2% / 22.8% |
| preemptions | 35 | 53 | 2 |

`vllm bench serve`, random prompts, concurrency 128, on the same servers:

| workload (in/out) | metric | TP4 | DEP4, generic MoE | DEP4, MegaMoE |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192 / 1 | total tok/s | 46,334 | 63,900 | **115,081** |
| | mean TTFT | 20.8 s | 15.2 s | 8.4 s |
| 1024 / 1024 | output tok/s | 7,895 | 8,478 | **11,691** |
| | mean TTFT | 4.31 s | 1.86 s | 0.85 s |

GSM8K (lm-eval, 5-shot, 1,319 questions): TP4 0.9757 ± 0.0042 (nightly `43b4aaea`), MegaMoE 0.9735 ± 0.0044.

On current `main` only the new unit tests and pre-commit were run.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 PYTHONHASHSEED=42 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --language-model-only --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5,"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.61}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true,"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[6,12,18,24,30,36,48,60,72,96,120,144,192,240,288,384,480,576,768,1020,1536,2046,3072,4092,6144,8190]}' \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 8190 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 \
  --prefix-match-unit 16 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":300000000000,"enable_cross_layers_blocks":"true","lazy_offload":false}}'

vllm-router --port 8000 --worker-urls http://127.0.0.1:8001 --intra-node-data-parallel-size 4 --policy consistent_hash

aiperf profile --scenario agentx --url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --concurrency 96 --benchmark-duration 3600 \
  --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126
```

The baselines drop `moe_backend` (DEP4, generic) or use `--tensor-parallel-size 4` alone with `--intra-node-data-parallel-size 1` on the router (TP4). The generic path picked `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` for the FP8 experts. The random-prompt rows were measured on the same servers before the replay with `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --max-concurrency 128`.
</details>

## Details

- The checkpoint's experts are block FP8 (E4M3, one float32 scale per 128x128 block). DeepGEMM's SM100 MegaMoE feeds scales to the block-scaled MMA and needs UE8M0 scales per row and 32 columns, so the routed and shared expert weights are requantized once at load (`requant_block_fp8_to_ue8m0`).
- This requantization is lossy: about 2.4% relative L2 per weight tensor and about 3.9% on one MoE layer's output (layer 15, real weights, random inputs). The generic TRTLLM path uses the checkpoint's scales as they are. The GSM8K gap above is within one standard error; I have not run other evals.
- Routing stays outside the kernel: `fused_topk_bias` (sigmoid, score correction bias), with `routed_scaling_factor` folded into the top-k weights. DeepGEMM's Mega Gate only supports `sqrtsoftplus`.
- The FP8 path is a `DeepGemmSm100Fp8MegaMoEBackend` (`mma_type="fp8xfp8"`) selected through `get_deep_gemm_mega_moe_backend`; `Glm5NextMegaMoEExperts` subclasses `DeepseekV4MegaMoEExperts` and only changes the loader parameters.
- `--prefix-match-unit` matters for this model independently of this PR: the KDA state page makes the KV block 8,960 tokens under DEP4, and without the flag prefix hits land on whole blocks.
- Limitations: `tensor_parallel_size=1` only; SM100 only. Under DEP4 each rank holds 8.8M KV tokens.

title: [RFC]: A standard for Specialized (MonoKernels) Decodes in vllm/models
body:
### Motivation.

A **Specialized Decode** implementation is one where most/all operations in a model’s forward pass are manually implemented in a way that optimizes for the model’s specific shapes and execution patterns on certain hardware. Typically, these include heavy kernel fusions and overlap for low-latency execution, and custom kernels that tune exact grid sizes for certain batch sizes. These implementations can reach tens of thousands of lines of code, and present a major challenge in managing their complexity. This RFC proposes a standard way to modularize and integrate these runtimes into vLLM under `vllm/models/<model>/<vendor>/`.

#### Why Specialized Decodes like MonoKernels?

At low concurrency, decode is bound by launch overhead and weight reads, and a MonoKernel removes most of both. On 8× MI350X a graph-mode GLM-5.2 decode step issues ~2,459 kernels in vLLM. With the MonoKernel it issues ~210: 75 MonoKernel launches plus ~135 for dense layers 0–2, input prep and the head.
 
| GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (#60889), TP8, MI350X, ~3k-token context | vLLM | MonoKernel | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Time per token, batch 1 / 8, defaults (BF16 attention) | 13.70 / 17.33 ms | 5.92 / 11.44 ms | 2.31× / 1.51× |
| Time per token, batch 1, FP8 attention opt-in | 13.70 ms | 4.80 ms | 2.85× |
| MoE layer w/o indexer (57 of 75), batch 4 / 8, FP8 | 178.8 / 189.6 µs | 69.1 / 100.6 µs | 2.59× / 1.88× |
| MoE layer with indexer (18 of 75), batch 4 / 8, FP8 | 214.9 / 227.6 µs | 88.5 / 123.4 µs | 2.43× / 1.84× |
| AgentX time between tokens, 1 / 8 users (3,600 s/point), FP8 | 15.0 / 20.4 ms | 6.5 / 12.7 ms | 2.28× / 1.68× |
| GSM8K strict, 1,319 questions, graphs, BF16 | 1228, 1234, 1235 (3 runs) | 1240 | parity: paired McNemar p = 0.22–0.63 |

Layer times are profiler-corrected, from one run. The gain shrinks with batch size, so the target is latency-bound serving: agents, chat and small-batch decode.

### Proposed Change.

#### Goals

1. **Opt-in:** off by default, enabled with one switch (`additional_config={"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}` today).
2. **Refuse at startup:** an unsupported deployment fails with one error listing every reason, never a silent fallback.
3. **The model owns it:** code lives under `vllm/models/<model>/<vendor>/specialized_decode/`, with no core changes.
4. **One `plan()` per step:** it picks the specialized kernels or vLLM's stock forward; prefill and mixed batches always run stock.
5. **One `step()` or `run()` per pass**  If specialized_decode exists, run the `step()` or `run()` function, else call stock
6. **Fixed batch sizes:** the decode kernel declares the batch sizes it serves; larger batches run stock.
7. **Avoid duplicating weights** where prudent, reading vLLM's loaded weights and caches in place.

#### Layout
Layout (shown for a monokernel; Kimi-K3 uses `nvidia/` and `cutedsl/`):

```
vllm/models/<model>/<vendor>/
    model.py                 # calls specialized_decode_config() in __init__, plan() in forward
    model_state.py           # MRV2 ModelState: builds the decode after load, binds KV caches
    specialized_decode/
        README.md            # supported checkpoints, refusals, options
        runtime/
            __init__.py      # DecodeConfig, batch sizes, specialized_decode_config(), unsupported()
            decode.py        # SpecializedDecode: plan(), run() or Step.layer()
            ...              # weight views, guards, model-specific helpers
        mono/                # the kernels, when the decode uses monokernels
tests/models/<model>/        # proposed: CPU tests for refusals and plan() routing
```

Instantiation of specialized decode happens at startup
```
self.specialized_decode_config = specialized_decode_config(vllm_config)
self.specialized_decode = SpecializedDecode(
            self.model, self.specialized_decode_config
        )
```
Two methods to Available. 

Replace the whole forward function with the specialized decode (and let it decide when to call the stock version)
```python
# Kimi-K3 (step mode, #61867): the whole step runs in the specialized decode
decode = self.specialized_decode
step = decode.plan(positions, intermediate_tensors)
if step is not None:
    return decode.run(step, input_ids, inputs_embeds)
return self.model(input_ids, positions, intermediate_tensors, inputs_embeds)
```

Replace the Decode Layer within the forward function with the specific kernel to run, and let the forward function decide.
```python
# GLM-5.2 (layer mode, #60889): a kernel per layer, or vLLM's layer
step = None if decode is None else decode.plan(positions, intermediate_tensors)
...
kernel = step.layer(idx) if step is not None else None
hidden_states, residual = (kernel or layer)(positions, hidden_states, residual)
```

**Not in Scope**

- Prefill and mixed steps. These always run vLLM's layers.
- Models compiled with `@support_torch_compile`.
- Launches that span more than two layer (some fusions may fuse end of one layer with beginning of another)
- No Runtime fallback. If a megakernel fails the engine should stop.

##### Enabling and refusal

- **Switch:** `--monokernel` (with `--no-monokernel`), the same for every model and off by default, like `--async-scheduling`. It sets `KernelConfig.monokernel`, so it also works from a config file or the Python API.
   - Additionally we can use `--additional_config={"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}` As this will be used in the more generic case. 
  - It applies to the loaded model's spec. A model has at most one spec per vendor, so there is no name to pick.
  - There are no other user knobs. Tuning lives in the spec's `options`.
- **Refusal** happens in three stages: config (before load), model (after load) and caches (at every bind). Each stage reports every reason, not only the first. If the switch is on and the config is refused, startup raises.
- **Default-deny:** any feature in use that `supports` doesn't list is refused, then the spec's own checks run. The features are: PP, DP, EP, EPLB, DCP, PCP, LoRA, KV connectors, routed-expert capture, speculative decoding, sleep mode, CPU weight offload, weight updates, partitioned GPUs, and EAGLE3 aux layers among the kernel layers.
- MonoKernels run only under Model Runner V2.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4-Pro returns wrong answers on long prompts (>~380k tokens) when --long-prefill-token-threshold=256 is set (v0.30.0)
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM 0.30.0 (official image `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0`), torch 2.13.0+cu130
- 6 × NVIDIA B300 (driver 595.71.05), one node
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813` (revision `72e1d323`)

Serving arguments (relevant part):

```
--tokenizer-mode=deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser=deepseek_v4 --tool-call-parser=deepseek_v4
--kv-cache-dtype=fp8 --block-size=256 --moe-backend=deep_gemm_mega_moe
--attention-config={"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}
--kernel-config={"sparse_indexer_topk_backend":"deep_select"}
--max-model-len=1048576
--data-parallel-size=6 --data-parallel-size-local=6 --data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb
--enable-expert-parallel --enable-prefix-caching
--long-prefill-token-threshold=256        <-- the flag in question
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `--long-prefill-token-threshold=256`, DeepSeek-V4-Pro returns wrong or garbage answers for long prompts. Removing the flag (nothing else changed) makes every test pass up to ~1.03M prompt tokens. There is no error or warning; the answers just look confident and are wrong.

We set the flag to keep short requests responsive while a very long prompt is prefilled. On v0.30.0 the cap is applied to every request (`v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:661-662`), so a 1M-token prompt is prefilled in ~4,000 steps of 256 tokens instead of steps of `max_num_batched_tokens`.

**Test.** One document with N "facts" (`FACT: the code of warehouse W-<seed>-<i> is <6 digits>.`) separated by random filler words; the question asks for the codes of five named warehouses at a given position in the document (start / 25 % / 50 % / 75 % / end). Thinking off, temperature 0, one request at a time, sent directly to one data-parallel rank. A second test uses real prose (source code and docs) with 12 uniquely named facts inserted. Script below.

**Results** (correct answers out of 5 for the flat document, out of 3 for the prose test; two rounds where two numbers are given):

| Prompt tokens | with `--long-prefill-token-threshold=256` | flag removed |
|---|---|---|
| flat, 299k | all correct | all correct |
| flat, 404k | 25 %: 4, 5 · 50 %: 4, 1 · rest 5 | all 5/5 |
| flat, 598k | 50 %: 3, 4 · 75 %: 0, 0 · rest 5 | all 5/5 |
| flat, 793k | only the first question correct, then 0–1 of 5 | all 5/5 |
| flat, 1,033k | all 0 | all 5/5 |
| prose, 300k | all 3/3 | all 3/3 |
| prose, 629k | 3, 0, 3, 2, 3, 1 of 3 on repeated questions | all 3/3 |
| prose, 992k | 0, 0, 1, 2, 0, 1 of 3; output partly garbage | all 3/3 (two ranks, two engine starts) |

Typical wrong outputs with the flag: the same code repeated for five different names (`W-…-1000=297845 | W-…-1001=297845 | …`), names echoed as codes (`W-…-3000=W-…-3000`), or unrelated text from elsewhere in the prompt. At 629k the result changes between identical requests at temperature 0. Enabling thinking does not help.

Things we ruled out on the way (each tested alone, with the flag still set):
- the default top-k backend instead of `deep_select`: worse around 400–600k (middle of the document 0/5), same failure at 793k and 1M. Both columns above were measured with `deep_select`.
- `--attention-config={"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}` instead of `mxfp4`: no improvement (992k still garbage).

Other observations:
- Cold prefill is also faster without the flag (992k tokens: ~150–170 s TTFT vs ~245 s).
- `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` on vLLM 0.31.0 (TP2) passes the same tests at ~1M tokens **with** `--long-prefill-token-threshold=256`, also when the cap is actually active (another stream running; note that since #57951 the cap is skipped for a lone request, so a single-request test on 0.31.0 does not exercise it).
- We did not locate the faulty code. Our guess is the DeepSeek-V4 compressor / sparse-attention state carried across prefill chunk boundaries when the chunks are small. We have not tested other threshold values (e.g. 2048, 4096, 8192) or V4-Pro on 0.31.0, and can do so if that helps.

It would help if vLLM either supported small prefill chunks on this model or rejected/warned about `--long-prefill-token-threshold` values that the DeepSeek-V4 path cannot handle.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script (flat document; simplified, non-streaming version of the one we used)</summary>

```python
# usage: python probe.py <base_url> <served_model_name> <n_facts>     e.g. 4000 facts ~ 598k tokens, 6900 ~ 1.03M
import json, random, sys, time, urllib.request
base, model, nfacts = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
seed = f"{int(time.time()) % 100000}f"; r = random.Random(seed)
words = "river stone ledger harbor copper violet meadow lantern orchard granite signal compass anchor timber saffron".split()
parts, facts = [f"Reference document {seed}. It lists warehouse codes. Each line 'FACT' gives the code of one warehouse.\n"], {}
for i in range(nfacts):
    name, code = f"W-{seed}-{i:03d}", f"{r.randrange(10**6):06d}"; facts[name] = code
    parts.append(" ".join(r.choice(words) for _ in range(120)) + ".\n")
    parts.append(f"FACT: the code of warehouse {name} is {code}.\n")
text, names = "".join(parts), list(facts)

def ask(want):
    q = "Give the codes of these warehouses, one per line as NAME=CODE, nothing else: " + ", ".join(want)
    body = {"model": model, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": text + "\n" + q}], "max_tokens": 1500,
            "temperature": 0, "chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking": False}}
    req = urllib.request.Request(base + "/v1/chat/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    j = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=900))
    out = j["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] or ""
    return sum(1 for n in want if facts[n] in out), j["usage"]["prompt_tokens"], out[:120].replace("\n", " | ")

for tag, frac in [("start", 0.0), ("25%", 0.25), ("50%", 0.5), ("75%", 0.75), ("end", 1.0)]:
    i = min(int(frac * nfacts), nfacts - 5)
    print(tag, *ask(names[i:i + 5]), flush=True)
```

</details>

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix] Pin long-lived host buffers at their exact size
body:
## Overview

torch's caching host allocator, which `pin_memory()` and `pin_memory=True` go through, rounds every block up to the next power of two. That's fine for short-lived staging buffers. But for buffers that live as long as the process the cache doesn't buy anything, and a buffer just over a power of two pins up to twice its size in page-locked memory the OS can't reclaim.

This adds a small `empty_pinned()` helper (`vllm/utils/pinned_memory.py`). It allocates exactly the requested size with `cudaHostAlloc` / `hipHostMalloc` through the existing `CudaRTLibrary` wrapper and frees it once the last view is gone. I've used it in the two GiB-sized places that don't already have an open PR:

- The private per-tensor CPU KV offload tier. CUDA normally uses one exactly registered region (#50094), but ROCm has been on the private tensors since #57160, so the rounding from #53042 is back there. Fixes #53042 on ROCm.
- CPU-resident weights, which is what the prefetch weight offloader leaves on the host (CUDA and ROCm). Two places allocate those: the offloader's own copy, and `device_loading_context`, which moves a CPU weight to the GPU for `process_weights_after_loading` and then copies it back into a new pinned tensor. The second copy is the one that stays, so both have to change.

XPU keeps torch's allocator.

## Claims

- The CPU KV tier on ROCm pins exactly what it asks for instead of rounding each tensor up to a power of two. In my repro that's 4.25 GiB less page-locked memory for a 4.75 GiB tier, with identical output.
- CPU-offloaded weights are pinned at their exact size too. With the prefetch offloader on Qwen3-1.7B that's 168 MiB less page-locked memory (main pins 1.25x the offloaded weights), with identical output.
- No change to what gets pinned or when, only how big the allocation is.

## Validation

```
pytest tests/utils_/test_pinned_memory.py \
  "tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py::test_private_cpu_tier_pins_its_exact_size" \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_device_loading_context.py
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

All 10 pass on CUDA (RTX A2000 Laptop, sm_86, torch 2.13.0+cu132). The pinned memory and KV tier tests also pass on ROCm (Radeon AI PRO R9700, gfx1201, ROCm 10.0, torch 2.13). To make sure the tests check the right thing, I ran them against the code from before this change too:

- With `empty_pinned` pinning through torch and the old `gpu_worker.py`, two fail on both platforms, as they should: the fallback test (it pins when pinning is off) and the KV tier test (the caching allocator holds 128 MiB for a 66 MiB tier).
- The `device_loading_context` test fails on main: a 33 MiB weight comes back in a 64 MiB pinned block.

The KV tier test passes `mmap_region=None`, so it takes the private path on CUDA as well. The new tests are in `tests/utils_`, `tests/v1/kv_offload` and `tests/model_executor`, which CI already runs on NVIDIA and AMD.

KV tier memory, stock `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` on vLLM v0.31.1rc0 (ROCm build), `--kv-offloading-size 4.75`, which makes 36 per-layer tensors of 141,623,296 B. Pinned is the engine process's page-locked mappings minus the same baseline without a tier (about 212 MB in both runs):

| | pinned for the tier | greedy output |
|---|---|---|
| main | 9,663,676,416 B (36 x 256 MiB, 1.82x the 5,100,273,664 B asked) | `05304724...` |
| this PR | 5,098,438,656 B (36 x 141,623,296 B) | `05304724...` (same) |

Weight offload, stock `Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B` on CUDA (RTX A2000), `--offload-backend prefetch --offload-group-size 4 --offload-num-in-group 1`, so 7 of 28 layers on the host. Pinned is the server's page-locked mappings minus a run without offload. I booted main and this branch alternately, twice each, and got the same numbers both times:

| | pinned for the offloaded weights | per layer (gate_up / down / qkv / o) | c=1 decode | greedy output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 880,803,840 B | 64 / 32 / 16 / 8 MiB | 9.72 tok/s | same |
| this PR | 704,643,072 B (the 0.7047 GB the offloader reports) | 48 / 24 / 16 / 8 MiB | 9.73 tok/s | same |

I first only changed the offloader's own copy, and on ROCm with Qwen3-8B that made no difference at all (5,544,337,408 B pinned either way, 9 x (256 + 128 + 64 + 32) MiB where the weights are 192 + 96 + 48 + 32 MiB). That's how I found the `device_loading_context` copy.

## Details

Why not the alternatives:

- `cudaHostRegister` over pageable memory needs unregister bookkeeping, and registering one big region is what #57160 moved ROCm away from (`cudaHostRegister failed` at TP8 with a 500 GiB tier).
- torch's `pinned_max_round_threshold_mb` turns the rounding off, but on torch 2.13 it can hand an exact-size cached block to a larger request and overflow it (pytorch/pytorch#192722, fixed on torch main but not in a release yet). It's also process-wide.
- `get_accelerator_view_from_cpu_tensor`'s unpinned branch (what #56413 relies on) returns a device view, and these two sites need host tensors.

Trade-offs: one `cudaHostAlloc` per buffer at startup instead of a cached block, so allocation is a bit slower, but it only happens once. torch doesn't track blocks it didn't allocate across `non_blocking` copies, so the copy stays async but torch won't keep the block alive for it. Every buffer here lives as long as its worker, so that can't free memory under a copy.

Other open PRs on the same rounding, each at a different site and not touched here: UVA weight offload #56413 / #58185, the Qwen4Exp PLE table #59848, DSv4.1 Engram tables #59849, the sleep-mode CPU backup #60003, and the XPU KV tier #51956. #57506 changes `CPUOffloadingWorker.shutdown` in the same file, so one of us will need a small rebase, but the changes don't overlap.

V1's `CpuGpuBuffer` and MRV2's `UvaBuffer` also pin through torch, but they're KiB to MiB, so I left them out to keep core components untouched. Happy to do them in a follow-up with the same helper if that's wanted.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write the code, run the tests and measurements, and draft this description. I reviewed the change and the results before posting.

title: [Refactor] Move model-specific env vars into vllm/models/<model>/envs.py
body:
## Overview

Move env vars that only one specialized model reads out of the global `vllm/envs.py` and into `vllm/models/<model>/envs.py`, next to the model code that uses them. Also document this convention for contributors and agents.

## Claims

- `VLLM_KIMI_K3_SHARD_SP_SHARED_EXPERT`, `VLLM_KIMI_K3_AUX_ATTN_RES_STREAM` and `VLLM_KIMI_K3_GEMM_AR` move to `vllm/models/kimi_k3/envs.py`.
- `VLLM_DISABLE_DSV4_MEGAMOE_SHARED_EXPERT_FUSION` moves to `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/envs.py`.
- No user-visible change: the env var names, defaults and parsing are the same, and `vllm.envs.<NAME>` still resolves.
- `AGENTS.md` and `docs/configuration/env_vars.md` describe and list the model-local env vars.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_envs.py -q                        # 58 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_sequence_parallel.py \
    tests/models/kimi_k3/test_eagle3.py -q                              # 31 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>                                  # all passed, incl. mypy
```

Also checked by hand:
- `import vllm.envs` imports only `vllm.models.{deepseek_v4,kimi_k3}.envs`, not the heavy model packages.
- `Platform.validate_environ(hard_fail=True)` accepts the moved vars.
- `enable_envs_cache()` / `disable_envs_cache()` behave the same when the vars are read through the model `envs` module.
- Loading `vllm/envs.py` by path, as `setup.py` does, still works.

This is a pure refactor with no numerical change, so I didn't run model evals.

## Details

Several places look up env vars in `vllm.envs.environment_variables`: the unknown-`VLLM_*` warning, the list of vars copied to Ray workers, and `compile_factors()`. The last one matters here because `VLLM_KIMI_K3_GEMM_AR` changes the traced graph, so it has to stay in the compile-cache key. That means the model vars still need to be registered centrally.

How it works:
- Each `vllm/models/<model>/envs.py` imports only the standard library and has its own `environment_variables` dict.
- `vllm/envs.py` finds `vllm/models/*/envs.py`, loads each file by path (so the model package `__init__`, which pulls in torch and kernels, doesn't run), and registers it under `vllm.models.<model>.envs` in `sys.modules`.
- It merges each file's vars into the central dict and asserts that no name is defined twice.
- A module-level `__getattr__` in each model's `envs.py` forwards reads to `vllm.envs`, so they use the same cache.

Model code reads these vars through `from vllm.models.<model> import envs`.

Out of scope:
- Vars read by more than one model stay in `vllm/envs.py`: `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS`, `VLLM_MULTI_STREAM_GEMM_TOKEN_THRESHOLD` and `VLLM_DCP_Q_REPLICATE`.
- A few model files read env vars without the `VLLM_` prefix straight from `os.environ`: `INKLING_*`, `LAMPORT_RS_SCONV` and `XHS_VIDEO_JPEG_QUALITY`. Moving them means renaming them, so that's left for a follow-up.

**Not a duplicate:** I found no open PR that moves model env vars (searched for `model envs.py`, `VLLM_KIMI_K3` and "model-specific environment variables").

**AI assistance:** I wrote this change with Claude Code and reviewed it myself. I haven't tested the new `AGENTS.md` instruction with a fresh agent.

title: [Bugfix] Fix DeepSeek-V4 FP8 O-projection crash with a forced --linear-backend
body:
## Overview

Fixes #60587

DeepSeek-V4 with a block-FP8 checkpoint fails at engine init when `--linear-backend` forces a non-DeepGEMM FP8 kernel, for example `--linear-backend marlin`. The error is a `torch.bmm` shape error in `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`. This change picks the kernel again for block-FP8 `is_bmm` layers after loading. On CUDA, `wo_a` then always gets the DeepGEMM layout that the O-projection reads.

Compared with #56119, this fix:

- Fixes the other forced backends too, not only Marlin: [#56119](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56119) guards only the Marlin case. On its tree, `humming` still fails with the issue's 4x shape error, and `triton` and `cutlass` fail with `t.dim() == N`. All of them pass with this change.
- Keeps `wo_a` in FP8: [#56119](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56119) runs `wo_a` as a bf16 copy through `torch.bmm`. On the reproducer below, that leaves 0.75 GiB less KV cache per GPU (65.97 vs 66.72 GiB with FlashMLA, 66.33 vs 67.08 GiB with FlashInfer).
- Tests the path that failed: The new test builds a real block-FP8 layer and runs `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`. It fails on the old code with the issue's error. The regression test in [#56119](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56119) uses a fake Marlin kernel and checks only the weight dtype.
- Is smaller and reuses existing kernel selection: It adds 29 lines in `vllm/` against 76. It picks the kernel again after loading, as the ModelOpt MXFP8 path already does, and adds no new dequantize helper that repeats `scaled_dequantize()`.


## Claims

- `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp` with `--linear-backend marlin` now starts and serves. Both attention paths named in the issue work: the default (FlashMLA) and `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`. Before, engine init failed in the memory-profiling forward pass.
- The same change fixes `humming`, `triton` and `cutlass` as forced backends. They broke `wo_a` in the same way.
- All other linear layers still use the requested backend. Only `wo_a` takes DeepGEMM. The model never calls `wo_a`'s own kernel. It only reads its weight.
- A new unit test covers this. It fails on the old code with the issue's error.

## Validation

Setup: 2 x NVIDIA B200 in one machine (TP=2), driver 610.19, CUDA 13.3, torch 2.13.0+cu130. vLLM commit `81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93`, then the same commit plus this change. Weights: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp`, revision `6821d6ad3681a4b137b066b76094fa82ebd0a380`. The issue used 2 x GB10 (SM 12.1). This was not run on GB10.

Reproducer. No request is needed, because it fails during startup:

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --max-model-len 524288 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --enable-prefix-caching \
  --load-format safetensors --moe-backend marlin --linear-backend marlin \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
```

Before (on both TP workers):

```
File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py", line 501, in forward
    return self._o_proj(attn_out, positions)
File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py", line 62, in _o_proj
    return deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj(
File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/o_proj.py", line 98, in deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj
    torch.bmm(
RuntimeError: Expected size for first two dimensions of batch2 tensor to be: [4, 4096] but got: [4, 1024].
```

After:

```
(Worker_TP0 pid=2338534) INFO 10-09 05:03:03 [__init__.py:747] Selected MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel for Fp8LinearMethod
(Worker_TP0 pid=2338534) WARNING 10-09 05:03:27 [__init__.py:369] --linear-backend=marlin has no kernel for this linear layer type; using automatic selection for that layer type.
(Worker_TP0 pid=2338534) INFO 10-09 05:04:17 [gpu_worker.py:726] Available KV cache memory: 66.72 GiB
INFO:     Application startup complete.
```

`Available KV cache memory` is printed after the profiling forward pass, which is where it failed before. The logs have no `Traceback` and no `RuntimeError`. As a check of the O-projection output, two requests were sent with temperature 0. A completion of "The capital of France is" returned " Paris…". A chat request, "What is 17 times 23? Answer with the number only.", returned `391`.

| Tree | Attention backend | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `81198e97b` | default and `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` | 4 (1 editable install, 3 in the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image at the same commit) | all 4 failed with the error above | | with this change | default (FlashMLA) | 2 | both reached `Application startup complete.` and answered correctly | | with this change | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` | 1 | reached `Application startup complete.` and answered correctly |

New unit test, on the same machine:

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_fp8.py -k test_fp8_block_bmm_projects_under_linear_backend -v
```

- With the fix: `auto`, `marlin` and `triton` pass.
- Old code (old `fp8.py` and `kernels/linear/__init__.py`, new test): `auto` passes. `marlin` fails with `RuntimeError: Expected size for first two dimensions of batch2 tensor to be: [2, 512] but got: [2, 128].` `triton` fails with `RuntimeError: Assertion error (csrc/apis/../jit_kernels/impls/../heuristics/../../utils/layout.hpp:46): t.dim() == N`.

Nearby tests with the fix: 65 passed, 1 skipped. This includes the existing MXFP8 bmm test, `test_mxfp8_bmm_loads_and_projects_grouped_weights`. The 4 deselected tests download full models.

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py tests/quantization/test_fp8.py \
  -k "not test_model_load_and_run and not test_kv_cache_model_load_and_run and not test_load_fp16_model"
```

`pre-commit` passes on the three changed files. The test is in `tests/quantization/test_fp8.py`, which is already in Buildkite (`check-test-tethering` passed). It skips without CUDA or DeepGEMM. No accuracy eval was run.

## Details

**Root cause.** DeepSeek-V4 builds `wo_a` as a plain `ColumnParallelLinear` and sets `is_bmm = True` after construction. So `Fp8LinearMethod.create_weights` picks `wo_a`'s kernel as for any other linear layer. The model never calls that kernel. `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` reads `wo_a.weight` and its scales directly and runs DeepGEMM's grouped `fp8_einsum`. That needs an FP8 weight in DeepGEMM's `(groups, rank, K)` layout. On CUDA, only `DeepGemmFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` reads `is_bmm` and builds that layout. With the default backend, DeepGEMM comes first, so it works. With `--linear-backend marlin`, Marlin repacks the FP8 `(4096, 4096)` weight into int32 tiles `(256, 16384)`. The O-projection then sees a non-FP8 dtype and takes its bf16 `torch.bmm` branch. There, `view(4, 1024, -1)` gives `[4, 1024, 1024]`, which is 4x too small. Triton and Cutlass leave the weight 2-D, so DeepGEMM asserts `t.dim() == N`.

A debug print at the entry of `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` confirmed this. Before the fix, `wo_a.weight` was `torch.int32 (256, 16384)` with `MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`. With the fix, it is `torch.float8_e4m3fn (4, 1024, 4096)` with `DeepGemmFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`. The input shape was right (32 local heads = 4 groups x 8 heads).

**Fix.** This follows the ModelOpt MXFP8 path, which already picks the kernel again for `is_bmm` layers in `process_weights_after_loading`.

- `init_fp8_linear_kernel` takes a new `is_bmm` argument. For block FP8 it then uses `_POSSIBLE_FP8_BLOCK_BMM_KERNELS`. On CUDA that list holds only `DeepGemmFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`. Other platforms keep their usual lists, so ROCm, XPU and CPU do not change.
- `Fp8LinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading` picks the kernel again for a block-FP8 `is_bmm` layer, because `is_bmm` is set by then.
- If `--linear-backend` has no kernel in that list, the existing `_resolve_backend_kernels` logs the warning shown above and uses automatic selection for that layer.

**Limitations.**

- With `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` and `--linear-backend marlin`, startup now fails at load with `ValueError: Failed to find a kernel`. Before, it failed at the first forward pass. The message says only Hopper and Blackwell are supported, which is misleading on a B200.
- XPU may have a similar gap. `xpu_sparse.py` reads `wo_a.bmm_weight`, and only `XPUFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` sets it, so `--linear-backend triton` on XPU could fail. This is not changed, because XPU could not be tested here.
- Other quant methods that call `init_fp8_linear_kernel`, for example compressed-tensors FP8 block, do not pick the kernel again for `is_bmm`. No DSV4 checkpoint used here goes through them.
- Not run on GB10 (SM 12.1). `support_deep_gemm` includes the SM 12.x family, so `wo_a` should get DeepGEMM there too.
- `cutlass` and `humming` also failed before and pass now, but they are not in the test. Humming needs an optional package, and Cutlass block support depends on the GPU.

---

title: [Bug]: Exception on a non-output TP rank is logged and the worker dequeues the next RPC, so ranks desync and collectives mispair (cross-node deadlock)
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM nightly `af7f9488` (V2 model runner). The code path is unchanged on main `fa94ad41` (2026-10-09).
- Two DGX Station GB300 nodes, one GPU each, TP2 + EP2, mp executor, multi-node.
- DeepSeek-V4-Pro, DSpark speculative decoding K=5, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.99`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

When `execute_model` or `sample_tokens` raises on a rank that is not the output rank, `WorkerProc._execute_worker_rpc` logs `WorkerProc hit an exception.` and returns to `worker_busy_loop`, which dequeues the next RPC. Only the output rank reports the failure to the engine. The failing rank then starts step N+1 while its peers are still in step N, and the two sides' collectives pair with the wrong ops.

In our case this ended in a cross-node deadlock and, five minutes later, `RPC call to sample_tokens timed out` and EngineDead. In the CPU reproduction below it does not even hang: both processes exit 0 after summing mispaired all-reduces. So this is a correctness risk, not only a latency one.

This is the behaviour reported in #23985 (closed by the stale bot). A shorter `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, as suggested there, does not fix it: the failing rank never waits, so nothing times out on its side, and its peer may already have completed a mispaired collective by the time the timeout fires.

### What happened (from the logs)

1. 13:38:06: rank 1 raised `RuntimeError: ... lazy_cuKernelGetFunction ... CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` inside `sample_tokens` → `DSparkSpeculator.propose` → `_precompute_context_kv` → the drafter's `context_wkv_proj`. That is a DeepGEMM fp8 GEMM that had to JIT-load a kernel the process had not used before (reported separately: DeepGEMM warm-up skips the speculator model). Logged, then swallowed.
2. Rank 1 skipped the drafter forward and its all-reduces and entered `execute_model(N+1)`.
3. 13:38:17: last throughput line. 13:39-13:42: four `No available shared memory broadcast block` warnings.
4. 13:43:04: `RPC call to sample_tokens timed out`, EngineDead.

Per-layer call counters in an expert hook we run confirm the desync. At the hang, rank 1 was ahead of rank 0 by 3 layer calls and 288 tokens. 288 = 3 x 96, and 96 = 16 requests x 6 verify tokens, so rank 1 was three target layers into step N+1 while rank 0 was still in step N's drafter. (Drafter layers carry 80 tokens per pass and the hook does not count them.)

### Expected behaviour

An exception in a step RPC on any rank makes the engine fail promptly and attributably. No rank starts a later step's collectives after failing an earlier one.

### Minimal reproducer (CPU only, about 5 s)

Two gloo processes replay vLLM's step RPC shape (`execute_model` = 4 collectives; `sample_tokens` = a logits gather + 3 drafter collectives) with `_execute_worker_rpc`'s exception handling. Each all-reduce carries its op id, so a correctly paired collective sums to 2 x op id.

```python
# repro_swallow.py   usage: python repro_swallow.py [--failfast]
import datetime, socket, sys
import torch, torch.distributed as dist
import torch.multiprocessing as mp

STEPS, FAIL_STEP, FAILFAST = 6, 3, "--failfast" in sys.argv

def worker(rank, port):
    dist.init_process_group("gloo", init_method=f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{port}", rank=rank,
                            world_size=2, timeout=datetime.timedelta(seconds=20))
    step = 0
    def coll(op):
        t = torch.tensor([float(op)]); dist.all_reduce(t)
        if t.item() != 2 * op:
            print(f"rank {rank}: op {op} paired with peer op {int(t.item()) - op}", flush=True)
    def execute_model():
        for i in range(4): coll(1000 * step + i)          # target layers
    def sample_tokens():
        coll(1000 * step + 10)                            # logits gather
        if rank == 1 and step == FAIL_STEP:
            raise RuntimeError("drafter kernel load failed")
        for i in range(3): coll(1000 * step + 20 + i)     # drafter layers
    def execute_worker_rpc(func, output_rank=0):          # vLLM's handling
        try:
            func()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"rank {rank}: WorkerProc hit an exception: {e}", flush=True)
            if FAILFAST: sys.exit(86)
            if rank == output_rank: raise                 # only rank 0 reports
    try:
        for step in range(1, STEPS + 1):
            execute_worker_rpc(execute_model)
            execute_worker_rpc(sample_tokens)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"rank {rank}: {type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:60]}", flush=True)
    print(f"rank {rank}: finished", flush=True)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    s = socket.socket(); s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0)); port = s.getsockname()[1]; s.close()
    ctx = mp.spawn(worker, args=(port,), nprocs=2, join=False)
    for p in ctx.processes: p.join(60)
    print("exit codes:", [p.exitcode for p in ctx.processes])
```

Output with the stock handling (torch 2.10, CPU):

```
rank 1: WorkerProc hit an exception: drafter kernel load failed
rank 0: op 3020 paired with peer op 4000
rank 1: op 4000 paired with peer op 3020
rank 0: op 3021 paired with peer op 4001
...
exit codes: [0, 0]
```

Rank 0's first drafter collective of step 3 is summed with rank 1's first target collective of step 4. Every collective after that is mispaired, and both processes exit 0. With `--failfast`, rank 1 exits at once, rank 0 fails on the closed peer, no collective is mispaired, and the exit codes are `[86, 86]`.

On GPU we also confirmed this with an injected fault: raise once in rank 1's `propose()` after 200 proposals. With the patch below, rank 1 logged the failure and exited, and the engine reported `sample_tokens timed out` within the 120 s we had set for `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, instead of hanging silently for five minutes. The hook counters were identical on both ranks afterwards (80,517 calls / 9,379,974 tokens), so no rank ran ahead.

### Root cause

`vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py`, `WorkerProc._execute_worker_rpc` (main `fa94ad41`):

```python
except Exception as e:
    ...
    logger.exception("WorkerProc hit an exception.")
    if output_rank is None or self.rank == output_rank:
        self.handle_output(e)
```

Non-output ranks fall through, and the busy loop dequeues the next RPC.

### Proposed fix

For step RPCs (`execute_model`, `sample_tokens`, `execute_dummy_batch`), treat an exception on any rank as fatal for that worker:
1. log the traceback with the rank and method;
2. let the output rank hand the error to the engine, as today;
3. exit the worker process.

Leave other RPCs as they are. The peer ranks then fail on the closed connection or on the engine's RPC timeout, but they never complete a mispaired collective.

Alternatives considered:
- **Propagate the non-output rank's exception to the engine** (every rank replies on failure). Better attribution but more plumbing. It works alongside the fix above.
- **A per-step all-reduce of an "ok" flag.** Rejected: it cannot repair a desync, because the failing rank may already have issued some of its collectives.
- **A shorter execute-model timeout** (#23985). Needed for fast detection on the peer side, but not enough on its own.

### Evidence that the mitigation holds

We ran exit-on-step-exception as a local patch, together with drafter DeepGEMM warm-up at boot (reported separately) and an explicit KV size (`--kv-cache-memory-bytes`). That left 653-778 MiB of device memory free, against 14-470 MiB before.
- GSM8K-200 (thinking) completed at 195/200 = 97.5%, where the unpatched run had hung. A 30-minute mixed soak served 1,258 requests with 0 timeouts and 0 worker exceptions.
- A later 20-minute streaming soak on the final config: 801/801 OK, 0 timeouts, 0 hangs, 0 worker exceptions, 0 CUDA OOMs, and the hook counters stayed identical on both ranks.
- Before the fix, at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.99`, the same reproducer traffic killed the engine within about 2.5 minutes. That failure was a symmetric OOM on both ranks, so the output rank reported it and the engine died cleanly (17 HTTP 500s) instead of hanging. The hang needs a failure on one rank only.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the documentation page, which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug][Spec Decode]: DeepGEMM warm-up covers only the target model; speculator GEMMs JIT-load in the serving hot path
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM nightly `af7f9488`. The code path is unchanged on main `fa94ad41` (2026-10-09).
- DeepSeek-V4-Pro + DSpark (K=5), two DGX Station GB300 nodes, TP2 + EP2.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`kernel_warmup` calls `deep_gemm_warmup(worker.get_model(), max_num_batched_tokens)`. `worker.get_model()` is the target model, so the speculator's DeepGEMM linears are never warmed. Each new M range of a drafter GEMM is compiled and loaded while serving.

With DSpark this happens on ordinary traffic:
- The drafter replays a FULL CUDA graph that stores context K/V for at most `num_reqs_padded x 6` target rows.
- Any step with more target tokens than that (any step that includes a prefill) stores the extra rows eagerly (`dflash/speculator.py`, around L475-482 at `af7f9488`).
- That eager call is a DeepGEMM GEMM with M = target tokens - graph rows, and M varies with the traffic mix.

In our run, short staggered GSM8K prompts (135-210 tokens; 2 requests, then 14 more) reached an M range that 40 minutes of earlier benchmark traffic had not. The JIT load needs device memory. At `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.99`, rank 1 had as little as 14 MiB free, so the load failed with `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` on rank 1 only. That one-rank failure then triggered a second bug, reported separately: an exception on a non-output rank is swallowed, and the ranks desync.

### Expected behaviour

Every DeepGEMM kernel the serving path can use, including the speculator's, is loaded at boot. Nothing is compiled or loaded while serving.

### Proposed fix

After the target warm-up, run the same `deep_gemm_warmup` over the speculator model when there is one. In our local patch this covers every DeepGEMM linear of `speculator.model`, over vLLM's own M set. It warmed 1,164 drafter GEMMs at boot on our config. We saw no drafter JIT while serving in any later run, including a 20-minute streaming soak (801/801 OK).

A related docs note, not part of the fix: with `--gpu-memory-utilization` close to 1.0, anything else that loads lazily (NCCL, Triton, cuBLAS) can hit the same wall. We now size the KV cache explicitly with `--kv-cache-memory-bytes`.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the documentation page, which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
