title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Prototype Engram to delayed mHC input fusion
body:
## Overview

Prototype an opt-in fusion of the DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram gate/residual update with the following delayed mHC input collapse and RMSNorm. This is a **Draft for implementation review; GPU correctness, performance and model validation are pending**.

Inspired by the DP fusion in [SGLang #43065](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43065). Related vLLM tracking: [#57448](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57448).

## Claims

- Add a producer path that returns both the updated BF16 residual and the normalized input formed with the incoming pre-mix.
- Reuse the existing mHC `stats` specialization to generate the next coefficients without repeating the input collapse and normalization.
- Keep the prototype **off by default**. `VLLM_USE_ENGRAM_MHC_FUSION=1` selects it only on CUDA Blackwell with TP1, no sequence parallelism, and no active mHC overlap stream.

No speedup or GPU numerical-equivalence claim is made yet.

## Validation

Completed local checks: Ruff, six-file Python AST parsing, `git diff --check`, and independent source review. The extracted WKV preparation statements match the original preparation AST. The full pre-commit invocation passed its applicable hooks except for a macOS mypy error on the unchanged `mmap.MADV_HUGEPAGE` access. The original main source reproduces the same error under `--platform darwin`; the hook's mypy 1.20.2 passes all four changed source files and both test files with `--platform linux --python-version 3.11`. No source change or error suppression was used for that platform check.

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/envs.py \
  vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py \
  tests/kernels/test_engram.py \
  tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py
mypy --platform linux --python-version 3.11 \
  vllm/envs.py vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py
mypy --platform linux --python-version 3.11 --follow-imports skip \
  tests/kernels/test_engram.py tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py
```

One parametrized regression was added to the existing Engram suite, covering empty/single/odd token counts, shorter KV input, identity and carried pre-mixes, gate masks including a masked NaN, both BF16 rounding boundaries, and CUDA graph replay after changing and restoring inputs. Two existing fake-decoder setups initialize the new flag to false. **These GPU tests have not been run yet**:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py \
  -k 'fused_engram_post_wkv or engram_mhc_preserves_delayed_input' -q
python -m pytest tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k 'deepseek_v41_decoder_mixes or deepseek_v41_capture_previous_aux' -q
```

Before requesting review readiness: compile and validate on B300; compare the complete gate + coefficient projection + stats/input sequence using interleaved graph microbenchmarks; then measure cold DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill on two B300s with TP1/DP2/EP2, 16K chunk per rank, APC/EPLB off, output length 1, three independent AB/BA/AB rounds at 64K/c8 and 32K/c4, 32K/c8, 64K/c4 regression checks. Model output checks are also pending. A kernel improvement alone will not be reported as model throughput improvement.

## Details

The Engram boundary currently materializes the updated residual before delayed mHC reads it again for the input collapse. The new token program computes the HC gates, writes the same BF16 residual, and accumulates the incoming pre-mix collapse while those values are available. It rounds the collapse to BF16 before RMSNorm. The separate coefficient projection still consumes the complete updated residual and produces all next pre/post/residual coefficients using the existing math.

The full residual store, WKV computation, previous-layer auxiliary observation point, mask arithmetic, and both BF16 rounding boundaries are retained. This does not fuse communication or remove coefficient work. Triton and TileLang can use different normalization reduction trees; the regression reuses the existing delayed-mHC normalization tolerance rather than claiming bitwise normalized outputs.

One token program serializes the HC gates, which may cost more than the saved read/normalization work. Register pressure and whole-model benefit need measurement. The default-off switch keeps this unvalidated prototype explicit while those results are collected.

Duplicate checks covered current open `engram mhc` PRs, the #57448 tracker and linked work, and complete public Engram/mHC and Engram/fused searches. No matching vLLM gate-to-delayed-input fusion was found. [#56633](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56633) retains a separate Engram boundary; [#60153](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60153) excludes it. This is separate from packed Engram lookup [#59923](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59923) and WKV sharding [#58678](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58678). SGLang #43065 is prior art for the fusion, not a claim of original invention here.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Fix TP group hang on steps without scheduled tokens
body:
## Overview

With a host pool shared across TP ranks (#56629), a TP group can hang forever on a step with no scheduled tokens. On such steps, every TP rank now waits at a CPU barrier right after its event wait.

## Claims

- Fixes a hang between TP rank 0 and a TP rank whose host is one step behind, on steps with no scheduled tokens (`no_forward`).
- Steps with tokens are unchanged.

## Validation

**Reproducer.** The script below copies the shared-event protocol from `hisparse/worker.py` onto 2 GPUs and holds rank 1's host for 0.5 s before one wait. Run on H100s:

```
torchrun --nproc-per-node 2 hisparse_event_hang.py {zero_next|zero_now|tokens} {none|sync|barrier}
```

| Case | `main` (`none`) | rank 0 host sync (`sync`) | this PR (`barrier`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zero_next`: rank 1 late, next step has no tokens | HANG 3/3 | PASS 3/3 | PASS 3/3 |
| `zero_now`: rank 1 late on a step with no tokens, next step has tokens | HANG 3/3 | HANG 3/3 | PASS 3/3 |
| `tokens`: rank 1 late, every step has tokens | PASS 3/3 | | |

When it hangs, GPU 0 is at 100% (spinning in the all-reduce) and GPU 1 is at 0% (its stream is blocked on the event).

**Unit test.** `test_zero_token_step_holds_tp_ranks_after_host_write_wait` checks that start_step waits at the TP barrier after the event wait on steps with no tokens, and only when the host region is shared.

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py -k "zero_token_step or draft_layer or full_graph_step or no_forward"
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` `worker.py` | 1 failed (`shared=True, num_tokens=0`), 7 passed |
| this PR | 8 passed |

These tests ran in a vLLM 0.31.0 H100 image (`f6d5a33`) with this branch's `worker.py` and test file swapped in. The image has no pytest, so a small runner expanded the parametrization. `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes.

**Production.** A P/D decode deployment hit this hang. It runs HiSparse and NIXL through `MultiConnector`, at TP8 x DP4 with EP32 and MTP:
- One TP rank's GPU sat at 0% while its 7 TP peers sat at 100%.
- The other DP ranks then hit DeepEP dispatch timeouts.
- Each time, the engine was in its first minutes, when first contact with new prefill engines slows the NIXL read post on the main thread (0.1 to 2.4 s).

The reproducer shows the same GPU pattern. This patch has not yet run end to end on that deployment.

## Details

The protocol uses two shared events, A and B:
- Every step, each TP rank's stream waits on the event rank 0 recorded in the previous step.
- Rank 0 then records the other event in `finish_forward`.
- A stream wait binds to the most recent record at the time of the wait call.

**Trigger.** A TP rank's host falls one step behind rank 0, and the next step has no scheduled tokens.

**Mechanism:**

| | TP rank 0 | TP rank 1 (host late) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | step 5: wait A, launch forward 5, record B | still before its step 5 wait |
| 2 | step 6, no tokens: wait B, record A right away | |
| 3 | | step 5: wait A. The wait binds to rank 0's step 6 record |
| 4 | GPU: the forward 5 all-reduce waits for rank 1 | GPU: waits for the step 6 record, which is queued behind rank 0's forward 5 |

**Effect.** The TP group hangs and nothing times out. With DP and EP, the other DP ranks then block in their MoE collectives.

**Why steps with tokens are safe.** Before recording, rank 0 host-syncs on staging (`_finish_mirror_phase`). That staging is queued behind the previous forward's TP collectives, and every rank joins those only after its wait. A step with no tokens has no forward, so nothing orders rank 0's record after the other ranks' waits.

**Fix.** On steps with no tokens, every TP rank joins `get_tp_group().barrier()` (the CPU group) right after its wait. Every rank has then issued its wait before rank 0 can record again, on this step and the next.
- `num_tokens` comes from the same scheduler output on every TP rank, so all ranks take the barrier on the same steps.
- Without a shared host region, each rank uses its own local events, so there is no barrier.

**Why not a host sync on rank 0 alone.** The `zero_now` row: a sync can only prove that the other ranks reached the last step with a forward. A step with no tokens followed by a step with tokens still hangs.

**Cost.** One CPU barrier per step with no tokens. Those steps launch no forward.

**Not a duplicate.** I checked the 30 open PRs matching `hisparse`, plus searches for `host_write_event`, `hisparse hang`, `hisparse deadlock` and `hisparse barrier`. None changes how the shared host write events are ordered. #59877 fixes a separate NIXL thread-safety bug found in the same investigation.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation, the change, the test and the reproducer.

<details>
<summary>hisparse_event_hang.py</summary>

```python
"""Two-rank model of HiSparse's shared host write events (hisparse/worker.py).

Rank 0 creates two IPC events and shares them. Every step, each rank flips to the
other event and its stream waits on the previous one (`start_step`). Rank 0 alone
records the current event at the end of the step (`finish_forward`), after a host
sync on staging queued before the step on steps with tokens (`_finish_mirror_phase`).
The forward is matmuls plus an all-reduce, standing in for the TP collectives.
Rank 1's host is held DELAY s before its step 5 wait.

  PLAN  zero_next  step 6 has no tokens
        zero_now   step 5 has no tokens, step 6 has tokens
        tokens     every step has tokens
  FIX   none       as on main
        sync       rank 0 also host-syncs before recording on steps without tokens
        barrier    every rank joins a CPU barrier after its wait on steps without tokens

torchrun --nproc-per-node 2 hisparse_event_hang.py PLAN FIX [DELAY]
Prints PASS, or HANG with per-GPU utilization after 20 s.
"""
import os, subprocess, sys, threading, time

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist

plan, fix = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
delay = float(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 0.5
zero_step = {"zero_next": 6, "zero_now": 5, "tokens": None}[plan]
assert fix in ("none", "sync", "barrier")
rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
torch.cuda.set_device(rank)
dist.init_process_group("nccl")
cpu_group = dist.new_group(backend="gloo")
stream = torch.cuda.current_stream()

handles = [None]
if rank == 0:
    events = (torch.cuda.Event(interprocess=True), torch.cuda.Event(interprocess=True))
    for e in events:
        e.record(stream)
    handles = [tuple(e.ipc_handle() for e in events)]
dist.broadcast_object_list(handles, src=0)
if rank != 0:
    device = torch.device("cuda", rank)
    events = tuple(torch.cuda.Event.from_ipc_handle(device, h) for h in handles[0])
torch.cuda.synchronize()
dist.barrier()

done = threading.Event()


def watchdog():
    if not done.wait(20):
        util = subprocess.run(
            ["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu", "--format=csv,noheader", "-i", "0,1"],
            capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
        print(f"rank{rank} HANG at step {step}, GPU util: " + util.strip().replace("\n", " | "), flush=True)
        os._exit(2)


threading.Thread(target=watchdog, daemon=True).start()
a = torch.randn(4096, 4096, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
cur, nxt = events[1], 0
for step in range(10):
    has_tokens = step != zero_step
    staging = torch.cuda.Event()
    staging.record(stream)
    if rank == 1 and step == 5:
        time.sleep(delay)  # e.g. a slow NIXL read post before start_step
    prev, cur = cur, events[nxt]
    nxt ^= 1
    stream.wait_event(prev)
    if not has_tokens and fix == "barrier":
        dist.barrier(group=cpu_group)
    if has_tokens:
        y = a
        for _ in range(8):
            y = y @ a
            dist.all_reduce(y)
            y = y / 4096
    if rank == 0:
        if has_tokens or fix == "sync":
            staging.synchronize()
        cur.record(stream)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
done.set()
print(f"rank{rank} PASS", flush=True)
dist.destroy_process_group()
```

</details>

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Keep ds_mla cache-format canonicalization layer-local
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #48406.

`MLAAttention.__init__` canonicalizes the sparse-MLA KV cache format for FLASHMLA_SPARSE / SM120 (`fp8` -> `fp8_ds_mla`, `nvfp4` kept) and wrote the result back into the **shared global** `cache_config.cache_dtype`. Spec-decode drafters (DSpark / DFlash family) reuse that same `cache_config` object when the speculative config pins no `kv_cache_dtype`, so the drafter's non-MLA attention layers ran backend selection with `kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla`, which no non-MLA backend serves:

```
ValueError: No valid attention backend found for cuda with AttentionSelectorConfig(
    ..., kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla, use_mla=False, ...)
```

Simply deleting the writeback is not sufficient: the impl and the KV cache allocation are already driven by the layer-local canonical value (`self.kv_cache_dtype` -> `MLAAttentionSpec.cache_dtype_str`, 656B/token packed layout), but the metadata builders still read the global config, see the raw `fp8` alias, and skip building the fp8 metadata. The first forward then dies far from the root cause:

```
FlashMLASparseMetadataBuilder.__init__  -> use_fp8_kv_cache = False   (global says "fp8")
FlashMLASparseImpl                      -> use_fp8_cache = True        (layer says fp8_ds_mla)
forward -> _forward_fp8_kv_mixed_batch -> assert isinstance(fp8_metadata, FP8KernelMetadata)  # AssertionError
```

(the separate prefill/decode path asserts the same way at its two `FP8SeparatePrefillDecode` checks).

## Approach

The resolved cache format is a **layer property**, and it already has a propagation channel: `MLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec()` writes it into `MLAAttentionSpec.cache_dtype_str`. So:

1. `mla_attention.py`: drop the `cache_config.cache_dtype` writeback in `MLAAttention.__init__` (keeps the global config un-polluted for spec-decode drafters — fixes #48406).
2. `flashmla_sparse.py`: `FlashMLASparseMetadataBuilder` now resolves the layout from `kv_cache_spec.cache_dtype_str`, falling back to the global `cache_config.cache_dtype` when the spec carries no such field (non-MLA specs). The PCP+DCP guard message uses the same source, so a genuinely non-ds_mla layout still raises `NotImplementedError` while a spec-level `fp8_ds_mla` no longer misreports.
3. `mla_attention.py` (`MLACommonMetadataBuilder`): the DCP workspace `use_packed_fp8_cache` flag reads the same spec field with the same fallback.

The DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 packed-layout paths (`_resolve_dsv4_*`) are untouched: their drafters are MLA layers that need the ds_mla format, and their ~10 downstream readers (SWA page alignment, compressor, CuTeDSL kernels) still consume the global-config protocol as before.

## Not a duplicate

- #58773 fixes the same class of leak on the **drafter side** (strip inherited ds_mla dtypes in `load_dflash_model`); this PR fixes it at the **source** (the target no longer mutates the shared config). They are complementary: this PR covers drafters whose loaders pass `cache_config` through untouched, and also fixes the builder/impl split that a writeback removal alone would leave behind.
- #56155 adds a new `AttentionSpec.cache_dtype` field for layer-wise mixed KV encodings; this PR reuses the existing `cache_dtype_str` channel only and changes no spec schema.

## Test Plan

New regression tests in `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py`:

- `test_flashmla_builder_reads_fp8_layout_from_spec_not_global_config` — spec says `fp8_ds_mla`, global says `fp8`; builder must report `use_fp8_kv_cache=True` (red on a writeback-only removal, green here).

- The drafter's non-MLA layers no longer observe `fp8_ds_mla` (fixes the #48406 backend-selection crash).

- Local: ruff check + format clean on all three touched files; full pytest of `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py` not runnable in my local Windows environment (unix-only deps in the conftest chain); the two new tests were validated on the target server environment.

title: [KV Cache] Size packed Mamba groups by the unpadded state
body:
## Overview Block-outermost layouts pack Mamba states into blocks at their own page size (`_get_packed_kv_cache_groups`), so padding the Mamba page to the attention page only lowers the number of states per block. This drops that padding when the attention backends support only block-outermost layouts, and lets a packed Mamba group widen the block by up to one state when that saves a group. #55449, stacked on this PR, corrects the block size for packed ds_mla caches, which this PR leaves unchanged; the two change disjoint configurations. ## Claims - `_align_hybrid_block_size` skips the Mamba padding when every layout from `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` is block-outermost. If the layout still resolves to a layer-outermost one, `unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size` pads the Mamba pages to the largest page. - `_get_packed_kv_cache_groups` also builds the groups with one extra state per Mamba group and keeps them only if that saves a group and lowers the worst-case bytes per request. - GLM-5.3-Flash with MTP off and an fp8 or bf16 MLA cache: 4 → 3 KDA groups, up to +26% max concurrency. No measured configuration loses capacity. ## Validation GLM-5.3-Flash (real `config.json`) through the allocation path on CPU, 960 configurations: max concurrency is higher in 140, unchanged in the rest, including every `fp8_ds_mla` one.
Max concurrency vs main (main ec8a372566, this PR e5b4c3c184) SM90/SM100/SM120 × TP 1/2/4/8 × MTP 0/1/3/5 × 8k/32k/128k × prefix caching on/off × 8/40 GiB KV cache per GPU: | platform | `--kv-cache-dtype` | configs | better | equal | worse | max | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | SM90 | `fp8` | 192 | 48 | 144 | 0 | +25.6% | | SM90 | `auto` (bf16) | 192 | 44 | 148 | 0 | +21.5% | | SM90 | `fp8_ds_mla` | 192 | 0 | 192 | 0 | 0% | | SM100 | `fp8` | 192 | 48 | 144 | 0 | +25.9% | | SM120 | `auto` (→ `fp8_ds_mla`) | 192 | 0 | 192 | 0 | 0% | At 512k/1M: 76 of 192 better (up to +3.1%), none worse; without the bytes-per-request check, 20 lose up to 2.6%.
```bash pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -k "glm5_like_hybrid or hybrid_mla_block_alignment" ``` `test_packed_groups_glm5_like_hybrid[12288-8192-3]` and `test_hybrid_mla_block_alignment` fail on main; `test_packed_groups_glm5_like_hybrid[12288-32768-4]` pins the bytes-per-request check. Not run on a GPU. ## Details - With the padding, GLM-5.3-Flash's block holds 11 KDA states, so its 34 KDA layers need 4 groups; without it, or with the widening, 12 fit. Dropping the padding alone improves 96 configurations, the widening alone 108, both 140. - Only GLM-5.3-Flash (KPOOL tail cache) and Qwen4Exp with QSA side caches skip the padding today; Qwen4Exp is not measured. - Without this PR, #55449's corrected width makes GLM-5.3-Flash with MTP off need a fourth KDA group. - Related: RFC #58638 question 2 asks how to size blocks for block-outermost layouts; this keeps the alignment's block and changes only how Mamba states fill it. #56156 skips the alignment for opt-in layer-wise KV caches. #58380 and #60996 also restructure `_get_packed_kv_cache_groups` (textual conflicts); the bytes-per-request check uses the layout passed in, so it also works in #58380's planner. #60996 keeps the Mamba padding. title: [Bugfix] Warn when VLLM_PLUGINS names match no installed plugin
body:
## Overview

`VLLM_PLUGINS` matches plugin names against the entry point registry by exact string, so a name that matches nothing is dropped silently — no error, no warning, exit code 0. `docs/design/lora_resolver_plugins.md:13` names the built-in HF Hub resolver `hf_hub_resolver`, but `pyproject.toml:47` registers it as `lora_hf_hub_resolver`. Following the doc loads nothing: the resolver is never registered, and requests fail later with "adapter not found".

Fixing the doc alone is not enough. The wrong name has shipped in released docs (e.g. v0.25.0) and in configs the project does not control; and the existing guard in `hf_hub_resolver.py` cannot cover this case, because it is the entry point target and only runs once the plugin is loaded — which already requires the name to match.

This warns once per process when a `VLLM_PLUGINS` name matches no installed plugin, and lists the available names.

## Claims

- An unknown `VLLM_PLUGINS` name now emits a warning listing the available plugin names, instead of being ignored with no diagnostics.
- `docs/design/lora_resolver_plugins.md:13` now uses `lora_hf_hub_resolver`.
- No model output, accuracy, or serving behaviour changes, so no model evaluation is included.

## Validation

`load_general_plugins()` returns `None`, so the reproducer observes the log rather than a return value.

    # before (main) / after (this branch): the typo is silent on main, warned here
    VLLM_PLUGINS=hf_hub_resolver python -c "from vllm.plugins import load_general_plugins; load_general_plugins()"
    main:  (no output — a typo is indistinguishable from a correct name)
    here:  VLLM_PLUGINS contains ['hf_hub_resolver'], which match no installed plugin. These entries will be ignored. Available plugins: ['lora_filesystem_resolver', 'lora_hf_hub_resolver']

    # a valid name must not warn (guards the cross-group union against false positives)
    VLLM_PLUGINS=lora_hf_hub_resolver python -c "from vllm.plugins import load_general_plugins; load_general_plugins()"
    (no output)

    # with the documented name the resolver is never registered
    VLLM_LORA_RESOLVER_HF_REPO_LIST=foo/bar VLLM_PLUGINS=hf_hub_resolver python - <<'EOF'
    from vllm.plugins import load_general_plugins
    from vllm.lora.resolver import LoRAResolverRegistry
    load_general_plugins()
    print(sorted(LoRAResolverRegistry.get_supported_resolvers()))
    EOF
    []

    # real server, single GPU (vLLM 0.31.1rc1.dev245+gbe0823357): warning once per process at startup, before the model loads
    VLLM_PLUGINS=hf_hub_resolver vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --enable-lora --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8
    (EngineCore pid=6295) WARNING ... [__init__.py:104] VLLM_PLUGINS contains ['hf_hub_resolver'], which match no installed plugin. These entries will be ignored. Available plugins: ['lora_filesystem_resolver', 'lora_hf_hub_resolver']

Lint: `pre-commit run --files vllm/plugins/__init__.py docs/design/lora_resolver_plugins.md` — all hooks passed.

## Details

Root cause: `vllm/envs.py` parses `VLLM_PLUGINS` with `.split(",")`, and `load_plugins_by_group` tests `plugin.name in allowed_plugins` — exact membership; an unmatched name is dropped with no signal.

`VLLM_PLUGINS` is one global allowlist shared by all five plugin groups, so "unknown" is judged against the union of every group's entry points; a per-group check would false-positive on another group's names. The check lives in `load_general_plugins` rather than `load_plugins_by_group` because it does not use the `group` argument and can reuse the existing once-per-process `plugins_loaded` guard.

`PLUGIN_GROUPS` is a module-level tuple of every group whose entry points are filtered by `VLLM_PLUGINS`, kept next to the group constants so that a new group is added in one place rather than in a list inside `load_general_plugins`. It still has to be extended by hand when a group is added; `load_plugins_by_group` is the only consumer of `VLLM_PLUGINS` (`load_endpoint_plugins` goes through it), so this tuple is the definition of the filtered set and the module level is the right home for it.

It is informational, not a failure: it names both the unmatched entries and the available names, so an intentional absence (e.g. one `VLLM_PLUGINS` shared across heterogeneous containers) is recognisable rather than alarming. It only fires when `VLLM_PLUGINS` is set and lists a name not installed anywhere in this environment; unset, or `VLLM_PLUGINS=""` (which parses to `[""]` and is excluded), stays silent.

The available names are already logged, but only at `DEBUG` for this group, and that log never says a `VLLM_PLUGINS` entry matched nothing — searching it for the typo'd name even hits the module path, which reads as "it's there".

No new test is added: per `pr-checklist` §2 a bugfix is validated on a reproducer, and §2.1 discourages unnecessary tests.

**Duplicate check**: searched `gh pr list` / `gh issue list` for `"hf_hub_resolver"`, `"lora resolver docs"`, `"VLLM_PLUGINS plugin name"` and `"lora_resolver_plugins"` — nothing addresses unmatched `VLLM_PLUGINS` names. #54428 ("Don't fail the request when a LoRA resolver raises") is runtime error handling in `serving.py` / `filesystem_resolver.py`, no file overlap.

**AI assistance**: drafted with AI assistance (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash); the human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the commands above.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

title: [RFC]: Scheduler-owned KV transfer obligations: release blocks only after both recv and send complete
body:
### Motivation.

`Scheduler._update_from_kv_xfer_finished` asserts `req_id in self.requests` for every `finished_recving` and `finished_sending` id ([L3234](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c41b2639e29c3bc01add1d34bef3032a6d9d8aca/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L3234), [L3244](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c41b2639e29c3bc01add1d34bef3032a6d9d8aca/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L3244)). When it fires, EngineCore dies and every in-flight request on the replica fails. Recovery took about 2 min on Qwen3-8B and about 20 min on DeepSeek-V4-Flash for us.

The same assertion is reported for at least four connectors:
- LMCache: #43226, #57938
- Nixl: #46240
- Mooncake: #60755, and a comment on #43226
- MultiConnector: #53049

#49089 reports it for late reports on already-failed requests. Each report is fixed, or proposed to be fixed, inside one connector.

We think the scheduler is part of the cause. It records "this request still has a transfer outstanding" as **one boolean**, not per transfer. Whichever completion arrives first releases the blocks and deletes the request:
1. `finish_requests` sets `delay_free_blocks` when the request is in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` with its recv incomplete ([L2702](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c41b2639e29c3bc01add1d34bef3032a6d9d8aca/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L2702)).
2. `_free_request` ORs in the connector's `request_finished` result ([L2739](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c41b2639e29c3bc01add1d34bef3032a6d9d8aca/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L2739)).
3. Later, *either* loop calls `_free_blocks` for a finished request: the recv loop at ~L3241, or the send loop at ~L3245. That returns the blocks to the pool and `del self.requests[...]` ([L2748](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c41b2639e29c3bc01add1d34bef3032a6d9d8aca/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L2748)).

So a request aborted while it has both a recv in flight and a connector-declared send has its blocks released when the *first* direction reports. The second report then hits the assertion.

The `request_finished` docstring says that returning True means blocks "should not be freed until the request_id is returned from get_finished()". The recv-completion path does not honour that when a recv is also outstanding.

**The assertion fires after the hazardous event, not at it.** In the ordering *send reported, then recv reported*:
1. The blocks are released at the send report while the recv is still DMA-ing into them.
2. They can be reallocated to another request.
3. Only the later recv report trips the assertion.

In the reverse ordering, a real store can read blocks that have already been reused, and write another request's KV under the old prefix. So simply restoring a log-and-continue guard would trade a crash for silent corruption. #25067 removed exactly that guard (`"Got finished sending KV transfer ... but the request is already freed"`) because it masked a real lifetime race.

**Our reproduction** used vLLM 0.30.0 and LMCache v0.5.6rc1 (`LMCacheMPConnector`, `kv_both`). Clients disconnected while their KV was loading back from LMCache. We saw both assertion lines.

| Model | Workload | Crashes |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B, TP1 | 32 sessions × 24k tokens; flood to evict them; resume all; cancel after 100–300 ms | 6 in 12 iterations |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP8 | 256 multi-turn conversations, then SIGKILL the client | 3 in 4 rounds |

The LMCache-side cause, a store completion synthesized for an aborted load, is fixed by LMCache/LMCache#4939. With it applied we saw 0 crashes in 24 and 0 in 6 rounds respectively. That fixes one connector. The scheduler would still release blocks on the first of two completions for any connector that declares both.

### Proposed Change.

Make the scheduler the owner of each request's outstanding-transfer obligations. Release blocks only when all of them have completed.

1. **Ledger.** Keep `pending_xfers: dict[req_id, set[Direction]]`, with `Direction` being `RECV` or `SEND`. Generalising to operation ids for multi-transfer connectors is possible later.
   - Add `RECV` when a request enters `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`, removing it on `finished_recving` or `failed_recving`.
   - Add `SEND` when `request_finished[_all_groups]` returns True.
   - `finish_requests` reads the ledger instead of the recv-only `finished_recving_kv_req_ids` check.
2. **Single release point.** `_free_blocks` runs only when the request is finished and its ledger entry is empty. Both loops of `_update_from_kv_xfer_finished` just retire their direction, then call that release point.
3. **Unknown or duplicate reports.**
   - Once (1) and (2) hold, a report for an id that has no pending direction can no longer mean the blocks were released early. It is a duplicate or a connector bug. The scheduler drops it with a `warning` log and a counter metric, labelled by connector and direction, instead of asserting.
   - A report for a direction that was never registered is logged as a connector contract violation.
   - Either can stay an assertion under a debug or strict flag, so CI keeps catching connector bugs.
4. **Contract.** Document in `KVConnectorBase_V1` that recv and send obligations are independent, and that the scheduler releases blocks after both.

What this does not protect against:
- a connector reporting a transfer complete while its device copy is still running;
- transfers the scheduler was never told about;
- a connector that never reports, which needs the existing per-connector timeouts.

Those stay connector responsibilities.

Precedents: MultiConnector already counts `_extra_async_saves` per request across children, and the MoRIIO connector rewrites `finished_sending` in `update_connector_output` to keep this assertion from firing. Both are connector-local versions of the same accounting.

We are happy to write the PR, with unit tests covering each completion ordering and the duplicate and unknown cases, if maintainers agree with the direction.

### Feedback Period.

Two weeks.

### CC List.

@njhill, who on #49278 asked for this to be fixed in the connector rather than the scheduler. This proposal keeps the connector fixes and adds scheduler-side accounting so that a connector bug cannot release blocks early. Also @markmc (#25067) and @NickLucche.

### Any Other Things.

Related: #43226, #46240, #49089, #53049, #57938, #60755, #25067, LMCache/LMCache#4938, LMCache/LMCache#4939.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Include draft models in DeepGEMM warmup
body:
## Overview

DeepGEMM startup warmup now includes the draft model, covering eligible draft-only layer shapes before speculative serving starts.

Related: #60929

## Claims

- An available draft model uses the same warmup token limit as the target model.
- Absent drafts, unsupported DeepGEMM platforms and `VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip` retain their existing behavior.
- No latency, memory, model-quality or original-workload OOM improvement is claimed.

## Validation

After syncing main `0838cd6593ba` and resolving the append conflict at `e70e48087062`, the two warmup suites passed: **28 passed**, with 14 existing TorchScript deprecation warnings. All applicable pre-commit and commit hooks passed. The draft regressions and upstream MegaMoE tests are both retained. Before the original fix, the six new dispatch cases gave **1 failed, 5 passed**, exposing the omitted draft call.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py
```

Historical GPU validation (2026-10-10, `986a550`): RTX 5060 Laptop 8 GB (SM120), Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, nvcc/CRT/NVVM 13.0.88. That run used native artifacts from the official wheel for base `c41b2639e` and a production warmup file byte-verified against `986a550`. The GPU results below apply to that snapshot; GPU/native serving validation was not rerun on the merged head.

| Historical cold-cache CUDA probe | Base c41b2639e | Original fix 986a550 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full warmup, max tokens 64, target weight `(512,1024)`, draft `(768,1024)` | Only target shape warmed | Both shapes warmed |
| Subsequent eager draft at M=32 | Added one JIT kernel entry (4 files) | Added no JIT files |
| Target and draft M=1,7,32,57,64 | Numerical checks passed | All 10 numerical checks passed; no new JIT files |

The probe used synthetic registered FP8 layers and a worker stub, but the dispatcher, DeepGEMM warmup and CUDA GEMMs were real. Unrelated warmup hooks and the progress-bar rank query were stubbed. Cosine-style difference against FP32 GEMM on the same quantized inputs was at most `1.49e-6` (threshold `1e-3`); repeating the patched warmup added no cache files.

Full GPU generation also passed with one-layer synthetic FP8 Llama safetensors checkpoints: target hidden size 512, independent draft 384, vocabulary 128, TP=1, MRV2, eager mode, TRITON_ATTN, `linear_backend="deep_gemm"`, full warmup/max batched tokens 64, and three speculative tokens. Both actual models selected `DeepGemmFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` and completed startup warmup. Two token-ID prompts (lengths 4 and 23) generated 16 tokens each with greedy sampling; standard and speculative outputs matched. The speculative run accepted **24/24 drafted tokens**.

These checkpoints have random FP8 decoder weights and a zero LM head to make acceptance deterministic. This checks actual loading, backend selection, draft warmup and speculative generation, **not model quality or realistic acceptance**. The original DeepSeek-V4-Pro + DSpark / 2x GB300 / TP2+EP2 / memory-utilization 0.99 OOM scenario was not reproduced; only the local GPU was authorized. Someone with that environment is requested to verify the original workload. This PR addresses the general omitted draft warmup, with no claim that the original deployment's OOM is fully resolved.

On the merged head, hosted pre-commit still fails the author/label eligibility check before tests execute. GPU Buildkite CI has a separate trusted-reviewer authorization rule. Local results do not satisfy or bypass either policy. Human line review and confirmation of validation remain pending.

<details>
<summary>CUDA regression probe used for the cold-cache comparison</summary>

Run this probe in separate processes against the base and patched production warmup file, using the matching GPU environment described above and a fresh empty cache each time. `baseline` expects the missing draft warmup; `patched` expects both shapes warmed and no new serving-time JIT files. The executable portion below was run; only result-metadata serialization and blank lines are omitted. This is a validation artifact rather than an added CI test.

```bash
export VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=full
export VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER_PCIE_IPC=0
export DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
export JIT_CACHE_DIR="$DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR"
# CUDA_HOME/PATH must select the matching 13.0 compiler, CRT and NVVM.
.venv/bin/python gpu_dispatch_validation.py patched patched.json
# In a separate base environment/process with another empty cache:
```

The startup dispatcher previously passed only `worker.get_model()` to DeepGEMM warmup. It now uses the existing `Worker.get_draft_model()` API, which returns `None` when no draft model is available and supports both model runners. title: [KV Cache] Size packed groups by pooled bytes per request, not layer padding
body:
## Overview

`_get_packed_kv_cache_groups` sizes every block in the shared pool by the widest
group, but picks the group split with a heuristic that never looks at that cost:
`_approximate_gcd` minimizes the *layer-count* padding and prefers the larger
value on ties. Replace it with a search over the bytes a max-length request
draws from the shared pool. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at 1M context this takes the
KV pool from 1.88x to 3.16x concurrency with the pool size unchanged; a second
commit batches the sliding-window metadata build so the higher group count does
not add host time per step.

Related: #58207, #60967, #58380, #58818, #60426.

### Why this is not a duplicate

The four open PRs above cover adjacent ground, so I tested whether they subsume
this. Cherry-picking all of them onto the same branch and booting the model
leaves the allocation **exactly at the unfixed 1.88x**:

| applied | cached tokens | 1M concurrency | groups |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| #60967 + #58818 + #58207 | 1,971,956 | 1.88x | 18 |
| #60967 + #58818 + #58380 | 1,971,956 | 1.88x | 18 |
| **this PR** | **3,315,539** | **3.16x** | **50** |

- **#60967** gates its only behavioural lever on `MambaSpec`
  (`if widen and isinstance(spec.first_spec, MambaSpec)`), and then only takes
  the widened split if it also *reduces the group count*
  (`len(widened) < len(groups)`). DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has no `MambaSpec` at all
  (its caches are `CircularBufferSpec` and `MLASpec`), so the two builds are
  identical and the `bytes_per_request` comparison is never reached — a no-op
  for this model by construction.
- **#58207** rewrites the *uniform-page-size* path
  (`_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size`); a mixed-page-size model resolving
  to a block-outermost layout never reaches it.
- **#58380** chooses between block-outermost and layer-outermost layouts; the
  layout and the split here are unchanged by it.
- **#58818** / **#60426** share metadata *builds* across groups (host launch
  count); they cannot change block accounting.

None of them touches `_approximate_gcd`, which is the actual source of the
over-reservation. This is the "materially different approach" case from
`AGENTS.md`, not a competing implementation.

## Claims

- Packed allocation stops over-reserving: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's widest block
  goes 138,240 → 46,080 bytes and the split 18 → 50 groups, so at an unchanged
  6.32 GiB pool the cached tokens go 1,971,956 → 3,315,539 and 1M-context
  concurrency 1.88x → **3.16x**.
- The core change is a net simplification: `_approximate_gcd` is deleted
  (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` is net −7 lines).
- End-to-end serving is unchanged at the requested test points, and the higher
  group count does not cost per-step host time (second commit).

## Validation

**Environment** (the only configuration available to me): 4x RTX PRO 6000
Blackwell (sm120), TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, `--max-model-len 1048576`,
DSpark N=5, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, block-outermost (BLHNC) layout, cards under
a **fixed 350 W** power limit, `COOL_TEMP`-gated probes, and the thermal
controller checked for throttle events (0 during the window; max 65 °C).

Capacity, from the startup log (three boots of the patched build, identical
every time):

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `GPU KV cache size` | 1,971,956 | **3,315,539** |
| 1M-request concurrency | 1.88x | **3.16x** |
| `kv cache group sizes` | 18 groups | **50 groups** |
| KV cache memory (`gpu_worker.py`) | 6.32 GiB | **6.32 GiB** |
| bytes per 1M-token request | 3.417 GiB | **2.000 GiB** |

Performance, same-power A/B (2 arms x 2 boots, same probe order, decode window =
first 512 tokens, prefill = 128K anchor with `prefix_cache_hits == 0` asserted):

| probe | before | after (run 1 / run 2) | after's own spread |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| decode c=1 | 365.2 tok/s | 374.7 / 364.8 | 2.7% |
| decode c=4 | 771.1 | 774.6 / 765.7 | 1.2% |
| decode c=8 | 1329.2 | 1359.0 / 1274.1 | 6.7% |
| 128K prefill | 17,742 tok/s | 17,755 / 17,687 | 0.4% |

The cross-arm differences (<= 4%) are smaller than the patched arm's own
run-to-run spread (up to 6.7%), i.e. not separable from measurement noise.

Correctness, over 4 runs (both arms, each repeated), covering prefix-cache
read-back, a 6-request batch with prompts from 165 to 44,769 tokens
(asymmetric prefill + mixed batch), a 114,492-token needle, and c=8:

- the needle is retrieved in **all 4 runs**;
- final answers agree in every pairing for the short / reuse / long / mixed
  cases;
- the only disagreements are in think-block length at c=8, and they appear
  **identically when an arm is compared against its own repeat**, so they are
  engine nondeterminism (speculative-draft draw), not a behaviour change.

Commands:

```bash
# capacity
journalctl -u vllm-ds41 | grep -E "GPU KV cache size|kv cache group sizes"

# unit
python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py -q   # 28 passed
```

**CI coverage:** this needs 4x RTX PRO 6000 (sm120) and a 1M-context
checkpoint, so it cannot run in CI. The added/updated test is CPU-only
(`tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py`, 28 passed) and the numbers above
are from the real deployment.

## Details

### Root cause

For a balanced bucket (one layer per page size per repeat) the allocator splits
the repeats across groups, and every group draws the same number of blocks from
one shared pool. What a max-length request costs is therefore
`(blocks it needs) x (bytes of the widest group's block)`, and
`widest_group_bytes = sum(cdiv(len(names), n) * page)` grows as the group count
`n` falls, because each group then carries more layers.

The old heuristic picked `n` by minimizing
`sum((d - x % d) % d)` over the layer counts, tie-breaking toward the **larger**
`d`. Fewer, wider groups score better on that objective while making the block —
the quantity every block in the pool is sized for — larger. It optimizes a cost
the allocator does not pay.

### What changed

- The split is chosen by searching the repeats per group and taking the one that
  minimizes the bytes a max-length request draws from the pool, with the plan
  consumed by the existing emit loop.
- A state bucket (Mamba / circular buffer / unsplit sliding window) is capped at
  the states a block already fits instead of being allowed to widen the block.
- `_approximate_gcd` is removed.
- `SWAWindowMetadata` computes the sliding-window window rows for all groups in
  one batched kernel per step; each group's
  `DeepseekV41SparseSWAMetadataBuilder` returns its own view of the shared rows
  instead of launching its own kernels. Batches the shared rows do not describe
  (the non-causal DSpark draft, image spans, a missing state) fall back to the
  per-group build, which is also what runs when the state is absent.

### Tradeoffs and limitations

- **More groups cost per-group attention-metadata work.** That is why the
  second commit is here; without it the higher group count would spend the
  capacity win on the host side. Models whose metadata is already cheap, or
  those that prefer fewer groups, may want the opposite trade — that is the
  lever #58207's `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` exposes, which this change does
  not add.
- **Group counts are model-specific**; the 18 -> 50 figure is DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
- **Residual padding remains.** 2.00 GiB per 1M-token request against the
  ~1.87 GB nominal fp8 figure; the leftover is page padding inside one shared
  pool (the 8-token state group and the 128-token ratio-2 groups). Two pools
  would recover more and are deliberately out of scope here.
- **Textual conflict:** this touches the same region as #60967's `build_groups`
  refactor and #58380's planner, so it will need a rebase whichever lands first.
  Happy to rebase onto either.
- Validated on sm120 only; the allocation change is platform-independent, but I
  have not measured other architectures.

---

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR (DeepSeek Harness / deepseek-flash wrote the change; the submitter reviewed every changed line, ran the validations above, and can defend the change).

- [x] **Design Fit:** The core fix replaces an existing heuristic inside
  `_get_packed_kv_cache_groups` and deletes the now-unused helper rather than
  adding an abstraction next to it; the model-specific metadata batching is
  confined to `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/`.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validated end-to-end on the real deployment
  (capacity, same-power perf A/B, correctness), with the CI resource constraint
  documented above. `tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py` updated for the
  new split and passing; the existing `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`
  covers the uniform path and is unaffected.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** `ruff check` and `ruff format` clean on all

title: [ROCm] MonoSpec + abstractions
body:
# WIP, will be closed

## Overview

This is a first draft of a suggestion on the design of the monokernel abstraction layer. Feedback is encouraged and appreciated!

### Validation

Three types of validation needed to run a monokernel:
1. **Before model load**: check vllm_config and platform. _If no -> crash_
2. **After model load**: 
    1. **Model-wide check**: Ensure model is aligned with the monokernel. Example: requires mxfp4 moe backend. _If no -> crash_ 
    2. **Layer-wise check**: Ensure the layer is aligned with the monokernel. E.g. require layer not to be an MTP layer, i.e. `attn.layer_id <= num_hidden_layers`. _If no -> fallback_.
3. **At runtime** (every invocation): (1) once for all ranks: check row count, attn metadata (2) per rank: health check, poll, vote. If no -> fallback to vllm impl

Hence two types of methods:
- `refuse_*`. crash if not supported. Example: `refuse_config(vllm_config)`
- `skip_*`: fall back to native vllm impl if not supported. Example: `skip_layer(layer)`

### Abstractions 

Four abstractions:
1. `MonoOp`: key entrypoint of a _logical_ monokernel. This is the glue between model code and the flydsl monokernel. It can be used in place of an entire layer, or parts of a layer. Under the hood it can be a single launch or multiple (k1/k2), but from the outside it's considered a single fused operation.
    1. **Note:** here we deviate from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60904, which proposed two modes: "full layer" and "ffn" mode. We make this more general because PR's like https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60683 wants both full-layer mode, ffn-mode, and k2-mode (i.e. o-proj --...--> MoE AR)
    2. To implement this, we use a sort of reverse injection to offload the decision of what layers should use "full mode" and "ffn mode" etc. We do this as follows: 
        1. The model (like `DeepseekV4Model`) creates a MonoOp in its constructor, and passes in its layers
        2. The MonoOp is responsible for determining what monokernel to use for layer `i`, and binds `self.layers[i].mono = selected_monokernel`
        3. The actual layer does: `if self.mono is not None: self.mono.forward(...)`, unaware of what it actually being called as a monoop. The MonoOp is the one deciding if it's "eager+mono_ffn" or "full layer",
4. `MonoSpec`: declaration of when the MonoOp can run
5. `MonoKernel`: the flydsl launcher
6. `MonoRuntime`: shared utilities, e.g. for managing scratch space


### Adding a new monokernel

A new monokernel writer needs to write three things

1. A `MonoSpec` literal declaring supported features and constraints.
4. A `MonoKernel` implementation: the FlyDSL kernel and its launch.
5. A `MonoOp` subclass: the glue between vLLM model and the flydsl monokernel. This includes code for determining whether to run the monokernel for the given problem shape, and converting model weights into the format expected by flydsl. 

### Deviations from RFC

1. We make MonoSpec arch specific. E.g. gfx942 and 950 might have different max_rows and support different features. Implemented wiht `MonoOp.variant(vllm_config) -> Self`.
2. We don't enforce "whole layer mode" and "ffn mode" only. You can instead run a monokernel for arbitrary parts of a layer using MonoOp: `self.mono.ffn_only[layer_id].forward()` or `self.mono.window[layer_id].forward()`.  
3. 

#### Example 1.

DeepSeek-V4.1 pseudo-code. See PR for full details

```
# vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py

class DeepseekV4Model(nn.Module, EagleModelMixin):
    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config: VllmConfig, prefix: str = ""):
        # `create` validates the config and builds the monokernel per layer, and assigns it as `self.layers[i].mono`.
        self.mono = DSV41MonoDecode.create(
            vllm_config, layers=islice(self.layers, self.start_layer, self.end_layer)
        )

```
```python
# vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/mono_decode.py

DSV41_MONO = MonoSpec(
    name="DSv4.1 mono decode",
    supports=frozenset({Feature.SPECULATIVE_DECODE}),
    tp_sizes=(2, 4),
    device_archs=("gfx950",),  # the kernels' ISA: scaled MFMA and MX formats
    widths=tuple(range(1, MAX_ROWS + 1)),
    kernel_module="vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.runner",
    resident_blocks="BLOCKS",
    constraints=(_needs_a8w4_moe,),
    opt_in=lambda c: bool(envs.VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE),
    on_refusal="raise",  # the opt-in was explicit: say why it cannot be served
)

class DSV41MonoDecode(MonoOp):
    spec = DSV41_MONO

    def __init__(self, vllm_config, layer: "DeepseekV4DecoderLayer") -> None:
        self.layer = layer

        self.vllm_config = vllm_config
        super().__init__(vllm_config)
        self._weights: MonoLayerWeights | None = None
        self._kernels: DSV41MonoLayer | None = None

    def refuse_model(self) -> list[str]:
        backend = getattr(experts.quant_method, "mxfp4_backend", None)
        if backend != Mxfp4MoeBackend.AITER_MXFP4_BF16:
            return [f"needs the AITER_MXFP4_BF16 MoE backend, not {backend}"]
        return []

    def skip_layer(self, layer: "DeepseekV4DecoderLayer") -> str:
        attn, ffn = layer.attn, layer.ffn
        if attn.layer_id >= hf.num_hidden_layers:
            return "draft layer"
        return ""

    def build(self) -> None:
        """Attach self to each layer. Here we make the decision on how to run the layer being substituted for the monokernel. 

       Example:
           - "ffn only" layers: record which layer this is, and disable reduction on the out projection
           - "whole layers": set the `mono` attribute on the layer
           - ... other layers can be treated differently if needed
"""
        self.rt = MonoRuntime(
            DSV41_MONO,
            self.vllm_config,
            peer_factory=peer_factory,
            epoch_words=EPOCH_WORDS,
        )
        for layer in self.mono_layers(self.layers):
            why_ffn_only = "Engram" if layer.engram is not None else None
            self.ffn_only[layer.attn.layer_id] = bool(why_ffn_only )
            layer.mono = self
            if why_ffn_only :
                layer.attn.wo_b.reduce_results = False
        if not self.ffn_only:
            self.skips.append("no layer with the kernels' seams and MoE")

    @property
    def kernels(self):
        if self._kernels is None:
            from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.runner import DSV41MonoLayer

            self._kernels = DSV41MonoLayer(self.rt)
        return self._kernels

    @property
    def weights(self):
        from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.runner import MonoLayerWeights

        layer = self.layer
        a, f = layer.attn, layer.ffn
        e, sh = f.experts.routed_experts, f.shared_experts
        self._weights = MonoLayerWeights(
            attn=None if self.ffn_only else self._attn_weights(a),
            hc_attn_fn=layer.hc_attn_fn)

    def skip_step(self, rows: int, tensors, whole_layer: bool) -> str:
        if not is_forward_context_available():
            return "no forward context"
        fc = get_forward_context()
        if not self.spec.graph_mode_ok(fc.cudagraph_runtime_mode):
            return f"{fc.cudagraph_runtime_mode} step"

    def forward(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        positions: torch.Tensor,
        residual: torch.Tensor | None,
    ):
        if residual is None or x.dim() != 2:
            return self._skip("first layer")
        tensors = (x, residual, post_mix, res_mix, pre_mix)
        step = self.step(x.shape[0], tensors, whole_layer=True)
        if not step:
            return self._skip(step.reason)
        attn = self.layer.attn
        logger.info_once(
            "DSv4.1 mono decode layer active (decode steps of <= %d rows)", MAX_ROWS
        )
        return self.kernels.forward(
            self.weights,
            x,
            residual,
            post_mix,
            ),
            comp_block_table=comp.block_table,
        )
```
 
### Example 2: adding a new arch

Create a new spec, and potentially implement it's own additional refusals
```python
# vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/mono_decode.py

DSV41_MONO_950 = MonoSpec(
    name="DSv4.1 mono decode (gfx950)",
    device_archs=("gfx950",),
    widths=tuple(range(1, 48 + 1)),
    kernel_module="vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.runner",
    constraints=(_needs_a8w4_moe,),
    ...
)

DSV41_MONO_942 = replace(
    DSV41_MONO_950,
    name="DSv4.1 mono decode (gfx942)",
    device_archs=("gfx942",),
    widths=tuple(range(1, 42 + 1)),
    kernel_module="vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.runner_942",
    constraints=(_flydsl_target_matches_gpu,),  # the A8W4 MoE rule does not apply
)


class DSV41MonoDecode(MonoOp):
    """The model: the seams and MoE routing these kernels need, either ISA."""

    @classmethod
    def variant(cls, vllm_config):
        return DSV41MonoDecodeGfx942 if on_gfx942() else DSV41MonoDecodeGfx950

    def skip_layer(self, layer):
        ...  # fuse_seam_norm, draft layers, 384 / 6 / sqrtsoftplus / x1.5


class DSV41MonoDecodeGfx950(DSV41MonoDecode):
    spec = DSV41_MONO_950

    def refuse_model(self):
        """These kernels read the experts in AITER's A8W4 MXFP4 layout."""
        ...

class DSV41MonoDecodeGfx942(DSV41MonoDecode):
    spec = DSV41_MONO_942

    def __init__(self, vllm_config, layers):
        super().__init__(vllm_config, layers)
        self._copy_weights_at_load()  # pre-load: the copies size the KV cache

    def skip_layer(self, layer):
        if why := super().skip_layer(layer):
            return why
        if get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size() != 4:
            return "gfx942 builds for tensor parallel size 4 only"
        return ""
```

No further changes needed on the model side.

title: [Bugfix][V1] Retain the EAGLE hit blocks below a sliding window across a KV connector import
body:
## Purpose

Related: #57610 / #57613 (same all-or-nothing miss from a different trigger), RFC #54661.

With the hybrid KV cache manager, an EAGLE-family drafter whose layers use sliding-window attention (DFlash, window 2048, block 64) and prefix caching, a prefix-cache hit on the draft group needs `cdiv(window - 1, block) + 1 = 33` contiguous cached blocks (`SlidingWindowManager._contiguous_blocks_for_hit`): one more than the window spans, because EAGLE matches one block past the boundary and drops it. The hybrid lookup reconciles to the shortest group, so a 0 draft hit zeroes the target's hit too.

On a decode engine in P/D disaggregation that run never exists. A KV connector import allocates only the blocks inside the window (`get_num_skipped_tokens(P) = P - window + 1 - extra_retained_tokens`), NIXL ships only those, and `cache_blocks` after the load hashes only those: 32 blocks. Every later request whose prompt is longer than the window misses on all layers; the fallback only accepts a run reaching block 0. Prefill engines are unaffected, because local compute hashes the block before `remove_skipped_blocks` nulls it, which is why this only shows on the decode side.

Fix: for an EAGLE group (annotated, or every group when none is, mirroring the coordinator), widen `SlidingWindowSpec.extra_retained_tokens` by `(cdiv(window - 1, block) + 1) * block - (window - 1)` (65 tokens here), so `get_num_skipped_tokens` lands exactly that many whole blocks below the last full-block boundary for every prompt length. This includes groups packed as `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` by block-outermost layouts (e.g. BLHNC); the scheduler unwraps those to their first spec. The block below the window then stays allocated on the prefill until `request_finished`, is shipped by NIXL (`blocks_per_sw` now includes the retained tokens), is allocated by the decoder's import and is hashed after the load. The same spec field drives admission and pool sizing, so they stay consistent (+1 block per request on that group). `+block_size` alone was considered and rejected: it still misses prompts with `P % block == block - 1`.

Non-EAGLE sliding-window groups (gpt-oss and Gemma without spec decode, and DeepSeek-V4.1's bounded-replay groups, which are not prefix-cacheable) are unchanged: the helper is gated on `use_eagle_block_drop()`, the EAGLE annotation and `prefix_cacheable`, and `blocks_per_sw` adds a field that is 0 for them.

Out of scope, noted for reviewers: under `prefix_cache_retention_interval=0` only the previous prompt's tail is hashed, so hits are capped at that prompt's boundary; non-EAGLE sliding-window groups have a pre-existing miss at `P % block in {0, block - 1}`; Mooncake P2P and MoRIIO compute their own transfer tails and are untouched.

Not a duplicate: #57613 widens the local retention mask for the prefill-computed path and cannot help here, because the missing block is never allocated on the decode side. #60767 nulls stale block-table entries in the worker and is consistent with this change. No open PR touches `extra_retained_tokens` for EAGLE groups or NIXL's sliding-window transfer tail.

## Test Plan

- `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py::test_eagle_swa_resend_hits_after_connector_import[packed x prompt length]`: hybrid full-attention + sliding-window manager, `use_eagle`, `retention_interval=0`, groups built through `get_kv_cache_groups` with and without a block-outermost layout; connector import of a prompt longer than the window, `cache_blocks`, free, resend; asserts a hit of `(P // block - 1) * block`. Prompt 175 covers the `block - 1` residue.
- `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py::test_eagle_sliding_window_group_retains_hit_blocks_below_window`: the spec is widened only for EAGLE groups. (The helper and its call site moved from `kv_cache_utils.py` to `kv_cache_planning.py` with #61183.)
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py::test_sw_sizes`: `blocks_per_sw` includes `extra_retained_tokens`.
- End to end on 2x B300: GLM-5.3 NVFP4 + DFlash2 drafter, P/D with 2x DEP4 prefill and 2x TP4 decode over NIXL, Mooncake store, `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC`, `--block-size 64`, decode prefix caching on. Identical-resend probes to one decode engine, then AgentX multi-turn traffic, 30 min per concurrency.

## Test Result

- Unit tests (B300): the tests above pass. The packed cases fail on the first version of this change (hit 0), which is how the BLHNC gap was found.
- Rebased 2026-10-13 onto `main` `791f92135a` (only the #61183 file move; the retention logic on `main` is unchanged): on B300 (2026-10-14): 344 passed; the one failure, `test_nixl_connector_hma.py::test_fewer_blocks_with_hma[google/gemma-3-1b-it-512]`, is a gated Hugging Face repo without a token in that environment and fails identically on clean `main` `791f92135a`.
- Lint: ruff check / format and mypy pass.
- Decode-side resend probes (hit tokens on the second request):

| prompt tokens | before | after |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,543 (below the window) | 1,472 | 1,472 |
| 2,194 | 0 | 2,112 |
| 3,062 | 0 | 2,944 |
| 30,359 (identical resend) | 0 | 30,272 |

- AgentX at 32 concurrent sessions: decode prefix-cache hits 46K -> 127K tokens, NIXL transfer p90 179 -> 38 ms; draft acceptance unchanged (39-40%).
- AgentX at 64 / 72 concurrent sessions, this change vs the same deployment with block 1024 (where the draft is allocated as full attention and the bug cannot occur): TTFT p50 1,252 vs 1,685 ms and 1,821 vs 8,165 ms; E2E tok/s per user p50 65.9 vs 63.0 and 57.7 vs 37.1.

AI assistance: this change was developed with Claude (Anthropic) under human direction; every changed line was reviewed by the submitter, who ran the tests and measurements above.

title: [Model] Qwen4Exp: support batch-sharded sampling (compute_logits_local)
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Let Qwen4Exp take the batch-sharded sampling path (#50465). `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration` inherits `compute_logits_local` from `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, which calls `language_model.compute_logits_local`, but `Qwen4ExpForCausalLM` does not define it. This PR adds the method on the NVIDIA and AMD `Qwen4ExpForCausalLM`, the same 3-line pattern as Qwen3.5 and MiniMax M3.

**Draft:** the end-to-end serving validation below is still running. I will mark the PR ready only after it is filled in.

The first serving run reached "Batch-sharded sampling enabled." on all 8 ranks. It then failed in warm-up, with NCCL out of memory at the first all-to-all. That failure is not specific to Qwen4Exp: the profile run never executes the sharded all-to-all. The fix is #61025, and the serving retry runs with both PRs.

**Retry with #61025 (measured):** start-up passes. All 8 ranks log "Batch-sharded sampling enabled.", warm-up is clean, and the server answers requests. The NCCL all-to-all buffers now take about 2.9 GiB per GPU (non-torch memory 17.75 → 20.62 GiB), so the KV cache falls from 2,128,699 to 1,742,619 tokens (−18 %) on 40 GB A100s. That is a real trade-off for capacity-bound serving; the 3 × 60 min result will show whether the sampling saving outweighs it.

**Serving result (measured, MLPerf agentic full set, 20 concurrent sessions, 3 × 60 min per arm, same node type, strict per-request SLO TTFT ≤ 2.93 s and TPOT ≤ 21.74 ms):**

| Arm | Joint SLO pass r1/r2/r3 | Goodput (req/s) | TTFT p50 / p95 (s) | TPOT p50 / p95 (ms) | Accuracy score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Flag off | 90.0 / 89.2 / 89.5 % | 1.83–1.89 | 0.93–0.98 / 2.22–2.35 | 14.1–14.3 / 23.9–24.5 | 0.540–0.542 |
| Flag on (this PR + #61025) | 75.2 / 77.4 / 75.3 % | 1.35–1.38 | 1.35–1.41 / 3.22–3.35 | 15.8–16.1 / 27.3–29.2 | 0.536–0.543 |

On this memory-tight, KV-capacity-bound workload, the 18 % smaller KV cache costs far more than sampling saves; nsys on the flag-off run puts redundant sampling at about 1.5–2 % of step time. So **I do not claim a speed-up**. This PR only makes the existing option work for Qwen4Exp (today `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration` advertises `compute_logits_local` but the language model lacks it). It should pay off where the KV cache is not the limit, for example GPUs with more memory, or after limiting NCCL point-to-point channels; I have not measured those. If reviewers prefer, I will close this PR rather than add an option that does not help on the hardware I can test.

## Claims

- `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling` works for Qwen4Exp. Each TP rank computes its vocabulary shard of the logits (`skip_gather=True`), and the existing `BatchSharder` all-to-all gives each rank the full vocabulary for its share of the requests.
- No change when the flag is off: the new method is reached only from the sharded path.
- (Pending) Serving result on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP8 + EP, 8 × A100-SXM4-40GB.

## Validation

**Unit test** (`tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_compute_logits_local.py`, NVIDIA and AMD classes):
- `Qwen4ExpForCausalLM.compute_logits_local` calls the logits processor with `skip_gather=True`.
- The VL wrapper `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration.compute_logits_local` reaches it.
- It follows the existing `test_rocm_compute_logits_local_skips_gather` pattern in `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_vl_rocm.py`.
- Status: TODO, a CUDA run in the vLLM 81198e97 image (scheduled). My local macOS environment cannot import the Qwen4Exp model, because its transformers lacks `Qwen4ExpConfig`.

**End to end** (TODO, running):
- Setup: `vllm serve` Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP8 + EP, MTP 3, prefix caching, FP8 KV, `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling`, against the same command without the flag. Same node.
- Load: MLPerf agentic dataset (full set), 20 concurrent sessions, 3 × 60 min per arm.
- Checks:
  - the start-up log says "Batch-sharded sampling enabled.";
  - no errors;
  - TTFT/TPOT p50/p90/p95/p99 and goodput against the control.
- Correctness: greedy and seeded requests should give the same tokens with and without the flag, because the Gumbel path draws its noise from (seed, position, token id). I will report a seeded comparison.

## Details

- **Root cause:** models opt in to batch-sharded sampling by implementing `compute_logits_local` (`ParallelConfig.enable_batch_sharded_sampling` docstring). The Qwen3.5 VL base class delegates the call to its language model. `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration` reuses that base class, but its language model class did not implement the method.
- **Expected effect (estimate from an nsys trace of this model at 16 concurrent sessions):** top-k/top-p and the logits all-gather run redundantly on all 8 ranks, about 0.6–0.8 ms of a 42 ms average step (1.5–2 %). That trace also counted the Triton top-k/top-p kernel at 6.8 % of the eager kernel time.
- **Size:** +14 lines of model code; +57 lines of test.
- **Limitations:**
  - I have not checked whether the MTP drafter's logits take the sharded path; the drafter code is unchanged.
  - LoRA is rejected by the flag itself (#56074).
