title: [Roadmap] vLLM Roadmap Q4 2026
body:
In [#32455](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/32455), we broke down vLLM's goals into various special interest groups (SIGs). Building on the [Q3 roadmap](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48168), please find below each SIG's Q4 roadmap. You can find regular meetings of these SIGs on the public vLLM calendar.

## Key takeaway

* **Agentic Workload:** Q3 established Model Runner V2 as the default and brought production-ready Rust frontend and distributed KV offloading support. Q4 focuses on making optimized agentic serving easier to deploy: better day-0 performance, tuned production recipes, adaptive speculative decoding, richer agent hints, and fault tolerance across hardware.
* **Ecosystem:** We are expanding low-precision serving and checkpoint conversion across NVIDIA and AMD, strengthening speculative decoding and RL integration, and advancing Agentic API and vLLM-Omni. Frontier models and new hardware need a clear path from initial support to validated, optimized production configurations.
* **OSS Maintenance:** We are simplifying engine and model interfaces, completing quantization dispatch refactors, and improving CI coverage, time to signal, security, and performance evaluation. Agent-assisted review and better test-quality checks should help the community maintain a growing model, feature, and hardware matrix.

### SIG Core ([Meeting Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1x36yhn655LiuV6bPK2C1M-6jfMzgXDLQf2PIngJndgc/edit?tab=t.0))

- [ ] Fully remove Model Runner V1 and close the remaining [Model Runner V2 gaps](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47172).
- [ ] Implement [extensible KV cache support](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56492), pluggable `KVCacheConfigBuilder` implementations for models, and better cache-grouping heuristics for sliding-window attention speculators.
- [ ] Refactor CUDA graphs: separate prefill/decode graph sizes; clarify capture, dispatch, and padding semantics, including adaptive verification and sequence parallelism; and simplify encoder and DeepSeek V4.1 prefill-skipping graphs. Validate prefill graph sizing against padding overhead and performance regressions.
- [ ] Simplify and harden the engine's model loop, data-parallel flow, and scheduler, and improve streaming-input reliability.
- [ ] Reduce coupling between model implementations and the engine through a clearer model interface.
- [ ] Advance the Rust frontend toward default use, including resolving Responses API readiness and parity requirements.
- [ ] Add native per-step observability through [forward-pass metrics](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52061), in collaboration with Dynamo.

* Aspirational work:
  - Simplify KV connector interfaces through standardized KV layouts, including exploring parallel interfaces.
  - Revisit automatic prefix caching and investigate lookahead EAGLE block caching as a replacement for block dropping.
  - Explore a more comprehensive scheduler redesign beyond the immediate cleanup.

### SIG Large Scale Serving ([Meeting Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/15A9zid75c41pcn8hzIKXOW2R6VFgeUfGuIMq-ebgEEI/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.prqroxfe0fr1))

- [ ] Extend agent hints across routers and KV connectors with Dynamo and llm-d: multi-tenancy, cache-tier TTLs, filesystem eviction, and request-level control of prefetching, eviction, and selective offloading.
- [ ] Publish production recipes with clear explanations of deployment and performance tradeoffs, including disaggregated prefill/decode and KV offloading.
- [ ] Harden numerical fault handling, including NaNs, and expert-parallel recovery through restart and scale-down; integrate recovery with llm-d and Dynamo.
- [ ] Achieve state-of-the-art agentic workload performance for priority models across AMD and new hardware, including Rubin and MI455X.
- [ ] Integrate native [forward-pass metrics](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52061) into the serving observability work with Dynamo.

* Proposed work: define the scope and milestones for AFD.

### SIG Model Performance ([Meeting Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A1TOuCTPQ_72npOSzhWKfYOmDIF7OoagLGaL8gHe1TQ/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.wmm9txlfqo9w))

- [ ] Improve day-0 performance and the workflow from initial model support to optimized agentic serving configurations.
- [ ] Continue sprints for frontier models, including DeepSeek V4.1, GLM 5.3, and Qwen3.8, with continuous model and feature tracking.
- [ ] Optimize Vera Rubin performance and publish reproducible serving recipes.
- [ ] Expand FP4 KV cache support to more models and add disk-backed KV offloading.
- [ ] Continue the [performance-evaluation dashboard](https://vllm-ci-dashboard.vercel.app/perf) and broaden regression tracking with SIG CI.

* Proposals to evaluate: bring `vllm-recipes` into the main repository, restructure model-specific tests, and clarify the scope and feasibility of deprecating vLLM IR and custom Torch compile passes.

### SIG Spec Decode ([Meeting Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1DlgW4dWZyGup_BOZm24Bo50AFIiQgPXfSLqMGDLt6Ic/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.1efi34fxtsr2))

- [ ] Improve HMA and heterogeneous attention support between drafter and verifier. Make sliding-window drafters compose efficiently with different target attention types and reduce KV cache padding and memory overhead.
- [ ] Polish adaptive verification and extend support to Mamba2, GDN, and QSA. Research oracle verification to quantify remaining performance opportunities and guide optimization.
- [ ] Migrate speculative model code to Flat Model, then optimize fusion and kernels for low-latency inference, including rejection sampling.
- [ ] Enable block rejection sampling and probabilistic verification by default.
- [ ] Finalize `open-spec-config` configuration details for popular draft algorithms and implement draft-model loading.
- [ ] Improve configuration ergonomics and robustness with tool calling, reasoning, and structured outputs. Enabling speculative decoding itself by default remains an aspiration.

### SIG CI ([Meeting Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/u/2/d/18VJOuEyAZmRVILWpOtYx5jC4iFZLwjHVw5TAdfJnjXQ/edit?tab=t.0))

- [ ] Collect test-coverage data and maintain a feature-combination matrix, including prefill/decode disaggregation.
- [ ] Bring time to signal toward 30 minutes through automatic test selection, pytest-level granularity, automatic sharding, and default job timeouts.
- [ ] Migrate remaining four-L4 jobs to H200 MIG, reduce Docker build/pull and environment-setup overhead, and retire obsolete jobs for old models.
- [ ] Improve infrastructure-failure detection, quarantine, and retries, and carry forward flaky-test management.
- [ ] Perform offensive security testing of vLLM and make CI safe for projects throughout the vLLM ecosystem.
- [ ] Expand performance and accuracy evaluation to disaggregated serving and TPU, including InferenceX-style benchmark sweeps and throughput/latency Pareto curves.
- [ ] Develop agent-assisted reviewers and CI shepherds, with checks for unit-test quality.
- [ ] Clarify and document CI trigger paths and coverage for RDNA, XPU, and other accelerators, including projects maintained outside the main repository, to reduce cross-backend breakage.

### SIG Quantization

- [ ] **LUT-B (W3A8) on Rubin:** finalize the NVIDIA format specification, including tile sizes, codebooks, and scales ([Model Optimizer #2204](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer/issues/2204), [compressed-tensors #801](https://github.com/vllm-project/compressed-tensors/pull/801)); provide an [LLM Compressor calibration recipe](https://github.com/vllm-project/llm-compressor/pull/3018), validated checkpoints, and optimized dense/MoE kernels with MXFP8 activations.
- [ ] **Production FP4 and lower-bit KV caches:** publish accuracy evaluations and recommended configurations for priority models. Cover long-context interactive serving and high-concurrency data generation, and compose with hybrid attention, speculative drafters, NIXL disaggregation, and tiered offloading.
  - Expand NVFP4 coverage across FlashMLA/DSA sparse attention, FA4, Rubin kernels, and [SM8x–SM12x enablement](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46963).
  - Advance ROCm low-bit KV work, including [UltraQuant](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57057) and the [Octave KV proposal](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59773), with platform-specific validation rather than assuming one format fits every backend.
- [ ] **Checkpoint requantization:** complete the [online quantization from arbitrary precision roadmap](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59062) through a common online quantization API, including [requantization](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55684), [activation QuantKey overrides](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51808), [shared experts](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55686), and [MLA `kv_b_proj`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55741). Initial conversions include MXFP8 to FP8 per-channel/block on Hopper and MI300, and FP8/NVFP4 to MXFP4 across vendors.
- [ ] **Unified dispatch and inspectability:** finish QuantKey/QuantConfig adoption in [Quark](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56099), [ModelOpt MoE](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55339), and compressed-tensors. Declare weight and activation QuantKeys across methods, complete the [MoE oracle and linear-kernel migration](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54959), extend QuantKey into `FusedMoEQuantDesc`, and log selected kernels/backends by layer type.
- [ ] **Kernel consolidation:** make [Humming the default over Marlin on Hopper](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56997), then extend to SM10x/SM12x. Consolidate autotuning configurations and benchmark overlapping CuTe-DSL, b12x, FlashInfer TRTLLM, Marlin, Qutlass, and Humming paths to choose per-architecture defaults and retire superseded paths.
- [ ] **Compression ecosystem:** deliver day-0 NVFP4/MXFP4 checkpoints for priority models, advance [MoNe](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50415) and [REAP expert pruning](https://github.com/vllm-project/llm-compressor/pull/2906), and make `convert_checkpoint` the general format-conversion entry point.
- [ ] **Quality validation:** add quantized-model accuracy CI, tensor-parallel parity checks for online quantization, and quantized weight-reload correctness checks with the RL ecosystem.

* Research directions: LUT-B attention support, FP4 with rotations through QuTLASS, HIGGS, and QAD. Continue evaluating [legacy format deprecation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/30136).

### SIG AMD

- [ ] Close frontier-model prefill, decode, speculative decoding, and long-context performance gaps on ROCm, prioritizing DeepSeek V4/V4.1, Kimi K3, GLM 5.x, and Qwen3.x.
- [ ] Productionize context parallelism for sparse, MLA, and hybrid-attention models, and harden prefill/decode disaggregation and KV transfer.
- [ ] Improve multi-tier KV offloading across GPU, host memory, SSD, and distributed storage, including Mooncake, MoRI/UMBP, and NIXL integrations.
- [ ] Expand AITER kernels and fused FP8/MXFP8/FP4/MXFP4 execution paths, with automatic backend selection and fewer AMD-specific configuration requirements.
- [ ] Strengthen AMD/Quark day-0 support: FP4 and FP8-PTPC for priority CDNA models, plus INT4 and other low-bit formats for priority RDNA models. Coordinate online requantization and flexible activation QuantKey overrides with SIG Quantization.
- [ ] Advance UltraQuant and MXFP4 KV-cache/attention support on ROCm, and support MTP, EAGLE, and DFlash for priority models, including quantized draft heads.
- [ ] Maintain MI355X as the primary performance platform while closing MI300X/MI325X gaps, expanding RDNA support where applicable, and improving AMD CI parity, performance regression coverage, and ROCm release readiness. Document the RDNA validation and CI trigger path with SIG CI.

### SIG Agentic API

- [ ] Deliver [multi-agent APIs](https://github.com/vllm-project/agentic-api/issues/298).
- [ ] Add a [code interpreter tool](https://github.com/vllm-project/agentic-api/issues/308).
- [ ] Use the [shared Rust frontend library](https://github.com/vllm-project/agentic-api/issues/359) for direct vLLM engine inference.
- [ ] Add a [file search tool](https://github.com/vllm-project/agentic-api/pull/278).

### vLLM-Omni

- [ ] Continue optimizing frontier diffusion models, including MiniMax H3.
- [ ] Integrate with RL frameworks, including verl with ve-omni as the training framework.
- [ ] Expand acceleration backends and framework integrations, including FastVideo.
- [ ] Complete the [full-duplex redesign](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/7181), carrying forward Q3 prototyping work.

### RL Ecosystem

- [ ] Execute the [Q4 vLLM × RL roadmap](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58990): weight updates, training–inference consistency, and feature enablement such as LoRA for RL.
- [ ] Improve day-0 RL support for new models.
- [ ] Refactor weight updates and advance the auxiliary connector design to address correctness at the architectural level, including quantized weight reloads with SIG Quantization.

title: [Perf][GDN] Cut host op calls in the eager prefill path of mixed steps
body:
## Overview

Cut host-side PyTorch op calls in the GDN (gated delta net) layer's eager prefill path. That path runs in every mixed prefill + decode step, between the piecewise CUDA graph pieces. This PR changes no kernel and no numerics; outputs and states are bit-identical.

CUDA parity tests pass on A100 (below). The end-to-end serving A/B gives +1.0 point SLO pass and +2.4 % goodput at concurrency 20, and lets concurrency 18 pass in all three repeats. nsys shows mixed steps 11 ms shorter; py-spy shows the host-time drop in the GDN path.

No new CPU/GPU sync: the new `spec_tokens_first` flag is computed from a CPU tensor in the metadata builder, and py-spy shows 0 % of the worker's main thread in host syncs with the change. Validated outside CI (no A100 in CI). The new kernel tests need SM80+ and run on any such CI GPU. Written with AI assistance (Claude Code); the submitter reviewed every line.

## Claims

- **(a) Prefill SSM state gather / zero / scatter:** Python indexing becomes `index_select`, one `masked_fill_` and `index_copy_`. The metadata builder computes the mask and an int64 copy of the prefill state indices once per step.
- **(b) Spec / non-spec token split and merge:** the builder sets a CPU flag, `spec_tokens_first`, when all spec-decode rows lead the batch. MRv2 `sort_batch_req_ids` normally gives that order. With the flag set, the layer uses slices and 2 `copy_` instead of 6 `index_select` and 2 `index_copy_`. Other orders keep the gather path.
- **(c) q/k/v:** `rearrange_mixed_qkv(..., contiguous=False)` returns strided views at the three call sites that feed the recurrent update kernel. That kernel already calls `.contiguous()`. Other callers are unchanged.
- **Expected effect (estimate):** about 9–14 ms less host time per mixed step on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (36 GDN layers), A100, TP8. The estimate comes from a py-spy profile, summarised below.

## Validation

**Why (measured, py-spy at 100 Hz on all TP workers, MRv2, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP8 + EP, 8 × A100-SXM4-40GB, MLPerf agentic set at 16 concurrent sessions):**
- Mixed steps are host-paced. The worker's main thread spends about 80 ms of Python per mixed step, and 0 % of it is in host syncs.
- 71 % of that piecewise-forward host time is the eager GDN core.
- The three blocks changed here take about 8.0 ms (a), 8.1 ms (b) and 6.1 ms (c) per mixed step. These ms values are estimated from the sample shares.

**CUDA parity tests (A100-SXM4-40GB, vLLM 81198e97 image with this change backported, unchanged otherwise):**
- New `tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_mixed.py` (SM80+). It checks outputs, conv states and SSM states **bit-exactly** (atol = 0) against the previous code path:
  - `test_prefill_state_gather_and_scatter_match_indexing[prefills, spec-decodes-then-prefills]`; fresh-prefill state slots hold NaN, to prove they are not read;
  - `test_spec_token_slices_match_gathers`;
  - `test_strided_qkv_views_match_contiguous_copies[4 batch types]`.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py` (CPU): new `test_spec_tokens_first_matches_token_indices`, new `test_prefill_state_indices_int64_matches_prefill_state_indices`, and the new fields added to `test_update_block_table_matches_build`.
- Regression run of `test_gdn_metadata_builder.py`, `test_gdn_fused_mtp.py`, `test_gdn_forward_core_split.py` and `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py`, without and with the change:
  - Old tests: the same 11 failures in both runs. They are not caused by this change: the fused MTP kernel is not built in the cu12.9 image, and the FP8 QSA selection tests need sm_89+.
  - New tests: they fail without the change and pass with it.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`: clean.

**End to end (measured, 11 Oct 2026):** 8 × A100-SXM4-40GB, one node (the same node for both arms, runs 8 h apart, not interleaved). Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP8, MTP 3, FP8 QSA KV, bf16 SSM state, native CPU KV offload 256 GiB. ArtificialAnalysis-style multi-turn agentic replay at concurrency 20, 3 × 60 min per arm. SLO (Artificial Analysis percentile convention): P95 TTFT ≤ 2.93 s and P95 TPOT ≤ 21.74 ms (P5 output speed ≥ 46 tokens/s). "SLO pass" is the share of requests that meet both limits; the SLO holds when it is ≥ 95 %.

| Arm | SLO pass r1 / r2 / r3 (%) | Mean | Goodput r1 / r2 / r3 (req/s) | Mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Without this PR | 92.01 / 90.92 / 92.18 | 91.70 | 1.851 / 1.875 / 1.872 | 1.866 |
| With this PR | 92.58 / 92.62 / 93.06 | **92.75** | 1.885 / 1.885 / 1.960 | **1.910 (+2.4 %)** |

**Higher load, concurrency 18 (same setup, measured):** without this PR 96.49 / 94.72 % (one repeat under the 95 % target); with this PR **97.81 / 96.44 / 96.55 %** (all three repeats above 95 %), goodput 2.06 / 1.95 / 1.92 req/s. TPOT p95 per 10-min bin stays at or under 19.9 ms for the whole hour of repeat 1.

All three repeats with the change are above all three without it. The gain is small: the workload is limited by KV cache capacity, and this PR changes only host time in mixed prefill + decode steps. No request errors in either arm. **Host profile (py-spy, measured shares):** C16, the same replay window, 100 Hz for 300 s on every TP worker, without (6 workers) and with (7 workers) this PR. Share of main-thread samples:

| Part of the mixed-step (piecewise) forward | Without | With | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| GDN eager path (36 layers) | 24.4 % | 19.1 % | −22 % relative |
| QSA + indexer eager path (12 layers) | 8.5 % | 8.0 % | — |
| Whole piecewise forward | 34.5 % | 28.6 % | −17 % relative |
| Worker idle (waiting for the next step) | 33.7 % | 36.5 % | +2.8 points |

Converted with the same factor as the baseline analysis (about 1,100 mixed steps in the window, an estimate), the GDN host time per mixed step falls from about 47 ms to about 37 ms. The two traces ran on different nodes of the same type. No host syncs in either trace.

**GPU timeline (Nsight Systems, device 0, 256 steps per trace, measured):**

| | Without | With |
|---|---|---|
| Decode step, GPU period (median) | 24.67 ms | 24.40 ms |
| Mixed prefill + decode step, GPU period (median) | 103.7 ms | **92.6 ms** |
| Mixed step, host NVTX range (median) | 96.0 ms | **85.4 ms** |
| Prefill tokens per mixed step (median) | 296 | 672 |

Decode steps do not change. Mixed steps are about 11 ms shorter, although the window with this PR had larger prefill chunks (which costs more GPU time, not less).

**Reproduce the serving runs.** The serving setup, client and dataset are the same as in #60602 (see its "Reproduce the serving runs" section). Both arms use the same server command (below). The two arms differ only in this PR's two files. A second node of the same type, with this PR, gave 94.70 / 93.37 / 94.33 % at concurrency 20 (no control run on that node).

<details>
<summary>Server command (both arms)</summary>

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --max-num-seqs 32 --enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml --reasoning-parser qwen3 --max-model-len 262144 --distributed-executor-backend mp --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' --cudagraph-capture-sizes 1 2 4 8 16 24 32 40 48 56 64 96 128 192 256 384 512 768 1024 1536 2048 --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 --prefix-match-unit 16 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}' --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "bf16"}' --mamba-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --kv-offloading-backend native --kv-offloading-size 256
```

</details>

## Details

- **Assumptions:**
  - Prefill state indices are non-negative and unique. Padded rows use `NULL_BLOCK_ID` 0.
  - `causal_conv1d_update` writes in place into its input. With (b), that input is a slice of `mixed_qkv`, so the spec rows of `mixed_qkv` are overwritten. The spec-only and decode-only paths already do this, and no later code reads those rows.
- **Not done:** the FLA chunk kernel reading and writing the state in place through indices, and folding (c) into `fused_post_conv_prep`. Both need kernel changes. With them the saving would be about 15–18 ms (estimate).
- **Size:** `qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py` +66 / −13 (with the int64 fix), `gdn_attn.py` +24; tests +371.
- **Commits:** (a), (b), (c), plus a fix that uses int64 indices for `index_copy_`. The A100 run caught that bug: the GDN state indices are int32. I am happy to squash.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

title: [Bugfix] Skip the DeepSeek fused A GEMM kernel under batch invariance
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

`DeepSeekV2FusedQkvAProjLinear` (`vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py`) runs the fused q/kv A projection through the `dsv3_fused_a_gemm` kernel for batches of at most 16 tokens and through `F.linear` for larger ones (`_min_latency_fused_qkv_a_proj_impl`). With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` a request's projection therefore depends on how many tokens share its batch, and the difference propagates through every layer. Only bf16 checkpoints with a 2112x7168 fused weight on Hopper/Blackwell are eligible for the kernel: `moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Thinking` (q_lora_rank 1536 + kv_lora_rank 512 + qk_rope_head_dim 64 = 2112, hidden 7168, bf16 attention weights) fails every bitwise batch-invariance test at TP=4, while the FP8 `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1` (same architecture, FP8 fused weight, so not eligible) passes them.

This PR adds `not envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` to the kernel's eligibility, so in batch-invariant mode the layer takes the regular `MergedColumnParallelLinear` path (`linear_batch_invariant`). Nothing changes when the flag is unset.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `tests/model_executor/test_deepseek_v2_fused_qkv_a_proj.py` (CPU, mocks the platform checks): the kernel is eligible without the flag and not with it. It fails on `main` for the flag-on case.

GB300 (4 GPUs), `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, TP=4, `main` at `d09ff7763` versus `main` + this PR:

- Online bs=1-vs-batched check (32 random prompts sent one at a time and then as one batch, `temperature=0.6` with a fixed `seed`, sampled tokens and their logprobs compared bitwise; standard 10-50-word prompts and a ragged variant with 1024-2048-word prompts), for Kimi-K2-Thinking.
- `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py` bs1-vs-bsN ids for Kimi-K2-Thinking (TRITON_MLA).
- How the cause was isolated (all on `main`, same node, same check): Kimi fails identically with `--disable-custom-all-reduce`, with `--enable-expert-parallel`, with `--no-enable-prefix-caching` and with the FlashInfer MLA prefill backend, and passes with `VLLM_MLA_DISABLE=1` (plain attention does not construct the fused projection). DeepSeek-V3.1 passes, also with `--hf-overrides '{"n_group": 1, "topk_group": 1}'` (Kimi's router config).

## Test Result

Blocks are copied from the logs; only `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` and pytest plugin flags were dropped. The `main` tree also carried my pending batch-invariance fixes (#60479, #60524 and the custom all-reduce padding one), none of which touches this layer.

**1. `main`: Kimi-K2-Thinking, TP=4**

```text
python /data01/gb300/kit/run/online_bi_check.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8405/v1 --model moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Thinking --num-prompts 32 --max-tokens 8 
{"model": "moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Thinking", "num_prompts": 32, "max_tokens": 8, "ragged": false, "bs1_seconds": 17.4, "bsN_seconds": 4.0, "mismatches": 32}
BATCH_INVARIANCE_VIOLATED 32/32 prompts
python /data01/gb300/kit/run/online_bi_check.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8405/v1 --model moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Thinking --num-prompts 32 --max-tokens 8 --ragged
{"model": "moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Thinking", "num_prompts": 32, "max_tokens": 8, "ragged": true, "bs1_seconds": 19.1, "bsN_seconds": 3.7, "mismatches": 32}
BATCH_INVARIANCE_VIOLATED 32/32 prompts

VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Thinking VLLM_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.9 python -m pytest -v 'tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_bs1_vs_bsN[16-16-TRITON_MLA]'
E           Failed: Batch invariance violated in 32/32 prompts. See output above for details.
================== 1 failed, 16 warnings in 223.63s (0:03:43) ==================

VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Thinking VLLM_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.9 python -m pytest -v 'tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_bs1_vs_bsN[8-16-TRITON_MLA]'

```

**2. `main`, isolation runs (same check; only the changed flag is shown)**

<details><summary>online_bi_check.py (the online check used above)</summary>

```python
"""Batch-invariance check against a running OpenAI-compatible vLLM server.

Mirrors tests/v1/determinism/test_online_batch_invariance.py: N random prompts,
BS=1 (one request per prompt, sequential) versus one batched request with all
prompts; sampled tokens and per-step logprobs must match bitwise.
"""
import argparse
import json
import random
import sys
import time

import openai


PROMPT_TEMPLATES = [
    "Question: What is the capital of France?\nAnswer: The capital of France is",
    "Q: How does photosynthesis work?\nA: Photosynthesis is the process by which",
    "User: Can you explain quantum mechanics?\nAssistant: Quantum mechanics is",
    "Once upon a time in a distant galaxy, there lived",
    "The old man walked slowly down the street, remembering",
    "In the year 2157, humanity finally discovered",
    "To implement a binary search tree in Python, first we need to",
    "The algorithm works by iterating through the array and",
    "Here's how to optimize database queries using indexing:",
    "The Renaissance was a period in European history that",
    "Climate change is caused by several factors including",
    "The human brain contains approximately 86 billion neurons which",
    "I've been thinking about getting a new laptop because",
    "Yesterday I went to the store and bought",
    "My favorite thing about summer is definitely",
]


def _random_prompt(min_words: int = 1024, max_words: int = 1024 * 2) -> str:
    """Copy of tests/v1/determinism/utils.py::_random_prompt (same templates, padding and RNG use)."""
    base_prompt = random.choice(PROMPT_TEMPLATES)
    if max_words < min_words:
        max_words = min_words
    target_words = random.randint(min_words, max_words)
    if target_words > 50:
        padding_text = " This is an interesting topic that deserves more explanation. " * (target_words // 50)
        base_prompt = padding_text + base_prompt
    return base_prompt



def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--base-url", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--tests-dir", default=None, help="unused; kept for the caller")
    ap.add_argument("--num-prompts", type=int, default=32)
    ap.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=8)
    ap.add_argument("--min-words", type=int, default=10)
    ap.add_argument("--max-words", type=int, default=50)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=12345)
    ap.add_argument("--temperature", type=float, default=0.6)
    ap.add_argument("--ragged", action="store_true", help="every other prompt is 1024-2048 words")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    random.seed(a.seed)
    if a.ragged:
        prompts = [
            _random_prompt(a.min_words, a.max_words) if i % 2 == 0 else _random_prompt(1024, 2048)
            for i in range(a.num_prompts)
        ]
    else:
        prompts = [_random_prompt(a.min_words, a.max_words) for _ in range(a.num_prompts)]
    sp = dict(temperature=a.temperature, top_p=1.0, max_tokens=a.max_tokens, seed=42, logprobs=5)
    client = openai.OpenAI(base_url=a.base_url, api_key="EMPTY", timeout=1800)

    def req(prompt):
        for attempt in range(4):
            try:
                return client.completions.create(model=a.model, prompt=prompt, **sp).model_dump()
            except Exception:
                if attempt == 3:
                    raise
                time.sleep(0.5 * 2**attempt)

    def extract(choice):
        lp = choice.get("logprobs") or {}
        return list(lp.get("token_ids") or lp.get("tokens") or []), lp.get("token_logprobs")

    t0 = time.time()
    bs1 = [extract(req(p)["choices"][0]) for p in prompts]
    t1 = time.time()
    choices = req(prompts)["choices"]
    assert len(choices) == len(prompts), f"BS=N choices {len(choices)} != {len(prompts)}"
    bsn = [extract(c) for c in choices]
    t2 = time.time()

    mismatches = []
    for i, ((ta, la), (tb, lb)) in enumerate(zip(bs1, bsn)):
        if la is None or lb is None:
            mismatches.append((i, "missing logprobs"))
        elif ta != tb:
            mismatches.append((i, f"tokens differ: {ta} vs {tb}"))
        elif len(la) != len(lb):
            mismatches.append((i, f"steps {len(la)} vs {len(lb)}"))
        else:
            for t, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(la, lb)):
                if x != y:
                    mismatches.append((i, f"step {t} logprob {x!r} vs {y!r} (abs diff {abs(x - y):.3e})"))
                    break
    print(json.dumps({
        "model": a.model, "num_prompts": len(prompts), "max_tokens": a.max_tokens, "ragged": a.ragged,
        "bs1_seconds": round(t1 - t0, 1), "bsN_seconds": round(t2 - t1, 1), "mismatches": len(mismatches),
    }))
    for i, m in mismatches:
        print(f"MISMATCH prompt {i}: {m}")
    if mismatches:
        print(f"BATCH_INVARIANCE_VIOLATED {len(mismatches)}/{len(prompts)} prompts")
        sys.exit(1)
    print(f"BATCH_INVARIANCE_OK {len(prompts)}/{len(prompts)} prompts")


main()
```
</details>

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4.1 crashes in decoder-replay CUDA graph with --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_* (input_ids int32 vs int64)
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `main`: `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` reproduced on `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` arm64 `sha256:f853a683…` (built from 7d0b4e57aa); `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` reproduced on c41b2639e2 + #59912 + #59900, which that backend needs to start. Both include #59532.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (revision `2cba9e42`), 4× GB200, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, torch 2.13.0.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

DeepSeek-V4.1 served with a FlashInfer MegaMoE backend at TP=1 with DP+EP starts and answers short prompts, then crashes once it serves long prompts or batched prefills (here GSM8K 5-shot at `--max-concurrency 128`):

```text
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm
  # or flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl (needs #59912 + #59900 to start)
```

```text
    torch.index_select(t, 0, rows, out=buf[:num_rows])
RuntimeError: Expected out tensor to have dtype int, but got long int instead
```

```text
  File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v41/decoder_replay_layers.py", line 99, in _run_in_graph_break

  File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v41/decoder_replay_layers.py", line 120, in _run

RuntimeError: Expected out tensor to have dtype int, but got long int instead
```

</details>

On 4× GB200 at DEP=4, GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot) scores 0.027 with `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` (0.117 in an earlier run; the score depends on when the engine dies) and 0.070 with `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`, versus 0.899 for both with the fix. Once the engine dies, requests get HTTP 500 until the API server exits, then fail with connection errors.

**Cause.** `DecoderReplayCudaGraphManager` sizes its `input_ids` buffer as int64 for every backend in `MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/decoder_replay_cudagraph.py:59-60`), which includes both `flashinfer_moe_ep_*` backends. `DeepseekV4Model.forward` casts `input_ids` to int64 only for `NATIVE_MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py:929-930`), so the FlashInfer backends pass the runner's int32 ids and `index_select(out=)` rejects the mismatch.

It doesn't show at startup or on short prompts because `run()` is only reached when a step is large enough to use a replay batch (a PIECEWISE step of at least 768 padded tokens, or an eager step with a prefill chunk over the 128-token window) and that batch dispatches to a replay CUDA graph; capture feeds the buffers directly and the eager fallback has no `out=`. By the code, a single prompt of 768 or more tokens is enough; GSM8K 5-shot at concurrency 128 reaches such steps right away.

The two checks diverged when #54049 narrowed the model's cast to the native backend while #59532 was in flight with the wider check. `deep_gemm_mega_moe` and the default backend are unaffected.

Keying the buffer dtype on `NATIVE_MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS` fixes it; PR to follow.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Add VLLM_KV_OFFLOAD_DISABLE_BATCH_MEMCPY to bypass cuMemcpyBatchAsync
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #61052

On NVIDIA vGPU guests (H200 NVL, vGPU 595.91.x), `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` resolves fine via `cuGetProcAddress` but faults at runtime (host Xid 31, `unspecified launch failure`), even for a single in-bounds descriptor. Plain per-copy memcpy on the same addresses works at full PCIe bandwidth. As a result, CPU KV offload crashes on the first transfer with both connectors on these platforms.

vLLM calls `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` from two independent places:

1. **C++** `swap_blocks_batch` (`csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu`), used by `OffloadingConnector` (and the EC CPU connector / hisparse). It already has a per-copy `cudaMemcpyAsync` fallback for older drivers and the legacy default stream.
2. **Python** `copy_blocks` (`vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/cuda_mem_ops.py`), used by `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, which calls the driver entry point through ctypes and has no fallback.

This PR adds one opt-out, `VLLM_KV_OFFLOAD_DISABLE_BATCH_MEMCPY=1`, honored by both:

- `cache_kernels.cu`: `batch_memcpy_disabled()` reads the env var once (cached, same pattern as `resolve_max_batch_descriptors()`). When set, `batch_fn` resolves to `nullptr`, so the **existing** per-copy fallback is used. No new copy path in C++.
- `cuda_mem_ops.py`: when set (CUDA only), `copy_blocks` issues one `cuMemcpyAsync` per descriptor on the same stream, reusing the already-expanded `src_all` / `dst_all` / `sz_all` arrays. `cuMemcpyAsync` is resolved via `cuGetProcAddress`, matching how the batch entry point is resolved in the same file.
- `envs.py`: register `VLLM_KV_OFFLOAD_DISABLE_BATCH_MEMCPY` (default `False`) next to `VLLM_KV_OFFLOAD_MAX_BATCH_DESCRIPTORS`.

Default behavior is unchanged. ROCm (`hipMemcpyBatchAsync`) is intentionally left untouched in both places since I can only validate on CUDA; happy to extend it if preferred.

Notes:
- `VLLM_KV_OFFLOAD_MAX_BATCH_DESCRIPTORS=1` does not help, since the batch API faults even with one descriptor.
- In `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, `build_params()` still resolves the `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` pointer; resolving it is harmless on vGPU, only calling it faults. Kept as-is to minimize the diff.
- The Python fallback loops over `num_blocks × num_layers` descriptors per transfer on the connector's background copy thread. This only applies when the opt-out is set.

## Test Plan

1. Standalone repro (no model), calling `vllm._custom_ops.swap_blocks_batch` with vLLM's own descriptor buffers, `/dev/shm`-backed `cudaHostRegister` memory and in-bounds addresses, 4 MiB per descriptor, both directions: [swap_test.py](https://gist.github.com/jerry102039/860de1bb1810a962c58bab7668bd2a03)
2. End-to-end with `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8`, once with `OffloadingConnector` (`cpu_bytes_to_use=64 GiB`) and once with `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` (`cpu_bytes_to_use=128 GiB`), each under a saturating random-dataset benchmark (1000 requests) so that both stores and preemption-driven loads occur.
3. Check host `dmesg` for Xid after each run.

Hardware: H200 NVL vGPU (70 GiB profile), host vGPU manager 595.91.04, guest driver 595.91.07, Python 3.14, TP=1.

## Test Result

| Run | Flag unset (default) | `VLLM_KV_OFFLOAD_DISABLE_BATCH_MEMCPY=1` |
|---|---|---|
| repro (`ops.swap_blocks_batch`) | ❌ crashes on the first call, Xid 31 | ✅ GPU→CPU 48.5 GiB/s, CPU→GPU 47.5 GiB/s, 0 mismatches |
| `OffloadingConnector` end-to-end | ❌ engine dies on the first offload store, Xid 31 | ✅ stores ~50 GiB/s, loads ~49 GiB/s, no Xid |
| `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` end-to-end | ❌ engine dies on the first store (copy thread), Xid 31 | ✅ stores and loads run continuously

title: [CI] Fix Buildkite path filters that point at moved or deleted files
body:
## Overview

Fix Buildkite path filters (`source_file_dependencies` and two other path lists) that point at files which were moved or deleted. Part of #51225; complementary to #51345, whose six entries this PR leaves untouched so the two do not conflict.

## Claims

- 78 dead path entries across 16 pipeline files now match real files (or are removed), so the affected steps trigger again when the code they cover changes.
- Most dead entries were in the AMD/Intel mirrors and `test-amd.yaml`, which missed renames the main steps already picked up (e.g. `rust_frontend.yaml` main step lists `tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_shutdown.py`, its AMD mirror still listed `tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_shutdown.py`).
- No step, command or other dependency entry changes.

## Validation

- Dead-entry scan (every YAML list item under `.buildkite/` that is a repo path, matched by prefix against `git ls-files`): 84 dead entries on `61f084b5f3`, 6 after this PR, exactly the ones #51345 changes (engine `logger.py`, the two DeepSeek V4 kernel `.cu` paths, `csrc/mamba/`, the first samplers step and its mirror).
- Every remapped path was resolved from git history (`git log --diff-filter=DR -1 -- <path>`, `git show -M --stat <sha>`), not by name guessing; removed entries point at files deleted outright or never added.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass, including `check-buildkite-step-keys` and `check-test-tethering`; all changed YAML files parse.
- Changed-line tally (`git diff -U0 | grep '^[-+] ' | sort | uniq -c`) checked so only dependency entries changed.
- Not run: the rendered pipeline itself (the Jinja template lives in `vllm-project/buildkite-ci`).

## Details

Mapping (old -> new):

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `vllm/worker/worker_base.py` | `vllm/v1/worker/worker_base.py` |
| `vllm/executor/` | `vllm/v1/executor/` |
| `vllm/entrypoints/logger.py` (mirrors only) | `vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/request_logger.py` |
| `vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py` | `vllm/renderers/chat_utils.py` |
| `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/pcp.py` | `vllm/v1/attention/ops/pcp.py` |
| `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/cutlass_moe.py` | `.../fused_moe/experts/cutlass_moe.py` |
| `vllm/model_executor/layers/fla/ops/` | `vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/` |
| `csrc/quantization/{cutlass_w8a8,w8a8/cutlass}/moe/` | `csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/moe/` |
| `csrc/quantization/fp4/`, `csrc/attention/mla/` | `csrc/libtorch_stable/...` |
| `csrc/mamba/`, DeepSeek V4 `.cu` (mirrors / test-amd only) | `csrc/libtorch_stable/...` |
| `requirements/rocm-test.txt` | `requirements/test/rocm.txt` |
| `examples/offline_inference/data_parallel.py` | `examples/features/data_parallel/data_parallel_offline.py` |
| `tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_shutdown.py`, `tests/entrypoints/openai/test_uds.py` | `tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_shutdown.py`, `tests/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/test_uds.py` |
| `tests/plugins_tests/test_gguf_plugin.py` | `tests/plugins_tests/gguf/` |
| `tests/test_config/` (Intel) | `tests/test_config.py` |

Removed (deleted outright or never added): `vllm/sampling_metadata.py` (remaining copies), `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/qwen4_exp.py`, `vllm/v1/spec_decode/qwen4_exp.py`, `vllm/v1/distributed/`, `vllm/v1/kv_connector/`, `.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-amd-test.py` (the `.sh` is already listed), and the `!vllm/scripts.py` (removed in #60923) and `!scripts/` (moved to `tools/` in #58572) exclusions in the Ascend pipeline. Where the new path was already in the same list, the stale line is dropped instead of duplicated.

Tradeoff: restoring these filters means some AMD/Intel mirror steps trigger again on changes to the files they were meant to cover, which slightly raises CI load back to the intended level.

Interaction with #59706: after this PR, 18 of the 22 entries in its `source_file_dependencies_allowlist.txt` are no longer dead (the other four are the paths #51345 owns), so whichever lands second should shrink the allowlist; after both, it can be empty.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Fuse C1/C2 compression with FP8 KV cache insertion
body:
## Overview

Fuse DeepSeek-V4.1 C1/C2 compression with RoPE, FP8 quantization and the 584-byte main-cache write. Integrate ordinary attention and the target model's KV-only bounded-prefill replay path on SM90.

**Draft with complete serving integration.** Measured operator speedup is **1.18–1.53x**. The completed H20 two-TP4 crossover shows a positive cold 16K/c4 signal, but **does not establish a stable general end-to-end gain**.

The fusion boundary is inspired by [SGLang #41660](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41660) by @DarkSharpness. This implementation retains vLLM's own FP32 pooling/RMSNorm and BF16 latent rounding.

## Claims

- Preserve the indexer's BF16 latent, ring-state ordering, distinct state/cache slots and padding semantics.
- Integrate both callers for CUDA SM90, uint8 584-byte cache, PCP1/DCP1. Other hardware, KV formats and context-parallel configurations retain separate insertion.
- No weight conversion, extra persistent weight/cache allocation, Humming backend change, scheduler change or model-runner change.
- Operator acceleration is measured; **model acceleration is not established**.

## Validation

H20-3e / SM90, torch 2.13.0+cu130, baseline vLLM 1ee69dde9, PR head 4fe427bd. The three original runtime files were also byte-identical to main 93d2cab35 when checked on 2026-10-11. GPU-tested candidate source hashes match this PR.

- **46 targeted full-module pytest cases passed**, 132 unrelated cases deselected. The existing reference test covers C1/C2 and fused/split modes; six consumption cases cover serial, auxiliary-stream and CUDA-Graph execution.
- **18 additional exact-byte cases passed** for state, latent and full cache contents: changed/restored graph inputs, ragged/empty/padded requests, ring wrap, negative cache slots, shrinking buffers, 128-request six-query verification and 16K prefill. No tolerance was relaxed.
- Full pre-commit passed on all four changed files, including Ruff, mypy and test tethering.

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
      --confcutdir=tests/kernels \
      -k 'test_v41_fused_save_compress_and_insert or test_v41_attention_joins_cache_writes_before_consumption'

The confcutdir option excludes unrelated top-level model fixtures; it does not bypass these test bodies.

**Operator measurements:** each graph captures 128 complete operator chains, with one host launch per sample. After 20 calibration graphs, measure 50 alternating AB/BA pairs per shape. All 26 decode/verification/prefill shapes improve 1.18–1.53x. Reused buffers are L2-warm; this is not a model or HBM-saturation claim.

| Shape | Split µs | Fused µs | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| C1, 16 requests × 6 queries | 3.406 | 2.266 | 1.503x |
| C2, 16 requests × 6 queries | 6.231 | 4.978 | 1.252x |
| C1, 16K prefill | 48.681 | 41.252 | 1.180x |
| C2, 16K prefill | 45.905 | 33.412 | 1.374x |

[All shape medians and exact harnesses](https://github.com/xijiaat/vllm/tree/9b8678843704c27453a25e80db11dc84bb8f8c0c/integration). The earlier host-launched protocol independently measured 1.19–1.49x; its full raw pairs remain in [the initial evidence](https://github.com/xijiaat/vllm/blob/16cd0e863250da9e7c25ebb7ebb55ac931718bdd/result.json).

**Completed two-TP4 full-model crossover:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4/EP, DP1, MRV2, Humming dense/MoE, Engram CPU offload, APC on, 16K chunk and **real DSpark 5 acceptance**. Both arms use the same image/weights/precision/sampling, the existing #60613 sentinel fix and identical unmodified TileLang compile seeds. Only the PR runtime files differ.

Two TP4 instances use disjoint GPU groups, CPU sets and NUMA memory. Only one receives requests at a time, with unchanged peer request/token/draft counters verified. The second phase restarts both engines with GPU groups swapped and reverses the AB/BA order. Each arm/cell has three measured batches per placement, **six total**, following two excluded calibration pairs per placement. All **72 measured batches / 1,152 requests** completed. These are two engine startups per arm, not six independent restarts.

All six workloads generate **1,024 actual tokens** per request from fixed 4K/16K ledger prompts. Throughput includes the complete HTTP batch and tail drain; it is not pure-prefill or permanently saturated steady-state throughput. Cold requests all report exactly zero cache hits. Warm requests retain 64 residual tokens: observed hits are 99.609375% at 16K and 98.4375% at 4K, not literal 100%.

| Workload | Baseline output tok/s | Fused output tok/s | Pooled median change | Phase 0 | Swapped phase 1 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cold 16K / c16 — primary | 355.06 | 354.86 | -0.05% | -0.09% | +0.61% |
| Warm 16K / c16 | 846.13 | 839.59 | -0.77% | -2.09% | -0.15% |
| Cold 4K / c4 | 479.74 | 470.55 | -1.92% | -11.39% | +19.68% |
| Warm 4K / c4 | 562.92 | 520.78 | -7.49% | -15.63% | +9.45% |
| Cold 16K / c4 | 270.43 | 276.63 | +2.29% | +3.81% | +2.45% |
| Warm 16K / c4 | 526.67 | 531.65 | +0.95% | +8.60% | -14.68% |

Cold 16K/c4 is positive in both placements, but its pooled throughput CV is 7.04% / 5.12%, and real acceptance is also higher for B in both phases. This is a positive signal, not proof of a stable code-derived gain. The primary cold 16K/c16 CV is 1.92% / 1.70%; warm 16K/c16 is lower in both phases. Other low-concurrency cells reverse direction. No samples or unfavorable cells were dropped, and throughput was not adjusted by acceptance.

Runtime inventories confirm four affected producers per rank: C2 at layers 2/8/14 and C1 at layer 20, with the expected branch in every rank. This limits the whole-model opportunity. [All batch samples, medians, ranges/CV, TTFT, TPOT, actual acceptance, source hashes and reproduction scripts](https://github.com/xijiaat/vllm/blob/9fe3daffb76889a0fc996b42961fb02b6dd3cb16/dual-tp4/REPORT.txt). The report also includes a separate geometric placement estimate; it is not substituted for the pooled-median ratio above.

<details>
<summary>Earlier single-engine sequential cohort — retained separately</summary>

**Initial full-model A/B:** same ordered four H20 GPUs, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4/EP, DP1, MRV2, Humming dense/MoE, Engram CPU offload, APC on and **real DSpark 5 acceptance**. Both arms share the existing #60613 sentinel fix and identical unmodified TileLang compile seeds. Weights, precision, inputs, sampling and cache protocol are unchanged.

One sequential A/B pair. Each cell has two excluded calibration samples and **three measured samples**, each sending twice the concurrency through continuous refill workers. Warm cells generate 1024 tokens; cold controls generate one token with verified zero cache hits. Warm requests retain 64 residual prompt tokens: observed hit ratios are 99.609375% at 16K and 98.4375% at 4K, **not literal 100%**.

| Workload | Baseline tok/s | Fused tok/s | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Warm 16K / c16, output — primary | 836.11 | 837.23 | +0.13% |
| Warm 4K / c4, output | 570.55 | 559.84 | −1.88% |
| Warm 16K / c4, output | 556.11 | 524.30 | −5.72% |
| Cold 4K / c4, input | 8874.16 | 8871.57 | −0.03% |
| Cold 16K / c4, input | 9464.59 | 9463.22 | −0.01% |

Primary throughput CV is 1.76% / 3.90%, larger than +0.13%. Low-concurrency decode CV is 7.14–12.98%, and acceptance varies between samples. Primary median server-mean TTFT is 463.44 / 478.96 ms, TPOT 15.823 / 15.841 ms, and mean acceptance length 3.997 / 4.099. The candidate's 1.089 s TTFT outlier is retained. This pair establishes neither a stable gain nor a causal regression.

Runtime inventories confirm four affected producers per rank: C2 at layers 2/8/14, C1 at layer 20, with the expected branch in both arms. This limited producer count constrains the whole-model opportunity.

This earlier cohort is not pooled with the crossover above.
</details>

**Regression and memory:** fixed first 128 GSM8K test questions, five-shot, natural EOS, maximum 1024 tokens. An explicit-final-number extractor frozen before B gives **123/128 baseline, 124/128 candidate**, with 125 parsed per arm, 122 matching numeric answers and 46 identical response messages. Neither arm truncated a response. Original hash-marker-only scores (20/17) are retained; that extractor misses boxed answers. This subset establishes neither full-model accuracy nor an accuracy improvement. Allocated/reserved memory after model load is identical on all ranks: 79,796,461,056 / 80,065,069,056 bytes. The crossover readiness snapshots were 119,175 MiB/GPU for A and 119,177 MiB/GPU for B (+2 MiB), identical in both placements. These snapshots are not peak VRAM.

[All measured samples, acceptance, latency, hashes, failure summary and reproduction settings](https://github.com/xijiaat/vllm/blob/9b8678843704c27453a25e80db11dc84bb8f8c0c/model/REPORT.txt). Exact benchmark and analysis scripts are in the same directory. New device-batched/model raw archives are retained on the test host with SHA256 records; they are not represented as uploaded raw data in this evidence branch.

## Details

fused_save_compress_norm gains optional RoPE/cache arguments. It shares the original 584-byte store implementation with the separate insertion kernel and explicitly preserves BF16 store/reload rounding. Ring-state slots and main-cache slots remain distinct.

Q/SWA preparation still overlaps compression. Fused compression publishes both latent and main cache before the existing join; indexer preparation then consumes that latent. This removes the second insertion fork/join but can delay indexer start, so kernel gains need not translate into model gains. KV-only bounded-prefill replay also avoids duplicate insertion. The separate DSpark drafter does not own C1/C2 compressors.

**Remaining before Ready:** NCU/causal profiling, convincing repeatable model benefit, and human review. H20 counter access requires additional permission that remains pending; no capabilities or host settings were changed. Other SM90 products have not been benchmarked.

Earlier harness attempts failed before any timed samples: an incorrect draft-inventory assertion, an unavailable cache-reset endpoint, an omitted dataset manifest, and a GPU UUID metadata-prefix mismatch in the initial crossover attempt. All are archived. The crossover launcher was interrupted by the bastion idle timeout after its independent phase-0 client completed; a detached controller verified ownership and resumed only phase 1 under the original time bound, without repeating or removing samples. All six crossover containers exited 0, and all eight test GPUs were verified at 0 MiB / 0% with no compute processes.

Duplicate-work checks for the compressor/fusion area and exact fused_save_compress_norm / rope_quant_insert symbols found no equivalent CUDA producer/cache fusion PR. Adjacent #56935/#57523 concern attention/KV formats, while #57977 concerns MXFP8 activation chaining. This is a bounded public search, not a claim about private work.

AI assistance was used to implement and validate this change with Codex. Human line review remains pending; please keep this as Draft.

- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** 46 GPU tests, operator measurements, GSM8K subset and complete two-TP4 model crossover; NCU, stable model benefit and human validation remain pending.

title: [Bug]: V2 block verification (rejection_sample_method="block") reuses position-keyed uniforms across rounds, so sampled output is biased
body:
### Your current environment
Environment (from the run logs; collect_env.py was not captured on that machine) ```text vLLM 0.31.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12 GPU: Tesla T4 (sm_75), driver 580.82.07 (Colab), V2 model runner Kernel-level check also run on main 1dfe9fbdae73 under TRITON_INTERPRET=1 (triton 3.8.0, torch 2.13.0+cpu) ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug With the V2 runner, `rejection_sample_method="block"` and temperature > 0, the sampled output does not follow the target model's distribution. Standard verification on the same setup is fine. The acceptance uniform is `tl_rand32(seed, pos)` with one seed per request and the absolute position. In block mode every draft row reads its uniform, including rows after the accepted length. Those uniforms have been conditioned on that round's decision, and the next round verifies the same positions again with the same uniforms. A small case: the target is p = (1/2, 1/2) at every position, the drafter always proposes token 0, and gamma = 2. The third generated token is 0 with probability 5/12 instead of 1/2. The script below calls the V2 `rejection_sample` round by round with the inputs the model runner builds (rows `[last committed, d_1, d_2]` at positions `[L-1, L, L+1]`), so no model is needed: ```python import argparse import torch from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.rejection_sampler_utils import rejection_sample def run(block, fresh_seed, n_req, n_tok=6, gamma=2, p0=0.5, base_seed=12345, device="cuda"): logp = torch.log(torch.tensor([p0, 1 - p0], dtype=torch.float32)) g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(base_seed) out = [[int(torch.rand((), generator=g) >= p0)] for _ in range(n_req)] # prefill token seeds = torch.randint(0, 2**31 - 1, (n_req,), generator=g, dtype=torch.int64) rnd = 0 while True: active = [r for r in range(n_req) if len(out[r]) < n_tok] if not active: break rows, n = gamma + 1, len(active) L = torch.tensor([1 + len(out[r]) for r in active]) # prompt length 1 target_logits = logp.repeat(n * rows, 1).contiguous() draft_sampled = torch.zeros(n * rows, dtype=torch.int64) # drafts are always 0 pos = torch.zeros(n * rows, dtype=torch.int64) for k, r in enumerate(active): draft_sampled[k * rows] = out[r][-1] pos[k * rows:(k + 1) * rows] = torch.arange(L[k] - 1, L[k] - 1 + rows) cu = torch.arange(0, (n + 1) * rows, rows, dtype=torch.int32) idx_mapping = torch.arange(n, dtype=torch.int32) expanded_idx = idx_mapping.repeat_interleave(rows) expanded_local = torch.arange(rows, dtype=torch.int32).repeat(n) temperature = torch.ones(n, dtype=torch.float32) seed = seeds[active].clone() if fresh_seed: seed = (seed * 1000003 + 7919 * (rnd + 1)) % (2**31 - 1) args = [t.to(device) for t in (target_logits,)] + [None] + [ t.to(device) for t in (draft_sampled, cu, pos, idx_mapping, expanded_idx, expanded_local, temperature, seed)] sampled, num_sampled = rejection_sample(*args, gamma, use_block_verification=block) sampled, num_sampled = sampled.cpu(), num_sampled.cpu() for k, r in enumerate(active): out[r].extend(int(t) for t in sampled[k, : int(num_sampled[k])]) rnd += 1 return [sum(o[j] == 0 for o in out) / n_req for j in range(n_tok)] def main(): ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--device", default="cuda") ap.add_argument("--n-req", type=int, default=100000) a = ap.parse_args() for block, fresh in [(False, False), (True, False), (True, True)]: m = run(block, fresh, a.n_req, device=a.device) name = f"{'block' if block else 'standard'}, {'fresh' if fresh else 'fixed'} seed" print(f"{name:22s} P(token j = 0), j = 0..5:", " ".join(f"{x:.4f}" for x in m)) print("exact: 0.5 at every j") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` On a T4 with 10^6 requests I get: ```text standard, fixed seed P(token j = 0), j = 0..5: 0.5012 0.5000 0.5001 0.4999 0.4994 0.5005 block, fixed seed P(token j = 0), j = 0..5: 0.5012 0.5003 0.4167 0.4862 0.4694 0.4661 block, fresh seed P(token j = 0), j = 0..5: 0.5012 0.5006 0.5005 0.4989 0.5008 0.4998 exact: 0.5 at every j ``` "fixed seed" is what the runner does (one seed per request). Changing only the seed every round removes the bias, so the cause is the reuse of the position-keyed uniforms. Token 0 is the prefill token, which doesn't go through verification. On main 1dfe9fbdae73 under the Triton interpreter (20000 requests) I get the same pattern: .506 .498 .415 .486 .461 .466, which is 24σ off at the third token. End to end it shows up the same way. With a tiny context-free model (p = (1/2, 1/2)), a draft model that always proposes the same token, gamma = 2 and 10000 samples on the T4, block verification rejects the correct output law (chi-square 3152, df 64, p ≈ 0) and fits the law the kernel above predicts (p = .48), while standard verification on the same models fits the correct law (p = .87). With probabilistic drafts (p = (.3, .7), q = (.7, .3)) block mode gives P(third token = a) = .3509 instead of .30. With the same kernel and freshly drawn drafts it is .3003 there, so in that case the extra bias comes from the draft Gumbel noise, which is keyed the same way by (seed, position). Code, at f26d9f432ced (byte-identical to v0.31.0 for the lines below): - one seed per request: [rejection_sampler_utils.py#L547](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f26d9f432ced7b1087d02d29bffed2249df1a18e/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler_utils.py#L547) - uniform from (seed, position): [#L567-L569](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f26d9f432ced7b1087d02d29bffed2249df1a18e/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler_utils.py#L567-L569) - block mode reads it on every row and keeps verifying past a failed row: [#L595-L627](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f26d9f432ced7b1087d02d29bffed2249df1a18e/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler_utils.py#L595-L627) - draft noise from (seed, position + constant salt): [gumbel.py#L192-L193](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f26d9f432ced7b1087d02d29bffed2249df1a18e/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/gumbel.py#L192-L193), called from [speculator.py#L439-L449](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f26d9f432ced7b1087d02d29bffed2249df1a18e/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py#L439-L449) Standard verification stops reading uniforms at the first rejection, so a uniform it has read is never read again for a new decision. That is why only block mode is affected. Related: #47386 (closed) noted in its description that re-proposals at the same position reuse that position's draft key across steps, and #54282 decoupled the draft and target noise within a round. Neither covers the acceptance uniform in block mode. Suggested fix: it might be enough to mix something that changes every verification step into the uniform's offset (for example a per-request step counter), and the same for the draft noise. In the script, a fresh seed per round is exact. --- AI-assisted: found, reproduced and written up with Claude.

title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Transfer DeepSeek-V4.1 packed MLA rows whole
body:
## Overview

> **Stacked on #61074.** Only the last commit (`c673ff04e9`) belongs to this PR: +8/−4 in `base_worker.py`, and one test case.

#61074 registers packed MLA rows as one NIXL region, but DeepSeek-V4.1 does not reach that path: its compressor-state `CircularBufferSpec` ring sets `_is_csa_linear`, which forces `packed_storage=False`. This PR replaces that gate with the property it was protecting, so DSV4.1 transfers whole rows.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D (pull): about 11k → about 430 NIXL descriptors and 179 → 104 MB per 100k-token transfer. GSM8K does not change.
- No other model changes behavior: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Mamba) and non-MLA models keep per-layer regions.

## Validation

GB200, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 1P1D, TP4 + TP4, NIXL pull, BLHNC. The bench uses random 100k-token prompts, 16 output tokens, and concurrency 1 and 4. GSM8K is 5-shot, temp 0, concurrency 512, run twice so that pass 2 hits the prefix cache on both P and D.

| | main | this PR (on #61074) |
|---|---:|---:|
| descriptors / 100k transfer | 11,118 | 426–455 |
| MB / 100k transfer | 179.2 | 103.6 |
| avg xfer time, 100k | 4.56 ms | 2.83 ms |
| avg post time, 100k | 1.10 ms | 0.30 ms |
| TTFT p50, 100k, conc 1 / 4 | 1078 / 3339 ms | 1057 / 3426 ms |
| GSM8K flexible-extract, pass 1 / pass 2 | 0.924 / 0.927 | 0.922 / 0.922 |

GSM8K varies by ±0.6 pt between runs of identical code (14 runs: 0.920–0.933). Each column above is one run; earlier runs of the same change gave the same descriptor counts.

**Push mode.** NixlPushConnector, same setup, GSM8K pass 1 / pass 2 = 0.930 / 0.923, with 0 failed transfers. In a separate diagnostic run, I checksummed every pushed row with async GPU reductions and no CPU sync, at P hand-off, at P WRITE completion and at D receipt. All three matched: 2800/2800 and 2965/2965.

**Unit tests.** `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/{test_nixl_desc_geometry,test_hisparse_connector,test_nixl_push_connector,test_nixl_connector,test_nixl_connector_hma}.py -k "not ray"`: 602 passed. The new `v41-aliased-groups` case of `test_register_packed_dsv4_mla_cache_as_single_region` fails on #61074 alone and passes here. The deselected `ray` case also fails on main, because the environment has no reachable Ray address.

## Details

**Root cause.** DSV4.1 packs all layers into one shared storage with a 135,168-byte block row. Seven transfer groups alias each row from byte 0: five SWA groups, the compressed MLA + indexer group, and the compressor-state ring. `_is_csa_linear` was added for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (#53896) and is true when any group is a `CircularBufferSpec`. It sets `packed_storage=False`, so DSV4.1 registers per-layer regions. Those regions overlap, and the `_SHARED_REGION_GROUP_ID` ones are read for the blocks of every group. The result is about 14 overlapping descriptors per block.

**Fix.** A row may transfer whole only if every page in it is replicated across TP ranks: MLA without SSM state. The gate is now `use_mla and not _has_mamba` instead of `not _is_csa_linear`. The ring itself is TP-replicated, so it never needed the exclusion. What the exclusion really protected was Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's head-sharded attention and SSM state; `_has_mamba` still excludes that model.

**Behavior by model.**

| model | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1 (MLA + `CircularBufferSpec` ring) | per-layer regions | whole rows (#61074 path) |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (CSA + Mamba) | per-layer | per-layer (`_has_mamba`) |
| GLM-5.3-Flash (KDA Mamba) | per-layer | per-layer (`_has_mamba`) |
| non-MLA target with an MLA draft, BLHNC | MLA draft layers took whole rows that also hold head-sharded target pages | per-layer (`use_mla`) |
| other packed MLA (V4.0, GLM-5.3) | #61074 path | unchanged |

The non-MLA row is the only other behavior change. On #61074, such a row also carries the target's head-sharded pages, so transferring it whole is wrong under heterogeneous TP.

**Limitation.** On #61074 only MLA layers join the whole-row region. A ring page that does not start at byte 0 keeps its own region. DSV4.1 holds one ring block per request, so this adds two descriptors per request.

**Versioning.** The metadata schema does not change. Mixed versions fail at handshake because the region counts differ; they do not silently transfer wrong bytes.

---

title: [Attention] Remove cascade attention
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Remove cascade attention from vLLM: its kernels, heuristics, metadata, scheduler/KV-cache plumbing, model-runner logic, config/flag handling, tests, and docs.

Cascade attention has been opt-in (`disable_cascade_attn=True` by default), already hard-disabled for FlashInfer (see #25679), force-disabled for async spec decode / DBO / batch invariance / CPU, and unsupported by most backends — yet it still costs a per-step scheduler scan, branches in the model runner and backends, and recurring bugs (#55674, #47183, #39208, #55227, #53690 are open fixes/workarounds that this PR makes moot).

**This PR is non-breaking for hardware plugins.** Plugin-facing APIs (`build(common_prefix_len, ...)`, `SchedulerOutput.num_common_prefix_blocks`, etc.) are kept as deprecated no-ops; a follow-up PR removes them once plugin maintainers have been notified.

## Claims

- No behavior change for default configurations (cascade was off by default); net **-901 lines in `vllm/`** (+504 / -1,405; most `+` lines are de-indentation in the FA/AITER forward paths after removing the cascade branch).
- The scheduler no longer scans the running request's blocks every step.
- Out-of-tree plugins keep working unchanged (checked against vllm-ascend, tpu-inference, vllm-gaudi, vllm-spyre, vllm-metal).
- `--disable-cascade-attn` / `disable_cascade_attn=` still parse; they warn and have no effect (to be removed in v0.33.0, same schedule as `--log-config-file`).

## Validation

**Accuracy** — GSM8K 5-shot, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`, GB200, default backend:

| | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 0.5906 ± 0.0135 | 0.5345 ± 0.0137 |
| this PR | 0.5906 ± 0.0135 | 0.5345 ± 0.0137 |

```bash
lm_eval --model vllm --model_args pretrained=Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct,gpu_memory_utilization=0.4,max_model_len=4096 --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto
```

**Shared-prefix batch** (the workload cascade targeted; same setup as the deleted `test_cascade_attention.py`): `Qwen/Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct`, >1K-token shared prefix, 64 identical greedy requests vs. 1 reference request → 64/64 identical outputs on both `FLASH_ATTN` and `FLASHINFER` (FlashInfer autotune disabled).

**Unit tests** — rows other than the last ran on the first commit (full removal); the second commit only re-adds the no-op shims, and the last row re-runs core suites on the final revision. (GB200; `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1` for a local cubin version mismatch; writable `HF_HOME` for the sliding-window tests):

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| Scheduler / KV cache / prefix caching / cudagraph dispatch / arg utils / CPU platform / KV connectors / GPU model runner / mamba utils / simple KV offload | 923 passed, 22 failed — the same 22 fail identically on `main` here (`test_cpu.py` needs a CPU-only host; one PP test needs 3 GPUs; EC-connector priority tests) |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py` | 151 passed, 7 skipped (incl. 18/18 sliding-window correctness) |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k small` | 84 passed, 300 skipped |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -k small` | 576 passed, 192 skipped |
| Other builder/runner suites (GDN, mamba2, linear, kpool, mm_prefix, trtllm, rocm selection, attn_utils, flex, prefix_prefill, kda, qsa, fusion) | 596 passed, 226 skipped, 42 failed — all 42 are `test_prefix_prefill.py::test_contexted_kv_attention*`, which fail identically on `main` here (Triton `OutOfResources`: tensor memory 656 > 512 on GB200) |
| Compat-shim commit: scheduler / KV cache / runner / attention backends / builders | 996 passed, 84 skipped, 8 failed — all 8 also fail on `main` here (6 EC-connector priority tests; 2 PP tests needing more GPUs than the 1 visible) |

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_dispatch.py tests/platforms/test_cpu.py \
  tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_connector_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_prefill_tail_classification.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k small
```
</details>

## Details

- **Config / CLI:** removed every place that read or force-set `disable_cascade_attn` (`VllmConfig` for async spec decode, batch invariance, DBO; `CpuPlatform`) and the "no piecewise cudagraph for cascade" warning.
- **Scheduler / KV cache:** the scheduler no longer computes common prefix blocks; `get_num_common_prefix_blocks` is removed from the coordinators and all single-type managers.
- **Model runner (V1):** removed `_compute_cascade_attn_prefix_len(s)`, cascade-driven FULL-cudagraph exclusion, and the cascade-only `num_sms` / `_init_device_properties`, `num_query_heads`, `use_alibi`. MRV2 never used cascade.
- **Backends:** removed `cascade_attention()` / `use_cascade_attention()` from FlashAttention (and diffkv), `MultiLevelCascadeAttentionWrapper` from FlashInfer, and `use_cascade` / prefix–suffix metadata fields and branches from Triton, ROCm, ROCm AITER FA/unified, segmented, flex, CPU, and `CacheOnlyAttention`. `merge_attn_states` is unaffected (still covered by `test_merge_attn_states.py`).
- **Tests / docs:** deleted `test_cascade_flash_attn.py` and `test_cascade_attention.py` (and the system-message fixture/data only the latter used); updated `docs/design/cuda_graphs.md`.

**Kept as deprecated no-ops for out-of-tree plugins** (removed in a follow-up):

| API | Used by |
|---|---|
| `AttentionMetadataBuilder.build(common_prefix_len, ...)` (always 0) | ~20 vllm-ascend builders, tpu-inference, Cambricon, MetaX, Enflame |
| `SchedulerOutput.num_common_prefix_blocks` (now last field, defaults to `[]`) | vllm-ascend, tpu-inference, vllm-gaudi, vllm-spyre |
| `KVCacheManager.get_num_common_prefix_blocks()` (returns zeros) | vllm-ascend custom schedulers |
| `GPUModelRunner.cascade_attn_enabled = False`, `_determine_batch_execution_and_padding(use_cascade_attn=...)` (ignored) | vllm-ascend `NPUModelRunner` |
| `ModelConfig.disable_cascade_attn` (no effect) | vllm-ascend, vllm-metal |

**Known plugin impact:** the cascade fields of vLLM's attention metadata dataclasses (`use_cascade`, `common_prefix_len`, `cu_prefix_query_lens`, `prefix_kv_lens`, `suffix_kv_lens`, `prefix_scheduler_metadata`) are removed. Cambricon vllm-mlu's `MLUFlashAttentionMetadata(FlashAttentionMetadata)` passes them and will need to drop them when it moves to a release containing this PR (it currently tracks vLLM releases, not main). Enflame vllm-gcu pins `vllm==0.11.0` and is unaffected.

**Tradeoffs:** users who explicitly opted in with `--no-disable-cascade-attn` lose the heuristic-gated, FA-only cascade speedup for large shared-prefix batches. No new CPU/GPU syncs (the Triton/ROCm cascade paths' `seq_lens.cpu()` and FlashInfer's cascade-forced `seq_lens_cpu` requirement are gone). vllm-ascend's service-profiling config references `GPUModelRunner._compute_cascade_attn_prefix_lens`; that entry only matters when that profiler is enabled.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

title: [Core] Expose prefix reuse policy in KV cache group metadata
body:
## Overview

External prefix-cache-aware routers cannot determine a group's prefix reuse policy from its attention kind alone. This PR exposes `prefix_cacheable` and `prefix_replay_tokens` from the resolved spec through `EngineCore.get_kv_cache_group_metadata()`.

## Claims

- Report whether each group participates in prefix caching and its required tail replay length.
- Cover KpoolTail, Sliding MLA with bounded replay on/off, and uniform-type wrappers in the existing CPU metadata suite.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q \
  tests/v1/engine/test_kv_cache_group_metadata.py
.venv/bin/ruff check vllm/v1/engine/core.py tests/v1/engine/test_kv_cache_group_metadata.py
.venv/bin/ruff format --check vllm/v1/engine/core.py tests/v1/engine/test_kv_cache_group_metadata.py
git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD
```

Result: **5 passed**, including the existing DCP effective-block-size test. Omitting the added fields caused all 4 new cases to fail with `KeyError: 'prefix_cacheable'`. Ruff and whitespace checks passed.

Validation ran in CPU mode with Python 3.12.3 and PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. Model evaluation is not applicable to this metadata-only addition.

## Details

KpoolTail is classified as sliding-window attention but has `prefix_cacheable=False`. Bounded-replay Sliding MLA also opts out of shared prefix lookup and declares a replay window. These properties let external consumers identify participating groups and account for replay when estimating reuse benefits.

Related to [#48121](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48121), which expands canonical metadata and frontend access. Its current diff does not include these two prefix-policy properties; this PR adds only those fields to the existing RPC.

AI assistance was used to prepare the implementation and tests.

title: [Bugfix] DeepSeek-V4.1 parser: tolerate drifted DSML tool-call openers
body:
## Overview

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash can emit DSML tool-call blocks with a `parameter`-style tool-name opener and no outer `calls` wrapper. This change lets the V4.1 parser return structured tool calls for those variants instead of exposing the block as plain content.

## Claims

- Recognize canonical `invoke`, DSML-prefixed `parameter`, and bare `parameter` tool-name openers in the existing V4.1 parser configuration.
- Close reasoning and start a tool call when the block arrives without a preceding `</think>` marker.
- Cover streaming, non-streaming, thinking on/off, and small-chunk parsing in the existing V4.1 regression suite.

## Validation

Validation was rerun after merging upstream `main` at `6a70913` on October 12, 2026:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py -q
30 passed, 1 warning

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files vllm/parser/deepseek_v41.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py
Passed

git diff --check
git diff --cached --check
Passed
```

The warning reports missing generated `vllm._version` metadata in the source checkout.

For a before/after reproducer, the new tests were also run against the unmodified V4.1 parser from upstream `main`, keeping the PR's test file:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py -k drifted -q
7 failed, 3 passed, 20 deselected
```

The seven failures cover both parameter-style openers in streaming and non-streaming parsing, plus the missing reasoning-end case. Restoring this PR's parser makes the complete suite pass.

These are deterministic parser replay tests using the repository's existing mock tokenizer. No live DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model-serving or GPU evaluation was performed in this follow-up; the original production failure report motivated the fixtures. Upstream Buildkite validation and human review are still pending. The parser tests are included by the existing `pytest -v -s parser` step in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`.

## Details

The canonical V4.1 invoke opener can already be recognized from `CONTENT` without the outer wrapper. The missing pieces are recognition of the two parameter-style opener variants and an `INVOKE_PREFIX` transition directly from `REASONING`. The fix extends the existing configuration inherited from `deepseek_v4_config`; it adds no parser engine or serving-layer implementation.

Related work: #52645 addresses DeepSeek V4 missing/malformed outer wrappers with provisional recovery, tool-name validation, and rollback. This PR targets V4.1's different DSML spelling and parameter-style tool-name openers. It does not implement or replace #52645's broader recovery policy. Bare parameter text remains ambiguous when it appears as prose; this patch retains the existing parser's acceptance policy rather than adding a new validation layer.

AI assistance: Codex assisted with this follow-up's branch synchronization, source inspection, regression validation, and PR-description update. The original parser implementation and test changes were not modified by this follow-up. The submitting human remains responsible for understanding the implementation and validating the affected serving deployment.
