title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Preserve target-only tokens with narrower draft vocabularies
body:
﻿## Overview

Fix probabilistic rejection sampling when the draft vocabulary is narrower than the target vocabulary in both Model Runner V1 and V2, including the CPU V1 fallback.

Fixes #61112.
Fixes #61113.

## Claims

- Treat q(token) as zero for target-only token IDs without materializing padded draft tensors.
- Prevent V1 GPU and CPU kernels from reading narrow draft-probability rows with the target row width.
- Keep the CPU override, C++ signatures, and Torch operator schemas aligned with the V1 dispatch arguments.
- Preserve the full target vocabulary in V2 ordinary, block, and watermarked recovery.
- Keep equal-width, one-hot, greedy, and synthetic verification behavior unchanged.

## Validation

### CUDA

Hardware: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050, 8 GB; Torch 2.13.0+cu130; Python 3.12.

Command: `python -m pytest -q tests/v1/sample/test_rejection_sampler.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py`

Result: **137 passed**.

The narrow-vocabulary V2 regression is parameterized over standard and block verification. The watermarked path has separate coverage.

Independent 50,000-request CUDA evaluations used target probabilities `[0.5, 0.3, 0.2]` and narrower draft probabilities `[0.3, 0.7]`:

| Runner | Observed first-token frequencies |
|---|---|
| V1 | `[0.4976, 0.3003, 0.2021]` |
| V2 | `[0.5001, 0.2991, 0.2008]` |

Both recover the target-only token and match the target distribution within the predeclared 0.015 absolute tolerance.

### CPU

Built the editable CPU extension under WSL with Python 3.12 and Torch 2.13.0+cpu, including the `_C`, `_C_AVX2`, and `_C_AVX512` variants.

For the dispatch-order follow-up, Triton was removed from the isolated CPU environment and `HAS_TRITON=False` was confirmed before running:

Command: `python -m pytest -q tests/v1/e2e/test_cpu_spec_decode.py::test_cpu_rejection_sampler_supports_narrow_draft_probs`

Result: **1 passed**.

The regression launches both kernels through `KernelOverride` using the original Triton argument names, then executes the genuine CPU C++ fallback. It covers positional forwarding, residual recovery of a target-only token, and acceptance handling of a draft token ID outside the draft probability width. Static signature validation also confirms that both CPU override orders exactly match their Triton kernels.

### Static checks

Command: `pre-commit run --files csrc/cpu/spec_decode_utils.cpp csrc/cpu/torch_bindings.cpp vllm/utils/cpu_triton_utils.py tests/v1/e2e/test_cpu_spec_decode.py`

All applicable hooks passed, including ruff, formatting, clang-format, mypy, test tethering, SPDX, forbidden imports, CUDA API checks, Docker graph validation, suggestions, and DCO sign-off.

A representative review microcheck showed that padding a 128 x 5 x 66 BF16 V2 buffer to width 50,257 allocated 61.3 MiB and cost about 1.67 ms per call. The final implementation performs masked in-kernel loads and introduces no padded allocation.

## Details

The V1 kernels used the target vocabulary width as the draft row stride and residual-loop bound. Narrow draft tensors therefore caused cross-row and out-of-bounds reads. The fix passes the real draft stride and width to the acceptance and recovery kernels and returns zero for out-of-range draft probabilities.

The CPU override and C++ Torch operator schemas now accept the same dispatch arguments. The C++ acceptance path treats an out-of-range draft token as having zero draft probability, while the residual loop reads draft probabilities only below `draft_vocab_size`.

V2 previously truncated the target vocabulary to the draft width. The first patch corrected the distribution by padding the full max-capacity draft-logit buffer on every verification call, but that introduced substantial steady-state allocation and copy overhead. The final fix instead threads the draft width through the logits-statistics, acceptance, block-verification, residual, and resampling kernels and masks draft loads beyond that width to negative infinity.

The change adds no host reads, device synchronization, public API, or documentation requirement. Model Runner V1 is included because #61113 demonstrates incorrect and potentially out-of-bounds behavior on deployments that still require that runner; Model Runner V2 is independently affected by #61112.

This does not duplicate #42775. That PR adds opt-in model-loading and output masking for suffix-compatible `draft_model` pairs. This PR repairs rejection sampling for already-produced narrow probabilistic tensors, including EAGLE-style heads, in both runner implementations.

AI assistance was used to review and refine this change. The human submitter reviewed every changed line, ran the listed CUDA and CPU tests, and is responsible for the implementation.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Refresh block verification RNG per round
body:
﻿<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes the cross-round RNG reuse that biases V2 block verification at nonzero temperature. Closes #61114.

No open PR found by issue-number search addresses this bug; the broader speculative-decoding search results are unrelated feature/model work.

## Claims

- Gives each block-verification round a request-local RNG stream keyed by its starting position.
- Applies the round key to acceptance uniforms and probabilistic draft Gumbel noise, including the shared DFlash2/LiLiCorr candidate walk and watermark fallback.
- Preserves existing standard-verification RNG streams and batch invariance.

## Validation

- Exact issue reproducer encoded as a 100,000-request CUDA regression; all five generated positions remain within `0.01` of the expected `P(token=0) = 0.5`.
- Full neighboring CUDA suites:
  - `python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_gumbel_sample.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py`
  - Result: `83 passed`.
- End-to-end V2 generation on an NVIDIA RTX 3050:
  - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`
  - Config: n-gram drafter, `num_speculative_tokens=2`, `rejection_sample_method="block"`, temperature `0.8`, 16 output tokens.
  - Result: engine initialized with the V2 runner and completed generation successfully.
- Full DFlash2/LiLiCorr CUDA suites: `52 passed`.
- Full Gumbel-watermark and rejection-sampler CUDA suites: `87 passed`.
- The focused multi-round candidate-walk and non-null watermark round-key tests: `3 passed`.
- All changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, test tethering, SPDX, and import-policy checks.

## Details

Block verification evaluates every draft row, including rows after the ultimately accepted prefix. Those uniforms become conditioned on the current round's outcome. Keying them only by `(seed, absolute_position)` reuses that conditioned randomness when a later round revisits the same position. Probabilistic draft Gumbel draws have the same cross-round problem.

The fix mixes the round's starting position into the request seed. That position strictly advances after every round, is available to both drafting and verification, and is independent of batch composition. The extra work is one integer mix in block mode, with no CPU/GPU synchronization or mutable per-request counter. Standard verification remains unchanged.

title: [Bug]: Cross-request context contamination via shared-prefix KV reuse in PD disaggregation with automatic prefix caching — clean with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`
body:
## Summary

With automatic prefix caching enabled (the default) in a NIXL prefill/decode disaggregated deployment serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, responses intermittently contain **content from other requests** — cross-request context contamination ("crosstalk"). We have a scriptable reproducer on `/v1/chat/completions` (details below): with a long **identical shared prefix** across requests, 46/48 *sequential* requests returned another request's canary code; at concurrency 128 it was 122/128. Disabling prefix caching on the prefill node **and** all decode nodes (`--no-enable-prefix-caching`) eliminated the contamination.

## Deployment topology (at reproduction time)

```
Clients (multi-turn agent sessions; every request starts with the same large system prompt)
        |
        v
vllm-router 0.1.15  --policy round_robin --kv-connector nixl   (port 30000)
        |
   +----+------------------+
   v                       v
Prefill node              2x Decode nodes
1x node, 8x H100, TP=8    1x node each, 8x H100, TP=8
kv_producer  :8001        kv_consumer  :8002
        \____ NIXL KV transfer ____/
```

(Since 2026-10-12 we run 2P1D; all reproduction data below was collected on the 1P2D topology above.)

## Environment

- vLLM 0.31.0, built from main @ `db9527a46` (2026-10-02), local build tagged `+cu129`; torch 2.13.0+cu129, transformers 5.17.0, nixl 1.4.1
- Driver 550.54.15, nodes of 8× H100 80GB (sm90)
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (1M context), `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` attention backend, block size 64
- Speculative decoding: `{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":true}`
- `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 32 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`
- Note: PR #57662 (fix for #57661) was **not merged** at the time of writing, so this build cannot contain it.

## Symptom

Every request shares a long common prefix — in the wild this was Claude Code on the Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` endpoint, whose fixed large system prompt is identical across all sessions. With automatic prefix caching on, users in **different, unrelated sessions** intermittently received responses containing content from *another* session (the model "remembered" details, file names, or instructions belonging to someone else's conversation). Affected requests completed with HTTP 200; no errors or warnings in server logs.

## Reproducer (scriptable, `/v1/chat/completions`)

Design: N requests, each consisting of a **long identical shared prefix** plus a per-request distinct tail that embeds a unique canary code. After all responses complete, each output is scanned for canary codes belonging to *other* requests ("foreign" hits).

Results with automatic prefix caching **enabled** (default):

| Scenario | Requests | Outputs containing a foreign canary code |
|---|---|---|
| Sequential (C=1) | 48 | **46/48** |
| Concurrent (C=128) | 128 | **122/128** |

Key observations:

- Concurrency is **not** required — sequential single-stream requests contaminate at ~96%. Sharing a long identical prefix is the trigger.
- Canaries that varied the prefix, or shared only long *suffixes*, did **not** reproduce; earlier negative canary results were a design gap, not evidence against the bug.
- With `--no-enable-prefix-caching` on P **and** both D nodes: 0 foreign hits, and the Claude Code symptom disappeared entirely (verified by the same users plus a 16-way concurrent keepalive, ~3,000 rounds over 17 h).

The canary script is available on request.

## What we have *not* isolated

- We disabled prefix caching on all three nodes at once, so we cannot attribute the reuse to the prefill-side cache, the decode-side cache, or the P↔D KV-transfer interplay (e.g. a consumer trusting producer block IDs for freed/reused blocks, or refcount/eviction asymmetry between P and D).
- No root-cause analysis on the vLLM side yet; happy to invest in narrowing this down with maintainer guidance.

## Hypothesis (unverified)

Under PD disaggregation, prefix-cache blocks belonging to a completed request are re-served to a later request that hashes to the same shared prefix, but the physical KV content behind those blocks has been freed/reassigned — so the later request decodes against another request's KV. The serial (C=1) repro suggests the race is between request completion/reuse bookkeeping rather than simultaneous scheduling.

## Why this is not #57661

#57661 (and fix PR #57662 — still unmerged) describes NIXL transfer regions deduplicated by `base_addr` alone, truncating the compressor `state_cache` transfer for hybrid-attention layers, producing **garbled/empty output**. Our failure mode is different:

1. Symptom: our outputs are coherent but contain **another request's content**; we never observed garbling or empty content/reasoning fields.
2. Toggle sensitivity: our contamination disappears completely with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`; the region-geometry bug in #57661 is independent of the prefix-caching toggle.
3. Mechanism: truncated/misaligned compressor state cannot inject well-formed content from a different request.

We plan to validate our repro against #57662's branch as well, to rule out any interaction; both issues affect the same model + NIXL PD combination with silent HTTP-200 failures.

## Related issues

- #57661 — NIXL P/D silent output corruption (hybrid-attention region dedup), fix PR #57662 (unmerged at writing)
- #56009 — request/response cross-talk symptom, no root cause identified
- #52627 — silent output corruption in 1P1D NIXL PD, different connector combination
- #47930 — DSpark draft acceptance collapse with automatic prefix caching (another prefix-caching × disaggregation interaction)

## Offer

We keep a H100 1P2D/2P1D testbed with this exact model and can: share the canary script, run targeted repro attempts on candidate patches (including #57662), or provide `collect_env.py` output on request.

title: [Bug]: custom all-reduce creates its NVLink multicast reduce-scatter buffer mid-serving (not at startup); the run then crashes (Xid + CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED)
body:
## Summary

In `CustomAllreduce` (`vllm/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce.py`), the NVLink-multicast ("multimem") reduce-scatter buffer is not created at startup. It is created the first time a reduce-scatter of a particular size happens, which can be many minutes into serving. On our 8× B300 node, the two runs that took this path both crashed right after the buffer was created. The many runs that never took it ran clean.

## Background

On NVLink-connected GPUs (MNNVL), custom all-reduce can run reduce-scatter on a low-SM "multimem" kernel. That kernel needs a dedicated multicast buffer: device memory mapped into an NVLink multicast object shared by all ranks. The other MNNVL buffers are set up when the communicator is constructed. This one is not.

## What the code does

1. `_select_reduce_scatter_backend` (`custom_all_reduce.py:621` on main at `242e4213f`) picks the `mnnvl_multimem` backend only when the reduce-scatter input is **larger than 16 MiB and at most 64 MiB**. These are `_DEFAULT_MNNVL_REDUCE_SCATTER_MAX_SIZE` and `_DEFAULT_MNNVL_MULTIMEM_REDUCE_SCATTER_MAX_SIZE` (lines 132–133).
2. The first time it picks that backend, it calls `_init_mnnvl_multimem_reduce_scatter_buffer()` (line 674). That allocates and maps the multicast buffer **in the middle of serving**, while other kernels and CUDA graphs are running.
3. It then logs `Using the low-SM MNNVL multimem reduce-scatter kernel.` (line 682).

Whether a run ever lands in the 16–64 MiB window depends on how many tokens are batched at runtime. So the same deployment can hit this path in one run and not in another. The two thresholds are hard-coded defaults; there is no setting to change them.

## What we observed

- **Setup:** 8× NVIDIA B300 (sm_103), one node with NVSwitch. NCCL 2.30.7, torch 2.13.0+cu130. Kimi-K3 with TP=8 + expert parallel + decode-context-parallel 8, MegaMoE, CUDA graphs on.
- **Run 1:** the log line above appeared 13–14 minutes into the run. In the same second the GPU raised an NVML Xid error and cuBLAS failed with `CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED`, and the engine died.
- **Run 2:** same log line at the same point, then `EngineDeadError`.
- **Every other run on the same GPUs** (dozens, same config family) never logged that line and finished cleanly. ECC errors stayed at 0 and there were no row remaps, so a faulty GPU is unlikely.

We have not proven causation. The lazy buffer creation is the only code path unique to the two failing runs, and it ran immediately before the fault.

## Suggested fix

Do either of these:
- Create the multimem reduce-scatter buffer at communicator setup, like the other MNNVL buffers, so it never happens during serving.
- Make the two size thresholds configurable, so a deployment can stay out of the 16–64 MiB window without disabling custom collectives altogether.

title: [ROCm][DSv4] Enable EPLB on AITER MegaMoE
body:
## Summary
- AITER MegaMoE no longer rejects `--enable-eplb`.
- Physical expert slots follow the DeepGEMM placement: routed experts, then redundant copies. `(n_routed + num_redundant_experts)` must divide the EP size.
- Logical top-k ids are mapped to physical ids before MegaMoEV2, and EPLB swaps the shuffled MXFP4 rows in place.

## Test plan
- [x] `python -m py_compile` on the three changed files
- [ ] `pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_aiter_mega_moe.py -m cpu_test` (not run here: this machine has no vLLM test env)
- [ ] 8x MI355X, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, same MegaMoE flags, A/B with EPLB off vs `--enable-eplb --eplb-config '{num_redundant_experts:32,step_interval:200,log_balancedness:true}'`. Bench 8k/1k at concurrency 512. The load log should move from about 0.71 to about 0.97 after the first rebalance. Do not compare absolute tok/s with SGLang.

The 8-GPU run is not in this PR.

title: [Perf][Attention] FlashInfer prefill for DiffKV attention on SM12x
body:
## Overview On SM12x (RTX 50 series, RTX PRO 6000, DGX Spark/GB10) there is no FA3/FA4, so DiffKV models (K/V head sizes differ; MiMo-V2: 192/128) run every attention step on `TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV`. This PR adds `TRITON_FLASHINFER_DIFFKV`, built with the existing `create_composite_attention_backend`. It routes batches that contain a prefill on plain causal full-attention layers to FlashInfer's paged prefill (`head_dim_vo`), using the same packed cache. Decode-only and verification-only batches, and all CUDA graph capture and replay, stay on `TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV`. Related: - #58177 and #59673 optimize the Triton DiffKV kernel. They are complementary and are benchmarked against below. - #59052 pins Triton DiffKV to `UNIFORM_BATCH` CUDA graphs, the same support level this composite reports. - #46963 also uses FlashInfer prefill on SM12x. ## Claims All on DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), MiMo-V2.6-Flash. - **Prefill attention, one full-attention layer at TP2,** vs Triton DiffKV with #58177 + #59673 applied. Cold-L2 CUDA-graph timing; `plan()` host time is reported separately below. - 2.27–2.29× for 512+-token chunks over a 32K prefix; - 2.17× for a fresh 8K chunk, 1.84× fresh 2K, 1.24× fresh 512; - 3.07× for 64 tokens and 6.41× for 17 tokens over a 32K prefix; - slower for fresh chunks of ≤64 tokens: 0.45–0.83×, i.e. 1.2–3.6 µs per layer. - **End to end on the PR base** (main `18c19eaf2` with and without this PR): cold-prefill TTFT at 96K tokens goes from 72.3 s to 40.6 s (**1.78×**); 1.46× at 48K, 1.23× at 24K. - Single-request decode is unchanged. - Fresh 23–34-token prompts are 2–6 ms slower at p50 (1–4%); 66–515-token prompts are 4–10 ms faster. - **Accuracy:** no observed degradation in gsm8k or full-vocabulary logprobs. - **Cost:** on this configuration the KV cache is 0.59 GiB smaller (6.6% fewer tokens), mostly from FlashInfer's workspace (details below). - **Off switch:** `VLLM_DIFFKV_FLASHINFER_PREFILL=0` restores `TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV` for every layer. ## Validation **Not a duplicate.** I searched open and closed PRs for `diffkv flashinfer`, `DiffKV FlashInfer prefill`, `TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV`, `diffkv sm120` and `MiMo FlashInfer prefill`. None route DiffKV attention to FlashInfer. ### Environments The hardware is GB10 throughout. SM120 (RTX 5090 / RTX PRO 6000) is **not validated**; confirmation from an SM120 owner is requested. | label | vLLM | FlashInfer | used for | |---|---|---|---| | **PR base** | main `18c19eaf2` precompiled cu130 aarch64 wheel; "+PR" adds this PR's Python files (the PR changes no compiled code) | 0.7.0.post1 (main's pin) | tests, layer timing, end-to-end A/B, short-prompt TTFT | | **rebased** | this PR as `c379d3fab` on main `74f4404f5`, run from the main `fe4df3df0` wheel (one unrelated commit earlier) + this PR's files | 0.7.0.post1 | tests, serving re-check | | **old base** | `7f1a539` + this change (plus a local `max_decode_query_len` shim) | 0.6.18.post1 | gsm8k, logprobs, mixed load | - **Shared stack:** torch 2.13.0+cu130 and triton 3.7.1. The MoE backend is b12x 1.5.0, which needs `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` 4.7.1 (main pins 4.8.0); this only affects the MoE path. - **Model:** `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD` @ `2479e2d0029e`. - **Server:** ```bash vllm serve MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD --tensor-parallel-size 2 --nnodes 2 \ --distributed-executor-backend mp --gpu-memory-utilization 0.87 \ --max-model-len 300000 --max-num-seqs 16 --moe-backend b12x \ --no-async-scheduling --trust-remote-code --generation-config vllm \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD/dflash","num_speculative_tokens":7}' ``` - **Video profiling:** on the PR base both arms also pass `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video": 0}'`. Main's encoder profiling with a maximum-size video exhausted GB10's unified memory during startup and hung the GPU driver, independent of this PR. All workloads below are text-only. - **Rebase:** #57169 removed `set_kernel_block_size()` from the metadata builder base class; the builder now takes its page size from `kv_cache_spec.block_size`, as other builders on main do. - **Memory on the rebased base:** at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.87`, main `fe4df3df0` + PR sized the KV cache at 20.05 GiB, compared with 18.42 GiB for `18c19eaf2` + PR with the same flags. Host MemAvailable then fell below 3 GB during startup warmup, and my watchdog stopped the server. The re-check therefore ran at 0.85. I did not measure main without this PR on this base, so the cause of the larger KV cache is not isolated. ### Tests ```bash pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_diffkv_prefill.py ``` | environment | result | |---|---| | rebased (main `fe4df3df0` + PR), FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 | **99 passed** | | PR base (+PR), FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 | **99 passed** | | old base, FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1 | 98 passed, 1 failed | The old-base failure is `test_layer_eligibility[kwargs3]` (FP8 KV), which needs #58128 (on main). **Numerics.** The backend's own plan/run is checked against an FP32 PyTorch reference, because the existing DiffKV test needs FA3/FA4 and skips on SM12x. - Inputs: - a scattered block table; - physical layouts HND / NHD, each with and without layer interleaving; - block sizes 16 and 64; - a fresh 2K prompt, 2K over an 8K prefix, 256 over a 32K prefix, and 17 over an 8K prefix; - a mixed batch with decode rows. - Checks: `assert_close(atol=rtol=2e-2)` and relative L2 < 1e-2. - An FP16 subset covers both layouts. **Behavior** tests check: - auto-selection and its fallbacks: sinks, sliding window, FP8 KV, unvalidated head sizes, and the opt-out variable; - per-layer eligibility on real impls; - `host_seq_lens` for pure-prefill (no readback) and mixed speculative batches (exact lengths); - that the capture variant is Triton for uniform batches up to `1 + num_speculative_tokens`. **GPU sync.** Repeated pure-prefill and mixed speculative plan+run steps pass after warmup under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, via `enable_gpu_sync_check` and `with_gpu_sync_check`. With pinned staging disabled, the checker raises on the unpinned non-blocking copy. (Old base, both FlashInfer versions.) **CI coverage.** Buildkite has no SM12x runner, so the GPU cases skip in CI. ### Layer timing (PR base) ```bash python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_flashinfer_diffkv_prefill.py --method cudagraph \ --block-sizes 64 --chunk 17 64 512 2048 8192 --prefix 0 32768 ``` - MiMo-V2.6-Flash full-attention layer, TP2 (32 q / 2 KV heads, K192/V128, BF16), one request, block size 64. - Median of FlashInfer's `bench_gpu_time_with_cudagraph` with `cold_l2_cache=True`. Inputs are preallocated and passed through the timer, so it rotates them. CUPTI was unavailable. - Triton+PRs is main's kernel with #58177 @ `2e41b30` and #59673 @ `9103f7d` applied; their outputs are bit-identical to main's. | chunk | prefix | Triton main (µs) | Triton+PRs (µs) | this PR (µs) | vs Triton+PRs | vs main | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 17 | 0 | 3.0 | 3.0 | 6.6 | 0.45× | 0.45× | | 17 | 32K | 1,399 | 1,446 | 225 | 6.41× | 6.23× | | 64 | 0 | 7.7 | 6.1 | 7.3 | 0.83× | 1.06× | | 64 | 32K | 3,108 | 1,737 | 566 | 3.07× | 5.50× | | 512 | 0 | 153 | 102 | 83 | 1.24× | 1.85× | | 512 | 32K | 17,435 | 10,979 | 4,846 | 2.27× | 3.60× | | 2K | 0 | 2,092 | 1,211 | 660 | 1.84× | 3.20× | | 2K | 32K | 70,411 | 41,449 | 18,291 | 2.27× | 3.86× | | 8K | 0 | 34,095 | 19,443 | 8,964 | 2.17× | 3.78× | | 8K | 32K | 314,982 | 180,821 | 79,054 | 2.29× | 3.96× | - Relative L2 against Triton is 6.6e-4 to 3.9e-3. - Warm-L2 timing (same buffers repeated) gave the same speedups within 3%, except fresh 512 (1.47× warm vs 1.24× cold). **Per-step costs added by the FlashInfer path,** reported separately because host planning can overlap GPU work: - Kernel: 1.2–3.6 µs slower per layer for fresh chunks of ≤64 tokens, about 11–32 µs per step over MiMo's 9 full-attention layers. Faster for every other measured shape. - `plan()`: 101–134 µs host time per step that routes to FlashInfer (median of 20 calls), shared by all layers. One outlier: 548 µs for the fresh 17-token case in the Triton+PRs run. That was the first case in its process (after one untimed `plan()` call), and the identical case measured 104 µs in the Triton-main run. A warmup effect is likely, but I did not verify it, so it is reported here rather than excluded (raw log: `results_v8_bench_coldl2_triton_prs.txt`). - Serving impact, measured directly in the short-prompt table below. ### End to end on the PR base (main ± PR) Single request, cache-cold prompts. | prompt tokens | main TTFT | main + PR TTFT | speedup | |---|---|---|---| | 1.5K | 0.78 s | 0.75 s | 1.04× | | 6K | 2.17 s | 1.96 s | 1.11× | | 24K | 9.95 s | 8.12 s | 1.23× | | 48K | 25.33 s | 17.40 s | 1.46× | | 96K | 72.31 s | 40.59 s | 1.78× | - **Decode** (2048 tokens, DFlash k=7): main 55.9 / 53.7 (code) and 29.0 / 27.9 (prose) tok/s; main + PR 54.4 / 53.4 and 29.2 / 28.1 tok/s. - **Engine logs:** - main + PR selects `TRITON_FLASHINFER_DIFFKV` for full-attention layers and `TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV` for SWA layers, on Model Runner V2. - Both arms captured full decode and DFlash CUDA graphs. - Chat and tool-call smoke requests succeeded on both. - **Old base** (`7f1a539` ± this change): the same TTFT pattern, 96K 72.8 s → 40.6 s. **Short cache-cold prompts.** One request at a time, 30 requests per size, `max_tokens=1`, after warmup; one server start per arm. | prompt tokens | main p50 / p90 | main + PR p50 / p90 | Δ p50 | |---|---|---|---| | 23 | 173.0 / 185.5 ms | 179.5 / 187.5 ms | +6.5 ms | | 34 | 198.3 / 211.7 ms | 200.6 / 214.4 ms | +2.3 ms | | 66 | 228.3 / 235.7 ms | 224.1 / 235.3 ms | −4.2 ms | | 129 | 266.5 / 286.1 ms | 256.0 / 276.7 ms | −10.5 ms | | 515 | 296.9 / 301.3 ms | 291.2 / 296.6 ms | −5.7 ms | ### Re-check after rebase (main `fe4df3df0` + PR, 0.85) One server start, PR arm only. There is no main arm on this base, so the speedups above come from the PR base. - The engine log selects `TRITON_FLASHINFER_DIFFKV` for full-attention layers and `TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV` for SWA layers. Chat and tool-call smoke requests succeeded. - Cold-prefill TTFT: 1.5K 0.74 s, 6K 1.98 s, 24K 8.33 s, 48K 17.44 s, 96K 41.25 s (PR base: 0.75, 1.96, 8.12, 17.40, 40.59 s). - Decode: 53.8 / 49.3 (code) and 28.0 / 26.9 (prose) tok/s. - Short prompts, p50: 23 tokens 178.2 ms, 34 207.9 ms, 66 225.5 ms, 129 265.7 ms, 515 299.2 ms. ### Concurrent generation with arriving prompts (old base) - Workload: 8 streams generating up to 600 tokens (DFlash k=7, temperature 0). - Phase A has no arrivals. Phase B adds a cache-cold 8K-token prompt every 6 s, so prefill shares batches with decode/verify rows. - One run per arm. - **The arms got different random arrival prompts of the same length.** The workload seeded with `hash()`, which is randomized per process; the script now uses a fixed seed. | phase | metric | base | this PR | |---|---|---|---| | decode only | stream tok/s | 127.8 | 124.3 | | decode only | chunk gap p50 / p99 | 249 / 316 ms | 250 / 329 ms | | with arrivals | stream tok/s | 88.8 | 92.7 | | with arrivals | chunk gap p50 / p90 / p99 | 262 / 775 / 846 ms | 260 / 741 / 759 ms | | with arrivals | arrival TTFT mean / p90 | 3.76 / 3.86 s | 3.50 / 3.64 s | No regression was observed in one synchronous-scheduling run (`--no-async-scheduling`). The decode-only phase runs identical code, which suggests about ±3% noise. Async scheduling is not measured. ### gsm8k (old base) ```bash python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --use-chat-completions \ --max-tokens 1024 --temperature 0 --max-concurrency 32 \ --request-timeout-seconds 14400 --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' ``` 1319 questions, 5-shot, chat, thinking off; two runs each. | config | run 1 | run 2 | invalid | |---|---|---|---| | base (`TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV`) | 0.963 | 0.961 | 0.0% | | this PR | 0.961 | 0.964 | 0.0% | The longer timeout is needed because the evaluator starts all 1319 requests at once behind a connection limit. Each request's `aiohttp` timeout includes time spent waiting for a connection, so queued requests expired at the 600 s default.
Full-vocabulary logprobs vs base (old base) These are `prompt_logprobs` on a fixed text set, compared token by token. The noise column is two runs of one fixed configuration against each other. | text | tokens | mean \|Δ logprob\| | ppl ratio | top-1 agree | noise \|Δ\| / ppl | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | code (agent) | 1785 | 0.0941 | 0.997 | 97.4% | 0.0896 / 1.001 | | code (site) | 1931 | 0.0573 | 0.997 | 98.0% | 0.0518 / 0.996 | | prose | 529 | 0.0194 | 1.002 | 100.0% | 0.0246 / 1.011 | | json | 2330 | 0.0045 | 1.002 | 100.0% | 0.0041 / 1.002 | | math | 1376 | 0.0054 | 0.999 | 99.9% | 0.0068 / 0.999 | | tool call | 303 | 0.8095 | 1.211 | 98.7% | 0.7744 / 0.982 | The tool-call sample is short and high-entropy (mean NLL 4.3). Its perplexity ratio swings by about ±20% even between two runs of the identical FlashInfer kernel (1.246).
Raw results, logs and scripts: https://gist.github.com/siddharth1825/7e3c542800bef7f7ee6c03f6ba80487c ## Details ### Selection `MiMoV2Attention` keeps its order: FA DiffKV when FA3/FA4 is usable, then `TRITON_FLASHINFER_DIFFKV`, then `TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV`. The new backend is auto-selected only when all of these hold: - CUDA, compute capability 12.x, FlashInfer present; - full attention: no sliding window, no sinks; - FP16/BF16 compute with a 16-bit KV cache; - head sizes (192, 128), the only pair tested. It is also selectable with `--attention-backend TRITON_FLASHINFER_DIFFKV`. ### Routing - FlashInfer when the batch's longest query exceeds `max(16, max_decode_query_len)`; Triton otherwise, and for image-prefix batches. - Decode or verify rows that share a batch with a prefill run on FlashInfer with it. - `capture_variant = 0`. The threshold is never below the uniform decode/verify width, so CUDA graph replay always selects Triton. - A KV cache group containing any layer FlashInfer does not cover (window, sinks, ALiBi, soft-cap, FP8 KV) always uses Triton. - The 16-token floor is not tuned for fresh prompts. Over a cached prefix, FlashInfer wins from 17 tokens; fresh prompts break even around 64 tokens. ### Metadata - `plan()` runs once per step in the builder, shared by every layer in the group. - As in `FlashInferMetadataBuilder.build`, the query offsets, page offsets, last-page lengths and an explicit `seq_lens` are staged in pinned memory, so `plan()`'s non-blocking copies stay asynchronous. - The builder reuses `_copy_page_indices_kernel` and joins the composite's workspace sharing. ### Host sequence lengths - `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` is exact for prefill rows, and for all rows without speculative decoding, so those batches never read back from the GPU. - A batch with a row that may be a spec-decode row (query length ≤ `max_decode_query_len`) reads exact `seq_lens` back inside `gpu_sync_allowed()`. That row's upper bound assumes every draft was accepted, and FlashInfer needs exact lengths. - Without async scheduling the bound is often exact too. That is not used, because MRV2 adaptive verification also makes per-row token counts an upper bound. ### Cache and FlashInfer path - The FlashInfer child subclasses the Triton DiffKV backend, so both share one cache spec and tensor. K/V are passed as last-dim strided views of the packed cache, in HND or NHD physical layout, with or without layer interleaving. - The call is `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(workspace, "HND")` with `plan(..., head_dim_vo=128, causal=True, seq_lens=...)`; the wrapper resolves to the `fa2` backend on SM12x. - The SM120 fused 192×128 kernels reported unreachable in the 0.6.18/0.7.0 wrappers are not used. - **JIT build on 0.7.0.post1.** The aarch64 `flashinfer-jit-cache` wheel is a stub that depends on per-architecture packages vLLM does not install, so the 192/128 module is JIT-built on first use: 19 s in isolation. In serving it completes during startup; the first long prompt after a restart was not measurably slower. ### Memory - **Workspace.** It is sized like the FlashInfer backend's: `max(VLLM_FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BUFFER_SIZE, tokens × heads × head_dim × 16)`. With this config's 2048-token budget, that resolves to the 394 MB default. - **KV cache.** On the PR base, KV cache memory went from 19.01 to 18.42 GiB (1,428,918 → 1,335,006 tokens). - **Possible follow-up.** A smaller floor for this prefill-only use could recover most of it. It is not changed here: FlashInfer errors rather than grows when the workspace is too small, and the default is the same one the FlashInfer backend uses. ### Why decode and CUDA graphs stay on Triton - Decode is bandwidth-bound with short queries. Triton DiffKV already has 2D/3D split-KV paths for it, and measured decode was unchanged. - Only Triton is captured. Moving decode/verify-only batches to FlashInfer needs a graph-safe DiffKV decode/verify plan (persistent buffers, `fast_plan`), which is a separate change. - **Cost.** The composite reports `UNIFORM_BATCH` instead of `ALWAYS`. - Under the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, uniform decode still runs as full graphs, and mixed batches already ran piecewise. - Only `cudagraph_mode=FULL` with mixed batches loses full graphs on these layers. ### Complexity About 460 new lines in one new backend file, plus small edits: - selection: 18 lines in `mimo_v2.py`; - the env var; - the registry entry; - docs. There are no changes to the model runner, scheduler, KV cache manager or the Triton kernel. ### AI assistance Claude (Anthropic) was used to write the change, run the tests and benchmarks on our DGX Sparks, and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line and the validation results. cc @mgoin: SM12x + FlashInfer prefill, related to #46963. ---

title: kv offload: invalidate cached absent verdicts after a successful store
body:
## Overview

A block that a secondary KV-offload tier previously probed as **absent** keeps
serving that stale "absent" verdict even after the block is later **stored**
into the tier. `AsyncLookupManager` only corrects a cached negative verdict on a
*failed load* (`mark_miss`); there was no path to correct it when the block was
later *written* to the tier, so the scheduler kept skipping a block that was
actually on disk.

This PR adds `AsyncLookupManager.invalidate()` and calls it from
`FileSystemTierManager.get_finished_jobs()` when a store job succeeds, so freshly
stored blocks are re-probed instead of served as a stale miss.

## Claims

- Fixes a correctness bug: a block stored into a secondary tier after its
  absence was cached is still served as absent (the cached negative is never
  invalidated on a successful store).
- `invalidate()` is conservative: it drops **only** resolved-absent
  (`result is False`) entries. Present, in-flight, and unknown keys are left
  alone, so it is safe to call with a store job's full key list.
- `FileSystemTierManager` now tracks store-job keys unconditionally (previously
  only when KV events were enabled) and pops them unconditionally on completion,
  so the key map cannot leak.
- No change to KV-event emission: an event is still emitted iff a store succeeds.
- Additive and non-breaking: `invalidate()` is a new method, and the `cleanup()`
  change is a strict superset of the previous behavior.

## Validation

New unit tests in `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_async_lookup.py`:

- `test_invalidate_drops_stale_absent_and_reprobes` - after a stored block, the
  cached negative is dropped and the next lookup re-probes and sees the block as
  present (not the stale miss).
- `test_invalidate_is_noop_for_present_and_unknown_keys` - `invalidate()` leaves
  a present entry alone and is a no-op for an unknown key (plants nothing).
- `test_cleanup_is_safe_after_invalidate` - `cleanup()` does not raise
  `KeyError` when a tracked key was dropped by `invalidate()`.

Command + result (run on a local build):
```
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_async_lookup.py -q
```
- With the change: all tests pass (including the 3 new ones).
- Without the change: exactly the 3 new tests fail (`invalidate` not defined);
  all pre-existing tests in the file still pass.

Pre-existing tests in the file are unaffected - the change is an additive method
plus a strict-superset `cleanup()` guard, so no existing behavior changes. Model
evaluation is not applicable: this is offload bookkeeping and does not change
model output, accuracy, or serving. The full suite runs in CI.

## Details

Root cause: `AsyncLookupManager` caches a probe's verdict per key. A negative
verdict (`result is False`) is only ever overridden by `mark_miss()` (the
failed-load livelock fix, #49176). But the *store* path
(`FileSystemTierManager.get_finished_jobs`) never touched the lookup manager, so
once a block was cached as absent, storing it into the tier left the stale
negative in place and the scheduler kept treating the block as absent.

Design:
- `AsyncLookupManager.invalidate(keys)` drops only entries where
  `result is False`. It intentionally does **not** touch present (`True`),
  in-flight, or unknown keys, so it is safe to call with a job's full key list
  and idempotent.
- `FileSystemTierManager` tracks `_store_job_keys` for every store job (it used
  to only track them when KV events were enabled) and, on a *successful* store,
  calls `invalidate()` on those keys before (and independently of) emitting any
  KV event. The map is popped unconditionally in `get_finished_jobs`, so no keys
  accumulate when events are disabled.
- `AsyncLookupManager.cleanup()` switches its per-key lookup from a direct index
  (`self._lookup_state[key]`) to a guarded `.get()` + `continue`, because
  `invalidate()` can drop a key that a tracked request still references; without
  the guard that path would raise `KeyError`.

Tier-agnostic: the fix lives in the shared `AsyncLookupManager`, so it applies to
any secondary tier, not just the filesystem tier.

## Why this is not duplicating existing work

Searched open PRs and issues in `vllm-project/vllm` (2026-10-12):

- No open PR invalidates a cached absent verdict on a successful store. The
  "invalidate" PRs are unrelated subsystems (startup plans, GPU budget, LazyDict,
  KDA conv weights, HiSparse, CPU metadata).
- The closest open offload PRs are distinct: `#59096` guards the *mark_miss*
  (failed-load) path - the complement to this store path; `#53158` is hash
  promotion; the rest are telemetry / wait-bounding / per-group publish / metrics.
- No open issue tracks this bug, and the fix is not present on `main`.

## Related

- #49176 - failed-load livelock (the `mark_miss` path this complements).
- #59096 - open, guards the `mark_miss` path (complement to this PR).

title: [Bug] MooncakeStoreConnector drops secondary views of multi-tensor KV caches
body:
## Problem

The Store worker reduces a list-valued layer cache to `cache[0]`. In the observed Ascend configuration, the layer supplies `[K, V]` views at different offsets in one storage. Physical buffer registration covers the storage, but the transfer layout omits V. Save, lookup and load succeed; a fresh consumer then generates corrupted output.

Tuple-valued entries instead fail the helper's type assertion. Single-tensor caches do not exercise this branch.

## Reproduction

1. Run producer and fresh consumer instances with `MooncakeStoreConnector`.
2. Save a long prompt on the producer, then request a shared prefix on the consumer.
3. Observe a successful external-cache load followed by corrupted generation.

Observed: Qwen3.8-27B, TP2, LBNHC, Ascend 910B2; vLLM `ced6857`, vllm-ascend `39fef3f8f`, Mooncake NPU wheel 0.3.11.post1. The consumer loaded 15,360 tokens with no transfer errors.

## Proposed fix

Preserve every list/tuple view when constructing the non-HiSparse transfer layout. Keep storage registration and region deduplication; no cache merging or data copy is needed. The recorded clean-pool Ascend run restored the expected generated text after this change.

HiSparse is outside the proposed fix.

title: [Bugfix] Inherit target --revision/--code-revision for MTP draft; readable error for n_predict=0
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61197: with `method="mtp"` and no explicit draft model, the draft is the target checkpoint itself, but the draft `ModelConfig` was built with the speculative config's own (unset) `revision`/`code_revision`, so config and weights resolved from the repo's default branch instead of the target's `--revision`. This PR inherits both from `target_model_config` (unless explicitly overridden), mirroring the existing `model`/`quantization` inheritance. It also replaces a `ZeroDivisionError` with a readable `ValueError` when a draft checkpoint resolves to `n_predict=0`.

## Claims

- MTP draft config/weights now resolve from the target's `--revision`/`--code-revision` instead of the default branch (regression vs 0.29).
- Explicitly set speculative `revision`/`code_revision` still take precedence over the inherited values.
- Other speculative methods (e.g. `dspark`, separate `draft_model` checkpoints) are unaffected.
- A draft checkpoint with `n_predict=0` (missing `num_nextn_predict_layers`) now raises a readable `ValueError` instead of `ZeroDivisionError`.

## Validation

Unit tests (mocked, no HF downloads / no GPU), from a fresh `main` checkout (`32b05ad`):

```
PYTHONPATH=$PWD python -m pytest tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py -q
# 21 passed (17 pre-existing + 4 new regression tests)
PYTHONPATH=$PWD python -m pytest tests/config/test_bailing_mtp_config.py -q
# 2 passed
ruff check vllm/config/speculative.py tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py
# All checks passed
```

New regression tests (in `tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py`):
- `test_mtp_draft_inherits_target_revision`
- `test_mtp_draft_explicit_revision_wins`
- `test_explicit_draft_model_does_not_inherit_revision`
- `test_mtp_zero_n_predict_raises_readable_error`

A standalone reproducer confirmed the bug before the fix (draft got `revision=None` despite target `revision="pre-final"`, and `ZeroDivisionError` for `n_predict=0`) and the fixed behavior after.

Note on environment: this sandbox is CPU-only with no HF Hub access, so every test in this file also reports a teardown error from `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()` in `tests/conftest.py` — this happens identically on the unmodified tree (17 passed / 17 teardown errors before my change), and HF-download-dependent tests elsewhere (e.g. `tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py`) fail for the same environmental reasons. Model evaluation is not applicable: this is a config-time-only change that does not affect model outputs, accuracy, or serving behavior.

## Details

**Root cause:** in `SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__`, the `method == "mtp"` branch sets `self.model` from `target_model_config.model_weights or .model` and inherits `quantization`, but leaves `self.revision`/`self.code_revision` as `None`. The draft `ModelConfig(...)` built later passes `revision=self.revision` / `code_revision=self.code_revision`, so the draft resolved config and weights from the default branch rather than the target's pinned revision.

**Design decision:** inheritance is placed next to the existing `model`/`quantization` inheritance and guarded by `is None` checks, so explicit values remain overrides. It intentionally applies only when no explicit draft model is given (i.e. the draft *is* the target checkpoint); a separately provided draft checkpoint is a different repo and keeps its own revision. The `n_predict == 0` guard sits at the top of the existing `elif n_predict is not None:` branch, so `dspark` (separate branch) and valid `n_predict > 0` behavior are unchanged.

**Why this is not a duplicate:** searched open PRs for "61197", "mtp revision inherit", and "ZeroDivisionError n_predict speculative" — no open PR addresses this fix.

**AI assistance:** AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR (with human review of every changed line).

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] V2 rejection sampler: return logprob_token_ids scores
body:
## Overview

With the V2 model runner and speculative decoding, a request that sets `logprob_token_ids` (and no `logprobs`) gets no logprobs back whenever another request in the same batch has draft tokens. `RejectionSampler` only looked at `max_num_logprobs`, so `logprob_token_ids` was dropped on that path. The regular V2 `Sampler` already handles it through `get_logprobs_dims`.

`/v1/systemone` reads are such requests (`max_tokens=1`, `logprob_token_ids`): next to a streaming chat on an MTP model, every read failed with `HTTP 400: No logprobs available for item 0`. This passes the per-request token ids to `compute_topk_scores` in the rejection sampler. Related: #42592 / #44727 (the same kind of mixed batch, on the V1 sampler, a different file).

## Claims

- Qwen3.8-27B with MTP 3, 6 `/v1/systemone` calls (4 questions, 2k-token state) while 4 chat streams run: 6/6 fail before, 6/6 succeed after.
- Chat is not affected: time to first token 0.52 → 0.60 s and inter-chunk latency p50 191 → 192 ms with and without systemone on the engine.
- The returned probabilities are not changed by the chat load: mean absolute difference 0.007 (max 0.041) between a cold call and the same call next to chat, the same as between a cold call and the same call repeated alone on a cached state (0.007, max 0.039).
- Batches without `logprob_token_ids` are unchanged (`compute_topk_scores` takes its fast path when `max_token_ids == 0`); without speculative decoding this code path is not used.

## Validation

Qwen3.8-27B 4-bit with MTP 3 on gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S), nightly `0.31.1rc1.dev273` (`2eb491e18b`), V2 model runner, `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --logprobs-mode raw_logprobs`, `--max-num-seqs 8`. The same change was applied to the nightly's copy of the file for the runs. Chat: 4 closed-loop streaming requests (256 tokens).

| | systemone alone | systemone + 4 chats, main | systemone + 4 chats, this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| errors | 0 / 6 | 6 / 6 (HTTP 400, no logprobs) | 0 / 6 |
| chat errors | | 0 | 0 |

After the review changes the run was repeated (mixed: 0 errors, cold vs next-to-chat mean absolute difference 0.004, max 0.033). The same server also runs `/v1/systemone` accuracy (120 synthetic tickets: 0.90 / 0.67 / 1.00, unchanged) and the question-count cases (6.4 / 8.2 / 11.9 / 28.7 s for 1 / 4 / 16 / 64 questions, unchanged) with the change applied. MTP off, on main: no errors (no drafts, so the batch does not go through the rejection sampler); not re-run with the change.

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py
```

31 passed with the change. New tests in `test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py` build a real `LogprobTokenIdsState` and check the returned ids and scores against `log_softmax` / the raw logits for every row:
- `test_logprob_token_ids_without_topk_logprobs`: token ids only, raw and logits modes, and nothing is computed when none are requested;
- `test_logprob_token_ids_with_topk_logprobs`: top-k `logprobs=1` narrower than the widest `logprob_token_ids`, requests with and without ids;
- `test_logprob_token_ids_with_adaptive_verification`: one chunk over compacted logits, device `cu_num_logits` and a host-side upper bound, same result as the fixed-boundary layout;
- `test_get_logprobs_dims_with_only_token_ids`.

`test_gather_sampler_output_logprobs_and_nans` is parametrized over top-k only, token ids only and token ids wider than top-k. The CUDA tests of these files are skipped on ROCm by `current_platform.is_cuda()`; I ran them locally with that check replaced by `torch.cuda.is_available()`. The new tests fail on main. The `model_runner.py` call site of the sharded gather (TP > 1) has no test and was not run.

## Details

- `RejectionSampler.__call__` calls `Sampler.get_logprobs_dims` once and passes `logprobs_dims` to `_verify_in_chunks` and `_get_logprobs_tensors`, which also takes the chunk's `expanded_idx_mapping` (`compute_topk_scores` needs it to map each logits row to its request).
- `Sampler.get_logprobs_dims` no longer has `include_token_ids`: the sharded gather in `model_runner.py` sizes its buffers with the token-id columns for batches with draft tokens too.
- Not covered: DSpark and the other speculators were not run; they go through the same `RejectionSampler.__call__`.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Order shared host writes with a step counter
body:
## Overview

Alternative to #60941 for the same HiSparse TP hang. Instead of adding a CPU barrier on steps with no scheduled tokens, TP rank 0 publishes each step's host writes as a step index in the shared host pool, and the other ranks wait for that exact index.

## Claims

- Fixes the TP group hang that occurs when a rank's host falls a step behind rank 0 on steps without scheduled tokens (#60941).
- No CPU barrier is added on any step.

## Validation

H100 (ibm-h100-1). Both harnesses (collapsed below) drive the real `HiSparseConnectorWorker.start_step`/`finish_forward`, using the real vLLM TP group. Only the transfer, restore and host-mirror paths are stubbed; they are empty in these runs. Each step with tokens runs matmuls plus an all-reduce, and the given rank's host sleeps before `start_step`.

```
torchrun --nproc-per-node N <harness> {zero_next|zero_now|tokens|stress:SEED}
```

| Case | `main` @ `7d1d866`, #60941's base (`real_worker_hang.py`) | this PR (`sem_worker_hang.py`) |
|---|---|---|
| TP2, rank 1 0.5 s late, next step has no tokens (`zero_next`) | HANG 3/3 | PASS 3/3 |
| TP2, rank 1 late on a step with no tokens (`zero_now`) | HANG 3/3 | PASS 3/3 |
| TP2, every step has tokens (`tokens`) | PASS 3/3 | PASS 3/3 |
| TP2, 300 steps, random zero-token steps and delays (`stress:1-3`) | HANG 2/3 | PASS 3/3 |
| TP4, same (`stress:1-3`) | HANG 2/3 | PASS 3/3 |
| TP8, same (`stress:4-5`) | not run | PASS 2/2 |

When it hangs on `main`, rank 0's GPU sits at 100% and the late rank's GPU at 0%.

`sem_worker_hang.py` also checks ordering. Each step, rank 0's stream writes the step index into the shared pool behind slow GPU work. After `start_step`, every other rank reads that value on its stream and counts reads older than the previous step. All runs above report 0 stale reads. With the peers' counter wait removed, rank 1 reads 7 stale values in 9 steps, so the check does detect under-waiting.

Unit tests, on H100:

```
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "hisparse or shared_host_pool or HiSparse"
```

98 passed. The extended `test_hisparse_step_waits_for_previous_host_write` fails on `main` (2 shared cases) and passes here.

**Not yet done:** an end-to-end serve run with HiSparse at TP>1, and before/after perf numbers. The change adds one driver call per step, which replaces an IPC event wait.

## Details

**Root cause.** With a shared host pool, rank 0 records two alternating IPC events, and every rank's stream waits on the one from the previous step. A stream wait binds to the event's latest record when the wait is issued. On a step with no forward, rank 0 can re-record an event before a lagging rank has issued its wait on it. That rank then binds to a record queued behind a forward that needs that same rank, and the group deadlocks.

**Fix.** The counter lives in one extra page at the end of the shared pool (`allocate_hisparse_host_pools`), pinned like the rest of the pool. In `start_step`, rank 0's stream waits on its own previous host writes, then `cuStreamWriteValue64` writes the step index. The other ranks' streams `cuStreamWaitValue64(>= step)`. A lagging rank waits for exactly the step it needs, which never depends on that rank, so no ordering on the host is required on any step. Rank 0 keeps local (non-IPC) events for its own ordering and for the host sync in `_copy_host_blocks`.

- The step index comes from `start_step` calls, which the alternating events already assumed are identical across TP ranks.
- The driver calls go through `cuda.bindings`, as `simple_kv_offload/cuda_mem_ops.py` already does. HiSparse is CUDA-only.
- Peers now also wait for rank 0's draft-layer mirror and post-forward transfer DMAs submitted at the start of the step. Rank 0's own forward already waits on these, so this adds no latency to the group.

**vs #60941.** #60941 is a 4-line fix that adds a TP CPU barrier on every step without scheduled tokens. On steps with tokens, it relies on rank 0's staging host sync in `_finish_mirror_phase` to order the record. This PR removes the race itself, so steps with tokens no longer depend on that sync. In exchange it uses driver stream memory operations and one extra pool page.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the design, implementation and validation harnesses.

<details>
<summary>sem_worker_hang.py (this PR)</summary>

```python
"""Drive the real HiSparseConnectorWorker.start_step/finish_forward under TP,
with the shared pool from allocate_hisparse_host_pools and its step counter.

Also checks ordering: rank 0's stream writes the step index into the shared
pool behind slow GPU work each step; after start_step every other rank reads
it on its stream and counts reads older than the previous step.

Real IPC host-write events (_create_hisparse_host_events), real vLLM TP group
(barrier/broadcast), real slot-mapping staging sync on rank 0. Only the
transfer/restore/host-mirror paths are stubbed (they are empty here anyway).

torchrun --nproc-per-node N real_worker_hang.py MODE
  MODE  zero_next | zero_now | tokens   (rank 1 held 0.5 s before step 5)
        stress:SEED                     (random zero-token steps and delays)
"""
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist

from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
from vllm.distributed import get_tp_group
from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import (
    init_distributed_environment,
    initialize_model_parallel,
)
from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.hisparse import worker as wm
from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.hisparse.connector import (
    HiSparseConnectorMetadata,
)

mode = sys.argv[1]
rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
world = int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
torch.cuda.set_device(rank)
device = torch.device("cuda", rank)

with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()):
    init_distributed_environment(world, rank, "env://", rank, "nccl")
    initialize_model_parallel(tensor_model_parallel_size=world)

import mmap
from vllm.v1.hisparse.runtime import (
    allocate_hisparse_host_pools,
    hisparse_host_write_counter,
)

page = mmap.PAGESIZE
cfg = SimpleNamespace(
    instance_id=f"semtest{os.environ['MASTER_PORT']}",
    parallel_config=SimpleNamespace(data_parallel_index=0),
)
(pool,), _, region = allocate_hisparse_host_pools(
    cfg, [4 * page], 4, page, use_shared_host_pool=True
)
is_writer = wm._is_hisparse_host_writer(region)
assert is_writer == (rank == 0)

MAX = 4096
w = object.__new__(wm.HiSparseConnectorWorker)
w.shared_host_region = region
w.is_host_writer = is_writer
w.host_write_events = (torch.Event(), torch.Event())
w.host_write_event = w.host_write_events[1]
w._next_host_write_event = 0
w._host_write_counter = wm._HostWriteCounter(hisparse_host_write_counter(region))
w._host_write_step = 0
handle = SimpleNamespace(
    slot_mapping=torch.full((MAX,), -1, dtype=torch.int64, device=device),
    runtime=SimpleNamespace(resident_source_index=0),
    all_context_pages_resident=True,
)
w.cache_handles = [handle]
w._slot_mapping_staging = (
    wm._SlotMappingStaging(
        stream=torch.cuda.Stream(device=device),
        event=torch.cuda.Event(),
        slots=torch.empty(MAX, dtype=torch.int64, pin_memory=True),
    )
    if is_writer
    else None
)
w._draft_mirror_pending = False
w._post_forward_transfers = []
w._pending_dma_descriptors = __import__("collections").deque()
w._dma_free_descriptors = []
w._dma_submitted = False
w._per_layer_mirrored = set()
w._submitted_mirror_layers = set()
w._forward_ready_event = torch.cuda.Event()
w._pending_invalid_block_ids = []
w._completed_host_copy_dst_ids = []
for name in ("_restore_pages", "_submit_transfers", "_enqueue_host_mirror"):
    setattr(w, name, MagicMock())
torch.cuda.synchronize()
dist.barrier()

if mode.startswith("stress"):
    seed = int(mode.split(":")[1])
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    steps = 300
    plan = [rng.random() < 0.35 for _ in range(steps)]  # True = zero tokens
    delays = [
        (rng.randrange(world), rng.uniform(0.0, 0.08)) if rng.random() < 0.25 else None
        for _ in range(steps)
    ]
else:
    steps = 10
    zero = {"zero_next": 6, "zero_now": 5, "tokens": None}[mode]
    plan = [s == zero for s in range(steps)]
    delays = [(1, 0.5) if s == 5 else None for s in range(steps)]

step = -1
done = threading.Event()


def watchdog():
    if not done.wait(30):
        util = subprocess.run(
            ["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu", "--format=csv,noheader"],
            capture_output=True, text=True,
        ).stdout
        print(f"rank{rank} HANG at step {step}, util: "
              + util.strip().replace("\n", " | "), flush=True)
        os._exit(2)


threading.Thread(target=watchdog, daemon=True).start()
a = torch.randn(4096, 4096, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
published = pool[:8].view(torch.int64)
stale = torch.zeros((), dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
step_value = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
meta = HiSparseConnectorMetadata(None, (), (), {}, True, {})
for step in range(steps):
    zero_tokens = plan[step]
    if delays[step] and delays[step][0] == rank:
        time.sleep(delays[step][1])  # slow host work before start_step
    n = 0 if zero_tokens else 16
    w.start_step(meta, None, [], num_tokens=n)
    if rank != 0 and step > 0:
        stale += (published.to(device, non_blocking=True)[0] < step - 1).long()
    if not zero_tokens:
        y = a
        for _ in range(8):
            y = y @ a
            dist.all_reduce(y, group=get_tp_group().device_group)
            y = y / 4096
    if rank == 0:
        y = a
        for _ in range(4):
            y = y @ a
        step_value.fill_(step).add_((y[0, 0] * 0).long())
        published.copy_(step_value, non_blocking=True)
    w.finish_forward()
torch.cuda.synchronize()
assert stale.item() == 0, f"rank{rank} read {stale.item()} stale host writes"
done.set()
print(f"rank{rank} PASS zero_steps={sum(plan)} stale=0", flush=True)
os._exit(0)
```

title: [Perf][Model] Qwen4Exp QSA DCP: opt-in sharded selector
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Opt-in **sharded** QSA selector for Qwen4Exp decode context parallelism (DCP). With `--attention-config '{"qsa_dcp_selector": "sharded"}'`, each DCP rank stores and scores only the compressed indexer keys of the tokens it owns. One all-gather of the ranks' local top-k candidates then gives the same global top-k as the replicated selector. The default stays `"replicated"` (#59279); nothing changes without the opt-in.

**Depends on #61728, which depends on #59279.** This branch is #61728 (head ce2f6f0c6) plus 5 commits; review only the commits after ce2f6f0c6. As @sungsooha asked, this follow-up is its own PR. It replaces this draft's earlier content (a full QSA DCP implementation that overlapped #59279).

## Claims

- With the opt-in, the selector cache and the selector scoring per rank shrink by the DCP size, for one extra collective per selection. The selection result is the same as with the replicated selector (end-to-end GPU test on N simulated ranks).
- Measured on 8 × A100-SXM4-40GB, DCP 4: the GPU KV cache holds **1.33×** the tokens at the same KV memory (6,545,304 against 4,925,984 tokens, 13.21 against 13.26 GiB).
- No change to core files: the only change outside the model code is the `AttentionConfig.qsa_dcp_selector` option. The sharded selector joins the main KV cache group (main block size), so it uses the runner's block-table width and needs no kernel block table.
- Requirement: `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` must be a multiple of the indexer compress ratio (4 here). The cache refuses other values at start.

## Validation

**Serving (8 × A100-SXM4-40GB).** TP8 + EP, DCP 4, interleave 4, FP8 KV, MTP 3, `--max-num-batched-tokens 2048`. MLPerf agentic multi-turn workload, 32 requests in flight, 1 × 60 min per arm, 0 failed requests. Both arms ran on an earlier base (#59279 c9de36da9 + its block-table fix + the #61728 follow-ups); they differ only in this opt-in.

SLO (Artificial Analysis percentiles): P95 TTFT ≤ 2.93 s and P95 TPOT ≤ 21.74 ms (P5 output speed ≥ 46 tokens/s). "SLO pass" is the share of requests that meet both limits.

| Selector (interleave 4) | GPU KV cache | Requests/s | Output tok/s per GPU | Output tok/s per user | TTFT P50 / P95 | TPOT P50 / P95 | SLO pass | Goodput |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| replicated | 4,925,984 tokens | 2.85 | 145.4 | 43.9 | 986 / 2,342 ms | 17.9 / 28.8 ms | 73.3 % | 2.09 req/s |
| **sharded (this PR)** | **6,545,304 tokens** | 2.84 | **149.4** | **45.1** | 989 / **1,940 ms** | 17.8 / **26.7 ms** | **77.3 %** | **2.19 req/s** |

One run per arm, so the SLO difference is not yet significant; the KV capacity difference is deterministic.

**Tests (1 × A100-SXM4-40GB, nightly 5555a2d8f image with this branch's Python tree, one pytest session per file).**

| File | #61728 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_qsa_dcp_sharded_selector.py` (new) | — | 72 passed |
| `test_qsa_dcp_localize.py` | 42 passed, 4 failed | 43 passed, 4 failed |
| `test_qsa_dcp_cache_policy.py` | 20 passed | 27 passed |
| `test_qsa_dcp_combine.py` | 15 passed | 15 passed |
| `test_gdn_metadata_builder.py` | 62 passed | 62 passed |

The 4 failures are the same as on #59279 and #61728: the FP8 cases of `test_sharded_ranks_reproduce_the_single_rank_result` do not compile on sm_80 ("type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture"). `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on every commit.

**Global top-k merge kernel (1 × A100-SXM4-40GB).** `_select_qsa_dcp_topk_kernel` sorts DCP × top-k = 2,048 int64 keys in one program. Launch-parameter sweep at the per-GPU shapes of the serving setup (32 requests × 4 query tokens, CUDA graph, L2 flushed before each replay): 32 warps take 64.0 / 48.9 / 49.1 µs at 8k / 32k / 128k context, against 91.2 / 70.3 / 70.3 µs with the earlier 8 warps (1.43×); the output is bit-equal. `test_qsa_dcp_sharded_selector.py`: 72 passed with the change.

**Engine start (4 × A100, Model Runner V2).** Qwen4Exp with 4 layers (3 GDN + 1 QSA), dummy weights, TP4 + EP, DCP 4, interleave 4, MTP 3, FP8 KV, `max_model_len` 262144: starts, captures CUDA graphs and generates with `qsa_dcp_selector` "sharded", and with "replicated" as the control.

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_qsa_dcp_sharded_selector.py tests/v1/attention/test_qsa_dcp_localize.py tests/v1/core/test_qsa_dcp_cache_policy.py
```

## Details

| Commit | What and why |
|---|---|
| opt-in sharded selector cache and metadata | `AttentionConfig.qsa_dcp_selector`; the sharded compressed-key cache spec (rank-local tokens) and its side-cache metadata (rank-local visible blocks). |
| sharded selector scoring and exact global top-k merge | Each rank scores its local compressed keys; the ranks' top-k candidates are all-gathered and merged into the exact global top-k. |
| fuse expand and localize for the sharded selector | One kernel expands the selected blocks and writes this rank's local token ids and count into the layer top-k buffer, so the indexer skips its separate localize step in sharded mode (the replicated path is unchanged). |
| warm the sharded selector kernels | Compile the new kernels before CUDA graph capture. |
| test the sharded selection end to end on N simulated ranks | The sharded result equals the replicated expand + localize result on every rank, also through the indexer. |
| more warps for the global top-k merge | `num_warps = min(32, max(4, BLOCK_N // 64))`: 32 warps for 2,048 keys instead of 8 (1.43× on A100, bit-equal). |

**Size:** +637 / −26 outside tests (7 files, most of it the new `ops/qsa_dcp_selector.py`); tests +929 / −7.

**Limits.** The serving A/B is one run per arm on an earlier base. MTP with the sharded selector uses the #61728 path (selection reused in `skip_topk` steps).

title: [HiSparse] GLM-5.3-Flash support
body:
## Purpose

Make HiSparse work with GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`). Fixes #59176. Builds on #60805 (merged).

**Changes**
- Read `index_topk` from `hf_text_config`. Flash's top-level config is multimodal, so startup failed with "HiSparse is only supported for DSA models with index_topk".
- `resolve_hisparse_specs` (worker, before the KV layout is resolved) groups only the MLA specs. It also grouped Flash's non-MLA caches (KDA state, kpool tail ring), which needs the resolved layout ("KV cache layout has not been resolved yet").
- Skip per-layer host mirrors outside connector steps. Flash's MLA layers take the generic MLA path, which mirrors each layer on the TP0 host writer. Graph-capture forwards run without `start_step`/`finish_forward`, so TP0 raised "HiSparse layer 0 mirrored twice" and startup hung in the custom all-reduce.
- Backends declare `supports_hisparse()`; with HiSparse on, sparse-MLA backend selection skips backends without a HiSparse path. On Hopper, Flash (head size 512) got FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA, which has no HiSparse path and read stale KV on prefix-cache hits: GSM8K fell on each pass over one server (0.901, 0.834, 0.745). SM90 support: #61277.
- Order the side-stream top-k convert after its block table. The leader's batch block table is built on the compute stream after the indexer recorded `logical_topk_ready`, so the side stream could read it before it was written: illegal memory accesses and NaN logits under load, and the graph-capture hang. Found by moving one HiSparse stream at a time onto the compute stream.
- **Core (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`, one line):** pass `attn_metadata` to `kv_connector.pre_forward` on PIECEWISE and eager steps too, as FULL steps already do. Without it, HiSparse's per-step prepare never ran under PIECEWISE replay; Flash's MLA layers otherwise prepare only inside the captured KV-update op, so the swap-row counter was never reset ("HiSparse swap rows exceed the configured speculative decode capacity: stop=62, capacity=32"). Other connectors ignore the kwarg.

**Not in this PR**
- Hopper with HiSparse: Flash needs #61277 (SM90 backend support). The two Hopper fallbacks failed with the side-stream race and the PIECEWISE prepare bug fixed here; not re-tested on Hopper.

## Test Plan / Results

**Re-run on this branch merged with main (`3ac5c23cf0`, includes #60805), 4×B200 TP4, CUDA graphs:** GSM8K 5-shot 0.913 / 0.912 / 0.915 (pass 1 / pass 2 / concurrency 1); long-context host-read run 0.920 / 0.955 (about 220–236 GB host-to-device per sampled interval). No errors. The tables below are from the earlier revision, with #60805 merged in by hand.


`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (rev eb9eb208), 4×B200, TP4, this PR + #60805, FlashInfer TRTLLM sparse MLA, bf16 KV, `--max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 32`, HiSparse `host_pool_gib=32`, prefix caching on (about 80% hit rate with HiSparse). `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` prompts, 5-shot, greedy. Three passes on one server: 1319 questions at concurrency 32 twice, then 200 at concurrency 1.

| | pass 1 | pass 2 | concurrency 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| no HiSparse, CUDA graphs | 0.920 | 0.915 | 0.910 |
| HiSparse, eager | 0.917 | 0.916 | – |
| HiSparse, CUDA graphs | 0.910 | 0.919 | 0.945 |

**Long context, reading from host.** 100-shot GSM8K (prompts ~16.9k tokens), 200 questions at concurrency 32, `--max-model-len 18432`, two passes on one server. HiSparse ran with `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 4G` (50.6k GPU KV tokens; ~4.6 concurrent 18k requests while reading from host), so decodes fetched from host: about 230 GB host-to-device and 220M hot-buffer misses per sampled interval.

| | pass 1 | pass 2 |
|---|---|---|
| no HiSparse, full GPU memory (4.1M GPU KV tokens) | 0.925 | 0.930 |
| HiSparse, 4 GiB GPU pool | 0.940 | 0.940 |

Before the side-stream fix (eager, no `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING`): illegal memory access during serving; with only the copy/DMA/staging streams serialized, 0.035 with NaN logprobs.

Unit tests:
- `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k index_group_convert` (B200): passes; the new block-table ordering test fails with the old event-only wait.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py` (12 pass, H200).
- `tests/test_attention_backend_registry.py -k opt_in`.
