title: [Kernel] Add FlashInfer GDN and KDA prefill backend selection
body:
## Overview

Add FlashInfer prefill selection for Qwen GDN (`auto`/`cudnn`) and all eight public KDA backends for bounded GLM/Kimi KDA, with shared state handling and versioned KDA metadata. This carries the integration from [Anerudhan/vllm#1](https://github.com/Anerudhan/vllm/pull/1); benchmark result files are excluded.

## Claims

- Add separate FlashInfer implementation selectors for GDN and KDA prefill, including `cute-dsl`, `cute-dsl-persistent`, `tirx`, `ptx`, `cake`, and `small-bh` for KDA.
- Share the KDA adapter across Kimi-K3, GLM and the bounded-gate shared Kimi path, including normalization and recurrent-state handling.
- Build contiguous int64 offsets with a tensor version counter for native KDA paths under inference mode. Omit sequence-order hints for persistent CuTe DSL, TIRx and PTX, which reject them.
- Validate hardware, dtype and gate limits. Protect borrowed state, permit updates to temporary gathered state, and reject unsupported cuDNN checkpoint and batch-invariance requests. Add CLI, metadata, state-contract and GPU replay tests.

### New arguments

| Argument | Values | Use with |
|---|---|---|
| `--flashinfer-gdn-backend` | `auto`, `cudnn` | `--gdn-prefill-backend flashinfer` |
| `--flashinfer-kda-backend` | `auto`, `cute-dsl`, `cute-dsl-persistent`, `tirx`, `ptx`, `cake`, `small-bh`, `cudnn` | `--kda-prefill-backend flashinfer` |

Both resolve to `auto` when omitted. `auto` delegates to FlashInfer's dispatcher; explicit choices retain FlashInfer's input checks. The existing provider argument must select FlashInfer to use these paths.

KDA state requirements: `auto`, `cake`, and `small-bh` use BF16; `cute-dsl` and `cudnn` accept BF16 or FP32; `cute-dsl-persistent`, `tirx`, and `ptx` require FP32. Set the existing `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` argument to match. Extra shape, GPU and dependency limits still apply. In particular, PTX requires SM103a and H64/H96. Persistent CuTe DSL, TIRx and PTX require an explicit warmed workspace for prefill graph capture; this adapter does not manage it, so use eager prefill for those choices.

```bash
# Kimi-K3: FlashInfer auto prefill with BF16 recurrent state
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --kda-prefill-backend flashinfer --flashinfer-kda-backend auto \
  --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16

# Qwen GDN: explicit cuDNN prefill
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B \
  --gdn-prefill-backend flashinfer --flashinfer-gdn-backend cudnn
```

These examples show backend options; add the model's normal deployment flags.

## Validation

Current branch: changed-file pre-commit, including Ruff, mypy and test wiring, passed. `git diff --check` passed. An isolated CPU harness ran **164 checks** for backend forwarding, state dtypes, inference/strided offsets, sequence-order metadata, CLI choices and existing GDN selection contracts. The accepted KDA values match [FlashInfer main at `c0e62fa7`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/c0e62fa7b18cbf051f729214984c235eb521a551/flashinfer/kda.py).

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  ../artifacts/vllm-kda-backends-20261012/test_kda_backends_cpu.py -q
# 164 passed; isolated source-level harness outside the PR.
```

AWS runtime passed 74 KDA GPU tests and 44 metadata tests for the original auto/cuDNN paths. Results below retain their measured revisions and are not measurements of this backend-list update.

> **Dependency caveat:** These FlashInfer prefill paths require **FlashInfer 0.7.2**. This PR does not update vLLM's `flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1` pin, so the serving environment must install 0.7.2 explicitly. The full backend list follows FlashInfer main at `c0e62fa7`; use a build containing the selected backend. Native CuTe DSL needs `nvidia-cutlass-dsl>=4.7` except for `small-bh`; TIRx needs CUDA-enabled TVM with TIRx and `tirx_kernels.tirx_lite`; PTX needs `ptxas>=13.2` and TVM FFI. The cuDNN path was validated with frontend **1.31.0** and cuDNN **9.20** on SM100/SM103. Benchmark results below retain their exact measured revisions.

### Latest microbenchmark results — GB200

Lyris job **3275022**. **B1 × 8,192-token prefill**; cells show **active CPU / GPU kernel interval union, µs/call** (lower is better), averaged over four fresh-process medians.

| Model | vLLM auto | FlashInfer auto | FlashInfer cuDNN |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Kimi-K3 H6 / TP16 | 91.216 / 319.663 | 213.388 / 115.296 | 156.604 / 111.760 |
| GLM-5.3 H16 / TP4 | 163.516 / 457.645 | 285.176 / 340.012 | 158.200 / 184.161 |
| QwenNext Q8/V16 / TP2 | 259.956 / 118.064 | 265.132 / 117.528 | 219.848 / 129.161 |
| Qwen3.5 Q16/V32 / TP1 | 272.872 / 179.055 | 277.384 / 179.354 | 230.468 / 171.261 |

For Kimi and GLM, vLLM auto uses FlashKDA. Both Qwen auto columns use the same native FlashInfer provider.

Kimi FlashInfer auto selects cuDNN for this shape. Against the previous FlashInfer baseline, GPU time falls **199.566 → 115.296 µs (42.23%)**; CPU time rises **173.512 → 213.388 µs (22.98%)**. GLM auto stays native. These runs establish no GDN auto GPU gain.

Measured FlashInfer baseline `461037fb` → candidate `669a153d` ([#6259](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6259)); unchanged vLLM caller `29ad8bda`. Frontend **1.31.0**, cuDNN **9.20**, Torch **2.13.0+cu132**; BF16 KDA state and FP32 GDN state. **555 scoped tests passed; 2,880 GPU traces passed audit.**

CPU and GPU were measured separately and must not be added. These are synthetic operator timings, not serving TTFT; small CPU shifts also occur in unchanged controls. [Full B1/B8/B32 prefill/decode results, repeats and raw evidence](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/agopal/kda-vllm-microbench/-/blob/codex/kda-vllm-microbench/measurements/lyris-native-pools-3275022/report.md) (NVIDIA access required).

### Kimi K3 inference — AWS B300, C1 and C8

**8× B300; one 3,600-second sending phase per point.** AWS FlashKDA and FlashInfer auto use the same runtime and node, with BF16 recurrent state, TP8/DCP8, FP4 weights, FP8 KV, DSpark K7 synthetic acceptance 3.84, prefix cache and Mooncake enabled.

| Concurrency | Series | Total tokens/s/chip | Output tokens/s/chip | Median tokens/s/user |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| C1 | Published InferenceX [C1](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/inference/agentic/439932) | 2,025.33 | 15.13 | 236.41 |
| C1 | AWS FlashKDA (BF16 control) | 2,055.41 | 15.52 | 225.82 |
| C1 | AWS FlashInfer auto | 2,159.70 | 16.00 | 259.98 |
| C8 | Published InferenceX [C8](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/inference/agentic/439935) | 5,180.44 | 40.63 | 127.88 |
| C8 | AWS FlashKDA (BF16 control) | 5,628.14 | 43.05 | 142.79 |
| C8 | AWS FlashInfer auto | 5,790.57 | 43.94 | 169.20 |

**FlashInfer auto change versus the AWS FlashKDA BF16 control:**

| Concurrency | Total tokens/s/chip | Output tokens/s/chip | Median tokens/s/user |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| C1 | +5.07% | +3.08% | +15.13% |
| C8 | +2.89% | +2.06% | +18.50% |

Total throughput includes cached input plus output. Median user rate is **1 / median TPOT**. Rates use the exact raw request window, including completed requests during drain; warmups are excluded. All four AWS points passed validation with **zero request errors or cancellations**. Eight Mooncake lookup errors occurred at startup per point; none occurred during warmup or profiling. JIT, event-loop and cleanup warnings remain in the evidence.

AWS measured vLLM `156420052`, FlashInfer `a7103ae2` (**0.7.2**), frontend **1.31.0**, cuDNN **9.20.0.48**, Torch **2.13.0+cu130**. These measurements predate the current rebase and use a different FlashInfer revision from the microbenchmark; they do not establish that AWS auto selected cuDNN.

**Comparison limits:** FlashKDA supports one intermediate prefill checkpoint block; FlashInfer auto supports zero. Cache settings stayed enabled, but this capability differs. Published InferenceX values are external reference points with runtime, state-dtype and platform differences. Each AWS point is one run; these results do not isolate a kernel-only gain or establish statistical significance.

<details>
<summary>Earlier model evaluation and limits</summary>

The earlier GB200 serving study used vLLM `7c3c1a3f`, FlashInfer `73b63f88`, and frontend `7f85a1f7`. In baseline/auto/cuDNN/cuDNN/auto/baseline order, full GSM8K correct counts were Kimi-K3 **1259/1254/1251/1247/1246/1248 of 1319** and Qwen3-Next **1142/1149/1136/1141/1149/1142 of 1319**. Invalid-answer counts were **1/1/1/1/2/1** and **1/0/0/0/1/0**, respectively. Model accuracy equivalence is not established.

The GLM auto C128 run failed with an RPC timeout and a CUDA error during cleanup. Qwen3.5 cuDNN missed its GSM64 gate (55/64 versus 56 required); those comparisons are incomplete. [Full scores, repeats and failures](https://github.com/Anerudhan/vllm/blob/932292abf35f7948d89255deb60bb844534c7b67/benchmarks/linear_attention/latest_full_gb200_results.md) remain on the source branch. The AWS workload uses synthetic speculative acceptance and does not measure model accuracy.

</details>

## Details

The shared adapter calls FlashInfer's public dispatchers. The cuDNN KDA path uses fused additive Q/K normalization and supports bounded gates with `-5 <= lower_bound < 0`. See `docs/configuration/optimization.md` for usage and limits.

Duplicate-work checks found no matching prefill-selection PR. Related #60470 changes KDA decode; #60050 adds GDN checkpoints; #60105 optimizes native GDN gate conversion and offsets. This PR adds explicit prefill implementation selection and shared KDA integration. It does not include those separate optimizations. AI assistance was used.

title: [Spec Decode] Add draft_context_window to bound DFlash/DSpark draft attention
body:
## What this does

Adds an opt-in `draft_context_window` to `--speculative-config` for DFlash and DSpark (MRV2). When set, the drafter only attends to the last N context tokens. Positions stay absolute. Target verification doesn't change. Default is `None`, so nothing changes unless you turn it on.

Context: #47930. We run Kimi K3 with `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` on long agent sessions, and acceptance falls off a cliff past ~128K. This fixes it for us.

## Why

Accept length (k=3, out of 4) on main, DCP 1:

| context | main | main + `draft_context_window: 32768` |
|---|---|---|
| 0-16K | 2.48 | 2.49 |
| 16-64K | 2.39 | 2.40 |
| 64-128K | 2.29 | 2.27 |
| 128-256K | **1.45** | **2.29** |
| 256K+ | **1.26** | **2.22** |
| mixed 16-300K, c16 | 1.90 | 2.28 |

Below 128K: no change. Above it: back to short-context levels. Output tok/s goes up +31% at 128-256K and +23% at 256K+, +9% on the mixed run.

Same thing with DCP 4 (with #59392 applied, since main still crashes there, see below):

| context | main | window 32K |
|---|---|---|
| 64-128K | 2.26 | 2.29 |
| 128-256K | 1.46 | 2.28 |
| 256K+ | 1.26 | 2.20 |
| mixed c16 | 1.92 | 2.27 |

## Is it the kernel? No

Same build, no window, only the drafter's attention backend swapped:

| context | FLASHINFER_MLA | TRITON_MLA |
|---|---|---|
| 128-256K | 1.448 | 1.437 |
| 256K+ | 1.257 | 1.253 |

Same collapse on both. And on v0.30 it's the same with prefix caching and KV offload fully off (numbers in #47930), so it's not restored KV either. Looks like the drafter just doesn't generalise past what it was trained on (the model card only goes to ~95K). 64K behaves like 32K. I can't prove which shared bit is to blame (drafter weights vs. its RoPE/YaRN handling), but the window fixes it either way.

## Quality

GSM8K, first 200, `reasoning_effort: low`, temp 1.0:

| | main | window 32K |
|---|---|---|
| plain prompts (window never kicks in) | 0.985 | 0.990 |
| same problems behind a ~98K prefix (window drops ~65K) | 0.985 | 0.980 |

1 problem out of 200 either way. Noise.

## Soak

c24, prompts 16-400K, 30 min, same seed. Prefill-bound on purpose (pool oversubscribed).

| | main | window run A | window run B |
|---|---|---|---|
| requests | 331 | 341 | 345 |
| errors / restarts | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| accept length | 1.61 | 2.27 | 2.27 |
| output tok/s | 130 | 153 | 146 |
| TTFT p50 | 58 s | 48 s | 47 s |

No shm_broadcast hangs after load, no Xid. One heads-up: our repeated-tail detector flagged one output in run A (129K prompt, ran to `max_tokens`). Didn't capture the text that time, so I couldn't look at it. Run B captured text and flagged nothing. 1 in 686 vs 0 in 331, so no conclusion either way. The shift can't reach target inputs or target KV (more below), and with probabilistic drafting the output distribution doesn't depend on the drafter anyway.

## How it works

In `DFlashSpeculator.propose`, right after `prepare_dflash_inputs` has computed slot mappings from the full table, a small Triton kernel does, per request:

- excess = `max(seq_len - num_query - N, 0)`, rounded down to whole block-table entries
- shift that request's `input_block_tables[gid]` row left by that many entries
- subtract the dropped positions from `seq_lens`

Keys already carry absolute RoPE, query positions aren't touched, so relative positions inside the window are unchanged. Draft sees at least N tokens, less than N plus one entry.

Why editing those buffers in place is fine:
- `input_block_tables` get re-gathered from the persistent tables at the start of every step, before the target runs. Nothing after `propose` reads them in the same step.
- `seq_lens` is the draft's own buffer.
- Slot mappings are computed before the shift, so KV writes land where they should.
- Dummy runs (capture, profiling) skip it.

DCP: one entry covers `block_size * dcp_size` positions, and `block_size % cp_kv_cache_interleave_size == 0` is already enforced, so whole entries keep every position on its rank. Draft KV groups share `seq_lens`, so all groups drop the same count (a multiple of `dcp_size * lcm(block sizes)`), and only the last one writes it back.

CUDA graphs: runs eagerly before replay and only writes buffers the graph already reads. No new host syncs.

Scope: all DFlash-family speculators go through this `propose`, so it covers `dflash` and `dspark`. Rejected for other methods and on V1, so it never gets silently ignored. Only measured on DSpark / Kimi K3 (MLA drafter). Non-MLA drafters take the same path with `dcp_size=1`, which the unit tests cover.

Tradeoffs: you lose long-range context the drafter could in theory use. For this drafter that's a net loss past ~128K anyway. The right N depends on the drafter, hence off by default. No memory saved, only attention is bounded.

## Related

- #47930: the issue. Our data there shows the collapse with nothing restored.
- #47926: hides prefix-cache-restored blocks from the draft. On this model those blocks hold valid draft KV, so it only helps by accident (shorter context). Hand-rebased on 0.30 it got 2.07 / 1.89 vs 2.30 / 2.25 for the window. Independent of this PR.
- #53827: similar bounded draft attention for EAGLE3 via sliding window. Different speculator and path. Happy to align the field name if both land.
- #60320: trims DSpark context precompute for all-SWA drafters. Compute-only, complementary.
- Side note: main still can't boot Kimi K3 + DSpark with DCP>1 on FlashInfer MLA (#59065). Our DCP 4 runs used #59392.

## Tests

```bash
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD                 # all pass
pytest tests/test_config.py -k draft_context_window -v               # CPU: 1 passed
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py -v         # B300: 10 passed (5 old + 5 new)
```

`tests/test_config.py -k "spec or draft or dflash or dspark"`: 98 passed, 5 failed. The same 5 fail on untouched main on this CPU box (three `test_vllm_config_defaults[RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3-*]`, `test_draft_model_enables_async_scheduling_by_default`, `test_dflash_allows_async_scheduling`).

Rebased onto main 8c60cf07b on 2026-10-19. The one conflict was in `vllm/config/speculative.py`, where #53987 added the FLy fields next to `draft_context_window`; both are kept. Nothing on main has touched the DFlash speculator or its test file since the previous rebase. #59511 moved the context combine and `prepare_context_anchor` into the FULL graph. Neither reads the draft `seq_lens` or block tables the window shifts, and the context K/V slots are still computed from the full table before the shift. After the rebase, pre-commit passes, and `test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py` gives 10 passed on CPU under `TRITON_INTERPRET=1`; with the window turned into a no-op, the 5 new tests fail.

New tests: window applied after slot mappings (through `propose`, DCP 1 and 2), whole-entry rounding, two groups with different block sizes, a long in-place shift across kernel chunks, and config validation.

GPU setup: TP8 on 8x B300, Kimi K3 fp8 KV, k=3, probabilistic drafting + block rejection. `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-fe4df3df0` with the spec-decode files overlaid from this branch's base, so the draft path equals main. Synthetic multi-turn agent sessions over public-domain text, natural stop, `max_tokens` 2048, prefix caching and KV offload on.

title: [Perf][HiSparse] Reduce residency hash probes
body:
Related to #60072.

At top-k 2,048, the resolver can fill 2,048 of its 2,049 hash slots. Looking up cached rows that aren't selected for the current step then requires long probe chains.

This lets the table grow toward the existing four-slots-per-position target, within the device's shared-memory budget.

Default shared memory rises from 26,148 to 75,300 bytes per block. Resident-only calls cost an extra 0.16–0.90 µs in the kernel checks. This is separate from #60103's slot-invalidation and all-resident work.

On **4 H200s, TP4, GLM-5.2-NVFP4**, with 32 concurrent requests, 16,384-token random prompts and 1,024-token outputs, median throughput improved **130.26 → 133.45 tok/s (+2.45%)**. Three runs each ranged from 130.21–130.32 and 133.36–133.69 tok/s. Reverting gave 130.01 tok/s.

This used FP8 KV, 10 GiB GPU KV per rank, a 64 GiB host pool, CUDA graphs, and no prefix caching. The serving comparison predates the rebase (`d61081dc` → `94b81a59`) and used targeted native builds with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Post-rebase serving, speculative serving, and other GPU architectures haven't been benchmarked.

On the final commit, `b605dfa0`:

- **1 H100 80GB:** 106 focused tests and 4 end-to-end tests passed with MRV2 and GPU sync checking enabled.
- **1 H200:** 18 resolver cases matched baseline indices, ownership, and LRU state. The 4× target beat 2× in every host-backed case tested.
- Pre-commit passed.

The earlier serving run also passed 12 cache-state comparisons and four short output checks. No full model-quality evaluation was run.

title: [HiSparse] Support the FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA backend
body:
## Purpose

`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (first sparse MLA choice on Hopper for NoPE models such as GLM-5.3-Flash) has no HiSparse path: it converts the logical top-k through `block_table` and reads the layer's paged KV, which holds stale rows for pages HiSparse offloaded. On GLM-5.3-Flash (TP4, H200, prefix caching on) GSM8K degrades across repeated passes on one server: 0.901 → 0.834 → 0.745.

This mirrors the HiSparse branch of the other sparse backends:
- decode rows and resident prefill-only batches: HiSparse physical top-k + hot cache;
- otherwise prefill rows: `stage_prefill_rows` + convert over the staging workspace.

SM90-specific: the backend plans one `BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper` per batch in `build()`. Decode-only and prefill-only batches keep that single plan (HiSparse's residency output keeps the indexer's valid-prefix layout, which the plan already assumes). Mixed decode + staged-prefill batches read two caches, so with HiSparse the builder plans the prefill rows in a second `_SM90State` (sharing the float workspace); its device `kv_end` clamp takes a row offset so it derives contexts from the right batch rows. Planning stays in `build()`, outside graph capture.

Not a duplicate: no open PR adds HiSparse to this backend. Companion: #61243 adds a `supports_hisparse()` capability; whichever lands second sets it to `True` for this backend.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py` (new cases fail on `main`)
- GLM-5.3-Flash, TP4 H200, HiSparse + prefix caching, `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90`, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` repeated passes on one server

## Test Result

Unit tests (H200): `test_flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py` 32 passed; the new HiSparse cases fail on `main`.

GSM8K, GLM-5.3-Flash rev eb9eb208, 4x H200 TP4, bf16 KV, HiSparse (32 GiB host pool), prefix caching on, max_num_seqs 32, `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90`, on top of #61243 + #60805 (needed for Flash to start with HiSparse). Three passes on one server: 1319 Q at concurrency 32 (twice), then 200 Q at concurrency 1:

| | c32 pass 1 | c32 pass 2 | c1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| before (`main` backend, HiSparse) | 0.901 | 0.834 | 0.745 |
| this PR, `--enforce-eager` | 0.911 | 0.915 | 0.930 |
| this PR, CUDA graphs (PIECEWISE) | 0.917 | crashed (see below) | – |

Both runs used `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`. Two shared HiSparse issues on GLM-5.3-Flash block a clean graph-mode run. Neither is in this backend: FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE and FLASHMLA_SPARSE show the same failures.
- Without `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING`, an illegal memory access happens during the capture warmup (and in eager serving on the FA backend). Serializing launches hides it, which points to a missing cross-stream dependency in the HiSparse swap/convert streams.
- In graph mode, `HiSparse swap rows exceed the configured speculative decode capacity: stop=62, capacity=32`. The per-forward `_swap_step` reset (`prepare_group_for_batch`) only runs from the connector's `prepare_forward` or from `prepare_kv_cache_update`. The latter is inside the captured region, so it does not re-run on breakable-graph replay.

These go in separate PRs.

AI assistance (Claude) was used; the submitter reviews every line.

title: [Bugfix] Hybrid prefix caching: keep the Mamba prompt-boundary state until the request ends and evict it after its attention blocks
body:
## Overview

Fixes the lifetime of a hybrid request's reusable Mamba "align" state block: it stays referenced for as long as the request runs, and at request end it is the last of the request's blocks to reach the LRU free queue. FIX #61281

## Claims

- A running hybrid request no longer loses its prompt-boundary Mamba state to other requests' allocations: `MambaManager` holds one reference on that block from the moment it is registered, or taken over from the cache by a resumed or sibling request, until the request is freed, across the range retirement, the running-state swap and the partial-tail CoW copy.
- At request end attention groups are freed before Mamba groups on both the direct (`KVCacheCoordinator.free`) and the deferred (`pop_blocks_for_free`) path, so the single state block is evicted after the attention blocks it belongs with, not before.
- The next turn of a conversation now hits the previous prompt in every group; before, the attention group hit while the Mamba group returned 0 and the reconciled hit was 0.
- Cost: one extra block per Mamba group per running request (the running state plus the boundary state). Single-group and non-Mamba hybrid models are unaffected: no behaviour change in their managers, and the free order is the identity for them.

## Validation

Deterministic reproducer from the issue (no GPU, drives `KVCacheManager`), before and after:

```text
# main
--- 1. prompt boundary on a Mamba block boundary (remove_skipped_blocks)
after 1 decode step: snapshot ref_cnt=0 (0 = in the free queue while 'a' still runs)
after 12 unrelated requests while 'a' decodes: snapshot recycled
next turn: per-group hits (64, 0) tokens, reconciled hit 0
--- 2. prompt boundary inside a Mamba block (CoW copy released)
after 12 unrelated requests while 'a' decodes: snapshot recycled
next turn: per-group hits (48, 0) tokens, reconciled hit 0
--- 3. eviction order at request end
free queue position: snapshot 26, attention blocks [27, 28, 29, 30]   (both group orders, both free paths)

# this PR
after 1 decode step: snapshot ref_cnt=1
after 12 unrelated requests while 'a' decodes: snapshot still cached
next turn: per-group hits (64, 64) tokens, reconciled hit 64
next turn: per-group hits (48, 48) tokens, reconciled hit 48
free queue position: snapshot 30, attention blocks [26, 27, 28, 29]
```

New tests in `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_boundary_snapshot_lifetime.py` (fail on main, pass here):

- `test_boundary_state_outlives_decode[block-aligned|partial-tail × dense|sparse]`: the state block keeps a reference through decode and through 12 unrelated requests cycling the pool, the request holds at most two Mamba blocks, every block is back in the pool after `free`, and the follow-up prompt hits the boundary in both groups.
- `test_boundary_state_held_after_cache_hit[... × preempted|sibling × dense|sparse]`: a request that takes the boundary state over from the cache (re-admitted after preemption, or a second request with the same prompt whose producer finishes first) holds it the same way.
- `test_request_end_evicts_attention_before_boundary_state[attn-first|mamba-first × free|deferred]`: after the request ends, the state block sits behind all of the request's hashed attention blocks in the free queue.

Existing suites run locally on a CPU-only build (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`): 
| suite | result on this branch | note |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_boundary_snapshot_lifetime.py` (new) | 16 passed | fail on main |
| `tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`, `test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py` | 100 passed | |
| `tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py`, `test_swa_inflight_window_free.py`, `test_prefix_replay.py`, `test_async_scheduler.py`, `test_priority_preemption_bug.py` | all passed | |
| `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py` | 170 passed, 3 HiSparse failures | the same 3 fail on unmodified main in this environment (no accelerator) |
| `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, `test_kv_cache_utils.py` | all pass except the multimodal / encoder-cache tests | those cannot inspect a Llava config offline; identical on main |
| `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/`, `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py`, `test_mooncake_store_connector.py` | 250 passed, 6 failed + 2 errors | failures need an accelerator device or a model; identical on main |

Total over these suites on the branch: 908 passed, 53 failed, 2 errors; the failure set is exactly the environmental set seen on unmodified main.


`pre-commit run --all-files`: clean (ruff, mypy, typos, SPDX, test tethering and the rest all pass; nothing modified).

## Details

Root cause. Align mode keeps only the running state per request; every other state is a prefix-cache entry that lives in the free queue with its hash. That is fine for intermediate states, but the state at the prompt's reusable boundary is the one block a later turn needs together with the request's attention blocks, and those stay referenced until the request finishes. Three paths push the boundary block into the free queue a step into decode: `remove_skipped_blocks` -> `_remove_blocks_in_range` (boundary on a block boundary), the `last_state_block_idx` swap in the same function, and the release of the CoW copy of a partial tail by `Scheduler._free_cow_retained_blocks` once the copy step has run. Any allocation then recycles it (`get_new_blocks` -> `_maybe_evict_cached_block`), and the hybrid lookup is the minimum over groups. At request end the groups were freed in config order (direct path) or reversed config order (deferred path), so depending on the model's group order the state block was the first of the request's blocks to be evicted.

Design. Rather than special-casing each free path, the manager takes one reference on the boundary block on the request's behalf (`_retain_boundary_block`, mirroring the CoW retention refs that already exist) wherever the request comes to own that state: a full block whose hash ends at the boundary (`cache_blocks`), a re-keyed prefill checkpoint or a partial tail (`_cache_partial_tail_block`), and the hit block adopted by a resumed or sibling request (`add_local_computed_blocks`; registering the request's own boundary later replaces that hold). One helper, `_prompt_boundary`, defines the position at every site. The existing free paths then only drop the block's ref to 1 and null it out of the request's table as before. On the producer CoW the hold moves with the hash to `cow_block`, so the scheduler's post-copy release leaves the copy referenced. `pop_blocks_for_free` releases the hold: if the block is still in the request's table it just drops the extra ref, otherwise it lists the block first so it is the last one freed. The coordinator orders group frees once (`_free_order`: attention first, Mamba last) and `pop_blocks_for_free` returns groups in the reverse of that order so the caller's reversed free matches `free`.

Only the prompt boundary is held. Under sparse retention (the default `prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`) that is the request's only hashed state apart from a shared-prefix junction; under dense retention intermediate states keep their existing free-queue lifetime, so memory stays bounded at two blocks per Mamba group per running request.

Not covered / residual risk:

- A shared-prefix junction state (`shared_prefix_boundary`, behind `enable_mamba_shared_prefix_checkpoint`, off by default) is registered the same way and keeps the old lifetime; holding it too would double the per-request cost for a feature that is off by default, so it is left out.
- EAGLE/MTP: the hold follows `drop_eagle_checkpoint_block` like the partial-tail registration does, so it lands on the dropped-block boundary; the speculative scratch blocks are above the running state and never hashed, so `_relocate_speculative_block`'s writable assertion is unaffected.
- `evict_blocks` (connector-driven eviction) strips the hash from a held block; the block then stays allocated until the request ends. Harmless, and the same as a held attention block today.
- Non-align Mamba modes and non-Mamba groups take none of the new paths.

title: [Bugfix] Merge supported KV cache layouts across pipeline stages instead of asserting they match
body:
## Overview With pipeline parallelism, a model whose stages use different attention backends fails at startup. `resolve_kv_cache_layout` asserts that every worker reports the same list of supported KV cache layouts, but PP stages hold different layers, so their lists can differ. This PR makes the engine core merge the worker lists with the same rule `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` already uses for the backends of one worker. This addresses failure 1 ("PP2 on SM100") of #60791. Failures 2-5 in that issue are not touched here. ## Claims - `vllm serve` of a 10-layer MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 with `--pipeline-parallel-size 2` on B200 now starts, picks `LBHNC`, and answers requests. Before, it died in `_initialize_kv_caches` with `AssertionError: Workers disagree on supported KV cache layouts`. - When all workers report the same list (one GPU, TP only, PP with equal stages), the result is the same as before. - If no layout is supported by every worker, the existing `ValueError` is still raised. - New unit test `test_pipeline_stages_resolve_a_layout_every_stage_supports`. It fails on the old code with the bug's assertion. ## Validation Hardware: 2 x NVIDIA B200 (SM100, x86_64). The issue was reported on GB200 (aarch64), which has the same SM. Software: vLLM `0.31.1rc1.dev173+g8cbd5d030` (commit `8cbd5d03006c33185f402249ff2b448efd594986`), with and without this patch. Attention backend chosen: FLASHINFER. Model: the issue's 10-layer cut of `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` is not published, so I rebuilt it from the Hub checkpoint (revision `c5454eb03678d8710e54a4e0fc681b9f3b4a3dba`) with the script below. Layers 0-2 are dense and layers 3-9 are sparse. I cannot show it is tensor-identical to the reporter's cut.
cut script (replace $HF_HOME with your Hugging Face cache path) ```python # Cut MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 to its first 10 decoder layers (+ vision tower), as the report describes. import json, re, glob, os, shutil, sys from safetensors import safe_open from safetensors.torch import save_file src = glob.glob("$HF_HOME/hub/models--MiniMaxAI--MiniMax-M3-MXFP8/snapshots/*")[0] dst = "/tmp/m3-10layer" os.makedirs(dst, exist_ok=True) N = 10 for f in os.listdir(src): if f.endswith(".safetensors") or f == "model.safetensors.index.json": continue shutil.copy(os.path.realpath(os.path.join(src, f)), os.path.join(dst, f)) def trunc(o): if isinstance(o, dict): return {k: trunc(v) for k, v in o.items()} if isinstance(o, list) and len(o) == 60 and all(isinstance(x, int) for x in o): return o[:N] return o cfg = json.load(open(os.path.join(dst, "config.json"))) cfg["text_config"] = trunc(cfg["text_config"]); cfg["text_config"]["num_hidden_layers"] = N q = cfg["quantization_config"] q["ignored_layers"] = [x for x in q["ignored_layers"] if not (m := re.search(r"layers\.(\d+)\.", x)) or int(m.group(1)) < N] json.dump(cfg, open(os.path.join(dst, "config.json"), "w"), indent=2) wm = {} for shard in sorted(glob.glob(src + "/*.safetensors")): out = {} with safe_open(shard, "pt") as f: for k in f.keys(): m = re.search(r"language_model\.model\.layers\.(\d+)\.", k) if m and int(m.group(1)) >= N: continue out[k] = f.get_tensor(k) name = os.path.basename(shard) save_file(out, os.path.join(dst, name), metadata={"format": "pt"}) for k in out: wm[k] = name print(name, len(out), flush=True) json.dump({"metadata": {}, "weight_map": wm}, open(os.path.join(dst, "model.safetensors.index.json"), "w")) ```
Reproducer. It fails at startup, so no request is needed to see the bug: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 \ vllm serve /tmp/m3-10layer --trust-remote-code --block-size 128 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' \ --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager --enable-prefix-caching --pipeline-parallel-size 2 ``` Before: 4 of 4 runs failed like this, about 160 s after start. 3 runs used the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-8cbd5d03006c33185f402249ff2b448efd594986` image and 1 used a source install. One more source run never got this far, because of a file permission problem in my setup, so it is not counted. ``` AssertionError: Workers disagree on supported KV cache layouts: [['LBHNC', 'BLHNC'], ['LBNHC', 'LBHNC', 'BLNHC', 'BLHNC', 'BHLNC', 'LHBNC']]. ``` After: 5 of 5 runs started and answered one request with HTTP 200. 3 of the runs used the final code (the last one was run by a separate reviewer) and 2 used an earlier version of the patch. ``` Using LBHNC KV cache layout. INFO: Application startup complete. "POST /v1/completions HTTP/1.1" 200 OK ``` The request was `curl -s localhost:8000/v1/completions -d '{"model":"/tmp/m3-10layer","prompt":"The capital of France is","max_tokens":8,"temperature":0}'`. The returned text is junk, which is expected from a 10-layer cut of a much deeper model. I did not run an accuracy eval. Startup takes more than 10 minutes, mostly for FlashInfer autotuning of the MXFP8 MoE kernels. Unit tests (run with `--noconftest`, because my environment had no `tblib`, which `tests/conftest.py` imports): - `pytest --noconftest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py -k pipeline_stages`: passes with this patch. With the old `vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py` it fails with the same `Workers disagree on supported KV cache layouts` assertion. - `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py`: 197 passed, 76 skipped. The 8 errors are tests that need the `caplog_vllm` fixture from `tests/conftest.py`. The 2 failures are PP tests that need 4 GPUs (`World size (4) is larger than the number of available GPUs (1)`). They fail the same way on the old code with 1 GPU, and they pass with 4 GPUs visible. - `pre-commit run --files` on both changed files: all hooks pass. ## Details Root cause: each worker reports the layouts that all of its own attention backends support (`WorkerBase.get_supported_kv_cache_layouts`). `resolve_kv_cache_layout` then asserted that all reports are equal, because "all ranks run the same backends". With PP, each stage builds only its own layers. For this model with PP2: - PP0 holds layers 0-4. Layers 0-2 use FlashInfer, which supports only `(LBHNC, BLHNC)` on SM100, so PP0 reports `['LBHNC', 'BLHNC']`. - PP1 holds layers 5-9, which are all sparse. `MINIMAX_M3_SPARSE` and `MINIMAX_M3_SPARSE_INDEXER` declare no layout set, so PP1 reports the default list of six layouts. The two lists differ, but they share `LBHNC` and `BLHNC`. With PP=1 the model works, because one worker sees all backends and intersects their sets. A debug run that printed each stage's backends confirmed this. Fix: the merge code in `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` moves into a helper, `_merge_supported_layouts`, and `resolve_kv_cache_layout` now uses the helper on the worker reports. - Identical lists keep their order, so setups where all workers agree are unchanged. - Otherwise, the candidates are the layouts that appear in every list, and the layout that the most lists put first wins. - A worker that reports the default list (no backend declares a set) does not vote, in the same way that a backend that declares nothing does not vote inside one worker. Without this rule, an all-sparse stage would vote for `LBNHC`, and PP could pick a different layout from PP=1. The second case of the new test covers this. - If no layout is in every list, the code still raises `ValueError: No KV cache layout satisfies every supported set`. Tradeoff: the removed assertion also caught TP ranks of one stage that report different lists, for example after one rank picked a different backend by mistake. Those lists are now merged like PP stages. The chosen layout is still one that every worker supports. A per-stage check could be added back, but the engine core would then need to know which worker is in which stage, and this fix does not need that. Limitations: only failure 1 of the issue is fixed. Validation used B200 with FLASHINFER and `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, not GB200. ---

title: [Core] Shared abstractions for specialized decode kernels
body:
_(the text below is written by myself)_

This is an effort to (1) increase standardization and (2) limit LoC changes in model files as a result from adding numerous specialized decode kernels (_aka "monokernels"_). 

The kernels themselves will naturally remain difficult to review thoroughly, but ideally model code should remain easy to review. The abstraction layer should deliberately be made as thin as possible,

Heavily inspired by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61867, and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60904.

**Note: this PR drops `--monokernel` in favor of `--specialized-decode`**

# 1. Goal

**An author of a specialized decode kernel should write:**

1. A FlyDSL/CuTeDSL implementation and its utilities, in `vllm/models/<model>/<vendor>/`
2. The conditions under which it can run
3. Minimal glue connecting it to the model code

**The author should not have to write:**

1. Another new way to glue the kernel into the model code
3. Basic config checks during start up, re-used by many specialized kernels needs anyway (parallelism, spec decode, graph mode)
4. Checks of whether to run the specizlied kernel or regular vllm code at every step
5. TP rank agreement of the above
6. Updating of CUDA graph capture sizes
7. Kernel selection when one model has more than one specialized kernel
8. Optional: JIT/warm-up registration


This PR implements the latter points.

# 2. How

Declare when the specialized kernel can run:
```python
# refuse causes crash, skip causes fallback to regular vllm execution

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DecodeSpec(Generic[KernelT]):
    name: str
    supports: frozenset[Feature]
    widths: Callable[[VllmConfig], tuple[int, ...]]
    refuse_config: Callable[[VllmConfig], list[str]]
    refuse_model: Callable[[Any], list[str]]
    refuse_caches: Callable[[VllmConfig, KernelT, Mapping[str, Any]], list[str]]
    skip_step: Callable[[VllmConfig, KernelT, int], str | None]
    build: Callable[[VllmConfig, Any, tuple[int, ...]], KernelT]
```

`KernelT` is a stand-in for the entire model forward, implementing

```python
class DecodeImpl(Protocol):
    cache_layers: tuple[str, ...]

    def run(self, step: Step, input_ids, inputs_embeds, **kwargs) -> Any: ...
    def bind_caches(self, caches: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None: ...
```

**Optional:** A kernel that compiles its launches from keys (one per width, per layer plan, or whatever the kernel keys on) can additionally implement

```python
@runtime_checkable
class DecodeWarmable(Protocol):
    def warmup_keys(self) -> list[Any]: ...
    def compile(self, key: Any) -> None: ...
```

which will cause the dispatcher to auto-register it for warmup. The existing DSv41 implementation uses this, and so would https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60889, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60731, and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60683. The Kimi K3 nvidia kernel jits eagerly since its specialized decode kernel is not created in a region with an active jit registry; hence, this feature is optional.

Once the kernel author has written their CuteDSL/FlyDSL kernel, the two remaining points

> 2. The conditions under which it can run
> 3. Minimal glue connecting it to the model code

is implemented through a Spec and wiring the kernel code through a DecodeImpl. The remainder is taken place by the shared `SpecializedDecode` utility.

_Note: we deliberately put no further constraint on how one implements `run`. There is a big benefit letting each model decide exactly how to structure this. We've already seen many different ways of structuring the underlying flydsl/cutedsl kernels._

## 2.1 Model-side code

The model-side code will look like this:

```python
class MyForCausalLM(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config, prefix=""):
        self.decode_spec = select_decode_spec(vllm_config, SPECS)
        self.specialized_decode: SpecializedDecode[MyKernel] | None = None

    def process_weights_after_loading(self):
        # optionally: this code can also be placed in the model state init, but then you cannot benefit from auto-registration of warmup
        if self.decode_spec is not None:
            self.specialized_decode = SpecializedDecode(
                self.model, self.vllm_config, self.decode_spec
            )

    def forward(self, input_ids, positions, intermediate_tensors=None, inputs_embeds=None, **kwargs):
        decode = self.specialized_decode
        if decode is not None:
            step = decode.plan(positions, intermediate_tensors)
            if step is not None:
                return decode.run(step, input_ids, inputs_embeds, **kwargs)
        return self.model(input_ids, positions, intermediate_tensors, inputs_embeds, **kwargs)
```

plus one hook to prepare the kv cache

```python
class MyModelState(DefaultModelState):
    def initialize_kv_cache(self, kv_cache_config, block_tables):
        super().initialize_kv_cache(kv_cache_config, block_tables)
        if self.model.specialized_decode is not None:
            self.model.specialized_decode.bind_caches()
```

On the model side nothing else needs to be touched. 

# 3. How to: adding a second kernel for the same model

Say DSv4.1 gets a gfx942 kernel next to the gfx950 one. Write the FlyDSL kernel, then:

```python
# vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/specialized_decode.py

class DSV41Gfx942Kernel(DSV41Kernel):           # reuse what you want
    def run(self, step: Step, input_ids, inputs_embeds, **kwargs) -> Any: ...
        ...
        return self.runner.run_gfx942_kernel(...)

    def compile(self, key):
        width, idx = key
        self.runner.kernels(width, self.plans[idx])


def _refuse_config_gfx942(vllm_config) -> list[str]:
    reasons = []
    if not current_platform.is_gfx942():
        reasons.append("needs a gfx942 GPU")
    ...
    return reasons


DECODE_SPEC_GFX942 = DecodeSpec[DSV41Gfx942Kernel](
    name="dsv41-cdna3",
    supports=frozenset({Feature.PIPELINE_PARALLEL}),   # no spec decode here
    widths=lambda cfg: tuple(range(1, 17)),            # fewer rows than gfx950
    refuse_config=_refuse_config_gfx942,
    refuse_model=_refuse_model,                        # shared with gfx950
    refuse_caches=_refuse_caches,
    skip_step=_skip_step,
    build=DSV41Gfx942Kernel,
)

SPECS = (DECODE_SPEC_GFX950, DECODE_SPEC_GFX942)
```

Then one line in the model:

```python
self.decode_spec = select_decode_spec(vllm_config, SPECS)
```

The dispatcher takes the first compatible spec. Specializing on something other than arch works the same way. A hyper-specialized batch-size 1 kernel can just set `widths= lambda cfg: (1,)` and be placed first in the `SPECS` list.

# 4. How to: a kernel that only covers part of a layer

A specialized decode kernel might cover only part of a layer, e.g. only o-proj through post-moe AR.

The common dispatcher has no concept of this, and does not need one, because the kernel owns the layer loop. Hence it can decide at every layer whether to run it as a single monokernel, or to run it in the regular vllm model code. 

When we run part of a layer as a specialized kernel, we simply run the regular vllm model code and _inject_ the specialized kernel:

```python
class DSV41Kernel:
    def run(self, step: Step, input_ids, inputs_embeds, **kwargs) -> Any:
        self.model.prologue(input_ids, inputs_embeds, **kwargs)
        ....
        for idx in range(self.embed_layer, self.layer_end):
            layer, plan = model.layers[idx], self.plans.get(...)
            ffn = out = None
            if plan.ffn_only:
                ffn = partial(self.launch_ffn, plan)      # a part of a layer
            else:
                out = self.launch_whole(plan, hidden, positions, ...)
            if out is None:
                out = layer(hidden, positions, ..., decode_ffn=ffn) # run regular vllm and inject
            hidden, residual, post_mix, res_mix, pre_mix = out
        ...
```

```python
class DeepseekV4DecoderLayer(nn.Module):

    def forward(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        ...
        decode_ffn: Callable | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        ... # run pre etc
        x = self.attn(positions, x, None)
        if self.use_sequence_parallel:
            x = sp_reduce_scatter(x)
        elif not self.attn.wo_b.reduce_results:
            # run the "partial-layer specialized decode kernel"
            if decode_ffn is not None:
                out = decode_ffn(x, residual, post_mix, res_mix, attn_pre)
                if out is not None:
                    return out

```

## 5. Add specialized decode support for a drafter

See the DSv41 code for an example. It's treated basically identically as to another other regular model.

# Validation

# 1. DeepSeek-v41 on MI350

On MI350, force max 8 seqs
```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --language-model-only \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype=mxfp4 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --moe-backend aiter \
  --speculative-config "{\"method\":\"dspark\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":5}" \
  [--specialized-decode]
```

## 1. Performance non-regression check

```
vllm bench serve \
  --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \

  --max-concurrency "$CONC" --num-prompts "$((CONC*10))" --num-warmups "$((CONC*2))" \
  --ignore-eos --seed 0 \

```

## Accuracy


title: [ROCm][Perf][Qwen3.8-Flash-Next] Mono decode layer for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on MI355X (TP2)
body:
# [ROCm][Perf][Qwen3.8-Flash-Next] Mono decode layer for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on MI355X (TP2)

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

**Draft, stacked on #60833, which is stacked on #60683.** Until those merge, the compare view also shows their commits. This PR is the four commits after #60833's head `1301a7cfcf`, from `1e6de71f3a` on: 2,931 added and 6 removed lines in 12 files ([this PR's commits only](https://github.com/mjkvaak-amd/vllm-project/compare/rocm/qwen38-mono-decode...rocm/flashnext-mono-decode); Files changed shows 13.8k, #60683's and #60833's included). The code both Qwens share (`vllm/models/qwen3_5/amd/mono/{moe,gdn}.py`, `mono_base.py`, including the MTP verify-step path) is in #60833.

This PR ports the Qwen3.8 mono decode (#60833) to Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`, `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`) at TP2 on MI355X (gfx950). It is opt-in behind the existing `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1`. On pure decode steps, and on MTP verify steps, of up to 8 rows, each decoder layer runs as two persistent launches instead of the stock chain of hyper-connection (HC) GEMVs, norms, GDN kernels, all-reduces and MoE kernels. It reuses #60683's mono framework (mailboxes, the peer buffer, the GEMV stage). The GDN stages, the fp4 GEMV and the whole MoE are #60833's, shared rather than copied: Flash-Next passes its dimensions (`GdnDims`, `MoeDims`) and two hooks, the b / a source and the norm's gate. Both models' host code shares one base, `QwenMonoDecode`, holding the refusals, the step gate, the buffers and the MTP verify steps. Flash-Next's own code is 2,233 lines.

Flash-Next differs from Qwen3.8 in ways the 2.4T kernels did not cover: a 4-stream hyper-connection around each attention and MLP block (low-rank 320 mix, gated inject), sigmoid output gating in the GDN norm, QSA attention with an indexer on every fourth layer, a PLE layer, and TP2 shapes (8 / 24 GDN key / value heads per rank, a 320-wide MoE intermediate padded to 384).

Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs for "mono decode", "Flash-Next" and "qwen4_exp". #60833 (Qwen3.8 2.4T), #60683 (Kimi-K3) and #60397 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) are the same technique for other models; none covers the hyper-connection or QSA layers.

## Claims

Measured on `nightly-2eb491e1` plus this branch, MI355X, TP2, stock vs mono in the same image:

- Mean TPOT drops 45% at 8k/1k concurrency 1 (6.34 → 3.46 ms), 29% at concurrency 8 (10.39 → 7.38 ms), and 17–25% at 60k/600; output throughput rises 8–73%. TTFT is unchanged (prefill runs stock).
- A decode step at 8k/64, concurrency 4, takes 4.86 ms instead of 8.59 ms of GPU time, with 270 kernels instead of 1,398 (torch-profiler trace); the host gap between steps is unchanged (0.22 ms).
- GSM8K (model card recipe, two paired runs) 0.966 / 0.966 → 0.963 / 0.967, inside the stock spread on this nightly (0.962–0.966 over four stock runs). NIAH 64k 0.722 → 0.722, 128k 0.248 → 0.286 (paired p = 0.18).
- With MTP-3, the verify steps on the kernels take mean TPOT from 3.04 to 2.16 ms at 8k/1k concurrency 1 (−29%), from 4.39 to 3.47 ms at concurrency 2 (−21%) and from 2.56 to 2.02 ms at 60k/600 (−21%). At concurrency 4 a verify step has 16 rows, past the 8-row cap, so it stays on the stock path. GSM8K with every verify step on the kernels (2 threads) 0.962 stock, 0.970 and 0.960 in two mono runs; at 8 threads (mostly stock steps) 0.965 → 0.967.
- The kernels match vLLM's ops on random weights in the checkpoint's formats, and a mixed-width FULL graph of both layer kinds replays bit-identically 300 times (see Unit tests).

## Validation

**Unit tests.**

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_amd_mono.py \
  tests/models/qwen3_5/test_amd_mono_layout.py tests/models/qwen3_5/test_amd_mono_decode.py
```

The gate and layout tests cover both Qwens in one file each, parameterized by model. On `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-2eb491e18b1ce5b8a25e4c88f32dbb5d028d525c` plus this branch, 2x MI355X (one NUMA domain):
- `test_amd_mono.py`: 12 passed.
- The gate tests: 71 passed, host only, both models.
- The layout tests: 13 passed, host only.

The Qwen3.8 tests (`tests/models/qwen3_5/test_amd_mono.py`) run in the same CI step and pass on this branch, since the MoE and GDN stages are shared.

- `test_amd_mono_decode.py` (host only):
  - every refusal reason at once, and each parallelism refusal;
  - MTP: accepted with `num_speculative_tokens` + 1 ≤ 8, refused past that or for another method;
  - decode steps of 1–8 rows take the kernels, and so do MTP verify steps;
  - the same steps in a piecewise cudagraph, mixed or prefill steps, wider steps and steps without attention metadata do not.
- `test_amd_mono_layout.py` (host only): every fp4 byte and e8m0 scale of a routed expert (w13 and w2, with the intermediate padded from 320 to 384 and AITER's scale columns padded to a multiple of 8), and of the online-MXFP4 linears, is at the address K1 / K2 read.
- `test_amd_mono.py::test_hc_front_matches_vllm_ops` (1 GPU): the HC front (grouped Gemma norm, the down + inject GEMM, `hc_silu`, the up GEMM, the gate-mix) against `GatedResidual.mix`, at widths 1, 3 and 8, from K2's sums of squares or its own.
- `test_amd_mono.py::test_k1_matches_vllm_ops` (1 GPU): K1 against the HC mix → online-MXFP4 `in_proj_qkvz` / `in_proj_ba` → AITER's conv update and fused gated delta rule → `RMSNormGated` (sigmoid gate), with pad rows. It checks the conv state, SSM state and core output, that pad rows output zero, and that the null block is left untouched.
- `test_amd_mono.py::test_k2_tp2_matches_vllm_ops` (2 GPUs): K2 against `out_proj` (MXFP4) / `o_proj` with the attention output gate + all-reduce + `hc_combine`, the MLP HC mix, softmax top-10 renormalized routing, the MXFP4 experts with the fused shared expert, the MLP HC combine and the next layer's sums of squares, at widths 1, 3, 4 and 8 (both epoch parities). The MoE matches a torch emulation of the stock decode kernel's numerics (cosine > 0.9999), the same emulation as #60833's test. Against AITER's `fused_moe` itself the two differ by MXFP4 rounding (cosine about 0.999, `fused_moe` and the emulation alike), so the test requires K2's error against an unquantized fp32 MoE to be within 2% of `fused_moe`'s. Both ranks must agree bitwise.
- `test_amd_mono.py::test_mixed_width_graph_replay` (2 GPUs): the race stress, as in #60833. A GDN layer (K1, K2 with the MXFP4 `out_proj`) and a QSA layer (the HC front, K2 with the gated `o_proj`) run at six consecutive decode steps of widths 8, 1, 3, 8, 2 and 5 with pad rows. They are captured in one HIP graph, as a FULL decode graph holds them, and replayed 300 times. Every replay must be bit-identical to the eager run on both ranks. The steps share the peer buffer and the epoch, so a scratch race between widths shows up as a mismatch.

Both kernels compile for widths 1–8 at gfx950 with no VGPR spills. K1 uses up to 55 KB of LDS and K2 up to 68 KB.

**Serving smoke test.** `vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 -tp 2` with the flags below and `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1`: the first decode steps of 8, 4, 2 and 1 rows took the mono path, and requests returned. Serving found four bugs the unit tests could not, all fixed here: the GDN norm's gate is sigmoid in this checkpoint (`output_gate_type`), not silu; the multimodal wrapper passes `inputs_embeds` on decode steps too; the routed-expert weights sit on `MoERunner.routed_experts`; and (`4871661d38`) the runner builds attention metadata for the dummy runs that capture the piecewise cudagraphs, so the gate took the piecewise captures of 1–8 tokens and left those graphs uncaptured. A prompt of at most 8 tokens then replayed one and sampled from garbage logits. The gate now leaves piecewise steps to vLLM; with greedy decoding, short prompts give the same completions as stock again. The evals below use prompts longer than 8 tokens, ran before the fix, and their decode steps take the FULL graphs that the fix does not change.

**End to end.** Stock vs mono, both arms the same image, only `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE` differs, empty vLLM and AITER caches, the #59575 uplifts already on main and their flags (fused shared expert, online-MXFP4 GDN projections on the ASM FP4 GEMM, FlyDSL GDN prefill, FlyDSL MoE sorting, INT4 QuickReduce). The two arms ran at the same time on two GPU pairs of one NUMA domain; one run per cell.

| ISL / OSL | Conc (prompts) | Output tok/s, before → after | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8k / 1k | 1 (8) | 146.8 → 253.8 (+73%) | 494 → 491 | 6.34 → 3.46 (−45%) |
| 8k / 1k | 2 (12) | 267.4 → 417.0 (+56%) | 644 → 643 | 6.86 → 4.17 (−39%) |
| 8k / 1k | 4 (16) | 443.5 → 632.2 (+43%) | 1,209 → 1,233 | 7.84 → 5.13 (−35%) |
| 8k / 1k | 8 (32) | 642.5 → 854.7 (+33%) | 2,114 → 2,032 | 10.39 → 7.38 (−29%) |
| 60k / 600 | 1 (6) | 84.5 → 99.8 (+18%) | 3,175 → 3,078 | 6.55 → 4.90 (−25%) |
| 60k / 600 | 4 (16) | 143.3 → 154.7 (+8%) | 7,616 → 7,917 | 15.22 → 12.67 (−17%) |

**Accuracy**, at most 8 requests in flight so every decode step is within the 8-row cap:

| Eval | Stock | Mono |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GSM8K, model card recipe (SGLang `run_eval`, 1,319, 2,048 tokens, thinking off, 8 threads), two paired runs | 0.966 / 0.966 | 0.963 / 0.967 |
| NIAH `niah_single_2`, 64k (lm_eval RULER, 500 needles, 8 concurrent) | 0.722 | 0.722 |
| NIAH `niah_single_2`, 128k | 0.248 | 0.286 |

Mean over the two runs: 0.966 stock vs 0.965 mono, about 1 question of 1,319; three earlier stock runs on this nightly scored 0.962, 0.965 and 0.966. On NIAH, paired per needle (McNemar): 64k 97 vs 97 discordant needles (p = 1.0), 128k 100 mono-only vs 81 stock-only (p = 0.18). An earlier mono NIAH run on another GPU pair scored 0.708 / 0.284.

**MTP-3** (`--speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' --max-num-batched-tokens 8192`), stock vs mono in the same image, side by side. A verify step has 4 rows per request, so concurrency 1 and 2 run on the kernels, and concurrency 4 (16 rows) runs stock in both arms, which gives the noise floor:

| ISL / OSL | Conc (prompts) | Output tok/s, before → after | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8k / 1k | 1 (8) | 284.4 → 379.1 (+33%) | 494 → 489 | 3.04 → 2.16 (−29%) |
| 8k / 1k | 2 (12) | 397.2 → 491.2 (+24%) | 576 → 563 | 4.39 → 3.47 (−21%) |
| 8k / 1k | 4 (16), stock in both | 654.0 → 684.5 | 718 → 742 | 5.07 → 4.88 |
| 60k / 600 | 1 (6) | 123.7 → 133.0 (+8%) | 3,319 → 3,300 | 2.56 → 2.02 (−21%) |

A GDN layer's gated norm on a verify step runs in the uncompiled mono forward. An earlier build ran it as `RMSNormGated`'s eager ops, ~12 kernels a layer, and measured −12% / −15% at concurrency 1 / 2 (2.87 → 2.53 and 3.97 → 3.39 ms) in a run whose stock arm was faster than this one's. The table is this head, with the norm compiled into one launch (#60833).

GSM8K with MTP-3, model card recipe (8 threads): 0.965 stock, 0.967 mono. Mean acceptance length 3.41 stock, 3.45 mono. At 8 threads most verify steps exceed 8 rows and run stock, so this mainly checks that steps switching between the two paths stay sound. At 2 threads, where every verify step has at most 8 rows and runs on the kernels: 0.962 stock, 0.970 mono, mean acceptance length 3.46 in both (the earlier build); this head's mono scores 0.960, acceptance length 3.52.

Serving MTP on this checkpoint needs a config fix. `quantization_config.exclude` lists the bf16 draft layer as `mtp.layers.0.*`, but vLLM builds it as `mtp.layers.48.*`, so stock MTP fails at load (`size of tensor a (1280) must match the size of tensor b (2560)`). These runs add `re:mtp\..*` to the exclude list; the proper fix belongs in the checkpoint.

**Reproduce:**

```bash
# the stock arm: the same command with VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=0
VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 AITER_USE_FLYDSL_MOE_SORTING=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 \
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 -tp 2 --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 256 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --gdn-prefill-backend aiter_flydsl --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --quantization-config.targets '{"*linear_attn.in_proj_qkv": "mxfp4", "*linear_attn.in_proj_z": "mxfp4", "*linear_attn.out_proj": "mxfp4"}'

# End to end (one cell)
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm --model amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 8 --warmup-requests 1 --seed 41

# GSM8K, model card recipe
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --host localhost --port 8000 \
  --model amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --num-threads 8 --num-examples 1319 --max-tokens 2048 \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'
```

## Details

**Path.** The step is chosen as a whole in the uncompiled outer forward (`Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration.forward`, and `Qwen4ExpForCausalLM.forward` for the text-only class). Eligible steps have no prefill, 1–8 rows, no intermediate tensors, and are not a piecewise cudagraph step (those graphs also serve short prefills, so they must be captured from the stock model). With MTP, the eligible steps are verify steps of up to 8 rows, i.e. up to 2 requests at `num_speculative_tokens` 3. They run the mono forward on the materialized 4-stream state; everything else runs the stock compiled model unchanged. The FULL decode graph captures the mono forward once per width.

Per decoder layer (48: 36 GDN, 12 QSA):

- **K1, GDN layers** (`gdn_pre`): the attention HC's grouped norm and mix (down + inject GEMV, `hc_silu`, up GEMV, gate-mix) → online-MXFP4 `in_proj_qkvz` and bf16 `in_proj_ba` → causal conv1d update → gated delta rule → sigmoid-gated `RMSNormGated`, writing `out_proj`'s input. No cross-rank traffic.
- **K1, QSA layers** (`hc_front`): the attention HC's norm and mix alone; vLLM's QSA attention (fused prepare, indexer, attention) then runs up to `o_proj`'s input and the output gate.
- **K2, every layer** (`layer_post`): `out_proj` (MXFP4) / `o_proj` (bf16, with the sigmoid output gate) + its TP all-reduce + the attention HC combine → the MLP HC's norm and mix → softmax top-10 renormalized router → MXFP4 routed experts with the shared expert fused as expert 512 → MoE all-reduce → the MLP HC combine, writing the next state and the next front's sums of squares.
- The PLE layer (decoder layer 1) and the final HC mixer run vLLM's modules on the materialized state.
- **MTP verify steps:** a request's rows are consecutive tokens of one sequence, so the GDN conv and recurrence need vLLM's spec-decode state handling. GDN layers run K1's HC front (`hc_front`), then vLLM's GDN core (`qwen_gdn_attention_core` with the step's spec metadata) and gated norm; QSA layers run as above. K2 runs unchanged, so the HC GEMVs, the all-reduces and the MoE stay on the kernels. The drafter's input, the final hidden states before the HC mixer, is copied to the buffer the stock model fills.

**Design decisions.**
- **Materialized HC combine:** stock defers each HC combine into the next mix; K2 materializes it with the same bf16 rounding, so the PLE layer, the QSA path and the final mixer read a plain state.
- **Numerics contract** as in #60833: K1 reproduces AITER's decode conv and gated delta rule; the routed experts run x and silu(g)·u through dynamic MXFP4 like AITER's decode MoE. The MoE intermediate is padded from 320 to 384 as vLLM loads it (zero codes); K2 reads only the real 320.
- **Buffers:** per-width scratch for K1 and K2; a width-independent peer buffer; mailbox tags carry a device epoch bumped once per step.
- **Refusals, as in #60397:** an explicit `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1` that cannot run raises at init, listing every reason (CDNA4, TP2, no PP, no expert / data / context parallelism or EPLB, no LoRA, spec decode only as MTP with `num_speculative_tokens` + 1 ≤ 8 and the AITER GDN path, no KV connector, the fused shared expert on, at least 256 CUs). The checks are `QwenMonoDecode.refusals`, shared with Qwen3.8. A weight layout the kernels cannot read raises at the first decode step. A model variant outside the kernels (other shapes, GDN or HC variants, attention without the QSA indexer or the output gate) stays on the stock path, logged once.

**Shared code.** `qwen4_exp/amd/model.py` gains 23 lines: the import, the constructor hook and the forward dispatch in both model classes. With the env var unset, or off ROCm, `_mono` is `None` and nothing else changes.

Flash-Next uses #60833's shared Qwen mono code instead of copies of it:
- the MoE (route, gate | up, down, the fp4 GEMV, x through MXFP4) from `mono/moe.py`, sized by `MoeDims`;
- the GDN stages from `mono/gdn.py`, parameterized by `GdnDims`, the b / a source and the norm's gate;
- the K-split GEMV reduction (for the HC down GEMV) and the `in_proj_ba` tasks;
- the host side from `mono_base.py` (`QwenMonoDecode`: refusals, the step gate, buffers, the MTP verify steps).

A CPU-only ISA dump of all 160 kernel variants of both models (widths 1–8, every flag) checked each move. Every Flash-Next variant is byte-identical to before, except K2 at 4–8 rows (the same instructions, reordered). Qwen3.8's K2 is identical. Its K1 with the split `in_proj_ba` gains 10–24 instructions (of 3.4k–9.4k) for the b / a rows' addresses, with the same registers and spills.

**Limitations and TODOs.**
- **Scope:** TP2 only (`Layout.TPS`). The dims records carry the per-rank shapes, so another TP size is a matter of the layout's divisibility checks, but only TP2 has been run. TODO: TP1 (stock TP1 has open issues), TP4 and TP8.
- **MTP:** only verify steps of up to 8 rows run on the kernels: 2 requests at `num_speculative_tokens` 3. Larger batches verify on the stock path. The GDN core of a verify step is vLLM's. Serve with `max_num_batched_tokens` 8192, as stock MTP needs on Qwen3.8-2.4T. Other spec-decode methods are refused.
- **TODO:** K1's GDN variants spill 6–63 SGPRs, to VGPR lanes, at 5–8 rows (`s_movk` / `v_writelane` pairs, no scratch memory). No variant of either kernel spills VGPRs.
- **TODO: fail-stop.** A mailbox wait on a peer that never posts spins until the engine's timeout. #60683 has since gained RFC #60904's MonoKernel framework, at `vllm/models/common/mono` (`a717180301`). It brings bounded in-kernel waits with per-CTA error words, a runner-side check that fails the step before its tokens are returned, `--monokernel` in place of `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE`, and `MonoSpec` declarations. This stack is on #60683's earlier head. Porting both Qwens onto it means two changes: the kernels take its health / alarm words through the shared `Mailbox`, and the host side becomes a `MonoSpec`. The per-layer hook returns what vLLM's layer does, so Flash-Next's materialized HC combine has to move to a layer-boundary contract.
- **CI:** Flash-Next's tests run in the Qwen3.8 mono step (`models_basic.yaml`: 8x MI355X, 40 minutes), next to the shared code's other user. The numerics tests need gfx950 and 1–2 GPUs. The gate and layout tests are host only.
- **Size:** 2,233 lines under `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/amd/`. That is 1,704 of kernels (K1, K2, the HC stages), 390 of host code and 139 of layout and sources. Tests add 671 lines. Before the sharing, Flash-Next's own code was 3,186 lines.

title: [Model Runner V2] Add override_model_forward hook for forward benchmarks
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add `GPUModelRunner.override_model_forward(fn)` (MRV2): a context manager under which `execute_model` still builds the step's inputs, attention metadata and forward context, then calls `fn(input_batch, **model_inputs)` instead of the eager model call. Its user is `vllm bench forward` (#61339, stacked on this PR), which times the model forward of an exact batch as a one-shot CUDA graph.

## Claims

- A benchmark can run the real per-step preparation (input batch, `ModelState` metadata, DP sync, forward context) for a batch it built, and take over only the model call, without copying runner code or patching private state.
- No behavior change unless the context manager is active: one attribute check in the eager branch.

## Validation

Exercised by the stacked bench PR's tests (`tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py`, end-to-end on Llama-3.2-1B in the Benchmarks CLI job) and its validation on DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 (1 to 8 GPUs, DP/TP/EP, 2 nodes). The hook alone has no caller in this PR, so it has no separate test.

## Details

- Only the eager branch (`cudagraph_mode == NONE`, no micro-batching) is overridable; the context manager asserts both, since otherwise the override would never reach the model.
- `fn` receives the `InputBatch` so a caller can check the layout the runner built (request order, query and computed lengths) and write per-request inputs, without reading runner internals.
- `sample_tokens` must not follow an overridden step, so the pending `execute_model_state` is dropped on exit.

title: [Kernel][Spec Decode] Fuse temperature scaling into the rejection-sampling kernels
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Targets #61024 (Q4 2026 roadmap, SIG Spec Decode: "optimize fusion and kernels for low-latency inference, including rejection sampling"). Folds temperature scaling into the rejection-sampling kernels so `target_logits` can be passed raw instead of pre-divided into a fresh FP32 buffer.

## Claims

- Adds `target_logits_pre_scaled: bool = True` to `rejection_sample()`. Default unchanged, so every existing caller is a no-op.
- When `target_logits_pre_scaled=False`, `target_logits` is passed raw and divided by `temperature` on load inside the kernels, in the same 5 places `draft_logits` is already handled this way (`_compute_local_logits_stats_kernel`, `_compute_global_logprobs_and_logsumexp`, `_compute_global_residual_mass`, and `_resample_kernel`'s three `residual_logits` branches), guarded against div-by-zero where the bonus-token branch can be reached at `temperature == 0`.
- This is kernel-side groundwork. It does not yet remove the FP32 `processed_logits` buffer itself -- see "Not yet done" below.

## Validation

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_synthetic_rejection_sampler_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_i64.py -q
# 88 passed (71 + 17 across the four files, no regressions)
```

New test: `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py::test_raw_target_logits_matches_pre_scaled_target_logits`. Builds the same `rejection_sample()` inputs twice -- once with pre-scaled `target_logits` (default path) and once raw with `target_logits_pre_scaled=False` -- with the same seed, and asserts sampled tokens and `num_sampled` are bit-identical (`rtol=0, atol=0`). Parametrized over temperature (0.0 greedy / 0.73 / 1.0), one-hot vs full `draft_logits`, and block verification on/off: 12 cases, all passing on A100.

No model eval: this path isn't wired into any model's forward pass yet (nothing calls `rejection_sample` with `target_logits_pre_scaled=False` outside the new test).

## Details

**Why:** right at the top of `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler.py`:
```
# TODO(mgoin): Chunking is a workaround. The rejection kernels already upcast
# per vocab block on load and apply ops like temperature and gumbel, so folding
# sampling-param application into those kernels would remove this buffer and
# its traffic entirely.
```
`apply_sampling_params` currently copies `target_logits` into a fresh FP32 buffer and divides it by `temperature` before `rejection_sample()` ever sees it. That buffer is the reason verification has to chunk the batch at a 1GB cap (`MAX_CHUNK_BYTES`) at all. `draft_logits` already skips this: it's passed raw and every rejection kernel divides it by `temperature` on load. This PR extends the same "scale on load" convention to `target_logits`.

**Scope:** temperature only. `min_p`/`top_k`/`top_p` are nonlinear filtering ops, not linear rescalings of the logits, so they can't be folded the same way -- out of scope here.

**Duplicate-work check:** searched `gh issue list`/`gh pr list` (open PRs/issues, several keyword variants against #61024's roadmap bullet and against this specific TODO) before starting; found no existing issue or PR claiming this slice. Left a comment on #61024 noting this PR is in progress.

**Not yet done** (follow-up commits on this PR, not yet started): wiring `rejection_sampler.py`'s `_verify` to pass raw `target_logits` with `target_logits_pre_scaled=False` and skip `apply_sampling_params`'s temperature step and its FP32 buffer materialization when no other sampling-param processing (logits processors, min_p, top_k/top_p) is active. That caller-side change is what actually removes the buffer and lets the chunking cap be raised or removed -- this commit is only the kernel-side groundwork enabling it.

title: [Spec Decode] Support the Liquid LFM2.5-VL DSpark drafter
body:
## Overview

Enable `LiquidAI/LFM2.5-VL-3B` with its official DSpark drafter, reusing vLLM's existing dense DSpark implementation.

## Claims

- Normalize the draft architecture, interleaved RoPE flag, and confidence-head layout before model inspection.
- Expose trained LFM2 target features through the VL wrapper and include speculative history in ShortConv cache planning.
- Add focused regression tests and a documented usage example.

## Validation

**30 tests passed** with repository fixtures enabled. All selected pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy and CI test tethering.

Validated on one H100 80GB, MRV2, BF16, TP=1, K=9, eager; async scheduling, adaptive verification, and prefix caching disabled.

| Workload | Baseline tok/s | DSpark tok/s | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Full MMSpec: 600 samples / 723 turns | 73.87 | 202.77 | 2.74x time ratio; 31.33% acceptance, mean acceptance length 3.82 |
| Text: 3 warmup passes / 5 measured passes | Median 89.31 (89.02–90.01) | Median 258.18 (247.93–262.34) | 2.89x median time ratio; all 25 request pairs matched |

MMSpec is one unwarmed pass including image encoding, prefill, and request overhead. Loading/downloads are excluded. The output cap was 512; 12 turns reached it in each mode. 722/723 turns matched exactly; one BF16 replay reproduced a top-score tie with different greedy selection. Gold-answer accuracy was not scored.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands and pinned versions</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py tests/model_executor/test_lfm2_aux_hidden_states.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/config/speculative.py vllm/model_executor/models/lfm2.py vllm/model_executor/models/lfm2_vl.py tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py tests/model_executor/test_lfm2_aux_hidden_states.py docs/features/speculative_decoding/dspark.md docs/features/speculative_decoding/README.md
```

GPU validation harness and commands: https://gist.github.com/haror1/bf4c18968bff28f174cebba26922760d

Target: `35a118d938ce6d123ac2d371649f24a8efb69058`; draft: `af77e9306a26e8625fde74d2a3051ab6d21bd955`; MMSpec: `290486861eabd746075ca776adb66175636c1fc0`. PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.95.05. Greedy sampling with the target chat template; separate processes with uncontrolled GPU placement/clocks. Unit tests emitted 14 Torch deprecation warnings. Upstream pre-commit is gated by contributor/label eligibility; full Buildkite CI awaits a reviewer trigger.

</details>

## Details

The published drafter is attention-only and Qwen3-shaped; no new draft class, scheduler, runner, or kernel is added. Target capture reconstructs full residual streams using the existing layer-index convention.

Open/closed searches found no direct integration duplicate. [SGLang #40651](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40651) implements a different engine and uses `tugot17/mango-9`. Related vLLM PRs [#44296](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44296) and [#59600](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59600) address target rollback and ShortConv drafter recovery, respectively; those paths are unchanged here.

Pipeline-parallel capture is unsupported. CUDA graphs, mixed batches, async scheduling, adaptive verification, and prefix caching were not evaluated for this pair.

AI assistance (Codex) was used for implementation, review, and validation. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the relevant tests/model evaluations.
