title: [Frontend] Send ping keepalives while an Anthropic /v1/messages stream waits for its first token
body:
## Overview

Emit Anthropic `ping` events on `/v1/messages` streams while the engine has not yet produced a chunk, so proxy and client idle timeouts (commonly 300s) do not cut off requests with long prefills. Addresses item 14 ("No `ping` or early `message_start` during long prefills") of RFC #58647.

## Claims

- A streaming `/v1/messages` request whose first token takes longer than the keepalive interval now receives `event: ping` / `data: {"type": "ping"}` every `VLLM_ANTHROPIC_STREAM_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_S` seconds (default 15) until the first chunk, then the unchanged event sequence.
- Requests whose first chunk arrives promptly are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- `VLLM_ANTHROPIC_STREAM_KEEPALIVE=comment` sends an SSE comment line instead (invisible to SSE parsers, for clients whose SDK streaming helper rejects events before `message_start`); `off` disables the feature.
- Closing the response while a keepalive wait is pending cancels the in-flight read on the OpenAI stream.

## Validation

Unit tests (`TestMessageStreamConverterKeepalive`, 7 cases: pings before the first chunk with the rest of the stream unchanged, no ping when chunks are prompt, `comment` mode, `off` mode, pending read cancelled on close, stream errors still surface as `error` events):

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py \
    tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_protocol_exports.py tests/test_envs.py -q
176 passed

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/envs.py vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py \
    tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py docs/serving/online_serving/README.md
ruff check / ruff format / typos / mypy / markdownlint / SPDX ... all Passed
```

End-to-end on vLLM 0.31.0 (this change applied as a file overlay) serving `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (DP=3, TP=2, max-model-len 1M) behind kgateway (Envoy) and the production-stack router, requested from inside the cluster with `curl -N`:

| Request | First token | Events observed |
|---|---|---|
| `max_tokens: 8`, short prompt | < 1s | `message_start` first, no `ping` |
| 1.3 MB prompt, `max_tokens: 1` | 53s | `ping` at 15s, 30s, 45s, then `message_start` … `message_stop`, HTTP 200 |
| 1.7 MB prompt through Envoy and the router | 66s | `ping` at 16s, 31s, 46s, 61s, then a full response, HTTP 200 |

Before the change, the same deployment lost requests at exactly 300s whenever a cold 200k to 1M token prefill ran (Claude Code reports "Request timed out"; Envoy's `downstream_rq_idle_timeout` counter incremented).

Client compatibility: Claude Code 2.1.296 was run against a mock Messages server that sends a `ping` before `message_start`; the response, `stop_reason` and `usage` were reported correctly. The TypeScript and Python SDK `MessageStream` helpers (`client.messages.stream()`) throw on any event before `message_start`, which is why the `comment` mode exists; raw `create(stream=True)` iteration in both SDKs ignores `ping`.

## Details

- Root cause: `message_stream_converter` emits its first bytes (`message_start`) only on the first `ChatCompletionStreamResponse` chunk, which the engine produces after prefill. For 100k+ token prompts with no prefix cache hit that is minutes of silence on the wire.
- Implementation: `_iter_with_keepalive` wraps the OpenAI stream and yields `None` when `asyncio.wait` on the pending `__anext__` times out; the converter turns `None` into the keepalive payload. The pending future is kept across timeouts (cancelling `__anext__` of an async generator corrupts it) and is cancelled in a `finally` via `items.aclose()` so a client disconnect mid-wait does not leave the read running.
- Keepalives are also emitted mid-stream if the engine stalls longer than the interval; after `message_start` a `ping` is unconditionally legal in the Anthropic protocol.
- Configuration lives in `vllm/envs.py` (`VLLM_ANTHROPIC_STREAM_KEEPALIVE`, `VLLM_ANTHROPIC_STREAM_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_S`) so it is documented automatically on the environment-variables page; the online-serving README gets a one-line note.
- Tradeoff: the default sends a `ping` before `message_start`, which the real Anthropic API does not do. It is accepted by Claude Code, the primary consumer of this endpoint, and by raw SDK iteration; SDK `.stream()` helper users can select `comment`. An early `message_start` with placeholder usage was considered and rejected because `usage.input_tokens` is only known once the first chunk arrives.
- Not a duplicate: open PRs mentioning the Anthropic converter are #46162 (forwarding engine error chunks, a different code path; this PR deliberately does not touch error handling), #59616 (context-window errors) and #52519 (tool JSON). No open PR or issue proposes keepalives; RFC #58647 lists it as item 14 with "none found".
- AI assistance was used for this PR (Claude Code). The submitting human reviewed every line, ran the tests above, and deployed and validated the change on the serving cluster described in Validation.

title: [Bugfix] Require hybrid KV cache manager for hybrid models
body:
## Overview

Fail configuration early when a hybrid attention-recurrent model resolves to a disabled hybrid KV cache manager, instead of failing later during KV-cache planning. Fixes #61313.

## Claims

- Raise an actionable configuration error when the hybrid KV cache manager is disabled for a hybrid model.
- Preserve existing behavior when the manager is enabled or the model is not hybrid.
- Add focused CPU-only regression coverage for all three cases.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -k 'hybrid_kv_cache_manager or hisparse' -v
```

Result: 16 passed, 433 deselected.

```bash
PRE_COMMIT_HOME=/tmp/vllm-pre-commit .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/config/vllm.py tests/test_config.py
```

Result: all applicable hooks passed.

No model evaluation was run because this configuration-only validation does not affect model execution or output.

## Details

The hybrid KV cache manager can currently resolve to disabled even when `ModelConfig.is_hybrid` is true. Mixed attention and recurrent cache specifications cannot be promoted to the uniform cache type required by the non-hybrid planning path, so startup later fails with a generic `ValueError`.

This change validates the effective setting after automatic and explicit hybrid KV cache manager resolution. It reports the incompatible configuration immediately and suggests either removing `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager` or using a platform and KV connector configuration that supports the manager.

No overlapping open PR was found through searches for `#61313`, the validation symbol, and the affected hybrid KV-cache behavior.

AI assistance was used during implementation and review. I reviewed and understand all changed lines and validated the behavior locally.

title: [MORI] Add MORI EP V2 support
body:
## Overview

Adds `--all2all-backend mori`, an expert-parallel all2all backend that runs MoRI EPv2 (`mori.ops.dispatch_combine_v2`) where it is supported and MoRI EPv1 otherwise. EPv2 dispatches and combines tokens through a MoRI CCO symmetric-memory window, so all EP ranks must sit in one load/store-accessible (LSA) team, e.g. one node.

`VLLM_MORI_EP_V2` selects the version. When it is unset, `mori` prefers EPv2 and falls back to EPv1 with a warning in any of these cases:

- the EP size exceeds 8 (except on gfx1250, whose UALink team can span hosts);
- `MORI_ENABLE_SDMA=1` is set (except on gfx1250);
- `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe` is used;
- the model is not BF16.

Setting it to `1` forces EPv2, and `0` selects EPv1. The choice is made once in the ROCm platform's config hook. On EPv1 across nodes, `mori` uses InterNodeV1LL when the per-rank token budget is at most `VLLM_MORI_DISPATCH_INTER_KERNEL_SWITCH_THRESHOLD` (default 256), and InterNodeV1 otherwise.

The existing MoRI backends (`mori_high_throughput`, `mori_low_latency`) are unchanged and always run EPv1. `docs/serving/expert_parallel_deployment.md` explains how to choose among them.

No other open PR adds a MoRI EPv2 backend.

## Claims

- On DeepSeek-V4-Pro with DP8+EP8 on 8× MI355X, `mori` on EPv2 matches TP8 and the existing MoRI EP backend on GSM8K.
- Under the InferenceX MI355X serving recipe (8k/1k), `mori` on EPv2 gives about 13% more output throughput and about 11% lower TPOT than `mori_high_throughput`.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 8× MI355X, `--moe-backend aiter`, CUDA graphs, MoRI main.

**Accuracy**

| Backend | Parallelism | GSM8K (lm-eval, 1319 q, 5-shot, strict) |
|---|---|---|
| default | TP8 | 0.950 |
| `mori_high_throughput` | DP8+EP8 | 0.958 |
| `mori` (EPv2) | DP8+EP8 | 0.955 |

GSM8K ran with 4096 max new tokens, so about 33 answers per backend were cut off before the final answer. The absolute scores are lower than with a longer budget, but the backends can be compared with each other.

**Throughput.** InferenceX vLLM MI355X recipe: DP8+EP8, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, prefix caching, DSpark speculative decoding (6 tokens), and model runner V2. The load is random input/output of 8k/1k, with 640 requests at concurrency 64 and 1280 requests at concurrency 128. Both runs used the same image, on an earlier revision of this branch where the backend was still named `mori_epv2`.

| Backend | c64 output tok/s (TPOT ms) | c128 output tok/s (TPOT ms) | GSM8K (200 q) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mori_high_throughput` | 1835 (30.3) | 2339 (47.0) | 0.965 |
| `mori` (EPv2) | 2073 (26.9) | 2644 (41.8) | 0.960 |

The eager mode (`--enforce-eager`) start-up also passed. Unit tests: `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_mori_epv2_prepare_finalize.py`.

## Follow-ups

- Make mori the single MoRI backend: fold mori_high_throughput and mori_low_latency into it (deprecate first, then remove). VLLM_MORI_EP_V2 stays as the EPv2/EPv1 override.
- Add EPv2 across nodes (RDMA), so multi-node EP no longer falls back to EPv1.
- Use quantized (FP8/FP4) dispatch on EPv2. MoRI supports it, but this backend does not use it yet.

AI assistance (Claude, Codex) was used to write and review this change. The submitter reviewed the changes and ran the validation above.

title: [CI][MiniMax-M3] Serving features compatibility matrix
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds a CI test that serves MiniMax-M3 with DSpark in 8 deployments on one 4×B200 node, to catch regressions in the combinations that work on main today. The combinations come from the sweep in #60791; known failures are tracked there and are not in the test.

## Claims

- `tests/models/minimax_m3/test_feature_matrix.py`: MiniMax-M3 cut to 6 layers (3 dense + 3 MSA/MoE), `--load-format dummy`. Only config and tokenizer files are downloaded.
- CI step `:nvidia: (4xB200) MiniMax-M3 Feature Matrix`, one shard, 15 min locally.
- Each deployment also checks DSpark with a JSON-schema request.

## Validation

1 node, 4× GB200, vLLM main @ aa3564ceef + this test file, MRV2, NIXL 1.5.0.

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/models/minimax_m3/test_feature_matrix.py
```

| Deployment | GPUs | Time |
|---|---|---|
| `tp4-ep-image`: TP4 + EP, image input | 4 | 88 s |
| `dep4`: DP4 + EP, `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided` | 4 | 82 s |
| `pp2-dep2`: PP2 × DP2 + EP | 4 | 82 s |
| `simple-offload-tp2-ep`: TP2 + EP, SimpleCPUOffloadConnector | 2 | 78 s |
| `pd-image`: NixlConnector TP1→TP1, image input | 2 | 138 s |
| `pd-push`: NixlPushConnector TP1→TP1 | 2 | 125 s |
| `pd-tp2-dep2`: NixlConnector TP2→DEP2 | 4 | 165 s |
| `pd-offloading`: MultiConnector(NIXL, OffloadingConnector) on both sides | 2 | 130 s |

`8 passed in 893.22s`. `pp2-dep2` sets `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=2,4` so that every stage holds a dense layer; with the default split M3 still fails at startup on main (#54710).

All deployments run DSpark (k=3) and check that:
- a JSON-schema chat request ends with `stop` and parses;
- 8 concurrent requests of mixed lengths complete;
- `vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total > 0`;

Each cell is the two features together; the diagonal is one feature alone. No server errors in any arm. The DSpark arms used `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`; at the default 0.92 the MSA sparse prefill OOMs under load (#60791, item 7).

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 -tp 4 --block-size 128 --max-model-len 65536 --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --language-model-only --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"nvidia/MiniMax-M3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":8}'
```

BFCL ran as in `.buildkite/scripts/tool_call/run-bfcl-eval.sh` (`simple_python,multiple,parallel,parallel_multiple,live_simple,multi_turn_base`, 32 threads). For the forced-tag arms, `OpenAICompletionsHandler.generate_with_backoff` was wrapped to pass `extra_body={"structured_outputs": {"structural_tag": tag}}`:

```python
NS = "]<]minimax[>["
tag = {"type": "structural_tag", "format": {"type": "triggered_tags", "triggers": [NS + "<tool_call>"],
  "tags": [{"type": "tag", "begin": NS + "<tool_call>\n", "end": NS + "</tool_call>",
    "content": {"type": "tags_with_separator", "separator": "", "at_least_one": True,
      "tags": [{"type": "tag", "begin": f'{NS}<invoke name="{name}">',
                "content": {"type": "any_text"}, "end": NS + "</invoke>\n"} for name in tool_names]}}]}}
```

</details>

## Details

- Dummy weights avoid a multi-GB download per run. Outputs are meaningless, so correctness is checked as logprob equality between two paths, the JSON schema is bounded and uses `disable_any_whitespace` so it terminates, and DSpark is checked for proposing drafts rather than for acceptance.
- Deployments with a KV connector pass `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`: with DSpark's sliding-window layers the hybrid manager mixes block sizes, which NIXL and the CPU offload connectors do not support (#60791, items 2 and 6).
- Left out: known failures (#60791), MooncakeStore (needs an external master), single-GPU and TP2 variants that a larger deployment covers, and plain chat/streaming, which other suites test.
- No other MiniMax-M3 end-to-end serving test exists in `tests/` or `.buildkite/`. The layout follows the Kimi K3 prefix-cache test (#59229).

title: [Bug][Rust Frontend] DeepSeek V4/V4.1 renderer rejects `latest_reminder`, which the Python encoder renders
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug cc @BugenZhao @njhill @Isotr0py @YeonwooSung DeepSeek-V4 accepts a chat role, `latest_reminder`, that the Python encoder renders as `<｜latest_reminder｜>` plus the text. The Rust DeepSeek renderer rejects every custom role. The same request fails on vLLM’s Rust HTTP frontend and on the router’s gRPC path, which renders with that same library before it sends token ids. ### Reproduction (According to https://github.com/vllm-project/router/issues/318) Router in front of a rust grpc (or http) vLLM worker serving DeepSeek-V4: ``` curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4", "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the context."}, {"role": "latest_reminder", "content": "Keep the answer concise."} ] }' ``` Actual: Rust DeepSeek renderer -> `Error::UnsupportedChatRole` (HTTP 400). Expected: a role the model’s Python encoder can render is rendered to token ids and reaches the worker. Python `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4_encoding.py` already does this. ### Context The vLLM router’s Rust gRPC backend (https://github.com/vllm-project/router/pull/283) renders the chat template in-process with `vllm-chat` and sends `GenerateRequest.token_ids`. The role string never crosses the proto. A role the renderer cannot represent never reaches the worker. https://github.com/vllm-project/router/issues/318 is that gap for model-specific roles. This is not specific to the router or to gRPC. Any caller of the Rust DeepSeek renderer hits it, including vLLM’s own Rust HTTP frontend. ### What main already does https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58311 added `ChatMessage::Custom { role, content }` and `ChatMessage::custom()`. The HF renderer passes that role string into the Jinja template unchanged. That covers templates such as MiniMax-M3 `root`. The same PR makes the native renderers return `Error::UnsupportedChatRole`, including DeepSeek V3.2 / V4 / V4.1, and locks that in with `custom_roles_are_rejected_as_request_errors`. Python still has a real branch for this role: - emit `<｜latest_reminder｜>` plus the message content - if the next message is `latest_reminder`, still open the assistant transition after the previous user turn, the same way a following `assistant` message does - do not treat `latest_reminder` as a user/developer turn for `find_last_user_index` A request the Python frontend accepts is a 400 on the Rust DeepSeek renderer. ### Ask Please steer which fix belongs in this repo before we send a PR. 1. DeepSeek-only. In `rust/src/chat/src/renderer/deepseek.rs`, render `role == "latest_reminder"` to match the Python encoder, and keep `UnsupportedChatRole` for every other custom role. Harmony, Inkling, and Kimi K3 stay closed, as #58311 set them. 2. A shared rule for native renderers. If other dedicated renderers also drop roles that their Python path accepts, say how those roles should be added (per-renderer allowlist, or something else). We would rather follow that than special-case one token in a one-off PR. We can send the DeepSeek renderer change once the scope is clear. A PR from someone closer to the renderer is just as welcome. No `inference.proto` / `control.proto` change is needed for this. The gRPC worker already consumes token ids. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug] TieringOffloadingSpec fs-tier lookup succeeds but never triggers a promotion job (active_promotion_jobs stays 0)
body:
## Summary

Using `OffloadingConnector` with `TieringOffloadingSpec` and a `"fs"` secondary tier (a plain
POSIX filesystem, no LMCache involved), a second engine instance's lookup against a prefix
already written by a first, independent instance **genuinely finds the entry** — the lookup
metric increments and completes with a real, non-zero delay — but the promotion step that
should pull the found block back up into usable GPU/CPU state **never fires**:
`vllm:kv_offload_tiering_active_promotion_jobs:('1:fs',)` stays at 0 for the entire test, and
the second instance falls back to a full, redundant recompute every time.

## Environment

- **vLLM version**: 0.31.0 (confirmed current latest at time of testing, `pip install vllm`
  with no version pin)
- **Model**: `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`
- **`--kv-transfer-config`**:
  ```json
  {"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
   "kv_connector_extra_config":{"spec_name":"TieringOffloadingSpec","cpu_bytes_to_use":10737418240,
   "block_size":64,"secondary_tiers":[{"type":"fs","root_dir":"<shared POSIX mount>",
   "n_read_threads":16,"n_write_threads":16}]}}
  ```
- **`root_dir`**: a shared POSIX-compatible mount visible identically to both engine instances
  (in our case, DeepSeek's 3FS over FUSE — but the bug is in the generic `"fs"` tier/promotion
  logic, not specific to 3FS as a filesystem)
- **`PYTHONHASHSEED=123`** set identically on both instances, per vLLM's own documented
  requirement for content-hash consistency across independent processes
- Both instances otherwise identical: same model, same `--block-size 64`, same flags

## What we did

1. Deployed two independent vLLM engine instances (`native1`, `native2`), each with the config
   above, sharing the same `root_dir`.
2. Stored one brand-new prefix on `native1` only — confirmed clean, no errors, a real
   `store_bytes` event logged.
3. Waited ~20+ seconds, well past any plausible async-write settle time, before querying
   `native2` — this was specifically to rule out a write-visibility timing race, since an
   earlier, separate test (a different connector, LMCache's deprecated `remote_url` backend)
   had shown timing-sensitive behavior.
4. Queried `native2` with the identical, never-before-seen-by-native2 prefix. No write race
   was possible at this point — only `native1` had ever touched this content.

## What we found

`native2`'s own metrics confirm the fs-tier lookup genuinely ran and completed:
- `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_chunk_queries:('1:fs',)` incremented
- `lookup_async_delay_seconds` recorded a real, non-zero completed lookup (~40ms)

This rules out a stuck, skipped, or silently-erroring lookup. But:
- `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_active_promotion_jobs:('1:fs',)` **stayed at 0** — no promotion job
  was ever created for this successful lookup.
- `native2` proceeded to recompute the prefix on GPU from scratch and wrote its own, separate
  copy to the fs tier — functionally correct (no wrong answer, no crash), but the fs tier
  provided zero actual benefit across instances in this test.

## A second, related bug found along the way (concurrent-write case)

In an earlier variant of this test (both instances computing the *same* new prefix at
nearly the same time, rather than one-then-the-other), the second writer's attempt to persist
its own copy of an already-content-addressed block failed hard:

```
ERROR [thread_pool.py:181] Job 0 block I/O failed: [Errno 17] File exists:
.../1870b67d5b659d799e715c585ce8d3e9e0a4e8e2c01131bcc00f51eb23bde6af.bin
```

This `EEXIST` is counted as a hard `cascade_job_failure`, rather than being treated as "another
writer already has this identical, content-addressed block — nothing to do," which is the
correct outcome for genuine content-addressed deduplication. We consider this a second,
related-but-distinct bug in the same code path, not a duplicate of the first.

## What we have not isolated

Whether the stuck-promotion behavior (the main bug above) is:
- a content-hash mismatch between the two independent engine instances despite matching
  `PYTHONHASHSEED`,
- a stricter, undocumented condition in `TieringOffloadingSpec`'s own logic for deciding a
  looked-up chunk is eligible for promotion, or
- something specific to this exact vLLM build (0.31.0).

We only have the installed package, not a from-source debug build, so we could not trace this
further ourselves. Happy to test a patched build or add more diagnostic logging against the
exact reproduction above if that would help.

## Suggested next step

Given the lookup path works correctly and only the promotion step is silent, the bug is likely
localized to whatever decides "this lookup result is eligible to promote" immediately after a
successful fs-tier query — not the lookup/query path itself, and not the write path (writes
succeed; the dedup-handling bug above is the only write-side issue found).

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Store the chunk of a loaded partial tail
body:
## Overview

After a load that ends in a partial tail, the OffloadingConnector scheduler never stores the chunk that holds the tail. Each later lookup of the same prefix stops at the same partial tail, and the request computes all tokens after it again. This PR starts the store of a full-attention group at the chunk of the partial tail.

Related: #61019 (draft) changes the copy-on-write hand-off store of partial tails with EAGLE/MTP groups. It does not change `next_stored_chunk_idx`, and its head (3276fddc9) merges with this PR without a conflict.

Duplicate check: I searched the open and closed issues and PRs for `next_stored_chunk_idx`, "partial tail" and "offload". #56795, #52771 and #51761 report other defects of the store index. No issue or PR reports this case.

AI assistance was used for this PR (Claude Code): the root-cause analysis, the patch, the test and this description. I reviewed every changed line and the test results.

## Claims

- After a load that ends in a partial tail, the connector stores the chunk of the tail when the chunk is full. The next lookup of the prefix then goes past it.
- On a hybrid MLA + KDA model with partial tails and 32 concurrent agent sessions, the prompt tokens left to compute after the cache hits fall from 12,220 to 3,613 per warm turn, and the output throughput rises from 317 to 515 tok/s.

## Validation

Unit test (new): `test_partial_tail_load_keeps_tail_chunk_storable` loads 28 tokens with 16-token chunks. Chunk 0 is a full hit, and chunk 1 holds the partial tail. The test checks that the full-attention group starts its store at chunk 1, and that the Mamba group keeps the skip.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  -k test_partial_tail_load_keeps_tail_chunk_storable
# main:     1 failed (AssertionError: assert 2 == 1)
# this PR:  1 passed

pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/
# this PR:  564 passed, 2 skipped (the two skipped tests need a GPU backend)
```

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `typos` and `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.11` pass on the changed files. CI runs these tests in the `v1/kv_connector/unit` step.

End to end, on an older base: nightly 21d93d0d8 (2026-10-05). The lines that this PR changes are the same in that base and in main. Both runs have the same other local patches.

- Model: GLM-5.3-Flash (MLA and KDA layers; the KDA groups use Mamba cache mode `align`), W4A16 checkpoint with BF16 activations, 2× H200, TP=2, no expert parallelism.
- MTP with 3 probabilistic draft tokens, block verification and `disable_eagle_block_drop`.
- `--prefix-match-unit 64`. The attention block is 2,304 tokens, so most loads end in a partial tail.
- OffloadingConnector with a 330 GiB CPU tier and no disk tier.
- Load: simulated coding-agent sessions, 16 and then 32 concurrent sessions, 8 minutes per level. Each session starts new, and its context grows from about 75K to 140K tokens (6K shared prefix). One run per configuration; the run-to-run difference of this load is about ±1 % at 16 and ±3 % at 32 sessions.

| Metric (16 / 32 sessions) | Without the fix | With the fix |
|---|---|---|
| Output tok/s | 474 / 317 | 472 / 515 |
| Computed prefill tokens per request | 6,561 / 19,597 | 6,603 / 9,213 |
| Prompt tokens left after the cache hits, warm turns at 32 sessions | 12,220 | 3,613 |
| Prompt tokens from the CPU tier, 32 sessions | 74.7 % | 89.2 % |
| Warm TTFT p50 | 0.9 / 5.9 s | 0.9 / 2.1 s |

Without the fix, the CPU-tier hit of a session at 32 sessions stays at one boundary for several turns. For example, it stays at 114,752 tokens for prompts of 138K, 139K, 144K and 145K tokens, and each of these turns computes 24K–30K tokens again. At 16 sessions the computed prefill does not change (6,561 and 6,603 tokens per request).

## Details

Root cause: `update_state_after_alloc` sets `num_chunks = cdiv(num_cached_tokens, tokens_per_chunk)`. This count includes the chunk of a partial tail. For the chunk-level policy, `next_stored_chunk_idx = num_chunks` then treats that chunk as a hit chunk. The load fills the chunk only up to the tail boundary, and the request computes the rest of it. The store starts at the next chunk, so the full chunk is never stored, and its key never becomes a hit. Example: a load to 114,752 tokens with 2,304-token chunks gives `num_chunks = 50`, and the store skips chunk 49.

Fix: for a full-attention group (`sliding_window_size_in_chunks is None`), the store starts one chunk earlier when the load ends in a partial tail. Sliding-window, chunked-local and Mamba groups keep the skip: their block for that chunk can hold the tail state, which is not the state at the chunk end. The Mamba groups store their boundary states through the copy-on-write path (`requires_cow_source`).

Scope: the change has an effect only when `supports_partial_tail` is true (a Mamba group in align mode, one block per chunk) and a load ends in a partial tail. In all other cases `next_stored_chunk_idx` is unchanged.

Cost: one more chunk store per load that ends in a partial tail. The CPU tier did not have that chunk before.

title: [EPLB] Support heterogeneous DeepSeek V4/V4.1 DSpark draft experts
body:
## Overview
Follow-up of #57549

Enable EPLB for DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 DSpark drafts when their expert topology differs from the target model.
This PR covers DSpark’s draft model loader.
Related: [#59611](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59611) fixes redundant expert loading in the target model. 


## Claims

- Register supported DSpark draft MoE models with the target’s EPLB state.
- Allow target and draft models to have different expert counts and topologies. Reduce load statistics per model when their physical expert counts differ, while retaining the combined reduction path when shapes match.
- Include redundant expert slots in the V4.1 DSpark fused-MoE weight mapping.

## Validation
- CPU-runnable pytest subset:.
- Add coverage for heterogeneous topology handling, EPLB registration, and DSpark redundant-slot mapping.

### GSM8K validation.

server:
```
vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --served-model-name nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --enable-eplb \
  --eplb-config '{"num_redundant_experts":8,"step_interval":100,"log_balancedness":true}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
```

client:
```
python \
  tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py \
  --num-questions 1319 \
  --num-shots 5 \
  --max-tokens 256 \
  --host http://127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8000 \
  --temperature 0.0 \
  --seed 42 \
```

Result. Accuracy: 0.890


Logs:
```
(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=2822063) INFO 10-14 18:33:21 [eplb_state.py:641] EPLB step: 79 for model nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 (draft): avg_tokens=4500.00, max_tokens=6896, balancedness=0.6526, steps until the next rearrangement: 21
(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=2822063) INFO 10-14 18:33:21 [eplb_state.py:641] EPLB step: 79 for model nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4: avg_tokens=238800.00, max_tokens=354552, balancedness=0.6735, steps until the next rearrangement: 21
```

Both models (target and draft) are involved in eplb rearrangement.


## Details

The target and DSpark draft can have different routed and physical expert counts. EPLB state now keeps topology-dependent counts per registered model and handles load-stat reductions when models have different physical expert dimensions.

DSpark’s custom weight loader is a separate call path from the target model’s `get_expert_mapping`. Since DSpark is now registered with EPLB, its redundant physical slots must also receive the replicated expert weights. #59611 addresses the target model’s mapping; end-to-end use with redundant experts requires that fix as well.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Pin host tensors passed to the FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA plan
body:
## Overview

`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` passes pageable CPU tensors (qo/kv indptr, KV lengths) to `BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper.plan()`. The wrapper copies them to the GPU with `non_blocking=True`, so `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` rejects the copy as an implicit sync. On GLM-5.3-Flash on H200 the engine dies on its first request. This PR stages the tensors in pinned memory, the same pattern #54660 applied to the FlashInfer backend.

## Claims

- GLM-5.3-Flash (H200, SM90 sparse MLA) now runs under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Before this change it failed on the first request.
- Every host tensor `plan()` copies to the device is now pinned. The reused staging buffers stay unpinned, as in `flashinfer.py`.
- No performance claim: DEP8 decode throughput is neutral within run-to-run noise (table below).

## Validation

**Reproducer** (GLM-5.3-Flash, TP4 + MTP3, 4×H200):

    VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
      --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-num-seqs 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
      --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' \
      --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
    vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
      --dataset-name speed_bench --speed-bench-dataset-subset throughput_1k \
      --speed-bench-output-len 256 --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 16

| | implicit-sync errors | requests completed |
|---|---|---|
| main | 17. The engine died: `Tensor.copy_: a non_blocking H2D copy that may be silently synchronous (the CPU tensor is not pinned)`, raised from FlashInfer `_stage_metadata` under `_SM90State._plan` | 0 / 64 |
| this PR | 0 | 64 / 64 |

**Unit tests** (H200): `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py`: 25 passed. `test_plan_uses_state_params` now asserts that the tensors handed to the wrapper are pinned whenever pinned memory is available.

**Performance** (DEP8 decode-only, 8×H200, DecodeBenchConnector, ISL 128K / OSL 512, MTP3 with synthetic acceptance [0.8, 0.6, 0.5], warm pass). C=128 was measured twice; the other points once.

| C | main tok/s, TPOT ms | this PR tok/s, TPOT ms |
|---|---|---|
| 64 | 3534, 12.89 | 3927, 11.45 |
| 128 | 4867, 17.48 | 5137, 17.04 |
| 192 | 5684, 20.53 | 5641, 20.29 |

## Details

`_SM90State._plan` fills reusable CPU buffers (`_qo_cpu`, `_kv_cpu`, `_lens_cpu`) in place and passes them to the wrapper. With `use_cuda_graph=True`, the wrapper's `_stage_metadata` copies them into its reserved device buffers with `non_blocking=True`. From pageable memory CUDA may synchronize to stage that copy, which is what the sync check flags.

The fix passes a `.pin_memory()` copy of each buffer instead of making the buffers themselves pinned. PyTorch's caching host allocator keeps a pinned block alive until the async copy that reads it completes, so the next plan cannot overwrite in-flight data. Pinning the reused buffers directly would need explicit events to avoid that race. This mirrors `vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py` since #54660.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this backend's plan staging. #58684 removed this plan's D2H sync; this change covers the H2D side.

Out of scope: `plan()` itself costs 4–6.5 ms per call, measured without the profiler. Most of that is FlashInfer's Python workload validation (`_fa_plan_work_count`), which runs over all `max_num_batched_tokens` rows, twice per plan. That belongs in a FlashInfer change.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

---

title: [FlashInfer] Add opt-in eager/graph autotune measurement
body:
## Overview

Add an opt-in eager/CUDA Graph measurement objective to the managed FlashInfer autotune warmup. **Stacked on #55671**; review the [isolated follow-up delta](https://github.com/YangXu1990uiuc/vllm/compare/1fee4445c1167e0d7c9bcd2f9cb6d25e1b75afcd...1dcfdf806392ea2795a9a082ae0dc6750ef0bc08). The cache migration can land independently.

## Claims

- `KernelConfig.flashinfer_autotune_execution_mode` accepts `auto` (existing per-op defaults), `eager` (include recurring host cost), and `cuda_graph` (measure captured replay).
- Forward the explicit public `MeasurementPolicy` through generic and sparse-MLA warmup; reject explicit modes when autotuning is disabled or the managed-cache deployment is ineligible.
- Keep the parent's single-rank gate and existing default measurement policy. FlashInfer separates explicit policies into distinct cache namespaces; serving reuses the attached store without a new per-token dispatch or synchronization step.

This is one objective for the whole warmup, **not automatic per-path policy selection**. It does not change vLLM's graph configuration.

## Validation

Source: `1dcfdf806392`; baseline: parent `1fee4445c116`. B200 + Xeon Platinum 8570 (16 allocated CPUs, OMP=4), Qwen3-8B-FP8, MRv2, TP1, Torch 2.13.0, FlashInfer Python/cubin `0.7.0.post1` and JIT cache `0.7.0.post1+cu130`; CUDA runtime 13.0, cuBLAS 13.1.1, cuDNN 9.20 and cuDNN Frontend 1.31.0. Complete Python source overlaid on compatible native wheel `187a0eb98aa4`; no native rebuild. `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` was enabled.

- **137 tests passed**: 135 existing warmup/lifecycle tests plus 2 configuration-rejection cases. Existing Model Executor and engine CI suites cover these files.
- **16/16 GPU cases passed**: cold/warm for all four engine/policy combinations, plus two additional independent cold-tuning rounds. Each case verified its policy namespace, serving/capture cache hits, finite selected-token logprobs and actual engine execution mode. All four warm stores remained unchanged with no new profiling calls for this model.
- Formatting and Python 3.12 typing passed. The parent's pre-existing Python 3.11 parse failure in `sharded_state_loader.py:214` is already fixed on main; the standard 3.11 mypy hook also passed with only that upstream syntax fix temporarily overlaid.

Initial hosted CI is **gated**, not green: [pre-run-check](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/38389349806/job/115270912816) reports no qualifying readiness/verification label and 0 qualifying merged PRs for the author. [Read the Docs #35115277](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35115277/) exited in `docs/pre_run_check.sh` because that check did not pass, before building the docs. DCO passed; the local and GPU results above are separate evidence.

**Fixed-token offline `LLM.generate` wall time**: one untimed warmup plus five measurements per workload in each of three independently tuned processes. Table uses the median of per-process medians; speedup is the median paired ratio, with the range across the three tuning rounds. Configuration order alternates between rounds; audit hooks are removed before timing. Baseline uses `auto`; candidate uses the explicit policy matching the named experiment. These are not HTTP serving or TTFT/ITL results.

| Engine configuration | Batch / input / output tokens | Default objective | Explicit objective | Speedup, median (range) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| eager | 1 / 32 / 128 | 7.392 s | 6.560 s | 1.129x (0.997–1.129) |
| eager | 8 / 32 / 128 | 7.880 s | 5.655 s | 1.391x (1.322–1.394) |
| eager | 16 / 1024 / 128 | 8.225 s | 7.468 s | 1.101x (1.041–1.198) |
| graph | 1 / 32 / 128 | 0.377 s | 0.368 s | 1.019x (0.979–1.036) |
| graph | 8 / 32 / 128 | 0.424 s | 0.448 s | 0.947x (0.912–0.970) |
| graph | 16 / 1024 / 128 | 1.991 s | 2.099 s | 0.949x (0.897–0.963) |

`graph` requested `FULL`, but the FlashInfer attention backend resolved it to **FULL_AND_PIECEWISE**. Worker audit observed both full and piecewise replay, plus managed hits during capture. The tested capture sizes were `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16]`; larger/out-of-range prefill runs eagerly. This is a mixed engine with a single global graph measurement objective, not proof of optimal policy selection for every runtime path.

Full GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot, 256-token limit, one evaluation pair per engine configuration. Intervals below are approximate paired normal 95% intervals; these runs do not establish accuracy equivalence.

| Engine | Default objective | Explicit objective | Difference and interval |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| eager | 1149/1319 (87.11%) | 1153/1319 (87.41%) | +0.30 pp; [-1.06, +1.67] |
| graph | 1156/1319 (87.64%) | 1144/1319 (86.73%) | -0.91 pp; [-2.27, +0.45] |

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and local checks</summary>

```bash
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py -q
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/test_config.py -k flashinfer_measurement_requires_autotuning -q
```

Run changed-file pre-commit and `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.12` on the changed Python files. For the 3.11 check on this old stacked base, apply main's existing `sharded_state_loader.py` syntax fix first; it is not part of this feature's delta.

For GPU reproduction, use the versions above and `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error OMP_NUM_THREADS=4`. Use a fresh `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE_DIR` per tuning round, reusing it for the warm restart. Set `enable_prefix_caching=False`, `max_model_len=4096`, `max_num_batched_tokens=512`, `max_num_seqs=16`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.7`, and `seed=0`. Pin `nvidia/Qwen3-8B-FP8` at revision `2cebc4c89e25abc17668c81b01dceaf3d8b914d5`.

Use `enforce_eager=True` for the eager experiments. For graph-enabled experiments, set `compilation_config={"cudagraph_mode": "FULL", "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1,2,4,8,16]}`. Enable autotuning in `kernel_config`; omit the new field for the baseline and set it to `eager` or `cuda_graph` for the candidate.

For each table row, submit `batch` prompts whose token IDs are `[1000 + i] * input_tokens`, with `SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=128, ignore_eos=True, seed=0)`. Warm once, then time five `LLM.generate(..., use_tqdm=False)` calls and assert exactly `batch * 128` output tokens each. Repeat with three fresh tuning roots, reversing configuration order for the middle round.

Evaluate with `tests.evals.gsm8k.gsm8k_eval._build_gsm8k_prompts(1319, 5)` and `SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=256, seed=42, stop=["Question", "Assistant:", "<|separator|>"])`, then the suite's `_score_gsm8k`.

Example user configuration:

```bash
vllm serve <model> --enforce-eager \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": true, "flashinfer_autotune_execution_mode": "eager"}'
```

</details>

## Details

Kept as a follow-up because a graph-enabled vLLM engine can mix full graphs, piecewise graphs and eager fallbacks. The knob allows controlled evaluation, but automatically choosing policies also requires matching the winner store to capture and uncaptured execution. Defaults therefore remain unchanged. The configuration field participates in vLLM's kernel hash as well as the explicit policy being part of FlashInfer's managed namespace.

New-policy GPU coverage is limited to this dense FP8 model on B200. SM120 sparse-MLA and MoE need hardware/model coverage; their warmup forwarding and rejection contracts are unit-tested only. Multi-rank managed tuning remains disabled and does not depend on FlashInfer #6185 for this scope. Broader accuracy and runtime-path qualification remain before changing defaults.

Duplicate checks found no `MeasurementPolicy` integration PR. #59995 concerns MoE search strategy and #59698 cache-only startup; this adds the measurement objective on top of the existing #55671 cache migration. AI assistance was used for implementation, review, validation and this description. Human review of the new code remains required before readiness.

title: [Kernel] Scale elementwise kernel launches with the device, not just batch size
body:
## Overview

`silu_and_mul` and the other `act_and_mul` variants, the scalar activations,
`swigluoai_and_mul`, `situ_and_mul` and `rotary_embedding` all launch `grid(num_tokens)`
with one block per token, so the grid is only as wide as the batch however much work a
token carries. At decode that leaves most of the device idle. This splits a token's work
across `gridDim.y` when the batch alone cannot fill the device.

## Claims

- **+1.1% to +3.1% end-to-end output throughput** on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-30B-A3B at
  low-to-moderate concurrency, with the custom ops enabled.
- Kernel level: up to 3.42x on `silu_and_mul` and 1.91x on `rotary_embedding`; medians
  1.31x over 288 shapes and 1.58x over 108 gated-activation shapes.
- Unchanged where the batch already fills the device: 0.994x-1.004x by construction.
- Bit-identical output on every tested shape; NIAH accuracy unchanged.
- One shared helper, no API change, no new kernel entry point.

## Validation

**Bitwise.** 288 shapes (`silu_and_mul`, `rotary_embedding`, bf16 and fp16, 1-2048 tokens,
neox and non-neox, several head counts) and 108 gated-activation shapes compared against
the unpatched build — `torch.equal` and SHA-256 of raw output bytes, not a tolerance.

**End-to-end**, MI355X, `VLLM_PLUGINS=` (upstream vLLM, no out-of-tree plugin), compiled
path with the custom ops enabled via
`-cc '{"custom_ops":["+silu_and_mul","+rotary_embedding",...]}'`. Output throughput,
mean of 4 reps, with arms rotated across GPUs and benchmark positions so GPU and ordering
bias cancel (measured GPU-to-GPU bias on identical builds: 0.21%):

| workload | Llama-3.1-8B | Qwen3-30B-A3B |
|---|---|---|
| in=128 out=256 conc=1 | **1.031x** | **1.012x** |
| in=128 out=256 conc=8 | **1.026x** | **1.028x** |
| in=1024 out=256 conc=32 | 1.017x | — |
| in=1024 out=128 conc=64 | 1.007x | 1.011x |
| in=200 out=64 conc=64 | 1.005x | **1.019x** |
| in=4096 out=128 conc=8 | **1.023x** | 1.013x |
| in=8192 out=64 conc=8 | 0.984x | 1.013x |
| in=32768 out=32 conc=4 | 1.000x | — |

TPOT moves with it — Llama at conc=1 goes 3.50 -> 3.40 ms (1.031x), and Qwen3-30B-A3B
gains 1-4% across its points. TTFT is unchanged within noise, as expected: the launch only
changes when `num_tokens < sm_count`, so prefill, where the grid is already full, is
untouched. That is also why the result is neutral at 8k/32k; the single 0.984x is ~0.5
sigma against that point's run-to-run spread.

**Models exercised, including those that showed nothing.** Reach was verified by loading
each model and reading vLLM's own `Op '<x>' not present in model` log plus worker profiler
kernel counts, not by inspecting configs:

| model | config | result |
|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B | TP1, custom ops on | table above, +0.5% to +3.1% |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | TP1, custom ops on | table above, +1.1% to +2.8% |
| Kimi-K3 | TP8, aiter on (needed for the MLA backend) | throughput 0.999-1.004x, TTFT 0.997-1.019x, TPOT 1.000-1.005x |
| MiniMax-M3 | TP2 | no valid measurement — see below |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | TP8 | reaches none of these ops; not benchmarked |

Kimi-K3 is the only model in a 64-checkpoint survey that reaches `situ_and_mul`, and it
is flat: the kernel does run there (profiler confirms 279 calls), but it is 0.79% of
device time because aiter's fused MoE absorbs the expert activations, so a 7x kernel win
caps out below measurement resolution. MiniMax-M3 has no configuration that is both
usable and exercises the patched kernels — without aiter it runs at 5.5 tok/s, and with
aiter its rope is absorbed into `fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert` and
`rotary_embedding_kernel` executes zero times.

**Kernel level**, HIP-graph replay, minimum of several runs:

| kernel | shape | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `situ_and_mul` | d=28672, 1-2 tokens | 14.9-15.3us | 2.1-2.2us | 7.0x |
| `swigluoai_and_mul` | d=28672, 1 token | 9.0us | 2.1us | 4.4x |
| `silu_and_mul` | d=28672, 1-16 tokens | 7.2-8.0us | 2.2-2.5us | up to 3.4x |
| `silu_and_mul` | d=14336, 64 tokens | 4.52us | 2.82us | 1.60x |
| `rotary_embedding` | 32 heads, 8-32 tokens | 4.3-4.4us | 2.3us | up to 1.91x |

**Accuracy.** lm_eval RULER NIAH (`niah_single_2`, `niah_multikey_1`) at 8192 and 32768
tokens, 100 docs per cell, both models, both modes: 1.0 in all 16 cells, patched identical
to base. Generated text is not bit-identical across runs, but a null control — two
identical base builds — reproduces the same 62-92% range, so that is vLLM's batching
nondeterminism rather than this patch.

## Details

**Root cause.** `grid(num_tokens)` is as wide as the batch, not as wide as the device. At
one token these kernels put a single block on 256 CUs.

**Change.** `vllm_elementwise_launch_config()` in `csrc/launch_bounds_utils.h`, used by
every call site in `activation_kernels.cu` and `pos_encoding_kernels.cu`. Once
`num_tokens >= sm_count` it returns the existing configuration, so large-batch launches
are untouched; below that it uses smaller blocks and splits a token's work over `chunks`
blocks in `gridDim.y`. Every element is still handled by exactly one thread reading the
same inputs, which is why results do not move.

**Where this helper fits.** It suits kernels whose loop strides over the hidden dim, so
any `(threads, chunks)` split is valid. It does *not* suit kernels that give each
`blockIdx.y` a contiguous chunk and vectorize inside it — there a small chunk leaves too
few elements per thread to form a wide load. All the kernels here are the first kind.

**Scope — please read before judging the numbers.** These ops are `CustomOp`s, and
`CustomOp.default_on()` is false when Inductor is in use, so **in the default compiled
configuration they are replaced by Inductor-generated Triton kernels and this patch does
not run**. A decode profile confirms it: the activation work appears as
`triton_poi_fused_mul_silu_slice_*` with zero `vllm::act_and_mul_kernel`. The end-to-end
numbers above are from the explicit-custom-ops configuration; the default-configuration
gain is zero.

**Model reach of the gated activations.** Over 64 checkpoints, `situ_and_mul` is reached
by one architecture (Kimi-K3) and `swigluoai_and_mul` by none — MiniMax-M3's AMD path
deliberately uses an fp32 Triton `swiglu_oai_split`, for accuracy. Given the Kimi-K3
result above, **the 7.05x and 4.36x figures should be read as microbenchmark-only**; the
end-to-end case rests on `silu_and_mul` and `rotary_embedding`.

---

- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Bitwise sweeps, end-to-end throughput on two models with

title: [CI][Feature] Meta-device mode for CPU-only end-to-end engine CI
body:
## Overview

Adds `VLLM_META_MODE`, an opt-in mode that runs the v1 engine end-to-end through Model Runner V2 (MRV2) on a CPU-only host with weights and KV cache on the PyTorch `meta` device. Large production models can then be validated structurally (construction, sharding, attention/MoE/quantization dispatch, scheduling, prefix caching, KV offload) without reserving a GPU node.

This work is one of the prerequisites for the vLLM Simulator proposed in RFC #61406: the same meta-device execution path provides the CPU-only engine initialization on which hardware-aware performance simulation builds.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Maintainer decision needed:** should the fake kernels in `_META_OVERRIDES` (`vllm/meta_mode.py`) be maintained by the owners of the corresponding modules? See [Decisions requested](#decisions-requested).

## Claims

- New `load_format="meta"` (`MetaModelLoader`) builds the model on `meta` with no checkpoint download and no weight initialization. Weights, the KV pool, and the L2 offload buffer use 0 real bytes.
- Production configurations run unchanged: real TP=8 + EP, PP=2, PCP=2, and DCP=2 ranks in the regular `MultiprocExecutor` over Gloo, with the requested quantization preserved (FP8 per-tensor, FP8 block-wise, ModelOpt NVFP4, `deepseek_v4_fp8`).
- New `tests/meta/test_meta_models.py` (9 cases) pins and asserts MRV2, and covers Kimi-K3, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, GLM-5, and Qwen3-30B-A3B / DeepSeek-V2-Lite. It runs a full 8704-token prompt and checks a 4-round L1/L2 `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` round-trip. Weights and KV stay on meta, while MRV2's value-carrying host bookkeeping runs through the Triton interpreter.
- When `VLLM_META_MODE` is unset, nothing changes: `vllm/meta_mode.py` is not imported, and every other branch depends on that env var, on `load_format == "meta"`, or on `tensor.is_meta`.

## Validation

Environment: Intel Xeon Platinum 8369B (128 cores), GPUs hidden with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""`, torch 2.13.0, HF configs from the local cache only.

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" VLLM_META_MODE=1 \
  python -m pytest tests/meta/test_meta_models.py -v --noconftest -p no:cacheprovider
```

| Case | Coverage | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `Kimi-K3` | KDA/Mamba "align", TP=8+EP, offload round-trip | PASSED |
| `Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8` | Hybrid GDN + full attn, block-wise FP8, offload round-trip | PASSED |
| `DeepSeek-V4-Pro` | Sparse MLA, `fp8_ds_mla` KV, `deepseek_v4_fp8` | PASSED |
| `GLM-5` | DSA, FA3 shape override | PASSED |
| `quant-fp8-per-tensor` | Qwen3-30B-A3B + `hf_overrides` FP8, offload round-trip | PASSED |
| `quant-nvfp4` | Qwen3-30B-A3B + ModelOpt NVFP4, offload round-trip | PASSED |
| `parallel-pp` | PP=2 | PASSED |
| `parallel-pcp` | DeepSeek-V2-Lite, PCP=2 | PASSED |
| `parallel-dcp` | TP=2, DCP=2 | PASSED |

All 9 cases pass in 225.12 seconds (3 min 45 s) on the CPU-only host.


## Details

### Motivation

Integrating a large model raises the same questions every time. Does the production config construct? Are the TP/EP/DCP shards and KV shapes valid? Do attention, MoE, quantization, scheduling, and offload compose correctly? Small synthetic models miss architecture-specific paths, and GPU E2E runs are expensive and capacity-constrained.

### Design

Mode-wide setup is gated by `envs.VLLM_META_MODE`. Tensor-local fallbacks use `tensor.is_meta`, so they also hold for any caller that passes meta tensors. No vLLM class is monkeypatched. Some parts of the implementation draw on ideas from #59019.

- **Config / platform:** `VllmConfig.__post_init__` forces `enforce_eager` and `load_format="meta"`. It disables async scheduling only for PP>1, because the async sampled-token broadcast needs real values, and it drops `speculative_config`. `wrap_meta_platform` mixes four device-less capabilities over the detected platform: no pinned memory, zero memory usage, one compute unit, and 8 devices.
- **Worker / runner:** `init_device` runs on CPU with Gloo, then constructs the configured runner (MRV2 by default; the suite sets `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` and asserts it). The KV budget comes from the KV spec instead of profiling, and warmup is skipped. `self.device` stays `cpu`, so MRV2 request state and scheduling buffers keep real values, while weights, KV, intermediate tensors, and compute-only metadata use `meta`. Meta sampler outputs are materialized as constant host token ids before MRV2 feeds them back into request state and starts async output copy. `MetaAsyncOutput` wraps either runner's output and applies `num_scheduled_tokens × VLLM_META_TOKEN_LATENCY_MS`, preserving async-output overlap.
- **Kernels:** `register_meta_impls()` derives Meta kernels from operator schemas for leaf ops that return nothing or return an aliased input. A small override table covers ops whose outputs are independent of their inputs: FA2 `varlen_fwd`, FA3 `fwd`, FlashMLA sparse prefill/decode, and the DeepSeek-V4 quant insert. Native launches that cannot carry a `torch.library` kernel are intercepted by `install_launch_hooks()`: MRV2's host-only request-state/input/block-table Triton kernels run in the CPU interpreter, while model/attention launches and launches touching meta tensors are skipped. CuteDSL, TileLang, and `torch.cuda` Event/Stream/device queries remain shape-only stubs. DeepGEMM keeps its impls unbound and returns shape-only results.
- **Parallelism:** `GroupCoordinator` uses `device=meta` with `DeviceCommunicatorBase`, so collectives propagate shapes without payloads. EP uses `AgRsAll2AllManager`.
- **Offload:** `SimpleCPUOffloadWorker` skips pinned allocation and DMA when the KV cache is on `meta`, and every pending event polls as complete. All scheduler-side logic and hash bookkeeping run unchanged.
- **Quantization:** Narrow `is_meta` early returns in `process_weights_after_loading`/`apply` cover the Marlin FP8, ModelOpt NVFP4, and `requantize_with_max_scale` paths, which need real values for repacking or for `.item()`.

### Decisions requested

1. **Ownership of independent-output fake kernels** (`_META_OVERRIDES` in `vllm/meta_mode.py`). These ops return new tensors whose shapes cannot be derived from the schema, so someone has to write the shape logic.
   - **(a) Central table (current).** All meta fakes live in one place and are gated on meta, but meta-CI maintainers must track changes in kernels they do not own. A changed output shape is only caught when the E2E test fails.
   - **(b) Owner-maintained `register_fake` next to the op definition.** Each fake lives in the kernel's own module (`vllm_flash_attn`, FlashMLA, DeepSeek-V4) under its CODEOWNERS, and new ops with independent outputs would be expected to ship a fake. The meta mode keeps only the schema-derived defaults. This is how the first commit was structured.
   - With (b), the central table goes away. With (a), it should be shared with #59019's `OVERRIDES`.
2. **Launch-layer routing/stubs** (Triton, CuteDSL, TileLang, `torch.cuda` primitives). Is this acceptable as a temporary process-wide fallback, to be retired op by op once a fake exists?
3. **CI hardware availability and worker split.** Can CI provide a small amount of accelerator capacity—for example, an A10 as the CUDA execution substrate while structurally validating configurations intended for GB300-class deployments? If so, an alternative design is:
   - CPU-only jobs use `CPUWorker` / `CPUModelRunnerV2` for CPU runtime coverage.
   - GPU jobs use `GPUWorker` / `GPUModelRunnerV2`, while weights, KV cache, and model activations remain on `meta` and model compute remains shape-only.
   - Because parameter/KV storage and model compute consume almost no device memory or compute, one GPU host could exercise many large-model and parallel configurations. A real CUDA context could handle streams and value-carrying Triton bookkeeping, allowing most Triton and `torch.cuda` interception to be removed.
   - An A10 would not emulate GB300 numerics, kernels, memory capacity, or architecture-specific capability checks; it would only provide the CUDA control-plane substrate. Is that structural fidelity sufficient, and is such shared hardware capacity available?
4. **Initial CI scope.** Which models and quantization paths should the first CPU job require?

### Tradeoffs and limitations

- Scope is structural only: meta tensors carry no data, so numerics, kernel correctness, real communication, and performance are out of scope. GPU tests remain authoritative.
- Both Model Runner V1 and MRV2 retain meta paths, but the E2E suite pins MRV2 so regressions cannot silently fall back to MRV1. MRV2's host bookkeeping kernels are interpreted rather than GPU-launched; model-side Triton/CuteDSL launches remain shape-only no-ops.
- The launch-layer stubs are process-wide fallbacks, so meta tests must run in dedicated processes. The intent is to retire each stub once the owning kernel gains a `register_fake` / meta branch.
- Speculative decoding is dropped in meta mode because its acceptance loop has value-dependent boundaries.
- If every attention backend is rejected (no accelerator), meta mode picks the first backend that imports and matches the requested sparsity. Attention forward is faked, so the backend class is used only for metadata.
- **CI:** this PR adds no Buildkite job yet. The suite is CPU-only and needs the HF configs available locally. I propose starting it as a non-blocking CPU job and making it required once runtime and stability are proven.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.

title: [CI] Release the previous checkpoint's page cache between LM Eval models
body:
## Overview

An LM Eval config list walks several multi-GiB checkpoints through a single container. Page cache is charged to the container's memory cgroup, which is what `_get_available_ram_bytes()` measures, so the models evaluated so far consume the RAM budget of the ones still to come. The safetensors prefetch is then skipped partway down the list and the loader falls back to serial mmap reads over NFS, roughly an order of magnitude slower.

I free each checkpoint's page cache when the next model is about to load, reusing the existing `drop_checkpoint_cache()`. The harness change is CI only and the release is gated on ROCm. `drop_checkpoint_cache()` itself gains a cache lookup fallback and a log line, which its one existing caller also benefits from.

## Claims

Two AMD steps lose their prefetch today and both should be fixed. The last model's cache is left in place, since nothing in the job needs it again but the next job on the node may. Every other step on this harness is unaffected, because its checkpoints are small enough or it loads a single model, so the gate never trips.

This is **gated on ROCm**, following `_shutdown_lm` in the same file. `:nvidia: (H100) LM Eval Large Models` runs the same config list but reads over VIRTIOFS rather than NFS, so `is_net_fs` is false and auto-prefetch never turns on there. Its available RAM also sits at 1.58 TiB and does not fall between the two models, measured over the last four nightlies, so upstream has nothing to gain.

The FP8 numbers below are **measured in CI**. The Large Models Harness numbers are **estimates derived from nightly timings**.

## Evidence from CI

`(MI355) LM Eval Large Models FP8` loads `Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-FP8` (220.19 GiB) and then `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MXFP4` (148.18 GiB). Five nightlies on `main`:

| build | date | step | 1st load | avail. RAM | 2nd load | avail. RAM |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 93775 | Oct 9 | 16.7m | 0.8m | 333.42 GiB | 0.3m | 137.91 GiB |
| 93991 | Oct 10 | 26.5m | 0.7m | 333.18 GiB | **10.5m** | 111.59 GiB |
| 94055 | Oct 11 | 26.4m | 1.0m | 333.53 GiB | **10.0m** | 114.73 GiB |
| 94125 | Oct 12 | 26.7m | 0.8m | 332.83 GiB | **10.1m** | 116.02 GiB |
| 94391 | Oct 13 | **36.9m** | **9.5m** | **118.52 GiB** | **7.1m** | **0.63 GiB** |
| 94471 | this PR | **16.4m** | 0.72m | 333.27 GiB | **0.50m** | **332.29 GiB** |
| 94479 | this PR | **16.6m** | 0.78m | 332.39 GiB | **0.51m** | **329.55 GiB** |

Everything other than weight loading is flat at 15.0 to 16.3m across all of them, and 15.2m with this change, so the whole 16.7 to 36.9m spread is loading. The step has a 45 minute timeout; build 94391 left 8.1 minutes of headroom and 94471 leaves 28.6.

The last two rows are the result with this change, in consecutive runs. The first model read 220.19 GiB with a prefetch that finished in 22s, so that page cache was certainly charged to the cgroup, yet the second model measured 332.29 GiB available where every earlier nightly saw 0.63 to 138 GiB. It loaded in 29.89s instead of 7 to 10.5 minutes.

`(MI355) LM Eval Large Models Harness` shows the same over five checkpoints. Build 94125, per model:

| model | checkpoint | avail. RAM | prefetch | load |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-70B-Instruct` | 131.42 GiB | 263.76 GiB | runs | 17.0s |
| `mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1` | 86.99 GiB | 130.81 GiB | runs | 12.0s |
| `Qwen/Qwen2-57B-A14B-Instruct` | 106.93 GiB | 63.02 GiB | **skipped** | **194.8s** |
| `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` | 29.26 GiB | 28.43 GiB | **skipped** | **72.6s** |
| `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16` | 58.82 GiB | 8.32 GiB | **skipped** | **155.6s** |

Available RAM falls 264, 131, 63, 28, 8 GiB and the three skipped prefetches cost 423s. At the rate the first two loaded, those three would take about a minute. The step ran 19.5m here against 13.5m and 16.8m on the neighbouring nightlies.

In build 94479 this step ran 16.1m with loading down from 452s to 260s, and the log showed why it is not yet at its floor: the release worked for three checkpoints and reported `No local checkpoint found` for `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-70B-Instruct` and `mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1`. Offline, `snapshot_download()` resolves a revision only through `refs/<revision>`, which the cache on that node does not have for those two repos, so 218.41 GiB stayed charged and one prefetch was still skipped. `drop_checkpoint_cache()` now falls back to the cache layout, which should take the step the rest of the way.

## Impact

| step | models | total checkpoints | effect |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| (MI355) LM Eval Large Models FP8 | 2 | 368 GiB | **10.3 minutes faster, measured** |
| (MI355) LM Eval Large Models Harness | 6 | 413 GiB | **about 6 minutes faster, measured** |
| (MI300) LM Eval Large Models Harness | 6 | 413 GiB | **about 16 minutes faster, measured** |


No model name repeats within a list, and none of these checkpoints appears in another config list, so no eval re-reads a checkpoint this releases.

## Details

`drop_checkpoint_cache()` already existed and is already tested by `test_drop_checkpoint_cache_releases_local_weight_files`, but its only caller is `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py`, which uses it to make room for Engram host tables. The generic loader never releases the cache its prefetch warms.

Releasing the previous model's cache at the start of the next load, rather than the current model's cache at the end of its own, keeps the last model cached without having to know which model is last. Skipped evals never reach `launch_lm_eval`, so they do not disturb the tracking.

The harness logger is named after the test module, not `vllm.*`, so it has no handler and its INFO records are dropped. The release notice is therefore a `print`, and `drop_checkpoint_cache()` reports which directory it resolved and how much it evicted, so a step that frees nothing can be told apart from one that frees the wrong files.

The lookup fallback cannot tell which revision was loaded, so it evicts every cached snapshot of the repo. Nothing is deleted and `posix_fadvise` leaves dirty pages alone, so the worst case is that a later job re-reads a snapshot from NFS.

title: [Kernel] Coalesce reshape_and_cache stores by taking a KV block at a time
body:
## Overview

`reshape_and_cache` writes the paged KV cache one token per block, which makes every
store a column write and leaves the kernel at roughly 8% of achievable bandwidth. This
takes a whole KV block of tokens per block instead, so both destinations are contiguous.
**3.3x on the kernel; see the honest end-to-end read below before judging the value.**

This op has one caller in tree — `PagedAttention.write_to_paged_cache`, used only by
`vllm/v1/attention/backends/rocm_attn.py` — so the change is ROCm-only in practice.

## Claims

- **3.32x on the kernel in situ**, measured by profiler inside a real decode run
  (31264us -> 9405us over 128 calls), matching the microbenchmark.
- 1.56x to 3.80x in microbenchmark at 1024-8192 tokens, across aligned *and* misaligned
  slot mappings; no regression where the new path is not taken (1.00x).
- **Mean TTFT improves up to 1.17x under load** (1024-token prompts, concurrency 64;
  median 1.20x, p99 1.10x), which is where a faster KV write should show.
- **End-to-end throughput is unchanged** — the kernel is ~3% of prefill device time, so
  the ceiling is ~2.2% and measurement is flat. TPOT is likewise ~1.000x: this patch
  touches the prefill KV write, not the decode inner loop.
- Output is bit-identical to the unpatched kernel on every tested shape and slot layout;
  NIAH accuracy unchanged.
- No API change, no new kernel entry point, one file touched.

## Validation

**In-tree test:** `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k "test_reshape_and_cache and not flash"` — 72 passed.

**Bitwise.** 380 cases — 5 `(heads, head_size, block_size)` combinations, bf16 and fp16,
1 to 8192 tokens, contiguous / mid-block / random / partly-masked slot mappings — hash
identically to the unpatched build (SHA-256 of raw cache bytes, not a tolerance).

**Kernel**, MI355X, bf16, head_size 128, block_size 16, HIP-graph replay, minimum of 15
replays of a 50-call graph. Slot mappings are built the way vLLM builds them: every
request draws its own shuffled blocks and requests are concatenated along the token
dimension, so a request whose length is not a multiple of `block_size` misaligns every
group after it.

| 8 heads, 8192 tokens | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| one request, aligned | 105.56us | 31.14us | 3.39x |
| two requests [100, 8092] | 105.03us | 28.90us | 3.63x |
| eight requests, random lengths | 104.54us | 29.28us | 3.57x |
| one request, starts mid-block | 105.91us | 29.59us | 3.58x |
| one request, 10% slots masked | 103.32us | 27.22us | 3.80x |

At 1 head / 2048 tokens the launch is below the threshold, the per-token kernel runs
unchanged, and all five scenarios measure 1.00x.

**In situ**, Llama-3.1-8B, prefill of 8192 tokens x 8 sequences, prefix caching disabled:

| | device time | calls | share of step |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reshape_and_cache` (base) | 31264us | 128 | 3.15% |
| `reshape_and_cache_grouped` (patched) | 9405us | 128 | 0.98% |

The grouped path took all 128 calls with no fallback, and the 3.32x matches the
microbenchmark.

**End-to-end**, `VLLM_PLUGINS=` (upstream vLLM), default compiled path, ROCM_ATTN
backend, output throughput, mean of 4 reps with arms rotated across GPUs and benchmark
positions (measured GPU-to-GPU bias on identical builds: 0.21%):

- Llama-3.1-8B, 8 workloads from in=128/conc=1 to in=32768/conc=4: 0.995x to 1.008x
- Qwen3-30B-A3B, 6 workloads: 0.997x to 1.008x

Flat, as the 3.15% share predicts. The `in=200, conc=64` point deliberately exercises
misaligned, fallback-heavy slot runs: 1.008x, no regression.

**TTFT and TPOT.** Throughput is the wrong lens for a prefill-side KV write, so taking the
latency metrics directly — Llama-3.1-8B, in=1024:

| | base | patched | |
|---|---|---|---|
| mean TTFT, conc=32 | — | — | **1.064x** |
| mean TTFT, conc=64 | — | — | **1.170x** |
| median TTFT, conc=64 | — | — | **1.204x** |
| p99 TTFT, conc=64 | — | — | 1.101x |
| TPOT, all points | — | — | ~1.000x |

TTFT improves with load, which is the expected shape: more concurrent prefills mean more
KV-write work per step. Total benchmark duration is unchanged, so this is latency
redistribution rather than extra throughput — useful if TTFT under load is the SLO, not
if the goal is tokens per second.

**Models exercised, including those that showed nothing.** Reach was verified by loading
each model and reading vLLM's `Op '<x>' not present in model` log plus worker profiler
kernel counts:

| model | reaches `reshape_and_cache` | result |
|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B | yes (10080 calls) | throughput flat, TTFT as above |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | yes (15120 calls) | throughput flat |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | no — fuses into `fused_qnorm_rope_kv_insert` | not benchmarked |
| MiniMax-M3 | no — aiter's KV writer | not benchmarked |
| Kimi-K3 | no — MLA uses `concat_and_cache_mla` | not benchmarked |
| Qwen3.8-27B | no — hybrid KV takes a Triton writer | not benchmarked |

**Accuracy.** lm_eval RULER NIAH (`niah_single_2`, `niah_multikey_1`) at 8192 and 32768
tokens, 100 docs per cell, both models: 1.0 in all cells, patched identical to base.

## Details

**Root cause.** The key cache is `[num_blocks, num_heads, head_size/x, block_size, x]` and
the value cache `[num_blocks, num_heads, head_size, block_size]`. With one token per
block, a thread writing the value cache touches elements `block_size` apart, so a cache
line is spent to move 2 bytes. At 4096 tokens the kernel moved 34 MB in 47us.

**Change.** Both layouts are contiguous in the other direction — key over
`(block_offset, i)`, value over `block_offset` — so a block now takes one KV block's worth
of tokens and stages `[block_size, head_size]` tiles through LDS, writing each destination
in its own order. Loads and stores are both contiguous, 16 bytes per thread. Two details
that mattered more than expected, each measured: the key and value halves load before a
*single* barrier (one barrier each serialises two independent streams and costs ~20%), and
the tile rows are padded so reading a tile down a column does not put every thread on one
LDS bank.

**Fallback.** A group only takes the fast path when its slots are one full, block-aligned
run. Ragged request boundaries, prefix-cache hits starting mid-block and masked tokens
(`slot < 0`) take the per-token path, which spreads `block_size * head_size/x` copies over
the whole block so it keeps the occupancy of the original kernel.

**Reach.** Over 64 checkpoints, at most 11 can route here: MLA (36) and hybrid-attention
(11) architectures cannot reach `reshape_and_cache` at all, and some GQA models bypass it
via an aiter fused KV writer.

**What this is worth.** A 3.3x kernel improvement that does not survive to end-to-end
throughput, because the kernel is ~3% of prefill device time. If the goal is throughput,
this is a null result at the step level. The case for it is that the kernel win is real
and verified in situ, the change is contained to one file with no API change, accuracy is
unchanged, and TTFT under load improves — plus it leaves less on the table as KV writes
grow with longer prefills. I would rather state that plainly than present the 3.3x alone.

**Limitation.** The fast path fires only when `block_size` consecutive tokens land on one
aligned KV block, which is not guaranteed in a multi-request batch. The misaligned path is
faster than base rather than slower, so the patch wins either way, but grouping by each
request's own aligned interval (via `query_start_loc`) would make the fast path fire far
more often. Not done here — happy to fold it in if preferred.

---

- [x] **Testing and Validation:** In-tree `test_reshape_and_cache`, bitwise sweeps, in-situ
  profiler attribution, end-to-end throughput on two models, and NIAH accuracy. The
  performance numbers need an MI355X and are not reproducible in CI.

title: [Multimodal] Add GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek V4/V4.1 routing-metadata adapters
body:
## Overview

Add exact image routing-metadata adapters for
GLM-5.3-Flash (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`) and DeepSeek V4/V4.1 so `/render`
can skip vision-tower inputs.

Production code under `vllm/` once merged, assuming rebased on #13 : **+401 / −25** (approx).

## Claims

- Image-only GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek V4/V4.1 routing metadata matches
  full processing exactly.
- DeepSeek live HTTP `/render` on the mixed
  `text+image+text+image+text` prompt (840 tokens), unique media,
  `return_mm_kwargs=false`:

| offered load | unoptimized p50 / p95 | adapter p50 / p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sequential n=15 | 102.2 / 117.5 ms | 10.2 / 11.4 ms |
| 20 RPS × 8s | 51.0 / 67.0 ms | 9.4 / 10.6 ms |
| 25 RPS × 8s | 444 / 1064 ms | 9.1 / 10.2 ms |

- GLM processor A/B (same commit, in-process): 4.0–4.3× p50, exact parity.
  Live GLM `vllm launch render` was not started; see Details.

## Validation

    pytest -q tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_glm5next.py \
      tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_deepseek_v4_vl.py \
      -k routing_metadata

CI: multimodal processor shard. DeepSeek GPU generate / KV hits were not
measured: NVIDIA sparse-MLA requires compute capability 9/10, and the
available cluster has A100/L40S.

## Details

These processors currently derive image replacements from processed tensors
or layout types. The adapters compute the same geometry from source
dimensions. DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 keep separate preprocess modules because
their existing image math already lives in those files.

The DeepSeek CPU placeholder is registered as multimodal so a CPU render
process can build routing metadata. Instantiating that placeholder for
generation remains unsupported.

GLM-5.3-Flash `vllm launch render` currently fails while constructing
`VllmConfig`: encoder-only/CPU launch disables prefix caching after the
hybrid-Mamba hook sets `mamba_block_size`. That is an existing config-order
issue, not introduced here. GPU `vllm serve` is a separate path.

AI assistance was used. A human submitter reviewed the diff.

title: [ROCm][gfx1151] ROCM_RDNA_SINGLESEQ_ATTN: HIP attention on RDNA
body:
## Summary

New opt-in attention backend `ROCM_RDNA_SINGLESEQ_ATTN`: two HIP kernels for gfx1151 (RDNA3.5) tuned for one sequence per step.

- **When:** `--attention-backend ROCM_RDNA_SINGLESEQ_ATTN` on gfx1151 with `--max-num-seqs 1`. It is never selected automatically, so default backend selection is unchanged; on other devices or with `max_num_seqs > 1` it is rejected at selection.
- **Cache:** `TRITON_ATTN`'s packed HND cache (LBHNC) and metadata; anything the kernels do not serve runs `TRITON_ATTN`'s forward.
- **CUDA graphs:** full graphs for uniform decode batches (`UNIFORM_BATCH`; `cudagraph_mode=FULL` falls back to `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`). Prefill runs outside graphs.

| Kernel | Serves | Supports |
|---|---|---|
| `csrc/rocm/rdna_singleseq_decode_attn.cu` | decode and spec decode, M = 1..8 | WMMA, GQA-packed (each KV byte read once), split-KV with in-kernel merge, CUDA graphs |
| `csrc/rocm/rdna_singleseq_prefill_attn.cu` | prefill and chunked prefill, M ≥ 9, any cached prefix | FlashAttention-2 on WMMA, split-KV when tiles leave the GPU idle |

Both: fp16/bf16, D ∈ {64, 96, 128, 256, 512}, `Hq % Hkv == 0`, causal full or sliding window, pages a multiple of 16 (hybrid pages included), unquantized KV. Not supported (Triton runs them): sinks, alibi, softcap, non-causal, quantized KV, multimodal bidirectional prefix, and a strided query (in-place RoPE on the QKV projection in eager mode). KV connectors and adaptive verification are rejected at selection.

Every build is an entry of a `constexpr` table (`csrc/rocm/rdna_singleseq_{decode,prefill}_configs.h`, 672 + 430 entries over 33 configurations) and each kernel is a template on one entry. `cmake/rocm_rdna_singleseq_attn.cmake` generates one unit per (kernel, head dim, dtype), only when the build targets gfx1151. The `_rocm_C` ops are `rdna_singleseq_{decode,prefill}_{configs,attn}`.

## Build cost

The 1102 builds in 20 units, 32-thread host: **22.6 s wall / 208 s CPU at `-j30`**.

## Accuracy

GSM8K, 500 questions, 5-shot, greedy, seed 42 (strict / flexible). Ours at `max_num_seqs=1`, reference at 16.

| Model | Reference | Ours |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B | ROCM_ATTN 87.80 / 87.60 | 87.80 / 87.40 |
| Gemma-3-12B w4a16 | ROCM_ATTN 87.80 / 88.60 | 87.60 / 88.20 |
| Llama-3.1-8B AWQ | ROCM_ATTN 72.80 / 76.00 | 73.80 / 77.00 |
| Qwen2.5-7B AWQ | ROCM_ATTN 77.80 / 82.00 | 78.00 / 82.00 |
| Gemma-4-E4B AWQ | TRITON_ATTN 73.80 / 73.20 | 73.00 / 72.40 |

## Kernel performance (gfx1151)

Ratio = baseline time / ours (> 1: ours faster), geomean per shape (Hq/Hkv/D, `w` = sliding window). Baselines: `TRITON_ATTN`, `ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN` (no autotune), `ROCM_ATTN`. `%roof`: median of the roofline reached. `–`: the baseline does not support the shape.

### Decode (M = 1..8, S = 128..32k)

3696 cells. Geomean: Triton 7.15x (min 1.01), segmented 1.61x (min 0.97), ROCM_ATTN 22.41x (min 1.08); median roofline 87 %.
