title: [ROCm][Perf][Kimi-K3] Specialized decode on MI355X: K1/K2 + MLA M1a/M1b (FlyDSL, TP8, DCP1/DCP8)
body: ## Disclaimer This is an additional work on #60683. Added MLA prologue (M1a) and epilogue (M1b) around asm MLA attn. Performance gain ## Purpose Kimi-K3 specialized decode on MI355X, structured like #60683 and enabled the same way: `--additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}'`. A Kimi-K3 spec-verify decode step (TP8, DCP1 or DCP8, fp8 KV) runs each MoE decoder layer on persistent FlyDSL kernels instead of vLLM's per-op launches. Everything lives in `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/specialized_decode/`; nothing under `vllm/v1/` or `vllm/config/` changes. Based on `main`; six commits: 1. **Specialized decode for Kimi-K3 on MI355X.** - **K1:** a KDA layer's attention prologue and epilogue. - **K2:** AttnRes, the o_proj all-reduce, the router and the MoE (shared and routed experts). It handles up to 64 rows a launch, with a few-rows route table at ≤ 16 rows. - **M1a / M1b:** an MLA layer's prologue and epilogue around AITER's `mla_decode_fwd`, which is unchanged. - **M1a** does AttnRes, the input norm, `qkv_a` + `g_proj`, the q/kv norms, the fp8 KV-cache write, `q_b`, MXFP4 W_UK and the DCP query all-gather, done in-kernel through peer memory. - **M1b** does the DCP LSE combine, MXFP4 W_UV and the gate. - At DCP1 the peer traffic compiles out: M1a writes `forward_mqa`'s query directly, and M1b reads AITER's `o` as the latent. - **Row cap:** a step serves at most 16 rows (`MAX_ROWS`). The kernels tile up to 64 (`MAX_TOKENS`), but 32 and 64 rows measured slower than vLLM's path. - **MXFP4 bmms:** M1 runs W_UK / W_UV as AITER's MXFP4 bmms, so the specialized decode is refused unless `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=1`, which is off by default since `main`'s 81503550f3. - **Reference:** `runtime/mla.py` runs the same split with vLLM's ops and is the tests' reference. 2. **Faster K2 at every served width.** Per launch, TP8, graph-replayed: | Rows | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | before | 74.6 µs | 99.4 µs | 156.3 µs | ~287 µs | 446.4 µs | | **after** | **73.6 µs** | **96.2 µs** | **138.3 µs** | **273.9 µs** | **408.1 µs** | - **Route:** the router keys go through a threshold select and compaction. A 32-step radix select runs only when more than 64 candidates tie. The logits are polled in one batch, and the shared SiTU's h is issued before the route so its loads land under the logits. - **Latent norm:** each token's row runs on one CTA, so the sum of squares needs no peer hop. - **Above 8 rows:** the o_proj all-reduce and the final reduction are two-shot. Each partial goes to its columns' owner rank, which reduces and broadcasts, so each link carries 2/8 of the one-shot's bytes. Above 16 rows, the up tasks also split by 16-row token tile. - **At ≤ 16 rows:** the latent's last partial producer quantizes the MXFP4 latent and puts it, so the routed experts poll once instead of quantizing. - **sdown:** its remaining tasks are pipelined a task ahead. 3. **M1a writes AITER's padded cprr query.** At DCP8, a k ≥ 2 verify step takes AITER's round-robin (cprr) asm decode, which has kernels only at 16/32/64/128 heads. So in every MLA layer, `forward_mqa` copied the 96 gathered heads into a 128-head q (repeat + slice + contiguous). - M1a's unpack now writes that layout itself: gathered head g < 32 also lands at 96 + g. - `forward_mqa` takes a q that already has the cprr head count as is (moved into the model in commit 6). - M1a's own cost doesn't change (36.1 µs at 8 rows). - The removed copy cost 7.1 / 8.8 / 12.6 / 19.3 µs per MLA layer at 8 / 16 / 32 / 64 rows (about 23 MLA layers). - DCP8 c1 TPOT: 4.01 → 3.94 ms. 4. **M1b runs inside K2's launch, and the DCP8 push is untagged.** - **Fusion:** an MLA layer's K2 now carries its M1b (`K2Build.m1b_qlen`). Every CTA pushes its DCP partials; CTAs 0..55 combine and run W_UV, writing core with a ready flag per (head, 4 tokens); the o_proj CTAs, their weights already in flight, poll a core tile's flags before they load it. The M1b → K2 launch boundary is gone. `runner.fuse_m1b` (on) keeps the separate M1b launch reachable. - **Push:** M1b's DCP8 push was xGMI-bound (15 µs at 8 rows). A wave now pushes a (token, head)'s `o` row untagged, drains, then puts the LSE pair as the row's flag: half the bytes. - M1b + K2 per MLA layer, TP8, graph-replayed: | Rows | 8 | 16 | |---|---|---| | DCP8 before | 120.1 µs | 169.5 µs | | **DCP8 after** | **108.6 µs** | **148.8 µs** | | DCP1 before | 101.6 µs | 143.1 µs | | **DCP1 after** | **98.2 µs** | **140.6 µs** | 5. **Restructure as #60683.** - **Switch:** `--monokernel` is gone. `additional_config={"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}` turns the path on; `auto` (the default) runs vLLM's decode. - **Trigger:** the model's `__init__` calls `specialized_decode_config()`, which raises with every reason from `unsupported()` (#60683's checks plus DCP, KV interleave, fp8 KV and FP4BMM). The loaded weights (`weight_reasons`, including each MLA layer) are checked when the model state builds the executor; the KDA states and MLA caches (`cache_reasons`) at every KV-cache bind. - **Removed:** the shared `vllm/models/common/mono` runtime, `SupportsMonoKernel`, `KernelConfig.monokernel`, `step_health`, the monokernel metrics and every `vllm/v1` / `vllm/config` change they needed. - **Fail-stop:** as in #60683, `compute_logits` queues a non-blocking copy of each rank's FAILED word; every 16 steps the TP ranks agree and all raise at the same step (`guards.FailStop`). - **Layout:** `hooks.py` (`SpecializedDecodeMixin`), `model_state.py` (`KimiK3ModelState`), `runtime/` (config check, executor, guards, layer kernels, runner, peer memory, MLA reference), `mono/` (kernel source). The model files only call in: `linear.py`, `model.py`, `mla.py` (`skip_o_proj`), as in #60683. 6. **Hand M1a's padded query over from the model.** Commit 3's AITER backend change is reverted. - `runtime/mla.py`'s `attend` gives `forward_mqa` the real 96 heads, a view of M1a's 128-head buffer. While that call runs, `AiterMLAHelper.get_mla_padded_q` returns the whole buffer for that view instead of copying; any other query is padded as usual. - Same speed: DCP8 c1 233.06 tok/s, TPOT 3.88 ms (3.87 ms before). With real rejection sampling at DCP8, greedy output matches `auto` for the first ~20 tokens, then diverges (fp8 numerics). ## Supported concurrency × speculative tokens A decode step runs on the kernels when **requests in the step × (k + 1) ≤ 16**, where k is `num_speculative_tokens`. `DecodeConfig.widths` builds one kernel width for every multiple of k + 1 up to 16 (`MAX_ROWS`). A step whose row count isn't one of those widths runs vLLM's layers. | Spec tokens k | Rows per request | Max requests per specialized step | Kernel widths built | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 2 | 8 | 2, 4, …, 16 (8 widths) | | 2 | 3 | 5 | 3, 6, …, 15 (5) | | **3** | **4** | **4** | **4, 8, 12, 16 (4)** | | 4 | 5 | 3 | 5, 10, 15 (3) | | 5 | 6 | 2 | 6, 12 (2) | | **7** | **8** | **2** | **8, 16 (2)** | | 15 | 16 | 1 | 16 | **Deployments refused at startup** (one `ValueError` listing every reason; `decode_backend=auto` runs vLLM's decode): - TP other than 8; pipeline, data, expert or prefill context parallelism; EPLB; DBO. - DCP other than 1 or 8, or a KV interleave other than 1 at DCP8. - No speculative decoding, k + 1 > 16, adaptive verification, dynamic speculative decoding. - A non-fp8 KV cache; KDA cache dtypes other than BF16 conv / FP32 recurrent; ReplaySSM / RecoverSSM. - MLA without the AITER MXFP4 bmms (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=1`). - LoRA, KV connectors, routed-expert capture, sleep mode, CPU weight offload, weight updates. - The V1 model runner, `STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE`, another model's shapes, a GPU other than a full MI355X. - At load: kernel layers whose weights aren't the expected contiguous BF16 shapes (e.g. FP8 dense linears), a MoE backend other than `AITER_MXFP4_BF16` (K3 SiTU), or MLA layers the M1 kernels can't serve. **Steps that run vLLM's layers even with valid settings:** - More requests than the table's limit for k. - A step with any prefill in it, or requests of different lengths. - A Gluon MLA decode step. - Piecewise cudagraph steps. ## Test Plan Hardware: 8× MI355X (pit2-p03-g09), image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294` (AITER 0.1.25, `main`'s pin) with this PR's Python mounted. - `pytest -v -s tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode` (the new CI step `:amd: (MI355) Kimi-K3 Specialized Decode`, as in #60683): - `test_runtime.py` (CPU): the switch, widths up to 16 rows, every refusal including DCP / interleave / fp8 / FP4BMM, weight and cache refusals (KDA and MLA), `step_reason` (KDA and MLA metadata), `plan()` routing. - `test_numerics.py`: K1 and K2 against vLLM ops, TP8, at 4–64 rows plus graph replays; M1a / M1b single-GPU (DCP1); TP8 + DCP8 M1 (cprr-padded q, combine, fused M1b → K2 bit-identical to unfused, replayed graphs); warm-up compile; the stalled-rank kernel fault. - `test_engine_fault.py`: a served dummy model with a stalled rank; every TP rank raises at the same step through `FailStop` and the server exits. - End-to-end serving, below. ## Test Result **Unit tests, this PR's head:** 135 passed in 12 min. ### InferenceX Kimi-K3 recipe, k = 7, concurrency 1 Recipe `kimik3-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-mtp`, arm `override_tp8_c1`: TP8, fp8 KV, DSpark with 7 speculative tokens, `--max-num-seqs 2`, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs (capture sizes 8, 16), `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=1`. - **Workload:** random 8k in / 1k out, `--ignore-eos`, 5 prompts, synthetic acceptance (acceptance length 3.84–3.85 in every run). - **Setup:** this PR's head, same tree and image for every arm; the four arms ran one after another on pit2-p03-g09, each in a fresh container. Base and specialized differ only in `decode_backend` (`auto` vs `latency_specialized`). The server log confirms 92 kernel layers at widths 8 and 16. - **Change from the recipe, in every arm:** `--quantization-config` (FP8 online quantization of the dense linears) is removed, because the kernels need BF16 dense weights. The base is therefore no-quant too. | Metric | DCP1 base | **DCP1 specialized** | Change | DCP8 base | **DCP8 specialized** | Change | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | Output tok/s | 179.77 | **232.87** | **+29.5%** | 164.79 | **233.11** | **+41.5%** | | Total tok/s | 1617.89 | 2095.86 | +29.5% | 1483.08 | 2097.96 | +41.5% | | Mean / median TTFT ms | 431.20 / 489.49 | 430.72 / 488.83 | −0.1% | 432.30 / 489.85 | 431.29 / 486.20 | −0.2% | | Mean / median TPOT ms | 5.15 / 5.18 | **3.88 / 3.87** | **−24.7%** | 5.65 / 5.62 | **3.87 / 3.87** | **−31.5%** | | Mean ITL ms | 59.16 | 44.56 | −24.7% | 64.96 | 44.51 | −31.5% | These match the pre-restructure head (9c993258a8: DCP1 232.6, DCP8 234.0 tok/s), so the restructure costs nothing. ### Performance, #60683's matrix Same matrix as #60683's "Performance" table: `vllm bench serve`, random, 1024 output tokens, `--ignore-eos`, 2 seeds (4 × conc prompts each, 4 at c1), DCP8, `--stream-interval 10`, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs (capture sizes: every multiple of k + 1 up to 16), `--max-num-seqs` = conc. Head 149f85abc3 (Kimi code byte-identical) on pit2-p03-g23, each arm in a fresh container; "off" is the same image, tree and flags with `decode_backend=auto`. title: [Bug][Spec Decode] DFlash2 (SWA) draft group is never annotated `is_eagle_group` under the generic packed KV layout (GLM-5.3-Flash shape)
body:
### Summary

On current `main` (post #57169 / #61183), a GLM-5.3-Flash-shaped hybrid with the
`dflash` drafter groups successfully, but the drafter's KV cache group is never
flagged `is_eagle_group`. The engine logs:

```
Speculative decoding (method=dflash) is enabled but no KV cache group could be identified as the draft model's.
```

so the block-drop optimization is silently disabled and consumers fall back to
the conservative path (per #60560, actually *enabling* the SWA draft group costs
~5.5 points of DFlash2 acceptance on BLHNC + NIXL P/D — so the annotation path
here matters in both directions).

### Repro (CPU-only, no weights)

The spec set from #59656's description, adapted to the new interface (11
`MLAAttentionSpec` bs=1280 + 11 indexer MLA `tokens_per_state=8` + 11
`CircularBufferSpec` tail ring=16 + 34 `MambaSpec` KDA + 5 `SlidingWindowSpec`
draft bs=16 + 1 `HiddenStateCacheSpec`), run through
`vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_planning.get_kv_cache_groups` with
`speculative_config.method="dflash"`, `use_eagle()=True`, `use_eagle_block_drop()=True`:

- on `BLHNC`, `_get_packed_kv_cache_groups` emits a dedicated uniform-SWA draft
  group, but neither detection rule in `_annotate_eagle_groups` fires:
  1. spec-driven — plain GQA `SlidingWindowSpec` carries no
     `non_causal_multi_token_decode` marker (that marker is MLA-only today);
  2. positional fallback — gated by `_uses_trailing_mtp_layers`, which returns
     `False` for `method="dflash"` (it only enables for `method == "mtp"` and the
     `deepseek_v4*` model types).
  Result: 0 groups flagged, warning emitted.
- an EAGLE-family drafter whose layers are plain `SlidingWindowSpec` (dflash /
  eagle3-aux recipes for hybrid MLA targets) hits the identical hole.

### Expected

`is_eagle_group` is set on the draft group when `use_eagle_block_drop()` is on
and a uniform sliding-window group can be identified as the drafter's — e.g.
extend rule 2 (trailing layers) to `dflash`/`eagle3` whose draft registers after
the target layers, or add a spec marker on drafter SWA layers analogous to
`non_causal_multi_token_decode`.

### Context

Found while re-verifying #59656 after #57169 removed the GLM-specific KV builder
(that PR is now closed as superseded — the crash it fixed no longer reproduces).
Related: #60560 (SWA draft group + acceptance regression), #58638 (RFC: KV cache
grouping for hybrid models with speculative drafters).

<details>
<summary>CPU-only repro script (runs against a checkout of main; no GPU, no weights)</summary>

```python
# RED/GREEN probe for upstream main (post #57169/#61183): does the GLM-5.3-Flash
# shape with a DFlash2 sliding-window drafter (+ aux hidden-state) still break
# get_kv_cache_groups? CPU-only: pure dataclass + planning code, torch imported
# but never touches a device. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" in the runner.
import sys
import traceback
from types import SimpleNamespace

# strip the prod venv's editable-install finder so `import vllm` can only
# resolve to the scratch checkout put first on PYTHONPATH
sys.meta_path = [
    f for f in sys.meta_path
    if "vllm" not in getattr(type(f), "__module__", "")
    and "editable" not in getattr(type(f), "__name__", "").lower()
]

import torch

from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_planning import get_kv_cache_groups
from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (
    CircularBufferSpec,
    HiddenStateCacheSpec,
    MambaSpec,
    MLAAttentionSpec,
    SlidingWindowSpec,
)
from vllm.v1.kv_cache_layout import KVCacheLayout

BF16 = torch.bfloat16
BS = 1280  # unified block (mamba-aligned), TP4


def make_specs(with_draft: bool, with_hidden: bool):
    specs = {}
    for i in range(11):  # dense MLA + DSA indexer + kpool tail
        specs[f"layers.{4*i+3}.attn"] = MLAAttentionSpec(
            block_size=BS, num_kv_heads=1, head_size=576, head_size_v=0,
            dtype=BF16)
        specs[f"layers.{4*i+3}.indexer"] = MLAAttentionSpec(
            block_size=BS, num_kv_heads=1, head_size=128, head_size_v=0,
            dtype=torch.uint8, tokens_per_state=8)
        # Glm5NextTailCache: ring = kpool * next_pow2((kpool+num_spec)/kpool)
        # kpool=8, num_spec=8 -> ring=16
        specs[f"layers.{4*i+3}.tail"] = CircularBufferSpec(
            block_size=16, num_kv_heads=2, head_size=128, head_size_v=0,
            dtype=BF16, dcp_sharded=False)
    for i in range(34):  # KDA/mamba layers
        specs[f"layers.{i}.kda"] = MambaSpec(
            block_size=BS, shapes=((8, 128, 128), (8, 128, 256)),
            dtypes=(BF16, BF16), mamba_cache_mode="align")
    if with_draft:  # DFlash2: 5 GQA sliding-window layers, draft worker bs=16
        for i in range(5):
            specs[f"draft.layers.{i}.self_attn.attn"] = SlidingWindowSpec(
                block_size=16, num_kv_heads=2, head_size=128, head_size_v=128,
                dtype=BF16, sliding_window=2048, dcp_sharded=False)
    if with_hidden:  # aux EAGLE3 hidden states: 5 streams x hidden 4096
        specs["layers.45.hidden"] = HiddenStateCacheSpec(
            block_size=BS, num_kv_heads=5, head_size=4096, dtype=BF16)
    return specs


def make_cfg(layout_name: str):
    layout = KVCacheLayout[layout_name]
    return SimpleNamespace(
        scheduler_config=SimpleNamespace(disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager=False),
        cache_config=SimpleNamespace(
            get_resolved_kv_cache_layout=lambda: layout, block_size=BS,
            num_gpu_blocks_override=None, prefix_cache_retention_interval=1280, mamba_cache_mode="align"),
        attention_config=None,
        model_config=SimpleNamespace(
            hf_config=SimpleNamespace(model_type="glm5_next"),
            max_model_len=262144),
        parallel_config=SimpleNamespace(
            pipeline_parallel_size=1, decode_context_parallel_size=1,
            enable_expert_parallel=True, tensor_parallel_size=4),
        speculative_config=SimpleNamespace(
            method="dflash", use_eagle=lambda: True,
            use_eagle_block_drop=lambda: True, num_speculative_tokens=8),
        num_speculative_tokens=8,
        device_config=SimpleNamespace(device_type="cpu"),
        max_in_flight_tokens=64,
        scheduler_block_size=BS,
    )


def describe(groups):
    out = []
    for g in groups:
        s = g.kv_cache_spec
        out.append(
            f"    group: n={len(g.layer_names)} eagle={getattr(g,'is_eagle_group',None)}"
            f" spec={type(s).__name__} bs={getattr(s,'block_size','?')}"
            f" page={getattr(s,'page_size_bytes','?')}"
            f" layers={sorted(g.layer_names)[:3]}...")
    return "\n".join(out)


def main():
    import vllm
    print("vllm tree:", vllm.__file__)
    print("torch:", torch.__version__, "cuda available:", torch.cuda.is_available())
    failures = 0
    for layout_name in ("LBHNC", "BLHNC"):
        for with_draft, with_hidden in ((False, False), (True, False),
                                        (True, True), (False, True)):
            tag = (f"layout={layout_name} draft={int(with_draft)}"
                   f" hidden={int(with_hidden)}")
            try:
                groups = get_kv_cache_groups(
                    make_cfg(layout_name), make_specs(with_draft, with_hidden))
                print(f"[GREEN] {tag}: {len(groups)} groups")
                print(describe(groups))
            except Exception as exc:
                failures += 1
                print(f"[RED]   {tag}: {type(exc).__name__}: {str(exc)[:220]}")
    print(f"=== done: {failures} failing combinations ===")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

</details>

title: [Bugfix] Reject mismatched float16/bfloat16 kv_cache_dtype with model dtype
body:
## Issue

Fixes #61314 (and #60859 on the same code path).

A `bfloat16` checkpoint with an explicit `kv_cache_dtype="float16"` (or the
reverse pair) crashes during CUDA-graph capture on the FlashAttention and
FlashInfer backends because those kernels require query and key tensors to
share a dtype. Quantized linear layers (`quantization="fp8"`) do not change
the attention query dtype, so the crash happens identically on the online
fp8 quantization path reported in #61314.

## What this PR does

Add a config-level check in `VllmConfig.__post_init__` that rejects any
unquantized `float16`/`bfloat16` `kv_cache_dtype` that does not match the
checkpoint dtype, before the attention backend is selected or CUDA-graph
capture runs. The error is a descriptive `ValueError` with a hint to use
`auto` or the matching dtype.

Quantized KV cache dtypes (`fp8`, `fp8_e4m3`, `nvfp4`, `*_per_token_head`, …)
are intentionally left alone — they have their own per-backend support checks
and a different failure mode. `auto` is also skipped because it resolves to
the model dtype.

## Root cause

FlashAttention `mha_varlen_fwd` asserts `query and key must have the same dtype`.
The engine accepted the mismatched pair until backend selection or graph
capture, which is late for a user-facing configuration error. This check runs
right after `try_verify_and_update_config()`, so model hooks (e.g. DeepSeek
V3.2 rewriting an explicit `bfloat16` cache to `auto`) still run first.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py::test_post_init_rejects_mismatched_float_kv_cache -q
```

Tested cases:
- Rejects `float16` KV with `bfloat16`, `float16` with `float32` model dtypes
- Accepts matching dtypes (`float16`+`float16`, `bfloat16`+`bfloat16`)
- Accepts `auto` and quantized KV dtypes (`fp8`) regardless of model dtype

End-to-end `LLM.generate` was not run (this sandbox has no CUDA GPU).

## Not a duplicate of existing open PRs

#60885 and #60951 both address #60859 on the same plain-dtype path. This PR
reuses the same fix shape (`_reject_mismatched_float_kv_cache` in
`VllmConfig.__post_init__`) and additionally frames it as also covering the
online fp8 quantization crash reported in #61314 — the same underlying issue
because quantized linear layers do not affect attention query dtype. If one
of the existing PRs lands first, the overlapping hunks will merge cleanly.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used during diagnosis, implementation, and PR drafting.
The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the test cases above.

title: [Core][KV Cache] Move KV cache allocation policy onto manager configs (RFC #42449 part 2)
body:
## Overview Part 2 of #42449: `KVCacheSpec` now describes only a layer's **tensor layout**. **Allocation policy** (windows, recycling, prefix caching, Mamba modes) moves onto the KV cache manager that enforces it. Layers declare `(manager_cls, manager_config, spec)`, and a group is simply *layers that share a block table*. **Draft:** CPU unit tests only so far; GPU and E2E validation pending. ## The payoff: no more `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Spec classes | 15 (8 encode only policy) | 5 layout classes: `AttentionSpec`, `MLAAttentionSpec`, `HiddenStateCacheSpec`, `MambaSpec`, `HiSparsePageSpec` | | Policy | spec fields + subclasses | `Manager.Config`, e.g. `SlidingWindowManager.Config(sliding_window, ...)` | | Spec → manager | global `KVCacheSpecRegistry` + platform hook | the layer names its manager: `SlidingWindowManager.layer_config(spec, sliding_window=w)` | | Mixed-layout groups | `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` wrapper | `group.kv_cache_specs[layer]` | | Sizing | per-spec methods + wrapper aggregation | `manager.max_blocks_per_request(config, ...) × group.page_size_bytes` | | `kv_cache_interface.py` | | +177 / −889 lines | Overall, production code changes 113 files, +2388 / −3157 lines. No compat shims: out-of-tree specs and platform-registered managers need updating. ## Validation - CPU unit tests (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=`), run on this branch and on its base `df6c7ad031`: ``` pytest tests/v1/core tests/v1/kv_connector/unit tests/v1/worker -q --timeout=120 \ --ignore=tests/v1/core/test_scheduler_e2e.py --ignore=tests/v1/core/test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e.py ``` Branch: 3540 passed / 313 failed / 125 errors (base: 3543 / 313 / 126). Every failing test ID also fails on the base (GPU, NCCL or world-size requirements), apart from renamed tests whose old names fail the same way. Tests in `tests/v1/{engine,spec_decode,attention,simple_kv_offload,kv_offload}` and the model and kernel tests touched here pass or fail for device reasons only. `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy) passes. - **Pending:** GPU unit tests, and E2E serving/eval on hybrid SWA, Mamba hybrid, DSv4/GLM packed, HiSparse and P/D connectors. ## Details - **Grouping:** one rule replaces the planner's "identical spec" and "uniform type" paths. `MambaManager` additionally requires equal page sizes. Page-size unification, padding and group splitting are unchanged. - **Behavior changes:** - Same-policy layers with different layouts can now share a group. - Builders that need policy declare `requires_kv_cache_manager_config` (Mamba, GDN, linear attention, KDA, QSA, Dots3). - Encoder-only attention is a manager policy, which lifts its one-spec limit. - **Hazard reviewed:** collapsing policy subclasses into `AttentionSpec`/`MLAAttentionSpec` broadens any `isinstance` check that really meant a policy. All such checks were audited, and the ones that meant policy now test the manager: - the coordinator's cache-hit batching key now includes `dcp_sharded` - the Mooncake store's TP-sharded layout gate - the HiSparse MLA filter - **Out of scope:** planning still runs in the engine core. Backend-declared configs and worker-driven allocation are later parts of #42449. - **Not a duplicate:** open PRs were searched for #42449, `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs`, `KVCacheSpecRegistry`, `manager_config` and `KVCacheTensorSpec`. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

title: [Quantization] Enable per-layer fused shared expert selection
body:
## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

Allow compatible layers to use AITER fused shared experts (FSE) while other layers retain higher-precision shared experts.

Current vLLM rejects the entire model in case FSE can't be enabled for all layers, and various places assume all-or-nothing selection.

**Motivation: certain layers are less sensitive to MXFP4 shared expert quantization than others, and fusion can be enabled for them.**

## Claims

- Enable per-layer FSE through the existing `resolve_layer_fused_shared_expert` API for models migrated to layer-scoped checkpoint loading.
- Redirect checkpoint weights only for layers that allocated fused shared-expert slots; preserve separate MXFP8 shared experts alongside MXFP4 routed experts.
- Explicitly reject mixed FSE with EPLB, whose expert-weight handling assumes uniform row counts across layers.

Left to other PRs:

- [ ] Migrate MiniMax M3 to `resolve_layer_fused_shared_expert` and layer-scoped checkpoint loading: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/12b005eefa06f97eeebfae3e14bcac5fa3b81197/vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/model.py#L393-L414 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/12b005eefa06f97eeebfae3e14bcac5fa3b81197/vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/model.py#L1560-L1561
- [ ] Migrate DeepSeek V4 to `resolve_layer_fused_shared_expert` and finish layer-scoped checkpoint mapping: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/12b005eefa06f97eeebfae3e14bcac5fa3b81197/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py#L643-L662 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/12b005eefa06f97eeebfae3e14bcac5fa3b81197/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py#L1392-L1396
- [ ] Move FHMOE's separate model-wide eligibility policy to this per-layer API: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/12b005eefa06f97eeebfae3e14bcac5fa3b81197/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py#L212-L240 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/12b005eefa06f97eeebfae3e14bcac5fa3b81197/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py#L1077-L1092
- [ ] Update remaining model-specific loaders to redirect shared weights and build expert mappings per layer:
  - DeepSeek V2: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/12b005eefa06f97eeebfae3e14bcac5fa3b81197/vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py#L1627-L1664

  - GLM5Next: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/12b005eefa06f97eeebfae3e14bcac5fa3b81197/vllm/models/glm5next/common/model.py#L892-L902 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/12b005eefa06f97eeebfae3e14bcac5fa3b81197/vllm/models/glm5next/common/model.py#L929-L930
  - AXK1: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/12b005eefa06f97eeebfae3e14bcac5fa3b81197/vllm/model_executor/models/AXK1.py#L825-L852
  - GLM4 Lite: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/12b005eefa06f97eeebfae3e14bcac5fa3b81197/vllm/model_executor/models/glm4_moe_lite.py#L361-L387
  - Applicable MTP loaders: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/12b005eefa06f97eeebfae3e14bcac5fa3b81197/vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_mtp.py#L327-L353, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/12b005eefa06f97eeebfae3e14bcac5fa3b81197/vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd/mtp.py#L277-L303, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/12b005eefa06f97eeebfae3e14bcac5fa3b81197/vllm/models/glm5next/common/mtp.py#L309-L320, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/12b005eefa06f97eeebfae3e14bcac5fa3b81197/vllm/models/glm5next/common/mtp.py#L342-L343, and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/12b005eefa06f97eeebfae3e14bcac5fa3b81197/vllm/model_executor/models/glm4_moe_lite_mtp.py#L290-L305

Limitations:

- Mixed FSE with EPLB is unsupported.
- Routed and shared experts must have compatible quantization within each fused layer; heterogeneous precision inside one fused GEMM is unsupported.
- Fused layers must share routing-buffer geometry; Mori remains unsupported with FSE requested.
- Forward execution, graph replay, model evaluations, and performance are not validated; Qwen4 Exp lacks full FSE initialization/loading coverage.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py -k test_models_fse_init -s -vvvvv`
- `python -m pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py -s -vvvvv`

## Compatibility changes

- Compared with `main`, migrated models accept mixed fusion eligibility with EPLB off, retaining incompatible shared experts separately at their configured precision.
- Internal breaking changes: `maybe_fuse_shared_experts()` requires a `fused_shared_expert_layers` collection instead of the optional `enabled` boolean/environment fallback; migrated model-wide FSE booleans become layer lists; `FusedMoEConfig.aiter_fmoe_shared_expert_enabled` becomes `is_fused_shared_expert_requested`.

## Related work

- This addresses per-layer policy, not the ModelOpt MXFP8 compatibility support in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57916; the duplicate-work search found no open PR implementing this same policy migration.

title: [Perf][Kernel] Tune fused mHC post + pre-norm for SM90 at up to 8 tokens
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The fused mHC post + pre-norm kernel runs twice per decoder layer in DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 and GLM-5.3-Flash. Its split configs were tuned on GB300 (#56633). This PR gives SM90 its own config for 1–8 tokens: `(tile_n, n_splits, n_thr) = (12, hidden / 512, 256)`. Other architectures and token counts are unchanged.

## Claims

- On H20 at 1–8 tokens, the op gets faster:
  - DeepSeek-V4-Flash and GLM-5.3-Flash (hidden 4096): 4.4–16.3%.
  - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (hidden 5120): 9.1–14.1%.
  - DeepSeek-V4-Pro (hidden 7168): 2.1–22.8%.
- The band includes DSpark k=5 decode at C1, which runs 6 tokens per step.
- Residual streams are bit-identical. The mixing coefficients, and through them the layer inputs, differ only in FP32 summation order.
- Startup warmup compiles the new variant. Off SM90, the set of compiled kernels is unchanged.

## Validation

**Microbenchmark.** H20, `hc_mult = 4`, FlashInfer CUPTI with a CUDA graph and a cold L2, median of 3 runs of 200 replays. Outputs are checked before timing.
- The 4096 and 7168 columns time `mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang`, which DeepSeek-V4 and GLM-5.3-Flash call.
- The 5120 column times `mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_tilelang`, which DeepSeek-V4.1 calls.

All columns come from one run of this PR's `tilelang_kernels.py`. Each cell is main → this PR, in µs.

| Tokens | 4096 | 5120 | 7168 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 10.94 → 10.05 (−8.2%) | 11.58 → 9.98 (−13.8%) | 13.92 → 10.75 (−22.8%) |
| 2 | 10.85 → 9.84 (−9.3%) | 11.55 → 10.08 (−12.8%) | 13.54 → 10.62 (−21.5%) |
| 3 | 11.04 → 10.14 (−8.1%) | 11.73 → 10.08 (−14.1%) | 13.70 → 11.30 (−17.5%) |
| 4 | 10.82 → 9.86 (−8.9%) | 11.62 → 10.14 (−12.7%) | 13.50 → 11.20 (−17.1%) |
| 5 | 10.85 → 9.82 (−9.4%) | 11.60 → 10.46 (−9.8%) | 13.63 → 11.30 (−17.1%) |
| 6 | 10.85 → 10.24 (−5.6%) | 11.65 → 10.59 (−9.1%) | 13.66 → 13.38 (−2.1%) |
| 7 | 11.01 → 10.53 (−4.4%) | 11.71 → 10.59 (−9.6%) | 13.86 → 13.54 (−2.3%) |
| 8 | 12.48 → 10.45 (−16.3%) | 13.54 → 11.68 (−13.7%) | 16.42 → 14.21 (−13.5%) |

- The minimum tensor traffic is 1.7–3.9 MB per op, corresponding to an effective bandwidth of 152–308 GB/s.
- From 9 to 32 tokens, main and this PR pick the same config, and their times agree within ±1.1%.
- At 5120, the new config had the lowest total time over 1, 2, 4, 6 and 8 tokens in a sweep of 63 configs. It was within 4.6% of the best config at each of those token counts.

**Tests.** `pytest tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_jit_warmup.py tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py` passes on H20, with one exception: `test_mhc_fused_post_pre[4-7168-128]`. That case runs 128 tokens, outside the band, and fails the same way without this change.

A 1-hour TP8 serving run built no TileLang kernels after warmup. CI runs `kernels/mhc` on B200 only, so this H20 run is the only coverage for the SM90 cases.

**E2E sanity check.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8×H20 with TP8, 1K in / 1K out. It ran on main 240ee8d (2026-10-07) with this change applied; `kernels/mhc/` has not changed since.
- DSpark k=5 at a synthetic acceptance length of 3.51.
- One run per server, in the order main, PR, PR, main.

At C1, both PR runs beat both main runs: output throughput +0.9%, TPOT p50 −1.0%. At C64, which is outside the band, both PR runs fall between main's two runs in throughput and TPOT p50.

**Accuracy.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on the same build, GSM8K, 5-shot, with real DSpark verification:
- Correct answers: 1274 / 1319 on main, 1276 / 1319 with this PR.
- Acceptance length: 3.863 and 3.868.

GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4 were checked at the op level only.

## Details

- **Why it is faster.** Every (token, tile, k-slice) block recomputes the post mapping.
  - main's `(2, 8, 128)` runs 12 tiles, and each thread makes 4–7 serial memory round trips.
  - The new config runs 2 tiles with 2 round trips each.
- **Band.** A separate candidate config, `(12, 8, 128)`, improved latency at 9–18 tokens on H20. Those gains may depend on H20's 78-SM grid scheduling and have not been validated on H100/H200, so this PR leaves that band unchanged.
- **H100/H200.** These GPUs are not measured. Both grids should fit in one wave on 132 SMs, so the gain is expected to carry over. The 6–7-token dip at 7168 looks like a wave spill on H20 and is not expected there.
- **Scope.** SM100, SM120 and ROCm are untouched. No open PR changes this config.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Sync cluster before DSMEM stores in ll_bf16 split-K router GEMM
body:
## Purpose

The cuteDSL `ll_bf16` split-K router GEMM (#42562, used for M >= 8) writes each CTA's partials into every peer CTA's shared memory (`st.shared::cluster`) before any cluster barrier. CUDA requires a cluster sync before the first DSMEM access, since a peer CTA may not have started yet. When it hasn't, the GPU raises Xid 13 `Graphics SM Cga Exception: CTA Not Present`, which surfaces as `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure`.

Fix: a relaxed cluster arrive/wait at kernel start, the same pattern `gemm_rs_ar.py` already uses. No other cuteDSL kernel under `kernels/linear/cute_dsl/` uses DSMEM.

cc @LopezCastroRoberto

## Reproduction

Only seen with HiSparse P/D over NIXL, the default HiSparse P/D path on `main`, where the decode server's host-pool KV imports keep many copy streams busy alongside the router GEMM. It is a timing race, so the fault can't be forced from software.

**Decode on `main` (`cbe1f9740d`; `_ll_bf16_splitk.py` identical to current `main`):** GLM-5.3 (`RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`) P/D across 2 coreweave H200 nodes, no instrumentation. Setup:
- Decode TP4, PIECEWISE cudagraphs, `MultiConnector[HiSparseConnector (host_pool_gib=300), NixlConnector kv_consumer]`.
- Workload: evalscope `swe_smith` multi-turn, `--parallel 8 --number 16 --max-tokens 220`.

Caveats: the decode tree also carried the 11-line `hisparse/connector.py` patch from #60117 (P/D connector only, unmerged), and prefill ran the #55398 tree. Result: crash about 6 minutes into pass 1.
```
(Worker_TP2) torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure
dmesg: Xid (PCI:0000:cb:00): 13, Graphics SM Cga Exception on (GPC 7, TPC 6, SM 0): CTA Not Present ... name=VLLM::Worker
```
The same signature appeared in two more decode-on-`main` runs: FP8 GLM-5.3 TP8 P/D, one with PIECEWISE and one with `sparse_indexer_topk_backend=persistent`. The persistent run rules out `cooperative_topk`, the other cluster kernel on that path.

**#55398 stack, same P/D setup, decode TP4 with `--num-gpu-blocks-override 14000`:**

| Decode router GEMM | Result |
|---|---|
| unpatched | crashed 4/4 runs within 2 passes; `dmesg`: Xid 13 CTA Not Present |
| `ll_bf16` disabled | 6/6 passes clean (48,439 host imports) |
| this PR | 6/6 passes clean (1,248/1,248 requests, 48,411 host imports) |

**Not reproduced:**
- **Single-server HiSparse on pristine `main` (`67516b6`, 4xH200 TP4):** same flags without NIXL; 10 passes plus 6 passes with 2000 output tokens, 256/256 requests clean. Host-to-device traffic was heavy (54M hot-buffer misses in one sample window).
- **Standalone stress on H100:** ~45M split-K launches PDL-chained in CUDA graphs, against 8–32 background streams of HiSparse-like zero-copy and spin kernels.
- **compute-sanitizer:** memcheck is clean with and without the fix. synccheck reports the same pre-existing warnings in both. racecheck hangs on this kernel.

So the trigger needs the SM contention from the P/D host-import path. A pristine-`main` P/D run will replace the `cbe1f9740d`+#60117 evidence once an 8xH200 node is free.

## Test results

H100 (rdu4), this branch:

```bash
pytest -q tests/kernels/test_ll_bf16_gemm.py
```
136 passed.

On H200, the fixed kernel matches `torch.mm` on 25 shapes (K ∈ {4096, 5120, 6144, 7168}, N ∈ {64, 128, 160, 256}, M ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8, 16}; split-K path used for M >= 8): all cos = 1.000000, max_abs <= 3.3e-6.

Kernel latency on H100: median of 30 CUDA-graph replays of 200 back-to-back PDL launches, µs per call.

| K, N | M | main | PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6144, 256 | 8 / 12 / 16 | 2.71 / 2.75 / 2.81 | 2.81 / 2.85 / 2.90 |
| 7168, 256 | 8 / 12 / 16 | 2.84 / 2.89 / 2.91 | 2.93 / 2.96 / 3.01 |
| 4096, 256 | 8 / 12 / 16 | 2.39 / 2.57 / 3.24 | 2.49 / 2.68 / 3.30 |

The barrier costs ~0.1 µs per call. Moving the wait to just before the DSMEM stores recovered only ~0.04 µs. That version also leaves the DMA warps exiting without a wait, so I kept the simpler form that was validated in the serving workload.

No regression test is included: the fault requires the hardware to delay one CTA of the cluster, which can't be forced from a test.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4] Mono decode layer for DeepSeek-V4-Pro on MI355X, on shared mono kernels
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR moves the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash mono decode kernels of #60397 into a shared package, `vllm/models/common/amd/mono/`, and plugs DeepSeek-V4-Pro into the same kernels at TP8 on MI355X (gfx950). Pro adds no kernel code of its own. It uses a `MonoSpec` (widths, numerics, variant flags) and a `MonoDecode` subclass of about 300 lines. Opt-in with `--monokernel`, as for V4.1.

Related: RFC #60904. #61311 drafts the RFC's runtime layer (`vllm/models/common/mono/`: routing, fail-stop, guards) and leaves the kernel code to each model. This PR covers the other half: one set of FlyDSL kernel stages shared by two models. The two can coexist; see Details.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP8, MI355X, InferenceX AgentX (`inferencex-agentx-mvp`, DSpark with 6 drafts, synthetic acceptance 3.77), mono on vs off:

  | | c1 off → on | c4 off → on | c8 off → on |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Interactivity P50 (tok/s/user) | 241 → **299** (+24%) | 218 → **247** (+13%) | 192 → **201** (+5%) |
  | Interactivity P90, InferenceX's slow tail (tok/s/user) | 227 → **278** (+22%) | 169 → **176** (+5%) | 119 → **147** (+23%) |
  | Inter-token latency P50 (ms) | 4.16 → **3.34** (−20%) | 4.59 → **4.04** (−12%) | 5.20 → **4.96** (−5%) |
  | Output throughput (tok/s) | 87.8 → 93.8 | 144 → 194 | 292 → 302 |

  One 900 s run per point. AgentX replays agent sessions closed-loop, so a faster server completes a different mix of turns. Mean inter-token latency and total throughput therefore move with the prompt-length mix and with prefill stalls, not only with decode speed. For example, the c4 mono-on run happened to serve shorter contexts (mean input 136K vs 181K tokens). P90 at c4 / c8 mostly reflects stalls behind other users' long prefills, which run vLLM's own path. The P50 rows are the decode-speed comparison.

- GSM8K at TP8 matches mono off (see Validation).
- V4.1 builds the same kernels as on `main`: 48 of 48 variants are byte-identical, apart from one race fix in the combine stage of index-source layers. That fix was timed and shows no regression.
- One more model of this family needs a spec and a docking class, not a kernel fork. The package README has an "Adding a model" section.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/models/test_dsv4_mono_numerics.py` (TP8, MI355X) | 2 passed. Each stage checked against vLLM's own ops and an exact fp32 reference; CSA layers, and HCA layers at the 64K deployment's key-table width (512) and a long context's (2048); hash routing in the FFN launch; widths 7–56; one- and two-hop all-reduce; 200 graph replays. |
| `pytest tests/models/test_dsv4_mono_layers.py` (TP8, MI355X) | passed 5 of 5 runs. A five-layer Pro (hash HCA first layer, hash HCA, hash CSA, bias HCA, bias CSA) on random weights with `--monokernel` on vs off, every layer's outputs at every decode step. A 3% routed-scale error in the kernels fails it. |
| `pytest tests/models/test_dsv4_mono_decode.py` (CPU) | 25 passed: the docking's path choice and the startup refusals |
| `pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` (TP2 / TP4) | pass |
| GSM8K, InferenceX `gsm8k.yaml`, chat, greedy, 1319 questions, TP8, real DSpark | mono off 0.9757 / 0.9765. Mono on 0.9750 / 0.9757 (before the HCA fix) and 0.9735 / 0.9742 (final). Flexible / strict; stderr 0.0044. |
| AgentX sweep (Claims) | one run per point, 900 s, fresh server per point |
| V4.1 ISA, 48 variants, `FLYDSL_DUMP_IR` + `COMPILE_ONLY` vs `main` | identical except the 6 index-source K2 variants (race fix) |
| V4.1 index-source K2 timing, race fix vs without, µs per layer (TP2 / TP4, 6–48 rows) | within ±1% run-to-run noise (A/B/A) |

<details>
<summary>Per-layer kernel bench (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP8, µs per layer, 8 layers back to back in one graph, cold weights)</summary>

| rows | CSA vLLM | CSA mono | HCA vLLM | HCA mono |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7 | 195.7 | 125.3 | 197.8 | 123.6 |
| 14 | 216.6 | 170.4 | 215.6 | 169.1 |
| 28 | 261.5 | 242.4 | 259.1 | 239.3 |
| 56 | 345.3 | 356.5 (two-hop) | 338.1 | 344.3 (two-hop) |

The compressor and indexer run vLLM's own ops on both paths, so the bench excludes them.

</details>

CI: the existing MI355 V4.1 jobs now also depend on `vllm/models/common/amd/`. The Pro docking test runs in the MI355 Basic Models step, and a new `mi355_8` job runs the Pro numerics and layer tests. Neither runs in upstream CI without MI355 runners. Everything above ran on 8× MI355X.

## Details

- **Package layout.** `spec.py` holds `MonoSpec` and `Dims`, a rank's share of every width. `stages/` holds the mHC seam, MoE, router and all-reduce. `attention/` holds the sparse-MLA front and back. `layer.py` and `runner.py` hold the launches and host side. `decode.py` is the vLLM-side base class: deployment checks, step eligibility, record views. A variant is a spec flag read with `const_expr`, so each model's kernels are compiled only from its own flags:
  - `delayed_seam` (V4.1)
  - `q_head_norm`, `preshuffled`, `padded_rows` (Pro)
  - `two_hop_rows`
- **What Pro needs beyond V4.1:**
  - the non-delayed mHC seam (aiter's `mhc_pre` collapse)
  - a weightless per-head q RMSNorm
  - aiter's (16, 16)-preshuffled FP8 weights and `VLLM_ROCM_FP8_PADDING` row strides
  - hash routing for layers 0–2
  - HCA layers, which read every compressed row from vLLM's c128a table
  - 128×128 block scales, expanded exactly to the kernels' 32×32 E8M0 scales
- **HCA key table.** At a 1M context the table is 8192 rows wide. The key table, the split units and the combine stage cover only each token's own keys (`bounded`). Without this, an HCA layer took ~240 µs and mono was 10% slower end to end than mono off.
- **Two-hop all-reduce.** In `stages/allreduce.py`, each rank sends a column to its owner rank. The owner sums the ranks in order and sends the bf16 sum back out. This moves 2/tp of the bytes of the one-hop path and is bit-identical to it. It costs ~10 µs at 7 rows and saves ~20 µs at 56, so Pro enables it from 42 rows.
- **Race fix (V4.1 and Pro).** On index-source layers, K2's combine stage could read a token's key count before the CTA building that key table had published it. Combine now waits on the table's ready flag and reads the count at device scope.
- **Limits:**
  - Pro's compressor and indexer still run as vLLM ops between K1 and K2, serially, where vLLM overlaps them on side streams.
  - At 56 rows a layer is ~3% slower than vLLM in the kernel bench; AgentX c8 still gains.
  - TP8 only for Pro.
- **Relation to #61311 / #60731.**
  - This PR does not touch the runtime layer #61311 proposes. If it lands, `MonoDecode` here can become that PR's per-model glue.
  - #60731 (V4.1 on gfx942) edits the files this PR moves, so whichever lands second needs a rebase. The move is a pure `git mv` plus spec parameterization.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the implementation, the tests and this description. The human submitter reviews every changed line before this PR leaves draft.

title: [Bug]: HiSparse with --enable-dbo crashes in dbo_register_recv_hook; construction-time workspace reservations only size ubatch slot 0
body:
### Your current environment

B200, upstream `main` @ 61d9c777bf, Model Runner V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Found while reviewing #60424. Tracking: #60072.

HiSparse needs Model Runner V2, and DBO on V2 needs `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, DP > 1 with EP, FULL CUDA graphs (the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` works; HiSparse rejects plain `FULL` and DBO rejects `PIECEWISE`), and DeepEP low-latency. With HiSparse on, the first microbatched step fails:

```
  File "vllm/v1/worker/ubatching.py", in dbo_register_recv_hook
    next_ctx.recv_hook = recv_hook
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'recv_hook'
```

**Repro**

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 \
  -tp 4 -dp 2 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --enable-dbo --all2all-backend deepep_low_latency \
  --attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":64}}'
```

Then send enough concurrent requests to go over the DBO token thresholds.

**1. Crash in `dbo_register_recv_hook`.** The `None` is the other microbatch's `UBatchContext` slot. `UBatchContext.__exit__` clears that slot, so microbatch 1 had already left its forward pass (almost certainly by raising) when microbatch 0 reached its next MoE dispatch. `UBatchRunner.finish` re-raises only the lowest-index microbatch error, so microbatch 1's real exception never shows up. That error reporting is a general V2 DBO problem. The underlying failure appears to be HiSparse-specific: #60734 reports GLM-5.3 running with V2 + DBO + DeepEP LL + FULL graphs when HiSparse is off. Note that #60734 also makes HiSparse + DBO raise at startup for models with shared top-k layers, which includes GLM-5.3.

**2. Latent: construction-time workspace reservations only size ubatch slot 0.** `WorkspaceManager` (`vllm/v1/worker/workspace.py`) keeps one workspace per `(ubatch, lane)` slot, and `_ensure_workspace_size` only resizes the slot that asks. Attention impls reserve their scratch in `__init__` on the main thread, which is ubatch 0. Examples: FlashMLA sparse `workspace_specs`, Triton MLA `_reserve_attn_logits_workspace`, AITER MLA fp8 prefill buffers, TurboQuant `_reserve_workspace`, and the HiSparse prefill staging added in #60424. So only slot 0 gets sized. MoE scratch is requested inside forward, so the microbatched runs before `lock_workspace()` (the ubatched FULL-graph captures) size slot 1 for it. Nothing does that for the construction-time reservations. Once (1) is fixed, the first ubatch-1 use of such a reservation on a path that didn't run before the lock (for example, sparse-MLA or HiSparse prefill staging in a microbatched prefill) will hit `AssertionError: Workspace is locked but allocation from ... Workspace growth is not allowed after locking.`

Possible fix for (2): a small `WorkspaceManager` method that reserves a spec across all `(ubatch, lane)` slots. Construction-time reservations would call it instead of `get_simultaneous`.

title: [KV Transfer] Connector-agnostic KV checksums for P/D disaggregation
body:
## Overview

> **For review, this series is split into stacked PRs:** #61578 (1/N, framework + NIXL pull), #61579 (2/N, TP replicas and block sizes), #61580 (3/N, NIXL push); Mooncake, Mamba state and the Triton kernel follow. This PR stays as a draft reference implementation of the whole series and holds its end-to-end validation.

Connector-agnostic KV checksums for P/D disaggregation. Some transfers complete without error but deliver the wrong KV: a read after the producer has already reused its blocks, or KV placed at the wrong position because producer and consumer disagree on the layout. With `kv_transfer_config.enable_kv_checksum` on both sides, the consumer verifies every KV load against checksums computed by the producer. Under `kv_checksum_fail_closed`, a mismatched or unverifiable load goes through the existing KV load failure path (`kv_load_failure_policy`: `fail`, or `recompute` locally).

Related, not duplicated: #57912 and RFC #54363 add integrity checks for the filesystem KV offload tier; this PR covers producer-to-consumer transfers. It also references #58860, #59746 / #59747 and RFC #47812 / #48216 (see the commit messages).

## Claims

- Detects KV corruption from a P/D transfer before the request runs, for NIXL pull, NIXL push and Mooncake P2P. It works across TP and PP layouts, block sizes, KV cache layouts, and Mamba state, including TP-split state between producers and consumers with different TP sizes.
- Does not change model outputs. With checksums on vs off in a deterministic setup, 200/200 outputs are identical token for token.
- Adds no CPU<->GPU synchronization to the engine step. The results are copied to the host on a side stream.
- Off by default, so it has no effect unless enabled.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (CPU, plus CUDA tests where a GPU is available):

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_checksum.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_checksum_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_checksum_cuda.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_output_aggregator.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py
```

595 passed and 12 skipped (the CUDA tests, on a CPU host). One test failed: `test_multi_example_connector_consistency` needs a gated model and fails the same way on the base commit. On GPU, `test_kv_checksum_cuda.py` passes, and the Triton kernel matches the PyTorch path bit for bit. pre-commit and mypy pass.

Mutation checks: each of the following edits makes the listed tests fail.
- disabling the comparison;
- summing only one PP stage's fingerprint;
- ignoring received checksums;
- comparing unsummed blocks across block sizes;
- skipping Mamba groups;
- taking the speculative scratch block as the Mamba state;
- for TP-split Mamba state: numbering rows per rank, reading pieces as signed values, or ignoring B/C replicas.

**End to end on GPU** (NIXL, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, with a test-only fault-injecting connector that is not part of this PR):
- Qwen3-0.6B. NIXL pull: TP1 -> TP1 and TP2 -> TP1. NIXL push: TP1 -> TP1, TP2 -> TP1 and TP1 -> TP2. In every case, clean runs report no mismatch, every injected bit flip is detected, fail-closed rejects the load, recompute completes the request, and there is no host sync.
- granite-4.0-h-micro (Mamba2, n_groups == 1), TP2 -> TP1 and TP1 -> TP2, pull and push. Upstream NIXL corrupts this transfer without reporting an error. Checksums report a mismatch for every request, only in the Mamba groups, and recompute matches the single-instance output. Nemotron-H and Qwen3.5 (GDN) across TP, and granite at equal TP, verify with no mismatch.

**Outputs unchanged (determinism test).** Setup: Qwen3-8B, P/D TP1 -> TP1 with NIXL pull, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, FlashInfer autotune off, temperature 0, concurrency 1, the first 200 gsm8k questions, max_tokens 512. Comparison is on full output token ids:

Three runs on fresh servers: two with checksums off and one with checksums on (consumer fail-closed). Each pair of runs is compared on all 200 outputs:

| comparison | outputs with identical token ids |
|---|---|
| checksums off vs checksums off (run-to-run baseline) | 200 / 200 |
| checksums on vs checksums off | 200 / 200 (0 mismatches over 200 KV transfers) |

**Accuracy (MiniMax-M3, P/D TP4 -> TP4, NIXL pull).** The comparison is checksums on (fail-closed with recompute) against checksums off and against a single instance. Differences are paired by problem; the 95% band treats the problem set as fixed.

| comparison | aime25 avg@16 difference |
|---|---|
| P/D on − P/D off | +0.62 pp (±2.3) |
| P/D on − single instance | +0.52 pp (±1.9) |

gpqa_diamond: P/D on − single instance = −1.11 pp (±1.5).

In the first aime25 run with checksums on, the consumer stalled for about 80 s. Its NIXL heartbeats stopped, and the producer's 30 s lease expired for 31 requests. The consumer later read those blocks after the producer had reused them. The checksums flagged exactly those 31 loads, matching the producer's lease-expiry log one to one. The consumer recomputed them locally, and every request completed with a full answer. This is the failure reported in #61229; #61549 makes the NIXL pull consumer check the lease itself.

**Heterogeneous TP (MiniMax-M3, P TP4 -> D DEP8, i.e. DP8 x TP1 with EP8 on two nodes).** Each decode rank pulls its KV heads from all 4 producer ranks.
- Smoke, checksums on (fail-closed with recompute): 50/50 requests complete, all 8 DP ranks serve requests, 0 mismatches, 0 unverified loads.
- aime25 avg@16: checksums on 0.8604 vs off 0.8729, a difference of -1.25 pp (±2.6), with 0 mismatches, 0 unverified loads and 0 expired leases over 480 requests.
- gpqa_diamond avg@5: 0.9071 with checksums on and off (0.00 pp, ±1.5), 0 mismatches over 990 requests.

**Data-parallel producer (MiniMax-M3, P DEP2 -> D DEP8, i.e. P DP2 x TP4 with EP8 on two nodes).** Each request is prefilled by one of the two producer engines, and the consumer checks the checksums from whichever engine prefilled it.
- Smoke, checksums on: 50/50 requests complete, both producer engines and all 8 consumer DP ranks serve requests, 0 mismatches, 0 unverified loads.
- aime25 avg@16: checksums on 0.8500 vs off 0.8646 (-1.46 pp, ±2.7); gpqa_diamond avg@5: 0.9020 vs 0.9010 (+0.10 pp, ±1.7).
- 0 mismatches, 0 unverified loads and 0 expired leases over 1,470 requests with checksums on.

**Performance.** Qwen3-8B, P/D TP2 -> TP2 with NIXL pull on GB200, prefix caching on, consumer fail-closed with recompute, `vllm bench serve` on random prompts. Checksums off and on were launched 3 times each, interleaved; values are the mean of the 3 launches, with 0 failed requests in every run.

| workload | metric | off | on | difference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1K in, 128 out, concurrency 1 | median TTFT (ms) | 35.56 | 39.01 | +3.45 (+9.7%) |
| | median TPOT (ms) | 2.93 | 2.93 | 0 |
| 1K in, 128 out, concurrency 32 | request throughput (req/s) | 51.16 | 49.20 | -3.8% |
| | median TPOT (ms) | 3.64 | 3.80 | +4.4% |
| 8K in, 1 out, 128 requests at once | median TTFT (ms) | 4270.5 | 4267.4 | -0.1% |
| 32K in, 128 out, concurrency 1 | median TTFT (ms) | 865.8 | 871.2 | +0.6% |

The cost at short prompts is mostly the fixed cost of one kernel launch per layer in the steps that finish a prefill or a load. Fusing the layers of one layout into one launch reduces the concurrency-1 cost to +1.5 ms and the concurrency-32 cost to -1.5%; that change is being evaluated and is not in this PR yet.

## Details

The series is split by component. Each commit message gives the design, the alternatives that were rejected, known limitations and validation.

1. **Worker computation.** The checksum definition: per (layer, KV head) slice, s = Σ x_j (2j+1) over the 8-byte pieces in token order, weighted by m = 2(layer·H + head) + 1, all mod 2^64. Each worker sums its own slices. Replicated heads count once on the producer and are checked per replica on the consumer. The sums use global coordinates, so they do not depend on the TP/PP split, the block size or the cache layout.
2. **Scheduling and verification.** Selects which blocks to checksum on each side. The comparison reports each group as mismatched or unverified, and fail-closed routes failures through the existing load-failure path. Adds the connector API `kv_checksum_carrier`. NIXL pull carries the checksums in `kv_transfer_params`.
3. **NIXL push.** The checksums ride on the completion notif of the WRITE that delivers the KV. Bumps `NIXL_CONNECTOR_VERSION` (once for the series).
4. **Block sizes.** Producer and consumer may use different block sizes.
5. **Mooncake P2P carrier.**
6. **Triton kernel.** One launch per layer, and each piece is read once. The PyTorch path is kept for CPU. A microbenchmark is added in `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_kv_checksum.py`.
7. **Mamba state.** Layers declare how TP splits their states (`MambaSpec.state_splits`, for Mamba1, Mamba2 and GDN), so state can be compared across different TP sizes.
8. **NIXL push cleanup.** Drops an unreachable producer-side branch.
9. **MiniMax-M3.** Declares the indexer cache replicated across TP.
10. **Several KV caches per layer.** Supports layers with more than one KV cache.
11. **MLA defaults to replicated.** An MLA spec without `max_tp_shards` is treated as replicated, which matches how NIXL classifies it.
12. **Host-side preparation.** Rows are built with numpy and copied to the GPU in one H2D per step.

Limitations:
- Mooncake is covered by unit tests only; it has not been run end to end on GPU.
- ROCm is untested.
- A Mamba group whose layers do not declare a split is skipped when producer and consumer TP sizes differ.
- When the producer's block size is a multiple of the consumer's (possible with NIXL push and Mooncake P2P), a consumer prefix hit that ends inside a producer block leaves that group unverified, so a fail-closed consumer recomputes the request.

title: [Bugfix] Size YaRN cos/sin cache to cover max_position
body:
## Overview

Generic YaRN (`rope_type: "yarn"`) precomputes only `original_max_position_embeddings × factor` cos/sin rows. A model whose `max_position_embeddings` is larger than that reads past the end of the cache for positions beyond it. This PR sizes the cache to at least `max_position`.

## Claims

- Fixes out-of-bounds cos/sin cache reads for YaRN configs where `max_position_embeddings > original_max_position_embeddings × factor`.
- Leaves every existing row bit-identical and the cache size unchanged for configs where `max_position ≤ original_max_position_embeddings × factor`.

## Validation

- **New unit test** `test_yarn_cos_sin_cache_covers_max_position` in `tests/kernels/core/test_pos_encoding.py` (factor 2, original 16384, max_position 131072):
  - It **fails on main**, on the row-count assertion (32,768 rows instead of 131,072).
  - It **passes with this change**. The test also checks that the first 32,768 rows match the short cache exactly, and that the new rows follow the same YaRN frequencies.
  - The existing `test_rope_module_cache` still passes.
  - Run: `pytest tests/kernels/core/test_pos_encoding.py -k "yarn_cos_sin or module_cache"`.
- **End-to-end:** we served a Kimi-K3 DSpark draft (qwen3 layers, trained at 16k, served with YaRN factor 2 / original 16384 / `max_position_embeddings` 1,048,576) as the speculative draft for Kimi-K3 on 8×B300. The run used a vLLM 0.17.2rc1-based build carrying this patch (same two-file change).
  - 500 real requests with prompts up to 842k tokens completed with no errors.
  - Acceptance on 64k+ prompts was in line with shorter prompts (3.27 tokens/step on 64k+ vs 3.14 pooled over all 500).
  - Every rank logged a 1,048,576-row cache.
  - The draft's cache also matched the Transformers YaRN reference (`ROPE_INIT_FUNCTIONS["yarn"]`) up to position 841k, within fp32 rounding.
  - We did not run upstream `main` end-to-end with this model.

## Details

**Root cause.** `get_rope(..., max_position, ...)` passes `original_max_position_embeddings` as the class's `max_position_embeddings`, which is needed for the YaRN correction range. `_compute_cos_sin_cache` then builds `max_position_embeddings × scaling_factor` rows. Two things make this a problem:
- Since #56446, `max_model_len` is `max_position_embeddings` for YaRN, matching Transformers. Nothing ties that value to `original × factor`.
- The rotary kernels index the cache by absolute position without bounds checks.

So any config with `max_position_embeddings > original_max_position_embeddings × factor` gets out-of-bounds reads past position `original × factor`. That means garbage rotations, or an illegal memory access. A concrete case is a draft model trained at 16k that rides along with a 1M-context target: it serves with YaRN ×2 (32k rows) but sees target positions up to 1M.

**Fix.** `get_rope` passes `cache_max_position=max_position` to `YaRNScalingRotaryEmbedding`, and the cache uses `max(original × factor, cache_max_position)` rows.
- The frequencies (`_compute_inv_freq`) still depend only on `original_max_position_embeddings` and `factor`, so the extra rows are the same YaRN rotation evaluated at larger positions, which is what Transformers computes on the fly.
- `MRotaryEmbedding` borrows `_compute_cos_sin_cache`, hence the `getattr` default. Its sizing is unchanged.

**Tradeoff.** Affected configs need more cache memory: `max_position × rotary_dim × dtype bytes`, e.g. 256 MiB for 1M × 64 in fp32. The cache is shared through `get_rope`'s module cache. Configs that were already in bounds are unaffected. The DeepSeek YaRN path is out of scope; it has its own cache class.

title: [ROCm][Perf][Kimi-K3] Mono decode layer for Kimi-K3 on MI355X w/ vanilla decode
body:
## Overview

Extend Kimi-K3's MI355X MonoKernel from [#60683](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60683) to support ordinary autoregressive decode without speculative decoding.

This is a stacked extension of [#60683](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60683) and should merge only after that PR.

## Claims

- Supports pure, uniform regular-decode steps with widths 1–8.
- Preserves the existing speculative-verification path.
- Continues routing prefill, mixed batches, unsupported graph modes, and widths above eight through standard vLLM layers.
- Requires no speculative decoding, MTP, or DSpark configuration.
- Improves output throughput by 46.2% at concurrency 1, 37.4% at concurrency 4, and 17.5% at concurrency 8 on the tested 80K-input workload.
- Falls back as designed above width eight: concurrency 16 remains within 1.3% of mono-off throughput.

## Validation

All model runs used one TP8 MI355X node with:

- Feature commit: `746699b45070b15d2c3e69f293d230d5a4340ee4`
- Image: `local/kimi-k3-monokernel:746699b45070b15d2c3e69f293d230d5a4340ee4`
- Model: `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`
- Model revision: `f831ab66814297da540d832a5235f8e904f29d06`
- No speculative decoding, MTP, or DSpark

### Correctness: Unit Tests

```console
$ pytest -v -s tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_mono tests/models/common/mono
78 passed, 15 warnings in 434.35s
```

This covers routing and configuration, regular-decode state handling, K1/K2 TP8 numerics against vLLM, 300 CUDA-graph replays, compile-without-launch warm-up, and engine fault/fail-stop behavior.

### Correctness: Benchmarks

I'm running several accuracy benchmarks as well to ensure that the monokernel exhibits the same accuracy as the non-mono code path. I'm happy to run more than those listed below, please just let me know!

- [X] GSM8k
- [X] AIME25
- [X] GPQA-Diamond

| Eval | Protocol |
|---|---|
| GSM8K | 5-shot, 1,319 questions, temperature 0, `do_sample=false`, concurrency 8, `max_length=40960`, `max_gen_toks=32768` | 
| AIME25 | 30 questions, four seeds, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, 64K generation budget |
| GPQA-Diamond | 198 questions × two answer orders, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, 128K, effort max | 

| Benchmark | Concurrency | Mono off | Mono on | Change|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K | 8 | 96.13% | 95.45% | **-0.68%** |
| AIME25 | 1 | 82.50% | 85.00% | **+2.50%** |
| GPQA-Diamond | 1 | 88.89%* | 86.87%* | **-2.02%*** |
| GPQA-Diamond | 8 | 87.37%** | 91.41%** | **+4.04%** |
| NIAH single_1, 32K–256K | 1 | 100.0% | 100.0% | **0.0%** | 
| NIAH multikey_2, 32K–256K | 1 | 100.0% | 100.0% | **0.0%** |
| NIAH multikey_3, 32K | 1 | 100.0% | 100.0% | **0.0%** |
| NIAH multikey_3, 128K | 1 | 85.0% | 90.0% | **+5.0%** |
| NIAH multikey_3, 256K | 1 | 82.5% | 75.0% | **-7.5%** |

>[!NOTE]
> The GPQA-Diamond and AIME25 tests are very sensitive to seed and are only 30 questions long so they tend to fluctuate a lot. For these benchmarks, I made sure that mono on/off always used the same seeds so the numbers are comparable to each other but may differ from numbers reported elsewhere.


## Details

### Motivation

[#60683](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60683) currently requires speculative decoding and only routes spec-verification steps through the Kimi-K3 MonoKernel. Ordinary autoregressive decode is refused at configuration time even though its one-token decode shape can use the existing `qlen=1` K1 specialization and K2 kernels.

This change removes only that restriction and adapts regular-decode metadata to the existing kernel interface.

### Design

For regular decode:

- `non_spec_state_indices_tensor` supplies one KDA state slot per active row.
- State indices are exposed to K1 as `[requests, 1]`.
- A device-resident tensor of ones supplies graph-stable accepted-token counts.
- Eligibility requires:
  - no prefill rows;
  - no speculative rows;
  - one regular-decode row per active request;
  - valid one-dimensional state indices;
  - launch width no greater than eight.

When speculative decoding is configured, the existing spec-verification path remains unchanged.

### Limitations

The existing [#60683](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60683) constraints remain:

- MI355X/gfx950.
- TP8.
- FULL CUDA graphs for decode.
- Pure decode steps only.
- Maximum MonoKernel width of eight rows.

Other steps continue using standard vLLM execution.

At concurrency 16, the width limit intentionally routes almost every step through standard vLLM execution, explaining the near-parity performance result.

### Performance
`vllm bench serve`, 64K shared cached prefix + 16K unique input, forced 1K output with ignore-EOS, 16 warm-ups, and `10 × concurrency` measured prompts. Mono off and on use the same image and server settings; only `--monokernel` differs.

| Concurrency | Output tok/s off | Output tok/s on | Change | Median TPOT off/on | Mono route share |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 55.20 | 80.68 | +46.2% | 16.69 / 10.99 ms | 99.8% |
| 4 | 165.12 | 226.90 | +37.4% | 21.15 / 13.82 ms | 99.1% |
| 8 | 278.00 | 326.78 | +17.5% | 23.99 / 19.65 ms | 98.3% |
| 16 | 397.23 | 402.21 | +1.3% | 33.48 / 33.41 ms | 0.4% |

### Not a duplicate

This does not duplicate [#60683](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60683): it is a small stacked extension enabling the non-speculative case that the base PR currently refuses.

A search of open vLLM PRs found no other Kimi-K3 change adding ordinary regular decode to this MonoKernel.

Related Kimi-K3 MonoKernel work:

- [#60683](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60683) introduces the MI355X Kimi-K3 MonoKernel for spec-verification steps and is this PR's base.
- [#61435](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61435) extends the speculative path to 64 rows and adds M1, but explicitly refuses non-speculative configurations.
- [#60997](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60997) ports the Kimi-K3 MonoKernel to gfx942; this change targets regular decode on MI355X/gfx950.
- [RFC #60904](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60904) defines the shared MonoKernel design and validation expectations.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61568 was opened after I opened this PR last night, adding it here now. I'll review it soon to see how much overlap we have

---

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Report failed pulls per request with several KV cache groups
body:
## Overview

On a model with several KV cache groups whose transfer groups are all full attention, one failed NIXL KV pull stops the decode engine. HiSparse decode is such a model: it adds KV cache groups that take no part in the transfer (`enable_kv_transfer=False`). The worker reports the failed request's block IDs in `invalid_block_ids`, and `Scheduler._handle_invalid_blocks` raises for any model with more than one KV cache group. This reports those failures through `failed_recving` only, so the request fails (or is recomputed) and the engine keeps serving.

Related: #53779 (transfer groups), #53781 (HiSparse host-resident groups), #52232 (HMA receive failures).

## Claims

- With more than one KV cache group, a failed pull is reported only in `failed_recving`. `invalid_block_ids` stays empty, so the scheduler no longer raises, and the request ends as `FINISHED_ERROR` (or is recomputed under `kv_load_failure_policy: recompute`).
- With one KV cache group nothing changes: the request's block IDs are still reported.
- HMA layouts are unchanged; they already skip `invalid_block_ids`.

## Validation

**Unit, CPU.** `test_transfer_setup_failure_returns_finished` gains a case with a second KV cache group outside the transfer, the shape HiSparse adds. On main the new case fails with `assert {7, 8, 9} == set()`: the block IDs the scheduler then rejects. With this change it passes.

```text
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  -k transfer_setup_failure_returns_finished
# main: 1 failed (test_transfer_setup_failure_returns_finished[True-False]), 3 passed
# this branch: 4 passed

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py
# main:        366 passed, 3 failed
# this branch: 368 passed, 3 failed (the 2 new cases)
```

The 3 failures are the same on both: `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[ray]`, `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[None]` and `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma[google/gemma-3-1b-it-512]` start an engine and need a GPU and a model download.

**Production, GLM-5.3 on H100.** P/D with NIXL 1.5.0, decode TP8 with HiSparse, vLLM main `d6aca837c3` plus three unrelated PRs. On 2026-10-13, 15 decode engines died in 4 hours, each with `RuntimeError: A KV connector reported block-level load failures (invalid_block_ids) which is not supported for models with multiple KV cache groups` right after a pull failed with `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT`. The condition in this change has run as a startup patch on every decode engine started after 15:56 UTC, all 36 by 20:15 UTC. None has died this way since. Two engines of one decode group failed 101 requests on pulls from two prefill workers between 18:46 and 19:33 UTC and kept serving. Why those connections fail is a separate issue; #61500 recovers from it.

## Details

Path of the failure, decode side:

1. The scheduler admits a request with remote KV and allocates blocks in every KV cache group, including the HiSparse groups outside the transfer.
2. `NixlConnectorWorker.start_load_kv` posts the read for the transfer groups. The read fails (`NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT`, or `transfer_setup_failed`).
3. `get_transfer_results` lists the request in `failed_recving`. Because `_is_hma_required` is derived from the transfer groups only (all full attention here), it also puts the request's group-0 block IDs in `_invalid_block_ids`.
4. `Scheduler.update_from_output` handles `failed_recving` (`_handle_failed_recving`), then `invalid_block_ids`. `_handle_invalid_blocks` raises because `kv_cache_groups` has more than one group, and the engine core dies.

The change gates step 3 on `len(kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups) == 1`, the same group set and condition the scheduler checks. Step 4 then only sees `failed_recving`.

Not a duplicate. Open PRs found with `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search` for "invalid_block_ids", "failed_recving", "nixl hma failed transfer" and "kv load failure hybrid":

- #52232 propagates HMA receive failures per request. It keys on `_is_hma_required`, which is false in this case, and has merge conflicts with main, which has since gained `failed_recving`.
- #54733, #48216, #50742, #45497 and #56135 make the scheduler recover failed block loads for hybrid models. Each would let the scheduler accept these block IDs in some form. This change keeps the NIXL worker within the scheduler's current contract and does not depend on them.
