title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Re-handshake with a pull peer after a failed read
body:
## Overview

With NIXL 1.5.0, a pull that fails with `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT` leaves the UCX endpoint to that prefill worker failed for good, so every later read between the two workers fails until one side restarts or the peer is evicted. The decode worker releases a failed peer only when `check_remote_metadata` reports its metadata missing, which it never does here. This adds a second release trigger next to that check: a peer is also released once two requests to it fail with no completed read in between, so the existing drain, backoff and re-handshake path builds a fresh connection.

Related: #55471 (added the invalid-peer path and the metadata check), #61238 (invalidates peers whose READ has stalled; touches the same lines), #61499 (keeps the engine up through these failures with HiSparse).

## Claims

- Confirmed missing local metadata releases the peer after the first failed read, unchanged from #55471.
- When two requests to a pull peer fail with recorded transport failures and no completed read in between, the peer is released once its reads drain, and the next read to it re-handshakes. A completed read resets the count, so a single failed request keeps the peer.
- A release that repeats within 60 s backs off from 1 s to 60 s before the next re-handshake, for either trigger; reads to the peer fail fast meanwhile.
- KV lease expiry and reads rejected while a peer drains are not transport failures and do not count. Push mode is unchanged.

## Validation

**Unit, CPU.** The #55471 tests are unchanged, including `test_recovery_requires_confirmed_missing_metadata`. `test_failed_reads_release_peer_with_loaded_metadata` fails two requests with the peer's metadata still loaded: the first keeps the peer, the second releases every rank of it. `test_completed_read_resets_failed_requests` checks that a completed read clears the count. With `_PEER_FAILED_REQS_BEFORE_RELEASE = 99` the first new test fails; with `1` four tests fail, including the #55471 cases where metadata is still present.

```text
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py
# main 8c60cf07b3:  375 passed, 3 failed
# this branch:      377 passed, 3 failed (2 tests added)
```

The 3 failures are the same on both: `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[ray]`, `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[None]` and `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma[google/gemma-3-1b-it-512]` start an engine and need a GPU and a gated model download.

<details>
<summary>Production trace, measured on df2c1c9172 (release on the first failed request)</summary>

GLM-5.3 on H100, P/D with NIXL 1.5.0 (UCX backend), vLLM main `d6aca837c3` plus three unrelated PRs and #61499. The change ran as a startup patch on decode engines started after 17:17 UTC on 2026-10-13.

| decode engine | after its first failed read to a prefill worker |
|---|---|
| without the change | the link failed every later read over it: two engines of one decode group failed 101 requests against two prefill workers between 18:46 and 19:33 UTC |
| with the change | one failed request; the peer released 50 ms later and a fresh handshake (`NIXL compatibility check passed`) 5 s after that (20:16 UTC). Two peers released this way at 18:24 UTC failed no further reads through 18:26 UTC |

With the count trigger, the same incident fails one more request, the next read over the failed endpoint, before the release.

</details>

## Details

Path of the failure on main, decode side, pull mode:

1. A decode worker reads a request's KV from a prefill worker. The UCX error callback fires for that endpoint (`nixlUcxEp::err_cb`, `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_utils.cpp` in NIXL 1.5.0) and moves it from `CONNECTED` to `FAILED`. Nothing moves it back; only `loadRemoteConnInfo`, run when the remote agent's metadata is added, creates a `CONNECTED` endpoint.
2. Every later read posted on a `FAILED` endpoint returns `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT` (`nixlUcxEp::read` and `postSgl` call `checkTxState`). The request fails, and `_handle_failed_transfer` records the remote engine in `_failed_remote_engines`.
3. `_cleanup_remote_engines` calls `check_remote_metadata` on the peer's agents without descriptors. `nixlAgent::checkRemoteMD` then only checks that the remote section exists locally, which it does, so the peer is kept.
4. The next request routed to that prefill worker reads over the same `FAILED` endpoint and fails at step 2.

The change keeps the metadata check in step 3 and adds a second trigger after it. `_failed_reqs_by_engine` holds, per peer, the requests that failed since its last completed read; `_cleanup_remote_engines` marks a peer invalid once it holds `_PEER_FAILED_REQS_BEFORE_RELEASE` (2) of them, or as before when its metadata is missing. The release path keeps its logic: reads to the peer are rejected until in-flight reads drain, its agents are removed, and the next read re-handshakes.

Why two failed requests: an invalidated peer rejects every new read while its reads drain, so releasing on one failure would cost a few seconds of recomputes for an error that might not repeat. A failed endpoint fails every later read (101 requests in the trace above), so on a dead connection the second failure arrives with the next read, at the cost of one more failed request. Requests count once however many of their transfers fail. There is no NIXL call that reports endpoint health, so one failure with metadata loaded cannot tell the two cases apart. Missing metadata already confirms stale state, so that trigger does not wait.

Not a duplicate. Open PRs found with `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search` for "check_remote_metadata", "nixl remote disconnect", "nixl rehandshake" and "nixl invalid peer": #61238 invalidates a peer whose READ stays in `PROC` past a timeout, which never records a failed transfer; #60279 handles stale P2P tiering registrations. Neither releases a peer after failed reads.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Sparse MLA: build pure-decode indptr on the host and skip the NoPE q copy
body:
## Purpose

Two small per-step cuts on the ROCm AITER sparse MLA decode path. Split out of the draft #59739. Independent of the MXFP4 KV cache work (#60321).

1. **Host-built decode indptr.** On a pure-decode step (`num_prefills == 0`, `max_query_len == 1`) with no speculative decoding, `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` is exact. So `paged_kv_indptr = cumsum(min(seq_len, topk))` is computed on the host into a pinned buffer and uploaded with one non-blocking copy. This replaces the `generate_sparse_seqlen_triton` launch, the device cumsum, and the tail fill. A `torch.Event` guards reuse of the pinned buffer. `req_id_per_token` is `0..n-1` on pure decode, so it is only rewritten when the decode batch grows past what the buffer already holds. Mixed and prefill batches, and any run with a speculative config, keep the existing device path unchanged.
2. **Skip the NoPE query copy.** When `qk_rope_head_dim == 0`, the MQA bmm output is already the token-major query. `forward` uses it directly instead of copying it into `q_concat_buffer`, provided it is contiguous and the dtype matches.

## Test Plan

- `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_sparse_host_decode_indptr.py` (new): checks that the host `cumsum(min(seq_len, topk))` matches `generate_sparse_seqlen_triton` for topk 2048 and 64.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py`:
  - The builder fixture gains the new attributes.
  - New `test_pure_decode_builds_indptr_on_the_host` asserts the device seqlen kernel is not launched, and checks the resulting `paged_kv_indptr` and `req_id_per_token`.
- Existing ROCm sparse MLA suites: `test_rocm_aiter_mla_sink.py`, `test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_index_remap.py`, `test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py`, `test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`, `test_rocm_aiter_triton_sparse_mla.py`.

## Test Result

- MI355X (gfx950), nightly ROCm image:
  - Before the fixture update: 94 passed, 8 skipped. The only failures were 18 `metadata_sync` cases where the `object.__new__` fixture lacked the new attributes.
  - The fixture update and the new test have **not yet been re-run on GPU**. All cards were occupied. Will update.
- pre-commit: clean.
- **Perf on current main is not measured yet.** Expected saving per pure-decode step per builder: about 3 kernel launches plus 1 H2D copy. The NoPE path also skips a `[tokens, heads, 512]` copy. Decode benchmark numbers will be added before marking this ready.

title: [Simulator] Timing, recording, disaggregated prefill and configuration search for simulated execution
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Simulated execution for vLLM. The real engine runs (scheduler, KV cache manager, prefix caching, async scheduling, frontend), but each step takes the time a timing model predicts instead of running the model, so a deployment's TTFT, TPOT and throughput can be predicted, and its configuration searched, without its hardware. Design and discussion: RFC #61305.

This includes and builds on @sagearc's KV cache simulator (#47922, which this PR contains with its commits and authorship), at the maintainers' choice of landing order: #47922 first and this on top, or both together.

## Claims

- **Timing:**
  - `SimulationConfig` selects a per-step timing provider: `zero`, `linear`, `table` (k-NN over recorded steps), `replay` (exact batch-composition match), or a plugin class.
  - A step's predicted host time holds the engine thread; its device time runs on a modeled device queue, as under async scheduling.
- **Recording:** `record_step_timing` logs a real deployment's per-step device and host times, KV transfers and NIXL read postings in the providers' format, without waiting on the device.
- **Clocks:** offline runs on `fast_forward` or deterministic `virtual` clocks, much faster than real time; `vllm serve --simulate-forward` runs on the real clock behind any client.
- **Simulated features:**
  - speculative decoding (sampled acceptance);
  - TP / PP / DP, including MoE DP, and prefill and decode context parallelism;
  - quantized checkpoints, built with their weight quantization as deployed, including online FP8 quantization;
  - GPU-free runs on the CPU platform, modeling the GPU deployment's settings;
  - CPU KV offloading;
  - multi-turn sessions;
  - a host-time model fitted from a recording.
- **Disaggregated prefill (NIXL):**
  - in-process driver for any P:D ratio;
  - served instances behind any proxy;
  - heterogeneous TP;
  - push mode with prefill PP;
  - the decode instance's read-posting cost (see #55434).
- **Configuration search:** `vllm bench sweep simulate` runs a `vllm bench sweep serve` experiment's combinations in simulation, optionally searching each for the highest request rate meeting latency SLOs. It covers aggregated and P/D combinations, and its output works with the existing sweep plots.
- **Off by default:** with simulation off nothing changes. There are no new CPU/GPU syncs, the config hash is unchanged, and the core changes (about 370 lines outside the simulator) are seams it reuses (the CPU platform's hybrid block-size fix it needed landed separately as #61805):
  - MRV2: `ActiveKVConnector.register_kv_caches`, and runner and worker methods split out for overriding (KV cache allocation, request-state updates, connector creation, device binding);
  - NIXL: a `worker_cls` attribute on the pull and push connectors, and shared lease and side-channel-port helpers;
  - `vllm bench serve`: `get_request_delays` and the metric-result builders factored out, so simulated runs report the same metrics;
  - fake implementations of the three FP8 quantization ops, so online quantization runs on meta weights;
  - the worker-class selection in `SimulationConfig`, CPU-platform settings that keep a modeled GPU deployment's configuration, and optional `trace_decode_token_ids` on the completion and chat requests;

## Validation

All on H200. Each simulated run replays a recording of the real deployment.

| Area | Workload | Real vs simulated |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Served replay | Qwen3-0.6B, 10 req/s, ISL 512 / OSL 64 | mean TTFT −2.1%, TPOT +1.7%, E2E +1.0% |
| Speculative decoding | Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3, MMLU-Pro, 4 req/s | TPOT +1.5%, TTFT and E2E within 2.5% |
| Parallelism | Qwen3-8B TP=2 / PP=2, 8 req/s | TTFT 19.94/20.09 and 18.81/18.30 ms; TPOT within 0.6% |
| KV offloading | Qwen3-8B, 24 shared 4k-token documents | TTFT 45.5/44.9 ms, TPOT 5.622/5.616 ms |
| Sessions + offloading | 32 sessions × 5 turns | TTFT 420.9/417.0 ms, TPOT 6.161/6.162 ms |
| P/D, served, TP=2 | 1P1D | TTFT 73.4/73.2 ms, TPOT 3.874 ms on both |
| P/D, push + prefill PP | TP1 PP2 prefill → TP2 decode | median TTFT within 8%, TPOT within 0.1% |
| Config search, aggregated | Qwen3-8B, 10 configs, SLO P99 TTFT ≤ 500 ms, TPOT ≤ 8 ms | real runs at the predicted max rates: TPOT and throughput match; all violate the SLO at +15% |
| Config search, P/D steady state | 1P1D, 2P1D at 16.7–47.6 req/s | TPOT −11% to +5%, median TTFT −11% to +22% |

![Simulation error across the validation scenarios](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/lucifer1004/904481063b5ed5c4537ec3e4b21b6cce/raw/1865b502c6d974b1e7a870fee191eeb3e90a86a5/accuracy.svg)

Simulated vs real error for each scenario above; the shaded band is ±5%.

![Simulated sweep vs real runs](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/lucifer1004/904481063b5ed5c4537ec3e4b21b6cce/raw/92255089200de3cfb581475848612449627639f3/config_search.svg)

Aggregated config search: the simulated rate sweep (lines) and real runs at the predicted max rate and 15% above it (circles), against the SLO (dashed).

**Sensitivity to step-time error.** Simulated execution keeps the scheduler in the loop, so an error in step time also changes queueing and batch sizes. To see how far that carries, Qwen3-8B (AISimulate timing, H200) was run with every step's device time scaled by 0.97 and 1.03, on the same 400 requests (random 1024/256, Poisson arrivals) at each load. The table gives each metric's relative change divided by 3%, as the mean (min–max) over 5 seeds:

| Load ρ (fraction of saturated throughput) | 0.3 | 0.6 | 0.8 | 0.9 | 0.96 | 1.0 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mean TPOT | 1.3× | 1.6× | 2.1× | 2.4× (2.1–2.6) | 2.3× | 2.1× (1.5–2.6) |
| P99 TTFT | 1.4× | 2.0× | 2.0× | 4.7× (2.2–14) | 5.2× (1.9–14) | 14× (2.2–27) |
| Max rate meeting P99 TTFT ≤ 500 ms | 1.06× (1.00–1.09), independent of load |

The max rate under an SLO moves about as much as step time does. Mean TPOT moves up to about 2.4× as much, and the factor stops growing near saturation. P99 TTFT close to saturation moves by a large, seed-dependent amount. A step-time model that is accurate to a few percent therefore gives max rate and TPOT to a similar accuracy, but cannot pin down tail TTFT near saturation.

![Amplification of a 3% step-time error](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/lucifer1004/904481063b5ed5c4537ec3e4b21b6cce/raw/ba4d3055d1908f7be87f551a0f758d13f9f12ac4/conditioning.svg)

**Tests run:**

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/simulated tests/benchmarks/sweep/test_simulate.py tests/v1/e2e/test_simulated_forward.py  # 54 passed on H200
pytest tests/platforms/test_cpu.py tests/v1/worker/simulated tests/benchmarks/sweep/test_simulate.py tests/v1/e2e/test_simulated_forward.py  # 68 passed on a CPU build
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant_group.py tests/compile/passes/test_rope_kvcache_fusion.py  # 258 passed (FP8 op fakes)
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_heartbeat.py  # passed
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD)  # clean
```

The simulator tests also ran GPU-free on a CPU build of vLLM (triton-cpu 3.8.0). The new `cpu-simulated-forward-tests` Buildkite job runs all three test locations there; it is `soft_fail` while new. Recording (`record_step_timing`) needs a GPU and is not covered in CI; it was validated with real recordings, including EAGLE3.

The frontier-model matrix of #61407 (Kimi-K3, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, GLM-5, FP8 and NVFP4 checkpoints, PP, PCP, DCP) builds and runs under simulation on 8×H200; the full-size models also with prefix caching and CPU KV offloading.

## Details

- **Not a duplicate:**
  - #47922 is the base of this PR and is included.
  - RFC #61406 and #61407 propose a related simulator, with a meta-mode forward for CPU CI and the simulation outside the tree behind import-time hooks. This PR keeps simulation in the tree behind `SimulationConfig` and skips the forward instead of running it. The two meet at the step-timing contract: an analytical predictor plugs in as a `TimingProvider` plugin, and one wrapping AISimulate (the successor of AIConfigurator) already runs out of tree. We would like to converge with it rather than maintain two simulators; on #61406 we proposed landing #47922, then this PR, then #61407's meta forward as an option of the simulated runner, and its author agreed with that option.
- **Size:** about 6.9k lines, roughly 2.1k of them tests, docs and CI. The feature commits are kept separate and can be split as maintainers prefer.
- **Reading guide:** the parts build on each other, and each part after the first can be reviewed on its own.
  1. *Overview:* `docs/features/simulated_execution.md`.
  2. *Core changes* (about 370 lines, listed under "Off by default" above). The largest are in `vllm/benchmarks/serve.py`, `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py`, `vllm/platforms/cpu.py` and `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`.
  3. *Simulator core* (about 1.5k lines): `vllm/config/simulation.py` (options and worker-class selection); `simulated/timing.py` (`StepDescriptor` → `TimingProvider` → `StepCost`, the built-in providers, and the clocks); `simulated/model_runner.py` (MRV2 bookkeeping with the forward replaced by the predicted time); `simulated/worker.py` (no weights or KV tensors). Tests: `tests/v1/worker/simulated/test_timing.py`, `tests/v1/e2e/test_simulated_forward.py`.
  4. *Offline driver and recording:* `simulated/offline.py` (`make_engine`, `run`, `simulate` on the virtual and fast-forward clocks) and `simulated/recording.py` (`record_step_timing`).
  5. *KV transfers* (about 1.5k lines): `simulated/kv_transfer.py` (connector worker side, CPU offloading), `simulated/kv_nixl.py` (pull- and push-mode NIXL), `simulated/disaggregated.py` (in-process P/D driver). Tests: `test_kv_transfer.py`, `test_kv_nixl.py`.
  6. *Configuration search:* `vllm/benchmarks/sweep/simulate.py`, `docs/benchmarking/sweeps.md`, `tests/benchmarks/sweep/test_simulate.py`.
- **Known limitations:**
  - Real prefill steps run about 4% slower under sustained load, which a replay cannot capture.
  - The read-posting model is linear in runs of consecutive blocks.
  - Recording MoE-DP gathers step descriptors on the engine thread every step.
  - The simulation clocks are process-wide objects. An explicit runtime handle would be cleaner, at the cost of threading it through engine construction.
  - On the CPU platform, layers still pick the CPU's attention backends and kernels, so a model needing a GPU-only one (sparse MLA, DCP, NVFP4 or MXFP4 weights, online FP8 quantization) does not build there.
- **AI assistance:** this PR was developed with Claude Code, and the author reviewed every change. The submitting human has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above.

Co-authored-by: Sage Ahrac <80211083+sagearc@users.noreply.github.com>

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Don't count adaptive verification profiling cache as CUDA graph memory
body:
## Overview

With adaptive verification on, Model Runner V2 counts the allocator cache left by adaptive verification's cost-profiling dummy runs as CUDA graph memory, and takes it from the KV cache. This PR releases that cache before `capture_model` takes its closing memory reading.

## Claims

- Fixes the over-counted CUDA graph memory under adaptive verification, in both the memory-profiling estimate pass and the real capture (0.92 → 0.07 GiB in the run below). The KV cache gets that memory back.
- When KV capacity is the bottleneck, decode throughput recovers: 40.5 → 113.2 tok/s in the run below, matching the same config without adaptive verification (110.2 tok/s).
- Startup only. Nothing changes in steady-state execution, and runs without adaptive verification are unaffected.

## Validation

**Startup log.** 1× L4, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct` with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` as `draft_model`, `num_speculative_tokens=4`, `enable_adaptive_verification=true`, `TRITON_ATTN`, `max_model_len=32768`, `max_num_seqs=3`, prefix caching on:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 3 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.36 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "draft_model", "model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
    "num_speculative_tokens": 4, "enable_adaptive_verification": true}'
# compare the two "Graph capturing finished ... took X GiB" lines and "GPU KV cache size"
```

**Throughput.** Decode-bound long-context workload, greedy, `max_tokens=256`:
- 12 prompts, each a 24K-token slice of vLLM's docs followed by a question.
- Contexts are processed in groups of 3. Each group is first prefilled with one question, then timed with a different question, so the timed requests reuse the warmed prefix.
- One run per config. The memory numbers are deterministic: both runs without the fix logged 0.92 / 0.88 GiB.

| `gpu_memory_utilization` | Config | "Graph capturing ... took" (estimate / real) | GPU KV cache | Prefix hit rate | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.36 | main, adaptive verification | 0.92 / 0.88 GiB | 64,688 tokens | 37.8% | 40.5 |
| 0.36 | this PR, adaptive verification | 0.07 / 0.04 GiB | 86,960 tokens | 50.0% | 113.2 |
| 0.36 | adaptive verification off (reference) | 0.07 / 0.03 GiB | 87,376 tokens | 50.0% | 110.2 |
| 0.9 | main, adaptive verification | 0.92 / 0.88 GiB | 376,432 tokens | 50.0% | 110.6 |
| 0.9 | this PR, adaptive verification | 0.07 / 0.04 GiB | 398,912 tokens | 50.0% | 110.1 |

At 0.36, 64,688 tokens can't hold three ~24.3K-token requests. Prefixes get evicted and re-prefilled (hit rate 37.8% vs 50%), and decode runs fewer requests at once. At 0.9 there's enough KV either way, so only the KV size changes.

The effect is larger with bigger models. With #60339's suffix speculator and adaptive verification on Qwen2.5-7B at 24K context (L4, utilization 0.9), the leftover cache was 1.88 GiB:
- KV cache: 44,400 tokens before, 79,584 after.
- Long-context decode: 0.28× of no speculation before, 1.39× after.

**Tests.**

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py
# 48 passed
```

The new `test_capture_model_excludes_adaptive_verification_profiling_cache` covers both `profile_only=False` and `profile_only=True`, and fails on main.

## Details

**Root cause.** `capture_model` reads free memory, captures the graphs, then reads free memory again. The difference is reported as CUDA graph memory. When adaptive verification is on, the profiling for its cost curves also runs between those two readings: `batches_to_profile`, i.e. 5 replays of each capture size plus tail sizes up to `max_num_batched_tokens`, with the profiling context length. Those dummy runs free their tensors, but the caching allocator keeps the blocks. `get_memory_info` therefore sees them as used: about 0.85 GiB here, and 1.9 GiB with a 7B target (allocated delta ≈ 0, all of it reserved cache).

The same `capture_model` serves `profile_cudagraph_memory`'s estimate pass, whose result is subtracted from the KV budget. So the KV cache is sized as if graphs needed that memory.

**Fix.** Call `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()` after `set_initial_cost_curves`, matching the `empty_cache()` that already runs before the first reading. The profiling timings are already collected by then, since `StepTimingCollector.collect` synchronizes on exit.

**Scope.**
- Model Runner V1 has no adaptive verification.
- #52233 (opt-in persistent profile cache) touches the same block. On a cache hit it would skip the dummy runs, but it's off by default and doesn't change the accounting.
- #54065 and #54077 change the shapes of the profiled tail, not the memory accounting.

**Not duplicating existing work.** I searched open and closed PRs and issues for "empty_cache adaptive verification", "capture_model memory adaptive", "cuda graph memory adaptive verification", "adaptive verification KV cache memory" and "batches_to_profile". The only related results are the PRs listed under Scope.

title: [Perf][Mamba] Capture the Mamba2 mixer in piecewise CUDA graphs
body:
## Overview

Lets the Mamba2 mixer run inside the piecewise CUDA graphs of prefill and mixed prefill+decode
steps, instead of eagerly between graph pieces. It is opt-in: leave `vllm::mamba_mixer2` out of
`compilation_config.splitting_ops`. This PR is part of a series that brings piecewise CUDA graphs to
Mamba2 prefill steps, and it is stacked on #61501 and #61497. Tested with #61293 applied, but it
does not depend on it. Like #61501, it needs flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6100 (`cu_seqlens` in
`SSDCombined`), which is merged into FlashInfer main but not yet in a release.

## Claims

- Up to 1.30x output throughput (OTPS/gpu) over `main` + #61293 with the whole series, on 1x B200
  with Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-NVFP4-W4A4 and MTP=2 (up to 1.14x without this PR). On its own, this
  PR is 1.08-1.14x over #61501 at concurrency 8-32, 1.05-1.06x at 2-4 and 64, and flat at 1 and
  128.
- At concurrency 16, a mixed prefill+decode step takes 10.3 ms instead of 24.9 ms (nsys, vs
  #61501): 7 graph launches and 105 eager kernels instead of 30 and 336, and 5.9 ms of host time
  instead of 22.4 ms.
- p90 inter-chunk latency at concurrency 16-32 drops from 21-22 ms to 11-12 ms (vs #61501).

## Validation

End-to-end serving throughput:

- **Base:** `main` + #61293.
- **+ #61497 + #61501:** Base plus both PRs, with `--mamba-prefill-backend flashinfer`.
- **+ this PR:** the same, plus this PR, with `vllm::mamba_mixer2` left out of `splitting_ops`.
- **Hardware:** 1x B200, TP1.
- **FlashInfer:** upstream main at `2a2cceab0`, which includes flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6100 and
  flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6206.
- **Workload:** SPEED-Bench `throughput_1k`, `low_entropy` category (512 prompts),
  `max_tokens` 200, served through aiperf.
  - Warm-up: 256 requests at concurrency 128, discarded.
  - Then the full 512-prompt dataset at each concurrency from 128 down to 1.
  - Concurrency 64 and 128 were run 2 more times; those rows are the mean of 3 runs. The #61501
    column at concurrency 1-4 is the mean of 4 runs.

Values are OTPS/gpu (output tokens/s per GPU); both speedups are over Base:

| Concurrency | Base | + #61497 + #61501 | + this PR | Speedup through #61501 | Speedup with this PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 760 | 822 | 822 | 1.08x | 1.08x |
| 2 | 1250 | 1364 | 1433 | 1.09x | 1.15x |
| 4 | 1890 | 2106 | 2209 | 1.11x | 1.17x |
| 8 | 2896 | 3313 | 3639 | 1.14x | 1.26x |
| 16 | 4398 | 4999 | 5681 | 1.14x | 1.29x |
| 32 | 7045 | 7979 | 9159 | 1.13x | 1.30x |
| 64 | 11506 | 12751 | 13640 | 1.11x | 1.19x |
| 128 | 16641 | 18167 | 18135 | 1.09x | 1.09x |

Mid concurrencies have the most prefill and mixed-batch interruptions, so they gain the most; the
effect is smaller at low and high concurrency.

Accuracy: GPQA-diamond through NeMo Gym on 1x GB300, TP1, MTP=2 (198 questions x 8 repeats, thinking on,
temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95), with the serve command below plus `--max-model-len 262144
--reasoning-parser nemotron_v3`. pass@1, mean over the 8 repeats ± standard error:

- No prefix reuse (as below): 75.69 ± 0.68%
- Prefix reuse (`--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align`, no ReplaySSM; the mixer runs eagerly here, since capturing it needs `--mamba-cache-mode none`): 76.52 ± 0.65%

<details>
<summary>Serve and client commands</summary>

`--mamba-prefill-backend flashinfer` selects #61501's scan for prefills, and `splitting_ops`
without `vllm::mamba_mixer2` captures the mixer in the piecewise graphs. The #61501 column used the
same command without `splitting_ops`; Base also dropped `--mamba-prefill-backend`.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
MODEL=${MODEL:?path or HF id of the Nemotron-3.5-Lightning NVFP4 W4A4 checkpoint}
NUMA_NODE=${NUMA_NODE:?NUMA node local to the GPU}
CAPTURE_SIZES='[1,2,4,8,16,24,32,40,48,56,64,72,80,88,96,104,112,120,128,136,144,152,160,168,176,184,192,200,208,216,224,232,240,248,256,272,288,304,320,336,352,368,384,400,416,432,448,464,480,496,512,528,544,560,576,592,608,624,640,656,672,688,704,720,736,752,768,784,800,816,832,848,864,880,896,912,928,944,960,976,992,1008,1024,1152,1280,1408,1536,1664,1792,1920,2048,2560,3072,3584,4096,5120,6144,7168,8192,10240,12288,14336,16384,18432,20480,22528,24576,26624,28672,30720,32768]'
# vLLM's default splitting ops without vllm::mamba_mixer2.
SPLITTING_OPS='["vllm::unified_attention_with_output","vllm::unified_mla_attention_with_output","vllm::mamba_mixer","vllm::short_conv","vllm::qwen4_exp_ple_short_conv","vllm::qwen4_exp_qsa_with_output","vllm::linear_attention","vllm::qwen_gdn_attention_core","vllm::qwen_gdn_attention_core_fused_norm_packed","vllm::gdn_attention_core_xpu","vllm::olmo_hybrid_gdn_full_forward","vllm::sparse_attn_indexer","vllm::rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer","vllm::deepseek_v4_attention","vllm::hpc_rope_norm_forward","vllm::unified_kv_cache_update","vllm::unified_mla_kv_cache_update"]'

vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --served-model-name nemotron-3.5-lightning \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --async-scheduling \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2,"moe_backend":"flashinfer_trtllm"}' \
  --mamba-cache-mode none \
  --mamba-backend flashinfer \
  --mamba-prefill-backend flashinfer \
  --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 \
  --enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding \
  --mamba-cache-philox-rounds 5 \
  --use-replayssm \
  --compilation-config "{\"mode\":3,\"cudagraph_mode\":\"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE\",\"max_cudagraph_capture_size\":32768,\"cudagraph_capture_sizes\":${CAPTURE_SIZES},\"splitting_ops\":${SPLITTING_OPS}}" \
  --numa-bind --numa-bind-nodes "$NUMA_NODE" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001
```

Client, run once per concurrency level:

```bash
aiperf profile \
  --model nemotron-3.5-lightning --tokenizer "$MODEL" --tokenizer-trust-remote-code \
  --endpoint-type chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --streaming --use-legacy-max-tokens \
  --url http://localhost:8001 \
  --input-file "$SPEED_BENCH_1K_LOW_ENTROPY_JSONL" \
  --extra-inputs max_tokens:200 --extra-inputs skip_special_tokens:false \
  --random-seed 1234 --use-server-token-count \
  --concurrency "$CONC" --request-count 512 --num-dataset-entries 512
```

</details>

## Details

`vllm::mamba_mixer2` is a piecewise splitting op, so in every prefill or mixed step each Mamba2
layer runs eagerly between graph pieces. That work is host-bound: a decode request that shares a
step with a ~1k-token prefill waits 20-30 ms instead of ~3 ms. #61497 and #61501 trim the host
overhead; this PR captures the mixer.

Changes:

- Opt-in with no new flag: leave `vllm::mamba_mixer2` out of `splitting_ops`. Requires the V2 model
  runner, FlashInfer ReplaySSM decodes, `--mamba-prefill-backend flashinfer` and
  `--mamba-cache-mode none`, checked at startup.
- Captured steps run `conv_ssm_forward_static()`, whose shapes depend only on the padded token
  count. `Mamba2AttentionMetadataBuilder` writes its per-step metadata into persistent buffers with
  one upload, on piecewise steps only.
- Prefill: `causal_conv1d_fn` and `mamba_chunk_scan_flashinfer_static`. Decode rows and padding up
  to the next 128-token boundary are identity rows (zeroed inputs, dt = -1e4); later padding is
  skipped. Steps with more prefills than the scan's slots (about one per 512 tokens, at least 8)
  run eagerly.
- Decode: the varlen conv1d update and FlashInfer ReplaySSM over the padded decode rows.
- Steps above the largest capture size, FULL decode graphs and eager steps keep the existing path.
  A static Triton scan is a separate change.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [ ] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

title: [ROCm][Qwen4Exp] Enable fp8 KV and indexer caches on the AMD QSA path
body:
## Overview This PR enables the recipe's two fp8 cache flags on the Qwen4Exp AMD (ROCm) QSA path, mirroring the NVIDIA-side support: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 ... \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8 ``` Three commits: 1. **`[ROCm][Bugfix] Apply FP8 cache scales to FNUZ destinations in the AMD fused QSA prepare`** — `_to_dst_dtype` divided by the main-attention KV cache scale only for `tl.float8e4nv` (OCP) destinations. On ROCm, FP8 KV caches type as `float8_e4m3fnuz` (Triton `tl.float8e4b8`), so the scale was never applied: FP8-typed destinations received `k_scale`/`v_scale` times the intended magnitude. Latent before this PR (the AMD path restricted KV dtypes to auto/bfloat16), required before FP8 KV can be enabled. 2. **`Support indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`** — wires `--attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype` through `amd/indexer_qsa.py`, mirroring the NVIDIA reference (`fp8` → `torch.float8_e4m3fn` for the compressed key cache and the query side; the raw state cache stays bf16). The fused kernel already handled fp8-typed indexer caches; only the wiring and test coverage were missing (the indexer cells were skipped as "bf16-only"). 3. **`Support fp8 main KV cache`** — lifts the remaining dtype gates and reinterprets the uint8 main cache at the boundaries in the platform's native fp8 flavor — **OCP (`float8_e4m3fn`) on gfx950/CDNA4, FNUZ (`float8_e4m3fnuz`) on gfx942/CDNA3** — matching the C++ cache-update op, which follows the platform flavor the same way (`HIP_FP8_TYPE_OCP`), so no C++ changes are needed. The sparse attention kernel gains an `IS_FP8` constexpr with the NVIDIA port's casts (fp8 K upcast to the query dtype for the QK dot; fp8 V to fp16 for the PV dot). A `kv_reads_bypass_flash_attn` class attribute lets the QSA impl skip the FlashAttention library's kv-dtype support check, since QSA reads its cache through its own Triton kernel. The test's `main_fp8` parametrization covers both flavors. ## Claims - **KV capacity: +33%** at TP1 (2,505,113 → 3,336,874 tokens) with both flags; the main KV cache is the dominant consumer and halves. - **Quality-neutral** on GSM8K 5-shot (6-run pairs): strict-match 0.899 vs 0.902 baseline; flexible-extract 0.881 vs 0.895 with fully overlapping run ranges. - **Quality-neutral** on GPQA-Diamond (198 questions, greedy): 0.4596 vs 0.4747 flexible-extract (within the ±3.5 pt binomial SE); NIAH retrieval identical (90/90 at every length and depth, 8K-32K). - **Greedy outputs byte-identical** on the arithmetic/coherence gates in-session (391 ×3 + a France continuation, temperature 0). - **Throughput**: decode is unchanged; concurrency-16 aggregate is ~6% lower with both flags (documented tradeoff below — the flags are opt-in, a capacity-vs-concurrency choice). ## Validation **Unit tests** (gfx950 / MI355X, ROCm 7.2.3, torch 2.13.0+rocm7.2): ```bash pytest -v tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py ``` `48 passed` at this PR's HEAD — the `main_fp8` parametrization now covers `bf16 | fnuz | ocp` crossed with the indexer dtype. Before commit 1, the fp8 cells failed with a systematic mis-scale (stored/expected code differences ~8 steps across the whole cache — exactly the 0.5 scale factor). Before commit 3, serving with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` failed at four dtype gates (impl, layer, backend init, and the FlashAttention base check). Raw captures:
Red run (commit 1's fix reverted), 8 FAILED — the mis-scale signature ``` FAILED tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py::test_qsa_fused_prepare_matches_unfused[mrope-indexer_dtype0-True] FAILED tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py::test_qsa_fused_prepare_matches_unfused[text-indexer_dtype0-True] FAILED tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py::test_qsa_fused_prepare_matches_unfused[mrope-model-1d-indexer_dtype0-True] ... (8 total) ============ 8 failed, 8 passed, 16 skipped, 14 warnings in 11.37s ============ ``` The assertion output shows the stored/expected code differences are a systematic ~8 code steps across the whole cache (the k_scale=0.5 mis-scale), far outside the tolerance (`code_diff <= 2 | abs_diff <= RTOL*|expected| + 2*ATOL`).
Pre-change boot failures with --kv-cache-dtype fp8 (the lifted gates) ``` NotImplementedError: Qwen4Exp QSA requires a BF16 main KV cache # impl + layer + backend gates NotImplementedError: FlashAttention does not support fp8 kv-cache on this device. # FA base check ```
Green at HEAD ``` ======================= 48 passed, 14 warnings in 16.10s ======================= ``` `pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/ --ignore=tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_amd.py` → `186 passed, 86 skipped`; `pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_amd.py` → `16 passed`. (Whole-directory collection has a pre-existing custom-op registration clash, reproducible on the clean tree.)
**Serving / capacity** (MI355X, TP1, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, max-model-len 16384, max-num-seqs 16, no MTP; identical flags otherwise): | config | GPU KV cache (tokens) | greedy gates | | --- | --- | --- | | bf16 baseline | 2,505,113 | 391 ×3, France continuation exact | | indexer fp8 | 2,541,158 (+1.5%) | identical | | main KV fp8 | 3,238,570 (+29.3%) | identical | | both | **3,336,874 (+33.2%)** | identical |
Raw boot-log lines ``` bf16: GPU KV cache size: 2,505,113 tokens indexer fp8: GPU KV cache size: 2,541,158 tokens main KV fp8: GPU KV cache size: 3,238,570 tokens both: GPU KV cache size: 3,336,874 tokens ```
At TP4 (cards 4-7, same protocol), the indexer-fp8 gain grows with tensor parallelism because the indexer side cache is replicated (`num_kv_heads=1`, unsharded) while the main KV shards: 11,541,981 → 11,893,691 tokens (**+3.05%**, vs +1.5% at TP1; the absolute gain scales ~9×). Note the FP8 checkpoint at TP4 currently needs `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0` and `--disable-custom-all-reduce` on this tree — both are the failure modes #60839 automates fallbacks for. **Quality: GSM8K 5-shot** (chat template, 250-problem deterministic subset, 6 runs per config, lm_eval against the served endpoint): | config | flexible-extract (6 runs) | mean | strict-match (6 runs) | mean | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | bf16 | 0.900 0.888 0.908 0.884 0.900 0.892 | 0.895 | 0.888 0.904 0.904 0.904 0.904 0.908 | 0.902 | | indexer fp8 | 0.900 0.892 0.876 0.892 0.884 0.896 | 0.890 | 0.908 0.896 0.884 0.916 0.884 0.912 | 0.900 | | both fp8 | 0.892 0.884 0.868 0.876 0.884 0.880 | 0.881 | 0.896 0.904 0.896 0.884 0.904 0.908 | 0.899 | Strict-match is neutral; flexible-extract is −1.4 points with fully overlapping ranges. All configs share the same build, so the comparison is internally controlled. *(Correction: our earlier caveat attributed the TP1 GSM8K absolutes to the un-merged #60816 — that was wrong. The relevant fix (#55104) is already in this build, and TP1 and TP2 score identically on it. The table's numbers are consistent with the shared lm_eval setup — same build, server config, and harness across all arms — so the claim is the within-build delta.)*
Raw score lines (first two runs per config) ``` bf16: |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.900|± |0.019| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.888|± |0.0200| both fp8:|gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.892|± |0.0197| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.884|± |0.0203| ```
**Quality: GPQA-Diamond and NIAH long-context retrieval** (added per review; both arms on the PR head, TP1, MI355X, max-model-len 32768, greedy temperature 0): | arm | GPQA-Diamond, flexible-extract (198 q) | NIAH ({8, 16, 32}K × depths {0…100}% × 2 needles × 3 seeds) | | --- | --- | --- | | bf16 (auto) | 0.4596 ± 0.0355 | 90/90 = 100% | | fp8 main + indexer | 0.4747 ± 0.0356 | 90/90 = 100% | GPQA is within the binomial SE (fp8 nominally +1.5 points); NIAH retrieval is perfect in both arms at every (length, depth) cell — the fp8 indexer scores and fp8 main KV preserve long-context retrieval identically up to 32K. Strict-match is 0.00 in both arms (a CoT answer-format artifact of this task; flexible-extract is the paired metric). At this eval's max-model-len (32768), the same boots hold 3,336,874 → 5,005,312 KV tokens (+49.9%); the headline +33% above was measured at max-model-len 16384 — the capacity metric on current main depends on max-model-len through the concurrency formula, so capacity comparisons are same-len only.
Commands ``` lm_eval --model local-completions \ --model_args model=...,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=16,tokenizer_backend=huggingface,max_gen_toks=2048 \ --tasks gpqa_diamond_cot_zeroshot --seed 0 --apply_chat_template # NIAH: Paul Graham essay haystack, magic-number needle at depth d, # substring-scored; {8192, 16384, 32768} x {0, 25, 50, 75, 100}% x 2 # needles per run, 3 seeded runs per arm. ```
## The concurrency-16 tradeoff (and where the fix work is) Decode throughput is unchanged (110.5-110.6 vs 111.0-111.5 tok/s baseline, 7k context / 512 tokens). At concurrency 16, aggregate throughput is ~6% lower with both flags, stable across host load levels: | config | conc16 aggregate tok/s (×3) | | --- | --- | | bf16 baseline (same session) | 509.0 / 510.1 / 508.4 | | indexer fp8 | 509.1 / 512.1 / 510.6 | | main KV fp8 only | 491.7 / 510.3 / 497.9 | | both fp8 | 464-485 across 6 runs and two load levels | Both flags are opt-in, so this is a capacity-vs-concurrency choice for the operator: +33% KV capacity (more concurrent long-context requests) against ~6% at conc16 on this workload. Where we believe the fix work is: - The `IS_FP8` cast sites in the sparse attention kernel (`amd/ops/qsa.py`): fp8 K is upcast to the query dtype (bf16) before the QK dot and fp8 V to fp16 before the PV dot, per the NVIDIA port's measurements on its own hardware. On gfx950 the fp8 tensor cores are native, so **revisiting native fp8 QK dots on CDNA4** is the first thing to try — the NVIDIA-side comment's "fp8 QK measured slower and less accurate" does not necessarily transfer to this arch. - A concurrency-16 profile of the attention kernel to pin the mechanism (decode is unaffected, so the cost only appears under batch). ## Details - **Flavor design**: the C++ cache-update op selects its fp8 flavor from the platform (`HIP_FP8_TYPE_OCP`: FNUZ on CDNA3, OCP on CDNA4), and the cache is allocated as uint8. This PR reinterprets the cache at the typed boundaries in the same per-arch flavor, so the fused Triton writes, the triton reads, and the C++ unfused-path writes all agree on both arches with zero C++ changes. The `_to_dst_dtype` scale divide covers both flavors (commit 1). - **Cross-arch scope**: validated end-to-end on gfx950 (MI355X). The gfx942/FNUZ leg is design-consistent and kernel-side-unit-validated (the fnuz flavor cells pass), but a serve-level gfx942 run has not been performed; happy to add one on request. - **Known gap**: per-tensor dequant scales are not yet folded into the kernels. Default scales are 1.0 and this checkpoint declares no `kv_cache_scheme`, so it is a no-op today; the NVIDIA port's host-side folding (K scale into the softmax scale, V scale as the output scale) is the follow-up if calibrated scales ever matter. - TP4 notes: the FP8 checkpoint at TP4 on this tree requires `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0` and `--disable-custom-all-reduce` (#60839 automates both fallbacks); with those flags both TP4 arms serve and gate correctly. - ruff check + format clean on all touched files; DCO-signed commits.

title: [Model][DSV4.1] Support MXFP4-packed Engram embedding tables
body:
## Overview

Support DeepSeek-V4.1 checkpoints whose Engram embedding table is stored as MXFP4 (E2M1 nibbles packed two per byte, UE8M0 block-32 scales) instead of FP8. FP8 behavior is unchanged.

## Claims

- A checkpoint with `quantization_config["engram_embed_quant"] = "mxfp4"` now loads: the table is allocated as `[rows, dim // 2]` uint8 and decoded in the lookup kernel.
- The packed table halves the host memory: 12.16 GiB per rank vs 23.60 GiB for FP8 (`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, TP=4).
- GSM8K accuracy of the packed checkpoint matches the FP8 baseline (0.967 vs 0.966), including with `dp_shared_memory`.
- An unknown `engram_embed_quant` value raises instead of being ignored.

## Validation

### End to end (GB300)

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, one GB300 node per run, on `vllm 0.31.1rc1.dev360+g44f0ddfd7` (this PR's base). Compiled ops come from the precompiled wheel for that commit, with this PR's Python overlaid. GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot, chat endpoint, `--max-tokens 4096`.

| Run | Engram table | Parallelism | GSM8K acc. | Invalid | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FP8 baseline | 23.60 GiB per rank (host-pinned) | TP=4 | 0.966 | 0.004 | 1275 |
| MXFP4-packed | 12.16 GiB per rank (host-pinned) | TP=4 | 0.967 | 0.005 | 1218 |
| MXFP4-packed, `dp_shared_memory` | 48.64 GiB shared across 4 DP replicas | DP=4, TP=1, EP | 0.967 | 0.003 | 1299 |

- One run per row. A 0.001 accuracy gap is within noise (about ±0.5 points standard error). tok/s is not a clean comparison (single runs, different parallel layouts).
- DP-shared packed storage (`DPSharedEngramStorage`) loads and serves correctly.
- The FP8 baseline is `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-nvfp4-experts-blend`. I did not check that its expert quantization matches the packed checkpoint's, so the accuracy comparison is not isolated to the Engram table.
- Not covered: long-context and other benchmarks, DP=4 with FP8.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
# Packed, TP=4
vllm serve <packed-ckpt> --served-model-name m --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --language-model-only \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 32

# Packed, DP-shared host table
vllm serve <packed-ckpt> --served-model-name m --port 8000 \
  --data-parallel-size 4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --engram-config '{"dp_shared_memory": true}' \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --language-model-only --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 32

# Eval, against each server
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --use-chat-completions \
  --max-tokens 4096 --save-results gsm8k.json
```

The checkpoint needs `quantization_config["engram_embed_quant"] = "mxfp4"`.
</details>

### Unit and kernel tests

Run on 4xGB300 before the test trim in 1800929afd (which removed the `EngramBatch` skip test and the FP8/THP allocation matrix); not yet re-run after it:

- `tests/kernels/test_engram.py`: 127 passed, 2 skipped (THP without offload).
- `tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py`: 27 passed.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format` are clean.

### Lookup microbenchmark

24 columns, us per lookup (FP8 / packed): host-pinned 8192 tokens 356 / 365; GPU-resident 8192 tokens 115 / 156 (the nibble decode); no extra peak GPU memory.

## Details

- `ParallelEngramEmbedding` takes `packed_fp4`; the row size is `dim // 2` bytes when packed. `DPSharedEngramStorage` and the offload memory log count the packed row size.
- `_engram_lookup_kernel` gets a `PACKED_FP4` constexpr (even column in the low nibble); the block scales are unchanged.
- `EngramBatch.create` returns `None` for packed tables, because the staged exchange carries FP8 rows only.
- `Engram._create_embedding` reads the format from the HF config (default `"fp8"`).
- Limitations:
  - GPU-resident lookup is about 36% slower for packed tables (nibble decode). The deployed host-pinned mode is within 1-3%.
  - `can_share_engram_tables` still sizes `/dev/shm` from the FP8 row size, so it over-estimates by about 2x for packed tables. This is conservative, and I left it out to keep the diff small.
- Existing tests that build layers through `__new__` need a `model_config` stub, which this PR adds.
- Not a duplicate: #58782 (DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 hybrid FP8/MXFP4 quant routing, AMD) changes quant config and weights mapping, not the Engram table path. #60938 also edits `engram.py` and `test_engram.py` (Engram to mHC fusion prototype), so it may conflict textually.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Keep DFlash full-attention layers bidirectional for speculators checkpoints
body:
## Overview

This fixes speculators-format DFlash/DFlash2 checkpoints that have full-attention layers being served with causal full attention. Fixes vllm-project/speculators#1232. It follows up #47745, which is unchanged for all-sliding checkpoints.

## Claims

- Full-attention draft layers in speculators checkpoints are served bidirectionally, the way Speculators trains them, whatever `sliding_window_non_causal` is set to.
- `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16` converted with `speculators convert`: mean acceptance length goes from 3.087 to 3.759 (+22%), with per-request metrics identical to the original head on 32/32 requests.
- No change for all-sliding checkpoints (e.g. the RedHatAI DFlash checkpoints, #47745) or for checkpoints without the flag.

## Validation

**Unit:** `pytest tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_dflash_config.py tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_dspark_config.py`. The new test resolves served per-layer causality through `SpeculatorsConfig.extract_transformers_pre_trained_config` and `_dflash_layer_causal`. It has 6 cases; on `main`, the 3 cases that have full-attention layers and `sliding_window_non_causal: false` fail (all-full `dflash`, mixed `dflash`, mixed `dflash2`). With the 3 existing DSpark config tests, 9/9 pass on this branch.

**End to end** on 1×H100 (vLLM `624a5ddafd` with precompiled kernels, without and with this patch; its causality and config code is identical to this PR's base; transformers 5.17.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130; converted heads from speculators `e83f9d0`), `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, `--speculative-config '{"method": "dflash", "model": <draft>, "num_speculative_tokens": 15}' --per-request-spec-decode-metrics detailed --enforce-eager`. Each run is 32 prompts sent one at a time, greedy, `max_tokens=256`. Output text is identical across runs; only acceptance changes.

| draft | vLLM | accepted / drafted | mean acceptance length |
|---|---|---|---|
| `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16`, original | main | 4889 / 26580 | 3.759 |
| same, converted with `speculators convert --algorithm dflash` (all full, flag `false`) | main | 4508 / 32400 | 3.087 |
| same, converted | this PR (MRV2) | 4889 / 26580 | **3.759**, 32/32 per-request metrics identical to the original |
| same, converted | this PR (MRV1, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) | 4889 / 26580 | **3.759**, 32/32 per-request metrics identical to the original |

## Details

**Root cause.** `update_dflash` sets `dflash_config["causal"] = not sliding_window_non_causal`, and `_dflash_layer_causal` applies an explicit `dflash_config.causal` to every draft layer. In Speculators, that flag only controls sliding-window layers; full-attention layers are always trained bidirectionally (`speculators/models/dflash/attention.py`). The flag's meaning is fixed by how existing checkpoints were trained, and those checkpoints can't be re-trained, so the loader has to match it.

**Fix.** Set `causal=False` only when the flag is true, and otherwise leave it unset. `_dflash_layer_causal` then falls back to "sliding layers causal, full layers bidirectional", which is exactly what Speculators trains:

| layers | `sliding_window_non_causal` | trained | served before | served after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| all sliding | `false` | causal | causal | causal |
| all sliding | `true` / absent | bidirectional | bidirectional | bidirectional |
| all full | `false` | bidirectional | **causal** | bidirectional |
| full + sliding | `false` | full bidirectional, sliding causal | **all causal** | full bidirectional, sliding causal |

**Compatibility.**
- Every consumer of this config goes through `_dflash_layer_causal` / `dflash_has_any_non_causal`: the DFlash model, `gemma4_dspark`, the MRV1 proposer and the MRV2 speculator.
- I checked with `get_config` that `layer_types` from the speculators `transformer_layer_config` reaches the hf_config, so the fallback sees the real layer types.
- DSpark's loader never sets `causal`, so it isn't affected.
- Mixed full + sliding drafts still need MRV2, as before.

**Affected checkpoints.** No published RedHatAI DFlash checkpoint is affected; they are all-sliding with the flag `false`. Affected: z-lab heads converted with `speculators convert`. The same applies to drafts trained natively in Speculators with full-attention layers (`--full-attention-indices`, or an all-full draft config), since `sliding_window_non_causal` defaults to `false` for DFlash. A converter-side mitigation for the all-full case is vllm-project/speculators#1233. Converted checkpoints that already carry a copied top-level `is_causal` are unaffected by this change (it takes precedence); that Speculators converter fix stops writing it.

This is separate from my other open spec-decode PR (#58656). cc @mgoin (DFlash/DFlash2 in both repos; happy for both to be reviewed together) @eldarkurtic (#47745).

title: [Bugfix] Annotate DFlash draft KV cache groups via the trailing-layer rule
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61443: DFlash drafters' KV cache groups were never annotated `is_eagle_group`, so the EAGLE last-block-drop optimization was silently disabled and consumers fell back to the conservative flag-all path. The positional (trailing-layer) detection rule now covers `method="dflash"`.

## Claims

- With `method="dflash"` and `use_eagle_block_drop()` on, the draft group (e.g. a DFlash2 uniform sliding-window group) is flagged `is_eagle_group` when the draft layers register after the target layers.
- No behavior change for other speculative methods; the exact-partition guard still applies before the positional rule fires.

## Validation

- Reproduced with a CPU-only script derived from the issue's repro (GLM-5.3-Flash-shaped hybrid: MLA + Mamba target, 3-layer DFlash2 SWA drafter, BLHNC layout): before the fix, the "no KV cache group could be identified as the draft model's" warning fired and 0 groups were flagged; after the fix, exactly the draft group is flagged and no warning fires. Mamba groups stay unflagged.
- New regression test `test_dflash_draft_group_annotated_by_trailing_layer_rule` fails on unfixed main and passes with the fix.
- `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py -k "eagle or draft or mtp or trailing or unidentifiable"`: 17 passed.
- Full `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py`: 37 passed, 32 failed — the 32 failures are byte-identical on unmodified `main` (verified via a clean worktree): they construct real `ModelConfig`/`VllmConfig`, which requires HuggingFace Hub network access unavailable in this sandbox. My change adds the 1 extra passing test and introduces no new failures.
- No GPU in this environment, so no end-to-end serving eval; coverage is at the planning layer where the annotation logic lives (CPU-only tests).

## Details

**Root cause.** `_annotate_eagle_groups` has two detection rules. Rule 1 (spec-driven) needs `non_causal_multi_token_decode` on the spec — declared only on `MLAAttentionSpec` (set by Kimi-K3 DSpark drafters). Rule 2 (positional: flag the group holding the last registered layer) was gated by `_uses_trailing_mtp_layers`, which returned true only for `method == "mtp"` or DeepseekV4/V4.1 `dspark`. DFlash drafters register their KV layers after the target layers, but their plain GQA `SlidingWindowSpec` layers carry no marker — so neither rule fired, `is_eagle_group` stayed false everywhere, and `KVCacheCoordinator` fell back to flagging *all* groups (which, for hybrids with Mamba, also sweeps Mamba groups into the drop, where align-mode checkpointing never produces the widened lookup window).

**Design decisions / limitations.**
- Chose the issue's option 1 (extend the trailing-layer rule) over option 2 (a spec marker on drafter SWA layers): the rule already exists, is guarded by the exact-partition check, and the diff stays minimal.
- Deliberately **not** extending to `eagle3`: the existing `test_non_mtp_eagle_hybrid_still_warns` (parametrized with `eagle`/`eagle3`/`dspark`) pins the warn behavior for those methods, and the registration-order invariant for eagle3-aux recipes isn't established by a concrete case. That can be a follow-up (likely via the marker approach).
- Function name `_uses_trailing_mtp_layers` kept as-is (private, docstring updated) to keep the diff small.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR references #61443 (`gh pr list --state open --search "61443 in:body"` empty as of 2026-10-14); the issue timeline shows no linked fix PR and the filer did not state one was coming.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimal change to `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_planning.py` (gate extension + docstrings); reuses the existing positional rule and its exact-partition guard; <50 lines added outside tests.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Bug validated on a CPU-only reproducer; regression test added to the existing suite; full planning test file passes. GPU end-to-end eval not run (no GPU in this environment) — noted above.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Lines within the 88-char limit; docstrings updated; no unrelated formatting changes.

title: [DSv4.1][PCP] Enable fixed DSpark and shared Engram storage
body:
## Overview

Enable fixed-verification DSpark on the DeepSeek-V4.1 PCP path from #59857, and add opt-in shared host Engram storage so colocated PCP replicas do not duplicate the same TP head shard. This draft now contains an implementation and four-H20 model validation; broader compatibility and accuracy validation remain pending.

## Claims

- Preserve compressor ring tails across PCP ranks after speculative rejection. Publishing only the newest open row loses states needed when the next step resumes at an earlier accepted position.
- Synchronize replicated draft proposals across PCP ranks. A model trace reproduced different draft tokens despite matching target inputs; the corrected path passed cross-rank checks and the model canary.
- Add `pcp_shared_memory` for CPU-offloaded Engram tables. **Hash heads remain TP-sharded; PCP replicas with the same TP rank share the same weight/scale pages.** This changes storage ownership, not precision, lookup arithmetic or token ownership. It reuses the existing `DPSharedEngramStorage` from #57651.

## Validation

Real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on four H20 GPUs: TP1/PCP4/DP1/EP4, DSpark5, Humming MoE, `fp8_ds_mla`, chunk8192, max-seqs64, eager/synchronous execution, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, APC and SWA bounded replay **off**.

| Validation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Distributed Engram suite, original DP plus PCP2/4 and TP1/2 | 31 passed |
| DSpark configuration suite | 13 passed |
| Focused compressor regression, PCP2/4 with 0/5/9 speculative tokens | 12 passed |
| Fixed GSM8K canary, shared TP1/PCP4 | 32/32, zero HTTP errors/truncations |
| Actual DSpark acceptance | 3900/5695 drafted tokens across 1139 draft rounds; mean 4.424 tokens including bonus |
| Engram physical memory | Two shared backing files, eight rank mappings, total PSS 188.83 GiB |

Private TP1/PCP4 requires approximately 755.33 GiB for four copies of these tables and failed at the container's 650 GiB limit. Shared storage used 188.83 GiB for the tables, with total container peak 218.25 GiB and no OOM. `/dev/shm` was 256 GiB **within** the 650 GiB container limit. The failed private and initial shared-startup runs were retained.

The tests exercise exact private/shared lookup parity, uneven head partitions, different/empty PCP inputs, single-writer visibility, changed/restored graph inputs, failure cleanup and storage lifetime. The draft configuration test confirms that disabling PCP sharing for the PCP1 draft does not modify the target. Storage graph tests do not establish model CUDA Graph support; 32 canary questions are not a comprehensive accuracy evaluation.

<details>
<summary>Initial cold-prefill measurements and reproduction</summary>

65536 input tokens, one output token, concurrency four, eight requests per round with continuously replenished workers, zero cached tokens. Same deterministic random token-ID generator and timing definition in both arms; one calibration then three measured rounds per instance.

| Configuration | Round 1 | Round 2 | Round 3 | Median input tok/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TP2/PCP2, private Engram | 5266.766 | 5270.280 | 5273.134 | 5270.280 |
| TP1/PCP4, shared Engram | 5658.446 | 5665.052 | 5664.641 | 5664.641 |

Median difference: **+7.48%**, a sequential topology/configuration comparison, **not an isolated shared-storage speedup or three independent A/B campaigns**. PCP4's measured range is 0.117% of its median. Calibration samples (excluded) were 5256.846 and 4095.625 tok/s. Private PCP4 had no performance result because it could not start. No PCP4 decode-throughput improvement is claimed. This does not claim to match SGLang: its attention/EP layout, activation precision and bounded-replay setting differ.

Focused test commands in a CUDA vLLM environment with four free GPUs:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py
python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_dspark_utils.py
python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
  -k 'v41_pcp_ring_links or v41_pcp_compressor_preserves'
```

Validated launch settings, with the checkpoint path supplied by the operator:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error \
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --prefill-context-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"pcp_shared_memory":true}' \

```

The runtime used a Python overlay at parent `7908ee8` plus the patch, reusing native extensions and missing runtime files from an `a982` image. It was **not** a clean native rebuild of the full PR head; that validation remains pending. Raw manifests, source hashes, all measurements and failures are retained under run IDs `20261014T034634Z_single_h20-56_tp2-pcp2_dspark5` and `20261014T044752Z_single_h20-56_tp1-pcp4_dspark5` in the experiment archive.

</details>

All applicable pre-commit checks passed except native macOS mypy's pre-existing `mmap.MADV_HUGEPAGE` error, reproduced on the unmodified parent file. Linux-target mypy passed for all five changed production files; the three changed test groups also passed mypy. Final post-GPU edits are a type annotation and the equivalent accelerator synchronization API in the test, with no inference arithmetic changes. Existing Buildkite files cover the extended suites; full-model CI additionally needs the checkpoint and sufficient host memory.

## Details

Stacked on #59857 at `7908ee8906475842ba0ecd1c09eed6d878718f05`; its MoE prerequisite #60946 remains relevant. Review this implementation incrementally against that SHA. The GitHub diff against main includes the parent's commits.

The new option defaults off:

```bash
--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"pcp_shared_memory":true}'
```

For TP2/PCP2, each of two TP head partitions is stored once and mapped by its two PCP replicas. For TP1/PCP4, one full table is mapped by four replicas. Placement/shm checks fail closed. The initial scope requires V4.1, CPU offload, PCP>1, DP=PP=1 and same-host/shared-namespace replicas; it excludes DP sharing and THP combinations. The PCP1 draft receives a copied config with PCP sharing disabled.

No duplicate implementation was found in the refreshed checks. #56107 supplies generic replicated DSpark; #54036's sharded draft context-KV precompute is complementary and is not implemented here. #57195 concerns SP token-owner Engram lookup, whereas this change preserves TP head partitioning and PCP ownership. #61554 (bounded replay) and #61555 (model graphs) remain separate work. See `docs/design/deepseek_v41_pcp_dspark.md` for storage diagrams, constraints and validation details.

title: [DSv4.1][PCP] Enable cold decoder SWA bounded replay
body:
## Overview

Enable DeepSeek-V4.1 cold-prefill decoder SWA bounded replay with PCP by adapting the existing replay batch to PCP's local segments and collective layout. Stacked on #59857 and #61553 (fixed DSpark and optional shared Engram); the GitHub diff against main includes those dependencies. Keep this PR in Draft for broader evaluation and human review. GitHub currently reports merge conflicts against main; dependency/main integration remains pending, and the measured source has not been silently rebased.

## Claims

- Reuse `ReplayBatch`, `InputBatch`, the existing gather kernel, attention builders and PCP process group; no new scheduler, partitioner, kernel or public configuration field.
- Keep each PCP segment's intersection with the request's global scheduled tail, preserve its original owner, agree on padded sizes, and gather retained KV slots in the same rank-major order as their payload. Empty local prefill/decode partitions are dispatched by token count.
- Initial four-H20 cold-prefill measurement: **5,664.64 -> 9,729.21 input tokens/s (+71.75%)** at 64K input, concurrency 4, one output token. The global-tail follow-up measures +4.58% over the previous local-segment-tail implementation (9,302.84 tokens/s). These are sequential comparisons with three within-arm samples, not independent interleaved A/B pairs.

## Validation

**Runtime:** four H20-3e GPUs, TP1/PCP4/DP1/EP4, fixed DSpark5, Humming A16, shared CPU Engram, 8,192-token chunks, max-seqs 64, FP8 DS-MLA KV, eager/MRV2, synchronous scheduling, APC off. `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` remained enabled. The lab reused compiled extensions from its existing a98247ab4 runtime; this is not a clean full native rebuild.

- Three existing replay suites: **27 passed** (10.50 s), including global-tail intersections, retained local slots, empty query partitions, padding, output scattering, prompt-logprobs and existing graph regressions. A separate CPU oracle using the actual PCP partitioner and selection logic passed 900 PCP2/4/8 cases; it does not replace distributed GPU validation. PCP collectives in unit tests are mocked; distributed evidence comes from the real model below, not these mocks.
- Four-rank real model: **32/32 fixed GSM8K canaries**, no HTTP errors or truncated answers; **3,965/5,645 real draft tokens accepted** over 1,129 draft steps.
- **8/8 additional checks:** exact 1,023/1,025-token prompts with replay and full-row prompt-logprobs controls; ragged concurrent 8,191/8,193/16,385/65,537-token prompts followed by natural decode. These are public math questions with neutral context, not a full long-context accuracy evaluation or logit-equivalence test.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy, passed. Tests extend existing CI-wired files; the four-rank checkpoint evaluation was run outside CI. No PCP full-model CUDA Graph claim is made.

**Cold-prefill benchmark:** eight requests per round, four continuously replenished workers, 65,536 input tokens/request, output length 1, temperature 0. Every response reports zero cached tokens. One warmup followed by three formal rounds; all samples retained.

| Input tokens/s | Replay off | Local-segment tail (previous) | Global request tail (current) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Warmup (excluded) | 4,095.62 | 9,255.63 | 9,674.12 |
| Sample 1 | 5,658.45 | 9,302.84 | 9,729.21 |
| Sample 2 | 5,665.05 | 9,301.57 | 9,729.46 |
| Sample 3 | 5,664.64 | 9,303.91 | 9,729.19 |
| Median | **5,664.64** | **9,302.84** | **9,729.21** |
| (max-min)/median | 0.117% | 0.025% | 0.003% |

Launch arguments match except for the replay flag, and input hashes match in all four rounds. The replay-off baseline precedes this patch and a non-executable shared-Engram type annotation; it has not been rerun on the final source. The two replay arms use identical launch arguments, runtime and assigned GPU identity; all input manifests match. Backend autotuning was not explicitly frozen across engine restarts. Independent interleaved A/B repetitions, broader accuracy coverage and PCP2/TP2 performance remain pending. No SGLang-relative or decode speedup is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Validation commands and workload reproduction</summary>

GPU tests executed in the lab's virtual environment:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/work/source /opt/block32/.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -q \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_start.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py
```

The local experiment harness ran `launch_model.py --pcp 4 --spec-tokens 5 --pcp-shared-memory --bounded-replay`, then `probe_model.py --quality-only`, `probe_replay_boundaries.py`, and `probe_prefill_sglang_inputs.py`. The replay-off arm omits `--bounded-replay`. These are validation harnesses retained with the raw artifacts, not new vLLM interfaces.

The equivalent model arguments are:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --served-model-name dsv41-pcp --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"pcp_shared_memory":true}' \
  --max-model-len 131072 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --swa-bounded-replay --no-async-scheduling --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
  --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager --seed 0 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 --moe-backend humming \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --enforce-eager \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}'
```

Each prompt uses Python `random.Random(65536*100000 + 4*1000 + round*100 + request_index)`, then 65,536 `randrange(1000,32000)` token IDs, replacing the first ID with `1000 + request_index`. Rounds are 0..3 (0 is warmup), request indices 0..7. Inputs are prepared before the timer. Four HTTP workers stream completions with `max_tokens=1`, `ignore_eos=true`, `temperature=0` and usage enabled; each worker picks up the next request on completion. Throughput is actual total prompt tokens divided by round wall time. No forced synchronized waves, cached prefixes or profiler are used.

All successful and failed runs, full responses, manifests, input hashes and test logs are retained in the experiment archive. Both the initial real-trim startup failure and the first global-tail empty-decode failure are preserved rather than omitted.
</details>

## Details

PCP presents two local segments per original request and gathers cache slots in rank-major order. Replay metadata therefore needs per-segment capacity, local slot selection before compaction, and a fresh gather after padding to a common size. Two small CPU-group all-reduces recover global scheduled bounds using shared request-state IDs, then agree on whether to trim and the retained size. Empty segments do not contribute to the bounds. They do not read GPU tensors, but add host collectives per preparation. The global tail floor uses a separate UVA staging pool so prefix-layer metadata remains intact. Inputs/indexer buffers are zero-padded and only real output rows are scattered back.

The first real trim at 1,025 tokens exposed lazy attention-builder construction copying an indexer constant to the GPU in the checked hot path. Creating those existing builders during initial metadata startup fixes this without exempting synchronization checks.

The first global-tail model run exposed an empty decode partition with nonzero decode request metadata in a mixed batch. Dispatching FlashMLA prefill/decode by actual token counts fixes the zero-row reshape; outer KV publication and PCP collectives remain intact.

Unlike the previous local-segment-tail implementation, this retains the request's global tail, as motivated by SGLang's decoder CP replay. It preserves vLLM's original zigzag owner rather than adding a new token-layout protocol. Consequently, a single long request's retained tail may concentrate on one rank while peers execute padded work; SGLang's interleave layout distributes it across ranks. Globally short chunks retain the existing replay floor. Targeted canaries do not establish equivalence to replay-disabled logits. Prefix hits, KV transfer, sequence parallelism, microbatching and PCP CUDA Graph integration remain unsupported by the applicable parent guards. Prompt-logprobs requests keep all rows.

Existing #56227/#58132 provide the replay mechanism. #60046 concerns P/D replay endpoints; #58289/#57872 concern encoder-only P/D. This change covers the cold colocated PCP adapter and does not duplicate those implementations. SGLang's decoder bounded replay and CP tail-layout code informed the comparison; the runtime patch reuses vLLM's existing components. The parent MoE padding prerequisite #60946 still applies.

AI assistance was used to implement, review and validate this change with OpenAI Codex. Human line-by-line review and broader model evaluation remain pending; this PR remains a Draft.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Reuses existing replay classes, metadata, collectives and kernels; five incremental production files.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Targeted GPU and real-model validation passed as above; broader model-quality and independent A/B confirmation remain pending.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Applicable pre-commit checks passed; existing tests and design note updated.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Dependencies, results, failed-run diagnosis, methodology limits and AI assistance are explicit.
</details>
