title: [DSv4.1][PCP] Enable decode-only CUDA graphs with fixed DSpark
body:
## Overview

Enable NVIDIA DeepSeek-V4.1 PCP decode-only CUDA graphs by stabilizing graph-read metadata and sizing decode graphs by rank-local requests. Reuses the existing MRV2 graph implementation; prefill and bounded replay remain eager. Stacked on #59857, #61553 and #61554.

## Claims

- Preserve the addresses of gathered SWA positions, compressed cache slots and compressor ring-link metadata across graph replays.
- Use the largest rank-local request count for request-sharded decode graph dispatch, while retaining global input staging.
- Allow only V4.1 `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` on CUDA; speculative graphs require the existing flattened/varlen indexer path. Unsupported configurations retain explicit guards.
- In a small, matched four-H20 experiment, short-question output throughput was **5.22× at c1 and 4.51× at c4** versus eager. This is not a long-context or general throughput claim.

## Validation

Tested parent `9516299b96954da52ce7a7416c08db2b8b9db763` versus the frozen implementation in `b2e6404` (current Python files unchanged at `34c4a21`). Four H20 GPUs, TP1/PCP4/EP4, fixed DSpark5, Humming MoE FP8 activations, dense A16, `fp8_ds_mla`, shared CPU Engram, bounded replay ON, APC OFF, chunk8192, max-seqs64, max-len131072, utilization0.85 and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` in both arms. Same read-only checkpoint mount, native runtime, packages, backend dispatch and inputs. The container's existing native extensions were reused; this was not a clean native rebuild from the candidate commit.

**Fresh sequential Graph → Eager pair**, three measured repetitions per concurrency after separate warmup. Each repetition has the same four natural GSM8K questions (prompt lengths 63/60/78/110 tokens), temperature0, thinking disabled, natural EOS and real speculative acceptance. All measured answers passed; no cache hits or length truncation. Natural output lengths vary. Throughput includes the whole request round; TPOT is first-to-last content latency divided by generated tokens minus one. Reported TPOT is the median of each round's request medians.

| Workload | Eager | Graph | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| c1 output tok/s, median [min–max] | 32.494 [31.889–32.985] | 169.756 [167.900–171.100] | 5.22× |
| c4 output tok/s, median [min–max] | 82.069 [81.581–97.824] | 369.892 [349.078–380.643] | 4.51× |
| c1 TPOT, ms | 29.293 | 5.023 | −82.85% |
| c4 TPOT, ms | 29.936 | 5.631 | −81.19% |
| c1 TTFT, ms | 143.575 | 138.941 | −3.23% |
| c4 TTFT, ms | 294.792 | 284.813 | −3.39% |
| Cold 64K/c4/output1 prefill, input tok/s | 15,255.437 | 15,265.495 | +0.066%; effectively unchanged |

Real accepted/drafted counts over the three decode repetitions:
c1 eager **1614/2385 (67.67%)**, graph **1575/2220 (70.95%)**;
c4 eager **1573/2260 (69.60%)**, graph **1618/2420 (66.86%)**.
Acceptance was neither fixed nor simulated. These results do not establish logit equivalence or unchanged acceptance on a broad corpus.

Both arms passed **32/32** fixed GSM8K canaries, with no HTTP errors or length stops. Graph additionally passed **8/8** long/ragged/replay boundary checks and **27/27** natural-EOS requests through concurrency **1→3→4→5→8→5→1**, including empty owners and changed graph shapes. Runtime target `CUDAGraph Stats` reported FULL execution (1491 counted steps across the recorded log, versus zero for eager). Draft capture completed; this alone is not evidence of draft replay.

Per-card model-load memory was **81.79 GiB** in both arms. Final graph-pool log: **0.21 GiB actual** (0.48 GiB estimated budget; an earlier profiling capture logged 0.44 GiB). Available KV budget decreased **30.79→30.31 GiB**, token capacity **8,959,121→8,818,195**. These are engine memory logs, not a sampled peak-memory comparison. No second weight layout is introduced.

<details>
<summary>All performance samples and reproduction</summary>

| Arm | C | Output tok/s, all 3 samples | Median TPOT ms, all 3 samples | Output lengths (4 requests per sample) |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| eager | 1 | 32.494, 32.985, 31.889 | 28.965, 29.293, 29.329 | 177/165/110/289; 154/165/109/208; 177/165/109/266 |
| eager | 4 | 81.581, 82.069, 97.824 | 30.651, 29.936, 28.765 | 177/160/109/255; 153/165/110/242; 179/160/110/208 |
| graph | 1 | 167.900, 171.100, 169.756 | 5.143, 5.023, 4.963 | 153/165/109/221; 177/160/109/222; 154/160/110/282 |
| graph | 4 | 380.643, 349.078, 369.892 | 5.535, 5.631, 5.902 | 159/165/110/254; 152/165/110/289; 152/160/118/270 |

Cold64K/c4 uses 8 requests per round, continuously replenished workers, output1, exact input hashes and actual cached_tokens=0. One warmup round is excluded; all three formal samples:
- Eager: 15246.559407, 15255.436697, 15261.405470 input tok/s.
- Graph: 15256.233934, 15265.495489, 15274.008424 input tok/s.

Both arms use `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`,
`VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"float8e4m3","allow_fallback":false}'`,
`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, `--moe-backend humming`, and
`--kernel-config '{"enable_jit_warmup":false}'`.
On the same launch configuration, remove `--enforce-eager` and use:
```bash
--compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[5,6,10,12,20,24,40,48],"max_cudagraph_capture_size":48}'
--cudagraph-metrics
```
The experimental ladder covers the tested DSpark5 target/draft batches through global concurrency8. It is not a universal tuning recommendation; unmatched sizes retain existing eager fallback. Both arms used the same kernel-warmup setting and graph metrics.

Raw requests, event timing, Prometheus counters, input manifests, launch arguments, startup backend audits, source hashes, failures and shutdown receipts are retained in the experiment archive. Run IDs:
- `20261014T090251Z_single_h20-56_tp1-pcp4_dspark5_replay_humming-fp8_decode-graph-full`
- `20261014T091437Z_single_h20-56_tp1-pcp4_dspark5_replay_humming-fp8_decode-graph-none`

An independent raw-data audit recomputed timings, token usage, cached tokens, answers, acceptance, input hashes and allowed source/config differences. Decode audit SHA256: `8c4adf1a8173c2e16020eaaca3d0672fbfa0e428cafa1da14d40802dcd1bd5bb`; prefill audit SHA256: `7f9a0bbd8eb6494cbd80d72543e9d11f178660792715497a71eacc233c1e05c3`. The complete raw archive is retained on the test host, not publicly attached.

</details>

**157 selected tests passed**, and all applicable pre-commit checks passed, including Ruff and mypy. Three unchanged Ray-dependent configuration cases failed in the initial wider attempt because Ray was absent; that failure log is retained. The focused rerun explicitly deselected them.

<details>
<summary>Focused test commands</summary>

From the candidate source, with its PYTHONPATH and the existing runtime:
```bash
python -m pytest --noconftest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py \
  -k 'not parallel_config_manages_decode_sharding' # 122 passed, 3 deselected
python -m pytest --noconftest -q tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py \
  -k 'zero_token_pcp_rank or v41_pcp_metadata' # 4 passed
python -m pytest --noconftest -q tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
  -k 'v41_pcp_ring_links or v41_pcp_compressor_preserves_pairs' # 14 passed
python -m pytest --noconftest -q tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py # 17 passed
```

`--noconftest` isolates these focused suites from unrelated optional dependencies. This is not a full repository test run. Existing test areas collect these worker/attention/kernel suites; the full V4.1 PCP4+DSpark FULL model configuration is not currently covered by the standard model CI, so the evidence above was collected externally.

</details>

The performance result is one sequential pair, not several independent AB/BA campaigns. These canaries are not a complete accuracy evaluation. Wider decode contexts/concurrency, repeated order reversals and broader model accuracy remain follow-ups; keep this PR Draft pending human review.

## Details

Simply relaxing the graph guard is unsafe: captured kernels retain temporary compressor/cache metadata addresses, and a global request count mismatches request-sharded decode graph dimensions. This change uses persistent metadata buffers and the existing rank-local token dispatch machinery, adding only the corresponding request count. Global staging still reserves every request. No weight, quantization, acceptance-policy, attention kernel or graph-manager implementation changes.

Incremental production diff: **5 files, +101/−8**. Review against `9516299`; the GitHub diff against main also contains the dependency stack (#59857/#61553/#61554 and the parent's MoE padding prerequisite #60946). Existing V4.1 restrictions remain: PP=DP=DCP=1, no microbatching, KV transfer, APC or MegaMoE, fixed DSpark verification when enabled. Native speculative query metadata unable to refresh empty decode owners remains rejected. Prefill graphs and prefix caching are separate work.

Credit/reuse: merged #53867 supplies generic PCP decode-only FULL graph capture/padding but retained sparse-MLA rejection. #56107 supplies replicated DSpark. #53639 concerns generic rank-local token dispatch with replicated decode. This patch supplies V4.1 metadata stability and request-sharded graph sizing; it does not claim those existing generic optimizations. ROCm #58352 handles different ragged packing. Searches found no exact duplicate of this scoped implementation.

AI assistance was used for implementation, source review and validation.

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Mono MoE on #60683's mono decode, with K2 in plain decode
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

**Draft, stacked on [#60683](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60683) at its head `df3693c8f8`.** Only the top 3
commits belong to this PR; everything below them is #60683. **This PR's changes alone:
[df3693c8f8...kimik3/stack-plain-k2](https://github.com/amd-mghanimi/vllm/compare/df3693c8f8...kimik3/stack-plain-k2)**
(3 commits, 21 files). It puts the mono MoE launch of
[#60793](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60793) on top of #60683's mono decode for Kimi-K3 on MI355X (gfx950),
and adds K2 in plain decode steps so the two work together. The 3 commits:

1. Mono MoE: one launch for a decode MoE layer of up to 32 rows (from #60793).
2. Mono MoE: numerics and path-selection tests (from #60793).
3. Mono decode: K2 in plain decode steps.

**K2 in plain decode steps.** #60683 runs K2 (o_proj, its all-reduce, the MLP AttnRes and the latent MoE) only on
speculative-verify steps. K2 does not depend on how o_proj's input was made, so KDA layers now run vLLM's AttnRes and
KDA up to o_proj's input (`KimiK3DeltaAttention.forward_core`), then K2, as MLA layers already do. A plain decode step
of at most 8 rows takes this path.

**Rebased on #60683 `df3693c8f8` (Oct 16).** The previous head (`4929a0ada8`, on #60683 `a717180301`) had a 4th commit
that merged the mono widths into the resolved CUDA graph sizes. `df3693c8f8` fixes the same capture-size issue in
#60683, so that commit is dropped. The mono MoE now also runs on AITER v0.1.25 and later, which removed
`communication_ops_utils.traced` (ROCm/aiter#6377) and `compile_gemm2_a4w4_port(g2_kstatic=)`. The device helpers use
a local `traced` (`ASTRewriter.transform`, as #60683's own helpers do) and their own `!llvm.ptr` casts, and
`g2_kstatic=True` is passed only where AITER still takes it (v0.1.24.post1, which vLLM's ROCm base image pins). **All
results below were measured at the previous head, on AITER v0.1.24; the current head has not been re-measured yet.**

Steps above 8 rows keep vLLM's layers, with the mono MoE launch (up to 32 rows) for the MoE. Switches: `--monokernel`
(#60683's mono decode, now with plain decode) and `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_MOE=1` (mono MoE), each usable alone.

## Claims

- Speculative decoding (DSpark), 9 to 32 rows per step: as fast as #60683 or faster, never slower beyond noise.
  Measured at the previous head, k = 3: 12 rows -5.7%, 16 rows -4.9%, 20 to 32 rows within 1%. Repeated on the earlier
  base with k = 3 and k = 7: 12 rows -5.7%, 16 rows -2.5% (k = 3) and -5.0% (k = 7), 32 rows 0% (k = 3) and -3.0% (k = 7).
- Speculative decoding, up to 8 rows per step: the same as #60683 (both run #60683's K2).
- Plain decode, 1 to 8 rows per step: median TPOT 1.19x to 1.38x better than stock, measured at the previous head. 12 and 16
  rows: 2% to 3% better; 24 and 32 rows: 0.3% to 0.9% slower than stock, in both runs. #60683 alone refuses plain
  decode.
- Every decode step of at most 8 rows runs #60683's K2 (60,698 of 60,698 counted at the previous head, below), so the
  mono MoE launch only serves steps above 8 rows.

## Validation

`moonshotai/Kimi-K3`, TP8, MI355X, MI355X OOB serving settings, 8k input / 1k output, median TPOT in ms. A step
carries `concurrency` rows in plain decode and `concurrency x (k + 1)` rows with DSpark (TRITON_MLA drafter). Every
request succeeded and no server logged a memory access fault. Negative is faster. Each table compares builds on one
node only.

### At the previous head (`4929a0ada8`, on #60683 `a717180301`)

Both builds on one node, 2 runs per cell (TPOT is the mean of the two). Image: vLLM nightly `5555a2d8` (main
`c077dc663d`, #60683's base, plus 6 commits without compiled-code changes; AITER v0.1.24), with each tree's `vllm/`
Python on top, so the builds run exactly #60683 at `a717180301` and this PR at that head over the same compiled base.
Both use `--monokernel`; this PR adds `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_MOE=1`. #60683 gets an explicit CUDA graph size list (its
capture-size issue, since fixed in #60683 by `df3693c8f8`).

### Repeated runs on the earlier base

4 rows, 1.20x at 8, -3.0% at 12, -2.6% at 16, +0.2% at 24 and +1.0% at 32 (slower in all 3 runs at 24 and 32).

#60683 alone does not start without speculative decoding. Above 8 rows, #60683's MoE cannot run unchanged (its rows
are held in LDS); an earlier #60683 version's standalone MoE launch, chunked into 8-row launches, was 8% to 39% slower
than stock at 12 to 32 plain rows, so this PR uses #60683's MoE (inside K2) up to 8 rows and the mono MoE above.

### Which path steps of at most 8 rows take

Steps of at most 8 rows that K2 declines would fall to the mono MoE instead of #60683's MoE. Counted at the previous head with
vLLM's `monokernel_steps` counter, labelled per step with the graph mode and the row count (a measurement-only copy of
`routing.py`), on this PR's server: 8k / 1k at c1 to c8 plus short requests (256 in / 128 out, 64 requests per
concurrency, frequent arrivals).

| DSpark k=3 | 9,537 | 9,537 | 4,509 full graph, 244 piecewise, 137 eager |
| plain | 51,161 | 51,161 | 250 piecewise, 137 eager |

Every step of at most 8 rows ran K2; the only declined steps had more than 8 rows (prefill and mixed steps, and
speculative steps above K2's widths, which take the mono MoE). The earlier base gave the same counts.

### Tests and accuracy

- At the previous head on MI355X: this PR's mono MoE numerics and gate tests 27 passed; #60683's mono tests 49 passed (44 on

  both trees.
- GPQA Diamond (198 questions, no thinking, 4k tokens, greedy) at the previous head: 0.803 with DSpark k = 3, 0.773 in plain

## Details

- The mono MoE commits are #60793's eleven, squashed into the kernel and its tests and moved beside #60683's
  `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/mono/` (as `mono_moe/`); #60793 itself stays based on main. Its switch is
  `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_MOE` because `--monokernel` turns on the mono decode, which refuses at startup the configs it does not
  serve (TP other than 8, more than 7 speculative tokens, Model Runner V1, piecewise-only graphs); the mono MoE checks
  each layer on its first forward instead and falls back to the multi-kernel path where the launch does not fit.
- On the rebase, `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE` and the fault-injection variables, which #60683 removed, were dropped from

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][NIXL] Support heterogeneous P/D TP for mixed MLA models
body:
## Overview Fixes the NIXL KV-transfer crash when a P/D disaggregated deployment uses **heterogeneous TP** (e.g. prefill TP16 + decode TP8) with a **mixed MLA** model — a model that combines a replicated MLA latent cache with head-sharded attention regions (GLM-5.3 `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` with `sparse_mla_force_mqa`, i.e. MLA + DSA sparse-attention indexer). Extends the per-region classification introduced in #44583 to heterogeneous-TP page geometry. ## Claims - Heterogeneous P/D TP works for mixed MLA models: prefill TP16 + decode TP8 and prefill TP8 + decode TP16 both complete full benchmarks with correct output quality. - Pure-MLA (DeepSeek-class), pure-GQA, and symmetric-TP deployments keep their existing behavior — every change is gated on conditions only hybrid + mixed-TP produce. - Measured on GLM-5.3 785B fp8 (8xH200): `1P×TP16 + 2D×TP8` = 0.81 req/s vs 0.48 req/s for the best symmetric split (**+68%**) — prefill is compute-bound (wider TP wins) while decode is latency-bound (smaller TP group wins); heterogeneous TP lets each role sit at its optimum. ## Validation Live on an 8xH200 cluster, GLM-5.3 785B fp8, full request-load benchmarks per config: - D>P (prefill TP8 + decode TP16): EPP registration 3s, full benchmark, quality ok - D

Failure signature (before the fix) ``` ValueError: Replicated region i=99 local_len=8192 remote_len=16384 (NIXL handshake validation, decode engine, first request) ``` followed, after each layer was fixed in sequence, by descriptor-size mismatches and finally a multi-source read assertion in `pull_worker`. Performance evidence and the full 11-iteration investigation: internal benchmarking on ServeIt Studio (GLM-5.3 asymmetric TP analysis).

title: [Bugfix] Reserve construction-time scratch across workspace slots
body:
## Overview

Reserve construction-time attention scratch in every workspace microbatch/lane slot, so a path first reached after warmup does not try to grow a locked workspace. Addresses the workspace-reservation portion of #61487; HiSparse + DBO state isolation remains separate work.

## Claims

- Construction reservations cover all configured execution slots, including slots not exercised during warmup.
- Runtime requests retain slot-local growth, independent storage, and the existing lock contract.
- Reservations retain no tensor views and use the existing allocation context.

## Validation

Tested on WSL with an RTX 3050 8 GiB, Python 3.12, and an editable precompiled install, based on main at `ec8a372566`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Real FlashInfer/TRTLLM prefill-constructor regressions on unmodified production code | Both fail with the locked-workspace allocation error |
| Workspace, microbatch runner, and prefill registry suites with the patch | 67 passed; ROCm AITER module skipped on NVIDIA |
| All applicable pre-commit checks, including Ruff, mypy, and CI test wiring | Passed |

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_registry.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py -q
```

Coverage includes CPU/CUDA slot isolation, simultaneous-view alignment, locked capacity, peer-storage stability during runtime growth, CUDA graph capture/replay, and real prefill constructor reservations. No full-model multi-GPU serving or ROCm kernel validation was performed; this PR does not claim that the original HiSparse serving repro is fixed.

## Details

Constructors run in microbatch 0, so their previous `get_simultaneous` calls only sized that slot. Other slots could subsequently request the same scratch after locking and fail. `WorkspaceManager.reserve` sizes each slot with the same per-tensor alignment as runtime allocation. Construction call sites use this API; forward calls continue to use `get_simultaneous`, avoiding replacement of storage another microbatch may still be using.

This allocates required scratch for every configured slot before profiling, so memory accounting includes slots that warmup misses. Single-slot configurations retain the same capacity. The API is intended for construction before execution or graph capture, when no slot holds scratch views.

Updated reservations cover FlashMLA sparse, Triton MLA, AITER MLA, TurboQuant, FlashInfer/TRTLLM prefill, B12x, and Dots3Note. HiSparse staging from #60424 is not in this base and should adopt the API when integrated.

Duplicate checks found no open PR implementing construction-time reservations across all slots. Related #60734 addresses shared DSA top-k state; #48179 sizes MoE scratch. Neither implements this fix. The separate HiSparse state-sharing and zero-row-write problems described in #61487 remain unresolved by this PR.

title: [Core][Spec Decode] Lookahead block hashes for EAGLE prefix caching
body:
## Overview

Part 1 of 2 split from vllm-project/vllm#50897 (implements vllm-project/vllm#50438): **lookahead block hashes** for the local prefix cache. EAGLE-family drafters write the draft KV at a block's last position from the token after the block, so `main` drops the last matched block on every hit. This PR puts that token into the block hash and removes the drop when no KV connector is configured. KV connector support is in the stacked PR (part 2).

## Claims

- Local prefix-cache hits with EAGLE, EAGLE3, MTP, DFlash and DSpark reach `floor((N - 1) / B) * B`, the same as without speculative decoding, instead of one cache unit less (544–1600 tokens on hybrid attention + Mamba/GDN models).
- A block is reused only when its lookahead token matches, so a hit reads the same draft KV as a cold run.
- New `SpeculativeConfig.disable_lookahead_block_hashes` restores `main`'s behavior. With any KV connector configured, this PR keeps the legacy hashes.
- Model runners are unchanged; no new CPU/GPU synchronization.

## Validation

Unit tests on this branch (CPU, local):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/core tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py \
  --ignore tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py -k "not ray"
```

Result: 1,184 passed. `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` is excluded because it launches the `vllm` CLI and needs a GPU node.

End-to-end and draft-KV results from the combined PR (vllm-project/vllm#50897, earlier revision; not yet re-run on this split):

| Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B, MTP k=4, 1x GB200, `prefix_repetition` | `main` | lookahead hashes |
|---|---|---|
| Prefix-cache hit rate | 72.7% | **85.0%** |
| Request throughput | 9.09 req/s | **12.43 req/s** |
| Mean / median TTFT | 404 / 304 ms | **318 / 226 ms** |
| GSM8K 5-shot | 0.4359 | 0.4359 |

Hit length, Qwen3.5-2B + MTP k=1, unit 544, 1,367-token prompt sent twice: `main` without spec decode 1088, `main` with MTP 544, lookahead hashes 1088.

Draft-KV check (KV of the hit blocks vs a cold run, bf16 max abs diff): Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3 0.09–0.14 (negative control with a stale lookahead token: 7.55); Qwen3.5-2B MTP 0.19 (control: 14.53).

TODO before review: re-run `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py`, `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` and the benchmark on GPU.

## Details

**Enablement.** `is_lookahead_block_hashing_enabled` (`v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`) requires `use_eagle_block_drop()`, `not disable_lookahead_block_hashes`, `num_prefill_lookahead_tokens == 1`, no HiSparse, prefix caching on, and no KV transfer config. Part 2 replaces the last condition with a per-connector capability.

**Hashing.** `get_request_block_hasher(..., use_lookahead_block_hashes=True)` hashes a block ending at `e` only once token `e` is in `all_token_ids`, with `(block_keys, token_e, token_e_keys)` as extra keys. All KV cache groups share these hashes. KV events carry the same extra keys.

**Caching.** Blocks are cached at allocation, as without lookahead hashes; `SingleTypeKVCacheManager.cache_blocks` stops at the last hashed block. At request finish, `update_from_output` caches the block whose lookahead token is the last sampled one.

**Drop removal.** The scheduler clears `use_eagle_block_drop`. `KVCacheCoordinator.drop_eagle_group_ids` is empty in this mode and drives the per-group drop and `replay_boundaries`, so the last-block drop, the Mamba checkpoint back-off and the replay-boundary shift are all skipped from one place. `eagle_group_ids` stays, since `mamba_shared_prefix_checkpoint` still applies.

**Why it is correct.** The drafter writes the draft KV at `e - 1` (input `(h_{e-1}, token e)`) in the step that prefills or samples token `e`. The hash exists only once token `e` is in `all_token_ids`, which never holds draft or in-flight tokens, so a cached block's draft KV is written by the end of that step.

**Limitations**

- Multi-module MTP (`num_nextn_predict_layers > 1`) keeps the block drop: module j at position p reads token p + j.
- HiSparse keeps the block drop; it is not validated with lookahead hashes yet.
- Hybrid models lose the hit when a prompt diverges exactly at the producer's last retained Mamba boundary (0 vs one unit on `main`); see vllm-project/vllm#50897 for the reproducer.
- KV event extra keys become `(block_keys, lookahead_token_id, lookahead_keys)` in this mode, with no field marking the scheme.

<details><summary>Duplicate-work check</summary>

Split from vllm-project/vllm#50897 by the same author. No other open PR adds the successor token to the prefix-cache key (vllm-project/vllm#44986, vllm-project/vllm#45614, vllm-project/vllm#48375 and vllm-project/vllm#39171 change when the drop applies, not the key).

</details>

title: [ROCm] Default AITER on for CDNA3+ when the package is installed
body:
## Summary
- When `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` is unset, vLLM now turns AITER on only if the package is installed and the GPU is CDNA3 or newer (MI300, MI355). NVIDIA, MI250, and machines without AITER stay on the current path.
- Explicit `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0` still opts out. `=1` still forces it on. Recipes on supported GPUs no longer need to export `=1`.
- A partial AITER install that cannot do non-causal MLA now reports unsupported instead of raising, so backend selection can fall through to Triton MLA.

## What this does not close
This is a draft. Do not merge until AMD CI is green with the new default.

- An AITER kernel that passes the support check and then faults at runtime is still a crash. The known gfx942 case is non-causal MLA reaching `cannot get heuristic kernel!` when the backend is selected anyway. Selection now rejects that case when `supports_non_causal()` is false, but other shape or arch gaps inside AITER are not covered.
- Custom allreduce, RMSNorm, GEMM, and the fusions whose sub-flags already default on will follow the master switch. Numerics change for recipes that were calibrated on the Triton path and did not pin `--attention-backend` or `--moe-backend`.
- Explicit `--attention-backend` and `--moe-backend` still win. FP8 MoE that is explicitly requested with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` and is unsupported still fails the same way it does today. Omitting the variable uses the existing try-next-backend loop.
- unified attention, shared-expert fusion, sparse MLA, Triton RoPE, FP4 ASM GEMM, and HIPBMM stay default-off.

## Test plan
- [ ] `tests/rocm/test_aiter_default_on.py`: explicit 0/1, unset without AITER, unset on CDNA3, unset on MI250
- [ ] `test_missing_causal_arg_fails_closed` expects False instead of RuntimeError
- [ ] AMD CI on MI300 and MI355 with the variable unset: MLA, MoE, and a recipe that previously set `=1`
- [ ] Confirm `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0` still matches today's off path
- [ ] Confirm a recipe that pins `--attention-backend TRITON_MLA` does not switch

title: [XPU] Add Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) model architecture support
body:
# [XPU] Add Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) model architecture support

  Adds the `xpu/` sibling to the existing `amd/` and `nvidia/` implementations under
  `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/`, routed through the existing platform dispatch. It reuses
  `Qwen3NextAttention`, `QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention` and `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock`, so
  it is much smaller than the other two backends.

  **Changes outside the model package**

  - `speculator.py` / `llm_base_proposer.py` - the MTP hidden buffer was widened via
    `hc_mult` (the DeepSeek-V4 spelling). Qwen4Exp calls it `hc_count`, so the `getattr`
    fell back to 1 and the MTP head got an un-widened buffer. Both names now accepted.
  - `inc_wna16_linear.py` - guard the `qzeros` copy, which can be empty or mismatched
    under symmetric group quantization and crashed weight load on the 512 routed experts.

  **`layer_types`** - Transformers v5.18 renames `full_attention` to `indexed_attention`;
  all three spellings map to the dense GQA block here. This does not branch on
  `indexer_n_heads` like `amd/`/`nvidia/` do: on `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16` that field is
  set (`4`) but the checkpoint ships no indexer tensors, so keying off it would pick a QSA
  path the weights cannot feed.

  **Known limitations** - no QSA/indexer path on XPU (such checkpoints fail at weight load
  rather than silently running dense attention); TP=4 needs `--enable-expert-parallel`
  (`moe_intermediate_size=640 / 4 = 160` is not divisible by `group_size=128` - checkpoint
  arithmetic, not an XPU limit); requires `transformers >= 5.16.1`, same as the other
  backends; TP=4 validated with `--enforce-eager` only.
  
**model** - https://huggingface.co/devan-carlin/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16

title: [Bug]: enable_tower_connector_lora: get_mm_lora_token_counts() under-sizes punica wrappers in 8 models (startup/runtime token_lora_mapping asserts)
body:
## Summary

While validating tower/connector LoRA for Voxtral (#45697), the e2e run crashed at engine
init inside encoder-cache profiling with punica's
`assert token_lora_mapping.size(0) == M` (`vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_shrink_op.py:291`).
Root cause there: the `mm_kwargs=None` sizing path of `get_mm_lora_token_counts()` returned
the raw encoder budget, but profiling batches maximum-size items whose per-item counts are
chunk-padded, so the rows through the wrapped connector exceeded the punica wrapper's
buffer (evidence: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45697#issuecomment-6155052085,
fixed in that PR by chunk-ceiling the bound).

That is a bug *class*, not a one-off. I swept all implementations of
`get_mm_lora_token_counts()` on `main` (26 in `vllm/model_executor/models/` + 1 in
`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/`), checked each model's sizing branch against its processor's
dummy/profiling items and its tower/connector forward, and found **8 models where the rows
actually flowing through LoRA-wrapped tower/connector linears can exceed the wrapper budget
computed from the sizing branch** — same assert, at engine init or on the first unlucky
batch. 4 further implementations are dead code (class flag unset), and the remaining 10 are
provably safe (details below).

## Mechanism

- Sizing (engine init): `LoRAModelManager` sizes the shared tower and connector punica
  wrappers from `get_mm_lora_token_counts(modality, mm_kwargs=None,
  num_mm_embeds=encoder_budget)` — `vllm/lora/model_manager.py:280-323`. Let `B` be the
  encoder budget (`MultiModalBudget.get_encoder_budget()`, typically
  `max_num_batched_tokens`, floor `max_tokens_per_item`).
- Runtime: for every scheduled encoder item the hook is called with the item's real
  `mm_kwargs` and its placeholder count, and the per-item counts are concatenated into the
  tower/connector `LoRAMapping` — `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/mm/lora.py:55`,
  `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:2852`.
- The scheduler budgets encoder items in **placeholder-embed currency** (`Σ embeds ≤ B`),
  but the wrapped linears run in **row currency** (padded chunks, CLS tokens, batch-max
  padding, pre-unpad tiles). Whenever a legal batch's rows exceed the wrapper buffer, the
  kernel metadata can't cover `M` and the assert fires. Engine-init profiling runs
  `max_items_per_batch = min(B // max_tokens_per_item, decoder caps)` identical max-size
  items, so an under-sized bound can crash before any request (the Voxtral case).

So a sizing implementation is only correct if it upper-bounds the rows of **any**
schedulable batch — `Σ embeds ≤ B` with up to `max_num_seqs × limit_per_prompt` items — not
just `N` identical max-size items. Several implementations return the raw budget (or miss
fixed per-item overheads), which is exactly the Voxtral failure mode.

(Kernel semantics, for precision: `meta_args()` slices the prepared mapping buffer to the
layer's row count `M` (`lora_kernel_metadata.py:198`), so `M >` wrapper buffer is a hard
assert, while a *mapping* that undercounts rows ≤ buffer silently applies stale adapter
indices to the uncounted rows — a correctness bug rather than a crash. Both appear below.)

## Affected models

### 1. Ultravox — short-audio batches overflow tower and connector

`ultravox.py:741-762`. With tower/connector LoRA, every chunk's mel input is padded to the
tower's full context (`pad_audio_to_max_context`, `ultravox.py:653-662`), so each chunk
contributes a fixed **1500 tower rows / 188 connector rows** regardless of its placeholder
count, while a short audio's placeholder count is tiny (~7 embeds per second). The sizing
branch bounds chunks by `ceil(B / 188)`, which only covers batches of *full* chunks.

Arithmetic (`B = 8192`): tower buffer `= ceil(8192/188) · 1500 = 66 000`. Forty-five
1-second audios: `Σ embeds ≈ 315 ≤ 8192` (schedulable), tower rows `= 45 · 1500 = 67 500 >
66 000` → assert. Connector: `45 · 188 = 8460 > 8272`. At `--max-num-batched-tokens 2048`
the threshold is **12 concurrent short audios** (`12 · 1500 = 18 000 > 11 · 1500`). This is
an ordinary ASR serving load.

### 2 & 3. Qwen3-ASR and Qwen3-Omni (audio) — `conv_out` runs on chunk-padded rows

Hook: identity (`qwen3_asr.py:678-691`; `qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py:2361-2374`, audio
branch). The shared `Qwen3OmniMoeAudioEncoder` splits mel input into 100-frame chunks and
pads the tail chunk to 100 before the conv stack; `conv_out` (a `ReplicatedLinear`, i.e.
LoRA-wrapped) runs on the **padded** `[chunks, 13, …]` tensor →
`13 · total_chunks` rows per item (`qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py:460-520`). Placeholders count
only valid positions: `13 · full_chunks + f(tail)` (`qwen3_asr.py:175-182`), so every
non-whole-second audio contributes up to 12 rows of slack that the identity bound ignores.
(The transformer and `proj1/proj2` run on the unpadded gather, so those match embeds.)

Arithmetic (`--max-num-batched-tokens 2048`, so `B = 2048`): ~1.01 s audios (101 mel
frames) give 14 embeds but `2 · 13 = 26` `conv_out` rows. 79 such audios: `Σ embeds = 1106 ≤
2048`, rows `= 2054 > 2048` → assert. At `B = 8192` the same overflow needs ~316 items, i.e.
`max_num_seqs > 256`. Engine-init profiling survives only because the dummy audio is
exactly 30 s (3000 frames, a whole number of chunks).

### 4. Gemma4-MM (audio) — tower/connector run on batch-max-padded rows

Hook audio branch returns per-item `ceil(frames/4)` from the item's own (unpadded) features
(`gemma4_mm.py:2299-2305`); sizing returns the raw budget (`tower = connector =
num_mm_embeds`). But `_process_audio_input` re-pads all items in the encoder batch to the
batch max before the tower, and `embed_audio` (the connector) runs on that padded tensor —
padding is stripped only afterwards (`gemma4_mm.py:1579-1604`). Both modules contain
vLLM linears (`recursive_replace_linear` at `gemma4_mm.py:1125`; `Gemma4MultimodalEmbedder`
at `gemma4_mm.py:1119`), so both are LoRA-wrapped.

With one max-length audio (`E` embeds) batched alongside `k` short audios, the wrapped
modules see `(k+1) · E` rows while the scheduler only accounted `E + Σ eᵢ ≤ B` — for
`k ≳ B/E` the wrapper overflows and the assert fires. Below that threshold the problem is
still there, just silent: the per-item mapping (`Σ ceil(fᵢ/4)`) is shorter than the padded
`M` of any heterogeneous batch, so the padding rows pick up stale adapter indices. The
hook's per-item signature cannot express batch-max padding at all.

### 5. LLaVA — CLS token missing from the tower bound

Hook: identity (`llava.py:733-736`). vLLM's CLIP tower prepends a class embedding
(`clip.py:324`), so each 336² image runs **577** tower rows against 576 embeds. Overflow
when `(B // 576) · 577 > B`, i.e. whenever `B mod 576 < B // 576` — e.g.
`--max-num-batched-tokens 5760`: profiling runs 10 items → `5770 > 5760` → **crash at
engine init**. The default `B = 8192` escapes by residue (`8078 < 8192`). (The pixtral-HF
vision variant has no CLS and is fine.)

### 6. LLaVA-NeXT — sizing ignores tiles, CLS and un-padding

Runtime counts are exact (`tiles · 577` / `tiles · 576`, `llava_next.py:612-629`), but the
`mm_kwargs=None` branch returns `(B, B)`. Anyres un-padding makes placeholder counts
*smaller* than tile rows for non-square images, so row/embed ratios up to ~1.9 are legal.
Verified against the real HF processor (`llava-hf/llava-v1.6-mistral-7b-hf`):

| image | tiles | embeds | tower rows | connector rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 672×672 (dummy) | 5 | 2928 | 2885 | 2880 |
| 336×500 | 3 | 1476 | 1731 | 1728 |
| 500×336 | 3 | 1464 | 1731 | 1728 |

Five 336×500 images: `Σ embeds = 7380 ≤ 8192`, tower `5 · 1731 = 8655 > 8192`, connector
`8640 > 8192` → assert. Profiling is safe only because the square dummy's ratio happens to
be < 1.

### 7. LLaVA-NeXT-Video — CLS token again

`llava_next_video.py:496-520` inverts the 2×2 pooling (`frames · 576` tower rows) but CLIP
runs `frames · 577`. Tower buffer `= (8192 // 144) · 576 = 32 256`; seven 8-frame videos:
`Σ embeds = 8064 ≤ 8192`, rows `= 56 · 577 = 32 312 > 32 256` → assert on any
budget-saturating video batch.

### 8. BLIP-2 — sizing branch asserts on the budget itself

`blip2.py:689-706` does `assert num_mm_embeds % num_query_tokens == 0` on the **budget**.
Any config where `B` isn't a multiple of 32 (e.g. `--max-num-batched-tokens 5000`) raises
`AssertionError` *inside wrapper sizing* at engine init. The bound should floor instead
(`B // 32` items), as InternVL does.

## Safe implementations (for contrast — these get it right)

- **InternVL / H2OVL / Mllama4 / Idefics3**: tiles are uniform, embeds are exact per-tile
  multiples, and the CLS (+1) is accounted (`internvl.py:906-918`,
  `mllama4.py:1255-1268`) — `Σ rows ≤ bound` holds for every legal batch.
- **Qwen2-VL / Qwen2.5-VL / Qwen3-VL / Qwen3-Omni (vision) / GLM-4.1V / Keye / dots.ocr /
  Pixtral (native)**: varlen ViTs (no CLS, no batch padding) with processor-enforced
  merge-divisible grids, so `tower = merge² · embeds` is exact.
- **Gemma3 / PaliGemma**: fixed-size SigLIP crops, exact ratios.
- **LFM2-VL, DeepSeek-V4 VL**: varlen towers; bounds can only over-provision.
- **Gemma4-MM (image)**: sizing already ceils to whole soft-token groups.

Inert (hook implemented but `supports_tower_connector_lora` is not set, so nothing sizes or
maps today): `bailing_moe_v3_vl`, `cohere_compass`, `moondream3`, `openvla`. Note if
Moondream3's flag is ever flipped, its overlapping-crop encoder (729 rows per crop vs a
fixed 730-embed placeholder) overflows immediately — worth a comment before anyone enables
it.

## Proposed fixes

Short term, per model (mirroring the Voxtral fix, #45697 commit c553427):

1. **BLIP-2**: replace the assert with floor division. One-liner.
2. **LLaVA / LLaVA-NeXT-Video**: account the CLS token in the sizing bound
   (`(B // per_item_embeds) · (per_item_rows)`), like InternVL's `+1`.
3. **LLaVA-NeXT**: bound by worst legal row/embed ratio from the grid config instead of raw
   `B` (or `max_tiles · 577 · (B // min_embeds_per_item)`).
4. **Ultravox**: slack-aware bound. Per batch, `Σ ceil(eᵢ/188) ≤ B/188 + num_items`, so
   sizing with `(ceil(B/188) + max_num_seqs · limit_per_prompt)` chunks (× 1500 tower / 188
   connector rows) is sound. (Voxtral is immune to this variant because its placeholder
   counts are themselves chunk-padded — every item's embeds are a multiple of 375.)
5. **Qwen3-ASR / Qwen3-Omni audio**: move the valid-position gather *before* `conv_out`
   (it is a per-position linear, so masking first is semantics-preserving) — then rows ==
   embeds and the identity bound becomes exact.
6. **Gemma4 audio**: strip padding before `embed_audio` (also per-position). The HF-side
   tower's internal batch padding can't be expressed per-item, so it needs either an
   unpadded path or a batch-aware bound.

Longer term, central (this keeps recurring — see also the open per-model hook PRs #53149,
#58658, #54832, #51949, #61470 which reviewers must re-check for the same conditions):

- **Document the contract** on `get_mm_lora_token_counts()` (`interfaces.py:426`): the
  runtime path must return exactly the flattened rows entering wrapped modules *including
  every padding the forward introduces*, and the `mm_kwargs=None` path must upper-bound
  **any** schedulable batch (`Σ embeds ≤ num_mm_embeds`, item count ≤
  `max_num_seqs × limit`), not just identical max-size items.
- **Fail with context instead of a triton assert**: at mapping-build time
  (`gpu/mm/lora.py`, `gpu_model_runner.py`) check `Σ rows` against the wrapper budget and
  raise a descriptive error naming the model and hook.
- Optionally, size wrappers centrally as `max_items_per_batch × hook(dummy max item)`
  (always sound, costs buffer memory), or teach the encoder scheduler to budget in tower-row
  currency. Happy to hear which direction the maintainers prefer.

I'm glad to send the per-model fixes as one or two PRs (with CPU-runnable regression tests
pinning each model's profiling/batch-shape case, in the style of the Voxtral tests in
#45697) once there's agreement on the approach.

## How this was found / validated

Code analysis of all 27 hook implementations on `main` (commit 8a8e2baa02), cross-checked
against each model's processor dummy-input builder and tower/connector forward; LLaVA-NeXT
numbers validated by running the real HF processor on CPU; the Voxtral instance of the
class was reproduced and fixed on an A100 in #45697. No other GPU repros were run — the
arithmetic above says exactly which batch shapes trip each model, and I can run targeted
repros on request. Analysis was AI-assisted; all findings were manually reviewed against
the cited code.

title: [Attention][DCP] Support DCP on the FlashMLA sparse bf16 KV path
body:
## Overview

Enables decode context parallelism (DCP) for `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` with a bf16 KV cache. Until now the bf16 path raised `NotImplementedError` under DCP.

Related: #46514 (DCP for the `fp8_ds_mla` mixed-batch path, which added the bf16 guard), #61285 (`a2a` comm backend for the same backend).

## Claims

- `--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16` with `--decode-context-parallel-size > 1` now runs on `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`. On Hopper, no other sparse MLA backend supports DCP.
- GSM8K accuracy matches DCP1: 0.904 at DCP4 vs 0.894 at DCP1 on GLM-5.3-Flash.
- bf16 is not bound by the fp8 DCP limits (mixed-batch only, head envelope). For example, 32 local heads at DCP4 and 16 at DCP8 are accepted.
- On GLM-5.3-Flash, DCP4 holds 1.40× the KV tokens of DCP1.

## Validation

**Setup.** One GH200 node, 4× GPUs (96 GB, SM90). `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, TP4, `--quantization fp8` (weights only; the KV cache stays bf16).

**Unit tests.** `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k dcp`: 10 passed, 3 of them new.

**GSM8K.** `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 500 questions, 5-shot, greedy, seed 42, CUDA graphs on. Both runs set `sparse_mla_force_mqa`, so prefill rows also take the changed path; otherwise GSM8K prompts (shorter than `index_topk`) would go to dense MHA and only decode would be tested.

| DCP | Accuracy | Invalid | Output tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.894 | 0.000 | 833 |
| 4 (`ag_rs`) | 0.904 | 0.000 | 726 |

The difference is within the ~1.3-point standard error at n=500.

**KV-cache capacity.** Same per-rank KV memory budget in each row.

| Mode | DCP1 tokens | DCP4 tokens | Ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| eager | 225,475 | 315,665 | 1.40× |
| CUDA graphs | 216,892 | 302,557 | 1.39× |

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

```bash
# DCP1: drop the three DCP flags on the second line
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 4 --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4 --dcp-comm-backend ag_rs \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE \
  --attention-config '{"sparse_mla_force_mqa": true}' \
  --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 --port 8000

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 \
  --num-questions 500 --num-shots 5 --max-concurrency 64 --seed 42
```

- `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4`: required by GLM-5.3-Flash's indexer KV compression (`compress_ratio=4`) under DCP.
- `--max-num-seqs 128`: keeps the per-request state blocks within memory for CUDA graph capture.

</details>

## Details

- **Root cause.** Under DCP each rank holds a shard of the KV cache, but the indexer emits global token ids. The bf16 path converted them with `triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index`, which treats every index as local, so it would read slots owned by other ranks. #46514 enabled DCP for fp8 only and added a guard rejecting bf16.
- **Fix.** `_forward_bf16_kv` converts top-k with `triton_filter_and_convert_dcp_index`, as the fp8 path and the sparse MLA base already do. Its compacted output and valid counts map directly onto `flash_mla_sparse_fwd`'s `topk_length`.
- **Empty rows.** For a row where this rank owns none of the selected tokens, `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` returns `lse=+inf` (FlashMLA `tests/ref.py`). Those rows are set to `-inf`, the identity of the cross-rank merge, as the fp8 path does. The output is made contiguous for the combine.
- **Guards.** The bf16 kernel returns the LSE for every token and pads the gathered heads itself, so the builder's mixed-batch and head-envelope checks now apply to fp8 caches only. PCP+DCP with bf16 and HiSparse+DCP are still rejected.
- **Cost.** bf16 KV is ~1.75× the size of `fp8_ds_mla`, so fp8 stays preferable where its DCP path applies. This PR covers the configs it rejects and deployments that need a bf16 cache.
- **Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs and issues for "DCP FlashMLA sparse bf16" and "DCP sparse bf16 fp8_ds_mla". #54541 touches the same conversion but backports to v0.28.0, which predates #46514's guard.
- **Tests.** `test_bf16_dcp_skips_fp8_guards` covers the builder and `test_bf16_dcp_filters_topk_and_neutralizes_empty_rows` covers the forward path, both in `test_sparse_mla_backends.py`.

---

title: [Bugfix] Read step-start seq_lens without holding the CUDA driver context lock
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61621. Step-start `seq_lens` reads in attention metadata builders use `.cpu()` into pageable memory. While that copy waits for the previous step's GPU work, libcuda holds its context lock, so CUDA calls from every other thread in the process stall until the forward pass ends. This PR reads into pinned memory and waits on an event instead.

## Claims

- New `sync_copy_to_cpu()` in `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py`: pinned destination, `copy_(non_blocking=True)`, then a blocking `torch.cuda.Event` record + synchronize on the current stream. Falls back to `.cpu()` for non-CUDA tensors or without pinned memory.
- Used at the three step-start reads: `FlashInferMetadataBuilder.build()` (spec decode, or no `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound`), `FlashInferMLASparseSM90Builder._kv_lens_host()` (no upper bound), and `make_local_attention_virtual_batches()`.
- The host waits for the same work as before, so the step's implicit host/device barrier is kept (see #61239). Only the driver lock is no longer held while waiting.
- In a stock engine (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, FlashInfer, MRV2, async scheduling, EAGLE3 k=3, H100), another thread's `cuEventRecord` was blocked 5.68 s / 5.64 s out of 14.7 s before this change and 1.20 s / 1.21 s after. Wall time is unchanged.

## Validation

All runs on one H100 80GB HBM3 (driver 595.91.07, torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0) in the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-77154ca61` image, whose touched files match this PR's base. Changed files were copied over the installed package for the "after" runs.

Unit test (GPU, H100, before the warm-up was added to the test; see the GB10 re-run below):

```text
$ pytest tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py -k "sync_copy_to_cpu or async_tensor_h2d"   # 3 runs
3 passed, 35 deselected in 5.60s
3 passed, 35 deselected in 5.63s
3 passed, 35 deselected in 5.58s
$ pytest tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py
38 passed in 9.36s
```

Mutation check: with the helper body replaced by `return t.cpu()`, the new test fails at `assert not copy_done.is_set()` (the side thread's launch waited for the copy).

Re-verified after rebasing onto `8a8e2baa0` (head `d2be95f5e988`) on GB10 (aarch64, driver 580.82.09) in `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-77154ca6116ae34cbfe314beef1016bde9b63989`, whose four touched product files are byte-identical to `8a8e2baa0`. Results: full `tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py` 38 passed, the new test 3/3 passed (and 20/20 in a loop), the mutation failed 3/3, and the torch-only repro from #61621 showed 1180 ms with `.cpu()` vs 0.1-0.2 ms with pinned + event.

The GB10 run also showed the test needs a warm-up: without one, the first `add_` launch in the process lazily loads its kernel module, and that load waits for the queued GPU work, so the test failed 6/12 with `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=LAZY` and 0/12 with `EAGER`. The test now launches the side kernel and calls the helper once before timing anything.

End to end: `repro_engine.py` from #61621 (in-process engine, a side thread timing `cuEventRecord` on its own non-blocking stream every 2 ms, 3 rounds of 32 x 3000-token prompts, 256 output tokens, two runs each):

| | spec decode | side thread blocked (calls > 1 ms, summed) | calls > 5 ms | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, before | EAGLE3 k=3 | 5.68 s / 5.64 s | 25 / 20 | 14.7 s |
| main, after | EAGLE3 k=3 | 1.20 s / 1.21 s | 11 / 10 | 14.7 s |
| v0.30.0, before | none | 5.40 s / 5.43 s | 24 / 19 | 15.8 s |
| v0.30.0, after (same change backported) | none | 1.17 s / 1.13 s | 12 / 3 | 15.8 s |

The remaining ~1.2 s is a few long stalls with the engine thread in the forward pass (`linear`). They are the same on main without spec decode, where this builder path is not reached (1.84 s), so they are not from these reads.

Pre-commit (`pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD`, Python 3.12 container): ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy, check-test-tethering, SPDX, forbidden imports, torch.cuda call check and the other applicable hooks passed.

Not validated: the SM90 sparse MLA builder and `make_local_attention_virtual_batches` (chunked local attention) paths were not run end to end, since this hardware run had no model that uses them. The change there is the same one-line swap. Not tested on ROCm, where `t.is_cuda` is also true and the pinned + event path is taken. Other devices fall back to `.cpu()`.

## Details

Root cause: a synchronous `cudaMemcpy` D2H into pageable memory waits for the stream's earlier work while holding the CUDA context lock. Any other thread that enters the driver blocks for the rest of that wait (measured here: kernel launch and `cuEventRecord`), even on an idle non-blocking stream. `cudaEventSynchronize` on a blocking-sync event does not hold the lock while it waits. The torch-only repro in #61621 shows a 1.18 s stall for the other thread with `.cpu()` and 0.2 ms with pinned + event, on the same GPU work.

Design: one helper instead of per-backend changes, because other step-start reads (e.g. if #61239 restores the blocking read under async scheduling) can reuse it. The event is created per call; `torch.empty(pin_memory=True)` is served by the caching host allocator after the first step, so no `cudaHostAlloc` on the hot path. `blocking=True` matches the existing per-step events in the model runners (#47081). Call sites keep their existing `gpu_sync_allowed()` wrapping, since this is still a host sync.

Why this is not a duplicate: searched open/closed issues and PRs for `seq_lens.cpu`, pageable copies, driver/context lock, `cudaLaunchHostFunc`, and KV connector stalls. #57214 and #58684 removed some of these reads where a CPU upper bound is exact. #61239 is about the barrier those removals dropped, and it proposes bringing the blocking read back. #47081 changed spin events to blocking events. None of them addresses the lock held during a pageable D2H wait. #57352 (open) plans FlashInfer from CPU bounds with speculative decoding on fa2 and keeps the `.cpu()` fallback this PR changes, so the two compose. #59493 (open) makes FlashInfer's `plan()` staging buffer pageable, which is a separate race.

AI assistance was used to prepare this PR (code, tests and measurements). I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and measurements above.

title: [ROCm][MLA][DCP] Drop VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY
body:
## Purpose

Remove `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY` and always select the DCP multi-token (spec-decode) verify kernel heuristically.

Default behavior is unchanged: the builder now always does what `auto` (the default) did.

- **gfx950:** AITER round-robin asm decode (cprr) when the DCP-gathered head count pads to a native kernel (16/32/64/128), otherwise segmented MLA.
- **gfx942:** segmented MLA where it fits in LDS, otherwise Triton split-KV decode. The env var never affected gfx942.

What goes away:
- `segmented`: the opt-out from cprr on gfx950.
- `asm`: the hard error for head counts cprr can't serve. These now fall back to segmented, as `auto` already did. A config with neither kernel still fails at builder init.

This also clears the way for a follow-up gfx942 verify-kernel work to choose a new assembly verify kernel. 

## Test Plan

    pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py \
           tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr_numerics.py \
           tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_verify_gfx942.py \
           tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py

## Test Result

- Routing tests pass. Env-parsing and forced-override tests are removed; native head counts, K3's 96→128 padding, fallback above 128 heads, and off-gfx950 routing are covered.

## Accuracy validation on gfx942

title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Poll transfer completion on a background thread
body:
## Overview

Adds an opt-in thread to `NixlConnector` (`kv_connector_extra_config.async_completion_poll`) that checks NIXL transfer completion every 1 ms, so the transfer latency vLLM reports is the actual transfer time rather than the time until the next engine step.

## Claims

- **Currently, reported NIXL transfer latency includes engine-step stalls.** NIXL stamps `xferDuration` at the first status check that sees a transfer complete ([`nixlAgent::getXferStatus`](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/blob/22df9863d891112974f7454a454e8449ff83b911/src/core/nixl_agent.cpp#L1268-L1297)). vLLM makes that check only in `_pop_done_transfers()`, once per engine step.
- **In production this shows up as false network tail latency.** A first-use Triton JIT compile of a sampler kernel stalls a decode step for 0.8–3.8 s. Every in-flight KV transfer then reports over 1 s, on all DP ranks at once, which looks exactly like a fabric problem. With polling on, that tail disappears (the stalls themselves remain).
- **Typical latency is overstated too**, because completion is noticed one step late: 9–25 ms average falls to 1.7–3.5 ms.
- **No serving change.** It is off by default. When on, the engine consumes completions at the same point in the step, and release, notification and failure handling are unchanged.

## Validation

GLM-5.3 (HiSparse, 1M context), P/D on 8×8 H100 over RoCE (prefill DP4 × PCP8/DCP8, decode DP4 × TP8, MTP-3), aiperf agentic traces (≈100k-token inputs), with a 25-minute window per level and one run per arm. The table shows transfer latency reported on decode, before → after:

| backend | level | avg | ≤ 5 ms | > 200 ms | > 1 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| UCX | c96 | 8.9 → **1.7 ms** | 76.3 → **93.8%** | 89 → **5** | 72 → **0** |
| UCX | c128 | 8.7 → **2.5 ms** | 75.6 → **90.8%** | 151 → **18** | 0 → 0 |

- **The tail is the JIT stalls.** Before the change, every > 1 s transfer at c96 (72/72 UCX, 246/246 UCCL) fell within 60 s of a logged compile.
- **The mechanism.** On a single GPU pair without vLLM, checking every 1 / 5 / 30 ms makes `xferDuration` p50 read 1.08 / 5.08 / 30.1 ms, against 0.36 ms when busy-polled. UCX and UCCL behave the same.
- **Serving (UCX).** Throughput was +1% and ITL p50/p99 within 1 ms. TTFT p99 moved both ways, within run-to-run spread. There were no transfer failures.
- **The final branch, end to end.** The GLM runs used the original patch on `f6d5a33`. This branch (`a3fca5e525`) passed a 1P+1D smoke test (Qwen3-0.6B, one H100 node): all requests completed with 0 transfer failures, shutdown was clean, and outputs were byte-identical to a run with polling off.
- **Unit tests** (`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_async_poll.py`, CPU, in the `cpu_test` CI job) cover:
  - completion stamping while the step is blocked;
  - failures reported identically with polling on and off;
  - exactly one check and one release per handle;
  - shutdown;
  - where the option is supported.

## Details

- **The poll thread** walks `_recving_transfers` under a lock shared with `_pop_done_transfers()`, and records each terminal state with its telemetry, or the exception raised. The engine step reads that result through `_poll_xfer()` and does everything else as before.
- **One checker per handle, never after a terminal state.** UCCL frees the transfer status at the first DONE, so a second check would read freed memory.
- **The agent uses `NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_STRICT`.** The thread is joined at shutdown before handles are released. An unexpected error is logged and retried instead of killing the thread, which would otherwise leave every transfer in progress.

**Limitations**
- **All NIXL calls on the worker are serialized** by `NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_STRICT`. This was measured as neutral on one configuration only.
- **The thread needs the GIL**, so native code that holds it can still delay a stamp. The full fix is for NIXL to stamp completion in the backend.
- **Pull mode only.** `NixlPushConnector` also completes `_sending_transfers`, which is not polled, so it ignores the option with a warning. So do NIXL builds without `nixl_agent_config`.

Both options are documented in `docs/features/nixl_connector_usage.md`.

title: [HiSparse] Pad staged prefill KV to avoid a trtllm-gen out-of-bounds read
body:
## Problem

HiSparse prefill randomly crashes with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access` in `sparse_mla_attention.forward_mqa` → `_forward_mqa_kernel` on the staged prefill cache. `HiSparseRuntime.gather_prefill_cache` stages a request's KV into an exact-size buffer (often 1–3 blocks of 64 rows), and FlashInfer's trtllm-gen sparse MLA decode kernel reads ~170–250 rows from the start of its KV cache regardless of the cache's size or the top-k indices (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6484). It faults whenever the caching allocator puts the staged buffer near an unmapped page. Surfaced in #61487 (HiSparse + DBO); DBO makes it more frequent but it is not DBO-specific.

## Fix

Allocate at least 256 rows behind the staged buffer and return the exact-size view, so all downstream shapes are unchanged. Cost: ≤168 KB of transient allocation per staged layer.

## Test plan

Hardware: 4x B200 pod (pirate2 dell-b200-01), flashinfer 0.7.0.post1, torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0. vLLM `2f18d13cf` (main at the time the env was built) with and without this PR's diff.

Repro (DP2 + EP + DBO, eager, GLM-5.3 NVFP4 with dummy weights, 8 layers; `crash.sh` starts the server below and sends 3 rounds of 128 concurrent 30-word completions with `max_tokens=128`):

```bash
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --load-format dummy --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": 8}' \
  -tp 1 -dp 2 --enable-expert-parallel --enable-dbo --all2all-backend deepep_low_latency \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-model-len 8192 \
  --attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":24}}' \
  --dbo-decode-token-threshold 2 --dbo-prefill-token-threshold 512 --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}'
# env: VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
```

| Revision | Servers | Load rounds (128 req each) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 2 | 1st server: round 1; 2nd server (`CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`): round 2 | illegal memory access, engine dead. With launch blocking the trace points at `sparse_mla_attention.py:858` (`_forward_mqa_kernel` on the `stage_prefill_rows` cache) → `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` |
| main + this PR | 3 | 3 × 3 | 1152/1152 requests 200, no errors |

Unit tests (B200):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "hisparse or HiSparse or staging"   # 40 passed
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py                              # 15 passed
```

The new `test_hisparse_staged_prefill_cache_backs_min_attention_rows` fails without the fix and passes with it.

title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Mono decode layer for GLM-5.3-Flash on MI355X
body:
## Purpose

Opt-in (`--monokernel`) MonoKernel decode for GLM-5.3-Flash (`amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`) on MI355X (gfx950), in the shape RFC #60904 proposes. Each MoE decoder layer of a decode step is one persistent FlyDSL launch (256 CTAs):

| Launch | Layers | Stages |
|---|---|---|
| KDA layer | 30 of the 41 MoE layers | attention-side mHC seam, in-projections, short conv, KDA gates and recurrence, gated norm, o_proj and its TP reduce, FFN mHC seam, RMSNorm, router, top-8, shared expert and MXFP4 experts, MoE TP reduce |
| Sparse-attention layer | the other 11 | attention-side mHC seam, fused q_a / kv_a, q norm, KV and kpool index-cache writes, q_b, the indexer query (FWHT-128 + FP8), W_UK, pool scoring and top-2048 selection, split attention, W_UV, o_proj and its TP reduce, then the same FFN half |

A decode step issues 220 kernels instead of 1,699 (TP4, 4 rows), and its time between tokens drops 29–45% at TP8, concurrency 1–8; GSM8K is at least at parity at TP8 and TP4.

**Scope**
- **Layers:** the 41 MoE layers 3–43. The dense layers 0–2 and layer 44, whose mHC post contracts the streams, run vLLM's code.
- **Steps:** pure decode, 1 token a request, widths 2 / 4 / 8 at TP4 and TP8, 2 / 4 at TP2 (wider steps there are slower than vLLM's path). FULL graphs (vLLM resolves this model's default to FULL_DECODE_ONLY) or eager.
- **Everything else** runs vLLM's layers unchanged: prefill, mixed and wider steps, PIECEWISE replays. Kernel and vLLM layers take and return the same `(hidden, residual, post, comb)`, so they interleave freely.

### Layout

```
vllm/models/common/mono/          RFC #60904's shared runtime (849 lines)
    spec.py      MonoSpec, LayerKernel, MonoStep, MonoContext, Feature
    guards.py    configure, config-stage refusals (default-deny), graph-mode checks
    layer.py     attach, forward_layer, after_step, health
    routing.py   per-step decision, cache re-binding on (data_ptr, numel)
    failstop.py  error-word health check, fail-stop, VLLM_MONO_UNSAFE_WARN
    peer.py      symmetric peer buffers
    abi.py       error-word and fault-hook layout
vllm/models/glm5next/amd/mono/    the model's spec (885 lines)
    spec.py      MONO_SPEC, geometry and config refusals, declared numerics
    weights.py   weight views and their checks
    kernel.py    model refusals, cache binding, eligibility, build per width, launch
vllm/models/glm5next/amd/ops/mono/  kernel source (4,174 lines; ffn/kernel.py 3,155)
vllm/models/glm5next/common/model.py  the hook (+16 lines)
```

`ops/mono/{ops,layout}.py` and `ffn/{kernel,layout}.py` are adapted from ROCm/aiter#6173 at c39b56c36 (Apache-2.0). Each names its origin. The changes from aiter:
- GLM-5.3-Flash's layer kinds: the KDA path and the sparse-attention path with the kpool indexer, both new;
- the mHC seams of this model, FP8 block-128 or bf16 per attention projection (vLLM loads the checkpoint's FP8 q_a / kv_a as bf16);
- bounded waits with per-stage error words and an early out after the first expiry, so a stalled peer stops the engine with the kernel's error rather than an RPC timeout;
- 64-bit cache-block bases: the caches sit in a ~248 GB pool.

### Design

- **Weights** are views of vLLM's loaded tensors, no second copy. Every view is checked for shape, dtype and sharding at attach and raises on a mismatch. The routed experts stay in AITER's MXFP4 layout, and any other MoE backend is refused.
- **Path selection** is plain Python (the model is not torch.compiled), decided once per step for all kernel layers from metadata every rank holds alike: pure decode, a built width, the spec's eligibility. Under FULL graphs it is baked in at capture. PIECEWISE captures are declined, since they replay mixed batches.
- **Caches** are re-bound whenever a cache tensor's `(data_ptr, numel)` changes, because memory profiling runs real steps on throwaway caches first.
- **Refusals** run at config, after load and at every bind, and report every reason at once. Default-deny on PP, DP, EP, EPLB, DCP, PCP, LoRA, KV connectors, routed-expert capture, speculative decoding, sleep mode, CPU weight offload, weight updates, prompt embeds and EAGLE3 aux layers. The spec adds: gfx950 only, TP 2/4/8, bf16 KV cache, an fp32 KDA recurrent state, no sequence-parallel MoE, the exact model geometry.
- **Failure modes.** Every cross-CTA and cross-rank wait is bounded. An expired wait sets its stage's error word; after each step the health check reads them, and the output rank raises with the stage names while the other ranks exit their workers. `VLLM_MONO_FAULT_INJECT` stalls a chosen rank at a chosen step for the fault test.
- **Numerics** that differ from vLLM's path are listed in the spec and logged at startup. All are at least as precise as vLLM's: expert inputs MXFP8 (vLLM MXFP4); the FP8 attention projections on bf16 activations (vLLM: FP8 per 128); W_UK / W_UV in bf16 from `kv_b_proj` (vLLM: AITER FP4 / FP8 BMM). The attention TP reduce and the split-attention partials are summed in bf16.
- **Dependencies:** the `flydsl` wheel and AITER helpers this path already uses (`aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels.buffer_ops`, `dpp_utils`, `aiter.ops.shuffle`).

## Duplicate check

- No open PR targets GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5next`) MonoKernel decode. Searched "GLM-5.3-Flash mono", "glm5next mono", "MonoKernel GLM", "Flash MonoKernel" and PRs naming #60904.
- Related, other models: #60831 (GLM-5, the same submitter), #60889 (GLM-5.2), #60397 (DeepSeek-V4.1, merged), #60683 (Kimi-K3), #61325 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next).
- #61311 proposes the shared runtime under `vllm/models/common/mono/` too. This PR carries its own copy of that layer, written to RFC #60904; the two need to converge before either lands.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/models/common/mono` (CPU, wired into the existing models CPU job): refusals reported at once and default-deny, graph modes, routing at every width against mixed / prefill / over-width / PIECEWISE / profiling steps, the decision on every simulated rank, cache re-binding, fail-stop on the output rank and the others, `VLLM_MONO_UNSAFE_WARN`, the fault spec.
- `pytest tests/models/glm5next/amd_mono/test_flash_spec.py` (CPU, the GLM5Next job): model refusals, width caps per TP, layer kinds, FP8 / bf16 projection views rejecting every other format, sparse-attention weight checks, the per-step row table.
- New CI step "(MI355) GLM-5.3-Flash Mono Decode Kernel" (4 × MI355): `test_flash_{ffn,kda,dsa}_kernel.py` check each stage against vLLM's own ops (the mHC op, the KDA conv / recurrent / norm kernels, the kpool and FWHT-quant kernels, the MLA attention) at widths 2/4/8, then capture every width in one graph and replay 300 times, bit for bit against the first run. `test_flash_moe_vllm.py` builds vLLM's real `Glm5NextMoE` from random weights in checkpoint layout through `process_weights_after_loading` and compares. `test_stalled_rank_reports_expiry` stalls one rank in the kernel and expects the error words.
- Compile-only build (`COMPILE_ONLY=1 ARCH=gfx950`) of every launch kind at every width and TP.
- GSM8K: full 1,319, 5-shot, strict match, greedy, 3 runs a path on the same node and day, paired McNemar, TP8 and TP4; 250 questions at TP2.
- Long context: NIAH, 10 needles at each of 32K, 64K and 120K (128K is the served maximum), TP8.
- Sanity per RFC #60904: 50 bare-completion prompts, greedy, first 8 tokens, each server run twice.
- Performance: `vllm bench serve`, graphs against graphs, same batch cap (`--max-num-seqs 256`), bf16 KV cache. Median ITL per width at 512 and 32K tokens of context, median TPOT at 8K in / 256 out, c1–c8 at TP8 / TP4 / TP2; a profiled decode step; cold and warm startup.
- Fault injection in a server: rank 1 stalls 120 s at kernel step 300 under load, TP4 and TP8.

## Test Result

**Unit:** 45 CPU tests pass (rebased build). **Kernel CI step:** passes at TP2, TP4 and TP8 on idle GPUs (rebased build). On a shared node, where another container ran a GEMM tuner on some of the same GPUs, the two sparse-attention `mixed` cases reported an expired wait; see the co-tenancy note below. **Compile-only:** every launch kind builds.

**MoE against vLLM's `Glm5NextMoE`** (random weights): relative error against an fp32 MoE on the dequantized weights and unquantized inputs is 0.044–0.048 for the kernel and 0.211–0.257 for vLLM, whose MoE quantizes expert inputs to MXFP4; routing identical. TP2, TP4 and TP8.

**GSM8K** (strict, full 1,319, each path's runs on one node and day, paired McNemar over all runs):

| | build | MonoKernel | vLLM | discordant (mono / vLLM) | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8 | rebased | 0.9052 / 0.8969 / 0.9030 | 0.8954 / 0.8969 / 0.8795 | 220 / 176 | 0.03 |
| TP8 | pre-rebase | 0.8999 / 0.9052 / 0.8969 | 0.8795 / 0.8840 / 0.8886 | 229 / 163 | 0.001 |
| TP4 | rebased | 0.8961 | 0.8999 | 53 / 58 | 0.70 |
| TP4 | pre-rebase | 0.8992 / 0.9045 / 0.8961 | 0.9014 / 0.8923 / 0.8931 | 190 / 173 | 0.40 |

TP2, 250 questions: 0.920 vs 0.896. **NIAH** (MonoKernel, TP8): 10/10 at each of 32K, 64K and 120K.

**Sanity.** The 90% bar on the first 8 tokens is out of reach for vLLM itself on this model, so the MonoKernel is measured against vLLM's own run-to-run agreement:

| first 8 tokens identical | TP4 | TP8 |
|---|---|---|
| vLLM vs vLLM | 26% | 32% |
| MonoKernel vs MonoKernel | 36% | 34% |
| MonoKernel vs vLLM (two runs) | 36% / 30% | 34% / 36% |

Several prompts differ at the first token already, which comes from prefill (vLLM's code on both paths). Tokens outside the other run's top 5 before the first divergence: 2–7 across the 50 prompts on every pair, vLLM vs vLLM included.

**Decode step, TP4** (median ITL in ms, 128 out, concurrency = width; rebased build):

| width | 512 in: vLLM → mono | 32K in: vLLM → mono |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 7.60 → 4.34 (−43%) | 7.74 → 4.70 (−39%) |
| 4 | 8.08 → 5.00 (−38%) | 8.21 → 5.40 (−34%) |
| 8 | 8.70 → 6.57 (−24%) | 8.88 → 7.20 (−19%) |

**Profiled step** (TP4, c4, 512 in; pre-rebase build): 9.36 ms and 1,699 kernels → 4.82 ms and 220 kernels. Per layer, from kernel durations, which the profiler does not inflate: sparse-attention layer 110 µs (×11), KDA layer 89 µs (×30); the rest of the step (embedding, layers 0–2 and 44, head, sampling) 0.90 ms.

**Time between tokens** (median TPOT in ms, 8K in / 256 out, vLLM → mono; rebased build):

| conc | TP8 | TP4 | TP2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 7.04 → 4.16 (−40.9%) | 7.23 → 4.85 (−32.9%) | 8.60 → 6.17 (−28.3%) |
| 2 | 7.67 → 4.19 (−45.4%) | 8.07 → 4.94 (−38.8%) | 9.75 → 6.51 (−33.2%) |
| 4 | 8.75 → 5.35 (−38.9%) | 9.26 → 6.32 (−31.7%) | 12.70 → 8.98 (−29.3%) |
| 8 | 10.66 → 7.53 (−29.4%) | 12.58 → 10.89 (−13.4%) | — (4-row cap) |

The pre-rebase build measured the same points within 1%, except vLLM at TP4 c8 (11.92 ms then, 12.58 ms now) and vLLM at TP2 c4 (13.22 ms then, 12.70 ms now).

**Startup** (TP4, checkpoint already in the page cache, rebased build): 661 s → 707 s; the 46 s is the FlyDSL compile of 2 launch kinds × 3 widths, which a kept FlyDSL cache skips.

**Fault injection** (pre-rebase build): at TP4 and TP8 every rank logs `GLM-5.3-Flash MonoKernel rank N: expired waits in <stages>; tokens of the affected steps are wrong`, the workers stop, the container exits and no GPU memory stays held. Without the early out the engine still stopped, but on vLLM's 300 s `sample_tokens` RPC timeout.

**Co-tenancy.** The kernel needs every compute unit of its GPU. A TP8 server on the rebased build that shared GPUs 4–7 with another user's GEMM tuning job stopped during GSM8K: ranks 4, 5 and 7 reported expired waits, the fail-stop raised the MonoKernel error and the engine exited, with no hang and no tokens served from the failed step. The same build on an unshared node ran 3 full GSM8K passes with no expiry. Detecting a co-tenant at startup is RFC #60904's open question 3; this PR only documents it.

**Provenance of the numbers.** All on MI355X. *Rebased build:* this PR's head on the `nightly-77154ca6` ROCm image (45 commits behind main), AITER `v0.1.25`, with #50535, #59478 and ROCm/aiter#6435 / #6436 (router-GEMM and fused-MoE tuning for this model) in both arms; the kernel tests, the rebased GSM8K rows, ITL, TPOT and startup come from it. *Pre-rebase build:* the same kernels on the week-41 nightly with AITER `main` at the time (`0.1.25.dev181`), the same four PRs, and the switch still an env var; NIAH, sanity, the profile, the fault runs and the pre-rebase GSM8K rows come from it. The code changes since are the switch, the refusal of a bf16 KDA recurrent state, and CI.

## Draft status

Open before review:
- AITER: main pins `v0.1.24.post1` again (#61559); every number here ran on `v0.1.25` or the `main` before it, so `test_flash_moe_vllm.py` needs a run on main's pin.
- Converge `vllm/models/common/mono/` with #61311.
- CODEOWNERS entry for `vllm/models/glm5next/amd/`.
- A parameter-name test (`named_parameters()` and loaded values with the switch on and off), and source digests in the FlyDSL build keys.
- Attach the run logs.

## AI assistance

Written with AI assistance. Opened as a draft for the submitter to review every changed line before it is marked ready.
