title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Quarantine consumer slots until writes settle
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61532 by retaining consumer CPU destination slots when a P2P load fails before remote WRITE completion is confirmed. This follows the [consumer-only scope requested in the issue](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61532#issuecomment-6165941559) and builds on the producer fix already merged in #59790.

## Claims

- An abort-ack timeout for a sent fetch reports failure once and makes the keys miss, while keeping their slots unavailable to other requests.
- A late completion/abort acknowledgement releases quarantined slots without reporting the failed load as successful. Session close preserves quarantine when confirmation can no longer arrive.
- Never-sent fetches fail safely on handshake failure, cancellation or load timeout. Retired queued messages cannot be sent later, including after request-ID reuse.
- Quarantined slots remain counted as pending writes until confirmation. Cache reset rejects unresolved quarantine, including failures first discovered while draining, and retries when a late terminal confirmation makes the drain safe.

## Validation

Validated on the updated source tree `314a38c824d59bd43b624ee236a8d5f52765cd54`, based on upstream `9cede34a674c`. Environment: WSL2 Ubuntu, RTX 4060 Ti 8 GiB, driver 617.42, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, CUDA runtime 13.0, NIXL 1.4.1, UCX over TCP (`UCX_TLS=tcp,self`).

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Tiering/P2P, CPU manager/shared-region and complete offloading connector regressions | **1289 passed, 1 skipped** (optional `kvcr` package unavailable) |
| Latest producer/reset lifecycle review | **11 cases passed**: actual P2P sessions over in-memory test transports, parked producer store and CPU/tiering manager reset; sync/async finish-before-drain, rejected retries, late worker completion, metadata continuation, and active/signaled/retired tail stores |
| Latest producer/reset negative control | Before the fix, 7 cases fail and 2 active-store controls pass; includes the real parked producer assertion |
| Earlier rejected-reset review | **4 cases passed** across sync/async scheduling: failed reset retries preserve scheduler state, worker completions remain usable, eventual reset finalizes once; existing load-reset cases also retain flush coverage |
| Earlier rejected-reset negative control | Both failure cases reproduce request-state loss before the fix; 2 successful-reset controls pass |
| Earlier handshake/drain review | **6 cases passed**: expired/cancelled queued fetches before/after handshake, request-ID reuse, reaped unsafe load rejection and safe disconnect control |
| Earlier handshake/drain negative control | Both reported races fail before the fix; 4 controls pass |
| Earlier disconnect review | **6 cases passed** in the full suite: buffered TransferDone/AbortAck, previously-reported unsafe failure, new-work suppression and invalid terminals |
| Earlier disconnect negative control | Old behavior fails all 4 valid-terminal cases; 2 invalid-terminal controls pass |
| Rebase integration | 6 quarantine cases through step, tier-poll and drain paths, including one initial promotion-latency sample and no duplicate on late confirmation; includes upstream lookup-timeout and tier-poll-thread regression suites |
| Earlier review regressions | **12 passed**: dead connections/partial queue flush, unsafe results during drain, delayed AbortAck/TransferDone, request cleanup and slot/gauge preservation |
| Earlier review negative control | 9 regressions fail before the behavioral fixes; 3 controls pass; all 12 pass after the fixes |
| Earlier cleanup review regressions | **10 passed**: cancelled queued fetches, close, buffered results, request-ID reuse and safe reset retry; unrelated drain errors remain visible |
| Earlier cleanup negative control | 6 regressions fail with the old behavior restored; 4 controls pass; all 10 pass after the fixes |
| Reset regression negative control, before adding the pre-drain guard | Both parameter cases fail; both pass with the guard |
| Real 1 GiB NIXL WRITE, abort-ack timeout | WRITE observed in `PROC`, only 2,621,415 bytes present at stall; slots remain unavailable; delayed terminal confirmation permits reuse; full payload matches |
| Real 1 GiB NIXL WRITE, session close | WRITE observed in `PROC`, only 2,621,415 bytes present at stall; slots remain unavailable even after the late WRITE lands because the closed consumer cannot receive confirmation; full payload matches |
| CUDA generation with `OffloadingConnector`, CPU primary and P2P secondary | Two 192-token requests each generate 8 tokens with identical greedy outputs before/after an actual connector-cache reset; tiny 2-layer Llama, dummy weights, V2 runner |
| Style and types | Repository pre-commit checks and Python 3.11 type hook pass on all changed files; Linux Ruff and Python 3.12 production-source checks pass. The supplemental Python 3.12 test check reports two ZMQ constant export errors reproduced in the unmodified upstream test file |

Reproduce the repository regressions from the repo root using the configured test environment:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector
```

The added regressions extend existing suites and pass the repository's Buildkite test-tethering check. The full pre-commit run was on the Windows host; its Bash-only Dockerfile graph hook was run separately under Linux (no Dockerfile changes). The editable install uses official precompiled artifacts from published ancestor `5d88c034f605`; there are no C++/CUDA or kernel-build changes between that ancestor and the rebase base (the `setup.py` differences only raise optional zentorch/InstantTensor dependencies). Wheel CRC and all 5,469 RECORD entries were verified.

The real transport probe uses two actual `NixlTransport`s and `P2PSession`s. It temporarily stops the target before issuing the WRITE, then stops the producer only after observing a real `PROC`/`PEND` state. A watchdog resumes the target, allowing timeout/close to occur while the producer cannot send terminal confirmation. Only the probe's abort-ack deadline is shortened to 0.5 s. It calls the actual CPU allocator's quarantine/release APIs; session-to-tiering result routing is covered by the repository regressions.

Upstream CI admission is currently blocked by the new-contributor pre-run-check policy; the docs build also stops at that dependent check. The validation above was run locally.

These are single-host UCX/TCP tests, not RDMA or a multi-node serving failure test. The dummy-weight generation check verifies GPU engine integration, not pretrained-model accuracy. No model-quality or performance improvement is claimed.

## Details

1. The producer starts a WRITE into CPU slots reserved by the consumer.
2. The consumer's abort-ack timer expires, or its session closes. Neither event establishes that the WRITE has stopped, so immediately recycling these slots can let a late WRITE corrupt a different request.
3. `memory_safe=False` separates request failure from permission to reclaim memory. The tiering manager removes failed keys from lookup while keeping their chunk IDs quarantined. A subsequent memory-safe result releases the IDs without recording a second completion.

Track the queued Fetch object until handoff to the transport, so a retired message cannot match a newer load with reused request/round IDs. Never-sent fetches fail locally without sending an abort. The send gate also checks the original load deadline, so a delayed handshake cannot flush an already-expired fetch before the timeout walk. This addresses the [delayed-handshake review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61667#discussion_r4283622153). Connection liveness is checked before recording handoff, so later queued fetches remain safe after an earlier send kills the connection. A raising send on a live connection remains conservatively unsafe because it may already have exposed destination IDs. This also addresses the [dead-connection review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61667#discussion_r4274467514). This addresses the [queued-fetch review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61667#discussion_r4274078909).

CPU write occupancy and tier promotion/write gauges stay charged throughout quarantine and decrease only on confirmed release; failure is counted once. This addresses the [accounting review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61667#discussion_r4274078928).

P2P draining stops on an unconfirmed unsafe result instead of waiting forever. It checks result safety before returning idle, including when a disconnect has removed the last session. This addresses the [reaped-session drain review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61667#discussion_r4283622168). Reset consumes results before rejecting an unsafe drain. If a late terminal result confirms safety during that poll, reset retries the interrupted tier and drains the remaining tiers. A typed `UnsafeTransferError` keeps unrelated drain errors visible. This also addresses the [late-confirmation reset review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61667#discussion_r4275023865). This addresses the [drain review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61667#discussion_r4274467527).

The connector scheduler notifies finished requests before draining the manager, allowing a bound producer round with parked jobs but no active NIXL transfer to settle. Each successful notification is recorded once. Flush IDs, request deletion and job/stale bookkeeping changes are committed only after the manager reset succeeds. If quarantine rejects reset, request/job records remain usable for retry and late worker completion; normal metadata construction skips further stores and duplicate finish notifications for already-signaled requests. Successful resets still deliver worker flush IDs and ignore old completions. This addresses the [producer ordering review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61667#discussion_r4290287893) and the [rejected-reset review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61667#discussion_r4289843026).

Late terminal notifications carry whether their failure was already reported. They still release quarantine, but do not add a finished request ID to the failure set again; session close likewise omits already-reported failures. Results also carry local request completion, including queued cancellations and buffered results, so a first failure arriving after request cleanup cannot restore a stale failure ID. A reused ID starts with fresh load state. This also addresses the [cancelled-fetch cleanup review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61667#discussion_r4275023850). This addresses the [request-failure review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61667#discussion_r4274467538).

Rebased onto `9cede34a674c` after the [merge-conflict notice](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61667#issuecomment-6190452982). This retains upstream lookup deadlines/cleanup and the new manager lock/tier-poll thread. The quarantine regression now covers both unsafe results and late safe release through `poll_tiers()` under the manager lock, in addition to step/drain paths. The CUDA generation run enabled the upstream default tier-poll thread.

Validated `TransferDone` and `AbortAck` messages already buffered by the control transport still settle existing loads after a disconnect is observed. Other messages stay suppressed, so draining the inbox cannot start new fetches or handshakes. Unconfirmed loads remain unsafe at close, and malformed terminal messages cannot release their slots. This addresses the [buffered-terminal review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61667#discussion_r4280126143).

The latest rebase retains upstream promotion-latency recording and NIXL agent-removal changes. A promotion's initial failed completion records one latency sample while its write occupancy stays charged; late terminal confirmation releases that occupancy without recording another completion or latency. The existing quarantine regression covers this combination.

The default `memory_safe=True` preserves existing results from other secondary tiers. No producer transport or server behavior is changed. Chunk IDs are converted to a list at the existing session boundary to satisfy its `Sequence[int]` contract.

Tradeoff: if a peer never confirms completion, or the session is closed, quarantined capacity remains unavailable until engine shutdown. Reset rejects that state instead of recycling potentially live WRITE targets. Stop peers before restarting the engine. Producers must also contain #59790 so an abort acknowledgement really means the WRITE is terminal.

Duplicate-work check: no open PR referencing #61532 was found before submission. #59790 is merged and covers the producer; #60279 covers stale NIXL registrations and #56836 covers unanswered lookups. This PR addresses the remaining consumer timeout/close lifetime paths.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex was used to rebase, implement, review and run the validation for this PR.

<details>
<summary>Real NIXL fault probe and reproduction commands</summary>

Save the following two files side by side, then run from a Linux vLLM environment with NIXL and CUDA:

```bash
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
export UCX_TLS=tcp,self
.venv/bin/python real_p2p_lifetime.py --case timeout
.venv/bin/python real_p2p_lifetime.py --case close
```

**`real_p2p_lifetime.py`**

```python
"""Exercise real P2P sessions and UCX writes with GPU-produced payloads.

No transport states are mocked. A child producer is SIGSTOPped while a
WRITE is PROC/PEND. The abort-ack timer is shortened to avoid ZMQ heartbeat
expiry; production source files are unchanged. CPU-primary quarantine and
release use the actual allocator APIs; scheduler result routing is covered
separately by the repository regression tests.
"""

import argparse
import faulthandler
import gc
import json
import multiprocessing as mp
import os
import signal
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import traceback
import uuid
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch
import zmq

from vllm.v1.kv_offload.base import LookupResult, ReqContext, make_offload_key
from vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.p2p.control.zmq import ZmqTransport
from vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.p2p.data.nixl import NixlTransport
from vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.p2p.session import P2PSession
from vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.p2p.session import client as client_module

BLOCKS = 64
BLOCK_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024
PAYLOAD = 90
REQUEST = "lifetime-probe"
KEYS = [make_offload_key(f"probe-{i}".encode(), 0) for i in range(BLOCKS)]


def free_port():
    with socket.socket() as sock:
        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        return sock.getsockname()[1]


def producer(control_port, consumer_id, consumer_pid, management):
    data = control = session = None
    try:
        gpu = torch.full((BLOCKS, BLOCK_BYTES), PAYLOAD, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
        payload = gpu.cpu().numpy()
        del gpu
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        local_id = f"127.0.0.1:{control_port}"
        reported = False

        class PausingNixlTransport(NixlTransport):
            def write_blocks(self, peer_id, local_idxs, remote_idxs):
                nonlocal reported
                os.kill(consumer_pid, signal.SIGSTOP)
                transfer_id = super().write_blocks(peer_id, local_idxs, remote_idxs)
                if transfer_id is not None and not reported:
                    state = self._agent.check_xfer_state(self._inflight[transfer_id].handle)
                    management.send({"event": "submitted", "state": state})
                    if state in ("PROC", "PEND"):
                        management.send({"event": "running", "states": [state]})
                        reported = True
                        os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGSTOP)
                os.kill(consumer_pid, signal.SIGCONT)
                return transfer_id

        data = PausingNixlTransport(f"producer-{os.getpid()}", memoryview(payload), num_threads=1)
        assert data.available, "NIXL transport unavailable"
        control = ZmqTransport(local_id, "127.0.0.1", control_port)
        control._zmq_ctx.setsockopt(zmq.LINGER, 0)
        control._router.setsockopt(zmq.LINGER, 0)
        session = P2PSession(consumer_id, local_id, data, BLOCK_BYTES, "0")
        management.send({"event": "listening"})
        supplied = completed = False
        end = time.monotonic() + 120
        while time.monotonic() < end:
            if management.poll() and management.recv() == "quit":
                break
            for conn in control.poll():
                session.attach_connection(conn)
            if session.ready and not supplied:
                session.add_stored_blocks(REQUEST, KEYS, list(range(BLOCKS)), 100)
                supplied = True
            session.poll()
            if data._inflight and not reported:
                states = [data._agent.check_xfer_state(x.handle) for x in data._inflight.values()]
                if any(s in ("PROC", "PEND") for s in states):
                    management.send({"event": "running", "states": states})
                    reported = True
                    os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGSTOP)
            if reported and not data._inflight and not completed:
                management.send({"event": "terminal"})
                completed = True
            time.sleep(0.001)
        else:
            raise TimeoutError("producer exceeded 120 seconds")
    except Exception:
        management.send({"event": "error", "traceback": traceback.format_exc()})
        raise
    finally:
        if session is not None:
            session.close()
        if data is not None:
            data.close()
        if control is not None:
            control.close()


def run_case(mode):
    from vllm.v1.kv_offload.cpu.shared_offload_region import SharedOffloadRegion
    from vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.manager import CPUPrimaryTierOffloadingManager

    faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(45, repeat=True)
    client_module._ABORT_ACK_TIMEOUT_S = 0.5
    parent_pipe, child_pipe = mp.get_context("spawn").Pipe()
    consumer_port, producer_port = free_port(), free_port()
    consumer_id = f"127.0.0.1:{consumer_port}"
    producer_id = f"127.0.0.1:{producer_port}"
    process = mp.get_context("spawn").Process(target=producer, args=(producer_port, consumer_id, os.getpid(), child_pipe))
    region = data = control = session = primary = view = None
    paused = False
    events = []
    watchdog = None
    def checkpoint(name):
        print(json.dumps({"stage": name, "case": mode, "pid": os.getpid()}), flush=True)

    try:
        region = SharedOffloadRegion(f"probe_{uuid.uuid4().hex}", BLOCKS, None, BLOCK_BYTES, BLOCK_BYTES)
        primary = CPUPrimaryTierOffloadingManager(BLOCKS, region)
        view = primary.get_kv_memoryview()
        np.frombuffer(view, dtype=np.uint8).fill(0)
        ctx = ReqContext(req_id=REQUEST)
        prepared = primary.prepare_write(KEYS, ctx)
        assert prepared is not None
        chunk_ids = [int(i) for i in prepared.store_spec.chunk_ids]
        data = NixlTransport(f"consumer-{os.getpid()}-{mode}", view, num_threads=1)
        assert data.available
        control = ZmqTransport(consumer_id, "127.0.0.1", consumer_port)
        control._zmq_ctx.setsockopt(zmq.LINGER, 0)
        control._router.setsockopt(zmq.LINGER, 0)
        process.start()
        assert parent_pipe.poll(120), "producer startup timed out"
        event = parent_pipe.recv()
        assert event["event"] == "listening", event
        conn = control.connect(producer_id)
        session = P2PSession(producer_id, consumer_id, data, BLOCK_BYTES, "0", conn=conn)

        def tick():
            control.poll()
            result = session.poll()
            while parent_pipe.poll():
                event = parent_pipe.recv()
                assert event["event"] != "error", event
                events.append(event)
            return result

        end = time.monotonic() + 20
        while not session.ready and time.monotonic() < end:
            tick()
            time.sleep(0.001)
        assert session.ready, "session handshake failed"
        checkpoint("handshake_ready")
        watchdog = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, str(Path(__file__).with_name("resume-target-watchdog.py")), str(os.getpid()), str(process.pid)])
        session.request_blocks(1, REQUEST, KEYS, chunk_ids)
        end = time.monotonic() + 15
        while not any(e["event"] == "running" for e in events) and time.monotonic() < end:
            result = tick()
            assert not result.loads, ("WRITE completed before it could be stalled", result.loads, events)
            time.sleep(0.001)
        assert any(e["event"] == "running" for e in events), "no running WRITE observed"
        os.kill(process.pid, signal.SIGSTOP)
        paused = True
        checkpoint("producer_stopped")
        bytes_at_stall = int(np.count_nonzero(np.frombuffer(view, dtype=np.uint8)))
        assert bytes_at_stall < BLOCKS * BLOCK_BYTES, "target already received the complete WRITE"

        if mode == "timeout":
            session.finish_request(REQUEST)
            end = time.monotonic() + 3
            failures = []
            while not failures and time.monotonic() < end:
                failures.extend(tick().loads)
                time.sleep(0.002)
            assert len(failures) == 1 and failures[0].success is False
            assert failures[0].memory_safe is False, failures
        else:
            closed = session.close()
            assert closed.failed_jobs == [1], closed

        checkpoint("unsafe_failure_observed")
        primary.quarantine_write(KEYS)
        replacement = [make_offload_key(b"replacement", 0)]
        assert all(primary.lookup(k, ctx) is LookupResult.MISS for k in KEYS)
        assert primary.prepare_write(replacement, ctx) is None, "unsafe slot was reused"
        try:
            primary.reset_cache()
        except RuntimeError as exc:
            assert "quarantined slots" in str(exc)
        else:
            raise AssertionError("reset_cache reclaimed unsafe slots")
        checkpoint("quarantine_assertions_passed")
        os.kill(process.pid, signal.SIGCONT)
        paused = False

        end = time.monotonic() + 30
        safe = []
        while time.monotonic() < end:
            if mode == "timeout":
                safe.extend(tick().loads)
                if safe:
                    break
            else:
                while parent_pipe.poll():
                    events.append(parent_pipe.recv())
                if any(e["event"] == "terminal" for e in events):
                    break
            time.sleep(0.002)
        if mode == "timeout":
            assert len(safe) == 1 and safe[0].memory_safe is True, safe
            assert safe[0].success is False
        else:
            assert any(e["event"] == "terminal" for e in events), events
        checkpoint("terminal_confirmation_observed")
        assert np.all(np.frombuffer(view, dtype=np.uint8) == PAYLOAD), "late WRITE payload differs"
        checkpoint("late_payload_verified")
        sample = torch.from_numpy(np.frombuffer(view, dtype=np.uint8)[:65536].copy())
        assert torch.equal(sample.cuda().cpu(), sample)
        checkpoint("consumer_gpu_roundtrip_passed")

        if mode == "timeout":
            primary.release_quarantined_write(chunk_ids)
            assert primary.prepare_write(replacement, ctx) is not None
        else:
            assert primary.prepare_write(replacement, ctx) is None
        return {"case": mode, "passed": True, "bytes": BLOCKS * BLOCK_BYTES,
                "bytes_at_stall": bytes_at_stall,
                "source_gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(0), "torch_cuda": torch.version.cuda,
                "abort_ack_timeout_s": client_module._ABORT_ACK_TIMEOUT_S,
                "slots_reused_before_confirmation": False,
                "quarantine_released": mode == "timeout", "events": events}
    finally:
        checkpoint("cleanup_started")
        if watchdog is not None:
            watchdog.wait(timeout=35)
        if process.pid and process.is_alive():
            os.kill(process.pid, signal.SIGCONT)
        if process.pid and process.is_alive():
            parent_pipe.send("quit")
            process.join(8)
            if process.is_alive():
                process.terminate()
                process.join(5)
        if session is not None:
            session.close()
        if data is not None:
            data.close()
        if control is not None:
            control.close()
        if view is not None:
            view.release()
        if primary is not None:
            primary.shutdown()
        del session, data, control, primary, view
        gc.collect()
        if region is not None:
            region.cleanup()
        checkpoint("cleanup_finished")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    faulthandler.enable()
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--case", choices=["timeout", "close"], default="timeout")
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    result = run_case(args.case)
    if args.output:
        args.output.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
```

**`resume-target-watchdog.py`**

```python
"""Resume only our probe's target once its producer has SIGSTOPped itself."""
import os
import signal
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

target_pid, producer_pid = map(int, sys.argv[1:])
deadline = time.monotonic() + 30
try:
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        try:
            status = Path(f"/proc/{producer_pid}/status").read_text()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            break
        state = next(line for line in status.splitlines() if line.startswith("State:"))
        if state.split()[1] in ("T", "t"):
            print("Watchdog: producer stopped; resuming probe target", flush=True)
            break
        time.sleep(0.005)
finally:
    try:
        os.kill(target_pid, signal.SIGCONT)
    except ProcessLookupError:
        pass
```

title: [Spec Decode] Enable fused MTP updates for FlashInfer sparse MLA
body:
## Overview


Enable graph-safe fused multi-step MTP metadata updates for the FlashInfer sparse MLA backend.

## Claims


- Enables draft-decode metadata updates for FlashInfer sparse MLA when DCP is disabled.
- Refreshes `req_id_per_token` in place using the existing GPU metadata kernel.
- Preserves CUDA graph compatibility without adding allocations or host synchronization.
- Keeps the optimization disabled under DCP until its additional metadata requirements are supported.

## Validation



```bash
pytest -q \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py \
  -k flashinfer_sparse_draft_metadata
```

## Details



The FlashInfer sparse MLA metadata builder did not advertise support for draft-decode metadata updates. As a result, fused multi-step MTP decode could not refresh its token-to-request mapping through the graph-safe metadata update path.
This change implements update_draft_decode_metadata by rebuilding req_id_per_token from the GPU-resident query_start_loc with compute_token_to_req_indices. The operation writes into the preallocated metadata buffer, matching the existing sparse FlashAttention MLA implementation.
Fused draft metadata refresh is enabled only when `dcp_world_size == 1`, matching the existing FlashAttention sparse MLA behavior. DCP continues to use the existing per-step metadata build path because its indexer refresh also requires rank-local sequence-length and slot-mapping updates (There is a separate [PR ](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54790)already open to enable this for DCP)

title: [ROCm] Re-bump AITER to v0.1.25 and pin the DSv4.1 mono reference MoE
body:
[DO NOT MERGE]

[ROCm] Re-bump AITER to v0.1.25 and pin the DSv4.1 mono reference MoE



## Overview

Re-lands the AITER v0.1.25 bump (#61230), which #61559 reverted because `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py::test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm[4]` failed. The failure came from AITER v0.1.25's new DSv4.1 tuned MoE configs changing the reference's numerics, not from a mono-kernel bug. This PR pins the test's reference MoE to AITER's base tuned table.

## Claims

- ROCm base images (`Dockerfile.rocm_base`, `Dockerfile.rock_base`) move from AITER v0.1.24.post1 to v0.1.25.
- `test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm[2]` and `[4]` pass on AITER v0.1.25 (MI355). At TP4, mono vs reference MoE is back to 0.49% relative error, from 1.53%.
- No change to the mono kernels or to production kernel selection.

## Validation

MI355 (gfx950, 4 GPUs), vLLM built from this branch, AITER v0.1.25:

pytest -v tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py

| | TP2 | TP4 |
|---|---|---|
| AITER v0.1.25, before this PR | ✅ | ❌ `ratio 1, 1 x 6`: cos 0.999882 (limit 0.9999), rel 1.5344% (limit 1.5%) |
| AITER v0.1.25, this PR | ✅ | ✅ cos 0.999988, rel 0.49% |

Root-cause A/B at TP4, varying only `AITER_CONFIG_FMOE`:

| Reference MoE kernels | Result |
|---|---|
| stock (base + `model_configs/` tuned rows) | ❌ |
| base `tuned_fmoe.csv` only | ✅ |
| TP4 rows: fused-fp8 stage 1, stage 2 `reduce` → atomic | ❌ |
| TP4 rows: unfused stage 1 + atomic stage 2 (TP2's kernels) | ✅ |

`tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` (same CI step): TODO

Model eval (DSv4.1 TP4, AITER v0.1.24.post1 vs v0.1.25): TODO

## Details

**Root cause.** The mono kernel re-implements AITER's a8w4 `fused_moe` numerics. That includes quantizing the stage-2 input to MXFP8 the way the standalone `fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort` does: values rounded to bf16 first, scale exponent `ceil(log2(amax / 448))`.

AITER v0.1.25 adds `aiter/configs/model_configs/dsv41_fp8_tuned_fmoe.csv`. For TP4 (intermediate 576, padded to 640) at M=4/8, it selects `_fp8` stage-1 kernels such as `flydsl_moe1_afp8_wfp4_bf16_t32x128x256_w2_gui_fp8`. These fuse that quant into the stage-1 epilogue with a different rule: quantize from f32, exponent `round(log2(amax)) - 8` (`mixed_moe_gemm_2stage_common.py` in AITER). For blocks with amax mantissa in about [1.41, 1.75), the fused rule picks a 2× larger scale. Both are valid MXFP8, but the reference drifted from 0.49% to 1.53% against mono, just past the limit. TP2's rows (intermediate 1152) at the test's batch use unfused kernels, which is why only TP4 failed.

**Fix.** In the Ray worker, `_mono_numerics` sets `AITER_CONFIG_FMOE` to AITER's base `tuned_fmoe.csv`. The reference MoE then uses the quant mono implements, independent of which tuned kernels a given AITER release picks for DSv4.1 shapes.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- On the non-mono path, production TP4 decode still uses the fused-quant kernels. Its MoE numerics differ from mono's by about 1.5% relative. Both are legitimate MXFP8 roundings.
- The proper fix belongs in AITER: make the fused `_fp8` epilogue use the same scale rule as `fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort`, so numerics don't depend on tuner choice. AITER issue: TODO. AITER `main` (2026-10-14) still has the same rule and rows.
- The `.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml` trigger on `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` (added in #61559) is kept, so AITER bumps run the mono tests.

**Not a duplicate.** This follows up the #61559 revert. Open PR search for an AITER v0.1.25 re-bump: TODO.

title: [Perf][HiSparse] Segment host KV pool backing files
body:
HiSparse stores its host KV pool as one logical chunk. The segmented backing support in merged #59546 splits whole rows, so this pool still uses one `/dev/shm` file, where page-cache insertion limits parallel pre-faulting.

Split the single chunk at 2 MiB boundaries and enable up to 32 backing files for HiSparse. The mapping stays contiguous; capacity and CUDA registration ranges stay unchanged. This is the HiSparse follow-up to #59546; the landed prerequisite is no longer part of this PR's diff.

Previously measured on two nodes with 8 H100 workers and a 1 TiB pool each: RAM preparation fell from **264.5 / 232.3 s to 44.5 / 44.4 s**. Preparation plus pinning fell from **378.1 / 340.6 s to 152.3 / 146.8 s**. These benchmarks were not rerun for the merge update.

Validation after merging current main:

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py -q --tb=short`: 161 passed, 2 skipped. In the CPU-only validation pod, 5 GPU-dependent cases failed because no NVIDIA driver was available, and 3 errored during device detection. The previous GPU validation before this merge update passed all 171 tests.
- Pre-commit checks for the four PR files, including mypy: passed.

Updated with Codex assistance.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSV4] Keep one decoder-replay row on unfinished prefills on gfx942
body:
## Overview

On ROCm, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decoder SWA replay (#59039) keeps `min(query_len, 128)` rows through layers 20–39 for every prefill chunk. Keep one row when that chunk does not finish the prompt. The finishing chunk, decode, and prompt-logprobs stay on the window. The check is `current_platform.is_rocm()` in the shared model state. CUDA keeps `min(query_len, window)` and the capture walk that starts at the window.

## Claims

- On ROCm, an unfinished prefill chunk keeps 1 replay row. The chunk that finishes the prompt, decode, and prompt-logprobs stay on `min(query_len, window)`. CUDA takes the previous branch: `min(query_len, window)`, and the capture walk that starts at `layers.window`.
- Median TTFT, one run of 20 prompts: 8k is flat with DSpark on or off. 256k MC2 is −7.1%. 256k MC8 is −4.9%.
- Median TPOT at 256k MC2 is +0.33 ms (+4.2%). On that same run mean TPOT is 7.81 → 7.71 ms, P99 TPOT is 11.88 → 11.47 ms, and tok/s rises. Decode keeps `min(query_len, window)`. The other median TPOT points stay within 0.1 ms, except 256k MC8 at −1.60 ms.
- On ROCm, an empty `decoder_replay_cudagraph_capture_sizes` now includes 1. The previous default started at the 128-token window, so a 1-row replay missed every graph and ran eager. An explicit list that omits 1 is rejected on ROCm for the same reason. CUDA still uses the previous default.

## Validation

### Performance

4× MI325X (gfx942), TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, vLLM `0.32.0rc1.dev100+g77154ca61.rocm723`, ROCm 7.2.3. Same process and flags on both arms. The numbers are from the nightly with this kept-length rule. This commit is that rule behind `current_platform.is_rocm()`. With a 128-token window and a capture bound of 512, an empty capture-size list on ROCm is `[1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384, 512]`. Each entry is a padded replay-batch length that gets a CUDA graph. The baseline arm used the previous default, which starts at 128. The measured one-row arm passed that list explicitly, because the previous default did not generate it. A serve of this head is still required before the PR leaves draft.

QuickReduce is the upstream INT4 path: `Using ['QUICK_REDUCE', 'AITER_CUSTOM', 'PYNCCL'] all-reduce backends`. MXFP8 is the emulation kernel: `Using EmulationMxfp8LinearKernel for MXFP8 GEMM`.

`vllm bench serve`, random data, 20 prompts, `--num-warmups 1`, output length 1024. One run per cell. Each cell is baseline → one-row. Δ% is that difference divided by the baseline.

| Shape | Median TTFT | Δ | Median TPOT | Δ | tok/s | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8k→1k MC2, DSpark, seed 7 | 336.2 → 337.1 ms | +1 ms (+0.3%) | 3.96 → 4.03 ms | +0.07 ms (+1.8%) | 431.1 → 430.2 | −0.2% |
| 8k→1k MC2, no DSpark, seed 7 | 463.2 → 463.7 ms | +1 ms (+0.1%) | 11.67 → 11.63 ms | −0.04 ms (−0.3%) | 165.8 → 165.7 | −0.0% |
| 8k→1k MC6, DSpark, seed 9 | 1075.7 → 1068.3 ms | −7 ms (−0.7%) | 6.22 → 6.29 ms | +0.07 ms (+1.1%) | 699.8 → 714.8 | +2.1% |
| 256k→1k MC2, DSpark, seed 7 | 13109.6 → 12181.2 ms | −928 ms (−7.1%) | 7.94 → 8.27 ms | +0.33 ms (+4.2%) | 95.5 → 98.2 | +2.9% |
| 256k→1k MC8, DSpark, seed 10 | 23984.5 → 22806.5 ms | −1178 ms (−4.9%) | 47.31 → 45.71 ms | −1.60 ms (−3.4%) | 109.3 → 113.5 | +3.9% |

An 8k prompt is one chunk, and that chunk finishes the prompt, so both arms replay the same 128 rows. The 8k median TPOT movement is 0.07 ms. At 8k MC6 the median TPOT is +0.07 ms while mean TPOT is −0.10 ms and P99 TPOT is −0.80 ms.

On vLLM `0.31.1rc1.dev23+g43b4aaea3`, a profile timed the replay launches inside one incomplete 16k chunk. Layers 0–19 still run on all 16384 tokens. Layer 20 writes KV for every token, and the rest of layer 20 plus layers 21–39 run only on the kept rows. With 128 kept rows those short launches were a median 9.45 ms on a pure prefill step (17 steps). With 1 kept row the same span was 1.80 ms. Steps that also contain decode went from 17.05 ms to 3.26 ms (175 steps). The table above is the nightly serving measurement.

### Accuracy

One-row arm only, probabilistic DSpark (`draft_sample_method=probabilistic`). GSM8K 5-shot, n=1319: strict-match 0.9196 ± 0.0075, flexible-extract 0.9196 ± 0.0075. Published off scores are 0.9272 / 0.9265. RULER `niah_single_2` at 16384, 0-shot, n=500: 1.0. A kernel-level max abs difference was not measured. The synthetic acceptance schedule on the benches is the configured schedule.

### Test plan

No pytest. The runs were `vllm serve` and `vllm bench serve` on 4× MI325X. GSM8K is `lm_eval run --model local-completions` with `num_concurrent=256`, `max_gen_toks=2048`, `max_length=262144`, `batch_size auto`, and the task's default 5-shot. RULER is `niah_single_2` with `max_seq_lengths=[16384]`.

<details>
<summary>Serve and bench</summary>

```bash
export HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4

vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8014 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-model-len 266240 \
  --moe-backend aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --language-model-only \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-log-requests \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"greedy","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_rates":[0.9,0.8,0.7,0.6,0.5],"enable_adaptive_verification":false}'

vllm bench serve \
  --backend vllm --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8014 \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer "$MODEL" \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 262144 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts 20 --max-concurrency 8 --num-warmups 1 --seed 10 \
  --ignore-eos --trust-remote-code \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
```

</details>

## Details

An unfinished 16k chunk was still building a replay batch of up to 128 rows through layers 20–39. One row carries that chunk forward. The chunk that finishes the prompt still replays the window.

`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model_state.py`: `is_prefilling` stays true on the chunk that finishes the prompt, so an unfinished chunk is `num_computed_prefill_tokens + query_len < prefill_len`. On ROCm that request's kept length is 1. `_keeps_rows_np` still keeps every prompt-logprobs row. `layers.window` stays the scalar the gather kernel already reads. `kept_lens` was already a host array, so this adds no device sync. CUDA leaves the limit as `layers.window`, which is the previous `min(query_len, window)`.

`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/decoder_replay_cudagraph.py`: when the capture-size list is empty, ROCm also captures `[1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96]` below the window. The walk from `layers.window` up is unchanged. On CUDA that walk is the whole list. An explicit list that does not contain 1 raises on ROCm.

`amd/model.py` and `amd/vl_model.py` still return the NVIDIA model state. There is no AMD replay-batch class.

The numbers above are gfx942 only. CUDA was not measured. The CUDA lines are the previous expressions. #59039 is the 128-row replay path this trims. #61554 is cold replay under prefill context parallel. #60320 trims DSpark draft context, not these decoder rows.

Depends on: none beyond #59039.

title: [ROCm][Perf][Kimi-K3] Limit mono verification to conc4 shapes through M32
body:
## Summary Optimize Kimi-K3 mono speculative verification for conc4 serving on MI355X TP8, with selected batches through **32 verification tokens per step (M32)**. This covers four requests with up to eight verification tokens each. Dispatch follows the model step's row count; batches above M32 use the existing vLLM operators. - **K1:** bounded LDS staging, tiled state updates and shape-specific worker assignments. - **K1/K2 fusion:** one persistent launch with worker reuse for eligible batches through M16. - **K2:** compact routing and cached expert intermediates through M32, with projection-panel pipelining at M28/M30/M32. - **Graph replay:** immutable pinned argument tables remain alive across capture and replay. This extends #60683 at `9c6c96d8ef` with K1/K2 worker reuse and panel-based K2 scheduling for speculative verification. The scope differs from #61435's row-tiling and MLA prologue/epilogue fusion; MLA attention and DCP output merging complete before this PR's K2 consumes their output. ## Performance — AgenticX conc4 **Kimi-K3 · 8× MI355X · TP8/DCP1 · DSpark k5 · 3600 seconds.** FP8 GPU KV cache, offload disabled, prefix caching enabled, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs; synthetic acceptance length 3.62, seed 42. Concurrency 4 refers to AgenticX session trees. | Metric | Base (no mono) | #60683 | #61694 | vs base | vs #60683 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Output tok/s | 159.84 | 181.91 | 190.84 | +19.4% | +4.9% | | Total tok/s | 22453.69 | 24149.27 | 25436.55 | +13.3% | +5.3% | | Mean / median TTFT ms | 1061.39 / 521.11 | 790.88 / 525.92 | 828.82 / 523.70 | −21.9% | +4.8% | | Mean / median TPOT ms | 5.47 / 6.36 | 4.82 / 4.47 | 4.80 / 4.39 | −12.2% | −0.4% | | Mean ITL ms | 5.47 | 4.82 | 4.80 | −12.2% | −0.4% | | p90 interactivity tok/s | 118.98 | 123.45 | 146.53 | +23.2% | +18.7% | Percentage changes compare #61694 with each reference and use the mean for paired latency rows. Interactivity follows AgenticX's definition: `1 / p90 ITL` with ITL in seconds; higher is better. All three benchmark results passed validation; successful/failed profiling requests were 475/2, 507/3 and 538/2, respectively. *Measurement scope: one run per build. The #60683 reference is `9c6c96d8ef`; the #61694 candidate was measured before the M32 cap, on a different MI355X TP8 system from Base/#60683, with different KV-cache capacity. These comparisons do not isolate the kernel effect; throughput of the current M32 revision remains pending.* ## Kernel design K1 covers attention residual mixing and normalization, input projection, convolution, KDA state updates and gated RMSNorm. K2 covers output projection, TP reduction, MLP residual mixing, routed/shared experts and the final reductions. | Rows in the step | Selected implementation | |---|---| | 1–16 | K2; eligible KDA verification lengths 2, 4, 6 or 8 use combined K1/K2 outside FULL graphs | | 18, 20, 24 | K2 with compact routing metadata, sparse expert-pick lists and expert intermediates cached in LDS | | 28, 30, 32 | The same K2 schedule, with projection consumers advancing on ready input panels | | Other widths | Existing projection and MoE operators; eligible K1/post-projection KDA paths are also bounded by M32 | ### Small batches: reuse K1 workers in K2 The #60683 snapshot uses separate K1 and K2 launches for batches through eight rows. This PR combines eligible batches through sixteen rows: ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph F["K1 + K2: one persistent launch"] A["AttnRes + input RMSNorm"] --> B["Input projection + f_b
bounded LDS slices"] B --> C["Convolution + gates
tiled KDA state update"] C --> D["Gated RMSNorm
publish ready values"] W["Completed K1 workers
prefetch K2 weights"] --> E["K2 output projection"] D -->|"matching epoch ready"| E E --> G["TP sum + MLP AttnRes
routed and shared experts"] G --> H["Latent TP sum + RMSNorm
up projection + shared merge
final TP sum"] end ``` Each CTA reuses its workers and private LDS as its work completes. Epoch-tagged handoffs prevent K2 from reading unfinished K1 output; TP consumers also wait for the required peer data. FULL graph execution uses separate launches. ### M18–M32: compact K2 routing and panel handoffs Wide K2 stores compact routing metadata and sparse expert-pick lists, keeping expert intermediates in LDS. At M28/M30/M32, the output-projection reduction and MLP AttnRes publish input panels for the router, latent projection and shared-expert projection. M30/M32 KDA uses the existing input projection followed by eligible fused post-projection work. Deep residual-block schedules use streamed AttnRes staging to bound LDS usage. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Output projection"] --> B["TP sum + MLP AttnRes"] B -->|"ready input panel"| R["Router + top-16 selection"] B -->|"ready input panel"| L["Latent down projection
+ quantization"] B -->|"ready input panel"| S["Shared gate/up projection
+ SiTU"] R --> X["Selected experts
gate/up + SiTU + down"] L --> X X --> N["Latent TP sum + RMSNorm"] S --> SD["Shared down projection"] N -->|"normalized output ready"| U["Up projection + shared merge"] SD -->|"shared output ready"| U U --> O["Final TP sum"] ``` Panel handoffs apply to the front of K2; the final merge waits for the completed latent-normalization and shared-output stages. Cross-CTA handoffs use global/peer memory and readiness tags. Scratch and peer buffers are sized for M32. The diagrams show dependencies; actual overlap depends on the selected shape and worker schedule. ## Validation | Check | Result | |---|---| | K1 numerics, state updates and dispatch/fallback | 92 passed | | TP8 K2 numerics and K1/K2 graph replay | 10 passed | | Changed-file pre-commit, including mypy | Passed | | Diff checks | Passed | | GSM8K smoke, 64 samples, 5-shot, conc4/k5 | 61/64 (95.31%); no empty or truncated outputs | The 102 kernel/dispatch cases cover M24/M28/M30/M32, deep residual blocks, block resets, changed-input graph replay, scratch allocation and fallback above M32. The GSM8K smoke used an earlier candidate, seed 42, temperature 0, thinking disabled and a 4096-token output limit. Full-model accuracy equivalence of the current M32 revision remains pending.

title: [Bug]: NixlConnector P/D: first handshake per remote engine stalls all DP decode ranks (THP compaction in `_build_fa_remote`); late reads after lease expiry return HTTP 200
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM 0.31.0 (`vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0`), numpy 2.2.6, NIXL over UCX
- 2 nodes, 8x H200 each, Linux 6.x, THP `enabled=madvise`, `defrag=madvise`
- Most of host RAM (more than 60%) is pinned in `/dev/shm` by the OffloadingConnector CPU tier and Engram

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On the first P/D traffic after startup, a decode rank's first NIXL handshake with a prefill engine can stall the whole decode instance for seconds to minutes (up to about 45 min in our runs). With the default 30 s `kv_lease_duration`, the prefill frees the KV unread. The decode later reads the freed blocks and returns HTTP 200.

The cause is the descriptor build on the handshake path combined with numpy's huge page advice:

1. For each new remote engine, `NixlBaseConnectorWorker.add_remote_agent` (`nixl/base_worker.py:2438` at v0.31.0) calls `_build_fa_remote` (`:2065-2112`). It builds one descriptor per block per KV region of the whole remote pool with numpy (`np.arange`, `np.empty((n, 3))`, `np.concatenate`). With a large KV pool this is several million descriptors and about 100 MB of fresh arrays per handshake.
2. numpy calls `madvise(MADV_HUGEPAGE)` on large allocations. With THP `enabled=madvise` and `defrag=madvise`, the first touch of each 2 MB range runs synchronous direct compaction.
3. When most host RAM is pinned, compaction almost always fails (`compact_fail` rises with `compact_stall`), and each fault costs milliseconds to seconds.
4. The faulting thread holds the mmap lock, so the worker's other threads block too.
5. With DP + EP, all decode ranks meet in the all-reduce of `sync_cudagraph_and_dp_padding` (`v1/worker/gpu/dp_utils.py:77`) every step. One stalled worker stops all ranks, so other requests cannot start their handshakes and no rank sends lease heartbeats.

The duration depends on memory fragmentation at that moment, so the same setup is sometimes fine.

#### Evidence

Fresh servers, no warm-up, 30 s lease, 10 concurrent cold requests:

| numpy huge pages | Handshake thread system CPU per worker | Client warmup | Expired leases / invalid reads |
|---|---|---|---|
| default (on) | 0.5 to 69.6 s | 89 s | 8 / 8, all HTTP 200 |
| `NUMPY_MADVISE_HUGEPAGE=0` | 0.26 to 0.80 s | 25 s | 0 / 0 |

A py-spy profile of one decode worker put 263 of 286 samples in `add_remote_agent` inside `_build_fa_remote`, mostly memcpy under `np.concatenate`. The NIXL calls themselves took about 0.2 s per handshake.

Prefill log:

```
(Worker_DP5_EP5) WARNING 10-14 18:59:20 [base_worker.py:3074] Releasing expired KV blocks for request <id> which were retrieved by 0 remote worker(s) before lease expired.
(Worker_DP5_EP5) ERROR 10-14 19:00:00 [pull_worker.py:663] Potentially invalid KV blocks for unrecognized request <id> were retrieved by a decode worker. They may have expired.
```

#### Expected behavior

- A handshake should not stall the engine. The remote descriptors should not cost O(remote pool) fresh memory per remote engine. Prefill engines share one block layout and differ only in base addresses, so the descriptors could be built once, or only for the blocks a request reads.
- At minimum, the connector should not request huge pages for these arrays.
- Lease heartbeats should start before the handshake finishes, and a read after lease expiry should fail the request instead of returning HTTP 200 (#61229, PR #61549).

#### How to reproduce

This script repeats the numpy work of `_build_fa_remote` for 4.3M descriptors and prints the time and the compaction counters:

```python
import sys, time, numpy as np
def vm():
    return {k: int(v) for k, v in (l.split() for l in open("/proc/vmstat"))
            if k in ("compact_stall", "compact_fail", "thp_fault_alloc")}
n, regions = 4_300_000, 100
v0, t0 = vm(), time.perf_counter()
parts = []
for i in range(regions):
    addrs = np.uint64(0x7F0000000000 + i * 2**33) + np.arange(n // regions, dtype=np.uint64) * np.uint64(19008)
    out = np.empty((addrs.shape[0], 3), dtype=np.uint64)
    out[:, 0] = addrs; out[:, 1] = 19008; out[:, 2] = 0
    parts.append(out)
arr = np.concatenate(parts)
v1 = vm()
print(round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3), "s", {k: v1[k] - v0[k] for k in v0})
```

On a decode node next to a running vLLM instance: 0.96 s with 94 failed compaction stalls by default, 0.11 s with no stalls under `NUMPY_MADVISE_HUGEPAGE=0`.

To see it in vLLM, run a P/D pair (DP8 + EP8 per node) on hosts with most memory pinned, using NixlConnector in pull mode plus the OffloadingConnector CPU tier:

```bash
--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[
  {"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"},
  {"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"spec_name":"TieringOffloadingSpec","cpu_bytes_to_use":<bytes>}}]}}'
```

Send concurrent first requests to cold rank pairs through any P/D proxy. Watch the system CPU of each decode worker's `vllm-nixl-handshake-initiator` thread and `compact_stall` in `/proc/vmstat`, then repeat with `NUMPY_MADVISE_HUGEPAGE=0`.

#### Workarounds

- `NUMPY_MADVISE_HUGEPAGE=0` in the server environment.
- A longer `kv_lease_duration` on the prefill.
- One warm-up request per prefill and decode rank pair, sequentially, before real traffic.

#### Related

- #61229 and PR #61549: lease expiry during a pending READ makes the decode consume overwritten KV silently. Same consequence; our trigger is a slow first handshake.
- #60019: synchronous O(num_blocks) NIXL peer registration in the P2P offload tier stalls the rank.
- #53095: push connector leases expire under concurrency with the same `retrieved by 0 remote worker(s)` message.

This report was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code) from our logs and reviewed by the submitter.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Perf][Model Loader] DeepSeek V4.1 Flash mixed RunAI loading
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Consolidate the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash RunAI loading stack: stream the VL wrapper, keep ordinary weights distributed, read shared CPU Engram tables once, and preserve/select the DSpark S3 weight source. This draft includes ported prior work and the experimental integration measured on eight H200s.

## Claims

- Keep TP1/DP8/EP8 ordinary loading distributed while oversized Engram shards load into CPU staging. Shared embeddings/scales have one reader; the small non-shared tensors in those shards still reach every GPU.
- Pass the reader process group to the streamer before metadata; only the single shared Engram CPU reader passes `None`. Independent readers retain shared filesystem queue sizing.
- Preserve streamed tensor lifetimes without materializing the full language checkpoint. Borrowed GPU tensors keep vLLM's normal clone; shared CPU embedding sources are consumed synchronously.
- Load the same-checkpoint DSpark draft from S3 and select its three required shards from the verified local index.
- Require `runai-model-streamer>=0.17.0` in the Python extra and Docker default, with matching 0.17.0 CI requirements and cloud adapters. Released Linux wheels require glibc 2.30; CUDA/CPU/ROCm lock generation targets 2.31, the lowest compatible target supported by the pinned `uv`. XPU already targets 2.39.

## Validation

Real DeepSeek V4.1 Flash revision `5254448`, eight H200s, TP1/DP8/EP8, Engram CPU offload and shared DP storage, DSpark5, RunAI **0.17.0**, `spans`, plus the separate streamer rank-discovery fix [model-streamer #252](https://github.com/dsx-ai-factory/model-streamer/pull/252). Ordinary staging remained **4 GiB/rank** (32 GiB node total under 0.17.0); oversized CPU staging remained **100 GiB**.

| Loading scope | Earlier S3 integration | Combined patched integration |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Ordinary 286.1 GiB | 585 s | 37.7 s |
| Engram 189.1 GiB | 140 s | 88.4 s |
| Target payload, ordinary plus Engram | 725 s | 126 s |
| Draft-containing 7.4 GiB | — | approximately 6 s |

This is the **combined stack/configuration result**, not the isolated effect of this PR: released 0.17.0 already supplies native read coalescing/ring improvements, and different nodes were used. One full model run per integration configuration; no repeated same-node A/B startup campaign is claimed.

The patched integration reached Ready with zero restarts. Full vLLM model loading, including approximately 150 s of host-table initialization, took **291 s**. Cold container-to-Ready took approximately **15m28s**, including regression preflight, setup and kernel/graph warmup. The two-minute payload time is not a two-minute server startup claim. Cached NFS/page-cache default-loader controls took 110–113 s for target weights and 265–279 s for full model loading; this does not claim a speedup over cached filesystem loading.

- Focused wrapper/loader/draft regressions: **12 passed**, 27 deselected, 9.62 s.
- Real eight-H200 shared Engram toy loading: **all eight ranks passed**, including FP8/scales, follower synchronization and independent GPU weights in the CPU shard.
- Updated process-group integration: **4 passed**, one unrelated GPT-2 download test deselected, 5.38 s. Covers the three distinct mixed-loader paths and real native borrowed-buffer cloning.
- Updated streamer dependency: **45 passed + 7 subtests**, no skips, 3.50 s. Real eight-process Gloo coverage verifies metadata/payload reader sizing, idle peers, a non-contiguous subgroup, sequential handles and caller-group lifetime; cleanup-failure coverage verifies environment restoration.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks and Linux-target mypy completed. Native macOS mypy reports two pre-existing Linux-only `os.posix_fadvise`/`os.POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED` errors; equivalent Linux-target checks passed.
- Dependency bump: CUDA/CPU/ROCm/XPU locks regenerated with `uv 0.11.1`; `prek run --files` passed all applicable hooks, including the four dependency resolvers and Docker version consistency. Existing unrelated pins were retained; regeneration also restored the `openai-harmony==0.0.8` transitive entry required by the already-pinned `gpt-oss` package.

The updated process-group tests ran on an isolated CPU-only Linux pod with the released native core 0.17.0 and the modified Python SDK from [model-streamer #252](https://github.com/dsx-ai-factory/model-streamer/pull/252), now at [0e0ebbb](https://github.com/SherifWaly/runai-model-streamer/commit/0e0ebbb8a97f3b8ccf42c62f3b5afcc632934c1c). **This revision requires that matching Python SDK; the released 0.17.0 Python API does not yet accept `process_group`.** The final dependency version must be set after the companion API is released. These tests do not establish a new model-loading or NFS performance result, and no revised serving deployment was validated.

Latest integration reproduction with that matching SDK installed:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -s \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/runai_streamer_loader/test_weight_utils.py \
  -k 'not test_runai_model_loader'
```

Focused reproduction in a CUDA vLLM environment:

```bash
VLLM_RUNAI_BORROWED_WEIGHTS=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_vl_stream_weights.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/runai_streamer_loader/test_weight_utils.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/runai_streamer_loader/test_runai_model_streamer_loader.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_dspark_utils.py \
  -q -k 'streams_language_model_group or clones_reused_buffers or explicit_cpu_shards or index_selection or inherits_only_shared_checkpoint_uri'
```

The hardware results came from the original integration on `fe4df3df0` (PyTorch 2.13.0/CUDA 13). This branch is rebased on main; a complete model rerun on the rebased head, HTTP text/image/tool checks, draft acceptance and quality evaluation remain pending. No output-quality equivalence is claimed. The new wrapper test is ported with its Buildkite entry; existing model-executor/worker jobs cover the extended suites. Full-model CI additionally needs the checkpoint, eight GPUs and sufficient host memory.

## Details

The reproduction example explicitly selects the Python API frontend with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0`. It supports an explicit local tokenizer metadata path for S3 deployment. This is independent of RunAI tensor loading. A separate eight-B200 canary using preserved image digest `e5c9e6bb82f645e8fca04e4d395743ee5ed473a62b98942d65f83c35d0c69301` and the cached filesystem loader reached Ready with zero restarts and passed 16 serving checks: health/model discovery, text, SSE streaming, image input, forced/automatic tool calls, concurrent requests directed to DP ranks 0–7, and per-engine metric deltas of exactly one request per rank. It validates the existing Python frontend and DP header routing; it does not validate this PR's loading changes or its rebased head. The H200 Python/S3 canary remains unvalidated because BAR's requested SUNK QoS has reached its 80-GPU quota.

Included prior work and attribution:

- **Ported VL streaming and its regression/CI wiring from #58857**, by @gitbisector; original author credit is retained in the commit trailer.
- **Adapted the model-owned draft shard-selection approach from #60759**, by @zhy76. This integration uses a verified local index and a DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark unused-weight predicate; it is not the full generic metadata-selection implementation from that PR.
- **Related draft-source fix #48023**, by @kunling-anyscale, and issue #42060. The recipe uses `method=dspark`, not `method=mtp`. This branch fixes the observed DSpark config-only-cache failure in its loader using a shallow copy of the resolved config; it does not cherry-pick the older generic speculative-config patch.

These pieces are deliberately included in one reviewable draft alongside the CPU Engram integration. Refreshed duplicate checks found the existing PRs above; their overlap is explicit. #61303 optimizes pinned GPU staging and #57195/#61553 change shared-storage inference/topology support; they do not implement this mixed RunAI single-reader path.

The current loader's sorted VL input retains the stream; the GPU streamer cannot safely stage the oversized CPU tables on an H200. Splitting GPU/CPU phases addresses that destination mismatch. Shared followers receive meta placeholders so the existing single-writer weight loaders retain equal call counts/barriers; non-shared tensors are broadcast as raw bytes. The streamer dependency scopes reader discovery before metadata: ordinary readers supply their process group, while the lone CPU reader passes `None` to avoid discovery collectives.

Before merge:

- Replace checkpoint-specific file-list/index opt-ins and private storage-owner discovery with a reviewed configuration/metadata contract; validate missing/stale index and shard failures.
- Harden collective/error ordering, tensor lifetime and configuration validation across supported topologies; test TP/PP, reload and multi-node compatibility explicitly.
- Re-run the model on the final head, complete request/acceptance/eval validation and human line review.
- Resolve/release the separate streamer dependency. It is not vendored into this vLLM diff.

All experiment switches default off. The documented initial scope is one eight-H200 DP/EP server. See `docs/models/extensions/runai_model_streamer.md` for the exact environment and staging configuration. This draft adds loader-time synchronization, not steady-state inference synchronization, and remains experimental until the items above are resolved.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [ ] **Design Fit:** Initial integration is measured; generic metadata/configuration and compatibility review remain pending.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Regressions, eight-rank toy loading and real-model startup recorded; final-head request/acceptance/eval validation remains pending.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Applicable checks completed, docs and ported CI wiring included; platform limitation documented.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Scope, port attribution, dependencies, measurements, root causes and draft limitations are explicit.

title: [XPU] Fix XPU attention-sink reload test failures (Event shim + hy_v4 skip)
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes two XPU-only failures in `test_attention_sink_deepseek_hy_loading_uses_parameter_loader` seen in [Buildkite intel-ci build 14222](https://buildkite.com/vllm/intel-ci/builds/14222#01a13cd3-6a2e-4f68-90bb-bf8575cef5c1). Follow-up to #57797, which added this test.

## Claims

- `torch.cuda.Event` shim (`_xpu_event`) was a plain function, not a class. `_torch_cuda_wrapper` patches it onto `torch.cuda.Event` permanently (by design), so any later `torch.cuda.Event | None` annotation evaluated in the same process (e.g. in `deepseek_v41/common/engram.py`) raised `TypeError`, since only types support `|`. Fixed by making `_xpu_event` a class, matching the existing `_EventPlaceholder` pattern in `vllm/v1/worker/cpu/shm.py`.
- `hy_v4` legitimately doesn't support XPU (`vllm/models/hy_v4/__init__.py` raises `NotImplementedError` on import). The test parametrization didn't skip it on XPU, so it failed outright. Added `skipif(current_platform.is_xpu())`, following the existing ROCm-only `skipif` pattern already used in this file.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_xpu_model_runner.py tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k "torch_cuda_wrapper or attention_sink_deepseek_hy" -v
```
All pass (hy_v4 cases skip, since this sandbox itself resolves to the XPU platform). Also reproduced the original `TypeError` against the pre-fix code and confirmed it's gone after the fix. `ruff check` passes.

title: [Core] Add max_async_kv_loads_per_step to cap new async KV loads per step
body:
## Purpose

On a P/D decode instance, a request that starts an async KV load moves to `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` and does not take a running slot. At very high concurrency the waiting queue is long and the decode batch is full. Then each time one running slot frees, a single `schedule()` call starts a load for every waiting request whose blocks fit and allocates KV blocks for each of them. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with ~130K-token prompts that is 90-140 requests per engine and about 1.6 ms of Python each, so one step stalls for 150-290 ms. With data parallelism every DP rank waits for that step.

- New `SchedulerConfig.max_async_kv_loads_per_step` (`--max-async-kv-loads-per-step`). Once N async KV loads have started in a step, the scheduler stops taking requests from the waiting queue until the next step. Requests that already hold KV blocks are still drained first, as before.
- The default `None` keeps the current behavior. The limit only matters at very high concurrency, when the waiting queue is much longer than the number of slots that free per step. At low or moderate concurrency, few requests start loading per step anyway.

Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs for `async kv load per step`, `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS admission`, `limit async KV loads scheduler` and `max async kv`. #42568 lets completed async loads be promoted under saturation; it does not limit how many loads start per step.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/config/scheduler.py vllm/engine/arg_utils.py vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py
```

New test `test_max_async_kv_loads_per_step`: with a limit of 2, five remote-prefill requests start loading 2, then 4, then 5 at a time over three steps.

## Test Result

238 passed on CPU. The 2 failures (`test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`, `test_diffusion_read_deferral_keeps_a_longer_pp_wait`) need GPUs for pipeline parallelism and fail the same way without this change. Pre-commit (ruff, format, typos, mypy, config docstrings) passes.

## E2E (P/D, very high concurrency)

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB300, 7 prefill instances (DEP2) and 1 decode instance (DEP16), NIXL, AgentX multi-turn agentic trace at concurrency 4800, with the decode batch full:

| | tok/s/GPU | P90 interactivity (tok/s/user) |
|---|---:|---:|
| no limit | 460K | 109 |
| limit 4 | 516K | 153 |

The decode step time returned to the decode-only level (22.4 ms). These runs used a development tree and also included two smaller CPU fixes on the same admission path, which will be sent separately: the in-flight prefill reservation is summed once per scheduling pass instead of once per admitted request, and the block-id walk reads `_block_hash` directly. A limit of 4 beat 10-12. With a full decode batch, a higher limit let 40-80 requests that already hold KV blocks pile up per engine, and each 10 of them added 0.12-0.15 ms per step.

---

title: [Perf][Model] Qwen4Exp QSA DCP: follow-ups to #59279 (combine, workspace buffers, MTP decode path)
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Follow-up to #59279, as discussed with @sungsooha. It cuts per-step DCP cost of Qwen4Exp QSA decode context parallelism, mainly on the sm_80 (A100) path: fewer kernels and copies in each DCP attention step, no indexer prefill path for MTP verify rows, and MTP with an interleave above 1.

**Depends on #59279.** This branch is #59279 (head 6f650772a) plus 10 commits; as @sungsooha asked, the follow-up work and its benchmarks are here, next to the code. Until #59279 merges, the diff below also shows its commits; review only the commits after 6f650772a. Our earlier commit that dropped the empty-owner LSE neutralize is gone: @sungsooha made the same change in #59279 (6f650772a).

## Claims

- MTP verify rows stay on the QSA decode path under DCP. Before, every DCP + MTP verify step ran the indexer prefill path, also inside FULL CUDA graphs.
- The DCP combine runs without layout copies and fuses the output gate; the DCP buffers come from the workspace, reserved before CUDA graph capture.
- Each new selection is localized once and reused by MTP `skip_topk` steps.
- The reader stores the LSE directly when it runs one split (no merge kernel). Bitwise equal.
- The replicated selector declares `supports_mtp_with_cp_non_trivial_interleave_size`, so MTP works with `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size` > 1.
- No change without DCP. The default selector stays replicated.

## Validation

**Serving (8 × A100-SXM4-40GB).** TP8 + EP, DCP 4, FP8 KV, MTP 3, `--max-num-batched-tokens 2048`. MLPerf agentic multi-turn workload, 32 requests in flight, 1 × 60 min per arm, 0 failed requests.

SLO (Artificial Analysis percentiles): P95 TTFT ≤ 2.93 s and P95 TPOT ≤ 21.74 ms (P5 output speed ≥ 46 tokens/s). "SLO pass" is the share of requests that meet both limits.

| Arm | Requests/s | Output tok/s per GPU | Output tok/s per user | TTFT P50 / P95 | TPOT P50 / P95 | SLO pass |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #59279 (+ its block-table fix) | 2.72 | 140.8 | 42.5 | 990 / 2,137 ms | 18.8 / 29.3 ms | 68.8 % |
| **This PR** | **2.80** | **149.8** | **45.3** | 967 / 2,233 ms | **17.4 / 27.8 ms** | **76.2 %** |

These two runs used an earlier #59279 head (c9de36da9). On that head the reader returned a BF16 partial, and this PR combined it in BF16. This branch keeps the FP32 partial of the current #59279 head, so the combine moves twice the bytes; serving numbers on the current head are still to be measured. One run per arm.

**Tests (1 × A100-SXM4-40GB, nightly 5555a2d8f image with each head's Python tree, one pytest session per file).** #59279 base / this PR:

| File | #59279 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_gdn_metadata_builder.py` | 61 passed | 62 passed |
| `test_qsa_dcp_combine.py` | — | 15 passed |
| `test_qsa_dcp_localize.py` | 13 passed, 3 failed | 42 passed, 4 failed |
| `test_qsa_selector_write_mask.py` | 7 passed | 7 passed |
| `test_qsa_dcp_cache_policy.py` | 18 passed | 20 passed |

The failures are the same in both: the FP8 cases of `test_sharded_ranks_reproduce_the_single_rank_result` do not compile on sm_80 (`_qsa_sparse_paged_gqa_splitk_kernel`: "type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture"). This PR adds one more parametrization of that test, which fails the same way on sm_80. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean.

**Engine start (4 × A100, Model Runner V2).** Qwen4Exp with 4 layers (3 GDN + 1 QSA), dummy weights, TP4 + EP, DCP 4, MTP 3, FP8 KV, `max_model_len` 262144: #59279 and this PR both start, capture CUDA graphs and generate. #59279 c9de36da9 (before its block-table fix) fails in the same check, so the check reaches that path. On Model Runner V1, this model cannot start with MTP at all (`llm_base_proposer.load_model` reads `config.image_token_index`; `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration` is not in its list), with or without DCP; that is unrelated to this PR.

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_qsa_dcp_combine.py tests/v1/attention/test_qsa_dcp_localize.py tests/v1/core/test_qsa_dcp_cache_policy.py tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py
```

## Details

| Commit | What and why |
|---|---|
| keep MTP verify rows as decodes | `supports_dcp_with_varlen=True` for the GDN builder and the QSA side-cache builder. The QSA side caches, the GDN state and the replicated selector are not DCP-sharded, so the reorder threshold stays 1 + num_spec. MRV2: QSA side cache only (GDN routes by draft count). Not bitwise: verify rows move from `qsa_select_paged_prefill` to `qsa_select_paged_decode`. |
| copy-free LSE combine, fused gate | `qsa_dcp_lse_ag_out_rs`: all-gather of the LSE, head-major LSE correction into a reserved buffer, dim-0 reduce-scatter; no `movedim`/`contiguous` copies. One Triton gate kernel (`expf` + IEEE division, the fp32 PyTorch sigmoid formula). Other combines (`dcp_a2a_lse_reduce`) are called unchanged, with `ctx` and `is_lse_base_on_e`. |
| reserve DCP buffers in the workspace | Partial output, LSE and the combine buffer come from `current_workspace_manager().get_simultaneous`, sized for `max_num_batched_tokens`, so the workspace does not grow after capture. |
| localize each selection once | The indexer writes the rank-local selection into `topk_buffer`; MTP `skip_topk` steps reuse it, and the attention no longer localizes. |
| store the LSE directly for one split | With `return_lse` and one split, the reader writes output and LSE without the merge kernel. Bitwise. |
| tests: indexer wiring, combine, DCP 4 interleave 1 | |
| allow MTP with a non-trivial interleave | The replicated QSA impl declares `supports_mtp_with_cp_non_trivial_interleave_size`; a GPU test checks MTP verify rows against the single-rank result at interleaves 1, 4, 16 and 8. |
| run the FP8 cases on Ampere | Below sm_89 the reader takes e4m3 as uint8 bytes; the tests use that storage instead of skipping. |
| keep the FP32 DCP partial of the base | Rebase adaptation to the FP32 partial of #59279. |
| import the QSA module after the model module | Test-only: qsa.py and model.py import each other, so the tests import the model first. |

**Size:** +378 / −93 outside tests (6 files); tests +702 / −1. Most of it is two Triton kernels (combine correction, gate) and their warmup.

**Limits.** The serving A/B is one run per arm and on an earlier base. The sharded selector (opt-in) is not in this PR; it follows as a separate PR on top of this one.

title: [Core][Scheduler] Context-aware long prefill chunking
body:
`--long-prefill-token-threshold` cuts a long prefill into fixed-size chunks so it can't eat the whole token budget. That bounds how many prefill tokens land in a step, but not how long the step takes

Each chunk token attends over everything already computed for that prompt, so the per-token cost of a chunk grows with how deep into the prompt it is. With a very long cold prompt the same threshold-sized chunk gets slower and slower as the prefill goes on, and every decode batched with it waits on that step. Everyone else's TPOT climbs for as long as the long prefill runs, and it's worst near the end of the prompt

This adds an opt-in context budget that shrinks the cap as the prefill's context grows, so each chunk costs about the same however far into the prompt it is:

```
cap = budget / (1 + num_computed_tokens / scale)
```

with a small floor so huge prompts keep making progress, and never above the existing threshold

- it only kicks in where `long_prefill_token_threshold` already caps a chunk, so a request alone in the batch is still never capped (there's nobody to stall)
- ordinary prompts keep the plain threshold, it only applies to prefills with a lot left to do or a lot of context already computed (both gates are derived from the scale)
- with the default budget of 0 the helper returns exactly the old cap
- setting the budget without a threshold raises an error instead of silently doing nothing
- encoder-decoder models already zero the threshold, they zero the budget too

The trade-off is the long prompt's own TTFT. It gets more, smaller chunks, so it finishes later. That's the right call for interactive multi-tenant serving where one huge prompt shouldn't stall everyone else, and it's why this is off by default

Flags:

- `--long-prefill-context-budget` (default 0, off): the chunk cap at zero context
- `--long-prefill-context-scale` (default 262144): the context depth at which the cap halves. It roughly tracks where a chunk's attention cost catches up with its dense cost, so it depends on the model and backend, dense attention probably wants a smaller value than sparse MLA

Heads up: the cap produces more distinct chunk sizes than a fixed threshold. On backends that specialize kernels on token count, the very first long prefill at new chunk sizes can hit one-time Triton compiles and stall for a bit. After that the shapes are cached

It's plain integer math in the scheduler, no new state and no new CPU/GPU sync

Related: #61080 (defer mode) and #58420 (SRPF) change which prefill runs, this changes how big each chunk is. They don't touch the same code

## Test plan

- [x] new unit tests in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: chunks shrink as context grows, a cap table (short prompt passthrough, deep context tail, the floor, never past the remaining tokens), a lone request stays exempt, budget without threshold raises
- [x] `pytest tests/v1/core` gives the same results as main apart from the new tests passing
- [x] `pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py` passes and both flags show up in `--help`
- [x] end to end with an agent-style load plus one cold long prompt injected: decodes that overlap the long prefill stall a lot less, the long prompt's TTFT goes up as expected, turns that don't overlap it are unchanged
- [x] pre-commit clean on the changed files
