title: [Feature][DSv4.1][NIXL] Support PCP Prefill with NIXL P/D
body:
## Overview

Enable text-only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D serving with PCP on the NIXL Prefill producer and PCP=1 on Decode.

Built on merged #59857 and stacked on #59325 and #59330. The remaining prerequisite commits are included with attribution; only the final commit, `af96945ccb`, implements this feature's model capability gate, focused tests and deployment documentation.

## Claims

- Allow GPU `NixlConnector` pull producers to use PCP with PP=DP=DCP=1 and synchronous scheduling; retain the existing model/backend restrictions and reject consumer PCP, push, bidirectional and custom connector paths.
- Reuse NIXL's canonical PCP-rank-0 transfer workers to carry compressed KV, indexer keys, the SWA tail and the compressor ring into a PCP1 decoder, including heterogeneous TP for replicated MLA caches.
- Preserve a matching N−1 handoff boundary and producer KV reclamation through the existing prerequisite fixes.

## Validation

Rebased onto main `fa75d3456d` on 2026-10-16. The GPU results below were collected at pre-rebase head `a888e22d83` and have not been rerun on rebased head `af96945ccb`. All 11 remaining patches are unchanged by `git range-diff`; post-rebase static checks pass. No tests or local CI were run for this rebase.

Target-GPU validation used one 8x NVIDIA H20 node for Prefill and one for Decode (driver `535.161.08`):

- Prefill: TP4/PCP2 on `192.168.1.186`
- Decode: TP8/PCP1 on `192.168.1.220`
- NIXL 1.5.0 pull over `mlx5_1..4`
- PR head: `a888e22d831b48873b9c5decca51154de3e6feca`
- Base image source: `77154ca6116ae34cbfe314beef1016bde9b63989`
- The base image is the PR merge base. Validation overlaid the PR's 17 runtime files from backport commit `2b40794c22` before launch.

Functional and transfer checks passed:

- Tiny completion, exact token-ID boundaries `127/128/129/4095/4096/4097`, repeated 4097, and 8192-token requests all returned HTTP 200.
- All eight Decode ranks passed the compatibility handshake. The topology reported `tp_ratio=2`, `local_tp=8`, and `remote_tp=4`.
- Across seven boundary requests, Decode recorded `+16769` external queries and `+16762` external hits. The exact N−1 relation was `16762 = 16769 - 7`.
- The same requests produced `+56 = 7 requests x 8 ranks` NIXL transfers, with zero failed transfers, failed notifications, expirations, or notifications after expiry.

Full GSM8K test-split coverage also completed:

- EvalScope 1.11.1, 1,319 examples, 0-shot, batch size 8
- `temperature=0.2`, `top_p=0.95`, seed 42, `reasoning_effort=high`, `max_tokens=256`
- Requested/succeeded/errored: `1319/1319/0`
- Accuracy: `6/1319 = 0.4549%`
- `stop_reason=max_tokens`: `1314/1319 = 99.62%`
- Mean/P99 latency: `32.324s/32.902s`
- Decode external queries/hits: `+139749/+138430`, preserving `138430 = 139749 - 1319`
- NIXL transfers: `+10552 = 1319 requests x 8 ranks`; bytes: `+32652656128` (30.41 GiB)
- Failed transfers, failed notifications, KV expirations, and new notifications after expiry: all zero
- Prefill, Decode, and Router remained Ready with restart count zero

The GSM8K score is dominated by the requested 256-token output cap: 99.62% of responses exhausted the cap before natural completion. This result qualifies bounded-output P/D transport and sustained stability, not model accuracy, and must not be compared with an uncapped or historical `max_tokens=65536` result.

## Details

1. P stops before the final prompt token, computes the prefix with PCP and gathers cache writes/open ratio-2 state onto equivalent replicas.
2. D reads the compressed KV, indexer keys, SWA tail and per-request compressor ring from the PCP-rank-0 replica's TP workers. Non-transferring PCP ranks retain their synthetic completion notifications.
3. D resumes at N−1, computes the final prompt token and closes any pending ratio-2 pair using the transferred ring. NIXL completion notifications release the producer's replicas.

Both sides use NVIDIA CUDA, Model Runner V2, `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41`, the same KV dtype/block size and this revision. The initial configuration uses GPU buffers, eager execution, no prefix caching, no SWA bounded replay, no speculative decoding and no microbatching. The usage guide includes TP4/PCP2 Prefill and TP8/PCP1 Decode arguments. Both sides must keep handshake compatibility checks enabled; the inherited N−1 protocol change uses NIXL version 15 because main already assigned version 14 to the PLE metadata change.

This does not duplicate the open fixes: #59325 owns the generic replicated-PCP completion repair and #59330 owns the generic P/D endpoint change. They are reused here without a competing implementation. #58289 targets encoder-only Prefill, and #61121 optimizes packed-row transfer registration; neither enables this full-model V4.1 PCP/NIXL path. Main already includes the generic MoE padding fix from #60946.

Local CPU/static checks: `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_pcp.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py -k 'pcp or dsv41_nixl_handoff or mamba_n1 or ring_scratch' --confcutdir=tests -p no:cacheprovider -q` covers 57 passing cases; `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD` and `git diff --check origin/main` pass. Target-GPU transport and capped GSM8K stability validation are complete; uncapped model accuracy and performance validation remain TODO.

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests and drafting. The human submitter remains responsible for reviewing every changed line and completing uncapped accuracy and performance validation before marking this draft Ready.

title: [Simulator] Add vLLM Simulator for hardware-aware serving simulation on CPU
body:
## Overview Adds `tools/vllm-simulator`, the simulator half of RFC #61406. It runs the real vLLM v1 engine on a CPU-only host and bypasses model forward. A simulation clock then advances by a hardware-aware per-step latency prediction. The output is the same set of metrics `vllm bench serve` reports, for a target model, accelerator, and parallel configuration. This PR is fully independent of the CPU-based CI PR (#61407) and modifies no file outside `tools/vllm-simulator`. Once #61407 lands, the simulator can be simplified on top of it: its own mock platform and model-runner stub can be replaced, and real parallel ranks become possible. See [Relationship to the CPU-based CI PR](#relationship-to-the-cpu-based-ci-pr). The simulator is built by the same team, and with the same design, as the SGLang simulator (sgl-project/sglang#21891). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Maintainer decisions needed:** where the simulator should live, and which engine seams it may hook. See [Decisions requested](#decisions-requested). ## Claims - **Transparent to users.** Serving and the local engine API accept the same arguments and expose the same interfaces as `vllm serve`, `vllm bench serve`, and `AsyncLLM`. - **Zero changes to vLLM.** All 56 files are under `tools/vllm-simulator`, of which the core vLLM hooks (`src/vllm_simulator/simulation/vllm`) account for 1428 lines. Request admission, scheduling, prefix caching, block allocation, and KV-connector bookkeeping run on unmodified vLLM code. - **Two clock modes.** `NON_BLOCKING` (default) advances a virtual clock. `BLOCKING` sleeps for the predicted latency, so the server can stand in for a real deployment in real time. - **Pluggable predictors:** [AIConfigurator](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aiconfigurator) (default), replay table, sklearn model, and linear model. See [Predictors](#predictors). - **Topologies:** multi-instance with load balancing, and PD disaggregation through the native `DecodeBenchConnector`. - **Baseline collector.** Exports per-iteration batch composition and latency from real GPUs, for replay tables, ML predictor training, and accuracy validation. ## Validation **Functional tests.** Run on a CPU-only host with no CUDA runtime, against the [AIConfigurator](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aiconfigurator) `SOL` database for a simulated B300. Models cover the main attention and KV-cache layouts: - dense GQA: Qwen3-8B; - hybrid full attention + Gated DeltaNet: Qwen3.5-27B; - sparse MLA (DSA): GLM-5; - hybrid MLA + KDA: Kimi-K3; - compressed sparse MLA: DeepSeek-V4-Pro. ```bash cd tools/vllm-simulator && pip install . for t in test/test_simulation_*.py; do python -m pytest "$t" -v -s; done ``` | Test | Coverage | Result | |---|---|---| | `test_prefix_cache_and_offload` | All models above: device prefix-cache hit, CPU-offload hit after eviction, cache flush | PASSED | | `test_vllm_serving_blocking` | OpenAI server, `BLOCKING` | PASSED | | `test_vllm_serving_non_blocking` | OpenAI server, `NON_BLOCKING`, `bench_serving` client | PASSED | | `test_benchmark_round_robin` | 3 engines, round-robin routing | PASSED | | `test_pd_disagg_benchmark` | 1P + 1D, merged TTFT across instances | PASSED | **Large-scale deployment test.** A one-hour workload on the prefill instances of a large-scale PD-disaggregated test deployment was replayed in the simulator: 60 prefill instances, behind cache-aware routing, with an external prefix cache (KV connector to an external KV store) enabled. | Metric (1 h mean) | Simulation | Real | Difference | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Request rate (RPS) | 168.29 | 168.25 | +0.02% | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 478.35 | 518.23 | −7.7% | | Cache hit ratio (%) | 77.25 | 77.86 | −0.61 pp | - **Request rate** matches by construction, because arrivals are replayed from the trace. - **Cache hit ratio** follows the per-minute fluctuations within about 1 pp. - **TTFT** tracks the real trend but stays consistently lower. That is the same direction as the unmodelled engine residual listed under [Limitations](#limitations). ## Details ### Why hooks instead of in-tree changes The primary goal is a workflow that is transparent to users. | Workflow | Real | Simulated | |---|---|---| | Serving | `vllm serve` | `python -m vllm_simulator.simulation.vllm.launch_server` | | Benchmark | `vllm bench serve` | `python -m vllm_simulator.simulation.bench_serving` | | Local engine | `AsyncLLM.generate` | same code, after `init_hook()` | Arguments, request formats, and output metrics are unchanged. The entry point can also stay unchanged by installing the hooks from a startup file, either a [`.pth` import line](https://docs.python.org/3/library/site.html#path-extensions-pth-files) or, on Python ≥ 3.15, a [`.start` entry point](https://docs.python.org/3/library/site.html#startup-entry-points-start-files). Such a file would need an environment-variable gate, and this PR does not ship one. An in-tree implementation would spread non-serving changes across `vllm/`: - arrival replay; - a virtual clock; - stats export; - a device-less platform and model runner; - no-op connector transfers. Each of these would add branches to hot paths. Hooks keep all of them in `tools/vllm-simulator`. They are installed at class-definition time, before vLLM is imported. **Maintenance cost.** Keeping the hooks outside `vllm/` does not make them free to maintain. The cost depends on how close each hook sits to low-level code, and the hooks fall into two kinds: - **`wrapped_*` functions** keep the native call and only add simulation state around it: arrival replay, the clock, and stats. They sit on engine-level interfaces (`EngineArgs`, `EngineCore`, `UniProcExecutor`) that rarely change. - **`override_*` functions** replace native behavior, almost entirely to remove hardware dependencies: device initialization, memory profiling, pinned buffers, and transfers. Together with the mock platform and the model-runner stub, these are the hooks most tightly coupled to low-level code. That is exactly the layer meta-CI (#61407) covers in-tree, alongside the code it depends on. Once #61407 lands, these hooks can be removed, leaving only the stable `wrapped_*` interfaces. Hooks also apply to modules outside vLLM. External components, such as KV stores with their own capacity management, can therefore be brought into the simulation directly instead of waiting for each one to add simulation support. ### Design - **Engine core.** `EngineCore.add_request` parks requests until the clock reaches their logical `created_time`. `UniProcExecutor.execute_model` converts each `SchedulerOutput` into `(scheduled tokens, past KV length)` pairs, queries the predictor, and advances the clock. `EngineCore.profile` dumps per-request and per-iteration stats. - **Worker.** A stub stands in for Model Runner V2. The KV-cache spec comes from a meta-device model walk under the simulated TP size and accelerator architecture. The KV budget comes from the target accelerator's HBM. - **Connectors.** KV offload and PD transfers complete immediately, so scheduler-side hits behave normally. ### Predictors Each predictor maps one step's batch, a list of `(scheduled tokens, past KV length)` pairs, to a latency. The predictor is selected by `predictor.name` in the simulator config. | Predictor | Source of latency | Typical use | |---|---|---| | `aiconfigurator` (default) | [AIConfigurator](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aiconfigurator) per-operator performance model for the target model, accelerator, and TP/EP size. Database modes: `SILICON` (measured kernels), `HYBRID`, `EMPIRICAL`, `SOL`, `SOL_FULL` (speed-of-light). | Hardware that is not available locally; capacity planning | | `replay` | Real per-iteration latencies exported by the baseline collector, matched by exact batch composition, with optional KNN interpolation on misses | Debugging by separating predictor error from scheduler and cache behavior | | `ml` | sklearn regressor trained on collector exports, over batch-composition features | A deployed model and accelerator with collected baselines | | `linear` | `base_ms + per_token_ms × scheduled tokens`; a constant step latency when `per_token_ms = 0` | Debugging | ### Relationship to the CPU-based CI PR The two efforts are independent by nature. - **Origin of meta-CI.** #61407 grew out of discussions in which functional CI also turned out to need CPU execution. It is in-tree because it goes deeper than the simulator: execution reaches model forward and runs fake kernels through their full lifecycle. - **What the simulator gains.** The simulator never executes model forward. For it, meta-CI only reduces the CPU-execution support it has to carry itself. - **Plan.** #61407 is not merged and may still change, so this PR ships its own minimal mock platform and model-runner stub. Once meta-CI lands, a follow-up will drop the `override_*` hooks, simplify the model runner, and allow real TP/EP/PP ranks. The `wrapped_*` hooks and the out-of-tree approach stay as they are. ### Decisions requested 1. **Location and ownership.** Is `tools/vllm-simulator` acceptable as a separately installed package with its own dependencies? 2. **Hooked seams.** The hooks cover `EngineArgs`, `EngineCore`, `Scheduler`, `UniProcExecutor`, `Worker`, the platform, and three KV-connector workers. Should any of these become narrow public extension points, such as a request-arrival hook or a step-latency callback? ### Limitations - **Version coupling.** A hook that fails to apply logs a warning, so a renamed method can degrade silently. - **Accuracy.** Only the comparison above is reported. `NON_BLOCKING` does not model the ~2.5 ms/step engine residual. - **Scope.** Text generation only, on Model Runner V2, eager mode, synchronous scheduling. Parallelism is modelled by the predictor only. - **KV cache transfer.** Transfer time is not modelled yet, for either external prefix cache loads and stores or PD prefill-to-decode transfers. Both complete instantaneously, so only the hit and miss decisions are simulated. Transfer models are follow-up work. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Evict invalid blocks of requests aborted mid-step
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61768. A request aborted in the same step its synchronous KV load fails leaves the scheduler before the failure report is processed, so its never-loaded blocks stay prefix-cache hits. This keeps the departing request's block ids until its in-flight outputs arrive, and evicts them when a late failure report names them.

## Claims

- After a sync KV load failure whose owner was aborted in the same step, the invalid block and every block after it are evicted, under both `kv_load_failure_policy` values and with sync and async scheduling. With async scheduling or PP this relies on deferred freeing, which is on for a top-level `kv_consumer`/`kv_both`; see Tradeoffs and limits for a top-level producer whose connector loads.
- A later identical prompt recomputes instead of decoding from never-loaded KV (GPU: r2 cached 1904 → 0, output matches the full-recompute baseline).
- An abort whose load succeeded keeps its valid cached KV (unchanged behavior).

## Validation

**Tests** (`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py`). The four regression tests fail on main at the eviction assertion; with this change all of them pass:

| Test | Role |
|---|---|
| `test_aborted_sync_load_invalid_suffix_evicted` (policy × delayed connector free × PP 1/2) | regression: evicts from the first invalid block; next request hits only the valid prefix |
| `test_aborted_load_survives_other_queued_step` | regression: a batch without a failure keeps the blocks; the later failing batch evicts them |
| `test_aborted_load_survives_empty_schedule` | regression: an empty schedule between the load step and its output keeps the record |
| `test_aborted_sharer_suffix_evicted_by_earlier_batch_failure` | regression: a finished request computed over a block that failed in an earlier batch |
| `test_aborted_successful_sync_load_preserves_cache` | guard: an abort with a successful load keeps the cache |
| `test_finished_request_retained_until_all_outputs_processed` | lifecycle: under async scheduling a record lives until its last in-flight output |

`assert_scheduler_empty` in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` and `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/utils.py` now also checks the record is empty, so existing tests guard against leaks.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py   # 25 passed
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" pytest --timeout=300 tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/ tests/v1/core/
```

The second command ran on this branch and on main at the same commit (`81e1c3f1`) without this change, with the GPU hidden: the precompiled kernels available locally are for an older commit, so GPU tests can't run meaningfully here and are left to CI. This branch: 2911 passed, 217 failed, 112 errors. Main: 2889 passed, 239 failed, 112 errors. **No test fails on this branch that passes on main.** The only difference is the 22 new tests, which fail on main. The 329 shared failures and errors are mostly tests that need a device, plus a few that already fail on main; all of them fail identically there:

<details>
<summary>Shared failures and errors by file (identical on main without this change)</summary>

| File | Failed + errored |

| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py` | 142 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py` | 101 |

| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_worker.py` | 9 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py` | 9 |

</details>

**End-to-end** (RTX 5090, Qwen3-0.6B, greedy; harness: [inference-correctness-lab](https://github.com/ArijitDeb/inference-correctness-lab/tree/orphaned-load-failure-v1/cases/orphaned-load-failure), full table: [RESULTS.md](https://github.com/ArijitDeb/inference-correctness-lab/blob/orphaned-load-failure-v1/cases/orphaned-load-failure/RESULTS.md)). The GPU rows measure this patch applied at `04462732` (commit `e23ecfa8`), whose precompiled kernels were available; this branch is the same patch rebased onto current main. Request r1's 1904-token external load is dropped and r1 is aborted inside the same step through `EngineCore.aborts_queue`; r2 repeats the prompt; the baseline is a full recompute. Three trials per cell, `fail` shown, `recompute` identical:

| Tree | Scheduling | r2 cached | r2 == baseline | P(baseline's next token) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main `04462732` | sync | 1904 | 0/3 | 0.0005-0.005 |
| main | async | 1904 | 0/3 | 0.0005-0.005 |
| #53298 at `a7dd070b` merged onto main | sync / async | 1904 | 0/3 | 0.0005-0.005 |
| **this PR** | sync | **0** | **3/3** | **0.962** |
| **this PR** | async | **0** | **3/3** | **0.962** |
| this PR, load succeeds + abort (control) | sync | 1904 | 3/3 | 0.963 |

Baseline P(next) is 0.962. With this change, the new bookkeeping is empty after every trial.

## Details

**Root cause.** `EngineCore.step` and `step_with_batch_queue` apply queued aborts before `update_from_output`. `allocate_slots` hashes blocks at schedule time, before an external load completes, and `free_blocks` keeps hashes. `_handle_invalid_blocks` only looks for affected requests in `running` and `kv_holding_waiting`, so when the owner was freed in between, it returns before evicting.

**Why the request's lifetime isn't enough.** The request object is gone once it is freed, but outputs of the steps that scheduled it can still arrive, and only they carry the failure report. So the departing request's block ids are kept for as long as it has scheduled-but-unprocessed tokens.

**Change** (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`, +51 lines):
- *Capture:* `_free_request` records the block ids and `num_in_flight_tokens` of a request freed while it still has in-flight tokens, before the delayed-free branch, so connector-delayed and `defer_block_free` paths are covered. Only with a KV connector and a single KV cache group, matching `_handle_invalid_blocks`.
- *Evict:* `_handle_invalid_blocks`, before its early return and under both policies, evicts from the first invalid block onward for every recorded request. The `recompute` no-evict path stays for live owners only: a finished request never recomputes. Every record is checked, not only those in this batch, because a finished request may have computed its own later blocks over a block that failed in an earlier batch.
- *Retire:* `update_from_output` counts each record down by the step's scheduled tokens before its main loop and drops it at zero. It runs before the loop because the loop decrements `num_in_flight_tokens` first, so records created there already exclude this step.

**Relation to other work.** [#42461](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42461) ([RFC #35780](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35780)) proposes replacing block-level failure reporting with request-level reporting. If it lands, this path and this bug go away with it; until then, every connector that reports `invalid_block_ids` reaches this code, under the default `fail` policy too. PR [#53298](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298) covers the recompute-policy repair of requests that are still alive; this change covers the owner that is already gone. Against its head `1eca68f4`, `scheduler.py` merges cleanly; both add a line to the test helper `assert_scheduler_empty`, a one-line conflict for whichever lands second.

**Tradeoffs and limits.**
- No GPU work and no host sync: Python bookkeeping only. With sync scheduling, records are created only for requests aborted mid-step. With async scheduling, also for requests that finish while their next batch is in flight; each such record holds a tuple of block ids for one step. A record lives at most `max_concurrent_batches` steps, so the number of records is bounded by the requests that finish within that window. The retire step returns immediately when there are no records; the scan over recorded block ids runs only when a failure is reported.
- Keeping physical block ids, without hashes, requires that a recorded id not identify a different allocation when the failure report is handled. With one batch in flight, nothing allocates between the abort and `update_from_output`, which handles the report and retires the record. With several batches in flight, this holds when `defer_block_free` is on (top-level `kv_consumer`/`kv_both`): the freed blocks are held until the step fence at free time has been processed. Deferred frees may drain before `_handle_invalid_blocks()`, but no scheduling allocation occurs between that drain, failure handling, and record retirement in the normal engine output path. With overlapping batches and a top-level producer whose connector loads, `defer_block_free` is off and a recorded id can be reallocated before the report. In CPU probes this PR then additionally evicts the new allocation's cache entries; the late report failing or rewinding that unrelated request already happens on main (#61905). Whether producer-role loading needs handling before this merges is a call for review.
- Known limit: preempted owners are not tracked here. A consumer-role `reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True)` can preempt an owner whose load is in flight and then fail to clear the cache, leaving failed-load blocks as prefix hits; producer-role synchronous loaders can also reach this through KV-pressure preemption. Tracked in #61912.
- Multiple KV cache groups are out of scope: `_handle_invalid_blocks` already raises for them, because block ids are only unique within a group.
- Requests still running that share an invalid block are handled by the existing `running` scan; recompute-policy repair ordering for live sharers is #53298's scope.
- The model's next-token distribution is used in validation because greedy equality alone can miss partial corruption.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix non-power-of-two sparse MLA split-K reduction
body:
## Overview

Fix a Triton compilation error in the ROCm sparse MLA split-K reduction kernel when the combined head dimension is not a power of two, such as the 512 NoPE + 64 RoPE layout used by DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.3.

## Claims

- Pad the reduction block width to the next power of two and mask out-of-range loads and stores.
- Preserve the existing memory layout and power-of-two reduction behavior.
- Add BF16 regression tests covering 512/576-dimensional layouts, different split counts, attention sinks, and invalid KV indices.

## Validation

- gfx1100 (W7900): 18/18 new regression tests passed.
- gfx1201 (R9700): 18/18 new regression tests passed.
- Baseline: All 12 cases exercising the 576-dimensional reduction failed compilation before the fix.
- gfx1100 E2E: Successfully ran inference-optimization/GLM-5.3-0.6B-A0.4B with real weights, BF16 KV cache, and long-context decode. Observed 204 successful split-K reduction launches with COMB_DIM=576 and COMB_BLOCK=1024.
- gfx1201 E2E: Successfully ran the same checkpoint with BF16 KV cache and long-context decode. Observed 204 successful split-K reduction launches with COMB_DIM=576 and COMB_BLOCK=1024.
- Numerical comparison: Split-K versus single-pass output had a maximum absolute difference of 1.56e-2 and relative L2 difference of 9.5e-4.
- Existing 512-dimensional path: No measurable performance regression in the tested configurations.

The gfx1100 E2E test used the routing change from #59628, temporarily extended to gfx1201 for testing. Additional environment-specific workarounds were required on gfx1201. These changes are not part of this PR.

## Details

The partial attention kernel already handles non-power-of-two head dimensions, but the shared reduction kernel previously used tl.arange(0, COMB_DIM), which fails compilation when COMB_DIM=576.

This change introduces COMB_BLOCK=next_power_of_2(COMB_DIM) for Triton block shapes while retaining the original logical dimension and memory strides. Padded lanes are masked off.

Related: #59628

title: [Bug]: KV offload back-pressure ignores failed secondary-tier stores, so a full filesystem tier keeps receiving every cascade
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Not environment-specific: the issue is in the scheduler-side tiering logic (vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/manager.py + backpressure.py) and is present on current main (a9fe30e9f6). Reproduced at the unit level in a CPU-only environment (Python 3.13, torch 2.11). ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `TieringOffloadingManager` only reports **successful** primary→secondary store completions to the tier's `BackpressureDetector` (added in #50045): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a9fe30e9f6f73a982eab0730476df165484ad4d4/vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/manager.py#L545-L546 ```python self.primary_tier.complete_read(transfer_job.keys, transfer_job.req_context) if completed_job.success: self._update_backpressure(tier, job_metadata, completed_job) ``` `EMABackpressureDetector` is driven only by store latency. A tier that rejects writes does not get slow; it fails fast. A typical case is a shared filesystem tier that has filled up (`ENOSPC`) or hit a directory quota (`EDQUOT`). For example, an external evictor such as the llm-d PVC evictor has a soft threshold, and the volume can reach 100% before it frees space (llm-d/llm-d-kv-cache#218). In that state: 1. No latency samples arrive, so the EMA never crosses the high water mark. 2. If the detector already reached the healthy fast-path (`_HEALTHY_THRESHOLD` fast completions), `should_store()` returns `True` without consulting the policy. `_healthy_streak` is only reset by a slow *successful* completion, so the tier stays "healthy" for as long as every store fails. 3. If the tier fails from its very first store, warmup never completes. Pressure can never be signalled at all. As a result, every cascade keeps going to the failing tier. Each store job pins the primary chunks, and for the `fs` tier it also runs `exists` + `makedirs` + `open(O_CREAT|O_EXCL)` and then the temp-file cleanup against a filesystem that is already in trouble. Each job also logs `Job ... block I/O failed: [Errno 28] No space left on device` at ERROR level. Back-pressure, which is meant to protect a struggling tier, is effectively disabled exactly when the tier is unwritable. The job-failure metrics in `TieringMetricsTracker` do count these failures, so operators can see them. Nothing acts on them, though. **Where it shows up in practice** (the `fs` tier on a filesystem that runs out of space, with back-pressure enabled): ```json { "kv_connector": "OffloadingConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "spec_name": "TieringOffloadingSpec", "cpu_bytes_to_use": 8589934592, "secondary_tiers": [{ "type": "fs", "root_dir": "/mnt/small-tmpfs/kv", "backpressure": {"backpressure_cls": "EMABackpressureDetector"} }] } } ``` Once the filesystem is full, every cascade is still submitted to the tier and fails with `Errno 28`. Following the code path above, `Tier #1 (fs) back-pressure activated` is never logged for these failures. **Minimal reproduction (unit level):** use a `SecondaryTierManager` whose store jobs all complete with `success=False` behind an `EMABackpressureDetector`. Every store is still submitted, no matter how many have failed before. When the detector has already reached the healthy fast-path, `should_store()` keeps returning `True`. The PR below adds tests that fail on current `main` for exactly these cases. ### Proposed fix I have a small patch ready and will open a PR referencing this issue: - Add `BackpressureDetector.on_store_failed()`. It is a no-op by default, so out-of-tree detectors are unaffected. The manager calls it for store jobs that complete with `success=False`. - In `EMABackpressureDetector`, any failure leaves the healthy fast-path. After `failure_threshold` (default 3) consecutive failures, the tier enters pressure with the EMA raised above the high water mark, so the default `ThrottledDropPolicy` drops every store. - Recovery reuses the existing idle decay and cooldown, which then let probe stores through at a bounded rate. A failed probe re-trips pressure immediately, and a successful one resets the streak. Failure-induced pressure can also decay before warmup completes. This deliberately does **not** add capacity management or eviction to vLLM. Per the discussion in #38260 and #54363, capacity and eviction for storage tiers stay with external tools such as the llm-d PVC evictor. This change only makes vLLM back off while the tier cannot accept writes, and resume on its own once the external evictor frees space. ### Related - #50045: introduced `BackpressureDetector` / `EMABackpressureDetector`. - #38260: multi-tier KV offloading RFC, including the request for an `fs` tier disk-usage limit. - #54363: data integrity and I/O liveness RFC for the `fs` tier. Item 4 classifies `ENOSPC` as terminal, and tier health is listed as tracked by the back-pressure RFCs. - #53485, #51240, #51576: back-pressure / admission-policy consolidation. If `CascadeBackpressurePolicy` replaces the current detector, the same failure signal should be carried over (e.g. in `on_completed`). - llm-d/llm-d-kv-cache#218: the PVC evictor's soft threshold can let the volume reach 100%, after which vLLM cache writes fail. cc @orozery @dannyharnik @bnellnm ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix][EPLB] Move 1-byte expert tensors as uint8 views
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #51567.

When EPLB is enabled, expert tensors whose dtype NCCL does not support make engine startup fail. MXFP4 and MXFP8 experts store block scales as `torch.float8_e8m0fnu`. ROCm AITER MXFP4 also views expert weights as `torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2`. Neither dtype exists in NCCL or RCCL.

I hit this with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash using MXFP4 experts (Humming MoE backend), TP8 + EP + EPLB, on 8x H20. The crash happens in the first rearrange during memory profiling.

With `communicator=torch_nccl`:

```text
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 572, in determine_available_memory
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/eplb_utils.py", line 126, in step
File "vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_state.py", line 580, in step
...
File "torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py", line 4280, in all_gather
    work = group.allgather([tensor_list], [tensor], opts)
TypeError: Input tensor data type is not supported for NCCL process group: Float8_e8m0fnu
```

With `communicator=pynccl`:

```text
File "vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_communicator.py", line 756, in create_eplb_communicator
    return _create_pynccl()
File "vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_communicator.py", line 693, in _create_pynccl
    raise RuntimeError(
RuntimeError: EPLB communicator 'pynccl' requested but expert weights contain unsupported dtypes: (torch.float8_e8m0fnu).
```

## When this triggers

The bug is not tied to a specific model architecture. It depends on the dtype that the MoE backend leaves in the expert parameters after weight post-processing. Startup fails when all of these hold:

1. EPLB is enabled (`--enable-eplb`, with EP).
2. The experts use MX quantization (MXFP4/MXFP8 with E8M0 block scales).
3. After post-processing, the backend stores an expert tensor in a 1-byte dtype that NCCL/RCCL does not support. For example:
   - Marlin MXFP4 MoE: `mxfp4_marlin_process_scales()` returns scales as `float8_e8m0fnu`.
   - ROCm AITER MXFP4: expert weights are viewed as `float4_e2m1fn_x2` (`oracle/mxfp4.py`).
   - Humming MXFP4 (my repro): scales are stored as `float8_e8m0fnu`.

   Backends that keep these tensors as `uint8` are not affected.
4. The tensor is returned by `get_expert_weights()`, so it is registered for EPLB transport.

Converting at load time is not enough. DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 loaders already view checkpoint E8M0 scales as `uint8`, but the backend's kernel-format conversion writes `float8_e8m0fnu` back into the parameter. The fix therefore belongs where the tensors are registered for EPLB, not in individual loaders or backends.

## Root cause

EPLB treats expert tensors as opaque payload. It only sends, receives, and all-gathers them, and never reduces them. However, it passes their numeric dtype straight to the communicator. On the first rearrange (the dummy all-gather during `determine_available_memory`), the communicator has to map that dtype to an NCCL dtype. NCCL only supports `int8/uint8/int32/int64/fp16/fp32/fp64/bf16` and FP8 E4M3/E5M2, so the mapping fails:

- `torch_nccl` raises `TypeError` inside `all_gather`.
- `pynccl` rejects the dtype earlier, when the communicator is created.

## Fix

EPLB only copies expert bytes between ranks. It never reduces them, so the numeric dtype does not matter to the transport. In `MixtureOfExperts.set_eplb_state()`, every 1-byte expert tensor is now registered as `w.view(torch.uint8)`:

- The view keeps the shape, stride, and storage, so a rearrange writes directly into the parameter that the kernels read in the original dtype.
- Applying the view at this registration point covers `FusedMoE` layers, models with their own `get_expert_weights()` (for example DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE), and elastic EP re-registration.
- 1-byte dtypes that NCCL already supports (`int8`, `uint8`, `float8_e4m3fn`) move the same bytes as before.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py -k byte_dtypes -v
pre-commit run --files tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py
```

## Test Result

**Unit test:** the new test is parametrized over `float8_e8m0fnu` and `float4_e2m1fn_x2`. Both cases pass with this change and fail on `main`. pre-commit (ruff, mypy) passes.

**MXFP4 deployment with EPLB (8x H20, SM90):** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with MXFP4 experts, Humming MoE backend (`HummingIndexedExperts`), TP8 + EP + EPLB (sync, `pynccl`, 16 redundant experts, `step_interval=1500`). The image is `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0` with this PR's diff applied to `interfaces.py`. On this setup, startup previously failed with the tracebacks above.

- Startup: the profile rearrange passes and the server starts.
  ```text
  Rearranging experts sync mode (profile)...
  Rearranged experts  (profile)  in 2.30 s.
  Application startup complete.
  ```
- Real rearranges: three ran during the GSM8K run below. The first took 6.64 s and the next two took 0.27 s each. Balancedness was about 0.70 before the first rearrange and 0.82 to 0.87 after.
- Accuracy across rearranges (GSM8K, all 1319 questions, 5-shot chat, concurrency 32): flex-extract 89.92% ± 0.83 (1186/1319). This matches our production deployment of the same model without EPLB (90.1%). All 8 smoke prompts were also answered correctly.
- None of the 8 ranks logged `Traceback`, `Float8_e8m0fnu`, `unsupported dtypes`, or `TypeError`.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bug]: DSpark draft token count inflated by reusing target DP sync state with adaptive verification
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text commit id: ac71b175172f2c092d7141f41f0777b914788cfb ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug With adaptive verification and DP enabled, DSpark reuses the target model’s DP sync state, whose `num_reqs` may reflect the target CUDA graph’s padded request capacity rather than the logical request count. This causes unnecessary padding in the draft batch. For example, a single request requiring 7 draft query tokens is expanded to 112 tokens when the target graph has a request capacity of 16. The drafter then selects and replays a 133-token CUDA graph. title: [Chore] Use upstream Transformers MiniMaxM3VLConfig
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Split from #60823: replaces the vendored MiniMax-M3 config and ports the MiniMax-M3 code to the upstream Transformers `MiniMaxM3VLConfig` schema.

Related PRs:
- **#60823:** the larger unvendoring PR this is split from; MiniMax-M3 has been dropped from it.
- **#61392:** the same split for DeepSeek-V4.

## Claims

- Registers upstream `MiniMaxM3VLConfig` for `minimax_m3_vl` in `_CONFIG_REGISTRY`, because the hub remote code uses the old schema.
- `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/minimax_m3.py` shrinks to `MiniMaxM3MTPConfig`, a subclass of upstream `MiniMaxM3VLTextConfig` for standalone MTP checkpoints (`model_type: "minimax_m3_mtp"`). These copy the main model's 60-entry per-layer lists, which upstream rejects for a 1-layer config, so the subclass keeps the leading entries the MTP layer reads. No public checkpoint uses this format, but private ones may.
- The NVIDIA and AMD model code, indexers and vision tower read the upstream fields:
  - `layer_types` / `mlp_layer_types` replace `sparse_attention_config["sparse_attention_freq"]` / `moe_layer_freq`.
  - `index_*` fields replace the rest of `sparse_attention_config`.
  - `rope_parameters` replaces `rope_theta` / `partial_rotary_factor` / `rope_scaling`.
  - The vision tower reads `spatial_merge_size` / `temporal_patch_size` directly.
- Upstream reports `hidden_act="silu"` and drops `swiglu_beta`, so the `swigluoai` check is removed and beta is fixed at 1.0, the value in every checkpoint and in the upstream reference model. `sparse_init_block` and `sparse_score_type` fall back to the indexer's defaults (`0`, `"max"`), which also match every checkpoint.
- **Fix:** re-saved checkpoints in the upstream schema (e.g. `lukealonso/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4`) failed with "Unsupported activation: silu"; they now build.
- No numerics change: greedy outputs are bit-identical to `main`, and GSM8k and GPQA Diamond match.
- Open MiniMax-M3 PRs that add reads of the old field names will need a rebase once this lands: #60930, #61370, #57909, #59653, #57832, #60528.

## Validation

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Stop declaring the MXFP4 MoE intermediate padding to AITER
body:
## Purpose

The AMD CI job `dsv41-mono-decode-numerics-amd` goes red intermittently with

```
AssertionError: (0, 1, (973, 973), 'residual', nan)
```

(e.g. https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94971). The NaN comes from AITER, on
vLLM's ordinary MoE path, not from the mono kernels the test compares against.

AITER's a8w4 MoE (FP8 activations x MXFP4 weights) allocates several scratch
buffers with `torch.empty`, sized for the padded sorted length, and reads them
where the producing kernel never wrote. In FP8/E8M0 a garbage `0xFF` byte is
NaN, so a whole token row of the output comes back NaN. It only happens with a
non-zero `intermediate_pad`, at decode-sized batches, after larger calls have
run in the same process — which is why it shows up as a flaky decode failure.
Root cause, a standalone repro and a fix are filed upstream:

- https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/6565
- https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6568

## This change

Stop declaring `intermediate_pad` to AITER on the MXFP4 path. It is redundant
there, and dropping it keeps the call off the buggy AITER path.

Why it is redundant — the padded region is zero at the point AITER sees it, and
stays zero through every step between allocation and the kernel call:

| step | padded region | where |
|---|---|---|
| allocation | `torch.zeros` for `w13`/`w2`, their scales and `w13_bias`/`w2_bias`, at the **padded** intermediate size | `Mxfp4MoEMethod.create_weights` |
| checkpoint load | the destination is narrowed to the loaded shard before the copy, so the padded rows are never written — this is deliberate, the helper is named for it and its docstring calls out "padding ... on the shard (intermediate) dimension (e.g. for MXFP4 GEMM)" | `RoutedExperts._narrow_expert_data_for_padding`, used by `_load_w13` / `_load_w2` right before `expert_data.copy_()` |
| weight shuffle | pure `view` + `permute` (asserts `N % 16 == 0`, `K % 32 == 0`, no re-padding), so zeros stay zeros | `aiter.ops.shuffle.shuffle_weight` |
| scale shuffle | re-pads the scale to 256 rows / 8 cols, but fills the pad with `0x7F` (E8M0 = 1.0) before copying, so it is never garbage | `aiter.utility.fp4_utils.e8m0_shuffle` |

So for the padded columns the kernel computes

- stage 1: `x @ 0 = 0` (gate and up are both zero there, and the bias is zero,
  so the activation output is exactly `silu(0) * 0 = 0`)
- stage 2: `0 @ 0 = 0`

Exact zeros also mean the padded columns cannot disturb the stage-2 activation
quantization: `amax` over an MX group is unaffected by zeros, whether or not a
group straddles real and padded columns.

Two things are deliberately left alone:

- **`hidden_pad`** — the activation columns it covers are not guaranteed to be
  zero, so dropping it would not be equivalent.
- **SITU** (`activation == MoEActivation.SITU`, the a16w4 FlyDSL port used by
  Kimi K3) — that kernel consumes the pad. The surrounding code already skips
  the rounding for it ("SITU's A16W4 FlyDSL kernel pads per gate/up half; pass
  through unrounded"), and on that path AITER keys its own scratch
  initialization on the value: `_alloc = torch.zeros if inter_dim_pad > 0 else
  torch.empty` in `aiter/ops/flydsl/moe_kernels.py`. Zeroing the declaration
  there would *remove* an initialization that is currently happening, which is
  the opposite of what this PR is for.

This is a workaround and should be reverted once the AITER fix is merged and
pinned. The surrounding code already carries a similar TODO about AITER padding
behaviour.

## Test Result

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, stock AITER 0.1.25 — i.e. **without** the
AITER-side fix — running `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` unmodified,
each run covering TP2 and TP4:

| build | runs | cells | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| exactly this patch | 4 | 8 | **all passed** |
| same logic, earlier iterations of the comment/wording | 10 | 20 | **all passed** |

14 runs, 28 cells, no NaN. Before the change the same test failed intermittently
— locally about 2 runs in 6 — so 14 clean runs is about 0.3% likely if the
change did nothing.

Overhead: none measurable. Timing the same shape with and without the
declaration (median over 6 rounds, per `fused_moe_2stages` call):

| M | declared | not declared |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0.139 ms | 0.141 ms |
| 4 | 0.156 ms | 0.158 ms |
| 1439 | 0.534 ms | 0.536 ms |
| 16384 | 2.010 ms | 2.010 ms |

All within run-to-run noise (~4%).

## Scope and limits

- Validated on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 (`model_dim=5120`, per-rank
  intermediate 576 padded to 640, E=384, topk=6). Other MXFP4 models on this
  path (e.g. gpt-oss with INTERLEAVE) are covered by the same zero-fill
  argument but were not run here, so reviewers may prefer a narrower gate.
- The zero-fill chain above is established from the code, with the citations in
  the table. It is not confirmed by a run against a real MXFP4 checkpoint that
  actually has padding: the test that exercises this path uses a random-weight
  loader which also zero-fills the padding, and every MXFP4 checkpoint we have
  locally has `moe_intermediate_size = 2048`, which is already aligned per rank
  (pad = 0). DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (2304) is the one that pads, and the local copy
  of it is FP8 rather than MXFP4.
- Models whose per-rank intermediate size is already 128-aligned get
  `intermediate_pad == 0` and are unaffected either way.
- The `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4` opt-in is a sub-case of
  `use_mxfp4_w4a16`, so it is covered by this change as well. The same
  zero-fill argument applies to it, but it runs different kernels and was not
  exercised here.

title: [MRV2][Spec Decode] Optimize DSpark with local argmax reduction
body:
## Overview

This PR introduces local argmax reduction for DSpark speculative decoding to reduce Tensor Parallel (TP) communication overhead during draft token sampling.

Previously, DSpark gathered full vocabulary logits across TP ranks before applying Markov bias and selecting draft tokens. However, greedy sampling only requires the token with the highest score, making the full-vocabulary All-Gather unnecessary.

This PR performs argmax locally on each TP rank after applying the corresponding Markov bias, and then uses a lightweight All-Gather to determine the global winning token.

## Validation

This optimization reduces the amount of data exchanged during TP synchronization from full-vocabulary logits to a pair of values per TP rank and draft step. The expected benefit is lower communication overhead and improved speculative decoding performance, particularly for large vocabularies and communication-bound workloads.

Benchmark results will be added after validation.

## Details

- **Local Logits Computation:** Skip the full-vocabulary All-Gather during LMHead computation and retain vocabulary-sharded logits on each TP rank.
- **Local Argmax Reduction:** Apply the corresponding local slice of Markov bias and compute the local maximum score and its global token ID.
- **Lightweight TP Communication:** All-Gather only the local maximum score and token ID from each TP rank to determine the global argmax.
- **Preserve Sampling Semantics:** Maintain sequential Markov dependencies, vocabulary index mapping, padding handling, and deterministic argmax tie-breaking.

title: [ROCm][DSv4] Opt-in aiter ASM sparse MLA decode with FP8 Q (VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_ASM_SPARSE_MLA)
body:
## Overview

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_ASM_SPARSE_MLA=1` (opt-in, default off) runs DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA decode on MI355X (gfx950) the way ATOM does: KV cache in aiter's two-buffer layout, FP8 Q, and aiter's v4 nm ASM decode kernels.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 8x MI355X, DP8 attention + EP8, AgentX agentic workload. These numbers were measured on a development branch, not on this upstream branch:
  - decode step at 16 requests per rank: 53.6-54.5 -> 49.6-50.3 ms;
  - sparse MLA kernels: 7.31 -> 2.56 ms per step;
  - e2e, same node, c128: P90 interactivity 27.37 -> 30.95 tok/s/user, total tok/s/GPU +10.5%;
  - e2e, same node, c64: P90 interactivity 50.1 -> 60.32 tok/s/user, total tok/s/GPU +7.1%.
- KV capacity: -10.5% tokens per rank, taken by the RoPE side pool.
- Off by default; with the switch off, nothing changes.

## Validation

Accuracy and performance on this upstream branch are still to be added.

Development branch:
- gsm8k 5-shot, real speculative decoding, flexible / strict: 0.9704 / 0.9712 with the switch, 0.9727 / 0.9735 without.
- Unit checks with real shapes on one GPU:
  - the compressor writers write identical NoPE, scale and RoPE bytes in the old and new layouts;
  - the prefill gather is bit-identical;
  - the ASM decode vs an fp32 reference with the same FP8 Q: cos 0.999998.
- Real-weight decode calls at ~100K context vs an fp32 reference with bf16 Q: cos >= 0.99996.

This branch:
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass, mypy included.
- No GPU tests have been run on this branch yet.

## Details

- **KV layout.** Every DeepSeek-V4 attention cache page (SWA, CSA, HCA; target and DSpark draft) holds 512-byte rows: 448 fp8 NoPE, then the 7 UE8M0 scales (each written twice), then padding.
  - The bf16 RoPE lives in a side pool. Rows are numbered across the whole block-outermost KV buffer, so the pool is 1/4 of that buffer, and the KV planner gives the cache 4/5 of the budget.
  - `register()` asserts the block-outermost layout and 512-byte alignment at KV bind time.
- **Q/K.** aiter `fused_qk_norm_rope_group_quant` does Q RMSNorm + RoPE + FP8 group quant, and K norm + RoPE + UE8M0 quant + SWA row write. The DSpark context-KV insert uses the same kernel.
- **Decode.**
  - Each row gets one merged index list: SWA window + top-k compressed rows. It is built from the persistent metadata buffers, so it is CUDA-graph safe.
  - CSA and SWA-only layers run `mla_decode_fwd_v4_nm` with aiter's split plan.
  - HCA layers run the persistent `mla_decode_fwd_v4_nm_ps` (15-32768 rows).
- **Prefill** stays on the existing bf16 path; the gather kernel reads the new layout.
  - aiter's ASM sparse prefill is gfx1250-only.
  - The gfx950 fp8 OPUS prefill measured no gain: +3.2 ms per 8K-token step in a unit A/B.
  - With the switch on, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA` is ignored, because that kernel reads the fp8_ds_mla pages.
- **Off path.** All new code is behind the switch. The Triton edits to the compressor writers, the prefill gather and the global top-k kernel are constexpr branches whose defaults reproduce today's code.
- **Precision.** Decode Q is FP8 (UE8M0 per 64), and RoPE is applied with bf16 cos/sin tables in aiter's kernel. Prefill attention is unchanged.
- **Limits.**
  - DeepSeek-V4 only; DeepSeek-V4.1 is unchanged.
  - fp8_ds_mla KV cache only.
  - No KV connector or offload: the side pool is not transferred.
  - The ROW_OFFSET constexpr compiles the top-k kernel once per CSA layer.
- **Relation to #56426.** That draft targets the same aiter kernel but keeps vLLM's layout and repacks the selected pages on every decode call; it reports an e2e loss. This PR changes the KV layout itself, so decode needs no repack.
- **Follow-ups.**
  - GPU unit tests: writer / gather round trip, and ASM decode vs an fp32 reference.
  - Accuracy and performance numbers on this branch.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2][Spec Decode] Sync standalone draft token counts across DP ranks
body:
## Overview

MRV2 `draft_model` (`StandaloneARSpeculator`) with a MoE target and DP > 1 crashes at startup: the drafter passes the target's `num_tokens_across_dp` to its own forwards, which run a different number of tokens, and `DPMetadata.make` asserts.

Related: #56281 (same assert in DSpark, fixed by #54856), #56734 (dummy-run masking for EAGLE). Not a duplicate: no open or closed PR covers these fixes. #56136 touches the same dynamic-SD gate but not which managers capture per K.

## Claims

- Fix the `draft_model` + MoE + DP > 1 startup crash (`AssertionError: 7168 1024`).
- Port #56734's dummy-run `idx_mapping` masking to the standalone drafter, so idle DP ranks don't write draft KV through stale block tables.
- Fix the draft prefill's `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound`, which was one short.
- Stop `DFlashCudaGraphManager` (DFlash/DFlash2/DSpark) capturing per-K FULL graphs under dynamic SD that it never dispatches.

## Validation

Qwen3-30B-A3B target, Qwen3-0.6B draft, K=3, MRV2, H100s. GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions.

| Config | GSM8K | Acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DP=1, no spec | 0.889 | — |
| DP=1, draft_model | 0.889 | 81.6% |
| DP=2, draft_model, main | crash at startup | — |
| DP=2, draft_model, this PR | 0.899 | 81.8% |

- No sync warnings with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn` at DP=2.
- Prefill bound: a temporary check found the actual draft `seq_lens` above the CPU bound on 539/549 prefills before, 0 after.
- Idle-rank dummy batches: a tiny random-weight MoE at DP=2 with single and burst requests completes; main crashes.
- `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py`, `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd_cug.py`, `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py`: 56 passed. Both new tests fail on main.

<details>
<summary>Repro</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --max-model-len 4096 --port 8001 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"draft_model","model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8001
```
</details>

## Details

- **DP sync.** The draft prefill runs `num_tokens + num_reqs` tokens and each decode step `num_reqs`, so each syncs its own count via `dispatch_cg_and_sync_dp(need_eager=True)`: once for prefill, once before the decode loop. That adds two CPU all-reduces per `propose` at DP > 1. Reusing the target's sync (as the target-dependent drafters do) would mean padding eager attention metadata here, since the target sync only carries the max request count.
- **Prefill bound.** The prefill kernel writes `seq_len + 1` per request for the correction token, so the prefill now passes `step=1`, as decode already does. FlashInfer TRTLLM prefill with FP8 KV and the sparse MLA backends size work from this bound.
- **DFlash capture.** New `CudaGraphManager.dynamic_sd_query_lens = True`, set to `False` on `DFlashCudaGraphManager`.
- **CI.** No CI step runs a MoE target with a draft model at DP=2; the e2e runs above were local.

title: [Feature]: Candidate-only scoring for DeepSeek-V4.1 indexer consumers on SM90 (H20)
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

> **Scope:** this is a CUDA / SM90 (Hopper) request. ROCm is referenced only as prior art — the bot CC'd ROCm maintainers on keywords, apologies for the noise.

DeepSeek-V4.1's two-level indexer publishes candidate blocks at `candidate_source_layer_id`; later consumer indexers are meant to select their top-k **inside those candidate blocks only**. On SM100 this is implemented with DeepGEMM's sparse MQA-logits kernels (`fp8_fp4_(paged_)sparse_mqa_logits`). On SM90 there is no equivalent, so the consumers fall back to dense scoring over the full context followed by a mask.

vLLM currently implements candidate-consuming indexers in one of two ways:

1. **SM100** — `fp8_fp4_sparse_mqa_logits` / `fp8_fp4_paged_sparse_mqa_logits` via `DeepseekV41SparseIndexerBackend`. Opt-in through `AttentionConfig.indexer_sparse_logits` and hard-gated on SM100-class hardware (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_indexer.py`, the `is_device_capability_family(100)` check), the MXFP4 indexer cache, DeepGEMM >= 2.8, and the DeepSelect extension.
2. **ROCm (gfx950)** — candidate-only MQA scorers reading the candidate pool in place, in review as #57858 (prefill) and #57859 (decode).
3. **SM90 (H20)** — neither. The consumers run the full-width `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py` and then mask the scores down to the candidate blocks with `_apply_candidate_mask` (`vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py`). The candidate mechanism keeps the semantics but not the compute saving.

Measured on H20 (SM90), TP8, 1M context, decode, FP8 indexer cache, torch profiler:

| Concurrency | Per consumer layer | 4 consumer layers | Share of a step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ~10 | 2.067 ms | 8.28 ms | 20% of 40.75 ms |
| 1 | 196 µs | 0.78 ms | 6% |

Layers 24/28/32/36 each make one full-context `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` call per step. With `candidate_topk_blocks` = 2048 and `candidate_block_size` = 8, the candidate set is 16 384 positions against a 1 048 576-position compressed context — **1.6% of the scored columns** — so roughly 98% of each consumer's scoring work is discarded by the mask. The cost scales linearly with both concurrency and context length.

The requested feature is a CUDA/SM90 way to score only the candidate blocks.

### The MXFP4 coupling blocks SM90 today

`indexer_sparse_logits` cannot be enabled on SM90 at all, and not only because of the GPU-family check. The flag also requires the MXFP4 indexer cache (`sparse_indexer.py`, and again in `models/deepseek_v41/attention.py`), and MXFP4 itself is rejected before that:

```python
# vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py
if use_fp4 and not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100):
    raise ValueError(
        "indexer_kv_dtype='mxfp4' requires Blackwell datacenter GPUs "
        "(sm_10x, e.g. B200/GB200); sm_120 (consumer Blackwell) and "
        "earlier architectures are not supported."
    )
```

Hopper has no FP4 datapath, so SM90 necessarily runs the FP8 indexer cache (the `auto` default, one float32 scale per token). MXFP4 is an input requirement of the SM100 DeepGEMM kernels, not part of the "score only the candidate blocks" semantics — the ROCm path, for instance, scores the candidate pool with fp32 logits. So enabling candidate-only scoring on SM90 means letting that semantic flag be satisfied by an FP8 implementation.

**Question for maintainers:** should candidate-only scoring on SM90 reuse `indexer_sparse_logits` (relaxing its MXFP4 requirement to a per-platform one), or should it be a separate opt-in with its own builder type? The former keeps one user-facing knob and makes a future SM100 migration a no-op; the latter keeps each platform's preconditions self-contained.

### Alternatives

- **A. Gather + reuse the existing dense kernel (preferred).** Consumers gather their candidate K from the index cache (~2 MB per request) and score the gathered candidate set with the existing dense logits kernel, dropping the mask pass. No new scoring kernel. The scored K set and the query are identical to the dense-then-mask path, so the resulting logits should be bit-identical. A relevant primitive already exists on CUDA: `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache` (`torch.ops._C_cache_ops`, added in #25931 / #26456) gathers paged indexer K — FP8 values plus the 4-byte scale — into a contiguous workspace, and the prefill path uses it today. It gathers contiguous ranges addressed by `cu_seq_lens`, so it is a starting point rather than a drop-in: candidate-block gathering needs scattered block IDs.
- **B. Native SM90 sparse MQA-logits kernel.** Mirrors the SM100 DeepGEMM semantics with a new SM90 kernel, removing the gather hop. Better ceiling, substantially more implementation and validation cost.
- **C. Two-level selection inside the consumer (HISA-style).** Block-level coarse pass plus a refined pass inside the candidates. Extends the saving to the candidate-source layer and the ratio-2 layers, but changes the scoring semantics and needs accuracy re-validation. Better treated as a follow-up.

Both A and B need a profitability gate, because gathering loads more per key than the dense walk. #57858 measured the crossover at ~1.0–1.5× `span/capacity` and gates at 2.0×. This workload sits at 62.5×, well above the gate, so the gate should not engage in the target scenario.

### Additional context

**Relationship to existing work.** This is the SM90/CUDA counterpart of the ROCm candidate-only scorers. #57858 (prefill) and #57859 (decode, open) implement candidate-only scoring on gfx950, with measured operator speedups of 3.28× (66 rows, ctx 72.1k) and 4.85× (192 rows, ctx 88.5k), and +5.80% end-to-end output throughput with −4.9% p90 TPOT at TP=4, C=32. They list the same consumer layer positions (24/28/32/36). Those PRs are ROCm-only and touch `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`; the CUDA path is unimplemented. This is not a duplicate of them, though all three would touch `candidate_blocks.py`, so ordering matters.

Related, and deliberately out of scope here:

- #56254 wired the DeepGEMM sparse MQA-logits kernels into the V4.1 indexer. Its stated scope is SM100-class GPUs, and it documents "there is no PyTorch fallback anywhere on the path". That is the scoring path this issue proposes to extend to SM90, not to replace.
- #59204 (draft, conflicting) enables the DeepSelect sparse-indexer **top-k** on sm90. That covers the selection stage, not the scoring stage, and does not touch the SM100 gate on the sparse-logits backend.
- #61039 (merged 2026-10-14) made candidate selection length-aware in the decode indexer, removing ~850 µs/step of full-width work at 1M. It explicitly keeps the full-width path as the fallback when DeepSelect is unavailable, so **SM90 does not benefit from it**: `has_deep_select()` is SM100-only, so `select_candidate_blocks` keeps `FULL_WIDTH=True` on Hopper and still runs `torch.topk(2048)` over the full width. SM90 does have usable top-k backends (`cooperative`, `persistent`), so the same length-awareness looks portable. That is a separate, much smaller item (2.1% of a step at conc≈10, but ~6.5% at conc≈1) and would most naturally ride along with the scoring work rather than be filed on its own.
- The DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash kernels tracker (#56217) has no discussion of non-SM100 hardware.

**Open items to validate.**

1. Candidate block alignment: `candidate_block_size` = 8 vs the kernel page sizes (32/64).
2. Bit-identical results between the gather path and the current dense-then-mask path, to be confirmed by measurement rather than assumed.
3. The profitability threshold tuned for SM90 rather than copied from the ROCm measurements.
4. Whether the FP8 indexer record (`head_dim` + one float32 scale) gathers efficiently into the layout the dense kernel expects on SM90, where `mqa_logits_use_mx_scales()` is False.

**Environment (target).**

```text
GPU: H20 (SM90, Hopper)
TP: 8
Context: 1M
Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
Indexer K cache: FP8 (MXFP4 is unavailable on SM90, see above)
```

**Status.** Happy to implement the SM90 candidate-only scoring path (alternative A), but the flag question above decides where the code lands, so filing this first to get direction. The measurements above predate #61039; they will be re-taken on current main before any PR.

title: [DARFT][Core][DP] Add an opt-in cross-DP prefill delayer (--dp-prefill-delayer)
body:
## Overview

The DP ranks of a MoE engine step in lockstep. When any rank has prefill, the step becomes a long mixed (and, on some backends, eager) step for every rank. Agentic multi-turn traffic makes prefill frequent, so decode keeps getting interrupted. `--dp-prefill-delayer` (opt-in, default off) aligns prefill across the ranks and protects the decode steps after a prefill. It follows ATOM's PrefillDelayer.

## Claims

Measured on a development branch with an earlier version of this change: DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 8x MI355X, DP8 attention + EP8, AgentX agentic workload, 1200 s runs, metrics over 300-1200 s, single runs per configuration.

| Concurrency | Configuration | P90 interactivity (tok/s/user) | P50 interactivity (tok/s/user) | Total tok/s/GPU | TTFT p50 (s) | Node |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 64 | no delayer (`--prefill-schedule-interval 32`), mean of 2 runs | 16.65 | 31.03 | 22.0K | 3.76 | A, B |
| 64 | + prefill delayer (10 protected steps) | **45.54** | **56.89** | 22.2K | 8.63 | A |
| 128 | no delayer (`--prefill-schedule-interval 32`) | 7.29 | 11.96 | 23.8K | 7.47 | D |
| 128 | prefill delayer, 10 protected steps | 22.82 | 26.97 | 39.7K | 5.41 | C |
| 128 | prefill delayer, 20 protected steps | **26.36** | **28.92** | 38.6K | 10.03 | C |

- The c128 rows use a later recipe with other changes; they differ only in the prefill policy. The no-delayer c128 row ran on a different node of the same type.
- The trade-off is TTFT: prefill waits for the other ranks, and long prompts wait for alignment chunk by chunk.

Validation on this upstream branch is still to be added.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefill_delayer.py`: 14 passed (CPU). The tests cover each FIRE / HOLD rule and bound, the per-rank state, the scheduler gating and the config check.
- `pytest -m cpu_test tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py` and `tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py`: pass. They cover the changed `defer_prefills` expression with the delayer off.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass, mypy included.
- No GPU runs on this branch yet.

## Details

- **Protocol.** Once per engine step, each rank reports 6 ints in one CPU SUM all-reduce on the DP group: prefillable, pending prefill tokens (capped at `max_num_batched_tokens`), running decodes, KV usage >= 0.9, chunk in progress, prefill ran. Every rank then takes the same FIRE / HOLD decision for its next schedule.
- **Placement.** The all-reduce sits next to `_has_global_unfinished_reqs()`. Every rank reaches that point on every non-idle step (real, dummy and pause steps alike), which the existing DP state sync already relies on, so the extra collective cannot be skipped by one rank. The state resets at each DP wave boundary.
- **Rules (ATOM's), in order:**
  1. A step that ran prefill arms `--dp-prefill-delayer-protected-steps` (default 10) steps that HOLD while decodes run.
  2. FIRE if no rank has prefill, no rank decodes, or KV usage is high.
  3. FIRE after 200 held steps, or after 100 with a chunk in progress.
  4. HOLD until all ranks have prefill.
  5. FIRE when the pending tokens reach 0.9 x prefillable ranks x `max_num_batched_tokens`, or when the backlog stops growing for 10 steps.
- **HOLD scope.** HOLD defers all prefill compute, new requests and in-progress chunks, even on a rank without local decodes, so that ranks prefill together.
- **Interaction with `--prefill-schedule-interval`.** The delayer replaces it; setting both is an error.
- **Cost.** Off: none. On: one 6-int CPU all-reduce per step.
- **Not supported:** elastic EP and custom scheduler classes.
- **Relation to #51199** (cc @kjiang249). That PR coordinates releases through the DP coordinator (asynchronous, with acks and a 2-step lead); this one uses a synchronous per-step all-reduce in the engine loop and adds protected decode steps and a token fill target. We drove both decision functions in a CPU simulation of 8 lockstep ranks with agentic traffic:
  - #51199's all-ranks release rarely triggered; most of its releases came from its capacity and 30-pass fail-open bounds.
  - This delayer had 2-4x fewer mixed steps and about half the mean decode latency.
  - #51199 had about 3x lower TTFT.

  The two are complementary, and I am happy to merge efforts.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Avoid distributed RunAI draft loading with PP
body:
## Overview

Avoid distributed RunAI loading for speculative draft models instantiated only on the last pipeline stage. Reuse the existing MRV2 pipeline-safe draft loader helper and preserve distributed target loading.

**Dependency before merge:** [model-streamer #252](https://github.com/dsx-ai-factory/model-streamer/pull/252) must ship in the required RunAI version. Released 0.16.1 still performs a global collective during non-distributed safetensors header reads; this vLLM guard alone is insufficient with that release.

## Claims

- With PP>1, copy the RunAI draft extra config and disable its distributed mode, preserving S3 access and other loader options.
- Preserve PP1 behavior, the target configuration, and the existing fastsafetensors fallback.
- Resolve the reproduced PP2 draft-loading deadlock when paired with the RunAI fix.

## Validation

Six parametrized configuration regressions passed against the candidate helper in the deployed Linux vLLM 0.30.0 image, with GPUs hidden. Relevant pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, formatting, typos, mypy, and test tethering; `git diff --check` passed.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_dspark_utils.py -q \
  -k 'runai_draft_loading_preserves_target_configuration or pp_draft_preserves_loader_without_distributed_streaming'
```

A real two-process Gloo reproducer loads a local safetensors target on both ranks through `RunaiModelStreamerLoader.load_weights`, then loads the draft on rank 1 while rank 0 waits at the final barrier. It verifies exact loaded tensors. Runtime: Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, RunAI 0.16.1, safetensors 0.8.0; target streaming remained distributed.

| Configuration | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline | Collective timeout |
| vLLM guard only | Hidden header-discovery collective timeout |
| RunAI #252 only | Distributed draft-payload collective timeout |
| Both fixes | Target and draft load; exact tensors |

Full Kimi-K3 verification used two eight-B200 nodes, TP8/DCP8/PP2, InfiniBand RDMA, MRV2, and DSpark with three speculative tokens and block rejection sampling. Both patches were applied before startup inside isolated containers using pinned vLLM 0.30.0. All 16 ranks finished model loading, including the last-stage draft. A nonempty 512-token SSE response ended with `[DONE]`; arithmetic, cached prompt logprobs, images, ordered images, tool calls, and all 80 concurrent requests passed. Acceptance was **6,799 / 12,123 draft tokens (56.08%)**.

These are short synthetic correctness checks, not a broad quality evaluation or controlled throughput comparison. The full-model run used the exact helper backported to v0.30.0, rather than a complete build of this main-based branch. Kimi's existing CPU-offload count fix was present with one explicit test block per rank; production speculative offload sizing was outside this loading validation.

The unit cases are covered by the existing `v1-executor-worker` Buildkite job (`pytest v1/worker`). Full-model CI additionally requires the Kimi checkpoint and 16 B200 GPUs; the canary supplied that validation outside CI.

## Details

PP0 finishes target loading and never instantiates the draft. A draft inheriting distributed RunAI loading enters collectives requiring those absent PP0 participants. The existing shared helper already avoids this topology mismatch for fastsafetensors; extend it for RunAI while retaining its S3 loader. DSpark, EAGLE, and DFlash already call this helper. The change runs only during loading and adds no steady-state inference synchronization.

Independent draft reads can increase startup I/O compared with distributed draft streaming. A future process-group-aware RunAI API could support distributed reads scoped to the draft ranks. The target's large checkpoint retains its configured distributed loading mode.

Duplicate checks reviewed related work: #53901 addresses ROCm Kimi/fastsafetensors loading, #61699 applies the existing helper to standalone drafts, and #61715 integrates DeepSeek mixed CPU/GPU loading. None implements this RunAI PP draft guard. The loader deadlock is also described in comments on #44697; this change does not implement that RFC's broader PP token-accounting work. The existing RunAI #252 is reused rather than duplicated or vendored here.

---
