title: [Docs][Model] Sync supported-model tables with the registry and add a consistency test
body:
## Overview

Syncs the supported-model docs tables with the model registry (36 undocumented architectures, 5 stale rows, 1 removed-architecture row, 2 missing `<sup>C</sup>` markers) and adds three consistency tests to `tests/models/test_registry.py` that pin the docs to the registry in both directions. Docs-only change plus tests; no runtime code touched.

## Claims

- Every architecture in the documented registry dicts (`_TEXT_GENERATION_MODELS`, `_EMBEDDING_MODELS`, `_LATE_INTERACTION_MODELS`, `_REWARD_MODELS`, `_TOKEN_CLASSIFICATION_MODELS`, `_SEQUENCE_CLASSIFICATION_MODELS`, `_MULTIMODAL_MODELS`) now has a row in the model docs tables.
- Every architecture token in the docs tables is now either a registry architecture, a converted model (row marked `<sup>C</sup>`), or a documented non-registry architecture (out-of-tree plugin / Transformers fallback / speculative decoding); pooling-mode enum tokens (`ALL`, `CLS`, `LAST`, ...) are allowlisted as non-architectures.
- Removed architectures (`_PREVIOUSLY_SUPPORTED_MODELS`) no longer appear in the docs tables.
- Three deterministic CPU-only tests enforce all three invariants going forward, red/green-verified against the pre-fix docs.

## Validation

Red/green, CPU-only (macOS arm64, `.venv`, torch 2.14.1 + repo requirements). The tests are from this PR in both runs; only the docs differ.

**Red** — docs at upstream `main` (`0c2584929`), tests added:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k "are_registered or are_documented or are_absent" -v
```

- `test_docs_architectures_are_registered` **FAILED** — 9 stale tokens: `KimiAudioForConditionalGeneration`, `MiniMaxVL01ForConditionalGeneration`, `NVLM_D_Model`, `Qwen2_5OmniThinkerForConditionalGeneration`, `Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerForConditionalGeneration` (×2, main + transcription tables), `GemmaForSequenceClassification`, `JinaVLForSequenceClassification`, `Qwen3VLForSequenceClassification`
- `test_registry_architectures_are_documented` **FAILED** — 36 missing architectures (BertForMaskedLM, CohereCompassForConditionalGeneration, DeepseekV3BidirectionalModel, DeepseekV41ForCausalLM, Dots3NoteForCausalLM, EmbeddingGemma2Model, ExaoneMoEForCausalLM, FunAudioChatForConditionalGeneration, Glm5NextForCausalLM, Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration, HfMoondream, InklingForCausalLM, InklingForConditionalGeneration, JinaVLForRanking, LLaMAForCausalLM, LagunaForCausalLM, Llama4ForCausalLM, LongcatFlashNgramForCausalLM, MiniCPMV4_6ForConditionalGeneration, MiniCPMV4_7ForConditionalGeneration, Ministral3ForCausalLM, MoonshotKimiaForCausalLM, NVLM_D, NemotronHPuzzleForCausalLM, NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3, NemotronH_Super_Omni_Reasoning_V3, NemotronParseForConditionalGeneration, Qwen2_5OmniForConditionalGeneration, Qwen2_5OmniModel, Qwen3OmniMoeForConditionalGeneration, Qwen3_5ForCausalLM, Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM, Qwen4ExpForCausalLM, Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration, Step3TextForCausalLM, Terratorch)
- `test_removed_architectures_are_absent_from_docs` **FAILED** — `MiniMaxVL01ForConditionalGeneration` (in supported_models.md)

**Green** — with this PR's docs changes, same command: **3 passed**.

`pre-commit run --files <4 changed files>` — all hooks passed (incl. forbidden-imports, ruff, typos).

## Details

The worklist was generated mechanically (AST parse of `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py`, resolving the `**{...}` merge of `_TEXT_GENERATION_MODELS` aliases into `_EMBEDDING_MODELS`, diffed against first-column tokens of every model docs table), not by hand. Per-row facts come from source: LoRA/PP flags from the module class bases, example models from `tests/models/registry.py` (`TBA` where the test registry has none).

Fix classes:

1. **New rows** for recent registry additions, in the table their dict dictates (text vs multimodal vs pooling page): Qwen3.5 text-only pair, Qwen4-Exp pair, GLM-5.3 pair, Laguna, Llama 4 text-only, Step3 text-only, Inkling pair, DeepSeek-V4.1, Cohere Compass, Dots3Note, FunAudioChat, Nemotron-Parse, EmbeddingGemma 2, Terratorch, DeepseekV3BidirectionalModel.
2. **Alias merges** into existing rows where the registry key is an alias of a documented arch: `LLaMAForCausalLM`, `Ministral3ForCausalLM`, `ExaoneMoEForCausalLM`, `NemotronHPuzzleForCausalLM`, `LongcatFlashNgramForCausalLM`, `HfMoondream`, `MiniCPMV4_6/4_7ForConditionalGeneration`, `NemotronH_(Super_)Omni_Reasoning_V3`, `BertForMaskedLM`.
3. **Stale renames** to current registry keys (listed in Validation). `D3ForSequenceClassification`, `ClefFlashForJointSchema` and `ClefOmniForJointSchema` were left as-is: they are already documented in `structured_decisions_models.md`, which the tests scan.

Test design: deterministic file parsing (no network, no GPU, no model loading), skips when `docs/` is absent (installed-package runs), and carries `skip_global_cleanup` since it creates no global vLLM state. title: [Attention] Add opt-in FlashInfer fused DCP combine for MLA and GQA/MQA
body:
## Overview

Add opt-in `--dcp-comm-backend fi_a2a_fused` for MLA and FlashInfer GQA/MQA decode. It calls `decode_cp_a2a_lse_reduce` to exchange partial attention outputs and perform LSE-weighted reduction in one operation, reading vLLM's output/LSE views without layout copies.

**Draft:** depends on [FlashInfer #6483](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6483), which extends the NCCL implementation from [#4929](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4929) with mask and stride support. The repository's pinned dependencies cannot run this path. Dependency pins are unchanged; a supported minimum version will be selected after [FI #6483](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6483) is released and qualified.

## Claims

- Wire the backend into the MLA manager and FlashInfer GQA/MQA decode dispatcher. Existing defaults, Q/KV partitioning and prefill paths requiring merged LSE are preserved.
- Pass destination-major O and independently strided LSE through tensor views. FI receives the existing LSE log base and a source-rank token-validity mask.
- Use one `DCPValidTokenMask` helper across dense MLA, sparse MLA and FlashInfer metadata builders. Each builder owns its persistent buffer; existing normal, capture and drafting paths refresh it, including empty shards and graph padding. `AttentionGroup` and `CommonAttentionMetadata` are unchanged.

## Validation

| Check on the current source | Result |
|---|---|
| Local configuration/reference, metadata and worker utility tests | 114 passed, 51 skipped, 13 deselected |
| CUDA metadata tests; 2 × H100 80GB visible, TP=2 fixture | 19 passed, zero skips |
| Scoped pre-commit, including Ruff/mypy, and diff checks | Passed |

### Test commands

Local:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/test_dcp_a2a.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_dcp_spec_reorder.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_noncausal.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py \
  -q --confcutdir=tests/v1/attention -k 'not TestPackedA2AKernels'
```

GPU metadata:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_dcp_spec_reorder.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_noncausal.py \
  tests/distributed/test_dcp_a2a.py::test_fi_dcp_valid_token_mask_reuses_storage \
  -q -s -ra -x --confcutdir=tests/v1/attention
```

## Details

The adapter lives in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/flashinfer_dcp.py`; mask allocation/update is owned by the DCP helper and uses the Triton metadata kernel. Workspace capacity includes speculative width and graph padding, with independent state per observed stream and existing microbatch slot.

The path requires SM90+, FP16/BF16 O, FP32 LSE, compatible PyTorch/NCCL device APIs, NCCL ≥2.29, DCP size 2–64 within one supported NCCL LSA domain, and PCP=1. GQA/MQA additionally requires the FLASHINFER attention backend, unquantized KV cache and no attention sinks; existing TP/KV-head constraints apply. Initialization requirements and explicit opt-outs for conflicting symmetric-memory collectives are documented in `docs/serving/context_parallel_deployment.md`.

Related work:

- [#48248](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48248) replaces exchange with `decode_cp_a2a_alltoall` and retains separate Triton combine. This PR includes reduction in the FI call.
- [#48196](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48196) targets sparse MLA projection/merge ordering and Helix exchange. This PR adds the fused-combine backend and its metadata integration.
- [#50484](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50484) provides the existing native direct symmetric-memory path, which remains a comparison baseline alongside packed NCCL.

Reviewer notes:

- Dependency:  [FI #6483](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6483).
- Review mask lifetime/padding and workspace warmup. Each capture stream must be warmed on every rank.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4] Use AITER tuned GEMM for the compressor projections and inverse-RoPE einsum
body:
**Overview**
Route the DeepSeek-V4 compressor projections and the inverse-RoPE einsum on ROCm through aiter's tuned GEMMs instead of torch.mm / torch.einsum.

**Claims**
Replaces four torch.mm call sites in the DSv4 ROCm attention path with aiter.tuned_gemm.tgemm.mm, which selects a tuned kernel per shape.
Covers the multi-stream fork, not just the single-stream path. The fork splits the 2560×K compressor projection into 2048×K (main) and 512×K (indexer); both previously fell through to torch.mm.
Replaces torch.einsum("tgd,grd->tgr", …) in rocm_inv_rope_einsum with aiter's batched_gemm_bf16.
Validation
Profiled DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP4, gfx1250, ISL 1024:

before
Cijk_…MT256x128x64 (hipBLASLt, from torch.mm)	120.7 ms over 364 calls
tuned _gemm_a16w16_gfx1250_compute_bound_kernel	30 calls
The 364 Tensile calls are the two multi-stream projections; only the single-stream path was reaching the tuned kernel. Both multi-stream shapes have tuned configs shipped in aiter:
configs/gfx1250/gluon/gemm/gemm_a16w16/GEMM-A16W16-N=2048-K=7168.json and …N=512-K=7168.json.

pre-commit run --files on both changed files: 13 passed, 21 skipped, 0 failed (incl. ruff check, ruff format, mypy, typos, SPDX).

**Details**
tgemm.mm takes the weight untransposed and handles the transpose internally, so torch.mm(x, W.T, out_dtype=…) becomes tgemm.mm(x, W, otype=…).

On gfx1250 there is no tuned ASM/skinny/hipBLASLt bf16 kernel, so tuned_gemm.py routes unscaled bf16/fp16 to the Triton (gluon) a16w16 kernel; an explicit tuned-CSV entry still takes precedence where one exists. The torch.mm fallback instead lands on hipBLASLt, which is what the measurement above shows.

The tgemm imports are function-local, matching the existing style in this file and avoiding an import-time dependency on aiter.

title: [WIP][Attention] Shard MiniMax M3 indexer cache across TP ranks
body:
## Overview

Add opt-in tensor-parallel sharding of the MiniMax M3 FP8 indexer cache. On supported TP4 Blackwell deployments, each rank stores one quarter of the token rows in every index-K page and exchanges partial block maxima for the existing Top-K selection.

## Claims

- Reduce persistent index-K bytes per block per rank by 75%, with separate symmetric receive/staging buffer overhead. Main attention Q/K/V partitioning and cache precision are unchanged.
- Support decode, CUDA Graph replay, and prefill reconstruction through the MSA backend, behind `--attention-config '{"indexer_cache_sharding":"on","indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}'`. The default is `off`; `auto` applies backend-specific eligibility and workload thresholds.
- Coordinate catchable rank-local allocation failures and prefill-gather kernel compilation/loading failures before the corresponding peer rendezvous, so ranks select the same fallback instead of entering different collectives.

## Validation

Validated commit `f2f35b3785` (parent `de7d70676d`) on four GB200 GPUs:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Saved pre-fix initialization + rank-1 receive-allocation failure | Reproduced the hang: peers blocked in rendezvous while the failing rank entered the fallback CPU all-reduce. The 90-second watchdog terminated the test. |
| Fixed TP4 integration and three injected initialization failures | Passed, 149.10 seconds. |
| MSA/CuTe baseline, sharded score, packed-cache layout, and FP8 insertion | 30 passed, 198.53 seconds. |
| Full M3 checkpoint, sharding off/on with matched FlashInfer tactics | 1,024 generated tokens matched exactly; maximum absolute difference across 5,120 paired top-5 logprobs was 0. See the numerical control below. |

```bash
cd /work/source
export PYTHONPATH=/work/source OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MAX_JOBS=8
/work/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_minimax_m3_indexer_sharding.py -v -s
/work/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py \
  -k 'sharded_decode_index_score or indexer_cache_squeezes or fmha_sm100_indexer_matches_reference or decode_index_score_cutedsl_correctness or sparse_full_fp8_index' -v
```

All changed-file pre-commit checks passed. Runtime: PyTorch `2.15.0a0+875d815502.nvinternal.main`, CUDA 13.5, CUTLASS DSL 4.8.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2rc4, and Ray 2.56.1. Official ARM64 wheel extensions from `9b99ccb56` were used after verifying that all compiled-source/build paths match the tested commit; no operator replacement was used.

<details>
<summary>Full-model E2E setup and numerical control</summary>

Loaded the complete `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4` checkpoint at revision `901464083161bf8612a29ff7ad29914cd4ab4a85`. Settings: TP4, BF16 activations, FP8 index cache, 128-token pages, 16,384 maximum model length, 8 maximum sequences, 2,048 batched tokens, 4 GiB KV-cache budget per rank, chunked prefill and prefix caching enabled, and full decode CUDA Graphs captured at sizes 1/2/4/8. Each request generated 64 greedy tokens with raw top-5 logprobs. No speculative decoding was used.

| Workload | Compared generated tokens | Token mismatches | Max absolute logprob difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Sequential prompts of 128, 2,304, and 8,192 tokens, each repeated twice with prefix cache reset | 384 | 0 | 0 |
| Mixed batch of 8 prompts, spanning 128 to 8,192 tokens | 512 | 0 | 0 |
| Two requests reusing cached prefixes | 128 | 0 | 0 |

Both modes also reproduced their sequential outputs exactly across repeats. The compared mixed and prefix-reuse runs had matching dispatch signatures, exercised mixed prefill/decode and full CUDA Graph replay, and completed with the one-sided page gather enabled on all four sharded ranks.

**Numerical control:** Independently autotuned off/on runs did not meet the exact-output criterion. Replicating index-Q changes the combined QKV projection width from 2,560 to 2,944; FlashInfer selected different GEMM tactics, including split-K counts. Matching common GEMM/MoE tactics alone still left 115/192 sequential tokens different. Matching the shape-specific QKV split-K count as well (4 for both widths at decode batch sizes 1/2/4/8) produced the results above. Every rank loaded the same 144-entry controlled tactic cache; the caches were unchanged after execution, with no retuning logged. These are finite-workload equivalence results under matched tactics, not a guarantee of exact outputs with independent autotuning or a model-quality evaluation. Tactic-cache controls are test setup only and are not added to production code.

Worker inspection confirmed index pages changed from `[882, 128, 128]` to `[1031, 32, 128]`, reducing index-K storage from 16 KiB to 4 KiB per page per rank. Under the fixed KV budget, total token capacity increased from 112,896 to 131,968. This excludes additional replicated projection weights and symmetric buffers (3 MiB receive plus two 64 MiB staging buffers per rank in this run). No E2E speedup is claimed.

`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn` was used in both modes because the existing prefill planner performs a CPU transfer; this is not a strict sync-free validation.

</details>

The committed tests extend the existing M3 score/cache-insert suites and add one manual four-GPU test for production MSA dispatch. The TP4 test exercises DQL 1/4/8, multiple layers, mailbox reuse, CUDA Graph replay, mixed prefill/decode, shared pages, one-sided and NCCL page reconstruction, and rank-local initialization failures. No CI jobs are added or changed; TP4 symmetric-memory coverage requires four peer-accessible SM100-family GPUs and is documented in the existing manual-test allowlist.

## Details

Rank `r` owns token rows `r, r+4, ...` within each 128-token page, retaining all 128 index-K dimensions for each owned token. All index-Q heads are projected locally. The score kernel sends partial block maxima to each head's owner, which reduces them before existing Top-K selection. Prefill reconstructs full pages using symmetric staging, with NCCL fallback.

Eligibility is limited to TP4, SM100-family GPUs, FP8 index cache, MSA top-16, supported speculative methods with index-head count times maximum query length at most 32, and no prefill/decode context parallelism. Unsupported deployments retain replicated storage. Query replication and communication add work; shorter contexts may be slower. The change keeps the upstream prefill planner.

Initialization coordinates each local preparation phase over the TP CPU group before its corresponding peer rendezvous. Receive-buffer allocation/initialization is coordinated first; page-gather allocation and kernel compilation/loading are coordinated before the later staging-buffer rendezvous. This handles catchable local setup failures; process death or communication-internal failures remain engine errors. Decode kernels compile during the normal warmup path.

Related work: [#59980](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59980) retains replicated index-K storage and distributes whole-block scoring, with query and Top-K candidate gathers. [#57909](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57909) implements AMD block-scoring CP and shares the replicated index-Q loader mechanism; that loader support should be reused when either change lands. This PR changes physical token-row ownership and reconstructs pages for prefill. [#59979](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59979) separately changes prefill planning.

Adapted from Suyog Gupta's [index-K sharding commit](https://github.com/xinli-sw/vllm/commit/69a7c7bf290843181349fc958b10f902276e7b09), with backend integration, reduced scope, initialization coordination, and tests. AI assistance was used for extraction, implementation, review, and validation.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono: issue the FFN seam's static loads before their polls
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

DSv4.1-Flash mono decode (MI355X): K2's FFN seam read its static data (norm weight, score bias, slice inputs) only after the poll before it, so that load latency sat on the layer's critical path. They are now issued before the poll, as the attention front and back already do. Follow-up to #60397 and #61082; outputs are bit for bit unchanged. Touches the same files as #60731 (gfx942 port), so whichever merges second needs a rebase.

## Claims

- K1 + K2 per layer is 2.8-3.6 us faster for M = 1 and 6 at TP2 and TP4 (-2.5% to -4.8%); larger steps gain 0.4-1.5%. No point is slower.
- End to end, TP4 c1 decode ITL drops 1.7-1.8% (1.704 -> 1.675 ms and 1.710 -> 1.680 ms, DSpark, synthetic acceptance 3.51).
- Kernel outputs are bit for bit identical to `main`, and `test_dsv41_mono_numerics` passes at TP2 and TP4.

## Validation

**Kernel level.** One layer with random weights in the checkpoint's formats (the numerics test's fixtures), K1 + K2 launched 10 times back to back in one HIP graph, median of 7 timed batches. Each cell is the mean of two runs with the two builds on swapped GPU sets (`main` in a separate worktree). Two runs of identical code differ by up to 0.4 us (M <= 12) and 2.4 us (M = 48).

| TP | layer, M | `main` (us) | this PR (us) | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | ratio 1, M=1 | 67.6 | 64.8 | -2.8 (-4.1%) |
| 4 | ratio 1, M=6 | 93.5 | 90.4 | -3.2 (-3.4%) |
| 4 | ratio 1, M=12 | 124.5 | 123.0 | -1.6 (-1.3%) |
| 4 | ratio 2, M=48 | 295.2 | 291.5 | -3.8 (-1.3%) |
| 2 | ratio 1, M=1 | 75.4 | 71.8 | -3.6 (-4.8%) |
| 2 | ratio 1, M=6 | 121.4 | 118.4 | -3.0 (-2.5%) |
| 2 | ratio 1, M=12 | 182.1 | 179.5 | -2.7 (-1.5%) |
| 2 | ratio 2, M=48 | 458.3 | 456.3 | -2.0 (-0.4%) |

All 16 pairwise comparisons (8 cells x 2 GPU placements) are faster than `main`, from -0.13 to -6.1 us.

**Bit-exactness.** The layer's outputs (out, residual, post / comb / pre mixes, the normed FFN input, the mid-layer state) are `torch.equal` to `main`'s on every rank at TP2 and TP4, for all four cases above.

**Numerics.** The body of `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` (`_check_layers`: the layer against vLLM's ops, the FFN launch, and 300 replays of both step widths in one graph, bit for bit) passes at TP2 and TP4. It was run through a Ray-free `torchrun` wrapper because Ray is not installed on the dev node; CI runs the test itself.

**End to end.** Offline decode at TP4, c1, 30K-token prompt, DSpark with 5 drafts and synthetic acceptance 3.51, ITL from `(t(576 tokens) - t(64 tokens)) / 512`, 4 valid repeats per arm (the first repeat of each run is a warm-up artifact).

| arm | GPUs | ITL median (ms) | repeats (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 4-7 | 1.704 | 1.702, 1.704, 1.728, 1.769 |
| this PR | 0-3 | 1.675 | 1.603, 1.675, 1.687, 1.725 |
| `main` | 0-3 | 1.710 | 1.683, 1.710, 1.716, 1.753 |
| this PR | 4-7 | 1.680 | 1.648, 1.680, 1.720, 1.733 |

The `main` arm is within 2% of the 1.680 ms of #61082's AgentX run. 40 layers x about 3 us is 0.12 ms per step, 0.034 ms per token at acceptance 3.51, as measured. No AgentX or accuracy run was made: the outputs are bit for bit unchanged.

**GSM8K.** InferenceX's task, as in its DSv4.1-Flash eval runs ([run 38377181342](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38377181342), reference 0.9727 at TP4): the custom `gsm8k` task whose prompt ends "End your response with the answer on the last line, formatted as: #### [number]", `local-chat-completions`, `--apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn`, 5-shot, full 1,319 questions, `max_tokens=12288`, temperature 0, 64 requests in flight. Servers use the InferenceX #3690 recipe with `--monokernel` and DSpark (5 drafts, block rejection, real acceptance). One run per cell, `main` and this PR on separate servers.

| TP | `main` strict / flexible | this PR strict / flexible |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0.9674 / 0.9666 (+-0.0049) | 0.9750 / 0.9742 (+-0.0043) |
| 2 | 0.9727 / 0.9719 (+-0.0045) | 0.9750 / 0.9742 (+-0.0043) |

- Every cell is within one standard error of InferenceX's 0.9727; the differences between the arms (+0.2 to +0.8 points) are inside the noise.
- The serving stack is not deterministic at this level (100 greedy c1 completions on the TP2 `main` server, run twice, are identical in 55 of 100; `main` against this PR in 55 and 52 of 100), so output identity is not a usable check; the bit-exactness above is at the layer level.

Reproduction: the task is lm-eval's `gsm8k` with `doc_to_text: "Question: {{question}}\nEnd your response with the answer on the last line, formatted as: #### [number]\nAnswer:"` and `until: ["</s>", "<|im_end|>"]`, run with `--model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs max_tokens=12288,temperature=0,top_p=1` and `num_concurrent=64,max_length=16384`.

## Details

A per-CTA timeline of K2 (stamps after each stage, TP4, M=6) put the FFN seam on the critical path as: last slice -> norm (3.8 us) -> xrdy -> router -> route -> ug. Inside the norm, the 8 norm-weight loads per thread were issued after the rstd, so the apply step took 2.4 us. The same pattern was in two more places:

- `stage_norm`: the norm weight is loaded before the `lin` poll (K1's seam norm shares this function and gains too).
- `stage_route`: the score bias is loaded before the logits poll.
- `stage_slice` in K2's FFN seam: the residual rows, mixes and `hc_fn` are loaded before the attention all-reduce's poll (`slice_preload`; `batched_rounds` takes the first batch's loads ready-made, later batches load as before). The FFN launch (`part`) takes the same path.

The values read are unchanged, so every output is too. The change is 47 lines in the mono package, and the K2 kernel's VGPR (246) and LDS use are unchanged.

<details><summary>Tried and not included</summary>

All measured with the same kernel microbenchmark; none changes the outputs.

- **Router gate weights before the x wait:** -1.4 us at TP4 M=12, but +1.9 us at M=6 (repeatable on other GPUs). The 3.9 MB burst lands while the norm stage is on the critical path (norm finishes about 0.9 us later). Kept out.
- **Deeper weight-load pipelining in the routed ug GEMV** (`ahead = slices`): neutral at TP4, +7 us at TP2 M=48.
- **Two poll loads in flight:** LLVM merged the duplicate loads, so only instructions were added; +0.7 to +1.4 us.
- **L2 weight prefetch of the static weights** (an oracle that touches them before each launch): under 1% of K2, so no kernel work was done.
- **The gate stage is not on the critical path:** it runs on CTAs 160-165 in parallel with norm (166-171); a faster Sinkhorn would not shorten the layer.
- **Attention back and the expert phase:** the back already issues its static loads before its polls; the expert phase is HBM-bound and its tasks quantize (22 experts x 18 parts on 256 CTAs). No cheap change found.

</details>

Limitations: MI355X only (CDNA4, as the kernels), TP2 / TP4, decode steps of at most 48 rows; the kernel-level numbers use warm weights, so they say nothing about expert-weight streaming (which this change does not touch). I found no open PR making this change. Developed and measured with Claude Code; the submitter's line-by-line review is still pending.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Default AITER fused shared experts on for GLM-5.x MXFP4
body:
## Overview

On gfx950, GLM-5.x MXFP4 checkpoints now turn on `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` when it is unset, because AITER tunes their fused MoE only for the fused shared-expert shape. Related: #28985, #59221, #60604.

## Claims

- GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X, TP4, MTP: output throughput +7-14%, mean TPOT -6-12%, prefill TTFT -6-7%; gsm8k within stderr, MTP acceptance unchanged.
- An explicit 0 or 1 still wins. Other models, platforms and layouts keep the default (off).

## Validation

- `pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py -k "not test_models_fse_init"`: 90 passed, 9 new (the deselected cases need a free GPU). pre-commit clean.
- `create_engine_config()` on real checkpoints: flag on for GLM-5.1/5.2/5.3-MXFP4 at TP4 and GLM-5.2-MXFP4 at TP8; unchanged for TP2, EP, GLM-5.2-FP8, AITER off.
- Serving, GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X, TP4, MTP3, two runs per arm in ABBA order, no failed requests. Flag on is this PR's default:

| workload | output tok/s, flag off → on | mean TPOT (ms), flag off → on |
|---|---|---|
| 1k/1k c16 | 1472.6 → 1671.6 (+13.5%) | 10.09 → 8.89 (-11.9%) |
| 1k/1k c64 | 3095.1 → 3365.6 (+8.7%) | 19.34 → 17.71 (-8.4%) |
| 8k/1k c64 | 1541.9 → 1654.7 (+7.3%) | 35.51 → 33.19 (-6.5%) |

- 8k-in prefill median TTFT: 475.8 → 449.0 ms at c1, 6701.5 → 6240.0 ms at c16.
- This PR's head with the flag unset, one run: 1681.7 tok/s / 8.87 ms at 1k/1k c16, 3503.5 tok/s / 17.32 ms at c64; the server log shows the auto-enable line and every FP4 MoE lookup on the tuned 257 / top-9 rows.
- gsm8k 5-shot strict: 0.9386 flag off, 0.9393 flag on, 0.9333 in both runs of this PR with the flag unset (stderr 0.007). MTP acceptance length 3.31, 3.31, 3.30.

<details>
<summary>Per-run numbers, kernel lookups and reproduction</summary>

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (AITER 0.1.25) running main at 7f730b4 and this branch from source. The decode rows and gsm8k compare main with the flag set to 0 and 1 (F1-F4). The prefill rows compare main and this branch with the flag unset (P1-P4). P2/P3 ran an earlier revision of this branch with the same enable conditions. R1 is the head (c716073) with the flag unset, one run; its c64 throughput is 4% above the F2/F3 mean, and Claims use F1-F4 only.

| run | arm | 1k/1k c16 tok/s, TPOT | 1k/1k c64 tok/s, TPOT | 8k/1k c64 tok/s, TPOT | 8k/1 c1 / c16 median TTFT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | main, flag 0 | 1463.5, 10.07 | 3105.2, 19.57 | 1515.4, 35.77 | |
| F2 | main, flag 1 | 1691.1, 8.80 | 3383.7, 17.73 | 1646.9, 33.42 | |
| F3 | main, flag 1 | 1652.0, 8.98 | 3347.4, 17.68 | 1662.5, 32.96 | |
| F4 | main, flag 0 | 1481.6, 10.11 | 3084.9, 19.10 | 1568.3, 35.24 | |
| P1 | main, unset | | | | 475.2 / 6703.7 |
| P2 | branch, unset | 1632.5, 9.04 | 3359.5, 17.37 | 1654.9, 32.93 | 450.8 / 6247.8 |
| P3 | branch, unset | | | | 447.2 / 6232.1 |
| P4 | main, unset | | | | 476.4 / 6699.2 |
| R1 | branch head, unset | 1681.7, 8.87 | 3503.5, 17.32 | | |

gsm8k strict / flexible: F1 0.9386 / 0.9371, F2 0.9393 / 0.9378, P2 0.9333 / 0.9333, R1 0.9333 / 0.9340. MTP acceptance length over each gsm8k run: F1 3.31, F2 3.31, P2 3.30, R1 3.30. Decode-run TTFT is within noise (8k/1k c64 median 1022 / 1245 ms flag off, 1274 / 1284 ms flag on; mean 4466 / 4508 vs 4220 / 4323 ms).

AITER fused-MoE lookups in the server log (120 FP4 lookups per run across the 4 ranks):
- flag off (F1, P1): all are `(6144, 512, 256, 8, ..., float4_e2m1fn_x2, per_1x32)` and log "using 2stage default".
- flag on (F2, P2, R1): all are `(6144, 512, 257, 9, ...)` and pick tuned FlyDSL kernels (`flydsl_mxmoe_g1_a4w4_*` or `flydsl_moe1_afp4_wfp4_*`, then `flydsl_moe2_*`). The BF16 MTP layer stays `(256, 8)` in both arms.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0 \
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'

# C in {16, 64}. 8k/1k c64: --random-input-len 8192 --num-prompts 256 --seed 43.
# Prefill: --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1, 16 prompts at c1, 256 at c16.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 \
  --num-prompts $((8 * C)) --max-concurrency $C --seed 42

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --model_args model=amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False
```

</details>

## Details

- Cause: AITER 0.1.25's `glm5_fp4_tuned_fmoe.csv` tunes this model's gfx950 W4A4 MoE only at 257 experts / top-9 (TP1/2/4/8 per-rank sizes); the unfused 256 / top-8 MoE gets default heuristics.
- Placement: the `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` config hook sets the env var, like the `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` auto-enable: the MoE router reads the process-wide flag, and the env var is in the torch.compile cache key.
- Gate: TP4/TP8 without DP, PCP or EP, as in #59221. The per-layer quantization check still runs, so the BF16 MTP layer of GLM-5.2/5.3-MXFP4 stays unfused (one existing warning per worker).
- Limits: TP8 and GLM-5/5.1/5.3-MXFP4 (same shapes) checked at config level only. TP2 stays opt-in, unmeasured. MI355X serving is not in CI.

Not a duplicate: #59221/#60604 cover GLM-5.3-Flash, #57916 MXFP8, #58904 weight loading; none changes the `glm_moe_dsa` default.

<details>
<summary>Design notes and duplicate search</summary>

- #28985 turned the flag off globally for mixed-precision shared experts (Kimi INT4 routed + BF16 shared), DeepSeek FP4 precision and EPLB. Here the shared expert is MXFP4 like the routed experts, the per-layer quantization check still applies and EP is excluded; gsm8k is unchanged.
- The gate is per model, like GLM-5.3-Flash's `_fused_shared_experts_tuned` and DeepSeek-V4's, because each follows its own AITER table (GLM-5.3-Flash adds gfx942 in #60604; this model's table is gfx950 only).
- A per-layer default inside the model, leaving the env var unset, would also need `GroupedTopKRouter`, `rocm_aiter_grouped_topk`, `FusedMoEConfig` and `RocmPlatform.apply_config_platform_defaults` to stop reading the global flag.
- The env var stays set for the rest of the process, as with the breakable-cudagraph auto-enable. With `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` unset (vLLM's default) nothing changes.
- Searched `gh pr list --state all` for "fused shared experts GLM", "VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS default", "GLM-5 MXFP4 ROCm", "GLM-5.2 MXFP4 AITER" and "shared experts fusion ROCm GLM". Also related: #60831 (opt-in GLM-5 MonoKernel decode, which requires this flag on), #53248 (Quark exclude check), #53953 (AITER fusions for GLM-5.2-MXFP4, no FSE change), #61345 (DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE FSE opt-in).

</details>

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the implementation, the measurements and this description.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip DSA indexer scoring for short dense-MHA prefills
body:
## Overview

On ROCm, the `deepseek_v32` path (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x) now skips the sparse indexer's scoring for pure short prefills that run on dense MHA, as CUDA already does (#48407, #51298). Builds on the ROCm dense-MHA prefill from #49263.

## Claims

- GLM-5.1-FP8, MI355X, TP4: 1K-token prefill median TTFT -8.1% at c1, -1.6% at c32. gsm8k unchanged.
- GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (indexer on 21 of 78 layers): no significant change.
- Mixed batches, prefills longer than `index_topk`, MTP layers, FULL cudagraph and capture still score. Other platforms are unchanged.

## Validation

- `test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py`: 35 passed, 8 skipped (CUDA-only) on MI355X, 7 new. pre-commit clean.
- `test_rocm_fused_v32_dense_prefill_matches_mqa` (existing, AMD V1 Attention CI): passed, auto and fp8 KV. Its dense run skips one step whose keys a later 2049+-token decode scores.
- Serving, GLM-5.1-FP8, TP4, output 1 token, 2 runs per arm, ABBA, no failed requests:

| workload | median TTFT (ms), main → PR | change |
|---|---|---|
| 1K in, c1 | 164.5 → 151.2 | -8.1% |
| 1K in, c32 | 1948.6 → 1918.0 | -1.6% |
| 1900 in, c1 | 175.6 → 173.6 | within noise |
| 8K in, c1 (sparse path) | 620.2 → 623.4 | within noise |

- gsm8k 5-shot strict, GLM-5.1-FP8: main 0.9469 / 0.9424, PR 0.9447 / 0.9462 (stderr 0.006).
- GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MTP3, 3 runs per arm: TTFT -0.6% to -1.9%, within noise. gsm8k strict 0.9356 → 0.9356, acceptance length 3.31 → 3.31.

<details>
<summary>Per-run numbers, probes, profile and reproduction</summary>

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (AITER 0.1.25) running main at 7f730b4 and this branch from source, MI355X.

GLM-5.1-FP8 (78 indexer layers, no spec decode), median TTFT in ms:

| run | arm | 1K c1 | 1900 c1 | 1K c32 | 8K c1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | main | 166.5 | 175.8 | 1950.1 | 622.9 |
| F2 | PR | 149.2 | 174.6 | 1916.9 | 623.1 |
| F3 | PR | 153.1 | 172.7 | 1919.1 | 623.6 |
| F4 | main | 162.5 | 175.4 | 1947.0 | 617.4 |

gsm8k flexible: main 0.9462 / 0.9409, PR 0.9439 / 0.9484. 1K c32 total throughput 16616 → 17042 tok/s (+2.6%, within noise).

GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (21 indexer layers plus the MTP layer; TTFT runs use MTP3 with synthetic acceptance 3.0), median TTFT in ms, runs in order A B B A A B:

| arm | 1K c1 | 1900 c1 | 1K c32 | 8K c1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 152.4 / 154.3 / 152.8 | 148.9 / 150.3 / 152.2 | 1501.8 / 1503.7 / 1513.2 | 471.6 / 475.7 / 473.0 |
| PR | 152.0 / 150.6 / 154.1 | 145.7 / 147.4 / 149.5 | 1489.8 / 1492.2 / 1492.2 | 471.8 / 470.5 / 457.9 |

GLM-5.2 gsm8k with real MTP3: strict 0.9356 → 0.9356, flexible 0.9356 → 0.9363, acceptance length 3.310 → 3.311. At concurrency 1 (250 questions, every prefill a pure short prefill): 0.952 → 0.944 (stderr 0.014). A probe on TP rank 0 counted indexer-layer calls on pure dense-MHA prefills: main scored 8382 of 8382, the PR 382 of 8404, all on the MTP layer.

Why 1K gains more than 1900 (GLM-5.1-FP8, TP rank 0). Prefill runs eagerly, and on main the host needs about 148 ms to issue a step at either length. A probe timed the forward without a profiler (median of 20, ms). Host times move by up to 10 ms between sessions with node load; a first main session under heavy load (1K host issue 187 ms) was repeated:

| arm | 1K: host issue / GPU tail after it | 1900: host issue / GPU tail after it |
|---|---|---|
| main | 147.6 / 4.4 | 149.8 / 12.3 |
| PR, run 1 | 131.3 / 6.9 | 131.1 / 27.6 |
| PR, run 2 | 142.0 / 0.4 | 143.4 / 15.3 |

At 1K the GPU finishes within a few ms of the last launch, so the step is host-bound and the indexer's host work shows up in TTFT. At 1900 the GPU runs 12-28 ms past the host; host + tail stays at 159-162 ms in every run, and only the indexer's GPU time is saved. A torch profiler trace per step: the PR removes 312 kernels (4 per layer), 1.43 ms of GPU time at 1K and 2.17 ms at 1900; on main the indexer op costs 190-198 us of host time but 24-34 us of GPU time per call (host time inflated by the profiler).

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0 \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9
# GLM-5.2: amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4, same flags plus
#   --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'

# 1K c1 shown. 1900 c1: --random-input-len 1900 --seed 45.
# 1K c32: --num-prompts 512 --max-concurrency 32 --seed 46.
# 8K c1: --random-input-len 8192 --num-prompts 16 --seed 47.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1 --temperature 0 \
  --num-prompts 40 --max-concurrency 1 --seed 44

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False

VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -v tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  "tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_rocm_fused_v32_dense_prefill_matches_mqa"
```

</details>

## Details

- Placement: `DeepseekV32MLAAttention._fused_attention`, which already holds the MLA metadata. CUDA passes the layer name into its op only because the op cannot see that metadata.
- Conditions: the CUDA op's, plus the layer taking the dense-MHA branch. The flag in `DeepseekV32Attention` moves from `is_cuda()` to `is_cuda_alike()`.
- K cache: still written by `fused_norm_rope`; only scoring is dropped.
- The gain is host time: an eager 1K prefill is host-bound and each indexer call costs about 0.2 ms on the host; at 1900 the step is GPU-bound and the indexer kernels take about 2 ms per step.
- Not measured: DeepSeek-V3.2 (same code path), GLM-5.1 with MTP, TP8.

<details>
<summary>Design notes</summary>

- Moving the check into `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer` would mirror CUDA but add an argument to an op that DeepSeek-V4 shares; the model already has the MLA metadata and the dense-MHA decision.
- The ROCm indexer op is built with `skip_k_cache_insert=True`. `fused_norm_rope` writes the indexer keys and clears the top-k buffer before the decision.
- PCP leaves the flag off, as on CUDA; ROCm sparse MLA rejects DCP. MTP layers keep scoring, as on CUDA.
- This model is not torch.compiled. Prefills run eagerly under the default FULL_DECODE_ONLY; under breakable cudagraphs the eager segment re-evaluates the decision on replay. Profile and dummy runs (no metadata) still call the op, so its workspace is reserved.

</details>

Not a duplicate: no open or closed PR skips indexer scoring on ROCm.

<summary>Duplicate search</summary>

Nearest: #56944 and #60601 (shard indexer prefill rows across TP), #61504 (sparse MLA decode indptr), #60294 (aiter `mqa_logits` for indexer prefill); none skips scoring.

title: [KV Offload] Load small CPU-tier hits synchronously within the step
body:
## Overview

On wide-EP MoE prefill (such as GLM-5.3), a step takes 0.3 to 0.5 s. Almost every request has a small CPU-tier hit, and an async load parks it for about 2 steps although the copy takes ~1 ms.

This adds an opt-in `sync_load_max_tokens` option (`kv_connector_extra_config`, default 0, off): smaller hits load in the same step. The change stays in the offloading connector's scheduler and worker.

## Changes

- `scheduler.py`: hits up to `sync_load_max_tokens` return `load_async=False`, so the request is scheduled in this step; the load targets its blocks by position and is marked sync.
- `worker.py`: waits for sync loads before the forward pass and does not report them in `finished_recving`.
- `common.py`: a `TransferJob.sync` flag carries that decision from scheduler to worker.

## Claims

- Hits up to the limit load in the same step. The limit exists because the whole batch waits for the copy. A hit that would leave nothing to compute stays async.
- Sync-load blocks are hashed at allocation, so the load range is found by position. Other requests can match them in the same step, which is safe since the forward pass waits for the copy.
- The worker waits for sync loads with the existing `OffloadingWorker.wait()` before the forward pass.
- With the option at 0, behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

Qwen3-30B-A3B on H100, OffloadingConnector + TieringOffloadingSpec. 12k-token prefix in GPU cache, 2k-token tail only in the CPU tier. Median extra TTFT vs a GPU-hit control:

| Setup | Without fix | With fix (limit 4096) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 node: DP=2 + EP (this version, 10 reps) | +219 ms | +1 ms |
| 2 nodes: TP=8, DP=2, EP over 16 GPUs (12 reps) | +344 ms | +8 ms |

GLM-5.3, one prefill group (4x8 H100, wide EP), request latency with a CPU-tier hit: ~1.9 s without the fix or above the limit, ~0.85 s under it (hits of 2k to 15k tokens).

Correctness: greedy continuation with the tail served from the CPU tier is correct 7/7 (Qwen3 and GLM-5.3).

    pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/   # 595 passed

## Details

Not a duplicate: no open PR adds sync offload loads (closest: #60574, #58198).

title: [AMD][DSV4.1Flash] Quantize MoE activations to MXFP8 before the MoRI dispatch
body:
## Motivation

MXFP4 W4A16 experts declare BF16 activations, so MoRI dispatches raw BF16 and
AITER quantizes to group-32 MXFP8 on arrival. A token routed to `k` distinct
ranks is therefore quantized `k` times — expected ~4.4 of 8 ranks at topk=6 for
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash — and the dispatch carries 2 bytes/element instead of
1 + 1/32.

Quantizing in `prepare()` moves that to once per token on the rank that owns it,
and roughly halves the dispatch payload.

AITER already consumes the result: with a pre-quantized FP8 operand and E8M0
scales, its stage-1 path sorts the scales (`mxfp4_moe_sort_fwd`) instead of
running its own quant. This mirrors the MXFP4 W4A4 dispatch added in #59596,
which takes the same pre-quantized route for a4w4.

## Summary of changes

**`all2all_utils.py`** — adds `mori_use_mxfp8_dispatch()` and wires a third
dispatch mode into `maybe_make_prepare_finalize()`. MoRI infers the payload
dtype from the input tensor and transports `scale_dim` scales of
`scale_type_size` bytes per token, so the new branch sets
`scale_dim = hidden_dim / 32` and a 1-byte scale element. E8M0 exponents are
bytes, not the fp32 the per-token/per-tensor FP8 paths use.

**`prepare_finalize/mori.py`** — adds the `use_mxfp8_dispatch` flag and the
corresponding quant in `prepare()`, via `get_hip_quant(QuantType.per_1x32)` with
`scale_type=dtypes.fp8_e8m0`, matching the FP4 branch directly above it. The
mutual-exclusion assert becomes `sum(...) <= 1` now that there are three modes.

**Gating is deliberately narrow.** A pre-quantized operand is only safe when
AITER would have produced MXFP8 itself: a BF16-activation kernel would cast the
FP8 payload back to BF16 and never apply the scales, silently losing the
scaling. `mori_use_mxfp8_dispatch()` therefore asks AITER directly via
`resolve_activation_dtype()`, which is documented for exactly this case ("lets a
caller that produces the activations itself -- an all-to-all dispatch, a fused
epilogue -- emit that dtype directly") and returns `None` rather than guessing
when the answer would have depended on a token count that does not exist yet.
It also fails closed on `ImportError` and on a hidden dim that is not a multiple
of 32.

## Results

8x MI355X (gfx950), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DP8/EP8 with `mori_high_throughput`,
speculative decoding off. 8192 in / 1024 out, 256 prompts at concurrency 64,
against a stock nightly (`0.32.0rc1.dev190+g3f1bcfd82`) with **only this change
applied** — this PR was measured on its own, with no AITER-side patches, so the
numbers are attributable to the dispatch change alone.

Engagement was confirmed rather than assumed: `resolve_activation_dtype(M=None)`
returns `torch.float8_e4m3fn` under the `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0` that vLLM
pins for this model, and the dispatch kernel switches from
`EpDispatchIntraNodeKernel_bf16` to `EpDispatchIntraNodeKernel_fp8_ocp`.

### Performance

| Metric | Baseline | With patch | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 1103.58 | 1309.33 | **+18.6%** |
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 9932.18 | 11783.95 | **+18.6%** |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 54.16 | 46.83 | **-13.5%** |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 54.68 | 46.69 | **-14.6%** |
| Median ITL (ms) | 51.40 | 44.29 | -13.8% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 3392.14 | 2248.40 | -33.7% |
| Benchmark duration (s) | 237.54 | 200.21 | -15.7% |

### Accuracy

gsm8k, 5-shot, all 1319 questions.

| Arm | strict-match | stderr | Delta | flexible-extract |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 0.9196 | 0.0075 | — | 0.9196 |
| With patch | 0.9280 | 0.0071 | +0.0084 | 0.9287 |

Within ~1 sigma of baseline. The same mxfp8 quantization is applied either way;
this only changes which rank performs it and how many times.

### Reproduction

Server:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1
export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1

vllm serve /model/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput \
  --moe-backend aiter \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --language-model-only \
  --no-swa-bounded-replay \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}'
```

Benchmark:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tokenizer /model/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 \
  --random-output-len 1024 \
  --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 256 \
  --max-concurrency 64 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --seed 0 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \
  --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```

Accuracy:

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 \
  --model_args base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,tokenizer_backend=None,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,timeout=3600
```

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] HIP sparse MLA decode kernel for batched decode on gfx942
body:
On gfx942 the Triton split-K sparse MLA decode path for DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 spends most of its time gathering scattered fp8 rows out of the paged cache. At batch the MFMAs mostly wait on those gathers, so the kernel is latency bound rather than compute bound

This adds a gfx942-only HIP kernel that keeps K in registers as the MFMA A operand, pipelines tiles through a small register ring, and brings V through LDS. It is registered as `_rocm_C::sparse_mla_decode_fp8_ds_mla` and covers the per-rank DSv4 / V4.1 decode shape (16 heads x 512 = 448 nope + 64 rope) over fp8_ds_mla caches, including the SWA main cache, optional top-k extra cache, optional attention sink, ragged indices with -1 holes, and a split-K plus reduce

`rocm_sparse_attn_decode` dispatches to it on gfx942 when the op is present, the output is bf16 (no MXFP8 epilogue), the head shape matches, and the step has at least `_HIP_SPARSE_DECODE_MIN_TOKENS` (64) decode tokens. Below that gate the HIP path's fixed cost (split-K plus a separate reduce kernel) is not paid back, and Triton is as fast or faster, so smaller steps stay on the Triton split-K kernel. Like the aiter path it returns 0 so the caller applies the inverse RoPE

NaN elements of gathered rows count as zero, matching what the Triton scrub intends. Device code is compiled only under `__gfx942__`. Other targets build empty kernels and the host op refuses to run off gfx942. CUDA builds never see `csrc/rocm`

Complementary, not overlapping: #60583 turns on AITER sparse MLA on gfx942 for other models and excludes DSv4 / V4.1. #60731 is an opt-in mono decode path for very small steps. This PR is the batched decode path at 64+ tokens on the Triton fallback shapes those leave alone. #61968 retunes the Triton tile on gfx942 for the small steps that stay on that path

## Test plan

- [x] new / extended kernel tests compare the HIP path against the fp32 reference on gfx942 at DSv4 / V4.1 decode shapes (re-run on this tip)
- [x] `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py` on MI300X: same pass/skip/fail set as main on this image, plus the new HIP cases (one pre-existing unrelated failure: `test_v41_rocm_combine_uses_shared_kernel`)
- [x] `_rocm_C` builds clean with vLLM's existing warning flags on this tip
- [x] pre-commit default and `--hook-stage manual` clean on the changed files
- [ ] qualitative end to end on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (decode throughput up at high concurrency, low concurrency unchanged since the path is not taken, accuracy unchanged vs main) - done earlier on an older tip, not re-run after this rebase
- [x] `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_rocm_sparse_mla_decode.py` is in the tree for reproducing the Triton vs HIP crossover

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] gfx942 sparse MLA decode: BLOCK_K=16 with 2-stage pipelining
body:
On gfx942 the split-K sparse MLA decode kernel was running with the 32-row K tile that was tuned for gfx950, and a single-stage loop

That loop is latency bound, not compute bound. Each iteration loads the slot indices for the tile, gathers that many scattered rows (fp8 nope + bf16 rope) and their scales out of the paged cache, dequantizes them, then does two small dots against a few heads. The dots are tiny, so with `num_stages=1` the MFMAs mostly sit idle waiting on the current tile's gather

The fix is to let Triton pipeline the loop. With `num_stages=2` the next tile's index load and row gather are issued while the current tile is still in the dots. Holding two 32-row tiles in flight is a lot of on-chip storage for MI300X (64 KiB LDS per CU, MI355X has 160 KiB), so the tile drops to 16 rows, where two fit comfortably. Smaller tiles also waste less work on the masked tail of each split

`block_k` also feeds `_decode_num_splits`, so the split count on gfx942 can shift a bit for the same batch. That's expected, the heuristic is already written in terms of `block_k`

gfx950 has its own partial kernel and split heuristic, both tuned around 32-row tiles with a lot more LDS, so it's left alone. Archs that are neither gfx942 nor gfx950 take the generic fallback earlier in the function and don't see this either

Numerics: same math, and the online softmax still accumulates in fp32. Only the order the KV rows are reduced in changes (tile size and split boundaries), so outputs differ from before at bf16 rounding level, not bit for bit

No other open PR changes this tile. #57880 is in the same function but only touches the gfx950 split logic, and it is still open, so there is a small conflict risk if both land close together. #61967 sends big decode steps to the HIP kernel, while this Triton path still handles small steps and builds without the HIP op

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py` on MI300X: same pass/skip/fail set as main on this image, all gfx942 split-K decode cases pass (one pre-existing unrelated failure: `test_v41_rocm_combine_uses_shared_kernel`)
- [ ] outputs compared against the old launch config at DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode shapes - done earlier, not re-run after this rebase
- [ ] kernel time at those shapes - done earlier, not re-run after this rebase
- [x] pre-commit default and `--hook-stage manual` clean on the changed files
- [ ] end to end on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash - done earlier (serving within noise, accuracy unchanged), not re-run after this rebase

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Share MegaAttn int32 positions across layers
body:
## Overview

MegaAttn converts the same RoPE positions from int64 to int32 in every layer. In a full CUDA graph those casts are separate GPU kernels: 40 per target forward on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Share the converted tensor within the forward context so the graph records one cast.

## Claims

- Removes 39 redundant cast kernels per 40-layer target forward.
- Target GPU time drops from 17.903 to 17.834 ms (0.39%) in the DEP8 decode measurement below.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8 x GB300 across two nodes, DP8 x TP1 + EP, 64 requests/rank, 131,072 input tokens, 2,048 output tokens, attention top-k 1024, DSpark with 5 draft tokens (384 target tokens/rank). FlashMLA built with CUDA 13.4, MegaMoE, Engram on GPU, full decode CUDA graphs. Both runs restore and freeze the same EPLB mapping.

| Target forward | Before | Shared positions |
|---|---:|---:|
| GPU time, median (ms) | 17.903 | 17.834 |
| GPU time, p10 / p90 (ms) | 17.847 / 17.996 | 17.793 / 17.941 |
| Full-batch samples | 366 | 342 |
| Kernels in the captured forward | 766 | 727 |

One run per version on a development tree, using real weights and synthetic KV through `DecodeBenchConnector`. Times are CUDA events around the target graph, without the profiler, taking the slowest of eight ranks for each step and discarding the first ten full-batch steps. Kernel counts come from a separate CUDA-only trace. This measures GPU target time, not request latency or serving throughput.

The measurements used the equivalent helper implementation; the final diff inlines it. The final `forward_mqa` was checked locally on GB300 with a copy consumer: 40 uses share one converted buffer during full capture, offset views stay distinct, replays see updated positions, independent captures do not reuse another graph's cast, and separate piecewise graphs sharing a context remain correct. NONE, FULL and PIECEWISE cases pass. These local checks are not added to the PR.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_dsv41_mega_attn_layouts.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flash_mla_mega_attn.py
```

Existing layout suite on the development tree: 7 passed. Pre-commit, including Ruff, formatting and mypy: passed. No accuracy evaluation was run; the integer conversion is unchanged. The capture checks above were run outside CI.

## Details

The cache is keyed by the input tensor and scoped to `ForwardContext`. The cast still executes on every graph replay. Eager execution and PIECEWISE capture keep their per-call conversion, since separate piecewise graphs must own their buffers. Check actual stream capture as well as runtime mode: MRV2's full capture can run with mode NONE.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for `mega attention positions`, `positions int32`, `mega_attn_positions_int32`, and `MegaAttention reuse`. #60613 fixes a prefill index sentinel; #60543 autotunes the indexer GEMM. Neither shares the RoPE position conversion. No linked issue.

AI assistance (Codex) was used to implement and validate this change.

title: [Model] Add Reflection Beam
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Day-0 support for Reflection's Beam-1.0 (`BeamForCausalLM`), a 501B-parameter MoE with 23B active parameters, and its DFlash2 drafter (`DFlash2BeamDraftModel`).

**This PR is now a tracking PR and is not meant to be merged.** It was split into the reviewable PRs below; everything on this branch is either in `main` or in an open slice.

## Status

| PR | Scope | Status |
|---|---|---|
| #62042 | Router GEMM kernels for (5120, 256) and BF16 output in `ll_bf16_gemm` | ✅ Merged (2026-10-16) |
| #62052 | `beam` reasoning and tool parsers, `VLLM_BEAM_ALWAYS_CONSTRAIN_OUTPUT` | ✅ Merged (2026-10-16) |
| #62074 | Beam model and DFlash2 drafter (Blackwell kernels, standard TP all-reduce) | ✅ Merged (2026-10-19) |
| #62366 | Fused MNNVL all-reduce with Beam's sandwich norms and MoE finalize | 🔄 In review |
| #62073 | Attention DP + CuTeDSL NVFP4 MegaMoE (needs FlashInfer nightly); stacked on #62366 | 🔄 In review |

**What landed differs from this branch:**

- `BeamConfig` and the model follow the released `config.json` schema (`layer_types`, `mlp_layer_types`, per-type `rope_parameters`). Handling only pre-release checkpoints needed was removed, and switches the release never sets are fixed. Code built on this branch that reads the removed keys (for example `enable_sandwich_norm`, `mlp_only_layers`, `nope_layer_ids`, `moe_router_dtype`) must use the released behavior instead.
- The DFlash2 drafter no longer subclasses the Qwen3 DFlash classes.
- The DFlash `max_position_embeddings` override was dropped: the released drafter already matches the target.

**Remaining work:**

- Serving re-run on `main` (NVFP4 + DFlash2, TP8 GB200) with the released checkpoints. The numbers below were measured on this branch with the full stack, including the fused all-reduce.
- #62366: end-to-end before/after against `main`, and whether `allreduce.cu` (and #62073's `moe_finalize.cu`) stay runtime-JIT through FlashInfer or are built into vLLM.
- #62073: validation with FlashInfer nightly, which the MegaMoE paths and the DP-boundary test require.

## Validation (this branch, full stack)

**Serving:** Beam-1.0 NVFP4 + DFlash2 (7 draft tokens), TP8 on GB200, SPEED-Bench `throughput_1k` low-entropy subset, greedy decoding:

| Concurrency | Fixed draft (tok/s) | Adaptive (tok/s) | Acceptance length |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 708 | 707 | 3.71 → 3.61 |
| 128 | 15,012 | 16,632 | 3.68 → 3.23 |

**Prefill**, 4×GB300, 32K input / 1 output token:

| Configuration | Peak input throughput (tok/s) |
|---|---:|
| Attention DP + MegaMoE | 168.8K |
| TP4 | 98.7K |

**Decode/prefill kernels:** compared with the first implementation, TP8 batch-1 decode went from 8.95 ms to 3.30 ms per step (2.71×), and an 8 × 2K prefill from 328 ms to 176 ms (1.87×). Part of this comes from the fused all-reduce in #62366.

```bash
vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4 -tp 4 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --reasoning-parser beam --tool-call-parser beam --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER"}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN"}'
```

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; the submitter reviewed every changed line.

title: [ROCm][Perf] MXFP4 indexer K cache for GLM-5 / DeepSeek-V3.2 DSA
body:
## Overview

On gfx950 with AITER, `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}'` now also serves DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.x, MTP drafts included: their indexer writes the paged MXFP4 K cache that #58671 added for DeepSeek-V4.1, and the existing ROCm MXFP4 indexer scores it in place. FP8 stays the default. The code applies to main on its own; the gains below are measured on top of #61943, which should land first. Related: #48558, #60834.

## Claims

- GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X, TP4, on top of #61943: KV cache +3.0% tokens; 128K/1K TPOT -5.4% / -5.9% at c8 / c16, MTP3 c8 -6.8%, TTFT -7% to -8%; c1 and 8K/1K within noise; gsm8k and passkey unchanged.
- Against main: 128K/1K TPOT -7.6% / -9.6% / -9.5% at c1 / c8 / c16, MTP3 c8 -6.7%.
- DeepSeek-V3.2, TP4, on top of #61943: KV cache +10.2% tokens; 128K/1K c8 TPOT -12.5%; c1 and 4K/1K c16 within noise; gsm8k unchanged.
- The FP8 default, gfx942, AITER off and non-ROCm platforms are unchanged.

## Validation

- `test_fused_deepseek_v32_norm_rope.py`, `test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py`, `test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py`, MI355X: 274 passed, 8 skipped. pre-commit clean.
- Serving, mean TPOT (ms), 4 runs per arm for GLM-5.2 128K c8 / c16, MTP3 and DeepSeek-V3.2 4K, 2 elsewhere, no failed requests:

| workload | #61943 | + this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.2 128K/1K c1 / c8 / c16 | 13.90 / 43.17 / 76.66 | 13.69 / 40.82 / 72.15 | -1.5% / -5.4% / -5.9% |
| GLM-5.2 MTP3 128K/1K c8 | 33.95 | 31.63 | -6.8% |
| GLM-5.2 8K/1K c8 | 17.50 | 17.49 | within noise |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 128K/1K c1 / c8 | 13.74 / 66.02 | 13.67 / 57.78 | -0.5% / -12.5% |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 4K/1K c16 | 22.85 | 23.34 | +2.1%, one outlier run (below) |

- gsm8k strict: GLM-5.2 20-shot 0.9272 to 0.9325 (stderr 0.007), DeepSeek-V3.2 5-shot 0.9515 to 0.9575 (stderr 0.006). GLM-5.2 passkey 26/26 in both arms.

<details>
<summary>Per-run numbers, kernel data and reproduction</summary>

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (AITER 0.1.25) running #61943 at 0473a1e and this branch cherry-picked onto it (no conflicts), from source, MI355X. GLM-5.2 runs use `--max-model-len 133120`; DeepSeek-V3.2 runs keep the default (163840).

The new kernel tests compare the written K pages byte for byte with a reference built from the layout description, score them with AITER's kernel, and check the MXFP4 query against torch. A transposed scale plane, scales in natural order or a wrong `n_per_tile` each make them fail. MTP3 acceptance length: 3.49 without, 3.45 with this PR.

Mean TPOT per run (ms). Sessions, one server each: #61943 | PR, PR | #61943, then for the 4-run points PR, PR | #61943, #61943. MTP3 and DeepSeek-V3.2 follow the same order.

| workload | #61943 | + this PR |
|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.2 8K/1K c8 | 17.45, 17.55 | 17.58, 17.40 |
| GLM-5.2 128K/1K c1 | 14.14, 13.66 | 13.81, 13.58 |
| GLM-5.2 128K/1K c8 | 43.41, 43.07, 43.05, 43.15 | 41.02, 40.68, 40.84, 40.73 |
| GLM-5.2 128K/1K c16 | 77.92, 76.08, 76.51, 76.12 | 74.48, 71.18, 71.55, 71.38 |
| GLM-5.2 MTP3 128K/1K c8 | 34.80, 33.38, 33.91, 33.69 | 32.33, 31.51, 31.26, 31.42 |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 4K/1K c16 | 22.68, 23.09, 22.86, 22.77 | 23.09, 24.46, 22.89, 22.92 |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 128K/1K c1 | 13.79, 13.70 | 13.69, 13.65 |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 128K/1K c8 | 66.49, 65.55 | 57.96, 57.60 |

- Median ITL (ms): GLM-5.2 128K c1 13.80 to 13.69, c8 17.12 to 16.74, c16 20.24 to 19.54, MTP3 c8 25.44 to 24.34; DeepSeek-V3.2 128K c8 20.78 to 19.38, 4K c16 21.26 to 21.37.
- Mean TTFT (s): GLM-5.2 128K c1 8.20 to 7.84, c8 36.9 to 33.9, c16 68.2 to 63.3, MTP3 c8 38.1 to 35.0; DeepSeek-V3.2 128K c8 62.4 to 53.6. Output throughput at 128K: GLM-5.2 c8 +7.0%, c16 +7.0%, MTP3 c8 +7.8%; DeepSeek-V3.2 c8 +15.2%.
- The DeepSeek-V3.2 4K/1K c16 run at 24.46 ms had tail stalls (p99 ITL 33.7 ms, 22-25 ms in the other seven runs); without it the PR mean is 22.97 (+0.5%).
- KV cache tokens: GLM-5.2 3,206,592 to 3,303,424 (MTP3 2,969,088 to 3,058,112); DeepSeek-V3.2 2,074,240 to 2,286,656. DeepSeek-V3.2 has an indexer on every layer, GLM-5.2 on 21 of them.
- Against main, earlier sessions with the same flags (main | PR, PR | main; MTP3 PR, PR | main, main): 128K/1K TPOT 14.69 / 44.95 / 79.01 to 13.58 / 40.63 / 71.52, MTP3 c8 34.65 to 32.31, TTFT -9%, 8K/1K c1 / c8 / c16 within 1%, gsm8k 20-shot strict 0.9181 to 0.9212. Its PR arm matches the PR arm above within 1.5%.

Decode indexer per step (us), GLM-5.2 indexer (32 heads, k=2048, 64-token pages), scoring and top-k for 21 layers captured in one graph, LLC flushed before each replay, median of 20. FP8 scorer with AITER top-k (#61943) to this PR's MXFP4 path, its per-step schedule included:

| context | 1 row | 8 rows | 16 rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4K | 209 to 210 | 230 to 263 | 257 to 252 |
| 32K | 406 to 413 | 580 to 487 | 745 to 570 |
| 128K | 762 to 704 | 1419 to 972 | 2027 to 1274 |

At 128K and 8 rows the scorer alone drops from 816 to 334 us; top-k is the same AITER kernel on both sides. With 4 rows per sequence (MTP3) the MXFP4 path takes native next_n rows: 128K, 8 sequences 2573 to 1209 us.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0 \
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 133120 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}'
# MTP3: --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# DeepSeek-V3.2: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2, same env and flags without --max-model-len.

# 128K/1K: num-prompts max(C, 3), --seed 43. 8K/1K c8: --random-input-len 8192,
# 24 prompts, --seed 42. DeepSeek-V3.2 4K/1K c16: --random-input-len 4096, 48 prompts, --seed 42.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 \
  --num-prompts $N --max-concurrency $C --seed 43

# --num_fewshot 5 for DeepSeek-V3.2
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 20 --batch_size 1 \
  --model_args model=amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False

VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -v tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v32_norm_rope.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py
```

Passkey: a 5-digit key at a random depth of 32K / 64K / 120K tokens of filler, chat completion with thinking off, 26 prompts.

</details>

## Details

- Write path: AITER's `k_norm_rope_mxfp4_cache` (DeepSeek-V4.1) applies RMSNorm and RoPE on the last dims; the V3.2 and GLM indexer key takes LayerNorm with bias and interleaved RoPE on the first 64 dims. So `fused_norm_rope` and `fused_q` quantize the key and query themselves, with AITER's scale rule and the page order from AITER's `cache_format()`.
- Gain: the scorer reads 68 instead of 132 bytes per key, and prefill scores the paged cache in place instead of gathering K. Both grow with context and batch. Short contexts pay the per-step decode schedule (about 25 us at 8-16 rows); 8K and 4K serving shows no change beyond noise.
- Limits: 64- or 128-token pages (other `--block-size` values fail at startup), no DCP or PCP (rejected at startup), gfx950 with AITER only. The new kernel tests need gfx950 and run in the optional MI355 kernels step.

<details>
<summary>Design notes, related PRs and duplicate search</summary>

- MTP draft layers that reuse the target's top-k skip the query quantization. The model check uses `architectures`, because MTP drafts carry the rewritten `deepseek_mtp` model_type.
- #60834 (open) edits the same check in `dsa_indexer_uses_fp4` to add DeepSeek-V4 by model_type and adds its backend class next to this one; whichever lands second takes the union.
- #48558 (open, needs rebase) adds an MXFP4 indexer cache for GLM-5.2 on CUDA sm_100 through the legacy `deepseek_v2` indexer and the `use_fp4_indexer_cache` flag that #52550 replaced. It does not touch ROCm and reports +3.5% KV with neutral latency on B200.
- #57517 and #56834 add ROCm MXFP4 indexing for DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 only. #60042, #60294 and #60756 change the ROCm FP8 scorer kernels and #59421 adds native FP8 decode above next_n=2; each would narrow the gain if it lands. #53953 edits `deepseek_v32/amd/rocm.py`.
- Duplicate search, `gh pr list --state all --search`: "mxfp4 indexer ROCm", "fp4 indexer cache", "indexer_kv_dtype", "MXFP4 indexer GLM", "mxfp4 indexer DeepSeek-V3.2", "paged mxfp4 indexer", "RocmSparseAttnIndexer", "fused_norm_rope mxfp4", "GLM-5 ROCm indexer", "indexer cache fp4 AMD".

</details>

Not a duplicate: #48558 covers CUDA through a removed flag, and the ROCm MXFP4 indexer PRs (#57517, #56834, #60834) cover DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 only.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the implementation, the measurements and this description.

title: [Model][Spec Decode] Migrate HY V3 to the Flat Model layout
body:
## Overview

Next slice of #61024's "Migrate speculative model code to Flat Model" bullet (RFC #44219). Moves the HY V3 model and its MTP drafter from the legacy `vllm/model_executor/models/` layout into the new `vllm/models/<name>/<hw>/` layout.

## Claims

- Moves `vllm/model_executor/models/hy_v3.py` and `hy_v3_mtp.py` to `vllm/models/hy_v3/common/{model,mtp}.py`, repointing the `HYV3ForCausalLM` and `HYV3MTPModel` registry entries to `vllm.models.hy_v3`.
- No logic change. The only diff inside the moved files is fixing imports that crossed the old package boundary (`.utils`, `.interfaces` → `vllm.model_executor.models.{utils,interfaces}`, and the MTP file's `from .hy_v3 import HYV3DecoderLayer` → `from .model import HYV3DecoderLayer`), verified by diffing old vs. new file content.
- HY V3 needs only a `common/` directory, no `nvidia`/`amd`/`cpu`/`xpu` split: zero custom kernels, and zero platform-conditional code (`grep -c "is_rocm\|is_cuda\|sm90\|sm100"` → 0). HY V4 (`vllm.models.hy_v4`), by contrast, needed a real `nvidia`/`amd` split for `flashmla_sparse`/`triton_ihc` -- V3 predates those optimizations.
- Unlike every other remaining legacy drafter, `hy_v3.py`/`hy_v3_mtp.py` have zero dependency on any other model file -- confirmed by grep across the whole tree, they're the only two files that reference each other. That made this pair the next candidate after Medusa.

## Validation

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -q -k HYV3
# 2 passed

pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py vllm/models/hy_v3/__init__.py vllm/models/hy_v3/common/__init__.py vllm/models/hy_v3/common/model.py vllm/models/hy_v3/common/mtp.py
# all hooks passed (ruff check/format, mypy, SPDX headers, etc.)
```

No e2e acceptance-rate test exists for HY V3 under `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/` (unlike Medusa, which had one) and I don't have a validated local checkpoint-loading path for it on this change, so the above is the available coverage. `tests/models/registry.py` lists `tencent/Hy3-preview` as the example checkpoint if a reviewer wants to validate a real weight load.

## Details

**Why HY V3 and not another drafter:** every remaining legacy drafter (EAGLE/EAGLE3 variants, the other MTP variants, DFlash) imports its base model's decoder-layer class directly from a still-legacy file (`llama`, `qwen2`, `qwen3`, `deepseek_v2`, etc.), so migrating any of them means migrating a shared, heavily-reused base model too -- a much bigger, higher-blast-radius change. HY V3 is the one pair with zero such entanglement.

**Previous attempt:** #61357 targeted Medusa as the first migration in this series, but Medusa was removed from vLLM entirely in #61701 while that PR was in flight ("Medusa is not supported by Model Runner V2, and EAGLE/MTP/DFlash/DSpark cover its use case"). Closed #61357 as superseded by that removal rather than resurrect deleted code.

**Duplicate-work check:** searched open issues/PRs for existing HY V3 Flat Model migration work; found none.

**Scope:** this PR only moves HY V3 + its MTP drafter. The remaining legacy drafters are out of scope here and need their base model migrated alongside them, which is a larger, separate decision per model family.

title: [Spec Decode] Support PCP with DSpark for DeepSeek-V4.1

## Overview
Enable fixed-length DSpark speculative decoding with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Prefill Context Parallelism (PCP) on NVIDIA CUDA, extending the standalone PCP path from #59857. Preserve compressor rollback states and keep replicated draft proposals consistent across PCP ranks.


## Claims
- Retain and publish compressor ring tails across PCP ranks so rejected speculative suffixes can resume at an earlier position without losing the predecessor needed by ratio-2 compression.
- Broadcast draft tokens and, for probabilistic drafting, their corresponding logits from PCP rank 0 before target verification. The shared DFlash path also synchronizes confidence values when adaptive verification is enabled; V4.1 PCP still rejects adaptive verification.
- Cover PCP2/4, 0/5/9 speculative tokens, ring capacities 8/16, partial rejection, odd/even accepted prefixes, empty local ranks, and decode-owner changes through the existing compressor regression.


## Validation
