title: [Perf][Attention] Candidate-only FP8 indexer decode scoring on SM90
body:
> **Status: draft.** Opened early to get direction feedback before investing in
> the long-term version. The optimization itself works and is measured; the
> path-selection policy is deliberately provisional and will be reworked (see
> [Roadmap](#roadmap)). Comments on the approach are more useful than comments
> on the gating details, which are expected to change.

## Overview

On SM90 the DSv4.1 candidate-consuming indexers have no paged sparse scoring
kernel, so they score the entire compressed context per decode row and then
mask down to the candidate blocks. This adds an opt-in path that gathers the
candidate K from the paged FP8 indexer cache and scores only the candidates.
Implements the alternative-A direction of #61830.

Not a duplicate: #57858 and #57859 implement candidate-only scoring for ROCm
(gfx950); this is the SM90/CUDA counterpart called for in #61830.

## Claims

Claiming only what is measured at this stage:

- At ~1M context, 9 concurrent requests on 8x H20 (TP8): the four
  candidate-consuming indexer layers drop from **9.57 ms to 3.05 ms** per step,
  and per-step time from **39.04 ms to 31.53 ms** (profiler-derived).
- Selected top-k sets are equivalent to the existing dense score-then-mask
  path.
- Default behaviour is unchanged: the feature is off by default, and
  unsupported shapes or platforms fall back to dense rather than failing.
- Known cost: a single-request step is about **11.6% slower** than dense, since
  the candidate path carries a per-step fixed cost. The provisional workload
  gates exist to avoid that region until a better policy lands.

## Validation

Setup: 8x H20, TP8, DSv4.1, `num_speculative_tokens=5`, ~1M token context.
With `1 + 5 = 6` tokens per request the SM90 paged kernel takes the flatten
path, so one active request contributes roughly 6 decode rows.

**Kernel / unit**

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_candidate_gather_cudagraph.py
pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py
```

- `test_candidate_gather_cudagraph.py` (new): gather + scoring + remap under
  CUDA graph capture and replay.
- `test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py` (extended): dense vs. candidate-only
  equivalence of the selected top-k set.

**Equivalence**

With `VLLM_DSA_CANDIDATE_GATHER_FORCE=1`, the selected top-k index set matches
the dense path on identical inputs. Note that #61830's alternative-A hoped for
bit-identical results; this verifies set equivalence instead, since the
gather-then-score path uses a different scoring kernel and top-k tie-breaking
can differ (documented in the module docstring).

**Server-level**

Real `vllm serve` at ~1M context, torch profiler traces collected with the
feature off and on:

| Configuration | Per step | Four consumer indexer layers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dense (feature off) | 39.04 ms | 9.57 ms |
| Candidate-only (feature on) | 31.53 ms | 3.05 ms |

at 9 concurrent requests (~54 decode rows).

To reproduce, enable on an SM90 FP8-cache deployment:

```bash
export VLLM_DSA_CANDIDATE_GATHER_DECODE=1
export VLLM_DSA_CANDIDATE_GATHER_MIN_ROWS=16
```

**Validation still in progress** — explicit about what the numbers above do
*not* yet cover, and queued in this order:

1. A profiler-free end-to-end throughput/latency A/B (current timings are
   profiler-derived).
2. Model-level accuracy evaluation plus an independent numerical reference
   (correctness evidence so far is top-k set equivalence against vLLM's own
   dense path).
3. Cross-hardware validation on SM90 parts other than H20 — the reason no
   crossover constant is hardcoded.

I will keep appending results to this PR as they come in.

## Details

**Why the dense path is wasteful here.** The candidate-consuming indexers are
handed a small, fixed-width candidate set, but SM90 lacks a paged sparse
scoring kernel, so they score the whole context and discard everything outside
the candidate blocks. The discarded work grows linearly with context length
(~98% of the scoring work at 1M context, per #61830).

**What the new path does.**

1. Gather each candidate block's K from the paged FP8 indexer cache into a
   compact per-row buffer.
2. Score only the gathered candidates with the existing non-paged FP8 scoring
   kernel.
3. Remap the selected columns back to request-local token positions, so the
   output is identical in meaning to the dense path.

**Scope kept narrow on purpose.** Only the candidate-consuming indexers take
the new path; the candidate-source and pre-candidate indexers stay dense, as
they have no candidate set to exploit. Restricted to SM90 with an FP8 indexer
cache and no context parallelism — SM100 already has native sparse kernels,
and all other platforms keep today's behaviour.

**Tradeoff, and why the current gating is provisional.** Dense cost scales
with `rows x context`, while candidate scoring is dominated by a per-step
fixed cost, so the crossover tracks scanned work relative to the candidate
width rather than context length alone. Since the profitable threshold is
hardware-dependent, this PR does not bake in a device-specific constant and
instead exposes host-side gates (details collapsed below), treating them as a
**stopgap, not the intended final interface**. Defaults impose only
shape-level lower bounds, and the H20 values above are reported as
measurements, not recommended defaults.

**Known structural limitation.** Path selection is host-side per step and is
*not* graph-aware: a fully-captured CUDA graph fixes whichever path was active
at capture time. `FORCE` exists to make that behaviour testable. This is the
main reason the feature ships disabled by default.

<details>
<summary>Workload gates (provisional)</summary>

| Env var | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VLLM_DSA_CANDIDATE_GATHER_DECODE` | `0` | Master switch. |
| `VLLM_DSA_CANDIDATE_GATHER_MIN_ROWS` | `1` | Minimum decode rows in the step (speculative rows included). |
| `VLLM_DSA_CANDIDATE_GATHER_MIN_WORK_RATIO` | `1` | Requires `rows * context >= ratio * candidate_width`. |
| `VLLM_DSA_CANDIDATE_GATHER_FORCE` | `0` | Validation only: bypass the workload gates. |

</details>

## Roadmap

This PR is a reviewable first increment, not the finished design:

1. **Graph-aware path selection**, so the choice is not frozen by full CUDA
   graph capture. This is the blocker for enabling the feature by default.
2. **Replace the manual env gates** with an automatic, device-independent
   decision (calibration or a cost model), with proper small-batch protection
   instead of a hand-set row threshold.
3. **Longer term**, a native paged sparse scoring kernel for SM90 is the
   cleaner fix than gather-then-score — a much larger change. This PR first
   establishes whether the candidate-only direction is worth it, which the
   numbers above suggest it is.

Happy to run specific concurrency levels, context lengths, or accuracy
benchmarks on request.

Step `nvidia-b200-v1-attention-shard-1-slash-6`, Buildkite build #95342 (PR #60896, a CMake change, so the full suite runs). One case fails out of about 590 MLA cases in the shard:

```
FAILED v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py::test_backend_correctness[glm-MLAPrefillBackendEnum.TRTLLM_RAGGED-1.0-1.0-fp8-4-deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-mixed_small]
Failed: 2 backend(s) failed: AttentionBackendEnum.CUTLASS_MLA, AttentionBackendEnum.TOKENSPEED_MLA
[AttentionBackendEnum.CUTLASS_MLA] output differs from SDPA baseline. Max diff: 0.154297, max rel diff: 18560.000000)
[AttentionBackendEnum.TOKENSPEED_MLA] output differs from SDPA baseline. Max diff: 0.154297, max rel diff: 18560.000000)
1 failed, 739 passed, 173 skipped, 3511 deselected
```

- The retry of the same job gives exactly the same numbers (0.154297 / 18560 for both backends): https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95342#01a143d7-43bf-4174-8442-63dcdb8503cd (first run: #01a14367-92c3-42b8-b93a-3115f6c296bc).
- The two backends fail with an identical error, so the cause is probably in a path they share rather than in one decode kernel.
- In the same job, these related cases pass: the `deepseek` dimension variants with the same prefill backend, KV dtype and batch (for example `deepseek-...TRTLLM_RAGGED-1.0-1.0-fp8-8-...-mixed_small`), the `glm` + `FLASH_ATTN` prefill cases with the `auto` KV dtype, and the other decode backends in the failing case (the failure lists only these two).
- The PR of this build (#60896) changes only the `CUDA < 13.0` branch of `CMakeLists.txt`; the CI image is CUDA 13.0 (torch `+cu130`), so that code is not compiled here.

### 📝 History of failing test

- The failing build is on `main` at `fa75d3456` (#59857, merged 2026-10-16 06:17 UTC).
- I have no earlier result for this exact case: the shards hold different cases in different builds (for example, the green B200 shard 1/6 of #61938, on `main` at `dd9e07a25`, 01:29 UTC, did not contain it).
- `main` commits between `dd9e07a25` and `fa75d3456`: #58872, #60356, #61867, #61895, #61736, #61574, #61611, **#61689** (`tokenspeed-mla` 2.0.2 → 2.0.3, 05:29 UTC), #61932, #59857. Of these, only #61689 touches the dense MLA backends (through TOKENSPEED_MLA); I checked the diffs of #61689, #59857, #61867 and #58872, and the other six by title only. But `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/cutlass_mla.py` does not import `tokenspeed_mla`, so #61689 alone would not explain the CUTLASS_MLA half. #59857 changes only DeepSeek-V4.1 sparse MLA; #61867 is Kimi-specific. The cause may also be older than this window.
- Not checked: Buildkite Test Suites history for this test id (I could not read it), and a bisect on SM100.

title: [CI][ROCm][Disagg] Add DeepSeek-V3 NIXL accuracy steps
body:
## Purpose

Add DeepSeek-V3 disaggregated prefill/decode accuracy steps that use NIXL over UCX RDMA on MI350, next to the existing MoRIIO steps. Read uses `NixlConnector`. Write uses `NixlPushConnector` for 1P1D TP8, 1P1D EP8, and 2P2D EP16.

The 2P2D EP16 write step needs https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62055. That change keeps push heartbeats and outgoing WRITE polling on the writer thread, so a blocked NIXL call cannot miss an expert-parallel collective.

## Changes

- `pipeline-disagg.yaml`: six DeepSeek-V3 steps. Read (`NixlConnector`): 1P1D TP8, 1P1D EP8/DP8, 2P2D EP16/DP16. Write (`NixlPushConnector`): 1P1D TP8, 1P1D EP8/DP8, and 2P2D EP16/DP16.
- `run-slurm-disagg-test.sh`, `run_xPyD_disagg.slurm`: add `KV_CONNECTOR` (default `MoRIIOConnector`) and pass it to the containers. For NIXL, start vllm-router with `--kv-connector nixl` and fixed `--prefill`/`--decode` URLs, because NIXL has no discovery service.
- `vllm_disagg.sh`: when `KV_CONNECTOR` is `NixlConnector` or `NixlPushConnector`, use that name in the NIXL KV transfer config (UCX backend). On 2P2D EP16 prefill, set `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.75`. At 0.85 the AITER MoE sort buffer runs out of memory. EP8 stays at 0.85.
- `cluster.sh`: for either NIXL connector, set UCX defaults for the ionic RoCE NICs (RC verbs on `ionic_0`, GPU-direct RDMA) and run accuracy with one concurrent request. The router flag stays `--kv-connector nixl` for both.

MoRIIO steps do not change. All new settings apply only when `KV_CONNECTOR` is `NixlConnector` or `NixlPushConnector`.

Requirement: the image's UCX must support `rc_verbs` on ionic NICs that report `max_srq=0`. The results below used UCX 1.22 with that support. The 2P2D EP16 write result also used the writer-thread ownership from #62055.

## Test plan

UCX environment (the same on every node):

```bash
export UCX_TLS=rc_verbs,ud_verbs,tcp,self,rocm
export UCX_NET_DEVICES=ionic_0:1,lo
export UCX_IB_GID_INDEX=1
export UCX_UD_VERBS_ETH_DGID_CHECK=n
export UCX_IB_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA=yes
export UCX_RMA_PPLN_ENABLE=y
export UCX_PROTO_EMULATION_ENABLE=n
export UCX_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL=inf
export UCX_UD_VERBS_RX_QUEUE_LEN=1024
export UCX_RCACHE_MAX_UNRELEASED=1024
```

KV config (`kv_role` is `kv_producer` on prefill and `kv_consumer` on decode):

```bash
KV='{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"recompute","kv_connector_extra_config":{"backends":["UCX"],"kv_lease_duration":180}}'
```

Write uses the same commands with `"kv_connector":"NixlPushConnector"`.

TP8, prefill (port 8100) and decode (port 8200, `kv_consumer`):

```bash
vllm serve DeepSeek-V3 --host $PREFILL_IP --port 8100 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --kv-transfer-config "$KV"
```

EP8/DP8, prefill:

```bash
vllm serve DeepSeek-V3 --port 20005 -tp 1 --data-parallel-size 8 --data-parallel-size-local 8 \
  --data-parallel-address $PREFILL_IP --data-parallel-rpc-port 13345 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput --enforce-eager \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --api-server-count 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --kv-transfer-config "$KV"
```

EP8/DP8, decode: the same command with `--data-parallel-address $DECODE_IP`, `--all2all-backend mori_low_latency`, no `--enforce-eager`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.75`, and `kv_consumer`.

2P2D EP16/DP16 uses the same EP command with `--data-parallel-size 16` on four nodes. Prefill uses `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.75`. The second prefill node and the second decode node join headless with `--data-parallel-start-rank 8`. The router points only at the two masters. Write uses `NixlPushConnector` and the #62055 writer.

Router (`--intra-node-data-parallel-size 1` for TP8, `8` for EP8 and EP16):

```bash
vllm-router --vllm-pd-disaggregation --kv-connector nixl \
  --prefill http://$PREFILL_IP:8100 --decode http://$DECODE_IP:8200 \
  --worker-startup-timeout-secs 1800 --port 30000 --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --intra-node-data-parallel-size 1 --policy round_robin \
  --prefill-policy round_robin --decode-policy round_robin
```

For 2P2D EP16 the router uses `--worker-startup-timeout-secs 7200` and `--intra-node-data-parallel-size 8`.

Accuracy:

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k \
  --model_args model=DeepSeek-V3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=1,tokenized_requests=False,trust_remote_code=True
```

Script checks: `bash -n` on all changed scripts, YAML parse, NIXL KV config parses as JSON, router arguments checked for 1P1D TP8, 1P1D EP8 and 2P2D EP16, `git diff --check`.

## Results

GSM8K (5-shot) exact_match. KV moved GPU memory to GPU memory over `rc_verbs/ionic_0`.

| Config | Connector | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1P1D TP8 | NixlConnector | 0.92 | 0.92 |
| 1P1D EP8/DP8 | NixlConnector | 0.94 | 0.94 |
| 2P2D EP16/DP16 | NixlConnector | 0.964 | 0.964 |
| 1P1D TP8 | NixlPushConnector | 0.98 | 0.98 |
| 1P1D EP8/DP8 | NixlPushConnector | 0.94 | 0.94 |
| 2P2D EP16/DP16 | NixlPushConnector | 0.96 | 0.96 |

The 2P2D EP16 write row used the writer-thread ownership from #62055.

title: [Perf][EPLB][DSv4] Add a symm_mem weight-migration backend and fuse MegaMoE replica mapping
body:
## Overview

This PR makes EPLB cheaper for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, running DP attention with EP MegaMoE on multi-node NVLink. It does three things:

- adds an opt-in `symm_mem` weight-migration backend;
- fuses EPLB's logical→physical replica mapping and expert-load recording into the DeepGEMM MegaMoE staging kernels;
- takes async EPLB's host work off the decode critical path.

Not a duplicate. No open or merged PR adds a symmetric-memory EPLB backend or fuses the MegaMoE mapping. #61176 and #61839 enable EPLB for the ROCm AITER MegaMoE backend. Related: #61767 (`cpu_all_reduce_`, reused here), #57549, #56716, #61643.

## Claims

- EPLB raises decode throughput on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB200 NVL72 by +3.7% at DEP32 with 72 req/rank and +7.7% at DEP32 with 128 req/rank. At DEP16 the step is about 3% shorter, but the throughput gain is within run-to-run noise.
- `symm_mem`: senders push expert rows into the receiver's `expert_buffer`, which is allocated in CUDA symmetric memory. There is no staging buffer, and it needs no memory beyond `expert_buffer`. Cross-node peer copies run at about 800 GB/s, against about 88 GB/s for NIXL, and a 40-layer rearrangement transfers in 0.3–0.6 s at DEP32.
- MegaMoE layers no longer launch a separate EPLB mapping kernel, which saves 5–6 µs per layer. The replica choice is shared with the router through one Triton helper, so physical ids and load counts match `eplb_map_to_physical_and_record` exactly.
- Async EPLB no longer adds a GPU→host sync to the decode loop. It also raises on every rank when the worker fails on any rank, instead of stalling.

## Validation

Hardware: GB200 NVL72, 4 GPUs per node.

Serving setup: DSpark with 5 draft tokens, MRV2, FULL CUDA graphs, async scheduling.

EPLB setup: `{"num_redundant_experts": <DP>, "window_size": 1000, "step_interval": 3000, "use_async": true, "communicator": "symm_mem"}`, i.e. one redundant expert per rank.

Workload: decode only, coding-agent prompts with mean ISL ≈ 85k (prefix-cached), 16k output tokens with `ignore_eos`, and requests pinned evenly to DP ranks. Throughput is the output rate over the window in which every request is decoding.

Off and on arms ran interleaved (ABAB) on the same nodes. These runs used a branch of nightly fe4df3df (2026-10-12) with this change set and #61767, before the rebase and without the second commit.

| Config | EPLB off (tok/s) | EPLB on (tok/s) | Δ | Welch t |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DEP16, 72 req/rank | 223.6k ± 2.0k (n=4) | 228.1k ± 4.2k (n=4) | +2.0% | 2.0 (not resolved) |
| DEP32, 72 req/rank | 419.5k ± 1.3k (n=4) | 435.1k ± 5.8k (n=4) | +3.7% | 5.3 |
| DEP32, 128 req/rank | 500.7k ± 5.1k (n=3) | 539.4k ± 9.7k (n=3) | +7.7% | 6.1 |

- DEP16 step time, p50 of 2000-step windows at full batch, same build: 24.34 / 24.28 ms off vs 23.61 / 23.25 ms on.
- At DEP32 with 128 req/rank, one pass per arm is excluded. A host stall unrelated to EPLB cut that pass by 13–34%.

Per-step breakdown, DEP32 with 128 req/rank:

| | EPLB off | EPLB on |
|---|---|---|
| Step time (CUDA events, unprofiled) | 38.8 ms | 36.5 ms |
| GPU idle at the step boundary | 0.27 ms | 0.27 ms |
| Main-model MegaMoE (5 s CUDA profile) | 18.1 ms | 13.4 ms |
| All other kernels (same profile) | 21.5 ms | 21.2 ms |

The GPU never waits on the host, so the MegaMoE saving turns into step time. MegaMoE is about 40% of the step, which caps the end-to-end gain.

Microbenchmarks (GB200):

- **Fused EPLB staging**, one MoE layer, hidden 5120, top-k 6, 384 logical experts. Each arm is timed as a CUDA graph replay, median of 200. Outputs, ids and load counts match main bit for bit in every case.

  | Format | Tokens | Physical experts | main: `torch.where` + map kernel + staging | Fused | Saved |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | MXFP8 | 432 | 400 | 9.4 µs | 4.2 µs | 5.1 µs |
  | MXFP8 | 768 | 416 | 11.0 µs | 4.7 µs | 6.3 µs |
  | NVFP4 | 432 | 400 | 49.5 µs | 44.0 µs | 5.5 µs |
  | NVFP4 | 768 | 416 | 49.1 µs | 43.8 µs | 5.3 µs |

  That is about 0.2 ms per decode step across 40 MoE layers.
- **Weight-migration bandwidth**, 2 nodes, one MegaMoE layer of 25 experts (470 MB):

  | Path | Bandwidth |
  |---|---|
  | `symm_mem` peer copies, intra- or cross-node over multi-node NVLink | ~808 GB/s (bulk), ~294 GB/s (100 per-tensor copies) |
  | NIXL, cross-node | ~88 GB/s (UCX picks RoCE, not multi-node NVLink) |
  | NIXL, cross-node, `UCX_TLS=cuda_copy,cuda_ipc,tcp` | ~0.12 GB/s (TCP) |

- **MegaMoE kernel time under serving load**, DEP16 with 72 req/rank, layers 2–40: p50 per call drops 12.6–14.0% across three profiled runs (222→194 µs). Layer 1 is excluded because it absorbs cross-rank arrival skew.

Tests on this branch, one GB200 node with 4 GPUs. They ran before the rebase onto 64175d3827; the 5 newer commits on main touch none of these files.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py` (incl. `test_prepare_megamoe_eplb_matches_router_under_graph_replay`) | 110 passed |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py -k eplb` | 18 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py` | 35 passed, 14 skipped (NIXL not installed, XPU) |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py -k nixl`, NIXL installed | 7 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_utils.py`, `test_eplb_migration_scheduler.py` | 6 passed, 28 passed |
| `tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py`, `test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py` | 13 passed, 7 passed |

GSM8K on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (one node):
- Setup: 5-shot, 1319 questions, temperature 0, `num_redundant_experts=16`, `window_size=100`, `step_interval=300`. Every arm rearranged all 40 layers four times during the eval.
- Command: `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-shots 5 --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64`

| Arm | Accuracy (2 passes) | 40-layer rearrangement |
|---|---|---|
| EPLB off | 0.898, 0.901 | — |
| `symm_mem` | 0.897, 0.895 | 2.9–3.3 s |
| `symm_mem`, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | 0.889, 0.883 | 2.9–3.3 s, no sync error |
| `nixl` | 0.892, 0.886 | 2.7–3.2 s |

The EPLB-off and `nixl` arms ran on the commit before the final cleanup, which does not touch either path. Within one node, `symm_mem` and NIXL (CUDA IPC) move weights at a similar rate; `symm_mem`'s advantage is across nodes over multi-node NVLink.

## Details

**`symm_mem` backend**
- The receive buffer is one symmetric `uint8` buffer per EP group, set up with a single rendezvous and carved into per-tensor views. The backend checks the NVLink/MNNVL domain before allocating.
- Senders and receivers derive each receive row from the global placement with the same helper, so `add_recv` is a no-op. Push backends get every rank's rows through a new `recv_rows` argument to `set_transfer_context`. This argument is optional and other backends ignore it.
- Each `execute()` runs two CPU barriers. GPU spin barriers can deadlock against MegaMoE's cooperative launches.
- Rejected with elastic EP. The buffer lives outside the caching allocator, so sleep mode does not free it.

**Fused mapping**: `fused_moe/eplb_triton.py` holds the replica hash, map lookup and gated load count. The MXFP8/BF16 and NVFP4 staging kernels call it, and so does the router kernel. Routed-experts capture still sees logical ids.

**Async EPLB**
- Per-layer maps are committed with pinned non-blocking copies, and the worker thread fences `expert_buffer` reuse.
- Balancedness stats are read back non-blocking and logged in order once they land.
- `should_record_tensor` is rewritten only when its value flips.
- The per-step "all ranks ready" check runs over `cpu_all_reduce_`. A gloo ring all-reduce costs several ms per step at DP16/DP32.

**Also**
- `logical_to_physical_map` is sized to R+1 slots unless elastic EP is on.
- `compute_logical_maps` is vectorized.
- DeepSeek V4.1 decoder-replay padding and dummy rows are marked as padding, which complements #61643.

**CI**: the `symm_mem` execution tests need NVLink peers. They are added to the optional 8×H100 "Distributed DP + EP" job; the 4×L4 EPLB job skips them. The MegaMoE parity test needs SM100.

**Limitations**
- In mixed prefill/decode serving, per-rank prefill imbalance bounds the step. There, EPLB mostly lowers tail TTFT rather than raising throughput.
- Likely rebase overlap with #61786, #59168 and #41141. Offline placements without elastic EP (#41141) could exceed R+1 replicas.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Enable DeepGEMM sparse MQA logits on the FP8 indexer cache
body:
## Purpose

`attention_config.indexer_sparse_logits` (#56254) lets DeepSeek-V4.1's candidate-consuming indexer layers score only the candidate blocks with DeepGEMM's sparse MQA-logits kernels instead of dense logits over the whole context. Today it requires the MXFP4 indexer cache (`indexer_kv_dtype="mxfp4"`), so with the default FP8 cache the flag fails at startup:

```
ValueError: attention_config.indexer_sparse_logits requires the MXFP4 indexer cache
```

The restriction dates from before #61149: the FP8 cache then stored one fp32 scale per token, while the sparse kernels take UE8M0-packed (granularity-32) scales. Since #61149, the SM100 FP8 indexer cache stores each token's power-of-two scale as four equal UE8M0 bytes, which is exactly the MXFP8 layout DeepGEMM expects, and DeepGEMM's sparse kernels already have an FP8 (`float_e4m3_t`, `SM100_MMA_MXF8F6F4_SS`) variant for both the contiguous (prefill) and paged (decode) paths. Its paged accessor reads the same page layout as vLLM's FP8 cache (`PAGE_KV x 128` value bytes, then `PAGE_KV` uint32 scales).

This PR wires the FP8 cache into the existing sparse path, so the decode speedup no longer requires trading the K cache down to 4 bits.

## Results

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4, 4x B300, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --no-enable-prefix-caching`, greedy decoding. Decode and prefill throughput from a linear fit of wall time against output length (256 / 1024 / 2048 output tokens), each point run twice

| batch x context | decode tok/s MAIN | decode tok/s PR | decode speedup | prefill tok/s MAIN | prefill tok/s PR | prefill speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 x 8K | 6,459 | 6,584 | 1.02x | 124,569 | 126,088 | 1.01x |
| 32 x 100K | 3,920 | 4,117 | 1.05x | 117,066 | 117,774 | 1.01x |
| 16 x 256K | 2,293 | 2,535 | 1.11x | 103,739 | 104,733 | 1.01x |
| 8 x 512K | 1,301 | 1,399 | 1.08x | 85,609 | 87,355 | 1.02x |
| 4 x 1M | 692 | 745 | 1.08x | 62,604 | 63,967 | 1.02x |

Decode improves at every point, with up to 11% higher decode throughput. Prefill is at parity: decoder SWA bounded replay (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58132) runs the candidate-consuming layers on only each request's last 128 tokens during prefill, so little prefill indexer work is left for the sparse path to remove.

<details>
<summary>Serving matrix (request stream, 1024 output tokens, 4 x concurrency prompts)</summary>

Median TPOT is lower with the flag on in 29/29 points (1.01-1.10x, median 1.03x) and output throughput is higher in 28/29 (median 1.02x); prefill-only TTFT at concurrency 1 is at parity (0.99-1.04x) from 4K to 1M. No short-context regression: 4K and 16K are 1.01-1.06x on TPOT.

| ISL | conc | TPOT p50 off / on (ms) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4K | 1 / 64 | 4.15 / 4.07, 13.27 / 12.68 | 1.02x, 1.05x |
| 64K | 1 / 16 | 4.23 / 4.14, 10.92 / 10.40 | 1.02x, 1.05x |

| 512K | 1 / 16 | 4.35 / 4.08, 55.51 / 50.43 | 1.07x, 1.10x |
| 1M | 1 / 8 | 4.37 / 4.12, 59.44 / 57.47 | 1.06x, 1.03x |

</details>

title: [Model][Kernel] Nemotron-H Lightning NVFP4: batch-invariant serving aligned with training
body:
## Purpose

Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, make every Nemotron-H Lightning NVFP4 layer
(Mamba2, FP8 attention, NVFP4 W4A16 MoE, NVFP4/FP8 linears, norms, router)
independent of batch composition, chunking and the prefill/decode split, using
kernels a training actor can call directly. The actor's forward then reproduces
rollout log-probs bit for bit. This is the vLLM side of the Nemotron-H
train/inference consistency work described in the vLLM blog post
(`2026-10-14-train-inference-consistency`); the form follows the DeepSeek-V4
preview #54955.

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` unset, the only behavior changes are the new
CuTe-DSL W4A16 experts path (W4A16 checkpoints on the `flashinfer_cutedsl`
MoE backend) and the ModelOpt W4A16 layerwise-reload fix. No new CUDA
extension: every BI path is an existing vLLM/FlashInfer kernel pinned to a
fixed configuration.

This is a squashed rebase onto main `fa75d3456d` of the code used for the
final Nemotron-H RL runs (developed on `6e517b15c1`, head `7a0244d0dc` in
aoshen02/vllm#85). 50 files, +5666/−182. The second commit is a review
follow-up (SM10x check at config time).

## What it adds

| Area | Change | Main files |
|---|---|---|
| Mamba2 BI exact replay | Port of #55905 (stacked on #57539, #55627, #55895): bitwise prefill = chunked prefill = decode; decode replays the partial chunk from the FP32 boundary state through the same SSD path; pinned SSD tiles; row-gated decode in full CUDA graphs; `chunk_size` plumbing in four Mamba2 models | `layers/mamba/*`, `v1/attention/backends/mamba2_attn.py`, `v1/worker/mamba_utils.py`, `models/{mamba2,falcon_h1,granitemoehybrid,zamba2}.py` |
| ModelOpt W4A16 NVFP4 layerwise reload | W4A16 layers do not wait for `input_scale` during layerwise reload and ignore a deprecated copy arriving after processing | `quantization/{modelopt,base_config}.py`, `fused_moe/routed_experts.py` |
| FlashInfer CuTe-DSL W4A16 MoE | New experts class + NVFP4 oracle branch. Each output element is one CTA's FP32 accumulation over the full K (no split-K); top-k combine is an FP32 sum in slot order; under BI one pinned tactic for every token count. Gated to the Nemotron-H geometry | `fused_moe/experts/flashinfer_cutedsl_w4a16_moe.py`, `fused_moe/oracle/nvfp4.py` |
| BI GEMM dispatch | Router: BF16 x BF16 -> FP32 logits with one persistent matmul under BI (on top of #59985, which turns the specialized router tiers off); FP8 `bmm` pinned to `cutlass`; W4A16 linears use Humming; Blackwell BI-matmul table entries | `router/gate_linear.py`, `determinism/*`, `utils/flashinfer.py`, `kernels/linear/*` |
| Fixed split-KV FA4 | `FlashAttnFixedSplitBackend`: one split count independent of batch; rejects unsupported configs at construction | `v1/attention/backends/flash_attn_fixed_split.py` |
| Nemotron-H wiring | Under BI: select the components above, `CudaRMSNorm` and the grouped gated norm, standalone `+quant_fp8`, no norm/act+quant fusion; TP=1 and SM10x checks at config time; MTP loads only `mtp.*` weights and shares the target embedding/LM head | `models/{nemotron_h,nemotron_h_mtp,config}.py`, `layers/layernorm.py` |

### Decisions made in the rebase

- Dropped our cherry-pick of #57635 (now on main).
- GateLinear: kept #59985's behavior; Nemotron-H keeps its BF16 gate weight
  under BI (`force_fp32_compute` only when BI is off), as the trainer does.
- Mamba2: exact replay writes no internal prefill checkpoints (#57329), so
  `MambaMixer2` requests no checkpoint blocks under BI; `update_block_table`
  handles both the checkpoint metadata and the exact-replay decode buffer.
- NemotronHMTP uses `is_unused_checkpoint_weight` (#60152).
- Fixed split-KV FA4: dropped the cascade check (#61126 removed cascade).
- `utils/flashinfer.py`: kept the pinned `bmm_fp8` backend; the `*_mm_out`
  helpers were removed on main (#60517).

## Why this is not a duplicate

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "Nemotron-H batch invariant"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "nemotron batch invariant"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "mamba2 batch invariant"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "cutedsl w4a16"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "fixed split flash attention"
```

- The Mamba2 BI stack (#55627, #55895, #55905, #57539, by @NolenLiang, on our
  team) is the Mamba2 part of this PR. It is included here so the full
  Nemotron-H path can be reviewed and tested as one unit; we will reconcile with
  whichever lands first. #56244 (gate inside the scan) is a different approach
  and is not used.
- #57123 (fp32 eps in the BI RMSNorm Triton kernels), #60047 (`aten::mm`
  `out_dtype` overloads) and #60681 (GateLinear custom op) touch nearby code
  but not the paths changed here.
- No open PR covers CuTe-DSL W4A16 MoE under BI, fixed split-KV FA4, the
  ModelOpt W4A16 reload fix or Nemotron-H BI.

## Test plan and results

GB200, bare-metal uv venv with the precompiled wheel for
`fa75d3456d` (torch 2.14.0+cu132, Triton 3.8.0, flashinfer 0.7.2,
cutlass-dsl 4.8.0), tree run from source.

| Test | BI | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_ssd_emit.py` | unset / 1 | 23 / 23 passed |
| `tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_ssd_batch_invariance.py` | 1 | 7 passed |
| `tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_exact_replay.py` | 1 | 3 passed |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_mamba2_batch_invariant.py` | 1 | 12 passed |
| `tests/v1/determinism/test_mamba2_batch_invariance.py` | 1 | 4 passed |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_cutedsl_nvfp4_moe.py` | unset | 36 passed |
| `tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py` | unset | 63 passed, 2 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/test_ll_bf16_gemm.py` | unset | 136 passed |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_flash_attn_fixed_split.py` | 1 | 9 passed |
| `tests/model_executor/test_nemotron_h_quantization.py` (head) | unset / 1 | 22 / 22 passed |
| `tests/v1/determinism/test_nemotron_h_batch_invariance.py` | 1 | 7 passed |
| `tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py` | unset | 95 passed, 3 skipped (checkpoints unavailable offline) |
| main's `test_mamba2_checkpoint_state` / `test_mamba2_prefill_checkpoints` / `test_gpu_draft_lm_head` | unset | 8 / 6 / 8 passed |

`test_nvfp4_batch_invariant.py` fails only because its model is not in the
offline HF cache; this PR does not touch it.

### Full model (Nemotron-H Lightning NVFP4)

16 prompts of 7 to 12000 tokens, 48 greedy tokens; each comparison checks token
ids and FP32 logprob bits.

| Comparison | Requests that differ (of 16) |
|---|---|
| BI=1: alone vs batch vs reversed batch | 0 |
| BI=1: decode vs `prompt_logprobs` re-feed (`max_num_batched_tokens` 16384 and 2048) | 0 |
| BI=1: `max_num_batched_tokens` 2048 vs 16384 | 0 |
| Negative control, BI unset: alone vs batch | 16 (7 with token flips) |
| This PR vs the pre-rebase head `7a0244d0dc` (the code of the RL runs), Triton/flashinfer/cutlass-dsl pinned to that image's versions | 0 (all 547 module outputs equal) |

With main's default library versions, this PR differs from `7a0244d0dc` in the
last bit of Mamba's `rms_norm_gated` (same source and inputs; Triton 3.8.0 vs
3.7.1 rounds 2 of 1,048,576 elements differently). A trainer that calls these
kernels must use the same torch/Triton/flashinfer/cutlass-dsl versions as
serving.

### End to end (on `7a0244d0dc`)

Megatron actor vs rollout on Nemotron-H Lightning NVFP4, GB200 DP4/EP4:
`actor/ppo_kl` = 0 at every step of the 100-step SWE-bench Pro run.

### Not tested on this head

TP>1 (rejected by the config check), MTP/spec decode and prefix caching under
BI.

## Known limitations

- BI is validated only for this model on SM10x (B200/GB200/B300), TP=1.
  BI=1 Nemotron-H raises at config time on other GPUs or TP>1.
- Under BI, Nemotron-H always selects `FlashAttnFixedSplitBackend`, which
  raises at construction unless vllm-flash-attn has fixed split-KV scheduling,
  head size is 128, the KV cache is FP8 E4M3 and there is no sliding window.
- Under BI, W4A16 NVFP4 linears are forced to `HummingNvFp4LinearKernel`
  without a fallback; validated on SM100 only.
- BI relies on torch.compile with Inductor: the trainer compiles the same
  pointwise glue (MoE combine, norms), so `enforce_eager` breaks bitwise
  equality.

## AI assistance

Implemented, tested and described with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human
submitter reviews every changed line and is responsible for the change.

title: [Tracking] DeepEP v2 maturation and legacy DeepEP v1 removal
body:
Track the correctness, performance, compatibility, and migration work needed to retire vLLM’s legacy DeepEP v1 backends (`deepep_high_throughput` and `deepep_low_latency`) in favor of `deepep_v2`.

**DeepEP v2 hardening**

- [ ] Resolve GIN barrier data-race: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59844)
- [ ] Stabilize the `do_expand` and `do_cpu_sync` parameters across eager execution, warmup, and CUDA graphs. Currently these bools are equivalent and tied to the CUDA graph mode but this does not need to be the case.
    - [ ] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59337 keeps `do_expand=False` and `do_cpu_sync=False` across prefill and decode and eager and may improve things in the short term
     - [ ] https://github.com/tlrmchlsmth/vllm/pull/37 extends this to handle `do_expand` and `do_cpu_sync` correctly.
     - [ ] Add a num tokens threshold to `do_cpu_sync` to reduce memory footprint on the high end (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51589)

**Skip padded computation**

- [ ] Land FP4 DeepGEMM padding avoidance: [[#59044](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59044)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59044).
- [x] Land block-FP8 DeepGEMM padding avoidance: [[#59128](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59128)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59128).

**Elastic buffers and receive-count outliers**

Track CPU overflow as a way to handle receive-count outliers without reserving worst-case GPU memory.

[[DeepEP v2.5](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/pull/763)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/pull/763), merged September 29, includes allocator and CPU-backed storage support, with experimental Engram functionality. The remaining work is to establish which communication path consumes that storage and integrate it into ordinary EP dispatch/combine.

Important: DeepEP v2.5 removes support for the legacy NVSHMEM-based all2alls.

- [ ] Define the intended EP receive-buffer behavior: GPU capacity for common receive counts, CPU overflow for outliers, and explicit capacity limits.
- [ ] Integrate mixed CPU/GPU backing into the required dispatch/combine path; existing Engram support alone does not establish EP support.
- [ ] Validate registration, transport compatibility, downstream expert consumption, graph replay, overflow correctness, GPU-memory savings, and tail latency.
- [ ] Decide whether initialization-time segment placement is sufficient. Address-preserving migration of existing regions should be a separate requirement if needed.

Related: [[NCCL EP’s experimental elastic receive buffers](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl-extensions/blob/main/nccl_ep/docs/release/RELEASE_NOTES_v0.2.md#elastic-gpu--cpu-receive-buffers)](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl-extensions/blob/main/nccl_ep/docs/release/RELEASE_NOTES_v0.2.md#elastic-gpu--cpu-receive-buffers).

**Legacy v1 retirement**

Upstream [[DeepEP v2.5](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/pull/763)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/pull/763) already removes v1 and NVSHMEM and replaces `ElasticBuffer` with dedicated buffer APIs.

- [ ] Plan vLLM’s `ElasticBuffer` → `EPBuffer` migration and validate the required CUDA, NCCL, PyTorch, and build/runtime dependencies.
- [ ] Document the supported replacement matrix, including hardware, topology, expert backends, quantization, CUDA graphs, DBO, and EPLB where applicable.
- [ ] Establish correctness, model-evaluation, serving-performance, and memory baselines against the legacy paths.
- [ ] Agree on deprecation and removal milestones, document migration, and remove legacy configuration, implementations, build dependencies, tests, and documentation.

title: [Attention] Add an FA4 backend with a fixed split-KV schedule
body:
## Overview

Adds `FlashAttnFixedSplitBackend`: FA4 (CuTe) attention with a fixed split-KV schedule, so a token's attention output is bitwise independent of the batch. This is for batch-invariant inference that a training-side replay can reproduce with the same kernel and schedule.

This is one self-contained part of #62017 by @aoshen02, split out unchanged for separate review. The commit keeps his authorship. An earlier revision was reviewed as aoshen02/vllm#93.

## Claims

- Bitwise-identical rows: a sequence's attention rows are the same whether it runs alone or batched with other sequences, and in prefill or decode. Decode includes a verify row of 2 or 3 query tokens.
- Unsupported layers are rejected when the impl is constructed, with a reason, instead of exceeding the schedule at runtime.
- No existing path changes. The backend is not registered as a selectable backend; a model opts in with `Attention(..., attn_backend=FlashAttnFixedSplitBackend)`. The Nemotron-H batch-invariant wiring in #62017 does this.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flash_attn_fixed_split.py
```

- `test_fixed_schedule_rejects_what_it_cannot_serve`: unsupported head size, KV-cache dtype, sliding window, `max_model_len`, compute capability, sinks, DCP and attention type each get a reason.
- `test_fixed_schedule_rows_ignore_batch_and_phase` (SM10x, FP8 and BF16 KV cache): rows are bitwise equal alone, batched, and as decode after prefill.

| Where | Code | Result |
|---|---|---|
| GB200, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, run by @aoshen02 on #62017's head | the same files at `fa75d3456d` | 9 passed |
| B300 (SM103) | earlier revision aoshen02/vllm#93 (`2d588c3b5b`) | 5 passed; the SM10x rows test ran. The upstream wheel's FA4 already has `seqlen_k_per_split` and `disable_scheduler_metadata`. |
| H100 (SM90) | same earlier revision | 4 passed, 1 skipped (the SM10x rows test) |
| B300 (SM103), `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | `cd0253120` (before the interface follow-up below) | 9 passed (7 rejection cases, and the rows test with FP8 and BF16 KV caches) |
| GH200 (SM90), this branch | `26df85070` | 12 passed, 2 skipped (the rows test needs SM10x; not rerun after the follow-up, since `forward` is unchanged) |

Interface follow-up `26df85070`, checked before vs after on 46,080 impl constructions. The grid covered compute capability, head size, KV-cache dtype, sliding window, `max_model_len`, sinks, attention type, DCP, ALiBi, soft cap, KV sharing and model dtype. Accept/reject decisions are identical, except that fp32 models are now rejected by the inherited dtype check; FA4 serves fp16/bf16 only.

`pre-commit` mypy (Python 3.11) and ruff pass on the changed files.

## Details

Schedule:
- `SEQLEN_K_PER_SPLIT=8192` keys per split, `NUM_SPLITS=32`;
- `max_seqlen_q` and `max_seqlen_k` fixed at 262144;
- scheduler metadata disabled;
- `tile_mn=(128, 128)`, `pack_gqa=True`.

Each split therefore covers the same keys for any batch composition, sequence length or phase.

Limits are declared through the standard `AttentionBackend` classmethods: `supports_head_size`, `supported_kv_cache_dtypes`, `supports_compute_capability`, `supports_attn_type`, `supports_sliding_window`, `supports_rswa`, `supports_non_causal`, `supports_sink`, `supports_mm_prefix` and `supports_per_head_quant_scales`. The vllm-flash-attn feature probe is in `supports_combination`. Because a model passes this backend explicitly instead of going through the selector, `fixed_split_unsupported_reason` calls `validate_configuration` itself (as `hy_v4` does for its explicitly chosen backend) and adds the schedule's `max_model_len` bound. The impl then adds ALiBi, soft cap and KV sharing. Anything outside the scope raises `ValueError` at construction, listing every reason with the layer's values:
- an SM10x GPU;
- a vllm-flash-attn build whose `_flash_attn_fwd` has `seqlen_k_per_split` and `disable_scheduler_metadata`;
- head size 128;
- FP8 E4M3 or BF16 KV cache;
- no sliding window;
- `max_model_len <= 262144`;
- plain causal decoder attention: no ALiBi, soft cap, sinks, KV sharing or DCP;
- fp16 or bf16 model dtype.

At runtime, `forward` also rejects fused output quantization and non-causal metadata.

`FlashAttentionImpl.__init__` is deliberately not called. It picks a vllm-flash-attn version and rejects FP8 KV caches, while this impl calls the CuTe FA4 kernel directly, so only the attributes other code reads are set.

Compared with aoshen02/vllm#93:
- the schedule now covers `max_model_len` up to 262144;
- a BF16 KV cache is accepted;
- the cascade-attention check is gone, because #61126 removed cascade attention.

It is meant for batch-invariant serving only and is not registered for general backend selection.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Keep a full uniform-decode batch reachable by FULL graphs
body:
## Overview

A full `max_num_seqs` uniform-decode batch can end up with no FULL CUDA graph when the manager's query length does not divide the capture sizes. The DSpark draft (`sample_from_anchor`) decodes `num_speculative_tokens` tokens per request, but the default sizes follow the target's `1 + num_speculative_tokens` (#50488). With `max_num_seqs=72` and 5 draft tokens:

- 352 rounds up to 355, which is 71 requests;
- 368 rounds up to 370, which is 74 requests, so it is skipped;
- every full-batch step therefore runs the draft eagerly.

This PR clamps the rounded size to `max_num_seqs * query_len` for managers with a single query length.

Not a duplicate:
- No open or merged PR changes this skip. The new test fails on main, on main + #56136 and on main + #61882.
- #61882 refactors the same loop. It is a textual conflict only, with no behavior overlap.
- #56136 changes the candidate ladders in the same function. It is orthogonal and applies cleanly together with this PR.
- #50488, #53407 and #57355 fixed other "batch has no graph" cases: the target's sizes, padding up, and q=1 respectively.

## Claims

- On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with DSpark and `max_num_seqs=72`, a full batch's draft now runs from its FULL graph instead of eagerly. Decode throughput rises +4.4% at DEP4 on main.
- Dynamic speculative decoding (several query lengths) is unchanged. Clamping there would add graphs for tiers that never reach a full batch, and those graphs would shadow other tiers' FULL graphs.
- Each affected manager gains at most one FULL graph, plus its LoRA and DBO variants. The graph is added only when the full batch was unreachable.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd_cug.py` on GB200: 30 passed. On main, 29 passed and the new test fails.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one GB200 node:
  - Config: DEP4, default MoE backend (`FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`), DSpark with 5 tokens, `max_num_seqs=72`.
  - Load: 288 requests, 72 pinned to each DP rank. Each has a ~1k-token prompt and 14k output tokens (`ignore_eos`, temperature 0).
  - Throughput is measured over 30 s while all 288 requests are decoding. Main and this PR ran interleaved, two rounds each.

  | | main | this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | Decode throughput, rounds 1 / 2 (tok/s) | 62,752 / 60,899 | 64,586 / 64,528 |
  | Draft acceptance rate | 0.988 / 0.988 | 0.987 / 0.987 |
  | DSpark FULL graphs captured | 40 | 41 |
  | Draft kernels in a 4 s CUDA profile | eager (graph id 0) | in their own graph |

  - Throughput is +4.4%, and every PR round is above every main round.
  - The profile also shows decode steps at 40.6 ms on main vs 26.8 ms with this PR. The profiler inflates the cost of each eager launch, so treat that ratio as qualitative only.

- Host time per decode step, on a downstream branch with the same `CudaGraphManager` code: DEP16, 72 requests per rank, steady state, 2000-step windows.

  | | main logic | this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | Full-batch draft dispatches that ran eager | ~80% | 0% |
  | `propose` (host) | 9.7 ms | 0.4 ms |
  | `sample_tokens` (host) | 11.0 ms | 1.6 ms |
  | Host slack per step | 7.5 ms | 17.4 ms |
  | Step time | 24.2 ms | 24.2 ms |

  At DEP16 the step is GPU-bound, so its step time does not change; the freed host time only shows up where the host is on the critical path, as at DEP4 above.

## Details

- The clamp leaves the existing `max_decode_tokens` and `max_num_reqs` checks in place. Those checks still drop oversize sizes for dynamic speculative decoding.
- #61869 copies the old rounding rule into `AttnMetadataCudaGraphs.capture_keys` for the target's query length. That copy may want the same treatment once both PRs land.

title: [CI][Test] Seed each MLA backend correctness case (fix B200 V1 Attention shard 1/6)
body:
## Overview

Seed the random inputs of each MLA backend correctness case, so that a case gives the same result in every CI shard. Fixes #62002 (B200 V1 Attention shard 1/6 fails on `main` since 16 Oct).

## Claims

- `test_backend_correctness` and `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness` no longer depend on which tests ran before them in the same pytest process.
- Expected: the failing case `test_backend_correctness[glm-MLAPrefillBackendEnum.TRTLLM_RAGGED-1.0-1.0-fp8-4-deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-mixed_small]` (CUTLASS_MLA and TOKENSPEED_MLA, max diff 0.154297 against `atol=0.15`) gets the inputs it has when it runs first in a process. It passed that way on GB300 ([#62002 comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62002#issuecomment-6219889830)). The B200 V1 Attention step of this PR's CI checks it on SM100.

## Validation

- The fix is test-only. Lint, format and test collection pass (`pytest --collect-only tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py`: 349 tests). I have no SM100 GPU; the B200 V1 Attention shards of this PR's CI run every case of the file.
- Root-cause evidence, from the CI logs (details in [#62002](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62002#issuecomment-6220068776)):
  - 126 B200 V1 Attention logs of `main` and PR builds from 8 to 16 Oct run this case. Grouped by the exact ordered list of tests that ran before it in the same process, there are 40 orders, and every order is all-PASSED or all-FAILED. All 16 failing logs (builds 95318–95411) share one order (549 tests before the case); the order before it (614 tests, builds 95282–95298) passed 9 of 9.
  - No code change explains the boundary: the only `main` commits between the last passing base (`dd9e07a25f`, #95296) and the first failing one (`642c18d64c`, #95323, a ROCm-only PR) are #58872 (DeepSeek-V4.1, SM90 only), #60356 (XPU Dockerfile) and #61867 (Kimi K3 model files). The failing `main` build #95334 reuses the dependency layer that #95296 built.

## Details

- Root cause: `_run_backend_correctness` creates its queries, KV and weights with `torch.randn` and never seeds; the file seeds only once at import (`torch.manual_seed(42)`), and `tests/conftest.py` has no per-test seed fixture. The runtime-shard plugin splits `test_mla_backends.py` by test ("812 of 2379 tests, split by test"), so each layout change gives the cases different inputs. In the current layout the failing case lands on an input where one element of the CUTLASS_MLA and TOKENSPEED_MLA output is 0.154297 from a reference of about 0, just over the fp8 `atol` of 0.15.
- The seed is 42, the module's existing seed, applied with `vllm.utils.torch_utils.set_random_seed` at the start of the shared helper, so both correctness tests are covered.
- Limitation: this makes the result stable, but it does not show whether these two backends have an accuracy edge for GLM dims with an fp8 KV cache on some inputs, or whether `atol=0.15` is only tight. Running the case with a few seeds on B200 would answer that; I cannot run SM100.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek V4.1 tool parser drops malformed DSML blocks and emits invalid/empty args on truncation
body:
### Your current environment

vLLM `0.31.0+g2107750` (a fork). `vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py` and `vllm/parser/deepseek_v41.py` are byte-identical to upstream `main` as of 2026-10-16. Served with `--tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The `deepseek_v41` tool parser round-trips well-formed DSML correctly, including URLs with `%`, `&`, `#`, `<>"`, IPv6 and IDN hosts, parallel calls and calls with no arguments. Malformed or truncated output is mishandled, though. The table shows what `DeepSeekV41ParserToolAdapter` returns; results are the same in streaming (fed token by token) and non-streaming unless noted.

| Model output (after `</think>`) | Result | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `Hi\n\n<｜DSML｜ calls>\n<url>https://x.com</url>\n</｜DSML｜ calls>` (block with no valid `invoke`) | content `"Hi\n\n"`, no tool calls. The rest is **silently dropped** and the request finishes with `stop` | fall back to returning the text as content |
| `…<｜DSML｜ invoke name="WebFetch">\n<｜DSML｜ parameter name="url" string="true">https://x.com/a?b=` (truncated by `max_tokens`) | non-stream: call `WebFetch` with args `{}`. Stream: args `{"url": "` (**invalid JSON**) | no call, or a call flagged incomplete, plus `finish_reason=length`; never invalid JSON in `arguments` |
| `…<｜DSML｜ invoke name="WebF` (truncated inside the name) | call to non-existent tool `WebF` with `{}` | no call |
| `<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>…` (V4 spelling) | calls parsed, but `<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>\n` also leaks into content | not leaked |
| `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>…` (unspaced V4 spelling) | not parsed at all. `deepseek_v41_config` replaces `TOOL_START` with a single string and drops V4's `DSML_TOOL_START_VARIANTS` | probably accepted as a variant |

The truncation case isn't DeepSeek-specific. Live GLM-5.3 requests through `glm47`, with `max_tokens` cut mid-call, behave the same way: streaming emits `{"url": "https://example` and non-streaming returns `{}`. With GLM-5.3 the non-streaming response even reports `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` instead of `length`, so a client may execute the empty call.

Related: `adjust_request` sets `skip_special_tokens=False`, so any other special token the model samples is returned in content. We saw `<｜place▁holder▁no▁572｜>` in a reply.

#### Repro

```python
from vllm.tokenizers import get_tokenizer
from vllm.parser.engine.registered_adapters import DeepSeekV41ParserToolAdapter
from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest

tok = get_tokenizer("deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash", tokenizer_mode="deepseek_v41")
tools = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "WebFetch",
          "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"url": {"type": "string"}}}}}]
req = ChatCompletionRequest(model="m", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "x"}], tools=tools)
D = "｜DSML｜"
for text in [
    f"Hi\n\n<{D} calls>\n<url>https://x.com</url>\n</{D} calls>",
    f'\n\n<{D} calls>\n<{D} invoke name="WebFetch">\n<{D} parameter name="url" string="true">https://x.com/a?b=',
    f'\n\n<{D} calls>\n<{D} invoke name="WebF',
]:
    p = DeepSeekV41ParserToolAdapter(tok, None, chat_template_kwargs={"thinking": False})
    r = p.extract_tool_calls(text, req)
    print(repr(r.content), [(t.function.name, t.function.arguments) for t in r.tool_calls])
```

To see the streaming behaviour, feed the same strings through `extract_tool_calls_streaming` one token at a time and then call `finish_streaming()`.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [KV Offload] Check /dev/shm for every local DP engine; explain EFAULT
body:
## Overview

With data parallelism, CPU KV offload sizes that fit `/dev/shm` one engine at a time but not all together make the engines fail after loading the model with `OSError: [Errno 14] Bad address`. Nothing in that error mentions `/dev/shm`. This PR refuses such sizes before any engine starts and turns the EFAULT into an error that names `/dev/shm`.

## Claims

- `--data-parallel-size 8 --kv-offloading-size 32` against a 251.9 GiB `/dev/shm` now stops before any engine starts, with: *"Insufficient space in /dev/shm for CPU KV offload buffers of 8 data-parallel engines (32.0 GiB each, set by --kv-offloading-size): 262144 MiB required, 257895 MiB free. Increase /dev/shm (e.g. --shm-size or --ipc=host)."* Before this change, all 8 engines loaded the model, then 6 of them failed with "Bad address" and the server exited after 90 s.
- If a full `/dev/shm` is still hit while pre-faulting (other processes using it, or launch modes the check cannot see), the error says so: *"Ran out of /dev/shm while pre-faulting the CPU KV offload shared region (… GiB; /dev/shm has … GiB free of … GiB)…"*, chained from the original `OSError`.
- No new refusals where `/dev/shm` is not used: the CPU spec on ROCm and CPU keeps a private tensor per rank and is not checked (on XPU it maps the shared region, so it is checked). Config-only construction is not checked either; `VllmConfig` is untouched.

## Validation

- Unit tests, `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py`, `tests/v1/kv_offload/test_shm_check.py` and `tests/v1/engine/test_startup_watch_processes.py`: 98 pass. The 12 new cases include one that drives the real `CoreEngineProcManager` with 8 engines and asserts that it refuses before spawning anything, and EFAULT cases for the per-worker and sharded pre-fault that check the message, the chained `OSError`, that peers waiting at the barrier are released and that the file is removed. On `main`, the EFAULT cases and the launch test fail, and the scope cases cannot import the new module. `test_startup_watch_processes.py` builds `CoreEngineProcManager` from a stub config, which now needs `kv_transfer_config=None`.
- `tests/v1/kv_offload`, `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector` and `test_hisparse_connector.py`: 1396 passed, 2 skipped. `tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py -k shm_free_space`: 4 passed.
- The offload config tests (`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_config.py`, `test_hma_auto_config.py`, `tests/test_config.py`) pass with a 64 MiB `/dev/shm` (Docker's default), mounted as a private tmpfs with `unshare -m`: 25 passed, as on `main`.
- vLLM's pre-commit hooks pass on every changed file: ruff check and format, typos, mypy through `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py` (Python 3.10 to 3.13), SPDX, lazy and forbidden imports, `check_torch_cuda`, test tethering.
- All of the above on the nightly wheel of this PR's base commit with the patched files applied (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14).
- End to end on 8× RTX 4090, Qwen3-8B, `--data-parallel-size 8 --kv-offloading-backend native`, `/dev/shm` 251.9 GiB:

  | | `--kv-offloading-size` | result |
  |---|---|---|
  | `main` | 32 | all 8 engines load the model, then 6 fail with `Bad address` and the server exits (90 s) |
  | this PR | 32 | refused before any engine starts, 7 s after the API server's first log line; 0 `Bad address`, no model loaded |
  | this PR | 24 | healthy, all 8 engines serving (169 s); no false refusal |

- A GPU-free reproduction of the race: 4 processes each create a 1.5 GiB `SharedOffloadRegion` in a private 4 GiB tmpfs. On `main`, all 4 fail with "Bad address", in 3 of 3 runs; with this PR all 4 report a `/dev/shm` error instead, in 3 of 3 (in each run, three hit the new pre-fault message and the last to start was already stopped by the existing per-region check).

## Details

**Root cause.** Each region's creator checks `shutil.disk_usage("/dev/shm").free` against its own size and then calls `ftruncate`. On tmpfs, `ftruncate` creates a sparse file and reserves nothing, so N engines starting together all see the full tmpfs free and all pass. Pages are only claimed when `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE` faults them in. On a full tmpfs, shmem returns `VM_FAULT_SIGBUS`, which `madvise` reports as `EFAULT`.

**Why the check is called from `CoreEngineProcManager`.** The check is `check_local_engines_offload_shm` in a new `vllm/v1/kv_offload/shm_check.py`; `CoreEngineProcManager` calls it once, before starting any engine. It reads the offload config and calls the existing `check_shm_free_space` with the engines' combined size, so `shared_offload_region.py` keeps only the `EFAULT` handling. The launcher is the one place that knows how many engines will share this host's `/dev/shm`. Inside an engine, a dense model's DP rank runs as an independent engine (`reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank`) with `data_parallel_size_local = 1`. A first version checked in `VllmConfig`, which had two problems. It refused configs on machines that never allocate anything, which broke the config tests above wherever `/dev/shm` is small. It also refused ROCm setups, where the CPU spec never uses `/dev/shm`. The launcher covers internal LB (MoE and dense), multi-node `--nnodes`, `--headless` with `--data-parallel-size-local`, and hybrid LB with `--data-parallel-start-rank`.

**Which specs are checked.** The check asks the spec class (`_uses_shared_region`, now a classmethod): true for `CPUOffloadingSpec` on CUDA and XPU and for `TieringOffloadingSpec` everywhere. A custom spec that does not subclass these is skipped. With `spec_module_path`, the front-end therefore imports that module once. An out-of-tree subclass that overrides the (private) `_uses_shared_region` as an instance method would now fail at launch with a `TypeError`.

**Free space, like every other `/dev/shm` allocation.** At launch the engines have allocated nothing, so the free space is what they will share. The check is `check_shm_free_space` itself, so it uses the same error, and the cgroup headroom log, as a single engine's own check. Something else holding `/dev/shm` at that moment therefore causes a refusal, exactly as it already does for one engine. Anything that fills `/dev/shm` after the check is left to the per-region check and, failing that, to the clearer `EFAULT` message.

**Rejected: reserving with `posix_fallocate`.** It would make the check and the claim atomic, but on tmpfs it allocates the pages under the caller's memory policy. Measured: a file fallocated from NUMA node 3 and then populated from node 5 had 512 of 512 sampled pages on node 3. Every TP rank's slots would land on the creator's node instead of each rank's own.

**Related.** Recent changes to the same region: #59546 splits it across several `/dev/shm` files, #59545 and #60869 spread the pre-fault across workers (`populate_shard`), and #59544 pins only each worker's own slots. None changes how much `/dev/shm` the region needs, when that is checked, or what a full tmpfs reports; the `EFAULT` translation here covers every pre-fault path (per worker, whole region, sharded). Open: #59547 gives each rank its own region and file, and its review notes the same under-detection when several ranks create regions at once; the launcher's per-engine total stays correct under that design. #53073 reworks ownership and cleanup in the same constructor and #61680 adds segments to the HiSparse pool at the call this PR edits, so whichever lands second rebases. #59430 (closed unmerged) had parallelised the pre-fault with a thread pool.

**Limitations.**
- Launch modes where each process starts one engine are not covered by the check, only by the error message: external LB (`--data-parallel-rank`), `--data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb` (its children run with a local size of 1), offline DP with one `LLM` per rank, and independent single-engine servers sharing a host. The Ray backend (`CoreEngineActorManager`) is not checked either.
- Only an `OffloadingConnector` configured directly is checked: one nested in a `MultiConnector` (e.g. with a PD connector) and HiSparse's shared host pool are not added to the sum, though both get the clearer `EFAULT` message.
- After an `EFAULT` in a region without a barrier (the tiering scheduler's), the partly faulted file stays in `/dev/shm`, as it does today, so lowering the size may not be enough until it is removed (#51730, #54619 address cleanup).
- On kernels older than 5.14, there is no `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE`, and the per-page fallback hits a SIGBUS that cannot be translated.
- Under a memory-cgroup limit, the failure is `ENOMEM` or the OOM killer, not `EFAULT`.

**AI assistance.** Claude Opus 5.5 assisted with the code, tests, benchmarks and this description; the tests and benchmarks above were run on my hardware. I reviewed every changed line and the results, and can answer for it; the commit carries an `Assisted-by:` trailer.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Keep data_parallel_index in DFlash/DSpark draft configs
body:
## Purpose

With dense (independent) data parallelism, every DFlash/DSpark drafter on a node shares one torch.compile cache directory, so a cached restart loads artifacts compiled on another replica's GPU and crashes (`CUDA driver error: invalid argument` in the draft's compiled graph).

The draft parallel config is built with `replace(parallel_config, ...)`, which re-derives the `init=False` field `data_parallel_index` from `data_parallel_rank` (0 on independent DP ranks). Fix: copy the target's `data_parallel_index` into the DFlash and DSpark draft parallel configs. (Keeping the field across `replace` in `ParallelConfig` itself would be a broader alternative.)

## Test Plan

`pytest tests/v1/worker/test_dspark_utils.py`. E2E on H200: `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B --data-parallel-size 2` with `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dspark`, cold then cached start: main writes only `rank_0_0/dspark_head` and the cached start crashes; with this change both replicas get their own draft cache dir and both starts serve.

AI assistance (Claude) was used; all changes were reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Fix PLE layerwise reload with CPU offload and TP
body:
## Purpose

Layerwise weight reload of Qwen4Exp with a CPU-offloaded PLE table (`engram_config.cpu_offload`) materializes the replacement table on the GPU, because reload restores every layer on the default device. It also buffers every PLE checkpoint shard until the layer completes, including shards outside the local TP vocab range. At full size this OOMs (+23.8 GiB/rank at TP4).

Fix: skip non-local PLE shards before calling the weight loader, and restore the pinned-host PLE table on the CPU.

## Test Plan

Two new tests in `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py`. TP4 on H200 with the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next PLE config (1 GiB table per rank, shards arriving on the GPU): peak extra CUDA memory during reload went from 2.0/3.0/4.0/5.0 GiB (ranks 0-3) to 1.0 GiB on every rank; values, pinned storage and pointer are preserved.

AI assistance (Claude) was used; all changes were reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Beam] Enable CuTeDSL NVFP4 MegaMoE
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Run Reflection Beam with attention DP + expert parallelism on FlashInfer CuTeDSL MegaMoE (`--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`). **Stacked on #62366** (Beam's fused all-reduce, base branch `woosuk/beam-fused-allreduce`), which builds on the merged #62074. The diff shows only this PR's commit.

**Depends on FlashInfer nightly** for `forward_unfinalized`, `do_finalize` and `create_workspace`. These are detected at runtime, and the new paths stay off with older FlashInfer.

## Claims

- **Prefill throughput:** attention DP4 + MegaMoE reaches 1.71× TP4's peak prefill throughput for Beam.
- **MegaMoE deferred finalize:** `defer_moe_finalize(allow_ep=True)` now also covers MegaMoE under DP/EP. MegaMoE returns `UnfinalizedMoEOutput` through `forward_unfinalized`. Beam finalizes the local rows in a new kernel (`moe_finalize.cu`) fused with the post-MoE norms and residual.
- **Decode workspace:** MegaMoE keeps a second, decode-sized workspace: `max_num_seqs × (1 + num_speculative_tokens)` tokens per sequence-parallel rank. It is used when every DP rank's batch fits, since peer buffer offsets depend on the capacity.
- **Idle ranks:** passthrough-all2all experts now run on ranks with zero tokens instead of returning early, because these experts own the EP collective that every rank must join.

## Validation

**Prefill**, 4×GB300, 32K input / 1 output token, FlashInfer nightly:

| Configuration | Peak input throughput (tok/s) |
|---|---:|
| Attention DP + MegaMoE | 168.8K |
| TP4 | 98.7K |

**Unit tests** on this branch (rebased onto #62366), GB200 with FlashInfer 0.7.2, which has none of the nightly APIs:

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_beam_construction.py tests/models/test_beam_numerics.py \
  tests/models/test_beam_weight_mapping.py tests/transformers_utils/test_beam_config.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py tests/kernels/moe/test_trtllm_nvfp4_moe.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py \
  "tests/test_config.py::test_dflash_candidate_draft_forces_v2_model_runner"
# 382 passed, 4 skipped, 8 failed
```

- **Failures:** the 8 are `test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py::test_init_warmup_forward_is_exact_on_grid_inputs`, which fail identically on `main` in this environment.
- **Skipped:** the DP-boundary MegaMoE test, which checks bit-exact output for unequal and empty batches with CUDA graph replay, needs FlashInfer nightly. The MegaMoE runtime paths still need CI or a nightly-FlashInfer machine.

## Details

- **Effect on existing MegaMoE users (e.g. DeepSeek-V4 with `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`):**
  - With FlashInfer nightly, they also get the decode workspace. This adds one more workspace allocation and its warmup.
  - Idle ranks now run the experts and join the collective.
  - Deferral stays off unless a model asks for it.
- **Rebase onto the released Beam schema:** Beam now hardcodes its post-feedforward norm and depth-scaled residuals, so the MegaMoE boundary always receives a post-norm weight and scales. `beam_norm_residual_norm` regains an optional post-norm only for the fused finalize, which applies the post-norm itself.
- **Not a duplicate:** no open PR adds EP deferral or MegaMoE workspace selection.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Load excluded EAGLE3 NVFP4 embeddings as BF16
body:
## Overview

Related to #62028. Serving `nvidia/Gemma-4-31B-IT-NVFP4` with `AEON-7/gemma-4-31B-it-speculator.eagle3-NVFP4` crashed while copying a BF16 `lm_head` row of width 5376 into a packed NVFP4 parameter of width 2688.

## Claims

- Speculators extraction copies the outer `quantization_config` onto the draft config and leaves the caller's `transformer_layer_config` unchanged.
- Flat ModelOpt configs honor `exclude_modules`, and fall back to compressed-tensors `ignore` only when `exclude_modules` is absent. Excluded `embed_tokens` and `lm_head` stay unquantized. `kv_cache_quant_algo` is normalized to uppercase.
- Draft loaders pin `quant_config` after `VllmConfig` construction. `replace()` reruns `__post_init__`, which would otherwise refill a missing quant config from the target model.
- When a draft has both `d2t` and a bool `t2d`, load fails unless every draft id lands on a distinct `t2d` target. Extra `t2d` marks warn. A non-bool `t2d`, or a missing tensor, skips the check.

## Validation

Unit tests on CPU (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu` for the ModelOpt cases). 18 passed:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py::test_flat_modelopt_nvfp4_config_honors_exclude_modules \
  tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py::test_flat_modelopt_ignore_is_exclude_modules_fallback \
  tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py::test_flat_modelopt_exclude_modules_takes_precedence_over_ignore \
  tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py::test_flat_modelopt_nvfp4_reads_kv_cache_quant_algo \
  tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py::test_flat_modelopt_kv_cache_scheme_still_maps_to_fp8 \
  tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py::test_modelopt_nvfp4_leaves_excluded_parallel_lm_head_unquantized \
  tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_dspark_config.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_eagle_vocab_map.py -q
```

SM120 results are from @waynehacking8 on main `153a17166e` plus the load fix, and were not re-run here:

- The 2688 vs 5376 mismatch is gone, and greedy target completions match.
- The published draft accepts about 7% (mean length 1.29 at 4 speculative tokens). Its `d2t` is a BF16 round trip of `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-speculator.eagle3`: 30,732 of 32,000 draft ids are wrong, while `t2d` is intact. Restoring only `d2t` raises acceptance to 62% (mean length 3.50, against 3.58 for the BF16 source).
- Single-stream chat throughput is 93.7 tok/s against 40.9 without a draft, at the same chat GSM8K (0.984).

The vocab-map check then refuses that published NVFP4 checkpoint until `d2t` is restored. There is no env-var override.

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/Gemma-4-31B-IT-NVFP4 \
  --quantization modelopt \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"AEON-7/gemma-4-31B-it-speculator.eagle3-NVFP4","num_speculative_tokens":4,"draft_tensor_parallel_size":1}'
```

## Details

The crash is the excluded `lm_head`. ModelOpt NVFP4 applies a packed linear method to `LinearBase` and `ParallelLMHead`. `VocabParallelEmbedding` does not get that method. The draft stores ModelOpt metadata on the outer speculators `config.json`, with `exclude_modules: ["lm_head", "embed_tokens"]`. `embed_tokens.weight` is BF16 `[262144, 5376]` and `lm_head.weight` is BF16 `[32000, 5376]`. Linear weights are packed NVFP4.

Extraction kept only `transformer_layer_config`, so the draft lost that quant block. The flat parser read compressed-tensors `ignore` and dropped `exclude_modules`. The weight loader then copied a BF16 row into a packed parameter.

The draft already resolved its own quant config through `get_draft_quant_config()`. It did not inherit the target scheme. Pinning after construction keeps an explicit `None` from being replaced by the target config still attached during draft setup.

`d2t[i]` is the offset from draft id `i` to target id `i + d2t[i]`. Sampling uses only `d2t`. `t2d` is a bool mask, so `d2t` cannot be rebuilt from it. A BF16-rounded `d2t` still loads on main and proposes the wrong tokens. This check rejects that case. It does not fix the #62028 shape mismatch, and the published AEON-7 checkpoint still does not load until `d2t` matches `t2d`.

This is not #49900 (compressed-tensors `draft_model` prefix) and not #59040 (MTP fc quantization). No other open PR covers this exclude path.

AI assistance was used. The submitting human should review every changed line before requesting review.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests listed above (18 passed).
- [x] Load the #62028 draft on SM120 and confirm the 2688 vs 5376 mismatch is gone (reported by @waynehacking8).
- [ ] Confirm a checkpoint whose `d2t` matches `t2d` still loads on GPU, and that the published NVFP4 `d2t` is rejected with the new error.

title: [Bug]: Stop sequences match inside reasoning, so responses come back empty (breaks Claude Code auto mode)
body:
### Your current environment

vLLM `main` @ `ae8f41238c`, 8xH100, served with `just serve` equivalent:

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Stop sequences are checked against the model's reasoning, not just the answer. If the reasoning contains the stop string, generation ends inside `<think>` and the response has **no text**.

This breaks Claude Code's auto mode on vLLM. Its safety classifier sends `stop_sequences: ["</block>"]` and expects `<block>yes|no`. The model often writes `<block>no</block>` while thinking, so the request stops before the answer and the classifier gets no verdict. Claude Code then retries the check or escalates to its slower second stage, which adds latency and extra calls (see the comment below for traces across Claude Code versions).

### Repro

Without `stop_sequences`, the response is correct:

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/messages -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash", "max_tokens": 2048,
  "system": "You are a security classifier. Decide whether the shell command should be blocked.\nIf it should be blocked, output <block>yes</block>. Otherwise output <block>no</block>.",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Command: ls -la\nYour response MUST begin with <block>."}]
}' | jq -c '{stop_reason, text: [.content[]|select(.type=="text")|.text]}'
```
```json
{"stop_reason":"end_turn","text":["<block>no</block>"]}
```

The same request with `"stop_sequences": ["</block>"]` comes back empty (the end of the thinking block is shown for clarity):

```json
{"stop_reason":"stop_sequence","stop_sequence":"</block>","text":[],
 "thinking_tail":"...Command ls -la. Clearly safe. Must output <block>no"}
```

It reproduces in **100/100** requests. `/v1/chat/completions` with `"stop": ["</block>"]` behaves the same way: `content: null`, and the reasoning is cut off at `<block>no`.

### Expected

Stop sequences should only apply to the answer, after `</think>`. The model would then finish reasoning and return `<block>no`. That is how hosted APIs behave.

### Related

- #53066 (same root cause, found via lm-eval)
- #58647 item 3 (Claude Code `/v1/messages` hardening RFC)
- Open fixes: #52486, #38533
