title: [Bugfix][Attention] Chunk sparse indexer decode logits by request
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The CUDA sparse-indexer decode path scores the whole batch into one fp32 `[batch * next_n, max_model_len]` logits tensor. Full CUDA graphs keep that tensor in their pool, while the profiling run reserves only `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` for it. This PR scores whole requests in chunks bounded by that budget, as the prefill path already does. At long context with many sequences, this frees several GiB per GPU for KV cache.

## Claims

- Decode logits never exceed `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` (default 512 MiB) per chunk on SM90/SM120. At least one whole request goes into each chunk.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 8x RTX PRO 6000, TP8, 1M context, 1,024 sequences: the CUDA graph pool drops from 12.45 to 3.09 GiB per GPU, and KV cache capacity grows 2.12x (6.31M to 13.39M tokens).
- Accuracy is unchanged (GSM8K 0.901 before, 0.904 after, with 1,024 concurrent requests so the chunked path runs).
- Nothing changes when the batch fits in one chunk. Varlen decode (SM100), DCP and XPU keep the single full-batch call.

## Validation

**End to end.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8x RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition (SM120). Image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294`; the files under test are identical to current `main`. Both arms add #60762 on top, because without it V4.1 cannot boot on SM120 (#59203). This PR does not depend on #60762.

`vllm serve <DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash> --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' --compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size":1024}' --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41`

| Arm | CUDA graph pool / GPU (actual) | Available KV memory / GPU | GPU KV cache size | GSM8K accuracy, 3 runs (mean) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main + #60762 | 12.45 GiB | 13.10 GiB | 6,306,185 tokens (6.01x of 1M) | 0.901 / 0.904 / 0.901 (0.902) |
| main + #60762 + this PR | 3.09 GiB | 27.82 GiB | 13,392,984 tokens (12.77x of 1M) | 0.895 / 0.900 / 0.917 (0.904) |

GSM8K: `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 --temperature 0 --max-concurrency 1024`.

- Every run had 0 client errors and at most 0.001 invalid responses.
- Running requests peaked at 1,024 (sampled from `/metrics`), so the patched runs took the chunked path.
- The spread within each arm comes from batch-order nondeterminism at temperature 0.
- The memory figures are identical across the two boots of each arm.

**Unit tests.** All on SM120 in the same image:

- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py`: 25 passed, 18 of them new.
- The new test compares chunked against full-batch top-k through the real `sparse_attn_indexer` entry point. It covers `next_n` 1/2, top-k 128/512/2048, and candidate blocks off/write/read. It also covers a zero-length request and an incomplete last chunk.
- Every chunk's allocation must stay within a 1 MiB budget.
- A captured CUDA graph is replayed after context lengths and weights change.
- Negative control: the new test fails 18/18 against unpatched `main`, with one unchunked allocation of 2,359,296 or 4,718,592 bytes.
- `tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_tp_row_shard.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py`: 174 passed, 12 skipped. The result is the same with and without this PR.
- `pre-commit` passes.

**Not covered:**

- SM90 was not run locally. The new test runs in CI in the "(H100) DeepGEMM Kernels" step.
- SM100 is not exercised. Its varlen path is unchanged, and the new test skips there.
- The FP4 indexer cache and XPU are not tested on hardware.

## Details

**Root cause.** The decode branch calls `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` once for the whole batch. For V4.1 at 1M context, each row has 262,144 compressed columns (1 MiB of fp32). During FULL-graph capture, that allocation is made at the captured batch size and stays in the graph pool. The profiling run's dummy allocation reserves only `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB`, and prefill is already chunked to that budget, but decode was not. The measured pool shrinks by 9.36 GiB per GPU. That is more than one 1 GiB logits tensor; I have not broken it down per captured size.

**Change.**

- `chunk_size = max(1, budget // (next_n * max_model_len * 4))` requests.
- Each chunk slices Q, Q scales, weights, block-table rows, candidate rows and top-k rows.
- Each chunk rebuilds its DeepGEMM schedule metadata from its own context lengths. It uses `get_num_sms()`, DeepGEMM's current SM count, which dual-batch overlap lowers. That is the count the kernel checks the metadata against (the full-batch case of this is #60732).
- Each chunk's logits are freed before the next chunk is allocated.
- The chunk size depends only on shapes, so it adds no host sync, and graph capture stays deterministic. The test captures the chunked path in a graph.
- The extra cost is one small metadata kernel per chunk per indexer layer, paid only when the batch is larger than one chunk.
- GSM8K throughput was the same in both arms: 2,339–2,541 output tok/s patched, against 2,313–2,556 unpatched, over 3 runs each. This is not a performance claim.

**Scope.**

- SM100 decode is varlen (`indices`, with bf16 logits). Chunking it would need varlen-aware schedule metadata that I cannot test, so that path keeps one call.
- DCP keeps one call, because `_merge_dcp_topk_global` runs over the full rows.

**Not a duplicate.**

- #58068 fixes the prefill logits width (#55569), not decode.
- #56686 and #42856 size decode logits by `max_seq_len` for eager steps. Under graph capture, `max_seq_len` is `max_model_len`, so captured graphs keep the full width.
- Searches for open PRs on decode-logits chunking, `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` and `sparse_attn_indexer` decode memory found nothing else.
- #58536 (TP-sharded decode rows) and #60732 touch the same decode branch but solve different problems. I will rebase onto whichever lands first.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude). The tests and evaluations above were run as described.

title: [Perf] Emit the DSA indexer weights in BF16 on SM100
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On SM100, `fused_q` now writes the DSA indexer weights directly in BF16, the dtype DeepGEMM's MQA logits kernels
take. This removes the FP32 to BF16 copy `mqa_logits_mx_inputs` launched on every indexer call.

## Claims

- One fewer kernel per indexer call (prefill chunks and decode) on SM100/SM103 for DSA models using `fused_q`
  (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x). The logits are bit-identical: the weights are still computed in FP32 and rounded to
  BF16 once, just inside `fused_q` instead of in a separate copy.
- Other platforms are unchanged (FP32 weights).
- On InferenceX AgentX, GLM-5.3 vs SGLang: together with #62171 and #62172, decode time on the same turns drops 2.0-2.9% on 4x GB200 (2.5-4.1% on 4x B300) at concurrency 1-16; by the forward benchmark this PR is about 1/6 of that.

## Validation

- `tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v32_norm_rope.py` on B300 (SM103): 214 passed, 8 skipped. The weight
  assertions now check BF16 output on SM100 and FP32 elsewhere.
- Target verify forward latency (`vllm bench forward`, GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, dummy weights, exact KV lengths, MTP verify shapes of B requests x 4 tokens, `max_model_len` 1M, CUDA graph; spread < 0.1%), B300:

  | shape | before (us) | after (us) |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1x4 @25K | 8724.8 | 8696.4 (-0.33%) |
  | 3x4 @25K | 12264.2 | 12231.4 (-0.27%) |
  | 7x4 @25K | 17688.4 | 17649.7 (-0.22%) |
  | 1x4 @94K | 8829.5 | 8799.6 (-0.34%) |
  | 3x4 @94K | 12561.0 | 12532.0 (-0.23%) |
  | 7x4 @94K | 18148.9 | 18116.0 (-0.18%) |

- Exactness: with real MTP verification (32 GSM8K questions, greedy, one at a time), this PR stacked with the other GLM-5 top-k changes gives the same outputs (32/32) and the same acceptance length (3.4904) as main.
- End to end on B300 x4 (SM103): GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, MTP 3 with synthetic acceptance length 3.0 (fixed step count), `max_model_len` 1M, FP8 KV, CUDA graphs (default sizes). Decode ms/token per request, median of 9 repetitions of (T1200 - T200) / 1000 on cached prompts (repetition spread at B=1 is about 1.5%):

  | context | B | main | this PR |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 25K | 1 | 3.182 | 3.171 (-0.3%) |
  | 94K | 1 | 3.227 | 3.207 (-0.6%) |

  Batches of 3-7 move within the measurement noise (about ±1.5%).

<details>
<summary>InferenceX AgentX setup and full results (GLM-5.3-NVFP4, vLLM vs SGLang)</summary>

InferenceX c801c9f2d AgentX scenario (pinned AIPerf), 20-minute fast mode, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 rev e3b8f9f2, TP4, MTP 3
(synthetic acceptance 2.99), native KV offload 135 GB per rank, Rust frontend, MoE autotune, `max-num-seqs` =
2 x concurrency. vLLM is main dcd07967ca with its default linear backend and default CUDA graph config, plus the
PRs cumulatively. SGLang a916d91cd3 with IMEX, TRT-LLM all-reduce fusion, `--mem-fraction-static 0.90`. Fresh
server per point, SGLang and the four vLLM variants alternating per concurrency. "Decode" is request latency minus
TTFT, summed over the turns both runs finished (a few hundred per point); fast-mode throughput alone moves about
+-2% between runs.

4x GB200 (c=1/4 on driver 580.173.02; c=8/16 on 580.178.04 after a host reinstall, SGLang rerun there too):

| decode time vs SGLang, same turns | main | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6630, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6631, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6632) | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 | +8.9% | +5.8% | +4.0% | +3.2% |
| c=4 | +12.7% | +10.6% | +7.3% | +7.3% |
| c=8 | +12.3% | +9.5% | +7.9% | +7.3% |
| c=16 | -22.6% | -25.0% | -24.5% | -24.3% |

| tok/s/GPU vs SGLang | main | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 (SGLang 5,681) | -3.2% | -0.4% | -1.1% | +0.6% |
| c=4 (SGLang 6,783) | -0.6% | -2.4% | +0.4% | -1.7% |
| c=8 (SGLang 11,799) | -11.5% | -9.4% | -8.8% | -8.4% |
| c=16 (SGLang 10,529) | +44.7% | +45.6% | +45.8% | +46.8% |

| decode time vs the previous column, same turns | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 c=1 / c=4 / c=8 / c=16 | -2.9% / -2.0% / -2.1% / -2.9% | -1.6% / -3.1% / -1.2% / -0.4% | -0.8% / -0.9% / -0.5% / -0.1% |
| B300 c=1 / c=4 | -2.5% / -4.1% | -1.6% / -3.1% | -0.5% / -1.1% |

#62170, #62171 and #62172 were measured together; `vllm bench forward` (target verify forward, spread < 0.1%)
splits their gain about 1/6, 1/2 and 1/3.

</details>

## Details

`mqa_logits_use_mx_scales()` already decides that the SM100 logits kernels take BF16 weights, and
`mqa_logits_mx_inputs` returned `weights.to(torch.bfloat16)`. That was a real copy kernel for every indexer call,
since `fused_q` (Triton and CuTeDSL) always wrote FP32. `fused_q` now allocates its weights output in the dtype the
logits kernels take, and both kernels cast on store. `.to(torch.bfloat16)` then returns the tensor as-is.

The CuTeDSL kernel's compile key gains the output dtype.

title: [Perf][Kernel] Let cooperative_topk read the BF16 indexer logits
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Stacked on #62171 (row-length single pass); only the last commit is new.

`cooperative_topk` now also reads BF16 logits. On SM100 the DSA indexer then keeps the paged MQA logits in BF16
instead of upcasting them to FP32 before the decode top-k. This extends what main already does for
`deep_select`.

## Claims

- One fewer kernel per indexer decode call on SM100/SM103 (the FP32 upcast `as_fp32_logits`), and the top-k reads
  half the bytes.
- The selected top-k values are the same as from the FP32 upcast: BF16 widens to FP32 exactly. Among exactly
  equal logits, which index wins was already unspecified.
- DCP, top-k backends that take only FP32, and BF16 rows that are not 16-byte aligned still upcast as before.
- On InferenceX AgentX, GLM-5.3 vs SGLang: together with #62170 and #62171, decode time on the same turns drops 2.0-2.9% on 4x GB200 (2.5-4.1% on 4x B300) at concurrency 1-16; by the forward benchmark this PR is about 1/3 of that.

## Validation

- `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py` on B300 (SM103): 285 passed, 37 skipped.
  - `test_cooperative_topk_rows_shorter_than_stride` now runs FP32 and BF16 logits through every cluster size and
    both paths. It compares the selected values with `torch.topk` and checks that no index repeats.
  - `test_sparse_indexer_topk_backend_resolution` checks when BF16 logits skip the upcast: `auto` or `cooperative`
    within the row limit, with a 16-byte-aligned stride. `persistent` and over-limit batches still upcast.
- Kernel time on B300 is the same for BF16 and FP32 input (10.3 us at 4 rows x 40K, 11.1 us at 16 rows), so the
  saving is the upcast kernel and its extra pass over the logits.
- Target verify forward latency (`vllm bench forward`, GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, dummy weights, exact KV lengths, MTP verify shapes of B requests x 4 tokens, `max_model_len` 1M, CUDA graph; spread < 0.1%), B300, on top of #62170 and #62171:

  |---|---|---|
  | 1x4 @25K | 8630.6 | 8589.8 (-0.47%) |
  | 3x4 @25K | 12136.9 | 12090.4 (-0.38%) |
  | 7x4 @25K | 17547.7 | 17497.8 (-0.28%) |
  | 1x4 @94K | 8702.3 | 8654.3 (-0.55%) |
  | 3x4 @94K | 12361.1 | 12284.4 (-0.62%) |
  | 7x4 @94K | 17940.9 | 17806.9 (-0.75%) |

  In an nsys node-level trace of the batch-1 verify graph, `_upcast_logits_kernel` (36 us per step) is gone.

- Exactness: with real MTP verification (32 GSM8K questions, greedy, one at a time), this PR stacked with the other GLM-5 top-k changes gives the same outputs (32/32) and the same acceptance length (3.4904) as main.
- End to end on B300 x4 (SM103): GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, MTP 3 with synthetic acceptance length 3.0 (fixed step count), `max_model_len` 1M, FP8 KV, CUDA graphs (default sizes). Decode ms/token per request, median of 9 repetitions of (T1200 - T200) / 1000 on cached prompts (repetition spread at B=1 is about 1.5%), on top of #62170 and #62171:

  | context | B | before | this PR |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 25K | 1 | 3.145 | 3.132 (-0.4%) |
  | 94K | 1 | 3.190 | 3.167 (-0.7%) |
  | 94K | 7 | 5.814 | 5.740 (-1.3%) |

<details>
<summary>InferenceX AgentX setup and full results (GLM-5.3-NVFP4, vLLM vs SGLang)</summary>

InferenceX c801c9f2d AgentX scenario (pinned AIPerf), 20-minute fast mode, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 rev e3b8f9f2, TP4, MTP 3
(synthetic acceptance 2.99), native KV offload 135 GB per rank, Rust frontend, MoE autotune, `max-num-seqs` =
2 x concurrency. vLLM is main dcd07967ca with its default linear backend and default CUDA graph config, plus the
PRs cumulatively. SGLang a916d91cd3 with IMEX, TRT-LLM all-reduce fusion, `--mem-fraction-static 0.90`. Fresh
server per point, SGLang and the four vLLM variants alternating per concurrency. "Decode" is request latency minus
TTFT, summed over the turns both runs finished (a few hundred per point); fast-mode throughput alone moves about
+-2% between runs.

4x GB200 (c=1/4 on driver 580.173.02; c=8/16 on 580.178.04 after a host reinstall, SGLang rerun there too):

| decode time vs SGLang, same turns | main | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6630, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6631, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6632) | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 | +8.9% | +5.8% | +4.0% | +3.2% |
| c=4 | +12.7% | +10.6% | +7.3% | +7.3% |

| tok/s/GPU vs SGLang | main | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 (SGLang 5,681) | -3.2% | -0.4% | -1.1% | +0.6% |
| c=4 (SGLang 6,783) | -0.6% | -2.4% | +0.4% | -1.7% |

splits their gain about 1/6, 1/2 and 1/3.

## Details

- `CooperativeTopKParams`, the TMA staging buffers and the histogram loads are templated on the input type.
- TMA units are 16 bytes (8 BF16 or 4 FP32 elements), so the stride and per-block alignment follow the element
  size.
- Scores are widened to FP32 when binned, so both input types use the same radix keys.
- The extension dispatches on `logits.scalar_type()`.
- `SparseIndexerTopk.takes_bf16_logits` reports whether the resolved backend reads BF16 directly: `cooperative`
  (also as `auto`'s choice) when its constraints hold, and `deep_select`. The indexer upcasts only when it doesn't
  or when DCP is on. This replaces main's `topk_backend != "deep_select"` check with the same rule extended to
  `cooperative`.
- Candidate-block selection (DeepSeek-V4.1) already handles BF16 logits under `deep_select`. With `cooperative` it
  now gets them too. I could not run that model here.

title: [Perf] Fuse GLM-5.x MoE finalize into the next RMSNorm's all-reduce
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

GLM-5.x (the `DeepseekV32` NVIDIA path) now leaves each decode MoE layer's top-k reduction open. The next RMSNorm's
fused all-reduce then finalizes it in one FlashInfer kernel (`trtllm_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion`). This uses
the existing deferred-finalize contract (`MoEOutput`, `defer_moe_finalize`) that DeepSeek-V4.1 and Kimi-K3 already
use.

**Needs flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6630 (deadlock fix) and flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6631 (speed); draft until a
FlashInfer release with both is pinned.** Without the first the kernel can hang under back-to-back launches; without the
second, deferring is slower than the unfused path. flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6632 (cluster sizing) adds most of the gain
at 5-7 running requests.

## Claims

With the FlashInfer fixes, on GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, MTP 3, B300:

- Target verify forward (`vllm bench forward`, spread < 0.1%): -1.2% to -1.3% at 1 request, -1.5% at 3, -0.8% at 7.
  Serving decode at batch 1: -1.2% ms/token.
- Per MoE layer, the GEMM2 tail is one kernel instead of three: finalize, shared + routed add, all-reduce +
  residual + RMSNorm.
- Accuracy: GSM8K unchanged within run-to-run noise (see below). The fused kernel accumulates in FP32.
- On InferenceX AgentX, GLM-5.3 vs SGLang, with FlashInfer flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6630 to flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6632: decode time on the same turns drops 1.2-3.1% at concurrency 1-8 and 0.4% at 16 on 4x GB200 (1.6-3.1% on 4x B300).

## Validation

- New `tests/kernels/core/test_fused_allreduce_rms_norm.py`: a `MoEOutput` holding an `UnfinalizedMoEOutput`
  through `fused_allreduce_rms_norm` must match finalize, shared add, then `RMSNorm(all_reduce(.))`. It runs on TP
  1, 2 and 4, with 1, 4 and 64 tokens, hidden 2048 and 6144, on both the fused kernel (checking it was called) and
  the fallback. Result on B300 with the FlashInfer fixes: 30 passed, 6 skipped (TP=1 has no fused path).
- End to end on B300 x4 (SM103), GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, MTP 3, `max_model_len` 1M, FP8 KV, on top of the other GLM-5 decode changes
  (#62170, #62171, #62172). "fix only" is FlashInfer with flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6630, "fix + perf" adds
  flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6631.

  Target verify forward, `vllm bench forward` (dummy weights, exact shapes, CUDA graph), us:

  | shape (requests x 4 tokens @ KV) | no deferral | deferral, fix only | deferral, fix + perf |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1x4 @25K | 8570.1 | 8618.4 (+0.56%) | 8464.4 (-1.23%) |
  | 3x4 @25K | 12075.2 | 12128.4 (+0.44%) | 11891.7 (-1.52%) |
  | 5x4 @25K | 15470.2 | 15784.6 (+2.03%) | 15357.2 (-0.73%) |
  | 7x4 @25K | 17472.5 | 17849.5 (+2.16%) | 17337.3 (-0.77%) |
  | 1x4 @94K | 8639.5 | 8676.0 (+0.42%) | 8528.0 (-1.29%) |
  | 3x4 @94K | 12267.1 | 12318.9 (+0.42%) | 12081.3 (-1.51%) |
  | 7x4 @94K | 17785.9 | 18160.8 (+2.11%) | 17644.7 (-0.79%) |

  Serving decode ms/token (synthetic acceptance length 3.0, median of 9), batch 1: 3.131 -> 3.094 at 25K and
  3.169 -> 3.131 at 94K (-1.2%) with fix + perf; 3.158 / 3.182 (slower) with fix only.

  nsys node-level trace, batch-1 verify graph per step: `finalizeKernel` (297 us) and most of the
  shared + routed add (elementwise 217 -> 70 us) are gone; finalize + all-reduce + norm 1438 -> 1265 us.

  GSM8K (lm_eval, 5-shot, 1319 questions, real MTP verification, concurrency 32), flexible / strict:

  | | run 1 | run 2 |
  |---|---|---|
  | main | 0.9439 / 0.9424 | 0.9439 / 0.9424 |
  | this PR (with all the changes above) | 0.9401 / 0.9401 | 0.9447 / 0.9424 |

  (stderr 0.0063). Greedy outputs differ from main: the finalize now rounds once instead of after each step.

<details>
<summary>InferenceX AgentX setup and full results (GLM-5.3-NVFP4, vLLM vs SGLang)</summary>

InferenceX c801c9f2d AgentX scenario (pinned AIPerf), 20-minute fast mode, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 rev e3b8f9f2, TP4, MTP 3
(synthetic acceptance 2.99), native KV offload 135 GB per rank, Rust frontend, MoE autotune, `max-num-seqs` =
2 x concurrency. vLLM is main dcd07967ca with its default linear backend and default CUDA graph config, plus the
PRs cumulatively. SGLang a916d91cd3 with IMEX, TRT-LLM all-reduce fusion, `--mem-fraction-static 0.90`. Fresh
server per point, SGLang and the four vLLM variants alternating per concurrency. "Decode" is request latency minus
TTFT, summed over the turns both runs finished (a few hundred per point); fast-mode throughput alone moves about
+-2% between runs.

4x GB200 (c=1/4 on driver 580.173.02; c=8/16 on 580.178.04 after a host reinstall, SGLang rerun there too):

| decode time vs SGLang, same turns | main | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6630, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6631, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6632) | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 | +8.9% | +5.8% | +4.0% | +3.2% |
| c=4 | +12.7% | +10.6% | +7.3% | +7.3% |
| c=8 | +12.3% | +9.5% | +7.9% | +7.3% |
| c=16 | -22.6% | -25.0% | -24.5% | -24.3% |

| tok/s/GPU vs SGLang | main | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 (SGLang 5,681) | -3.2% | -0.4% | -1.1% | +0.6% |
| c=4 (SGLang 6,783) | -0.6% | -2.4% | +0.4% | -1.7% |
| c=8 (SGLang 11,799) | -11.5% | -9.4% | -8.8% | -8.4% |
| c=16 (SGLang 10,529) | +44.7% | +45.6% | +45.8% | +46.8% |

| decode time vs the previous column, same turns | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 c=1 / c=4 / c=8 / c=16 | -2.9% / -2.0% / -2.1% / -2.9% | -1.6% / -3.1% / -1.2% / -0.4% | -0.8% / -0.9% / -0.5% / -0.1% |
| B300 c=1 / c=4 | -2.5% / -4.1% | -1.6% / -3.1% | -0.5% / -1.1% |

#62170, #62171 and #62172 were measured together; `vllm bench forward` (target verify forward, spread < 0.1%)
splits their gain about 1/6, 1/2 and 1/3.

</details>

## Details

- `fused_allreduce_rms_norm` accepts a `MoEOutput`. If the routed part is unfinalized, and TP > 1 with the TRT-LLM
  workspace in use, it calls `trtllm_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion`, which does the top-k sum, routed scaling,
  shared add, all-reduce, residual add and RMSNorm. Called without that kernel available (only possible from
  outside these layers, for example the unit test), it finalizes in torch and takes the normal path.
- `moe_finalize_allreduce_max_num_tokens` bounds deferral by the kernel's one-shot limit (128 tokens) and by the
  size up to which vLLM already picks the one-shot all-reduce. It also creates (or reuses) the shared TRT-LLM
  all-reduce workspace and returns 0 if that fails, so a layer only defers when the fused kernel will run. Above
  the bound, or when the backend isn't `trtllm`, the layer finalizes as before.
- A decoder layer defers only when its experts are TRT-LLM-Gen (NVFP4 or BF16 monolithic/modular, the ones that
  can stop after GEMM2), it isn't sequence parallel, and the router folds `routed_scaling_factor` into the routing
  weights (the deferred output carries no scaling of its own, so the experts' factor must be 1.0). Each
  local layer defers except the last one on a non-last PP rank, since its output leaves as `IntermediateTensors`.
  Layers that feed an aux hidden state (EAGLE-3) don't defer. The MTP block defers into its final norm.
- `_forward_impl` and `_unpack` are used directly, as in `deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py`, because the runner's
  custom op returns tensors only.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Open a new assistant turn after a final assistant message in the DeepSeek V4/V4.1 renderer
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Rust-frontend fix for #46256 (DeepSeek V4 / V4.1 renderer, `rust/src/chat/src/renderer/deepseek.rs`). When the last message is an assistant message and `add_generation_prompt=true` (`StartNewAssistant`, the default), the prompt ends at `<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>` without an `<｜Assistant｜>` turn prefix. The model then returns empty or garbled text with HTTP 200. This PR appends the turn prefix in that case. `continue_final_message` and `add_generation_prompt=false` are unchanged. **Behaviour change:** an assistant prefill sent *without* `continue_final_message` now starts a new turn instead of continuing after EOS (see Details).

## Claims

- When the final message is an assistant message and `add_generation_prompt=true`, the prompt now equals the DeepSeek reference encoding of the conversation followed by the reference assistant turn prefix. That prefix is `<｜Assistant｜><think>` in thinking mode and `<｜Assistant｜></think>` in chat mode. The comparison is token-for-token.
- These prompts are token-identical to before:
  - prompts that do not end in an assistant message;
  - prompts that use `continue_final_message` or `add_generation_prompt=false`.
- Fixes empty and garbled replies on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Example: with thinking off, `[user, assistant(answer)]` gave empty replies 25/200 times before this change and 0/200 after.

## Validation

**Reference encoder.** The reference encoder has no generation-prompt control. It writes `<｜Assistant｜>` + think token only after a user-like message; its README calls this the assistant turn prefix. So a conversation that ends with an assistant message is encoded as closed history ending at EOS. That is why the old output in the "before" column matches the reference: the reference has no "start a new turn" output to compare against. `add_generation_prompt=true` asks for a new turn, so this PR appends the same turn prefix the reference encoder uses. The choice between `<think>` and `</think>` follows the reference rule for the turn after the last user message.

The server's `/tokenize` output was compared, as token ids, against `encoding/encoding.py` from `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash@df42c109`. 7 conversation shapes were tested, each with thinking on and off:

| Shape | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| ends with user (2 shapes) | = reference | = reference (unchanged) |
| ends with assistant (5 shapes): plain, with `reasoning_content`, after a multi-turn history, with a system message, with `tool_calls` | = reference closed history (ends at EOS, no turn prefix) | = reference + `<｜Assistant｜>` + `<think>`/`</think>` |

**Unchanged paths render identically.** The exact lm-eval requests from our quality runs were re-rendered with both binaries:

| Requests | identical |
|---|---|
| GSM8K 8-shot (1,319) | 1,319 / 1,319 |
| IFEval (541) | 541 / 541 |
| HumanEval-instruct + `continue_final_message` (164) | 164 / 164 |
| HumanEval-instruct, prefill **without** `continue_final_message` (164) | 0 / 164: each differs by exactly the 2 opener tokens (see Behaviour change) |

**End-to-end.** Setup: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4×H200 with TP4, image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-92044241`, `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, with speculative decoding through the model's built-in draft module (`--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}'`). The same Rust sources were built with and without this change and swapped into the same container. Sampling: T=1.0, top_p=0.95.

| Request (no extra flags) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `[user, assistant(answer)]`, thinking off, 200 requests: empty replies | 25 | 0 |
| `[user, assistant(answer)]`, thinking on, 20 requests: `</think>` in content | 4 | 0 |
| `[user, assistant(answer)]`, thinking on, 20 requests: replies with a reasoning block | 0 | 20 |
| `[user, assistant(answer, reasoning_content)]`, thinking on, 20 requests: empty replies | 14 | 0 |
| `[system, user, assistant(tool_calls)]`, no tool result, 20 requests each (chat / thinking): reply is empty or starts with `<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>` | 20 / 19 | 0 / 0 |
| 20 other shapes (user-terminated, streaming, tools, `reasoning_effort`, inline/trailing system, long history, `json_schema`), 11 requests each | clean | clean |

A 900 s serving benchmark at concurrency 16 gives the same throughput before and after (132,437 vs. 131,919 tok/s, within noise). This is expected, because rendering cost does not change.

**Unit tests** (`rust/src/chat`, Rust 1.95, `main` @ `21e09ea9`):
- `cargo test --lib deepseek`: 73 passed before this change, 76 after it.
- Control: with only the new tests and no renderer change, the V4.1 and V4 new-turn tests fail. The continuation / closed-history test passes on both.
- `roundtrip_deepseek_v41` passes, and `cargo fmt --check` is clean.
- The refactor that computes `next_rendered_entry` once is render-neutral. A binary with the full PR renders all the requests above token-identically to a binary with the original fix:
  - 2,188 lm-eval requests;
  - 14 reference-encoder cases;
  - 340 saved end-to-end request bodies.
  So the end-to-end numbers carry over.

## Details

- **Root cause:** the render loop calls `write_assistant_transition` only after user-like entries.
- **Change** (`deepseek.rs`, +34 / −23):
  - `next_rendered_entry` is now computed once per entry.
  - A final assistant entry with `add_generation_prompt()` true calls the existing `write_assistant_transition`, with the same arguments the user path uses.
- **Tests:** full `expect!` snapshots.
  - New turn after a complete answer: one V4.1 test (`thinking` off/on) and one V4 test (`enable_thinking` off/on).
  - V4.1 prefill rendered with `continue_final_message` and with `add_generation_prompt=false`: unchanged.
  - The existing V4 test `system_to_assistant_transitions_…` checks a transition, not the trailing prompt. It now pins `NoGenerationPrompt`, as the shared fixtures do; its expected strings are unchanged.
- **Behaviour change:**
  - A client that sends an assistant prefill without `continue_final_message` used to continue after EOS. It now gets a new turn instead.
  - Measured impact: lm-eval `humaneval_instruct` sends such a prefill. Without `continue_final_message` its pass@1 goes from 0.4207 to 0.0000. The old score already came from continuing after EOS, which is not a supported format.
  - Why exactly 0: lm-eval scores `doc["prompt"]` plus the reply cut at its first `` ``` ``. In the new turn the model writes a complete fenced answer: 160/164 replies start with `` ```python ``, so the cut keeps nothing and the program is the bare function stub. The other 4 replies are reasoning-style prose with no code before the cut, so the program is the stub followed by prose. All 164 fail. The low score measures the scorer's assumption (the reply continues the prefill), not a broken reply.
  - With `continue_final_message=true` the same task scores 0.9573 before and 0.9634 after.
  - Score noise: HumanEval has 164 problems, so one problem is about 0.006. These runs are greedy, but outputs are not bit-reproducible under batching and speculative decoding. Differences of 1–2 problems, such as 0.9573 vs 0.9634 on token-identical prompts, are run-to-run noise.
  - Alternative considered: treating a trailing assistant message as a prefix by default (continue in place). That recovers this prefill case (0.9756 without the flag). But it breaks completed answers: when the final assistant message was a full answer, 15/20 greedy and 9/20 sampled replies were empty. It would also contradict the documented meaning of `StartNewAssistant`, so it was not adopted.
  - A request that ends with an assistant `tool_calls` message and no tool result now also gets a new turn. Over 20 requests each:
    - chat mode: the model re-issued the call 14 times and replied in text 6 times;
    - thinking mode: it re-issued the call 1 time and replied 19 times that no result came back.
    Before this change, 20/20 (chat) and 19/20 (thinking) replies were empty or started with `<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>`. The OpenAI API rejects this request shape. Rejecting it in vLLM would be a request-validation change, which is out of scope for this PR.
  - If maintainers prefer, I can add a debug log for the prefill-without-`continue_final_message` case.
- **Prior work:**
  - #57882 (Python V4.1 tokenizer) used the same semantics: "opens a fresh assistant turn after a completed assistant message". It received no review and was closed by its author.
  - #56593 (merged) covers a final user message with `add_generation_prompt=false`.
- **Python frontend:** this PR changes only the Rust frontend. The Python tokenizers still have the gap (#46256, and #46257 for V4), so the two frontends render this case differently until the Python side is fixed. A follow-up PR can port the same semantics to `deepseek_v41.py`.
- **Coverage:** unit tests cover the new path for both V4 and V4.1. The end-to-end runs used V4.1-Flash only.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). The submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation above.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][ROCm] MoRIIO hybrid READ: skip locally cached prefix pages
body:
## Overview

Draft, written with Claude Code; stays draft until the submitter reviews every line. MoRIIO hybrid (KDA/Mamba) READ re-reads attention pages the decoder already caches; this reads only external-token pages.

Not duplicates: #48471 (non-hybrid length mismatch), #62165 (SWA tail clipping), #60867 (multi-group hybrid READ at the same call site; the later one rebases).

## Claims

- With a decoder prefix-cache hit, hybrid READ moves only the attention pages for tokens `[N-1-E, N-1)` (`N` prompt length, `E` final `num_external_tokens`). KDA/Mamba transfer is unchanged.
- Tables that do not cover that range raise `MoRIIOError` instead of being tail-aligned.
- No throughput claim; the tested workload is prefill-queue bound.

## Validation

- `test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py`: main @ 237d99b 104 passed, PR 112 passed, new tests on main connector 11 failed. ruff 0.14.0 clean.
- Kimi-K3 1P1D TP8/DCP8, 2 x 8 MI355X: on all 8 decode ranks, 32 sampled prefix-hit transfers READ exactly the missing pages; attention READ 45.77 GB to 12.11 GB.
- 3600 s agentic replay, concurrency 48: 4273 succeeded, 9 empty-content errors (unpatched: 9).
- No accuracy eval: skipped pages are the decoder's own cached pages, checked page exact.

<details><summary>Commands, revert-red and GPU setup</summary>

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=$PWD \
  python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py
uvx ruff@0.14.0 check <changed files>
uvx ruff@0.14.0 format --check <changed files>
```

Revert-red, new tests with the main connector: 6 x `test_scheduler_accepts_dspark_with_wrapped_full_attention` (main has no `_attn_block_size`), 2 x `test_update_state_rejects_incomplete_attention_tables`, `test_update_state_selects_missing_attention_pages[128]` and `[192]`, `test_update_state_uses_final_external_token_count[128]`.

`test_moriio_routing.py` and `test_moriio_connector.py`: 3 passed, 32 skipped (they need ROCm and mori).

GPU build: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-81198e97` plus this fix; the connector lines it adds are identical to this PR. MoRIIO READ, prefix caching on both sides, prefill-side MultiConnector (MoRIIO + SimpleCPUOffloadConnector), DSpark speculative decoding, FP8 KV. One attention page is 12288 tokens after DCP sharding. The decoder's local prefix hit was 89.7% of prompt tokens.

Sampled transfers came after warmup, with `E > 0` and at least one complete cached decoder page. A per-rank observer recorded READ submissions and completions; bytes are logical payload.

| | attention pages | attention GB | KDA GB | total GB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| old selection, same transfers (offline) | 223 | 45.77 | 15.03 | 60.80 |
| this PR (observed) | 59 | 12.11 | 15.03 | 27.14 |

Throughput 10557 tok/s/chip vs 10882 for the unpatched run, which used a different cluster, so not a controlled A/B. Decoder `request_prefill_time` avg 0.12 s unpatched vs 0.11 s patched; prefill-side queue avg 13.8 s vs 16.2 s.
</details>

## Details

Root cause on the decoder:

1. The local prefix hit covers `[0, L)`, so `E = N - 1 - L`.
2. `update_state_after_alloc` receives the complete attention table, cached pages included.
3. `_align_read_blocks` paired P and D tables by length and tail, so READ also covered `[0, L)`.
4. Fix: slice both by page `[(N-1-E) // B, ceil((N-1) / B))`, `B` = attention block size x DCP when sharded.

```diff
-local_attn, remote_attn = self._align_read_blocks(local, remote, self._max_decode_tail_blocks)
+local_attn, remote_attn = self._select_read_attention(request, num_external_tokens, local, remote)
```

- Block hashes cannot mark cached pages: synchronous READ may hash new receive pages first.
- Contract change: a shorter decoder table (the removed test's receive suffix) now raises; a real `KVCacheManager` case and the GPU run pass complete tables.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Sync DeepSeek V4.1 encoder with the 1017 reference (tool-result turns, content-block tool results)
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR syncs vLLM's DeepSeek V4.1 prompt rendering, both the Python tokenizer and the Rust chat renderer, with DeepSeek's updated reference encoder. The reference change is [deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash@314113f](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/commit/314113f8a7dadb388215396ba5fbee2c610a04d6), "fix(encoding): preserve tool image order and current-turn thinking" (2026-10-16). The resulting `encoding.py` is byte-identical to the [`encoding/encoding.py`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017/blob/1bae0e1088993b9b82de08f59de5be5a34e42170/encoding/encoding.py) shipped with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017. 1017's config and tokenizer are unchanged from V4.1-Flash, so it is served by this same code path.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open and closed PRs and issues for "deepseek v4.1 encoding", "1017", "drop_thinking", "find_last_user_index", "current-turn thinking" and "tool result", and found nothing that ports this change. #60792 is related but separate: it fixes tool-result image order in the Python frontend (see Details).

## Claims

- **Tool results no longer end the assistant's turn.** In thinking mode with `drop_thinking` in effect (the default when no `tools` are declared), the reasoning of the assistant message that made a tool call is now kept while its tool results come back. Before, it was dropped from the prompt partway through its own turn. Reasoning from completed turns is still dropped, as in the reference.
- **Content-block tool results stay structured.** At the encoder level, tool results passed as content-block lists (`content_blocks` or list `content`) are kept as blocks, as in the reference.
- **Image placeholder in text is a request error.** A literal `<｜deepseek_image｜>` in message text or reasoning now raises a `ValueError` (400). Before, it was rendered as an image sentinel with no image behind it.
- **Byte-identical prompts.** On 10,679 test conversations, Python prompts match the 1017 reference byte for byte (760 differ on `main`). The Rust renderer matches on every comparable request.
- **No rendering-time cost.** The first commit alone made rendering quadratic in two places: long agent loops in Python, and large blocks of parallel tool results in Rust. The second and third commits make both linear again, back to `main`'s speed (timings below).

## Validation

| Check | `main` (c0b6f74) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Python prompts vs the 1017 reference (7,815 OpenAI-format requests through `apply_chat_template` + 2,864 direct `encode_messages` calls) | 9,919 / 10,679 match | **10,679 / 10,679** match |
| DeepSeek's updated `encoding/test_encoding.py`, run through vLLM's encoder/tokenizer | 36 pass, 6 fail | **42 pass** (6 n/a, 1 xfail, see below) |
| Rust `DeepSeekV41ChatRenderer` prompts vs the 1017 reference (7,354 requests) | 416 differ | **0 differ** |
| Rust `media_order` vs the reference image order | all match | all match |
| `pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py tests/test_request_input_bounds.py` | the 8 new tests fail | **122 passed** |
| `cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib deepseek` | 73 passed (the new turn test fails) | **75 passed** |

**How the `main` mismatches break down.** All 760 fall into three groups: the 660 cases where the reference itself changed, 28 placeholder-validation cases and 72 encoder-level list inputs. Every other case equals the previous reference. Reverting any single behavioral hunk fails exactly that hunk's cases. Reverting the prompt-neutral `context` reorder is caught by the no-mutation assertion.

**Rust exclusion.** The Rust row leaves out 204 requests that send `thinking: true` together with `reasoning_effort: "none"`. That is a pre-existing Python/Rust divergence that this PR does not touch: Rust keeps thinking on at the default effort, while Python switches to chat mode. Under Rust's own resolution those 204 match too. On developer-message conversations (a vLLM extension, 96 cases), Python and Rust agree before and after this PR.

**Reference test suite.** The 6 n/a tests are 5 tool-namespace tests and 1 completion-parser test, none of which vLLM implements. The xfail is tool-result image order through the Python renderer (see Details).

**Rendering time** at 500 / 1,000 / 2,000 tool rounds, median of 5 runs, thinking mode, no tools declared. "Loop" is one user turn followed by k rounds of (assistant tool call, tool result). "Parallel" is one assistant message with k tool calls followed by k tool results.

| Renderer and shape | `main` | First commit alone | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python `encode_messages`, loop | 4.8 / 9.6 / 15.1 ms | 85 / 337 / 1,428 ms | **3.8 / 7.6 / 15.4 ms** |
| Python `encode_messages`, parallel | 1.8 / 3.6 / 7.3 ms | 1.9 / 3.7 / 7.5 ms | **1.9 / 3.7 / 7.5 ms** |
| Rust renderer (release), loop | 0.06 / 0.12 / 0.24 ms | 0.07 / 0.13 / 0.26 ms | **0.06 / 0.14 / 0.27 ms** |
| Rust renderer (release), parallel | 0.06 / 0.13 / 0.26 ms | 0.19 / 0.73 / 2.70 ms | **0.07 / 0.13 / 0.27 ms** |

The Rust parallel case at 10,000 tool results takes 1.4 ms on `main`, 56 ms with the first commit alone, and 1.4 ms with this PR.

<details>
<summary>Differential corpus coverage</summary>

- **OpenAI-format requests:** plain multi-turn; thinking on/off; every effort; `drop_thinking` true/false/default; tools declared or not; multiple and out-of-order tool calls; string and list tool results; consecutive tool results; tool results followed by user text; mid-conversation system messages; images in user content and in tool results; DeepSeek's golden fixtures and examples.
- **Direct `encode_messages` calls:** `context` split at every position, `content_blocks`, `latest_reminder`, `task`.

The harness is not part of this PR. I can share it if useful.
</details>

**Commands run:**

```bash
pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py tests/test_request_input_bounds.py
cd rust && cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib deepseek
cargo clippy -p vllm-chat --all-targets -- -D warnings   # clean
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD      # ruff, ruff-format, mypy, typos, cargo fmt, SPDX, test tethering: pass
```

The Python tests ran on a CPU-only machine with `--noconftest`, because the root conftest's GPU-memory fixture needs an accelerator.

**Model evaluation.** The first commit, backported to nightly 386ac2573, serves DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 in our deployment. Smoke checks pass on it: thinking on/off, a tool call, vision and a long-context needle. No accuracy eval was run, because this change only alters prompt text and the target prompts are defined by DeepSeek's reference encoder, which they now match byte for byte.

## Details

**Root cause.** Before 2026-10-16, vLLM's V4.1 encoder was a faithful port of the reference: every corpus case outside the reference delta matches the previous reference. DeepSeek then changed the reference.

In both the old reference and vLLM, `find_last_user_index` treated the user message built by merging tool results as the latest user turn. `drop_thinking` keeps reasoning only after that index, so it dropped the reasoning of the assistant message that had issued the call, partway through its own turn. That is not what the model sees in DeepSeek's agentic loops.

Example (thinking mode, no `tools`, `drop_thinking` default): `[user q1, assistant a1 (reasoning r1), user q2, assistant (reasoning r2, calls lookup), tool]`

```text
before: <｜User｜>q2<｜Assistant｜></think>\n\n<｜DSML｜ calls>…<｜User｜><tool_result>value</tool_result><｜Assistant｜><think>
after:  <｜User｜>q2<｜Assistant｜><think>r2</think>\n\n<｜DSML｜ calls>…<｜User｜><tool_result>value</tool_result><｜Assistant｜><think>
```

`r1` belongs to a completed turn and is still dropped. `r2` belongs to the turn in progress and is now kept.

**Changes.**

| Reference change | vLLM |
|---|---|
| Tool-result-only user messages do not start a turn | `find_last_user_index` in `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v41_encoding.py`. Rust: new `starts_user_turn` in `rust/src/chat/src/renderer/deepseek.rs`, used for both the last-user render index and the historical-developer boundary, and gated to the V4.1 dialect (V4 unchanged). |
| Keep tool `content_blocks` / list content; use user list content as blocks | `merge_tool_messages`. The OpenAI path already flattens list content in `_normalize_messages`, so this only affects callers that pass encoder-format messages directly. |
| Validate image placeholder tokens on every message before merging | `_normalize_messages` in `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v41.py` rejects `<｜deepseek_image｜>` in string content, text parts and reasoning, for every role, before image parts become placeholders. |
| Merge/sort before image collection | `encode_messages` merges `context` before the joint call-order sort. Prompts are unchanged, but the encoder no longer mutates the caller's `context` dicts. |

**Who is affected.** Only thinking-mode requests with `drop_thinking` in effect, which means no `tools` declared (declaring tools already disables `drop_thinking`), and whose conversation contains tool results. With tools declared, prompts are byte-identical to before. The placeholder check turns requests that contain a literal `<｜deepseek_image｜>` in text into 400s. Existing serving controls are unchanged: thinking defaults, `reasoning_effort` (including `xhigh` and `"none"`), `drop_thinking`, and tools attached to the first system message.

**Performance (second and third commits).** Deciding whether a user-content block starts a turn now looks at the whole block. On its own, the first commit made that check quadratic in both frontends. Neither fix changes the rendered prompt.

- **Python (second commit).** `render_message` calls `find_last_user_index` once per rendered message. Now that tool-result-only messages no longer stop that backward scan, each call walks back across every tool round since the last real user message, so agent loops render in O(n·k) time. The fix computes the index once in `encode_messages` and passes it down, as the V4 and V3.2 encoders already do. It also extends `test_encode_messages_scans_last_user_once_per_conversation` to V4.1.
- **Rust (third commit).** `starts_user_turn` scans the whole block for a user message, and the last-user `rfind` called it for every entry, so a block of k consecutive tool results cost O(k²). Sequential loops were not affected, because their blocks hold one tool result each. The fix evaluates only the first entry of each block. The resulting index is only compared with developer message positions, which never fall inside a block. On the 7,354-request corpus, the prompts are identical to those before the fix. `large_tool_result_blocks_render_in_linear_time` renders 100,000 parallel tool results in a debug build: about 0.13 s now, about 27 s without the fix. It fails above 5 s.

**Not in this PR.**
- **Python tool-result image order.** When image-carrying tool results arrive out of call order, the Python renderer attaches images in message order rather than placeholder order. The pre-fix reference had the same bug, and the Rust frontend already returns `media_order` in placeholder order. #60792 addresses this. Both PRs edit `_normalize_messages`, so whichever lands second may need a small rebase.
- **Tool namespaces.** The reference has supported them since 2026-09-10. They are not ported to either frontend, which is unrelated to this change.

---

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Fix DeepSeek-V4 decode on gfx11/gfx12 (missing inverse RoPE)
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4 decodes garbage on ROCm GPUs other than gfx942/gfx950. Prefill is fine. Affects every arch on the fallback kernel (gfx11, gfx12, …). Tested on gfx1151 only.

#57435 folded the inverse RoPE into the split-K sparse decode reduce, and `rocm_sparse_attn_decode` now returns how many rows it already rotated so `forward_mqa` can skip them. But only gfx942/gfx950 run that split-K reduce. Every other arch takes the fallback kernel, which never applies the inverse RoPE, yet the function still reports every row as rotated. Those rows never get rotated.

This PR reports rotated rows only when the split-K reduce ran. Nothing changes on gfx942/gfx950.

Tests: a new arch-agnostic test checks that the fused path plus the caller's pass matches the unfused path.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs for `rocm_sparse_attn_decode` and `inv_rope_positions`. No duplicate. #60154 and #61967 change the gfx942/gfx950 decode paths, not this return value.

## Test Result

`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` on 2× Strix Halo / gfx1151, TP=2, ROCm nightly wheel, `--enforce-eager`, greedy.

**Before:**

```
"What is the capital of France?"
-> We need answer (1) \n"**） * ... (so Paris</think> ** ( ) ) **

5 prompts with checkable answers: 1/5
```

**After:**

```
"What is the capital of France?"
-> We need answer simple. Capital of France is Paris. One short sentence.</think>The capital of France is Paris.

5 prompts with checkable answers: 5/5
GSM8K, first 25: 25/25
```

**`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`** (TP=4 over 4× gfx1151, main @ 39983a5e7): DeepSeek-V4.1 decode calls the same function with `inv_rope_positions`, and needs this fix too.

```
                                     before   after
5 prompts with checkable answers     5/5      5/5
GSM8K, first 25                      1/25     25/25
```

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py   (gfx1151)
  before: 1 failed (the new test), 56 passed, 74 skipped
  after:  57 passed, 74 skipped
```

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change. The submitting human has reviewed every changed line and ran the tests reported above.

title: [ROCm] Enable RDNA3 MXFP4 kernels on gfx1151 and for DeepSeek-V4
body:
> **Stacked on #46676.** The first commit is #46676 squashed and rebased onto main (authored by @JartX, unchanged apart from one enum conflict). **Only the second commit is new in this PR.** I'll rebase onto main once #46676 merges.

## Purpose

#46676 adds native MXFP4 kernels for gfx1100. gfx1151 (Strix Halo / Radeon 8060S) has the same WMMA and dot instructions, and the kernels compile to identical code on both, but #46676 gates them to gfx1100 only. On top of #46676, this PR:

- Opens the gfx1100 gates to gfx1151: the two kernel files, the CMake source gate, and the dense + MoE support checks.
- On gfx1151, uses the scalar `bsm=4` tile instead of WMMA-16 for steps of 16+ rows. WMMA-16 is 1.5–57× slower there at every shape I tried (table below). gfx1100 keeps #46676's rule.
- Makes the backend reachable from DeepSeek-V4, which loads its experts through `Mxfp4MoEMethod`: `RDNA3_MXFP4` goes before `TRITON_UNFUSED` in its ROCm priority, and the repack uses `gate_up_interleaved=False`, because DeepSeek-V4 stores `gate_proj`/`up_proj` contiguously.

Tests: a new dispatch test for the gfx1151 tile rule.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs for MXFP4 on gfx1151 / gfx11 / Strix Halo and for `RDNA3_MXFP4`. No duplicate.

- #46676 is the base. This PR depends on it.
- #52970 (AITER on RDNA) does not touch the MXFP4 MoE path. The DeepSeek-V4 numbers below include it.
- #62197 fixes an unrelated gfx11 decode bug that makes DeepSeek-V4 decode garbage with either MoE backend. Both DeepSeek-V4 arms below include it.

## Test Result

All on gfx1151, with `_rocm_C` built from the branch. Unit tests ran on this branch; end-to-end runs used the ROCm nightly wheel (main @ 49cb2bbf7) + #46676 + the new commit, `--enforce-eager`.

```
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_rdna3.py           24 passed (all skipped before)
       tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_rdna3_dispatch.py  223 passed
       tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_kernel_selection.py 27 passed
```

TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR= ```
This is a CPU-only box. The reproduction drives only the `Scheduler` and `KVCacheManager`, which are plain Python. ### 🐛 Describe the bug With HiSparse and async KV loads, two loads can both be admitted under `scheduler_reserve_full_isl` and then never run once both loads finish. The older one is at the head of `kv_holding_waiting` and needs more host blocks than are free. The waiting pass stops there, so the newer one, which would fit, is never tried. Nothing is running, so nothing frees host blocks, and every later step schedules nothing. Setup: a host pool of 6 blocks (1 null, 5 usable), `max_model_len` of 4 pages, so `min_host_blocks` (`vllm/v1/hisparse/layout.py:250`) is 6 and the pool is accepted. Ample GPU blocks, and an async connector that reports 2 matched pages per request. 1. A1 has a 4-page prompt. 4 <= 5 free, so it is admitted and takes 2 host blocks, leaving 3. 2. A2 has a 3-page prompt. 3 <= 3 free, so it is admitted and takes 2, leaving 1. A1 still needs 2 more host pages, but nothing is reserved for that. 3. Both loads finish. A1 needs 2 host blocks and 1 is free, so `allocate_slots` returns `None` and the loop breaks. A2 needs 1 and is never reached. Reproduction (CPU, no model, standalone version of the scheduler test helpers):
repro.py ```python """HiSparse: two async KV loads admitted under scheduler_reserve_full_isl can stall the scheduler on host capacity with nothing running. Host pool of 6 blocks (1 null + 5 usable), max_model_len of 4 pages, ample GPU blocks, an async connector that reports 2 matched pages per request. A1: 4-page prompt, admitted at 5 free host blocks, allocates 2 -> 3 free A2: 3-page prompt, admitted at 3 free host blocks, allocates 2 -> 1 free (nothing is reserved for A1's remaining 2 host pages) Both loads finish. A1 is at the head of kv_holding_waiting and needs 2 host blocks with 1 free, so allocate_slots returns None and the waiting pass stops. A2 needs 1 and would fit, but is never tried. Nothing runs, so nothing frees host blocks. Runs on CPU with the Scheduler and KVCacheManager only; no model is loaded. Pass a host pool size as argv[1] to compare (7 schedules A1). """ import os import sys import tempfile from math import lcm os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE", "cpu") import torch # noqa: E402 import vllm # noqa: E402 from vllm.config import ( # noqa: E402 CacheConfig, KVTransferConfig, ModelConfig, SchedulerConfig, VllmConfig, ) from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.factory import ( # noqa: E402 KVConnectorFactory, ) from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.base import ( # noqa: E402 KVConnectorBase_V1, KVConnectorMetadata, ) from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams # noqa: E402 from vllm.utils.hashing import sha256 # noqa: E402 from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_manager import KVCacheManager # noqa: E402 from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import ( # noqa: E402 get_request_block_hasher, init_none_hash, ) from vllm.v1.core.sched.scheduler import Scheduler # noqa: E402 from vllm.v1.core.single_type_kv_cache_manager import ( # noqa: E402 register_all_kvcache_specs, ) from vllm.v1.hisparse.coordinator import get_hisparse_coordinator # noqa: E402 from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import ( # noqa: E402 FullAttentionSpec, HiSparseHotSpec, HiSparseResidentSpec, KVCacheConfig, KVCacheGroupRole, KVCacheGroupSpec, ) from vllm.v1.request import Request # noqa: E402 from vllm.v1.structured_output import StructuredOutputManager # noqa: E402 B = 16 # tokens per page MATCHED_PAGES = 2 HOST_BLOCKS = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 6 MAX_MODEL_LEN = 4 * B class AsyncLoadConnector(KVConnectorBase_V1): """Reports MATCHED_PAGES external pages per request, loaded asynchronously.""" def get_num_new_matched_tokens(self, request, num_computed_tokens): return MATCHED_PAGES * B, True def update_state_after_alloc(self, request, blocks, num_external_tokens): pass def build_connector_meta(self, scheduler_output): return KVConnectorMetadata() def start_load_kv(self, kv_caches, finished_req_ids): pass def wait_for_layer_load(self, layer_name): pass def save_kv_layer(self, layer_name, kv_layer, attn_metadata, **kwargs): pass def wait_for_save(self): pass if __name__ == "__main__": sys.modules.setdefault("repro_connector", sys.modules["__main__"]) KVConnectorFactory.register_connector( "AsyncLoadConnector", "repro_connector", "AsyncLoadConnector" ) def make_scheduler(model_dir): model_config = ModelConfig( model=model_dir, dtype="float16", seed=42, skip_tokenizer_init=True, max_model_len=MAX_MODEL_LEN, ) scheduler_config = SchedulerConfig( max_num_seqs=16, max_num_batched_tokens=8192, max_model_len=MAX_MODEL_LEN, enable_chunked_prefill=True, is_encoder_decoder=False, watermark=0.0, ) cache_config = CacheConfig(block_size=B, enable_prefix_caching=False) vllm_config = VllmConfig( scheduler_config=scheduler_config, model_config=model_config, cache_config=cache_config, kv_transfer_config=KVTransferConfig( kv_connector="AsyncLoadConnector", kv_role="kv_both" ), ) spec = FullAttentionSpec( block_size=B, num_kv_heads=1, head_size=1, dtype=torch.float32 ) base_config = KVCacheConfig( num_blocks=10000, kv_cache_tensors=[], kv_cache_groups=[KVCacheGroupSpec(["layer"], spec)], ) cache_config.num_gpu_blocks = 10000 register_all_kvcache_specs(vllm_config) return Scheduler( vllm_config=vllm_config, kv_cache_config=base_config, block_size=B, log_stats=True, structured_output_manager=StructuredOutputManager(vllm_config), ) def make_hisparse_manager(num_gpu_blocks, host_blocks): source = FullAttentionSpec( block_size=B, num_kv_heads=1, head_size=1, dtype=torch.float32 ) groups = [ KVCacheGroupSpec( ["source"], source, role=KVCacheGroupRole.HISPARSE_SOURCE, host_resident=True, ), KVCacheGroupSpec( ["indexer"], source, enable_kv_transfer=False, role=KVCacheGroupRole.HISPARSE_INDEXER, ), KVCacheGroupSpec( ["resident"], HiSparseResidentSpec(block_size=B, page_size=B * 4), enable_kv_transfer=False, ), KVCacheGroupSpec( ["hot"], HiSparseHotSpec(block_size=B, page_size=B * 4, blocks_per_request=2), enable_kv_transfer=False, ), ] config = KVCacheConfig( num_blocks=num_gpu_blocks, hisparse_host_num_blocks=host_blocks, kv_cache_tensors=[], kv_cache_groups=groups, ) manager = KVCacheManager( config, max_model_len=MAX_MODEL_LEN, max_in_flight_tokens=None, enable_caching=False, hash_block_size=B, scheduler_block_size=lcm(*(g.kv_cache_spec.block_size for g in groups)), ) get_hisparse_coordinator(manager) return manager def make_request(request_id, prompt_token_ids): params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=17) params.update_from_generation_config({}, eos_token_id=100) return Request( request_id=request_id, prompt_token_ids=prompt_token_ids, sampling_params=params, pooling_params=None, block_hasher=get_request_block_hasher(B, sha256), ) def main(): init_none_hash(sha256) print("vllm:", vllm.__version__) print(f"host pool: {HOST_BLOCKS} blocks, max_model_len: {MAX_MODEL_LEN}") with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as model_dir: with open(os.path.join(model_dir, "config.json"), "w") as f: f.write('{"architectures": ["OPTForCausalLM"], "model_type": "opt"}') scheduler = make_scheduler(model_dir) manager = make_hisparse_manager(32, HOST_BLOCKS) scheduler.kv_cache_manager = manager scheduler.kv_cache_config = manager.kv_cache_config print("scheduler_reserve_full_isl:", scheduler.scheduler_reserve_full_isl) host = get_hisparse_coordinator(manager).get_host_block_pool() a1 = make_request("A1", list(range(4 * B))) a2 = make_request("A2", list(range(1000, 1000 + 3 * B))) for r in (a1, a2): scheduler.add_request(r) scheduler.schedule() print( f"after admitting {r.request_id}: host free blocks " f"{host.get_num_free_blocks()}, in-flight loads " f"{sorted(x.request_id for x in scheduler._inflight_prefills)}" ) admitted = {r.request_id for r in scheduler._inflight_prefills} # Both async loads complete. scheduler.finished_recving_kv_req_ids.update(admitted) steps, scheduled_steps = 50, 0 for _ in range(steps): scheduled_steps += scheduler.schedule().total_num_scheduled_tokens > 0 print( f"observed: {scheduled_steps} of {steps} steps scheduled any tokens; " f"host free {host.get_num_free_blocks()}; " f"kv_holding_waiting {[r.request_id for r in scheduler.kv_holding_waiting]}; " f"running {[r.request_id for r in scheduler.running]}; " f"status A1={a1.status.name} A2={a2.status.name}" ) print( "expected: after both loads finish, at least one of A1/A2 is scheduled" ) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
Output on 0.31.0, followed by a control with a pool of 7: ```text python: 3.12.3 vllm: 0.31.0 torch: 2.13.0+cpu os: Linux-7.1.5-76070105-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 $ python repro.py max_num_batched_tokens (8192) exceeds max_num_seqs * max_model_len (1024). This may lead to unexpected behavior. Triton is not installed. triton-cpu is expected on x86 CPUs. CPU backend prefers block_size is multiples of 32, otherwise the performance is not optimized. Model Runner V2 requires Triton; using the V1 model runner instead. Turning off hybrid kv cache manager because `--kv-transfer-config` selects a KV connector that does not support it. Impact: hybrid SSM models (e.g. Jamba, Bamba) require HMA and will fail at startup without it; models with sliding window attention will run with reduced performance. To add HMA support to a KV connector, subclass `SupportsHMA` defined in kv_connector/v1/base.py (for MultiConnector, all child connectors must support HMA). Initializing KVConnectorBase_V1. This API is experimental and subject to change in the future as we iterate the design. vllm: 0.31.0 host pool: 6 blocks, max_model_len: 64 scheduler_reserve_full_isl: True after admitting A1: host free blocks 3, in-flight loads ['A1'] after admitting A2: host free blocks 1, in-flight loads ['A1', 'A2'] observed: 0 of 50 steps scheduled any tokens; host free 1; kv_holding_waiting ['A1', 'A2']; running []; status A1=WAITING A2=WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS expected: after both loads finish, at least one of A1/A2 is scheduled $ python repro.py 7 # control: one more host block max_num_batched_tokens (8192) exceeds max_num_seqs * max_model_len (1024). This may lead to unexpected behavior. Triton is not installed. triton-cpu is expected on x86 CPUs. CPU backend prefers block_size is multiples of 32, otherwise the performance is not optimized. Model Runner V2 requires Triton; using the V1 model runner instead. Turning off hybrid kv cache manager because `--kv-transfer-config` selects a KV connector that does not support it. Impact: hybrid SSM models (e.g. Jamba, Bamba) require HMA and will fail at startup without it; models with sliding window attention will run with reduced performance. To add HMA support to a KV connector, subclass `SupportsHMA` defined in kv_connector/v1/base.py (for MultiConnector, all child connectors must support HMA). Initializing KVConnectorBase_V1. This API is experimental and subject to change in the future as we iterate the design. vllm: 0.31.0 host pool: 7 blocks, max_model_len: 64 scheduler_reserve_full_isl: True after admitting A1: host free blocks 4, in-flight loads ['A1'] after admitting A2: host free blocks 2, in-flight loads ['A1', 'A2'] observed: 1 of 50 steps scheduled any tokens; host free 0; kv_holding_waiting ['A2']; running ['A1']; status A1=RUNNING A2=WAITING expected: after both loads finish, at least one of A1/A2 is scheduled ``` The stall needs A1's load to finish no later than A2's. If A2 finishes first, it runs and frees host pages. Expected: after both loads finish, at least one of them is scheduled. The config check that requires `scheduler_reserve_full_isl` for HiSparse says it exists to keep admitted loads from waiting on each other's host pages. Cause, at main `21e09ea95`: - `vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:2271-2277`: the HiSparse host manager returns the admission sentinel (`num_gpu_blocks + 1`) whenever the host blocks it needs exceed the host pool's free count. #59036 made the host pool a hard limit. Before it, host capacity was best effort and missing pages were padded with the null block, so A1 would have been scheduled. - `vllm/config/vllm.py:1866-1873` rejects HiSparse without `scheduler_reserve_full_isl`, relying on full-ISL admission to prevent this. - `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:1297-1306`: for async loads, `reserved_blocks` is computed from `_inflight_prefill_reserved_blocks()`. That covers the GPU side. For the host group, `_request_remaining_blocks` (3149) gets 0 back from `get_num_blocks_to_allocate(..., apply_admission_cap=True)` as long as A1's remaining host pages fit the current free count. So A2 is admitted against host blocks A1 still needs. - `scheduler.py:969-971` always drains `kv_holding_waiting` first, oldest first (`skip_request` at 959-965 and `prepend_requests` at 1462). At 1330-1336, `if new_blocks is None: ... break` ends the pass on A1. Waiting requests are never preempted. - The test added with #59036, `test_hisparse_admitted_async_loads_can_finish_with_nothing_running` in `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py`, uses 3 usable host blocks and two 3-page prompts. Only one load is ever admitted there, so the two-admitted case is not covered. This is in 0.31.0 through the cherry-pick of #59036 and is unchanged on main. Proposed fix: at async admission, subtract the remaining host pages of the requests in `_inflight_prefills` from the host free count, the way the GPU side reserves for in-flight loads. Alternatively, let the `kv_holding_waiting` pass skip past a host-capacity failure instead of breaking. A regression test with the shape above (pool of 6, prompts of 4 and 3 pages, 2 matched pages each, both loads finished) fails today. I can open a PR for this. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [ ] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Reject an empty conversation in every renderer
body:
## Overview

Renderers with their own chat encoding (DeepSeek V3.2/V4/V4.1) render an empty conversation to a bare BOS prompt, so `/v1/responses` with `input: []` returns 200 with text generated from nothing. This returns the same 400 that HF-tokenizer models already return.

## Claims

- An empty conversation now returns 400 `BadRequestError` ("Cannot apply chat template to an empty conversation. Provide at least one message.") for every renderer.
- Non-empty conversations are unchanged, including Responses requests with `input: []` plus `instructions` or `previous_response_id`.

## Validation

New `tests/renderers/test_empty_conversation.py`: the 3 rejection cases fail on `main` and pass with this change; the 2 controls pass on both.

## Details

`transformers` refuses an empty conversation in `apply_chat_template`, but the DeepSeek tokenizers override that method and skip the check. The check now runs at the start of `BaseRenderer.render_chat` and `render_chat_async`, after each endpoint has built its messages. The Rust frontend already rejects an empty conversation (`ChatRequest::validate`); this brings the Python frontend in line.

Claude Code used to create the new tests.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek V4.1 rejects reasoning_effort "medium" and "minimal" with 400
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `v0.31.0` serving `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` with `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41`
- Same code on `main` (`237d99b4af`), Python and Rust frontends

### 🐛 Describe the bug

DeepSeek V4.1 rejects `reasoning_effort` values `"medium"` and `"minimal"` with a 400, although vLLM's API accepts them:

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/responses -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash",
  "input": "Reply with ok.",
  "reasoning": {"effort": "medium"}
}'
```

```json
{"error":{"message":"DeepSeek V4.1 reasoning_effort must be low, high, xhigh, max, or an integer within [1, 100] in chat_template_kwargs","type":"BadRequestError","param":null,"code":400}}
```

The same happens on `/v1/chat/completions` with `"reasoning_effort": "medium"`.

This breaks common clients: Codex sends `reasoning.effort: "medium"` by default, and gateways that turn Anthropic `thinking.budget_tokens` into an effort (e.g. LiteLLM with a 2048-token budget) send `medium` too.

**Where:**
- Python: `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v41.py` only accepts the keys of `REASONING_EFFORT_MAPPINGS` (`low`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`) in `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v41_encoding.py`.
- Rust: `rust/src/chat/src/renderer/deepseek.rs`, `DsDialect::V41` matches the same four values.

DeepSeek V4 already maps these values instead of rejecting them (`minimal`/`medium` → `low`, in both frontends).

**Expected:** accept the full set and map it the way DeepSeek's API does ([thinking mode docs](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode/)):

| Requested | DeepSeek API uses |
|---|---|
| `minimal`, `low` | low |
| `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` | high |
| `max` | max |

Related: #52739 (open) adds a generic flag to map unsupported efforts to the nearest supported level; its default rounds down, which would map `medium` to `low` rather than to DeepSeek's `high`. #58316 updated the V4.1 effort values but kept the four accepted names.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend][Rust Frontend] Accept DeepSeek V4.1 reasoning effort aliases
body:
## Overview

Accept the standard `reasoning_effort` aliases `minimal` and `medium` in the Python and Rust DeepSeek V4.1 renderers. Fixes #62220.

## Claims

- Map `minimal` to the existing low budget of `50`.
- Map `medium` to the existing high budget of `75`.
- Preserve all existing named efforts, numeric budgets, precedence rules, and validation behavior.
- Keep the Python and Rust frontend implementations consistent.

## Validation

Focused Python tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py -q
```

Result: **32 passed**.

Focused Rust tests:

```bash
$HOME/.cargo/bin/cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-chat renderer::deepseek_v41 -- --nocapture
```

Result: **16 passed**.

All applicable pre-commit hooks passed:

```bash
PRE_COMMIT_HOME=/tmp/vllm-pre-commit .venv/bin/pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
```

No model or GPU evaluation was run because this change only affects deterministic frontend effort mapping and does not alter model execution or generated output.

## Details

The DeepSeek V4.1 renderers previously accepted only `low`, `high`, `xhigh`, and `max`, even though clients can send the standard `minimal` and `medium` effort values.

This change adds model-specific compatibility aliases in both implementations. `minimal` uses the same numeric budget as `low`, while `medium` uses the same numeric budget as `high`. Focused tests cover the aliases at the Python encoding boundary and through both the request-level and template-argument paths in the Rust renderer. Invalid names and out-of-range numeric budgets remain rejected.

No overlapping open PR was found through searches for `#62220`, DeepSeek V4.1 reasoning-effort aliases, and the affected Python and Rust renderer paths. Related PRs #52739 and #61094 provide optional generic, operator-configured mappings rather than this model-specific zero-configuration behavior.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Skip blocked requests in kv_holding_waiting to prevent host block deadlock
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #62217.

Under HiSparse full-ISL admission (`scheduler_reserve_full_isl`), admission reserves the request's full prompt against free host blocks at admission time, and only the imported prefix blocks are actually allocated while the async KV load is in flight:
1. Request `first` (4 blocks, 1 imported) is admitted against 4 usable host blocks (5 total including null block) and allocates 1 host block (leaving 3 free).
2. Request `second` (3 blocks, 1 imported) is also admitted because `3 <= 3` free host blocks, and allocates 1 host block (leaving 2 free).
3. Once both async loads finish, `first` at the head of `kv_holding_waiting` needs 3 more host blocks (cannot fit in 2 free), while `second` needs 2 more host blocks (can fit and finish).

Previously, when `allocate_slots` returned `None` for `first` in `kv_holding_waiting`, `Scheduler.schedule()` executed `break` instead of skipping `first` and continuing to inspect the rest of `kv_holding_waiting`, permanently stalling the scheduler with `running == []`.

Additionally, `test_hisparse_admitted_async_loads_can_finish_with_nothing_running` previously used `host_num_blocks=4`, which only admitted `first` (`admitted == {"first"}`) and rejected `second` at admission time rather than admitting both.

## Test Plan

- Updated `test_hisparse_admitted_async_loads_can_finish_with_nothing_running` in `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py` so both `first` and `second` are admitted (`assert admitted == {"first", "second"}`) and verified that `second` is scheduled and completes when `first` is blocked on host blocks.
- Ran `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py`.

### Credits & Acknowledgments
- Full credit to **@digit50** for reporting #62217, providing the standalone CPU reproduction script, tracing the interaction between HiSparse full-ISL admission (`scheduler_reserve_full_isl`), `_inflight_prefills`, and `kv_holding_waiting` in `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`, and pointing out why `test_hisparse_admitted_async_loads_can_finish_with_nothing_running` (#59036) only admitted one request with `host_num_blocks=4`.
- If @digit50 would like to open their own PR as offered in #62217, we are happy to yield/close this PR in favor of theirs or add `Co-authored-by:`.

title: [DeepSeek-V4.1] Enable Engram disk offload for memory-constrained nodes
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's Engram tables are about 197 GB, so they fit neither in GPU memory nor, with `cpu_offload`, in host memory on a 128 GB node. At TP=4, each rank owns about 50 GB of table rows on top of about 78 GB of weights. On an APU (Strix Halo, DGX Spark), host and GPU memory are the same RAM.

This PR adds `--engram-config '{"disk_offload": true}'`. The tables stay in the checkpoint's safetensors files:

- After loading, each rank memory-maps only its own row range, located through the safetensors header.
- Each step it gathers the distinct rows it needs through the page cache and copies them into fixed GPU buffers.
- The existing `_engram_lookup_kernel` (SORTED mode) runs over that compact table, so results are bit-identical to the in-memory table.

The gather needs the hash ids on the host, so the lookup is an `@eager_break_during_capture` segment. It runs with `--enforce-eager`, or with `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 -cc.cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`. Startup rejects other graph modes, the host-memory options, and models other than DeepSeek V4.1.

The change is in the shared Engram code and is not tied to a platform. It was tested on gfx1151 and should equally serve CUDA unified-memory machines such as DGX Spark (not tested there).

## Duplicate-work check

- #56757 (disk-backed DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram, NVIDIA-only) was closed unmerged.
- #59958 / #58815 / #58439 add file-backed PLE tables for Qwen4Exp on CUDA. This PR is an independent implementation for DeepSeek V4.1 and uses the same `disk_offload` name, so the two compose.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py -k "disk or reconstruct or matches_torch or rejects_empty or prepared_rows"
pytest tests/test_config.py -k engram
```

New tests check bit-exact lookups at TP 1/2/4/8 for single-file and sharded checkpoints, and a breakable-graph capture plus replay.

End-to-end: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` on 4x Strix Halo (gfx1151, 128 GB), TP=4 over Ray, `--enforce-eager`.

## Test Result

```
test_engram.py   64 passed, 12 skipped   (gfx1151)
test_config.py   49 passed
```

On `main` the model does not load on these nodes: the Ray worker dies pinning its ~47 GiB of table rows. With `disk_offload`:

| | |
|---|--:|
| table rows mapped per rank | 2 x 23.6 GiB |
| KV cache | 1.74M tokens |
| decode / prefill tok/s (tg128 / pp2048) | 11.0 / 208 |
| GSM8K, first 100 | 97/100 |

Graph mode is covered by the unit test only. On this cluster (RCCL over TCP), graph mode hangs on the first request in a collective; the same hang occurred with DeepSeek-V4-Flash on stock kernels.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change. The submitting human has reviewed every changed line and ran the tests reported above.
