title: [ROCm][Perf] MXFP8 emulation: run the dequantized weight through the platform GEMM
body:
## Purpose

Since #56560, `EmulationMxfp8LinearKernel` dequantizes MXFP8 weights to BF16 once at load time, but `apply_weights` still calls `F.linear` directly. That skips the platform's unquantized-GEMM dispatch, which a BF16 checkpoint of the same layer would use.

On ROCm, that dispatch (`rocm_unquantized_gemm`) picks the skinny wvSplitK / LLMM1 kernels at decode batch sizes, while `F.linear` runs the 1-row GEMM on large hipBLASLt tiles. This PR calls `dispatch_unquantized_gemm()` instead. On CUDA and XPU the dispatcher returns `F.linear` for the default backend, so nothing changes there.

This affects every MXFP8 linear on ROCm GPUs without native MX (all but gfx95x), for example the DeepSeek-V4.1 attention and shared-expert linears.

## Duplicate-work check

- #56751 (closed) added a skinny dispatch table for DeepSeek-V4.1 on SM100 only.
- #48427 and #59782 / #60169 / #60384 / #62088 add requantized or native MXFP8 paths on CDNA; none changes the emulation path.
- #51511 proposes disabling skinny GEMM on gfx1151. The results below are on gfx1151 with skinny GEMM on, and the output matches `F.linear`.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp8_emulation_linear.py
```

The new test checks that the output matches `F.linear` on the dequantized weight for the DeepSeek-V4.1 shapes at TP=4 and 1-256 tokens, which covers the wvSplitK, LLMM1 and hipBLASLt branches.

End-to-end: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` on 4x Strix Halo (gfx1151), TP=4 over Ray, llama-benchy pp2048 / tg128, mirrored A B B A in one server instance.

## Test Result

```
test_mxfp8_emulation_linear.py   36 passed   (gfx1151)
```

| | main | this PR |
|---|--:|--:|
| decode tok/s (tg128) | 6.87 | 8.85 (+29%) |
| prefill tok/s (pp2048) | 93.5 | 93.7 |

GSM8K (first 25) with this PR: 25/25.

Per-shape latency at 1 token, weights rotated through 128 MB so each call reads from DRAM as in decode (median of 5 windows; 2 and 4 tokens are within 10%):

| linear (TP=4) | N x K | main | this PR | |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| fused wq_a + wkv | 1792 x 5120 | 182 us | 83 us | 2.2x |
| wq_b | 8192 x 1280 | 117 us | 90 us | 1.3x |
| wo_a | 2048 x 4096 | 248 us | 89 us | 2.8x |
| wo_b | 5120 x 2048 | 430 us | 110 us | 3.9x |
| shared expert gate_up | 1152 x 5120 | 171 us | 55 us | 3.1x |
| shared expert down | 5120 x 576 | 38 us | 28 us | 1.4x |

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change. The submitting human has reviewed every changed line and ran the tests reported above.

title: [Perf][DSA] Rank the prefill indexer logits with DeepSelect in BF16
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With `sparse_indexer_topk_backend="deep_select"`, the sparse-indexer prefill path still upcasts DeepGEMM's BF16 MQA logits to FP32 and ranks them with `top_k_per_row_prefill`. This PR ranks the BF16 logits with DeepSelect directly, as decode already does since #56464.

## Claims

- On SM100 with `deep_select`, each indexer prefill chunk drops the FP32 upcast (`as_fp32_logits`) and its top-k gets 3.7x faster.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill, DEP2 on GB200, 8 requests per rank of 4,096 new tokens on a 128K prefix hit: 429.8 -> 401.5 ms per step (-6.6%), indexer 64.5 -> 30.9 ms.
- The selected top-k values are unchanged: BF16 widens to FP32 exactly. Which index wins among exactly equal logits was already unspecified (see #56749).
- Accuracy is unchanged: GSM8K strict-match 0.924 / 0.923 over two runs and passkey retrieval 20/20 at ~8K / 31K / 62K-token prompts (DEP4 on GB200).
- Default behavior is unchanged: only `--kernel-config '{"sparse_indexer_topk_backend":"deep_select"}'` takes the new path. DCP, XPU, other top-k backends and logits whose row stride DeepSelect cannot read keep the FP32 path.

## Validation

Top-k alone, one GB200, CUPTI, cold L2, median of 3 rounds. Rows of one query chunk over 65,536 compressed keys (a 128K V4.1 request) with causal row ends, top-k 512, random BF16 logits. Base is `as_fp32_logits` + `top_k_per_row_prefill`, new is `deep_select_topk(..., end=row_ends)`:

| rows | base (us) | new (us) | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 66.5 | 13.6 | 4.9x |
| 2048 | 414.4 | 110.1 | 3.8x |
| 4096 | 777.2 | 210.0 | 3.7x |
| 8192 | 1503.9 | 410.7 | 3.7x |

On every row both select exactly the values `torch.topk` selects; index sets differ only among ties at the 512th value, and all indices lie inside the row.

Prefill step, `vllm bench forward`, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with dummy weights, DEP2 on one GB200 node, `--case 'ds8x4k=8*4096@131072' --kv-len-jitter 0 --max-num-batched-tokens 34816`, no speculative decoding, FlashMLA MegaAttn with the MXFP4 indexer, `deep_select` top-k, rank 0 under nsys, ms per step:

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| step (bench median) | 429.8 | 401.5 |
| indexer logits + top-k | 64.5 | 30.9 |
| of which upcast + top-k | 39.4 | 5.7 |

The step numbers come from our DSv4.1 branch (nightly 49cb2bbf plus DSv4.1 changes outside the indexer); `sparse_attn_indexer` there is identical to main before this change.

Tests on GB200, same branch with this change:

```
pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k "deep_select or sparse_indexer" \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_tp_row_shard.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py
43 passed, 4 skipped
```

No new test: `test_deep_select_topk` and `test_deep_select_topk_preallocated_output` already cover what this path relies on (BF16 input, per-row `end`, -1 fill for rows shorter than top-k, output into a slice of a wider buffer).

Accuracy with this change (`vllm serve`, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 on one GB200 node, `sparse_indexer_topk_backend="deep_select"`, DSpark K=5 with standard rejection sampling, greedy):

| eval | result |
|---|---|
| passkey retrieval, ~8K / 31K / 62K-token prompts (20 each; 4K-31K compressed keys per row, well above top-k) | 20/20, 20/20, 20/20 |
| GSM8K, lm_eval 5-shot, max 1024 tokens, concurrency 32, strict-match (two runs) | 0.9242 / 0.9227 (±0.0073) |
| DSpark acceptance length over the second GSM8K run | 3.44 (48.9% per draft token) |

The GSM8K and acceptance numbers match what we saw before this change on the same model (0.9318 strict-match and 3.36 in a P/D setup).

## Details

- Multi-request chunks: since #61149, DeepGEMM returns compressed logits in which every row starts at column zero (`row_starts is None` on CUDA), so `end = cu_seqlen_ke - cu_seqlen_ks` is each row's full causal interval for any number of requests in a chunk. #57206 tried this before that change, limited itself to single-request chunks, and was closed.
- Duplicate check: #57206 (closed, see above); #62172 lets `cooperative_topk` read BF16 logits on the decode path; #60618 (WIP) fuses scoring and top-k for prefill in a new kernel; #56749 changes tie-breaking of the existing prefill kernel. None changes the `deep_select` prefill path.
- The logits chunk budget (`VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB`) still assumes FP32 logits; counting BF16 would allow chunks twice as tall and is left for a follow-up.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Report every transfer group as loaded in Decod…
body:
## Purpose

`DecodeBenchConnector` fills a new request's own blocks in every KV cache group, like a P/D transfer, but it inherits the base `get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids`, which reports only the prefix-cacheable groups (what a hash-addressed store holds). A bounded-replay sliding-window group (DeepSeek V4.1) is not prefix-cacheable, so the scheduler treats the window as not loaded and replays it on the first step of every filled request. That step becomes a mixed prefill step instead of a padded decode, and with DP it pulls every rank out of the FULL decode graph, so decode-only benchmarks with this connector do not reflect P/D decode.

This returns `transfer_group_ids`, the same as `NixlConnector` and `MooncakeConnector`.

## Test Plan

- New `test_decode_bench_connector_loads_bounded_replay_groups`: a full-attention group plus a bounded-replay `SlidingWindowMLASpec` group; the connector must report both groups. It fails without the fix (`(0,) == (0, 1)`).
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_decode_bench_connector.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py`

## Test Result

44 passed (30 in test_decode_bench_connector.py, 14 in test_prefix_replay.py).

title: [XPU] Enable spec-decode adaptive verification without a confidence head
body:
## Overview

PR #52228 provides support adaptive verification without a confidence head and this PR enable it for XPU path. We identified perf gap caused by FA kernel and can be addressed by PR [647](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels/pull/647). With these 2 PRs, we got below bench results:

## Performance Summary

Benchmarked Muse-Glimmer-30B + DFlash2 on **8 Intel Arc Pro B60 GPUs (TP8)**,
comparing adaptive verification enabled/disabled at K=3/5/7.

Server launch:
```
ADAPTIVE=true

"${VLLM[@]}" serve "$MODEL" \
  --served-model-name "$MODEL" --port 8000 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config "{
    \"method\":\"dflash\",
    \"model\":\"z-lab/Muse-Glimmer-30B-DFlash2\",
    \"attention_backend\":\"FLASH_ATTN\",
    \"num_speculative_tokens\":${K},
    \"draft_sample_method\":\"probabilistic\",
    \"enable_adaptive_verification\":${ADAPTIVE}
  }"
```

Output throughput change with adaptive verification enabled, relative to
disabled at the same K:

| Workload | K3 | K5 | K7 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SPEED, high entropy, BS24 | -2.59% | +5.40% | +6.25% |
| SPEED, low entropy, BS24 | -4.99% | +3.81% | +2.21% |
| Sonnet, BS32 | -3.18% | +11.10% | +11.70% |

- **SPEED:** 12 configurations, 512 requests/configuration, 512 output
  tokens/request. Adaptive verification improves K5/K7 throughput, while K3
  without adaptive remains the fastest measured configuration.
- **Sonnet:** 6 configurations, 96 requests/configuration, 2048 output
  tokens/request. K5 + adaptive achieves the highest throughput
  (**468.55 tok/s**), 2.80% above K3 without adaptive. Mean E2E latency decreases
  by **8.17% at K5** and **10.98% at K7** versus their respective disabled controls.
- All **6,720 requests succeeded**, with zero failures.

title: [Docs] Add ROCm decode megakernel (MonoKernel) authoring guide
body:
## Summary

Adds a single developer guide, **`docs/design/rocm_decode_megakernel.md`**, documenting how to
write a **decode megakernel** ("MonoKernel" / specialized decode) for a dense transformer on AMD
ROCm (MI300X / MI355X, CDNA3 / CDNA4) inside vLLM — the technique behind the in-flight AMD mono
decode work (DeepSeek-V4.1 #60397/#61082, Qwen3.8-27B dense #61573, Kimi-K3 #60683/#61435,
GLM-5.2 #60889) and the NVIDIA CuTeDSL specialized decode (#61867), standardized by RFC #60904.

It is **top-down**: architecture → compute contract → toolchain → a from-zero FlyDSL bootcamp →
step-by-step implementation → testing → an executable task breakdown → pitfalls → reference
appendices. It uses a **Gemma-style dense FP8 model as the worked example** (the closest template
is the dense Qwen3.8-27B path), but the technique sections are model-agnostic.

> **Status: DRAFT.** This lands the material as one page so reviewers can react to the content and
> agree on its home/vocabulary; a proposed multi-page split to fit the docs layout is below and
> would be done as a follow-up (or folded into this PR) once there's agreement.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- Checked `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search "<mono decode / megakernel /
  specialized decode / kernel authoring> docs/guide in:title"` and
  `gh issue view 60904` — **no existing documentation PR** covers this.
- RFC **#60904** ("A standard for Specialized (MonoKernels) Decodes in vllm/models") is the
  umbrella design discussion; the related PRs (#60397, #61573, #60683, #60889, #61311, #61867…)
  are **code**, not end-to-end authoring documentation. This page is the missing how-to that ties
  them together and points readers at the canonical sources.

## Proposed split (the analysis requested)

The page is intentionally one file today, but it maps cleanly onto vLLM's docs conventions, which
separate **`docs/design/`** ("how it works" — e.g. `paged_attention.md`, `cuda_graphs.md`,
`model_runner_v2.md`, `fused_moe_modular_kernel.md`) from **`docs/contributing/`** ("how to build"
— e.g. `model/`, `profiling.md`). A megakernel guide has both halves, so the natural seam is:

**`docs/design/specialized_decode/`** — conceptual
| Page | From current parts | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `index.md` | Part 0 (TL;DR) + Part 1 | What/why, the AMD mono family, execution model, tagged-mailbox + peer-memory sync, the K1/K2 split, where it plugs into vLLM |
| `compute_contract.md` | Part 2 | What to fuse (model-agnostic) + the Gemma dense worked example |
| `toolchain.md` | Part 3 | FlyDSL, the reusable device primitives, CDNA3/4 hardware contract, AITER |

**`docs/contributing/specialized_decode/`** — how-to
| Page | From current parts | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `index.md` | new (scope/prereqs + links) | Entry point, prerequisites, nav |
| `flydsl_bootcamp.md` | Part 3.5 | EX0–EX7 hands-on warm-ups (write → run → measure → understand) |
| `implementation.md` | Part 4 | Steps A–K (directory layout, eligibility, build keys, K1/K2, runner, TP, integration, warm-up, fail-stop) |
| `testing.md` | Part 5 | Numerics / accuracy / performance validation |
| `task_breakdown.md` | Part 6 | The milestone checklist |
| `pitfalls.md` | Part 7 | Gotchas from the real PRs |
| `reference.md` | Appendices A/B/C | File map, PR index, external links |

Rationale:
- **Design vs contributing seam** mirrors the repo and lets each page carry a single `#` H1 and a
  focused nav entry, instead of this draft's many `# PART …` sections in one file.
- **`awesome-nav`** auto-includes files in a directory; a small `.nav.yml` per subdir would set
  order/titles. No root `nav:` edits are needed (the design dir has no `.nav.yml` and auto-navs
  today).
- **Vocabulary:** I used directory name `specialized_decode` to match the in-tree package
  (`vllm/models/common/specialized_decode/`) and RFC #60904's terminology. Open question for
  reviewers: prefer **`specialized_decode`** or **`monokernel`**? And should the conceptual half
  live in `docs/design/` while the how-to lives in `docs/contributing/`, or should the whole thing
  sit under one tree?
- **The Gemma example stays inline** (it's a teaching device for the technique), *not* under
  `docs/models/`, since the guide is about the method, not a specific model.

## Test plan / commands run

- `markdownlint-cli2 --config tools/pre_commit/.markdownlint.yaml docs/design/rocm_decode_megakernel.md`
  → **0 issues** (single H1, code-fence languages, blanks, table style, no bare URLs — matches the
  repo's CI config).
- Heading tree verified: 1× H1 (title) + H2 parts/appendices, proper `MD001` increments.
- Not run here (no GPU / full docs toolchain in this environment): `mkdocs build --strict` and a
  rendered-nav check — please let CI exercise these, or I can add a `.nav.yml` + run it in the
  split follow-up.

## Caveats for reviewers

- The referenced mono-decode PRs are **mostly unmerged and still converging** (the enable switch is
  moving `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE` → `--monokernel` → `--additional-config decode_backend` per
  #60904). The guide flags this and the stable-vs-in-flux parts explicitly; paths/flags should be
  re-checked against tip before anyone implements from it.
- Content is AMD/ROCm + gfx950-first; CDNA3 (gfx942) notes are included but secondary.

## Disclosure

**AI assistance was used** to research the referenced PRs/sources and draft this document. As the
human submitter I will review every line, keep it in sync with RFC #60904, and own it end-to-end;
the DCO sign-off should be re-applied with the submitter's identity before this leaves draft.

title: [Tool Parser] Fix truncated/unclosed DSML parameters and add incremental DSML arg streaming
body:
## Purpose

Part of #62051 (the truncated/unclosed-parameter rows only; the block with no invoke, the cut inside a tool name, and the V4 spellings are not addressed here, so the issue should stay open) and extends the `arg_value_extender` incremental streaming architecture (introduced for `qwen3_xml` in #62027 and `minimax_m2` in #62035) to the DeepSeek DSML parsers (`deepseek_v32`, `deepseek_v4`, and `deepseek_v41`).

### Problem (#62051)
1. **Unclosed / Truncated DSML Parameters Produce Invalid JSON on Stream Flush**:
   - In `_dsml_args_to_json(raw_args, partial)`, trailing unclosed `<｜DSML｜parameter name="..." string="...">...` tags were matched via `_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE` **only when `partial=True`**.
   - When `partial=False` (called during `extract_tool_calls(...)` or during `_flush_arg_converter()` at `</｜DSML｜invoke>` / `finish_streaming()`), `_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE` was skipped.
   - As a result:
     - **Case 1 (Truncated at `max_tokens`)**: During streaming, `converter(raw_args, True)` emitted `{"url": "https://example.com` (`prev_converted_len > 0`). On `finish_streaming()`, `_flush_arg_converter()` called `converter(raw_args, False)` which returned `"{}"` (length 2 < `prev_converted_len`), so no closing `"}` delta was emitted—leaving clients with invalid, unclosed JSON (`{"url": "https://example.com`).
     - **Case 4 (Model omits `</｜DSML｜parameter>` before `</｜DSML｜invoke>`)**: Non-streaming `extract_tool_calls` dropped the parameter (`{}`), while streaming emitted unclosed JSON (`{"file_path": "/tmp/a`).
2. **Quadratic Re-conversion of Long DSML Tool Arguments**:
   - Unlike `Qwen3Parser` (#62027) and `MinimaxM2Parser` (#62035), DeepSeek DSML parsers lacked an `arg_value_extender` and re-ran full regex conversion over `slot.args` whenever `>` appeared inside streamed argument content (e.g., code, HTML, shell redirects, markdown).

### Solution
1. **Consistent Unclosed Parameter Recovery + Partial Tag Holdback**:
   - Extract `_dsml_parse_args` so trailing unclosed `<｜DSML｜parameter ...>` blocks at the end of `raw_args` are recovered in both `partial=True` and `partial=False`.
   - Add `_value_end_window(text, value_end_re)` using `regex.fullmatch(..., partial=True)` against `</｜DSML｜parameter>|<｜DSML｜parameter\s+name=` so any trailing suffix of an open parameter value that could still complete into a closing or sibling parameter tag is held back during `partial=True` streaming (since `DeepSeekV4Parser` has no lexer transitions on `PARAM_START`/`PARAM_CLOSE` in `TOOL_ARGS`).
   - Hold back `_unwrap_wrapper_args` when `partial=True` and a single `arguments`/`input` wrapper parameter contains an incomplete JSON string, preventing premature streaming of `"arguments": ` before unwrapping.
2. **Incremental DSML String Argument Streaming (`_dsml_arg_value_extender`)**:
   - Implement `_dsml_arg_value_extender` for `deepseek_v4`, `deepseek_v41`, and `deepseek_v32`, streaming open `string="true"` DSML parameter values in $O(1)$ conversions with respect to argument length (reducing partial converter calls on a 200-line `write_file` call from 206 to 6).

## Test Plan

- Added `TestArgValueExtender` in `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py` (long 200-line DSML call with `>`, `<`, quotes, backslashes, and partial DSML tag lookalikes; $O(1)$ conversion count verification; #62051 truncated & unclosed parameter streaming/non-streaming parity).
- Added parametrized streaming and non-streaming tests for truncated and unclosed parameters in `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py` and `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v32.py`.
- All 279 tests in `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v32.py`, `test_deepseek_v4.py`, `test_deepseek_v41.py`, and `test_parser_engine.py` pass.

### Credits & Acknowledgments
- Credit to **@robertgshaw2-redhat** for reporting #62051 and providing the DSML truncation/unclosed-parameter reproduction cases, and to **@YaashuDave** for reproducing all five cases and analyzing `StreamingParserEngine.finish()` on #62051.
- Credit to **@deadstrobe5** (#62027, #62035) for designing the `ArgValueExtender` incremental argument streaming architecture in `ParserEngine`, and **@jayzuccarelli** (#58780) for prior work on incremental DeepSeek V3.2/V4 tool argument streaming.
- Special thanks to **@JohnZhao01** (#62290) and **@smiyamoto3** for end-to-end validation, edge-case reproductions, and review feedback on this PR.

title: [ROCm][Perf][MiniMax-M3] Enable the fp8 indexer cache on gfx942
body:
## Overview

Unlocks `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}'` for MiniMax-M3 on ROCm gfx942 (MI300-series, CDNA3). gfx950 (MI350-series) keeps its fp8 routing through the AITER indexer, and CUDA behavior is unchanged.

## Claims

- fp8 indexer cache now selects on gfx942: Triton scorers get an e4m3**fnuz** cache instead of bf16, with correct saturation in both index-cache writers.
- +32% KV cache capacity for the same GPU memory.
- Serving throughput is neutral at short context and better at long context; GSM8K is unchanged.
- gfx950 keeps the pre-patch routing (fp8 via the AITER indexer, e4m3fn/OCP convert); NVIDIA keeps e4m3fn, `constexpr` 448.

## Validation

8x MI325X (gfx942), nightly `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-39983a5e`, `EmbeddedLLM/MiniMax-M3-FP8-dynamic`, TP4, `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 262144`.

| run | log line |

| before | `MiniMax M3 indexer: selected Triton (no fmha_sm100) [topk_blocks=16, indexer_kv_dtype=bf16, sm100=False]` |
| after | `MiniMax M3 indexer: selected Triton (no fmha_sm100) [topk_blocks=16, indexer_kv_dtype=fp8, sm100=False]` |

KV cache (same `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`):

| | KV tokens | max concurrency @ 262k |
|---|---|---|
| before | 4,554,368 | 17.37x |

| ISL/OSL/conc | Out tok/s | Δ | TTFT p50 (ms) | Δ | TPOT p50 (ms) | Δ |

| 8k/1k/8 | 468.6 → 470.4 | +0.4% | 3540 → 3519 | −0.6% | 13.95 → 13.93 | −0.1% |

GSM8K (lm-eval 0.4.13, `local-chat-completions`, 8-shot, chat template, temp 0, 1319 samples):

| | strict-match | flexible-extract |

Kernel tests on gfx942 (`tests/kernels/test_fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py`, `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_fp8_triton_indexer.py`): **61 passed, 32 skipped (nvfp4-only), 0 failed**, including the new insert-saturation, foreign-flavour-rejection, and fp8-vs-bf16 top-k equivalence tests. 

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash

export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1

vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --model minimax-m3 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 8 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 \
  --save-result --result-dir . --result-filename result.json

pip install "lm-eval[api]"
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,model=minimax-m3,num_concurrent=16,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 8 --apply_chat_template \
  --gen_kwargs temperature=0,max_gen_toks=1024 --output_path gsm8k_out

python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_fp8_triton_indexer.py -v
```
</details>

## Details

Root cause, three pieces:

- `select_indexer_impl_cls` refused `indexer_kv_dtype="fp8"` on every ROCm platform, although the Triton scorers are flavour-agnostic (fp8 x fp8 accumulated in fp32).
- The index cache was pinned to e4m3**fn** (`torch.float8_e4m3fn`), which gfx942 cannot convert.
- The fused qknorm/rope/kv-insert writer picked its convert with `#if defined(HIP_FP8_TYPE_OCP)` — the macro is always defined (to 0 or 1), so gfx942 took the OCP branch and emitted OCP-labelled bytes that read back as wrong fnuz values (e.g. 1.1 -> 1.0, 0.77 -> 0).

The fix: the cache takes `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` (fnuz on gfx942, fn on gfx950/CUDA as before), the selector admits fp8 on ROCm gfx942 via the platform's `on_gfx942()` predicate, and the writer picks the flavour per target (`__gfx942__` -> fnuz) with saturation at `quant_type_max_v` (224 for fnuz, 448 for e4m3fn). Host checks expect the device's own flavour via the existing `is_fp8_ocp()`, and the Triton index-cache insert (AITER sparse-PA path) saturates at the same bound instead of producing NaN for out-of-range keys. gfx950's fp8 path keeps going through the AITER indexer (`SUPPORTED_ARCHS=("gfx950",)`), selected before this fallback is consulted.

Not a duplicate: the closest open PRs touching this area (#60930 CuTe prefill scorer, #59979/#59980 FMHA/MSA) are NVIDIA-side work; none enable the fp8 index cache on gfx942

AI assistance (GLM5.3-Flash) was used during the creation of this PR

title: [Bugfix][Core] Treat a shared-prefix junction as a set of positions under EAGLE
body:
## Overview

Fixes the shared-prefix junction under per-group EAGLE flags (#61455): with a dropping EAGLE group in the lookup, siblings that share a prefix get 0 prefix-cache hits under sparse retention (default `prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`). The junction becomes a set of positions, `{J - A, J}`, computed in one place (`junction_boundaries()`) and used by every junction consumer. This is an alternative to #62206, which keeps an extra SWA tail at `J - block_size` inside the SWA mask only.

The MooncakeStore side (store lookup as a junction source, `store_mask` as a consumer) is a follow-up PR stacked on this one: #62400.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP (retention 0): siblings that diverge 8 tokens past an aligned shared prefix of 3840 tokens get 0 hit tokens on main and 3584 with this PR. Siblings that diverge 160 tokens past it get 3840 on both.
- Shared-prefix GSM8K (1319 questions): the prefix-cache hit rate goes from 4.7% to 82.1%, and accuracy does not change (0.943 → 0.945).
- One helper produces the junction; all consumers read it: SWA and Mamba retention masks, the Mamba junction checkpoint, the scheduler's chunk stops (one per position) and `OffloadingConnector`.
- No behavior change without EAGLE, or when no dropping (non-Mamba) EAGLE group takes part in the lookup.

## Validation

**End to end** (GB200, 4 GPUs, base 83c9a547bf):

```
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'
```

Junction probe: requests A, B, C, D share exactly F + d token ids (F = 3840 = 15 × 256), then each has its own 1500-token suffix. They are sent one at a time; the table shows `cached_tokens` of C and D.

| d | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | 0, 0 | 3584, 3584 |
| 160 | 3840, 3840 | 3840, 3840 |

Shared-prefix GSM8K: every prompt is the same 3848-token prefix (instructions, 8 train exemplars, filler), then about 600 tokens of per-question distractor text, then the test question. 1319 questions, concurrency 32, greedy, `max_tokens` 512.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| accuracy | 0.943 | 0.945 |
| prefix-cache hit rate (`vllm:prefix_cache_hits / queries`) | 4.7% | 82.1% |
| `cached_tokens` per question | 0 for 1248 questions | 3584 for 1247, 3840 for 71 |

The per-question suffix is longer than the hit alignment on purpose. With a shorter suffix, a request's own prompt-end replay tail lands on the shared prefix and hides the bug.

**Unit tests** (CPU):

```
pytest -n 16 tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/prefix_cache tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_*.py \
  --deselect tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py::test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate \
  --deselect tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py
1695 passed
```

`test_swa_shared_prefix_reuse_under_zero_retention_eagle` covers uniform and mixed block sizes, with only the SWA draft group flagged and with all groups flagged. `test_mamba_shared_prefix_reuse_eagle_draft_group` covers a Mamba hybrid with a flagged draft group. The offloading scheduler test checks that every junction position is a reachable boundary. The flagged cases fail on main.

## Details

**Root cause.** The junction is where the longest single-group hit exceeds the reconciled hit. A dropping EAGLE group needs a peek block past its hit. So after #61455, a sibling that shares F tokens hits F in a non-EAGLE group but at most F − A in the dropping group (A = hit alignment). Main pinned only F, and no sibling can resume there.

**Why a set.** Where a sibling resumes depends on how far past F it diverges. Divergence of less than the drop unit past F resumes at F − A; divergence further than that resumes at F. When the drop unit is smaller than A (DeepSeek-V4: SWA block 64, A 256), both cases occur, so a single position cannot serve both. The junction is therefore `{F − A, F}` whenever a dropping EAGLE group takes part in the lookup.

**Why not #62206.** #62206 fixes the SWA mask only. The Mamba checkpoint, the scheduler chunk stop and `OffloadingConnector` keep the wrong junction.

**Supersedes the first version of this PR.** The first version moved the junction to `F − A` only. That lost the hit at F for siblings that diverge further than the drop unit (a regression with mixed block sizes). This version keeps both positions.

**Cost.** One extra retained tail per junction, only when a dropping EAGLE group exists. Without EAGLE, the junction is one position, as on main.

title: [Bug][KV Offload]: Direct-layout offload is treated as parallelism-agnostic, so engines with different TP sizes sharing a secondary tier load corrupted KV
body:
### Your current environment

4×H200, vLLM nightly `0.32.0rc1.dev100`, model `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B`, `OffloadingConnector` with `TieringOffloadingSpec` and a `p2p` or `fs` secondary tier.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

When two engines with **different TP sizes** share a secondary tier (`fs`, `obj` or `p2p`) and `canonical_layout` is off (the default), the reading engine can load KV written by the other engine and produce **silently wrong output**. Nothing errors, warns or recomputes.

**Root cause.** For a single head-sharded full-attention group on the V1 model runner, `build_offloading_config` marks the **direct** layout `is_parallelism_agnostic` (`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/config.py`, around line 179). The FS, OBJ and P2P managers then build their namespace with `parallel_agnostic=True` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/file_mapper.py`), which drops TP from the namespace hash. But a direct-layout CPU chunk is just each worker's page side by side (`|W0|W1|...`), not head-interleaved per-layer data. The same block hash therefore maps to bytes that mean different things under different TP sizes, and a cross-TP reader treats them as its own.

**Reproduction.** Llama-3.2-1B, gsm8k via `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/run_accuracy_test.sh` from #61846; baseline accuracy 0.332.

| Setup | Model runner | `canonical_layout` | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P2P, TP1 prefiller → TP2 decoder | V1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) | false | all tokens transferred, **accuracy 0.0, gibberish** |
| FS tier, TP1 writes → TP2 reads, same `root_dir` | V1 | false | 3072 hits, same namespace hash, **0/4 outputs match** |
| FS tier, TP1 → TP1 (control) | V1 | false | correct |
| P2P, TP1 → TP2 | V2 (default) | false | config fingerprint mismatch, 0 tokens transferred, recompute (safe) |
| P2P, TP1 ↔ TP2, both directions | V1 and V2 | true | correct (0.340 / 0.343), 5120/5120 tokens |
| P2P MLA (DeepSeek-V2-Lite), TP1 ↔ TP2 | V1 and V2 | true | correct (0.656 / 0.661) |

The V2 runner is safe only because the gate requires `not use_v2_model_runner`. The defect is the direct-layout portability claim itself, shared by every secondary tier, not anything P2P-specific.

**Expected behavior.** A cross-TP lookup on direct-layout data either misses and recomputes, or the engine refuses to start. It never loads bytes written under a different TP size. Sharing KV across TP sizes should require `canonical_layout`, whose pages don't depend on the topology.

**Fix.** #55191 removes the direct-layout exemption from the shared gate in `offloading/config.py`, so direct caches keep TP in their namespace for all secondary tiers (FS, OBJ and P2P). Cross-TP reads then miss instead of corrupting.

**Follow-ups:**
- A startup check: when a secondary tier is configured and `canonical_layout` is off, log a warning, or raise if cross-TP sharing is intended, so users learn that sharing across TP sizes needs `canonical_layout` instead of just seeing misses.
- An e2e guard that a direct-layout mixed-TP run reuses no KV. #61846 has an `EXPECT_TRANSFER=0` check for the P2P tier.
- `canonical_layout` is documented in the usage guide by #61822.

Related: #61886 (TP-agnostic KV offloading tracker), #55904 (namespace not keyed by KV cache layout).

AI assistance was used to write this issue. The reproduction results come from runs I did on the hardware above.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: Draft model construction resets data_parallel_index to 0 (load_draft_model / create_draft_parallel_config) — residual site not covered by #62062
body:
> **Correction (2026-10-18):** After review, the residual site described below is real but was **mis-scoped in this issue**:
> - It does **not** affect DFlash/DFlash2/DSpark. DFlash overrides `load_draft_model` and builds via `load_dflash_model(target_model, self.vllm_config)` — the config fixed by #62062 — and DSpark is covered by #62062 as well.
> - It only affects the standalone `method="draft_model"` path, and the code lives at `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/standalone_ar/speculator.py` (`StandaloneARSpeculator.load_draft_model`), not `draft_model/speculator.py` as written below (that path/class names came from a local build's layout).
> - The analysis has been consolidated into a comment on #62062; closing this issue to keep the discussion in one place.

---

## Summary

#62062 correctly fixes the `data_parallel_index` reset for the DFlash and DSpark draft **parallel configs**. However, tracing the same mechanism end-to-end, we believe one more site still collapses `data_parallel_index` to 0 on independent dense DP ranks: **the config under which the draft model itself is constructed** (`DraftModelSpeculatorBase.load_draft_model`), fed by `SpeculativeConfig.create_draft_parallel_config`. On a shared torch.compile cache directory this leaves the same cross-replica artifact reuse the PR describes, now via the draft model's own compiled modules. This is a code-path analysis finding; we have not isolated a crash attributable to this site alone (details below), and we would appreciate a maintainer sanity-check.

## Background / mechanism

- `ParallelConfig.data_parallel_index` is an `init=False` field re-derived in the post-init validator as `data_parallel_index = data_parallel_rank` (`vllm/config/parallel.py`, `self.data_parallel_index = self.data_parallel_rank`).
- For independent dense DP, each `EngineCore` gets `parallel_config.data_parallel_index = dp_rank` set **directly as an attribute** at launch (`vllm/v1/engine/core.py`, non-MoE branch), and then `reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank()` sets `data_parallel_rank = 0`. So the replica identity lives only in the attribute — **any `dataclasses.replace()` (or fresh construction) re-derives the index to 0**. This is exactly the root cause #62062 fixes at two sites.

## Remaining sites

1. `SpeculativeConfig.create_draft_parallel_config` (`vllm/config/speculative.py`) builds a **fresh** `ParallelConfig(...)` copying only pp/tp/EP/backend fields — `data_parallel_rank` defaults to 0, so `draft_parallel_config.data_parallel_index == 0` from birth, regardless of the target rank.
2. `DraftModelSpeculatorBase.load_draft_model` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/draft_model/speculator.py`) then does:

```python
draft_vllm_config = replace(
    self.vllm_config,
    model_config=self.draft_model_config,
    quant_config=None,
    parallel_config=replace(
        spec.draft_parallel_config,
        rank=self.vllm_config.parallel_config.rank,
    ),
)
```

The inner `replace()` re-derives `data_parallel_index` to 0 again. `get_model(draft_vllm_config, ...)` — i.e. the draft model construction, including DFlash2's `CandidateSelector` — therefore runs under a config whose `data_parallel_index` is 0 on every replica.

## Expected impact

Anything keyed on the draft config's `data_parallel_index`:

- **torch.compile cache keys for the draft model**: with a shared compile cache dir, replica N can load artifacts compiled on replica M's GPU — the same "cached restart loads artifacts compiled on another replica's GPU" failure mode #62062 describes (`CUDA driver error: invalid argument`), but for draft-model compiled graphs. We observed the sibling symptom on DFlash2 + `--data-parallel-size 2` (cross-device `mm` inside a compiled draft module during profile run), which the DFlash/DSpark sites' fix resolves; this remaining site looks like it leaves the draft model's own compile artifacts unsegregated.
- Any device-mapping code path consulting `get_local_gpu_index()` with the draft config.

We have **not** empirically isolated a failure caused by this site alone — flagging it based on the code path, since it sits on the same mechanism #62062 fixes.

## Suggested fix

One line in `load_draft_model`, after the `replace(...)`:

```python
draft_vllm_config.parallel_config.data_parallel_index = (
    self.vllm_config.parallel_config.data_parallel_index
)
```

Alternative (broader, as also noted in #62062's description): preserve `data_parallel_index` across `replace()` in `ParallelConfig` itself, or copy the target index inside `create_draft_parallel_config`. The one-liner is the minimal, lowest-risk option and composes fine with #62062.

A regression test in the style of #62062's `test_dspark_parallel_config_keeps_data_parallel_index` (capture the config passed to `get_model` in `load_draft_model`, assert the index survives) would pin the behavior.

## Environment

- Reproduced bug family on: vLLM 0.31.0 built from main @ `db9527a46` (2026-10-02), 8xH100 and 2-GPU DP=2 runs; the three sites above are byte-identical on latest `main` as of 2026-10-18 (verified by fetching the files).
- Related: #62062 (primary fix, open), #61827, #58984 (same DP x spec-decode family).

Happy to test a candidate patch (including #62062 + the one-liner above) on our H100 testbed with DFlash2 + DP=2 and report back.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Drop an incomplete DeepSeek DSML tool call at max_tokens instead of leaking it into content
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

When a DeepSeek V3.2 / V4 / V4.1 response is cut by `max_tokens` inside a DSML tool call, the Rust frontend returns the half-written markup as `content`, for example `…\n<｜DSML｜ invoke name="get_weather"` with `finish_reason=length`. This PR adds `ToolParserError::IncompleteToolCall` and drops the buffered text only for that error at `max_tokens`. Related: #62051 (Python parser, same class of problem), #62259.

## Claims

- A tool call cut by `max_tokens` no longer appears in `content`: DSML in content goes from 22/88 to 0/88 on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Earlier text and completed calls are kept.
- For every other finish reason (stop, EOS, a stop string), and for any other parser error, the buffered text still falls back to content, as before. The existing Gemma4 EOS-recovery test passes unchanged.
- With thinking on, reasoning that was emitted before the cut is kept, and only the unfinished markup is dropped: DSML in content goes from 32 and 35 / 154 on two base runs to 0 / 154.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (Rust 1.95, `main` @ `953fa442`; the same counts on `83c9a547`):

| Crate | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `rust/src/parser` | 578 passed | 583 passed |
| `rust/src/chat` | 357 passed | 361 passed |

`cargo fmt --check` is clean on the 6 touched files.

New tests:
- DSML cut at 4 positions, each at every two-chunk split. The positions are inside a parameter, inside `invoke`, inside the opener, and after `<｜DS`. In every case the earlier text is emitted, `finish()` returns `IncompleteToolCall`, and `reset()` holds only the unfinished markup.
- V3.2 and V4: a half-written opener (`<｜DSML｜function_ca`, `<｜DSML｜tool_ca`) returns `IncompleteToolCall`. The open-block case is covered by the existing V3.2 tests.
- A completed call followed by a truncated one: the first call is returned with its arguments.
- Ordinary trailing text is kept.
- `unified.rs`, four cases:
  - `IncompleteToolCall` at `length` drops only the buffer, and the reasoning and text emitted before it are kept;
  - a tool call that was already emitted is kept;
  - a different finish error at `length` still falls back to content;
  - with the real `CombinedParser` (DeepSeek reasoning parser plus the V4.1 DSML parser), `<think>plan</think>` followed by a cut inside the opener: at `stop` the half opener falls back to content, at `length` it is dropped. In both cases the reasoning `plan` is kept. This also checks that `IncompleteToolCall` is still recognised after `CombinedParser` wraps it.

**End-to-end.** Setup: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4×H200 with TP4, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-92044241`, `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`.
- `deepseek_dsml/mod.rs` and `tool/error.rs` are identical in 92044241 and `main`.
- The PR build applies the non-test hunks to 92044241. Its `unified.rs` differs from `main` only in an unrelated `timestamps` field.
- Each request has a `get_weather` tool. Greedy plus T=1.0 / top_p 0.95, streaming and non-streaming.

| Case | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Thinking off, cut by `max_tokens` 20 / 40 / 80 / 160 (88): DSML in `content` | 22 / 88 | **0 / 88** |
| Thinking off, cut by a stop string inside the call (`</｜DSML｜ parameter>` / `</｜DSML｜ invoke>`, 44, `finish_reason=stop`): falls back to `content` | yes (24 / 44 with DSML) | yes (27 / 44 with DSML) |
| Thinking on, `max_tokens` 20 / 40 / 80 / 160 / 320 with the tool, 20 / 40 without (154): DSML in `content` | 32 / 154 and 35 / 154 (two runs) | **0 / 154** |
| Same 154: empty `reasoning_content` | 30 and 35 (two runs) | 37 |

- In the stop-string rows, both builds fall back to content. The counts differ only by sampling: in the other requests the model declined to call the tool and answered in plain text.
- Untruncated tool calls still return valid arguments.
- Greedy outputs are not reproducible across server restarts here: two runs of the unchanged base build agree on 8 of 14 greedy samples. So the thinking-on rows compare counts, and the unit test above covers the reasoning check deterministically.

## Details

- **Root cause:**
  - `DeepSeekDsmlToolParser::finish()` fails while a tool-call block is open (`deepseek_dsml/mod.rs`).
  - The unified output path (`rust/src/chat/src/output/default/unified.rs`) handles a failed `finish()` by emitting `parser.reset()` as text, so the unconsumed DSML ends up in `content`.
  - The `calls` opener was already consumed, which is why the leaked text starts at `<｜DSML｜ invoke`.
  - A cut inside the opener itself (`\n\n<｜DSML｜ ca`) was emitted as text directly.
- **Why only `IncompleteToolCall` at `length`:**
  - `finish()` knows that a call is unfinished, not why. At `max_tokens` the buffer holds a call that was cut off, so dropping it is safe: there is no tool call, `finish_reason` stays `length`, and the client can retry with a larger `max_tokens`.
  - On any other finish reason, the buffer may hold malformed output (for example a missing `</｜DSML｜ invoke>`), and falling back keeps it visible. The same holds for other parser errors.
  - The drop is logged with `warn!` and the dropped length.
- **Scope:**
  - Only the DSML parser returns the new variant, so only DeepSeek V3.2 / V4 / V4.1 change.
  - Other parsers that report `incomplete … tool call` with `ParsingFailed` keep their current behaviour. They can switch to `IncompleteToolCall` in follow-ups, for example Gemma4, GLM, Kimi or MiniMax.
  - The error message text is unchanged, so the existing V3.2 tests that check it pass unmodified.
- **Known, unchanged:** on `main`, `CombinedParser::finish` discards output produced earlier in the same `finish()` call when the tool parser fails. This PR does not change that, and it does not trigger for DeepSeek: its reasoning parser flushes only reasoning or only content at finish. The combined test above covers this path.
- **Other open PRs:** the Rust DSML PRs #56302, #56334 and #58057 keep the `finish()` error for an open block, so they do not overlap with this change. #58057 composes with it.

title: [CI][ROCm] Run ROCm-capable tests that are currently skipped on AMD
body:
Removes or narrows ROCm skips on 112 test sites that pass on MI355, and wires the tests whose files no AMD step ran into the AMD CI steps. This is one draft that I will split into smaller PRs by area (engine/V1, kernels, models, CI config).

- Engine / V1: widen `is_cuda()` gates to `is_cuda_alike()` and drop stale ROCm skips in the worker, sampler, KV connector/offload, EC connector, DP and spec-decode tests (51 sites, 42 files).
- Kernels: unskip attention, MoE, top-k, mamba, mHC, compressor-KV and quant kernel tests; make the fnuz-gated fp8 references use `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` (39 sites, 28 files including `quant_utils.py`).
- Models and quantization: unskip the inkling, QSA reference, mistral3 patch-embed, mimo-v2 sinks and model-init tests, plus `test_compressed_tensors.py`, `test_auto_round.py` and `test_fp8.py` params (22 sites, 13 files).
- Where only some params fail on ROCm, the skip is narrowed to those params with a true reason instead of removed (4 partial sites).
- CI config: add the tests that no AMD step ran to the matching steps in `test-amd.yaml` and their `test_areas/` mirrors, and move `test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py` and `test_mla_backends.py` to the `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` command.
- No `vllm/` source changes. Tests that need a source fix stay skipped, and the fixes are listed below.

<summary>Test commands</summary>

```bash
# loop gate, per group (cwd tests/), single-GPU groups sharded over GPUs 0-5
for i in $(seq 10); do
  python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider <group selection> || echo "FAIL run $i"
done

# examples of the selections
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py kernels/moe/test_triton_moe_ptpc_fp8.py
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider quantization/test_auto_round.py
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider v1/attention/test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=6,7 python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider v1/distributed/test_eagle_dp.py

# collection and lint
python -m pytest --collect-only -q -p no:cacheprovider $(git diff --name-only -- 'tests/**/test_*.py')
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only)
```

</details>

- `kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py:1153`: inf garbage row poisons the per-tensor scale (ROCm/aiter#6275).
- `kernels/moe/test_shared_fused_moe_routed_transform.py:121`: stale against the MoERunner API on every platform.
- `models/kimi_k3/test_prefix_cache.py:54`: GPU memory access fault in the MXFP4 emulation MoE path.
- `models/language/pooling/test_token_classification.py:161`: workspace growth after lock (#48510).
- Flaky: `kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py:1055` (1 of 4 runs, aux-stream join after HIP graph replay), `v1/engine/test_async_llm.py:40` (`test_abort_final_output`, 3 of 5 runs).
- Needs a source fix: `jit_monitor/test_hooks.py:329`, `kernels/helion/*`, `kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py:326`, `kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py:215`, `kernels/test_relu2_fp8_quant.py:19`, `model_executor/test_jit_warmup_triton_launcher.py:122`, `models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py:197`, `v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py:889`, `v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py:120`, `v1/engine/test_abort_final_step.py:40`, `kernels/moe/test_moe.py:358` + `test_batched_moe.py:390` (TD path), `models/qwen4_exp/test_hc_ops.py:18`.
- No ROCm caller (pass, but ROCm never runs the code under test): `test_kimi_k3_mla_key_concat_kv_cache.py`, `test_kimi_k3_mla_fused_epilogue.py`, `models/kimi_k3/test_attn_res.py`, `test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py`, `quantization/test_auto_round.py:729`, `test_minimax_m3.py:1386`, `test_minimax_m3_fp8_triton_indexer.py`, `kernels/moe/test_unquantized_backend_selection.py:306` (the tests mock `is_cuda=True`, `is_rocm=False`).

Also found along the way: `test_engine_core.py::test_engine_core_tp` is broken on every platform with 2 or more GPUs (`num_cpu_blocks` is never set since 65b2f405dc), and `test_mistral3.py::test_mm_device_do_normalize` fails on ROCm with main's file, so the AMD command selects only the patch-embed test from that file.

<details>
<summary>Source fixes still needed (not in this PR)</summary>

1. `amd/quant_utils.cuh` has no bf16/half `scaled_convert`, so the Kimi-K3 ds_mla fp8 insert truncates instead of encoding.
2. `layers/mhc.py:71` initializes HIP in the parent on import, which forces spawn.
3. `benchmarks/forward/capture.py` records external events inside HIP graph capture, so replay hangs.
4. glm5next AMD KDA grid z = N*HV overflows 65535 (the NVIDIA copy moved it to gridDim.x).
5. `router/dsv4_topk.py` gates a plain Triton kernel on `is_cuda()`. It passes on gfx950, but needs perf and lm_eval before enabling.
6. `fusion/fused_act_quant.py` registers the ReLU2 static-FP8 producer only for CUDA SM90+.
7. `jit_warmup_triton_helper.py` disables parallel Triton compile on ROCm; the AMD LLVM abort needs a root cause.
8. `utils/jit_monitor.py` disables the TileLang hook on ROCm (#51159).
9. compressed-tensors `transform/module.py` calls CUDA-only `hadacore_transform` with no ROCm fallback.
10. `inc_mxfp4_moe.py` falls back to Marlin on ROCm instead of the AITER MXFP4 backend.
11. qwen4_exp `amd/ops/hc.py` does not accept `injection_logits=None`.
12. deepseek_v41 `amd/vl_model.py:343` materializes the whole checkpoint instead of streaming it.
13. `vocab_parallel_embedding.py` enables the fused embedding only on CUDA, though the kernel passes on ROCm.
14. `kernels/triton/activation.py:103` marks the `gelu_and_mul_sparse` Triton provider as CUDA-only.
15. `csrc/topk.cu`: `persistent_topk` is a stub on ROCm.
16. `BlockWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel.is_supported` returns True on ROCm without 128x128 block scaling.
17. fp8_e5m2 KV is advertised by ROCM_ATTN/TRITON_ATTN but not dispatched.
18. Helion has no `amd_instinct_*` tuned configs.
19. batch-invariant persistent matmul has no gfx942/gfx950 buckets.
20. Torch symmetric memory is gated to CUDA, although ROCm torch exposes `_SymmetricMemory`.
21. deepseek_v41 aux-stream event joins leave intermittently stale compressor state after HIP graph replay.
22. qwen4_exp `amd/ops/hc.py` registers the same `vllm::qwen4_exp_*` op names as the NVIDIA module.
23. `moe_use_td_hw_supported` returns False on ROCm, but the TD paths pass 10/10 on gfx950.
24. `Fp8MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading` normalizes to fnuz unconditionally, so reloading trips the e4m3fn assert.

</details>

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Preserve DP replica index for standalone draft models
body:
## Overview

Preserve the target DP replica index when constructing a standalone `method="draft_model"` model. This prevents separate replicas from sharing device-bound compiled draft artifacts and fixes a reproduced DP=2 warm-cache startup failure. Follow-up to #62285 and the standalone analysis on #62062; the root-cause analysis and suggested restoration were reported by @Siquan-Li.

#62062 currently changes DFlash/DSpark paths; this PR fixes the standalone `draft_model` loader and does not duplicate those changes.

## Claims

- Restore the replica index after draft config construction and before loading the model. General `ParallelConfig` semantics and sibling speculators are unchanged.
- Isolate draft compilation/AOT artifacts by replica. Existing loader regressions cover zero and nonzero target indices.
- Fix the observed warm-cache `CUDA driver error: invalid argument`; do not claim an accuracy improvement or serving speedup.

## Validation

61 targeted CPU cases pass:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/v1/worker/test_dspark_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py -q
```

The scoped regression without the fix fails for the three nonzero-index cases; rank-zero controls pass. It is part of the existing Buildkite `v1-executor-worker` suite. Scoped pre-commit checks passed during implementation; upstream pre-commit execution is currently gated by contributor eligibility.

[All raw commands, server logs, evaluation outputs/samples, benchmark outputs/per-request JSON and checksums](https://github.com/MuonChaser/vllm/releases/tag/pr-62301-validation-20261019).

GPU experiment: 2 H100 PCIe 80GB per arm on a shared host; Qwen3-0.6B as both target and draft; DP=2/MP, MRV2, BF16, compilation enabled, CUDA graphs disabled. Both arms start with a fresh shared compilation cache, then restart without removing it. Baseline cold serves successfully but warm restart fails in the standalone draft path; PR cold/warm both serve successfully. Reproduced over two separate cold/warm cycles per arm, with nonzero speculative acceptance on both replicas. The 16-request smoke outputs/finish reasons/token counts match across successful arms.

Full GSM8K (`lm_eval` 0.4.13, 5-shot, 1,319 questions, greedy, seed 256): default-mode accuracy **41.39% baseline vs 40.71% PR**. Unchanged-baseline repeats also varied (48/128 vs 46/128; prefix cache not reset). A separate `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` comparison produced identical responses for all 1,319 questions (40.33% each), with compilation still enabled. These controls do not rule out a default-mode regression; all raw results are retained.

Three sequential `vllm bench serve` runs per arm: 128 prompts, input 256/output 128, concurrency 8, 16 warmups, fixed seed 256; **768 measured requests and zero failures**. All six raw outputs are retained. Shared GPU load and repeated prefix-cache effects prevent an isolated-GPU speedup/non-regression claim.

Source is the full Python tree at main baseline `494663940b9b44f667c4f61c8c2407ba8e725ceb` and PR `b2303c5e49471603cd31c1904352ad7d99164dbd`, using official nightly native/build-supplied files from parent `3c13653738dad0acd877c23373816fefffbdd373` (PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Python 3.12.13). Native-source files do not change between the wheel parent and baseline; CUDA kernels were not rebuilt. This is not a claim about the latest moving main. Both arms disable the unavailable optional FlashInfer sampler/toolchain. Same-model serving/cache validation does not establish different-draft quality or broader model coverage.

## Details

Independent dense DP stores replica identity in `data_parallel_index` while its distributed DP rank is reset to zero. Constructing the draft config with `replace` reconstructs the parallel config and resets the index. Restoring the target index before `get_model` gives distinct `rank_0_0`/`rank_0_1` draft caches. No steady-state inference operation or synchronization is added.

AI assistance was used for implementation and to execute/document these validations. The detailed results were collected by the agent and do not represent independent human-run H100 validation.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][ROCm] MoRIIO: get the attention backend from the model layers
body:
## Overview

`MoRIIOConnectorWorker.__init__` re-runs the attention backend selector with the global cache dtype. DeepSeek-V4 sets that dtype to `fp8_ds_mla` at model init, and the selector call passes no `use_sparse`, so no ROCm backend matches and the worker raises at startup. This PR reads the backend from the model's attention layers with `get_current_attn_backends`, as the NIXL and Mooncake workers already do.

It is the one hunk of #48989 that MoRIIO READ mode needs, split out so it can land on its own.

## Claims

- Fixes the `ValueError: No valid attention backend found` that the MoRIIO worker raises for DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm, for both the producer and the consumer.
- No behavior change for other models. `backend_name` is only logged and sent as `attn_backend_name` in the handshake metadata, and no code compares it.
- Unit tests keep the same path: with no registered layers, `get_current_attn_backends` falls back to the same selector call.

## Validation

| Check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| The selector call of `MoRIIOConnectorWorker.__init__`, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 config, cache dtype after model init (`fp8_ds_mla`) | `ValueError` (below) | call removed |
| `test_moriio_connector.py` + `test_moriio_kv_layout.py` + `test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py` (ROCm, MI350X, mori installed) | 185 passed | 185 passed |

```text
ValueError: No valid attention backend found for rocm with AttentionSelectorConfig(head_size=512,
dtype=torch.bfloat16, kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla, block_size=None, use_mla=True, has_sink=False,
use_sparse=False, ...). Reasons: {ROCM_AITER_MLA: [kv_cache_dtype not supported], TRITON_MLA:
[kv_cache_dtype not supported], ROCM_AITER_TRITON_MLA: [kv_cache_dtype not supported]}.
```

<details>
<summary>Reproducer for the selector call (no model load)</summary>

```python
import sys
from vllm.engine.arg_utils import EngineArgs
from vllm.config import set_current_vllm_config
from vllm.v1.attention.selector import get_attn_backend

cfg = EngineArgs(model=sys.argv[1], trust_remote_code=True, kv_cache_dtype="fp8",
                 max_model_len=8192, enforce_eager=True).create_engine_config()
mc, cc = cfg.model_config, cfg.cache_config
cc.cache_dtype = "fp8_ds_mla"  # what DeepseekV4 attention sets at model init
with set_current_vllm_config(cfg):
    get_attn_backend(mc.get_head_size(), mc.dtype, cc.cache_dtype, use_mla=mc.use_mla)
```

</details>

- The unit tests ran in a ROCm 10 vLLM nightly container, with this branch's Python tree on `PYTHONPATH`.
- Not validated end to end on this branch. Our DeepSeek-V4-Pro 1P1D MoRIIO READ setup (2x MI350X) runs a nightly that carries a local workaround at this call site (retry the selector with `use_sparse=True`). The nodes are not available right now; I will add the E2E result when they are.

## Details

**Flow.**
1. `DeepseekV4` attention init rewrites `cache_config.cache_dtype` from `fp8` to `fp8_ds_mla` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py`).
2. `Worker.initialize_from_config` calls `ensure_kv_transfer_initialized`, which builds `MoRIIOConnectorWorker` after the model is loaded.
3. The worker calls `get_attn_backend(head_size=512, bfloat16, "fp8_ds_mla", use_mla=True)` with no `use_sparse`. Every ROCm MLA backend rejects the dtype.

The layers already hold the backends they selected. `get_current_attn_backends` reads them, so the connector no longer needs to repeat the selection with a partial set of arguments.

**Relation to #48989.** #48989 (@itej89) makes the same backend change, plus CI and Dockerfile updates, a spec-type check, WRITE-mode HMA changes and a `block_len` check removal. READ mode needs only the backend change. `MLAAttentionSpec` subclasses `FullAttentionSpec` and `SlidingWindowMLASpec` subclasses `SlidingWindowSpec`, so main's HMA check already accepts DeepSeek-V4's groups. #48989 has had merge conflicts since 10-15. If this lands first, #48989 can drop the hunk on rebase. @itej89 is credited as co-author.

**Duplicate check.** I searched open PRs for `moriio backend`, `moriio get_attn_backend`, `moriio get_current_attn_backends`, `moriio DeepSeek-V4`, `moriio fp8_ds_mla` and `moriio attention backend`. Only #48989 changes this call site.

title: [Rust Frontend] Add --reasoning-effort-map to rewrite request reasoning efforts
body:
## Overview

Rust frontend version of #61094: adds `--reasoning-effort-map`, which rewrites the reasoning effort a client sends into one the chat template supports.

## Claims

- `--reasoning-effort-map '{"medium": "high"}'` rewrites listed efforts; unlisted efforts pass through.
- Works for `vllm-rs serve`, the render server, and the Python-launched frontend (`--args-json`), so it follows #61094's flag once that merges.
- `reasoning_effort` in `chat_template_kwargs` is not rewritten (same as #61094).
- Unknown keys fail at startup.
- With the flag unset, behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

End to end with the render server on `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` (V4.1 rejects `medium`):

| Flag | `reasoning_effort: "medium"` |
|---|---|
| none | 400: `DeepSeek V4.1 reasoning_effort must be low, high, xhigh, max, ...` |
| `{"medium":"high"}` | renders the same tokens as `high` |
| `{"mediun":"high"}` | startup error: ``unknown variant `mediun`, expected one of `none`, ...`` |

Tests:

```bash
cd rust
cargo test -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd     # 468 + 82 passed
cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib             # 358 passed
cargo clippy -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

New tests: the map rewrites the typed effort but not `chat_template_kwargs`, args-json passes the map through, and an unknown key is rejected. `roundtrip_{qwen3,kimi_k25,mimo_v26}` grammar-replay tests fail locally, and they fail the same way on clean `main`.

## Details

The map is applied in `ChatRequestProcessor` before rendering and before the output processor is built, so chat completions, render and tokenize all use it. CLI keys are parsed as `ReasoningEffort`, which is how unknown efforts get rejected.

Not a duplicate: no other open PR adds an effort map to the Rust frontend. AI assistance (Claude) was used.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][ROCm] MoRIIO READ: skip zeroing READ destinations for mixed-precision caches
body:
## Overview

#59164 removes synchronous MoRIIO READ destinations from `new_block_ids_to_zero`, but only for models with Mamba layers. `needs_kv_cache_zeroing` is also true for mixed-precision attention caches (#47574). DeepSeek-V4 is one: its MLA cache is `uint8` (`fp8_ds_mla`) and its compressor state cache is `float32`. Its READ destinations are still zeroed on the compute stream, and the zeroing can run after the RDMA READ has landed. This PR applies the same exclusion to every READ group of models without Mamba layers.

## Claims

- Closes the race between zeroing and synchronous READ for attention-only models with mixed-precision KV caches (DeepSeek-V4) in MoRIIO READ mode.
- No change for Mamba hybrids: they still exclude only the aligned attention pages, as in #59164.
- No change for uniform-precision models: the scheduler sends no zeroing list, so the branch does not run.
- Local recompute tails, pages that are not READ destinations, and later allocations of the same pages are still zeroed.

## Validation

| Check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_update_state_drops_decode_recompute_tail_block` (the non-Mamba cases now expect the exclusion) + new `test_attention_only_read_skips_zeroing_in_every_group` | 3 failed | pass |
| `test_moriio_connector.py` + `test_moriio_kv_layout.py` + `test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py` (ROCm, MI350X, mori installed) | 183 passed, 3 failed | 186 passed |

- The unit tests ran in a ROCm 10 vLLM nightly container, with the branch's Python tree on `PYTHONPATH`. The main column runs main's code against this PR's test file.
- **Draft: not validated end to end yet.** Our DeepSeek-V4-Pro 1P1D MoRIIO READ setup (2x MI350X) closes the same race with a host `torch.cuda.current_stream().synchronize()` in `start_load_kv`, before the READs are posted. We did not A/B the race itself. The nodes are not available right now; I will add an E2E accuracy run (with and without this change) before marking the PR ready.

## Details

**Flow (decode side, one step, `--async-scheduling`).**
1. The scheduler allocates the new request's blocks. DeepSeek-V4's cache is mixed precision, so they all go to `new_block_ids_to_zero`.
2. `build_connector_meta` keeps the list unchanged, because `_has_mamba` is False.
3. The V2 runner's `update_requests` queues `kv_block_zeroer.zero_block_ids` on the current stream. The stream is still running the previous step's forward, so the zeroing kernel waits behind it.
4. `pre_forward` -> `start_load_kv` posts the RDMA READs from the host. The NIC writes the pages directly and does not wait on the stream.
5. If the READs finish before the previous forward, the queued zeroing kernel then overwrites the KV it just received.

**Fix.** `build_connector_meta` subtracts the READ destinations of every group when the model has no Mamba layers. The Mamba path keeps `block_ids[:1]`, the aligned attention pages. This is the exception that `KVConnectorBase_V1.build_connector_meta` already documents for synchronous READ connectors.

**Why skipping the zeroing is safe here.**
- MoRIIO READ copies `block_len` bytes per block (`compute_block_transfer_offsets`), so each destination page becomes a byte copy of the prefiller's page. The prefiller zeroed that page when it allocated it.
- The worker awaits every READ before the forward (`_await_reads_issued_this_step`; #60808 makes this unconditional), so no kernel reads a destination page before the READ has landed.
- `_reqs_need_recv` holds only the aligned destination blocks. The decode-side recompute tail is not a READ destination, so it stays in the zeroing list (covered by the existing test).

**Alternative considered.** A stream sync before posting READs (what our internal build does) also closes the race. It makes the host wait for the previous forward on every step that receives KV, so the READs cannot overlap it. The exclusion needs no synchronization.

**Related PRs.**
- #60867 (MoRIIO hybrid READ for several attention groups) changes the same set comprehension for the Mamba path to `block_ids[: len(self._attn_group_ids)]` and keeps the `_has_mamba` condition. The two compose. Whichever lands second needs a one-line rebase.
- #54301 and the async READ RFC #49643 avoid the race differently: async loads already pass `skip_zeroing_group_ids` (#59504).

**Duplicate check.** I searched open PRs for `moriio zeroing`, `moriio zero`, `new_block_ids_to_zero`, `READ destinations zeroing` and `moriio mixed precision`, and checked the diffs of #60867, #60808, #61726 and #54301. Only #60867 touches this exclusion, and only for Mamba hybrids.

title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Read only a group's own regions in hybrid SSM transfers
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

In hybrid MLA+SSM models, the NIXL hybrid descriptor path made every attention group read **all** registered regions. Some regions hold only SSM-layer pages or only scratch (`CircularBufferSpec`) pages, so each MLA block also re-read bytes owned by other groups. On GLM-5.3-Flash, about 38% of the bytes on the wire were duplicates. This PR records, per transfer group, which regions hold its layers and addresses only those.

Related: #57662 (dedup regions by `(base_addr, block_len)`) touches the same registration code. It is complementary, not a duplicate; see the Duplicate check below.

## Claims

- On GLM-5.3-Flash (fp8, TP2→TP2 P/D), this cuts transferred bytes by 38% at 100k ISL (2.18 GB → 1.35 GB per request), with transfer time ~20.5 → ~12.4 ms. Accuracy is unchanged.
- Layouts where every group spans every region produce byte-identical descriptors. This covers pure attention, non-SSM models and FA+GDN hybrids such as Qwen3.5 (verified e2e).
- An SSM group no longer reads SSM slots of regions that hold none of its layers, i.e. a group with fewer layers than the others.

## Validation

**E2E.** Prefill TP2 → decode TP2 on separate GB300 nodes, NixlConnector pull mode, fp8 KV, `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. The KV pool was scrambled, and each point was run twice.

| Model | ISL | Bytes / req (before → after) | Descs | Xfer avg | GSM8K through P/D (before → after) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.3-Flash | 32k | 859,615,744 → 565,391,872 | 950 → 646 | ~8.4 → ~5.2 ms | |
| GLM-5.3-Flash | 100k | 2,177,711,104 → 1,348,099,072 (−38%) | 2150 → 1306 | ~20.5 → ~12.4 ms | 81.8% → 80.6% (run-to-run spread 80.8–82.8%) |
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B (regression check) | 32k / 100k | identical (977,829,888 / 2,626,191,360) | identical (672 / 1440) | | 40.8% → 41.2% (non-P/D baseline 41.2%) |

Before the fix, a byte-level model of the descriptor layout reproduced all 9 measured points exactly (6 fp8 ISLs + 3 bf16). At 100k it predicts 1,347,815,936 B of useful data out of 2,177,711,104 B on the wire, i.e. ~38% duplicates and ~40% at 262k. After the fix, 283,136 B over the useful amount remain, which equals 2 × (143,616 − 2,048). This comes from the tail region aliasing an indexer region and being read at the indexer's block length. That case is the base-address-only keying that #57662 addresses, so it is intentionally out of scope here.

**Unit tests** (GB300 node):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_tp_mapping.py
# 621 passed, 6 failed
```

The 6 failures also fail on unpatched main, and all are environmental:
- `test_compatibility_hash_validation` ×2 and `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma[gemma]` (offline HF);
- `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller` ×2 and `test_nixl_keeps_packed_sparse_mla_manager_block` (FlashMLA module not available in the test env).

- New: `test_mla_hybrid_groups_read_only_their_own_regions[False/True]`. `True` adds a KDA-only tensor, i.e. a region without MLA pages. **Without the `base_worker.py` change, `[True]` fails**: MLA reads the KDA-only region (desc 9), and the second KDA group reads the extra layer's SSM slots. `[False]`, where every group spans every region, passes both before and after, as expected.
- Existing `_scratch_region_indices` assertions moved to `_group_region_indices[<scratch group>]`, which keeps the same values.

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.

## Details

**Root cause (P/D flow, pull mode):**
1. P and D each call `register_kv_caches`. Regions are keyed by tensor base address. On GLM-5.3-Flash, each rank registers 40 regions: 11 MLA, 11 indexer, 8 KDA-only (34 KDA layers vs. 11 MLA) and 10 `KPOOL_TAIL`-only.
2. D's scheduler gets the remote block ids per KV group and issues a read in `_read_blocks`.
3. `_compute_desc_ids` takes the hybrid path (`num_ssm_regions > 0`). Each non-scratch attention group used `np.arange(num_regions)` and emitted one desc per block for all 40 regions.
4. The 18 KDA-only and tail-only regions hold no MLA/indexer pages. At an MLA block id they contain another group's (aliased) bytes, which D had already fetched through that group's own descriptors, so every MLA block pulled them a second time.

**Fix:**
- `register_kv_caches` now records the set of transfer groups whose layers live in each region, as `_group_region_indices[group] -> sorted region ids` (`None` if the group registered none).
- Attention groups address exactly those regions. This generalizes the previous special case for `CircularBufferSpec`; `_scratch_region_indices` is removed.
- SSM groups keep the `[FA descs | SSM descs]` layout. They address only the SSM slots (`ssm_regions_per_layer` consecutive descs each) of their own regions. The PLE group and groups with no recorded regions keep the previous behavior.

**Why other layouts are unaffected:**
- Pure attention and non-SSM models return before this code, via the fast path (`region_group_ids` / `uses_region_group_mapping`).
- In FA+SSM hybrids where every group has a layer in every tensor (Qwen3.5, GDN), `_group_region_indices[g] == range(num_regions)`, so descriptors are identical. This was confirmed byte-identical e2e above.
- DSv4 packed rows, heterogeneous TP and block-size ratio operate on the desc list and stride (`num_blocks`, `num_fa_descs`, `logical_blocks`), which are unchanged. Only the selected region subset changes.
- Push mode calls the same `_compute_desc_ids`.

**Duplicate check:** no open PR or issue fixes this. #57662 is adjacent (region identity at registration) and touches the same block of `register_kv_caches`, so a small rebase may be needed depending on merge order. #52408 is a docs issue on the SSM region-count invariant.

### Reviewer notes

Please take a careful look at:
- **(a)** Remote-side descriptor ids are computed with the **local** group→region map. This assumes P and D have identical region layouts, the same assumption the code already made about `num_regions`.
- **(b)** The SSM branch assumes each SSM layer owns `ssm_regions_per_layer` consecutive descriptors, in `_ssm_region_indices` order.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to develop this change and write this description. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and e2e validation above.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: load checkpoints with quantized q/k/v and a BF16 QSA indexer
body:
## Overview

Fixes #62308. Since #59533, `Qwen4ExpForCausalLM.packed_modules_mapping["qkv_proj"]` lists `indexer.index_qk_proj`. Quant configs read that class-level mapping before the model is built, so they check q/k/v and the QSA indexer as one fused layer. Checkpoints that quantize q/k/v but keep the indexer in BF16 fail to load with `Found different quantization schemes for the shards of ...qkv_proj`.

This PR keeps the indexer out of the mapping that quant configs see, and fuses it into `qkv_proj` only when both resolve to the same quant method.

## Claims

- Checkpoints with quantized q/k/v and a BF16 indexer load again, for example `ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AWQ`. Their indexer runs as its own GEMM, as before #59533.
- No change for BF16, ModelOpt FP4, and checkpoints that treat q/k/v and the indexer the same way: the indexer stays fused.
- The `--enable-lora` mapping override is removed. It is no longer needed, and it never reached the quant config.

## Validation

End to end on 4x A100-PCIE-40GB (TP4 + EP) with the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image built from `1b2a666` (2026-10-18). Its `model.py` and `qsa.py` match this PR's base `371745e`; for "after", the two files from this PR were mounted over them. A test-only hook (not part of this PR) logged the fusion decision of every QSA layer.

| Checkpoint | Code | Server start | QSA layers (12 per worker, 4 workers) | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AWQ` (q/k/v W4A16, indexer BF16) | before | fails: `ValueError: Found different quantization schemes ... layers.3.self_attn.qkv_proj` | - | - |
| same | after | ok | 48/48 unfused: `QKVParallelLinear` (`CompressedTensorsWNA16`) + BF16 `index_qk_proj` | GSM8K 86.2% (n=500), 0 invalid |
| `cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-AWQ-INT4` (attention BF16) | before | ok | 48/48 fused (`Qwen4ExpQSAQKVIndexerLinear`) | - |
| same | after | ok | 48/48 fused, same layer and quant method | sample request ok |

The cyankiwi "after" run used the previous revision of `_same_quant_method`, which read `scheme` only from the quant method. The final revision also reads it from the layer, which matters only when both layers are quantized.

GSM8K (an API key header was added by a small wrapper):

```bash
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8002 --use-chat-completions \
  --model swift-1.5-flash-next-awq --reasoning-effort none --num-shots 0 \
  --num-questions 500 --max-tokens 512 --temperature 0 --max-concurrency 32
```

The default 5-shot completions mode does not suit this model family: it emits EOS right after `Answer:` once the prompt is longer than about 400 tokens, on vLLM and on llama.cpp alike.

- Unit tests (CPU): `pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_quant_indexer_fusion.py`: 7 passed. With the old mapping, the two mapping tests fail with the error from #62308.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: passed.
- CI: the new tests run in the existing Qwen4 Exp step. CI has no Flash-Next checkpoint with this layout (about 165 GB), so the end-to-end load is validated only as above.

## Details

- Root cause: `configure_quant_config` passes the class-level `packed_modules_mapping` to the quant config before `__init__` runs. Even the plain `QKVParallelLinear` built before fusion is resolved as a four-shard layer. The LoRA branch rebinds the mapping on the instance, so the quant config never saw it.
- Change:
  - `packed_modules_mapping["qkv_proj"]` is `["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj"]` for both model classes.
  - `Qwen4ExpQSAAttention` builds q/k/v and the indexer as before, then fuses only if `_same_quant_method` holds: the same quant method type and the same scheme type (compressed-tensors keeps the scheme on the layer, INC on the method). Without a quant config for the fused layer (BF16, or ModelOpt FP4 via `without_modelopt_fp4`) it fuses as before.
- Limitation: if q/k/v and the indexer use the same method and scheme class but different parameters (bits or group size), they are still fused, and loading fails at weight loading. None of the 82 quantized checkpoints in #62308 has this layout.
- I used AI assistance (Claude) for the investigation, the code and the tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and GPU checks above.
