`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-92044241` with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. The code path is unchanged on current `main` (`e80b6c64`). ### 🐛 Describe the bug A chat request that fails validation gets different status codes on the two endpoints. One example is a role the renderer does not support (`latest_reminder`, until #61446 lands): | Endpoint | Status | Body | |---|---|---| | `POST /v1/chat/completions` | **400** `invalid_request_error` | `chat role latest_reminder is not supported by this chat renderer` | | `POST /tokenize` (chat form) | **500** `server_error` | `tokenize failed: chat role latest_reminder is not supported by this chat renderer` | The request itself is invalid, so `/tokenize` should return 4xx, as the chat endpoint does. Repro: ```bash curl -s localhost:8000/tokenize -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}, {"role": "latest_reminder", "content": "be brief"}]}' # -> 500 {"error":{"message":"tokenize failed: chat role `latest_reminder` is not supported ...","type":"server_error",...}} ``` **Cause.** `rust/src/server/src/routes/tokenize.rs` wraps every error in `server_error!("tokenize failed: …")`, at three sites: - line 94, `tokenize_completion()`: the text tokenize step of the prompt form; - line 116, `tokenize_chat()`: `prepare_for_tokenization`, where the chat template is rendered, so an unsupported role fails here; - line 122, `tokenize_chat()`: the text tokenize step. The generation endpoints use `chat_submit_error()` / `text_submit_error()` from `rust/src/server/src/error.rs`. These map errors where `is_request_validation_error()` is true to `invalid_request!` (400) and keep everything else at 500. **Suggested fix.** - Use the same mapping at the three sites: `chat_submit_error("tokenize failed", e)` at line 116 (a chat error), and `text_submit_error("tokenize failed", e)` at lines 94 and 122 (text errors). - Add a test asserting that `/tokenize` returns 400 for an unsupported role. - Other request-validation errors, such as a prompt that is too long, get the same fix. Possibly related: `/detokenize` (line 136, `server_error!("detokenize failed: …")`) also returns 500 when decoding fails. If the client sent invalid token ids, that is a request error and should be 4xx. I searched existing issues and found none for this. This issue was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code); I checked the code references and the repro.

title: [Bugfix][DCP] Finalize the NIXL DCP interleave size before profiling
body:
**TL;DR**: there's a mismatch between the CG we generate at profile time and the one that runs for the Indexer. The mismatch is due to PD requiring adjusting dcp-interleave-size, so we move that adjustment earlier. I don't think cp-interleave-size is particularly interesting per-se, just any runtime config adjustment, even non-trivial like here where block size must be resolved, should happen before we fix CG shapes.

## Overview

With `NixlConnector` + DCP, `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` is auto-pinned to the kernel block size only in `ensure_kv_transfer_initialized`, i.e. *after* the profiling run. This PR finalizes the value in the existing per-worker pre-profiling hook (`WorkerBase.set_kv_cache_layout`) instead, turns the late adjustment into a fail-closed guard, and removes the indexers' caching of the value.

**Relation to #60671:** this fixes the same bug as #60671 by @andylolu2 (draft), which first diagnosed the stale value in `SparseAttnIndexer`; credit for the root cause goes there. This PR is offered as a **smaller alternative**.
## Claims

- NIXL P/D + DCP: every worker uses the final interleave size from the first forward pass (profiling, compile, CUDA graph capture) onward, so the sparse indexer and the attention metadata builders always agree.
- Fixes wrong sparse top-k (degraded or garbage outputs) for models whose indexer read the cached `SparseAttnIndexer` / `SparseAttnIndexerKpool` value with DCP, e.g. the `deepseek_v2` V3-with-indexer path and `glm5next`.
- Fixes a startup failure on Model Runner V2 for `glm5next` (GLM-5.3-Flash) with NIXL + DCP, where profiling builds the indexer metadata with the stale `1` and raises.
- If the post-profiling value would ever differ from the pre-profiling one, startup now fails with an actionable error instead of silently running with an inconsistent value.

## Validation

**Real weights, GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5next`, MRV2 default), 1x GB300 node, TP4 + DCP4, single instance with `NixlConnector` (`kv_both`), GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions:**

| Build | Config | Result |
|---|---|---|
| main (e80b6c642f) | NIXL, interleave auto | fails at startup: `NotImplementedError: DCP with sparse indexer KV compression (compress_ratio=4) requires --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size to be a multiple of it` (raised from the indexer metadata builder in `_init_minimal_kv_cache_for_profiling`, interleave still `1`) |
| main (e80b6c642f) | NIXL, explicit `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4` (workaround) | 0.921 |
| this PR | NIXL, interleave auto (resolved to 4 before profiling) | **0.920** |

```bash
VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --language-model-only --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"}'
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000
```

**Value-level repro (tiny dummy-weight `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM` with `index_topk`, i.e. the `deepseek_v2` indexer path), TP2 + DCP2, NIXL `kv_both`, `compilation_config.mode=0` + `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` CUDA graphs, debug prints of the value seen by each component:**

| Phase | main: indexer op | main: sparse MLA builder | this PR: both |
|---|---|---|---|
| profiling | 1 | 1 | 64 |
| `initialize_from_config` | - | 64 (adjusted 1 -> 64) | 64 |
| warmup / serving | **1 (stale)** | 64 | 64 |

With an explicit `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 64` (no NIXL), main and this PR give identical tokens/logprobs to this PR's NIXL run. Dummy weights are not sensitive enough to show the accuracy impact; on a DSA-style sparse-MLA model with real weights (P/D, P at TP8 + DCP8), we previously measured GSM8K ~1.5% on main vs ~85% with the stale value fixed (that run used the fix from #60671).

On current main, GLM-DSA (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` -> `deepseek_v32`) is **not** affected: it passes `parallel_config.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` per call rather than the cached property. This PR keeps it unchanged.

**Unit tests** (GB300 node, HF offline):
- New: `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py` (4 parametrized cases for `set_kv_cache_layout` finalization incl. user-set value / non-NIXL connector / no connector, plus the post-profiling guard) and updated `tests/test_config.py` cases: pass.
- `tests/test_config.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_config_builder.py`, `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/{test_kv_connector_lifecycle,test_nixl_connector,test_nixl_connector_hma,test_nixl_desc_geometry,test_config,test_multi_connector}.py`: same failure IDs on main and this PR (all pre-existing, models not available offline in my environment); this PR adds 5 passing tests.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` (0.14.0): clean. `mypy` on the changed files reports only 2 pre-existing errors in untouched lines.

## Details

Worker startup order on main (per worker; the engine drives the RPCs):

1. `load_model`, then `update_block_size_for_backend` (kernel block size becomes final here).
2. `set_kv_cache_layout` RPC from `EngineCore._initialize_kv_caches`. **This PR: interleave finalized here.**
3. `determine_available_memory`: profile run, plus (with CUDA graphs) a minimal KV cache with real attention metadata. On main the interleave is still `1`; `SparseAttnIndexer` / `SparseAttnIndexerKpool` cache it on the first forward with real metadata, and MRV2 builds indexer metadata with it.
4. Engine computes `KVCacheConfig`s; `initialize_from_config` -> `ensure_kv_transfer_initialized` -> `adjust_dcp_kv_cache_interleave_size`. **Main: 1 -> block_size happens here**; metadata builders recreated afterwards see the new value, the indexers keep the stale one -> top-k global indices computed with the wrong token-to-rank layout.
5. Compile / CUDA graph capture, serving.

Changes:
- `WorkerBase.set_kv_cache_layout`: for DCP > 1 with a KV transfer instance, derive the worker's KV cache groups with the same builder the engine uses (`get_kv_cache_groups_from_builder(get_kv_cache_config_builder(...))`) and call `adjust_dcp_kv_cache_interleave_size`. Runner-agnostic (MRV1/MRV2), and also runs on the elastic EP scale-up path.
- `adjust_dcp_kv_cache_interleave_size` takes the KV cache groups instead of a `KVCacheConfig` (logic unchanged).
- `ensure_kv_transfer_initialized`: re-runs the adjustment and raises if the value changed after profiling.
- `SparseAttnIndexer` / `SparseAttnIndexerKpool`: read the value from `parallel_config` instead of caching it.

Tradeoffs / limitations:
- The pre-profiling value is derived from the worker's own KV cache spec, whereas the engine's `KVCacheConfig` groups are computed from the merged specs of all workers. They are identical when all workers hold the same layer types (e.g. PP=1). In exotic PP layouts where page-size unification across stages could change the minimum block size, the guard fails startup and asks for an explicit `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size`, rather than silently diverging. #60671 handles this case by publishing the global groups to workers.
- `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` is a compile-hash factor; it is now final before the first compile, so the hash is consistent.
- The engine-process copy of the value is not updated (same as main; nothing in the engine reads it).

---

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Tune MoRI decode dispatch grid and MXFP8 block32 packed cutoff on MI355X
body:
## Purpose

Two small, self-contained decode-path tunings for **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X (gfx950)** under the DEP8 MoRI expert-parallel recipe with DSpark speculative decode. Both are driven by the observation that DSpark verifies `num_speculative_tokens + 1` rows per sequence each step, so the *effective* decode width is ~7x larger than a single-token decode and the stock decode-regime heuristics are mis-sized for it.

1. **MoRI decode dispatch/combine launch grid.** MoRI's intra-node dispatch/combine has a grid-wide barrier (every block waits for the last to arrive), so the launch grid sets the dispatch tail. The handle's fixed `80x16` launch leaves CUs idle at this decode width. Launching the dispatch and combine with a `128x16` grid (block count capped at the CU count so the barrier stays resident) is **~4% better TPOT** across concurrency 64–256; going wider (`192`) regresses.

2. **MXFP8 32x32-block GEMM packed-kernel cutoff.** The packed kernel fills the MFMA rows with K panels instead of tokens and beats the tiled kernel while there are only a handful of real rows. The per-shape `_TUNED` table switches to the tiled kernel above small M; the decode GEMMs (incl. the indexer projection) land in that tiled range once DSpark inflates M, and those tiled launches dominated the attention stream. Keeping the packed kernel through `M <= 64` recovers that time without fighting the table above it.

Both knobs are env-overridable (`VLLM_MORI_DECODE_BLOCKS` / `VLLM_MORI_DECODE_WARPS`, `VLLM_PACKED_DECODE_MAX_M`) so they can be re-tuned per platform; the defaults are the MI355X-tuned values. With the defaults nothing else changes.

### Files changed

* `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/mori.py` — `_mori_launch_config(num_tokens)` returns `(block_num, warp_per_block)`; `prepare()`/`finalize()` pass them to `dispatch()`/`combine()`.
* `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/rocm_block32_gemm.py` — `_PACKED_DECODE_MAX_M` keeps the shape's largest packed tier through small decode M in `_config`/`_default_config`.

## Test Plan

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MI355X 8x (gfx950, ROCm 7 nightly), vLLM `0.32.0rc1.dev369`, DEP8 (data-parallel 8) + `--enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput`, aiter MoE, MXFP4 sparse indexer, block size 128, V2 Model Runner, DSpark MTP `num_speculative_tokens=6` with adaptive block verification, FULL CUDA graphs. "Baseline" = the same image, branch and server flags with the stock image kernels; "tuned" = with this change.

* **Accuracy:** GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions, temperature 0, parallel.
* **Serving:** `ISL 8192 / OSL 1024`, streaming `/v1/completions`, `ignore_eos`, closed-loop at fixed concurrency 4 / 64 / 128 / 256; TTFT p50, TPOT p50, total tok/s.
* **Tuning sweep** (ISL 8192 / OSL 256 decode-TPOT probe, conc 64 and 128) to justify the chosen values: MoRI decode grid `{80x16, 128x16, 192x16}` and packed cutoff `{0, 32, 64}`.

## Test Result

### Accuracy (GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 q)

| build                         | accuracy |
| ----------------------------- | -------- |
| baseline (stock kernels)      | 90.07%   |
| as-ported (untuned: 64x4 grid, packed M<=384) | 90.52% |
| **tuned (128x16 grid, packed M<=64)** | **90.75%** |

### Performance (ISL 8192 / OSL 1024)

TPOT p50 (ms, lower is better):

| conc | baseline | as-ported | **tuned**   | tuned vs baseline |
| ---- | -------- | --------- | ----------- | ----------------- |
| 4    | 23.45    | 28.32     | 27.80       | +18.5% (wide grid overhead at a ~28-row batch) |
| 64   | 55.38    | 59.65     | **53.39**   | **-3.6%**         |
| 128  | 55.46    | 59.75     | **53.50**   | **-3.5%**         |
| 256  | 55.45    | 59.68     | **53.53**   | **-3.5%**         |

Total throughput (tok/s, higher is better) and TTFT p50 (ms):

| conc | baseline tok/s | **tuned tok/s** | baseline TTFT | **tuned TTFT**   |
| ---- | -------------- | --------------- | ------------- | ---------------- |
| 64   | 22432          | **22700** (+1.2%) | 11099       | 11857            |
| 128  | 24599          | **27285** (+10.9%) | 27179      | **23059** (-15.2%) |
| 256  | 27082          | **28701** (+6.0%) | 56207       | **50009** (-11.0%) |

The untuned ATOM-direction port (narrow `64x4` grid + packed through `M<=384`) was 7–8% *worse* than baseline on TPOT everywhere; re-tuning on MI355X reverses that into a win from conc 64 up. The only soft spot is conc 4, where a ~28-row decode batch cannot fill the wide grid; this is the opposite end of the same mechanism and could be removed later with a token-count-scaled decode grid.

### Tuning sweep (TPOT p50 ms, ISL 8192 / OSL 256 probe)

| config                         | TPOT@64 | TPOT@128 |
| ------------------------------ | ------- | -------- |
| baseline (stock)               | 55.38   | 55.46    |
| MoRI 80x16 + trust-table       | 55.37   | 55.34    |
| **MoRI 128x16 + trust-table**  | 53.15   | 53.18    |
| MoRI 192x16 + trust-table      | 54.04   | 54.04    |
| MoRI 128x16 + packed M<=32     | 53.19   | 53.30    |
| **MoRI 128x16 + packed M<=64** | **52.97** | **53.03** |

title: [Perf][Model] Qwen4Exp QSA: SM80 launch config for indexer prefill scoring
body:
## Overview

On A100 (sm_80), the Qwen4Exp QSA indexer prefill scoring kernel `_qsa_mqa_paged_prefill_kernel` uses the GB300 launch config (16 K tiles per CTA), which leaves most of the 108 SMs idle. This PR adds an sm_80 config for the BF16 indexer cache and one warp per row for the compressor kernel on sm_80. Both keep the output bit-equal.

## Claims

- Indexer prefill scoring on A100, upstream TP8 shapes, 32k context: **2.03×** for a 512-token chunk, **1.50×** for a 2048-token chunk; the logits are bit-equal.
- `_compress_qsa_groups_kernel` on A100: 1.05–1.32× with one warp per row; bit-equal.
- No change on other GPUs, for the FP8 indexer cache, or for any other QSA kernel.

## Validation

**Kernel benchmark** (1 × A100-SXM4-40GB; Qwen3.8-Flash QSA per-GPU shapes at TP8 read from the model config; the wrapper's exact launch re-run with only the launch kwargs changed; CUDA graph of 20 calls, 128 MB L2 flush before each of 5 replays, median; each config's output compared with the default's).

| Kernel | Scenario | Before (GB300 config) | This PR | Speedup | Output |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| indexer prefill scoring | 512-token chunk at 32k | 87.4 µs | 43.0 µs | 2.03× | bit-equal |
| indexer prefill scoring | 2048-token chunk at 32k | 212.5 µs | 141.7 µs | 1.50× | bit-equal |
| compress groups | decode, 8k / 32k / 128k | 5.89 / 4.04 / 3.89 µs | 5.53 / 3.53 / 3.69 µs | 1.07 / 1.14 / 1.05× | bit-equal |
| compress groups | prefill 512 / 2048 | 4.86 / 9.98 µs | 3.99 / 7.58 µs | 1.22 / 1.32× | bit-equal |

The same sweep at DCP 4 shapes (with the open QSA DCP PRs, where each rank scores a quarter of the states) gives 4.38× (512-token chunk) and 1.72× (2048) for the indexer prefill scoring with this config family.

For the BLOCK_N choice: the sweep's best config was BLOCK_N 128 with 2 K tiles at both main-shape points (and 4 K tiles at 2048, 1.59× against this PR's 1.50×). At the DCP4 512-token point (4× fewer columns), BLOCK_N 32 won; the CTA-count rule picks BLOCK_N 128 when that grid gives at least 2 CTAs per SM and BLOCK_N 32 otherwise, which selects the winner at all four measured points.

Per 12 QSA layers, the indexer change saves about 0.5 ms per 512-token prefill chunk and 0.85 ms per 2048-token chunk on A100.

**Tests:** new CPU test `test_qsa_prefill_scoring_launch_config` in `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py` (selection per GPU and cache dtype). It has not run in our environment (the vLLM test environment there could not import the newer `main` tree); it relies on CI.

**Not done:** end-to-end serving A/B; GPUs other than A100 (the change applies to capability 8.0 only); `pre-commit` (ruff not available on the machine used).

## Details

- `_prefill_launch_config(num_requests, query_rows, logits_width, cache_dtype)` returns the launch kwargs; on other GPUs it returns the existing GB300 values, so `_prefill_logits` behaves as before there.
- Measured but left out: decode scoring and sparse-attention split counts. Their best configs differ between shapes (sparse attention: 8 splits at upstream shapes, 2 at DCP4 shapes), and a split change also changes the summation order.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Share Engram host tables as host-NUMA cuMem across DP ranks
body:
## Overview

With `dp_shared_memory`, node-local DP ranks share one registered `/dev/shm` mapping for the Engram host tables (2 layers x 94.4 GiB on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash). Lookups are random row reads and on GB200 they are bound by GPU TLB misses: the registered mapping uses 64K pages.

This PR allocates the shared table as host-NUMA cuMem instead, which the GPU maps with 2M pages. Rank 0 creates it and broadcasts a FABRIC handle; the other node-local DP ranks import and map it. Where FABRIC handles are unavailable (probed once: create + export), the existing `/dev/shm` path is used and logged. Rank 0 decides the backing and broadcasts it so every rank runs the same collectives. A mapping failure on any rank raises on all ranks.

- New NVIDIA-only `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/engram_host_table.py` (~125 lines of code).
- `common/engram.py`: +42/-7, `DPSharedEngramStorage` keeps its interface; startup log says `via cuMem` or `via /dev/shm`.
- No new config option.

Not a duplicate: open Engram PRs cover pinned sizing (#59849), SP/PCP sharing (#57195, #61553), Mooncake and disk offload (#57023, #62238); none changes the shared host table backing.

## Performance

GB200, DEP4, `--numa-bind`-equivalent binding (`numactl` per rank), dummy weights, uniformly random tokens. Same node, back-to-back A/B.

Engram lookup, one layer, fresh ids every iteration:

| tokens | /dev/shm | cuMem |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 16 | 69 us | 49 us |
| 128 | 184 us | 90 us |
| 1024 | 1.21 ms | 0.47 ms |
| 4096 | 3.78 ms | 1.21 ms |
| 32768 | 9.92 ms | 4.36 ms |

`vllm bench forward` (median per-rank forward):

| case | /dev/shm | cuMem | change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prefill 32768 | 346.76 ms | 333.93 ms | -3.7% |
| prefill 4 x 8192 | 347.18 ms | 333.65 ms | -3.9% |
| prefill 4 x 8192 @ 16384 ctx | 353.86 ms | 338.71 ms | -4.3% |
| prefill 16384 | 181.99 ms | 170.87 ms | -6.1% |
| prefill 4096 | 56.72 ms | 50.87 ms | -10.3% |
| decode 64 @ 16384 | 16.61 ms | 16.61 ms | 0% |
| decode 128 @ 16384 | 17.10 ms | 17.10 ms | 0% |

Decode lookups already overlap on the side stream. Real text repeats 15-22% of rows, so real prefill gains should be somewhat smaller than the random-token numbers.


title: [DSv4.1][BI] Bitwise batch invariance for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with CUDA graphs
body:
## Purpose

Make DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash inference bitwise batch invariant under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` with CUDA graphs on (FULL_AND_PIECEWISE), DEP4, DSpark MTP and MegaMoE. Under BI, token ids and logprobs are bitwise identical regardless of batch composition and order, chunk size, decode vs `prompt_logprobs` re-feed, prefix-cache hit vs miss and DP rank placement. Target is RL true on-policy rollouts.

BI=0 behavior is unchanged except for the DSv4.1 model fixes in the first commit (Engram stack entry, SWA block stride alignment, stale `-1` tail in combined indices).

## Changes (grouped)

1. **DSv4.1 fixes**: Engram stack entry, 32 B SWA block stride, combine index tails, replay-disable conditions.
2. **BI CUDA op library** (`csrc/batch_invariant/`): K32 block-scaled GEMM, fused SiLU-mul + group quant, deterministic radix top-k (larger index wins ties), sparse paged indices, SWA-first index combine, ordered expert permute/combine.
3. **Dense**: row-invariant BF16 / MXFP8 projections, RMSNorm, logits and logprobs.
4. **Attention**: FlashMLA sparse and indexer under BI. Every causal row (decode, spec verify, prefill, `prompt_logprobs` re-feed) runs in one call on the unsplit sparse decode kernel (`flash_mla_with_kvcache(enable_batch_invariant=True)`), reading the fp8 SWA and nvfp4 compressed caches directly; the BI CUDA op `sparse_paged_indices` derives each token's slots and lengths from (request, position) only. The opt-in mega attention keeps decode on its decode kernel and makes prefill match it (SWA-first layout, compressed length by position).
5. **Exact SWA bounded replay**: replay stays on but becomes exact under BI (decoder trimming keeps W+(n-1)(W-1) rows, prefix-hit replay recomputes W+L(W-1) tokens), optional layer-wise staging, padding rows masked.
6. **MoE**: MegaMoE under BI, ordered BF16 EP reduce-scatter + rank-order FP32 combine, router pinned, `empty_cache` before symmetric-memory allocation.
7. **mHC**: fixed split counts for every M, fused post+pre-norm kernel with warmup.
8. **DSpark**: draft rows and aux hidden-state capture under BI.
9. **Opt-in faster BI tiers** (`VLLM_BI_*`): tensor-core MXFP8/BF16 GEMM (non-split-K tactics only), MXFP8 prequant, startup precompile of every reachable M.
10. **Opt-in Mega tier**: Mega mHC with fixed split, split-mHC overlap side stream, mega attention under BI, Mega Gate in deterministic mode.

Opt-in tiers are bitwise batch invariant but round differently from the default BI path. A trainer that wants true on-policy must call the same kernels.

## Test Plan / Results

Measured on GB200 (DEP4, DSpark 5 tokens, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, 8192 in / 1024 out) on the pre-rebase tree. This branch is the same stack rebased onto current main with mechanical conflict resolution; it has not been re-run on GPU after the rebase.

**Bitwise gates (BI=1, graphs on): all 0 diff.**
- alone / batch / reversed, pinned and unpinned DP ranks
- decode vs `prompt_logprobs` re-feed
- `max_num_batched_tokens` 2048 vs 8192 vs 16384, cross-run
- prefix cache hit vs miss
- MTP on, batch combinations

**Throughput, BI=1 / BI=0, same image and recipe, only `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` differs.** 12 AB/BA pairs, median output throughput ratio:

| c=1 | c=8 | c=32 | c=64 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.911 | 0.922 | 0.919 | 0.907 |

**Unit tests**: new BI op tests are bitwise against reference implementations on the target shapes, including decode == prefill across ragged/compact top-k, multi-chunk and h_q in {64, 128}. They run under BI=0 and BI=1. Remaining failures in the touched suites are pre-existing on the base.

**Lint**: `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD` passes, including mypy.

**After the rebase** (3 extra commits move the replay gather and decode top-k lengths from Triton to BI CUDA ops), the full bitwise gate matrix was re-run on an image built from this branch: all 0 diff, and 6711 token/logprob records are bitwise equal to the pre-rebase image. Rebase adaptations:
- `FixedBf16Gemm.dispatch` accepts the new `output_dtype` (#62042).
- BI forces `use_psum_layout=False` for DeepGemmFP4Experts (#59044).
- Compressor test config gains PCP fields (#59857).

**FlashMLA sparse path (latest commit, f1ff0f0341)**, `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` without the mega tier: full gate matrix 0 diff (28 rows across 2048/8192/16384, MTP, batch combinations, cross-rank, graph vs eager, short prompts 1–31 tokens); `tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py` 167 passed under BI=0 and BI=1. BI=1 / BI=0 throughput on this path, 4 AB/BA pairs: c=1 0.911, c=8 0.890, c=32 0.876, c=64 0.835. RL rollout step time (128 trajectories per DEP4 node, response up to 8192, real rejection sampling), BI=1 / BI=0: 1.072 fixed-length, 1.023 natural EOS (mega attention: 1.034 / 1.036).

## Image

`docker.io/aosheninferact/vllm-dsv41-bi:pr-f1ff0f0341` (linux/arm64, digest `sha256:7daa6030cc52838f6e05a280ffe34946660451d95b50156532e43e02df563ab2`), matching the current head: official nightly `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294` plus a layer with this branch's vLLM package and the two rebuilt extensions, a Python layer with the per-call eager break and CuTe stream commits, and a layer with the FlashMLA sparse commit (its Python files and the rebuilt `_vllm_batch_invariant_C`). The gates and throughput numbers for the FlashMLA path above were measured on these exact bytes.

## Known gaps

- Only the V2 model runner (the default) is supported under BI. The V1 runner is not covered.

- `prompt_logprobs` with very large row counts can still JIT-compile the lm_head GEMM while serving.
- Validated on GB200 only.

## Duplicate-work check

This overlaps with in-flight work on batch invariance (#54955 and its splits #59925, #59929, #60442; #59863 fused SiLU-mul quant; #62208 / #60613 DSv4.1 fixes; my own #57815). This PR is the end-to-end DSv4.1-Flash stack that the bitwise gates above were measured on. It is submitted as one PR at the maintainer's request; reconciling with those PRs can follow in review.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write and audit this change. The submitter reviewed the change and the results above.

title: [Kernel][Perf] Bound DSA candidate mask writes to each row's extent
body:
## Summary

`_mask_candidates_kernel` (DSA/NSA indexer candidate mask, shared CUDA path) poisoned the **full logits workspace width** with `-inf`, although only each row's `[start, end)` extent is ever read back. The workspace is `max_model_len` wide (CUDA-graph static) while each row's live extent is its own request's block range in the packed column space, so most of those stores hit padding or other requests' column ranges.

This PR bounds the store predicate to the row extent and early-returns from tiles beyond `end`. It aligns the shared kernel with the semantics the ROCm strided variant already relies on (#56628, see also #59668): every consumer of the masked logits is extent-bounded:

- `top_k_per_row_prefill` / `top_k_per_row_decode` read `rowStart`/`rowEnd` from the cu_seqlen tensors (`csrc/sampler.cu`);
- `_block_scores_kernel` loads with `cols < end`;
- `_merge_dcp_topk_global` is a no-op at `dcp_world_size == 1`.

Not a duplicate of #59668: that PR fuses the two ROCm kernels in `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`; this one shrinks the shared kernel's write set.

## Performance (H200 ×8, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP2×DP4+EP, DSA sparse indexer, saturated decode)

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `_mask_candidates_kernel` per call (nsys) | 145.1 µs | **54.9 µs (−62%)** |
| Output throughput (rate 1.3 req/s, 10k/5k, 320 prompts) | 4918.8 tok/s | **5096.2 tok/s (+3.6%)** |
| TPOT p99 | 30.59 ms | **27.02 ms (−12%)** |

End-to-end numbers are back-to-back clean runs on the same deployment, same seed/params.

## Correctness

- Greedy outputs over 8 fixed prompts are **byte-identical** before/after (plus a revert control run), so no model-affecting output change is expected.
- New test `tests/kernels/attention/test_candidate_blocks.py` (8 cases; widths 1–262144; packed starts/ends; `row_repeat` groups; −1 padding and clamped/edge candidates) asserts agreement with a full-width poisoned reference within `[0, end)` and that the workspace outside each row's extent is left untouched — the same contract style as the ROCm test.

## Test commands run

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_candidate_blocks.py -v   # H200, this branch → 8 passed
```

Also verified end-to-end on a 2-node P/D deployment (NixlConnector, dspark): 320/320 requests, byte-identical greedy outputs, kernel timing above from nsys traces.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (ZCode agent). The human submitter has reviewed every changed line and re-ran the tests and benchmarks above.

title: [RFC][KV Cache] Reference implementation of programmable KV cache (#57103)
body:
Superseded by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62382, which uses the current `rfc-hint` branch. This draft is closed.

---

## Purpose

This is our **draft reference implementation of [RFC #57103: Programmable KV Cache](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57103)**, shared for design discussion and implementation review. It does not close the RFC or claim complete acceptance.

Agentic sessions span multiple inference requests, tool pauses, and branches. The RFC lets an application express lifecycle and cache intent through the existing `KvHintsEnvelope`, while the engine resolves targets, approves resources, executes operations, and reports actual completion.

### How this implementation maps to the RFC

- **Common control and logical state:** request-attached hints and independent Python/HTTP control share the envelope, dispatcher, and engine approval path. Hash/session/continuation/range selectors resolve logical content separately from physical residency. Results are correlated by message/action IDs, with bounded replay, queries, ACK, cancellation, and engine epochs. Existing backend-owned KVCR payloads retain opaque forwarding.
- **Execution through existing cache infrastructure:** `SET_PRIORITY`, `COPY_TO`, and `MOVE_TO` use `KVCacheManager`/`BlockPool` and CPU/Mooncake Store adapters. GPU-source operations run at successful request completion before references are released; accepted transfers can outlive the request. COPY publishes reusable GPU content only after all participating ranks finish. MOVE stores first and reclaims eligible source copies afterward. Shared loads share reservations and transfer holds; a resume can wait for an existing load.
- **Optional policies and rollout integration:** retention, tool-wait movement, and quota/prefix-reuse scheduling consume engine observations and submit proposals through the same approval boundary. Explicit commands keep their meaning. Startup configuration controls policy registration. The benchmark harness connects real verl `ToolAgentLoop` calls, tools, token logprobs, response masks, and rewards; weight-update checks exercise draining, invalidation, and cache namespace isolation.

Implementation contracts: [native primitives and lifecycle](https://github.com/zhhangBian/vllm-note/blob/rfc-57103-reference/vllm/v1/kv_hints/README.md). Reproduction: [benchmark commands](https://github.com/zhhangBian/vllm-note/blob/rfc-57103-reference/benchmarks/programmable_kv_cache/README.md).

### Current conclusions

Recorded local experiments use Qwen3.8-27B BF16, two A100 80GB GPUs, TP=2, concurrency 16, and 32 rollouts from 8 GSM8K questions. Each fixed-work replay has 113 model calls and 8,121 output tokens. The principal comparisons use three runs per configuration and report median throughput relative to native APC at the **same GPU KV budget**; movement additionally uses a host Store.

| GPU KV per GPU          | Configuration                 | Native / reference elapsed | Throughput change |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------: | ----------------: |
| 2 GiB, constrained      | Quota/prefix-reuse scheduling |          449.06 / 219.63 s |           +104.5% |
| 2 GiB, constrained      | Retention + movement + quota  |          449.06 / 247.60 s |            +81.4% |
| 8 GiB, working set fits | Retention + movement + quota  |            54.09 / 56.13 s |             -3.6% |

These measurements support executable lifecycle/resource contracts and a scheduling benefit under constrained KV capacity. They do **not** establish an additional benefit from movement/composition over quota alone, or a general serving speedup. The 2 GiB setting is an artificial pressure diagnostic. When the working set fits, both arms have zero preemptions and equal cache hits; control overhead produces a regression.

Separate live tool runs took 452.37 / 288.73 / 214.34 s for native/full-policy/quota, each scoring 32/32 rewards. These are single runs with different generated trajectories and only 8 independent questions. Fixed replay reruns model generation but does not rerun tools or evaluate rewards.

The [experiment report](https://github.com/zhhangBian/vllm-note/blob/rfc-57103-reference/docs/programmable-kvc/rollout-report-2026-10-12.md) records variability, tail-latency regressions, missing Store objects, methodology, and unfinished acceptance. Raw traces/logs remain local and are not included in this PR.

### Related work and remaining scope

Duplicate checks covered #57103's discussion, open PRs referencing it, and KV-hint/programmable-cache searches. [#58198](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58198) supplies a minimal request-free CPU-to-GPU primitive; [#59714](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59714) and [#38514](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38514) cover retention priority. This reference has a broader purpose: a runnable control/lifecycle/resource/execution path plus policy and rollout experiments. Its overlapping primitive, dispatcher, and priority code needs consolidation with those contributions before upstream merge. The experimental COPY/MOVE schema follows the direction discussed in #59708 and remains open to revision.

This draft preserves development baseline `30f5c01d4ebb5c493ed86195db24d0ec5b3ce3d7` and currently has conflicts with upstream `main`. Rebase and validation against current `main` remain open. Other gaps include the full prediction/fairness/outage/restart matrix, a fresh final 128-question evaluation, other models/layouts, Dynamo/llm-d integration, and full RL trainer/optimizer performance. CPU control requires one block per chunk; native Mooncake movement requires PCP=DCP=1. Cold-tier retention/deletion and mixed native/backend envelopes are unsupported.

title: [RFC][KV Cache] Implementation of programmable KV cache (#57103)
body:
## Purpose

This is our **draft reference implementation of [RFC #57103: Programmable KV Cache](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57103)**, shared for design discussion and implementation review. It does not close the RFC or claim complete acceptance.

Agentic sessions span multiple inference requests, tool pauses, and branches. The RFC lets an application express lifecycle and cache intent through the existing `KvHintsEnvelope`, while the engine resolves targets, approves resources, executes operations, and reports actual completion.

### How this implementation maps to the RFC

- **Common control and logical state:** request-attached hints and independent Python/HTTP control share the envelope, dispatcher, and engine approval path. Hash/session/continuation/range selectors resolve logical content separately from physical residency. Results are correlated by message/action IDs, with bounded replay, queries, ACK, cancellation, and engine epochs. Existing backend-owned KVCR payloads retain opaque forwarding.
- **Execution through existing cache infrastructure:** `SET_PRIORITY`, `COPY_TO`, and `MOVE_TO` use `KVCacheManager`/`BlockPool` and CPU/Mooncake Store adapters. GPU-source operations run at successful request completion before references are released; accepted transfers can outlive the request. COPY publishes reusable GPU content only after all participating ranks finish. MOVE stores first and reclaims eligible source copies afterward. Shared loads share reservations and transfer holds; a resume can wait for an existing load.
- **Optional policies and rollout integration:** retention, tool-wait movement, and quota/prefix-reuse scheduling consume engine observations and submit proposals through the same approval boundary. Explicit commands keep their meaning. Startup configuration controls policy registration. The benchmark harness connects real verl `ToolAgentLoop` calls, tools, token logprobs, response masks, and rewards; weight-update checks exercise draining, invalidation, and cache namespace isolation.

Implementation contracts: [native primitives and lifecycle](https://github.com/zhhangBian/vllm-note/blob/rfc-hint/vllm/v1/kv_hints/README.md). Reproduction: [benchmark commands](https://github.com/zhhangBian/vllm-note/blob/rfc-hint/benchmarks/programmable_kv_cache/README.md).

### Current conclusions

Recorded local experiments use Qwen3.8-27B BF16, two A100 80GB GPUs, TP=2, concurrency 16, and 32 rollouts from 8 GSM8K questions. Each fixed-work replay has 113 model calls and 8,121 output tokens. The principal comparisons use three runs per configuration and report median throughput relative to native APC at the **same GPU KV budget**; movement additionally uses a host Store.

| GPU KV per GPU          | Configuration                 | Native / reference elapsed | Throughput change |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------: | ----------------: |
| 2 GiB, constrained      | Quota/prefix-reuse scheduling |          449.06 / 219.63 s |           +104.5% |
| 2 GiB, constrained      | Retention + movement + quota  |          449.06 / 247.60 s |            +81.4% |
| 8 GiB, working set fits | Retention + movement + quota  |            54.09 / 56.13 s |             -3.6% |

These measurements support executable lifecycle/resource contracts and a scheduling benefit under constrained KV capacity. They do **not** establish an additional benefit from movement/composition over quota alone, or a general serving speedup. The 2 GiB setting is an artificial pressure diagnostic. When the working set fits, both arms have zero preemptions and equal cache hits; control overhead produces a regression.

Separate live tool runs took 452.37 / 288.73 / 214.34 s for native/full-policy/quota, each scoring 32/32 rewards. These are single runs with different generated trajectories and only 8 independent questions. Fixed replay reruns model generation but does not rerun tools or evaluate rewards.

The [experiment report](https://github.com/zhhangBian/vllm-note/blob/rfc-hint/docs/programmable-kvc/rollout-report-2026-10-12.md) records variability, tail-latency regressions, missing Store objects, methodology, and unfinished acceptance. Raw traces/logs remain local and are not included in this PR.

### Related work and remaining scope

Duplicate checks covered #57103's discussion, open PRs referencing it, and KV-hint/programmable-cache searches. [#58198](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58198) supplies a minimal request-free CPU-to-GPU primitive; [#59714](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59714) and [#38514](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38514) cover retention priority. This reference has a broader purpose: a runnable control/lifecycle/resource/execution path plus policy and rollout experiments. Its overlapping primitive, dispatcher, and priority code needs consolidation with those contributions before upstream merge. The experimental COPY/MOVE schema follows the direction discussed in #59708 and remains open to revision.

This draft preserves development baseline `30f5c01d4ebb5c493ed86195db24d0ec5b3ce3d7` and currently has conflicts with upstream `main`. Rebase and validation against current `main` remain open. Other gaps include the full prediction/fairness/outage/restart matrix, a fresh final 128-question evaluation, other models/layouts, Dynamo/llm-d integration, and full RL trainer/optimizer performance. CPU control requires one block per chunk; native Mooncake movement requires PCP=DCP=1. Cold-tier retention/deletion and mixed native/backend envelopes are unsupported.

## Validation

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,3 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/test_kv_hint_control.py \
  tests/v1/test_kv_hint_state.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_kv_control.py \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/kv_control/test_api.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --from-ref 30f5c01d4ebb5c493ed86195db24d0ec5b3ce3d7 --to-ref rfc-hint --show-diff-on-failure
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --from-ref 30f5c01d4ebb5c493ed86195db24d0ec5b3ce3d7 --to-ref rfc-hint
openspec validate programmable-kv-cache --strict
```

The recorded regression result is **680 passed**, with 14 PyTorch deprecation warnings. The implementation files tested are identical to those in this branch; the subsequent history edit changes attribution trailers only. The full branch pre-commit checks passed. Python 3.12 type checks and OpenSpec strict validation passed on the same implementation. The model and rollout measurements above are earlier experimental results, not newly rerun evaluations.

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, documentation, and PR preparation. The human submitter has confirmed reviewing every changed line and personally running the relevant tests.

title: [Bug]: Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) — single prefill crossing the 262,144 native boundary crashes the engine with CUDA illegal memory access (v0.32.0 and nightly, OK on v0.31.1)
body:
### Your current environment

Hardware: 1 node × 8× NVIDIA H200 (141 GiB), driver 580.126.20, 2 TB host RAM.
Each engine instance uses TP=2 + EP (2 cards per instance).

| | working | broken |
|---|---|---|
| vLLM | `0.31.1rc1.dev1+gbb87d227d` (image `sha256:a14b2535…`) | `0.32.0` (image `sha256:befccf0e…`) **and** `0.32.0rc1.dev369+g1b2a66639` (nightly `sha256:12496a6e…`) |
| torch | 2.13.0+cu130 | 2.14.0+cu130 |

Model: `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` NVFP4 checkpoint (`modelopt_fp4`, PLE-FP8, W4A16N).
Architecture in vLLM: `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`; attention backend reported as
`QWEN4_EXP_EXP_QSA_STATE`; MoE backend `marlin`.

Relevant engine flags (identical in both versions, only the image differs):

```
--tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel
--max-model-len 1048576           # native max_position_embeddings is 262144; YaRN factor 4.0
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --kv-cache-dtype fp8
--max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096
--long-prefill-token-threshold 2048 --enable-prefix-caching
--speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}
--hf-overrides {"text_config":{"rope_parameters":{"mrope_interleaved":true,"mrope_section":[11,11,10],
  "partial_rotary_factor":0.25,"rope_theta":10000000,"rope_type":"yarn","factor":4.0,
  "original_max_position_embeddings":262144}}}
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

A **single** chat completion whose prompt is slightly above the model's native
`max_position_embeddings` (262,144) kills the engine core with
`CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`. Below the boundary everything is fine.

Measured on the same machine, same flags, same client script:

| prompt tokens | 0.31.1 | 0.32.0 / nightly dev369 |
|---|---|---|
| 249,598 | ok | **ok** (11.7 s) |
| 261,840 | ok (13.0 s, needle recalled) | not tested |
| 262,397 | ok (24.2 s, needle recalled) | **crash** |

So the failure starts exactly when the prompt crosses 262,144 = native context, i.e. in the
YaRN-extrapolated region, and is triggered by the chunked prefill of that request.

This is a production incident for us: three independent TP=2 instances crashed in sequence
(a → c → b → a) as real long-document traffic was round-robined across them, each restart
taking ~4 min.

### Reproduction

Single request is enough — no concurrency needed (see matrix above).

```python
import json, time, urllib.request

BASE   = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"
MODEL  = "Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next"
REPEAT = 11394   # → ≈262,400 prompt tokens for this filler; use 10860 for ≈249,600

pad = "This is a filler sentence containing the number 12345 and some tokens."
prompt = " ".join(pad + " %d" % i for i in range(REPEAT))
needle = "ZQ-9917-LONGTEST"
half = len(prompt) // 2
hay = prompt[:half] + "\nKEY CODE: " + needle + "\n" + prompt[half:]

body = {"model": MODEL, "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 64,
        "messages": [{"role": "user",
                      "content": hay + "\n\nQuestion: what KEY CODE appears above? Output only it."}]}
req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + "/v1/chat/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                             headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=1800) as r:
    print(json.load(r)["usage"])
```

Expected: `prompt_tokens=262397`, completion with the needle.
Actual (0.32 line): HTTP 500, engine core dead, `/health` returns 503 until restart.

### Error output

Worker side (rank varies — observed on both `Worker_TP1_EP1` and `Worker_TP0_EP0`):

```
(Worker_TP1_EP1 pid=550) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1063] RuntimeError: CUDA error:
CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED when calling `cublasGemmEx( handle, opa, opb, m, n, k,
&falpha, a, CUDA_R_16BF, lda, b, CUDA_R_16BF, ldb, &fbeta, c, ..., CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP)`

torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
  what():  CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered

(EngineCore) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:315] Worker proc VllmWorker-1 died unexpectedly
                            (exit code: None), shutting down executor.
(EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1512] EngineCore encountered a fatal error.
  ... shm_broadcast.py:867 in acquire_read -> raise RuntimeError("cancelled")
```

Engine dump captured right before the fatal step (this is the whole batch — the 262k request
is the one being chunk-prefilled, `num_scheduled_tokens=2048`):

```
Dumping scheduler output for model execution: SchedulerOutput(
  scheduled_new_reqs=[],
  scheduled_cached_reqs=CachedRequestData(
    req_ids=['chatcmpl-bb96…', 'chatcmpl-9745…', 'chatcmpl-b238…'],
    new_token_ids_lens=[],
    new_block_ids=[None, ([68],[64],[60],[56],[],[]), None],
    num_computed_tokens=[199348, 262400, 16580],
    num_output_tokens=[237, 0, 269]),
  num_scheduled_tokens={chatcmpl-bb96…: 4, chatcmpl-b238…: 4, chatcmpl-9745…: 2048},
  total_num_scheduled_tokens=2056,
  num_spec_tokens_to_schedule=3, num_common_prefix_blocks=[])
Dumping scheduler stats: SchedulerStats(num_running_reqs=3, num_waiting_reqs=0, ...,
  kv_cache_usage=0.0526, ...)
```

Note `num_computed_tokens=262400` for the request being prefilled — 256 tokens past the
native limit. Cache config in the same build reports `swa_bounded_replay="True"`,
`mamba_cache_mode="align"`, and the 0.32 log line `Breakable CUDA graph enabled`;
on 0.31.1 the same workload is clean, so I suspect one of the 0.32 prefill/CUDA-graph
changes rather than the model itself. I have not bisected; happy to run experiments.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living inside the GitHub search bar (copilot)
- [x] Checked the docs for relevant options

### Anything else?

- Both ranks can fail (TP0 and TP1 observed), across 6 different physical GPUs; ECC counters
  are 0 and there are no retired pages, so this does not look like a hardware fault.
- The container stays up while the engine core is dead: `/health` → 503 and every subsequent
  request returns 500 until the process is restarted. Worth noting for anyone relying on
  liveness probes.
- `--max-model-len 262144` (dropping the YaRN region) is not a workaround we can use —
  long-context 1M is a product requirement — so we rolled back to `0.31.1rc1.dev1+gbb87d227d`.
- Full logs (three instances, including crash + restart cycles) available on request;
  I can also re-run any bisection you want (e.g. `enable_chunked_prefill=off`,
  `long_prefill_token_threshold`, cudagraph mode, `swa_bounded_replay`).

title: [Feature][PCP] Support decoder-side SWA bounded replay with APC for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
body:
## Overview

Extend #62183 to support DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decoder-side SWA bounded replay with PCP and APC, including prefix-hit continuation.

## Claims

- Retain each request's global trailing window on its original PCP owners while preserving cached compressed KV and indexer keys.
- Keep prompt-logprobs rows and existing non-PCP behavior; padded peers participate in the same collectives and only real outputs are scattered back.

## Validation

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017.
- Baseline: pinned nightly plus #62183 (`fc47cc8fff8282b7fa2b257468b8595f91a1a741`), encoder replay only.
- Candidate: identical baseline plus this PR at `8689ce06b2ac945c82e44cdb5ff52e925fc096bc`, with decoder replay enabled.
- Both services use the following launch command; node placement and the runtime overlay differ by arm:

```bash
vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 18001 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --block-size 64 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --moe-backend humming \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --swa-bounded-replay \
  --enforce-eager \
  --no-async-scheduling
```

### Uncached 8K prefill performance

- Node-local benchmark clients.
- Direct token-ID prompts: 8,192 input tokens, one output token, request rate infinity, no warmup, and `N=10*C`.
- C1/N10 seed `210101`, C8/N80 seed `210108`, and C32/N320 seed `210132`.
- Both arms receive the same unique prompts. Every accepted run has zero prefix-cache hit tokens.

| Case | Baseline Input TPS | Candidate Input TPS | Candidate delta | Baseline Mean TTFT | Candidate Mean TTFT | Candidate delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| C1 / N10 | 13,933.06 | 21,994.20 | +57.86% | 587.75 ms | 372.25 ms | -36.66% |
| C8 / N80 | 14,240.95 | 22,866.70 | +60.57% | 4,399.97 ms | 2,739.59 ms | -37.74% |
| C32 / N320 | 14,252.14 | 22,894.56 | +60.64% | 17,499.31 ms | 10,890.08 ms | -37.77% |

All 820 requests across both arms succeeded. Decoder-side replay improves uncached 8K prefill throughput by 58-61% across C1-C32.

### Paired GSM8K accuracy

Full 1,319 samples, four-shot, batch 64, seed 42, temperature 0, top-p 1, reasoning effort `high`, and `max_tokens=8192`, using EvalScope 1.11.1:

| Arm | Correct | Accuracy | API errors | Max-token stops |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline | 1,286/1,319 | 97.498% | 0 | 0 |
| Candidate | 1,282/1,319 | 97.195% | 0 | 1 |

The arms used the same sample indexes, prompts, targets, and total input-token count. Paired outcomes were 1,278 both-correct, 29 both-wrong, 8 baseline-only correct, and 4 candidate-only correct. The exact two-sided McNemar test gives `p=0.387695`, so the observed 0.303 percentage-point difference is not statistically significant.

Both arms recorded exactly 674,816 / 803,206 local prefix-cache hit tokens (84.02%) and zero external cache-hit tokens. The sole candidate truncation was sample index 119, which reached 8,192 output tokens; the corresponding baseline request stopped normally at 6,955 output tokens.

Both service pods remained Ready with zero restarts. The performance and accuracy runs had zero API failures, and post-test logs contained no critical runtime, CUDA, or engine errors.

## Details

Reuse the existing replay batch, gather kernel and attention builders. The PCP-local batch retains its global scheduled view to derive tail boundaries and a common padding bound without CPU collectives. Select local slots before compaction, gather them in rank-major order, and align MoE routing IDs with the compact rows. Batches that would not shrink after padding keep full execution.

Unlike #61554's APC-disabled cold-prefill path, this builds on #62183 for APC prefix hits and derives replay bounds from existing global PCP metadata. It retains the existing PCP restrictions and eager execution requirement, with no scheduler, generic model-runner or configuration changes. The branch is rebased on #62183 now in main. AI assistance was used for implementation and static checks.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Tests on H20 platform.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

title: [KVConnector][Mooncake] Detect shared-prefix junctions in the MooncakeStore lookup
body:
## Overview

Stacked on #62278; review only the last commit. The MooncakeStore lookup now detects shared-prefix junctions, and the store keeps the SWA tails at those junctions under sparse retention. Without this, a fresh instance (or one that evicted the prefix locally) gets 0 hits from the store for siblings that share a prefix, because store retention keeps only each request's own replay tails.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP + MooncakeStore, local prefix cache reset before every request: siblings get 3584 / 3840 hit tokens from the store (d = 8 / 160 past an aligned 3840-token prefix). On main they get 0 in both cases.
- Shared-prefix GSM8K (200 questions, local cache reset before each): 194 questions hit 3584 tokens and 4 hit 3840 from the store, with accuracy 0.975. On main every question gets 0 hits, with accuracy 0.97.
- No dense SWA retention in the store: the store keeps only the tails at junction positions, in addition to the existing replay tails.

## Validation

**End to end** (GB200, 4 GPUs, base 83c9a547bf): the same serve command as #62278, plus `--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"}'`. Before every request after the first, the client calls `/reset_prefix_cache`, so all hits come from the store.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| junction probe C, D (d = 8) | 0, 0 | 3584, 3584 |
| junction probe C, D (d = 160) | 0, 0 | 3840, 3840 |
| A replayed (own prompt, store sanity) | 4864 / 5120 | 4864 / 5120 |
| GSM8K accuracy (200) | 0.97 | 0.975 |
| GSM8K store hit rate (`external_prefix_cache_hits / queries`) | 0% | 81.2% |

**Unit tests** (CPU): the store coordinator, scheduler, worker and connector suites, plus the core suites from #62278: `1562 passed`. The new tests cover a two-instance save → lookup → save → lookup flow on one store, junctions in `store_mask` (several positions, never on Mamba groups), the tracker hand-off when a loading sibling skips its first save, and the lookup-response round trip, including payloads from writers that predate junction entries.

## Details

**Source.** `MooncakeStoreWorker.lookup()` already queries the store hits per group. The store coordinator now also returns the longest single-group hit, and computes the junctions with the same `junction_boundaries()` as the local coordinator. The lookup response carries them as 8-byte entries with a sentinel group id. Old readers ignore those entries, because the loader reads only real group ids.

**Consumer.** The scheduler merges the store junctions into `request.shared_prefix_boundaries` at lookup, before compute. So GPU retention, Mamba chunk stops and this request's own store saves all use them. `RequestTracker` and `ReqMeta` carry the junctions to `store_mask`, which adds them to the reachable boundaries.

**Lifetime.** Blocks are pinned when the save job is created, in the same `schedule()` pass. The worker skips null block ids, so a tail block that the GPU already freed is not saved with wrong data.

**Conflict.** #62255 moves the Mooncake metadata and wire structs to new modules; one of the two will need a rebase.

title: [Quantization] Use replace_parameter for params re-created in process_weights_after_loading
body:
**Depends on #62326; review only the last commit.**

## Overview

Part 2 of 3 of keeping the loaded parameter objects through `process_weights_after_loading` (PWAL). With #62326, `replace_parameter` keeps the registered object. This PR converts the PWAL sites that still register a fresh `torch.nn.Parameter` over a loaded one to `replace_parameter`.

## Claims

- `layer.x = Parameter(...)`, `setattr(layer, x, Parameter(...))` and no-op rewraps (`Parameter(layer.x.data)`) in PWAL now go through `replace_parameter`, so the loaded object (class, `weight_loader`, dim attributes) survives. This covers:
  - linear kernels: MXFP4, MXFP6, MXFP8, NVFP4 (CUTLASS, FlashInfer, FBGEMM, PyTorch, Humming scales), mixed precision (ExLlama, RDNA3, XPU);
  - compressed-tensors, Quark, INC, FBGEMM FP8, ModelOpt, AutoAWQ and online lm_head methods, and Marlin FP4 helpers;
  - `dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm`, CPU AMX MLA, and DeepSeek-V4 CPU attention.
- Coverage (whole-tree enumeration of PWAL-reachable sites on `main`, 1786 rows split across the three PRs): 141 sites converted here, plus 2 n/a rows inside the changed hunks. Deletes and renames in the same functions are left as on `main`; they are in the follow-up PR.

## Validation

- `pre-commit` passes.
- On GB200, `tests/quantization/test_keep_param_objects.py` and `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py` pass: 23 passed. This PR adds the `modelopt-fp8-pb-wo-linear` and `modelopt-mxfp8-linear` cases, which fail on #62326 alone.
- The end-to-end GB200 run is described in #62326. It compares `main`, #62326, and the top of the stack, which includes this PR. The rows that touch this PR's sites are below.

  | Config | GSM8K main / stack | Post-PWAL tensors |
  |---|---|---|
  | MiniMax-M3 MXFP8 (ModelOpt MXFP8 linear), TP4 | 0.859 / 0.859 | identical |
  | compressed-tensors W8A8 FP8 per-tensor + FP8 KV cache | 0.738 / 0.738 | identical |
  | same, Humming forced (reads `processed_weight_dims`) | 0.751 / 0.758 | identical |
  | same, Marlin forced | 0.738 / 0.734 | identical |

  - The same kernels are selected in both arms.
  - Every loader-visible param is the same object after PWAL; on `main`, 10% are for W8A8 FP8 and 49% for M3.

## Details

- Compressed-tensors W8A8 FP8 and ModelOpt FP8 per-tensor transpose the weight to (K, N). The kept param keeps its checkpoint dim tags, and the layout reaches Humming via `layer.processed_weight_dims` (added in #62326) instead of a retag.
- Where a site re-creates a param whose shape or dtype changes, `replace_parameter` rebinds `.data`; where the layout matches, it copies into the existing storage.
- `modelopt.py`, `quark_nvfp4.py`, `fbgemm_fp8.py`, `inc_wna16_linear.py` and `kernels/linear/nvfp4/humming.py` also delete or rename params. Only their `Parameter(...)` assignments are converted here.

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Keep the online MXFP8 MoE kernel across  weight reloads
body:
## Overview

Online MXFP8 MoE (`quantization="mxfp8"`) builds a new MoE kernel on every `reload_weights`, while decode keeps replaying CUDA graphs captured against the startup kernel. After the first reload, decode reads tensors freed with the old kernel and samples sporadic garbage tokens. This keeps the startup kernel on reload and refreshes its quant config in place.

Same class of bug as #61304 (ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE, behind `VLLM_RELOAD_KEEP_MOE_KERNEL`), which uses the same in-place refresh.

## Claims

- After `reload_weights`, online MXFP8 MoE decode with CUDA graphs matches eager prefill again, instead of sampling occasional tokens that prefill scores at logprob -10 to -30.
- Reload still serves the new weights.

## Validation

All results below are on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP8 + EP, `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` MXFP8 MoE, on 8x B300, with **vLLM 0.31.0** plus an equivalent patch that keeps the startup kernel on reload but doesn't refresh the quant config. **This exact diff has not yet been run on `main`. That run is pending, and the PR stays a draft until it's done.**

**Decode vs prefill self-check.** Generate, then re-score the same tokens with `prompt_logprobs`, and compare (KL of decode vs prefill logprobs):

| | fresh server | after reload |
|---|---|---|
| CUDA graphs, unpatched | 0.0027 | 0.0065 (garbage tokens) |
| `enforce_eager`, unpatched | 0.0026 | 0.0027 |
| CUDA graphs, patched | 0.0026 | 0.0028 (0.0025 after 10 reloads) |

**Reload serves the new weights.** Zero layer 2's routed-expert `w2`, then compare two servers:
- **Reloaded:** booted on the base weights, then given the zeroed checkpoint through `reload_weights`.
- **Fresh:** booted directly on the zeroed checkpoint.

| | KL |
|---|---|
| base-model tokens: reloaded server vs base | 0.0065 |
| base-model tokens: fresh-zeroed server vs base | 0.0066 |
| reloaded server's tokens: fresh-zeroed vs reloaded | 0.0026 (two servers on identical weights: ~0.0027) |

**In RL with weight updates every step:** over 60 steps, the trainer-vs-inference logprob KL mean went from 0.0437 to 0.0038.

**CI coverage gap.** `test_online_quantize_reload` covers `mxfp8` reload on a dense model only. Its MoE case (`DeepSeek-V3-debug`) is `xfail` because MXFP8 doesn't support MLA, and the test runs without CUDA-graph replay checks. So CI doesn't exercise this path, and I haven't added a test.

## Details

**Root cause.**
1. `Mxfp8OnlineMoEMethod._setup_kernel` runs from `process_weights_after_loading` on every reload.
2. Layerwise reload copies the re-processed parameters back into their original storage (`_copy_and_restore_kernel_tensors`), so pointers to layer parameters stay valid.
3. `_setup_kernel` then replaces `self.moe_quant_config` and `self.moe_kernel` with new objects. The old kernel is dropped, along with any tensor only it referenced.
4. The CUDA graphs captured at startup still point at those tensors.
5. Eager mode is unaffected, which is how the bug was isolated.

**Fix.** If a kernel already exists, i.e. on a reload:
- Build the new quant config.
- Copy each of its tensors into the matching tensor of the existing quant config.
- Keep the existing kernel.

Layer parameters are refreshed by the layerwise copy as before. The copy raises an error if a quant-config tensor changes shape or dtype, rather than silently serving stale values.

**Overlap with #61304.** `_refresh_moe_quant_config_inplace` is the same helper #61304 adds to `modelopt.py`. If both land, it should move to `fused_moe/config.py` and be shared. Unlike #61304, this applies unconditionally: online quantization exists to requantize on reload, and rebuilding the kernel is never correct under captured graphs.

title: [Quantization] Keep deleted and renamed params registered after process_weights_after_loading
body:
**Depends on #62326 and #62405; review only the last commit.**

## Overview

Part 3 of 3 of keeping the loaded parameter objects through `process_weights_after_loading` (PWAL). After #62326 and #62405, a loaded param can still disappear when PWAL deletes or renames it. This PR keeps those params registered, so after PWAL every loader-visible param is still registered under the same name, as the same object, and keeps its loaded data unless that would cost real memory.

## Claims

- **Renames alias one param under both names.** The new `move_parameter(layer, src, dst)` registers the `src` param object under `dst` as well and records `dst` as its runtime name. The loader writes through the checkpoint name and kernels read the runtime name, both pointing at one storage, so a later `replace_parameter` on either name updates both and no extra memory is used. This covers:
  - compressed-tensors `*_weight_packed` (linear, NVFP4/MXFP4/W4A8 MoE);
  - INC MXFP4;
  - the NVFP4 MoE oracle;
  - Humming NVFP4 and Humming's checkpoint-to-standard renames;
  - compressed-tensors W8A16 block FP8, which now aliases `weight_scale_inv` to `weight_scale`.
- **Loaded params no kernel reads keep their data and are marked retired** (`retire_parameter`). This covers:
  - consumed NVFP4 per-tensor scales (ModelOpt, Quark);
  - small Humming leftovers (at most 1/256 of the largest converted tensor);
  - the input scales of ModelOpt and Quark NVFP4 MoE when a weight-only backend (Marlin, Humming) is selected. These used to be set to `None`, which unregistered them. The method now leaves them registered and passes `None` to the MoE quant config.
- **Large released sources stay registered with empty storage** (`replace_parameter(layer, name, t.new_empty(0))`). Their data was converted into a different-layout kernel tensor, so keeping it would double that memory. This covers:
  - unused zero points (Conch, CPU, Marlin, Zentorch, int8 scaled-mm, Quark int8 linear and MoE);
  - KV-cache scale placeholders (`kv_cache.py`, compressed-tensors KV);
  - released weights (XPU W4A8, wNa8o8, dynamic 4-bit, CPU int8, Triton MXFP4 MoE, DeepSeek-V4 XPU MegaMoE L1 weight and SFs, dots3 vision experts, INC ARK);
  - Humming leftovers larger than 1/256 of the largest converted tensor.
- **Readers see the kernel view.**
  - `kernel_parameters(layer)` returns the live params, each object once under its runtime name. `get_live_param` treats retired or empty params as absent. Humming uses both helpers.
  - The Triton MXFP4 MoE wrapper is stored as a plain `<name>_triton` attribute read via `triton_weight()`, so it no longer takes over the param name.
- **Coverage** (whole-tree enumeration of PWAL-reachable sites on `main`, 1786 rows split across the three PRs): 73 delete/rename sites fixed here, plus 36 sites converted together with them (Humming's delete-then-recreate pattern), plus 7 n/a rows inside the changed hunks.

## Validation

- `pre-commit` passes.
- On GB200, `tests/quantization/test_keep_param_objects.py` and `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py` pass: 39 passed.
  - The keep test now also asserts non-empty storage for every loaded param.
  - It runs ModelOpt and compressed-tensors NVFP4 linear and MoE with Marlin and Humming forced.
  - `test_utils.py` covers aliasing, retiring, and the runtime name.
- End-to-end on GB200, `main` vs the stack with this PR. Each run is a cold start with GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot), greedy decoding, a byte digest of every post-PWAL tensor, and an object census of loader-visible params:

  | Config | GSM8K main / stack | Post-PWAL tensors | Loader params registered (main → stack) | Kept with empty storage |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | ModelOpt NVFP4 (Qwen3-30B-A3B) | 0.8878 / 0.8886 | identical | 69% → 100% | 0 |
  | ... forced Marlin (3 runs each) | 0.8749, 0.8901, 0.8863 / 0.8779, 0.8893, 0.8855 | identical | 62% → 100% | 0 |
  | ... forced Humming (3 runs each) | 0.8802, 0.8901, 0.8870 / 0.8734, 0.8863, 0.8961 | identical | 69% → 100% | 0 |
  | compressed-tensors NVFP4, forced Humming | 0.8931 / 0.8946 | identical | 36% → 100% | 0 |
  | compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE (CUTLASS, `*_weight_packed` → `*_weight`) | 0.8582 / 0.8582 (1314/1319 identical text) | identical | 46% → 100% | 0 |

  - Marlin and Humming are not run-to-run deterministic. Two `main` runs agree on about 390 of 1319 GSM8K outputs, so their rows show three runs per arm.
  - The extra tensors in the stack are aliases, with no extra memory, or kept scalars and per-tensor scales. Kept data adds at most 0.15 MiB per model (under 0.001%).
- Direct load of W1 into the live params (`model.load_weights`, no PWAL): every checkpoint name now resolves.
  - On `main`, ModelOpt NVFP4 with Marlin or Humming fails with `has no parameter 'w2_input_scale'`, and compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE fails with `has no parameter 'w2_weight_packed'`.
  - With this stack, compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE loads all 675 tensors with no param moved. ModelOpt NVFP4 then stops at a shape mismatch, because Marlin/Humming repack to a different layout.
  - Direct load is only exact for layout-preserving PWAL, as on `main`; layerwise reload is the supported path.
- Layerwise reload W0 → W1:
  - ModelOpt NVFP4: all tensors are byte-identical to a cold start on W1, and greedy matches `main` 8/8.
  - compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE: all tensors are byte-identical to a cold start on W1, and greedy matches 8/8.
- Earlier runs of the stack (#62326) gave `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py`: 74 passed, 1 failed (`test_kv_scale_reload`), the same as on `main`.

## Details

- **Stacked on #62405, not only on #62326:** the same functions (ModelOpt and Quark NVFP4, FBGEMM FP8, INC, Humming NVFP4) both convert and delete params, so this commit applies on top of #62405.
- **Reload:** layerwise reload restores checkpoint-format params before loading. It goes through `layer._parameters`, so both alias names are restored, and a param kept empty is never handed to a `weight_loader`.
- **Humming:** used to delete every param and re-create the set it needs. It now writes through `replace_parameter`. Leftovers are skipped if they alias a replaced param, retired if small, and emptied if large.
- **Weight-only NVFP4 MoE input scales:** Humming's MoE quant config reads the input scales from the layer, so they are retired rather than left live. A live loaded scale would switch Humming to the static checkpoint scale, while `main` uses none.
- **Not kept (exceptions, listed in #62326):** the online FP8 requantization-source `weight_scale`, AutoGPTQ placeholder MoE biases, and torchao tensor subclasses.

title: [Model] Support GLM-5.3 MLA DSpark drafts on CUDA
body:
## Overview

Add CUDA serving support for a GLM-5.3 MLA DSpark draft exported in the speculators format, without checkpoint-side Python runtime files or startup monkey patches.

Related: [speculators#1052](https://github.com/vllm-project/speculators/issues/1052), [vllm-ascend#14535](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/14535). The former covers training/export and the latter is an Ascend implementation; this change targets the CUDA model, latent cache, and anchor-relative mixed-window attention. Searches for open GLM/DSpark and `GlmDSparkMLA` PRs found no matching CUDA implementation. This is distinct from K3-specific MLA refactoring and generic draft-context limits.

## Claims

- Register `GlmDSparkMLAForCausalLM` and preserve its architecture and MLA geometry through speculators config conversion.
- Reuse the Qwen3 DSpark scaffold, Markov/confidence heads, MLP, and weight loading, with an MLA decoder and compressed `512 + 64` latent/RoPE cache.
- Resolve layer count, sliding/full layout, window size, and causality from configuration, preserving the tested draft's block-anchor-relative window semantics.
- Keep this PR separate from sampling-RNG changes. Existing model routes remain the defaults.

## Validation

### Serving environment and results

The serving validation was performed on the local **vLLM 0.31.0 integration**, not the current `main` checkout. The checkpoint tensors were unchanged.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Software | vLLM `0.31.0+glmmla.20261019`, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130` |
| Target / draft | GLM-5.3 MG43 NVFP4 W4A4C8 / MLA-distilled DSpark step1750 |
| Execution | V2 GPU model runner, single-node TP4, PP1, DCP1, eager |
| Precision | BF16 draft weights and target/draft KV caches |
| Speculation | 8 draft tokens, probabilistic drafting, standard rejection, adaptive verification off |
| Workload | Fixed internal 300-request corpus, concurrency 8, original per-request sampling |
| Length limits | Context 196608, output cap 1024, respecting EOS |

| Implementation | Mean accepted length, including one target token |
|---|---:|
| Historical checkpoint-side runtime | 3.396830 |
| Same-node checkpoint-side runtime reference | 3.341220 |
| Installed vLLM 0.31.0 integration | 3.368620 |

Both same-node runs completed 300/300 requests with zero errors. Ten fixed-input comparisons (five layers, prefix lengths 257 and 2305, real checkpoint TP-rank-0 head slices) had bitwise-identical attention outputs and latent cache entries against the old runtime. A dense-reference mask check covered causal sliding and noncausal full attention around the 2048 window boundary.

These are single stochastic runs, not confidence intervals or throughput benchmarks. The evaluated 0.31.0 build retained historical draft/verifier RNG isolation; that sampler change is intentionally **not included** here. Accordingly, the figures describe the validated integration environment, not an exact end-to-end measurement of this current-main source branch. Current main declares PyTorch 2.14.0.

### Source checks on this branch

Passed `git diff --check`, AST parsing of all seven changed Python files, and Ruff checks. The checkout is sparse, so Ruff was invoked with `vllm` explicitly classified as first-party and `INP001` excluded:

```bash
git diff --check
git diff --name-only HEAD^ HEAD -- '*.py' | xargs ruff check \
  --config 'lint.isort.known-first-party = ["vllm"]' --ignore INP001
ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/models/glm_dspark_mla.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/dspark.py vllm/config/speculative.py
```

The GPU checkpoint and request corpus are internal and are not uploaded in this PR. No automated GPU CI coverage or full pre-commit pass is claimed; the serving results above are the external-to-CI validation evidence.

## Details

### Scope and compatibility

The supported MLA geometry is deliberately restricted to Q rank 2048, KV rank 512, NoPE head dimension 192, RoPE dimension 64, and V head dimension 256. Hidden size and head count are read from configuration, subject to compatible tensor-parallel shapes.

The implementation does **not** hardcode five decoder layers or a four-sliding/one-full ordering. It resolves each layer through the existing DFlash attention configuration helper. The measured checkpoint uses four causal sliding layers with a 2048 window and one noncausal full layer; other layouts have not been evaluated. The sliding window starts relative to the draft block's anchor, not each individual query position. Default NeoX-style RoPE was evaluated; this does not claim arbitrary RoPE-scaling compatibility.

This initial path requires BF16 draft weights, eager execution, PP1 and DCP1. Graph support is explicitly disabled. The current paged kernel handles at most 16 query rows per request per call; the evaluated speculative width is 8. Cache insertion currently uses PyTorch indexed assignments; async-performance and graph-capture improvements are not claimed.

The dedicated kernel is retained because the draft's mixed causal/noncausal and anchor-relative window semantics must match training. This is not a claim that every GLM/K3 MLA checkpoint, weight layout, or backend is interchangeable. Future shared-backend work should preserve those semantics.

### Usage

The draft export declares `architectures: ["GlmDSparkMLAForCausalLM"]`; its `transformer_layer_config` declares `model_type: "glm_dspark_mla"` and the MLA dimensions. Matching weights and config are sufficient; no checkpoint-side runtime code is required.

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve /path/to/target \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enforce-eager \
  --max-model-len 196608 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"/path/to/draft","num_speculative_tokens":8}'
```

The human submitter has confirmed source review and authorized submission. AI assistance was used to develop and prepare this PR.
