title: [Bug][Spec Decode] DSpark corrupts thinking/chat outputs on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (all k; both v0.32.0 and nightly; clean without speculation)
body:
## Environment

- Hardware: 8x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96G (SM120), single node, TP8 + EP
- vLLM: **0.32.0 release** and **0.32.1rc1.dev24** (latest nightly) — both reproduce
- torch: 2.13.0+cu132 (release env) / 2.14.0+cu132 (nightly env) — both reproduce
- FlashInfer: 0.7.1rc5 (python + jit-cache; cubin 0.7.0.post1)
- Checkpoint: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` (site copy, 48 shards)
- Local patch: #60762 (SM120 uniform-64 block-size declaration only — 2 files, declaration-level; symptom is identical with/without it)
- Flags: `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --trust-remote-code --enable-expert-parallel --block-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 128 --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":N}'`

## Symptom

With DSpark enabled, `/v1/chat/completions` in thinking mode returns degenerate loops in the reasoning stream (e.g. `"to invoketo invoke..."`, `"*75*75*75..."`) and no structured tool calls are produced. Plain-text `/v1/completions` is **not** affected: a 25-tier benchmark suite (1K ladder c1-c128, long-context 32K-1M, 64K/64K ramp) ran with speculation on, all zero failures, and a 256-prompt needle-retrieval task scored 99.6% coherent — so the corruption is specific to the chat/thinking format.

## Isolation (every variable tested on the same box)

| Configuration | chat/thinking output |
|---|---|
| 1017 + DSpark k=3, vLLM nightly (torch 2.14) | degenerate loops |
| 1017 + DSpark k=3, vLLM 0.32.0 (torch 2.13) | degenerate loops |
| 1017 + DSpark k=4 / k=5 / k=7 | degenerate loops |
| **1017, no speculation (same boot, same parsers)** | **clean**: reasoning/content correctly separated (`17*19` -> reasoning "We need answer only number..." + content `323`); tools -> structured `tool_calls` (`get_gpu_alert({"node":"gpu-03"})`); 12-turn tools-API agent session 12/12, 0 errors |
| Original `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` + DSpark k=3, same hardware/config family | clean (prior deployment records on this box: 26-32 structured tool calls, 0 errors) |

Also ruled out: tokenizer files (byte-identical between the two checkpoints), template rendering (vLLM's built-in `deepseek_v41` template output is byte-identical to the official `encoding/encoding.py` reference for single-turn chat), tokenization (`/tokenize` parses the special tokens into their single IDs correctly), sampling temperature (0.0 and 1.0 both corrupt), and the parser flags (no-spec run uses the same three flags and is clean).

## Repro (minimal)

```bash
vllm serve <DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017> --tensor-parallel-size 8 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41

curl .../v1/chat/completions -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"17*19=? answer with the number only"}],"max_tokens":512,"temperature":0}'
# with spec: reasoning = repetitive token loops; without --speculative-config: reasoning "..." + content "323"
```

## Context

- The encoder/renderer sync PRs #62199 / #62196 / #62200 address the tool-result turn encoding delta from DeepSeek's `314113f` encoding fix — a separate problem. Our corruption is single-turn, reproduces on the current encoder, and flips solely on speculation.
- #58485 reports a related class (spec decode x thinking markers) on another model family.
- 1017 is a weight-only update of V4.1-Flash (config/tokenizer unchanged; the release notes describe shortened outputs/agent tuning), so the delta is in the fine-tuned `mtp.*` draft heads or their interaction with the verifier in thinking-format contexts.

## Impact / workaround

Chat or agent serving on the 1017 checkpoint should disable DSpark speculation until this is fixed (plain-text completion workloads are unaffected). Happy to run any follow-up experiment on this box.

title: [ROCm][Model] DeepSeek-V4.1 VL: stream language-model weights on ROCm
body:
- `amd/vl_model.py` loads through `stream_language_model_first` instead of `sorted()`.
- `test_deepseek_v4_vl_stream_weights.py` runs on ROCm and resolves the V4.1 wrapper through the platform dispatcher, so each platform tests the class it runs.
- The AMD Basic Models (Other) step in `test-amd.yaml` and its `models_basic.yaml` mirror run the test.

#58857 replaced the checkpoint sort with `stream_language_model_first` in the V4 and NVIDIA V4.1 VL wrappers, but the AMD V4.1 copy kept `sorted()`, which holds every tensor the loader yields before the first copy. #58782 reports host OOM from that sort and includes the same idea in a larger ROCm change. The AMD child loader is per-tensor and finalizes MegaMoE and mHC weights only after its group, so it needs the group contiguous, not totally ordered. On MI355 the test passes 10/10 with this change; with `main`'s `amd/vl_model.py` the `v41` case fails at the mid-stream assertion. A full DeepSeek-V4.1 load was not run here (475 GiB checkpoint).

This overlaps #62298, which currently skips the ROCm `v41` case of this test; that skip goes away once this lands.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix] Accept 16-byte cache strides in DeepSeek CuTeDSL gather
body:
## Overview

Allow the CuTeDSL DeepSeek gather kernel to accept 16-byte-aligned cache block strides. This fixes rejection of valid packed V4.1 MXFP8 caches during MRV2 warmup.

## Claims

- Relax only the block-stride specialization from 32 to 16 bytes, matching the kernel's existing 128-bit copies. The 32-byte base-pointer alignment is unchanged.
- Extend the existing writer/FlashMLA/gather comparison to include odd row padding; retain all numerical assertions and the three record formats.

## Validation

Native NVIDIA B300, Torch 2.14.0. Tests used a task-private FF01 runtime with the reviewed source/test overlays; the affected kernel, cache utility and original test bytes match the PR base. This is not a full build of current main.


e.g. from a configured vLLM test environment:

~~~bash
uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py::test_v41_cache_writers_match_flashmla_decode -q
uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py::test_dequantize_and_gather_k_cache -q
~~~

| Check | Original kernel | Changed kernel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Six V4.1 cases (same parametrized test in both arms) | 4 passed, 2 failed: odd-padding swa_fp8 and compressed_fp8 | 6 passed |
| Existing V4 gather vs PyTorch reference, separate invocation | Not rerun | 2 passed |
| Actual tiny MRV2 LLM startup + two-token generation | Warmup fails on the same stride divisibility check | Starts and generates two tokens |

The engine diagnostic used a three-layer DeepSeek-V4.1 configuration with the model's first-three-layer source topology (compress_ratios=[0,0,2], KV/index source layer 2, Engram layer 1), reduced dimensions/tables, dummy weights, BF16, TP=1, text input, eager execution and explicit FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41. Only this kernel module changed in the successful engine arm. It is a startup/generation diagnostic, not official-checkpoint accuracy or production CUDA-graph qualification. No speedup is claimed.

Ruff check/format, diff check, and seven applicable repository checks passed (test tethering, SPDX, lazy imports, forbidden imports, CUDA calls, config and boolean-context-manager checks). Full pre-commit and upstream CI were not completed locally. Dependency warnings were retained. The existing B200 miscellaneous-kernels CI selection includes this test file.

## Details

An MXFP8 record is 528 bytes. An odd number of padded rows can therefore produce a block stride divisible by 16 but not 32, even when the allocation's base pointer is 32-byte aligned. The current fake-tensor stride constraint rejects that layout before the gather executes. The existing copies require 16-byte alignment; lowering this stride constraint leaves the base alignment and data/scale addressing unchanged.

The additional padding case is accepted by FlashMLA decode and the Triton gather; after the fix, CuTeDSL agrees with them under the existing assertions. The existing aligned cases and NVFP4 control also pass.

AI assistance was used. The human submitter reviewed and confirmed understanding of every changed line. Open-PR searches for dequant gather, CuTeDSL stride and the exact module name found no matching fix. The broad SM12x PR #41834 still has the 32-byte stride constraint and does not address this change. This is an independently reproduced startup bug, not a performance cleanup.

title: [Deepseek v4.1][ROCm] Fix misleading loading hangs, ~5-10% faster load on cold load
body:
## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on ROCm appeared to hang after the shard progress bar reached 100%:

```
Loading safetensors checkpoint shards:  94% Completed | 45/48 [00:35<00:01,  2.15it/s]
Loading safetensors checkpoint shards:  96% Completed | 46/48 [00:35<00:00,  2.44it/s]
Loading safetensors checkpoint shards: 100% Completed | 48/48 [00:35<00:00,  1.34it/s]

(Worker_TP0 pid=9428) INFO 10-19 08:24:53 [default_loader.py:501] Loading weights took 240.81 seconds
```

This was fixed in #58857 for Nvidia but not AMD.

Cause is the AMD multimodal wrapper sorted the entire weight stream, which drained the lazy iterator before any weight had been copied, so all real loading happened afterwards with no progress output. That list also made the load itself slower: every shard was read once to build it and touched a second time during the copy phase.

This PR streams the language-model weight group instead, matching `deepseek_v41/nvidia/vl_model.py` and `deepseek_v4/common/vl_model.py`.

This PR also fixes misleading `Loading weights took` logs in case several models (base + draft) are loaded.

## Claims

The AMD V4.1 wrapper was the last place that sorted the entire weight stream before handing it to the child loader (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/255f14599ec0544c35539414810abdfa7e4e1c86/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/vl_model.py#L337-L347); it now streams the language-model group with `stream_language_model_first` (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/255f14599ec0544c35539414810abdfa7e4e1c86/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/vl_model.py#L82-L97), as the NVIDIA V4.1 wrapper already does (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/255f14599ec0544c35539414810abdfa7e4e1c86/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/vl_model.py#L323). Weights are copied while the shard bar advances instead of after it completes, which removes the multi-minute silent phase between `Loading safetensors checkpoint shards: 100%` and the next log line.

Target `Loading weights took` on MI350, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP=4, one run per row, checkpoint evicted from page cache:

| condition | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| warm page cache | 23.0 s | 23–25 s |
| cold page cache | 233.7 s | **213.6 s** |

The ~20 s reduction (~8.6%) comes from the checkpoint no longer being traversed twice — once while the bar advances, then again in sorted order during the copy phase. With a warm cache both branches load in ~23 s and the difference disappears. The message is also attributed to a model whenever a process loads more than one (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/255f14599ec0544c35539414810abdfa7e4e1c86/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py#L500-L505), so target and drafter timings are distinguishable; single-model loads keep the existing message.

Unattributed timings on `main`, cold page cache. The bar completes, then ~3.5 min pass with no output, then both loads report the same message:

```
Loading safetensors checkpoint shards: 100% Completed | 48/48 [00:35<00:00,  1.34it/s]
(Worker_TP0 pid=9428) INFO 10-19 08:24:53 [default_loader.py:501] Loading weights took 240.81 seconds
Loading safetensors checkpoint shards: 100% Completed | 48/48 [00:26<00:00,  1.80it/s]
(Worker_TP0 pid=9428) INFO 10-19 08:25:21 [default_loader.py:501] Loading weights took 26.72 seconds
```

With this change, same command and same conditions. The copies now happen inside the bar:

```
Loading safetensors checkpoint shards:  98% Completed | 47/48 [03:12<00:08,  8.74s/it]
Loading safetensors checkpoint shards: 100% Completed | 48/48 [03:39<00:00, 14.36s/it]
(Worker_TP0 pid=14044) INFO 10-19 12:00:31 [default_loader.py:506] Loading weights took 220.06 seconds (model=DeepseekV41ForCausalLM)
Loading safetensors checkpoint shards: 100% Completed | 48/48 [00:05<00:00,  9.24it/s]
(Worker_TP0 pid=14044) INFO 10-19 12:00:38 [default_loader.py:506] Loading weights took 5.20 seconds (model=DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM)
```

## Validation

Command (ROCm, MI350, TP=4; identical for both branches). The checkpoint is evicted from page cache first, because with a warm cache both branches finish in ~23 s and the difference is not observable:

```bash
# 1. Evict the checkpoint from page cache (advisory, no root needed)
python3 - <<'EOF'
import glob, os
snap = glob.glob(os.path.expanduser(
    "~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--deepseek-ai--DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017/snapshots/*"))[0]
for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(snap, "model-*-of-00048.safetensors")):
    fd = os.open(os.path.realpath(path), os.O_RDONLY)
    os.posix_fadvise(fd, 0, 0, os.POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED)
    os.close(fd)
EOF

# 2. Serve
export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1
export AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1
export VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=INFO
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export MKL_NUM_THREADS=1
export HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3

vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --moe-backend aiter \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --port 8001 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"standard","enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --block-size 64 &> ds_serve.log &
```

Method: the server log was sampled every 30 s during the load.

| | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| shard bar | 42 s, iteration only | 219 s, iteration + copies |
| silent phase after bar | ~210 s | none |
| `Loading weights took` (target) | 240.81 s | 220.06 s |

Unit test for the streaming behavior, enabled for ROCm in this PR (`is_cuda_alike()`, and the V4.1 parameter now resolves through `vllm.models.deepseek_v41`, so on ROCm it exercises `amd/vl_model.py`):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_vl_stream_weights.py -v -p no:cacheprovider
```

```
tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_vl_stream_weights.py::test_load_weights_streams_language_model_group[v4] PASSED [ 50%]
tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_vl_stream_weights.py::test_load_weights_streams_language_model_group[v41] PASSED [100%]
======================== 2 passed, 14 warnings in 2.78s ========================
```

Reverting only `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/vl_model.py` to `main` makes `[v41]` fail with `assert 0.0 == 1.0` at `test_deepseek_v4_vl_stream_weights.py:65` while `[v4]` still passes, so the test does cover the regression.

Unit test for the loader log line, parametrized over a single-model and a multi-model process:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_registry.py -v -p no:cacheprovider
```

```
tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_registry.py::test_loading_weights_took_names_the_model_only_for_multiple_models[False] PASSED [ 90%]
tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_registry.py::test_loading_weights_took_names_the_model_only_for_multiple_models[True] PASSED [100%]
======================= 11 passed, 14 warnings in 3.53s ========================
```

Restoring the unconditional variant makes `[False]` fail, so the test pins the "named only when several models are loaded" behavior.

## Details

**Root cause.** `AutoWeightsLoader._groupby_prefix` groups with `itertools.groupby` on the first path component (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/255f14599ec0544c35539414810abdfa7e4e1c86/vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py#L263-L281), so a child module is delegated once per *contiguous* run of its names, and the V4.1 language model finalizes fused expert weights inside `load_weights` and must be called exactly once. `sorted()` therefore drained the mmap-view generator (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/255f14599ec0544c35539414810abdfa7e4e1c86/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py#L1083) while the tqdm bar is driven by the shard loop (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/255f14599ec0544c35539414810abdfa7e4e1c86/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py#L1169), leaving every `copy_` for after the bar.

**Alternative considered.** `finalizes_weights_during_load = False` (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/255f14599ec0544c35539414810abdfa7e4e1c86/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py#L1466) would drop the contiguity requirement, but nothing on this path reads the flag and it would move the backbone's finalization (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/255f14599ec0544c35539414810abdfa7e4e1c86/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py#L1404-L1412) after per-layer quantization finalize; left as a follow-up.

**Behavior changes.**

- No API, configuration or numerical change: same tensors, same order, finalization at the same point.
- The shard bar is slower per shard because it now includes the copies; total load time is lower and the post-bar stall is gone.
- `Loading weights took` gains a ` (model=<Class>)` suffix only in processes that load more than one model.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve DP rank in Responses requests
body:
## Overview

Forward `X-data-parallel-rank` from the Responses API to the engine, matching Chat Completions. This prevents the frontend from silently discarding a gateway's selected DP replica.

## Claims

- Preserve the selected rank for streaming and non-streaming Responses requests, including subsequent built-in tool turns.
- Keep existing default routing when the header is absent or cannot be parsed; rank zero is preserved.

## Validation

On upstream base `fb61ac07bd1d5b8b9722c80085b99ef770efb265`, Python 3.12.13, CPU platform with accelerator visibility disabled:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py \
  -k 'responses_data_parallel_rank or harmony_tool_followup_preserves_render_params' -v -ra --tb=short
```

Result: **11 passed, 66 deselected**, no skips. Tests exercise header parsing through the Responses serving entrypoint to `engine.generate`, and reuse the existing tool-follow-up test. They are included in the existing Buildkite Responses test area.

Serving reproduction on an Ascend-native downstream deployment with a DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model, Mooncake PD, prefill TP4/DP4 and decode TP8/DP2:

| Request | Before forwarding | After forwarding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Same reconstructed streaming Responses request, reasoning effort `max`, approximately 7.1k prompt tokens | No generated output within 45 seconds; decode waiting for KV fetch | Completed in approximately 3 seconds, including text and `response.completed` |

The serving comparison used a runtime implementation of the same rank-forwarding change on prefill API processes, without restarting the model. It validates the routing correction on that deployment; it is not a deployment of this exact upstream commit. The original client tool schemas were unavailable, so this was a reconstructed reproducer, not a byte-identical replay. No accuracy benchmark or general performance improvement is claimed.

## Details

The gateway can select prefill replica R and direct decode to fetch KV from R. Responses previously omitted `data_parallel_rank` from its engine call, allowing internal load balancing to choose another replica. Decode can then wait for KV at the wrong producer. The fix uses the existing header parser and passes the rank explicitly through `_generate_with_builtin_tools` to every `engine.generate` call. No connector-specific behavior or hardware branch is added.

Duplicate-work checks found no existing PR for this fix. Related #40285 changes internal DP coordinator notifications, and #49246 adds PCP/DP support; neither changes Responses rank forwarding.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, and test this change.

title: [Bugfix][DeepSeek V4.1] Fix system-only prompt rendering
body:
## Overview

Fix DeepSeek V4.1 prompt rendering when the final rendered message is a
`system` message. This covers a `system`-only request and a leading `system`
message before an `assistant` history turn. The V4.1 encoder only appends the
assistant transition for system messages at index > 0, so these prompts ended
at the system role and generation could stop immediately or continue the
system text.

This mirrors the V4 fix from #51262 in both the Python tokenizer and the Rust
frontend.

## Claims

- A `system`-only chat request now renders `<｜Assistant｜><think>` (thinking)
  or `<｜Assistant｜></think>` (chat) and returns a normal response instead of
  an empty or malformed one.
- A leading `system` message followed by an `assistant` turn now gets the
  assistant header, so the history turn is no longer concatenated
  (`rulesanswer` -> `rules<｜Assistant｜></think>answer`).
- V4 rendering is unchanged. The removed Rust dialect guard was already true
  for V4, and the V4 Python encoder already has the #51262 rule.
- Mid-conversation `system` messages and the existing
  `system -> user -> system` behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

### End-to-end

Deployment: vLLM 0.31.0, TP8 + EP.

| Request                                | Result after the fix                                         |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `system` only, thinking on             | normal answer, `prompt_tokens=30`, `reasoning_tokens=39`     |
| `system` only, `reasoning_effort=none` | normal answer, `prompt_tokens=5`, `reasoning=null`, `reasoning_tokens=0` |
| `system` + `user`                      | normal answer, `prompt_tokens=37`                            |
| `system` + `user` + trailing `system`  | normal answer, `prompt_tokens=45`                            |

Reproducer:

```bash
curl -s http://HOST/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "dsv41-flash",
    "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "Hello"}],
    "reasoning_effort": "none",
    "stream": false
  }'
```

```json
{
  "choices": [{
    "message": {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "Hello! How can6 can I help you today?",
      "reasoning": null
    },
    "finish_reason": "stop"
  }],
  "usage": {
    "prompt_tokens": 5,
    "total_tokens": 17,
    "completion_tokens": 12,
    "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}
  }
}
```

Before the fix, the same request rendered:

```jinja2
<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜System｜>Hello
```

and could return an empty or abnormal response. After the fix it renders:

```jinja2
<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜System｜>Hello<｜Assistant｜></think>
```

The reported `prompt_tokens=5` matches BOS + `<｜System｜>` + content +
`<｜Assistant｜></think>`, i.e. the two transition tokens are present. The
thinking-on request similarly reports `prompt_tokens=30` and a populated
`reasoning` field, confirming that `<｜Assistant｜><think>` is in the prompt.

### Unit tests

Python:

Adds:

- `test_system_only_request_opens_generation_turn`
- `test_system_only_request_opens_thinking_turn`
- `test_leading_system_before_assistant_gets_assistant_header`

Rust:

Updates `system_after_dropped_developer_becomes_leading_system` and adds:

- `system_only_opens_assistant_turn_in_chat_and_thinking_modes`
- `system_to_assistant_transitions_in_chat_and_thinking_modes`



## Details

Root cause: `render_message()` in
`vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v41_encoding.py` appends the assistant transition
only when `role == "system" and index > 0`. A leading system message is
rendered at index 0, so a system-only request ends the prompt at the system
content. The model has no `<｜Assistant｜>` role marker and can emit EOS
immediately or continue the system text.

Fix: append the transition when the system message is the last message or is
followed by an assistant message, matching the V4 rule merged in #51262.
Mid-conversation system messages keep their existing behavior.

Rust: `render_request_with_media_order()` in
`rust/src/chat/src/renderer/deepseek.rs` already gates the transition on
`should_write_transition()` (next assistant, or final message with
`add_generation_prompt`). The change only adds V4.1 system messages to the set
of entries considered for the transition, so:

- leading system + user/developer/system: no transition (unchanged)
- leading system as the final message: transition (fixed)
- leading system + assistant: transition (fixed)
- mid-conversation system: unchanged

No documentation update is needed. This restores existing tokenizer behavior
without adding options or APIs.

title: [Perf][SM90] Score only candidate blocks in the DSv4.1 decode indexer
body:
## Overview

Add a Triton candidate-only decode scoring path for DeepSeek V4.1 on SM90,
reading FP8 K directly from the paged indexer cache instead of scoring the
full context and masking it afterwards.

Related to #61830. This is a separate implementation from the gather-based
prototype in draft #62000: it avoids the intermediate candidate-K buffer.
The flag is off by default (`VLLM_DSA_CANDIDATE_PAGED_DECODE=1` to enable).

## Claims

- On H20 TP8 with ~1M input tokens, the evalscope A/B below measured a
  **9.6–23.8% reduction in mean ITL** across concurrency 1/2/4/8.
- Consumer logits use 16,384 candidate columns instead of the full compressed
  context. The candidate-source layers, pre-candidate layers and prefill path
  are unchanged.
- Path selection uses configuration checks, not capture-time context lengths.
  Live lengths and page tables remain device inputs during CUDA graph replay.

These results cover the measured long-context workload, not a general
no-regression claim. Accuracy and shorter-workload checks are still pending.

## Validation

### Environment

- Machine: 8x NVIDIA H20 96GB, TP8; driver 535.161.08, CUDA 13.0
- Software: torch 2.14.0+cu130, triton 3.8.0, deep_gemm 2.8.1, vLLM at this
  PR's commit
- Server: `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 16
  --enable-prefix-caching`, speculative decoding with
  `num_speculative_tokens=5`. The A/B runs differ only in
  `VLLM_DSA_CANDIDATE_PAGED_DECODE` (0 vs 1)

### Test guards

```bash
pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_candidate_paged_logits.py
```

The tests cover:

- **Scores and selection:** candidate logits against an FP32 reference
  (`rtol=2e-2`, `atol=1e-2`), plus selected-set comparisons for `persistent`
  and `auto` top-k. This is kernel-level coverage, not model accuracy.
- **Cache layout:** page gaps of 0/64/260 bytes with block sizes 16/64;
  invalid cache entry widths are rejected.
- **Bounds:** empty contexts, padded/out-of-range candidate blocks, and
  per-row causal limits during speculative decoding.
- **CUDA graphs:** capture on a short context, replay with changed lengths
  and page tables, then compare against eager execution.
- **Gating and workspace:** default-off behavior, rejected configurations,
  and reuse of the reserved workspace without growth during capture.
- **Performance smoke test:** an effective-bandwidth threshold over the
  candidate path, intended to catch severe regressions, not to measure
  isolated HBM bandwidth.

The current L4 attention CI job skips the SM90 GPU cases. A saved H20 pytest
report for the submitted revision is still needed; the coverage above does
not imply those cases passed in CI.

### End-to-end A/B (1M context)

I ran both configurations on the same commit with the same client arguments.
There is one run per configuration, with 2/4/8/16 measured requests at
concurrency 1/2/4/8 respectively. Set `MODEL` to the served model name and
`TOKENIZER_PATH` to the matching local checkpoint:

```bash
evalscope perf \
  --model "$MODEL" --api openai --stream --api-key EMPTY \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:8021/v1/chat/completions \
  --dataset random --tokenizer-path "$TOKENIZER_PATH" \
  --prefix-length 1028976 --min-prompt-length 1024 --max-prompt-length 1024 \
  --number 2 4 8 16 --parallel 1 2 4 8 --warmup-num 1 \
  --max-tokens 16384 --temperature 0.7 --top-p 0.95 --seed 42 \
  --extra-args '{"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}, "ignore_eos": true}'
```

The logs report 1,029,974 input tokens and 16,384 output tokens per request.
The configured prefix length is 1,028,976; input counts above are the measured
counts after prompt construction, not a sum of the CLI length arguments.
The tables report zero cached prompt tokens, but that alone does not verify
server-side prefix-cache hits, especially with this shared-prefix workload.

| Conc. | ITL avg (ms) dense -> cand | ITL p50 (ms) dense -> cand | ITL p90 (ms) dense -> cand |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 12.27 -> 11.09 (**-9.6%**) | 12.28 -> 11.14 (-9.3%) | 12.73 -> 11.73 (-7.9%) |
| 2 | 15.85 -> 13.68 (**-13.7%**) | 16.11 -> 13.50 (-16.2%) | 16.50 -> 14.37 (-12.9%) |
| 4 | 23.01 -> 18.31 (**-20.4%**) | 23.11 -> 18.81 (-18.6%) | 23.64 -> 19.47 (-17.6%) |
| 8 | 35.14 -> 26.78 (**-23.8%**) | 37.19 -> 27.05 (-27.3%) | 38.04 -> 27.88 (-26.7%) |

Secondary metrics from the same runs:

| Conc. | Decode toks/s | Spec. accept dense -> cand | TTFT avg (ms) dense -> cand |
| ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | +20.6% | 81.6% -> 83.0% | 4879.9 -> 4631.7 (-5.1%) |
| 2 | +30.1% | 81.7% -> 83.5% | 5822.9 -> 6107.6 (+4.9%) |
| 4 | +13.3% | 82.0% -> 80.8% | 8322.4 -> 7800.7 (-6.3%) |
| 8 | +21.5% | 81.8% -> 80.8% | 11900.4 -> 11179.7 (-6.1%) |

I use ITL as the main latency metric here, with TPOT and throughput as
supporting results. Under speculative decoding, streamed chunks can contain
multiple tokens: client ITL is not necessarily one GPU iteration, nor is it
independent of acceptance, scheduling or buffering. TPOT remains a valid
user-facing metric, but neither metric alone isolates the kernel change.

This is one A/B pair, not a confidence-interval result. Many intervals within
the same requests do not replace independent runs. At concurrency 4, overall
completion throughput was 827.33 -> 814.72 tok/s (-1.5%) despite lower ITL,
so this is not a throughput win at every concurrency.

I also ran an earlier TP4 test at 200K context. It showed a much smaller ITL
change; the TP8 evalscope run and trace below are the main evidence here.

### Kernel-level trace

The measurement record uses **PyTorch Profiler**, with 100 decode iterations
at ~1M context and client concurrency 12. On rank 0:

| Observation | Dense | Candidate-only |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Mean decode rows/step | 55.2 | 44.3 |
| Scoring time/call | 2027.0 us | 56.4 us |
| Candidate expansion + remap/call | — | 8.2 + 1.8 us |
| Candidate mask + flags, total | 68.10 ms | absent |
| Cooperative top-k time/call | 221.1 us | 94.2 us |

The dense scoring bucket groups the candidate source and four consumers;
the new scoring kernel runs only for the four consumers. All eight ranks
show the new kernel and no consumer mask kernel (400 scoring calls per rank).
This confirms that serving actually exercises the new path.

The batches differ, so these are attribution measurements, not a matched-load
speedup. Even dividing by row count does not fully remove differences in
occupancy and batch composition. End-to-end latency comes from evalscope,
not the profiler's summed CUDA time.

### Accuracy

Model-level accuracy results are pending. I'll compare the flag on and off
with lm-eval and add the results here before merge. Kernel tests alone do not
establish model accuracy. Other SM90 GPUs have not been tested.

## Details

The path prepares per-row candidate blocks and causal bounds, reads candidate
K directly through the page table, scores into a compact buffer, runs the
existing top-k, and remaps the selected columns to request-local positions.
It reuses candidate preparation and remapping from vLLM's SM100 sparse path.
FP8 dot products use FP32 accumulation; invalid columns are masked and valid
column counts are passed to top-k.

For the tested model, `index_head_dim=128`, `index_n_heads=32`,
`candidate_topk_blocks=2048`, `candidate_block_size=8`, and `index_topk=512`.
The compact FP32 logits buffer is `[rows, 16384]` (1.5 MiB at 24 rows).
With five speculative tokens, six decode rows represent one fully populated
request in the kernel input; this is not necessarily the client's concurrent
request count because scheduling and graph padding can change the batch.

The path requires SM90, an FP8 indexer cache, no DCP/PCP, and supported
candidate geometry. When disabled or rejected by the availability check, the
existing dispatch remains in use; existing unsupported combinations may still
raise errors. The gate has no batch-size or context-length profitability
threshold. Avoiding a K copy does not remove preparation, sorting, top-k and
remapping costs, so short-context performance still needs checking.

## What's next

- **Accuracy:** compare lm-eval results with the flag off and on.
- **Performance outside 1M:** benchmark shorter contexts, small batches and
  smaller real datasets to check for latency or throughput regressions.
- **Kernel work:** try a CUDA/CUTLASS implementation and compare it with
  Triton. I'll profile scoring, candidate preparation and top-k before
  deciding which part to optimize; there is no measured speedup for this yet.

I'd appreciate feedback on the implementation while I finish the accuracy and
short-workload checks. Those results still need to be confirmed before merge.
Prefill optimization is outside this PR.

---

- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.

</details>

title: [Bug]: persistent_topk returns indices past the row length when length % 4 != 0 and fewer than k scores are above -inf
body:
### Your current environment
Summary of python collect_env.py ```text vLLM Version : 0.32.1rc1.dev61+g3e96f9cf6 (main, git sha 3e96f9cf6) PyTorch : 2.14.0+cu130 CUDA runtime : 13.0.88 GPU : NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (sm_103), driver 610.43.02 Python : 3.12.13 OS : Linux 6.12 (x86_64) ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `torch.ops._C.persistent_topk` can return indices `>= lengths[row]`. It happens on the `histogram_2048_topk` path in `csrc/persistent_topk.cuh` (k < length <= 8192, at most 32 rows) when: - the row length is not a multiple of 4, and - fewer than k of the row's scores are above the fp16 `-inf` bin. Any score at or below about -65504 lands in that bin, so `-inf`, `-1e30` and `-7e4` all count. Cause: the last float4 load of the row (`load_float4_predicated`) fills the lanes past `seq_len` with `-inf`. Those lanes get binned like real elements. The collection loop checks only `vec_valid = i < n_vec`, never `elem_idx < seq_len`. When the threshold lands in the `-inf` bin, the tail lanes become candidates. The refinement pass then reads `logits[idx]` past the row and can select them. If the row ends at the end of the allocation, those reads are out of bounds. Where it could matter: DeepSeek V4.1 two-level selection (`apply_candidate_mask`) writes `-inf` inside decode rows before the top-k. If a row's candidate blocks cover fewer than `index_topk` positions, the threshold lands in the `-inf` bin. The shipped DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash config keeps 2048 candidate blocks of 8 (16384 positions), so every row on this path (<= 8192) is fully covered. I found no shipped model or default config that reaches the bug end to end. The other callers produce finite in-row scores: the DSA decode indexer (V3.2 / GLM-5 style), Qwen4-exp QSA, and Step5, which rejects this backend. The persistent backend is used with `--sparse-indexer-topk-backend persistent`, with `auto` on SM12x and pre-SM90 GPUs, and with `auto` when the logits row stride is not divisible by 4. If the bug is hit, `triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index` only drops `tok < 0`, so a bad index becomes a wrong KV slot with no error. Minimal repro (the public op only): ```python import torch import vllm._custom_ops # noqa: F401 (registers torch.ops._C) K, STRIDE = 512, 516 ws = torch.empty(1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda") for length in (513, 514, 515, 516): logits = torch.zeros(1, STRIDE, device="cuda") logits[0, :length] = float("-inf") # every in-row score is -inf lengths = torch.tensor([length], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") out = torch.full((1, K), -2, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") torch.ops._C.persistent_topk(logits, lengths, out, ws, K, STRIDE) bad = sorted(i for i in out[0].tolist() if i >= length) print(f"length={length}: {len(bad)} indices >= length {bad}") ``` Output on main (B300): ```text length=513: 3 indices >= length [513, 514, 515] length=514: 2 indices >= length [514, 515] length=515: 1 indices >= length [515] length=516: 0 indices >= length [] ``` Expected: no index >= length. Filling the row with `-1e30` or `-7e4` gives the same result; `-6e4` (above the fp16 range limit) does not. compute-sanitizer, with one row of length 513 that is also the tensor width (`PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1 compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck python repro_sanitizer.py`): ```text ========= Invalid __global__ read of size 4 bytes ========= at ... void vllm::persistent::histogram_2048_topk<(int)512>(const float *, int *, int)+0xe490 ========= Access to 0x7f1a2c000804 is out of bounds ========= and is 1 bytes after the nearest allocation at 0x7f1a2c000000 of size 2052 bytes (3 invalid reads; the kernel then aborts with "unspecified launch failure") ``` Layer-level repro of the V4.1 decode composition (`apply_candidate_mask`, then `SparseIndexerTopk("persistent")`), with a candidate set smaller than k (32 blocks x 8 = 256 < 512), 4 rows of lengths 1001/2003/3001/4093: on main, row 0 (length 1001) gets index 1002. The `torch` reference backend returns no index >= length. Which tail lane gets picked among the `-inf` ties varies, so not every row shows it. `cooperative_topk` and the other `persistent_topk` paths (`histogram_256_topk`, radix) are not affected; they bound their loops by `seq_len`. A fix that skips lanes with `elem_idx >= seq_len` in the collection loop is in PR #62467. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions. --- _Generated with Claude and reviewed by a human._

title: [Deepseek v4.1][ROCm] Fix misleading loading hangs, ~5-10% faster load on cold load
body:
## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on ROCm appeared to hang after the shard progress bar reached 100%:

```
Loading safetensors checkpoint shards:  94% Completed | 45/48 [00:35<00:01,  2.15it/s]
Loading safetensors checkpoint shards:  96% Completed | 46/48 [00:35<00:00,  2.44it/s]
Loading safetensors checkpoint shards: 100% Completed | 48/48 [00:35<00:00,  1.34it/s]

(Worker_TP0 pid=9428) INFO 10-19 08:24:53 [default_loader.py:501] Loading weights took 240.81 seconds
```

This was fixed in #58857 for Nvidia but not AMD.

Cause is the AMD multimodal wrapper sorted the entire weight stream, which drained the lazy iterator before any weight had been copied, so all real loading happened afterwards with no progress output. That list also made the load itself slower: every shard was read once to build it and touched a second time during the copy phase.

This PR streams the language-model weight group instead, matching `deepseek_v41/nvidia/vl_model.py` and `deepseek_v4/common/vl_model.py`.

This PR also fixes misleading `Loading weights took` logs in case several models (base + draft) are loaded.

## Claims

The AMD V4.1 wrapper was the last place that sorted the entire weight stream before handing it to the child loader (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/255f14599ec0544c35539414810abdfa7e4e1c86/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/vl_model.py#L337-L347); it now streams the language-model group with `stream_language_model_first` (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/255f14599ec0544c35539414810abdfa7e4e1c86/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/vl_model.py#L82-L97), as the NVIDIA V4.1 wrapper already does (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/255f14599ec0544c35539414810abdfa7e4e1c86/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/vl_model.py#L323). Weights are copied while the shard bar advances instead of after it completes, which removes the multi-minute silent phase between `Loading safetensors checkpoint shards: 100%` and the next log line.

Target `Loading weights took` on MI350, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP=4, one run per row, checkpoint evicted from page cache:

| condition | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| warm page cache | 23.0 s | 23–25 s |
| cold page cache | 233.7 s | **213.6 s** |

The ~20 s reduction (~8.6%) comes from the checkpoint no longer being traversed twice — once while the bar advances, then again in sorted order during the copy phase. With a warm cache both branches load in ~23 s and the difference disappears. The message is also attributed to a model (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/255f14599ec0544c35539414810abdfa7e4e1c86/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py#L500-L505), so the target and draft timings of a speculative-decoding worker can be told apart in the log.

Unattributed timings on `main`, cold page cache. The bar completes, then ~3.5 min pass with no output, then both loads report the same message:

```
Loading safetensors checkpoint shards: 100% Completed | 48/48 [00:35<00:00,  1.34it/s]
(Worker_TP0 pid=9428) INFO 10-19 08:24:53 [default_loader.py:501] Loading weights took 240.81 seconds
Loading safetensors checkpoint shards: 100% Completed | 48/48 [00:26<00:00,  1.80it/s]
(Worker_TP0 pid=9428) INFO 10-19 08:25:21 [default_loader.py:501] Loading weights took 26.72 seconds
```

With this change, same command and same conditions. The copies now happen inside the bar:

```
Loading safetensors checkpoint shards:  98% Completed | 47/48 [03:12<00:08,  8.74s/it]
Loading safetensors checkpoint shards: 100% Completed | 48/48 [03:39<00:00, 14.36s/it]
(Worker_TP0 pid=14044) INFO 10-19 12:00:31 [default_loader.py:506] Loading weights took 220.06 seconds (model=DeepseekV41ForCausalLM)
Loading safetensors checkpoint shards: 100% Completed | 48/48 [00:05<00:00,  9.24it/s]
(Worker_TP0 pid=14044) INFO 10-19 12:00:38 [default_loader.py:506] Loading weights took 5.20 seconds (model=DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM)
```

## Validation

Command (ROCm, MI350, TP=4; identical for both branches). The checkpoint is evicted from page cache first, because with a warm cache both branches finish in ~23 s and the difference is not observable:

```bash
# 1. Evict the checkpoint from page cache (advisory, no root needed)
python3 - <<'EOF'
import glob, os
snap = glob.glob(os.path.expanduser(
    "~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--deepseek-ai--DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017/snapshots/*"))[0]
for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(snap, "model-*-of-00048.safetensors")):
    fd = os.open(os.path.realpath(path), os.O_RDONLY)
    os.posix_fadvise(fd, 0, 0, os.POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED)
    os.close(fd)
EOF

# 2. Serve
export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1
export AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1
export VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=INFO
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export MKL_NUM_THREADS=1
export HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3

vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --moe-backend aiter \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --port 8001 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"standard","enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --block-size 64 &> ds_serve.log &
```

Method: the server log was sampled every 30 s during the load.

| | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| shard bar | 42 s, iteration only | 219 s, iteration + copies |
| silent phase after bar | ~210 s | none |
| `Loading weights took` (target) | 240.81 s | 220.06 s |

Unit test for the streaming behavior, enabled for ROCm in this PR (`is_cuda_alike()`, and the V4.1 parameter now resolves through `vllm.models.deepseek_v41`, so on ROCm it exercises `amd/vl_model.py`):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_vl_stream_weights.py -v -p no:cacheprovider
```

```
tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_vl_stream_weights.py::test_load_weights_streams_language_model_group[v4] PASSED [ 50%]
tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_vl_stream_weights.py::test_load_weights_streams_language_model_group[v41] PASSED [100%]
======================== 2 passed, 14 warnings in 2.78s ========================
```

Reverting only `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/vl_model.py` to `main` makes `[v41]` fail with `assert 0.0 == 1.0` at `test_deepseek_v4_vl_stream_weights.py:65` while `[v4]` still passes, so the test does cover the regression.

Unit test for the loader log line:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_registry.py -v -p no:cacheprovider
```

```
tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_registry.py::test_loading_weights_took_names_the_model PASSED [ 83%]
======================= 10 passed, 14 warnings in 3.42s ========================
```

Dropping the model name from the message makes that test fail, so it pins the new format.

## Details

**Root cause.** `AutoWeightsLoader._groupby_prefix` groups with `itertools.groupby` on the first path component (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/255f14599ec0544c35539414810abdfa7e4e1c86/vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py#L263-L281), so a child module is delegated once per *contiguous* run of its names, and the V4.1 language model finalizes fused expert weights inside `load_weights` and must be called exactly once. `sorted()` therefore drained the mmap-view generator (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/255f14599ec0544c35539414810abdfa7e4e1c86/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py#L1083) while the tqdm bar is driven by the shard loop (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/255f14599ec0544c35539414810abdfa7e4e1c86/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py#L1169), leaving every `copy_` for after the bar.

**Alternative considered.** `finalizes_weights_during_load = False` (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/255f14599ec0544c35539414810abdfa7e4e1c86/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py#L1466) would drop the contiguity requirement, but nothing on this path reads the flag and it would move the backbone's finalization (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/255f14599ec0544c35539414810abdfa7e4e1c86/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py#L1404-L1412) after per-layer quantization finalize; left as a follow-up.

**Behavior changes.**

- No API, configuration or numerical change: same tensors, same order, finalization at the same point.
- The shard bar is slower per shard because it now includes the copies; total load time is lower and the post-bar stall is gone.
- `Loading weights took` now always carries a ` (model=<Class>)` suffix, so per-model timings are attributable.

title: [LoRA][Step5] Support LoRA for Step5
body:
## Overview

Adds LoRA support to Step5 (`Step5ForCausalLM` and `Step5ForConditionalGeneration`), added in #61727.

## Claims

- LoRA on attention (`q/k/v/g_proj`), the sparse indexer projections, `sparse_indexer_w`, dense MLPs and routed experts (per-expert keys, via `FusedMoEWithLoRA`), for the text model and the VLM.
- `Step5FusedQKVIndexerWithLoRA` slices LoRA B for the seven fused slices with the layer's own offsets (KV and indexer replication included).
- `Step5SparseIndexerIndexTPLinear` becomes a `ColumnParallelLinear` with its logical index-TP rank/size, so `Step5SparseIndexerWWithLoRA` slices B like the weight loader. Non-LoRA loading is unchanged.

## Validation

GB300, `tests/lora/test_step5_lora.py` (run by the existing `lora` CI step). For every TP rank, the full weight is loaded through the layer's own weight loader, and the LoRA B slices must equal the loaded rows exactly. The fused layer's forward must also return the full `[qkv | indexer]` output.

| Tree | Result |
| --- | --- |
| main (a608b6e6) + new test | collection error: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'vllm.lora.layers.step5'` |
| this PR | 13 passed (fused layer TP 1/2/4/8 × 1/4 indexer KV heads; `sparse_indexer_w` TP 1–16) |
| this PR without `apply = BaseLinearLayerWithLoRA.apply` | 2 failed (TP=1 drops the indexer half of the output) |

## Details

- `share_expert` is renamed with an idempotent regex. The VLM mapper and the text model mapper both apply it, and the old substring rule produced `.moe.moe.share_expert.`.
- LoRA is rejected with `moe_backend='deep_gemm_mega_moe'`: its experts are not `FusedMoE`, and its sequence-parallel mode gives the MLP linears `N/tp` tokens.
- `fully_sharded_loras` leaves these two layers without LoRA, like other custom linear subclasses.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] DeepSeek V4.1: don't leak a `<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>` opener into content
body:
## Overview

The `deepseek_v41` parser now accepts `<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>` (V4's wrapper name, V4.1's spacing) as a tool-call opener, so it no longer leaks into `content`. Part of #62051 (the "V4 spelling" row); the other rows are not changed here.

## Claims

- For V4.1 output whose tool block opens with `<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>`, the opener no longer appears in `content`, in both streaming and non-streaming. The tool calls are parsed as before.
- Like the canonical `<｜DSML｜ calls>`, this opener also ends an open reasoning block.
- No change for the canonical spelling, the unspaced V4 spelling, or truncated calls.

## Validation

The table uses the inputs from #62051, run through `DeepSeekV41EngineToolParser` on CPU (non-streaming, and streaming one character at a time followed by `finish_streaming()`):

| Model output | main @ `bde4d00113` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `\n\n<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>\n<｜DSML｜ invoke name="WebFetch">…</｜DSML｜ tool_calls>` | call `WebFetch {"url": "https://x.com"}`, but `content` = `"\n\n<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>\n"` | same call; the opener is not in `content` |
| Well-formed `<｜DSML｜ calls>` block | call parsed, `content` = `"Hi\n\n"` | unchanged |
| Unspaced V4 block (`<｜DSML｜tool_calls>…`) | returned as text, no call | unchanged |
| Truncated value / truncated name / block without an invoke | as described in #62051 | unchanged (rows 2-3 are #62259) |

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v32.py
```

- New `test_v4_wrapper_name_opens_tool_block` (streaming at chunk sizes 1/7/10000, plus non-streaming, thinking on and off) and `test_v4_wrapper_name_ends_reasoning`. All 7 cases fail on main and pass with this change.
- All 147 tests in the three DeepSeek parser test files pass.
- `tests/parser` and `tests/tool_parsers`: 8064 passed vs. 8057 on main (the 7 new tests). Both have the same 15 errors, all in `test_llama3_json_tool_parser.py`, which needs the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes.

Validated with parser-level tests on CPU only; I did not serve DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. The change is limited to the parser config, and these tests run in CI under the existing `parser` step in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`.

## Details

**Root cause:** `deepseek_v41_config` replaces V4's `TOOL_START` (canonical spelling plus `DSML_TOOL_START_VARIANTS`) with the single string `<｜DSML｜ calls>`. When the block opens with `<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>`, the V4.1 invoke that follows still matches through the existing `(CONTENT, INVOKE_PREFIX)` transition, so the call is parsed. The opener before it, however, stays in `CONTENT` and is emitted as text.

**Fix:** add it as a `TOOL_START` variant in `deepseek_v41.py`, the same way #56141 added misspelled wrappers to the V4 config. `token_id_terminals` is unchanged: in the V4.1 tokenizer only `｜DSML｜` is an added token (non-special), so the tags reach the parser as text.

**Notes for reviewers:**

- A prose mention of `<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>` now behaves like a prose mention of `<｜DSML｜ calls>`: it opens a tool block. This matches what #56141 accepted for the V4 variants.
- **Open question (the "unspaced V4 spelling" row of #62051):** a fully V4-spelled block (`<｜DSML｜tool_calls>`, `<｜DSML｜invoke …>`) is still returned as text. That matches the Rust frontend, which keeps V4 tags as text in the V4.1 dialect on purpose (`v4_tags_remain_text_in_v41_dialect`, #56208). If V4.1 should accept V4 spellings, I can do that in both frontends in a follow-up.
- **Rust frontend:** it parses invokes only inside a recognised block, so it returns this whole block as text, and this PR doesn't change that. I can align it in a follow-up if you'd like.
- Related: #62259 (truncation rows of #62051) touches other parts of the same file. #61142 (another V4.1 opener drift) edits the same config; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

title: [ROCm][CI] Bump the default ROCm image to ROCm 10.1; use TheRock's triton wheel
body:
Bumps the default TheRock image from ROCm 10.0 to 10.1, keeping torch 2.13 (`2.13.0+rocm10.1.0`).

TheRock's 10.1 torch pins `triton==3.8.0+git669b31ac.rocm10.1.0`, the `release/internal/3.8.x` commit we build from source today, so this also:
- installs TheRock's triton wheel; drops the triton source build, the torch repack and the torch METADATA edit
- drops the nightly extra index: every pin resolves from `stable.repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-next`
- deletes the unused `requirements/build/rock.txt`, refreshes `requirements/build/rocm.txt`

The variant becomes `rocm101` (setup.py derives it from the SDK version): renames the release pipeline's `rocm100` steps and the perf-eval image tag, and updates the install docs. `:nightly`/`:latest` move to 10.1; `nightly-rocm100` stops updating.

**Open**
- `build_rocm_runtime` (patched ROCr/CLR from rocm-systems `25e14349`) is kept; need to confirm it still builds on 10.1 / whether 10.1 already carries the fixes
- Recipes pinned to `nightly-rocm100` (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Kimi-K3) need re-verification on `nightly-rocm101` by their owners

Conflicts with #61939 and #62530 (same `Dockerfile.rocm_base` lines); will rebase. No other open PR bumps ROCm to 10.1.

**Test**
- `pip install --dry-run` (stable index only) of SDK 10.1, torch/torchvision/torchaudio, device extras and triton: resolves, all from stable
- `therock_wheels.py external-links` with the new Dockerfile + real torch wheel: all 36 linked projects (9 arches) found
- Image build + GPU tests: pending CI

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; I reviewed every change.

title: [RFC]: [V1 Scheduler][KV Offload] Eliminate 1.0–1.8s Re-Queueing Stall for Completed Async KV Pulls via Front-of-Queue Re-Admission
body:
### Motivation. ## Motivation & Problem Summary When running vLLM V1 (`main`) with asynchronous KV cache pulling—such as `OffloadingConnector` configured with `TieringOffloadingSpec` (`CPUPrimaryTierOffloadingManager` + `p2p` secondary tier over RoCE RDMA) or remote KV connectors (`NixlConnector`, `MooncakeConnector`)—there is a **5×–7× gap** between **hardware KV transfer latency** and **end-to-end pull latency on a busy destination pod (`WaitingQueueSize >= 1`)**: - **Idle Destination Pod (`WaitingQueueSize == 0`)**: On `NVIDIA H200` GPUs with `200 Gbps` RoCE v2 RDMA (`mlx5`), pulling a `49,152`-token cached prefix (`1.82 GB` on `openai/gpt-oss-120b`; `4.83 GB` on `Qwen3-30B-A3B`) takes only **`207.6 ms` (`20 ms` fixed + `3.8 µs/token`)** on Monolithic and **`282.6 ms` (`24.8 ms` fixed + `5.3 µs/token`)** on Disaggregated P/D—**`8.6×` to `10.0×` faster** than local GPU prefill recomputation (`1,874 ms` to `2,280 ms`). - **Busy Destination Pod (`WaitingQueueSize >= 1`)**: When the exact same P2P pull executes on a destination pod with concurrent traffic, OLS calibration across multi-turn agentic workloads reveals **two large scheduler re-admission stalls**: 1. **Stage 1 Re-Queue Stall (`transferFixedMs` = `419 ms`, up `21×` from `20 ms` idle)** while waiting in `self.waiting` during and after `Secondary Tier (P2P) -> Primary Tier (CPU RAM)` promotion. 2. **Stage 2 Re-Queue Stall (`requeueMs` = `637 ms` on Monolithic / `1,410 ms` on Disaggregated P/D)** while waiting in `self.kv_holding_waiting` (`KV_FETCH_COMPLETED_WAITING`) after `Primary Tier (CPU RAM) / Remote -> GPU HBM` (`WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`) completes. Over **`80%` of the wall-clock time of a loaded KV pull (`1,056 ms` to `1,829 ms` of queueing delay vs. `~200 ms` of actual wire + PCIe transfer)** is spent waiting to be re-admitted by the V1 scheduler *after* the KV cache blocks have already arrived. --- ## Root-Cause Analysis (Against `vllm` `main`) Consider a destination pod receiving **Request `R`** (`48,000` cached prefix tokens on a remote peer + `256` uncached suffix tokens) alongside **Cold Request `C`** (`49,000` uncached tokens). ``` [ R arrives at Destination Pod ] │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Queue 1: self.waiting (Holds 0 GPU HBM blocks) │ │ • Hop 1 runs here: Remote Peer ──(RoCE RDMA)──► Local CPU Primary Tier │ │ • TieringOffloadingManager.lookup() returns RETRY / HIT_PENDING │ │ -> get_num_new_matched_tokens() returns (None, False). │ │ • Scheduler.schedule() (L1041–L1046) calls skip_request(self.waiting) │ │ and continues scanning younger requests, admitting Cold Request C │ │ into self.running (L1408) for a 6-step, 49K-token cold prefill. │ │ • STALL 1: When Hop 1 finishes in _complete_promotion() (L456–L496): │ │ (a) R is NOT moved to the head of self.waiting, and │ │ (b) primary_tier.complete_write() drops ref_cnt from -1 to 0 (L485, L834),│ │ leaving R's promoted CPU chunks evictable before R is re-scanned! │ └───────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘ │ Scheduler eventually re-scans R -> allocates 48K GPU HBM blocks (L1313) │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Queue 2: self.kv_holding_waiting (Holds 48K GPU HBM blocks = 1.8–4.8 GB!) │ │ • Hop 2 runs here: Local CPU Primary Tier ──(PCIe DMA)──► Local GPU HBM │ │ • R sits in self.kv_holding_waiting with status = WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS. │ │ • STALL 2: When Hop 2 finishes in _update_from_kv_xfer_finished() (L3318), │ │ R enters stage KV_FETCH_COMPLETED_WAITING (L3319). R already holds │ │ 1.8–4.8 GB of locked GPU HBM and only needs 256 tokens (~10 ms) of │ │ compute, yet R is starved of token_budget by C's multi-chunk cold prefill │ │ in self.running (L712–L943) and sits behind unready requests in │ │ self.kv_holding_waiting! │ └───────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Queue 3: self.running (GPU Execution) │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ### Fault 1 (Stage 1 — `self.waiting`): No Front-of-Queue Promotion & Unpinned CPU Chunks After `_complete_promotion()` In [`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/manager.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/manager.py) and [`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py): 1. **Leapfrogging & Scan Breakage in `self.waiting`**: - When `TieringOffloadingManager.lookup()` (`tiering/manager.py#L584-L666`) initiates a secondary-to-primary promotion via `_initiate_promotion()` (`#L677-L729`), it returns `LookupResult.HIT_PENDING` (`#L653`) or `LookupResult.RETRY` (`#L665`). - In [`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py) (`_maximal_prefix_lookup`, `#L766-L775`), both `HIT_PENDING` and `RETRY` set `defer_lookup = True`, so `get_num_new_matched_tokens()` (`#L1109-L1171`) returns `(None, False)`. - In `Scheduler.schedule()` (`scheduler.py#L1041-L1046`), `if ext_tokens is None:` calls `skip_request(request_queue)` and `continue`, allowing younger cold requests (`C`) behind `R` in `self.waiting` to be popped (`#L1406`) and admitted into `self.running` (`#L1408`). - Meanwhile, if any request `A` ahead of `R` in `self.waiting` fails block allocation (`new_blocks is None` at `scheduler.py#L1332-L1339`), the `while token_budget > 0:` loop executes **`break`** (`#L1339`) and stops scanning `self.waiting` before ever reaching `R`—even if `R`'s promotion into CPU RAM has already completed! 2. **Unprotected CPU Eviction Window (`ref_cnt == 0`) Right After `_complete_promotion()`**: - In `TieringOffloadingManager._complete_promotion()` (`tiering/manager.py#L456-L496`), as soon as the `secondary -> primary` transfer completes, lines `484–489` call: ```python if successful_keys: self.primary_tier.complete_write( successful_keys, transfer_job.req_context, True, ) ``` - As explicitly noted in `TieringOffloadingManager.prepare_store()` (`tiering/manager.py#L833-L848`), `_process_finished_jobs()` (`#L842`, or the background `vllm_offload_tier_poll` thread in `poll_tiers()` at `#L420`) transitions those promoted chunks from `ref_cnt = -1` to **`ref_cnt = 0` ("making it evictable for the first time")** *before* `R` is re-scanned by the scheduler and pins them via `prepare_load()` (`#L757-L776`). - Consequently, a running request calling `prepare_store()` (`#L848`) can immediately evict `R`'s freshly pulled P2P chunks from `primary_tier` while `R` is still waiting in `self.waiting`! ### Fault 2 (Stage 2 — `self.kv_holding_waiting`): Starvation in `KV_FETCH_COMPLETED_WAITING` Behind `self.running` Cold Prefill Chunks & Unready Requests In [`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py): Once `R` is re-scanned in `self.waiting` and hits in the CPU primary tier (`load_kv_async = True`), `Scheduler.schedule()` allocates `48,000` tokens of **GPU HBM `KVCacheBlocks` (`1.82–4.83 GB`)** (`#L1313`), sets `request.status = RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` (`#L1386`), and calls `skip_request(request_queue)` (`#L1403`), which places `R` into `self.kv_holding_waiting` (`#L962-L963`, `#L1464`). When the worker finishes the GPU DMA copy (`_update_from_kv_xfer_finished`, `scheduler.py#L3300-L3327`): - Line `3318` adds `req_id` to `self.finished_recving_kv_req_ids`, and line `3319` transitions `R`'s metric stage to **`KV_FETCH_COMPLETED_WAITING`**. - At this point, `R` is **already holding `1.82–4.83 GB` of populated GPU HBM blocks** and only needs **`256` uncached suffix tokens (`~10 ms`)** to complete prefill and emit its first token (TTFT). - Yet `R` remains stuck in `KV_FETCH_COMPLETED_WAITING` for `637–1,410 ms` due to two bottlenecks in `Scheduler.schedule()`: 1. **`self.running` Multi-Chunk Cold Prefill Starvation (`scheduler.py#L712-L943`)**: `Scheduler.schedule()` always schedules `self.running` (`#L712`) **before** `self.kv_holding_waiting` (`#L970`). Unless `long_prefill_token_threshold` (`#L678`, default `0`) is set, an in-progress cold prefill chunk (`request.is_prefill_chunk == True`) in `self.running` consumes **100% of `token_budget` (`max_num_scheduled_tokens`)** at `#L765` / `#L911`. When execution reaches `while token_budget > 0:` for `self.kv_holding_waiting` at `#L967`, **`token_budget == 0`**! Thus `R` sits starved in `self.kv_holding_waiting` step after step—locking gigabytes of GPU HBM—waiting for `C` to finish all of its cold prefill chunks in `self.running`. 2. **No Front-of-Queue Prepending in `self.kv_holding_waiting` (`scheduler.py#L3313-L3320` & `#L3266-L3281`)**: When `_update_from_kv_xfer_finished()` (`#L3318`) marks `R` as `KV_FETCH_COMPLETED_WAITING`, `R` stays at its existing position inside `self.kv_holding_waiting` behind older requests whose `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` transfer is still in flight (or behind a request in `self.kv_holding_waiting` whose suffix allocation fails and triggers `break` at `#L1339`). --- We are happy to submit a PR if this direction looks good to the maintainers! ### Proposed Change. ## Proposed Solution: Mechanism 1A & Mechanism 1B Both stalls can be eliminated cleanly using the existing `self.waiting` and `self.kv_holding_waiting` queues (`RequestQueue.remove_request` + `RequestQueue.prepend_request` in [`vllm/v1/core/sched/request_queue.py#L39-L52`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/core/sched/request_queue.py#L39-L52)): ### Mechanism 1A: Front-of-Queue Promotion in `self.waiting` & CPU Read-Pinning on `_complete_promotion()` (4 Files) #### File 1: [`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/manager.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/manager.py) (`TieringOffloadingManager`) 1. **In `TieringOffloadingManager.__init__()` (`~L300`) — Add tracking sets for newly promoted requests and pinned CPU keys**: ```python self._newly_promoted_req_ids: set[str] = set() self._promoted_pins: dict[str, tuple[list[OffloadKey], ReqContext]] = {} ``` 2. **In `TieringOffloadingManager._complete_promotion()` (`#L456-L496`) — Pin promoted CPU chunks (`ref_cnt: 0 -> 1`) and record `req_id` when promotion finishes**: ```python if successful_keys: self.primary_tier.complete_write( successful_keys, transfer_job.req_context, True, ) if transfer_job.req_context is not None: req_id = transfer_job.req_context.req_id # 1. Pin promoted chunks in CPU primary tier (ref_cnt: 0 -> 1) # so prepare_store() (#L848) cannot evict them before R is scheduled: self.primary_tier.prepare_read(successful_keys, transfer_job.req_context) prev_keys, _ = self._promoted_pins.get( req_id, ([], transfer_job.req_context) ) prev_keys.extend(successful_keys) self._promoted_pins[req_id] = (prev_keys, transfer_job.req_context) # 2. Record that req_id finished its secondary -> primary promotion: self._newly_promoted_req_ids.add(req_id) ``` 3. **In `TieringOffloadingManager.prepare_load()` (`#L757`) and `on_request_finished()` (`#L1036`) — Release the temporary read-pin once `prepare_load()` claims the chunks for GPU DMA (or if the request is aborted)**: ```python # At the start of prepare_load(self, keys, req_context) and on_request_finished(self, req_context): pinned = self._promoted_pins.pop(req_context.req_id, None) if pinned is not None: pinned_keys, pinned_ctx = pinned self.primary_tier.complete_read(pinned_keys, pinned_ctx) ``` 4. **Add `pop_newly_promoted_req_ids()` to `TieringOffloadingManager` (after `has_pending_work` at `#L1117`)**: ```python @override def pop_newly_promoted_req_ids(self) -> set[str]: # Ensure any finished secondary -> primary jobs are harvested first: self._maybe_process_finished_jobs() if not self._newly_promoted_req_ids: return set() promoted = self._newly_promoted_req_ids self._newly_promoted_req_ids = set() return promoted ``` #### File 2: [`vllm/v1/kv_offload/base.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/kv_offload/base.py) (`OffloadingManager` Base Interface, `#L648`) Add a default no-op method on the base `OffloadingManager` class so non-tiered managers don't break: ```python def pop_newly_promoted_req_ids(self) -> set[str]: return set() ``` #### File 3: [`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading_connector.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading_connector.py) & [`offloading/scheduler.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py) (and [`v1/base.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/base.py)) Plumb `pop_newly_promoted_req_ids()` through the connector interface so `Scheduler` can call `self.connector.pop_newly_promoted_req_ids()`: - In **`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/base.py`** (`KVConnectorBase_V1`, `#L688`): ```python def pop_newly_promoted_req_ids(self) -> set[str]: return set() ``` - In **`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading_connector.py`** (`OffloadingConnector`, `#L255`): ```python def pop_newly_promoted_req_ids(self) -> set[str]: assert self.connector_scheduler is not None return self.connector_scheduler.pop_newly_promoted_req_ids() ``` - In **`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py`** (`OffloadingConnectorScheduler`, `#L2017`): ```python def pop_newly_promoted_req_ids(self) -> set[str]: self._acquire_step() return self.manager.pop_newly_promoted_req_ids() ``` #### File 4: [`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py) (`Scheduler.schedule()`, right before `#L712`) In `Scheduler.schedule()` right before **Line `712`** (`# First, schedule the RUNNING requests.`), pop newly promoted request IDs (`self.connector.pop_newly_promoted_req_ids()`) and move each matching request in `self.waiting` to the **very front of `self.waiting`**: ```python # [INSERT BEFORE LINE 712 of vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py] if self.connector is not None: promoted_reqs: list[Request] = [] for req_id in self.connector.pop_newly_promoted_req_ids(): req = self.requests.get(req_id) if req is not None and req in self.waiting: self.waiting.remove_request(req) self.deferred_waiting.discard(req) req.priority = -100 # Top of heap in PriorityRequestQueue promoted_reqs.append(req) for req in reversed(promoted_reqs): self.waiting.prepend_request(req) # Index 0 in FCFSRequestQueue ``` --- ### Mechanism 1B: Front-of-Queue Prepending in `self.kv_holding_waiting` & Short-Suffix Priority Over `is_prefill_chunk` *(Note: Mechanism 1B is 100% self-contained in [`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py) in `~25 LOC` and applies universally to **all** async V1 KV connectors—including `OffloadingConnector`, `NixlConnector`, and `MooncakeConnector`.)* 1. **Immediate Head Prepending in `_update_from_kv_xfer_finished()` (`scheduler.py#L3313-L3320`) / Start of `schedule()`**: When a request in `self.kv_holding_waiting` finishes receiving remote KVs (`self.finished_recving_kv_req_ids`), immediately run `_update_waiting_for_remote_kv(req)` (`#L3214`), transition `req.status` to `WAITING`/`PREEMPTED` (`#L3277-L3280`), and prepend `req` to the **very front of `self.kv_holding_waiting`**: ```python def _promote_finished_recving_to_front(self) -> None: if not self.finished_recving_kv_req_ids: return ready_reqs: list[Request] = [] for req_id in list(self.finished_recving_kv_req_ids): req = self.requests.get(req_id) if req is None or req.status != RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS: continue self._update_waiting_for_remote_kv(req) req.status = ( RequestStatus.PREEMPTED if req.num_preemptions else RequestStatus.WAITING ) self.kv_holding_waiting.remove_request(req) self.deferred_waiting.discard(req) req.priority = -100 ready_reqs.append(req) for req in reversed(ready_reqs): self.kv_holding_waiting.prepend_request(req) ``` 2. **Drain `KV_FETCH_COMPLETED_WAITING` Requests Before In-Progress Cold Prefill Chunks (`request.is_prefill_chunk` in `self.running`, `#L712-L943`)**: When `self.kv_holding_waiting` has ready requests at its head (which already hold gigabytes of allocated GPU HBM and only need their uncached suffix tokens to finish prefill), do not let `request.is_prefill_chunk` in `self.running` consume 100% of `token_budget` ahead of them: - **Pass 1**: Schedule running decode requests (`not request.is_prefill_chunk` in `self.running`) so decode ITL/TPOT is completely unaffected. - **Pass 2**: Drain ready requests (`status in (WAITING, PREEMPTED)`) at the head of `self.kv_holding_waiting`. - **Pass 3**: Schedule in-progress cold prefill chunks (`request.is_prefill_chunk` in `self.running`) and `self.waiting` with the remaining `token_budget`. --- ### Feedback Period. _No response_ ### CC List. _No response_ ### Any Other Things. ## Expected Quantitative Impact | Latency Component of a Loaded `49,152`-Token P2P Pull | Current `vllm` `main` | With Mechanism 1A + 1B | Mechanism | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- | | **1. RoCE v2 RDMA Wire Transfer** | `187 ms` *(Mono)* / `258 ms` *(P/D)* | `187 ms` / `258 ms` | Hardware wire speed | | **2. Stage 1 Stall + CPU Staging (`transferFixedMs`)** | `419 ms` | **`~65 ms`** *(PCIe H2D copy only)* | **Mechanism 1A**: Front-of-queue promotion in `self.waiting` + CPU read-pinning in `_complete_promotion()` | | **3. Stage 2 Queue Re-Admission (`requeueMs`)** | `637 ms` *(Mono)* / `1,410 ms` *(P/D)* | **`~15 ms`** *(1 engine step)* | **Mechanism 1B**: Head prepending in `self.kv_holding_waiting` + priority before `is_prefill_chunk` | | **4. Suffix Prefill Compute (`256` tokens)** | `10 ms` | `10 ms` | Tensor Core prefill compute | | **Total Loaded P2P Pull TTFT** | **`1,253 ms` (Mono)**
**`2,097 ms` (P/D)** | **`277 ms` (`4.5×` faster)**
**`348 ms` (`6.0×` faster)** | **Eliminates `976 ms` to `1,749 ms` of queueing delay per pull** | ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Tune MXFP8 block32 GEMM for DEP8 full-shape projections on MI355X
body:
## Summary

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash runs attention **data-parallel** at DP8/EP8 (TP=1), so each rank sees the **full (unsharded)** attention + shared-expert projections. Four of these decode shapes were **not** in the `_TUNED` table for `rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm` and fell through to `_default_config`, which drops to a `128x128x128` tile past M=256 that under-occupies these large-N shapes and roughly **doubles** the per-call cost.

This PR adds tuned tiers for the three shapes that benefit (microbenched per-shape on MI355X, DSpark K6, same method as the existing TP2/TP4 tiers). `shared_down (5120x2304)` was already optimal and is left unchanged. The kernel math is unchanged — only tile selection differs (each candidate was checked to match the baseline output numerically).

## Per-kernel wins (decode M, MI355X)

| Shape | Projection | Win |
|---|---|---|
| `4608 x 5120` | shared gate_up | ~**2.0x** at M≥272 (45→22 µs) |
| `5120 x 8192` | wo_b | ~**1.9x** at M≥272 (61→32 µs); 1.2–1.3x at low M |
| `32768 x 1280` | wq_b | ~**1.4x** at M=224–256 |

## End-to-end (8k/1k, DP8/EP8, MoRI; A/B = these entries on vs off)

| | c256 | c384 |
|---|---|---|
| decode TPOT | −3.9% | −3.8% |
| prefill TTFT | −5.8% | −9.1% |

0 failures over 1k+ requests per side.

## Test plan
- Per-shape microbench vs `_default_config`, with numerical-equality check against the baseline tile.
- End-to-end serving benchmark (8k/1k) at c256/c384, tune on vs off.

title: [Bugfix][Worker] Keep prefill-bearing batches out of FULL (decode-only) cudagraphs
body:
## Purpose

Fixes the DSpark speculative-decoding output corruption reported in #62417 (and any other model where a prefill-bearing batch can land in a FULL cudagraph).

## Root cause

Under `cudagraph_mode=FULL`, MRV2's varlen decode graphs are captured on a decode-shaped batch (num_reqs x 1 token per request, bucketed by padded token count). At dispatch time, a batch that contains prefill tokens sets `max_query_len=None` (documented as "varlen decode graphs replay decodes only"), but `_is_compatible` treats `desc.max_query_len is None` as "no constraint" — so an unconstrained FULL descriptor matches, and the prefill batch is padded into a decode-shaped graph. The query block layout no longer matches the graph's capture shape, and the target's logits for the prefill's last position come out flattened (observed top-1 logit ~16.9 with the top-5 packed within 0.6, vs the usual 26-31 spike); every subsequently generated token is garbage.

We confirmed this on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 + DSpark k=3: `1 req / 6 tokens` was dispatched into a `num_tokens=8, num_reqs=8, cg=FULL` decode graph. Only 4-token prompts (= bucket size, no padding) looked unaffected, which made the bug look content-dependent.

## Fix

Pass `allow_full=False` through `dispatch_cg_and_sync_dp` -> `CudaGraphManager.dispatch` whenever the batch has prefill tokens, and skip FULL candidates in that case. Decode-only batches are unaffected.

## Validation (8x RTX PRO 6000, SM120, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, DSpark k=3, fp8 KV)

Applied on both v0.32.0 and the current nightly:

- 7-probe corruption set (short prefill + thinking scaffold, CJK, cat-repeat, chat, tools): byte-identical to the `--enforce-eager` and cudagraph-NONE baselines after the patch; before the patch, 4/7 emitted degenerate loops from the first token.
- chat + tools end-to-end: `17*19=? answer with the number only` -> reasoning + `content=323`; tools request -> structured `tool_calls` (`get_gpu_alert({"node":"gpu-03"})`).
- token-length sweep 1-12 and 6/7/11/12/13/20/110/455: all clean after the patch.
- `--no-swa-bounded-replay` and `engram cpu_offload=false` variants: logits unchanged (rules out replay/engram interactions).

Co-worker evidence, dispatch debug lines, and the probe corpus are archived in xzwgit/llm-test `dsv41-flash-1017-sm120`; the issue thread has the full isolation matrix.

## Notes

A separate, subtler effect remains after this fix and is tracked in #62417: with DSpark on, greedy generation is not token-identical to no-speculation (first token always matches; occasional later-token divergences, e.g. `.` vs `.\n`). Per-row attention bounds (SWA lens, indexer top-k bounds, verify positions) were verified correct by instrumentation; the divergence is k-independent and graph-mode-independent, pointing at multi-row verify numerics rather than dispatch. That is out of scope for this PR.
