title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Warm up adaptive verification budget kernel at startup
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adaptive verification's draft-budget kernel (`_assign_draft_token_budget`, `torch.compile(dynamic=True)`) never runs at startup. Dynamo therefore compiles it during serving: on the first trimmed step, and again for each specialization it meets later. This PR compiles those specializations at startup.

## Claims

- No budget-kernel compiles during generation (main: 2 per run).
- Adaptive throughput +10% at concurrency 16, matching fixed verification again.
- About 1 s extra startup.

## Validation

`pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py -v` → 18 passed (RTX 5000 Ada). The new test checks that no recompile happens under `fail_on_recompile`. It fails with `warmup()` stubbed out, and with an int32 `idx_mapping`.

`pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage manual` passes locally, including mypy.

GSM8K 1-shot, `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` + `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7`, 7 speculative tokens, probabilistic drafts, concurrency 16, 128 prompts, RTX 5000 Ada, `TRITON_ATTN`. Main and this PR alternated:

| | Output tok/s, median (range) | Compiles during generation | GSM8K accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fixed verification (n=2) | 1,909 | – | 0.828 |
| Adaptive, main (n=5) | 1,738 (1,615–1,753) | 2 | 0.82–0.84 |
| Adaptive, this PR (n=5) | 1,914 (1,710–1,921) | 0 | 0.820 |

An earlier RTX 3090 run (Qwen3.5-0.8B) showed the same: −7.9% before, no loss after.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark script</summary>

Compiles were counted with `TORCH_LOGS=dynamo`, as `start tracing _assign_draft_token_budget` lines between the two markers. "Main" runs used this branch with `vllm/` checked out at `HEAD~1`.

```python
import json
import sys

from tests.evals.gsm8k.gsm8k_eval import evaluate_gsm8k_offline
from vllm import LLM

mode, conc = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2])
llm = LLM(
    model="Qwen/Qwen3-4B",
    speculative_config={
        "method": "dspark",
        "model": "deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 7,
        "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic",
        "enable_adaptive_verification": mode == "adaptive",
    },
    max_num_seqs=conc,
    max_model_len=4096,
    enable_prefix_caching=False,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.9,
    attention_backend="TRITON_ATTN",
)
print("=== GENERATE START ===", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
result = evaluate_gsm8k_offline(llm, num_questions=8 * conc, num_shots=1)
print("=== GENERATE END ===", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
print("RESULT", json.dumps({"mode": mode, "conc": conc, **result}), flush=True)
```

</details>

## Details

- Startup never reaches the kernel: `warmup_kernels` disables adaptive verification, and cost profiling never trims. Dynamo then specializes on a full batch (duck-sized to `confidence_probs`), a single request, and a budget of 1.
- `warmup()` runs batch sizes {1, max−1, max} × budgets {1, 2}. It uses the manager's real buffers and `prepare_inputs`' int64 `idx_mapping` (#60736), since guards check dispatch keys and dtypes. It's skipped on the `profile_only` pass, whose buffers are torn down.
- Not a duplicate: #59976 skips adaptive verification; #58340 only adds metrics.

Sync the Kimi-K3 **GB200: InferenceX AgentX alignment** guide section with the current revision of [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#3748](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3748) (`240ad154`). The section was written from `49a8e45` (vllm-project/recipes#1092, before recipes moved here in #61302). The source PR is still in review on InferenceX; a reviewer there has asked for a smoke test after the NATS removal, and this section will be updated again if that changes the configuration. Only the GB200 section of `recipes/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.yaml` changes.

## Claims

- **Revision link:** point the pinned InferenceX link at `240ad154`. The per-concurrency recipe files were consolidated into variant files there.
- **Disaggregated:** NATS was removed from the lane, and the request plane is TCP, so the services text no longer lists NATS and the environment now includes `DYN_REQUEST_PLANE=tcp`.
- **Aggregated frontend:** this lane runs vLLM's own frontend with no Dynamo install, so it no longer says it runs through Dynamo's frontend.
- **Missing settings filled in from the effective recipes:**
  - Aggregated: `MC_STORE_MEMCPY=1`, `MC_ENABLE_DEST_DEVICE_AFFINITY=1`, `MC_WORKERS_PER_CTX=4`, `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL=0`, `--load-format fastsafetensors`, `--moe-backend auto` and `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`.

- Every value is taken from the InferenceX recipes at `240ad154` (`agg-tp8pp2-variants.yaml`, `disagg-variants.yaml`). Concurrency points (agg c1/c4/c8/c24/c32/c48/c56, disagg c16/c48), parallelism, memory, capture sizes and Mooncake segment sizes are unchanged from the published section.

## Selector (command builder)

**Stacked on #62563** (merge commit `bffe4310`): both PRs add GB200/GB300 keys to the same `pd_cluster` role maps, so this branch builds on #62563 to avoid duplicate YAML keys. Merge #62563 first (or both together).

The GB200 profiles are now builder-backed, scoped to `gb200`:
- **Multi-Node TP + Pipeline Parallel** (`strategy_overrides.multi_node_tp_pp.hardware_overrides.gb200`): TP8 x PP2 + DCP8 across four trays (the strategy alone gives TP4 x PP4 on 4-GPU trays), TRTLLM_RAGGED prefill, `mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16`, `gpu-memory-utilization 0.88`, `--moe-backend auto`, `--language-model-only`, the DSpark K4 draft and the direct-DCP/Mooncake env. Pick Mooncake in the KV Offload row for the store connector.
- **Prefill/Decode Disaggregation** (native and Dynamo routers): `parallelism: {gb200: tp}`, `nodes: {gb200: 4}` on both roles plus a shared `gb200` block (DCP16, TOKENSPEED_MLA + TRTLLM_RAGGED, fp8 KV, prefix caching, cumem allocator, lazy safetensors loading, DSpark K4, env). Prefill: `gpu-memory-utilization 0.88`, `max-num-seqs 32`, capture 512, `VLLM_KIMI_K3_SHARD_SP_SHARED_EXPERT=0`, autotune left on. Decode: TP pool without EP (`--no-data-parallel-hybrid-lb`, default 16384 batched tokens, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE), `gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`, `max-num-seqs 32`, capture 160. The old GB200 decode MegaMoE entry is removed (no EP in this pool).

**Render verification** (`resolveCommand`, rank 0 and followers): every serving flag in the qualified launch lines of [InferenceX run 38450060269](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38450060269) matches (agg: TP8/PP2/DCP8, `--nnodes 4`, followers `--headless`; PD: TP16/DCP16 per role, both roles' memory/batch/capture values at concurrency 16). title: [Model] Add opt-in PrimTS attention for Step5 on SM103
body:
## Overview

Add opt-in PrimTS DSA and sliding-window attention for Step5 on SM103, with BF16 and pure E4M3 QKV. Requires [FlashInfer #6774](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6774); follows merged #61727.

## Claims

- PrimTS handles supported prefill. BF16 decode uses PrimTS at captured/padded batch size ≥32 with MTP=3; FP8 decode always uses PrimTS.
- Reuse Step5's selector, cache producers and gate. Produce FP8 Q in the existing Q/KV kernel and write INT32 selector metadata directly.
- Native remains the default. No scheduler, CUDA graph bucket, or dummy-request changes.

## Validation

On 4×GB300, TP=4/MTP=3, PyTorch 2.13/CUDA 13.0: rebuilt the modified CUDA extension; 29 focused tests and eight decode reference/graph cases passed. Both precisions completed real-checkpoint graph capture, 33 smoke requests, and the evaluations below. The final transfer-only change passed three prefill tests and a sync probe; both final-source sync-check smokes passed (33 requests each with dummy weights).

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/models/step5/test_prims_ts_attention.py \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_qknorm_rope_cache.py
```

Natural prompts, two matched repeats, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, high reasoning, max_tokens 1,000,000 and max_model_len 1,048,576; no invalid answers, truncations, or request errors across 9,282 responses.

| Dataset | Questions/repeat | Native | PrimTS BF16 | PrimTS FP8 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GPQA Diamond | 198 | 92.93% | 94.19% | 92.93% |
| AIME 2024 | 30 | 96.67% | 98.33% | 98.33% |
| GSM8K | 1,319 | 97.19% | 97.65% | 97.65% |

These are two-repeat averages; equal scores do not establish equivalence. Post-evaluation setup fixes remove blocking offset/scale initialization while preserving identical INT32/FP32 values; attention math and routing are unchanged.

Existing H200 CI cannot exercise the SM103 adapter cases; these require the manual GB300 validation above. Historical internal benchmarks are not presented as public-main speedups.

## Details

Enable with `--kernel-config '{"step5_attention_backend":"prims_ts"}'`; choose `--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16` or `fp8_e4m3`. FP8 query dtype follows the backend/cache configuration, independently of batch routing. MTP=3 uses three draft tokens plus one target token (Q=4); the validated configuration uses `--block-size 32` so the FP8 cache page fits the existing MTP tail ring.

The duplicate search found no existing Step5 PrimTS integration; the Qwen-specific PrimTS work is distinct. AI assistance was used to port and validate the previously reviewed integration.

title: [Doc] Add Kimi-K3 GB300 Dynamo disaggregated profile to the recipe selector
body:
## Overview

Add the GB300 Kimi-K3 disaggregated Dynamo + vLLM profile from [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4047](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4047) to the recipe's interactive selector, as requested in [this review comment](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4047#issuecomment-6276636819). #62528 documented the profile as guide text only; this encodes it in the structured `pd_cluster` fields so GB300 + **Prefill/Decode Disaggregation** + the **Dynamo** PD router (`?pd_router=dynamo`) renders the qualified prefill and decode commands. Only `recipes/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.yaml` changes.

## Claims

- GB300-scoped `strategy_overrides.pd_cluster` additions:
  - `hardware_overrides.gb300` (both roles): TP8 + DCP8 (`--decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a`, direct-DCP env), `TOKENSPEED_MLA`, fp8 KV, `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16`, prefix caching with `--prefix-match-unit 128`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`, `--max-cudagraph-capture-size 512`, `--enable-cumem-allocator`, the DSpark K4 draft (`Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark`, probabilistic draft sampling, block verification), and the NCCL/UCX/connector env.
  - Prefill: two trays (`nodes: {gb300: 2}`, TEP8), `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, `trtllm_ragged_backend: cute-dsl`, `--max-num-seqs 64`, `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1`, `VLLM_KIMI_K3_SHARD_SP_SHARED_EXPERT=0`.
  - Decode: `parallelism: {default: dep, gb300: tp}` on two trays, `tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv: 8`, `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=0`, and overrides for the DEP-only decode flags (`--no-data-parallel-hybrid-lb`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, `cudagraph_mode` FULL_AND_PIECEWISE). The GB300 decode MegaMoE entry is dropped because this decode pool has no expert parallelism.
- One guide line points from the existing GB300 section to the selector and lists what stays guide-only.

## Validation

- `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <this checkout>/recipes` from vllm-project/recipes passes; `git diff --check` is clean.
- Rendered `pd_cluster` through `resolveCommand` for GB300 with the Dynamo router (ranks 0 and 1): the prefill and decode argv/env match the qualified InferenceX launch lines for these settings.
- Rendered `pd_cluster` (native router and Dynamo) for GB200, B300, B200, H200 and MI355X: byte-identical to `main`.

## Details

- **Guide-only, because the schema has no field for them:** xPyD worker counts (1P2D-2P5D; the builder renders one pool per role), the qualified MooncakeStore `MultiConnector` options and Mooncake master (the KV Offload row's Mooncake option emits its generic connector last), and the Dynamo frontend's `least-loaded` router mode with 900 s session affinity (the frontend's router mode comes from `strategies/pd_cluster.yaml`).
- **Rendering notes:** role `vllm_args` apply to every GPU and the renderer cannot remove a flag per hardware, so GB300 shows both `--no-enable-prefix-caching` / `--enable-prefix-caching`, `--data-parallel-hybrid-lb` / `--no-data-parallel-hybrid-lb` and (prefill) `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` / `--enable-flashinfer-autotune`; argparse applies the later flag, which is the qualified value. The existing pd_cluster Blackwell `UCX_TLS=rc,cuda_copy` still applies on GB300.
- `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384` is vLLM's API-server default on >=160 GB GPUs (`vllm/engine/arg_utils.py`), which is what the qualified decode ran with.

## Render re-verification

Re-checked with `resolveCommand` against the qualified launch lines of [InferenceX run 39140771499](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/39140771499): every GB300 prefill and decode serving flag matches; the only difference is the benchmark-only synthetic acceptance in the run's speculative config. The contradictory-looking pairs (`--no-enable-prefix-caching` / `--enable-prefix-caching`, `--data-parallel-hybrid-lb` / `--no-…`, `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` / `--enable-…`) come from shared pd_cluster role flags that a model recipe cannot remove per GPU; the GB300 value is always emitted later, so argparse keeps it. Other hardware and strategies render byte-identically to main. Companion: #62542 (GB200) is stacked on this branch.

title: [KV Offload] Warn when secondary-tier KV is tied to the parallel config
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Log a startup warning when `TieringOffloadingSpec`'s secondary-tier KV can't be shared across tensor-parallel sizes, i.e. unless `canonical_layout` is on **and** the model's KV cache layers (and the parallel configuration) are certified parallelism-agnostic. This is the first follow-up listed in #62283.

Related: #62283, #55191 (core fix: direct caches keep TP in their namespace), #61822 (`canonical_layout` docs).

## Claims

- One warning per engine at startup when there is at least one secondary tier and either:
  - `canonical_layout` is off (direct layout), or
  - `canonical_layout` is on, but the layers can't all be certified as parallelism-agnostic (for example Mamba/GDN hybrids, which fall back to the opaque mapping), or PP, DCP or PCP is > 1. Today, this case starts up normally with nothing in the log saying sharing is off.
- No warning when canonical KV is portable, and none without secondary tiers.
- No behavior change: it doesn't raise, and lookups and namespaces are unchanged.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/spec.py tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py`: all hooks pass.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py`: 192 passed (macOS, CPU).
- New `test_tiering_spec_warns_when_secondary_tiers_are_topology_bound` drives the real `get_manager()` with the `example` tier, faking only the `/dev/shm` region and the primary tier, as the `create_worker` tests in that file do. It covers 5 cases (direct layout flagged agnostic, direct, canonical uncertified, canonical portable, no tiers) and asserts that exactly one warning is logged, or none. Mutation checks against it:
  - `spec.py` from `main`: 3 failed.
  - Gating only on `is_parallelism_agnostic`: the "direct layout flagged agnostic" case fails, so the test guards the case #62283 is about.
  - Gating only on `canonical_layout`: the "canonical uncertified" case fails.
  - Logging the warning twice: 3 failed.

  CI runs it in the "V1 KV Offload" step (`pytest -v -s v1/kv_offload`).
- End-to-end on one L4 (Colab, base `04631c4915`): `vllm serve <model> --max-model-len 2048` with `OffloadingConnector`, `spec_name: TieringOffloadingSpec`, `cpu_bytes_to_use: 2 GiB`, `secondary_tiers: [{"type": "fs", "root_dir": "/tmp/kvfs"}]`. For each case I waited for `/health`, sent one completion, and counted warning lines. This run used the previous revision, which logged a separate message for each case. The trigger conditions are identical, and the current revision only merges the two messages into one.

| Model | `canonical_layout` | Healthy, completion OK | Topology warning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | off | yes | 1 |
| Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | `true` (`all_layers_portable=True`) | yes | 0 |
| Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B (GDN hybrid) | `true` (`all_layers_portable=False`) | yes | 1 |

<details>
<summary>Log excerpts (previous two-message revision)</summary>

```text
# Qwen3-0.6B, canonical_layout off
(EngineCore pid=7823) INFO 10-19 22:37:09 [spec.py:458] Created TieringOffloadingManager with primary tier (lru, 1170 chunks) and 1 secondary tier(s)
(EngineCore pid=7823) WARNING 10-19 22:37:09 [spec.py:466] Secondary-tier KV is only valid for engines with the same parallel configuration; set canonical_layout=true in kv_connector_extra_config to share it across TP sizes.

# Qwen3-0.6B, canonical_layout: true
(EngineCore pid=9036) INFO 10-19 22:37:59 [spec.py:589] Canonical KV layout enabled (all_layers_portable=True)
(EngineCore pid=9036) INFO 10-19 22:38:10 [spec.py:458] Created TieringOffloadingManager with primary tier (lru, 1170 chunks) and 1 secondary tier(s)

# Qwen3.5-0.8B, canonical_layout: true
(EngineCore pid=9775) INFO 10-19 22:41:54 [spec.py:589] Canonical KV layout enabled (all_layers_portable=False)
(EngineCore pid=9775) INFO 10-19 22:42:12 [spec.py:458] Created TieringOffloadingManager with primary tier (lru, 321 chunks) and 1 secondary tier(s)
(EngineCore pid=9775) WARNING 10-19 22:42:12 [spec.py:472] canonical_layout is set, but not every KV cache layer (or the parallel configuration) is parallelism-agnostic; secondary-tier KV is only valid for engines with the same parallel configuration.
```

The current message for both warning cases:

```text
Secondary-tier KV is only valid for engines with the same parallel configuration; sharing it across TP sizes needs canonical_layout=true in kv_connector_extra_config, parallelism-agnostic KV cache layers, and no PP, DCP or PCP.
```

</details>

## Details

- **Why:** without `canonical_layout`, the direct layout's bytes depend on the engine's parallel configuration. Engines with different TP sizes sharing a tier get silently wrong KV today (#62283), or always miss once #55191 lands. Nothing at startup tells the user why. With `canonical_layout` on, a model with layers that can't be certified (for example Mamba/GDN layers, which fall back to the opaque mapping) keeps TP in the namespace and never shares across TP sizes, and only an `all_layers_portable=False` info line hints at it.
- **Where:** `TieringOffloadingSpec.get_manager()`, next to the existing "Created TieringOffloadingManager" log. It runs once per engine on the scheduler side, whereas `__init__` also runs in the workers.
- **Condition:** `secondary_tiers and not (canonical_layout and is_parallelism_agnostic)`. It requires the user's `canonical_layout` flag, not just `is_parallelism_agnostic`: before #55191, that flag is True in exactly the direct-layout case that corrupts, so gating on it alone would hide the warning where it matters most. After #55191, `is_parallelism_agnostic` is False whenever `canonical_layout` is off, so the same condition stays correct. With `canonical_layout` on, the static `is_parallelism_agnostic` check decides whether the tier's namespace drops TP. It is also False for DCP > 1 or `world_size != tp_size` (PP or PCP > 1), so the message names "no PP, DCP or PCP" alongside the layer requirement.
- **Wording:** the warning says KV is "only valid for" engines with the same parallel configuration, not "only reusable by". Until #55191 lands, a cross-TP read on the V1 runner loads wrong KV instead of missing, and "only valid for" is accurate before and after #55191.
- **Known false positives:** the advice is harmless in each case. Excluding them would mean hardcoding tier names or more namespace rules in the spec.
  - Replicated MLA without `canonical_layout`: it can already be shared between engines with TP > 1, but still gets the warning.
  - The `example` tier (in-process memory) and the `kvcr` tier: they don't share KV across engines through the `FileMapper` namespace, but still get the warning.
- **Level:** `warning`, as the issue asks. Happy to switch to `info` if it's too noisy for single-topology deployments.
- **Docs:** no changes here. #61822 documents `canonical_layout` in the KV offloading usage guide.
- **Not a duplicate:** no open PR references #62283 or adds this check. #55191 changes the namespace gate in `offloading/config.py`, and this PR doesn't touch that file.

title: [Core][Frontend] Process checkpoint lifecycle with HTTP prepare/status/resume
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Make process checkpoint/restore (CRIU plus `cuda-checkpoint`, run by an external orchestrator such as [ai-dynamo/snapshot](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/snapshot)) a first-class engine lifecycle with a production HTTP surface: `POST /checkpoint/prepare`, `GET /checkpoint/status`, `POST /checkpoint/resume`, and `--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup`. Implements the minimal API from RFC #60422 ([summary](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60422#issuecomment-6187366614)), building on the communicator hooks from #46877 and the paused-request rejection from #51488.

## Claims

- The engine owns a repeatable lifecycle: `running → preparing → prepared → resuming → running`, or `failed`. `AsyncLLM.checkpoint_prepare(mode)` and `checkpoint_restore()` each run as one engine call, so repeated and concurrent calls (several API servers, DP) are no-ops. `checkpoint_state()` reports the state; DP engines merge as failed if any failed, otherwise the shared state.
- `POST /checkpoint/prepare?mode=wait|abort|keep` drains with the pause mode, discards the KV cache and runs the workers' `checkpoint_prepare` hooks. It returns 200 once started (poll status), or 409 with the reason if the engine cannot prepare now (no sleep mode, asleep, mid-cycle).
- `GET /checkpoint/status` returns 200 when prepared, 503 until then and 500 after a failure. `POST /checkpoint/resume` returns 200 when resuming or done (orchestrators redeliver), 409 while preparing or failed. Both work after a restore or in place.
- While an engine does not serve, `/health` returns 503 (checked whenever sleep mode is on), new requests get the retryable `engine_paused` error from #51488, and `sleep`, `wake_up` and `resume_scheduler` are refused.
- `--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup` prepares each engine once it starts, for capture-at-startup orchestrators.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run` on the changed files (ruff, mypy, typos, markdownlint, SPDX, config docstrings) passes.
- New unit test `test_checkpoint_prepare_then_restore_run_in_order` (`tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py`): preparing releases the KV cache before the worker hooks, restoring runs the hooks before the KV cache wakes and scheduling resumes, repeats are no-ops, and new requests are rejected in between.
- End to end with ai-dynamo/snapshot (CRIU plus `cuda-checkpoint`) on 8x B200, using an earlier revision of this lifecycle with the same status and resume routes and `--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup`, restoring into a new pod:

  | Configuration | Result |
  | :-- | :-- |
  | Qwen3-30B-A3B DEP8, Python frontend | Source status 200 `prepared` and `/health` 503. After restore and resume: `/health` 200, a repeated resume 200, correct greedy completions, 16/16 concurrent requests. |
  | Same, Rust frontend (stacked follow-up) | Same results. |
  | P/D over NIXL, prefill and decode restored on different nodes, then a second prefill from the same checkpoint (stacked follow-up) | 3/3 greedy matches per phase, 0 failed transfers, two concurrent empty resumes both 200. |

- This revision on 1x B200 (`vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --enable-sleep-mode`, Python frontend), two prepare/resume cycles in one process with no capture:

  | Step | Result |
  | :-- | :-- |
  | Serving | status 503 `running`, `/health` 200, completion `" Paris. The capital of France is also the capital of the"` |
  | `POST /checkpoint/prepare` | 200 `prepared` (idle server), status 200, `/health` 503, a completion gets 503 `Generation is paused. Please retry after it resumes.` |
  | Repeated prepare | 200 `prepared` |
  | `POST /sleep` (dev mode) mid-cycle | refused: `Cannot sleep while the checkpoint state is prepared` |
  | Two concurrent `POST /checkpoint/resume` | both 200 `running`; `/health` 200, status 503 `running`, same completion as before |

- `pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py -k "checkpoint or pause or kv_cache_release or wake_up or reject"`: 21 passed (on the stack with the follow-ups, whose version of the new test adds their extra call).



## Details

**Why this shape.** The pieces exist upstream, but an external orchestrator cannot use them safely: `/pause`, `/sleep` and `/wake_up` are dev-mode routes, `checkpoint_prepare/restore` (#46877) only run the worker hooks and leave sequencing to the caller, nothing reports where the engine is, and other calls can interleave. Moving each step into one engine call gives an idempotent, observable contract that any orchestrator (Snapshot, scripts, future live migration) can drive over HTTP, and that the Rust frontend can call without copying the sequence.

**Breaking change.** `AsyncLLM.checkpoint_prepare()` and `checkpoint_restore()` previously only ran the worker communicator hooks, and callers paused and slept first. They now run the whole step and refuse an engine that is already asleep. The only known caller is NVIDIA Dynamo, which would call `checkpoint_prepare()` alone. The worker-level hooks are unchanged.

**Not duplicate.** #51360 (`vllm snapshot`), #52132, #35934, #37921, #58183 and #61544 implement checkpointing inside vLLM (CRIU and/or `cuda-checkpoint`). This PR adds no checkpointing code; it is the boundary an external orchestrator needs, and those paths could reuse the same lifecycle later. #48311 owns pause/drain/sleep for RL; this PR reuses `pause_generation` and adds no new pause semantics.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- With sleep mode on, `/health` asks the engines for the lifecycle state on every probe (one utility round trip), so a prepared server leaves rotation even when other API servers prepared it.
- The routes are always on and need no API key, like `/sleep` and `/pause` under dev mode and `/scale_elastic_ep`. They are listed in `docs/usage/security.md`. A deployment that does not want them can block the paths at the proxy.
- `EngineCoreProc.resume_scheduler` now clears `reject_new_requests` after the base class's checks, so a refused resume keeps rejecting requests.
- Follow-ups, already prototyped: Rust frontend routes (galletas1712/vllm#4), a checkpoint resource registry for CPU offload and HiSparse host memory (galletas1712/vllm#5), and independent P/D restore over NIXL (galletas1712/vllm#3). No gRPC `Control` methods yet.

title: [Doc] Document B300 disaggregated Dynamo serving for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash / 记录 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 在 B300 上的 Dynamo 分离式部署
body:
## Overview

Document the B300 disaggregated Dynamo + vLLM deployment of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash from [InferenceX #4231](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4231). Follow-up to #62534, whose Dynamo section defers disaggregated settings to Dynamo's examples; those examples do not cover this topology.

## Claims

- `pd_cluster` gains a `b300` hardware override and `b300: dep` pool parallelism: N two-GPU DEP2 prefill engines (four per node) and one DEP8 decode node, with the engine flags and EFA transport env (`FI_PROVIDER=efa`, `UCX_TLS` with `srd`, `NIXL_UCX_SGL_ENABLE=0`, cumem allocator off).
- Per-role B300 overrides: prefill scheduling (`--prefill-schedule-interval 2`, `--prefix-cache-retention-interval 32768`, 16384 batched tokens); decode `--enable-eplb` with 16 redundant experts over `symm_mem`, `VLLM_MAX_ASYNC_KV_ADMITS_PER_STEP=4`, graphs every six tokens.
- A short "Disaggregated serving on B300" guide subsection documents what the builder cannot express: the `push_as_nixl` connector on NIXL's `LIBFABRIC` backend, the prefill `MultiConnector` with `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` (70 GiB host KV per rank), the libfabric install the image needs, and the sidecar and frontend flags.

## Validation

- `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <checkout>/recipes` from vllm-project/recipes: passed.
- Every new JSON argument and the guide's JSON block parse.
- Deployment evidence: InferenceX #4231 full sweep, [run 39015109057](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/39015109057), on the original DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash checkpoint and the `nightly-x86_64-dev-20261012-59e75f4` image. No new GPU validation for the 1017 checkpoint.

## Details

The B300 override block mirrors the GB300 one and differs where the hardware does: 8 GPUs per node (DEP8 decode on one node), EFA instead of NVLink between trays (LIBFABRIC backend, VMM allocator off because the EFA provider cannot register cumem memory), and a longer gloo timeout for the Engram shard load. The `--kv-transfer-config` JSON stays in the guide rather than `extra_args` because the strategy emits its own NixlConnector config and the two would collide.

AI assistance was used: Claude (claude-fable-5-1, via Claude Code) drafted the overrides and guide text from the author's validated recipe; the author reviewed and ran the validation.

title: [Performance]: Long-prefill decode starvation survives prefill/decode interleaving — head-to-head from two stacks on 2× GB10, plus a 4×98k-prefill OOM boundary
body:
## Summary

We run DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (MoE + sparse MLA) on a **2× DGX Spark GB10 pair** (TP=2 over a 200 Gb RoCE fabric, one 128 GB unified-memory node per rank) as a small-office shared service. Long-document ingestion (one user pastes a 100k-token document) repeatedly starves concurrent short chat requests.

We already reported the raw phenomenon and the `--prefill-schedule-interval` mitigation in #54919 (that fix works for the *Qwen* model we tested: 1.2 → 22.6 tok/s on the short stream). This issue is different: we ran a **controlled head-to-head between two complete stacks** — one stock fork build, one heavily patched community recipe — and the conclusion is that the patched recipe does **not** fix starvation, it only changes its shape. We also hit a hard memory boundary at 4 concurrent long prefills that looks like #50298.

Posting because we would like to know what upstream considers the sanctioned path here.

## Setup

Hardware: 2× DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, 128 GB unified memory each), 200 Gb RoCE v2 (`GID_INDEX=5`), TP=2 + EP across nodes.
Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, fp8 checkpoint, 156 GB / 48 shards, ~79 GB per rank.
Workload, identical for both stacks (same script, same weights):

- long request: 560,000 chars of English filler (~**98,620 prompt tokens**) + a Chinese instruction, `max_tokens=8`
- short request: an 11-token prompt, `max_tokens=128`
- short requests are launched 3 s after the long ones start
- a random 16-byte hex prefix is prepended to every long doc so prefix caching cannot mask the prefill
- 3 short-chat concurrency runs: 8 and 16 simultaneous 300-token answers

### Stack A — stock-ish fork build (baseline)
`vLLM 0.25.2.dev0+g752a3a504` (vendor fork image `ghcr.io/anemll/dspark-vllm-gx10:0.1.1`, no source patches), `--max-model-len 1048576`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, `--max-num-seqs 12`, `--long-prefill-token-threshold 1024`, `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla`, `--block-size 256`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.80`, speculative DSpark k=5.
Log: `Available KV cache memory: 10.61 GiB`, `GPU KV cache size: 1,576,402 tokens`, `Maximum concurrency for 1,048,576 tokens per request: 1.50x`.

### Stack B — patched recipe (`vLLM 0.21.1rc1.dev339+g1967a5627bc3`)
Same model, plus 4 bind-mounted source patches (draft proposer, base proposer, `v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`, spec-decode `dspark.py`), `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 24e9` (or 16e9), `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90`, `--cudagraph-capture-sizes [2,4,6,12,24,48,72,96,144]`, `--enable-flashinfer-autotune`, speculative DSpark k=5.
Log at 24 GB pin: `GPU KV cache size: 3,386,611 tokens`, `Maximum concurrency …: 3.23x`. At 16 GB pin: 2,257,740 tokens, 2.15x.

Both stacks: single-stream idle decode is the same, 34–36 tok/s. So the difference is purely in scheduling under contention.

## Results

`short decode (tok/s) / short TTFT / long TTFT median`, all measured end-to-end via streaming:

| scenario | Stack A (1.50x KV) | Stack B (3.23x KV) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 long + 1 short | **3.6** / 1.78 s / 73.9 s | 3.3 / 1.61 s / 65.0 s |
| 2 long + 2 short | **21.1** / **124.4 s** / 127.3 s | 1.8 / **3.03 s** / 115.9 s |
| 3 long + 2 short | **16.9** / **117.3 s** / 120.3 s | 0.6 / **9.22 s** / 167.4 s |
| 4 long + 2 short | **19.4** / 108.3 s / 111.3 s | **crash** (24 GB pin) / 0.5 / 6.5 s / **269.2 s** (16 GB pin) |

How to read it: the two stacks make opposite trade-offs.

- **A** keeps the short requests queued until the long prefills finish (`TTFT 108–124 s`), then decodes them at 17–21 tok/s. Total wall for the short answer 108–119 s (grows with concurrency).
- **B** admits the short request immediately (`TTFT 3–9 s`), but the decode trickles at 0.5–1.8 tok/s. Total wall for the short answer 63–80 s.

So B buys 3–9 s of "first character on screen" and roughly 40 s of wall clock, but a user watching a chat box still gets ~1 character per second. And the interleaving is not free:

- at 3 concurrent long prefills, B's long-prefill TTFT is **167 s vs A's 120 s** (+40%)
- B's 3.23x KV pool does not buy stability (see next section)

Concurrency, pure short chat (the load where B actually wins):

| concurrency | Stack A | Stack B |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | 85.5 tok/s aggregate, 11.9 per stream, TTFT 0.68 s | **99.2 tok/s**, 13.9, TTFT 1.32 s |
| 16 | 74.5 tok/s, 12.7, TTFT 1.36 s | **112.3 tok/s**, 14.0, TTFT 0.82 s (4 requests queued by `max-num-seqs=12`, TTFT 22 s) |

So B is genuinely better for many concurrent short conversations (+16% / +51%), and that gain is independent of the KV pin size.

## The hard boundary at 4 concurrent long prefills

With `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 24e9`, 4 concurrent ~98k-token prefills reproducibly kill Stack B:

- prefills reach ~58% (`num_computed_tokens ≈ 55k–58k` of 98.6k) with `total_num_scheduled_tokens=4096` (1024 per request)
- `dmesg`: `NVRM: … Out of memory [NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY] … from _memdescAllocInternal(pMemDesc)`
- the worker hangs, `shm_broadcast` warns "No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds" ×4, then `EngineCore encountered a fatal error` ~5 min later
- Stack A completes the same 4-prefill workload in 111 s with no memory error

Dropping the pin to 16 GB makes B survive the same workload, but long-prefill TTFT goes **111 s → 269 s**.

This is the part that most resembles #50298 (attention workspace sizing). It would help to know whether there is a supported way to size the attention workspace when `kv-cache-memory-bytes` is pinned manually — we pin it because `max_model_len=auto` plans a KV pool fine but then dies during init.

## What we would like to know

1. **Is per-step prefill admission by *time* supported anywhere?** `--prefill-schedule-interval` (#54919) admits prefill every N *engine steps*, which works well when the chunk size is small (`--max-num-batched-tokens 1024` gave us 22.6 tok/s on the other model), but it is a step-count proxy for time. A wall-clock budget per step, or explicit prefill/decode SM partitioning, is what the workload actually wants.
2. **Is PD disaggregation the sanctioned answer on this hardware?** On a 2-node GB10 pair the weights are ~79 GB/rank out of 128 GB unified, so the KV/workspace headroom is thin. Is there a recommended PD topology here, or is the expectation to run smaller models per node?
3. **Any guidance on attention-workspace sizing with a pinned KV pool?** If `kv_cache_memory_bytes` is the intended knob for "leave room for workspace", what is the supported relationship between pin size, `max_num_seqs`, `cudagraph_capture_sizes` and the sparse-MLA workspace?

Happy to run further measurements on this pair — including a git bisect, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM` fallbacks, or PD prototypes — if that would help narrow it down.

Related: #54919 (original starvation report + cadence mitigation), #50298 (attention workspace).

title: [Feature][HiSparse] Add a platform backend for device operations
body:
## Overview

Introduce a platform-selected device backend for HiSparse so hardware plugins can reuse its common cache runtime and connector. Keep the existing CUDA operations as the default implementation.

Related: #60072; Ascend plugin integration: vllm-project/vllm-ascend#19109.

## Claims

- Add `Platform.get_hisparse_backend_cls()` and a lazily resolved `HiSparseBackend` interface. Platforms without an implementation remain rejected.
- Delegate cache ops, host registration, stream/event handling (including IPC export/import), resident-row and FP8 prefill gathers, DMA submission, LRU initialization and statistics dtype through the backend. Keep CUDA's generic-stream and CUDA-stream APIs distinct.
- Add cache-format validation before host allocation and an initialization-only `prepare_kv_cache_views()` hook before handle binding, inside the existing allocation rollback scope.

The common scheduler, HMA allocation, residency algorithm, KV format and attention math remain owned by the existing implementation. This patch contains no Ascend kernels, C8 format changes, performance optimization, experimental manifests or independent profiling-cache lifecycle repair. Existing PP/CP/graph restrictions remain.

## Validation

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on all nine changed Python files: passed.
- `git diff --check` and Python syntax checks: passed.
- Twenty isolated CPU contract cases passed using real torch and the checked-in test functions: platform-class-scoped backend selection, strided and byte-packed resident payloads, runtime gather dispatch, shared-pool event dispatch for writer/reader ranks, CUDA stream/LRU delegation, validation before allocation, same-storage view preparation before binding, rollback for allocation/view/bind/buffer failures with private/shared pools, and synchronize-before-unregister behavior. The local harness loads the relevant production definitions with AST to bypass unrelated Windows serving imports; this is **not** full pytest collection or hardware validation.
- Normal collection was attempted with `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest --noconftest -q tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py -k 'hisparse_cuda_backend or hisparse_cuda_lru'`; it failed during unrelated imports (`pybase64` missing). The full suites and standard pre-commit/CI have not passed locally.
- Earlier Ascend integration runs exercised the interface on real Ascend950 hardware, including full GLM TP8 Decode-graph/MTP3 execution. Those snapshots include separate plugin and compatibility changes and do not qualify this narrowed, rebased PR head. CUDA/ROCm hardware regression and independent final-head model validation remain pending. No performance or accuracy improvement is claimed; no accuracy evaluation was started for this submission.

Intended focused CI/reproduction command, in a prepared vLLM environment:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -k hisparse
```

## Details

A hardware plugin opts in by overriding `Platform.get_hisparse_backend_cls()` to return the qualified name of its `HiSparseBackend` implementation. The default CUDA backend delegates to the same torch/CUDA functions and `_C_cache_ops` entry points. Backend lookup is cached by class name; no new environment variable is introduced. Common code selects the backend through `current_platform`; device-specific FP8 byte-view compatibility belongs in that backend. The common connector retains TP broadcast and request ownership, while backends create, export and import their own events. The non-HiSparse sparse-attention path is unchanged. Plugins must implement the newly exposed resident-gather and optional shared-pool/FP8-prefill operations before enabling those paths; this PR does not establish Ascend feature readiness.

The view hook runs once per cache initialization, after allocation and before binding. It may alias device-specific views while retaining common allocation ownership; per-forward metadata and transfers do not belong in this hook. Its no-op default preserves CUDA behavior. A partially submitted backend DMA batch is drained before descriptor ownership is released on the error path.

Duplicate-work review checked open HiSparse PRs, including #57602 and #60358. Those implement ROCm execution/registration and other fixes; this patch supplies a platform extension interface and does not port their kernels or take over their lifecycle fixes. The broader fork integration PR (zhenwenqi2024/vllm#1) is a separate experiment snapshot, not this upstream diff.

This is a **draft for design feedback**, not a merge-ready hardware qualification. AI assistance was used for implementation, tests and preparation. Human line-by-line review and personally executed validation are not asserted; those remain required before requesting readiness/merge.

title: [Perf][MoE] Hopper MegaMoE: run block-FP8 MoE on FlashInfer's SM90 megakernel
body:
## Overview

vLLM has no MegaMoE that runs on Hopper today:

- the DeepGEMM MegaMoE (`deep_gemm_mega_moe`) requires SM100;
- the FlashInfer MoE-EP megakernels (`flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`, `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm`) require SM100

This PR runs block-FP8 MoE checkpoints on Hopper with FlashInfer's SM90 FP8 MegaMoE, which ships in FlashInfer 0.7.2. The kernel fuses dispatch, both expert GEMMs and combine. It goes through the existing `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` path with no model code, so any block-FP8 MoE can use it.

Related:
- #58540: the same kernel, but for DeepSeek-V4 FP4 checkpoints converted to FP8, and on files that #54049 removed.
- #62073: Beam on SM100. It contains the same idle-rank change as this PR.
- #60895: DeepGEMM MegaMoE for GLM-5.3-Flash, SM100 only.
- #53527: DeepSeek-V4 through a DeepGEMM fork.

## Claims

- GLM-5.3-Flash on 8x H200 (DP8/EP8, 128K/512 decode, MTP3): +11% to +18% output throughput and -6% to -14% TPOT p50, at concurrency 8 to 192.
- One MoE layer at EP8: -7% at 8 tokens/rank, up to -48% at 8192 tokens/rank.
- GSM8K: 0.919 vs 0.917.
- The backend is opt-in. Default backends do not change.

## Validation

**Decode.**
- Hardware and model: 8x H200, GLM-5.3-Flash FP8.
- Baseline: the default FP8 path, FlashInfer CUTLASS with allgather/reducescatter. All other settings are vLLM defaults.
- Load: DecodeBenchConnector, ISL 128K / OSL 512, MTP3 with synthetic acceptance [0.8, 0.6, 0.5], N = 2C prompts.
- Runs: A/B/A with two passes per arm. "Base" is the mean of the two baseline arms.

| C | 8 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 192 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| output tok/s, base | 911 | 2895 | 5204 | 7977 | 10074 |
| output tok/s, this PR | 1009 (+10.8%) | 3402 (+17.5%) | 5893 (+13.2%) | 9326 (+16.9%) | 11917 (+18.3%) |
| TPOT p50 ms, base → this PR | 7.60 → 6.86 | 9.20 → 7.96 | 9.27 → 8.72 | 10.81 → 9.85 | 11.58 → 10.87 |

**MoE layer, EP8.** GLM-5.3-Flash expert shapes, milliseconds per layer:

| tokens/rank | 8 | 64 | 128 | 512 | 1024 | 8192 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline | 0.265 | 0.381 | 0.446 | 0.834 | 1.378 | 9.204 |
| this PR | 0.247 | 0.294 | 0.310 | 0.461 | 0.754 | 4.798 |

**GSM8K.** 1319 questions, 5-shot, natural MTP3: 0.917 → 0.919.

**Tests.**

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_fi_moe_ep.py tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py
# CPU: 29 passed. SM90 GPU: 8 passed (4 expert shapes x EP2/EP4).
```

The SM90 GPU tests need at least two Hopper GPUs and `nvshmem4py`, so CI does not run them.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve <GLM-5.3-Flash FP8> --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"DecodeBenchConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_rates":[0.8,0.6,0.5]}' \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl   # omitted for the baseline

vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 512 \
  --ignore-eos --request-rate inf --max-concurrency $C --num-prompts $((2 * C))
```
</details>

## Details

- **Kernel.**
  - FlashInfer `Sm90PullFp8MegaMoeConfig`, with FP32 128x128 weight scales and a SwiGLU clamp.
  - FlashInfer's push-style SM90 backend has no SwiGLU clamp, so it cannot serve `swiglu_limit` models.
- **Weights.**
  - The kernel wants FC1 rows interleaved as `[pair, {gate, up}, 8]` under one 128x128 scale. Each scale block therefore covers rows from two checkpoint blocks, and both use `max(s_gate, s_up)`.
  - This is exact for power-of-two scales, which GLM-5.3-Flash has. Other checkpoints get one extra E4M3 rounding on half of the FC1 rows.
- **Workspaces.**
  - The kernel always processes its whole token buffer, with a launch geometry picked for that size. With a single buffer sized at `max_num_batched_tokens`, decode is slower than the baseline.
  - The adapter therefore adds 64-, 256- and 1024-token workspaces. Each call uses the smallest one that fits the largest batch across DP ranks.
- **Loaders.**
  - The fp8, compressed-tensors, online FP8 and Quark FP8 MoE methods now call the experts' `process_weights_after_loading`. It is a no-op for other experts.
  - The SM90 path is chosen from the quant config, not the weight dtype. FP8 weights keep their dtype, so a rebuild from preprocessed weights picks the same path.
- **Idle ranks.** With pass-through stages, the experts own the EP collective. A rank without tokens therefore still enters them. The change is identical to the one in #62073.
- **Limitations.**
  - The backend needs expert parallelism and `nvshmem4py`.
  - It rejects DBO, runtime weight transfer and `apply_router_weight_on_input`.
  - Shared experts are not fused.
  - FlashInfer's SM90 input staging is torch-composed, about 1.2 ms per step at C128.

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Sharded greedy verification and fused vocab-parallel draft argmax
body:
## Purpose

With a vocab-parallel LM head, greedy speculative decoding all-gathers the **full-vocabulary** logits across TP ranks: on the target side before rejection sampling, and (without `use_local_argmax_reduction`) on the draft side before the argmax. For a 200k vocabulary at TP4 that is a large gather on every decode step, although greedy verification only needs the argmax of each row.

This PR keeps the logits on each rank:

1. **Sharded greedy verification** (`v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/sharded_greedy_verifier.py`, opt-in via `VLLM_SHARDED_GREEDY_VERIFY=1`). Each rank reduces its vocabulary shard to compact per-block `(max, token id)` statistics, only those are all-gathered, and one kernel finishes the global argmax, acceptance (including synthetic acceptance), bonus token and sampled/rejected counts. The blocks keep the native kernels' global boundaries (8192 for draft positions, 1024 for the bonus), also across shard edges, so ties resolve exactly as on the full logits.
   - Models opt in through `compute_logits_local`, the hook batch-sharded sampling already uses (added here to the ROCm MiniMax-M3 model, matching the NVIDIA one). Any TP size > 1 (including non-power-of-two), vocabulary < 2^24, hidden size and number of speculative tokens; CUDA and ROCm.
   - Per step, the batch falls back to the native path, before any logits are computed, unless every request is greedy with no logits processing, logprobs, structured output, draft logits, adaptive/block verification or watermarking.
2. **Fused `LogitsProcessor.get_top_tokens`** (`model_executor/layers/vocab_parallel_argmax.py`), i.e. the existing `speculative_config.use_local_argmax_reduction` draft path. The in-place padding mask, the torch reduction, the stack and the last-dim all-gather become two Triton kernels with a dim-0 all-gather. Same result (lowest id on ties, NaN wins, as `torch.argmax`); it applies to every model using `LocalArgmaxMixin`.

## Results (MI355X, MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 TP4, EAGLE3-GQA, K=3)

Base image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm72-1b2a666391f2a24228a1436b64d547c34cc6b6ce` plus the AITER gfx950 unified-attention routing fix (ROCm/aiter#6336) so an unrelated draft-attention regression does not dilute the numbers. This branch is based on the same vLLM commit; the measured image contains exactly these files. Server: `VLLM_SHARDED_GREEDY_VERIFY=1`, `--speculative-config '{..., "use_local_argmax_reduction": true}'`.

**8k/1k C24** (240 requests, zero HTTP warmup, warmed compile caches, interleaved rounds vs same-round baseline):

| | output throughput | rounds |
|---|---:|---|
| this PR (verification + fused get_top_tokens) | **+1.75%** | +1.47 / +2.02 |
| first, MiniMax-specific revision of this PR (same batch) | +1.78% | +1.68 / +1.88 |
| verification + unfused `use_local_argmax_reduction` | +1.25% | +1.46 / +1.04 |
| verification only | +0.65% | +0.65 / +0.64 |

Mean TPOT −3.0%, p99 E2EL −1.3%. Per decode step (profiler, 24 req × 4 tokens), NCCL in the cycle went from 385 µs to 83 µs.

**AgenticX C24** (InferenceX recipe `minimaxm3/vllm/mi355x-fp4-mtp/agentic.yaml`, 3600 s, one run of this revision vs the same baseline): P50 interactivity +1.9%, P90 interactivity +0.7%, mean TPOT −0.5%; throughput is trace-saturated (+0.3%). **TTFT regresses: mean +6.8%, P90 +8.1%.** Two earlier runs that combined this change with a draft-metadata change showed the same TTFT shift (+6.3% / +5.3% mean), while other changes measured against the same baseline did not, so the TTFT cost is attributed to this PR and is being investigated before this leaves draft.

Correctness: real-acceptance greedy EAGLE3 smoke (24 concurrent ≥8k-token prompts + 4 short requests): generated text and token counts identical to the baseline (24/24, 4/4).

## Test Plan

- `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sharded_greedy_verify.py`: TP2/3/4/8 emulated in one process (per-shard statistics concatenated in rank order, as `all_gather(dim=0)` produces), compared with `rejection_sample` + `get_num_sampled_and_rejected` on the full logits. Covers vocab 1000/50257/200064 (including shards narrower than a block), K=1/3/5, synthetic acceptance, prefilling requests and placeholder drafts, bf16 ties and planted cross-shard ties, unaligned vocabulary padding, and NaN rows staying in-vocabulary.
- `tests/model_executor/layers/test_vocab_parallel_argmax.py`: fused argmax vs `torch.argmax` for TP1/2/3/4/8, fp32/bf16, ties, NaN, padding, empty batch and all `-inf` rows.
- 157 passed on MI355X.

Draft: E2E measured on MiniMax-M3 / ROCm only so far.
